title: Surviving the Game as a Barbarian 1-823
author: Jung Yun-kang 정윤강

chapters.title: Surviving The Game As A Barbarian
paragraphs: The protagonist, Hansu Lee, finally reached the boss stage after nine years of playing the game “Dungeon and Stone”, which no one had been able to clear until now.

However, just as he entered the boss room, he saw a notification alerting him that he had cleared the tutorial and that he had possessed the body of the barbarian, Bjorn Yandel, who was a playable character in the game!

In the world of “Dungeon and Stone”, only one city remained standing after the destruction of the world. A labyrinth would open every month, offering explorers a chance to clear it for rewards. In this world where barbarians are seen as useless in everything but battle, a barbarian who does not fight will not be able to survive. If one cannot pay the outrageous taxes demanded by the city, the only fate that awaits is a downgrade in status to a ‘lower-class citizen’. If it is revealed that you are possessing the character you are playing, you will be named an “evil spirit” and killed. The only way for Hansu Lee to survive is to enter the labyrinth and fight while risking his life.
With the skills he has accumulated over nine years of gameplay and a stupidly strong barbarian physique, he strives to survive in this game!

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Prelude
paragraphs: I’d loved games ever since I was little. The reason was simple. Because I spent all of my days in a hospital, I naturally had nothing to do other than play games. And as time passed, gaming became an integral part of my life. But when you did anything for long enough, you were bound to get tired of it.
“Fuck... is this AI for real? Why are you healing that bastard?”

At some point, I found that no matter what game I played, it wasn’t as enjoyable as it used to be. It wasn’t a matter of genre, whether it was AOS, RPG, FPS, etcetera. The problem was that all of the games that were released every year were trash. The plots and universes were pretty much copy-pasted, and the systems lacked depth.
I wanted a game with something more unique. That was when I discovered Dungeon and Stone.
Click, click.

The genre was single-player RPG. It was a foreign indie game. There was no Korean language support, and it featured 2D pixel art graphics, which was rare these days. To be honest, the game was far from my taste. Still, it was free, so I installed it to give it a try. And it wasn’t long before I fell in love with it.
“Wow, we almost died at the end because of that fucking priest.”

It was an unusual game in many ways. When a character died, they had to be trained up again from scratch. NPCs were essential to the progress of the game, and the degree of freedom was also extremely high for a vertical-scrolling game. The skill system and worldbuilding were charming, and the story was interesting even in English. Most importantly, there was a strange distinct quality to this game.
Tap-tap. Ta-ta-ta-tap.

A social service agent who had just been assigned to work in the subway as an alternative to military conscription, I delved into the world of Dungeon and Stone and hit the ground running. It wasn’t easy. Combat in this game was not simply decided by HP/MP. Even with full stats, a single mistake could mean that the character that I had been painstakingly playing for three months was gone.
“Let’s get it...”

Two years into playing the game, I hadn’t even reached the halfway point. Swallowing my pride, I combed the internet for a strategy guide. Since I couldn’t find any information on Korean websites, I had to translate from English to read anything. Even so, the sites I found weren’t much help. There weren’t many users abroad either, so there were very few relevant articles and no useful tips. Unlike the people who had played it for only a month or two before writing it off as a failed game, I, who had been seriously exploring this world for two years, had a much better understanding of it. So, I stopped looking for a walkthrough.
“Three up, four to the left, one down, two to the left, then six up again, and four to the right. Finally, avoid the trap and... nice.”
This game had come to me at a time when I was desperately looking for a new game to play anyway. No matter how long it took, I decided I wanted to progress forward on my own. And...
“Whew.”
Just like that, I made it to where I was now.
[Gate of the Abyss.]

My current character was standing in front of the portal connected to the final boss’s lair. But of course, I wouldn’t be seeing the end until I revisited this place several more times. This was not a game where you could defeat the boss in just one try. Even so, my stiff fingers were a telltale sign of how nervous I was at that moment.
“The final boss...”

It might mean nothing to some, but it took me nine years to get here. It would not be an exaggeration to say that this game had been with me for the entirety of my twenties. When I was discharged from social service, when I returned to school after years away, and even on the day I received a letter of acceptance from the job I wanted after graduation—I had been playing Dungeon and Stone the entire time.
[Will you enter?]

As my character approached the portal, I was asked if I was willing to enter. Of course, I clicked [Yes]. However, since it was the final boss’s room, another pretty ominous message popped up right after.
[You may never return.]
[Are you still willing to enter?]
From the player’s point of view, this was an unnecessary prompt. Why wouldn’t I enter this place?
[Yes/No]
Once I clicked [Yes] again, the screen changed to a loading screen. Staring at the darkened monitor, I focused all of my attention on the game.

How many attack patterns will this guy have? What are its attributes? It definitely has an instant kill move. Mm, I should forget trying to succeed on the first try and just gather as much information as possible, because I may have to completely overhaul my leveling method or class combination.
My brain, stimulated with excitement and anticipation, was filled only with thoughts of the final boss—which was why I noticed what was going on a moment too late.
[You have reached the abyss.]
[Tutorial complete.]
Tutorial complete? No, wait. Why is it suddenly written in Korean? Wasn’t Dungeon and Stone only available in English?
[The transmission will now begin.]
At the same moment, a bright light burst into existence. The light was so intense that it was hard to believe it was coming through a screen.
“Ugh— Fuck! My eyes!”

In an instant, everything turned white. There was a ringing in my ears, and a strange heat touched my skin. My mind quickly grew hazy, like someone had just injected anesthesia into my veins. I was normally confident in my ability to handle crises, but at that particular moment, I had no idea what was going on.
Flash—!
I lost consciousness as the light grew stronger. And when I opened my eyes again, I was a barbarian inside the game.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Tutorial (1)
paragraphs: I closed my eyes and asked myself: If this were the beginning of a very, very tough game, what should I be doing right now?
First, I needed to get a grasp of the situation and collect some information.

Phew. I could feel my thoughts slowly clearing up. With this first task I set for myself in mind, I slowly opened my eyes and scanned my surroundings again. Unfortunately, they were the same as before.

The fact that I was in a clearing in the woods, that the light illuminating my dark surroundings was not an LED streetlight but a flickering torch, and that there were muscular brutes everywhere I looked... Fuck, my eyes definitely weren’t deceiving me. I didn’t know what these people were doing here in the middle of the night, but they seemed pretty devoted to whatever it was.
“Congratulations! Young warriors!” shouted one of the savages in the middle of the tribe.
Is that man in the middle the chief of the tribe? I thought.
Well, that wasn’t important.
The chieftain continued. “As of today, you will leave this sacred land and be reborn as true warriors!”
I closed my eyes, filtering the chieftain’s words out. I wasn’t a doctor, but if I were to self-diagnose, I was probably experiencing symptoms of dissociation at the moment.
“Now, step forward one by one and choose the weapon that best suits you!”
So, let’s think through it again... What had I been doing just before this?

As I looked back on the events that had just taken place, a realization suddenly came to mind. I had been playing a game. The final boss’s lair had been in front of me, and I had activated the portal while bursting with excitement. Then, suddenly, a message saying that the tutorial had been completed and something about a transmission appeared, and a bright light flooded the screen. And then... When I came to, I was here. Somehow, I was even more confused now...
“Step forward, Karak, third son of Fanun!”
First, I needed to check the condition of my body. I wasn’t feeling any pain, but you never knew. With that thought in mind, I looked down and immediately froze.
...What’s this?
“A two-handed axe! Excellent!”

The hands that I saw were so large that they were almost obscene. And surprisingly, they moved according to my will. While I was at it, I scanned the other parts of my body and found that they were all truly a sight to behold. In addition to having no shirt on, tattoos of all shapes were drawn on my powerful muscles, and I was at eye level with these other giant people. I tried to make sense of all this information. No, actually, there was nothing to make sense of. For some reason, I had become a savage.
“Karak, third son of Fanun! You are now a warrior!”

Kidnapping, a hidden camera show, or perhaps a psychological experiment—I immediately erased these possibilities from my mind. It would be foolish in this situation to create false hope by trying to push theories that did not make sense. It would be more productive to accept reality and move on. What was happening to me right now was something that modern science or common knowledge could not explain. Even aside from this large body, there were plenty of other things that supported that assertion.
“Next!”

First of all, the language that the brutes were speaking was not Korean, English, or even Spanish. It was a language I had never encountered in any media in my entire life. However, I could somehow understand this language as naturally as my mother tongue. It was as if this knowledge had been inscribed on my brain.
“Come up, Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin!”

Second, I had been in this situation before. That might sound ridiculous, but it was true. At first, everything had felt unfamiliar, but now that I had come to my senses, I felt a strange sense of déjà vu.
“You chose a sword! A good choice for an intelligent warrior like you!”

The way these young barbarians were all choosing their weapons one after another... I had seen this before. This was reminiscent of the intro to Dungeon and Stone. To be precise, when ‘Barbarian’ was selected from among the various possible classes, the game always started out this way. But was this just a coincidence? The game I had been playing when the mysterious light swallowed me was Dungeon and Stone, and the character I had been playing was a barbarian.
“Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin! You have become a warrior. May the blessing of Rafdonia be with you!”
What the...

I didn’t bother running through the remaining theories. Rafdonia, the name the chieftain had just mentioned, made them all meaningless. I now knew where I was. I was inside the game I’d been playing for nearly ten years.
“D-Dungeon and Stone.”
“Eh? What is this? Why is he speaking for me?”
As I glanced at the barbarian next to me, I froze. Even at a glance, he was different from the other barbarians.
“What—what is this? Why am I here?”

His breathing was rough and his eyes were full of confusion. And he knew about Dungeon and Stone. Could it be that he was in the same situation as me? I felt the need to investigate, but unfortunately didn’t get a chance to even attempt it.
“Who just opened their mouth?!”

The voice was so loud that it pierced my eardrums, and my mind went blank for a moment. But that didn’t last long. I didn’t know when he had arrived, but the sight of the chieftain looking down at me woke me right up.
“Was it you?”

As soon as the question was asked, I shook my head. And naturally, I looked at the barbarian sitting next to me. It was a swift movement that surprised even me. The chieftain also moved his gaze to the barbarian instead of asking me any more questions.
I’m sorry, but you were the one who spoke.
“Was it you?” the chieftain asked the barbarian next to me.
“Pardon?”
“I asked if it was you who just mumbled.”
I was only just now noticing it, but the chieftain’s expression was strange. He couldn’t be reacting like this just because of the noise...
“Oh, you mean about Dungeon and Stone? What about it?”
This guy didn’t seem to understand the situation he was in here.
“So, it was you...”
A brief flash of pity passed through the chieftain’s eyes as he clenched his jaw. Feeling a sense of foreboding for some unknown reason, I unconsciously took a step to the side.
Then, the man next to me tilted his head and asked:
“Is this like an event? Oh, did I notice it too soon—”
I could not see what happened with my naked eye. Something flashed, followed by a horrifying sound.
Slice—
That was all there was to it. The fleeting moment passed and a head fell to the ground with a dull thud. The head continued to roll. It was a gruesome sight that seemed almost unreal.
A man’s neck had been cut off right in front of my eyes. The bones and the cross-sections of the muscles were visible. Something white splattered on my face, along with blood and flesh.
What is this? Is it fat?

Mm, I couldn’t be sure. It was not as shocking as I thought it would be, though. There was no feeling of nausea or mental collapse like there always was in the movies, and I didn’t lose my sanity either.
Squirt!
As I watched the blood spurt out of the man’s throat, only one question remained in my mind. Why the hell had the chieftain killed him?
“An evil spirit resided in the soul of Oreum, son of Kadua. Young warriors, erase from your memory the words the evil spirit has just uttered!”
The moment I heard the chief’s words, everything came together in my head.
Number one: I am an evil spirit.
Number two: If this is revealed, I will die.
Number three: That head on the ground could’ve been mine.
When I came to that conclusion, a chill ran down my spine, something that hadn’t even happened while I was watching someone’s head get cut off.
“Vulcan! Hurry and report this to the temple with the corpse!”
“What should we do about the coming-of-age ceremony?”
“I will proceed!”

A pool of blood had been shed, but the coming-of-age ceremony resumed. This must have been a common occurrence here, because, after looking around, I noticed no one had even batted an eye. This was also true of the young warriors. Maybe it was because I’d played so many hostile games, but even though no one told me what to do, I was certain of what my objective was now.
[Safely complete your coming-of-age ceremony without anyone finding out that you are an evil spirit.]

If this had been a friendly game, a message like that would have appeared. Committing this new task to memory, I forced my body to stop shaking. Using the behavior of the people around me as a guideline, I copied their facial expressions. No one would be able to detect anything out of the ordinary about me, because, to them, I would be nothing more than an “evil spirit” that had possessed someone’s body.
“Next!”
But then I realized something, and my heart sank.
“Kenick’s fourth son, Serum, step forward!”
I don’t know my name.
This was a serious matter with my life hanging in the balance. If I didn’t step forward even after my name was called, I would definitely look suspicious.
“Next!”

Well, I guess I could say that I misheard him. Obviously, that was much more likely than me being an evil spirit. But if you asked if I was confident about that, that was a different story altogether. What if it didn’t work? What if the chieftain became suspicious and questioned me? I wouldn’t be able to stand up under scrutiny.
“Next!”
The anxiety triggered the adrenaline in my brain. Naïve thoughts began to come to mind. Cowardly thoughts such as, If I’m the last one called forward, it won’t matter if I don’t know my name, right?
“Next!”

I felt pathetic. Depending on luck? When I’d never been lucky a day in my life? The fact that I had been summoned to this place while gaming just drove that home. For a guy like me to get through a crisis like this, I needed a more definitive plan. So, I kept looking around.
“Next!”
With my chin facing forward, I examined the facial expressions, movements, and habits of the others in my peripheral vision. As I was doing this, a strategy came to my mind.
“Next!”
Of course, this strategy was not 100 percent foolproof either. However, I had little time, and I had to make a final decision. This was the most probable way to survive.
“Next!”
“Next!”
“Next!”
The summons continued. I counted about two seconds between each call and the respective warrior stepping forward. And then, after I had repeated this about eight times...
“Step forward, Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
Finally, the long-awaited moment had arrived. Even after two seconds, no one had stepped forward. Noticing this, I stepped forward. Proudly and with my shoulders squared, I walked toward the chief.
Thud.
It wasn’t that I wasn’t afraid. Even as I walked forward, I was not sure that the name was mine.
Thud.
If I misjudged, the crazy chieftain was going to be suspicious and immediately stop me. He was going to ask, “Who is your mother?” and I was not going to be able to answer. However...
Thud.
I didn’t hesitate. Even as my heart pounded, I took measured breaths and continued to walk forward. The reason was simple. I had already decided that this was the most plausible time to step forward.
“Young warrior, choose your weapon!”

In the end, my hypothesis was proven correct. There was no suspicion in the chieftain’s eyes as he looked at me. It was the same warm gaze he wore while dealing with the other young warriors. I held my breath, fighting back a strange feeling of excitement.
I had lived.
Not even ten minutes had passed since I opened my eyes, but I had accepted the reality I was now facing for what it was. It may have seemed strange to some... but refusing to accept it was pointless.
This was not a dream.
Bjorn Yandel.

From now on, I had to live by this name. No, not just the name—I had to truly be this barbarian for an indefinite amount of time. With no idea how I might be able to go back home, or if that was even possible, it hit me that as of that moment, I didn’t know anything.

Well, I hypothesized that if the game’s win conditions were met, I would be able to return. But it was still too early to draw any conclusions. And honestly, I hoped that wasn’t the case. I hadn’t even cleared the 2D version—how was I supposed to clear this game in real life? I might have to live here forever...

Because of that, weapon selection was important. Dragging it out might attract suspicion, but I still carefully examined each weapon one by one. There was a one-handed sword, a two-handed great sword, a mace, an iron club, a spear, a harpoon, a two-handed axe, a flail, a large hammer, and a few others. There were no bows or wands. These savage bastards didn’t seem to care for bench-players like healers, wizards, or archers. Considering their massive builds, that was a given.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! Quickly choose your weapon!”

As my selection time dragged on, the chief of the tribe began urging me to hurry. I finally gathered my thoughts. Barbarians had no natural talent for magic, but had strong physical capabilities. For that reason, when playing barbarians, I always gave them melee weapons and placed them in the vanguard. Out of curiosity, I once tried to play as a barbarian archer, but it had been no good. Their true worth always shined in close combat.
And among those...
This.
After much deliberation, I chose a weapon.
“Hmm.”
The chieftain, who had praised the other young warriors after every selection, reacted strangely this time. His feelings were fully understandable.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! You are now a warrior!”
I had chosen a weapon that no one wanted.
At that same moment, inside a dark room with dim lights...
[Synchronization is complete.]
[Character information and journal have been logged and sent to the administrator.]
The fan on the main console, which had been turned off, started to spin, and the light from the monitor illuminated the empty room. However, the loading did not progress as expected.
Beep, beep, beep, beep—
The typing on the otherwise black DOS screen stopped. According to the beeping, there had been an error.
[The coming-of-age ceremony has been successfully completed.]
[New items have been equipped.]
[Total Item Level has increased by +12...]
Almost as if someone was writing it down in real time, those were the only sounds ringing out quietly in the unoccupied room. Endlessly, continuously.
[Bjorn Yandel]
[Level: 1
Physique: 25
Spirit: 35
Special Ability: 1
Item Level: 24 (New +24)
General Combat Power: 67 (New +6)]

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Tutorial (2)
paragraphs: Barbarian.

The first time I ever played a character of this class, the weapon I chose was the Greatsword. The reason? Because it was cool. I had pictured how cool it would be to wield a sword in both hands and spin it around like crazy in the middle of an enemy camp.
The problem is, they die too easily.

Fascinated by barbarians, I started doing my own research. How could I keep a barbarian alive? Despite many attempts, my barbarian characters still died much too easily. No matter how durable they were, they all turned into berserkers. It was like I was walking a narrow tightrope during every battle. This made barbarians an unstable character.
Then, at some point, I started to feel skeptical.
Do I really have to use him as a damage dealer?

Barbarians were the most durable of all the classes, and their max strength potential was also high, which meant they could wear adamantium. Although their special skill stats were not as good as a dwarf’s, barbarians had the basic skills of a tank. Though, to be honest, I didn’t really want to be a barbarian tank. But I also didn’t want all that time spent researching barbarians to go to waste, so I tried it out. And after a bit of trial and error, I created my own character build.
What is this broken character?

Without thinking twice, I abandoned the dwarf that I had originally used as a tank. So what if you couldn’t fight a flashy fight? I had always valued efficiency and was a gamer who could set aside personal taste in pursuit of strategy. Just like I was deciding to now.
Thud.
When I returned to my place after choosing a weapon, I could feel the other barbarians looking at me.
What, you’ve never seen a barbarian holding a shield before?
I returned to my spot with a dignified, unflinching expression on my face, just like a true barbarian. There was no need to put on an act this time.
“Next!”
I had no regrets about my decision for three reasons:
One, of the starting weapon options, the shield was the most expensive when resold.
Two, there was a strong possibility that even if I were holding a sword in my hand right now, I would not be able to wield it properly.
Three, I was ultimately pursuing a shield barbarian build.
I had made the most rational decision I could make today.
“With this, you have become a warrior!”

After choosing a weapon and going back to my spot, I was finally given some time to think. While the other barbarians went through their coming-of-age ceremonies, I decided to speculate on how I had gotten into this situation. I should really have thought about this earlier, but... well, what could I do?
I had been too busy saving my own life.
[You have reached the abyss.]
Let’s summarize the course of events. I had reached the final boss’s lair. That had more than likely been the trigger.
Wait a minute. Then who was the other guy who died earlier? Does that mean he was someone who also reached the final boss’s lair?
...Maybe he had. There were a lot of people in the world, and some of them were bound to be weird like me. Let’s skip that part for now.
[Tutorial complete.]

I interpreted that particular message to mean the following: I’ve taught you everything I need to teach you, so use this knowledge to survive. I didn’t know who it was who wrote that, but they had to be a vicious bastard. If they had really wanted me to survive, they should have included an explanation of the ‘evil spirit’ situation.
I had almost been killed on arrival for that. Asshole.

Maybe it was because I was inside the body of a barbarian, but I was having a hard time controlling my emotions like usual. For that reason, I abandoned that train of thought. Getting excited might lead to trouble, and it wasn’t like me to think about the reasons and get stressed out.
What had happened had already happened and there was no turning back. It was more productive to focus my energy on thinking about how to get through this situation.
So... Okay, let’s just think about that for now.
How do I survive this?

The coming-of-age ceremony had ended and I was currently walking through the woods. The chieftain was out in front and the young barbarians were behind him. Everyone seemed to be having fun, almost like they were going on a picnic. But I couldn’t laugh along with them... because I knew their final destination.
“Halt!”
The place we arrived at after passing through the thick forest was a castle wall that was easily a hundred feet tall.
“Open the door!”

The castle gate opened with the sound of crude gears grinding. The speed was slow enough to make you yawn. But the young barbarians watched the sight like they had forgotten how to breathe. It was in this strange silence that a gray city finally appeared beyond the gates.
“Rafdonia...”

At that moment, at least, the gleam in my eyes probably did not look much different from that of the others. Organized roads and stone buildings, along with a towering spire that could be seen piercing into the sky. I had never dreamed that I would see in real life this image that I had only ever seen in the illustration on the loading screen.
God damn it.
“Warriors!”
As the door opened, the chief of the tribe turned around and shouted at us. I had hoped he would provide some words of wisdom before sending us off, but...
“Leave! Your destiny is out there!”
There was no need for boring speeches when it came to barbarians.
“Ahh!”

The barbarians who had just entered adulthood ran into the city shouting. I didn’t want to, but I shouted and followed after them. There were probably people sleeping soundly inside those dimly lit buildings, but what did that matter?
I was a barbarian.
Boom!

The sound of the gate closing could be heard behind us. Of course, none of the barbarians cared. The overly excited group ran for a long time before finally calming and slowing down. Only then was I able to pick up my train of thought.
Currently, I was feeling conflicting emotions.

I felt fear of the situation I had found myself in, but also a kind of anticipation at becoming a part of the world of my favorite game. It was a little ridiculous. It was just a little while ago that I decided to focus solely on surviving, yet these emotions still bloomed. I definitely couldn’t be normal. Although I was nothing compared to these savage bastards.
“Halt!” The leader-type barbarian running at the forefront of the group stopped, turned around, and proudly shouted, “I think I have lost my way!”
The barbarians murmured amongst themselves at the shocking confession.
“Fanun’s third son, Karak, has led us astray!”
“He is not qualified to be a leader!”
“You have to take responsibility!”
Bullshit. You guys all followed him willingly. Was this what barbarian society looked like? Cold-hearted.
“I understand. Stop. I will admit that I am not worthy and will step down as the leader.”
Karak, Fanun’s second or third son, bowed his head deeply and returned to the group. A female barbarian was appointed as the next leader.
“Ainar, the second daughter of Fenelin!”
“Wise Ainar will lead us down the right path!”
The female barbarian took the lead and smiled at the encouraging words. However, it didn’t take long for her to follow in the footsteps of the previous leader.
“...I think I have lost my way.”
Their words were shockingly identical.
“Unbelievable! We must get to the labyrinth within the set time!”
“Ainar is not qualified to be a leader!”
“That’s right!”
Distressed, the barbarians began to urgently discuss who they should nominate as the third leader.
“I think the second son of Tetran would be a good choice.”
“No. I don’t think so. Instead...”
Were these kids brainless? Did they really not realize that no matter who took the lead, they wouldn’t reach their destination like this?
At this rate, it might even end up being my turn.
I quietly fell back from the group and approached the second leader. Standing at around six feet tall, she stood slightly away from the group with a disheartened look on her face.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel? Did you come to blame me too?”
No way. To me, they were all the same. As I shook my head, the female barbarian cocked hers.
“Then why? I don’t need comforting.”
“No. I have come to show you how to find the way.”
“...Is that true? How?”
I lifted my hand and pointed in a direction.
“You just have to follow them.”
“Just follow them?”

She looked like she didn’t believe me. Exercising my patience, I explained it logically, step by step. This was a city in the middle of the night. All the lights on the streets were turned off. However, despite it being late at night, there were quite a few people on the streets. The people were all dressed in armor rather than everyday clothes. Where could they be heading?
“Certainly... That makes sense. I will give it a try.”
The female barbarian returned to the group and shouted, “I have found a way!”, and the barbarians stopped the voting process for the third leader and cheered.
“Yes, Ainar!”
“Wise warrior!”

Anyway, the group started moving again. It seemed we were going the right way, as more and more armed people appeared in the area as time went on. At some point, I started to see a bunch of lights in the distance, shining in all directions. If we’d come this far, at least we wouldn’t lose our way.
“It’s the labyrinth! I see the labyrinth!”
“The Dimension of Divine Battle!”
One of my biggest concerns right now was whether entering the labyrinth was the right decision.
“I feel it! The labyrinth is calling my soul!”

The barbarians, who were in the crux of excitement, wouldn’t notice if I snuck out of the pack. That way, I wouldn’t have to enter the labyrinth or fight monsters to the death. However, even though I knew that better than anyone, I knew doing that would not resolve my dilemma.
Because I know running away isn’t the solution.

Dungeon and Stone had a tax system. From the age of twenty onward, all city dwellers were required to pay taxes, and failure to pay taxes was punishable by death. Hearing that would probably make you think this was a stupid game, but when you learned about the universe of the game, you realized that system was quite justified.
I don’t think it’s something to worry about right now, but...
“Ainar! Let’s speed up!”
“Ohh!!”

Anyway, I had to make money. Of course, my method of doing so didn’t necessarily have to be entering the labyrinth and fighting monsters. If I found work at a tavern, I wouldn’t have any issues finding a place to eat and sleep... unless, of course, I was a barbarian.
Barbarians were the only characters who were given a weapon from the very beginning of the game. This was for a very simple reason...
[“Barbarian? I’m sorry. I already found someone.”]
[“Go away! There’s nothing for a barbarian here! What are you going to break this time?”]

Barbarians could not have ordinary jobs. Due to the way the game was set up, there was no way for barbarians to earn a living other than fighting monsters in labyrinths. Well, I wasn’t sure how things would play out in real life, though. I could possibly find a job more easily than I thought I could. But breaking away from the group on just that hunch was not sitting right with me.
“Ten minutes left until closing. Hurry inside!”

The labyrinth in the game only opened once a month. In other words, if I didn’t enter this time, I would have to survive in this city for a month. But what if I couldn’t find a job at that time? What if no one was willing to hire a barbarian?

The future was bleak. Even if I survived a week on the food provided by the chief of the tribe, I would have to survive the remainder of the time on food scraps and trash. I might even starve to death before then.
One thing was certain. Even if I survived that, it would change my body completely from its current state.
“I will be the first to go in!”
“No! I’m first!”

Hunger, the cold, and sleeping in unsanitary conditions... I knew better than anyone how devastating these things were to the human body. So, if I was going to have to go in anyway, the most logical thing to do was enter now while I was in top condition.
The problem is that it might just be cutting my life even shorter.
I was deep in thought when someone grabbed my shoulder.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
When I looked, it was that female barbarian. Her name was...
“Ainar, third daughter of Fenelin.”
“Second daughter.”
Anyway, what did she want from me?
“All the other warriors have already entered the labyrinth. The only ones who haven’t entered yet are you and I.”
“Ah.”

No wonder it was suddenly quiet. Looking around, there were not many people left in the square, let alone other barbarians. Ainar, as the second leader of the group, seemed to have come to check in with me because I was standing there unmoving.
“We need to hurry. Since we arrived late, there is not much time.”

At that, I raised my head and looked straight ahead. The portal, which previously emitted an intense light even from a distance, had noticeably decreased in size. Just then, the guide informed us of the remaining time once more.
“Five minutes until closing!”
Five minutes... it was tighter than I had thought. I was going to have to make a decision soon.
“Head inside first. I will follow behind you.”
“Okay.”
Ainar nodded and headed toward the portal, which just compounded my troubles.
So, what should I do now?
As someone who thoroughly favored efficiency, I preferred to do things quickly, but it was not easy to make a decision in this particular instance. Unlike a game, my actual life depended on this.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
I was about to take an involuntary step backward, when Ainar, who had been walking forward, suddenly turned around.
“Thank you for earlier.”
“...There’s nothing to thank me for.”
“And there is one thing I want to ask you.”

Anything other than my mother’s name, sure. I nodded, and Ainar asked in a completely sincere voice, “How can I be wise like you? I’ve never seen a barbarian as smart as you in my life. I want to be like you.”

How to be smart? That was a really difficult question to answer. To be honest, I wondered if the quickest method for them would be to be reborn... No, wait, why was I even thinking about this? Just throw her a vague answer and send her on her way.
“You have to always think before you act.”
“Hmm, I see!”
I had said it without much thought, but Ainar took in my words with a serious expression on her face. And then she said something a little unexpected.
“Thank you for your advice. If I return from the labyrinth, I will repay you.”
What do you mean ‘if?’ I wondered.
That sounded far too strange coming out of a barbarian’s mouth. So, despite my usual efficient personality, I asked her an unnecessary question.
“...Are you afraid of dying?”
“Isn’t it obvious? Of course I’m afraid to die. The other warriors probably are as well, even if they don’t show it.”

Is that right? To be honest, her words didn’t really make sense to me. The barbarians in the game couldn’t feel fear, and they didn’t seem much different in reality either. When I fell silent, Ainar added, “We were born warriors. If we don’t fight, we die.”
Her tone was clumsy and rigid, but somehow I could completely understand what she was trying to say.
“I see.”
Because they were born barbarians, they didn’t have a choice. Just like me.

If they didn’t kill the monsters in the labyrinth, they wouldn’t be able to survive in this city, which was why they learned how to overcome their fears from an early age. Yes, that was all. That was why they took the form of savages.
“I hope to see you alive, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
Ainar soon entered the portal.
“One minute left until closing!” said the guide.
Now there was nothing holding me back. Just my decision. Just like the line that had appeared onscreen when I was about to enter the final boss’s lair, I had two options.
[Yes/No]
My jumbled-up thoughts cleared up.
Yeah, I’d rather think of it as playing a game.

Whenever I played games, I always played with an emphasis on efficiency for the sake of a goal. Before moving, I always weighed the odds first and always moved forward with the next step in mind. If I judged that my actions would eventually result in a loss, even if there was an immediate benefit, I would choose [No]. Otherwise, I would choose [Yes]. So, there was never really a question of what I would do.
“The gate will be closed soon! Stand back!”

I ran forward. Deep down, fear was boiling over inside of me just like when the chieftain had called my name. Needless to say, after being sickly for my entire life, I did not have even the slightest bit of fighting experience. And to face off against monsters? My knees were already shaking.
“Wait, it’s dangerous!”

However, now I had a chance. Right now, I had the body of a ridiculously strong barbarian, and the knowledge gained from leveling thousands of characters. Above all else, I had the ultimate goal of surviving this. So, I had no choice.
Even though I knew better than anyone that this was a decision that could lead to terrible consequences and one that no sane person would choose, I had made up my mind—
[You have entered the first floor of the crystal cave.]
—that this was the most logical thing to do.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Tutorial (3)
paragraphs: As far as Dungeon and Stone was concerned, I was an expert. What kinds of monsters were going to appear and from where, their behaviors, and what their weaknesses were—I could recite all of that information without trouble. Based on this, I made my final decision. With the body of a barbarian combined with my knowledge of the game, I could survive in this labyrinth just fine. Or at least I thought I could.

As soon as I entered the labyrinth, my vision went dark. Not as an omen for the future, but literally—I couldn’t see anything. I probably wouldn’t even notice if someone put a blindfold over my eyes right now. There really wouldn’t be much of a difference.
“Fuck.”

I felt like I’d been slapped hard over the back of the head. The other barbarians had each only been carrying their one weapon, so I hadn’t been concerned either. There should be no need for a torch on the first floor because the crystals on the wall acted as a light source. Of course, the first floor also had a dark zone. But except for the outermost part of the labyrinth that led to the second floor, the dark zone was strictly confined to one section—
Oh, did I fall into that section?

I quickly thought this through. When entering a labyrinth, the place you spawned was random. I mean, it was supposed to be random, but you were usually never thrown into an area like this. Even if you started at the outskirts, there was always a glowing crystal nearby. However, this was not the world of a game being experienced through a screen. What if all of those things were a kind of courtesy the creators of the game provided to the player?

What if, in reality, a shitty starting position like the dark zone was the norm? If so, that could explain my current situation. Yes, that had to be the case. If the entire first floor was like this, I didn’t have confidence that I’d survive a single day.

I was able to calm down after getting my thoughts in order. Fortunately, my eyes had now adapted to the darkness, so my vision was much better than before. However, I could still only make out outlines. At least the situation was not so dire that I needed to bite my tongue and take myself out. I decided to go ahead and run through all the necessary tests. After all, I was finally alone.
“Status window, equipment window, character information, stats, inventory. Journal check, and fuck my life.”
Of course, none of it worked. Well, I didn’t expect it to, anyway.
“Let’s go.”

With the shield in one hand and gripping the wall with the other, I moved forward. My speed was slightly faster than a crawl. Well, maybe not? Perhaps crawling would be faster, but I couldn’t go any faster than this. It was dangerous—
“Aaaaaah!”

Suddenly, a sharp pain erupted in my ankle. It was a pain unlike anything I’d ever felt before in my life, and my nerve endings went crazy. But even in a situation like this, I tried to figure out what had just happened. What had gone wrong? Even without a battle log, the answer came to me quickly.
[You have stepped on a goblin trap.]
Fuck, I just walked into a trap.
Where did I slip up? The answer was simple.

The shield provided me with a sense of stability, but it also obscured much of my line of sight. If I had put my shield on my belt and focused on watching my step, I might have seen the trap in my path. What’s the use of a shield if you can’t see, anyway? I should have focused on practicality rather than peace of mind.
God damn it.

My mind went blank. I wanted to scream, but I desperately suppressed it. I couldn’t be sure whether screaming would make me feel better, but I did know for sure that it would make the situation worse.
Thump-thump-thump.
My heart was pounding like crazy.
“Hoo, hoo, hoo....”
I pressed my lips together and forced myself to control my breathing. I couldn’t think about the pain I was feeling.
There was only one type of monster on the first floor that used traps. Goblins. And they had to be nearby.

I reflexively raised my shield up to cover my head. Then, I stopped breathing and focused all my attention on what I could hear. I couldn’t hear anything. It was so quiet, it was as if time itself had stopped.
Maybe they’re not here...?
I didn’t know. That might be the case. I might have gotten lucky and they left their stations right at this exact moment. Even goblins needed to poop.
As if. You don’t actually think that.
I stomped down the hope creeping up inside of me and threw it right out of my head. There were two reasons for that.
One, there was a difference between being positive and being unrealistic.
Two, what I needed right now was a pessimistic mindset.
If you cannot be sure, assume the worst.

The goblin heard my scream. It was hiding somewhere in the dark, waiting quietly for me to lose all my strength. That was why I hadn’t heard any sounds. It was just like this in the game too. If there was a trap, there was always a goblin in its vicinity.
I slowly resumed breathing. Since my surroundings were quiet, as long as I stayed on guard, I would be able to detect any movements.
First, I had to take care of pressing matters.

Lowering my stance, I opened the trap with both hands and pulled my foot out. Then, after tearing off the hem of my trousers, I took off my shoe and applied pressure to the wound. I decided to get rid of the bloody shoe. In fact, it couldn’t even be called a shoe. They were sandals that were closer to flip-flops. Damn barbarian idiots. If only they’d sent us out with leather boots, I wouldn’t have been practically incapacitated by a single trap...
Fuck, what am I thinking about right now?

I caught myself being illogical and my mind froze. Let’s not be even more pathetic. No matter how much I cursed out the barbarians, the situation would not change. In the end, this was my fault for not properly watching my step.
So stop whining and check your injury... Damn, this is really bad.
I couldn’t feel anything in my right foot anymore. I could only feel heat, but even that sensation was starting to grow duller.
“I know you’re hiding, so come out,” I muttered quietly.
Still, beyond the darkness, there was no sign of movement. So, I slowly moved forward. My steps echoed softly off the labyrinth’s walls.
Step. Step.
My leg was crushed, but the pain was not as severe as I had expected. It was probably because of a paralyzing poison on the trap... I didn’t know if that was a good thing.
“Come out, you asshole.”

I didn’t hesitate to provoke the goblins this time as I continued to move forward. Time was not on my side. If I was going to have to fight, the sooner I got to it, the better. There was my injury to think about, but also, the possibility that this bastard was waiting for his comrades could not be ignored.
“Aren’t you coming?”

Of course, there was a possibility I was being delusional and there was no such thing as goblins here. That would make me the blockhead who had stepped on a trap and was now acting like a lunatic. But what was wrong with that? If I was a lunatic, I would like to be a lunatic who survived.
“Then just stay there. I’m leaving.”
I sped up. It was still only a little faster than a crawl, but it felt like sprinting a marathon.
Left foot. Right foot. Left foot...

As I was walking, my right foot started to throb. I panted loudly. It was either one of two things. Either the effect of the paralyzing poison had expired, or the pain had become severe enough that the poison was not enough to numb it. Come to think of it, neither of those two things were bad. If the poison’s effects were over, that was good, and the fact that I could feel pain meant that my nerve endings were still intact.
Why can I only think positively when it comes to stuff like this?
Well, I didn’t want to think about that right now. I didn’t even have the capacity to think about that right now.
“...Your mom’s a goblin.”
Words came out of my mouth without a filter. Maybe I had lost too much blood. I felt like my brain was soaked in alcohol.
“Your dad’s also a goblin.”
Of course, as I was spitting these insults out, my feet did not stop moving.
“So you’re a goblin.”
At that moment, the creature made a sound for the first time. It was a small noise, but it was very loud to my ears, which were listening to it.
Splat—
Finally, the bastard was showing himself.
“What? Can’t stand your parents being cursed at?”

Of course, I knew that was not the case. It hadn’t even been an insult in the first place... The sound came from behind me. It was far more likely that the goblin had been forced to move as I got farther and farther away from it. I accelerated even more. The sound of the monster’s footsteps also accelerated.
Splat... Splat... Splat...

The sound of its footsteps, which were getting clearer, was unusual. Every time it walked, it sounded like something sticky had stuck to a smooth surface and then fallen off. Even though I knew goblins were no taller than three feet tall, it felt as if a huge monster was chasing after me. To shake off my fear, I kept talking to it.
I was a barbarian. If I engaged in close combat, I would never lose to a goblin.
“Don’t just follow me, come at me. You fucker.”
For that reason, I continued to provoke the goblin, but it just kept following behind me at the same distance. It didn’t even seem to want to hide itself anymore.
“Grk, Grk...!”
The noise it made sounded almost like howling, but I could somehow tell.
“Grgh! Grk!”
The bastard was giggling. It was genuinely delighted to see its prey bleeding and dying. It probably hoped I would hear it and be terrified.
...Smart bastard. Okay. Change of plans.
I stopped in my tracks. Then, I stumbled and fell to the floor.
Thump!

My forehead hit a rock and felt like it was going to split open, but I didn’t make a sound. From now on, this was a battle of patience. If it thought I passed out and approached first, I would win. If I actually passed out before that, I’d lose.
“Grk?”
I decided to put my faith in the toughness of this body that had walked about three hundred yards with a busted foot.
Splat—
The sound of its footsteps was getting closer and closer. Its progress was so slow it was yawn-inducing. Despite the fact that its prey had collapsed just like it had wanted, it was still suspicious.
Damn, why is this goblin so careful?

At that moment, the curses came easily. Goblins were the weakest trash mobs in the game. They used poisons and installed traps, but aside from that, their combat power was low. But the goblin I had just encountered?
Splat—

It was definitely not something to underestimate. I realized now why the village’s NPCs always talked about the goblins’ cleverness. From what I could tell, these goblins were several times more intelligent than those barbarian clowns.
Splat—
It stopped somewhere between five to ten yards behind me. Why? Just as I was questioning this, a dull shock jolted through my shoulder.
Tap. Roll...
What? Did this fucker throw a stone at me? ...It’s not going to keep throwing, is it?
“Grk...! Grk!”
Despite my fears, the monster spat out a howl of joy. As I hadn’t given any reaction to the stoning, it seemed truly convinced I was dead.
Splat, splat, splat, splat—
The goblin came over to me quickly. I could feel how excited it was as it skipped over. I steeled my nerves and used the sound to estimate its distance. And when I figured it was close enough—
“You fucker!”

I jumped up and shot a fist toward him. I figured punching was quicker than picking up the shield and slamming the monster down with it. However, I soon had a gut feeling that my plan had gone awry. Again, there were two reasons for this.
First of all, the distance between us was about a step too far.
And second, the bastard was much more agile than I had expected.
“Grk!”
The goblin bent its back and stepped backward. I couldn’t see it, but it felt like that was what it had done. I instinctively realized that I had missed it.
Damn it, what now?
I turned the gears in my head and prepared my next plan of action. But at that moment, my body moved on its own.
It was truly a strange feeling. My surroundings were still dark, but I intuitively knew where the goblin had jumped. Once I realized that, my hand was already flying toward the goblin.
“Grk?!”
I felt something with my fingertips. It didn’t matter if it was a wrist or an ankle or a neck.
“Ahh!”
I screamed and slammed the goblin to the floor. Crack! There was the sound of something breaking. But I couldn’t relax yet, so I immediately climbed on top of the goblin’s body.
“G-Grk!”
The tables had turned.
“I’m above you, and you’re below me. You fucker!”

I punched the goblin in the face like a madman. There were times when I punched the floor during the frenzy, but this barbarian’s body was much stronger than I had assumed. Instead of hurting my fist, the stone floor cracked under it.
Soon, the goblin’s movements ceased. And...
Whish—!
Dust scattered. It was an unusually shiny dust. I stopped my fists. At some point, the body below me had disintegrated into little pieces.
I mean, come on.
“Ha! Fuck, even this is the same?”
Please, one or the other. Is this a game, or is this just a world that’s similar to the game? How am I supposed to know which one it is?
[You have defeated the goblin. EXP +1]
Soon after, the goblin’s body disappeared without a trace. Feeling dejected for some unknown reason, I picked up a small stone that had been left in the spot it had once occupied.
[You have acquired a tier nine Mana Stone.]
It wasn’t strong, but it shone faintly. This was a type of magic stone that acted as currency in Dungeon and Stone. How much was this worth? A memory soon came to mind.
“A slice of bread.”
That had been the average value of the mana stones spat out by goblins in the game. I scoffed.
“Hahaha... This is all I get after all that?”
My jumbled-up mind became a little clearer. It felt like that moment of laughter that always came after a good cry.
“Heh heh...”

I was inside a labyrinth, and there were monsters. Dead monsters disappeared, leaving an item drop. And in the city outside, otherworldly races existed and lived side by side. That was genuinely how this world operated. But...
There was no way I was going to treat this new reality like it was just a game. I wasn’t going to let it trip me up anymore.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Give and Take (1)
paragraphs: Looking back, I had always been a weird person. Even though I’d always thought life was boring, I’d never once considered killing myself. Boredom was, after all, just an emotion. And to me, life was more precious than anything else. In many ways, death wasn’t worthwhile to me. That thought still stuck with me.
That was why...

I was crawling through the dark on three limbs. You may be wondering what that meant, but it was exactly what it sounded like. I was crawling on the floor on my arms and left leg, dragging my completely shredded right foot behind me. If anyone saw me in that moment, I was sure they’d be reminded of a stray dog with a broken leg. How did I know that? Because that was what I was thinking then.

The reward for giving up human dignity was sweet. First of all, I was no longer in pain because I didn’t have to use my injured foot anymore, and I was also moving faster than before. Most importantly, I didn’t have to worry about stepping on a trap. The flip side was that my elbows and knees were sore, but this... it was bearable. I could endure it. What wouldn’t you do to survive? I would even eat dog poo with a smile. Or, well... If I had enough time to prepare myself to do it, it was a definite possibility.
But what happened to that guy? The other player at the ceremony?

“Guy” was just what I was calling them. I didn’t know their gender, age, or even name. I was just guessing based on the way they spoke. I had a feeling he had to be a white man in his 30s with glasses. Or not.
[You are still bleeding.]
Anyway, what happened to that person who woke up in the body of Kadua’s son, Oreum? Did he die? Or did he wake back up in his original body?
That was a question that I had had ever since I opened my eyes in this place. Even if I intentionally tried not to think about it, the worse things started to get, the more I thought of that guy.
[You are still bleeding.]

I could now understand why people turned to religion. Life was much too difficult to deal with alone. When disaster struck, you needed a place to turn to. Especially in situations like the one I was in right now.
[You are still bleeding.]
[You are still bleeding.]
[WARNING! Your health has gone below 5%. You may die if your injury is not treated soon.]
Man, I had managed to come pretty far while I was busy thinking. It was a subtle difference, but I could tell that my surroundings were getting brighter. This was a positive thing in many ways.

At least I’d headed in the right direction, and my hypothesis that the entire first floor couldn’t all be completely dark was correct. I had to get somewhere bright, because there would be people there. I could give them this mana stone in exchange for help. Then somehow...
Don’t kid yourself.
I was whispering positive words to myself when my other side reared its head.
Hey idiot, they’re already going to be busy. You think they’ll help you for one loaf of bread? They’ll probably steal your mana stone and shield, and then kill you.
Maybe it was because the voice was me, but the bastard was smart.
And what are you going to do if you run into a goblin before a human? Are you brain-dead? Huh?
I refused to tolerate any further insults.
Well, then what the hell am I supposed to do? I still have to keep going. At least I’ll be able to kind of see over there. Wouldn’t that be better than fighting a goblin over here?
...That’s true.
My other self agreed, and my head was quiet again. I kept crawling.
“Heh heh...”

I was going crazy. No, I might have already gone crazy. After all, I had lost a lot of blood, hadn’t I? Just a second ago, my personality split in two, then merged again, and then shut down completely before reverting back. It was a kind of virtuous cycle. If my mind shut down one more time, I wasn’t sure I would be able to open my eyes again after.
“Heh heh heh...”

I laughed out loud. I didn’t have the energy to, but I still laughed. At some point, my surroundings became lighter. In the distance, at the end of the passage, I could see a crystal shining brightly. More importantly, I could see the form of a backlit man standing in front of it. It wasn’t a goblin. That was definitely a person.

I wanted to shout, but I couldn’t produce a sound. I crawled forward desperately, my eyes closing and opening. Then... oh? The human form looked closer now, almost as if it had teleported. Surprised by that, I closed my eyes and opened them again.
[You are still bleeding.]
This time it was even closer. About five or six people were now standing in front of me. Was this real? I closed my eyes again and reopened them.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: HP drops below 2% at any point.]
[Reward: your Spirit stat is permanently increased by +1.]

Then, I saw a blond man bend down on his knees. He was right in front of me, but only studied me and my surroundings without asking me any questions. Rather than listening to someone else’s opinions, he was making his judgments based on his own experiences and intuition. And like a veteran, he quickly came to a conclusion.
“You’re a newbie.”

Fuck, so help me, you bastard. As you can see, I’m an amateur barbarian with only a shield, and all I have to offer in exchange for a leg is a goblin mana stone. I’ll give you all of this if you want it. So...
“This is strange. How did a newbie get here faster than us?”
I quickly opened my mouth. But what came out was a sound similar to a gurgle.

To be honest, it sounded more like that goblin than human speech, but... it was enough to let him know that I was not in any condition to answer. After a moment, the blonde asked his comrade, “Priestess Ersina, could you heal this man?”
Priestess? Are you saying that there is a healer in their party?

I looked at the person next to him with wide eyes, like I was witnessing a miracle. There was indeed a priestess in white robes right there. The priestess, who now made eye contact with me, used her beautiful lips to bluntly reply:
“I refuse.”
Huh? What did you say?
“I see. Understood.”
Why are you just accepting that?
I wanted to cry.
Fuck, I didn’t know why I had been brought into this world if I was just going to be treated like this.
Then, right when my temper started to flare to life in my chest...
“Patzran, will you hand me a potion?”
“I was keeping it handy for when I can’t use divine magic.”
“You have a lot anyway. I will pay for it when we get out.”
“Tsk.”
Just then, a man with a sword on his waist clicked his tongue and tossed a potion from his bag forward. My heart sank as I realized my life depended on that.
Fortunately, the blond deftly caught the potion.
“It’s not divine magic, so this will hurt a little.”

The blond opened the stopper and poured half of it on the wounded area before pouring the other half directly into my mouth. Before long, I felt an unbearable pain. It felt like all of the pain that I had accumulated was now rearing its head all at once.
[Your health is rapidly regenerating due to the Recovery (Medium) effect.]

It felt like my whole body was melting. This must have been why potions could not be used during battle in the game. I thought it was just blocked by the system for some random reason, but it turned out that the game had just been reflecting reality extremely accurately. I panted.
God damn it. How many minutes have passed?
The pain gradually subsided and I came to my senses.
“Now, tell me, barbarian. How did a newbie like you get here before us? If you know of a new passage, I want to buy that information off of you.”

So that had been his angle this whole time? Not that I minded. Rather, I felt reassured by the thought that he had helped me for a reason. There was nothing more sinister than good intentions without a clear motive. Still, it was unfortunate. I didn’t know about any secret passages.
“...I was transported here as soon as I entered the labyrinth,” I told him honestly.
The blond tilted his head and then nodded in understanding.
“I’ve definitely read about that in a book once. Occasionally, dimensional instability can cause that to happen. But this is the first time I’ve seen it in person.”
My heart was pounding heavily. I asked for clarification as I had misheard him.
“The first time... you’ve seen it?”
I couldn’t believe it. I mean, this party had a priestess and a mage. That meant that they were legit adventurers who were active and at least mid-level. But, the first time?
“Yeah, the book described it as a once-in-a-century phenomenon. Spawning so far in the outermost section of the labyrinth, that is.”

Oh, I see. It was something that happened once in a hundred years or so. And this had happened to me during my first time in a labyrinth. Now I could see why the other barbarians hadn’t bothered carrying torches. Nobody worried about getting struck by lightning just because it was raining.

“It seems like it’s your first time here. It must have been hell to go through something so rare.” The blond gave me a pitying look. “That wasn’t the information I wanted, but it was interesting information, nonetheless. Don’t worry about the cost of the potion and be on your way.”
Although his tone was a bit douchey, he seemed to be a good guy.
“Oh, and don’t forget your shield back there.”
I looked where the blond was pointing and saw a shield on the floor. The distance was about twenty yards. I thought I had tied it securely to my waist, but it seemed to have fallen off.
“We’ll be on our way, then.”

They passed me by before I could even say thank you. In the labyrinth, time was money, so I could understand. The fact that they had wasted so much time on me in the first place was a miracle. I stared at the place where they had been standing for a moment, then quickly ran and picked up the shield that had fallen to the floor. It was definitely nice to have survived...
But something felt strange.
[Bjorn Yandel]
[Level: 1
Physique: 25
Spirit: 36 (New +1)
Special Ability: 1
Item Level: 24
General Combat Power: 68 (New +1)]
“That barbarian, he’s very lucky.”
“Well, I wouldn’t call that luck. To go through something like that on his first adventure...” the blond answered with a placid smile.
The male swordmaster snorted. “An idiot who steps on a goblin trap would have met with some other horrible fate somewhere else. He was lucky that he ran into us.”
“Lucky he ran into Drous, to be exact. Not us. You didn’t even want to use your potion, did you?”
When the female archer, who had been listening quietly, interrupted, the swordmaster shrugged.
“Because there are tons of guys like that out here. They won’t live long anyway. Surely our priestess must have had the same thought?”
The priestess smiled bitterly but did not answer, and instead, the female archer fired back.
“Priestess Ersina would have treated him if it weren’t for the laws of the temple. No, if not for the potion, she might have broken the laws herself. Do you think that everyone is like you?”
“Well, who knows? I’ve seen a lot of two-faced people in my life.”
“...Patzran, you need to have better manners like Drous.”
“Like how he was considerate enough to ask the barbarian if he knew about a secret passage?”
“Yes. I’ve heard that barbarians don’t accept help from others. That’s probably why he was being so considerate.”
“Hey, I think you’re flattering me too much.”
As he became the topic of conversation, the blond smiled awkwardly and scratched his head. But he also did not deny being considerate.
“Ah, if you want to take the shortcut, you have to turn here.”
“It’s quite nice to have a wayfinder in the party,” said the priestess.
“Priestess Ersina! Wayfinders usually only know the direction a portal is in. Drous isn’t like the others at all. He memorized all the landmarks on the first floor,” said the archer.
The male swordmaster glanced at the female archer and shook his head.
“How far does that bloodstain go? Haven’t we already walked quite a bit?” he asked.
“I am not sure. But judging by the resilience that man must have had to crawl such a long distance, I think you’re wrong to say he was just lucky.”
“Hmph, like this is a big deal... I’m sure it ends somewhere around here.”
The party followed the bloodstains and then turned onto a shortcut midway. And then, after about fifteen minutes, they reached their destination.
“It seems that we are the first to use this route. Good thing we rushed here. Let’s get to work.”
When the blond placed his hand on the tombstone that could be found in the dead end, an intense beam of light burst out and took the shape of a sphere. It was a portal leading to the second floor.
“Wait.”
Just as everyone was about to throw themselves into the portal, the female archer stopped the party.
“Isn’t that what the barbarian was wearing on his foot earlier?”
“What?”

The party looked in the direction the female archer was pointing and fell silent for a moment. In the darkness, made visible by the light emitted by the portal, a bloodstained trap and an unfamiliar sandal had been tossed to the side.
“...It seems like it.”
The mage, curious, created a new sphere of light and moved it through the passage.
Whooom—!

The bloodstains that began at the trap continued along the curved passageway. No matter how far they moved the sphere of light, they couldn’t see the end of the passageway. There was a moment of silence.
“...Hey, Drous, how long does it take to get from here to where we were earlier?” asked the mage.
“...Assuming no shortcuts are used, about nine miles.”
“Hahaha, that beast! To crawl that distance alone in this darkness.”
The mage chortled in surprise. The male swordmaster next to him, however, could not.
“He’s out of his mind...”
He felt that this was a matter of willpower, not the body. He tried to think.
How many hours would I have been able to crawl if I were in that situation? When I couldn’t even be sure I’d ever come across another human?

He had no way of knowing. But he was certain that the barbarian had still been crawling even when they had first discovered him. Even when he had been practically unconscious, he had continued to move his arms and legs. What had happened after that? Unable to speak properly, he had held out a small mana stone in his hand. At the time, he hadn’t thought much of it, but he was beginning to understand what that gesture meant now.
He was probably asking for help in exchange for the stone.

Other than that, the barbarian had had nothing to offer in return. So, the entire time he had been crawling this long distance, he had clutched that mana stone tightly in his hand just in case he came across someone. That way, he could show it to them right away.
He soon came to a decision.
“...Forget what I said earlier.”
Just lucky?
Not possible. He knew that from experience.
“Drous, what was that barbarian’s name?”
A lunatic like that wasn’t the type to die easily. No matter how hard and how hopeless the situation was. Death was never their way out.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Give and Take (2)
paragraphs: Dungeon and Stone was an unusual game.
Although companion NPCs were essential to the progress of the game, you could never trust them.
Especially if it was a bastard you’d just met.
I was walking through the cave.
Wobble, wobble.
Missing a shoe, my gait was off-balance.
Nevertheless, I was happy. The discomfort I felt now was something I hadn’t been able to feel when I had been crawling on three legs.
I had recovered my human dignity.
Although, I didn’t know how long it would last.
“Phew...”

I proceeded, securing my shield to my upper body. I no longer had to keep my eyes glued to the ground like before because there was finally light. The light emitted by the crystals embedded in the walls and ceiling brightened my surroundings.

The memories of crawling and bleeding through these halls felt like a distant dream now. I could affirm that being able to see was a blessing from god. It would allow me to slaughter those goblin bastards, there was no doubt about that.
“Ahh!”
“Grk?!”
Surprised by my cry, a goblin jumped out from behind a rock. Having already roughly predicted its hiding spot, I activated a skill on cue.
“Smash! Asshole!”
[Smash] was a skill with decent attack power that didn’t consume MP. For reference, I just made it up.
Wham!
The goblin leapt and was hit by my shield, falling to the floor. I approached nimbly and stomped on the goblin’s upper body with my foot.
“G-Grk!”
No use making pitiful eyes at me. I knew how cunning and evil these fuckers were.
“G-Grk!”
What, you’re different?
Then go talk to your friend who died earlier, because that bastard was the one who made me like this.
Crunch!

I slammed the goblin’s face as hard as I could with the edge of the shield. It was different from [Smash], which only swung or pushed the enemy in front of me. The name of this was... [Final Shield Attack].
Similarly, I had also just made it up.
Shhhhhh!

Soon, the goblin, who died a quick death, disappeared in the form of light. It was proof that evil had diminished in the slightest bit and that the world had become a little more beautiful. I picked up the mana stones left behind as a reward and stuffed them into my pocket. That was my tenth mana stone since entering the labyrinth.
“Whew, you weak bastards.”
I had continued to encounter goblins since my first near-death experience. At first, I was nervous, but I soon realized that goblins were not a threat in the light.
They were not as smart as I had thought. That was made evident by the carelessly placed trap up ahead.
At least cover it up with some dirt. Are you stupid or what? If you leave it out in the open like that, who the hell is going to step on it?

The goblin traps were so shoddy that they could be detected even at a distance. And if you tried to pass by the trap without stepping on it, the goblins would jump out and attack first. Apparently, they only followed after you like a freak if you actually stepped on a trap...

Gradually, after figuring out the goblins’ fight patterns, facing them became easier. First of all, their main weapon of choice was a short dagger, and their physical strength was that of a junior high student. On the other hand, I was now a muscular barbarian with a 6′5″ tall body. In an outright battle, I could subdue a goblin within three seconds.
That meant I only had to be wary of surprise attacks, but it was possible to figure out the location of an ambush in advance using the traps.
Hmm, why not become a goblin slayer while I’m at it?
I immediately moved my hand to slap myself in the face.
Wham!
I was now wide awake because of the pain.
What was I just thinking...? I’m clearly going crazy.

If I wasn’t, there was no way I’d be entertained by such a pathetic thought. I couldn’t get cocky just because I had killed a few goblins. I had only been given a second chance at life less than two hours ago. Plus, I had yet to solve any of my most recent problems.
“Ugh, I’m hungry...”
First, there was the issue of food.

The shield wasn’t the only thing I had dropped while crawling through the darkness. About five days’ worth of food had been lost due to a hole in the bag of food provided by the chieftain. Of course, I couldn’t wander through the dark just to find it either. It wasn’t like I was Hansel and Gretel.
While I was thinking that, I opened my pouch, took out a piece of bread, and ate it.
Bite, bite.
The bread was hard and lacked moisture, probably for preservation purposes, but by softening it with my saliva, I could feel the sweetness of carbohydrates on my tongue.
Why is this so delicious?

My tastes must have changed with this barbarian body. After a few bites, the bread that had been the size of my palm disappeared. I sighed, feeling the strange taste of regret and bitterness on my tongue.
I was thirsty.
This was the second problem.
Fuck, where do I find water?
[You have killed a goblin.]
[You have killed a goblin.]
[You have killed a goblin.]
[You have killed a goblin.]
[WARNING! Your hydration levels are low. Obtain drinking water quickly...]
Dungeon and Stone had a thirst mechanic. Of course, it only activated inside a labyrinth, and there was no need to carry drinking water because the gauge could be refilled with just a meal.
But this was not a game. To be more exact, this place was more like a different universe that was just very similar to the game I knew.
It was already a hardcore game, but now that I’m living it, the difficulty is insane.

I wasn’t too worried, though. It was true that water was a more important resource than food, but the chief of the tribe had not provided us with water. That obviously meant it was possible to be self-sufficient in the labyrinth.
It didn’t take long to actually find it, either.
“Smash!”
I spent the next hour slaying goblins and wandering through a maze that was as complicated as an ant hill. Then, while following the sound of dripping water, I found a small pond.
There was already one explorer squatting at the pond and drinking from it. Excluding the blond’s party, this was actually my first time running into another person...
But no words were exchanged. The other person looked at me from across the room and left without a word, and I didn’t bother talking to them either.

The other adventurers I ran into after that were all the same. As soon as people saw me, they avoided me. There seemed to be an unwritten rule among adventurers that they did not interact with each other, just like in the game.
Well, maybe they just didn’t want to get involved with a blood-soaked barbarian.
Anyway, after hunting more goblins, I ate some bread when I was hungry and drank water when I was thirsty before restarting the cycle anew. Time flew by like that.
“One, two, three, four, five, six...”
Counting the number of mana stones I had earned so far, I found that I had a total of forty-four. Converted to bread, that was equivalent to forty-four loaves.
If I thought of the days when I had been on the brink of death, this was truly a triumphant feat, but nothing was free in this world. In return, I was deeply exhausted.
This was the third problem I had.
I’m getting tired...
Since I was a living creature, I had to sleep. Not even a souped-up barbarian was special in that regard.
So, how did you sleep in a labyrinth where monsters existed?
There were two ways. I could put my life in the hands of the universe and just take a nap, or I could find an ally so we could watch each other’s backs.
I had already decided which option I was going with.
Entrust my life to the universe? In my experience, the universe could not be trusted. In my case, at least, it really couldn’t be.
Let’s find an ally.
Of course, I wasn’t planning on creating a formal party. Everyone had to be just as exhausted right now, so I planned to find a suitable person and form a temporary alliance.
In fact, even when I was playing the game, I used that strategy for most nights when my exhaustion meter was filled.
Trudge, trudge.
After making that decision, I focused on moving rather than battling and began wandering through the labyrinth. As I walked, I began to see groups of people everywhere, unlike before.
Trudge, trudge.
A group of two or three adventurers was resting, taking turns on watch. After evaluating their appearances and demeanors, I mustered up the courage to approach a few groups, but they were all a bust.
“I’m sorry, but we’ve got all the people we need.”
Although they said that, I noticed that when I approached them, they frowned and covered their noses. The reason was very clear.
Assholes. How clean do you think you are?
I was grunting to myself inwardly when someone spoke to me.
“Hey.”
He was a human man who looked to be in his thirties. His height was about six feet. Although he had a warm demeanor that seemed pretty kind, in his hand was a hammer coated in goblin blood.
The man smiled and asked me, “Are you looking for a night companion?”
What the fuck.
As I instinctively took a step back, the man tilted his head.
“Isn’t that what you were looking for? I thought I could rest easy because you are a barbarian, but that’s unfortunate.”
Why didn’t you say that in the first place, mister...

Apparently ‘night companion’ was slang for a temporary cooperative relationship. That was the phrase used in the game too. I had always translated it as ‘night comrade’ or ‘night buddy,’ but actually hearing it out loud in real life, there was something very perverted about it.
“...No, I actually am looking for a night companion.”
“Are you? I’m glad. Then will you come with me?”
“I will.”
So I became night companions with this man.
“My name is Hans.”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Then can I call you Bjorn?”
The man seemed to have a lot of experience with this. He smoothly introduced himself and led the conversation.
“A group of three night companions is best, but that seems like a waste of energy at this point. Bjorn, what do you think?”
Simply put, he was saying the two of us should sleep together.
Maybe this man really was perverted? I didn’t know if it was because of his slick tone of voice, but I kept getting the feeling I was being led into something weird.
“Fine.”
“Good. If someone asks to join us, then we can discuss it with each other and decide whether to accept their offer or not.”
After a brief discussion, we decided to guard each other that night.
However, the problem was...
“So, let’s decide on the watch order with rock-paper-scissors.”
Rock-paper-scissors seemed to be the law of the land here as well.
Shit, I’m not good at this game...
Once again, I had terrible luck.
“Hmm, looks like I won.”
Damn it all.
“I’ll put my trust in you. When a goblin or another adventurer approaches, wake me up. Got it?”
“...Okay.”
“Here, take this.”
The man lent me a watch with the numbers zero to twenty-three on the dial and was kind enough to teach me how to use it.
“When the short hour hand reaches here, you can wake me up.”
Perhaps this was what most people thought of barbarians.
“Don’t break it. It’s expensive.”
“...Okay.”
How fussy.

Soon, the man took out a blanket, covered himself with it, and laid down using his backpack as a pillow. And soon after that, he fell asleep. I supposed this was what experience looked like. He looked damn comfortable.
If I asked him to lend me that when it’s my turn, he’d probably say no, right?
“Phew...”

By the way, this night watch thing was super boring. The goblin bastards were nowhere to be seen, and there were no other adventurers trying to pass through this passage. Maybe everyone had found a night companion already and was resting?
As the silence continued, I continued to get sleepy. Still, time passed quickly. I leaned against the wall and thought about the future.
Then, “Hans, get up.”
“...Did anything happen?”
“No.”
“I see. Good work. Then hand me the watch and get some rest. I’ll wake you up in two hours.”
