Before I could ask about borrowing it, the man packed his blanket back into his backpack and stood up.
Welp.
I quickly got over it, sat with my back to the wall, and pretended to nod off.
That was a given. No matter how kind or intelligent this man seemed, and even if he had no intention of harming me—
How could I trust a bastard I’d just met?

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Give and Take (3)
paragraphs: I began snoring. I envisioned what it must sound like to be a snoring barbarian who had fallen asleep after a tiring day.
Honk! Honk!
...Mm, is this overdoing it a little?
I was a little worried that was the case, but I heard a laugh.
“...Truly a curious people.”
I think it worked.

I guess my appearance was better than my acting skills in this case. The common perception was that barbarians were simple-minded and ignorant. That was why I acted like a barbarian all the time, even in situations that had nothing to do with evil spirits. Essentially, I was hiding a dagger behind a smile.
Using the preconceived notion that barbarians were naive as a weapon to see through people’s true intentions...
...sounded a bit too teen-angsty.
To summarize, it was easier to lure someone out this way. Just like this.
Honk! Honk!

Scratching my stomach to make for a realistic performance, I curled up on my side. Even so, I continued to listen and focus all my attention on the man’s movements. Since I was exposing so many of my weak spots, he would act soon if he had an ulterior motive. If not, I could just sleep.
To be honest, however, I didn’t know if I would be able to sleep in this situation.
“Bjorn, it’s time to switch.”
Ah, mm... I really didn’t expect that I wouldn’t be able to sleep at all, though.
“Don’t lower your guard too much just because there have been no goblins up until now. They are cunning creatures.”
The man apparently didn’t trust me because he tiptoed around essentially telling me not to slack off. And in less than five minutes, he fell asleep again.
Disappointment crept in.
I should’ve just slept too. What the hell have I been doing for two hours? God damn it.
Was it because a person I had just met had been beside me? Even though I had decided halfway through that he was trustworthy, I still couldn’t fall asleep.
If I had known this would happen, I would have just fended off the goblins myself and gotten some sleep on my own. That way, I could have slept even just a little bit.
“Phew...”
I was so tired I could die. And I felt even sleepier because the guy next to me was asleep.
Since it was still my turn to take watch, I kept my mind on other thoughts in an attempt to fight off sleep when someone suddenly called out to me.
“Bjorn, get up.”
“I wasn’t asleep.”
“How about wiping the saliva from your mouth before you say that?”
When I wiped my mouth with the back of my hand, it really was wet.
“Since you slept standing up, you didn’t even snore.”
It seemed I really had fallen asleep, even if it was just for a short while during the last ten minutes of my shift...
My heart dropped. However, there was something I had to do before berating myself for letting my guard down.
“I’m sorry,” I said sincerely.

I wasn’t pretending to be a barbarian this time—I was being serious. Night companions were a kind of quid pro quo relationship. Even though the man had provided a safe environment for me during his watch, I hadn’t done the same. I had to apologize if I didn’t want to become the kind of person I despised.
“Fortunately, we didn’t have any problems while you were sleeping, so I’ll wipe the slate.”
“Thank you. You can sleep more if you want. I can be on watch again.”
“No. That won’t do. It’s your turn, so go to sleep. And give me the watch.”
He could have turned the blame on me, but he instead forgave me with a friendly smile.

So without further ado, I went over to my seat and curled into a ball. Again, sleep did not come. All adventurers, including that guy, were truly amazing. To entrust your life to someone you had just met for the first time every day?
That took incredible guts. No matter how hard I thought about it, something like that was beyond my ability. For that reason, I started snoring just like before.
Honk! Honk!
I couldn’t help it.
I’m sorry, sir, but for some reason, you seem even more suspicious now.
Honk! Honk!
The fact that he had the kind face of a con man.
The fact that he had been the one to suggest not looking for a third companion.
The fact that he hadn’t called me out for smelling bad.
All of that was fine.
But just now, he didn’t blame me for falling asleep. He even refused the offer of being able to sleep again.
Of course, maybe I was just a crazy bastard, and this guy was in fact just a kind person. But in my mind, nice guys like this were the most suspicious ones of all.
It’s always guys like these who stab me in the back.
If I had been the old me, now would have been the moment when I let my guard down. But I wouldn’t make the same mistake. This was a matter of common sense.
Honk! Honk!
If he really seemed that suspicious, wouldn’t it have been better to just give up on this and say goodbye?
Even as I was wondering that, however, I continued to snore.
How much time has passed?
Click.
I heard a faint, but strange sound. A backpack buckle? A belt? Or perhaps the heel of a shoe?
I couldn’t get a sense of what had caused the sound.
However, at the same time I noticed, my barbarian body came to its own conclusion.
Danger.
Was this the physical sensation of murderous intent they talked about in martial arts books?
Goosebumps erupted on my skin. Immediately, I opened my eyes and looked around.
“You’re up.”
The old guy was smiling as kindly as ever... while holding a two-handed sledgehammer covered in goblin blood and flesh over his head.
What the f—
Run! The reaction time of this warrior-trained body was faster than mine. My body was already rolling sideways before my brain could give the command.
Booom!
Hearing the sound of something smashing right in front of my nose, I used the recoil to quickly rise and get back on my feet.
“Ugh!”
The man, whose surprise attack had failed, had a bewildered expression on his face. Rather than asking why, I dashed forward.
“W-Wait!”
Was he trying to make an excuse or something? Say that he didn’t mean to do it? That he was just trying to warm up? If that was the case, that was kind of—no, extremely funny.
Fuck, how stupid do they think barbarians are here?
Crack!
The shield smashed right into the man’s chin. However, a strong human was different from a goblin. The man staggered but did not fall over.
Then, I struck him again.
Crack!
[Smash.]
“Ahhh!”
The hammer in the man’s hand fell to the ground with a thud. His nose was already red and dripping with blood.
Oh, that’s gonna hurt.
But I wasn’t going to lower my guard, because I wanted to be the guy who didn’t know what that pain felt like.
So, once again—
“S-Stop! I can explain...!”
“Smash.”

I slammed the man in the face with the shield again and again until he fell to his knees. If this were a game, he would be incapable of combat. In other words, it was now possible to have a conversation.
“Mister.”
“I-I was wrong! Please!”
Had he decided to ask for forgiveness? It was a quick decision, but not a very wise one. That was not the conversation I wanted to have.
“Why did you do it?”
“I-I wanted your mana stones... I was just going to knock you unconscious and steal them. Please trust me!”
Trust? Trust, my ass. If I had that kind of love for humanity, I would have had at least a few more friends.
As I slowly raised the shield, the guy quickly added to his excuse.
“The shield! I was going to take that shield too!”
This was without a doubt the reason why I didn’t trust other people. Everyone lied far too easily, even when they weren’t good at it.
“Why the shield?”
“...Because barbarian weapons are good quality. I was going to sell it once I returned to the city.”

Certainly, the weapons that the barbarians received during the tutorial were usually valuable. This was because the amount of iron in them was significantly higher than the amount found in generic weapons. My current shield was made entirely of iron.
But even so, killing someone just to get this? Well, when I think about it, it’s not that hard to wrap my head around. But...
“Bullshit.”
This man was still hiding something.
“Be honest. Why did you do it?”
Just like when dealing with a fallen goblin, I stomped on the man’s upper body and crushed it under my foot.
“Ahh!”
Fear was deeply engraved in the man’s eyes. Surprisingly, it provoked no emotion in me. Was it because this bastard had tried to kill me?
I could kind of understand now why they said not to look into the eyes when butchering a cow, though... However, I found I could ignore the feeling.
Just as I was considering ending the conversation, the man shouted, “H-Heart!”
“Heart?”
That’s an unexpected word.
When I gave him a questioning look, the man continued with a resigned expression on his face.
“...Barbarian hearts are selling for a high price.”
“Why?”
“I-I don’t know for sure, but they say they’re used as an ingredient in a newly developed spell!”
“I see.”
Now I understood the motive. I was a goblin to this man: a creature that was difficult to catch, but once caught, came with a great reward.
“Why did you act now instead of when I first fell asleep?”
“...I had to sleep too.”
Oh, I see. He wanted to earn money and also sleep while he was at it. I had thought it was because the man was very cautious, but he was just an efficient freak.
“I’ve told you everything, so please forgive me...”
“Forgive?”
To be honest, I couldn’t help but laugh.
Forgiveness? Is that something a guy who tried to tear out someone’s heart and steal their gear should ask for?
Had my own reaction been a little late, I wouldn’t have even gotten a chance to beg him for my life.
“Please...”
I’m sure he wants to live. How could he have known this would happen? That attitude is commendable. However—
“Mister, it is only right to pay the price.”
I hated bastards who did whatever they pleased and avoided facing the consequences. Which meant...
“I-I will give you everything I have! Even if it’s not much right now if I just return to the city...”
He could not be trusted.

In that respect, I didn’t even know how this guy was any different from a goblin. Although you couldn’t befriend a goblin even if you wanted to, this guy had a choice. That was the only difference, and that made him much worse than a goblin.
Of course, this was just an emotional opinion, and I did not make choices based on emotions. It couldn’t always work out that way, of course, but I at least tried not to.
“I will probably meet countless people like you in the future. And they’ll say the same thing. Should I forgive them every time?”
Forgiveness was a very scary word. A decision made with good intentions often came back as a dagger and stabbed you in the back. I knew that better than anyone.
So this time I had no choice. A mistake in this primordial world wouldn’t just hurt my heart, but would even threaten my life.
“I’m sorry, mister. I’ve been stabbed in the back too many times for that.”
“N-No! I wouldn’t! I am different!”
Come to think of it, a goblin once said something like that to me. Or, rather, that’s what I interpreted from the look in its eyes. And what did I do next then?
Grip.
I raised the shield high with both hands. However, unlike back then, I paused.
Of course, the moment of hesitation did not last long. I felt an unknown force pulling my arm and—
“Oh no—!”
I brought the shield down with all my strength.
Crunch.
A heavy silence fell after the crack of breaking bones.
[Achievement]
[Condition: Commit your first murder.]
[Reward: Permanently increases your Spirit stat by 1.]
I did not look away from what I had done and accepted it for what it was.
About a day had passed since I had entered the world of the game. And I had killed a human being.

From the dead man, I retrieved a large hammer, shoulder guards, leather boots, a compass, a knife, a pocket watch, a water bottle, a backpack, a blanket, herbs and bandages, a potion, six days’ worth of food and snacks, and thirty-two tier nine mana stones.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Night Companion (1)
paragraphs: I was walking through the cave. But this time without limping.
[You have acquired Worn Leather Boots.]
[Total Item Level has increased by 5.]

The boots were a little roomy. Thanks to that, I learned one more thing: the man’s feet had been quite big for his height. Anyway, the shoes were pretty sturdy, so stepping on a trap wouldn’t leave as serious an injury as last time.
[You have equipped a Two-handed Hammer.]
[Total Item Level has increased by 30.]
This sledgehammer was made of a lump of iron and was about three feet long. When the man had used it, it had been a two-handed bludgeoning weapon, but I was strong enough to wield it with one hand.
[You have equipped Worn Shoulder Guards.]
[Total Item Level has increased by 13.]
The guards were made of iron. I tied the laces a little loose and they fit just right. Wearing the guards without anything underneath, I looked like a gladiator.
[You have equipped a Backpack.]
[Inventory size has increased.]
Now, the blood-stained mana stones didn’t have to be stored with the bread, and were much less cumbersome to transport around.
Chew.

I took out a piece of jerky and chewed on it. There were only a few pieces and they were little more than a snack, but they tasted better than the bread. I cut the remainder with a pocket knife and stored them carefully to avoid them touching any liquids.
On the second day, I had graduated from my uncivilized lifestyle.

When I was thirsty, I drank water from the water pouch. If I wanted to know the direction I was headed, I took out the compass, and if I wanted to know the time, I looked at the pocket watch. The emergency health potion I had would also help deal with any potential injuries.
How ironic. Now that I have killed another human being, I’m able to live more like one.
[Bjorn Yandel]
[Level: 1
Physique: 25
Spirit: 37 (New +1)
Special Ability: 1
Item Level: 72 (New +48)
General Combat Power: 81 (New +13)]
[Smash] was a good technique to use with a shield, but with the right weapon, it was different.
Crunch—!

A goblin disappeared into a flash of light with a single swing of the hammer. Had I known that would be the case, I would have just picked a weapon from the start. After all, I could have purchased a shield later on with savings.

Well, I hadn’t known at the time that I could fight so well. Maybe it was because I was inside the body of a barbarian, but when I fought, I felt like my body wasn’t mine. I should have been getting used to it by now, but watching this body continue to exceed my expectations still amazed me.
“I’m tired as fuck.”

Yawning, I picked up the two magic stones that had fallen to the floor nearby and put them in the bag. This was a change that had occurred at the start of the second day. The goblins had started appearing in groups of two. Tomorrow, it would probably increase to three, and would continue to increase like that until the seventh day when the labyrinth closed. That was how it had been in the game.

In that sense, things weren’t so bad yet. My combat power had increased with the new gear, and thanks to all of the supplies, the journey had become a little safer. Everything was progressing quite smoothly.
Except for the fact that my eyes keep closing.
Ever since yesterday, I had been on the move, fighting goblins. But, I had only managed to sleep for less than ten minutes while I was with that guy, and even then, I had fallen asleep standing up.
I wanted to sleep. I didn’t even wish for blankets and pillows. At this point, I could curl up into a ball on the bare ground.
I’m really gonna bite the dust if this—
I almost fell asleep while walking and tripped over a stone.
“Ah, shit!”
I had been lucky despite the fall. Had it been a trap, I would have been in real trouble.
“I might as well get some actual sleep...”

As soon as I made that decision, I leaned against the wall with my shield in one hand and my hammer in the other. Even though I didn’t have any night companions by my side, it felt safer this way. If I was going to be ambushed anyway, it was better if it was by a goblin than my companion. If it was going to happen, I had a better chance of surviving a stab from a carving knife. Compared to being beaten with a hammer in my sleep, at least.
Step—
Damn.

I woke up to the sound of incredibly familiar footsteps. They had been nowhere to be seen during my four-hour night watch but just had to show up right when I was dozing off alone. I could see why that guy had told me to stay on guard.
...Stubborn bastards.
I immediately ran forward and drove the hammer into the goblin’s head.
Wham!
“G-Grk...”
There had been a total of two goblins sneakily approaching me, but one of them turned around and ran away as soon as its friend was turned into mush.
Yes, run away. I don’t even have the energy to follow you.
“Ha, these assholes...”

When I checked the time, less than ten minutes had passed. In the end, I had no choice but to go back to the cave and hunt more goblins. When I was tired and couldn’t stand it any longer, I leaned against the wall and dozed off for a while.

There were a few close calls as I was resting, but only two moments where I really thought I was going to meet my maker. The first was when I sensed a presence and opened my eyes. A shady adventurer had been quietly approaching me.
When our eyes met, he smiled guiltily, then backed away and disappeared. Just remembering it gave me chills... In terms of close calls, twice was more than enough.
Especially since another close call was happening right now.
[You have been attacked by a goblin in your sleep.]
For the first time, I opened my eyes to pain rather than a presence.
A goblin was right in front of me. Once I slammed the hammer down onto it and killed it, another of the fuckers jumped up.
“G-Grk!”
I immediately identified the cause of the pain.
Oh my god, there is a carving knife stuck between my clavicles.
...Shit, so that was why my left arm wasn’t moving well.
Whew, at least I had walked out of this with just pain. If I had been a little shorter, or if the goblin had been a better jumper, this carving knife would have been embedded in my neck.
I clenched my teeth and pulled out the knife.
Shhunk!
Then, taking out the potion from the bag, I placed a few drops on the wounded area. As soon as I closed the stopper and put it back in the bag, my blood started to boil and regenerate quickly.
Chhh.
The dirtbag who made this potion, was he a psychopath? Somehow, this hurt more than getting stabbed in the first place.
“Ouch, ugh.”

After about five minutes, the pain went away. A pain like that should have chased away all thoughts of sleep, but my eyelids were much heavier than before. If I stopped concentrating for even a moment, my vision went blurry. It was time to make the call I’d been putting off.
Although the body of a barbarian was attuned to sensing murderous intent, there was clearly a limit when trying to doze off like this. And just now, I only woke up after I had already been stabbed.
I need to rest.

When I checked the time, I found that about fourteen hours had passed since I left the guy. Perhaps the adventurers active on the first floor were slowly wandering around looking for night companions for tonight.
And actually, as I roamed the area, some adventurers approached me first.
“Hey, barbarian, are you looking for a night companion?”
And very passionately, too.
“Hmm, you look pretty tired. Will you join up with me?”
“Barbarians are trustworthy. If you join us, that would make three. How about teaming up?”

I felt like a popular prostitute. Maybe it was because we had all been in the same boat for about two days now, but today, no one brought up how I smelled. Or maybe the smell hadn’t been the problem in the first place?
To be fair, my appearance yesterday, covered in blood and hobbling around thanks to my missing sandal, had been a bit intense.
“Really? How unfortunate.”
Numerous offers flooded in, but I refused all of them and kept moving through the cavern.
Ha... are there no other strong barbarians around here anywhere?
My best bet was to find a fellow barbarian and become night companions with them. The problem was, even now on the second day, there was no sign of any barbarians anywhere.
“You’re looking for your own people? Hmm, that’s going to be tough.”
“Tough? Why?”

“Even a barbarian who has only just finished their coming-of-age ceremony will be upstairs on the second floor of the labyrinth within two or three months. I don’t know for sure, but there are probably less than a hundred of you guys on the first floor by now.”

When I looked into it, I learned that barbarians as a whole were rare on the first floor. True, it was strange for someone with a body like this to still be scrounging the first floor. Ninety-nine percent of the adventurers I ran into on the first floor were just regular humans.
“Why don’t you join us instead?”
“I’m sorry, but I can’t.”
“I see. Well, may Rafdonia be with you on your journey.”
“Thanks.”

This man looked pretty trustworthy, but I kept moving along once the conversation came to an end. Now that I had learned that barbarian hearts were valuable, all adventurers had started to look like shady bastards to me.
Click.
I took out the compass. I’d been moving south since I got this, but I still hadn’t gotten out of the goblin zone. I was once again realizing how big the first floor was.
...Should I give up on looking for my own people?
I didn’t have to think it over for long. I decided to stop looking for a needle in a haystack and instead made a more realistic plan.
It doesn’t have to be a barbarian. I’m now just going to find a night companion... excluding anyone human.

I decided to look for a fantasy race, which made up less than 1 percent of the population. My best bet would be an elf who placed a high value on oaths or a dwarf with a personality as valorous as a barbarian. It didn’t matter much if they were a different race. Unlike most humans, they had patience. Given time, they had the talent to climb all the way up to the top, so they wouldn’t be blinded by money and hurt another adventurer.
Having come to that decision, I wandered around the cave for about an hour.
And...
[You have encountered an unfamiliar, injured elf.]
I finally came across someone from an otherworldly race.
The moment our eyes met, a strangely suffocating stillness filled the air.
The pointy-eared elf was sitting with their back against the wall and staring at me without saying a word. Were they sleeping there alone with no companion?
Their amber eyes, which glowed like a cat’s, betrayed alarm and deep hostility. It was clear they hoped that I would just pass them by, but...
As our stare-off dragged on, the elf got up with a nervous look on their face. They seemed to wince and groan.
Ack... hemmm—
The way they were holding their body was awkward. Upon further examination, I spotted a wound on their stomach.
“You’re hurt.”
It wasn’t deep, but it was still a long cut... a cut that could not have been made by a goblin’s carving knife. I quickly came to a conclusion.
“Was it a human?”
The elf didn’t answer. They must have been afraid of me. I could understand that. I would also be very scared if someone of my stature approached me while I was injured.
Plus, this elf was also female and very small. Maybe not even five feet?
Anyway, this wasn’t a bad situation—
“Spare me.”
Huh?
“Please. Just this once, Mr. Barbarian. I have a younger sibling in the city I have to look after.”
I was struggling to understand what kind of plot development this was when the elf knelt down to her knees without hesitation. At some point, tears had formed in her eyes.
“I beg of you.”
Huh? What kind of elf is this cowardly?
To be honest, I had thought she would be a cool beauty type because of her appearance. Most of the elves in the game spoke and had personalities like that.
Whoops, if I had known she was this kind of character, I would have approached this completely differently. I should clear up the misunderstanding before things get worse.
“I have no intention of killing you,” I said, careful to properly enunciate while making eye contact with her.
The eyes are the windows to the soul, so if I give her time to calm down, she’ll see that what I’m saying is sincere—
“...Do you have to do this, Mr. Barbarian?”
What is she talking about?
Next came the identity crisis.
“Just once, please, let me go just this one time.”

As my silence went on, the elf stepped backward with an even more fearful expression on her face and opened the collar of her shirt. I was dumbfounded. I felt like a pervert harassing a high school student in front of her school. This misunderstanding made me feel terrible.
What kind of life do these other barbarian bastards lead? What could our reputation be to make this kid go this far?
I let out an involuntary sigh.
What do I do? Would the misunderstanding be cleared up if I showed her that I’m not that kind of scum with actions rather than words?
That didn’t seem like a bad idea. I took a step back, took the herbs and bandages out of my bag, and tossed them her way.
“Treat your injury first. We’ll talk after.”
“This is... a licho herb...?”
So it was a licho herb. Now I could use it with peace of mind. I had been worried that it was poisonous this whole time.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Night Companion (2)
paragraphs: “...Why are you giving me this?”
“Do I need a reason to help someone?”
The phony, insincere words splintered like wood chips on my tongue, but it couldn’t be helped. This sort of thing worked on this type of character.
I wanted to be night companions with this elf. It sounded creepy when I said it that way, but it wouldn’t be a bad deal for this woman either.

From her injury and exhaustion to her beauty, her situation was several times worse than mine. She probably knew that too, which was why she had acted like that earlier. To be honest, even I was surprised by how committed she had been to surviving just now.
“As I said before, treat your injury first. We can talk after.”
“I’m going to stand guard.”
After I turned around dismissively, I soon heard a sound behind me. It sounded like she was chewing on the herb to make it easier to apply.
“I’m done...”
Already? Surprising. She must have good technique.
I turned around and saw that between her torn clothes, there was a tightly wrapped bandage. And it seemed her guard toward me had lowered a little based on the way she now looked at me.
First, some introductions to close the distance.
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“...Erwen.”
“I don’t know what you misunderstood earlier. But nothing you thought would happen is going to happen.”
“Sorry? Oh. Okay...”
She pretended it wasn’t, but the fear in her eyes was still there. I had thought that after doing all this, the misunderstanding would be resolved by now. What had gone wrong?
In the end, I bluntly asked, “Why are you so afraid of me?”
“...Barbarians and elves are enemies, right?”
“Enemies?”
“S-Sorry. That’s not what I meant... I don’t want to fight you.”
At my question, she suddenly realized what she had said and started acting as submissive as earlier.
I was just curious now...
Elves and barbarians, enemies? This is my first time hearing that. The two races definitely got along pretty well in the game. How had this happened?
I only stared at her, wide-eyed, but she immediately started spilling the information I wanted to hear.
“T-The war ended ten years ago. I-I have no hard feelings! Really.”
Ten years ago...
I didn’t know what had happened, but those words made it sound more like a grudge than an adversarial relationship.
Mm, then, after hearing bad things about us from a young age, maybe she had grown up to be afraid of barbarians?
The situation was worse now.
What should I do? Should I look for someone else before it’s too late?
But then the herbs and bandages I already gave up would go to waste...
Okay, let’s try first.
“I have no hard feelings either.”
“R-Really!”
“That’s right. That’s why, Erwen, would you like to be my night companion tonight?”
“...Night companion?”
“I am tired. You must be as well. So how about we work together for today, with or without hard feelings?”

Suddenly, her eyes lit up and she almost looked like a different person than before. I gave her time to think without being impatient, and she considered the offer with a frown before offering a condition instead of an agreement.
“I heard barbarians value their honor as a warrior. Can you swear on it? That you won’t harm me?”
“Swear?”
“O-Of course, I will swear the same to you in the name of my clan. I will never do harm to you either, mister.”

In Korean culture, this was the equivalent of us each bringing our thumbs to our tongues and pinky fingers to our foreheads. Of course, I could do that all day. However, there was one issue that needed to be addressed before that.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel. Not ‘mister.’”
Despite my real age, Bjorn was only twenty years old.
The contract was established. There was no signing of thumbprints involved, but we did something similar to that in this culture’s terms.
Thanks to that, I found out the elf’s real name: Erwen Fornacci di Tersia. She was twenty years old, the same age as me.
Whew, good thing I wasn’t actually Bjorn. I was sure the real Bjorn would have thought so too. Didn’t matter to me, but this woman would have... I wasn’t gonna tell her, though.
“Then how should we decide on the shifts?”
“I will sleep first. That will make you feel safer.”
“I wouldn’t say that, but if you insist, I wouldn’t exactly say no...”
In other words, she would like that very much.
“I’ll take that as a yes.”
“Yes.”
Phew, I’m glad that worked. If she had suggested doing rock, paper, scissors, things would have looked bleak.
My eyes had been shutting for a while now.
Please, I just want to get some sleep. Is it so hard to get a good night’s sleep?
“Oh! How will I know the time?”
Tsk, this is why newbies are a pain.
I took the watch out of my backpack and gave it to Erwen.
“It’s an expensive item, so don’t break it.”
“Okay...”
Seeing her not only say that but also treat the watch like a newborn baby gave me peace of mind.
“I will take good care of it,” she said. “Good night.”
I laid down with my backpack as a pillow and covered myself with a blanket, just like that man had.
And...
Honk!
I passed out.
“Mister!”
I told you it’s Bjorn.
“Mister, wake up. It’s time.”
I forced my eyes open and got up. I couldn’t believe it. It had been two hours already?
“Here, your watch.”

I looked at the time and two hours had in fact passed. Come to think of it, I hadn’t even gotten a chance to fake-snore for a while. I had been planning on faking it for about ten minutes just in case...
Wow, is this the effect of combining a backpack and a blanket? It’s almost scary.

If the man had lent these to me back then, I wouldn’t have been able to avoid his surprise attack. I would have slept so comfortably that I wouldn’t even have been able to tell if the world was ending around me.
Is this karma...? In that case, I should lend it to this woman as well.
“Use the blanket. If you want to use the pillow, you can use that as well.”
“Sorry? But...”
Although she was refusing it, I could see that the corners of her mouth were lifted. I decided to pretend not to see that.
“Well, then, thank you...”
Without needing any further convincing, Erwen managed to crawl into the blanket and curl up like a cat. And soon after, she began to breathe rhythmically.
She was sleeping fine even with a strange man right next to her. She must really have been tired. While I had had a tiring day, her day must’ve been grueling as well.
“Phew...”
I leaned against the wall and opened the clock out of habit.

It felt like at least five days had passed, but in reality, there was still more than an hour left until the end of the second day. I wanted to return to the city as soon as possible. To be honest, it was ridiculous to talk about ‘going back,’ but... I planned on sleeping for a few days once I got back.
...Seeing as I can think like this, it looks like my body really has recovered.
I put away the watch and fell deep into thought. It had been a while since I had had a peaceful moment to think, so my mind kept wandering from this to that.
What happened to me in the real world? Did I become a missing person? Not yet, obviously. No one would have come by my place. Even my job wouldn’t take a few days of absence too seriously.
“Ha.”
There was a reason I hadn’t thought about that issue until now. It would only make me sad. If I started to think that there was nothing to go back for, I would totally destroy my will to go on.
It was better not to think of these things for various reasons, no matter how self-deceiving it might be.
Since I was pretty mentally disciplined, I manually altered my train of thought.
All right, let’s recap what’s happened over the past two days: the coming-of-age ceremony, entering the labyrinth, fighting the goblins, fighting the heartstealer...
I could applaud myself for doing well so far, right? I had really thought I was going to die. Since there was no one to pat me on the back, why not pat my own back?
Click—
I decided to only think about congratulating myself once I got back to the city. When I opened the watch, it was already time.
“Erwen, get up.”
“Five more minutes...”
What? Five minutes? Get up.
I vigorously shook her shoulder with my barbarian hand, and Erwen rubbed her eyes and got up.
This looks dangerous. I can see why that heart stealer couldn’t trust me.
“Don’t even think about falling asleep just because there have been no monsters around so far.”
“Okay...”
I was a little nervous, but I still lay down. Because I had lent Erwen the blanket and backpack, her warmth lingered even when it was my turn to sleep.
It was kind of ironic. How long had it been since I had felt someone else’s warmth? It felt very strange. Perhaps even more so than anything else that I’d been through over the past two days.
Honk!!
This time I had quite a bit of energy, so I started fake-snoring. To be honest, it was more to make sure Erwen wasn’t going to fall asleep.
...It doesn’t seem she is.
I peeked my eyes open and glanced in her direction, then I decided to let go of my worries and closed my eyes again.
And, how long has it been since—
I sensed a presence and immediately sat up.
“Ahh!”
For some reason, I was holding Erwen’s pale wrist. It looked like it had been outstretched toward me.
“What are you doing?”
“Y-You were having a nightmare and you were sweating...”
As I glanced at the handkerchief in her hand, it didn’t seem like she was lying. If it had been a weapon, I would have slammed my shield into her without asking for an explanation.
“S-Sorry.”

After taking stock of the situation, I relaxed my fingers. Then, with a pained expression on her face, Erwen cradled the wrist that I had grabbed. There were already red marks appearing on her skin. I didn’t apologize. It would’ve been an empty apology anyway.
“How much time has passed?”
“...Ten minutes left until we switch.”
“I see. Then let’s switch now.”
“If I sleep now, I will just end up feeling more tired.”
At my words, Erwen lay down with an apologetic look. Then she twisted and turned a little before speaking up.
“Um.”
“Is there a problem?”
“No. I just have a question.”
“Ask.”
Erwen hesitated for a moment before opening her mouth.
“...Who is ‘mister?’”
What? Is that a pun?
“You kept saying you were sorry in your sleep... Oh, I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have asked. You don’t have to answer. I’ll just sleep now.”
Before I could answer, Erwen ended the conversation and pulled the blanket over her head. It seemed that this young lady was realizing that I wasn’t so scary and was starting to get curious.
“Ugh.”
Stretching my body, I thought it over in my head.
I couldn’t remember anything, but it sounded like I really had had a nightmare. Suddenly, I was a little curious too.
Who the hell was the mister I was asking for forgiveness?
Two candidates came to mind: the unnamed man who had been decapitated at the coming-of-age ceremony, and Hans, the heartstealer who had allowed me to be human again.
...But when I thought about it, both options were weird. I hadn’t done anything to either of them that needed an apology.
I soon came to a conclusion.
Whatever dream I had, it must have been a silly dream.

Day three had begun, and there were about ten minutes left before I was supposed to wake Erwen up. Observing her as she curled up in a ball and slept with the blanket between her legs, I pondered whether to ask her to join me again. That was to say, whether to ask her to become my comrade.
Of course, there was the downside of having to share loot. Even though goblins would appear in threes and fours from day three onward, a partnership would definitely reduce my income.
This had nothing to do with her strength. Well, since she was an elf, she would pull her weight well enough...
Could I say that I was already powerful enough on my own?

Even without Erwen, I could easily kill three or four goblins on my own. That wasn’t me being conceited, it was just an observation after having gone through several battles with this body. That was what I genuinely believed. Remaining alone would leave me in a position to collect as many mana stones as possible to prepare for my living expenses in the city and subsequent taxes.
“Phew...”
A risk-free bed, or more mana stones. I continued mulling this over in order to make the most rational decision when—
Tap—

From the passageway on the left, I could hear the steps of another adventurer. This had happened several times over the course of the night, so I wasn’t particularly concerned. Most of the time, they had glanced over at us and then passed us by.
However...
Tap—
This duo of adventurers, Chubby and Boney, looked in our direction. They immediately stopped walking and whispered to each other.
“Isn’t that the elf?” Chubby asked.
“Looks like it. The shape of the bow matches up,” Boney sneered in reply.
The two men whispered to each other and when they came to a decision, Chubby became the spokesman and spoke up with a question.
“Barbarian, what is your relationship to that elf?”
“As you can see, we are night companions.”
“A barbarian and an elf as night companions... What a strange sight. So, how long do you have left?”
“I have no reason to answer you.”
Chubby did not ask any further questions after that. He just grinned and took Boney, who had been next to him and left.
“I see. Let’s go.”
“What? Y-Yeah...”
Soon, the duo disappeared from our passageway. However, I couldn’t relax.
Who the hell were those creepy assholes? That felt as threatening as when the chieftain yelled in my face.
I slowly moved to the side and tapped sleeping Erwen on the shoulder.
How can you sleep in a situation like this?
“Hurry, wake up. I think we’re fucked.”

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Night Companion (3)
paragraphs: Strictly speaking, “we” was not the correct term here, because it was Erwen, not me, who the Chubby and Boney duo were interested in. I tapped Erwen with my foot again.
No ‘mmm.’ Wake up right now. I know you’re not asleep.
The moment I heard their voices earlier, I glanced over and caught her covering her face with the blanket.
“Ah!”
It was a waste of time to argue with her, so I just grabbed her by the shoulders and forced her up.
“Why are you pretending to be asleep?”
“Because...”
Erwen trailed off mid-sentence and avoided my gaze. This was rather frustrating behavior for me, because I had to get information from her as quickly as possible to make a decision.
When I grabbed her chin to look her in the eye, Erwen reluctantly opened her mouth.
“Because you were going to leave once I woke up...”
Is that true?

I had made a promise: if there was a fight with an adventurer while one of us was standing on night watch, we would fight them together. But unfortunately, this situation happened on my last promised watch.

Well, I didn’t care about a warrior’s honor or any of that, but... this woman didn’t know that. So, she had tried to make our alliance last as long as possible. She knew that the moment she opened her eyes, our night companion contract would be over.
“Whew.”

First, I took a deep breath. If a grown man like Mr. Hans had done something like this, I would have been angry... However, since she was just twenty years old, a sense of pity welled up within me first.
Of course, the situations were completely different.
“What happened with those two?”
“Nothing.”
“Then why were you hiding?”
“...The symbol stitched into their clothes was the same. The same as the human man who tried to hurt me. They must belong to the same guild.”
A guild... Shit, things were getting more serious. I was starting to wonder whether it would be better to just say goodbye to this elf girl and go our separate ways here.
“Let’s talk while we move.”
“Are you going to help me?”
“I’ll decide after I hear the rest.”
First, I got Erwen out of there. While practically running, I tried to understand the rest of the situation.
“Tell me everything that happened.”
Apparently reading the atmosphere, Erwen gave me a brief summary of just the important information without any unnecessary details.
“On the first day, I met a night companion who attacked me while I was asleep. I found out later that he was a member of a guild whose main base was the first floor.”
For reference, the guild’s name was the ‘Crystal Union.’
“I managed to escape, but ever since then, people from the same group have been attacking me whenever they see me. That’s how I got injured.”
I stopped her there.
“Wait, how did they know what happened?”
“A message stone.”
What was that? There was nothing like that in the game I had played.
“In more detail,” I said.
“It’s a magic tool that allows you to communicate with other message stones that have been linked to each other. I heard the radius is about three hundred yards.”
“I see.”
It was a kind of walkie-talkie, then. If you established a frequency in advance, communication was possible up to a radius of three hundred yards.
Gradually, I started to understand the situation. If these people had magic tools like that and enough manpower, transmitting information would be easy, even in such an isolated environment.
However, the problem was...
“Why are they going this far to catch you?”
Erwen had done nothing wrong. So, why were they working so hard to chase after this victim?
“Is it to keep you quiet?”
“...I don’t think it’s just that.”
“There’s more?”
“Well, it’s because...”

Erwen, who had been answering my questions straightforwardly, hesitated to speak this time. If she was going to act like that, there was no way I could help. At least that was what I was thinking when she finally answered.
“W-When I first escaped, I swung my knife. But it happened to strike a not-so-nice location...”
“...Not-so-nice?”
Chills broke out all over my body. A breeze blew past my groin.
“You know, that—that area...?”
I was right.
“Ahem, anyway, from what the people chasing me have said, it was completely cut off, so it can’t even be reattached with a potion... I guess that’s why...”
I could understand now why their eyes were blazing with revenge.
“S-S-Sorry......”

But there was nothing to apologize for. Wasn’t he the one whose fault this was in the first place? It was karma. The problem was that there were way too many people in the world who didn’t understand that simple logic.
“Mister, I think we have someone following us.”
“What?”
“Don’t look back.”
I concentrated on trying to hear them, but I couldn’t hear anything.
“The distance... they’re about 150 yards away,” she said.
That was a strange distance to be able to sense someone’s presence from, but it didn’t seem like a lie. There was no reason for her to lie.
So, was this an elf’s keen senses at work?
Suddenly, her estimation went up in my eyes.
“We need to speed up, is that okay?”
“Yes. I can still take it.”
Even though her white bandage was stained red from her wound, Erwen did not utter a single pained sound. She showed great determination. It challenged my view of her.
“How far is the pursuer?”
“...They’re still about 150 yards away.”

Even though I had increased our speed, the distance between us had not changed. That wasn’t good. By now, our pursuer was no doubt announcing our location to their allies with the message stone or something.
Get rid of them.

If I were the one they were targeting, I would have certainly decided to do just that. But I was still just running. Once I killed one of them, I would no longer be able to get out of this. So, I needed to confirm some things before I made the call.
“M-Mister...?”
How much risk would I take on, and what could I get in return? I needed more detailed information.
“Erwen.”
“Y-Yes?”
“What are you good at?”
“I am confident in my laundry and cleaning skills. I-I can’t really cook, but...”
What is she talking about?
“When you’re in battle!”
“A-Archery! Oh, and elemental magic too!”
A standard elven archer.
“Type?”
“...Fire.”
Hmm, that was the rarest type of magic. Thanks to that, I could now picture her skillset in my head.
“Have you ever killed anyone?”
“No... But I could.”
That was something you could only think you knew about yourself.

“I see.” I finally asked her. “Erwen, would you like to be my comrade? Our party will last until we get out of the labyrinth, and the loot distribution will be nine to one, nine for me and one for you.”
“Y-Yes!”
And that gave me all the reason I needed.
“I promise in the name of my clan.”
“I also swear on the honor of a warrior.”
We stamped something as a token of trust just like before and upgraded our relationship from night companions to temporary party members.
All while, of course, running like crazy.
“Distance?”
“About one hundred yards!”
Even at my maximum speed, the distance between us and them was getting smaller. I made up my mind.
“We’ll escape into the outskirts.”
“Okay!”
I turned us around and entered the dark passageways. The crystals that shone on the walls and ceilings became fewer and fewer, and, before long, a pitch-black darkness fell upon us.
I was feeling mixed emotions. After all, I hadn’t thought I’d come back here voluntarily.
“Erwen, summon a spirit.”
A flame the size of a watermelon floated in the palm of her hand, illuminating our surroundings. Keeping an eye on the floor, we quickly made our way through the darkness.
And then...
“Unsummon it.”
We hid in the dark.
“Presence?”
“Soon you will be able to hear it too.”
“I see.”

I kept as quiet as I could and focused my attention on listening. The best-case scenario was for our pursuer to miss us and pass us by. Then, there would be no need to kill them, and I would be able to back out of this deal too.
Tap-tap-tap-tap-tap.

Before long, I could hear the sprinting tracker’s footsteps even with my own ears. However, despite what I was hoping, they didn’t pass us by. The sound of their footsteps stopped just in front of the crossroads we had just turned at.
Shit!
It seemed the tracker had a method of tracking us down. Smell, sound, or perhaps even something magical.
Tap. Tap. Tap.
They turned and walked slowly toward us, stopping at a distance of about thirty yards, right at the border where the abyss-like darkness began.
He stuck his head in and looked around. We held our breath inside the darkness and watched.

“There you are,” the man murmured to himself after sniffing a few times into the quiet stillness. Then, he pulled something out of his pocket. It was an item I had never seen before in my life, but I intuitively recognized its function.
A message stone.
The moment I spotted the item, I sent a signal by mouthing a word at Erwen, who had been aiming her arrow, the bowstring pulled taut, this entire time.
“Shoot.”
Swooo... Shawnnk—
Before I could even finish my message, the arrow was embedded in the man’s forehead.
Thunk.
Even though the man lay dead on the ground, I did not move right away. Next to me, I could feel an uncontrollable trembling from Erwen.
“Good job. If you had hesitated, things would have been dangerous.”

This was not an empty compliment, but the truth. Hadn’t I also hesitated when I slammed the shield down? Erwen hadn’t even had time for that. Even if I hadn’t told her that, she knew it herself. She could not have hesitated.
“Get some rest.”
The words of comfort ended there. I left the darkness and searched the body. Perhaps he had left his backpack behind to move quickly because our pursuer was only modestly equipped.
The fact that I’m feeling disappointment right now must mean I’ve fully assimilated into this world.
First, after removing all of the tracker’s equipment from head to toe, I organized the acquired items one by one.
A belt, a leather shirt and bottoms, two daggers, a fairly heavy pouch of mana stones, a potion bottle that was kept in a bottle tied to his belt, and even a message stone.
After the rough inventory was complete, I called Erwen.
“Good. Come here.”
Then I removed her bandages and treated her wound using the potion. The wound began to heal with a sizzling sound.
It was okay to make noise at this point, but Erwen clenched her teeth and endured it silently.
So this woman also has a tough side. Or maybe she’s just lost it?
I hoped it was the former. I was not confident in my abilities as a therapist.
“Are you feeling better?”
“Yes. Much better.”
“Then change into this.”
After a few minutes of treating the wound, I held out the leather shirt and bottoms I had just obtained. I judged that they were much more practical than loose-fitting clothes.
“Let me go put it on.”

Maybe she had decided that following my instructions was the best way to keep herself alive. They might have been uncomfortable, but Erwen immediately picked up the clothes and stepped into the dark to change.
“It’s a little big. Come here.”
I cut the excess fabric at the arms and legs for her.
“Wear this too. It will be a little better.”

It looked a little baggy overall, but it looked quite comfortable with the belt on. However, because of the change in clothes, she gave off a completely different vibe. Previously, she had looked like an elven girl on an outing, but now she looked like a full-fledged female warrior. Even her face.
“...It feels very strange.”
“You will get used to it.”
“Will I...?”
“Yes, you will.”
I shoved all of the other items into my backpack and dragged the naked corpse into the dark. Then, I held the message stone in my hand.
“How do you use this?”
“Just a moment. I’ll try.”
Erwen looked at the message stone and then clicked something.
“...Serdin was chasing the elf bitch and barbarian, but we’ve lost contact. Anyone who receives this message, gather in the goblin zone.”
So far, this was all going how I had expected it to.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: 2nd Floor (1)
paragraphs: My description was shared over the transmission.
“It is possible that they have split up by now. If you see a barbarian wielding a one-handed hammer and a shield, don’t hurry to approach him and instead wait for reinforcements.”
It wasn’t detailed, but it didn’t matter. There were probably no other barbarians wielding a shield here.
“Mister...”
Erwen looked up at me with anxious eyes. I smirked, knowing what she was thinking.
“Don’t worry. I’m not going to leave you.”
I had already decided to help Erwen. The reason was simple. I had always loved helping people in trouble... if it was beneficial to me.
“As I said before, we’ll split the loot nine to one. All right?”
“Of course. I will definitely repay the favor.”
Favor...
“Yes, please pay it back.”
If she wanted to repay it, there was no reason for me to refuse. Although I wasn’t expecting much in return.
“Yes, I promise...”
Erwen clenched her fists with determination in her eyes, and I tightened the laces of my boots and prepared to move.
“So what are we going to do now?” she asked.
“First, we’ll move through the outskirts. Summon the spirit again. We’ll talk about the rest on our way.”
“Okay.”
As we walked through the darkness with a fist-sized flame as a lantern, I confirmed a few more things.
“Exactly how long can spirits be summoned for?”
“If I’m using one to light up the surroundings, it can last for a good ten hours.”
“How long will it take you to recover afterward?”
“Two hours of rest should be enough.”
“I see.”
The situation was a lot better than I had thought. If all went to plan, we would be able to escape from them without facing any danger. Then I would reap the benefits of taking this risk.
“Mister?”
While I was organizing my thoughts, Erwen spoke to me.
“May I ask where we are going now?”
Oh, right. I didn’t mention that.
“The second floor.”
“Sorry...?”
Don’t give me that look. You heard it right.
“We’ll go to the second floor.”
“You and I, just the two of us?”
“Yeah, you and me.”

It was not that we had no other options, but rather that this was something I had been thinking about for a while. On the first floor, even if the two of us worked together, our profits would only decrease. However...
If we were on the second floor, that would be a different story.
“Um... M-Mister? The second floor is completely different from the first floor. You know that, right...?”
“I know.”
The three or four monsters that appeared at once on the first floor increased to ten on the second, and other random species, even high-rank monsters, could appear.
“But, if we stay in the first section, we will be fine. We mesh quite well.”
“Y-You and I do?”

I didn’t know why that was so surprising—melee tanks and ranged damage dealers were a good combination. It was for that reason that I had been thinking about going upstairs with Erwen from early on. There, even if we split the mana stones in half, our income would increase significantly. But since there had been no way for me to get past the darkness, I had previously discarded this idea.
“N-No matter how hard I think about it, it feels like walking into an orc’s den to avoid a goblin...”

Well, given her current reaction, it seemed that even if I had known about her fire abilities and made the offer, she would have flat-out rejected it. Right now, the situation was completely different from before.
“So, do you have any other plans? As you know, those guys are all over the first floor.”

Erwen now had a reason to go to the second floor, and I was able to use that opportunity to raise the ratio to 9:1. Of course, that didn’t mean the decision was made entirely without emotional considerations.
The message stone sounded again.
“Whoever catches that elf bitch will be given ten thousand mana stones and the opportunity to enjoy her first.”

I didn’t like these kinds of bastards. No, it was more hatred than dislike. But what if I could give these bastards the middle finger, earn a reward bigger than the risk, and even get the self-satisfaction of doing something good? Wasn’t that the epitome of efficiency?
“I will give you a chance to decide. What will you do?”
“I’ll go with you...”
Erwen reluctantly nodded. It seemed that the transmission from the message stone just now had played a decisive role in her decision.
Nice timing.
“Then let’s keep moving.”
“...But do you know the way to the second floor?”
“I don’t know the precise location.”
“Sorry?”
“Don’t worry, though. If we keep moving north, we’ll get there at some point.”

It wasn’t wishful thinking, but the truth. If you stuck to one direction as you moved through the darkness, you would reach the portal one way or another because this darkness was like a passageway pointing upstairs. But it was also a maze-like structure, so we’d probably stumble through it.
It was worth the effort.
“It’s a goblin trap!”
As we were walking, we saw a trap. It was much further into the passage than I expected. Originally, one would have appeared a lot earlier.
...Maybe there weren’t many goblins where there was no light? Like in the game? If that was the case... my heart tightened.
How unlucky was I to have fallen into darkness immediately and met a goblin right away?
“I will deal with it! You rest!”
Seeing this as an opportunity to appeal to me, Erwen stepped in front of me.
“I’m just telling you just in case, but don’t use any spirits.”
“...O-Of course I wasn’t going to!”
With a flustered look that said otherwise, Erwen approached the trap. And...
“Grk!”
The moment the goblin popped out, she fired an arrow that was already knocked on the bow from a very close range.
Stab—!
Oh, she kind of looked like Legolas there. She had much better technique than I had expected, and she was also quite agile when she moved.
“What do you think?”
After she killed the goblin, Erwen looked at me with a pleased expression on her face.
“If you were alone, would you have used a spirit?”
“Good job. After seeing you use a bow, I can see you really are an elf.”
Erwen looked shy and happy. Was it that nice to be acknowledged? To be honest, some of that was subtle sarcasm. Not the part about her skills, but the jab at her personality.
“But I will fight the battles from now on. It would be best to conserve arrows as much as possible.”
“Oh, I can just pick them up and use them again. There is no need to even pull them out.”
Erwen bent over and returned with a mana stone and an arrow. The arrow was in good shape with no visible damage.
“I see...”
What an embarrassment. In the game, arrows were disposable items that disappeared with each shot. To make up for that, you could carry a thousand of them per compartment.
“Here!”
Erwen held out a small hand.
“Take it! When you have nine, I get one, right? I will work hard! Then I can earn a little too, right? I promised to buy something for my younger sibling when I return!”
Uh, ah, um...
“Yeah, work hard...”
What was this? Subtle sarcasm?
We quickly moved northward in the dark and continued taking care of goblins from time to time. Then, after it had been quiet for some time, a voice came through the message stone.
“I have an update. Harts, who was attacked by the elf, said that he would raise the bounty to twenty thousand mana stones. Dead or alive.”
That meant the bastards were within three hundred yards of us.
Almost on instinct, Erwen closed in next to me.
“Relax. No one will come here with a torch to find us.”
“Really?”
“Yes.”

In fact, I was nearly certain. What I had realized while listening in on the conversations on the message stone was that these guys were like a group of delinquents loitering around. It didn’t seem like the guild was well-organized. Presumably, at best, they just served as a convenient community for each other. The first floor was a place where a group of more than five people could not actually work together anyway.
The message stone rang out with more transmissions from the guild members.
“I’m planning to move to another area to hunt Blade Wolves. Is there anyone who wants to join? No transmission required.”
“I’m tired, so I’m looking for someone to rest with. Come to the pond next to the big rock. No transmission required.”
In fact, as we moved through this tunnel, we heard these kinds of transmissions from all over. That meant that there were people who didn’t care about the chase at all, bounty or not.
However, I did not relax.
It wasn’t that things had gone wrong—it was that things were going too smoothly.
God damn it...
That was the way my life always unfolded. Something bad always happened right about now, and the fact that it was quiet made me even more anxious.
“Mister!”
“What?”
“There, it’s a ghoul!”
I didn’t see it. As I cocked my head, Erwen moved the flame forward.
...You really do have good eyes.

It was then that the form of a ghoul entered my line of sight. Rotten skin, empty eye sockets, sharp and long nails reminiscent of claws, and even four legs with a humanoid form. It was the same as the illustration I had seen on the loading screen.
However, something was off...
What? Why is there a ghoul here?
On the first floor, the type of monsters that appeared was different based on location—east, west, north, and south. The ghouls appeared in the southern region.
Had we reached the border while we were wandering? Well, maybe. We had been headed north, but when we came to a dead end, we ended up going in circles. I’d have to figure it out later, though.
“...Should I fight alone again this time?”

Erwen, who had been full of determination while fighting the goblin, now made it very obvious that she didn’t want to fight. Was she scared because it was her first time seeing this type of monster? This woman was quite quirky.
“I will take the lead. You take care of the one in the back.”
“Okay!”
Having come up with a rough strategy, I moved forward slowly. There were a total of three ghouls blocking the passageway, and they were all sitting like dogs.
Step.
Even though I had gotten pretty close, the ghouls didn’t move. Hmm, in the game, you had to get within a certain range for them to attack you first. Could it be the same here?
Step.
As I carefully took one more step forward, the three ghouls ran toward me at the same time.
“Grghghgh!”
The sound they made was similar to that of a goblin. Was it because ghouls were a tier-nine monster as well? Talk about no personality.
“Hiya!”
Rather than retreating, I took a step closer and pounded the ghoul in the head with my hammer.
[Hammer Smash.]
Crunch!
The moment one ghoul’s head had been crushed, an arrow fired from somewhere behind me hit another ghoul.
Thunk!
She seemed to really like the forehead.
Then, after knocking back a charging ghoul once with my shield, the battle ended easily with another [Hammer Smash.]
[You have defeated the ghouls. EXP +1]

The battle had ended in an instant, but I still took a brief moment to review it. In terms of combat power, ghouls were superior to goblins. They were a lot stronger and faster. The goblins had traps, but well... if a moron stepped on them, it was their own fault.
...Assuming, of course, there was light around.
“Still, this is better than a goblin.”
“Pardon? Why?”
“Because it takes time to catch goblins.”

As long as you didn’t get knocked prone in an all-out battle, hunting ghouls seemed more efficient than fighting goblins in many ways. At least these guys didn’t set one trap on the ground and stupidly wait around nearby. It was also a huge advantage that they didn’t attack unless they were approached first.
“Next time, it would be more efficient to start by taking one ghoul down first with an arrow.”
“Okay. That sounds good.”
After briefly establishing a strategy for future battles, I collected the mana stones that had fallen on the ground and put them in my pocket.
“Um, mister...?”
“What is it?”
“I-It’s just that— it’s now my turn to take one...”
“Ah, that’s right.”
We continued down the tunnel.
My prediction that we were near the border was correct. For a while, the ghouls and the goblins alternated, but as we continued northward, we were back to only seeing goblins.
How long has it been?
It was already nearing the end of the third day. After taking a break for about four hours along the way, we found something on the route north. A dark red line was drawn on the ground.
“Uh, a bloodstain? I don’t think it’s from a goblin. Who could it be?”
...Somehow, I felt like I knew its owner.
As we walked, we also saw pieces of bread that had been dropped at regular intervals. With confidence, I continued to follow the bloodstains.
“Um, you haven’t said anything in a while...”
Ten minutes passed.
“Are you mad at me, by any chance?”
Thirty minutes passed.
“Pardon? Mister?”
Two hours passed. After walking that long path, I finally came across a sandal abandoned on the ground. The curses came to me instantly.
“Fuck, are you kidding me?”
“I-I’m sorry! For whatever I did!”
There had been a portal right under my nose.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 2nd Floor (2)
paragraphs: I had almost expected the portal to appear here. It was obvious.

The fact that I had run into the blond’s party, a group of top-class adventurers, was a strong indication that the portal to the second floor was located in the direction I had originally come from. That was why I had followed the bloodstain with confidence.
But I hadn’t expected it to turn out this way. To think there had been a portal less than ten yards from my starting position.
You’re kidding.
Memories of crawling through these halls on three legs unfolded before me like a panorama.
How unlucky can I be A few steps in the opposite direction and I would have activated the portal and secured a light source. Had I done that, I could have avoided that damn trap!
Mister, please speak to me. Don’t just make that scary face. If I did something wrong, I’ll fix it...
What is she talking about Oh, it’s because of me. That’s annoying, let’s just make up an excuse.
Don’t worry. I was just reminded of something that happened earlier.
Oh...
Erwen looked at me and seemed relieved. Then, her gaze shifted to pity. I couldn’t believe it.
The bloodstains, the pieces of bread, the sandals, and the look on my face. Had she inferred what had happened during my first day in the labyrinth from these details alone
I’m sure this person is in a better place now.
Of course she hadn’t. I had had faith in her.
Yeah... thanks.

Judging from what she had said, she probably thought I was mourning the death of a comrade. But I didn’t feel the need to correct her. It was too long a story to explain. Mostly, if I started talking about it, I felt like my rage would get the best of me.
So I decided to just bury it away.
Are you ready to go upstairs
Honestly, I’m still scared, but for some reason, I feel like I won’t die if I’m with you.
Then again, this woman had a strange way of dragging out simple sentences. Just say yes if that’s what you mean.
Then let’s go.
Okay...
The moment I entered the portal with Erwen, our surroundings were dyed a pure white not unlike the light that was emitted from a monitor.
Flash!
It had only been four days since I had entered the labyrinth.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
And I had reached the second floor.
If anyone asked me how I felt right now, I’d answer like this I feel like I just got spat out of the mouth of a giant frog who was using me as a chew toy.
Ahh!
Our bodies flew through the air like we had bounced off of something. I didn’t scream out loud like Erwen, but in terms of outcome, she was a lot better off than me.
Thud!
While I landed on my butt with a blunt thump, Erwen quickly regained her balance and landed without a problem.
Wow, that was a surprise. My sisters didn’t tell me about that.
I was realizing once again how physically fit this woman was. She had an agility that a barbarian could never have.
Mister, is this the second floor
Yes.
Um, I never heard anyone mention it’s a forest. Are you sure
Perhaps the information you heard was referring to another second floor.
Another second floor
Do elves not share information about the labyrinth with each other Why don’t you know this
There are four portals on the first floor—one in the east, another in the west, another in the south, and another in the north—and each connects to a different region.
Ah, I think I did hear about that!
...I guess she just forgot.
As I looked at her like a hopeless fool, Erwen, startled, blurted out the first thing that came to mind.
Oh! The third floor! I heard that no matter which route you take on the second floor, everything is connected again on the third floor. Right
It seemed like she wanted to show off her knowledge. When I nodded back approvingly, Erwen smiled with satisfaction. Slowly, I was getting a sense of how to deal with her.
Now, what do we do
Wait. I’m thinking.

First, I carefully studied the terrain. It was necessary to note which things were different from the game and which were the same. Things that couldn’t be seen through a monitor. For example, the fact that we had just flown about three yards while jumping through the portal.
Hmm.
First, I scanned our surroundings once more.

Behind us was a portal that could be used to go down to the first floor at any time, and there were no living creatures within a radius of about fifty yards. Well, I couldn’t speak for what was in the trees beyond the field.
Is there anything I can do to help
Quiet.

The second floor was a forest map. The surrounding area was as dark as night, but thanks to the lights scattered in the sky like the Milky Way, visibility was secured... to a certain extent. It was about as bright as an alleyway without the street lights. However, even as time passed and it became daytime, it would not get any brighter. After all, this was a labyrinth, and the thing above us was not actually the sky, but a high ceiling. However, there were floors where the sky and sun really did exist.
Let’s move slowly.
Pardon Where are we going
To explore the nearby area.

I had mapped out a rough plan back on the first floor. However, there were a few things that needed to be confirmed to determine whether this plan would actually work. So, I started with what I could see...
Bam—!
Erwen was startled when I suddenly swung my hammer at a tree on the outskirts of the clearing.
What—what are you doing
Checking to see if it is possible to knock down a tree.
Why are you checking that
I was thinking of building a barricade around the portal.
Oh, I see.
Only then did Erwen nod her head in agreement. It was very annoying to have to answer each of her questions.
Anyway, I’m giving up on that plan.
Erwen didn’t ask why because she had eyes too. Even after I had hit the tree with all my might, the tree bark was just slightly chipped.
How was this a tree It was more like a boulder.
So, what’s the next plan
Search this area as planned. And from now on, you take the lead.
...Me
I decided not to take any more questions.
Your job is to go ahead of me and find traps. And pay attention to potential enemies and be on the lookout as much as possible. You have these two jobs.
...You want to divide up the work. All right.
Surprisingly, Erwen accepted the role assigned to her without complaint. So why was I disappointed Was it because I had already planned what I would say to convince her
I forgot how much I missed being in a forest until we got here. Even though the only things in this forest are monsters.
Erwen walked through the forest, saying things that I couldn’t relate to at all.
Ah, there don’t seem to be any traps, but just in case, please follow in my footsteps.
What was this Suddenly, I felt reassured that this woman was here. She was even taking big strides forward like she wasn’t afraid of any traps.
Before long, Erwen murmured something.
It’s a trap.
It was invisible to my eyes.
Look over there and you will see something hidden under the leaves, she said.
But no matter how she tried to describe it, it was invisible to me.
A moment later, Erwen looked at me as if to say, Why can’t you see this and threw a stone.
Clamp—!

She was right. How could she have detected that from that distance when it was so dark Even though I had already known that she had a detection ability as an elf, seeing it with my own two eyes was fascinating. There was a reason why she could walk forward so confidently.
What do you think
You seem to be good at throwing stones.
...Is that all
What else do you need
Erwen’s shoulders, which had been lifted in anticipation, drooped down. This was the perfect time to give her a carrot. Subtle, so as not to be too obvious.
Finding traps was an ability I was expecting you to have from the beginning. You are already a full-fledged adventurer. Don’t get too excited about something this basic.
Hmmm...

Although she feigned nonchalance, I could clearly see the slight twitch of her shoulders from the back. Thanks to that, I knew I had totally gotten the hang of this. I just had to deal with her like this from now on.
Are you saying that I’m at least pulling my own weight As a full-fledged adventurer
Yes.
The mana stone distribution was still 91, but the variation of the every warrior must do their share motto that my chieftain particularly seemed to favor had worked out better than I expected.
But it’s strange. No matter how hard I listen for them, it doesn’t seem like there are goblins here.

That was to be expected. The second floor was different from the first floor. Goblins were not always nearby just because there was a trap. It was easier to view the traps on the second floor simply as a part of the landscape.
Stop chatting and focus.
Okay.
I refocused on our peaceful surroundings and scoured the area. The place where we currently were had been called the Goblin Forest in the game.

The other key characteristic of this area other than the traps was that goblins appeared in groups of fifteen or so. Occasionally, variations of goblin, such as goblin swordsmen or goblin archers, also appeared. Of course, the number of variants increased in the outskirts, and higher-rank monsters appeared as well. But that was something we didn’t have to worry too much about as we were only going to cover the area near the portal.
There is nothing nearby for now.
We finished searching a radius of about two hundred yards around the portal.
There were countless traps, but no goblins to be found.
What should we do
First, we disable all of the traps in this area and gradually increase our range.

We slowly expanded our territory by disabling traps using stones thrown from a distance. This would allow us to, in the case of danger, escape to the first floor. If we stepped on a trap while running away, there would be trouble.
Once we had expanded our radius to over five hundred yards, Erwen stopped moving and whispered, Mister.
I held my breath too.
It’s a group of goblins.
How many
I don’t know. There definitely seems to be over ten...
Distance
About fifty yards. I don’t think they’ve noticed we’re here yet. What do we do
Isn’t that obvious
Fight, I said confidently.

Erwen didn’t argue. Although it was a little scary, she also knew that there was no choice but to fight. After all, if she hadn’t wanted to fight, she shouldn’t have entered the labyrinth in the first place.
How much closer can we get without being detected
I think I can go thirty yards on my own. Anything more than that will be too close. Goblins have a more sensitive sense of smell than I thought.
I see.
After a brief deliberation, I decided to go ahead with the plan I had mentioned earlier. At this, Erwen also slowly walked through the bushes in the direction of the goblins.
That was the advantage of being an elf. It was amazing that she didn’t so much as rustle a leaf while walking through the bushes.
Soon, Erwen stopped advancing. Then she glanced back at me. When I nodded, she turned around, nocked an arrow on the bow, and shot it.
Swiiish.
Was it a bullseye I didn’t know. It was so far away that I couldn’t even hear the arrow hitting the target. I hoped she had pierced the forehead again.
Thud, thud, thud.
Once the arrow was fired, I ran straight to Erwen.
Grk!
Grghghgh!
Even as the goblins rushed toward her in a frenzy, Erwen calmly prepared the second arrow.
Whiiishh!
I thought so every time, but the speed at which she shot her arrows was insane. I hadn’t noticed these little things while playing the game.
Thunk—!
A goblin that was running forward fell down. It got hit in the neck, not the forehead.
Well, even if she was an elf, it must have been difficult to accurately hit a moving creature from a distance.
Erwen, step back.
Okay!

Erwen stepped back without hesitation and disappeared from my line of sight. Now all I could see were the goblins rushing toward me. The number was three times the number of the goblins that you saw on the first floor.
They may have just been goblins, but they were a little daunting in numbers like this... But surprisingly, I felt no fear.
Instead...
Babum-babum-babum.
The warrior’s heart in this body pounded aggressively and sparked a rage in my head.
Grk, Grk!
Grghghgh!
Hearing the menacing, howling shouts of numerous goblins, I shouted back, SPARTAAA—!
Bring it on, assholes!

chapters.title: Chapter 13: 2nd Floor (3)
paragraphs: The total number of goblins charging toward me was nine: eight regular goblins and one goblin swordsman. But, although it was called a “swordsman,” it was holding a scimitar that was only about two feet long. Compared to carving knives, it was definitely a long blade.
“Grghghgh!”
As a goblin charged out in front of the others, I gripped the end of my hammer and slammed it down on its temple.
Whack—!
One shot, one kill. The goblin turned into a cluster of light and disappeared before even hitting the ground. However, it was too early to be pleased.
I had only killed one.
“Grghghgh!”

Immediately after, two goblins with carving knives in their hands simultaneously flew at me from opposite sides. I lunged to the right and shoved one back with my shield, then turned around and hammered the other.
Whack—!
That made two, but I didn’t even have time to catch my breath.
Having already reached my flank, another goblin drove in from behind. It was the goblin swordsman.
“Kyaaah!”
It made a snake-like sound typical of a swordsman. I immediately stopped moving and rolled onto the floor.
Whip—!
A knife passed just above me with a sharp ripping sound. The other goblins saw me roll to the ground and rushed in on cue.

This was why the second floor was several times more dangerous than the first floor. Four normal goblins could be subdued with brute strength, but with this many, it was impossible. There were bound to be injuries.
That is, if I was alone.
An arrow shot from within the bushes drilled through the forehead of one of the goblins. It seemed Erwen had taken up the sniper role once again.
Jump!
I used the resulting momentum from rolling on the ground to quickly stand up. Using the shield, I rushed into the middle of the enemy line. It was only natural for the warrior to be the tank.
“Come at me, you assholes!”

I blocked their attacks with my shield, swung my hammer, dodged, and kicked and head-butted the goblins away. While I was walking a tightrope with my boiling barbarian blood and running rampant in the middle of the goblins’ formation, Erwen took position again and fired arrows like crazy.
Whip, thunk! Thunk! Thunk!
The goblins were panicked by the arrows being fired every two or three seconds.
“G-Grk!”
But, because she was in a rush, the arrows didn’t always hit their vitals.
Thunk!

But they always managed to hit either the shoulder, arm, stomach, chest, or thigh. At times, it was clear that she was infusing the power of an elemental into her shots because the arrows were on fire. In order to not be outdone, I bashed the heads of the goblin bastards one by one while they were busy trying to avoid the arrows.
Whack! Whack!

Soon, when the number of goblins had decreased to two, they attempted to run away. I grabbed onto the head of one who was running like crazy, and the other was handled by Erwen launching an arrow into the back of its head.
[You have defeated the Goblin Swordsman. EXP +1]
When the battle was over, Erwen appeared from behind the bushes where she had been hiding and approached me.
“Are you hurt?”
“No. You?”
“Me neither.”
“Good. We’ll collect the mana stones, then.”

After that, we split into two groups and went around picking up arrows and mana stones. We had managed to defeat the goblin swordsman in the melee, but acquiring the scimitar was impossible. That was because the goblins’ clothes and weapons had also turned into light and disappeared just like on the first floor.
“Here are six.”

In total, we had harvested eleven mana stones, including two from the goblins that Erwen had killed with a surprise attack.
