Considering the fact that I had only collected forty-four mana stones after an entire day of walking around on day one, I was more than satisfied. That battle had been less than two minutes long.
“Here, take it.”
“Two? Thank you!”
I took nine and Erwen took two. This was because even though they were the same tier nine monsters, the stone from the swordsman had slightly more weight to it than that of the ordinary goblin.
“I guess we’ll keep proceeding like this?”
“Yes. Was there anything that made you feel uncomfortable or in danger during this battle?”
“No, not really.”

After that, I took time to review the battle and identify areas of improvement in our fighting method. I wasn’t able to find anything to fix at the moment, but that was proof that we were still new to this.
As the number of battles increased and our experience accumulated, we would naturally get better and better.
“Okay, then let’s move on.”
“Okay!”
I checked the time one last time.
How much can I expect to earn by the end of day four?
We continued to move by expanding our radius around the portal. After increasing the radius by more than two miles, we began encountering groups of goblins about once every five minutes.
And naturally, we ran into a goblin archer.
“Kikikiki!”

The goblin archer, who made a slightly more distinctive sound than ‘Grk,’ was definitely a menacing opponent. It used a small wooden bow reminiscent of a harp as a weapon, and like other goblin weapons, the arrowheads were poisoned. The archer even knew how to use stealth magic.
However...
[You have defeated the Goblin Archer. EXP +1]
As long as I was paying attention, this barbarian body would react to all flying arrows, making it possible for me to dodge or block them with a shield. Well, I still needed to be careful, though.
“There is one more goblin archer! Get rid of it first!”
“Okay!”
I may have been a barbarian, but an arrow in the head would still mean instant death for me. When I got back to the city, I’d have to make the first thing I did was buy a helmet.
“Let’s rest for a while.”
“Ha! Finally!”
After finishing one more battle, we moved to the empty clearing near the portal and rested.
“You can sleep first if you want.”
“Really?”
This woman really didn’t know how to turn down an offer. As I nodded my head with a smirk, Erwen dropped down to the ground and glanced at me like an expectant puppy.
“Um, what about the backpack and blanket?”
“...Here.”
I set down the bag, which had gotten a lot heavier, and took out the blanket to place over her body. Then, less than a minute later, she began to snore.
Zzz—

Compared to the traditional barbarian style of snoring, it was definitely a small and gentle sound. She must’ve been really tired—up to now, Erwen hadn’t made a sound in her sleep. Well, maybe it was because she felt more psychologically secure now than she had back then.
We hunted around the goblin forest for about fifteen hours.

Although we had to fight more than ten each time, the more we got the hang of it, the less dangerous the battles became and the faster they went. As a result, we were able to turn a profit that would have been unimaginable on the first floor. But there were also moments of high tension.
“Phew...”

As the cleared radius around the portal increased, we began to come across other adventurers. So far, there had been a total of eleven encounters. They had all been groups of three or more people, and sometimes there had been parties with someone of a fantasy race on them. Each time we crossed paths with these groups, we both distanced ourselves and passed by, as was customary, but each time, weariness came along as a companion.
I was more afraid of the adventurers than the goblins. Especially now, because there was a reason to be even more vigilant.
“The problem is that she’s too pretty.”

I looked at Erwen, who was sound asleep, and sighed. Even though she had been homeless for several days, her silver hair was still shiny, her amber eyes lured people in, and her facial features were those of a beautiful woman.

As a woman, these would be good things... but as an adventurer, I wasn’t sure. In fact, in the parties of adventurers we had encountered, there had been some creepy bastards who had licked their lips as soon as they had seen Erwen.
I hoped I didn’t have to worry about anything bad happening...
“Am I that pretty?”
What the fuck? You were just snoring.
“Go to sleep.”
“Okay.”
She seemed to have said that in her sleep, because she answered quickly and immediately started snoring again.
Zzz...
What is up with her?
The elves I had heard of were not like this.
Day four, day five, day six...
After entering the Goblin Forest, time flew by quickly, and soon it was the start of the seventh day. The day had finally come to leave the labyrinth.
“When I get back, the first thing I’m going to do is sleep...”
“Same here.”
There was only one way to leave the labyrinth and return to the city—waiting for the floor to close.

At a set time, the labyrinth would spit out the adventurers on a certain floor back into the city. It was 168 hours for the first floor and 240 hours for the second floor. The higher the number of floors you climbed, the longer you could be active in the labyrinth. However, we planned to head down to the first floor and leave for the city just before the end of the seventh day.
“Today, we won’t go as far as yesterday, and only move in the area.”
“Okay!”
There were several good reasons to leave early.
For one, when the first floor closed, the portal would also disappear. That meant that there would be no way for us to retreat in case of unforeseen circumstances.
Food was also slowly running low. We had the option of buying food in exchange for mana stones from the adventurers we occasionally came across, but...
There is no need to overdo it.

Above all, we had no more than ten usable arrows left. No matter how sturdily the arrows were crafted, they were consumable items and therefore losing them was inevitable. If they had been regular arrows made of wood back on Earth, they would not have been reusable in the first place. I was once again reminded that I was inside a different world.
After that, we continued hunting for a while before I checked the time and paused.
“Let’s return now, just in case.”
“Okay!”
Currently, we were at a point about two and a half miles away from the portal. At most, it would take forty minutes for us to reach the portal.
Of course, that would leave us some time to spare, but... it would set me more at ease if we headed down early rather than late.
I also had something to discuss with Erwen before we parted.
“Look out. Another trap has been set.”
We were going back the way we came, but at some point, a trap had been planted in the forest again.
That meant the goblins had respawned.

Well, just because it was a respawn, that didn’t mean they suddenly appeared out of thin air like in the game. In the forest, you often saw things that looked like rabbit holes. The goblins always crawled out of those.

Once, I had tried waiting in front of one and had even used Erwen to start a fire, but nothing had happened. I couldn’t check what lay at the bottom either because the whole thing collapsed soon after I started digging.
Erwen was walking in front of me when she suddenly stopped.
“A group of goblins at one o’clock about seventy yards away. Eight ordinary ones, two swordsmen, and two archers.”
Now that she was used to it, she provided a perfect report without even being asked.
“Are we going to fight?”
“Yes.”

Long conversations were not necessary. When I nodded, as usual, Erwen took the lead and cleared our way through the bushes. Then she stopped me with a hand gesture, moved about ten yards closer on her own, took a seat, and pulled back the bowstring.
Wheeesh!
The arrow flew forward.
Thunk!
It was probably the goblin archer who had been hit. After all, I had told her to make them her top priority whenever possible.
“Mister!”
“Okay, you move back now.”

Erwen shot one more arrow at the rushing goblins and then fell back. This maneuver was incredibly familiar to us by now. I ran forward and smashed the swordsman standing among the ordinary goblins with my hammer.
Whack—!
From the feedback I received from my hand, I knew there was no need to whack it twice.
“AHH!”
As I roared from the center of their formation, the goblins faltered.
Scared?
Whack—!
The moment the goblins hesitated, I dashed forward and shattered the other swordsman’s skull.
“Grghghgh!”
I had now mastered these kinds of dogfights after numerous battles. The same was true for Erwen.
Whiz! Thunk!

She had already taken position and had officially started raining down arrows. There had been times when our attacks overlapped and I almost got hit by an arrow, but those incidents had gradually disappeared. I had started to roughly predict who Erwen would prioritize and what to expect.
Well, the same went for her.
Whack—!

After less than a minute, the battle ended as I crushed the head of a goblin trying to escape. Earlier, I had heard that there were two goblin archers, but no arrows had flown toward me during the battle. It seemed Erwen’s first two surprise attacks had taken down the archers.
“Good job, Erwen.”
“Hehe.”
“But if you take care of all the archers, tell me. It’s annoying to keep worrying about them.”
“I wasn’t sure if the last arrow hit it or not.”
Hmm, that made sense. Inaccurate information could in turn be dangerous. She really had grown a lot.
I was pleased for some reason.
“Hurry, let’s take what we need and go.”
“Okay!”
After that, I was walking around to pick up mana stones when Erwen urgently called out to me.
“Mister! There is something strange here!”
I quickly headed over and saw a ball of light the size of a fist floating in the air. I knew what this was. It was the first time I was actually seeing it in real life, though...
“...It’s an essence. It’s definitely from that goblin archer.”
To be honest, there was a sour taste in my mouth as soon as I saw it.
Could we really be this lucky?
“E-E-Essence? This thing?”
“Yes. I’m certain.”
“Uh, uh, uh, what should we do?”
As you could tell by this reaction, essences were worth more than gold to an adventurer. This essence was similar to the one found in the skill system of Dungeon and Stone.
“I-If you eat this, do you turn into a goblin?”
“Unlikely. You only gain a fraction of the abilities that goblins possess.”
For example, the guy who tracked us down by our scent on the first floor had perhaps absorbed the [Essence of a Blade Wolf.]
“What do we do...?”
How many times are you going to ask the same question?
Although the ratio was 9:1, she seemed to covet this as well.
“Do you want it?” I asked.
“No, it’s not that. But... if you want me to have it, then, well...”
I had no reason not to let her have it, but why did it feel like she was getting more and more thick-skinned?
I smirked and spoke up.
“If you promise me one thing, I will give you the essence.”

The [Essence of a Goblin Archer] was not very attractive to me as a barbarian. It could potentially be of some use right now, but the total amount of essence that a character could absorb was fixed. If I wanted to get rid of it in the future, I’d end up spending a lot of money.
“...Really?”
“Yes.”
As I took in her wide eyes, a laugh slipped out. It was strange, though, even when I thought about it now.

The odds of an essence being dropped while hunting a monster were very low. But the [Essence of a Goblin Archer] appearing instead of that of a regular goblin? It would be wrong to call this beginner’s luck.
Is this how my bad luck turns around?
“I was planning on saying this when we were back on the first floor, but I’ll say it now. Erwen—”
“Hey, you guys! What are you doing?”
Damn it, right as I was feeling lucky.
Just as I was about to get Erwen to promise me something, we heard a shout in the distance.
“Don’t move!”

It was a party of four human adventurers. They had spotted us from afar and were now quickly closing the distance between us with hard expressions on their faces. To be honest, I knew this would happen.
“Mister?”
This was an appropriate development. Me? Lucky? No way. Ever since I was young, I had always been different. For me, luck had always been something you could only have when you earned it yourself.
“Erwen, prepare to fight.”
Just like now.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Return (1)
paragraphs: The moment Erwen nervously picked up an arrow, I shoved her forward.
“Eh?”
Erwen, who had been suddenly pushed from behind, stumbled forward, and in the process, the essence floating in the air came into contact with her skin.
Shaaa—!
The essence emitted a light and swirled into Erwen’s body.
“You crazy bastard!”
So, that was what those bastards were after.
“I said, don’t move!”
Soon, the group of four adventurers got within ten yards of us. But, look. The essence had already been absorbed by this elf. I hid my nerves and took an intimidating step forward.
“Why should I listen to you?”
“That essence was ours!”

I pictured a different scenario unfolding, one where I hadn’t fed Erwen the essence. They probably would have forced us to give it up on ridiculous grounds. They probably would have claimed they took the monster down themselves with a long-distance arrow or whatever excuse they planned to use.
“If you want to fight, go ahead. I’ll fight you as long as you want.”

Four against two. Although we were outnumbered, I firmly held my ground. To me, this was similar to when small dogs barked loudly in order to avoid fighting as much as possible. Humans were like animals in that when someone looked down on them, they’d bite.
The redhead, who seemed to be the leader of the group, silently clenched his teeth.
I was sure they had enough brains to think this through. It was not as if the essence was still floating in the air. Its owner had already been decided, so there was nothing to gain from fighting us.
So it would be wise to give up and go back—
“I demand compensation.”
—Or choose to whine.
Seeing the essence disappear in front of his eyes must’ve been a big disappointment. There was no reason for me to care about that, though.
“We took the essence that we earned. What compensation are you talking about?”
“Is there any evidence? That goblin was ours.”

I didn’t bother asking, “And do you have any proof of that?” It was obvious there was no such thing. There was no CCTV in the labyrinth. In the end, the words of the man with the most power became law.
“Again, if you want to fight, go ahead. I will not run away,” I replied stubbornly, leaving no room for debate.
If you’re going to attack, go ahead. If you’re just going to talk, don’t push it and get lost.
I didn’t even give them the time to think.
“I’ll give you three seconds. If you do not make a decision before that, we will consider you our enemy.”
“Mister...?”
Read the room, Erwen. Be quiet. Can’t you see that they’re all scared of how strong I’m coming across?
“Three. Two—”
“We will leave.”

The man made a choice before I could count to one. Seriously, if a tattooed barbarian of my size started counting down the seconds in front of me, I would have done the same. And if the essence was really theirs, their eyes would be burning with rage right about now. But they knew damn well that it was not theirs. Soon, they disappeared from our sight.
“Are they gone?”
“Yes. I think so.”
“We’ll speed up until we reach the portal. Take the lead.”
At my words, Erwen cleared the path at a speed not unlike someone on horseback. She also knew. Although the encounter had ended without bloodshed, it wasn’t over yet.
“Any sign of those guys?”
“I don’t sense anything. Oh, there’s a group of goblins at three o’clock, what should I do?”
“Ignore them.”
“Okay.”

Originally, I had planned to go back to leisurely hunting goblins on our way to the portal, but things had changed. We were going to get out of the second floor as soon as possible. And if we could manage it, get as far away from the portal as possible once we were on the first floor.
Hearing my plan, Erwen tilted her head.
“Would they really follow us to the first floor?”
“They’re not following us. It’s just that our destination is the same.”
“What does that mean?”

It was a simple guess. They were a party of four. This was more than enough people to be active on the first area of the second floor. But, they had been moving toward the entrance rather than the outskirts. Their intention was clear.
“It’s very likely they’re planning on returning to the first floor on the seventh day to then return to the city. Which is why we ran into them back there.”

To put it simply, like us, these guys were a ragtag bunch who were only on the second floor to get a taste of it. That was why, even though they had doubled our numbers, they had gotten scared and ran. It was possible they were not even a proper party but just a group of people who had met by coincidence on the first floor.
“I see...”
At my next words, Erwen quietly nodded. Though I didn’t know if she actually understood.
“You really are amazing!”
...I guess she didn’t.
“I will only do what you tell me to do!”
Well, that was probably for the best. Letting someone turn the rusty gears in their head was bound to lead to more trouble.
“Mister, it’s a goblin!”
“Avoid it.”
“But it looks like they have already found us. They’re running this way right now!”
“What?”

As soon as I heard that, I felt a sense of despair. From the fourth day until now, the goblins had never detected us first. In that sense, Erwen’s sensing ability was excellent. Even though we were currently running somewhere, this could not be a coincidence.
Plus, she had just absorbed an essence.
“Detour in the opposite direction for now.”
“Okay!”
At my instruction, Erwen turned.
And right at that moment—
Whip!
An arrow hurtled from the direction we had turned away from. As soon as I saw this, I grabbed Erwen from behind.
“Eek!”
Erwen groaned as her airway was pressed in, but... choking for a short while was better than getting impaled in the neck.
Bam!

As soon as I picked Erwen up and used the shield to cover my upper body, the arrow bounced off of it. But although it bounced off at an angle, it still felt solid against the shield. Could it have been that bastard with the crossbow earlier?
“I-I could have... a-avoided it on my...”
Erwen squeaked something.
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the time to listen to you.
“Just run.”
I started running with Erwen taking the lead again.
“Mister, if an arrow flies again, you don’t need to pull me like—”
“Be quiet. I’m thinking,” I said in a low voice, and Erwen shut her mouth.

I kept thinking it through as we ran, and stayed aware of my surroundings. I didn’t know how they had done it, but those guys had lured the goblins here. Then, they ambushed us from the opposite direction and tried to trap us.
Even if we escape, will we be able to safely reach the portal? No way.
I tried to calculate the possibility that we would reach the portal, but I knew it was extremely low. They had a crossbow, and the goblins would continue to pursue us as well.
If we were lucky, we might be able to get out of this alive despite all of this... But, I knew I wasn’t going to be the lucky one in this situation.
“We have to fight.”
We had time to take a few breaths. In that time, I came to a conclusion.
“Erwen, use your powers.”
“Powers?”
“Use the power of the essence.”
The essences contained the special abilities of each monster they dropped from.
For example:
[Goblin Archer]
[Agility: +2
Flexibility: +4
Vision: +6
Smell: +2
Perception: +2
Cognitive Interference: +6
Accuracy: +8
Poison Resistance: +4
Obsession: +7
(P) Poison Arrow — When using a bow, you deal poison damage.
(A) Thief Step — You can enter stealth mode.]
In the game, the information had been displayed like that. Increased stats, and one passive (P) and one active (A) ability.

This information would also apply in this world. There had been some differences so far such as the monsters, starting points, etcetera, but this part at least had always been consistent with the game.
“B-But I don’t know how to use it...”
Erwen was startled by my unreasonable request. I smiled.
“Good.”
“What do you mean?”
“I mean that you’re in stealth mode.”
As Erwen was running, her body turned hazy. Even so, it was a weak effect and could be detected from a distance, but...
“Stop.”
When I stopped her from moving, the stealth effect became stronger. This must have been the reason why the characters moved slowly in the game.

As time passed with us standing there, her body turned from translucent to almost transparent. Although there was a clear disparity between her outline and the surrounding area, she would not be visible except at close range.
Or even less, in this dark forest.
Erwen looked down at her body and exclaimed, “Wow...”

It was fascinating to me too. Although I was fascinated by a different thing. Without a command or anything like that, she had activated the skill by sheer force of will. Anyway, we could study this in more detail later.
“Erwen, take this.”
“Huh?”
I handed the backpack to Erwen and quickly added, “You hide here, and when I give you the signal, shoot the crossbow archer first. Do not come out before then. Do you understand?”
“What? What do you mean?”
“There is no time. I’ll assume that you understand.”
I quickly finished what I had to say and immediately started running.
“Wait, the signal?! What is the signal—!”
I heard a small shout ring out behind me, but it was too risky to go back.

After moving about thirty yards from my original position, I stopped. I had no intention of going far in the first place. If I kept going like this and ended up stepping into a trap, that would be a huge problem.
“Grk, grk!”
As I turned back, I heard goblins rushing in from the front left. And those cowardly adventurers... they were yet to be seen.
After I had blocked that first arrow, they didn’t reappear. But I didn’t worry too much about it. It was obvious what those bastards were thinking.
“Grk, grk!”

If I started fighting these goblins, they were sure to appear. They had lured the goblins here with that plan in mind in the first place. Refocusing on the present moment, I watched the goblins swarming around me.
“Grghghgh!”
Of the ten goblins, there were two swordsmen. Fortunately, there were no archers among—
Clang!

I was wrong. I ran toward the goblins, fending off the arrows flying toward my shield. Of course, I couldn’t run around like I usually did. The goblin archers were after me, but so was the human crossbowman.
Clang!
After a period of about ten seconds, another arrow flew in. Again, it belonged to the goblin archer.
Clang!
After blocking the arrow with my shield, I bashed the scimitar-wielding goblin swordsman’s head in. In return, another goblin stabbed me in the leg with a carving knife.
Stab!
Oh well. I had to take risks here. The number of goblins would decrease, but the adventurers would also start to feel impatient and show themselves.
Whack! Whack! Whack!

Knocking down the goblins like a rampaging barbarian, my injuries gradually increased... Forearm, thigh, ribs, etcetera. None of them were serious injuries individually, but as they accumulated, I couldn’t just brush them off.
Whack!
The poison from the goblin weapons had begun to circulate, and a tingling sensation spread from the injured areas. But despite this, I killed all seven goblins. Then—
Whizz!
The arrows flew in. Two at the same time.
Whizz!
Their direction was also different. One was no doubt the goblin archer, and the other would be the crossbowman.
It was difficult to block both with my shield. I chose to block the crossbowman’s arrow coming in from the side.
Bam!
The sound of the impact was different from the one I usually heard when blocking arrows fired by goblin archers.
Is this really a crossbow?
As I was thinking that—
Stab!
With the squelch of something tearing through my skin, a goblin arrow pierced my left elbow.
“Shit.”

That hurt. Had it reached the bone? The pain was one thing, but now my arm couldn’t move at all because of a single arrow. I’d tried to deflect it with a shoulder guard, but it was harder than I had thought.
Thud.

I threw down the hammer in my right hand without hesitation and held up the shield in its place. My left arm, which had been holding the shield, was now paralyzed. If I had to choose between the hammer and the shield, the shield was always the better option.
Especially in this situation.
Whack! Whack! Whack!
Holding the shield in one hand, I pummeled the three remaining goblins, clearing my immediate vicinity. The goblin archer must’ve run away because the arrows stopped coming.
It was a painful victory in the first round, but I survived.
“Come out! You sons of bitches!” I shouted.
I didn’t realize that I’d be saying that to a human, not a goblin. Well, I guess they were basically the same.
Whiiip!
Instead of coming out, an arrow flew at me from far away. It was a human crossbow. Since I expected it, blocking it was no problem. However...
Bam!
Fuck, what is that? I thought.
The arrow had pierced right through the shield’s iron plate, its tip pointing at me through the metal.
One wrong move and this could fuck up my hand too.
As I covered my upper body with the shield and looked out over the bushes, I heard a voice calling out to me before long.
“Barbarian.”
Three people appeared. The red-haired man and presumed leader, a samurai with a single-edged sword similar to a Japanese sword, and a very skinny man holding a one-handed sword and shield.
The crossbowman, meanwhile, was still unaccounted for.
“So, it was you.”
“Yes, it was us.”
How had they lured the goblins here? I didn’t ask any questions like that, because, if I did, I knew they would just look down on me more.
“Come at me.”
“A true barbarian. You’re full of fighting spirit even after dealing with so many goblins alone. Where is that elven bitch?”
I was wondering why they were talking so much. So that was their objective.
“Looks like you even handed over your backpack. If you don’t want any more trouble, you better spill.”
As soon as I heard that, I smirked and let out a snort of laughter.
If I tell you, you’ll let me go? Yeah right. I’m not a brainless dimwit.
“Crazy bastard.”
The leader frowned when he saw me laughing. The look on his face suggested he’d had enough of this. Apparently, I seemed like a standard barbarian to him.
“In that case, we’ll subdue you first and question you again later.”
The leader exchanged glances with his comrades, and they slowly approached together.
Capture the enemy, huh... That was nice to hear.

True, even if they killed me, the risk and reward weren’t balanced. There could be any number of reasons why they had gone through the trouble of an ambush. The mana stones we had gathered over seven days, the equipment we wore, Erwen’s pretty face, or revenge for having to witness someone else get lucky right in front of them.
I was realizing once again...
“Everyone be vigilant. Think of it as hunting a large monster.”
Seriously, there were too many min-maxing freaks in this world. Well, that was probably what I would grow to be like too.
I slowly forced my left hand, which was now paralyzed from the poison arrow stuck in my elbow, to move above my head. And then...
“What are you doing?”
I raised my middle finger up high.
Whiiip!
Anyone who had lived in this world would know that this was a unique signal.
Thunk—!
Soon, a faint sound echoed through the forest.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Return (2)
paragraphs: “Percy? Percy!”
The leader hastily called out a name. Of course, there was no answer. I had instructed Erwen to shoot the crossbowman first.
Only then did the leader turn to me.
“What the hell did you do?”

But even so, he was wary of whatever was behind me, suggesting he had come up with his own theory. That was a very big mistake. I hated bastards who asked a question with an answer already in their heads. A lot.
Smash!
The moment the leader’s gaze turned to the bush, I dashed forward and swung my shield without hesitation.
Voom!
Unfortunately, there was no answering jolt in my hand. To avoid something like that... if it had been a goblin, they would have no doubt disappeared into light.
“Illis! It’s time!”
When the leader called for him, the samurai dashed toward me with a disciplined horizontal slash.
Khak!
I heard the sound of sparks bouncing off my shield.
Shit, what was that shock?
I almost dropped the shield. But, despite being surprised, I ran toward the three instead. I hoped to distract them and give Erwen a more decisive opportunity.
However...
Voom!
Another smash missed.
So you’re saying you’re not a newbie, huh?

Dealing with these guys was the first time the short reach of the shield was bothering me. But the more I thought about it, the more I closed the distance and swung my shield aggressively. Then, I heard the sound I had been waiting for.
Whiiip!

At last, Erwen’s supporting fire had begun. However, the arrows fired did not land in anyone’s forehead, neck, legs, or arms. Instead, the skinny bastard with the sword and shield blocked all of them with his shield.
“I will stop the arrows! Don’t worry about it and get the barbarian!”
I wondered why he was still standing all alone. Had he decided to focus on just the arrows? Again, humans were too meticulous compared to goblins.
Bam!
As I was deflecting the samurai’s strike with my shield, the leader sneakily swung his sword and aimed at my left arm.
Slice—!

Luckily, I reacted in time so the cut was not too deep. Although he had cut me, it didn’t mean much because the arm had already been useless. Plus, it hadn’t hurt that much because of the paralyzing poison circulating through my veins.
“What kind of monster...” the leader muttered when I didn’t even flinch at the injury.
Shit, don’t blame it on me. You’re just not a good swordsman.
I cussed inwardly and pushed the samurai back with my shield and brute strength.
Then another support arrow was fired.
Wheee!
Maybe she had changed positions because this arrow came from a completely different direction from before. The skinny man was not an easy mark either.
Clang!
Skinny once again blocked the arrow with his shield.
What is he? An outfielder?
Skinny flung his body in front of an arrow aimed at someone else. I was on the verge of getting frustrated that the fight showed no signs of progressing when—
Whoosh!
His shield, which looked like a hedgehog with all those arrows sticking out of it, quickly erupted into flames.
“Shit!”

Skinny could not stand the heat and tossed away his shield. I smirked in my head. Sorry, our archer is an elementalist. That’s why you should have used a 100 percent iron shield like me, you poor bastard!
Whizz!
As the annoying shield disappeared, Erwen fired more arrows without hesitation.
“Aaaah!”
The arrow hit Skinny’s shoulder. Soon after, he lost even the sword he had been holding and became a useless prick.
“Illis! I’ll take care of the elf bitch!”
Only then did the leader get a handle on the situation and entrust me to the samurai so he could run for the bushes. It was already too late for me to catch up.
Grrr! Damn you!
It seemed that I had no choice but to put my faith in Erwen.
The samurai stepped back and spoke in a pompous tone.
“Give up, barbarian.”
This was why humans got on my nerves. Who did he think he was fooling? It was clear that he was trying to buy time until his leader returned.
Dash!
As I dashed forward and used [Smash], the samurai’s face crumpled up.
“What’s wrong? Are you afraid now that you’re alone?!”
“He’s not alone!”
The question had been directed at the samurai, but the answer had come from Skinny. In his left hand was the one-handed sword he had dropped earlier. But...
Voom!
Is it because he’s right-handed? His knife work wasn’t cutting it. He might have been a hot shot with the shield but with the sword? He was weak.
Whack!
By taking a step back, I cleanly evaded Skinny’s attack and then kicked at his kneecap. Skinny squealed, the veins on his neck bulging.
“Aaah!”

Oh, I hadn’t expected it to turn out like that. Skinny fell to the floor cradling his knee, which now had a bone protruding from it, with both hands. I wanted to use this opportunity to finish him off, but unfortunately, that hope was dashed thanks to the samurai.
Khak!
It was a powerful blow that I couldn’t seem to get used to no matter how many times I blocked it. Why was someone like him hanging out with these dickheads?
Maybe there was some kind of story behind it? I wasn’t sure, but I knew this was going to be the biggest mistake of this bastard’s life.
Voom!

When I used [Smash] the samurai dodged it with an experienced move and widened the distance between us. Immediately, I dropped my shield and reached out my hand, dashing once more. This move was called... “Reaching Out While Pretending to Smash.” I was too lazy to even name it right now. It wasn’t that fun either.
The samurai’s face was flooded with alarm as I caught him by the nape of his neck.
“Didn’t expect that, huh?”
I yanked the samurai back with bountiful strength. Then, instead of using my paralyzed left arm, I used my mouth to bite the samurai’s neck, and—
Rip—!
Ripped it off.
“Ah, ah, ahhhh...”
The samurai couldn’t even scream. He took a step backward with blank eyes, covering his neck, which was now pouring blood like a fountain, with both hands...
And then he collapsed to the ground.
“Mister!”
Did she settle her end of the fight on her own?
As soon as the battle was over, Erwen appeared from the bushes.
“Mister?”
I spit out the chunk of flesh in my mouth and wiped my lips with my arm.
Shit, that was fucking disgusting.

The arduous battle was now over. Was I the only one injured? Fortunately, Erwen was in the same state as she had been when we parted, implying the battle had ended before the man had gotten too close. I, on the other hand, was completely in tatters.
“Mister! Drink this, quick.”
As my adrenaline faded, I fell to the ground on my knees. Erwen held out a potion.
Gulp, gulp, gulp...

I carefully emptied the bottle like I was drinking a deadly poison. The poison in my body was one thing, but since my injuries were not concentrated in a single area, Erwen explained it was better to drink the potion rather than pour it on the wound.
Since I had emptied an entire bottle, it felt completely different than usual.

Something was boiling inside my intestines. The pain felt like small beads were bouncing around in my blood vessels, and my skin was so hot that it was close to driving me crazy. That went on for over ten minutes.
“...Mister, be strong.”
Erwen wiped my sweaty body with the old handkerchief from a while ago. Perhaps because of the poison, or perhaps because I was just dirty, the white handkerchief turned completely black.
...I’d have to buy her a new one later.
“It’s fine. I’m... okay now.”
Feeling slightly better, I struggled to my feet.
Looking down, I could see scabs sitting on top of my wounds, both large and small. If I drank another bottle of potion, those would disappear too, but I decided not to.
“This one is going to leave a scar...”
So what, though? I’m a barbarian.
“Water.”
“Right! Here.”

Straight away, Erwen quickly rummaged through her bag and pulled out a water bottle. I felt like I’d become a lord or something. I gulped down the whole bottle and energy began to slowly return to my body.
Was water always this good?
All of a sudden, the bulging veins that had sprung up all over my body also sank down.
“Take out my watch.”
With Erwen’s help, I checked the time. Then I froze.
Damn, they didn’t even leave us time to rest.
There were just forty minutes left until the seventh day ended. If we couldn’t get down to the first floor by then, we’d have to spend three more days in this goddamn place.
“Erwen, the clothes. Take them off.”
“Wh-what?”
Not yours, theirs.
Lacking the energy to speak, I pointed toward the corpses with my hand, and Erwen dropped the hand that was holding her shirt closed.
“No, actually, forget the clothes,” I said. “We don’t have time. Just pack their gear, mana stones, and backpacks.”
“O-Okay!” Knowing that there was no time, Erwen moved quickly. “Oh, I’ll bring that red-haired guy and the crossbow guy’s stuff too!”
Yes, and be careful not to step on a trap.
While Erwen was busy with that, I took off the samurai and Skinny’s equipment. I tossed away the chest guard, samurai sword, and the wooden shield that had turned into charcoal...
After sorting through their equipment, I did a rough inventory and took only the items that looked expensive. And just as I was putting them in my backpack, Erwen returned.
The two backpacks seemed quite heavy for her.
Sorry, I can’t hold them for you because I have three.
Soon after, I checked the time one more time.
Only twenty-five minutes left.
“Let’s run.”
“Are you sure? You look tired...”
“Don’t worry about it.”
Erwen looked full of concern, but when she saw my expression, she nodded and led the way.
And so, a forced marathon began.
“I’ll follow behind you, so speed up as much as you can and clear the way.”
“Okay.”
Sending Erwen ahead, I continued running while adjusting my pace. My body was weirdly heavy, probably due to mental fatigue. Or was it just because of these backpacks?
...Still, I couldn’t just leave them there. After all that hard work, there needed to be a reward. That was justice.
Pant, pant...
After I had run for who knew how long... a portal appeared in the distance.
Erwen had arrived first and was waiting for me in front of it. Her expression both cheered me on and pitied me at the same time, like she was a young female protagonist in an anime.
Shit, this is the kind of vibe you feel right before you get rejected.
Feeling a bit anxious, I mustered the rest of my strength and sped up my steps.
And...
“I’m going in first!”
“Eh? Me—me too!”
Unlike in an anime, I boldly skipped the emotional hug and entered the portal.
Flash—!
The burst of brilliance was the same as it had been last time. But somehow, this time, I felt like the light was embracing me.
The sensation of returning to the first floor was not much different from when we had entered the second floor. It was the sensation of being spat out of the belly of a beast.
“Ahh!”
Unfortunately, even the outcome was the same. No, it was maybe worse.
Thudㅡ!
While I was tossed headfirst and thrown into the ground, Erwen once again landed just fine.
...How the hell was that possible?
When we had been thrown into the second floor, she had at least drawn an arc through the air. In terms of baseball, this time she was no different from a fastball.
Damn, every single one of my bones ached.
“That was kinda fun!”
Uh, right.
Well, I would laugh too if there was someone like me beside me.
“Whew...”
Stretching out my aching body, I got up and dusted off the dirt. Then, I checked the time.
Safe, but it had been a close call.

I didn’t want to say we were lucky, because then there would be too many things I could blame the universe for. If things went well, it was because of me, and if things didn’t go well, it was also because of me. That mindset was better for my mental health.
“You worked hard, mister.”
“Yeah, you too.”
We looked at each other for a moment and said our goodbyes.
Wait, I feel like I’m forgetting something...
“Loot distribution!”
“Oh, right! The essence!”
Erwen and I shouted at the same time.
“The essence?”
“Yeah! You told me to promise you something earlier!”
Oh, yes. That.
Now I remembered what I had forgotten. But, there was no time for a long conversation. I quickly checked the watch again.
I looked at the second hand and there were about fifteen seconds left. I quickly closed the clock and raised my head to look at Erwen.
So, that... that... What was the name again? Black something?
“Black Whale! Let’s meet at the Black Whale Tavern!”
“Okay!”
Erwen nodded in response to my urgent cry. Now, I could rest easy—
[The labyrinth is closed.]
[You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
Oh shit, I didn’t say what time.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Return (3)
paragraphs: Light flooded my surroundings, and an even whiter light shone beyond that before my sight returned.
I stared blankly up at the sky. It had been a long time since I had been somewhere so bright. Well, it was still just a gloomy gray sky, though.
“Derek, are you going home?”
“No way, after a month of that? I’m going straight to the tavern after washing up.”
“I’m back!”
“All adventurers below rank seven, please come this way!”

To say my surroundings were noisy would be an understatement. It was only natural that all the adventurers from the labyrinth would gather in one place... but still. I had no idea there were so many adventurers in this city. It was like Gwanghwamun Gate during the World Cup.
Click, click.
I set my watch to twelve o’clock.
When you entered a labyrinth, only a day passed in the city outside. No matter how many days you spent inside, it was noon the next day when you exited.
When I was playing the game, I thought that was just something the game designer did to help out the player. But it’s in the world of the game as well...?
This meant that even after you exited a labyrinth, you could immediately continue on a quest in the city. So, I had thought it was just a convenience thing for players.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
Who was that? The voice was familiar... As I turned my head in the direction of the sound, I met the eyes of a barbarian. I vividly remembered him being the first leader of our group.
“Karak, second son of Fanun.”
“It’s the third son.”
Eh? So, is Ainar second?
Anyway, it was easy for tall barbarians to find each other in this crowd.
“Kenick’s fourth son, Serum! You came back alive as well!”
“I’m glad you look all right too, Karak, third son of Fanun!”
I was just standing there, but the barbarians started flocking toward me.
“Ha ha ha ha ha! The Blade Wolf was no big deal! Nothing can hold out against my axe for more than one strike!”
“Of course, you wield your axe valiantly, Parman, son of Nerun!”
Was this a school reunion? It was instant chaos.

The barbarians greeted each other by calling out their long names and titles nonstop and praised each other’s valor. They were fascinating. How did they memorize those long names with thick skulls like that?
“Bjorn! What are you doing?! We’re going to exchange mana stones now, aren’t you coming?”
I cleared my throat once and answered as loudly as I could.
“Oh, I will go!”
“You seem pretty tired! There is no strength in your voice!”
“That’s right!”
I had thought my barbarian act was pretty good, but now my confidence was waning. Natural-born barbarians were different.
“There it is!”
“The place for warriors to prove their bravery!”

As I moved along with the group of barbarians, I was consequentially able to go through the process that all adventurers completed. It was nothing special—it was just the process of exchanging mana stones for money at the checkpoint.
“That’s 24,476 stones.”
“That’s 28,420 stones.”
“That’s 41,498 stones.”
It was like a checkout line at a grocery store. Especially when it came to speed.

The officials sitting at the table doing their work were super quick. They placed the pouch of mana stones on top of something like they were scanning a barcode, and when a number appeared, they took out the corresponding amount of money like a well-oiled machine. As I watched this curiously, the barbarians around me shouted and chatted at the top of their lungs without an ounce of shame.
“Oh! To earn more than forty thousand stones, amazing!”
“Karak, the third son of Fanun, is a warrior among warriors!”
Ha... I wasn’t sure if it was because I had lived with an elf for the past few days, but I just couldn’t get used to this.
I still needed to find Erwen as well... Why did these punks have to show up instead? I had just been standing there.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! It’s your turn now!”
As I was sighing to myself, my turn arrived. I walked over to the table and placed my pouches in front of the seemingly soulless civil servant.
“Are all three pouches mana stones?”
The other two pouches had belonged to Skinny and the samurai. But now they were all mine... as of about forty minutes ago.
“That’s right.”
As I nodded, the official placed the pouches on the scale-like contraption. Soon after, it relayed the exact amount.
“That’s 182,413 stones.”
A loaf of bread was about twenty stones, so that was over nine thousand servings of bread in seven days.
It was just yesterday that I had been upset about beating a goblin and earning a single slice of bread.
...I was starting to get a bit emotional.
“He’s earned 180,000 stones! Bjorn, son of Yandel, has earned 180,000 stones!”
“That is the highest amount ever! Bjorn, son of Yandel, is the greatest warrior of all time!”
But these bastards didn’t even give me the time to be emotional.
I quickly retrieved the money from the official and left the checkpoint. But as soon as I came out of the crowd, the barbarians noticed my appearance and started making a fuss.
“Not just the stones! He’s even holding a hammer!”
“And he’s even wearing shoes! I’m jealous!”
“He has three bags!”
“He’s looking at a clock! Does he know how to read time?”
“How is that possible? Is Bjorn, son of Yandel, a wizard?”

Well, it was not like I couldn’t understand why they were reacting the way they were. It probably would seem like magic to them. I was the first barbarian to go into the labyrinth naked and come out an evolved, civilized man!
Shit, all this hype was getting me excited too.
Whoa, calm down, Bjorn. I’m...
“I am the greatest warrior!”
“Ahh!”
As I cried out, the barbarians went wild. Then, they picked me up and started tossing me in the air. Surprisingly, it felt better than I expected.
Well, I would roll with it.
“You can’t make too much noise here.”
“I’m sorry! I apologize!”
“I mean, please lower your voice....”
“Okay!”

Finally, the madness subsided only after a checkpoint worker came to tell us off. Then I regained my composure and sat on the floor like the barbarians around me, waiting for the remaining barbarians to finish at the checkpoint.
It was then that I sensed eyes on me and turned my head to see an elf staring at me through the crowd of adventurers. It was Erwen.
How long has she been watching? I hope it was after I was done crowd-surfing...

Unbothered, Erwen smiled when our eyes met like she was pleased to see me. However, when the elegant elves next to her started talking to her, she quickly took her eyes off of me. Curious, I listened to their conversation, which turned out to be quite refreshing. Seeing Erwen talking quietly with elves who were older than her was almost surreal.
“Sis! I think I know how to handle elementals now! I understand why Grandma Grinderin insisted that you have to be friends with them first.”
“Oh, really? Fire spirits have a rather short temper, so you will be able to hear their voices soon.”
Mm, so you’re part of that world, huh? I only have savage beasts next to me. I’m jealous...
Watching Erwen with a longing for what I was missing, our eyes met again. I took this opportunity to mouth something.
Tonight.
Erwen cocked her head, then smiled and answered:
Okay!
It was clear that this secret conversation was quite exciting to Erwen. But I didn’t know if she actually understood what I had said. Did she even reply “Okay,” or was I just imagining things?
Ha... I’d have to try to talk to her once I left the checkpoint.
As I was lost in thought—
“Why are you looking over there like that? Is there someone you know?”
“N-No! Sis! Of course not!”
Erwen waved her hands dismissively in response to the other elf’s question. Then, waiting for an opening, she glanced at me and mouthed, “I’m sorry!”

I thought I was reading her lips right this time. I could also understand the gesture of secretly pointing at the other elf and shaking her head that followed. It must have meant that she didn’t have a choice. Well, it was the same over here.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! What are you looking at?! Do you know that elf?”
“I do not!”
“Well, of course! There is no way that the greatest warrior of all time would ever know a vile fern-face!”
I wanted to shut the bastard’s mouth, but I couldn’t. At the sound of the loud, booming voice, the elves around me turned to us and glared.
Among them was Erwen. But while her eyes were pained, she nodded her head as if in understanding.
Looking at those sad eyes, I had a realization.
What are we doing right now? Is this Romeo and Juliet?
“Let’s go!”

Soon after, the barbarians finished their exchanges and headed out. Talking to Erwen when she was with the elves seemed like an impossible task no matter how long I waited, so I followed them out. Annoyingly, there were more people gathered out front.
“Dad! Are you hurt? I missed you!”
“Bro! I’m here!”
Hmm, yes, there was something similar in the game as well. Put simply, the people gathered here were family members or acquaintances of the adventurers.
“Let’s go! I will clear the way!”
“Ohhh!”
I followed the barbarians through the crowd, every person in it overcome with joy, despair, sorrow, or affection.
I studied their faces one by one. It felt strange.
“Limarion! My husband, where is my husband? Is he...?”
“I am sorry. He asked me to give this to you.”
“No... no. No... Ahh!”
I’d played Dungeon and Stone countless times, but I could now see faces and expressions that I had never seen through the 2D graphics on the screen.

One of the reasons why I had to go with the barbarians was that, just like with the checkpoint, there were still more procedures newcomers to the city had to complete. However, my expectations of where we were headed were surprisingly inaccurate.
“Drink! Let’s drink!”
“Ohhh!”
As soon as they got out of the labyrinth, the barbarians headed straight to the tavern.
You’re all underage, you idiots. Oh, wait. You already finished your coming-of-age ceremony.
“I will be going.”
“Why! Bjorn, son of Yandel, the Greatest Warrior!”
A modifier had been attached to my already long name. I made an excuse that I had somewhere to go and left the group, all the while repeating to myself that patience was a virtue.
“I pray that fortune in battle be with you, Bjorn, son of Yandel, the Greatest Warrior!”
The realization had already hit me multiple times, but at that moment, it hit me again: I really could never use common sense to predict what these guys were going to do next.
“Finally, some quiet.”
After being with the savages for a short while, I felt like I was going insane. Had Erwen felt the same way when she had stayed with me?
Next time, I’d have to tone down the barbarian act.
Trudge, trudge.
After splitting off from the group, I wandered around the city without stopping. I had a destination in mind, but right now, I just wanted to walk wherever my footsteps led me. It was peaceful.
It had been midnight when I first saw this city, but now that it was daytime, the streets were full of people. Surprisingly, it gave me a sense of security.
There were no monsters here. No one could hurt me. Even if I fell asleep on the side of the road, I would wake up in one piece. Someone might even give me a helping hand.

There were laws, rules, and leisure here. Of course, it was still a distant world in another universe, and I knew that, despite its appearance, almost everything from their ideas, culture, and social system would be uncivilized compared to the 21st century.
But it was still peaceful. At least compared to the labyrinth I had spent seven days in.

I wanted to experience that sense of security a little more, so I kept walking. Because adventurers had just poured out of the labyrinth, being covered in blood didn’t really make me stand out. No one even looked at me strangely. But, as I kept walking down the street, I felt the urge to wash myself off. So, I went to the first inn I saw, got a room, and bathed.
It was interesting. I had never seen bathwater with more blood in it than dirt. When I headed outside after bathing for about an hour, I felt that the clothes I was wearing were too dirty.
Damn, I should’ve bought some clothes before I took a bath.
All I wanted to do was go to sleep, but I went out into the street again and looked for a clothing store.

But why was I doing that? No one was looking at me strangely, but I was still embarrassed for some reason. My bare upper body and my pants stained with blood and dirt were the same as they had been earlier in the labyrinth. Well, no, my body was at least a lot cleaner, but still...
I felt like a savage again.
Why?
“Welcome!”

As soon as I entered a store that I presumed to be a clothing store, a kind worker approached me and smiled, even at a seemingly homeless barbarian. I’d never seen such a professional employee, even in Seoul...

“A shirt? If you would like to make a custom order, please visit the building next door... Oh, you’re looking for something to wear right now? I’m not sure if there’s anything in your size, but I’ll take a look.”
With the help of the worker, I was able to buy a tight-fitting shirt and black cloth pants. The total was 2,500 stones.
I couldn’t tell if I had been ripped off or not. I’d never tried on or bought clothes that didn’t have any function when I was playing the game.
“See you next time!”

Now that I looked more like a person, I returned to the inn. After watching that civil servant exchange my mana stones and also speaking to that clothing store employee just now, I felt that the city exuded a strangely modern vibe.
Rafdonia.

Most of the buildings were made of stone and had many floors. It was hard to even find a building with less than three stories on this street, and my bath water had even come out of a faucet. Perhaps living in this city was going to be more viable than I thought.
Soon after arriving at the inn, I lay down on the bed. As I recalled the events of the past seven days one by one, it hit me that I was also a human, not much different from Hans.
When I had first fallen into this world, my only goal had been to survive. But now?
I finally let out the words I had been swallowing back for days.
“I want to go home.”
I wanted to go back. Even if no one was there to welcome me.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Rafdonia (1)
paragraphs: I slowly opened my eyes. Then, I closed my eyes again and said to myself:
Get up and do what you have to do.
As I recalled the various tasks I had to get done in the city, my tired body began to feel energized.
Yeah, let’s do it.
First, I checked the time.
It had already been noon when I came out of the labyrinth, so I had slept for about four hours. But thanks to sleeping on a bed, I felt incredibly refreshed despite the short nap.
Growl!
I still had bread left over from the labyrinth, but I decided to eat out.
Although this was a world where your money was your life... this amount of luxury should be fine.
Despite bathing myself earlier in the day, my body still smelled, so I quickly washed up once more and left the inn.
Trudge, trudge.
Compared to how I felt during the day, walking through the quiet streets at night felt a bit suffocating. Not psychologically, but physically.

The beige shirt I was wearing now was a medieval-style top with a cutout chest and laced-up sleeves and collar. Instead of a button, a string was attached to the deep v-neck that could be tightened like a shoelace. Even with the string completely untied, however, the shirt was too small. I could see why barbarians were always half-naked. Nothing fit them. How sad was this life of theirs?
...But where should I go?
Right now, the first thing I had to do was meet Erwen at the agreed-upon rendezvous point. But I didn’t know where the Black Whale Tavern was.

I was certain that it was in the southern part of the city based on the area where the portal to the labyrinth opened, but the city map in the game was tens of thousands of times smaller than its actual size, so my knowledge of it was not helpful in this task. So I ended up asking for help from a passerby.
“The Black Whale Tavern? What’s that?”
“I’ve never heard of it before.”
Most people responded that they had never heard of it, but one middle-aged man with gray hair proved to be different.
“The Black Whale tavern... I haven’t heard that name in a while. You seem very young—how do you know about that tavern? It must have closed down more than ten years ago.”
I was flattered that he said I looked young, but the actual contents of his words were not very welcome.
“...You mean it’s gone?”
“Yes, it was a restaurant that ran for several generations, but their son fell into a gambling habit and so it had to change owners. The name has changed as well.”

It was then that the hypothesis I had been keeping to myself was lent credibility. The game was set in the past of the world I was currently in. If that was the case, things like ‘evil spirits’ or the rivalry between barbarians and elves could also be explained. I’d have to visit a library sometime during the day.
“Thank you. You have been very helpful.”
“Heh heh, I don’t think I’ve ever met a barbarian as polite as you.”

After that, I said goodbye to the native Rafdonian and walked down the dark street. The name had changed, but it looked like the tavern was still in business, so I thought I’d at least drop by. I hoped that Erwen would also have the same thought and come to see me.
Fidenpus.

As soon as I reached my destination, I paused for a moment. I could understand the pronunciation, but I didn’t know the meaning. Was this written in a language that was ancient even in this world? It was also probably a good idea to study this language that came to me intuitively.
“Ha ha ha!”
“If you’re going to fight, go outside, you bastards!”

The inside of the tavern was exactly what I had imagined it to be. Drunk people, adventurers, music, sleaziness, cigarette smoke, and even the occasional nonhuman species. As I stood at the entrance and scanned the interior, I saw a familiar silver head of hair in the corner. Even their slightly protruding ears were pointy. I was glad to see that and was about to step forward when—
A drunken jackass shouldered past me to get through the aisle first. That alone wasn’t a problem, but...
“Elven ladies, you look bored on your own. How about a drink with me?”
He also approached Erwen and threw out those cliché lines. Well, actually, that wasn’t a big deal either.
But...
“Fitting for a pub that smells like a sewer. It seems that all kinds of rats keep popping up.”
E-Erwen? What happened to you?
“...What? Rat?”
The swaggering douchebag looked bewildered by her superb clap back. My face probably looked similar.
“Get lost. If you don’t want a hole in the middle of your forehead.”
Judging by the fact that they were fond of the forehead, this had to be the right person...
What the hell?
I had to go check this out. But first, I knew I should get rid of this scumbag.
“What? Who the hell are you!”
As I approached and grabbed his shoulder, the arrogant man turned his head and...
Immediately looked away.
“She said get lost.”
“...Right.”
“Then why are you still standing here?”
Instead of answering, he carefully squeezed by me, then went back to his seat without so much as staggering and sat down.
That was when...
“Mister!”
I heard the word I was so familiar with. But I was not surprised I hadn’t noticed Erwen’s apparent split personality from the start.
...Really.
Because that guy had just said elven “ladies.”
“Are you that barbarian?”
Hidden from view by a pillar in the corner seat, there were a total of two people sitting at the table.
“Yes, I am that barbarian you speak of. But who are you?”
“Her older sister.”
Oh, she was Erwen’s real sister. No wonder they looked exactly the same from the side.
“Is ‘older sister’ your name?”
“...Idiot. Call me Tersia.”
Erwen’s last name was Tersia. Apparently, the older sister didn’t want to tell me her name.
“Okay. Tersia, can I sit down, then?”
“Do as you please.”
I sat down without hesitation and studied Tersia.

First, they didn’t look like twins. She looked about three or four years older than Erwen, and now that I was looking at her from the front, their features were also quite different. She gave off a ferocious vibe because of her eyes. Or maybe it wasn’t just because of her eyes.
“Barbarian.”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Whatever. Anyway, why the hell did you ask my little sis to come to this bar?”
“Um, Sis...?”
“You be quiet.”

Erwen tried to intervene and clear the air but was stopped by her sister. Hmm, things were getting interesting. Aside from why Erwen brought her sister along in the first place, I didn’t think my being a barbarian was the only reason that her sister disliked me.
It was a hunch I’d have to look into.
“And for what reason did you come to see me, Tersia?”
“Erwen did not come home last night. And when I pried further, she said she had been waiting for someone at the tavern all night. I was curious who would stand my sister up.”
Wait, I don’t understand.
“What do you mean? Last night?”
“Are you going to pretend you don’t know?”
Judging by her reaction, she didn’t seem to be joking around.
“...Erwen, how many hours have passed since we came out of the labyrinth?”
“Ah, oh... about thirty hours!”
Fuck, so I’ve just woken up after sleeping for over an entire day. Not just four hours.
No wonder I felt so refreshed.
“I apologize. I didn’t know that a day had passed because I was asleep.”
When I politely apologized, Tersia shot me a look of surprise. That made me kind of sad. She also didn’t seem to have any questions about the fact that I had slept for a full day.
“Well, I never expected a barbarian to be on time anyway.”
I really had nothing to say.
“So, why did you summon Erwen?”
Well, the reason was quite long and complicated... so I just made it short and clear.
“I don’t think I need to tell you that. Ask Erwen later if you’re curious.”
When translated literally, that meant ‘don’t worry about it and get lost,’ but luckily, Tersia seemed to understand. I saw the corners of her lips turn up.
“Funny, for a newbie who just entered a labyrinth for the first time.”
“What does being new have to do with it? Erwen is an adventurer. Unless you’re going to take care of her for the rest of your life, you’d better ditch that attitude.”
“How barbaric.”
“Sis? Mister...?” Erwen said quietly.
When a staring contest ensued, Erwen restlessly stomped her feet. Soon afterward, Tersia put a pouch on the table.
“That’s 350,000 stones.”
“...Why are you giving this to me?”
“It’s the value of the essence that Erwen absorbed.”
Oh, so take this and get lost?
It was a plotline I’d seen often in morning dramas, so it felt weird.
“Why aren’t you taking it? Did you come into this meeting with other intentions?”
It’s not like that.
If she really wanted to pay with money, I had no intention of asking Erwen for a promise in return for the essence. However, I hadn’t heard Erwen’s thoughts yet.
“Are you of the same opinion?”
Erwen trailed off. Was she that scared of her sister?
Originally, I was going to share this when we were alone, but now that this was happening, I decided to share it.
“The promise I was going to ask of you was for you to help me out until I obtain the essence that I seek.”
“Eh, is that all?”
“That’s right. If possible, I would like to continue as a team after that as well, but that is another matter. You don’t have to promise that. And in the future, we can divide the loot five-to-five.”
In a nutshell, I was asking her to form a two-person party. How would Erwen respond?
She didn’t need much time.
“I’m sorry.”
Her answer was a rejection. Erwen dropped her head, and her sister explained to her.
“Erwen will be going into the labyrinth with me from now on.”
“Why?”
“She merely ventured in alone for the first trip as per tradition. I had no intention of leaving Erwen alone from the start.”
...I see. So she had a chauffeur waiting for her after the tutorial...
Damn blood ties.
“If you understand, take this bag.”
I decided to give up on Erwen. Although she had been a good teammate, there was no reason to insist upon having her. But still, the valuation had to be correct.
“You calculated 350,000 stones as half of the average market price, right?”
“Of course. It’s joint loot.”
Judging as a pro at this game, seven hundred thousand stones was a pretty decent amount. But the ratio was wrong.
“Then it’s 280,000 stones short. The agreed-upon distribution ratio was 9:1.”
“Fine.”
Tersia readily pulled out another pouch.
I was suspicious, but when I checked it, it contained exactly 280,000 stones.
Damn, did I almost get scammed just now?
If I hadn’t said anything, this deal would have ended with just 350,000 stones. These sly fern-faces... I could see why barbarians hated elves so much.
“If your business here is done, will you get up? I have something to discuss with Erwen.”
“I don’t see why that’s necessary.”
Before another fight could start, Erwen stepped in.
“Sis, thank you for worrying about me and coming all the way here, but I think you can go now.”
“Erwen?”
“I have to say goodbye to him too... Hmm?”

“...Well, since you are no longer a child...” Tersia said something she didn’t even seem to believe, took a deep breath and looked at me. “Barbarian, swear the following: that you won’t sleep with Erwen. Then I will leave immediately.”
Huh? Did I mishear her?
“S-Sis?!”
Hmm, I guess I did hear her right. Don’t “sleep” with Erwen... Did that mean that everything up to that was allowed?
“I swear. On a warrior’s honor.”
“Mister?”
“Good.”
At last, Tersia got up from her seat.
And...
“Oh, I forgot. Barbarian, thank you for saving Erwen.”
With that, she casually left the tavern.
Ring, ring.
The moment she heard the bell over the door ring, Erwen slumped over the table.
“Ahh! What should I do? I’ve never talked back to her like that before... Do you think she’ll be angry?”
“She won’t be.”
“How do you know that?”
“Because before she left, she looked over at you and grinned. You wouldn’t have seen it, though.”
“...Wait, if that’s the case, why did she even ask?”
Erwen scratched her head a few times and then came to her senses.
“Oh, right! I’m sorry. I appreciate the offer, but I’ve been talking about working with my sister for a long time...”
“No need to apologize.”
If a high-level elf offered to take me along with her, even I wouldn’t follow around an amateur barbarian and go through all that hardship out of loyalty alone.
“Um, take this first.”
Erwen took out a small pouch and placed it on the table.
“Exactly 63,000 stones.”

That would be the price of the mana stones from the crossbow and the leader. I didn’t know what the actual amount was, but I did not doubt her. Being suspicious was pointless anyway. The more important thing was, how much should I pay her if I divide this 9:1?
“Ah, I took care of my earnings, so you don’t have to give me anything.”
Ah, I see. She was very shrewd when it came to things like these.
“I left their two backpacks at my place for now. There are lots of things inside, but... I think it would be good for you to see for yourself tomorrow.”
“I will.”

Because we had been together for a few days, she knew very well the things I would be interested in. I hadn’t said a word, but the issue of loot distribution was settled in an instant. However, when it came to the next item on the agenda, Erwen opened her mouth more cautiously.
“So... how can I repay you?”
“Repay me?”
“I told you I would definitely repay your favor.”
Oh, right, she had said that at some point.
“Favor...”
Erwen gulped as I trailed off.
...Could it be that this was why her sister had forced me to make that oath? Because I might make a strange request?
“Please don’t tease me, just tell me.”
She had gotten better at reading the room, so she knew right away that I was teasing her.
“I can’t think of anything right now. First, I want to order something. Is there anything you want to eat?”
“I’m not hungry...”
“Then I’ll just order for myself.”
As soon as I looked at the menu on the wall, Erwen remembered something and said, “Oh, then a drink! Please order me a drink!”
“Alcohol?”
“Yes. I didn’t even take a sip yesterday because I wanted to have my first drink after our return with you! Hehe.”
Erwen smiled brightly and looked at me with eyes that seemed to beg for praise. A return drink, huh... I had forgotten about that tradition.

Well, this was a bit different from drinking a can of beer after work, but still. For these otherworldly beings who grew up exclusively in the holy land until they reached adulthood, their first return drink likely had a greater meaning than one might assume.
Hmm, but what should I say in this situation?
“...That’s great.”
“This is when you should say thank you!”
“Thank you?”
“You’re welcome! We were comrades who went through a lot together in the labyrinth. Of course we should have the first return drink together.”
What did she want from me?
As I wondered this, Erwen scratched her cheek.
“Of course, to you, this won’t be your first return drink...”
“What do you mean? This is also my first.”
“Really?!”
Why is she surprised?
“I told you I’m also twenty years old.”
“...That wasn’t a joke?”
No wonder she had kept calling me Mister.
“This was the first time I entered a labyrinth.”
“O-Oh I see...”
Erwen, wary of my reaction, went to the waiter and started ordering on her own. The food came out about twenty minutes later.
“Mister, you worked hard.”
I guess she’s going to keep calling me that. Sure, well... do what you want. We won’t be seeing each other for long anyway.
“...You worked hard too.”
We chatted over food and drinks. In the labyrinth, we had only spoken when necessary, so this was the first time we were having such a personal conversation.
But it couldn’t last forever.
“Mister, you’re wearing a shirt today.”
Yes, and I am wearing a skirt. Enough small talk.
“Erwen, did you say you would repay the favor?”
“Pardon? Yes, I did.”
“Then, use the ability you used back then right now.”
Erwen cocked her head.

I didn’t know if this could really be called a reward, but... It was important to me. What was the difference between the essence found in the game and the real-life essence? I had to know in advance because I might need to modify my leveling strategy.
“But why this all of a sudden?”
“There is something I want to check.”
“But it’s illegal to use your powers in the city. I’ll get taken away by the guards.”
So that was the reason why skills couldn’t be used in the city when you were playing the game.
So was there no way around it at all?
While I was thinking this over, Erwen made a suggestion.
“How about going to a place where there are no people? Oh, my place is not an option, though. Other races are prohibited from entering.”
Elves had their own accommodations, it seemed. Hmm, what could we do? Should I take her to a dark alley?
Erwen was the one who came up with a solution to the problem. “...That leaves us with your room.”
Okay, that works.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Rafdonia (2)
paragraphs: Returning to the inn, I studied Erwen’s tipsy form.
Of course, the oath I had made with her sister was never going to be broken. Although an oath on a warrior’s honor meant nothing to me as a husk of a warrior, but still.
“Erwen, open up a little more.”
“Huh, but even if you say that...”
Currently, I was forcing Erwen to stretch.
“Ahh! My shoulder! I think my shoulder’s going to fall off!”
“Hmm.”
“I-It was never able to twist like this in the first place! I swear!”
“Are you sure?”
“Y-Yes! I swear on the name of my clan!”
As soon as I relaxed my hand, Erwen immediately dropped down onto the bed.
I guess [Flexibility +4] didn’t make a huge difference. Well, that was the same as in the game at least.
“I-Is that all?”
“Yes. You can rest for now.”

Dungeon and Stone was an unfriendly game; that was obvious just by looking at the stats. [Physique], [Spirit], and [Special Ability] were the three main stats. But, if you clicked the [+] button next to them, thousands of detailed stats were revealed.

For example, if [Strength], a sub-attribute of [Physique], increased, the weight that you could carry, physical attack power, etcetera was adjusted. [Flexibility]? That slightly increased your chances of dodging and rate of critical hits. [Vision]? The range of long-distance weapons and the character’s visual range increased. [Sense of Smell] became a factor in related special abilities, and [Accuracy Rate] was exactly what the name suggested.
Therefore, even if the Physique stat was still fifty, the character’s abilities could be completely different depending on the detailed stats.

And as an FYI, this was something I figured out all on my own. It was information that neither the game company nor any foreign users provided me, so I had to conduct numerous experiments and create my own statistical data, all for the sole purpose of beating this game.
Fuck, back then, I never dreamed that that passion would turn into poison and come bite me in the behind.
Err, I’m getting pissed off again.

Once again, I was going on nine years as a genuine expert. However, I still didn’t know the effect of some of the stats. A prime example was [Obsession +7], found on the essence dropped by the goblin archer. Everything about that stat was a mystery, except that it was a sub-attribute of the Spirit stat.
“Erwen.”
“You make me nervous whenever you sigh like that. Can you just not say whatever it is?”
“Has anything changed since you came out of the labyrinth? Like something that keeps popping up in your head, a desire that’s hard to get rid of, anything like that.”
“...M-Mm, I don’t know. Maybe?”
“What is it? Tell me.”
“Snacks...? Yes, snacks. Looking back, as soon as I came out of the labyrinth, I bought a bunch and ate them all...”
“Did you used to dislike sweets?”
“No, I loved them. Still, I think that’s the first time I’ve eaten that much in a day.”
“I see.”
Perhaps Obsession made a desire grow stronger. That was why it had no special function in the game.

This made my head hurt more. It seemed that, because the game had been adapted into reality, additional functions may have been added to the more detailed stats. Or at least, that was true for Flexibility.

In the game, the more natural someone’s movements became, the easier it became for them to dodge an attack. If the situation was right for it, it might even be possible to move in a way that would otherwise not have been possible and inflict a fatal wound. But was that all?

[Greater Flexibility], for example, would make it easier to get into tight spaces and absorb shock when landing better than before. This kind of stuff had not been obvious in the game. So, in the future, I’d have to reevaluate my leveling strategy and take all of these factors into account.
“Mister, I’m sleepy now...”
Oh, did I let her rest too long?
Her eyes were already half closed. I still wanted to check if there were any issues with using an active skill, how long it would take to be able to use it again, and things like that...
“Okay. Go to sleep.”

I blew out the fire and lay down next to Erwen. Erwen didn’t find it strange, and neither did I. In the labyrinth, we had shown each other all kinds of sorry sights. It would be weirder to be awkward about something like this now.
Honk!
Even though I had slept for so long, my eyes slid shut once again. Tersia’s words to not sleep with Erwen came to mind, but...
Mmm, I don’t think I need to worry about that. This is probably not what she meant, anyway.
I woke up quite early in the morning. Or, well, since I had pretty much slept for two days straight, “early” wasn’t exactly the right word.
“Mister, water...”

Erwen had also just woken up, so we had a quick meal on the first floor after washing our faces. Then we headed to Erwen’s place. Because the city was so big, it took more than an hour on foot just to get there.
“I’m glad it’s at least in the same area!”

She was right. If it had been on the other side of the city, it would have taken a long time to get there, even in a carriage. Rafdonia may have been called a fortified town, but in truth, it was ridiculously big.
“You have to be quiet here. Okay? My sister is still the only one who knows about you.”
“I will.”

As I waited in an alley three blocks away from her place, Erwen struggled over with two backpacks. They were the backpacks of the leader and the crossbowman who had attacked us just before the seventh day had ended. Their weapons stuck out of the packs so they couldn’t be closed.
“I’ll hold them.”
“T-Thank you!”
She truly doesn’t know how to refuse. I swear she wasn’t like this in the beginning.
“Weapons here, armor here, tools and consumables piled separately.”
“Okay!”

When we returned to the inn, we spent some time looking through and organizing the items in the backpacks. It took about an hour, but because they were loot items, it was quite enjoyable. Erwen and I sat side by side on the bed, examining the neatly arranged items on the floor.
“Are you going to sell them all?”
“Except the necessities.”
“Then, can I keep the leather clothes and belt that you gave me?”
“Doesn’t matter. As long as you take it out of your share.”
“Then, please!”

After deciding what to sell and what not to sell, we went back out into the city. Except for extras, such as watches and compasses, we decided to share expedition gear and consumables such as potions and sell almost all of the equipment. It was better to exchange the equipment for money and buy something better than to continue using something that didn’t even fit. And it wasn’t like I couldn’t afford to do so now.
“Here it is!”

The place we arrived at was a weapon shop that Tersia had told Erwen about. The items up for sale included a Japanese-style sword, two longswords, a crossbow, a two-handed hammer, two daggers, and three throwing knives.
“The total is 350,000 stones.”

I had been kind of worried since this place was introduced to me by someone I knew, but I ended up selling everything here anyway because they gave me a better price than all the other stores I had stopped by for comparison.
As soon as we left the store, Erwen let out the awe that she had been holding back. I felt a similar sentiment.
“Mister, is this a dream?”
Excluding the stolen mana stones, the money we had earned purely through hunting for seven days was only around a hundred thousand stones. But 350,000 stones?
We hadn’t even sold the armor yet.
...Now I understood why those adventurer bastards went crazy each time they came across another person.
Equipment was money. A lot of money.
“Mister, how much is my share, then?”
A desire for money shone in Erwen’s eyes.
“Wait, we still have a lot to sell.”
Our next destination was the armor shop located ten minutes away.
“Here are 180,000 stones.”

A majority of the items had been pieces of armor, but their total value had come out to less than the weapons. I heard that the asking price was low because it was more difficult to sell used armor, which seemed a good enough explanation to me. After all, we were also selling it because of how big it was.
“I will sell for that price.”
“A straightforward personality, just like a barbarian. Please come again the next time you have something like this. I’ll give you a good price then as well.”
“I will.”
Soon after, I stopped by a general store and sold several items that I had deemed unnecessary, and in the end, I had a sizable sum of 1.45 million stones to my name. Well, not all of it was my money.
“Here. It’s forty-five thousand stones.”
“Huh? Isn’t that a bit too much?”

Even excluding the leather clothes and belt which cost twenty thousand stones, I had added exactly seven thousand stones more. Not because of her pretty face, but because that was her share if I divided the mana stones that the samurai and Skinny had by our 9:1 ratio.
