“I didn’t know exactly how much it was, so I divided up the amount we got from the samurai and Skinny.”
“Oh, I see! Thank you!”

Anyway, after all the deductions, my total assets amounted to a whopping 1.4 million stones. It was a little—no, very exciting. Even in the game, I’d never possessed this much money in the first round...
It was a good start.
“Then, let’s say goodbye here.”
“Pardon?”
Why do you look surprised? The money calculations are over, so let’s go our separate ways. I have a lot of work to do now that my plans have gone awry thanks to you.
“Well, we can head to the central square together.”
Suddenly, Erwen grew quiet. As we walked down the street, we arrived at the central plaza where the crossroads met.
“Huh? There are lots of people here all of a sudden.”

Unlike when we had passed by earlier, a crowd was swarming the plaza. Half of them were soldiers, and the other half were criminals tied with ropes. Well, “criminals” might not have been the right word.
“Mm, hmm! Ugh! Hnnnng!”

They were not violent criminals convicted of murder or arson. The crime committed by these people currently trembling in fear with gags in their mouths was a failure to pay their taxes. In other words, they had no money.

That young woman in her twenties over there, that man of childbearing age, and that old man with wrinkled hands who probably lived a more diligent life than anyone else were all being sentenced to death.
“We will begin the execution!”
When the tax collector shouted this, the soldiers shoved a man’s head under the guillotine.
And...
Slice!

The man’s head, which had been chopped off with a terrible sound, dropped perfectly into the wooden barrel in front of him. Some of the people in the crowd standing nearby soaked their bread in the spray of blood and gobbled it down in a hurry.
Erwen started malfunctioning at the bloodshed that was suddenly unfolding before her eyes.
“W-What is that! Why? Why are they dipping their bread in human blood?”
“There is a superstition that drinking the blood of a person executed by a tax collector will bring you wealth.”
Erwen frowned like she could not wrap her head around that. It seemed that was more shocking to her than chopping off someone’s head.
“Erwen, how much is the first-year tax payment?”
“For nonhuman races, it’s seven hundred thousand stones.”
“I see.”
It had been six hundred thousand stones in the game. There was a slight difference, but it was still roughly the same.
“Still, you won’t have to worry, since you earned all that money.”

Hmm? Yes, but... That was not something someone being supported by her big sister should say. Besides, I had no intention of saving this money for next year’s taxes in the first place. And the reason for that was simple.
“Erwen, how much tax is paid during the second year?”
“I think it’s eight hundred thousand stones. And there is a currency-exchange fee.”

Taxes continued to increase until a certain number of years were under one’s belt, which meant that now was the time to invest in myself. The first year, when exchange fees were waived and taxes were relatively low, was the optimal time for rapid growth.
“Ahh! H-help me...”
“Gag them properly!”
“Next month! I can pay the money next month—uh, uh! Ughh!”
Anyway, I was glad. Of all living beings, humans were the ones who were most reliant on visual information.
Slice!
Seeing this with my own two eyes made something clear to me.

Returning to the real world... Rather than aiming for such an unrealistic goal, it was necessary to set clear intermediate goals and strive for them instead. For example, assuming my life span was ninety years and that I couldn’t find a way back home and had to spend the rest of my life in this place—
How much money do I need?
Well, I’d have to do some calculations.
To live in a house with a kitchen, receive medical treatment when needed, and be able to live a leisurely life with three puppies after retiring at fifty...
“Floor six.”
By my calculations, I’d have to save like hell until retirement, so it would have to be at least the sixth floor.
Aha. So—
“Pardon? What did you just say?”
“It’s nothing.”
I had to make it at least to the sixth floor. Whether I would be able to go back home or not, however...
That’s something I can think about later.
[You have been given 630,000 stones by rank six adventurer Daria Whitember di Tersia.]
[You have sold equipment.]
[You have sold equipment.]
[Your total item level has decreased by 43.]
[You have sold equipment.]
[You have sold...]
[TIP: Your total funds are currently 1,403,520 stones. Use this to increase your character’s General Combat Power!]

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Rafdonia (3)
paragraphs: “Then I’ll be heading out now.”
“Ah, yes... Goodbye...”
After saying goodbye to Erwen, my next destination was the library.
The soothing smell of paper and ink. The quiet atmosphere forced you to hold in a sneeze. Among the other twig-like people searching for books, I felt like an outsider here, but...
Honk—!
To my surprise, there was another barbarian in the library. I reached out and poked them in the back, glad to see them.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel?!”
So it is you.
“Ainar, third daughter of Fenelin. I’m happy to see that you’re unscathed.”
“As am I!”
“...I think we need to lower our voices.”
Ainar also sensed the piercing gazes aimed at us, so she lowered her voice.
“Sorry. I was surprised because I didn’t expect to see another one of us here.”
The feeling was mutual.
“Why are you at the library?”
“Last time we met, you told me I should always think before I act, remember? While exploring the labyrinth, I felt the need for knowledge I could use to think.”
Hmm, I see.
Her determination was quite commendable... if not for the fact that she had been snoring over an open book.
“Something must have happened to you in the labyrinth.”
“It was difficult from beginning to end. Fighting wasn’t a problem, but...”
Ainar continued her thought with a grimace.
“It wasn’t just the monsters I needed to watch out for.”
She certainly was different from the other barbarians. They had only bragged about how easily they had defeated the monsters. They would never admit how hard it actually was.
“That’s why you decided to come study.”
“That’s right. But as expected, this is not a good fit for me. Reading is very difficult. I should have studied harder when I was younger.”
...Oh, so that was the root of the problem?
“So, starting today, I plan to visit the holy land and learn from the elders again. But now that I am an adult, I will have to pay a price.”
This was a little surprising. I hadn’t expected that my half-hearted advice would get someone to change so much.
Immediately after she finished speaking, Ainar closed the book she had opened and got up from her seat.
“Are you going to go right now?”
“I gotta do it when it comes to mind, so I won’t forget.”
I see. The more I got to know them, the more I thought of the barbarians as tragic.
“Then see you later.”
Ainar headed toward the exit after a brief goodbye, but then she turned around as if she had just remembered something.
“Oh! Come to think of it, I said I would repay you for the advice if I came back alive. If you ever need any help, come to the Angry Rhino Inn. Whatever it is, I will help as much as I can.”
“I will.”
I hoped she wouldn’t forget this promise within a day or two. I’d be asking for her help pretty soon.
After Ainar left, I looked around the library for a while.

It was not every day that you saw a building the size of the National Assembly being used entirely as a library. In the game, the library only ever displayed the sign “under construction” and did not let you enter.
Hmm, but how do you find a book in a place like this?
I didn’t think you could find the location with a few clicks of a keyboard like you could in modern times...
I decided to ask for help instead of spending the time trying to figure it out.
“Ahem.”
When I coughed, the librarian who had been sleeping at the desk slowly opened her eyes.
“Can I help you?”
“I am looking for a book. It’s related to history—”
“Parsytiev.”
Before I could explain what kind of book I was looking for, the sleepy-looking librarian murmured something. At the same time, a faint light entered my body.
What? Is this magic?
“Now you will be able to find the book you are looking for while you’re looking around. You can’t take the book out. And after reading it, be sure to put it back in its original place.”
As the light faded, the librarian rattled that off like a robot and then dozed off again.
...What is this woman?

I didn’t want to wake her up again, so I wandered around the library as instructed. While doing so, I came across books here and there that I felt like I was drawn to. Slowly, I quickly realized what kind of magic this was.
Demons, history, labyrinths, explorers, essence and more. As soon as the keywords in my head changed, the books that called to me did as well.
What is this convenient spell?

With magic like this, I could understand why there was only one librarian. And compared to the size of the library, there were almost no visitors in the library to begin with. Of the books, I selected only the ones that I felt the greatest attraction to and opened them one by one.
The Fallen World.
The first book was nearly seven hundred pages and described the early history of this world. Most of the content matched up with the game.

Thousands of years ago, living on this land became impossible due to a witch’s curse, and only one stronghold, Rafdonia, was able to escape that calamity. It was said that a portal to another dimension had been opened by the royal family for the citizens starving from a lack of resources. That portal had become the labyrinth of today.
The Annotated Edition of Basic Understanding of Alchemy IV.
The second book described the process through which mana stones derived from monsters were turned into bread, water, and iron. I didn’t understand any of these laws.
Still, I read whatever books I could find and drilled the knowledge into my head.
Holy War III.

From this book, I learned more about how the barbarians and elves’ relationship had reached its current state, and what the evil spirits were. People believed that evil spirits were beings that came from another dimension to possess their bodies. Well, that wasn’t completely wrong.
Demons of the Abyss.

Unfortunately, this book did not explain why evil spirits appeared in this world. However, the Rafdonian royal family and the Temple declared the evil spirits agents of annihilation and included ways to identify evil spirits written in relative detail. From the point of view of an evil spirit, this was useful information. According to the book’s contents, as long as you didn’t blurt out taboo words, you’d hardly ever be suspected of being an evil spirit. For example, “Dungeon and Stone.”
...I should also put a limit on shouting “Sparta” from now on as well.
How Have Adventurers Evolved?
The Royal Rafdonian Twins.
About A Hero.
Life in Camp Bifron.
I was able to finally get the information I wanted as I continued to read all kinds of books.
About the King’s Death.

This book dealt with the death of Ravigion III, who was called the First King and the Immortal King. However, the various suspicions surrounding it and the changes that resulted from his death were all positive. What was important to me was the timing.
Let’s see, the date was...
“It was 150 years ago...?”

It was at that moment that my hypothesis was proven correct. The book stated that the date of the king’s death was about 150 years ago. In other words, it was now 150 years after the setting of the game, as, no matter which character you chose, the game started the day after the death of Ravigion III.
God damn it. I’d have to live in the library for the time being.
“Whew...”

I closed the book and let my eyes rest. Even though I had only read the important parts, after looking through ten books, I felt like my eyes were going to fall out. But still, I decided to read the last two books I had pulled out.
Just a little more. They may have valuable information.
A Record of Dimensional Instability.
Was this the book that the blond who had saved me from crawling on three limbs had read?

The book contained cases and statistics about situations similar to mine. Just as the blond had said, falling into the outermost part of the labyrinth was something that only happened once every hundred years...
“Bullshit.”
Speaking as someone who had experienced it firsthand, there must have been a lot more of these cases. However, they were just not recorded because the people it had happened to had all dropped dead.

The rest of the book was just statistics, so I flipped through the pages and paused at the last chapter. The author’s explanation for the phenomenon was written at the end: “Entering the portal at the moment it closes may cause an instability event.” If that was true...
Ultimately, it had been my fault. Before I could get upset, I moved on to the next book.
Compilation of Rank Nine Essences.

This was finally the last book. In this book, the abilities of the essences dropped by rank nine monsters were organized like an encyclopedia, but unlike the in-game notations, the information was not provided with exact numbers.
[Goblin]
[Patience (low), Smell (low), Poison Resistance (low), Dexterity (low), Sight (low)
*When using a close-combat weapon, paralyzing poison is always applied.
*Creates traps.]

Looking through the information on other monsters, if the stat was twenty-one or higher, it seemed to be marked as medium rather than low... But there was no way to know the exact metric for a “high” ranking stat using this book. According to the information on the first page, it seemed that information on creatures above rank eight had to be purchased from an adventurer guild.
“Phew...”
I closed the book and stretched. Time flew by, and it was now dark outside the window. It was almost time for the library to close, and there were almost no visitors left.
I put all the books I had read back in their original places and returned to the inn. After a simple meal, I jumped into bed. With this, my third day in the city had passed.
“Is it twenty-seven more days...?”
The labyrinth opened at midnight on the 1st of every month. A month here was exactly thirty days, so that meant that I had to enter the labyrinth again in about four weeks.
What could I do in the city for the rest of that time? No, what should I do? As I was organizing these thoughts in my head, I quickly fell asleep.
When tomorrow comes, let’s start with finding a new ally.
“Mister! Mister! Come on, get up!”
Erwen came and knocked on my door first thing in the morning.
The excitement in her voice was one thing, but... Why the hell did she come here?
She probably wasn’t here to say that she’d follow me instead of her sister... To be honest, I had thought we wouldn’t see each other again.
“What is it?”
“Look! I succeeded in making a contract!”
As soon as the door opened, Erwen started rambling.
“Contract? Oh, have you consumed a Spirit Stone?”
Spirit Stones were items that allowed elves to make contracts with spirits of other attributes.
That is, if they were lucky....
“Yes! Yesterday, after you left, I successfully signed a contract with a new spirit!”
“You were lucky.”
Spirit Stones cost about 150,000 stones in the game, and the success rate was only 10 percent. It must have been the equivalent of gambling her entire earnings, but she had succeeded.
“Yes! I used the ones my sister bought me, and after about ten tries, it worked!”
...Fuck, was she here to mock me?

As a barbarian who had just inherited this body, I suddenly felt destitute. When we first met, I had thought she was a pitiful girl with a younger sibling to take care of, but it turned out she had been born with a silver spoon in her mouth. Her bow and arrow had probably also been given to her by her sister.
“Anyway, it looks like you made a contract with a wind spirit.”
“Yes! I was lucky in many ways. Because fire and wind go well together!”
“Okay, let’s cancel the summons first,” I said with a sigh.
I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t envious but for a different reason than this.
“Pardon? But I didn’t even get to properly show you...”
“Are you going to make more of a mess in here?”
“Oh! Sorry!”
Only then did the raging whirlwind in my room subside.
Ha... Why did I have to wake up to this mess?
I frowned, and Erwen, who was overjoyed, began to notice my reaction.
“S-Should I clean it up?”
I didn’t know why that was even a question.
Were you going to make me clean it up?

As I nodded, Erwen quickly organized the messy room. Surprisingly, it took less than ten minutes. She had said she was good at cleaning and doing laundry, and it seemed to be true. There was not a single wasted movement, just like a master in a martial arts novel.
“Should I clean up some more?”
“I’ll clean up more...”
“No. This is enough.”
To be honest, I wondered if it was even possible to tidy the room any further. For some reason, it seemed cleaner now than when I had first checked in.
Well done, let me give you a carrot. I have a favor to ask of you later as well.
“Looks like I haven’t said this yet: congratulations on making a contract with a new spirit.”
“Hehe, thank you!”
“Did you have breakfast?”
“Not yet.”
We went down to the first floor to have a meal and talked.
“What can you do with a wind spirit?”
“Change the trajectory of an arrow that has already been fired, or make it go much faster, things like that!”

Compared to what I had expected, this was a very simple, straightforward effect. Was it not possible to rotate arrows to make them penetrate deeper, or silence the arrows as they were shot? If either was possible, her combat power would increase even more.
“Uh, I hadn’t thought of that... but it should be possible?”
What’s with that tone of voice?
It got on my nerves.
“Anyway, good thing you’re here. When you’re done eating, let’s go back upstairs.”
“Pardon? Why?”
“We need to do something in the room.”
Erwen cocked her head. She looked like she had no idea what I was talking about...
“You didn’t think that you had repaid all of your debts last time, did you?”
“S-Sorry? Didn’t I?”
How naive.
Rattle!
I locked the door so no one could enter and then sat Erwen on the bed.
“Now, use your powers.”
Any difficulties using the essence’s ability, how long it took to be able to use it again, what kind of weaknesses were hidden in the stealth ability, etcetera.
There were a whole load of things I needed to learn.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: Rafdonia (4)
paragraphs: “Good job. You can leave now.”
“Goodbye!”
Erwen did not argue and quickly prepared to leave. It seemed that the half-day I had spent studying her abilities had taken quite a toll...
“I’ll be back!”
You’re coming back? Oh, I forgot to mention.
“You don’t have to make time to come all the way over here anymore.”
“Ehhhh?”
Why are you surprised? This is normal. You are no longer my teammate.
“You will need some time to get used to your new ability. It would be better to spend your time before the labyrinth opens again more productively.”
Strictly speaking, that advice applied to me as well.
Yesterday, I set a new goal for myself: become a middle-class adventurer and reach the eighth floor.

So, there was much work to be done going forward. First, I had to use three million stones to develop my abilities. If possible, I also wanted to receive professional combat training. I hadn’t been able to fully utilize the abilities of this monstrous body yet. In addition, I needed to acquire common sense and common knowledge of this world by reading more books and taking time to wander around the city as much as possible to adjust to the city’s prices and culture.
In short, I had no business fooling around with Erwen.
“Yes! T-That’s true.”
“You said you have a younger sibling. You should spend time with them since you will be back in the labyrinth in three weeks.”
“Right...”
Erwen nodded with a sullen look on her face.
Is it because I was her first ally?
She seemed to have some strange fantasies about me. To be honest, I could kind of guess what kind of fantasies they were. But business relationships lasted longer.
“I plan to stay here until then, so if anything goes wrong, don’t hesitate to come find me here. I will help out as much as I can.”
“R-Really?”
“Aren’t we comrades?”
“Hehe, we are! Okay!”
As soon as I tossed in that extra tidbit, Erwen left with a satisfied look on her face. She was still easy to handle.

Since things had turned out like this, I decided to keep this friendship with Erwen going. This was also its own kind of networking. I may not have had blood ties here, but relationships with locals could be acquired.
Perhaps they would be of use someday.
“...Does that make me a social climber?”

Well then, let it be so. This was not the time to be picky. After a quick shower, I went straight to the library again. I read books for about five or six hours after the lazy librarian I had seen the day before cast her spell on me.
Is there a restaurant here that sells beef stew?

It was a little late, but for lunch, I headed to a cheap-looking restaurant and took care of lunch with a thick stew and a few slices of bread. The price was 450 stones. It seemed to me that it would be more cost-efficient to have meals back at the inn.
“It’s Bjorn, son of Yandel, the Greatest Warrior!”
After eating, I visited the Angry Rhinos Inn where Ainar was staying. Surprisingly, it was crawling with barbarians.
“Are you here to stay at this inn too? Good idea, man! It’s only 300 stones a day!”
What, 300 stones?

Surprised by the unbelievable price, I looked into it and found there was definitely a reason for that number. As soon as you entered one of the rooms, which had five narrow beds, the thick scent of sweat that had been ripening for several days filled your nose.
“Are five people sharing a room?”
“No! Ten warriors are staying together!”
“...But there are only five beds?”
“We set a time and take turns sleeping!”
So it was not that it was cheap, it was just that several people were paying for it. These guys had each earned thirty to forty thousand stones at most, so they probably didn’t have a choice.
“But what brings you here?”
“I am looking for Fenelin’s third daughter, Ainar.”
“Fenelin’s second daughter, Ainar, headed out in the morning!”
Right. Second daughter. I shouldn’t have changed it at the last minute.
Anyway, after waiting for about an hour, Ainar returned.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel? Did something happen?”
As a barbarian herself, she got straight to the point.
“I want to fight you.”
“Are you talking about a match?”
“Yes.”
What I currently needed was training. In the labyrinth, I had accomplished more than any other barbarian, but in terms of pure combat skill alone, I was no match for them.
“How strange.”
Ainar cocked her head in confusion, though I didn’t think it was because it was a difficult request to fulfill...
“If that’s the case, why not just go out to the yard instead of asking me?” she said.
Yard?
Soon Ainar led me out through the inn’s backdoor. Around fifteen barbarians were already gathered there, sweating as they threw fists and rolled together on the floor...even shedding some blood.
“Ha ha ha ha! Your punch just now was pretty strong!”
“So was yours!”

No wonder it had been so noisy this whole time. While elves just chatted about the voices of the spirits, this was what barbarians’ daily life looked like. While I watched the barbarians flashing pained smiles and fighting as viciously as if they were facing off against life-long enemies, Ainar asked, “Is there a reason why you have to face me?”
As a matter of fact, there was not. I just thought that Ainar would grant my request. But it would seem strange if I said no here.
“Because you’re the only one who uses a sword.”
“Do you want to learn how to fight a swordsman?”
“Yes.”
“If that’s the reason, okay. I have to learn the alphabet in the morning, so come here around this time and I will face you as much as you want.”
In other words, her schedule was free after five o’clock. From now on, I would visit this place every day.
“You want to start today?”
“Of course.”
I waited for a bit while Ainar went back to her room and came back with her sword.
“Ainar and Bjorn are going to face off!”
The other barbarians stopped fighting and came to watch.
I had come here to learn, but I had no intention of getting utterly defeated, so I grabbed my shield and readied myself. However, the end result was...
“Then here I go!”
She completely pummeled me. It took maybe three minutes for me to drop the shield after getting the crap beaten out of me.
Ainar fought really well. Still, it was a good experience in many ways.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, was not the greatest warrior of all time!”
“Now Ainar is the greatest warrior ever!”
“Ahhh!”
Except for these bastards.
How many more strikes had I taken since? Soon the sky turned dark.
“You want to do more? I would like a break sometime soon.”
“No. Today’s match will end here.”
The other barbarians had already left the yard. After much deliberation, I made a decision.
“Ainar.”
“What is it?”
Ainar, who was walking toward the building, stopped and stretched.
“Are you planning on entering the labyrinth alone next time as well?”
“Yes. I don’t have enough money to build a party. If possible, I want to try the second floor this time.”
Once again, I realized how hardcore these barbarians were.

A compass and a torch. With just these two things, they could advance to the second floor. But to make enough money to buy consumables during the first expedition, and go straight to the next floor with that money...
“Wouldn’t it be difficult on your own?”
“I have no choice.”
No choice, huh...

Perhaps this was the reason why the lower floor was only populated by humans. Otherworldly races, whose taxes were several times higher than humans, could not pay their annual taxes simply by operating on the first and second floors. That much was clear from my barbarian colleagues. The guy who had earned the most out of them had earned just over twenty thousand stones.
“If I am lucky, I may even be able to find other barbarians on the first floor and form a party.”
“I see.”
“So, what did you want to say?”
As my point was getting longer, Ainar immediately got straight to it.
So, like a barbarian, I said outright, “Ainar, would you like to be my comrade?”
“Comrade?”
“I will bear the cost of setting up the party.”

I had felt it after going against her a few times today. Ainar was strong. Based on what the others had said, it seemed that she was at the top of the class among the barbarians. And, on top of all that, she was pretty smart.
“Thanks for the offer, but why?”
Well, you needed a teammate. It was hard work to look for a night companion every night, and having a partner increased your profits.

Plus, Ainar was not only powerful in combat, but she also came with the advantage of me not having to worry about being betrayed due to the nature of barbarians. Our classes would overlap, but... since Erwen was gone, Ainar was the best option I had.
Of course, there was no need for a long explanation.
“I just want to.”
“I see.” Ainar nodded and immediately came to a decision. “Fine. Entering the labyrinth with a clever warrior like you is what all warriors wish for.”
This was a much more positive response than I had expected. Could I be a bit greedier?
“However, there is a condition.”
“What is it?”
“I take eighty percent.”
Ainar frowned at my abuse of power.
Did that offend her?
I opened my mouth again and continued to explain.
“I’ll pay the cost of forming a party. And I promise, even with that ratio, you will make much more money than if you went into the labyrinth alone. Besides, I’ll pay for all the other supplies—”
“Stop, no further explanation needed. Even if you explain it, I won’t understand. So pay me as you like. I trust you.”
“I see.”
I had no choice but to admit that I had underestimated the barbarians.
“I will be indebted to you, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
Soon after, Ainar came over and slapped me hard on the back. It was too powerful to be considered a gesture of goodwill by most normal people, but...
Well, I had better get used to it quickly.
“I’ll do my best.”
I now had a reliable barbarian ally.
The next morning, I visited the holy land with Ainar.

The holy land was a community childcare facility. Barbarians who left for the city sent their children here. Because they had to be warriors until the day they died, they didn’t have the ability to raise children. And once those barbarians grew up and left for the city as adults, the cycle repeated. However, that was not something I needed to worry about right now.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
Upon arrival, the chieftain came over to greet us.
Shit, this was why I had wanted to avoid coming here as much as possible...
“It is rare for a warrior who has left the nest to come visit. Have you come to learn to read like Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin?”
Calming my racing heart, I shook my head.
“No, Chief, the reason I came to the holy land is a different one.”
“A different reason...”
The chieftain looked at me with curiosity in his eyes.
Don’t be nervous.
Hadn’t I learned things like how barbarians spoke and what titles they used from Ainar right before this? Just don’t make any mistakes.
“Tell me what it is.”
I took a deep breath and said calmly, “I want to imprint a soul.”
Different races had different characteristics. For example, elves made deals with spirits, and dwarves dealt with artifacts.
Similarly, Barbarians had the [Soul Imprint.]

It was a way of gaining power that couldn’t be used at the beginning of the game because it required a lot of money... But luckily, I now had a whopping million stones. So, after much thought, I had come to a decision.
Although it was still terrifying to stand in front of this fucking chieftain bastard...
“To be more precise, I want to receive the [Imprint of Immortality.]”
There was no doubt. This was the best way to spend my money.

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Level Up (1)
paragraphs: The chief’s eyes narrowed, and very fiercely at that.
“Where did you hear about the Spirit Imprint? It’s not something a young warrior like you should know about.”

Of course, the place I had originally learned about it was the game. There was no way that I, a pro gamer, could be oblivious to such a basic thing. I didn’t have to admit that, however, because I had already confirmed that this information could easily be found in books at the library.
“I read it in a book,” I said bluntly. “In the book, it said that Spirit Imprints were a great help in fighting the elves during the War of Sacred Relics—”
“Hahaha!”
Interrupting my words, the chieftain burst into laughter. To be honest, it was fucking scary, but I thankfully didn’t end up pissing my pants because the laughter sounded quite joyous.
“You read a book? How funny! Both you and Ainar—how strange it is to have two odd students like you show up at the same time!”
Fortunately, in the eyes of the chieftain, we were just young barbarians full of a desire for knowledge.
“...If the contents of the book are true, I want to receive this secret art.”
“Of course, I have no reason to refuse a Spirit Imprint if a warrior demands it! But young warrior, there is a problem!”
“A problem?”
“It costs a lot of money.”
Dang, I had been scared for no reason. Why was he saying something as obvious as that in such an ominous tone?

A Spirit Imprint required a lot of expensive ingredients. The problem with higher-level imprints was not the cost of the ingredients, but that if there were no ingredients available, there were a lot of things you’d have to collect.
“Hahaha! It’s commendable that you’ve come this far after reading a book, but it seems you haven’t learned everything yet!”
“I have money. How much is it?”
The chief looked at me like I was a clueless child.
“The cost of an Immortality Imprint is, well, about eight hundred thousand stones!”
I frowned. Ugh, that was 150,000 stones more expensive than the game, but still, I could pay for it.
“I’ll pay.”
“What?”
“...You will?”
The chieftain and Ainar both shouted at the same time.
Before they could bombard me with questions, I opened my pouch and took out one five-hundred-thousand stone and three one-hundred-thousand stones. At this, suspicion appeared in the chieftain’s eyes.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, where did you get so much money?”
It would have been a shame if he hadn’t asked. I had even planned my lines in advance and rehearsed the story with Erwen.

Gruffly, I explained that I ran into an elf on the first floor and had been treating her like a slave when an essence happened to appear in front of her by chance. Then I made her sister pay the price for it...
“Hahaha! Those idiots!”
“You’re the first to ever rob those sly fern faces, Bjorn, son of Yandel!”

The barbarians liked this story even more than I expected. Not just Ainar and the chief of the tribe, either—the elders who hadn’t been anywhere near us also came over to laugh. Did they really have that much bad blood with the elves?
“Hahaha! I don’t know how long it’s been since I’ve laughed like that!”
Soon the chieftain took six hundred thousand stones from my hand.
Huh? I’m sure he just said eight hundred thousand stones...
As I cocked my head, the chieftain patted my shoulder.
“Consider it a gift, for a young warrior who has shown the mark of greatness!”
It felt like my shoulder had just been dislocated, but the reward was sweet. Shit, two hundred thousand stones with just a few words!

Our chieftain’s personality was as fiery as any barbarian’s. I cried out with all my heart, “From now on, I will make sure to become an even greater warrior by screwing over even more fern faces that come my way!”
“I look forward to it, Bjorn, son of Yandel, young warrior!”
Was this what people meant when they said, “The more I look at it, the more attractive it is?”
I was gradually starting to take a liking to the barbarians.

A Spirit Imprint was a kind of strengthening technique. The idea behind it was that it bestowed a special ability on a person’s body by infusing the “spirit” present in a magical ingredient into the body. It was also the reason why all barbarians were covered in tattoos.

I think I read somewhere that they had to be tattooed as infants while they still had relatively clean souls so that the soul pathways could be completed in adulthood. That was definitely the gist I got from it.
“I will give you one more chance to reconsider. If you choose this path, you cannot receive the imprint of another path. Will you still continue?”
“Of course.”

I knew about all the other paths, so there would be no changing my decision. The higher-level Immortality Imprint was at the core of my leveling method and even disregarding that, all the abilities you gained from the Immortality Imprint were mostly higher-quality ones.
“It seems that the elders have arrived, so you should go now.”
“I will.”
After Ainar left, the chieftain took me to the shaman’s tent. Then, the ritual officially began.
“Hmm, your pathways are fairly clean. If you continue to keep your heart pure, this spirit will provide you with great power in the future.”
The blindfolded shaman spoke words I couldn’t understand and poked a needle into the tattoo on my upper body. And...
“Ughhh...”
“Young warrior, do not hold back. You may scream. They all do.”
“Aaargh!”
It felt like a pain ten times as strong as any healing potion was overwhelming my body.
Damn it, I had thought it was just a regular tattoo. Would I have to go through this pain every time I went up to a higher level?
“Okay, it’s over. I’m tired, so you may leave.”
By the time the shaman uttered the words I had been waiting for, it was already dark outside. The chief of the tribe, who had brought me here, was nowhere to be seen.
“Thank you.”
“This is the first time a warrior has ever thanked a shaman,” he chuckled.
Hmm? Did I do something wrong?
I didn’t know, but I got out of the tent before he could get suspicious.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 1. Your healing factor has greatly increased.]
[Your Physique stat has increased by +20.]

Although I was mentally exhausted, strangely, my body was full of energy. Was this the power of a spirit? It felt very strange. I could almost feel an unknown presence in my body. I should look into it in more detail later.
“Open the door!”
After leaving the holy land and returning to the inn, I tested my newly acquired abilities a few times, then collapsed and fell asleep.

Another day passed and morning came. I went back to the shopping district I had visited with Erwen the other day. I wanted to invest the remaining nine hundred thousand stones I had thanks to the chieftain’s discount in myself.
“You’re the one who came in the other day. Are you looking to sell again?”
“No, this time I came to buy.”

I needed a new weapon. I had sold the hammer I had gotten from the heartstealer along with the other equipment from my stint in the dungeon. The hammer hadn’t felt bad in my hands, but the handle was too long for it to be used as a one-handed weapon, which made it awkward for me.
“I want to see one-handed blunt weapons.”
“One-handed blunts...”

As a result of my battle with Ainar, I had decided that something like that suited me better than something sharp. Sword-type weaponry required skill and technique. Well, there’s nothing you can’t achieve with enough practice, but...

The weapon itself would only be used in the earlier levels anyway, so it was pointless to spend too much time learning it. After all, once I managed to acquire a particular essence, I was just going to focus on using the shield.
“Hmm.”
The clerk studied me before showing me a one-handed blunt that didn’t look like a one-handed blunt. The lightest one seemed to be three times heavier than the two-handed hammer I had sold.
This is a one-handed weapon?
“These are all one-handed blunt weapons favored by barbarians.”
Oh, yeah, those guys would go crazy over these.
Even my shield was a simple piece of equipment made of a lump of iron, but...
“I want something a little more plain.”
“Understood.”
I didn’t need something as flashy as the ones he had shown me. Weapons like that would prove to have a destructive power in each blow that was several times stronger than my last weapon, but...

The monsters on the first floor were already one-shot kills. It wasn’t like I was going to fight against any large monsters, so there was a strong possibility that carrying a weapon like that would just end up being cumbersome.
Soon, the clerk brought out new weapons.
“How about these?”
Of course, these were also not at all standard, but for a barbarian’s body, they were just right. I chose a mace of moderately average size.
“How much is this?”
“It’s 250,000 stones.”
What, 250,000? Just the other day, I sold six weapons for only 350,000!
When I frowned, the clerk explained, “The crafting of the weapon itself is not difficult, but there’s a lot of iron that goes into making it, so the price can’t be helped.”
Oh, I see.
I accepted that explanation. Although, not without complaints.
“If you adjust the price to 220,000 stones, I will buy it right away.”
When I tried to haggle, the clerk gave me a curious look.
...What kind of a pushover life did these barbarians lead?
“No one else will buy this kind of weapon anyway.”
“Many barbarians often come in looking for things like this.”
Well, maybe if it’s the first weapon you show them.

The barbarians I knew wouldn’t pick something so middling. Most importantly, most barbarians preferred a sharp-bladed weapon like an axe rather than a blunt weapon. When I threw this reasoning out there, the clerk agreed to the barter so easily that it almost took the wind out of my sails.
“All right. I’ll sell it for 220,000 stones.”
...Maybe I should’ve said two hundred thousand.
[Total Item Level has increased by +85.]
Anyway, after that, I went around and bought two additional pieces of equipment.
First, a half armor set.
[Total Item Level has increased by +57.]

It was shaped like a bulletproof vest but made of a flat iron plate. The price was 360,000 stones, and I was able to get it at a lower price because there happened to be one in stock that was just the right size for me. If it had been made-to-order, I would have paid twice as much... like the helmet I bought next.
“It will take three days. Write down your address and I’ll have someone deliver it to you.”

In the case of helmets, they had to be made to order because they had to fit snugly on the head. Instead of giving up on my plan altogether, I was able to reach an agreement at the relatively low price of 170,000 stones.
[Total Item Level has increased by +47.]
As a result, I had about fifty thousand stones left.
...I don’t think I’ll be able to eat any more meat any time soon.
My daily routine was this:
Wake up at 7 a.m., then breakfast with Erwen.
“Wow, today’s stew even has potatoes!” she cheered.
“But why do you eat breakfast here every day?” I replied.
“It’s delicious and cheap!”
After eating, I headed straight to the library. If I walked slowly, I could head in as soon as it opened at eight o’clock.
“Parsytiev.”
By now, I was used to being on the receiving end of the chronically tired librarian lady’s spell.
“Good luck, then.”
Of course, we still hadn’t had a proper conversation yet.
Growl!
After reading until 4 p.m., if possible, I always tried to eat a simple meal at a restaurant I’d never been to.
Mm, this place is expensive but bland.
But there were a lot of adventurers around, so it was a good place to eavesdrop on their conversations.
“Is Ainar not here yet?”
“No! Until she comes, I will face you!”

After the meal, I headed to the barbarian dormitory and made it there around 5 p.m. After my seventh day of training, I started sparring with the other barbarians as well. Like them, I took off my shirt, swung my fists, strangled their necks, and fought fiercely.

Although it was far from the refined fighting style I was expecting... The matches with the barbarians, whose instincts and intuitions were extremely well developed, were a great help to me in the end since I was a barbarian too.
[Reflexes have improved slightly with repeated training.]
[Flexibility has improved slightly with repeated training.]
[Perception has...]
[Your Physique stat has increased by +1.]
Now I had a better sense of how to use this body.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, has won!”
“The greatest warrior ever!”

Even without the help of the new equipment, I occasionally won against Ainar. She was definitely skilled, but her weakness was that her fight pattern was always the same. I gave her some tips about that, but it seemed it had already become an ingrained habit that she wouldn’t be able to easily fix.
“I’m tired! I am going to sleep!”
“Me too!”
“A wise warrior knows when to rest!”

By 9 p.m., all the spars, which were more like actual battles, ended. Then, I took my sweaty and dirt-covered body back to the inn. By the time I finished washing up, Erwen dropped by to see me again.
“Mister! Hurry up and take a bath! The food is going to get cold!”
“Okay.”
Not every day, but about five times a week, we would meet once more in the evening to eat and chat. Most of the conversations were about normal things like what Erwen did and how she felt that day.
“Aren’t you tired of walking an hour to come here?”
“No? The food here is cheap and delicious!”
“Cheap and delicious,” she says.
I didn’t know why she was here when she had an older sister who made a lot of money.
“Thank you for the meal!”
By the time we finished eating, it was around 11 p.m. At this point, Erwen usually headed back to her inn.
“Good night, then. Oh, and I can’t come tomorrow.”
“Even if you did come, I wouldn’t be able to see you anyway. After all, we’ll both be busy tomorrow.”
Up to this point, this had been my daily routine.
After checking the time, I quickly went up to my room and fell straight into the bed. A month had already passed. And...
About twenty-four hours remained before the labyrinth opened.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 1
Physique: 46 (New +21)
Spirit: 36
Special Ability: 1
Item Level: 202 (New +185)
General Combat Power: 133.5 (New +67.25)]

chapters.title: Chapter 22: Level Up (2)
paragraphs: Library, get used to the city, combat training.
Today, I skipped this daily routine I had been completing every day for the past month. That wasn’t what an adventurer should be doing on the day the labyrinth opened.

As soon as I woke up, I skipped breakfast and ran to the meeting place I had agreed on with Ainar. I was running because I had been told that I would have to wait several hours if I was even a little late.
“Here! Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
To my surprise, Ainar was there before me.
“...When did you get here?”
“You said you’d leave me behind if I was late, so I slept right here! Come on! We are first!”

Even though it was thirty minutes before opening, there was already a long line in front of the entrance. However, thanks to Ainar’s dedication, we were able to enter the Adventurers’ Guild as soon as the door opened.
“What can I help you with?”
“We have come to receive a binding spell.”
“Are there two people in your party?”
“That’s right.”
“Please place your hands here.”
When we followed the instructions, a faint greenish light emanated from the crystal ball.
“Two rank nine adventurers... The cost is fifteen thousand stones.”
Fifteen thousand stones... If I hadn’t made sure to budget my food money, things would have been a little tight. I obediently opened my stone pouch and paid the price.

It left a bitter taste in my mouth, but it was an inevitable expense. When someone entered the labyrinth, their starting point was random. But with this spell, we could at least spawn in the same place.
“How do you rank an adventurer?”
“It’s measured by the total amount of essence engraved on their soul.”
“I see. So does the cost of a bond increase as someone’s rank goes up?”
“Of course.”
Ha, now this part didn’t have to be exactly the same as the game.
“All done. Please note that this will only last for the next twenty-four hours.”
“All right.”
It was a little past nine o’clock when we finished our business and left the Adventurers’ Guild.
“Let’s go back to my inn for dinner. The food is pretty good.”
“Inn? The inn provides food?”
What kind of life has she been leading?
When I indirectly asked her this, Ainar’s reply was nonchalant. “I usually buy the same bread I ate in the labyrinth.”
Ah, the one that cost twenty stones each.
I had tried to do the same once to save money on food, but gave up after a while. I didn’t know how it worked, but what had been quite edible in the labyrinth was hard as stone out here.
That’s why it’s even called stone bread...
But seriously, she had eaten only that for a month? I felt bad for her, so I ordered her both meat and a stew, and Ainar responded with an oath of allegiance.
“Bjorn! I will jump into a pit of fire if you ask me to! So don’t leave me!”
After a tearful meal, we went up to the room and took time to organize our backpacks.
“Make sure you have everything. If we forget to bring something and end up needing it, it will be a problem.”
“Don’t worry! I have nothing to bring with me!”
Time passed surprisingly quickly as I inspected my equipment and put the adventuring supplies and consumables into my backpack.
“Let’s get some sleep now, then.”
“I have never seen such a soft bed. It looks wide enough for two people! It doesn’t even smell!”

After organizing everything we needed to be able to enter the labyrinth at any moment, we laid down next to each other and went to sleep. But the bed was pretty cramped with Ainar next to me. When I laid down with Erwen, there was still room left.
“Even if you can’t sleep, force yourself to get some rest. We won’t be able to sleep properly for a while—”
Mm, what was I worried about again?
Rumbleee—!
Before I could even finish my words, there was a typical barbarian-style snore coming from beside me.
I smiled and closed my eyes as well. Time flew by.
We woke up a little early and had our last meal on the first floor of the inn, a special, luxurious meal of eight hundred stones per person.
“What is this taste?” Ainar, who had been fawning throughout the entire meal, took a bite of the cream pie that was being served as dessert and froze. “I-Is this magic? I cannot stop crying.”
“Ah, that’s called ‘sweetness.’”
“I feel like I should work really hard in the future...”
It wasn’t intentional, but I think the meal gave her the exact motivation she needed.
“Let’s go.”

As we grabbed our bags and headed out into the dark streets, we saw a lot of people walking outside, which was different than usual. Most were armed like me and carried a large backpack. But not everyone was like that, and there were also some barbarians with just a single weapon on their person. It seemed they had just finished their coming-of-age ceremony and arrived in the city today...
“Stop! I think we are lost.”
“Unbelievable! We must get to the labyrinth within the set time!”
“Partun does not deserve to be the leader!”
So this happens every month, huh. How do these barbarians even get to the labyrinth every time?
I was seriously contemplating this when Ainar approached them and gave them advice.
“If you follow them, you will reach the labyrinth.”
The young warriors looked at her the same way you’d look at a successful senior and thanked her.
“Thank you. We will definitely repay this favor!”
As she watched barbarians disappear into the distance, Ainar rubbed her nose.
“Haha... reminds me of how things used to be.”
Please don’t pretend like this is a thing of the past.
It seemed to me that nothing had changed since then.
“Everyone, back away!”
Thousands of people had already gathered in Dimension Square. As we sat in the crowd and waited for midnight to arrive, a light burst into life in the center of the square.
Although it was small at first, the glow quickly grew in size and rippled into the form of a sphere.
“You can enter now!”
When the guide shouted this, the adventurers in the surrounding area quickly threw themselves into the portal. I led Ainar to the outskirts to avoid the crowd.
“Bjorn, aren’t we going in?”
“Just wait.”

The adventurers gathered in the square disappeared by the dozen every second. But the square was still crowded because of the other adventurers who continued to arrive on time, one after another. Forty minutes after the portal opened, the crowded square had quieted down, and the line now consisted of seven to eight hundred people.
“...Shouldn’t we go in now?”
The portal, which had already devoured tens of thousands of adventurers, was now smaller in size.
But I kept waiting.
Ainar picked up on my expression and when she next spoke, her tone was different. “Bjorn, what are you waiting for?”
Mm, it’s kind of a long story... and I don’t know if it will work or not.
However, I decided to give her a brief explanation as we had quite a bit of time left.
“I plan to enter when the dimensional portal is unstable. The book says it only happens once in a hundred years, but if we take advantage of this phenomenon—”
“I don’t know what that means, but I will follow your lead.” I stared at her, and she added, “I have a feeling I won’t understand your explanation anyway!”
I had honestly figured that would be the case. It was annoying that she was saying that after asking me first, but... Honestly, it was quite convenient to not have to explain my every action.
“The gate will be closed soon! Stand back!”
Eventually, the portal’s light began to fade. There were no adventurers left at this point. Only then did I slowly walk toward the labyrinth with Ainar.
The guide spotted us and shouted, “It is dangerous to enter now!”
I pretended not to hear.
I don’t know why they’re saying it’s dangerous.
I didn’t understand why they thought that. Seeing that there were even published books with this information in them, others must have been aware of this phenomenon too...
“B-Bjorn! That official-looking person says it’s dangerous! We have to move back!”
So why is no one taking advantage of it?
One second, two seconds, three seconds...
Mm, maybe counting down was pointless. When I got a strong feeling that it had been long enough—
“Now’s the time. Let’s go in.”
Squeal.
I gave Ainar a shove in the back and entered the labyrinth.
Flash—!
A flash of light obscured my vision, and when I reopened my eyes, a thick darkness greeted me. This meant my plan had worked.
“See! I can’t see in front of me! We should have listened to the official-looking person! Bjorn is stupid!”
“Ainar, calm down.”
Ainar regained some composure when I hurriedly lit the torch I was keeping in my backpack.
“W-What’s going on?”
“Even if I tell you, you won’t understand.”
“...That’s true!”
Having easily convinced Ainar, I slowly studied our surroundings. And, when I spotted a statue located in front of a dead end, I was overcome by a strange feeling.

It seemed that the dimensional instability phenomenon indeed strongly correlated to the time you entered the portal. That fact was both pleasing and upsetting. It meant that if I had made the decision to enter the labyrinth just a minute earlier during my first trip inside, I wouldn’t have destroyed my leg and had to crawl on three limbs!
Whooosh!
As soon as I set my hand on the headstone, a beam of light burst out of it and turned into a circle.
“What is this?”
“It is a portal to the second floor.”
In other words, we had skipped having to navigate with a compass, fight all the monsters we encountered, and wander our way through the dark. With this, we had saved at least a day or two.
“What?! The chieftain said it would take three days to find the portal! What magic have you used?”
Even if I tell you, you won’t understand.
[You have opened a portal for the first time. EXP +2]
[You have leveled up.]
[Your Spirit stat has increased by +10.]
[The maximum number of essences you can absorb has increased by +1.]
In order to become a pro, you have to take advantage of the bugs.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 2 (New +1)
Physique: 46
Spirit: 36
Special Ability: 4 (New +3)
Item Level: 202
General Combat Power: 136.5 (New +3)]
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
I found myself hanging about ten feet in the air for a moment, but I quickly found my balance and landed on two feet.
Tap!
Yeah, I had practiced while wrestling the barbarians.
“Ugh!”
As I watched Ainar fall on her butt, I realized how far I had come and began to understand why Erwen had laughed at me.
“Ugh... my butt is numb.”
It was pretty fun to watch. Well, with her reflexes, she’d learn to land properly soon enough.
“What is that?” she asked. “That disappointed expression on your face?”
“It’s nothing.”

Glossing over that question, I took out my watch and set it to 00:05. I should’ve done it the moment I opened my eyes, but I had forgotten to. Still, I set it five minutes faster, so there wouldn’t be any issues down the line.
“...Ainar, can you feel it too?”
“What do you mean?”
“It feels like my heart is vibrating.”

If I had to put it into words, it felt as if something dense had entered my veins and was now filling my body. It had been like that from the moment I had crossed through the portal, and now I felt it very clearly.
What could it be?
After explaining the symptoms to Ainar, she quickly came up with a diagnosis.
“Looks like the Dignity of Soul has increased! Congratulations!”
Ah, I’d leveled up.

Dungeon and Stone also had levels, and Dignity of Soul was based on level. In other words, MP, the resource required to use this ability, increased as your Dignity of Soul did, and the total amount of essences you could absorb also increased.

For example, at level one I could only have absorbed one essence, but as I had now become level two, it was now possible for me to absorb a maximum of two. Well, either way, that only mattered if I had an essence to begin with.
“Interesting. You haven’t fought any monsters, yet your Dignity of Soul has risen!”
“It’s not a surprise. It’s just that I achieved being the first person to open the portal.”
Achievements were what gave you experience points in this world.
“Um, is that even an achievement?”

It was. Once you reached a certain level, speedrunning to get to portals as fast as possible was the easiest way to increase your experience points. That was because Dungeon and Stone was a game with a slightly unusual leveling system. You could only gain experience points from each monster once, and only for the first kill. Therefore, like filling out a sticker book, you could only level up by defeating different kinds of monsters.
Uh, wait, isn’t this a bit dangerous?
“...Ainar, this needs to be a secret between you and me. Got it?”
“A secret? What’s the secret?”
“That I was the first one to open the portal. This one thing. If anyone asks, say that it took us two days to get to the second floor.”
The experience gained from opening a portal was only +2. In other words, it was only about the same as killing two rank-nine monsters, but...
Unlike monsters, you can collect EXP for this over and over again.

Therefore, adventurers who had reached a certain level ended up speedrunning because the monsters they had left to hunt were limited. This also depended on the nature of the god worshiped by a party’s priest, how compatible they were with the monster, the area in which they were active, and the presence of a wizard. When you were faced with a wall, the only way to break through the wall was with backbreaking hard work. But was that possible as a newbie?
Only I could know this trick, because if it was common knowledge, it would definitely not end well for me.
“I swear on a warrior’s honor.”
Was the look on my face too serious?
Ainar’s expression had changed and, even though I hadn’t asked for one, she had made me an oath. Thanks to this, I felt a lot better, but I knew we needed to move quickly.
“We should get out of here.”

In a few hours, other adventurers would enter the second floor. And when they saw two beginners here, they’d start to have suspicions. ‘Who are you that you got here earlier than we did?’ Yeah, it was best not to be seen at all.
As always, I was more afraid of those asshole adventurers than the actual monsters.

chapters.title: Chapter 23: Level Up (3)
paragraphs: I inserted the torch into the groove carved onto my helmet and tied it tightly with a rope. I called this Barbarian Candle Mode.
...It was kind of humiliating, but it was a practical method used by other adventurers.
Ainar brought her hand to the flickering flame and exclaimed, “Oh, amazing! It really isn’t hot!”
That’s because it’s a magical tool.

Measuring in at only the length of a palm, the torch did not reduce the user’s mobility, and it was a useful item that could be maintained for about three days once lit. The crossbow group had used it too.
The average price was about ten thousand stones, though...
I suddenly missed Erwen.
“But where are we?”
Slowly, Ainar started to take in her surroundings, looking around.

Even though there was a huge gulf between the 2D pixel graphics I was familiar with and the world I could see in front of me, it was easy to figure that out this time around. The black ground that slurped with every step, the remnants of stone ruins that could be seen everywhere, and even the mournful cry that could be faintly heard in the distance...
“This is the Land of the Dead.”
“Ah, so this is where the ghouls and the death fiends come out!”
That was true. To be precise, the monsters that appeared here were elder ghouls, skeletons, banshees, and even a type of intermediate boss-like monster, dullahans.
“I will take the lead.”
The combat power of the monsters in the Land of the Dead was much higher than in the Goblin Forest. But as for which was trickier, I’d say the Goblin Forest took the win.
It was a lot darker here, but... at least it didn’t have any traps. This kind of place was much more well-suited for two barbarians working together.
“It’s a ghoul.”
Before long, we encountered monsters. Their numbers were less than three. Of course, by the third day, the spawn rate would increase to three times what it was now.
Yet another reason to move.
“Bjorn, there is a mana stone!”
“Take whatever you see. You don’t have to report every item to me. We can distribute it later. Let’s speed up.”
Unlike in the Goblin Forest, I immediately left the beginning of the map and continued to move north.
Then, I heard a scream nearby.
“Kyaaargh!”
“B-B-Bjorn?!”
“It’s a howling banshee. Just ignore it. They rarely attack first.”
“O-Okay... But shouldn’t we kill it? It could be dangerous.”
Well. Not unless there’s an Erwen nearby who can control a spirit.
Two physical-type adventurers would never be able to catch a banshee no matter what we did. And even if we did manage to catch it, that was a problem in itself.
“If you attack a banshee first, you will be cursed.”
“Cursed?”
“It is a curse known as the Mark of Resentment. The banshee will continue to chase after you until you escape the labyrinth.”

Unless you were planning to hunt solely banshees for the next ten days, it was best not to touch one at all. If experience points were the goal, a common strategy was to take down just one or two on the very last day.
“You are a very wise warrior. I’m glad I followed you.”
Thank you for the compliment.
She tried not to show it, but it was obvious that these sorts of things scared her.
But that was neither here nor there.
“Kyaaah!”
Crush!
Please stop clinging to me every time something makes a sound, I thought. It was uncomfortable, but most importantly... it felt like my arm was breaking.
“L-let go... It’s a skeleton.”

At the same time, a group of skeletons appeared, making a rattling noise. There were ten of them. Even on the first day, the skeletons appeared in large numbers, fitting for a monster that boasted high reserves. Nonetheless, the total number of mana stones you could receive from a group of this size was only three or four.
“Ahem! I will get rid of them!”
Maybe she felt embarrassed about being scared of the banshee’s screams because Ainar jumped forward.
Tsk tsk, I clicked my tongue inwardly.
“Ainar! If you look between the ribs, you’ll see their essence. To take down a skeleton with a sword, you’ll need to aim for that, but—”
Crunch!
“Huh? Did you say something?”
“...I didn’t say anything. Don’t worry about me.”
Crunch! Crack! Crack!
Who cared about weaknesses? Whenever Ainar swung that enormous greatsword, the skeletons were mercilessly crushed, never to rise up again.
[You have killed an Elder Ghoul. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Skeleton. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Skeleton Warrior. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Skeleton Archer. EXP +1]

We moved north like that for about eight hours. Naturally, we encountered a variety of new monsters. An elder ghoul that was twice as large as a normal ghoul, and skeleton warriors and archers that were classified as mutants.

We hadn’t come across a wizard yet, so I couldn’t be sure, but everything had gone pretty smoothly so far. Since it was only the first day, the number of monsters was small, and my combat power had significantly increased compared to the previous trip.
Smack!
That much was obvious just by looking at our current equipment.

I had only been able to use the heartstealer’s two-handed hammer with a short grip due to its center of gravity. Now that I was holding a mace about thirty inches in length, however, it was possible for me to smack monsters from a distance. It was much safer and much more powerful.
Most importantly...
Klaaang—!

I now had armor. Because it was vest-shaped, metal sheet armor, my forearms were exposed and defenseless, but the area that I needed to protect under my shield was significantly reduced by the vest alone. As a result, I was able to engage in much more ferocious combat. It felt like my shackles had been lifted.
“Bjorn, be careful! There is also a skeleton archer!”

The iron helmet I was wearing had a T-shape design that revealed only the eyes, nose, and mouth, and protected the most important, most vulnerable parts of the head. Of course, I’d still be in trouble if I was hit directly by something like a crossbow bolt, but it easily deflected arrows shot with a busted bow.
And plus, I had another barbarian by my side with combat power similar to mine.
“Behelaaa!”
We cried out to our barbarian ancestral god and together continued a battle that was no different than a massacre.
Smack! Smack! Crunch!

No matter what kind of monster appeared before us, ten seconds was enough to defeat the entire group. Maybe that was why I now felt a refreshing sense of satisfaction after every battle that I hadn’t felt with Erwen.
Ah, is this the true barbarian experience?
“Bjorn, you are injured.”
Huh?
Only after Ainar commented on it did I notice a slight scratch on my forearm. However...
“Don’t worry. It will go away soon.”
There was no need for me to apply herbs, let alone drink a potion.
“Oh! It’s already closing up! Is this the ability of your Spirit Imprint?”

One of the first things granted by the Immortality Imprint’s abilities was a noticeably improved healing factor. Of course, it was still nothing compared to potions. When I had experimented with it the day before, a cut that was about as deep as a fingernail took about a minute to significantly heal. However, this alone dramatically increased my durability. I now recovered stamina faster, which made my endurance go up tremendously.
“Get ready. It looks like we’re almost there now.”
I told Ainar to stay vigilant and we decreased our speed.
Then, suddenly, the terrain changed. The ground was no longer soggy and hard, and it was no longer level because of the mounds everywhere. The banshees’ howling was even louder here.
“Kihehehe!”
“Ahhh!”
Of course, the biggest difference was something else.
From here onward, we’d be dealing with higher-level monsters. In other words, rank-eight monsters would now appear.
“...Bjorn, are you sure they won’t attack first?”
Ainar had started grinding her teeth a while ago, probably afraid of the banshees’ cries. It seemed barbarians apparently clenched their jaws when they were scared. But I wouldn’t know.
Is it because I’ve never been that scared yet?
“Kwohhh!”
As we kept moving, we heard a bizarre roar in the dark.
Whew...
Actually hearing it in real life made me shudder.
“Ainar, prepare for battle.”
“D-Didn’t you say we were not hunting banshees?”
Doesn’t she have ears?
“That’s not a banshee.”
It was a death fiend.
Of the many rank-eight monsters that greatly contributed to raising the game’s barrier to entry, they were undoubtedly the most annoying motherfuckers of the bunch.
Bam! Bam! Bam! Bam!
The sound of heavy footsteps, which I had picked up on even from a distance, grew louder and louder, and soon, the monster appeared before us.
“...We’re going to fight that?” Ainar asked, and before I could answer, she added, “Looks like fun.”
Truly, I couldn’t figure this woman out. Last month, she had said she was afraid of dying, so how could she smile like that after seeing a monster like this?
And yet she’s afraid of banshees...
Boom!
Perhaps the light bothered it because the death fiend stopped walking as it reached the edge of our torch’s range.
“Don’t be nervous.”
“Don’t worry. I wasn’t nervous.”
I wasn’t talking to you. I was talking to myself.
Oh geez... I had made a plan on the way here, but when I saw the death fiend in person, my legs started to shake.

The death fiend was a humanoid undead monster. No, it was closer to a chimera. It was over ten feet tall and had both a sword and shield for arms. Yeah, no, it wasn’t holding a sword and shield—it genuinely had them for arms.

One hand extended in a long curve and had a blade in the shape of a half-moon, and the other arm, which widened outward at the elbows, took the shape of a shield. Namely, the Protein Blade and Shield.
“Kwohhhg—!”
Shit, don’t scream like that, you look scary enough as it is.
I tried to somehow decrease my stress levels, but it wasn’t easy.
“As long as you stay calm and follow the plan, you can defeat it.”
“Of course, I trust you.”
Thank you for that, but again, that was meant for me.
...Calm yourself.
Although this was my first encounter with this kind of monster, as long as I stayed focused, I shouldn’t have any trouble. If things went south, however, we’d have to run without hesitation.
“As I said before, aim for the head no matter what. The other parts of its body are meaningless. Got it?”
“Okay!”
No, wait, that wasn’t a signal to charge in—
“Behelaaa!”

Ainar ran forward holding her greatsword in both hands. It was too late to stop her now. But her shout must have succeeded in pulling aggro because the bastard rushed forward from the border of the shadows with its sword and shield in position.
“Kwohhhg—!”
Clang!
Ainar’s greatsword and the death fiend’s Protein Blade collided as it released a roar.
“Bjorn, be careful! This monster is no joke!”
That should have been obvious from the start, right?
“Behel-aaah!”

I shouted the name of our ancestral god and followed her lead. Then, I set up a wall in front of me with my shield and bludgeoned the monster from the side as it moved to attack Ainar, who had been bounced back by their collision.
Bam!
But how could its body be so heavy? It was like hitting a boulder.
Chzzz.

The monster exerted more force, pushing me back along with my shield. There was really no reason for me to keep holding my ground here, but my pride was hurt. So, I stood on my toes even higher. Then, as I shifted my entire weight forward, I let out a scream instead of a roar.
“Ahhh!”
Fuck!
It felt like my muscles were going to burst open. But also, I felt a shiver that was difficult to put into words. I had thought I was going to die there... but I had survived.
And Ainar wasn’t stupid enough to let this opportunity pass.
Voom—!
Soon, her swing cut through the air with a heavy thud and struck the side of the death fiend’s head. Not stabbed, but literally struck.
Kagak!

Even that thick greatsword only penetrated about half an inch into its head. The blunt thud probably came from its skull. The death fiend’s defenses were notorious even in the game. It was its ability to heal itself rather than its defenses that caused many beginners to quit the game.
“Kwoooh!”
“Back up for now!”

Avoiding the furious death fiend, we retreated a short distance. Dark red blood dripped from the slice left by the sword, but the bleeding stopped in less than three seconds. This guy’s passive skill was [Body Preservation.]
“Ainar! Give me an opening. This time, I’ll attack!”
After giving the order, I was about to run in when—
Rumble!
Suddenly, the ground began to shake. This was the first time I had ever seen an effect like this, but I knew immediately what it was. The death fiend’s active skill: [Call of the Dead.]
“Move back, the ghouls are coming!”
When the rumbling ended, ghouls dug out of the dirt and climbed up to the surface. Looking around, I saw there were exactly ten.
“Get rid of these guys first!”
“Okay!”

While Ainar was swinging her sword at the ghouls with a “Kwohhh!”, I paid close attention to the death fiend and watched him carefully. However, the stupid angry ghouls were constantly scratching at my skin with their fingernails, tearing my flesh to ribbons in an instant.
Of course, this wasn’t that big a deal.
I have the ability to regenerate too. Although, not like you.
“Bjorn! I’ll take this guy!”

After I had held out for about two minutes, the ghouls were cleared out. It was actually kind of funny when I thought about it. I had survived a death fiend’s summoning ability by literally being torn to shreds.
I didn’t even do this kind of stuff in the game.
While I passed the baton over to Ainar to let her face him one-on-one, I took out my mace and moved behind the monster.
Then I delivered a blow to the back of his head.
Smack!
The blow produced a good thunk and an even more satisfying jolt in my hands. Rotten blood actually leaked out from the back of its messed-up head. Nevertheless, I continued to wield my mace.
Smack! Smack! Smack!
Enough power to turn a goblin to dust was in each strike. But fuck, why wouldn’t it die?
Kagak!
The durability of this monster’s skull was beyond imagination. Even while it was being hit, its flesh continued to heal.
...What should I do?
We lacked power.
If I had known this would happen, I would have bought the weapon that the weapons dealer had recommended to me. Should we just give up on taking this one down and hunt rank nine monsters instead?
Hack! Hack! Hack!
I continued to swing the mace as I thought this over, but the mace wasn’t enough to destroy the creature’s brain.
Voom—!
In the end, I had no choice but to step back to avoid the swinging Protein Blade. And it was then that—
“Kooot!”

Suddenly, the death fiend lost its balance and started leaning to the side. When I checked, I saw Ainar using this opportunity to grab one of the legs of this ten-foot-tall monster and lift it up. It was a technique I had often seen in the UFC.
Is that...
A single leg tackle?
“Behel—aaah!”
With her muscles pumped up and veins bulging out like they were about to burst, she was the one who looked more like a monster between the two of them...
Her goal was obvious and even feasible. I immediately joined in.
Smack!
When I struck the grounded ankle with the mace as hard as I could, the massive body lost its balance and experienced a moment of weightlessness. And then...
Boom!
It crashed to the floor. In technical terms, it was a takedown.
This was the first time it had occurred to me that this kind of strategy was viable against a monster classified as medium to large-sized.
...Nothing was impossible for a barbarian, apparently.
“Kwooohhh!”
I could see the death fiend floundering like an overturned turtle. Ainar and I were about to rush in but flinched back simultaneously.
“Kwooohhh!”
No way... It can’t get up on its own!
“Bjorn!”
“Ohhh!”

A single look was all it took for us to get on the same page. Ainar and I ran to the fallen monster and swung our weapons down like a bunch of lunatics. Like putting a rice cake in a mortar and taking turns bringing down the mallet, we worked in harmony.
Punch! Punch! Punch! Punch! Punch!
Come to think of it, I once made rice cakes the exact same way at a folk village I visited in elementary school.
“This is fun!”

I could remember my partner back then crying as they asked to switch into a different group from me. But seeing Ainar having fun with me healed that old wound in my heart. It felt like my soul itself was being purified.
[You have killed a Death Fiend. EXP +2]
We smiled brightly as we watched the death fiend disappear into the light. We didn’t have powerful magic, the divine power of a priest, or the elemental magic of an elf, but—
“Bjorn! Look at this! This mana stone is huge!”
We had succeeded in hunting a rank-eight monster.

chapters.title: Chapter 24: The Plunderer (1)
paragraphs: A rank-nine mana stone was equal to one slice of stone bread. In other words, each loaf had a value of about twenty stones.
So, what about a rank-eight mana stone? Unfortunately, one death fiend was worth only five goblins.
“What? You mean it’s only a hundred stones?!”
“...Including those ghouls it summoned, we have three hundred stones total.”
Of course, even taking that extra bit into account, there was no denying that the amount was low, especially considering that we had just risked our lives for it.
“Bjorn... How much was that bread we ate at the inn?”
“...I remember it was about three hundred stones.”
“Then... That means I can taste its sweetness every time I take down a death fiend!”

Apparently, the cream pie we had eaten earlier had established itself as a new unit of measurement for Ainar. Of course, if you divided our earnings by 8:2, that would only be 0.2 Sweetness per death fiend... But I decided that I’d rather not tell her that.
“Bjorn! This is not the time to stand around. Hunt! Let’s go hunting!”

The disappointment didn’t last long. I smiled as I saw Ainar radiating enthusiasm once more. In this respect, working with a barbarian wasn’t bad. I liked Erwen as a comrade, but the downside was that she was kind of passive about everything. It was a lot easier to get motivated this way.
“Okay, let’s go!”

After that, we continued to hunt around the area for death fiends. If it took more than twenty minutes to take down each one, our business wouldn’t be profitable even if we earned three hundred stones per fiend, but... The first attempt should always be considered an exception, not the rule.
“Kwoooh!”
“Behel-aaah!”
Each time we came across a death fiend, we cried out the name of our ancestral god and charged. Then we’d each grab a leg, lift it up, and throw the monster to the ground.
We named this strategy the Double Barbarian Tackle.
Bam!
A fallen death fiend was easy prey. As we hammered each monster’s head at a distance further than arm’s length, the monsters soon disappeared into motes of light. That all took about three minutes.
The moment the monsters fell to the ground, they realized how screwed they were and summoned ghouls, which made it difficult for us to shorten that time any further.
“Woooh!”
As the hunt continued, the speed with which we filled our mana stone pouch also increased. However, we were not satisfied with that and accelerated our pace more and more.

This was because, come the third day, hunting death fiends would become impossible. If we hadn’t reached the second floor faster than anyone else using that bug, we wouldn’t have even dared to take these guys on. They normally never traveled alone. Handling two was possible, albeit difficult, but groups of three or four would be tough with just the two of us.
I checked the time and decided to take a break. Although the saying was that you should strike while the iron was hot, accidents always happened in moments of haste.
“Bjorn, I’m thirsty.”
“Drink it sparingly. The corpse flower only blooms tomorrow.”
“Corpse flower?”

The corpse flower was our only means of replenishing our drinking water in the Land of the Dead. When the time came, flowers would bloom on the vines that covered the rubble, and you could find water inside them if you cut them open. When I told her this, Ainar’s expression went stony.
“Bjorn, isn’t that a bit unsanitary?”

Honestly, it was. I’d heard that it was okay to drink, but I still wasn’t all that up for it either. However, this was not something that someone who slept in a five-person room with ten filthy people should be complaining about.
“Do you have an alternative, then?”
“No! I will drink it!”

After resting for about twenty minutes to replenish our energy, we continued hunting again. Finally, when we were just about to collapse from exhaustion, we finished hunting our seventieth death fiend. That meant that we had earned more than twenty thousand stones in a single day.
This is much better than only hunting rank-nine monsters.
However, the essence I was hoping for had not appeared.

“Atrocious” was not a strong enough word to describe the drop rate of an essence. That was why most people who played the game had to develop a leveling strategy based on whatever essence dropped for them at the beginning. But the skill of the player determined how well that went.
It was for that reason that I had been looking forward to coming here. A death fiend’s essence was among the top essences you could get in the early stages.
The problem is that there’s no sign of it appearing.

Its ghoul-summoning active skill, Call of the Dead, was honestly quite underwhelming, but its passive skill, Body Preservation, was good enough to make up for it.
