Of course, absorbing their essence wouldn’t give you the ability to regenerate like those bastards... But since my Immortality Imprint increased my healing factor already, my compatibility with the essence was very high.
I listened to Ainar’s snoring as I checked the time. A day had already passed and the second day had begun.
From now on, we’d have to fight two death fiends at once, but in some ways, I was relieved.
At least now we wouldn’t look strange if we ran into other adventurers. Again, adventurers were the ones I was the most worried about.
“Ainar, get up.”
“...I-I didn’t eat it!”
“It’s time to trade shifts.”
Three hours per person. After resting for a total of six hours, we began a second day of once again hunting death fiends without issue.
“Kwoooh!”

They came in twos today. Their combined active skills summoned twenty ghouls now, but hey, we may as well give it a shot. Our success in this endeavor was thanks to the fact that we had learned and refined our technique for dealing with them countless times on the first day.
Boom!

Before the creatures knew what was happening, I ran forward and flung one onto the ground. Then we knocked the other down as well. A single misstep could make things quite precarious for us... But whenever that happened, we just ran without looking back.
“Ainar, run!”
“Oh!”
The death fiends were slow to move and had a habit of not following you if you moved out of their territory, so things weren’t too dangerous yet.
Shhh—!

Each battle took about ten minutes. In reality, three out of every ten attempts we made were failures, but since we got to deal with two at once, our profits ended up being similar to the first day. On the first day, it had taken quite a while to even find the monsters. However, as we neared evening on the second day, groups of three started appearing from time to time, and as time passed, the frequency of our encounters with them increased as well.
“We should leave this area soon.”
“A wise warrior knows when to retreat.”
When the second day was coming to a close, we left death fiend territory, and all associated regrets, behind. Then we returned to the sticky, muddy field and found a suitable campsite.

It was around that time that we encountered a group of other adventurers for the first time. They were a group of three humans and they were prowling through the dark, relying on a torch just like us. It was only after we were within ten yards that we could actually see each other.
“What are you looking at?” Ainar asked coldly. “If you don’t have any business here, get lost.”
“Ahem, excuse us.”

The group passed us by and disappeared back into the darkness. It was quite interesting. They had only gotten twenty steps away, and I could still faintly hear the sound of their footsteps, but the light of the torch they were holding was no longer visible.

So that was what people meant when they said that most of the floors in the labyrinth could absorb all light. It seemed that even the glow of a torch was almost impossible to see with the naked eye even from just ten yards away. As I was pondering this phenomenon...
“Bjorn, we must move,” Ainar said, her voice hard. “They know where we are. The walls here are convenient, but it would still be safer to find a new campsite.”
Indeed, she was right. I had been thinking the same. However, I couldn’t seem to get used to this.
Who is this woman? Growling at other adventurers to get lost...
It was like she had suddenly switched personalities.
“Bjorn, humans cannot be trusted.”
“...Agreed.”
Now that I thought about it, Ainar and I had one other thing in common, other than the fact that we were both barbarians... A distrust toward humans.
It seemed something had happened to her during her first expedition as well.
I’ll have to ask her about it later.
“Then let’s go,” she replied.
Soon after, we packed our bags and moved on. However, it was difficult to find a campsite with as good a location as our last one.
Do we have to compromise and just settle for having one wall protecting our backs?
As I was thinking this—
We heard a groan from somewhere not too far away.
“Mm!”
It was not a banshee. First of all, it was not a woman’s voice, and...
“...W-Wait!”
It sounded coherent.
“H-Help—”
God damn it. We should’ve just set up camp somewhere else. After a cut-off scream, there was silence.
“That wasn’t a monster attack,” Ainar whispered.
I know. I have ears too.
It was rare for a person to bother begging for their life when fighting a monster. What had happened was obvious. Someone had just killed another person.
Fuck, what kind of shitty mystery is this? I’m not a fucking detective.
Not wanting to get involved, I grabbed Ainar’s wrist and backed away slowly. But whoever it was seemed to sense us.
“Who’s there?”
The voice was cold and low. It was gruff, but it was definitely a woman’s. We held our breaths and went stone-still at the same time.
But at that exact moment—
Pyuuu! Boom! Boom!

Something like a flare was shot into the sky, and it faintly illuminated a radius of about fifty yards. Thanks to this, I was able to see the eyes of the person who had just spoken. The distance between us was less than fifteen yards.
If Erwen had been here, she would have been able to detect her presence from a distance and avoid this situation entirely.
“Hmm, a newbie?”
The strange woman looked at us and came to an immediate conclusion. The feeling was mutual.
A dagger dripping with blood. Four scattered corpses...
“...A plunderer.”
“First time seeing one?” the woman asked calmly.
“You could say that.”
It’s my first time seeing one as professional as you.
“I see.”
The woman was not at all concerned that we had seen the scene of the crime and just nodded her head serenely. And I suspected I knew why.
Plunderers—those who professionally hunted adventurers.

They generated a high income by looting adventurers’ equipment instead of mana stones. Of course, if caught, you would be sentenced to death the moment you returned to the city. But that rarely happened.

Although it had been in self-defense, I had also killed six adventurers and hadn’t been investigated at all. There was no way for people in the outside world to know what happened inside the labyrinth. Not unless someone said something.
“...You’re not wearing a mask.”
This was the most disturbing thing about my current situation.
This bitch is operating as a plunderer with her face in plain sight.

She was a little over five foot five and skinny. She had red hair down to her shoulders, a tattoo under her eye, and half of her right ear was missing. It wouldn’t be difficult to track someone with these features down.

If this was the modern day, the suspect could argue a lack of evidence... But this was a world where magic existed. This meant that it was possible to distinguish truth from lies without physical evidence.
“...Were they members of your party?”
“Well...” The woman looked down at the bodies and shrugged. “They might’ve thought so.”
That was why her face was bare, then. As I asked questions with obvious answers, I quickly took stock of the facts I had in front of me.

There were four bodies in total. Due to the quality of the equipment they were carrying and the fact that there was a wizard in the group, I could tell that they were adventurers who were active on at least the fifth floor or above.
Also, three of the corpses had sustained no visible injuries. However, since there were traces of vomit and blood on their lips...
Were they poisoned? And maybe the man who died last had resistance to it, so he survived a little longer?
I hoped this hypothesis was correct. Our situation would be bleak if she was a talented assassin who could kill four mid-level adventurers herself without leaving a single wound.
Rattle, rattle.

Soon, the woman squatted down and began skillfully removing the equipment from the corpses. She placed each item one by one into a bag. The bag seemed to be enchanted with magic because large, bulky items seemed to fit into it without a problem.
Fear was followed by envy. Just possessing an item like that made the difference between her and us desperately clear.
“Barbarian.”
The woman called out to us. I didn’t answer.
“Are we going to fight?” Ainar asked me quietly.
She was amazing. If it had been Erwen, she would have been shaking in fear right now. Was this what it meant to have a warrior’s pride, wanting to fight an enemy no matter how powerful they were?
I kept my reply brief.
“I am thinking.”

To be honest, I wanted to avoid a fight. The difference in our levels was obvious just by looking at the equipment she was holding. If her skill in combat was as impressive as that equipment... Even taking into account that it was a two-on-one situation, our odds would be much lower.
Whooom—!
The flare burned out and the light in the sky vanished, plunging us into darkness once again. I immediately made a decision.
“Run. At full speed.”
Pride doesn’t save lives.

chapters.title: Chapter 25: The Plunderer (2)
paragraphs: We ran through the dark. Occasionally, I opened the compass to check the direction we were headed, but otherwise I ran like crazy.
“Gahhhk!”
Various monsters, such as ghouls and skeletons, were blocking the way, but it wasn’t a problem because they were all slow. However, that meant they wouldn’t be a problem for our pursuer either.
Whoosh!
Had it been about five minutes? The ruthless plunderer must have finished looting the bodies by now.

That was the one thing we had going for us. If we hadn’t been dressed like amateurs, that bitch would have given up on looting those guys and pursued us right away. In other words, that meant she was confident she could catch up with us even if she gave us time to run away.
Still. At least we had bought some time.
“Bjorn, isn’t that the mark?”
The good news continues.
In the Land of the Dead, collapsed stone buildings were everywhere. Every time I had passed one, I had left a mark so that we could find our way back to the portal to the first floor.
“This way!”
Although we had been active in the general vicinity, the marks were closer than I had expected.
Maybe luck is—
“Who are you?!”
Damn, I shouldn’t have thought that.
Ainar and I stopped at the same time. We had encountered another group of adventurers. But wait, maybe this was a good thing?
Plunderers were a common enemy of all adventurers. If I explained the situation to them and offered appropriate compensation, there was a possibility we’d be able to get help from them.
“Barbarians?”

The group of adventurers who had emerged from the darkness pointed their weapons at us and cocked their heads. There were four in total. They were all human, and their equipment looked at least twice as good as ours.
Humans are hard to trust, but we have no choice.
“We are being chased by a looter. Help us.”
“And how do we know you’re not the looter?”
“I swear it on my honor as a warrior. Every word I say is true.”
Unlike an elf’s vow, a warrior’s oath didn’t have any actual authority behind it. But surprisingly, it worked every time.
The bald man, who seemed to be the leader of the group, thought it over for a moment and then opened his mouth.
“If we catch the looter, we take the entire reward. Do you agree to those terms?”
“Of course.”
“Fine.”
At Baldy’s signal, the other adventurers lowered their weapons. If I hadn’t been a barbarian, it definitely would have taken longer for them to lower their guards.
“Come over here for now. We’ll talk more afterward.”
As I approached them, a blond-haired man standing at around five feet tall activated his special ability.
“This is a gnome’s special ability. When cast on a certain area, it will make you blend into your surroundings as long as you stay within a radius of three yards.”

To put it simply, it was basically a goblin archer’s stealth ability, but instead of only affecting the user, it could be used on any creature within a certain area of effect. In return, it had the disadvantage of not being a mobile ability—you couldn’t change where you wanted it once you activated it.
“Are you injured?” Baldy asked.
“No.”
“How lucky...”
“Lucky” was indeed the only way to describe it.
The group of adventurers we just so happened to stumble upon had a ranged stealth ability? With them by our side, it might be possible to avoid a battle altogether—
“...for two barbarians to come up to us all on their own.”
Fuck, he had been talking to himself.
No wonder things had been working out so well. Of course.
[You are now Restrained.]
“Haha.”
Greed danced around in the eyes of the adventurers, including Baldy. One of them had already rummaged through my backpack and opened the pouch of mana stones.
“You made a lot in just two days.”
I wanted to crush his ribs with the mace, but my body wouldn’t move. And it was the same for Ainar.
“What? Are you scared because you can’t move?”
This was clearly the power of an essence, and I could already guess what kind of essence it was. There were many similar abilities, but there was only one that adventurers at our level could have.
Is it a Stone Golem’s Restraint...?
Without a doubt. We had just been taken down by the active skill of a rank-eight monster, a Stone Golem. The easiest way to get out was to take even the slightest bit of damage, but...
If these bastards had any sense, they’d know to be careful.
“Hey, buddy, there’s no use glaring at us like that. This isn’t an ability you can deal with that way.”
“Horrible” was not a strong enough word to describe this situation.
Fuck, I went through all that to live another day and now I’m going to die like this?
“Look at those ferocious eyes. Still don’t understand the situation?”
“Okay, Ramod. Let’s wrap this up here. If the looter they mentioned shows up, it’ll be a problem.”
“Tsk, that’s too bad. We finally caught a woman, but she’s a barbarian.”
“You idiot, isn’t it better that she’s a barbarian? You know how much money you can make from their hearts alone?”
With that, their ugly desires were finally revealed and I felt a shiver run down my spine.
Soon, Baldy pulled out a sharp blade.
“Kill them in one shot. Don’t mess this up.”
“Tut, don’t worry.”
Whip!
Murderous intent flew forward on the wind. And the spot it was aiming for was none other than my neck.
...The neck?

Even now, when death was imminent, my brain synthesized the information it was given and suggested a solution. Of course, I didn’t know if it would actually work. However, it would be much more productive than reflecting on my past regrets.
Stab!

Time seemed to pass in slow motion. Then, suddenly, a sharp blade cut through my neck. At the same time, a tingling sensation ran through me, and my body went slack. I immediately tilted my head back like a boxer turning his face to take a powerful punch.
I could see the dumbfounded expression on Baldy’s face. The hand that had been holding the dagger was empty.
That was when I registered a strange sensation in my neck.
Oh, it’s already half-stuck.
The moment I realized it, my brain reached a prompt conclusion.
It isn’t that bad. As long as there’s minimal bleeding, I can hold on a little longer.
Sting.
I forced my weakening legs to move and found my balance. Then, I swung the mace in my hand... right toward the bald man’s shiny head.
Crunch!
With his face half sunken in, Baldy collapsed. Time still seemed to be moving at about half-speed.
“Darvan!”
There were many startled faces around me now.
Why, you didn’t think a guy with a knife in his neck could fight back?
Actually, I hadn’t expected that either.
“...fucking...bastard...”
Something kept oozing up my throat. My body began to lose all strength and the lights around me began to blur.
Am I going into shock?
Everything tingled from my head to my toes. I was low on both oxygen and blood.
Clang!
The mace and shield I was holding fell to the floor as my hands lost their grip on them. I wanted nothing more than to collapse and rest, but...
There was still work to be done.
I didn’t get into this mess just to take one asshole down with me.
Sting.
I staggered forward and straightened my swaying form. Then, after pulling out the knife stuck in my neck, I threw it toward Ainar, who was about four steps away.
Stab!
Oops, I didn’t think it would stab you like that.
“Ugh!”
Sorry, but at least your body is moving now.
Stab!

At the same time the dagger pierced into her forearm, Ainar swung her greatsword at the nearby archer’s waist. Then, in a connecting movement, she rotated her body once more, leaped upwards, and slammed it down on the other guy’s head. The iron helmet he was wearing was useless against her blow.
Crunch!
Blood dripped from his helmet as it was turned into scrap metal.
“What the fuck—!”
The blond guy, who was farther away, saw this and immediately made a run for it. It was a quick decision, like that of a goblin.
“Bjorn!”
Ainar, who had finished clearing out the surrounding area, rushed to me and knelt down.
Whew, then I can leave the rest to you—
“Bjorn...!”
Ainar hugged me and sadly called out my name... like she was holding a dead person.
Getting a somewhat ominous feeling, I forcefully opened my hazy eyes and said, “Po...”
“Okay! I will avenge you!”
No, don’t worry about that.
[Achievement Unlocked.]
[Condition: Health drops below 0.1%.]
[Reward: Your Spirit stat has permanently increased by +1.]
I used the last of my energy to open my mouth.
“Potion...”
Fuck, don’t let me die.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 2
Physique: 46
Spirit: 39 (New +3)
Special Ability: 4
Item Level: 202
General Combat Power: 139.5 (New +3)]
Chhhh!
As the hole in my neck began to heal, it was accompanied by pain. But I was happy. I could feel the life being breathed back into my dead body.
The burning pain revived my fading consciousness. I had lived.

I had really thought I was going to cross the Jordan River this time. I was glad I didn’t do anything else with the 1.4 million stones and had gotten the Immortality Imprint first. If it hadn’t been for that, I would have been dead a long time ago.
“Ainar.”
“Are you okay?”
“Gear, get their gear first...”
As soon as I had the energy to speak, I gave instructions to Ainar. After that, I forced myself to get up and toss the remaining potion down my throat.
Gulp.
This was all money, but it couldn’t be helped.

Even if the wound on my neck felt like it was getting better, I couldn’t tell what was happening on the inside. I also didn’t know what kind of damage had been inflicted on my brain thanks to what had just happened. So, it was better to take precautions in advance.

In fact, before long, a tingling sensation began in the back of my head. Considering the intensity of the pain, it didn’t seem to be serious, but if left unattended, it might have led to a major problem.
“Can I check it?”
“...What about the equipment?”
“I grabbed everything I saw.”
In that case...
When I nodded, Ainar lifted my chin and carefully inspected the wound.
“It will leave a scar.”
It felt weird. Erwen had once said the same thing. However, the sentiment behind it had been completely different.
“Amazing! You will be the only barbarian with a scar from getting stabbed in the neck!”
Does this look like a medal of honor to her?
It was true, though. No matter how many barbarians were out there in the world living like brutes, it was probably rare for one to survive after being stabbed in the neck.
“Now what?” Ainar asked, wondering about our future plans.
This woke me up as well. Just moments before I had been walking the line between life and death... But none of our problems had actually been solved.
“How long has it been?”
“Max? About five minutes.”
Five minutes...
Contrary to what I had initially believed, running into these bastards had made the situation go from bad to worse.
How stupid of me.
No matter how dangerous the situation was, I should have known better than to ask for help from scumbag adventurers.
Anyway, let’s moan about this later.
“Which direction did that guy run off to?” I asked.
“That way.”
I led Ainar and moved in the direction the blond-haired guy had escaped. Although the floor was muddy, there had been no footprints left behind, so it was impossible to properly track him.
But, just as expected...
“There you are.”
Not too far away, I could see blond hair.
After all, since it’s so dark here, how far could he possibly have gotten?

It seemed that while running, he had banged his head on one of the ruins, fallen over, and passed out on the ground. After taking away anything that could be a weapon, I stomped on his back to wake him up, and his blond hair fell flat across his face.
“Eek! H-Have mercy!”
Compared to before, he was being very polite. Earlier, he had complained that the woman they had happened to catch was a barbarian, but now?
“Ahh!”
Ainar grabbed the man’s neck and easily lifted him up with one hand. The blond-haired man was so small that his feet didn’t touch the ground.
He started to choke.
As I watched him getting strangled, instead of feeling sympathetic, all I thought was “good riddance.”
That’s why you should always make sure to aim for the head, not the neck.
If he had, regardless of any potions or my Immortality Imprint, I would have been helpless.
“Ainar, release him.”
Despite clearly questioning my orders, Ainar released her grip. I approached the guy as he slumped on the ground and spoke into his ear.
“Use your powers if you want to live.”
That was the only reason I hadn’t ripped this blond rat’s head off right away. The gnome ability this guy had. I needed it right now.
“I-I already did!”
“How long can you keep it going?”
“Thirty minutes! No, I can last forty minutes! So—!”
Too many words.
I wished he would just answer my question. I gripped his collar and asked another.
“How long will it take for you to use it again?”
“I-I need to rest for as long as I last used it.”
“I see.”
I released the hand that was holding him by the neck and pressed his upper body into the ground with my feet before he could even think of escaping.
Like dealing with a goblin...
“Wouldn’t it be better to just kill him? I think that woman has given up on us anyway.”

I wondered how Ainar had come to that bullshit conclusion, but it really might look like that from her point of view. Although we had managed to escape, it wasn’t clear whether or not we had actually been pursued in the first place. Even factoring in the time it would have taken to loot the corpses, it was definitely strange that that woman hadn’t shown her face yet.
“Given up, huh...”
Certainly, that possibility existed. Perhaps the plunderer bitch didn’t think we were worth chasing.

As for the issue of us potentially returning to the city to testify against her, if the face we saw earlier was actually some kind of magical illusion, that would explain her brazen, bare-faced murder.
But...
Smirk.
Things couldn’t work out that well, could they?
Not for me, at least.

chapters.title: Chapter 26: The Plunderer (3)
paragraphs: “Ainar. Whenever something happens, always consider the worst-case scenario first.”
Just look at what happened earlier, when we had gotten our hopes up about coincidentally encountering human adventurers. Life didn’t always work out the way you wanted it to.
“The only reason we were able to run away was because she let us go. She must have thought that, if she wanted to, she could catch us easily. So it’s too early to let our guards down.”
The explanation was starting to get long despite myself.
Let’s get to the main point.
“By now, she must be—”
“Watching you from nearby.”
Mother—
I thought she would at worst be on her way here. Apparently, there was another rock-bottom below rock-bottom. Or maybe I just wasn’t as clever as I thought I was.
“Bjorn!”
As Ainar and I set down our backpacks and prepared to fight, the woman emerged from the darkness, once again with no mask.
“I’m sorry, barbarian.”
...What’s with this creepy bitch?
“Still, your earlier battle was impressive.”
Despite the gnome’s ability, it seemed like she’d been watching us for a while... but that didn’t make logical sense.
“...Why didn’t you show up before now?”
It had taken a few minutes for me to be able to move again after drinking the potion. So, why hadn’t she come after me during that time?
While I was waiting for an answer...
“Ahhh!”
The blond-haired guy jumped up from the ground and started running with all his might. Ainar and I didn’t react in time to stop him because we were focused on the psychopathic bitch. However...
Thud.
A thin, needle-like thing flew out in a straight line and pierced the blond-haired man’s neck.
Could it have been poisoned? Despite the minor injury, his blond hair fluttered like the branches of an aspen tree, and he soon fell limp.
It was at that point that I realized that this was not the time to be leisurely asking questions like “how” or “why.”
“Ainar!”
Lengthy conversations weren’t necessary between us. The moment I called her name, Ainar pushed off the ground and leaped forward like she had just been waiting for my signal. I did the same.
If you can’t run away, there’s no choice but to fight!
Whooom!
The plunderer bitch easily evaded Ainar’s greatsword by ducking. Then she simultaneously blocked my mace with a dagger as it was coming down at her.
Clang!
What the...
How many essences had she guzzled down? The dagger that had blocked my mace was completely fine. And, when the woman exerted more force, I was helplessly pushed back.
“Stop this meaningless fight, barbarian.”
Well. That sounded like a very hard ask.
Even if it’s pointless...
“Behel-aaah!”
I was a barbarian. And of course, my mind had not yet forgotten my time as a member of modern civilization either.
Clang!

I was constantly afraid, there was no sign that my pain tolerance was improving, and I still thought of a way to run away in every situation. Nevertheless, there was one thing about me that was the same as the barbarians.
Clang!
If there was only one possible path forward, I chose to follow through—without hesitation.
Clang!
As my mace collided with her dagger, I discarded it and attempted a tackle. As expected, she didn’t budge.
Why is a random adventurer so strong? I unconsciously whined.
Still, even if I couldn’t knock her down, I could use my grit to stall her.
“Ainar! Now!”

Before I was even done shouting, Ainar’s greatsword was already swinging in a perfectly straight line. For the first time, the plunderer, who had been expressionless this entire encounter, showed some glimmer of emotion. Surprise, or annoyance.
Mmm, or maybe it was anger.
Stab!
Pain erupted in my back.
Did she stab me in the spine? But what happened to my armor?
Before I could even question what was happening, the strength left my body.
[You are now under the Paralysis effect.]
I tried to grab onto her pants and hold on somehow, but my body, which was capable of rampaging like a monster even while stabbed in the neck, did not listen.
Stab!
Then, a moment later, the sound of stabbing flesh was heard again.
Clang!
With that sound, Ainar’s greatsword fell to the floor. When I moved my eyes upward, I saw a dagger buried in Ainar’s wrist. I wondered if this was the end of us...
But even when she was in pain, Ainar did not stop.
“Ahhh!”

Having lost her weapon, instead of her paralyzed right arm, she swung her left fist. Seeing her fighting spirit, I realized it all over again... Why barbarians, who were no different from large humans in appearance, were treated like monsters.
However, this was not a good matchup for her.
Whooom!
The woman escaped the fist with an evasive maneuver and didn’t stop there, instead grabbing Ainar’s wrist, twisting it, and—
Boom!
—throwing her to the ground.
Ainar immediately pushed off the ground and tried to stand up, but she kept slipping and falling. Her arm was trembling and her tendons were tense. At the sight, the woman let out an apathetic sigh.
“Give up. There is nothing you can do after being paralyzed by a basilisk’s poison.”
This was like a death sentence. My mind went blank and my eyes darkened.
Equipment, skills, experience... There was a stark, insurmountable difference between us in every domain.
No matter how much I turned the gears in my head, I couldn’t think of any way to turn the situation around. But just when the word “death” was stamping itself on my mind—
“That’s why you should have listened when I gave you the chance.”
—the woman bent over, released the tight fist I had around the hem of her pants, and said dryly, “Barbarian, swear that you won’t speak of what happened today to anyone. Then I will spare you.”
...What?
After that announcement, a brief silence followed. Then, the woman opened her mouth.
“I was going to make this offer before you ran away. I owe your people something.”
I could instinctively sense that taking this deal was the only way to survive, but... I couldn’t understand it.
“I don’t want to kill a barbarian with my own hands if I can avoid it,” the woman briefly explained as I desperately raised my head.
With my own hands...
Is that why she had just sat back and watched while the blond-haired man had been attacking me? Because she wanted to let someone else take care of her mess?
“Bjorn... the plunderer’s words... don’t believe them... she is just toying with us.”
But even if you say that, we don’t have a choice.
Whether she toyed with us and then killed us, or just killed us... There was no difference either way.
I spat out the blood that had reached the back of my throat and asked, “If I turn down the offer, what will you do...?”
“Kill you, of course. That was our agreement in the first place.”
“Agreement...with who?”
“That’s not for you to know.” Her voice was the same as usual, but somehow it sounded a bit harsher. “Choose. I’ll give you a little time—”
“I swear on my honor as a warrior.”
No time was needed. It wasn’t like there were any other options.
“...No doubt about it, you are a little odd.”
The plunderer looked down at me for a moment with a strange look in her eye then sprayed something.
Chhhz.
I felt a familiar pain. It was a potion.
[You have consumed a Recovery Potion (Greater.)]
[The Paralysis status effect has been removed.]
My tense muscles began to relax and strength gradually began to return to my body. The woman looked away from me and asked, “Lady barbarian, what will you do?”
Ainar gave an answer after a brief pause.
“...I refuse.”
“I see.”
The woman did not ask again. She just nodded slightly. However, her intentions were clear as day from that single action. She didn’t take out her weapon, nor did she pose a physical threat, but...
This woman was going to kill Ainar now.
And to prevent that, there was only one thing I could do.
“...Ainar, make the oath.”
“Bjorn?”
“Didn’t you say you would obey me no matter what?”
“Still, the oath of a warrior is...”
Fuck, what’s so important about pride?
“Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin!”
Ainar stiffened at my shout. I lowered my voice, looked into her eyes, and spoke calmly.
“Trust me. This is the right decision.”
After a brief silence, Ainar struggled to open her mouth.
“...Okay. I swear.”
“Smart choice.”
After Ainar made the oath, the plunderer healed her by using up another potion. This was a true carrot-and-stick situation. The feeling of being forced to choose between them was the same.
Nauseatingly disgusting.
As soon as the treatment was over, the woman turned to leave when I decided to ask her a question.
“...What floor?”
To this random question, the woman tilted her head for a moment and gave a brief answer.
“Floor eight.”
Of course, way higher than floor five.
No wonder she was so strong despite being a plunderer. Even if there had been ten of me, we would have been no match for her.
But...
I closed my eyes.
As I watched the psychopath disappear from my vision like smoke, I made a promise to myself. Next time, things would be different.
“Ainar, are you okay?”
“...I am okay. I can get up on my own.”
Ainar pushed my hand away and stood up on her own. I wondered if she was disappointed in me, but maybe the person she was disappointed in was herself, not me.
After all, barbarians were honest to a fault.
I decided to leave Ainar and the complicated look on her face alone for a while and took stock of my current state.
First, this thing...
Click!
Taking off the armor and checking the back, I could see that there was a hole the size of a dagger in it. It had penetrated very cleanly.
...Could she be an Auror?
Damn it all.
Why did we have to run into a monster like that on the second floor, not to mention somewhere as wide and vast as the Land of the Dead? What kind of shitty situation was this?
All I could think was that I needed to get stronger as fast as possible. Whether I went home or not, that was the only way to protect myself in this rotten world.
“Bjorn, what are we going to do now?”
“...Go down to the first floor.”
The Land of the Dead was not a bad hunting ground. But I had no intention of staying here with that crazy bitch roaming around. We could come back if I changed my mind.
“Right... Okay.”
Ainar, dejected, followed my instructions without argument. Therapy was not my specialty, but...
Ha... I should at least say something when we get down there. She looks like the world has ended.
“Follow me.”
Skirting around most of the avoidable encounters, we followed the markers. After about six hours, we were finally able to return to the portal that led down to the first floor.
Thudㅡ!
Once again, I landed fine while Ainar rolled across the floor, and quite badly too. But she got up slowly as if nothing had happened.
“...Didn’t that hurt?”
“It does.”
“But why...”
“Since I am not a warrior, I don’t deserve to feel pain.”
...The situation was much worse than I had thought. Was it really so disgraceful to beg for your life? Well, it had been the same in the game too.
“Um, Ainar...?”
“What is it?”
“The strongest warrior is the one who lives to see another day. Instead of things ending with one defeat, we’ve opened up the possibility of a later victory!”

“I can’t understand what you say when you use so many words.” Although I kept my tone deliberately cheerful, Ainar’s voice was still gloomy. “However, I think I understand what you mean by ‘the strongest warrior is the one who lives to see another day.’”
“I-Is that so?”
“Being able to overcome such humiliation and the urge to commit suicide at every moment must make someone a strong warrior. Just like you, Bjorn.”
No, I don’t have any of those thoughts...? Commit suicide? It’s not like I’m a samurai.
That wasn’t what I had originally meant, but there was no need to get into that right now.
“Ainar, you can do it.”
“I don’t know if I’ll be able to get through this pain... but I will try.”
“Yes, one day you will make up for this disgrace.”
With my sincere support, we continued moving. And after deciding to camp in a suitable location, I let Ainar sleep first.
“I’ll wake you up in two hours.”
“...I will accept your kindness this time.”
Kindness...
Her assumption was half right and half wrong.

Time-wise, it was the morning of the third day. I hadn’t slept in over twenty hours. After everything we’d been through, the mental fatigue I was under was enormous. But I knew that even if I closed my eyes, I wouldn’t be able to fall asleep for a long time anyway.
It wasn’t like I was being driven by emotions as extreme as Ainar’s, but... I still felt dirty.
It was like the pain of drinking a potion. No matter how many times I experienced the feeling, I could never get used to it.
Chomp!

The time I had been saved by that blond and his party had felt similar. The priestess had looked into my eyes and refused to treat me. The swordsman had thrown the potion at me like it was a waste. But despite all that, I had taken the potion anyway, drinking it while lying on the ground like a dog.
Of course, I was happy to have survived, but...
All the same, emotions that were difficult to describe also rose up inside of me.
“Whew...”
I let out a long breath in an attempt to dispel them.
What the hell am I doing right now? It’s not like me to be swayed by my emotions. Maybe it’s time to use that.
I closed my eyes and remembered the advice given to me by someone I had admired as a child.
“Remember, you are nothing. You will never be special.”
It was a magic spell that always made me feel a little bit better. Yes, let’s use even this feeling as fuel, just like I always did.
That would be a little more effective.

chapters.title: Chapter 27: Rift (1)
paragraphs: People evolved, and each had their own method of doing so. By reading books, reflecting on the past, having an honest conversation with a friend for the first time, or realizing a dream they truly wanted to see come true.
Or...

By being jealous of someone else’s good fortune, witnessing someone’s misfortune, or realizing the power that came with having a desire. Every experience stimulated and contributed to a person’s growth.
I was no different. Well, psychological growth was probably only a small part of that, though.
As I was organizing the backpacks for the blond-haired guy’s party, I smirked.
“One wooden bow, one metal plate gaiter, three low-rank potions, a dozen regular torches... What is this? A portrait? A family portrait, maybe? Anyway, toss that away...”
Adding it all up, this stuff would be worth over eight hundred thousand stones.
I’d always been like this, after all. Growth didn’t always correlate with living through a fucked-up situation. But...
“With this, I can afford three more pieces of armor for myself.”
Every time I leveled up as a person, it had always been following a fucked-up situation.
Damn, I knew what I had to do after this.
I was walking through the cave with Ainar.
“Bjorn, where are we going now?”
“We will move south to the gnomes.”
After taking a break of four hours per person, for a total of eight hours, Ainar also came back to her senses. Her energy levels were still low compared to her usual, though.
“Bjorn, you can move faster. You don’t have to worry about me.”
“Why are you in such a hurry?”
“I...I want to become stronger as soon as possible.”
“I see.”
It seemed that I didn’t have to worry about her anymore. As long as she had a clear goal in mind, negative emotions would act as nourishment, not poison.
Mm, maybe I was the same way.
“I am of the same opinion.”

The entire time I’d been on watch, I reflected on my journey so far. The coming-of-age ceremony, my arrival in the labyrinth, my night companionship with Hans, Erwen, the Goblin Forest, the 4 v 2 battle with the crossbow party, etcetera.
When I thought about it, there was nothing really wrong with anything I had done in those situations. I’d always looked for the best possible option to choose in a given situation. But...
Plainly speaking, I had spent every moment solely focused on escaping.
“Why did you suddenly stop?”
“No reason. We’ll keep moving.”
This was worth thinking about.

I’d had no tutorial fairy or system text to rely on. As soon as I opened my eyes, a man’s head had been cut off, and from then on, events that were far outside the realm of reality had continued to unfold. Therefore, I had had no choice but to react as passively as possible, putting my safety above all.
But how had that worked out for me?
“Bjorn...? You don’t look good.”
“Don’t worry about it.”
I always chose the best possible option? Bullshit.
In the end, that was just a coping mechanism. How great could the decisions I made have been, coming from a guy who only managed to handle a situation after it happened?
If I really wanted to survive here, I needed to start being more proactive. That way, the choices I was faced with would be different.
My gambling-addict uncle once told me, “Instead of playing a game someone else has planned, throw the dice on a board you made for yourself.”
Okay. Change of plans.
I stopped in my tracks. “Ainar, do you really want to be strong?”
Ainar expressed deep confusion in response to my sudden question.
“What... do you mean?”
“I’m asking for your commitment. There is a way to definitely become stronger. But it comes with risks. What do you think?”
High risk, high reward. How would she respond to this proposal?
As I stopped to watch her, Ainar swallowed and a fire roared to life in her eyes.
“Of course I will do it. If we don’t become strong, we’ll die anyway!”
Yeah, that’s true. That’s how this world works.
After expressing her consent, Ainar shouted, “I am a warrior!”
I thought you said you weren’t one before?
I snickered.
As I watched the impractical mindset of a barbarian—which was also sometimes weirdly more practical than anyone else’s—in action, I realized something.
“So, how can I get stronger?”
The slow way was the easy way. And fucked-up situations were like a natural disaster; no matter which path you took, they could hit you without warning.
And with my luck, the number of natural disasters would be many. That was why...
“We will enter the Rift.”
The first punch wins.
This time, I was going to seek out the natural disaster myself. As someone famous once said: “What doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.”
“Oh! I see!” Ainar exclaimed after listening to my plan. Then, she hesitantly asked, “...But what is a Rift?”
How come you’re a native of this world but have less knowledge than me? I wished she would read some books.
Oh, right... She still hasn’t learned how to read.
“The Rift is... in short, it is a labyrinth within a labyrinth.”
I skipped any detailed explanations. She wouldn’t understand anyway.
“A labyrinth in a labyrinth?”
“That’s right.”

It was an element of Dungeon and Stone that made it unique compared to many other games these days. If the person I had to explain this to were someone from the modern world, I would have described the Rift as an ‘instance dungeon.’
“Sometimes a portal opens at a random location on each floor. When you enter it, it takes you not to the second or third floor, but to a new space.”
“Oh! Are you talking about the Frostlord’s Palace?”
I guess she has heard of Rifts, then.
The Frostlord’s Palace was a space you could access by going through the Rift on the eighth floor. I remembered working like a dog to try to obtain the Frostlord’s essence in the game.
“But is it feasible with just the two of us? I heard the chieftain went in there when he was young and almost died.”
“It’s okay. We are only on the first floor.”
There were a total of four types of Rifts that could be opened on the first floor. No matter which one you chose, the difficulty was incredibly low compared to the Rifts of the other floors.
Using the two of us as a benchmark, it would still be rated seven stars...and that was out of five.
“But how can we get into a place that appears randomly?”
“Don’t worry. There is a way.”
I may not look it right now, but I had spent nine years of my life playing this game. And I discovered hundreds of hidden things in its unfriendly interface.
“Bjorn, I will trust you!”

I turned away from our original southern trajectory to move east. Originally, I had wanted to hunt gnomes, kobolds, and stone golems on the southern route of the second floor, Black Rock Mountain. The stone golem’s [Restraint] ability was a pain in the ass to deal with, but if you prepared in advance, it could be overcome. However, there was no telling how many years it would take us to reach the eighth floor by playing so cautiously.
“Two barbarians. Are you looking for a night companion? If the three of us sleep together, we can sleep a lot more—”
“Get lost.”
“I was just asking—”
“I will crush your head if you don’t leave in three seconds.”
As we crossed the first floor, we came across other adventurers as well as monsters, but Ainar took care of it each time.
...But can’t she just tell them “no?”
“I hate humans more than fern faces.”
It seemed that Ainar had evolved from distrusting humans to flat-out hating them.
Smack! Smack! Crunch!
We finally reached our destination after traveling for about twenty hours, demolishing the monsters standing in our way. The time was around 4 a.m.
It was once again hitting me how big the first floor was. I knew this place was a maze-like anthill, but to think it took more than a day to get from the west end to the center...
“Bjorn, isn’t this the entrance?”
Strictly speaking, the word “entrance” was incorrect. Most starting points tended to be in a certain direction, either north or south or whatever. Most importantly, there was no light here.
Whoosh!
Burning a torch we had obtained from the blond-haired guy’s party, we entered the dark zone.
And how long had it been since?
[You have defeated a gnome. EXP +1]
[You have defeated a blade wolf. EXP +1]
“To think all four types of monsters appear here!” Ainar exclaimed in fascination as she finished off our eighth battle. “I didn’t know there was a place like this in the middle of the first floor.”

It was probably common sense to most adventurers, but this was not a place you casually wandered into. If I had to compare it to something, this was like a spot where a cold current met a warm one. Blade wolves from the east, ghouls from the west, gnomes from the south, and goblins from the north all coexisted in the area we were standing in.
However...
“It’s strangely quiet.”

This area was not popular amongst adventurers, and the reason for that was simple. Even though all four types of monsters appeared, that only made the job of the hunter harder. The number of monsters that spawned was also few.
Besides, the fatal flaw of this area is how expensive it is to constantly light a torch.

As a matter of fact, almost no one came here except for those who chose to pass through it in an effort to save time on travel. But pros enjoyed this space, mainly because it was unique. Plus, from a game designer’s point of view, it was the perfect place to hide something.
“So, why are we here?” Ainar asked.
“Just wait. We’ll be there soon.”
After an hour of wandering around in the dark, changing directions here and there, we eventually got to the place I wanted to go.
“Now we’re here.”
It was a hole with a radius of about thirty yards sitting in the middle of an open space. In the first floor, which had been designed with an anthill-like structure, this peculiar monument stood out.
“...What is that?”
“It is a memorial. To honor the first person to discover this labyrinth.”
I cautiously approached the tombstone and read the inscription at the bottom.
[The Last Great Sage, Diplan Groundel Gabrilius. In honor of his great first step.]
The text was the same as it was in the game. In other words, it would be reasonable to assume that the hidden place that I had found back then was likely the same one I was looking at now.
“Ainar, what happens from now on is a secret. Got it?”
“Okay.”
“I need your oath, not simply an agreement. If this becomes known, we may both be in danger.”
“...I swear on my honor as a warrior.”
“Thanks.”

I slowly loosened the pouch tied around my waist. Goblins, gnomes, ghouls, and blade wolves. Mana stones of the four types of monsters that appeared on the first floor and the mana stone of a death fiend, a rank-eight monster.
And then, the monument of the great sage right in front of me.
“I’ll get started.”
All the preparations to force open the Rift were in place.
In Dungeon and Stone‘s instance dungeons, Rifts had a cooldown time.

Using the first floor as an example, it took at least three cycles—three months in city time—for the Rift to reopen. Of course, it was rare for the Rifts to open immediately after three months, and most opened randomly after five to six cycles.
The maximum was...eight cycles? Yes, I was sure of it.

Keep in mind, that these were all things that I had discovered on my own. While grinding for the Frostlord’s Essence, I needed to know more about the Rift. It wasn’t efficient to just constantly wander around the floors and wait for the Rift to appear.
“Is something wrong?”
“No.”

Having momentarily been caught up in memories of the past, I placed the death fiend’s mana stone in front of the monument. If the most recent Rift had opened within three cycles, then the cooldown clock would still be running, and there would be no response. But...
Before long, the mana stone I had placed disappeared in a flash of light, and vibrations spread through the monument.
It had really worked.
Whooom!
The vibrations became stronger and a black portal opened up.
“Hurry, let’s go inside.”
“Um, uh... Okay!”
As I remembered that the Rift usually reached max capacity in ten seconds, I hurriedly threw myself inside with Ainar.
[You have entered the first-floor Rift.]
Leaving behind Ainar, who had landed on her butt as usual, I studied our surroundings.

A red sky that seemed to signal the end of the world at any moment, a flock of crows flying above it, and a black fortress in the distance... Needless to say, this was one of the four types of Rifts on the first floor, the Bloody Citadel.
That was to be expected, since the rank-eight mana stone I had offered as a sacrifice belonged to a death fiend.
Whooom!

After we stood around waiting for a while, a portal opened in the air and a person was spat out. This was the main reason why I had put off coming to this place, despite knowing exactly how to open a Rift as well as the best strategy to clear it.
I was more afraid of adventurers than monsters.
“Hahaha! I finally managed to get in!”
Wouldn’t it be nice to be a member of a five-person party that was guaranteed to trust each other?

When you entered the Rift the way we did, you had to clear it alongside a random group of adventurers who entered it on a first-come, first-served basis. If this were the game, we would be matched with other players by an automated system. I glanced nervously at our first party member.
“Oh! How reassuring to have two barbarians! Nice to meet you! My name is Hikurod Murad! As you can see, I’m a dwarf, hahaha!”
First, a talkative dwarf.
I didn’t know about his skillset, but that wasn’t bad.
I hope the rest of the group will be like this...
I snorted.
But that would be asking for too much, right?
Shit, come at me, anyone who wants to come. I don’t have my hopes up anyway.
[A new party member has joined the campaign.]
Two more party members were added soon after.

chapters.title: Chapter 28: Rift (2)
paragraphs: Daria Whitember di Tersia.
An adventurer with five years under her belt, she was currently wandering around the first floor of the crystal cave. She had her younger sister, who she still saw as a little kid, with her.
“Erwen, you used a spirit again.”
“Ah, it’s too hard with just the dagger...”
“I told you. You need to be able to protect yourself without a bow or a spirit.”
“No, I know that, but—”
“Stop. If you keep practicing, you’ll get better.”

Tersia was taking Erwen around the first floor and training her mercilessly. It was all for her younger sister’s sake, and her sister was not ignorant of that fact. But as the training dragged on, it was clear that she was getting tired.
“M-Mr. Barbarian said that it is better to specialize in what you are good at...”
“...What?”
“To trust your party and do your best to fulfill your role. That—That is the key to being an adventurer...”
Tersia, who had been impassively hearing her out, was speechless. The statement itself was... reasonable. Wouldn’t it be great if the world was that nice a place?
“Erwen, party members are just party members. Don’t place too much value on them.”

Tersia had been a part of many parties. From the adventuring party on the sixth floor that she had belonged to until just a while ago, to the hunting team that had only hunted monsters that were particularly profitable, to the speedrunning party that had aimed to open portals.
After working with a lot of different people, she had gotten to experience many different things. Among them were things that she didn’t want to tell Erwen about.
Party members could not be trusted unless they were related by blood.
“All right...”
Erwen didn’t fight back after noticing the hardened look on Tersia’s face.

Time passed, and it was soon the fourth day. Erwen had traveled the first floor in a clockwise direction and was now able to defeat any monster they came across with her dagger alone. In the process, she had naturally leveled up.
“Um, Tersia? I’ve leveled up. Can’t we go to the second floor now? Mr. Barbarian must be making so much money up there right now...”
Tersia laughed at how cute her sister was. What was the big deal about catching a few more monsters on the second floor?
“Erwen, the Rift is going to open soon.”
The Rift: a place that even mid-level adventurers who had been in the business for several years weren’t able to enter without the right amount of luck.
Erwen cocked her head. “How do you know that?”
“Because the last Rift on the first floor opened eight months ago.”

Tersia kindly explained it step-by-step like she was talking to a young child. Today was their fourth day in the labyrinth, so she used statistics to explain why she believed the Rift would have to open in the next three days.
“I see... Mr. Barbarian didn’t mention that.”
Well, of course, Tersia thought.

Erwen had been continuously singing the barbarian’s praises for the past month, but he was still only a newbie. Recklessly advancing to the next floor and suffering through all kinds of trials and errors in the process was the epitome of inefficiency to an experienced adventurer.
“Erwen, don’t be impatient and trust me. Within a year, there will be a huge gap between you and that barbarian in terms of level.”
Sometimes the slow way was the fastest way.
“Mm... then when that time comes, I can help him!”

“Yes, you can do that,” Tersia allowed, nodding her head. She wasn’t sure whether the barbarian would still be alive or not by then, and even if he was, Tersia would come up with a way to dissuade her sister when the time came.
She wanted to preserve her sister’s innocence as much as possible.
Just as she was thinking this, the labyrinth began to shake like there was an earthquake. This was a phenomenon that occurred whenever a Rift opened.
“Erwen!”
Tersia grabbed Erwen’s hand and ran down the tunnel at full speed. Soon after, she found a portal that was vibrating unsteadily.
It was a Rift.
There would be thousands of portals just like this all over the first floor by now, and every minute was now a critical race against the clock.
Whooom—!
Tersia and Erwen flung themselves into the portal. But at that moment...
Whoom—
...the portal disappeared.
Thud.
Tersia, who had jumped through the air and landed on the ground, clicked her tongue in disappointment.
“...One step too late.”
If they hadn’t attempted to enter at the same time and she had pushed her sister in before her instead, they might have successfully made it. But...
“...There will be another opportunity later.”
It couldn’t be helped. After all, what if her younger sister had ended up entering the Rift alone and had died in there?
“Erwen, let’s go to the second floor.”
Again, sometimes, the slow path was the fastest.
The Law of Equivalent Exchange. I really liked that theory. But, sadly, the world did not run on it.
Just consider the time we ran into that psychopathic bitch. We had barely survived and hadn’t gained anything from the experience.
No, rather, we got kicked out of the Land of the Dead and ended up wasting time.
But this time it was different. This time I had made the choice, so I would reap the appropriate rewards.
Mm, probably.
Boom.
I looked at the woman and the human man who were our last two party members, keeping my guard up. The man, who had landed with a heavy thud, didn’t seem to be anything special, but...
The woman was different.
Tap.
As if in defiance of the laws of gravity, the woman descended to the ground slowly and landed gently. Even the talkative dwarf could not hide his surprise at the sight, his mouth falling open.
I was in the same boat.
“Didn’t expect to see a wizard here.”
Wizard—the best class you could choose in Dungeon and Stone and the only class that was worthy of the title. Wizards were treated with respect wherever they went just for their status as wizards.
“Bjorn, are wizards that impressive? That librarian was a wizard too!”
At Ainar’s question, the wizard woman frowned as if displeased. Before we could get on the wizard’s bad side, however, I opened my mouth.
“The librarian is a rank nine wizard.”
“Is that different?”
It was different. Very different.

While librarians were upper-class workers who worked in guilds, public institutions, or workrooms, this woman was a real wizard. The fact that she had come into the labyrinth was proof of that. Wizards were an important resource in Rafdonia, so if they didn’t prove themselves capable, they weren’t allowed to enter the labyrinth at all.
“I see!”
Once I was done leveling with Ainar and explaining the situation as clearly as possible, the wizard calmly joined the conversation.
“Yes, that’s right. You are knowledgeable for a barbarian.”
Seeing the smug smile on her lips, I could immediately tell what kind of character she was.
“Hello. My name is Arua Raven, a rank-six wizard. And this is the professional porter I hired... What was your name again?”
“It’s Tarzine, Lady Raven.”

So they were a duo. That wasn’t too bad. She seemed to have a tendency to look down on others, but she wasn’t that bad compared to other wizards. In the game, there had been scumbags a lot worse than this.
“May I ask for an introduction from all of you as well?”
“Hikurod Murad. It’ll be a short adventure, but I hope we do good work together, Miss Raven.”
“How experienced are you, Mr. Murad?”
“I’ve been an adventurer for three years.”
A third-year adventurer... No wonder his equipment looked so high-quality.

“Bjorn, son of Yandel.” After providing that brief introduction, I decided to just bluntly ask the question that was on my mind. “I don’t see why someone like you is on the first floor. Why did you enter the Rift?”

Most of the adventurers who were active on the first floor were those who didn’t even have proper equipment. And so, I had expected that clearing the Rift would be a tough job. But with a third-year veteran and a rank-six wizard?
I couldn’t just accept this stroke of luck. Writing it off as a happy coincidence would be a stupid decision too.
“I can’t get into details, but I heard that the Rift would be opening during this cycle.”
“As did I.”
Is this what people meant by ‘gatekeeping’? Raven and the dwarf both remained tight-lipped about how exactly they got here.
Of course, it didn’t really matter to me. I now had a guess as to how they had inferred when the Rift would be opening.
“Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin.”
As soon as everyone’s introductions were done, Raven took charge of the conversation.
“The loot will be divided according to the number of people, minus Mr. Tarzine here. In exchange, will you all follow my lead?”
“I have no objections. Following a wizard’s orders is the most logical thing to do in a labyrinth.”
“Thank you for saying that.”

When the dwarf expressed his consent, Raven’s gaze turned to the two of us. I didn’t have to think for long. With a wizard in the party, it wouldn’t be good to stand out. After all, wizards were the ones who had first noticed the existence of evil spirits and persuaded the royal family to declare them targets of annihilation.
Shit...
Clearing the Rift was no longer my main goal.
“I agree as well.”
Just play nice. She may have complimented me earlier for being a knowledgeable barbarian, but that could turn into suspicion at any moment.
“I refuse.”
Huh?
Everyone’s eyes turned to Ainar at her headstrong declaration.
“I don’t know what’s so great about a wizard. I want Bjorn to lead us.”
But even I already agreed! What are you doing?!
I wanted to shut her mouth right now, but if I did that, it would only look more suspicious.
“Bjorn... is this barbarian, right?” the wizard asked slowly.
“That’s right. Bjorn is no ordinary barbarian!”
“What do you mean ‘no ordinary barbarian?’”
“Bjorn is a wiser warrior than anyone else. He reads books in the library for six hours a day every day.”
“Hmm, that’s definitely unusual.”
“It’s not unusual, it’s great! I’ve never seen a barbarian as smart as Bjorn!”
Shit... Please, stop...
Everyone gave me strange looks thanks to Ainar’s praise, but the situation was thankfully brushed over as just a minor blip. They seemed to write it off as a barbarian’s naiveté.
For now, at least.
“Still, it’s a majority vote, so it can’t be helped. Hahaha!” the dwarf laughed.
“What is a majority vote? What do you mean it can’t be helped?!” Ainar demanded.
Sensing the atmosphere growing tense again, I calmed Ainar down. I didn’t know what was making her so upset, but she was huffing and clearly dissatisfied.
“But Bjorn, you are better than that wizard!”
Could it be that the words “for a barbarian” had offended her?

I was not sure, but I was glad I had made her swear an oath in advance. Otherwise, our use of the dimensional instability phenomenon and the fact that I was the one who had opened the Rift might’ve been revealed.
“It’s a blessing to have a wife who holds you in such high regard. I envy you, barbarian! Hahaha!”
“W-Wife! I’m not a wife!”
“Hahaha. There is no need to be embarrassed!”
“Gahhh! I-I am not embarrassed!”
Anyway, thanks to the talkative dwarf, Ainar’s ire was drawn elsewhere. Relieved, I took the time to study Raven’s face. Despite my fears, she didn’t look particularly interested in me.
“Hmm, a barrier that prevents you from going outside. Interesting. It seems to separate the dimensions, but how can we see the other side with our naked eyes?”

Should I chalk the way she was acting up to a mage’s passion for knowledge? As I watched her muttering to herself while recording something in her notebook, I noticed that she seemed to be curious about the qualities of the barrier that prevented us from leaving the map. I hoped that intense curiosity would not end up fixating on me while we were working together.
“Why don’t we stop all this chitchat and start moving? I have a lot of research to do in order to retrieve the sample I need.”
At Raven’s words, the dwarf cocked his head. “Start moving? We still only know each other’s names.”

I felt the same. Every party should know what each other’s abilities were and what each member was capable of. No matter how quickly the party was formed, providing your teammates with a basic gist of who you were was fundamental.
However, Raven deemed that nonessential.
“Is that necessary? All of the monsters from the Bloody Citadel are rank seven or lower.”
Her voice was full of total confidence. The dwarf looked slightly uncomfortable at this, but he did not say anything.
...Until she added one more thing.
“Oh, I forgot to mention. I’ll be taking the loot from the guardian. I need it for my independent research.”
What kind of selfish bastard...
No wonder she had seemed so normal for a wizard.
God damn it.
Just as expected, things were about to get shitty again.

chapters.title: Chapter 29: Rift (3)
paragraphs: When playing Dungeon and Stone, in-fighting was bound to occur. And the cause of said in-fighting was always money. Research might have been the top priority of an economically secure wizard, but the reason why most adventurers entered the labyrinth was to make money...
So this wizard bitch had just touched on a very sensitive subject.
“You’re going to take all of the guardian’s loot?”
The dwarf was no longer smiling kindly. His voice was low and his eyes were gleaming through his thick hair.
“Do I look like a fucking fool?”
The atmosphere went ice-cold in an instant.
And sensing this—
Click.
The human man placed his hand on the hilt of his sword. Of course he wasn’t just an ordinary porter. Breaking the heavy silence, Raven opened her mouth.
“...In return, I will give you all the mana stones that come out of the Rift.”
“So you want us to eat your crumbs.”
“...I think this is a reasonable trade-off. The loot isn’t guaranteed to drop every time anyway.”
Although she tried not to show it, there was obvious alarm on Raven’s face. She probably hadn’t expected such a hostile reaction.
You naive woman. You should have known this would happen.
The guardian’s loot was pretty much the crown jewel of the Rift. And of the loot that could drop, the Numbers Item was a priceless treasure to a dwarf.
“I will not yield the Numbers Item,” said the dwarf.
“...Fine. I’ll take the guardian’s essence instead. And please acknowledge my ownership of any items we discover using my knowledge.”
“Fine. Then the two of us can flip a coin over who will take the Rift Stone fair and square.”
Haha. Fair and square, my ass.

The two did not even bother to look at me and Ainar as they started fighting for their own interests. Watching them gave me a headache. It was even making me think that it would have been better to clear the Rift through blood, sweat, and tears with other first-floor beginners.
If things continued like this, I was really going to have to pick up their crumbs. Being powerless was such a sorrowful state of being.
“Bjorn.”
“I know what you’re thinking, but for now, be quiet.”
“Okay.”

My job became clearer. I had to get stronger. Whether those assholes wanted to gatekeep or not, I needed to find my own way to the top. Only then would I be able to protect my interests like they could.
Of course, that wasn’t an excuse to concede today.
“Wait.”
When I opened my mouth, the two, who had begun conversing in a more civilized manner, turned their eyes to me.
“Take the essence and Numbers Item. But we will take the Rift Stone.”
“How greedy.”
“Do you think we’d have a problem clearing this map without two barbarians?”
Her eyes were very sharp as they landed on me.
Shit, where did those friendly smiles from the beginning of our encounter go?
Yeah, well, I was just testing the waters.
“Okay, I’ll give up the Rift Stone. In exchange, give us first dibs on two essences aside from the guardian’s.”
“Fine. That much is doable.”
“That’s fine with me too.”

As expected, Raven and the dwarf readily accepted my request. This must have been their Maginot Line. At their level, an essence from a monster other than the guardian wouldn’t be all that attractive anyway.
“Shall we go now, then?”
“Yes, standing still is making my body itch to move! Hahaha!”
Once the negotiations were over, the wizard bitch and the dwarf reverted back to their previous selves and laughed.
Freaky adventuring bastards.
How long had it been since we had started climbing the mountain road along the fortress?
When we reached the entrance to the fortress, we encountered two winged demon sculptures.
“It’s a gargoyle statue.”
[Rank Eight Monster: Gargoyle Statue.]

It was a tricky monster that usually didn’t move, but when an enemy came into view, it used Petrification and began attacking. The common strategy for dealing with these monsters was to sacrifice one person to Petrification, while the rest defeated the gargoyle statue to release the curse, but...
Unlike most parties, we now had a wizard.
“Kyaaah!”
As the dwarf and I approached the statue, the gargoyle opened its eyes and spread its wings. At the same time, my lower body turned to stone, but it didn’t last long.
“Artena Viar.”
Raven recited the [Curse Removal] spell, and the battle officially began. Ainar and I took on one gargoyle, and the dwarf took the other.
Bang!

The short dwarf swung his hammer like a madman and smashed both of the gargoyle’s legs. Then, when the gargoyle fell to the ground, he smashed its head with the hammer as if he had been waiting for that exact opening.
Is this a dwarf’s fighting style?
Taking the enemy down from below was quite a manly-man technique. Well, it was the same on our end too.
“You guys are pretty good too!” yelled the dwarf.
There was not much difference in the time it took us to destroy the gargoyle statues. We, too, were confident in melee combat.
[You have killed a Gargoyle. EXP +2]
The two gargoyles turned into light and disappeared, dropping their mana stones, but there was no need to pick them up. They floated up on their own and were propelled into a large burlap bag.
“I will save the mana stones and distribute them as we go,” Raven said.
“That works for me! Hahaha!” replied the dwarf.
The dwarf didn’t seem to be worried about the wizard stealing the stones. To be fair, there was no way a wizard would get hung up on such a small amount of money.
“Then, let’s go!”
The dwarf smashed through the old wooden door with a hammer and cleared the way.
Is this the start of the real dungeon?
A strange feeling came over me and I followed him inside.
“We’re going to need some light.”
“Leait.”

A sphere of light floated above Raven’s hand, illuminating the dark room. The space we were currently entering was the outer checkpoint of the castle. It was a place that would have been used to perform various administrative tasks like checking the cargo of wagons and the identity of visitors before they entered the gates.
“Guhhh...”
Attracted by the light and sound, rotten corpses emerged from within the closet on the wall and under the table and began approaching us.
“It’s a horde of deadmen.”
Deadman: an unranked monster that didn’t even spit out mana stones, let alone experience points. Their bodies didn’t even disappear when they were defeated, except for when they dropped an essence.
“Since these monsters only bite and scratch, I’ll save my mana here,” said Raven.
Even without the help of magic, it didn’t take long to clean out the entire room.
“Mr. Murad and Mr. Yandel, can you go check out the top floor while I open the door?”
“We’ll be back soon! Hahaha!”

As I followed the dwarf to the second floor, a space that looked like a common sleeping area appeared before us. There were also about ten deadmen, but since the room was larger than the one on the first floor, they were even easier to take care of.
Smack! Smack!

We cleared out the second floor in an instant and climbed the ladder to the roof without much conversation. On the third floor, there were a dozen deadmen soldiers wearing rusty armor and a commander deadman who was slightly larger in stature. It couldn’t exactly be called our first boss monster, but it was one we had to get rid of in order to progress through the map.
“It’s big, but it doesn’t look all that different from the others, so let’s get rid of it! Hahaha!”

Once again, we quickly cleared out the area and went through the deadman commander’s clothes, picking up a horn. When we headed back down to the first floor, the iron door on the other side was already open.
“It’s very reassuring to have a wizard with us.”

As light poured in from both directions, the windowless room became quite bright, but it didn’t matter. All the work that needed to be done at the outer checkpoint was finished. Now, it was time to cross the 160-foot-long bridge.
“Please watch your step, Lady Raven.”
“Ah, thank you.”
The bridge stopped in the middle about twenty yards away from the gate. It wasn’t eroded, though—that was just how it had been designed.
Boooooo!
When the horn we obtained earlier was blown, the drawbridge began to descend with a rattling sound. And not only that...
[A long-dormant water-based magic circle has been activated.]
“Bjorn! Water is rising from below!”
The moat. Liquid began to fill the trench that had been dug around the fortress walls to prevent foreign invaders—dark, crimson blood.
That was why this place was called the “Bloody Citadel.” The sky was red and the ground was too. But there was something else that magnified this macabre vibe.
“Bjorn! Hand! There’s a hand waving above the water over there!”
“Don’t be nervous, they’re deadmen.”
“Hmph, who said I was nervous?”

As soon as the blood reached the bottom of the bridge, the deadmen who had been floundering on the surface of the river were able to climb onto it. The drawbridge had not yet come down a fifth of the way. The concept behind this part of the map was simple.
[Stay alive until the drawbridge comes down.]
If we were in the game, that was the message that would have appeared.
“Guhhh...”
However, while there were no specific instructions given here, everyone instinctively knew what to do and started pushing the deadman off or smacking them down with their weapons.
Smack! Smack! Crunch!
Although our opponents were deadmen, which were unranked monsters, they were a rather difficult foe on the bridge. That was because if you fell off, it was game over.
“All done.”
After about a minute, Raven completed her magic spell.
“Uterna Dertu!”
If I were to translate the spell name directly, it would be [Storm of Blades.] A strong, dense gust of wind surrounded us and ground the deadmen up in an instant, almost like a blender.
Tututututu.
Almost immediately, the bridge was covered in the corpses of deadmen.
“...Amazing,” the dwarf exclaimed.
“They’re just deadmen, of course.”

In contrast to her humble words, however, Raven’s eyes were full of pride. But it didn’t feel like arrogance to me at all. This was not a part of the map that could be easily traversed without a wizard with some kind of wide-range spell. As we continued to turn the deadmen that had climbed up onto the bridge into mush, the slowly descending drawbridge finally came into contact with the bridge.
Boooom!
The first stage of the Bloody Citadel was over... ridiculously easily.

Having crossed the drawbridge, we had three remaining stages ahead of us: a battle in the outer wall of the city, the dungeon in the inner wall, and then the demon worship room inside the lord’s castle.
“This is interesting.”
Raven’s eyes lit up once she entered the castle and took a look at the ruins. It was like a treasure had just been dropped right in front of her.
“Blacksmiths, taverns, inns, churches, stables used by merchants... Most of this wreckage appears to be public facilities.”
The dwarf grinned.
“Is that all that surprising, Miss Raven?”

“Of course. Neither the mountain road we climbed nor the castle had any farmland or dwellings. Meaning there were no farmers in this city. Aren’t you curious? What did everyone in this fortified city, built in such a remote mountain area, eat to survive?”
“Well, aren’t there alchemists in this dimension too? They must have just turned mana stones into bread like we did. Hahaha.”
“...In truth, most scholars agree that’s the most likely explanation.”
“Haha! Is that right? Even smart people agree with me!”

“But, Mr. Murad, that’s not the only thing that’s interesting. With that long drawbridge and those high walls, this citadel was clearly built to be functional. But who was the enemy they were guarding against?”
As the conversation dragged on, the dwarf grew bored and started to distance himself from the wizard.
“I don’t understand why you’re asking all these questions. After all, isn’t this entire dimension man-made?”
“A constructed space... People who haven’t studied dimensionalism might think so, but—”
“Stop, Miss Raven, there are monsters coming.”

Monsters appeared not too long into our journey into the inner city, from deadmen to skeleton archers, mages, ghouls, and even a rank eight monster, a death fiend. The level of the creatures spawning was not much different from those that could be found in the Land of the Dead, but there was a big difference in scale. Each group had at least several dozen monsters.
“Everyone, get close to me.”

Moreover, while we were dealing with one group, others heard us and gathered. Within a minute of encountering the first group, hundreds of monsters surrounded the area. But at that moment, the Storm of Blades we had gotten to witness earlier swept the surrounding area once more.
Shhh—!

Like any magic spell made for mass slaughter, it couldn’t grind through every single one of them. Some of the ghouls survived with just one severed limb, and that wasn’t even taking into account the high defense and regenerative ability of the death fiend. But...
“Please take care of the remaining monsters.”
There was no doubt that by slaughtering the deadmen and skeletons, which accounted for more than 90 percent of the monsters, Raven had done the work of multiple people.
“Ainar!” I shouted, and Ainar ran out. Our target was the death fiend, and our method of hunting it was... Well, it didn’t require any verbal explanation. One glance at each other was all it took.
“Behelahhh!”
We had fought hundreds of monsters together and had now reached a point where we hardly made any mistakes. It was time for the True Double Barbarian Tackle.
Boom!
The dwarf watched in astonishment as we lifted both of the death fiend’s legs up into the air, slammed it onto the floor, and then smashed its head open.
“...Do you normally hunt like this?”
His eyes seemed to say, ‘Who are these barbarians?’
“Is there a problem?”
“No. Quite—quite exciting, just like a typical barbarian! Hahaha!”
There was no point in being embarrassed, but I found this a little ironic. I mean, the fighting method dwarves used wasn’t particularly elegant or sophisticated either.
“Raviod Eheltun.”

There were seven death fiends left, but when Raven put a Wound Exacerbation Curse on them, they were easy to take down. Death fiends, which had an innate Body Preservation passive ability, weren’t that difficult of a monster to deal with.
“I think I can see why everyone thinks wizards are great...” Ainar muttered blankly.
Had she come to understand how useful wizards were in just two battles?
Raven didn’t respond, but when I looked, I could see her lips twitching. She seemed pleased about the admiration coming her way.
The dwarf threw in his two cents too.
“Haha! No doubt about it, having a wizard completely changes what you’re able to do.”

I agreed as well. If we had attempted the Bloody Citadel with a party of five beginners, a head-to-head battle like this would not have been possible. We would have been stuck trying to pick off their numbers from the outskirts, and it would have taken ten times longer.
“Hmm, well... This is what I studied so hard for. You also need to have a talent for it, of course.”

Raven fidgeted at the successive compliments. Slowly, I was beginning to get a grasp of her character—a gifted wizard girl who pretended to be humble but loved to show off and was extremely passionate about magic and research. And I was starting to get a sense of how to deal with her too.
“Then I’m going to go around and collect some research data for a bit. If it’s okay with you, can you all give me a hand?”
“We’re ahead of schedule thanks to you, so of course we can help. Hahaha!”
“Thank you.”
So, after the battle, we scoured the rubble of the city, collecting antiques, books, soil, metal, and the flesh and bones of the deadmen.
“Thanks to all of you, I finished early. So, let’s move on!”
I was stunned for a moment.
Huh? Wait, you’re done? You defeated all the monsters and searched the entire area, so why are you not taking it?
“What are you doing over there? We’re leaving.”
Could it be...they really didn’t know? What about the item that you could easily find if you broke the statue in the fountain?

chapters.title: Chapter 30: The Bloody Citadel (1)
paragraphs: Every gamer had a habit of pressing the interaction key whenever a suspicious wall or unusual sculpture appeared, and I was the same way. That habit had helped me uncover many hidden Easter eggs—that is, hidden elements—in my time playing Dungeon and Stone for the past nine years.
...Like the fountain statue here, for example.
“Bjorn?”
“Oh, coming.”
Setting my apprehension aside, I followed my party into the inner city. I decided not to mention the statue.
A barbarian knowing something that even a wizard who had dedicated their life to knowledge didn’t know?
It would be better to avoid attracting suspicion.
It was obvious that lying and saying I had seen it in a book wouldn’t work this time, and the thing in the statue was an item that couldn’t be taken out of the Rift even with warp magic anyway.
