“So this is the inner city.”

If the outer fortress served as the first line of defense in the Middle Ages, the inner fortress was closer to the last stronghold. Originally, this place would have held various military facilities, such as an armory where the vassals, knights, and soldiers of the lord would have been stationed.
Raven looked around and sighed.
“...I heard it was like this, but it looks like I won’t get anything out of this area.”
The inner city, which was one-third the size of the outer fortress, was entirely destroyed. All the buildings had collapsed and only ruins remained. There weren’t even monsters there.
“Let’s move on to the next area as fast as possible.”
Under Raven’s command, we cleared the rubble for about thirty minutes until we found a way to the basement.
“Mr. Murad, can you take the lead?”
“Sure!”
“Ah, I need to conserve my magic, so please light a torch as well.”
The dwarf took out a torch and placed it on his head. Maybe it was because he was short, but he looked like a mole miner from a cartoon.
Whoosh!
We pushed away the thick wooden planks and slowly descended the stairs hidden beneath them. This was the third stage of the Bloody Citadel: the Underground Prison.
I gulped and prepared myself.
[You have entered the first floor of The Underground Prison.]
Damn it, I don’t know if my stomach can handle this...
“Miss Raven, what kind of monsters show up here?”
“I know there will be skull rats, banshees, death fiends, chimera wolves, ghoul lords, and a corpse golem.”
“Except for the corpse golem, those are all monsters I’ve dealt with before.”
“That makes sense. Corpse golems are monsters that only appear in the Bloody Citadel.”
“Hahaha, I’ll be earning an achievement for the first time in a while!”

The dwarf was happy to hear that he would be increasing his experience points by fighting new monsters. But I wasn’t. Even the 2D pixel drawings of them were horrifying. How disgusting were they going to be in reality?
“Is there anything else we should watch out for?”

“You just have to be careful of the corpse golem’s Flesh Burst. The explosion itself is not very strong, but its bodily fluids are mixed with an acidic toxin, so it can be fatal if you get hit at a close range. Of course, I’ll try to stop it before that happens.”
“Haha! There is nothing to be afraid of when there is a wizard around!”
“Well, it’s all possible because there are strong warriors like you here, Mr. Murad.”
Ha...
It was not that long ago that they had been glaring murderously at each other over the loot.
Step.

As soon as I reached the last stair, a labyrinthine dungeon structure unfolded before my eyes. Chained deadmen roared at us from inside cages, and on the floor, rats with only bones left on their bodies roamed around making strange noises.
“Bjorn, are those monsters too?”
“Those are the skull rats I mentioned earlier.”
“I didn’t ask you, wizard!”

To clarify, skull rats were unranked like the deadmen were. In fact, they didn’t even have enough fighting power to be called a monster, so we walked forward, crushing the ones we could see with our feet. And not long after, we encountered a banshee.
“Heh heh heh!”
The banshee was flying around like a vengeful spirit, only the outline of its bizarre face visible.
“B-Bjorn...”
Oh, right. She’s afraid of banshees.
Noticing Ainar clinging to me, Raven grinned. I was glad Ainar hadn’t noticed. Otherwise, she would have thrown another fit.
“Be careful not to bump into the banshee. Once or twice isn’t too much of a problem, but...”
“Otherwise, you will have a very, very, very, very terrible experience.”
“A-A very, very terrible experience? What does that mean?! Speak clearly, wizard!”
“Hmm. How about I leave it to your imagination?”
Raven flashed an ominous grin at Ainar, who was as pale as a ghost. Given that she was taking revenge like this, I could tell her personality wasn’t all that great.
I sighed inwardly and cut into their conversation.
“I heard wizards have a way of dealing with banshees.”
“Right, you did say you like to read. You’re very well-informed, aren’t you?”
Was this something to call me ‘well-informed’ over? Well, given that I was a barbarian, that could be the case...
Still, this was probably within the realm of something even a barbarian could know.
“Anyway, enough joking around. I’ll clear out the banshees first. Tayrun Shell.”

Immediately, Raven fired an arrow of light from her staff and shot the banshee. The name of the spell in the game was [Magic Arrow.] The spell didn’t even require any casting time because it was a basic attack spell.
“Keeheee!”

We stood and waited for a moment, and soon dozens of vengeful banshees began to flock to the area with clear hatred in their eyes. They had sensed the “mark” that had been left behind by their fellow banshee when it died. Although, this was probably a welcome sight for a wizard who possessed a large number of powerful area-of-effect spells.
“Iherno Heindar.”
[Flame Baptism.]
Flames emitted from the magic staff filled the straight passageway. And by the time the fire slowly began to die out, there were no banshees remaining.
Whooom!

Once again, the mana stones that poured onto the floor floated into the air and found their way into her bag. That was what I envied even more than the attack spells she had—not having to pick up mana stones every time.
Man, how long would it be until I could add a wizard to my party?
I still had a long way to go.
The 2D world I saw through the monitor and the real world were different. The chill that permeated through my skin was even more so.
[You have entered the second floor of The Underground Prison.]

The dungeon that I was now getting to experience firsthand was a lot like a mad scientist’s laboratory. In it, there was a chimera wolf with three or four heads and the ripped muscles of a mutant, and a ghoul lord accompanied by around thirty elder ghouls.
These rank eight monsters were not only grotesque in appearance, but the small props around them were also reminiscent of a horror game. However, the cherry on top was...
“By the way, Miss Raven, you’re amazing. Aren’t you scared at least a little bit?”
“Hmm. I love anatomy, you see. This much doesn’t faze me.”
Shit, I hope that isn’t barbarian body parts I’m seeing.
Come to think of it, the reason why barbarian hearts were sold at high prices was because they were magical ingredients...
“Ah, we’ve arrived.”

After hunting all the monsters in the Underground Prison and reaching the third floor of the basement, we discovered a hidden door leading to an underground part of the collapsed lord’s castle. We usually would have had to obtain the map from the guard room first, but...
“So the door was hidden behind the wall. Good thing I memorized the map in advance.”

Thanks to Raven, who had thoroughly studied up on the map, we didn’t get lost. Well, even if I had been alone, I wouldn’t have had any problems either. The layout of the Underground Prison had been identical in the game.
But that’s only possible for me because I’m a player.

Once again, I realized just how high-status wizards were. Powerful attack spells, highly useful support abilities like the [Wound Exacerbation Curse], and knowledge that must have been accumulated through reading numerous books... There was a reason that wizards were even more appreciated by their parties than priests.
“It would be best to leave our backpacks over here. Especially Mr. Yandel.”
Feeling a little embarrassed, I placed the oversized backpack that went down from my head to my thighs in front of the door.
...Once I make money, the first thing I’m going to buy is a magic backpack.
This was not the first time this bag had caused awkwardness.
“Ah, from now on, Mr. Yandel, you should light a torch as well.”
Following Raven’s instructions, I also put a torch on my head. With this, we were ready to go.
Creak, creak, creak—
When we turned the round valve to open the iron door, the stench of rot burned our nostrils.
“This place isn’t what I was expecting.”
“W-Wizard... Do we really have to go in?”
“I would also like nothing more than to not enter, but we have no other choice.”

The space was reminiscent of a wastewater treatment plant. The cylindrical walls were lined with large water pipes that had black filth dripping down them. In addition, broken and severed limbs and heads were piled up in a heap on the ground, and the gas that had accumulated from their decay stung my nose and gave me a headache.
Wretch.
The first to vomit was the porter. The guy, who had up to this point been standing next to Raven as solemnly as a bodyguard, emptied his stomach on the ground.
The second was Raven.
Wretch.
Even with a lot of dissection experience, she was still vulnerable to smell.
Surprisingly, I rode it out. Even though the scene before me would have made me faint in the past, it had no effect on this barbarian’s strong stomach.
“I’m glad you’re all right, at least,” said the dwarf. “Come on, get up here.”
I slowly approached the center of the room, and as I did, a strange feeling came over me.
Squish.
Each step sounded like stepping on a sponge. And as the torchlight neared the center, the huge shape we could see outlined in the darkness became clearer.
“Hi.”
Surprisingly, it spoke to us. It was a female voice that sounded like a broken audio guide.
“Heeek! Help! I... Help me! I! Crunch, crack, tas-ty, Father, hehe!”
Uh, um, uh...
To be honest, it was kind of terrifying.
I inhaled sharply.

Fuck, you were quiet in the game. Why are you doing this to me? I couldn’t help but complain in my head, but I knew that whining “woe is me” wasn’t going to change anything. When I glanced to the side, I noticed that even the steadfast dwarf was frozen in place.
“Everyone, snap out of it!” I immediately shouted, waking up my stunned teammates. But this seemed to provoke the voice even further.
“Father! Father! It hurts! It hurts! It hurts! It hurts!”
The pile of corpses on the ground stood up and stepped forward with something that looked like a foot.
Booom—!
This was the miniboss of the Bloody Citadel—the corpse golem.

Dungeon and Stone was the definition of an indie game, but it was not without popularity. At the very least, the game’s art was famous. This was because the realistic illustrations that looked almost like black-and-white photographs were often used as memes on the internet.
But very few people knew what game those illustrations were actually from.
In that moment, I once again realized—
“Shit.”
No matter how realistic a drawing was, it didn’t compare to the real deal.
“It hurts! It hurts! It hurts!”
Is that what a monster that has collected thousands of human arms, legs, and heads looks like?

Every limb even seemed to move individually, like they all had a life of their own. The same was true for the hundreds of mouths on its body. Each one of them spouted whatever they wanted to say without anything controlling them. Most of those words were cries of pain, cold, resentment, pleas to be killed, to be saved. Fragmented, irrational emotions.
“Kyaaah!”
Sometimes, it was just screaming.
Everyone once again froze at the disturbing cacophony created by the blending of all these bizarre voices.
“Hikurod! Be careful!”

A wizard who was knowledgeable in human anatomy, a dwarf who was a three-year veteran of the dungeons and must have encountered all sorts of monsters, and a human man who exuded a distinguished vibe for a porter. All of these people had treated the two novice barbarians as their benchwarmers, but...
Surprisingly, at this very moment, Ainar and I were the only ones who did not lose our cool.
“What are you all doing!”
Ainar, who kept her eyes locked on the corpse golem, grabbed the dwarf by the collar and lifted him up. And in that moment—
Bam!
A pile of corpses flew in like a shotput and exploded right where they had been standing. Blood and flesh splattered and stuck to Ainar and the dwarf.
Czzzzzz!
Fortunately, Ainar was uninjured thanks to her clothes, but the same could not be said for the dwarf.
“Ahh! Eyes! My eyes!”
Shit, it seemed that some of the blasts had somehow gotten through the narrow gap in his helmet and hit his eye.
In an instant, the dwarf was incapacitated. And the wizard who had told us not to worry and to just trust her...
Wretch!
Was still throwing up her guts.
...What are you guys doing?
No wonder things had been going so smoothly up to this point.
Of course.
“Ainar! Move the dwarf back and protect the wizard!”
After shouting that, I raised my shield and faced the corpse golem.
I had no choice. I wanted to avoid standing out as much as possible, but... The bastards who had been showing off their skills on the front lines were now fucking around.
“Behelaaah!”
So, in order to survive, I had no choice but to stand on the front line myself.

chapters.title: Chapter 31: The Bloody Citadel (2)
paragraphs: The corpse golem’s attack patterns were simple: fire corpse bombs at distant enemies and yank in nearby enemies and devour them using the hundreds of arms that sprouted all over its body like tentacles.
“Bjorn!”
Hearing Ainar’s worried cry, I kept my distance. If I got close enough, I would no longer be seen as a target for a corpse bomb, but...
Then the new target would be the wizard.
Slam!
I had to stall for time somehow, at least until the wizard came to her senses. Which meant I had to pull aggro on my own.
Slam!
Each time a corpse bomb flew in, I rolled to the side to increase my distance, then crouched behind the shield to protect myself from the acidic bodily fluids.
And, after doing this about three times—
“Iherno Heindar.”

Purifying flames appeared. In a stroke of luck, the wizard seemed to have recovered. I didn’t have to look back to confirm this and focused my attention solely on the corpse golem. With the screams of hundreds of people, the corpse golem’s body caught fire and its shell began peeling off.
My original plan of playing cat-and-mouse with it by narrowing the distance between us and then pulling back to burn the monster’s body with a torch had been carried out with one magic spell.
[The corpse golem’s outer skin has been nullified.]
But the smell of rotten corpses burning was evidently too much for her to bear.
Wretch!
I heard another round of vomiting start up behind me.
Please get it together soon...
Whatever. I didn’t need a wizard anymore.
“Ainar! It’s all right now. Come up next to me!”
I immediately called for Ainar. The corpse golem was a rank seven monster, but now that its skin had been peeled off, it was a monster that two barbarians could overcome.
“Kwohhh—!”

Its huge frame had shrunk a remarkable amount and was now only about ten feet in diameter. Now that the piles of animated dead bodies had been burned off and melted, only its iron-bar-like skeleton remained. It moved with a creak.
It had entered Bone Golem Mode.
“Kyaaah!”
Because of its reduced weight, it was much more agile. As I used my shield to block the arm the golem swung at me in a violent arc, I shouted behind me.
“Porter! You help too!”
“I must protect Lady Raven.”
Damn it all, I thought. That’s what I thought you’d say. Just you wait, I’ll make sure my hard work pays off right now.
Smack!

I leaped up high and slammed the mace down on the monster’s upper body. There was a shattering sound, but that was all. The ribs were so hard that only a small piece of bone chipped off. But now I just had to do it over and over again.
“Ainar! Aim for the chest!”
“Okay!”

Ainar and I attacked the corpse golem’s ribs, giving and taking aggro in turn. After about forty blows, its ribs, which were once as hard as walnut shells, cracked open, revealing the “nut” inside. It was its mana essence, a golem’s weak point.
Crunch!
After breaking the core with a mace, the corpse golem stopped moving and turned into light.
[You have killed a Corpse Golem. EXP +3]
The reward was one mana stone the size of a fist—fitting for a rank seven monster.
“Oh! How many loaves of bread is this—”
Ainar, who was admiring the size of the mana stone, suddenly froze. This was because the reward did not end with just one stone.
Whooom!
A halo of soft black light began to shine in the air.
“Bjorn, is this...?”
I gave a slight nod.
It was an essence.
The Rift was no different from a treasure trove.

Exclusive monsters who did not appear on the regular map were precious opportunities for adventurers who were otherwise unable to receive more experience points, never mind the loot one could get from the guardian.
Well, the main point was that the drop rate of essences here was exponentially higher.
Actually, probability-wise, it’s strange that an essence has only just appeared...
“What are you going to do?”
Ainar’s question forced me to refocus.
We were the rightful owners of the essence. The two of us had pretty much defeated the monster alone, for one, and that had been the agreement from the very beginning anyway. However...

Originally, I was after two specific contenders: the regenerative power of a death fiend and the strength of a chimera wolf. Both were essences of rank eight monsters. However, in the process of pursuing that goal, the essence of a corpse golem, which could only be earned by defeating a rank seven elite monster in the Bloody Citadel, had now appeared in front of me.
The difficulty alone of obtaining this rare essence was unmatched by the other two prospects...
But it was too early to celebrate. The penalty for this item was as severe as its unique effects were great.
[Corpse Golem
Pain Resistance +70
Bone Strength +55
Poison Resistance +12
Strength +15
Perception -5
Appetite +9
Weight +21]

First of all, the basic stats were well-suited for a tank. The decline in perception would affect the user’s eyesight and reaction time, and their overall senses would become duller. But in turn, their other stats would increase a lot. Bone Strength, which affected defense as much as physical resistance, was +55, and Weight, which affected recoil and bludgeoning damage in-game, was +21.
Pain Resistance would also be very useful in the real world, and Appetite was a stat that would 100 percent be useful with Strength and Poison Resistance. But...
[Special:
(P) Acid Fluid — Blood becomes acidic.
(A) Flesh Burst — A powerful burst originating from a part of the body.]
The active skill was the only flaw.
Flesh Burst dealt a high amount of damage, but the character paid the price in HP.
Could I just use the passive skill?

Sealing off a skill was not only a huge loss, but by consuming this essence, the durability of your equipment would be drastically reduced every time you got injured because your acidic blood would get on it.
“Whew...”
From the outrageous potion cost to the equipment cost, it was an essence that was both useless and useful.

Usually, when this essence appeared in the game, I’d feed it to the NPC I carted around with me for the purpose of abandoning it. It was a waste to throw it away, but too iffy to feed it to the main character.
But the essence you consume at the beginning has to be discarded someday anyway, so taking this now wouldn’t be a bad idea...
“Let’s hold onto it for now and treat the dwarf first.”
Even without an owner, the essence could last for thirty minutes, so there was no need to make an impulsive decision. I might even be able to use it to strike a deal.
Having come to that conclusion, I turned around and bore witness to a scene that was nothing less than a mess.
Had the porter provided him with a potion? The dwarf was rolling around from the pain of the potion, and for some reason, the wizard also seemed to have one foot in the grave.
“Do not come closer.”
His name was... Tarzine, I think? This rude-ass escort bastard now stood in our way despite having done nothing this whole time.
Shit, what did we do?
“Why is she like that?” I asked from a distance.
“She is experiencing backlash from using too much magic,” the porter answered.
Backlash, huh...

He seemed to be referring to a “circuit break,” a condition that sometimes occurred when an attempt to cast a spell failed. Upon closer inspection, she was literally vomiting blood, not just her dinner.
Wretch!
Was this because she’d used magic while her stomach was rebelling from the smell? That was ridiculous to me, but it was definitely plausible for Dungeon and Stone.
Unlike other games, where cause and effect are usually very clear, in this game, a seemingly insignificant “cause” could be life-threatening.
“Are you going to keep standing there? It would be best to move her out of the room,” I said.
“...Please take care of the dwarf here.”
After escorting Raven and the dwarf back out to the underground prison and waiting for a while, her condition started to improve. However, the first one to wake up was the dwarf.
“How shameful... Thank you. We would’ve been in trouble if it weren’t for the two of you.”
“I’m glad you realize that.”

I had no reason to act humble. It wasn’t like I would gain anything from it. It was true that I had made a big contribution, and using that as leverage, I was planning to raise my pay. To that end, it would be best to inflate our worth.
“If it weren’t for Ainar, you’d be dead already.”
“I know. It’s embarrassing to admit, but as soon as I saw the monster, my body froze. Until now, I thought I’d seen everything there was to see in this world...”

It once again hit me that this place was real. If this were a game, we would have had more than enough manpower to kill that monster, but for psychological reasons, these people had almost been killed by a mid-level boss who wasn’t even a guardian.
“But what happened to this lady?”
“Apparently, it’s backlash. She took a potion, though, so she’ll get better soon.”
After taking the potion, the wizard, who had gone from vomiting to screaming, came to her senses just ten minutes later.
“I’ve caused an inconvenience.”

She pretended to be fine when she opened her mouth, but she no longer had an aristocratic air to her. The corners of her lips and neck were smeared with vomit and blood, and even her fine blonde hair was loose and dirty. Her shiny robes were also a mess from rolling around on the ground.
“We took care of the corpse golem.”
“Yes. I know. Good thing I cast that spell, even though it took a toll.”
Was this the habit of all adventuring assholes? To mention your own achievements without saying thank you?
If I didn’t speak up now, I knew that raising my pay would be impossible. I needed to secure proof.
“We saved you both. It could be argued that we’ve done more than our share. Do you agree, wizard?”
“...I agree.”

Raven nodded like she didn’t want to admit it. It seemed that it was quite shameful to her that the two barbarians she had been ignoring had accomplished such a big feat. To be honest, it was really satisfying, but leaving some breathing room right now would help with negotiations.
“Of course, your magic was excellent. Such a strong flame. You have overworked yourself for the sake of the team.”
“I did, but... So, what do you want?”
“We will take the Rift Stone,” I said bluntly.
Essence, Numbers Item, Rift Stone.

Those were the three items of loot a guardian could drop. When I had first asked for the Rift Stone, they had sent sharp glares our way, called us greedy, and said that they didn’t need two barbarians anyway.
But now, things were different.
There was an awkward silence. I waited patiently without pressing. The key to negotiation was in the waiting.
The dwarf expressed his approval first. “I accept those terms. If it wasn’t for this barbarian lady here, I’d be dead.”
So he was repaying the favor, then?
However...
“I refuse.”
Raven wasn’t going to agree so easily. However, that didn’t mean she didn’t concede anything at all.
“But if the Rift Stone does come out, I can at least give you a fair chance.”

Simply put, that meant that she would give us a chance to bid on it. That was a little disappointing, but it was true that her role in this quest was vital. I knew I was going to have to be satisfied with this outcome, especially since we didn’t have much time left anyway.
Then came the next point of debate.
“Ah, and there was an essence.”
“An essence? The corpse golem dropped an essence?”
“That’s right.”
The dwarf and Raven’s jaws dropped, surprised that something so difficult to obtain had appeared.
“Amazing. It looks like you haven’t obtained an essence yet. To think this is the first one you managed to get...”
“I heard that the essence of a corpse golem is so rare that even the Adventurer’s Guild doesn’t fully understand its abilities.”

Raven relayed that the essence of a corpse golem was ranked higher than the essence of a guardian in terms of rarity. The thirst for knowledge in her eyes was the icing on the cake. I finally pulled out the offer I had been keeping close to my vest this entire time.
“You may trade it for the essence of the guardian if you wish.”
“Pardon? But I’m not sure if the guardian will give us an essence at all...”
Raven trailed off with a strange look on her face. From the look of things, she liked my suggestion.
“I will take on that risk.”
“Okay then, that’s okay with me. I don’t know about other adventurers, but the corpse golem is actually more my interest. I didn’t expect this to come out, though...”
With that, the negotiations were finalized.
“Miss Raven, I heard that wizards can’t absorb essences. Will you be giving that essence to that porter?”
“No, the essence itself is worth studying.”

Raven took out a test tube from the bag on the porter’s back. This was one of the reasons why wizards were overpowered characters. They could carry an essence outside the labyrinth without even directly absorbing it into their bodies.
To do so, they did need to prepare one thing, though.
“Oh! Did you bring a test tube? I heard that that is an exorbitantly expensive item.”
“...I only have one too.”

If you put the essence of a monster below rank six in a test tube, it was almost impossible to store the real deal afterward. However, Raven seemed to place more value on the essence of the corpse golem than the guardian.
Whooom!
Raven chanted a spell and the essence was sucked into the test tube. She carefully double-wrapped the box and stored it in her backpack.
“Let’s get out of this terrible place.”
“I’ve been waiting for you to say that!”

We climbed up the sticky ladder and moved quickly through the large water pipe. The only monsters that appeared were skull rats and deadmen. The pipes had a foul odor, but nothing compared to the room where the corpse golem had dwelled.
After traveling for about thirty minutes, we reached our destination.
“I will head up first.”
There was a staircase beyond a rusty iron fence that we knocked down with one kick. When I climbed it, a spacious stone chamber lay before me.
Breathing in as much fresh air as I could, I studied my surroundings.
“What is that? It doesn’t look like a gargoyle statue.”
“Since I don’t sense any mana, it must just be a sculpture.”
Intimidating demonic statues were everywhere. And there was a floor filled with human skulls...
“There must have been a lord’s castle right on top of this chamber. If it hadn’t collapsed, I would have been able to investigate inside...”
As if she didn’t pick up on the creepiness of this place, Raven licked her lips like it was a pity.

“It’s just as I was told. The layout of this room is typical of a place of worship. However, the fact that it’s hidden underground means that the religion did not fit the social sentiments of the time. For example, it might have been a religion that worshipped an evil god.”
“I-I see.”
The dwarf was freaked out by Raven’s overly unnecessary explanation. I spoke up to get them both back on guard before the speech could get too long.
“Why don’t we stop chatting and get ready?”
Actually, I was talking to myself too. That was because the last stage of the Rift, the [Demon Worship Room,] was not a place to be taken lightly...
“Bjorn, I have a bad feeling about this.”
...Especially for an unlucky bastard like me.

chapters.title: Chapter 32: The Bloody Citadel (3)
paragraphs: Push.
Once Raven pushed a stone on the wall, the candles in the stone chamber lit up all at once, brightening the interior of the hall.
“Oh, how did you know about that?”
“Books are a treasure trove of knowledge.”
Why can’t you just say you read it in a book?
“Let’s see. Ah! Here’s another one.”
Raven pushed in another brick, and after a mechanical click, a book fell from the ceiling—the Necronomicon. It was a book of black magic and an item sold at a fairly high price.
Damn it...
“Since I found this myself, I’ll keep it as agreed.”
“Fair. That’s something we can take along without distortion magic anyway.”
“Hahaha...”
Raven laughed awkwardly. Of course she already knew that. The Necronomicon was considered an item, so it could be taken outside the Rift even without distortion magic.
“Would you mind putting this in my backpack?”
“Yes, Lady Raven.”
It left a bitter taste in my mouth, but all I could do was watch the wizard take the loot for herself.
Dang, I thought I’d be able to collect that item myself later on... How come she knew about that, but not about the one that was hidden under the statue?
“Shall we keep going, then?”
The passageway we were walking down was about thirty feet wide, and soon we came to a huge devil statue and a fork in the road.
“Miss Raven?”
“It doesn’t matter which path we choose. We’re going to hunt all the monsters on the way anyway, right?”
We went around a rectangular demon worship room and took down the monsters one by one. The monsters that appeared were gargoyle statues, death fiends, chimera wolves, and bone knights.
“We’ve been really lucky in many ways. The fact that we got the essence of a corpse golem was already a stroke of luck, but these also happen to be longing-type knights.”
In sharp contrast to my usual state of affairs, luck continued to be on our side.
The bone knight, a rank seven monster, had one of three random attributes—Hate, Sorrow, or Longing. And we were getting the easiest and most rewarding type of them all.

“The longing type only has the Vitality Absorption ability, which restores their health after an injury. And that can be easily canceled out by my Wound Exacerbation spell,” Raven proudly bragged, but the fact was that with or without her, the longing-type knight was the easiest to deal with. The sorrow-type bone knight emitted a mist that caused hallucinations, which was a very annoying ability even in the game. However, even that couldn’t compare to the hate-type.
“That would be lucky,” the dwarf quibbled, “but I heard that the hate-type monster is the weakest.”
Bullshit.
Knights of Hate had the Soul Slash ability, an insane skill that caused no physical damage but reduced the target’s level by a terrifying amount.
[Comrade A has suffered serious damage to their soul. Their level has dropped.]

Once the skill was deployed, these battle logs would pop up, whether about HP, defense, or magic resistance. And when this log appeared, it was easier to just restart with a new character—much easier than recovering the lost experience points by working your ass off to open portals.
“A decrease in Dignity of Soul... How terrifying.”
At Raven’s explanation on my behalf, the dwarf shuddered and let out a breath of relief. However, the wizard did not miss the opportunity to show off her knowledge even more and continued to explain.
“Ah, also, if you possess as many essences as your soul can hold, one will be lost at random. That’s probably something other adventurers don’t know.”
As was typical of a wizard, she only spoke the truth. However, if I could add one thing as a pro...
Soul Slash was more effective against lower-level characters. And my current level was only two.
Plus, with my streak of bad luck, I was extremely lucky not to have met a Hate knight—
“There’s an essence.”
Fuck, is my luck finally turning around for the better?
Even though we had only taken down a few monsters, an essence that belonged to none other than the rank seven bone knight popped out.
What the hell? First came the corpse golem, and now... Was I in some kind of special event?
“It’s like god is watching over you two. Hahaha!”
“I agree. Maybe this means the guardian’s essence will appear too.”

They each sent words vaguely reminiscent of congratulations my way. But there was an unspoken question in their comments, and that was which one of us was going to consume the essence—me or Ainar. After taking a moment to think it over, I made a difficult decision.
“Ainar, you take this.”
“I-Is that all right?”
It’d be a lie to say I didn’t want it. In fact, the guardian was the only boss monster that was left, and no one could guarantee that another essence would appear. However...
“You said you wanted to get stronger, right? You take this.”

From a gamer’s point of view, it was more logical for Ainar to take this instead of me. Vitality Absorption was a good fit for someone who wielded a sword, and I was going to have to throw out my weapon someday.

Above all else, Ainar was reliable. Given her honorable personality, I knew she would stay by my side. So, rather than being impulsive, it would be more efficient to use Ainar’s new strength to acquire an essence that was better suited for me.
“T-Thanks, Bjorn! You are the best! I will definitely repay this favor!”
With my permission, Ainar excitedly took the essence. The change was dramatic and immediate.
“W-Wow! You guys suddenly grew taller!”
“You’re the one who’s gotten smaller, Ainar.”
“What?! Is that true?”
Ainar, who used to be around 6‘5”, had shrunk. In an instant, her height dropped to just under six feet.
“That’s a basic side effect of using a bone knight’s essence. As bone density significantly increases, height decreases proportionately.”

Raven, who liked to explain things, was now even reciting information about the natural laws of the world. However, if you weren’t interested in expressing things in terms of (High), (Middle), (Low), etcetera, the exact numbers would look something like this:
[Bone Knight
Cutting Force: +12
Bone Density: +55
Agility: +15
Endurance: +15
Flexibility: -7
Height: -25
(P) Antiseptic — Effects that increase wound severity (Poison, Bleeding, Decay, etc.) are halved.
(A) Vitality Absorption — Temporarily increases the user’s healing factor when attacking a living creature.]
“Don’t worry. You haven’t lost muscle mass just because you’ve gotten shorter—”
“I-I am ruined! No one will see me as a warrior! Everyone already looks down on me because I am a woman!”
...Looks down on you because you’re a woman? Could it be that she has an inferiority complex?

“By the way... You’re very pretty now,” Raven murmured even as she bore witness to Ainar’s despair as if that was at all relevant information right now. “Is it because your bone structure has shrunk? Maybe this essence could be sold to nobles for cosmetic purposes—”
“T-That means that I no longer look like a warrior!”
I hadn’t realized she was going to take it this hard. I rushed to fix things.
“No, Ainar, everyone knows you’re a great warrior!”
To be honest, except for the tattoos on her upper body, she kind of just looked like a tall human woman now.
“What’s wrong with being a little shorter?”
“This isn’t a little!”
“...But you’re much stronger! Doesn’t that make up for it?”
I had to be the one to console her. The rest of these people were sociopaths who were busy using the misfortunes of others to discuss their own interests.
“Hahaha! What a strange essence. If a dwarf like me took it, he’d become invisible!”
“Hmm, that’s an interesting thought. Whether the reduction in height is proportional or absolute is something I should do further research into once I get back.”
“I am ruined!”
“Hahaha! Even though you’re short, your voice is very loud! I wonder if it’s because you’re a barbarian!”
“Miss Ainar, if it’s okay with you, can I conduct some tests on you once we get back to the city?”
“I am ruined!!”
I wish everyone would just shut up... My ears and head were hurting.
“A death fiend!”

The noise thankfully subsided once a monster approached us in the middle of the commotion. However, curious about Ainar’s transformation after absorbing the essence, everyone took a step back and signaled their intention to observe.
“Behelah...”
Ainar swung her greatsword with a lifeless shout. And...
Slice!
I hadn’t heard it wrong. For the first time, her sword made a slashing sound instead of a ‘bang!’
Did +12 to Cutting Force make this big a difference?
“Ainar! Aim for the head!”
“Uh, uh... okay!”
Startled by her own transformation, Ainar jumped high and slashed the greatsword vertically. At which point...
Slice!
The death fiend, who we normally needed to hit dozens of times between the two of us, was killed in a single blow. She had cut right through its hard skull and reached its brain.
“Look! You’ve gotten much stronger!”
“Then, am I still a warrior...?”
“Of course not.”
She looked at me in confusion.
“Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin! You are not just a warrior! You are a strong warrior!”
“Behelahhh!”
Thank god. That cheered her up. Her new body would still be strange, but Ainar would become much stronger once she got used to it.
“What a great couple they are.”
“I feel the same way.”
I ignored the conversation between Raven and the dwarf and proceeded. I realized once again that the only way to shut these guys up was by fighting some monsters.
“Come on! Bjorn! If you take an essence too, you can become a stronger warrior like me!”
Regaining her motivation, Ainar fought the battle with her entire heart and soul.
Smack! Smack, clang—! Slice!
Unfortunately, even after we finished hunting all the monsters in the prayer room, no additional essences came out. But I did not lose hope...
The crown jewel of the Rift, the guardian, still remained.
If I had been this lucky so far, didn’t it make sense to expect a little more?
Just as I was thinking that...
“I had a lot of fun with you guys, but now it’s coming to an end.”
The dwarf uttered words that set off red flags. Raven said the same.
“That’s too bad. This is the first time I’ve entered a labyrinth, but I think I can understand why my seniors do this work.”
Instantly, that sobered me up.
Come to think of it, had my life ever gone this smoothly? Mm, well, I was sure this wouldn’t be the first time...
But the problem was the big events that always followed these periods of smooth sailing in my life.
The relaxed screws in my head tightened all at once, while a strange, ominous feeling fell over me.
“I will head in, then.”

What could be the problem? What was the worst that could happen? In-fighting? No, I didn’t think that would be it. We’d already agreed upon the loot distribution, and something like that would only become relevant after the guardian died anyway.
...Creak.

Even as the dwarf was opening the door to the stone chamber, I studied our surroundings. Certain that something was going to happen, I paid close attention to every little detail I could catch. Also, I reviewed all the information about the Bloody Citadel that I could think of from the game.
And then, I figured it out.
“Door! Shut the door!”
“What do you mean—”
Damn it, is it already too late?
Dddddd!

At the exact moment the door opened, the ground began to shake violently. Then, in the center of the spacious stone chamber, a dark figure stood up and took off their robe to reveal a pale face. Only the wizard, Raven, realized the gravity of the situation we were currently in.
“N-no way...”
The guardian of the Rift had changed. The creature in the room wasn’t the Death Knight that should have been waiting for us here...
[The lord of the Bloody Citadel has awakened from a deep slumber.]

Instead, it was a boss monster that worked alone, yet a monster with a rank five difficulty rating. A true hybrid monster that was proficient in black magic as well as hand-to-hand combat. A monster that could normally only be met—and even then the odds were slim—after the sixth floor.
“Vampire...”
And it was a high-rank mutant, not even an ordinary vampire, at that. Simply put, the figure standing before us was a named monster with intelligence, its own name, and a backstory.
I even knew his name.
“You are the first living thing I’ve seen in a long time.”
Vampire Duke Cambormere.
“Where did you all come from?”
On behalf of the frozen group, I opened my mouth.
“Run.”
Fuck, why are you doing this to me?
I had put so much effort into getting him in the game, but he hadn’t appeared once.

chapters.title: Chapter 33: Warrior (1)
paragraphs: Monsters could be broadly classified into four categories.
1. Mutants. Similar to goblin archers and swordsmen, the race is the same but the monsters’ class varies.

2. High-rank species. The death fiend I ran into in the Land of the Dead falls under this category. This classification was relative—if the monster’s rank was higher than the average rank of the other monsters on that floor, it was considered a higher-rank species.
3. Rare species. Monsters that could only be found in certain Rifts, like corpse golems, or monsters that were extremely difficult to find in normal maps, like mimics, fell under this category.

4. High-class mutant. This category refers to named monsters with individual and unique personalities and names. The most important characteristic of these monsters, however, was that they had the ability to use an essence. In short, these monsters were much tougher and more challenging.
What would happen if an ogre, known for its thick skin, possessed the healing factor of a troll? A crazy monster would be born.
That was why...
I was running with all my might.
“What the hell is that? Why is there a vampire here?”
“You better run instead of whining, dwarf.”
As we were fleeing the entrance to the boss room...
Pant, pant.
“I can’t run anymore...” Lady Raven was out of breath.
“Pardon me, then, Lady Raven,” the porter picked her up.
Running down the path we had used to get here, then going past the water pipe...
“We won’t be able to leave this place if we don’t defeat him anyway. Wouldn’t it be better to fight?”
“We have to at least get to a place where there’s sunlight.”
“All we have for sunlight is a blood-red sky!”
“That’s still better than being down here.”
Even as we entered the labyrinthine underground prison...
“Turn left here!”
...we continued to sprint.
This place was nothing less than his home turf. We had to get outside no matter what. That way, we might have a chance of survival.
“A h-high class mutant as a guardian... this is unprecedented.”
Well, that wasn’t actually true.

A higher-rank mutant species served as the guardian of the third floor’s White Temple Rift as well. Plus, from the eighth floor—which was classified as a deep floor—on, it was safe to say that all Rifts were like this.

Well, it wouldn’t be inaccurate to say that there was no precedent for this on the first floor, though. Even I, a nine-year veteran of this game with an accumulated ten thousand playthroughs, had never encountered the Vampire Duke. I had only learned about his existence from a recording posted by a player on the game’s only community forum.
“Oh, right! Mr. Bjorn, how did you figure it out so fast? You told us to shut the door!”
Does that damn thirst for knowledge of hers have to be active even in a situation like this?
“Again, run instead of talking.”
“But I’m not running, am I?”
Well, you’re not. But I am.
“...I just had a feeling.”

Before she could pester me any further, I made up an excuse and cut the conversation short. But if I were to give a proper answer... It was thanks to the color of the doorknob that I had been able to pick up on the fact that something was off. In the recording that the user uploaded, that had been the only difference from the usual Bloody Citadel. When the vampire refused to appear even after I had attempted the Rift hundreds of times under the same conditions as the user, I wondered if there was a special condition I was missing, so I examined the recorded video and just barely managed to spot it.
If I hadn’t been so worried about the lucky streak I was having, would I have noticed it before the door opened?
Well, I didn’t think that was something to think about right now.
“I see that my guests are very rude.”
The moment we reached the second floor of the underground prison, the monster appeared.
Shhh—!
It was chasing us in the form of a black mist. This was not an active or passive ability vampires had, but one of the dozens of black magic spells that he possessed, [Vengeful Spirit State.]
This was why I hated monsters that used magic. The advantage it gave them was crazy good.
“Raven!”
I immediately called out to the wizard on our side. I wanted to ask if she knew how to use sun magic, a natural enemy of vampires. But it turned out that was unnecessary.
“Everyone, close your eyes!”
The wizard lady had already finished casting a spell.
“Ahessenbert tu!”
[Light Explosion.]
It was a support spell normally used to blind opponents within a wide area of effect. Even with my eyes closed, I could clearly sense the sudden and intense flash of light.
Beeep—
When I opened my eyes, ignoring the ringing in my ears, I saw that the black smoke chasing after us had disappeared.
Thank god.
The spell had prevented the vampire from using its core combo Original Body State after the Vengeful Spirit State.

It is safe to say that we had won ourselves at least three minutes. He must have woken up in that worship room just a little while ago. But, the laws of the universe stated that with success always came bad news.
“Bjorn! The wizard has been hit!”
“What?”
At Ainar’s words, I saw that Raven was unconscious in the porter’s arms. It looked as if she had suffered an internal injury, and blood was dripping from her mouth.
...What? Did that bastard use some sort of spell?
He shouldn’t have been able to use attack magic in the Vengeful Spirit State.
Maybe it’s the power of whatever essence he has?
That could be it. In the clip I had seen, the player had been wiped out before they could do anything, so it had been impossible to see what kind of monster essence the Vampire Duke had.
Various possibilities ran through my mind, but I decided to think about it later.
“What are you doing? Run!”
“The wizard is the one who knows the way, but she has fainted!”
“Don’t worry. I know the way.”
I glanced at the doubtful dwarf. “I memorized it,” I said shortly.
“After being here once...?”
In truth, I’d been here hundreds of times.
I had wanted to find the Vampire Duke, so I had gone in and out of this place more times than I could count. I hadn’t expected to see his face here rather than through a monitor, though.
“Follow me.”
I accepted no further questions and took the lead.
When the wizard wakes up later, is she going to think I’m strange for a barbarian? But what’s the problem if she does, anyway?
The most important thing right now was getting out of here alive.
“You really did memorize the way...” the dwarf exclaimed once we reached the first floor of the basement after running nonstop. “You two, is it true that your coming-of-age ceremony was last month?”
“Of course! I told you! Bjorn is a great warrior!”
“A great warrior... he really might be one day.”
There was a saying in Korea that a compliment could make even a whale dance, but I wasn’t a whale. Please...
I wished he would use that energy to run harder rather than speak. I had been leading us for just about two minutes now.
Sprint.
Left, right, straight, straight, right, left, straight, straight.
With a mental map in my head and my legs continuously moving, the exit finally came into view. Had it been three minutes?
I checked behind us one last time before heading up the stairs.
Huff, huff...
Everyone was breathing hard, but there were no stragglers because they all had good stamina. The problem was that I could see a cloud of dark smoke following behind us.
Shhh—!
Maybe we should’ve abandoned all of our bags. Then we could have maintained a slightly wider distance.
However, I knew there was no point in having regrets right now. It wouldn’t change anything.
Let’s focus on what we can do now.
Sprint.
I sped up even more.
But could he be using Original Body State?
Rattle.
I could hear the sound of something reassembling behind me. From now on, I had nothing to lose. I jumped up two to three steps at a time with a last-minute burst of speed, and...
“We’re out!”
...finally got aboveground without a single fatality.
“Honestly, I was worried, but... it really... didn’t follow us...” the dwarf muttered, out of breath.

However, still not fully relaxed, his gaze was fixed on the stairs that led to the basement. Anyone with a brain would know that we’d only bought ourselves a little more time and that none of our problems had actually been solved yet.
“...How long do you think we have?” he asked.
In response to the dwarf’s question, I shrugged my shoulders as I glanced at the mountain ridge beyond the castle wall. I didn’t know the exact time, but...
“Definitely not long.”
It was obvious that time was not on our side. Soon, that dark red sky would turn completely black. So, we needed to get ready before that happened.
“What exactly is the wizard’s current state?”
“She’s taken a potion, so she’ll wake up soon.”
“Are you sure?”
“...She surely will.”
That’s just what you’re hoping, you bastard.
Did this guy have no idea what had happened to her either?
“This time, you have to pull your fair share of the weight as well,” I told the porter firmly.
No “buts.”
“Do you want all of us to die here?”
Sometimes the most direct statement was the most effective. If we all died, he wouldn’t be able to protect the wizard on his own anyway.
“...What can I do?”
In truth, not much. I had just wanted to set that straight before the battle began.
“Guard the wizard. Even if you have to put your life on the line.”
“...Of course.”
His tone changed to one that was quite trustworthy.
Well, that bastard was taken care of, so there was only one more thing to do to prepare.
“Let’s move to the outer wall. It would be better for us to have some cover.”

I used a flimsy excuse to lead the party to the outer wall. In reality, the best thing would have been for me to leave all of my stuff here and take a quick trip on my own, but... If he popped out in the meantime, it was game over.
“Wait here for a moment. I’m going to take a look around and come back.”
“It’s not a good idea for us to split up!”
The dwarf shouted something, but I pretended not to hear it and ran to the fountain I had noticed earlier. I had to get the item I had left behind.
Bang! Shhh.
The fountain was full of dry pebbles. After cracking the statue in the middle, I looked through the ruins and pulled out a small box.
[The character has obtained the Tears of a Goddess item.]
When I checked inside, the contents of the box matched the game. And more good news followed.
“Where am I...”
When I got back after hiding the item in the groove of my boots, Raven had come back to her senses.
“Vampire! What happened to the vampire?”
“We managed to escape for now. But it’s going to show up again once the sun goes down.”
“I see.”
She grimaced, apparently still in pain. This time it was my turn to ask questions.
“What happened to you?”

Raven took a sip of the potion the porter gave her like it was water and answered in a half-dead voice. “Ugh, I’m not sure, but... ah... based on the symptoms, ugh... it is very likely to be Pain Sharing.”
Pain Sharing? If that was true, then I was relieved.

The monster that had this skill, the nightplar, had the lowest basic stats of all rank eight monsters. If the essence the vampire had consumed had been sixth rank—no, even seventh rank—the difficulty of this encounter would have risen even more.
“Ugh... there was a rebound just as I was about to cast a spell...”
Raven grabbed her chest with a pained look on her face. The sight made me feel quite bad for her. It seemed it would take some time for her to be able to do her part again.
“How long will it take for you to recover?”
“Ugh, a complete recovery will be tough. My circuits are completely fried.”
“A rough estimate is fine, so tell me in numbers.”
“Twenty minutes? Then I’ll be healed enough for up to five rank-seven attack spells.”
Only five Flame Baptism spells. That was really bad.
“Do you know any other solar spells?”
“Do you know it is very rude to ask a wizard about the spells they possess?”
Of course, I knew that was the case in the universe of the game. But right now, I was a barbarian who came from a culture of being coarse to everyone except the king.
Raven sighed when I responded with a look of “So what?”
“I can use a Sunspot Sphere.”
“A Sunspot Sphere...”
At its core, it was similar to a fireball, but a Sunspot Sphere was a rank six attack spell that used solar properties instead of fire.
This might work.
“Would it be possible for you to use the Attribute Strengthening spell on top of the Sunspot Sphere?”
“...If I can gather mana for another ten minutes.”
“Okay. Until then, we’ll hold him back somehow. So, don’t go out of your way to help and save your magic.”
“Yes, I will... Wait, but why are you acting as the leader, Mr. Yandel?”
Typical wizard. She was sharp. The dwarf had just followed along as I took the lead.
“Is there anyone else who can?”
Raven glanced at the porter, Ainar, and the dwarf in turn and then shook her head, apparently convinced.
“That’s definitely... fair.”
“Haha! I’m sorry! Can’t help being born a dwarf!”
The dwarf scratched the back of his thick neck in apparent embarrassment. Ainar, who had been waiting for the right time to chime in, saw this and joined in on the conversation.
“Are you admitting that barbarians are better than dwarfs?”
“I am not! However, as you have said, this fellow here is special. I felt it myself, even if it was for a short moment.”
“Special...?”
“I may look like this, but I have keen eyes when it comes to reading people.”
Raven was obviously curious about what had happened while she was unconscious, but unfortunately, she couldn’t waste her precious time on that.
“Murad, how many essences do you have?”
“Four.”
“What kind?”

I kept my questions as short and concise as possible to get a grasp of the dwarf’s abilities. Among the essences he had, there were no wild cards that could completely turn the game around. Still, I was able to piece together a strategy in my mind. If there was one issue, though, it was that I didn’t have enough time to share said strategy with my teammates.
Shhh—!
A cool wind blew, and the shadows covering the ground grew thicker. The remaining time for preparation was thirty minutes.
[It has become nighttime.]
Now there was nowhere for us to retreat to. The only option was to survive no matter what it took.

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Warrior (2)
paragraphs: “Bjorn.”
The moment Ainar called my name, the sun, which was obscured by red clouds, completely disappeared under the horizon. And at that exact moment, a pale-skinned man appeared under the red moonlight.
“Strange, very strange...”
He glanced around the ruins of the town and then fixed his gaze on us.
“Looking at you all, I can’t suppress my thirst for blood. Would you happen to know the reason for that?”
The reason? Well... How should I know?
And I didn’t want to know either.
“If you give me some time to think about it, I might remember,” I said slowly.
I wanted to buy at least another minute. However, at that moment, the vampire’s eyes lit up.
“My thirst is too unbearable for that. Hehehe.”
To be honest, this was a little ridiculous. I didn’t realize vampires could be such assholes.
“Kekeke! Hahaha!”
The vampire, who suddenly started to cackle like he was possessed, stopped just as suddenly. And then...
“Kyaaah!”
He let out a roar that sounded like it was from some kind of otherworldly creature.
Sring!
His nails, a vampire’s main weapon, extended with a sharp sound. After that, all that remained in his eyes was a madness that cast a reddish glow.
It’s just like in the game.
Now that I was thinking about it, this was the same as in the game. No matter how intelligent the monsters were, they only ever exchanged a few words of conversation as a prelude to the fight.
“I’m used to fear like this,” said the dwarf.
“Everyone back up!”

The murderous intent emitted by this rank-five monster was enough to make my body numb, but surprisingly, the dwarf was completely fine. I was actually a little amazed. He had looked pathetic in front of the corpse golem, but I guess he was still a third-year adventurer.
At the same time the vampire’s physical form disappeared, the dwarf stepped forward and raised his buckler.
Bang, bang, bang!
A cloud of dust stormed past us, carried on a gust of wind. The power behind the blow was obvious even from a few steps back, but...
“Hahaha. How powerful!”
The dwarf hadn’t been pushed back a bit. It wasn’t that his stats had overpowered the vampire—it was all thanks to the help of an essence.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Balance Weight.]

That was the skill of a rank-seven monster called Iron Tusk. It was a Knockback Immunity skill that prevented the character from falling over or being pushed back as long as their feet were touching the ground. Additional variations included Shock Absorption.
“Tarzine, you stand back!”
As the battle began, I called out orders. However, I heard nothing in response.
When I glanced to the side, I saw that the porter was already far away with the wizard in his arms. That was a good call, but also kind of infuriating.
I decided to revisit that feeling later and shouted, “Ainar!”
“I’ll take the right side!”

Thanks to the countless battles we had fought together, she could understand what I wanted to say with a single look. I nodded my head briefly at the vampire’s left side, then rushed forward at the same time as Ainar.
“Kyaaah!”
The vampire retreated. It was clear his ability to strategize was still intact. At the same time, the dwarf’s half-crumpled buckler was restored to its original state like time had been reversed.
The buckler couldn’t have come with that feature...
[Hikurod Murad has cast Emergency Restoration.]

This was the ability of a monster called Living Armor. It was a useful skill that not only saved on equipment costs, but also greatly increased the performance of equipment when the user was equipped with a magic item.
The dwarf finished his repairs in an instant and shouted, “I’ll take the front, so you guys support me from the side!”

There were no objections there. The only reason we were able to hold on this long was because of the dwarf. To be honest, I was the least helpful person here. Even Ainar had an essence now. I had nothing other than the expensive Immortality Imprint.
Well, I guess I could technically be a human shield.
“Kyaaah!”
At that moment, the vampire, who had been watching us from a distance, split his body into hundreds of crows. The flock of crows flapped their wings and flew toward us at a high speed.
“Get as far away as you can!”
Soon, the crows flying toward us dove head-first into the ground and exploded.
Bang, bang, bang! Bam! Bang!
There wasn’t much explosive power behind each blast. However, we also had to avoid the blood splattering all over the place.
God damn it.
It wasn’t like the corpse golem’s acidic blood, of course, but...
Considering the combo that followed, this was more of a headache.
“B-Bjorn! What the hell is this!”
A red tattoo etched itself into our blood-drenched foreheads, and a bright light shone.
[You have been designated as a sacrifice.]
[Vampire Duke Cambormere’s physical stats have temporarily increased according to the number of sacrifices within a hundred-yard radius.]

Ignoring the game log that popped into my head, I clenched my teeth. The vampire’s form slowly regenerated from the pool of blood left on the floor by the exploding crows. Now that he had a buff, it was going to be even harder to deal with him.
Has it been three minutes yet?
There was still a long way to go before our preparations came to fruition. Would we be able to survive until then?
I shook my head. There was no point wondering whether or not it was possible.
“Behelahhh!”
We just have to hold on for a little while longer... with the grit of a barbarian.
[Buff skill: Offering Imprint.]
[Eternal Life: the user’s ability to regenerate increases significantly in proportion to lost stamina.]
[Master of Blood: the ability to absorb some of the target’s stats by directly sucking their blood.]
Each of these three active skills vampires possessed made them ridiculously powerful in hand-to-hand combat. The problem was, though, that those weren’t the only things this vampire had.
Even ignoring these three skills, this greedy son of a bitch was able to use various types of black magic.
“Bjorn, more crows!”

Morphing into crows that exploded, transforming into smoke to dodge a sword, using spilled blood to summon monsters, and more. This vampire bastard demonstrated a cunning that characterized high-rank monsters.
This is why no one who reaches the sixth floor just quits the game.

Once again realizing just how crazy difficult Dungeon and Stone was, I raised my shield. The shield had already been torn up by the vampire’s nails, and it was pretty much just scrap metal at this point, but...
Better than nothing.
Clang—!
I used the recoil to bounce back and absorb the shock as much as possible.
Strength, speed, and skill. Plus a bonus skill that I had naturally picked up by fighting an enemy who overwhelmed me in every way.
At that moment, Raven’s voice echoed through my head.
“Please hold on for another five minutes!”
I wondered if that time would have been a bit shorter if she had just saved the mana she was using to send that message...
But after hearing that hopeful news, I was feeling more energized—
“Hikurod has been hit!”
—yeah, right.

After demonstrating the skills of a third-year adventurer, the dwarf who had been closely marking the vampire had fallen. Thankfully, Ainar, who had been nearby, rushed in and prevented the vampire from sucking his blood.
[Hikurod Murad’s status has changed to “Incapable of Combat.”]

In an instant, the tide had turned. Ainar and I were already in tatters. It was almost impossible for the two of us to stop him without the dwarf who had been taking on more than fifty percent of the burden in this fight.
So instead...
I quickly made a call.
“Ainar! Take Murad and get back!”
“I’ll stop him!”
“A-All right!”
The moment Ainar put Murad on his shoulders, I dashed forward and swung my mace.
Smack!
This was my first real hit in a while.
“Ahhh!”
As the attack successfully landed, a sharp throb went through my skull from the recoil. It was all because this crazy bastard was a high-rank mutant.
[Vampire Duke Cambormere has cast Pain Sharing.]
He was even able to fully recover from his injuries by taking just one step back to catch his breath.
Damn it—meanwhile, I’m still in pain. What kind of a dickhead is this guy?
“Kyaaah!”
Still, the aggro was focused on me, just as I had wanted. Out of habit, I double-checked that the item hidden in my boots was still there.

The name of the item was Tears of a Goddess. Simply put, it was a holy object. Although it was only a one-time use item, it could be used for healing purposes and could also be used to attack evil monsters.
...Should I use this now?

It wouldn’t be a waste to use it. No matter how unique the item’s effects were, it was a special item that could only be used in Bloody Citadel anyway. If I used it on the dwarf, his strength would be restored immediately, and if used on the vampire, it would inflict considerable damage. But...
No.
I ceased my pointless worrying.
What was the reason I’d been diligently biding my time up until now? Because one blow was more than enough. Anything more than that would go badly for us.
We’d only get one opportunity. And when it came, we’d have to pour everything we had into it.
There was only one way for the five of us to take down a rank-five monster.
Click.
I took a potion bottle from my waist and opened the stopper. I poured the potion into my mouth, my eyes still on the vampire charging toward me, and—
Chhhhhh!

The countless wounds I had accumulated during the battle began to heal and the pain rushed in like a tidal wave. I felt the strength leave my hands, and all I wanted to do was collapse to the ground. After all, it was nearly impossible to drink a potion and continue to fight, but...
It doesn’t matter.
I wasn’t trying to fight.
Stab!
Soon, the vampire’s claws were embedded in my abdomen. The metal armor on my chest was rendered useless as his nails dug deep into my flesh.
My nerves were going haywire as they sent danger signals to my brain. My mind went blank, my senses utterly overloaded.
Shit, if I had known this was going to happen, I would have just taken the corpse golem’s essence for myself.
Leaving behind my belated regrets, I poured another potion into my mouth.
Chhhhhh!
The wound healed quickly from the layered healing effects of both the [Immortality Imprint] and the potions.
“Kyaaak—”
I stared right at the startled vampire bastard who looked like he did not understand what was currently happening.
To be honest, I felt like passing out from the pain.
“Behelah, you son of a bitch...”
Pain cannot kill me. The fact that I’m still alive is proof of that.
“What the hell is he doing...!”

Raven, who was watching the battle from behind some rubble in the distance, couldn’t hide her shock. She had read about the extraordinary strategies and hunting methods of many adventurers in her books, but this was unlike anything she’d seen.
Is he planning to hold the vampire back with just potions?
“T-There’s no way he’s going to succeed. H-He’ll die!”

It just didn’t make logical sense. She knew because she had consumed potions several times before. The pain was unimaginable, and the severity of the pain increased depending on the severity of the injury.
But that barbarian?
Chhhhhh!
There weren’t just bubbles boiling and steaming on his body—smoke was completely smothering it. Even she had never seen anything like this before.

Suffering an injury wasn’t the main issue right now—it was that dying from shock in situations like this was not at all rare. In fact, cases of people dying from potion consumption were rather common.
“Huh?”

Raven stopped restlessly jumping from foot to foot, her eyes going wide. The pain that that barbarian would be feeling right now was beyond her imagination, and one thing was for sure: in his current state, he shouldn’t be able to even move.
But what was this?
Clang—!

Even as he collapsed to the floor with his shield which was now little more than a lump of scrap metal, the barbarian blocked the vampire’s nails as they swung toward him. And, as if to prove it wasn’t a coincidence—
Clang—!
He did it several times, over and over.
Of course, he didn’t successfully block every attack. As she watched, his whole body was being punctured by those merciless claws. But...
Clang!
Attacks that targeted the most vulnerable parts of his body like the head or heart were blocked by timely thrusts of his shield.
Is this logically possible...?

She couldn’t tell whether he was purposefully pushing through the pain to avoid the attacks using superhuman willpower, or whether it was just the last of his fighting instincts that were making this possible. However, a document she had read a long time ago suddenly came to mind. In it, the writer had said that barbarians’ true value lay in their psychological strength, not their superior physical prowess.
Somehow, I think I get it now...

At that moment, Tarzine, who had been watching the battle with her, suddenly spoke up. “Lady Raven, it would be better to retreat while we can,” he said firmly. He spoke of retreating, but in reality, he intended to abandon these people and run away. “I am not certain I will be able to protect you at this rate. It is too dangerous here.”
She was too dumbfounded to speak.
You think I don’t know that?

If she could, she would have left already. Although she was often told that she was a wizard with a soft heart, Raven was not naive enough to risk her life for the sake of the adventurers she had just met. But...
“Are you crazy? Retreat? To where?”
There was nowhere to run. There was only one way to get out of the Rift, and that was to defeat the Guardian and exit through the portal.
...That man must be fighting so desperately because he knows that too.
It felt like a spark zipped through her brain.

Even a barbarian who had just undergone his coming-of-age ceremony was keeping a cool head, making smart calls, and doing the best he could under the current circumstances... Meanwhile, what was she, a wizard, doing right now?
“If Bjorn dies, it’s all over. We have to keep him alive somehow.”

A wizard was not someone who just cast powerful spells from the back of the battlefield. It was also a wizard’s duty to coolly analyze the situation using their knowledge of various fields and suggest the most efficient route for the party.
Raven reevaluated the current situation. The third-year dwarf warrior was incapable of combat. The female barbarian was feeding him potions and helping him recover.
No problems there...
But the wizard was hiding in the back and waiting for her mana to be restored with a human swordsman guarding her. Now that she thought about it, that was a waste of resources.
“Tarzine, go to Mr. Murad.”
“Pardon?”
“I’m fine. At least go over there so that the female barbarian can join the battle.”
“...Understood.”
“Leave your backpack here.”
Tarzine followed her somewhat high-strung commands without voicing a complaint. Without even watching him leave, Raven dug her hand into her subspace backpack.
The essence of the corpse golem.
As soon as she pictured it in her head, the test tube appeared in her hand.
I don’t really... no, I really, really don’t want to have to use this, but... this is nothing compared to a person’s life.
Raven slowly pooled her mana and started drawing a magic circle.
Whooom!
Accuracy support. Range support. Auto-lock onto the target.
If she added a few more things to the formula, she wouldn’t even have to move her arms herself...
But I have to save at least a little bit of my magic.
After completing the circle, she threw the test tube in her hand as hard as she could. And...
Shatter!
The test tube, which flew in a smooth arc, hit its target and shattered, emitting a light.
[The Essence of the Corpse Golem is being absorbed into your soul.]
[Pain Resistance has increased by +70.]
[Strength has increased by +15.]
[Bone Strength...]
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 2
Physique: 80 (New +34)
Spirit: 46 (New +10)
Special Ability: 30 (New +26)
Item Level: 202
General Combat Power: 203.5 (New +70)
Acquired Essence: Corpse Golem - Rank 7 (New)]

chapters.title: Chapter 35: Warrior (3)
paragraphs: My mind was blank and my vision was blurry.
Was I in pain? Obviously.
It felt like my whole body had been stabbed and was now being pickled in salt water. All I wanted in that moment was to give up, but...
Shut up.
I forced myself to set aside those weak thoughts. When standing at a crossroads, you had to choose: what were you willing to give up and what would you protect in return?
Stab!

Something sharp pierced my thigh. That was okay, though. That wasn’t an area that would pose an immediate threat to my life. However, the vampire was getting enraged at the fact that his prey was refusing to die, no matter how many times he ripped into it.
“Kyaaah!”
The vampire bastard’s movements became more vicious. But what I needed to do was clear.
Lifting the shield that had been cut, torn in half, and reduced in size, I managed to at least protect my most vulnerable parts.
Crack!
The shield’s face, which could not withstand the attack of a rank-five monster, was finally torn off, leaving only the handle. Without even thinking, I raised my arms to protect my head.
At that moment...
Clang!
Something other than a claw collided with my head and shattered, sharp shards pouring down my back.
[The Essence of the Corpse Golem is seeping into your soul.]
The pain quickly subsided.
[Pain Resistance has increased by +70.]
A newfound vigor filled a body that had previously reached its limit.
[Strength has increased by +15.]

My eyes, which had just been foggy, started to clear up. The first thing I saw was the vampire’s sharp claws swinging down onto the arms I had wrapped around my head. As soon as I saw this, my subconscious conjured up an image of my arms being sliced off. But what actually happened was completely different.
Slice!
The claws easily pierced the soft flesh. However, that was all they were able to do.
Khak!
The claws were stopped by bone and did not go in any further. It was at that point that I realized what this mysterious new power of mine was.
[Bone Strength has increased by +55.]
[Poison Resistance has increased by +12.]
[Perception has decreased by -5.]
[Appetite has increased by +9.]
[Weight has increased by +21.]
[Your blood is now acidic due to the passive skill Acid Fluid...]
A sense of relief and disappointment flooded me at the same time.
Did she feed me the Essence of the Corpse Golem?

Because of this, my strategy for leveling up would have to be heavily revised. However, as I looked at the present from a short-sighted perspective for the first time... Things were looking up. I now had an increased chance of surviving.
Jump!
I rolled backward and jumped up from the ground.
Was it a side effect of Pain Resistance? Now that the pain problem had been resolved to some extent, nothing prevented me from moving.
But what about the Essence of the Guardian? Since I absorbed the Essence of the Corpse Golem, is that up for grabs?
The thoughts that had suddenly crossed my mind were tossed aside. That was something I could think about later.
“Kyaaah!”

Perhaps the sudden liveliness of his prey was intriguing to him because the vampire flung himself at me enthusiastically. I moved to avoid it, but what followed was not much different from what had been happening earlier.

It was of course impossible to overpower a rank five monster with just one rank seven essence. The only difference was that the meat shield that was initially getting beaten up on the ground was now able to stand up and move.
That’s probably all that’s changed.
But despite the self-deprecating assessment, I smirked.
Stab! Slice! Khak!

Nails cut through flesh, tearing up my intestines. The potion I had previously consumed had already been digested, so my healing speed was hindered. But it didn’t matter. The wizard, who had been passively watching the fight this entire time, must have realized that her life was in danger as well because she started tossing her entire fortune at me.
Clang!
A glass bottle was flung and shattered, pouring its contents onto my body.
[Your body is rapidly regenerating due to Recovery (Greater)‘s effects.]
Was this perhaps a high-class potion? It was obvious that this was a higher quality than the potion I got from the blonde.
Chhhzz!
My wounds began to heal faster than they had previously. In response, I decided to throw myself at the vampire more enthusiastically.
So what if my flesh is slashed and my muscles are torn? It’ll all heal in a few seconds anyway.
“Kyaaah!”
“AHHH!”

I screamed as I was pushed back by the vampire, and proceeded to engage in super close combat. I had no other choice. My hammer was all the way over there, and my shield had been turned into a pile of scrap metal.
“Kya-kyak?!”
Perhaps he hadn’t run into an adventurer who used foundational skills yet, because he was extremely startled when I jumped onto his back like a cicada and strangled his neck.
Or maybe he was just in pain?
“Kyaaah!”
Smoke began to rise where our flesh came into contact.
Chhhhhh!
It was impossible to tell for sure whether the smoke was from my acidic blood touching his skin or if it was the usual smoke that came from healing myself with a potion. But it didn’t matter.
It’s probably both.
Even in a tense combat situation like this, another potion flew in and broke with a shattering sound.
[Your body is rapidly regenerating due to Recovery (Greater)‘s effects.]

There was no doubt potions and acids were two different things. At the exact moment the potion broke, the choking vampire screamed louder and easily threw me off of him. I could clearly feel the overwhelming difference in our strength. But...
“Shit, this bastard’s no big deal.”
I was beginning to see a way out. In this current state, a barbarian’s Immortality Mode, I could survive a few minutes against this bastard. I was sure of it.
“Bjorn! I will help you!”
Ainar even rejoined the battle.
“What about Murad?”
“The porter is looking after him!”

The addition of Ainar worked out heavily in my favor. I could take on the role of the main tank by consuming potions, and whenever things got a little too dangerous, Ainar could swing her sword to give me time to catch my breath.
This battle had become a little bit easier.
“Kyaaah!”
“Ainar! Watch out! The crows are going to fly in soon!”
The moment Ainar took a big step back at my cry, the vampire’s body turned into hundreds of crows that flew toward us. However, the flock did not reach us, as we were one step ahead.
“Bjorn, you are amazing! How did you know that was coming?”
Because that guy always squints one eye before using that skill. Rather than a characteristic of all vampires, it seemed more like a habit that only applied to this guy.
I could really see an end to this fight now.
“How shameful of me! Everyone held up very well! Hahaha!”
Soon, the dwarf, who had healed his wounds with a potion, joined the fight again. He even brought the porter with him.
“From now on, I will help as well.”
“We will help you from the wings!”
I naturally continued to play my role of the main tank. Not to say that the others were being cowardly. They seemed to genuinely believe this was the best strategy.
The dwarven warrior with three years under his belt addressed the barbarian with two months under his.
“Bjorn, the great warrior and son of Yandel! You are more than capable! Hahaha!”
He seemed to think that was a compliment, but...
That just means I’ll have to work like a dog until this is over.
I’d never been able to freeload in my life. That was nothing new at this point.
“Behelahhh!”
As the four of us were dealing with the vampire in a formation with me at its center, the moment I had been desperately waiting for finally came. A foreign thought entered my mind.
“It’s ready.”

If that meant that she had finished recovering enough mana to cast [Sunspot Sphere] and even [Attribute Strengthening]... That meant that everything was finally in place. In other words, it was time to end this long-ass fight and get out of here.
“I can use the spell at any time.”
The moment I heard her confirmation, I loudly shouted, “Murad! Now! Use Lightning Release!”
The order was given without any previous discussion, let alone strategy. However, the dwarf immediately carried out my instructions without a word.
Zzz, zzz!
A yellow light shimmered on the dwarf’s hammer, and sparks began to shoot out.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Lightning.]

This was the ability of a rank seven monster, Illatrek. It allowed a strong current to flow through a part of the body. The dwarf readied his hammer, keeping it low like he was preparing for an upward thrust.
“Everyone, best stay back for a bit! Hahaha!”
After delivering a brief warning, the dwarf swung his hammer through the air with all his might.
Too far away from the target, you say? Little details like that didn’t matter.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Release.]
Release was one of the rare Transformation abilities in Dungeon and Stone. It allowed the user to fire the energy acquired through other abilities out of the body.
Whooom-!
