A ball of lightning shot out of the hammer like a cannonball and...
Exploded. Literally.
Bang, bang, bang!
Compared to the sound it made, the force of the explosion was weak. There were no craters made on the floor, vampire limbs torn off, or anything like that. However...
[Vampire Duke Cambormere has fallen into an Unconscious state.]
The key component of this combo wasn’t its power to begin with. In an instant, the dwarf had dazed the rank five monster and turned around to give a signal...
In a very analog way.
“Raven—!”
Fortunately, the signal got its point across well, and a powerful light immediately condensed on a rooftop two hundred yards away. I hurriedly took out the item I had hidden in my boots.
It was a small jewel the size of a fingernail, [Tears of a Goddess.] Despite all the crises we’d faced, I had waited and waited to use it at this exact moment.
Sprint.
With the item in hand, I ran.
And, after shoving it into the vampire’s mouth...
Smack!
I cracked him with an uppercut as hard as I could to close it.
Crunch!
There was the sound of something breaking, and before long, a pure white brilliance erupted from his mouth.
[The Tears of a Goddess have been destroyed.]
[Grace has descended over the ruins.]
[All of Vampire Duke Cambormere’s resistances are temporarily suppressed by Grace and he takes a critical hit.]
Blood gushed out from the vampire’s lips like a fountain. He looked fine on the outside, but his insides seemed to be wrecked. It was shocking.
So, a single item was not enough, huh.
[Due to the strong shock, the Vampire Duke Cambormere is paralyzed.]
No longer unconscious, the vampire’s fingers started to twitch.
Still not yet? It can’t wait any longer...
The moment that thought popped into my mind I began to turn my head...
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-six attack spell Sunspot Sphere.]
A dazzling, shimmery sphere flew through the darkness and right past my nose. Regret sank in a moment later.
Booom!
Fuck, I should’ve bounced earlier.
[You have been caught up in the explosion of the Sunspot Sphere and have fallen into an Unconscious state.]
[Vampire Duke Cambormere has cast Pain Sharing.]
[Hikurod Murad has fallen into an unconscious state.]
[Ainar Fenelin has fallen into an unconscious...]
Beeep!
A ringing sound echoed in my ears that was not unlike the sound a radio TV broadcast made after the national anthem. And through the tinnitus, I could hear a conversation.
A conversation not unlike a comedy skit on TV.
“How can a butcher sell cooked meat?”
“No! This is raw meat!”
“How is cooked meat raw meat?”
Still listening to their conversation, I opened my eyes.
“It’s alive?”
A dark sky appeared. I could smell the scent of cooked meat through my nose.
Was the smell coming from my body?
When I opened my mouth, there was a scratching sound from my parched throat. My ears were apparently fine too. I decided to focus on the positives as much as possible.
“Krrggh! Agh!”
Sunspot Sphere: an attack spell with solar properties combined with fire and holy attributes. It was weaker than its equivalent, [Fire Ball.]
That was the lucky thing for me. If it wasn’t a weaker spell, I might have really met my maker.
But why is it so quiet...?
Caught up in the blast of the [Sunspot Sphere,] I had temporarily fainted. That much was clear, but I lacked enough information to understand my current situation.
Why haven’t I been healed yet, and why can’t I hear anything around me?
I gripped the ground with hands that were slick with blood from my wounds and stood up. Then, I forced my eyes to focus and looked ahead.
The first thing I saw was the vampire bastard.
“Fuck.”
Why was he still alive?
Of course, he was in rough shape too. Both of his arms were torn off, and bones were visible through his damaged upper chest. He didn’t even seem to be conscious.
But...
[Vampire Duke Cambormere’s ability to regenerate has been significantly increased by the Eternal Life effect.]

Even at this moment, his wounds were healing. Considering that his healing factor was proportional to the amount of HP he lost, it wouldn’t take too long for his chest to heal and his torn-off arms to grow back.
“Fucking... hell...”
I looked around and saw several unconscious bodies. The dwarf, Ainar, the porter bastard... I had a feeling the wizard, who I saw on the roof in the distance earlier, was in a similar state...
I was confounded. What kind of crazy situation was this? Why had everyone fainted after we finally cornered the bastard?
What the hell happened while I was out?
It seemed like it hadn’t even been that long.
All kinds of questions filled my mind, but...
I decided to shove them all aside and instead took a step forward with my motionless foot.
Trudge.
I still couldn’t accept the current situation. But one thing was very clear. I needed to decide what to do now.
Trudge.

Vampire Duke Cambormere... I needed to get rid of him before he came to his senses. There were no other options. No matter how rich a wizard was, the number of potions they had was not infinite. In fact, it would no longer be possible to use the same strategy of sustaining my body with potions.
Trudge.
So I staggered forward.
A pain that had managed to penetrate even my [Pain Resistance] ability? Ignoring it, I extended my steak-scented legs in front of me.
Trudge.
The pain was a signal to live. I thought so, at least. It wasn’t like there hadn’t been a time when I’d thought the exact opposite, but for now, it was. So I kept walking.
As I got closer, I noticed that even the vampire bastard smelled of grilled meat. I relaxed my knees and fell right on top of him.
“You...fucking...bastard...”
The scar on his chest, which was deep enough to show bone, had already fleshed up quite a bit while I was walking over. I couldn’t help cursing him out.
Smack!
So I slammed my fist into his chest.
A vampire’s weakness was their heart. Even if their brain was destroyed, these bastards could be revived as long as their hearts were intact.
Ah, so that’s why the asshole’s arms were torn off. Did he block the [Sunspot Sphere] with his arms?
I could picture the events in my mind, but as usual, I let the thought fade—
Smack!
—and slammed my fists down again.
I felt the absence of my equipment more keenly than ever. But hey, when you didn’t have teeth, you had to chew with your gums.
Smack!
I didn’t even know where my mace was, and my shield had long since been rendered useless and dumped somewhere. Of course, Ainar’s greatsword and the dwarf’s battle hammer were on the floor...
The thought of picking them up didn’t even occur to me, though.
I wouldn’t have even had the strength to pick either of them up anyway. As I was slamming my fists down, the seams of my crumpled, perforated half-armor tore and it dropped to the floor.
My 360,000 stones...

I took a glance at the half armor, which had been corroded by my newly acidic blood, and noted that it seemed like repairing it would be tough. Although the thing that really fucked with my head was something else entirely.
“Damn it all.”
It was like pouring water into a sieve. No matter how much I punched the vampire, nothing changed.
Why the hell were his ribs so durable? I had assumed that if I kept beating him, his ribs would break and eventually pierce his heart.
Okay, change of plans.
I always liked to have a plan B because my plan As had rarely ever been successful. Thanks to my horrible luck, things always ended up getting fucked up in the end.
But I’ve never done this before... is this how it works?
Erwen said it was important to visualize it clearly.
[Flesh Burst.]
Boom!
The hand I placed on the man’s chest exploded.
Well, that works.
Although the explosion itself was not very powerful, the acid mixed in with the flesh and blood had put a slight dent in the vampire’s chest. Even that healed up fast, though...
Well, I wasn’t expecting this to be a one-hit kill anyway.
I cast Flesh Burst consecutively.
Boom! Boom! Boom!

By about the tenth explosion, my left hand was in complete tatters. But because of my increased bone strength, my bones remained intact even as my skin dissolved, making me look like some kind of skeleton.
Anyway, I couldn’t use my left hand anymore.
Then it’s the right hand’s turn.
Even though I knew this was insane, I placed my right hand on the vampire’s chest, continued to chant the spell in my head, and kept blowing him up.
Flesh Burst, Flesh Burst, Flesh Burst...
All the while, I ignored the pain racing toward, hitting, and exceeding my limits as much as I could. I felt like I was going to die, but I wasn’t doing all this just to keel over afterward.
I was going to survive. No matter what.
Boom!
And after eight more uses of the spell, I wobbled. I just need a few more...
[Warning: Your health has dropped below 1%. If you do not receive treatment soon, you will die.]

I sensed it instinctively. I had reached a point where I could no longer push through this pain on sheer willpower alone. I had to stop now. Otherwise, while I might be able to kill the vampire in the process, I would die too.
Even as I had that moment of insight, however, my logical side reasoned:
Well, if I’m going to die anyway...
I couldn’t stop. But it definitely wasn’t for my teammates’ sake.
Boom!
I might have looked like a lunatic to anyone watching... But at that moment, I was sure. If I had even the slightest chance of survival, this was it.
Boom!
The moment I exploded my flesh again...
[Warning: your health has reached 0%.]
...I felt something change.
It felt like something was escaping from my body, but also felt strangely...light? Soon enough, I realized what was happening.
[The countdown has begun.]
Oh, that’s it.
The thing I called the “flashing light at the end of the tunnel.”
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (43/46)]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (40/46)]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (37/46)]
Even though I felt like the reaper was looming right over my shoulder, I exploded my flesh again.
Boom!
The dent in the vampire’s chest grew in size. But were these my barbarian battle instincts at work? It felt like the road ahead was clearer than ever.
One.
Just one more time. I only needed to do it one more time.
So...
[Flesh Burst.]
Instead of my right arm, which now had almost no flesh left on it, I let my chest drop on top of the vampire and cast another explosion. And at that moment...
[Vampire Duke Cambormere has been slain. EXP +5]
The vampire bastard’s body turned into particles of light.
So, you can die.
[Higher-class mutant bonus. EXP +1]
[Guardian kill bonus. EXP +3]
My heart swelled. Not emotionally, but literally. Having experienced this sensation before, I immediately realized what was happening.
[You have leveled up.]
[Soul Power has increased by +10.]
[The maximum number of essences you can absorb has increased by +1.]
I had leveled up, but I couldn’t be particularly happy about it. That was because the time had come...
Dungeon and Stone was not a game that replenished your blood when you leveled up.
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (16/46)]
How many seconds did I have left until I died? I couldn’t be sure, but I would say I had at best about five seconds.
...Do I leave this up to fate?
No matter how I looked at it, I couldn’t help but hate the situation I was in. However, I chose not to have regrets.
In-game, there’s about a 33 percent chance that a Rift guardian will spit out an essence.
Thirty-three percent.
Too low of a probability to bet your life on it. However, it was undoubtedly a non-zero chance.
I have no reason not to try.
I grinned, shaking off all my regrets. I had fought back. Until the end of the end.
Now all that was left to do was wait for the outcome.
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (13/46)]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (10/46)]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per...]
One second, two seconds, three seconds. As time ticked by, my eyes slowly slid shut.
Have I failed?
I hadn’t failed because of any mistake I had made. I was just out of luck.
Maybe this is the kind of ending I was always meant to have.
I closed my eyes, leaving things up to fate. Hoping that, when I next awoke, I would once again be Lee Hansu, the 29-year-old office worker.
“Ha.”
Well, I knew for a fact that wasn’t going to happen.
[Vampire Essence - Guardian has been absorbed into your soul.]
[Natural Regeneration has increased by +45.]
[Strength has increased by +15.]
[Agility has increased by +15.]
[Magic Resistance has increased by +30.]
[Thanks to the passive skill Source of Darkness, you will not die unless your heart is destroyed.]
[Your healing factor has significantly increased thanks to the Eternal Life ability.]
[Your HP is now above 1%.]
[The countdown has ended.]
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Survive after a countdown.]

Level: 3 (New +1)
Physique: 155 (New +75)
Spirit: 90 (New +44)

chapters.title: Chapter 36: Guild (1)
paragraphs: “Hey! Mr. Yandel! Wake up!”
While Raven was shaking Bjorn’s shoulder, the other members of their party woke up one by one.
“Miss Raven? What happened...?”
“Bjorn! Is Bjorn dead?!”
“Lady Raven! I’m glad you’re all right—”
Questions flew at her from all directions, and Raven was the only one who could provide them with answers... because she hadn’t passed out.
“The vampire is dead. Mr. Yandel is alive. Tarzine, I’m fine, so can you stop yelling in my ear?”
“Amazing! Your magic killed a vampire in a single blow!”

Murad’s exclamation made her purse her lips. She felt enraged for some reason. It hadn’t been [Sunspot Sphere] that had killed the vampire. In terms of contribution, their victory wouldn’t have been possible without her efforts, but...
“...It wasn’t me, it was Mr. Yandel.”
“What do you mean?”
“It was Mr. Yandel who killed the vampire.”
Murad’s eyebrows furrowed.
“This fellow here?”
Although he had praised him as “special” and a “great warrior” earlier, he couldn’t believe Bjorn had killed a rank-five monster. And Raven understood how he felt.
If I was the one hearing about it secondhand... I would think the same thing.

Maybe it was thanks to how far away from the battle she had been, but she’d been unaffected by [Pain Sharing,] and had served as the sole witness, watching these incredible events unfold. Yes, literally. Just watching. What else could a wizard who had run out of mana have done?
“Everyone, thank Mr. Yandel. Without him, none of you would have been able to open your eyes again.”
“W-Well, yes... But can you tell us a little bit more about what happened?”
She was wondering how to explain it when Ainar interrupted.
“Then what happened to Bjorn?! Shouldn’t we give him a potion?”
In other words: If you have a potion, pull it out.
Raven shook her head. “A potion would be... pointless,” she replied. “It seems like his body has mostly already healed.”
If she were to hazard a guess, this man wouldn’t have much of a need for potions from now on. Most of his injuries would heal relatively quickly.
“Then why hasn’t he woken up yet!”
“I’m not sure either. However...”
“What do you know?! What is it? Wizard! Speak!”
Raven took a deep breath before answering. “It’s probably... exhaustion.”
“...Exhaustion? Didn’t you just say that his body is healed?”
Ainar placed a hand caked in dirt and dry blood on Raven’s shoulder. She looked like the world itself was ending.
“What, are you two actually lovers?” Raven asked.
“Ah, ah, no! Why did you jump to a conclusion like that all of a sudden!” Ainar snapped.
“Huh. Anyway, I don’t know for sure either. I am not a priestess. I only know of a few similar cases.”
“Cases? Miss Raven, is this common?”
“It’s not common, but... occasionally, it happens. The body has healed, but the mind has not recovered enough to wake up.”
Warriors who had undergone extreme trauma or who had really poured everything into a battle sometimes fell into this state.
After hearing this explanation, Ainar raised her voice. “I’ve never heard of anything like that! Besides, it doesn’t even make sense! Too mentally exhausted to wake up? Bjorn isn’t that weak!”
Not that weak, huh...

On that point, Raven was in complete agreement. A few hours ago, she would have snorted inwardly at that comment, but now she couldn’t. She alone had watched as he fought that vampire to the bitter end. But...
That was why she was sure her theory was correct.
“To be honest, I am almost certain. The reason Mr. Yandel is not waking up is because he is mentally exhausted.”
Too exhausted to wake up? This had nothing to do with being weak or strong. It was just the logical consequence of what he had endured.
This woman wouldn’t have said what she did if she had seen the fight for herself.
She may have just witnessed something incredibly rare today.
“Wizard! So, when will Bjorn wake up?”
“I am not sure. It may take at least a day or two at the latest.”
“Then he’ll be up in a few hours! Since Bjorn is a great warrior!”
...So why did you ask me?

Raven was getting annoyed again, but for some reason, she didn’t feel compelled to argue with her. More precisely, she didn’t have the energy for that. In fact, the barbarian’s words didn’t sound as arrogant as they used to.
“A Great Warrior...”
Since ancient times, less than ten barbarians had officially received that title from the king.
Well, it seems barbarians these days use it more as a regular compliment.
She organized her thoughts again before continuing. The [Essence of a Corpse Golem] and the [Essence of a Vampire]—and the [Essence of a Guardian,] at that. The barbarian had absorbed both.

He had completed his coming-of-age ceremony just last month, and hadn’t he said that this was his second time entering the labyrinth? As she looked at the dead-to-the-world barbarian, she opened her mouth.
“...Truly, that may one day be the case.”
Of course, in order for that to happen, he would have to survive dozens of more trials like this one.
Did I survive...?
When I woke up, it was late at night. For some reason, I was lying on Ainar’s lap, and as soon as our eyes met, she shouted, rendering me wide awake.
“Bjorn!”
“...Where are the others?”
“Everyone is gone! Bjorn, are you okay? I was worried! You were passed out for three whole days!”
It’s been three days? So, does that make today the seventh day?
That sobered me up, and I sat up right away. Then I took stock of my current state. No visible external injuries. Health-wise, besides being hungry, I was generally all right.
“By the way, Ainar, what are these pants I’m wearing?”
“Pants” was a generous description. A cloth that could have been used as a handkerchief was wrapped around my lower body, covering only the important parts.
To be more accurate, it was closer to a skirt than pants... and a very small one at that.
“Oh! The wizard gave me some extra cloth.”
“...A-And you put it on me?”
“Of course!”
A bit of shame crept in, but it was a little lessened because Ainar didn’t seem at all bothered. True, it would be weird for a warrior to be awkward about stuff like this.
“There is no reason to be embarrassed. Bjorn, you truly are a great warrior!”
Well, that doesn’t mean you can sexually harass me.
“...So, what happened after that?”
I changed the topic to wipe the humiliation from my mind. I was wondering what had happened after I blacked out... Especially to the loot.
“The Numbers Item? Murad took it, and the Rift Stones were taken by the wizard.”
“What?”
It was one shock after another.
The fact that I was alive right now meant that I’d absorbed the vampire’s essence... Did that mean that the vampire had dropped all three drop items?
What kind of special event was this?

“Oh, right! We didn’t roll any dice when distributing the Rift Stones. The wizard argued that she had to take it all to make up for her losses, so...” Ainar continued to try to justify what had happened to me. “Murad said he didn’t mind, but I said no! But then the wizard said something strange.”
“Strange?”
“She said that you took the greatest reward of all, so you can’t complain about her taking the Rift Stones.”
Sounds like the wizard is the only one who realized that I absorbed the vampire’s essence.

I nodded silently. I had no complaints about this loot distribution. Whatever the reason was, the wizard had fed me the Essence of the Corpse Golem. In addition, considering the cost of the potion she had poured on me, she had basically only incurred losses while in the Rift. Being greedy about the Rift Stones at this point would only make me an asshole.
Ainar seemed to think a little differently though.

“W-Well, I told her to wait until you wake up and then we could decide, but I couldn’t stop her! They waited for more than half a day, but you still didn’t wake up so they all went through the portal and left!”
“You don’t have to blame yourself. You couldn’t have done anything.”
I could only imagine the expressions on the faces of the people who had been held captive for half a day by Ainar’s arm-twisting. The best thing to do here was just thank her.
“Thank you. I’m glad you were on my side.”
“...I-I just did what made sense! We’re comrades!”
I checked my belongings, which Ainar seemed to have gathered. A backpack, a mace, a few pieces of scrap metal that might have previously been my shield...
Still, if I sell it, the price of the iron may add up.
Once I put everything I could see in my backpack, I took out food and a canteen and filled my hungry stomach. Then I glanced at the time.
Less than an hour left before the portal closes.
“Bjorn! When you’re done eating, how about we leave? There isn’t much time left now!”
I firmly refused. “We can’t.”

In truth, I desperately wanted to leave this nauseating place right now, but... After everything I went through, I should at least take everything I could with me. I also wanted to check out the boss room.
The wizard took the Necronomicon, so there is only one thing left.
It looked like I was going to have to move quickly.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
[The labyrinth is now closed.]
[You are being transported to Rafdonia.]
As I felt sunlight on my skin for the first time in a while, I exhaled.
Just barely made it...

Time had been tighter than I expected. It had taken less than ten minutes to find the item that was hidden in the ceiling of the outer wall’s watchtower after climbing up the ladder... But reaching the boss room had been a race against time.
...And it was all in vain.
Ainar said the others had waited for me for half a day, but maybe the wizard had actually just wanted to use that time to conduct her research.
Well, it would be weird for someone with her personality to just sit around doing nothing.
The boss room had walls that were caved in here and there. A torn picture frame. There was even a box in a shape I had never seen before left open and abandoned.
I’m sure there was an additional bit of loot there, but she must’ve grabbed it for herself.

We had run over at full speed, and the room already showed signs of a thorough investigation. However, rather than feeling angry about being dine-and-dashed, I was more curious about what the item had been. And rightfully so, because this was an unusual Rift that had never been cleared before. An element that even I, someone who had been playing this game for nine years, didn’t know about?
My curiosity as a gamer was piqued.
It’s not like she would have let me have it if I’d asked... I’ll just have to ask about it the next time I see her.

Anyway, I searched everywhere to see if there was anything the wizard had missed, and soon time got tight. In fact, the portal closed as soon as we came out of the Rift, so we had been cutting it closer than close. We had almost been trapped in the boss room without a boss monster, forever.
“Serum, fourth son of Kenick! You have more scars! I envy you!”
“This is nothing, Karak, third son of Fanun!”

As I was getting my thoughts in order, I heard the scattered voices of barbarians in the crowd. Fortunately, they hadn’t noticed me yet. I bowed my head to stay out of sight and headed to the currency exchange for rank nine adventurers. Fortunately, I had arrived early so the line wasn’t long. There were no barbarians to bother me either.
When I handed them my mana stones, the worker exchanged them for money just like last time.
“That’s 231,520 stones.”
230,000 stones.
It was an amount that seemed infinitely small compared to the hardships I’d suffered.
That’s not all of it, though.
I had absorbed two essences during this adventure. Plus, the profits I would receive once I sold off the items in my possession would be several times higher than the profits from the mana stones.
For whatever reason, mana stones always become an adventurer’s supplementary, not primary, source of income.
I didn’t know if I should be happy or sad about that.
With a bitter smile, I was about to pick up my pouch when—
“That amount is too high for a rank nine adventurer.”
The official took back the pouch they had put down and gave me a strange look.
“What’s in the backpack on your back?”
What do I have in my backpack? It wasn’t like I couldn’t answer the question, but...
“...Why are you asking?”
I felt a chill go down my spine.
I looked around and saw guards rapidly approaching me in the distance. It seemed that the worker had pressed some sort of emergency call button that had been hidden under the desk.
“Is this the man?”
“Yes.”
I raised my hands to express my intent to cooperate with the authorities, but the guards exchanged a few words with the officials and forcibly grabbed my arms.
Shit, had I come back from the dead just for this to happen?
“Barbarian, let’s have a chat somewhere private.”
Instinctively, I knew I was fucked.

chapters.title: Chapter 37: Guild (2)
paragraphs: I was sitting on a chair. Strangely, the iron restraints on the arms and legs seemed like an added feature, and they were secured to the ground with nails.
Can’t I catch a break?
To summarize the situation, I was currently in an interrogation room located in the basement of the Adventurers’ Guild.
Across from me was my interrogator. He was somewhere in his mid-thirties, and his defining trait was that he was a highly obese man who had a high-and-mighty way of speaking.
“I am Koldo Biermann, and I am in charge of the investigation of this case. I am going to ask you some questions now, so I hope you cooperate with my inquiry.”

“Investigation? Shouldn’t you tell me why I’ve been arrested first?” I asked, not backing down. I didn’t even bother hoping for an ‘innocent until proven guilty’ approach to be used here, but this was a reasonable right for a defendant to have even in this era—
Smack!
The investigator cunt kicked me in the shin. When I looked up at him, he smirked as if to ask what was wrong.
“Rule number one, you only talk when you are answering my questions. Got it?”
“...Fine.”
“Follow the rules, and you won’t get hurt. You can be assured of that.”
Hurt, my ass.
After what I had gone through in the labyrinth, getting kicked in the shin was like getting tickled. This bastard must have some delusions about his job.
“Anyway, to answer your question... Bjorn Yandel, you have been arrested on the charge of plundering inside the labyrinth.”
“...Plundering charges?”
What kind of dumb nonsense is this?
The investigator picked my backpack up upside down and spilled the contents on the floor. He whistled sarcastically.
“That’s a lot of stuff.”

Adventuring supplies such as torches and a sleeping bag and one of the special items I obtained in the Bloody Citadel could be seen in the pile. Sorting through the food and other miscellaneous items, the investigator took out the pieces of equipment and placed them on the table. It was mostly stuff from the party of four that had stabbed us in the back in the Land of the Dead.
“If you didn’t loot anyone, where did these come from? A barbarian wouldn’t use a bow.”
“That... belonged to a group who tried to kill me first.”
“And your evidence?”
Evidence? I had no such thing, but I had no reason to be cowed by that.
“Then do you have any proof that what I’m saying isn’t true?” I fired back.
“Well, I’ll have to investigate that going forward.”
“You’re going to arrest and investigate someone for this one thing?”
That was the part I really didn’t understand.

This was different from the Adventurers’ Guild’s usual process. There was an unwritten rule in the city to not question adventurers without evidence, no matter what they brought out of the labyrinth. For that reason, the guild never took the initiative to search for looters themselves until reports or testimonies came in.
However...
“The guild’s internal rules changed a few days ago.”
Well, that left me at a loss for words. I was once again reminded that this wasn’t just a game, but a world in which many people lived.
“The official guidelines have instructed us to first enforce the rules on rank nine explorers to deter acts of plundering.”

In a nutshell, it meant that the small fry were going to be the test rats. Didn’t matter where you went, being the lowest rung on the ladder meant you were going to suffer. I could roughly guess how they picked who they were going to target with these investigations as well. Either someone who had collected a lot of mana stones or someone with equipment that appeared to belong to someone else in their backpack. Something like that.
So I already had two strikes against me.
“Well then, tell me. Where did you get this thing?”

Anyway, his initial attitude must’ve just been to kill my spirit, because after that, the bastard carried on a normal investigation. So I explained what happened during my time in the labyrinth as cooperatively as possible. While leaving out the psychopathic bitch, of course.

To tell him about that, I would also have to tell him about the oath, and a barbarian who broke an oath was going to look weird. It was far more dangerous to be charged as an evil spirit than to be charged with murder. Especially because I’d have no chance to explain myself.
Plus, reporting that woman could get me assassinated in the middle of the night.
Therefore, I just briefly recounted meeting a group of four looters, being restrained, and then miraculously killing them. However, the investigator fucker was blasé about it all.
“What? You survived being stabbed in the neck? You tell lies that even a child wouldn’t believe.”
“I only speak the truth.”
“Then where is the scar on your neck? If your words are true, it should have left a mark, right?”
I subconsciously touched my neck. It was smooth with no defects. And there was a clear reason for that.
By consuming the vampire’s essence, my healing factor had increased so much that even the scar on my neck had healed.
...Why are things getting so complicated?
Reluctantly, I explained about the Rift as well. The only problem was that the asshole investigator didn’t listen to a word I said.
“Hahaha! A Rift? A vampire? There’s no logic to your barbaric words!”
“I swear, everything I say is true.”
Perhaps he had hardened himself against me even more because the oath of a warrior, which usually always worked for me, proved useless this time.
“What honor is there to a looter?”
At this point, I was pissed too.
“Then call a wizard! You can verify my words with magic!”
In fact, there was never any need for such a long conversation in the first place. Just one spell would reveal the truth. However, Detective Asshole just smiled like I wasn’t worth the effort.
“Only adventurers who are rank seven or higher can make a formal verification request to the guild.”
Damn, and when had this changed? Rank nine adventurers weren’t even being treated like human beings.
“Even if I pay the fee?”
“That’s money that will be turned over to the state when you die. We can’t let you waste it on something useless.”
Bull. I knew it was only because they’d have less money to steal from me.
“Now, just admit to the crime.”
It seemed that it would take some time to prove my innocence.

As if in celebration of the end of her fifteen-day stint in the labyrinth, the dazzling noon sunlight wrapped around her body like a cloak. Erwen stood there for a moment to enjoy the warmth. Snippets of memories filled her head, perhaps because of the stark contrast between her surroundings and the environment she was just in.
I didn’t know the third floor would be so hard...

Erwen had gone up to the third floor with her sister. There, she had experienced the strength of rank seven monsters for the first time. Even though her sister had pretty much fought them on her own, even the rank six monsters they had met by chance at the end... Truly, it had been the first expedition she’d been on that felt like a real adventure. Her trip to the labyrinth with Mr. Barbarian hadn’t been bad either... But at the time, she had been so focused on getting out alive that she hadn’t been paying attention to anything else.
He’s going to be so surprised when I tell him about this.
She wanted to find him right away so she could tell him about what she had experienced in the labyrinth and ask him about his experience too. Just thinking about it reinvigorated her tired body.
If I tell him that I obtained a new essence, will it be like last time...?
The thought was a bit troubling... But for some reason, her steps were lighter than usual as she quickly headed over to the currency exchange for rank nine adventurers.
Maybe we missed each other this time. I don’t see him over here...
“That’s 184,100 stones.”
“Woah...”
“That’s quite a lot of money for a rank nine adventurer.”
“Because I went with my sister!”
“What is her name?”
“Daria Whitember di Tersia.”
“All right, that checks out. You may go.”
After exchanging her mana stones, meeting her sister outside, unpacking at the inn, bathing for three hours, and changing into new clothes, she headed straight to Bjorn’s inn.
But how did things end up like this?
“You’re that elf girl who comes by every day. But, uh-oh. Room 302 hasn’t come back yet.”
“Oh, really?”
Bjorn was not at the inn. What could have happened? His room had already been paid in advance, and there was other luggage left in it as well...
“Are you going to keep waiting?”
“Yes! I’m sure he’ll be back soon!”
“Tut.”
The owner of the inn, who was usually kind, had clicked his tongue in a show of displeasure. How long had it been since then?
The sun had gone down by now. And a few hours ago, at that.
“Excuse me, why are you taking Mr. Barbarian’s things out of his room?”
“Hey, move it. Wait, Miss, do you have any papers?”
“P-Papers?”
“You know. A certificate stating that you are acquainted with that barbarian, or that he has agreed to hand over his keepsakes to you, or something like that.”
“I don’t, but—wait! What do you mean by ‘hand over his keepsakes?’”
“The labyrinth has been closed for a long while but he hasn’t returned. Why else would he not be here? He clearly died in the labyrinth!”
Finally, the innkeeper kicked her out semi-forcibly. Erwen squatted down in front of the inn.
Dead? That’s not possible...
That was nonsense. No matter how common it was for adventurers to die in the labyrinth, it was impossible for her to imagine him dying.
So she sat there and waited until morning came, then night, and then morning again.
“I’ve been looking for you.”
Her sister came looking for her. She didn’t scold her about not coming home for two days, nor did she ask any other questions. She just held out her hand.
“...Let’s go get some food.”
Erwen took her hand and stood up. Then, she had a thought.
She didn’t know the exact reason, and she knew it had nothing to do with this, but...
“I want to be strong.”
For some reason, that was what she was thinking at that moment. More intensely than ever.

I was trapped in a thick iron cage. All of my stuff had been taken away, and I was wearing just one scrap of cloth rolled up and tied below my waist. I was currently standing slumped against the wall for the second day in a row.
Fuck my life...

After the first day, the situation had just gone from bad to worse. In response to my repeated denial and requests for magical verification, the investigator had had no choice but to summon a wizard, but...
[Your Spirit stat is higher than 90.]
[You have a resistance to spirit magic due to your increased magical resistance.]
The magic of the rank-nine wizard working at the guild did not work on me.
“His mental barriers are too thick. It appears we need to call a wizard from the Magic Tower.”
The situation was turning into even more of a headache. Even from the guild’s point of view, the help of a high-rank wizard would inevitably be needed to close my case.
“It doesn’t make sense to call someone here for a case about a rank-nine adventurer.”

Ever since then, the investigator had thrown all kinds of bullshit my way to get a confession out of me. He probably thought this was the easy route. But there was no way I was going to make a false confession just because this bastard was trying to intimidate me.
I even name-dropped the rank-six wizard, Arua Raven, and the dwarf, but the frustrating asshole hadn’t even listened.
The case was starting to drag on when—
“Hahaha! Bjorn Yandel, apparently this isn’t the first time you’ve committed an act of plundering.”
A totally new charge was pressed against me, unrelated to anything in the previous investigation.
“What are you talking about?”
“We discovered this while investigating your case.”
“This” was none other than a familiar message stone that the investigator was holding up with a triumphant look in his eyes.
“Message stones have a unique serial number, so each owner is on file. So I looked up the number of the stone in your backpack, and lo’ and behold, it belongs to a dead adventurer.”
By the way, the owner’s name was apparently Artoa Serdin.

“Since they were registered under a union, I made some inquiries, and they told me about everything you did. It wasn’t enough to just run away after injuring Harts Young—you also killed the person that was pursuing you, right?”
This asshole seemed to think he was the main character of a crime novel, so his explanations were unnecessarily long.
I cut him off and got to the point. “So what is going to happen to me?”
No matter what I said here, this dickhead was desperate to wrap up my case and wouldn’t bother listening.
“Since we now have context, testimony, and evidence, the guild has decided to reject your request for verification and execute a sentence.”
The guild? Yeah, right.
He had probably just turned down my request himself.
“...So how long will I get?”
“What strange words you speak. Rafdonia’s law has never been tolerant of plunderers. Oh, is that too difficult for a barbarian to understand?”
The bastard had smiled and continued.
“That means you’re getting the death penalty.”

And that was what had transpired last night. Then, this morning, the jailer came by to tell me the date of my execution and asked if there was anything I wanted to eat. It was at that moment that I finally realized the mess I was in.
If I didn’t do anything, I was really going to bite the dust. So, I needed to do something.
Unfortunately, the time to resolve the issue with words had already passed. But if I broke out of the cell and left, I’d just become a plunderer who’d broken out of jail.
I may be able to escape to the city, but I will quickly become a wanted criminal.
I thought about it for a while, but in the end, there was only one way for me to survive this. I had to prove my innocence somehow.
It wouldn’t be easy, of course. You could in fact judge a forest by its trees. If a mere investigator was this uncommunicative, how could I expect the rest of the guild to be different?
Whether I’m guilty or not, the Adventurers’ Guild will decide that it is easier and quieter for me to just disappear.
With that thought in mind, I made a plan, and something of a path forward began to appear in front of me.
First of all, the key was to create a situation where the Adventurers’ Guild could not silence me. And in terms of a method for doing that, I had an idea.
Of course, I would have to go through a lot of trouble in return...
Crunch!
I pictured the look on the investigator’s face in order to further motivate myself. From a young age, I had been a precocious child who knew how to take revenge with my words.
No matter how I look at the situation, just saving my ass won’t cut it.
I was going to make them pay for this...
[You have cast Flesh Burst.]
The full price!

chapters.title: Chapter 38: Guild (3)
paragraphs: Flesh Burst was one of the few deranged skills that used a character’s life force as fuel.
The pain managed to overpower Pain Resilience before adrenaline was released into my body... But the toll my suffering took couldn’t be easily ignored.
Chhhhhh!
The iron bars half melted thanks to the blood splattered in the explosion. The bars bent easily when I applied some sideways force.
Aside from the pain, both of my hands healed quickly, not just because of the [Immortality Imprint,] but also thanks to the vampire essence I recently obtained.
As soon as I got out into the hallway, I spotted a guard.
“What? What?! What are you doing?!”
It was the same guard who had come by to ask what I would want for my last meal. It seemed he heard something explode and ran straight here.
“Eek! J-Jailbreak! The prisoner has escaped!”
Before he could make any more noise, I quickly sprinted forward and slammed a fist into his stomach.
Smack!
The guard dropped like a fly.

When I promptly searched his clothes and took out the keys, the other prisoners who had been watching the situation with interest from inside their cells went crazy. They realized what I was trying to do.
“Hey! Barbarian! Are you really going for it?”
“Kekeke! You’re crazier than I thought!”
“Me too! Take me too!”
Considering that this place was under the Adventurers’ Guild, most of these people were likely looters. But...
Necessity knows no law.
A poor barbarian who had been unfairly framed for a crime didn’t care about something like that.
They’re going to end up dead soon anyway.
The only good plunderers were dead plunderers. This belief, which had been solidified in my mind within a few days of waking up in this world, would probably remain there for the rest of my life.
“Hahaha! Freedom! I’m free!”
“Let’s get out!”
I released all the prisoners on my floor. These weren’t the kind of bastards that I’d be able to control, but that didn’t matter. That hadn’t been my intention in the first place.
“Woahhh!”
After that, I really didn’t have to do much.

Madness was contagious. The prisoners joined forces, headed upstairs, subdued the guards, and released more prisoners with the keys they obtained. Of course, there were quite a few who refused to participate in the escape even though their doors were unlocked. Percentage-wise, the amount was about 50 percent.
Either their investigations are still ongoing, or they’re really innocent like me.
As I was quickly advancing through the chaos, I noticed a group of prisoners gathered at a specific door. It was the interrogation room I’d gone in and out of countless times these past two days.
It was immediately obvious what was happening.
“G-Go back to your cells!! I-If you go back now, we’ll pretend this didn’t happen—”
Some guards were trembling behind the locked door and the prisoners were trying to rip the door open.
“We need their key to go upstairs!”
“Tear it off!”
However, the odds of that thick iron door just falling off were low, no matter how hard they shook it.
Damn it, do I have to do that shit again?
That was what I was thinking when—
“Do you think you’re going to get out of this alive? You’ll all receive death sentences! Execution!”
A familiar voice came from behind the door. Looking through the small grate, I saw a familiar asshole investigator sandwiched between the two guards.
I didn’t expect to see you this early.
“Get out of the way!”
With a happy heart, I pushed past the prisoners to get closer to the door. And then I exploded my left arm, which had only just recovered, again and again.
Flesh Burst, Flesh Burst, Flesh Burst.
After five repetitions, the handle melted and the locking mechanism was destroyed. The product of my flesh, blood, and pain.
The prisoners burst into mad cheers.
“Ahhh!”
“Barbarian! Barbarian! Barbarian!”
“He is a free barbarian!”
Afterward, the investigator’s eyes widened as I entered the interrogation room.
“Y-You! H-How in the world...?!”

To be fair, no one would have been able to see this coming. Most of the Special Abilities possessed by ninth-rank adventurers were trivial. That was the reason why, aside from the iron bars, I hadn’t been restrained any further. How could he have known that I had such an ability?
All I could say to him was this:
“Blame the horrible childhood that forced you to grow up with such a lack of imagination.”
“I-I grew up in a decent family!”
“It was so bad that you have to lie?”
“W-What!”
Cough!

I clocked the investigator with all the anger I’d been suppressing these past few days, and he promptly dropped to the floor wriggling like a worm. Thanks to the thick layer of fat absorbing the shock, he was still conscious.
“Y-You crazy bastard...!”
This uneducated swine slurred all kinds of curses at me despite being unable to properly breathe.
“You’re dead! How dare you use a Special Ability inside the prison and cause this chaos! Do you think you can handle the fallout?!”
Handle it?
“That sounds like something you should be wondering right now. If my plan succeeds, you’re fucked.”
“W-What can scum like you do to me?!”
I smirked.
“What can I do?”
Wrong question.
“You should be asking what I can’t do.”
I was a son of a bitch who was willing to do just about anything when my life was at stake. Which was too bad for this poor, unimaginative bastard—
“For now, go to sleep.”
When you wake up, either you’ll be in hell, or I will.
Smack!
This time I threw a fist at his face instead of his plump body, and the bastard passed out with foam in his mouth. It was then that the prison officer shouted something at me.
“Key,” I said.
“D-Do you know what you’ve just done!”
I did. But, what about it? I would have ended up dead if I had just stayed put.
I said just one word.
“Key.”
“Hey, it’s not too late—”
“Key.”
“H-Here...”
When I took the key and turned around, the prisoners cleared the way just like in the movies.
Trudge, trudge.
Passing by them and standing in front of the stairs that would take us aboveground, I took a deep breath. Was it really okay to go this far?
Worries suddenly filled my mind, but...
These assholes are the ones who didn’t give me a choice.
I turned the key and shouted, “Let’s go!”
Everything that happened from now on was self-defense—to protect my life, which was more precious to me than anything else.

This branch of the Adventurers’ Guild’s prison system was deep underground. The double doors connecting it aboveground were also so thick that the people on the ground floor of the guild were unable to tell something was wrong until it was already too late to stop it.
How fortunate for me.
Rattle!

Climbing up the long stairs and opening the door, I saw the interior of a peaceful building that sharply contrasted with the dungeon. Administrative staff and adventurers were swarmed in front of a counter.
An employee noticed me showing up inside the building, which couldn’t be accessed by ordinary adventurers, and asked, “Uh, how did you get in here?”
Of course, no response was necessary. The employee then spotted the open door behind me and realized what was going on in an instant.
“P-Prison break!”
As soon as they shouted this, the eyes of everyone inside the building turned to me. A heavy silence descended in an instant.
However, even among these adventurers who led spontaneous lives, there was a bastard who was particularly impulsive.
“Miss! If I catch that thing, will you have coffee with me after work?”
A man standing next to a female employee jumped over the counter in an instant and ran toward me. And at that exact moment—
“Ahh!”
“That’s the smell of freedom!”
Prisoners started pouring out from the stairway.
“Huh... hu-huh!?”
“S-Stop them!”
“Adventurers, please lend us your strength! The guild will offer a reward!”
“Aaah!”
The prisoners charged forward without fear and the adventurers took out their weapons to fight back.
“Kill them!”
Blood abruptly began to spill in the peaceful branch building. As the one who had spearheaded this fiasco, I took a step back from the front lines and quickly headed for my destination.
I don’t have time.
The prisoners would buy me maybe five minutes, no more. Except for a few clubs stolen from the guards, they didn’t have any weapons.
I climbed the stairs to the second floor and looked out the window.
And getting outside will be impossible.
News of the commotion had already reached the streets and adventurers outside were also starting to take notice. If I went outside right now, I would just be beaten and taken downstairs again.
The solutions to my problems were above.
“You! Who are you?”
All the employees that I encountered in the hallway were knocked out cold by my fists. Then I glanced over the railing to take stock of the situation on the first floor.
The brawl now involved dozens of people. I reached a hand out over their heads.
And...
Flesh Burst.
As my hand exploded, acidic blood poured down on them all like a sprinkler.
“Aaaaaah!”
Dozens of people screamed in unison after coming into contact with my blood, whether they were adventurers, prisoners, or what have you.
That made me feel a little guilty, but... It had to be done to increase the odds that the next stage of my plan would succeed.
[You have activated Offering Imprint.]
When I activated the combo move, an engraving appeared on the foreheads of those covered in my blood, and a red light filled the area.
[Your physical abilities are temporarily increased by the number of sacrifices located within a 100-yard radius.]
The number of sacrifices was tens of people.
So this is why all those athletes take steroids.
Power rushed through my veins. The railing I had unintentionally been gripping onto was dented with a creaking sound. Even the anxiety I had been experiencing disappeared.
If this is how it’s going to be, I can definitely pull this off.
“Arghhh!
After leaving the commotion on the first floor behind, I climbed the stairs again and headed to the third floor.
Fortunately, it looks like he hasn’t left.

I peeked into the rooms on the third floor and found that they were completely different from the ones on the lower floors. The entire floor was made up of offices. The wooden furniture, decorations, and plaques on the wall gave off a rather old-fashioned vibe.
“What is this commotion? You, go downstairs and check it out!”
“Yes, Mr. Branch Manager, sir!”
So that’s the branch manager.

Having identified my target, I hid behind the door. And, the moment the man who had just gotten his orders from the branch manager opened the door and came out, I punched him in the chin with all my might.
Crack!
Whoops, I hadn’t meant to break a bone.
Thud.
As the assistant to the branch manager, I thought he would at least fight back, but the man dropped to the floor. At the same time, the branch manager jumped up.
“Y-You! Who are you?!”
Me?
“An innocent barbarian.”
To clarify a bit more, I was here to prove my innocence. But, like a typical barbarian, I was doing so in a physical way.
“So you’re the one who caused the commotion down there!”

Like a true branch manager, the man quickly assessed the situation and immediately took the sword decorating the wall down. As a former adventurer, his stance was perfect, unlike all the employees down below who were just bookworms.
It didn’t matter, though, since I had doped up in anticipation of this exact scenario.
“Miss, stand behind me.”
“Y-Yes!”
A moment later, the woman who had been sitting and facing the branch manager hid behind him, and both sides were ready to fight.
If I were playing the game, would this be considered a boss battle?
I took one last deep breath. For my plan to succeed, I had to subdue this man. If possible, it had to be before the commotion on the first floor ended.
“Behelahhh!”
Thanks to the dozens of people in Offering Imprint’s area of effect, the moment I jumped off the ground, it was with an explosive burst of speed that flung my body upward.
To be honest, even I couldn’t get used to the speed. But the branch manager wasn’t too shabby either.
“You fool!”
He accurately read my movements, mapped my exact trajectory, and buried his sword into my wrist. However, with me in super-barbarian mode, the swing was not enough to cut into my bone.
Khak!
There was a dull thunk as if something in my body had blocked the sword’s path. Then, the blood that sprayed from the wound soaked the branch manager’s shoulder.
Czzz!
“Ah! Arghhh!”
The branch manager was distracted by the unexpected pain. After that, it was too easy. Taking advantage of his moment of hesitation, I targeted his throat with my fist, and that was the end of that.
The branch manager groaned and dropped to his knees.

Despite my concerns, the boss battle had quickly come to an end. I guess they hadn’t ever expected something like this to happen. Apparently, it was a common trait of all Adventurers’ Guild employees to lack imagination.
But I did not.
I always imagined the worst-case scenario. Since I had no way of knowing what kind of essence this former adventurer might possess, I smacked him in the back of the head to knock him out.
And so, the first phase was complete.
“P-Please don’t kill me!”
What should I do about this woman, though? Judging by the way the branch manager had been groveling before her, she must be of very high status.
“T-That’s the district chief’s daughter! If you touch her, you will never get out—”
What the heck, how did he wake up so soon?
Smack!
I knocked him out again with more strength than before and calmly continued to think this through.
The daughter of the district chief...
It seemed that things were going to go much easier than I had expected.
...Or get way out of control.
“Sir! Are you all right!”

An employee came up to assess the situation on this floor after finally sorting out the mess on the first floor. Of course, that wasn’t a problem for me. The branch manager had already completed his career change to become my pet parrot.
“Say you’re fine.”
“...I’m fine. But what happened downstairs?”
“It’s all sorted out for now! A few escapees are hiding in the city, but they will be found soon.”
“That’s... good news.”
“Oh! But where is your secretary, Robert? I thought he’d be with you...”
The secretary? He was sleeping in a closet with a broken chin. Of course, the branch manager wasn’t allowed to give that question an honest answer.
“Make up an excuse.”
“...I sent him out to do some work. I have urgent work to do myself, so make sure no one comes up here unless I ask for them.”
“Yes sir!”
Soon after, the employee left and I immediately got out from under the desk. In my arms was the daughter of the district chief.
The branch manager’s mustache trembled as he glared at me.
“I’m sincerely warning you that it would be in your best interest to stop now.”
“I see.”
The branch manager’s advice went in one ear and out the other.
Best interest, my ass. If I quit here, what are the chances I’ll end up anything but dead?
“Think about it. I don’t know what you’re aiming for, but I can help—”
“I see,” I replied, picking my ear with my little finger.
“You crazy bastard!” the branch manager roared, apparently hitting his limit. “Do you have any idea what you’re doing?!”
I did.

To be honest, I’d already heard that question multiple times on my way here, and I was getting sick of hearing it. What did he want me to do? Either I did something crazy, or I died. It was a black-and-white situation.
I nodded my head once more. “I see.”
“What exactly do you see—” the branch manager started to shout, but...
“If you don’t shut up, I will kill this woman.”
When I pretended to tighten the arm I had wrapped around the district chief’s daughter’s neck, the branch manager shut his mouth.

Upon closer inspection, his face was white as a sheet. Well, I could understand why. In addition to the jailbreak at his branch, the daughter of the district chief had also been taken hostage. What a terribly troubling situation.
No matter how this fiasco ended, this bastard wouldn’t be getting out of it unscathed either.
You reap what you sow.
As I was thinking this, the woman I was holding hostage suddenly opened her mouth.
“My name is Julian Urbans. Not ‘this woman.’”
Her voice was calmer than the terrified tone she’d used before. I could also feel her heartbeat thanks to our close proximity, and it seemed quite stable.
“Tell me what you want,” she said. “There must be a reason for someone like you to pull a crazy stunt like this, right?”
“Someone like me?”
Had I ever met this woman before? When I cocked my head, she continued.
“You are not at all frightened by what you’ve done. Your breathing is even and your eyes are completely steady.”
“Your point?”
“You planned this all out, right? A long time ago.”
Plan? I had made one... About thirty minutes ago.
I thought she was about to say something worthwhile, but it was just a waste of time.
“Maybe you even knew I was going to be here today—”
“Quiet.”
She gasped.
After covering the apparently overly conceited woman’s mouth with my hand, I asked the branch manager for what I needed.

“Bring me the investigator who was in charge of my case, a guy named Harts Young of the Crystal Union party active on the first floor, a wizard from the Tower, and an official priest from the temple.”
All my preparations were complete. Now it was time to turn this situation around.

chapters.title: Chapter 39: Guild (4)
paragraphs: “Master, what do you mean? Go to the guild? So suddenly?”
“You mentioned you needed to visit the guild to look for someone anyway, didn’t you?”
“Yes, but...”
Arua Raven, a rank-six wizard associated with the Magic Tower, had a sour expression on her face as she trailed off. It was true that she had business at the guild, but...
She had planned on first taking some time to get a decent rest and then conducting preliminary research into the thing she had obtained on her expedition.
“The branch manager has put in an official request for aid. From what I hear, something big has happened at the guild. Wouldn’t getting some pocket money be worth it?”
“...All right. I will go,” Raven reluctantly agreed.
She really did need to drop by the guild soon anyway. And if she went now, she could get a monetary reward as well, so there was no reason to put it off.
I spent a lot of money in the labyrinth this time too...

Besides, it wouldn’t be bad to potentially run into that barbarian a little earlier than she had planned to. After all, they had experienced an unprecedented variant rift, and he was the one who had absorbed the guardian’s essence. He was just as interesting a specimen as the thing she had found.
“Then I will be back soon.”
“Oh, take Tarzine with you.”
“It’s fine. He’s pretty much useless anyways.”

Raven used the warp gate on the first floor of the Tower to teleport to the gate closest to the guild’s branch building. From there, it would take about ten minutes to reach her destination on foot. As soon as she stepped out onto the street, however, she frowned.
“Why are there so many people?”

It seemed to be significantly more crowded than usual. And the closer she got to her destination, the more people there were, making it hard to even walk forward. It seemed like something really big had happened.
He did say that the branch manager had officially requested aid.
Raven let out a deep breath. This was just a way to earn some pocket money, but for some reason, she had a feeling that she was going to have to work hard for it.
Raven grabbed the nearest, most approachable onlooker. “Excuse me, can I ask you something? What is going on here?”
The response she received from the man made her doubt her hearing.
“A large number of plunderers that were locked up in the branch’s dungeon have escaped.”

This was truly unheard of. Not only had a jailbreak occurred, but some of them had managed to escape into the city center too. One of the instigators was even said to have taken the daughter of the district chief, who had happened to stop by the branch, hostage.
“I guess whoever it is doesn’t have a brain. There is no way the guild will negotiate with them over that.”

In fact, whether they wanted to negotiate or not, the guild had no authority to do so in the first place. The Rafdonian royal family provided the guild with a lot of power over labyrinth-related matters, but they adhered to a strict code when it came to punishing plunderers.
If that person had just run away like the other prisoners instead, they might have had a slight chance of surviving.
“But you see, the situation has gotten interesting.”
“What do you mean?”
“The person responsible for the hostage situation is claiming that he was framed.”
“Framed?”
“That’s right. All he’s asking is that the guild bring in the parties involved and use magic to reveal the truth fair and square in front of everyone.”
He wasn’t asking to be exonerated—the culprit was simply demanding that the truth be verified. Because of this, suspicion was spreading among the gathered crowd that he was telling the truth.
What kind of crazy bastard would do something like this?

Of course, if the story she had heard was true, the first person at fault was the investigator who had mishandled the case. But to instigate a large-scale dungeon break and, in the process, take the daughter of the district chief hostage? That definitely wasn’t something a sane person would ever do.
“Anyway, that’s why everyone is waiting here. The branch manager requested help from the Tower but—tsk. Who knows when they’ll get here?”
Raven smiled awkwardly as she watched the onlookers click their tongues. Now she knew for sure...
The wizard they were waiting for was her.
Raven took a deep breath and recited a spell.
“Batuna Cor Vier.”
Her body began to float into the air as blue light bloomed under her feet.
“M-Miss! You’re a wizard?”
Raven flew over the crowd and landed on the third-floor terrace of this chapter of the Adventurers’ Guild. And the man she saw there left her stunned.
“Bjorn... Yandel?”
Why was he here?
Because it was the district chief’s daughter being held hostage, the matter was being handled promptly.
“This is Koldo Biermann. The man you asked for. He was unconscious downstairs, just like you said.”
“Thank you,” said the branch manager. “You can leave.”
The first to arrive was the asshole investigator. To clarify, he was still out cold. That wouldn’t look too good to any witnesses, so I shoved him into a closet for now.
After a short wait, my second delivery arrived.
“W-Wait! Guild or not, you can’t strong-arm me like this!”
The name of this male explorer in his twenties with an awkward gait was Harts Young... the moron who had lost his masculinity trying to mess with Erwen.
“Thank you for taking care of this without asking questions. You may go downstairs.”
“Yes sir.”
“A-Are you the branch manager? I—why am I...”
At the moment the employee headed down the stairs, I jumped out from behind the door and shoved my fist into the idiot’s face.
Smack!

One punch couldn’t alleviate my anger, though. If the investigator was the number one contributor to the situation reaching this point, the second contributor was this bastard. Had it not been for this man’s false testimony, the investigator would have had no excuse to sentence me to death.
“Ahh! Wh-what are you doing? Who are you—?”
“Shut up. I’m not done.”
One, two, three punches...
As I continued to pummel my fists into his face one after another, Harts Young passed out as bloody bubbles foamed from his mouth.
This also didn’t look so good, so I put him in the closet as well. Although it was a little cramped thanks to the blubbery mass of the investigator, it shouldn’t be an issue.
The more I looked at them, the better they looked together. As I was appreciating the sight, the branch manager cautiously spoke up.
“...What is it that you want?”
Oh, I hadn’t told him that yet. But I figured there was no need to explain the whole thing twice. After all, when the next delivery arrived, it would all become obvious.
With that in mind, I decided not to say anything. However...
“Sir! It’s going to be difficult to get a priest here.”

The key component of this plan, the priest, was missing. The reason being was that the priest officially associated with this branch was currently absent. It was also impossible to call another priest in. This might have been the Adventurers’ Guild, but even they couldn’t just call in a god-serving priest like they were a buddy from down the street.
Even at the request of the branch manager, it would take at least a day for one to arrive.
In this universe, priests were nobles. Not in terms of their title, but how they acted. All of a sudden, I had a bitter taste in my mouth.
How is it that not a single thing I plan plays out the way I want it to?
I had wanted to handle this matter as quietly as possible. If the branch manager had heard me say that, however, he probably would have called bullshit considering the mess I’d made so far.

But while I could spin the prison break as some kind of accident, what about the fact that the guild had sentenced an innocent rank-nine adventurer to death? The moment this became known to the outside world, the reputation of the Adventurers’ Guild would go down the shitter.
First and foremost they claim to be an organization that protects adventurers.

That was why I had asked for a priest. If I could prove my innocence in front of a priest, I could do things relatively quietly. And that way, the Adventurers’ Guild wouldn’t dare try to cover all of this up. But my plan had been hampered from the very beginning.
“Thank you for letting me know. Head downstairs.”
“Yes sir! Please let me know if you need anything else!”
As I listened to the footsteps of the guild employee retreat, I finished my deliberation.
If it is impossible to get a priest here to be my witness...
I had no choice but to expand the playing field even more. Only then would the Adventurers’ Guild be unable to silence and kill me.
So, of all the ideas that came to my mind, I chose the most radical and effective one.
“Ahhh!”
“W-What are you doing!”

As I stepped out onto the terrace with a sword pointed at the district chief’s daughter, I saw that people had flocked to the streets. They seemed to be spectators who had gathered because of the dungeon break.
One of them noticed me and shouted, “Look! The culprit is up there!”
The crowd’s attention honed in on me in an instant.
“Ahem.”
After clearing my throat once, I shouted out using a barbarian’s talented vocal cords.
“My name is Bjorn Yandel! A rank nine adventurer that the guild has tried to frame and kill! I swear to the gods I am innocent!”
The reactions rolled in immediately.
“Who is that guy?”
“Did he break out of jail?”

It didn’t matter whether they believed me or not. Since I’d tossed out the bait, more curious people would join the crowd soon enough. This might be the Adventurers’ Guild, but even they wouldn’t be able to bury something that everyone had watched happen in real-time. Now, I just had to wait until the wizard arrived.
And instead of a shield that was now little more than a lump of scrap metal...
...I’d make good use of the district chief’s daughter as a shield.
How long had it been since the jailbreak?
“What? Why are you here, Mr. Yandel?”
“I didn’t know the Tower would be sending you.”
As the conversation between an unknown man and woman reached his ears, Koldo Biermann opened his eyes. The place he was in was completely dark and his body wouldn’t move.
What is this? Am I locked up? Why?
Pushing aside his developing headache, he searched his memories. There were a few snippets that immediately came to mind.

Prisoners had been rioting and escaping their cells. He had run away from them and locked himself in the interrogation room. And then a barbarian had smashed through the door and punched him in the face!
Oh, but what happened after that?
He didn’t know. He had no idea at all.
So he focused on what he could hear.
“If you managed to hear about what happened out there, that means news is traveling fast.”
“Fast or not, what are you thinking?! Mr. Yandel, do you think you have multiple lives or something?”
“If I had more than one, I wouldn’t be doing this.”
Mr. Yandel?
What was that? Was that the barbarian out there?
“Enough. Cast your spell quickly.”
“Only if you promise to do me a favor later.”
“I don’t know what you want, but if it’s within my ability...”
“Fine. You promised. Dertei Narvas! Huh...? Why isn’t it working? Mr. Yandel, do you have an item that gives you a psychological barrier?”
“Can’t you tell just by looking at me that I have no such thing? I guess I have no choice but to wake these guys up, then. Do you know how to use video memory magic?”
“Yes. You want me to record everything from now on, right?”
The more he listened to the conversation, the more confusing it was. But just then—
“Ah! Arghhh!”

Suddenly, the space he was in widened and his center of gravity tilted. He fell with a bang and hurriedly raised his head. He was in the branch manager’s office on the third floor, which even he had not entered more than a couple of times.
“What? Are you already awake?”

A total of four people were looking at him: the barbarian and the branch manager, a woman who he presumed to be a wizard, and a woman who looked quite aristocratic. He didn’t know what was happening, but he decided to start in right away.
“B-Branch manager! This is the guy! This guy led the jailbreak!”
“I already know that.”
“You... you do?”
His mind went blank for a moment. He didn’t understand. If he knew this man had committed such an egregious crime, why was he just sitting there and watching?
“I heard you were in charge of this man’s investigation,” said the branch manager. “Is that true?”
“Yes, yes, that’s right.”

It was then that he picked up on the heavy tension in the air. He could tell because it was his job as an investigator to read the room. He knew that things were definitely not looking favorable for him right now.
“This barbarian—no, Mr. Yandel here—is claiming that you have charged him as a plunderer using inconclusive evidence. What do you say to that?”
“That’s ridiculous!”
“Those words... They had better be true. Otherwise, you won’t just be losing your job by the end of this.”
“W-W-What do you mean? He’s just a rank nine adventurer!”
“Watch your words! How can a guild employee judge someone by their ranking!”
“S-Sorry?”
Biermann completely froze at the thunderous roar. Why was this man, who had always been the first to scorn low-rank adventurers, acting like this all of a sudden?
...Like he was conscious of the eyes on him right now.
Oh! Looking back, they said something about video memory magic!
Apparently, the conversation they were having now was being recorded on the crystal ball that the wizard was holding.
“Ahem! As one who judges right from wrong, you know that all guild activities must be carefully and perfectly conducted. Tell me how you came to your verdict.”
Coming back to his senses, he recited the contents of the investigation as directed by the branch manager. He was beginning to think that was the only way he’d survive this.

“F-Firstly, there were the mana stones. At the checkpoint, he presented a number of mana stones that far exceeded the average income of a rank nine adventurer. As this was suspicious, his backpack was checked and it seemed to hold stolen equipment.”
“So?”
“The results of the investigation were inconclusive, as we couldn’t confirm what had really happened. Because no magic would work on him.”
“Then, on what basis did you rule that Mr. Yandel was a plunderer?”

“Thanks to a separate incident. A message stone was found among his belongings. We tracked down the original owner, and then we were able to obtain a testimony from a member of the owner’s adventuring union that Bjorn Yandel had murdered an innocent person and robbed them of their belongings.”

The more details of the investigation he relayed, the more confidence filled his voice. He didn’t know why the branch manager was treating him like he’d done something wrong, but there must have been a misunderstanding.
“Sir, there were no flaws in my ruling. If you suspect that I may have lied, you can use magic to prove it.”
“I’m already on it. Everything he has said so far is true,” the wizard, who was watching quietly, confirmed.
However, the ignorant barbarian spoke up, his tone scathing.
“All you have is a testimony from a member of the same group. It was neither confirmed by magic nor conclusive.”
“Is what Yandel says true?”
“Tha-tha-that’s true, but—”
“Why didn’t you look into it?”
The branch manager’s voice suddenly grew cold again. But Biermann had an excuse for that too.
“First, this barbarian’s physiology is a problem! Knowing that magic wouldn’t work on him, he was uncooperative and gave false testimony!”
“False testimony? What exactly do you mean?”
Biermann answered confidently.

“At one point, he claimed he survived being stabbed in the neck. But there was no scar, so I asked him about it, and do you know what he said? Well, I’ll be darned! The scar disappeared after he absorbed the Essence of a Vampire in the Rift!”
“He absorbed the Essence of a Vampire?”
“Yes sir! How ridiculous! A vampire? In a Rift on the first floor?”
From start to finish, this barbarian had said nothing but nonsense.

“Spitting out a new lie to cover up a previous one—that’s a textbook sign that the person giving the statement is a criminal. How could I just listen to this man and give our city’s precious wizards extra work for no reason?”

Of course, while listening to the barbarian’s repeated claims of innocence, there had admittedly been moments when Biermann had wondered if there was actually truth to said claims. But he had decided it wouldn’t matter.
After all, what was the worst that would happen if an innocent barbarian who had only just completed his coming-of-age ceremony died an unjust death?
...Besides, if I had called a wizard, I would have had less money for myself.

Still, this was a bit of fortune in the middle of a misfortunate situation. Really, a vampire on the first floor? If this ridiculous statement reached the crowd, everyone would be convinced he had made the right call.
You should’ve come up with a more believable lie!
He looked up at the barbarian with triumph in his eyes. But the feeling didn’t last long.
“But it’s true,” Raven said plainly.
His gears ground to a halt at the wizard’s words.
“...Pardon?”
“Well, I was there, but... well, I can’t exactly cast a spell on myself.”
What the hell is this wizard talking about?!

chapters.title: Chapter 40: Guild (5)
paragraphs: The investigator panicked and opened his mouth. “W-W-What do you mean? No matter how familiar you may be with this man, you mustn’t cover for him...”
He wasn’t saying that because he didn’t believe her, though. It sounded more like he just wanted to ignore the truth. However, her reaction was harsh.
“Are you saying that I’m lying?”
“Oh, no, t-that’s not what I meant. You see—”
“Then what? Does using your measly position to investigate adventurers make even wizards seem beneath you now?”

A wizard of the magic tower was basically a semi-noble, largely because, although there were several different schools of wizardry, they were united as a group and thoroughly protected their own rights and interests. The problem here was that the investigator, a low-ranking employee, had dared to doubt the truth of her words. The branch manager couldn’t just stand back anymore and cautiously inserted himself into the conversation.
“How about we cut him a break? You likely have information he doesn’t, and without context, the idea is bound to sound absurd.”
She nodded in acknowledgment.
“Certainly, there is no precedent for a vampire sighting in a Rift on the first floor.”
Unlike when she was dealing with the investigator, there was a friendly smile on her lips as she spoke to the branch manager. It was only there for a very short moment, though.
“Thank you for saying that—”

There was barely a pause before sharp criticism rolled from her lips. “But from the very moment the labyrinth was first created until today, it has been a hub of all kinds of strange phenomena. But, ‘absurd’? Is that something that someone from the Adventurers’ Guild, much less a branch manager, should be saying?”
Was this what it meant to be a wizard? Even the position of the branch manager of the guild did not seem to matter to her.
Thus, the branch manager was promptly silenced after his fruitless attempt at butting in.
Knock knock.
A knock was heard. It wasn’t a polite one. Before anyone could even let them in, the door swung open.
“Are you the barbarian?”
“Who are you?”
“My name is Niall Urbans.”
Two men entered the room—a middle-aged man wearing a tailored tuxedo and a young man who seemed to be escorting him.
“D-District chief!”
“Father...?”
Julian, who was currently being held hostage, and the branch manager opened their mouths at the same time. I, meanwhile, raised my guard again after having let it drop.
So.... even the district chief is here.

The structure of a guild was simple. Each of the hundreds of branches in the city had a branch manager, and there were thirteen district chiefs who oversaw them. The only person above them was the Guild Master, so the thirteen district chiefs were essentially the guild’s second-in-command.

There was no doubt that they were powerful figures that a mere rank-nine adventurer could never hope to meet with. But the world didn’t always work the way you wanted it to, even for people like these guys.
“You... I hear you’ve caused quite an unamusing mess.”
As the district chief’s displeased glare fell on me, I smirked.
Unamusing, huh...
“Yeah, it probably would be unamusing for you guys.”

If only Harts Young hadn’t given that false testimony. Actually, even if he had, if only the investigator hadn’t been greedy and had handled the case correctly. No, if only the Adventurers’ Guild was an association that properly managed its employees... Then I wouldn’t have had to go to all this trouble.
But they hadn’t done any of that.
“This must have been something very minor to you.”
But it wasn’t for me. For me, my life was at stake.
“Is that why you’ve caused all of this insanity?”
“Insanity?” I asked. “Is it insane to want to live?”
“Well, wasn’t there another way you could have handled this? You’ve gone too far.”
Another way, my ass.

Until I broke through those iron bars and arrived here, the branch manager hadn’t even known I existed inside his branch. And that was also the case for this district chief, who had no doubt had a say in changing the guild’s internal rules so that rank nine adventurers could be investigated on suspicion alone.
“If you had done things right, none of this would have happened,” I said in a low, cold tone.
At the exact same moment, the branch manager stepped in. “You! How dare you speak that way in front of the district chief!”

The investigator bastard and the district chief’s escort were also looking at me like they were looking at a madman. Well, to these guys, I was no different from a madman. A misfit among misfits that couldn’t be explained with logic alone.
The district chief sighed and shifted his gaze.
“What is your name, wizard?”
“Arua Raven.”
“Okay, Miss Raven. How much would you sell me that crystal ball for?”
Any way you looked at it, he was proposing a coverup. I didn’t think he would do it so openly though.
For a moment, my heart dropped.
“I decline your offer.”
“That’s too bad.”
