“You’re not going to try to take it away by force, are you?”

The district chief immediately flashed a breezy smile. “Haha! Of course not. If I did that, the master of your school wouldn’t stand for it.” He looked around. “Why is everyone so tense? It was just a joke. With all those people out there waiting to see how this ends, why would I dare do something like that?”
Joke, my ass.
Cold sweat trickled down my spine.

This was why I had tried to bring in a priest. Video Memory or not, wizards could be bought any number of times in pursuit of their own self-interest. If I hadn’t known Raven at all, she would have been successfully bribed by the district chief...
Regardless of the crowd gathered outside, I would’ve died here.
Anyway, the way things had worked out wasn’t bad.
Raven held fast and now even the district chief wouldn’t be able to use his power to cover this up. In other words, now I just needed to prove that I was innocent.
Either way, we’d reached the end of this mess.
“Okay, how about finishing this now?”
I approached the closet and woke up Harts Young, who was sleeping inside.
“Wha-what is this? Why am I here...?”
There were audible gulps all around. That was, of course, because the moment it was confirmed that this guy had given a false testimony, things really were going to get “unamusing” for everyone.
“This man is lying.”
The moment Raven spoke, a heavy silence descended on the room.
“What will you do now, district chief, sir?”
“Bjorn Yandel, I believe you said your name was? You are innocent.”
“It’s too bad I can’t thank you for that,” I said in response to the district chief’s forced smile.
This time, even the branch manager, who was right next to me, did not dare comment on my tone. He just stood there trembling, his eyes glued to the district chief’s reaction.
“Then, what do you want us to do for you now?”
“Isn’t it obvious? I demand compensation and for them to be punished.”
“I see.”
The district chief silently nodded like he was pounding the buttons on a calculator inside his head, then opened his mouth.
“First, the investigator in charge of your case will be fired.”
“B-Branch manager! I-I swear to the gods, I only conducted the investigation according to protocol—!”

“Are you trying to push your incompetence onto the entire guild? All past rulings you’ve made will be thoroughly reviewed. And, if there are any injustices found in the process, you will be punished accordingly.”
“I-It can’t be!”
The arrogant investigator went pale and fell to his knees. Considering how scared he looked, it seemed like he hadn’t exactly lived a life of complete integrity.
Well, judging by his recent behavior, I wasn’t surprised.
“P-Please spare me! Please...!”
Shouldn’t you be saying that to me, not him?

I thought that he was barking up the wrong tree, but I didn’t say this out loud. If he had been an asshole with common sense in the first place, we wouldn’t be here. This was how the world worked. No one ever regretted hitting the other person. The regret only showed up when it came time to pay the price.
“Then what’ll happen to this man?” I asked while looking at Harts Young, the supposed witness in this case.
The district chief replied without much thought.
“This man has seriously muddied the investigation with false testimony to cover up his own guilt. He will be taken care of in the same manner.”
“The same manner?”
“After a thorough investigation, he will be executed.”
The district chief’s words carried much weight. The investigation had not yet begun, let alone reached trial, but the fact was that this was the same as a death sentence.
Soon, Harts Young’s eyes rolled up and he fainted, but no one paid him any mind.
“I hope you will investigate the group this guy belongs to while you’re at it.”
“If it’s the Crystal Union, they have a reputation for many things. I’ll do as you say.”
The district chief readily agreed to my request. I was starting to think he was a pretty smart guy. That meant that he had clearly recognized that he had no choice but to give in to my demands.
“Is this enough punishment, then?”
“Well...”
As I trailed off, staring off into space, the branch manager met my eye and hurriedly looked away. I smiled and nodded my head.
“Asking for more here would be overzealous of me.”
“Thank you for being so considerate of our situation.”
There was nothing to be thankful for. I planned to take what I deserved for this in a different way.
“Okay then, now that the punishment side of things is over, we should talk about your compensation for the mistake we made. Is there anything you want?”
“I’ll decide after I hear you out.”
“First, I will raise your rank to rank seven.”
“A rank upgrade, huh...”
Not bad.

Once I became a rank seven adventurer, the currency exchange line would be less crowded and there would be many other benefits. For example, if I hadn’t been rank nine, that asshole investigator wouldn’t have gotten so uppity in the first place.
“District chief, sir! You are promoting an adventurer with only two months of experience to rank seven in one go!”
The branch manager added that he was worried about potential issues of fairness that might arise in the future, but the district chief stubbornly shook his head.
“We are apologizing to this man right now. So don’t disagree with me on this.”
“...All right.”
The district chief was acting exactly like a politician making a sincere apology, especially his hollow words.
“Just a moment. That’s a bit strange, isn’t it?”

Just as I was about to open my mouth, Raven, who had been standing there quietly, jumped into the conversation first. I was nervous about what she was going to say this time, but... she did not seem to care in the least.
“How can a rank upgrade be considered compensation? Isn’t it already the guild’s job to reward adventurers with certain abilities by raising their rank?”
“But, according to what we were just told, this man is—”
“Still a beginner? What does that matter?”
“It’s unprecedented—”

“Of course it’s unprecedented,” Raven said. Having interrupted the district chief several times already, she continued on in rapid fire. “There have been no other adventurers who have consumed the essence of a rank five monster—a vampire and a Rift Guardian—within their first two months.”
“...What is it that you’re trying to say?”
“I am not sure. It just seemed a little unfair of you to want a pat on the back for doing something that you’re supposed to do anyway.”
She turned to me and smiled. Since I wasn’t naïve enough to throw out a readily available opportunity, I quickly played along.
“Then I guess I’m waiting to hear what the real compensation is now.”
“...What do you want?”
Well, since I’d suffered this much hardship, I should get just as much compensation in return. I was just about to request something... when Raven’s mouth opened again.
“Of course it’s money. What else could the Adventurers’ Guild do for him?”

I was sure if I had time to think about it, there would be something. Receiving free bonding magic for life, or permission to post personal announcements on bulletin boards within the guild, etcetera...
Actually, that’s all stuff that money can buy anyway.
When I nodded in agreement, the district chief sighed and raised a white flag.
“How much?”

Now all that was left was to write out the amount I wanted on the blank check I had been presented. I looked at Raven, who now seemed rather trustworthy to me for some reason, and tried to convey that I had faith in her wizardly judgment. Fortunately, it seemed I had managed to get my point across because she opened her mouth with a somewhat proud look on her face.
“Since you almost accidentally executed an adventurer with a bright future ahead of him...” She trailed off, then snapped, “At least five million stones?”
The district chief nodded his head without a word.
“...All right, it’ll be paid.”
I wasn’t that surprised. Five million stones went far beyond my expectations, but...
That was if I had been the one asking for it.
Without Raven, the transaction would not have gone so smoothly.
Was this the true power of having status? Profoundly aware of its influence, I wondered how I could repay Raven for the favor I had received today.
It was at this point that Raven opened her mouth again.
“Ah, my payment will be another one million stones.”
“Payment? What do you mean? If you’re talking about your payment for aiding us, the amount we agreed upon with the tower is—”

“I’m including the price of this crystal ball that recorded the ‘joke’ the district chief made earlier. It may have been a joke, but... I’m sure there are many people who would be interested in hearing it, don’t you think?”
“...Hahaha, what a funny young woman.”
“I’m not joking.”
When Raven’s expression hardened, the district chief’s expression grew harsh in return. He didn’t need to think for long.
“All right...”
He soon shook his head. He had pissed away one million stones with one slip of the tongue.
...I guess there’s no need to pay her for her help.
Were all wizards like this?
Just as I was admiring the way she looked out for her own interests, her voice resounded in my head.
“Thanks to you, I’ve earned some pocket money.”
And as I heard those words, I thought something I hadn’t thought about someone in a long time...
I thought that we should hang out more often in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 41: The Wizard and the Barbarian (1)
paragraphs: “N-No! Just once! Please, just give me one chance!”
“What are you all doing? Throw these two in jail, now.”

First, the pleading investigator and unconscious adventurer were carted off. Then, the compensation process proceeded swiftly. As soon as they signed a letter agreeing that they wouldn’t discuss this matter with anyone, the two were given a total of six million stones with an added tip. But that wasn’t all.
“These are all the items in your name.”
“So? Is everything there, Mr. Yandel?” the wizard said, a strange look in her eyes as she watched the barbarian dig through his belongings. “There might be something missing.”
“...Missing?” The barbarian flinched, then smirked like he saw what she was getting at. “Now that I’m looking again, it does seem like something is missing.”
“My oh my. Could it be that something was misplaced?”
“Not an item... but about one million stones in cash has disappeared.”
Anyone could tell they were acting. The branch manager’s eyes glazed over as his blood pressure rose. What kind of scamming assholes were these?
“What are you talking about? How could an adventurer have such a large sum of money straight out of the labyrinth?”
“Then are you saying we’re lying?”
The branch manager flinched at the wizard’s cold tone. “I-I-It’s obvious—”
“Your proof?”
“Of course I don’t have—”
“Oh my. Are you accusing us of scamming you without any proof? Mr. Yandel, I think this branch manager should be placed on the list of people that need to be punished.”
“That’s true. To decry an innocent barbarian and wizard as liars, he’s clearly poorly trained—”
“That’s enough,” the district chief interrupted with a sigh. “We will compensate you for the lost money as well.”
“Since that’s a given, I won’t say thank you.”

They may not have been holding knives, but they were no different from a bunch of muggers, shameless to the point that it was ridiculous. However, the branch manager couldn’t do anything except watch the scene unfold.
“Here are one million stones.”
“Wow, the Adventurers’ Guild must be as wealthy as the rumors say, seeing as how the money comes straight out of your pocket.”
“...I believe I have shown you all of the respect I owe the magic tower. Do not push it any further.”
“Sure, why not.”
“Then will you hand me the crystal ball now?” asked the branch manager.
“No. I think I’d better hold on to it until the punishments are properly carried out. Of course, I promise to not show anyone until then.”
“...You will have to keep that promise.”
“Of course. Don’t worry. We’ll be on our way now, so please take care of the crowd outside.”

With that, the barbarian and wizard left, and a heavy silence descended over the room as it had just been ravaged by a series of heavy storms. In the end, the guild had lost another million stones and was not even able to retrieve the crystal ball right away. In addition, the crowd gathered in front of the guild, as well as the other individuals involved, had to be dealt with. The district chief’s face, which had worn a forced smile in front of the man and woman, was now as cold as the icecaps.
Feeling a suffocating chill go down his spine, the branch manager barely managed to open his mouth. “Um... D-District chief? Th-thank you for earlier...”
“Thank me?”
“W-well... you played along with their blackmail to protect me.”
“Of course, because you are one of my people.”
“Sir! I won’t forget what happened today and I’ll work for the rest of my life—”
“So if someone’s going to get rid of you, it’ll be me.”
The branch manager, who had had a deeply moved expression on his face as he spoke, now looked dazed. “...Sorry? W-What do you mean?”
“How naive you are. You thought you’d walk out of here unscathed after what you’ve done?”
“B-But I truly—”

“Enough. I’ll take care of everything from now on, so if you at least want to save your skin, you’d better lay low until the public calms down. Whether you lose your job or that bastard meets a sudden death, it’ll have to be seen as unrelated to this incident.” Before he could say anything back, the district chief whipped around and looked at his daughter. “I’ll hear your reasoning for being here today later.”
“...Yes, Father.”
“Then let’s leave.”
The office was empty in an instant. Left alone, the branch manager thought to himself that this all had to be a nightmare.
“Hahaha...”
A black spire soared high into the sky, and I was currently on its thirty-first floor.
“So? Your first impression of the magic tower.”
“The lack of windows is a little suffocating.”
“Um... Well, sort of. But if we hadn’t compromised on the windows, we wouldn’t have been able to build such a high-rise building in the city.”
I was currently in the office of Arua Raven, a wizard affiliated with the school of Altemion.
“Here, sit.”
Clearing away the pile of documents on top of the chair, I sat down and she brought me a drink in an Erlenmeyer flask.
“Oh, I don’t have any cups here.”
I took a moment to study the drink she gave me and came to a conclusion. “...It’s water.”
“Yes, what about it? Did you want some Basilisk extract instead?”

“No, this is fine.” Of course, I didn’t drink it. I knew it was just water, but I was still uncomfortable drinking it. Not long ago, this same flask likely held colorful liquids and organ specimens from monsters. I set it aside and got straight to the point. “So, why did you bring me here?”
“I have something important to discuss with you. You promised to owe me a favor, right?”

Of course. At the time I had hastily agreed, but sitting here now, I was beginning to regret it. She wouldn’t ask for a medical experiment, would she? “As I said back then, as long as it’s within reason.”
“Fine. That’s enough for me.”
“So, what’s your favor?”

“I want you to grant me exclusive rights to research the essence that you consumed. My studies will definitely be of help to you as well. Considering how rare it is, we may even discover something special.”

The more she spoke, the more the look in her eyes changed from the calculating look she had while negotiating with the district chief to the zealous eyes I saw back in the Rift. To be fair, I could understand that look. Even ignoring the fact that we’d experienced a variant Rift, there had never been a Rift where a vampire had appeared as its guardian.
“But what do you mean by exclusive research rights?”
“Oh, that? To put it simply, it means that you will only provide samples to me. I want to submit the thesis to the academy in my name.”

Were wizards in this universe kind of like graduate students? I didn’t really get that motive myself, but... I’d also heard that scholars had a strong desire for accolades. Oh, wait. “Is that why you asked the district chief to get rid of all records related to the vampire earlier?”

When we were signing the letter of agreement back at the guild, she had been the one to request that my consumption of the vampire’s essence be omitted from any official documents. Of course, I didn’t expect that alone to guarantee perfect secrecy, but it was better than nothing, so I had agreed.
They say to keep 70 percent of your abilities hidden.
To be honest, I was beginning to feel grateful that she was taking care of even minutiae like that.
She scratched her cheek awkwardly. “Uh, mm, well... can’t say that’s not why...”
Denying a denial. That meant I was right.
After a moment, Raven completely changed the subject. “Ahem! Anyway, I won’t ask for much. Come see me once a week for about three hours.”
Three hours a week, huh? “For how long?”
“Mm, half a year should be enough.”
“Three months.”
“All right. So you’ll agree to my request?”
“I will.”
With the first item on the agenda settled, Raven immediately brought up the next topic. “Now... should we finish up the calculations?”

Calculations? There was still something left to be sorted? When I gave her a look asking what kind of nonsense she was talking about, she came at me from a different angle, just like how she had negotiated with the district chief head-on.
“You got out of that mess thanks to me. Not to mention you also earned a total of six million stones. I don’t think it’s unreasonable to claim my share.”

Haha, of course. Now I was getting a better sense of these wizards. If I was an efficiency freak, these people were the ultimate profit freaks. So, I decided to shift my mindset to the same one I used when I was crushing a goblin’s head.
“Give you money? What an interesting request.”
The quarrel continued in voices that were slightly more raised than before.
“Any other wizard would have done the same,” I argued.
“I’m not sure about that. If it had been someone else, they would have sold the crystal ball as soon as the district chief made the offer.”
“But the price for that has already been paid. A whopping one million stones.” Actually, since she had earned so much thanks to me, by the name of Behela, I should be the one claiming my share.
“...Then at least give me the one million you got for the backpack at the end. That was purely thanks to my help.”
Did I really say I wanted to be friends with her earlier? I had officially changed my mind. Do barbarians look like idiots to you? “I refuse.”
“All right. Since you agreed to cooperate with my research, I won’t ask for everything. Give me half—five hundred thousand stones.”
“I refuse.”
“Ha, then 250,000 stones—”

“I won’t hear any more of this. I refuse.” I wouldn’t make the slightest compromise. That was because anyone who tried to steal from me was a fucking bitch, and I didn’t make compromises with bitches. On the contrary, I was the only one who could steal. “End of conversation.”
“What? Do you have any idea how much money I lost in the Rift because of you?”
Soon, I made up my mind. I have to crush her spirit before she starts looking down on me even more.

To be honest, it wasn’t that I wasn’t grateful. But regardless of that, if we were going to have a long-term and friendly relationship, I needed to show her what kind of man I was. The kind of bastard who just laughs things off no matter how he’s treated isn’t a nice guy, but a total fool.
The reason why she’s being so persistent is probably not because she actually needs the money, but to crush my spirit.
“Let’s move on to the other calculations,” I said out loud.
Raven cocked her head like she couldn’t think of what I could be referring to. “What other calculations?”
I spoke straightforwardly, like a barbarian. “You have to give me five million stones.”
“F-Five million stones? And why should I do that?”
“Because you fed me the corpse golem’s essence without my consent.”
“W-What?” she shouted like that was absurd. “Ha! I gave you an essence anyone would kill to have, yet I should pay you money for it? Do you think that makes logical sense?”

It did. It wasn’t an ignorant, outlandish request. I didn’t know why everyone here lacked creativity, but if you looked at it piece by piece, my argument was perfectly reasonable. “Why do you think it makes no sense? You forcibly fed me that essence without my consent for your own survival.”
“Y-You don’t think I was trying to save you?”
“I don’t know about that, nor do I want to. So, give me ten million stones. I heard that that’s how much it costs to remove an essence at the temple—”
“Why would you get it removed, you crazy barbarian!?”
“Because it wasn’t the essence I wanted. You have done me serious damage.”

Unlike before, when she had been the one negotiating a price, her face turned red. My words sounded like a total stretch, but at the same time, they made some sense, which was clearly infuriating to her.
After breathing hard for a while, she finally quieted down. “...I heard that adventurers can’t even buy an essence with money. Which is why this doesn’t make sense. I should be the one getting paid!”
“That’s just a preconceived notion you have as a wizard. You can ask another adventurer if you’d like—how they would feel if someone forcibly fed them an essence they didn’t want.”

“Ha! You think I don’t know any other adventurers? Wait here. I’ll ask them right now.” Raven frantically picked up the crystal ball on her desk. Then, she manipulated it like she was dialing a phone number and soon established a connection. “Ah, is this Mr. Patzran?”
“And who is this?”
“Hello. This is Arua Raven of the Altemion School. We met a while ago along with my master.”
“Ah! Miss Raven! I remember. But how can I help you all of a sudden?”
“I have a question for you. How would you feel if someone fed you an essence you didn’t plan on taking without your consent?”
“Hahaha! I don’t know why you’re asking such a bizarre question, but to give you an answer... I would be very angry.”
Her triumphant expression did not last long. “...Pardon? Why angry? W-What if it’s a rank seven essence? And a rare one that can only be obtained from the Rift?”

“Even so, my answer is the same. To me, an unplanned essence would only ever have a negative effect. You must not be aware, Miss Raven, but adventurers cannot advance to the upper floors by consuming just any essence.”

After hearing the adventurer’s friendly reply, Raven glanced over at me, beginning to pale. “O-O-Of course. But, assuming something like that were to happen... How should someone be compensated for it?”
“If it were me, I would demand compensation in cash.”
“About how much...?”
“Oh, fifteen million stones would be appropriate.”
“That much?!”
“When it comes to essences, the cost of erasing one increases the more you erase. I wonder where those god-worshippers even use the money, but... tsk.”
“Ah, ahh, that’s right...” Apparently losing feeling in her hands, she dropped the crystal ball and it rolled onto the floor.
I picked it up for her and put it back into her hand. “You still have one more question to ask,” I whispered in her ear.
“...I-I-If you couldn’t be compensated with money,” the blonde young woman asked in a trembling voice, “what would you do?”

“Hmm, I’m not sure. If something like that happened to me and the perpetrator was right in front of me...” The man on the other side of the transmission paused, and when he next spoke, it was with enthusiasm. “I’d probably snap their head off. Hahaha!”

chapters.title: Chapter 42: The Wizard and the Barbarian (2)
paragraphs: Drop.

After the transmission dropped, Raven’s laboratory fell silent for a while. To be fair, she couldn’t have expected this. How could she have known that her plan to rip me off would instead end with her having to give me five million stones?
The people here really have no imagination.

Actually, there was a way she could’ve won the argument. If she had asked that question to any rank-nine adventurer living paycheck to paycheck, they would’ve replied that they’d have been happy to take the essence and her point wouldn’t have been so easily dismantled. However, the adventurer she had contacted was clearly a skilled one.
If it’s someone close to her master, he can’t be an ordinary adventurer.
That had been her decisive mistake. Now it was time to pay for it.
“Hahaha! A barbarian who can best a wizard? He’s even more fascinating than I heard!”

A grey-haired and wrinkled old man opened the door without a knock. His back was not hunched and he looked very youthful despite his age. After being momentarily bewildered by the sudden interruption, I was able to quickly deduce the identity of the old man just as he spoke again. “Oh, I didn’t introduce myself. I am the teacher of the young lady you just made cry.”
“I-I didn’t cry!”

It was Raven’s teacher. In other words, the master of the Great School of Altemion, a school that occupied a whopping five floors of the tower we were in. In a way, he was as much of—no, an even more powerful figure than that district chief earlier.
“Anyway, I heard your conversation.”
“Pardon? How? The soundproofing spell should be active—”
“Ah, you should reinforce that spell. It had too many holes in its design. Tut.”

His speech was no different from that of a neighborhood grandpa, but because of his position, I couldn’t help but feel a bit intimidated. It was clear he cherished Raven as a disciple, and I was kind of the bad guy here.
“Ha... You completely destroyed my magic circle. It couldn’t have been easy to destroy that without me realizing, even for someone like you, Master... Why did you eavesdrop on our conversation?”
The old man chuckled. “My youngest disciple has brought home a man. And a living barbarian at that! Of course I’m curious.”
Something about that was strange. “Living?” I mumbled.
The old man gave another hearty laugh. “Haha! Most of them come here dead! Or just get delivered as a heart!”
I stared at him.
“Don’t give me that look. It’s a joke!”
Oh, I see. Is this what a wizard’s sense of humor is like?
Since I was a barbarian who could read the room, instead of looking unamused, I responded with a hearty laugh of my own. “Hahaha! I want to smash your head in!” This was a barbarian joke.
“...W-What?”

Why isn’t he laughing? Oh, right. I didn’t mention that. “Hahaha! It was a joke!” No matter what bullshit you spewed out, all you had to do was say it was a joke afterward, right? “So don’t look like that, Gramps!”
“Gramps...?”
“Ah, that was a joke as well! Hahaha!”
At my joke, the Master of Altemion, Gramps for short, frowned in apparent displeasure.
When I looked to the side, Raven was watching us with her jaw dropped like she couldn’t believe what was happening. “...Mr. Yandel, is it possible that you are a lunatic?”
Was she trying to be considerate, or was that just an insult? Her polite tone of voice confused me.
My mistake.

Judging by her reaction, I may have taken things a bit too far. I guess that was fair. A fucking barbarian had just cracked an unhinged joke in front of the head of a magical school in the middle of the magic tower.
“Ha... I should’ve known from how you acted at the guild...”
Still, this was a bit unfair. This may sound like an excuse, but joking about a dead barbarian in front of a barbarian who had just escaped being executed was insensitive too.

“It seems I am on the defensive thanks to the stress. I apologize if my words made you feel bad.” It was my first time making an apology like this in a long time, but Raven immediately shouted at me as if it was in no way enough.
“How is that being defensive!”
“The best defense is a good offense.” This had been my motto from a very young age.
So. How should I fix this?
I glanced at the old man and noticed he was still standing there frozen with a blank look on his face. As the silence stretched on, I was beginning to feel genuinely concerned for my safety.
Then the old man started laughing out of nowhere. “Hohoho! This fellow is definitely something!”
I didn’t know what was going on, but I laughed along. “Hahaha!”
“Hohoho! What an interesting fellow!”
Anyone could tell I was just laughing along, pretending to be unintimidated. But that might be enough to resolve this mess.

“Don’t worry! This old man is different from other sensitive and narrow-minded fools.” Even as he said this, however, his lips were still quivering. But there was no point in drawing attention to that.
I can roughly guess what kind of character he is, along with how to deal with him.

“Haha! What barbarian line do you come from?” I asked. “Forget my earlier words! You took my joke very heartily! I’ve never seen such a spirited wizard in my life!” I hadn’t met a lot of wizards, to begin with. But, oh well.
“Haha, well, this old man has a side like that to him too. I have a feeling we’ll get along!”
“I agree!”
The cold air between us quickly dissipated. Raven watched as we cheerfully laughed with a dumbfounded expression on her face. “Ha... What exactly is going on?”
I actually wasn’t sure, either, and I was pretty sure that even the old man didn’t know what he was doing. “I am Bjorn, son of Yandel! Great wizard! I want to know your name!”
“Bjorn Yandel! Meeting you after rubbing elbows with such narrow-minded wizards is like a breath of fresh air! Nice to meet you. This old man’s name is Deian Tveherion!”
For some reason, the old man introduced himself in a loud voice. The sight of the veins sticking up on his neck made me worry for his health, but I pretended not to notice.
“Amazing! That’s the voice of a true, ambitious man!”
I, Bjorn Yandel, was a barbarian with social skills.
“So what I said to those narrow-minded wizards then was—”
“Amazing!”
“Hmm? I haven’t said any—”
“I’m sure it was amazing!”

After many minutes of friendly conversation like the one above, the old man finally seemed to come back to his senses after getting to show off and slowly circled back to the point. “So. What do you plan to do with Aru?”
“Aru?”
“Ah, that’s sort of my nickname for my youngest disciple.”
Aru as in Arua Raven? It seemed some things were culturally universal.
“Anyway, that five million stones earlier, what if this old man—”
My friendly barbarian mode immediately shut off. “I will not go back on that.”

The old man clicked his tongue at the way I had cut him off so bluntly. “Tsk, who said you wouldn’t get your payment? If it’s okay with you, this old man would like to give you something else instead.”
That changed things. “What is it?”
“This.” The old man put his hand inside the robe he was wearing and pulled out a box the size of his palm. However, I was more interested in the robe he was wearing than the box.
Is there some kind of subspace enchantment on that robe? Hmm, he wouldn’t give me that if I asked, would he?
“Well? Open it up.”
Inwardly licking my lips, I opened the box to find a single ring.
“It’s an object named the Ring of the Frost Spirit.”
“The Ring of the Frost Spirit?”
The old man continued his explanations at my mumbling, but I decided I didn’t need to listen. I was already familiar with this item.
“Although it’s in the 9000s, I’m sure an adventurer like you would know just how precious a Numbers Item is.”

A Numbers Item: an item that could only be obtained from a Rift guardian. Each held a unique and special ability. In fact, except for crafting and exploring, in Dungeon and Stone, the only way to create equipment was through a Numbers Item. Of course, most of them were still expensive regardless of the number.
“You are very lucky. If I hadn’t taken a liking to you, I would never have—”
“This is an item no one uses.”

No. 9425: The Ring of the Frost Spirit. The Ring of the Frost Spirit was only dropped in Rifts below the third floor and carried a special ability. It wasn’t an ability that helped in battle, but it sealed one of the essences absorbed by the wearer. Of course, the essence’s stats still applied, and only skills were sealed, but...
In that case, it would be cheaper to remove the essence at the temple.

Think about it. Increasing your level became astronomically more difficult with time. And when you wore this ring, all of the skills you got from an essence were completely discarded. It was the same as one of your skill slots disappearing altogether. Forward-looking adventurers would choose to erase the essence at the temple and absorb a new one rather than wear this.
“But this must be very useful to you, right?”

There was no doubt that was the case. When you were just starting out, your stats were more important than your skill combinations. Moreover, even though the corpse golem had mediocre skills, its stats were quite high.
If you take into consideration the fact that you can always reactivate the essence’s abilities by taking the ring off, it’s not a bad item in itself.

I finished doing the math in my head. In fact, I hadn’t even been considering rejecting the offer in the first place. That was because the information I had just listed was only a fraction of this ring’s true value.
Judging by the fact that he hasn’t mentioned it once even though I was testing him, I guess he really doesn’t know about that event.

Wizards were the foremost intellectuals in this universe. However, when I realized Raven was unaware of the Tears of a Goddess hidden inside the statue in the Bloody Citadel, I became certain. They were just newbies to me. And in any game, newbies were the easiest to extort.
“Why are you hesitating? To be honest, this ring isn’t worth five million stones. But it isn’t something you can get just by buying it, either.”

“I see.” I nodded in agreement. Even in the game, the auction price for this item was only about 1.5 million stones. However, since there was a lack of supply, I had only ever been able to acquire it one out of every ten times.
But he’s giving me this valuable item?

I hadn’t expected to receive all five million stones in the first place. Likewise, the old man must’ve been planning to send me back with whatever useless item he had from the start. Inwardly, he was probably thinking I was a stupid barbarian.
But I was thinking the same of him. “Thanks to you, I’ve acquired a great item. I’ll put it to good use.”
“Think of it as a gift from an old man.”
As I watched him chuckle kindly, I thought, With some effort, I’ll be able to extort more things from him in the future. I can see us getting along.
“Mr. Yandel, today is probably not the best day for you, right? You must be tired after everything you went through. Shall we meet in two days to discuss the rest?”
“Just what I wanted.”
After a quick conversation to arrange the time and place for their more detailed discussion, Bjorn left the laboratory.
After that, Raven awaited her master’s reaction.
“I’m sorry, Master, it’s my fault...”
“It’s all right. That item wouldn’t have been sold, anyway. And once that barbarian realizes what that ring is worth, he’ll be in for quite a headache.”

“Is that right?” Fortunately, he didn’t seem to be particularly angry that she had brought Bjorn here, so Raven relaxed and asked a question that had been bothering her. “But why did you do all that earlier?”
The master’s attitude today had been very strange. He hated rude people and had never demeaned his fellow wizards as narrow-minded before.
“Ah, there was something I needed to check.”
“To check?”
“That’s not for you to know.”
She pursed her lips grumpily. That made it clear that there had been some kind of reason behind him matching Bjorn’s high energy, but she had no way to figure it out.
“Anyway, he’s an odd one. So odd that I’m even starting to look forward to it... I hope I am correct...”
“Are you going to keep doing that? If you’re going to talk to me, would you just explain things?!”
“I will tell you later when the time is right. Oh, when you have a moment, write down everything that happened with that barbarian and send it to me.”
“Aren’t you going to tell me why?”
“I’ll tell you when I’m certain.”
Soon after, her master left her laboratory with the same gentle smile on his face as usual. As she stared at the empty seat he left behind, she started to get a strange feeling.
What is he thinking?
She wondered if it had been a bad idea to bring Bjorn to the tower. She now remembered that the last days of the people her master took such an interest in usually weren’t very good.
Oh, but would Mr. Yandel end up the same way?
As she thought of the rank-nine adventurer who had razed an entire guild, she started to grow anxious.
Nah, no way. The magic tower isn’t some neighborhood convenience store.
The guild and the magic tower were completely different. This was without a doubt not the kind of place that a single barbarian could take on.

chapters.title: Chapter 43: The Wizard and the Barbarian (3)
paragraphs: “Oh! Bjorn, son of Yandel!”

As soon as I left the magic tower, I headed straight to the barbarians’ dormitory. But since it had been two months now, half of the faces I knew had disappeared and newbie barbarians instead took their spots. I heard that there was an implicit tradition to leave this place as soon as you made money to make room for new barbarians.
Among the ones who are no longer here, there are probably many who died during this month’s expedition.

When you were born a barbarian, this was your destiny. Unlike elves, who had more experienced people helping them out, the barbarian way was to have to survive all on your own once you entered the city.
“Is Ainar here?”
“Ainar left for the holy land first thing in the morning!”
Yeah, I figured that would be the case. I came to visit since I hadn’t seen her in the two days since we left the labyrinth, but it turned out to be a wasted trip.
“Oh, did you hear the news?”
“What news?”
“The free barbarian! News of that man is rampant around the whole city. You haven’t heard?”
I flinched instinctively. “I-I didn’t know that. Do you happen to know his name as well?”
“Hmm? I don’t know! Strangely, that’s the only thing that wasn’t revealed!”
Thankfully, it seemed that the guild had made me anonymous.
“Anyway, to have such a person among our people, I am proud! He beat up hundreds of people by himself and courageously removed a false accusation placed on him by the guild. Isn’t that amazing?”

“...He beat up hundreds of people?” I swear to god nothing like that happened. All I did was hold onto the daughter of the district chief and complain. But had the rumors already evolved into stuff like this? I was already starting to get worried about the future.
I’m sure it’ll subside soon. The guild’s employees are not idiots.
“I’ll be back tomorrow evening. Will you tell Ainar that if you see her?” I asked.
“I will!”
Soon after, I turned around and headed to my inn. But what was this? As soon as he spotted me, the innkeeper looked like he had seen a ghost.
“Y-You...! You aren’t dead?”

It seemed my analogy had been pretty accurate, then. Thanks to that, I didn’t have to ask many questions and quickly extracted a confession that he had gotten rid of my room, thinking I was dead. “What happened to my belongings?”
“I got rid of them...”
“I clearly paid for three days in advance.” Unbeknownst to me, my voice was filled with annoyance, and the innkeeper’s face turned white.
It’s not like I can just beat him up—
Wait. Since when had I started thinking like this? I flinched at the strange sensation that something was out of place.
It may have even started on the first day.

In fact, looking back, everything had been a little strange from the very beginning. As soon as I opened my eyes, even though a person’s head had been chopped off, my mind was calm. It was the same when I committed my first murder inside the labyrinth. I knew it was something I had to do, but the process of doing it was far too easy. It hadn’t even been a gradual change. From the day I had woken up in this body, I was as aggressive as the barbarians, and I just hadn’t noticed.
It was the same even today.

A jailbreak? Of course, it was a course of action I had selected after much deliberation, but strangely, I hadn’t felt any hesitation. The argument I had had with the old man in the magic tower had been in a similar vein. I was angry because I had heard something that didn’t tickle my fancy? The twenty-nine-year-old office worker Hansu Lee would never have done something like that. He wasn’t timid, but he wasn’t bold, either. He was very suspicious of everything, so he was the kind of person who observed a situation for a long time before taking action.
But what about now?
Up until now, I just thought that it was a change that had occurred because I had been placed in a strange environment, but the feeling of incongruity was growing bigger and bigger.
I’m positive.

Soon, I was convinced. Just like how in every battle the instincts ingrained in this oblivious body surfaced of their own accord, something had changed in my mind as well. No, it was more like I had found some sort of balance than experienced an actual change.
“Th-that’s why I said s-sorry! Stop glaring at me!”
Having finished thinking it over, I sighed. I had changed. It was strange I had only noticed now, but at least I had confirmed it. But what about it?
If I want to survive in this world, it’s better this way.
I decided to focus on the positive. I could just be more careful about controlling my barbarian instincts from now on.
“...If you give me thirty thousand stones, I’ll let it go.”

Therefore, though the innkeeper’s behavior had been very offensive, I decided to let this pass with just fair compensation. The most expensive thing I owned was my 2,500-stone clothes, and I wanted to get some rest more than I wanted to stand here and argue.
“Thirty thousand stones! Just because I sold some of it—”
“Didn’t you just say you threw it all away?”
The man silently gulped.
“If you don’t want to give me the money then just say so, so that I can tell everyone here what you did to me.”
“...What if I just let you stay at the inn for however many days that amount of money would get you instead?”
“No.” I had no intention of staying at this kind of inn in the future. Stealing from a dead adventurer was one thing, but he didn’t even bother to wait until the date we agreed upon.
“Ha... Promise that you won’t tell anyone.”
“Of course.”

After that, with an additional income of thirty thousand stones in my pocket, I headed to the inn I had been eyeing earlier. Although the average meal and the cost per night were twice as expensive, it was worth the price.
Now I finally feel like I’m living like a person.
First of all, the room was 1.5 times larger than before. It had windows and even had a private tub in the bathroom. The fact that it was much closer to Dimension Square was a bonus.

After scrubbing my skin clean for about an hour to wash off all the dirt I had accumulated in the labyrinth, I jumped straight into the bed. It was soft, to the point that I wondered whether this was the kind of momentary happiness that people lived for. Was this why everyone else woke up in the morning?
Suddenly, all the events from the labyrinth up to everything that had occurred since I had returned to the city flashed through my mind like a montage.
“Fuck.”
Why was it so hard for me to get some rest?
As soon as the morning dawned, I headed into an open clothing store and bought everyday clothes. Then I headed back to the barbarians-only dormitory.
“Bjorn! Where have you been all this time?!” cried Ainar.
“I had some things to take care of. Sorry to worry you.”
“Worry? What are you talking about? There’s no way I’d do that! Even if you were thrown into hell itself, you’d come back alive!”
Right, that’s your impression of me. Well, I like that much better than a reunion scene out of a B-grade soap opera.
Since neither of us had eaten, we headed to a nearby restaurant.
“Oh, did you hear?” Ainar asked once we were seated and had placed our orders.
I wasn’t caught off guard this time around because I had seen this coming. “Oh, that free barbarian?”
“Hmm? A free barbarian? What are you talking about?”
Uh, that wasn’t your question? “...Nothing. So, what were you going to say?”
“Ah!” Returning to her original point, Ainar lowered her head and her voice. “I heard this from the elder... Someone stole the Genesis Treasure!”
“The Genesis Treasure?” I genuinely shouted.
The Genesis Treasures referred to the six treasures kept by the six races: dwarves, barbarians, elves, beastmen, dragon people, and humans. The problem was...
Without that thing, I can’t enter the last floor!

The Genesis Treasures were the most important items in Dungeon and Stone. The ending— Well, actually, at this point, I didn’t know if the ending even existed, but in order to open the Gate of the Abyss, all six of the Genesis Treasures had to be combined. But now the barbarian treasure was gone?
“Who would do such a foolish thing?”
“I don’t know either. But apparently it was stolen on the day of our coming-of-age ceremony. The elder said that the other races might be in a similar boat.”
“...I see.”
It felt like someone had clocked me over the back of the head with a hammer, but I finished my meal without saying much.
Shit, does that mean I have to live here for the rest of my life?
In a way, it was as if my biggest hope had just disappeared. But to be honest, it would take at least several years for the Genesis Treasures to be of use to me anyway.
This isn’t something I should worry about when I haven’t even made it to the third floor yet.

Ultimately, my job remained the same. When the day came to make a choice, I needed to be as strong as I could so I would be able to choose from as many options as possible. Plus, you never knew. While I was focusing on that, the thief might even be caught.
“Ainar, are you free today?”
“Yes. I’ve decided not to go to the holy land today.”
“Good.” After a short meal, I headed to the business district with Ainar.
“Is this Kommelby? It’s my first time being here in person! There are so many people!”

Kommelby was the name for Sectors Two and Five, which surrounded Karnon like a belt. It was colloquially referred to as the Free Market by most people. That was how commercially prosperous this part of the city was. Inhabited by Rafdonia’s middle class, many artisans and shops were concentrated here. I had stopped by here with Erwen the other day.
I wonder if she’s doing okay.

Belatedly, Erwen came to mind. Our rendezvous almost always started with her coming to see me at the inn where I was staying, but now that I’d left that inn, it had become quite difficult to run into her. I couldn’t remember the exact location of the elves-only dormitory I had visited that one time, either.
Well, I’m sure I could find it if I wanted to.
Still, I wondered if that was necessary. As long as her older sister was still alive, there would be no need for Ainar to journey into the labyrinth with me.
If we’re meant to meet again, we will.
To be honest, after everything I’d been through these past few days, my memories of Erwen had also faded quite a bit. It hadn’t even been that deep of a relationship in the first place.
“Oh! Look over there, Bjorn! People are eating clouds on skewers!”
What? There was cotton candy here? Intrigued, I bought one to get a taste and gave the rest to Ainar. It really was cotton candy.
“I-I can’t believe it! Are all humans geniuses? To create food like this—!”
“Stop gushing over it and follow me.”
“D-Don’t leave me here! I can’t get home on my own!”

Speeding up a bit, we quickly reached our destination: the surplus store where we had sold our equipment before. I sold off all the equipment that had landed me in jail, as well as the equipment that had turned into a lump of scrap metal. The selling price was about eight hundred thousand stones. I didn’t sell the thing I got just before coming out of the Rift, but...
I can probably just round up and call this five hundred thousand stones.
“Ainar, this is your share.”
“This much?! I even absorbed an essence thanks to you...”

“Do not hesitate, take it. It’s your fair share.” The split was 80:20, as promised. Still, compared to the rest of our party, she probably earned the most during this adventure. “I promised you that if you followed me, you’d earn more money.”
“Still, three hundred thousand stones! That’s too much! How many cloud snacks is that!” Suddenly, the cotton candy had been upgraded to another monetary unit for Ainar.
“By the way, I’m getting hungry.” Was it because the corpse golem’s essence had Appetite +9 attached to it? I felt like I was getting hungry much faster.
“Already? It hasn’t even been three hours yet!”
“So you’re not coming?”
“Of course I’ll come! Today, I will buy you meat!”
After quickly disposing of the equipment, we stopped at a nearby restaurant to eat. Just as we were about to leave, Ainar looked straight into my eyes and said, “Thank you, Bjorn.”
There was still sauce left on her lips, but her eyes were more serious than usual.
Ha... it was always awkward when she got like this. “No need. Like I said before—”
“I’m not talking about the money.”
“Hmm? Then what is it?”
“It’s just... I want to thank you for treating me the same way.”

I wondered what she was going to say—I couldn’t understand where she was going with this at all. Ainar’s expression was far too serious for her to just want to say that. So I just stared at her without a word, and she continued.
“Um... As you know, my appearance has changed a lot. The others are avoiding me because they don’t think I’m a warrior.”
“That’s—”
“These days, wherever I go, even humans keep coming up to me! That’s never happened before!”

This was no doubt a serious concern for a woman who was very proud of being a warrior. To be honest, I couldn’t really empathize, but that must have been because my personality was different than a regular barbarian’s.
“Bjorn! Be honest!” Ainar cried out angrily when I didn’t do anything but sit there and listen quietly. “Am I that ugly?”
...What?
“I have decided! Bjorn! From now on, I can’t enter the labyrinth with you!”
Wait. Why was that the conclusion you reached?
I was currently sitting alone drinking lukewarm beer in the first-floor parlor of the inn I was staying at.
How could beer be this tasteless? It seemed I was staying at the wrong inn. The food was pretty good, but the innkeeper had a bad taste in alcohol.

“Ha...” I let out a long breath in an attempt to shrug off my bitterness. My earlier conversation with Ainar came to mind. After her bombshell declaration, we had a long talk, but the outcome hadn’t changed.
“I am alone again.”
Ainar had left. Like all barbarians, she tended to ramble, but from what I managed to gather, it seemed her decision wasn’t just because of her appearance.
“To be honest... an elder asked me to become his successor yesterday,” she had explained.
An elder of the holy land—and one known for his reputation as a respected swordsman—had favored Ainar. Today, she made the decision to officially learn the art of the sword under him.

“But even if you go into the labyrinth with me, it’s only a day out here,” I had pointed out. Just one day a month was all I was asking for. Couldn’t she miss one day of training to enter the labyrinth?
But the question only made Ainar upset. “I want to do that too... but there is a special training program, so I can’t leave the holy land for six months.”

Special training program? Could it be the one I was thinking of? If so, I could understand why she wouldn’t be able to enter the labyrinth with me for six months. I also knew how great an opportunity this was.
“I won’t ask you to wait. Nor will I ask you to take me back when I return. But I will definitely train hard and come back as a great warrior so as not to be a burden.”

It was for that reason that I hadn’t been able to hold her back. During this expedition, she had been restrained by a plunderer and forced to make an oath. Inside the Rift? While the wizard, the dwarf, and I had played active roles, Ainar had been helpless.
Actually, that must have been the deciding factor for why she made this decision.
Her change in appearance would have only been a contributing factor.
“Ugh...” I took another sip of the lukewarm beer, feeling a strange thirst. A bitter taste filled the back of my throat.
Do I have to find another teammate now?
I had been hoping to be able to get some rest and prepare for the next expedition at my leisure. So how come I had a new quest every day?

chapters.title: Chapter 44: Line (1)
paragraphs: But do I really need a teammate?
That was the first thing that came to mind after Ainar said she was leaving the party. After all, I wasn’t the same person I was two months ago.
I can probably hunt a group of death fiends on my own now.

I had the essence of a corpse golem and a vampire, and a guardian at that. My general stats, including strength, had all gone up immensely. Taking my healing factor into account, I had virtually no competition up to the second floor.
It definitely wouldn’t be impossible.

There would be no night watch and no teammate to turn to in emergencies. However, I came to an objective conclusion. Even taking all of that into consideration, at my current level, I could play a pretty reliable solo game.
Well, the third floor is still a stretch.

Dungeon and Stone pretty much forced party play as a default. No matter how strong a character was, it was impossible to play without a team given the game’s structure. That was how strictly defined the roles of party members were. The higher up you went, the more fatal the absence of a specific class was. For example, a scout was essential in the goblin forest. As a barbarian in a tank role, I served as an indomitable wall.
From the third floor onward, the scale of monsters also changes.

After much deliberation, I made a decision to find a new party member of a similar level. If I couldn’t, I’d join a party that fit that criteria and together, hunt monsters on a higher floor and aim for the top.
It’s more efficient than wasting time playing alone on the second floor.
Of course, this was going to be a headache, since I’d have to make sure they were trustworthy on top of gauging their strength and forming a group.
Ha... Where can I find people like that?
It seemed that this month would be another busy one. Aside from Ainar and Erwen, there was no one in this world I could call an acquaintance.
Throwing back the rest of my beer, I was about to head up to my room when a party of adventurers, who had been guzzling down alcohol at the table next to me for a while, started speaking to me.
“Hey there, Mr. Barbarian! What do you think?”
“What do you mean?”
“Oh, you didn’t hear? Our little friend here said something cute.”
Hmm, I didn’t think they were looking for a fight. When I gestured that I would hear them out, an adventurer in his mid-twenties explained the situation in detail.

To summarize, it was like this: somehow, the topic of the free barbarian had come up. Naturally, the group of adventurers started badmouthing the guild. But then, a young adventurer came over and praised the guild, asking if the group really believed crap like that. The adventurers who were listening then started laughing and making fun of them, at which point they saw me walking by and stopped me.
“That’s why we want to hear what you think. How about it? Do you also believe that those bastards at the guild are trustworthy?”
Fuck, are you kidding? “I’d rather place my trust in a pile of shit on the road than the guild.”
“Hahaha! Yes! I knew you’d say something like that! I could tell just from looking at your eyes that you were different from the rabble!” That seemed to please the man and he continued to laugh.

The young guy who had been huddled in the corner suddenly got up, his face red. “Wait! How can you call yourselves adventurers, then? Who would protect us if not for the guild? You should be grateful!”
There was a short silence. Then everyone at the table burst into laughter.
“What? Be grateful? Hahaha!”
“Kid! That’s why you’re treated like a child wherever you go!”
Apparently, a key part of the adventuring culture was that you had to distrust the guild to be recognized as a full-fledged adult.
“That’s enough, everyone. He’ll figure it out when he experiences it firsthand. That no one, aside from your own self, can protect you.”
“Wow, what touching words.”
“On that note, let’s drink!”
After this brief exchange, the adventurers continued drinking. I was about to leave again when the man who stopped me earlier came up to me with a friendly look on his face.
“I’m Hans.”
“Hans...?”
“Haha! It’s a common name, huh?”
I didn’t know for sure, but it definitely seemed to be common. The name of the first man I had killed in the labyrinth had also been Hans.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“I see! Since fate brought us together, if you’re not tired, why don’t you have another drink with us? I’ll pay!”
I contemplated his offer and then nodded. Although I had eavesdropped on the conversations of other adventurers here and there, I hadn’t had a lot of direct conversations with them.
“So, what kind of trouble are you having that you were drinking alone like that?”
I figured I might receive some unexpectedly helpful advice, so I decided to be honest and share my worries. “My party disbanded, so I’m looking for new teammates. But I don’t know where to start.”
Hans, who had been listening seriously, cocked his head. “Why don’t you head to the guild for a problem like that?”
“Guild?”
“Haha! It’s true they’re untrustworthy bastards, but shouldn’t we use whatever resources are available to us? They run on our tax money, anyway!”
Hmm, that was true. No matter the circumstances, an adventurer could not exist separately from a guild. Even in the game, you could easily find new comrades through the guild. But...
“I’m worried about whether I can trust the people I meet through them.”

“Hahaha! It looks like you haven’t properly used it yet. It’s changed a lot from the past. Because there are a lot of cases of party members betraying their team, it is now mandatory for them to wear a video recorder.”
Really? That never happened in the game.
“Trust me and see for yourself. The worst usually doesn’t happen.”
Well, now that I’d heard that, it didn’t seem like a bad idea.
The next morning, after waking up with a slight hangover, I headed straight to the tower.
“You cannot enter without a visitor’s pass.”

Shouldn’t you ask if I have one first? I was annoyed about having to experience discrimination first thing in the morning, but when I showed them the pass that Raven gave me, the staff let me in without another word.
Ding!
I arrived on the thirty-first floor. As soon as I entered Raven’s private lab, I was greeted by an interior that was more bustling than it was two days ago.
“Oh, you’re here?”
It seemed that a lot of books and documents that had been cluttering the room had been cleared out, but instead, the room was full of terrifying-looking devices.
“...Where are you going to use this?” I asked, pointing to the scariest-looking object.
“That’s nothing special, it’s just a magic item that makes drawing blood easier.”
Her answer surprised me in two ways. Both in that this thing wasn’t designed to crush human skulls, and in that this savage device was apparently a magic item.
“Then are you ready?”
“...I don’t think so.”
“Don’t be scared. Come over here.”
“...All right.”

At first, I was half suspicious and half worried, but surprisingly, all of the examinations that used the magic tools were quite humane. Also, the process was so quick that it didn’t take long to finish. But the results themselves were no different from the information I had gathered myself while I was in jail.
“First, there’s not a big difference between the essence of a guardian and a regular essence. Oh, you know what I’m talking about, right?”
“I do.”
Essences dropped by guardians had two characteristics. The first was that their base stats were 1.5 times higher than those of a regular essence.
“Well, since you know that already, it would be best for you to see this for yourself.”

She summarized the stats of the vampire’s essence, which she had estimated using various magic tools. It wasn’t really useful, though. As expected, the paper had numbers written on it along with “high,” “middle,” “low,” and more. But I was already able to calculate the exact stats by multiplying the stats of a regular vampire by 1.5.
[Vampire
Natural Regeneration: +45
Strength: +15
Agility: +15
Mana Resistance: +30
Physical Resistance: +12
Soul Power: +21
Mana Sensitivity: +30
Dark Resistance: +12
Solar Resistance: -12]

Some people might think that those stats were low for a rank-five monster. That was definitely not untrue. The essence of the corpse golem, which was only rank seven, provided a high Pain Resistance of +70 and Bone Strength of +55. And the numbers I just gave for the vampire were multiplied by 1.5.
But Natural Regeneration, Mana Resistance, Physical Resistance, Soul Power, and even Mana Sensitivity...

The rarity of the stats themselves put this essence on a whole different level. Even in the game, these precious stats tended to be doled out in low amounts because too much of them would create a monster.
“I’m once again realizing it, but you are very lucky, Mr. Yandel. Even the essence of a regular vampire is very rare, but you have the essence of a guardian.”

In truth, “lucky” was not a strong enough word to describe it. It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to treat a guardian essence of rank five or higher as a high-rank essence. In many ways, this was definitely not something you should be able to find right off the bat.
“If you’re done looking at that, come check this out, too. I’ve listed all the special abilities just in case. There are four in total.”
Unexpectedly, the corners of my lips turned upwards. “Four, huh?”
The second key characteristic of a guardian’s essence was this: normal essences had only two skills, one passive and one active, but the essence of a guardian was different.
[(P) Source of Darkness — Grants you the ability to resist death while your heart is intact.]
[(A) Offering Imprint — Temporarily increases your physical abilities based on the number of creatures stained with your blood.]
[(A) Eternal Life — Temporarily increases your ability to regenerate in proportion to how much your health drops.]
[(A) Master of Blood — Upon directly sucking a target’s blood, you can temporarily absorb one of their skills.]

Along with the basic passive skill that came with a vampire’s essence, all available active skills were attached. Normally, in order to earn Offering Imprint you would need to consume a yellow vampire essence, and you’d need a red essence for Master of Blood. However, that didn’t matter for the essence of a guardian. The trade-off was that it was just as difficult to acquire as the two extra essences.
Now that I’ve got this and the Immortality Imprint, is it safe to say that I’m done setting up the regeneration part of my build?
My healing factor was so fast that even I, someone who had been playing this game for ten years, couldn’t believe it.
Inwardly satisfied, I heard Raven talking to herself. “Okay, that’s it for today. You did well. Come anytime next week at your convenience. I will be here no matter what.”
“But is there even anything else to look into?”
“What are you talking about? In order for the academic society to adopt this as their official data for this monster, we need to conduct research at least ten more times.”
“...I see. I was just checking because I didn’t know. Don’t be so angry.”
“I’m not angry. Anyway, I’m going to check out the corpse golem essence when I have time too, so don’t even think about ditching me halfway through.”

“...All right.” I was almost naked from the examination, so I started putting on my clothes. And, since I was already there, I asked, “Raven, do you have any plans to enter the labyrinth in the future?”
“I’m not sure. Probably not for a while... Why?”
“Ahem! Wouldn’t it be better to go with someone you know?”
Could she tell just how awkward I felt? She laughed like I’d just said something silly. “Excuse me, we’re not that close, wouldn’t you agree?”
“Never mind. Pretend you didn’t hear me.”

“I don’t want to.” Her tone became aggressive all of a sudden. Looking back, her personality had always been like this. She was usually quiet, but on occasions when her feelings were hurt, she became incredibly rude. “How could you ask me to join a party of just two barbarians? Who do you think I am?”
To be more accurate, it wasn’t even two; one had resigned yesterday. Although if I said that, this would probably take an even more brutal turn.
“...That’s why I said to pretend you didn’t hear it!”

“How can I pretend I didn’t hear something that I did?” Was this really something to get so upset about? I was wondering how I should react to her sudden distress when she let out a long sigh like she was doing some kind of breathing exercise. “Ha... Mr. Yandel. If you want to make an offer like that to a wizard, at least bring a proper party to the table. It would be nice if all of the party members were rank six or higher, and if there was a priest.”
Shit, you think I don’t know that?
If I had been in a better situation, I wouldn’t have made her an offer in the first place. “O-Okay.”
I swear, wizards and their high horses.
“Then I’m going to head out now.”

“Ah! Wait!” Raven caught Bjorn just as he was about to leave. She had remembered something she forgot to ask. “Back then! What was that back then? You put something in the vampire’s mouth while he was unconscious. I thought I sensed divine power...”

It was a question that had arisen while she had been writing down past events to pass on to her master. What was that? No matter how she looked at it, an item with divine power wasn’t something a rank nine adventurer would have.
“Hmm? I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
“Pardon?”
“Maybe you mistook it for something else since things were so hectic.”
“Mistook it? That’s not possible. I could clearly feel—”
“I’m going to get going. I have somewhere I need to be.”
“Excuse me! Wait! One se—”
Slam!
Bjorn closed the door and left before she could say anything else.
Yeah, so you are hiding something.

Staring at the place where he had been standing, she huffed and headed to the study. Then she pulled out a thick book, The Complete Book of Rifts III. It was a record filled with all the information compiled about the Rift. As the simple title implied, it was an old book that did not even have the author’s name written on it. She had purchased it on a whim at the Free Market as a child and, surprisingly, it had information inside that even the academic society didn’t have recorded.
“What page was the Bloody Citadel on...?”

As she was flipping through the pages, her hand stopped when she reached a certain part. A map of the Underground Prison, the exact location of the hidden passage... This was a page that contained advanced information about the Bloody Citadel, such as how to obtain the [Necronomicon] in the Demon Worship Room. Unfortunately, there were parts that were illegible.
[Tears of a Goddess]
Where to get it: _________.
[Golden Mask]

Years of weathering had caused the descriptions of these two items to disappear, and information on how to obtain them had also been erased. Raven had searched all over the place to find them herself, but in the end, she had been unsuccessful. She smacked her lips in disappointment and cocked her head again.
Wait, I think I’ve heard of the Tears of a Goddess somewhere before...

Where did she hear it? Searching her hazy memories, she pulled out a few religious books and quickly turned the pages one by one. Who could say how much time passed? Finally, though, her hand stopped.
[Tears of a Goddess
A consumable relic of unknown origin.

When destroyed, it has the effect of releasing a powerful Grace in a given area. During the Dimensional Collapse 150 years ago, Cardinal Androne used all three to save the Pope, and they have since disappeared from the public eye.]

“A holy relic?” Surprised, she even checked the picture drawn on the next page. It was too early to say for sure because of how far away she had been, but it seemed like it was roughly the same shape and size as the object she saw Bjorn holding. Even the method for use and effects were the same.

Raven was perplexed. There was no way that this was a simple coincidence. But if it wasn’t, how could a barbarian who had just become an adult know where the Tears of a Goddess were hidden and even think to use them in that situation?
Could it be that Mr. Yandel is...
One possibility popped into her head, and her eyes lit up as she wrapped her arms around the book.
I’ll have to look into it.
No matter how long it took, it would be worth it.

chapters.title: Chapter 45: Line (2)
paragraphs: Back at the inn, I was organizing my pack when I fell deep in thought about the metal helmet in my hand.
Do I sell this or not?

The official name of this helmet in the game was the Golden Mask, an item that could be obtained by defeating the boss monster of the Bloody Citadel and satisfying various special conditions. The effect was simple: it allowed the wearer to customize the appearance of their face for thirty days.
It’s even a consumable item with a limited number of uses.

Was it a max of five times? After that, it naturally disappeared. Of course, my memory wasn’t perfect, even more so because aside from the first time I acquired it, I’d never used this item. After that first use, I always sold it in the auction for about five hundred thousand stones.
Still... I don’t know what to do with this.

Of course, if this were the game, I wouldn’t even be worrying about this. It was obvious. An accessory? What was the point of accessorizing a 2D pixel character, and for a short time period of just thirty days? Even if the market price were ten thousand stones, it would be more useful to sell it. But right now, this was undeniably a reality. After contemplating it for a short while, I came to a decision.
You never know. I’ll just hold onto it for now. It’s not like I’m short on cash.

The situation I was in was different from a game in many ways. I had even been framed and sent to jail recently. If there came a time when this city turned against me, this item was sure to play a big role in my survival. Perhaps it could even have a different use.
After all, having money is the best.

I once again realized the importance of money. If I hadn’t made so much recently, I would definitely have chosen the option of selling it. As you can see, the more money you had, the more options you had to choose from, whether you were in a game, in reality, or even in a distant world.
“Hey! Did you hear? The Crystal Union has been disbanded!”
A silver-haired elf was quietly eating in the corner of the restaurant. Her name was Daria Whitember di Tersia, and her ears pricked upward because this was a topic of interest to her.
“What? The Crystal Union disbanded?”

The Crystal Union was a clan of adventurers that had experienced explosive growth in the past ten years by providing various conveniences to first-floor adventurers, forming an extensive communication network through countless message stones.
“Isn’t it surprising? An entire clan of run-of-the-mill adventurers evaporated overnight.”
“Ha! Run-of-the-mill? When have those adventurers ever done adventurer work?”

From what Daria had heard, the members of the Crystal Union had mostly been ordinary civilians who, under the pressure of having to pay taxes, stepped into the adventurer role. She remembered hearing that they had regular jobs in the city and just made time one day every month to enter the labyrinth. Of course, there was nothing really wrong with that. In fact, it was rather good at fulfilling its purpose. She’d heard that the union had kept many civilians from getting arrested for being unable to pay their taxes.
“Anyway, this is good news! I was starting to get sick of them calling themselves adventurers and acting all criminal.”

However, as of late, the Crystal Union had become corrupt. As their power had grown, they began rejecting outsiders and even manipulating members to commit crimes against new adventurers. Her sister had been one of them. And it wasn’t enough for them to perpetrate an unforgivable act of cruelty, they had even tried to silence her.
I hate to admit it, but if it wasn’t for that barbarian, something unthinkable would have happened.
When Daria heard Erwen’s story, she had been determined to teach them a lesson one day. But now, it seemed that wasn’t necessary. Coincidentally, it was also thanks to a barbarian.
“By the way, I forgot to ask. Why did they suddenly disband?”
“Ah, didn’t you hear the other news?”
“Other news?”
“The free barbarian!”

Secretly overhearing the story that followed, Daria’s lips twitched into an involuntary frown. It was a story that got more and more interesting as it went on. It wasn’t enough that the man had escaped from jail and cleared his name, he had even taken the district chief’s daughter hostage.
“Now that the situation has gotten so out of control, they say that the looting law that was only going to apply to rank nine explorers may even fall apart.”

It was truly an incident worthy of the buzz around it. The person who had allegedly framed the barbarian had already been hung, and even the Crystal Union, which boasted an inflated sphere of influence, seemed like it was being held accountable for its past behavior and had taken a heavy blow.
“But you know what’s even more surprising? That barbarian is apparently only a rank nine adventurer! In other words, it hasn’t even been that long since his coming-of-age ceremony!”
For some reason, the story brought one barbarian in particular to Daria’s mind, one who had acted imposing even in front of her, and had also proven to be unique in many other ways.
That would be too much of a coincidence...
She shook her head in an attempt to shake off her thoughts, then left the restaurant and went home. But with each step, she began to wonder.
Is that barbarian really dead?

So far, there had been no reason to doubt that that was the case. But if he really was the one the rumors were referring to, then that would explain why he hadn’t returned to the inn for two days. Could she really tell her younger sister about all this, though?
Click.

When she opened the door with those concerns still swirling through her head, she saw her sister, who had lost a noticeable amount of weight. Sitting on the bed with her eyes closed, she was manipulating three small flames that looked like they were on the verge of going out. Two had been her limit in the labyrinth.
“Oh, you’re here?”
“...You haven’t been summoning spirits this whole time, have you?”
“Mhm. That way I can increase my affinity with them...”

Daria’s lips thinned at those words. The training method itself wasn’t out of the ordinary. She had been the one to teach it to her sister in the first place. However, she had never pushed herself to the limit like this before.
“You know, I think I heard the voice of the fire.”
“What?”

“I get it now. How to get stronger. Why I was weak this whole time? Why I always needed help from others.” Her sister, who always averted her eyes and looked self-conscious when she spoke, looked straight into Daria’s eyes as she continued. “I wasn’t desperate enough.”

There was no life in her cracking voice, but the cynicism in it, at least, was clear. It was a spiteful anger. Finally, her younger sister had developed the one thing that she had lacked the most. It was clear what had caused this change, which was why Daria kept her mouth shut.
Even if what I’m thinking is true...now isn’t the best time to tell her.
Just like ten years ago, this was all for the sake of her precious little sister.

It was past noon when I visited the Adventurers’ Guild near the magic tower. To be honest, after the horrors I underwent here, I didn’t think I’d be back for at least a long while. But in order to proceed with the quest I had been given yesterday, I had no choice.
The guild admin worker got straight to the point without any unnecessary niceties. “What can I help you with?”
“I am looking for a teammate of my same level.”
“Are you looking for a particular role?”
I answered without hesitation. “I want to join a party active on the third floor and made up of a minimum of four people.”

As long as I was here to find a teammate, I had no intention of simply filling Ainar’s vacancy. Rather, I planned to use my promotion to rank seven to join a party with the best skills and effectively fight our way to the top.
Well, that’s assuming that there is a good party.

As soon as I handed over my identity card along with the personal information questionnaire I had filled out in advance, as was the procedure, the tired administrator flinched. Then they glanced at it several times with a strange look in their eyes. “...Five stars?”
“Is there a problem?”

“N-No!” The administrator was strangely on alert. I didn’t know what the stars meant, but for some reason, their voice was now much friendlier. “T-This is a list of teams that meet your criteria. Would you like to look at it?”
I was finished going through the list within five minutes. “It’s quite short?”
“I-I swear that among the recruitment requests that have been posted, these are the only ones that fit your criteria!”

Did I say otherwise? I had just been stating facts. I didn’t know why they were even swearing over something like this. “Hmm.” The document they printed gave a brief description of each of the fifteen teams. The first one read:
[Third Floor Exploration - Ellen Bornev
Preferred Areas of Exploration: Twilight Slope, Ironrock Hill, Jet Black Estuary
Average Rank: 7
Current Number: 2 melee human warriors (Rank 7), 1 melee beastman warrior (Rank 7), 1 melee dwarf warrior (Rank 7)
Recruiting: 1 melee warrior
*Equal distribution
*No elves
*Participation in after-battle dinner is required
*Drinking is allowed during the expedition if desired]

What the hell was this team? I had only read the description, but I could already smell the sweat dripping off of them. Shocked, I read through the other recruitment requests, but there were none that I was particularly interested in. If the party members were good, the loot distribution ratio was bad. If the distribution ratio was good, there was a problem with the team’s composition.
If I can tell just from reading the posting, it would be even worse in reality.

Perhaps finding a party would have been easier if my adventuring career had been a little longer. The furthest I’d gone was the second floor. If it wasn’t for being a so-called newbie, the range of options would have been much wider and there wouldn’t be any parties so openly trying to screw me over with the distribution ratio.
How unfortunate.
If I could, I would rather put up my own listing to find teammates, but no one would sign up in that case. And if they did, they wouldn’t be normal people.
I didn’t think I’d find one all that quickly, anyway.
“Is there a party you’d like?”
“Not today.” I returned the documents with a shake of my head, and the admin employee replied like an NPC.
“Oh, is that so? I’m sorry we couldn’t be more of a help after you’ve come all this way. If you wish, we can make your information available to other parties—”
“No thanks. I’ll come back another time.”
“Ah, is that so? I’ve been Terbes, your ever-friendly guild employee.” Their tone, words, and actions were all very friendly. Their performance was flawless too. “Goodbye, then!”
But... why did I feel so weird?
