Leaving behind the Adventurers’ Guild with mounting discomfort, I was on my way back to the inn when I ended up stopping at the corner of an alleyway because of a barbarian.
Tap.

A bushy beard, pants that were frayed and stained with dirt... most barbarians tended to act like beggars, but even taking that into consideration, this one was resting against the wall of the alleyway miserably.
What’s this?

As soon as I saw him, I was hit by a sense of wrongness. Although I stayed at a different inn, I often hung out with the other barbarians, and I knew it wasn’t necessarily strange for a barbarian to be sleeping on the street.
But... how come he has no weapon?

This was a very serious anomaly. No matter how poor, hungry, and cold they were, barbarians carried their weapons like they were their life. I normally shoved my curiosity down, but I found myself instinctively drawn to this person. What was happening?
“Hey.”

“Eeeek!” The barbarian, who had fallen asleep leaning against the wall, spotted me and was incredibly bewildered. Well, having a fear of strangers was a natural reaction for most living beings, but that was for other races. We intrepid barbarians didn’t bother with stuff like that.
Shit, is this bastard...?
That vague feeling of incongruity gradually began to take form. My heart dropped, but I quickly pulled myself together and made a list of what I had to do in my head. First, I should put him at ease.

“Don’t be afraid, I won’t hurt you.” To prove that I was friend and not foe, I pulled out a stick of jerky from my backpack and forced it into the barbarian’s hand, the greatest kindness you could show as a barbarian. Of course, he just took the jerky and didn’t eat it in front of me. However, I could see that the caution etched into his eyes had eroded at least a bit.
Well, that should be enough to have a conversation.
“What are you doing here?” I asked as soon as I got the chance.
“I-I... d-don’t have money, sir...”
I nodded silently. Barbarians had no money in the beginning, so that made sense. No, actually, it was a matter of course.
“What about your weapon?”
“I sold it, sir...”
He sold his weapon and he was using polite speech? “Let’s introduce ourselves. I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“T-Tarikan, son of R-Riyen!” Apparently realizing his mistake, he spoke louder this time, but it was already too late. I was sure now.
“Nice to meet you, Tarikan, son of Riyen!”
This guy was an evil spirit, and it hadn’t been long since he had arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 46: Line (3)
paragraphs: Tarikan Riyen. Of course, that wasn’t his real name, but anyway.
I think it would be best to get something in his mouth before we talk.

Since the inn wasn’t far, I brought him to my room and bought him a meal on the first floor. The meal was a three-hundred-stone house special for that week. Although it was just chicken stew, a few pieces of bread, and some roasted vegetables, that alone made him overjoyed. However, there was one thing bothering me.
“I will not f-forget this favor!”
Whew, what is this clumsy barbarian talk all about? I’m glad that he’s come to his senses, but if he’s going to try to speak like a barbarian, he should at least do it better.
He lacked confidence and his voice was too quiet. We barbarians were at our happiest when someone bought us food.
He eats just fine, though. Perhaps because he’s really starving?
Watching him hurriedly gobble down his food, I smiled bitterly because of what I learned after the meal was over.
To think, he’s not a newbie...

Surprisingly, this man was older than me, if only by a little. He had been called to this world a month before I had opened my eyes within Bjorn’s body. And there was one more surprising thing about him.
“CComing-of-age ceremony? Oh, that was a real surprise. W-Who would’ve thought that there was an e-evil spirit among us?”
An evil spirit, huh?

Coincidentally, this man and I shared similar beginnings. An evil spirit had appeared at his coming-of-age ceremony too. In other words, there had been an incident where a player was executed by the chieftain. One question arose in my mind at this point.
How did he survive that?

At the coming-of-age ceremony, your name was called. However, an evil spirit had no knowledge of what body it was going to be in when it opened its eyes, which was why I had had to stand there, suffocatingly tense, and count inwardly to myself each time the chieftain called out a name.
But even without that, maybe there hadn’t been anything for the chieftain to be suspicious about. Hmm, that could be the case. Or maybe he used a similar strategy to mine to avoid suspicion.
Curious, I asked a bit about this, but the answer I got in return was useless.
“What place was I during the ceremony? I don’t know why you’re asking that but... I was the last!”

I see. His had been the last name called. So he wouldn’t have needed to know his name because there would have been no other warriors left anyway. All I could think was that he was lucky, but he didn’t seem to even realize that, which slightly annoyed me.
“So what happened after that?”
“W-What do you mean? Why... do you ask?”
What do you mean why? Because I’m an evil spirit too. It’s called data collection. I deliberately kept my answer as vague as possible. “If I feel bad about what I hear, I may even help you out.”

However, in his head, he had already registered my help as a given. “I-I see! Then I’ll tell you!” He did not hide the anxiety in his eyes as he slowly began to tell his story, from the day he woke up in the body of Tarikan Riyen to today.
As I listened, I didn’t particularly feel bad for him. He had actually brought everything on himself.
“...You didn’t enter the labyrinth after the ceremony?”
“I-I had no choice! I got lost on the way...”
First, he did not enter the labyrinth. The excuse he gave was that he got lost, but...
I should probably filter that out on my end.

His actual reason was likely that the idea of fighting monsters was inconceivable to him. It would have been very easy to break away from the overexcited horde of barbarians. The problem would have been what happened next. Left behind in the city, he survived a week on stone bread, wandering around to find a job, but no one would take him because he was a barbarian.
Actually, that’s the biggest con of being a barbarian.

Other races could have multiple jobs. For example, if you went into any tavern, there were beastmen who served you, and you could occasionally find dwarves who worked as blacksmiths. They dug for mana stones on the days that the labyrinth was open and worked in the city for the rest of the month to earn money, unlike barbarians, who had no options other than combat.
“But you didn’t know that? You would have been told about that at the holy land, no?”
“Tha-that... For a while, I forgot! And oh, didn’t I tell you earlier? I got lost, so I didn’t have a choice...”
I’m saying this because I know you’re lying.

I phrased it like it was something barbarians learned while at the holy land, but in reality, I was actually saying that it was a plot point in the game that he should have known about if he had played it before.
But that’s his answer?

I was slowly starting to get suspicious. Was it really true that evil spirits were the people who had opened the Gate of the Abyss on the last level of the game? If you were skilled enough to accomplish that, you should at least know how barbarians were set up, right?
“...So, can I continue?”
“Ah, sorry. Go ahead.”

Anyway, back to the main point of the story. After starving for several days, he sold his starting weapon for fifty thousand stones. I didn’t know who the buyer was, but they really scammed him. A barbarian’s starting weapon was worth 150,000 stones on average.
Well, that’s not the important part.
He spent a month living on that small amount of money until he reached another opening of the labyrinth. That had been the same day I woke up in this body and decided to enter it myself.
“Ha! You didn’t enter the labyrinth then, either? Are you crazy?”
“But how can I fight a monster without a weapon!”
That’s why you should have just entered in the first place. You must have been a player who reached the Gate of the Abyss too, right? But you couldn’t even figure that out?
“P-Plus I ate something bad that day and had a stomachache!”
Now I’m really speechless. My head was spinning. It’s not like I can openly ask if he’s ever played the game...

Now that I thought about it, I didn’t even know if all of the evil spirits, including this man, were from the same Earth as me. Wasn’t this a world where monsters and magic existed? It could also be possible that some of the evil spirits were summoned from another strange dimension.
“Anyway, keep going.” It didn’t seem like he was going to say anything special, but I patiently heard out the rest. Of course, it didn’t deviate much from my expectations.

The money ran out, he got kicked out of the inn, and days of hunger, cold, and fighting illness ensued. One day, when he found out about the existence of the dormitory where the barbarians were staying, he went to see if he could get help, but for some reason, he was denied.
“That’s what makes you so different! Everyone else looked at me strangely.”
To be honest, he was even stranger to me. How had he managed to survive the past three months in such a half-assed way?
Should I praise him for at least figuring out that he needs to act like a barbarian?

Although I couldn’t understand all of his decisions, on one hand, I was relieved. If I had made a different choice that day if I had run away because I was scared of fighting, perhaps I would have ended up in a similar situation as this guy.
“...But how much does this place cost per day?”

Then I would have ended up on the streets instead of in an inn with a window and a private bath. Without soup to eat and unable to eat the stone bread, I would have been digging around in the trash, and I may have had to tell my sob story and rely on a stranger’s sympathy.
“Oh! So how was my story? Do you feel bad for me?”
I thought it over one more time before answering and made a decision.
“It was definitely a sad story.”

“Then will you help me?” The color instantly returned to his face. “O-Of course, I will pay you back. You may not believe it, but I know a lot about the labyrinth! If you take me along, I will be of great help to you!”
Help? To me? Judging by those words, it seems he does know a thing or two about this world...

I could even tell what kind of hopeful future he was picturing in his head. He was probably imagining journeying into the labyrinth with me as a team. He may really have been offering that to repay me, too, because he didn’t know who I really was. But I drew a line there early on.
“I will not enter the labyrinth with you.”
There is no such future. I’ve got bigger fish to fry. I can’t take dead weight into the labyrinth just because he’s in a similar situation as me. Why would I do something so crazy?
“But you said you would definitely help me!”
His voice was now tinged with a little bit of anger. I forcefully swallowed back another pained smile. “I will help you in a different way.”
“Different way?”
“Here. This is 150,000 stones. Buy a weapon with this and go into the labyrinth.”
When I took out three fifty-thousand-stone coins and placed them in his hand, his face brightened again. “Are you really just giving this to me? Thank you! I will definitely repay this favor!”

I really didn’t expect him to pay this back. Even with this money, with that kind of mindset, he wouldn’t last long. The labyrinth I had personally experienced was not a place I could easily navigate with just knowledge of the game. But I gave him 150,000 stones. I handed him the money, knowing that doing so would not do me any favors.
“I’m tired. Will you leave now?”
“Ah, I-I see! Okay! I’ll come back another—”

“Don’t come.” To make sure that fully sunk in, I lowered my voice and repeated it. “Tarikan, son of Riyen, whether you lose that money or survive the labyrinth and make a lot more, or even if things turn out well enough for you to be able to repay me...” When I approached him and grabbed his shoulder, he flinched. I could tell he was flustered by the touch, but I continued. “...The reason doesn’t matter. Once you leave this room today, do not come find me. If you understand, answer me. Do you understand?”
“...Okay.”
After hearing that, I semi-forced him out of the room. Then I stretched out on the bed and pondered what I had just done. I smirked.
What, did this situation remind me of the past?
Perhaps it reminded me of a time when I had desperately needed someone’s help. But even taking that into consideration...
I have done something sickening even in my own opinion.

A calculating person would surely find me foolish. An emotional person would think of me as crooked and question how what I did could possibly have been helpful. They weren’t wrong. I had neither the apathy needed to step away from the line nor the recklessness to cross it, so I stopped right on top of it.
I’m sure this is what you would call hypocrisy.
I closed my eyes and thought again. Even if my actions today were nothing but hypocrisy, this was the best I could do, something I would never have been able to do if I didn’t have money.
“Tarikan, live as long as you can.”
The next morning, I visited the nearby branch of the Adventurers’ Guild again. Unfortunately, the staff member who helped me today was a different person.
“Five stars...?” Just like yesterday, the expression of the employee checking my identification card changed in an instant and her responses got friendlier.
What the hell was this? Did the district chief do something to my ID? I was curious, but I didn’t manage to extract a definitive answer from the employee.
“Stars? D-Did I say something like that?”
Well, come on now, don’t pretend like you don’t know.
I didn’t dig deeper, though. It must have been something like a code used just by the guild, something to designate either a VIP or a nuisance. I suddenly wondered which side I was on.
Either way, this works better for me.
Who cared if it was good or bad? The friendly service I got as a result was the same.
“This is a list of parties that meet the criteria you mentioned. Would you like to read it, sir?”
I looked through today’s recruitment listings that fit the same criteria as yesterday. Aside from the addition of a few new parties, the contents were pretty much the same.
Will I be able to find a proper team today?
Looking through the documents with a focus on the new parties, my eyes stopped at one section in particular. A familiar name stood out.
[Third Floor Exploration - Hikurod Murad
Preferred Areas of Exploration: None, to be decided at a later meeting
Average Rank: Undefined
Current Member: 1 Close-combat dwarf warrior (Rank 7)
Recruiting: 4 people (regardless of role, may vary depending on team composition)
*Equal distribution]
The team leader’s name is Hikurod Murad? And he’s a dwarf. This doesn’t seem to be a different person with the same name...Did his previous party disband?

Whatever the reason, this wasn’t a bad option. It was a bit odd that there weren’t any other members yet, but at least I knew the team leader was quite trustworthy. I was curious which Numbers Item he got from the Bloody Citadel too.
I should at least meet up with him.

After that, I filled out a short application, submitted it to the person working admin, then left the building and headed straight for the business district. Maybe tomorrow at the earliest, or the day after at the latest, a meeting would be arranged.
So let’s spend some cash in the meantime.
I was certain that this was going to be the most fun I’d had in a while.
Uh... but have I ever had an enjoyable moment?
I decided not to worry about the minutiae.

chapters.title: Chapter 47: Teammate (1)
paragraphs: I got 230,000 stones by exchanging raw mana stones. The cost of the equipment from the blond-haired party of four was just eight hundred thousand. I received five million in settlement money from the guild, and obtained one million through blackmail. In addition, I had the thirty thousand in compensation from the innkeeper.
The Golden Mask is worth about five hundred thousand stones but... since I’m going to hold onto it, pass.
If I did the math, excluding the 300,000 I gave to Ainar and the 150,000 I threw down the drain, my current worth was...
6.61 million stones.

In truth, that number was huge. If I maintained my current lifestyle, that amount was enough for me to get by for the next three years without having to enter the labyrinth once. Of course, that calculation was based on the relatively low cost of taxes in the first few years.
If I subtract about seventy thousand stones for a sufficient standard of living, that leaves me a total budget of... 6.54 million stones.
I sped up my steps, recalling the items on the shopping list I had prepared last night. I didn’t walk to my destination, though.
“Is this wagon heading to Sector Two?”
“That’s right.”
When I arrived at the shared platform, I paid the five hundred stone fee and got on a ten-person carriage.
The actual price per person was 250 stones, but the reason I had to pay this much was because a barbarian was too big for another person to sit in the seat next to them.
God damn it.
That enraged me for some reason, probably because it was a reasonable explanation.
“We’re here.”

After sitting in my seat and falling asleep with drool running down the side of my mouth, we arrived at Sector Two, the northern region of Kommelby, the commercial district. It took about four hours. If we had been able to cross through the royal capital of Karnon, that time would have been cut in half, but with my current reputation that was impossible.

After a quick meal at a nearby restaurant, I headed to my destination using a map I had purchased in advance. Getting there was much easier than I thought. It wasn’t long before I spotted a majestic building in the distance.
[Alminus Central Exchange]

This was one of my favorite facilities to use in the game, the Central Exchange. It gave you the advantage of not having to wander through the city to sell products, and instead allowed you to find specific items much more easily. But in return, you had to pay a fee to use it.
“Are you registered for licensed sales?”
“No. I’m here to search for stuff.”
After taking a numbered ticket and waiting for a while, I submitted my pre-filled documents to the worker.
“There are a total of twelve items that meet your criteria. Would you like to check the list?”
“Of course.”
The search fee for each item was three thousand stones. After paying this and waiting for a while, the worker pulled out some papers and brought them to me.
“Once you read through those, you can tell that employee back there which items you’d like and they’ll take you to see them.”
In the game, you just had to press the Buy button, but I guess this was how it worked in real life. It made sense why there would be a fee for this kind of system. It covered the cost of labor.
Anyway, let’s read this first.
Like the other customers crowding the exchange, I sat down in an empty spot and read through the documents. There were only twelve items that met my criteria, so it didn’t take long to read them all.
“I want to see this item here.”

Having selected the item with the most reasonable price on the list, I headed to the storage area with the help of the staff. After checking for defects several times, I bought it with cash without hesitation.
[Expandable Backpack
Storage Area: 8th grade
Shape: Standard mid-size backpack
Enchantments: Automatic Organization, Individual Deposit, and Withdrawal, Lightweight (low)
Price: 2.5 million stones]

The expandable backpack was a little different from a normal subspace, but at my current budget, I was grateful to at least be able to get this. If the storage level was grade eight, it was already three times the size of my extra-large backpack.
And it comes with all three sets of magic enchantments.

All in all, it was worth it. Even if I could forgo the Automatic Organization enchantment, which stored items in the best possible arrangement, Lightweight was pretty much essential. Think about it. No matter how wide the space in the bag was, if the weight of the items inside remained the same, it would be useless.
On that note, it’s the same for putting things in and taking them out easily.

This was an expandable backpack I had bought for convenience. However, if there were no way to put an item in and easily get it out of the bag, you’d have to do last-in, first-out and take them out in the order you put them in.
It was already so inconvenient in the game, but in the real world, it would be no joke.

It was a bit disappointing that it was a backpack and not another type of bag, but I shouldn’t get greedy. I decided to be satisfied with this, and with the purchased backpack in hand, I returned to the spot I was sitting before. Then I continued to search for other items. My remaining budget was about four million stones.
[You are wearing an Expandable Backpack. Inventory has significantly increased.]
Now that I’d taken care of convenience, it was time to raise my actual combat power.

Four million stones. It was a huge amount, enough to fit you with a full set of iron armor or raise you to level three of the [Immortality Imprint.] Neither option was bad, but I didn’t choose either of them. That was because the situation now was different.
[(P) Source of Darkness — Grants you the ability to resist death while your heart is intact.]

I now had the essence of a vampire that I had not been planning for. Thanks to that, I had a body that would not die as long as my heart was intact. In other words, strengthening the Immortality Imprint or buying things like fitted gaiters would inevitably have a low efficiency-to-cost ratio. After much deliberation, I made my final decision.
Raise the tier of the equipment instead.
In other words, instead of iron, which was a grade one metal, I decided to purchase equipment made from a grade two metal, commonly referred to as the upper tier.
[You are wearing a lithinum breastplate. Your Item Level has increased by +270.]
Lithinum: a grade-two metal that is two times lighter and stronger than iron. Its most notable characteristics were its white color and ridiculously expensive price.
It’s 1.91 million stones for one breastplate...
The breastplate I purchased through the exchange had the same shape as the iron half-armor I had sold for scrap metal, but the price was over five times higher.
True, I mean, you need to be at least a fourth-floor adventurer to use a second-grade metal, so that’s pretty obvious.

Of the equipment for various body parts I could have purchased, my reason for choosing a breastplate was pretty simple: the more my heart was kept safe and protected, the greater the benefit of the passive skill Source of Darkness. Either way, safety was paramount, so there was no debate about the breastplate. However, for the second piece of equipment, I was thinking it through until the moment I finalized the purchase.
[You are wearing a large battle shield made of lithinum. Your Item Level has increased by +315.]

Should I replace my weapon or my shield, which had been sold for the price of scrap metal? After much deliberation, I paid 2.1 million stones to purchase a shield. There were many reasons for that, but the main one was because I had no reason to deal damage now. So far, I’d only entered the labyrinth in duos. However, heading to a higher floor required team play with a minimum of four people. That meant it was far more efficient for me to hold a shield and become a human barrier that protected the party.
The vampire’s essence is not the essence of someone in a damage dealer role.
Above all, unlike a weapon, a shield was a piece of equipment that I could continue to use even after obtaining that essence. And without a shield, I felt like something was missing.
At this point, my wallet was completely empty.
Hmm, the equipment is starting to shine now.
When I looked in the mirror, my heart was filled with a deep satisfaction. Was that also a change that came with becoming a barbarian?
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 3
Physique: 155
Spirit: 90
Special Ability: 115
Item Level: 683 (New +585)
General Combat Power: 527.75 (New +146.25)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7 / Vampire (Guardian) - Rank 5]

By the time I finished my reasonable spending spree, it was already dinnertime. Having had dinner at the same restaurant where I had lunch, I took the wagon back to Sector Thirteen, where my inn was located. After that, the day was over.
It takes too long to travel...

Later, once I really made a lot of money, I’d have to relocate to the city center. Living on the outskirts came with many inconveniences. Even though this new inn was a little closer to the center, I still had a long way to go to get to Dimension Square.
At the end of the day, everything is about money...
As I’d spent a lot today, I went to sleep with a determination to earn more money.
Then, the next morning, like a diligent barbarian, I went to the library first thing.
I’ve taken care of the things I need to deal with immediately, so I should head there again.

It was a habit of Korean gamers to do manual labor in their spare time. Well, this was manual labor that I could do because this was reality and not a game. I still lacked the common sense and common knowledge of this world.
On that note, it would be nice to find a house near the library too.
Books were food for the soul. The reason I was able to make such smart purchases at the exchange in the first place was that I’d been reading about it at the library.
What was the title of that book?

I couldn’t remember, but it recorded the average trading price of items on the exchange for the past ten years. It was hard to read because there were so many numbers, but there was no better textbook to learn market prices than that book.

As I walked around, my thoughts wandering, I arrived at my destination. Nothing had changed from my last visit: the scent of books emanating from the entire building, the skinny nerds who arrived even earlier than I did, and the librarian sitting at the counter with a sleepy look on her face.
“Long time no see.”
As I greeted her just like I did the last time I saw her, the librarian glanced up and gave me a strange look. Then, she mumbled, “...How?”
Oh, did she notice this stuff? “Haha, it’s a lithinum breastplate and shield. It came out to a total of four million stones. Ah, and this on my back is an Expandable Backpack—”
“Parsytiev.”

Hmm, humorless as always. I left behind the librarian and her chronic fatigue. She started to doze off again after casting the spell on me, and I headed into the library. Because of the quality equipment I was wearing, I could feel more eyes on me than usual. Most of them had a look of awe. Well, actually, I couldn’t be sure exactly what the looks meant, but any other possible looks were embarrassing so I just decided to assume it was awe.
...Was coming to the library in full armor a little too much? Possibly. But who cares? I am a barbarian.

I decided to stop caring and do my own work. With some keywords in mind, I pulled out a bunch of books: Establishment and Development of the Adventurers’ Guild, Casebook on the Judgment of Plunderers III, Reading Comprehension of Legal Vocabulary, Birth of Mozlan. After being framed and almost killed, my interest in the Adventurers’ Guild, the institutions directly under the crown, and the law increased. There was a famous saying in the gaming world:
What you don’t know gets you hit. So, you have to learn whatever you can.
Growl!

After going out to eat every four hours and returning to the library to read, another day came to a close. I decided to read the books I hadn’t had a chance to read yet tomorrow and returned to the inn. A letter had arrived for me, which had never happened before. The sender was the Adventurers’ Guild. Inside, the letter said that Hikurod Murad wanted to meet with me.
I guess I can’t go to the library tomorrow.
After wiping down my shield and breastplate with a dry cloth for about an hour, I lay down on the bed and fell asleep.
I had time to spare this morning, so I slept in more than usual. It was a little past noon when I lightly bathed myself and headed to the meeting place.
Ding!

The shop doubled as an inn, a restaurant, and a tavern. Entering the hall on the first floor, I could see quite a few people having their meals and chatting. Scanning the interior for a while, I finally found the person I was looking for. Dwarfs were so small that they were hard to spot. I wished they would just eat standing up. Wasn’t it the same either way?
“It’s been a while, Hikurod.”

“Ha! It really was you! The application was marked as rank seven, so I wasn’t sure—” The dwarf, who had been in the middle of greeting me with a smile, was startled at the sight of me. “Wait, what is that equipment?”

Oh, so you noticed it too. I decided to reply like it was no big deal. “Oh, this? As you can see from its shiny brilliance, it’s a piece of lithinum armor and a shield. And this on my back is called an Expandable Backpack. It’s nothing. Just something I bought for next time.”
Really, it was nothing.

chapters.title: Chapter 48: Teammate (2)
paragraphs: After a moment of silence and much contemplation, the dwarf, who had been hesitating to speak, opened his mouth. “I-I see?” His reaction was one of both bewilderment and surprise.
“What are you so surprised about? You must have at least one of these!”
“That’s true, but... Was your personality always like this?”

Well, I didn’t know what this guy thought he knew about me, but that was enough embarrassment for today. With the dwarf’s expertise, he should have gotten a feel for the quality of my equipment just from that information alone.
With this, he won’t be able to try any funny business with the distribution ratio despite my short career.

Of course, the recruitment posting clearly stated “equal distribution,” but I still remembered the dwarf’s angry eyes at the Bloody Citadel, calling me greedy when I said I would concede all the other loot for the Rift stone.
After all, he is an adventurer.
If he started looking down on me now, there would be no end to it.

Without asking if I could sit down, I sat across from him and declared, “Hikurod, you buy the drinks, since you earned the Numbers Item thanks to me.” The comment both showed off my skills and reminded him of his debt to me.

“What? Hahaha! Is that how it is?” The dwarf just laughed loudly and didn’t deny it. He couldn’t, because I was the one who’d made the greatest contribution at the Bloody Citadel. “Well, that’s not wrong! It’s a bit early, but I can buy you as many drinks as you want. Let’s catch up while we drink!”
“All right.”
It looked like it would take some time until the food we ordered arrived, so we naturally started chugging down our drinks first. Then we got to the real matter at hand.

It was the dwarf who first brought it up. “When I found out it was you who submitted the application, I was very surprised. What the hell happened? Was there some kind of treasure hidden in that Rift? I was sure that wizard girl had looked everywhere.” Unsurprisingly, the questions came pouring in. That made sense given my current appearance, although I didn’t have enough loyalty to him yet to provide an honest answer to any of them.
“Something like that.”
“What does that mean? Give me more details!”
“As you said, there was a treasure. That’s it. Don’t ask any more questions.”

When I drew the line, the dwarf looked disappointed, but I guess he realized that it was going to be difficult to get an answer out of me. “I don’t know what kind of treasure you found, but you are very lucky.”

Lucky? This guy was the one who had benefited the most from the Bloody Citadel in the first place. I almost died in there. All he had done was the work of one person before taking the Numbers Item and getting the hell out of there.
I’m curious what got dropped... I should ask about it later.
Our plates started arriving, so the rest of the conversation happened as we filled our stomachs.
First, I should lead with this.
“So, have you found any party members yet?”
“Not anyone who interests me. You’re the first one I’ve actually met with.”
“I see.” Nodding, I got straight to the point, just like a barbarian. This was the real objective of this meeting. “So, what are you going to do?” Would Hikurod Murad accept me as a party member?

“Um, that’s... Until just a few minutes ago, I mostly just came out here to check that it was really you. Apart from building a party, I mostly wanted to speak with you. Ah, also, I’ve written down floor three, but with the right people, I plan to go to the fourth floor too...”

It was a needlessly long explanation. Just saying that he’d had no intention of accepting me onto his team would’ve been enough. “So, have you changed your mind now?” I asked, staring at him intently.

“Ahem, you could say that,” the dwarf responded while stroking his beard. “After all, who would look at you now and think you’re a beginner? If it wasn’t for the fact that it would be difficult to recruit the rest of the party if a beginner joined, I wouldn’t have even worried about bringing you on in the first place!”

Instead of making such poor excuses, I wondered if it would’ve been better for him to just tell me that in the first place. However, the lack of that kind of craftiness was one of the things that made dwarves so attractive. “Then are we done here?”
“Hahaha! You could say that.”
When I picked up my glass, the dwarf followed suit. “I hope we’ll work well together again.”
Thus, a party was formed. There were still only two of us but when it came to that part, I’d just have to pretend to discuss it with him while recruiting members that suited my own tastes.
“Hikurod, didn’t you say earlier that a lot of people applied?”
“I did.”
“Who were they?”
“You don’t have to worry about that. They were just rank-eight greenhorns without even a year’s experience.”
What is this? An indirect insult?

While I was seriously mulling that over, the dwarf suddenly opened his mouth like he’d just remembered something. “Oh! I forgot to ask! How did you level up so quickly? It wouldn’t be easy to get a rank seven ranking with just a corpse golem’s essence.”

“Just the corpse golem’s essence?” I realized my mistake immediately after the words came out of my mouth. Right. He was passed out when it happened so he didn’t know that I had the essence of the vampire. Would it be okay to just tell him something like that?
I was deep in thought when suddenly, the dwarf shouted, “Aha! I see! Haha! I didn’t think that far ahead! True, equipment like that would surely bring you up to rank seven!”
Ah, uh, um... That’s a plausible guess, but... “Yeah, something like that.”

Now that he’d already thrown that out there, I decided I would keep that particular fact to myself. It was not like the party had officially been formed yet, and I couldn’t know what kind of people were going to join later. It was best to plan for everything. Someday, this essence may become my trump card.
I can just say my ability to regenerate comes from the Immortality Imprint.
With the most important matter of business dealt with, we continued to drink and converse. Through that, I was able to find out why the dwarf had left his previous party to recruit another.
“As you know, I left my party for a brief period recently.”
“You did.” I heard that he had applied for a leave of absence in the hopes of entering a Rift.

“But when I tried to return, they were more interested in the warrior they recruited temporarily to fill my empty spot!” The dwarf then furiously spat out his anger toward his former comrades, but I could not empathize with him at all.
The fact that he left his party for personal reasons is the real problem, no?

The biggest victim in this situation was his former team leader. Whilst planning for their upcoming expedition, the dwarf suddenly took a break, leaving him scrambling. Maybe if the replacement warrior they recruited ended up having issues, things would have turned out differently. But if they were better?
If I were that team leader, I wouldn’t accept this selfish dwarf back into my party, either. He’s sure to act up again.
Of course, I kept that to myself.
“My gosh, what disloyal bastards, don’t you think?”

“That’s right. It sounds like they don’t know what loyalty is!” In these situations, I learned that unconditional agreement was the best way to go. Maintaining the act, I decided to ask about the thing I was really curious about. “I don’t know how great they are, but if they found out about the item you obtained during your last trip, I’m sure they’d regret it for the rest of their lives!”
“What I obtained?”
“The Numbers Item!”

“Ahh! Come to think of it, that’s right! If I run into them later, I have to let them know how foolish they were!” The dwarf seemed to already be picturing that in his mind. After taking a swig of his drink, he burst into laughter.
Nice, that seemed like a natural transition, right? “So, I wanted to ask...” I started cautiously. “What did you get?”
“Hmm, have I not told you yet?”
“You haven’t!”

It was something I’d been curious about since we reunited. I knew all the Numbers Items that could possibly be dropped, but what I had cleared was an unprecedented Rift. Perhaps a unique item had appeared, just like the mysterious box that Raven had left open in the boss room.
Come to think of it, I didn’t ask what was in that.
I decided to ask her about it when we saw each other next week.
The dwarf grinned and set his thick arm on the table. “This wrist guard is what I got from it.”
Hmm, I couldn’t get a feel for it just by looking at it. “What’s its name?”
“The appraiser at the guild said it’s called a Guardian’s Wrist Guard.”
“Shut up.” That came out?
“...Hmm? Do you know of it?”
“O-Oh, no. I was just surprised at how cool the name was.”
“Hahaha! We have something in common after all! I thought so too!”

No. 3112: Guardian’s Wrist Guard was a Numbers Item belonging to the 3000s, which could usually only be obtained from the Rifts on the fourth floor or higher. Its actual effects were of secondary importance. How much did this thing cost, again?
“I checked the price through the Central Exchange and it seems to be worth around fifty million stones.”
Damn it all. Was I being messed with? What exactly did this dwarf bastard do in that Rift to deserve this?

“Hahaha! They even said that was the old price, and it could be more expensive now since there’s almost no stock for sale! Of course, I have no intention of selling it!” He paused when I didn’t reply. “Uh, hey, why are you so quiet all of a sudden?”
“It’s nothing. I’m... just... surprised, that’s all.” To be honest, I was so surprised that my stomach, filled with alcohol and meat, was starting to ache unbearably.
“I understand. Fifty million stones? I thought I was going to faint when I first heard it, so you must be too.”
Was this what it meant to sow the wind and reap the whirlwind? Now that I had seen this, my showing off earlier was nothing compared to this bastard dwarf’s.
“Don’t be too jealous. If you keep on exploring, you’ll find a Numbers Item someday too. Of course, it won’t compare to the one I have! Hahaha!”
Avoiding the gaze of the smiling dwarf, I slowly lowered my hand under the table.
Slide.
It was the hand wearing No. 9425: Ring of the Frost Spirit.

A karma wrist guard? Fifty million stones? I decided to think as positively as possible. The minor issue of my insides turning to the point that I wanted to throw up could be overlooked. After all, it was a good thing to have a strong teammate.
Let’s just focus on building a party.

Calming myself with this thought, the next thing I did was raise this dwarf guy’s adventurer ranking one level higher. In order to find good teammates, we first had to look like an attractive party. There was a huge gap between a team leader being rank seven and being rank six, one that couldn’t be put into words.
“Hikurod, go to the guild today and raise your adventurer rank as soon as possible.”
“...Why so suddenly?”
“Don’t you have fifty million stones’ worth of equipment? If you apply for a review, the guild will definitely take it seriously!”
“But, it’s too sudden—”
“So you don’t want to?”
“No, it’s not like that...”
“Then, let’s go!”

I even followed him to the guild and watched him submit the application just in case he tried to slip away. For reference, it took six days for the results of the evaluation to come back, a little more than what I had expected, but fortunately, the rank promotion was successful. As a result, the skills of the applicants we received greatly increased from this point on. More than ten applications arrived every day.
I carefully reviewed the applicants with the dwarf. We were in the middle of a spirited discussion when suddenly, a wizard’s application arrived.
“A w-wizard?”
Of course, it wasn’t a wizard from the Tower—it was instead a rank eight wizard who was likely working in a guild, or perhaps a public institution. But it was a wizard nonetheless.
“Hey, Bjorn, is this some kind of mistake? Why would a wizard be applying for our team?”
“It definitely is strange. There should be a lot of parties with more attractive conditions than ours.”
“What should we do, then?”
A few things about this were a bit fishy, but we decided to meet with the wizard anyway and communicated this to the guild. That morning, finally, a place and time for the meeting were set.
“They won’t ask for half of the earnings, will they? They say all wizards are very entitled...”
I didn’t know what was making Hikurod so nervous. He had defended his share of the profits against Raven, who was a member of the Tower, without being cowed in the slightest.
“What are you so worried about? If they make a request like that, we can just say ‘no thanks’ and leave.”
“R-Right?”

Was it because this was the first wizard he was meeting as a team leader? While I was reassuring Hikurod, who was bouncing his leg without pause and getting worked up, a robed man entered the tavern. When he saw us, he waved.
“Oi, you there! Barbarian! Dwarf!”

Shit, was this another landmine? How could you piss someone off with such a short greeting? I could already sense a catastrophe waiting to happen, but just in case, I decided to observe him a little longer before making a judgment.
“Hahaha! Nice to meet you, are you the wizard we’re meeting today?”
“What is the probability of you meeting another wizard by chance at the exact same time and place?”
At the bastard’s question, the dwarf looked at me in bewilderment. I couldn’t help but sigh. “Ha... He means you’re right.”
“R-right? Hahaha! Anyway, nice to meet you, my name is Hikurod Murad!”
“What an odd name. I am a Riol Warb Dwalkie, a rank eight and Rafdonian royal family-approved wizard.”
“...Rafdonian royal family-approved?” asked Hikurod.
Why are you so surprised? “That means he works in a public institution as an administrator, not a guild.”
“Ahh, I-I see?”
The wizard jerk kept speaking in tongues, but the dwarf who kept falling for it each time was also starting to get on my nerves.
The wizard laughed. “Haha! Even though you’re a barbarian, you’re very knowledgeable. What’s your name?”

“Bjorn, son of Yandel. Sit down.” I had originally been planning to just observe, but feeling frustrated, I decided to lead the conversation myself. That would save more time. “Dwalkie, I read your application. I have a few questions that I would like to ask. Is that all right?”
“Of course.”
“Do you have a labyrinth pass?”
“Would I have come if I didn’t?”
Just say yes, man. “One more thing, why would you want to be an adventurer if you can already make enough money in the city?”

It was rare for a rank eight wizard to go on an expedition. The reason for that was simple: they weren’t skilled enough to operate in the middle floors or higher, but exploring the lower floors didn’t make much money. The income they could earn by working for a public institution was much higher. Considering how hard it was to get a labyrinth pass and the risk involved, in many ways, it was not worth the money.

“Hmm, that’s an unexpected question.” Dwalkie cocked his head and continued, “It’s simple. I want to become a great adventurer and bring glory to our Baron Martoin.” He expressed his aspiration proudly with a face full of confidence.
Hikurod, who had been quietly listening to this, promptly freaked out. “B-Baron? Could it be that you’re a n-noble? No, er, are you a nobleman... sir?”
Nobility. Rafdonia’s most powerful, and individuals an ordinary person may never encounter in their entire life.

Hikurod’s reaction was apparently quite satisfying because Dwalkie burst into laughter. “Hahaha, my mother’s sister, Aunt Enka, is married to a man who is the one and only Baroness Martoin’s third youngest brother,” he said proudly. At that, the dwarf took in a deep breath like he was about to faint. Dwalkie patted him on the shoulder like he understood completely, a kind smile on his lips. “Don’t be so nervous. I have no intention of using my status to mistreat anyone.”
Seeing that smile, I thought to myself, This guy... could it be that he’s a nutcase?

chapters.title: Chapter 49: Teammate (3)
paragraphs: With his polished appearance, delicate blond hair, height of around 5′5″, and scrawny figure, Riol Warb Dwalkie—a rank-eight wizard who dealt in lifestyle and administrative magic, along with some curses and cold magic—was a man who reeked of fraud the more he spoke.
Fuck, is he even a wizard?

Doubting this, I tested him a bit, but surprisingly, he really was a wizard. Looking back, he hadn’t actually lied. He only said that his uncle was the baroness’s third brother; he didn’t say he was a nobleman himself. Well, he probably knew his place and that impersonating a noble was a felony that could lead straight to a quick execution.
“So, how about it? Do I pass?”
After much deliberation, we decided to add him to the party. “...From now on, you will be our teammate.”
“Haha! How great. Since this is my first expedition, I wanted to join a party with as many warriors as possible.”

His two major flaws were a personality full of bravado and hot air and zero experience in the labyrinth, but still. He was a wizard. He didn’t request a bigger cut of the loot and he even said that he would follow orders once we were in the labyrinth, so this seemed to be enough to keep him content.
After all, when something is cheap, it’s for a reason.
Plus, if it became known that there was a wizard on our team, the specs of the new applicants would obviously get even better. That was because you couldn’t see a wizard’s personality on paper.
“Once the rest of the party has been recruited, we’ll contact you.”
“All right. I’ll see you then.”
Once Dwalkie left, Hikurod, who had been frozen for the entirety of the conversation, let out a long breath. “Isn’t it amazing? That a wizard, even a nobleman, could be that humble...”
“Hikurod,” I replied, utterly sincere, “you are much more amazing.” It was 100 percent the truth.
My subsequent routine in the city was simple. Aside from visiting Raven’s lab once a week, I got up at 7 a.m., grabbed a bite to eat, and went straight to the library.
“Parsytiev.”
“Have a nice day.”
If I counted the last time I was here, I had been coming to the library almost every day for the past two months, but I had never had a proper conversation with this librarian lady.
Growl!

After grabbing a meal every four hours between books, it soon became time for the library to close. Today, I had an appointment. I was about to leave a little earlier than closing time when the librarian suddenly spoke to me.
“I have something to ask you.”
“...What is it?”
“Why do you always wear your armor to the library?”
Oh, so that was what she was curious about. I gave an honest answer. “What if someone steals it from my room at the inn?”
“...If that’s the reason, I understand.” As soon as I was done answering, the librarian closed her eyes as if her business with me was now over.
Feeling like I was losing for some reason, I tossed in my own two cents. “I thought you were completely indifferent to others, but I guess that isn’t the case, huh.”
A bit of displeasure appeared on the librarian’s face. “We’ve been receiving many complaints from the library’s other patrons. That they can’t read because you’re too distracting.”
“...I-I see?”
“Yes. So, if your business here is over, will you please stop disturbing me and leave?”
Disturbing? You’re just going to fall asleep as soon as I leave.

I wanted to say that, but if I kept bothering her and ended up banned from the library, I’d be the only one getting screwed. I pretty much ran out of the library and headed to the meeting place a little past 9 p.m.
“Over here! Bjorn! Why are you so late today?”
“I’m sorry, I couldn’t find you because you’re too small.”
“Hahaha! More jokes! Come sit down!”
I was meeting up with Hikurod pretty often in the evenings, about three to four times a week. Of course, the purpose of these meetings was not just to be friendly, but to discuss the party.
“So, how was the person you met with this time?”
“He was a serious and reliable fellow.”
“No, not that. How were his skills?”
“Oh! It wasn’t as bad as I’d feared. He’s had a long career as an adventurer, and I believe he can pull his weight in any situation.”
“I see.”

“So I ask... What do you think?” After thinking it over for a while, I nodded, and Hikurod’s face brightened. “Phew, that’s a relief. I was worried you’d say no again since we don’t have much time left.”
In that breath, I could feel the pain of the dwarf, who was practically the team’s puppet leader. True, he would have been the one to suffer the most if I’d said no.
Time for a compliment. It wasn’t like it cost money, right? “You did great, Hikurod. You’re a great team leader. I’m glad I chose you.”
“Hahaha! Is that right?”

“Of course. Is there any other team leader who respects the opinions of his team members like you do? Don’t lose your focus and just do exactly what you are doing now. Then, unlike that idiot who kicked you out, you will become a great leader.”
“Haha! What flattery, my friend! I was worried about trying to play this role for the first time, but I’m glad to have you with me!”
My heart soared at those words. Once, Hikurod had complained about my frequent attempts to meddle. To think he had become such a great leader. “On that note, you buy the drinks today!”
“...Again? Didn’t I buy last time too?”
“Again, a good team leader shouldn’t be stingy with these kinds of things!”
“I-It’s not that I’m being stingy!”
There was exactly one week left before the labyrinth opened.
“Darn it! I’ll buy it today! We finally have all the party members we need—what’s the harm in paying for some drinks?”
Finally, the party was complete.
There was a difference between games and reality. You couldn’t enter the labyrinth just because you had a complete party. There were other things you needed to deal with first.

First, everyone should get acquainted and discuss how many floors to climb, which areas to focus on while hunting, and, as was appropriate for adventurers who were practically the embodiment of money, have a heated discussion about whether the ratio of loot distribution was fair. If after that there were still no problems, you had to officially register the party with the guild. Then you had to train with each other almost every day, finalize the plans for the expedition, and more.
It flew by before I even realized it. My busiest week since waking up in Bjorn Yandel’s body had passed, and the long-awaited moment had arrived.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
The Crystal Cave on the first floor of the labyrinth was surrounded by brightly colored lights.
“Oh! So this is a labyrinth!”
Unlike my bygone days spent alone or in a duo, there were five men and women in our circle including myself. They were my new teammates, with whom I was going on this expedition.
“Leait!” shouted Dwalkie as he cast a spell.
“Ah! Fuck! My eyes!” The name of this scrawny blond wizard who had shot light into our eyes before they could even adjust was Riol Warb Dwalkie. In short: Dwalkie the Weasel.
“This son of a—”
Before I could cuss him out in annoyance, the dwarf beat me to it. “Dwalkie, save your magic as much as possible.”
“Mm, but it’s so dark!”
“In the labyrinth, this is considered bright. If it’s really dark, we can light a torch.”
“Okay then. All right.”

This was a change that had occurred in the previous weeks. Hikurod had soon realized that Dwalkie was not a noble and began to handle him with ease. Somehow, they became quite friendly. The dwarf pretended otherwise, but each time the weasel goofed, he went all tsundere and helped him out. That was their relationship dynamic.
“Why did you pack so much in here? Are you trying to make it obvious that you’re a beginner? Give it to me. I’ll put it in my bag.”
“I will not decline your thoughtful offer.”
While Hikurod was taking care of Dwalkie as usual, I heard a high-pitched, cheerful-sounding voice. “Captain, shouldn’t we get moving?”

As was obvious from the triangular ears on her head, Missha Karlstein was a beastwoman. She was twenty-five, and she had five years of experience as an adventurer as of this year. Her height was around 5′6″, with a long, skinny figure. Combined with her lofty expression, she exuded a cold vibe.
“Stop playing around and let’s go. I want to smash some monsterrr heads.”
Her odd, cat-like way of speaking seemed more pronounced than most. She claimed that it was an inevitable result of the way her body was built. Ah, and one more thing about her was...
“Haha! How can I refuse the princess’s command!”
“Eeet! I told you not to call me purrrincess!”
“But, you’re the daughter of the chieftain of the Red Cat Tribe, how could I—”
“I’ll kill you! You dwarrrf!”

Missha was a princess of the Red Cat Tribe, one of the Big Five. Did she say she was the thirteenth or the fifteenth...? I couldn’t remember where she was in the birth order. In any case, there was no need for special treatment or anything like that. She was only a princess in the eyes of human society, not her own.
On the contrary, there was someone else to be careful about. “Hikurod, stop it. Even if it’s a joke, she doesn’t like it.”

Brown Rotmiller. Race: Human. Age: 34. He was rank seven, but with eight years of experience. No matter how meritocratic the adventuring industry may have been, he was the most experienced of us all, which was why the dwarf always backed off at Brown’s words.
“Ahem, I was a bit much, wasn’t I? I will be more careful in the future.”
“Serves you right, dwarrrf—”
“The same goes for you, Miss Karlstein. No matter how mad you are, is it reasonable to threaten to kill your team leader?”
“...I’m sorrry...”

Personally, I liked him the best. In a way, he was the only normal person on this team. As true as that was, however, there was a disadvantage to not being able to jerk him around like the other party members.
“Hikurod, can we depart before it gets too late?”
“Ah, please.”
“From now on, everyone, follow behind me,” Brown ordered.
But Dwalkie spoke up just as we were about to leave. “Wait, wouldn’t it be better for Bjorn or Hikurod to take the lead? They’re warriors, after all...”
“We’ll need their help from the third floor onward, but before that, we’ll be fine with just me.”
Honestly, I didn’t know what this punk was so worried about. Brown was a professional scout who had survived in the labyrinth for eight years.
Even though his adventurer ranking is low compared to the time he’s spent in here...

I had a high opinion of him for that. Eight years was long enough to go through all sorts of things in the labyrinth, so to still be as hale as him was amazing—a product not of his combat power, but his use of his other strengths.
It must have been the result of his seriousness and refusal to bend for any reason.

Afterward, guided by Brown, we finally reached our destination, smashing the monsters that occasionally appeared on the way. The outermost part of the first floor was often called the dark zone. Even though we ran here, took the shortest route, and didn’t get lost, the portal had already been opened by other adventurers.
“Of course. People got here earlier this time as well.”
“Don’t blame yourself. You’ve done enough.”
“Hikurod, that is no reason not to work hard. If you don’t feel frustrated by your own shortcomings, that means your life as an adventurer is over.”
“I-Is that so?”

For reference, it had taken about ten hours to get here. I couldn’t say this in front of the ever-passionate Brown, but this was a very good performance for the average party of adventurers. It was not like we were a speedrunning team after the portal-opening experience points. To be honest, I hadn’t expected him to find the portal so easily.
If his navigation is this good as a non-guide...
While I was beginning to look forward to his other as-yet-unseen abilities, a kind of regret also filled me.
If it were Ainar or Erwen with me, they could’ve earned the experience points for opening the portal.

By using the dimensional instability phenomenon I had reduced to a bug, it was possible to get guaranteed portal-opening experience points. However, this method could only be used when you could ensure secrecy with a promise or an oath.
That’s for later... when the party is truly reliable. After all, experience points aren’t an urgent issue right now.
Taking a deep breath to shake off any remaining regrets, Hikurod shouted, “Come on then, let’s go inside!” The dwarf stepped into the portal first, and I followed immediately after.
Please, I hope nothing bad happens this time...
But was that too much to ask for?
[You have entered the Den of Beasts on the second floor.]
The adventure had officially begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 50: Teammate (4)
paragraphs: In order to be able to retain your teammates, having the right skills was very important. However, there were other virtues that were just as important, like trust. In other words, were they reliable? Of course, when things were going smoothly, this wasn’t exactly a problem. In that case, everyone could just laugh and smile and be happy. But when things weren’t like that? Whether you could trust your teammates to have your back during the worst possible scenario was a whole other issue.
It may not even be about trust, but their true character.

These were the sorts of things that you couldn’t learn about another person no matter how many times you read their application or chatted with them. A person’s true nature was hidden deep within. I hoped we would never have to show each other our true selves. That would be better for everyone.
“No matter how many times I come here, I can’t get used to the smell! Hahaha!” Hikurod laughed. “Dwalkie, are you okay?”
“Please don’t talk to me—!”

Turning away from the nauseous Dwalkie, I quickly scanned our surroundings. I was currently in a sector on the second floor that was inhabited by blade wolves and could only be accessed through the eastern portal on the first floor: the Den of Beasts. As the name implied, it was mostly populated by beast-type monsters, which was probably why it smelled bad. Really bad.
“Rotmiller, are you okay? I heard you have an essence that affects your nose.”
“Thank you for your concern, but I’m fine. It’s not my first time here.”
“I see.” Was this the ease of an eight-year adventurer? This man gave me peace of mind just by looking at him. Although there was someone else I needed to keep a bit of a closer eye on.

“By the way, when will our wizarrrd come to his senses? I need to go make some money...” Missha showed no empathy toward her teammate’s suffering and only cared about her own interests. I was about to add another note to the character evaluation tab open in my head when I paused.
Hmm, am I the same way, though?
“Dwalkie, snap out of it. How much more time are you going to waste?” I snapped, going off on him.
“Right, right. If you’re feeling sick from something as minor as this, you can’t be an adventurerrr. Grow up, wizard!” Missha immediately agreed with a teasing tone.
However, Dwalkie had an unexpected reaction to hearing this. “You’re right. I need to be an adult now.”
Uh, had he always been like this? To be honest, I figured he’d just make up some ridiculous excuse or get angry in response.
“Let’s go,” Dwalkie continued.
“B-But are you orkay?”
“It definitely isn’t easy. But how pathetic is it to become a burden to my party just because it’s my first time here and I’m a wizard?”
Missha was startled by the unexpected apology. “I didn’t say you were a burrrden...”
Dwalkie stood up, looking much more haggard than earlier and wearing a look of determination on his face. “I cannot bring disgrace to the name of Baron Martoin,” he grunted.
“...Eeet! Are you pretending to be a nobleman again?! I won’t fall for that anymorrre!”
“Hahaha! Let’s hurry. I’m really fine now!”
At the sight of him acting all cheerful like he’d been fine from the beginning, Missha got angry, realizing she had fallen for his prank again. With that, we slowly started advancing.
“From here on, everyone, please follow me,” Brown announced. “Although it looks flat, this is an area with many pits.”
Hikurod looked around. “Pits? I don’t see any...”
“They’re usually filled with filth, so it’ll be hard to tell. But if you don’t watch your step, it’s easy to fall in.”
“...Rotmiller, we trust you.”
The Den of Beasts had a canyon terrain with narrow paths and high-soaring cliffs on both sides. Explorers who crossed this map had to wander between the maze-like cliffs to find their way.
Although there are no traps, having a scout is even more important on this floor.

For reference, the monsters that appeared here were blade wolves, wall-mole rats, saber tigers, werewolves, and vulkars, and most of them lived in the caves on the cliffs. It was common for adventurers whose main goal was hunting to enter a cave and do a sweep of the monsters inside. However, our objective was to reach the third floor, so pass.
[You have killed a Giant Blade Wolf. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Saber Tiger. EXP +2]
[You have killed a Werewolf. EXP +2]
[You have killed a Wall-Mole Rat. EXP +1]
Moving quickly, we killed the monsters hanging outside the caves on the way, and soon it was time for a break. There were three hours left until the start of the second day.
We had spent the entire day crossing the map, but it would have taken twice as long to get here without Brown, the scout.
“The entrance is narrow. This would be a good campground,” Brown said with a nod.

We cleared out a wall mole rat’s den and started preparing it as the base for our camp. Hikurod, Brown, and Missha were adventurers with years of experience, so the process of setting up camp was instantaneous. Even Dwalkie, who had made no contributions other than creating drinking water until now, shone a light on them.
“Since we have alarm magic, one person should be sufficient for the night watch,” said Brown.
“Why do we need a night watch?”

“Dwalkie, it’s not because I don’t trust you, so don’t get offended. As you know, it’s not just monsters that you need to be wary of in the labyrinth.” In order to become a proper adventurer, you had to be on the lookout for fellow adventurers as well.
“Brown can take the first watch since he has done the most work today, and afterward we can take turns,” Hikurod offered.
“Wait, do I have to stand watch?” asked Dwalkie.
“Leave that stuff to us. You get some rest,” Hikurod assured him.

The wizard was excluded from night watch duty. It wasn’t out of consideration for his low stamina, but because it was customary. Adventurers rewarded others according to merit, and the alarm spell was counted as one person’s share of the work.
Well, in truth, this custom probably came about from having to go along with a wizard’s whims.

Anyway, having one person stand watch every two hours made for an unbelievably comfortable night. To think I would be getting six hours of sleep... Compared to working as a duo, it was like heaven on earth. Of course, it came with the disadvantage of having to share a proportional cut of the loot, but that could be balanced out by hunting more, stronger monsters.
“I am... the great wizard Riol...”
“Stop sleep-talking and wake up, wizard!” Missha shouted.
“...Is it morning already?”
“I don’t know about that, but I know it’s time to wake up.”

Day two, 5 a.m. Despite my concerns, the first night went by without a hitch. Monsters were detected by the alarm spell four times during Hikurod’s watch and we were once approached by a group of adventurers, which led to all of us waking up, but that was the norm.
“Since Dwalkie has adjusted to the labyrinth now, we’ll increase our speed a little,” Brown announced.
“Is there a need to rush?” Dwalkie asked.
“It’s better to arrive on the third floor as early as possible to set up camp.”
On the second day, we reduced the amount of unnecessary chatter and focused solely on moving. Of course, every few minutes, monsters came to block our way, but I welcomed the interruption.
[You have killed a Moon Rock Bear. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Queen Wall Mole. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Bloody Blade Wolf. EXP +1]
At this point, I had killed all the rank-nine monsters in the den. Since this was my first time here, my experience points accumulated quickly. Of course, I didn’t have an EXP bar to refer to.
But if I count all the monsters I’ve caught so far...
It was exactly forty. If the High-Rank Mutant Kill Bonus and the Guardian Kill Bonus were added, that made forty-four EXP.
I still have a long way to go before I reach level four.
As one’s level went up, the required amount of experience points you needed to accumulate increased exponentially.

Level 1 required 6 points; level 2, 30 points; level 3, 150. Of course, it didn’t always increase by five times each level, but it was safe to say that the difficulty felt even greater each time. It was only a +1 EXP increase for a higher-rank monster, but if there were no monsters you could hunt, even getting them became impossible.
Well... it’s not like I’m in a hurry to level up.

My current level was three; I was now able to absorb up to three essences. In other words, I still had space for one more. Of course, I didn’t expect another essence to come out before I hit level four. Dungeon and Stone wasn’t such a user-friendly game.
Of all the games, why did I have to play one like this?
I was starting to regret my choices but to no avail. After all, I was the freak who felt more alive the higher the difficulty was.
“Everyone, get ready,” Brown called. “From this point on, we’ll be seeing high-rank species and their numbers will increase dramatically.”
We had spent half a day following right behind Brown. The terrain—to be precise, the color of the cliffs—had changed from reddish brown to black.
Is this the start of the second half?
No rank-nine monsters appeared here. However, no one, including me, was very nervous about that.
“It’s still just rank-eight monsters on the second floorrr!” Missha rumbled.

Our party had an average rank of seven. Whatever teams they had been a part of in the past, they would have been active at least on the third floor. Well, I was a beginner, but I was an exception because I’d been here numerous times while playing the game.
“By the way, Bjorn, you haven’t been on the third floorrr yet, right?” Missha added.
“So?”
My response was headstrong, as I expected her to pick a fight, but Missha expressed genuine admiration instead. “Amazing. It took me a full year to reach the third floorrr!”
That made me feel bad for how I’d acted. “...I was just lucky.” I didn’t want to dwell on this topic for long so I kept my answer vague.
Then Hikurod entered the conversation. “One year for the third floor? So how long did it take you to get to the fourth floor?”
“Um, two yearrrs? I think it took that long.”
“Same as me.”
“Eeet! That’s not fairrr! You have less experience than me but you’re a rank six!”
“Instead, Miss Karlstein was born into a good family!”
“Eeet! I told you not to talk about my family!”

Sensing the conversation was about to turn into another long argument, Brown took a step back from navigating and interrupted. “Both of you, stop it.” His voice and expression were the same as before, but why could I sense that he was more annoyed this time?
True, if I heard them bickering while I was busy working in the front, I’d also get pissed off.
I brushed it off without much thought.
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]

A little past noon on the second day, we entered the third floor thanks to the accurate directions we had received from Brown. It was a bit disappointing that I hadn’t been able to catch many of the huntable rank-eight monsters in the Den of Beasts, but they weren’t just active on the second floor.
I’ll get another chance someday.
Shaking off the disappointment, I focused on the current situation. “Rotmiller! Get out of the way!”

I was currently on the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor. In particular, I was at Ironrock Hill, the starting point that connected the third floor to the Den of Beasts. Immediately upon entering, we encountered two rank-seven monsters.
“Dwalkie! Use corrosion magic!”
It was easy to think of the Iron Tusk as a wild warthog with iron molars. Though, it was about five times the size of a wild warthog on Mount Jiri.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-8 spell Corrosion.]

While Brown, the first to enter the portal, avoided the monster and retreated, Dwalkie immediately cast a spell. Right after that, Hikurod and I dashed forward and each took on a monster with our shields.
Bam!
A heavy shock jolted through the shield. My old shield would have dented at the moment of impact like the dwarf’s was doing right now.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Emergency Restoration.]
“Bjorn, why are you looking at me all of a sudden? I am not jealous.”
“Sure. If you used a hard shield in the first place, you wouldn’t have to repair it every time.”
“What are you talking about? Anyway, Bjorn! Don’t push them away, just stop them from stepping back!”
“You don’t have to tell me twice!”
The Iron Tusk’s active skill was Balance Weight. Its effect was Knockback Immunity. This also happened to be the essence Hikurod had.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Balance Weight.]
Do you have no shame?

A wild warthog cub with a main skill just like that one, and the dwarf was ordering me not to get pushed back by one of them? The rage inherent to this barbarian body welled up inside of me. Maybe that was why instead of waiting for the other party members to attack, I swung my mace and smacked the Iron Tusk’s jaw.
“Behelaaa!”
Kak kak kak!
The steel molars that had been affected by Corrosion were shattered with a single blow.
“Come to me, essence!” Missha, who leaped off of my back without permission, stuck a dagger into the Iron Tusk’s head.
[You have killed an Iron Tusk. EXP +3]
That made one for now. I was going to take care of the other one next, but I stopped and watched for a bit. Dwalkie was casting a spell, one of the few offensive ones he had.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-8 spell, Ice Lance.]
An ice skewer flew into the Iron Tusk’s stomach. If it had pierced the head or the heart it would have been a one-shot kill... But more detailed feedback could wait until later.
Stab!

The battle ended with Brown approaching the falling Iron Tusk, holding a crossbow to its forehead, and firing an arrow. Of course, no essence came out, although that wasn’t something to worry about right now.
A monster right in front of the portal?
It seemed the son of a bitch was nearby.

chapters.title: Chapter 51: Team Half-Wit (1)
paragraphs: “Rotmiller, is there anyone nearby?”
Could he have had similar suspicions? Brown closed his eyes, then opened them without a word. His pupils were contracted as he looked around.
[Brown Rotmiller has cast Thermal Search.]

Thermal Search was an ability that Lizardman Scouts had. Its effects were similar to a modern-day thermal imaging camera. It was a pretty useful skill in the game as well. Whether the enemy used Conceal or something else, this one skill could see through everything.
“There is no one nearby,” Brown replied shortly, deactivating the ability. “But judging from the smell, it looks like someone was here not too long ago.”
As this was the opinion of someone with two essences that adjusted his olfactory stat, the possibility of him being wrong was low. I asked him a few more questions. “How long ago, do you think?”
“I can’t be certain, but this much of a scent means it hasn’t been more than two minutes.”
“That means they must have left after seeing us fight, right?”
“...That’s right.” Rotmiller nodded with a grim look on his face.
Hikurod, who had been listening quietly to the conversation, interrupted, startled. “Wait, then someone was targeting us on purpose?”

Brown did not deny it. “Probably not us, exactly. They would’ve been waiting for anyone to pass by.” He went on to explain that luring monsters in front of portals was a technique often used by plunderers, a low-risk method employed by those groups.
They sure are good at pulling tricks.

Using monsters to ambush a party was a way to take advantage of the moment when the adventurers who had just crossed the portal were most vulnerable. A total party kill would be the best outcome for the plunderers, one or two injured was pretty good, and if the party happened to get out unscathed, the ambushers just had to retreat for a bit and lie in wait for their next prey.
“Rotmiller! Shouldn’t we find them and finish them off? Killing looters is a moneymakerrr!” shouted Missha.

“Even if we were to do that, they will be difficult to track down. It’s not like we can just wait around here... Plus, there’s no evidence. We cannot rule out the possibility that we may end up being framed in return.”
“Eeet, the dead don’t talk!” Missha huffed angrily when Brown finished up his explanation, but the dwarf then stepped in and made a cool-headed decision as the team leader.
“In the name of good conscience, let’s go back to the second floor to leave a sign warning people about the looters in front of the portal before we go.”
I agreed. “That’s a wise decision.”

After that, we did the bare minimum any adventurer was expected to do and left the portal behind. On the way, we continued to discuss the topic of plunderers. However, the more I listened, the stranger things sounded.
“Brown is grrreat. Until now, I didn’t even know they used tactics like that.”
“I’ve only heard talk of it before,” Hikurod said with a nod. “This is the first time I’ve been subjected to this trick.”
“True, it’s not every day that you run into a plunderrrer!”
Uh, what the hell are you guys talking about?
I felt alienated by the other adventurers’ talk and found it difficult to empathize with, so I asked about it. At which point I learned something shocking.
“Me? I’ve run into maybe eight of them in the past five years. Once, it was my own teammate, and the rest were all good-forrr-nothings!”
“Only eight times in five years? Shit, isn’t running into looters a daily thing for adventurers?”
“Definitely not... I heard that was the case about 150 yearrrs ago, though!”

Missha added that after the death of the first king, also known as the Immortal King, various policies were put into place that greatly reduced the number of looters. However, I couldn’t accept this explanation. There had to be some kind of mistake. Otherwise, I couldn’t make sense of it.
Once in the Crystal Cave, once in the Goblin Forest, twice in the Land of the Dead...
Including today, I had come across five plunderers in the past three months.
So what does that say about me?
When I told them this to get their opinion on it, everyone, including Brown, gave me a strange look.
“How many sins did Bjorrrn commit in his past life?”
“Hahaha! Maybe it’s your fault that we ran into a plunderer today!”
I really had nothing to say to that. What kind of life had I been living?
As I walked in silence, unable to muster the energy to refute them, Brown sighed and opened his mouth. “Everyone, stop teasing. We all know that Miss Karlstein is one of the lucky ones, right?”
“Ah! That’s tr—!”
“I also tend to see plunderers about once every three months. So don’t worry too much.”
Ah, uh— um... Thanks for the comforting words, but that’s not five in three months.
[You have killed a Wormstone. EXP +2]
[You have killed an Iron Falcon. EXP +2]
[You have killed an Ironrock Hill Guardian Soldier. EXP +2]

Third floor, Pilgrim’s Path. Whether you passed through the Land of the Dead, the Goblin Forest, or the Den of Beasts, you inevitably ended up on this level. The starting point was different for each route, though, so in order to run into adventurers coming from a different path, you had to follow the road to the fourth portal at the center of the map.
It takes around three to four days to reach the center on average...

For reference, that was the minimum time required for travel. To that end, the scale of the third floor was incomparable to that of the other floors. While the name of the floor itself was Pilgrim’s Path, the areas here were referred to by the names of the monsters that inhabited them. I was currently at Ironrock Hill.
“We will camp here today, and tomorrow we will move on to the next area.”
On the ambiguous border between where one region ended and another began, we started setting up camp. As this was an area where monster territories overlapped, only a few monsters showed up.
“By the way, Dwalkie, are you okay?” Hikurod asked. “You’ve looked off for a while.” The dwarf spread out a sleeping bag, wrapping up his preparations for the night.
Brown, Missha, and I pretended not to be listening. We were curious why this usually talkative bastard looked like he’d stepped on dog poo.
“Maybe I’m wrong, but that’s how it seemed to me.”

“I see...” Dwalkie flashed a bitter smile and nodded. After hesitating for a moment, he soon spoke his mind. “I know what I’m going to sound like. I probably seem naïve and immature to you. But... To be honest, I was shocked earlier.”
“Shocked?”
“I guess it would be more accurate to say that I’ve been disillusioned. I’ve been hearing stories about adventurers ever since I was young but... I was never told stuff like that.”

‘Stuff like that’ being adventurers who killed other adventurers; on top of that, another adventurer who spoke of making money by killing said adventurers. It was certainly not a reality full of sunshine and rainbows.
“Eeet, that was a joke!” cried Missha.
“Whether it was a joke or not, if I continue to work as an adventurer, I will one day kill another person, right?”

At that, everyone in the party shut their mouths. Anything we said to try to comfort him here would be a lie. Hikurod, Missha, Brown, and I had all killed someone before. If Dwalkie continued on in this career, he would inevitably go through the same thing one day.
“So I’ve made up my mind. The whole time we were traveling here, I kept thinking about it...”
Hearing his determined muttering, I asked, “And your verdict? Have you decided you’ll do it?”

“I have. But... I don’t know if I’ll be able to do it when the moment actually comes.” Dwalkie’s resolve was full of contradictions. He had no confidence in himself, just fear of what could potentially happen in the future.
