However... I thought it was actually better that way. “That is enough.” Better to be honest than to be one of those idiots who rattled off promises that they couldn’t keep, and then whined that they couldn’t do it.

Perhaps he had a similar thought, because Brown, who was listening to the conversation, said, “It is important not to be overconfident in yourself. To me, what you just said sounds a lot more reliable than just saying ‘I can do it.’”
“I-Is that so?”

Dwalkie’s bashful expression made a warm smile appear on Brown’s face, almost like he was looking at a young man following in his footsteps. “You’re aware that it is something you’ll have to do, and you’re even determined to do it. If that’s the case, I’m sure you will be able to follow through when the moment arrives.”
“I hope that really is the case...”
“Hahaha! Cheer up, my friend!” The conversation finally ended when Hikurod slapped Dwalkie on the back.

However, after we planned out the night shifts and just as we were about to go to bed, Brown suddenly summoned the party. “Wait. Can you all give me a bit of your time? I know getting as much rest as possible is the most beneficial thing for us right now, but I have something I want to show you.”
“What is it?”
At my question, Brown looked at Dwalkie and said, “That this profession isn’t only full of difficult and terrible things.”

Soon after, Brown checked his watch and moved to the edge of the cliff near the campsite. We followed without knowing what was going on. All we could see was the usual darkness of the labyrinth that swallowed light itself and always obstructed an explorer’s vision.
“You have something to show us?” asked Missha.
“Wait,” Brown answered while looking at his watch. “It’ll only take a moment.”

As I watched Brown, I had a guess as to what he was referring to, so I took out my own watch. It was 23:59, one minute before the start of day three, when the monster population peaked. The second hand moved with a ticking sound. Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five...

I closed the watch and stared into the darkness at the opposing cliff. Before long, a silver sphere of light appeared in the distance, and soon there were too many little lights to count. Starting from the ground, they all fluttered like dandelion seeds and drifted up toward the sky. The dark labyrinth gradually brightened around us. It was then that I understood why this place was called Ironrock Hill.
“It’s a view that only adventurers who get here early enough can see,” Brown explained. “Isn’t it wonderful?”

Even within the labyrinth, this place was considered a highland. It was usually dark, so it was hard to tell, but now that countless lights were clearing away the darkness, the entirety of the spacious third floor could be seen at once. Mountains and fields with a river flowing through them, a dense forest, and a high, towering spire reaching toward the ceiling in the center... It was a sight that I would never have gotten to see if I had lived my whole life within the walls of Rafdonia.
Dwalkie stared blankly at the lights and murmured, “...I think I can sort of understand now why adventurers always call it a big world.”
I raised my head to look up. It was a closed ceiling, but at that moment, it felt like I was really seeing a clear night sky, and one filled with the Milky Way at that.
Of course, it was just for a fleeting moment. It took only a minute or so for the spheres of light that had lifted off the ground to reach the ceiling and completely disappear.
“No one knows why this only happens on the third floor.”

There were many hypotheses about this: come the third day, the labyrinth dimension grew oversaturated with mana that then had to be released, or it was a blessing from god. Everyone chose what they wanted to believe, but Brown set the record straight.
“Whatever the explanation, the truth is that whoever sees this sight no longer wonders the reason why.”
“That’s right! I’ve only ever heard of this—it’s my firrrst time seeing it! Normally, I would have been fast asleep in my sleeping bag!”
“Hahaha! I have a feeling that my friend here won’t be able to sleep tonight.”

After that, the lights completely disappeared, and a familiar darkness enveloped the labyrinth again. Aside from me, as I was taking the first watch, everyone got into their sleeping bags and fell asleep.
It was only a long while later that I could finally hear the sound of breathing from Dwalkie’s bed.

It was daybreak, not that our surroundings were actually bright. But time-wise, it was morning, 8:10. After clearing up our campsite, we walked downhill for a long time and left Ironrock Hill. Soon we reached our first destination.
“Now, from here on is the Orc Colony,” Brown announced.
Among the various regions on the third floor, this was the one most populated with monsters. Its key characteristic was that only rank eight or higher monsters appeared here.
Unless we’re planning to head up to the fourth floor right away, there are no better hunting grounds.

The difficulty level was the second-highest of the different regions on the third floor, but if my calculations were correct, we shouldn’t have any major trouble. With these party members, we were more than capable of being active even on the fourth floor. We had a wizard, and aside from myself, the rest of the team were adventurers previously active on the fourth floor.
“So let’s work on our fighting techniques for a while here and decide what to do next based on the results,” Brown suggested.
After rearranging our formation, we stepped into the large bushes. The rearrangement only involved sending Brown to the back and me and Hikurod to the front.
“Hikurod, there is a group of orcs coming at one o’clock.”
Like any popular hunting ground with a high population of monsters, even though we were still on the outskirts, we managed to encounter a group of orcs after only walking a little while.
“Ch-chwiik!” It was a basic gang of four orc warriors, one archer, and one sorcerer.
“Just do as we practiced!” Hikurod yelled.

We got into the formation we had drilled previously: Formation A. Hikurod and I protected the front, and Missha, as the close-combat damage dealer, went back and forth between our shields to close in on the enemies at the very front first.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight spell, Ice Lance.]

Orcs didn’t necessarily require curse-type spells, so Dwalkie was focused on attack. The same went for Brown. He focused on using his crossbow to provide rear support during the battle. However, he also took on one other role.
[The Orc Sorcerer has cast Frenzy. The Physical Resistance of the Orc Warriors has increased by 3x for 10 seconds.]
In case a monster ignored the wall of shields and headed to the back of our formation, he had to protect Dwalkie, the most vulnerable one of us all.
“It’s a Frenzy spell! Be careful!”
“Dwalkie, stay behind me!”
“Okay!”

One of the orc warriors who was in a Frenzy state ignored us and rushed toward Dwalkie, but Brown pulled out a shield to block them. Of course, as a scout, he didn’t have the physical ability to defeat an orc warrior one-on-one.
“Whew, that was a close call!”

But he just had to use his main weapon, his crossbow, or a buckler, dagger, or gasoline bomb to buy a little time. After that, either Missha could come to their aid, or Dwalkie could cast an attack spell.
[You have killed an Orc Warrior. EXP +2]
[You have killed an Orc Archer. EXP +2]
[You have killed an Orc Sorcerer. EXP +2]
So, our first battle against orcs ended smoothly. The total time taken was about eight minutes and there had been no injuries, but the time used up by the battle was longer than expected.
We’re definitely lacking damage dealers.

In addition to a scout, we had two shield warriors, and orcs were among the rank-eight monsters with fairly high physical resistance. Of course, we had a wizard on our team, and they were considered the most dignified damage dealers in this universe... But Dwalkie was not from the Magic Tower. The only rank-eight attack spell he knew was Ice Lance, which could inflict damage on a single monster.
Well, we brought him here for his curse spells rather than his attack magic in the first place.

The value of a wizard didn’t just lie in having powerful attack magic. There was something commonly referred to as “compatibility” between adventurers and the monsters they fought. However, if there was a wizard on the team, it was possible for the party to battle monsters of a much more diverse nature.
It took a while, but we’re pretty reliable.
It had its pitfalls, but all of this combined made a pretty great party.
“Then let’s go further in.”
Afterward, we fought toward the center of the orc colony. The more we fought, the more orcs appeared in each group. Once, there was even a rank-seven Mighty Orc Warrior in the mix.
[You have killed a Mighty Orc Warrior. EXP +3]

This, too, we took down without difficulty. However, shit always happened when everything seemed to be going smoothly. This time, it happened when we had just found our footing and were slaughtering orcs left and right.
“Ihenro Teuntine.”
Suddenly, we heard a low-pitched chanting from some bushes in the distance.
Kaboom!
A flaming meteorite promptly fell and blew up the orc horde we were hunting.
“...The fuck?”
What kind of bullshit situation was I in now?

chapters.title: Chapter 52: Team Half-Wit (2)
paragraphs: Whoosh!
The heat of the meteor could be felt even from thirty feet away and the acrid scent burned our noses.
Thump!
As soon as my brain processed the situation, my heart tightened.
If that thing had fallen on our heads... It would’ve been game over for all of us.
“P-Prepare for battle!”
The moment Hikurod—who had momentarily blanked out from the abrupt turn of events—shouted, adventurers appeared from the bushes. Four people were closing ranks around one wizard.
Fuck, they clearly don’t belong on the third floor. Why are these assholes here?

As I was inwardly praying that they were not plunderers, a beastman with triangular ears smirked at our battle formation and spoke in an arrogant tone. “This orc colony is the domain of the Dzarwi clan. Go somewhere else.”
Clan? No wonder... they all had the same seal on their chest.
Damn it all...
I couldn’t stop myself from cursing. Not because I couldn’t understand what these people were doing, but because they were controlling a hunting ground on the third floor.
Shit, doesn’t that only happen from the fifth floor on?

Dungeon and Stone was a single-player game, but surprisingly, it had a control function. At first, the game seemed to prevent movement between maps during a quest, but once you created a clan later down the line, the player was able to oversee a hunting ground. Of course, a huge amount of manpower went into this, so it was a losing game unless done inside a select few rare monster or boss monster territories.
But they’re doing it on the third floor?
I couldn’t understand it. I mean, what were they going to gain by dominating rank-seven monsters? Just look at that wizard. Using a high-ranking person like that just to catch orcs was a waste.
Hikurod also seemed to have no idea what was going on. “I know that the Dzarwi are active above the sixth floor. But why are your people in an orc colony?” he asked carefully.
The answer we got in return was a cold, “We have no reason to explain anything to you.”

Aha, I see. I could understand that, but apparently the dwarf couldn’t. Even though we had shown each other a lot of our more idiotic sides since joining up as a party, this man was still an adventurer. He was perceptive when it came to matters related to self-interest, especially if the reasons behind them were external rather than internal.

The dwarf laid out his doubts in a logical and orderly manner. “I’ve heard that the royal family grants some clans rights in the labyrinth in recognition of their achievements. But I’ve never heard of this place being Clan Dzarwi’s territory. Moreover, I cannot be certain that you are actually a part of said clan.”

It was definitely a sensible argument. It was clear from their equipment and the level of that spell just now that they were much more experienced adventurers than we were, but there was no proof that they were part of the clan that they claimed to be.
However... I think we should just bounce in this situation...
Honestly, I was more worried that they weren’t Dzarwi. Large clans were usually conscious of public opinion, but these impersonating bastards wouldn’t care about that in the least.
The beastman glared at Hikurod, his expression displeased. “You tell an amusing tale.”
Hikurod didn’t back down. “I often get told that.”
As a silent battle for dominance resumed, the tension continued to go up.
Step.
I felt someone come up behind me. When I checked, it was none other than Missha. Why was she right behind me all of a sudden? Almost like she was hiding or avoiding something...
“Are you... Wait, Half-wit?” the beastman asked with a frown. I felt a flinch behind me. What the heck, was she actually hiding?
“B-Brotherrr...” Missha stuttered, slowly walking out from behind me.
This made the beastman’s frown deepen. “I told you not to call me that in public.”
“S-Sorrry.”
“And you still talk like a half-wit, huh.”
Missha didn’t respond to the beastman’s taunt and just dropped her head. As I suspected, he was not calling her a half-wit affectionately.
But what’s their relationship? Could they really be family?
As I was pondering this, the wizard standing behind him asked the question that sated my curiosity. “Just wondering, but is that lady your younger sister?”
The beastman politely nodded his head. “Yes, for now.”
The wizard stroked his shiny beard. “Hmm, I am indebted to Sir Karlstein. And if she’s your younger sister, she can’t be called a stranger, so as a special exception—”
“There’s no need.”
“Hm? But—”

The beastman once again firmly refused the wizard’s attempt to be considerate. “Father will not care either. I can’t tell you the reason why because it’s personal business,” he said coldly, a stubbornness in his tone.

“All right, if you say so.” The wizard promptly changed his mind and nodded his head without another word. But maybe he thought we deserved an explanation. “Look here, men.” He stepped forward and spoke persuasively. “Due to the clan’s internal workings, we urgently need the essence of a Mighty Orc Warrior. If things go well, you will be able to hunt here after the next cycle, so just go hunt somewhere else this time. Or go to the outskirts where there are no mighty warriors.”
Maybe it was because he was a wizard, but his tone was much softer than the beastman’s. Anyway, he was still essentially telling us to get lost.

“I will decline.” Hikurod shook his head and ridiculed his opponent in a sharp tone that was quite out of character. “It seems that you are claiming rights over this land without the royal family’s official recognition, so why should we have to play along with your clan’s internal issues? And did you know that what you’re doing right now is illegal in the first place?”

“...Illegal?” That seemed to strike a nerve. The gentle wizard’s eyes sharpened. “A wise adventurer would know when to be careful with his words.” But he didn’t seem to want to invite trouble later on. “When did we break the law? We were just being considerate and letting you know it’d be best for you to hunt somewhere else since there won’t be any monsters left for you to hunt here.”
Although he was beating around the bush, what he meant by that was that if we didn’t leave, they would hunt in full force so as to interfere with our own hunt.
Picking up on this as well, Hikurod bit his lip, an angry expression on his face. “Damn it...”
Unless we were forced out or injured, these sorts of situations were not governed by labyrinth laws. In other words, there would be no legal precedent to support our case.
Trying to rely on the law is a problem in the first place.

I felt bad for Hikurod, who was trying his best to protect our party’s interests, but I had wanted to back out of this from the beginning. The labyrinth was a place where the words of the powerful became law. If you forgot that and kicked up a fuss, you might disappear without a trace.
He’s probably realized by now that this isn’t the time to be prideful, so it’d be smart to coax him to step back.
At the exact moment that I decided to stop observing and act, Dwalkie suddenly interrupted out of nowhere, blurting out words that made no sense. “Don’t worry, all of you. I’ll take care of this.”
Take care of it? What the hell is this kid saying?
I didn’t even have an inkling. Before I could ask him to explain the meaning behind his words, however, Dwalkie approached the wizard on the other side with a smile. “Hahaha! Nice to meet you, sir.”
“...Sir? Have we met?”
“No, but as a fellow student devoting their life to the study of magic—”
“That’s enough. So, who are you?”

Dwalkie hadn’t expected such a harsh reaction. He paused for a moment, then replied with a forced smile, “My name is Riol Warb Dwalkie. I am a rank-eight wizard and public service worker under the Rafdonian royal—”
“Aha, so you’re trash.”
“...Pardon?”

A look of displeasure appeared on the wizard’s face. He appeared even more displeased than he had been when the word “illegal” was mentioned, and he seemed to have no intention of hiding it. “The study of magic? Devoting your life? Is that something a piece of trash who’s only memorized a few basic spells and makes a living exploiting the name of wizardry on the street should be saying? Your shamelessness is giving me goosebumps, so I implore you not to go around saying things like that.” The sharp accusations shot out like rapid cannon fire.
Is it because he’s a wizard? Even his choice of words is no joke.
Even as I admired the wizard’s fast-paced, nonstop rant, I was worried about Dwalkie. If someone said that to my face, I think my soul would leave my body too.
“...Urgh!”

Oh, it already left. When I looked to the side, I saw that Dwalkie seemed to be unable to breathe properly and was only barely managing to blink his eyes. The way his mouth opened and closed repeatedly was almost reminiscent of a fish that had just been thrown into the sand.
Hikurod, witnessing his best friend’s mental breakdown, could not take it and exploded. “Hey! That’s too harsh!”
“I only spoke the truth.”
“What? The truth?” A stiff vein bulged out on the dwarf’s neck and his eyes were shining with an uncharacteristically murderous energy. “Why you—!”

As soon as I detected this, I grabbed Hikurod by the neck and lifted him up. Then I immediately confiscated the battle hammer in his hand. As expected, a tingling sensation transferred to my fingertips.
Chhhhh!
[Hikurod Murad has cast Lightning.]
Fuck, had this bastard lost his mind? I stamped down my anger as much as possible and lowered my voice. “Snap out of it, Hikurod,” I muttered.
We almost all died just now.
“You have a great teammate,” said the enemy wizard. “Be forever grateful to that barbarian. He just saved all of you.”

Had Hikurod finally come back to his senses? He didn’t respond to the wizard’s provocations and hurriedly led the party away. As soon as we reached the outskirts of the orcs’ territory, he gave us a tense bow. “I’m sorry. I lost my temper and my reason. As he said, if it wasn’t for Bjorn...”
We would probably have all been dead. Those guys didn’t seem benevolent enough to kindly send someone who had attacked them first on their way.
“You just did something rash that almost led everyone in your party to their downfall,” Brown rebuked, his tone strong.
“...I have nothing to say.” Acknowledging his mistake, the dwarf bowed his head instead of making excuses.

To be honest, I wished Brown hadn’t stopped there and had scolded him even more. However, he was too soft-hearted to play the role of commander-in-chief. “But nothing ended up happening as a result, so I won’t say anything else. You may have been rash, but I personally think it is a good thing to stand up for your teammates when they are being looked down on.”
I couldn’t understand that at all. Instead of cursing him out, he was complimenting the dwarf.
Shouldn’t we at least cut his share and make him work for free during this quest?

Mistakes should come with punishments. Only then would people not make the same mistakes. My heart was already set on that realistic plan I had come up with, but the mood wasn’t right for me to bring it up.
Shit, am I the weird one here?
When Brown generously forgave the dwarf, the vibe in the group grew strange. It was hard to describe, but it was the kind of mood I’d been most uncomfortable with ever since I was young.
“...I’m sorry, too. If it wasn’t for me, things may have worked out betterrr.” Missha was the first to get swept up in the moment.

“T-That isn’t true!” The second to follow was Dwalkie. He was startled by Missha’s self-blame and waved both his arms to dismiss those claims. He then spoke in a stuttering, but steadfast voice. “I-I... Of course, I’m not always right, but... I think it was thanks to you that we at least got to hear the reason we were getting kicked out! So don’t ever think like that!”

It wasn’t the best reassurance in the world, but the emotions blended into it were sincere and came across to everyone. Perhaps that was the reason Missha started talking about herself out of nowhere.

“Do you know... why I hate talking about my family? I am treated like I’m invisible at home. Some of you might alrrready know why that is.” Missha watched us for our reaction. Brown seemed to know what she was talking about, because he looked away first, and I looked away after him.

Elves dealt with spirits, dwarves had the blessing of arms that increased their efficiency when dealing with Numbers Items, and barbarians had the Spirit Imprint. In addition to their unusually high base Agility stat, beastmen also had other racial characteristics.
“I’m the only one in my family who couldn’t sign a contract with ourrr soul beast.”

The beastmen were able to make contracts with ancient beasts. There were many different types. They could summon soul beasts to fight alongside them, increase their physical abilities with a power-up, or use a special ability possessed by their beast through blessings.

Of course, not all beastmen were able to do this. Only a few talented beastmen were chosen by a soul beast. But the problem here was that she was a blood relative of the chieftain, a direct line of the Karlstein family. In other words, it was a big problem for a pureblooded woman like her to not be able to handle a soul beast. It was not simply a matter of whether she had talent, but circumstantial evidence that could fuel speculation about her bloodline.

“When I was young, I got along well with my siblings. But it all changed when I couldn’t make a contrrract with a soul beast, even after I became an adult. Everyone called me a half-wit, said that I share only half their blood...”

In other words, they accused her of being a child born of infidelity. Since her mother died early, no one could know for sure what the truth was, and Missha could not stand the looks she would get and left home. Then she focused solely on martial arts and slowly climbed the ranks as an adventurer.

“Thank you for telling us such a difficult story.” When the short but painful explanation was over with, Hikurod patted Missha on the shoulder, looking unusually solemn. Missha was no longer as on edge as before. Now, she was more like a domesticated cat.
“Hikurod... you rrreally think of us as your comrades and fight for us.”
Huh, is that what we’re going with?
All this emotion continued to get harder and harder for a pessimist like me to understand.

Missha’s confession seemed to move the dwarf, because he began to calmly tell his own life story. “Hahaha! Since you said all that, I should tell you my story too. It was my dream to become a blacksmith. But because I didn’t have the talent for it, I held the title of apprentice for ten years. That’s why I only became an adventurer after thirty! I had to make money, so I figured it was the right time to quit.”

Next was Dwalkie. “T-There’s no one worse than me when it comes to being incompetent. Although I was able to break into the world of magic due to my family’s wealth, I was not able to join the Magic Tower due to my lack of talent. If only I were a true wizard... That guy would have respected me at least a little bit.”

Dwalkie then revealed that his goal was to advance his studies in magic by earning money as an adventurer. I thought this was the end of the conversation when Brown, who had been silent this whole time, smiled and stoked the fire.

“I’ve been in several parties so far, but this is the first time I’ve been in a situation like this. I also have something to apologize for. When Hikurod and Miss Karlstein were talking about their years of experience the other day, I couldn’t help feeling a surge of anger.”
“Is that what that was?”
“Yes. And the reason for that was my ugly jealousy. At the time, not knowing you each had your own reasons, I thought you two were complaining far too much for people born as other species.”

Human adventurers had advantages of their own. For instance, they could use auras, or become elementalists, wizards, or priests. Some grew to be as large as barbarians. In fact, they had the strengths of all races. But in the end, that was only in terms of potential, and only a select few actually ended up having special talents.
Hikurod smiled a clumsy smile, breaking the tension. “Hahaha! So we’re a team of all half-wits, then? I think it’s better this way. It means we don’t have to be intimidated by each other anymore.”
The talentless wizard Dwalkie was overjoyed by those words. “It certainly is.”
“I’ll worrrk harder to be useful to the team!” The beastwoman who was born a pureblood but couldn’t summon a soul beast was likewise touched.

“It may be too soon to say this on the third day of our first quest, but I hope this party lasts a long time.” Brown, an eight-year human adventurer at the pinnacle of mediocrity, apparently felt the same. Everyone acknowledged their own shortcomings, spoke openly about them, and comforted each other.
As a result, all eyes then naturally honed in on the person who had not confessed anything yet, as if to ask if I had anything to share.
Uh, I don’t have anything like that... I should probably say something to avoid being the party’s outcast, but...
Panicking at the gazes on me, the words just left my mouth. “I-I don’t have a mother!”

chapters.title: Chapter 53: Team Half-Wit (3)
paragraphs: After my shocking confession that I didn’t have a mother, a strange silence fell between us and startled gazes flew my way.
“Uh-uhh...”
“I-I see?”
I rushed to explain. “My mother died after giving birth to me. And when I was young, my father never came back from the labyrinth. I am an adult now, but I can’t see them again even if I wanted to!”
For reference, what I said was 100 percent the truth as told to me by Ainar.
“I see...”
“Your childhood must have been hard.”
Perhaps because it was an admission from the youngest member of the party and a barbarian who had just completed his coming-of-age ceremony, but sympathy began to shine in the eyes looking at me.
“Bjorn, you don’t have to keep pretending that everything is okay in front of us anymore.”
“I’m sorry. I didn’t know you were going thrrrough something like that. And I talked about my family...”
“Bjorn, I may not be able to be your parent, but if you want—”
What was this prick talking about? I decided not to entertain the rest of the dwarf’s sentence. “No need.”

For some reason, I seemed to have quickly become the most pitiful one here but... oh well. Since it wasn’t the truth, I probably didn’t have to worry about it. It wasn’t like I actually didn’t have a mother. Most importantly, I was a young barbarian who, unlike them, was progressing on the ultra-elite track and had been promoted to rank-seven adventurer in three months. That was the gist of the most important stuff.
Um, but doesn’t that really make me the most pitiful one here?

Suddenly, I began to suspect that might be the case too. I had been dragged into a game world that hadn’t exactly been in my five-year plan, and I’d had to overcome death numerous times ever since. Shit, why was my life so miserable?
“Bjorn, your face doesn’t look good! Did you think of your mother?”
“Yes, something like that...”
“If you miss your family, you can call me sisterrr—”
I cut off the beastwoman’s words before she could start up again and got straight to the point. “Anyway, what are we going to do now?”

Our original destination, the orc colony, was no longer a viable hunting ground because of those pricks. Of course, they’d said it was okay for us to stay on the outskirts, but what share would I be left with if we hunted here at that speed and divided that by five?
Hikurod offered up his two cents as the party’s leader. “I think it would be better to head to the Witch’s Forest now.”

The Witch’s Forest referred to the huge woodland surrounding the portal that led to the fourth floor. Most of the monsters that appeared there were ranks seven and eight, and among them were spirit-type monsters who were immune to physical damage.
“Of course, it’s not a great fit for our party since we’re mostly close-combat fighters, but since we have a wizard too, it shouldn’t be too bad.”
Brown offered a differing opinion. “Hmm, wouldn’t it be better to just go up to the fourth floor, in that case?”
I also thought that was a better option than Hikurod’s. For most adventurers, the Witch’s Forest was just an area they had no choice but to go through since it had little merit as a hunting ground.
And it doesn’t produce any essences that would work for me.
The problem was that the dwarf wasn’t so keen on this idea. “The fourth floor is... It’s still too early.”

I knew what he was worried about. The majority of the monsters that appeared on the third floor were ranks seven and eight, and the same went for the fourth floor. However, there was a very crucial difference between the two.
“As I’ve said many times during our meetings, I’ve seen a lot of parties underestimate the fourth floor and then get wiped out,” Hikurod explained. “One time, that party was almost my own.”

The difference was the presence or absence of a rank-six monster. From the fourth floor onward, there was a slim chance of rank-six monsters appearing. In terms of how frequent these encounters were, you basically ran into one every three days you spent walking around all day. But that, in turn, meant that you’d undoubtedly encounter a rank-six monster at some point when you were active on the fourth floor.
Whether we’ll be able to handle that chance encounter or not is the question.
In fact, even while playing the game, there were many times when I entered the fourth floor with a mid-level character and met a bloody end. So, the dwarf’s concerns were reasonable.
“I don’t think it’s too early to decide whether we’ll go to the fourth floor after working together for at least a few more days,” Brown countered.

True, but despite the deeply emotional exchange and increased bonding that this incident had brought about, this was our first quest together. It had only been three days since we entered the labyrinth, and we still weren’t familiar with each other.
“Still, as you know, this is also Dwalkie’s first expedition. And Bjorn has never been to the third floor before, either.”
To summarize, Hikurod’s argument was that it was okay for us to go to the fourth floor, but that we shouldn’t be so impatient to do so.
“Well then, why don’t we just go to another arrrea on the third floor? I think Greentail Marsh would be fine.”
Missha, who had been listening to the debate with an apparent headache, offered a fresh perspective and was immediately shut down by Brown.
“If we had decided to travel that way from the start, it would have been. But getting to Greentail Marsh from here would take us at least six days.”

The labyrinth closed at the end of day seven on the first floor, day ten on the second floor, and day fifteen on the third floor. To invest another six days just on travel? Since today was already the third day, even if we left straight away, that would mean we’d only get in six days of hunting.
“In this particular case, I think it would be better to head back to Ironrock Hill,” Brown concluded.
In response to the expert’s words, Missha smiled sheepishly and scratched her cheek. “R-Really? Since I always just followed someone else over there, I didn’t realize...”

I listened to their conversation to see if anything interesting would come of it, but it ended up going nowhere. It was now time for me to wrap things up. “How long are we going to just stand around and talk? That’s enough chatter. Everyone, circle up. Let’s decide what to do by majority vote.”
“Majority vote?”
“Why, Brown? Do you prefer rock-paper-scissors?”
“No, that’s a bit...” Brown shot me an appalled look. Actually, I was just joking about that being a better option, but since I was a barbarian, sadly, no one seemed to notice.
“I am in favor of deciding by majority vote.”
“It’s simple, but it’s the most reliable way.”
“I’m fine with anything!”

In any case, we decided to use a vote to figure out what to do next. I was the first to speak. “I think it would be better to head up to the fourth floor.” I figured that leading with that would help influence public opinion a little more.
“...I’m starting to think that the fourth floor is dangerous. It feels like we’re rrrushing.”
“Oh, do you feel the same way as me, Miss Karlstein?”
Regardless of how they responded, once we each took turns speaking our minds, we quickly came to a decision.
“Whew, it seems there is no point arguing against the majority.”
We were now heading to the fourth floor.

Despite the dwarf’s concerns, I had a reason for pushing forward with this decision. Of course, it came down to a majority vote, but that wasn’t really saying much. If I had judged that it was too early for us to enter the fourth floor, I would have kept them locked up on the third, even if I had to destroy their self-esteem to do it.
“Hmm? It suddenly got a little cold...”
“Already? There’s still a long way to go before we reach the Witch’s Forest.”
“No, it’s differrrent from that. I can’t really explain it.”
Following Brown’s lead, we made our way through the darkness toward our destination. Hikurod still had an uneasy look on his face.
I don’t think he was like this back in the Bloody Citadel. He’s been overly cautious these past few days.

Was it because this was his first time leading a party he had hand-picked? It seemed that the weight of that responsibility was constantly on his shoulders. He really didn’t need to worry about all that since he was just the puppet leader...
Well, since he doesn’t know that I have the vampire’s essence, his actions do make sense.

The dwarf didn’t know my exact specs, which was why advancing to the fourth floor would’ve made him a little nervous. Not to mention he didn’t know how great of a Numbers Item the Guardian’s Wrist Guard really was.
“Hikurod, once we enter the Witch’s Forest, use that item without holding back.”
The dwarf pondered my advice, then gave me a determined nod. “I will do as you say.”

No. 3112: Guardian’s Wrist Guard was a rare piece of equipment worth fifty million stones. They say to see something was to want it. Hikurod had asked that I not disclose the fact that he was carrying such an item to the rest of the members of our party.
But that’s pointless if he can’t use it when he needs to.
After all, I wasn’t the owner, and just now we filmed a whole soap opera vowing to rely on each other, right?
“‘That item?’ What’s that? Why are you two having a private converrrsation?” Missha demanded.
“You will know when the time comes.” I ignored Missha’s curiosity and took stock one last time.
With the tank’s stats at this level, I think a rank-six monster is doable. The problem is the damage dealer line...

It seemed to be a little lacking in terms of specs alone, but after hunting for a short while longer at the orc colony, I gained some confidence. With how solid the front line was, with these members, even a rank-six monster wouldn’t be too dangerous.
Unless someone in the back suddenly trolls us and dies early.
There had been a lot of NPCs like that in the game. I hoped these guys weren’t the same...
Damn it, now I’m getting worried.

While I was growing more and more concerned, Missha’s face was glowing. “It’s been a while since I’ve been to the fourrrth floor, so I’m kind of excited!” I’d heard that this was her first return to the fourth floor since her party had disbanded a year ago. Perhaps because she was a cat, I swore I could hear her purring with each exhale.
After moving along the outskirts of the orc colony for a while, it was time to take a break. “We should start to look for a place to camp,” Brown called.
“Brown, everyone looks good physically, so how about we travel a little more?” Hikurod suggested.
“We’d have to go three more hours to find a better spot than this.”
“Hmm, all right, then.”
The time was around 9 p.m., which coincided almost perfectly with the time we’d set up camp on the first and second days. To be honest, I was very impressed.
Is this what a skilled adventurer looks like?

Brown must have chosen the location for our camp according to our trajectory and adjusted our travel speed accordingly. Despite there being no difference between night and day in the labyrinth, it was best to have a set time for breaks.
“Brown, what’s our itinerary for tomorrow?”

“We might be able to reach the Witch’s Forest by mid-day.” Hmm, that meant we’d enter the fourth floor the day after. He answered each question without buffering, almost like a human GPS. “Bjorn, you are on the last watch, right? Since tomorrow’s journey through the forest will be a tough one, you should get some rest.”
“I will.”

Hikurod took the first watch today and I took the last. The Witch’s Forest was a place that was most taxing on close-combat warriors, so we agreed on this regardless of the shifts we had previously planned out. Well, I was sure I’d wake up once or twice during the night anyway.
“Bjorn.”
I opened my eyes to the sound of whispering. I could see Brown’s face beneath the flickering torchlight. Since he was the one on watch before me...
“...Is it my turn?”
“Not yet.”

“Then why...?” I froze in the middle of rubbing my sleepy eyes. Dwalkie, Hikurod, and even Missha—everyone on the team was already awake and fully armed except for me. “Is it a monster?” I asked brusquely.
“It’s both.”
A monster and an adventurer. I was about to ask how far away they were when I heard an urgent cry from somewhere in the darkness.
“Damn it! They followed us all the way here!”
“Run!”
It seemed to be some adventurers being chased by some monsters, but Brown closed his eyes and sniffed the air. “Now I know for sure,” he muttered after a moment.
“What do you mean?” Whenever he frowned like that, there was usually a problem, so I couldn’t help but be anxious.
As expected, he said, “The people coming toward us right now... I’m certain they are the same people who were lying in wait when we arrived at Ironrock Hill.”
Things were getting interesting.

chapters.title: Chapter 54: The Witch’s Forest (1)
paragraphs: “Does that mean these people are the plunderers from earlier?”

Brown nodded at Hikurod’s question, which made the situation perfectly clear. It couldn’t be a coincidence that the people proudly looting on the third floor happened to end up where we were while being chased by a monster.
“I don’t know who they are, but it’s clear they are deliberately targeting us,” I said.

“Although we don’t know the reason why. They’re probably pretending they’re being chased so they’ll be able to join our group,” Brown agreed, throwing in his own two cents. I had had the same thought.
“T-Then what should we do now?” Missha asked.
What was there to do? Thanks to Brown, we had been able to see through their tricks in advance. “We should take advantage of this opportunity.”
Missha cocked her head. “Take advantage of it?”
However, there wasn’t enough time to explain in detail. It seemed they had already arrived.
“L-Light! It’s a light!” At one man’s cry, two men and one woman covered in blood hurriedly entered the radius of our torchlight.

“If you’re not a confident actor, just sit back and watch,” I whispered under my breath, making eye contact with Brown. He nodded slightly. I swear, this guy understood me so well. Even Hikurod, whom I had been a bit worried about, seemed to understand exactly what I meant.
Then, shall we get started?
“Do not come closer.” As they ran up to us, I immediately grabbed my shield, walked forward, and stood in their way.
“H-Hey! Our party was wiped out. Help us! We’ll pay you back!” He was wearing a desperate yet urgent expression. This guy was good at acting too. I guess that was par for the course for a plunderer.
“Put down your weapons.”
“B-But there’s a monster—!” The human man in his mid-thirties pointed behind him. A group of orcs was watching us from beyond the torch’s perimeter.
“Ch-chwiik!”
Since there were more people now, they were unable to approach, but we couldn’t be sure how long that would last.
This guy seemed to want to say, “So hurry up and let us in,” right? But so what?
I once again spoke firmly. “It is your choice. Either put down your weapons or get lost.”

They did not readily respond to my demand. Of course, I was sure there was a lot to consider. In the labyrinth, your weapon was your life. They were possibly realizing at this point that we were somewhat suspicious of them, but it didn’t matter. Whatever choice they made, we had nothing to lose.
“...We will.” The mustached man made his decision and dropped his weapon to the ground. The other two followed suit.
Have you decided to be greedy?
That decision was both satisfying and worrying. They would really take on this much risk to come after us? I didn’t even have a guess as to why.
“Okay then, walk this way, but slowly. And stay as far apart from each other as you can.”
“T-There’s no need to go this far, is there? We just want help...”
“If you want help, do as you are told.”
“Okay.”
Then, as they arrived one by one as instructed, Brown approached them and checked for hidden weapons. “...They don’t have anything that seems like a threat.”
“I see. Hikurod, you watch them.”

“A-All right!” The dwarf stiffened and nodded his head, then marched along with his arms and legs completely straight like a North Korean soldier. A sigh escaped me then. Fortunately, judging by the looks on their faces, it seemed that the other group didn’t pick up on the awkwardness of his actions.
“Ch-chwiik...”
“Chwiik, chwiik, chwiik!”

After I left Hikurod with the trio of plunderers and returned my attention to the orcs, the monsters soon turned around and left. It seemed even they considered it too much of a risk to fight such a large group of people.
Those monsters are clever bastards.

Well, they were nothing compared to human bastards. In any case, avoiding a pointless battle was good news for us. Given our newest problem, having to focus on a battle with the orcs would be very draining.

“Ugh, I thought I was going to die...” As soon as the group of orcs disappeared, the woman in the group slumped down to the ground. She came back to her senses a beat later, then did a double take, stood up, and bowed politely to us. “Ah! My name is Elisa. Thank you for saving us!”

Her ripped shirt was revealing her chest, and the dwarf coughed and turned his head. “Ahem. I’m Hikurod Murad.” It didn’t seem like he was pretending to be innocent, though, considering the fact that his head was turned but his eyes were still riveted to one particular area.
“So your name is Mr. Murad! And how about everyone else?”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

“Oh, I see!” The woman who introduced herself as Elisa came up to me and grabbed my hand, then bowed her head again like last time, of course accentuating her chest. “Ha, thank you all so much! I don’t know what would have happened if we hadn’t run into all of you...” Her panting breaths and voice that seemed to caress the ear were icing on the cake. Now that I was thinking about it, that was likely the reason that her shirt was the only one particularly ripped out of all of theirs...
“Bjorn! Your eyes are glazing overrr!” Missha muttered, clearly misreading my reaction.
I made no effort to correct her right then; I’d have an opportunity to do so soon. “Give us your names, one by one.” To set them at ease, I started with a simple roll call.
The first one to introduce themselves was the mustached man who also seemed to be the leader. “Hans Argo.”
What? “...Hans?”
“It’s a common name. Do you know another?”

“Uh, um, well... Something like that,” I said with an awkward nod. Hans A had had his head smashed in by my shield. Hans B I had met by coincidence at a tavern, but I never saw him again after the advice he gave me. I could see Hans C, the mustached man, following in the footsteps of A today. Anyway, next person.

“My name is Irita Taison.” Irita was a tall, blond spearman. He was in his mid-twenties, and had no other distinguishing features. If I had to pick something, it would be his polite attitude. “I thought I was going to meet my maker just now, but thanks to you all, we lived to tell the tale. I want to thank you once again.”

When Irita bowed 90 degrees, Elisa started gushing in her distinctly innocent tone. “It’s true! If it weren’t for you guys, I don’t know what would’ve happened to us... This must’ve been a blessing from Reatlas!”
“Reatlas?” Brown stiffened at that particular word, then carefully asked, “Could it be... that you are—”

“Oh, I haven’t told you my last name yet. My full name is Elisa Behenk. As you can see...” Elisa trailed off and looked down at her clothes with a tearful expression on her face. They were torn and covered in sweat and dirt but would have once been white. “I guess you can’t really see. But I currently serve Reatlas!”
“Ha!”

While the dwarf just let out a brief exclamation, Brown closed his eyes and drew a brief cross in front of Elisa. “You really are a priestess.” Wow, this guy was good at acting. “May the blessing of the twilight star be with you.”

Elisa smiled brightly and made a cross as well. “Yes, may the blessing of the twilight star be with you.” She probably thought her plan had worked. After that, the suspicion in the air seemed to dissipate in an instant. Well, at least that was what it seemed like to them.
Since we all know that she can’t possibly be a real priest—
“Lady Elisa, would you be able to look at my wound?” asked Hans.
What?
“I’m sorry! I should have helped you with that first thing...”

Wait, was she a real priestess? While I flinched at this unexpected turn of events, Hans C rolled up his sleeve to reveal a stab wound. Then Elisa chanted a prayer and brought her white, glowing hand to the wounded area.
Would you look at that?
Swaa...

The wound healed instantaneously. Although I had watched the whole process with skepticism, there was no doubt that this was truly divine magic. How could I be sure if I’d never seen it before, you may be asking? For one, it sounded different from when a wound was healed by a potion, and there was also Hans C’s expression to take into account. Peaceful, without the slightest bit of pain.
“May the blessing of the twilight star be with you...”

This was a shock to everyone else too. Brown froze for a moment, then moved to make the sign of the cross like a sinner who had just witnessed a miracle right before his eyes. His reaction seemed a bit exaggerated to me, but in truth, it was probably the normal reaction for someone to have given the structure of this universe. Just as other races grew up in their respective holy lands, most human children learned to read and were taught at the temples from an early age. The weight of the word ‘priesthood’ was different to them.

“Ah! So can we have our weapons back now?” Elisa asked casually as if she had just remembered she didn’t have hers. Perhaps showing off her divine power was her way of paving the way for this next part. This must have been why they had made the bold decision to toss aside their weapons earlier.
But, uh-oh. “That’s not going to happen.”
“N-No?”
As her expression grew puzzled, I made sure to act natural. There was no need to reveal that I already knew her identity. “I see that you are a real priestess. But what about it?”

I was a barbarian who believed solely in my ancestors. The clergy had never done anything for me, so it wasn’t strange for me to react in this way. Elisa smiled awkwardly and looked at Brown and Dwalkie, who were both human. It seemed like she was trying to get help from them, but I firmly cut off any chances of that at the pass.
“We will return their weapons on their way out after we receive compensation.”
“C-Compensation?”
“Why are you surprised? Priestess or not, you’re an adventurer as long as you’re in the labyrinth. You have to follow convention.”
“Ah, yes... I’ve heard of such a custom. So... How much should we give you?”
I pretended to think for a moment and then said, “About two million stones should be sufficient.”
“...W-What?” Elisa asked to make sure she didn’t hear me wrong, but I stood firm.

“That shouldn’t be an unreasonable request.” On the contrary, that was almost nothing. I’d heard of bad guys even taking equipment in return for their victims’ lives. “Think about how much your life is worth.”
“But... We don’t have that kind of money.”
That, I already knew. Who carried cash into the labyrinth? Now that the response I expected had been put out there, it was time to switch tactics.
“I’m not asking you to lower the price. At least let us pay you outside—”
“No. I don’t believe the words of anyone other than my own people. If you don’t have the money, pay with your equipment.”
“...Equipment?”
“Hmm, that man’s armor should do it.”

When I pointed at Hans C with my finger, the man frowned. However, after exchanging a few looks with Elisa, he let out a deep sigh. “Ha... If it’s in return for my life, that’s not a loss. However, I have a condition. We will stay with your group tonight until we recover our strength.”
“Fine.” I nodded readily. Their intentions were obvious, but I wasn’t going to keep the promise anyway.
“Irita, can you help me?”
“I will.”

Hans C took off his heavy armor with the help of the spear guy next to him, then handed the equipment to Brown. Nice. Now that we’d stripped one bastard of their armor, we’d taken everything we needed to at this point.
“Now then. We’ve paid the price, so will you return our weapons?”
I decided not to wait around any longer and let myself smile brightly. To be honest, I hadn’t thought things would work out this well.
Hans C’s expression hardened. “...Why are you laughing?”
I didn’t answer, just like I hadn’t corrected Missha for saying my eyes had glazed over while looking at Elisa earlier. They were going to figure it out soon, anyway.
“Uh, Mr. Yandel? We really can’t afford to give you more than—”
“Ah, there’s no need for that,” I replied moments before I struck Elisa in the head with my mace.
Smack!
“L-Lady Elisa!”
No matter what game you were playing, cracking the healer’s head open first was a universal rule.

chapters.title: Chapter 55: The Witch’s Forest (2)
paragraphs: With an innocent look, a voluptuous body, and a sweet voice to boot, Elisa had an appearance that most men would readily enjoy. Or she did, until one second ago.
“L-Lady Elisa!”
Hans C’s eyes widened just as the slender woman of about 5′2″ collapsed to the ground.
Slump.
Her temple was dented, her eyes popped out theatrically, and crimson blood shot out like a water gun from where her ear canal should have been. Pretty-faced Elisa was now gone.
“You, w-what did you do?!” Hans C, witnessing her misfortune, shouted in shock. “Why?! Why did you harm Lady Elisa!? What did we do to you?!”
True, you haven’t done anything yet.
“Ah, sorry. It was a mistake,” I answered in brief. My hand slipped because the mace was heavy. Truly. “Why don’t you come closer for a moment? To talk about compensation for my mistake.”
“Y-You crazy bastard!”
Well, that didn’t work. To be fair, he had a brain too. As soon as he sensed the fate that awaited him, Hans C fell into a state of panic. “Ah, no... w-we’re all going to die...”
I no longer bothered denying it. “I’m glad you’re aware.”
“B-Because of these crazy assholes...”

Except, as I was smiling at Hans C’s terror, I sensed a disparity that was hard to describe. Wondering what it was, I carefully analyzed the feeling and realized it was caused by the direction of the man’s gaze.
He’s not looking at us. Why, is he afraid of something else?
I instinctively moved my head to follow Hans C’s gaze. At the end of it was the late Elisa, a woman who had tragically lost her beauty and had become a cold corpse.
But it seemed she sensed my gaze on her.

“Gigig, gigi, gigig...” Elisa, who should have already returned to her maker’s embrace, started to convulse and spit out strange noises. Her limbs flailed and bent like she was being electrocuted. It was reminiscent of a dance performed by zombies in a movie.
What the fuck is this now?

I couldn’t understand what was going on at all. When I smacked her in the head, I definitely felt the unique sensation of a one-shot kill jolt up my arm. Why was she still alive and wriggling and making those creepy noises?
“Gigit, gigigit, gig!”
“B-Bjorn? What is happening?”
Don’t ask me, you dwarf, I’m fucking scared too.
I had killed many people since waking up in this body, but I’d swear on my ancestors themselves that I’d never seen a corpse dance like that before.
Crunch!
However, this habit of clenching my jaw when I was nervous was a reminder that my body belonged to a brave barbarian. “...I will resolve this.”
“Resolve it?”
Instead of answering, I sprinted forward and slammed my mace down. The target was Elisa’s face.
Smack!
Her skull, which was far softer than a death fiend’s, once again caved in, which almost made Hikurod pass out.
“M-Mutilating a corpse? Even if these people are plunderers, that’s—!”
What, it was immoral? So what? “I was so scared I couldn’t help it.”
“What? Is that something a scared person would do—?”

I cut him off. I didn’t know why I had to explain this to people over and over again. “The best defense is a good offense.” Of course it was. I was scared, so I destroyed it. To protect oneself, one must mutilate the enemy without mercy. That was the barbarian way.
Now I get it.
That was why Ainar had been afraid of the banshees—because spirit-type monsters could not be beaten up. They required magical damage, not physical.

Having come to this new realization, I looked at the late Elisa again and tutted bitterly. “Damn, still dancing, huh?” Even though her entire face was caved in now, Elisa continued to crack her joints and perform a creepy dance. Did this call for a magical solution? “Dwalkie! Use magic!”
“But—”
“Hurry up!” No buts. There was no need to play nice with kids like this. They only listened to firm commands. As soon as I yelled at him, Dwalkie began to chant a spell.
Right at that moment, Hans C turned his back on us and started running away. “I-I can’t die!”
It was a stupid thing to do. Before he could run even a few steps, the crossbow bolt Brown fired hit his back.
Stab!

With his back turned, Hans C collapsed in a miserable heap. As I watched his tragic end, I muttered, “Fucking idiot.” If he hadn’t given us his armor, he would’ve been able to withstand a single arrow. Low intelligence always brought about suffering.
Soon, I shifted my gaze and looked at our last remaining enemy, the spearman, Irita. “Aren’t you running away?” I asked.
“I know it’s pointless.” His eyes and voice implied he had already given up. However, my warrior blood sensed something strange in that voice, just like in Hans C’s. And it was at that moment—
Shaaaaa!

Suddenly, a black glow burst from Hans C’s body. To be honest, I was scared shitless, so I quickly hid behind Dwalkie, but nothing special happened after that. The light radiated for about five seconds before disappearing, after which I straightened up my crouched form and looked in front of me.
“Damn?”

I didn’t know what kind of bizarre combo this was, but by the time the light show died out, Hans C’s body had been transformed into a mummy. Any and all moisture was gone, leaving a dry, lifeless corpse. Everyone’s eyes instinctively turned to Brown, who had shot the arrow.
“Rotmiller, what did you...?” Hikurod asked.
“I-I didn’t do anything! Really!”
I know, old man.
This had to have something to do with (the late) Elisa as well. We hadn’t even done anything to Irita, and he already looked the same as Hans C.
Dwalkie, our wizard, hastily offered his interpretation. “The life force that was extracted from those two was absorbed into the body of that woman over there!”
Huh, was that how it was? Having played games for so long, I now had a sense of what was going on, and I had a guess.
“Gigig, gigi, gigig...”
Soon, Elisa performed a dance with her joints and got up from the ground. Her face was still half-squashed, but her mouth opened regardless.
“How...did...you...know?”
“What?”
“That...we are...a foe.”

“Oh, that.” I was petrified, but I answered anyway, pretending to be calm. “All motherfuckers smell like garbage.” Was that a satisfactory answer? I thought it was, seeing as how Elisa and her half-destroyed head laughed out loud at it.
“Ki, hee, hee, hee!”

Shit, why was my life always uphill climb after uphill climb? This was just like the corpse golem battle. Everyone in our party froze at the unbelievable scene unfolding before us, and I woke them up by shouting at them just like last time.
“Everyone, wake up! Otherwise, we are all going to die!”
I had been playing Dungeon and Stone for ten years. It wasn’t a popular game, but I was proud to say that there wasn’t anything about it that I didn’t know, and I was sure about that.
“Ki, hee, hee, hee!”
“W-What happened? Why is a dead person...”

The corpse had revived. To my knowledge, this was not likely to be a miracle performed by the god of exploration, Reatlas. No matter what the people who served him did, Reatlas was a good-natured god. I arrived at a conclusion based on everything I had inferred so far.
“She is a priestess of Karui.”
A priestess of the dark god Karui.

“Priest of Karui” was a hidden class that could only be selected when you started as a human and became a priest. It came with the advantage of your character being able to use holy power and dark spells at the same time, but the penalty for that was just as huge.
“A priestess of Karui!”
“That woman serves the evil god Karui?!”

As a priest of Karui, the moment others found out about your class, you were dragged to prison. Therefore, it was necessary to form a party of only malicious NPCs you had made your minions, and it was also necessary to periodically offer live sacrifices to maintain your position.
That’s probably why she’s a plunderer. Finding a sacrifice inside the labyrinth is the safest option.
This explained most of what had happened. However, one question remained: why did it have to be us? Why had they hounded us so persistently? But there was no time to question things like that.
“Because of you...I lost...my precious...underlings.”

Was it because she had absorbed all of Hans C and Irita’s life force? Elisa’s appearance returned almost to normal again as she stared at me. Her crushed brain seemed to have been restored because her speech was better than before too. In other words, her intelligence was back.
However, were intelligence and a good personality two separate things?
What is this crazy bitch talking about?
“If you’re blaming other people even in a situation like this,” I bluntly replied, “you must not have gotten a proper education at home.”
“...What?”
It was all her fault that Hans and Irita had died in such a tragic way at such a young age. If she had accepted her fate in her crushed-skull state, this wouldn’t have happened.
Soon, I made up my mind. “I will avenge Hans and Irita.”
And I will take all the equipment and valuables they have too, although it won’t be easy.
But when was my life ever easy?
[Elisa Behenk has cast Call of Death.]
“L-Look, over there!” Hikurod cried out and pointed at something. When I looked, the mummified Hans C and Irita were slowly getting up.

If she was a priest of Karui, I was not surprised. I’d also played one a few times. Call of Death was the most basic and fundamental skill of that class. At first, it only summoned undead monsters, but using a corpse as a medium allowed you to manipulate stronger minions. The way their eyes lacked any sense of awareness was proof of that.
“Grrrrr...”
Before long, Hanson—short for Hans and Taison—transformed into undead and set their sights on us.
“Destroy the enemies, my servants!” At Elisa’s command, they charged.
Bam!
The battle officially began when Hanson collided with the shield wall Hikurod and I formed.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight spell, Ice Lance.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Enhance. The effect of any active skills increases in proportion to the user’s Soul Power.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Toxin Bestow.]

While we were taking a pounding from the front, Missha and Dwalkie worked to deal some damage, but there were no hits. With strength that exceeded that of regular humans and a high level of physical resistance, not even a mace could leave a scratch on them, not to mention that their bodies had been turned into undead and had gained resistance to poison and cold damage. This wouldn’t be a good match for us.
Shatter! Whoosh!
Of course, Brown, who had a lot of experience fighting the undead, used his Molotov cocktails generously.
“How foolish!”
[Elisa Behenk has cast Fire of the Dead.]
Black flames flickered to life in the air and began to absorb all the surrounding fire.
God damn it.
This situation was turning into even more of a headache. The sacred power of fire, which was the undead’s opposing attribute, was not working.
Do we have no other choice than to break through their cores?

The undead could not die while their core was still intact, even if their entire body got cut up. A skeleton’s core was hidden between the ribs, and a death fiend’s core was in the brain. So what about these guys, who had been brought back to life by the power of a dark god? The answer was simple.
“Missha, can you kill that woman?”
The core of a summoned was usually inside the summoner. In other words, if Elisa were killed, Hanson could also find the light and return to the bosom of the true god.
“You don’t have to kill it. Just doing some damage would make things a lot easier.”

After a moment, Missha nodded. “I’ll trrry.” Immediately, she stepped off my shoulder, leaped high into the air, and flew at Elisa. The move was agile and flexible enough to outshine an elf. However, our opponent was not someone it would work on.
[Elisa Behenk has summoned a Shadow Guard.]
Shadowy soldiers rose up from the ground and surrounded Elisa without leaving any openings. Even Missha wouldn’t be able to break through that barricade and cut off Elisa’s head any time soon.
However, there is no reason not to play the long game.

It was not like Hanson had weapons in their hands. Since we had already confiscated their weapons earlier, they were not really a threat even in undead form. In fact, Hikurod and I could drag this out for as long as we wanted.
After making my decision, I redistributed our manpower. “Dwalkie, Brown, you two help Missha.”
“But—”
“It’s okay. The two of us will do whatever we can to hold the fort here.”
“All right! Then I’ll leave it to you!”
As soon as Dwalkie and Brown joined in, the tide slowly began to turn.

Of course, the Shadow Guards regenerated as soon as they were destroyed, and they even had the free time to throw various curses at us, but at a certain point, the large number of summoned Shadow Guards significantly decreased.
“Looks like she’s slowly running out of steam! Stay strong!”
Even though she worshiped an evil god, there was a limit to Elisa’s power. Perhaps she hadn’t expected to end up in this situation.

“Damn... you... all!” Finding herself forced to play defense apparently startled Elisa, and she started shaking in anger. She seemed to still have a survival instinct, though, because she clenched her jaw and quietly muttered, “I will not forget... this humiliation...”
The number of Shadow Guards had decreased over the course of about twenty minutes, leaving fewer than five. Realizing what she was about to do, I loudly blurted, “What? Fuck, no!”
We’re so close to catching you, where are you going?!
I pushed aside Hanson, who had been on me the entire battle, and ran at her with all my might.
[Elisa Behenk has cast Spiritization.]
Soon, Elisa’s body turned translucent and floated into the air. In that state, she paused to look around at us. “You will never... return... alive.” Then she flew into the darkness in the distance.
Whiiip!
I let out a big sigh as I looked out in that direction like a dog who had just been chasing a chicken. “Fuck...”
The boss monster we were so close to taking down had escaped, armed with a grudge against us.

chapters.title: Chapter 56: The Witch’s Forest (3)
paragraphs: Priestess of Karui was a hidden class that a player could only switch to after reaching the fifth floor, and it was chock-full of all kinds of battle spells and cursed abilities, unlike a regular priest.
“What is this! It rrran away!”

I had been expecting us to get totally annihilated in the worst-case scenario, but instead we were able to overcome this dangerous situation safely. How could that be? To recap, there were several reasons.
“A priestess of Karui...” Brown murmured. “It was as the rumors say, a terrifying existence. Bjorn, if it weren’t for you, we’d have been in a lot of trouble.”

I made sure to take away their weapons early on: the sword, shield, spear, and even Elisa’s wand. At the time, I’d had no idea, but it was a stroke of luck that the wand got confiscated. Without it, casting a spell wasn’t as easy. There were other key factors, though.
“As expected, reliable barbarians are the best. I wondered if Brown was wrong when she said she was a prrriestess. But I didn’t think you’d whack her over the head!”
“N-Neither did I,” stammered Dwalkie. “Bjorn, when you wielded that weapon, I thought I felt my heart drop...”

It had been an unexpected blow for both friend and foe. Due to her head getting cracked open with that single hit, Elisa had had to absorb the life force of her comrades in order to be resurrected. However, she hadn’t been resurrected to her usual state. Her brain had been crushed, so her body couldn’t have possibly returned to normal.
Perhaps the reason why she had been talking like a simpleton was because she hadn’t completely recovered.

There were many good calls made. However, with my relief came a certain wooziness. What would have happened if we had fought in a situation where we were both at 100 percent? Well, the win rate would have been about half and half. Assuming that whichever side won, at least two people would have died on each side, it definitely would’ve been a ruthless battle. Knowing that, they approached us in a victim cosplay.
Then maybe our being almost equal in terms of combat power ended up being helpful to us.
After completing my review of this incident, I did a basic check of my physical condition. Needless to say, it was terrible.
[Decreased Energy is active. The speed at which your energy is restored is reduced.]
[Low-Level Decay is active. The speed at which your wounds are healed is reduced.]
[Tracking is active. Your location is being transmitted to the caster.]
[Spirit Walk is active. When you move, you will feel a slight pain.]
[Stamina Decrease is active...]

Fuck, I was about to lose my mind. My eyes were sore and my head felt like it was being fermented in salt. And for some reason, I couldn’t feel my lower body. Shit, how many curses did she cast on me?
[Warning: More than 15 curses have been stacked on you. If not healed through divine power or magic, your physical attributes may be permanently reduced.]

My physical health was a mess. A total disaster, if you will, to the point that it was hard to even explain in words how bad it was. But I didn’t worry too much, since we had a wizard on our team. “Dwalkie, cast a curse-release spell on me.”
“A-A curse-release spell?”
Why are you so surprised? It’s making me nervous. “Didn’t you say you can use curse magic?”
“Yes, but...”
But what? As I continued to stare at him in a way that clearly said “Keep talking,” Dwalkie avoided my gaze.
“I said I could use a few kinds of curse magic, but I didn’t say I could dispel them...”
Huh? “What kind of nonsense is that?”

“It’s because I taught myself instead of learning at the Magic Tower. I also heard that the ability to dispel a curse usually isn’t needed during a quest...” Dwalkie continued offering up long excuses but in short, the explanation was simple.
“In other words, you didn’t have the money.”
When I summarized the situation in one sentence like a barbarian, Dwalkie nodded unhappily. “That’s right. I thought it would be better to learn the things that are most necessary first.”

Yes, that was how our team was from the very beginning. No point in blaming each other at this point. Since we were all in the same boat, complaining here would only make me the bad guy. I decided to forget about what wasn’t possible and do what I could. “Brown, is there any way to pursue her?”
“...Unfortunately, there isn’t. I’ve been looking for a way since she left, but I can’t even find a trail.”
Hmm, I see. This was... quite a big headache, although it seemed like some of the others hadn’t realized that yet. “What’s your opinion? How dangerous do you think it would be?”
“Well, I don’t know yet. But it’s clear that we need to leave this place right now.”
“Leave... but where?”
“Wait!” The serious conversation I was having with Brown was promptly interrupted by Dwalkie. “What are you guys talking about?”

To be honest, I wanted to tell him to get lost and let the adults do the talking, but... Still. He was a wizard. He might offer up some good ideas during the discussion, so I gave him a brief explanation. “Didn’t you hear what that woman said while running away? She will never let us leave this place alive. She will definitely come back to find us soon.”
“Yes, but if she does, we can just deal with her like we did this time, no?”
You think that’s going to be easy?
Maybe it was because it was his first time in the labyrinth, but even though he was a wizard, he seemed to have a lower level of common sense than Missha.
“This is a really big deal! If she attacks us from behind while we’re fighting against a monsterrr, it’ll be trouble!”
It was common knowledge everywhere that an invisible enemy was scarier than a visible one. By the time she came to find us, she would pretty much have recovered all her strength as well.
She’ll choose the timing of the surprise attack too.

As could be seen from how much I’d benefitted from the tactic of being the first one to get a punch in, being the one to initiate the fight was almost always the most advantageous strategy. When Brown kindly explained this, Dwalkie kept his mouth shut, terrified.

“A priestess of Karui is gunning for us in the dark. Sounds like we have a major obstacle in our path. Hahaha.” The puppet leader (aka Hikurod) pretended he wasn’t panicking as he patted Dwalkie on the shoulder, but the tension in the air did not subside at all.
Well, since they had also just engaged in the same one-on-five fight that I had, they should know better than anyone how troublesome those bastard priests of Karui were.

As the anxiety was gradually brewing, I offered the only possible solution for our current situation. “Since this has already happened, I think it would be better to get to the Witch’s Forest as soon as possible.”
“Your reasoning?” Brown asked brusquely.
“She won’t be able to track us in there. And the curse problem will be resolved as well.”

I had omitted much of the explanation, but that was good enough. Judging by his expression, he seemed to have understood everything I said. “Utilize the topography of the Witch’s Forest, huh... That’s a reasonable plan.” Brown nodded, but there was one thing that caused him to grow suspicious. “By the way, didn’t you say this was your first time on the third floor?”
Yeah, it is. Which is why I’m asking you to take care of things and get on with them before I have to say them out loud, old man. “...I studied it in the library.”
Brown cocked his head at my excuse. “Library?”
I wasn’t too worried though, because I happened to have a witness right next to me. “Surprisingly, it’s true. Bjorn goes to the library every day to read,” Hikurod said with a nod.
“Wow, barbarians rrread books?”
“No wonder. Even the way he speaks is different than other barbarians.”
Everyone looked at me like I was a mutant. Enough attention. Could we please make a decision and do what we needed to do? “So, what do you all think?”
“I agree with your plan.” After Brown backed up my argument, Hikurod and Missha followed suit, and a decision was quickly reached. There was only one thing left to do before we hurried out of here.
I looked at Hanson, who had both collapsed like puppets with their strings cut when Elisa ran away. “What are you all doing, not taking off their gear?”

No matter how urgent the situation was, we still needed to take whatever we could. Weren’t we adventurers who slaughtered plunderers and monsters? Adding it all up, this stuff was worth over eight hundred thousand stones. I wondered if it was because they were third-floor plunderers, but the drop items from Hanson were different from the ones I had seen before. Of course, dividing this by five, my income would still be roughly the same as it had been in the past.
“For real? That makes over a hundred thousand stones per perrrson! I was cutting it close for this year’s taxes, so that’s great!”
“With that money, I can learn a few more spells! Oh, I’ll definitely learn a curse-release spell this time too!”
Having earned a large sum of money in an instant, Dwalkie and Missha happily sketched out their future plans.
Brown, Hikurod, and I just smiled awkwardly and stayed silent. No matter how much money you earned in the labyrinth, it didn’t matter unless you returned to the city alive.

“Money from this loot will be distributed once it’s sold back in the city,” Hikurod explained. The three of us with expandable backpacks decided to split the loot between us for the trip. No one could be sure of the future, after all. Someone could die during the expedition, lose a backpack, or attempt to run off with one. However, I was a little surprised.
I knew the dwarf did, but I didn’t think Missha owned an expandable backpack too...
In contrast to my initial impression of her, it seemed Missha might have been thriftier with money than I thought. It was unexpected, but she could even be smart with her finances.
“Then let’s go.”

We gathered our loot, cleaned up the camp, and hurriedly left. Brown took the lead and found the way, and the rest of us followed behind him, on the lookout for any surprises. We used Brown’s sense of smell to avoid as many battles with monsters as possible and focused solely on moving forward.
How long had it been?
[Warning: Your energy is steadily decreasing. If not promptly dealt with, permanent...]

I felt like I was on the verge of death. Carrying around a laundry list of curses while also running for five hours straight left me feeling horrible. If it wasn’t for the stats I had gotten from the vampire such as Mana Resistance and Dark Resistance, I would probably have collapsed from exhaustion already.
“Bjorn, you... are you okay?”

“I can handle it, don’t worry.” I pretended to ease the dwarf’s concerns, but to be honest, I wasn’t okay at all. Unlike the others, who only had two or three curses to their name, that crazy bitch threw too many at me to count, and one curse in particular had only been placed on me.
Damn Decreased Energy...

Energy Decrease was a shitty skill that significantly lowered the amount of stamina your character recovered after moving or performing an action. Since Stamina was separate from Vitality, it didn’t matter how high your healing factor was—it was useless.
In terms of the game, I would probably have, like, 30 percent left?

In the game, when the Stamina gauge dropped below 10 percent, the character was unable to move at all. There had been a lot of times when NPCs would whine and just ask to be killed instead, but I wasn’t quite there yet. Of course, I was insanely exhausted, but not enough to die. I could still get by on my mental fortitude, which meant there was still plenty of time left.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Your energy level reaches 5 percent or less.]
[Reward: Your Spirit stat has permanently increased by +1.]
Of course there’s still time. If I don’t think like that, I won’t be able to go on.
I decided to just focus on the positive. Even though I’d pushed myself a little too far, our destination was slowly approaching.

“Considering the soil is damp here, we should be there in another ten minutes,” Brown announced. The journey had taken about five hours. Despite my concerns, we reached the Witch’s Forest without being attacked once.
If we’ve gotten all the way here without seeing her yet, that means that bitch’s body hasn’t fully recovered yet.

It was a good thing I had pushed myself, at least. I didn’t think there was any chance Elise would give up on us considering she had even used the power of the dark god in front of us to save herself. If we returned to the city alive as witnesses, that would put her in a tough spot.
“We’re here.”

As I heard Brown’s words, I shook off the thoughts that had been filling my head. It really was best to distract yourself with other things when you were tired. Case in point, I just got through ten minutes without even noticing.
“So this is the Witch’s Forest...” said Dwalkie. “I don’t know why, but it’s giving me the creeps.”
“For some reason, all wizards say that the first time they come here.”
“It feels like an ominous energy is vibrating through the forest.”
Before us was a withered thorn tree with a vine wrapping around it like a snake, and—
“W-Wait! That tree moved!”
The Witch’s Forest was a place where everything came to life.
[You have entered a special area on the third floor.]
[Field Effect - Witch’s Forest has activated.]
[Status effect Loss of Direction is now active.]
[Status effect Auditory Hallucination is now active.]
[Status effect Visual Hallucination is now active.]
[Status effect Pain Enhancement is now active.]
Stepping into the forest with only a torch to light the way, we felt the cool air sink into our skin.
[All status effects except Field Effects will be deactivated.]
Whew, now I felt like I could breathe.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 3
Physique: 155
Spirit: 90 (New +1)
Special Ability: 115
Item Level: 683
General Combat Power: 528.75 (New +1)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7 / Vampire (Guardian) - Rank 5]

chapters.title: Chapter 57: The Witch’s Forest (4)
paragraphs: The numerous curses that had been following me were gone. Instead, the voice of the forest kept ringing in my ears.
“Die! Die! Die! Die! Die!”
Yup, not going to happen.
“You motherless bastard!”
