Mhm, I had a mom in my real life.
“Kekekeke! Kekeee!”

I smiled, ignoring the auditory hallucinations that came every few seconds. Although they were a bit annoying, so what? They were just hallucinations. Their words could do no real damage, and the real curses had disappeared without a trace thanks to them.
All of their taunts are lame too. If you’re going to attack me psychologically, do better.

These insults had no originality or sincerity to them. My colleagues seemed to think differently, though. “Bjorn! How can you laugh off all of these curses? Have you gone crazy, purrrhaps? All this noise is hurting my head!”
The trio of Missha, Hikurod, and Brown, who had all been to the Witch’s Forest before, were in good shape. The problem was Dwalkie.
“Ugh, uh...” His eyes were hazy and his face was haggard, making it look like he was about to lose his lunch at any moment. Well, this kind of place was bound to give anyone motion sickness.
I didn’t know it would feel like this, but it’s fascinating.

With the effects of Visual Hallucination and Loss of Direction, everything started to look curved. I was definitely looking to the right, but I was seeing something directly in front of me. On top of that, my sense of distance was less reliable than usual. It was like looking at the world through a convex mirror.
Retch!
Soon, Dwalkie could not stand it any longer and vomited thick gastric acid. Somewhat worried, I asked, “Can you use magic in that state?”
“Bjorn is a meanie! Is that really morrre important than your teammate being sick?!”

What was she saying? Last time Dwalkie vomited, she had been the one telling him to act like an adult. Whew, this was why getting attached to your fellow party members should be avoided as much as possible. It prevented you from making rational decisions.
“Missha, I didn’t ask you. So Dwalkie, what’s the answer?”
“Y-You d-don’t have to worry. Magic is no problem—blaargh!”
Well, I guess there would be no magic until he got used to this. Why were wizards so weak?

As I clicked my tongue, unable to understand this, Brown looked at me, fascinated. “Still, it’s impressive. No matter how strong-willed a barbarian you are, the first journey into the forest is bound to be at least a little tough...”
Well, I had heard the same thing. But considering how awful a time I was having just a few minutes ago, I was able to laugh this off.
Of course, the tsundere dwarf had to step in for his best friend. “Tsk, this is because you sit in front of a desk all day.”
“Look, I’m actually one of the few wizards who exercises—”
“Uh huh. Until you get used to our surroundings, take a break. You didn’t sleep well last night, either. It must be worse because you’re tired.”
“Your kindness... I will not forget it.”

In the end, we decided to stay at the entrance of the forest for a while until Dwalkie got used to the environment. I wasn’t all that against this plan, either. In the end, a wizard’s presence was the most important thing in the labyrinth, and I also needed to recover my exhausted energy stores if only a little.
“I will stand watch,” said Hikurod. “You all can rest.”
As soon as the words were out of his mouth, I lay flat on the floor and closed my eyes. I didn’t even bother taking out my sleeping bag.
But what was this? “Bjorn, you know...” I was just about to get some sleep when Hikurod came up to me and started whispering. “That lady from earlier, Elisa—”
That woke me up. What the hell was he talking about? “She’s not a lady, she’s a bitch.”
“Yeah, yeah, that bitch. Anyway, I can’t shake the feeling that I’ve seen her somewhere before...”
What? I thought he was going to say something pointless as usual, but this seemed pretty important.

When I raised my upper body to indicate I was listening, he hesitated for a moment before opening his mouth. “Remember when I visited the Adventurers’ Guild on your advice? When I was filling out the application sheet, someone next to me was asking the employee there all kinds of stuff.”
“I’m tired. Get to the point.”
“Now that I’m thinking about it, that person was her.”
Much better, although even the concise summary wasn’t without its frustrations. “Then why didn’t you recognize her right away?” I asked flatly.
“Because... unlike in the city, her appearance was all messed up and dirty. A-And her clothes were ripped and torn!”
Oh. So he didn’t look at her face properly because he was too busy staring at her chest. However, one question had now been answered: the reason why Elisa and her group were after us.
This is all because of that thing.

No. 3112: Guardian’s Wrist Guard was an expensive numbered item that traded for a whopping fifty million stones on the exchange. Since the application Hikurod had submitted was for a promotion, there must have been a section on the sheet asking about it. That was more than enough motive for a plunderer. The more money you had, the better.
Were we a target from the start, then?

As I acquired this new information, a correlation that I didn’t consider earlier suddenly occurred to me. Most of our team meetings had been held at a bar. It wouldn’t have been too difficult for them to figure out that we were going to use the Den of Beasts route if they wanted to, and it would have been possible for them to get there first to set a trap.

“They say fortune always brings misfortune. I guess there’s no better way to describe this situation,” the dwarf said with a deep sigh. It seemed like he wanted sympathy, but unfortunately, he chose the wrong companion for that.
Fortune brings misfortune? “Don’t put the blame in the wrong place. Isn’t it your fault for filling out the application where everyone could see?”
“A-Are you blaming me right now?! You were there too!”
Yes, but I didn’t think I had to babysit you while you were doing something as simple as that.

I looked at him like he was pathetic. Hikurod kept his mouth shut, at a loss for words. I didn’t bother saying anything after that. It was already in the past. It would be more sensible to get some rest.
My rest didn’t last very long. I only barely got to close my eyes. In less than thirty minutes, a monster appeared, so we had to wake up from our sweet sleep.
Oh, well, “we” wasn’t really the right word here.
“You really slept soundly.”
“How could you sleep thrrrough all that noise?”
I guess I was the only one who had slept deep enough to even dream, but that was only because these guys didn’t know how to adapt. “Anyway, where is the monster?”
“Over there.” When I looked where Hikurod was pointing, I saw the shape of a winged man about the size of my palm. “It’s a fairy.”
A rank-nine monster, its only skill was the ability to spit out poison powder mixed with narcotic substances. In the game, it was classified as a monster that wouldn’t attack first.
Except... The fact that there were so many fairies in one place had to mean that guy was also nearby. “I guess we’re starting with a headache.”
“Are we going to fight?” Hikurod asked.
Brown nodded. “Since they’re not monsters you often see, yes. Dwalkie’s condition has also improved.”

I guess that meant we were going to fight. Well, I wasn’t against it. From my point of view, this was a monster that had not yet given me experience points. Plus, it would be great if an essence happened to come out. Although it was an essence that I did not need now, it was a rare one, so no matter which one of us absorbed it, it would definitely sell for a high price.
“Then if everyone is ready, I’ll get their attention.” After making brief preparations for the coming battle, the dwarf raised his battle hammer and used his signature combo.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Lightning. Hikurod Murad has cast Release.]

Lightning Release: at the exact moment the hammer swung, the electric current that had been crackling inside of it shot out in the form of cannon balls and mercilessly blew up the fairies, which were immune to physical damage.
[You have killed a Fairy. EXP +1]
I wasn’t sure about the other stuff, but this I was a bit envious of. I thought it would be nice to have one of these elemental damage-dealing abilities.
“Keeeeeeeeek!”

Anyway, as soon as ten of the fairies exploded, we heard something chilling in the distance, a roar that sounded like hundreds of beasts simultaneously growling in anger. Before long, it appeared from the darkness with heavy, thundering footsteps.
Boom!

A rank-seven monster, the Half-Troll. As the name implied, it was not a real troll but almost a mixture of a human and a troll. It was a monster that only appeared in the Witch’s Forest, and it had a habit of stalking groups of fairies. Unfortunately, I had never learned the reason for that. That lore couldn’t be found anywhere in the game.
Anyway, enough idle chitchat.
“Grrr...”

The eight-foot-tall monster hunched like it was wary of us. However, as a monster faithful to its nature, its patience did not last long. “Kyaaaaah!” The Half-Troll swung its gigantic club at us for slaughtering the horde of fairies it had been following around. But instead of aiming at the dwarf beside me, it aimed at me.
Boom!

It was powerful, more so than the Iron Tusk at Ironrock Hill. I guess that made sense since, even though they were both rank-seven monsters, the Iron Tusks lived in packs. It had been a while since my arm had been this sore.
Slide.

I tilted my shield and let the Half-Troll’s club slide past me. Then, as a natural consequence, the aggro shifted from me to Hikurod. This technique could be used when there were two tanks in a party. It wasn’t fair if I was the only one having a hard time, right? I had learned recently that sharing burdens was what a team was for.

“Kyaaah!” The second clubbing was followed by a scream. Hikurod’s small shield groaned slightly as his bones jolted from the shock. It was then that I realized something. “Ugh...” He had no pain resistance.

This was one of the biggest reasons why warriors typically avoided the Witch’s Forest. A warrior was usually beaten up on the frontlines, but here, the pain was multiplied several times thanks to Pain Enhancement.
At the same time, more than half of the monsters that spawn here are immune to physical damage and have some kind of psychological skill.

There was a reason that Brown had wanted to give me and Hikurod the first and last night watch. In the Witch’s Forest, warriors inevitably had to face all kinds of hardships. Since I had a Pain Resistance stat, however, I could brush it off, which was a blessing in disguise.
Pain Resistance is literally such a cheat stat.
The Essence of the Corpse Golem I had absorbed by coincidence continued to be a great help to me.
Voom!
The Half-Troll swung his club again. The dwarf, who unlike me was stubbornly engaging in a power struggle with the monster, shouted, “Is the spell not ready yet?”
Not yet. You know he takes forever to cast a spell.
“Behelahhh!”
Hikurod looked like he was having quite a tough time, so to help him out, I whacked the Half-Troll with my mace. Of course, it was pretty pointless.
Smack!

Its hard bones and muscles didn’t budge under the force of a single blow, and even though it was only half of one, this was still a troll. Its regeneration was phenomenal, though still nothing compared to a vampire’s.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight spell, Freeze Enhancement. The power of the next ice-type spell is greatly increased. Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight spell, Ice Lance.]
After I ping-ponged the aggro back and forth with Hikurod for a while, the spell was finally complete. This was Dwalkie’s specialty: Reinforced Ice Lance.
Shoooooot!

The ice lance, double its normal size, flew forward and pierced through the Half-Troll’s abdomen with a force greater than anything any of us could imitate. However, I just found this extremely frustrating.
When will this kid learn to read the situation?

Although I had given him some advice last time, he once again shot the lance somewhere unhelpful. If it had been aimed at the heart or head, it could have killed the troll in one shot. Why was he being so wasteful? Was it that hard to aim?
“Keeeeee!” The Half-Troll screamed in agony, writhing in pain, but that didn’t last long.
[The Half-Troll has cast Frenzy. Its pain temporarily disappears, and any Physique stats increase significantly.]
Although it had a lance stuck in its stomach, it started jerking around and flailing like a fish out of water. Ha... this was why he should’ve killed the thing in one shot.
He’ll get better someday, right?
I really hoped so. Otherwise, there was no point in suffering through all of this trial and error.

“Ah! It was a little shallow!” While I was busy fighting the frenzying Half-Troll, Missha drove a poisoned dagger into its heart. Unfortunately, it was too short to pierce through the thick muscle, and the crossbow bolt Brown fired barely pierced its skin.
In the end, we have no choice but to wait until Dwalkie casts the spell again.

Dwalkie was still the only damage dealer on the team to be able to cause significant harm. I was once again becoming very aware of our weaknesses. The tank line was sturdy enough to fight against a Half-Troll in a Frenzy state, but the damage-dealer line wasn’t able to keep up. But that was something that couldn’t be rectified at this particular moment.
“It’s done! Back up!” After another ten minutes of a strength contest, Dwalkie once again performed his signature. Fortunately, this time, it hit the head.
[You have killed a Half-Troll. EXP +3]
As the head blew off, the Half-Troll disappeared into the light. Naturally, the essence I had been hoping for did not appear—only a single mana stone the size of a fist.
“How unfortunate. That’s not an easy monster to run into.”

Missha and Brown licked their lips like they had been looking forward to the essence. It was not that I didn’t understand. If this had been before I got the vampire’s essence, I would have been drooling profusely too. A rank-seven regeneration essence was uncommon, but my body wouldn’t be satisfied with that kind of thing anymore.

It was 7:13 a.m., the morning of the fourth day. Tomorrow we would reach the fourth floor, and our real journey would begin from there. Rank-six monsters appeared up there too, and my one hope was to find one rank-six essence—no more, no less.
“Let’s go, then.”

After defeating the Half-Troll, we resumed moving. Everyone seemed to be tired from staying up all night, but the Witch’s Forest was not a good place to rest. We decided to reduce the time required to reach the fourth floor as much as we could, even if that meant we had to push ourselves for the day.
Except...
“Adventurers.”

When we were just about to resume our journey, unfamiliar adventurers emerged from the darkness. That shouldn’t have been all that surprising even in the Witch’s Forest, since we’d been killing time at the entrance for a while. It was about time for a new group to enter.
However, there was one problem.
One, two, three, four... What? Why six?

Generally, a party consisted of a maximum of five people. This was because you could only tie five people together with bonding magic. But a team of six adventurers? As I stared curiously at the group, I thought I spotted a familiar face. Sadly, she seemed to recognize us too.
“...Adventurers! It’s them! They’re the ones who killed my comrades!”
Fuck... I really hadn’t expected this to happen.

When all of us stood there gaping at those words, the man who appeared to be the leader of the opposing party of adventurers drew a large cross in the air. “May the blessing of the twilight star be with you...”

Judging by all of the Reatlas-themed religious symbols he was wearing, he was presumably one of this world’s rare religious zealots. Damn, that bitch was lucky. How the hell did she find someone like this guy in the labyrinth?
“God, grant me the strength to destroy these seeds of evil!”
This probably couldn’t be resolved with a conversation.

chapters.title: Chapter 58: Rules of Survival (1)
paragraphs: “H-How did that woman manage to follow us! Didn’t you say the Witch’s Forrrest was safe!?” Missha shouted, looking visibly exhausted.
“Tenacious bitch!” said Hikurod.

I agreed with that too. But if I were to logically process this situation instead of simply cussing... that fucking bitch would not have been able to track us down the second we entered the forest, which was why she would’ve searched for a suitable adventurer to manipulate, pretending to be a poor priestess who lost her comrades to vicious plunderers.
“Look, there seems to be some kind of misunderstanding. That woman is a priestess of Karui—”
“What!” cried the adventurer. “I see now that they are not mere looters, but followers of an evil god!”
“No, it’s not us, it’s Elisa—”
Hikurod tried using his words, but the man whose brain was apparently pickled by god’s blessing could only hear what he wanted to hear. “Come lay down your necks and be punished by god!”
“Sir! Please give those evil people the iron mace of the Lord! That way, my comrades wandering the afterlife will be able to let go of their grudges and return to god’s arms!”
In sync with Elisa’s plea, the opposing party of adventurers pulled out their weapons. It was the same for us. In conversations with adventurers, sometimes fists spoke louder than words.

“Don’t worry about injuries, just focus on killing your enemies! The blessing of Reatlas will be with you!” After telling them Elisa would heal them even if they fought like dogs, the leader of the opposing party charged at us with eyes ablaze, shouting out that fucking slogan: “May the blessing of the twilight star be with you!”
To be honest, it was hard to understand why they would do all this to help that bitch. That guy seemed to be a devout believer, but the other guys didn’t have to play along with this.
“Fight your hardest! If we kill them, our party will earn a priestess!”

“Ohhh!” So that was it. They were trying to kill us for practical reasons, not religious ones. Now that I knew that the bitch had apparently promised them some sort of reward... Okay, I understood the situation to some extent.
Boom!

Once I took the leader bastard’s axe with my shield, I planted the seed of discord. “You dumb fucks!” I shouted. “Which one of you will leave the party once the priest comes on?” These bastards had been a team of five from the get-go. If a priestess joined, someone else would have to be kicked out.
As I pointed this out, the leader exclaimed, flustered, “D-Do not be swayed by their evil wit!”
What evil wit? It was obvious they hadn’t even thought this far ahead. “Uh, huh?”
As if to prove my point, the four adventurers other than the leader paused for a moment. Unfortunately, that didn’t last long.
“Um, but it probably won’t be me?”
“Hey, isn’t that something to think about later?”
“One of us might even die today.”
“I don’t care about the priestess. Just selling their equipment will make enough money for me to fuck around for a whole year.”
Fuck, I forgot these were adventurers. Every single one of their reasons was psychopathic.
So all you guys need is money and a cause, huh? Yeah, actually, it’s better that you never change.

I built a shield wall with Hikurod and analyzed our opponents’ combat power. Three melee warriors, two long-range fighters, and one priestess in cosplay... Like most adventurers who entered the Witch’s Forest, it was safe to say that the difference between our levels was almost nonexistent. They even had one more person than us. This time, there was nothing more to analyze. Even considering that Elisa was currently unable to invoke the power of the evil god because of her disguise, we were clearly at a disadvantage. If I were to come up with some sort of strategy...
The only option is to plow them down with a single surprise attack.
I immediately called out to the wizard on our side. “Dwalkie!” No lengthy sentences were needed.
“Ten seconds! Just wait ten seconds!” Dwalkie replied as soon as I called his name, proving he was more experienced now.
But the other side wasn’t lacking in experience, either. “Wizard! There is a wizard on the other side!” Noticing Dwalkie’s existence, the other party focused their attacks on him.
The three melee warriors could have been covered by me and Hikurod, but it was physically impossible for us to block the arrows and projectiles that flew toward the chanting Dwalkie.
Whip!
But I wasn’t too worried. We were a team of adventurers, weren’t we? I didn’t have to do it all by myself.
“Ugh!” Missha struck down a flying arrow with a dagger, and Brown blocked a projectile-type ability with a shield. By then, the spell was complete.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight spell, Ice Lance.]

It was not a reinforced ice lance, but it didn’t matter. Our opponent wasn’t even a large monster. This would be enough to send them back to the arms of god in one blow. Of course, that was based on the assumption that it would hit somewhere vital.
Whiiip!
Preparing to cast magic at people, not monsters... The time to test Dwalkie’s earlier determination came much sooner than we expected. What decision would he make?
Bam!
Despite my worries, the ice lance flew right at Elisa’s head. Unfortunately, it wasn’t a hit. This was the reason adventurers were tougher to fight than monsters.
“Wow, that was dangerous. Are you all right?”
“Y-Yes! Thank you for saving me!”

The other team had realized that an attack spell had been cast and that it would probably be aimed at the priestess. There was no reason for them not to be able to block it. Any adventurer heading from the third floor to the fourth should be capable of that much.
Once again... humans are the most annoying bastards of them all.

We weren’t making good progress. Just as Brown and Missha had been able to successfully protect Dwalkie, our opponents were uninjured by our attacks. It was time to come up with a final solution. By now, we’d tested the waters enough.
“Dwalkie! Cast a Voice Control spell!” I ordered in a tone that brooked no further questions.
“A-All right!” At my strong command, Dwalkie cast the spell without any objections.

Voice Control was, simply put, a convenient spell that allowed a team to communicate. Now, even if we talked to each other, the other side wouldn’t hear us. I glared at my opponents aggressively and shouted, “Hikurod!”
“What is it?”
“Let’s bounce!”

“Hahaha! That’s a great idea!” Fortunately, the dwarf who had the right to give us orders in emergencies like this agreed with my judgment. Hell, he wasn’t that stupid. Even if we won this battle, it was likely to end in injury. And once we were hurt, that crazy bitch would use the power of her dark god without hesitation. No matter how much effort we put in, the future that awaited us here was bleak.
“Missha! When you’re ready, get Dwalkie!”
“Okay!”
“Hikurod, you use that item when I give you the signal!”
“I will!”
Missha and the dwarf nodded without argument. That left Brown with the most important task, but I didn’t need to tell him what to do. With a single glance, he understood what I was thinking.
“When I leave, everyone, follow me closely!” Brown was the only one here I could count on. Anyway, it seemed that there was nothing more to communicate at this point. “Now!”
The moment I gave the signal, Missha finished getting ready to run with Dwalkie on her shoulders, since he had weak stamina. At the same time, the dwarf’s wrist guards began to shine.
[Hikurod Murad has used Guardian’s Wrist Guard.]
No. 3112: Guardian’s Wrist Guard.
In the game, the item reduced damage to the user by 5 percent, and it had the effect of increasing the user’s power in proportion to the reduction in damage. But it had another effect as well.
[All enemies are knocked back by a powerful blow and all allies temporarily become immune to all harmful effects.]
Wide-range knockback and debuff removal. As a numbered item in the 3000s, it took precedence over Field Effects.

[Status effect Loss of Direction has been deactivated. Status effect Auditory Hallucination has been deactivated. Status effect Visual Hallucination has been deactivated. Status effect Pain Enhancement has been deactivated.]

The moment the three melee warriors were flung away, our skewed field of vision returned to normal and became brighter, but it didn’t last long. I didn’t know how much of a beating Hikurod had received since the start of the battle, but it would only get us about twenty seconds maximum. This time also took into account Hikurod’s special ability, which increased the efficiency of Numbers Items by 1.5 times. However, this would be sufficient time for us to run away.
“What are you doing? Run!”
Somehow, it seemed like we were being chased all over the place during this quest.

The first person to sense an enemy’s movements and guide their party members to an optimal route was the scout. Some might ask, what qualities did you need to become an adventurer? The answer was extremely simple: data accumulated from prior knowledge and experience in the labyrinth. With just these two things, you could find your way around the first and second floors, not to mention the third floor, which was a kind of open-world concept where the topography didn’t change.
However, from the fourth floor on was a different story. Actually, to be more accurate, I should include the Witch’s Forest, where the portal to the fourth floor was located, in that too.
[The duration of the Guardian’s Wrist Guard’s effect has ended. Field Effect – Witch’s Forest is now active.]

Our compass was dead, we were completely lost, and the only landmarks were trees that also moved like they were alive. Therefore, a scout’s special talents would be necessary from here on out if we were going to find our way.

“This way.” Brown’s main ability was his sense of smell. Having changed his olfactory stats through an essence, he was able to accurately navigate us to the fourth floor even in this ghastly forest. When your sense of smell reached a certain level, you could smell the scent of mana, which allowed people like him to find their way around. I didn’t quite understand it, but that was roughly the way it worked.
“It seems the scout on that side isn’t a normal person either. They’re closing the distance to our exact location.”
Those motherfuckers were still following us expertly. Of course, I couldn’t even sense their presence. But if Rotmiller said they were, then it had to be true.
Then, in the end, the deciding factor is who gets to the fourth-floor portal first.
While I was analyzing the current situation in my mind, Brown spoke as if he was of the same opinion. “Let’s speed up from here.”

It was a race against time now. If we could get there first, we could forgo any unnecessary battles. On the other hand, if they caught up to us before that? Then we would have no choice but to fight until one of our parties was defeated.
The problem is that everyone is tired...
Life just didn’t turn out the way you wanted it to—even more so if you were exhausted.
“Miss Karlstein, give him to me!” Hikurod decided to take over Dwalkie for Missha, and this was where disaster struck.

“Ah!” Their mistake was that they attempted to hand off Dwalkie while still running in order to save just a little extra time. Missha lost her balance and fell. Fortunately, Hikurod managed to grab Dwalkie, wrapping him around himself like a backpack.
“Cramp! I think I have a crrramp in my foot! It won’t moooove!”
Yeah right. It was obvious she sprained it when she fell. “Don’t move and stay still.” I immediately stopped, grabbed Missha by the back of her neck, and lifted her up.
The moment I put her on my shoulders, the light disappeared and a deep darkness shrouded my vision.
The fuck? What’s this now? Hikurod was just beside me holding the torch...
“B-Bjorrrn?”

“...Hush.” I calmly opened my backpack and took out a torch. Then, I lit a fire by measuring the distance with my hand and then put it into the groove of my helmet. Unsurprisingly, the party members who had been next to me just a few seconds ago were now nowhere to be seen.
“Did we lose them?!” Missha pretty much screamed.
I didn’t want to believe it, but... “It looks like... we have.” In a matter of seconds, we had been left behind.

“Then what arrre you doing! Follow them!” Missha hurriedly urged when she realized what was happening, but I chose to stay put. How was I supposed to know where they went? “That way! They must have gone that way!”
That was just what it seemed like to us. In the Witch’s Forest, you couldn’t rely on sight. If we headed down the wrong path and ended up traveling away from the party, we’d only be wasting our time.

“In times like these, it’s best to stay still.” Trust your comrades and your own judgment. Wasn’t Brown an olfactory scout? He must’ve noticed that we were missing by now and would be coming back to find us.
“Hey, Bjorn...?”
Without a doubt, that should have been the case...
“How long do we have to wait?”
A minute had passed but the party still hadn’t come back. Damn it, what was going on? Should I wait longer?
The moment my worries intensified, I heard a brief, faint scream somewhere in the darkness. “Aaagh!”
“Bjorn! Did you hearrr that? It was clearly Hikurod’s voice!”
I couldn’t be sure, but that seemed to be the case. It made sense—they would’ve already come to find us unless something else happened to them. Except...
“They must be in trrrouble. We should go help—”
“Lower your voice.”
“Why?”
“Because we might end up in trouble too.”
It was not a good idea to make noise. We still didn’t know what was happening over there. If it was simply a monster encounter, they would have had enough time to come find us.
“Which is another rrreason why we should go hel—”

Even if I wanted to help him, there was no way. Maybe if I could hear some kind of continuous sound coming from that direction at a certain volume, but otherwise I wouldn’t be able to track him just from the screams of a man in the throes of death. The Witch’s Forest was that kind of place.
“Mm!” That was why I covered Missha’s mouth with my hand for now and focused on listening.
“...miller... bitch is... there.”
“...make a g...”
“Ha... can’t... and leav—!”
“At least... scout... defe... so... can run...!”

After that, I heard several more faint shouts that sounded like final death throes, and soon they disappeared altogether, swallowed by a forest where even the slightest breeze couldn’t be heard. Silence fell around me, but I stood still and waited for about five more minutes. There was no sign of our missing party returning. It was too early to know for sure whether they were dead or alive, but one thing was clear: waiting any longer was not going to bring them back.
“We’re fucked.”
That meant I had been left alone with a beastgirl in a labyrinth of monsters and plunderers, in the middle of the Witch’s Forest, which was impossible to get out of without a scout.
Fuck.

chapters.title: Chapter 59: Rules of Survival (2)
paragraphs: What was the most important thing in an emergency situation? Water? Food? Health? Tools? Well, these were all very important, but if I had to choose just one, I would choose “having the right mentality.”
“Nooo... I can’t die like this, I can’t! I went through all that for nothing!”
“Missha, calm down.”
When you find yourself in a shitty situation, you need the courage to face reality instead of trying to hide from it. Only then can you gain an objective perspective. So, I pushed aside all my fears.
It doesn’t matter what happened over there.

A strange monster may have appeared, or Elisa and that party may have launched a surprise attack in that brief span of time. Anything was possible. But that was not what I needed to be focusing on right now.
Think.

I was now separated from the group. Next to me was my beastwoman teammate, but unfortunately, she was a warrior who could only use moves that dealt physical damage. The chances of our lost comrades returning here seemed infinitely low. Yes, in a word, we were fucked.

This place, which was inhabited by monsters who were immune to physical damage, was also known as the Graveyard of Warriors. It was almost impossible to get through it with just a barbarian and a beast warrior. On top of that, we also had pursuers after us.

Actually, that was the biggest problem here. If the two of us ran into them, it would be an immediate game over. But unless we planned to bite down on our tongues and take ourselves out, we needed to think. Not about how fucked up this situation was, but about what we needed to do right now. What actions should we take in the future? Even if that was no different than trying to resist our doomed fate kicking and screaming, what did we need to give up and what did we need to prioritize for our survival?
Simply put, what was the best thing we could do in this situation?
“...Let’s move.”
“What did you say? Even though—”
“Even if we can’t find our way, it’s better to get out of here.” After getting an objective grasp of the situation, I could see what needed to be done even if we were in the worst possible situation.
After organizing our options into a list of priorities, I decided to address them in order of importance. First, getting out of this place.
“It’s too dangerous here.”
My reasoning was simple. We had no information as to what Hikurod and the others had run into nearby except that it was dangerous enough that they couldn’t come looking for us.
“And if that bitch was the one who did something to them, she’ll eventually find us too.”
“But then, wouldn’t she have shown up by now?”

Well, maybe we just got pushed down in her priorities because the dwarf ran away and she had to follow him, or maybe there was some other explanation. I had no intention of pondering the ifs, ands, or buts in this situation. And the first things we had to sacrifice in order to survive were intangible things like warmth and kindness.

“So what are you going to do? The choice is yours.” I had no intention of carrying dead weight around with me just because she was my teammate. You couldn’t even call that a real team in the first place. So, I drew a clear line in the sand. “If you don’t agree with my judgment, we’ll travel separately from now on.”
“W-What are you talking about?!”
“Answer me.” I didn’t intend to waste time arguing. It was a yes or no question.
Missha, who was wordlessly staring into my eyes, bit her lip and came to a decision. “...I will follow yourrr lead from now on. I can’t do anything else as long as I’m injured anyway.”

This was a great answer that showed an understanding of exactly what the person asking the question wanted to hear. I hadn’t thought of her that way, but it seemed she was actually quite quick on the uptake. Despite how she usually acted, she had five years of experience for a reason.

“S-Still, you’re too harrrsh!” Once my hardened expression relaxed, Missha started whining like I had hurt her feelings, but oh well. I didn’t care about that as long as she followed my orders efficiently.
“Drink.”

When I opened a bottle of potion and handed it to her, Missha drank it slowly, as if she was drinking poison. Then she started to moan. Not the weird kind; that wasn’t something you could do after taking a potion anyway.

“Ugh!” Based on the sounds of her suffering, it was clear that the potion was doing its job, so I put Missha on my shoulders. Since it was just a sprained ankle, the pain would subside in about five minutes and she’d be able to walk, but it would be nice to save that time. “Ah! Please, slowly! No, walk morrre gently!”
As soon as I started to properly jog, Missha started begging me to stop. Apparently, she was experiencing motion sickness. All I could say to that was, “Deal with it.”

I’m sorry, but right now, I’m a coldhearted barbarian who has forgotten all warmth and kindness. As long as the survival alarms are blaring, efficiency trumps all. A little bit of motion sickness never killed anyone, right?
Sprint.

Anyway, while I was running through the forest with no particular direction in mind, Missha started smacking my back like crazy from her perch on my shoulders. “Let—ugh! L-Let me down! I-I’m all good now!”
“Don’t lie.”
“It’s trrrue! I-I swear on the name of my clan’s guardian!”
“Hmm, then why is your voice so weak?”
The loophole I pointed out in Missha’s argument was a logical one, but for some reason, I was the one who got reamed. “How could it not be! You boneheaded barrrbarian! Let me down now!”
“Okay.” If she was able to pound me on the back like that, that meant she at least had the presence of mind to move on her own, so I let her down as requested.
“Ahh, I rrreally thought I was going to die!”
How dramatic. At least she looked fine on the outside, but I double checked just in case. “So, is your foot okay now?”
“As you can see.”
“Give it to me straight. Does that mean you can fight right now?”
“Forrr now... yes! But why do you ask?”
Because we had a fight coming our way. “Good. There’s a monster coming.”

Missha’s head turned in the direction I was pointing. There stood a gigantic tree that was planting its roots into the ground as it moved, a rank-eight monster called Snetree. It was a creepy creature that attacked adventurers with its tentacle-like branches. For reference, this guy was one of the few normal monsters aside from the Half-Troll in the Witch’s Forest. In other words, it was possible to take them down just with physical damage.
“But do we need to fight that thing? Since it’s slow, it won’t be able to follow us... Ah! I’m not saying I won’t follow your orrrders, though!”
Well, good, I was glad. Anyway, the question itself was reasonable, so I took a moment to answer it. “It may drop an essence.”
“An essence?” Missha cocked her head like I’d just said something strange. That was understandable. If it weren’t for the situation we were in, I wouldn’t have come up with a plan like this, either.

“All of the monsters in the Witch’s Forest have attribute-based abilities.” To be more exact, all of the monsters except the Half-Troll. Well, even if one of those guys happened to come out, we would just avoid it anyway.
Soon, Missha grasped the gist of my plan and was stunned. “Is that why you want to fight this one?”

Yep—not just this one, but every single one that appeared in our path. I had to acquire an attribute-based ability somehow. We couldn’t keep avoiding spirit types forever. As things were right now, I wouldn’t be able to get a good night’s rest in here. Although, if we happened to find a way out of the woods while we wandered around, then that would be an unnecessary concern.
But there’s no way a miracle like that would happen to me.

Of course, the drop rate of an essence was also infinitesimally small, but in a way, this was basically just a side quest. I had no intention of getting hung up on this plan. If an essence came out, great, and if it didn’t, there was nothing I could do about it. That was all.
The moment that bitch finds us, it’ll all become trivial anyway.

If the scouts on the other side killed the dwarf or lost track of him and then came looking for us instead, then all of these efforts would be in vain. But that wasn’t a reason to go gently into the night.
“Anyway, get ready to fight.”
“Okay!” A moment later, Missha pulled out her weapon, raised it, and charged at the Snetree, which was using its roots to crawl across the ground.
“Glurggleggleggle!”
The number one rule of survival was this: you had to fight to live.
[You have killed a Snetree. EXP +2]

We were walking through the Witch’s Forest without a scout. If anyone asked me how I felt about that, I would answer like this: it was like walking through a house of mirrors in an amusement park all day, if the house of mirrors happened to have constant background noise.
“Just kill her! Or enjoy her! Why are you being so nice to such a useless bitch?”
“Khihee, khiheehee!”
“It’s all your fault! If it wasn’t for you—!”
Was I mistaken, or were the auditory hallucinations getting more detailed? No, I didn’t think that was it. The visual hallucinations were also more vivid than before.
“Hansu, why are you the only one who survived?”
Unlike earlier, when the hallucinations had taken the form of mere monsters, now they were individuals from my past, people I would never be able to run into in this world.
“It hurts! It hurts! It hurts!”
When are you going to kill that girl? When are you going to kill that girl? When are you going to kill that girl? When are you going to kill that girl?
Sometimes they showed up in the form of visual hallucinations and wreaked havoc on me. At some point, the visual and auditory hallucinations began to merge.
There is no way that the Field Effect has suddenly gotten stronger. Is it just that I’ve gotten weaker?

I calmly and coldly assessed my condition. However, it was what it was. I had stayed up all night, and in that state, I had been forced to fight a fierce battle. I was cursed not too long ago and just barely came back from death’s door, and now I had found myself in a hopeless situation and also lost. It was only natural that I had hit my mental limit. But, so what?
I have no choice but to endure it.
That was how life went, at least for me. Persevere, persevere, persevere, and do the things you could without dwelling on the things that you could not change.
“Missha, use this instead of a dagger.”
“Hmm? I’ve never used a spear beforrre...”

After defeating the Snetree, I took a break and rifled through my expandable backpack, handing Missha the spear that used to be Irita’s. We decided earlier to sell it and distribute the payout when we got back out to the city, but now wasn’t the time to worry about stuff like that.
“Just do as I say.”
“Hnnng, okay...”

Out of respect for each person’s preferences and years of experience, I had been keeping my mouth shut about this, but my working theory was that the longer the weapon, the more practical it was. Even when Missha had been fighting the Snetree earlier, if it hadn’t been for the dagger’s length, she would’ve been able to dig in deeper and destroy its core in one hit.
“It feels so awkwarrrd! Can’t you give me a sword instead?”

No. I didn’t know which one was easier to handle, a sword or a spear, but I did know that a spear was a lot longer. When I made a wall with my shield, a spear would make it easier for her to help me out from behind. “You’ve fought with both weapons before. Just use that one.”
“Hnng.”
Quit your whining. I don’t know what you think is going on here, but I don’t consider us to be that close.
I wished she would stop complaining and ruining my mood. After all, it hadn’t even been two weeks since we’d met.
This... I should use.
It wasn’t just Missha who upgraded her equipment.
[You have equipped Iron Plate Gaiters. Your total Item Level has increased by +45.]

First, I wrapped Hans C’s gaiters around my calves. The gear was made of leather on the inside and iron on the outside. It would’ve been nice if I had the part for the thighs too, but unfortunately, that piece of equipment was stored in the dwarf’s bag.
[You have equipped Worn War Boots. Your total Item Level has increased by +38.]

I also changed my shoes to new ones, the ones Hans C had been wearing as well. The boots were made of quality leather, but strangely, they had iron plates on the top, and in the form of pointed spikes at that.
Adventuring assholes are only useful when it comes to things like these.
I looked around for additional items, but I couldn’t find any more that Missha or I could use among the equipment I had on me. However, instead, I found something unexpected.
“Huh? Bjorn! Isn’t this holy water?”
“...Looks like it.”

Pieces of bad news had been piling up one after the next. Was it now time for things to slowly start to recover? This made me so much happier than finding the gear. With holy water, it would be possible to enchant our weapons.
[Sacred energy permeates the enchanted equipment. You now inflict additional holy damage when attacking monsters with the Evil attribute.]

The additional damage granted by the Holy attribute meant that even if we didn’t get the attribute-type abilities we’d been hoping for, we’d be able to slaughter spirit-type monsters. Although it was limited to evil-attribute monsters, the spirit-type monsters that appeared in the Witch’s Forest usually had the Evil attribute, so I didn’t need to worry about that.
The problem is that there are only five bottles.

Holy water had no time limit. The effect just disappeared once all of the damage the bottle was capable of causing had been done. How many monsters could we potentially fight with five bottles? I wasn’t sure, but it wasn’t near enough for generous use until the fifteenth day, when the third floor closed.
It would be best to use it sparingly.

Still, this was the first bit of good news in a while, which was why I continued to dig around in the bag. Earlier, I hadn’t had the time to look through the exploration supplies properly. There could have been something else that was useful.
“Hmm? Bjorn!” As we were each rummaging through our bags, Missha called my name. “I found something weirrrd, do you know what it is?” It was a pendant with an unusual design. I recognized it.
Isn’t that the symbol of Karuiism?
Unfortunately, that was all I knew as of right now. Besides the fact that it was related to Karui, I couldn’t figure out its purpose.
At this point, I think I’ve checked everything I need to for now.

I put everything back into the bag and organized it. Then, since there was the new variable of the holy water to consider, I also revisited the plan I had quickly thrown together. At first glance, we had three options.
One: seek help from an adventurer we happen to stumble upon by coincidence.

The Witch’s Forest was huge. Due to its geographical characteristics, it was rare to encounter other adventurers. However, if we kept looking around, we’d come across one eventually. If we promised to give them equipment in exchange for help, any adventurer would be tempted.
The problem is that we won’t be able to trust them.

There were a lot of efficiency freaks among those adventuring bastards. They could just kill us and take our stuff for themselves. Why would they bother helping us on top of that? Some of them might think like that.
Besides, Missha is a girl...
As I glanced at Missha, who was currently hungrily eating jerky, I continued thinking.
Two: walk around until we reach the end of the forest or find the portal to the fourth floor.

That, however, would just mean relying on luck. Therefore, I decided that it was not necessary to set this as our ultimate goal. Like it or not, we were going to have to wander through the forest anyway. It wasn’t like any amount of wishing was going to make a path appear, and no amount of non-wishing, either.
Anyway, next.
Three: Focus on surviving until the labyrinth closes.

We had enough food and drinking water. Moreover, by securing holy water, it was possible to establish a low level of immediate safety. If an elemental essence came out along the way, our odds of survival in this damned forest would increase dramatically.
That’s all under the assumption that those bastards won’t find us, though.

I let out a long sigh. It had only been four days since we had entered the labyrinth. There was much more journey left to go than had elapsed. When I thought of all of the things we had experienced over the past four days, it was hard to assume the rest of our time here would be smooth sailing.
I don’t think an essence will appear anytime soon. If I’m going to do it at some point, might as well do it now.
So, I decided. “Missha, are you married?”

“Huh? Where did that come from?” Missha, who was chewing on a piece of jerky, was startled by my question. It was clear she was wondering what the hell I was talking about. Still, since she had agreed to hear me out, she gave me an answer. “I’m not at the moment...”
Okay. I asked another question, this time a more direct one. “Then do you hold any particular beliefs, such as one that would prevent you from showing your naked body to a strange man?”
“Uh, n-no, I don’t think so...”
“Good.”
“W-What exactly is good? Ah! S-Stop! D-Don’t come any closerrr!”
This was an option I would never have chosen if I hadn’t played Dungeon and Stone for close to ten years. A pity to use it already, but it was our best bet.
Four: Awaken Missha.

chapters.title: Chapter 60: Rules of Survival (3)
paragraphs: To save time, I took off the ring first. No. 9425: Ring of the Frost Spirit, was a Numbers Item I had obtained by tricking an old man who happened to be the master of the school of Altemion.
“Here, take it.”
“Huh? A ring? Why...?” Missha took the ring without much thought, but her expression soon changed to one of alarm.
“It’s a ring I’ve been saving for the right person.”
“But... why are you giving it to meee?”
That was because things had changed. “Swear to your guardian spirit,” I said shortly, “that if you accept this, you will continue to be by my side in the future.”

The market price of the Ring of the Frost Spirit was 1.5 million stones. However, since there was no available stock for sale, it was difficult to obtain even if you wanted to buy it. If the true value of this ring was known, its price would skyrocket.
“Huh?! Bjorrrn! Have you gone insane?!” Missha screamed, scolding me, but my head was clear as day at the moment.

What, did she think I’d just give this to her? I was choosing to use it for our survival, but I needed a promise that she would continue to follow and help me in the future. Of course, this was not a one-sided contract. “The moment you accept this ring, I swear on the honor of a warrior to be by your side and help you in the future. So, I want you to do the same.”
“Are you being serrrious...?”
To prove just how serious I was, I looked into Missha’s eyes. “I am sincere.” This would be a win-win in the truest sense of the word. It was a kind of pledge of comradeship.

Picking up on this, Missha stared at me in surprise for a while and soon spoke with a voice free of any playfulness. “...It’s very sudden, but I can tell you’re not saying all this to mess with me. To be honest, this is the firrrst time I’ve ever received an offer like this, so it’s not that I’m not happy!”
“Then I’m gl—”
“But I’m sorry, Bjorn. I’ve neverrr thought of you like that.”
“...What do you mean?”
Missha squeezed her eyes shut. Then, she met my gaze with determination. “I... I like skinny men,” she replied.
“Skinny men...? What does that mean? I don’t understand—”
“Eeet! It means that you have no charrrm as a man!”
For a moment, my mind went blank. Was this what it was like to be rejected when you weren’t even confessing? One thing was certain, however. “...You’ve misunderstood.”
“Yeah, let’s just go with that. We have to keep working togetherrr, but this will only make it awk—”

What was this kid talking about? I guess it was my fault for not speaking more directly in order to avoid seeming elitist. I forgot we barbarians had our own way. “What I meant was that I want you to make a pledge of comradeship in return for this ring.”
“Pledge of comradeship...?”
“Of course, you can end the contract at any time if you find another one of these rings or give me a payment of fifteen million stones. Do you understand now?”
“Y-You think?! What the hell is this rrring that it costs fifteen million stones in the first place?”
“Fifteen million is actually cheap for this ring.”
“No, I mean, what the hell is this thing—?”
I cut her off. “This ring can make your long-awaited desire come true.”
“...What? Dream?”
“For example, if you take it, your brother will no longer be able to call you a half-wit.”

Had I touched on something I shouldn’t have? Missha stiffened, but after thinking it over for a moment, she gave me a strained smile. “Wow, you think I’d fall for that? No matter how embarrrassed you are, you shouldn’t lie—”
“It’s not a lie.”

The conversation stopped for a while, and silence fell between us. Missha, who had been smiling awkwardly up to this point, was no longer doing so. Instead, she shot me an icy look. “This isn’t something to joke about.” Her voice was uncharacteristically cold and hard. “I clearrrly gave you the chance to backpedal, so why do you keep lying? Do you think I’m some kind of fool just because I keep laughing at your jokes?” Missha angrily bit her lip. “...I shouldn’t have told you about my past.”
This reaction was unexpected, but it made sense. A wound that had been picked at and burned for the entirety of someone’s life was bound to hurt at the slightest touch.
“I didn’t bring this up to reopen old wounds. I really—”
“I have never hearrrd of such a thing. How do you know something that not even my clan knows about?”

Instead of answering, I kept my mouth shut. This wasn’t something I could offer a detailed explanation for, nor did I want to. We couldn’t stay here forever. I decided to end this quickly. “Missha, let me ask you one thing.”
“Go ahead.”
“If everything I said so far were true, would you accept my offer?”
“Still joking at—!”
Cutting her off before she could get worked up again, I shouted back, “Answer me!”
You just have to answer the question. Yes or no.
As I loudly demanded an answer, Missha flinched and bit her lip again. “...If all of what you said is trrrue, even treating you as my benefactor until the day I die wouldn’t be near enough. But—”
“No buts. That’s it, then.” I took a step closer and grabbed her wrist. “Missha Karlstein, it may be hard to believe, but I swear on my honor as a warrior that everything I have said so far is true.”
“....W-What?” Missha looked baffled. Seeing this, I wondered if it would have been easier if I had used the oath of a warrior sooner. Well, it didn’t matter now.
“So, when you wake up, keep your word too.” I yanked Missha toward me and put the ring on her finger.
Crack!
Then, I smashed the blue glass jewel on the ring with just the force of my fist.
[The Ring of the Frost Spirit has been destroyed. The seal on the Ice Beast Skadia has been released.]
Like ripples on the surface of a lake, a wave of cold air rolled across the earth.
Whoosh!

When no. 9425: Ring of the Frost Spirit was destroyed, it activated a unique effect. In the game, choosing to destroy it was practically pointless because doing so dealt no damage, but I was able to make a discovery after various experiments.
[The special conditions have been met.]
If the wearer was a beastperson, something else happened at the time it was destroyed.
[Ice Beast Skadia has offered Missha Karlstein a contract.]
It would forcibly awaken the beastperson’s innate special ability.
[The contract has been successfully completed.]
A gust of cold wind wrapped around Missha like the eye of a typhoon. As it slowly subsided, Missha opened her red eyes. In her gaze, there was a complex, yet somewhat blank look.

Missha stared at me and spoke. “It was so easy... Why did I spend all that time...” Then, with a look of betrayal, she asked, “Bjorn, what the hell is this rrring? If there was such a thing as this, then why didn’t my father tell me about it?”
I didn’t know whether the beastpeople were aware of the existence of this ring, but in the interest of giving her the answer that she wanted... “Perhaps he didn’t know, either.”
“...He didn’t know?”

“Yes. It seems that some wizard only recently learned about its effects after researching it for a long time. It’s probably not that your father didn’t think of you as his child and hid it from you on purpose.”
This explanation would be better for her mental health. But even with my answer, Missha seemed to be full of questions. “Wait, then how the hell did you know? Where did you get this rrring?”

This wasn’t difficult to explain, because I had pre-planned explanations. But before that, there was one thing that needed to be done. “It would be better to talk after you put on some clothes first.”

“...Clothes?” Missha cocked her head, then tilted it downward, following my gaze. When she confirmed her current state... “Uh, ah? Huh? W-W-Why am I naked?!” she screamed, malfunctioning like a robot.
“I left your clothes folded beside you, so let’s talk after you put them on.”
“A-All right...” After I turned around, Missha picked up her clothes and dressed. “Y-You can turn back arrround now.”
“That was fast.”
“What, should I have taken my time!?”
I turned around and saw that Missha was in casual clothes, a thin garment that was worn under most equipment and armor. Because it fit tightly, the curved lines of her body were more clearly defined.
“Aren’t you going to wear any gear?”
“Beforrre that, answer this! Why was I, uh, ah, naked?!”
“That’s because I undressed you.”
“U-U-Undressed?! Y-Y-You?!”
“I had no choice. I heard that all the equipment on your body would disappear during this ritual.”
This was a lie. I hadn’t just heard about it, but experienced it myself. Fuck, I had worked so hard to level up that character, but when all my equipment reset, there was nothing I could do.
“...W-Wait! Is that why you asked me that question at the starrrt?”
“Question?”
“Whether I was marrried or not.”
Oh, that. I nodded honestly. “If you had a spouse, that would have made you uncomfortable.” I was a proud Korean Confucian. I could never undress a married woman with my own hands.
But Missha screamed at me like that was ridiculous. “Someone who was able to think that far ahead somehow didn’t think to warn me what would happen in advance?!”
“I had no intention of keeping it a secret. But you didn’t believe me at all anyway.”
“Y-Yes, but...” When I countered all of her questions with reasonable explanations, Missha had nothing more to say.
I could be a little more tough on her now. “Actually, because I had to undress you in a hurry, you can imagine the hardships I went through. Tsk. Why do you have to wear so much gear?”
“...I-I’m sorrry.”

“Before you apologize, isn’t there something you should do?” I looked straight at her, beating around the bush a bit. In situations like these, the rule was that you had to be as patronizing as possible.
“...Thank you.”
“Is that it?”
Missha thought it over for a moment before speaking again. “...Thank you verrry much?”
“Don’t try to avoid it. Isn’t there something else that needs to be properly addressed?”

“D-Do I rrreally have to say it?” Missha avoided my gaze with a shy, embarrassed look on her face, but I wasn’t the type of person to let her get away with that. These sorts of things should not be left unsaid.
“Of course.” At my stubborn reply, the look in her eyes changed, suggesting we had reached the limits of her playfulness.
Like she had had no intention of skipping over this from the beginning, she straightened her shoulders and met my eyes head on. “Bjorn, you know... I... in the past... trrried to kill myself.”
What now? I’d honestly had a feeling that was the case, but for now, I just listened to her solemn tale.
“It was my fatherrr who found me and saved me back then.”
“You must be grateful to your father, then.”

“I wish I could be, but... It’s not all that pleasant a storrry. When I woke up, you know what the first thing he said was? That if I really wanted to die, I should die in the labyrinth. That I should stop brrringing shame to our family.”

Ah... uh... um... Her family was turning out to be shittier than I’d thought. As I was seriously contemplating whether I should correct the inaccurate assumption I made just a few seconds ago, Missha calmly continued.

“That’s why I first entered the labyrinth. Of course, I didn’t come here to die as my father suggested. I just wanted to rrrun away from home. Even if I didn’t have a Soul Beast, I hoped that if I became a great adventurer and got recognition for it, my father would look at me differently.” In that rough, restrained voice, I could hear all the emotions she must have felt growing up. “Of course, I don’t know if my fatherrr will accept me because of this. But somehow... Now I don’t really care.” Then Missha bowed at me. “...Thank you, Bjorn. I will not forrrget this kindness for the rest of my life, and I will keep it close to my heart until I pay you back.”

Even if that promise might end up being diluted by time someday, it seemed silly to doubt Missha’s sincerity now. But anyway, enough New Wave drama. “You swear on your guardian spirit?” I asked after hearing her out.
Missha grinned and nodded. “I swear on my guardian spirit.”
Okay, nice and easy.
Summoning, Strengthening, Special Ability—a beastperson who made a pact with a Soul Beast generally acquired one of these three abilities. Missha had gotten Strengthening.
[The power of the ice beast Skadia resides permanently in Missha Karlstein’s body.]
Aside from an improvement in physical stats, the Freeze attribute was always granted to the user, hence why my stomach was cold from her punch.
“Ah! I punched you because you told me to, but I didn’t know that was going to happen! A-are you all rrright?”
My skin was red like it had been frostbitten. I smiled at the sight.
It’s a pity that she didn’t get a summon or special ability, but... Still, this is something.

After that punch, I was even more certain. The long-awaited attribute-based attack strategy was now solidified in my mind. With this, it would now be possible for us to beat up some spirit-type monsters.
“Huh? Snap out of it, Bjorrrn! Why are you laughing like an idiot?!”
“It’s nothing. Let’s go. We’ve been in one place for too long.”
After tidying up our surroundings, I led Missha out of there. We tried fighting against a rank-nine spirit-type monster, a Wraith, that we ran into along the way.
[The Wraith has cast Corpse Fire.]

Corpse Fire was an active skill that combined dark and fire abilities. Its strength was lower than that of a rank-nine spell, and for me, with the dark resistance of a vampire, it only felt warm. In truth, most of the spirit-type monsters in the forest had low combat power compared to the rest of the monsters in their rank. They had really only been difficult to deal with because we had had no means of attacking them in the beginning.
[You have killed a Wraith. EXP +1]
With my holy water-sprinkled mace and Missha’s two frosty fists, we beat up a group of about fifteen Wraiths.
“Hmm, it feels weirrrd every time I hit something.”
The reason she used her fists instead of a spear was simple.
I guess the first stage of the awakening doesn’t apply to weapons.

Just as there were stages in a barbarian’s Spirit Imprint, a beastperson’s Soul Beast contract also developed gradually. Still, it was fortunate that Missha had originally been a fighter. I was pretty sure she used to fight with just her fists until she noticed her limits and switched over to a dagger, which likely seemed like the easiest weapon to adapt to.
[You have killed a Witch’s Lamp. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Dairouter. EXP +2]
[You have killed a Mutant Low-Rank Spirit. EXP +2]

Anyway, after that, we continued to wander through the forest. We slaughtered all the monsters that we saw as long as we didn’t have to push ourselves. In addition, whenever there was an opportunity, we rested as much as possible and preserved our stamina.
[You have killed a Woodman. EXP +1]
[You have killed a Homunculus. EXP +2]
[You have killed an Owl Bear. EXP +2]

About eleven hours passed like that. We hadn’t encountered any rank-seven monsters yet, but the lower-ranking ones weren’t difficult to defeat. There hadn’t been any precarious situations, either. Contrary to what we had feared, there had been no sign of the bitch, Elisa, coming to look for us yet.
Did something happen to them too?
That could be the case, or it might not be. Rather than holding out hope that things would be easy, I continued to prepare myself for the opposite by doing everything that I could do in the moment.
Ha... still no essence.
That left a bitter taste in my mouth. With holy water and the ice beast Skadia, we were able to hunt spirit-type monsters without any problem, but still, not much had changed.
About 30 percent.
That was what I thought our chances of returning to the city safe and sound were.
[It has been 12 hours since you entered the Witch’s Forest. Field Effect – The Witch’s Forest has strengthened. Status effect Witch’s Eye is now active.]
The real test of survival started now.

chapters.title: Chapter 61: Rules of Survival (4)
paragraphs: The evening of the seventh day—that is, about eighty hours after we got separated from our party in this goddamned forest—I was still there, wandering through the woods and blankly watching the hallucinations getting worse by the fucking day.

This was the change that had occurred at the start of our second day together: we didn’t speak unless it was necessary. Not because we were on bad terms or anything—we just no longer had the strength to do so.

Oh, there had been one other development. I used a rope to connect Missha and I together by using the same kind of knot used to weave oysters on a line. This was a technique I had naturally picked up after spending so long in the Witch’s Forest. This way, even if one person fell behind or to the ground, we could rely on the rope to find each other.
“Bjorn... slower, go a little slowerrr...”
“Okay.” I slowed down.
This morning, Missha’s condition had rapidly deteriorated. It wasn’t due to an illness or a serious injury; it was just that her fatigue had finally reached its limit.
Trudge, trudge.
I slowed down for her, but I still felt a tug at my waist. She couldn’t even keep pace at this speed. After contemplating for a moment, I stopped walking. “Get on.”
“Huh?”
“You’ll feel better once you get some rest.”
“B-But...” Missha trailed off and looked at me. Honestly, my offer must have been funny. If you judged exclusively by our outward appearances, I was in much worse condition than her.
I bet she’s never seen such a roughed-up barbarian.

My underclothes were torn and covered in random holes, and even my iron equipment was corroded all over. These were all side effects of awakening Missha. The passive skill of the Corpse Golem had reactivated when I removed the Ring of the Frost Spirit. Grazes from battles with monsters were a daily occurrence, and my current state was a result of my acid blood.
The repairs alone are going to break the bank.
I smiled bitterly. My lithinum breastplate and shield were made of grade two material and were in good condition, but their former brilliance and pure white beauty had long since been lost.
But Missha seemed to misunderstand my smile. She opened her mouth worriedly. “I-I am fine. You should rrrest instead. I’ll carry you!”
Thanks for the offer, but... Do you think that’s realistically possible?

“Just come here.” Rejecting any further argument, I grabbed Missha’s waist and lifted her up. I could feel lethargy radiating from her light form. She didn’t even have the strength to resist. “I’ll wake you up if there’s a problem, so get some rest until then.”
“But—”
“Hush.”
“...Thank you.” Missha draped herself over one of my shoulders and finally gave in, but she wasn’t able to fall asleep right away. After a while, she spoke up in a small voice. “Bjorrrn?”
“What is it?”
“You know something?”
“What?”
“Mm, smells good...”
What smells good? At least finish your sentences.

I was curious about what she had been about to say, but... I was sure she was just sleep-talking. There was no way a body covered in blood and dirt that hadn’t been washed in several days could smell good.
Before long, I heard the sound of slow, steady breathing, which made me laugh.

I’m telling you, you guys don’t know how good you have it. No matter how many hallucinations come your way, if you’re really tired, you can fall asleep anywhere. That’s how the human body is designed. It has to be able to survive in any environment. Anyway, let’s keep moving.
I continued walking through the forest with Missha draped across my shoulders. I was tempted to put her down and get some rest myself, but I couldn’t do that.
[It has been 84 hours since you entered the Witch’s Forest. Field Effect – The Witch’s Forest has strengthened. Status effect Witch’s Eye has been upgraded to level 5.]

The field debuff Witch’s Eye was the real reason why the Witch’s Forest was seen as an area you should only ever pass through. Its effect was simple. If you stayed in one place for a certain amount of time, the rank-seven monster Carnivaro would appear, and that amount of time gradually decreased as the level went up. It had started off as one hour on the first day, and now...
It should be about ten minutes.

That pretty much meant that we couldn’t afford not to move at this point. The problem was that there were two of us. If a Carnivaro appeared, we didn’t have any allies around to stop it, and at this point, we’d pretty much be dead meat if one showed up since it took at least fifteen minutes to kill one even when we had the stamina. Theoretically, another bastard would appear before the first one even died.
That was why I kept walking. I felt like passing out from fatigue, but I had to walk. Otherwise, things could get really bad.
Still, seeing as how they haven’t appeared yet, does that mean I can stop worrying about them now?

Distracting yourself is the best thing you can do when you’re tired. After finishing one train of thought, I moved on to another topic. Today marked four days of being lost in the Witch’s Forest. If that bitch Elisa had the means to find us, she would’ve done it by now. It seemed that we could rest more easily now.
That eliminates our biggest problem, at least.

I didn’t know why they hadn’t been able to find us, but if I were to take a guess, they must’ve run into an unexpected problem as well. Just like how I’d fallen behind with Missha. Life was shitty because you never knew what would happen or when.
Anyway, how long had I been walking to avoid those monsters? Hmm, it had to have been at least an hour.
“Oppa, why are you leaving her alone?”
I raised my head at the familiar hallucination.
“You’ve granted her lifelong wish... If you seduce her the slightest bit, she’ll totally drop down for you.”
A woman wearing a white blouse and suit skirt appeared next to a tree and looked at me with her characteristic arrogant and harsh gaze. It was my ex-girlfriend.
“Is it because you are afraid of being abandoned again?”
Ugh, fuck... Up until now, it had been obvious that these were hallucinations, but this one was different. It felt like if she walked toward me, I would be able to feel the heat coming off her body.
“Oh, you’re sly.”

What now? Because this hallucination had come straight out of my head, its mannerisms were exactly like the real her. Did that mean that all the hallucinations I’d been hearing were actually based on my subconscious mind?
“That’s the problem with you. You always have to know everything.”
Can’t deny that, I agreed. Fear of ignorance was an instinct found in all living things.
“Still, you’re too much. When you never even reveal anything about yourself...” she said.
You were the same way.
“Pardon? What do you not know about me? You know every corner of my body even better than I do, remember?”

My eyes shifted unwillingly at the coquettish voice. There had been a new development with the visual hallucinations. The white blouse and the short suit skirt... they were the same as before, but black stockings were now on her long legs. Previously, they had been flesh-colored.
“Your taste is the same.”
Fuck, was this the kind of person I was?
“Get rid of that beast girl and come to me. You need to be with me. No one else will ever understand, right?”
Was that true? Without realizing it, my feet moved forward. That was the moment.
“Make me feel good—”
The face of my ex-girlfriend, smiling bashfully with her arms wide open as if to embrace my everything, was suddenly bizarrely distorted. Not metaphorically, but actually.
Smack!

Her facial muscles were crushed with a single punch. For some reason, Missha, who should have been on my shoulders, was bashing my ex-girlfriend’s face in with her fist. And repeatedly, too, like the high-agility character she was.
Smack! Smack! Smack!
What was this? Was this also a hallucination? I watched the scene unfold like I was dreaming.
“Kyaaaaah!” A scream that sounded like nails on a chalkboard resounded, bringing me back to my senses.
At some point, Missha, who had beaten my ex-girlfriend to a pulp, came back and shook me by the waist. “Bjorn! Are you all rrright?”
“Uh, yeah...”
“I got rid of the dryad, so wake up!”
What? Dryad? The rank-eight monster that used Charm and made very rare appearances in the Witch’s Forest? No wonder the hallucination had been so detailed.
[You have killed a Dryad. EXP +2. Status effect Charm has been deactivated.]
I suddenly understood what had happened. I hadn’t been hit with the field effect but a skill. “Thanks... If it wasn’t for you, this would have been a disaster.”
“Hmm, it was noth—” But at that moment, Missha stiffened and pointed somewhere. “Uhh? B-Bjorn? I-I think the disaster has already struck...”
After looking at where she was pointing, I nodded involuntarily. “...Looks like it.”

Had it already been ten minutes since I was put under the Charm effect? Near a bush not far away, the rank-seven monster Carnivaro was slowly walking toward us with murderous intent gleaming in its eyes.
“I... will... kill... you...”
Carnivaro was classified as a humanoid undead, and had a fairly high level of intelligence. The problem, though, was that it only used that intelligence to kill people.

“Blood... flesh... give... me...” The Carnivaro aimed a crossbow at us. Already salivating, its protruding fangs were glistening with fluids. I didn’t know about Missha, but being a barbarian, I probably looked quite tasty. Considering I had low body fat, I would probably be a bit tough to chew though.
“Missha, stand behind me.”
“O-Okay!”

Sending Missha to the back, I blocked our openings with a shield. Now that we’d encountered it, it was no longer possible to run. The Carnivaro chased its prey to the bitter end. In fact, its fighting style was similar to that of a hunter.
[Carnivaro has cast Mana Mine.]
It set invisible traps in the vicinity. The moment we approached it, a strong explosion would detonate. Therefore, it was difficult to quickly close the gap between us.
[Carnivaro has cast Chasing Arrow.]
The arrows flew in with a power incomparable to that of a goblin archer, and with a high level of precision correction. Therefore, it was better to block them than to avoid them.
Clang!
I took an arrow shot directly at me and bounced it off to the side. Last time, I had blocked the arrows while Missha threw stones that were lying around to detonate the mines.
We don’t have time for that now.
We had to kill this monster within ten minutes. Otherwise, another one would appear and the process would repeat over and over again until we were dead. We only had one option now.
“Missha, get on my back.”
“What are you talking about?” Missha was picking up stones she could throw. She cocked her head, but I had no time to explain.
“It seems we’re going to have to push ourselves right now. So hurry and do as I say.”
When I spoke firmly, Missha got onto my back. Immediately, I sprinted forward, protecting my head and upper body with the shield.
Kablam!
The landmines dotting the ground nearby exploded with every step, but I kept running.

“W-What are you doing?!” Missha screamed at me, but to be honest, this wasn’t particularly odd for me. Since waking up in the body of a barbarian, I’d been able to overcome most crises with just my body. This was exactly the same—the only option I could choose in this shitty situation.
Kablam!
The pain broke through my Pain Resistance. Every time an explosion sounded, I could feel my legs getting torn apart.
[Carnivaro has summoned a Hound.]
Meanwhile, a pack of summoned wild dogs rushed in. Arms, shoulders, thighs, legs—they dug their teeth in everywhere and tugged their jaws side to side aggressively.
Kablam!

Still, I did not stop walking. I continued on, defending myself from the flying arrows and pushing off the hounds by using Flesh Explosion. It was at that moment that the tenth mine exploded, and my body suddenly swayed.
Bang!
I tried to reach my other foot out to find my balance but I soon realized it was pointless.
How fucking disgusting.
It was hard to describe the limb below my leg as a foot anymore. It was more like a crushed piece of meat.
Well, since we’ve come this far, I’m sure she’ll figure it out.
As soon as I realized that going any further forward was impossible, I threw Missha as far as I could. “Take care of it.”
I received no verbal response. However, Missha answered me by leaping into the air.
Stab!
Missha, who did some agile somersaults in mid-air, drove a spear into the Carnivaro’s shoulder instead of his head, a mistake caused by her lack of proficiency with the weapon.
Stab!

However, she made up for her mistake by rotating her body using the spear as an axis, then pulling out the dagger she was wearing on her waist and stabbing it into the monster’s forehead. The time it took her couldn’t have been longer than five minutes. Anyway, we got through another crisis. Satisfied with that fact, I collapsed.
[Warning: a part of your body has been lost. If not treated promptly, this may lead to permanent injury.]
After the battle was over, Missha hurriedly ran toward me. “Bjorn!” she yelled. “What werrre you thinking?!” She looked angry, but also like she was about to cry.

“This was the best option,” I replied simply. There had been no other choice. And right now, what Missha needed to do wasn’t scolding or worrying about me. “If that’s enough explanation, can you give me a potion now?”

Missha’s eyes had gone blank as she took in the sight of me indifferently giving orders as I lay on the floor with my feet crushed. However, my request had still penetrated her skull, apparently, and she poured the potion on me with trembling hands.
Chhhhhh!

It was an advanced potion that cost a whopping two hundred thousand stones per bottle. As expensive as it was, it was an essential consumable that could even repair amputated limbs. But Missha still looked worried.
“T-This kind of injurrry can’t be fully healed with a potion...”
Well, I wasn’t sure about that.
[Your regeneration factor is greatly increased thanks to the Eternal Life effect.]

Between the Immortality Imprint, the high healing factor granted by the vampire’s essence, and the active skill Eternal Life, in game terms my natural regeneration level was easily over 150. Even if it wasn’t an advanced potion, given enough time, it was possible for me to recover from a limb amputation injury. If it wasn’t for that fact, I wouldn’t have done such a crazy thing in the first place.

“W-What?! T-There’s no way it should be healing so quickly...” Missha was astonished to see that the effect of the potion was making the wounds quickly knit back together. As far as she knew, I only had the essence of the Corpse Golem.
In less than a minute, my crushed leg was healed. Unfortunately, I was barefoot.
Should I have taken off my shoes before I ran? Those boots plus the potion would have sold for at least 150,000 stones.

It was too big of a loss to call it an investment for a rank-seven monster, but there was no point regretting it now. I opened my backpack, put on the leather boots I was wearing originally, and got up slowly.
Okay, I think my toes feel normal again.
“Bjorn, what the hell are you?! You’rrre not even in pain from the potion!”
“It is the spirit of a barbarian.”
It was true. Ainar had never groaned when she took potions, either. Although I was running purely on Pain Resistance. Well, it was just the outcome that needed to be the same, right?
