chapters.title: Chapter 62: The Hut (1)
paragraphs: “Let’s move quickly.”
We hurriedly left. After going through all that trouble to hunt a Canivaro in five minutes, there was no time to rest.
“So, are you okay now?”
“Now that I got some rest, I feel betterrr. Thanks. But how long did I sleep?”
“Probably about three hours.” That was a lie. In reality, it couldn’t have been more than one.

“T-That long? No wonderrr...” In technical terms, this was called the placebo effect. Thinking she slept that long would be more beneficial to her mental and physical health. Although I was starting to become the problem now. “Bjorn, you don’t look good.”
Having slept, Missha was no longer falling behind. However, my speed was rather slow now. That was to be expected. Just because my natural recovery rate was high didn’t mean my fatigue would go away.
“I’ll carry you. Why don’t you get some rrrest?”
I mean... thanks for the offer, but how does that make sense?
“It’s okay, I can handle it.” Of course, I was tired. I’d probably pass out in one second if I were to lie down right now. But... “Let’s speed up a little more.”

Again, there was no other choice. A cool analysis of my current condition told me that even if I pushed myself as hard as I could, I only had a few hours left in me. After that, mental fortitude or not, my body wouldn’t be able to stand anymore.
“Speed up?”
“Yes, that’s the only way.”

We needed to find a safe place while I still had stamina. Such places were randomly generated in the Witch’s Forest at regular intervals and would exist for eight hours. The field effects were nullified there, and no monsters appeared, either. In other words, you could sleep safely.
“But what if we can’t find it?”
Well, then things will get a lot worse.
Still, the last time we found the safe zone had been two days ago. At this point, it was likely to appear again.
I don’t know about me, but she seems to have some luck on her side...
Just look at the last time we found a safe zone. We had been taking a break because she was whining that her leg hurt when a safe zone appeared right next to us.
“From now on, you take the lead.”
“M-Me?”
“Just go where you want to. It’s not like we know our way around here, anyway.”
I didn’t believe in superstitions, but I put Missha at the forefront just in case. We moved quickly by destroying only the proactive monsters we encountered.
How much time had passed?
“Huh? Bjorrrn! Look over there! Isn’t that it?”
“...Looks like it.”

Some people seemed to have all the luck. To our surprise, in less than thirty minutes, we found an unusual tree. It looked similar to the other trees around it, but a soft purple glow was radiating from the bark. It was a sign that this was a conduit that would take us to the safe place.
“Good job, Missha.”
“Hehe! You can prrraise me more!”
What was she saying? After ruffling her hair to indicate that she did a good job, I approached the tree and, together with Missha, put my hands on the bark.
[You have entered the Witch’s Hut.]
The moment we put our hands on the tree, a purple mist wrapped around us. Before long, a warm wind reminiscent of a spring breeze blew to disperse the fog that had been covering our surroundings.
Shaaa!

Eventually, when all the fog disappeared, the gloomy forest was nowhere to be seen. The floor beneath us was a lawn in full bloom. The skinny thorns covered with rotten vines had been replaced by an abundance of leaves.
“Bjorn! Look at this! Aren’t the flowerrrs pretty?”
Yeah, sure. But since I already noticed that last time...
“Don’t do anything pointless and go in and rest.”
“Hnng, you unromantic barbarian!”
Romance? That’s only for people with the freedom to be romantic. Being a romantic while you were on the verge of starving to death only made you seem like a poor person who was lying to themselves.
Creak...

Leaving behind Missha, who was strangely energetic, I opened the door of the central hut. There was one bookshelf, a dining table, a carpet, and a stove. Despite the fact that it was called the Witch’s Hut, there was nothing special about the interior. It was an ordinary hut that anyone could come up with.
Still, I think Raven or Dwalkie would have liked it.
Wizards loved unusual spaces like this. There were also books on the bookshelf, so they would have checked those out as soon as they arrived.
But I was a barbarian, and a very exhausted one at that.
Slump.
So I went straight to the bed and collapsed on it. Then I buried my face in the pillow and muttered, “This time, you sleep on the chair.”
Reaching my physical limit, I sent Missha to the rocking chair I slept on last time.
“A-All right! You must be tirrred, so get some rest.”
Crackle.
As I closed my eyes, I heard the sound of wood beginning to burn in the fireplace. Missha seemed to have sat down too, because I could hear the sound of creaking at regular intervals.
Creak, creak.
“...Good night, Bjorrrn.”
My consciousness gradually faded away.
Was it because I was exhausted? I was dreaming for the first time in a while.
As always, I was at work. I was working on administrative stuff, and once I finished, my ex-girlfriend came to greet me.
...Wearing black stockings.

Anyway, we went back to my place and ordered chicken and each did our own thing. I played games and she read a book quietly in the corner. A peaceful silence ensued. When it was time for bed, we naturally curled into each other’s embrace and went to sleep.
That was all that happened in the dream.

As soon as I realized that all of it was just a dream, I was booted out back into reality. A small hut we had found while wandering through the Witch’s Forest... an old bed inside... and a large barbarian body filling it. Once that barbarian woke up from his slumber, he’d drag his monstrous body out to face monsters in order to survive. This was my reality.
...So let’s do what we have to do.

It didn’t seem like I could fall back asleep, so I turned my head to the fireplace. The fire which had been blazing bright before I fell asleep had lost its strength and was almost going out. This meant that the hut was about to close. I checked my watch to see just how long I had slept.
Still, I slept nearly seven hours.

It was quite fascinating that my body had woken up at the appropriate time without even an alarm. I forced my eyes open and looked up at the ceiling. As I slowly woke up, a strong headache erupted from the back of my head, like my brain was whining at me that it needed more sleep.
I knew that if I sympathized with such a feeling of weakness, there would be no end to it. And so I sat up.
When did she get here?
I didn’t know why, but Missha was sleeping with her body on top of mine, using my torso as a pillow. While also drooling. She seemed quite comfortable, because she was even purring with every breath.
Was the chair uncomfortable?

I lifted her head and moved it to the side, then got up from the bed. Waking her up early would help get her in good physical condition before it was time to leave, but I decided to let her sleep for now.
Crack!
I stretched out my stiff body, then went outside the hut to get some sun. To be honest, I was in a much better mood.
...Is this why Missha likes looking at the flowers?

When I thought about it that way, I could understand how Missha felt, but it was still a difficult sentiment for me to empathize with. Not that it was wrong, but it was just a matter of preference. Exposing yourself to the sun at least made you feel like you might be getting some vitamin D. Looking at flowers wasn’t even hypnotic. It was less effective as a placebo.
But anyway, I should probably wake her up now.
“Missha, wake up.”
“Mmmm, five more minutes...”
“Get up. We have to get out of here soon.”
“Then just until then...”
What was this kid talking about? She seemed incapable of rational thought because of her sleepiness, so I forcibly lifted her up by the waist. Then I shook her up and down.
“Ahh! Agh! O-Okay! I’m awake! Stop!”
“Sure.”
“You barrrbarian jerk!”
That’s why you should’ve woken up when I told you to.
I handed a canteen to a huffing Missha. I knew that she was grumbling, but not because she was really mad.
“...Oh, thanks.”
Now that she was awake, we sat next to each other and chewed on some bread and jerky. Although I didn’t have an appetite right after waking up, I knew I wouldn’t have time to eat once we got out.
“If you’re finished, you should stretch. There are only a few minutes left.”

“Okay.” Soon, Missha slowly stretched and warmed up her muscles. Because she was a high-agility character, her body was incredibly flexible. I was organizing my backpack in the meantime when Missha spoke up while stretching. “Uh, Bjorn...”
“What is it?”
“About Hikurod, Dwalkie, and Brrrown...”
“Spit it out.”
“What do you think happened to the thrrree of them? Do you think they’re still alive?”
Oh, so that’s your question.
I figured she’d ask about that. Humans had a tendency to start wondering about other things after their bodies got better. I answered without hesitation. “I don’t know.”
“Yeah, but you can make a guess.”
It wouldn’t be a guess but a wish. Before she launched into a needlessly lengthy speech, I cut her off. “No matter what I predict, it won’t change anything.”

Whether they were alive or not, it was pointless to worry. Even if they had found themselves in a difficult situation, what could we do when we were lost in the Witch’s Forest? We had to focus on surviving above all else. After all, we would inevitably know the outcome once we returned to the city.
“So if you’re done stretching, check over your equipment.” Because that was all we could do right now.
Crackle.
The last remaining log had gone out.
[The Witch’s Hut is closed. You will be moved to the Witch’s Forest.]
It was time to leave.
[Status effect Witch’s Eye has been upgraded to level 6.]
[Status effect Witch’s Eye has been upgraded to level 7.]
[Status effect Witch’s Eye has been upgraded to level 8.]
[Status effect Witch’s Eye has been upgraded to level 9.]
Day eleven of exploring the labyrinth. In other words, it had been almost eight days since I had been left behind in the Witch’s Forest.
[Status effect Witch’s Eye has been upgraded to level 10.]

Now we really didn’t have time to catch our breaths. We had to keep walking. Witch’s Eye should have entered its most powerful phase by now. According to my calculations, a Canivaro would appear if we stayed in one place for even three minutes.
Still, the fortunate thing is... for now, things can’t get worse from here. That is, assuming that nothing else pops up.
Of course, there was also the possibility of something positive popping up. For example, an essence, or an essence, or an essence...
Fuck.

Wandering through the Witch’s Forest, we had to hunt many monsters regardless of whether we wanted to or not, but no essence appeared. It was extremely unlucky. Any essence would increase our fighting power right now, plus some essences would be powerful enough to turn this situation around.
For example, this bastard’s.
“Bjorn! It’s a Witch’s Lamp!”
“Let’s take it down quickly and move on.”

The rank-nine spirit-type monster the Witch’s Lamp looked just like a goblin fire on the outside. It had low combat ability, so it could be dealt with using elemental powers without any issues. Its active skills were also garbage, except in the Witch’s Forest.
[The Witch’s Lamp has cast Witch’s Lamp.]

Its summoning skill, Witch’s Lamp, shockingly summoned a Witch’s Lamp. Yes, this bastard summoned itself. In other words, if you ate the essence of a Witch’s Lamp, you could summon a Witch’s Lamp too.
“Come to me, essence!” Missha chanted that spell and quickly defeated the Witch’s Lamps, which had quickly multiplied from one monster to six. However, once again, there was no essence.
Dang... getting an essence from this joker to use as a guide would secure our way out of this forest... I guess we have no choice but to hold on until the last day.

Realistically, that was the most plausible scenario since the third floor closed on the fifteenth day. If we could survive the next four days, we could return to the city. The problem was, though, that I couldn’t be confident that we’d even survive those few days.
“Missha, how is your stamina?”
“Mm, I’m pretty tired, but it’s not bad since we took that break earlierrr.”

Last night, we were lucky enough to find another hut to rest in for a while. The discovery had been made and the break had been taken after nearly fifty hours. In a nutshell, we hadn’t been able to sleep or eat properly at all during that time, and had just kept moving.
Plus, we discovered the hut pretty late, so we only had four hours to rest.

Finding a hut was pure luck. If we were unlucky, we may not find a single hut in the remaining four days. This was also why we’d been hunting Witch’s Lamps every chance we got since it was better to try everything we could.
“Bjorn.” Missha, who was leading the way, suddenly stopped, so I stopped too and looked ahead. “An adventurrrrer.”
For the first time since we had been left behind, we had run into a non-monster.
“A barbarian and a beastwoman? Is it just the two of you?”
We couldn’t be sure yet whether this was a positive or negative turn of events.

chapters.title: Chapter 63: The Hut (2)
paragraphs: It was day eight of being stranded.

While wandering through the Witch’s Forest without any direction in mind, surprisingly, we hadn’t encountered any adventurers until now. Given the terrain here, we probably should’ve come across at least one, but in truth, that wasn’t strange at all.

First, the Witch’s Forest was huge. Second, since it was not used as a main hunting ground, the population of people who took up residence here was small. Third, we were wandering aimlessly instead of heading toward the center. As a result, the chances of us running into someone were lower.
Plus, at this point, those who will pass through this place would have already passed it.

Still, I figured that when the third floor closed, some adventurers would come through here to go up to the fourth floor, since it was common to want to get a taste of a floor before you went up during your next quest.
So these people want to go up to the fourth floor?
That seemed very likely. Of course, that didn’t mean we could trust them.

“A barbarian and a beastwoman? Is it just the two of you?” Just as I judged them the moment I laid eyes on them, they also evaluated us. To be fair, it must be strange. A duo, not on the first two floors but the third floor, and in the Witch’s Forest at that.
The man, who seemed to be the leader of the team of five, reached a conclusion. “Have you two... been separated from your team?”

“That’s right.” I readily admitted it. It was good to bluff, but there was a time and place for that. If I tried to deny it while looking like a beggar like this, we’d just look suspicious. And what would we gain from insisting on denying it? Of course, I should still be careful.
“Ahh! Bjorn! Arrre we saved now?”
“Stay put.” I pushed back Missha, who was already getting excited, blocked the front, and slowly raised my shield.

“Don’t be so guarded. We’re not bad people.” A middle-aged human woman on the man’s side smiled warmly at us. “I have a son and daughter around your age in the city. I know why you’re worried, but you must be exhausted, so com—”
“No thanks.”
A son and daughter? So what? Rather, that made them seem even more dangerous to me. Having children to feed meant that her motives for earning money were even more apparent.
“B-Bjorn, why are you doing that? They may be able to help us...”
“Be quiet.”

How should I react if we come across an adventurer? I had thought a lot about that over the course of our travels. The conclusion I had reached was to first ask for help. Promising sizeable compensation in exchange for them getting us out of the forest would be a good deal for them too. Except, in order to make said deal, we had to find out what kind of people they were. Verification came first.
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
When I revealed my name, the leader of the other side responded in kind. “You are a very wary friend. I’m Hans Staub. I play the role of the scout on this team.”
But the problem was... “Your name... is Hans?”
“Haha, it’s a pretty common name.”
“Exactly.”
Why were there so many Hanses in the world? I deducted one point because of his ominous name.
“My name is Anuman Beit. In the city, my husband and I have a general store—”
I cut the woman off before she could start reciting her personal information at me. “There is no need for that.”

There was no way in the labyrinth to confirm whether that statement was true, and we did not have much time. Would we take their help or not? Whichever option we chose, we had to make a quick decision.
Two warriors, two archers, one scout.

I quickly swept my eyes over them and evaluated their combat power, faces, expressions, tones of voice, and vibes. Of course, it wasn’t necessary to closely examine each one. Sometimes intuition made for more accurate decisions. Experience and data were accumulated in the unconscious mind.
“Missha.” Soon, I made up my mind. There was no guarantee that this was the correct answer, but... “Will you go along with my decision?”
No detailed explanations were necessary here. As such, Missha gave a short, succinct answer to my question, one that likewise omitted many things. “Of courrrse.”
Nice. Now that I had her consent... “That’s enough introductions. We’ll be leaving now.”
“Leaving? Didn’t you guys need our help?”
Yes, but for some reason my instincts are screaming that you’re dangerous.
“Come to think of it, I don’t think we do. Missha, let’s go.”
“O-Okay!”
“Hmm, all right then,” said Hans. “There’s no reason for us to stop you. Goodbye.”
Okay. Now that I’d gotten them to agree, I slowly retreated with my eyes still on the group, covering my body with my shield.
That was the moment I heard the familiar sound of something ripping through the air.
Whip!
Before my brain could figure out what was happening, my body reacted.
Whip!
As my neck bent sideways, an arrow passed right by the side of my ear. Fuck, how did they do that? It flew in from behind me. The bastards who shot the arrow were definitely in front of me...
“Ms. Beit, what are you doing!” A member of the party shouted something at the archer lady. Had this not been mutually decided upon?

The lady who’d said that she had a son and daughter our age no longer spoke in a gentle tone. “You idiots! Didn’t you see the equipment he had? It’s made of lithinum! Do you know how much that sells for?”
“B-but they’re still adventurers...”
“If you can’t do it, stay out of it, kid. You see that backpack over there? It’s an expandable backpack. Something you won’t be able to buy even if you spend an entire year in the labyrinth.”
Perhaps it was true that she owned a general store with her husband. This lady had a good eye, although I wasn’t bold enough to compliment her on it.
“I-I can’t.”
“Then whoever wants out can back out.”
“I’ll join in. This isn’t my first time. I’m not in a situation to turn down free money.”
Originally adventurers, an agreement was quickly reached between them. I watched the exchange intently.
Missha anxiously grabbed my shirt. “B-Bjorn... shouldn’t we rrrun away?”
“Wait.”
They had a scout on their side. If we ran now, we wouldn’t get very far.
It should be here about now...
“I... will... kill... you...”
There.
I smiled sharply.
It was the only reason I had been trying to make a quick decision, be it sink or swim. When the Carnivaro emerged from the darkness, the group of adventurers who had been targeting us were startled.
“A C-Carnivaro?”
“Why are there two of them?”
That was because this was our eighth day as castaways. They may have just entered the forest, but we had already reached level ten of the Witch’s Eye.
“Missha, now.” I pulled Missha in with one hand, and with the shield in the other, I rushed forward instead of backward.
[Carnivaro has cast Chasing Arrow.]
[Carnivaro has cast Chasing Arrow.]
On our right, a Carnivaro notched an arrow on its bow. When I caught sight of it, I ran even faster.
Whiiip!

Eventually, my dynamic barbarian perceptiveness recognized that the two arrows had been shot simultaneously, but there was no need to worry about protecting my back. I now had something else to block them instead.
“A-Ahh! Stop them!”
“W-What the hell are these things?!”
The moment I pushed and shoved into the opposing group with the oblivious strength of a barbarian, I heard a scream. It was the kid who had said he wanted to back out. “Aaagh!”
Hmm, so the arrow hit you. Yeah, it’s usually the good guys who go first.
Bang!
“Agh! Fuck, my foot!”

An explosion sounded from the direction of the Carnivaro. When I glanced back, it appeared that Hans D, who had been startled by my sprint forward, had tried to fan out and had accidentally stepped on a mana mine.
“Mr. Staub!”
Okay. At this point, it looked like the aggro had completely gone their way.
“Missha, you run from now on.”
“O-Okay.”
I put Missha back down and then ran forward without looking back.
“What are you all doing! Don’t look at them, take care of the monsters!”
They wouldn’t be able to follow us for a while.

Dungeon and Stone was a roguelike game. Once you died, that was it. The character disappeared. Of course, at the end of the day, it was just a game. A character could be created again and new equipment could just be adjusted. The main point of this game was to advance to the next floor with the information you gathered from the previous attempt, anyway.

In Dungeon and Stone, death became a part of everyday life. But what if the world of the game became real life? Rebuilding a character was not possible. Whatever you saw, heard, or learned in this life lost meaning the moment you died.
And in that sense, I got lucky this time.
“But Bjorrrn, how the hell did you know that those people would act like that?”
“It was a hunch.” I had been right to follow the quick decision my subconscious had come to.

When Missha learned the truth, she couldn’t help but be stunned. “...A hunch?” No wonder she had agreed to obey me without asking questions. She seemed to assume that I had to have an actual logic behind my actions.
“Their leader’s name was Hans.”
“Sorry?”
“I hate that name.”
Missha just stared.
“Anyway, thanks to that we escaped safely, which is all that matters.”
“Yes, but...” Missha trailed off with a slightly uneasy look on her face and changed the subject. “Anyway, I never thought that kind-looking woman would turrrn on us so quickly...”
Missha trembled slightly, perhaps thinking about the old woman who had been glaring at us and screaming at the top of her lungs. Her rapid one-eighty seemed to come as quite a shock.
I didn’t know if it would be of any consolation, but I threw in my two cents. “She could’ve actually been a very kind person.”
“Hm? What do you m—”
“If only we hadn’t looked so weak.”

And if we didn’t have expensive stuff. If only we hadn’t run into each other in the labyrinth, but in the city, that woman may have been remembered as a kind person. However, instead, she had nocked the arrow on the bow and pulled it faster than anyone else.
“I don’t understand...she stopped being furrriendly to us because we looked weak?”
“Missha, why did you enter the labyrinth?”
“Because I have to earrrn money...”
“Those five were the same.”

Money was a means of protecting yourself, especially in a world where failing to pay taxes was punishable by death. There were likely many other interests that the woman was trying to protect besides her own life.
“...I think I learrrned a lot from this expedition.”
“Then move faster. They might come after us.”
We sped up some more.
How much time had passed? Despite my concerns, they did not reappear even more than an hour later.
The monsters may have attacked them first, but I’m sure two Carnivaros wouldn’t have wiped them out. Could there have been another problem?

Hmm, that seemed to make more sense. It may have been Hans stepping on a mana mine. If the scout had been injured, it may have disrupted their pursuit of us. Whatever the reason, that meant that one crisis had been successfully averted.
Please, I hope this ends with that.
Even as I thought that, however, I forced myself to remain vigilant. I vowed not to relax until the very end. As always, the shittiest things always happened when you let your guard down.
Day eleven of being stranded, and day thirteen of being in the labyrinth. The time was 7 p.m., exactly fifty-three hours before the labyrinth closed.
“Bjorrrn, I found it!”

We found a tree leading to a hut. Seeing as the light radiating from it had slightly faded, it seemed that quite a while had already passed since the entrance had formed, but beggars couldn’t be choosers.
It’s over.

The worst had somehow been avoided. Even if we could only rest for four hours, we could survive the remaining two days on willpower alone. In other words, the chances of us getting back safely had increased dramatically.
[You have entered the Witch’s Hut.]

Because every minute of rest was precious, I immediately put my hands on the tree and entered the area. The scenery beyond the portal was the same as before: the smell of grass and flowers, the idle chirp of grasshoppers, the sound of the wind blowing through the leaves.
Damn it all...
Sadly, in the middle of the peaceful pocket dimension was something foreign.
[Current number of visitors: 5. The entrance is now closed.]
Previous occupants. In other words, people who had discovered the hut before us.
“Bjorn.”
“Shh.”
I covered Missha’s mouth, scanning the area with my eyes as quickly as possible.
One on the bed, one on the chair, and one on the lawn.
Looking through the window, there were places I couldn’t see from this angle, but it would be logical to assume there were three people in total since the hut was limited to five people.
What a headache.
I slowly approached the man who was sleeping on the grass. Just then, rolling in his sleep, the man turned onto his back and faced us.
I flinched. Surprisingly, the face I was looking at was a familiar one.
I didn’t expect to see you here...

chapters.title: Chapter 64: The Hut (3)
paragraphs: Since being stranded in the Witch’s Forest, I thought about this from time to time: wouldn’t the others be wandering through the forest looking for us as well? If so, wasn’t it still possible for us to reunite with them by coincidence? In short, it had been a useless delusion.
No way.

Expectations and reality were never aligned. When I saw that the number of occupants was three, I’d had my hopes, but I smiled bitterly. Miracles weren’t my style, after all. I was more suited to tragedy.
“...Bjorn,” Missha whispered very softly into my ear, climbing onto my back. “What are we going to do now?”
Well, I’m thinking. I never thought I’d run into these bastards here, either. His name was... Davis?

As I prepared myself to smash his head in with my mace at any time, I closely inspected the sleeping man, Davis. The religious freak had a necklace, bracelet, and buttons all covered in symbols of the Reatlas religion. Simply put, he was the leader of the group of adventurers who had attacked us thanks to Elisa’s scheme days ago.
Why the hell is this bastard here?

The more I looked at this guy’s face, the more my suspicions deepened. Why was he resting here? What the hell did he do with Elisa for there to only be three of them? And why the hell did he look as roughed up as us?

After setting my suspicions aside, I looked into the hut again through the window. Fortunately, the other two were still sleeping. Since I knew that they were his teammates, I could infer their identities based on their hair color and body type.
Those must be the bow and the sword guy.
The large shield warrior and red-haired archer were nowhere to be seen.
...Could it be that they were also separated from their group?
The thought suddenly came to mind, but I couldn’t be sure. Dang it, what should I do? This was making me anxious. Should I just smash his head in while he was asleep?
As I was contemplating this, Missha whispered to me, “Bjorn, we might even be able to learrrn about what happened to Hikurod and the others.”
Hmm, that was true. It seemed a conversation was in order. Before that, though, we needed to create the appropriate environment for a conversation.
“Let’s knock them all out first, then tie them up with ropes.”
“Good idea.”

After reaching an agreement, I escorted Missha into the hut so that if they woke up, I could subdue them before they came to their senses. Once the preparations were complete, I exchanged glances with Missha through the window and nodded. Then, lifting the mace up into the air, I slammed it down on his head with half my strength.
Smack!
As expected, the religious freak sagged without even making a sound. I let out a long breath, wiping the blood and bits of flesh from my clothes.
Whew, one down.
Now it was time to stun the next one.

When I snuck into the hut, I found the other two completely passed out from the hard journey and lost in their respective dreams. Which one should I take care of first? After thinking for a while, I noticed one of them tossing and turning.
Yeah, this guy should be good. Just as I was about to bring down the mace, Missha hurriedly grabbed my arm and cried out in a hoarse whisper, “You said you were just going to knock him out!”

I cocked my head, then belatedly realized what she was getting at and nodded. “Don’t worry.” Even in fighting games, low-damage blows were my specialty. I was confident in my ability to control my strength. And, well, if he died, then that was just bad luck. That was how the world worked, wouldn’t you agree?
Smack!
The moment the mace struck, the man resting in the rocking chair slumped. At the same time, the man on the bed heard the sound and lifted his upper body off the mattress.
Of course, that was no problem for me. Whether awake or asleep, my mace was an equal opportunity weapon.
Smack!
Without needing to sneak up on him, I ran forward and introduced the half-warm mace to his face. Since my objective was to knock him out, I named this skill [Bash.] That sounded about right.
The first step was completed with a successful Bash. “What are you doing?” I said to Missha. “Tie them up.”
Missha looked at the three bloody bodies and answered, “Is that necessarrry...?”
Uh, well... Better safe than sorry.
There was nothing to lose by being thorough. That was my motto.
“Wow, they really arrre alive...”
Despite getting struck by a mace one by one, the three of them luckily survived.
“I told you not to worry—”
“But I think they’rrre going to die soon.”

Seeing as their breathing was getting shallower and more irregular, it seemed they would indeed meet their end soon. The one who had been smacked in the face was in the worst shape of them all. But as long as they were alive, there should be no problem. After all, wasn’t this a fantasy world?
“Found it.” I picked up one of the bags on the floor and pulled out a potion bottle. Then I poured the potion on top of their unconscious heads.
We can’t have them getting too spirited, so just a little.
Czzzzzz!
The reactions came at different intervals.
“Ahh! Aaah!”
“Ahhh!”
The broken heads slowly healed, and the three of them flopped on the lawn like live fish. I pulled over the rocking chair, sat down, and waited for them to come to their senses.

“Boneheaded barrrbarian...” Missha noticed and scolded me, but what could I do? They may have been tricked by Elisa, but they still tried to kill us once. The heart of Bjorn the barbarian did not feel sympathy for the enemy at all.
“That barbarian!”
“It was a misunderstanding! A misunderstanding! We’re not your enemy!”
As time passed, the three of them came to their senses. Since they were all yelling at the same time, things were getting a little hectic.
“One at a time,” I grumbled while wiping the blood off my mace, which silenced the room.
The three of them, tied together like a line of fish, glanced at each other and reached an agreement with just a look.

“Look, this is all a big misunderstanding. It’s just a misunderstanding.” It was the leader and religious freak who ended up getting selected as their representative. “I’ll explain everything, so please—”
“Uh-huh, and what’s the misunderstanding?”
Davis continued talking like I was the one being unfair. “That bitch! She used us. We had no idea that she was a slave to the cursed Karui!”
Oh, so you’ve realized that now?
Something definitely happened to them.
“So, why don’t you let us go and we can talk about this in more detail?”

“Stop asking that.” What mattered now was not how unfair things were or how difficult they’d had it. “Tell me from start to finish, what the hell happened after we ran away?” A confirmation of what had transpired. This was the only reason I had used Bash instead of Smash.
“Uh, that’s...”
“Don’t even think about lying.”
“A-All right. In the end, it’s our fault for trusting her, but I’ll tell you the truth.”
“It’s up to me to decide whether it’s the truth or not.”

The religious freak gulped. Then he vomited out the side of the story that I didn’t know. “When we fell for that evil villainess’s plans and caught up with your group, for some reason there were only three of you guys.”
Yeah. That was right after we had been left behind.
Crunch!
Really, that was shudder-inducing. What kind of fucked up timing was that?
“Should I keep going...?” asked Davis.
“Of course. Continue.”
“We thought it would be difficult for us if you guys kept running, so we attacked and wounded the man who looked like the scout first.”
“A-Are you talking about Rrrotmiller!?”
“I don’t know his name. But don’t worry. With a wound like that, he’ll still be alive.”

Anyway, piecing together the remaining story, it went like this. The surprise attack had incapacitated Brown, leaving our party in a truly desperate situation. The dwarf would have determined that was the case. They would have had to defeat the enemy scout to be able to safely escape.

“I don’t know what it was, but just like the first time we met, there was a blast of light that pushed us back. When I woke up, Anderson had been stabbed in the head by an ice lance. Ah, Anderson is the name of our scout. He wasn’t the kind of person to be taken down by something like that... Maybe it was because we had numbers on our side, but we were not able to avoid the attack because we weren’t vigilant enough.”
Whatever the details were, the moment the dwarf managed to buy some time, Dwalkie defeated the enemy scout. Then, without looking back, they ran away with the wounded Brown.
As soon as we heard this, Missha slapped me on the back. “Like I thought, it was all thanks to Hikurod! Hikurod killed their scout forrr us!”
Well, I didn’t know what the dwarf was thinking at the time, but I couldn’t deny that it was thanks to him that we were still alive. Anyway, back to the main point of the story.
“Anderson’s death left us wandering through the forest too. We couldn’t chase after anyone.”

The religious freak and his party had been eagerly pursuing us, but when their scout passed away, they were left in a similar situation as us. Of course, they were still better off than us. They had five people on their side and even a priestess. But...
“It was about two days after we got lost...”
While they had been taking turns on night watch to recover their energy, the bitch Elisa revealed her true nature and killed one of them.
“When I saw him shriveling up and drying out, I knew right away. That she was a worshiper of the evil Karui!”
“Okay, so why did that bitch kill your friend?” I asked.
“I don’t know either... But anyway, the moment we witnessed that horrific sight, the three of us realized we had no choice but to leave and inform the public.”
Bullshit. You just ran away and abandoned your teammate so you would survive.
Anyway, they just skipped the rest of the story after that. Except for the fact that they were three, it was no different from what Missha and I had been through.
“So, now that the misunderstanding is cleared up—”
“I think I already told you not to bring that up?” I sighed at the third request for freedom.
“Bjorrrn, what will you do now?”
“Ahem. It seems that you are in a similar situation as us,” said Davis. “Why not work together with us?”
“You keep your mouth shut.”
There was more to consider. Of course, I had no intention at all of accepting this guy’s proposal and joining forces for the remaining two days.
“C-Come to think of it, I haven’t apologized yet! Let me apologize! We were stupid enough to fall for that bitch’s tricks. I’m sorry!”

However, there was room to accept that apology. Could I really judge these guys? Of course, a lot of our suffering over the past few days had been caused by these bastards, but no one had died as a result. It seemed that the dwarf and the others were all alive too.
“O-Of course, we’ll compensate you for the damage we’ve caused too!”
And they were even offering material compensation. Did I still have to kill them?
“Bjorrrn, I will do whatever you tell me to.”

I’d killed several people so far, but my life had been at stake in those moments. And those people had been pieces of trash with no capacity for redemption. But these guys? It was iffy. Yes, as I’d said before, there was room for consideration. My modern mind, the mind of someone who had not yet learned the ways of this world, was putting off making a decision.
“What are you thinking so hard about! I-It was a mistake! I never imagined a priestess would lie—”
“Be quiet. Keep talking and I might accidentally crush your skull.”
Davis shut his mouth.
I answered harshly so as not to be seen as weak, but internally, I continued to fret. Is it right to kill them? I finally asked myself.
The barbarian warrior Bjorn Yandel answered me. Does right or wrong matter? It’s easier to just kill them, so why should I leave room for uncertainty?
Truly a ridiculous answer. The twenty-nine-year-old Seoul-born Hansu Lee spoke as well. Idiot, what is there to think about? Of course killing someone for making a mistake is nonsense. But...
For once, their opinions aligned.
But that’s when you’re in our world, Hansu finished.
Killing someone for making one mistake would be completely unreasonable... if I were still in the place where I was born and raised.
Grip.
I grabbed the mace. However, I still couldn’t make a decision. “Missha, what do you think?” I impulsively asked.
Missha, who had been born and raised in this world, answered, “I can’t trrrust these guys.”
“And?”
“Mistake or not, they trrried to kill us. In situations like these... my father taught me never to forgive people.”
Hmm, I see. So this is normal in this world.
Like a fog clearing up, my mind became sharper. When in Rome, do as the Romans do. The reason for that was simple: otherwise, you might end up dead.
Slide.
So I lifted the mace up.
“I-I said it was a mistake!” the religious freak screamed from the floor.
I nodded. “Mistake, huh?”
It may have really been a mistake, but for some reason, I get the feeling you’ll make the same mistake again in the future.
Crunch!
So I slammed down the mace as hard as I could as if to eliminate all hesitation.
Crunch!
Successively.
Crunch!
After three macings, the surrounding area became quiet.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Reach a kill count of 10.]
[Reward: Permanently increases your Spirit stat by +1.]

I had no intention of justifying my actions. If I had wanted to do that, I would have set up a trap and waited for them to make a mistake. The worse the bastard I killed acted, the better for my mental health.
But now is the time to throw all of that away.
Since the moment I woke up in this body, I knew.
Bjorn Yandel.
From now on, I had to live by this name. No, not just the name, but I had to truly be this savage. That was the only way to survive here.
Drip, drip.
Blood and flesh dripped from the mace.
“Bjorn... arrre you okay? Your hands are shaking.”
If you were weak, you died. If you made a mistake, you died. In this world, you died if you had no luck.
“Don’t worry. It’s nothing.” Soon, my hands stopped shaking. I took off the religious freak’s gear, then dragged the body, clad only in underwear, into the hut.
“Eh? W-What are you going to do with him?!” Missha asked, disgusted.
“What I have to do,” I answered.
It was something I had to do even if I didn’t want to. Without hesitation, I threw the body into the half-extinguished fire.
Whoosh!

The fire came back to life in an instant. At the same time, a disgusting smell wafted through the room. Actually, that was just what I thought. This agreeable barbarian body couldn’t sense the difference between this smell and the scent of meat.
Whoosh!
As I stared at the burning fire, I let out a breath. It seemed this was also the same as in the game.
[A new sacrifice has been made. The duration of the Witch’s Hut has increased by 8 hours.]
Since there were two more pieces of firewood left, my calculations told me we could rest in the hut for at least twenty-four more hours.
“What are you doing? Go rest.” As soon as the words were out of my mouth, I lay on the bed. Missha said something back, but honestly, I couldn’t hear it. “...How comfortable.”
I closed my eyes and counted down from one meaninglessly. My tired body slowly fell asleep like it had just discovered what rest was.
Crackle.
The sound of the burning fire gradually faded from my consciousness.
After all, a person has to sleep in a bed.
It wasn’t even ironic anymore. In this world, I lost the weariness of modernity—the more I did, the more human I became.

chapters.title: Chapter 65: Field Boss (1)
paragraphs: I slept soundly for twelve hours. When I woke up, for some reason, Missha was sleeping on my stomach and drooling again.

Anyway, we had quite a bit of time left, so I organized our loot. I checked what was in their backpacks, removed the rest of the equipment from our three enemies, and put it all in our expandable backpacks. It was fortunate that Missha owned one too. After shoving all the equipment in, they became quite heavy despite the weight reduction magic.
This should be enough compensation for all that hard work.
Letting Missha sleep, I took out some jerky and chewed on it. Well, if she woke up and was hungry, she could take care of herself.
Whoosh!
After eating, I washed my body with a cloth dampened with water. I even shaved for the first time in a while.
Now I feel more like a person.

After all the firewood left in the fireplace was burned, there was nothing left to do, so I went outside and sat on the rocking chair. There was a faint scent of blood coming from the serene, grassy field. As I was basking in the sun and letting my thoughts drift, I slowly closed my eyes.
Suddenly, I remembered the religious freak whose head had gotten bashed in mid-nap...
The entrance to the hut must have closed already, so I don’t have to worry about that.
It was peaceful.
At least I’m safe as long as I’m here. Yes, that’s all that matters.
“Bjorn, wake up. You should at least eat something. Otherrrwise, you’ll have a stomachache!”
When I opened my eyes, Missha was shaking my shoulder. I looked at my watch and saw that fourteen more hours had passed since I last checked it.

“Here, even if you don’t have an appetite, eat!” Missha split some jerky and bread and lifted it to my mouth. I had already got up once in the middle of resting to eat, but since I was hungry again, I took it. “Arrre you going to sleep some more?”
“No.”
“Mm, okay. Oh, right! But how did you know that if you put people in the firrre, you can stay here longer?”
“I read it in a book.”
“...Bjorn, do you like smart women?”
“That’s right.”
After we finished eating, I provided some half-assed answers to Missha’s questions and checked the fireplace. Judging by the strength of the fire, it looked like we had less than an hour left.
Click.

I closed the watch and secured it in my clothes. Stretching my body to wake it up from its long rest, I started preparing to go out. It was still too early to claim success, but my heart felt strangely full.
The day really has come.
The fifteenth day would begin soon. In other words, if we survived for just one more day, we could escape from this goddamned forest and return to the city.
So, let’s keep our heads in the game until the end.
[The Witch’s Hut is now closed. You are being moved to the Witch’s Forest.]
Because, as always—
“B-Bjorn! What’s happening?”
“Fuck...”
—it ain’t over ‘til it’s over.
[A 5th sacrifice has been made in the hut.]
[A 6th sacrifice has been made in the hut.]
[A 7th sacrifice has been made in the hut.]
[Special Condition – 7 Sacrifices has been satisfied. The Lord of Chaos, Riakis, has begun to wander the floor.]
The moment we stepped out of the hut, I could sense the change in the forest with every part of my body.
[Field Effect – The Witch’s Forest has been deactivated.]
I could see straight ahead. All of the hallucinations had disappeared. Our surroundings became bright enough for us to be able to see far into the distance without a torch.
“B-Bjorn...?”
The ceiling emitted an ominous red light. In addition, the spirit-type monsters that we had seen everywhere in the forest had completely disappeared.
This was the first silence I encountered since entering the Witch’s Forest. I bent down and touched the ground.
Dddddd.
I could feel a slight tremor through my fingertips. There was no longer any need to confirm or deny what was currently happening. I knew the cause of this phenomenon.
“...It’s the Lord of the Floor.”

This was a monster that acted as a kind of field boss. In the game, they were called the Lords of the Floor. There was a Lord with a different nickname on each floor. Except for a few of the floors, most were summoned with a trigger.
“L-Lord of the Floorrr? D-Don’t tease me. I heard that there is no Lord on the third floorrr!”
“It’s not that there isn’t one. Just that the method for summoning it is kept secret.”

In the case of the Crystal Cave on the first floor, after the third day, it was common knowledge that when there were more than five people around, there was a certain probability of the Lord appearing.

However, the Lord of the third floor was different. The royal family and the guild kept the summoning method top-secret, and once even made a new law to severely punish those who summoned it without prior notice. According to the books, that had been about 150 years ago.
“The guild kept it a secrrret? But, why?”
“Because if some lunatic decides to summon it, it won’t end with just a few deaths.”
The Lord of the first floor disappeared once it killed whoever had activated the trigger, but the Lord of the third floor—Riakis, the Lord of Chaos—was different.
[Erosion has begun. All the monsters on the floor have concealed themselves in chaos. A creature of chaos has awakened.]
This guy didn’t just affect the entire third floor.
[Riakis, the Lord of Chaos, has begun to wander the floor.]
Once summoned, it wandered around the labyrinth and committed massacres until it died. To make matters worse, the ability to move between floors was also blocked.
[The portal is temporarily disabled due to Erosion.]
That meant that escaping to another floor was impossible. When I explained this, Missha’s complexion turned white.
“T-Then what is this?! I-If it is a secrrret, then why has the Lord of the Floor appeared now?!”
Ah, uh... um...
Should I tell her the truth or not? I was a little worried, but the decision ultimately wasn’t a hard one. “Probably because of us.”
It would be better to make her an accomplice here. Whether she considered me her savior or not, that would be a more effective method of making sure she kept the secret.
“U-Us? I-I don’t underrrstand...”
“We burned the bodies back in the hut. That’s one of the conditions.”
After I kindly explained this, her reaction was delayed. “...T-That was the summoning method?! Bjorrrn! What the hell did you do?!”

No, I didn’t know things would end up like this, either. Even the books I had read in the library had said that only a few people knew about this, and the last time Riakis had been summoned was more than ten years ago. So I had thought it wouldn’t be a big deal even if we burned three people.
Fuck, but who would have thought someone had already burned four?

I couldn’t help but curse the ridiculous coincidence. But who could I blame? In the end, it must have been my fault for not considering the worst-case scenario. So, in that sense... “Missha, make one more promise with me.”
“Promise?”
“You must not tell anyone that we summoned the Lord of Chaos.”
He hadn’t been summoned after extensive preparations had been made by a giant clan. There would no doubt be a lot of deaths. But if it became known that we had been the ones to cause it...
They will make us take responsibility somehow.

As our situation slowly dawned on her, Missha drew a line in the sand. “U-Us? What do you mean? You’re the one who burned the bodies!” She spoke very urgently, and even her pronunciation was very clear for once.

That reaction made me kind of sad. She was the one who said she’d treat me as her savior and repay me until the day she died. Anyway, if that was how she wanted to play, I had no other choice. I had to corner her a little bit. “Do you think the guild will believe that? No, even if they do, the outcome will be the same. When it comes to quelling the citizens’ anger, the more sacrifices, the better.”
“Ugh...” Well, based on that reaction, I didn’t think I needed to threaten to screw her over with a false testimony.
“If you understand, snap out of it. We will be lucky if we even die back in the city.”
“...Okay. Then what should I do now?”
The answer was simple. “Let’s run.”
First of all, we needed to get as far away from here as possible. I never thought I’d be leaving this place like this, but...
It would be safest to go to that place first.
It was time to leave the Witch’s Forest.

Finding a way out of this damned forest was simple. Since the status effect Loss of Direction had disappeared, we only needed to move in one direction while following the compass. The problem was that the whole third floor was teeming with new types of monsters.
“Bjorn! Something’s following us!”
“It’s a spirit of chaos.”
For reference, it doesn’t even have a ranking. It doesn’t give any mana stones, and it doesn’t drop an essence.
“We should take care of it.”
Spirits of chaos were targeting monsters, and once their aggro was fixated on something, they would follow it to the bitter end.

“...Is it something we can take down?” Missha seemed wary of hunting a monster she had never seen before. True, in this place, ignorance was the same as death. I myself had learned by dying countless times in the game.
“Its attack power is on the higher side, but that’s all. Don’t worry, it will probably disappear with one elemental attack.”
“...Is that rrreliable information?”
“Yes, I read it in a book.”
“Okay.” Relieved to hear the monster’s stats, Missha adjusted her grip on her holy water-enchanted spear. Then, she thrust it toward the spirit of chaos that was slowly following us.
Pop!
The spirit exploded with one blow from the spear. Something like slime wet the floor, turning the ground black.
[The Spirit of Chaos has been destroyed. This location will be eroded.]

Standing on that ground would now deal chaotic-type damage if you stood there long enough, but there was no need to worry about that. It was not like we were hunting the Lord of the Floor here, and it hadn’t even been a full day since it had been summoned.
After today, the labyrinth will close, so we can just ignore the erosion rate.

That, at least, was a positive. Although the Lord of the Floor had been summoned out of nowhere, the clock had just rolled over to 00:01. Day fifteen had just begun. If we could survive the next twenty-four hours, we could get back to the—
“H-Hey! Help me!”

As we were just about to leave the area, a single adventurer ran toward us from somewhere in the distance. I couldn’t see any other party members, but I did not wonder why he was alone. The dozens of chaos spirits following behind him were explanation enough.
“B-Bjorn?”
“What are you worried about? Run.”

Grabbing onto Missha’s flinching wrist, I ran in the opposite direction of the man asking for help. Thanks to that, we would have to go around a little bit, but what could we do? It was better than the aggro being redirected to us.
“Agh, ah!” Apparently, he was already at his limit. The sound of the brief scream made me turn to look behind us, and I saw that the adventurer had fallen.
“H-Help—!”
God damn it, our eyes met.
“B-Bjorn...?”
“Don’t look back.” I tugged on Missha’s wrist and looked forward again.
“No! D-Don’t go!”

His screams of despair were drowned out by the sound of the wind speeding past my ears. “Harden yourself,” I muttered to myself. “If it was the other way around, do you think he would’ve stopped for you?”
“But! It’s our fault the thirrrd floor is like this now!”
Well, I had nothing to say to that.
Fuck...
I felt dirty, like every part of myself had been thoroughly exposed. But one day, this would all just be a fleeting memory to look back on. We should just do what we had to do.
This should be far enough.
After heading south for a while, we turned east again and moved. We could see eroded land and the bodies of adventurers throughout the forest. The more I saw, the more I just looked ahead and ran.
Pop!
After we had been traveling for about an hour, destroying the spirits of chaos that were following us, we noticed the forest was coming to an end. A wide-open plain could be seen.
I thought it would take at least seven hours...
Had we already been on the eastern outskirts of the forest? We got out much earlier than expected.
We were lucky.
Soon, we quickly cut through the plains and entered the Orc Colony. How much time had passed since we’d last been here?
“Now, now, everyone. Please calm down and follow the rules!”
As expected, a large number of people were swarmed there.

chapters.title: Chapter 66: Field Boss (2)
paragraphs: The Lords of the Floor were field bosses that existed on each floor. Their names, attributes, and fight patterns were all unique, but they all shared one thing in common: they were impossible to deal with as a lone adventurer. To subdue the Lord of the first floor, for example, you needed to organize an expedition of more than thirty people. Of course, this assumed that everyone was at least a fourth-floor adventurer at the absolute bare minimum.

That was what got me thinking. For Missha and I, it’d be game over if the two of us happened to run into the Lord of this floor because it was impossible to outrun them at a normal movement speed. So, where should we go? Rather than just trembling and hoping we didn’t run into it, what could we do to improve our chances of survival even slightly?
The solution was to go to the Orc Colony, like the majority of adventurers here.
“Why are therrre so many people here, Bjorn?”
“Due to the presence of the Dzarwi clan.”

The Dzarwi was a large clan that typically operated on the sixth floor and higher. Hikurod estimated that the number of members was in the hundreds. They couldn’t all be in the same place at the same time, but at least ten parties must have come down here. Even though it was only the third floor, that was the amount of people required to control a hunting ground. Even with this amount of manpower, however, vanquishing the Lord would be difficult.

Well, if you’re willing to accept the consequences, it wouldn’t be a bad plan... But that assumes you know the best way to fight it and have been planning your battle strategy for months. However, if we stay with them, we’ll buy ourselves some time to escape, even if we run into the Lord of the Floor.
Having made an informed, practical decision, I drove Missha through the densely-packed crowd of adventurers. An interesting scene was unfolding.
“H-Hey! I heard you have a high wizard among you! Please use portal magic on my behalf! I’ll pay you anything!”
“You! You’re the one who summoned the Lord of the Floor!”
“W-What will happen to us? They won’t kick us out just because they’re a big clan, right?”

There were those earnestly begging for help, those refusing to accept reality and looking for a target to take their rage out on, and those calmly trying to come to terms with the situation. While this diverse group of people were clamoring, a Dzarwi leader spoke up.

“Calm down, everyone. This area is secure. Our priest has proclaimed the end of all evil here, and our scouts are already on the lookout in all directions. As the agreement between the royal family and the guild states, we, the Dzarwi clan, will do our best to keep as many adventurers alive as possible in this disaster situation. But! If anyone does not obey our orders or starts a riot, please understand that we’ll have no choice but to take removal measures!”
It seemed a little wordy, but it was a fairly straightforward announcement. And, considering the screamers were no longer shouting, the last warning was especially effective.
“We don’t have to worry about being kicked out for the time being,” I told Missha.
“Whew, I’m rrrelieved.”
I found a suitable spot after looking around for a while and sat with my back to a tree.
“...Aren’t you a little too rrrelaxed?”
“There is nothing else we can do.” We needed to get some rest while we could. There was no telling what would happen in the future.
“Hmm, that’s trrrue.” Missha sat next to me after accepting my explanation.
“I’m asking just in case, Missha, but are you confident in your ears?”
“I’m not sure. People have purreviously told me that they like my ears.”
What was she talking about? “I meant are you good at hearing sounds from far away?”
“Ah, I’m prrretty sure of my ability to do that.”
“Then listen carefully to the conversation over there. But don’t look at them or make it obvious.”
“Okay.” At my orders, Missha leaned back and closed her eyes. Her triangular ears perked up as she concentrated. “I’m not sure, but they appearrr to be arguing.”
“For what reason?”
“I can’t hear the details because they’re too farrr away. One thing’s for sure, though: they’re discussing the Lord of the Floorrr.”

Okay, fine. What else could the leaders possibly be discussing in this situation? It would be too obvious to get any closer to them than this, though. This was likely the best we could do. “Please continue to listen in. And please let me know if anything else comes up.”
“Okay.”

I slowly looked around after setting Missha on eavesdropping mode to see how the crowd was reacting to our situation. Aside from a few minor complaints and some signs of anxiety, the vibe was now generally reassuring.
“I couldn’t believe it considering I got kicked out of here earlier, but you never know what’ll happen.”
“That’s exactly what I’m saying. Only a clan of that size could have a priest capable of such a widespread Destruction of Evil spell.”
“The only explanation I can come up with is that the gods are on our side. The Lord of the Floor has appeared for the first time in ten years, but these guys are here at the same time? How?”

Whatever evil the Dzarwi clan had committed while occupying the Orc Colony, the majority of the adventurers were grateful for and content with the current situation. Though not all of them, of course.
“Are you two by yourselves?” A man approached me as I was taking in my surroundings. He couldn’t be looking for trouble right now, could he?
“What exactly do you want?”
“It’s nothing major, but shouldn’t we all band together in times like these?”
“Get to the point.”
“The Dzarwi promised to protect us, but we have no idea what will happen. How about we work together?”
So he wanted a short-term alliance?
“Around thirty people have already agreed to gather. You appear to have lost a comrade in this incident, so it would be nice to have someone to lean on for a little while, I assume.”
Before responding, I double-checked one thing. “My name is Bjorn, son of Yandel. How do I address you?”
“Jack Fletcher.”
So long as it wasn’t Hans. “Fine.”
For the time being, let’s just say okay. If it looks like things are going downhill, we can just back out. We’re not signing a paper contract here.
“A barbarian with a cool personality. I’ll leave for now, then. Get some sleep. If anything happens, I’ll contact you later.”
“Okay.”

The man soon left, and the next two hours passed without incident. Even the spirits of chaos couldn’t approach us because of the high priest’s Destruction of Evil spell. There didn’t appear to be any obvious issues, either. At least, that was how it seemed from the outside.
“Wake up, Missha.” I jostled Missha, who had gone from eavesdropping mode to sleep mode, awake.
“Is there something wrrrong?”
“No, not yet. But, if my predictions are correct... There will be shortly.”
“What exactly do you mean?”
“Take a look around; there are far too many people.”

The Dzarwi clan had welcomed refugees wholeheartedly, and the upper limit of their hospitality had finally been reached. The area under the Destruction of Evil effect was only about twice the size of a school track field. We were also in the woods, not a clearing, and there appeared to be more than five hundred people here already.
“Hey... shouldn’t we keep more people out?”
“Any more people, and we won’t even be able to sit down.”
“If a monster gets in here when things are like this...”
Selfishness was always driven by context. There was a growing sense of unease among those who had arrived first, and claims like that gradually began to emerge.
“What are we going to do now, Bjorrrn?”
“Well, that depends on how the Dzarwi choose to react.”
Whether they accepted people until they reached their limits, or whether they stopped accepting people and closed the doors, the clan would have to make a decision.

As it happened, the clan’s cadre made another announcement shortly after. “Because of the Proclamation of Destruction of Evil, this is the only safe zone on the third floor. This is truly a miracle that will never be repeated. However...”
The contents of the announcement made it easy to edit out the unnecessary bits.
“The priest would like all of you to express your respect for God.”
Reverence. It should be noted that this did not imply any spiritual values like prayer, conversion, or worship.
“Each individual must pay one million stones immediately, on the spot. Mana stones or items may be used.”

Nobody believed this was actually the priest’s request. Well, there must have been an agreement reached with the priest, but the clan must have suggested it first. At first, they had pretended to be honorable by emphasizing their pact with the royal family, but in the end, they chose their own interests. If they prevented the refugees from entering entirely, they would be condemned for their decision, so it seemed they had decided to instead make money while they were at it.
Of course, there was inevitably backlash.
“We don’t have that many mana stones!”
“You’re suggesting that we give up our equipment? In a situation like this, that’s the same as telling us to just die!”

Jack Fletcher was the one who raised his voice the loudest. “Your tyranny will not be tolerated by our one-hundred-man squad!” Jack looked around. Having anticipated this, I avoided his eyes. Were the other one hundred people in the group doing the same? “Uh, um... Everyone, please speak up. We won’t be able to resist their tyranny if we remain silent!” Jack stuttered, taken aback.
The short-lived protest had come to an end.
“One million stones are a tribute to the gods and the price of your protection. You may not have some of your equipment for the time being, but what are you worried about? You’re with us.”
We’re worried about you bastards, of course.

Even though the Proclamation of Destruction of Evil was an overpowered skill, to the Lord of the Floor, it was nothing more than a flimsy piece of paper. Of course, these complaints remained safely in my head, because I was a barbarian who could accept reality.
“Missha, leave the consumables like potions alone and only give them what we don’t need.”
“Okay.”

Like the other adventurers around us, we rummaged through our backpacks, looking for items that could be converted into cash. We didn’t have to remove our clothes because we had some equipment that we had looted from the plunderers earlier.
Whew, a million stones to sleep on a dirt floor...
The price was exorbitant, but it was well worth paying the fee for the Proclamation of Destruction of Evil. Plus, he said it himself: this included the cost of our protection.
“If those guys don’t intend to lowball the prices, this should suffice.”

We had gathered a few pieces of equipment from the religious freak’s party and were ready to distribute them, but not everyone was doing as well as we were. For a third-floor adventurer, giving up the gear they were wearing should add up to one million stones, but...
“Are we supposed to starve to death without this?”
“Would you give up a million stones just to live one day? It’s ludicrous.”

Many people refused to give up their equipment and instead chose to leave. The clan didn’t hold them back, either, and continued to demand payment from the newcomers and a minimum of three hundred other people.
Have they made three hundred million stones since they started? All in a single day...

This was basically copy-pasted money. In the end, power truly made you invincible and a god. At the end of the day, though, these guys were all praying to the same gods as everyone else. If the Lord of the Floor arrived, the market would plummet immediately.
Those people would have paid the protection fee if they had figured that out.

These cretins, as usual, lacked imagination. Of course, I was sure they had reasons for their decision. Because the third floor was so large, they probably believed their chances of running into the Lord of the Floor were slim. Because today was the fifteenth day, they also believed that they only needed to get through today. With the amount of combat power they had, it should be possible.

I was sure that was what they were thinking, as enthusiastically as possible and as much to their advantage as possible. But they had to know. They clearly never imagined ending up in a situation like this, with the Lord of the Floor summoned and all adventurers on this floor forced to stop hunting.
Well, the same could be said for me.
But, at the very least, I always imagined the worst thing that could happen to me. Of course, these scenarios didn’t come to fruition more often than not, but... How about this time?
I guess I’ll have to find out.
I closed my eyes quietly. After that, time passed like a stormy eve. Suddenly, it was 19:07, five hours until the end of the fifteenth day.
Tap... tap... tap.
Rainwater fell through the trees and wet the ground black.
[The area has deteriorated. Destruction of Evil has been deactivated.]
In an instant, the pure white pattern covering the ground lost its light.
“Kwohhh!”
And outside the forest, a massive beast howled.

chapters.title: Chapter 67: Field Boss (3)
paragraphs: Tap, tap, tap.
Just touching the black rain made your skin burn. I knew what this was: the Rain of Despair, Lord of Chaos Riakis’s passive aura skill.
[You are receiving continuous chaos-type damage. Your mana resistance is greatly reduced.]
[Warning: When continuously exposed to chaos-type damage, there is a chance that the status effect Confusion will come into effect.]
This skill did a lot of damage over a wide range, and it also turned the rain-affected terrain into an erosion zone, nullifying all kinds of field effects.
Damn it all...
I had hoped it wouldn’t, but it had really come.
“I-It’s here! The monster is here!”
“H-Hey! What are you all doing? Go stop them!”
A panic broke out among all the adventurers on the third floor who had paid the fee for their protection. Their eyes all turned to the same spot.
“You’re not thinking of abandoning us, are you?!”
“You even took our equipment as payment! Take responsibility!”

The emotional shouts of dozens of people rang out. The clan executive in question, who had designated himself as their representative in front of the crowd several times, sighed heavily, a bitter smile on his face. “...So this is how it’s going to go.”
It wasn’t that I couldn’t understand how he felt. Now that they had taken people’s payment, the only option they had was to give their all to face the Lord of the Floor.

“This quest is going to end in a lot of damage.” Surprisingly, there was only a slight uneasiness on the executive’s face, but no sign of anxiety or impatience. He took a deep breath. “The Lord of Chaos Riakis has arrived!” he shouted. “Take out everything you have prepared!”
The command rang through the forest. In response, those with the Dzarwi clan’s emblem embroidered on their chests moved in unison.
“Each team to their positions!”
Wizards, priests, and long-range damage-dealers moved to the center, while close-combat warriors moved to the outskirts. They started using all kinds of consumables without hesitation.
[You have used an Advanced Endurance Auxiliary Scroll.]
[You have used an Energy Regeneration Auxiliary Scroll.]
[You have used the Numbered Item: Sun Lord’s Flag. Your weapon is now infused with Ersium’s light.]

Various magic doping scrolls, consumable numbered items, and even various types of secondary equipment consumables... in less than a minute, at least ten million stones’ worth of consumables vanished into thin air.
“There are enough supplies, so don’t try to conserve them! At least one person will return alive!”

I was beginning to think I had underestimated them. Now that I was reassessing, I could see that they didn’t lack imagination—they had already planned for the worst-case scenario and had fully prepared for it behind the scenes.
Still, they took a protection fee because...
They had literally staked their lives on the fact that not encountering the Lord was slightly more likely. I don’t know why that made me laugh.
Seriously, there are too many optimization freaks in this world.
I should have been humbler. These people had also taken an untold number of risks in order to become adventurers and get to where they were today. They couldn’t have gotten here on luck alone.

“To think they always carry this many supplies... They really are a large-scale clan!” It was more becoming to watch them closely than to criticize them. It would also be more productive to find something to learn from them than be jealous.
“Bjorn, what arrre we going to do now?” Missha asked.
“What is there to do? We should watch how this unfolds first.”
That had been my plan from the start. As long as the Lord of the Floor was in the area, it would be incredibly risky to get out. If things got hopeless, though, we’d have to leave immediately.
But this should be enough to at least survive.
As if to prove this, a wall of fire wrapped around us in the shape of a circle. This wasn’t a skill granted by an essence, but a magic spell.
[The Spirit of Chaos has been destroyed. This location will now deteriorate.]
Once it started to rain, the Spirit of Chaos, which rushed in like a tidal wave, was destroyed before it could breach the fire wall.
Whooom!
Furthermore, a massive barrier appeared over our heads and stopped even the pouring rain.
That’s the only thing a wall of fire will be able to stop, though.
“Bjorn, look over therrre!”
In the direction Missha was pointing, I could see a huge shadow gradually taking shape as a deep rumbling rolled through the ground.
Boom! Boom!
Horns of rough, heavy-looking black leather sprouted from the top of its head, and an ominous aura hovered around it.
“Guoooooo!”
Easily breaching the barrier of fire, a beast the size of a movie monster—large enough to make you lose all sense of scale—emerged.
“T-That’s the...”
“L-Lord of Chaos, Riakis!”
The crowd, frightened by the sight, stepped back, but the clan members remained calm. “Stand your ground! Do not let it move to the back!”
As if battles with large monsters were their daily routine, the warriors silently held their positions. That didn’t please this guy.
Bam!
Once Riakis slammed its front foot down, the battle officially began.
What did an actual raid look like inside the world of this game? The answer to this age-old question was actually quite simple.
“Make no effort to stop it. Avoid it at all costs! Understood?”

Even in close combat, the tanks and damage dealers avoided head-on encounters, dodging swishing tails or slashing claws with remarkable dexterity. That made sense since they were probably well aware that no matter how tough their bodies were or how high their strength stats, there was no way they could compete with a monster like that.
Is this how a battle with a Lord of the Floor usually goes? It’s interesting.

Perhaps because it was a role I would have to play someday, my focus was definitely on the close-combat warriors rather than the wizards or damage dealers. There was a lot to watch and learn. There were also a few close calls.
Booom!

No matter how hard they tried to avoid it, injuries were inevitable against such a high-ranking monster. In fact, when you were hit by a blow like that, you’d die instantly rather than just suffering an injury.
“They’re still alive after all that?”
“...It’s truly incredible.”
With their stats sky-high thanks to various essences and the assistance of scroll doping, priests, and support-type adventurers, each of these people was a weapon in themselves.
“Ahhh!”
“Fuck, I almost died!”
Wounded warriors were patched up and sent back to the front lines. Of course, not everyone was.
“Damn it, that son of a bitch shouldn’t have died like that...”
“Concentrate on the fight at hand! Don’t take your eyes off of it!”

The number of casualties rose as the battle dragged on. A close-combat warrior was instantaneously killed by the monster’s foot, and three long-range damage dealers were vaporized by its breath. However, if I examined the current situation objectively...
Things are solid for the time being.
“F-Four deaths already... isn’t this getting too dangerous?”
Whatever the reaction of the third-floor adventurers, the warriors were still holding up on the front lines. The magic of the wizards was strong enough to force Riakis out of the center as well.
They seem to be aware of the dark sphere attack pattern too.
“Let’s just keep watching for now! They’re still the famed Dzarwi clan! I’m sure they’ll figure out a way.”
A black marble materialized from the eroded land and headed for Riakis.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis is drawing in the Power of Origin.]
The thing I had been most worried about got blown up by the long-range damage dealers before it could be absorbed by Riakis.
“Hold your fire!”
“You can’t attack the bastard anymore!”
Plus, upon seeing the way they stopped firing from time to time to ensure the monster stayed alive, I grew certain these guys knew the strategy for taking it down.
Which is why they’ve just been biding their time. Jumping into Phase Two without that item would mean a game over.
“Why have they stopped attacking? Are they stupid? While they have the momentum, they need to—”

In a way, it made sense. It would be arrogant for me to assume that I was the only person who knew everything about this world. An expert who had played Dungeon and Stone for ten years and knew everything there was to know about the game? So what? Labyrinths had existed for thousands of years. This wasn’t like a video game world; for the people here, this was reality. They had to enter the labyrinth in order to make money to survive, and had probably gone through much trial and error in the process. This information was then passed down to future generations through records.
Although only a few people have a monopoly on real, valuable knowledge.

I wasn’t too worried. The hidden elements that had been particularly difficult to find in the game seemed to hardly be on the radars of even the people living here. The knowledge I had as a pro would still be my greatest weapon in surviving here.
Click.

I opened my watch and checked the time. It was 22:37. More than three hours had already passed. Despite the long battle, the clan members were still faithfully performing their respective roles without losing concentration.
After all the consumables they’ve used, the amount of money they earned from the protection fee doesn’t even matter anymore.

I suddenly realized why these large clans didn’t hunt Lords of the Floor despite knowing the strategy for handling them. The rewards for taking them down were not exactly small, but a huge amount of supplies went into doing so. There was also the possibility that a powerful member of your clan could die. Furthermore, there was a high possibility that the monster would return if the attempt failed.
It’s not a profitable business.
Booom!

Just as I was thinking this, Riakis for some reason ignored the warriors and rushed to the center, crushing five long-range damage dealers in an instant. Stuff like that could definitely happen during a raid. Fortunately, the warriors got up, rushed to Riakis, and turned it back around, but two close-combat damage dealers died instantly in the process.
Still, they’ll be able to hold on for the rest of the time.

I analyzed the state of the battle again. A total of eleven people had died so far. Although that was equivalent to 20 percent of their total manpower, the remaining personnel continued doing their jobs without panicking. There may have been some gaps in their formation now, but definitely not enough to lead to a catastrophe. The problem was that there were a lot of bastards around them who were incapable of coming to such a basic conclusion.
“Horrible! These incompetent bastards!”
“Do you realize how many people have died?!”

They hadn’t even stepped on the erosion zone and fallen into a state of Confusion, but another wave of panic hit the crowd. It wasn’t difficult to understand where they were coming from. Eleven deaths so far, and that was only counting the clan members. Countless adventurers who had paid the protection fee died every time Riakis wreaked havoc.
Has their sense of judgment become clouded now that they feel their lives are threatened?
The way I saw it, it was their own fault for watching a raid right next to the sidelines like idiots. But they wouldn’t listen to me if I said that.
“Bjorn, the mood herrre is getting tense.”
“I know,” I told Missha.
“We have to do something—”
“Just wait. I’m thinking.”
I scanned as wide an area as possible. The clan didn’t seem to have noticed the unrest yet, as they were focused only on Riakis. In the meantime, one man’s loud voice fanned the flames of chaos.

“We can’t just keep watching like this, let’s all work together to survive!” It was Jack Fletcher, who had been the first to take off his gear and pay for protection. “Do you know how many people have already died? They can’t protect us. We must defend ourselves!”
“Right!” someone shouted.
“But I don’t have my equipment,” another called out, “so how—”
“Those guys need to return it! After all, did they keep their promises?”
At his instigation, the corps that had turned away from him earlier lent him their strength, and the scale of the uproar quickly grew out of control.
“Missha, get ready,” I muttered quietly.
“Rrready for what?”
“We’re leaving this place right now.” This was already a lost cause.
As soon as we quickly grabbed our backpacks, like the beginning of a riot, a bunch of adventurers rushed to the center of the clan’s formation where the supplies were stocked up.
