“E-Everyone, calm down! This will put everyone at risk—”
Only then did the clan realize what was happening, but by then it was too late.
“Don’t make me laugh!”
“Give me back my gear!”
Soon after, the clan’s wizards and archers were pushed aside, and the adventurers began to take whatever they could get their hands on, greed in their eyes.
“Give it to me! That’s mine!”
“W-Who cares about that in a situation like this!?”
“Get away right now! If you don’t, I’ll attack!”
“Whether I die here or over there, it’s the same either way!”
“What are you hesitating for?” screamed a clan member. “From now on they are looters! Destroy them all!”
At some point, the sight of all these people full of confusion and madness wiped even my last remaining regrets away.
“Bjorrrn...”
“Enough watching, let’s go.”
“O-Okay!”
I took Missha in the direction opposite Riakis. Before long, a wall of fire blocked our path.
“W-What are we going to do now?!” Missha screamed.
“What do you mean? We go over it.”
I’m going to use this body like a barbarian would. I’ll get some burns, but I can soothe them with a little spit.
“A-Are you serrrious?!”
Oh, I guess it’s not the same for you.
“Ah! Kyaaa!”
Picking Missha up with both arms, I lifted her up high as if cheering. Then, sprinting forward, I quickly crossed the five-yard-thick barrier of fire.
Czzz!
The faint smell of cooking meat sizzled in the air. Even through Pain Resistance, my skin stung a bit.
“Missha, are you okay?” I asked.
“...Thanks to you, I’m fine. Look ahead!”
After putting down Missha and looking in front of me, I saw that the area was teeming with Spirits of Chaos. We didn’t have time to get rid of each one.
“Run.”
“Eh? Thrrrough that?”
“Is there another way?”
The spirits had already noticed us and were slowly creeping in. I made my way through them quickly so as to avoid drawing any further aggro, since I didn’t know how the battle was going.
Fuck.
After running for about five minutes, our surroundings suddenly went dark. It was so dark, in fact, that it was difficult to see even an inch ahead.
“Bjorn, are you therrre?!”
“I’m here.” Fortunately, I could still hear.
“W-What’s happening?”
Instead of answering, I sighed heavily. There was no need to analyze anything. It was already clear what was happening.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has succeeded in absorbing the Power of Origin. The field effect Evil Hiatus is now active within a three-mile radius.]
Riakis’s instant death and annihilation weapon, Evil Hiatus. The son of a bitch had finally swallowed all those damned marbles.

chapters.title: Chapter 68: Barbarian Hero (1)
paragraphs: After absorbing ten marbles, Riakis unleashed the instant-kill ability Evil Hiatus. If you didn’t escape it in time, no matter how hard you worked to level up your character, they would die. In the game, the amount of time you had was forty-five minutes. And one key feature was that no matter what your location was when the effect activated, you were dragged to the center regardless.
Boom!
Before I could even adjust to the darkness in front of me, I felt the sensation of my entire body being pulled by an unseen force.
“Bjorn...! What...is...this...?!” For some reason, I heard Missha’s voice at half-speed.
So I spoke at double speed. “Don’t worry, we won’t die right away.”
“What... does that...” Missha shouted slowly, but her sentence was left incomplete.
For a moment, there was total silence, as if my sense of hearing itself had been lost. Of course, it didn’t last long.
[All characters within the affected radius will be moved to the Center of Evil.]
When I opened my eyes, there was light.
“Bjorn!” I could also hear normally again, and besides Missha, there were many people in my line of sight muttering.
“Where am I...?”
“W-What the hell! I was clearly running away!”

It was a decent gathering of two hundred adventurers. I checked behind Missha, who was clinging to me with an anxious look on her face. Those bearing the Dzarwi clan’s emblem were quickly gathering together in formation.
Their numbers have already dwindled this much from the original fifty...?

There were a little over twenty people. There had been eleven deaths during the three hours of confrontation with Riakis, but even more manpower had been lost in less than five minutes. What the hell had happened in that brief moment? Well, it wasn’t hard to guess.
“Hey! If you know what’s happening—”

“Shut up, you scum,” an angry voice erupted at an adventurer’s attempt to ask a question. “Because of scumbags like you... Do you know how many people have died?! If you come any closer, I will attack you immediately!”
In reality, the Dzarwi clan had banded together and were on high alert to keep anyone from approaching them.
At this, the adventurers were perplexed. “W-Why is this our fault?”
“If you hadn’t taken our equipment in the first place, this wouldn’t have happened!”

“I heard that large clans swear to the guild and the royal family that they will fulfill their duties in emergency situations. We can discuss right and wrong later, but for now, we must all gather our strength—”
“P-Please let me in! I didn’t even participate in that riot in the first place! If you ask me to pay more for protection, I’ll pay...”
Unaware of the situation they’d ended up in, the adventurers all shouted different things. They probably knew that getting abandoned by these guys would mean having no chance of survival.
But, uh-oh. The will of the Dzarwi clan was strong. “Be thankful that I haven’t killed you yet, you piece of trash.”
“W-what kind of selfishness is this?! What, do you mean to tell us to die?!”
“You heard me right.”

“...What? You bastards! Do you think we’ll just sit here and take this?” The man at the forefront was the one who had caused the riot in the first place. A lot of adventurers sympathized with Jack Fletcher’s cry, but the clan just laughed in their faces.
“And what are you going to do?”
“Well, we’ll join forces to—”
“I’m warning you now: don’t expect us to be jerked around like before. If we wanted to, we could burn trash like you on the spot.”

This wasn’t an unsubstantiated bluff. The situation had changed from earlier. The Dzarwi had regrouped into a proper, dense formation, in contrast to their dispersed formation while confronting Riakis. From the looks of it, they were ready to cast magic at any time.
It was then that the adventurers realized the situation they were in. “God damn it!”
“You think we’re going to die without you?”
A human man who appeared to be about 5′2″ at the front of the crowd opened his mouth. “I know about this ability.”
“You do?”
“N-Not the details. But if we don’t get out of here in time, we’ll all die. It was written in an ancient book.”
“...Is that true?” When Jack gave him a suspicious look, a woman stepped forward in the shy man’s place.
“I can swear it!” she shouted.
Jack stared at her. “An elf?”

“I’ve been teaming up with this guy for over a year and I’ve been through a lot of incredible things with him. This man is mysterious. He really knows everything. I have no doubt that his words will save us.”
Jack’s expression shifted. “If it’s the words of an elf... they’re worth listening to. Look, how do we get out of this place?”
“There’s not much of a strategy to it! I’ve heard that you can escape if you go straight for about three miles in any direction...”
Surprisingly, what the human man said was true. The problem was that the moment you left this area where there was light, clones of Riakis emerged from the darkness.
“I-I heard there will be monsters, but if we all work together, I’m sure we can do it!”
“Hmm, there is definitely merit to that,” Jack mused.
Bullshit. If it was that easy, the clan guys would have run in headfirst instead of having such a serious discussion amongst themselves with such sober expressions on their faces.
“Bjorn, what arrre you going to do?”
“What?”
“If an elf is willing to swearrr it, then that person must have something special.”
Hmm, really? He just looks like an asshole to me...
“Don’t be swayed by things like that, and hold steady,” I told Missha.
“Okay!”

Anyway, things progressed quickly after that. When Jack made a decision and started agitating the crowd again, public opinion slowly shifted. “Even with the guarantee of the elf, the man’s words could be false. However! Rather than sit here and await death, I’d put my faith in him!”
“Yeah, it’s either die here or die in there!”
“I don’t think they’re going to help us anyway, so do we have any other options?”
“There are so many of us, so I’m sure something will happen!”
“But, no matter how I look at it, I don’t think it will be easy...”
There were initially many skeptics, but as people gathered, the fear of being left behind grew.
“I will ask you one last time!” Jack called. “If anyone wants to join us, step forward now!”
More than one hundred adventurers gathered together. The number of people remaining was about forty, including me and Missha.
Jack surveyed the crowd, spotted me, and started talking. “Hey, was your name Biagron, son of Yandere?”
“...It’s Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Hmm, was it? Anyway, are you not joining us?”
Why are you bothering me again? Isn’t it obvious, considering I’m standing here?
I responded by shrugging my shoulders.
“Stupid, just like a barbarian. You’ll regret this.”

The fuck? And what was that? Why add that shit at the end when all he had to do was go his own way? I didn’t understand this mindset, but I always dished out what I took, so I gave him some advice. “The dying scumbag has spoken. Quit your rambling and just jump into your grave. That would be better for humanity and the planet as a whole.”
“W-What?”

“You want to fight me? Then come at me. I’ll smash in that empty head of yours.” When I strode forward with my mace, the scoundrel quickly turned his head, even though there were hundreds of adventurers behind him. I heard him muttering to himself as he left. “Jeez, I was saying that to help him...”
Then he raised his voice and addressed the others. “It seems there is no one else joining us, so let’s go! We can’t afford to waste more time here!”
Despite the hiccup, more than half of the people disappeared into the darkness. No, something like that would be more accurately described as willingly walking into danger.
Anyway, once they left, Missha leaned into me and whispered, “Bjorn, what arrre we going to do?”
“Why do you always ask me that?”
“That’s because... everything you say is right. I trrrust you.”
“I see.”

Thanks for that, but Missha was wrong. My choices were not right. How could a mere human know that? I just picked the option that seemed the most likely to succeed at the moment the problem occurred. So, in that spirit...
Step.
I walked toward the Dzarwi clan, who were in the middle of a discussion.
By this point, they should also be aware of just how fucked they are.
It was finally time to take a gamble I had judged would have the highest success rate, based on various factors.
As I approached, the clan stopped me. “Stop, Barbarian. Come closer and—”
Coincidentally, the one shouting was someone familiar to us.
“B-Brotherrr...”
“Half-wit? Why are you...”
A sudden reunion. It was clear that there would be no touching sibling reconciliation, so I smirked and pointed between the two of them. “Long time no see.”
“...What? Long time no see?” Missha’s older brother, Taylon, frowned.
Right. We were not that close. So, while he was distracted, I immediately got to the point. “So, did the Orc Hero essence show up yet?”
“Well, we were lucky—”
Oh, so you were lucky.
“Wait, how did you know that?”
As Taylon stared at me with horror in his eyes, I smiled. My gamble had been successful, at least halfway.
Iraj McGrain, the deputy leader of the Dzarwi clan, was currently thinking, We’re fucked.
There had been a total of twenty-seven deaths, a number equivalent to 20 percent of the Dzarwi’s total manpower. He had no idea how long it would take to recover those numbers.
Well, there is no guarantee that we will return alive, either.

He opened his eyes and looked at the faces of the members around him. A total of twenty-three clan members had survived. Looking just at the numbers, you would say that about half of the troops were alive, but in reality, that wasn’t the case.
“What exactly is our current manpower?” he asked his lieutenant.
The report he received was delivered in a miserable tone. “Three priests, six wizards, twelve long-range supports... and two melee fighters.”
It had to be. “Only two melee warriors...”
“Unbalanced” was not a strong enough word to describe the current distribution of their group. When the riot broke out, the unsupported warriors had been nearly annihilated.
“It’s still not all bad,” the lieutenant added. “If it weren’t for your judgment, we wouldn’t have had time to reorganize like this—”

“That’s something you’ll only know for sure once we return alive.” McGrain steadied his breathing. As soon as he had judged that it would be impossible to put an end to the riot, he had issued an order to let Riakis absorb the dark sphere. As a result, they were able to reduce the damage to their numbers and buy time.
Yeah, time... we only bought time.
“Look, Sir McGrain! What will you do now? You won’t be giving up, will you?”
“I’m thinking.”
“Then you should think quickly. If you’ve studied Lord of Chaos Riakis even a little bit, you’ll know that we don’t have much time left.”
At the wizard’s sharp tone, McGrain sighed.

“May the blessing of the twilight star be with you...” The priest who was praying while drawing the holy cross in the air was better, but it was clear that if McGrain got on their bad side, he would pay for it even if he managed to get out of there alive.
Think, how can I get out of here alive with as many people as possible?
McGrain deliberated and deliberated. What was the best thing he could do in his current situation?
“Sir, the adventurers are forming a group. It seems like they are trying to get out of this place on their own.”
“That’s the first bit of good news in a while. Leave them,” ordered McGrain.
“Sorry?”

“They’ll act as bait.” Deciding to thoroughly exploit any advantages he was given, he gave much thought to the best escape route to use, how to divide up his troops while they were moving, and what formation would be most effective. There was no concrete answer. “As ordered, I’ll make sure everyone knows the formation when we move. We can go at any time.”

For now, he had done as much as he could, but even assuming luck was with them, at least half of them would die. The absence of warriors was too damning. Two people couldn’t properly pave the way for their group, and what was more, they were a swordsman and spearman—as in, professional defense warriors. In other words, there was no adventurer in the sentry position.
At this incredibly crucial moment, we’ll have to pave the way with just these two men.
Things would have been a lot better if there had been even just one proper adventurer in the sentry position...
“Sir, the adventurers have left.”
“Quick, make a decision!”
As the clan members looked at him, McGrain squeezed his eyes shut.
“The number that left was over one hundred,” the wizard pressed. “Unless we move while they’re attracting even the slightest bit of the monster’s attention—”
“I know.” There was no time. A decision had to be made fast. McGrain finally opened his mouth, which he had shut.
“That’s why I told you, I’ll clear the way!” a barbarian shouted. It was as if he knew exactly what McGrain was worried about, concerns that no one else was aware of.
“Hey, who is that fellow over there?” McGrain asked his lieutenant, almost entranced.
“I heard a bit of their conversation; it sounds like he’s a teammate of Karlstein’s younger sister. You don’t need to worry about—”
“That’s for me to decide, so answer me.”
After a beat, the lieutenant replied. “I don’t know how that man has figured out we have it... But he is asking for the Essence of an Orc Hero.”
“The Essence of an Orc Hero?”
“Yes. He said he could pave the way with just that.”
After activating one of his abilities, Survival Instinct, McGrain looked at the barbarian again. “It’s the first time I’ve ever seen someone shine so brightly,” he murmured.
The ability that had gotten him out of numerous crises was speaking, and it was saying that this man was worth listening to.

chapters.title: Chapter 69: Barbarian Hero (2)
paragraphs: “He must be in a bind because there’s no one to clear the way for you. Give me the Essence of an Orc Hero, and I will clear the way as the vanguard.”
Missha’s brother gave me a cold look. “I see now—you’re just a lunatic. No one to clear the way? What are you talking about? Can’t you see the wizards over there?”

It was then that I realized something: talking to this guy was a waste of time. He was only a low-ranking member who didn’t have enough knowledge to make his own calls, and he was not fully aware of the current situation. The same was true for the other members currently observing this interaction from the sidelines.
“Half-wit, you come here. I don’t want to bear the stigma of leaving my younger sister in danger.”
“B-Bjorn...?”
I needed someone I could actually communicate with. For example, the top guy who would have led the battle with Riakis.
Someone like that would have some sense. But I don’t think this guy’s going to bring me his boss if I ask nicely...
“Ahem.” First, I cleared my throat. Then, like a barbarian, I shouted with all my might. “Invest in me if you don’t want to die. I’ll clear the way!” Anyone with ears couldn’t help but hear my yell.
A moment later, a man stepped forward. “You, what’s your name?”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

“Iraj McGrain. For now, I am the deputy commander of the Dzarwi clan.” Introductions were finished in an instant, and he immediately got to the point. “Tell me, Bjorn Yandel. Who told you that we defeated an Orc Hero?”
Is that where you want to start?
“I guessed.”
“You guessed...?”

“Yes.” Of course, I didn’t understand it at first, either. Why would such a large clan come down to control something like an orc colony? But after carefully combining the clues, I came to a conclusion. “If you really came down just to catch an Orc Warrior, you wouldn’t have brought all those supplies.” What, you’re a large clan? Do you always carry that many consumables? No way. Maybe that was true to some extent, but this went way past that. “Unless you had another objective.”

The rank-five monster Orc Hero was a kind of hidden boss that could be summoned by sacrificing 777 mana stones from Mighty Orc Warriors at the altar in the center of the colony. This had to have been their goal. An Orc Lord, a rare monster whose odds of appearing were very low, couldn’t be taken down no matter what they did.
All of those supplies must have been in case the Orc Lord did come out.
“But it seems the Orc Lord hasn’t appeared.”

“Ha. And you know about that too?” McGrain was surprised but didn’t ask any further questions. “Okay, then, explain to us the reason we need you.” His sentence omitted many questions that he must still have had. There was no more time to waste here.

Since I could pick up the scent of an efficiency freak from this man, I got straight to the point too. “I have the Immortality Imprint and the essence of a vampire. By the way, it’s the essence from a Guardian of the Rift.”
“That means you can use all three vampire abilities.” To hear that a vampire had appeared as a rift guardian would have been a first to him, but McGrain just nodded and moved on. “And?”
“I have the essence of a Corpse Golem. It’s not well known, but Pain Resistance—”
“There is no need to explain in detail. That means you can fight while drinking potions.”
“...That’s right.”

“Is that it?” When I nodded truthfully, McGrain closed his eyes as if to put his thoughts in order. As a person suspected of being an efficiency freak, he didn’t take much time to do so. “That’s definitely not bad. No, compared to the two of them, you’re far superior.” When he said this, his reaction was completely different from that of Missha’s brother, who had looked at me like a madman. He was even quicker to come to a decision. “Okay, I’ll invest in you.”
Taylon spat out something from beside him. “Deputy Chief! That essence was commissioned by the royal family—!”

“Enough! All we have to do is say that the essence did not appear. If one essence can save even a few more people, isn’t that worth investing in?” McGrain immediately dismissed his counterargument and continued talking to me. “Of course, there is a condition. If we get out of this alive, come join our clan.”
Fuck, no wonder he had agreed so easily. It wasn’t even worth considering. “I refuse.”

Once you joined a clan, it was difficult to get out. It wasn’t like it couldn’t be done, but you’d end up branded as a traitor. Once I had even been the target of a raid in the labyrinth after not paying the fee to leave my clan.
But this was reality, not a game. “Why?” McGrain asked. “This should be a good deal for you.”

“I have no intention of working under anyone yet.” Unless I created my own clan in the future, there was no need to join a group and have my actions constrained. Well, if my life were really at stake, I wouldn’t have had any other options, but they didn’t have a choice either. We were playing a sort of game of chicken where the winner had already been decided. I only had my life at stake, but this guy was carrying the lives of twenty-three people on his shoulders.
“How unfortunate,” McGrain finally said.
“So, what is your decision?”
“Okay, I’ll give you the essence.” Did he think it was a waste of time to even argue? McGrain shook off his disappointment and had someone bring me a box.
This is strangely nerve-racking.
I tried to calm down as I slowly opened the box.
Click.

There were three Orc Heroes that could be summoned with mana stones. Each had a unique name. In other words, as high-ranking mutants, they left behind fairly formidable essences. Therefore, even though they were rank-five monsters, attacking in them in a raid was essential.
Denish? Belta? Tarugas? Which of the three spat out the essence?

I usually referred to these guys as the three orc brothers, and they each dropped an essence of a certain color. Denish had the red essence containing Cry of Frenzy. Belta had the blue essence containing the Fighting Flag. Tarugas had the green essence containing the skill that was also the core of my shield barbarian power-up method. Which of the three had come out?
“Whew...” Immediately after opening the box, I checked the color of the transparent test tube. “It’s green.”
Luck was on my side, and it was making me anxious.

[The Essence of the Orc Hero seeps into your soul. Strength has increased by +70. Agility has increased by +35. Fighting Spirit has increased by +40. Physical Resistance has increased by +20. Bone Strength has increased by +30.]
The shift was dramatic and immediate. There were no external changes like there had been for Ainar, but like with any physical essence, I was overflowing with power.
Grip!
Not even taking into account the improvement in muscle strength, my weight felt like it had decreased as my agility increased. From now on, I would be able to move more agilely than before.
Is this because of Combative Spirit?
Above all, unlike usual, the desire to wield this power as quickly as possible was creeping up.
“Take off your gear first.”
I suppressed this excitement and took off my equipment as instructed. While I was doing that, someone spoke up from my side.
“How did you know, anyway? That we were hired to just retrieve the essence.”
“I didn’t know.”
“...You didn’t? But why did you ask for the essence so confidently then?”

Well, I had figured they probably didn’t know which of the three essences would come out. I had expected that the member who would take the essence would only be decided after putting it in a test tube for a while because the cost of a tube was not a big burden for a clan. I explained this.
“Hmm, come to think of it, that makes sense.”
“Is that the last of your questions?”
“For now. There is no time.”
As soon as I put my gear in a backpack and handed it to Missha, McGrain handed me a bundle of scrolls. I didn’t ask what it was. I just grabbed the whole thing in my hand and ripped it open at once.
[You have used a Physical Defense Auxiliary Scroll. Your Physical Resistance has increased by +10 temporarily.]
[You have used an Advanced Endurance Auxiliary Scroll. Your Stamina Reduction has temporarily decreased.]
[You have used an Energy Regeneration Auxiliary Scroll. Your Stamina Regeneration has temporarily increased significantly.]
A soft, colorful aura began to glow on my skin from the effects of the various scrolls.
“Then drink these too.”
Next to the scrolls were various potions.
[You have taken a Strength Enhancement elixir. Your Strength has temporarily increased by +10.]
[You have consumed Tears of Spirit. All elemental resistances are temporarily increased by +15.]
[You have taken a Basilisk Flask. Your Pain Resistance has temporarily increased by +15.]
Shit, was this the effect of a spending spree? “To be honest, I can’t get used to this.”
“We’re not even finished yet,” my companion replied.
“...Right.” The real doping had not even started yet. When McGrain gave the signal, the support-type adventurers cast their abilities on me.
[Aaron Deflain has cast Blessing of Spirits. Your Mana Resistance has significantly increased.]
[Aaron Deflain has cast Regeneration Flame. Your Physical Regeneration has significantly increased.]
[Tarrotes Fian has cast Coffin of Sacrifice. Your Threat Level has significantly increased.]

Every time a new kind of energy entered my body, I felt an unknown thrill. I felt like I had become an emperor. But it still wasn’t enough. In order to break through that darkness full of Riakis’s clones, I had to become a monster greater than an emperor.

“Okay, now it’s your turn.” When McGrain gestured at him, Missha’s older brother approached me. He couldn’t say anything in front of the deputy commander, but I could tell he wasn’t pleased. The feeling was mutual. “Whatever power you absorb, his will be very helpful.”
“I see.”
In order to make a rational decision, you had to let go of personal feelings. And so, I bit Missha’s brother in the neck.
“Ugh!”
The bite was strong enough for me to taste the fishy tang of blood.
[You have cast Master of Blood.]
The effect of a vampire’s active skill, Master of Blood, was simple.
[You have temporarily absorbed Taylon Karlstein’s passive skill The Unclean.]
When a target’s blood was directly consumed through the mouth, one of the target’s skills was absorbed at random.
“Judging by the color of your eyes, it seems you have taken that skill.”
“You don’t have to explain.”
The Unclean was a passive skill that increased the performance of all active skills by 1.5 times while reducing the user’s maximum essence value by 1.
“You’re a lucky one.”
I strongly agreed, but I wished he wouldn’t say things like that. It made me feel like something shitty was going to happen later.
“Then why don’t we get started?” asked McGrain.
I nodded and, slowly imagining the skill I obtained through the essence of an Orc Hero, activated it.
[You have cast Giantization.]
In an instant, the ground grew far away and the people on it got smaller.
[Your Threat Level and Physical Attributes increase in proportion to your increase in size.]
This was also known as Barbarian Hero Mode. Everyone’s eyes converged on my splendid form.
“O-Oh my...”
“That... that’s a monster.”
In awe, McGrain removed his cloak and the lieutenant’s and handed them to me. “...You’d better cover that with these for now.”
I also agreed with that assessment, so I quickly took the offered cloaks and tied them around my waist. With that, all preparations were complete.
“Now we only have about thirty minutes left. Can you do it?” McGrain asked.
Could I do it? Barely controlling the power boiling within me, I shouted, “Behel—ahhh!”
At that moment, nothing was impossible for me.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 3
Physique: 310 (New +155)
Spirit: 104 (New +12)
Special Ability: 115
Item Level: 683
General Combat Power: 695.75 (New +167)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Vampire (Guardian) - Rank 5  Orc Hero - Rank 5]

chapters.title: Chapter 70: Barbarian Hero (3)
paragraphs: I ran with all my might, dragging my giant, sixteen-foot-wide, monster-like body along.
Boom! Boom!
Every time my feet touched the ground, they made a thud similar to that of a large monster.
“Don’t fall behind and follow him closely!”

Behind me were twenty-three clan members and Missha, and behind them were forty third-floor adventurers who had not been swayed by Jack Fletcher’s agitation. How these two groups came to be together was simple.
“We will take you with us if you give up all your equipment.” McGrain was a rationalist who wanted to make up for even the slightest loss.
[You have cast Offering Imprint. Your physical abilities are temporarily increased by the number of sacrifices located within a 100-yard radius.]
I judged that the more sacrifices, the better.
“Behelahhh!”
I was overflowing with power. And an unbearable destructive instinct overwhelmed my body just as much.
This is probably because of the increase in Fighting Spirit.
I was glad, though, that I didn’t have to hold back this desire.
“Kyaaah!”
Miniature clones of Riakis swooped in from the front. They were six feet in size, though... Still, to me, they were small.
Whooom!
I swung my mace mercilessly. Because my body had grown so large, it felt more like I was swinging a spoon. Well, the bastards getting hit would likely think differently.
Smack!

A clone I struck in the chest vanished in a puff of powder. If I were my usual self, it would have taken a few more hits. Once again, I was realizing how much my physical stats had risen. However, the problem was that every time I smashed one, an explosion occurred.
Bam!
Not where the clone died, but where I was standing.
[Riakis’s Hatred is now active. You will receive continuous chaos-type damage over time.]

This was why the presence or absence of a main tank was so important when dealing with Evil Hiatus. These self-destructive corpses always inflicted damage on the ones who killed them. In other words, it didn’t matter whether it was a powerful swordsman or a famous archer—their attacks would be ineffective here.
Bam!

If it had been a weak wizard bastard doing the attacking, the damage would have been enough to take them out. My whole body was numb, even with Pain Resistance. If I had been in my original body, each explosion would’ve made me scream.
Chzzz!

The black fluids clinging to my skin dissolved away with smoke. In places where it was really bad, my muscles had already melted down and my bones were exposed. However, this wasn’t a problem. I was a dark barbarian who had inherited a vampire’s legacy.
[Thanks to the passive skill Source of Darkness, you will not die unless your heart is destroyed.]
I just needed to protect my heart as much as possible. Given the current situation, though, it just seemed like a matter of time...
Shatter!
Countless glass bottles flew at me while I was turning the clones into dust and clearing the way. The priests, working hard to catch up, were doing their best to shower me with heals.
“That was dangerous! Don’t kill too many at once!”
“Behelahhh!”
“If you heard me, answer!” someone shouted at me.
You think it’s that easy?

With Giantization, your threat level was proportionate to your size, which meant there was a greater chance of drawing monster attacks. And for a barbarian who already possessed a massive frame, this increase was exponential. It was the same as being in a perpetual state of instigation. Thanks to this, the adventurers following me were able to travel in relative peace—because the clones were all flocking to me.
“Hey! Can’t you hear me—”
“I hear you.”
However, once I adjusted my pace according to McGrain’s advice, Taylon and some of the other melee warriors who were right behind me blew up some nearby clones.
“Priest! What are the priests doing? I-I need treatment, quick!”

The sight of them panicking after taking down just two or three clones was not at all reassuring. I also didn’t like the fact that the priests’ heals were dispersed. Above all, if I slowed my pace, I couldn’t unleash my passive ability to its fullest extent.
[Your HP is below 50 percent. All Resistance and Resilience stats have increased due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]
The Orc Hero’s passive skill, which activated when the user’s health got lower than half their max, increased defense stats of all types. And according to my research...
When I go lower than 20 percent, the maximum effect will be applied.
That was why I had wanted the Orc Hero’s essence in the first place. No matter what color the essence, the passive skill was the same.
“Okay, both of you get back,” I called down.
“What? I can still—”
I didn’t need a damage dealer imitating a noble tank, so I used gentle persuasion to get the two damage dealers to retreat to the back. “Something might approach from the rear.”
McGrain, who was watching from behind them, didn’t say anything this time, either. He just shouted, “There are ten minutes left. This stretch is critical, so we’ll need your help getting through it.”
Yeah, just cheer me on from back there.
As the rank-five adventurer Taylon Karlstein stepped back from the front lines, a middle-aged man started speaking to him. “Oh, are you back here now?”
“Yes, sir.”

When Taylon nodded, Anton Hernesion, a wizard belonging to Team Seven, brightened. “Yes, the deputy commander made the right call. Since we don’t know what might show up behind us, we have to focus our attention here too. Don’t you think so?”
“Yes... that’s right.” Taylon replied weakly, swallowing down the bitter feeling in his throat. He looked away to avoid conversation. At the end of his gaze was the barbarian.
“Behelahhh!”
Countless monsters flocked in from the dark. The barbarian screamed and wielded his mace, looking more monster-like than the actual monsters.
Bam!
Taylon chewed on his lip as another explosion rang out; he had lost count of how many times he’d heard that sound already.
Crunch!
The deputy commander made the right call? We don’t know what might show up behind us? He was disgusted with himself for nodding like he didn’t know what had really happened.
God damn it.

The truth was simple. It hadn’t even been the deputy commander who told him to step back in the first place. It had been the barbarian, who he had considered just a mere warrior that happened to be a member of his sister’s party. A party that also included a half-wizard who couldn’t even be called a wizard, and who hadn’t even been able to argue with them when told to get lost.
“Something might approach from the rear.”

When the barbarian spoke those words without even looking back, Taylon couldn’t respond. No, he didn’t respond. It had only been a brief moment, but he had realized in that moment that this was not something anyone should do.
Bam!

One swing of a weapon immediately brought terrible pain. No matter how agile you were, you couldn’t avoid it. And the problem was that this fact made the body falter. Even in a situation where he had to swing his weapon nonstop, his hands were stiff and refused to move. How pathetic.
“Hey, don’t be too hard on yourself. Anyone could do it if they couldn’t feel pain.”

Perhaps his face was too readable. Another man spoke up in an attempt to comfort him—one of the two remaining warriors who had also withdrawn from the front lines. “I’ve heard that most of the essences with Pain Resistance are not well-researched, but if they make this type of tactic possible, that will need to be reconsidered.”

Despite the man’s comfort, Taylon kept his mouth shut. He had thought that at first too. Guzzling down potions like that was only possible with Pain Resistance, and in the first place, he and that barbarian had different roles. As a warrior, he may also be fighting on the front lines, but it wasn’t his job to take the hits with his body and buy time. Rather, he was supposed to wait for an opening and get the enemy in the back of the neck.
Bam!
So this was only natural. He didn’t need to feel any shame. Yes, that was what he had thought.
But...
“Behelahhh!”
The more he watched that huge figure from behind, the more he doubted that conviction.
How can he not hesitate even in a state like that?

The parts of his flesh caught up in the explosions melted off of him like water. The incoming monsters bit down on his exposed bones with their teeth. But despite all that, that barbarian was wielding his weapon with accuracy and without any hesitation, unlike Taylon’s own frozen-stiff muscles. He continued to do what he had to do without stopping.
But this is somehow something anyone can do?

Of course not. He’d heard that even with Pain Resistance, that didn’t mean you felt no pain at all. If that was true, having potions, priests, and the Essence of a Vampire did not make him invincible.
“They say that no one can match a barbarian in bravery,” said Anton. “I guess that’s true.”
“It’s almost like he doesn’t even know what death is.”
As one famous adventurer said, there was nothing in the labyrinth that couldn’t die there. The same went for that barbarian.
There’s no point in denying it anymore.

Ironically, after admitting it, his heart felt more at peace with the idea of wordlessly doing what one had to do in a situation where their life was at stake. How many people couldn’t even do that one simple thing? What that barbarian was doing was not something anyone could do. That much was obvious even just from the shifting opinions of the people around him.
“The deputy commander’s insight is truly remarkable. I didn’t expect that fellow to do his job so well.”
“Does anyone know what his name was? Someone like that must be somewhat well known...”
“How did his conversation with the deputy commander go earlier? It would be very reassuring if a person like him joined the clan!”
Even if they didn’t know the details of Pain Resistance, they couldn’t help but feel that the barbarian had saved their lives.
“It is terrifying to think of what would have happened if that man hadn’t been here.”
Someone turned to Taylon’s half-wit sister. “Did you say your name is Missha? Who is that man?”
“Uh, I don’t know...”

They didn’t receive a proper answer, but something the wizard, Anton, whispered beside him a moment later made Taylon think. “If the legendary hero of the barbarian tribe, Balkan, came back to life today,” Anton mumbled, “he would probably look like him.”
There was no need to wonder what that barbarian’s name was right now.
“The end! The end is in sight!”
“Speed up!”
Soon, everyone would know.
[Field effect Evil Hiatus has deactivated.]
The moment I stepped out of the darkness, there was a storm-like roar.
Whooom!
At the exact same moment, dark red rays shot out from the ceiling and toward the center of the darkness.
Booom!
It was like watching an apocalypse in action. “That was a close one,” McGrain mumbled.
“I agree.”

Beyond the darkness, which dissipated like mist, absolutely nothing remained. All that was left in the place where the orc colony had once been were the ruins of a ravaged land. My head, which had heated up thanks to the battle, was cooling. If we had been just a little late getting out...
Source of Darkness or not, we would’ve died on the spot.

In fact, it was ridiculous to call it “a close one”. My Soul Power at the end... To put it simply, I had run out of MP and the Giantization had been shut off. Animated corpses began to flood in like a tidal wave, most likely because all the adventurers who had set off together earlier had been annihilated. It was a miracle we had even escaped in time.
Still, it wasn’t over yet.
Now is when we should really start praying.
I quickly checked the number of survivors. There were exactly thirty. This was because, at the last minute, many of the adventurers who had tagged along in return for their gear had died.
In other words, the odds are one in thirty. No, if I include Missha, they’re more like one in fifteen.
They were low, still not odds to feel optimistic about. Instead of relaxing, I studied the others for any changes.

“B-Bjorn...?” It was then that I heard Missha’s voice next to me. She sounded flustered. “I-I can’t move my body for some rrreason...” When I turned my head to look at Missha, I could see she had gone rigid.
[Missha Karlstein has been designated as Prey. Missha Karlstein will now fall into a state of Incapacitation.]
Fuck, are you serious?
McGrain let out a wordless exclamation. “Amazing. I didn’t know it would come out on your side.”
“Why... why is everrryone looking at me like that?”
I didn’t have time to explain it to her. I stared directly into Missha’s brother’s eyes. “Would you be able to take her with you?” I asked just in case.
“Th-that’s...”
On behalf of the older brother who was having a hard time answering, McGrain decisively put his foot down. “I think that would be difficult. We can’t afford to take on any more burdens.”
But I asked again anyway. “Do you feel the same way? You’re still her brother, regardless of your relationship. Are you going to let her die this way?”
“B-Bjorrrn... Whatever this is about, it’s okay...”
What’s okay? Your life is at stake here.
“So, what’s your answer?” I demanded.
Taylon glanced at McGrain and then gave me a brief response. “To me... This is more important than family.”
Bullshit, it’s because you don’t think of her as family.

Anyway, he was an asshole through and through. “I’ve wasted precious time,” I muttered. Then I picked up Missha, who had turned into a log, and tied her to me with a cloth. I quickly checked the time. It was 23:45. The remaining time until the labyrinth closed was about fifteen minutes, a time frame most would consider neither too long nor too short.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has awakened.]
However, this would probably be the longest fifteen minutes of my life.

chapters.title: Chapter 71: Barbarian Hero (4)
paragraphs: Those subjected to the Prey condition fell into a state of incapacitation. It was a kind of curse. The only difference was that Riakis’s aggro would be fixed solely on the Prey. In other words, we needed to increase our distance from him before he woke up. Only then would our odds go up even slightly.
As we were rushing to prepare to leave, McGrain noticed Missha. “You’re not leaving her behind?” he asked.
“Of course not.”
Are you kidding?

When I laughed him off as if his words weren’t even worth listening to, McGrain nodded, pleased. “It is an important virtue for an adventurer to cherish the other members of their party. Are you sure you don’t want to join our clan?”
“I’m sure.”
“Even if we promise to help protect that woman?”
“...I still refuse.”
“Hmm, that’s too bad. If you were the one who got designated as the Prey, you wouldn’t have had a choice.”

That was true. Missha wouldn’t have been able to carry me on her own for fifteen minutes. In that situation, I would’ve taken on the risk of joining a clan in order to survive. But I guess McGrain really was an adventurer too, considering how fucked up it was that he said that to my face.
“Anyway, our alliance ends here,” he said. “We’re going to leave now. Maybe we’ll see each other in the city someday.”
“If we get back alive, that is.”
“Well, when it comes to you, I have a feeling that will be more than possible. I have a hunch.”
Ugh, I wished he’d stop raising those death flags. I had thought he might make some useful suggestions, but this conversation ended up being a waste of time.
“I hope this will be of some use to you on your journey. What are you all doing? Get started.” When McGrain shouted at his clan mates, the light started pouring in from all around us on cue.
[Daniel Carmine has cast Wind Blessing. Your Movement Speed has significantly increased.]
[Tarrotes Fian has cast Voyage. Your Soul Power will recover much more quickly than usual.]
[Aaron Deflain has cast Regeneration Flame. Your Physical Regeneration has significantly increased.]

So this was what loyalty looked like. Their MP must’ve run out during our escape, so I hadn’t expected to receive so much kindness. While they may have resolutely refused to protect Missha, in times like these, a thank-you was in order. “...Thanks.”

“Just don’t die. If you do, the bastard will come after us.” Upon uttering the words of a true efficiency freak, McGrain began preparing to leave with his clan members. After all, all I had to do was carry this girl and secure my backpack so that it didn’t fall off, but for those guys, it was a different story.
“Then we’ll get going first.”
“Sure. You leave first, and we will head in the opposite direction.” This man was truly logical to the max.
There was no point in being upset anymore, so I smiled and started running off in a direction, carrying Missha.
“Kwohhh!”
Not long after, I heard a cry in the distance.
I was currently being chased while being carried like luggage on the back of a barbarian. We were attempting to escape the Lord of Chaos, Riakis, or whatever his name was.
“Hoo, hoo, hoo...”
My body was hot. Not metaphorically, but literally. Like oil being poured onto a bonfire, I could feel the heat from his exhales on my skin as he sprinted.
“Kwohhh!”
I couldn’t move my frozen muscles to look back, but I could hear it. That trembling cry was getting closer and closer.
So, I called his name.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.” But I guess he couldn’t hear me because there was no reply, so I called it a little louder. “Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“Speak.”
“You can stop now.”
I knew my place. The person that the monster was chasing after was not Bjorn, but me. That was why everyone had looked at me with those eyes—even my own family. My existence was a burden.
“What do you mean?” he said in his usual tone. As if he didn’t understand, as if he was asking why I was bothering him with pointless rambling.

So, as usual, I tried to sound upbeat. “This is good enough. Otherrrwise, you’ll die too. We’re not that close, right?” There was no answer, so I shouted a little louder. “If it wasn’t for you, I would have died already anyway! B-Besides, my lifelong wish has already come trrrue!”
An answer came back after a few seconds. “That’s funny.”
“...What?”
“Why are you saying things you don’t mean? I know you don’t want to die.” His voice was strangely derisive.
Sensing I’d made a mistake, I found myself making excuses. “That’s not true, I rrreally—!”
“You’re just scared of being abandoned.”
That hit home. Was that really why? My voice grew even louder. “Why won’t you listen to me! I just don’t want to cause any more trrrouble!”

“So are those guilty feelings more important than your life?” he replied, slightly annoyed. I was speechless. I’d thought this before, but why was this barbarian so well-spoken? “Stop bothering me with things you don’t mean. If you want to live, just ask for help. At least that way, you’ll have a chance of surviving.”

It was a barbarian-like, blunt statement. Still, I thought I understood what he was trying to say. Ever since we got left behind in the Witch’s Forest, he had been demonstrating with his actions just how to respond to and assess a situation in order to survive.
Which is why I must seem pathetic right now...

He always said things like, “Do what you have to do to live.” So what was I supposed to do now? I couldn’t be sure, but it was definitely not whining about being abandoned by my own family to someone who was currently risking their life to help me.
“Bjorn,” I called out to him again. I knew now just what I had to do. “If you save me, I will aid you for the rest of my life.”
If I was really afraid of being abandoned, the right thing to do was anything that would help me keep someone from leaving me. Except...
“That sounds like something I’ve already heard from you.”

His reply made me notice my mistake, and my mind went blank. Uh, then what should I say? I didn’t have to think for long. “If I return to the city alive, I will give you all the money I earrrned on this expedition! How about that?”
Soon, he replied with a smirk. “Better.”
“I-I’m glad you’re happy with that...” There was a sigh of relief over my shoulder. I sighed for a different reason and ran faster.
Okay. That should be enough mental health care... and that should stop her from bothering me anymore. The real trouble starts now...

I turned my head a bit to check behind me. I could see hundreds of Spirits of Chaos chasing after me. Of course, those guys weren’t the problem. They would follow the target of their aggro until the end, but their movement speed was rather slow, unlike that bastard.
“Kwohhh!”

We had had at least a two-mile head start, and the monster was already this close. At this rate, it would undoubtedly catch up to us within five minutes, and that was assuming I maintained my current speed.
[Wind Blessing has expired.]
[Voyage has expired.]
[Regeneration Flame has expired.]
This was the biggest problem I faced: the various buffs bestowed on me by the Dzarwi were coming to an end one by one. The energy in my body slowly drained away. My pace had noticeably slowed.
Max three minutes.

I took this unexpected turn of events into account and revised the plan. Of course, there wasn’t a big difference between this plan and the original one. After all, there was just one thing I had to do: run with all my might.
Tap, tap, tap.

As expected, after about two minutes, it started to rain, which was evidence that the monster was close. In fact, the number of Spirits of Chaos blocking the way increased considerably. But I did not look behind me. I just accepted that the time had come and whipped out the thing I had been saving for this moment.
[You have cast Giantization. Your Threat Level and Physical Attributes increase in proportion to your increase in size.]

My muscles and bones expanded in an instant. In turn, my arms and legs also grew longer. In addition, as my physical abilities improved, my overall combat power increased. But the important thing here was the increase in movement speed.
Boom! Boom!

While a powerful tremor accompanied each step, my strides were wider than before. Unfortunately, this wouldn’t last long. My Soul Power, or MP, had hit rock bottom while we were escaping the Evil Hiatus.
In this state, the effect will last two or three minutes at most.

I used all my knowledge as a pro at this game to estimate the time I had left. This estimate was higher than it would have been thanks to the buff provided by Voyage, which increased the recovery rate of Soul Power. Without it, I wouldn’t have even lasted a minute.
“Missha, time?” I asked brusquely.
Missha checked the watch I had put in her hand. “Uhh, it’s 23:56!” she quickly replied.
“Exact time.”
“Oh, 196 seconds left!”
Okay, just over three minutes until this damn labyrinth closed. “If you’re bored, count down the time on the watch.”

While Missha was counting down the numbers and acting as a timer, I entered the final stretch and let out a shout that was all too familiar to me by now. “Behelahhh!” As if my ancestors were pushing me forward, my body moved faster.

The more the second hand ticked, the more rainwater fell and the more enemies blocked my way. With that, my job also changed. Up until now, I had been focused on going forward no matter what was coming up behind me, but now I had to pave the way too.
“This is going to hurt a bit.”
Either Missha didn’t hear me, or she considered her task a higher priority. Probably the latter. Either way, she didn’t answer me.
[The Spirit of Chaos has been destroyed. This location will now be eroded.]

The Spirit of Chaos that I hit with the holy water-coated mace exploded, splattering fluids everywhere. It must have landed on her skin as well, but Missha continued to focus on reciting the numbers like it was the only thing she could do.
“That’s 165 now!”
And so I did the best I could do in my role by destroying the Spirits rushing in like a tidal wave or jumping over their heads with this giant body of mine.
“Kwohhh!”
I put all my energy into distancing us from that son of a bitch just a little more. Could that have been where I went wrong?

My right arm, which was holding the mace, was now completely covered in mucus. It was starting to turn numb. Fuck, was this a Paralysis effect? I made a snap judgment and changed the positions of my shield and my mace.
“Ninety!”
Suddenly, I felt a hot fire behind my back. I didn’t have to look to know what it was.
That would be Breath.

Fortunately, there was no major damage. On the contrary, that spell likely blew up many of the Spirits of Chaos on my tail, but it was too soon to be happy. If the bastard had used Breath, that meant I was within its attack range.
“Seventy-five...”
One minute, fifteen seconds remaining. After Breath, it made its first direct attack against me.
Bam!

A huge front paw descended where I had been standing. Thanks to the barbarian’s hyperactive fighting instincts, I was able to dodge it in time, but when I looked straight ahead, I could see the bastard blocking my way.
“Seventy-four...”

Its enormous body was over one hundred feet tall. Even the Orc Hero’s Fighting Spirit stat was no match for that gigantic form that could break a person’s will to fight just by them looking at it. After all, Fighting Spirit was only relevant to people who could afford to start a fight.
Thump-thump-thump!
My heart pounded like crazy, and rightfully so. An expert’s knowledge or not, there was no way to guarantee our survival against that bastard in our current state.
Instinctively sensing this, Missha stopped counting down. “B-Bjorn. You can stop now.”
That again? I thought you were done with the whining.
“Kwohhh!”
As the monster roared in my face, I immediately turned around and ran. It was still making a racket behind me, though.
“Can’t you hearrr me? Hurry, leave me and run away—”
“Stop,” I said firmly. “That’s out of the question. I have no intention of letting you die.”
Toss you aside? Now? Then who’s going to reimburse me for the Ring of the Frost Spirit I invested in you?
“Why... Why are you doing this for me?”
I jumped over a group of chaos spirits. “I made a promise to you,” I grunted.
A Pledge of Comradeship, a promise to help each other. At the very least, if I didn’t grind her enough to make that ring worthwhile, I’d suffer a huge loss.
“Promise? You’re going to die for just a prrromise?!” Missha shouted like she couldn’t understand what I was saying.
“Who said I’m going to die?”

I was going to live, reaping all the rewards I could possibly reap like the efficiency freak I was, and return to the city outside this labyrinth. Of course, it would be a heck of a lot of work, but there was nothing particularly strange about that. I’d never gotten what I wanted without taking some risks.
Bam!
A gigantic front paw came down above my head. I tried to avoid it, but I was a little too late.
“B-Bjorn! Your arm!”
The arm that had been holding the mace was now gone. It hadn’t just been hit by a toenail or anything, but literally torn off. However, I had bigger fish to fry right now. “The time?”
“L-Leave me. No. You’re sure to die with me here...” In her panicked state, her voice shook.
I sprinted forward with all my might and shouted, “Missha Karlstein! Tell me the time!”
“...Sixty seconds! Sixty seconds left!”
So I just needed to hold on for one more minute.
I have to stop relying on luck here and now.

I stopped in my tracks and turned around to look at the son of a bitch. My instincts were screaming at me that I needed to run away right now, but I figured that since the distance between us had already narrowed this much, running away was impossible.
“W-Well,” I heard Missha say, “if I die, that thing will—”

Even if I ran away, I would still be within its attack range. Just look at what had happened moments ago. If I hadn’t been running with my back toward the monster, I could’ve avoided that attack without losing an arm. So, I ran again.
“Kyaa! W-What are you doing?!”

“If you have time to whine, spend it counting the time instead!” While dismissing Missha’s complaints and hoping that the blessings of my ancestors would be with me as I faced my fate, even a little bit... “Behell-ahhhhhhhhh!”
...I ran in the direction of the son of a bitch.
Right at that moment, Missha had a change of heart and started counting again. “Fifty-five...”
The giant son of a bitch spat out a flame from its atrocious mouth. At that moment, my decision proved to be the right one.
“Fifty-four...”

If I had followed my instincts and had run away, the only thing awaiting Missha and I in the future would have been getting grilled alive. But I didn’t run away, which was why I managed to get out of the radius of the flames by sliding under its crotch just in time.
“Fifty-three! Fifty-two!”
Before I could even get up from the slide, the bastard brought down its hind foot—and its center of gravity.
Boom!
Rolling sideways, I dodged it, but the jerk immediately backed away and clawed at me with its front paw.
“Fifty...”
I ducked and dodged. While watching the Dzarwi fighting it earlier, I had memorized its attack pattern.
“Forty-nine.”
Downward strike. Dodge by jumping sideways like a grasshopper.
“Thirty.”
Claw attack—either lie flat like a bug or roll through its legs to avoid it.
“Twenty-six...”
Use all your might to jump over its lashing tail.

I repeated the moves the warriors of the Dzarwi clan had performed against the bastard for hours. In fact, except for Breath and Dark Sphere, these three moves were all the physical attacks it had. Well, once it killed its Prey, it’d begin a new pattern.
“Twenty.”
But, not a chance.
“Kwohhh!”
The bastard let out a loud roar. It was getting angry and its attacks were becoming more vicious.
“Seventeen.”
Perhaps it wanted to make an unexpected attack because it swung its tail one more time.
“Sixteen.”
I leaped up like I was jumping rope, but I guess I didn’t get enough air.
Smack!
The tail caught my ankles and threw my body off balance.
“Fifteen—ahhh!”

I flipped over in mid-air and fell. I rolled across the dirt and nimbly got back up, but one ankle was completely swollen. Meanwhile, the beast slammed its front foot down again. I rolled to the side one more time, but even as I did, I could sense it. I was one step too late. There was a chance I might really die here.
Bam!
What the fuck? Surprisingly, for the first time in a while, that ominous foreboding of mine was wrong.
[You don’t have enough Soul Power. Giantization has expired.]

At that exact moment, my body shrunk in half. When I turned my head to the side, I saw a huge footprint right in front of my nose. If the timing had been a second off, my head would’ve been popped open like a watermelon and scattered all over the place.
Dash!
Feeling my heart sink, I quickly got up from the ground. I felt pain in my left ankle, but I ignored it.
Is it ten seconds now?
Missha seemed to have passed out after I got hit by the tail, so I counted to myself in my head.
Nine.
The situation was not looking good.
Eight.
Before I knew it, the Spirits of Chaos had closed in around me, limiting my range of movement. To add to that, my ankle was messed up, slowing me down.
Seven.
I climbed on top of the front paw that slammed down because it was clear that this bastard was going to flail around to try to shake me off.
Six. Five.
With my remaining arm and strong barbarian teeth, I held onto the monster’s skin as hard as I could. But of course that wouldn’t work.
Bam!
When the asshole slammed its foot down once again, my body bounced off from the recoil. To my surprise, it swiftly snatched me up with its other foot while I was still in the air.
Pshhh.
Having finally succeeded in its hunt, it snorted happily. Its open maw quickly advanced on us. With those vicious teeth, lithinum armor or not, it’d all be over in one bite.
“You’re too late, you bastard.”
This was a world of labyrinths and monsters, where dead monsters disappeared, leaving loot behind.
[The labyrinth is now closed.]

The sight in front of me faded away, darkness instantly rushing in. As I watched the monster in my line of sight grow blurry, I thought that the Lord of Chaos, Riakis, was definitely a tough son of a bitch just like in the game. Even though he hadn’t even moved on to Phase Two, at my current level, I hadn’t been able to do anything other than get chased and beaten.
But... if the time came for us to see each other again...
“Kwohhh!”
It would be different then.
[You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
When she opened her eyes, there was light. Although it was cloudy, the brightness of the world around her was nonetheless incomparable to the lighting of the labyrinth.
I’m alive...
Missha kept her eyes closed for a moment, savoring the warmth, but then she hurriedly sat up.
Bjorn! What happened to Bjorn?
She soon came to her senses in Dimension Square, where the mood was different than usual.
“Priest! Call a priest!”
“J-Just hold on! You’re back in the city!”
There were casualties all over the place and cries for help.
“What the hell happened?”
“I don’t know. I asked a guild member, but they were too busy to answer.”

Those unaware of what was going on buzzed around asking questions. That was a given. It was not uncommon for an adventurer to miraculously survive something thanks to the labyrinth closing, but there had only been a handful of times that so many injured people returned at once.
“Did you hear? It seems that the Lord of the Third Floor appeared.”
“What? The Lord of the Floor?”
“...Then they must all be adventurers from the third floor.”
Missha pulled her headache-ridden body to its feet and slowly started walking.
“Hey! It looks like you came from the third floor too. Sit back and relax—”
A male adventurer approached her, but Missha pushed him away. “Move.”
Relax? Get treated? That sounded great, but there was something she needed to do before that. And so, she wandered through a crowded Dimension Square.
“That guy, he’ll die soon.”
“Even a barbarian is in that state...”

Barbarian? At that word, Missha headed in the direction they were looking at like she was possessed. Pushing away the crowds gathered to gawk, she moved toward the center. And just as they said, there was a barbarian.

“Bjorn...” Missha slowly approached him. One of his arms was torn off, his left ankle was crooked, and a black mucus covered his entire body. She didn’t have to guess what had happened after she had passed out. It must have been a desperate fight for survival, as always.
“Don’t get too close! The priest is coming, just leave—”

She could see why everyone else was watching from a distance. Missha didn’t reply and instead brought her ear to Bjorn’s chest. The mucus stung as it came into contact with her cheek, but she couldn’t help but release a sigh of relief.
Huff... huff.
Bjorn was breathing as steadily as a sleeping baby.

“Ah, so you’re just asleep. You scarrred me...” Her arms and legs felt weak. Missha gathered up her remaining strength and wiped the mucus off of Bjorn’s body with her hands so that he could rest a little easier. “The priest is coming, so don’t worry and just rrrest.”
As soon as she wiped away the mucus on his face, she could see Bjorn’s expression properly. It was very comfortable, like the face of a man who had finished all the work he had to do.

Suddenly, the words of a certain wizard came to mind. “If the legendary hero of the barbarian tribe, Balkan, came back to life today, he would probably look like him...” They were the words of a wizard who had admired Bjorn as he paved the way for them.
Of course, Missha had no idea who Balkan was, but... “I think I know what that wizard meant.” If this world had a hero, they would certainly look like this.

chapters.title: Chapter 72: Ghost Busters (1)
paragraphs: I looked at the unfamiliar ceiling above me.

Since the last thing I saw before I lost consciousness was the city’s typical gloomy sky, this must be an emergency medical tent set up for patients. There must be a lot of other wounded people besides me.

As a matter of fact, when I looked to the side, I could see a bunch of beds lined up next to each other. I easily grasped the situation. A stillness filled the tent, and most of the usable beds were empty.
That must mean quite some time has passed.

So my plan of action was decided. First, I needed to find out how much time had passed. As I tried to raise my body slowly so as not to shock my muscles, I felt a strange heaviness on my abdomen. As soon as I realized what it was, I chuckled.
I was wondering where you went...

Missha was sleeping on my stomach, letting out those distinctive, purring snores of hers. On the one hand, it was commendable that she had taken it upon herself to take care of me, but on the other, it seemed to be a moot point.
Well, she must have been tired too.

Elisa, the priestess of Karui... Getting left behind in the Witch’s Forest... The Lord of Chaos, Riakis, chasing us... It wasn’t hard to understand why she would be when I thought about everything we’d been through.
“Missha, wake up.” Right now, though, my curiosity was my first priority, so I shook Missha awake without any hesitation.
“Hm? Mm... B-Bjorn! You’rrre awake! How is your body? Is it okay?”

“As you can see, everything is fine.” My injured left ankle had good mobility and my torn-off arm had been restored to its original state. On that note, my first question was: “Did you use an advanced potion?”
“No, a priest came and treated you.”
“And the cost?”
“D-Don’t worry. Th-the guild prrrovided disaster assistance, so it wasn’t that much...”
In truth, her words just worried me more. “So how much?”
“...Three hundred thousand stones.”

“I see.” Whew, that was still cheaper than an advanced potion. I was worried when she mentioned a priest, but thankfully, it seemed the guild’s subsidy had been quite generous. “Why are you making that face? You did well.”
“But Bjorn likes money...”
Well, yeah, but... Wait, is that what she thinks of me?
“Even so, money can’t be more important than my health, right?”

This wasn’t just a matter of restoring ripped-up flesh or reconnecting bits that had been cut off—it was regrowing an arm that had been torn to the bone, an arm that had been left behind in the labyrinth.
Healing naturally would’ve been out of the question.
I let go of all my regrets. In previous experiments with Raven, it took an incredible amount of time for me to grow back even a severed finger.
Anyway, second question. “So, how long has it been since we got out of the labyrinth?”
“About six hours.”
Hmm, no wonder it was still bright outside the tent. So I hadn’t lost an entire day. “The backpacks?”
“They’re fine. And everrrything inside too!”
“The mana stones?”
“I converted both yours and mine into money.”
“Did anyone come to see me while I was passed out?”
“Ah, Hikurod and the otherrrs came by!”
“...The dwarf did?”

When I cocked my head, Missha explained everything that had transpired while I was out. To summarize, Hikurod and the others came by about five hours ago just in case we happened to be here and reunited with Missha.
“I’m glad all three of them are fine. So where did they go?”
“After they confirmed we were alive, they said they were tirrred and left to get some rest.”

“I see.” That didn’t upset me. I would have done the same. It wasn’t like I would have woken up faster just because they were here. We could discuss everything we had missed during the meeting we had scheduled in two days’ time. “Then what do I have to do to get out of here?”
“You just have to pack yourrr things and go. I already took care of all the trrroublesome parts.”
“I see.”
As I was about to pull back the blanket and leave, Missha hurriedly stopped me. “Wait, don’t get up! P-Put this on first...”

No further explanation was needed. “Oh...” While Missha turned her back on me and looked elsewhere, I put on the new set of clothes that were folded on the table next to me. I hadn’t expected her to prepare clothes in advance. She may have seemed clumsy, but I guess she had a thoughtful side to her too.
“Does it fit?”

“It fits well.” To be honest, it was a bit small, but finding clothes that fit me in this city was difficult to begin with. Anyway, when we stepped out of the tent, the sun was setting. “Missha, where are you staying?”
“District Eight.”
“Then we can walk together.”

We were headed to our inns, which were in the same direction, when I noticed the contrast between our appearance and those of the people around us. The people on the streets were wearing clean, everyday clothes instead of heavy, tough armor.
“Bjorn, what are you looking at? Let’s go, I’m super tirrred.”
After walking for about thirty minutes on the pristine streets, we reached my inn. Missha’s inn was about ten more minutes from here. “They’re closer than I thought.”
“Right? Why didn’t I realize beforrre?”
“Anyway, you can go now. You must be tired too. Thanks for today.”
“W-Wait!” Just as I was about to enter the inn after saying my goodbyes, Missha grabbed my wrist.
“Is there anything else I need to know right now?”

“No, but...” Then, what? When I looked at her in a way that clearly said spit it out, Missha grinned and released my wrist. “Neverrrmind. You’re just going to tell me to stop repeating the same thing over and over again.”
“The same thing?”
“See you tomorrrow, then!” Before I could ask what she meant, Missha disappeared.

“Tomorrow?” Didn’t we decide to all get together the day after tomorrow? That last sentence was a bit confusing, but I couldn’t be bothered to wonder what it meant, so I quickly entered the inn. After washing myself a bit, I had a quick meal on the first floor.
As always, it was only when I lay on the bed that it hit me.
So, I made it back this time too.
I had come back alive.
Fuck.
At noon the next day, I woke up to the sound of knocking on my door. I wanted to ignore it, but whoever it was was too persistent.
“...Missha?”
“I knew you’d be asleep.”
“Why are you here? We agreed to meet tomorrow night.”
Missha grinned at my annoyance and opened her sack on the table. When I looked, it was full of food. “Come, sit quickly. Not getting enough food while you’rrre recovering is bad for you.”
Barbarians didn’t have that kind of problem. When I looked at her like that was ridiculous, Missha ended up dragging me over by the arm.
“Just come. You can go back to sleep afterrr you eat.”
Skipping one or two meals wasn’t the end of the world, but I obeyed because of the sincerity behind her gesture. The menu was stir-fried vegetables and grilled meat with eggs.
“How is it?”
“...It’s good. Did you make it yourself?”
“Of courrrse, who would sell something like this?”
You can just say yes.
I had no idea she could cook too.
“At first, I mostly cooked to save some extrrra money, but now I keep doing it because it’s fun.”
“Mm, but aren’t you staying at an inn?”
“Ah, yes, but I ended up becoming frrriends with the chef, so they let me use the kitchen once in a while.”
“I see.”
“If you have a chance later, you should trrry it too. You can save a lot more money than you’d think, which is good.”
Cook? You shouldn’t say things like that to a barbarian. Or maybe she just didn’t know a lot about barbarians? “Cooking is a warrior’s shame.”
“I-Is that so?” When I nodded firmly, Missha cautiously made a suggestion. “Well then, I can do it for you...”
What was she saying? “It’s fine. Why would you do that? I can just buy my own food.”
“R-Right.”
“By the way, how did you know my room number? I don’t remember telling you that.”
“Oh, that? When I asked the innkeeper where the barbarian was staying, they just told me.”
“...I see.”
After that, we chatted and put food in our mouths, and the bowl was empty in no time.
“What arrre you going to do now? Are you going to sleep some more?”

I pondered this for a while before answering. “Now that I’m awake, I’m thinking of visiting the business district.” Originally, I had planned to sleep until tomorrow, but even if I laid down again right now, I didn’t think I’d be able to sleep at all. It was my own kind of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Unless I felt like I was going to immediately collapse from exhaustion, I couldn’t ever allow myself to procrastinate and take a break. “It’s better this way. Missha, you come with me.”
“Huh? Me too? I was going to go back and sleep some morrre...” Missha trailed off, a surprised look on her face.
In my experience, it was necessary to come out swinging in situations like these. “You’re the one who woke me up. Take responsibility.”
“Hnng, fine. I have to rrrepair my equipment anyway...”
Don’t even think about running away.

First, we completely offloaded the equipment we had acquired. The money wasn’t quite as satisfying as I expected, as I had paid the Dzarwi a protection fee of two million stones’ worth of equipment earlier.
From here, the money we got from Hans’s group will have to be divided into five...

Still, after selling the equipment and various consumables of the three religious freaks, our profits ended up being quite sizable, particularly because one of those three had owned an expandable backpack. However, this also meant that there were more costs.
“...The repair costs five hundred thousand stones?”
“It’s made of lithinum. The corrosion is too severe, so there’s no other option.”
But, still, how could it cost five hundred thousand stones to repair equipment worth four million? Was this guy trying to cheat me?

“Bjorn, don’t push it. It’s not like he’s wrrrong...” It left a bitter taste in my mouth, but considering Missha, an adventurer with five years of experience, was saying that, I figured the price must not have been outrageous and just paid it.
...How much gold have I lost, then?
All efficiency-obsessed gamers were afraid of losing gold. I counted each stone one by one.
I left my mace back in the labyrinth along with an arm, used an advanced potion on the way, paid three hundred thousand stones for that treatment, and five hundred thousand stones for repairs...
The more I thought about it, the more it hurt. If I hadn’t had to pay a whopping two million stones in equipment for the clan’s protection fee, this much money would’ve been nothing.
“Bjorn, don’t worrry. I’ll earn a lot more money in the futurrre...”
Yes, let’s think positive. In fact, my second-biggest gain from this expedition would be her. Of course, the first was the Essence of the Orc Hero.
I got a lot of consumables like potions, so I don’t actually have a lot of money to spend later.
“Bjorn, what are you doing? Arrren’t you going in?”
I finished my calculations and entered the inn with Missha. It wasn’t mine or Missha’s, but an inn located in the commercial district of Kommelby.
“Who would’ve thought the carriages stopped running so early?”
“That’s why I said we should speed up,” she scolded.
“Okay, stop nagging.”
Upon entering the inn, I asked for two rooms at the counter, and Missha slapped me on the back. “Are you nuts?! Do you know how much one of these rrrooms costs per day? Just grab one.”
“...Just one?” Wasn’t this usually the other way around?
“Do you think we’re in Ravigion? These sorts of inns have rrrooms for ten thousand stones per night!”
“I see. One room should be enough.”

I deserved that slap on the back. We came to this inn because it looked like the cheapest one around, but ten thousand stones for one night? The prices were crazy in the center of the city. My food expenses last month were just over twenty thousand stones.
So that’s why she kept urging me to move quickly...

However, the room itself was well worth the price. It wasn’t like the tiny half-room I was staying in—it had a living room, bedroom, and a separate bathroom. It had a window, obviously, and the living room even came with a small terrace. A faint scent of flowers could be picked up throughout the room.

“Bjorn, look at this! Artian Studio Soap! This is frrree!” Missha had been telling me off for spending money unnecessarily before she noticed something and disappeared into the bathroom. When she came out again, she looked very pleased. “Bjorn, we should make a lot of money in the futurrre.”
I wondered why she was making such a fuss, but when I lay down on the spacious bed, I couldn’t help but agree. “Yeah... let’s make a lot of money.” This was what a bed should feel like.
When will I be able to sleep in a bed like this every day?
There was a long way to go. This was a city where barbarism and civilization coexisted. How many more predators and monsters did I have to kill in order to live like a normal person?
Honkkk!
Before I could think too hard about it, my eyes slowly closed.
At a time when most were asleep, those feeling sorry for themselves were loud, or even more so than usual.
“Hey, did you hear the news?”
“Are you talking about the Lord of the Floor appearing on the third floor?”
“Yeah. They say over thirty Dzarwi died because of that monster.”
“Who cares about thirty people? The guild will probably announce this tomorrow, but the total number of deaths is said to be in the hundreds.”
“So the culprit who summoned the Lord of the Floor hasn’t been caught yet?”
For adventurers, this news was extremely interesting. However, in addition to what everyone already knew, there was a story being spread slowly and unintentionally by the gossip.
“Oh, you guys know what? This is something I heard from one of the survivors... The reason why so many Dzarwi were able to survive was apparently thanks to one person.”
“Are you talking about the Iron Lion, deputy commander McGrain?”
“No, I heard it was a third-floor adventurer who happened to be there.”
“Hmm, is there a third-floor adventurer who could do something like that? What was their name?”
“Their name is...”

Bjorn, son of Yandel. A barbarian who had set foot in the third floor after just three months. The story of the unbelievable bravery he had shown while saving so many people from disaster was sometimes accurate, and sometimes a little exaggerated as it spread. However, each retelling ended with one thing.
“The wizard who told me this story did not hesitate to say this about the barbarian.”
“What?”

“He may not have achieved a hero’s feat but, young as he is, it is clear that he shall follow in his footsteps, and so he shall borrow the name of a hero who was greater and more valiant than anyone else...”
An epithet, a second name that only adventurers with skill and fame could obtain.
“It would only be fitting to call him Little Balkan.”
That nickname always accompanied each retelling.
