chapters.title: Chapter 73: Ghost Busters (2)
paragraphs: Inside a quiet office, a man was sipping tea and muttering to himself. “Little Balkan, huh?”
It was the first tempting rumor in a while. After all, how many adventurers had earned an epithet in just three months? No more than three since he took on this job.

“Interesting.” Even the information on his essences, which had been corroborated by the guild, were fascinating. Normally, adventurers started with a rank-nine essence and slowly worked their way up. But this man? A corpse golem, a vampire, and this time even the essence of an Orc Hero. “This can’t be explained by luck alone.”

It was like he was using a cheat code. If you looked back on history, you would be able to find quite a few people who had walked similar paths. There were definitely people born into this world with special destinies, talent, and luck.
“I wonder which one this guy is...”

Most of these people went on to be chronicled and praised as heroes or great names in history. So what about this barbarian? Seeing his achievements so far, the possibility definitely existed. Of course, he’d have to prove he had a basic foundation first.
“I’ll have to look into this before he gets any cleverer.”
This matter would have to be dealt with more carefully and cautiously than usual.
As soon as I opened the door to the standard upscale pub, Hikurod (on a seat made for dwarves) and Dwalkie greeted us warmly. “Oh, you’re here! Come sit! Hahaha!”
“I’m really glad that both of you are safe.”
I sat across from Missha, who had come with me. “What about Rotmiller?”
“He’s not here yet. But he should be soon.”

As it happened, after we ordered food and chatted for a while, Brown arrived at 8 p.m. Was it some kind of curse of his occupation to arrive right on time? “Bjorn, Miss Karlstein. I’m glad you’re safe.”
“No! I’m glad you’re all right too, Rotmiller. I heard you were injurrred running away...”
“Ha... I feel that because of that, I’ve wronged you. If I hadn’t gotten injured, then we wouldn’t have had to leave y—”
I stopped him there, knowing that if I didn’t, there would be no end to this pity party. “Why don’t you sit down first? The food is here.”
“...All right.”

As soon as Brown was seated, the whole party was officially gathered in one place for the first time in a while. It was a miracle that, despite the party being separated in the labyrinth, all of us had come back alive.
“The gods must be looking out for us.” The real conversation began with those bold words from Brown. The main topic of discussion was, of course, updates.
“So, Hikurod, what happened to you guys?”

“Oh, you mean back then?” In response to my question, the dwarf explained what happened in the labyrinth step-by-step in chronological order. Brown had apparently been taken down in a surprise attack as soon as they got separated from us. However, with a decisive counterattack, they succeeded in escaping by taking out the scout on the other side. The beginning wasn’t much different from the story I’d heard in the hut, but since Hikurod was the teller, I was now able to hear the details.
“Then I used Emergency Restoration to use the Guardian’s Wrist Guard once more and buy us time.”
So that was the combo he went with.
“Wow, I didn’t know you could link numbered items with abilities like that.”
“Hahaha, I would’ve been none the wiser too. This is all wisdom that was passed down by my ancestors.”

Emergency Restoration didn’t repair equipment but was a skill that returned equipment to the state it was in five minutes ago. A Numbers Item was no exception, although there was the downside that it consumed more MP than usual.
The wisdom of his ancestors...
It seemed that as important as numbered items were to the dwarves, related information also got passed down. Anyway, to summarize the rest of the story, it went like this:
“First, we ran away, then we treated Brown. Then we tried looking for you too, but...”

Because of the distance between us, Brown’s scouting abilities were unable to detect us. Still, they did not give up and continued wandering the Witch’s Forest. But on the third day, they ran into Elisa.
“What? You ran into that crrrazy woman again?!”
“That’s right. I don’t know what kind of tricks she used, but she chased us through the forest relentlessly.”
“And? So what did you do?”
“Hahaha, what could we do? We ran away!”

They shook Elisa off their tail and had no choice but to go through the portal and up to the fourth floor, and that was the end of that. The Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor had a stage-type format. After somehow finishing the first stage, they chose to stay put until the labyrinth closed, judging that if a rank-six monster appeared next, they might get annihilated.
“It was quite difficult to kill time for more than ten days, but... Still, I was able to hold on thanks to Rotmiller and Dwalkie.”
Difficult, my ass. We should be the ones saying that.
Ha... and after that, they claimed they were tired and went to bed?
For some reason, my stomach was hurting again. Resting while we were working our asses off... fine. But...
“Oh, by the way, I didn’t mention this. Miraculously, an essence came out during our first battle.”
“An essence... came out, huh?”

Was this a fucking game? The essence that had refused to appear despite our hopes and despite countless battles with monsters in the Witch’s Forest just so happened to pop out up there? And it was the essence of a rank-seven monster, Mimic—a rare monster famous for dropping at least a mid-rank essence—at that.
“Once Rotmiller absorbed it, he opened the Treasure Vault.”
Treasure Vault was Mimic’s active skill. It was not a combat-type ability, but it could open a personal storage dimension when used.
“And? What came out?”

The key here was that when Treasure Vault was activated for the first time, various items were randomly placed inside of it. If you were unlucky, you might end up with just a few high-rank potions. I really hoped that was the case for them.
“It contained about two million stones’ worth of mana stones, three high-rank potions, and two Numbers Items.”
“Holy shit.”
“...Why are you swearing all of a sudden?”
“I’m sorry, I’m just surprised.” I continued to feel vomit coming up my throat but I pushed it down and asked, “So what are the numbered items?”
“Unfortunately, one was in the 8000s and the other was in the 9000s.”
That still meant they had earned more than ten million stones. Of course, since the two of us weren’t there, they’d split that in three. Why was this dwarf bastard so lucky?

“It turned out that we didn’t really need them, so we decided to sell them. Rotmiller, who absorbed the essence, decided to subtract that amount from the standard price of the essence according to the guild.”
“I see... Congratulations...” Brown had a new essence, and Hikurod and Dwalkie had hit the jackpot. Maybe that was why I was able to smile and say congratulations out loud, but...
Crack!
The spoon I was holding bent in half.
“B-Bjorn? Why are you suddenly destrrroying a spoon?!”
“I couldn’t control my strength because of the Orc Hero’s essence.”
“Huh? That’s never happened before!”
That was because nothing like this had happened before. These damned freeloaders...

Having heard the dwarf’s side of the story, it was now our turn. “Actually, we are more curious about what happened on your end. I heard some rumors about it yesterday, but... What exactly happened to you?” Hikurod asked.
If I left the explanation to Missha, she might end up blurting out the wrong thing, so I provided a short summary. Life after being left behind. Missha’s “accidental” awakening.
“Miss Karlstein, congratulations. That must’ve weighed on your heart for so long...”
“No. I didn’t do anything, it was all thanks to Bjorrrn.”
“...To Bjorn?”
“Ah, no! I mean, without Bjorn, I wouldn’t have come back alive!”

There were times when the story got confusing too. Like how we ran into the three religious freaks in the hut, and how when we came out of the hut, for some reason the Lord of the Floor was wandering around. As the dynamic story (unlike the one told by the people who had killed time on the fourth floor) continued, the three of them listened intently.
“Ha, you were really smart to think of going to the Orc Colony.”
“If it were me, I wouldn’t even have had time to think of the Dzarwi clan.”
“And? What happened after that?”
Their sincere reactions implored me to tell the rest. However, rather than exaggerating and inflating it, I continued the story from an objective point of view, with some exceptions.
“Huh, you mean they asked for a protection fee in a situation like that?”
“The two of you paid two million stones... I’m so ashamed. Hey, Rotmiller, Dwalkie, why don’t we pool some money together for them?”
“Good idea. We can’t pretend we aren’t responsible for what happened.”

I guess we sounded a bit pitiful after that. At the mention of the protection fee, some destroyed equipment, and five hundred thousand stones spent on repairs, the three of them gathered one million stones in total. To be honest, I didn’t know how to react. “...Are you really giving this to us?”
“Of course. We made all that money—you don’t think we can at least give you this much?”
What was this? Could it be that he was not a dwarf but a god? “Hikurod, you are truly a great leader...”
“Hahaha, thanks for the compliment. But tell us the rest.”
“Okay.” Scolding myself for denouncing such a wonderful dwarf as a freeloader, I decided to continue the rest of the story with more sincerity.
“Ha, do you mean that the Lord of the Floor actually showed up?”
I told them about the Lord of Chaos appearing with five hours remaining.
“To think they would blow through all those supplies... It makes sense why they collected a fee.”

Then I told them about the battle to subdue the monster and the tremendous amount of resources it required, the infighting that broke out, and the Evil Hiatus getting triggered. After that, I mentioned the essence I negotiated from the Dzarwi, who lacked a tank, and our escape.
“I see. I was wondering what the rumors meant about the Essence of an Orc Hero, but I guess that’s what they were talking about.”
I even brought up having a vampire essence, but the dwarf was pretty generous about it.
“At first, I was reluctant to talk about my numbered item too. We’re fine, so there’s no need to bow your head.”
Bow my head? I was just looking at some food I had spilled on the ground by accident. But I didn’t feel the need to correct him.
“Anyway, congratulations. You already have two rank-five essences. The foundation for becoming a top adventurer has been laid for you.”
“...Thank you for saying that.”

After that, the story ended with me calmly recounting our escape from Evil Hiatus and getting chased by the Lord of the Floor while carrying Missha. The three of them listened intently and each expressed their admiration at the end.
“Hahaha, I knew right away that this fellow would one day do something great.”
“Indeed! That was the greatest and most extraordinary story I have heard in recent years. It’s a pity that I didn’t get to be part of it!”
“Truly... With an achievement of this magnitude behind you, no one will dare take issue with calling you Little Balkan.”
There was only one thing that caught my ear, something Rotmiller said. I cocked my head. “Wait, Little Balkan?”
“You haven’t heard yet? It’s your epithet!” the dwarf kindly explained.
Little Balkan. After the Free Barbarian, this was a new title.
Epithet...
However, I couldn’t be sure whether this would have a positive effect in the future, or the opposite.

The day after the meeting, I met up with Hikurod early in the morning and visited the guild to report Elisa Behenk.
“...A priestess of Karui?”

Since this wasn’t a common occurrence, the staff who received our report could not hide their bewilderment. However, their complexions changed when I submitted my five-star ID card and the video recorder that Hikurod had worn on his head throughout the expedition as evidence.
“This... I don’t think this is something that I can resolve on my own. Could you please wait a moment?”

We were immediately called to the branch manager’s office, and there we explained what had happened. As a result, the news spread to the temple. Elisa was excommunicated from the temple of Reatlas, and immediately became a most-wanted fugitive.
“The checkpoint records indicate that the villain has returned to the city, so we will be able to catch her soon.”
The guild and temple representatives spoke confidently, but for some reason, it didn’t seem to me like the bitch would be so easily caught. I didn’t have evidence, but I had a feeling.
I don’t know if it’s a good idea to leave it like this.
Therefore, I decided to keep checking in for updates about Elisa later, and closed this case. Right now, there was nothing more we could do. We even received an unexpected reward.
“Hahaha! Anyway, this was a surprising profit.”
“Rewards always follow justice.”

We were given about three million stones by the temple in exchange for providing key evidence. Well, it’d have to be divided by five, but that wasn’t bad. This amount of luck was fine to take at face value. Any more than this would start to scare me.
“Whew, there was a lot to testify on so it took longer than I thought. Let’s leave now. Everyone will be waiting.”
After finishing our report on Elisa, we headed to the rendezvous point. The final distribution of loot was completed after a brief discussion.
“Let’s just divide everything we got before we split up into five equal parts. Anything we got after we separated can be negotiated on either end.”

We split up the equipment and consumables from Elisa’s faithful servants, Hans, and the mana stones we had earned up to day four by the number of people in the party. Having anticipated this, I had paid the protection fee with only the equipment from the religious freaks, so the calculations shouldn’t be too complicated.
Oh, shoes.

I remembered Hans’s boots, which later got blown up by a landmine, but I decided to just stay quiet. Not only would it be annoying to redo the math, but I used up all their holy water and potions anyway.
“Dwalkie?”
“I-I’m calculating. Ah! We get a share of 1.22 million stones per person!”

For Missha and I, that was a total of 2.44 million stones, plus 1.2 million stones from the reward given by the temple and the 1 million stones that the three others gave us as aid. The amount we got from selling the three religious freaks’ expandable backpack and the equipment that remained after paying the protection fee was 3.11 million. And we had earned eight hundred thousand mana stones after fifteen days of work. Simply put... that was a total of 8.55 million stones. And if I had split this with Missha, my profit from this quest would have been 4.27 million stones.
If it hadn’t been for that promise.

As you could tell just by looking at Missha’s regret-filled eyes, all of this profit was mine. That had been the deal. Well, at the time I had mostly accepted her offer to ease her guilty conscience, but...
It’s better that I keep and manage the money myself.
Missha was now my main comrade. All essences, wearable equipment, and overall training techniques would go through me now. Of course, a lot of money would go into them as well.
In that sense, if I subtract three hundred thousand stones for the cost of repairing my equipment and Missha’s, plus the cost of my treatment...

The net profit from this expedition could be calculated as 7.65 million stones. Even taking into account the damaged boots in the Labyrinth, the lost mace, etcetera, it was a ridiculous gain. Including all the pluses and minuses, it was still an amount that far exceeded what you could earn from simply hunting monsters.
Though it’s not a lot if you consider the amount of money I will be spending in the future as well.
“Why are you looking at me like that?” asked Missha.
“Never mind. Finish your food.”

Things had changed. After the vampire essence, I had absorbed the essence of an Orc Hero, which I had thought could only be obtained later on. Also, I had found a comrade who could grow stronger with me.
I’ll have to start with that when I get back.
Therefore, it was necessary to reevaluate the plan.

chapters.title: Chapter 74: Ghost Busters (3)
paragraphs: I ate out of my lunch box while sitting by a fountain with Missha next to me. The meal consisted of potato stew, bread, and vegetable salad with beef.
“Bjorrrn, eat some of this.”
“You’re giving me the meat?”
“I ate a lot while making it earlierrr.”

Well, in that case... I chewed and swallowed the meat Missha gave me. How long had it been since I ate beef? It melted in my mouth. However, the only downside was that it was difficult to fully enjoy the taste thanks to all of the staring.
“Did she just call him Bjorn?”
“Then that man must be Little Balkan.”
“Hmm, he doesn’t look all that special at first glance...”
At some point, people started to occasionally recognize me when I went places. Invitations to join a clan, offers to join a party... I could overlook these things but...
“Hey there, are you really Little Balkan?”
There were also those who came up to me just to pick a fight or pester me into recounting the incident in the labyrinth.
Hey, can’t you see I’m eating? I may have just finished, but still.
“Missha, get up.”
“Huh?”
“Since we’re done eating, let’s get going.”
We hurriedly cleaned up and left the fountain. I could hear some muttering behind me, but they didn’t cross the line by following us.
Missha glanced behind her. “It’s kind of cool,” she muttered. “I thought people only rrrecognized really famous people.”
What is this? Are you picking a fight too?
But I could understand what she meant. It must be strange to have someone around you suddenly become famous.
Little Balkan, huh?

In the game, there was no downside to your reputation level going up. You were able to get previously unavailable quests or high-reward commissions unexpectedly. Above all, if your reputation level was low, it was impossible for you to enter District One, the royal capital of Karnon, so a high reputation was essential to progress forward in the game.
But I don’t know if this is a good thing or not.

I wasn’t just playing a game right now. In a world where players were treated as evil spirits and put on the guillotine as soon as they were discovered, it was clear that the more well-known my name became, the more unwelcome attention I would attract. But I had no other choice if I wanted to live. In order to gain something, you had to give something up. I had obtained the Essence of an Orc Hero, saved lives, and reaped several other rewards, so I’d have to deal with this.
“I think we’re done with today’s to-do list.”

By the time we got done collecting the equipment we had left at the store for repairs, buying various essentials, and dropping by the auction house while we were in the area to see if there were any items worth buying, the sun was beginning to set.
I’ll have to go back to my inn and come up with a training plan.
“I’m heading back now. What are you going to do?” I asked. Translation: let’s go back now.

But Missha grew evasive for some reason. “Ah, well...” What was this? It was making me anxious. As I silently urged her along, Missha cautiously opened her mouth. “...I’m going to visit my family for a bit.”
“Family?”
“Yeah. I’ll probably be there until tomorrow or the day afterrr.”
“I see.”
Why are you saying that like you’re doing something wrong? If you have plans, then that’s fine. It’s a family affair, so it’s not my place to get involved.
I was a bit concerned, but I was sure she could handle it on her own. Still, I decided to offer her some words of encouragement because I also knew what her family symbolized to her. “Cheer up.”
Missha chuckled. “That does cheerrr me up a bit...”
Really? Because your voice is still weak.
It looked like I’d have to give her a push forward. The barbarian way, of course.
Smack!
“Agh! You blockheaded barrrbarian!” Missha shouted in surprise, but whatever.
“Much better.”
“I’ll be back in two days, so make surrre to eat well until then, okay?”

I smirked and said, “Okay.” This was a change that had occurred since our return to the city. She did say she would treat me like a benefactor. Maybe this was what she had meant. These days, she was acting like my mom.

Missha and I parted at the carriage platform. She headed to her family home, and I got into the carriage heading to District Eight, where my inn was located. My body shook each time the carriage creaked. I had nothing to do, so I closed my eyes and started thinking, letting myself ride out the rough waves.
For the time being, it would be a good idea to stay with this party.

When I absorbed the Essence of the Orc Hero, my stats rose sharply. In fact, if I submitted an application to be promoted to a rank-six adventurer, it would be accepted right away. I even had a reputation as Little Balkan, so I might be able to jump to rank five. In other words, I could find a better party if I wanted to.
Except it would be difficult to bring Missha with me.

Missha had the combat power of a rank-seven adventurer—no more, no less. There was, of course, plenty of potential for her to move to the higher ranks. She not only had a Spirit Beast now, but also Strengthening—her game-changing special ability and the decisive reason I had chosen to build her up as a comrade.
So, in that sense, my first task is to level her up.
I made my final decision. The most productive thing would be to focus on Missha’s growth for a while.

First, we should raise the level of her contract with her Spirit Beast and, if possible, choose our next expedition with that in mind. That way, an essence might come out. Oh, I think it would be better to also change her main weapon if I can...
As I mapped out Missha’s training plan in detail, the carriage arrived at its destination.
Whew, next time, I need to find an inn closer to the platform or something.
There was an advantage to living near a station. The price would be proportionately expensive, though.
Step.

I got off the wagon, expertly found my way, and headed home. Go straight and turn left at the candy store. Then, at the statue of the Immortal King, take a right at the fork. After another five minutes, I should come across the central plaza...
“The execution shall now begin!”
Damn, no wonder it’d been quiet for a few days. I could see crowds gathered in the usually empty square. Everyone was craning their necks to look at the guillotine.
Slice!

The sight was no longer so terrifying to me, but I had no desire to pay it any mind. Ignoring the chilling sounds coming from the platform, I sped up my steps, but even so, my subconscious picked up on something strange about the visual input I was getting.
...Why are there so few people today?

I wasn’t referring to the crowd gathered under the guillotine, but the inmates on death row scheduled to be executed. It was common to execute dozens of people at a time, but today there were only four.
For some reason, I don’t see people waiting in the front for blood today, either.
Just as I was questioning this, the murmuring, which had been indistinct background noise up to now, grew clearer.
“I was expecting something different from an evil spirit, but that was nothing special.”
“You’re right. Their blood is red too.”
“Isn’t it disgusting that these evil spirits are among us, pretending to be people?”
What? Evil spirits? My feet stopped on their own. When I turned my head to look at the guillotine, I saw the inmates on death row trembling and waiting for their turn.
“I-It’s not me! I’m not one of them!”
“What are you doing? Re-gag her.”
There were three left: a young elven girl, a dwarven man who looked to be the same age as Hikurod, and a barbarian with a familiar face.
Slice!
The elf’s head rolled down into the prepared barrel, and the dwarf was shoved in front of the guillotine. However, my eyes were fixed on one particular spot.
Tarikan, son of Riyen.
Yes, that was the name of that barbarian over there, trembling with terror in his eyes.
Fuck, I knew the way he was acting was risky.

His awkward barbarian speech and fearful personality, his weakness and urge to rely on someone... There were so many things that could’ve given him away that I couldn’t even pinpoint exactly what had gone wrong. But for some reason, I had a hunch.
I guess he didn’t use the money I gave him to buy a weapon.

I had no basis for that assumption since any weapons he had would’ve been taken away from him before he was brought to death row. But for some reason, I kept thinking that he probably didn’t enter the labyrinth this time either.
But why?

I was seriously wondering what the source of my baseless intuition might be when the man who had been quietly shivering suddenly began to writhe. His gagged mouth kept moving like he was trying to say something, and his wide-open eyes looked in my direction. This was probably not a coincidence.
“Mm! Mmm!”
Did he recognize me from this far away? Well, I was the only barbarian in the crowd, so I must have stood out despite the distance.
“What are you doing? Get him to his knees!”
Eventually, overpowered, he was forced to thrust his neck under the blade of the guillotine. Meanwhile, he kept trying to say something, staring at me in the crowd.
“Mm, hmm!”
I had no way of knowing what that muffled commotion could possibly mean. Was he asking for help? Hmm, but his eyes looked too venomous for that.
“M-Mmm!”
While my heart was heavy at the sight of him unable to escape like that, I also felt a bit of relief.
It’s a good thing I kept my distance, then.
If I hadn’t ended our meeting by giving him 150,000 stones... If I had made a different call and revealed that I was in the same situation as him... If we had depended on each other...
“Yandel’s son—!”
...I could have been up there with him.
Slice!

At the end, the gag tore and he shouted something, but the cold blade fell and squashed his voice. I immediately turned my back on the platform and started walking in the direction I was headed earlier. Still, I felt a lesson being carved into my heart.
Next time, I need to remember not to do even that.

I needed to be more careful. In this fucked-up world, plunderers and adventurers weren’t the only ones after my life. Who could really sympathize with whom? I should focus on taking care of myself and proceed with caution in the future.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, right?” Someone called my name from somewhere behind me. When I turned around, a man with a well-groomed appearance was looking at me.
“Don’t bother me and get lost.” There had been a lot of strangers coming up to me lately, so I decided to ignore him and move on. But...

“Don’t be so guarded. I’m in a similar situation to you.” There was a nuance to his speech that was very strange. I unconsciously stopped walking and turned around to look at the man again. “America? Taiwan? Europe? Where did you come from?”
What the fuck was this now?
After gaining notoriety, I had considered the possibility that something like this could happen.
I didn’t expect it to happen so soon.

My head cooled like an ice cube. Of course, my next course of action was already decided. Whether this guy was a real player or just someone pretending to be one, it didn’t make a difference. I just had to do what I had planned. I already figured out that evil spirits aside from me existed the moment I woke up in this body.
The other day, I asked myself, Do I need to engage with them despite the risk?

The answer I came up with was simple. There was absolutely no value in doing so whatsoever. What would I do with another player? Share information? Maybe to some extent, but in the end, the only thing I would gain would be reassurance that I was not alone in this unfamiliar world. And it was foolish to take on such a risk just to make yourself comfortable.
No matter who it is, I don’t have to show them my cards.

There was a thing in this world called a poker face. There were times when people waged psychological warfare using it, but in the end, it basically just meant wearing an expressionless look on your face. After all, the face was the part of the body that best reflected the human mind. However, I had decided that what I needed to do right now was not put on an emotionless expression.
So, as soon as he finished his question, I answered, “What are you talking about?”
Of course, this strategy wasn’t perfect, either. So, as I replied to him in a barbarian tone, I thought to myself, If it were Ainar, what would her reaction be to this?

As we had spent quite a bit of time together, the answer came easily: “Don’t use complicated words and speak clearly.” Yeah, that was it. Barbarians didn’t know much and were not ashamed of what they didn’t know. Also, if the stranger talking to them was a human, they showed a bit of vigilance and aggression.
I stepped forward with a slightly menacing look on my face. Barbarians also snorted like they were going to bust your head open if you said the wrong thing.
Despite my actions, the man just let out a surprised exclamation. “Wow, you almost fooled me. You’re really good at acting. Aren’t you just three months in?”
“Acting? I said not to use complicated words, didn’t I?”

“Ah, there’s no need to keep your guard up. I’m from America. I shouldn’t have even touched this damned game.” His voice was dripping with regret and sorrow, and he referenced information that no one other than a player could know. This gave me some confidence. “Anyway, you’re amazing. You’ve earned an epithet in three months. It took me three years. I just had to be human...”
This bastard was not a player.

chapters.title: Chapter 75: Ghost Busters (4)
paragraphs: I had several grounds for this suspicion.
“Hey, why aren’t you saying anything?”
First of all, I had never revealed my identity to anyone. In other words, this person could only be making assumptions about me. They had none of the evidence needed to conclude I was an evil spirit.
“I told you. I come from America. We’re like aliens here—shouldn’t we stick together?”

This behavior was therefore clearly abnormal. Sure, a player could feel me out if they suspected I was one as well, but to be this obvious about it? It didn’t make logical sense. I might actually be a local. What kind of guts would they have to have to be the first one to reveal their identity?
I mean, in a city where you receive the death penalty the moment you get caught as an evil spirit?

Well, maybe if they’d only been here a month, it would make sense for them to be naive. But he just said that it’d been over three years since he had arrived. It was ridiculous to think he could have survived for three years acting like that.
“We’ve created a sort of game association amongst ourselves. I’ll tell you about it.”
Above all else, however, the way he pronounced the noun “game” was stupid, like a Korean character in a foreign movie.
Plus, if he didn’t intend to hide his identity from me, he would have just spoken to me in English.

Maybe if he had, it would’ve reduced the number of suspicions I had, but this bastard was beating around the bush instead of going about things the easiest way. That was why I reached a firm conclusion based on the evidence provided.
“Hey, can’t you trust me now?”
This guy wasn’t a player, but he was pretending to be one to feel me out. And I could only think of one reason why a local would take on the identity of an evil spirit.
He’s here specifically to catch me.

Well, I guess I did see this coming, given that I was in a city where the existence of evil spirits was common knowledge. I couldn’t find anything about it in any of the books in the library, but there must have been an institution that specialized in dealing exclusively with evil spirits.
He must still be unsure since there can’t be any concrete evidence.

And so my mission was clear. I had to get him to cast aside all his doubts. He may have just been feeling me out right now, but one day they could use magic to launch an investigation against me. I needed to nip this in the bud now so they would never even consider that option later on.
But, how?
What actions did I have to take to convince them that I was not an evil spirit? The answer to that question was really simple.
I took a big step forward.
“...Why are you coming toward me all of a sudden? That’s too close—”
“I have a question for you.”
My statement was met with silence. The guy paused for a moment, then smiled as if he was relieved and nodded. “Ah, yes, anything.”
“Then I’ll speak freely. Are you an evil spirit?”
“What do I have to hide? I am. Which is why—”
Okay, I had a definitive answer. “Enough. You don’t have to say anything else.”
“Pardon? What do you mean—”
“The chieftain told me that evil spirits need to be killed on the spot.”
A face full of bewilderment blinked back at me. “S-Sorry...?”
I charged at him, shouting loudly so that the sound would reverberate through the square. “Behelahhh!”

Barbarians did not tolerate injustice. A fist landed right on his temple. Confusion, doubt, and fear appeared in the man’s eyes, which had turned into kneaded dough, but there was no use looking at me. It was not like I was doing this because I had a personal grudge against him. And if you thought about it, he had been asking for it.
Smack!

The man had openly revealed his identity to me, but if I pretended to not know what he was talking about and ran away, he would only get more suspicious. That was something a local barbarian who was raised the right way would never do.
Bang!
Therefore, I grabbed the man’s neck as he lost his balance and threw him to the ground in a combo move.
Smack! Smack! Punch! Punch! Punch!

In one smooth movement, I got on top of him and struck him with fists the size of watermelons over and over again. His physical resistance level seemed to be quite high and his skin was hard, but all of that was useless in the face of my recently beefed-up strength stats.
“W-Wait...!” His face was bloodied in just a few punches, but I did not hesitate and did what I had to do. Of course, he shouted at me like this was unfair. “I-I’m not one of them! I’m not!”
Yeah, of course you’re not an evil spirit. But what can I do? I have to live too.
“You’re lying too? You must really be a wicked evil spirit.”
“No, I mean—! Agh! Ahhh!”
How many more punches did I get in after that? A large crowd, as well as nearby guards, gathered around the sudden brawl—just as I wanted.
“Hey! What are you doing? How dare you use violence in the middle of the city?”
“Get him off!”

I stopped punching him immediately and got up. Was it because of my grade-two armor? Unlike when I had been framed and arrested by the guild before, the guards were hypervigilant and approached with caution. That wasn’t necessary, though.
Thud!

I picked up the unconscious man, threw him at the guards, and shouted out loud for everyone around to hear. “This man is an evil spirit! He revealed that to me himself and tried to do something funny!”

“What? An evil spirit?” The guards, who had been approaching the unconscious man under the assumption that he was the victim, flinched at my words. The onlookers watching us also murmured. Of course, most of them were skeptical.
“Evil spirit? That barbarian must’ve misunderstood.”
“...Misunderstanding or not, that fellow’s going to have to pay a lot of money for turning a person into pulp like that.”
It made sense. A barbarian’s shouts wouldn’t be considered all that trustworthy. But what about this? “I am Bjorn, son of Yandel! I swear on my honor as a warrior that I do not tell lies!”
Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel. Not to praise myself, but that was the hottest name in the city these days.
“Little Balkan?”
“...Come to think of it, I did hear that he wears a lithium breastplate.”
“Then is that man really...?”
“If he is, it’s worth believing...”
“An adventurer as well-known as that wouldn’t beat up an innocent person and spout such nonsense.”
The murmurs continued and public opinion shifted. Even the guards realized who I was, and looked confounded about what they should do.

At that moment, a man who appeared to be the captain of the guards approached me. “May I check your papers?” It was the kind of polite request that would have been unimaginable in the past. As soon as I handed it to him, he gave me a strange look. “You really are him. First, let me say thank you. My brother has returned from the labyrinth thanks to you.”
“Is your brother in the Dzarwi clan?”
“No, but he’s one of the people who paid the protection fee and followed you.”

Huh, there had to be less than ten of those people still alive. This could not be a more incredible coincidence. But this and that were two different things. “So when are you going to kill that evil spirit? It’s a pity he’s still alive.”
“That will be decided only after the investigation is over. It looks like you will have to accompany us to the authorities, is that all right with you?”
“Hmm, I’m quite hungry, though...”
“We will provide you with a meal, of course. If what you say is true, you have just done us an outstanding service.”

“An outstanding service, huh?” Unlike usual, I thought this over carefully. How would a barbarian answer that? As always, I didn’t have to think for long. “What does that mean?” It was the kind of question that you couldn’t come up with without tapping into a barbarian psyche.
The captain of the guard chuckled. “It means you did something great,” he answered.

“Something great? Then will I get meat as a side dish?” Maybe that was going a bit too far, even for a barbarian. That thought came to mind, but a glance at the captain’s eyes told me that didn’t seem to be the case.
“...I will treat you with my own money if I have to, so I hope you’ll come with us.”
“In that case, well...” After that, I followed the guards out of the central plaza.
But for some reason, this was what I kept hearing behind me:
“Little Balkan slayed an evil spirit!”
“With this story, I won’t have to pay for drinks today.”
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
I was slightly anxious about this plan I had totally improvised on the spot, but everything went smoothly after that. When the guards searched the unconscious man’s clothes, a badge came out.
“Oh, this is the stamp of an evil spirit hunter.”

At first, there was an uproar in the ministry of security. It made sense, given that the person who had been brought in under suspicion of being an evil spirit had the stamp of an evil spirit hunter on him. Therefore, the mininstry of security contacted their association, and soon, a person who seemed to be the man’s superior arrived.
“Uh, so, this man... is an associate of ours...”
“This man revealed to me that he is an evil spirit with his own lips. How do you explain that?”

At first, he had a confused look on his face, but once he understood what was going on, he answered my question with dread in his tone. “That’s... a customary measure that is usually taken against those who have achieved fame in a short period of time or who have accomplished an extraordinary feat.”
“Stop. I can’t understand if you make it so complicated.”
“We were suspicious of you.”
“What? Are you saying you suspected me of being an evil spirit? Who was it? Who was the one who suspected me? Was it you!?”
When I snorted furiously as if in offense, the superior began to sweat profusely. “As I said before, it is a customary measure take—”
“Speak plainly! Are you joking with me!?”
“What is certain is this will never happen again! So please, lower your voice...”

I was beginning to understand why barbarians lived like this. It was easy. The baffled reactions you got were also quite amusing. “Hmm, then what will happen to me? If he’s not an evil spirit, shouldn’t I be punished?”
“O-Of course not.”
“That’s a relief. I’m tired, so I’m going to leave.”
“S-Sorry? Ah yes... go ahead...”
As soon as there was an opportunity to dip, I left the building and headed back to the inn. I had acted assertively in front of those people, but inwardly, I had wanted nothing more than to leave.
Fuck...
To be honest, I was tired, just as much as I had been after getting chased by the Lord of the Floor.
I had no idea they would have such detailed information.

America, Europe, and everything else. He had even mentioned the game, and the way he spoke was natural enough for anyone to assume he was from Earth. Well, I was able to see through it because of his terrible Korean pronunciation, but still. What kind of crazy difficulty was this?
Yeah. Not all of the bastards here are stupid...
It was no wonder that Tarikan Riyen had been dragged off to the guillotine.
“America? Taiwan? Europe? Where did you come from?”
“Wow, you almost fooled me. You’re really good at acting. Aren’t you just three months in?”
“Ah, there’s no need to keep your guard up. I’m from America. I shouldn’t have even touched this damned game.”
In a strange city with no one to turn to, if someone suddenly came up to you and said something like that, it was only natural that you’d feel tempted.
Damn it all...

The more I thought about it, the more fucked up this world was. It was depressing enough to be suddenly dragged here and treated as an evil spirit, but now these assholes were even throwing in some bait? Monsters could just be beaten to death, but it wasn’t like I could do the same with these guys, which made them worse.
“Whew...”
I breathed out the sigh of relief I had been holding back.
But I think I’ve passed for now.

Of course, I didn’t know if the evil spirit hunters or whoever the hell had really stopped suspecting me, but I had done everything I could right now, so there was nothing more for me to do but wait patiently.
From now on, I have to act more like a barbarian.

After revising my future course of action, I entered my room. Then I lay down on the bed in my clothes. But... what now? There was an envelope on the bed. When I opened it and scanned the contents, I found a letter and a pill the size of a thumbnail.
What is this? Did Missha write me a letter? No, she wouldn’t have had time.
As soon as I read the letter, I stiffened.
This is a random letter sent to an adventurer thought to be a player. If you can read this...

It was a letter written in English. I almost panicked and tossed it, but when I remembered there was no one else there, I got under the blanket and read it carefully. When roughly translated, the contents were as follows:

This is a random letter sent to an adventurer thought to be a player. If you can read this, never reveal to anyone that you are a player. Oh, and I ask that you do not translate the contents of this letter even if you are caught by an evil spirit hunter. Anyway, what I want to say is this: we have a completely anonymous community, and you can join us by taking the enclosed pill. If you do not wish to join, please throw away the pill. I sincerely hope for your survival.
The more I read it, the more scrambled my mind got. Was this the work of those same bastards?
Fuck, but it’s too believable to be from them...

The fact that the letter only used simple words? Perhaps they were being considerate of non-English speakers. This game only supported English, after all. They would’ve assumed that I could understand this much.
If it were me, I would have used this exact method to identify and invite players.
This was different from the evil spirit hunters, who could only imitate us. This letter was thoroughly written from a player’s point of view.
GHOST BUSTERS
Just look at the community name at the top. Wasn’t it too witty to have been written by an evil spirit on the verge of death in the interrogation room?
But could those assholes write something like this?

Of course, it could be like a delayed attack, pretending to be sloppy and then taking you down when you got careless. Therefore, I hoped that the sender of this letter was a player. I didn’t really need a community, but... If this really was a letter from the evil spirit hunters, I wasn’t confident I could survive in this city.
P.S. Rafdonia’s king, Motherfucker!
After all, how could you beat a bunch of bastards dedicated to hunting evil spirits?

chapters.title: Chapter 76: Ghost Busters (5)
paragraphs: [Rafdonian Royal Family Ministry of Security.]

“What? He came back covered in blood?” Upon hearing his subordinate’s report, the man burst out laughing. He didn’t know what to start getting angry about first. “Tell me this, why did he make contact with him? My orders were just to follow him.”
“...I believe he made the decision alone on the field.”
“You believe? Are you kidding me? Explain.”
“Since the individual in question was a barbarian just three months in, our associate decided that he could easily expose his true identity.”

The man let out a deep sigh. It wasn’t impossible to understand that logic. Most evil spirits under a year old were naive. More than half of them readily revealed their identities to anyone who got close to them and pretended to be in the same situation, and the other half gave themselves away through their facial expressions. “So, you were saying there was no such reaction from him?”

“Yes, sir. The individual frowned as soon as he heard what the associate was saying, then got angry and told him to speak plainly rather than use complicated words. It would be easier to see for yourself.” The subordinate pulled a button out of his pocket—a specially designed video recorder. When he brought it over to the crystal ball on the desk, it copied the events of the incident. The man watched the recording over and over again, studying the shifts in the barbarian’s expression, eyes, and facial muscles thoroughly.
“America? Taiwan? Europe? Where did you come from?”

The associate may have made a mistake by approaching too carelessly, but nevertheless, the man’s reaction was certainly special. “What are you talking about? Don’t say complicated words and speak clearly.” The answer came without a pause. Normally, evil spirits were startled and racked their brains to try to identify their assailant. But this barbarian?
“Wow, you almost fooled me. You’re really good at acting. Aren’t you just three months in?”
“Acting? I said not to use complicated words, didn’t I?”
His vocabulary, tone of voice, thoughtful questions, and responses to the situation were all different from previous evil spirits.
“Then I’ll speak freely. Are you an evil spirit?”
“What do I have to hide? I am. Which is why—”
“Enough. You don’t have to say anything else.”
“Pardon? What do you m—”
“The chieftain told me that evil spirits need to be killed on the spot.”
Rather, they were all consistent with the distinct reaction only someone who wasn’t an evil spirit could reproduce.

“Even those who don’t want to reveal their identities usually choose avoidance in situations like that.” But that man? As soon as he made a decision, he chose to go for it head-on without any hesitation, like a barbarian. After mulling this over for a while, the man made a final decision. “He certainly doesn’t look like an evil spirit.”
Bjorn Yandel. The evil spirits must have started showing interest in him after his name caught their eye. But he had only gained fame a few days ago.
The gathering is yet to be held, so time-wise, he will not have learned of our methodology...

All signs pointed to him not being an evil spirit. Even if he somehow figured out the existence of the secret Ministry of Security, it was debatable whether it was possible to react like he did in the first place. Most of all, the incident in the guild left a strong impression. After being framed while on the verge of death, he escaped from prison and wreaked havoc. That was not something that an evil spirit who was trying to pretend to be honorable could do. A barbarian with nothing to lose, though?
“Bjorn Yandel is acquitted.”
The man stamped a blue stamp on the report, placed it in a file, and inserted it into a cabinet. At this, the subordinate watching him let out a sigh of relief. “...I’m glad, sir.”
“Yes, it’s very fortunate. If our man had been beaten bloody by an evil spirit, I would have killed him myself.”
“Then what will you do about the punishment?”

“He took it upon himself to make contact with the target while on a tailing mission. After three months of suspension, he will have twelve months of reduced pay, and his performance and promotion evaluation will be postponed until next year.”
“I will relay that information.”
After that, the subordinate left his office, and the man sat alone with his thoughts for a while.
So he earned an epithet in three months without being an evil spirit, huh?
Regardless of this incident, it was worth keeping a close eye on this barbarian in the future.
Could he really be destined to be a hero? Perhaps the count will take a liking to him.
There was always a shortage of talented individuals in this city.
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
Is it morning already...?
I hadn’t slept all night because of the letter I found. Were its contents real or not? I let out a sigh as I pondered this over and over until the sun came up.
Well, it looks real, but...

That was just a hunch, and I couldn’t be sure. So, as soon as the sun came up, I washed up and went out. To start, I was planning on learning more about this pill. Of course, there was a good chance that this was a strategy used by evil spirit hunters but...
Actually, that’s all the more reason I should show them that I’m trying to figure out what it is.

Well, think of it like a local. Someone broke into my room and left a letter with unreadable text along with a pill. It was only normal to wonder what it was. For someone who lived here, this would be fucking terrifying.
“I thought you forgot about our appointment since you haven’t come for the past few days, but I guess that’s not the case.”
For that reason, I visited the Magic Tower, figuring one of this world’s academics, a wizard, might know something. And as a matter of fact, she did—much more than I had expected.
“Oh, if you’ve gotten one of those pills, you really must have gotten some notoriety this time.” That was Raven’s reaction to the letter and pill.
“Notoriety?”

“Yes. You don’t have to worry too much. I heard that anyone who gets a little famous gets one of these.” After that, Raven looked at the letter and licked her lips. “But it’s too bad. I wish you had come to me right away.”
The letter was now blank. There must have been something magical added to it because the ink erased itself less than ten minutes after I read through it.
“Aren’t you curious, Mr. Yandel? What the evil spirits must’ve written in the letter?”
“Evil spirits?”
“Oh, I didn’t tell you. This is a letter from an evil spirit.”
“I didn’t even know it was a letter. You really are amazing.”

Raven made her distinctive snorting sound as I used words of flattery on her. Then she entered into TMI mode, as usual. “Well, that’s true. Most people don’t know about this. Can you give me that pill?”
“Here.”
“Do you know what this pill is?”
“I do not know.”
“It was made by a very talented wizard, someone who possesses tremendous knowledge of psychic magic, dimensional magic, and alchemy.”
“So, what is it?”

She had begun to launch into a long explanation about how many wizards had worked diligently to figure out the formula, but at my blunt question, she finally got to the point. “If you take this pill, you can enter a certain spiritual world.”
“Spiritual world?”

“Oh, was that a little too complicated? It’s a kind of parallel dimension. The body is asleep, but the mind goes somewhere else.” After that, Raven’s explanation continued. To summarize, it went like this:
1. If you took this pill, you were summoned to a spiritual world at midnight on the fifteenth of every month.
2. The evil spirits there were likely exchanging information with each other.
3. This was why many people took the pill in an attempt to infiltrate their world. However, the next morning, they were all found dead with their mouths full of blood.
I startled. “They were found dead?”
“Yes. So, Mr. Yandel, do not take it even if you’re curious.”
“Wait. Isn’t this just poison, then?”
“Hey, is that what you think of us wizards? I swear there are no poisonous ingredients or components in this pill.”
“Then what happened to the people who died?”

“Well, there are a lot of hypotheses, but... The most likely explanation is that these people have a way to distinguish between those who are and are not evil spirits. And when the soul and body separate, the body dies.”

“...This is a dangerous pill.” This statement was sincere. This all meant that the moment I took this pill, my life would be in their hands. Of course, I could now believe to some extent that the person who had sent the drug was a player, but I had no information on what kind of player they were.

“Anyway, it’s definitely not poison. Although there’s no official record of it, there is a rumor that a captured evil spirit made a statement about this gathering. That means the pill is not lethal for everyone.”
“I see.”
“Oh, and one more peculiar thing is that in this world, everyone apparently appears in the form of their souls, so no one is able to tell who is who.”

That was some good news, and it cleared up some of my concerns. Was this why networking was so important? If it hadn’t been for my connection to a wizard, I wouldn’t have heard this kind of information anywhere else. However, I asked one last question. “Do you mean there is no way to figure out who took this pill?”
“Never. If we could, all the evil spirits would have been arrested by now.”
I could see why the sender was confident that the anonymity of the community was thoroughly guaranteed.
“So, on that note, can I study this pill?” she asked.
“I don’t care as long as it counts as today’s research.”

“How stingy, even though I answered all of your questions. Never mind. I don’t think anything else will come out of me taking a look at it, anyway.” She gave it back to me. “Now, if we’re done chatting, come sit here.”
As directed, I sat down on a chair. I didn’t bother asking if the chair was a torture device used to crack open human skulls.
“Then, let’s begin.”
“...Please wrap this up quickly.”
I already knew that this chair was a magic device designed to collect blood.
Zzzzzz!
At about four o’clock in the afternoon, a day’s worth of research was over, meaning I wouldn’t need to waste my time coming all the way here until next week.
“Oh, that’s the famous guy these days, right?”
“I heard that it was Lord Hernesion who gave him the nickname of Little Balkan.”
“That stingy man spoke that highly of a barbarian? How strange.”
As I left Raven’s private lab, I saw wizards gathered in the lobby shooting looks my way. Was this the power of fame?
Last time, they looked at me like I was raw material for their experiments just walking around...
I was realizing once again how well-known my name was.
“They say he has the essence of an Orc Hero?”
“Aru said that he even has the essence of a guardian vampire.”
“That is... definitely rare.”
Their gazes seemed to suggest they were looking at a very, very valuable ingredient for their experiments. After all, an adventurer’s reputation was out of these bastards’ wheelhouse.
“Hey! Can you come here for a second?” one called to me.
“I’m busy.”
“Just for a se—”
“I’m hungry, so no.”
Walking past stares that were several times more uncomfortable than usual, I escaped the Magic Tower.
I don’t have time to go to the library, so I should just get back to the inn and rest.

Organizing my thoughts on the trip over, it took me about an hour to get back to the inn, where I collapsed onto the bed. Then I took out the pill and studied it carefully. My thoughts wandered further and further, as if my mind itself was withdrawing from reality.
A community where anonymity is guaranteed...

The biggest reason I didn’t want to be in contact with other players was because of the risk. If even one person knew who I was, it wouldn’t be a secret anymore. But from what Raven was saying, it seemed like a virtual chatroom. Well, in the past, I had thought it wouldn’t be useful to have any contact with other players, but... Now, I changed my mind.
The people there would no doubt know a lot more than I do.

I was not thinking about hidden bits of information in the game. There was nothing someone else would know that I didn’t already know as well. However, this was another world, not a game made up of code. Now that the risk of my identity being exposed had been reduced, the advantages of doing this were more prominent than before.
I’ll have to check it out myself to be certain, but getting insider information wouldn’t be bad.

For example, what tactics the evil spirit hunters used, or whether the Adventurers’ Guild had come up with a new law and implemented it or not. Joining this community would make it easier to keep up to date with news like that. In other words, it would be a secret source of information.
I’m not really holding out hope, but they might even know the way to get back.
After staring at the pill for a long time, I made my decision.
It’s still better to take it.

I reached this conclusion after carefully weighing the risks I had to take and the return I could get. However, I didn’t plan on taking it right then. Not only would it take time for me to confirm there were no other risks, but...
Even if anonymity is guaranteed, someone sent me this invitation.

Think about it. If three invitations were sent, what would happen if all three people joined the community? The sender of the invitation would be able to infer the identities of the three new members.
It would be safer to take it after at least three months or half a year.
Of course, all of these assumptions were pointless if the community didn’t function the way I was envisioning.
Anyway, I’m not desperate for information right now.
I’d wait slowly and patiently, as always. Better safe than sorry.

Inside a laboratory on the upper floors of the tower, the moment the minute hand of the clock passed midnight, a man lying on a chair opened his eyes. Then he immediately got up and communicated with someone through a crystal ball. “Soul Queen, how did the most recent invite pan out?” He tried to hide it, but the excitement in his voice was obvious.
Soon, however, a well of deep disappointment appeared on the man’s face. “Nothing.”
“Huh, then I guess he really isn’t a player.”
“That’s very likely the case. So, what are you going to do with the unsent letters from this wave?”

The man thought for a moment. Originally, a total of seven letters were supposed to have been sent before this meeting. However, this time he only sent one because there was something he had wanted to confirm. “I must not delay them any longer on my account. Will you send out the letters that couldn’t be sent this time before the next meeting?”
“Yes, I will pass them on.” The short conversation ended with that. The lab was then filled with silence.
“I had my hopes up because he chose a shield at the coming-of-age ceremony...” the man muttered with a sigh. “But it wasn’t him this time, either.”
At this point, even he had started to think that the rumors circulating among the players might be true. As a fan, he had been continuously denying it this whole time, but...
Actually, it doesn’t make any sense for one person to have collected such a huge amount of data by himself.

Did he really exist? Or, as many had guessed, was he simply a person from the game company? It had been twenty years since he woke up in this unfamiliar world, and cracks were slowly forming in the man’s faith.

chapters.title: Chapter 77: Request (1)
paragraphs: It had already been fifteen days since I had returned alive from the labyrinth. In other words, there were about two weeks left until the portal reopened in Dimension Square. I couldn’t say I had taken a decent break. While I was completing tasks every day like chores, time had just passed without me realizing it. I wasn’t the only one who was busy, though.
“Hahaha! Isn’t that the famous Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel? If you have time today, let’s have a drink—”
“I’m tired.”
Except for Hikurod, who spent the whole time doing nothing, all the members of Team Half-Wit had had a busy two weeks.

First, Brown, having absorbed the essence of a Mimic during our last quest, had devoted himself to training every day to get used to his new ability. “Um, I think I now understand how to use the Sixth Sense ability.”

Dwalkie was the same. “...Oh, me? Don’t worry about me. I just haven’t slept in two days.” Now that his financial problems were resolved, he was cutting back on sleep to learn new spells from the Magic Tower. At one point, the dwarf grew worried he might be overdoing it, but he just answered, “No one knows what might happen on the next expedition, right? I have to prepare while I can.”

I was proud. When the hell did he get so mature? I was starting to think it was a good idea to stick with this party. Although I had the essence of an Orc Hero, if they kept leveling up at a similar pace, these teammates wouldn’t be a hindrance to me.
On our next expedition, we won’t have any issues even on the fourth floor.
They weren’t the only ones growing, though. In the past two weeks, Missha and I had also undergone a lot of changes. To start with me...
“Hahaha! Congratulations,” Hikurod told me. “You received an epithet in three months and even got promoted to a rank-six adventurer. I’m starting to get worried that I’ll end up falling behind soon!”
“If you are worried, how about making an effort?”
“Actually, I’m looking for some rare items I can use!”

A few days ago, I was promoted to a rank-six adventurer. Contrary to what I had believed, going straight to rank five was not possible. Starting at rank five, you had to take a test, and in order to take the test, you had to build a kind of public service record by filling requests sent into the guild.
Man, the game didn’t have anything like this.

There was no use complaining at this point. The game I played took place about 150 years ago. Over the course of more than a century, this society must have undergone countless updates, just like the library, which had only been under construction in the game.
“Oh, is that the new weapon you bought? It seems dependable just looking at it.”

I also underwent a slight upgrade in terms of equipment. First, I bought a new mace to replace the one I lost. It cost four hundred thousand stones, making it more than twice as expensive as the previous one, because it required that much more iron.
[Your Total Item Level has increased by +185.]
Its size and weight were overwhelming, but as my strength had increased significantly this time, I had no issues using it.
“By the way, I remember Miss Karlstein said she was going to change her weapon too. How did that go?” asked Dwalkie.
“Oh, that? I don’t even want to talk about it, so ask him.” Missha pointed at me.
Mm, I had thought she would quit whining by now. “She bought a pair of swords.”

Missha’s main weapon changed a few days ago to a Lich’s twin blades, which were each about 70 percent the size of a standard sword. I paid 550,000 stones for them at a blacksmith that Hikurod told me about.
“Dual swords?” Hikurod and Brown muttered at the same time, and Missha took the opportunity to whine.
“Right? It sounds weird to you guys, too, rrright?”
“Weird? I think you’ve misunderstood.”
“Hmm?”
“I was surprised because I had been thinking the same thing,” Brown said. “Being ambidextrous, using both hands is good, so I wondered if you had any reason for sticking with a dagger.”
“...What do you mean?”
“Maybe it’s different if you’re facing off against a person, but we mainly fight monsters, right? From now on, you will run into a lot of large monsters too.”

In summary, it had been a bit concerning to him that she had been using a short dagger, so this worked out well. Perhaps this was a different reaction than she had been expecting, because Missha turned to the dwarf in bewilderment.

“Twin blades, huh? It’s definitely not a bad choice. After all, we’ll be holding the front lines anyway. Hahaha!” Hikurod, in the tank position, was just pleased that the close-range damage dealer had moved into a full attack role.
Then, Dwalkie spoke up. “I’m unfamiliar with this subject, but I think handling a new weapon, and two at that, will be difficult to adjust to...”
“Right! That’s what I was trrrying to say! I might end up getting taken out by a goblin during the next quest!” Missha was bolstered by Dwalkie’s sympathy and glanced at me.
All I could say was this: “Then practice more so that you don’t get taken out by a goblin.”

Again, the easy way was the slow way. It may be difficult to acquire proficiency in a new weapon now, but in the game, an Ice Dual-Sword Master was the strongest melee damage dealer in the second half, because there was a super-overpowered numbered item they could use.
“Whew, okay, stop nagging.”
“I’m not nagging but giving you advice for your future.”
“That’s nagging.”
When Missha and I began to bicker, Dwalkie interrupted like a dunce. “But if you don’t like it that much, can’t you just keep your weapon?”
“Hmm?”
“I mean, it’s not like Bjorn is your father. Do you really have to do what he says? To be honest, it seems to me that he is crossing the line, which is making me uncomfortable.”
Crossing the line? Well, it might look like that to a third party, but there was one thing he didn’t know.
“I-I don’t hate it that much. Although it’s tough now, there are cerrrtainly some advantages over using a dagger...”
“I-Is that right?” Dwalkie stuttered.
“Yeah, so don’t blame Bjorn. The decision is mine.”
I had never forced anything on Missha. I just strongly persuaded her with reasonable incentive.
Hikurod cut in. “Then, for the next expedition, we can aim for the middle of the fourth floor. Hahaha!”
“If possible, when passing through the second floor, I would like to take a route I haven’t been to yet,” requested Brown.
“Hmm, is it because of experience? If that’s the case, I’ll have to revise the route.”

After we had dinner and finalized the plans for our quest, this week’s meeting quickly came to an end. Actually, it was called a meeting, but it was more like a get-together once a week to update each other.
“Bjorn, are you two leaving together again?” Hikurod asked, glancing at Missha.
“We’re going in the same direction.”
“Hmm, I mean, you guys have gotten really close recently.”
Well, it seems to me that you and Dwalkie are closer.
Ignoring the dwarf’s meddling, Missha and I left the tavern. “Oh, right. Bjorn! The equipment we orderrred a while ago is ready to be picked up!”
“It’s late today, so I can go pick it up tomorrow.”
“But what did you orderrr that it took so long?”
“Oh, didn’t I tell you? It was underpants.”
“Underpants...?”

Of course, not just plain underpants. Among male adventurers, it was a piece of equipment that was colloquially called an egg guard. Put bluntly, it was a scrotum guard. “I bought it at a slightly higher price because it had to be imbued with magic.”
“Eh? W-Why do you need to enchant something like that with magic?!”
“Something like that?”
“N-No, that’s not what I mean... Well, I’m sure it’s difficult for you to find one that fits, so I can understand...”
What now? “I can’t end up naked every time my body grows larger.”

The role of a player was to customize their equipment according to the essences they had consumed. So, to prepare for Giantization, I found clothes of the desired size, then enchanted them with Automatic Repair, Shape Change, and Acid Immunity. Because the panties—no, the underpants—I wanted were unlikely to be sold on the market, I spent about nine hundred thousand stones.

“Ah, that’s why you enchanted it. I thought it was something else...” Missha released a big breath, implying whatever misunderstanding she had had been cleared up. But she seemed to have a new question. “Then... are you just going to be wearing that in the labyrinth?” she asked in a strange voice.
“That’s right,” I answered proudly.

I didn’t have an exact word to describe them so I called them underpants, but they were actually closer to shorts that went down to the thighs, the kind that cyclists often wore. Besides, they were not made of a tight material but leather, so there was nothing to be ashamed of. Well, I hadn’t tried them on myself yet, but there definitely wasn’t. Was I not a barbarian? Efficiency was more important than feelings.
Anyway, as the two of us were chatting and walking, we arrived at the inn. “Go to sleep, then.”
“Mmm, I will. But do you want me to come with you to pick up the equipment tomorrrow?”
“Don’t be lazy; keep swinging your sword while I’m away.”
“I’m not being lazy!”
Of course you’re not. “I have somewhere to go by myself tomorrow, anyway.”
“Alone? Where arrre you going?”
“I am going to the Holy Land,” I replied succinctly.
I had money, and I had the essence of an Orc Hero now, which was the core of my training method. It was time to gradually upgrade the level of my Spirit Imprint.
I woke up early in the morning and balanced my ledger once more.
The mace, underpants, and double sword combined are 1.85 million stones.
The Beast Blood I had purchased to raise Missha’s Soul Beast level was two million stones. The cost of enchanting the lithium breastplate and shield with Acid Immunity was 510,000 stones.
If I subtract ninety thousand stones for a month’s living expenses...

There were already only 3.7 million stones left. Of course, these were all necessary expenses, so it didn’t feel like a waste. Without Beast Blood, it would have taken a long time for Missha to be able to add an Ice attribute to her weapon.
Equipment enchantment should have been done earlier too.

When I first bought the equipment, I had the Ring of the Frost Spirit, and I didn’t have any money on hand, so I skipped it. As a result, I’d had to pay five hundred thousand stones’ worth of repair costs. Shit, I should’ve saved money on something else.

After washing off a bit and walking for a while, I arrived at the Holy Land, where the chief of the tribe welcomed me with a small smile on his lips. “Bjorn, son of Yandel! I can no longer call you a young warrior. I hear you have the moniker Little Balkan?”
“That’s right!” I nodded proudly as I played the part of a barbarian making a glorious return.
But this was a cold barbarian world.

“So, why are you here?” After exchanging a word or two, the chieftain got straight to the point. Like a barbarian, he cut the small talk very short. To be honest, I had thought that words of admiration, praise, or encouragement would follow.
Well, this lets me save time, which is nice.
Perhaps barbarians were the most rational race in this city. As I seriously contemplated this, I promptly brought up my reason for being here. “I have come to receive a Spirit Imprint.”
“I see. I’ll call a shaman. Talk to him.”
After that, everything was quickly arranged. The chieftain left on important business, and the shaman’s apprentice came and led me to the tent.
As I entered, a shaman with impressively wrinkled skin greeted me. “Haha. It’s you again.”
“How did you know it was me?” I asked.
“Well, it is rare for a warrior to thank a shaman.”
No, I meant how did you recognize me while wearing a blindfold?
I didn’t ask again. Being a shaman, there must be something mystical about him.
“Are you here to get the second imprint of the Immortality Path?”
“That’s right.”
“It costs a million stones.”
I flinched. “A million stones?”
“Are you not prepared?”
“...That’s not it.” I was just surprised that the price was the same as in the game. The first stage had been 150,000 stones more expensive.
Clink.

But that was unimportant. I took out the money and dropped it in the jar in front of me as instructed by the shaman. Then he chuckled. “I’m glad you paid the right amount. Last time I received fifty thousand stones less than expected, which was a headache.”
“...Fifty thousand stones less? What do you mean?”
“Young warrior, you have nothing to worry about. It’s all the fault of the stupid chieftain.”
I mean, it still bothered me. I had an inkling, so once I lay facedown on the blanket as instructed, I asked another question. “Shaman, what is the original cost of the first stage of the imprint?”
“It’s 550,000 stones.”
“...I see.”

With that one answer, all my suspicions were confirmed. At that time, the chief said the cost was seven hundred thousand stones. Of course, I didn’t think he said that to con me. It was just that I hadn’t noticed at the time.
“The cost of the Immortality Imprint is... well, it must be around seven hundred thousand stones!”
The chieftain was also a barbarian, so he was very weak when it came to letters and numbers.
Huh, and didn’t he say that he was giving me a discount of two hundred thousand stones or whatever?
Well, as a result, I was now saving fifty thousand stones, so there would be no loss on my end. Still, I felt like an idiot for being so innocently happy back then.
“Let’s begin then.”
As soon as the needle pierced my skin, all the worries, concerns, and thoughts that filled my head disappeared. It was the first intense pain I had felt in a long while.
“Young warrior, do not hold back. Even if you scream—”
“Aaargh!”
Fuck, I thought I’d be fine with Pain Resistance. I didn’t think it wouldn’t work on this.
...I’ll have to proceed with the third stage tomorrow.
Apparently, a reevaluation of the plan was in order.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 2. Your Endurance and Mana Resistance have increased significantly. Your Physique stat has increased by +20. Your Spirit stat has increased by +20.]
‘This would be the longest fifteen minutes of my life?’ I had been a fool when I said that.
“Okay, it’s over.”

The first stage took twelve hours to complete, but the second stage only took ten minutes. However, the pain was beyond imagination, to the extent that I wondered if all the pain I’d had to endure for those first twelve hours had been compressed into ten minutes for this one.

“Haha, I’ve never seen anyone finish while conscious.” At the sight of my half-passed-out form, the shaman giggled like a psychopath. Then he held something out to me. “Here. Pick one. There is still time, so let me steal a look at your fate.”
What was this? Fortune-telling? As it was a fantasy world, the accuracy of it must be high...
“It’s nothing grand, so go ahead and pick one. I can still determine whether good things will happen in your future or not.”
In that case, since I didn’t sense any malice, I pulled out one of the dozens of sticks from the barrel without much thought.
Then the shaman was silent for a moment. It made me anxious. “Young warrior, what is your date of birth?”
Uh, I didn’t think you’d need to read my birth chart...
As I contemplated how to respond, the shaman giggled again. “Hahaha, that was a joke. How can a warrior know something like their date of birth?”
“...So what is my fate like?”
“It is special. I have seen the fates of many warriors, but this is the first time that I have seen such bad luck.”
Hmm, that was exactly what the shaman that my mother went to see a long time ago had said too. I guess my fortune had been rotten from the start.
“You have probably gone through countless hardships that most others only experience once in their life, and will continue to experience them.”
“I see.” Damn, this was why you shouldn’t go to a fortune teller. I already knew that deep down, but hearing a shaman from a fantasy universe flat-out say it made me depressed.
“Don’t be too discouraged, young warrior. Bad luck is not necessarily a bad thing for you.”
“It’s not a bad thing?”
“Your destiny is not just bad luck, but good fortune that is second to none. And if you are not consumed by evil, your bad luck will eventually turn into good luck.”
“What do you mean? Say it simply.” I wasn’t pretending to be a barbarian this time—I was being serious. Was it customary in this trade to speak incomprehensibly, whether here or on Earth?

“Hahaha. It means you are destined to experience countless once-in-a-lifetime events, both good and bad.” It felt like my head was vibrating. “It is a fate that many who are deemed heroes are born with.”

I didn’t know about being a hero, but one thing was clear. There had been countless shitty things that had happened in my life, but in the end, I was still alive and breathing. I just thought it was because I had powerful bad luck. But looking back now, shitty things weren’t the only thing that happened to me.
“Haha, it looks like you know what I’m talking about.”

Even in the case of the Bloody Citadel, I had almost died when the Vampire Duke Cambormere appeared, but as a result, I was able to acquire the bastard’s essence. And the Lord of the Floor? All sorts of insane things went down, but in the process, I was able to obtain the essence of an Orc Hero.
“If it’s the fate of a hero, does that mean I won’t die no matter what I go through?”

“Of course not.” The shaman smiled like he was talking to an innocent young warrior. Then, his mood shifted to something more solemn. “Some are devoured by fate, some conform to it, and some overcome it,” he murmured.
“Make it easier to understand.”
“It is up to you, not fate.”
So you’re just going to say things I don’t understand the whole time, I see.
Fate or whatever, this changed nothing. I shouldn’t even consider relying on something else. I just had to stay alert and do whatever I had to do so that I could survive whatever came my way.

chapters.title: Chapter 78: Request (2)
paragraphs: “Do you know what is going to happen in the near future too?” I asked the shaman.
“No, I can’t see anything like that. However, be wary of those who harbor resentment toward you at any time, anywhere. Your destiny attracts gatherings of such people.”
“Easier.”
“If you can fix their pain, that would be a blessing, and if you can’t resolve it, it will become an issue.”
Did he not know what “easier” meant?
“I’m hungry, so you can leave now.”
“I will.”
After the shaman ordered me to leave, I exited the tent. Then, with a body that had been utterly drained of energy, I trudged toward the city. As I was walking, however, energy slowly returned to me.
Is it because of the Spirit Imprint?

In the first stage of the Immortality Imprint, your natural healing factor increased, and in the second stage, endurance and mana resistance increased. Mana resistance was literally resistance to magic spells, and endurance affected your maximum stamina and regeneration speed. In other words, unlike physical stats such as strength and agility, these weren’t values that stood out.
Not bad.

However, if you didn’t dedicate time to supporting these boosts too, your character would not be able to function properly later. Not only that, but in order to unlock the six-step imprint, which was the core of my training method, I needed to slowly build it up starting now.
The imprint is already quite useful on its own from the third phase onward.
Originally, I had planned to go straight through to phase three, but I left that for tomorrow. So, since I had some time today—

“Bjorn!” As I was reevaluating my plans for the day, I heard a familiar voice from somewhere nearby, a call that sounded like a whisper. I wondered for a moment if I’d heard wrong, but... “Bjorn!” As soon as I looked in the direction the sound was coming from, a face popped out of a rustling bush.
“...Ainar?”
“Be quiet! If I get caught, I’ll be in big trouble!”
