At Ainar’s urgent request, I squatted down in front of the bushes and lowered my voice. “...Why are you here?”
“I heard from the elder that you had come to the Holy Land, so I came to visit. You have to cross this road to get to the city, right?”
Hmm, I see. But did you know when I would be passing by?
“I’m glad you came early, though. My legs were getting numb!” I guess she had been planning on waiting here until I did. Very Ainar-like. “Anyway, we don’t know who will walk by, so get in.”

Not only was she a welcome sight, but I was curious about how things were going for her, so I walked over to the thick bush and squatted inside. Only then did I get a proper look at Ainar’s body. “Why are you so skinny?” I asked with genuine concern.

Due to the essence of the Bone Knight, her height had decreased to around 5′7″. Back then, she hadn’t seemed so small because of her muscles, but now? Ainar smiled bitterly. “Hahaha, don’t look too closely, otherwise I’ll get embarrassed. I know I look unattractive.”
In just one month, her rugged warrior’s body had been transformed into a slender, muscular one. “Doesn’t the elder feed you?”
“It’s not like that, but because I’ve been compressing my muscles every day, I ended up like this.”
“Compress?”
“It’s a long story. I don’t know much about it, either, so don’t ask for details.”
“I see...” Whatever it was, what kind of training turned a healthy kid into this? I couldn’t help feeling bad and kept my mouth shut.
Ainar then smiled and changed the subject. “I heard about you from the elder. You earned the nickname of Little Balkan, right? You’re amazing, Bjorn!”
“It’s nothing.”
“What happened out there? I’m curious what your story is.” Ainar looked at me with shining eyes. After training day in and day out, she must have been curious about the outside world.
I felt bad for her, so I sat down and started telling her the story in earnest.
“Oh, you’re in the same party as Hikurod? That’s a relief. I was nervous about leaving you, but I can trust him.”
I told her about teaming up with Hikurod and many of the events that happened in the labyrinth. But just when the story was about to end, we heard a roar in the distance.
“Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin! Did you run away again!?”
Ainar hurriedly got up at the roar that made our ears ring. “Th-this is bad. I think the elder noticed that I’m not there.”
“Are you going to be okay?” I asked worriedly.
“It’s okay. It’s just that my training for today will be doubled. Don’t worry too much, I’ll just have to forget about sleeping.”
No, that only worried me more...
“I was about to die of boredom, but it was nice hearing an exciting story from you. So please come again soon.”
“Okay.”

“Then I’ll get going now!” Soon, Ainar turned around and started running in the direction of the shout. When I was just about to leave as well, however, Ainar suddenly turned around and called out something unexpected. “Oh, right! Bjorn! I didn’t say it earlier, but it’s nice to see your face is looking well!”
“My face?”
“In the past, it was, I guess, full of hostility? Well, there wasn’t a problem with that, but! Now it looks more relaxed! Maybe because your new teammates are trustworthy people!”
Hmm, really? I’m not sure about that...
“Ainar! Get over here!”
“Ugh, see you later! I will continue to train hard and return a more reliable warrior!”
Soon, Ainar’s figure disappeared from sight. I continued to look in that direction for a moment, lost in thought.
No more hostility, huh?
Could this be a positive change or a negative one? I couldn’t be sure yet.
Since the Spirit Imprint session had ended early, I had quite a bit of time left, so I visited the Magic Tower to meet this week’s research quota.
“Oh? Mr. Yandel?” Raven asked. “Why...? Weren’t you coming tomorrow?”
“I’m here today because I have things to do tomorrow.”
“If you had a previous engagement, shouldn’t you have moved it to another date?”
...That was a reasonable argument. However, I was a noble barbarian, not bound to society’s manners and customs. “What is a previous engagement?”
“Ugh, only in times like these... All right. Wait here. I’ll just finish what I’m doing and we can start.”
“Sure.”

After I had waited for a while, preparations for today’s experiments were complete. She told me that the goal of today’s tests was to check how the vampire’s mana resistance affected psychological magic, and to measure the exact threshold of reduced solar resistance...
“Enough explaining. Just do it.”
“Okay, then, I’ll begin.”
Zzzzzz!

The tests were over sooner than I expected, as I had been fixated on the brutal experimentation tools. Just as I was about to bolt out of there, Raven hastily called out to me. “Wait, Mr. Yandel!” I wondered if this was about something related to the research, but she instead asked, “So, when are you going to tell me?”
“What do you mean?”
“The holy relic you used to kill the vampire! How did you know? That the Tears of a Goddess were there?”
Oh, this again? We had this conversation every time I came to this place. “Again, I told you I don’t even know what that is.”
“That again, huh?” Raven crossed her arms and glared at me. Did she know? With that small stature of hers, that pose just made her look huffy.
“Arua Raven, what are these Tears of a Goddess and why are you so obsessed with them?” I asked bluntly.

At first, I had wondered if she suspected I was an evil spirit. However, judging by her behavior since then, it seemed that was not the case. Just look at when I asked her about the pill and letter. If she had been suspicious of me, it would’ve been revealed in some way or another during that conversation.
“...It’s not because of the relic,” she finally answered.
If you’re not suspicious of me, then what is it?
The answer I received was something I never really considered. “It’s because of the book that contains information about the relic.”
“Book?”
“The Complete Book of Rifts. You’re not going to deny knowing about it, are you?”
No, even if you look at me like that, I’ve really never heard of it...
“I understand you want to keep the existence of the book a secret because I did too. Knowledge becomes more valuable the fewer people know it, right?”
“...So what is it that you want to say?”
“If you have the book or know its contents, I want to buy it off of you. Mine wasn’t properly stored, so there are many sections of it that are unreadable.”

As I looked into those zealous eyes, I didn’t get the impression that she was trying to use a lie to feel me out. This was really all because of a book? “If that was your goal, you could’ve just asked me without beating around the bush.”

“But the one who seems desperate is the one who loses the negotiation.” That was true. As I nodded absentmindedly, she frankly confessed what her aim was. “If you admitted that you found the relic, then I was considering acting like it wasn’t anything special so I could negotiate with you. The fact that you seem to know the value doesn’t help, though...”
“So you chose the straightforward tactic.”
“Yes. So, can’t you please tell me the truth now?”

I pondered this for a moment. At the time, I had been completely confident that the item I was using was a holy relic, so it didn’t seem like a good idea to lie here. It was probably better to admit it. “I got the Tears of a Goddess or whatever by breaking the statue in front of the fountain.”
“Of course! I knew it!”
“But that’s it.”
“...Pardon?”
At her bewildered look, I quickly added, “While you guys were looking around, I broke it because I was bored and that’s what came out.”

“Then... you don’t know about the book?” she mumbled with a blank expression on her face. But then she quickly gathered her wits and shot back, “Wait. There’s a contradiction here. If that’s true, how did you think to use the item in that situation when you didn’t know what it was?”

Quite an astute question. However, since I had already anticipated it, it didn’t at all obstruct my answer. “There was a symbol of a goddess on the box, so I figured it was that kind of item. And it actually worked.”
“...Really?”
“On my honor as a warrior, everything I just said is true.”
Raven’s expression turned into a gloomy one as soon as I made the vow of a modern barbarian, which was little more than a cheat code at this point. “Then... what have I been doing this whole time?”
When she realized that she had been shadowboxing on her own for weeks, she felt ashamed.

Although I felt sorry for her, at the same time I also thought of the community of players, the Ghost Busters. I thought that the greatest strength of that community was its ability to exchange information, but...
For someone else, maybe it wouldn’t be.
I was a player to some, and an evil spirit to others.
“I’m hungry, so I’m going to go!” Like a barbarian, I flung the door open and left.

Missha, who followed me like her savior; Hikurod, who treated me like a friend; even Ainar, who always told me that I would become a great warrior one day and looked up to me... they were all the same. Bjorn, son of Yandel. I could not be honest with anyone while I was in this body.
Well, I didn’t think Hansu Lee’s body would be any different.

After leaving the Magic Tower, I headed straight to the commercial district and picked up the finished magic panties. The time was 5 p.m. It was a little early to end the day here, so I dragged my weary body to the library. That would be more productive than going to get some rest.
“Parsytiev.”

After getting enchanted by the librarian, I headed straight for the bookshelves. Even if I tried to say hello, she wasn’t going to acknowledge it, and I didn’t have the energy to deal with that today.
“...I heard you’re famous now.” However, the librarian, who usually couldn’t be bothered to even talk to me, came up to me for some reason.
“It’s a long story,” I replied vaguely before walking away. I used to think that, with her being a wizard, it would be beneficial to me if we were on friendly terms.
Actually, it’s funny to even entertain that kind of thought now.

I was a rank-six adventurer and even had the moniker of Little Balkan. Not only were my specs sufficient enough to join a party with a wizard, but my current team already had one, although he may not have been from the Magic Tower.
Seeing as this one is working as a librarian, she must be the same.
The thought made me smile. I knew that no matter what the reason was, it was just an attempt at rationalization, just a way of legitimizing my decision.
Step.

In the end, my intentions were different. I just didn’t want to. I didn’t want to try to win the favor of others by calculating every single action I took—at least for today. Which was why I was a little tired.
Step.
Therefore, I stopped walking toward the bookshelf and faced the problem I had been neglecting head-on.
It’s only natural that Ainar said my hostility is gone.

I had a problem, a mental problem. The emotions that I had assumed ran dry a long time ago were rearing their heads now that my body was doing well. That was bad news for me, for whom survival came first. So what was the solution?
I don’t know, so let’s do what we have to do.
I turned around and walked up to the librarian. “Don’t stare blankly. If you have something you want to say, say it quickly,” I said.
“...How did you know I had something to say?”
“From your eyes.” There were several clues, actually, but they were too annoying to explain.

As I stared at her with sentiments like that in my eyes, the sharp-witted librarian succinctly explained, “I have a friend who works at the administrative office. She is looking for an adventurer to entrust with a request, so I recommended you.”
“You recommended me?”

“Strictly speaking, it wasn’t a recommendation. Your name came up during the conversation, and when my friend heard it, she asked to meet you. Of course, if you’re busy or don’t want to, you can say no—”
“All right. Let me hear her out.”
The librarian, who looked surprised at my answer, nodded slightly. “I’ll pass that information on to my friend, then.”
A request, huh? It was about time for an event like that to happen.
Do I now have a way to earn money in the city?
It was a good idea to hear this out.

chapters.title: Chapter 79: Request (3)
paragraphs: “Bjorn, arrre you going to the Holy Land again today?”
“There was something I couldn’t finish yesterday. I’ll be back in the evening, so don’t skip out on training.”

As soon as the day dawned, I headed to the Holy Land to get the third phase of the imprint. The cost was two million stones, the same as in the game. This also corresponded with the fact that the user was given a characteristic each time their Spirit Imprint’s level reached a multiple of three.

“Hahaha, I’ve never seen a barbarian with as much money as you. You have three paths in front of you. There is the soul of flame, the soul of iron, and the soul of the wild.” When I put the money into the jar, the shaman asked, “Warrior, what will you choose?”

I listened to the shaman’s explanation just in case, but it didn’t seem like the reality patch had changed anything. And so... “I will choose the soul of the wild.” I chose it without any hesitation because this trait was one of the core features of the shield barbarian.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 3. Your Physical Resistance and Fire Resistance have significantly increased. Your Physique has increased by +50.]
[A spirit of the wild now resides in your body. Your base Threat Level is greatly increased. You can now use Wild Outburst.]

Threat Level—in other words, your probability of attracting aggro from monsters just by breathing was increased. In addition, Wild Outburst temporarily increased the user’s Threat Level by three times, and I could earn a bonus to my physical stats proportional to that number.
Originally, I only occasionally used this when developing a greatsword barbarian.

In my early days, I often compensated for the barbarians’ inability to survive with Immortality Imprints. However, at the time, Wild Outburst had been a double-edged sword. The stronger the character, the more enemies came at them. Of course, it was different for a shield barbarian.
No risk, high reward.

Monster aggro? As a tank, that was rather welcome. Plus, the increase in Physique not only meant an improvement in sturdiness, but when used in conjunction with Giantization—which greatly increased the user’s Threat Level—you could achieve a temporary, extreme payoff.
I didn’t realize that I would finish the third phase of the Imprint for Giantization in three months.
While I was satisfied with my growth, it also felt bittersweet. All I had done was struggle to survive, but somehow, I had ended up here.
“I’m tired, so you may leave.”

It was 5 p.m. by the time I left with the Soul Imprint. Since Missha had promised to cook beef, I quickly stopped by the library and returned to the inn after double-checking our appointment time. Then, after various experiments, I figured out the conditions for triggering Wild Outburst.
“Behelaaah!”
So that was how it worked.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 3
Physique: 330 (New +50)
Spirit: 124
Special Ability: 115
Item Level: 828
General Combat Power: 822 (New +50)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Vampire (Guardian) - Rank 5  Orc Hero - Rank 5]

For lunch the next day, I headed to the meeting place by myself. The name of the store was “The Promise of Flowing Water,” so I was wondering what kind of place it was, but it was just an ordinary dessert shop. Fuck.
“...A barbarian?”
“What the heck? Is the owner in debt?”
As soon as I walked in, all eyes turned to me. Somehow it was even worse than the library. It wasn’t like I wasn’t allowed to be here.
“Are you Mr. Yandel? Over here!”
It wouldn’t be efficient to change seats, so I went and sat down. “Were you the one who made the request?”
“Yes. My name is Shavin Emoor, a rank-seven officer at the Ravigion Administrative Office. You can call me Shavin.”
“Sure.”

Shavin Emoor, race: human. When the librarian said the requestee was a friend of hers, I had expected her to be young, but she looked to be in her early thirties. She seemed like a nice person, but I’d know her actual personality after some conversation.
“I didn’t order because I didn’t know what you would like. What do you want to eat?”
“I’ll get grilled meat with beer.”
“...Pardon?”
“If not, then never mind. I don’t like sweets.”
“Ah, I see...”
That should be enough of an unspoken protest for being called to meet at a place like this. I hurriedly got to the point. “So, what is your request?”
“Didn’t you hear from Ragna?”
“Ragna? Oh, you mean the librarian?”

Shavin seemed startled by my question, then nodded like she understood. “I guess you didn’t know her name. Yeah... makes sense for Ragna. Her name is Ragna Litaniel Peprock. She’s not a bad kid, so please don’t get too mad at her.”
I had nothing to be mad about since I had never asked her name in the first place. I repeated the name to myself. “Ragna Litanel Peprock, huh?”
“Not Litanel, Litaniel.”
Anyway, that. Why was her name so difficult to pronounce? “...Is she a noble?”

“No, it’s not like that...” When I asked the first question that popped into my head, the response I received was quite strange. “I can’t tell you in detail. If she finds out, she’ll definitely get angry.”
So, there was a story behind it, huh? “Tell me the contents of your request.”

“It’s a simple patrol request. Sometimes criminals and non-taxpayers hide in the sewers, so they require regular patrols. But...” Shavin trailed off, her tone strange, like she was waiting for something.

Just in case, I chimed in, and Shavin’s expression shifted in a way that suggested she had been waiting for exactly that. She continued her explanation. “But the adventurers who are usually commissioned for patrols didn’t return from the labyrinth this time. As you well know, Mr. Yandel...”
“...Know?”
“There was a big incident on the third floor. It appears they got caught up in that! It’s such a tragedy.”
I didn’t know if it was a tragedy or not, but I did know there was something up with her. “That’s why you decided to entrust this request to me.”
“Yes. Because it is an official request from the administrative office, it cannot be entrusted to just anyone. So, while I was looking for the right person, Ragna told me about you!”
“I see.” I understood the basic context. Except... “Why me? There must have been other people who were better suited.”

Now that I had listened to the details, it seemed more like a chore than a commission. The administrative office must have entrusted the requests to adventurers in the same way one might deal with a subcontractor, and the pay couldn’t have been that great either. However, even so, the number of people in this city willing to take on this request would have been many.
This person wasn’t sent by the evil spirit hunters, was she?
In my heart, I momentarily assumed the worst, but the answer I received was absurdly succinct.
“Aren’t you the most talked-about person these days?”
“What?”

“Honestly, I was a little curious. I also wanted to meet you in person...” In a nutshell, she took up the role of making a request for the administrative office to satisfy her personal curiosity. “Oh, I’m going to buy some cookies to go for later. Can I brag to my co-workers that you bought them for me?”
“...Do as you like.”

Judging by that bright smile, this didn’t seem to be an act. “So, what will you do? The pay is only two hundred thousand stones, but it wouldn’t be a bad deal for you, either. I’m embarrassed to say this out loud, but...”
Ugh, again? Can’t you just tell me straight-up?
It was like she was playing games with me. “...But?”

When I urged her on again with a soulless question, Shavin happily continued. “There are some people who consider receiving a request from the administrative office a reward in itself! And can I also mention that, since our selection criteria are a bit strict, the people we hire are considered by other organizations to be verified talent?”

This time, her statement ended with a question. When looking at this from a barbarian’s perspective, there seemed to be a lot of vagueness mixed in to the things she was saying. “So that means that my credibility will also go up.” I was a barbarian with a savage body and a modern mind.
Shavin applauded my short and concise summary. “Yes! Simply put, yes! Mm, well... with your reputation, I’m sure you’re receiving lots of requests from all over.”

“Not exactly.” I smiled bitterly. It had been two weeks since I got the reputation of Little Balkan. Nevertheless, this was the first time someone had contacted me for the purpose of commissioning me. I could roughly guess the reason why.
It must be because I am an uneducated barbarian.

There was a difference between being good at fighting and being smart. Maybe I could use this opportunity to alter the public’s perception of me. But I shouldn’t stand out too much, either... Soon, I made up my mind.
“That request, I will do it.”
“Then I’ll be going now.” After hearing the details of the request, the barbarian left the shop without any regrets.
Shavin smiled as she watched him leave.
“He’s the first interesting person I’ve met in a while.”

She had wondered why Ragna had brought him up in conversation, but she could see it now. She felt a sense of inner peace after talking to someone who was innocent, unlike so many others. That child must have felt the same way, no matter how flippant her words were. It was safe to say that it had been a few years since Ragna had brought someone up in conversation first.
Still, I was worried, so I asked to meet him in person. But he doesn’t seem bad.

It seemed like he didn’t know anything about Ragna, either. Shavin sipped on her tea and got her thoughts in order. Next time, it would be a good idea to set up a meeting for the three of them while staging it as a coincidence. If she left them alone, they would never get to know each other for the rest of their lives.
Maybe I’m going too far...
The time had come for that child to make friends.
Two days later, ten days before the labyrinth opened, I arrived at the entrance to the sewer under the guidance of the staff—with the entirety of Team Half-Wit somehow tagging along.
“...Bjorn, you didn’t say it was going to stink like this,” complained Hikurod.
“I didn’t know it was this bad, either. But shouldn’t you have expected this when I told you it was a sewer?”
“W-Well, yes, but...”
Yesterday, when we all got together, I brought up the request I received and this was what happened:
“You don’t have to share the payment, but exploring the sewer with all kinds of ghost stories? Hahaha! How can I miss out on an opportunity like that?” Hikurod laughed.
“Can I come along?” Dwalkie requested. “My head’s been hurting from reading books every day, so this will be a good change of pace.”
“Hmm, the roads in the sewers are complicated, right? It would be a perfect place to test out my new abilities,” Brown said thoughtfully.
“A place where criminals go to hide? It might be dangerrrous alone,” Missha cautioned.

Everyone was bored from training every day, so it was decided that they would tag along. I just said yes. There was no need to share the pay from the commission, so there was no need to shy away from free manpower.
I don’t know about the others, but Rotmiller, the scout, will be of great help.

After passing the map I had received from the staff to Brown, I put a video recording device into the groove of my helmet to record the patrol process. That concluded the preparations. “Let’s get going.” I took the lead and opened the iron doors, then headed down the damp stairs to the basement. When I reached the last step, there was hardly any light, so I had to light a torch.
“It’s bigger inside than I thought.”
“That’s why there are some people who live down here. Hahaha!”
The flowing gutter water and the ditch next to it painted a bleak picture in the flickering torchlight.
“This way.”
Following Brown’s instructions, we walked over the ditch, careful not to fall into the water. The farther away we got from the entrance, the noticeably darker our surroundings became.
“Do you know about this? There’s a myth that a terrible monster lives in the sewers...” The dwarf laughed and spread rumors like he was just here to have fun.
Missha and Dwalkie naively egged him on. “Dwalkie, could therrre really be a monster here?”
“I heard that all the waste from the Tower ends up in the sewer. If reagents randomly met and reacted with a monster corpse, it might be possible to create such a creature.”
“I-is it?”
Of course it wasn’t. Our predecessor had been paid 150,000 stones per patrol and had gone in and out of the sewers for two years without any problems.
Splash, splash.
I sighed inwardly and was careful where I stepped. But, was it because of the nonstop ghost stories that Hikurod was telling? Every step suddenly sounded a lot louder.
Since the five of us are here, it feels like we’re in some sort of dungeon.
Fuck, nothing bad was going to happen, right?

chapters.title: Chapter 80: Sewerage (1)
paragraphs: I walked through the sewer like that for who knows how long. After a while, Missha and Hikurod began to get bored.
“There’s really nothing here.”
“Rrright? I hope something comes out soon...”
No wonder they had asked to come. What did they expect? “I told you. It’s just a patrol commission, that’s it.”

This request was simple. Placing the video recording device I had borrowed on my head, I just had to go around a set route and look for anyone hiding there. Well, a fight might end up happening in the process, but they said my predecessor had found less than thirty people in two years. The frequency of encounters with strangers itself was low. And even if I did run into one, I explained, I didn’t have to chase after each one and fight them.
“Huh? You don’t have to chase after them?”
“There is extra pay if they’re caught, but there is no need to get hung up on that.”
“Why?” Missha asked.
“That’s because the request I received was Sewer Patrol. Capture and arrests will be handled by new personnel after the Administrative Office has checked the video records.”
“I see...”
While I was briefing Missha on the request, Brown, who was at the front leading the party, suddenly stopped walking. “I can sense something nearby.”

There was an unfounded murmur about his senses, but at that one word, everyone in the party looked around. Since the sewer was full of a musty smell, his olfactory stats wouldn’t shine as brightly here, but Brown had +50 to his Sixth Sense stat and +20 Luck from the Mimic’s essence.
After a moment, Missha pointed somewhere and shouted, “Oh! I-It’s a person!”
When I shifted my gaze to where she was pointing, I saw a startled man.
Huh, how did she see that?

The small gap would be tough to fit a human body into, but the man was hiding in the hole anyway, crouching like a shrimp. “Eek!” I thrust my hand inside and pulled the man out by his collar. He was quite tall, but because he was so skinny, it was like picking up a goblin. His behavior was not all that different from a goblin either. “Die!”
As he was yanked out, the man thrust the dagger he was holding at me. It was a good attempt. You gotta do what you gotta do to live, right?
“Ugh!” The fight promptly ended when I grabbed onto the wrist holding the dagger and bent it back.
“Why were you hiding there?”
The man quickly changed his tune at my question. “H-Have mercy! Please! I-I didn’t harm anyone, I just didn’t have any money!”
That wasn’t the answer I was looking for, but if I had to guess, he was probably saying that he couldn’t pay his taxes and ran. No one believed that, though.
“This reminds me of the old days!” said Hikurod. “Back in the day, when I was working at a blacksmith’s shop, thugs with tattoos like this often came to visit me. Hahaha!”

This man’s tattoos were different from the geometric pattern of a barbarian’s tattoo; his skin was covered in pictures of skulls, naked women, and monsters. Of course, I didn’t judge a person’s insides by their outsides.
“Bjorn, look at the mark on his forehead,” Brown pointed out. “He has to be a criminal who escaped into the sewers.”

The forehead marking hidden under his hood was evidence of a heinous crime that could not be forgiven even with a fine. There was no room for sympathy. Well, even if he really hadn’t paid his taxes, that wouldn’t have changed much.
“Bjorn, what will you do with him now?” asked Hikurod.
“I don’t know.”
“Shouldn’t the Administrative Office have given you some guidelines in advance?”

Well, they certainly did give me some advice. Their basic policy was to catch the criminals and bring them back, but as long as the video was properly filmed, there was no problem if I killed them and tossed them in the sewers.
“You can kill him? What if he’s just a normal person?”
“They said there’s no such thing as an ordinary person who comes into a place like this by accident,” I answered.
“Hahaha! That’s the heartless Administrative Office that I know!”
Well, in my opinion, they were just being considerate of the heartless adventurers. That wasn’t something to worry about now, though.
“So, what are you going to do?”

“For now, we’ll take him.” If I were alone, it would have been different, but because there were five of us, we had extra hands. Above all, bringing him back alive gave us an additional pay of five thousand stones.
“P-Please let me go just this once. You just have to pretend you never saw anything. I only ended up like this because I wanted to live—”

“Stop.” Long conversations were unnecessary. Whether he was a tax delinquent, a criminal, or had committed a crime out of necessity, so what? “I was commissioned, so I will take you. They will be the ones to make any judgments.”
“...Fuck! You fucking bastards! How are you any different from me?”
We’re very different. If we were the same, you wouldn’t be begging me like you are now.
“Dwalkie, shut his mouth.”
“A-All right.” Dwalkie used his newly learned Paralysis Poison spell to silence the man. His body went rigid. I carried the prisoner on my shoulders as if carrying a bag of rice.
An hour or so passed.
“Rotmiller, how much furrrther do we have to go?”
“We’re halfway there now.”

“Eh? We still have half left?” Missha sighed deeply, suggesting she regretted coming along. Then she opened her mouth like she was curious about something. “Dwalkie, why do you look so norrrmal? Last time we were in the labyrinth you were vomiting all over the place.”
“Haha, that? I learned a spell that makes someone lose their sense of smell. It turns out that it’s considered an essential bit of magic among wizards who have lived as adventurers.”
“Ohh, I see. But can’t you cast it on otherrr people too?”
“Uh... I-I don’t know how to change the formulas yet...” Dwalkie, who had been proudly explaining his new spells, trailed off.

I chuckled. It was not that he didn’t know how—he just couldn’t do it. “Changing the formula” was pretty much what kept the wizards of the Magic Tower fed. Although they taught basic spells in exchange for money, they never revealed how to convert the magic or create new types of spells.
As the effects of Paralysis Poison expired, my captive suddenly started screaming and writhing. “L-Let’s make a deal! If you let me go, I will give you information!”
I stopped Dwalkie from casting Paralysis Poison again. “Information?” I asked.
“That bitch!” the man hastily added. “If you catch that bitch, you’ll earn a lot more than from me!”
“Bjorn, what are you listening to him forrr? It is clear that he’s just doing whatever he can to survive.”
That was what I thought too, but one word stuck with me. “...Tell me more about the bitch.” It was worth a listen.

Negotiation: the act of persuading someone and discussing things to come to a decision. This was both a reasonable and irrational process. If the two parties weren’t on equal ground, someone would end up losing out in the end—just like this.
“...Before I tell you, I need a promise!”
“Dwalkie, just make him like he was before—”

“I-I’ll tell you!” Not wanting to waste this opportunity, the man started explaining his situation. “There are many other people living in this sewer besides me. Usually, it’s just hard to see them because they know the routes of the patrol officers so they can avoid them...”
“Shorter.”
“...Some bitch stole my hiding spot a few days ago.”

To sum up the man’s story, it went like this: he had been doing pretty well in the sewers when a woman came and took his home. And she was no ordinary woman. Although she looked small, he had no choice but to leave because she was leading a bunch of skeletons around with her.
Missha cocked her head. “Skeletons? Werrren’t they just people who took the essence of a Nekramia?”
But the man seemed convinced. “I don’t know exactly what they were. However! It was completely different from the skeletons in the labyrinth! I was once an adventurer too, so I’m confident!”
“So what is your verdict?”
“It has to be wicked black magic. If you hand her over to the temple, you will definitely receive compensation. Money that won’t even compare to what you’ll get from me!”
I thought this over for a moment. The timing was too coincidental to just dismiss. A woman who had been hiding in the sewers for a few days and used wicked black magic...
“Could it be that woman?”
“Elisa Behenk. No doubt she had no other choice but to hide here.”
Brown and Hikurod apparently thought the same thing. They gulped and each tossed in their two cents.
Damn, could it really be that bitch?
I needed to know more because there was not enough evidence to be sure. “What was she wearing? Describe it in detail.”
“She was wearing a robe and her face was covered with a hood, so I couldn’t see it clearly. I knew she was a woman from the lines of her body and her voice, but that’s all.”
“I see.”
“Oh! Now that I think of it, she was wearing a very unusual necklace...”
“What shape was it?”
“It’s hard to explain in words.”

I had an inkling as to what it was and quickly pulled an item out of my bag, the symbol of the church of Karui that I found while digging through Hans’s backpack the other day. “Was it something like this?”
“Yes! It was just like that!”
I let out a deep sigh as I stared at the nodding man. The possibility that it really was that bitch had increased dramatically.
“What arrre you going to do?”
“I’m thinking,” I told Missha.
“Hahaha, what are you thinking about?! We need to go catch her now and deliver justice!”
Justice my ass, you just want the reward money.

Anyway, if Hikurod was an extremist, Brown was on the moderate side. “I think it would be better to go back to the Administrative Office and file an official report. We’re not sure if it’s that woman yet, so why should we risk it?”

Both of their opinions were definitely valid. If we caught her ourselves, we would earn the reward money, but if we didn’t take the risk, filing the report would allow someone else to handle the matter.
Something doesn’t feel right.

If Elisa was the crazy bitch this guy was talking about, I felt especially uncomfortable with the idea of heading back like this. Elisa was not just a bitch—she was one with a grudge against me. Because of that, I was inwardly worried that she might be plotting something from the shadows.
Even if the administration office or the temple mobilized to send people over here, it would take several days.
And if she ran away in the meantime, I’d have to keep feeling this way. “I want to check it out, but what do you guys think?”
Missha immediately agreed. Dwalkie, who was neutral, likewise cast his vote according to the opinion of his best friend, the dwarf.
Brown was worried but followed the majority rule. “Since the four of you are in agreement, I will come along. But before that, how about finishing the patrol quest?”
“You are right. Let’s do that.”
Soon, we moved a little faster and finished patrolling the route set by the Administrative Office.
“Where is your hiding place? Lead me there,” I ordered the prisoner.
“Promise me that you’ll let me go.”
“If it’s the woman we’re looking for, or if I feel it’s worth it, I’ll let you go.”
“Okay, follow me.”
I stopped him. “Wait, wear this first.”
“Huh?”
I tied a rope around the man’s waist. He had a puzzled expression on his face. Then I grabbed the remaining rope like a dog’s leash since it would be annoying if he ran away.
“Okay, now that that’s done, take the lead.”
“...The route is not on the map, so follow me.”

Soon, the man began to find his way through the maze-like sewer. It was then that I realized how complicated the structure was. So far, we’d only been walking on the main path where the water from the gutters flowed, but if you squeezed through a narrow gap that looked like a wall, you found a new area. Then there was a fork in the middle and a hole in the ceiling you had to climb through.
There was one question on my mind at this point. “Why did you get caught hiding in a place like that?”
“...I’ve been wandering around looking for a new hideout. Then I heard you guys, so I had no choice but to hide in a hurry.”
I see. He had some bad luck too.
“We’re here.”

The man stopped at a hole with a diameter of about six feet. I didn’t know what this place was designed for, but it seemed that if you followed the path into the hole, you would find a large, open area.
“From now on, everyone, lower your voices,” I instructed.
“Haha, this is quite nerve-racking.”

Unlike Hikurod, who looked a little excited, or Missha, who looked a little scared, I wasn’t too worried. By coincidence, all five of us were in the sewers together. Everyone was much stronger than they were back then. So, if the woman hiding down there was Elisa Behenk...
“Hey, is there anywhere you can escape from in there?” I asked the prisoner.
“There are no entrances other than this hole.”
This time, I would be able to show her what justice was.

chapters.title: Chapter 81: Sewerage (2)
paragraphs: “Rotmiller, can you sense whoever is inside?” I asked.
“The smell of filth is too strong to tell who it is.”
“I see. Then I will go down first, so follow after me when I give the signal.”

The pit was about sixteen feet deep and reminiscent of a water tank. With the shield on my back, I quickly descended the creaking ladder. When I gave them the hand signal, the rest of the group followed suit.

“This is a bit creepy.” Once our line of sight was illuminated by the torch, a passage that we couldn’t see from above thanks to the angle became visible. “From now on, you take the lead,” I muttered quietly so as not to make a sound and placed the prisoner up front. Then, holding the rope, I proceeded down the passageway.
About a minute later, I saw bodies piled up like sacks of clothes.
Fuck...
The dozens of corpses were in the form of mummies, like Hanson, who had been drained of life. No wonder the smell of rot was especially bad here.
“U-Uh... what is...?” Considering the bewildered look on my guide’s face, it didn’t seem like this place was originally like this.

“Be quiet and keep moving.” Since he had stopped, I gave him a shove in the back and kept walking forward. However, I kept all my senses on high alert so that I could respond to anything that came our way immediately. Which was why I was able to react in time.
Clink.
There was a mechanical click right before a faint light began to leak through the pile of corpses, and an imposing voice echoed through the tunnel.
“Saveum, Bania, Hartia.”
I didn’t need to hear anything else. This was one of the trap-type skills possessed by the priests of Karui. Because of its unique sound effect, it was usually called “Sabaha” for short.
[You have entered the radius of Call of the Evil God.]
Fuck, was this a trap?

“Get back!” As I warned my teammates, I tugged on the rope with my hand and pulled the man toward me. The reason was simple. Sabaha was not a skill that could be blocked with physical resistance or a lithinum shield.
“Eh, huh?” The man I was holding in my hand in place of a shield made a stupid sound.
Right at that moment, hundreds of banshee-like ghosts poured out from the other side of the tunnel.

“Agh! Aaaah!” Seeing this, the prisoner screamed and began to struggle, but I did not loosen my grip and hid as much of myself behind the man as possible. I was glad this guy was tall. Otherwise, it would not have been possible for me to get out with the amount of damage I did.
[You have absorbed 102 ghosts. Dark Resistance is above the specified threshold. The effects are reduced by 30%. Dark Resistance has temporarily decreased your maximum HP by 29%.]
Life drained from my body like there was a hole somewhere that it was leaking from. My skin grew dry like that of a person who had not had water for several days.

Missha was the first to notice the changes in me. “B-Bjorn, are you all rrright?” She immediately ran toward me to look me over. I stopped her from trying to get me to immediately drink a potion and straightened up from my crouch. My muscles ached from holding myself so tensely.
Fuck, I almost died there.

Call of the Evil God was a trap-type skill that caused hundreds of souls to rush in a designated direction when activated. Its key feature was that the affected person’s Maximum HP decreased by the number of times their soul got hit. Naturally, if your maximum dropped to zero, you died instantly, just like the guy dangling in my grip here.
“Are you guys all right?” I asked.
“We’re okay thanks to you blocking the attack from the front. Anyway, that man... is he dead?”
I didn’t have to answer. It would have been incredibly impressive if he had somehow survived with nothing but bones and a hide left.

As soon as I set down the man I was holding tightly in my hand, I heard Hikurod faintly mutter, “...This may not be the best thing to say right now, but it was a good thing to place that guy at the front.”
Agreed, and I was not ashamed of that fact. We were merciless adventurers.
“What are you going to do? If there’s another one of those attacks, going any further will be too dangerous.”
After a moment’s consideration, I made a decision. “We’ll keep going.”

There were several material requirements for triggering Call of the Evil God, mostly human lifeforce. There were a lot of corpses around, but it still wasn’t hundreds, so this must have been a one-time activation.
Besides, if we don’t take care of her now, it’ll just cause trouble later.
I had nothing to back that up but a feeling.

Just as I was about to get moving, the dwarf handed me something. “It’s nothing important, but when I dug through his belongings, I found this.” It was the identity card of the man who had been turned into a mummy. I didn’t know why the fugitive had been carrying an ID, but... “You can submit it to the administrative office when you go to pick up the additional pay later...Wait, why does your face look like that?”
After checking the ID, I was stunned. Hans Marcom. He was a Hans too? Dang, now I was getting worried.

After walking about twenty steps, I came to the hiding place that Hans E had spoken of. It was better furnished than I had expected. There was a makeshift bed, a table with leftover bread and coffee on it, and even a candlestick hanging on the wall. Except...
“Hahaha, no one’s here.”
“Hmm, I think she either left this place altogether or is away for the time being.”
No other presence could be sensed inside. It wasn’t like there was any place to hide, either.

“Stay vigilant. She could be hiding.” I looked around and searched the area thoroughly, checking under the bed, under the table, and even the wall for any hiding places. I did a close investigation for about five minutes, but made no significant gains—at least until Dwalkie used his magic.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-8 supplemental spell Mana Detection.]
Mana Detection: an investigation-type spell that made apparent anything that contained additional mana. “How does it look?” I asked.
“It’s hard to say.”
“How so?”
“There is something faintly magical about the floor here... but it’s too faint. To the extent that I may even be mistaken.”

I checked the patch of the floor Dwalkie was pointing to. Since I was not a wizard, I didn’t see anything strange. There wasn’t even a slight flaw or anything. “Is there any way to use a spell here to learn more?”
“No. I can only guess, though, that this magic is hiding something underneath it.”
“I see.”
Upon receiving an answer to my single question, I immediately lifted my mace.
Seeing that, Hikurod asked, “What are you doing?”
“I’m slamming it down.”
“...Slamming it down?”
I didn’t answer this time. Well, if our magical means were exhausted, it was time to use physical means, like a barbarian.
Bam!
The moment my mace (which was double the price and size of the last one) hit the floor, the ground shook.
However, that was all.
“Bjorn, magical devices cannot be opened that way,” scolded Dwalkie, who was watching me, but I silently continued my macing.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Perhaps because it was made of steel, the mace was completely fine after being slammed into the ground. The floor was a little dented, of course, but there were no major changes there either.
“That’s enough,” said Hikurod. “Dwalkie already told you. This method...”
I removed my breastplate, shoes, and helmet, and even set down the backpack I was carrying. Everyone looked at me as if to say, “What’s he doing all of a sudden?”
[You have cast Giantization. Your Threat Level and Physical Attributes increase in proportion to your increase in size.]
As my body doubled in size, my strength increased accordingly. The dwarf continued to spit out unhelpful advice, though. “Even if you do that, without magic, it’s—”
Impossible? As an expert in this game and a currently active barbarian, I still found that hard to accept. If I couldn’t break something with force, it was simply because I lacked the power to do so.
Banggg!
Oh, except for ghosts, of course.
“Wow, so it is possible,” Missha gaped.
“Dwalkie, what happened? Didn’t you clearly say it’s not?”
“Uh, that’s... I’m not sure, either. How did he do that...?”

Dismissing everyone’s comments, I checked the floor. Now that I had hit it a couple of times, light was leaking out from cracks in the surface. On the third hit, I was surprised to find a staircase under the smashed-up hole. “Hidden stairs, in these sewers?”
The staircase was so long that even if you held the torch inside, you wouldn’t be able to see the end of it. It felt like a path to the underworld.

“We’re not going down there, right...?” Missha looked at me with reluctance. To be honest, I didn’t like it, either. This bunker was being used as a hiding place, so I figured this cavity would only be big enough to hide a body.
But what’s this, now?

Despite feeling like I’d gotten caught up in something troublesome, I was also a little curious. That was because the sewer itself was a no-go zone in the game. Of course, I had no intention of risking my life for curiosity.
“Bjorn, I can faintly pick up the woman’s scent coming from down there,” announced Brown.
“What?”
“It’s clear she passed through this place. And not too long ago, either.”

Fuck, what should I do? Should I just turn back here and let the authorities figure it out on their own? My worries intensified. Therefore, I asked for Brown’s opinion too. “Rotmiller, what do you think? Would it be better to retreat here?”

“...Just a brief look around should be fine. I can’t pick up the scent of anyone other than that woman down there.” That was a slightly surprising answer. Was that a little too conspicuous? Brown chuckled and added, “For some reason, I have a feeling that it won’t be too dangerous.”
Well, the Sixth Sense stat was backing him up. So, though he had no clear evidence, I heeded his words.
I mean, the hit rate is higher than I thought.

In fact, Brown very accurately sensed him when Hans E had been hiding. Hadn’t he also been reluctant to come to this hideout? If he had sensed the danger from the trap in advance, it made sense that he was the only one to oppose our decision to come despite a majority vote.
Sixth Sense, huh? That may be a better stat than I thought.
Soon I came to a decision. “Rotmiller, you take the lead from now on. If you feel like something is wrong, we’ll turn back right away.” Brown’s senses were quite reliable.
“Vice-captain, the door has been destroyed.”

The man frowned at his subordinate’s report. Thousands of years ago, before Rafdonia, an underground shelter had been created. It had been the castle of a mere lord and was built up to what it was today—the city of Noark. Most of the entrances to this place were guarded by members who were standing watch at all times.
“The door was destroyed? Could it be an attack from the royal family?”
“The probability of that has been determined to be low.”
“...Give me details.”

At the urging of the vice-captain, the subordinate hurriedly explained. “Upon inspection, it was a gate that had been forgotten after the Karui incident. I looked over the last scouting report, which stated that it was being used as a hiding place for a single vagrant.”

“Hmm.” The man rubbed his chin. It was an old habit of his that came out whenever he was troubled. “There is no reason for the royal family to bother us now, but... Still, it’s obviously an intruder, so we’ll need to check it out.”
“Yes sir. Which unit would you like to contact?”

“Is there any reason to send troops?” the vice-captain asked the woman next to him. She had been conversing with him until his subordinate came in to give him this report, talking about a barbarian she let go a while back who had apparently become a famous adventurer in the city. Unfortunately, the interesting conversation had been interrupted in the middle. “Amelia, if you went, you could quietly deal with whoever this is yourself. Will you go check it out for us?”
The rest of the story could be finished later.

chapters.title: Chapter 82: Sewerage (3)
paragraphs: I went down the stairs. Even with the torch and after activating a light sphere spell, we couldn’t see an end to the darkness. It was like walking through an abyss.
“Let’s speed up a little more.” Following Brown’s advice, we increased the speed with which we were descending the stairs. How long had it been?
“To think there was such a big place under the sewers.”
“Hahaha! Human beings alone wouldn’t be able to construct something like this. I don’t know why it was made, but it must have been made by my ancestors,” Hikurod laughed.
Finally, when we stepped on the last step, an open cavity appeared before us. The ceiling alone was over twenty feet high, so it felt unbelievably expansive for a basement.

“From here, there’s only one visible path.” Brown scanned our surroundings and then pointed to a specific place. There was a passage behind an untitled stone statue that had been weathered by time. “That woman’s scent also continues in that direction. If my predictions are correct, we will probably run into her soon.”

Nice. “I’ll take the lead from now on.” Since it was a straight passageway, I decided to tweak our formation. I stepped in front, and Brown followed behind me to help navigate. I sent Hikurod to the rear to prepare for any sudden surprises.
“Dwalkie, stay close to me,” called Missha.
“I-I will.”
Missha’s role was to protect the wizard and actively support both the rear and the front guards from the center.
“Let’s go, then.”
As we walked down the tunnel, we soon came to a fork in the road. I didn’t know the way, but that was no problem; we had Bloodhound Brown with us on our journey.
“She must have gone that way.” We took the path on the left, which had her scent.
But what was this now? “...There’s another fork in the road.” This time, we had a whopping five options. “Rotmiller?”
“Ah, it’s a little unclear. She must have gotten lost, because each route has her scent.”
“Does that mean we can no longer follow her trail?”
“That’s not it. Go that way. It has the strongest scent, so that must be the one she went down most recently.”
“I see.” Pathfinding and manhunts were not my domain, so I willingly followed the expert’s advice.
What the hell is this place?
Soon, a new fork in the road appeared. Slowly, I got a sense of what this place was like. I didn’t know what the hell it had been designed for, but it was a maze.
“Hikurod, you’re a dwarf. Do you know what the hell this place is forrr?”
“Hahaha! Assuming that all dwarves are well-versed in architecture is narrow-minded of you. So... Dwalkie, what do you think? You’re a wizard, after all.”
“Do you think all wizards are enlightened, wise beings? As for why people from the past deliberately created a space like this underground, I have no idea.”
Confusion spread amongst the team. Before it could get any more annoying, I cut them off. “Enough chatting. Whatever this place was for, all we have to do is catch that bitch and head back.”
“That’s trrrue, but...”
“If you’re really curious, you can ask the administrative office. That would give you more accurate information than anything we could guess.”
The three of them shut their mouths at my words. Why did I, as the barbarian, have to play the cop? The only one I could rely on was Brown. He was the only one who always quietly did his job.
“Bjorn, stop,” he said.
“What’s wrong?”

“The scent has suddenly gotten stronger. It’s not a scent trail, but...” Brown suddenly trailed off and sniffed the air again. The look in his eyes changed. “I’m sure of it. It’s coming from over there.” Brown pointed to the second fork on the left.
To think she would come to greet us herself. It was a bit sudden, but I ran through the important things first. “ETA?”
“I’m not sure because I can’t tell how fast she’s moving.”
“Even just an estimate.”
“...I would say about two minutes.”
“Has she already noticed us?”
“I don’t think so. This is just a guess, but... I think she may be lost for whatever reason.”

Hmm, that was definitely a plausible assumption. I made a plan on behalf of Hikurod, who only seemed capable of widening his eyes during this entire conversation. “Everyone, prepare to fight. We’ll hide and then attack when she arrives.”
First, we hid ourselves at the crossroads nearby. Brown began loading his crossbow and Dwalkie prepared to cast a surprise attack spell. Just as we finished up, we heard footsteps in the distance.
Trudge, trudge.
The sound was getting closer, but at some point, it stopped.
Step.
What happened?
Just as I was patting Brown on the shoulder and asking him this question with my eyes, the sound of urgent footsteps echoed through the tunnel.
“Bjorn!” Missha whisper-yelled, and I closed my eyes.
I was disoriented because the echo was so loud, but when I focused my hearing, I could tell. She wasn’t running toward us. “She’s running away.”
“It seems she noticed us hiding,” Brown said urgently.
I agreed as well. What other reason could she have for making a sudden U-turn and sprinting away after walking normally up to now?
“What are you going to do?” Brown asked.
“Are you getting a bad feeling?”
“I’m not sure.”

In that case... “What are you doing, then? Take the lead.” In the Witch’s Forest, we had been the ones being chased, but the tables had turned. “We need to catch her and kill her before she gets any further away.”
Karui—a being called an evil god, or even a dark god. He was as rational as he was unpredictable. Blind faith in him always came with a reward.
“I offer this blood, flesh, and soul—please show me the way!”

It was all thanks to the god’s divine nature that Elisa had been able to survive in the Witch’s Forest. After offering up the three adventurers she ran into by chance in the Witch’s Hut as sacrifices, she received the advice that burning the corpses would increase her rest time, and learned a new ability called Deadify. When she used it, she couldn’t be attacked by any monster, and it even granted immunity from the field effects in the Witch’s Forest.
“Oh! That woman is—!”
“What are you all doing? Hurry, run!”

That was why, when she came across Hikurod’s group in the forest again, she was able to pursue them relentlessly. Without the field effects, the Witch’s Forest was just a forest. Unfortunately, the chase ended in failure. When her targets advanced to the fourth floor, she quickly followed them, but the color of the portal had changed a moment later and she ended up being sent to a different location.
For ten days, she had dealt with the monsters in front of the portal using Deadify. Then she returned to the city.
“Priestess Behenk, where are you going with all that luggage?”

She immediately grabbed everything she needed and ran. She had seen the fate of apostates many times before. Now the city was a more dangerous place for her than the labyrinth. But even when the sky fell down, there were always ways to survive.
Of course, there was also advice from a capricious, evil god and a sewer full of filth and vile fugitives. And the city that lay below it would accept her.
“What the hell! That’s my spot! Get lost!”
With the evil god’s guidance, finding the door hidden in the sewer was not difficult. The vagrant who had settled there first also wasn’t a big problem.
“Offer a sacrifice.”

The capricious, evil god didn’t even tell her how to open the door. Therefore, she wandered around the sewers, collecting and offering dozens of sacrifices. In return, she learned how to open the door and went downstairs.
What the hell is this?!
However, the paths were much too complex. She wandered for hours in the dark. The temperamental, evil god had no intention of showing her the way until another sacrifice was made.

At the same time, the Call of the Evil God spell that she had set just in case using the remaining life force from the sacrifices had been triggered. She began to feel a strange sense of unease. It could be a tracker sent by the temple. She wandered through the maze, examining her surroundings a little more carefully.
“Kehehehe!”
Suddenly, the evil god started laughing. Getting a foreboding feeling, she stopped walking. In situations like this, danger and hardship usually lay on the road ahead.
Is it a pursuer?

She paused for a moment, focusing her hearing. She could hear faint breathing in the silence coming from the other side of the path she was heading down. As soon as she detected this, she ran in the opposite direction. Which probably wasn’t a bad idea because soon after, she heard the sound of someone pursuing her.
“What are you doing, then? Take the lead. We need to catch her and kill her before she gets any further away.” Short, clipped words, a voice that was somehow familiar...
“Bjorn! Be carrreful! That wicked bitch might have laid a trap!”
She soon realized who these people were: Bjorn Yandel, that thoughtless barbarian who attacked her with a mace even after she revealed that she was a priest, and his party members.
It isn’t a tracker from the temple?
Upon learning their identities, she subconsciously slowed down. She didn’t know how they found out she was here and followed her this far.
But this is a good thing.
Soon, she stopped walking. Last time, she had been defeated and was forced to run, but that was after she had already used up a lot of energy resurrecting herself.
[Elisa Behenk has summoned the Demon’s Mirror Gate.]
If both sides were in perfect condition, there was no way she would lose.
Just as the distance between us was starting to narrow, the sound of footsteps sprinting through the darkness stopped.
Dash!
A strange sound echoed through the passageway and rapidly grew closer.
“Kyaaah!”
“Kekekekekeke!”
Suddenly, whatever was making the sound entered the torch’s radius, and dozens of four-legged monsters appeared.
It’s Gate of the Dead.
Honestly, I was amazed. This was definitely different from back when she couldn’t use her powers after resurrecting.
[Elisa Behenk has summoned a Shadow Guard.]

You could almost describe it as a difference in sheer quantity. In addition to Gate of the Dead, which spat out monsters for a few minutes, she summoned Shadow Guards at random, and the momentum was truly like a tsunami. But...
“What are you doing? Go destroy her.” There was no reason to be afraid. This changed nothing.
Elisa laughed. “Hahaha! Barbarian! It was a pity to leave you behind, but to think you’d come crawling to me willingly! I won’t let you escape this time!”
Escape, my ass. I’m the one who should be saying that.
“This time, I’ll bash your head in!”
The battle promptly began following an exchange of objectives. This was different from our last fight, which had to be fought over a few hours.
Slice!
Her shadow guards had a fairly high level of physical resistance. But every time Missha swung her dual swords at them like a maniac, they were cut down helplessly. “...Was this always this easy?”
That was because she now had the bonus of an ice attribute. Moreover, the curses that had been plaguing her back in the forest no longer applied.
[Elisa Behenk has cast Low-Rank Decay.]
[Elisa Behenk has cast Decreased Strength.]
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-7 support spell Brilliance. All evil-attribute effects bestowed on party members are removed.]
Thanks to hitting the jackpot last time and following my orders to learn a curse removal spell, Dwalkie had come back with the wide-range purification spell Brilliance. “Haha, what do you think?”
“It’s great.” I tossed a compliment at the now hoity-toity Dwalkie. For some reason, it seemed he had taken what I said the other day personally.
Anyway, I gradually joined the battle. It would be enough for one person to just build a shield wall and protect the frontlines, but that wasn’t efficient.
“Behelahhh!” With a cry to my ancestral god, I could actually feel the energy flowing through me.
[You have used Wild Outburst. Your threat level is increased by times 3, and your Physical Attributes increase in proportion to that value.]
The passage was narrow and it was impossible to follow Wild Outburst up with Giantization, but this effect was sufficient.
“Grrr.” The summoned beasts sensed a threat and started recklessly rushing toward me.
This is like playing some kind of hack-and-slash game.
As if to vent my past frustration, I swung the enlarged mace like crazy.
Smack! Smack! Punch!

Guards exploded with every swing despite their physical resistance. A strange sense of pleasure arose in me as I suddenly remembered the good old days of fighting against just a few goblins. Yes, this feeling was the reason that I played RPGs.
Stab!
“Aaagh!”
While aggro was focused on me and the guards were dispersed, Brown released a crossbow bolt and Hikurod made a temporary opening by using his Lightning Discharge combo. I rushed through the gap.
“Bjorn, it’s dangerous to go alone—”
“Behelaaah!”
Despite the summoned beasts blocking the passageway, I quickly narrowed the distance. Finally, I was able to see that bitch Elisa’s face properly.
“Th-this is not possible...” She looked like she was witnessing something unbelievable unfold. Why, never imagined such a one-sided defeat?
“Dwalkie, now!” I shouted.
“Now?” Dwalkie asked back in confusion.
I was a barbarian who didn’t repeat the mistakes of the past, you see. “Hurry!”
“A-All right!”

While Missha and Hikurod came to my side to help support me, I continued to plow forward. One hundred feet, fifty, thirty—the distance quickly grew shorter. I leaped forward at Elisa the bitch as I was sliding, but the moment I reached out to grab her, Elisa’s body turned translucent and began to float into the air.
[Elisa Behenk has cast Spiritization.]
This was an advanced movement spell that granted physical immunity bonuses.
“You bastards! I will never forget this shame!”
Never forget what, exactly? If you think we’re the same as we were back when we could only watch helplessly as you escaped, you’re mistaken.
“Dwalkie!”
As soon as I called behind me, I heard, “It’s ready!” The prepared spell was completed and fired, a spell Dwalkie had paid a whopping 1.3 million stones to learn from the Magic Tower.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-8 curse spell Materialization.]

When it hit, Materialization nulled the enemy’s physical immunities. In other words, it made it so that even an unarmed warrior was able to beat up a spirit-type monster. Of course, if it missed, it was useless.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-8 support spell Accuracy Support.]
But our Dwalkie was slowly coming out of his half-wit wizard phase.
“Uh—ah! Kyaaa!”

At the exact moment Spiritization deactivated, a sensation flooded my outstretched fingertips. It was similar to the first time I fought a goblin. It didn’t matter if it was the wrist, the ankle, or the neck; I just grabbed the collar or whatever I could as tightly as possible and slammed her down to the ground with full force.
Bam!
I immediately climbed on top of her upper body. It seemed the damage had knocked her into a dazed state, shaking and furious.

“Ugh! Uh, ah, ugh, mm...!” It appeared that she was shouting some cusses, but I guessed she still hadn’t fixed those vocal cords of hers. Of course, I did not intend to lower my guard just because my opponent was now incapacitated. This was the same person who had risen up from the ground like a zombie even after her skull was bashed in.
Slide.
Immediately, I lifted the mace, but just when I was about to slam it down with all my might, Dwalkie hurriedly stopped me.
“W-Wait! If you want a bigger reward, wouldn’t it be better to take her alive?”
Hmm, the wanted posters definitely did say that, but I didn’t think this kid would worry about something like that. Was it a result of having gotten a taste for money? He was a real adventurer now.
“True, it would be a waste to kill her.” I got up from on top of Elisa. Then I made Dwalkie cast a Paralysis Poison spell and, without any hard feelings, struck Elisa’s arms and legs with the mace.
Punch! Punch! Punch!
I neatly crushed her bones and flesh.
“...Is that necessary?” Hikurod frowned.

“She might run away.” In this respect, my general philosophy was that it was better to do too much rather than not enough. So, after tying the crippled Elisa down with a rope, I carried her on my shoulders like luggage.
“We’re really strrrong now. I didn’t think we’d beat her so easily...” Missha muttered after taking care of the last few summoned beasts.

I agreed. The battle had taken less than three minutes from start to finish. Having fought this enemy in the relatively recent past, we got a good sense of how much we had grown. However, we could praise and say thanks to each other later at the bar.
“Rotmiller, take the lead,” I said, patting Brown on the shoulder. I had achieved all of my objectives. It was time to leave this spooky underground area.
Hmm? But what the hell is this? Why isn’t he moving?

I called out to Brown again. “...Rotmiller?” Again, there was no answer. It was only then that I realized something was wrong and hurriedly checked on the other members of my party. “Missha? Dwalkie? Hikurod?”
None of them answered. I wished they would say “Surprise!” or that it was just a joke, but I was sure that wouldn’t be happening.
The sudden silence around me was suffocating. “We’re fucked,” I muttered quietly.
No wonder things had been going so smoothly up until now.

chapters.title: Chapter 83: Sewerage (4)
paragraphs: I didn’t know exactly when it had happened, but by the time I realized it, everyone was already frozen with their eyes open like stone statues. “Missha? Dwalkie? Hikurod?”
What’s going on?
Just as I was beginning to question this, something I had overlooked before came to my attention. Very long, thin needles were sticking out from each of my comrades’ necks.
I probably have one in my neck as well.
The important thing here was that my neck muscles were stiff and that tingling sensation was spreading downward.
[You have been poisoned by Basilisk’s Paralysis Poison. Your Physique stat is higher than 300. The poison’s effect is reduced by half.]
Processing the threat, my heart pounded like crazy. My brain, on the other hand, calmly issued orders, telling me what it was that I had to do right now.
Slide.

My thick arms lifted the shield and covered my upper body. My legs were slightly bent, lowering my center of gravity so that I could react at any time. The stillness squeezed my throat. I avoided even breathing to concentrate on the sounds around me.
Drip. Drip. Drip.

I heard dripping water in the distance. That was it, but I didn’t have any doubts. Just like when I had stepped on that goblin trap, the enemy had to be nearby. A tremulous silence followed for a few seconds. It felt like every nerve in my body was on edge.
Tap.
Then, I heard a faint sound. It was hard to call it a footstep... It was more like a pebble rolling in the wind.
...Is that a stealth skill?
I quickly made a decision. I didn’t know what that was, but the poison was slowly spreading through my body. So it would be better to see the end of this battle before it finished.
[You have used Wild Outburst.]
That would make survival a little more likely.
“Behelahhh!” I shouted with all my might. Of course, unlike monsters, the Threat Level stat did not always work on humans, but I had looked into this before.
“Ummm... i-it was a very strange feeling. It was like my mind knew that there was nothing dangerous, but my body was telling me that I should run...” Dwalkie had told me.
When exposed to Wild Outburst, those with weak willpower felt fear. Therefore, those opponents might run away before I could even properly provoke them.
“Forrr some reason, I felt like I had to get rid of you quickly. Oh, of course, that was before you turned big. After that, I felt similar to Dwalkie.”
Conversely, if the target was more aggressive, some degree of provocation was possible. So, what about my mysterious enemy who was hiding in the dark?
“This is a strange situation, Barbarian.”
I knew it. I should have been the one saying it was strange, though. I wasn’t sure what she was doing, but I could somehow hear her voice both from in front of me and behind me.
Wait, that voice sounds familiar...
I flinched. Aside from the issue of not knowing where the enemy was, the voice I had just heard was that of a woman. It was a little husky, but that much was certain.
Who could it be?
My inquisitive brain combined several keywords: a woman who hid like an assassin and shot paralyzing needles. I remembered. “It’s you.” The bitch we met in the Land of the Dead. It had to be her.
She was possibly uninterested in hiding her identity. “...I didn’t think you’d be able to tell who I was just by my voice.”

Soon, she appeared in front of me. A slender body a little over 5′5″, flaming red hair, and a half-missing right ear; everything was the same as back then, except that the clothes she was wearing were casual.
Step.

The woman took a step forward and narrowed the distance between us. To be honest, I was sweating profusely. Recently, I had grown exponentially and even earned the nickname of Little Balkan, but still, I was nothing in front of this bitch.
“You’ve gotten strong, Barbarian. To think you can still move after being hit with that.”
An adventurer who is active on the eighth floor and even knows how to use aura...

No matter how I thought about it, I couldn’t do anything on my own. But that didn’t mean I was going to go down without a fight. Putting strength into the hand holding my shield and mace, I refocused my frightened mind.
The woman watched me do this. “Is it because of your comrades that you are not running away?” she asked.

Of course, she was a disturbed bitch. The fact that she had to ask that sent shivers down my spine. “I’ll ask the questions first. I kept my promise. Why have you come to kill me?” I asked, gulping. I was curious about her motives. If I knew what they were, I might be able to come up with another way out of this.
“Kill you?” She furrowed her eyebrows and cocked her head. “It was you who opened the door and broke in, Barbarian.”
“...Door?”
“Tell me. Who told you about this place?”
What the hell is she talking about?
For some reason, this conversation was one-sided. “I don’t understand, so speak clearly. Break in? What is this place?” I asked bluntly.
The woman frowned again. She seemed to have realized that there was something majorly wrong with this interaction. “...How did you open the door?”
“If you’re talking about the magical thing in the sewer, I bashed it in with a mace.”
“You...broke it?”
“Is there a problem?”

The woman closed her eyes for a moment at my confident question, then shook her head as she got it. “No, there isn’t.” As a top-level adventurer, she didn’t seem to believe in magic blindly like Dwalkie or Hikurod. But, still curious, she asked, “But why did you break it?”
“Because this bitch escaped through there.”

At that moment, I took the opportunity to lower Elisa to the floor. Actually, she had been annoying me for a while. There didn’t seem to be any signs of one happening now, but she was sure to get in my way if a battle broke out.
“...That’s the priestess of Karui who was wanted a while back.”
“I’m glad you know about that. So are we on the same page now?” I asked.
“Sure.”
“Good. It was nice seeing you. We’ll be leaving now. Ah, no need to give us any potions. I’ll take care of the rest—”
“Stop. Now that you know about this place, I can’t just let you go.”
“...Even if I destroy the video recorder and swear to keep everything that happened today a secret?”
“The situation is different from back then.”
Fuck... so that’s a no-go, huh?
I rid my mind of all weaknesses. Having heard an affirmative answer from the bitch’s own mouth, I had only one option left. Therefore, I took off the armor I was wearing.
Click.
“...Why are you doing that all of a sudden?”
Ignoring her question, I took off my gaiters, helmet, and shoes and tossed them aside. “Hey,” I said.
Fortunately, the other party decided to humor the conversation. Her eyes were saying, If you have something to say, say it.
I quickly continued. “Do you know the top two ways to make someone angry?”
“...What?”
“The first is to stop talking in the middle of a sentence. And the other is...”
I didn’t know, either. No one told me the rest.
“Behelahhh!” I dashed forward with all my might, hoping that had diverted the bitch’s attention even a little bit. I pulled back the arm holding the mace.
The woman, who was startled for a moment, smiled like she’d caught onto my trick. “How funny.”
After all, running at you from this distance wouldn’t be startling for you. But what about this?
Voom!
I swung my arm forward and threw the mace.
Whip!

As expected, she avoided that too. She turned her body sharply to dodge the mace and gave me a questioning look. It seemed she hadn’t expected a barbarian to throw a weapon at the very start of a fight. I threw the shield in my other hand without any regrets.
Whip!

The shield spun in mid-air and flew like a disk, making all of my practice worthwhile. Its speed was unrivaled by that of a mace. However, that needlessly flexible bitch easily dodged the shield by bending backward. This wasn’t disappointing though, because I had expected it.
Dash!

Using the opening created by the mace and shield, I sprung off the ground once more and continued to sprint. The distance narrowed in an instant as my physique stat now surpassed that of ordinary people.
Now.
I reached my hand out like I had when sliding toward Elisa. The bitch’s expression was still relaxed, as if to say, This punk?
Dash!
To prove that, she avoided the attack by taking exactly three steps backward. I had reached out my hand so that she could clearly see it in the first place.
Just like I thought.

We were in a straight passageway that could not exactly be called wide. If a large barbarian ran at you from the front, the only place you could escape was backward. Of course, if my opponent actually managed to move way further back, I couldn’t do anything about that. Even then, she would only move just enough to avoid the attack. Rather than an issue of personality, this must be a symptom of being an efficiency freak, one that had naturally developed as a result of always seeking higher ground.
I guess I can proceed with Plan A.

And so, I cast Giantization at the exact right time. It was a connecting move inspired by my dramatic survival against Riakis. My body grew and my arms lengthened accordingly. The distance that should have been three steps longer immediately shrunk.
For the first time, I saw a little bit of surprise on her face. I hadn’t even started yet. I immediately grabbed her shoulders and pulled her toward me, feeling significant resistance.

“You...” It was different from our last meeting when I had been pushed back by brute strength. That was because back then I had been a novice barbarian at level one who had no essences. “...need to build up some strength.”

With the power of a Corpse Golem, a vampire, and an Orc Hero, I dragged my helpless opponent toward me. Gripping her tightly by the neck so that she couldn’t escape, I landed a punch right to her face.
Smack!
Both the sound and blow were powerful. But once again, a one-hit KO proved impossible.
One more time.
I quickly recovered and slammed my fist down again. Right at that moment, I sensed movement in my keen peripheral vision. She had come to her senses and was wielding her dagger.
Is she planning to cut off my whole wrist?

I quickly made a decision. The bitch was an aura user. Therefore, neither physical resistance, bone strength, nor mana resistance really mattered against her. That dagger would definitely cut off my arm before I could touch her.
I’m going to move on to Plan B.

I stopped my outstretched fist. I wasn’t thinking of my safety last minute. I had just deemed it unreasonable to suffer one-sided damage. I wasn’t afraid of getting hurt if that was what I needed to do to live.
Flesh Burst.
The moment I finished thinking the words in my head, a strong explosion erupted from the hand that was holding my opponent, one of bursting flesh and acid blood.
Pop! Chhh!
The stubborn bitch just frowned, not moaning in pain even once. But it seemed she might not have Pain Resistance; she may have taken the pain, but for a brief moment, her movements grew stiff.
Okay, then Plan A again.
Dodging the dagger that she swung, I landed a fist in her abdomen. Knowing that this was an opportunity that would never come again, I kept going.
Smack! Punch! Punch!

Like any damage dealer with a scrawny body, the results of my efforts appeared on her soon after. Blood leaked out of her mouth as if her intestines had been chewed up. At the sight, an immense feeling of exhilaration rushed through my head and I could even feel pressure in my eyes. Fuck, the only thing that could beat this bitch was—
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Self-Replication.]
Just when my brain sensed hope, instinct sounded the alarm and sent me a warning. The reason for this was simple.
“...Barbarian.”
Why was I hearing a voice from behind me? She was clearly in my grip right in front of me.
Sprint!
Sensing the presence of another person, I subconsciously stopped my punching and looked back. A woman who looked exactly the same as the one I was holding was running toward me.
Fuck.

I didn’t even wonder how something like this could happen. Self-Replication was a super rare power that could only be obtained from the essence of the Guardian of the fourth-floor Rift, Doppelganger Forest.
“Since you have the essence of a vampire, this much should be fine,” the woman in my grip murmured.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Asura’s Kick.]
Amelia’s clone took a big leap forward, spun in mid-air, and kicked me in the face.
Bam!
