The impact felt like my head was getting blown off. Wait, did it actually blow it off?
Tap.
The sound of a heavy thud filled my ears. My vision darkened. My consciousness faded like a cell phone that was out of battery.
“Fuck...”
[Due to the passive skill Source of Darkness, you will not die until your heart is destroyed. Your regeneration speed is greatly increased by the Eternal Life effect.]

chapters.title: Chapter 84: Sewerage (5)
paragraphs: Thud.
As soon as the barbarian fell, scattering dust in the air, Amelia clenched her teeth and doubled over.
Is this the price of my carelessness?
Her ribs were broken. Her skin, covered in blood, was beyond hurt and just painful. It seemed her organs had also been damaged in some way.
I don’t even know how long it’s been since I’ve been in a situation like this.

Her body would recover on its own soon enough, but the pain she had long forgotten was all too vivid at the moment. If there was anything she was used to, she had prided herself on the fact that it was pain. She didn’t know why the thought made her laugh. Regardless of this being the result of her arrogance, it was absurd to think that a three-month-old barbarian had been the one to put her in this situation.
He’s a fascinating one.
She wasn’t just thinking about his abilities, but his skill at reading situations, the boldness and determination he had to put his plans into action, and above all, his will to live.
She had a sudden thought. If we met again a little later down the line... the results may have been different.
Of course, in reality, that wasn’t plausible. She had grown up being told she had the most special talent there was, and she had been in and out of the labyrinth for twenty years.
The fact that I’ve begun to think like that is a problem. That shows how dangerous he is.

Their first meeting had only been a month ago. In that time, he would have been able to enter the labyrinth only once. How had this barbarian transformed like this? The man who hadn’t even been able to touch her before had managed to make this much progress since then.
Czzzzzz!
His body didn’t die even after the head was completely blown off, and his flesh began to restore itself. Amelia slowly walked toward him.
Like Source of Darkness, there were several abilities whose effects allowed the user to overcome death, but that still didn’t make a person invincible. Just look at this barbarian.

His head was completely destroyed and he was now defenseless. He may have activated Eternal Life and been recovering quickly, but it took a tremendous amount of time to recover from an injury like this, and even that became impossible when Soul Power ran out. That meant she could kill him at any moment. But, without any hesitation, she put away her dagger and pulled out a potion.
It’s clear that they haven’t been sent by the royal family, so there’s no need to kill them.
No matter what anyone said, she was not a ruthless killer.

There had been hints—voices coming from the front and back at the same time. If I had been smarter and calmer, I might have noticed the use of Self-Replication. If I had, Plans A and B would have been slightly altered too.
Well, even still, the result would have been the same.
Feeling a strange sensation akin to a fragmented mind being stitched back together, I slowly opened my eyes.
“What a monstrous healing factor you have.” The first thing I saw was that bitch. “One bottle of potion, and you’re as good as new.”

“Potion...?” I asked, voice cracking, and lifted my upper body. It was only then that I noticed my neck was very wet. It didn’t all look like blood... Could it be that this woman poured a potion on me? “Why...”
“Why did I not kill you?”
I nodded. Well, I was glad I was still alive, but to be honest, I had been sure death was coming the moment I lost consciousness.
The woman studied me with an annoyed look in her eyes. “You...are still exactly the same as back then.”
“What?”
“Why do you always charge at me whenever you see me? I never thought I’d say this, but don’t people usually think to talk things over first?”

Well, I had nothing to say to that. That was all thanks to my habit of always assuming the worst. “As long as you were planning on killing me, I thought that was the only way,” I answered calmly. While there was still the slightest chance before the paralysis poison spread even further, I decided I had to see the end of this battle.
The woman just let out a sharp sigh. “Why? I let you go last time, didn’t I?” Her voice was still blunt but at the same time the tiniest bit upset.

But it was really me who should be upset. “You said so yourself: as long as I know about this place, you can’t let me go.” If she hadn’t said that, Plan C, which had been begging for my life, would’ve remained Plan A instead.
Do you think I want to fight a monster like you?
“I believe I said I can’t ‘just’ let you go.”
To-may-to, to-mah-to. For some reason, she had been weirdly patient with me so far, so I decided to get bolder. “So, what are you going to do with me now?” I asked.
“I have no intention of killing you. So stop moving those hands of yours.”
I stopped moving the arm that was sneakily sliding toward the mace and announced, “This is a misunderstanding.”
“Misunderstanding?”
“I didn’t mean to surprise attack you with this. It’s just—”
“You wanted to be prepared for when I change my mind?”
...Hmm, yeah, that. The best defense was a good offense.

When I neither confirmed nor denied this, the woman stared blankly at me as if to ask what kind of lunatic I was. “You really haven’t changed at all,” Amelia said, then spat on the floor. For a moment, I wondered if she was a thug, but when I looked closely, it was blood, not saliva. It seemed that the active defense I had launched before falling unconscious did do some damage.
“...Did you not take a potion?”
“It’s because of my body type.”
“I see.” That brief explanation was not enough, but I held my tongue. Some essences inflicted a penalty when mixed with potions.
Anyway, back to the main point of the story. “Barbarian, take this.” She pulled out something like a magic pellet from her clothes. It was dark-colored and looked like something a cat would throw up.
“What... is this?”
“It’s a medicine made by an alchemist in Noark. If you take it, it will erase your memory of the last hour.”
“Erase... my memory? Then why didn’t you give me this when we met in the Land of the Dead?”
“It’s not something that can easily be obtained. If they hadn’t given this to me just in case, I wouldn’t have it on me, either.”

So it was a rare item. But that led to another question. This wasn’t something someone in my situation should be saying right now, but... “It would be much easier for you to just kill me. Why would you willingly choose such a troublesome method?”

They say there is nothing more precious than human life, but that only applied in my home world. Here, there were countless things more valuable than human life. For example, aboveground, many people still lost their lives just because they could not pay their taxes.
But despite all that, she’ll use a rare consumable like this just to keep us alive?
“There must be some reason,” I said confidently.
“...What makes you think that?”
“If you killed the five of us, our equipment alone would be worth tens of millions of stones.”

At my astute observation, Amelia remained silent for a while. I thought it was because I had hit the nail on the head. However, the words that followed the silence were unexpected. “What exactly do you think of me?”
“That’s...”

As I was contemplating whether or not I should answer honestly, she cut me off. “You don’t have to say it. I think I know already.” It looked like she felt a little guilty about that too, but I guess she didn’t want to make any excuses. “Whatever. Whatever it is, think however you want. It changes nothing.”
Amelia bent over and forcibly opened my mouth, then shoved the pellet down my throat.
The medicine quickly dissolved, leaving nothing to even throw up later.
Whoosh!
It felt like something was burning in my mind. It was a different kind of sensation from pain. “...Hey, are you sure this just erases memories?”

“If it doesn’t, do you have any other options anyway?” I didn’t really have much to say about that. Noticing my silence, she smirked. “I haven’t heard of any side effects. So rest assured, Barbarian.”
Well, in that case... To be honest, I was not relieved at all, but I closed my eyes.
Just then, Amelia opened her mouth like she’d remembered something. “Oh, so what was the other thing?”
“Huh? Other thing?”
“The two ways to make someone angry.”
Oh, that. “It’s...”
I blacked out right after that.
[Lethe’s blessing permeated your soul.]
[Your soul cannot be blessed. The blessing permeating your soul has been removed.]
When I woke up, I was in the sewers. My stripped equipment was scattered all around, and it was the same for the others.
Thud.
Using my hands as support, I slowly raised my filthy body from the floor. As I was getting my gear back on, my teammates came to their senses one by one. They all looked confused.
“Uh, is this the sewer...?”
“W-What is this? We should be chasing after that evil villainess right now!”
“Video recorder! If we check the video recorder... Damn it, it’s broken!”
The bitch’s words must have been true because the others didn’t remember a thing. It seemed like their last memory was of following Hans E to his hideout.
...Why am I completely fine?
Even though my memory recall was a little slow right now, I could clearly remember what had happened before I lost consciousness. Why?
Wait, so what happened to that bitch?
Belatedly, Elisa came to mind, and I came back to my senses.
...Could it be that Amelia revived her and took her back with her?
Right now, at least, I didn’t see Elisa anywhere. Damn, if I had known this was going to happen, I would’ve just killed her back then.
“Everyone, look over there!”
“Huh? Isn’t that that woman?”
What? I immediately turned my head to see a woman lying a short distance away. Blonde hair covered in filth, a cute head that made me want to smash it in... It had to be Elisa.
Hikurod rushed to check her pulse. “Sh-she’s dead!” This added to the confusion.
“W-We’ve been cursed. Why is it that we can’t remember a thing, and that woman is dead?”
“D-Dwalkie, maybe the monster you talked about rrreally appeared!”
They made all sorts of speculations in bewildered tones. But Brown, who had managed to maintain his composure, came up with a plausible hypothesis. “...I think it was all this woman’s doing.”
“What? Elisa?”

“Maybe we found her after chasing her down, and we probably won.” Brown pointed to Elisa’s limbs as a basis for his claim. He probably thought nothing but my mace could possibly have crushed her arms and legs so precisely.
Soon, Dwalkie also noticed traces of Paralysis Poison on the corpse and solidified this hypothesis. “C-Come to think of it, I can sense traces of my magic coming from this woman.”
Now, one question remained for them. “Then why can’t we rrremember anything?”
“If my theory is correct, we would have tried to take her back to the city alive. However... perhaps she came to her senses and played a trick on us.”
This was quite a compelling theory. If I had lost my memory too, I probably would’ve analyzed the situation the same way.
“Definitely... it might be possible with a little-known ability from an evil god.”
“Hahaha! But considering she’s dead, it seems like we did a good job!”
“...Bjorrrn, what do you think?”

“Well...” I thought it over for a while. The conclusion they had come to and agreed upon was quite far off from the truth I remembered, but there was no need to tell them that. “I think Rotmiller is right.” If it became known that I hadn’t lost my memory, there was no telling when that bitch would pay me another visit.
“Let’s get out of here and visit the temple. Something might have happened to our bodies besides the memory loss.”

At Brown’s concerned suggestion, everyone quickly prepared to leave. I quit my pondering. Something hidden beneath the sewers, huh? A secret part of this world that I didn’t know about. I’d be lying if I said my curiosity wasn’t stirring as a long-time player of this game, but...
Let’s never set foot in the sewers again.
My life was more important than curiosity.

chapters.title: Chapter 85: Baron Martoin (1)
paragraphs: When I got out of the sewer, I was greeted by a dark sky and two familiar faces.
“Mr. Yandel! You’re safe!”
“Shavin? Why are you here?”
“What do you mean? I came because you disappeared without a word for hours! I was worried!”

Hmm, I see. I was kind of grateful that she came personally. “But, the two of you?” If something really had happened to us, wouldn’t it have made more sense to send another adventurer in the morning? Not organize a party of an administrative officer and a librarian.
“What? What’s that look? Ragna is a very talented wizard, thank you very much!”

It was only then that I looked at the librarian. She definitely looked different than she usually did at the library. “Hmm.” She wore shining robes, had numerous scrolls and potions hanging from her belt, and had an expensive-looking wand in her hand. I didn’t know how skilled she was, but this was definitely not equipment that an ordinary librarian could afford with their salary. Maybe she came from a rich family?
“Bjorn, who arrre these people?”
“Shavin Emoor, the administrative employee who entrusted this request to me. And this is... Ragna Litanel Peprok.”
“It’s Litaniel, not Litanel!”
“Anyway, she’s the librarian at my library.”
“Ohh, I see,” Missha said with a nod.
After giving a brief introduction to everyone else, I offered some cursory words to the librarian. “I’m sorry for making you come all the way here at night.”
“No need to apologize.”
“Then, thanks. I never thought you’d come.”
“...You should thank Shavin. I was just forced into it.” After that, the librarian whipped her head around. Why did she seem colder than usual?
I was wondering if I was just being sensitive when Shavin grinned and glued herself to Ragna’s side. “Ragna, what do you mean forced? You were super worried too, remember?”
“W-Worried? I was not!”
“Didn’t you say that he might have gotten lost because the paths in the sewer system are complicated?”
“Shavin, stop making up lies. I was just speculating on what happened. And I only said that to then say that I was sure it was nothing.”
“Hmm, is that so?” Shavin smiled at the annoyed librarian. That alone gave me an idea of what kind of relationship the two of them had. Well, that wasn’t important right now.
“Enough chitchat. Here’s my report.” If I wanted to be able to return to the inn before the day ended and get some sleep, I needed to move quickly.

The results of our sewer patrol were simple: we found and killed one vagrant, and that was all. There was no evidence that we properly completed the quest because the video recorder got smashed, but saving the guy’s ID ended up being helpful.

“Hans Marcom. I’ve heard of him. He’s a wanted criminal who was on the run for robbery and murder. Including the commission fee and additional pay, that will be 180,000 stones. If you visit the administrative office tomorrow, I will pay you right away.”
“I don’t have to pay for breaking the video recorder?”
“That’s... I’ll explain it to the higher-ups. I’m sure they’ll say it’s all right since these are rather special circumstances.”
“Special circumstances, huh?”

She wasn’t wrong, but I hadn’t thought she would even take that into consideration. However, rather than assuming the administrative agency was a flexible organization unlike the guild, it would probably be more accurate for me to say that Shavin just did me a favor.

“May the blessing of the twilight star be with you.” After a while, the person Shavin called from the temple arrived. This wasn’t an ordinary priest, but a paladin with a terrifying bayonet on his back. The paladin thoroughly inspected the corpse we brought back with us and nodded. “This is the traitor Elisa Behenk. Our sect will not forget this feat.”
His voice was kind, without any hint of arrogance, and there was even some respect for us there. But what did he mean by “Will not forget?” Wasn’t that a bit vague?
“By feat, do you mean there’s reward money?” I asked flat-out, like a barbarian who knew no shame.
The paladin just smiled kindly. “I see there’s been a misunderstanding. The bounty will be paid by the Adventurers’ Guild.”
“Does that mean that if I hand the body over to you guys, I won’t receive the money?”
“Haha, I’ll send an official letter to the guild as soon as the sun rises tomorrow, so you need not worry about that.”
“...I see.”
Welp. You could’ve started with that.
“Hey, Mr. Paladin?” asked Missha. “When we were fighting with that woman earlier, we all lost our memory... Can you check if that’s caused any other prrroblems?”
“Of course.” After that, the paladin cast Advanced Purification on each of us and left. Apparently, he needed to take the corpse to the temple quickly.

“We’ll get going too. There will be a lot to include in the report tomorrow. You should get some rest.” Shavin and Ragna followed the paladin’s lead. As it was late, they turned around and disappeared as soon as the matter was finished.
Hmm, were we done with the most pressing work, then? “Let’s meet again tomorrow to talk about the bounty.”
“Ugh, finally going home!”
“I think I smell worse than I did when I came back from the labyrinth! Hahaha!”

We dispersed too and headed to our respective inns. It was eleven o’clock at night when I got in. I wanted to sleep right away, but I went into the bathroom and scrubbed my body for a while to wash away the filth. It was only once I was lying in bed that I realized.
This was a tough day.
I didn’t know why I was being forced to feel this way by a 150,000-stone quest, but... I made it back alive this time too.

The next morning, everyone gathered and stopped by the guild to accept the bounty. Fortunately, the paladin took care of his side of things quickly, so I was able to receive it simply by presenting my ID.
“Ten million stones, I can’t believe it. Hahaha!”

Even when divided by five, it was a huge payout of two million stones each. When we met that morning, smiles bloomed on the faces of those who had previously been complaining about the smell of sewage, which had not yet gone away.
“I see now. Bjorn, you’re a lucky charm. For some reason, ever since I met you, it feels like money is just raining down from the sky!”
Yes, I’m sure you feel that way. I was the one who got my brain blown up by that bitch.
Even Brown added his two cents. “...I don’t believe in superstitions, but at this point, I have no choice. Bjorn, it is clear that the goddess of fortune is with you on your journey.”
I knew that was meant to be a compliment, but it didn’t feel that great to hear. Why were the achievements I’d obtained by working like a dog now thanks to a goddess I’d never even met before?
“Then I’ll be going now,” I said.
“Huh? Where are you going? We should have a drink!”
“I have to visit the administrative office too.”
“Ah, right. They told you to collect the commission fee. You go do that. We’ll be having a drink.”
Wow, not even an empty offer of “I’ll go with you.”
Well, I did get one from Missha. “Bjorn! Want me to go with you?”
“It’s fine. After yesterday, you should take a break.”
“Mm, okay.”

After distributing the bounty, I headed straight for the administrative office, a five-story building reminiscent of the old Seoul Station building. When I climbed the stairs to the facility management department on the third floor, I was able to find Shavin without any trouble.
“Mr. Yandel! You’re here!”
As always, she was in uniform. However, because everyone was wearing the same thing, she didn’t really stand out. Instead, I was the one who was out of place.
“Ehh, is that Little Balkan?”
“I heard he has a power where he grows super big!”
“What are you all talking about? Oh my gosh, so embarrassing...”

Were there mostly female workers here? As soon as I entered the facility management department, fussy whispering erupted all around me. It was like being a monkey in a cage. I decided to leave right after finishing my job.
“Now all you have to do is sign here to accept the payment. If you do not have a registered signature, you can simply write your name.”
“Sure.”
Soon after, the money was paid out and the documents were signed. However, just as I was about to leave, Shavin stopped me. “Ah! Right! If you have time, please visit the library.”
“Library?”
“Ragna has something prepared for you.”
She did? The playful look in her eyes made me suspect I could just ignore her request, but I instead answered, “Okay. I’ll stop by if I have time.”
“All right! You have to, okay?”
Sensing there was definitely something going on there, I decided I’d have to stop by.
After leaving the administrative office, I returned to the pub where my party was. Needless to say, it was a mess. It was still broad daylight, so I thought they’d be a little more low-key.
“No, it’s true! Hahahahahaha!”
“Don’t lie, you dwarrrf! How can someone’s name be Dick Johnson?! Ahahaha!”
Hikurod and Missha were drunkenly chatting. Dwalkie had his head glued to the table and was giggling to himself. “Keke, I am the great wizard Riol Warb Dwalkie...”
Brown sighed at the sight and greeted me like a gentleman. “Ah, you’re here? Was there any trouble?”
“It seems like I should be asking you that question. Why are they already like this?”
“They made good money. I’m sure everyone was in a good mood.”
“...I see.” With that, I approached Missha. After taking the mug of beer she was holding, I grabbed the nape of her neck and lifted her up.
“Ahh! W-Who...?! Bjorrrn? When did you get here?”
“Just now. And stop drinking.”

“....Eek! Arrre you my dad?” Missha protested, shooting me an outraged glare. I was about to say something before she could get any more rebellious, but then she burst out laughing. “Ah! Right! My dad doesn’t carrre about anything like that! Hahaha!”
This kid was not doing great today. Whew... I thought I would be taking a break here. “Enough. If you’re bored, drink this instead.”
“Okay.”

I couldn’t let her get any more drunk, so I ordered tomato juice, shoved it in Missha’s face, and sat down next to her. The dwarf wasn’t my problem, but if this kid got too drunk to even move, I was the one who was going to have to take her home since I was the only one who lived in that direction.
“Haha! You two are really weird!” Hikurod teased. “There’s something! There’s something here!”
“Don’t be silly and drink some water if you’re drunk.”
“Kahaha, you’re still young too, it seems. Does this look like beer to you? I’m just drinking water! Water!”

“...Do what you want.” I decided to pay him no mind and ordered a bunch of dishes to satisfy my hunger. Missha perked up a bit, studying me intently while squirming in her seat. “...Do you have something to say?”
The answer was immediate. “I do!”
That made me a little anxious, but I just nodded for now. “...Say it.”
Missha slapped her flushed cheeks twice, took a deep breath, and opened her mouth. “My father wants to see you—”
“Wow! Who’s this? If it isn’t Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“Huh? Who is this purrrson?”
The man who had interrupted Missha and called out to me in a loud voice was someone I recognized. “You’re...”
“Did you forget my name already? It’s Hans! Hans Hodge!”

“...Right.” I remembered his name right away, but his place on the list was a bit confusing. Characterized by a scrawny body and freckles, this guy’s Hans Code was B. We met at a bar after Ainar left my party. He had even advised me to go to the guild to find a teammate.
But what business does this bastard have with me?

Maybe it was just because I’d encountered a lot of Hanses since then, but as soon as this guy started talking to me, I started to worry. For some reason, it felt like something horrible was about to happen.
“Can I sit down?” Hans asked.
“No, I have nothing to say to you.”
“Hmm, still, it’s quite a coincidence that we ran into each other like t—”
“I’m getting up soon. So, leave.”

“I-I see. I was just happy to see you again...” As I shut him down so as not to get involved with him, Hans B turned around, looking all sullen. I had no basis for this, but for some reason, I felt like I had just dodged a bullet.
Wham!
The door on the first floor opened, and a group of knights with the same family crest engraved on their chests entered the bar.
“It’s the Mozlan!”
“Why are they at a rundown bar like this?”

The Mozlan: one of the city’s most powerful armed groups that only knights of noble origin could join. They were notorious for leaving nothing but blood and death behind when captured. The moment the Mozlan entered the bar, everyone’s attention was drawn to them, and the room suddenly fell completely silent.
“That way.” At the commander’s order, the knights moved in unison. Unfortunately, it was in the direction I was seated.
Damn it all.
What was it this time? As I looked back on my recent progress to see if I had made any mistakes, I suddenly remembered what the clan’s shaman had said while telling me my fortune.
“Be wary of those who harbor resentment for you at any time, anywhere.”
I also spotted Hans B on his way back to his original seat, pushed to the wall to make way for the Mozlan.
Wait a minute, someone who’s bitter... Could that be referring to Hans?
The truth was I’d never had anything good come from getting involved with those guys, but just when my thoughts reached that conclusion, the group of knights stopped in front of our table.
Click.
They looked at us, and one spoke in a deep and authoritative voice. I froze in place, still holding my fork. “Riol Warb Dwalkie, you are being arrested for contempt of nobility.”
Surprisingly, it wasn’t me this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 86: Baron Martoin (2)
paragraphs: The Mozlan were swift and efficient.
“Keke, I am... the great wizard—hmm? Who are you guys...?”
“This is him. Take him.” After lifting Dwalkie’s head by the hair to check his face, the knights quickly restrained his arms.
“Um, e-excuse me, is there a problem...?” Only then did the drunken dwarf come to his senses and try to figure out what was going on, but to no avail.
“You guys don’t need to know.”
“B-But...”
“Are you dissatisfied with our handling of the situation?”
It seemed to me that if he nodded his head, they would take Hikurod too. I covered his mouth and answered in his stead. “No.”
“...Are you Little Balkan? You are wise for a barbarian.” The tone of voice and look in the knight’s eyes made it difficult to take that as a compliment.
As soon as they left the pub with the drunken Dwalkie, the dwarf began to fuss. “Bjorn! There must be a misunderstanding. Th-that guy would never do such a thing!”
He definitely wasn’t wrong. Contempt of nobility? Maybe identity theft, but contempt? That was hard for even me to accept.
“We have to help!”
What should I do to save a comrade who had been taken away by the authorities? I closed my eyes.
“Hikurod, c-calm down. When Bjorrrrn is like that, it means he has a solution!”

Whew, and I thought I’d get to rest today. Why was it that something like this always happened? Before I could do anything, I needed to get a clearer picture of the situation. We didn’t have any information yet. I didn’t even know whether Dwalkie had insulted a real noble, if they’d just misunderstood, or if he’d been framed. So, I left the pub and headed for Mozlan’s headquarters.
“Wait until the investigation is officially closed.”
Even in the game, the closed-minded and arrogant Mozlan had never released any information. So, I went to Shavin.
“He was taken away by Mozlan? I’ll look into it. I can’t guarantee I’ll learn anything, though...”
“That’s good enough. Thanks.”
“It’s nothing.”
Since Shavin was a civil servant, I decided that she would have an easier time accessing information than an adventurer on the ground.
“...He’ll still be alive, right?”
“Hikurod! I underrrstand that you’re worried, but stop saying things that will bring bad luck and sit still!”
“A-All right.”
We were all waiting on word from Shavin and spent all day outside Mozlan’s headquarters.
“Huh? Isn’t that Dwalkie?”
“Looks like it.”
Dwalkie came out through the front door with slumped shoulders. Despite what the dwarf was worried about, there seemed to be no signs of torture on him, or even any injuries.
Hikurod burst forward. “You! Are you okay? How did the investigation go? I-If they released you, that means there was a misunderstanding, right? I knew it!”

“Ah, well...” For some reason, Dwalkie just bowed his head, not even happy to see us. “...Let’s move somewhere else. I’ll tell you everything there.” For now, we obeyed Dwalkie’s wishes and relocated ourselves to a tavern that we often visited when holding labyrinth-related meetings. After a few snacks and the beer we ordered arrived, Dwalkie started in, his tone sad. “It seems... I will have to leave the party.”
After Erwen and Ainar, this was the third time I heard something like this. The dwarf gasped. “No, what are you talking about?! Explain in detail!”
“Well...” Dwalkie began, then let out a long breath. “It would be ridiculous to try and hide it now. To be honest, there is something I have kept hidden from you all.”
“Hidden?”
“My older brother... is Baron Martoin.”
“What?” Missha gasped.
“S-So you’re saying you really are nobility?”
Everyone’s mouths fell open in shock, but Dwalkie closed his eyes and continued speaking. “That’s half-true. I am the child of the last Baron Martoin and one of his maids.”
An illegitimate son of a noble family. This story wasn’t unfamiliar to me, as I had been exposed to many modern-day soap operas. The story that followed was not much different than those, either.

“Because I was the family disgrace, I was adopted away to the third younger brother of the baroness as soon as I was born—my adoptive father, Tirva. Of course, that was just a formality, and it was my mother who actually raised me.” Still, the baron had regularly sent him money, and thanks to that, he was able to learn magic and grow up comfortably. It was a complicated family history just hearing it.
The dwarf didn’t seem to have the time to wait patiently, though. “So what does that have to do with leaving the team?”
“A year ago, my father, Baron Martoin, passed away. And my second brother took his place.”
“Hmm, not the first?” Brown interrupted with a question.
“That’s right,” Dwalkie continued frankly. “The second son. That’s the problem.”
“I don’t underrrstand, why is that a problem?”

“After the late baron died, a lot of other people died, from the first son to many others in the line of succession...” Those words were enough explanation to determine that the cause of this incident was a bloody power struggle on Baron Martoin’s part. “It was my second brother who sent the Mozlan.”
“Makes sense. Perhaps as a warning: live a quiet life like you always have,” I suggested.
“But why now?”
“I think my becoming an explorer bothered him. I’ve been learning a lot of magic lately, too... He must have been concerned because there is even a famous person on my team.”
Ah, uh... um... Are you blaming me right now?
Honestly, that was kind of a stretch, but I summed up Dwalkie’s story. “Anyway, does that mean that you can’t go into the labyrinth anymore because you’re afraid of your second brother?”
“You really... don’t know how to beat around the bush. You’re not wrong. But no matter what I want, things would be the same either way.”
“What do you mean?”
“Instead of punishing me for insulting a noble, they took away my access to the labyrinth.” Simply put, that meant that even if he wanted to work with us, there was no way for him to do that anymore.
“Bjorn, is there no other way?” The earnest eyes of Hikurod and Missha turned to me.
I quietly closed my eyes. Rather than looking for the answer to a problem that could not be solved, I thought about what day it was today.
What a headache.

Nine days left until the labyrinth opened again. Would I be able to find a new party member before then? Honestly, nothing in my life was ever easy. “For now, let’s think this issue over individually, and then we’ll meet again tomorrow and discuss it.”
“Yeah, I’m sure even you won’t be able to come up with a plan of action right away. Let’s do that.”
After setting up our next meeting, we parted ways. Hikurod and Dwalkie decided to have a drink in a quiet place, and Rotmiller went home. I decided to head to the library.
“Huh? You’re going to the librrrary?” asked Missha.
“I have business with the librarian from yesterday.”
“...At this late hour?”
“If I hurry, I’ll get there before it closes.”
“I see... d-do you want me to go with you?”
What was this kid talking about? “It’s fine. You go rest.”
“It’s not like I have anything to do back home...”
“What do you mean? If you have free time, swing your swords one more time. You played around the whole day today.”

After sending off Missha, who tried to insist on following me, I hurriedly headed to the library. Originally, I had planned to get a good rest today and go tomorrow, but there had been a change of plans.
“Parsytie—” When I arrived at the library, the librarian was about to mechanically cast her spell on me when she flinched. “You’re...”
“Come to think of it, I never formally introduced myself. I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“...Of course I know your name.”
That was fair. Anyway, after that bit of conversation, there was silence. I always felt awkward around this one.
“...We’re closing soon. Are you heading in?”
“No, I didn’t come to read today.”
“Then...?”
How should I explain my situation? After thinking about it for a while, I just got straight to the point, like a barbarian. “Ragna Litaniel Peprok.”
“You don’t have to call me by my full name.”

“Ragna, what rank are you as a wizard?” I asked casually, but there was no answer for a while. The look on her face seemed to be asking, “What kind of rude bastard is this?” True, Raven had also been angered by this question.
“Let me ask you this first: why are you suddenly curious about that?” Ragna asked calmly, apparently a milder type than Raven.
I answered honestly. “Something has happened and the wizard on my team cannot enter the labyrinth. I want to ask if you’ll take a break from your work here and go into the labyrinth toge—”
“I refuse.”
Uh-huh, so it’s a rejection. At her resolute refusal, I shook off my inhibitions. “I see. If your rank is so low that you can’t enter the labyrinth, there’s nothing you can do about it.”
“...When did I say that?”
“Then you are skilled enough.”
Realizing that I was feeling her out, Ragna stopped in the middle of getting angry and put a blank expression on her face instead. “Because... you’re curious about my skills?”

“...What are you talking about? Anyway, this conversation ends here. If you don’t want to, there’s nothing I can do.” I changed the subject. “So what is it? Shavin Emoor told me you would have something prepared for me.”

“...I beg your pardon? Something prepared for you?” Ragna furrowed her brows like this was the first she’d heard this, then put a hand on her forehead as she figured out what was going on. “Ha... is that what she said?”
“Speak in a way I can understand.”

“I’m warning you in advance to not misread this.” Ragna only confessed to her actual situation after I promised not to misunderstand her. “Shavin said her position in the department has risen thanks to you. So she asked for my advice on a way to repay you, and... I told her you like to read books.”
“And?”
“That was all. All of a sudden she mentioned I owed her something and asked me to pay you back instead. So this is not coming from me, but Shavin. Do you understand?”
“...Understood.”
To put it simply, she had something for me, although I didn’t know why she was exerting so much energy emphasizing that it wasn’t coming from her. If it were me, I would be giving myself more credit.
“Did you really understand me correctly?”
“I did. So what is the gift?”
“It’s a book.”
“...A book?”
When I cocked my head, Ragna closed her eyes and chanted a spell. “Bierdo Parsytiev.”
When the spell was completed, my body shined with a dazzling golden light. The chant was even a little different than usual. “What is this?”
At my question, Ragna uncharacteristically explained in detail. “There are high-security books in this library that do not respond to normal book recognition magic.”
“...I didn’t know something like that was hidden here.”
“Originally, accessing them was a privilege granted only to nobles or a select few with permission.”
A kind of secret library for the establishment. I felt like I’d received an unexpected gift, and I was dazed. “Is it okay for you to grant me access to something like that?”

“As long as you don’t go around telling everyone, it won’t be a problem. Since... I took over as librarian, I’ve only used this spell a handful of times, anyway.” When Ragna continued, her voice was slightly gloomy. “Who would be interested in this place?”
I was beginning to get curious about her story too.
Click, clack.
In the empty library with only the clicking of shoes resounding through the silence, I was reading a book thanks to Ragna’s thoughtful gesture.
“—In that case, why did you come so late? Hah, fine. I will allow it just for today.”

When it was closing time, all visitors were kicked out, but Ragna allowed me to remain until the books were all organized. It felt a little strange as if I had entered an authorized-persons-only area.
Click, clack.
I set down the book I was reading for a moment and glanced at Ragna.
I was wondering how she organized this place. I guess it’s all done by magic.

Books fell into place on the empty bookshelves each time she moved her wand the slightest bit. I suddenly wondered if they were going to the right places, but... Come to think of it, the books in this library didn’t need to be in a particular spot since magic allowed you to find the books you wanted.
Wait. “Ragna?”
“Tell me.”
“When we first met, didn’t you tell me to put all the books I read in their original places?”
“I usually say that when I’m too lazy to give a detailed explanation. Because it’s magic, there are a lot of people who ask unnecessary questions.”
“...I see.”
Those were very hurtful words for a barbarian, but I didn’t let it show and continued reading. The books’ high security level was obvious just from their contents.
Rafdonia Organization Chart
There were books dealing with the public institutions in this city, describing groups that included the Ministry of Security—i.e. evil spirit hunters.
World of Evil Spirits
Some books even dealt with the Ghost Busters in depth. This book spoke of an agent who had entered their spiritual dimension and returned half-dead.
With a system like that in place, I wouldn’t be in any danger.

Thanks to this, I was now convinced that I could take the pill in my possession when the right time came. I switched my focus to another book. But just when I finished one and was about to start the next, my hands froze as I read the title.
The Complete Book of Rifts II
Wasn’t this the name of the book Raven had mentioned? I quickly opened the first page to check the contents and soon understood why she had acted the way she did.
...I see why she was so obsessive.

It was a kind of strategy book. All of the hidden information that I had discovered through countless experiments and tricks while playing the game was written down, although only four rifts were described due to the physical limitations of the book.
This must be a treasure trove to the people here.

The contents were so perfectly outlined that even I couldn’t see any gaps to fill. And because this copy was so well-maintained, contrary to Raven’s assumption that the book was written by an anonymous source, the author’s name was also written on the last page.
“Auril Gavis...?” Without realizing it, I read the name aloud and promptly froze like a statue.
Shit, why is this bastard’s name here?
Auril Gavis was the name of the creator of Dungeon and Stone.

chapters.title: Chapter 87: Baron Martoin (3)
paragraphs: Auril Gavis was the creator’s alias, which always appeared at the bottom of the loading window. Well, I didn’t know if it was an alias or a real name, but anyway.
Why is that name...

It was a bit unexpected, but there were two possible reasons for this. The Complete Book of Rifts II had either been written by a player, or by Auril himself. The thought that it might be the latter had me feeling restless. At the very least, that meant that the creators of the game were closely tied to the events that led to the awakening in this body.
Is that bastard really some kind of divine being?

Anyway, getting this clue was a good sign. Auril Gavis. If I followed this name carefully, I would be able to figure out a way back home one day. Though, again, I didn’t know anything yet. I didn’t even know whether reaching the last floor and opening the door to the Abyss once again was the key to returning.
Recklessly asking around will end with bloodshed, so I should look into this carefully.

With that thought in mind, I read the book closely. Nothing really came out of doing so. The only thing on the back page was the signature of the presumed author—not even the year the book was written was there. After confirming that Ragna was not around, I tore off just the corner and slipped it into my bag.
If I can just figure out what year this book was made it’ll be a huge—

Wait, was it morning already? I cut my thoughts off there and got up from my seat. When I headed to the desk, I saw Ragna nodding off. Just as I was about to cover her with the blanket next to her, she woke up from the sound. “Mm.”
“Why didn’t you tell me? If I had known that this much time had passed, I would have left sooner.”
“Don’t misunderstand. I was just taking a break because it was taking a little longer to organize the books than expected.”
A little longer? It was already almost close to opening.
“It’s true. Don’t take this the wrong way.”
“...Okay.”
Since she insisted, I just nodded and left the library. Before I opened the door, I glanced behind me and saw her stretching with a tired look on her face.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you leaving?” she asked.
Maybe she was actually a nice person?
It was already morning, so I just started the day. I was a barbarian anyway, so it didn’t make a difference whether I washed up or not.
But I’ll still have to eat first.
I went to whatever nearby restaurant was open, grabbed a quick meal, and headed straight for the Magic Tower.
“What are you doing here so early, Mr. Yandel?” Raven asked.
“I have come to ask you something.”
“Well, hurry up. I’m tired.”
“There’s a vacancy for a wizard on our team, and I wondered if you might join—”
Click.
She closed the door.
Fuck, if you don’t want to, just say so.
Another failure. Whatever, I didn’t expect her to agree, anyway. “Wait! I have another favor to ask!” I hurriedly shouted.
As I knocked on the door, it cracked open with a squeak. “Another favor?”
“I want to know when this paper was made.”

“Hmm? Let me see.” Raven carefully inspected the scrap of paper I handed over with obvious curiosity, but she couldn’t find anything interesting on it. “It wouldn’t be impossible, but why do you want to know?”
“Can’t you just do it?”

“Well, all right. But I won’t do this for free—I’ll have to get something in return...” Raven trailed off and then continued when she thought of something appropriate. “My seniors are very interested in you, so go help out with their research. They’ve been bothering me about that for a while now.”
Are you telling me to entrust my body to those perverts, now?
“...Just once?”
“Yes, it’s not that difficult a favor. I’ll have the analysis of this paper done by your visit next week. Ah! Right. And don’t come looking for me at such an early hour if you can help it.”
“...All right.”

When I finished my business and left the tower, it was 9 a.m. It was a little early, but there was nothing to do, so I headed to the meeting place, a bar. To my surprise, someone had gotten there before me.
“Bjorn! What! I went to your inn and you weren’t therrre!” Missha cried.
“Oh, I was at the library.”
“W-What? All night...? Was that what you meant by business?!”
“What are you talking about? I was reading thanks to Ragna’s generosity.” I only spoke the truth, but Missha gave me a doubtful look. It wasn’t like she was my mom...
“Is that trrrue...?”
“Why would I lie to you?”

“That’s... true. Okay.” Surprisingly, when I looked her straight in the eyes and said that, she readily accepted my explanation. A good son wouldn’t lie—was that the vibe she was getting? Anyway, when I sat down next to her, Missha handed me the drink she was sipping. “Drink some of this. It’s made from a frrruit called tomato and it has a very interesting taste!”

I didn’t know about interesting, but that reminded me of something. “Before that, what did you want to tell me yesterday?” Judging by her tone, it had seemed like she was going to say something important, but because Hans B interrupted, I hadn’t been able to hear the rest.
“Huh? What arrre you talking about?”
“Don’t you remember?”

“Uh, uh... Could it have been that I misspoke?” Given the innocent look in her eyes, it seemed she really had been too drunk to remember. I even asked if there was something she had been meaning to tell me, but nothing came of that either. “Huh? I don’t have anything like that.”
“I see.”
“...Are you mad?”

“No.” There were two ways to make someone angry, but I didn’t get angry from things like that. It wasn’t like it was her fault. After that, as I was passing the time by using the quiet bar like a cafe, the others arrived.
“Oh, were you here first?”
“I’m sorry, you all had to come here this early because of me...”

As always, Hikurod and Dwalkie appeared as a pair. We waited for a while, and then Rotmiller arrived right on time. The meeting started. The topic was, of course, how to get rid of Dwalkie’s ban from entering the labyrinth.
“Then let me know if any of you have any ideas. First... Yes, Bjorn, let’s start with you.”
Uh, me first? That was quite nerve-wracking, but I gave my presentation frankly and concisely. “I think it would be better to find a new party member.”
“...What?”
“Of course, finding a wizard seems unrealistic. I suggested it to two other wizards, but they turned the offer down.”
“...W-What are you saying right now? You already spoke with other wizards?”

“Is there a problem?” I asked confidently. Hikurod may have been saddened that I was trying to find any solution possible, but the difference between selfishness and altruism was always a fine line. I was just assuming the worst and trying to find a realistic alternative for the team. “One of us had to say it. Isn’t that right, Rotmiller?”
“That’s... true.” When I singled him out for an opinion, Rotmiller nodded with a rather uncomfortable look on his face.
At that, the dwarf sobered.
“M-Murad! I’m all right, so don’t look like that. Bjorn didn’t say anything wrong, did he?” When even Dwalkie agreed, Hikurod shut his mouth.
Missha raised her hand brightly as if to try to dispel the tension. “Th-then I’ll go next!”
“G-Go ahead, Miss Karlstein.”
Of course, it was nothing I needed to genuinely hear out. “I looked into it and I heard the Mozlan are weak against brrribes. What if we collect some money and give it a shot?”
Soliciting bribes with that innocent tone. There was no doubt Baron Martoin or whatever his name was must have offered the Mozlan money to take care of Dwalkie too.
“Miss Karlstein, the Mozlan never do business with people who are not nobles,” Brown explained.
The Mozlan thoroughly excluded commoners. Although most of them were without titles themselves... No, rather, that was probably why that was their last point of pride.
“I-Is that so...? I didn’t know that. Then, Rotmillerrr, you go next.” Missha passed, embarrassed.

Since it was Rotmiller’s opinion this time, I also waited to hear him out. “To be honest, I don’t know how to get what you want from a noble... especially a titled one. I’m sorry...” It seemed Rotmiller hadn’t found a proper solution, either.
However, unlike earlier with me, Hikurod sighed and comforted him. “How could that be your fault? In truth... It’s only natural.”
Then why did you glare at me?
As I grunted inwardly, the dwarf opened his mouth to voice a suggestion of his own. “So I wanted to ask... Last night, Dwalkie and I put our heads together.”
“Get to the point.”
“I wonder if we should go speak with Baron Martoin in person.”
In other words, a face-to-face match. But there was a serious problem here. “How are you going to meet with him?”
Most nobles lived in Sector One, the capital of Karnon. That area was not even accessible to low-level adventurers like us. A conversation? We lived in two different worlds to begin with.
However, it seemed that Hikurod had already devised a detailed plan. “There is a teahouse that Baron Martoin visits regularly. If we wait for him there, we will definitely be able to run into him.”

Well, in that case, that definitely wasn’t a bad idea. The problem was that the baron was unlikely to change his mind. But there was nothing to lose by trying. “Then there’s no issue with that. You two go.”
“W-What kind of cold reaction is that! Come with us!” urged Hikurod.
What was he talking about? “You’re just going there to beg, at best. Why should we all go?”
“...We need courage! The opponent is a man of nobility!”

At my command to figure it out on their own, the dwarf started to whine. I was already sighing at that hopeless reaction, but considering everything we’d been through together, I began weighing the practical benefits of this.
Finding a new wizard with just nine days left would be unreasonable...

Even if we were able to find someone regardless of their job in the city, if it wasn’t someone who had their head screwed on right, that would only result in us having a hard time. It was still best for Dwalkie to stay on this team.

And if we send just these two, they won’t be able to say anything and will cause more problems. No matter how I look at it, it seems that we only have a chance If I go myself. But... I don’t really want to go meet a nobleman.
The iron rule in the game had been to avoid getting entangled with nobles as much as possible since none of them were sane.
“However this ends, I’ll give you three hundred thousand stones! Per person!” Hikurod offered.
Hmmm, that was a bit tempting. If there were motivations other than loyalty on the table, there was no one I couldn’t meet, even a nobleman. “If that’s the case, then it wouldn’t hurt to meet him.”
“Really?” At my acceptance, Hikurod’s face noticeably lit up.
However, rather than being swept up in his tactics, I calmly asked what I needed to know. “So, when can we go?”

This man may have been nobility, but this was not a world where you could just kill someone on a whim, especially a respected adventurer. In any case, this meeting would pose no serious threat, but this would still be my first time seeing a real noble since waking up in this body. I also wanted time to prepare myself.
“T-Today.”
“What...?”
“I-If not today, he won’t be visiting that teahouse again until next month.”

Huh, no wonder I had wanted to refuse. Still, I had agreed to do it, so I asked about the other things one by one: how old the baron was, whether he was really a man, if there was anything he didn’t like, and anything else I should know. Time flew by quickly as I familiarized myself with all this.
“L-Let’s go,” said Hikurod. “If we want to pretend we ran into him by coincidence like you said, we should be there in advance!”

The baron’s visits to the teahouse were usually between three and four o’clock in the afternoon, so we arrived at the teahouse at two o’clock and waited for his arrival. How much time had passed since?
Dwalkie suddenly pointed. “Th-that man is my second eldest brother.”

Baron Martoin appeared with his attendants. Apparently, he visited the shop himself to enjoy tea made directly by the owner. If he entered the private rooms, there would be no time to talk, so I quickly got up and took the lead.
“Who goes there?” When I got close, a gigantic knight blocked my way.
As planned, Dwalkie stepped forward. “B-Baron Martoin! It’s me! Riol Warb Dwalkie! Please listen to me just this once!” Dwalkie fell flat on the floor to show submission, as I’d advised.

At that, the baron’s interest shifted from the tea shop owner to Dwalkie. His reaction was completely different from what we’d expected. “Dwalkie...? That sounds familiar.” His murmurs suggested he couldn’t even remember who Dwalkie was.
A man who looked like a butler spoke into his ear. “The Dwalkie family is the family of the former baron’s third wife, Karlina.”
“Ahh, that’s right! So, what business does he have with me?”
“I-I... i-it’s just that...” Unlike what I had planned, Dwalkie struggled to get the words out from the onset.
It was earlier than I had expected, but it was my turn to step forward. “Nice to meet you. I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

Nobility or not, I spoke proudly. If I had been of a different race, that alone would have resulted in a charge of contempt for nobility, but a large, valuable barbarian was an exception. In the past, my ancestors had accomplished something very impressive and had received such allowances from the king.

Fortunately, the baron looked interested. “It’s been a while since I’ve spoken to a barbarian. It’s always a strange feeling.” True, when would someone like him run into a barbarian and get spoken to so casually? “So, what’s your business with me?”
“After he was dragged out by the Mozlan yesterday, this guy was banned from entering the labyrinth.”
“How unfortunate. But why are you telling me this?”
Because you were the one who ordered them to do it. What is this? Why do you look like you have no idea what I’m talking about?
At first, I thought he was just acting, but at this point, I was starting to have doubts too. Just then, the butler whispered to the baron again.
“Hmm, a bastard? Was there such a thing? I see. It was your doing...”
“Yes, my lord. I did not feel it was something to bother you with.”
“Well done. Something as trivial as that would have been a waste of time to learn.”
Now I was seeing that the baron didn’t know anything about this. It seemed that the butler had taken care of everything.

“Something... as trivial?” Dwalkie muttered. Despite his shock, if you only looked at the outcome, this wasn’t so bad. It meant that the possibility that we’d achieve our goal had increased, as long as the other party regarded this matter as insignificant.
“Could you possibly withdraw the ban on entry into the labyrinth?” I asked.

“Hmm, why should I do that?” The baron cocked his head as if he didn’t understand. What was annoying here was that I didn’t sense any malice from him. His way of thinking was just completely different from ours.
This mighty fucking noble...

As I was inwardly cursing the baron and wondering what to do next, the butler once again whispered in his ear. I was not sure how he was doing it, but once again, I couldn’t hear a single thing. Still, I had a rough idea of what he was saying.
“Huh? What did you say? This is that barbarian?”
“Yes, my lord.”

“Huh, Little Balkan... I have heard of that name. At a banquet two days ago, the count mentioned that an interesting adventurer had appeared.” The baron looked at me in a completely different way from earlier. As if he had discovered an interesting toy, his eyes were full of life. “Did you say your name is Bjorn? If I grant your request, can you do me a favor?”
Ah, uh... um... I didn’t expect this to happen...
“It’s not a big favor. Besides, I’ll offer a fitting reward for it! How about it?”
Somehow, I received my second quest.

chapters.title: Chapter 88: Baron Martoin (4)
paragraphs: The core of the baron’s request was simple. In two months, some count was holding a big banquet. All I had to do was accompany him there.
“Is that it...?”

“Hmm, and I also wish for you to show off some tricks in front of the people. Something like bending steel with your bare hands.” In a nutshell, he was going to use me as a trophy to make himself stand out at the banquet. “Can you do it?”
Well, what do you think a barbarian would say?
“That is no problem,” I agreed.
“All right, then.”
The reward was one million stones and the dismissal of Dwalkie’s ban. Wow, was this what nobles were like? To think he would waste that much money just to show me off to people.
Well, all I have to do is sweep up the crumbs.
Even if it weren’t for Dwalkie’s predicament, it was good bang for my buck. One million stones for humoring him for a single day? The smelly sewer request had been 150,000 stones.

“Hmm, good. Then I’ll deal with your friend’s problem right away. Think of it as a favor to you.” The baron was even charitable enough to solve Dwalkie’s problem first. I wondered what he planned to do if I didn’t keep my promise.
Nobles are entities that don’t have to worry about things like that.
Once again, I felt that I had a long way to go. I had created some amount of protection for myself and even earned a decent reputation.
But I’ll have to come up with a plan for this soon too.
I needed power, just like in the game. Ever since waking up in this place, I’d found that events that threatened my life didn’t just happen in the labyrinth.
The next morning, we gathered at our meeting place again to check if Dwalkie had been granted permission to enter the labyrinth.
“How did it go? Did the baron keep his prrromise?”
“When I checked today, they said there was no problem,” Dwalkie answered.
“But why don’t you look happy?”
“Haha, it’s nothing...”

Nothing, my ass. Had it been such a shock that his half-brother, Baron Martoin, couldn’t even remember him properly, let alone pay attention to him? Ever since yesterday, Dwalkie had been completely out of it, although he tried not to show it.
“Whew...” He became lost in thought several times a day and kept sighing deeply. I hoped he’d come to his senses before the labyrinth opened up again.
“Oh, before I forget, take this. It’s the reward I promised.” Hikurod offered me three hundred thousand stones.
“Reward?”
“You came with us to face the baron.”
“It’s fine, we’rrre a team.”
“I didn’t go there seeking a reward,” Rotmiller added. “Besides, we faced the baron for the party’s sake.”
I decided not to take it. The other two had waved off the money, so it would be awkward to accept it.
It’s not like I’m in need of three hundred thousand stones right now anyway.
It would be better to save this one as an IOU for later. If we continued entering the labyrinth together, there would be more give-and-take and also times when we’d each have to make concessions.
“Anyway, thank you,” Hikurod said to me. “It must not have been easy to throw away your pride as a warrior.”
Uh, well... To be honest, hearing that only made me sheepish. One million stones was too much money to care about self-esteem.
“I will never forget this and will pay you all back,” Dwalkie vowed.
“Why would you pay it back? Bjorn, I will surely repay this debt tenfold,” interrupted Hikurod.
“Either one of you is fine, so you guys can figure it out,” I said.
“Hehe, Bjorn is shy!” giggled Missha.
No, I’m serious.

There were eight days left until the labyrinth opened. What I’d gotten done so far was simple. Aside from daily routines such as helping Missha train and reading the hidden books at the library, I found out the year The Complete Book of Rifts II had been printed.
“The paper was made 150 years ago.” It was just a plain sheet of paper that had been the standard for printing at that time.
Huh, what the hell happened 150 years ago?

That had been the same year the game began, the year the first king of a dynasty had died, and even the year this book had been made. Many question marks kept popping up no more and no less than 150 years ago.
I’m sure that’s not a coincidence.
The events above were somehow related. That was all I had found out so far, but that was still enough motivation to move forward.
I’ll have to look into historical events from 150 years ago.
Who brought the players here? What was their purpose, and who the hell was Auril Gavis? If I kept collecting clues, I may be able to learn the truth one day. Anyway, onto the next one.
“Uh, uh...you want to do that? No! Not that I don’t want to, it’s just a bit sudden...”

I opened an Alminus bank account with Missha and we designated each other as our next of kin upon death. In the future, I planned to put some of the money we earned together in this account and use it as shared funds.
“In that case, I’m going to put the two million stones we earned this month in here.”
“Ehh? All of it?”
“We’re not using it right now, are we?”
“Ugh... Are you sure you’re not trrrying to use it for something strange without me knowing?”
“What kind of person do you think I am?”

I decided to put two million stones in the account and keep the remaining nine hundred thousand stones in cash. I didn’t have a place to use it right now. Plus, gone were the days of barely scraping by each month. It was about time I started saving up.
“You... Bjorn, son of Yandel?!”

Oh, and this happened. While walking down the street, I accidentally reunited with one of my barbarian peers. His name was Karak, the third son of Fanun. We didn’t do anything, just asked each other what was going on and parted ways. Apparently, he’d become a rank eight adventurer and was working as a tank in a party of humans.

“What are the other guys doing? Most are dead. Aside from you, Ainar, and me, there aren’t many left. As you know, the labyrinth is no playground.” Since teaming up with those humans, his personality had changed quite a bit. I was pretty sure he used to be more simple-minded. “If they had told us more about the place rather than sticking to the old traditions, we wouldn’t have lost so many...”

As I watched him express bitterness toward the ways of our race, I even momentarily wondered if he was truly a barbarian warrior. To be honest, I was saddened to hear all this. A lot of things must have happened for a guy who used to be a warrior to the core to change like this.
I guess not all barbarians are the same.
Thanks to that, I learned something new: barbarians could grow psychologically. They may have been weak in words and numbers, but with a change in environment, they could gain wisdom.
...There may even be some elders whose personalities are almost like the humans’.
“Bjorn, what arrre you thinking about?”
“Nothing.” I cut off my train of thought at Missha’s voice. The whole time she had been laboring over the stove to prepare a meal for me, I was sitting there mindlessly ruminating.
“Hey, Bjorn... I think you grew tallerrr?”
“What?”
“Maybe I’m wrong. Stand here for a sec!”
...I’m too lazy.
But I still stopped mid-meal and measured my height. Missha brought her hand from the top of her head to my chest and nodded. “I was right, you grrrew! About this much?”
“Are you sure you’re not mistaken?” It was honestly hard to believe. Aside from the fact that I could even grow taller here, the difference was less than half an inch, so how could she know that?
“Hmm, I have a good eye for this kind of thing. You can trrrust me.”
“...If you say so.” Rather than arguing, I just nodded. Maybe I did get taller. I’d been eating a lot of meat dishes lately.
...If I really did, though, does that mean I should eat more meat in the future?

If true, it would be worth it. I was genetically taller than average, which was the decisive reason why I used a barbarian as a tank rather than a dwarf. The Giantization mechanism itself multiplied the base height.
To be exact, it was something like 1.771 times the character’s original size.
This was another reason to eat meat.
“...Don’t just eat the meat, eat the rrrest too! Hey!”
After the meal, I did an inspection of my backpack to make sure I hadn’t missed anything, since I’d be entering the labyrinth soon.
“Let’s go, the otherrrs will be waiting.”

When we headed to the agreed-upon meeting place, I could see our other party members in different clothes than usual. Hikurod was not wearing a shirt but heavy armor, and Dwalkie was holding a long, two-handed staff.
“Oh, Rotmillerrr! Why don’t you have a weapon?”
“Don’t worry. I put it in the Treasure Vault. Now that I’m used to it, it’s more convenient to take things out every now and then instead of carrying them around.”
“Oh, I see.”

The Mimic’s ability, Treasure Vault; I used to think of it as a skill that replaced subspaces, but maybe it was a convenient essence in many different ways for Rotmiller, who handled various pieces of equipment such as crossbows, shields, and swords.

“Can you all gather around me, then?” Dwalkie asked. “I want to start the Bind.” When Dwalkie chanted a spell, a green light spread out and seeped into all of our bodies. It was a kind of party formation spell. It was with this magic that several people could enter the labyrinth and all start from the same location.
In the past, Ainar and I had to wait in front of the guild at the break of dawn...

I realized that there was a reason adventurers insisted on having a wizard on the team. If you had one, you didn’t have to wait in line in front of the guild first thing in the morning. It also came with significant monetary advantages. For five adventurers with an average rank of 6.5 to form a Bind, we would have had to pay a fee of one hundred thousand stones.
“Then let’s go.”

As we all walked toward Dimension Square, there were more and more adventurers on the street. This was the kind of sight that could only be seen on the last night of each month, since on the way back, everyone always looked like beggars.
“Halt! I think we are lost.”
“Unbelievable! We must get to the labyrinth within the set time!”

Coincidentally, I encountered the barbarians this time as well. These young warriors who had just finished their coming-of-age ceremony were heading to the labyrinth, full of anticipation and excitement.
“...Follow us.” With the consent of my teammates, I assisted them. It wasn’t out of a sense of responsibility toward my race... I just felt that I should.
“Really? Thanks. If you tell me your n—what! Bjorn, son of Yandel?! Are you Little Balkan!? I admire you!”

Ignoring the overreaction from the young warriors, I gave them all kinds of advice on our way to Dimension Square. I told them that a barbarian’s heart sold at a high price and so they should be wary of other adventurers—especially humans. They should acquire other races as night companions wherever possible. Watch out for traps, and take the paths with light, etcetera—knowledge I wish I had had on my first trip into the labyrinth.
“If I do that, can I become a famous warrior like you?” the leader asked.
Well, I don’t know about that.
“That’s right,” I lied.
“Oooh! Is that right? Okay! I will definitely do just as you said!” It would be better for them this way. They could only understand when given simple instructions.
The dwarf spoke up quietly as he watched the young warriors heading off to the portal with my advice in mind. “You... are quite kind to your own people.”
“I just did what I could. Isn’t it harsh to learn only by experience?”
“Hm, that is true. Hahaha!”
After some chitchat, we also headed to the center of the square where the portal had opened.
Shaaaaaa!
My vision darkened, and a brilliant light consisting of five colors shone in my eyes. All of a sudden, the events of the past unfolded before me like a movie reel.
Is this the fourth time already?

During my first quest, I had reached the second floor by taking out countless bastards. The second? I had entered the Rift with the determination to become stronger, but it happened to be a variant rift. Things only got worse on my next trip. A party was formed but got split up along the way. In the end, the Lord of the Floor started running rampant, so I was only able to come back after setting a foot past the threshold of the underworld.
Flash!
I hoped nothing happened this time. What could possibly happen? I discarded these thoughts before they could even fully form.
Hah, I wonder what son of a bitch will show up this time.
There was no doubt something would happen this time, too, so I needed to be prepared.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor. TIP: You have reached the limit of essences you can currently possess. Hunt new monsters to level up!]

chapters.title: Chapter 89: Player (1)
paragraphs: “Name, Hansu Lee. Age, twenty-nine. After a month of unexcused absences, his company reported him missing, huh? Tsk, and family?”
“Just his mother. When she heard the news, she said she didn’t want to be involved.”

The man listening to the report sipped his coffee. This wasn’t a particularly unique case. It was not uncommon for people to have complicated family histories. “So, Detective Park. Why has this case been brought to our team?”
“That’s because... the CCTV footage shows him entering the house but there are no signs that he exited it. All of the windows are locked too.”
“That’s... definitely fishy.”

The man set his coffee down and started reading the report more seriously. He had seen all kinds of cases during his fifteen-year career as a detective, but even he found this one a very unusual one. No signs of forced entry, and no missing money or valuables. All credit card transactions ended a month ago. Most importantly, the clothes worn by the missing person had been found in the bedroom. The way they were lying there made it seem as if he hadn’t taken them off himself, but as if his body had just disappeared.

“I don’t know what kind of bastard he is, but he’s completely crazy.” The detective already had a feeling that this wasn’t just a simple disappearance. It may even be a crime violent enough to shake the Republic of Korea. “Did you preserve the crime scene? Put a request into forensics. Let’s see what their investigation turns out first.”
Detective Park hesitated for a moment at the man’s instructions, then opened his mouth carefully. “I, Chief... Before that, I have something I want to show you.”
Why not put it in the report? The chief questioned this, but when he nodded, Detective Park returned with a monitor.
“This is the computer monitor found in the missing person’s room.”

“What? Why do you have that? You didn’t take it out of the room, did you?” The chief raised his voice, finding this absurd, but when he noticed something, he was stunned. “Wait, Detective Park, how is the monitor still on?”
“...I have no idea.”

Letters were floating on the monitor’s black background, even though the cords connecting it to the main console, and even the power line, were not plugged in. It was even being updated with a sound as they spoke.
Beep, beep, beep.
[The coming-of-age ceremony has been successfully completed.]
[New equipment has been equipped.]
[Your Total Item Level has increased by +12.]
[Bjorn Yandel]
What were these letters that kept showing up on the screen?
“Chief, I looked into it a bit, and...there have been similar cases abroad.”
“Abroad?”
There was still no way for them to know for sure.
[The labyrinth is closed. You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
The darkness faded away and the light got brighter. As I habitually tilted my head upward, I could see the cloudy sky, as usual. I let out a long breath.
...I made it back alive this time too.

Actually, to say I had just made it back alive was not exactly true. I had lived each day in a state of anxiety, thinking something had to happen soon, but as a result, nothing had happened, and twice in a row at that.
Hmm, I really thought something was going to happen this time.

To be honest, I was still stunned. Our previous expedition had gone too smoothly. Thanks to a good starting point, we arrived at the Rock Desert via the second-floor portal connected to the Gnome District in only nine hours. I didn’t get any portal achievements because someone had already passed through it. However, there were a variety of rank-nine monsters such as gnome mutants and kobolds in the area, and various rank-eight ones, including stone golems.
[You have defeated a Corrupted Gnome. EXP +1]
[You have defeated a Kobold Shield Soldier. EXP +1]
[You have defeated a Stone Golem. EXP +2]
[You have defeated a Megalith Soldier. EXP +2]
[You have defeated a Sandman...]
Even though we hunted all kinds of monsters at my request, we were able to climb up to the third floor on the fourth day.
It was the same on the way to the Witch’s Forest.

On the eighth day, without any problems, we reached the center of the Witch’s Forest. The number of plunderers we encountered along the way? Not a single one. After entering the fourth floor, Tower of Heavens, we had no encounters with adventurers at all.
[The ordeal has been completed. You have chosen the Stairs of Courage.]

Time for the official hunt. We continued to climb the stairs and battle monsters. All the creatures that appeared on the third-floor Pilgrim’s Path rushed out in random groups up here, and once every three days, we encountered a rank-six monster.
[You have defeated a Vitol. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Lizardman Scout. EXP +2]
[You have defeated a Dullahan. EXP +3]
[You have defeated the Queen Banshee. EXP +3]
[You have defeated an Ilatrek. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Dragoon. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Living Armor...]

We spent twenty-three days in the labyrinth until the fourth floor closed. The rank-six monsters I’d been so worried about? Perhaps because it was my first time battling them, there were times when I made several mistakes, but thanks to my sudden increase in combat power, I was able to defeat them all without major issues. The experience points began piling up that way.
It’s not called the Tower of Training for nothing.

All of the monsters that appeared on the third floor appeared there as well. There were also rank-six monsters, but only the ones that spawned in that area. These battles hadn’t been enough for me to reach level four, though. Anyway, as a result of focusing only on hunting...
“Dwalkie?”
“S-So... if we each take a share, that’ll be about 720,000 stones.”
“It’s 780,000 stones.”
“Huh? Bjorn, what are you talking about?”
“Uh, uh.... now that I’ve double-checked my calculations, Bjorn is right.”
“What!?”

Each person was allocated 780,000 stones. That was thanks to the Mimic’s passive skill, Greed, which increased the drop rate of mana stones by 30 percent. Otherwise, our payout would have been around six hundred thousand stones.
“Um, it’s definitely not a small number... but it still feels a little lacking. Is it just me?”
“Somehow... I feel the same.”
“Hahaha! That’s only natural since we’ve been earning so much more lately! Now that I think about it, Bjorn, it seems that your ridiculous luck has come to an end.”

I didn’t know about luck, but as we hadn’t faced any hardships on this quest, our income was low as well. Even though plunderers were fucking annoying, they each wore gear. In the end, that earned a lot more money than mining mana stones.
...Somehow, I made less money than when I first entered the labyrinth.

I thought I could see why those bastard plunderers didn’t die out. It was easier to catch people than rank-six monsters, and they were worth a lot more money too. So they had no choice but to follow people like moths—even more so if they were efficiency freaks.
Let’s not be too disappointed. In fact, everything up until now has just been exceptional circumstances, and this is normal.

As I thought about the game, I barely managed to shake off my disappointment. With the cost of consumables and various other costs of living in the city, it was only natural to not see a sizeable income in the beginning. That was the reason why most newbies didn’t even have one million stones and failed to survive past the first or second year, getting executed for not paying taxes.
...Even getting to the fourth floor within a few months is ridiculously fast in the first place.

That was what I told myself as I busied myself back in the city. I met occasionally with my other party members to plan for the next quest and visited the tower every week to fulfill my research agreement with Raven.
This time, she said, “Hmm, there’s already only four more left.”
“So, when can I meet that senior of yours?”
“Ah, there’s been a bit of a problem. If it’s okay with you, I want to postpone that until next month...”
“...Sure.”

Training, library, socializing, and information gathering. This really was the first time I had ever had such peaceful days. As a result, I was so nervous that my hands and feet were shaking, but until the moment I entered the labyrinth again, no evil spirit hunters, Hanses, or anyone else approached me. So I thought something might happen in the labyrinth this time around.
In the end, though, nothing happened.

Passing through the Goblin Forest on our way up to the third floor, catching some extra monsters that we hadn’t been able to before thanks to that, and finally leveling up while spending time on the fourth floor—those were the only differences from our last expedition.
“Bjorn! What are you thinking so harrrd about? Let’s go.” I was roused from my thoughts by Missha tugging on my waist. “Snap out of it. If we’rrre late, we’ll have to wait a long time.”

No, we wouldn’t. Maybe if we were still rank-nine nobodies, but rank-six adventurers had an entirely different mana stone checkpoint and our wait time was less than half of theirs. The officials there were also much more polite.
“Well then, let’s go! Hahaha!”
Soon after, we each went through the checkpoint and gathered in one place. Then we quickly finished distributing the loot.
“Each person should take 790,000 stones.”
“Bjorn? Is that right?” At Missha’s question, Dwalkie’s pupils flickered. What kind of wizard was that weak with numbers?
“I do not know, either. If he says it’s right, I’m sure it is,” I answered.

This time the calculations were correct, so we proceeded without issue. As a result, 790,000 stones were deposited into my pocket. Was this a dog-eat-dog world after all? As easy as this adventure was, our pay was the same as last time.
“Everyone go home and rest today, and we’ll have a drink together tomorrow to celebrate our return!” Hikurod suggested.
“Sure.”

As soon as we finished distributing the loot, we disbanded and headed home. But what was this? Today, my room felt dirty and cramped. It seemed like just yesterday I had been delighted that my lodgings had gotten bigger and there was a window.
Slump.

Even after washing up and lying in bed, things didn’t feel real. Usually, I felt like every part of my body was alive. A sudden thought popped into my head. How long would it take to move to a place like that other inn with earnings like this?
My progress has pretty much stalled recently too.
As this peaceful period continued, the impatience within me increased in size as well. I could only laugh.
...I’m forgetting how lucky I am.

The first day I woke up in this body, I had mapped out a plan for the next few years, maybe even a lifetime. However, thanks to several coincidences, it was now possible for me to move that timeline up by at least two or three years.
Don’t get impatient. This is working out well enough... Fuck, what am I thinking right now?
I slapped myself on the cheek, hard.
Slap!
Working out well enough? The truer that was, the more dangerous things got for me. There was no way that things would continue to go well in my life forever.
