Don’t forget, the shittiest things always come for you when you let your guard down. Evil spirit hunters? The Guild? Mozlan? Nobles? Who is it going to be this time? Or, maybe I’ll be fine until I next enter the labyrinth?
I recalled the traumatic experiences etched into my mind and tightened up my loosened screws.
No, no way.
I couldn’t stop. I had to get stronger. Only then would I be able to survive. Anyone who saw me might have thought I was being overly paranoid, but in reality, I had been this way since day one.
Always think the worst.
If I had to be a madman anyway, I wanted to be a madman who survived.
“Bjorrrn? Did something bad happen?”
“No. Why do you think that?”
“Your eyes look meaner than usual...” That was the first thing Missha said to me the next day.
I decided to loosen the screws just a tiny bit since I’d need at least that much free space in my brain to make rational decisions.
“Want to touch my earrrs?”
“...What?”

For a moment, I thought I might have misheard because I wasn’t paying attention, but I hadn’t. “Well... my brother once told me that touching my ears put him in a good mood. Even though that was a long time ago...”
What? That twerp said that? No matter how young he was at the time, I couldn’t imagine that.
“Ah, by the way, I was talking about my big brotherrr! My eldest brother still takes good care of me.”

Good care or not, what kind of pervert was he? This was why your home environment when you were young was so important. Look at her, at her genuinely pure and benevolent eyes. She probably didn’t even know what was wrong with what she just said.
“Missha, don’t tell anyone that. They may misunderstand your intentions and take advantage of you.”
If I didn’t already know that Missha’s ideal type was a skinny man, I might also have misunderstood and thought something ridiculous, like that she might be flirting with me.
“But you’rrre not just anyone.”
Tut, you and your backtalk.
“Just say okay.”
“...Okay. Anyway, if you don’t want to do that, do you want me to grrrill you some meat?”
“...If you do, I’ll eat it with gratitude.”

Just like that, breakfast became grilled pork. Even if you cooked it yourself, it was still meat and therefore expensive, but I was logical about it. If I ate this meat and grew even a little taller, that wouldn’t be a loss.
“Eat slowly! Let me eat some too!”
“...Didn’t you say you don’t like meat?”
“You insensitive barrrbarian!”
Despite the small snafu at the breakfast table, I started the day with a full stomach. I was supposed to meet the others in the evening. “I’m going out for a while.”
“Oh, then can I take a brrreak today too?”
“If you’re bored, go swing your swords. Seeing as you dropped one of them during our last quest, it seems you’re still not proficient in them.”
“That’s—! I just lacked strrrength!”
“Then you should exercise.”
“You muscular idiot!” Anyway, I left Missha and headed out. “Bye! Come back as late as possible!”
Well, I didn’t think she’d really spend her time practicing like I told her to, but that was her choice.
Step, step.
Walking hard with two powerful legs, I quickly arrived at my destination, the place I always visited when I had free time: the library.
“Looks like nothing happened to you.” Now that I knew her name and after everything that had happened, Ragna even spoke to me. Of course, she wasn’t that friendly.
“As you can see, nothing did. And you?”
“Of course.”

“Then, I’ll need your help again today.” After exchanging hellos, I was about to receive the Advanced Book Detection spell when, for some reason, Ragna hesitated. She probably didn’t know this, but that was a habit of hers whenever she had something on her mind. “If you have something to say, say it.”
“...How could you possibly know that?”
“By your eyes.”

My candid response appeared to have hurt her pride. Hearing this from a barbarian apparently put her in a bad mood. However, as an intellectual who also valued logic, she skipped the unnecessary chitchat and got to the main point. “I’m telling you in advance, this information is not confirmed. But since you’re an adventurer, I thought I should give you a warning.”

“A warning?” This was a word I hadn’t expected to hear at all and it suddenly woke me up. Even if she had ascertained that this information might not be 100 percent accurate, I was sure that someone with her personality wouldn’t be talking nonsense. “What is it? Tell me.”
At my prodding, Ragna carefully opened her mouth. “In the near future, there may be a dimensional collapse within the labyrinth.”
As soon as I heard that, I understandably had doubts. A dimensional collapse in the labyrinth would be a real disaster that would be extremely out of the ordinary.
No wonder it’s been so quiet these days...
Was this the reason why?

chapters.title: Chapter 90: Player (2)
paragraphs: Silence ensued.

After taking a moment to sort through my thoughts, I let out a small sigh out of habit. Seeing that, Ragna slowly blinked. “You’re calmer than I expected. I knew you wouldn’t believe me even if I told you.”
Actually, I sighed because what she just said was plausible. “Well, maybe it’s better to just not think about it. A dimensional collapse is a catastrophe that cannot be foreseen nor prevented.”
That was definitely true. Even in the game, a dimensional collapse always happened randomly. There were more times when it didn’t explode than times when it did.
It happened maybe once every one hundred rounds.

Of course, once it did explode, there was no disaster like it. I wasn’t sure about the second half of the labyrinth, where it could be dealt with to some extent, but in the first half, pressing the escape key and just restarting the game saved more time.
“So where did your information come from?” I calmly investigated just what I needed to. I had an intuition that this was the source of my anxiety, but I still couldn’t be sure.

“A wizard of the Tarutein school by the name of Shernal Fergang. Apparently, they’ve been studying dimensional collapses for quite some time now.” After giving me the name of a wizard, she said that she knew nothing more.
“I see. I’ll look into the rest. Anyway, thanks for the warning.”
As soon as I turned to the door, I heard a voice from behind me. “Are you... just leaving today?”
Well, since a new quest had appeared, shouldn’t I start with that?
As always, the pub was loud. The silver-haired elf who sat in the corner tapped the table with her index finger. It was a habit of hers that showed up when she was troubled.

In the last three months, her kind, pretty little sister Erwen had changed. Not only did she ask for help with the training she hated so much, but she pushed herself to the limit in a way that seemed to suggest she thought sleeping was a waste of time. She had also become sharper. Not so much with Daria, who shared her blood, but the way she spoke, her eyes, and her actions when dealing with other people were completely different from before.
Still, it’s not a bad change, so I’m glad...

Excessive ambition and a wariness of others? As an adventurer whose fate was to enter the labyrinth, these were welcome personality traits. In fact, thanks to that, Erwen had been able to achieve a lot of growth. She had succeeded in contracting the Four Great Spirits and also succeeded in building her strength by enlightening three of them.

That wasn’t all. Her archery skills, martial arts, and dagger-based melee combat improved by the day. To be honest, it was getting to the point that Daria was wondering how this talent hadn’t manifested before now. However, what made her sigh was the cause of the change.
How long can I hide this?

It had been the death of a barbarian whom she called Mister and had been emotionally attached to. In reality, however, it was ridiculous to call it a death since he was actually alive and well, with a reputation as Little Balkan.
Should I tell her before it’s too late?

When Daria first heard the news, she was astonished. Then she grew anxious. She now thought it was just a matter of time before she got caught. But Erwen, who had been confining herself to her room every day and devoting herself to training, still had not heard the news.
“Did you guys hear? I heard that Jet-Black Sword might become a disciple of Swordmaster!”
“Huh, where did you hear such strange news? Swordmaster, that dignified man, would not accept a mere adventurer as an apprentice.”
Sitting alone in a corner of the pub, Daria grew relieved as she overheard the conversations of the adventurers around her.
The rumors are slowly fading now.

The stories once heard throughout the entire city had been buried under new ones. It had rattled her a bit when news of the barbarian spread through the taverns again—how he had exorcised an evil spirit and assassinated a priestess of Karui—but even all of that was almost gone now.
Yes, let’s leave things like this.

Soon, Daria made up her mind. Actually, this wasn’t something to even worry about. As someone who had chosen to live as an adventurer, when would there ever be another opportunity for Erwen to grow like this?
“Hey, elf lady. If you’re here alone—”
“Get lost if you don’t want a hole in the middle of your forehead.”

Pushing away an approaching drunkard, Daria left the tavern. She had visited this place wondering if the barbarian had done something else and become a hot topic again, but she decided not to come anymore.
Knock, knock.
When she returned home, she knocked on her sister’s door. There was no answer. She slipped the key in, wondering if Erwen had fallen asleep on the floor.
Click.
The door unlocked and opened with a squeak. Soon, she saw her younger sister. Her eyes were closed in meditation while she summoned all Four Great Spirits.

“Must...” Judging by the slight movement in her lips, it appeared she was muttering something. Daria silently approached and heard her more clearly. “Must get stronger. Must get stronger. Must get stronger. Then I won’t lose anything. I can have it all...” She was repeating the same words over and over as if to brainwash herself.
“Erwen?” Daria hurriedly woke her sister from her trance.
Surprisingly, Erwen’s expression was calm. “Oh, you’re here?”
“You... Are you okay?”
“Okay?”
“You... were muttering something to yourself—”

“Huh? I was just speaking to the spirits.” That obviously hadn’t been a conversation she would have with the spirits, but Daria pursed her lips as she was ordered to leave. “I’m training right now, can you come back later?”
“Sure...”

Daria left the room helplessly. She headed back to her bedroom and thought about what had just happened. This was the kind of thing that couldn’t be dismissed as zeal or dedication. It was almost like an obsession. It hadn’t been this bad after that incident ten years ago.
What’s the problem? That barbarian couldn’t have been that important.
Daria stiffened when she remembered the biggest change as of late.
Ah, maybe it’s because she absorbed that essence?

Daria pulled out a book from the shelf. She had purchased it at a fairly high price from the guild a while ago. The Compilation of Low Rank Essences contained information on all essences between ranks seven and nine. First, she read up on the essence Erwen had absorbed during their last trip.
Where is Carnivaro?
It was a monster that only appeared in the Witch’s Forest, but out of luck, she had gotten the essence in the process of saving an adventurer who was being chased out of the forest by one.
Ah, I found it.
As she turned the pages of the book, she read the text while summoning a fire spirit for light.
Carnivaro: Rank 7
Agility (Medium), Dark Resistance (Low), Endurance (Low), Accuracy (Medium), Sixth Sense (Low), Hearing (Medium), Obsession (High)
*Increased agility and accuracy when moving
*Mana Mine (Red)
*Hound (Blue)
*Chasing Arrow (Green)
As she thoroughly examined the contents, she froze at one particular part. “Obsession... is high?” She suddenly felt a sense of deja vu and checked the essence Erwen had absorbed three months ago.
Iron Hill Chaser: Rank 8
Strength (Low), Physical Resistance (Low), Leg Strength (Low), Jumping Power (Medium), Ground Resistance (Low), Cognitive Interference (Low), Agility (Medium), Obsession (Medium)
*Increased penetration during a successful surprise attack
*Piercing Arrow (Red)
*Terrain Eruption (Blue)
*Weakness Detection (Yellow)
What... is this?
There was Obsession again, and medium at that.
Could this one also...?
She even read up on the very first essence that her younger sister had absorbed. It was just as she feared.
Goblin Archer: Rank 9
Flexibility (Low), Smell (Low), Poison Tolerance (Low), Cognition (Low), Cognitive Interference (Low), Accuracy (Low), Vision (Low), Agility (Low), Obsession (Low)
*Inflicts a paralyzing poison when using a bow weapon
*Thief Step
Even here, there was Obsession. Now Daria could piece together the situation in her mind. Erwen’s obsession with power was all because of this stat.
So what do I do?
She couldn’t just use money to erase one of the essences that had been absorbed, but her heart was too heavy to just leave things like this.
If she consumes another essence to replace it... I’ll make her erase it then.

After much deliberation, she reached a conclusion. However, after she quickly washed up and lay in bed, she was faced with a new question. If Erwen found out that the barbarian was alive before then, where would her obsession direct itself?

Ten days had passed since I had heard the news of the dimensional collapse. However, was this a baseless rumor, a fact, or the delusions of someone who thought it was true? Although I kept myself quite busy looking for answers, I didn’t achieve much.

“Shernal Fergang?” Raven, who always helped me when I went to visit with a question, didn’t have anything for me this time. “Even if you ask me to meet them, I’ve never heard that name before. The Tarutein school doesn’t interact with mine in the first place.”
“...I see.”
“Anyway, when you come next week, leave the whole day free. The winner has been decided by a lottery.”
“Winner?”
“Did you forget? In exchange for looking into that piece of paper, you agreed to help my seniors with their research, right?”
No, I remember that. I just didn’t know you were going to draw lots. Dang, now I’m getting worried...
I’d never had luck with draws in my life. Anyway, after that, I tried various things to find the wizard called Shernal Fergang, but all of my attempts failed. Meanwhile, rumors began to circulate.

“Bjorn! Did you hearrr?! They say there’s going to be a dimensional collapse soon!” After meeting up with some of her old party members, Missha came back and kicked up a fuss. If she knew, that meant the news had already spread. In fact, when I headed to the tavern in the evening, everyone was talking about the dimensional collapse.
But the problem is, no one knows who the source is.
Whose mouth was this information coming from? And on what grounds? Without those details, everyone was fostering anxiety and inflating rumors.
This... is strange.

I felt an odd sense of dissonance. In order for news to be widely known like this, shouldn’t there be a plausible basis for it? By now, many stories had been offered up as evidence by gossip, but there was none of that at first.
Is someone deliberately stoking rumors?
Having been keeping a close eye on the situation from the start, I came to that conclusion. Of course, it was just a theory, but no matter how I looked at it, the current situation was strange.
Whew, I think there’s really something behind all this.

It was stifling. I wanted to learn about the information exchanging hands from a more discreet place than a bar, but the reality of my situation was too difficult to surmount. How would a barbarian who had built a reputation for fighting alone get information like that?
If it weren’t for Ragna in the first place, I wouldn’t have even heard the name Shernal Fergang.

Soon, I made up my mind. In my hand was the letter from the Ghost Busters and the accompanying pill. For the sake of thorough anonymity, I had originally intended to take it after at least three months, but...
I can move it up a month or so.
I put the pill in my mouth and swallowed it.
[You have consumed GB-027.]

There was no getting immediately dragged into the spiritual world. According to the information I had learned from Raven and found in the secret library Ragna had given me access to, the meeting was held at midnight on the fifteenth of every month.
I just have to wait three days.
Time flew by, and the moment I had been waiting for finally arrived. It felt as if my mind was moving away from my body.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn to a specific world.]

When I woke up, there was a computer in front of me in a pure white space reminiscent of the universe itself. It would probably have been difficult for me to even recognize where up and down were if it wasn’t for the machine sitting there.
What’s this now?

This was a completely different introduction than I had expected, but I slowly took a step forward to where the computer was. The feeling of moving was unlike any I’d ever felt before, like riding a robot and using controls to make it walk forward. As I stumbled toward the computer, I checked the monitor, which was turned on.
[Please enter the password.]
A short sentence was set on a black DOS screen. I entered the password without much thought.
[Rafdonia’s king, Motherfucker.]
The PS in that letter didn’t just mean postscript.

chapters.title: Chapter 91: Player (3)
paragraphs: It had been five months since I had woken up in this world. Counting the days I had spent in the labyrinth, that time felt much longer. A lot had happened since then: killing a person and monsters for the first time, and doing many other savage things besides that in order to survive. However, the nature of modern man was unchanging.
Tap, tap, tap!
As soon as the password was entered, my pinky finger naturally pressed the enter key. Then I noticed something and stiffened.
This is... my body?

This was not the rough, thick hand of a barbarian, much less the broad-shouldered body of a warrior covered in boulder-like muscles. It was the body of Hansu Lee, from his 5′7″ height to his average weight and soft skin. The moment I realized this, it felt like the ground beneath me disappeared and my body was sucked into another place.
“Oh, fuck!”
When I came to, my surroundings were dark. That wasn’t that strange because I’d experienced the same thing many times in the labyrinth, but...
Click.

With the sound of a switch, the area around me was lit up by a bright light. Surprisingly, I was in my room, the room of Hansu Lee, where I had enjoyed playing games until I got brought into this world.
...So, what am I supposed to do?

First, I examined my surroundings: bookshelf, computer, and slightly yellowed bed. When I left the room and inspected the living room, kitchen, and even the bathroom, everything was just as I remembered.
Oh, then maybe this is also...?

I hurriedly opened the refrigerator. For some reason, the inside was filled with only chilled cans of cola. I wondered what kind of realism this was supposed to be, but I didn’t think too hard about it. After all, how was I supposed to resist this?
Click, chiii!

Just listening to the sound made me feel refreshed. I could put up with everything else, but I had missed this so much. I quickly poured the soda into my mouth in case it disappeared right before my eyes.
Goddamn it.

I couldn’t taste it. There was no aching sensation that made my throat feel like it was being split in two either—just a tasteless, odorless liquid running down my throat. I couldn’t hide my disappointment.
Ding dong!

The doorbell rang. When I checked the intercom, there was a white woman with blonde hair standing there. I was sure this wasn’t some religious missionary. I was about to say, “Who are you?” in my usual tone when I realized that would be a mistake and opened my mouth again, figuring that they may be able to infer that I was a barbarian by the way I talked. “Can I help you?”
But why does it feel so awkward?
I was just speaking normally, but it felt like a thorn was growing in my throat. Before long, an answer came back over the intercom.
“I am Soul Queen, and I serve as a guide for the Ghost Busters. Is it okay if I come in?”
Hmm, I didn’t know it was this kind of system. I quickly opened the door before I ended up on their bad side. But what was this? “Um, why are you going through the wall?”
“Oh, was this the wall? It all just looks like white space to me.”
Was she talking about the space I saw earlier? They did say this was a spiritual world. There must be some mysterious rules at play here.
“You’re amazing,” the woman exclaimed in admiration as I gave her rough directions to the living room. “Normally, no matter how faint it is, I should still be able to see the outline.”
“Outline?”
“I mean of this place. Mister...”
“You can call me whatever you want.”

“...If you say so.” True to the contents of the letter, which guaranteed anonymity, the woman did not express any disappointment despite my firm refusal. “Anyway, this space is the embodiment of your imagination, the place your inner spirit first brings to mind. It is usually the place you feel most psychologically comfortable.”
“So?”
“It is usually visible to others. Sometimes there are people with strong defense mechanisms, but I could still see outlines in those cases...” The woman looked at me in fascination.
I couldn’t tell if it was curiosity or wariness, but I decided to start out by pointing out the contradiction. “Then how did you ring the doorbell earlier? I thought you couldn’t see it?”
“It seems to have manifested that way to you. I didn’t ring any bells. As soon as I got here, all I did was call for you. Does that make sense?”
To be honest, I got the gist of what she was saying, but at the same time, I understood nothing at all. I just smiled awkwardly and nodded. “Thanks for your kind explanation.”
“That’s a relief. In truth, this is a concept that is difficult for even wizards to understand, so I am at a loss as to how to explain it each time.”

Anyway, since she had introduced herself as a guide, I felt comfortable asking the things I was curious about. “Oh, what happens if someone enters the password wrong?” I had been able to deduce it, but there must have been some people who couldn’t.

“Oh, that? Nothing, really. It’s just a trick of the eye. There are very few people who guess the password before I get there in the first place. Whether you enter the password or not, I have to come and confirm who you are anyway.”

For reference, the process of confirming someone was a player was simple. Apparently, she could tell just by looking. I briefly wondered if she had a special ability, but then I realized what she meant when I noticed my current appearance. I was wearing a navy blue suit that fit snugly against my body—clothes my ex-girlfriend bought me to celebrate getting a job.
Is it obvious from the clothes...?
True, as soon as I saw this woman, I realized that she was a modern human too, so it must have been the same for her.
“Wow, you really are quick. The differences between players and NPCs are obvious from there.”
“NPCs?”

“It’s a slang term for locals. Anyway, the difference between the two is not just the clothes—you can also clearly tell when you enter this space. This is the first time I haven’t seen anything, though.”
“You mean you can tell by the room.”
“That’s right. Rockstar posters are not going to be hung in NPCs’ rooms, you know?”
I understood. With this kind of verification process, it would be impossible for locals—I mean, NPCs—to conceal their identities to get in here.
“Then did I pass?”
“Of course.”

I was worried since she couldn’t see the room because of my defense mechanisms, but the woman nodded without hesitation. Seeing that made me realize something. Apart from clothes, tone of voice, expression, and this imaginary space, there must be another clear way to identify NPCs.
They probably aren’t telling me for security reasons.
“Now, then... You are now officially a member of the Ghost Busters.”
“By the way, who came up with the name ‘Ghost Busters?’”
“Oh. You’ll see. I’m sure you’re wondering what kind of lame name that is, right? I pleaded with them to choose a different name, but...”
Uh, I thought it was a very sensible name.
“Everyone always starts with that question,” she sighed.

I nodded awkwardly. I couldn’t agree that it was a lame name, but I could pretend to. Being able to read the room and act accordingly had always been my main specialty. “It’s... definitely an unusual name.”

“Right? Oh, where was I...” Soon, the woman returned to the topic at hand and continued. “Ah, we can no longer use the method of forcibly killing NPCs who sneak in by separating them from their souls. Instead, we can ban you from being called here again, so if you have time, be sure to familiarize yourself with the rules.”
Afterward, the woman started to explain the basics of using the Ghost Busters community. “Is there a computer here? If there is, walk toward it. If there isn’t, you’ll have to imagine one up.”
“There is.”
“That saves time. Go ahead and turn it on.”
When I turned on the computer as instructed, a window popped up instead of the familiar OS screen.
“Oh, one second. Your code is...”
When I entered the code the woman told me, the screen changed to a page where I could assign myself a nickname.
“The nickname you choose here is final. Once you make it, you can never change it, so make sure you choose carefully.”
Hmm, what should I choose?
As I was wondering this, the woman offered a word of advice. “You used Stone Iven, right? Most people use their nicknames from that board. That’s how I chose my nickname of Soul Queen.”

Fittingly for a community forum for a failed game, less than thirty messages were posted on Stone Iven’s main discussion board a day. Still, anyone who’d played this game had used it at least once, including me.
It’s not my real name anyway, so I can probably use my username from that, right?
I typed in the nickname and clicked enter.
[This nickname cannot be used.]
“Oh, I see someone is already using that nickname.”
What? Someone is using it?
I didn’t get it, but I just changed the spelling a bit. When she saw what I chose, the woman gave me a strange smile. “Haha, I guess you’re a fan?”
Fan? What does that mean?

Before I could ask, she continued explaining how to use the community going forward. “Okay then, I’ve told you pretty much everything you need to know. I’ll leave you to explore. If you have any problems, please contact us directly!”
Soon after, the woman with the nickname Soul Queen left, and I was once again left alone in the room. After completing the onboarding process, I surfed through the community board without problems.
[For men in their 20s and 30s]
[American Union]
[Beastpeople Welcome]
[Wizardry]
[Hangout]
There were several chat rooms that were currently active. If I clicked and entered any of these, would I be able to chat with the people inside? This was a futuristic yet fantastical system.
Some rooms have level restrictions or passwords.
In order to get used to this place, I chose a random room and decided to enter as a test.
[Freshmen Room]
This was a special room that only those who had joined the community within the past year could enter. I chose it because I figured there would be many people like me in it.
Click-click.
The moment I double-clicked, a bright light emanated from the monitor. Like the day I woke up in the body of a barbarian mid-game, I was in an empty lot when I came to.
Crackle!
A bonfire raged in the center of the lot like a campfire. Fifteen people were standing near it—all men. True, I wondered how many girls would play this hardcore game.
“Oh, you’re new!”

Their eyes converged on me as I entered. White, Asian, Black—our races were more diverse than I’d expected, but having lived in a different world for several months, I felt a sense of kinship at the fact we all came from the same place. The same probably went for them.
“Which country are you from?”
“Ah, Korea.”
“I see! Welcome!”
I took a quick look around and studied my surroundings. There were no racist gazes at all, and the atmosphere was one that was purely welcoming to newcomers.
Are those their nicknames above their head?

Translucent letters floated above everyone’s heads. Just then, a black man dressed in a neat suit came up to me and started talking to me. “A little empty, right? We don’t even get points to decorate. I’m Darkman, the room leader. Could you make your nickname public and briefly introduce yourself?”
“My nickname?”
“It looks like this is your first time in this room. All you have to do is think about it. In this community, there’s power in clear cognition and thoughts.”
Clear cognition and thoughts... maybe I just had to think of it like an active skill?
Disclose nickname.
As I inwardly muttered that, people’s eyes shifted to my head. It appeared they could see my nickname now. “Hello. I’m Elfnunna.”
The moment I revealed my nickname, thinking it was an anonymous space anyway, dead silence fell in the lot.
“Elfnuna?!”
“Holy—the guy who made the stat summary?”
“Uh... wasn’t that someone from the game company?”
“So you were Korean! I knew it!”
“Excuse me! Is it true? Are you really him?”
After a moment, for some reason, a commotion broke out. However, before even trying to grasp the situation, I quietly exhaled a long breath.
Sigh.
What was this?

chapters.title: Chapter 92: Player (4)
paragraphs: The empty lot was whipped into a frenzy by the reveal of my nickname. I closed my eyes for a moment and took stock of the situation. First, the “Elfnuna” they were talking about. They were right, that was the nickname I used to use. I had come up with it without much thought because my character was an elf at the time.
I did write a stat summary...

Was it about three years into the game? It felt like a waste to keep the information I had compiled to myself after working so hard for it, so I posted it on the bulletin board partly to have a place to save it. As was fitting for a flop game, I remembered that the views did not exceed a hundred for a whole year.
Why is everyone looking at me like a rare item?
Come to think of it, that woman from earlier asked if I was a fan too. Why? The last time I used that community must have been five years ago.
...Have I become famous in that time?
Whatever the cause, I came to a conclusion: I had become famous. The reason why could be discovered later. I had collected enough clues to deal with it for now.

“Ah, there’s been a misunderstanding.” After taking about three seconds to figure out what was going on, I smiled brightly and waved my hand. “I am a fan of theirs. If you read my nickname carefully, you will see. It’s not Elfnuna, but Elfnunna. Nunna.” It was a relief that I’d had to spell it differently because of that other user. Unnecessary attention was not my thing.
“Oh, I see...”
“The nicknames are different.”
At my words, the men read my nickname again.
“It’s Elfnunna! Not Elfnuna.”
“What, it was a dupe?”
“Of course. Although I had my hopes up because he said he was Korean...”
They soon let out a collective breath of apparent disappointment. Maybe because they felt they’d been deceived, some people gave me slightly unkind looks.

“Haha, that can happen if you’re a fan!” The room leader, Darkman, stepped forward to mediate and explained the rules that had to be adhered to in the room. I think he said everyone had to be spoken to with honorifics. Aside from being expelled if you stirred up aggro, there wasn’t much to keep in mind.
“Then I’ll be on my way, so you guys can talk freely,” Darkman said. “You can leave whenever you want.”
The vibe of welcoming the newcomer was short-lived. Everyone went back to their original places and conversed amongst themselves.
As I was wondering where to visit next, a white man approached me. He was a player with the nickname Pinkguy. “How long has it been for you?”
“Oh, it’s been one year for me.”
Actually, it had been five months, but I figured it would be strange to say that I joined the community so early. However, the answer that came back was unexpected.
“Really? I guess you received your letter quite late?”
“Sorry?”
“Well, only a few people receive letters after gaining fame. Most others get them in the early days when their identity is obvious.”
“I see...”
“Considering you received the letter late, I guess you’re a good actor. I started off as a human and received the letter while I was transporting luggage.”
“Ah, I see...”
“Anyway, if it’s been a year, it will only have been about seventy days there... You probably know a lot about what’s going on these days. How are things there?”
I didn’t know if there were any incidents worth mentioning, but... “Seventy... days?” I asked like I’d misheard. I clearly said it had been one year. Why had that become seventy days?
Pinkguy continued with an apologetic look on his face. “Oh, if this is your first time, you wouldn’t know that, either. The flow of time is different between the two worlds.”
“Different?”
“Yes. One month on Earth is about five months here.”
Simply put, it was a time ratio of 1:5. As soon as I heard it, I felt strange.
It’s only been a month?
I was glad that less time had passed than I’d expected, but I wondered if I’d even been reported missing. No one would come looking for me other than my company.
After that, as I continued to talk with Pinkguy, I learned various things.
“How to get back? Well. There are many theories... But I heard nothing’s been confirmed yet.”
Even the players who had gotten here much earlier than me couldn’t figure out how to return. The founder of Ghost Busters was apparently a twenty-year longtime player.
“Isn’t it amazing that they managed to clear this game five years ago?”
“That’s true.”

The more new information I heard, the more defeated I felt, almost like my pride as a pro at this game was crumbling. No matter what, in the end, wasn’t everyone here an expert who had reached the Gate of the Abyss before me?
Even if they look stupid on the outside, they’re actually all amazing people—

“So which mode did you beat the game on?” Huh? Which mode? When I looked at him like I didn’t know what he was talking about, he added, “I’m sure it wasn’t the original version. You probably beat the remake version, right? Which mode was it?”
I still don’t understand what you mean... remake?
“The pirated version? You know, the game file where you can adjust the XP and drop rates that was posted on the Stone Iven discussion board five years ago.”
Uh... That’s a thing?
Pinkguy spoke, his pride obvious. “Oh, I’m not bragging, but I beat it on Times Fifty.”

How could there be so many people who beat this game? This was the moment when that long-standing question of mine was finally answered. Dungeon and Stone was a game whose final boss room I had only been able to enter after grinding for ten years of my life. As I had been playing it, I couldn’t help but wonder how a game of this difficulty could exist.
You can set the game up to a hundred times the maximum XP and a hundred times the drop rate?

What kind of scam was that? Until now, I didn’t even know the maximum level you could reach in the game was thirty. Even if you caught all the monsters that came out of the labyrinth, level eleven was the upper limit.
Wait a minute, if the max level is thirty, does that mean I could have fed thirty essences to my character?

To be honest, I couldn’t even imagine it. That meant you wouldn’t have to give any of them up and could just stuff your character with all of them. I felt like an idiot for trying to figure out what the best combination was by considering the compatibility of each essence. Based on what I was hearing, it seemed that even Rifts, which were the core of developing a character, could be opened whenever the user wanted.
If the drop rate is a hundred times its usual rate, Numbers Items would just fall from the sky.

Thirty essences and a super overpowered character armed with all kinds of treasures. If five of those characters banded together to form a party? The elder dragon that had taken me hundreds of attempts to take down, or the Lord of Destruction, or even the Leviathan could be killed with the touch of a finger.
“So which mode did you use to beat it?” Pinkguy asked again.
“...Times Fifty. Like you.”
“Oh, I see. Wasn’t it hard?”
Hard, my ass. Under those conditions, I was confident I could clear it in one try, no matter if a dimensional collapse or whatever the fuck kind of event occurred.
But it would be bad if I said that out loud.

As soon as I gained fame and an evil spirit hunter came to find me, I realized that excessive attention was poison. It was foolish to take risks by being showy. I had decided not to stand out and to learn just what I needed to know.
“Which mode did the person who created this place use?”
“Oh, him? Don’t be shocked, but he cleared it at Times Fifteen. He must have been able to do it because he was an original user.”
“Times Fifteen... I see.”

I figured this should be shocking, so I pretended to be surprised. Pinkguy said that the average player completed the game in Times Sixty to Times Eighty mode. After hearing that, the conversation of those laughing and chatting a little ways away began to fill my ears.
“Haha, what a ridiculous world! I’ve never even entered a Rift. In the game, it was just a click.”
“Ugh, right? If entering the Rift is this hard, how are we meant to get to the last floor?”
“I heard that the game had a lot of easter eggs, so I should have looked into it.”

Players were complaining while comparing the modded version they had played with the reality they were in. That, at least, was understandable, because this was a real-life version with a higher level of difficulty than the original.

A profound despondency crept in. Thinking these were more experienced players who beat the game before me, I had consoled myself by resolving to learn from them instead of belittling them. But this was, well, a joke.
“Elfnunna?”
“Oh, sorry. I got distracted...”

After that, I continued to chat with Pinkguy for a while. In doing so, I learned things that were common sense that any normal player should know and a lot more about how this community worked. However, one other question on my mind was also answered.
A remake... So, the game started to become popular again as the modded version circulated, and my nickname became famous as well.
In many ways, the conversation with Pinkguy was useful. It was kind of fun too.
“Ugh, if I could eat just one box of pizza right now, I could die happy... Do you have anything you want to eat?”
“Coke and beef soup.”
“Beef soup? What kind of food is that?”
“It is the most efficient food I have ever eaten.”

How long had it been since I had had a conversation like this? After conversing with a few other people, I left the Freshmen Room. At the end, Pinkguy asked if he could add me as a friend, and I politely declined. He was obviously a nice guy, but I didn’t want to be friends with him. He treated me too nicely.
Anyway, I think I know everything I need to know.
After returning to the room with the computer, I read through bulletin boards and notices and crammed more random information into my head. But now it was time to fulfill my purpose here.
I should start learning about the dimensional collapse.

Typing on the keyboard, I checked the timer on the bottom right. What was initially twelve hours had now been reduced to seven. I had to hurry because this space would close when the time was up, even if I didn’t manually log out.
[Exchange]

Using the mouse, I opened the Exchange page. It provided a service where information or goods could be purchased with Ghost Points, or GP. In other words, it was possible to obtain goods or purchase rare items using GP.
As expected, it would be better not to touch that.

I decided to avoid using that particular feature as much as possible, since in the case of goods, the exchange had to be done in real life. No matter how complicated the intermediary system may be, and even if the system seemed quite safe, in the end, there would be inevitable contact with me as a barbarian.
[Current GP: 0]

Therefore, I also passed on the option to use real money to purchase GP. Of course, I needed GP to buy information about dimensional collapses, but that wasn’t a big problem. I could be self-sufficient here.
Click-click.
Moving the mouse, I added the [Information] filter to the items in the Exchange and changed the category to [Purchase Request]. Then, countless questions popped up.
[20 GP] Is there any easy way to get to the second floor?
[100–500 GP] I’m developing a melee skill, but I want to know a strong training method from the start.
For easy questions, the amount of GP offered as a reward was small.
[7000 GP] I would like to know the special events that happen on each step of the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.
[2800 GP] Looking to learn exactly how the passive skill Lord of Dragon is used.
In the case of more in-depth questions, the reward was greater, so I sorted them in descending order of price. That was more efficient.
[70000 GP] Buying Lord of the First Floor clear strategy. Trolls will be ignored.
[69000 GP] Only people who know more about Skull Island on the sixth floor message me.
The Lord of the First Floor?
[You have requested a one-on-one conversation with TacitRonin.]
[The exchange has been completed. Current GP: 70,000]
Skull Island, a hidden section of the sixth floor?
[You have requested a one-on-one conversation with Bro_78.]
[The exchange has been completed. Current GP: 139,000]
There was nothing I didn’t know about this game.

chapters.title: Chapter 93: Player (5)
paragraphs: “Did you properly collect the computer that was handed over to the police?”
“Yes sir. I’ve erased all traces of it as well as its memory, so there won’t be any news about it or anything like before.”

The old man nodded at the woman’s report and slowly read the paper on the desk, a document summarizing a man’s life. It didn’t take long for him to read the entire page. “He has strong bad luck, but that’s all.”

The woman nodded in agreement. The man’s life had so many twists and turns that even that was an understatement, but other than that, there was nothing special about it. His workplace was normal, his academic background was normal, and his interpersonal relationships were normal. Everything about him was normal except for this game.
“I just don’t understand.”
That’s what makes him seem even more special.

Auril Gavis’ legacy, Dungeon and Stone, was a flop. This was a conclusion that had been reached after lengthy deliberation. No one disagreed that it captured that world better than any other work, but it was impossible to beat, which was why it had been scrapped five years ago.
“...But to think someone who has cleared it would show up at this point. Could it be that it wasn’t a failure?”

The old man, who had been muttering, shook his head. Didn’t everyone agree that even if someone managed to clear it, there was no guarantee that this project would produce better results than the others? His conviction was not wrong.
“However... I am a little curious how this turned out.”
Then, the old man opened his laptop and entered the name of the only player to clear his legacy, which had been deemed impossible: Hansu Lee.
[Current GP: 139,000]

After selling information about the Lord of the First Floor and Skull Island, I did not sell anymore. There were two reasons for this. First, each case took more time than I had expected because the buyers were suspicious of me due to my lack of transaction history. They believed me after a few questions, and both bought the information, but it would be more correct to say that they trusted this community rather than me, since you couldn’t reenter this place if you dared to scam someone and get kicked out.
The second reason was more important than time.
If I sell information all the time, I’m sure someone will notice.

As the saying went, an angular stone was bound to get hit by the chisel. No matter who it was from, I wanted to reduce the attention I attracted as much as possible. I didn’t really need GP at the moment, anyway.
Ding!
Just then, a message arrived.
[From: Ghost Master]

I had seen this nickname a few times in notices. In other words, this was a message from the community moderator. My heart pounded like I’d been caught red-handed, but when I opened it, the message itself was nothing special.
[Elfnunna’s transaction history now exceeds 10. EXP +10. Your member rank has been adjusted: Deadman -> Goblin.]

It was an automatic notice that got sent out as your community rank went up. It was not like there was a significant benefit to having a higher rank, but there was nothing bad about it going up since there were some rooms with rank restrictions.
Type.
I posted a question using the GP I had earned. The amount of GP I offered as compensation was ten thousand to one hundred thousand, showing a willingness to pay more for valuable information.
[Your Exchange request has been posted.]

After posting, I spent some time exploring the community in the same way I might surf the web. Looking at the jokes and humorous posts on the general bulletin board, I felt as if I had returned to the real world. It was in the middle of doing this that I learned the going rate of GP.
Two million stones for one hundred thousand points?
My current amount of GP was about 140,000.
Shit, then did I just earn 2.8 million stones by answering two questions?
This was jaw-dropping at first, but when I thought about it, this wasn’t so implausible. It wasn’t like the information I sold hadn’t been valuable.
I can sit on a pile of money just by selling information here.
All of a sudden, I even wondered if there was a reason to go into the labyrinth anymore. However, to me, the act of exchanging GP for money still felt dangerous.
Let’s not think weird thoughts. Let’s not get greedy and instead just use this as a place to earn information.
Therefore, I set up a new iron rule and made up my mind. As I was looking around the rest of the community board, I heard another notification.
Ding!
When I checked the monitor, I saw a new message had arrived.
[Elfnunalove requested a one-on-one chat.]
Elfnunalove was an uncomfortable nickname for me, but I pressed “accept” without hesitation. There was only one thing they could be contacting me about.
I was worried, but someone showed up before the end of the day.
Finally, an information seller appeared.
I was in a library with an old-fashioned interior and was a little surprised when I smelled the faint scent of books.
It’s very well decorated. How much did they spend on this?

This was on a whole other level from the vacant lot that was the background of the Freshmen Room, or the desolate field that became my base whenever I started a conversation. It must have cost a sizable amount of GP. However, I didn’t think it was just an act of indulgence.
There’s no doubt that this alone builds some level of trust...
After taking a brief look around, I spotted a white man and greeted him. “Hello.”
“Hello. You are Elfnunna, correct? Take a seat.” As soon as I sat down, the man immediately got to the point. “You want to know about a mage named Shernal Fergang, from the Tarutein School?”

“That’s right.” If I had only asked about the dimensional collapse phenomenon, it would have been difficult for me to discern whether the other person was lying or not. But if I asked about Shernal Fergang, that was a different story—as was evidenced here. “To be exact, I want to know more about what he’s done recently.”
“Hmm, is it because of the rumors about the dimensional collapse?”

The man immediately associated the name with the idea of dimensional collapse. The reliability of the information that followed further increased. So, I decided to be open with my questions. “Are those rumors true?”

The man asked for twenty thousand GP in exchange for an answer, and after I accepted, he continued talking. “If you’re asking if those words came out of his mouth, yes, that’s right. But if you’re asking how true the rumors are... Actually, they’re not.”
“What do you mean?”
The man took a moment to organize his thoughts, then said, tone matter-of-fact, “It means that there won’t be a dimensional collapse.”
“What grounds do you have for saying that?”
“I’m afraid those grounds include high-ranking figures and political tensions...” To put it simply, he meant that this was information too valuable for twenty thousand GP.
“I’ll pay twenty thousand GP more.”

“If you want to know that much...” The man nodded and smoothly continued. “The Tarutein School focuses on the study of labyrinths, especially dimensional magic. And the master wanted to do an experiment.”
“Experiment...?”
“I can’t go into details, but it’s not a dangerous experiment. There just need to be fewer adventurers than usual in the labyrinth.”

That was why the Tarutein School had spread a rumor from the mouth of one of its wizards into the city. They deemed that if rumors of a dimensional collapse went around, it would deter paranoid adventurers from entering.
“...Is it okay for you to just tell me all of this?”

“I’m not ‘just’ telling you, but selling it for GP.” That confident response left me with nothing more to say. The man chuckled and continued. “What do I care about all of this in the first place? It’s not like I’m the master of that school. Besides, sooner or later the royal family will post an official statement denying the rumors.”
“...The royal family will?”
“What, do you think the Rafdonian royal family will sit still? Fewer adventurers entering means the mana stone supply will also decrease.”

Hmm, that was true. After hearing the brief explanation that followed, everything made sense. The reasons he’d effortlessly provided were also convincing. It didn’t seem like he was lying, either. When I said that I would complete the transaction here and send the remaining twenty thousand GP separately, the man shook his head.
“Come to think of it, it’s all right. You seem to be a fan of theirs too.”

Twenty thousand GP was four hundred thousand stones, but he was saying he wouldn’t accept it just because I was a fan of a specific user? Although I just said thank you for now, curiosity blossomed inside of me. How long had this person been here? Five years? Ten? However long it had been, one thing was clear: he had established himself in this world firmly enough that four hundred thousand stones was nothing to him.
Which is probably why he knows information that I wasn’t able to learn for days no matter how hard I tried.

Once again, I was determined not to forget where I came from. I didn’t care which mode he had cleared—Times Fifteen, Times Twenty, Times Thirty, or Times One Hundred. This was not a game. It was a ruthless reality ruled by a savage provision that only the strong survived.
Little Balkan or not... I’m still just a newbie here.

I realized that compared to the road I’d walked thus far, I had a much longer way still left to go. But I wondered why—when only a moment ago I had been determined not to forget where I came from—I was now smirking.
This is fun.

The places that the man who’d bought the strategy for the Lord of the First Floor, the woman who wanted information on Skull Island, and the man standing in front of me would have reached over the years—it never once occurred to me that I couldn’t get there myself.
It started as a black DOS screen. After a brief loading period, a beep sounded and a log filled with the selected player’s actions filled the monitor.
Beep, beep, beep!
The log’s rules were simple. Only actions were recorded.
[The coming-of-age ceremony has been successfully completed.]
[New equipment has been equipped.]
[You have stepped on a goblin trap.]

Choosing a shield at the coming-of-age ceremony, a harrowing entrance into the labyrinth, stepping on a goblin trap and crawling on the floor bleeding for hours, killing someone on the first day, becoming friends with an elf met by chance, and reaching the second floor on the first try with no weapon...
“Crazy bastard.”

The more he read the log, the more speechless the old man became. All the more so because this was a log in which only actions were recorded. Every action had a rationale. The old man, who had seen many player logs, could see the reasoning behind the decisions that Hansu must have made in the moment. He had to because they were the right choices. And so, Hansu took action like he was playing a game. It was truly amazing. How many players had made illogical decisions in the disconnect between game and reality?
“...How many of them reached the second floor on the first try?”
“To my knowledge, 117 players.”
That was quite a large number, but the old man was sure that of the 117 players, there was no one who’d had to deal with such bad starting conditions.
He’s a fascinating one.
The old man, who continued scrolling down the journal, froze at one point.
[Vampire Duke Cambormere has been slain. EXP +5]
[Higher-class mutant bonus. EXP +1]
[Guardian kill bonus. EXP +3]
[The Essence of the Vampire Guardian is seeping into your...]
Before he knew it, the log on the screen had arrived at recent activity.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 3 (New +1)
Physique: 155 (New +75)
Spirit: 90 (New +44)
Special Ability: 115 (New +85)
Item Level: 98 (New -104)
General Combat Power: 381.5 (New +204)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7, Vampire (Guardian) - Rank 5 (New)]

Character stats that would have been hard to believe even for a player of several years had all been attained just two months after waking up in an unfamiliar body. Of course, some luck must have played a role.
However, if it was possible to do all this through pure luck, there would have been at least one similar case before.

Statistics were like that. As sample sizes and data accumulated, the number of special cases decreased, and unclear information became solid facts. Surprisingly, the probabilities derived from this process had almost no margin of error depending on how big the sample size got. In other words, the variable of luck was extremely insignificant in statistics.

However, there were some cases like this too, where the impossible became possible, like zero becoming one. An anomaly that existed beyond the realm of statistics, where even the reason for its existence could not be determined because there were simply no other samples for comparison.
Click, click.
The old man raised the player’s Observe rank to maximum.
[An abnormal amount of progress has been made. The administrator will now be monitoring your character.]

He suddenly thought back to when everyone had agreed that this was a failure. The last words he had offered were, “I only judged the situation logically. Even if it’s just one person throughout my entire life, if I can send them through to full completion, that would result in a higher potential.”
Maybe he was right.

chapters.title: Chapter 94: Barbarian Trophy (1)
paragraphs: Light slowly returned to my darkened vision.
This is my room.
Bjorn Yandel’s room at the inn, not Hansu Lee’s. When I checked my watch, exactly twelve seconds had passed since I had been taken to that place.
Is one hour there equal to one second here?
The time difference itself was not surprising, because the labyrinth was like that too. No matter how many days I spent there, when I returned to the city, it was always noon the next day.
I don’t know what the mechanism behind it is, but it’s definitely a convenient phenomenon.

Still, I should be careful. Put another way, this meant that I would be defenseless for up to twelve seconds every month. Of course, in case of an emergency, I could just log out and leave, so there was no problem... but what if there wasn’t an emergency? What if something happened in those twelve seconds, in the blink of an eye?
It will be hard to react appropriately.

Well, I had no intention of not using the community just for that reason. I was just filing the danger away in my unconscious mind. That way, when something really did happen, I could react as quickly as possible.
“Whew...”
I stretched and let out a long sigh. There was a slight fatigue lingering around me, not physical but mental exhaustion.
True, I’ve technically been awake for twelve hours.

I closed my eyes, thinking that if someone had a habit of sleeping in only on this particular day, it would be reasonable to suspect them of being a player. I didn’t want to go to sleep right away, though; I needed time to organize my thoughts.
It’s good that I joined early.

The Ghost Busters was a place made and operated with more professionalism than I expected. There was no doubt that it acted as the source of information I wanted, either. Thanks to it, I had been able to obtain information about the alleged dimensional collapse.
A rumor, huh?

That was a good thing. That much was clear. However, for some reason, my feelings of dismay and anxiety grew simultaneously. When I first heard about the dimensional collapse, I thought that this was the reason I was feeling the way I was. But if it wasn’t, what the hell was about to happen?
...I’ll have to be more careful.
With that thought in mind, I fell asleep. Time passed like that and then it was morning the next day. The day to keep my promise to Baron Martoin had dawned.
“Good luck! Tell me everrrything when you get back!” Missha saw me off and I walked out into the street. And after changing wagons many times at the platform, I arrived at Baron Martoin’s home.
“Come here. There is no time.”
As soon as I entered the spacious mansion, I was dragged into a splendid room where I changed my clothes. Apparently, my appearance was not savage enough for me to attend the count’s banquet today.
Goddamn it.
Being a barbarian, you experienced these kinds of things. Normally, I would have been more dressed up for the opposite reason.
“Oh my gosh, look at those muscles...”

With the help of the maid, I took off the breastplate and shirt I was wearing and put shoulder guards on my bare body, with thorns on one side and a design in the shape of a beast’s skull on the other.
“C-Could you please lower yourself a little?”
“Sure.”

The maid stood on a stool and whimpered as she wrapped something around my stomach, a championship belt that was thicker than the length of even my hand. Fuck, why did I have to wear something like this? One breastplate could protect my entire torso.
“Please raise your arm.”

Even after that, various decorative pieces of equipment focused on intimidation rather than defense were added to my body against my will. The weight distribution was likewise arbitrary, to the point that each movement was uncomfortable, and the maids untied my hair, so it kept flopping down and obstructing my sight.
But I can see what it is they’re going for.

When I looked in the mirror, there stood a barbarian warrior who probably drank dragon blood and ate ogre meat as a snack. I suddenly had a thought: so what if it lacked protection or practicality? Damn, if I walked around like this, everyone would be busy peeing themselves and running away. In that sense, the intimidation factor was great. I named it (True) Barbarian Mode, but I guess it still wasn’t enough to them.
“Tsk.” A goatee-bearded twig looked at me with disapproval. This bastard’s name was... He actually hadn’t told me yet.
“What’s your name?”
At my question, the steward frowned and answered tersely, like he didn’t want to converse with me. “I’m assisting the—”
“Okay, Steward.”
“...Tsk, ignorant barbarian.”

The steward was a guy I didn’t like for many reasons. They say those who grow up with less turn out to be worse. From beginning to end, he spoke to me in a tone that suggested he was speaking to someone lower than him. Even the baron didn’t treat me like that.
Who does he think he is? In the end, he’s still a commoner.

Even as I inwardly grumbled, I followed the steward’s instructions and put insoles in my shoes, plate boots weighing fifteen pounds due to excessive ornamentation. The uncomfortable things were truly agonizing.
“Now you’re worth looking at. You were too short before,” said the short son of a bitch.
Ha... it’s just one day.

No wonder he had agreed to pay me a million stones for one day. It was genuinely the cost of the real labor I was doing. In any case, by the time the unscrupulous steward explained the details about the order of events and where I was to stand while the baron spoke to others, it was already time to leave.
“Time is up. Let’s go.”
I left the palace-like room and headed for the main gates. A luxurious carriage was already waiting. Perhaps the baron, whom I hadn’t seen all day today, was riding in it.
“Why are you standing there? Your place is over there.”
I stood at the head of the carriage procession. Were they planning on following my lead?
“This is an important mission, so make sure to keep your eyes forward and keep your posture...” The steward jerk kept nagging me right up until we left, clearly not trusting me.
“Depart!” Before long, a knight on horseback right behind me shouted, raising a flag, and I led the procession at a moderate pace.
Trudge, trudge.

As we left the main gate, I could see the wide, paved streets in a single glance. These were the streets of Karnon, the royal capital of District One, which I would not have otherwise been able to enter with my status. Even the shops were grand, and the attire of the people around me was equally aristocratic. The Imperial Palace, which I couldn’t even see from where I lived, was peeking out in the distance.
I have to find a way into this place quickly in order to use the Sky Auction House...
The steward told me to only look in front of me, but I didn’t waste this opportunity to look around. Perhaps that was why...

“Halt!” As I took a wrong turn, the procession stopped at once. The steward bastard ran up to me, red in the face, and shouted something, but I confidently picked at my ears. Whose idea was it to leave this to a barbarian?

The distance from the baron’s mansion to the count’s, where the banquet was being held today, was about four miles. Although I had experience crawling a greater distance than that on three limbs, I had overlooked the fact that I was wearing a full set of equipment that was the very definition of irrational.
Goddamn it.
Sweat poured down my back. If it hadn’t been for the insoles that had been shoved in at the end, this wouldn’t have been this hard.
“Baron Martoin has arrived!”

As I was cursing out the steward, we arrived at our destination. As soon as the front gates to the count’s estate opened, curious eyes flew toward us from all over the place. They must have been nobles who wouldn’t have been satisfied with just any entertainment, but it seemed that this was their first time seeing a barbarian leading a carriage procession.
“Putting the barbarian up front, you must have been inspired by that story!”
“That created a great, intimidating atmosphere. It felt as if a giant was walking in.”
“Wow, Father, can we make an entrance like that next time?”

The nobility gathered in the outdoor hall where the banquet was being held and kicked things off by blurting out their impressions one by one. I guess the reactions were to his liking because when the baron stepped off his wagon, he burst out into a laugh I’d never heard him make before.

“This is the first time I’ve ever received so much attention just by standing here. When I return, I will give you generous compensation.” The baron was so pleased that he even promised me a bonus. “I’m going to greet the count, so you guys can enjoy the banquet in the meantime.”

Soon after, the baron entered the mansion accompanied only by a few retainers. Then, naturally, the knights scattered and mixed into the banquet. Only then did I notice that I had been left alone in this large banquet hall.
“Oh, look at the horns on that helmet. How scary!”
“It looks like it was modeled after the ancient devil Parseira!”

Suits, tuxedos, dresses with exposed backs, a knight’s armor boasting a white luster and precious metals that glimmered like the surface of the waves... and then there was me: the only one with the appearance of a savage. Was this some kind of zoo?
“Oh, it’s walking. I wonder where it’s going!”
Just by taking a single step, I heard the people around me burst into curious exclamations. I felt like the PTSD I thought I had overcome was about to come roaring back.

Just then, a man walked up to me. “Nice work.” It was a knight who had acted as a flag bearer in the row just behind me. “You really are a monster, wearing that and walking this far without rest.” The knight, who must have watched my hardships closer than anyone else, chuckled and patted my shoulder. “How about taking a seat with me over there until the baron returns?”

What was this? Was this man a god? “All right.” Soon after, I sat down in an empty seat with the knight. All kinds of delicacies surrounded me, but they didn’t pique my appetite. It must have been the same for the knight because he just sat there quenching his thirst with alcohol. I suddenly got curious and asked, “Is it okay that you’re not with them?”
“Even if I go over there, I won’t be welcome. I used to be an adventurer like you.”
No wonder he looked so forlorn. “I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel. What is your name?”
“I’m Carls Erimor.”

After exchanging brief introductions, we continued to converse. I had been able to tell from the beginning, but Carls was a pretty good guy. He was an adventurer, so we understood each other well, and even though he was a knight, he didn’t show their characteristic arrogance. That steward bastard should learn from this guy.
“What are you doing? Who told you to sit down?” The steward, who had entered the mansion with the baron, found me and came running toward me at once. He seemed displeased that I was resting.
“Look. No need for that. I told this fellow to take a break.”
When Carls stepped forward, the steward flinched and lowered his voice. “...Is that so? If you’re done resting, get up. What will people think if they see a barbarian sitting and resting?”
“...That he’s resting?”
“No, people will think you are weak. So get up. Regardless of your true nature, you must be an iron-blooded warrior today.”
At the steward’s prodding, I got up from my short break.
Yeah... just one day.

Didn’t I promise to become the baron’s trophy and main attraction? I was determined to thoroughly play my part. Of course, this was far from resignation. An iron-blooded warrior, a savage in this world whose fists came before the law, a barbarian. Yeah, if that was me...
“Behelaaah!”
As soon as I was done refocusing my mind, the shout erupted from my lips on its own.

“W-What are you doing?! Do you know how much it costs to customize the gear you are wearing today, or how pathetic you looked when you got lost earlier?” The steward, who was making these insulting remarks, frowned.

The sight made me wonder why I had been putting up with this. Was I not a barbarian? “I just felt like doing it!” In that spirit, I picked up a piece of meat next to me in a barbarian manner. Was it a tomahawk? The meat was attached to a bone that almost looked like a handle. “Yes, this is what I wanted.”
As I tore through the meat with bare hands like a savage, the steward nodded. However, the expression on his face hardened when he saw me chewing on the bone too.
To that, I responded respectfully while maintaining my dignity as a barbarian warrior. “Steward, I want to crush your skull.”
“...What?”

He would never have heard these kinds of words before in his entire life. Staring at the steward as he clearly doubted his hearing, I kindly offered an explanation. “I just feel like doing it for some reason!”
Crunch, crunch.
As I spoke, the bones of an unknown animal were being crushed in my mouth.
“Y-Your jokes go too far.”

“Joke?” When I cocked my head as if to ask what he meant by that, the steward’s complexion turned white. It seemed he had only just realized that I was a barbarian after all. “Did that sound like a joke to you?”
Barbarians were simple and ignorant, transparent about their feelings. Of course, the steward may have had no knowledge of barbarian physiology.
But if you’ve looked into my background, you’ll know what happened at the guild.

Of course, I had an explanation for what I’d done. At that time, I had no other choice. Except for looting, failure to pay taxes, and a few laws related to nobility, most things in this world could be sorted out with a fine. As long as you could prove that you were not a plunderer, you could handle the rest somehow. But that was something only I knew. To others, I must have just looked like a crazy bastard.
“...I have something I need to do, s-so I’ll be going. Y-You take a break.” The steward hurriedly fled with an uncomfortable look on his face, implying he really had looked into me.

Carls, who had been watching all of this unfold, laughed out loud. “Hahaha! I never knew that man could make that expression!” For some reason, my actions seemed to please him. “But are your teeth all right?”

“It’s okay. They’re quite tough.” Rather than an innate ability, this was a side effect of the increase in my Bone Strength stat. Anyway, for some reason, chewing on bones had given me an appetite, and I began to eat for real.
“Look at that!”
“Oh my, how barbaric!”

The noble ladies were looking at me like they were seeing a new species, but it didn’t matter anymore. Who cared if I looked barbaric? If I could ignore the humiliation, there would be no position more comfortable for me than this.
“Behelaaah!”
“Why are you screaming all of a sudden again?”
“Delicious!” The time of being hesitant in the face of all this elegance was over. I now began to enjoy the banquet in earnest.

chapters.title: Chapter 95: Barbarian Trophy (2)
paragraphs: I tore through meat and drank alcohol. My dirtied hands were roughly wiped off on the tablecloth. My reason for going this far was simple.
Regardless of what Baron Martoin wants, this will be beneficial for me too.

I was currently in the count’s banquet hall. Since this was a gathering of many people, it was best to behave like a barbarian. The more barbaric rumors accumulated, the more they would shield me when someone suspected that I was an evil spirit someday.
“Excuse me, can I touch your arm?”
“Do as you like.”
“Kyaaa! I really touched it!”
As I was enjoying the banquet, possessed by the spirit of a barbarian, curious nobles approached and started talking to me. It felt like working part-time as a mascot.
“Hey, can you scream one more time like before?”
“Behelahhh!”
“Hahaha, how superb!”

As I was demonstrating some professionalism befitting someone who’d been commissioned by the baron, more and more people gathered. There were also knights among them, a total of three, and all three had annoyed looks on their faces. It seemed they were jealous that everyone was paying attention to me and treating me favorably.
“They should call you little clown, not Little Balkan.”
“I heard he got his name in the first place because he’s small down there.”
“To go around farting like that... it seems that the pride of a warrior is a thing of the past.”
I pretended not to hear. Not only did they sound like apprentice knights who were only as strong as third-floor adventurers, but there was also nothing to be gained from causing a ruckus.

“Hahaha, have you been here this whole time?” As I was filling my stomach and appeasing the nobles, Baron Martoin returned. He looked around and smiled like he was really happy. “Sorry to break this up. I have someone I’d like to introduce him to, so I must take him away.”

The place the baron led me to was the banquet hall inside the mansion. The atmosphere was different from the outdoor space I had been in until just now. There, the band was playing merry tunes and young men and women were dancing in the gardens, but here?
Is this a meeting of real nobles?
The room was filled with quiet, soothing music. Those sitting at the tables and chatting looked elegant and gave off a dignified air.
“Come here.”

As I followed the baron, I studied my surroundings. About two hundred people were enjoying the banquet in the indoor hall. Most of them were direct blood relatives of the royal family, such as the young son of Baron Martoin, or had higher social status such as bank presidents or guild branch managers.
“Among the people I’m going to introduce you to from now on, there are many with a higher rank than me, so I’d like you to refrain from being rude as much as possible.”
Afterward, I followed the baron around to meet the titled nobles.
“Baron Martoin! Long time no s—who is your friend?”
“Perhaps you have heard of him, Viscount. He is the Little Balkan, a famous figure among the adventurers these days.”
“Aha, is this him? I’ve heard that name before. But how come he is here with you?”

Instead of answering the viscount’s question, the baron looked at me and winked. That meant it was time for me to hurry up and spit out the line I’d practiced. “When I was in trouble, the baron helped me. In return, I decided to protect him for the time being.”
“Hahaha! I envy you for getting to hear those words from such a strong-looking barbarian!”
“It’s nothing. I’ve said many times that it’s not necessary, but...” The baron trailed off and gave me another look.
“...A warrior never forgets a favor.”
“Ha! A true and honorable conviction. Did you say Bjorn, son of Yandel? I will remember your name.”

This kind of conversation unfolded twelve more times. There were only thirteen titled nobles in attendance, excluding the count who was hosting the banquet. Well, a titled aristocrat with even the slightest fief in this city had been a rarity in the game.
It turns out that I’ve become acquainted with the nobles now.

Originally, participating in such a banquet would only have been possible if my reputation level had been considerably higher, so I decided to be as careful as possible. I was not qualified to participate in this event, which also meant that I did not have the power to protect myself if I earned their disfavor.
“So, now that the greetings are over, you can take a break next to me until the count arrives.”
After finishing our rounds, I stood quietly by the baron and faithfully served as a trophy.

“...Tsk.” Was it because the baron was by my side, or because the warning from earlier worked? I wasn’t sure, but the steward just clicked his tongue and looked away whenever I met his eye and didn’t bother to nag me like before. Was this the life of a barbarian?
I should have done that way earlier.

Anyhow, things were rather cushy after that. Baron Martoin, a titled aristocrat, never got up first. Even if he stayed put, there were a lot of people who came up to him in order to introduce themselves, and I just had to entertain them whenever the baron wanted.
“Ooh!”
“As expected, the name of Little Balkan is not just for show, Baron!”
I did things like bending a prepared steel bar with my bare hands and arm wrestling. A good chunk of time passed by like that.
Then I saw a familiar face approaching through the crowd. “May the blessing of the twilight star be with you. Nice to meet you, Baron Martoin, and...”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

“Haha, my apologies, Sir Yandel, I am not great with names.” When I revealed my name, the paladin in white armor smiled kindly. He was the same man I’d met the other day after completing the commission in the sewer. Late at night, I’d brought Elisa Behenk’s body to him and was briefly acquainted with him. His name was...
“Do you know Captain Krovitz?”
Paal Krovitz. That was his name.
...Captain? This kid?

When I looked at the baron, surprised, the man scratched the back of his head as if embarrassed. “I’m unworthy, but I was lucky enough to be given the opportunity to serve as the captain of the Third Paladins.”
“I see...”

I was extremely shaken up. It hadn’t even occurred to me as a possibility because he had come so late at night for a chore like picking up a dead body, but the captain of the paladins? Didn’t that mean that he was a monster with more power than an eighth-floor adventurer?
“If you need a place to rest, please come visit our temple. As I said last time, the temple will never forget your achievements, Sir Yandel.”

Hmm, at the time, I had thought those were empty words. But since the man in charge was the one saying this, I’d have to make a visit someday. You never knew; even if it was impossible now, if I built a little more of a bond, he may even suggest a priest for the party.

In the middle of the conversation, the baron interjected in a coy tone. “Hmm, achievements? Captain Krovitz, what do you mean by that?” His eyes were full of curiosity. True, he probably had a hard time imagining what a barbarian could do for the order.

“Ah, it seems I didn’t tell you.” Krovitz looked at the people around him as well as the baron and then began to speak as if he was reading from a children’s storybook. To sum it up, it was nothing new, just the fact that I’d found the priestess of Karui in the labyrinth, not to mention that I’d located and punished the wicked woman while she was hiding in the sewer. That was the end of the story, but Krovitz was quite well-spoken.
“Ha! I’ve heard that name before. A worshipper of the evil god appeared a while ago. But to think this man was the one who got rid of them.”
“Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel. They say he was born with the destiny of a hero...”
When the story ended, everyone around him, led by the baron, let out exclamations.

“This is a divine connection blessed by the stars. The temple values our relationship with Sir Yandel as well. Oh, I have somewhere I must be, so...” Krovitz, who peppered me with flattery until the very end, announced he had business to attend to and left.
The baron’s eyes softened a little more. “You are a much greater man than I thought.”
[Your reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your reputation has increased by +10.]
“Oh, I’ll be darned.”
“Captain Krovitz, who is well known for being a good judge of character, said that, so it’s clear that he’s going to be a notable figure in the future.”
While the story Krovitz had told was spreading among the nobles without me realizing, the count appeared and the banquet officially began.
“Count Ferdehilt has arrived!”

Receiving everyone’s attention, a dignified-looking man descended a central staircase that led to the second floor. Beside him was his daughter, a girl in her late teens. In a way, she was the main character of this banquet.
“Thank you all for coming here for my daughter Arabella’s birthday. We have prepared a lot of entertainment, so I hope you set aside your worries today and enjoy yourselves!”

The music changed dynamically at the count’s words, and the static banquet hall began to liven up. Quiet voices grew louder, and laughter that was far from dignified erupted here and there. I was sure it was in part due to the alcohol kicking in, since everyone had been sipping on drinks up to this point.
“Would you give me the honor of allowing me to kiss the back of your hand, my lady?”
The young people each held the hand of the sex they liked and headed out to dance. The older ones sat down and engaged in vulgar conversation over the jesters’ show.

“Let’s get going.” The baron rose from his seat. His face seemed tense. When I asked where we were going, he answered, “You haven’t met the count yet, have you?
