When I saw him earlier, I talked about you, and he said he must meet you.” The baron’s expression was completely different from when he had gone around greeting the titled nobles earlier as if he was now dealing with a direct superior.
The count, huh?

I started to get nervous as well, but the count I met was actually a pretty upbeat guy and he was very kind to me. “Haha! It is you! I wanted to see you in person.” When I went to say hello, the count stood up and even asked to shake my hand.

“Nice to meet you!” Even as I responded to the handshake in a barbarian way, I couldn’t shake the thought that something was strange. Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel. I was definitely aware of my recent fame.
But is all that enough for the count to be acting like this?

I was not so sure about that. At least, I didn’t think so. After all, there were less than a hundred nobles with the rank of count in this vast city. He was incomparable to the district chief of the Adventurers’ Guild I’d met before, truly a man of omnipotent power. Even in the game, events from counts or higher-level magnates did not occur until the latter half.

“You’re taller than I thought. You should be called Big Balkan, not Little. Haha!” A man like that was complimenting me like he wanted to please me. “By the way, what is that weapon? I heard you normally use a mace.” He continued to subtly mention things that he wouldn’t have known unless he had been paying attention to me.
Why is that?

I couldn’t understand it. If he wanted, I was sure he could make even the top seventh-and eighth-floor adventurers, whose fame didn’t even compare to mine, do whatever he wanted. Why was he interested in me?
And making me fucking anxious...
Some might be happy an important guy like the count was paying attention to them, but not me, especially not at a troubling time when something might explode in the near future.
...If something happens, what could it be?

It was just when my innate anxiety naturally started assuming the worst about the count that he clapped, looked at me, and suggested something unexpected. “Seeing you so suddenly gives me an interesting idea. In a little while, there will be a showdown between the apprentice knights. Wouldn’t you like to participate in it too?”
“...Wouldn’t the knights not like that?”
“I will solve that problem. How about it?”
“I’ll think about it...” I didn’t give a definitive answer. It would be less troublesome to pass along my decision through the baron later, rather than rejecting him to his face.
“Hmm, if you say so. Do as you please.”

The count stopped paying attention to me at that point. Then he began conversing with the baron about this and that, a shallow conversation in which they praised each other’s wives and children and blessed the futures of their families.
“Haha, this conversation was so enjoyable that I kept you for a long time. You should go and enjoy the banquet as well,” offered the count.
“Yes, my lord.”
Afterward, when I left the count’s side and returned to my original table, the baron immediately spoke to me. “So... what are you going to do?”
“About what?”
“The showdown!”
Of course. I withheld my answer, saying I was thinking about it. I was going to refuse, but I judged that this would seem more sincere.
“Think carefully. You never know if this opportunity will be of help to you later.”

As expected, the baron tried to persuade me by talking about the benefits of participating in the tournament, saying the prize for even just participating was two million stones, and that it was a good opportunity to make a name for myself. The count was even giving away a 7000s numbered item as a prize for winning the tournament.
“What? Garphas’s necklace?”

“...Why are you so surprised? Do you know of it?” The baron, who wasn’t an adventurer, cocked his head at my reaction. That was rather fortunate. If he had been an adventurer, my reaction would have been even more questionable. “Hmm, I heard from Sir Elta that it’s not that attractive of a prize.”

No. 7777, Garphas’s Necklace, only dropped in the Rifts on the fifth floor, and the probability of it doing so was atrocious, making it extremely difficult to obtain. In many ways, it was an item similar to the Ring of the Frost Spirit, a lower numbered item with a strong personality but that wasn’t of great value to adventurers. Because of that, even though it was rare, it was treated kind of as a bust.
But it even holds a hidden special event.
I didn’t have to think it over for long. An ominous feeling that something was about to happen? My determination to sit back for a while?
Smirk.

So what? I should carefully calculate the gains and losses to be had in everything I did, but that didn’t mean I should cower like an idiot and shy away from what must be done. That was called putting the cart before the horse.
“I’ll do it.”
“Huh? What did you just say?”
“The tournament the count spoke of, I will enter it.”

chapters.title: Chapter 96: Barbarian Trophy (3)
paragraphs: “Haha! Hot-blooded like a barbarian!” The baron let out a loud laugh at my decision.

He could only laugh like that because he knew nothing about barbarians. Barbarians were not utterly fearless beings. Just as Ainar had once said, “We were born warriors. If we don’t fight, we die.” They just carried that fear with them and pushed forward because that was what they had to do. My decision here was just more of the same. As peaceful as things had been lately, something big might happen eventually.
I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t worried...

But so what? Choosing to flee from an uncertain future out of fear would only lead to ruin. How was I supposed to go into the labyrinth and make logical decisions with that mindset? If I had acted like that when I first got here, I wouldn’t even be alive right now.

While I sat quietly and organized my thoughts, the baron returned a short while later. “I just spoke with the count. He’s very pleased.” It seemed he was also quite thrilled with my decision. “Oh, but is that necklace really that important?”
The question implied he thought that the necklace had had a big influence on my decision. I didn’t deny it. “Numbered items sell for good money.”
“Hmm... if you say so.” Judging by his expression, the baron seemed to assume there must have been another reason for my decision, but he didn’t pry. He just asked, “By the way, how strong are you?”
“Huh?”
“Judging by your ambitions, you are already thinking you’ll win. Are you really that confident?”

I chuckled. How strong was I? There were too many monsters in this world for me to confidently answer that question. However... Applying the term “apprentice knight,” an opponent equivalent to a third-floor adventurer, to my strength was a different story.
“To be honest, I’m not hoping for much. But if you lose too quickly, I’ll lose face—”
“Oh, don’t worry about that,” I answered, cutting the baron off. I had never been worried about that part. “Ten seconds is enough.”
“Enough?”
“I can crack just about anyone’s skull in that time,” I clarified to the confused baron. This was my sincere, no-exaggeration-added truth.
“E-Eek!” I guess my sincerity worked because the steward, whose eyes happened to meet mine, freaked out.
Just like in the Middle Ages, knights were the very definition of strength here. Of course, that was only true if their title didn’t include the word “apprentice.”
What kind of knight can’t use an aura?

What made people fear knights was their aura. With 90 percent Defense and 90 percent Mana Resistance, auras were cheat abilities that allowed their users to cut down virtually anything and thoroughly develop expert swordsmanship. Those two things alone could create a monster.
But leveling up in a single leap and buying tons of high-rank essences with your enormous wealth? No wonder the people with power stayed in power in human society.

In a world where different otherworldly races prevailed and magic existed, a knight was a spear and shield that protected vested interests. Considering that the maximum level that could be raised with a leap was five, a proper knight could slice through several high-level adventurers on their own. That was just how well-suited knights were to warfare.
However, when it comes to apprentices, they’re at most level three. Even their essences won’t be anything higher than seventh rank.
And that was assuming the worst. No noble would invest that much in a knight who couldn’t even use an aura yet.
Actually, the tournament isn’t the real problem...

It was what came next that bothered me. Not only was there the count’s excessive interest to worry about but if some savage suddenly became the victor, there was a good chance that the powers that be would be displeased with me. However, since I had made my decision already, I didn’t have the luxury to have regrets.
For now, let’s just focus on this.

As I was quietly spending time in the corner thanks to the baron’s benevolence, deciding to worry about what would happen after I won the championship later, three guys in knightly armor approached me.
“You said something cocky earlier.”
I recognized all of them. Even if it had been a passing encounter, there was no way I could forget those faces when I had just seen them earlier that day.
“Ten seconds is enough? Has playing a clown all day like the thick barbarian you are made you forget your place?”
First, this guy. When I was entertaining the nobles at the outdoor banquet, he had ridiculed me and called me Little Clown.

As I sat there staring at his rat-like front teeth, the baton was passed to the guy next to him. “Barbarian, you’ll have to pray desperately to your ancestors that you don’t end up facing me in the tournament. I’ll slit your throat immediately. And it won’t even take ten seconds.” I didn’t know his name because he didn’t say it, but he was the one who had made his stupidity evident by claiming that the pride of a warrior was a thing of the past. Judging by what he was saying, he seemed to be a fan of bluffing too.
“If I face you—”

Just as the baton was about to pass to the next runner, I quickly got up and interrupted. I was usually careful to avoid speaking as much as possible, but at this point, I had no choice but to be blunt. “Do you all have something seriously wrong with your heads?” That was me being euphemistic. If I asked, Are you idiots? instead, I might end up being charged with contempt of nobility at some point.
“W-What?”
“Do you think ganging up on me like cowards will scare me? Not even a three-year-old warrior in my tribe would do that!”
“...Cowards? You dare insult—”
“If not, then what is this? Did you suddenly get braver now that the baron is not here? What great honor you have!”
“Th-that’s...!”

The fact was that they didn’t have the courage to approach me when the baron was next to me. When I pointed that out, the three little piglets just blinked at me like goldfish. However, since I was an unprejudiced barbarian, I didn’t think they had speech impediments. They were probably just shocked because they had no idea I would be so loud about exposing their ugliness.

“That’s why I’m asking! I heard knights are a proud people! But taking advantage of your superior numbers to do something so childish to another participant? There must be something wrong with your heads!”
The next cry accurately summed up the bastards’ actions. “S-Stop! Shut your mouth!”

The three little piglets now looked desperate. That made sense. Ugliness or not, if this interaction continued on like this, they were going to be known as the ones who had had a barbarian accuse them of being mentally unsound. But it seemed they’d decided that more conversation would only make things worse.
“...Just you wait!” The three piglets stormed off angrily. Maybe it was because they were locals, but their cheesy parting line was like icing on the cake.
Still, their ambitions were admirable so I responded in kind. “Anyway, don’t worry too much! Next time we see each other, I will definitely get rid of the problem with your heads!”
Did my sincere sentiments reach them? It was hard to tell just by looking at their backs as they ran away.
Incident or not, the banquet, which was filled with various delights, soon reached its climax. In other words, the time had come for the count’s tournament to begin.
“The barbarian we saw earlier is participating. Isn’t that exciting?”
“Hmm, I don’t know. He’s still just an adventurer. He may have earned fame recently, but I heard his career isn’t even a year old yet.”

The tournament venue was the lawn of the outdoor banquet hall. The area was already packed with people, and some nobles even sat down on the terrace on the second floor of the mansion to get a good look.
As I sat quietly in a provided tent, the baron started talking to me like a coach. “Are you nervous?”
“No.”

“Whew, truly a heart made of steel. I can’t even contain my excitement.” I didn’t know about that compliment, but it was clear that he was excited seeing as he promised me yet another bonus I didn’t even ask for. “If you win, I’ll give you another million stones. So do your best. My reputation now rests on your shoulders.”
“I will try!” Thanks to this unexpected financial incentive, a wave of enthusiasm suddenly surged over me.
“Sir Saboin of the House of Baron Serpia and Sir Arpheon of the House of Viscount Henslvania, please take your positions!”
A while later, the first match began. The two knights recited the dueling code of honor on stage and then wielded their swords with great flair, drawing cheers from the crowd.
This is the kind of thing that reminds you what a barbaric world this is.

As I secretly slipped out of the tent to watch the duel, I felt strange. It was almost like seeing the Roman Colosseum in person. In fact, there wasn’t much of a difference at all. There was a rule that said to avoid killing your opponent if at all possible, but conversely, that also meant there was no problem even if you did.
Well, it’d be more strange to have no casualties while fighting with a real sword.

Despite the fact that it was just the first match, the two knights were waging a bloody duel in front of the fired-up crowd. As intense as it was, the moment the winner and loser were decided was just as dramatic.
“The winner is Sir Arpheon of the House of Viscount Henslvania!”

The other knight’s sword hand was completely cut off, and the match was decided. Of course, the wounded knight’s hand was quickly reattached by a priest, but the blood that had gushed out like a fountain remained a stark decoration on the stage.
“Ahhh!”
Listening to the enthusiastic cheers of the crowd, I felt it again. This was a different world, and I’d already begun to belong here.
“Does seeing blood excite you too?”
Well, I didn’t know about that. But I did know that it was my turn next.
“Sir Sylvania of the House of Baron Hessen, and from the House of Baron Martoin... Bjorn Yandel. Take your positions!”

As instructed by the host, I made my way through the crowd to the stage. At the same time, a knight was climbing up from the other side. What a coincidence. I didn’t know his name so I hadn’t been able to figure out this would happen from the tournament bracket.
“Haha, you seem surprised.”
I nodded slightly, conceding that point. To think one of the three piglets would be my opponent in the first match. What a surprise.
And it also happens to be the most annoying one.
Unbeknownst to me, the corners of my mouth curled upward. Because I had cut off the baton from being tossed, I didn’t end up hearing his whole deal, but how could I forget him?
“I heard he got his name in the first place because he’s small down there.”
This was the man who had spread that nonsense. A mere human.
Maybe that was a bit weird coming from me.
Before the duel began, the bastard recited a pledge, a conventional oath to take this duel seriously, fight with the honor of a knight, and not resort to dishonest tactics. It was my turn next.
“Behelaaah!” I skipped any wordy speeches and let out a savage cry.
The crowd’s frenzy intensified. “Ahhhhhh!”
The attention on me pissed him off even more. “How vulgar and crude,” he grumbled.
What, did you think a barbarian would be sophisticated?

Soon, under the moderator’s watchful eye, we approached each other and tapped our weapons together. The bastard held out a long sword. Instead of the mace I had left back at the baron’s, I held out a huge, double-bladed battle axe.
...I’m not used to sharp weapons.

It was unfortunate, but it shouldn’t be too different. I just had to wield it as usual, and the outcome would probably be the same. The only difference between the two weapons was whether they left a scratch or cut a limb off completely.
“Ha!” As the duel began, the bastard swiftly kicked off the ground and charged at me. It looked like he wanted to reverse the ten-second promise I made earlier.
Interesting.
I stepped back and positioned myself to observe the situation for now. Since this was my first real time encountering swordsmanship in a real battle, I was curious.
Whip!
Even though he was labeled an apprentice, he was still a knight, and his sword was quite sharp. “Die!”

It was like an advanced technique from a wuxia novel—a sword thrust with three accompanying illusions. For a moment, I wondered which of them was the real blade, but that thought was quickly discarded. If I couldn’t tell which was real, all I had to do was shut them all down at once.
I’ve become a true barbarian.
Raising the blade of the axe to the side, I swung as widely as possible. That alone was enough.
Clang!

The sword’s trajectory was diverted by the powerful blow, and the bastard began to lose his balance. However, he did not let go of his sword despite the shock. Although he must have been startled, he twisted his body and swung his sword at my neck in a connecting motion.
Certainly not someone to take lightly.
His attack gathered slight torque from the bottom like a tornado. His personality aside, I had to admit this was truly a brand of swordsmanship passed down through generations.
His weapon technique is several levels higher than mine.
All else being equal, I would definitely not be able to beat him. However, that wasn’t a huge problem.
“Behelaaah!”
This guy and I were not on the same level.
[You have used Wild Outburst. Your Threat Level is temporarily increased by x3, and your physical stats increase in proportion to that value.]
There was still a lot of time left before the ten seconds we agreed on were up.

chapters.title: Chapter 97: Barbarian Trophy (4)
paragraphs: When activated, Wild Outburst increased the user’s Threat Level stat. However, this threat level didn’t provoke people the same way it did monsters. Just as Dwalkie had once told me: “Ummm... i-it was a very strange feeling. It was like my mind knew that there was nothing dangerous, but my body was telling me that I should run...”
The timid shrank away in fear, but the brave, on the contrary, usually responded with competitiveness. So how about this guy?

“Ha!” The answer was the latter. He flinched at the shout I spat in his face, but soon came back to his senses and finished swinging his sword. If I’d had my shield in my left hand as usual, I could’ve just deflected it.
There won’t be much difference now, though.
It was the same either way. The body of a tank existed solely to block enemy attacks.
Slide.
I removed a hand from the axe and used it to follow the trajectory of the swinging sword. A dull thud followed.
Kagak!

A question formed in the eyes of the bastard who believed he had secured victory. I was sure he must have been curious. When would you ever hear that kind of sound coming from a sharp blade and a bare arm? His eyes started moving, seeking an answer, and soon reached their destination.
“Confused?”

At my question, he nodded blankly. Why had his sword cut through skin, but not bone? There were many reasons for that: bone strength, physical resistance, my innately large and tough skeleton, increased physical stats due to Wild Outburst, etcetera. It would have been more ridiculous if he had somehow managed to cut off my wrist in one fell swoop despite all that.
There’s no need for a wordy explanation.

Because I was a barbarian, this was enough: “You’re weak.” Immediately after blurting that out I realized how cheesy it was, but it had a noticeable effect. As if he had just received the greatest insult possible, he pulled out the sword stuck in my arm. That was a bad move.
Splash!
Fresh blood splattered everywhere as the blade was pulled out.
Chhhhhh!
The sounds that followed were ones of corrosion and a moan of pain.
“Aghhh! What a dirty trick—!”
What do you mean? I’m just standing here.

It was clear that there was indeed something wrong with his head, so I reached out and grabbed him by the neck. It’d be a headache if he ran away. As the blood was cut off from his brain, what’s-his-name started to writhe. This was already a done deal. One twist of the neck and he would die.
[You have removed your equipment. Your Total Item Level has decreased by -495.]
However, I set down the weapon in my hand. The reason for that was simple.
Kakakang!

According to the steward, this double-edged battle axe had been bought with a lot of money just for today. Plus, if I brought it down on this guy’s head, I wouldn’t be able to use “I had no intent to kill” as an excuse.
Also, I promised.
I made a promise to the three knights that the next time we met, I’d get rid of the problems in their heads.
Squeeze.
So, with a fist the size of a watermelon, I punched him in the temple with all my might.
Smack!
“Behelaaah!”
If there was a problem with someone’s head, it just had to be removed—yeah, a barbarian would definitely think that way.
Or not.
Silence: a state in which there was little to no sound in a certain area. That state currently characterized the count’s lawn.
It was a very unusual sight. In a place where so many people were gathered—in the middle of a party, no less—how could a crowd of hundreds create such total silence without a tacit agreement?
“W-Where is the priest!” The silence came to an end when a knight carried whatever-his-name-was out of the amphitheater with a half-crushed head.
I approached the referee. “Don’t you have to proclaim the winner?”
The referee looked startled by my question, but then shouted to the crowd, “Th-the winner is Bjorn Yandel of the House of Baron Martoin!”
At first, I wondered if he was discriminating against me for being a barbarian. However, judging by the reaction from the crowd that followed, it seemed that wasn’t the case.
“Woahhh!”
“That barbarian! He’s the best!”
“I’ve never seen such an exciting duel! How liberating!”
“But isn’t that knight dead?”
“I-It was too gruesome. Feel this. Can you feel my heart pounding?”
“U-Uh... I-I think so...”
“It’s not the first time someone has died in a duel. An injury like that can be treated by the priest.”
The response was noticeably more enthusiastic than the one after the first duel.
“Behelaaah!”

I released another shout for the crowd and then walked down the stage toward the tent. Not the one where the baron would be waiting, but the tent where whatever-his-name-was had been moved for treatment.
“Y-You! How dare you come here!” As soon as I entered the barracks, a howl of rage erupted from the remaining two of the three knights.
Without replying, I approached the priest who was conducting the treatment. “Is he dead?”
“...It is not fatal.” Even as he answered me, the priest shot me a displeased look. “Couldn’t you have taken the rules into consideration?”

Hearing a follower of god say that made me flinch a bit, but I had excuses ready. “I didn’t know it would turn out like this. He’s a knight! I even put down my axe and used my fist! How could I know he would pass out with one punch?”
At my confident reply, the two piggies blushed with shame, and the priest’s mouth fell open in shock. “Pass... out? His brain was leaking from the injury, but you think he passed out—”
“If he’s alive, he’s passed out!”

It was an argument that even Ainar, who taught me how to live like a barbarian, would fold against. At that, the priest pursed his lips. He had apparently determined that there was no point in arguing with me anymore.
An awkward silence hung inside the tent. I was wondering if I should just leave when the bastard woke up right on cue.

“W-Where... am I...?” he muttered, eyes hazy. The divine power of a high-ranking priest had healed his crushed skull impeccably, but it was not an all-purpose cheat code. “I remember I was on my way up to the arena...”

At his mumbling, the priest explained the situation. There was a tournament happening, and he had incurred a serious brain injury. However, he had just been treated, and his memory would recover in time.
“I-I see. Thank you for your h—” When the bastard who was thanking the priest for his kind briefing saw me in the room, he stiffened. “W-Why are you...?”
His look was closer to one of fear than confusion. That was a little suspicious. If he had lost his memory during the duel, why was he reacting like this?
“Hmm, do you really not remember anything?”
“I-I don’t. S-So, leave.”
It didn’t seem to be a lie... Still, I should set things straight while I was here. “If you do one thing for me, I’ll leave right away.”
He looked at me quizzically.
“It’s nothing special, just repeat what I say.” So, after telling him exactly what he had told me earlier, I asked him to repeat it.
“I-If I say that, are you going to leave...?”
“Of course.”

When I nodded, what’s-his-name gulped, then repeated exactly what I said. “I-I heard he got his name in the first place b-because he’s... Ugh—” Suddenly, he trembled like an aspen tree and gripped his head. “Ahhh...! I-I remember!” It seemed that the memories that had been temporarily lost had come back while he was recreating the past.
“Good. Go on.”
At my urging, what’s-his-name froze like a statue, then began losing it. “S-Stop... I-I was wrong. So please...”
Apologizing? That was something I would never have expected from his past self. I breathed a sigh of relief. “Fortunately, the problem in your head seems to have disappeared.”
“Yes. So please take your leave. The patient needs to rest.”
“Sure.” At the priest’s words, I left the tent without regrets.
“I-I’m getting out of here. I-I need to leave, fast!”

I could hear a faint commotion from beyond the tent, and as I listened, I put two and two together. I was neither a doctor nor a priest with divine power, just a barbarian living in this savage world. But so what?
As I thought, barbarians are overpowered characters.
Just today, I resolved a problem that even a priest couldn’t fix.

When I returned to the waiting tent, the baron greeted me. “Good job. I really didn’t expect it to end so quickly... But where have you been?” When I told him that I went to see what’s-his-name and the state he was in, the baron grinned. “You are one peculiar fellow. You attacked him so mercilessly, yet you care about something like that?”
Mercilessly? That’s a bit harsh.
“If this were the labyrinth, I would have hacked him up with an axe.”
“Well, yes...”
“To be honest, I didn’t realize he would be that weak. I thought he’d at least be durable since he’s slow.” This was an answer I had prepared in advance in case there were any issues.
For some reason, the baron burst into laughter. “Yes, who could blame you? It’s their fault for not training enough.”
“But is it okay to keep going like this? They may be apprentice knights, but aren’t they nobles too?”
“Huh, are you really worried about the future? Don’t worry about that. It happened during a duel.”
“But aren’t knights property of the family? What if the nobles swear allegiance to harm me?”

“I said don’t worry! Why are apprentice knights participating in an amusement like this instead of official knights? Because it’s not a huge deal if they die,” the baron said firmly, before going on to explain that no one would try to get huffy with him over such a trivial matter and that even if it did happen, he’d put a stop to it. That was exactly what I wanted to hear. “So you just focus on winning. Everyone’s reactions to you were positive. The more you wreak havoc, the more pleased the count will be.”
Well, in that case. I now felt like I could crack all those skulls without worrying. It seemed that that priest’s abilities were no joke, either.
“The winner is Sir Tillen of the House of Viscount Henslvania!”

Afterward, I watched the other duels with the baron and waited for my turn. It was quite fun at first, but I soon lost interest. Their fighting techniques were all the same. I could see why everyone had gotten so excited during my turn.
Even if they’re just collateral relatives, they’re still aristocrats. There is no showmanship.
I was a bit tired, so with the approval of the baron, I went to take a nap in the corner. I wasn’t sure how much time had passed since then.
The steward woke me very carefully. “...Hey, hey, you, there is someone looking for you.”
“Looking for me?”
That was kind of out of the blue, but before I could ask, the steward finished saying exactly what he needed to say and disappeared. So, I went and checked it out.
What’s this now? The three piggies?

Two of the trio in question were standing there. Before I had time to ask what they wanted, one of them reached out to grab my collar. I didn’t know his name, but it was the one who had slandered me by calling me Little Clown.
“You b—!” When I stepped back and avoided his hand, Little Clown stiffened in embarrassment and continued. “A-Ahem. You! What did you do to Sir Sylvania?!”
“Sir Sylvania?”
When I picked at my ear and cocked my head, the guy got furious. “You don’t even know the name of the person you dueled!”
So that was his name. “Syl... mania...”
“It’s Sir Sylvania!”
“Yeah, him. Did something happen to him?”
At my question, the two shook in anger. “Are you joking? Each time your name comes up he loses it and goes wild!”
“How can you be so wicked? No matter how much resentment you may hold, to reduce a person to that state... Have you no mercy or honor?”

Mercy or honor? Those weren’t things a bastard who declared he’d slit my throat in ten seconds should be talking about. I made a final diagnosis. “...I never thought the situation would be this serious.”
Prompt treatment was needed.
“What are you doing here?” The commotion ended when Baron Martoin poked his head out of the tent. Flinching, the duo left as soon as they saw his face. “...Who were those men?”
“Nobody.”
“Well. Anyway, come this way. I have a great idea and I want to know if it’s actually possible.”
After that, I went back to the tent and had a frivolous conversation with the baron to kill time. The first round was over before I knew it and the quarter-final of the tournament kicked off.
Was this the “hero’s fate” that the shaman had talked about?
“Sir Quartean of the House of Baron Serpia and Bjorn Yandel of the House of Baron Martoin, take your positions!”
Surprisingly, I faced one of the three knights in the second round as well. It was the bastard with the tendency to bluff.

“Don’t expect this to be the same as last time.” Even though the duel had already started, the bastard took the time to deliver a line. “I don’t want to say this with my own mouth, but Sir Sylvania is the weakest out of—”
In truth, it was even easier than the first duel. Taking advantage of the opening created by his muttering, I sprinted forward.
“Uh, huh—?”
Ignoring the way he swung his sword in a fit of surprise, I reached out my hand, grabbed him by the neck, and threw a heartfelt punch at his temple.
Smack!
Soon, the flesh and bones of his head were crushed and he fell helplessly to the floor. This happened within three seconds of the duel starting.
“Woahhh!”
“Please crush it like that next time too!”
“Knight Crusher! He’s a Knight Crusher!”
Even though the duel had ended in an instant, the crowd erupted in enthusiastic cheers. It was ironic indeed.
I can’t believe they like watching people’s heads get bashed in that much.
At this point, I didn’t know who the savage was here.
[Your reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your reputation has increased by +10.]

chapters.title: Chapter 98: Barbarian Trophy (5)
paragraphs: Unfortunately, my opponent in the semifinals was not the last of the three piggies. He lost in the second round, and I got the feeling that he lost on purpose.
In the end, one of them didn’t get to receive my physical therapy.
Anyway, there was no more need to aim for the head, so as soon as the match started, I hacked at my opponent with the double-edged axe.
“N-Not yet!”

But I guess this guy didn’t want to lose to a barbarian. My opponent showed his determination to continue the duel with his bare hands even after losing his sword. And so, I also threw away my axe, charged, and snapped his spine.
“Th-the winner is Bjorn Yandel of the House of Baron Martoin!”
It was a bloodless victory, but the crowd’s reaction wasn’t bad.
“Woahhh!”
“Knight Crusher, Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
It seemed the sight of a person being folded in half was also quite stimulating for them.

The baron wasn’t all that different. As soon as I returned to the barracks, he looked at me with wide eyes. “That match! It even gave me goosebumps! Throwing a person into the air and catching him with your knees? Where did you learn such a skill?”
Hmm, if I had to answer that, it would be from a cartoon I watched a long time ago, although it was only today that I learned it was physically possible. Nothing was truly impossible for a barbarian.
“I’m going to take a little break until the next match.”
“Hmm? Oh, yes.”
With the baron’s permission, I closed my eyes. Not because I was sleepy or anything.
Only one more to go.
With the finish line now in front of me, my heart began to pound.
The long-awaited finals had begun.
“Sir Albatross of the House of Count Ferdehilt and Bjorn Yandel of the House of Baron Martoin, please stand!”

My opponent was an apprentice knight under the command of Count Ferdehilt, the host of the banquet and the one who had invited me to participate in the tournament. I didn’t know about the consequences I’d be dealing with in the aftermath, but I wasn’t very concerned about the duel itself. From watching the previous matches, I had a good understanding of my opponent.
“Nice to meet you.” The gigantic knight holding an enormous greatsword bowed a bit. Looking at him, I smirked.
I think I know what the count’s personality is like.

A knight was different from an adventurer. To them, an essence was nothing more than a way of boosting their swordsmanship. Therefore, most of them tended to choose essences related to physical stats, but the combination of essences used differed from house to house. After systematic research, I determined that a few effective combinations were the standard, but each character was bound to have a theme.
Orc Warrior, Giant Golem, and Cyclops, huh?

My opponent was a typical Strength knight. His build had more of a focus on physical resistance than regeneration, perhaps designed with the assumption that there would always be a priest nearby, and his high level of muscle strength was paired with a full set of armor made of lithinum, a second-grade material. He was practically a walking tank.
He’s spent a shit ton of money on a mere apprentice knight.

As I started to get an idea of the count’s tastes, I was once again surprised by his wealth. One seventh-rank and two sixth-rank essences. He must have bought them in test tubes. I wondered how much they had cost.
If you add in the equipment he’s wearing, he’s far beyond the level of a third-floor adventurer.

For a second, I had the thought that the count may not have even considered that I had a chance at winning. That was how unmatched this man was. The other participants were mostly level twos and had only seventh-rank essences at best.

“Where is your equipment?” my opponent asked as we stood there facing each other right before the match was to begin. He must have been confused as to why I was on the stage with nothing but a single axe, unlike my previous matches.

“It’s uncomfortable,” I replied bluntly. This wasn’t meant to provoke him—it was the truth. Heavy-plated boots, a helmet with excessive decorations, a belt, shoulder guards, etcetera. If I couldn’t rely on it to protect me, it should at least not interfere with my movement.

“I see. Well, with equipment like that, I’m sure it is difficult to fight like you normally do.” Fortunately, my opponent didn’t misinterpret my words, but that was all. “I was worried that this would end too quickly, but I’m relieved that you seem to be serious about this match.” That relaxed expression and manner of speaking displayed a confidence that no matter what I did, he would be the one who won.
I didn’t feel the need to prolong this conversation. “I’m glad.” If my opponent wanted to lower his guard, that was all the better for me.

I pulled back my weapon, which had been touching my adversary’s, and widened the distance between us. He did the same. When the distance between us was about fifty feet, the referee raised the flag. That meant we could attack each other now.
“Come.” My rival took a basic stance and flicked his sword.

With that, it was like I could see the exact scenario he was hoping for unfolding in my head. A savage with overwhelming strength, enough to earn him the new title of Knight Crusher, and the true knight who then secured his victory with sophistication and grace. The crowd would cheer and his master would acknowledge him. A rosy future would open up before him like a solid road.
Smirk.

I could tell just how easy this bastard’s life had been. Whether my theories were right or not, when there was something you wanted, you had to be more desperate. You should always think of how much better things could have gone when they went well, but the opposite too.
Still, seeing how careless he’s being, it’s a good thing I hid it ‘til the end.
“Behelaaah!”
This tournament the count had organized marked the first time I was using this combo.
[You have cast Giantization. Your level and physical stats increase in proportion to your increase in size.]
[You have used Wild Outburst. Your Threat Level temporarily increases by x3, and your physical stats increase in proportion to that value.]

Giantization and Wild Outburst—when these two skills were used in conjunction, the user’s Threat Level rose tremendously. In proportion to that, their physique stats also increased dramatically. The downside was that Wild Outburst only lasted thirty seconds. But so what? At least for that time, I got to experience what it was like to be on top-quality drugs.
But I didn’t expect it to be pointless.
I wondered if this was a side effect of the excessive increase in threat level. Whether competitiveness or otherwise, the threat level effect was applied regardless of the target’s personality.
“Uh, uh, uh...” And in this case, an overwhelming sense of fear enveloped my enemy.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Even when I made a sound like a large monster and dashed forward, the knight stood frozen, stupefied.

“E-Eek!” Right when I lowered the axe, he evaded it by rolling on the floor and began running away in a hurry. But he couldn’t run forever on this tiny stage. Like we were boxing, I skillfully drove him into the corner and reached out to grab him. That was the moment.
“O-Out of bounds!” The final round was decided without a proper fight when the bastard ran off of the stage entirely.
That makes things easier for me, but...
The crowd’s reaction was cold. Fortunately, there was no criticism directed at me, but the knight who showed dishonorable behavior was sharply booed.
“I-I didn’t realize... A-Again! I can fight properly this time!” Coming to his senses, the knight climbed onto the stage again, demanding a rematch from the referee, but it was too late.
“How much do you plan to embarrass me?” the count said coldly. The knight hung his head.
“The winner is Bjorn Yandel of the House of Baron Martoin!”

Dang. Maybe I shouldn’t have used Giantization, I suddenly thought. I claimed an easy victory as a result, but even I was starting to get uncomfortable. Somehow, it seems I’ve angered the count too...

This was bad news for me, as someone who was actually more worried about the aftermath than winning the tournament. I never thought that my trick of hiding my full power until the end in order to eliminate even the slightest of unexpected variables would lead to this variable emerging instead.
Fuck, I didn’t know he was going to run away like that.
He wouldn’t try to get revenge, would he? I was inwardly a bit worried, but the count climbed the stage himself and laughed cheerfully as he presented the prize, the necklace and the trophy.

“Haha! Today’s performance has impressed me.” Unable to reach my shoulder, the count patted my forearm. I couldn’t tell if he really held no grudge against me or if he was just acting. While I was trying to figure him out, the count whispered something so that only I could hear: “I will call you privately when you are more ready.”
“...Call me?”
“You don’t need to know the details. Until then, ignore the other nobles. Do you understand?”
I didn’t, but I nodded my head because it was obvious I should nod here.
Look at those fierce eyes...

It seemed that if I refused, something bad would happen. Anyway, the long banquet officially came to an end with the ceremony. There were a lot of people who stayed and enjoyed their seats until the break of dawn, but not Baron Martoin.
“I am tired. Let’s return.”
Heading back to the mansion with the same people I traveled there with, I got all my equipment back. I was also paid for my hard work, as promised.

“You did well today. I’m certain my name and yours will be the talk of the town for the next few months. So, if you ever get into trouble, don’t hesitate to come to me.” Even if it was just an empty offer, the fact that he was making it in the first place seemed to suggest that the baron liked me quite a bit.
Well, considering everything I’ve done, I’m sure he must be pleased.
“Then go home now. I’m tired as well. I’ve prepared a wagon for you, so you can take that home.”
“Thanks!”

It was past two o’clock in the morning when I left the royal capital of Karnon and returned to my lodgings in Ravigion. I was physically and mentally exhausted from all the things that had happened that day, but...
Shall I get started?

I sat not on the bed but at the table and commenced my final calculations. The cost of labor was one million stones, as promised at the start. Two million stones for entering the tournament. An additional one million stones for winning. A reward of three hundred thousand stones for transferring the championship trophy to the baron.
A total of 4.3 million stones in cash.

Was this what having a wealthy client got you? It was hard to believe that this large sum was the result of a day’s work. And that wasn’t all. The new nickname of Knight Crusher or not, I didn’t expect to get this thing so soon: no. 7777, Garphas’ Necklace. I now had in my hands an item that, if you had bad luck, you could never get your hands on in the latter half of the game. Of course, a huge amount of money would need to be burned to awaken the hidden element, but you couldn’t deny that this was an incredibly lucky acquisition. So I made up my mind again.
How many luck points have I already accumulated?
From now on, I’d have to be careful about even breathing wrong.
The morning after the banquet, one question was answered at least halfway.
What call...?

As soon as I woke up, mail started arriving nonstop. All of the letters were sent by nobles asking if I could attend different banquets. For reference, the letters also contained promises to pay me for attending. It was an amount of money that almost convinced me that I could just do this as my job for the rest of my life.
So this is what the count was talking about.
His statement that he would call me once I was ready was still ambiguous, but I was sure this must have been what he meant when he told me to ignore the summons of the other nobles.
Huh, how much of a loss is this?
So, I replied to all of the letters with words of refusal. If I just ignored them, the proud nobles might retaliate, but if I attended their banquets, that might also incur the count’s wrath.
What the hell is the count thinking?

To be honest, he scared me the most. Although he was still treating me favorably, it was always guys like him who went nuts when things went awry. The fact that his intentions were unclear made me uneasy. Why would someone like the count be interested in a mere barbarian adventurer?
The next time the community opens, I should investigate the count.
With a new quest logged in my head, I hurriedly finished getting ready and headed for the Magic Tower.
This is the last month of research.
My three-month promise with Raven was coming to an end. The purpose of today’s visit had nothing to do with that, though.
“Oh, you’re here?”
When I arrived at Raven’s private laboratory in the morning, she greeted me like a normal person, unlike usual.
“So, where is the senior I need to help with research today?”
“Ah, well...” Raven trailed off. For some reason, I got a foreboding feeling. And at that moment—
“Long time no see.” As if he had been waiting, an old man with white hair popped out from behind the door. It was the Master of the Altemion School, who I called “Old Man.”
“Hah...” Even without any explanation, I understood the situation right away.
“I thought you said it would be your senior.”
“I’m sorry. Master insisted.”
So, he had been the one to force this change. I glanced over at the old man, who laughed benevolently. “Haha, don’t be so nervous. It’s not such a grandiose experiment.”
That’s for me to judge.
As I turned to him for an explanation, the old man opened his mouth, his tone strangely ominous. “It’s an experiment to test whether my new magic tool can identify an evil spirit!”
Fuck. You’ve got to be kidding.

chapters.title: Chapter 99: Rumors (1)
paragraphs: A magic item that could identify the soul of an evil spirit? A second ago, I never would have expected to find myself in this situation.
No matter what this thing is, though, it changes nothing.

I dismissed the idea that this was purely academic curiosity on the old man’s part. Could it be that he really knew something? Or was it really just a coincidence? If I couldn’t be sure, I’d have to assume the worst. The old man was suspicious of me. So what should I do now?

“...Magic tool?” I frowned at the old man as if the words “magic tool” bothered me more than “evil spirit,” and that that was the reason for that short silence just now. “...Is it safe?” I said dubiously. I was a barbarian who didn’t know anything about magic, and I’d seen countless strange-looking magical tools in Raven’s lab.
This must be the right way to react.
Wrapping up my brief assessment, I took action. Now it was the old man’s turn.

“Hmm.” He studied me with a strange look on his face, but then his expression shifted as he opened his mouth. “Heh heh, you don’t trust me? Me, the master of the Altemion School?” When I looked at him as if to say, Isn’t that obvious? the old man clicked his tongue. “Tsk, what do you take me for, my friend? Don’t worry. Aru will prove that the magic tool is harmless to the human body.”
“...Pardon? Me?”
“That isn’t too hard, is it?”
“Yes, well... if it’s just to check what spells were cast on the item, then...”
The master of her school, or a three-month bond with a barbarian? Since it was clear which side Raven would prioritize, I found that particular claim hard to believe.
No matter what excuses I make here, I’ll end up falling into his trap anyway.

As I listened to the two of them talk, I grew certain. I didn’t know what exactly had tipped him off, but the old man was suspicious of me. Fortunately, it didn’t seem like he was entirely sure yet, judging by the way he was trying to suss me out with a non-existent magic tool.
Yeah, I’m sure that a magic item like that doesn’t exist.

Brushing off my anxiety, I thoroughly analyzed the evidence. A magic tool that could identify evil spirits? Nothing like that had existed for thousands of years. However, as this civilization continued to develop, it wouldn’t be strange if something like that was actually invented one day.
Still, it would be ridiculous to assume that the first person to make one would be this old man.

The Altemion school was an orthodox school of wizards. Rather than niche subjects such as dimensions and souls, their research mainly focused on things like the creation of new spells. Why would a wizard like that create an evil spirit reader?
If something like that really did exist, he would have done anything he could to trick me into letting him use it on me. He wouldn’t have felt me out like this.
Soon, I came to a conclusion. There was no evil spirit reader. The old man just wanted to see my reaction.
“So what do you think?” he asked. “It’s not dangerous, and it won’t take long.”
“...It won’t take long?”
“It should take about five minutes.”
“In that case, well...” I accepted the old man’s offer like I was a bit uneasy but had no complaints as long as this would be over with quickly. But I guess my response was an unexpected one.
“...Are you really all right with that?” The old man answered me with a question of his own. His reaction washed away the last dregs of my anxiety.
“What do you mean?” I asked calmly. “All right with what?”
“...Weren’t you worried that it might be dangerous?”
“If it is, she said she would check it out!”
“That’s true, but...”
“Let’s go. I’m already tired from waking up early. I want to go home and sleep!”
Who the fuck did this old man think he was messing with?
“He’s gone...”

Bjorn had left the laboratory. Raven let out a big sigh at her teacher’s mumbling, which sounded somewhat disappointed. She didn’t understand what had just happened. A magic tool to identify evil spirits? She had never heard anything about her master researching something like that.
“What was that?” Raven asked. When he didn’t answer, she pressed him. “Don’t just sit there. Are you really not going to tell me?”

Under her master’s instructions, she’d had to prove to Bjorn that the magic item was safe. It wasn’t difficult, because the ‘magic tool’ her master had called an evil spirit reader wasn’t actually imbued with any spells. It was just an odd-looking chair.
“Don’t say anything, just go with it,” he’d ordered. So, she kept her mouth shut at her master’s urging, not mentioning that fact to Bjorn. And now it was time for her to hear the truth.
Of course, she had her theories. She wasn’t that stupid. “...Did you really think Mr. Yandel was an evil spirit? Is that why you interrogated me about what happened in the labyrinth?”
Her master neither confirmed nor denied that, but sometimes silence was the most revealing answer of all.
“Ha... So have your suspicions been put to rest now?”
“...Yes, I was wrong.”
“It’s not like I don’t understand where you’re coming from, Master. He is a strange man, after all. But I have a question. And I would really like for you to answer it.”
“...What is it?” her master asked weakly.
“Why did you do that? If you suspected him of being an evil spirit, you could have let the Ministry of Security take care—”
“If I did that, he would die,” he murmured quietly.
“Sorry? What do you m—”
“I’m tired. I’ll take my leave now, so please clean this up.” Soon, her master lifted his elderly body from the chair and left the room with an uncharacteristic weariness in his gait.
Raven, now alone in her laboratory, pondered her master’s words.
He’d die?
In other words, could that also be taken to mean that her master needed a live evil spirit for some reason?
What does Master want?
She couldn’t shake off her sense of unease.
Flop!

Returning home, I immediately collapsed on the bed. For some reason, I felt like I had used up all of my energy this morning. I wanted to get some rest, but I took time to relax and reflect on what had happened today.
That really came out of nowhere.

I didn’t think I made any mistakes. Looking back, none of the moves I’d made were bad ones. Assuming the worst, and using the information provided, I prevented myself from jumping to conclusions. Because of that, I was able to come up with the best solution I could at the time.
Given his expression at the end, it seems that the old man has completely dismissed his suspicions.

The incident was unexpected, but it had been handled well. However, there was one thing that was a little unclear. Once I convinced him that I wasn’t an evil spirit, the old man looked almost disappointed. Why?
...Well, that’s none of my business.
After thinking about it for a while, I cleared my mind. That was a question that was impossible to answer, and I decided that whatever the reason was, it had no direct impact on my safety.
Still, I feel kind of relieved.
What a shit show first thing in the morning. But paradoxically, this incident gave me a strange sense of relief. This must have offset some of that luck that had been piling up to the ceiling lately.
“Bjorrrn! Wake up! It’s already broad daylight, how much longer are you going to sleep?!”
Did I fall asleep at some point? When I opened my eyes, Missha was shaking my body. I didn’t sleep with the door unlocked, so she must have entered with the spare key I gave her.
I gave it to you to use in case something happened...
“Missha, why are you here? I told you I was going to the Magic Tower today.”
“You came home late last night. I was going to wake you up if you slept in!”
Well, in that case, I’d have to consider taking away her spare key at some point. “Ah, but how did you know I got back late yesterday? Don’t tell me you were waiting for me.”

“You promised to tell me everrything when you got back. Besides, I didn’t wait long, so don’t worry about it.” She may be saying that, but it was clear she had stayed up late waiting for me. Was she that curious about what had happened at the banquet? “Well then, tell me. What happened?”

At Missha’s urging, I slowly recounted what had happened yesterday: wearing the barbarian equipment prepared by the butler, leading the wagon procession toward the banquet, the food I ate there, and even the tournament I happened to win.
“Eh, did you rrreally win? Against all those knights?”
“They were apprentice knights, not knights.”
“They’rrre still knights! That’s awesome!”
Not really. Except for the guy I faced in the finals, Missha would have easily beaten the rest. Her close combat was no joke.
“Never mind that. Write this down.”

Anyway, after briefly explaining what had happened, I started writing letters with Missha. They were responses I was going to send to the nobles. I had written a lot of them in the morning, but when I woke up, I found that the letters had piled up again.
“...Bjorn, is it really okay to send stuff like this out? They’rrre nobles. This could lead to problems later.”
“It’s okay.”
“Well, if you say so...” Despite the anxious look on her face, Missha wrote down what I dictated.
I’m telling you, there’s nothing to worry about. What more could you ask for in a letter from a barbarian?
Getting a reply was a miracle in the first place.
I can’t go. I’m busy. So find another barbarian. From: Bjorn, son of Yandel
Yeah, that was delicate enough.

Being in an aristocrat’s house—a spacious and shiny place where delicious smells wafted around every corner—was like being in a different world, from the people’s clothes to the way they talked to the sound of the music.
“I finally understand the chieftain’s words! The world is truly a big place!”
All we had were some drums...
“What are you doing?! Come this way.”
“A-All right!” A barbarian who became an adult one month ago, Dukat, son of Karpen, followed his client to the center of the banquet.
“Tsk, what is that gait? Walk more confidently!”
That was a bit unfair. He didn’t seem to know what it meant to walk confidently, and the equipment he was wearing was unnecessarily bulky and uncomfortable.
I’d be more comfortable naked...
Although he wanted to express his dissatisfaction, Dukat kept his mouth shut as he remembered an earlier conversation he’d had with his host.
“That man wore an even bigger one without a problem.”
A few days ago, after following a man who had promised to pay him a large sum of money, Dukat received various lessons, mostly about how to behave at a banquet. At first, he had been angry.
Are they making these unreasonable demands because I am a barbarian?
He wondered if they were looking down on him.
“Who is ‘that man’?! Who is he that you keep telling me to do these strange things!?”
“I’m talking about Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

After learning the identity of the man they were referring to, Dukat had had no choice but to bear all the demands made of him. Bjorn, son of Yandel was a warrior among warriors who had defeated all the knights at a banquet full of nobles and had even acquired the wonderful title of Knight Crusher.
Am I not good enough to be like him?
After hearing this anecdote, Dukat vowed to give a great performance at this banquet. There couldn’t be any fault to be found in the actions of a warrior the chieftain had praised so much.
If there is anything wrong here, it would be me.
He had decided to act like a warrior, but it was not as easy as he thought. In the middle of these elegant and noble aristocrats who looked so different from him, he couldn’t help but feel small.
“T-This is delicious...!”
“Louder! That man wasn’t this shy!”
“B-Behelahhh...”

It was embarrassing, to be honest. He may have been a barbarian, but why would someone start shouting in front of people just because the food tasted good? Well, to be fair, if he were alone, he would have shouted several times.
“Don’t just eat the meat, chew on the bones too!”
His teeth hurt now.
“You want a napkin? Why do you need that?”
The hand he was holding the food with was sticky.
“Ugh, why are you taking off your helmet again?”

His neck was sore and his shoulders heavy. However, soon, he would have to enter a tournament comprised of only barbarian participants. Would he be able to fight properly? The fact that he was worried in the first place made him feel pathetic. Unlike that man, his opponent was not even a knight.
They say if you follow a goblin troll, you’ll end up getting your head crushed...

After his coming-of-age ceremony, Dukat entered the city with the heart-pounding aspiration of becoming a famous warrior one day. However, the limitations of reality proved different than he’d expected. Less than a month later, he was being confronted by all the ways he was lacking.
“Why can’t you do that?”
Dukat finally spoke the words he had been holding back all night. “I am... an ordinary warrior.”

Screaming whenever you want, breaking whatever you want, behaving as you please regardless of who was beside you... that was for the truly powerful, a right granted only to real warriors with confidence in themselves.
“I can’t do that... Please, do not compare me to him anymore. Bjorn, son of Yandel... he is a great warrior who cannot be compared to the likes of me.”
“Hmm, I guess he was a special case...”
At Dukat’s confession, the noble sighed and stared off into space with eyes full of desire. No, maybe he wasn’t the only one.
“I see. It has to be him...”
“Well, how could such a savage barbarian be the norm?”
“I thought all barbarians were like him.”
“They’re more normal than I thought.”
Listening closely, it seemed similar words to these were erupting throughout the banquet hall.
[Your reputation has increased +10.]
[Your reputation has increased +10.]

chapters.title: Chapter 100: Rumors (2)
paragraphs: At our regularly scheduled meeting the next day, the whole party gathered at a tavern for the first time in a while. It wasn’t the tavern we normally went to, because the dwarf was strongly against it.
“Let’s go somewhere else! That place is full of bad luck!”
He must’ve been uncomfortable after Dwalkie got arrested by the Mozlan out of nowhere at that place. Missha and Rotmiller agreed as well, since adventurers were a superstitious bunch.
Well, it’s not like I don’t get it.
Considering the fact that the occupation we were in could be fatal without some luck, this sort of sensitive reaction wasn’t strange.
Isn’t this a bit much, though?

I sighed. I didn’t care about going to a different tavern. It was a bit troublesome, but it was not like that decision impacted our lives, contrary to the bombshell the dwarf had dropped just a moment ago.
“...Why aren’t you saying anything?” As I let out a sigh, Hikurod began to fidget, studying my reaction. I guess that showed he at least had some kind of conscience left in him.
“Just wait. I’m thinking.”
“O-Okay.”
A heavy silence fell over the drinking party. I quietly organized my thoughts. “To summarize, you guys are not going to participate in this month’s expedition.”

There were ten days left until the labyrinth opened, and at the last meeting before it did—which was usually just a formality to finalize our plans—Hikurod declared that he would not participate in this month’s quest, and that he wasn’t alone. In a manner that suggested that they had discussed this beforehand, Rotmiller and Dwalkie expressed that they were of the same opinion.
“Ahem! They say if there’s smoke, there’s a fire.”
“Since this is a dire situation, I decided it was right to take a break for about a month and watch how it plays out.”

Was this a collective boycott? Three out of the five members of our party were saying they wouldn’t be coming. The reason for this was simple—the rumors that there would soon be a dimensional collapse had spread so much that it must have made them anxious. That was how the human brain worked. Even if you deduced through logical reasoning that something wouldn’t happen, it was easy to get swept up by the crowd around you.
“All of my former teammates said they won’t be going in this time.”
“Wouldn’t it be better for you to take a break too? It’s not like you need to be worried about next year’s taxes.”
“If the collapse really happens, that’s the end of it!”
At first they brought it up apologetically, but now they were even worried for my safety.
Missha carefully asked me what I was thinking. “...Bjorrrn, what are you going to do?”

To be honest, it wouldn’t have been difficult to convince them otherwise. I could slip in some of the information I had learned from the Ghost Busters and, with time and some persuasion, these guys would change their minds.
But that’s not necessary.
When I thought about it, this wasn’t that bad since it had already been three months since my visit to the Bloody Citadel.
It’s better this way. I was going to come up with an excuse to enter the labyrinth separately sooner or later.
In the beginning of the game, the rule of thumb was that you should clear the first-floor Rift every time it showed up.
“If that’s what you guys think, there’s nothing I can do. Then Missha and I will head in alone this time.”
“Eh? M-Me too?”
“Then did you intend to make me go alone?”
“Uh, no, but...”
What do you mean “no”? She clearly looks like she doesn’t want to.
“If you’re that worried, then I’ll just—”
“Ugh, you barrrbarian! Shouldn’t you at least ask me properly? And do it nicely for once!”
Nicely? Hmm... “Would you like to come with me?”
“Tsk, you think I’d make you go alone?”
Well, I didn’t know what she wanted from me. “Then, good.” But it was decided. This time, I was going into a Rift.
“Extra! Extra!”

Coincidentally, the day after Hikurod announced his leave of absence, notices were posted all over the city. It was an official document distributed by the royal family stating that the rumors related to the dimensional collapse were, in fact, groundless.
It really turned out just as he said.

There was even mention of the Tarutein school in the official document, which explained that, blinded by the research they wanted to conduct, they intentionally spread rumors. I was a little surprised. I may have spent forty thousand GP for the information, but I didn’t expect it to be so spot on.

“Hahaha! Bjorn! Did you see?” Anyway, when evening came, Hikurod came to find me. With a happy look on his face, he withdrew his declaration from yesterday and said that he could now enter the labyrinth.
But, uh-oh. I’d already decided which Rift I was going to enter. “What? You want to go together? I’ve already received a commission, so I can’t do that!”
“Hmm? A commission?”

I recited the answer I had prepared just in case, explaining that since Missha and I would obviously not be able to earn much with just the two of us, I took a commission. The job was to escort someone through the labyrinth, so I had to stay by my client’s side until we returned to the city.
“Is it... possible to cancel?”
“I’ve already received advanced payment, but you want me to break the contract?”
“N-No, but...”

It was a perfect answer with no room for negotiation. The dwarf had no choice but to drop his shoulders and go home. What could he say here? In the end, the reason this was happening to begin with was because he’d declared he wouldn’t go.
Welp. Seeing him like that makes me feel a bit sorry for him...

Still, even if it wasn’t this time, I would have made an excuse to head in alone with Missha eventually. It was not like the five of us could enter a Rift together. Aside from enjoying fewer pieces of the pie if we had to split the loot, there were also increased risks.
This is the right decision.
I banished my regrets. Unlike Missha, with whom I’d built a trusting relationship beyond one of simple teammates, it was foolish to reveal the secret to the other three.
Thud.
When the door closed behind Hikurod, Missha came running. “An escorrrt request? When did you get that?”
“Don’t worry about it. That’s just an excuse.”
“Excuse?” Missha cocked her head as if she didn’t understand.
I told her honestly that we’d be going into a Rift during our next trip into the labyrinth, and that there was a method for opening them that ordinary people were not aware of.
“Did you learn that at the library too?”
“Well, something like that.”
“Well... But why did you keep it a secret from Hikurrrod? Wouldn’t it be nice if we went together?”
The question sounded too innocent. I smirked. “Missha, have you told anyone about the Spirit Beast contract you made with the Ring of the Frost Spirit?”
“Hmm? I haven’t!”
“Really? No one?”
“You told me to keep it a secrrret.”
“I did,” I said with a nod. “But what do you think would have happened if it had been Hikurod? If I had asked him to do the same thing, do you think he would have kept it a secret?”
Missha thought about it for a moment, then shook her head. “...It wouldn’t be out of the ordinary for Hikurod to tell everyone after some drrrinks.”
“What about Dwalkie or Rotmiller?”
“Well... I think Dwalkie would make a mistake even while sober, and Rotmillerrr... I don’t know.”
Did every person look at things the same way? To my surprise, Missha’s prediction coincided almost exactly with what I had been thinking myself, with the exception of Rotmiller.
Actually, that man is the easiest to read.
Rotmiller would have kept it a secret, and would have wondered to himself how I knew information like that and become suspicious.
“Oh! That’s why you kept it a secrrret!” Anyway, at this point Missha seemed to understand what I was trying to say. But another question arose. “So what about me? Why are you telling me?”

There were several reasons for that. Missha was surprisingly conscientious and could hold her tongue. At the same time, though, she was inherently bad at lying. That meant I could check whether the secret had spread in real-time just by asking her, like now.
However, a simple explanation would suffice this time too, because I was a barbarian. “You are someone I can trust.”
Missha hiccupped.
There were eight days until the labyrinth opened. Once again, this time passed quickly as I checked off things I had to do. To briefly recap...
Day one.
As our destination was a Rift, there were quite a few things to prepare. First, equipment.
“Buying equipment again?”
“Not buying, enchanting.”
I added properties to my mace and Missha’s twin swords.
[Lightning energy has filled your weapon. Some of the damage dealt by your weapon will now be converted into lightning damage.]

The total cost was six hundred thousand stones. It was a short-term enchantment that only lasted for thirty days, but since the two of us were attempting to clear a Rift, an investment of this size was worth it.
“If you’re going to do it anyway, shouldn’t you have made it perrrmanent?”
“Then it would have been twenty times more expensive.”

I also bought some consumable items that had the lightning attribute such as Thunder Herbs and Lightning Scrolls. Altogether they only cost three hundred thousand stones, but since these products were not in high demand, I had to go around doing some legwork.
“...Are you seriously buying something that expensive? You have an expandable backpack, why do you need that? That’s a consumable! Something that disappears after you use it!”

Finally, after much thought, I also bought a bottle of the highest quality potion on the market. The purchase price was 1.03 million stones. However, I wasn’t exactly buying it for the Rift. It was just something I’d been wanting to have in my possession and was just now purchasing. For an adventurer without a priest, a high-rank potion was the same as an extra life.
“If I’m ever in a situation where I need to use it, I won’t think it’s a waste of money.”
“Hmm, that’s trrrue...”
“Since we’re both paying for it, it’s not that much of a burden.”
For reference, the nearly two million stones that I had spent up to this point were all borrowed from the shared account.
“Ugh, then arrre we done spending money now?”
“You are.”
Day two.
I headed to the holy land first thing in the morning. The chieftain welcomed me this time too.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! I heard the rumors! I’m so proud! I heard your new nickname is Knight Crusher!”

Unlike the last time, when he just briefly stopped by, the chieftain spent a long time praising me. Apparently, rumors about me had already spread through the holy land and were hot amongst the young warriors. Anyway, this conversation was a waste of time to me, so I gave him a vague answer and headed to the shaman’s tent.
“Hehe, Warrior, you are resourceful, earning this much money in just two months.”
I paid a whopping four million stones to activate the fourth stage of the Immortality Imprint.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 4. Your Willpower and Soul Power have increased. Your Spirit stat has increased by +30. Your Special Ability stat has increased by +10.]

All the money I had earned from getting entangled with the baron was now blown, but it was still worth it. Aside from Willpower, which gave a big bonus to resistances against psychological magic or status abnormalities, there was virtually no way to raise Soul Power, which served as MP in this game, besides leveling up and a few specific essences.
Day three.
After returning to the dorm almost half-dead, I experimented with the change in MP as soon as I woke up. The duration of Giantization had increased by 1.5 times.
“Why are you up so earrrly? Go wash up. Let’s eat.”
Missha arrived after that so we had a simple breakfast, something that happened every day and had somehow become routine.
“You’re going to the librrrary? Can I go with you?” she asked.
“You?”
“What’s with that look?! Sometimes I want to read a book too!”
After eating, I headed to the library with Missha.
“Parsytiev.”

Why was it that Ragna was casting the basic Book Recognition spell and not the Special Book Recognition spell? Since this was strange, I asked why, but the answer I received was even stranger. Apparently, since it was specially done in secret, she couldn’t cast it in front of someone else.
“Well, if that’s the case, shouldn’t you be a little quieter when you explain that?”
“That is also true. Miss Karlstein, am I right? Please forget what you just heard.”
The heck? I didn’t want to think about this anymore, so I just took Missha and started reading.
Day four.
I visited the Magic Tower and helped Raven with her research. This was my last day, as I had filled my quota. From now on, I didn’t have to come here every week.
“You did well.”
“Thanks for noticing.”
“Geez... Anyway, don’t die.”
As our relationship was a business relationship, our goodbyes were brief. However, unlike what I was expecting, Raven did not take my Magic Tower pass.

“You can come if anything happens. Ah, but that doesn’t mean you can bother me by coming willy-nilly... You know what I mean, right? Since it seems you get involved in strange situations pretty often, I’m sure I’ll be curious what you’re up to.”
“All right.”

I ran into the old man on the way out, but he showed surprisingly little interest in me. It wasn’t anger or disappointment, but an absolute indifference. Then I realized that this old man must have suspected me of being an evil spirit from the moment we met. So that was why he had pretended to be friendly back then...
Day five, day six, day seven.

Time marched on as usual. I ate with Missha in the morning, I practiced sparring with her during the day, and in the evening, I went to the library and spent a while reading a book. The days flew by like that.
“Everyone, back away!”
Now, the long-awaited moment had finally arrived.
Shaaa!
In Dimension Square, which was full of adventurers, a dazzling brilliance began to burst out from the center of the plaza.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! Thank you for your advice today! I’ll head in first!”
“Behelaaah!”
As soon as the city and the labyrinth were connected, a group of nearby barbarians rushed into the portal. To think they even knew how to say thank you. Why were we barbarians so polite?
“Hahaha! They’re a very lucky bunch to have a good senior like you.”
“I just pointed out the way.”
“Don’t be embarrassed.”
Currently beside me were Hikurod, Rotmiller, and Dwalkie. Apparently, they had decided they didn’t want to spend an entire month slacking off.
“Be careful. If anyone is nice to you, always be suspicious,” I advised.
“Hahaha! Do I look like those young barbarians to you?”
Similar, actually. Well, I was sure Rotmiller would take care of them. Since they’d only be staying on the second floor this time, things shouldn’t get dangerous even for just the three of them.
“Then we should head in soon... Aren’t you guys going in?”
“Ah, our client is not here yet.”
“I see. Then tomorrow—No, see you later!”
After exchanging brief goodbyes, the three of them entered the labyrinth first. I just stayed where I was and watched people trickle out of the square.
“Bjorrrn, are we not going in?” Missha asked, curious.
“Just wait.”
“Hmm? Until when?”
Oh, newbies... Just wait if I tell you to.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
That was how you multiplied your EXP.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 4 (new +1)
Physique: 330
Spirit: 154 (+30)
Special Ability: 128 (New +13)
Item Level: 828
General Combat Power: 865 (New +43)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Vampire (Guardian) - Rank 5  Orc Hero - Rank 5]

chapters.title: Chapter 101: Rumors (3)
paragraphs: Darkness descended as soon as I entered the labyrinth. Quickly taking out a torch to light the surrounding area, I placed my hand on the tombstone in front of me. Wow, how long had it been since I’d done this?
Whooom!

The sight of a five-colored light emanating from a tombstone that had not yet been touched by anyone and a stabbing sensation in the heart—these were unique feelings that you only got to experience when you free-rode through life.
[You are the first one to open this portal. EXP +2]
“W-What?” Missha breathed, staring at the shimmering halo of light that had already taken shape in front of us. “Did you just open the porrrtal?”
She probably didn’t know a bug like this existed. I repeated exactly what I said to Ainar back then. “The dimensional instability phenomenon? You can use that like this.”

Unlike Ainar, who gave up on trying to understand, Missha tried her best to make sense of it. Of course, it didn’t work out very well. The actual principle behind it was difficult for even me to explain. I was just taking advantage of a phenomenon that I had come across by luck.
“...I feel sorry for Rotmillerrr.”
“Hmm?”
“If he knew something like this was possible... he’d be very surprised. Just like I was when I used that ring to make a contrrract with the Spirit Beast.”
Oh, that was what she meant. I had been wondering what she was talking about all of a sudden. Rotmiller would definitely feel a great sense of inadequacy if he found out about this cheat.
“Even if it’s not now, if I work hard, the day will come when I open a portal with my own hands. That is my dream as a scout.”

He had once carefully revealed his aspirations to us at the tavern. He was very serious about his job as a scout. It wasn’t even that wild a dream, either. In fact, his ability to pathfind was quite respectable. I didn’t know about the other floors, but at least on the first floor where he had worked his ass off for years, he was definitely a highly-skilled adventurer. If he could shorten his time by two more hours, that dream of his may come true. It wouldn’t be easy, though.
“Then let’s go up.”
Enough chatter. I entered the portal with Missha.
[You have entered the Rock Desert on the second floor.]
Sand crumbled beneath my feet and hot air rose up from below. Shadows cast by stone rubble followed the flickering torch as it moved through the pitch-black darkness.
“It’s the Rock Desert.”
Of all the places... I led Missha down to the first floor again. Then, following the compass, we headed east.
Since we landed on the opposite side, it’ll probably take two days to walk there.

If we had entered the labyrinth the normal way, it would only have taken us a day to get anywhere we wanted to go. Well, you win some, you lose some. Plus, the EXP gained from opening the portal may only have been two, but it was a type that could be perpetually accumulated. If I could earn that just by walking an extra day, I would definitely profit.
“Ugh, I definitely feel Rotmillerrr’s absence now.”
In about three hours, we got out of the outermost part of the dark zone. Even if we were following the compass, we still ended up at dead ends every once in a while.
“Still, isn’t it nice that the two of us are walking togetherrr?”
“What are you talking about?”
“Just... Being a noisy group of five is nice, but this isn’t so bad, eitherrr.”

At first, I wondered what she meant, but when I heard her out, I think I got what she was trying to say. Hikurod and Dwalkie talked too much. I couldn’t lie and say they didn’t make me laugh sometimes, but most of the time I was exhausted just listening to them.
“Gigeek!”

After escaping the dark zone, we were walking through the softly lit crystal cave when monsters attacked us. The monsters that appeared in this western section were gnomes. Like most rank-nine monsters, they were a one-shot kill.

They were like clay dolls that turned into a paste with a single macing and disappeared. Killing them wasn’t a problem, but it was annoying. Gnomes had the active skill of Unification, a stealth skill that meant you had to be within a radius of ten feet to be able to see them.
If Rotmiller were here, we could have killed each one the second he noticed them.

I wasn’t sure if it was because we’d been working as a five-person party up to this point, but while I may not have missed the dwarf, I kind of missed the other guy.
