He was the jack-of-all-trades type who always did his job quietly in the back. Oh, and Dwalkie. If he were here, we wouldn’t have to pick up the mana stones ourselves.

“Bjorn, there’s someone coming!” While I was lost in thought, Missha poked me in the side and called out to me in a quiet voice. As a beastwoman with highly attuned senses, she noticed their presence before me. “What are you going to do?”
What else was there to do? They must have sensed our presence a long time ago.
Clink, clink.

Before long, a party of five appeared in front of us—a legit party with a wizard and priest. As expected of a group of adventurers who had gotten this far in just three hours, the quality of their equipment was noticeable.
...Gotta be at least the sixth floor.

I didn’t know what essences they had, but the grade three and four equipment covering them from head to toe was a strong indicator of level. An adventurer’s equipment was akin to their ID. However, it seemed they were thinking along the same lines.
“Hmm.”

The look in their eyes as they passed us by was suspicious and wary. Well, yeah. They wouldn’t have imagined running into a barbarian and a beastwoman dressed only in second-grade materials here at this particular time.
Please just keep walking.
Fortunately, they passed us by without speaking to us. Rather than that being the result of my desperate wishes, they probably just didn’t have the time.
“Mr. Levron, let’s speed up a bit.”
“Okay.”
It was fortunate that they were speedrunning. They may not have known how we got here, but they probably assumed there were other rivals that may have progressed even faster.
You guys are already the fastest.
Since we were moving backward from the portal, I knew that these guys were at the very front of the herd. Though, even if they were, all they’d find was a portal that had already been opened.

“Wow, those people really run everywhere.” Missha expressed admiration upon seeing adventurers speedrunning for the first time. It took less than two seconds for them to come into view and pass us by, but it seemed to have been quite impressive nonetheless.
“What are you looking at? Someday we’ll have to do that too.”
“...Us?” Missha cocked her head.

Well, no matter how much I told her about our future plans right now, she wouldn’t be able to picture herself doing any of it. It wasn’t that long ago that she had been treated like a half-wit by her family because she couldn’t even contract a Spirit Beast.
“Sometimes, Bjorn, it seems like you have rrreally big ambitions. Is it because you’re a barbarian?”
“...Are you being sarcastic?”
“Idiot, I’m trying to say it’s cool!”
“Hmm.” This kid could be too direct sometimes. Did she think she was a barbarian herself or something?
“Did you see the weapon that swordsman was holding earlierrr?”
“You mean the sword made of Orichalcum?”
“Yes, that! So it was Orichalcum. I wonderrr how much it’d cost to make a weapon out of that...”

After that, Missha continued to talk about the party we ran into earlier. She seemed to have a longing to be a high-ranking adventurer. Well, that was a much more positive emotion than jealousy or arrogance, but just longing wouldn’t get you anything.
“Stop talking and move your feet.”
“Hmph, if anyone hearrrd you, they’d think I wasn’t moving at all.”

Anyway, as we continued walking eastward, the frequency of our encounters with adventurers gradually increased. In the beginning, like the party we saw earlier, most of them were high-ranking adventurers. As time passed, though, their levels gradually decreased.

I got out my watch. It was 18:57, nineteen hours since the labyrinth opened. That meant we’d spent all day walking. Thanks to that, we were already at the usual starting point. In other words, we had reached the center of the first floor’s Crystal Cave. Therefore, there was no need to worry about raising the suspicion of the high-ranking adventurers we ran into anymore.
Huh, I didn’t expect this.
When we actually arrived, we still attracted attention.
“Did you just see that? The size of that mace...”
“I think that backpack is also an expandable one.”

Adventurers looked at us with envy every time we passed them by. Well, I was sure we looked strange. Instead of hunting on a much higher floor like we appeared to be able to, we were in the middle of the first floor.
“Why is someone like that still here?”
It was around that time that we were looking for a companion for the night. Every time we passed a group of three or four adventurers, they all made comments. It felt a little strange.
There was a time when I was like that too.
When I first entered the labyrinth, like them, I found a night companion and took a break. The problem was that the first person I had met was Hans A.
“Why arrre you laughing all of a sudden?”
“Just thinking of the past.”
Remembering how I’d had to pretend I was asleep with Hans A beside me while actually being tired as heck made me laugh. Before meeting Erwen, I really suffered through all sorts of hardships.
Oh, I wonder how she’s doing.
Since she had a rich sister, I was sure she was doing fine, but I was curious. She was the first teammate I’d ever had in this world. Should I go looking for her?
As I was walking with those thoughts in mind, a man caught my eye, though not because he was doing anything particularly notable.
Geez, that’s one conspicuous fucking man.
I didn’t like the look in his eyes. I could sense envy and greed glistening in that nasty gaze he had on me. But for some reason, that made me laugh again.
I’ve really grown up.
In the past, I would have been nervous inside, assuming the worst from just that one glance. But I’d changed a lot since then.
Not that I’ve gotten softer, but...

I smirked. There was no reason to be frightened by goblins now. Not that he was a goblin, but when you compared combat power alone, there wasn’t much of a difference between the two. That was even coming from someone who always assumed the worst of the worst. I couldn’t imagine myself being stabbed to death by that basic knife.
Yeah... I’m sure. But why is he still pissing me off?
There was a reason to check him out.

“You.” When I suddenly stopped and looked at him, the man straightened up from where he was leaning against the wall, startled. Those beady eyes were now full of vigilance. “Do you have something to say to me?”
“Then why are you looking at me like that?”
“...I’m sorry.”
When the man apologized, Missha punched me in the side. “Bjorn! What are you doing? He didn’t do anything wrrrong.”
For some reason, I felt like I’d seen a scene like this play out on the streets back home before. When some thug had started a fight with a passerby, his girlfriend had held him back.
I’m telling you, this guy’s looks were especially dirty.
“You, what’s your name?”
“Hanst Ivan.”

“Hanst? Not Hans?” The man trembled at my question. It must have been insulting for some savage to suddenly come up to him and bother him about his name, but this was really important to me. “Is it really Hanst? You haven’t made a mistake?”

“I-It really is Hanst...” Hmm, was I actually the one in the wrong here? As I continued staring at him to sort out my thoughts, the man added nervously, “I-It was originally Hans, but I changed it because it was too common.”

“...What?” Fuck, no wonder he gave off such a bad vibe. Still, he’d changed his name so I decided not to say anything and continue on my way. Oh, of course, I should give him some advice before that, though. “Never go back to your original name. Keep living as Hanst. Understood?”
Hanst nodded vigorously. “I-I will.”
Dddddd!
That was when the labyrinth began to shake like an earthquake was happening. At the sudden change, Missha looked at me with eyes full of questions. “Bjorn?”
Of course, I knew the answer. There was only one thing in the labyrinth that accompanied this kind of shaking.
“Run!”
A Rift would soon be opening before the first day had even reached its end.
Fuck.
Few people knew this, but usually, Rifts took at least three days to naturally spawn.
So who was the bastard who did it?
That meant someone had beaten us to the punch by using the very same method I had been planning to use.

chapters.title: Chapter 102: Mafia (1)
paragraphs: “W-What was that!? It’s suddenly...”
“An earthquake...?”
Adventurers were awakened by the vibrations traveling through the ground. I realized it then. Once a Hans, always a Hans.
To think even a name change doesn’t help.
I sighed and looked at Hanst—no, the man who would forever be remembered as Hans F—for the last time.
“I-I didn’t do anything!”
Yeah, I know that. How would you have opened the Rift from here? It’s just my bad fucking luck.
“Bjorn?”
“Run!” I grabbed Missha and started running. We didn’t have time.
Even though I hadn’t provided any explanation, Missha asked, “...Is it a Rrrift? Has one been opened?”
“Yeah.”
As was typical in my life, shit was once again going down. Of course, it at least wasn’t the kind of shit that put us in danger this time.
Damn it all, I spent so much money.
I selected the Rift I wanted to enter and made my purchases accordingly. I was so excited that I even enchanted my stuff with the lightning attribute. So what the hell was this?
“Bjorn! There!”

I didn’t know who the bastard who did this was, but they had just smeared shit all over my plans. Was it a player? Or simply someone knowledgeable about this world? Well, I was sure I’d get a feel for it once I got in.
Whooom!
A portal formed in the direction Missha was pointing. By now, thousands of portals had probably been generated all over the first floor.
“Missha!” In case she fell behind, I pulled Missha into my arms and threw my body into the portal.
[You have entered the first-floor Rift.]
Boom!

After landing with a deep, resounding thud, I let Missha down from my arms and immediately examined our surroundings. Apparently, we’d just barely boarded the last train, because there were already three people inside this Rift. First, I took a closer look at each one.

“Oh, a barbarian and a beastwoman. How reliable. Nice to meet you. Please call me Carlson.” First, a human man. His height was around 5′6″ and his weapon was a sword. To describe the first impression he gave off in animal terms... a rat would suffice.

“...They won’t be a burden, then. I’m Abman Urikfried.” The second was a beastman. Judging by the round ears growing on top of his head, he seemed to be from the Black Bear tribe. His defining features were his muscular body and the super-large crossbow on his back that was reminiscent of a siege weapon.

“Hello. I’m Jencia Nephrin. As for my weapon, I use this sword here. I will do my best not to be a burden.” Last was a human woman around 5′4″ with a pretty face. Surprisingly, she had her black hair in twin tails. Not that it didn’t suit her, but I never thought there were people who actually walked around with this hairstyle.
Anyway, it was our turn next, so I stepped forward as our representative. “I am Bjon, son of Thor, and this is Michelle. As you can see, we are together.”
“Eh?”

No “eh”s. When I shot her a look telling her to keep quiet, Missha pursed her lips in a way that suggested she had pieced together what I was doing. Then she relaxed the pinched skin around her eyes and stared off into space. Was that supposed to be her poker face?

It was noticeably strange, so I redirected the conversation before she drew any attention. “I take on the role of the protector in the labyrinth, and I am most confident in it. What are you guys good at?”
When entering a Rift, learning each other’s strengths was the most basic of basic procedures.

The woman named Jencia told us about herself in more detail. “I use a sword! Oh, and I have the essence of a Goblin Archer, and was also trained as a scout from a young age, so I’m somewhat knowledgeable about traps and mechanical devices.”

Not a Goblin Swordsman but a Goblin Archer? When I heard that, I thought, What a useless character, but that wasn’t something I needed to be too worried about. It wasn’t like this was a character I was personally cultivating, anyway. Just by looking at her equipment, I could tell that she was a rookie.

Swordsman and defense warrior Carlson was better than Jencia, but ultimately similar. “I mainly use a sword and shield, Mister, um... Bjon? Anyway, it may not be as much as you, but I’m usually on the front lines taking attacks for the party too.”

He was mid-second floor at most. However, since he didn’t reveal his essence like the naïve woman who came before him, it seemed he had slightly more experience than her. That, or maybe he didn’t have one.
Two beginners, huh?

Well, I had kind of expected that. The situation was different from the first time I met Hikurod and Raven. It had only been three months since the last Rift opened, so it was impossible for anyone to have known it was happening in advance and prepare. It even opened on the first day, which led to this situation—if it had opened later, it would have been full of locals who hadn’t even been to the second floor.
In that sense, this is suspicious.

I looked at the last person. I guess he accepted that as a prompt to introduce himself. “As you can see...” The muscular, bearded macho man shrugged the large crossbow on his back. He was the only mid-level adventurer of the three.
Like a typical barbarian, I decided to be direct. “Tell us how reliable you are.”
“Shouldn’t the person asking that question be the first to answer it?”
Oh, that was true. “I’m rank six, and Michelle is rank seven. We’re mainly active on the fourth floor.”
“I see. I’m rank five.”

Shit, he wasn’t mid-level but high-level instead. Generally, rank six was considered mid, five was high, and anyone who was rank four was a top-class adventurer. That was because the gap between the ranks widened enormously from the sixth rank onward, and even included a promotion review. Dang, this was getting even more suspicious.
“What is a rank-five adventurer doing here?” I asked.
“Shouldn’t we be asking the same of you guys too?” This guy didn’t miss a single beat.

“...We were originally working with a party, but due to some circumstances, the two of us were the only ones who came into the labyrinth this time. We couldn’t move up to the second floor because we didn’t have a scout, and then the Rift opened.” This was the answer I had prepared in case there was anyone suspicious of me once I opened the Rift.
“What a coincidence. I’m in a similar situation. Well, it’s been a while since I left my original party, though.”
Goddamn it. Is he lying or what?
Even as I was wondering whether an archer tough enough to play solo actually existed, as soon as I looked at his face I knew.
Either way, I’ll have to be more careful with this man.
I promptly designated Mr. Bear as my number one concern. Aside from his brute strength, everything about him was suspicious.
Besides this man, there is no one here who can collect rank-eight mana stones.
Of course, that was only taking into account the information that was currently available. The possibility that Carlson and Jencia were hiding their skills could not be ruled out.

“Oh, but who came in first?” I asked the question casually like it was out of pure curiosity. Who had really opened the Rift? Unless the three of them were working together, I determined that this question alone would allow me to figure each of them out.
“I’m not sure. I think we all came in together...”
“It was so simultaneous that I can’t say who got here first.”
“You ask strange questions.”
I guess I wasn’t allowed to get my hands on that information so easily. Ugh, fuck. This was like playing Mafia.
An unknown person had opened the Rift. This trampled on many parts of my plan. First was the issue of loot distribution.
“Okay then, it’s decided.”

At the end of our discussion, we decided that Missha, Mr. Bear, and I would take three shares each, and Carlson and Jencia—Jenson for short—would each take one. The world of adventurers was a heartless one.
“It’s not that much of a loss. You’ll take all the leftover essences.”
“Okay...”

This strategy of kicking away the ladder was the same one Hikurod and Raven had used on me in the Bloody Citadel, and what I was going to use on these guys too. If I made concessions here, what would be left?
He has more compassion than he seems to. I wasn’t going to give them anything.

My plan had been to open the Rift on the third day. Then, once we had a team of first-floor regulars, I was going to let them take care of all the dirty work and take everything for myself. However, we now had to deal with the variable of Mr. Bear, and there was no choice but to make considerable concessions in the loot distribution process. For now, Missha had been selected to eat the guardian’s essence, but if a Numbers Item or Rift Stone were to drop, I’d have to roll the dice against Mr. Bear.
Ugh, I’m not confident in dice-rolling.
My stomach hurt already. I wasn’t confident I could win. This was why I tried to avoid the variable of chance.
“Let’s get going.” I shook off my lingering disappointment and moved forward. Behind me were Jenson to both sides, then Mr. Bear, then Missha.
Crackle!

Like we were walking on thin ice, I could hear the sound of cracking with each step. It wasn’t exactly an inaccurate comparison. We were traveling over a frozen lake right now. This was the one silver lining in the middle of this mess.
I guess I can use the items I’ve prepared.

There were a total of four Rifts on the first floor. Depending on the type, there were differences in the monsters that appeared, their difficulty, and the rewards. Which one should we go to? After much consideration, I chose one, and luckily, it was the same one I was walking through right now.
[Glacier Cave]

A particular rank-eight monster appeared in the Beast’s Den on the second floor, and this particular Rift could be opened by offering that monster’s mana stone to an altar. My only reason for selecting this Rift was Missha. Well, I had also reached level four, and now had space for one more essence.
But there aren’t really any to consume.
Even if this was a Rift, it was one on the first floor. Even the guardians were only rank seven, and they didn’t spit out an essence that suited me.
That’s probably why this man willingly gave up the essence in the first place.
Anyway, I decided that it would be more efficient to focus on Missha’s development for now and fill in the empty slot with a better essence later.
Wait a second. Didn’t Ainar leave for the holy land last time after I did something similar?
That won’t happen again... right?
“Why did you suddenly stop?”

“It’s nothing.” I shook off the thoughts that suddenly popped into my head and focused on my surroundings. At least I made it inside a Rift. Besides, with an unknown mafioso in our midst, this was not the time to be idle.
Shaaaaaa.
Frozen snow sat on the mountaintop, snowflakes fluttering and scattering down from above, and the sunlight reflecting on the ice made everything feel warmer.
It’s weird to be in a place like this after always being somewhere dark.
After walking for about thirty minutes, the lake area ended and a suspicious cave leading underground appeared. A monster was blocking the way.

“Kawww!” It seemed that the Yeti, a rank-seven monster and elite gatekeeper that appeared only in Glacier Cave, had appeared at the very beginning of our journey. As soon as it saw us, it let out a menacing shout.
“D-Do we have to defeat that and head down?” Jencia murmured.
Mr. Bear answered that. “I don’t know what this place is like, but in Rifts, monsters usually point the way.”
This was an answer that would make any gamer nod. For some reason, I was getting even more suspicious now.
“Don’t get involved recklessly. You guys stand back,” Mr. Bear ordered.
“...Is that really okay?” At his considerateness, Jenson glanced at me and Missha.

Well, I had enough conscience not to ask them to risk their lives to fight a guy like that for only 10 percent of the mana stones, so I just told them to do as he said. They’d only get in the way, anyway.
“I’ll go first.” Soon, Mr. Bear lowered the super-large crossbow from his back for the first time.
Whooom!
An arrow fired and the battle began.

chapters.title: Chapter 103: Mafia (2)
paragraphs: To be honest, when I first saw Mr. Bear’s crossbow, the following thought popped into my mind: Is it really possible to use that thing as a weapon? Surprisingly, the answer was yes, it was possible.
Whooom!
As if in direct defiance of my doubts, Mr. Bear skillfully loaded the crossbow, aimed at the head with accuracy, and fired.
“Tsk, as expected. It blocked it.”

The Yeti blocked the arrow with both hands and escaped an instant death. Of course, it didn’t escape anything else. Both its hands had been skewered by a single arrow. The Yeti screamed and tried to apply strength to the problem, but the arrow did not come out. The arrow didn’t seem particularly special, either.
Could this be Hook Arrow?
There was a skill I suspected was at play here, but I couldn’t be certain. That wasn’t something to worry about right now, anyway.
“Keeek!” The gigantic Yeti stomped toward us. Since both its hands were tied, it didn’t seem particularly threatening. But what was this?

“You guys finish off the rest.” Mr. Bear slung the crossbow on his back again as if to say he had done his job. One more arrow would have finished this but based on what I just saw, I could conclude that he didn’t want to do any free labor.
Is it because he’s an adventurer? The way he’s divvying up the labor is incredibly precise.
So that there would be no objections to our loot distribution in the future, I took up my shield and ran out.

“What is he—?!” I could hear Carlson freaking out. Even if I was a barbarian, it would likely seem impossible for me to stop a monster like that head-on. But that was only when you were a basic barbarian. Building a wall with my shield, I blocked the Yeti’s charge.
Bam!

The heavy blow jolted through me, but that was nothing. After absorbing the Essence of an Orc Hero, I had almost no excuse to be pushed back in a power struggle. Besides, the Yeti was only about three feet taller than me.
[You have taken cold damage from Chill.]
That chilled my bones, but not to the point of pain.
“Michelle!”

“Ah, yes!” When I shouted, Missha, who had been staring blankly at me, stepped on my shoulder and leaped. With the swords that she had now mastered, she stabbed both of the Yeti’s eyes from below at the same time.
Stab!
Since they weren’t daggers like the ones she had used in the past, the sharp blades were long enough to penetrate the Yeti’s brain.
Boom!
Soon after, the Yeti collapsed to the floor with a heavy thud and disappeared in a flash of light.
[You have killed a Yeti. EXP +3]
Unfortunately, there was no essence. If there were, I would’ve given it right to Missha.
This is a bad start.
Now there were only five possible essences, excluding the guardian’s, left for me to feed Missha.
“Hm? Why arrre you looking at me like that? D-Did I do something wrong?”
...There should be at least one, right?
“You two. You have good teamwork.” After a short comment from Mr. Bear, we kept moving.
We went inside the ice cave and, moving in formation, killed countless Frost Wolves, which were rank-nine monsters. These were the only guys that spawned in this area.
[You have killed a Frost Wolf. EXP +1]
Anyway, Missha and I had to do some labor here. Mr. Bear killed some wolves with his crossbow too, but not enough to compare to us.
He has a strong one-shot but not any wide range.
As I wandered through the cave analyzing Mr. Bear piece by piece, we reached the end of the first stage of the map. It took exactly six hours to arrive there because we got lost a lot.
...Not here, either.
If I had stepped forward in earnest here, we could have cleared this stage in under an hour. The topography was the same as the dungeon in the Bloody Citadel.
Left, left, right, right, left, seven consecutive straights, left...
Pillars appeared at regular intervals. If you wanted to find your way through this place, it was easy to do so. But I didn’t on purpose in order to feel the rest of the team out.
Someone who knows how to open a Rift would have been able to memorize a pattern as easy as this.
This left one of two possibilities: either the mafioso was not a player, or they were pretending not to know on purpose.
Well, if I keep an eye out, I’ll find an opening.
Thus, the second stage continued like that.
“This cave is kind of ominous...”

We traveled down the ice stairs at the end of the cavern and headed further underground. As we did, I carefully observed what my party members were doing. There was a hidden item here. Nothing special, but breaking the third pillar in this room revealed an elixir that granted the user a one-time boost in Cold Resistance.
They’re not going to take this, either?
Even though we were past that pillar and had reached the end of the stairs, no one was acting strange.
Well, even if they do know, they wouldn’t do something so obvious. They can just come back at the end and take it for themselves.
I decided not to foolishly underestimate my opponent. The stronger I assumed the enemy to be, the better. Well, at least I thought so.
“It seems like we went really far down, but it’s still surprisingly bright,” Carlson muttered behind me.
I felt similarly. The ice walls radiated white light, almost like the entire cave was made of transparent glass.
“It’s kind of pretty.”
“Yeah, rrright? I thought the same thing.”

“Uh, but what is that?” Jencia, who had been conversing with Missha on a topic that was hard for me to relate to, pointed to a huge cavity facing us at the bottom of the stairs. At first glance, the conspicuous, totem-like thing in the center stuck out.
“Oh!” she exclaimed. “I touched it and it started glowing.”
“It could be dangerrrous, so step back.”
“Ah, okay!” Jencia was clearly worried she may have done something wrong.
Mr. Bear chuckled. “What are you so startled for? That looks like the key, anyway.”
“Key?”

“Well, I’m sure a few monsters will come out first, but then the path will open to us.” Once again, Mr. Bear was demonstrating a gamer-like mindset. Indeed, what he was saying wasn’t wrong, although there were a few things that needed correcting.
[The long-sealed tyrant has awakened.]
In this section, it wasn’t just a few monsters that appeared, but a final boss’s mob. Of course, the Rift spat out a bunch of trash mobs before that.
Rumble!
The entire space vibrated and started filling with icy powder. Before long, a howl that seemed to pierce the eardrums resounded all around us.
“Gwaaaa!” In terms of pure intimidation, that roar was second to only a Lord of the Floor.
[The ancient monsters who sense the return of the tyrant have awoken from their long slumber.]
Shatter!
Soon, the ice walls that surrounded us peeled off layer by layer and began to spit out demonic beasts.
“Grrr...” The freshly-thawed monsters got to their feet slowly, like they didn’t have any strength yet.
“W-What do we do?”
“Huh, I didn’t expect it to go like this,” Mr. Bear murmured.
I doled out orders. “Let’s go toward the stairs. There are no walls there.”
Mr. Bear agreed with me. “Yes, that’s a good idea.”

The battle began. In the first wave, about twenty Frost Wolves appeared. From the second wave onward, rank-eight monsters also began to appear little by little: Saber Tigers and Wormstones, both of which we had fought in the Den of Beasts, and Ice Golems, which only appeared here.
“Kyaaa!”
“It looks like they’re not able to move properly...”
“Oh, that wasn’t just me?”
Since this monster released a Slowdown aura that grew more potent as time passed, I smashed every single one I saw with the mace.
[You have killed an Ice Golem. EXP +2]

Since this was a Rift that Missha and I had been preparing to clear on our own in the first place, we didn’t run into too much trouble. I was sure Jenson was being forced to risk their lives, though. Still, we were able to clear the monsters out before the next wave.
Once you start getting pushed back, that’s the end of it, but otherwise, it’s a pretty generic stage.

We reached the ninth wave in about thirty minutes. Another Yeti spawned here. Of course, it was completely different from the first one we ran into. If that one had just been a gatekeeper, this one was more like a mid-level boss.
“Koooooo!”

The Yeti appeared along with the lower-ranked monsters. That alone increased the difficulty of this wave by several times, but this time it was also a high-rank mutant. To put it simply, it was named. Besides a named monster having higher intelligence, its own name, and a unique backstory, it could also use the ability of another monster.
[Lord of the Snowfield, Katoomba, has cast Suppression.]
“Huh! W-What? Why is my body...?”
This Yeti’s extra skill was the Stone Golem’s Suppression. It was the same thing those asshole plunderers once used on me. The strategy for dealing with it was simple.
“Huh! A-Again...! Everyone, be careful! That monster is using something—!”
Either get beaten up by trash mob monsters every time your body froze up like Carlson over there or keep biting your tongue to keep bleeding, just like I’d told Missha to do in advance.
“Ugh.”
[Your Mana Resistance is above a certain level. You have total resistance to this effect.]

Otherwise, you could also prepare Mana Resistance stats in advance. As Suppression had the overpowered ability to temporarily keep someone from being able to act, it was also considered easy to escape. That was probably why this Yeti was still only a rank-seven monster.
“Behelaaah!”

After raising the level of aggro using Wild Outburst, I ran forward. Disregarding the fact that Jenson may or may not be almost half dead, if I didn’t get rid of this guy before the next wave, I’d be in trouble too.
[You have taken cold damage from Chill.]

When I got to the center, the Yeti—was its name Katoomba? Anyway, starting with this bastard, all sorts of trash mob monsters fixated on me. I only focused on Katoomba, though, because the rank eight or nine monsters clinging to me only felt like a tickle.

“Don’t ruh off uh your owh!” Missha, whose pronunciation had gotten even worse from chewing on her own tongue, followed right behind me and cleared out the surrounding monsters. The way she moved with the twin blades made it look like she was dancing.
[Lord of the Snowfield Katoomba has cast Cold Eruption.]
Was it because I had looked away for a moment? I found I couldn’t avoid or block the snowstorm the bastard flung at me. My skin was burning because I had no cold resistance.
But everything else is fine.
Since this body of mine healed instantly, it did not get to the point of frostbite. I intensified my battle against the Yeti.
“If you don’t want to die, get out of the way quick,” Mr. Bear muttered just loud enough for me to hear.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Enhancement. The effect of the next active skill used increases in proportion to Soul Power.]
[Abman Urikfried has cast Hazardous Materials.]
For some reason, my instincts told me to listen to the man’s warning.
Dash.
The moment I pushed off the ground and widened the distance, he shot an arrow.
Whooom! Kwaaang!

As soon as it hit the Yeti’s head, it exploded, flames bursting out in a ten-foot radius. Compared to the Area of Effect spells that Raven used, you couldn’t say this attack had a wide range, but all the monsters within it were dead.
“What kind of arrow d-does that?!”
Therefore, I tweaked the information about Mr. Bear that I had been collecting little by little. I thought he was a one-note nuker, but he had one Area of Effect attack.
[Higher-class mutant bonus. EXP +1]
In reality, I wasn’t sure if that was an Area of Effect skill, but anyway. Thanks to him showing off his full strength, the ninth wave was easily dealt with.
“A-An essence!”
The time for negotiation came a little sooner than expected. Mana stones could be collected later, but not essences.
“Two at once. That’s good luck.” Mr. Bear did not show much interest in the essences and just said we could each take one.

I felt similarly, at least partly. “You two take care of the red one over there.” I had no interest in a Frost Wolf or Saber Tiger essence. “We’ll take this instead.” A blue essence floated in the spot where the Yeti had taken its last breath.
“Could that be the Yeti’s essence?” Carlson asked, stuttering.
“Do you have any complaints?”
“O-Of course not. I don’t.” As if to physically shake off his greed, Carlson frantically waved his hands and stepped back. Still, he looked a little disappointed.
If you think this is unfair, you should get stronger, right? Strength is invincibility and king in this world.
“Then no problem.”
I called Missha over, but it seemed she had misunderstood something. “Congratulations, Bjorn. Now you’ll be even strongerrr!”
“What are you talking about? This is yours.”

“Hmm? Y-You’re giving this to me...?” Missha faltered, her words of sincere congratulations stuttering to a stop. Then she carefully opened her mouth. “It’s not that I don’t want it—no, I rrreally do want it, but... I’m just asking just in case, so don’t take this the wrong way, okay?”
“Say it.”
“...How much do I have to pay for this?”
Did this kid think of me as some evil boss?

chapters.title: Chapter 104: Mafia (3)
paragraphs: The essence of a rank-seven Yeti had pretty decent abilities.
[Yeti]
[Strength: +10
Agility: +10
Bone Strength: +15
Cold Resistance: +25
Cold Sensitivity: +15]
First, it had a pair of top-tier stats. Bone Strength and Cold Resistance were already defensive stats that were classified in the upper tiers. And adding Cold Sensitivity on top of all that?
This should be useful for a few years.

Sensitivity stats were key for attribute-damage dealers like Missha. Just as you dealt more physical damage when your Strength stat was high, the strength of an attribute depended on the amount of Sensitivity the character had.
As expected, she’s lucky.
I got this sense in the Witch’s Forest too, but Missha was the complete opposite of me. Anything she did worked out smoothly. Just look at this Yeti’s essence, and a blue one at that.
[(P) Chill—Adds additional cold damage to all attacks and reduces the Cold Resistance of the affected target.
(A) Cold Condensation—Temporarily and significantly increases sensitivity to cold.]

The passive effect was the same no matter the color of the essence, but of the active skills Yetis had, the exact one I wanted had been dropped. Cold Eruption wasn’t bad either, but if you compared them in terms of potential, there was nothing quite like Cold Condensation.
With that kind of skill, I could’ve used this as a support essence if only the base stats were good. Oh well.
Cold Condensation shined more in the second half of the game. Though, because the stat bonuses were too low, she’d also have to erase it in the second half.
It would have been much better if the Yeti had been a rank-five monster...
This game was needlessly consistent about things like that.
As I was thinking all that, Missha asked, “H-How much could it possibly be?”
“Huh?”
“H-How much will it cost that you’rrre hesitating so much?!” What the heck, was she still going on about that? “As you know, I spent a lot of money this time so I don’t have that much left...”

At this point, I almost wondered why she was like this, but if I thought about it, it wasn’t like I couldn’t understand where she was coming from. That was just how ruthless adventurers were about splitting essences. When an essence dropped, the party looked for the person to take it. When the owner was chosen, they had to pay the party members an amount based on the average value of the essence according to the guild.
But it’s a headache if there are no buyers on the team.

It usually wasn’t because they didn’t need it, but because there were times when no one could afford the cost of the essence. Rather, this was overwhelmingly common. However, even in that case, parties usually waited thirty minutes until the essence disappeared naturally before resuming their quest.
It’s a way of ensuring that you didn’t do some random person a favor for free.
That was the kind of people adventurers were. However, Missha was lucky this time. “Don’t worry about the money. You only distribute things like that when you will be parting ways.”
“I-Is that so?”
I was a barbarian who knew how to invest in the future. For the sake of my safety during future dungeon crawls, Missha needed to evolve into a better damage dealer.
“Then I’ll eat it...?”
“Why do you keep looking at me? Go ahead and eat.”
“Uhh, I’m really eating it?”
Geez, how many times did I have to say it? For Missha, who had been an adventurer for a long time, it must seem awkward to accept something without giving anything in return.
“What are you hesitating for? Your continued presence by my side is enough for me.”
“Well, thank you for saying that, but... Ahh, I don’t know anymorrre. I’m really going to eat it!” Despite that vigorous shout, Missha cautiously placed her hand on the essence.
[The Essence of a Yeti has seeped into Missha Karlstein’s soul.]
The essence emitted a light and wove its way into Missha’s body. “...It feels so weirrrd. Maybe because it’s been two yearrrs since my last one?”

“You will get used to it soon.” I decided to explain the Yeti’s abilities in detail later when I had time, and I turned around to look at Jenson. It seemed like their discussion was over too. “What did you decide to do with that?”
Carlson carefully answered my question. “Umm... Neither of us will absorb this one.”
This answer was slightly unexpected. They were going to throw away an essence? These beginner bastards?
“It’s just... Miss Jencia said she saw the essence come out of a Frost Wolf’s body.”
“And?”
“If it’s a Frost Wolf... I decided that’s not an essence that suits me.”
Was that how it was? “Do you know anything about Frost Wolves?” I asked, carefully studying Carlson’s expression.

Although they were only rank-nine, information about these guys was not well known because, excluding Rifts, you could usually only encounter them after reaching the sixth floor. So how did these first-and second-floor adventurers know anything about them? It was not impossible for them to, but it certainly wasn’t common either.
“Um... I don’t know the details, but it’s a rank-nine essence, right? There may be a better essence later...”

“...I see.” It was still a little suspicious, but there was nothing wrong with his answer. If we were outside, it would be a different story, but this was a Rift, where the drop rate of essences was significantly higher. It must have felt like a waste for him to fill his single essence slot with a rank-nine essence.
“Oh, I meant I’ll take what’s left over, of course. I didn’t mean to imply anything else.”
“I know. You don’t have to explain.” When my interrogation with Carlson was over, it was Jencia’s turn. “Are you the same?”
“Yes... I only have one free spot, so I want to be a little more careful...”
Careful, huh? I didn’t think that was something a swordswoman with the essence of a Goblin Archer should say.
“Well... erasing an essence costs a lot of money, right? So I thought I shouldn’t make the same mistake as last time.”
Learning from past mistakes, huh? If that was the case, there was nothing more for me to say on the subject.
“I’m sorry. You even handed it over to us.”
In the end, both interrogations ended without much success. That was the disappointing part.
Geez, I thought I could get a better grasp of at least one of them.
My plan had been to remove whoever stepped forward to take this essence from the list of suspects. But neither of them took it, and their answers were also believable.
Fuck, they’re not all in this together, are they?
Even with the worst-case scenario in mind, I stopped that train of thought at the station. The final wave was about to begin.
“By the way... Is it all over now?” Jencia asked anxiously.
Zzz, zzz!

Right at that moment, the time we had left over from dealing with the Yeti early came to an end, and the final wave of the second stage began. The nine-layered ice wall had already been shattered, and the hall was four times wider than before.
“Up above!”
The shattered ceiling cracked like a spider’s web, revealing a beast ten feet in diameter.

“Gwaaa!” Grayish-white fur covered its skin, and its mane climbed up its spine and covered the area around its neck. This was a rank-seven monster whose main specialty was walking around on two feet and tearing its enemies apart with sharp claws.
“...It’s a Lycanthrope!”

At Missha’s cry, Mr. Bear expressed some doubts. “Isn’t it too big to be a Lycanthrope? What’s that club in his hands?” These were reasonable questions. This guy was the final boss of the Rift we were currently in. If he didn’t know that this was the guardian of the Glacier Cave, the tyrant Tarunbas, it made sense that he’d be confused. “We’d better be careful.” Perhaps instinctively sensing this was not an easy enemy, Mr. Bear nervously offered me advice for the first time.
Of course, I just ignored it. This may be the final boss, but fighting this guy would come a bit later.
“Oh, be carrreful!”
At the appearance of a monster that was clearly, conspicuously extraordinary, everyone raised their guard and prepared for what came next.
[The tyrant Tarunbas has discovered the intruders and is very angry. Tyrant Tarunbas has cast Ice Crush.]
The bastard slammed down his club.
Kwaaang!
The shock was so great that the entire surrounding area vibrated. Soon, a crack spread across the floor, just like on the ceiling.
“Uh... huh?”
“B-Bjorn!”
“...The floor is collapsing!”
The ground shattered and we fell.
“Aaaaaah!”
It was time to move on to the third stage.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Glacier Cave is now active. Status effect Hypothermia has been activated. Agility is greatly reduced, and any cold damage taken is doubled.]
Heave!
I lifted my head above the surface of the water and let out the breath I had been holding in. Then I trudged out of the water and lay on the ground. The curses rained down instantly.
Goddamn reality patch.

In the game, all you had to do after falling was wait for the loading window. Your HP was significantly reduced, but the third stage began with the character already at the water’s edge. But in reality?
I thought that was really going to be the end.

Where we fell, an underground river was flowing, and very turbulently too. I was forced to ride the rapid current, pushed and pulled as I was swept away. By the time I came to my senses, I was being thrown down a waterfall.
I guess this is why my HP decreased.
Having hit every curve on the way down, my whole body ached. I wanted to rest like this for a bit, but taking a break wouldn’t suit a guy like me.
“B-Bjorrrn! Are you okay? Wake... uh, what do I do? Ah! Th-that!?”
When I opened my eyes, for some reason, I saw Missha’s face right on top of mine. I pushed her chin away with one hand and stood up.
“Ah! What arrre you doing!?”
I should be the one saying that. “It’s Bjon, not Bjorn,” I said quietly enough that only Missha could hear before quickly surveying our surroundings.
“Agh! Aghhh!” First, I saw Carlson gagging and throwing up water.
“Um, are you all right?” Next was Jencia, who kindly patted him on the back.
As for Mr. Bear... “It’s cold as hell.” He was warming up in front of a bonfire that he had somehow started. When our eyes met, Mr. Bear gestured to me. “If you’re awake, come.”
“Thanks.”
“Wow, do you usually carry firrrewood?”
“Since I travel alone, I have no choice but to pack everything.”
I guess he really did play solo. I was still unsure, but I dried myself in front of the bonfire. Before long, Jensen also came over and quietly crouched down.
“...Do you know where that Lycanthrope from earlier disappeared to?” Carlson asked, shivering from the cold.
“How would we know?” Mr. Bear said bluntly. “It’s not like I somehow researched it beforehand. Don’t disturb my rest.”
“Ah, yes... Sorry.”
After that, break time and recovery time followed. Everyone took off their clothes and gear, laid them out near the campfire, and then ate a simple meal.
“I-It’s strangely cold.”

Although we were pretty much dry and kept warming ourselves by the fire, the cold did not subside. It was better than being completely wet, but it was almost as if we couldn’t get warmer past a certain point.
Soon, Mr. Bear came to a conclusion. “I guess this is a special area.”
“Special... area?” asked Jenica.
“Oh! Are you talking about a place like the Witch’s Forrrest?”
“Yes, it’s not natural for the body to tense up like this, even despite the cold.”

“Hmm, is it that cold? I can’t rrreally tell...” Missha cocked her head at the sight of us all trembling in front of the campfire. She wasn’t messing with us—her words were probably sincere. Her cold tolerance was likely much higher than ours.
The damage she took must have been much less too.

Missha had a contract with Skadia, an Ice Beast. It was the enhancement-type monster with the largest stat bonus, and since she’d even absorbed a Yeti’s essence this time, her Cold Tolerance had to be about forty. In Dungeon and Stone, forty was by no means a low figure. My Pain Tolerance was only seventy. Aside from the damage reduction it offered, even with a Cold Tolerance stat that low, you wouldn’t feel the cold.
“...Are you rrreally cold?” Missha asked me.
“It’s okay. It’s cold, but it doesn’t hurt.”
“Uh, I don’t know what you mean by that...”
It was just as I said. I may have been trembling from the cold, but it didn’t feel painful. But I guess my answer just made me sound even more pitiful.

“Ugh, you blockheaded barrrbarian.” Missha sighed, then wiggled over to me. Instead of the clothes currently drying, she gently unfurled her rolled-up blanket and made a ridiculous proposal. “Come in here. You’ll feel betterrr.”
What was this kid talking about?
Whistle.
Judging from the way Mr. Bear was whistling, I didn’t think I was the weird one here, either.
Our recuperation time was longer than expected. It took a long time to dry all the clothes and equipment.
“It’s taken too long.”
It had already been twelve hours since we had entered the Rift. Since it had opened at around 19:00, that meant I hadn’t slept for a total of thirty-one hours.
“Um... it doesn’t seem like there are monsters here. Why don’t we all get some rest?” At Carlson’s suggestion, everyone agreed to take another short break.
“We’ll sleep on that side,” I said.
“It’ll be cold.”
“I have emergency firewood.”
“If you say so.”

It wasn’t reasonable for us to all sleep next to one bonfire, so I started a new fire a little ways away. Missha and I decided to take turns on watch. That would cut our sleeping time in half, but sleeping less and living sounded more attractive than getting as much sleep as I wanted in death.
“Bjorn, you sleep first,” offered Missha.
“Before that, I have something to discuss with you.”
“What?”
Since we were finally alone, we pushed off sleep and caught up on some conversations. First, the essence. She’d have to know what she absorbed to be able to use it better in real combat.
“Wow, did you memorrrize all of that?”

“It’s nothing impressive. Anyway, listen carefully from now on.” After reciting the information on the essence in the terms used by the people of this world, I lowered my voice even further and continued. “Did any of those three act suspiciously on the way here?”

I had deliberately sent Missha to the very back of the group. Ostensibly, the reason for this decision was to have someone guarding the rear in case a battle broke out, but the real reason was mainly observation. I had figured that since she’d be following us from behind, she’d be able to get a good look at the others’ behavior.
“Mm, suspicious? I don’t think so.”
“I see. That’s good. If possible, keep a closer watch from now on.”
“I will.”

Ending the conversation there, I got under the blanket and lay down. Then, I replayed the words and actions of Carlson, Jencia, and Mr. Bear in my mind to see if there was anything I had missed. I had observed their every move the whole day. Sprinkling bait in the middle of mundane conversations, I collected clues. And as a result, I had identified a prime suspect.
But as expected, there is no conclusive evidence.
It was still not enough to conclude they were the mafia member. If I had just one more lead...
I was gradually falling asleep with that train of thought in mind when Missha gently shook my shoulder. “Hey, Bjorn. Now that I think about it, there was one strrrange thing...”
I was tired, but I listened to her story. Then, I said, “Nice job, Missha.”
“Oh, did I help?”
“Of course.”
That wasn’t all she’d done. The final piece of the puzzle finally fell into place. I looked toward Mr. Bear’s campfire and smiled.
I wondered which one of the three it would be. So it was you. The mafioso.

chapters.title: Chapter 105: PK (1)
paragraphs: The one who had opened the Rift—in other words, the mafioso in this game of Mafia we were playing. Who could it be? This was a question that had been on my mind ever since I had entered Glacier Cave. To me, the mafioso was a wild card. Whether it was a positive or negative one was what I had to figure out. So, without just assuming off the bat that Mr. Bear was the mafioso, I opened my mind to every possibility and collected clues.
So, it was them.
As a result, I had discovered the person I believed to be the mafioso. However, that was all I knew right now. I had no idea what they wanted.
Hah, I can’t just kill them, either.

Because I couldn’t figure out their intentions, my sense of discomfort only grew. Rightfully so, because if that person really was the mafioso, there was a significant chance that they’d become a problem in the future.
I’ll have to keep an eye on it for now.
The mafia was one person, and that person hadn’t made a move yet. If they died, that’d be a problem in itself.
Whoosh!
Unless, of course, I planned to keep the other two quiet.
“Michelle, how are you feeling?”

“...Me? I’m fine?” Missha answered casually, but in reality, yesterday’s fatigue was probably ravaging her body. Unlike Jenson and Mr. Bear, we had only gotten three hours of sleep thanks to being on watch.
“Don’t worry. This is still better than the Witch’s Forest.”
“That’s... trrrue.”
I chuckled and brushed aside my concerns. The same kid who had endured all that wouldn’t buckle under the weight of something like this.
“Stop chatting and get ready to leave,” Mr. Bear commanded a moment later.

Missha ran back to her original position, the rearmost part of the formation. That position would allow her to immediately identify any funny business. If it weren’t for her, tank or not, I would have been uncomfortable being at the front.
Step.
As soon as I took the first step forward, the party followed along at my pace.
So this is how it looks in real life.

It was a dark cave of ice. The frost on the ground was slippery and the overall terrain was more three-dimensional than that of Crystal Cave. There were steep sections as well as places where the path cut off in the middle and had to be climbed over with a rope.
“Still, it’s fortunate that there seems to be only one path.”

Even without a scout, there was no getting lost. It wasn’t that there weren’t side roads here and there, but when you went down them, it was never long before you reached a dead end. All you had to do was follow the main path while smashing the monsters that appeared from over the ice wall.
Smack!

The monsters that spawned here were Wormstones, Saber Tigers, Frost Wolves, Ice Golems, and Owl Bears. Unlike the Bloody Citadel, where the rank-seven monster Bone Knight appeared, most of these guys were rank eight.
But the actual difficulty is higher here.
The status effect Hypothermia was a debuff field effect that reduced a character’s agility by up to thirty and doubled the amount of cold damage you took if you didn’t have any cold resistance.
“Miss Nephrin, be careful. Perhaps it’s because my body is stiff, but their attacks are more painful than they were earlier.”
“Oh, no wonder! So that’s why!”
As the journey continued, Jenson, who was in the second row on either side of me, began to moan in pain. Of course, I didn’t slow down for them. The two of them had almost no stake in this, anyway.
Smack!

In fact, as Mr. Bear, Missha (who was protecting him), and I paved the way, we slowly reached the end of the stage. It took maybe four hours to get here. As we walked through the winding passage, a wide cavity appeared.
“Wow, what a spectacle.”
Three monsters were trapped in a pillar of crystal-clear ice.
“Those must be Ice Orcs. Their skin is white.”
“...Ice Orcs?”
“They’re only rank seven, so don’t worry.”
Each orc held a different weapon. One held an axe, another a hammer, and the third a wand.
“...Do we have to fight those too?”
“They wouldn’t be here for no reason,” Mr. Bear cynically replied to Jencia’s muttering.
Riiip!
Right at that moment, the ice pillars that imprisoned the Ice Orcs began to crack and crumble all at once.
“No time to even look around?”
Mr. Bear’s relaxed reaction aside, I hurriedly shouted at the anxious Jenson. “Don’t panic and stand in formation!” It’d be easier for Missha to keep an eye on them that way.
“Ah, okay!” Soon, Jenson stood to my left and right, and Mr. Bear stepped back and took a sniper position.
Crack, tu-du-du-du.
Ice shards fell and the three Ice Orcs woke up, exhaling ferocious snorts to prove they were mini bosses.
Chhh!
One sorcerer and two warriors; they had a pretty well-balanced party comp, and with Hypothermia, they were pretty tricky opponents—if you didn’t know the right strategy to handle them, that was.
“Whew...” I let out a long breath and raised my shield. This was pretty nerve-wracking. Not because of the orcs, which I could take down any time, but because of something else.
If they’re going to pull something funny, now would be the perfect time.

There was a mafioso on the team. Of course, I didn’t know what their objective was. It could simply be that they wanted to clear a rift and had no intention of hurting anyone. However, I needed to be prepared for the other scenario.
Kwang!
I needed to focus on defense rather than attack. It was better to hide my combat power just in case. With that in mind, I had given Missha instructions to just watch and not join in.
“Haven’t run off to your lover yet?”
“You never know what might attack from behind. And he’s not my loverrr.”

“Yeah, well, seems like it.” Mr. Bear expressed his doubts about the position Missha had taken, but apparently, her reasoning was acceptable. “Tsk, those guys are useless, so I guess I’ll have to exert some energy this time.” With that, he whipped out an ability he had never shown before.
[Abman Urikfried has summoned the Iron Bear, Iradun.]
A gigantic bear jumped out of a portal that appeared in front of Mr. Bear. It was a Spirit Beast.
...Iradun?

To be honest, I was surprised. Since he was a rank-five beastman adventurer, I had been wondering if he had already signed a contract with a Spirit Beast, but I never thought he would be a summoning type. I could now understand how he could play solo even as an archer. With a tank for a summon, there was no need to make a point of forming a party.
“Gaaaaaa!” The summoned bear quickly ran in on all fours, then roared and reared up on its haunches next to me. Then it began to skillfully mark one of the warriors.
I’ll have to resort to Plan B, then.
I chose my actions based entirely on logic. This changed nothing. It was because we were hiding our full strength that Mr. Bear had brought out his Spirit Beast.
“Chhhhhh!”
For that reason, I allowed the Orc to swing its hammer at me. And since it’d be obvious if I pretended to be in pain, I just drove my head into it like I was making a header in a soccer game.
Bam!

In addition to wearing a helmet, I also had meaty Bone Strength stats, so the blow didn’t crush my skull. It just shook my brain a little and made me a bit dizzy. But even that was healing thanks to my natural regeneration stats.
Slump.
However, I collapsed to the ground on a suspicion that if I took down the Orc trio too easily, I wouldn’t be able to investigate the mafioso’s true intentions.
“A-Are you all—!” Carlson ran up to me in surprise and ended up on the receiving end of the aggro.
[You have killed an Ice Orc Warrior. EXP +3.]
Right at that moment, an arrow pierced the Hammer Orc’s head. As a result, the Sorcerer Orc’s aggro shifted to Mr. Bear, but a rank-five adventurer was a seasoned one.
Dash.
Moving nimbly despite his height of around 6′3″ to avoid the incantations, Mr. Bear loaded the crossbow and shot it perfectly.
[The Ice Orc Sorcerer has cast Frozen Iron Wall.]
The sorcerer’s defenses were meaningless in the face of that powerful arrow. How could a rank-seven monster stop that?
Kaboom!
The arrow shattered the ice wall, then drilled through the sorcerer’s head before exploding.
[You have killed an Ice Orc Sorcerer. EXP +3.]
There was only one Orc left now.
At this rate, he’s going to take down all three with that bow.
Disappointment crept in. If the battle was too easy, it’d overshadow my plan to make it difficult and turn this into a one-sided performance.
Is this the power of a rank-five archer? Welp, the ground is getting cold. Should I pretend I just woke up?
Just as I was thinking that, I heard someone nearby mutter something. “So that’s what a Spirit Beast is.” Their voice was cold. “I can proceed according to plan, then.”
Mr. Bear, who had been loading up the next arrow, suddenly collapsed and vomited up blood.
Slump.
The mafioso had finally begun to make a move.

In order to be identified as a mafioso, there were several prerequisites that had to be met: enough knowledge to know how to open a Rift, excellent navigation to be able to return from the second floor in nineteen hours, and the ability to clear the Rift alone. These factors could somewhat help reveal who it was. A scout with combat power equivalent to that of a rank-five adventurer was the mafioso’s true identity. The problem was, though, that all three temporary party members had this potential.
1. Mr. Bear. Rank five, a mindset somewhat similar to that of a player’s, etcetera. There was no point in going into detail.

2. Carlson. He was the only one who had only revealed his name during our introductions. He didn’t even mention the essence he possessed. Also, his equipment was suited for the lower floors and well-maintained, almost like it was new. I had kept my eyes on him in case it could be a disguise, and he also made an excuse for not absorbing the essence of the Frost Wolf. That was more than suspicious—but not more than this girl was.

3. Jencia. She said she had been trained as a scout and was adept in it, and even added that observation was her specialty. To me, this information was all just a smokescreen, a disguise to make the lines that followed sound natural.
When we ran into the Yeti blocking the entrance to the cave: “D-Do we have to defeat that and head down?”
While we were in the second stage: “Oh! I touched it and it started glowing.”
When the mini boss had cast Suppression: “It looks like they’re not able to properly move...!”
Even before the last wave, when everyone had lowered their guards: “By the way... is it all over now?”

She continuously pointed out key points while pretending otherwise, as if she had a clear strategy. Of course, all of this would have been nothing compared to Mr. Bear or Carlson if it weren’t for the dirt on her shoes.

The first thing I had checked upon entering the Rift was everyone’s shoes. To open Glacier Cave, you needed to go to the Den of Beasts on the second floor first. Jencia’s shoes were the only ones that had dirt on them.
Well, she could have just not wiped them before coming in from the city, but...
“Now that I think about it, there was something strrrange. Jencia’s scent changed after she fell into the water.”
Missha’s report convinced me. Although not as good as Rotmiller’s, her Smell stat was on the higher side as a beastwoman.
“It was stinkier before.”
“Like the Den of Beasts?”
“Ohhh! Now that you mention it, yeah. No wonderrr it smelled familiar!”
Jencia was the mafioso, and a bad actor that I had determined had plenty of room to become a malicious one. Thanks to that, I had been able to prepare for this in advance.
Stab!
The moment Jencia’s sword dug into Mr. Bear’s abdomen, Missha, who had been waiting, threw a vial right on cue.
Shatter!
The glass broke and its contents spilled out.

“Thanks, that should be about thirty million stones—Kyaaah!” While indulgently muttering something to herself, she got doused in a liquid and backed away in shock. “W-What the hell! What did you throw at me—”
I quickly got up. I guess the timing of her surprise attack had in part been brought on by my fainting act.
“Wha—what...?” Jencia looked even more baffled.
Instead of answering, I let out a shout. “Behelaaah!”
What do you think? From now on, this is all self-defense.

chapters.title: Chapter 106: PK (2)
paragraphs: Jencia Nephrin. This was a pseudonym she used while doing plunderer work.

Jencia was not particularly worried about entering Glacier Cave on her own. She was confident she could clear it, even if she had to kill everyone else in there with her. She had even purchased the information that Frozen Breath would be dropped here and had finished memorizing the optimal strategy.
“...They won’t be a burden, then. I’m Abman Urikfried.”
However, her plan went awry from the start.
“I’m rank six, and Michelle is rank seven. We’re mainly active on the fourth floor.”
“I see. I’m rank five.”
A rank five archer, a rank six barbarian, and a rank seven beastwoman.
Why are all these guys on the first floor right now?
She couldn’t understand this at all. Even if the Rift had been opened on the first day, at most she thought there would be one or two rank sevens or eights.
Anyway, what now?

Originally, she had planned to toy with them and enjoy her hobby, and then take out the Rift Guardian herself. That was because word of this could not reach the city. Her equipment, skills, and appearance were already known to the guild. If word spread that she was alive, it would lead to trouble.
It’s too risky to prey on them by myself. Maybe I should lay low this time and try for next time instead?
That was what she had initially been thinking, but her opinion had gradually changed. In life, a crisis could sometimes turn into an opportunity.
It’s not that I can’t wait another three months, but it’d be kind of a waste, no?
Thanks to her rich looting experience, appraisal came easily to her.
The archer bastard is worth thirty million, the barbarian is six million, that cat bitch over there... mmm, maybe three million.
A total of thirty-nine million stones... It wasn’t easy to loot this much money in the labyrinth, especially for a loner like her.
Yeah, let’s do it.
Soon, she was concocting a new plan. If she utilized the Rift’s unique conditions, she could devise a plan to get what she wanted.
The problem is this archer...

The barbarian and beastwoman had low ranks and were also warriors, which didn’t particularly scare her. There was no way either of them would have any sort of detection ability, so even in a two-on-one situation, she was confident she could win. But Abman was different.
Why the hell is he so thorough?

Like a typical high-ranking adventurer, he was seasoned. He hid his abilities in front of strangers, and whenever she tried to sneak into one of his blind spots, his gaze shifted to her seemingly out of habit. It was the same when they had been sleeping in front of the campfire. The archer bastard sat with the wall behind him and kept her and Carlson within his line of sight.
Is he a fucking surveillance camera? He didn’t pay any attention to the cat bitch even while she was right behind him.

Was it because they were both beastpeople? The archer did not give her or Carlson in particular any leeway. It didn’t seem like he’d noticed anything off, though. It was probably just a habit. As you accumulated experience, things like that became as natural as breathing.
...This is why human characters suck.
She waited patiently.
“Oh, and I have the essence of a Goblin Archer, and was also trained as a scout from a young age, so I’m somewhat knowledgeable about traps and mechanical devices.”
She put on the newbie adventurer act she had established for herself during their initial introductions and eased his concerns. And as she was doing that, the moment arrived.
“I guess I’ll have to exert some energy this time.”
The archer finally revealed a new ability. She had already confirmed what the four essences he had were, so it was his Spirit Beast ability that she was most wary of.
“Gaaaaaa!”

A grizzly bear appeared, roaring on all fours. As soon as she saw it, the corners of her lips curled up. The archer was a summoning type. Not only did the summoned beast have no detection abilities, but it was also a tank-type meat shield at best. The universe was once again helping her out.
Bam!

The barbarian got hit in the head by a hammer and dropped like a fly. It felt like he had been defeated too easily for a rank-six adventurer, but considering the decrease in agility brought on by Hypothermia, it wasn’t too far out of the realm of possibility. Or maybe he had been lying about his rank. The barbarian didn’t matter in the first place.
[You have cast Armed Shift.]

When she activated a skill to change her equipment, her old sword transformed into a treasure sword coated with a deadly poison, and other items on her person transformed into specialized equipment she had collected.
[You have cast Beast Walk. Your Stealth stat has increased. Your movement speed has significantly increased for 3 seconds.]
In that state, she activated stealth mode, the thing she often used during her hobby and which she usually introduced as the essence of a Goblin Archer.
Tap.
She pushed off the ground hard, but the sound of her footsteps, adjusted by an advanced stealth skill, was subtle. The archer guy, who was distracted by the orc, had not yet noticed her movements.
[You have cast Revenge. Penetration and Cutting Power are significantly increased for the first blow dealt, and the status condition Bleeding will be applied.]
Soon, her sword slashed through her target’s abdomen. This was a surprise because she had originally aimed to stab him in the heart.
I never thought he would be able to react to that.
Of course, his resistance was futile. She could feel his intestines with the tip of her poison-coated sword. This changed nothing. It just made dying more painful for him.
She was taking a moment to bask in the afterglow, watching the archer as he vomited up blood, when—
Shatter!

Something hit her head and broke, pouring out a viscous liquid. “W-What the hell!?” When she checked, it was the work of none other than the cat bitch. “What did you throw at m—” The moment she sensed something was wrong and attempted to move back, she could see the unconscious barbarian slowly standing up. “Wha-what...?”

It just didn’t make sense. The time between her activating the Beast Walk skill to successfully surprise-attacking this guy was less than two seconds. As someone with a lot of experience, she knew that when ambushed, most people usually just screamed in betrayal. That was the normal reaction. But not only did this cat bitch run forward and crack open the bottle, the barbarian stood up unscathed and seemed equally unsurprised. They didn’t ask why she was doing this, as if there was no need for that.
“Behelaaah!”
He just screamed and charged. From their strange behavior, she could infer one thing. No, it would be more appropriate to say that she realized something in the moment.
Did they... know this was going to happen?
Things weren’t going wrong.
[You have cast Beast Walk.]
[You have been hit by a Witch’s Lamp Solution. Your Stealth abilities have been nullified.]
Things were going very wrong.
[You have used Wild Outburst.]
With my cry to my ancestral gods, my whole body was energized, and the attention of the Ice Orc that was beating up Carlson was drawn to me.
“Chwi, chwiik?”
Of course, that was no problem. Getting hit in the head earlier made me realize that I could take their attacks. So, in that spirit, I ran forward while ignoring the orcs.
Dash!

As I moved my long and thick barbarian limbs without stopping, the distance between us quickly narrowed. Jencia still had a blank expression on her face. I was sure none of this made sense to her. How could she have predicted that someone would notice her perfect ambush in advance?
Smirk.

It would’ve been hard even for me to notice. If this bitch had entered a Rift I had opened, I’d have thought she was just an ordinary beginner adventurer. Regardless of the dirt on her shoes, I wouldn’t have thought much of it. Well, I would still have watched my back, though.
Why are there so many assholes in this world? Oh... maybe she’s not from here?
After clearing away the thoughts filling my head like a fog, I kicked off the ground again, hard. At which point...
“Huh...?” Jencia’s complexion turned white. It seemed she had only just realized that her stealth ability wasn’t active. “W-Why is this...”

Stealth was probably her secret weapon. She must have planned to kill Mr. Bear first, then use her stealth to get rid of us one by one. Assuming that there were no wizards or detection types in a group, even mid-level stealth abilities granted their users an enormous advantage in one-on-one battles. A warrior would have no choice but to just sit back and watch the ambush happen.
I had only one thing to say. “Stupid bitch.”
If you’re going to hide your identity, you should be more careful about what you say. I wouldn’t have known about your stealth if you hadn’t babbled on about having the Essence of a Goblin Archer.
Voom!

As soon as I got within striking distance, I swung my mace, but I guess she didn’t just have stealth going for her. Jencia shrewdly somersaulted to the side and evaded my attack. But, uh-oh. That was where the cat was.
“You fucking bitch!”
I stayed put while Jencia jumped toward me to avoid Missha’s knife. I figured that she’d figure out a way to dodge a wide mace attack, so...
Smack!
Shield Smash. Haven’t used that in a while.

I bashed my shield against her face like it was a tennis ball I was receiving, and Jencia’s body flew away like a piece of paper. However, it appeared she’d invested some stats into defense. Even though it was a decent hit, instead of passing out, she regained her balance in mid-air and managed to land.
Drip.
She cried out in annoyance as her nose began to bleed. “You fucking NPC bastards!”
So you really are a player.
She was only the second player I’d met after Tarikan Riyen, but that changed nothing. Player or plunderer, anyone who tried to kill me was scum.
“Bjorrrn! Look out!”
Just as I was about to rush forward again to crack open that bitch’s skull, I turned around at Missha’s cry and saw an orc.
“Cheeek!”

The bastard, apparently unable to read the room, was swinging his axe down to split my head open. I didn’t want to take that blow with my head, so I leaned sideways. The huge axe blade struck the shoulder pad of my lithinum breastplate.
Clang!

The blow rattled my bones a bit, but there wasn’t any significant damage, so I once again ignored the orc and continued rushing forward. That was because once this guy died, the boss monster would appear. However, I guess the sight of me carrying on after taking that orc bastard’s attack left quite the impression.
“Behelaaah!”

As I charged forward with a roar, shaking off the blow like I was bouncing off a bullet, Jencia hurriedly ran toward the entrance we came through. When I followed her, wondering why that was, she suddenly stopped.
“Uh, why is there a wall...?”
What? I followed her here thinking she might have something else up her sleeves, but was she just an idiot?
Smirk.

It was kind of funny. She called us NPCs, yet as a player, she didn’t even know this? When you entered the third stage, the ceiling collapsed and blocked your exit. In other words, this bitch had tried to run away without knowing that and steered herself into a dead end. So, I slowed down too. A cornered mouse was bound to bite the cat. I had to be more careful.
Step.

Covering my upper body with the shield, I slowly stepped forward. Although this passageway was big enough for two or three people to walk through, I was a big, imposing barbarian warrior. It was safe to say that there were no gaps she could use to slip past me.
Clang!
Even in the middle of all this, the orc managed to smack the back of my head again.
“Bjorrrn! I’ll take this guy!” Missha cried, promptly resolving that particular problem.
“Don’t kill it.”
“Huh? Uh, okay!”

I took one more step forward. Now the distance between me and the bitch was only six feet. Although we were practically within each other’s reach, Jencia didn’t make any hasty moves. She had already calculated her odds in her head.
Step.
I took one more confident step. Only then did Jencia urgently shout, “Wait! L-Let’s talk! This is all a misunderstanding.”
What misunderstanding? You just want to buy some time.
Seeing that her sword had been glowing red earlier, it looked like she was using Revenge.
I think the cooldown time for that is... three minutes?
Under the assumption there wasn’t a cool setting, that should be it. In other words, there was no way she’d be able to break through my shield for the next two minutes.
Whip!
But maybe that had just been an attempt to distract me, because Jencia cut herself off and brandished her sword.
Clang, smack!
I quickly blocked the attack with the shield and broke her wrist at the same time. Her hand bent at an odd angle and her sword fell to the floor.
Clang!

This appeared to be checkmate, unless this bitch had another skill or piece of equipment she could use to get through this situation. I couldn’t be sure yet. So, it would be better to get rid of any potential variables. She may have hidden a suicide bomb on herself.
“Tell me more about the misunderstanding.”
“Will you... really believe me?”
“If it’s reasonable.”
At my words, Jencia’s eyes went blank. She must have been trying to devise a believable story. Even if she couldn’t, she’d probably want to stall by using something plausible. “I... believe it or n—”
As soon as Jencia opened her mouth, I smacked her in the head with my mace.
Smack!
She was quite agile, but this time even she couldn’t react, and she collapsed to the floor.
Slump.
Soon, she convulsed and mouthed something. It seemed like she was still trying to say something.
Smirk.

Looking into her eyes, I had a guess as to what it was. She probably wanted to ask why I hadn’t kept my promise. So, like a barbarian, I gave her an honest answer. “You believed that? Is there something wrong with your head?”
Of course, it had been a lie.

chapters.title: Chapter 107: PK (3)
paragraphs: First, I took a peek into the chamber.
“Aaagh!”
“Don’t run away!”
Missha and Carlson were busy dealing with the orcs. It would have been over already if they could kill them, but they couldn’t do that thanks to my instructions.
I won’t have to worry about that for a while.

I quickly took Jencia’s equipment off of her unconscious body: a two-tier leather top, a boot with a blade that appeared as I was taking it off, a wrist guard that popped out a concealed weapon when I pressed on the groove, etcetera. Examining each piece, it was clear that they were designed to kill people instead of monsters. I stuffed everything into my backpack at random and couldn’t help but smile.
Some of these I can just give to Missha. Thanks to that, we saved some money.
Jencia’s equipment was fairly decent. And the crown jewel of it all was her long sword, which exuded extravagance starting from the handle.
No, wait... Isn’t this a numbered item?

I pulled it back out of the backpack and studied it more carefully. The sword glowed green. If I was right, this was No. 5991: Serpent’s Fang. It had no active effects, but gave the user a large bonus to Penetration and doubled any poison damage inflicted through the sword. I’d need an appraisal to be sure...
But it seems I’ve found something valuable.

Serpent’s Fang was a core item. It may not have been the greatest there was, but if used as a poison-type item, it was definitely useful up to the mid to late parts of the game. And of course, regardless of the number, it was very expensive.
If this really is a Serpent’s Fang, I’ll have to get Missha to use it before selling it.
With that thought in mind, I stood up. Now that I was done looting, it was time to talk. I had a few questions to ask, but before that, I’d have to establish the right setting for a conversation.
Smack!
I slammed down the mace. My target was Jencia’s ankle. I didn’t hesitate because I already took all the equipment that could be sold for money off her body.
“Grgh!” The moment her thin, white ankle was crushed under my mace, Jencia’s upper body shot up like she’d just been electrocuted. I pressed my foot on top of her chest to pin her down. “N-No!”
Smack!

Then I did the same to her other ankle. Since I took care of one wrist earlier, all that was left was the other. As my stance shifted, my eyes met Jencia’s. Apparently, she’d done something similar to this before, because it seemed like she knew exactly what I was trying to do.
“S-Stop... please... I-I’ll do whatever you want...”
Really? “Then stay still. Let’s finish talking.” I raised my mace above my head.
“D-Don’t! I won’t resist! So let’s just use our words—!”
Smack!

“Aaaaaah!” One last scream rang out and a suitable environment for conversation was finally established. Limbs had been crushed, and all equipment had been stripped from her person. So I could rest assured...
Oh, I guess I didn’t strip everything.
“You, use Armed Shift.”
It was beginner’s level stuff, but this bitch still had equipment she could swap into. However, at my request, Jencia stopped moaning in pain and just stared blankly at me. “How did you...”
What do you think? What other skill can change all of your equipment at once?
Instead of answering, I lifted my mace. Jencia’s complexion turned even whiter. She must have realized that the only thing left to crush was her little head.
“I-I will!” Soon, new equipment appeared on Jencia’s body, ordinary equipment that would come out to about five hundred thousand stones. I took that off too and put it in my backpack.
Now, it was time to move on to the main topic at hand. “I have a question for you.”
“A-Anything!”
First, I asked what kind of essences Jencia possessed. She had a total of four essences: Iron Knight’s (Armed Shift), Dinictis’ (Beast Walk), Saint Assassin’s (Revenge)...
And Toxin Bestow, huh?

I was once again wary that this might be a suicide bomb situation, but her last essence was a Hobgoblin’s, which Missha also had. To summarize, she had absorbed two sixth-ranks, one fifth-rank, and one seventh-rank essence. It was a pretty solid haul. It was a pity all she did with it was loot others.
No, when you think about it, she’s just found her proper niche.
As an adventurer facing monsters, Jencia was only a rank-six. However, in battles against other people, she must have been above rank five.
“Um, is that it? If you had just asked, I would have answered—”
I was just getting started. I went straight to the next question. “Why did you attack us?”
“My description is known throughout the Adventurers’ Guild. So I wanted to keep everyone quiet...”
