“So you were going to kill whoever came into the Rift.”
Jencia squeezed her eyes shut and nodded. At this point, she could’ve just asked me to kill her, but those words never left her lips. That wouldn’t change anything, though.
“Then why did you open the Rift? It looks like you have no room for another essence. If you hadn’t come here in the first place, there wouldn’t have been any need to keep other people quiet.”

“For the Heart of the Snowfield. I heard that that item is only available here.” Oh, so that was why. “Besides, I wasn’t even worried about the silencing part. I thought everyone would be a rank-eight adventurer at best—” As I listened to the last thread unravel, Jencia suddenly clamped her mouth shut, her eyes going wide in a way that suggested she’d noticed something important. “You knew I opened the Rift...?”
...That was my bad. “What are you talking about?” I casually replied, picking at one ear. But Jencia wasn’t fooled.
After a long silence, she came up with an explanation. “No way... are you a player too?”
Given the look in her eyes, I didn’t think there was a point in denying it now... But there was no need to confirm it, either. “Player? Are you an evil spirit?”
At my question, she stared blankly into space. Then, apparently coming to her senses, she wriggled and put her face on my leg. I looked down quietly.

“Mister, please don’t kill me.” Hope. “I want to go home. I can’t die in a place like this. You have no idea... what I’ve had to do to survive in this fucking world. Yeah? Please...” Pent-up anger. “Oh, I didn’t apologize, did I? I’m sorry. I-I was wrong. I thought you were an NPC. I never would have done all that if I had known. W-We’re real p-people, right? Wouldn’t that be murder?” Desperation. “Please... say something. Yeah? Fuck! Say something! You asshole...” Despair.
Jencia’s expression flipped from one emotion to the next as I continued to watch.
Thump.

Surprisingly, my heart was calm. I didn’t feel even the slightest shred of sympathy, much less sadness. There was no PK in Dungeon and Stone because it wasn’t an online game. Instead, it was possible to kill NPCs. Because of that, I had also used to enjoy playing a looter.
But you killed them because they were NPCs.
This wasn’t just a game. Although I wanted to believe that it was, there was so much evidence to the contrary that I couldn’t help but know that for a fact. She probably knew that just as well.
So my response to her was short and blunt. “You. You’re an evil spirit.”

An evil spirit—an entity that did not belong in this world, yet an entity that had to assimilate into its mind, body, and soul in order to survive. Yeah, what did it matter if she was a player or an NPC? That changed nothing. Whatever the modifier, this woman was nothing more than a plunderer, and a dangerous person who now knew that I was a player.
“You bastard!”
Therefore, I raised my mace. In a manner befitting a person who had fully adapted to this world, and knowing she would’ve done the same if the situation were reversed, I gripped my mace tighter.
Slide.
Jencia no longer begged for her life. She just stared at me with hate in her eyes, as if she never wanted to forget my face so she could curse me even in death.
Gasp, huff....

Every time she let out a ragged breath, her round chest rapidly rose and fell. I didn’t have to bring my ear to it to know how fast her heart must have been beating. I realized something at that moment. She had seemed to have only malice left in her, but there was actually one other thing left: fear.
Soon, Jencia closed her eyes. She let go of her hatred and finally sought peace. What could she see beyond those closed eyes? “M-Mom...” I brought down the mace before I could hear the rest.
Smack!

Flesh and blood splattered. Blood poured out of her nose and mouth each time her body convulsed. Of course, that didn’t last long. Soon, her body completely stopped moving. I let out the breath I had been holding and turned around.
[Achievement Unlocked
Condition: First Player Kill
Reward: Permanently increases your Spirit stat by +1.]
I had killed a player for the first time. However, I tried to push aside my feelings about it and took a step forward.
Step.

Whether the act had been easy or difficult, whether her flesh and blood had brought me excitement or fear, whether I felt cynical for wishing she would end up back at the place she had seen behind her closed eyes, or, if not that, whether I felt miserable about seeing myself gradually reduced to a savage... emotions didn’t matter.
Step.
It had had to be done. The moment I woke up in this savage world, that was the path I had decided to take.

“What took you so long? I thought something happened to you!” As I left Jencia’s body back in the open cavern, Missha scolded me. Mm, I had wrapped it up as quickly as possible, though... Only about three minutes had passed.
“H-Help us!”
When Missha glanced away from the battle to look at me, Carlson was helplessly pushed back by the orcs. However, I remained in a spectator position. “Missha, you can kill it now.”
“Ah, is that okay?”
“Yes. If possible, try using your newly acquired abilities.”
“Huh? I’ve never used them before, though...”
That’s why I’m telling you to do it.
There was no mafia anymore, and an Ice Orc was a good opponent.
“Ugh! I-I can’t hold them back any long—”
While Carlson blocked another axe strike with his dented shield, Missha closed her eyes and activated her skill.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Enhance.]
A faint white light appeared around her hand. This was the active skill of the rank-seven monster Vitol. Normally, the basic combo here would have had Missha use Toxin Bestow, but...
[Missha Karlstein has cast Cold Condensation.]
Blue particles appeared around Missha as if they had been separated from the air itself, and promptly sank into her body.
[Missha Karlstein’s Cold Sensitivity stats have significantly increased.]
She must’ve sensed that something had gone right because Missha opened her eyes.
Whip!
Swinging her swords in a fierce arc, she cut off the wrist of the orc who was trying to attack Carlson.
Slice!
The attack wasn’t enough to slice through the bone in one go. The orc’s hand partly dangled from its arm, still holding the axe. However, I was focused on something else.
“Ch-cheeek!”
Its wrist had been cut by a sharp blade, but no blood flowed from the wound. That was because the wound was frozen red and frosted over.
Is that Frostbite?

The Cold attribute stopped any bleeding. That seemed at first glance to be a drawback, but it also blocked healing, so it was quite useful depending on the type of enemy you were facing. It also had the advantage of limiting the opponent’s range of motion.
“Chwi, chwiik!”

Of course, Ice Orcs had high Cold Resistance, so only their wrists were frozen. A normal monster would’ve been different, though; they would have frozen up to the elbows. A monster with negative Cold Resistance might have even ended up in the Frozen condition.
Missha wasn’t finished warming up yet, so—“Missha, try aiming at the neck this time.”
“Hmm? Okay!”

One of Missha’s swords lodged itself in the orc’s neck. Orcs had high Bone Strength stats, to be fair. It must have been difficult to cut through it in one swing. However, as the area around its neck began to freeze, the orc stopped moving and began to tremble in place. It seemed that the cold had reached even its brain.
Crunch!

Now that I’d finished confirming everything I needed to confirm, I crushed the orc’s head with my mace. At the same time, the entire chamber shook and powdery ice began pouring down from the ceiling. The roar we heard earlier vibrated through the space.
“Gwaaaaaa!”
“W-What the hell?!”
What do you think? This is the start of the fourth stage.
[The tyrant Tarunbas has awakened from his long slumber and has recovered all his strength.]
Now that I’d even experienced an unplanned PK, it was time to take down the boss and get out.

chapters.title: Chapter 108: Baby Barbarian (1)
paragraphs: The first thing I did once the preparations were complete was send Carlson to the rear.
Bam!
The ice wall right in front of us shattered, and the monster appeared. Tyrant Tarunbas: the guardian of the Glacier Cave, based on the rank-seven monster Lycanthrope.
“Gwaaaaaa!”

This guy had several unique features. It was 1.5 times larger than a normal Lycanthrope. The basic skill composition was the same, but its stats were about twice as high. The most important thing, though, was that ice club in its hand.
[Tyrant Tarunbas has cast Ice Crush.]

As soon as it appeared, the Lycanthrope slammed its club into the floor. Ice Crush was usually a skill all about dealing damage to enemies in Frostbite and Frozen states. However, it was a little different in Glacier Cave.
Bam!
The vibrations spread through the ground. It wouldn’t collapse like it did in the second stage, but a layer of the ice wall was peeled away to reveal dozens of Frost Wolves.
“Bjorn! This guy is differrrent from other Lycanthropes!”
God damn it, my name is Bjon. Though since the mafioso is dead, I guess there’s no reason to correct her.
“Behelaaah!” Using Wild Outburst to attract the aggro, I used my shield to take the club flying at me.
Kwang!

With the heavy impact, a chill jolted through my bones. A thick layer of frost formed on the outer surface of the shield. This was not one of the Lycanthrope’s inherent abilities, but one granted by that ice club.
“Grrrrrr!”
“Woof, woof!”

In the meantime, the Frost Wolves, who had woken up, also attacked me and started scratching and biting everywhere. Even taking Hypothermia into account, the damage was negligible because they were rank-nine monsters. It would be different when the second wave started, though. But I planned on dealing with this first.
“Now!” After shouting instructions to Missha, I also took out a prepared item from my belt pocket and shoved it in my mouth.
[You have consumed Thunder Herb. For 10 seconds, any Lightning damage you deal is slightly increased.]

Thunder Herb was a doping consumable that increased all lightning damage for a very short period of time. Before its effects expired, I took advantage of it by tearing the Lightning Scroll already in my hand with my teeth.
Crackle!

Lightning fired at the nearest enemy and then jumped to nearby enemies in a chain. It was a cheap, low-rank Lightning Scroll, so it was hard for it to kill a Frost Wolf in one blow, but it managed to stun the monster.
[Tyrant Tarunbas has fallen into Paralysis.]

This was because this guy had a negative Lightning Resistance stat. That particular characteristic was not one that was shared by normal Lycanthropes; this was the only one that was weak against the Lightning attribute. It was a little weird that a cold-and beast-type monster would have a weakness to electricity, though.
[The tyrant Tarunbas has cast Fortitude.]
Soon after, the monster used its second skill to nullify the one stunning it, but it didn’t change much. It removed the effect, but it wasn’t an immunity. I just had to do it again.
Pop!
Soon, Missha threw a stone that burst and exploded. The in-game name for this was Storm Explosion, something I personally called Charcoal Briquettes.
[The tyrant Tarunbas has fallen into an Unconscious state.]

The seven briquettes Missha threw without hesitation exploded in succession, and Tarunbas zonked out. Against something like this, even Fortitude was useless. Unconsciousness was not a state of incapacity like Paralysis, Petrification, or Frozen. It was considered an abnormality in the character’s mental state.
Thump!

The monster that had appeared with the title of boss attached was thus incapacitated and taken down in just three seconds. What followed was really simple. Just like the good old days of beating up Death Fiends, all I had to do was strike the head.
Whack! Stab! Smack! Crack! Crunch!
As Missha and I tirelessly continued to deal damage with our lightning-enhanced weapons, before long, the monster’s body split into small pieces, the particles scattering on the wind.
[You have killed Tyrant Tarunbas. EXP +3]
[Guardian Kill Bonus. EXP +3]

That all took about ten seconds. The effect of the Thunder Herb ended just before it died, so there shouldn’t have been a big margin of error in that estimate. I calmed my pounding heart and looked where the monster had collapsed.
“What the...” Carlson, who had been watching from a distance, exclaimed with feeling.
Missha wasn’t much different. Unlike in the Bloody Citadel, there wasn’t a Rift Stone or Numbers Item here. “Bjorn... is this what I think it is?”
It was an essence.
“Uh, you want me to absorb this one too...?”
I didn’t know why she was reacting like this again. When we had discussed the loot distribution with Mr. Bear at the start, we had decided that Missha would take the guardian’s essence.
“Yeah, but... I thought you werrre just saying that. Since we weren’t the only ones in here.”
Oh, she thought I was going to take it away. What exactly did this kid think of me? “Hush. Hurry up and take it before it disappears.”
“Kya!”

I couldn’t be bothered to explain so I shoved Missha forward. While she was adjusting to her new essence, I approached Mr. Bear, who was lying motionless on the cold floor. I was a little apologetic. Although I had assumed and prepared for the worst, I never thought she would actually—
...The hell?
I froze mid-step.

“Uhn...” Surprisingly, Mr. Bear was still alive. In fact, not only was his life intact, but his consciousness seemed to be as well. As soon as I approached, I saw that he was desperately trying to say something despite his frozen state.
It’s been more than four minutes, right?
When I found out that Jencia’s sword was a Serpent’s Fang, I figured he would have died a long time ago. And the conversation I heard earlier had convinced me.
“Carlson! I’ll take care of this, so check on him first! Therrre must be potions in his bag!”
“H-He’s a-already dead!”
While I was interviewing Jencia, I overheard that conversation outside. That was why I had taken down the orcs first, and then the final boss, before even bothering to come over here.
How the hell did he survive?

While traveling together, I had been able to roughly gauge Mr. Bear’s four essences. Two of them had Poison Tolerance, but even without the poison, most people would have died by now if they were left alone for so long after their stomach was pierced like that.
“P-Potion...” Staring up at me, Mr. Bear spoke in a clear voice. I guess the others heard his quiet muttering, too, because—

“Huh? You’re alive! What a rrrelief! Just wait. I’ll make you feel better...” Missha, who had been basking in the aftertaste of the essence, ran our way in surprise. Then she rummaged through Mr. Bear’s bag and took out a high-rank potion. “I’m using the best one that you have, so don’t get mad about it later, okay?”
“Just... pour it...”
“Okay!” Missha opened the lid and poured the potion onto Mr. Bear’s wound.
Chhhhhh!
Air bubbles seeped from the blood that had filled the wound, and it was hardly healed. This was not an effect of Toxin Bestow.
...She must have coated the sword with something.
I had my guesses. I couldn’t be certain, but it must have been a wound exacerbation-type poison that prevented healing and recovery.
“Uh, huh? Why is this...”
“Keep... don’t stop...”
“You’rrre telling me not to stop? O-Okay!”

At Mr. Bear’s request, Missha continued to pour high-rank potions on him. However, after two bottles went by with no improvements, he must have realized something was wrong. “A-Antidote... yellow... tooth...”
“Ah, this! Is it the yellow bottle with the drawing of a fang?”
“Yes...” Mr. Bear got Missha to pull out the antidote. He must have stocked up on a lot of first-aid items like a solo player.
I don’t know about Toxin Bestow, but that’s not going to deal with the poison afflicting him.
Just as I expected, the antidote had little effect. The wound healed at the speed of an ant’s crawl. In the meantime, dark red blood began to flow out.
Chhhhhh...

Two bottles, three bottles, four bottles. Despite the increase in the number of empty potions, Mr. Bear’s condition continued to deteriorate. That was inevitable because the potions couldn’t stop the bleeding. As he continued to lose a significant amount of blood, Mr. Bear could no longer give orders. He couldn’t even feel the pain of the potion in his current state.
“Abman? Wake up!” Missha slapped his cheek and shook his shoulders, but Mr. Bear wouldn’t come to. “W-What do we do? Ah, the advanced potion! Bjorn, let’s use it!”
Missha looked at me like she had just remembered the high-quality potion I’d bought. I pulled it out without regret. “Move.”
“Ah, okay!”
More than one million stones in one bottle. Even this wouldn’t immediately heal the wound, but it should be enough to stop the bleeding.
Chhhhhh!

When a potion of the highest quality, which could even restore limbs, was poured on them, the minor injuries that had been slowly recovering began to heal more efficiently. The bleeding stopped, and Mr. Bear’s breathing stabilized. Of course, he was still in a precarious condition, so I continued to pour normal potions on him.
Chhhhhh!

Five bottles, six bottles, seven bottles... These weren’t mine, but all potions from Mr. Bear’s bag. I had no idea why he carried ten high-rank potions but no advanced ones. It couldn’t be because of money.

“I think that’s enough.” By the time I emptied an additional five bottles of potion on him, more than two-thirds of the wound had healed. Therefore, I stopped the treatment there. At this point, his wounds wouldn’t be fatal, so I decided it would make more sense to continue treatment after the Wound Exacerbation effect had disappeared.
His previously shot nerves seemed to have woken up midway through because Mr. Bear screamed in pain for a while before falling unconscious again. I slowly got up from the ground.
As our eyes met, Carlson said, “Y-You did well.”
I didn’t do anything.

“Come to think of it, we haven’t distributed the loot yet.” The Rift was cleared, so we split the mana stones. After dividing the procured mana stones up by rank, I handed Carlson his share and he cautiously expressed a hesitance to take it. “Uh, I think your math is off...”
He’s a weird guy too. I didn’t just give him a little, but a lot. But his reaction?
“Just take it. You couldn’t even eat the essence.”
Carlson’s share was originally only 5 percent. After Jencia died, that number had grown to 10 percent, but I had paid him 20 percent of the mana stones. That was the cost of his silence.
“If your heart is heavy, don’t go around talking about what happened today.”
“Ah, yes! I won’t!” I didn’t know if he’d actually keep that promise, but it was better than nothing. “But... why do you think Miss Jencia did something like that?”
“Is there any reason to plunder other than money? Apparently, this wasn’t even the first time.”
“I see...”

Carlson left the Rift through the portal after receiving his settlement and sating his curiosity. Having gone through so much shit, it seemed he didn’t want to stay here a moment longer than necessary. I was chuckling at that when Mr. Bear woke up.
“Where am I...?”

chapters.title: Chapter 109: Baby Barbarian (2)
paragraphs: “Ugh!”
“Don’t move. Your wound hasn’t healed yet.”
“...Did you save me?”
“Even used my advanced potion to do it.”

Mr. Bear was awake and had a complicated expression on his face. He seemed happy to be alive, but also a little suspicious. Well, he of all people should know how much profit we could have made if he’d died.
“Thank you, thirty million stones would be—”

That may not have been the exact amount, but since it had been Jencia’s estimate and she had a lot of plundering experience, it must be about right. Mr. Bear, who at this point in his career would be knowledgeable about the psychology of adventurers, quietly muttered, “...I was lucky.”
I agreed. In this situation, how many adventurers would choose to resuscitate someone rather than wait for them to die?
“I’ll pay for the advanced potion.” Well, duh. “How much is it?”
“Hmm, five million stones should do it.”
“...An advanced potion should be around one million.”
“Is it? Then it looks like the merchants scammed me.”

At my sly dealing, Mr. Bear looked dazed for a second, then smiled. “Certainly, the price of an item can change depending on circumstance.” Like the seasoned rank-five adventurer he was, he seemed to have understood exactly what I was saying. “Five million stones... That’s a reasonable price.”
“Thank you for thinking that.”
“...What arrre you guys talking about?”
You keep quiet. The adults are talking.
“But I don’t have that much money right now. I’ll pay you five million stones once we get back to the city.”
“Hmm.”

“I’ll leave this item with you instead. I’d like you to return it to me once I pay you back.” Mr. Bear took out a skull-shaped bracelet and handed it to me. “It’s a numbered item. I’ve only used it once, but it’s still worth more than five million stones.”

Afterward, Mr. Bear briefly explained the object to me, but even if he hadn’t, I already knew what it was. No. 7611: The Deceit of the Necromancer. When the wearer received a fatal blow, they fell into suspended animation and were immune to damage for a certain period of time. It broke after three uses.
I was wondering how he was still alive. It must have been because of this.
I asked him if he wouldn’t just give me this instead, but Mr. Bear firmly stated that this was collateral and vowed to pay me with money. “Don’t even think about stealing it, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
What the heck, how did you know?
When I flinched, Mr. Bear chuckled. “I’ve heard of the barbarian that travels with someone from the Cat Tribe. And that young lady also said your real name several times.”
“Uhh, did I?”
“Don’t worry. I understand the feeling of wanting to avoid attention. I won’t be telling anyone.”
Well, I was glad. I wasn’t sure about anyone else, but it’d get a little annoying if this reached Dwalkie’s or Hikurod’s ears, since I’d evaded them by saying I received a commission to be here.

“So, what happened? Is the bitch dead? And you two took down the guardian?” Mr. Bear, who had come back from the dead, first finished calculating the cost of his life, then asked what had happened. I just nodded my head because I couldn’t go into all the details. Fortunately, Mr. Bear, who knew adventuring etiquette, did not pry. “Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel. I thought your reputation was exaggerated, but looking at what you’ve done today, it doesn’t seem that’s the case.”

He must’ve been surprised that we took down the guardian with just the two of us. Anyway, after deciding on a time and place to meet back in the city and distributing his share of the mana stones, Mr. Bear’s wounds were completely healed.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, and Missha Karlstein. Thank you for saving me. I won’t forget this.”
With that, the man rode out of the Rift through the portal. A cool guy to the end.
After Mr. Bear left, we took a moment to look at The Deceit of the Necromancer. Two out of the three jewels on it glowed. In other words, there were two uses left.
I’ll just wear this until I give it back.
Just in case, I clipped the bracelet on my wrist. I remembered Mr. Bear’s words to take care of it before returning it but...
Well, I’ll make good use of it before that.
Anyway, I set this issue aside and took some time to think.
Five million stones...
In exchange for the highest-quality potion, I had gotten a decent payment. Well, if you compared it to thirty million stones, it was just a drop in the bucket.
I guess I’ve become a real savage.

I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t at all greedy. Besides, I didn’t have to go through the effort of saving him. Whether Mr. Bear was a good guy or a bad guy if I had just waited patiently, a sum large enough to upgrade my Spirit Imprint to stage six in one go would have landed right in my lap.

I had poured a potion on his wound not for some philosophical reason—like the fact that leaving someone to die for money that could be acquired another way would make me no different from a plunderer—but because of Missha.
“...W-Why arrre you looking at me like that? It’s making me anxious again.”
“It’s nothing.”

Whether my code of ethics was corrupted or not, I decided that waiting for a man to die was not something I could do while my colleague was by my side. However, after the dust settled, I began to think.
What if I was alone?
It wouldn’t just be to enjoy wealth and glory. In this world, money was power—it was like life itself. If it weren’t for Missha, what choice would I have made in the face of that huge temptation?
...That’s probably not a question to already be worrying about.
Whether I wanted to or not, as long as I kept working as an adventurer, I would learn the answer someday. So I cut my thoughts off there and packed my things.
“Huh? Are we not going out?”

Where would we go? There were still two things we needed to take with us. I led Missha through the icy passageway. It was originally blocked, but it opened up earlier when the tyrant Tarunbas appeared. If we moved along this passage, we’d reach the second stage we were previously in.
“Wow... how do you know something like that? Information on Rrrifts is very expensive.”
“Thanks to Ragna.”

“Oh... that woman...” When I used Ragna giving me access to the secret library as an excuse, Missha accepted it and moved on. Maybe it was because she didn’t read any, but she tended to believe me when I said I read something in a book.
Bam!

After reaching the second stage, I climbed the stairs and smashed the third pillar from the top. This item, which I had overlooked in favor of observing the mafioso, permanently increased Cold Resistance when taken.
[You have taken An Ice Chunk Imbued with Mana. Your Cold Resistance has permanently increased by +1.]

Since Missha had enough Cold Resistance, I took it. I was planning on giving her the next thing, though. After passing through the first stage, we left Glacier Cave. Then we passed the frozen lake and headed to the starting point.
Bam!
After breaking a small pond near the starting point with my mace, I dove into the ice water and took out a red bead made of ice.
“Here, eat.”
“Shouldn’t you tell me what it is firrrst?”
Would I feed you something bad?
Still, I offered a brief explanation, which rid Missha of her anxiety, and she swallowed it.
[Missha Karlstein has taken the Ice Crystal. Her Cold Sensitivity has permanently increased by +3.]

In truth, the Ice Crystal was Glacier Cave’s signature item. In addition to increasing the user’s sensitivity, you could eat it up to three times, so whenever I was building an ice-type character, I always came to Glacier Cave at the beginning of the game.
I’ll have to come back here again after the three-month cooldown.
I was quite cold from diving into the water so I built a bonfire and dried myself off. Then I put on the clothes I had taken off earlier. “We’re done now.”
“Oh, arrre we finally leaving?”
You wish.
I took a blanket out of my bag.
“...Why are you opening up a blanket?”

“We didn’t sleep much on night watch. Let’s get some rest before we leave.” There was no safer place in the labyrinth than a cleared rift. It was a bit cold, but there was no better place than this to get a good night’s sleep. “Don’t worry. There is no one here but us.”
“...I-I see. So are we just resting for a short while?”
“Yes. It’s cold, so come here. Let’s share the blanket.”
“...Sh-should we?”
A cold breeze brushed past my nose. The campfire was warm. It was nighttime, so the dark blue Milky Way spread across the sky above and twinkled.
“Bjorn... are you sleeping?”
Honkkk!
“D-Does that mean you arrre?”
We closed our eyes for a while.
[You have entered the first-floor Crystal Cave.]
Rank-five adventurer Abman Urikfried opened his eyes in the Crystal Cave and let out a long breath. It was then that he realized.
...I’m alive.

After leaving the party he’d been a part of for a long time due to an incident, he had been working on his own. As a result, he faced many dangers, since the labyrinth was not an easy place to navigate alone. But it had never been as dangerous as it had been this time around. He’d knocked on death’s door before just barely coming back to life.
...I was lucky.

He kept thinking about this, but it was true. Despite running into a disturbed bitch who had entered the Rift and hidden her identity for the purpose of looting others, there had been an adventurer in the party who had been kind enough to save him without having any connection to him. He also happened to have an advanced potion. What were the odds of that?
I’ll have to make an offering to the temple when I get back or something.
No matter how he looked at it, it was truly a miracle. After enjoying the afterglow of survival for a while, though, he shifted gears.
Anyway—Bjorn, son of Yandel?

Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel. He had heard his name many times in the city. Of course, back then, he hadn’t thought much of it, just that there was a peculiar new fellow in their midst. To a rank-five adventurer like him, an adventurer with an epithet was nothing strange.
He’s an interesting one.

He was different from the average barbarian. Although he may have seemed simple and ignorant, he was skilled, quick-witted, and good at negotiating. To put it bluntly, he was like a barbarian who had been adventuring for a long time. Pure, but never naïve. That was how he’d managed to notice the black heart of a woman he didn’t even know.
Earned an epithet in the third month and already this seasoned? He’ll be big one day.

He harbored no ill will toward him. No, on the contrary, all he felt was gratitude. They said it was the fate of an adventurer to chase after money, but how many adventurers had he met had gotten swallowed up by money instead? Asking for five million stones for treatment? It could be said that the barbarian had already done his duty as an adventurer by not just stripping Abman of his equipment. This only seemed more special when you considered the large number of people who had seemingly forgotten that duty.
That’s probably why that woman follows him so.
Abman recalled the cat woman who appeared to be the man’s teammate. The barbarian had given her the Yeti and Guardian essences for nothing in return.
That woman is very lucky too.
It must have been a blessing to have a comrade like that. If only his old teammates were half as great as that man, he wouldn’t be working alone like this.
No, wait...
At first, it was just a fleeting thought. However, his expression shifted as he seriously considered it. He was starting to doubt whether he should work alone because of this incident.
Certainly, a guy like that might not be bad. Even I can’t work alone forever. And it looks like they only have two people too.
Soon, Abman came to a decision. The various clans and regular parties that had tried to recruit him would be disgruntled if they found out, but... oh well.
I’ll have to bring it up when we meet up again in the city.
He liked that barbarian very much.

chapters.title: Chapter 110: Baby Barbarian (3)
paragraphs: Right around the start of the third day, at 00:51, we left Glacier Cave and returned to Crystal Cave. We’d run into a lot of trouble, but the income from this Rift was off the charts. Jencia’s equipment, Mr. Bear’s five million stones, and the essences of a Yeti and Guardian: As a reward for clearing a first-floor Rift, we saw an outrageous profit. I had earned less than two million stones in two months with a party of five on the fourth floor.
Goddamn it.
I realized once again that I could only be on the receiving end of this kind of luck by going through all kinds of shit first.
Slice!

Soon Missha sliced down a Blade Wolf that was approaching us with her new sword and exclaimed in admiration. “Ooh! What is this sword? It’s so nice!” It was still the same one-shot kill, but apparently it had a different feel to it.
“You’ll only know for sure after the appraisal, but there is a high possibility that sword is a numbered item.”
“A n-numbered item? Th-then isn’t it very expensive?”

Seeing the flustered look on Missha’s face, I let out an involuntary laugh. It wasn’t just the Serpent’s Fang. The leather greaves she was wearing were also high-quality equipment since they were made of Wyvern leather, a second-grade material.
With these specs, I won’t have to worry about her until the fifth floor.
I felt like I’d finished a homework assignment. Since the initial and mid-level setup was over, she would now pull the weight of one person without any additional upgrades for a while.
“So, are we going to the second floor now?”
“We should.”
I followed the compass with Missha. We had achieved what we’d entered the labyrinth to do this time around, but it would be a waste to spend the rest of the time messing around.
Although we don’t have a scout... we may be able to reach the third floor if we’re lucky.
Anyhow, Missha took full responsibility for the monsters we encountered on the way. Now that her sword had changed and her stats had risen significantly, she had to get used to her new abilities.
“Uh, Bjorn? I think I’m done now.”
“Are you sure?”
“Uh... that... noooo... I’ll keep going. But... I’m rrreally only asking this just in case, but... You’re not letting me do all the work because you’re too lazy, rrright?”
“...Are you doubting me?”
“N-No! Never! Why would I do that?!”

Missha’s reasonable suspicions aside, I moved along at a comfortable pace and helped her with her training. Her sword was new, but she also needed to get used to her new essence. The sight made me pleased.
I really didn’t expect the Guardian’s essence to come out.
When it came to an ice-type route, the Lycanthrope’s essence performed just as well as a Yeti’s.
[Lycanthrope – Rank 7
Agility: +10
Cutting Force: +12
Cold Sensitivity: +15
Cold Resistance: +10
Physical Resistance: +7
Fighting Spirit: +10]
It had Cutting Force, which was an essential stat for sword-type characters, and its passive skill was too good to be true.
[(P) Blood from the Snowfield - Increases Cold Sensitivity 1.5 times.]
Not only did that ability shine in the second half, but it also had good synergy with the Yeti’s Cold Condensation. The same went for its active skills.
[(A) Ice Crush - Slightly increases the damage dealt to enemies in the Frostbite state, and significantly increases damage to enemies in the Frozen state.]
There’s no need to explain that one, so pass.
[(A) Fortitude - Nullifies the Inability to Act state.]
Although it had the downside of consuming a lot of Soul Power, Fortitude was also a good skill that greatly increased the stability of damage dealers who were vulnerable to Cold Condensation.
Above all, with this, I don’t need to worry about the Mana Resistance stat that much.

Originally, we should have only been able to choose one of these skills, but what Missha had absorbed was none other than the Guardian’s essence. Not only could she use both skills, but its stats were about 1.5 times higher than normal essences.
“If possible, try to attack somewhere other than its vitals.”
“Uh, but it still dies in one blow...”
“Then punch it instead.”
“Ok—huh? It still dies in one blow.”

I licked my lips at the sight of the Blade Wolf getting turned into an ice cube in one punch with Cold Condensation. Was it because it was a rank-nine monster? Before she could follow the blow up with Ice Crush, it turned into light and disappeared, so Missha couldn’t properly train.
“You can do the rest on the next floor.”
“...I have to keep going?”
Tsk, who do you think you’re trying to swindle?
“I repeat—”
“I know. The easy rrroad is the slow road.”
Uh. Um... right.
After rendering me speechless, Missha took the lead with a grin. Judging by the gentle sway at the tip of her tail, she seemed to be having fun.
...If I ever do anything wrong, I’ll just have to pretend to lose an argument to make her feel better.
Writing this down as number thirteen in the Missha Manual in my head, I followed the excited beastwoman. Time passed just like that, until it was about seven hours after we came out of the Rift.
We should be in the dark zone.
I stopped in my tracks.
Whooom!
The ground shuddered slightly, and the crystals embedded in the walls of the cave began to glow brightly. The color of the glow also changed from a soft purple to an intense red.
I expected this to happen, but it looks like it really was summoned.
This all meant that the Lord of the First Floor had been summoned.
“It’s nothing, keep moving.”
“It’s nothing? I’ve neverrr seen anything like that in my life—”
“Someone just summoned the Lord of the Floor. There won’t be any fallout, so don’t—”
“What? The Lord of the Floor?!”
Geez, my eardrums. Perhaps the Lord of the Third Floor remained a point of trauma for her. Missha freaked out and clung to me. But there was no need for her to be so surprised.
“Missha, calm down.”

Unlike the one on the third floor, the first floor’s Lord was calm. The method for summoning it was based on probability—it appeared when more than five people gathered in one place after the three-day mark. Even after it was summoned, the portals to the second floor remained open and the monsters that spawned didn’t change, either. And the biggest difference was that, once summoned, Riakis went around slaughtering everyone on the floor until he died, but this guy just quietly disappeared if the raid against him failed.
“S-So we’re okay?”
“Yeah, so don’t worry.”

After I calmly explained the situation, Missha took a deep breath and regained her composure. But when her anxiety subsided, curiosity bloomed in its place. “But who the hell summoned it by mistake? Everrryone knows that no more than five people should be in the same spot down here.”
“Well, maybe it wasn’t a mistake.”
“Not a mistake?”

I just shrugged and kept quiet. It was highly likely that the person who’d bought the strategy for dealing with the first-floor Lord from the Ghost Busters community was the one who had summoned it... But I couldn’t just tell her that, could I?
What an over-eager one. They must have only had two weeks to prepare.
Alternatively, maybe they weren’t impatient but had enough influence to complete all their preparations in that time.
I might be able to find out who that user is.

I decided to see if there was a rumor going around about a clan or party that had succeeded in hunting the Lord of the Floor once I was back in the city. Meanwhile, I was starting to once again feel Rotmiller’s absence.
Geez, to think it took almost an entire day.
After wandering around with only the compass to guide us, we reached the second-floor portal. The one I chose was the Land of the Dead, which was connected to the Ghoul District in the south.
[You have entered the Land of the Dead on the second floor.]

Black earth soaked with moisture, exceptionally low visibility even for the second floor, and the screams of banshees serving as background music... for some reason when I set foot on this soil, nostalgia filled me.
“Long time no see.”
It was here that Ainar and I broke some skeleton bones, beat Death Fiends into mochi, and met that deranged bitch and almost died.
Goddamn it.
Was it because I was being reminded of the past? I suddenly felt my mood darken.
“Ugh, this place gives me bad energy every time. I prefer the Rock Deserrrt.”
“Rotmiller isn’t here, so we don’t have a choice.”

Since this was the center of the map, we could go anywhere, but I had chosen the Land of the Dead for a simple reason. Of the second-floor maps, this was the one where it was easiest to reach the third floor. We’d probably get a little lost at the end, but for now, we just needed to go north.
Besides, it’s just the two of us, so I should summon the Death Knight and kill it before we go.

I didn’t really need the essence, but this monster would be hard to catch when there were five of us, so I decided to gather the experience points now. Aside from a few rifts, it was a monster you could only run into on the sixth floor.
Since it’s a rank-six monster, I can test how strong she is now.
Of course, before I summoned it, Missha would have to complete her training.
“Let’s go.”
Moving north, we quickly escaped the area where rank-nine monsters such as skeletons and ghouls appeared. It took about five hours. The terrain changed from a wet swamp to hard stone.
“Kwoooh!”

Before long, a Death Fiend appeared. The so-called “newbie cutters” were walking around in groups of four since it was the third day. In the past, Ainar and I went through a lot of trouble just to take down one.
Well, now I have a body that won’t die even if I let it get beaten to a pulp.

The Death Fiend was a monster that specialized in defense and regeneration. It summoned ghouls, but there was no way a rank-nine would be able to deal with us. To put it simply, these were the perfect opponents to test out Missha’s new skills.
“I’ll divert their attention, so don’t worry and just focus on using your new abilities.”
“Okay.”
“Behelahhh!”
As soon as I cast Wild Outburst, the Death Fiend, who had been staring at us from the edge of our torchlight, screamed and charged.
“Kwoooh!”
First, I blocked two of them with my shield, then ducked and flung another to the side. The last one I let hit me because I couldn’t be bothered.
Slam!

Maybe it was because this was the first rank-eight monster I had ever successfully hunted, but a strange feeling came over me. In the past, just one of them had been enough to push me back in a power struggle.
“Kuwogh?!”
But this time, when I put a little more force behind my shield, the Death Fiend bastards got helplessly flung away.
“Not done yet?”
“I’m ready!”
Missha finished casting Enhanced Cold Condensation and brandished the Serpent’s Fang.
Khak!
It was blocked by a Death Fiend’s shield hand, which was made of bones and muscles, but the attempt at defense was pointless. Its arm froze up to the elbow in one simple blow.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Ice Crush.]
When Missha swung her other blade at the now-frozen area, its arm shattered and scattered all over the floor.

“Kwu... ogh?” The wound could not be regenerated even with Body Preservation because it had the Cold attribute. The monster didn’t even seem to feel pain, and only had a confused look on its face. It seemed to instinctively sense that it was in danger, though.
[Death Fiend has cast Call of the Dead.]

When the four monsters cast their summoning skill at the same time, the number of ghouls crawling out of the ground reached a whopping forty. Of course, this also didn’t mean much. My body, which had once easily been torn up by their nails, was now covered in a breastplate made of lithinum. And with an added increase in Physical Resistance, even my bare skin was quite durable.
“Grrr...?”
I shed no blood despite the beating. And even when I did, it melted the hands of the ghouls, who were weak to acid. But my wounds quickly healed even in the middle of all that.
“Bjorn... are you... some sort of monster?”
How can you call a person a monster?
“Stop standing around and get rid of it,” I answered in a grumble, covering my wounded pride.
Geez, once I was done with this build, she wouldn’t even see me as a person.

After that, we continued her training while moving north. Thanks to that, Missha got a sense of how much she had to freeze something until it was affected by either Frostbite or Frozen. After running into the Chimera Wolf, which had a skill that allowed it to incapacitate its targets, she also perfectly mastered Fortitude.
“Um, well? I just put more force into it and it worrrks.”

After she learned how, I advised her to only use it when absolutely necessary since it consumed a lot of Soul Power. If Soul Power ran out, she wouldn’t be able to use Enhance, Toxin Bestow, Ice Crush, or anything.
“Do I look like a little kid to you?”
She was not wrong. That was because she had only had two skills even after hitting level four. She wouldn’t have ever had to keep track of her Soul Power to avoid running out.
Even if I keep telling her this, it won’t be as effective as letting her experience it for herself.
For that reason, we continued to push ourselves while hunting. As a result of constantly and recklessly using her skills, her Soul Power finally bottomed out.
“...It feels kind of strrrange. It’s not that my body is tired or anything, but I guess it feels empty?”
“That’s why I told you to ration your energy better.”
“...I thought this much would be fine.”
It was about time for a break, so we prepared our camp. We found a building with a wall, and while starting a fire there, we took turns sleeping. I wasn’t sure how much time had passed when...
“Hahaha, is that true?”
“That’s right, my friend.”

I heard chattering from twenty or thirty yards away. At first, I thought they were just passing adventurers, but as I kept hearing conversations, I concluded that they had settled down for the night unaware that we were camping nearby.
Well, it’s about time to wake up Missha anyway. There’s no need to tell them to get lost.
I decided to be generous as I waited out the remaining time in my shift.
“By the way, this barbarian is sleeping without a care in the world.”
“Be quiet. He might wake up.”
“Leave him to sleep. That body of his is costly. He should sleep while he can.”
I heard something I couldn’t just ignore.
Honkkkkk!
As I took stock of the situation, it became clear that a baby barbarian was sleeping in a den of wolves.

chapters.title: Chapter 111: Baby Barbarian (4)
paragraphs: It was pretty common for barbarians to team up with humans. No matter how high their physical stats or fighting instincts, even barbarians needed allies after the first floor. The standard approach was to form a team around the second or third month to head up to the second floor.
The problem is that it’s rare to find decent teammates.

Elves, dwarves, beastmen—the other races got the better end of the deal. Not only were they less naive than the barbarians, who’d honed only their combat skills in the holy land, but their hearts didn’t sell for a high price as magic ingredients.
“What are the other guys doing? Most are dead.”
Already, not even a third of the barbarians who had gone through the coming-of-age ceremony with me were left. Could that really be attributed to monsters alone?
No way.
Reasonably suspicious, I listened in on their conversation.
“Then I’ll rest now too. Have a nice watch.”
“Was it my turn next?”

Everyone fell asleep in turns, and the topic of the baby barbarian did not continue beyond that. But that wasn’t a big problem because I had a rough idea of what the other three were like from that short conversation.
It doesn’t seem like they intend to do anything today.
They must have been planning on working him to the bone, then killing him on the last day, since that was more practical.
...What should I do?

I didn’t know what to do. As a barbarian myself, I did not want to ignore the baby barbarian in danger. But I couldn’t just follow them around forever and keep an eye on them until they revealed their true colors.
Should I just go and kill them all?

I frowned and shook my head. That was an easy and convenient option, but not the best. It didn’t matter that I still had no evidence that those three were plunderers. I was confident I could convince Missha and the baby barbarian with a plausible enough argument.
But even if I did, the same thing would just happen again.
Sometimes you had to experience something yourself to truly learn from it.
Anyway, our main goal here was training, so I can invest up to one day...
After thinking it over, I came up with a plan and woke Missha. “Missha.”
I held up a finger to tell her to stay quiet and moved to a place where we wouldn’t be heard. Then, I briefly explained the plan.
Even while rubbing her eyes, Missha listened without complaints. “Um... So, you’rrre saying they might be looters?”
“Yes. If it’s okay with you, I’d like to take some time to check it out.”
“I don’t mind. Since it’s a barrrbarian, it’s not like they’re a stranger.”
“...Not a stranger?”
“N-No! That’s not what I meant... I just mean it could be someone I’ve met beforrre.”

She seemed to be referring to how I had been acting as a guide for the young warriors for the past several months. Hmm, maybe this guy was one of them. Although I had advised the baby barbarians to be wary of humans countless times, they wouldn’t really understand what I meant until they experienced it for themselves.
“That’s it, then. Let’s change our clothes.” We needed to make some preparations to pull this plan off. I put my mace, breastplate, and the shield made of lithinum into my bag.
As for my weapon... I can just say I lost it.

After finishing my preparations, I did a final check of my appearance. Excluding the helmet, I looked exactly like a baby barbarian without any iron equipment. And beside me was an amateur beastwoman.

“Ughh... this is uncomforrrtable...” To make sure the plan went off without a hitch, I got Missha to put on Jencia’s beginner equipment instead of her usual things. But for some reason, Missha kept fiddling with the chest and annoying me.
“What are you doing?”
“Huh? It’s just the chest area is super tight...”
“Chest area?”

When I glanced down, Missha smacked me in the stomach. Judging from the chill seeping into my bones, it seemed I’d gotten a proper dose of cold damage. “Where arrre you looking? It’s definitely not because I’m fatter than that woman, okay?”
I mean, I didn’t say anything. I only looked in the first place because it was an issue I hadn’t considered. Her original armor must have been around the same size.
When I pointed out the contradiction, Missha replied without missing a beat. “The other one was small, too, but it didn’t have an irrron plate.”

Well, if you say so. Jencia and Missha both had the nimble bodies of agility characters, but I was sure they had their differences. For example, their builds. This kid was on the taller side. I hadn’t measured it, but she must have been around 5′6″. She also gave off a standoffish vibe, which made me think she was the feisty type at first.
“It’s just the chest area that’s tight, and the rest is rrrather loose. Understood?”
“Okay.” I didn’t know what she wanted from me here so I kept my response vague.
Sensing this, Missha let out a deep sigh. “Hah, right... what would you know about a woman’s body, anyway?”
“Yes, you are completely right.”
“Are you going to keep answering me so insincerrrely?”
“If you’re ready, let’s go.” This was not the time for idle chitchat, so we started walking back the way we came after that, deliberately making loud noises.
“Behelahhh!”
“Kyaaa! Why are you scrrreaming all of a sudden?!”
“I just felt like doing it!”
“What?” Missha shot me a bewildered look, but the payoff was great.
“W-Who are you!” A cry instantly rang out from beyond the darkness.

“Wait! There are people over there!” I shouted innocently and ran in the direction from which I’d heard the sound. Before long, the darkness of the labyrinth came to an end and the four adventurers around a lit bonfire came into view—three humans and one baby barbarian, who was still sleeping soundly.
“Stop, don’t come any closer.” The three humans were already awake and wary of us.
“Royce, wake him up, fast.”
A bowman named Royce woke the baby barbarian with a prod of his foot.
“W-What is it? Is it a monster?”
“It’s adventurers.”
“Adventurers? Then why are you waking me up? I was in the middle of a good nap...”
“Didn’t I tell you earlier? Adventurers can be just as dangerous as monsters.”
“Ah! I remember! But... that man is one of my people.” In the middle of nodding at the bowman’s words, the baby barbarian spotted me and waved happily. “I am Kharon, son of Tarson!”

“I am Bjon, son of Thor!” I took the opportunity to move forward, shake his hand, and even bump our shoulders together. Then, when I glanced over, the looks on everyone’s faces were a spectacle; not just the three humans, but even Missha, whom I’d told the plan to beforehand.
What the hell are these barbarian bastards doing?

The look in their eyes was clearly saying something like that. Picking up on this, Kharon shot me a look that seemed to say don’t worry, then told his teammates, “Everyone lower your weapons! Thor’s son, Bjon, is not a bad adventurer!”
“Yes! I am not a bad adventurer!”

At our words, the bowman and spearman looked at one person in particular. It seemed that guy was the leader. The man sighed and nodded, and everyone lowered their weapons. I guess he figured it would be ridiculous to keep their guards up at this point.
“So, barbarian—”
“It’s Bjon, son of Thor.”
“Yes, Thor—”
“Thor is my father’s name.”
“Ahem, Bjon—”
“We’re not that close yet, so I’d like you to call me by my full name.”
The leader, who had been interrupted three times in a row, looked quite annoyed but held onto his patience and smiled. He addressed me again. “So, Thor’s son, Bjon?”
“Speak.”
“If you have no business here, I’d like you to leave. As you can see, we were resting.”

The leader’s request was reasonable and logical. It was polite and customary for adventurers not to approach each other at all. But so what? Right now I was a big, sweet baby barbarian who didn’t know anything about stuff like that.
“What a coincidence that you’re resting!” I shouted like that was even better. “We were just looking for a place to rest!”
“So... what does that have to do with us?”
“This is meant to be. Let’s rest together! We could be... night companions? Yes, that!”
“Night companions?” As if they had just heard something they shouldn’t have, the expressions of the three humans screwed up.

It wasn’t that I didn’t understand why. Seeking out companions for the night was a tradition limited to the first floor. They would never have imagined they would end up receiving such a proposal from some barbarian on the second floor, where adventurers operated in parties.
“Hah...” As if he didn’t even know where to start explaining, the leader touched his forehead.
But meanwhile, Kharon nodded. “Ohh, that’s a good idea. Come here, I’ve been lying here and it’s not as hard as everywhere else.”
It was total chaos. The leader exhibited superhuman patience and explained the customs of adventurers to me. To sum it up, it was simple.
“So, you mean... you don’t make night companions on the second floor?”
“Yes, that’s it. If you understand—”

Well, understanding was for those who were willing to understand. Instead, I spoke in a tone that suggested I found everything he said genuinely pathetic. “You guys are so stupid! If we all sleep together, we can sleep more!”
“Huh?”

“If you have a brain, think about it. There are four of you and two of us. If six people take turns keeping watch, each person... Anyway, you can sleep more!” It was a hard-headed assertion from a barbarian, from start to finish. Everyone looked dazed, almost like they were wondering if they were hallucinating this entire conversation.

Oh, except for one person. “That’s... true! Why haven’t any adventurers done this sooner?” As Kharon vigorously nodded at my argument, his team realized that there was no point discussing this any further.

“Look. We’ll take care of our own, so you should take your group and go—” The leader looked away from me to speak to Missha, then suddenly stopped. Apparently, he had only seen her face up to this point. His voice, which had been filled with irritation, changed before he knew it. “Ahem. I mean, that’s definitely how it usually works, but what do you think?”

Apparently, Missha did not appreciate the way those eyes were scanning her. She tensed, but when I shot her a look, her expression shifted. “Well... I’m not surrre. Since you guys have a barrrbarian, too, you don’t seem like dangerrrous people...”
“Haha, the same goes for you as well.”

“Anyway, he’s lost his weapon, so I was worrried about leaving him alone during the night watch. So if it’s okay with you guys, I don’t think it would be a bad idea to just spend the night togetherrr...”
“Darn, you lost your weapon?” The man shot me a strange look at Missha’s words. It seemed that he had just now noticed that I was empty-handed.
“Oh, my weapon? I accidentally dropped it in a fight with a monster and it disappeared!”
“I see.” When I offered up an excuse, the man believed it, just like that. After all, barbarians were total cheat characters.
Anyway, this should be enough bait...
I made the final offer in a clear voice. “So, are you going to be our night companions or not? Decide quickly. Because I’m getting sleepy.”
If he declined, I was planning on going our separate ways. If he refused even after I had gone this far, then it was likely I had misread those three.

“Well... this is definitely not the norm, but...” the leader blurted, exchanging glances with the other two humans. Then he smiled brightly. “But since you’re in a tough spot, sending you away would be too heartless.”
“If you say it in such a complicated way, I can’t understand you.”
“...You can spend the night here if you want.”
I barely suppressed my laughter because I could see through his intentions so clearly.
It seemed everyone here was scheming.
Anyway, just like that, a one-night relationship happened to get established. It was kind of weird to describe it that way, but oh well. We exchanged introductions first.
“This is Royce, that’s Victor, and I’m Briol.” Royce the bowman, Victor the spearman, and the leader-slash-hammer warrior Briol.
...No Hans?
Maybe they were using fake names? No, if he had used fake names, that baby barbarian would have thought it strange.
Feeling slightly uneasy, Missha and I lay down nearby. The desire to open up a blanket was very tempting, but then they’d realize I had an expandable backpack.
“You guys get some rest. I’ll push your turn back to the end of the rotation.”
“Ohh, you guys are really nice adventurers!”
“Hahaha... this guy.”
Anyway, as soon as I lay down, Missha whispered in my ear. “Bjorn.”
“Be quiet.”
“Do we really have to go this farrr?” Although she had obeyed all of my instructions, Missha didn’t seem pleased about our current situation.
True, even if these guys were amateurs, no one would feel comfortable lying down defenseless like this.
“Just hold on. I’ll owe you a favor for this.”
“...Really? You prrromise?”

I stuck with my guns, even tossing Missha a new carrot. There was a possibility that as of today, the baby barbarian Kharon Tarson would be reborn as a warrior, suspicious of humans and killing predators.

chapters.title: Chapter 112: Baby Barbarian (5)
paragraphs: Honkkk!

After pretending to fall asleep with the baby barbarian’s snores serving as background music, I heard a rustling sound from the direction of the campfire. It sounded like the other three were having some kind of written conversation with each other. I could roughly surmise what the contents of said conversation were.
What are you going to do?
What else? Kill them now.
Starting with who?

They were probably deciding who to kill first. A proper son of a bitch would not let this opportunity pass them by. After all, it was a whopping double event, a chance to obtain two barbarian hearts worth 1.8 million stones.
The woman last. Let’s deal with the barbarians first.
I predicted what conclusion they would have reached. They’d probably try to kill me or Kharon first. Therefore, I focused more on my hearing.
Step.
I could hear quiet footsteps slowly approaching me—two moving this way, and one moving toward Kharon.
They’re planning on taking us both out at once.
That wasn’t a bad decision on their part. They’d have to split up, but a simultaneous attack would reduce the probability of something unexpected happening. Even so, the outcome would be the same.
Step.
The moment the two figures stopped right next to me, my upper body sprang up. “I’m hungry—huh? What are you guys doing over here?”
The spearman and leader holding the sledgehammer were so surprised that they choked on their spit. When I sneakily glanced to the side, I saw the bowman aiming at the sleeping baby barbarian.
I pretended not to notice, though, playing it cool. “Ah, did you wake up hungry too?”

When I rubbed my stomach, they concluded that I hadn’t seen the bowman. The guys exchanged glances with each other and then laughed awkwardly. “Th-that’s right. I mean, I’m hungry. Why don’t we go over there and have a meal together?”
“Is it meat?”
“...Of course. There’s dried meat in my backpack over there.”
“Dried meat!”
“Quiet. The others are asleep.”
“Okay...” I nodded. Just as I was about to take the lead, something collided with the back of my head.
Whack!

It seemed the leader had whacked me with his hammer. “Huh?” But there was no way that my skull, which was fine even after taking blows from an orc warrior, would be cracked by something like that. “What was that?”

When I calmly looked back at them, I could see dazed looks on the two men’s faces. I understood where they were coming from. Even though he’d hit me in the head with a hammer, I didn’t even stumble, let alone groan in pain.

“Uh, umm...” The leader didn’t even think to strike again and just stood there, frozen. Well, I was sure his thoughts were rather scrambled at the moment. After all, the most reasonable conclusion he could come to right now was that I had been hiding my identity, but that would be too devastating a truth to believe.
“Oh, did your hand slip?” I said with a grin.
“Uh, huh?”
“You shouldn’t make mistakes like that, no matter how hungry you are.”
Nothing I was saying made sense to me, either, but surprisingly the leader just flashed an awkward smile and nodded. “A-Ah! I’m sorry.”
Sorry, my ass. Do I really look like that much of a dumbass barbarian?
“It seems I’ve made a mist—”
Whack!
Slump.
Because I had no mace, I punched him in the face instead. The outcome was pretty much the same. The leader collapsed to the floor with the bones of his face sunken in.
“Huh...?” The spear bastard next to him was still staring at me like he had no idea what was going on.
“Ah, I was hungry, too, so my hand slipped.” I said this as a genuine apology but it seemed he wasn’t willing to accept it.
“Royce! What are you doing? Shoot!” The spearman gave the order in lieu of their unconscious leader.
Whip!

Soon, the bowman fired an arrow. I wondered if there was some kind of miscommunication at play here, though. He must’ve been ordering him to shoot me, but the arrow flew at the baby barbarian instead.
Stab!

Fortunately, Kharon, who woke up after hearing the spearman’s shout, twisted out of the way and avoided getting hit in a vital area. “Ugh, Royce! What are you doing?!” With an arrow stuck in his shoulder, he quickly stood up and grabbed the bowman by the neck.
Cough, cough!
“Speak! I asked why you shot me!”
“I-It’s... let me go...!”
“Aren’t you going to explain?!”
Looks like I won’t have to worry about that guy anymore.

When I moved my gaze back to the spearman, I saw him slowly stepping back toward the darkness. It was almost commendable that he could even come up with a plan to abandon his teammate in this situation, but did he really think that was going to work?
“...They really were plundererrrs.” The fight wrapped up when Missha, who had been watching the proceedings from start to finish, struck him on the nape of the neck with the handle of a knife.
“How did this happen?!” Kharon asked, unable to hide his confusion. However, the choked-out and unconscious bowman had no way of answering.

“These guys are looters.” With that, I kindly explained everything, from the fact that the heart of a barbarian sold for a high price to the fact that I hid my identity because these guys were suspicious.
“What? It can’t be! These are my teammates...!” Our innocent baby barbarian refused to believe it. No, to be exact, he didn’t want to believe it.
“Kharon, son of Tarson, grow up.”
“... Are you trying to insult me?! I am already a warrior!”
“Then why are you trying to deny reality?”
Kharon pressed his lips together at my question. He must have already known deep down that everything I had said was true.

The barbarian race wasn’t actually particularly unintelligent. It was just that they were not taught anything other than combat skills and, having spent their entire lives in the holy land, were overly naïve.

“That nasty bowman shot an arrow at you. If you hadn’t dodged it in time, it would have lodged itself in your neck, not your shoulder.” As I said that, I pulled out the arrow stuck in his arm. Although the pain must have been considerable, Kharon didn’t even let out a sound, so I just kept talking. “These guys are looters. They are the scum of the labyrinth, and they tried to kill you and take your heart.”
“...I want to hear what they have to say.”

Perhaps he was hoping there was some sort of misunderstanding at play here. Kharon asked to speak with the trio, and I had no reason to refuse. I just took their weapons and woke up one of the men from the pile.

“E-Eek!” I chose the bowman. I determined that he had suffered less damage than the others since he was only strangled. “H-Have mercy!” As soon as he saw me, the bowman kneeled and I took a step back. I wasn’t the one who wanted to talk.
“Royce, are you really a plunderer?”
“Kh-Kharon...? This is all a misunderstanding. I’ll explain everything, so first wake the others—”
“Answer me. What have I misunderstood?”
“That’s...” The bowman couldn’t answer Kharon’s question. That made sense, because it wasn’t a misunderstanding. To save time, I tossed the notebook I found while taking their weapons to Kharon.
“What is this?”
“Read it for yourself.”
“I... don’t know how to read.”
Oh. Right. “Then why don’t you ask him to read it for you?”
“I can... do that.”

Soon, Kharon handed the notebook he had received to the bowman. It contained the written conversation these three had shared while we were pretending to be asleep. As soon as he saw this, the bowman, who was dripping in cold sweat, dropped his head. It seemed that he had reached the acceptance stage.
Not on my watch. “If you don’t read it, I will kill you. Very painfully.”
“I-I’ll read...” Soon, the bowman began to read the text slowly and with trembling lips:
Briol, why did you agree to let him stay? Are you going to kill him too?
He’s practically begging to be killed. There’s no need to let them walk away alive, is there?
I think this guy is suspicious. The fact that he’s looking for a night companion on the second floor... not even a barbarian is that stupid.
Suspicious? I agree with Briol. You’ve killed so many barbarians and you still don’t know? They are just walking...
The bowman, who had been struggling to keep reading, shut his mouth at one point, so I broke one of his fingers. “Did my words sound like a joke to you?”
“Ahhh!”
“Continue.”

“Th-they’re just walking monsters! Th-their intelligence is similar to monsters, and especially in the sense that the person who catches one owns them.” After finishing the sentence, the bowman carefully studied Kharon’s reaction.
Kharon was trembling. “...Who said that?”
“Victor...”
“Yeah, that guy... All right, go on.”

After confirming that it was the spearman’s line, Royce continued the story. “Besides, even setting aside the barbarian, isn’t there already enough of a reward here? She seems to be as stupid as the barbarian, b-but her face is...on the pretty side...”
“Continue.”
“Agreed. But I don’t know how a bitch fooling around with a barbarian would be with—”

“Enough!” Missha stepped in and ripped the notebook from his hands. Then, after quickly scanning it, she asked the bowman, “This, and this here. Who wrote this?” Her voice was as cold as ice. I’d never seen her like this before.
When the bowman pointed at the leader with trembling hands, Missha looked at me and said straight up, “Bjorn, I’m going to kill this one.”
“Do as you like.”
In any case, there was no need to make Missha angrier, so I made the bowman skip the obscene parts. After that, discussions continued about who to kill first and how.
“I-I’ll take care of Kharon,” he read. “It pissed me off that he l-looked down on me for being an archer. He doesn’t even know that he’ll be dead after this hunt is over...’”

The conversation ended there with the bowman’s line. After a moment of silence, Kharon opened his mouth. “I... don’t get it at all.” The first thing that came out of his mouth was a question. “...Did I do something wrong?”
Despite it all, he first found fault in himself. Of course he didn’t do anything wrong. It was just that this world was too brutal for someone so innocent.
“Bjon, son of Thor...”
“It’s Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“I see. So you’re the famous... Good. Tell me, Bjorn, son of Yandel, are people like this common in the labyrinth?”
“They are.”

This side of the labyrinth wasn’t spoken about in the holy land. “Then...what do I do?” asked the young warrior who had been faced with this for the first time, as if sincerely hoping to learn the answer. As if, if I told him how to handle this, he would definitely follow my advice to the letter.

So, I answered him. “Doubt everyone, whether they be human or a different race. Just as I fooled them, conceal an axe behind your innocence. And even if it’s annoying and a little difficult, always think before you act.”
“...Can I really do that?”

“It’s not about whether you can, it’s about what you have to do,” I said firmly. “If you cannot distinguish between those two things, you will have no choice but to be a child forever. And remember this: if you kill one of these people, many more young warriors will be spared.”
At my words, Kharon pressed his lips together. “I see. That’s why you...” He now seemed to understand why I did what I did.
“Now, what are you going to do?” I asked for the last time. “I will abide by your choice.”
Squeeze.
Kharon, the young warrior and son of Tarson, just tightened his grip on his axe.
Slice!
In one swing, he finally became a warrior. The bowman’s head flew off as Kharon drew a rough x across his neck.

Missha, who had been waiting for this, woke the leader up by stomping on his groin and promptly slit his throat. I snapped the neck of the remaining one. He woke up in the middle of it and begged for his life.
“P-Please spare me! I’ll live an honest life from now on...”
“Do you mean to say you’ll be an honest plunderer?”
“A-An honest plunderer? Ah, yes, yes! I will—”
His promises meant nothing. There was only one way to be an honest plunderer.
“Here, it’s a potion.”
“Thanks.”
Once clean-up was pretty much finished, I handed Kharon a potion and he poured it on his shoulder wound.
“Why don’t you pour more?”
“If I do, it will heal completely. Scars are evidence of past mistakes. I don’t want to forget what happened here.”
“If you say so.” I knew barbarians had a habit of regarding scars as medals, so I didn’t contribute anything else.

“Thank you, Bjorn, son of Yandel. Now I know what I have to do next.” His eyes were already different from earlier. At the sight, I was officially convinced. “I won’t be able to do it like you, but I’ll crush the skulls of those I come across—no, even if I have to go find them myself. Also, if I see a young warrior, I will tell them about what I went through today and warn them, just as you did today, for the sake of my people.”
With his new outlook on life, it seemed he’d be able to make it clear to most plunderers: from this moment on, if you touched a baby barbarian, you’d be fucked.

chapters.title: Chapter 113: Reunion (1)
paragraphs: First, we gathered up the trio’s equipment in one place. Then I gave Kharon the first pick. “If you need anything, take it.”
“I’m not that shameless.”
“Don’t refuse. You took one of them down.”
“If you say so...” It seemed there was in fact something he wanted because Kharon did end up taking some of the loot for himself—a good quality leather bag and a few bottles of potion.
“That and a two-handed hammer? That’s it?”

“The rest is too small for my body, anyway.” That was true. Soon, Kharon smiled brightly, holding an axe in one hand and a sledgehammer in the other. “I can kill anything that’s hard to kill with an axe with this!” Although the way he spoke was unrefined, what he was saying was rather reasonable. Blunt weapons were more effective against monsters like Stone Golems.
Yes. Dual-wielding is a must for barbarians.
The sight of Kharon looking more like a proper barbarian pleased me, so I handed over a few more pieces of equipment. “Even if you don’t need it, keep it and sell it.”
“But—!”

No buts. Seriously, why were all barbarians so nice? If he were a human, he would have had a greedy look in his eyes instead. “Don’t forget that the stronger you become, the safer it’ll be for the young warriors.”
“...Okay. I will definitely sell these items and turn them into equipment that will help me.”

My reason for forcibly handing over the equipment while instilling a sense of responsibility in him was simple. If I took this stuff for myself, I would get an additional two hundred thousand stones, but in the long run, this would benefit me more.
“Become stronger, Kharon, son of Tarson.”
“I will. For the sake of my people, if nothing else.”

Of the six races, the barbarians were the weakest in terms of influence. Each individual had a good amount of potential, but most of them died off in the beginning. Of course, the winds of change wouldn’t start blowing just because one person had changed, but what if the number gradually increased, starting with this one? And what if it led to a virtuous cycle of more and more young warriors surviving to become top adventurers?
Then the amount of influence barbarians have will gradually grow.

Like it or not, I was a barbarian. The more influence my kin had, the more I could enjoy the trickle-down effect. Just look at wizards. Without the huge community of the Magic Tower, would they all be so arrogant?
“Then let’s go. If someone sees us here, there’ll be trouble.”

In that spirit, I escorted Kharon to the first floor and gave him whatever tidbits of advice I could think of. Like, when looking for a party, choose one with at least one member of a different race. Be warier of friendly people, but at the same time don’t make it too obvious and show your weaknesses.

“Now I think I know what you meant by ‘conceal an axe behind your innocence!’” Could it be from the great example I had set with the trio today? Kharon understood exactly what I meant. “I think it would be a good idea to intentionally find human night companions and pretend to be asleep. If they have any ulterior motives, that will definitely reveal them!”
Ah... uh... um... That isn’t something I told him to do...
“...That’s a good strategy too.”
It seemed that getting treated as a monster and betrayed by his party today had been quite the shock for him. He was absorbing all of my advice like a sponge.

Around the start of the fifth day, at 11:49 p.m., the two of us returned to the Land of the Dead after taking Kharon down to the first floor. Then we sped up a little and focused on our search, since we had deviated from our plans and lost almost an entire day. On the tenth day, the second floor would close. Unless we intended to finish this quest on the second floor, we had to move a little faster, especially since we had work to do before going up to the third floor.
“Hmm? We’re going to fight a Death Knight? Is that possible? I hearrrd it’s hard to even find them...”

The rank-six monster Death Knight was a piece of shit that on very rare occasions spawned in the Land of the Dead on the second floor. I’d had to cycle through several characters before I figured out the conditions for finding this guy.
“Don’t worry. Tracking one down won’t be a big problem.”

It seemed she was getting used to conversations like this because Missha didn’t even bother asking where I got that information and just expressed a different concern. “Um, but even so, I don’t know if the two of us can take it.”
It was not a strange concern to have. We’d run into rank-six monsters from time to time on the fourth floor, but currently, we were just two people instead of a full party.
Since she’s only hunted rank-eight monsters, she won’t have a sense of how strong she is now.

Missha had had a history of being active on the fourth floor with two essences before meeting me. Although her stats were on the lower side, she had made up for what she lacked with her martial arts skills, which she had acquired through hard work. But since then, she’d made a contract with a Spirit Beast, and even gotten two essences. One of them even belonged to a guardian.
And if you add the combo compatibility of her essences to that... It’s safe to say that she’s now several times stronger than she used to be.

I looked at the cold, hard facts from a gamer’s point of view. With our strength combined, the hunt could end up being successful. However, there was no need to explain this in detail, since barbarians had just the right way to communicate concepts like these. “Missha, trust me.”
“If you say that... It’s not like I can say no.”
“That’s it, then.”
With Missha’s consent, we continued searching the surrounding area. We expanded the search radius by taking out all the rank-eight monsters we saw—Death Fiends, Chimera Wolves, Ghoul Lords, etcetera.
“Let’s stop here for today and set up camp.”
The fifth day ended without success. The next day, the sixth, was the same. With a little over an hour left before the start of day seven, I let out a long sigh.
I didn’t think we’d be unsuccessful after over two days.

When a labyrinth opened, a tombstone was created at a random location in the Land of the Dead. At the beginning of the seventh day, it summoned the Death Knight. In other words, if you found the tombstone, you could easily encounter the Death Knight by waiting in front of it.
Of course my life is like this.

Although we’d half-heartedly hunted and searched the entire place for two days, we couldn’t find even a hint of a tombstone. This was unexpected. No matter how big the second floor was, all we had to do was search the rank-eight zone. I had determined that two days should be enough.
Dang, should we give up on the Death Knight?

As I was licking my lips, not wanting the past two days to have been a waste, Missha ran up to me. “Don’t be so dishearrrtened. How can a book be right all of the time? A big tombstone in the Land of the Dead? I’ve never heard of such a thing before now.”
Umm, this is supposed to be comforting, right?
“So stop locking yourself up in the library every day and come hang out with me from time to time.”
“...Why is that the moral of the story?”
“Th-that’s—! Hikurod said the same thing too. It’s more helpful to have some conversations with the other adventurers at a bar than rrread a few books!”

Now that I was thinking about it, it seemed that the dwarf was a bad influence on Missha. But I couldn’t really argue with her. In fact, most adventurers felt the same. They preferred to socialize and acquire information at a bar rather than by reading a book. There were some people out there who claimed that drinking and playing were extensions of work, which said it all.
“...Why arrren’t you saying anything?”
“I just don’t have anything to say.”
“Why don’t you have anything to say?”
“Stop talking about this, and let’s move on for now.” I didn’t want to waste time engaging in a pointless argument, so I resumed our journey.

How long had it been since? I checked my watch and brushed off any lingering disappointment. It was one minute to midnight. The seventh day would start soon. And as soon as the Death Knight was summoned, it started wandering around, so the fact of the matter was that this quest was already a bust.
