It’s the experience I was after, anyway...
Leaving my regrets behind, I took out my compass.
“Oh, are we finally going to the third floorrr?”
“Yes.”
Instead of wandering around aimlessly looking for a tombstone, we turned north. And at that moment—
“Huh? Bjorn?”
“Did you feel it too?”
“Yeah, a chill ran down my spine.”
The air around us shifted. It was hard to describe, but the moment it changed, my body registered it before my mind did. That was how obvious a change it was.
Could it be?
One possibility came to mind, and I borrowed a knife from Missha and slit the back of my hand.
Drip.
When I pressed the blade in and dragged it down my skin, acid blood flowed from the open seam.
“Ah! What are you doing?! You’re damaging the blade!”
Ignoring Missha’s complaints, I watched the wound and counted the time.
One, two, three, four, five, six...
As the number increased, a smile spread across my lips. The wound, which should have healed within seconds, was still not healing.
[You have been exposed to Grudge. Healing and regeneration effects significantly decrease.]
That meant the long-awaited Death Knight was near us, and very close.
No wonder we couldn’t find it anywhere. It really was nearby.
Even though I felt kind of depressed about that, my spirits were bolstered because of a piece of information that I realized soon after.
Grudge has already been triggered...

The curse-type aura Grudge was an active skill, one that turned on or off depending on the will of the monster or character who had acquired the essence. Simply put, there was no reason to use it outside of combat—the circumstances for activating it were very clear. Less than one minute after being summoned, the Death Knight leapt into battle as soon as it opened its eyes. It was not impossible that an adventurer who had been passing by at the exact right time could be caught up in combat with it, but...
That’s unlikely.
It would be much more reasonable to assume that, rather than such an incredible coincidence happening, some unknown person had been waiting in front of the tombstone.
Could it be a player?

That was my first thought. However, I couldn’t rule out other possibilities. The large Dzarwi clan knew how to summon an Orc Hero. It was possible that information on Death Knights wasn’t that high-level.
Well, I’ll know for sure when I get there.
I decided to reserve judgment for now and moved quickly with Missha. It was dark all around, but it wasn’t difficult to find the right direction.
Bam!

Judging from the sound of it, the fight seemed to be quite explosive. Missha was able to come to a conclusion from this information alone and grabbed my wrist. “Bjorn, do you think it’s a Death Knight? And someone is already fighting it?” she asked.
“Yes.”
“Wait a minute, stop! What are you going to do over therrre?”
What do you think? Throw a punch and take the experience points.

“What? If you do that, you might be attacked!” Missha was startled when I translated my future plans into words from this world. It was a legitimate concern on her part. Although not as horrible as plundering, the act of intruding or stealing prey during battle was considered extremely immoral among adventurers.
“It’s okay. I have no intention of claiming the right to an essence or mana stone, so I’ll just pretend I thought whoever it is was in danger.”
“Mmm, still...”
“Don’t worry. If anything happens, I’ll take responsibility for everything—”
“You idiot! Does it sound like I want you to take rrresponsibility? Ugh, how did I end up involved with someone like you? Whatever, let’s go! I don’t even know anymore!”
Um, that’s a little unfair. It’s not like I’m doing this just for myself... Anyway, I guess since we’re not looting, this much is within reason.
Noting that additional information down in my head, I sped up a bit. Maybe ten seconds passed when—
“Kyaaagh!”
I saw four adventurers past the Death Knight, who was wielding a sword and had its back toward us.
“Huh?”
Apparently, they saw us too. Therefore, without giving them time to stop me, I hit the Death Knight with my mace.
Whack!
Okay, that will get me experience points.
Just like I’d been waiting for, I shouted out the lines I had prepared. “Don’t worry! I will save you guys!”
This was why barbarians were cheat characters.
“Behelaaah!”
I didn’t know about humans, but who would ever think this was intentional?
The Death Knight took the heavy blow and stumbled.
“Kyaaak?!” Apparently, the monster was also bewildered by my sudden interruption. Not as much as the wide-eyed party of four, though.
“What are you doing!?” The human warrior who was closest to me shouted, belatedly realizing what was happening.
Next was the elven archer in the back row. “Why are you helping? If you don’t back down, I’ll attack you too.” Her voice was soft, but still very sharp.
I pretended to be confused and cried out, “I-I was just trying to help!”
“Who asked for help?”
“Huh? You didn’t? I thought I heard you...”
“Never mind, just step back if you don’t want to get caught up in this and get hurt!”
“A-All right!” Even as we spoke, I deflected the Death Knight’s attacks several times with my shield before retreating to where Missha was standing.
“Damn it, what the hell is this all of a sudden!?” Despite his complaints, the human warrior still skillfully took over the aggro and the battle smoothly resumed.

I dropped my clumsy barbarian act and spoke so that only Missha could hear. “How was that? I don’t think there’s anything to be concerned about.” I wanted to reassure Missha, who was worried that she would be seen as a rude adventurer.

However, the reaction I got in return was a little unexpected. “You are really...” My acting seemed to have left an impression on her because she couldn’t finish her sentence. “Hah... neverrr mind. What can I possibly say here? Other people need to know that you’re like this.”
“What do you mean? I only show all this to you.”
“Hmm? S-Still. I mean—what?”
The chitchat ended there and I watched the ensuing battle. How many opportunities would we get to watch another party hunt?
It’s not a full party, but the balance is good.
The human warrior could skillfully tank alone.
“I’m going to take another shot, so back up!” The damage dealer line was made up of a wizard and an elven archer who used fire magic.
I think this is my first time seeing a summoner in this world.
There was even a human man in a support position who dealt damage or gave buffs using monsters he called through his summoning ability.
“Bjorn, that man... doesn’t he look familiarrr?”
At Missha’s sudden comment, I looked at the summoner again, a small figure of about 5′2″. It was difficult to see his face because of the hood, but still, I felt a strange sense of déjà vû.
What is this? Where have I seen him? There’s no way I wouldn’t remember a summoner...

The moment I was trying to figure out why his face was so familiar... “E-Everyone get out of the way! The attack I was talking about i-is coming!” The summoner stammered and called out instructions. Thanks to that, my blurry memories grew clearer. Soon, I glanced at the face of the elf near the man once again and came to a conclusion.
Ah, that son of a bitch from back then.
It had to be him.

chapters.title: Chapter 114: Reunion (2)
paragraphs: “Bjorn! I got it! It’s that perrrson!”
“There is no need to explain. I remember too.”
Feeling strange, I combed through my memory, going back three months to when I was trapped in the Evil Hiatus of the Lord of the Floor, Riakis.
“Be thankful that I haven’t killed you yet, you piece of trash.”
When Clan Dzarwi had rejected the riotous adventurers, they fell into a collective panic. At that point, this man appeared.
“I-I know about this ability.”
He opened up a new path for the clueless adventurers. Of course, it was hard to blindly trust him.

“I’ve been teaming up with this guy for over a year and I’ve been through a lot of incredible things with him. This man is mysterious. He really knows everything. I have no doubt that his words will save us.”
The adventurers, who had no other choice, had followed him, trusting only the assurances of an elf who claimed to be his companion.
No doubt, my ass.
They had all died. That was all I had heard when I inquired about it later on, so that was all I thought had happened, too—until I saw this man today.
It looks like they’re the only ones who survived after leading over a hundred people to their deaths.

When I thought about it like that, he was an interesting guy. It couldn’t have been pure luck that he managed to come back alive. It would be fair to say he pulled something to survive. At the time, I thought he was just an asshole.
But to think he led them knowingly to their deaths.
“N-Now! Get out of the way!”

As I watched the man predict the Death Knight’s attack pattern and yell out orders, I narrowed my eyes. He had a total of four summoned beasts. The compatibility between the summons was good, but the rank of the essence itself was not high. This told me one thing.
I’m guessing an average of rank seven.

The man was a low-rank adventurer with nothing to his name. If he were from a rich family, his equipment, at least, would be of good quality. That made me even more suspicious. If he wasn’t from a good family, how could an adventurer with a short career know Riakis’s pattern and the conditions for making the Death Knight appear?
...It’d be reasonable to assume he’s a player.

I came to this conclusion through rational reasoning. That unfamiliar summoner was a player. I didn’t know why a guy like that had made the mistake of choosing a summoner role as a human being, though.
Dang, but that makes it confusing.

Perhaps if he was a beastman, dragon person, or dwarf instead, it’d make sense, but humans had no aptitude for summoning. Of course, the power difference at the beginning of the game was small, but it widened into a huge gap as you entered the second half. In other words, it was very inefficient.
Maybe that’s not important to him...

That was definitely plausible. Forget making a perfect character—it was human nature to want to choose a freeloader job. After all, who wanted to fight head-to-head? Although that probably wasn’t something I should be saying, considering I chose a shield as soon as I realized I was starting as a barbarian.
[You have killed a Death Knight. EXP +4]

I opened my eyes, relishing in the feeling of contentment that filled my body. After a fireball from the wizard pierced its inner core, the Death Knight turned into a cluster of lights and disappeared. There was no essence.
“That’s a shame. I even bought a test tube at a high price just in case.”
“B-Be careful with your words, Parteian...”
“Oh, right.” The wizard shut his mouth and looked this way.
Then it must be our turn now.
After watching them impassively for a while, I put the mask of a naïve barbarian back on. “Oho, amazing! What kind of magic was that at the end?”

When I tried to approach the wizard in a friendly way, the elven archer stopped me, coldly cutting me off. “I don’t think we need to be having that kind of conversation. Why did you do that earlier? If you don’t have a good explanation, I’ll consider you an enemy.”
Jeez, I’m pretty sure she was gentle in front of that big group of adventurers back then... Was it all an act? Ah, right. Elves and barbarians don’t get along very well.
“As I said earlier, I was just trying to help!”
“That’s strange. None of us asked for anything like that.”
“Death Knights are strong! That’s why I thought you guys were in danger!”
The elven archer glared at me suspiciously. How bad was the barbarians’ reputation among elves for her to look at me like that even in baby barbarian mode? “Is that really the only reason?”
“What other reason could there be?”
“Well, there’s the essence. I don’t know about you, but the beastwoman next to you would be very desperate for one.”
Missha was startled by the elf’s sharp accusation and waved it off with her hand. “Th-that’s not true! I do use a sword, but I can’t even take another essence because all my slots are full!”
“...Is that true?”
“You can check for yourrrself!”
Check what? What exactly are you going to do here?

It was a truly ridiculous response, but the elf just nodded. “Then I believe you.” Apparently, this elf archer’s snarky behavior was limited to barbarians. “But if you only stepped in to help us, something doesn’t add up.”
“Oh, you tree-huggers...”
“You! What did you say just now?”

“How wicked are you in your everyday dealings that you doubt me at first sight?” I asked right back, annoyed at her sharp tone. It wasn’t that I was actually angry or anything. I also knew that it was wrong to intrude on someone else’s battle. But, so what? “Are you belittling me for being a barbarian?” Coming out strong even in a situation where I was clearly at fault was the true barbarian way. “If you insult me any further, I will not stand for it! Tree-hugger!”

The elf was taken aback when she saw me start to raise my shield like I was willing to fight even in a four-on-two situation. “No, it’s not that! There’s something unclear, so I’m asking you to clarify!”
“What’s not clear?”
“I understand that your intention wasn’t to get an essence. However, it is difficult to accept that you had no intention of piggybacking off of our accomplishment.”
Wow, she was sharp. That was pretty much exactly what had happened, but there was nothing wrong with that either. “Why would I go through that trouble? I’ve already killed one of those before.”
“...Pardon?” At my words, the elf stared at me blankly. I’m sure what I was saying made no sense to her because Death Knights were a difficult monster to encounter before the sixth floor.
I quickly went on to explain, “I once went to the Bloody Citadel. Does that clear things up?”

It had been a variant Rift so a vampire had popped out instead of a Death Knight, but they didn’t need to know that. It wasn’t like they could somehow figure out the truth here. Plus, it was actually half true in the first place.
“B-But! How are we supposed to believe that?”
“In that case, you won’t believe anything! If you want to fight, come at me, tree-hugger.”
“You think I won’t—!”
Seeing the elf erupt in anger, the man jumped in surprise and stepped in. “Miss Meirin, p-please stop! What he said is probably t-true!”
“Pardon? What do you—”

“I-I remember now! That barbarian... h-he’s the one I saw back then! Bjorn, son of Yandel. The adventurer who earned the nickname of Little Balkan!” Although our last encounter had been brief, it seemed the summoner remembered my face.
Soon, the wizard and the warrior let out simultaneous exclamations of surprise. “No wonder he deflected the Death Knight’s sword so easily mid-conversation.”
“Oh, how incredible. Miss Meirin, it seems we had it wrong. Why would someone as famous as him do such a thing just to earn experience points?”
The elven archer pursed her lips, perhaps sensing that this situation was taking a strange turn.
“I understand how you feel. Admitting you were wrong is sometimes the hardest thing. But sometimes you have to learn to let go of stubbornness and accept things at face value too.”
“Hah, all right...” When all of her comrades concluded that I had no ill intentions, the elf didn’t press the issue any further.
Huh, is this why you need a good reputation?

Realizing once again the importance of fame, I stared at the summoner approaching me. “N-Nice to meet you, Bjorn, son of Yandel.” It was easy to look down on him because of his habit of stuttering, but this was no ordinary guy, either. After all, he once led hundreds of people to their deaths just to save his own life. “It was fate that we met like this. Sh-shouldn’t we introduce ourselves?” the man asked me cautiously. I was sure he wasn’t just curious about my name, so it was probably safe to say he wanted to get acquainted with me.

“All right.” I nodded without hesitation. There was no reason to refuse. After all, the reason I was still here in the first place was because I wanted to learn his name. “As you know, I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel. What’s your name?”

Since I was certain he was a player, I thought I’d learn his name and look into him later. Nothing major, but I was a bit curious. After observing his performance, I thought that he could serve as a reference for how normal players behaved.
“I’m Hans Chrisen.”
Fuck, I hadn’t expected this, either. A player in the body of a Hans? What kind of soap opera was this?
“If you don’t mind, I’d like to be acquainted with you in the f—”
I stepped back as he began to ask for a handshake with a friendly smile. “Stop right there. I’m busy with something, so I’m going to leave!”
“Pardon? What do you—”
“Missha! What are you doing?! We’re leaving!”
“Y-Yeah! Okay—wait! W-Wait for me...!”
Damn it, I should have brought some salt or something. My heart was already pounding at the thought of what was to come in the future.
As soon as I discovered Hans G’s identity, I fled the area. How much time had passed since?
“What arrre you doing?! Running is fine, but please explain why—”
“He was also a Hans.”
“Huh? What do you m—”
“I’ve never had things work out after meeting a Hans.”
I spoke with sincere concern in my voice, but Missha just looked relieved. “Jeez, that’s it? I thought something big happened!”
No, this is really big. He’s Hans! And also a player I met in the labyrinth!
“I guess you have a quirrrky side. I didn’t think you’d believe in superrrstitions.”
Missha’s nonchalant reaction upset me for some reason. “Missha... this is not something to be trifled with.”
“Pffft! Bjorn, you... You seem kind of cute today, huh?”

What was this kid talking about? I walked her through my Hans-related encounters one by one: Hans A, who kicked off the list; Hans C, who had been Elisa’s subordinate; and Hans D, who had been the leader of the band of plunderers we ran into in the Witch’s Forest.
“C-Come to think of it, you said you didn’t like that name back then too...”
“Yes. But at the time, I just thought it was ominous.”

When I told her about Hans B, who had been nearby right before Dwalkie got taken away by Mozlan, Missha’s complexion changed too. “W-What the—! What the hell is up with Hans?!” Like any adventurer vulnerable to superstition, by this point Missha also seemed a bit uneasy. “Now what? We already met him... you don’t think something bad is going to happen, do you?!”
Well, I didn’t know about that—just that we would need to be more careful in the future. “Let’s head up to the third floor as soon as possible.”
“...Not the first floor?” Missha, now even more serious than me, expressed her concerns, but my plan of action was the most reasonable one.

First of all, I was not sure if this was superstition or not... but even if superstitions were real, it changed nothing. If the Hans curse was real, running would be pointless. Fucked-up things happened in the city too. Just doing what needed to be done was the best way to reduce the damage.
“Ugh, if that’s the case, you shouldn’t have told me. Frrreaking me out like this...”
That was fair. Apparently, running into Hans, a former player, had made it hard for me to think clearly. Or was it that I had come to rely on her at some point?
“I don’t know about happy things, but sharing burdens is a surefire way to divvy up the suffering, right?”
“What are you saying?! You annoying barrrbarian!”
“...That was a joke.”
“Don’t lie! Your eyes were sincere!” When I told her the truth, Missha was greatly enraged.

Well, even so, the fact that I had unknowingly confided in her seemed to satisfy her. “Whew! Anyway, you did a good job telling me without hiding it. If something like this happens in the futurrre, don’t suffer alone and tell me. I’m older than you, remember?”
“Oh, right.” Missha was five years older than me. Though that only applied to Bjorn, of course.
“What’s with that rrreaction?”
“It means you’re more dependable.”
“I don’t think that was it...”
Anyway, the chitchat ended there and we resumed our journey. I wasn’t sure how long it had been since, but I started to feel fatigue building up in my body, which meant it was time to set up camp.
It’s been almost a day since we ran into those guys, so we’ll be arriving on the third floor tomorrow or the day after.
I was pretty tired too, but after I settled down, I put Missha to sleep first. Then I sat vigil, continuing my train of thought.

When I checked the time, it was past midnight. Since today was the seventh day, that meant that the first-floor Crystal Cave had already closed and spat its adventurers back out into the city. Well, whether we left earlier or later, we’d all arrive at the same time.
I hope he got home all right.
I was suddenly reminded of Kharon, whom I had escorted down to the first floor.
“I think it would be a good idea to intentionally find human night companions and pretend to be asleep. If they have ulterior motives, that will definitely reveal them!”
Was it because of those parting words of his? I was worried there might have been an incident.
Ah, I’m sure it’s all right.
It was time to switch, so I woke Missha and closed my eyes for a bit.
Dazzling light, noise from a crowd, and the humid air unique to the city filled his lungs.
Kharon let out an impulsive shout. “Behelahhh!”

He just felt like doing it. Should he say it was refreshing? He didn’t care about the stares of the people around him, looking at him like he was a savage. At one time he used to feel intimidated by those gazes, but...
Who cares!
“Behelaaah!”
Kharon had changed. No, he had shed his old shell, like a big hornworm breaking through its cocoon to become an adult. During this expedition, he’d grown into a true warrior.
“Tsk, they’re always showing off like that, those barbarians.”
“Hey, he’ll hear you. He might do something rash and headbutt you, so be careful.”
That condescending gaze was just a pleasant fuel for his motivation. It just showed how careless they were, just like the two night companions he’d killed in the past few days.
It was easy.

Everything was as Bjorn, son of Yandel, had said. The first floor was full of garbage who hid their true intentions, and as soon as they revealed an opening, Kharon went for it. Unaware it was a trap, when the people who once looked down on him as prey realized they had been tricked, the look on their faces was enough to evoke a new kind of ecstasy in him.
Clink, clink.

One on the back, one on the right arm, and one on the left arm—with a total of three bags on his person, he proudly headed for the checkpoint. The line was long, befitting a gate exclusively for rank-nine explorers.
When he arrived, his people found him and approached him. “Kharon, son of Tarson! What is that bag?”
“I-It’s full of gear! Have you been looting?”
Kharon shook his head firmly. “Pffft, looting? Of course not.”
This was not an act as disgusting as looting. No, it was a noble act to protect his own people. When he drew a clear line in response to their concerns, the looks in the barbarians’ eyes shifted.
“How can something like this be possible without looting!?”
“I-I’m jealous! If you sell all of that, how many loaves of stone bread will you be able to buy?”

These were his peers who had completed the coming-of-age ceremony with him, but today, they looked young to him. That was why he summoned as many of his own people as possible. He had once felt a sense of competition toward them, but he now knew the real enemy lay elsewhere. “Hoohoo, don’t be jealous. If you learn the right method, you can earn just as much. You won’t have to eat stone bread for the rest of your life.”
“What!? If there really is such a thing, please let me know!”
“I will tell you! But before that, I have something else to tell you first.”

First, Kharon told them what he had experienced in the labyrinth in order: getting betrayed by his teammates because of his heart, and even the way they regarded barbarians as easy and valuable monsters.
“We are not monsters!”
“We are warriors!”
As expected, the barbarians were extremely indignant. And when they heard that Little Balkan had been the one to save him, they raised their voices and praised him.
“Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“To be able to read the thoughts of those vicious predators, he is a great and wise warrior!”
The atmosphere instantly warmed. Kharon, in the middle of them all, proudly exclaimed, “He taught me. It is all thanks to his teachings that I returned with so many trophies!”
“Oooh! Is that true!?”
“It’s true! I will teach you what he taught me!”
Eventually, Kharon openly shared what he’d learned from Bjorn, and even the strategy he’d devised himself. Of course, all the credit went to Bjorn.
“I just need to find a human night companion and pretend to sleep!”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel! Is he a genius?”
“I wasn’t sure about it at first, but it is the word of a great warrior! I will follow it!”
As he watched his fellow countrymen burning up with excitement, Kharon was convinced.
“Tsk, those guys are starting up again.”
“I don’t know why they leave them alone when they always make so much noise.”
“I bet even if you take out their hearts and sell them, those howls of theirs will be the same.”

Up to this point, barbarians had been the lowest-level prey in the labyrinth. Although Kharon didn’t want to admit it, that was the reality he had been faced with not too long ago. They may have been strong in a head-to-head battle, but they were helpless in the face of cunning tricks. But...
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, has spoken! All of this will be a noble step forward for all of us!”
“Behelahhh!”
“Behelahhh!”
Things would be different from now on.

chapters.title: Chapter 115: Reunion (3)
paragraphs: [You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]
On the afternoon of the ninth day, after searching the northernmost part of the Land of the Dead for over a day, we found a portal and reached the third floor.
...Next time, I won’t come in without a scout.

I had figured that if we took the portal to the Land of the Dead, we could get to the third floor with just the two of us, but nevertheless, the absence of a scout took a significant toll. If it hadn’t been for secretly following a group of adventurers who happened to be passing by, we would still have been wandering around.
“Ugh, I feel sick whenever I come herrre.”

Anyway, after hardships like that, we arrived at Jet-Black Estuary. This was the starting point you spawned at when you came up to the third floor from the Land of the Dead—a field characterized by shallow streams that flowed in dozens of directions. Oh, and the gutter smell was a bonus.
“Let’s go, then.”

Since there was no scout, we continued using the compass to move northeast. As we were doing that, we quickly reached a dead end. In other words, we now had to dip our feet in the black river and cross it.
“...Can’t you just carrry me?”
Tsk, and let you travel in style?
“...Only this once.”
“Wow! Rrreally? Thanks!”

I carried Missha on my shoulder and crossed the river. The width was about five yards and the water reached just below the knee. After crossing carefully so as not to fall, we reached a patch of wet ground that continued forward like a road. However, the moment I was about to keep moving, as if following the sound of our crossing, a monster crept out of nowhere.
“Geruk! Gereuk! Gel, gel, gel!”
“Bjorn, that’s a Frogman over therrre.”

This rank-eight monster walked on two legs, with an appearance that resembled a frog’s. It used something like a harpoon as a weapon. It may have looked funny because of its small size, but since it had high agility, many adventurers were caught off guard by it and instantly met their deaths. Their skills were also a bit annoying.
...How bothersome.
These guys were not a good matchup for me. My mace had enough power to shatter a Death Fiend’s skull with one blow, but that was meaningless if it couldn’t hit anything.
Voom!
The Frogman stepped off the air itself, leaping up again to dodge my mace. I immediately dashed forward and hit it with my shield, but that didn’t do anything.
[Your attack missed due to Rotten Slime.]
The shield made contact with its body, but instead of making a thud, the Frogman just slid right off of it.
“Ghell-ghell!”
Are you having fun? Goddamn it.
These guys had total evasion against blunt weapons, so for me, they were tricky enemies regardless of their rank. However, since Missha was there, there were no problems.
“Hi-ya! Avoid this!” Missha, who had been laughing at the Frogman screwing around with me, took out her weapon and started a sword dance with zeal.
“Geruk!” Frogmen came with a considerably high dodge rate even against blades, but our swordswoman was an ice-type. “Geg?!” It wasn’t enough that its thigh was cut, but its lower body also froze.
Slump.
The frog bastard that had been running around willy-nilly collapsed.
“Missha, wait!”
“Huh?”
“I will do it.” After calling out to Missha, who was about to kill it, I finished it off with my mace.
Whack!
Whew, that relieved some stress.
The usual strategy was to catch this guy with magic, but since the level difference between us was so great, the battle wasn’t too hard.
“Ghell-ghell!”
“Gerreuk! Gereuk!”
Taking down more Frogmen like that, we kept moving.

Checking the time and finding that it was now 22:57, I slowly started looking for a place to camp. It was partly because of fatigue, but this particular area also forced you to take breaks at set times.
“Bjorn, the water is getting higher.”
“I’m already looking, so stop whining.”

After exploring the surrounding area for about thirty minutes, a checkpoint appeared. Unlike the dingy estuary, the reddish mounds of dirt were soft and not soggy. As if all the adventurers in the area had gathered in one spot, there were already about thirty people there.
The innermost spot will be taken already since we’re late.

Reluctantly, we settled down by the water, where the gutter-like smell wafted up to us directly. The soil wasn’t damp, at least, so the water wouldn’t come all the way up here. As I was drying my wet legs before laying out the blankets, the water level in the river began to rise rapidly, right on cue. It was midnight, though, so it wouldn’t get any higher from there. This state would last for the next six hours, so I put Missha to bed first. Since there were a lot of people around, some teams didn’t set up a watch and all took a break, but you never knew.
Since we even ran into a Hans a few days ago, we should be careful.
I was rummaging through my backpack, filling my stomach with snacks, when—
“Hahaha! Cheer up, my friend! They say little strokes fell great oaks!”
“But... as you know, she’s—”
“Geez, can’t you see people are trying to sleep?”
“Ahaha! I’m sorry! I’ll be careful!”
I heard a familiar voice in the distance. I guess she hadn’t fallen asleep yet, because Missha sat up, still wrapped in a blanket. “That’s Hikurod’s voice...”
Seeing as she was thinking the same thing, I didn’t think I’d misheard. Huh, what kind of coincidence was this?

It was not common to run into someone you knew in the labyrinth. First of all, each floor was incredibly big, and because of the darkness inside the labyrinth, even if you turned on a light, the visibility was less than ten yards. Clans sometimes divided into several parties and climbed the floors by deciding where and when to meet.
To think it’s really them.
Surprisingly, the owner of the voice really was the dwarf. Next to him were Dwalkie and Rotmiller.
“Hikurrrod? Is that you?”
“...Missha? Bjorn? What?! Why are you guys here!?”
“Wow, there’s no doubt that our party was connected by fate!”
What were the chances of us going in separately without any coordination and meeting again by chance?
“What about the commission? Didn’t you go off to do that? What happened?” After taking a moment to marvel at the amazing coincidence, Hikurod raised a question.
Well, it must have seemed strange to him because we were the ones who had entered the labyrinth separately. I gave him the excuse I’d prepared. “Ah, we finished it already.”
“Finished?”
“They had business on the first floor. When the labyrinth closed, our client returned to the city.”
“Ooh, did they?” That was apparently a good enough reason, because the dwarf nodded without any further concerns.
Now it was our turn to ask questions. “Why are you here? Didn’t you say you would only be on the second floor?”

As far as I knew, these three had been meant to be doing a simple collection commission in the Rock Desert. So why was the third floor, and oddly enough the Jet-Black Estuary connected to the Land of the Dead, their current location?
“Ah, that’s because the Stone Golem’s inner core came out earlier than expected. We came up here to complete the other request I prepared just in case.”
His reasoning was sound, but I asked why he didn’t tell us earlier if he had prepared the commission in advance.
“Hahaha! If I did, you would’ve stopped us from doing it!”
That was true. A combination of a tank, a mage, and a scout was quite unbalanced. That was probably hypocritical of us to say as a tank and melee combo, though.
“...So what is your request?”
“It’s a collection request again. All we have to do is get two eyes from a Frogman Sorcerer. Since you’re here, would you like to join us?”
“How much is the pay?”
“Two million stones. Of course, if you two join, the final payment will be divided into exactly five equal parts.”

A payment of four hundred thousand stones per person was not bad, and selling the other remains aside from the eyeballs would increase that amount even more. Of course, since the target was not an ordinary Frogman but a Frogman Sorcerer, the question remained whether the commission was achievable or not. That depended on luck.
“I’ll do it.”

After running into Hans, I was anxious about the two of us going around alone so I agreed. After all, Missha and I wouldn’t be doing anything other than hunting Frogmen anyway. If the commission ended early, I could suggest that all of us go up to the fourth floor together.
“Haha, then sleep. If we talk any more, I fear we’ll get stabbed.”
The glares from the other parties resting around us continued, so we stopped chatting and went to bed.
Thanks to this, I’ll be able to sleep for five hours.
This was the advantage of large numbers. Your watch time was shorter and your sleep time increased.
After that, time passed. When the morning of the tenth day dawned, the water level went down and we left the resting area. Wandering around, we focused our attention on hunting.
Having a scout is definitely ideal.
I was realizing it all over again, but the scout was a position that raised the quality of labyrinth life.

“If you go that way, you’ll run into a river. Come this way.” As if he had memorized the entire terrain, Rotmiller guided us along the optimal route. Even though we’d been wandering around for so long, we didn’t have to cross the water more than three times.
“Hmm, another bust...”

After defeating one Frogman Sorcerer in four hours, we licked our lips. The body had disappeared without a trace. This was the downside of a collection request. If you used Distortion magic on a monster, there was an extremely low chance you could acquire its corpse intact, but it wouldn’t drop an essence or mana stone.
Whew, I’m already at a loss thinking about all the manual labor I’ll be doing in the future.

As you progressed into the latter half of the game, there were more things that required monster remains: equipment, consumables, etcetera. For example, the Spirit Imprint. You could go up to stage five with money alone, but after that, you needed to collect the ingredients yourself.
...Let’s think about that later. As long as I have money, I can get that stuff from the exchange or entrust it to someone as a request.
Anyway, as traveling became easier, the battles became easier too, between Rotmiller’s arrows, Dwalkie’s magic, and Missha’s ice blades.

“...I’ve been meaning to ask, but how did this happen?” Staring at the frozen Frogman, Rotmiller expressed some suspicion, but this wasn’t a problem either. Cold Condensation and Ice Crush weren’t really obvious skills.
“Oh, that? My Spirit Beast evolved!” Missha smoothly replied with the answer I had prepared for her in advance.
“Ah, did it really? At this rate, you might be promoted to rank six.”
“M-Miss Karlstein! Congratulations!”
Everyone knew that Missha had signed a contract with an ice-type Spirit Beast, so no one doubted it. That was only natural since they had no reason to think it was a lie in the first place.
Every time I do this, my conscience gets stabbed.
But what could I do? I had to accept it. This was the fate of those of us who lived as evil spirits.
“Rotmiller, the water seems to be rrrising... is it okay?”
“Don’t worry, the safe zone is right next to us.”

Soon it was time for the tenth day to come to an end. The water gradually rose, but thanks to Rotmiller having memorized all the nearby terrain, we maximized our time before setting up camp after the hunt. The same thing happened the next two days, and soon it was the morning of the thirteenth day.
“Is this rrright? It’s done, right?”
“I-It seems so.” As soon as we resumed our quest, we hunted a Sorcerer. An arrow clearly pierced through its neck, but the corpse did not disappear.
“W-With Miss Karlstein here, luck is definitely on our side!”
“Haha, this blind fellow. The way I see it, this is thanks to Bjorn, not Missha. That guy is always lucky.”
Ignoring Dwalkie and Hikurod’s commentary, we obtained the corpse of the Sorcerer in just two days. Hmm, maybe it was too early to say it’d been obtained, though.
“Uhm, but what should we do with this?”
“W-Wait a moment. I’ll use magic on it.” First, Dwalkie used Preservation magic to prevent the corpse from decomposing, but that was it. It wasn’t like we could dump the whole corpse into a bag.
“Missha, since you use a knife, you must be good at things like this, right?”
“W-What are you talking about, you dwarf? I-I’ve never done anything like this beforrre! Shouldn’t you do it? The Stone Golem was your commission too.”
“W-Well... the Stone Golem was just a matter of taking out the inner core...”
Even just to take the eyeballs out and not the other remains, it was necessary to dismantle the whole body. None of us had experience with that except for the well-rounded worker Rotmiller.

“Get out of the way. I will do it.” Soon after, Rotmiller sighed and skillfully dismembered the Sorcerer’s body with a carving knife. Apparently, he had done this often while working as part of a collection party in the past.
“As expected, Rotmiller, you’re the best!”
“Ohh, I agree—ugh, I’m going to look somewhere else for a bit...”
After about thirty minutes, under Rotmiller’s skillful hand, the Sorcerer’s body was cleaved into muscle, blood, bone, and internal organs and placed in a box.
“Then what do we do now?” Missha asked. The third floor, Pilgrim’s Path, closed after the fifteenth day. In other words, there were still three days left.
I spoke up since I had been waiting for someone to ask. “The request seems to be over, so how about going to the fourth floor?”
“Um, true... It’s been a long time since the whole party assembled, so it’d be a pity to finish this adventure on just the third floor.”
“Rotmiller, what do you think? Do you think you can make it to the fourth floor in time?”

Rotmiller closed his eyes like he needed time to consider it. Going through several zones in three days and getting to the portal in the heart of the Witch’s Forest must require some thought. “It’ll be tight, but I think it’s possible.”
This was quite fascinating. Originally, I had planned to break the Rift, kill the monsters, and return straight to the city.
As expected, things never go according to plan.
Somehow, instead, I ended up going to the fourth floor.

The three-day journey that followed was harder than expected. First of all, our sleep time was drastically reduced, and we invested the rest of our time solely on travel. We even had to speed-walk the whole way, so as the days went by, the others grew incredibly tired. However, our goal was still in sight.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – The Witch’s Forest has activated.]

This was already my third time passing through the Witch’s Forest. The first time I was here, Missha and I had ended up stranded and had endured all sorts of hardships, but as long as Rotmiller was here, there was nothing to be afraid of.
“Everyone, follow me.”
Since there was an incident last time, we connected our bodies with rope and quickly ran through the forest. After a while, a little over three hours remained until the third floor closed.
“You did well, Rotmiller.”
We stood in front of a huge tower located in the heart of the Witch’s Forest. A colorful portal sat in front of a massive door that looked like the entrance.
“Now, let’s go in!”
We waited for the color to change just in case of any issues and entered at the same time.
“M-Mister?!” I heard a faint, familiar voice in the distance.

chapters.title: Chapter 116: Reunion (4)
paragraphs: Erwen Fornacci di Tersia was currently in the Witch’s Forest with her older sister, Daria.
“Ugh... I’m so dizzy...”
“Once you get used to it, it will be fine. When you do, concentrate on the sounds around you.”

The reason she’d entered the Witch’s Forest after hunting on the third floor for a while was simple. Lately, she’d been training as a scout. So she was using the last day before the labyrinth closed to enter the Witch’s Forest.
“Even if you don’t become a professional scout, you’ll have to know how to find your way to the fourth floor.”

Her older sister was a skilled navigator, so she had already inherited the knowledge and know-how to find her way on the lower floors by herself. However, the Witch’s Forest was different, a special terrain where you could only navigate by relying on your senses.
“So, do you think you can hear it?”

Erwen followed her sister’s instructions and focused on the sounds she could hear. Other races had to specialize in a specific ability, whether it was smell or sight, to avoid getting lost in the Witch’s Forest.
Thump!

However, elves, who naturally had enhanced hearing, didn’t have to do that. Although it would be difficult—which was the norm, according to her sister—any one of them could find their way to the fourth floor.
Thump!

As soon as she closed her eyes and listened, she noticed faint sounds that she hadn’t before—the blade-like whoosh of the wind, the resulting sway of the branches, the howling of monsters, the clang of sharp weapons, and so on. Examining them one by one, she was able to pinpoint a distinctly alien sound.
Thump!
A heavy thud, like a beating heart. This must have been the thrum of mana that her sister was talking about.
“Over there...”
When she pointed in the direction of the sound, Daria smiled proudly. “Good job. Shall we go, then?”

Erwen continued to focus on the sound and found her way. There were times when she didn’t sense a monster approaching because she was too absorbed in her task, but her sister helped her out every time so it wasn’t a problem. After traveling like that for a long while, the hum of the mana grew louder.
Thump!
It was now loud enough to roar in her ears without her deliberately focusing on it. She decided to stop concentrating on the sound.
“You did well, Rotmiller.”
Erwen frowned at the sudden voice. She didn’t know who Rotmiller was, but... “Hmm?”
“What’s wrong?”
That voice was familiar. It was a sharp yet warm voice... similar to one she missed.
Could it be...?
Though she didn’t think it was possible, Erwen’s legs were already moving in the direction of the speaker.
“Erwen? Where...? Stop—!” Daria called out behind her, but she continued forward as if possessed.

About a minute passed. A wide-open space appeared before her, revealing a huge tower hidden in the forest. A group of adventurers stood in front of it: one dwarf, two humans, one beastwoman... and one barbarian.

Of course, he looked completely different from the person in her memory. He was wearing the shiny armor of an experienced adventurer, and his shield was much larger and more extravagant. Plus, because he was wearing a helmet, his face wasn’t visible.
“M-Mister?!” But Erwen instinctively sensed it. It was that man. “Mister!”

A second too late, she shouted so loud that the entire forest echoed with the sound, but the barbarian did not look back. His body had already been half inside the portal when she spotted him, and now he had completely disappeared. So Erwen ran, intending to follow him and enter the portal right away.
“Erwen!”
Her speed now was incomparable to how it used to be back on the first floor, but she was soon stopped by her sister. “Let me go! I have to go—”
“Snap out of it!”
“That person is—”
“Don’t be so stubborn. You didn’t even see his face properly.”
Erwen went silent. She was belatedly realizing how she must have looked. “I... I know. But I can just tell!”
“And if it isn’t him? The fourth floor is dangerous for a two-person party. And you don’t even know what kind of people we might be following.”
“Th-that’s...”

Erwen hadn’t even considered that because she was already convinced she was right. However, she did not have the confidence to explain this feeling in her heart to her older sister. She was about to do something rash and shake off Daria’s grip when the color of the portal changed to red.
Now, even if she entered the portal, she wouldn’t be able to go where those people had gone.
“Why! Why did you stop me?!”
“Because I had to! Didn’t I tell you that if you follow someone up to the fourth floor, they might think you’re a looter?”
“But... that was Mister...!” Erwen pursed her lips. A wave of anger surged up from deep within her heart, but she let out a long breath and came to her senses.
Yeah, it’s okay. At least I know he’s alive...
For now, she decided to be content with that. If she hadn’t been mistaken just then, and if he really was alive...
I can see him again soon.
Surely, they’d meet again.
[You have entered the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.]
What was that? That voice? It seemed to be calling me... Could it be Erwen?
I jolted. The only person who called me Mister was her. However, that would be a little improbable.
Could a coincidence like that really happen?

After somehow managing to reunite with my fellow party members in this huge labyrinth, it was difficult to imagine such a coincidence happening again. It must have just been a conversation between other adventurers. Anyway, it was nothing to worry about right now.
“Bjorn, what are you doing? Come on, get moving!”

The Tower of Heavens was about 1,400 square feet, and there was a stone chamber with a tightly sealed door on each wall. This was the first trial you had to face right upon entry. In other words, waves of monsters were already coming straight for us.
“Kyaaagh!”

Seven rank-nine, three rank-eight, and one rank-seven monster. Monsters that normally appeared on the third floor attacked us in random groups regardless of their habitat. This was why I used to call this place the Tower of Training in the game. Because there were so many types of monsters, it was easy to get experience points, and you could deal with combinations you’d never seen before.
An Orc Sorcerer, a Stone Golem, Living Armor, and a Dullahan.
Right from the jump, we were met with an odd combination.
[Living Armor has cast Armor Boost.]
The Living Armor was draped over the Dullahan’s body, almost like it was using it as a host.
[Orc Sorcerer has cast Frenzy. Dullahan’s physical resistance increases by 3 times for 10 seconds.]
The Dullahan, which already had a ridiculously high physical resistance, pretty much became steel. The Stone Golem used Suppression to dispense debuffs in the meantime.
“Behelahhh!”
While Missha and Rotmiller were clearing out the rank-nine trash, Hikurod and I created a shield wall to block the Dullahan. It was a strong combination, but with two tanks, it was easy to manage.
Even having high physical resistance doesn’t mean much to us.
Our main damage dealers were Dwalkie and Missha. Dwalkie was a wizard, which went without saying, but Missha was now on a proper ice route, which raised her cold damage dramatically.
I was busy acting as a meat shield when the battle ended a moment later. The dwarf cocked his head. “Um, was this always this easy?”
“I guess we’ve all gotten strongerrr!”
“Haha, that was a new spell I learned just now. What do you think?”
Initially, no matter how strong a tank was, it wasn’t outwardly obvious. On the other hand, damage dealers exhibited obvious growth. As for the scout... Well, they were treated as non-combatants.
“Ahem.”
It was safe to say that the scout had done his job just by bringing us to our destination in time. It wasn’t just monsters that appeared on the fourth floor.
[The trial has been completed.]

Soon after all the monsters died, the tightly closed doors opened wide. Each door had a unique design engraved on it: Courage, Wisdom, Fate, and Patience. Normally, I would have opened the Stairway of Courage and fought a random monster.
“Since we don’t have much time, it would be better to climb the floors quickly.”

However, we decided to take the Stairway of Wisdom for now. The Tower of Heavens’s difficulty increased each time you passed a trial, but the Stairway of Wisdom was a route where you could climb all its floors in one go. With our combat power, we’d have to reach the twentieth floor before we got any real hunting in.
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]

For that reason, we walked through the abyss-like darkness. The path was complicated. There were traps, and monsters appeared occasionally, but none of it was dangerous with our professional scout, Rotmiller, with us.
Bam!

When we reached the sixth floor in about an hour, the door we came through shut behind us and monsters attacked. Unlike on the first floor, there were three rank-sevens, but none of our enemies were particularly dangerous. And unlike before, the combination was also on the more mediocre side.
“Hmm, I don’t think there is an option to take the Stairway of Wisdom this time.”
After finishing up our hunt, we had no choice but to take the Stairway of Courage. Fate had too many variables, and Patience... everyone shook their heads at that in unison.
We’d be more at ease fighting a few more monsters.
In this reality, trials of Patience were trials to avoid. They brought back memories of being hot, cold, sad, and really messed up.
[You have chosen the Stairway of Courage.]

Anyway, we climbed the stairs and reached the seventh floor. A monster appeared and that was it. The battle ended with ease, but there was no sign of the tightly closed doors opening. That was to be expected. If you chose Courage, you had to wait four hours even after killing all the monsters.
“Now then, let’s take a break and recharge our courage again!”

We were tired from running through the Witch’s Forest so, ignoring the dwarf’s joke, we took a break without any regrets. There was no need for a night watch. The monsters here did not respawn, and once the color of the portal changed, other adventurers could not enter behind us.
“Haha, then let’s go!”
After sleeping for four hours, we woke up and took the Stairway of Wisdom again as we climbed the tower. Soon enough, we reached the twelfth floor. But what was this?
“Gaaah!”
We froze as we saw the monster sitting alone in the center of the stone chamber.
Thump!
It had a large body that was over thirteen feet tall, huge fangs protruding from its mouth, gray-white leather covering its bulky muscles, and a hunched back with wide, deformed shoulder bones.
“A T-Troll...?”
“Why is that thing here?”
A Troll was classified as a top-notch bastard among rank-five monsters. If Death Fiends were notorious for flattening newbies, this bastard played the role of keyboard smasher for mid-level gamers.
Why is this asshole here?
I also had quite a few memories of slamming my fists down on my keyboard because of this bastard. As the memories came to me, so did the curses. “Goddamn it.”
No wonder things had been going so smoothly since meeting Hans. Was this why?
Fuck, I didn’t know it was going to be a monster this time.
In the labyrinth, plunderers weren’t the only thing you had to look out for.

chapters.title: Chapter 117: Dark Clouds (1)
paragraphs: It seemed a rank-five monster’s Fear ability was impressive. Dwalkie backed away, stuttering. “W-Why is a rank-five monster in the Tower of Heavens?”

It wasn’t that I couldn’t understand where he was coming from. It was common knowledge that only monsters up to rank six appeared here. But if I were to look at things through the lens of an experienced player, some rank-fives did actually spawn as well, although the odds were very close to impossible. I’d experienced it maybe seven times up to this point in ten years of playing the game. That was how often it happened.
I really didn’t expect to see one on the twelfth floor, though.

The difficulty of the Tower of Heavens was fixed from the hundredth floor on. Each time I ran into a rank-five monster, it had been while I was working my butt off on a floor above that. But this, on the twelfth floor?
Goddamn Hans Effect.
Despite how much I wanted to sigh, I instead shouted with all my might. “Everyone, look alive!”

Whether it was Hans, or my goddamned luck, this was not the time to calculate probabilities and think about how miserable we were. The causes were something that we could consider later. If we were already facing the effects, the most important thing to do was act.
“Behelahhh!”
I cast Wild Outburst and charged forward. If I stayed still, they would only come to their senses after someone died.
Voom!

When I charged at it with my increased Threat Level, the Troll immediately threw a punch. It was shocking that such a massive body could be capable of such speed, but what really surprised me was its power.
Bang!
Damn, I almost dropped the shield. It had really been a long time since I’d been overpowered in terms of strength, and I felt myself getting pushed back.
“I-I’ll help you!” Hikurod promptly joined in and took the Troll’s next blow.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Balance Weight.]
Thanks to the Iron Tusk’s active skill, he didn’t get pushed back and even got some shock absorption as a bonus.
Kakakak!
However, the dwarf’s buckler was immediately turned to scrap metal.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Emergency Restoration.]
He had only received one blow, but had already had to use his equipment repair skill.
I told you to get a new shield, didn’t I?
“Gaaah!”
Taking another fist, I hit the troll on the shoulder with my mace.
Whack!
I felt a heavy shock jolt through my hand, but that was all. The Troll bastard didn’t have a single broken bone and just threw another punch.
Dang, I guess damage from me won’t work.
I licked my lips and dodged the fist. Wounding it was pointless, and it was foolish to compete with a Troll in strength.
Voom!
The moment the Troll’s fist began to soar through the air, our damage dealers came to their senses and started to support us. The first shot was from Rotmiller’s crossbow.
Whip! Tick!
The arrow was shot with great force, but it bounced off like it had hit a stone wall. An arrow couldn’t pierce a Troll’s skin. Though one of Mr. Bear’s probably would’ve been a different story.
Slice!
Anyway, Missha’s blade, which I had been banking my hopes on, didn’t end up pulling through either. It cut through the Troll’s thick hide, but the slice wasn’t very deep.
Still, I’m glad she’s an ice swordsman.

The sight of the frosted-over wound soothed my disappointment. As a rank-five monster, the Troll’s resistance stat was too high for it to ever reach Frozen status, but still. Missha’s abilities would block its healing factor even just a little bit.
“I-It’s done!” Dwalkie finished a chant and fired his special Enhanced Ice Spear. It was aimed at the head, the monster’s weak point.
Crunch!
The Troll jerk, who had monstrous physique stats and high mana resistance, just broke the ice spear with its bare fist. The sight seemed to hurt Dwalkie’s morale.
“Gaaah!” Dwalkie began stuttering in fear. “W-We have to run. If we face a Troll unprepared...”
Yeah, it wasn’t exactly an easy monster. Usually, you had to make significant preparations to hunt one. But, where were we going to run to? “Shut up and focus on the battle!”
“A-All right!”
Huh, why did he have to be screamed at to listen? Anyway, now that he was done panicking, we needed to regroup.
Bam!
Certain basic specs were required to initiate a battle with a rank-five monster. I was sure rank six had requirements like that, too, but at rank five it was completely different.
What a headache.

Just look at the vampire in the Bloody Citadel. At that time, Raven, a rank-six wizard, had been there. Since a wizard’s ranking could be calculated as +1.5, that meant there was, in effect, a rank-five damage dealer on the team. We also had an overpowered item called Tears of the Goddess, a holy relic strong enough to kill a Death Knight in one shot. Not to mention the sun attribute curse spells being fired off on top of all that. But what were the results?
It still wouldn’t die in one blow.

That was the beauty of a rank-five monster. Even though I had endured and endured on potions alone and had poured everything I had into that one shot, it still wouldn’t die. And that had been a monster with high regeneration but low defensive power. But a Troll? It excelled in both regeneration and defense. To put it simply, it was similar to the Death Fiend, which served well as a sort of gatekeeper—a type of monster where the possibility of a lucky shot did not exist if you didn’t meet the required specs.
Still... we just made it past the cutoff.

I objectively analyzed our combat power, excluding both myself and the tank dwarf to focus on the damage dealers. Were their attacks really enough to take down a rank-five monster alone? The answer was: they could be, maybe. If all of Dwalkie’s mana were channeled into one curse, and as long as the two tanks persisted, it could be possible as long as Missha, who had gotten significantly stronger, continued to deal damage.
The problem is, it wouldn’t be strange at all if someone died in the process.
Due to the nature of Trolls, if it was impossible for you to beat it on specs, you had no choice but to resign yourself to a long battle. And the longer the battle, the more mishaps there were.
“Missha! Be careful!” I clenched my teeth as I threw my body forward to block the fist that had been thrown at Missha.
“Ah, th-thank you!”
It was clearly going to be a tough battle where a casualty wouldn’t be unheard of. If Missha or Dwalkie got hit at all, it would be a game over. However, we had no choice but to try.
“Behelahhh!”

Five minutes, ten minutes, fifteen minutes. Through dripping sweat, the battle waged on. Every minute, every second, went by with each of us focusing on our roles and pouring everything we had into achieving one goal.
Bam!
First, Hikurod and I took turns taking blows and conserving our stamina as much as possible.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight curse spell Aggravate.]
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-nine curse spell Slowdown.]
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-seven curse spell Weakening.]

Dwalkie devoted himself to the support role, casting curse magic instead of offensive magic. The Troll’s regeneration ability was reduced, its movements slowed, and its physical resistance somewhat decreased.
Slice!
Through it all, Missha continued stabbing it. Under my orders, she aimed solely at one spot.
Slice!
With her repeated slices, its right arm was left half-dangling.
“Gaaah!”

Rotmiller didn’t just sit around, either. Because the monster was running rampant, he couldn’t put an arrow in its eye as I had requested, but the attempt itself was helpful from a tank’s point of view because it divided the monster’s attention.
“Dwalkie, hold on to me!” Also, it was Rotmiller’s job to run away with Dwalkie when the Troll’s aggro honed in on him. Jeez, this whole fight was like walking on thin ice.
Bam!

I quickly wiped the sweat from my brow as I returned the Troll to its normal state using Wild Outburst, which had just happened to finish cooling down. It seemed like everything was going well, but every moment was a crisis, and all of it consumed resources.
I’m going to be breaking the bank for repairs again.

The lithinum shield and breastplate, which I had used a lot of money to fortify, were already dented in some places. It was only natural since I’d taken countless punches from the Troll at this point. Plus, lithinum was a second-grade material, not third-grade. I’d be a fool if I really expected it to remain intact after being attacked by a rank-five monster. Plus, repair costs weren’t the important thing in this situation.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Emergency Restoration.]

The dwarf, who was using one of his skills to repair his buckler after every attack, was now almost out of MP. Missha was in the same boat. After having maintained Cold Condensation to prevent the Troll from healing even a bit more, her MP had quickly been consumed. However, the most serious issue was Dwalkie.
“Huff... Huff!”

Trolls had high mana resistance. In order to keep the curses on it active, Dwalkie chanted spells without stopping and was becoming a corpse without even noticing. That meant it was time for a final check-in.
“How much mana do you have left?” I asked him.
“Two minutes... No, I can do three more minutes.”
“What if you drop Slowdown?”
“...Seven minutes should be possible.”
“I see. Skip Slowdown from now on.”

Without Slowdown, the Troll’s movements would become even more intense, but we’d have to deal with it. I didn’t know about the rest of it, but if Aggravation went away, its cut-off arm would heal, at best, within seconds.
Seven minutes...
A time limit had been set. If we couldn’t kill the troll in seven minutes, we’d be beaten. So, it was time to see this match through to the end.
“Missha, how much longer?”
“Ugh, even if you say that, I can’t saw it off!”

I could admit that there were problems with my plan. It was impossible to cut off a Troll’s arm with Missha’s sword. The Aggravation curse, Frostbite, and the acid blood that lay in the Serpent’s Fang cut through the muscle and managed to stop the wound from healing. But the problem was the bone, which had the same durability as a third-grade material. I guess that wasn’t exactly inaccurate since troll bones were third-grade materials. Anyway, that wasn’t a big problem. It wasn’t like anything in my life ever went according to plan.
Time to switch to Plan B.
Abandoning Plan A, I came up with a new one. I just made it up on the fly, but anyway. “Hikurod! From now on, you’re in charge!”
“All right! But what are you going to do?”

Instead of answering, I lifted my mace. Every round hole had a round peg to go with it. A knife wasn’t a good weapon for breaking bones in the first place, especially not when compared to a reliable blunt weapon.
Khak!
When I swung the mace down, a good vibration ran up my arms, real damage that could not be absorbed with leather or muscle.
[Troll has cast Frenzy. Its pain temporarily disappears, and its physical stats increase significantly.]
The Troll bastard stopped screaming in pain and began rampaging in earnest, even using its skills.
“H-How much longer!” The dwarf, who somehow managed to stop him, shouted more urgently than ever.
I didn’t answer. How was I supposed to know? I was just a barbarian who kept on going until it was over.
“Behelahhh!” Instilling the spirit of a barbarian into my heart, I swung down my mace without pause.
Khak!
The piece of shit Troll tried to push me off with its good arm, but the dwarf somehow stopped it.
Clunk.
I threw away the shield in my other hand, since swinging my mace with both hands gave me more power.
Kak-kak-kak!
When I wrapped both fists around the mace and hit it, a slightly stronger jolt ran through my hands. This was a feeling I had gotten while fighting the vampire, like just a few more hits would do it.
“Behelaaah!” Using Wild Outburst, I raised my physique stat a little more. Even the dwarf couldn’t stop a frenzying Troll, but I was confident in my durability.
Whack!
I concentrated on my macing while taking the troll’s hits head-on. Once, twice, three times.
Crunch!
After the third hit, its bone was slightly shattered. Four, five, six times.
Crunch!
After the sixth, the bones fractured and its arm bent at a weird angle.
“Gaaah!”
At this point, you’d think it would back down, but the prideful Troll kept on attacking.
Smack!
Even though I was getting my ass kicked, I swung the mace with pleasure.
Crunch!
Finally, on the tenth swing, its bone completely shattered. Its arm now dangled, relying only on a few tendons.
“Missha!”
Before I even finished shouting, Missha sped over and swung her sword to cut the tendons.
Boom!
The muscled arm fell to the ground with a heavy thud. This was the first win we’d had after twenty minutes of this shit.
And this is just the beginning.
I was a barbarian who couldn’t be satisfied with just that. Without even taking a moment to catch our breaths, we waited for the next opportunity. From now on, it really was a race against time.
[Troll has cast Super Regeneration.]
The Troll only used its active skill when its body was seriously injured or its life was in danger due to a brain injury.
Fuck, of course it’s using that.

After the skill activated, bone began to grow from the open wound and flesh and muscles began to emerge a beat later. Even with the Wound Exacerbation curse on it and the Frostbite state on top of that, the Troll still hadn’t reached Frozen status. What an overpowered healing ability.
It will take at least two minutes for its arm to grow back completely.

For at least the next two minutes, it wouldn’t be able to use Super Regeneration again. It wasn’t that the ability just dramatically increased the user’s healing factor—the skill could only be used on one designated area at a time. In other words, even if its brain exploded or its heart shattered in the next two minutes, none of that could be fixed until that arm completely regenerated.
Clunk.
I threw off my armor and helmet. Hikurod looked at me like I was crazy. “W-Why are you taking off your armor all of a sudden?”
Why do you think? This guy sure is slow.
[You have cast Giantization.]
My body grew rapidly. It was still small compared to the Troll’s thirteen feet, but this was enough for a fight.
Clunk!
Throwing away my mace and shield, I grabbed the Troll by the neck and hung on it. Then I wrapped my feet around the Troll’s other hand.
“Grrrrrg!”

I guess it had never imagined an adventurer would dare to wrestle with it. The Troll bastard was incredibly confused and began to struggle, trying to get its hand out of my grip. Of course, that didn’t change anything, no matter how much stronger it was than me.
Looks like he has a problem with his head too.
After all, what could a one-armed bastard really do in a situation like this?
“Missha, stab the eyes first!”
The stage had been set. Now it was time to watch this play out.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Dark Clouds (2)
paragraphs: Although practically synonymous with the word “regeneration,” like any other living thing, you could kill the rank-five monster Troll by destroying its heart or head. However, I instead invested all my party’s energy into cutting off its arm.
“Gaaah!”
Finally, I grappled its one remaining arm and rendered it incapacitated. In other words, the right environment for Missha to sneak in more hits without risking her life had officially been created.
Dash.
Missha, who had been wary of the Troll’s long arms and focused on keeping her distance, took the first leap. Landing on my shoulder, she stabbed her twin swords into the Troll’s eyeballs.
Stab!
No matter how high a monster’s physical resistance, it always had a weak spot.
“Gaaargh!”
When the acid blood-enchanted blades pierced its fragile eyes, the Troll’s struggling intensified.
Damn, what kind of strength...
“B-Bjorn?”

“Don’t worry about me, just keep poking!” I shouted, squeezing its arm with my thighs with all my might. Realizing this was not the time or place for a chat, Missha focused on driving her blade forward instead of answering me.
We reached our first unexpected hurdle here.
Stab, stab, stab—Hack! Khak!
While Missha was repeatedly stabbing the knife into its eye, we heard the sound of something scratching the blade. That was to be expected. Humans had bones behind their eyeballs too.
“B-Bjorn...? It’s too harrrd to stab in!”

Its bone strength was the problem. I had thought that since it wasn’t a thick bone in the arm or anything like that, she should be able to stab through it into its brain, but it seemed the Troll wasn’t willing to die so easily.
“Keep going.”
“Okay!” Soon, Missha grabbed the Serpent’s Fang behind her and continued to slash at its eyelids. Then, our second unexpected hiccup occurred.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
A short time later, the Troll started raging. After losing its vision, it gave up on trying to throw me off altogether and used its only free limbs, its feet, to charge in one specific direction.
“Dwalkie! It’s aiming for Dwalkie!”
Somehow, this eyeless Troll asshole was running straight toward Dwalkie.
“Gaaah!”
Rotmiller grabbed Dwalkie and tried to evade it, but the Troll violently pursued them like it could see them.
“Mana! It must be sensing his mana!” called Hikurod.
Even I had been unaware of this particular phenomenon. Could it really, as the dwarf said, be instinctively sensing and following mana?
Goddamn it.

Whatever the reason, just when I thought things were going according to plan, the situation turned to shit in an instant. Within just ten seconds, Dwalkie and Rotmiller were cornered. This made sense. Maybe it would’ve been different if Missha were the one it was chasing, but Rotmiller didn’t have the physical stats needed to carry another person while escaping a rank-five monster.
“Gaaah!”
Eventually, the Troll rushed toward the cornered men. The dwarf tried to stop it but to no avail.
Bang!

The Troll kicked Hikurod like a soccer ball, just in time for his MP to run out and the effects of Balance Weight to deactivate. As a result, he crashed into a wall. God damn it, the timing just had to play out like that, huh.
“B-Bjorn?”
“You just focus on killing it!”
“O-Okay!”
Using the momentary opening Hikurod had gifted them, Rotmiller escaped the bind he was in. Of course, Hikurod had only bought them a little time. Maybe three seconds?
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The Troll caught up to Rotmiller, who was running in the opposite direction and rolled on the ground to escape a kick. From my position, I now couldn’t see the situation below me.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
At this point, the Troll kicked down.
“Eeek!”
I didn’t hear the sound of anyone being trampled, but if things continued on like this for even a little longer, someone would definitely die—Dwalkie, Rotmiller, or maybe even both.
Boom!
I was at a crossroads. Missha was completely unaware of the situation below us as she was diligently stabbing the monster with her blade. All decisions were up to me.
Boom!

If I released my grip here and dropped down, I’d be able to protect Dwalkie and Rotmiller. But in the end, that choice would lead to total annihilation. If I let go, the troll would attack Missha with its free arm, and we wouldn’t get another opportunity to take it down.
God damn it.
I squeezed my eyes shut and a thought came to me unwittingly—wasn’t this something I was going to have to experience someday, anyway?
Boom!

Dungeon and Stone wasn’t a game where you pursued an adventure full of hopes and dreams. As the game progressed, the death of a teammate became inevitable, but as long as the main character survived, the adventure continued. That was the kind of game it was.
This fucking game—
Crunch!

Just then, I heard the sound of something being mangled, a sound I’d heard countless times since waking up in this world—the sound of flesh and bones being squashed. Sensing something was wrong, Missha stopped her blade. It was only for a very short moment, though.
“Keep going!”
At my cry, Missha continued to stab.
Kakak, kakak, kakak!
Gritting my teeth, I channeled all my strength into restraining the Troll’s remaining arm.
Smack!

Dwalkie came into view as the Troll kicked him away. His spine was seemingly snapped, his body bent at a deformed angle. With this, I realized something, and it wasn’t something I particularly wanted to know. The first sound had to have come from Rotmiller.

Did she see Dwalkie’s body as it rose to our eye level? Missha flinched for a moment, then continued to drive her blade down, looking like she could burst into tears at any moment. “Die! Die! Die! You monsterrr! Just die!”

As we were forced to watch our teammates suffer, the situation turned from worse to even worse. With the blow to Dwalkie, the curses on the monster had been lifted. Super Regeneration was able to activate normally and the Troll’s arm quickly recovered.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Ice Crush.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Ice Crush.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Ice Crush.]
Perhaps realizing that there was no time, Missha slashed her sword with all her might. It was a moment where each minute and second seemed to last a billion times longer.
Khak! Kak, kak... Crunch!
With a refreshing crack, the body of the Troll that I had been holding onto with all my might promptly disappeared.
[You have killed a Troll. EXP +5]
The bastard was finally dead.

The dead Troll’s body dissolved into light and disappeared, and Missha and I fell to the ground. Normally, we would have reoriented ourselves in midair and landed on both feet, but neither of us had the energy to do so.
Thud!
As I lay stretched out on the floor, staring blankly at the ceiling, a mana stone the size of a fist fell down right next to my head.
Tap. Roll...

That was all the loot there was. No essence dramatically appeared. All of a sudden, it hit me that this situation was real. Yes, this wasn’t a dream. The choice I’d made just now, and the image of Dwalkie, in such a horrible state, getting sent flying because of that choice...
“Rotmiller! Dwalkie!”
Discarding my desire to rest, I forced myself to stand up. Missha was already running to pick up one of our fallen comrades. “Rotmillerrr! Wake up!”
“D-Don’t... shake—!”
“S-Sorry!”

Surprisingly, Rotmiller was alive. One of his legs was broken and crushed, but it wasn’t a life-threatening injury. It was literally a miracle. If his head or upper body had been trampled, that would have been the end of it.
“Not me... D-Dwalkie first...”
“O-Okay!”
While Missha ran over to Dwalkie, I turned to check on the dwarf. He had no major trauma.
I guess he just hit his head on the wall and passed out.
The problem was Dwalkie.
“B-Bjorn! What should I do? D-Dwalkie i-isn’t breathing...”
“Move.” Pushing Missha away, I checked Dwalkie’s pulse. His breathing had stopped but his heart was still faintly beating. Survival was still on the table.
Chhh!

First, I took out a high-rank potion and let it trickle into Dwalkie’s mouth. I knew this was just a temporary solution. His spine was folded in half, and his legs had been broken by the impact of the fall. In addition, blood continued to flow from his nose and mouth, suggesting his internal organs were also damaged. Dwalkie was not only an ordinary human being but a wizard, and wizards were famous for being as fragile as glass.
Fuck.
I pressed my lips together. Not only was it unclear whether a high-rank potion could heal an injury like this, but even if he survived, he would surely suffer a whole host of side effects.
“Dwalkie! Hold on a little longerrr! Now that you’ve had a potion, you’ll be fine soon!”
If I had known this would happen, I wouldn’t have used the advanced potion back then...

“Potion...” I turned my head at Rotmiller’s voice, which he forced out with great difficulty. At first, I thought he was asking for a potion for himself. “Use... this.” Rotmiller, still shuddering in pain, held out a bottle of potion in his hand. “Advanced... potion.”
What? An advanced potion? You had that?
“I bought it... just in case. Use this... on him.”

Before I could answer, Missha quickly ran to grab the potion from him. I stopped her from immediately pouring it into Dwalkie’s mouth. “If you give him that in this state, he’ll never be able to walk again.”
“What?”
Potions were not all-powerful. Blindly feeding someone a potion without first setting their bones would have big consequences. “Pour it into his mouth slowly.”

While Missha fed him the potion little by little, I moved his spine and bent legs back into place. All I could do was vaguely rearrange them in a somewhat normal position, but I was sure the potion would do the rest. After all, an advanced potion could even heal a severed arm, right?

“Whew...” As I stared at Dwalkie, horribly tense, I let out a long breath. He was breathing again. It would take a while longer for him to regain consciousness, but his pale complexion had improved a lot.
“...That’s a load off.” The rest could be dealt with just by using a high-rank potion. Of course, there was no time to sit and rest. “Don’t just stand there. Help.”
“O-Okay. What can I do?”
“Bring Hikurod over and lay him next to Dwalkie. Just in case, give him a bottle of low-rank potion.”
While Missha followed my instructions, I looked at Rotmiller’s leg, which had been left untreated for a while.
“Dwalkie, how is he?” Rotmiller asked.
“Don’t worry. Thanks to you, he’ll live. So, why don’t you worry about yourself first?”
“That’s... true. Hahaha.”
“This will hurt quite a bit.”

“That’s all—Ugh! Arrrgh!” Soon, Rotmiller, who had been poisoned, passed out after momentarily seizing. With that, I had done everything I could possibly do in that moment. That seemed to be the case on Missha’s end too.
“Bjorn...” Missha stared at me, her eyes searching for confirmation.
I smiled and answered, “Yes, they all lived.”
“I’m glad... really, rrreally...” Missha slumped over as her body lost all its strength. It was only after hearing my answer that it hit her, even though it didn’t even feel real to me yet.
To think... no one died in the end.

It wasn’t that I wanted that to happen. No, I was more than happy that everyone had survived. However, there were too many things about this that made me uncomfortable. Because I did a decent job and we planned for them in advance, we had handled every unexpected situation that came our way well, but that wasn’t why we had gotten through this crisis.
We were just lucky...
After acknowledging this, I realized what it meant to be an adventurer in this goddamn world. Today, like a movie, everyone had survived.
But things won’t always be like today...
I knew that better than anyone else. There was no way a guy like me could have luck like today’s again and again.

As time passed, they all regained consciousness one by one. The first one to wake up was Hikurod. “...So, we all lived.” After confirming everyone’s survival, the dwarf did not smile heartily like usual. He just repeated my own words back to me. “I’m glad. Yes... I’m very glad...”
Well, if you’d been an adventurer for a few years like he had, you’d probably experienced this quite a few times. Facing the death of a comrade was pretty much the fate of an adventurer.
It was Rotmiller who woke up after him. “To think we’re all safe even after encountering a Troll. I guess I should at least make an offering to the temple when I get back...”
