I hesitantly approached him and blurted out an apology mixed with excuses. “I’m sorry. I didn’t expect the Troll to act like that while blind.”
“...How could that be your fault? We should say thank you. Without you, none of us would have survived.”
“But—”

“Your call was the right one, so don’t beat yourself up about it.” Rotmiller already seemed to know about my decision to risk his and Dwalkie’s lives. How could he not, when I kept shouting at Missha to do so?
“Ugh... ugh...” After a while, Dwalkie groaned and opened his eyes.
“Don’t move. Your wounds haven’t healed yet.”
“Everyone... is okay...?”
“We are! So don’t worry!”
“Ah... M-Miss Karlstein... I’m glad you’re all right.”
“You idiot! You’re one to talk!”
“Th-that’s...!” He coughed. “Y-You’re right... Hahaha.”
When Dwalkie, who was in the worst condition, woke up, the oppressively heavy atmosphere hanging over us instantly brightened.
“Haha, the five of us took down a Troll. I can’t even brag about this. No one will believe me!” Hikurod started cracking jokes like usual, along with Missha.
“Ugh, there should have at least been an essence! So unfairrr. After all that, we got nothing.”
“We survived.”
“Rotmiller, your problem is that you’re not grrreedy enough.”
“Yeah,” Hikurod agreed. “I heard you used an advanced potion this time, didn’t you? Ah, don’t worry. We’ll pool our money together and pay you back.”
“That makes me feel more at ease,” I said.
“Ah, but Bjorn. What are we going to do now?” asked Missha. “You’re not thinking of going higher, rrright?”
“Ha... who do you think I am? I’m just going to rest for the next while.”
“Missha? Why are you asking Bjorn that? Surely I’m the leader of this party?”
“Oh... right.”

Ignoring the dwarf’s question, no one objected to my suggestion to stay on this floor until the labyrinth closed. We weren’t in a state to continue our quest. So, on the site of our fierce battle with a Troll, we took a break to let our tired bodies and minds recover.
[The labyrinth is now closed. You will be transported to Rafdonia.]
A week passed just like that and my sixth expedition came to an end.

chapters.title: Chapter 119: Dark Clouds (3)
paragraphs: In the end, this quest came to a complete standstill after our battle with the Troll. Dwalkie’s condition was not improving like it did earlier.
“Even if he takes more potions, he won’t get better. Not everyone has a body as sturdy as yours.”

Without a boost from his body’s natural healing processes, it would take time for his muscles and bones to return to their proper places even after his wounds healed. So, upon returning to the city, we had to skip the checkpoint and head straight to the temple. Unlike Rotmiller’s, Dwalkie’s injury was something that couldn’t be solved with time.
“Whew, I feel much better now...” Dwalkie, who hadn’t been able to stand for a whole week, was finally able to walk on his own after receiving some high-level healing.
“Are there any repercussions? I was worried since the treatment was so delayed...”
“Haha, don’t worry. I feel so much better I could enter the labyrinth right now.”
“That’s a relief.”

Thanks to us reducing the severity of the injury with an advanced potion at the beginning, Dwalkie was back to normal after a shot of divine power. That took a weight off. If there had been any side effects, they would have interfered with our next quest.
“Then let’s meet up again in two days. We should head home and rest for now.”
The mana stones we managed to get after the team reunited in the labyrinth were not very many, so we decided to postpone the loot distribution until after we completed the commission.
Hmm, would it be around four hundred thousand stones per person?

We’d have to divvy it up later to be sure, but selling the Frogman Sorcerer’s remains should roughly net us that amount, since we promised to give up two hundred thousand stones each for the price of the potion.
Jeez, that goddamn Troll.
The losses we’d taken from that son of a bitch were no joke. Repairing our dented gear was sure to cost quite a bit.
If you were going to make me go through all that hardship, you should have at least spat out an essence.
If I hadn’t already gotten my hands on some stuff beforehand, the trip would have been a total loss.
“Bjorrrn, what are you going to do now?”
“I plan to go to the inn and wash up, then go sort through my things. Oh, with you too, of course.”
“Huh? Me too...?”
“Didn’t you get a good break in the labyrinth? Don’t even think about ditching.”
“I wasn’t! Anyway, I can’t be botherrred to go all the way to my inn. Can I just wash up at yours?”
“Of course.”

We headed to my inn because I didn’t want to waste time on unnecessary travel. I washed up first. We needed to move quickly to get to the commercial district before the carriages stopped running for the day.
“Eh? You’re done all rrready?”
“It’s okay if you take longer. It will take a while for me to sort through everything, anyway.”
“Oh, rrreally?”

After pushing Missha into the bathroom, I laid out the loot from this quest and organized it: the equipment and consumables we obtained after defeating the three men who were after the baby barbarian, as well as Jencia’s things.
I can sell this, and keep this for us to use later...

As I was organizing everything by jotting down a list, someone knocked on the door. “Is anyone here?” It was a male voice I’d never heard before. When I opened the door, I saw a man wearing the badge of an Adventurers’ Guild employee. “Are you Bjorn Yandel?”
“Could you please accompany me to the guild?”

Fuck, just out of the blue? This reminded me of the time I got imprisoned after being asked something similar, but judging by the worker’s tone of voice and expression, it didn’t seem like this was the same kind of situation. There were no guards around, either.
I decided to calm down and figure out what was going on. “Tell me what for. I’ll decide whether to go or not after that.”
“Ah, I didn’t tell you.” The employee carefully explained the situation. “A barbarian named Kharon Tarson has asked you to testify for him.”
“...Testify?”
“Yes. He said you would be able to prove that he is not a plunderer...”
The baby barbarian was in danger.

“Originally, this kind of request wouldn’t have been accepted, but as you know, regulations in regard to these things have become stricter ever since that incident. I realize I’m bothering you, but I’ve just come to check it out. If you have nothing to do with him, you can just say no—”
“Let’s go.”
“Sorry?”
“I’ll just change my clothes. Wait here.” Closing the door, I put my coat on and informed Missha, who was in the shower, that I was heading out. “Missha, today’s plans are canceled.”
“What? That’s so sudden—why?”
“Something seems to have happened to Kharon. I’ll be dropping by the Adventurers’ Guild, so after washing up, go home.”
“What? What do you m—! No, wait, give me more details!”
“I’m here. Let’s go.”
“Is that really so hard, you blockheaded barrrbarian?!”

Ignoring Missha’s justified yelling, I headed to the guild with the staff member who was waiting outside. Coincidentally, the place I was led to was the same branch I had escaped from. “Long time no see.”
“Pardon? Oh, yes... Let’s go in. The branch manager is waiting for you.”
“The branch manager?”

After taking a moment to glance around and reminisce, I followed the employee to the third floor and spotted Kharon dozing off on the sofa. Opposite him was the mustachioed branch manager, who had a very displeased expression on his face.
“Oh, how are you?”
“...Fine.”

How blunt. Still, the situation didn’t seem to be as troubling as I thought. If Kharon had really been accused of being a plunderer, he wouldn’t be dozing up here but instead locked up in the underground prison.
Honkkk!
I first woke Kharon up. Well, I guess I couldn’t say I woke him up. “Kharon, stop pretending to be asleep and get up. You don’t have to do that here.”
At my words, the branch manager and my guide cocked their heads simultaneously. Then Kharon slowly opened his eyes. “...How did you know?”
What do you think? Last I saw you, you disappeared with some very ominous parting words.
“I figured... you might do something like that.”
“Does this mean that you acknowledge me as a warrior?”
“Yeah, something like that.”
When I gave him a half-hearted nod, Kharon gave me a genuine smile and bumped me with his shoulder in greeting. “Anyway, thank you for coming, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Of course. Did they do anything to you?”
“They didn’t do anything, don’t worry,” said the manager. “If they did, would this fellow even be here?”
That’s true, but I didn’t ask you.
“Kharon, answer me.”
“Nothing happened.”
“I see.” I nodded and chuckled. This was why precedent was important. Would they have treated me this well if I hadn’t stirred up all that shit first?
Slump.
In that spirit, I did not ask for permission to sit comfortably on the sofa, just in case the branch manager had forgotten what kind of barbarian I was. “I’ll take rum.”
“...I don’t recall offering you anything to drink.”
“Are you discriminating against me for being a barbarian?”
The branch manager let out a long sigh. “Hah... we don’t have alcohol. I can give you tea—”
“Cold water. Float the ice.”
“...All right.”

Humans were definitely learning creatures. Instead of pointing out my argumentative tone or attitude, the branch manager gave me what I wanted. He had whole-heartedly learned how to deal with rude barbarians.
Again, barbarians are such OP characters.
When I put my dusty feet up on the expensive-looking table, Kharon stared at me with shining eyes. “You... are a true warrior...”

Apparently, acting so nonchalantly in front of a branch manager of the Adventurers’ Guild left quite an impression. Well, the branch manager seemed to feel the same way, seeing as his mustache was trembling in horror. “You guys are really...”
“What, do you have something to say?”
“...No.” As soon as I growled back, the branch manager dropped his tail between his legs for fear of getting bitten.
Smirk.
That was the reaction I had expected. A lot had changed since we’d last met. I was not the same rank-nine barbarian I was back then.
“I heard the rumors about you. They call you Little Balkan?”

I had become a rank-six adventurer in a matter of a few months, and a renowned adventurer with an epithet at that. Along with being acquainted with Baron Martoin, there were even rumors that the count had his eyes on me. Plus, if the branch manager had been watching me, he would also know that I’d been going in and out of the Magic Tower for Raven’s research. And that was just a few of the highlights on my reel.
“Here is your ice water...”

I was stronger, strong enough to squash the branch manager’s head like a tomato in a second. We may have been in the middle of a city where law transcended violence, but what do you know? The branch manager of all people knew I wasn’t the kind of guy to worry about stuff like that.
“Quit the chitchat and let’s get to the point. What do you plan to do with Kharon?”

I pushed aside my requested ice water and asked the question on my mind, but the branch manager just shrugged. “...Nothing. This fellow can leave now if he wishes. We confirmed through a wizard that it was self-defense.”
“...What?” I was momentarily caught off guard by the unexpectedly cool reply.
They already confirmed it with a wizard?

That certainly wasn’t out of the realm of possibility, since Kharon didn’t have high mana resistance like I did. Even without calling me here, they were able to determine whether Kharon’s words were true or not with a single spell.
That means they weren’t after Kharon, but me.
I quickly figured out what was going on. Yeah, that was the Adventurers’ Guild for you. Only now did my heart start to squeeze.
“Kharon, you can leave now,” I said.
“Can I? I was getting hungry...”
“If you skip meals, you won’t grow taller. Go ahead.”
“Okay! See you later, Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
I sent Kharon away first. It seemed the branch manager likewise wanted fewer people around to listen in. “Audrian, you did a good job. You may go downstairs as well.”
“Yes sir.”

Soon after, the employee who guided me here and gave me ice water headed out, and the two of us were the only ones left in the branch manager’s office. No one said a word, and silence naturally ensued. But I didn’t rush and waited for him to speak first.
“Actually, I was thinking of calling you here sometime soon, even if it wasn’t today.”
“Your reason?”
“Lord Urbans’ daughter wishes to meet with you.”
I shot him a questioning look. “Urbans? Who’s that?”
“Are you serious?” the branch manager replied, dumbfounded. “You really don’t remember the person you held hostage?”
Ah, the daughter of the district chief. Well, fuck, you should’ve just said that from the start.
“...I guess you haven’t completely forgotten.”
“Ahem, anyway, so why is she trying to meet with me?”
“Well, you’ll know once you meet—”
Who did he think he was baiting? “Then I refuse.”
“What?”
“I’m busy being hungry every day, so what time do I have to waste?”
When I stood up as if to say this conversation was over, the branch manager urgently spoke up. “I can’t say much, but it won’t cause you any harm. Rather, it would be helpful for you.”
Well, seeing as he was going this far, I didn’t think he would offer up any more information.
The woman I held hostage wants to see me, huh?
It wasn’t even worth considering. “Tell her no!”
I’m busy enough as it is. I refuse to get involved in something troublesome.
In the middle of a bright city street, Erwen was running through the crowd.
Huff, huff, huff.
Sweat had already soaked not only her body, which she had washed clean just a while ago, but also the skirt she had taken out for the first time in a while.
Uh... it won’t smell, right?
It should be fine. They’d seen each other in worse states. For now, seeing him again was more important.
...He really is alive!

While she was extremely happy about that fact, she also felt a sense of shame. Bjorn, son of Yandel—her first-ever teammate, and the barbarian who saved her when she had been wandering alone in the labyrinth. The person she had thought dead and who had disappeared before she could repay the favor he’d done her. She felt like an idiot for being so misguided and locking herself in her room.
To think he became so famous...
She didn’t even have to ask around. She just asked a few people after returning to the city, and most of them knew his name. One of them even knew the location of the inn he was staying at.
Oh, wait... Then why didn’t Daria say anything?
The question suddenly popped into her head but Erwen didn’t dig into it.
I’m sure she misheard the rumors.
There was no way her sister would intentionally hide this from her. And that wasn’t even important right now.
Ugh, what should I say when I see him? Now that I’m thinking about it, I just disappeared.

Her heart pounded nonstop. It was the first pleasant vibration she’d felt from it in a long time. Until now, she had been living with the curtains closed because she didn’t want to see the sun rise and set, but today, the sunlight that touched her skin was warm and cozy.
Let’s apologize first. He must’ve been looking for me too. He probably couldn’t remember where our lodgings were.
Arriving at her destination, Erwen prepared for the upcoming reunion and got her thoughts in order one last time. After smoothing out her rumpled clothes, she knocked on the door.
Knock, knock.
Step, step.
She heard someone walking around inside. They were quickly approaching.
Thump, thump!
It felt like her heart was going to explode. She wanted to hurry up and talk to Mister like they used to, like when they would tell each other about what was going on in their lives and laugh.
Will he be surprised to know I’ve commanded all four Great Spirits? Uh, wait... now that he’s much stronger than me, I guess I can’t brag about that.
She was a little worried, but she was sure he would praise her, tell her that she did well and must’ve had a hard time. Unlike other people, Mister definitely would.
“Hehe...” Just when she was smiling at that particular fantasy, the door finally opened.
Rattle.
But what was this?
“Huh? Who are you?”

The person who opened the door was a single beastwoman, someone from the cat tribe with triangular ears on her head. Erwen checked the number on the door: 201. She was at the right place. She couldn’t have misheard, either, since she had asked her informant to repeat the address several times just to confirm. Could it be that they had been wrong?

Hmm, it seemed so. Still, it could be the room next door, so she should ask. Since he was so famous now, someone from the same inn might know. “Um... do you know Mis—no, what room Bjorn Yandel is staying in?”
“Hmm? Are you here to visit Bjorrrn?”
“Pardon? I’m not sure what you mean...”
“Bjorn just left after washing up. Do you want to wait inside?”
He just washed up and left? No, wait a minute... does that mean that this is his room?
Erwen was confused. What was going on?
“Or tell me who you are. When Bjorn comes back laterrr, I’ll tell him you dropped by.”
It was almost like they lived together. Erwen numbly raised her head to look at the beastwoman’s face again. She was pretty, to the extent that even she as an elf couldn’t deny it.
Drip.
Water dripped from her red hair, as if she just took a bath.
“You said he just left, right?”
“Yeah, what about it?”
Erwen’s lips contorted when the woman replied in a way that seemed to ask what was wrong with that. Of course, it didn’t last long. “No. Nothing. Can I come inside and wait?”
“Oh, sure...?” Soon, she entered the room. Loot was scattered on the floor. “It’s a bit messy... It’s not usually like this...”
“I know. What this is. I’ve done it with him before too.”
“Hmm? You have? Oh... are you an adventurerrr too?”
“Yes.”
“B-But don’t misunderstand, this is all from a plunderer—”

“Don’t worry. I won’t.” Erwen interrupted the beastwoman’s words and focused on the thrum in her heart. Then she spoke with a smile. “Someone who steals something that belongs to someone else deserves to be punished, no?”
Her hot, pounding heart was cold all of a sudden.

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Dark Clouds (4)
paragraphs: In an office with a heavy, woody scent, Niall Urbans, the seventh district chief of the Adventurers’ Guild, chuckled. He had just remembered something his daughter had said a while back.
“I have no intention of living the rest of my life as my father’s doll.”

When the jailbreak incident first happened, he had noticed the rebellious moves his daughter was making. That was because she had had no reason to be speaking to the branch manager on her own. He couldn’t help but investigate this in earnest, and when he did, he found out that his daughter was secretly establishing a position within the guild.
“There’s fulfillment in living a woman’s life, you know,” he’d said.
For a one-time act of rebellion, it was quite a decent one. Even though it was a headache for him, he was a bit pleased by the realization that she really was his daughter.
“I told you, you should be careful about where you so much as breathe.”
Even ambitions like this could be interpreted as cute because she was his child.
The branch manager... so that man has chosen my daughter, after all.

Bjorn Yandel was a barbarian he’d intended to get back at one day, but he had undergone meteoric growth in a short period of time. The branch manager had tried to contact that man today. Niall still didn’t know what his daughter intended to do with the barbarian, but it was clear that the branch manager had taken his daughter’s side. That fact made him very irritated.
He dared to rebel against me.

It wasn’t like he couldn’t understand why the branch manager had made that choice. He was already out of Niall’s favor, and Niall had someone in mind to take over the branch manager position once he was gone. Since the manager knew that, too, he must have tried to at least cling onto a rotten rope. However, understanding and forgiveness were two completely different things.
I’ll have to use this opportunity to deal with both of them for good this time.

Niall sipped his tea with a gleam in his eye. He had originally intended to leave the barbarian alone. He still shuddered at the humiliation he’d experienced back then, but in just a few months the barbarian had established his own position. There was no reason to make another enemy, after all. But now things had changed. There must have been a reason why his smart daughter had been trying to contact that barbarian.
...Besides, it strangely keeps bothering me.
Niall made a decision. If something bothered him, all he had to do was get rid of it before it turned into a bigger problem later.
Rummmble!
How long had it been since I’d left the Adventurers’ Guild? As I was returning to my inn, thunder rumbled in the distance and rain began to pour.
Goddamn it.

Dark clouds were covering the once-clear sky all of a sudden. I debated just walking in it, but figuring it could just be a passing storm, I entered a nearby restaurant. It was time to eat anyway, so I decided to watch the rain while I did.
“Here is the meal you ordered.”

Grilled meat, pumpkin stew, and rye bread warmed up my insides, but it somehow seemed to be lacking. It wasn’t like this was a cheap restaurant that cost three hundred stones per meal like the ones I frequented in the past, either.
...Missha is definitely better at cooking meat.

I ordered another rum and contemplated buying some meat tomorrow and asking her to grill it. Now that I was here, I decided to pass the time until the rain quieted down. It wasn’t like Missha would be there if I headed back now anyway.
Oh, maybe she is still there because of the rain?

As I drank alone with the sound of rain as company, my thoughts wandered. It seemed like not too long ago that I was eating stone bread while watching out for goblin traps, but it had already been half a year.
Pizza and beer... they wouldn’t sell that here, right?

The thought of wanting to go home had faded a lot. I had just gotten used to everything—the creaky bed, the small single room with one bathroom, and the daily routine of laughing and chatting with my comrades while drinking cheap beer.
I’ve changed a lot too.

I could spend all day listing the shitty things about this world. But if you asked me if I hadn’t had any good times here... That wasn’t the case. At first, survival had been my goal. But as a gamer, I derived joy from gradually getting stronger. Chatting and laughing with my party wasn’t so bad, either. It felt a little strange.
If I hadn’t been brought here, I’d probably still be playing games alone in the corner of my room.

The twenty-nine-year-old office worker Hansu Lee had had a very small social circle. Of course, there were no complaints or issues there. I had been steadily preparing for my retirement, and had been able to live alone without relying on others, unlike in this world, where you were forced to find teammates.
Considering the fact that I’m thinking this way... I must’ve grown attached to them.
I took a sip of the rum, which had an unnecessarily sweet aftertaste. But when I thought about Hikurod, Rotmiller, and Dwalkie, my taste buds grew bitter.
If I want to go to the upper floors, I’ll have no choice but to form a new party.

Starting from the fifth floor on, our current members wouldn’t be strong enough. I could see the ways their growth was limited. First of all, Dwalkie was not from the Magic Tower, and had a pressing problem—namely, his low mana.
He can learn new magic now, but it’s safe to say he can’t use any rank-six spells.

Not to mention Rotmiller. On the lower floors all he had to do was navigate, but on the higher floors, scouts needed a high level of combat ability as well. That was because the maximum number of people in a party was five.
Unless he awakens as a guide... Otherwise, the fourth floor will be his limit.
Of course, unlike those two, Hikurod would be able to play an active role on the upper floors as long as his equipment was well-suited for it. But there was no need to have two tanks on a team.
...Once Missha’s specs go up a bit, I’ll have to form a new team.

To be honest, it was something I had been thinking about for a while, but I finally made up my mind. The battle we’d had with the Troll had had a big effect on me. I wanted to keep going upstairs, and I couldn’t achieve that goal with these guys. That may seem harsh, but it was also a decision I was making for their sake. The upper floors were teeming with monsters worse than Trolls. It would be better not to expect dumb luck to save us again.
“Yandel?”
Uh, what the heck? When I turned around at the sound of someone calling my name, there was someone standing there that I hadn’t expected at all: Mr. Bear.
“Urakburak?”
“...It’s Urikfried. If that’s difficult for you to pronounce, you can just call me Abman.”
“Then I’ll go with that.”

Mr. Bear sat across from me without asking for permission, as befit his macho-looking appearance. As this was something I also did often, I didn’t feel particularly offended. “I didn’t expect you to stop by here as a customer.”
“Customer?”
“Oh, I didn’t mention. This place is run by my wife.”

He was the owner, huh? This was new information, but it wasn’t all that surprising. A rank-five adventurer would have enough money to open a shop. If I was going to be surprised, it was going to be about something else.
“You have a wife, yet you enter the labyrinth alone?”
“The restaurant is in the red these days. I figure I should at least earn some money.”
Well, then I had no follow-up questions. This wasn’t something I needed to worry about. “Anyway, it’s a strange coincidence that you’re the owner of the place I came to to escape from the rain.”
“It’s not enough to call it a coincidence. Thanks to that, I’m now certain, Bjorn Yandel.”
“About what?”
“Will you let me join your party?” Mr. Bear replied as if this wasn’t a huge deal.

Huh? What was this? Accept him as a teammate? All of a sudden? It was an unexpected request, but after listening to him, I was convinced. From Mr. Bear’s point of view, I had proven myself as an adventurer.
“If you can save a total stranger in that situation, you won’t stab me in the back.”

Although I’d asked for five million stones, apparently saving him by using one of the most advanced potions on the market inside a Rift that was blocked off from the outside world had left a good impression.
...This is an interesting turn of events.
Tank support, summons, and strong long-distance physical damage. It was clear that Mr. Bear would be able to do his part without any trouble even on the fifth floor or higher.

However, I firmly declined his offer. “You must have misunderstood something. I went in separately this time, but I have a set party.” Dwalkie would be part of the party for a while, so I couldn’t just kick someone out to include this man.
Surprisingly, Mr. Bear nodded agreeably. “If you say so. What we talked about today can be discussed again later when there is an empty spot, or if you leave the party.”
“Empty spot?”

“You should know what I mean.” With a final significant look from Mr. Bear, the teammate issue was officially tabled. After that, we had a brief conversation about when he should pay back the five million stones. “Since I put some unused equipment up for sale on the exchange, I should be able to give you the money on the agreed-upon date.”
The sight of the shop’s empty interior was weighing on my heart, but we agreed to meet here again in ten days to exchange five million stones for his collateral. “Then I’ll see you then.”
“Wear this. It will fit you.” It didn’t look like the rain was going to stop even if I waited longer, so I borrowed a raincoat from Mr. Bear and headed to the inn.
Swaaaaaa!
Rain fell down in heavy, typhoon-like sheets. After running through the strangely deserted streets, I immediately arrived at the inn. But what was this?
“Ah, you’re here, Bjorrrn? You have a visitor.”
“Waaah! Mister—!”
Not unlike pouring rain on a sunny day, something unexpected was waiting for me.
Since that incident ten years ago, she had lived in moderation in many ways. She had been confident in her self-discipline—at least, until today.
“Someone who steals something that belongs to someone else deserves to be punished, no?” Erwen froze at the thought that unwittingly escaped her mouth.
“Hmm? You... are tougherrr than you look, huh?” Fortunately, the other party didn’t seem to have noticed the true meaning behind what she just said.
What did I just...?
Strictly speaking, ‘it’ wasn’t even stolen. Bjorn wasn’t an object. Also, she was the one who had made the choice to leave Mister’s side and be with her sister. But what was that feeling just now?
Crunch.
Strangely, hostility welled up inside her. Could she beat this woman in a fight? She found herself subconsciously considering this and analyzing her opponent accordingly.
“Come to think of it, we don’t even know each otherrr’s names. I’m Missha Karlstein.”
“...Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.”
“Wow, even your name is prrretty... Erwen, nice to meet you.”

“Right...” Hiding her reluctance, Erwen accepted the handshake. Then they sat and talked. She had no desire to get close to this woman, but she had a question to ask. “Miss Karlstein, are you seeing anyone, by any chance?”
“S-Seeing someone? Don’t be rrridiculous. Bjorn and I are just teammates, teammates!”

“Hmm, is that so?” For some reason, it felt like her anger was fading away, although it was strange that Bjorn’s name was being mentioned when she had only asked if Missha was seeing someone. There seemed to be more to investigate. “I’m sorry. You said you washed up together earlier, so I misunderstood.”
“W-Washed up togetherrr? What are you saying?! I was just borrowing his bathroom.”
“Borrowing a man’s bathroom? Your inn must be quite far...”
“Uh, it’s not that far...”
“...It’s not?” At those words, Erwen’s eyebrows furrowed. Bjorn may not have realized it, but it was clear this woman had shady intentions, enough that she’d use such a vulgar technique.
“Ahem! So how do you and Bjorn know each otherrr?” Was she trying to divert attention away from herself? This time Missha asked a question of her own.
Erwen answered honestly. “Mister and I were teammates.”
“Hmm? Mister? Bjorn is only twenty years old...”
“Ah, that’s just a nickname between us, so don’t worry about it.”
“Nickname...?”
“Is there a problem?”
When she tilted her head casually, the beastwoman smiled awkwardly. “No. What prrroblem? Of course not. Nyaha!” Her mouth was smiling but her tail was flicking unhappily on the bedspread.

Erwen felt a strange sense of victory at the sight—until an unexpected counterattack followed. “Mister and I have a special relationship. He was my first teammate and we also had our first return drink—”
“Hehe, but was it only special to you?”
“...Pardon?”
“I’ve been with Bjorrrn for months, and I’ve never heard anything about you. Nyaha!”
The beastwoman smiled brightly and thrust a dagger into her heart. Erwen couldn’t hide her bewilderment at her sudden change in attitude. However, instinctively, she realized one thing.

“Did you say your name is Erwen? You seem cute enough. But... didn’t you consider that being this blatantly hostile to another perrrson and treating them like an idiot would piss them off?” The hostility Erwen had felt upon meeting this woman was totally justified. “Um, but thanks for one thing. Thanks to you, I don’t think I’ll be confused anymorrre.”
“C-Confused about what?”
“I don’t know. Don’t you already know what I mean?”
This woman was her enemy, someone trying to take away something precious to her.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Dark Clouds (5)
paragraphs: I stood frozen for a moment, staring straight ahead. Inside the room I had believed would be empty after Missha’s departure were two people: Missha and Erwen.
There’s no way the two of them know each other. Did Erwen come to visit me and run into her by chance?
As soon as I entered the room, out of habit, I analyzed potential causes and effects of the current situation. However, that was all I had time to do.
Kablam!
Unlike the air outside, humid from the pouring rain, for some reason the air in my small single room seemed cool. The room was full of questions.
What the...? Why is this one so upset?

Having now spent months at each other’s sides, I could tell just by looking at her face. Missha was very, very angry right now, even more so than the time she caught me picking out only the meat and throwing away the carrots from my food. Seeing as even the fur on her tail was slightly fluffed up, she seemed to be wary of something too. Erwen was also acting strange.
Is she... crying?

There were tears in her eyes. She wasn’t shedding them or anything—in fact, it looked like she was trying hard to hold them back. Rather than crying out of sadness, she looked more like she was grinding her teeth in anger.
Did they fight or something?

Based on the information presented to me, I came to the conclusion that Erwen and Missha had fought. The reason? Well, I wasn’t sure about that. I didn’t think either of them was the type to be so emotional or confrontational with someone they had just met.
Rattle.
When I closed the door, their eyes flew to me. Maybe it was because of the sound of the rain and thunder, but it seemed like it was only after I closed the door that they noticed my presence.
It was Missha who spoke first, smiling and greeting me as usual. “Ah, you’re here, Bjorrrn? You have a visitor.” For some reason, though, her eyes weren’t smiling at all.

“Waaah! Mister—!” The tears Erwen had been holding back poured out as she jumped at me. I dodged her reflexively. I guess this wasn’t the reunion she had imagined, because she landed with the balance of an agility character and bit her lip. “Is it... because of that woman?”
What was this kid talking about? For some reason she seemed very different from the last time I saw her, but... Well, it had been a long time since then.
“Because of that woman...?”
“I-It’s nothing!”
When I asked a question of my own, wondering if the two had really fought, Erwen flinched and shook her head. Then she self-consciously glanced in what happened to be Missha’s direction.
“Bjorn, what took you so long?” Missha met my eyes and approached me with quick steps. “You left in a rrrush earlier, did something happen?” Her voice was strangely nasally.

It made goosebumps appear on my body for some reason, but for now I just answered the question. “It was nothing. Kharon got accused of being a plunderer, but everything worked out after I spoke with them.”
“Ohh, I see. That must’ve worn you out.” Missha said something weird and stroked my arm. Normally, she would’ve just patted me on my forearm or back.
At this point, I had no choice but to be blunt. “...What’s wrong with you?”
“What do you mean? I’m just prrraising you for doing a good job. Barbarians aren’t strangers to us, after all.”
I involuntarily cocked my head. That hadn’t even been my question in the first place, and the answer itself was full of contradictions. “Not strangers?”
“Yeah. Aren’t barrrbarians and beastpeople on good terms?”
Were they? Well, I guess on better terms than they were with elves.
“Here’s a towel!” I was about to say something else when Missha jumped up and put a towel on my head. “Dry your hair firrrst. You’ll catch a cold.”
“Ah, oh... yeah.” This still seemed a little suspicious, but I shifted my gaze to Erwen as I dried my hair. I couldn’t leave my guest unattended. “Erwen, did you come looking for me?”
“Pardon? Ah, yes...” When I turned to her, Erwen’s shoulders hunched and she avoided my eyes. Wasn’t she the one who ran toward me earlier? Oh, was it because I avoided it?
“Anyway, good thing you’re here,” I said. “I’ve been wanting to visit you for a while—”
“Pardon? You were looking for me?”
“Really? I’m happy. I-I thought you might have forgotten about me...”
I smile at the way the mood had changed with just a few words. “I could never forget the comrade from my first quest.”
“R-Right? That’s special to both of us, right?”
Huh? Feeling strangely like we were talking about two different things, I still nodded, won over by the earnest look in Erwen’s eyes. “...I guess so?”
“Yes! It was like that after all!” I didn’t know what just happened, but Erwen suddenly brightened at my answer.
That was enough small talk, so I decided to ask what I was curious about. “Anyway, it’s been a while. So, how have you been?”
“Me? You’re curious about how I’ve been?”
“Then I will tell you!”

A second later, Erwen began rattling off all the things that had happened since our parting, much like a chirping bird. Most of them were stories related to the labyrinth. She had climbed the floors with her sister, defeated monsters, and absorbed new essences. Oh, and did she just say she usually spent her days locked alone in her room practicing day and night?
“Look at this! I can handle all four Great Spirits now! Three of them I’ve even mastered!”
“What? Three already?”
“Yes! I worked really, really hard!”
To be honest, I was a bit surprised. Even if she had been piggybacking off of her sister, it was hard to believe this was the result of a few months of work.
Is this what people mean when they say ‘talent’?
She was different from me in many ways. I became stronger by using high-level essences and equipment, whereas she developed her abilities with real practice.
An elven archer who’s succeeded in reaching enlightenment in three attributes in under one year...
This was definitely rare. If you managed to master all four major attributes, you were able to unlock something in the latter half of the game.
Welp, if it wasn’t for her sister, I could’ve added her to my party.
It was a pity to lose a talent like that. However, I chose not to say anything. It wasn’t like I was forming a party right now, anyway, and there was no way she’d abandon her family.
“Anyway, I’m glad you were busy with training. I thought you couldn’t find me because I moved inns. Well, it was time for you to focus on your own growth rather than me, anyway.”
“Ah, that’s not completely true...”

“Yes, Bjorn is rrright. If you don’t have a year of experience as an adventurer yet, you should focus on finding ways to stand on your own two feet, right?” Missha, who had been silently listening to the conversation, stood up and wrapped her arms around Erwen’s shoulders.
Erwen stiffened and nodded weakly. “Right...”

Was it just my imagination, or was she self-conscious about Missha’s comments? Recalling the atmosphere when I first entered the room, I belatedly asked, “Ah, so what happened to you two while I was away?”
Actually, that was something I had been curious about from the jump. However, at my question, Missha tilted her head casually as if I had just asked something weird. “Hmm? Nothing happened.”
“Nothing happened? I thought you two were fighting—”
“Haha! Why would we be fighting? We’ve gotten so close. Right, Errrwen?”
“Yes, Miss Karlstein...”
“Miss Karlstein? Just call me Sis.”
“Yes, Sis...”

She was like a bully dragging an innocent classmate into an alleyway. Something was clearly up here, but as long as they kept their mouths shut, it seemed it’d be tough for me to get the answers I wanted.
I’ll learn what happened in due time.

I passed the two of them by and opened the window. The dark clouds had already cleared and sunshine glistened on the wet pavement. Therefore, I issued an order for them both to leave. “The rain has stopped. You two should head home now. I want to wash up and get some rest.”
For some reason, fatigue was settling in.
After leaving Mister’s room, Erwen found herself in a complicated situation.
“Huh? Are you going this way too?”
“Yes, why?”
“Then you go firrrst. I’ll leave a little after you.”
She was heading in the same direction as the beastwoman. Fortunately, the woman didn’t seem to want to walk with her, either.
“Then you go first. I’ll go after.”
“No. You go firrrst.”

This was a massive headache. Leaving after? How could she believe those words? It seemed that as soon as she left, this woman would return to his room. By the looks of her, it was clear that Missha had the same suspicions.
“Hah...” Erwen and Missha sighed at the same time.
“Then shall we leave together?”
“Yeah, that would be betterrr.”

On the way back, there was only awkward silence. No one spoke, and they just focused on walking. That was to be expected. Although they had told Bjorn nothing had happened, that wasn’t really the case.
“I don’t know. Don’t you already know what I mean?”

When she heard those words, Erwen had felt like a screw in her head was coming loose. Her heart had been pounding like crazy, and she couldn’t stand it any longer. So, without realizing it, the words came flooding out of her.
“You naughty cat...!” For the first time in her life, she insulted someone, and that wasn’t all. When she came to her senses, her hand was touching the dagger at her waist. That was when Erwen knew.
“You, arrre you sick in the head?”

If it weren’t for that one comment, she would have come to her senses only after swinging the dagger. The beastwoman was strong. This wasn’t just an assumption, but the truth. Elves were naturally perceptive when it came to these things and could sense the spiritual power of others.
She’s twice... no, maybe even three times as strong as me.

There was a big difference in their spiritual power, meaning this woman had absorbed several high-level essences. She could also tell from her posture and energy that Missha was not simply an adventurer who relied on the abilities of her essences in a fight. The moment she realized this, dizziness overcame Erwen.

Missha Karlstein... This woman was her enemy, but she could not defeat her in a fight. That was to say that something precious would be taken away from her, just like back then. Yes, it would be taken from her. Feelings utterly divorced from reason raged through her. The momentary flash of memory paralyzed Erwen’s mind. As she drowned in emotion, her mouth moved on its own.
“Please don’t take it from me... Please...” Miserable begging, something she would never partake in if she were in her right mind, flowed out of her.
“What...?” The beastwoman, who had been glaring at her with cold eyes, gaped at her, dumbfounded.

Erwen knew in her head how ugly and grotesque she must have looked, but in that moment, she had thought that if it would protect something precious to her, she could do even worse. She might really have broken down in tears and begged on her knees if he hadn’t arrived just in time.
Rattle.
“Waaaa! Mister...!”

She shook her head in an attempt to shake off her thoughts. It was an embarrassing incident that she didn’t even want to think about. For some reason, it was difficult for her to think rationally where Mister was involved.
...I probably seemed like a weirdo.
Blushing with shame, Erwen glanced at Missha. She was now standing at a fork in the road.
“I’m over there, where arrre you heading?”
“Thankfully... I’m the other way.”
“Mm, I see...”
The time had come to put an end to their awkward silence, but both of them stopped to look at each other, unable to move their feet.
The first to speak was Missha. “You... you’rrre not stopping by tomorrow too, are you?”
“Yes, I am.”
“Ha... how did I ever...” Missha gripped her forehead like she couldn’t believe she was in this situation.
The same went for Erwen. When she had been running over to the inn, all she could think about was seeing Mister again and laughing.
“Anyway, I’m leaving. You head home too. Got it?” said Missha.
“Huh?”
Erwen grabbed Missha just as she was heading to the other fork in the road. She had something to say, although she really didn’t want to say it. “...Thank you.”
“For what...?”
“You didn’t tell Mister about what happened earlier.”
“That you tried to fight me with your dagger?”
“Right...” Erwen dropped her head.
Missha let out a big sigh. “Forget it. Let’s make a prrromise.”
“Promise?”

“You’re going to come by even if I tell you not to, rrright? So let’s keep what happened between us a secret from Bjorn. Well... you prrrobably feel the same way, but... I-I don’t want him to have to worry about something like that.”
“...All right.”
“Then I’m leaving. You have to go home, too, okay?”
“Okay.”
With that, Erwen parted ways with Missha and headed to her dorm. It was quite a distance, but it didn’t feel all that long, perhaps because her mind was so preoccupied.
When she opened the door, Daria greeted her with an expression of concern. “Erwen.”
“Daria...” Erwen collapsed into her sister’s arms.
“That person... did you find him?”
“Yeah. He was really alive.”
“R-Really...? That’s great.”
She luxuriated in her sister’s arms for a long time, soaking up the comfort. Then she made a decision. “Daria, I’m going to get stronger.”
“Stronger...?”
“Yeah. Is that weird?”
“No, I actually thought you wouldn’t want to train anymore.”

At her sister’s insinuation, Erwen tilted her head. Why would she stop training? Well, when she found out Mister was alive, all the time she spent training in her room admittedly felt pointless, but now, Erwen felt a roaring desire that was even stronger than before. “I have someone I have to defeat, so please help me out even more in the future.”
If she didn’t want something to be stolen from her, she would have to be the one doing the stealing.

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Old Hand (1)
paragraphs: The next day, Missha woke me early in the morning. “Wake up, wake up! How long are you going to sleep for!?”
The time was 6:30 a.m. Even considering our plan to go to Kommelby, it was quite early.
“Let’s eat out today. I couldn’t pack lunch because I woke up earrrly.”
“Then let’s head down to the first floor and—”
“Here’s no good! Let’s go out to eat, huh?”
“I’m hungry, though...”
“Come on, I’ll buy you something delicious. Okay?”

I wasn’t even able to eat breakfast thanks to Missha’s prodding and ended up getting dragged out. Then, like we were being chased by something, we got on a carriage. Only after we had arrived at the business district of Kommelby did we eat at a restaurant located thirty minutes from the public carriage platform, which Missha explained was famous.
“How is it, does it taste good?”
“It’s delicious!” I didn’t know what they did to the stew, but it had a very familiar, savory taste. I was determined to remember this place and come back whenever I was nearby.
“I’m glad you look satisfied. Did you like it that much?”
“Except for how much a single plate costs.”
“That’s because you ate four plates, you barrrbarian!”
After a late breakfast, we stopped by the armor store and general store we frequented and disposed of all of our loot.
Three million stones, huh?

That was the amount we netted after selling all the equipment and consumables of the trio that we had encountered on the second floor plus Jencia. It wasn’t a small amount, but it didn’t feel all that big, either. The amount would have been many times bigger if we’d sold the Serpent’s Fang and second-grade leather armor too.
Well, those are things we can sell later.

After that, I hired a blacksmith that Hikurod had told me about to repair my equipment. I was worried about the cost of the repairs because my shield and breastplate got dented a lot in the battle against the Troll.
“All in all, three hundred thousand stones.”
However, the repairs were cheaper than I expected. Well, it was probably easier to repair dented gear than melted gear.
“Do you handle leatherrr as well?”
“Yes, do you have anything to repair?”
“Ah, this one is tight around the chest...” While we were there, Missha also entrusted him with her new armor.

Since it was leather, I wondered if alterations would be an issue, but it turned out to be no big deal. “I don’t even need to add new material. I think I can just use a softener on the tight parts to slightly loosen them.”

The cost of those particular repairs was only around fifty thousand stones. Maybe it was because I came here with a recommendation from Hikurod, but there were no attempts to screw us over. It seemed like a very conscientious business.
“Come back in three days.”

After leaving the smithy, we wandered around and bought supplies for our next expedition. I replenished our supply of Witch’s Lamp solution, which was a consumable that could counter Stealth abilities, and bought a few more items that came to mind.
“I’ll give you two bottles together for two million stones.”

I bought two more bottles of the advanced potion from the general store I visited before. I hadn’t known I’d use an entire bottle so quickly. It was a considerable expense, but it was a little better because the two of us were paying for it together.
“Fortunately, we didn’t have to touch the money in the shared account. Here are 325,000 stones.” I shared the remaining money with Missha. With that, we finished everything on the schedule for today.
“Then I’ll be heading home now! Good night, Bjorrrn!”
“Good night.”
We returned to Ravigion at night and parted after a simple meal.
What’s this?
When I returned home, I found a silver-haired elf crouched in front of my door with her head down. “Erwen?”
“Oh, you’re here?” Erwen greeted me with a smile as soon as she saw me. Her eyes looked tired for some reason, so I couldn’t help but ask the question on the tip of my tongue.
“...How long have you been waiting for me?”
“Not long. Did the two of you go out?”
“Ah, we had business in Kommelby.”
“Oh... I see.”
“So, what are you doing here?”

It was time to wash up and go to bed, so I asked what she was there for, but Erwen just kept her mouth shut. It seemed she was mulling something over because she had a somewhat serious look on her face. But when she spoke again, it was in her usual cheerful tone. “Mister, I can’t come by as often as I used to. I came to tell you that.”
“Hmm? Ah... well, things have changed since then.”
She wasn’t a month-old fledgling adventurer anymore—although she hadn’t even reached a full year yet, either. But that was all the more reason for her to focus on her growth right now.
“Yes, I decided to start special training with my sister tomorrow. So maybe once a week? I don’t think I can come by more often than that. I wish I could, but... if I did, it’d take a long time...”
“Long time?”
“...It’s nothing.” Erwen didn’t give a proper answer and before I could ask, she smiled brightly and disappeared. “Anyway! I’ll be back next week, so see you then, Mister!”
“Oh, right...”
What was this uneasy feeling?
The next day at lunchtime, the whole team gathered at a bar. Having a drink to celebrate our return, we took time to distribute the loot from our previous expedition.
“I think we can divide it into 550,000 stones per person. The Frogman Sorcerer’s remains sold at a much higher price than I thought.”
“Haha, isn’t it all thanks to Rotmiller’s dissection?”
“Ahem, since I’m not very helpful in battle, I should at least be able to do this much.”

After Rotmiller’s humble statement, I balanced our earnings from this quest. We had obtained 400,000 mana stones from the Rift and the first and second floors, then 320,000 stones from selling the equipment (after subtracting the cost of the potion, of course), and 550,000 stones from completing the commission and selling the remains. The grand total was 1.27 million stones.
Even though I spent that much, I still earned a lot.

Whatever the reason, on the fourth floor, I had earned a lot more than I had in the past two months. No, actually, considering the essence Missha consumed, the leather armor, and the Serpent’s Fang, it was safe to say that we had made a crazy profit. I also had five million stones I still needed to receive from Mr. Bear.
With this momentum, I’ll be able to get to the sixth stage of the Immortality Imprint soon.

I grinned and drank my beer. There were still two million stones left in the shared account with Missha, and the personal wealth I had accumulated so far was about 2.5 million. I had been a bit uneasy about my plateaued growth over the past two months, but looking at my bank account made my heart full.
“Bjorn! Don’t drink the first return drink on your own!” chided Hikurod.
“Hmm?”
“Let’s all drink together! We haven’t even celebrated properly yet, have we?”
“...Sure, do whatever you want.”
“Here’s to defeating that Troll bastard and the entire team returning alive! Now! Drink up, everyone!”

After we were done settling our accounts, everyone drank the return drink and let go of any regrets we were holding onto from the previous expedition. Maybe it was because we had all overcome another crisis together, but the leader of our party, Hikurod, seemed very happy. However, the drinking party ended rather quickly compared to the last time.
“Um... I have to go now. I have to stop by my parents’ today.”
First Missha left, then Rotmiller.
“I’m also finished for the night. I have business at the guild.”

Because they had things scheduled for afterward, the two just sipped their drinks to join in and left. Rotmiller wasn’t a talker anyway, but after Missha left, the rowdy drinking party quieted down. I figured the dwarf would get upset if I left, too, so I tried to stay and keep the celebration going.

Surprisingly, though, Hikurod slipped out and moved over to the next table. “Hahaha, I’m telling you! That Troll bastard was no big deal... A-A lie? Of course not. See that barbarian over there? That’s Little Balkan, I don’t know if you’ve heard of him...” Hikurod ditched his teammates to clink glasses with adventurers he had never met.
I was about to leave too when Dwalkie grabbed me. “Hey, how about we talk?”
“What?”
“W-Well, come to think of it, we’ve never had a quiet conversation just the two of us.”
That was true. I spoke with Rotmiller a lot whenever everyone passed out drinking, but Dwalkie had always been one of the ones sleeping.
Does he have something to say to me?
I sat back down and clinked glasses with Dwalkie, but that was it. Dwalkie sipped his drink hesitantly, but didn’t speak up first.
Fuck, I should’ve just left.
Despite our noisy surroundings, an awkward air settled on my shoulders. I eventually just opened my mouth first because there was something I was curious about. “How are you feeling?”
“Ah, fine... To be honest, I was in a bit of pain after I got treated by the priest, but now I am completely healed.”

“That’s good—then how about this?” I asked, tapping my forehead. Dwalkie tilted his head. “That must have been the first time that your body ever got folded in half like that. Do you think you can continue in the labyrinth?”
Adventurers with broken wills were more common than you’d think. Sometimes the cruel things that happened to the body scarred the mind in the form of intense memories.

“Ah, well...” Picking up on what I was really asking, Dwalkie hesitated to answer. It seemed things weren’t where he wanted them to be. “Hah... to be honest with you, I haven’t been able to sleep properly since that day. I thought it was just because I was inside the labyrinth, but it’s the same in the city.” Dwalkie let out a long, drunken sigh and confessed that his hands shook at the thought of entering the labyrinth again. “But, don’t worry. Isn’t this something everyone goes through and ends up overcoming? I will be fine before the next quest.”
Could he overcome it? From the look in his eyes, his words seemed genuine. But I had one question. “Is there a reason to push yourself that far?”

Most people overcame their trauma to continue working as adventurers because they had no other options. In a city where they had to pay taxes to survive, they had no choice but to work through it. But Dwalkie, a wizard, was different.
“You could get enough work in the city. Why do you want to continue working as an adventurer?”
Dwalkie hesitated, then answered only after taking a swig of beer. “That’s... because it’s fun.”
That wasn’t the answer I was expecting at all. “Fun?”
“Obviously, it was for a different reason at first. Do you remember what I said when we first met?”
“I remember. You said you would become a great adventurer and bring glory to the baron.”
“I was actually lying. I just thought that if I became a famous adventurer, my father... no, the late baron would show interest in me.”

Dwalkie was the illegitimate son of an aristocratic family. Like all illegitimate children, he felt both a deep love and contempt for his blood relatives, a contradictory combination of hating them but wanting to be loved by them.

“As you know, the baron is dead. And as you saw... my brother, who inherited his position, wasn’t even aware of my existence.” He had been frustrated at first. He said it felt like he had been lost at sea, like he’d lost his life’s goal in one fell swoop. Poeticizing his feelings at the time, Dwalkie stared straight into my eyes. “But I was able to overcome it because there were four people around me to lean on.”
“A-Are you... talking about us?”
“Who else is there? At first, I didn’t know that was what a comrade was. It felt like something beyond friends that you could trust and rely on... Like a family.”
“I-I see?”

“Yeah. After my mother passed away, I always felt like I was alone in the world... But I never feel that way when I’m exploring and laughing and chatting with you guys.” Maybe he also realized this was embarrassing, because Dwalkie ordered another beer and emptied it immediately. “Thank you, Bjorn. Thanks to you guys, I’m enjoying every day. Therefore... even though I went through something like that... I’ve been able to overcome it.”
“...I see.”
“That’s right. So don’t worry too much.”
“Okay, I won’t bother with that anymore.” Soon, I wiped my worries away. Whatever the reason, at this rate, it seemed I wouldn’t have to worry about Dwalkie’s mental health.
“Huhu, when you look a little closer, you have a big heart even if you don’t seem to.”
“Shush, let’s just drink.”

Perhaps thanks to our heartfelt conversation, the rather awkward vibe between us disappeared. Dwalkie, who had been hesitant in my presence, grew lively and started talking about whatever came to mind, and I listened and chimed in.
“Hey, Bjorn... I have a question for you.”
“Speak.”
“Are you and Miss Karlstein... dating?”
Instead of answering, I stared at Dwalkie. His face, flushed with alcohol, was full of nerves and tension. It was then that I realized something.
No wonder he asked to speak alone. So this was his objective.
“Brown Rotmiller. Thirty-four years old, and you’ve been an adventurer for eight years.”
As soon as he entered the office, he was met with a look of contempt. Disconcerted, Rotmiller replied, “...That’s right.”

He was more curious than confused, to be honest. He had received a summons from the Adventurers’ Guild this morning, so he arrived at the guild on time even after catching up with his teammates. When he followed the employee, he ended up in this room. A man was sitting in a chair, and he had a face Rotmiller recognized.
Niall Urbans, the seventh district chief of the Adventurers’ Guild. Why did this man call for me?

Questions filled his throat, but instead of doing anything impulsive, he waited for the man to continue explaining. You never knew what kind of misfortune you might be met with if you made a mistake in a situation like this.
“Hmm, I like you. Especially that you’re waiting for me to explain instead of trying to sate your curiosity.”
“Then can you tell me your business with me now?”
At his request, the district chief nodded with a pleased smile and explained his reason for calling him here. The more Rotmiller listened, the more ridiculous the explanation grew.
“You mean you want me to betray my teammate?”
“That’s up to you. To be precise, I just need that barbarian’s manners fixed.”
Rotmiller gritted his teeth. This man was one of this city’s thirteen district chiefs, and just annoying one could put an adventurer at a huge disadvantage. Which was why this took so much courage.
“That offer... I’m going to pretend I didn’t hear it.” With clenched fists, he spat out a refusal.
The district chief smiled, intrigued by this.
“If we’re done talking, I’ll take my leave.” Rotmiller hurriedly turned toward the door before fear could overtake him.

“It’s nice to treasure your comrade. What a wonderful value that is. But...how long do you think you’ll be comrades?” Rotmiller stopped mid-step at those words. “I saw your records. How terribly unfair. It took you eight years to make it to rank seven. On the other hand, didn’t a certain barbarian become rank six in half a year?”
“Feelings like that... I have never felt them.”
“If you say so. But isn’t it time you accept reality? Your comrades will keep moving up. They’re not ordinary humans like you.”

Rotmiller pursed his lips at the hard-hitting words. However, he couldn’t argue with them. And it wasn’t because he was afraid of the man’s power, either; he just knew very well that what he was saying was true.
“How much longer do you think you’re going to travel with them? Three months? Four months? Well, maybe even longer, if they pity you.”
Rotmiller didn’t listen any longer and opened the door.
“I trust you will make the wise decision.” The district chief, who he could see through the crack in the closing door, had a friendly smile on his lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 123: Old Hand (2)
paragraphs: “Missha and I are simply comrades.”
“I-Is that so? Ah, of course...”
Of course, what?
I took a sip of my drink, ignoring Dwalkie’s look, which seemed to imply he had expected that answer. Then he banged his head on the table.
Smack!
Well, I had been wondering how this kid who couldn’t take alcohol was chugging all those drinks.
Goddamn it.

Anyway, with this, our midday drinking party ended completely after less than a few hours. It was still broad daylight when I left the bar, leaving the blacked-out Dwalkie to his best friend, Hikurod.
I guess I should just go to the library.
I canceled my plans to go home and rest, and changed my destination. There was a lot I still didn’t know about this world.
It’s almost the same, yet subtly different.

Just look at the Troll we ran into this time. Even when we poked its eye and blinded it, it sensed Dwalkie’s mana and charged at him. There hadn’t been anything like that in the game. But you never knew, there could be something like that written in the books of this world. I couldn’t be satisfied with in-game knowledge—it was necessary to continue studying.
Auril Gavis. I have to keep learning more about that name, anyway.
Somehow, I seemed to read a lot more books here than I did when I was back in civilization.

“You are back.” When I arrived at the library, Ragna greeted me with a sleepy look. Perhaps it was because it had been several months since we’d finally introduced ourselves to each other, but we were on much friendlier terms than before, to the point that she even struck up conversations with me first now. “I get that you were resting two days ago, but why didn’t you come yesterday?”
“I had other things to do.”
“I know you’re busy with your work as an adventurer, but you shouldn’t neglect your studies.”
This girl had a very strange side to her, too, for her to tell a barbarian not to neglect his studies. “All right. Then I’ll leave it to you.”
“...Bierdo Parsytiev.”

After briefly saying hello, I received the Special Book Recognition spell as usual and entered the building. This time, I mainly looked at content related to monsters. Originally, that was a field that I hadn’t looked into because I had knowledge from the game, but things had changed.
“I’m hungry, so I’m going to go. Goodbye.”
“Um...” Ragna began.
“Hm?”
“I also haven’t... never mind. Don’t mind me.”
It was late when I left the library. But... what was this?
“Hello, Mr. Yandel.”

When I returned to my lodgings feeling like I’d had a productive day, someone was waiting in front of my door—a woman who was dressed in black from head to toe like she was headed to a funeral. The way she held herself exuded a sense of elegance. So, her name must have been...
“Are you... Urbans?”
“...Julian. Julian Urbans.”
“Right.”

“...Mr. Peta mentioned it, but I didn’t expect you to actually forget me,” she muttered, curling her brown hair around her index finger. It may simply have been a habit, but it could have been that she was subconsciously showing her nerves.
Her expression doesn’t give anything away, but could it be that she’s nervous?
With that thought in mind, I asked, “So, who is Peta?”
At my question, her eyes went wide in disbelief. “...You don’t know the name of the branch manager, either?”

“Ah.” So that was the name of that mustached man. But how was I supposed to know? He’d never told me his name before. I couldn’t say I wasn’t a little embarrassed, but I refused to show it as I got straight to the point. “So, what are you doing here? And alone too.”
“Since you wouldn’t meet with me, I had no choice but to come to you.”
“I’m very sure I turned down the offer.”
“Can’t you consider that I’m desperate?”

Desperate, huh? If the daughter of the district chief was saying that, it was clear there was something going on, probably something that was hard for her to discuss with others. Otherwise, there was no reason for her to be willingly visiting her hostage-taker. But I was a barbarian who didn’t care about any of that.
“Go home. I refuse to get involved in something troublesome.” I stamped out my curiosity and entered the room.
Just as I was about to close the door, the young Lady Urbans quickly shoved her parasol in the doorway.
Tap!
But that of course wasn’t going to work.
Bang!
The door firmly shut, destroying the parasol in the process with just a bit of force.
“Huh?” Not expecting this turn of events, Urbans urgently knocked. “W-Wait! Let’s talk for a moment. It won’t take long—”
“Stop it and leave.”
“No, really! Aren’t you curious? About why I’m going this far?”
“I’m not curious.”
“Eeek!”
Did my stubborn attitude work? When her parasol broke, the young lady gave the door an angry kick before disappearing with a click of her heels. Only then did I breathe a sigh of relief.
Looks like that’s over—
Click, clack.
Just then, the sound of the retreating heels grew louder again as she came back. Could it be that she still hadn’t given up?
Knock, knock, knock.
As soon as I heard the knock, I made a snoring sound.
Honnnk!
With nothing she could reply to, I determined that this would make her give up.

“Ha... how did I ever...” I heard her lamenting through the door, but apparently, she decided to switch up her strategy. “I know you’re not sleeping, so just listen,” Urbans whispered from the other side. “Brown Rotmiller. Beware of him. I don’t know the details, but I met with my father today and—ah! Don’t open the door so suddenly!”
This was worth a listen.

A man and woman in a room in the middle of the night. The air between us was full of awkward tension. That was a given. I’d even opened the door for her, but it turned out there was nothing to hear out.
“Is that it?”

Rotmiller had apparently been called to the district chief’s office and then came out within five minutes. That was all the information that Miss Urbans was able to give me. If I had known this was going to happen, I wouldn’t have opened the door.
“So, what do you want?” Now that this had happened, I decided to sate my curiosity. I was even more curious now. Why was this daughter so against her father that she would tell me this?
The young Lady Urbans’ expression grew solemn. “My ultimate goal is my father’s downfall.”
“It can’t be helped. If things continue on like this, I’ll truly end up living like a doll. Anyway, for this, your cooperation is essential—”
“Leave.”
“Pardon? No, you seem to have misunderstood something, but if you help me, you will benefit greatly—”
What benefit? There was nothing to be gained by opposing the district chief.
“Kyaaa!”
I could already see how tenacious this woman was from our brief interaction, so I sent her outside. Then I closed the door and locked it. Did my persistence slowly wear her down?
“If... If you change your mind, please come see me. Oh, and be careful. My father would have played a trick on that Rotmiller man.”
After those words, Miss Urbans left without any more of a fuss. So, I washed myself off and went to bed.
Rotmiller... I’ll have to keep an eye on him for now.

After that, the days continued on as usual. I ate meat that Missha grilled every morning and spent time in the library at lunchtime. When Erwen came by once a week, just as she promised, the three of us shared a meal together. Oh, we also had our usual meeting to plan our next expedition.

“Last time a Troll showed up on the fourth floor, but from what I’ve heard, it seems we’re the only ones with such bad luck. It doesn’t seem like there’s anything wrong with the floor itself, so I think it’s okay to go there as planned. What do you guys think?”

I watched Rotmiller throughout the meeting, but I couldn’t find anything unusual about him. If I had to pick something, he was quieter than usual. This muddled my thoughts even further. If there was something to discuss after his meeting with the district chief, I was hoping that he would tell me at our meeting.
Should I just straight-up ask him?
There was also the option of taking the bull by the horns, but I put that on hold for now. There was still time left before the labyrinth opened, so it was better to take a more cautious approach.
Anyway, time passed. Three days later, I received five million stones from Mr. Bear.
“With this, I’ve paid off all my debts. Give me back the item.”
“...Can’t you just give me this instead?”
I asked if he could just give me the bracelet, but Mr. Bear shook his head resolutely.

Geez, it’s not like it’s a one-time use, either. This item is most effective when equipped by a character with high regeneration. During the period where you’re immune to damage, your blood replenishes. I’ll have to coax him into selling it to me at a cheap price when we become a party later on.
With that thought in mind, I opened my eyes and checked my watch. It was just ten seconds until midnight on the fifteenth. I closed my eyes again.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn to a specific world.]
It was time to partake in a special event.
I was inside Hansu Lee’s bedroom, not Bjorn Yandel’s inn room. Although it wasn’t my first time here, I took a moment to lay on the bed thinking about how cool this was.
As expected, the softness is different.

At that moment, I could clearly feel the gap between our civilizations. It wasn’t even a particularly expensive mattress. Well, even in this world, I was sure a high-class inn was probably on another level too.
Press.

When I turned on the computer from the bed with my toe, the monitor lit up right away without needing to boot up. I got up and sat down in front of it. Since this place could only be accessed once a month, and with a time limit, I had to use my time here efficiently.
Click, click.
First, I entered the Exchange. Most of the messages were the same as the last time, but new posts were appearing in real-time. Considering the way this place worked, that made sense.
Let’s wait a little longer and check again...
I opened the list of chat rooms. When I first came here, I didn’t have enough time to peruse this feature at my leisure, but that wasn’t the case this time.
[Wizardry]
[Beastpeople come in]
[Elf of Night]

Looking closely, I could see that unlike the [Newbie Room], which had about ten people, many were gathered in different occupational and ethnic communities. It would be easier to get useful information from places like that, things like strategies for leveling up.
But... why aren’t there any barbarians?

As I kept scrolling down, I froze. Except for dragon people, who you couldn’t select on the character screen anyway, everyone had a dedicated chat room except for barbarians. Actually, there was one, but there was no one inside.
[Behelahhh! - 0 people are online.]

Looking closely, the last time it was accessed was several months ago, and a red line was drawn over the person’s nickname. That meant they had either been kicked from the server or were dead in the real world. Why were barbarians the only ones like this? When I thought about it, there was a compelling reason. Two, actually.

First, barbarians weren’t very popular as main characters. Even I had usually chosen beastmen or elves before I finally perfected my shield barbarian build. Either that or I chose a human with good potential in the second half. Second, barbarians had to enter the labyrinth with a weapon as soon as the game began. Otherwise, they would starve. There was an extremely difficult coming-of-age ceremony, along with the hardcore provision that in order to progress, you had to enter the labyrinth as soon as you woke up.
There are already a few people who choose barbarians, but even those people would have all died in the beginning.
For some reason, that brought on some secondhand embarrassment. So I looked for a job community instead.
[Noblesse - 21 people are online.]
[Treasure Hunter - 34 people are online.]
[Sword Master - 17 people are online.]
Healer, archer, swordmaster, etcetera—each community had more than ten users online.
[Shielder - 3 people are online.]

Meanwhile, there were only three tanks. Zero in my race community and three in my job... what path had I been walking? The thought made me a bit miserable, so I looked for a national community this time. Fortunately, there was a chat room.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 1 person is online.]
Only one person, but who was I to be picky? This was an overseas game that didn’t even have a Korean translation in the first place. I honestly thought I wouldn’t even find someone else here.
A Korean, huh?
I double-clicked the mouse without hesitation.
Surprisingly, the moment I opened my eyes, I saw a room that looked like an aristocratic mansion. I had thought it would be a basic skin like a clearing or a field.
“You’re hereee!”
Before I could look around, the player who was online—a man with short hair in his early twenties—greeted me with a loud shout.
[Sergeant Lee]
When I processed the nickname, I froze. “Sergeant Lee... are you...?”
“Bro... you get me. It happened the day I was discharged.”
What kind of shitty luck was that!?

chapters.title: Chapter 124: Old Hand (3)
paragraphs: First, I briefly introduced myself, not as Bjorn Yandel, but as Hansu Lee. “I’m Hansu Lee. I’m twenty-nine.”
“You have the same last name as me. I’m Baekho Lee. I was twenty-three.”
“Was?”
“To be honest... I’ve been here for more than ten years.”
“Oh, I see...” I had nothing to say to that. I had suspected that from the chat room’s luxurious interior, but ten years? Poor guy. “Wait a minute, then you’re older than me—”
“Big bro! We don’t say things like that! I’m going back, so we should be counting our real ages!”

“Uh... if you say so.” As a member of a Confucian nation where age was everything, there was no reason to stop him from wanting to be the younger one. Anyway, with that, the introductions were officially sorted out.
“Anyway, bro, I’m sorry, but will you excuse me if I do something?”
“Excuse you?”
“It’s... a kind of simple test. I’m certain you are, but... still, I think I should still confirm it.”
“What exactly are you confirming?”
“When I say a word, just tell me the first thing that comes to your mind. Oh, don’t worry. This is something a Korean can’t fail at.”

Based on that explanation, it sounded like some kind of Korean test. Apparently, he was kind of a big shot in this world, and it seemed some guys pretended to be Korean to freeload off of him because of that. In that case, then, well...
“Then, let’s begin?”
“Sure.”

When I nodded, the guy took a deep breath and squeezed his eyes shut. I didn’t think this was a big deal, but the way he was acting was starting to make me nervous too. Of course, as he said, the quiz itself was easy.
“Kimchi?”
“...Stew?”
“Beef head?”
“Beef soup.”
“Saudi?”
“Arabia.”
“Military Code of Conduct.”
“...Our resolution. By the way, I was a social service agent.”
“Ah... anyway, this is the last one.” Baekho paused to take a breath and gave me a grave look. Just as I was beginning to think all of that earlier was a joke, he opened his mouth. “Wan-yong Lee?”
“Son of a—hey, you asshole.”

The moment the curse was about to unwittingly leave my mouth, my body stiffened as I sensed a strange energy. At some point while I was talking, Baekho had fixed me with a cold look that made me wonder if his earlier personality was just an act.
“I believe you. You’re Korean.”

What the hell was this bastard talking about? Baekho Lee, a player from Korea who had been brought here on the day he was discharged from the military and had lived in this world for over ten years... He seemed like a good kid, but...
Is something wrong with this guy’s head too?
My eyes narrowed. However, after listening to the excuses that followed, I could see where he was coming from.
“Ah, sorry for being rude. That was a line I prepared for when someone passed the test. I didn’t think it was going to take more than three years, though.”

He must’ve been lonely. Even I, though thinking myself far removed from these kinds of feelings, missed conversations like this. Besides, when this guy first got here, there wouldn’t have been a community like Ghost Busters, so he was left alone in an environment that would have been perfect for ruining someone’s personality.
“So, what’s your name?”
“I told you earlier.”
“Not that, the name you use here. I have to know that to help you. Koreans are as good as dead without loyalty and community, am I right?”
I smiled and shook my head. “I’m grateful, but it’s okay.”

Baekho looked at me as if he couldn’t understand. “Why won’t you tell me? If you just tell me your name, you won’t have to worry about taxes anymore.” The boy’s voice was full of confidence that could only come from someone who had already reached a certain level of standing here.
However, my answer was still the same. “If I gave you the same offer, would you tell me your name?”
“Uh, well, even if it’s you, that’s...”
“I am the same.”
Had he finally realized that I was different from the average newbie? “What mode did you beat the game on?” Baekho asked, his expression much more interested than before.
“And you?”

“It was Times Ten.” I heard that the founder of Ghost Busters did it at Times Fifteen. When I looked at him in surprise, he scratched the back of his head. “And Times Ten is nothing, either. It’s still a cheat, anyway. That’s why even though ten years have passed, there are still plenty of things I don’t know. If I knew things were going to turn out like this, I would’ve just played the original.”
Maybe it was because he’d survived in this world for over ten years, but his mindset was definitely different from those I’d met in the Newbie Room.
“So, what about you?”
I thought it over for a while before answering. “I also beat it at Times Ten.”
“Oh, really?” I was a bit worried he’d think I was lying, but Baekho humbly believed my claim. “Yeah, anything else wouldn’t be considered Korean.”
“Huh?”
“Koreans are the best when it comes to gaming, right?”
That seemed like a little too much Korean pride for me but I didn’t comment on it. After all, I felt bad for him. The least I could do was embrace him wholeheartedly. “Yes, you are completely right.”

“Right? Ha, it’s really very sad. If only there were a Korean patch, there would have been at least a few people who beat the original version...” Apparently, spending time exclusively with foreigners had intensified Baekho’s patriotic pride. “Ah... then, do you want some GP instead?”
