“That would be nice, but I won’t cash it out. And there are a ton of ways to earn it.”
“Welp. Your GP will probably pile up like mine.”

Excluding our personalities, Baekho and I were similar in many ways. He didn’t hastily reveal his identity, and despite how ditzy he acted, his actions seemed carefully thought out. That was probably how he’d survived for so long.
“Um... so there’s nothing I can do for you?”
“It’s okay, I didn’t come in here expecting anything from you in the first place. Let’s just meet up and chat once in a while.”

“Bro...!” I guess my words made him feel like he was talking to a real countryman. Baekho wiped away non-existent tears, but only for a moment. “If you have any questions, just ask. I should at least do that much to save some face.”
Boy, were his emotional ups and downs intense. It was tough to follow his energy. Since he was offering, though, I asked, “Do you know who the game master is here?”
“Ah, I don’t know that. In fact, I only found the pill after robbing the Ministry of Security’s headquarters in the early days.”
“Then they won’t know who you are, either?”
“They probably have an idea. I also have a guy I’ve been suspicious of...”
“Who?”

“There are three. Should I tell you all of them?” Baekho called out the names of his suspects one by one. All of them were wizards, and except for one, they were so famous that even I had heard of them. “I’m sure you don’t need me to tell you this, but don’t ever expose your identity here. From what I can tell, there are a few bastards acquainted with the royal family too.”

Baekho seemed to like me quite a bit since he offered me advice without me asking. Unlike my newbie friends, who said this place was 100 percent safe, I really liked his pessimistic point of view. To that end, I had one more question. “Is there any way the founder can find out my identity?”
“No. That would probably be hard. In the first place, they didn’t make this space with their own efforts—it was more like a remodel.”
“Remodel?”
“There were evil spirits in this city even more than a hundred years ago. On Earth, that was more than twenty years ago. So who were those people?”
Honestly, I hadn’t even thought about that. Twenty years ago, Dungeon and Stone, not to mention LCD monitors, weren’t even really in circulation. “I don’t know, so just tell me.”
“The answer is that they were from another dimension!”
“Another dimension...?”
“Yeah. I’ve never actually met them, but as far as I know, they claim they were brought here by reading books written about this world.”

Apparently, there had only been a handful of evil spirits at the time, and rumor had it that all of them had unique powers. It was assumed that one of them created this space and that the person currently operating it had inherited it by chance.
I think I just heard some groundbreaking information.
At this point, I was getting curious about Baekho’s identity too. What kind of person was he that he knew all of this?
Well, this works out in my favor, though.
I shifted my mindset and continued to ask Baekho whatever questions came to mind to clear things up, but the guy wasn’t all-knowing, either.
“Ah... to be honest, I’m currently in hiding, so I’m a bit behind on current events.”
“You’re in hiding?”

“Yes. I can’t tell you the details, but if you want more recent information, I can introduce you to a chat room. It’s called Watcher of the Round Table. It’s a kind of club for people with eighth-grader syndrome.” The chat room Baekho told me about was a kind of community for experts, run in secret and only accessible via invitation. “Your nickname and face will be anonymous there, so you don’t have to worry. I’ve heard that if you don’t have any information to share you could get beaten up and kicked out, but... since you beat the game at Times Ten, I don’t think you’ll have to worry about that.”
Like someone about to send his child off on a field trip, he explained every step of the process. The explanation was quite long, but all of it was useful, so I listened without interruption.
“Then I’ll see you later,” he said.
“Are you leaving already?”
“Oh, I didn’t tell you. The pill I took was a prototype, so I can only stay here for an hour.”

What was this generational gap? At this point, even if he started complaining about things “back in his day” out of the blue, I’d probably just keep my mouth shut and listen. It was clear he’d lived a tougher life than me.
“Buddy, you have to come back again, okay?”
“Okay, see you next time.”
“And if anyone in the city messes with you, don’t forget to let me know.”
“All right...”
“Oh, and also—”
“It’s fine, just go. You can just tell me the rest next time.”
“Ah, right... next time... Okay! See you next time!”

Soon, the guy stopped looking at me with such an anxious expression and left with a simple smile. I exited the chat room too. Just as he instructed, I typed the code he gave me into the chat board’s search bar and entered [Watcher of the Round Table].
[You cannot enter at this time. OPEN 03:00-03:10]

Baekho didn’t tell me about this. I had no choice but to spend my time browsing through Exchange posts and other bulletin boards. When the clock on the bottom right of the monitor pointed to three, I tried to enter the room again.
[New member status has been verified. Congratulations on becoming a member of the Watchers of the Round Table. This gathering is strictly anonymous...]
Messages containing the exact contents Baekho had told me about popped up, and when I opened my eyes, I was in the customization room.
Flash!

The room was full of all sorts of costumes and accessories. I wondered why I had to go this far to hide Hansu Lee’s identity, but since these were the rules, it was probably better to just follow them. After perusing my options, I chose some relatively tolerable pieces, treating it like cosplay. I wore a slim-fit navy blue suit.
A mask is required, so I have to wear one.
The selection of masks was vast enough to fill an entire wall, but there were many empty spots, which suggested you couldn’t pick one someone else had already picked.
Creaaak.

As soon as I put on one of the masks, which was in the shape of a lion’s head, the door in the room opened by itself. A long red carpet guided the way. As I slowly walked forward, exploring my surroundings, a large round table appeared. There were dozens of seats, but only four people were there.
Tap.
They were talking familiarly with each other, but when I arrived, they all fell silent and stared at me. An oppressive silence ensued.
He wasn’t kidding about this being a community for pros. Oh, those eyes are fierce. Don’t you know that newbies should be cherished and cared for?
“Oh? I’ve never seen that mask before,” someone in a yellow clown mask commented.
“You,” said a woman wearing a fox mask, her voice high-pitched. “How did you get here? It’s been over a year since we’ve gotten any new members.”
Oh, I didn’t know that bit of context.
“Tell us. Who are you and who recommended you?”
However, this was a question I had prepared for, so no problem.
“You must only tell the truth. That’s how this place operates.”

Just as she claimed, a special skin was active in this space. If you lied, your mask would break and you would be immediately banished from the chat room. However, there was one exception to this. Before the gathering began in earnest, it was okay to lie as much as you liked.
But seeing as everyone’s keeping their mouths shut about that, they must all be in on this together. Or they’re just curious about what kind of person I am.

I could see why Baekho had told me to come out swinging in the first meeting. It must have been advice borne of experience. I didn’t particularly feel like it, but this time I decided to just follow the lines and directions that he gave me.
“Oh, m-me?”
“Yes, you—”
After acting like a noob for a bit, land a counterpunch when they least expect it. “Your mom sent me here.”
That was right, I’d already heard it all from Sergeant Lee.

chapters.title: Chapter 125: Old Hand (4)
paragraphs: Humans were often said to be social animals. I didn’t know who first said that, but it was a very appropriate analogy. Maybe they weren’t as primitive as animals, but the way they judged people through their first impressions of them was pretty much the same. In order to be respected, you needed to not be looked down upon, especially if you were a transfer student who had joined the class midway through the year.
“You... What... did you just say?” the fox mask asked, almost like she thought she’d heard me wrong.

On the other hand, the other masked members were just watching the situation unfold in interest. It was a kind of hazing ceremony. The actions I took here would determine the first impression I gave off.
“Run your mouth again.”
Therefore, facing the fox mask head on as she stared at me furiously, I drove my point home to make sure that there were no misunderstandings. “The person who recommended me was your mom—”
“What kind of asshole is this guy?!”
Weirdo, ridiculous bastard, moron, etcetera. It didn’t matter what they said about me—this was better than letting them perceive me as weak. However, I didn’t exactly expect this.
“Hey, you.” The moment the blue eyes beyond the cracks in the fox mask began to radiate light, my skin tingled with the clear threat.
This feels weird.

As I not metaphorically, but literally felt my life being threatened, my heart began to pound and goosebumps cropped up on my skin. In a world where physical forms did not exist, how was this possible? Fortunately, I had information about this phenomenon.
This is that skill.

This was the first time I’d ever been directly affected by it, but it must have been the technique Baekho taught me about earlier. It was said that it could only be used in Ghost Busters, a spiritual world that was operated by a clear mind and force of will. It was not particularly useful, and was a minor skill only ever used by old hands to scare off newbies.
“Can you say that again?” the fox mask asked, the murderous aura around her growing even denser. I thought I could sense a cold contempt through the mask.
“U-U-Uhh...” I stuttered.
Smirk.
I could hear laughter. It wasn’t from the fox mask, but someone else. It must have seemed funny to them—some newbie kid daring to mess with them and promptly tucking his tail between his legs.

“Why, can’t do it? You said it just fine earlier.” I guess she was genuinely angry. In a way that implied she had no intention of letting this pass, the fox mask’s murderous intent intensified. Of course, that wasn’t an issue.
“N-No... I j-just...”
“Say it. All of it.”
“Yeah, sure.” I decided to stop acting like an idiot at this point. “The person who recommended me was your mother. Is there a problem?”
“...W-What?” The fox mask looked very puzzled by my sudden change in attitude. “No, you were just acting? But how...?”
Instead of answering, I raised my pinky finger and picked at my ear, which had been itchy since earlier.
Apparently, everyone else had now noticed what was going on.
“This is definitely an interesting turn of events.”
“Rookie, enough joking around. It’s getting to be too much.”
“Impressive, but such an attitude is bound to make enemies, Lion.”
I licked my lips at each opinionated comment on my acting. Even though I’d had a hand in shaping my own image, I could hear their evaluations of me in each one: funny guy, cocky guy, pathetic guy.
Yeah, no surprises there.
Well, if you thought about it, it made sense. Wasn’t this a club for pros? Being able to take some murderous intent without flinching wouldn’t do much in the way of getting me special treatment.

“You dare mock me?” The fox mask had a belated, violent, reaction to realizing that I had just been acting like an asshole. Even so, as things stood, my first impression would just be that of an annoying guy. Therefore, I closed my eyes tightly and recalled the conversation I’d had with Baekho.
“You want me to use some murderous intent on you? No way. If something goes wrong, it’ll mess up your head. Since this ability is based on intention, the stronger the mind, the stronger the force...”
The power of murderous intent was proportional to the user’s mental strength. For reference, mental strength here meant real mental strength, not some numerical value.
“That’s why it’s only for veterans. Killing a lot of people and overcoming death on the daily is bound to increase your mental fortitude. Well, there are people who are just born with it too.”
Then what about me? I guess I just had to experiment with it. Baekho hadn’t had time for me to try it out with him, but it didn’t seem too hard.

“I’ll tell you how to use it for now. Well, it’s not really a method, but...” Baekho explained that in order to exude murderous intent, you needed to put yourself in a certain frame of mind first. “Think of the target as an enemy. An enemy that you have to kill and defeat.”
Coincidentally, self-hypnosis was one of my specialties.
“Hey, I’m talking... to you...” When I opened my eyes, the fox mask met my gaze and froze, then snorted dismissively. “Ha, what, is that your attempt at revenge?”
It had worked, but it seemed I hadn’t put enough juice into it. I delved deeper into my thoughts.
“How childish.”
These are goblins. Bastards trying to kill me. Yes, enemies threatening my life.
“Just apologize. I was trying to feel you out, too, so if you apologize properly, I won’t have any hard feelings about this.”
I fell into a trance, imagining running forward right now and bashing her head in with a mace. And at that moment...
Uh?
A sensation filled me, one that felt almost like something was coming out of my head. It was a bizarre feeling, but not a painful one.
“Are you too proud to apo—”

The woman in the fox mask, who had been scolding me, suddenly stopped talking and went as still as stone. She didn’t even move, almost as if she had been seized by some invisible force. The emotions in her wide eyes were also familiar to me: my enemies wore the same expression at the end of their lives, their eyes just like hers as they watched the mace slam down on them.
Oh, I didn’t expect it to be this effective.
Feeling suspicious, I glanced around to confirm. The other three, who were clearly skeptical of the fox mask’s reaction, visibly jolted every time my eyes met theirs.
Slide.
The deer mask, who was leaning on the pillar, moved his hand to his waist where his sword would have been. He was the one who had thought of me as cocky.
Whip.
The crescent moon mask covered their eyes as if to avoid my gaze. They were the ones who had seen me as pathetic.
“...Woah, I didn’t say anything.” The yellow clown mask waved his hands in an exaggerated manner and took a step back. He was the one who had just considered me a funny guy.
What is happening?
Rather than being pleased by the sight of their violent reactions, my questions only grew. Why was this so effective? I had no time to reason through it, though.
Bzzzzzz.

Suddenly, a sharp pain erupted in the back of my head. It felt like my brain was being squeezed like a wet towel. Sudden exhaustion swept over me, and I felt like I had been up for three days and nights in a row. I instinctively realized I could only maintain Barbarian Murderous Intent Mode for a few more seconds.
Fuck, he never mentioned this.

I hurriedly returned my attention to the fox mask. She was shaking. When I kept staring at her without saying anything, she pleaded with me, clearly struggling to force out the words. “Stop, please. Any more and I’ll be at risk...”
Just then, Murderous Intent Mode ended.
Gasp...!
Fox Mask took a deep breath like someone who had just been underwater. The way she winced as soon as our eyes met made me confident.
I don’t know what that was, but thanks to it, this all worked out.
This was the self-image I had wanted to cultivate since learning that this was a hostile environment for newbies. I had officially succeeded in becoming a madman who shouldn’t be messed with.
“...Making such a fuss about being questioned just once. This won’t be smooth sailing going forward.” With that muttered comment from the deer, the silence in the hall disappeared.
“Hehe, I think it was still an interesting experience.” The clown glanced at me with a strange look in his eyes. “I wonder how many more kills I need before I can do something like that?”
Rattle!
Just then, the four doors leading to the room closed all at once. Honestly, I was fucking startled, but I was glad it didn’t show. It seemed that the window for entering the room had closed.
“It’s already that time.”
“It’s just the four—no, five of us this time.”

Since everyone was seated, I took a seat too. However, before the gathering started in earnest, questions flew at me from all directions. But unlike before, they weren’t interrogating me about my identity.

“Lion, this will be your first gathering,” Crescent Moon addressed me by my mask. “I was wondering if you’d been a member from the early days based on your murderous aura, but... that lion mask has always been on the wall.”

At his words, I nodded. There was nothing more pointless than denying something that had clear evidence backing it up. Openly acknowledging that he was right would make me look better. “So, what is it that you’re getting at?”
“...Have you met the Master? Oh, if you don’t want to answer, just say so.”

I guess my madman image was quite effective, because Crescent Moon’s tone was both polite and cautious. Was this why some people lived like hooligans? This was a realization that I would have lived my whole life without having if I hadn’t become a barbarian.
“If you want something in return, we will give it to you. Although it may be difficult to find something you’ll be satisfied with.”
“Never mind that,” I answered arrogantly. “Why do you think I’ve met the Master?” I didn’t even know who the Master was.
“That’s... a strange question. Isn’t it only natural that we’d assume that? You’re the first recruit since the Master disappeared.”
“Which is why Fox took on the role of detective and got hit with a rebound,” the clown muttered to himself. The fox mask turned away in shame.
I think “The Master” is referring to the founder of this chat room.

As I strung the given information together and crammed it into my head, Crescent Moon spoke up again. “Ahem, not only that, but I also thought so because it seemed like you knew a lot about this place for your first time.”
Well, that’s not because of the Master, but because of Baekho Lee. But, wait, who the hell is he?
I decided to look more into his identity in the future, tabling those thoughts for later.
“So, can we get an answer to the question? Just tell us when you last saw the Master and that’ll be enough—”
“I refuse to answer,” I declared.
“Ha... I see. All right.” Crescent Moon let go of any lingering disappointment and backed off. If I had looked like a rookie, they probably would have interrogated me further.

“Anyway, putting that aside, why don’t we begin?” Unlike the other three, the clown did not seem very interested in the Master’s actions. He wrapped up the conversation and announced the start of the meeting.
It was a good thing I had learned the rules in advance. It was clear that if I’d had to ask how this worked here and now, my mysterious reputation would have been destroyed.
“Then I’ll start.” The first to speak was the clown. “The king of Rafdonia’s illness is getting worse.”

A red light radiated from the jewel embedded in the center of the round table. That meant that what he said was true, but half of the people at the round table already knew it. He wouldn’t be allowed to stop until he offered up higher-quality information.
“Getting worse? That’s too vague.”
“Everyone knows that the king’s illness is grave. Please tell us something more useful.”
The fox and the crescent moon frowned and criticized the clown. I just kept quiet.
I didn’t know that... The king is sick?
This was my first time hearing of it. Rumors like that never circulated in the city. Well, it would be strange if people discussed the king’s health out on the streets.
“You don’t know how significant this is? How pathetic.” The clown glanced at the fox and the crescent moon, then at me. I’m sure you know what that means, his eyes seemed to say.
I just kept quiet again. That should carry me at least halfway.

“The captain of the Order of the Rose passed away yesterday. How about that? Will you accept that?” The clown promptly released another piece of information, and a heavy silence fell over the round table.
“...Blood will be shed in the palace.”
“Yes, we should prepare too.”
Wait, who the fuck was the captain of the Rose Knights? Anyway, the jewel turned green, so it was the next person’s turn.
This time, it was the fox mask. “The Jagun Clan has succeeded in defeating the Lord of the First Floor.”
“Oh, so that guy pulled it off after all.”
“Ha. I saw the post disappeared from the Exchange. I guess they learned the strategy from someone? I thought they would never defeat it.”
I stayed silent this time, too, not because I didn’t know anything but because they were talking about me.
So the guys who beat it are from the Jagun Clan.
All I had been able to learn in the city was that the Lord of the Floor had been summoned, but that was it.
It’s a good thing I came here.
The jewel lit up green again, so it was Crescent Moon’s turn next.
“Haha, I’m certain that none of you know about this.”
“Can you just tell us already?”
“When a secret trigger is activated on the Island of Tranquil Fairies, up to three Ravganus are confirmed to appear.”
The fox and deer were extremely surprised by that information.
“That’s good news for anyone seeking the essence of a Ravganus.”
“No, wait. What is the secret trigger?”

“Don’t you think you’re asking for too much information at once? Anyway, the next person can go... hmm?” Crescent Moon, who was about to pass the baton, stiffened. This was because of the red light emanating from the jewel.
Unlike earlier, when anonymity had been maintained, it was easy to infer who already knew this information because the fox and deer had clearly demonstrated that they didn’t.
The clown offered up words of consolation. “Crescent, don’t be too discouraged. Most wouldn’t know the information you just shared.”
Crescent let out a sigh. “Until now you were the only one we needed to be in the dark about something, but now there’s someone else...”
I shrugged my shoulders.
Then don’t choose to reveal information anyone could learn just by playing the game.
“This is a dilemma. I haven’t prepared anything else,” said Crescent.
“You can just tell us about the secret trigger, then.”
“That... still needs to be kept secret.”
“Ohhh, then we have no choice but to banish you after this meeting—”

“Haha, nonsense. I just meant that this was a dilemma because it means I’ll have to reveal the ace up my sleeve.” Soon, Crescent Moon sighed and whipped out new information. “They say they’ve found evidence of a ‘holy relic extortionist’ among the elves.”
A green light glowed from the jewel, but the fox narrowed her eyes and objected. “Evidence? Isn’t that too vague?”
“This is information about the relic thief, which previously had no leads. This alone is top-secret enough.”
“Hmm, fine. I’ll accept it.”
“So you really are an elf, huh, Crescent?”
Crescent Moon’s turn ended when the fox withdrew her objections, and everyone’s eyes turned to me. Although Deer was also left, as we were moving clockwise, we inevitably reached my turn.
I don’t know why I’m nervous.

Was it because of the expectant look in their eyes? Even though I had already decided what information to use while the others were speaking, the pressure suddenly increased for no reason. If this was information all of them knew, that’d be embarrassing.
I’ll just have to discard the obvious first.

Wanting to maintain as much of an air of mystery as possible, I selected some information that would be difficult for others to already know. “If you take down a Vamdemon in a team of three people, an essence will most definitely drop.”
As expected, the jewel in the center of the round table emitted a green light.
However, one of them asked, “Take down a Vamdemon with a team of three?”
Why are you surprised by that part? Wouldn’t it be no big deal in cheat mode, even with three people? It’s even an easy monster...
I didn’t get it.

chapters.title: Chapter 126: Old Hand (5)
paragraphs: The monster Vamdemon was a rare species that was difficult to encounter due to its multiple spawning conditions, although it belonged to the lower end of the rank-three monsters’ spectrum. So, I chose to share this information first. Even cheat-mode players wouldn’t have much experience defeating Vamdemons, much less doing so as a team of three.
Above all, this is useless information.

In fact, that was the most decisive factor. Vamdemons were hard to come by and even harder to kill with three people. After all, this world wasn’t modded with a cheat mode where you could consume up to thirty essences. To put it simply, this should just have been, Oh, really? That’s interesting, kind of information.

“Is that true?! A-Ah! I’m not doubting you. Really. You know that, right?” The woman in the fox mask jumped in to challenge me, then rushed to explain herself. Everyone else’s reactions were also a bit strange.
“...Take down a Vamdemon with a group of three?”
“But a Vamdemon is a rank-three monster. How is that possible?”
They were reacting as if they’d never heard something so ridiculous.
“Anyway, let’s move on,” I replied like this was no big deal. I did so to divert attention away from me, but thanks to my mysterious vibe, no one noticed.
Fortunately, the green light came on.

After that, the deer mask offered up his information and received the okay, and the round ended. According to the notice I saw when I entered, at this point, the participants would consult with each other to decide whether or not to take one more lap around.
“I’ll stop here today.”
When Crescent Moon, who had not prepared much, declared that they were going to forfeit after the first round, it seemed that the rally would end there.
“Hmm, then I’ll stop here too,” said Fox. “I’ll save what I was going to use today for the next meeting.”
“If Fox is done, I’ll stop as well,” Deer replied. “I have other information prepared, but... I’m not confident that those two don’t already know it.”
The clown spoke to me in a low voice. “What are you going to do, Lion? I don’t mind continuing the meeting just the two of us—”
“I’ll stop here too.”
“Pardon? Why?”

I just shrugged and kept quiet. If it were up to me, I’d want to go around a few more times and collect more information, but if it was just the two of us, there was a chance of garnering too much attention. It was too risky. If I threw out some information just to feel them out and the red light turned on, they might figure out that I was a newbie. Giving and taking information one piece at a time wasn’t all that efficient, either.
“Hmm, that’s a pity. This is the first time I’ve met someone who could be of help to me, yet we must end here.”

The meeting came to an end with the clown’s disappointment-filled words. But what was this? Even though the meeting was over, everyone stayed in the chat room and just quietly studied each other. Although they pretended otherwise, it wasn’t hard to figure out that their attention was on me. They seemed to want to say a few words to me before leaving.
...Yeah, I guess I’m the main character for today.

I smiled but took a moment to seriously think this through. In my first meeting, I had succeeded in building an image that the veterans here wouldn’t be able to look down upon. So, what was the most appropriate course of action for someone with this reputation?
Clown, Deer, Fox, Crescent Moon... I looked at each of the four old hands I had met here one by one.
“That’s it?”
I left.
“He’s... gone.”
Right when Lion left, Fox let out a long breath.
“Fox, are you okay?” Crescent Moon asked cautiously. They didn’t clarify why they were asking, but their meaning was clear since things had gotten really dangerous earlier.
“...I’m fine.”

Murderous intent, the intention to kill someone, was something intangible that was usually difficult to pick up on unless you had good spiritual senses. However, in this special space where mind and spirit intertwined, it was a different story.
“Are you really okay? Your hands have been shaking since earlier.”

Without the filter of a body, overwhelming fear filled the mind the moment it was exposed to murderous intent. Of course, it usually just ended there. However, in severe cases, the spiritual body itself was seriously damaged, and the consequences even crossed over into the real world.

“It’ll stop soon. Fortunately, it didn’t go as far as damaging my mind.” Even as she was saying that, however, Fox was dizzy. What would have happened if Lion had pulled back his murderous intent even a second later? She shivered just thinking about it. Perhaps she would not have gone mad, but she may have been left with a stutter or some sort of speech impediment. “Who could he possibly be...?” Fox blurted out the question she had been holding back.

He was the first newcomer in a year since the Master had disappeared. She had thought her mental walls were high, but she had only been able to withstand his murderous intent for a few seconds. It made her wonder what the hell someone had to go through to reach a level of mental fortitude that high, but there was something else that was even more surprising.
“That person, as soon as he realized that I was at my limit, stopped emitting the aura in an instant.”
“...I guess I wasn’t mistaken.”

The oppressive energy had disappeared in less than a second. It was something difficult to describe in words. To erase such an intense pressure created by extreme concentration in one fell swoop? Was something like that possible with a human mind?
I shouldn’t have stepped forward...
While the Fox was regretting her carelessness, Deer opened his mouth. “What do you all think of what he said earlier?”
“You mean the Vamdemon?”
“Yes.”
“It... can’t be a lie, since the light of truth turned on.”
Of course, the jewel in the center of the round table was not perfect. If the speaker genuinely believed their words were the truth and had no doubts, the jewel glowed green.
“Somehow, I don’t think he’s misinformed.”
“That... I agree. That’s why it’s hard to wrap my head around.”
In order for the lion mask’s information to be true, a certain premise had to be accepted as truth as well: he had to have defeated a Vamdemon with a party of three.
“I’m sure that may be the case in the game, but it still sounds too farfetched to me,” murmured Deer.
Crescent Moon smiled and joined the conversation. “Wouldn’t it be possible at Times Fifty? I don’t think Lion would have cleared it on that difficulty, though.”
“Hmm, you’re assuming that this is information Lion learned in the game.”
A moment of silence followed Clown’s weighted comment. Of course, it didn’t last long. All three shook their heads and smiled.
“...Haha, it can’t be.”
“Clown, you always say weird stuff.”
Fox didn’t throw out words of denial like the other two, but she felt the same way. To attack a Vamdemon with just three people was tough even in the game. How could it be done here?
“Tsk, you all lack imagination.” Clown clicked his tongue in apparent displeasure. “But whatever, I hope you all prepare some more next time.”
“Prepare?”

“Information! I mean information! What is this? We had someone like that finally join but had to turn him away thanks to a lack of information. Are you going to take responsibility if he loses interest in this place? Who knows what he might tell us in the future?”
“Look, saying he’d lose interest is a little too much—”
“Did you not hear what he said earlier? He was clearly disappointed!”
“A-Ahem...”

“If you don’t have anything to use, at least find something stimulating and interesting. I don’t want to miss out on this opportunity because of the likes of you guys. Got it?” At Clown’s remarks, the three of them kept their mouths shut, falling awkwardly silent.
The Watchers of the Round Table were a secretive group ordinary players didn’t even know the existence of. The three of them held some pride in being members.
“That’s it?”

Those two words had shattered all of that. That cold, mocking gaze made them realize how arrogant they were. When he left without even looking back, they admitted it to themselves. In the end, the Watchers of the Round Table was just a little pond for some.
What an interesting place.
I opened my eyes with a feeling of complete satisfaction. Inside Hansu Lee’s room, filled with just a bed and computer desk, I checked the time before closing my eyes.
The Watchers of the Round Table, huh?
The community Baekho had told me about was more useful than I’d expected. It was a perfect source of high-quality information, which I was severely lacking.
I’ll have to find a way to stay in it as long as possible.
Of course, to do so, it was important that I keep up the act. Just discovering I was a newbie wasn’t grounds to kick me out, but they’d attempt to dig into my identity more openly if they found out.
Anyway, I can come up with the information I want to use there tomorrow.

I switched gears. Sergeant Lee, Baekho Lee. A pro of pros... and the very definition of bad luck, having been summoned here after clearing the game on the day he was discharged. He hadn’t even been able to finish his break. To be honest, I still couldn’t believe it. Was he really so generous as to help me out after all that?
I should say thank you to Baekho next time we meet.

I had only entered the room because I missed being around Koreans, but had ended up making a great connection. Of course, I had no intention of keeping the relationship one-sided. Not only did I not want that, but Baekho wouldn’t be that foolish, either.
Not crossing each other’s lines so we can still laugh together is the key to maintaining a long relationship.

With that in mind, I sat down in front of the computer and participated in community activities. Unlike last time, I earned GP by selling small pieces of information. In my spare time, I went to the bulletin board or chat rooms and got accustomed to the vibe there. Soon, my second visit to the community was over.
[You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
Inside Bjorn Yandel’s room, as soon as I opened my eyes, I checked my watch. Barely any time had passed this time, either.
...If only I weren’t tired, it would have been perfect.

Since I had been awake for about twelve additional hours during the time I usually slept, there was a considerable amount of mental exhaustion. Or maybe it was a side effect of using too much murderous intent? Whatever the cause, I was glad I’d cleared my schedule for tomorrow—
“Bjorrrn! How long are you planning on sleeping!”
Goddamn it. I’d just closed my eyes for a moment, but suddenly Missha was there. It must already have been morning, since light was streaming in through the window.
“A little more...”
“What little more? You always call me lazy. Did you stay up all night in the librarrry again?”
“No.”
“Hmm, rrreally...? Anyway, before you sleep again, eat this while it’s hot.”

Missha was particular about eating on time, so I obediently got up and we ate together before I sprawled out on the bed again. I’m not sure how much time passed after that, but when I slowly opened my eyes and looked out the window, I saw a dusky, scarlet light cast on the glass.
“You slept until sundown! What did you do yesterrrday?”
“I just had some trouble sleeping.”
“...You did?”
That reaction sort of hurt my feelings, but I couldn’t argue with her. The body of a barbarian could fall asleep as soon as it made up its mind. “But, anyway... have you been here this whole time?”
“Of courrrse not. After morning training, I met up with Dwalkie for a while, and I also went to my parrrents’ house.”
“What? Wait a minute, you met up with Dwalkie?”

“Yeah. He said he was worrried about something, so I gave him some advice.” Missha spoke like this was no big deal, but knowing about Dwalkie’s feelings, I couldn’t bring myself to react the same way. Even in Dungeon and Stone, relationships among party members had always been a one-way ticket to bloodshed.
“So... what was he worried about?”
“Mm... I can’t just rrreveal someone else’s business...”
Wow, that really hurt my feelings. “Aren’t we a team?”

“Well... I’m sure I can tell you, Bjorn.” When I acted disappointed, Missha revealed what was on Dwalkie’s mind without hesitation. It turned out he had reached out to her for some regular old relationship advice. He apparently had someone he liked, but was concerned about whether or not he should reveal his feelings.
To think there are people who actually do this kind of thing...
Fighting back laughter, I asked for more information. “So, what did you answer?”
“Hmm? I just told him to confess like a man.”

“I see...” That was about what I’d expected. Wasn’t Missha someone who still hadn’t had a relationship at age twenty-five? As was obvious from how she usually treated me, she wasn’t interested in the relationships between a man and a woman.

But at that moment, Missha abruptly avoided my gaze and blurted, “Which is why I want to say something...” Her face looked oddly red. The heck? Was it because of the sunset? Just as I was thinking that, Missha grabbed my hand. “Bjorn, if it’s okay with you, will you visit my house with me tomorrrow?”
“...Visit?” Not come over? Thinking that the words didn’t fit the context, I asked for clarification, but Missha just nodded.
“Yes. Can you? I’ll continue to do whatever you ask in the futurrre. Hmm?”

Wondering what the hell was going on, I soon pieced together what was happening. She wouldn’t be acting like this if she was just inviting me to her inn. “Could it be that you’re talking about your parents’ home?”

Missha lowered her head at my question. “Yes...” There was a nervous tremor running through her hands. The sun had gone down at this point, and the sunset shining on Missha through the window was getting darker. She gulped and gave an added explanation. “M-My father wants to see you, you see... So, I was thinking... can you... go with me...?”
An invitation from her parents? I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t taken aback, but I answered without hesitation. “All right.”
“...What? Rrreally? You mean that? Wow! No takebacks, okay?”
“Uh huh, what time should we leave tomorrow?”
It felt like some long-awaited moment had finally arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 127: Karlstein (1)
paragraphs: Although Missha Karlstein was from a pureblood family, she was an adventurer with five years of experience who was treated as a stranger by her relatives because she had failed to form a contract with a Soul Beast.
Her father wants to see me, huh?
I had been expecting this to a certain extent. Through Missha, I now had a good grasp of how the Red Cat Tribe operated. “Why aren’t you saying anything? What time do we need to go?”
“Uh... I-I don’t think tomorrrow will work. I also need to prepare myself... And I have to let my father know in advance.”
“What? What do you mean by that? You were the one who asked me to go tomorrow,” I asked incredulously.
Missha averted her eyes, fidgeting with her hands. “Well... honestly, I didn’t think you would agrrree so easily...”
“Which is why you asked me to go tomorrow?”
“Yeah, you said that’s how you negotiate, rrright?”
I didn’t know if I’d said that, but Missha’s plan was effective in its own way. If I claimed I didn’t have time tomorrow, she would’ve smoothly pretended to postpone the meeting to another day.
“Ugh, you always say you’re busy everrry time I ask you to hang out. What whim are you acting on this time?”
“Your father is asking. Of course I should go meet with him.”
“Huh? I-Is that so?” Missha averted her eyes at my made-up excuse. “Y-You’re so... how can you say something so embarrrassing?”
Aren’t you the one who said barbarians and beastpeople are pretty much family?
“When you set up the visit, let me know. Now leave. I need to sleep more. Oh, and don’t come tomorrow. I have to head out early.”
“What? You slept all day and you’rrre going to sleep again?”
“Keep it up and I won’t go—”
“No! I won’t bother you, get some rrrest!”
After Missha rushed out the door, I resumed my interrupted sleep. It was only after sleeping for a whopping thirty-six hours that I finally felt a bit refreshed.
Whew, I feel much better now.
In the future, I should refrain from using murderous intent. Anyway, after quickly washing up, I headed to the holy land, where the elder greeted me.
“Long time no see, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
Where did the chieftain go? Curious, I asked the elder, and the answer that I got in return was unexpected.
“The chieftain went into the city for business. He will probably be back tomorrow.”
“The chieftain left the holy land? What a surprise.”
“It’s certainly out of the ordinary. If you have business with him, why not talk to some of the young warriors while you wait? You will be a good influence on them.”
I kindly rejected the elder’s enthusiastic offer. It wasn’t bad being recognized as one of the barbarians’ greatest prospects, but I had other business today. “Could you call for the shaman?”
After a brief wait, the shaman’s apprentice came over to guide me to the tent. The bald-headed, wrinkly shaman was blowing smoke from the large pipe in his mouth.
“Kekeke, warrior, you’re back. What talent you have.” His voice sounded more high-pitched than usual today, and his speech was a little slurred, making him seem like some kind of druggie.
“Can I get the Spirit Imprint today?”
“If you have the money, kekeke.”
I was just asking if you could do it while high...
I was inwardly worried, but I opened my wallet anyway.
Clink, clink.
Every time I handed over a one-million mana stone, a corner of my heart ached.
With this, I’m broke again.

The cost of receiving the fifth-level imprint was eight million stones. After paying that, only about seven hundred thousand stones remained in my hand. There were still two million stones left in the account I shared with Missha, but those funds were not for personal use.
“Warrior, one is missing.”
“...I’m about to put it in.”
Soon, the payment came to an end with one more mana stone worth five hundred thousand stones. Dang, I hoped that was enough.
I guess I can stop worrying about there being any mistakes during the imprint.
I lay down on the bed, focusing on the bright side as much as possible.
“Uhhh...”
“Keke, warrior! Scream louder!”
“Aaaaaah!”
Before long, a familiar pain overtook me.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 5. Your Energy has increased significantly. Your Physique stat has increased by +30. Your Spirit stat has increased by +30.]

In Dungeon and Stone, Energy was an important stat. It didn’t have a big effect on your combat power, but running out of stamina in battle left you incapacitated. The Energy Regeneration Auxiliary Scroll was even considered an essential consumable during hours-long raids.
I didn’t expect it to be a useful stat in real life.

In the past, I had ended up pushing the limits of fatigue in the Witch’s Forest. Just yesterday, I exhausted my mind and fell into a state of half-hibernation. That was why I felt the change in my body and mind more keenly.
“Keke, you look better than usual today.”

Normally, I would have been half-dead by now, but today, the accumulated strain on my body and mind seemed to be less. I’d have to test it later, but I got the sense that I would be fine staying up for two nights thanks to this. Of course, if you asked me if these results were worth eight million stones, I would say definitely not.
...As expected, the cost-effectiveness of an imprint sucks.

In the mid-to-late stages of the game, stats were worth more than gold, but in the first half, buying equipment or essences with money was much more efficient. The way to shorten the timeline for building up your character was to improve as quickly as possible and earn enough money to take the next stage of the Imprint, which was why I’d originally planned to engrave just the first stage and leave it at that for a while. I didn’t know I’d end up with Giantization so quickly.
Whew, but having gone all-in on the Imprint, there’s now only one more stage left.

The dejection I felt from my decrease in wealth was short-lived. A feeling of pride bloomed in me again. The moment I engraved the sixth stage, I would be compensated for all the money I had invested several times over.
“Warrior, why are you zoning out? I’m tired, so get out of here.”

After I sat there for a while, immersed in thought, the shaman ordered me to leave, so I left the tent. The day was getting dark. I checked in between the bushes as I walked just in case Ainar was waiting for me like last time.
She’s not here.
Even after I reached the edge of the city, Ainar was nowhere to be seen. Well, since her training was nearing its end, she was probably busy.
Come to think of it, there’s only one month left.
As I walked down a street that was more deserted than usual, I smiled. Time went so fast, yet so slow. It seemed like just yesterday I was stepping on traps because I didn’t have leather boots.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 4
Physique: 330 (New +30)
Spirit: 154 (New +30)
Special Ability: 128
Item Level: 868
General Combat Power: 941 (New +60)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Vampire (B) - Rank 5  Orc Hero - Rank 5
Three days later, Missha and I got on a large wagon heading to District Thirteen. That was because the beast tribe’s holy grounds didn’t border District Seven, where we lived.
“A-Are you thirrrsty? Do you want some water?”
“I’m fine.”
“Hungry? Are you hungry yet? I brrrought a bunch of things just in case, do you want some?”
I laughed incredulously at Missha’s anxiety. “Stop it. I’m not going to change my mind halfway there or anything.”
“I’m just worried. It’s going to be an uncomforrrtable place for you. You’re going there because of me, so I should at least—”
“Never mind that. Wake me up when we get there.”
“O-Okay... It takes about three hours, so get some rest.”
Before she could bother me any further, I closed my eyes for an indeterminate amount of time. Just as she said, the carriage only reached its destination at noon.
A six-hour round trip... no wonder she spends the night there every time she goes.
If it were a straight trip it wouldn’t have taken that long, but it took longer than expected because we had to go around District Fourteen, which prohibited people from passing through.
Well, that must be why she settled down here. She wants to be as far from home as possible.
“Bjorn, why are you just standing there? Are you tired? Do you want me to give you a piggyback rrride?”
“Hush, just take the lead.”
“Okay!”

I followed Missha, who was arguably a local, and took a look at the streets around me. It wasn’t much different from District Seven. It was just that the roads were a little more complicated, and there were a lot more beastpeople and dwarves.
“Okay, we’ve arrived.”
All in all, the beastpeople’s holy land was very different from that of the barbarians.
I heard that was the case, but I didn’t expect it to be this different...
The holy land was located outside the city, but that was all they had in common. Instead of shacks or tents in the brush, there were mostly stone buildings and even roads in between them.
“Dad, there’s a barbarian. A barbarian!”
In addition, there were open shops and a number of families walking down the streets, implying they lived here instead of in the city.
We all got kicked out when we became adults...
The holy land of the beastpeople was literally like a village outside the city. I guess I must have looked strange just blankly taking it all in.
“What’s wrong...? Is something wrrrong? Even if there is, you can’t go back now!”
“...It’s just fascinating.”
“Huh? Fascinating?” Missha tilted her head in confusion.

There were many things I wanted to say, but I kept quiet. Venting about the barbarians’ poor living conditions would just be rubbing salt in my own wound. So I just asked, “Are all holy lands like this?”
“Uh, I don’t know what you mean...”
“Shouldn’t beastpeople be raising livestock in the forest or something?”
In fact, that was how their holy land had looked in the game, so maybe that had been the case 150 years ago?
“Ah, uh, I think I hearrrd that people used to live that way to preserve our traditions... But that was so long ago, I don’t know much about it.”
“I see...” Huh, why were barbarians the only ones who had stayed the same? As I walked down the street, fighting back my displeasure, a huge mansion appeared in front of us.
“This is my house.”
Goddamn it. Our chief still sleeps in a tent.

As soon as I let out a big sigh, Missha took another moment to study me. “Y-You don’t have to be nervous. Nothing will happen. You’rrre Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel, rrright? My father likes famous adventurers. Hmm?” Missha made an attempt to reassure me, but it was clear that she was the one who was worried.
“You should calm yourself. We’re at your house, why are you nervous?”
“Huh? I-I’m perfectly fine?”
“Then open the door. How long are we going to stand here?”
At my words, Missha steadied her breathing and rang the bell to call for a servant. “Um, I want to come inside. Can you open the doorrr?”
The servant didn’t say anything in response to Missha’s request. He spared her a single glance, then opened the door and left.
The heck?
It was a very strange sight. Missha was no longer in her half-wit era.
I’m pretty sure her father knows about her signing a contract with a Soul Beast, right?

I unwittingly glanced at Missha and our eyes met, as she was also observing me. The emotion in her eyes was familiar to me. My ex-girlfriend often gave me this look when I discovered something that she wanted to keep secret.
“Um... you know, Bjorrrn. There’s something I haven’t told you yet.”
“Tell me quickly.”
Missha gulped at my words and proceeded with caution. “My father is the only one who knows that I signed a contrrract with the Soul Beast. So no matter what happens inside, don’t get angry. Got it?”
“That depends on what happens inside.”
“It’s really no big deal. That person just now was just a little harsh.”
“Tell me more. Shouldn’t I know more to respond accordingly?”

Missha hesitated for a moment but then, with a resigned look on her face, told me about her brothers’ verbal abuse, the bullying under the guise of joking around, and the servants whispering behind her back when she could hear. None of it was horrible, but I figured it was because she’d picked out only the mildest incidents to tell me about. It must have been much worse in reality.
“Oh, of courrrse, no one will do that to you. So don’t worry too much about—”
For some reason, my lips curled like they had a mind of their own.

“B-Bjorn? Why are you smiling? D-Don’t smile. You look scarrry like that... This’ll all stop once my father rrreveals the truth about my contract later. I-I just need to be patient for a little longer.”

Missha uneasily mentioned her father, but I felt that he was the biggest problem. The man who was supposed to be her father was still neglecting her despite knowing the truth. Regardless of whether there was a valid reason behind that silence, he was letting his child suffer for his own selfishness. Yet he dared call me to his home?
He must really take me for shit.
Suddenly, I felt a shady malice from this huge mansion, like I was looking at a dungeon full of monsters. Was that why?
“Behelahhh!” The shout came to me out of nowhere.
At that exact moment, the servant who had disappeared without even a glance reappeared. “What are you doing, barbarian?! Mind your manners!”
“Manners, huh?” I approached him, mulling that over. “There must be something wrong with your head.”
After all, where in the world was there a barbarian who was polite to his enemies?

chapters.title: Chapter 128: Karlstein (2)
paragraphs: In the past, Missha used to think that all her worries would disappear if she just made a contract with a Soul Beast. But reality didn’t work out that way.

“So, it’s the Ice Beast, Skadia.” Her father’s cold voice and cold gaze that day had still been the same. It was as if he was speaking to a stranger. Only now, he didn’t speak quite as curtly as before. “Have you told anyone about this?”
“I-I haven’t...”
“Good. Let’s keep this between us for the time being.” It was an order, not a request.

“A-All right...” Missha hadn’t been able to bring herself to say anything else, instead just nodding. She felt ashamed. She hadn’t formed a contract with a beast in the usual way. Using a mysterious item called the Ring of the Frost Spirit, she had successfully tricked her way into an agreement. And if her father knew that...
This treatment makes total sense.

Of course, she didn’t have the courage to ask questions. Her father was someone she feared more than anyone else in the world. So, when he asked her to bring the barbarian back to the mansion, she just told him she would. But she didn’t say a word about his request to Bjorn, either.
Yes, this is a problem that I have to deal with alone.
Hadn’t he already done her a kindness that was nearly impossible to repay? She couldn’t burden him anymore. But although she tried to rationalize it that way, deep inside, she knew the truth.
I don’t want to be found out.

She didn’t want to disclose her situation. Hikurod, Dwalkie, and Rotmiller... Even if they all already knew, she wanted Bjorn to think she was getting along just fine. So, she visited home more often.
“I have to go now. I have to stop by my parents’ today.”

She tried her best. She faced down the looks from her brothers that clearly asked why she was visiting so often, the contemptuous gazes of the servants, and the lonely dinners that felt like being on a remote island.
I can’t run away anymore.
She had learned from Bjorn that you couldn’t get anything out of running away. So, one month, two months, three months passed like that.

“Is that man not going to come here yet?” Her father redoubled his efforts to get her to bring Bjorn. She pretended Bjorn was reluctant, but it seemed her father knew that was a lie since he made the following offer: “Bring him here within the month. Then I will reconsider your treatment. Do you understand?”

In simple terms, that meant that he would finally let the family know that she had signed a contract with a Soul Beast and would treat her like his real child. She couldn’t understand why he was going so far to meet Bjorn. However, Missha decided to invite Bjorn anyway, despite not liking the fact that she was technically using him.
I’ll just work hard to pay him back.

She thought that if she handled this well, she could be more confident in front of Bjorn. Also, she figured that if she secured him the support of the Karlstein family, it would help him on his journey.
“All right.”
“...What? Rrreally? You mean that? Wow! No takebacks, okay?”
“Uh huh, what time should we leave tomorrow?”

Despite her concerns, Bjorn had readily agreed. However, her happiness was short-lived and she quickly started to worry again. She wouldn’t be able to hide it anymore when they got to her home. What should she do? If Bjorn went on a rampage there, things would get out of hand.
...Woah, ego! That’s an overinflated ego you got there!

Missha waved off her concerns with a smile. Bjorn may have been a warm-blooded warrior, but he could be colder than anyone else at times. He wouldn’t do something like that in the home of a pureblood family, in the holy land of another tribe. It wasn’t like they were related by blood, either. There was no way he would choose to make an enemy of the Karlsteins when the costs of doing so were steep.
Mhm, no way. Why would he do that for me...?
Missha thus reigned in her unruly imagination. The realization had made her heart ache for some reason, but dreams and reality were two entirely different things. She knew that now.
But then, what was this?
“Behelahhh!”

Her tail stiffened at the ferocious shout, loud enough to make her ears hurt. That was only natural. The servant was asking what was happening, but having been with Bjorn for a while, Missha already knew.
“There must be something wrong with your head.”
That means “I’m going to crack your head open!”

“A-Are you crazy?! S-Stop it! Why are you doing that all of a sudden?!” Missha jumped up and grabbed my forearm, then swiveled her head and scanned our surroundings to see if anyone heard the commotion. Seeing that, even I felt sorry for her.
It’s like seeing me in elementary school.
Resigned and solitary, erasing my sense of self by prioritizing the feelings of others... at one time, I also thought that was all normal.
“Why am I doing this? I just wanted to!”
“W-What are you talking about?!”
I brushed aside Missha’s flailing arm and said, “Missha, you’re allowed to do what you want every once in a while.”
“W-What...?”
“Why are you holding back? Putting up with stuff like this only ever benefits the other person.”
“I-It’s my family...”
Family, my ass. At this point, they should be called your enemies.
“So is your family more important than your life?”

Missha clamped her mouth shut. I was sure she knew in her head what the source of her efforts to periodically visit her family, the source of her longing for a harmonious relationship, truly was. It was a foolish, lingering affection that had no use whatsoever—an emotion no different from the very definition of insanity.
“Answer me. If yes, I will stop here.”
I asked for her input one more time but Missha didn’t say anything. That was answer enough for me.
“From now on, just watch. You will have nothing to worry about.”
“B-But if you hurt him—”
Yes, there would be an uproar. A fine would be the least of my problems. I’d also have to face the wrath of the Karlstein family, who supposedly valued honor.
“Missha Karlstein, when have I ever made a promise I couldn’t keep?”
“...Neverrr.”
“Yes, so trust me.”
I wasn’t going into this without a plan. My ignorant barbarian mode, which toggled on and off while I monitored the situation, lit up again.
Step.
Leaving Missha behind, I took a step forward. The servant was still acting high and mighty. “What did you say to her? No matter how bad your manners– “
I grabbed and lifted the man up by his collar. “Aren’t you the one being impolite? A servant of the Karlstein family, behaving so arrogantly in front of their master?”
“Th-that’s...!”

The guy looked pained and wore an expression of disbelief. Well, I was sure this must have seemed surreal to him. This wasn’t a dark back alley. How could he ever have imagined something like this happening in front of the mansion’s gates in broad daylight?
“L-Let... Ugh!” Was he unoriginal? Even his words were similar to what those other guys with problems in their heads had said. “I-If you do this...”
What, something bad will happen to me?
Smirk.

Anyone aware of that wouldn’t do something like this. So if someone was doing it anyway, it would make sense to assume that he had a plan. To think they couldn’t piece together something as simple as that...

“There must be something wrong with your head.” I clenched my fist tightly and applied moderate force. If I killed him, even I wouldn’t be able to handle the aftermath. “Don’t worry. Most of the time, you can fix it with a light beating.”
“M-Mmm!”

I grabbed the guy by the neck as he tried to say something, silenced him, and gently patted the area I intended to hit. Then, I pulled back a fist like I was going to pound him, but struck him with only as much strength as it took to flick my wrist.
Whack!

The bastard passed out with one blow. Holding him by the neck, I checked over the wound like I was inspecting an object. Blood was flowing down from his broken nose, but it should still be enough to serve as an example.

“...What’s your plan now? If my fatherrr finds out about this, he won’t just sit back,” Missha asked what my next steps were with an almost resigned expression on her face. She hadn’t interfered because I told her to trust me, but I guess she was still uneasy.
“You’ll see.”
I lifted the unconscious man with one hand and headed toward the entrance of the mansion. As I passed by the garden, I saw servants milling around, mowing the lawn or carrying luggage.
“Eek! Hurry and call Master Karlstein!”
All eyes honed in on me. Some of the servants ran off into the mansion. I followed them through the open door.
“Stop, barbarian.”
I was besieged by a dozen beastpeople, fully armed combat personnel who seemed to be in possession of ferocious spirits.

As soon as I stopped, the leader of the group (who seemed to be the captain) opened his mouth and spoke in an authoritative tone. “Miss Karlstein, can you please explain what’s going on here? Who is that barbarian, and why is Brante, who is supposed to be guarding the front gate, in that state?”
So this guy’s name was Brante.
“Uh, that’s...”

“Missha, there is no need to explain.” I tossed the useless Brante toward them. The moment they caught him in surprise, I shouted so loud that my voice rang through the mansion: “What the hell are you guys doing?!”
The beastmen all looked dazed, like they couldn’t understand what was going on.
“I came here at the invitation of the head of your family. But this guy insulted me, calling me a brainless barbarian!”
Missha tilted her head at my ensuing declaration, then whispered low so that only I could hear, “Uh, did he really say that?”
She had a tendency to focus on trivial things. Luckily, I could just pretend he lost his memory from the punch.

“Don’t lie! There’s no way Brante would do something like that.” Their bewilderment was short-lived. The bald captain dismissed my claim like it was nonsense. The way I saw it, he was digging his own grave. Braindead barbarians were immune to logic.
“A lie? Are you insulting me too?”
When I took a threatening step forward, Baldy took a step back. I didn’t think it was because he was afraid of a fight, though. Maybe it was because I was a guest of the household.

“What is the meaning of this!?” While the guards were at a loss for what to do, a man vaulted over the central staircase, jumping down from the second floor. His face was one I recognized. “You’re... Bjorn Yandel?”

It was Missha’s older brother, whom I had met on the third floor. His name was... I didn’t remember. Wait, did I even catch his name in the first place? I decided to not sweat the small stuff and instead focused on the moment.
“No way, you’re my father’s guest?”
“Long time no see.”
“Skip the pleasantries. What’s going on here?” The older brother narrowed his eyes at me. “If you can’t offer up a good explanation for this, even you won’t be able to get out of here unscathed.”
Jeez, that’s a harsh look.
I saved your life a while back, remember? Anyway, I don’t like this bastard.

I repeated the same explanation—that I had been insulted by Brante the gatekeeper—and then added on to the story. “If it were just me, I would have dealt with it. But what’s the deal with this lunatic? How dare he insult Missha while serving the family?” I shouted, pointing at the unconscious Brante.
Clear wrinkles appeared on the brother’s forehead. “I told you all to refrain when there are visitors.”
This was a completely ridiculous response.
I made that story up, but you’re just going to let what I said pass? Damn, it’s even worse here than I thought.
This must have been something that happened every day. I spoke, not hiding my mounting disgust. “So you all knew about this but ignored it?”
“This is a family affair. I have no reason to explain it to you. And all of you, return to your positions.”
“Yes sir.”
Soon Missha’s brother waved away the guards and turned back around to stare at me. “Bjorn Yandel, this was clearly a mistake on our part, so we won’t make an issue of it.”
“And?”
“...And if it’s true that this man has insulted you, he’ll be punished appropriately. That should be enough to satisfy you.”
“Satisfy, huh...?” I trailed off and smirked. School a spoiled bastard, and furthermore impress upon a bunch of people that I wasn’t someone to mess with—that had been my original plan.
I guess I’ll have to go with Plan B.
I smiled and approached the brother. “Do you also have something wrong with your head?”
Plans could always change.

chapters.title: Chapter 129: Karlstein (3)
paragraphs: The head of the Karlstein family had invited me to his home. From what I’d heard, he’d been asking for about three months. If so, what could be the reason? The first thing that came to mind was curiosity; he just wanted to meet his daughter’s teammate. If Missha had been treated as an actual member of the family, that theory would have been quite plausible. Then, if he decided I was unreliable after meeting me, he might have asked me to cut his daughter loose from the party. It seemed that most of the offspring of well-established families adventured in style in large clans with connections.
“I-I just need to be patient for a little longerrr.”

But, as it turned out, Missha’s situation was still the same. The man who called himself her father kept her awakening a secret and didn’t even make an effort to try to improve her position in the family. The moment I realized this, I felt a dark malice from this mansion. The malice was directed not only toward Missha, but toward me as well.
They called me here, knowing that was the case...
What his plan was and what method he had chosen to achieve it were very clear to me.
He’s an even bigger maniac than I realized.

The head of the Karlstein family wanted something from me, but instead of politely setting up a negotiation, he’d created this kind of situation. This must have been a part of his plan. I was Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel, a warrior who hadn’t abandoned his comrades even against the Lord of the Floor—and a barbarian who might be in a romantic relationship with one of said comrades. He probably determined that if I, known to the public as all of the above, saw something like this, it would make me easier to manipulate. After all, the only one who could change Missha’s current situation was the head of the family.
However, based on this, I came to some conclusions of my own.
He’s a free-riding son of a bitch who’s even willing to use his daughter to get what he wants. Show one weakness and I’ll be done for.
Plan A wasn’t enough. If I stopped here, I’d be reduced to just an ordinary barbarian.
Step.

I took a step forward and stared at Missha’s brother. He didn’t seem scared at all as he watched me. He just laughed like none of this was worth me getting pissed about. “You’re hard to please.” He seemed to think I was after something else and that I was only kicking up a fuss to get my hands on whatever it was. Well, he wasn’t completely wrong.
“B-Bjorn! Don’t do it!” Missha hurriedly grabbed my wrist, and I stopped.
Well, I had no real intention of beating this guy. He wasn’t just a servant of the family but one of its direct blood relatives. Impulsively kicking his ass would screw me over.
“Behelahhh!” Therefore, I gave a loud roar that could be heard from anywhere in the mansion.
The older brother frowned at my actions. “What is the meaning of this?”
“I just felt like doing it!”
“...Lunatic.”

No matter what he said, my shout served as a catalyst that brought the people of the mansion to where we were. The servants set down their work and started watching us from the end of the corridor that connected the first floor. Glancing up toward the second floor, I saw several young men and women who were wearing high-quality casual clothes.
Are they Missha’s siblings?
I couldn’t tell, but they were looking down at me with curiosity in their eyes.
Anyway, that’s enough witnesses.
The stage was set, so I turned off naive barbarian mode and addressed the brother again. “Talon Karlstein.”
“It’s not Talon, it’s Taylon.”
“You pay attention to little things that are unbecoming of a man.”
“...Shut up. What is it that you want to say?” Apparently uninterested in discussing his manliness with me, he asked me to get to the point.
“Why is Missha being treated this way by your family?” I asked bluntly.
“Like I said before, it’s a family thing—”
“Is it because Missha is a half-wit? A direct blood relative of the family who couldn’t even contract a Soul Beast?”

His bemusement was short-lived. Taylon scowled and glanced at Missha with a look of contempt, clearly wondering if she had confided in someone like me about all of that. “If you already know, then there’s nothing to hide. Yes, what you said is true. So stop getting involved in our family’s affairs.”

Telling me to mind my own business was a reasonable response. Besides us barbarians, most of society valued bloodlines. It made sense for them to treat Missha like a stranger. If she had truly inherited her father’s blood, she should have been able to make a contract with a Soul Beast. In reality, she likely didn’t share a single drop of blood with them. It seemed that her mother, the fourth wife, also hadn’t had any children other than Missha, either.
“What if that was all a misunderstanding on your part?”
The truth didn’t matter, though. The important thing now was that Missha had already awakened and could use that fact to her advantage.
“If Missha made a contract with a Soul Beast, would you apologize for what you’ve done and accept her as a member of your family?”
“She’s already twenty-five, there’s no way—”
“Answer me. If you answer the question, I won’t cause any more trouble.”
The brother sighed and gripped his forehead before answering me with obvious annoyance in his tone. “Fine, we’d apologize.”
“And accept her as family?”
“That too,” he replied without hesitation, clearly under the impression that that would never happen.
I smiled and nodded my head. “That’s settles it, then.”
My confidence seemed to worry him. “Settles what?”
Instead of answering, I shifted my gaze to Missha. My part was over now. “Missha, show them.”
“Uh, huh...?” As she suddenly found herself the center of attention, Missha glanced around in bewilderment. When our eyes met, she lowered her head and murmured, “But, my father...”

No wonder she hadn’t come out yet. As expected, her father must’ve been forcing her to keep her mouth shut. But that was why Missha had to step forward herself. Revealing this fact in front of everyone would take away one of the aces up her father’s sleeve.
“Don’t worry. Nothing will happen.”
“...H-He won’t forgive me.”
“So, what? Just tell him you messed up. That’s what families do.”
“Bjorn, you’ll bear the brrrunt of it too.”

“So be it. I’m not scared.” He was an imposing parent to her, but to me, he was just the leader of the beastpeople, and there were five of those. “What are you so afraid of? Family isn’t everything in life. I’ve been doing just fine without it,” I said, picking at my ear.
Missha laughed like I was being silly. “That’s because—! No, never mind. There’s no point in arguing with you.”
“Yeah, just ignore the little things. That’s better for your mental health.”
“Oh jeez, I feel like I don’t even know what’s right and wrong anymorrre.”
At this point, I figured I’d won her over. “Missha Karlstein, just do what you want for once. After all, don’t you have a comrade here who’s willing to help you?”

I didn’t say any more after that. Time passed and soon Missha raised her head and slowly looked around. I guess this situation was quite the source of entertainment, because there were a lot of people just watching us from afar.
Missha gulped and then finally opened her mouth, resolute. “I—”
“Enough.” A cold voice filled the large mansion. In response, Missha went as still as stone. By the time she came to her senses, a middle-aged man was standing in front of her. “Everyone, leave.”
At his words, everyone silently left. The air in the room immediately grew heavy. The man’s gaze turned to me. Although he didn’t spare a single word of introduction, I knew who he was.
Okay, so this is the maniac.
Albrenive Karlstein, the head of the Karlstein family, who had served as the chieftains of the Red Cat Tribe for generations.
“Thank you for accepting my invitation, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Thank you for inviting me, Karlstein.”
In the middle of the now-vacated lobby on the first floor, we exchanged formal greetings.

“Haha, you seem to be more polite than I thought.” He laughed good-naturedly and approached me. Instead of a handshake, he patted my shoulder like he was addressing someone beneath him. But what was this?
[You have been put into a Fear state by the Nightmare Lord.]

Like I had just encountered a natural predator, my body tensed. In addition, the tingling sensation that I felt every time I crossed the boundary between life and death began to buzz in my brain. I now understood why Missha was so afraid of her father.
“But why did you do something like that? So uncivil,” the head of the family hissed, all traces of laughter gone from his voice.

It was a shitty feeling. I knew in my head that this was the power of a skill, but my body wouldn’t accept that logic. It felt like my sensory organs were malfunctioning. Of course, the effects didn’t last for long.
[Your Mana Resistance is above a certain threshold. Your Fighting Spirit is above a certain threshold. Your Willpower is above a certain threshold. Fear has been canceled.]
Whew, fuck, that’s finally over.

“Look—” I immediately removed the arrogant man’s arm from my shoulder. His brow furrowed in apparent confusion. Well, if he had anticipated this, he wouldn’t have spouted all that bullshit just now. “Don’t touch strangers.” I tossed the arm I was holding onto aside. “That’s uncivil.”
Respect goes both ways.
After a moment of silence, the head of the family spoke. “Funny.” It gave me goosebumps that he could say that without smiling with his mouth or even his eyes.
But when it came to spirit, I couldn’t be beat. “You have weird tastes. I’m not having fun at all,” I responded calmly, grabbing Missha’s hand, which was as rigid as a rock.
As a result, the man’s gaze shifted to Missha too.
“F-Father...”
“I didn’t think you’d rebel against me.”
“Th-that’s not what—”
“Enough. You’re not important here anyway.” Albrenive cut her off and looked at me. “I originally planned to have a talk after having lunch together.”
Talk, my ass. He had just been planning on showing me how Missha was treated around here.
When I stared at him without replying, Karlstein continued. “But it seems that’s no longer necessary. Get some rest. I’ll call on you later.”
“I refuse,” I replied without a second’s hesitation.
Albrenive’s expression twisted. “What?”

I decided to be blunt. “Why should I wait?” Giving him time was foolish. Although he’d had no choice but to step forward because of Missha, what had nearly just happened couldn’t possibly have been in his plans. He probably intended to regroup before summoning me again. “If you have something to say, do it here and now.”
“...Even for a barbarian, this is disrespectful.”
“You were the one who summoned this barbarian, beastman.”
Did he not expect to be called “beastman” instead of his name, “Chief,” or “family head?” Albrenive’s face hardened and he began to emit murderous intent—not just metaphorically, but literally.
You can do that in real life?
I was a little surprised, but it was much weaker than the fox mask’s. After all, that had been in the spiritual world. It made sense that there would be a difference in output.
When I picked my ear as if to say, “Stop screwing around,” Albrenive asked, almost genuinely curious, “Are you really not afraid of death?”
To me, that was a pointless question. Not afraid of death? Could someone like that even exist? “Well, I don’t know about that. But I’m not very afraid of you.”

That much was sincere. The fact that he used to be an adventurer on the eighth floor or that if we truly fought, I would be destroyed? So what? If he killed me, my chieftain wouldn’t just twiddle his thumbs.

“You think you can kill me?” I asked outright. It was absurd. Kill me? The most promising talent among the barbarians in recent months? In the middle of a beastpeople sanctuary I had been personally invited to? There would immediately be a repeat of the war with the elves from ten years ago. That was just how barbarians were.

“What? Ahahaha!” Albrenive made an effort to play it cool, but I could see the deep anger under the surface. It was probably frustrating. He was loathe to admit it, but my accusation was right on point. He was just trying to laugh it off. “It makes sense that things have gone so wrong. I never thought you would be such a clever guy.”
“Thank you for the compliment, but I’d like an answer before I get hungry. What do you want to say to me?”
Albrenive just looked at me for a moment to gather his thoughts. Then he said, “I know you used that item.”
With that, all my questions were answered. The Ring of the Frost Spirit had been the cause of all this shit.

chapters.title: Chapter 130: Karlstein (4)
paragraphs: What did the head of the family really want from me? That had been my question from the start. I had a guess, but it wasn’t a sure thing. So, Plan B. I had come up with a plan for Missha to come out in front of everyone. That was the thing Albrenive wanted least right now.
Mhm. The way to hinder your opponent is to prevent them from being able to go through with their plan.

Albrenive wanted to keep Missha’s awakening a secret. So, before Plan B came to fruition, I hurriedly showed my hand. As a result of pushing through the conversation like a barbarian, I was finally able to figure out what he really wanted.
“I know you used that item.”
He meant the Ring of the Frost Spirit, a Numbers Item that allowed you to make a contract with the Ice Beast Skadia when you activated a hidden trigger.
It’s not strange that a chief of the tribe would know that. After all, if he hadn’t known that item got used, there’d be no reason for him to still be treating Missha like an other right now.
I had already considered the possibility of this coming up. However, Albrenive didn’t know for sure yet.
“That item? What are you talking about?”
The odds of a twenty-five-year-old beastwoman of the Red Cat Tribe making a natural contract with Skadia were close to zero, but “close to” and “zero” were two entirely different things.
“Hmm.” That was why he was feeling us out. He might have suspicions, but he had no evidence. “Your acting is clumsy.”
Clumsy, my ass. Do you know how many people I’ve tricked so far?
“What are you talking about? Say it plainly.”
“I mean the item that allows you to sign a contract with the Ice Beast Skadia. You can’t say you don’t know about it.” Albrenive stared at me, silently demanding that I tell the truth.
Do you think barbarians are fools?
“Something like that exists? Then why didn’t you give it to Missha?”
“Because it is very valuable. I wouldn’t give it to someone who isn’t even my child.”

As soon as I heard that, I quickly checked on Missha. As expected, she looked like she was about to cry. However, I decided to console her later and continued acting like a barbarian who didn’t know anything. “A valuable item? Isn’t that even weirder? How could I have something like that?”
“Who knows? Perhaps you obtained it from the Magic Tower you used to visit so often.”
What the fuck. Does he really know everything?
