My body tensed up without me realizing it. In order to make up for my mistake, I stared at the family head. “...Did you investigate me?” With this, my actions just now wouldn’t seem so awkward. I was simply a barbarian who was mad about his out-of-line behavior.
“Didn’t I already tell you? Your acting is clumsy.”
Damn it, I believed in my acting skills, so I refused to budge. “So what is this thing you’re talking about?” I asked in annoyance. “Why do you keep bothering me like this?”
“I can’t tell you that.”
“What?”
“You keep denying it, and this is an item that the outside world can’t know about. If you admit you already know about it, I will tell you.”
Huh? The heck? There was no contradiction in his words. If he were just feeling me out, it’d make more sense for him to reveal the name of the item.
Why am I getting a weird vibe?
Something felt off. The intuition that had thwarted the countless sons of bitches who had tried to feel me out was talking to me. Something wasn’t right.

“Does something like that even exist? You don’t have an ulterior motive?” I once again asked, pouring all my concentration into carefully observing the head of the Karlstein family, looking for a momentary hesitation, a twitch in his facial muscles, a change in where he was looking, or how his voice sounded.
“Of course. What other reason could I have?”
I was not an expert, but I examined every part of that short sentence with suspicion. Then I instinctively sensed that he was lying.
Ha, yes, that was it. Thank you for clearing up my last suspicion. You could have felt me out in another way, you know.
“Tell me honestly,” Albrenive said. “If you’re keeping your mouth shut because you’re worried about this kid, I’ll take care of that.”
Why was he saying such contradictory things? Everything made sense when you concluded that it wasn’t Missha, but the ring he was after.
No wonder he kept saying “that item.”
Soon, I was convinced. Albrenive knew about the Ring of the Frost Spirit, but only partway.
He knows it exists, but not what it is.

Finally, I pieced together the situation in my head. The head of the family had invited me to his home. Whether or not Missha was his real daughter didn’t matter; it seemed like he wasn’t too enthusiastic about his children in the first place. His real objective was something else: an item that could definitely contract a Soul Beast. If I really knew something about it, he wanted to find out what. After all, this must have been important and priceless information to a beastman. That was why he was parading Missha’s miserable situation right in front of me, believing her to be my Achilles’ heel. He likely intended to use her against me in a trade or for blackmail purposes.

“On my honor as a warrior, I do not know about such a thing.” I threw down my trump card. The number one reason why barbarians were overpowered characters to me was the warrior’s oath. Bewilderment filled Albrenive’s eyes. I took it in and threw in the last punch before the timing passed me by. “But I will definitely find out what it is. Just you wait.”
Muttering like I was holding back anger, I studied his face. There was a light of deep disappointment in his eyes.
Geez, his acting is worse than mine.
“Forget the conversation we had today.”
With that order, we left the Karlstein home. Missha’s face had been blank since earlier and I didn’t initiate any conversation. I had things to think about too.
Whew, at least it didn’t get to the worst-case scenario.

When I heard about the invitation from the Karlsteins, there were two reasons why I gladly accepted. The first was Missha’s freedom. If the head of the household was trying to push Missha into a large clan, I had to stop it. After Erwen and Ainar, I couldn’t let Missha, who I’d put in all this effort to cultivate, get away. Even the thought was horrifying.

The second reason was to prevent anyone from suspecting me of being an evil spirit. If the head of the household knew the secret behind Missha’s awakening, it was critical to visit him at least once to properly cover my bases. I didn’t think he would call me there with incomplete knowledge, though.
Creak.
When we passed the garden, the gatekeeper opened the gates wide. I guess Baldy was taking a break after getting treated because it was my first time seeing this particular face.
It seemed the other party recognized me, though. “G-Goodbye.” When our eyes met, he even bowed briefly as he saw me off.

Soon, I turned around for the last time and looked at the mansion where Missha had lived from childhood to adulthood. The manicured gardens were gorgeous, and the fountains glistened with splendid jets of water. The mansion itself was not much different. Unlike the inn where I was staying, the architecture was antique and had an aristocratic feel. However, the cold hostility surrounding the mansion remained unchanged. Just like the first time I saw this place, I felt like I was looking at a dungeon full of monsters. And I was realizing now that Missha had survived here for a long time.
“You did a good job,” I said.
As I gave her a pat on the back, Missha came to her senses and shook her head. “I-It was nothing. You did all the hard worrrk...”
Well, I didn’t mean it that way. “Still, weren’t you the one who had the hardest time?” I smiled and slapped her on the back again.
“Agh! It hurts!” Yeah, that seemed more like regular old Missha.
“If you’re awake now, lead the way. I don’t know the way back.”
“Ha, rrreally... what would you do without me?”
“I wouldn’t have come somewhere I don’t know the way back from.”
“...True.”
We walked the streets, sharing in meaningless banter. There were happy faces everywhere.
“Dad, it’s that barbarian from earlier!”
Families of beastpeople were walking, laughing, and chatting happily.
“Bjorn, let’s eat there too.”
“Why do you want to eat out for once?”
“Mm, well... it’s been a long day?”
Missha and I stopped by a street vendor and bought some snacks, which we ate on a bench in the plaza. There was no problem with eating while we moved, but taking a break wasn’t bad either.
“Hey, Bjorrrn?”
“Speak.”
“Why haven’t you ever asked?”
“What?”
After taking a short break, watching the people around us come and go, Missha asked me a question. “Aren’t you currrious?”
“About what?”
“Whether... I’m really my father’s child...”
So that was what she was getting at. I chuckled and glanced at Missha. She hadn’t done anything wrong, but she dropped her head and stared at the ground anyway. “I’m not curious.”
“Really? Not even a little bit?”
“Yeah, what does that matter?”
“Wow, you rrreally don’t care about me...”
What was this kid talking about? I was about to slap her on the back again, but paused.
She said that hurt.

I thought about messing up her hair like in a cartoon, but that was too cringy. With nowhere to go, my hand landed on my knee again. I looked out into the distance and talked to her instead. After all, she was my teammate. Shouldn’t I clear up some misunderstandings?
“It’s not that I’m not interested, it’s just that it’s not really important.”
“Huh?”
“Rank-seven adventurer Missha Karlstein—that’s you. It doesn’t matter who your parents are. The fact that you are a comrade I can trust to watch my back won’t change.”
“Wow...” Missha’s mouth fell open like she’d just heard something incredible. Then she looked up at me and smiled. “How did you think that up?”
“...Are you picking a fight?”
“Hee hee, I’m saying thank you. Those words give me some strrrength.” That was a relief. After resting for long enough, I was about to get up when Missha grabbed my sleeve. “Bjorn?”
“What?”
“This is a secret, and you’re the only one I’m telling, okay?”
“Spit it out quickly.”
“I... really am a bastard. My mom told me. Before she died. While apologizing.”
Ah, uh... um...
I scrambled to figure out what to say, and decided to just nod my head. “...I see.”
“What? Why aren’t you surprrrised?”
Because I already knew. I hadn’t known the details, though. “It’s not that important, is it?”
“Oh, this cold-hearted barrrbarian!”
Soon, we got up from our seats. Then we left the holy grounds, entered the city, and arrived at the public carriage platform.

“Oh, by the way,” she said once we’d bought our tickets and were waiting for the carriage, “what was that earlierrr? You made an oath in front of my father. That was definitely...” Missha trailed off.
I was genuinely stunned. I hadn’t even thought about it, either because I was so comfortable with her now, or because I had been in front of the head of the Karlstein family.
“That... was a lie, rrright?”

I sighed and nodded. What was the use of hiding anything when she already knew everything? I just had to do decent damage control. “Yeah, that was a lie. Because you are more important than my honor as a warrior.”
“...Is that trrrue?”
“Yes.”
Missha didn’t say anything for a long while. Just like that, a period of anxiety ensued. Surely she wasn’t thinking anything weird, was she?

Just when I decided to speak up first rather than let this suffocating silence continue, Missha jumped up. Then she blurted out something basically unintelligible. “Oh! I left something at home, so I’m going to go!”
“...What? A carriage is coming soon—”
“You head home firrrst!”
And just like that, she was gone with the wind.
What the... Am I fucked?
Flip.
Sitting in his study, Albrenive Karlstein turned the pages of a book with a slightly hasty hand. Then, finally, he found what he was looking for.
No...
In the case of... it is possible to contract the Ice Beast, Skadia.

All of his suspicions began with this book, and an explanatory summary with only one intelligible sentence thanks to the page it was on being completely torn apart. The Complete Book of Relics VI contained descriptions of hundreds of numbered items. The important thing here was that said explanations were never wrong. That was what these books were—books of truths that there was no point in doubting.
If I hadn’t known about this, I could have been genuinely happy.

When that child had revealed she was awakened, to be honest, he was happy. He had thought that he wouldn’t have to hide the family’s disgrace anymore. However, the Soul Beast she’d made a contract with was the issue. Was this really a coincidence? He couldn’t shake a strange unease. He had questioned the child many times and soon came to a conclusion: she didn’t awaken naturally. And if his assumption was correct, she had received help, perhaps from that barbarian Bjorn Yandel.
“I-I can’t tell you anything related to Bjorn. I m-made an oath to the guardian spirit...”

However, the child avoided the conversation by invoking the guardian spirit’s oath. Although the oath held no authority and had no meaning now in a time when such traditions had faded, the child who had never been able to rebel had come up with an excuse for the first time and had lied to him. It would be difficult to get a proper answer from her.
It would be better to dig into that barbarian.

Albrenive thus changed targets. Then, suspicious details came to his attention, one after another. The barbarian was friendly with a wizard of the Artemion School, Arua Raven. Coincidentally, he knew of her. She was a rival he’d run into while wandering around to get another Complete Book.
Then a hypothesis formed in his mind. What if the wizard had somehow gotten her hands on The Complete Book of Relics? And what if she told the barbarian about it?
That makes a lot more sense.

He decided to aim for the barbarian rather than the bold wizard girl. Over the course of his investigation, he found out that his relationship with Missha was almost like that of a married couple, so it seemed to make sense to use her.
To think it really was a natural awakening.
He didn’t believe in things like oaths, but that barbarian hadn’t been acting. He really seemed oblivious, and Albrenive found himself lamenting his neglect toward that child.
Interesting. Even such insignificant blood has talent.
Just as his thoughts began to wander in that direction, someone knocked on the door. It was Beros, his aide. “Missha is asking to see you.”
“Send her in at once.”
The aide left and after a brief wait, the child came in. “I... there was something I didn’t say earlierrr—”
“Ah, don’t worry about that. I will keep my promise. No one will think of you as someone who isn’t part of the family anymore.”
Strangely, Missha did not react to that. He had thought she would be happier.

He even added, “That means you are my daughter now.” These were words that any child who grew up lacking love and resenting her family would have desperately hoped to hear. However, her silence continued. “...Why aren’t you saying anything?”
“Because I’m not here to hearrr something like that!”
“What?” He was taken aback by her disrespectful tone. What was this change in attitude?
Before he could regroup, Missha faced him head-on. “Father—no, you’re not even my fatherrr. Did you know that? We don’t share even a drop of blood.”
“What?” He was genuinely perplexed, not because he didn’t know that, but because he had never expected to hear it from her.
“My mother told me beforrre she passed away. I’m not actually blood-related to the Karlstein family. I came to tell you that. I hate you... but I feel sorrry for you.”
Perhaps it was because he hadn’t imagined she’d ever act this way, but Albrenive wasn’t even offended by that bold statement. He was just curious. “Why are you doing this?”

He knew who Missha’s real father was. He had secretly watched his wife confess the truth on her deathbed. He had just kept it a secret it until Missha became an adult for the sake of his family’s honor. He figured this matter would all be resolved if she just died in the labyrinth.

“If you hadn’t said that, I really would have accepted you as a member of the family.” He was giving her what she always longed for. Why was she refusing it? “Why? Why throw away this opportunity with your own hands?”

As if the question wasn’t worth answering, the child turned around and headed for the door. But did she have a last-minute change of heart? She turned her head to glance at him over her shoulder. “I just... wanted to!”
To Albrenive, those words were utterly incomprehensible.

chapters.title: Chapter 131: Team Play (1)
paragraphs: Ten days had passed since my visit to the Karlstein family home. On the first day, I was worried that Missha might have told her father everything.
“What? Are you crrrazy! You boneheaded barbarian! How can you say something like that!?”
“Then what did you do back there?”
“That’s—! You don’t need to know!”

My anxiety turned out to be unnecessary. I didn’t know why she’d kept the secret, but I could be certain that she hadn’t told him. I decided to focus on the issues that needed to be dealt with right away instead. Weren’t there two ticking time bombs on the team already?
“Dwalkie, let’s talk.”
The day after returning from the Karlsteins’, I had a meeting with Dwalkie right away. With a drink in hand, I fudged the issue.
“What? Is that true? Miss Karlstein likes fat guys?”
“Yes, she’s definitely said that before.”
“I-I see. Thank you for telling me. I almost made a mistake in my haste.”
After that conversation, Dwalkie ordered a bunch of dishes and stuffed himself until his stomach bulged out. Well, that was one solution.
He won’t confess until he gains some weight.

It was safe to say that I had bought at least a month or two. With Dwalkie’s personality, he wouldn’t be able to muster up the courage unless he gained a considerable amount of weight. And by the time he did, Missha and I would be out of the party.
This makes me feel like total trash...

But I had no other choice. Maybe if this guy had more mental fortitude it would be fine, but what would happen if he confessed to Missha and was rejected? He wouldn’t be able to focus even in the labyrinth. That could endanger the team.
Uh, but why am I so sure he’ll get rejected?
That question suddenly popped into my head, but I didn’t think too deeply about it. The data we accumulated in the unconscious mind sometimes made more accurate predictions than anything else.
Anyway, next was Rotmiller.
“Be careful. My father would have played a trick on that Rotmiller man.”

If, as the district chief’s daughter Julian had said, Rotmiller had made contact with the chief, there was a high probability that some kind of troublesome conversation had taken place. The district chief and I had quite a bad relationship. Although I wondered why he was making a move against me only now, months later.
Anyway, I can’t show that I’m suspicious.

In the case of Rotmiller, unlike with Dwalkie, I approached the matter cautiously and took my time. This guy was scary. I’d yet to see him get angry, but that just made him even scarier. Usually, this type of person had to see things through to the end when something went awry.

“Then, for the first floor, I’ll lead us toward the portal closest to the starting point... Haha, marriage? That’s a strange question to ask. I will not start a family until I can truly take care of another person... You sit on the inside. Since you’re big, you’ll keep bumping into people in the corridor.”

I continued to observe Rotmiller at our usual meetings as well as when we were out drinking socially. He was still the same. He was as quiet and serious as usual, and he was still considerate of others in most situations.
Ha, this is a big headache.

Even after hearing Julian’s warning, it was hard for me to imagine Rotmiller stabbing me in the back. No, on the contrary, doubting him made me feel even more guilty. We had shared highs and lows together for the past several months. Being swayed by a word from an outsider and not being able to believe in him?
There can’t be a greater contradiction than that.
The more I thought about it, the more ironic the situation was. However, I decided it was only right to clear things up. What did Rotmiller speak about with the district chief that day?
If he brought it up to me first, I would have been able to discard my suspicions without any regrets.

Rotmiller hadn’t said anything, though, so I invited him out and set up a conversation. I really didn’t have much time. The labyrinth would open the next day. That was why I dumped the contents of my glass into my mouth at once and got straight to the point.
“Rotmiller. What was the reason you went to the Adventurers’ Guild?”

Rotmiller was slightly taken aback by my blunt question, but I guess he put some of the pieces together. “No wonder you’ve been coming to see me more than usual. How did you know about what happened at the guild?”
So something did happen there. “I know someone in the guild.” After providing that brief response, I asked for an answer to my first question.
Rotmiller sighed. “...When I responded to the invitation, the seventh district chief was waiting for me. He offered me a reward to betray you.”
“And?”
“I told him I’d pretend I never heard the offer and left. Is that enough of an answer for you?” Although he tried not to show it, Rotmiller seemed very uncomfortable with my line of questioning.
I bore it and asked another question. “Then why didn’t you tell me before now?”
“I told you. I said I’d pretend I never heard it. Besides, I thought that if I told you, it would only make things weird.”
“I see. Thank you for answering.”

With that, the conversation came to an end. If I pushed any further, that would only signal to him that I didn’t believe him. Whatever Rotmiller’s intentions were, I decided that that wasn’t a wise move.
It wouldn’t change anything, anyway.

You could not enter the labyrinth without a scout. Finding someone new? That was risky as well. It would be difficult to find a skilled scout unless you went through the guild, and that would be the perfect opportunity for the district chief to insert a weirdo onto the team. It was doubtful whether Hikurod or Dwalkie would even agree to it in the first place.
Above all, I don’t think Rotmiller was lying when he said he turned down the offer.
Soon, I made my final decision. “Sorry to bother you so late. Get some rest and I’ll see you tomorrow at the meeting place.”
This changed nothing. Rotmiller would join the expedition.
The next afternoon, seven hours before the labyrinth opened...
“Mister, I’ll come find you once I’m back! So you have to come back safe!”
“Yeah, you work hard too.”
Erwen, who had been hanging around at my lodgings since receiving the binding spell with her sister that morning, left. Right on cue, Missha arrived.
“What the heck, why is she leaving from herrre?”
“She stopped by to say hello. Apparently, she had nothing to do after getting the binding spell.”

“Anyway, you came right on time. Let’s get some sleep.” I set a timer on the alarm clock I bought a while ago and slept with Missha so that we would be in peak condition. Some time passed, and then...
“Bjorrrn, wake up.”
We ate a simple meal and left with the backpacks that we had prepared earlier. Since we got there a little early, no one was at the meeting point yet.
As always, Rotmiller arrived right on time. “Hm, are the two of them not here yet?”
“Yeah. Dwalkie and Hikurod must be a bit late,” answered Missha.
“...That’s nothing new.”
Those two were always either early or late, so we waited.
“Oh, Bjorrrn! Look over there!”

When I glanced in the direction Missha was pointing, I saw a group of young warriors who had just finished their coming-of-age ceremony moving in clusters. I quickly approached them. At this point, I’d be bummed if I didn’t run into these guys before we left.
“Are you lost? Then you can follow those people who look like adventurers over there,” I offered.
“Who are you to say something so obvious?”
Huh? What was with that reaction? “...I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“What! Little Balkan! It’s an honor to meet you!”
“But why is that obvious?” I asked after introducing myself. “What do you mean by that? Could it be that you aren’t lost?”
“Of course not! We just have to follow the adventurers like we learned in the holy land. Why would we be lost?”
“You said you were taught that in the holy land? They didn’t show you a strange map and tell you to memorize it?”
“Map? We don’t know how to read maps!”
The young warrior’s answer left me dazed. What was this? Had their teaching methods changed? Well, I didn’t have an issue with that. This method made much more sense than memorizing a map.
“There is still time, so hear me out,” I said.
“What is it?”
“This will be helpful information for you.” I recounted the same stories I had told the former group leaders I’d run into.
“Beware of humans? Well, of course. Shouldn’t we protect our hearts?”
This group of baby barbarians was clearly different. Every time I said something, they always reacted as if I’d just said something obvious.
“Wow... the barbarians have evolved,” Missha commented.
It seemed I wasn’t the only one who thought this was strange. How had this change come to pass?
“Who in the holy land told you about all of this?” I asked just in case and was promptly stunned.
“Kharon, son of Tarson!”
Without my knowing, the winds of change had begun to blow from below.
“Then we’ll be going now! Bjorn, son of Yandel, it was an honor to meet you!”
I wanted to ask more, but the baby barbarians left, saying they wanted to enter the labyrinth. As soon as they disappeared, the two people we had been waiting for arrived at the meeting place.
“Oh, sorry for being late! Did you wait long?”
“Hahaha! Forgive us. Dwalkie had a stomachache!”
“W-W-Why are you telling them that?!”
“Ah, jeez. What’s there to be embarrassed about? It’s just us.”
“Okay, let’s get going as well.”
Because the duo was a whopping twenty minutes late, we hurriedly headed to Dimension Square. The portal was already open.
“Well then, let’s go!”
After getting a binding spell through Dwalkie, we entered the labyrinth.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]

The Crystal Cave was filled with a brilliant light. Last month, Missha and I had used the bug to skip this, so it had been a while since we saw this sight, but there was no time to leisurely take in our surroundings. That was because we had decided to try a speedrun this time at Rotmiller’s request.
“If you guys are willing, I want to give it a proper go. It’ll probably be hard to earn an achievement, but I’m curious to see what I can accomplish.”
As he was not usually someone to voice his own opinions when we were making exploration plans, everyone unanimously agreed.
“We’ll leave straight away.”
As soon as he opened his eyes, Rotmiller touched the wall, figured out our current location, and immediately began to find the way. He started running like a cantering horse.
This is actually pretty fun.

Rotmiller took point, searching for the path. Right behind him, Missha cleaned up the mobs of trash. Mine and Hikurod’s role was to take turns carrying Dwalkie and follow those two. Not only was this a novel formation designed just for fast travel, but because we started running from the very beginning, we got to see things that we hadn’t ever seen before.
“Wow, they’re rrrunning, too!”
Other adventurers were running through the cave to find portals, just like us. This was something we rarely saw when we were moving at a leisurely pace.
I can see why it’s difficult to shorten the travel time on the first floor.

I also came to some realizations. The cave on the first floor had many sharp turns, so it was hard to run with all your might. In other words, once you got above a certain level, all adventurers had the same movement speed. As a result, the skill of the scout became all the more important. Well, that and the stamina of the party members.
Huff, puff...
Even though our physical strength far surpassed that of ordinary people, sweat poured down our bodies in rivers as we sprinted for hours. Was that why? Conversation between us naturally faded.
“Hikurod, are you okay?”
“I’m fine.” The dwarf, who lacked agility and endurance, seemed to almost be at his limit, but he refused to whine. Well, how could he in front of Rotmiller?
“This way.”

I guess he had been telling the truth when he said he wanted to test his limits because Rotmiller stayed focused and led the way for several hours. If I were to put it nicely, it was passion. To put it rudely, it neared the point of madness.
Was this man always so passionate?
I admired this new side of him and continued to move my feet.
It took six hours to reach the portal. Unfortunately, it had already been opened by someone else.
“Wow, so it’s possible to get here that fast!” Missha exclaimed, but Hikurod and I immediately noticed Rotmiller’s expression.
“Damn it! Why am I...”
This was the first time he had ever made a face like that.

chapters.title: Chapter 132: Team Play (2)
paragraphs: The portal shimmered like an aurora on the North Sea, and a heavy silence settled in front of it. Neither Missha nor Hikurod said anything and just looked at each other. That was how unfamiliar the face Rotmiller was making right now was.
Crunch.

Like the very definition of “gritted teeth,” Rotmiller’s clenched-shut mouth trembled. It seemed we were seeing his rock bottom for the first time. His inferiority complex must have been hidden somewhere deep down by self-control and the desire to improve.

“...It’s not too late yet.” Rotmiller broke the silence. “There are three parties ahead of us. Even with the most high-level team, the time difference would only be about thirty minutes. If we follow them quickly, we might be able to get ahead of them on the second floor.”
At first glance, this sounded logical. However, when you broke it down point by point, it was full of issues. The problem was, even knowing this, everyone nodded awkwardly.
“A-Ah! That would work. I-I also don’t want to give up after we got here so earrrly.”
“H-Hahaha! S-So I wasn’t the only one?”
“...I-I also agree.”
Nice guys. It was obvious what they were thinking. Rather than refusing, they probably thought it was better to force themselves to agree and just suffer.
“Bjorn... what do you think?”
Eyes drifted to me, as I had not yet expressed an opinion. Ha, so annoying. Why did I always have to play this role?

I sighed inwardly, but decided to be blunt. “Do you all have something wrong with your heads?” There was already a thirty-minute gap on the first floor. That gap would widen further on the second floor. We were also already exhausted just from getting here. “You want to outrun them in this state? Do you really think we can do that?”
The three of them kept their mouths shut and avoided my gaze. Therefore, I ignored them and stared at Rotmiller.
“Brown Rotmiller, that’s enough. I’ll follow you on the first floor anytime. But the second floor is too much for us. Don’t put your teammates at risk because of your stubbornness.”
Rotmiller closed his mouth in a fit of indignation. I said nothing more and just stared at him. His reply came a beat later. “I’m sorry. I must’ve lost my mind for a while there. Forget what I said.”
“I already forgot it.”

Rotmiller offered words of apology, and I calmly let it go. The other three let out the breaths they had been holding back. Fortunately, it seemed that the situation had been handled without an argument.
What a headache.
The problem was, nothing was resolved yet.

The scout position existed to reduce travel time in a labyrinth where saving time meant survival. Their combat power was lacking in comparison to party members in other roles, but a scout’s betrayal was always fatal. Scout was the only position that could conspire with the environment itself.
Since the district chief knows that, he must have tried to appeal to Rotmiller first.
The scout controlled the journey through the labyrinth. In other words, it would be quite possible for one to pretend to guide us and lead us to a trap prepared by the district chief.
...Maybe I should’ve sat this expedition out.

I had decided to trust Rotmiller because I knew what he was usually like. His personality was straightforward to the point of stubbornness. He was a sincere man who stayed away from luck and stuck to effort. I had assumed that someone like that would not be tempted by whatever schemes the district chief tried to use him for.

But Rotmiller today? He was acting so strange that he seemed almost like a different person. His logic was nowhere to be found. He seemed impatient and desperate, like someone who had been driven to the edge of a cliff.
It’s probably because of that district chief bastard.

Of course, I still thought the possibility of betrayal was low. This man was not an idiot, and if he really meant to betray us, he wouldn’t have acted out of the ordinary. However, I still had to assume the worst and be careful.
...I should keep an eye on him for now.
With these worries in the back of my mind, the exploration resumed. However, despite my concerns, Rotmiller looked like his usual rational self as he led the group.
[You have entered the Rock Desert on the second floor.]
He found the exact route through the desert even when the compass went dead. On the morning of the second day, he located the portal to the third floor.
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]

There was no big difference on the third floor, which we arrived at earlier than ever. He headed straight to the Witch’s Forest with minimal combat, and at ten at night he took a break to rest. It was the same at midnight, the start of the third day. We all woke up for a moment to watch the third floor being dyed with silver light.
“Hahaha! I don’t know why I never watched this before and just slept through it all this time!”
“It’s probably because there was no one to share it with.”
“Dwalkie, that was so cheesy.”
This was perhaps a tradition unique to Team Half-Wit. No one suggested it, but ever since our first expedition, we always watched the lights together like an unspoken rule.
[You have entered the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.]

Anyway, the expedition went smoothly after that. On the evening of the seventh day, we reached the fourth floor. This calmed me down too. It meant that there was no longer any need for me to be suspicious of Rotmiller.
It must have been my mistake.

The fourth floor was an independent one. Once you entered, after about five minutes, no other adventurers could enter the same space as you. I watched my back throughout the first few battles to see if anyone came in after us, but no other adventurers had appeared by the time we cleared the Tower of Heavens’s first floor.
“Bjorn! What are you thinking so harrrd about?”
“Let’s go up.”

So, I completely let go of my worries and focused on the expedition. Well, not completely. I couldn’t help that this was a part of my personality. I believed that there was no such thing as 100 percent certainty in this world, especially if you were on an expedition where anything could happen.

Anyway, after entering the fourth floor, we focused on going up the tower by alternately taking the stairways of Wisdom and Courage. On the way, there was a moment when all the available staircases happened to be those of Patience, but it ended up going more smoothly than I thought it would. It was a psychological ordeal, but it wasn’t too difficult to get through. Whoever showed up and whatever they babbled, you just had to filter it out through the other ear.
To be honest, what came after the ordeal was more annoying.
“Wahhh, Bjorrrn...!”
“Stop crying. It’s over.”
“If you abandon me too, then I’ll rrreally be all alone!”
I didn’t know what the hell she saw or heard, but as soon as we cleared the floor Missha started wailing.
Hikurod, meanwhile, was on his knees in despair. “The swords I make are no better than scrap metal...”
Dwalkie was staring blankly into space like he was out of his mind and Rotmiller was silently clenching his fists. Both of them looked somewhat angry.
...That’s concerning.

While they were all recovering, I checked the box set in the center of the floor, a reward that you could only obtain by choosing a trial of Patience. If you were lucky here, you might get a numbered item or a random essence below rank six.
Of course, not a chance. Sure enough, there were only twelve rank-seven mana stones inside.
“If you’re all done resting, let’s get going again.”

After spending nearly thirty minutes calming down, the expedition resumed. After that, nothing happened. We beat up more monsters and continued climbing the floors. Soon it was the twelfth day and we’d reached the hundredth floor.
“I think this is the first time I’ve ever come this far.”

From the hundredth floor on, the difficulty of the trials locked on the highest level and rank-six monsters appeared more frequently. However, we didn’t run into too much trouble here either, thanks to the development of our two main damage dealers. Their compatibility was quite good too.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-seven attack spell Cold Storm.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Ice Crush.]

Dwalkie had used his hard-earned money to learn not only support magic, but also a rank-seven wide-range Cold spell. When you threw in Missha, dealing with rank-six monsters was no problem. With two tanks and damage support on top of that, our party’s balance had increased dramatically. It would be a different story if a rank-five monster like the Troll appeared again, though.
Still, I’ve been using our money to prepare a lot, so it makes sense that things are going much better than back then.
In fact, it was strange to worry about rank-five monsters on the fourth floor. It wasn’t like we’d run into a Hans on the way.
Looks like Rotmiller has come to his senses now too.
Despite our rocky beginning, the expedition continued to proceed smoothly. Then the start of the nineteenth day came.
It was 6:32 a.m. I checked my watch and scanned our surroundings. All four of my teammates were sleeping comfortably in their respective spots.
Being awake alone feels like I’m on night watch again.

I buried myself in my sleeping bag again and closed my eyes, but I couldn’t fall back asleep easily, perhaps thanks to my increased energy. No, wait, was it because there were already only four days left until the labyrinth closed?
I feel restless for some reason.

I’d been feeling this way for the past few days, but our teamwork had improved considerably. It felt like we finally had a good rhythm going. Even if I didn’t give an order, they were each on top of their game, and they had started communicating with each other a bit through looks and gestures. No matter what happened, we were gradually growing into a proper party.
Compared to our first expedition, the difference is ridiculous.

Just look at Dwalkie—the change was like night and day. He almost didn’t seem like a rookie anymore, and his battle instincts were growing sharper by the day. Except, although I felt that way, I also felt a little melancholy. I knew we didn’t have many days left together.
Think logically without being swept up in emotion.

This was the first full-time party I had formed in this strange world. I had decided to avoid showing affection to the people here as much as possible, but being human, that wasn’t up to my brain to decide. I was sure I’d remember this team for a long time.
Step.
When my thoughts reached that point, I suddenly sensed a presence. I lifted my head slightly to check, and it was Rotmiller. “Did I wake you up?” he asked.
“No, I woke up earlier.”
“Then I’m glad. I thought you woke up because of me this time too.”
This time too...?

Was it just me, or was there a hidden meaning behind those words? I was sure it wasn’t nothing. Rotmiller was smart. He must have been aware that I’d still been keeping an eye on him even though he’d been pretending not to notice.
“Why don’t we talk, since you’re awake?”
“...Fine.”

I got out of my sleeping bag and sat down against the wall with Rotmiller. There was an awkward silence. Ah, was this the first time the two of us had talked since that day? Feeling suffocated for some reason, I took a piece of beef jerky out of my pocket and chewed on it.
Munch. Munch. Munch.
Yeah, it was a little more bearable with some sound.
Rotmiller, who had asked to speak with me, only opened his mouth after I finished an entire piece of jerky. “...I plan to leave the party after this expedition.”
“You’re leaving the party?” It was abrupt, but not entirely unexpected. I had considered this exact scenario. “It’s because of me.”
“No, because of me.”
Huh? “What does that mean?”

“...Give me one of those.” When I handed over a piece of jerky, Rotmiller gnawed on it and continued. It was a bit of a long story. “I can’t say that the district chief’s proposal has nothing to do with this decision. I can’t claim not to be greedy. To be given a position as a scout in a large clan...? Even though I knew it was a lie, my heart kept pounding. That was the first time I realized that it was time for me to leave this team.

“Ah, but don’t be too hard on yourself. Actually, I’m used to this. The other races... no, those with talent easily rise to the top. I have been a member of many parties over the past eight years, and there have been many times I was left behind because I couldn’t keep up with them. Sometimes I was kicked out, sometimes I left on my own before it got worse. That’s how I’ve survived as an adventurer. But, it wasn’t an easy decision this time.”
I spoke up for the first time. “How so?”

Rotmiller replied with a grin. “Because I care for you guys. I knew it was time to leave, but I hated to admit it. So I tried to hide what happened with the district chief and participate in this expedition anyway. I wished this adventure could last even a little longer. But...” Rotmiller swallowed the jerky he was slowly chewing on. “Everything has to come to an end eventually.”
Those words left me speechless. Rotmiller stared straight ahead and said nothing as if he was waiting for some kind of an answer. Then the alarm went off, and the others started to stir one by one.
“It is time for everyone to wake up. I’ll be on my way, so you get ready to leave too.”
Rotmiller left to pack his sleeping bag. I took my watch out of my pocket. It was eight a.m., time for the nineteenth day’s adventure to begin.

Rotmiller was like me in many ways. He tried not to give others his affection, but he felt affection anyway. He nevertheless made logical decisions without being swept up in it. The only difference was that I just did this for myself, while this man was doing it for us.

It wasn’t that I didn’t have altruistic persuasions, though. If I continued moving up with these guys, the game would only end once someone died. So before that, I wanted to end this party with my own hands.
“Bjorn!”

To be honest, the back of my head was tingling. I hadn’t thought Rotmiller would be thinking about something like that. I wondered what he thought of me. What on earth had been going through his head as he felt my watchful gaze on him? Those endless questions ran through my head.
“Bjorrrn! Where has your mind run off to?” Missha shook my shoulder and jolted me from my thoughts. “Stop messing arrround and get packed up.”
“Okay...”
I came to my senses and helped clean up our campsite. Then, after gathering together and having a simple meal, we headed up the stairs.
I’ll tell him when we get back to the city. The two of us are leaving anyway, so there’s no need for him to leave.

My thoughts were jumbled up, but I decided to focus solely on this expedition for now. There were still four days left. We were able to easily defeat rank-six monsters, but the Tower of Heavens was a place where the difficulty level rose dramatically depending on the combination of enemies that appeared. I couldn’t let my guard down until we got back to the city.
[You have completed the ordeal.]
After defeating the latest group of monsters, I froze. But, no, it wasn’t just me.
“...All three routes are Stairs of Destiny,” Rotmiller said.
“What are we going to do? Didn’t you say those could be dangerous?” Dwalkie asked.
Wow, so this really does happen.

chapters.title: Chapter 133: Team Play (3)
paragraphs: The fourth floor, Tower of Heavens, was structured in stages. When you completed an ordeal, the door opened and you chose one of three staircases to advance to the next stage. There were a total of four types of stairs: Courage, Wisdom, Patience, and Destiny.

Up to this point, we hadn’t taken the Stairway of Destiny. For one, its appearance rate was less than 5 percent that of the other stairs. For two, it had way too many unknowns. There was no reason to choose it; at least, until all three doors that appeared were Destiny.
“Mm, does it matter which one we choose? Nothing’s happened to me beforrre. The monster just came out like normal and that was it.”
Of course, Destiny was not necessarily dangerous. As Missha said, most people faced trials of Courage, Wisdom, and Patience when they chose Destiny.
“That must be because you were lucky, Miss Karlstein. I read in a book that it’s random what kind of trial you’ll get,” said Dwalkie.

The problem was that there was a 20 percent chance that you would go through an entirely different type of ordeal. A total of thirty-two possibilities existed in the game: getting sent back to the first floor, rank-five monsters appearing, suddenly being locked in a closed room, etcetera.
It’s disgustingly hard and the rewards are sparse. Some ordeals are made deliberately to fuck with you.
So, unless you were after some special reward, if you came to hunt, Destiny was an ordeal you had to pass on. Well, that was usually the case, anyway.

While I was getting my thoughts in order, the team members who were discussing what to do asked for my opinion. “Bjorn, why are you staying quiet?” said Hikurod. “We agreed that it’s better to enter any one of them. It’d be a shame to waste the remaining days.”
I nodded in agreement. “That is true.”

On the second half of the fourth floor, at our current rate, we could mine up to three hundred thousand stones in four days. Not before dividing by five, but per person. Since most of our time since entering the labyrinth had been taken up by travel, each day spent here directly impacted our total income. Yes, their logic made sense.
There’s no way they know what this means.

On the fourth floor, three Stairways of Destiny almost never opened at the same time. If they did, it meant one thing: you had reached a special stage. It was then possible for you to enter one of three hidden levels.
The probability should be one in three.
I looked at the three doors and pondered which one to choose. Then I realized something and laughed. “Missha.”
“Yeah?”
“You choose where to go.” I obviously couldn’t be the one to choose.

Missha glanced at the rest of them as if to ask for their opinions, but all three just shrugged their shoulders in a way that suggested they trusted whatever Missha chose. “Ah, this is a lot of prrressure...” Eventually Missha sighed, glared at me, and approached an open door. It was the door located directly in front of the stairs we’d climbed. “I’m warning you, I can’t guarrrantee there won’t be a weird monster inside.”
Missha made a disclaimer, to which the dwarf giggled. “Hahaha, what do you mean? Are you trying to avoid taking responsibility?”
“...What? You rrridiculous dwarf!”
“H-Hikurod, that’s enough. You’re making Miss Karlstein uncomfortable...”
Team Half-Wit’s signature bickering routine played out three times a day. Sighing and looking to the side, meeting eyes and awkwardly laughing with Rotmiller—it was the same as usual.
“Now, now. Why don’t we get a move on?” When Rotmiller took the lead and cleared the air, everyone stopped talking and got in formation.
Bang!

The moment we all entered through the door together, it closed and darkness descended. It was difficult to see even an inch ahead in the pitch blackness. Courage, Wisdom, Patience... everyone was taken aback as we entered a stairway that was different from all others.

Rotmiller soon shared the most critical piece of information for any adventurer when faced with an unfamiliar environment. “I don’t sense any enemies right now.” Then, he warned, “Stay put. There may be traps.”
Despite it all, he was a great scout. He must have almost instantaneously assessed what it was he needed to do.
Of course, the dwarf was no different. “Bjorn, I’ll take care of the rear, so just pay attention to the front.” His tone was serious, bereft of all laughter.

The moment their voices rang out almost simultaneously, the darkness dissipated. The straight path ahead of us branched out in all directions like a maze. Torches hung on the wall at regular intervals, creating an eerie atmosphere.
I quickly surveyed my surroundings and came to a conclusion.
[You have entered the Labyrinth of Larcaz.]
This was one of the three hidden levels in the Tower of Heavens. Even a scout couldn’t show off their skills in this maze.
[Field Effect – Guardian of Balance has activated. The stats of the occupants have been evenly distributed.]
The characters’ total stats and abilities were redistributed according to the number of people.
“W-What the hell! What is this? Did I choose the wrong one? Rotmiller!” Missha looked around and glanced at Rotmiller with an uneasy expression on her face.
He couldn’t answer her, though. “I’m sorry. I’ve never heard of something like this happening, either.”
“N-Neither have I. I’ve never heard of something in the trials of Destiny that would lead adventurers to a place like this.”
“Ahh, it won’t be dangerous... rrright?”

At Missha’s words, everyone kept quiet. That was only natural. It was very ironic, but the unknown was the most terrifying thing there was to an adventurer. A cold silence fell over us, but it didn’t last long. The rest began speaking urgently like the silence hadn’t existed in the first place.
“...How about we stay put right here? There are only four days left, so we’ll just have to wait it out.”
“We don’t know how this space works yet. If it has a structure similar to a Rift...”
“Then that means after four days we’ll be trapped here foreverrr!”

All sorts of speculations and worries poured out. Well, who would’ve ever suspected a place like this would exist on the fourth floor instead of the fifth, which was known to have no knowledge available to the public?
Pretending not to know anything, I offered, “Why don’t we check how we feel first?”
“Yeah?”
“Missha, is there anything different about you?”
“Ah, now that you mention it... I feel like my body is strangely lighterrr?” Missha hesitantly replied.
“Hmm, I don’t know. Maybe you’re mistaken?” Hikurod didn’t feel any change, probably because he was right in the middle of the pack in terms of stat distribution.
“She’s not wrong,” said Rotmiller. “I feel so energized, there’s no way I could be mistaken.”
“M-Me too. My mana has increased significantly. Right now, not even rank-six magic seems like it would be too difficult. What the hell is going on?”
What do you think? That all came out of my muscles. Although I only have three essences, they all have ridiculously high stats. Damn communism. How much muscle did I lose?
I leaned my now-heavy mace on the floor to distribute its weight. The first to notice this behavior was Missha. “Bjorn? Are you hurt?”
“My body feels strange. For some reason, I can’t use my strength.”
“What?”
As Missha worriedly approached me, Rotmiller made a guess. “It’s clear that there’s some kind of a special condition at play here. This probably isn’t a space where everyone becomes stronger.”
“Condition?” I asked, deciding to throw in a hint. “What condition would make me weak and you guys strong? This isn’t fair!”
Then, as expected, Rotmiller came up with a fairly plausible hypothesis. “Maybe our abilities are mixed up...”
“Hmm? What does that mean?” asked Missha.
“I’m not sure yet, so I’ll tell you later when I’ve sorted it out.”

Well, I figured that was enough for these guys to puzzle it out without me having to step forward. I nudged us toward the next issue. There was no time to be idling around. “Then what are we going to do now?”
“Bjorn, what do you think?”
“I think we should explore this place and find a way out.”
“Your reason?”
I answered without hesitation. “If this place is special, that must mean the reward is just as great.”
“A very adventurer-like point of view.”
Despite Rotmiller’s comment, I proudly straightened my shoulders. No matter what they said, wasn’t money an adventurers’ ultimate goal? It was their one surefire motivation.
“True. We might get trrrapped here in four days, so just standing here probably isn’t a good idea...”
“Hahaha, aren’t we explorers? It would make sense to explore our surroundings, even if it’s slow going.”

There was even a small bit of enthusiasm in the eyes of the trio despite their nerves and anxiety. Of course, Dwalkie’s words were the deciding factor. “A-Ah! This just came to mind, but this might be an arrangement created by the last Great Sage!”
“What? Are you talking about Gabrielius?”
“It’s... definitely a possibility. Considering that three Stairways of Destiny appeared at the same time, and then we appeared in this strange place too...”
The Arrangement of Gabrielius was, to put it simply, how the people here referred to what I called a “hidden level.”
“Yes!” the dwarf shouted ambitiously. “Aren’t we on the fourth floor, anyway? It’s not like any ridiculous monsters will appear!”
With four days left until the labyrinth closed, that was how Team Half-Wit’s final quest began.
The Labyrinth of Larcaz wasn’t the hidden level I had really wanted Missha to pick, although it had the greatest final reward out of the three.
It will be difficult to crack it in four days.

Due to the nature of the labyrinth, it took a long time. Finding the boss was one thing, but defeating it with our current combat power would require a lot of groundwork. So, I decided not to overdo it. Contrary to their concerns, this was not a place you’d be trapped in if you couldn’t clear it in time, like a Rift. And even if we didn’t clear it, attractive rewards were scattered throughout this maze.
“Then let’s go.”
After taking up a formation we had created for moments like these, we stepped into the maze.
“I think we can keep going.”
I stood at the lead, and Rotmiller followed close behind me to look out for any traps. Hikurod stood at the very back of the pack, because monsters didn’t just appear from the front here.
“Miss Karlstein, don’t worry,” said Dwalkie. “I will stay by your side and protect you.”
“What are you talking about? I should be the one prrrotecting you.”
“Haha, then let’s protect each other.”
“...Whatever you say.”

In a place like this, our team’s two main damage dealers were located in the center. It was the safest position, and they also had to be able to support either the front or back of the group depending on the situation.
“Meg, Meeg, Meeg!” It must have been about three minutes after we officially started the expedition that a monster appeared at a crossroads. This was the first reward of Larcaz’s Labyrinth.
“I’ve never seen that monster before. Bjorn, be careful.”

An unknown monster: that alone was a boon to us. In Dungeon and Stone, even if you killed all the monsters on the fourth floor, you couldn’t get to level five. It was a contradiction. You needed at least five rank-six or seven essences to be able to hunt consistently on the fifth floor, but you couldn’t reach level five without going up there.
This is why there are no newbies.

I figured you couldn’t call someone a newbie if they were on the fifth floor. I shook off any unnecessary questions and gripped my shield with both hands. It was a bit awkward without a mace, but that was too heavy for me to wield with my current strength, so I put it in my backpack. I decided it was better to just leave the damage to the damage dealers.
“Mehhg!” Spotting us in the distance, the hesitant monster roared and charged at me.
At that exact moment, Dwalkie shouted, “Oh, I’ve seen that one in a book! Vaikundus!”

Vaikundus was a rank-six monster. The easiest way to describe it was as a mountain goat that walked on two legs. Including those dignified horns, its height reached about eight feet. Its weapon was a super-long halberd held between two tight fists.
Bam!

As the halberd struck down on the shield, the heavy impact jolted through my whole body. I began to think it had been a good idea to leave the mace behind. If I’d been one-handed right then, it would have been hard for me to stay standing.
Goddamn it.
Was it because I had shared my precious physique stats with my teammates? It felt like I was dealing with a rank-five monster, not a rank-six. Well, the battle itself wasn’t difficult, though.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight attack spell Freeze Enhancement.]
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight attack spell Ice Lance.]

While I parried the goat’s attack, Dwalkie prepared a single specialized attack spell. “Bjorn!” Soon, Dwalkie called out to me, and I immediately dove to the side just like we always practiced. Up to this point, it was business as usual.
Shoooooot!

But what was this? The size of the Ice Lance that passed me by was different. Even the wind it left behind was enough to leave me cold. And, of course, the results when it hit were also different than usual.
Kwaaang!
It wouldn’t be strange to call it a fireball instead of an Ice Lance.

“Huh?” Missha, who had been waiting for the right time to add to the combo, let out a questioning noise. This was understandable. The Vaikundus, a rank-six monster, had already turned into light and disappeared.
[You have killed a Vaikundus. EXP +4]
No wonder my physique stats had decreased tremendously. It must have been because everything had been converted into mana for Dwalkie.
“This is my magic...?” As I watched him muttering to himself, it hit me that here, he was no longer a half-wit.
That changes things.
It didn’t seem like a bad idea to aim for a Level Clear.

chapters.title: Chapter 134: Team Play (4)
paragraphs: We were wandering through a maze. No breadcrumbs or balls of yarn, but that was okay because we had Rotmiller.
“Wait, I’ll leave one more mark here just in case.”

In the past, I wondered what use a scout was in places where even a guide couldn’t find the way, but that had been arrogance on my part. Having built himself up from the bottom step by step, Rotmiller was a truly versatile man.
“Can I see the map?”
“Sure.”

He was making a map based on the path we were taking. It wasn’t just a crudely made map either, but an elaborate one reminiscent of a mini map. Just by pausing every ten minutes to draw, he had been able to make this.
“Okay, it’s done, so give it to me. I need to update the map.”
“...Here.”
Each time I watched Rotmiller move his pen over the map without hesitation, I was amazed. I didn’t ask how this was possible, though, because he had already explained it earlier.
“The terrain here is not too complicated, so I can memorize it just by walking. To measure distance, I can count my steps and note it down accordingly.”

Apparently, map-making and surveying were what he was most confident in since he’d been doing both for several years. I never realized this man had such talent. It was a bit unfortunate. Rather than a talent, this must have been the result of years of hard work as someone without an innate aptitude.
“Sorry for taking up time. Let’s go.”

After stopping for about thirty seconds, we walked through the dark maze again. Rotmiller followed close behind. In his hand was not a crossbow, but a longsword. It was a change that had come about after several battles.
“This should be enough to hold off one of them.”
Rotmiller, whose stats had risen, began to actively intervene in battle, just like the top scouts usually did to pull their weight in ways other than just navigating.
“This one’s all yours.”

After a warning from Rotmiller, who had an enhanced sense of smell, four Vaikundus appeared in front of us. Four rank-six monsters was a number I’d never dealt with on the fourth floor, but I wasn’t particularly nervous or anxious. We had Dwalkie.
Shoooooot!
An Enhanced Ice Spear was launched as soon as the monsters appeared. Even this was different than before. Then came two Ice Lances that were several times stronger than usual.
I didn’t realize he could double cast.
When I found out about this, I felt a bit embarrassed. Despite having been together for several months, I didn’t really know much about them at all.
Goddamn it.
Despite having abnormally low mana, Dwalkie’s talent in magic was considerable enough that he was able to use additional support magic while double casting.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight attack spell Trajectory Adjustment.]
Ice spears flew over our heads like cannonballs fired from somewhere in the distance. We didn’t even have to step aside to make room.
Kaboom!
Before the battle even started, two of the rank-six monsters turned into light and disappeared.
“Get rid of them and push forward. I’ll take one of them with Missha again.”
While I marked one of the monsters, Missha and Rotmiller teamed up to take on the other.
Shoooooot!
Around the time they killed one, Dwalkie finished chanting again and an Ice Lance shattered the head of the Vaikundus that had been knocking me down. This all took about four minutes.
“Bjorrrn, what are you doing? Let’s go.”
I cleared my head and started walking.
“Hahaha, no matter what appears, don’t worry. I, Riol Warb Dwalkie, will take care of it.” This was the last notable change to Team Half-Wit. Dwalkie became a douchebag again.

Usually, wizards benefited most from the Guardian of Balance field effect because wizards couldn’t consume essences. This inevitably meant that their main stat, mana, had no choice but to skyrocket under its effects.
There’s still a limit to that.

This was the first time I had ever seen such an extreme case as Dwalkie. However, when I thought about it, the change made sense. All the wizards I had brought here with me in the game were talented, so they had high magic-related stats—unlike Dwalkie, the former half-wit wizard.
“It really feels magical. Like all my shackles have been released.”
Dwalkie was human and he had a body that was far from fit. Moreover, his mana was at rock bottom, forget average.
His stats alone were three times lower than ours.

I didn’t know if it would be different for a team of all humans, but between me, Missha, and Hikurod, we had three different races with naturally high base stats on the team. As for Rotmiller? Although he was at a disadvantage, he couldn’t be compared to Dwalkie since he was a veteran with four essences.
...Did our stats somehow all go to the wizard?
After taking the entire day to observe, I finished analyzing the team’s strengths. I was the one who had suffered the most.
Could things really have worked out so well?

Looking at the team as a whole, it had become at least twice as strong. Because Dungeon and Stone was a team battle game, rather than one person being particularly exceptional, things were best when everyone was able to pull their weight. It was a bit bittersweet, but that was also why I wanted to leave Team Half-Wit.
This will be our first and last proper team play.

Today I had been able to see something I hadn’t ever seen in both Rotmiller and Dwalkie, but this changed nothing. With a lot of effort and luck, it would be possible for the two of them to permanently reach the level they were at today.
However, it would take several years.

Besides, that would be their peak. In that sense, their weaknesses were too clear. Rotmiller’s combat power could be compensated for with essences. However, in order to execute the kind of strategies that I wanted, I would need a scout with the Guide ability from the fifth floor onward. Dwalkie? Double casting or not, a wizard’s most important quality was their mana stat. That was probably why he hadn’t been accepted into the Magic Tower. It was a cold-hearted assessment, but according to the Magic Tower’s standards, Dwalkie’s talent was nothing special.
Just as I was thinking that, my heart suddenly froze. Not just metaphorically, but literally.
[You have taken Cold damage.]
A chill cut through my skin and bones. When I came to my senses, Missha was snorting. “Hey, Bjorn! How long are you going to ignorrre me!?”
“Oh, what did you say?”
“What did I say?! I said everyone is going to sleep, so keep watch!” After landing some punches on my chest in annoyance, Missha softened her tone, clearly worried. “But... are you all rrright?”
“I’m fine. It’s still cold, but it doesn’t hurt.”
“No, not that... You’ve had a serious look on your face since earlier.”
I cocked my head in genuine confusion. “I have?”
“Yeah. It’s hard to explain in words, but... oh! It was kind of like the face you make when I tell you to eat your carrrots.”
Uh, that just makes it harder to understand.
“Whatever, just go to sleep. I’ll keep watch, so don’t worry.”
“Mm, okay.” Missha went back to her spot, slipped into her sleeping bag, and chatted with our other teammates. “Ugh, today was rrreally tiring.”
“Haha, understandable. Dragged into unknown territory and fighting all those rank-six monsters...”

“...Maybe I shouldn’t say this, but I kind of had fun. It felt like being on a proper expedition for the first time. Up until now, the expeditions I’ve been on have been different from the one I’ve longed for.”
“Ah, I think I know what you mean, Rotmillerrr.”
“Haha, I felt like an adventurer in a story.”
A few words were exchanged as they lay down at the day’s end. Of course, the conversation didn’t last long as this was meant to be a time of rest.
“Oh, right. Dwalkie, you werrre amazing today.”
“I-It wasn’t a big deal. Being able to shoot spells without having to conserve mana or figure out the formula over and over again? A-Any wizard could’ve done that.”
“Uh... rrreally? I don’t know about that. Anyway, you worked hard today. Good night.”
“G-Good night, Miss Karlstein.”
After the sparse conversation ended, silence descended. It was 1:04 a.m. An hour had passed since the start of the twentieth day. I kept an eye on our surroundings while reviewing my plans.
I’ll be able to get that item in a few more hours, so now I just need to find the boss’s lair.

With our current strength, the boss fight didn’t seem like it would be too much trouble, so I wasn’t overly worried. However, the downside was that if we were unlucky, we might not be able to reach the boss’s lair in time.
If we had just a week more, we could’ve taken everything we needed...
While I was licking my lips in disappointment, I turned my head at the sound of rustling. It was Dwalkie, who had risen from his sleeping bag. “Um, Bjorn...”
“Sleep, even if you can’t. Tomorrow—”
“It’s not that I can’t sleep.” Before I had time to say anything, Dwalkie stood up and came toward me. He lowered his voice so that the others wouldn’t wake up. “I have something to tell you.”
Yesterday it was Rotmiller, so it seemed it was Dwalkie’s turn this time. “...Say it.”
“Remember what you said about Miss Karlstein’s taste the other day?”
“I remember.” I never forgot a lie once I told it. That way there wouldn’t be any discrepancies later. That wasn’t relevant right now, though. “So, what do you want to say?”

As I stared at him, Dwalkie opened his mouth with a determined look on his face. “I was going to ask if what you said was true. But now that I think about it, it doesn’t matter if it’s true or not.” Dwalkie’s voice was different from usual. There was not the slightest hint of a tremor, and the eyes looking up at me were also firm. “Whatever her tastes are, it’s fine. It would be cowardly to wish for her to be honest without showing my true self.”
“...What do you mean by that?”
“You should know that I have been secretly infatuated with her.”
Ha, so this was how it was going to go. I wished he’d at least wait until we were back in the city.
“If we survive this and get back to the city—”
“Stop.” I hurriedly cut Dwalkie off. There was a distinct difference between thinking that and saying it out loud.

However, he seemed to have misunderstood my sincere concern. “As expected, Bjorn, you also...” Dwalkie pressed his lips together and shook his head as if to shake off his thoughts. When he spoke again, his voice was firmer than ever before. “Still, this doesn’t change anything.”
“Stop talking. I know what you misunderstood—”
“When I return to the city, I will reveal my feelings.”
No, that’s a flag. Goddamn it.
Suddenly, I started to feel as anxious as when I met Hans.

“That’s all I had to say. I’ll go now.” Dwalkie then turned around and ran away to bury himself in his sleeping bag. Soon after, his breaths evened out. I had been worried that he wasted his precious sleep for this, but it seemed today’s journey had been pretty tiring after all.
...At least he’s not planning on proposing.
I tried to shake off my worries too and focus on my watch. Two more hours passed like that, and after waking up Hikurod for his shift, I lay down.
When I opened my eyes again, it was time to leave. For tonight, we had decided that just the dwarf and I would be on watch for four hours at a time.
“Both of you must be tired, but you worked harrrd.”
“Haha, well, it can’t be helped. There is not much time left now.”
“Tomorrow is my and Rotmiller’s turrrn, so after today you can get some rest.”

We sufficiently cleaned up camp and resumed our journey. Today’s goal was clear. Rotmiller summarized: “As Bjorn said, it seems that we have reached the outer walls of the maze. From now on, we’ll go in just one direction along this wall.”

In a corner of the Labyrinth of Larcaz was a square structure. We needed to defeat the mid-level boss there and get a hidden reward. For reference, I didn’t know which of the four mini-bosses would come out. It had always been random in the game.
Whatever shows up, though, we can easily take it down with our current combat power. Aside from that one guy, they all have obvious weaknesses.
“Mehhg!”

We sped up while defeating even more Vaikundus, which we had probably already defeated hundreds of. There was still no sign of an essence coming out, though. Instead, our mana stones were piling up high.
“Hahaha! Just the mana stones alone are a nice reward.”

In fact, this was the second gift the labyrinth granted its visitors. There was no place on the fifth floor where a single type of rank-six monster spawned over and over for easy hunting. On the fourth floor, it was normally difficult to encounter even twenty of them in a day.
After traveling for about twelve hours, we reached our destination, a point in the corner of the maze.
“...A dead end?”
“No way, there rrreally is nothing here.”
“It could be in another direction, or in a completely random place.”
“Haha, there has to be a way out, right?”
“There must be, since this is a maze.”
As the group reached the dead-end wall and each made a comment, Rotmiller studied the wall carefully. “Wait a minute,” he muttered, “something’s strange.”

I was honestly a bit surprised. Was it because of the Sixth Sense stat attached to the Mimic’s essence, or was it just this old-timer’s observational skills? I didn’t know the exact cause, but thanks to this, I wouldn’t have to step forward pretending I had found it by coincidence.
Click, rattle.
When he touched something, the wall slid to the side to reveal a hidden space.
“Wow, the doorrr is open.”
“It could be dangerous, everyone back away!”
Hikurod jumped forward and raised his shield, and I was quick to join him. Of course, no monsters suddenly popped out.
“...I guess nothing is coming out.”
This was not that kind of place. The space inside the wall was obscured by darkness, making it impossible to see inside with the naked eye. But none of that mattered to me.
“I will take the lead.”
“Bjorn! It could be dangerrrous!”
“I’m fine. That is my role.”
When I stepped forward instead of the hesitant-looking dwarf and went inside, the torches on the wall lit up the hall at once. I quickly examined my surroundings.
“This is...”
There was a stone chamber of about four square miles, a magic circle with geometric patterns drawn on the floor, and a pole with a goat’s head adorning it.
“This place is kind of freaky...”
“I don’t see a portal here. Can’t we just leave?”
Hearing Missha and Dwalkie’s muttering, I hid a smile. Well, they didn’t know that compared to the other rooms, this was nothing.
Anyway, since we got this room, finding the boss’s lair will be a piece of cake. As for how to do it, I can just give Rotmiller some hints...
That took a weight off. It would make it a bit more difficult to take the boss down, but if we had been unlucky, the quest could’ve ended without us ever seeing the boss’s face.
How do I summon him? If I just do it, it would look very suspicious.
I was happily thinking it over when everyone, including me, flinched at the same time.
“Huh?”
“...You too?”
I wasn’t the only one who sensed the change.
“What is this? My mana suddenly increased tremendously.”
“M-Mine too. Why is my body like this?”

The slightly burdensome pressure of my heavy armor after my loss in strength stats vanished, and it now felt almost like I was wearing the Styrofoam armor people used in cosplay. What was happening? As soon as I realized, curse words flew out.
What the f—!?
Energy had rushed into my whole body, the sort of change that I couldn’t manage even with Giantization. And I already knew the reason why.
“Rotmiller.”
“...You seem to be thinking the same thing as me.”
Another adventurer had entered this place.
The hidden level on the fourth floor, the Labyrinth of Larcaz, allowed a minimum of one to a maximum of five people to enter.
Common sense suggested that it would most likely be a party of five, but it was still too soon to be sure. Anything was possible. But at least one thing was certain.
[Field Effect – Guardian of Balance has activated. The stats of the occupants have been evenly distributed.]
Whether it was one person or several, they were frighteningly strong.

chapters.title: Chapter 135: Orcules (1)
paragraphs: Our assessment of the field effect, Guardian of Balance, was already complete. The abilities of those who entered the maze were distributed equally. All of our party members had agreed with the hypothesis Rotmiller, given various hints from me, had come up with, so unnecessary explanations weren’t necessary.
“Perhaps other adventurers have entered this labyrinth.”
“Other adventurers? But you can’t encounter other adventurers in the Tower of Heavens,” Hikurod muttered, clearly confused.
“Murad, you should know that our current situation is not normal.”

The fourth floor’s Tower of Heavens was an independent area. Unless several parties entered at the same time, no matter how much you wandered around, you would not come across another party. However, the place we were currently in was one the outside world didn’t know anything about.
“Anything could happen here.”
The unknown, the not yet known, meant that all possibilities were plausible.
“I understand. But maybe our guesses are wrong. Maybe some other effect gets triggered when someone just enters this space—”

Dismissing another possibility from Hikurod, I said firmly, “That seems like too much of a stretch.” Of course, this hidden level wasn’t an unknown to me. It would be better to quickly sort things out and move on to the next task without wasting time. “I think Rotmiller’s guess is correct. Dwalkie, what about you?”
“...I also think that’s more plausible.”
“So you agree. Missha, you?”
“Uhh... I’m just going to stay quiet.” Missha abstained. However, since we had already gotten the three votes needed for a majority, I didn’t force her to choose.
“Okay, then we’ve reached a decision. For now, let’s operate under the assumption that Rotmiller’s hypothesis is true. If you have any complaints, speak up now.”
“...There are none.” After the puppet leader dwarf gave a sullen nod, I quickly settled the matter.

Another adventurer had entered the maze, and they were stronger than us. It felt like my stats had doubled, so I was sure it was an adventurer active on the sixth floor or higher—not with a clan, but in a party unit. If so, what should we do now? Our party’s members each gave their opinions on the topic once I raised it, and I took advantage of the opportunity to fulfill the condition to summon the mini-boss.
[The devil in the labyrinth has detected blood.]
Okay, that just needs a little longer to work.
“Hmm, does it really matterrr? I think it would be better to join forces to find a way out...”
“We don’t know what kind of adventurers they are. Why don’t we just stay here? There is no guarantee that we will be trapped once the labyrinth closes.”

“Haha! My friend, what are you so worried about? Even if they are stronger than us, isn’t this a special situation? Even if we run into each other, they won’t be able to do anything to us so easily, so let’s just proceed as we normally would.”
“Um, but just in case, it would be best to avoid them as much as possible and find a way out.”

I smiled cynically. I wondered if they would say something useful, so I listened carefully while I waited. As expected, their collective intelligence did not amount to much. Rotmiller was at least better, but while he may have been skilled at preparing for different possibilities, he didn’t have the worst-case scenario in mind.
“Bjorn, what do you think?”
Eyes turned to me at that question. I finally gathered my thoughts and spoke. “I don’t think this is a coincidence, either.”
“What do you think it is, then?”
“An adventurering party with this much power on the fourth floor at this time? Wouldn’t it make sense to assume that they were wandering around with a goal in mind?”
“You mean they could have been trying to reach this area from the start?”
“Yes. And if so, they must have noticed our presence by now.”
Maybe they would see the marks we left behind and come after us. No, even if they didn’t use those, there might be a way for them to track us.
Dwalkie was in denial. “Ah, no way, h-how can that be? To think they knew about this place already...”
The dwarf also laughed it off. “Haha, even so, you’re talking as if they’re plunderers already.”
Rotmiller, for his part, just asked a serious question. “So what do you think is the best course of action?”

These people were unknowns—therefore, all possibilities were on the table. This could be good luck, or it could lead me to my death. Therefore, even if I seemed strange to my colleagues, I had to assume the worst. “We have to get out of here,” I answered.
Thump!
Not ignoring the foreboding feeling in my heart was the secret to my survival.
[You have killed Baphomet. EXP +5.]
[Higher-class mutant bonus. EXP +1]
We ran through the maze, not lost, but properly heading toward our destination.
“This way!”

Rotmiller, who followed close behind me, held a map in his hand. It wasn’t the map he had been working hard on up until now, but a map that detailed the layout of the entire maze. Of course, the location of the boss room was also written on it since it was loot we had obtained by defeating Baphomet, the mini-boss.
I didn’t expect to take it down that easily.

Baphomet had been summoned right when I finished talking. Normally, it would have been a close battle won by attacking his weak points, but it ended up taking less than a minute. It had been possible to just flatten him with pure damage. It didn’t feel all that great to call this a good thing.
How strong are they usually?
We had unknown, uninvited guests. I had long since thrown out the idea that it could just be one person. No matter how strong an individual was, there were limits.
Sprint!

I cleared my mind and sped up. Since everyone seemed to be keeping pace, I thought that would be okay. In fact, when I peeked behind me, even Hikurod, who lacked endurance, was running fine with Dwalkie on his back. Deciding to stop worrying, I smashed the head of the Vaikundus that jumped out in front of us.
“Mehhg!”
Of course, it staggered heavily, but did not die in one hit. However, I passed the reeling monster without slowing down. Missha had decided to take care of the cannon fodder for us.
Slice!
Light flashed in tune with the pop of exploding flesh. However, there was no accompanying sound of a mana stone dropping. It seemed Missha had caught it in the air again.
“Go left!”

I followed Rotmiller’s instructions and turned. Then, I spotted four Vaikundus in the distance. To be honest, Missha, Rotmiller, and I could get rid of them ourselves now, but it would be nice to save even a second of time.
“Dwalkie!”
At my cry, Dwalkie got off the dwarf’s back and cast a spell.
Shhhhhh!

Cold Storm—a rank-seven attack spell that dealt damage to a wide area instead of a single target. The spell was originally used against rank-eight or nine trash mobs or in the lead-up to a combo move from Missha.
“Meh... g?”

A blizzard of hailstones shot down the corridor, freezing the four Vaikundus. The rank-six monsters had received not only the Frostbite but the Frozen status with just one spell. However, they’d be released from that state in a few seconds.
Bam!

I quickly crushed them with my mace and we kept moving. Whenever we decided that we needed a break, we sprawled out in the passageway to catch our breaths. Time passed like that, and it was time to take a third break.

“Huff, huff... Bjorn, aren’t we rushing too much? I don’t think we have to be in such a hurry.” Hikurod breathed in and out and carefully vented the displeasure he had been holding back. I had somewhat expected it.
My first-ever request had been this: “I keep getting that ominous feeling. So, please. Trust me this once.”
The others did their best to be accommodating.
