“...Well, you have good instincts, anyway.”
“I-I don’t mind. And Bjorn, don’t think I’ve repaid my debt with this. I intend to properly pay it back later.”
As time passed, however, they began to question that decision.
“I-I also think this is good enough,” Dwalkie was saying now. “It seems like a stretch to say that they knew about this maze in the first place too...”

Wasn’t it more likely that they came here by accident like we did? And even if that weren’t the case, could they really be plunderers? Wasn’t believing they would deliberately hunt us down to harm us more of a stretch?
“If you are worried about the marks we left behind, we can start moving more slowly. Even if they are plunderers, they won’t be able to find us in a place like this.”
“To be honest, I’m not sure why you’re so certain there’s an exit here, either.”
Above all, what was the guarantee that there would be a way to escape in a room that may or may not be the boss’s lair?
“Mm, I have no complaints. You know that, rrright? I mean it. Hmm?”

These were all reasonable questions because they hadn’t had the same experiences as me. Hidden levels weren’t all that special. Just look at Jencia, whom we met in Glacier Cave not too long ago. She had opened the Rift through a hidden element. In addition, in Ghostbusters, information was exchanged every month and knowledge of hidden elements spread.
“Bjorn, you are not acting like yourself today. Even if everything you say is true, why not fight back?” Hikurod said persuasively, but that was the biggest problem.

The fact that Guardian of Balance was active? That still changed nothing. A situation where we’d normally get fucking crushed was now just a situation where we’d get crushed a normal amount. That was it. Even if our stats were the same as our opponents’, there was a difference in skill, ranks, and number of essences. With items, that gap would be even wider.
If we fight, we will definitely lose.
That was the source of my anxiety.
Thump!
A lion could afford not to care about a rabbit. But a rabbit, if it encountered a lion, had to run.
“There is no time for this. If you’re done resting, let’s go.”

“The Labyrinth of Larcaz...” muttered the man standing in the middle of the stone chamber. The man took off the hood that covered his face and approached the wall, then carefully swept the stone. “We’re finally here.” The corners of his mouth twisted up, and his burn-scarred skin crinkled. Anyone could see that he was genuinely happy.

“Lord, why have you given wings to such an evil person?!” an old man in black, priestly robes lamented, closing his eyes. To ask if this was truly god’s intention, throwing a meaningless question out into the air was the only thing he could do.
“Old man, do I need to pluck out your tongue?”
“How can I be afraid of you? Physical pain is—”
“Oh, of course, I meant your grandson’s tongue.”

As the old man shut his mouth, the burned man giggled and directed his gaze to the floor. His eyes landed on a middle-aged adventurer who was curled up on the ground like a shrimp. Cold sweat had broken out on his forehead, and his parted lips trembled as he let out a pained moan. “It’s just an arm, don’t exaggerate.”
The man laughed at the adventurer’s severed shoulder. Who would have known that there was a way to get inside the place that he had been searching for for an entire year?
“To show us the way just because it was offered the arm of a rank-five adventurer... that evil god is a funny guy.”
“Isn’t he...your teammate?”
“Teammate? I just brought him here because he’s useful. Hey, get up. We’re late, we don’t have time.”

As the burned man propped his foot on the adventurer’s waist and shook him, deep creases formed between the old man’s eyebrows. “Stop it. He has offered a body part to the evil god. The pain he is experiencing must be beyond imagination—”
“That’s enough, old man.”

The old man flinched at the burned man’s cold voice. Unable to hide his anger, the old man’s clenched fists shook, but that was all. He was disgusted by his own cowardice as he was forced to be a bystander to such an evil deed. However, the old man had things that he had to protect. Maybe this scout was the same.
“I am okay... high priest.” The scout struggled to get up, grabbing his empty shoulder socket.
The other man nodded in satisfaction. However, something soon occurred to him, and he frowned and repeatedly opened and closed his hand.
Squeeze.

He knew about the Guardian of Balance effect. However, even taking that into account, the changes that had just taken place in his body did not make sense. “Old man, has anything changed? Like your divine power?”
“...It has decreased a bit.”
“Decreased? Not increased? Are you sure?”
“I am sure.”
The man turned his head to stare at the scout. “What about you?”
“Including S-Soul Power, overall, my ph-physique stats are lower...”

“I see.” The man smiled ominously and stared down the passageway. A rank-five scout had lost some of his powers? “It looks like some rats got in first.” His eyes, illuminated by the flickering torch, glowed with a cold light.

chapters.title: Chapter 136: Orcules (2)
paragraphs: Emotions were contagious. Seeing someone cry could make you sad and seeing someone laugh could make you happy. The same went for feelings of fear. Come on, that won’t happen. Even as you were thinking that, you couldn’t help starting to get worried yourself when you saw someone else’s anxiety persist. That was how humans were.
“It feels like something really will happen just because you keep saying that.”
“S-Still, there’s nothing wrong with being careful...”
Thanks to my grave expression, my teammates slowly began to see reality. This was a change I couldn’t help but welcome.

Of course, Rotmiller’s words were the deciding factor here. “My head still isn’t connecting the same dots as you are. But for some reason, I have a feeling that something very bad will happen if I don’t follow your lead.”

Rotmiller, who had absorbed a Mimic’s essence, had a Sixth Sense stat. Team Half-Wit had benefited a lot from that ability. The fact that he was saying this out of nowhere would change how much weight the others gave my argument.
“B-Bjorn. We should keep moving, right?” asked Missha.
“H-Hahaha! Right! That would be best! We’ll just have to suffer for one more day!”
This was a bit frustrating. They wrote my concerns off as paranoia, but one word from Rotmiller and they would move mountains.
Well, the fact that he’s saying that is making me more anxious too...
Sixth Sense was usually literally just a sixth sense. However, with the arrival of our uninvited guests, weren’t we now in a situation where our overall stats had risen tremendously?
Whew, I really need to prepare myself.

It felt like a curtain had been torn back and the danger shrouded behind it revealed. Even as I was assuming the worst, deep down I had hoped this would all end up being paranoia on my part. I supposed that wasn’t going to happen.
Thump!
My heart tightened a little more, but this changed nothing. I was just doing what I could. “Let’s move again.”

After a short break, we started running again. Even though I increased my pace even more than before, everyone followed along without a hint of complaint. We ran through the maze in heavy silence for quite a while.
Then, suddenly, Rotmiller spoke up. “Now that I think about it, I wonder if you, Bjorn, are similar to me.”
“Similar? What do you mean?”
“I received this ability through an essence, but it could be that you innately have a good sixth sense.”

I’d never thought of that before, but the idea wasn’t totally out there. Dungeon and Stone was a game where, when you selected a character, their basic stats were randomly assigned a number within a range of default values.
The default range for Sixth Sense was zero to fifty, I think?

Considering that the Sixth Sense stat attached to the Mimic’s essence was +50, that meant the maximum default value was very high. It wasn’t a main stat like Strength, though, so there was no need to recreate a character to raise this particular stat.
“I’ve thought this for a while, but you’ve always had a sharpness to you.”
“Right! You beat up that Elisa bitch, too, when everyone else was confused because she was a prrriestess.”

Hmm, was that the case? Since everyone else was saying it, I started to believe it could be true. As I mentioned earlier, that was how humans worked. It was possible that Bjorn’s Sixth Sense was naturally high. But that wasn’t something to ponder right now.
“Anyway, keep following me.” I decided to think about this later and instead focused on clearing the way. Everything had a time and place.
Whack!
I wielded my mace.
Shooot!
Dwalkie shot Ice Lances.
Slice!

We continued plowing through the decapitated Vaikundus. After a long while, it was finally past five a.m. on the twenty-first day. Since killing Baphomet, we’d essentially been running almost nonstop for twelve hours.
Pant, pant...

The breaths I exhaled through my nose and mouth were hot. The others had to be in a similar state. I did one final check of how my comrades were faring, and saw that everyone looked exhausted. That made sense—even if their stats had risen, they hadn’t slept for two days.
However, the end was now in sight. “If we turn that way, we’ll reach our destination!”
After running through a long, straight passage, we arrived at our destination: a huge stone chamber, not a cramped, maze-like hallway.
Click!
The moment we entered it, iron bars came down on each of the three entrances that connected to the stone chamber.
“Ahh! We’re trrrapped!”
“Everyone, stay alert! We don’t know what’s going to come out!”

Though caught off guard by the unexpected situation, everyone took formation and prepared for battle. Our eyes naturally settled on one spot in particular, the only place something could come out of—a daunting stone door to one side of the chamber.
“...It won’t be a rank-four monster, rrright?”
[The lord of the labyrinth has sensed a challenger.]
Before long, the geometric patterns engraved on the door began to glow, and it opened.
Drrrrrr.

Soon, from the wide-open stone door appeared a monster with an unmistakable scream. It was about thirteen feet tall with an oversized build to match, and a menacing horn sprouting from the top of its head. It had brown fur short enough to reveal all the blood vessels and muscles bulging under its skin, and hooves supporting its thick thighs.
Boom!
“Moooooo!”
“Minotaur! It’s a Minotaurrr!”

The final boss of the Labyrinth of Larcaz was a monster famous enough for Missha to recognize it straight away. Well, at least the rank-five monster, Minotaur, wasn’t a rank-four monster like she had feared.
Technically it would be something more like rank 4.5.
This guy was different from a regular Minotaur—it was a named monster with the unique title of Larcaz. In other words, it was a high-rank mutant that possessed the skill of another monster.
Boom!

As soon as the monster looked at us and took its first step forward, everyone noticed that it was different. How could they not? It was obvious at a single glance that it had a skill no other Minotaur could use.
“Mmmuh!”
It let out a short breath and raised its arm upwards.
[Larcaz, the owner of the labyrinth, has cast Burning Leather.]
Whooosh!
Huge flames covered the creature’s skin. Even from a hundred feet away, I could feel the heat. Everyone froze, aghast.
“Uh, can this guy wield fire?”
“O-Of course not. There was no such thing in the books.”
“Then it must be a high-rank mutant, like the Baphomet we met in the hidden room on the map.”
“Ah! Come to think of it, that looks like another monster’s special ability!” Dwalkie’s expression lit up and he quickly shared the information he had recalled. “Ifrit! That must be Ifrit’s ability!”

That was the correct answer. It seemed he had been reading tons of labyrinth-related books for the past several months—he definitely seemed more like a proper wizard now. But this was no time for compliments.
“Moooooo!”
The creature looked at us as if to say, Who the hell are these assholes? and then charged forward with thundering footfalls.
Boom! Boom!
The sight of a thirteen-foot-tall monster running at us with its entire body on fire was unreal to say the least. However, it was still nothing compared to Riakis.
“Behelahhh!” I shouted and sprinted forward. The distance between us quickly narrowed. As soon as I entered its reach, a giant double-edged ax came down over my head.
Bam!
Hmm, so that’s how strong you are.
I smirked at the blow that slammed into my shield. It seemed that there was no need to use Giantization. As expected, I could handle Burning Leather.
Whooosh!

Even though red flames swayed right in front of my nose, it didn’t cause me any major damage. Thanks to the Fire Resistance attached to the third stage of the Immortality Imprint, it was just a little hot. Of course, if I continued to stay in this position, that would be a different story.
[You have taken Fire damage. The damage you receive will increase according to duration.]
Fire damage increased in strength as it accumulated. It was a similar principle to how you could cook meat by putting it in hot water for several days. However, there was a simple workaround.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight curse spell Cold Blood. Your Fire Resistance has significantly increased.]
As Dwalkie’s mana permeated my burning body, it cooled. I was a little surprised.
To think he cast a spell before I gave the order.
I supposed people could learn through experience after all. It seemed like just yesterday that he had struggled to aim an Ice Lance properly.
“I’ll help too!”
“Oh, it’s not hot anymore!”
After hesitating at the sight of the fire for just a split second, Hikurod and Missha received buffs and joined the frontlines.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Lightning Attack.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Toxin Bestow.]

We set off electric shocks, cut through the beast’s thick leather with a sword, threw in some deadly poison, and so on. Just like that, we easily handled the creature who filled the final boss role of this labyrinth.
“Mooooo—!”

Of course, it went on a rampage. In a frenzy, it threw its fists, feet, and ax at us, and used its special abilities generously. But nothing changed. It was still too slow to catch Missha, and lacked the strength to take down me and the dwarf.
Through it all, magical support continued.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight curse spell Aggravate.]
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-nine curse spell Slowdown.]
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-seven curse spell Weakening.]

Normally, Dwalkie’s magic support would’ve ended with him getting knocked out from mana depletion after casting Cold Blood alone. Rotmiller was at Dwalkie’s side right now guarding him just in case, but the monster couldn’t even get past a single tank. How would it get all the way to Dwalkie?
Bam!
It didn’t take much time. Soon, Missha cut the monster’s Achilles tendon, sending its huge body to the ground. The battle ended with her sword driven deep into its brain.
[You have killed a Minotaur. EXP +5]
[Higher-class mutant bonus. EXP +1]

The creature’s body suddenly turned into a halo of light and dissolved. The first thing I did was check the time. It was 5:21, less than ten minutes since I last checked. For some reason, I felt a strange sense of regret at the realization.
How nice it would be if everyone was still like this even outside.

If there was a final form of Team Half-Wit, it would probably look like this: a high-stability configuration of two tankers, a close-combat damage dealer who moved boldly and took advantage of that stability to land constant blows, a wizard who possessed high-level long-ranged and one-off damage spells and could support the team no matter the situation, and a scout who wasn’t a burden even in battle.
...What am I thinking?

Pointless musing like this wasn’t my style, especially when I hadn’t even dealt with our actual problem yet. I shook my head to clear my mind and began reprioritizing. What did I need to do right now to save even a little more time?
Quickly take what we need and get out of here.
Shaaaaaa!
The light completely dissolved, and everyone let out a sigh.
“Nothing again.”

The Minotaur did not drop an essence. Well, even though it was a high-ranking mutant, it wasn’t a Rift guardian, so that was more realistic. Welp. If a yellow essence had come out, it could have been quite useful through the second half of the game.
But the real reward is something else.
I tried to shake off my disappointment and examined our surroundings.
Clunk!
As if to announce that the boss battle was over, the bars blocking the passageways went up again.
“And the portal? Why didn’t a portal open?”
“Could it be that this place is different from a Rift?”
“M-Maybe there’s another monster aside from the Minotaur.”

The trio couldn’t hide their bewilderment and threw out various theories. I was about to say something, but Rotmiller spoke up first. “I have a feeling there might be something in there. Why don’t we check it out?” As expected, this man was a natural seeker.
“Oh, rrright! There’s still that area left.”
“Let’s go. Maybe there’s a portal open in there.”

Soon, we went through the door the Minotaur had appeared from. Of course, the portal—which had opened at the starting point—couldn’t possibly be here, but no matter how much of a rush we were in, we should still take the loot. This was something you couldn’t buy with money.
“This... seems like a very spooky place.”
There was a crypt beyond the door. And, like the mini-boss room, there was a summoning circle on the floor.
“I sense great mana from this object,” Dwalkie murmured.
“Then it would be best to take it with us.”

I put the jewel in the center of the magic circle into my backpack. Then, without hesitation, I turned back and headed outside. I also dismissed Dwalkie’s suggestion to investigate the room further, claiming it was creepy. That was because I already knew this was the only reward that was in there.
“Whew, what a headache. The portal isn’t here, either.”
“Right?”
“Rotmiller, it looked like there was a blue dot in the center of the map earlier. Is there any chance that a portal opened there?”
“Actually, I was thinking that too. I have a strong feeling about it.” Was this the Sixth Sense of a scout? I came out of the crypt where the Minotaur had been trapped with that thought in mind.
Then, a strange man’s soft voice rang out from the passageway right in front of us. “See, I knew it.”
The final boss’s lair was always generated at a random location in the maze. As soon as we had gotten the map, we rushed here and defeated the final boss in less than ten minutes.
It probably doesn’t matter how he got here already, though.

What was done was done. There was no way he’d found this place by accident, though; he must have had a relevant ability. Even in a place where the Guide characteristic was useless, essences, items, and other abilities could still be used.
“Look, old man. Didn’t I tell you? If we didn’t cut off another arm, we might’ve missed it.”
Shoving my questions aside for the moment, I focused on what was right in front of me.
Thump!

My heart was pounding wildly. When I first became aware of the existence of our uninvited guests, I had thought that if there were five of them, they’d likely be active on the sixth floor. If there were four, the seventh; three, the eighth. It wasn’t possible, but if there were only two of them, they’d have to be active on the ninth floor. This was a conclusion I had drawn based on the changes to my stats. So which assumption ended up being right? It looked like it was time for me to find out, whether I liked it or not.
“Hey, barbarian, shouldn’t you say thank you? You were able to take that thing down easily thanks to me.” The man was covered in burns, not only on his face but also on his slightly exposed wrists.
An old man in black, priestly clothes began to beg. “Please take the item you want and let them go.”
I didn’t know why, but a middle-aged man with his arms cut off was following behind them, his face blank. There were a total of three people.
Goddamn it.
I scrapped all the plans I had made in case we ran into them, from plan A to plan D.
“Hey, why isn’t anyone talking?”
The gut instinct I had developed after encountering all sorts of sons of bitches was telling me this wasn’t the kind of guy those strategies would work on.

chapters.title: Chapter 137: Orcules (3)
paragraphs: Chills ran down my spine.
“Hey, why isn’t anyone talking?”
Just from that one sentence, even though we hadn’t even properly fought him yet, an urgent roar filled my eardrums.
Thump-thump-thump!

My warrior’s heart, which instinctively sensed that this was a natural predator, was pumping nonstop, driving oxygen through my body. It started preparing for the worst before my head had even processed the situation.
Slide.

In the still silence, the only thing I moved was my eyes so that I could check on my teammates. Everyone was frozen mid-step. They must have also subconsciously sensed the danger this guy was radiating from every pore.
“Hello?” The man frowned and spoke again. “Are you really all going to just stand there?”

Thanks to that, my mind calmed down a bit. Time was money. It wouldn’t do to waste any more of the minutes and seconds that would be so precious from now on. That was why, with open ears and eyes, I faced our opponent and quickly gathered any information that I may have overlooked.
“Hey, barbarian, shouldn’t you say thank you? You were able to take that thing down easily thanks to me.”
This man had known about this place, and as soon as he noticed we were here, he immediately ran to the boss room.
Still, he got here too fast.

To arrive at the same time as us when we were the ones who had the map? That would have been impossible unless he somehow found the exact right path without wandering around at all. How could he have pulled that off?
What kind of a skill is it?
I had to figure that out. Our future plans would shift depending on that information. Looking back, though, it seemed the answer lied in an earlier part of the conversation.
“If we didn’t cut off another arm, we might’ve missed it.”
An offering. And it was obvious whose arm it was. It must have belonged to the poor man behind him.
...He must be a priest of Karui.
This was the silver lining. If he had simply found the way using some sort of scouting ability, we would have had no chance.
“I beg you. Please take the item you want and let them go.”
The old man, whom I presumed was the priest serving the evil god, also didn’t seem to have a very cooperative relationship with his leader.
Could it be that he kidnapped the priest and forced him to change classes? And that the man who offered his arm is in a similar situation?
After calmly analyzing the situation in the span of three breaths, I opened my mouth. I was out of time.
“Well, doesn’t matter,” the leader began, “I’ll just—”
“I never expected to run into another adventurer in a place like this,” I said.
“So you aren’t mute after all?” When I broke the silence, the man looked at me with amusement. Okay, that bought some time.
“Do you know how to get out of here?” I casually asked what he knew. That way I could seem more like a rookie.
Suddenly, though, his voice grew cold. “You... what are you?”
The heck? What did I do wrong?
While I was contemplating this, the man narrowed his eyes. “A yellow light has turned on because of these sons of bitches? Not green?”

Rather than interest or curiosity, his eyes were full of vigilance. Unconsciously, my eyes moved to the ring on his finger. It was studded with green, red, and yellow jewels and was similar to a numbered item I knew—the thing I used to call the Traffic Light Ring. No. 6111: Destiny Seeker.
If it turned green, the situation you were in was positive. A red light meant negative, and the item alerted you to a mix when it flashed yellow. The ring was currently shining a yellow light.
Goddamn it.

Was this what it meant to feel a mix of joy and sorrow? If it was yellow, that meant there was at least some chance of me downing him. This was good news for me. The bad news was that he’d figured that out too.
We’re screwed.
The sole advantage of the weak, to take advantage of the strong’s lack of vigilance, had disappeared because of that damn ring.
“Do you know what this is?” To make matters worse, he even noticed my split-second reaction and immediately showed his true colors.
Ssshing!
He pulled a blade of blue-silvery light from his waist. At that dazzling glow, the wannabe blacksmith reacted first. “Th-that’s a sword made of arc...”

Arc was a grade-six metal, considered the most refined kind in this world, and one that could chew up most any numbered item. This was why I had been hoping for a greater number of enemies instead. The higher floor an adventurer was, the more extreme the difference in equipment, not to mention rank and number of essences.
At least the ninth floor.

However, I didn’t turn away and accepted the cruel reality for what it was. This was not a clan of dozens of people. Assuming that skill corresponded with equipment, he was a strong player who could be active on the ninth floor with just five people. He must have had at least eight essences, too, and all of them above rank five.

“Barbarian.” At this point, though, those abilities were meaningless. He was at a level where he could cut all five of us down without even needing the help of the priest. “Give me the item you found inside. Unless you want to die.”
I made an assessment of what I had to do in order to live. And so, I held out the jewel I obtained from the boss room. “Oh, are you talking about this?”
Originally, this had been Plan D: giving up everything he asked for and begging for my life.
“So you did have it. Now, hand it over. Then I’ll let you live.”
I stared at the man without a word. As the silence stretched on, my teammates opened their mouths one by one.
“...We’re fine. Just give it to him. We don’t even know what it’s used forrr, anyway.”
“I agree as well. Wouldn’t it be better to avoid a fight if possible?”

These sentiments were worthless. This jewel was the only reason we were still alive. How could I make a deal with a crazy bastard who had kidnapped a priest and forced him to convert? That was out of the question.

“My stomach...” When I cautiously opened my mouth, it drew everyone’s attention. The man was also quietly watching me. I could see an impish smile on his lips, the arrogant smirk of someone who already seemed to know what choice I was going to make. So, I smirked too. “Oh dear! My stomach hurts!”
“...What?”
While the man was momentarily bewildered by my sudden shout, I stuffed the jewel in my mouth without hesitation.
Gulp!
I forced myself to swallow. My esophagus hurt from pushing down a jewel the size of a tangerine with force, but oh well. That would be resolved in a few seconds.
Burp!
A belch came out as I weathered the urge to vomit. Then everyone came to their senses.
“What is the meaning of this?” the man asked, eyes glinting murderously.
“I just felt like it!” I answered.

After that, there was a very brief beat of silence. The man stared at me in an apparent attempt to figure out exactly what kind of nutjob he was looking at. I guess my party members weren’t all that different either, but that didn’t matter. Doing what needed to be done and not caring about the opinions of others was the barbarian way.
“Barbarian, don’t think you’ll get to die with dignity.” The man kicked off the ground and shot at me with a speed that was difficult to identify as the same stat as mine.
Swoop!

Getting his money’s worth out of his longsword, he pierced my shield without resistance. It was obvious what the guy was thinking. He had to be planning to kill me and split me open to retrieve the jewel.
So what? What’s he going to do about it?
I applied strength to my shield, using it to adjust the position of the penetrating blade—not outward, but toward my stomach.
Apparently catching on, he hurriedly withdrew his sword. He was likely well aware that the jewel I had swallowed was not very durable. “Was this your plan?” he asked.
I didn’t deny it. This was Plan E, which had replaced all the plans that I had scrapped.
Burp!
Sue me. Now I really had no choice but to see this through to the end.
The man’s eyes kept darting around as he continued to look for the right opportunity to strike. If he could cut my head off in one go, then he’d just need to slit my stomach and take it.
Not a chance.
I pounded my stomach with a fist the size of a watermelon.
Boom! Boom!
Each time my hand swung, his eyes twitched. It was clear from the look on his face that he was worried that the item in my stomach might crack.
“Ah, it’s just that my stomach is bloated.”
“...You deranged bastard.”
I welcomed the label. No one avoided fallen leaves in autumn because stepping on them wasn’t an issue. But what about filth? You could accidentally step in it, but no one did so on purpose.
Whack!
I stopped pounding my stomach. The key to Plan E was to not cross the line. This should be warning enough.
“What do you want?” The man was now trying to converse with me. Not wanting to provoke me, he had already tucked his sword into his belt.
Yeah, so this thing is that important to you, huh?
I was tempted to taunt him even more, but I quietly moved to the other side of the passageway with my teammates and got to the point. “One day. Just give us one day.”
“Not let you go?” The man gave me a curious look. It wasn’t that I didn’t get why. Anyone in a similar situation would have asked something like that.

“I don’t beg for my life like that.” To be more precise, I didn’t bother doing pointless things like that. “Give me one day.” I judged that this was the maximum he would allow. “Then I won’t do anything cowardly.”
“How can I trust you?” the man asked curtly.

Without hesitation, I pulled out the ace up my sleeve. “I swear on a warrior’s honor. We are exhausted from not sleeping for days. But if you wait just one day, I will fight fair and square,” I shot back as if that was all I had wanted from the beginning, as if I wasn’t willing to do something cowardly in the first place.
In the face of my fighting spirit, the hesitant man quietly asked, “Do you really think you can win?”
I chuckled. Could I win? Well, I still thought the odds were slim, but so what? “Is that a reason to give up?” Without needing to put on an act, I spoke sincerely.

The man stared at my face. After a moment of silence, he finally gave me an answer, his voice adamant in a way that brokered no argument. “Twelve hours. I’ll give you twelve hours.” This was his Maginot Line. “I’m warning you in advance, though—don’t think the same trick will work then too.”

He would rather we just give up the item here and now, and his urge not to let us go was obvious in both his eyes and expression. I let out a long breath that I had been holding back. It was 5:40 a.m., and I had managed to get what I most desperately needed: time.
We ran through the maze. Our formation was a little different than usual. Rotmiller and Hikurod were in the front, and I was bringing up the rear. The reason for that was simple.
“It really doesn’t seem like he’s following us.”
Although Rotmiller said so, we couldn’t know how long the man would keep his promise. I had to watch my own back.
“So, what are we going to do now?” Rotmiller asked as he cleared the way.
He wasn’t the only one with questions. “Bjorrrn... are we really going to fight?”
“T-That doesn’t seem like a good idea. You saw what happened earlier. He sliced through your shield like paper.”

The questions and concerns that they’d been holding back were all directed at me. They had entrusted everything to me earlier, but now they were belatedly starting to worry. However, as of today, the era of democracy was over. There was not enough time to take everyone’s opinions into account and convince them all to proceed.

“Hikurod, Missha, Rotmiller, Dwalkie.” I called each of their names in turn and asked them for a favor. “In the near future, I may say something or give you orders that you don’t understand. But can you trust me and follow my lead one last time?”
“Of course.”
However, except for Missha, they didn’t answer right away. I waited in silence, trusting in the version of myself I had been showing them for the past several months.
The first to speak was Hikurod. “If it wasn’t for you, I would have already died in the Bloody Citadel. I will trust your judgment.”
The second was Dwalkie. “M-Me too. Bjorn, I will believe in the hero’s destiny you have ahead of you.”

“Hero’s destiny” was a bit of speculation that had accompanied my epithet of Little Balkan like seasoning as it spread throughout the city, and also something the shaman had mentioned to me. It was a little strange that Dwalkie was saying this to me so seriously when he knew me so well. In the current situation, though, this was a good thing.

The last was Rotmiller. “When I saw him, all I could do was tremble in fear. I couldn’t do anything else. I will believe and follow whatever you say.” I felt a deep trust in that brief statement. However, Rotmiller continued without lingering in the emotional moment. “But aside from that, there’s something I need to tell you first.”
“What is it?”
“If my predictions are correct, he’s extremely dangerous.”
“Do you have some information on him?”
“A long time ago, I heard about an adventurer who used an arc longsword,” Rotmiller replied. “Rumor has it that he was cursed by a dragon and his whole body was covered in burns.”
So, who the hell was this guy? Unlike me, who only had more questions, it seemed that the trio had someone in mind.
“A dragon’s curse? No way...”
“The Dragon Slayer! Rotmiller, are you talking about the Dragon Slayer?”
“That, that—then that means he is a member of Orcules...?”
I frowned at their urgent shouting. I still didn’t know who the Dragon Slayer was.
Orcules.
That was an ancient word in this world that meant “witch’s eyes.” I had acquired information about the group that used this name early on through books.
A group of lunatics who say their goal is to kill the king.

But you couldn’t just write them off as maniacs. The fact that they had continued to survive for decades even while doing such ridiculous things proved just how strong each of them was. Even though the royal family had put a huge bounty on them, they had only been able to get rid of seven.
We’ve run into an even more troublesome bastard than I thought.
Apart from the bitter taste in my mouth, one thought became clearer: Running away wasn’t the best solution here. Wasn’t there a famous saying?
“Well, then what should we do?”
Soon after getting the map from Rotmiller, I chose our destination. “We go here.”
There was no paradise for us to escape to, at least not this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 138: Awakening (1)
paragraphs: The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos, was of the dragon tribe and had been cursed by a dragon after killing the clan’s elder dragon chief. Vagos disappeared after the incident but had become active as a member of Orcules ten years ago, terrorizing the holy land of the elves all alone. His main weapon was an arc longsword nicknamed the Dragon Slayer Sword, and it was said that he had a total of six confirmed essences: three rank five, two rank four, and one rank three.

Based on the confirmed essences alone, it seemed he was essentially a typical swordsman with high stats. Since all his skills took the form of strength buffs, his compatibility with his opponents meant nothing as long as he had the right equipment. This information was from ten years ago, so it might have changed to some extent, but the chances of that were slim. After all, how could a criminal erase an essence?
So he must have crawled all the way here because of this one thing.

Dragon Speech was what I was most worried about. But rumor had it that his access to the dragon people’s unique skill had been sealed due to the dragon’s curse. This was good news. To be honest, I was fucking terrified when I found out that he was of a dragon race.
“That is all I know,” Rotmiller finished.
“Okay, thank you. That helped a lot.”
Having learned new information about the enemy, I calmly put my thoughts in order. Well, while running toward our destination, of course.
Sprint!
First of all, the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos, was an unexpected giant. If it hadn’t been for the Guardian of Balance effect, I would have been decapitated before I had even recognized the jewel.
Sprint!

Feeling chills for some reason, I checked the time. It was 8:57 a.m., about three hours since we ran into that bastard. In other words, in nine hours, our game of tag would begin. Of course, that was assuming that he kept his promise.
Just twelve hours, huh?
That was the disappointing part. In response to my proud demeanor paired with a warrior’s oath, Vagos had accepted my deal just in case, or perhaps with the thought that there was nothing to lose.
If it weren’t for that damn ring, he might have let us have the entire day.
There was a big difference between twenty-four hours and twelve. That was time we could have used to prepare all the items we needed and take our last break.
Whew, nothing is going smoothly.

I couldn’t help sighing, but I had to hold on to my determination. Recalling the hopeless situations I’d faced in the past—goblin traps, psychopaths, the Bloody Citadel, the Witch’s Forest, the Lord of the Floor, etcetera—I cleared my mind and replaced all those thoughts with just one goal: survive. If possible, all of us together, without fail.
“Bjorn, we’re here.”

Right when my thoughts reached that point, Rotmiller stopped walking. We had gotten to the dead end before I knew it. We were at the corner of the maze in the direction of eleven o’clock, closest to where the final boss’s lair was. Simply put, this was the place where the second mini-boss was located.
Click, rattle.
As Rotmiller activated the mechanism, the wall slid aside to reveal a hidden area.
Whoosh.
The stone chamber lit up with torches as soon as we stepped inside. There was just one difference from the seven o’clock corner where Baphomet had appeared.
“Ugh, I think the other place was actually betterrr.”
Instead of goat heads, the stone chamber was filled with piles of corpses with their eyeballs pulled out. I pushed through the stench and dripped a drop of blood onto the magic circle.
[The devil in the labyrinth has detected blood.]
Okay, got one.
[You have killed Argos. EXP +5]
[Higher-class mutant bonus. EXP +1]

In addition to the mini-boss rooms, there were many hidden spaces in the Labyrinth of Larcaz. The rewards were different for each one. One-time consumables could be hidden inside, or rare monsters might appear. But what I needed was something else.
Another bust?
After defeating Argos, we searched around and focused on finding hidden rooms. Not only was there not enough time to go beat another mini-boss, but for my plan to work, I had to find that room.
Whew, still, we’re doing a good job of finding them.

With Rotmiller at the forefront searching for the hidden rooms, we discovered one every two hours. It was all thanks to his Sixth Sense stat, which had gone up dramatically after the Dragon Slayer’s party entered. Those rooms we would have overlooked and inadvertently passed by before, Rotmiller found without fail.
The problem was that the room I wanted hadn’t appeared yet. Time continued to pass, until the twelve hours I was promised were coming to an end.
“Wait, stop. I sense something strange.” Rotmiller stopped the group and searched the surrounding walls for a hidden room.
Slide.
It was a 100-by-150-foot stone chamber without a single monster or hidden treasure. After checking the inside, I closed the stone chamber again.
Found it.
Finally, the first thing we needed to pull this plan off had been assembled. I stopped the party. “Everyone, take a break. I will stand watch.”
“Break? What could this room possibly be?”
“If we survive, I will explain everything. So just do as I say.”
“...All right.” Even the dwarf set aside his questions at the determination in my voice. No, rather than setting them aside, it was probably that he had chosen to trust me and not ask.

“Phew...” As my tired colleagues closed their eyes, I let out a long breath. The other guys weren’t really a problem, but lying to Rotmiller was already giving me a headache. From summoning the mini-boss by dropping blood onto the magic circle to just now, saying “I read it in a book” wouldn’t be able to explain everything.
Anyway, I’ll think about how to handle that later.

I took one more long breath and shoved aside my worries about the future. I was sure I could lie somehow, if only I returned alive. I decided to focus solely on the present moment and organized my thoughts for the last time.
Earlier, Rotmiller had asked, “I thought you said there might be a portal in the center of the map? Are we not going there?”

My reason for not going to the portal was simple: that guy would be there for the next twelve hours. If we went there and Vagos thought we were trying to escape, the twelve hours we had earned would go to waste. I decided it was best to use our time to make preparations instead.
He must’ve started looking for us too.

The agreed-upon twelve hours were over. Fortunately, our initial preparations had been completed on time. Thanks to that, I was able to take a break until he arrived, but the situation was still grim.
The success rate is less than 10 percent.

This was the highest probability I could calculate with a cool head. Of all the essences this bastard had, only six were known. There were two or three unknown essences that remained variables, and the biggest stumbling block was still Karui’s high priest.
Squeeze.

I took out the brilliant red jewel and held it in my hand. I had swallowed it as a hostage, but as soon as it was safe, I used Giantization to vomit it out. It was the final reward of the Labyrinth of Larcaz, and the item that the notorious criminal with the alias of Dragon Slayer must have been desperately looking for.
Restrained Wish.

I would have preferred not to use it now, if at all possible. This item had to be paired with a rank-four guardian essence for maximum effectiveness. But if I died, I wouldn’t be able to use it anyway.
I guess I have no choice but to use it.

I made a decision. I didn’t know how things would play out in the future, and if not now, this item might never be used. This quiet, like the eye of a storm, would come to an end soon. It was better to prepare in advance if possible. Plus, even if I wanted to use it later, I wouldn’t have the time to do so.
It’s a bit of a waste, but...
I gripped the jewel tighter.
Crunch!
The jewel split, emitting a brilliant red light.
[You have used Restrained Wish. You will now be moved to the Room of Balance.]
When I came to, I was standing in an unfamiliar place.
Whoosh!

A single flame rose to light up the space. I took a step and looked around. It was a stone chamber reminiscent of the Tower of Heavens. The flames floating in the air shimmered with bluish light, illuminating three stone gates at the end of the room.
This is cool.
So it looked like this in real life. In the game, all you had to do was manipulate the keyboard and make your choice.
[Select the essence you want to replace.]
I carefully studied the unique murals painted on each stone gate. They weren’t colored in, but it wasn’t hard to recognize them.
Step.
The first was a terrible monster with a mass of rotten arms and legs.
This must be a Corpse Golem.
Next was a figure in the form of a man with sharp fangs and sharp claws, with red jewels representing its red eyes.
This is a Vampire.
Finally, there was a muscular warrior roaring with a gigantic flag serving as a backdrop.
This must be an Orc Hero.

Each door represented one of the essences I had absorbed so far. There were no instructions whatsoever, but it was clear what I had to do. If you opened the door, the corresponding essence would be replaced. Restrained Wish was a gacha-type item that changed an essence of rank four or higher into a random essence of the same rating.
Step.
Without hesitation, I proceeded toward one of the doors. I’d already decided what to choose.
Orc Hero.
Obviously not that one. It was only rank five, but it was a core essence that belonged to my final build.
Corpse Golem.

Pain tolerance was surprisingly useful, but it didn’t help me much in terms of abilities. I had been saving this one to erase it later when my essence slots got full, but I was going to pass on it for now. Why would I do something as wasteful as use Restrained Wish on a rank seven essence?
Vampire.

A moment later, I stood in front of the stone gate with the shape of that particular monster drawn on it and reached out my hand. It had skill sets and stats that suited a tank. In addition, since it had been obtained by killing a Rift guardian, it was a rare essence with all three skills attached. However, thanks to that, there was no hesitation in my decision. Restrained Wish had a hidden element.
[You have chosen the essence of a Vampire. This essence is of a guardian. The rank of the selectable essence has risen.]

If you offered a guardian essence, the rating of the essence that could be selected went up. Put simply, it was possible to obtain a rank-three essence by offering the essence of a rank-four guardian.
That bastard is probably thinking the same, considering he came all this way for this one thing.

I had been the same when I played the game. Whenever I consumed a guardian essence that was high in rank but not suitable for my character, I went to the Labyrinth of Larcaz and aimed for a gacha. But a rank-five guardian? To think I would use this item just to give it away.
Sigh...
I erased my lingering disappointment and walked through the open door. Before I could even take a few steps, the straight passageway ended and three stone gates appeared past the burning flames.
Whoosh!

As this item had a balance theme, each of the three stone gates had a physical, mental, or special ability-type monster drawn on it. Up to this point, everything was the same as usual. But what was this?
[You have offered an essence that is currently possessed by no one. The Guardian of Balance has recognized its rarity and presents a new option that matches its value.]

I froze mid-mural inspection. The first option was a skeleton wizard holding a staff in one hand and a box containing a red jewel in the other: the rank-four monster, Lich. It was a typical special ability-type monster that possessed a passive skill called Soul Chest and several destructive active skills. No problems there so far, it was just that I didn’t understand the jewels embedded above the door.
...Rainbow?

Just a second ago, the Corpse Golem door had had a black jewel, and the Orc Hero door had had a green jewel. I assumed this meant the color of the essence. But a rainbow? Wouldn’t that be the same color as the jewel on top of the Vampire’s door, which was a guardian’s essence?
Then is this really another guardian essence?

I quickly checked the rest of the doors. There was a drawing of a rank-four monster, Soul Colossus—a spirit-type monster with no stats such as Strength or Agility, as all of its stats were centered on the spirit. The color of the jewel on the door signified a guardian. Of course, this could just be luck. Very occasionally, a guardian essence popped up as an option.
This can’t be a coincidence.
After checking the last option given to me, the physical-type monster, I had to acknowledge it. This was far from luck. There were still things about this game that I didn’t know existed.
Whoosh!
The jewel reflected in the flickering flame was red. In other words, it was not the essence of a guardian. But what did that matter in this situation?
Step.
I walked toward the door like a man possessed. It was unbelievable, but the mural on the door could mean just one thing.
Step.

This was a rank-three monster, and a boss-level monster that worked alone. To put it simply, this was a monster that could only be defeated by conducting raids made up of rank-three and rank-four adventurers. It was the monster that boasted the best specs among overworld monsters in terms of physical ability.
Ogre.
I opened the door without hesitation.
Hallelujah.

chapters.title: Chapter 139: Awakening (2)
paragraphs: [The Essence of an Ogre has seeped into your soul. Your Strength has increased by +140. Your Mana Resistance has increased by +80. Your Physical Resistance has increased by +40. All Tolerances have increased by +10. Natural Regeneration has decreased by -40. Cognition has decreased by -20.]

As soon as I opened my eyes, I checked my watch. Fortunately, little time had passed. I finished up and came out in a rush just in case, but, well. After watching my colleagues sleep for a while, I took out a knife. Then, as if sawing, I drew it over the back of my hand.
Slide, slide.

After pressing it into my skin and moving it back and forth about ten times, a single drop of blood flowed out. As I watched the wound fail to heal, I realized that my character build really had changed in an instant.
Squeeze.

I clenched my fist in the air. The change in my body was obvious, but not as stark as when I took the Orc Hero essence. I could understand why. The Vampire essence had disappeared, but Guardian of Balance was still active.
I’ll only be able to feel exactly how much my strength has increased after I go outside.
I took the time to calculate my gains and losses for a while, staring out at the other side of the torchlit passage.
An Ogre, huh?

An Ogre was a rank-three monster with stats and skills that made it every tanker’s dream. However, its essence hadn’t been included in my plan for my final build for more of a practical reason than an incompatibility issue. A rank-three monster was hard enough to take down as it was. Besides, out of seven possible active skills Ogres had, I had to make sure the color I wanted appeared. Not only was the acquisition difficulty too high, but in terms of defense alone, there was a rank-four monster called Steel Giant that was more practical than this one.
Instead, Steel Giant comes with the downside of not being able to use weapons.

In the end, it was a matter of strategy. Did you want to do more damage, or just focus on the tank? The difference in performance between the two essences was subtle, so in most playthroughs, I chose the extreme tank. I had decided that, considering the effort it took to find an Ogre essence, it would make more sense to just develop a damage dealer instead. Indeed, this assessment had proven correct. As a result, I was able to open the original version of the Door to the Abyss that no one else had reached.
But strictly speaking, Ogres are better.

Being able to adapt your cultivation method was the beauty of this game, and also the sign of a skillful player. My final plan was never strictly 1+1=2, anyway. Aside from the core essence, everything else was up in the air. For each key role, I determined three or four candidates with similar performances, took the one that came out first, and moved on to the next. What I wanted was to clear the game, not to complete just one main character.
It’s a little disappointing that it’s not a yellow essence, but it won’t change my entire cultivation strategy.
It felt too good to be true. I had exchanged the Vampire essence in anticipation of the Steel Giant, but what I had gotten was arguably far better than what I’d expected.
What are the conditions? With a Vampire Guardian essence, not only do I have the option of another guardian’s essence, but I also get offered an upgrade that’s two ranks higher?
It was an innocent question. As a gamer, curiosity welled up in me, but I forced myself to suppress it.
This should make it about 30 percent. No, maybe 40 percent?

Reconsidering our survival rate in light of this new development, I came up with a new, detailed combat strategy in my head. To raise the probability even a little more, what could I do at this moment?
...It would be better to take off my armor. There’s no way he’ll wait for us to get ready.
Like a swordsman sharpening his sword the night before a decisive battle, I refined my plans and looked for better options.
The Cognition penalty isn’t as severe as I thought. If the Strength ratio is this good, I won’t be pushed back in terms of brute strength.
The details of the plan began to fall together one by one to form a picture. However, the more I planned, the faster my heart pounded.
Thump!

The future was like broken glass. No one could perfectly predict how it would play out. No matter how thorough the plan was, countless variables were sure to pop up. From that moment on, I’d have to improvise everything, just like when the Lord of the Floor had been summoned.
Thump!

Because of that, was there anything else I could prepare? Was it possible that there was something about the situation I had misread? Like I was about to take a test that would decide my entire future, I worried over and over again without pause.
After a long while, Rotmiller woke up and quietly called my name. “Bjorn. Something is coming.”

That meant that it was time. I hurriedly woke up my teammates and checked my watch. It was 9:47 p.m., about four hours since we started our break. In other words, about thirty-eight hours remained until the labyrinth closed.
“This is sooner than we expected. They must have a way to track us.”
I let Rotmiller’s words flow in one ear and out the other. I already knew that, and if there was information that I needed to commit to memory right now, it wasn’t that.
So it takes four hours to get from there to here.
All the prerequisites for my new Plan A had been met.
Step.
Now I just had to throw the dice.
Trudge, trudge.
Steady footsteps began to ring out from the darkness. They came toward us like they were trying to strangle us—slowly and not in a rush.
Step.
It wasn’t long before Vagos came into view. His companion was the poor crippled man. The man must’ve been used to make another sacrifice because blood was dripping from his squinting eye.
“That’s too cruel!”
“Why would he do that to his own teammate...?”
Everyone frowned at the bizarre sight, but I let out a silent sigh of relief. He’d left the priest at the portal. If they had come together, we would have had no chance.
Step.
Just as I was thinking this, Vagos stopped walking, leaving an appropriate distance between us. A heavy silence fell.

“What, you’re all alive?” He laughed flippantly. This was far from the reaction I had expected. I wouldn’t have thought it strange if he’d started stabbing my stomach right away. What was this? “I thought someone must have died because my strength suddenly returned.”
Those words relieved all my unease. So that was why.
No wonder he’s strangely calm.
He hadn’t noticed yet. He thought that I still had the Restrained Wish in my stomach. After hearing that, it made sense why he’d think that one of us had died.
Until he continued. “Oh, yeah. I guess you absorbed the essence of a Vaikundus?” Even in the midst of this, the guy presented a new possibility. I couldn’t help laughing.
I didn’t expect him to be an asshole.

The essence I had gotten was a whopping rank-three essence. Even if the eight of us had to share the stats because of Guardian of Balance, a Vaikundus’s essence was nowhere near powerful enough to explain the increase we’d experienced. This guy must have realized that too. However, he’d already decided on the answer that he wanted and was looking for evidence to back it up. With that mindset, how could he reach the truth?
The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos.
I jotted down one more note about him in my head. Surprisingly, this guy was an optimist.
Perhaps my laughter seemed menacing, because his relaxed air vanished. “...Barbarian, you kept your oath, right?”
I stared at him silently, giving him a look that said, Do I even need to answer that?

It seemed that that wasn’t enough for him, though. “The item, where is the item?” he asked again. This time, his voice was tinged with annoyance. Although he was trying to deny it because of the sunk-cost fallacy, he was slowly picking up on the fact that he may have been fooled. Finally, he asked, “...Did you use it already?”
“Oh, it wasn’t intentional,” I answered.
“...What?”
“I’m sorry. I was just bored so I messed with it, but it broke.”

Despite my heartfelt apology, he shook like an aspen tree. He slowly came to terms with the truth. He had been fooled by the thing that barbarians, who only had honor, guarded and considered to be as precious as their lives: a warrior’s oath. “I see you had no intention of keeping your oath from the start.”
The prickle of murderous energy touched my skin. Like a K-Barbarian from Korea, I confidently straightened my shoulders. “I said I’m sorry—”
“Die.”

By the time his voice reached my ears, the sword was already right in front of me. In a split second, he’d managed to shorten the distance by this much. I was only able to react in time because I had been watching his every move even while provoking him.
Slide.
I raised my shield. Not to block him, but...
Clang!

I slammed the sword aside with all my might. This was a countermeasure I had come up with while running battle simulations in my head during the time we had left. His was an arc sword. Trying to block it head-on would only pierce a hole in my shield.
“Dwalkie!” I shouted, and as soon as I used my excessive strength to push him away, the spell I had briefed Dwalkie on in advance fired.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-seven attack spell Cold Storm.]
Fortunately, it seemed that he had completed the spell while I was conversing and buying him time.
Shhhhhh!

Sharp ice shards swirled around and filled the passage. It was so cold that a chill shot through me, even as I stuck to the walls and stayed out of range. Ironically, at the end of the blizzard, I sensed a strange heat. It was obvious what it was without even having to look.
[Regal Vagos has cast Blast Furnace.]

This was one of the abilities of the rank-four monster Lava Giant—a buff skill that made him immune to Cold and Fire damage when activated and greatly increased the user’s physique stats. I had been worried that this was outdated information from ten years ago, but it seemed he still had it.
Rip!
I tore a scroll open without hesitation. We obtained it after defeating one of the mini-bosses, Argos, and it should have been used to take down the Minotaur.
[The Flame of Greed has detected a Fire-type skill within its radius. Target locked. The Essence of the Lava Giant possessed by Regal Vagos will be sealed for forty-eight hours.]
The heat on the other side of the passageway stopped at the same time as the scroll burned away. Okay, one rank-four essence down. I wondered how the bastard was feeling now.
Shaaa!
Soon the blizzard freezing the entire hall lifted. The guy stood there perfectly unscathed without a hint of damage, behind a translucent black curtain reminiscent of a window.
“Is that all you’ve got?” The bastard looked at us with a mocking smile. That made sense if he thought that this surprise attack had been our finishing blow.
I never thought things would work out this well.
The skill he just used was Dark Veil, one that didn’t exist on the list of essences Rotmiller had told me about. In other words, one of the unknowns I had been worried about had now been disclosed.
There are only one or two unidentified essences left.
Of course, he could have other numbered items, so I’d need to keep an eye out for them.
Whip!
Before I had time to get my thoughts in order, he shot toward me again. Just like before, I tried to hit the sword with my shield, but he was also an intelligent guy who learned from his mistakes.
Voom!
The shield cut through the air. The second I realized what was happening, I felt a slight pain and a foreign sensation in my shoulder.
Slice!

When I checked, I saw that the arc longsword that had cut through the lithinum shield like tofu had dug into my upper arm about an inch. As our eyes met, there was a bewildered look on his face. He had been planning to slice my arm off, but the sword had only cut in this deep. The reason for that was simple.
Pft, do you know what my physique stats are right now?

Ogres had the passive skill Ironskin, a skill with insane performance that doubled the user’s physical resistance and quadrupled it for slash attacks. Since we currently had similar stats thanks to Guardian of Balance, it was only natural that I could withstand even a longsword made of arc.
Mm. I didn’t mean to reveal this to him so early, though.

I had wanted to block the sword with a shield and hide my new abilities as much as possible until the exact right moment. However, at the level he was at, he might be able to infer what essence this ability came from.

Staring at the top of his burn-covered head, I made a decision to use the active skill that came with the red Ogre’s essence, along with the first proper attack strategy I had developed back when I only had Flesh Explosion. I didn’t know why the guy with the nickname Tyrant of the Forest had this for a skill name, but...
[You have cast Swing. The damage you deal with blunt weapons has increased significantly in proportion to your Muscle Strength.]
Well, as long as the effects were good.
Voom!
I swung the mace with all my might.

chapters.title: Chapter 140: Awakening (3)
paragraphs: Because this skill was just a powerful swing, unlike other skills, there was no need for intense focus.
Voom!

Swing did not even have any common special effects such as light radiating from the weapon or gusts of wind blowing out. This was something I had always been dissatisfied with while playing the game. Skills tended to get fancier and have cooler names as they went up in rank, so why was Swing the only one that was like this? Today, I learned the answer.
Even Ogres are efficiency freaks.
In reality, flashy effects were of no help. They only stood out and exposed my abilities to a well-informed enemy. This was much more practical.
[Regal Vagos has cast Blackout Curtain.]

As if to prove my point, the bastard used a defensive skill. Exactly on what basis this decision was made was unknown. Maybe he just thought this would be enough. He might have decided that it made more sense to stick his sword into a vital point while maintaining distance rather than backing down entirely.
Crunch!

The rank-four skill Blackout Curtain shattered as soon as it touched my mace, barely a second after being cast. This was natural. Even though it may not have a grandiose name like Earth Tremor or Incarnation’s Fury, Swing was an attack skill that belonged to the upper tiers, even at rank three.
Only then did he realize the situation he was in and make an attempt to twist out of the way.
Oh, if you wanted to do that, you should have dodged it from the start.
Punch!
I had been aiming for the top of his head, but my mace succeeded in landing on his shoulder. Vagos hurriedly widened the distance between us with a bitten-off groan.
Dash.

His dislocated shoulder sagged in its socket to the point of deformity. He quickly held the sword between his teeth and moved his free hand into his pocket. It was probably a subspace, and what he wanted was a potion.
Do I look like a fucking fool?

I had no intention of giving him time to recover. “Dwalkie! Use Voice Control!” First of all, since my opponent was human, I turned on the team’s communications and rushed at him. I quickly gave orders. “Hikurod, Rotmiller! You two guard Dwalkie. Missha, you stick right behind me!”

Of course, there was no time to talk at length, so we took up our basic formation again. Then I talked them through the details step-by-step. Fortunately, my teammates accepted their respective missions without further comment. Dwalkie kicked things off.
Voom!
The moment the bastard evaded my mace with the deftness of a high-DEX character, curse magic seeped into his body.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-nine curse spell Slowdown.]
Actually, it was safe to say that Dwalkie had pulled his weight with just this spell. If we were to get into the technical side of things, this bastard had likely specialized in agility.

“You scum...!” He did not hide his anger and showed off the full range of his abilities, from Advanced Acceleration to Afterimage, which was from a rank-five essence. His Agility stat instantaneously increased.
Dash!
Perhaps because of my reduced cognitive abilities, my eyes felt sore just following his movements.
Even with a stat adjustment and Slowdown, he’s still like this.
I was once again reminded of what a monster he really was, but I calmly proceeded with what needed to be done.
Seeing that his arm isn’t healing, it doesn’t seem like he has any regeneration essences or numbered items.

I narrowed down the number of possible outcomes based on this newly acquired information and focused on the role assigned to me. Of course, my role was simple: standing in the middle of the passageway and getting beaten to a pulp.
Slice! Clang, stab!
“Don’t think I’ll grant you a clean death,” he said coldly.

It was impossible to dodge or avoid his attacks with my Agility while his full strength was on display like that. Blocking an arc longsword with a shield was virtually pointless, so I took it with my body instead.
Chhhhhh!

In an instant, my entire body was stabbed through ruthlessly and acidic blood flowed from the opening in my skin. Because the Vampire essence had disappeared, it didn’t heal on its own like it used to. However, that wasn’t a problem. When had I ever chewed on the enemy with teeth intact?
Shatter!
Rotmiller, who was holding back our opponent with a crossbow from the rear, noticed my condition in real time and threw me a potion from his Treasure Vault.
[Your body is healing due to the effect of Recovery (Medium).]
This was also known as Barbarian Beginner Mode.
It’s been a while since I’ve done this.

Unlike me, who was full of strange mixed feelings, the emotion in Vagos’s eyes was disbelief. It seemed that he’d realized from a look at my face that I wasn’t incapable of feeling pain. “Crazy bastard,” he mumbled incredulously. Even though he must have been going in and out of the labyrinth for a long time, it looked like he hadn’t encountered a guy like me yet.
Somehow, I’ve ended up getting a rave review.
Of course, my response to this was a macing.
Voom!
As he nimbly evaded it, the dwarf’s support continued.
[Hikurod Murad has cast Lightning Attack.]
[Hikurod Murad has cast Release.]
An intense ball of electricity shot out into the air. Vagos stepped on the wall and jumped again to avoid it. However, that wasn’t too much of a letdown. This was not Hikurod’s true role, anyway.
“What do you think a bunch of scum like you can do?” Vagos yelled.
There were only three things I had asked the dwarf to do: provide support from a distance using Lightning Release, protect Dwalkie in case things went sideways, and use items in a timely fashion.
[Regal Vagos has cast Fear Imprint.]
[Hikurod Murad has used Guardian’s Wrist Guard. All enemies are knocked back by a powerful blow and all allies temporarily become immune to all harmful effects.]

The rank-four monster Nightmare’s ability, Fear Imprint, temporarily instilled a strong sense of fear in its targets, and the user received a physique buff equal to that amount. But before the skill could properly activate, a gust of wind blew through and cleared my mind. As I suspected, Guardian of Balance wasn’t deactivated by the wrist guard because it wasn’t a harmful effect.
“Behelahhh!” As my opponent had been pushed back, I quickly ran toward him—even using Wild Outburst—and slammed my mace down.
Voom!
I didn’t use Swing because it was clear that he would avoid the hit anyway.
Dash!
Vagos twisted his body sideways and swung his sword at me. Then Missha, who was close behind me, aimed for his side.
Stab!
The blade of the sword dug shallowly but surely into his skin. He flinched and immediately retaliated, but Missha quickly moved behind me.
Nice.
She had moved just the way I wanted.
Vagos gritted his teeth. “Acting up, I see.”
Seeing as another rave review had come in, it seemed there wasn’t a problem with my strategy. Therefore, we maintained the status quo.
[Your body is healing due to the effect Recovery (Medium).]

I took on the role of meat shield. Dwalkie, Rotmiller, and Hikurod provided ranged support. When he was electrocuted or avoided my attacks—basically whenever there was an opportunity—Missha jumped forward and stabbed him with her sword.
Slice, stab!
Damage steadily accumulated as the battle dragged on.
“Don’t think you guys will get out of here alive!”

In the end, the bastard used essences and numbered items no one in the city had heard of, but it changed nothing. The frequency of our having to use potions increased, but it wasn’t enough to turn the tide. He was all talk.
Anyway, it seems he really was level nine.
He had shown off all nine of his essences except a rank-three essence. Well, rank-threes weren’t easy to obtain even on the ninth floor, so I guess that was only natural.
“Bjorrrn! That shiny blade is coming again!”

I soon sensed that the time had come for the battle to end. After about thirty minutes of fighting, I had clocked all the cards he had up his sleeve. There was also the possibility that he’d retreat for a while and come back with the priest.
Now.

Now that the battle had dragged on for a while and we had gotten used to it, I dashed forward with all my might and reached out my hand. He backed away a bit to put some distance between us. It wasn’t much different from that other deranged bitch. Whenever they reacted to anything, they only ever moved as much as needed. Was this a habit of the strong or something?
Thank you very much.
[You have cast Giantization.]
My body grew and my arms lengthened accordingly. Not passing up this opportunity, I grabbed his neck.

For the first time, a flicker of panic appeared on his face. He probably hadn’t known I had Giantization, since I’d deliberately been saving it this entire time. It felt like all my hard work was paying off.
The light is red.
The jewel on his traffic light ring glowed red. I raised my mace and shouted without hesitation: “Behelaaaah!”

The finishing blow I had been waiting patiently for, this one golden opportunity, was the thing that would be my ultimate finisher from today on. With Giantization active and my stats inflated by Wild Outburst, I drove my mace down on my opponent’s head with all my might.
Swing.
I had the conviction that if this one blow landed right, it would all be over.
“Naundez Aunzo.”
That was why I could see every single change that occurred the moment his lips opened.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has ended.]
The strength left my entire body. In addition, my eye level dropped in an instant and my field of view narrowed.
Kwang!
The mace swung down in a regular blow and hit the floor.
Wheeze.
The bastard escaped my grip at some point and vomited up blood. As I watched this all happen, I could only think one thing:
Why, you damned prick? What did you just do?
The answer quickly came to me.
Goddamn it.
This was a unique skill that all dragon races were born with—something he shouldn’t ever be able to use because of the dragon’s curse on him.
[Regal Vagos has cast Dragon: Silence of the Soul.]
It was Dragon Speech.

The field effect Guardian of Balance evenly distributed our basic stats, and on top of that, he had to fight one-on-five. One of his rank-four essences was even sealed. Thanks to the Ogre essence, I had devised a strategy to deal with the arc longsword, which had been our biggest problem. We generously used the various consumable items we had obtained from the hidden room, and even a special move with decisive timing. Even if our opponent was a ninth-floor adventurer, I thought this would be enough to defeat him.

The miserable truth was that misfortune could befall anyone at any time. Getting diagnosed with a rare disease in full swing at a young age; being involved in a tragic accident on a day out and losing a loved one; a big fire breaking out at the home of a relative I had been taken to and forced to live at; or my mother, who said she would be with me tomorrow, suddenly disappearing—all of these things happened in real life without any notice, whether rain or shine. Misfortune had a way of following someone, just like right now.
Spit.
The man spat out bloody mucus on the floor and picked up the arc sword that had fallen on the ground.
Pzzzzz!
Sparks flew from the sword, almost as if it was rejecting his touch. Vagos frowned and forcibly grabbed the sword, put it into his subspace, and slowly walked toward us.
I struggled to lift the mace. The weapon, which had felt as light as a feather a moment ago, was as heavy as an iron bar now.
Step.
Information on what was going on popped into my head without me needing to wrack my brain.
[You have fallen into a state of Soul Exhaustion.]

Soul Exhaustion was an abnormal condition that occurred when a character’s Soul Power dropped to zero. I could count on my hands the number of times this had happened to me in the game. Even if you used your skills willy-nilly, your Soul Power should never drop to zero.
[All of your stats have temporarily decreased by 70 percent.]
I realized it right then. New Plan A was a failure.
“Why’s everyone so quiet all of a sudden?”
The consequences? Well, we were about to find out.
Punch!
He kicked me and I went flying. Although I blocked it with both arms, the impact reverberated through my bones.
“Bjorn!” Missha hurriedly brandished a knife and rushed at him, but it was too short to reach him. “Aaagh!”
Like a martial arts master, he wrapped his arm around Missha’s wrist and stole the sword. “Garbage bitch.” He kicked Missha in the stomach and sent her flying too.
The crossbow bolt that Rotmiller shot right on time was cut in two before it even touched him.

“Because of these pieces of trash...” He murmured coldly, staring at us. That one sentence sent shivers down my spine and my heart began to pound wildly like it was broken. However, even in the midst of all this, as usual, my mind combined the clues it was being provided. “None of you will ever know how much time I just threw out the window.”

Vagos wasn’t in good shape, either. Whether he was vomiting blood or not, if he were at 100 percent, my arms would’ve been broken by now. From what I could tell, he couldn’t even use a sword right now. There were many encouraging indicators. However, none of them were enough to balance out our current situation.
“M-Miss Karlstein! Wake up!” cried a voice behind us.
Vagos took one more step toward me. “Barbarian, don’t expect eternal rest. Even death won’t be able to save you.”
This was not just a comment made to scare me. I now knew what the sole rank-three essence he possessed was.
Step.
The situation was, in fact, hopeless. What should I do? At this rate, even escaping would be almost impossible. And it was right at that moment, when my head was filled with thoughts like that—
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight attack spell Ice Lance.]
An ice spear with the same strength as before fired. Two, actually, complete with Trajectory Adjustment.
Shooot!

Vagos hurriedly twisted to dodge one and barely blocked the other with his blade. Usually, he would’ve blocked it with Blackout Curtain or easily hacked it to pieces with the sword, but he struggled to handle it with magic.

It was then that I realized something. I didn’t know why I hadn’t thought of this right away, but wizards didn’t use Soul Power. In other words, the debuff caused by Soul Exhaustion did not apply to them.
“Yes, I will have to kill you first.”
That meant, if we wanted to live, we had to protect Dwalkie.
“Everyone, look alive!”

chapters.title: Chapter 141: Awakening (4)
paragraphs: Hector Ludwig was an unlucky old man who had once been a respected high priest of the Church of Reatlas, before being kidnapped by the Dragon Slayer in his later years and forced to become the subordinate of an evil god.
“May the blessing of the twilight star be with you...”
In the middle of making the sign of the cross out of habit, he paused because of the voice of the evil god that resonated through his head. “Hypocrite, do you still hold onto pointless hopes?”
No one needed to tell him that this was a pointless hope and nothing but hypocrisy. No matter what excuses he gave, all of this was the result of his own choices.
If, on that day...

If he hadn’t succumbed to evil, if, like the great men in folk tales, he had refused to give up his beliefs and shouldered all the sacrifices, that man would never have reached this place. He wouldn’t have had to disappear and wither away, and the adventurers he met today would have finished their expedition and returned to the city without trouble.
Squeeze.
Ludwig clenched his hands into wrinkled fists. It was pointless to speculate or regret what he’d done. Even if he were to go back to that day, he would inevitably make the same choice.
Whooom!

As if to prove it, he currently stood in front of a shimmering portal, following an order given to him by the Dragon Slayer. To be more precise, to protect his precious grandson, he was guarding this place just in case those people ran away.
Pray they don’t come this way.
This was the only hope he allowed himself. “Small” wasn’t a strong enough word to describe this crumb-like shred of optimism.
However, the evil god was not satisfied even with this. “Grow up.”

Over the course of this despair, his aspirations had been broken down and now he had lost even the determination to solve the problem. Just as a slave rejoiced in only being beaten once that day, he resigned himself to his miserable situation, assuring himself that this was the lesser evil and the best he could do, even as he ignored the fact that he had the means to end it all.
Still not satisfied, the evil god spoke again. “Hypocrite, watch. This despair and pain is because of you.” The voice resonated through him like it was etched into his brain.

Before long, a scene appeared behind his screwed-shut eyelids. A barbarian and his allies were fighting against a great evil in a seemingly hopeless situation, unlike him, who had long accepted his fate.
“Behelahhh!”
“So you won’t run away,” Vagos said with a sardonic laugh.
I forcibly lifted the corners of my mouth, as I had no intention of losing ground in a war of nerves.
It’s not like you’re going to let us get away, anyway.

The current situation was extremely simple. In a user-friendly game, a message probably would have popped up right about now that read something like: [Use the wizard to survive until the Soul Exhaustion state ends.] Soul Exhaustion lasted about twenty minutes. I just had to endure it until then.
Oh, also, running away was impossible. There was no easier prey than one that showed its back.
“Protect Dwalkie!” I shouted with all my might.
Dash!

Vagos kicked off the ground, not planning to give us any time. His body accelerated in an instant. In his hand was the Serpent’s Fang, which he had stolen from Missha. Damn, how could I get that thing away from him? I shoved aside any bitter feelings and decided to focus on the guy’s movements to the end.
Clang!
As I blocked the sword with the mace, my foot slid backward. This meant that I’d been pushed back in what I was most confident in: strength.
Whip!
