The sword swung again in a gentle curve. I hurriedly backed away, but I wasn’t fast enough to keep up with his movements. This meant that he also had the upper hand in agility.
Slice.

Acidic blood spattered from my gaping wound. Ironskin wasn’t working, either. I’d hoped otherwise, since he seemed unable to use the arc sword. Ironskin was a skill whose effectiveness increased as physical resistance increased.
Voom!
I banished my complaints and wielded the mace.
Slice.

I couldn’t even touch the guy. Instead, my wounds increased. However, I swung the mace again. Buying time for my teammates by getting beaten over and over again was my role. “Dwalkie, how much longer for the spell!?”
“It’s ready. But you two are too close—”
“Just fire it!”
Finally, the long-awaited Ice Lance fired. As expected, Vagos quickly backed away. He probably decided he didn’t want to get beaten up alongside me, thankfully.
Dash.

I also stepped back and got out of the Ice Lance’s vicinity. Without even taking a moment to catch my breath, I quickly stretched back my hand and pulled my shield from my backpack. I couldn’t use Giantization anyway, so I figured having the shield would be much more helpful in battle now that the arc sword was no longer on the table. I wanted to wear the breastplate if I could too.
He won’t give me enough time for that, though.

I swept away any lingering disappointment over something I couldn’t have. This wasn’t a sign of resignation, but that I was focusing more on what was urgent. Throwing away what wasn’t needed and taking only what needed to be taken. In that sense, I needed to check one thing right now. “What happened to Missha?”
“It seems her ribs broke and stabbed her intestines in the process. She’s had a potion, though, so she’ll be all right soon.”
Okay, so until then we had to fight one-on-four. This was cold-hearted, but I was glad Dwalkie wasn’t the one who was out. If it had been him, we wouldn’t have even stood a chance.
“Be careful!”
Vagos ran toward me again. Of course he wasn’t just going to wait patiently. But that was a good thing for now.
Yeah, you’re in a hurry too.

I suspected that was the case, but watching him just made me more confident. This guy wasn’t suffering from some sort of short-term status effect, as could be seen by the way he was charging forward like he didn’t even have a second to waste.
Clang!
He was pushing himself to end the match before Soul Exhaustion ended. Simply put, that meant we might get an opening if we held out for twenty minutes.
Hold out for twenty minutes? That’s nuts.

Time was not on our side. He didn’t know it, but we now only had four potions left: two advanced, one intermediate, and one high-rank. And with our current party composition, these would definitely be exhausted in just a few minutes.
“Behelahhh!”

I let out a mighty shout and pushed my shield away. Then I sprinted forward and swung my mace. I judged that taking things lying down would not buy twenty minutes. He seemed to be pleased with my shift toward recklessness. Of course, that pleasure lasted only for the first few minutes.
Dash.
If he tried to widen the distance between us, I caught up right away and focused more on offense rather than defense, whether Rotmiller’s arrows flew in or not, whether Dwalkie cast a spell or not.
“...Are you planning to die here together?” Vagos asked.

Like a person whose goal was to go down swinging, I stayed right on top of him and struck him with my mace. I called this Barbarian Persistence Mode. Ironically, this tactic actually reduced my injuries and made him not even dare to approach Dwalkie. It proved once and for all that the best defense was a good offense.
“Tsk.” The man stopped his sword mid-thrust and turned to avoid an Ice Lance. Unfortunately for him, he turned right into the path of a crossbow bolt.
Stab!

It was a monumental early hit. It didn’t dig in too deep due to his physical resistance, but since it hit his thigh, it would restrict his mobility. Perhaps he also started realizing something was happening here, because—
That’s enough of an easy mode.
At that moment, the look in his eyes changed. I quickly backed away in response. Someone willing to sacrifice things in order to gain something else was dangerous in any circumstance.

“Persistent assholes—!” I sensed a strong murderous energy from the sword he swung, as if its shackles had been released. His sword, which limited our attacks and pushed us toward defense, drew a clean arc with just one purpose. The biggest change was something else, though.
Whip!
Even though the arrow grazed his shoulder, he didn’t flinch and doubled down on his assault on me. As a result, after exchanging several blows, his blade penetrated deep into my abdomen.
Stab!
Thanks to the loss of my natural healing factor, the injury would have been fatal if left unattended.
[Your body is healing due to the effect of Recovery (Medium).]
One more bottle of potion was doled out at Rotmiller’s discretion. Now all that was left was one high-rank and two advanced. But, as if to add insult to injury, I failed to stop him.
Dash.
Like some kind of acrobat, he stepped on the swinging mace and jumped right over me.
Goddamn it.
I quickly turned around and reached out, but it was too late. The guy jumped off the ground once more and quickly closed the distance with the back line.
“Get back!” Hikurod stood in front of Dwalkie, but it didn’t do much. How could he stop that monster head-on when he didn’t have his key ability Balance Weight?
Bang!
With one kick, the dwarf flew like a soccer ball, still clutching his shield. Rotmiller tossed his crossbow aside and swung a sword. Of course, there was no way that would work.
Stab!

Vagos cut through Rotmiller’s sword all too easily, stabbing a green blade into his stomach. But the moment he tried to pull out the sword, Rotmiller gripped his hand and stopped him. “This thing’s ours.”
Shoooooot!
Fortunately, the Ice Lance fired in time. Vagos let go of the sword and stepped back.
Slump.

Without his support, Rotmiller collapsed to the floor like a puppet without strings. However, the sword that had been stuck in his abdomen had disappeared. In an effort to help the team even a little bit, he had put it in the Mimic’s Treasure Vault, which did not consume Soul Power, so that Vagos couldn’t use it.
I can save him if I give him a potion in time.
Despite my comrade’s injury, I kept my cool. However, not everyone could.

“What did you... to Rotmiller...!” Missha, who had been leaning against the wall and recovering, swung a sword at Vagos with a body that could not even move, knowing that she wouldn’t reach him. She did so for a singular purpose. “You won’t touch Dwalkie—Argh!”

Missha’s body hit the wall again as he kicked her aside. The bastard did not head straight to Dwalkie, however, but toward Missha, who had passed out. It was obvious what he was going to do. He intended to deal the final blow and steal her one remaining sword, the goddamn thieving bastard.
“We already told you. These are ours.” I swung my mace like I was using it to swat away flies and Vagos fell back from Missha without hesitation.
He laughed. “Barbarian, are you still thinking of trying to do this?”
What was this prick talking about? Wasn’t that obvious? Instead of answering, I ran toward him.
Voom!
He easily stepped back and avoided my next swing. “You really believe in that piece of trash? Someone who’s just... what, Ice Lance and Cold Eruption, minus a few curses?”

Of course. What was wrong with low-level attack spells? If they struck the brain, they could kill just the same. Even one lucky punch was enough, so Dwalkie just needed to hit him once. Until then, I’d buy time somehow.
“Dwalkie!” I shouted with all the strength I had left in me that it was time for a spell to come flying in. But what was this?
Goddamn it.
A spell did not fly.

It was no coincidence that royal family-certified wizard, Riol Warb Dwalkie, had dared to submit an application to join a team with two fighters. He had wanted to stand out as special, so he picked the team that looked the most basic. He thought that having two warriors would make the wizard look more impressive. However, it didn’t take long for the truth to come out.
“My name is Riol Warb Dwalkie. I am a rank-eight wizard and public service worker under the Rafdonian royal—”
“Aha, so you’re trash.”
Trash—someone not treated as a wizard by fellow wizards.
“Hahaha! So are we a team of all half-wits, then? I think it’s better this way. That means we don’t have to be intimidated by each other anymore.”

Still, these people were okay with that. They said they were in the same position and understood him. It felt like being saved. He even thought that maybe he had lived the past twenty-five years of his life just so he could meet them.
“You really believe in that piece of trash? Someone who’s just... what, Ice Lance and Cold Eruption, minus a few curses?”

But the reality of his situation hadn’t changed after all. Even though his time to shine had come for the first time, he couldn’t do anything right. No matter how strong his mana had become, he was still a half-wit wizard who couldn’t even live up to the expectations of his precious comrades. But, even still, he was protected by his friend.
“Get back!”
“This thing’s ours.”
He couldn’t save his laughing colleague, who had had a sword stabbed through him.
“You won’t touch Dwalkie—Argh!”

He couldn’t protect the woman he loved. His mind went blank at that realization. He struggled to breathe as helplessness crashed over him. If he could, he’d run away from this harsh reality right now.
“Unfortunately, he seems to have already given up.”
However, he couldn’t give up. Maybe he would have if he were all alone, but his precious teammate was still fighting to protect everyone on his own.
“Barbarian, you should know that this is all over.”
Despite the man’s ridicule, Bjorn silently swung his mace, even as he coughed up blood onto the man’s face. To the bitter end, he was giving his all and fighting back.
“Hey, there’s a fire in your eyes. Do you care about your comrades that much?”
As he started chanting, Dwalkie remembered a conversation he’d had in the past. It had been with the instructor at the Magic Tower’s training center, right after the Troll War.
“What? You want me to teach you a spell to fell Trolls? Mm, well... it’s not impossible.”
That day, Dwalkie had paid the master a large sum of money to learn a spell. To be more precise, he learned a combination of spells. The master agreed to teach him, but urged him to never use it.

Thought Acceleration dramatically improved the user’s cognitive ability and made the time pass more slowly. Mana Amplification temporarily stimulated the mana found in the heart to increase its output. Heart Stimulation forcibly raised the user’s heart rate and circulated mana throughout the body, and also happened to have many similarities to psychosensory magic, which was notorious for having severe side effects.
Thump-thump-thump!
Dwalkie’s heart pounded like it could explode any second, churning mana through his body. On the other hand, his mind was clearer than ever and his eyes were sharp. It felt like he could do anything.
“What’s the name? There is no exact name. It’s a combination everyone knows. However, if I were to give it a name... Hmm, well. Sacrifice probably gives off the wrong message.”
Dwalkie reached out his hand. That was all he did.
“Yes, Awakening would be more appropriate.”
Dozens of arrows of light shot out.

chapters.title: Chapter 142: Awakening (5)
paragraphs: Three minutes had passed since Dwalkie’s magical support ended. Well, maybe even shorter. Still, it felt like ten minutes.
“I admit it, barbarian. I’ve never, in my entire life, met a bastard like you.”
I did not look back once. Whether Vagos was trying to drive a wedge into this team or not, whether Dwalkie was in a state of panic or not—I decided it didn’t make a difference.
But did this guy find that boring? “I will put your soul to good use. So, just die.”

That meant that he was done playing around. He stabbed me with a dagger he took out from his waistband. It came in at such a perfect angle that it seemed impossible to block or avoid it. At best, all I could do was choose the lesser evil. I twisted my body as much as I could and gave him my lungs instead of my heart. It would be a near-fatal injury, but we still had the advanced potion left, right? After drinking it and treating this, I’d hold out somehow. Both Missha and Hikurod would wake up soon. Soul Exhaustion wouldn’t last forever.
I made the plan in a split second and was just putting it into action when a dazzling light from behind me flooded the hallway.
Shhhhhh!

Dozens of magic arrows warped into being, emitting pure white light. At the sudden downpour, the man took a step back, bewildered. But just as when Hikurod, Rotmiller, and Missha stood up to him, his reaction didn’t matter.
Whiiip!

The arrows of light pursued him, bending as if each shot had a mind of its own. In response, Vagos stopped running away and began to slash the arrows one by one using a small dagger. It didn’t look much different from someone trying to dry out a river with a gourd.
Holy...
Surprisingly, though, his actions worked. Although he became a hedgehog whose whole body was pierced by arrows of light, Vagos succeeded in protecting his vitals.
Step.

Suddenly, I heard someone behind me, and only then did I come to my senses. I had actually kind of expected it, but Dwalkie was the one standing there. Simply put, that meant the spells just now were cast by him.
“Sorry to have kept you waiting. It took me a while to make up my mind.”
“Mind? What happ—”
“That we can discuss after we get rid of that man.” Dwalkie looked away, dodging the question. At the sight, I was sure this was still the Dwalkie I knew.
What’s going on?
I couldn’t understand what was happening at all. Mana radiated from him, so concentrated that even a barbarian with a mana aptitude of zero could feel it.
It wasn’t just me wondering this. “Wizard, what have you done?” the bastard asked, even as blood dripped down his entire body. If I were him, I’d be the first to run.
“You ask, yet you already know,” Dwalkie said, his voice low and cold.
What? He knows?
As Dwalkie looked at him, Vagos went mute. What, did he really know?
“I’m sorry if you were trying to stall for time,” Dwalkie added. “I know your time’s running out.”
The heck? What the hell is going on?

Since when was Dwalkie so on the ball? It had been a while since my head couldn’t keep up with a situation. However, I could at least figure out one thing. This was a very positive development for me.
I can hear his explanation later.
I instead focused on what was right in front of me.
Dash.
Rather than sprint down the passageway and run away, Vagos’s wounded form lunged at us. “Stand back,” Dwalkie told me. “You might get hurt.”
“Ah, oh. Sure.” I couldn’t adjust to the personality change, but I did as he said. What now?
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-eight attack spell Ice Lance.]
Ice Lances large enough to fill half the passageway fired twice in a row.
Shooot!

Indeed, they shot at Vagos, releasing gusts of wind as they blew by. However, it appeared the guy had a lot of experience with magic on this scale. He calmly stared at the Ice Lances, then quickly took the arc longsword out of his subspace.
Pzzzzz!
The sword continued to spit out sparks, still rejecting his touch. However, he grabbed it and swung it anyway, the veins on his neck bulging.
Bam!

As befit an arc longsword with anti-magic properties, the huge Ice Lance shattered into pieces from a single touch of the blade. Even in the state he was in, Vagos kicked off the ground again to close the distance between us.
Dash.
Considering the way Dwalkie’s eyes went wide, this was a surprise to him too. But his shock didn’t last long.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-seven attack spell Cold Storm.]
He completed the chant in less than one second.
Shaaa!

At this point, it wasn’t ice shards but small Ice Lances pouring down. This time, too, that rotten arc longsword proved to be a problem. Vagos got closer and closer through the blizzard. When it was possible to see him with the naked eye, I spotted his form advancing forward while cutting down only the largest blocks of ice with his sword.
Yeah, he won’t go down easy.

I let out a silent sigh and prepared for what would happen next. There was nothing special about it. My life was far from that of a freeloader, and wasn’t it the fate of a tank to protect the damage dealer?
“Behelahhh!”

The first punch always won. Aiming for the moment Vagos escaped the blizzard, I swung my mace. But despite everything else going on, the guy was alert. Even though it was a surprise attack, he reacted swiftly and blocked the mace with his sword—a clash between first-grade iron and the sixth-grade material arc.
Slice!
Regardless of its thickness or density, the mace was cut through like tofu. However, Vagos was not satisfied with this and aimed for my neck next.
Pzzzzz!

At that moment, a frenzy of sparks bounced from the sword, and he flinched. His hand was red-hot and even steaming. Could the fact that his whole body was covered in burns have something to do with that sword? I couldn’t know for sure, but he put the sword back into subspace as he decided that it was no longer possible to use.
Dash.

Vagos drew his dagger again and grabbed onto me. It was very clear what he wanted. I had been wondering why he would go so far to break through that spell, but it seemed that this was what he was aiming for.
“Bjorn, get away from him!”
It was a strategy similar to the Barbarian Persistence Mode I used before: using me as a shield to suppress Dwalkie’s magic. Huh, I didn’t realize I would end up getting used like this.
[Riol Warb Dwalkie has cast the rank-nine curse spell Slowdown.]
Instead of attack magic, curses were stacked on Vagos, but it wasn’t easy to get rid of him because he was clinging to me and swinging the dagger.
Okay, let’s try this.
I stabbed him with the mace that had been turned into a bamboo spear. After all, he didn’t necessarily have to be killed with magic.
Stab!

He wasn’t as difficult to deal with as before thanks to the reinforced Slowdown spell. Instead of Ice Lance or Cold Storm, Dwalkie maintained and exerted fine control over a small number of Magic Arrows. The situation was clearly in my favor, but that made me even more alert.
There’s no way he doesn’t know that too.
The bastard knew what was going on here, even though Dwalkie had avoided telling me. But he ran at me anyway. Why?
“I know your time’s running out.”
The answer was time. Dwalkie couldn’t maintain this state for much longer. Perhaps Vagos knew more about the time he had left than even Dwalkie did.
“Dwalkie, use Cold Storm!” I made a snap decision. And, judging by the expression on Vagos’s face, it was the right one.
However, Dwalkie hesitated. “But...!” Although he had changed somewhat, Dwalkie was still Dwalkie.
“Don’t worry about me and just use it!”
When I shouted a reprimand, Dwalkie cast the spell. Cold swirled over Dwalkie’s hand.
“Can you tolerate the cold well?” I asked Vagos.
“Deranged bastard.”
Hey, more praise. I raised my shield and distanced myself from Vagos. Blocking the incoming chunks of ice with the shield, I was determined to get through this somehow.
Shaaaaaa!

Soon, a blizzard once again filled the part of the passageway the two of us were standing in, freezing our skin. But what was this? Through the blizzard, in which it was difficult to see even an inch ahead, the man thrust a dagger.
Stab!

A blade of about eight inches penetrated deep into my lungs. I couldn’t breathe. In the meantime, chunks of ice flew at me and slammed into my body. Crystals as sharp as Ice Lances grazed my skin. But I wasn’t just going to sit here and take more damage.
Stab!
My body reacted first, and I thrust the short spear that was once my mace forward with all my might. At that moment, the snowstorm ended earlier than expected and visibility returned.
Shaaaaa.

The first thing I did was take a quick look around. Surprisingly, in that short moment, three unexpected events had unfolded. The first was that Dwalkie was kneeling on the floor with blood pouring from his eyes, nose, mouth, and ears. The second was that the short spear that I haphazardly thrust had pierced the guy’s heart.
[The activation conditions for Regal Vagos’s Second Heart have been met.]
The third was that it turned out that there was one more numbered item that he hadn’t used yet. Ha, I really didn’t want to curse like this anymore... but this fucking goddamned motherfucker.
[Until Regal Vagos’s heart recovers, they will be under absolute protection.]

Something red, reminiscent of muscle, covered his body. Looking at this, I thought, How the hell am I supposed to kill this bastard? Could he really be killed? I didn’t know, but for now, I just vomited blood.
Blechhh! Cough!

The heart-shaped shell did not even sizzle when covered in acid blood. I turned away without regret. No. 3120: Second Heart was a consumable numbered item that activated when instant-death damage was dealt to the heart. At my current level, no matter what I did, I couldn’t break through that barrier surrounding him. So, I’d have to focus on what I needed to do.
Trudge, trudge.

I forced my body, which couldn’t even breathe properly, to take slow steps. Thankfully, Dwalkie was a cold-attributed wizard. If it weren’t for the Frostbite state he was in, blood would probably be gushing out of him by now.

“Dwalkie.” To say that Dwalkie’s condition, still on his knees, was bleak was an understatement. Blood flowed from every pore of his body. When I checked his pulse, I felt his heart palpitating like the speed limit on it was broken. “Please... hold on.”
Since I couldn’t see any external trauma, I poured an advanced potion into his mouth—only half of it, though, because there were other people dying right now.
Trudge, trudge.
I walked as fast as I could. With each step I took, my stomach twisted and I couldn’t breathe, but I used the short spear as a staff to speed myself up.

“Rot... miller...” Fortunately, he was alive, at least for now. He was headed toward death in a completely different way than Dwalkie was. His heartbeat was faint like it could stop at any moment. I poured the remaining advanced potion on his wounds.
Chhhhhh!

The wounds boiled and began to heal. I sat down next to him and focused on my breathing. I kept coughing and blood gushed from my mouth, but all I could do was persevere and wait for Rotmiller to recover. After all, the two remaining potions were in this old man’s Treasure Vault.
Maybe a minute had passed before... “B-Bjorn...!” The dwarf, who had passed out after getting his head slammed into the wall, came to his senses. “What about Dwalkie? Where is Dwalkie?”
Hey, I’m dying too. Does your best friend come first?
Without the strength to speak, I pointed in Dwalkie’s direction.
“W-What the hell happened!?” He rushed over, inspected Dwalkie, and carefully picked him up to carry him toward us.
“Ugh...” Missha, who was lying about four yards away from the wall I was leaning on, struggled to raise her head. “...Bjorn?”
“Alive.”
“Good...”
As always, I only have you.
Missha struggled to stand up, holding her broken ribs. Then she came over and sat down next to me. “Rotmiller...?”
“I gave him... a potion,” I coughed.
It was like a gathering of the sick. I wanted to rest a bit, but after he finished transporting Dwalkie, Hikurod came to me and bandaged up my injury.
“Bjorn, what happened!? What is that strange shell over there?”
I didn’t want to explain. I didn’t have the energy, and what difference did it make, anyway? I focused on breathing and closed my eyes.
“I’m sorry. You must be tired too. Rest. I’ll take care of the rest somehow.”
The dwarf apologized and headed back over to Dwalkie to get filled in.
[Your Soul Exhaustion has lifted.]

Finally, about a minute later, my stats returned to normal and it became a little easier to breathe. Even if I didn’t have a natural regeneration ability anymore, the durability of my body itself was different. I slowly opened my eyes.
“...Hey! Hang on, my friend!”
“B-Bjorn...? Rotmillerrr is shaking. H-He should be fine, right...?”
The line between life and death was being drawn.

chapters.title: Chapter 143: Awakening (6)
paragraphs: Concentration and decision-making were important to survival—what to give up and what to choose. The more rationally I solved a problem, the higher the survival rate. However, this time I couldn’t do that.

There were three wounded and one bottle of advanced potion. Truthfully, the best course of action would have been to let Rotmiller drink the entire bottle. I had to revive him as quickly as possible and take out the other potions from the Treasure Vault. Then, the right course of action would be to treat me with a high-grade potion and feed Dwalkie the remaining advanced potion.
However, if I had done that, Dwalkie would have died.
It was difficult to make a rational decision. Even though I already knew all of the above in my head, my body had fed half of the potion to Dwalkie without the slightest hint of hesitation.
“Both of you, please hold on! Let’s all get out of this damn place alive!”

As a result, any certainty was gone. Because I hadn’t been able to give up on Dwalkie, I couldn’t even guarantee Rotmiller’s survival. Half a bottle of potion would have been enough for him if consumed right away, but the problem was that he’d been given it too late. Simply put, high risk, high return. I wanted the whole team to survive, so I made an irrational decision that might have just killed them all.
“B-Bjorn...”
I approached Rotmiller and checked his pulse and breathing. I hoped he would hold on. If this man died like this, all five of us would be as good as dead.
Ten minutes.
After that, the Dragon Slayer would wake up. Right now, the only one who was fine was the dwarf. If Hikurod couldn’t block Vagos, it would all be over.

“Oh, right! The stone chamber! Bjorn, what was that stone chamber!?” Hikurod, standing guard at Dwalkie’s side, looked at me and asked about the stone chamber that we’d finally found after searching the maze for twelve hours. The question was filled with hope. “Elixir? Potion? Was there anything like that inside? Ah, if there were, you would’ve packed it, right? Or, is it a healing spring or something like that?”
“...That stone chamber isn’t for that purpose.”
“Then, what is it!? We worked so hard to find it! There must be something!” Hikurod demanded, hoping for a certain answer.
I knew it was best not to answer questions like this, but after a brief pause, I opened my mouth. “That stone chamber is a trap room.”
“Trap room...?”
“Yes, opening the box inside will take you back to the starting point.”

If the bastard and the priest had appeared at the same time, I had been considering discarding Plan A immediately and using it to get to the portal and escape. In that situation, there would be no chance of winning no matter what I did.
“Y-Yeah! Then let’s use that and go back! That will do!”
“Hikurod Murad, snap out of it. Even if we can get back to the Tower, nothing will change.”

Getting to the Tower wasn’t going to give us any potions. Going back was impossible to begin with, unless we were planning to rob an empty room. And heading for the portal in an injured state? That was suicide. The priest of Karui, who I believed had changed his class with the divine power of a High Priest, would be guarding it.
“Oh, right! The priest! Wasn’t there an old man like a priest in their party? Let’s find him.”
“Stop.”
“From what I can tell, he must have been forced to follow him. If that’s true—”
“Stop it, Hikurod.”
“How can I stop? They’re both dying—something has to be done!” the dwarf cried, as if screaming at his own powerlessness.
“There is nothing we can do now,” I said coldly. “All we can do is watch.”
“Truly... is that all?”
“Yes.”
The dice had already left our hands. There were three possibilities that could unfold: we all lived, we all died, or some of us died and some lived.
Each minute and second passed like eternity. Eventually, Dwalkie regained consciousness. “The man... what happened...?”
“Dwalkie! Don’t speak!”
“Yes, stay still. As soon as Rotmiller wakes up, take the potion—”
Watching us babble above him, Dwalkie asked again, “The man...? What happened to him?” As if that was more important than his life, that was the only thing he asked when he opened his eyes.
I pondered this for a moment. Should I tell him the truth? I didn’t have to think for long, though. “Not dead.”
“But thanks to you, the immediate danger has passed. Leave it to us and rest.”
“I-I can’t do that.” Dwalkie shook his head desperately. “T-Time... is running out.”
“Did you not hear me? When Rotmiller wakes up, the potion—”
“Th-this is not s-something that can be treated... with a potion.”

There was a moment of silence at those words, and I calmly faced the facts. “...I see.” I still didn’t know what Dwalkie had done. However, he was the one who best knew his current situation. Dwalkie, who longed for life more than anyone else, had been the one to say it couldn’t be treated, so there was no point in denying it.
“What are you talking about?! I-It’s an advanced potion!”
“He’s rrright! You should know, too, what this thing is. S-So stop saying weirrrd things—”
“Miss Karlstein.” Dwalkie opened his eyes and looked at us. “Hikurod and... Bjorn.”

All he did was say each of our names, but having lived through many deaths after spending my childhood in a hospital, I knew what Dwalkie was about to do now. “Tell me. I will pass it on to Rotmiller.”

“...Thank you.” This was the flickering of a candle whose wick had run out. As if to leave something behind in this world, as if to be remembered, it emitted its greatest light in its final moments. “I have something to tell you all.”
Soon, the trembling in Dwalkie’s voice stopped.

His mother had loved the sea, that unfamiliar thing that she had never seen but only heard about. She wished to see it at least once in her life. He hadn’t been able to understand it when he was young, but as he grew older, he came to.
“There are things... you yearn to have because you cannot have them.”
There were some things like that in the world. Because they were unfamiliar, because they were things he couldn’t possess, they shone all the brighter.
“You all were that to me.”

He had been lucky—far more than he deserved. He had met nice people and explored. They had talked a lot and comforted each other. The empty spot that he thought would remain empty had finally been filled. So, he had to say it.

“Everyone, thank you for being my teammates.” He hadn’t said it before now because of embarrassment. These were words that had always been postponed, put off for later, but words that would be buried in his heart forever if he didn’t say them now.
Slide.
Dwalkie looked ahead with hazy eyes.
“Noooo! Don’t say that! Hm? Dwalkie, please...” The woman he loved was crying. That wasn’t what he wanted.
Slide.
He shifted his gaze sideways.

A dear friend looked at him and smiled. “I am... also thankful you were my friend. That you joined... a party I made.” He was grateful for the way Hikurod smiled through that trembling beard. And he was sorry. He’d promised to visit the smithy one day. Now he couldn’t keep that promise.
Slide.
He shifted his gaze again.

“Riol Warb Dwalkie.” The last was a rival and the type of comrade he had yearned for. Unlike him, a coward, Bjorn was a warrior who always fought to the bitter end and protected everyone. He gazed at Dwalkie with calm eyes. “I apologize. I misunderstood you. You were a greater wizard and teammate than anyone else. And the choice you made was heroic and noble,” said the man who was always stingy with praise, the warrior who never put words in his mouth he didn’t mean. “It was an honor to work with you.”

It was overwhelming, and he felt somehow relieved. He was being recognized for the first time. A great warrior, one who lived like a hero in a story, was telling him it had been an honor to know him. A half-wizard like him had added his own flourishes to a page of this warrior’s journey. With that, he could die in peace. Yes... he should be able to.
But why am I...
He was angry. This was unfair, scary, and hopeless.
Why...?
That was what death was—being erased from the next page of someone’s story.
“Do you have anything more to say? If you wish, we will step aside.” Soon the warrior spoke, and only then did Dwalkie realize the reason he felt this way.
“Nooo! Dwalkie! Don’t die! Please, hmm?”
There were some people in the world who shined. To him, Missha was one of those people. He still hadn’t said those words yet.
This must be selfishness.

He tried his best to cast aside his greed. There wouldn’t be another chance for him to say it after this, but because of that, he had to swallow it back. Her journey wouldn’t end today. He didn’t want to linger as a dark shadow for the rest of her life. If he was truly doing this for her, that was the right thing to do.
So, Dwalkie opened his mouth. “Bjorn.”
“...Do you have something to say to me?”
“I do.” Words were the only thing a departing person could leave behind. “You are not sneaky. Please stop averting your eyes and face it head-on.”
The warrior did not ask. He must have known what Dwalkie meant by that. He was much too smart and wise to call a barbarian.
“Answer... me...”
“All right.”
Dwalkie, who had finally received an answer, smiled brightly from the bottom of his heart. This was all the time he had been allotted.
The warrior’s eyes suddenly grew cold. “...He’s awake.”

Dwalkie’s fading heart began to thump again. The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos. Although he had fought him at the cost of his life, he was an enemy Dwalkie hadn’t been able to overcome. “Can you... win?”
“Don’t worry. We will definitely return home alive.”

With that, all of Dwalkie’s anxiety disappeared. He also dismissed his concern that his death would be a meaningless one. If this trustworthy warrior was saying that, it must be so. He could let go of his burdens now.
Slide.

He closed his eyes. Sound faded and the darkness around him deepened. With a gradually dulling mind, he thought, If I lived a heroic life, one that ended up recorded in a book, even if it was short, what would be written as the final sentence?
A rather plausible possibility came to mind. It might not have been a very fitting description for a wizard’s end, but it wasn’t bad, either.
Team Half-Wit’s wizard, Riol Warb Dwalkie, after protecting a precious comrade from a member of Orcules, the Dragon Slayer Regal Vagos, died bravely in battle.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: First death of a companion character.]
[Reward: Permanently increases your Spirit stat by +1.]

There was no paradise to escape to. From the first moment I learned the identity of this bastard, the Dragon Slayer Regal Vagos, this thought had been solidified more and more. He was a member of the group Orcules, which looked down even on the king. Although we hadn’t made introductions, it wouldn’t be difficult for him to find us. If he wanted to retaliate, the city wouldn’t be safe for us.

I had come up with a plan to get rid of him by taking advantage of the Guardian of Balance effect. I determined that if we didn’t take care of him now, there would never be another chance. But how did that end up?
Thump!
My heart beat lowly. My new plan had failed. A battle had been fought, but I hadn’t been able to save everyone.
Thump!
Even when I fought back, there was no paradise to be found. It wasn’t that I hadn’t already known that, because no such fictitious place existed anywhere in the world.
Thump!
Unlike my own quietly beating heart, this guy’s heart wasn’t beating anymore.
“Hikurod, you must prepare to fight.”
“I know.”

I stood up, using the mace as a staff. Those left behind had their own work to do. I gathered my breath and gazed into the passageway. The bastard was getting out from inside the shell, which had opened wide like a flower petal. It was time to end this bloody fight.

chapters.title: Chapter 144: The Great Inheritance (1)
paragraphs: Thump!

Regal Vagos opened his eyes to the sound of his heart pounding in his head. It was dark all around. His body wouldn’t move and he could feel sticky slime on his skin, as if he had been curled up in amniotic fluid.
Did I end up using this ability too?

It didn’t feel like a waste, though. If it had been his head and not his heart that had been stabbed, no matter who he was, he would definitely have died. He just had one question: how had things reached this point? It reminded him of a conversation he’d once had with an old teammate, before he had abandoned the heavenly principles and put a terrible curse on his body.
“Want to know why you lose money every time? You only bet and raise as much as you need each round. Even during moments when you need a big win.”

Of course, card games and battles were different. It would be absurd to apply the words themselves to his current situation, but the context was similar. Until all five cards were gathered in a complete set, the winner was still up in the air.
Thump!

To put it simply, it was a lack of decisiveness on his part. He managed to get this far by giving things up one at a time. He gave up nearly a year looking for the item he needed, and he gave in and used Dragon Speech. Still, these persistent bastards didn’t give up. He swung the Dragon Sword several times, even if it meant having to recuperate for at least a year, but they persevered. Now he had even used Second Heart.
Thump!
Vagos finally admitted it to himself. Because he had underestimated the enemy, and because he did not put everything on the line to face them as worthy opponents, things had gotten this far.
Thump, thump, thump.
The beat of his regenerated heart quickened and light returned to his eyes. He wiped off the mucus that clung to his body and stood up.

There was a barbarian across the passageway. He was already walking toward him with a hole in his lungs and red blood dripping from his mouth, without even getting support from the dwarf warrior next to him.
Trudge, trudge.
He was walking desperately with only one goal in mind: to kill his enemy.
Slide.

Vagos released his grip on the dagger at his waist and reconsidered his plan. The curse on his heart from using Dragon Speech had healed to some extent. The remnants of the curse remained intact, but his physical ability had returned to a certain level and he could use the power again too. This wouldn’t have been the case if it had not been for the distinct feature of the dragon people: that their source of power was located in the heart. This was an unexpected turn of events for him too, as this was his first time using Second Heart. He could perhaps say this was a happy accident. Thanks to that, his odds of winning were much higher.
Trudge.

Of course, his opponents seemed to have recovered from their Soul Exhaustion, too, but that changed nothing. All he had to do was defeat the dwarf warrior. Even that barbarian wouldn’t be able to stop him by himself with an injured body like that. Or so he thought, at least until he met his eyes.
It’s like looking at some kind of immortal god.

Instead of a dagger, Vagos grabbed the arc longsword. Because of the remnants of the curse left in his heart, as soon as he gripped it, excruciating pain overtook him. He instinctively sensed that using this here may mean he could never use this arm again. No, he was certain of it.
But if I want to kill that persistent bastard, I’ll have to risk it.
Give up an arm to kill an enemy so that he can survive.
“Come, barbarian.” He was determined to put it all on the line.
I took staggering steps forward. Hikurod was beside me and behind us was Missha, who insisted on fighting by herself.
“Good choice.”

The dwarf said that like he was concerned for Missha, but that wasn’t the only reason. Rotmiller hadn’t gotten up yet. If he woke up from his sleep, someone had to take the potion out of Treasure Vault and throw it to us from behind.
“So that man killed Dwalkie...”
“Hikurod, keep your cool. If you die, we are all finished.”
“...I will.” The dwarf tried to swallow back his burning anger. He must have been well aware how important his role right now was.
Trudge.
We took more steps and closed the distance between us and our opponent. It wasn’t long before we were able to see each other’s facial expressions. There was no need for a lengthy exchange.

“Come, barbarian.” Vagos stared at us with the arc longsword in hand again, apparently not sick of this yet. Damn it all, what the hell did it mean that he could take it out and use it whenever he needed it? Curses filled my throat, but there was no time to spit them out.
Dash.

The bastard ran toward us when we didn’t move. But what was this? It wasn’t comparable to our first encounter, but he was moving faster than the last time I saw him. In other words, his body had recovered quite a bit. How, though? I was certain his injuries weren’t short-term. Unexpected surprises were popping up from the start.
Slice!

Hikurod’s shield was cut through like tofu as he stood in front of me. I stabbed Vagos with the mace that had turned into a spear and drove him away, then handed the lithinum shield over to Hikurod without any regrets. “Use this.” My shield wasn’t in perfect condition, either, but I judged it to be better than a steel buckler.
Kak kak kak!

Vagos’s subsequent attacks penetrated deep into the shield. It was immediately repaired through Emergency Restoration, but Hikurod wouldn’t be able to use the ability again and again as Soul Exhaustion had just been lifted.
Nothing is going according to plan.
The bastard woke up earlier than expected. And besides the heart, other parts of him had been healed as well. He was even using skills he hadn’t been able to before.
[Regal Vagos has cast High-Rank Acceleration.]

As if ignoring the laws of physics, his blade seemed to slice through time itself. The dwarf chose to avoid the hit rather than block it, but he wouldn’t be able to clear the distance. Therefore, I sacrificed my left arm, which had no shield anyway.
Flesh Burst.
My outstretched hand exploded into dozens of chunks of flesh, but Vagos didn’t back down.
Chhhhhh!
Covered in acid blood and groaning, Vagos followed through on his swing, his sword cutting deep into Hikurod’s thigh.
Smack!
The dwarf hit him in the jaw with his battle hammer despite that. Vagos stiffened, indicating that the blow did do some damage. I immediately jumped forward, grabbed his shoulder, and rolled.
Flesh Burst.
I thrust my left arm, which had already become useless, into his gaping mouth and exploded it.
“Aaagh!” He screamed and pushed me away, and at the same time stabbed the sword right into my neck.
Shatter!
A glass bottle hit the back of my head and broke, spilling out its contents.
[Your body is rapidly regenerating due to the effect of Recovery (Advanced).]
This pain was that of an advanced potion. Wait, this meant Rotmiller had survived. I stepped back, brushing off these fleeting thoughts.
Stab!
The sword that pierced my neck came out, leaving me dizzy. This son of a bitch did not allow a moment’s rest. “Dieee!” The sword pierced my stomach and ripped through my intestines in an instant.
Taking a page out of the dwarf’s book, I took a step forward and thrust the short spear at him.
Tap.
Vagos hurriedly pulled his sword out and widened the distance, and I used Giantization without hesitation.
Where the fuck do you think you’re going?
I stabbed Vagos in the shoulder and spewed out a fountain of blood. However, it seemed this bastard had also come prepared for a sudden-death round. He took a step forward and swung his sword again.
It was already too late to avoid it. I grabbed the sword with my raggedy arm. Fleshless fingers were taken off and the sword came to a halt as it got caught in my wrist bone.
[Your HP is below 20 percent. All Resistance and Resilience stats have increased due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]

This was the synergistic effect of Ironskin and Path of Heroes. I lifted the short spear stuck in his shoulder and twisted it around, but he persevered as well, applying more strength to his sword thrust. A power struggle began. Unfortunately, he was the winner.
[Regal Vagos has cast Divine Blade.]
His sword, which began to glow with white light, cut diagonally up to my elbow.
Boom.
My arm fell to the ground, still Giantized, and I angled the cut side so it spurted acid blood into his face.
Chhhhhh!
“Aaah!”
Oh, you bastard with no pain tolerance. How dare you hold out?
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has ended.]
Due to a lack of Soul Power, my body shrank back to its original state in less than a few seconds. As a result, his feet, which had risen into the air, also touched the ground.
Dash.
Had I underestimated this guy’s determination? Instead of stepping back, Vagos thrust his sword again.
Damn it all.

Did a ninth-floor adventurer have no fear? Why was he so good at dogfighting? I was going to get stabbed in the head at this rate, so I quickly twisted out of the way and stepped back. I lost the skewer, the short spear that used to be a mace, as a result. To make matters worse, I stopped healing.
We’re fucked.

Even an advanced potion had its limits. And I hadn’t even gotten to drink it—it had been poured onto me. With my arm blown off and my organs shredded, even just maintaining my current state was a struggle.
“My... win!” Vagos ran toward me. It really was hopeless. I could already picture the worst in my head: an inevitable death.

But, so what? I had no intention of giving up and just accepting that. I stared at his sword with my eyes wide open until the end. As soon as he approached, I rolled to the side. Regardless of whether I would be defenseless against the attack that followed, it was my best option right now.
Boom.

Rolling on the floor, I used the recoil to get back on my feet—just in time to see his arc longsword fill my line of sight as it swung toward me. But then, as if an invisible force had yanked him back by the collar, he fell backward.
How the hell did that happen? When I looked up for an answer, I saw the old man in black priestly robes standing in the distance.
“Old man! What are you doing?!” Vagos shouted.
Ludwig closed his eyes and ears. But regardless, from the sounds he could hear, it was clear just how desperately they were fighting.
“So, you won’t run away.”
“Protect Dwalkie!”
At first, it had been painful to watch. He thought that putting up meaningless resistance would only lead to even greater despair and suffering.
“Why on earth do they...?” As their desperate fight continued, Ludwig found himself constantly asking questions.
“This thing’s ours.”
Why don’t they surrender?
“Noooo! Dwalkie! Don’t die! Please, hmm?”
Because they rejected the inevitable and naïvely held out hope? No, even so, why?
“Can you... win?”
“Don’t worry. We will definitely return home alive.”
Why can they still keep burning so brightly?
The answer was simple—they were strong, unlike him, who didn’t have the courage to shoulder sacrifice.

Ludwig knew, too, that no matter how much he waited, the day he hoped for would never come. Returning to the city with his grandson... that bright future had never existed in the first place. He just hadn’t had the courage to accept it.

“May the blessing of the twilight star guide me.” Ludwig made a short sign of the cross. His eyes were open and no longer trembled with fear. He just stared straight ahead, more certain than ever. “I will follow your will.”

Of the three gods, the Goddess of the Stars, Reatlas, presided over adventures and fate. As someone who had once served and followed her, how could he dismiss this as a coincidence? In front of a man who had given up on courage, these adventurers who embraced such a brilliant light had appeared. It was the final blessing given to this lost sheep.
“Even if I may not be held in your embrace...” The old man looked into the void and shouted, “Karui, I offer myself.”
At his words, the capricious god laughed gleefully, as if this was the moment he had been waiting for. There was no way he didn’t know what Ludwig was trying to do. “What do you wish for?”
“Send me there.”
“Your grandson will not be saved.”
His heart flinched at those words, but at the same time, they alleviated some of his weakness. He abandoned the thought of compromise. It was too late to turn back the clock. “It doesn’t matter.”
After all, he had learned from a young wizard he met in a maze that one could always be heroic and noble, if they only wished to be.

chapters.title: Chapter 145: The Great Inheritance (2)
paragraphs: The ancient, evil god Karui, unlike the other three gods in this world, demanded his subordinates pay an immeasurable price. He did not give graciously and instead only made desperate wishes come true without any distinction between good and evil. The payment offered just had to be enough. No more, no less—just right.
“I’ll allow it.”

The moment he finally heard the answer he had been waiting for, a beast’s arm tore through space itself to rip off Ludwig’s arm. When he came to his senses, he was standing in a place he had only been looking at before. This was undoubtedly the power of a devil, especially since there was always a price to pay.
“My... win!”
Right at the moment he had made up his mind, the desperate battle was coming to an end. Ludwig urgently reached out his hand, and that was enough.
“I will take it.”
He didn’t even have to explain to the evil god what it was he wanted in return.
“Old man! What are you doing?!” The body of the Dragon Slayer, who had thrust his sword at the barbarian warrior, bounced back as it was met with fierce resistance.
Rip!

Both Ludwig’s ears were torn off, a permanent sacrifice to the evil god that could not be healed with any divine power or potion. A pain seared through him that couldn’t even be compared to being lit on fire. However, Ludwig only thought of one thing.
Yes, those people are fighting through pain like this as well.
“Old man! Heal me!” the Dragon Slayer commanded, his eyes emitting a black light.

Against his will, Ludwig’s body moved as if possessed. Even more so than the threat to his grandson, whose soul Vagos had in his possession, this was because of one of Vagos’s supernatural powers, Subordination. As long as that cursed ability was binding him, Ludwig could not resist his commands.
“I will count to ten.”

The moment the huge beast’s claws tore off his remaining arm, his body stopped advancing against his will. But it still wasn’t enough. There were still many things he wished for, and he had much left to offer. Legs, eyes, heart, lungs—anything would do. He would give every part of his wretched body, which was nearing its end, if it could help the young heroes on their way. He would even give up the hope of ending his exhausting life and resting in Her arms.
“Give me the strength to kill that man.”
Ludwig spoke, and the evil god answered, “Impossible.”

It wasn’t a refusal. It was just that no matter how much he valued willful sacrifice, the payment Ludwig was offering wasn’t enough. However, Ludwig brushed off any lingering disappointment. This was different from the resignation he had been feeling every day for years. Wasn’t it just a second ago that he gave up on hoping for the impossible and decided to do everything he could?
The amount of freedom that the evil god had granted him was just ten seconds. There was no time to wallow in despair. “Then let me protect them.”
Ludwig spoke again, and the evil god laughed. “I’ll allow it.”
The beast’s arms reached out from the darkness, tore his body apart, and swallowed him.

The relief from escaping a near-death situation was momentary. Questions cropped up. How did the priest of Karui get here from four hours away, and why would he do anything to harm the Dragon Slayer? Could this all be part of another plan?

“Old man! What are you doing?!” From the look on the Dragon Slayer’s face, it didn’t seem like that was the case. To put it simply, this was also a surprise to him. However, it was difficult to see this as a positive. “Old man! Heal me!”

A black light began to glow from Vagos’s eyes as the priest stumbled backward, even dropping his sword. It was obvious what it was: Subordination, the ability of the rank-three essence that Vagos possessed. This was an OP skill that allowed the user to absorb the souls of the dead to increase their stats and, although there were some use conditions, allowed them to enslave a target if used on the living.
Step.

Soon, the priest stepped forward as if possessed. But right when everything seemed to be over, his remaining arm was ripped off as he apparently offered a sacrifice to an evil god hidden in the darkness.
Step.

The priest stopped walking. “Terrifying” wasn’t a strong enough word to describe how he looked. It looked like his two ears and arms had been bitten off by beasts. However, despite the state he was in, the priest spoke. “Give me the strength to kill that man.”

Only then did I truly understand the situation, who this unknown priest was speaking to, and what kind of deal was being made. If all my predictions were correct, there was a way for us to get out of this alive.

“Impossible.” The priest received a refusal in response to his request. The voice echoed through the passageway as if addressing everyone here. There were mixed reactions to this—while our hearts sunk, a brief light appeared in the Dragon Slayer’s eyes.
And at that moment—“Then let me protect them”—the priest’s request continued without the slightest hint of hesitation.
I heard laughter from somewhere. “I’ll allow it.”

The priest fell to the floor. This made sense, considering the two legs that had been supporting his body had been torn off. However, the evil god was a contradictory being that offered both hope and despair in turns.
Whooom!

So, in return, a portal made of black light formed in the center of the passageway. The color of the glow was different, but it was still a portal, the highest level of magic—and one that could open a door to the city from the labyrinth.
Whizz!
Soon, the mana-dense dimensional gate began to show what lay beyond it. It was not the familiar gray city of Rafdonia, but a dark and gloomy underground fortress.

“Old man! What are you doing!? Stop right now—!” As if an invisible gust of wind was dragging him, the body of the Dragon Slayer was slowly pulled back toward the portal. “Don’t you care what happens to your grandson!?”
The Dragon Slayer shouted in anger, but the priest just stubbornly replied, “This is something that should have been done long ago.”
“Fuuuck!” Perhaps Vagos had also accepted that there was no way to stop the priest’s plan, because he roared at me and then shifted his eyes to look at something. He stretched out his hand.
Slide.

The arc longsword, which had been left without an owner, scratched the ground as it began to move toward him as if magnetized. It was very clear what he was trying to do. Wherever he was going, he planned to take this with him.
Goddamn sword fetish bastard.
I forced my staggering legs to move and threw myself forward, not toward the remorseless piece of Dragon Slayer shit, but toward the sword being pulled to him.
Thud.
I was left dazed from the impact of my tattered body hitting the ground, but I reached out and grabbed the sword anyway.
Pzzzzzz!

The sword emitted heat as soon as I touched it, as if it had the imprint of its owner. Thanks to Pain Resistance, the pain was bearable, but I could clearly feel numbness taking over my hand. I got the sense that holding this for just a few more minutes could render my arm useless forever.
...Did this guy continue to use this sword despite that?
Any unnecessary questions that crossed my mind were immediately erased. I didn’t need to think about any of that right now.
“You!”

I had to endure this, even if I had to put my weight on the ground and drive my teeth into the floor so that the blade that he would one day point at me wouldn’t be this one ever again. So that it couldn’t harm my teammates.
Kak kak kak!
In an instant, the pull became stronger. My body began to slip as I lost traction. At this speed, there was a good chance I’d be sucked into the portal along with the sword.
Damn it, should I let go now?
Just as the thought was popping into my head—
C-Cough!
The bastard coughed up blood and the feeling of resistance disappeared.
Yeah, this would be too much for you too.

A moment later, he called to me. “Barbarian... You’ll see me again,” he bit out. It was a line that a dirty villain would say, something even Missha would be embarrassed to hear. He didn’t even say what he was going to do after that.
Thump!

My heart pounded at the warning. The skewer stabbed in his shoulder, his half-crushed jawbone, the murderous energy that made my skin tingle, and his right hand which had gone from red to black and smoking, all told me that if that day came, I wouldn’t be as lucky as I was today. This was clearer than hundreds of curses. But what about it?
Grip.

The fact that he was a member of Orcules, a ninth-floor adventurer with the nickname of Dragon Slayer? The fact that there wouldn’t be a Guardian of Balance next time? I already knew all that. Yeah, I couldn’t defeat this man right now. And if he had another trick up his sleeve, I would have to struggle desperately just like today.
Shaaa!

But I would survive because that was what I did best. Because that was what I’d been doing my whole life. Because it was something I had to keep doing in the future. I would survive and become stronger so that someday, when I no longer needed a fluke to beat him, I’d go find him.
“We will meet again, dragon man.”
You’re not the only one who lost something today.
Shaaa!
The portal’s greedy maw swallowed his body and despawned. At the same time, a warm light began to permeate my body. Not just mine, but everyone else’s too.
Divine power?
I stared at my hand blankly. Slowly but steadily, the wound was healing. And unlike when using a potion, there was no pain, only warmth.
Slide.

Only then did I come to my senses and look behind me. I saw the body of the priest, which had been torn to shreds. Could it even be called a body now? It had no arms or legs. Dark red blood flowed from its dug-out eye sockets, and his nose was cut off, making him look like a corpse on the battlefield. In addition, the things that should have been in his abdomen, which had a vertical slice running through it, were gone.
“Why...?” I muttered involuntarily. What on earth had this old man offered so much for, and to utter strangers like us?
Then I heard a faint sound coming from the priest. “Letter... pocket...”
I was in disbelief, but I quickly approached him and searched his robe. A letter appeared, crumpled and worn at the corners.
“Reat...”
“Don’t worry. Rest. I will make sure to deliver this letter to the Church of Reatlas.”

“Thank...” The priest closed his eyes. His body was covered in blood, but his wrinkled face was clean and at ease. As I stared at it, I felt like I was in a dream. How had he managed to talk in this state?
I couldn’t stand it and decided to ask, because I wouldn’t have another chance. “Why did you save us?”

Because it was the right thing to do? Well, if he had such sentiments, he would have had a shot at being freed long ago. Why today? It couldn’t simply have been a coincidence, and I was very curious about the reasoning behind it.
There was no answer. Could it be that he was already dead? As I began to stand, the priest’s lips parted slightly. “Wi... zar...”

The sentence was never completed, but it was enough. “I see. Thank you for telling me.” I got up without any regrets. There were many things I wanted to ask, but I got the sense that the old man was already gone.
I paused and took in the distinct, oppressive silence. Enjoying the afterglow of this quiet, I inwardly whispered, We survived.
Hikurod, Missha, and Rotmiller had survived.
But I can’t say I kept my promise like this.
I smiled bitterly as I looked down the passageway at my teammate’s corpse.
“Can you... win?”
“Don’t worry. We will definitely return home alive.”

I had said that confidently, but he was the one who had actually saved us in the end. The thing that had made it possible for all of us to get out of here alive was something that couldn’t be described as luck—it was closer to a miracle from a god.
Riol Warb Dwalkie was just a wizard who had fought to the bitter end. And this was the inheritance he had left us.

chapters.title: Chapter 146: The Great Inheritance (3)
paragraphs: Pzzzzz.
I picked up the sword I had momentarily set down and returned to where my comrades were. Then, I put the sword into my bag. It was clearly not an ordinary arc sword, but I’d look into that later.
“I’m sorry. I... just like earlier...” Hikurod trailed off and lowered his head, ashamed.
I just patted his shoulder. What could I say to him? I wasn’t the reason we had all survived either.
“Bjorn.” Missha approached with a sad gait and set her hand on my chest. “I’m glad... that you’re alive. Trrruly...”
It felt like something was climbing up my throat. I knew who I owed my continued safety and survival to. He must have wanted to share in this happy moment with us.

“Rotmiller.” I covered Missha’s small hand with mine and carefully pushed it away to keep walking. Then I approached Rotmiller, who had regained consciousness, and relayed the last few words of the will Dwalkie had left behind.

“I see. He...” After hearing everything I had to say, Rotmiller knelt down in front of Dwalkie’s corpse and made the sign of the cross. The goodbyes he couldn’t properly convey weighed down the air in front of him. “I remember when you first entered the labyrinth. You said you could finally understand why adventurers call it a big wide world.”

That had been back on the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor. In an effort to show us that adventuring wasn’t all hard and dreadful work, Rotmiller led us up a high hill. There, we watched together as the vast landscape was dyed in silver light, and Dwalkie had been so excited and happy that he couldn’t sleep that night.
“It would have been nice to have shown you an even wider world.”

Rotmiller finished his speech, but the others still had things to say. Missha and Hikurod knelt down and the words came tumbling out from deep inside of them. I took a step back and watched. It wasn’t that I didn’t have anything to say—it was just that it wasn’t all that different from these two.
“Waaaa! I-It’s my fault, I-I—! If I had just picked a differrrent door!”
“No. It’s my fault. I told him to trust me and that I would protect him no matter what, but that promise... I couldn’t keep it.”
No matter what I said, it would end up as self-reproach, and Dwalkie obviously wouldn’t want that. The world we had to survive was not kind enough to let us kneel here forever.
“Meehhhg!”
As I spotted the Vaikundus that appeared at the other end of the hallway, I spoke. “Everyone, stop. An enemy.”
While we remembered Dwalkie, we had to rise above the sadness. That was about all that those who had been left behind could do.
“Behelahhh!”
There was no choice but to move on.

The battle with the Vaikundus was unexpectedly arduous. The reason for that was simple. There were now only four people left in this wide maze, their stats had drastically decreased, and their injuries had not yet healed. It was thanks to Dwalkie that we had been able to take down rank-six monsters so easily in the first place.
“Let’s pack only what we need and go.”

After the battle, we started cleaning up. Equipment had scattered all over the floor during our desperate fight. After collecting the remnants, I even dug around the priest’s robe. The only thing I found was a necklace of unknown origin. I couldn’t tell if it was some kind of artifact or just decorative. After all, Dwalkie was the only one among us who had been able to sense the mana from objects.
“Looks like there’s nothing here, either.”

We even looted the middle-aged adventurer who had gotten caught up in battle and died early on, but there was nothing. Well, most of the stuff would be in that bastard’s subspace, anyway. Finally, I retrieved Dwalkie’s body.

“...I will deliver these according to your wishes.” He was carrying a wand and an expandable backpack. Taking off the boots and robes would make us money, but I left them untouched. “I will carry Dwalkie.”

Afterward, we used the trap room to get to the portal and returned to the Tower of Heavens. We each spread out and rested. Some sat in front of Dwalkie and wiped the blood from his body while others leaned against the wall and sobbed. This deceptive peace that fell over us forced them to accept that this was reality, not a dream.
“Bjorn, is there any way to get Dwalkie to the city?” asked Hikurod.
“I see...”

And reality was cruel. Although he had sacrificed his precious life for us, we couldn’t even take him to the city for a funeral, because the one who had died was our wizard. The corpses generated in the labyrinth were classified as objects, and were impossible to take outside without distortion magic. That was why barbarian hearts were special. They could be brought back to the city without magic. Wizards must have noticed that and started researching them as magical ingredients.
“Missha, get some rest.”
“I want to stay here a little longerrr. Once we leave... he’ll be lonely.”
“...Okay.”
Leaving the suffocating air behind me, I sat down in a corner and checked the time. It was 10:31 p.m., more than a day until the labyrinth closed. That left a bitter taste in my mouth.
It’s been less than an hour.

I felt truly insignificant, despite the fact that I had had numerous brushes with death in the past. It felt like I’d been fighting Vagos for days and nights. However, less than an hour had passed since we left, even taking clean-up into account.
Just focus on what you need to do.

I took out the letter left by the priest. The stains and wrinkles that could be found here and there told me that he had carried it with him for a long time. In the letter, in neat handwriting, was a description of how the old man had ended up in this situation. As I was reading it, I focused on one section in particular.
The underground city of Noark.
That was the name of the place where the old man and his young grandson had been taken to by the Dragon Slayer.
“It’s medicine made by an alchemist in Noark. If you take it, it will erase your memory of the last hour.”

It was also the name of that city that the deranged bitch had mentioned in the past, and it was something I couldn’t find information on no matter how much I searched through the library. So something like that existed under the sewer?
Could that woman have been a member of Orcules too?

With that in mind, I read through the letter. It contained one other surprising piece of information besides the fact that the underground city of Noark and Orcules apparently had a cooperative relationship.
...To think there’s a portal there too.

The thing that kept the city of Rafdonia running, the portal connecting to the labyrinth, also existed underground. That was how underground adventurers pulled off the miraculous feat of hiding their identities and mining enough mana stones to build a city with them.
Noark. I etched that name into my mind. I had a powerful hunch that I would end up entangled with that place in the future.
I should investigate it more when we get out.

With that thought in mind, I put the letter back into my pocket. After taking a look at the contents, it seemed no harm would come to me if I delivered it. Like they said, the enemy of your enemy was a friend. So anyway, that solved that particular issue.

I breathed out a long breath and closed my eyes. I was desperate for a break, but all sorts of distracting thoughts bothered me, repeatedly popping in and out of existence. What should I do now? As long as I had such an absurdly strong enemy out there, even being in the city wouldn’t guarantee my safety. He could try to harm me in the labyrinth with my teammates.
Damn it all.

Despite my determination to survive no matter what, realistic problems lingered in my mind without proper solutions. It was a pity that Vagos had gotten out of there alive. If only the priest had just healed me, I could have ended him myself.
What am I thinking?

I shook my head and brushed off my lingering regrets. The world didn’t work the way you wanted it to. The priest probably didn’t have a choice, either. The evil god had been like that in the game too. He may grant a wish for a price, but he never gave you the best-case scenario. Like a monkey’s paw that brought on misery even as it granted your wishes, he was a being that always dished out a helping of despair alongside hope.
This bastard also strangely keeps popping up in my life.
Adding the Evil God Karui to my research list, I cleared my mind. It was time for me to rest. This was not only a safer place than the city, but we had a lot to do once we got out of here.

After wiping my body off with a wet towel, I unfolded the sleeping bag and laid inside. It was strange, though. I had been fighting desperately for almost two nights straight, but I still couldn’t fall asleep for a long time.
[The labyrinth is now closed. You have been transported to Rafdonia.]

Sunlight poked my eyelids. Without a moment to linger in the afterglow, I went through the checkpoint and exchanged my mana stones. Then, I headed to our meeting place, the branch of the Adventurers’ Guild located closest to Dimension Square. When I arrived in front of it, there was a crowd of people who looked similar to me.

The silence was stark considering the dozens of people gathered. Everyone waited for the other members of their party to arrive with grim expressions on their faces. That was to be expected. There was only one reason you’d return to the city and come here before even washing up: the death of a teammate.
“If we’re all here, let’s go in.”
Soon after the entire party arrived, we entered the guild. We turned in all of the pieces of Dwalkie’s equipment we had collected, including his backpack, and we reported his death.
“...He left behind great teammates.” The staff looked at us with a strange look in their eyes.

True, what we had done wasn’t all that common. While we had no claim over the assets left in the city, this stuff, at least, could’ve been taken by the rest of the party. Most would just have reported the death and been done with it.
“Riol Warb Dwalkie, royal family certified rank-eight wizard. Your report of his death has been received.”
It didn’t feel like a waste, though. After all, we knew the contents of the will he wrote before he first entered the labyrinth.
“Haha, a will? I truly feel like an adventurer now.”
“It doesn’t matter what you write, but make sure you clearly state who will inherit your property. Otherwise, everything will go to the Adventurers’ Guild.”
“Don’t worry about that part. That’s already been decided.”

He wanted to donate his fortune to an orphanage under a certain temple. I only found out the details yesterday. According to Hikurod, Dwalkie had happy memories of staying there as a child for a while. His assets should be spent where he wanted. We’d already received something much more significant from him.
“It’s really over... Now, let’s go.”

At any rate, our first order of business after returning to the city was to report Dwalkie’s death. It was amazingly simple: one minute to fill out the paperwork, two minutes for it to be reviewed by staff. It took just three minutes to put an end to twenty-five years of life.
That’s how common death is in this world.
I left my bitterness behind in the guild. Then I headed to the Great Temple of Reatlas. That was the only way for me to repay the favor to the dead and gone. “You guys can go home and rest.”
“How can we? He saved our lives.”
“I... want to come with you too. I got enough rrrest inside.”
Actually, Missha cried all day and didn’t get any rest at all, but I didn’t mention it. It was clear that even if she went back to the inn, she wouldn’t be able to sleep.

We all headed to our destination together. Before long, we came to a pure white building that seemed untouched by the filth of the world, and we entered it. When the apprentice priest asked if we were here for treatment, I debated what to say before answering that we were here at the request of High Priest Ludwig.
“H-High Priest Ludwig...?”
They never imagined someone would lie in the home of a god. The youthful priest’s eyes widened and he ran straight inside to deliver the news.

“Long time no see.” As we were waiting there, a familiar face came out to greet us: the captain of the Third Paladins, Paal Krovitz. “I heard that you came at the request of High Priest Ludwig, who disappeared a few years ago. Do you have any items as evidence?” he asked politely. He also said this was a very sensitive matter for the church, and he hoped for our understanding. Apparently, there had been some big issues as a result of the reward placed all over the city.
“A reward?”
“Yes. Because the amount is so large, there have been people who have harbored wicked intent.”
I didn’t come here hoping for a reward. However, since I had a record of killing that Elisa bitch and receiving a large amount of money as a result, I blurted out, “How big is the reward?”

At the self-centered question, Missha jabbed me in the side. Hikurod did the same. Rotmiller, an adventurer and also a member of the church of Reatlas, didn’t seem too happy about it, either. “Bjorn, that’s not appropriate, even from you.”
However, Krovitz opened his mouth without a hint of contempt. “The amount varies depending on the information provided and the presence or absence of holy relics, but...”
“But?”
All of his answers remained steady. “I remember that the Treasury Office was offering up to seventy million stones.”

chapters.title: Chapter 147: The Great Inheritance (4)
paragraphs: As soon as I heard that huge number, seventy million stones, it made my heart thump. However, I forced myself to calm down and continue the conversation. I could wait to be happy after the money was in my hands. “Will this letter serve as evidence?”
Upon receiving the letter, Krovitz read it slowly from the top, his expression changing entirely. He did not speak for a long time.
“...Is there a problem?”
“Oh, I’m sorry. If the contents of this letter are true... This is a really serious matter for the church. I am not doubting you, but will you be able to wait inside for a moment?”
“Sure.”
Krovitz led us to a sort of drawing room inside the temple, then vacated his seat with a sense of urgency. Apparently, he needed to confirm the handwriting before informing his superiors.
“You don’t think... there’s something wrong, rrright?”
“Haha, of course not. They just want to discuss it after verifying it.”
“Murad is right. You guys read it as well. The contents of that letter are no laughing matter.”
The wait was longer than expected. Just when we were starting to throw around new theories, Krovitz returned. “I apologize. I made you all wait too long. Now, let’s go. Everyone is waiting.”
The place he led us to was the chapel on the second floor, a space that only those who were priests, not ordinary believers, could use.
“I heard that non-members of the church are not permitted here...”
“The goddess has connected our paths. How can we call you strangers?”
Upon hearing Krovitz’s answer to Rotmiller’s question, my worries vanished. If they had decided that the letter was fake, he wouldn’t be behaving like that.
Creak.
Soon, Krovitz opened the door and revealed the interior of the chapel. It was a fairly large space, but only seven people were seated inside. When I studied their faces, I froze.
Holy...

After my visit to the count’s family, I read several books on the positions of the church, so I recognized them right away. There were only two people here wearing armor—a man and a woman. The designs on their armor were different, but the silver thread adorning the hems meant that they were Captains of the Paladins. Including Krovitz, the three sole captains of the church were gathered here, but that wasn’t all. There were two high priests, one cardinal, and an elderly man standing in the center as if to receive their counsel.

As soon as Rotmiller saw him, he knelt down and made the sign of the cross. “...A servant of the stars greets the holy Archbishop.” His reaction was understandable. If you wanted to put it in Catholic terms, it was like the pope was right in front of us right now.
But who is that child?

Feeling strangely intimidated by the colorful lineup for a moment, I turned my attention to the small boy, about ten years old, seated in front of the archbishop. Now that I was looking, it seemed that everyone was standing in formation to protect the child. Even the archbishop was standing right behind him. Who could this kid be?
While I was questioning this, the archbishop made the sign of the cross, and all the members of the church silently looked at us. “May the blessing of the twilight star be with us.”

It was a very remarkable sight. Even Rotmiller, who was also a believer, seemed to be at a loss and went as still as stone. Was it because we were in a chapel? A strangely sacred yet imposing atmosphere pervaded the air.

After a moment of silence, the archbishop opened his mouth. “High Priest Ludwig was a very precious person to us. Thank you for delivering the letter. May I ask how this letter came to be in your possession?”
To be honest, this was a bit unexpected. The person who, of the three major religions, had the most authority was speaking much too politely and cautiously to mere fourth-floor adventurers.
This isn’t the norm, though. That man must have been really important.
I slowly opened my mouth and briefly explained what had happened in the Labyrinth of Larcaz.

Perhaps because of his clerical mindset, the archbishop replied, “The twilight star sent you to him because he had lost his way. Thank you for saving his soul. Even though he was possessed by an evil god, his soul will continue to shine forever even in darkness.”

It was a bit uncomfortable to listen to. It wasn’t a matter of being right or wrong, but it felt like they were fundamentally the opposite of me. Ever since my childhood, I hadn’t had a good relationship with religious people.

“...This belonged to him.” Soon, I took out the necklace the high priest had been wearing and handed it to them. If this was a holy relic, it would be worth a lot more than the reward, but it didn’t feel like a waste because it was the right thing to do. I was indebted to that high priest.
“Thank you. This isn’t the item we have been looking for, but this should comfort his soul even a little bit.”
Yeah, it wasn’t a holy relic. Well, if there had been anything like that, that bastard would have taken it away a long time ago.
“Cardinal Greyond, how much of the bounty will be going to them?”

“The relic was not recovered, but considering the importance of the handwritten letter’s contents, his belongings, and conveying his last moments, it would not be excessive to pay all seventy million stones designated by the Ministry of Finance.”
“Then, please do so.”
