I gulped without realizing it. I had expected to receive just half of the reward since we didn’t return the holy relic, but they were giving us all of it. I felt bad for feeling uncomfortable earlier. These were really excellent believers.
Of course, that wasn’t what was important. “I want to ask you something.”
“Ask away.”
Since the first matter had been settled, I got straight to the real point, something that may be more important than the reward. “So what are you guys going to do now?”
“May I ask what exactly you mean?”

“Didn’t you just find out about the culprit who kidnapped High Priest Ludwig? I’m wondering if you’re going to get revenge, since I’m caught up in this now too.” As I asked the question, I subtly hinted that they were sort of responsible for that.
The answer I received was incredibly vague. “I cannot confirm that here and now.”
“I see.”
Welp, I figured if these guys planned to seek revenge, that bastard wouldn’t come after me for at least a while. I supposed I had no choice but to act on my own. I nodded.
“Don’t worry, great warrior.” At that moment, the little child I had been keeping an eye on earlier opened his mouth.
Shaaaaaa!

An all-too-brilliant silver light poured out of him. When I came to, a ring made of three intertwined vines was sitting on my thick finger. I didn’t know what the hell was going on, but I realized what exactly I was looking at when I heard the cardinal’s cry that followed.
“A prophecy...! A prophecy has descended!”
It was something I had only ever heard from NPCs in the game and never experienced myself.
Goddamn it.

It was a prophecy, and apparently the first one to descend in a long time. That answered that question. And as for why that archbishop was treating this child like a treasure chest, the reason was simple.
To think he’s a saint.

A saint was a vessel that could hear the voices of gods and sometimes harness their power. A child who fit all the qualities of a vessel spoke. “The goddess has just spoken. That ring will ward off three powerful ill-fated encounters.”
“Do you mean the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos?”

An ordinary fortuneteller would have just said yes or no to this question, but the oracle was different. “Yes. She said it can only prevent encounters with that man. So you must be prepared to face your fate when all the stems of that ring are cut off.”

It felt like I had become a warrior who would defeat a demon lord or something. To be honest, I was dumbfounded. I may have defeated that Elisa bitch and dealt with the high priest, but why would the goddess give me a gift like this? Especially considering I was an evil spirit.
What is this? Is it a prank?

Suddenly, I wondered if all these people were scamming me with that child, but the ring on my hand erased those doubts. Even their expressions, which were stained with astonishment, seemed too sincere to be an act.
“May the blessing of the twilight star be with us.”
“Let it flow as it should.”
The top religious figures in this world all looked at me and drew the sign of the cross. I glanced at my teammates’ faces.
“Bjorrrn, who the hell are you?!”
“Are you really destined to be a hero?!”
“No, that’s not the biggest issue here. H-How could a barbarian be chosen by a human god?”
Even if you guys look at me like that, I really don’t know, either.
Only then did I turn to stare at the little boy, realizing that this wasn’t just something to celebrate. I had a lot of questions.
Slump.

However, the child collapsed weakly. Perhaps that was the price of receiving a prophecy. The archbishop lifted the child into his arms, promptly ending today’s meeting. “Sir Krovitz, please guide these people outside.”
“No, wait! I still have to ask—”
“I ask for your understanding. We’ll meet again later and I’ll explain everything. Until then, please keep today’s matter a secret. A great disaster may befall you otherwise.”
“What? A great disaster?” That was ridiculous, but the conversation ended there.
“Sir Krovitz will explain the details.” The archbishop’s adamance forced us out of the chamber. Then, following Krovitz’s lead, we headed to the drawing room we had been waiting in earlier.
“Krovitz, what is going on here?”
“I... am also unsure why she has chosen to give a prophecy to someone of another race.”
“...Has this never happened to a non-human?”
“No, as far as I know, this is the third time.”
“So, what happened to them?”
“According to the records, they were branded as heretics within their tribes and kicked out.”
Ha, this was a pain in the ass. It was like another suicide button had been handed to me in addition to the evil spirit thing. “I can see why you told me to keep this a secret.”
“Yes, because if it becomes public knowledge, it will do more harm than good.”

The core of the barbarian’s build was the Spirit Imprint. If I got kicked out of the tribe, from that day on, I’d be no more than a failed character. Barbarian shamans only existed in the tribe’s holy land.
“Don’t worry about us, though. We will not leak this information.” As he said that, Krovitz looked at his colleagues. They didn’t say anything, but their feelings were clear.
Therefore, I also looked at my teammates.
“Ah! I-I’ll keep my mouth shut! Rrreally! You trust me, rrright? Bjorn?”
“Don’t worry. I didn’t hear anything.”
Of course I wasn’t worried about Missha, nor Rotmiller all that much. He wasn’t that type of person, and he was also a follower of Reatlas. The real problem was...
“H-Hey! Why are you looking at me with those eyes?”
“Why do you think?”
“...I will stop drinking from now on.”

I let out a sigh as Hikurod lowered his head with a dejected expression on his face. Whew, we shouldn’t have all come together. Were all the gods here like this? Instead of relieving me of the biggest stone weighing down my heart, it felt like a new, smaller stone had just been placed on it.
But he’s not that much of a blabbermouth, so...

I decided to focus on the bright side. If this ring really prevented encounters with the Dragon Slayer, then this amount of risk couldn’t even be called a risk. In terms of pros and cons, what had happened today was unconditionally beneficial. I had managed to get what I needed most desperately: time.
This is the first time I’ve gotten a holy relic through an oracle, though.

Objects bestowed by the gods were called holy relics. Most of them had overpowered abilities. That was why I didn’t doubt the ring’s powers. I didn’t know how long it would last, but I was certain I wouldn’t run into him until all three strands were cut.
The problem is how long that will take.

Two years? Three years? I wondered if it was possible that it’d last that long, as this was a hot holy relic that had just dropped, but... it would be better to assume as short a duration as possible and prepare accordingly. I decided to assume it would last half a year to a year and finished getting my thoughts in order.
The moment I got up from the couch, one of the entwined vines snapped in two.
Rip.
“Uh, Bjorn? It looks like one just broke.”

“...No. It can’t be.” I rubbed the broken vine with a finger that was wet with saliva, like I was trying to twist a fraying rope back together. But, as always, reality was cruel. “Look. It’s still in one piece.”
The moment I held out my hand with the ring to show them, the severed vine turned into silvery particles of light and scattered into the air.
Shaaa!
I stared blankly at my hand.
[The activation conditions for Blessing of the Stars have been met.]
I couldn’t even laugh.

chapters.title: Chapter 148: The Great Inheritance (5)
paragraphs: There were some days when a momentary whim led to unexpected luck. For Amelia Rainwales, today was that kind of a day. Who could have guessed that, while climbing the castle in an attempt to burn off some frustration, she would run into this man?
“Regal Vagos.”

The member of Orcules, which divided this cursed city into two halves, that she wanted to kill the most was passed out on the floor in this remote area with injuries covering his body. And he was alone.
Could it be that he escaped through a portal? Is that why he was dropped here instead of the square?
That was the first possibility that came to mind. There were no wizards on the Dragon Slayer’s team, but he could have pulled it off if he sacrificed the poor old man he always took with him.
What kind of enemy did he run into...?
Amelia discarded her questions. It didn’t matter who had reduced him to this state. The only thing that mattered was that he had been hand-delivered to her. First, she bent down to check his pulse.
He’s still alive.

About two hours had passed since the labyrinth closed. Circumstantial evidence suggested that he had been unconscious since then. It would have been difficult for a normal person to survive for so long, but this guy was not normal. Perhaps the skewer stuck in his shoulder was stopping the bleeding.
Then he opened his eyes and stared at her. “You’re...” He had probably sensed her presence.
Before he could say anything, Amelia spoke first. “Dragon Slayer, do you have any potions?”
“Waist...”
“I see.” Amelia untied the pouch he wore around his waist and held it in her hand. “I’m going to pour the potion on you. Can I pull this out of your shoulder?”
“Do it...”
As soon as she heard his answer, she pulled out the skewer and the bleeding started again. If left as he was, even the Dragon Slayer would definitely die. Amelia just stood there and watched.
“What are you... the potion...” He was beginning to sense that something was off.
“Why should I do that?” she asked.
“You made... a contract...”

“Oh, the contract?” Amelia smirked. A long time ago, she had been given a contract by the lord of Noark. It was famous; everyone who lived in the city knew about it. Inside Noark, she could not kill. The contract was carved into her flesh, and it was impossible to break. “But aren’t you the one who asked me to remove the skewer?”

She had just done as he told her. Of course, this was the first time she had ever deceived someone like this, so she was also nervous. However, if it were a violation of her contract, she wouldn’t have been able to do it in the first place.
“You... bitch...”

Amelia put his entire pouch into her subspace. She stole his other equipment—not just the dagger hanging from his waist, but also the ring on his hand, his wrist guards, and his necklace. These were all things she had always had her eye on. “Thank you for ending up here. I’ll take good care of these. Oh, but who did this to you?”

He did not answer her mocking question. He just glared at her in a rage. Amelia leaned back against the wall and watched him, rather than continuing her pointless chit-chat. She intended to watch him die, just to make sure nothing unexpected happened along the way. But apparently, it wasn’t yet time for this guy’s string of fate to be cut.
Step, step.

Before long, she heard the presence of the castle’s patrolmen in the distance. Amelia thought fast. Actually, there was nothing for her to think about. Everything the patrols saw and heard was passed on to the lord. If she got caught, it’d all be over.
“You’re lucky, Dragon Slayer.” She pressed her lips together, bitter. If this guy died, Orcules’s authority would take a hit.
Upon realizing he was going to live, he gritted his teeth and bit out, “You won’t... be able to handle... the consequences.” She would pay for this.
Amelia just shrugged and closed the distance between them. “Doesn’t matter. You won’t remember anything, anyway.”
“...What?”

She took out a pill and held it in her hand, a magic pill named the Blessing of Lethe developed by an alchemist in Noark. Evil spirits were immune to it, but it had the convenient effect of erasing the memories of those who consumed it.
“Damn it! Mm, mm—!”

Amelia grabbed the struggling man by the jaw and shoved the pill down his throat. The higher someone’s Dignity of the Soul was, the less effective the pill was, so she used the best one she had just in case. The alchemist said that an ordinary person who took this pill would lose up to a week of memories.
Considering who he is, better safe than sorry.

It didn’t feel like too much of a waste. This wasn’t something she would be able to get another one of all that easily, but considering what she had earned today, it shouldn’t be a loss. Besides, the further back his memories were erased, the more advantageous it was for her. He’d think he lost his items in the labyrinth; he’d never think he was robbed in the underground city.
I don’t know who did this, but I should be grateful.
Hearing the patrol’s footsteps approaching, Amelia quickly left the castle.
Not even ten minutes had passed, and the available uses of the ring that blocked Regal Vagos-related death flags had already gone from three to two.
It’s not going to break once a day, right?

I tried to clear away the anxiety that suddenly filled me. I shouldn’t make a fuss before I even knew if that was actually going to happen, and I thought the possibility of that was really low. The goddess herself had said so, right?
“You must be prepared to face your fate when all the stems of that ring are cut off.”

The goddess had used her vessel to tell me to prepare myself, knowing full well how great the gap between me and that man was. I was sure she would have had the conscience to give me more than a couple of months.
Yeah, in the end, the most important thing is when the last vine will break.
Trying not to jump to conclusions, I calmed my quaking heart. What was important wasn’t what had just happened. It was the number of times it did—in other words, how long this ring would last.
Just focus on what you need to do.
With that thought in mind, I briefly discussed the bounty and left the church. The bounty would be paid out when we visited again tomorrow. “Then let’s each go home and meet again tomorrow.”

Just as we decided on a meeting place and were about to head back to our respective lodgings, Hikurod cautiously stopped us. “Hey, I don’t know what you guys will think about this, but why don’t we donate Dwalkie’s portion of the reward to the orphanage?”
“I’m... okay with that. We wouldn’t have earrrned it if it wasn’t for Dwalkie.”
“That’s fine with me too. In fact, it feels ridiculous for me to claim an additional share of such a large sum.”

To put it simply, the proposal was to donate 3.5 million stones per person to an orphanage. Unlike my colleagues, who agreed without much hesitation, I kept my mouth shut. This was completely irrational. Weren’t we in the middle of a battle with a major enemy called the Dragon Slayer? If we were really going to fulfill Dwalkie’s wishes, it would be better to use this money to make ourselves a little safer.
“...Bjorn, you don’t have to do it. Unlike us, you were the one who went thrrrough the most back there.”
“Th-that’s right. We’re doing this out of guilt, so don’t worry too much about it.”

My colleagues noticed my silence and quickly spoke up. If I nodded my head here, this matter would be settled. However, I put my decision on hold for now. “Let’s properly discuss this the next time we meet. We haven’t received the money yet, anyways.”

This was definitely a suggestion that I needed to flat-out decline, but for some reason, the words wouldn’t come out. It wasn’t that I couldn’t speak because I was swept up in their enthusiasm, but a weak part of me wondered if I would feel more at ease after donating the 3.5 million stones. Whew, this was why you had to be careful about affection. It made making logical decisions difficult. A few months ago, I wouldn’t have worried about this.
“See you tomorrow, then!”

Soon after, we parted ways and headed to our respective inns. I walked the peaceful streets for about an hour to reach the inn, and once there I washed my body, stained with blood and sweat, with clean water. While I was lying on my bed in a daze, someone knocked on the door.
It was Erwen. “Um, Mister? Are you there?”

When I opened the door, she was already washed up and wearing a fluttering skirt. I conversed with her, wondering if she had business with me, but it was mainly just chatter about what she did inside the labyrinth. A while ago, this was normal to me. In fact, usually, this would have been interesting to listen to, but today it was difficult to do so.
“Erwen, I’m tired today, so you should go home.”
“Pardon? But now is when things get really good...”
“Later. I’ll listen later. I’m tired today.”
“Okay...” When I firmly gave her the order to leave, Erwen headed out with her pointy ears drooping.
Silence soon followed. In it, I had some time alone to think. If there was a problem, you had to fix it.
How to survive.
Ever since I opened my eyes in this body, this had been my biggest goal, and that had not changed even now. However, the process of reaching that goal was the problem.
“...Barbarian, you kept your oath, right?”

I broke the warrior’s oath in front of everyone, and while leading the party, did countless things that would have made me seem strange. At that time, I justified everything as survival, but I knew differently. In the end, there was trust at the root of all those actions. If I thought there was anyone on the team who suspected me of being an evil spirit, I wouldn’t have done that even if it killed me.
“...Hey! Hang on, my friend!”

The same went for splitting the advanced potion between Rotmiller and Dwalkie. It had been an irrational decision that put me in more danger than anyone else. And it wasn’t much different from the dilemma I now faced.
Three and a half million stones...

I slowly decided to admit it. I had become weak. The reason was simple: I had become attached to others. My rationality, which had always been my greatest strength, was now majorly complicated. It wouldn’t be such an issue if I was just going to live in this world. But for me, whose top priority was survival, this problem couldn’t be ignored. So what was the solution?
I was unable to find the answer before I fell asleep.

The next morning, I received a letter from an administrative branch of the Adventurers’ Guild. The contents said that I had been designated as the beneficiary of Riol Warb Dwalkie’s inheritance, so I had to go and receive it.
“Did you get it too?”
“Eh, you too?”

This was the first conversation I had with my teammates the next day. It looked like all four of us had gotten a letter from the guild. But Dwalkie had definitely designated an orphanage as his beneficiary, so how did this happen?
“...Instead of trying to figure it out ourselves, it would be better to visit the guild and ask.”

At Hikurod’s behest, we all visited the guild together. The relevant department confirmed that it was not an administrative error or anything like that. Dwalkie had updated his will, appointing the four of us as beneficiaries, just last month.
“...After we fought the Troll.”

Having almost been killed by the Troll, the first thing Dwalkie had done back in the city was update his will. He had been preparing. The worst of the worst-case scenarios that I hadn’t even considered, that positive and optimistic guy somehow did.

A while later, Dwalkie’s equipment and backpack, which had been handed over to the guild, were returned to us intact. We were also given ownership of the house he owned while alive. We left the building like defeated soldiers.
“My debt to him... I don’t know if I’ll be able to repay it in my lifetime.”
“Dwalkie wouldn’t have wanted us to pay him back.”
“Yes, he certainly wouldn’t have. So, let’s spend the money he left us where we want. If he had one wish, that would be it.”

After that, we went to the temple and picked up the reward. The archbishop seemed busy, so all business was conducted through Krovitz. After telling everyone else to head to the bar first, I chatted with him for a while. “Can you promise to keep everything I say now a secret?”
“You can speak comfortably. As long as it doesn’t go against the will of the goddess, I swear I won’t reveal my savior’s words to anyone.”
The part about the will of the goddess bothered me a little, but I still pulled out the longsword made of arc without much hesitation and showed it to him.
“...That’s the Dragon Slayer’s sword.”
“For some reason, when we try to use it, it rejects us. Do you know why? If it’s a curse, I want to get it lifted.”

“The power within that object is not a curse.” Krovitz had no trouble answering my question, as he knew much about this sword. It was a long story, but the gist was simple. The original name of this sword had been the Dragon Sword. Regal Vagos had killed the guardian dragon and ran away with it, giving it the name Dragon Slayer. “Since ancient times, only dragons have been able to wield this sword. From generation to generation, guardian dragons inherited it and enjoyed a near-immortal lifespan.”
“But that man wasn’t able to properly use this sword.”
“Ah, that’s because of the Dragon’s Curse.”

The guardian dragon cast a curse before its death. As a result, Regal Vagos was both one of the dragon people and not. His dragon scales, a hallmark of the dragon people, had been burned off with fire, and his source of power, his heart, was more or less like a human’s now. The act of betraying his clan to obtain the sword had been repaid in bad karma, so the item was no longer usable.
“I know he has been looking for a way to get rid of the curse for a long time. However, from what you’ve said, it seems that there is no way to completely overcome it.”
“Anyway, you’re saying that it’s not this sword that’s cursed, but that guy.”
“Yes, that’s right.”
Afterward, I asked how we should dispose of this sword that we couldn’t use.
Krovitz’s answer was simple. “I think it would be prudent to return the sword to the dragon people and receive a well-deserved reward.”

Yes, that was the only way. Since the sword could only be used by someone of a dragon race, it would be difficult to sell as stolen goods. I decided to think about this more later. “I see. Thanks for the advice.”
“It’s nothing. You are a hero to our church. If you need my help, please visit anytime.”
“Oh, does that mean that I will be able to receive blessings for free in the future?” I asked just in case.

“Haha, that’s a bit...” Krovitz laughed awkwardly and drew a line in the sand. He said he would if he could, but apparently there had been another prophecy that morning. “The twilight star has said that everything will flow as it should, so we shouldn’t try to go against it by misinterpreting her will.”
For some reason, it felt like the goddess was talking to me: I already gave you a holy relic to settle our debt, so don’t even think about getting something else out of it.
“Still, I can always listen to your worries, so please visit us whenever it is convenient for you.”
After Krovitz’s very religious comment, I left the temple and headed to the tavern.

“Ah, are you here? Come sit.” The other three were already drinking. However, the atmosphere was very different from when we usually finished an expedition. There was no laughing and talking, just drinking. I realized at that moment that despite our team making more income than ever before, we had lost more than ever.
The window seat is empty.

At the table at the bar where five people used to gather was an empty chair that would never be filled again. However, we did not mention this at all and turned our conversation to more serious matters.
“We’ll divide the bounty and the rest of the money exactly by four.”
“Let’s do that.”

Even Hikurod, who at first suggested donating a share to the orphanage, just nodded. I sort of expected that. The reason why such a proposal had come about in the first place was in an effort to respect Dwalkie’s wishes. But if he wanted us to use the precious property he left behind ourselves, we were just following his last request.
We’ll have to meet again tomorrow to distribute the settlement money.
Everyone, including the dwarf, drank quietly in Dwalkie’s memory, so I passed my time like that too.

“He shouldn’t have died like that...” Hikurod, who had been drinking glass after glass, was the first to drop, his head falling onto the table. At this, Rotmiller said he would take him home, leaving me and Missha alone.
“Bjorn, let’s go home too...”
As always, the two of us walked together as we headed for our inns. Missha staggered from drinking too much.
“Lean on me.”
“Ah, thanks.”

It was still sunny out. We made our way through the busy streets smelling like alcohol. As usual, we reached my inn first, and it was time to say goodbye. But the two of us just stood there, staring at each other in front of the door.

The air was strangely hot, probably because of our drunkenness. Yes, if things were normal, that was what I would have thought, since that was easier and more convenient for me. Pretending not to notice, I would have ignored it like a barbarian.
Missha broke eye contact first. “Um... I-I’m gonna go now. Rrrest—”
“Missha Karlstein.”
She turned around when I grabbed her. I had made a promise to him.
“You are not sneaky. Please stop averting your eyes and face it head-on.”
He told me not to look away. With the precious time he could have used to reveal his feelings to Missha, he instead left me with those words. And I had agreed.
“Hmm?”
It was my turn to strike. Her wrist in my hand, Missha looked at me quizzically. I took a deep breath and cleared my throat. Then, I bluntly asked, “Do you like me as a man?”

It wasn’t a romantic line, and it wasn’t even that romantic of an atmosphere. I spat out the question like the barbarian I was, but Missha didn’t get angry. She didn’t even laugh and call the question strange. She flinched, then shifted her gaze to the ground to avoid my eyes. However, after dragging her feet through the dirt several times, she raised her head, looked up at me, and answered in a small voice. “...Yeah. I like you. As a man.”

chapters.title: Chapter 149: Barbarian Chief (1)
paragraphs: Not long ago, Missha had put her foot down with me.
“I... I like skinny men.”
“Eeet! It means that you have no charrrm as a man!”

When we got lost in the Witch’s Forest, she said this because she misunderstood my friendly offer of a contract. I had been relieved by those words. People often said there was no such thing as friendship between a man and a woman. I figured that if her tastes were that defined, we would be able to remain comrades without any issues even if we stayed together for a long time.
“Come, sit quickly. Not getting enough food while you’rrre recovering is bad for you.”

Missha’s attitude toward me gradually changed. She stopped by every morning to wake me up, and we ate homemade dishes together. She even conceded the meat to me. To be honest, it felt like I had a girlfriend instead of a comrade. At first, I thought it was because I had risked my life to save her so she was repaying me in her own way.
“...Yeah. I like you. As a man.”
So it had been that all along.
“Did you know?” she asked.
“I wasn’t sure.”

To be more accurate, I had been ignoring it for that very reason. It was not like she had ever brought it up herself. I decided not to face this problem, telling myself that I could just be mistaken, because now that I knew, there was only one option.
“I-I see...”

Watching Missha tremble as she looked at me, I realized how cowardly I was. If I had faced this problem earlier, I would have been able to solve it in a different way. I could have pushed her away with obvious hints, too, if Missha’s feelings hadn’t already grown to the point where even Dwalkie told me to stop ignoring them. Yes, I’m sure that would’ve been the case.
“So... what do you think?”
There were now two choices in front of me: bring my body closer and light a blazing fire, or put out the fire before it got any bigger. The answer had already been decided.

I was an evil spirit and a player. I was not Bjorn Yandel, and I hadn’t given up my hopes of returning home. But because I couldn’t say that, and since Dwalkie had also said that it would be cowardly to ask for her honesty without showing my true self, I spoke sincerely.
“I consider you a valuable comrade.”
I got an answer a few seconds later. “Yeah... it’s not going to worrrk with me, huh?”

“The same goes for anyone else. I can’t afford that. We don’t know when we will die. Besides, it hasn’t even been a year since I finished my coming-of-age ceremony.” In many ways, this was a time when survival should be my top priority, and Missha had to keep adventuring with me. If we were emotionally entangled, it would be difficult to make a logical decision in certain situations. This would put both of us at risk. I had to face the facts and draw the line. However, even if I packaged it as what was best for us, the root of my decision was selfishness. “I want you to only consider me as a teammate.”
Missha flatly rejected my suggestion. “No!”
“...What?”

“Why should I do that? In the firrrst place, I had no intention of revealing my feelings today, you horrible barbarian! You con man! All this, after asking me that as if you werrre going to accept them!” Missha shouted in annoyance and thrust her fist into my stomach.
Smack!

The cold damage even reached my heart. Still angry, Missha continued to shout. “When did I ask you to accept my feelings? I know you’rrre not in a position to do that! But! Telling me not to like you, that’s too crrruel!”
Smack! Smack! Smack!
Cold damage quickly stacked.
“No, that—”

Just as I was about to say something, Missha’s hand weakly dropped onto my stomach. “I... don’t even want much. The way things arrre now is enough for me. So don’t say stuff like that. Hm? Why are you trrrying to take this away from me too...?”

Tremors ran through my skin where Missha and I were connected. I couldn’t see her face because she had her head down, but it wasn’t hard to guess what expression she was wearing. I kept my mouth shut. I figured I wasn’t qualified to console her right now, whether through words or actions. A moment of silence passed, and soon the trembling stopped.
Missha stepped back and glared at me with red, swollen eyes. “You’rrre not getting any food tomorrow,” she said venomously and left.
I stood there like a statue and watched her leave.
Creak.
When I entered the inn, the owner sitting at the counter looked at me and clicked his tongue. “You did her wrong today.”
I knew that without needing to hear it.
Step, step.

I climbed the stairs and opened the door. Bjorn Yandel’s room was still cramped. For some reason, it reminded me of Hansu Lee’s empty room. It was time to admit it. It was not because I had gotten attached that I’d become weak. It was because I was weak that I didn’t want to get attached.
The next morning, Missha, who said I wouldn’t be getting any food, came to wake me up with a healthy lunchbox full of carrots in her hand. “Chew them all thoroughly. Got it?”

Because of the sins I had committed, I obediently chewed and swallowed them all. It didn’t take long as I gobbled them down. However, noticing me awkwardly averting my eyes after the meal, Missha opened her mouth first.
“It’s not bad, how things are now.”
“But—”

“No buts. You have no rrright to decide. So don’t look so worried. I’m just doing what I want to do.” This was the conclusion she must have reached at home last night. There was no room for me to argue. Missha was more mature than me. She must have been saying this so resolutely because she didn’t want this relationship to become any more uncomfortable.
I was sure Dwalkie wouldn’t want me to take such a wishy-washy stance, but I just said, “Okay.”
“Okay, then we won’t talk about this anymore frrrom now on. Got it?”
“Got it.”
With that, the matter had been settled. Nothing had actually changed from before.
“Wash up. We should leave soon.”
After eating, I quickly washed up and headed out with Missha. We headed to the meeting place, met up with our teammates, and all went to Kommelby together. The air in the carriage was quite heavy.
“This is the first time we’ve all headed there together.” Hikurod tried his best to sound upbeat, but strictly speaking, not everyone was here. Now, even if we wanted to, we never could.
“...Let’s finish our business fast and head back.”

After arriving at Kommelby, things got better. We repaired our equipment and sold what was to be sold. Finally, we went to the central administrative office and drew up a contract to transfer Dwalkie’s house to Hikurod. The reason was simple: the dwarf said he would buy it.
“...Is there a reason you’re going out of your way? I’m sure Dwalkie wouldn’t want you to go so far, either.”

“Haha! It’s always been my dream to own a house. Didn’t we make a lot of money this time?” I tried to dissuade him, but Hikurod’s resolve was unbending. “Now, that’s enough of your worrying. Hurry up and sign.”

With the government official as a notary, the signature was signed and Dwalkie’s house became property of the dwarf. The appraisal value of the house given to us by the administrative office was twenty-four million stones. However, we were told that it would have been sold for 20 percent cheaper at an auction, so we only received five million stones per person.
“Then let’s head back and have a drink.”

After finishing our business and returning to the residential area, we headed to the tavern. There, we did our final loot distribution. All income, including mana stones, was divided into four. Because of equipment repair costs or the cost of consumables used in the labyrinth, there may have been slight differences for each person, but an otherwise huge sum of money had fallen into each of our laps.
Twenty-five million stones...

Hikurod likely only had ten million stones left after buying the house, though. It was also agreed that the Dragon Slayer sword and the Restrained Wish I used in the labyrinth would be acknowledged as part of my share.

“Your Essence of a Vampire disappeared and got replaced by the Essence of an Ogre? That was definitely the item that man was looking for, then. But it happened while you were trying to save us, right?”
“I’m not so shameless as to be that greedy. If it weren’t for you, he would have kept the Dragon Slayer sword in the first place.”
I was very grateful to hear those words. If we were to convert those two items into money and divide them into four, I’d be filing for bankruptcy several times over.
“Now then, let’s drink.”
After a few more drinks, I quietly opened my mouth. “I guess we should start talking about the party.”
A seat on the team had become vacant. I wasn’t planning on filling the position, but instead leaving the party with Missha.
However, Hikurod was one step ahead of me. “I have something to say to everyone about that. I’m going to quit being an adventurer.”
“What?”
“I’m sorry for bringing this up at a time like this. However, I came to the decision after thinking about it all day yesterday, so I hope you understand.”
“If you quit this job, what are you planning to do in the future?” Rotmiller asked in response to the dwarf’s declaration.

“I’m going to set up a forge. That’s why I bought that house. I thought it was now or never.” No wonder he had stepped up to buy Dwalkie’s house. He was planning to renovate it and set up a forge. “To me, becoming an adventurer was always kind of like running away from reality. I gave up on my dream because I had no talent, because I needed money to live on in the present. That’s why I don’t want to live with regrets anymore. That would be an insult to my friend.”
No one dared to speak out against Hikurod’s resolute proclamation. We could only root for his success in his future endeavors.
“...I really hope your dream comes true.”
“Oh, does that mean you’rrre the boss, now? I will definitely come visit.”
“If I ever need to go to the blacksmith, I can just go to your shop from now on.”
“Yes, that will work! Really, just thinking about it makes me happy! Hahaha!”

After the fait accompli that was the dwarf’s resignation, it was Rotmiller who took over the conversation. “Murad, don’t feel too bad about your decision. After all, I was planning to leave the party after this expedition too.”
“What? You? But why?”

“I sensed that I was lacking. That’s all.” Hikurod didn’t say anything in response to that blunt reply. Rotmiller, who had perhaps anticipated this reaction, continued without hesitation. “Actually, I told Bjorn beforehand. I couldn’t have imagined at the time that it would end like this, though. Now that I’ve earned a sizable amount of money, I will take time to develop myself.”
“...I believe that with your diligence and perseverance, you will be able to achieve any goal.”
After Hikurod’s heartfelt statement, their eyes shifted to me and Missha. They must have been wondering what we were going to do.
I briefly outlined my future plans. “The two of us will form a new party. And we will go even higher.”
“Yes, I thought you would say that.”
“Miss Karlstein has a hard road ahead of her.”
“...Well, it’s my own karrrma, I guess. I can’t do anything other than this, eitherrr.”

We all raised our glasses and toasted to our last drinking party together as Team Half-Wit. Blessing and cheering for each other’s futures, we spent our parting reminiscing on the past. As always, however, time marched on mercilessly, and soon the dwarf and Missha got drunk and hit their heads on the table as they passed out.

“It’s time to start heading home.” I flashed Rotmiller a rueful smile. At the end of a drinking party, we were always the only two left to sort things out. We were finishing our meeting in true Team Half-Wit style.

Just as I was standing up with that thought in mind, Rotmiller deviated from the script, lowered his voice, and called my name like he had been waiting for the two of them to fall asleep. “Bjorn, I want to ask you something.”
“...Speak.”
I stared at him, feeling a strange tension settle on my shoulders. Rotmiller paused. Then, he spoke. “Are you an evil spirit?”
The biggest, most essential task for the safe dissolution of Team Half-Wit yet remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 150: Barbarian Chief (2)
paragraphs: Rotmiller was different from Missha and Hikurod. As a scout, he was attentive and quick-witted, and in many ways, he was a veteran from starting out at the bottom like he had. I didn’t expect him to ask so straightforwardly, though.
Since this is my lot, I guess I’ll have to bear it.

Just one option immediately came to mind. The idea of admitting that I was an evil spirit and appealing to our friendship was complete nonsense, so the only thing I could do was bust his head open in a fit of rage because I had been insulted.
No matter how I think about it, though, this is strange.

It was not just because of affection that my judgment was clouded. I knew a lot about Rotmiller. If he truly thought that I was an evil spirit, a conversation like this wouldn’t even be happening. If I had to compare it to something, he was acting like an herbivore. Put simply, Rotmiller himself also wasn’t confident in his theory. Besides that, I didn’t sense a threat from him. I quickly settled on a game plan.
Just as I thought, it would be best to wait and see for now.

Of course, I had no intention of begging him to trust me by lying and saying I wasn’t. That was not the way of a barbarian man. So, after a silence of about three seconds, I coldly opened my mouth. “Rotmiller, I hope you have a reason for insulting me.” I wanted him to think that it was only because he was my precious comrade that I was letting this slide just this once and asking for his reasoning. When you looked at my track record, this wasn’t a lie. If it had been anyone other than Rotmiller, my fist would have been flying at his head a long time ago.
However, the man only laughed. “You know, I would’ve believed you were genuinely angry. That is, if I hadn’t gotten to know you so well.”
“What?”
“Oaths, honor. You’re not the kind of person to get caught up in ego. And you’re not impulsive enough to be swayed by your emotions, either.”

Rotmiller knew me too well for me to keep acting. The warrior’s oath, which I used like a cheat code, wouldn’t work here, either. So I changed my approach a bit. “...Even I don’t like hearing that from a teammate.”
“Hm, that is true.” Rotmiller shrugged and gulped down his remaining liquor. The atmosphere was much more relaxed than before. “But you are much too special.”

Rotmiller continued. A barbarian who could read, a barbarian who was not controlled by emotions, a pragmatic barbarian who valued other things above honor—most of these were things that could be glossed over as simply exceptional. Except for the last one: a barbarian who knew information that a warrior less than a year into his career could never know.
“Back then, in the labyrinth, you claimed you heard a revelation.”

After we left Larcaz and returned to the Tower of Heavens, I told my suspicious teammates that I had heard the revelation of Behela, my ancestral god. This was a world where gods existed, right? Missha and Hikurod had taken the answer at face value. Even Rotmiller, who I had been worried about, didn’t say anything, so I thought I handled that incident well.
“Who would believe that? I couldn’t believe it, either. That’s why I thought you might be an evil spirit.”
So that’s what you’ve been thinking of me in secret.

Well, if you assumed that I was an evil spirit, everything strange about me could be explained. It was the truth to begin with. However, things seemed very favorable for me right now. “You mean you don’t think that now?”
At my question, Rotmiller nodded without hesitation. “In a book I read, evil spirits were described as beings that treat everyone in the world as puppets. However, you do not.”

Although I placed little value in honor, I cared for my own people enough to advise and lead our young warriors. I felt a sense of loss and anger at the death of a teammate, something that an ordinary evil spirit would never feel. The path I walked had become a shield that protected me without me even needing to come up with a clumsy explanation.

Well, it seemed there was something else that had completely removed Rotmiller’s suspicions. “Besides, didn’t the goddess of the stars give you a blessing? I saw it with my own two eyes, so how can I doubt it?”
A blessing given by Reatlas, the goddess of the stars herself; even though I had grumbled about the vine snapping within a day, this really turned out to be a godsend.
“Thanks to that, I realized how narrow-minded I was being. I thought you were an evil spirit because I was looking at you through normal eyes.”
No, you were looking right...
I listened to Rotmiller’s words, beating down my squirming conscience.
“In this world, there are undoubtedly people who are especially loved by the gods. And history has called them heroes.”
“...That’s too much.”
“Haha, I knew you would say that. You have a tendency to underestimate yourself. But I, at least, sincerely think so.”

I couldn’t say anything in response to Rotmiller’s barrage of compliments. Wouldn’t it be weird to agree with all that? I tried to set my embarrassment aside and asked the last question on my mind. “Then why did you say that?” Rotmiller didn’t think I was an evil spirit anymore. He may have in the past, but not now. So why did he throw a fastball at me and ask if I was an evil spirit?
His answer was completely unexpected. “I wanted to give you a warning and some advice.”
“A warning and advice?”
“Yes. You are wise, but inexperienced in this area. No matter how much you trust your teammates, you need to hide yourself.”
“I don’t know what you mean.”

“Aren’t you going to form a new party? Your special nature will inevitably stick out like a sore thumb. There may even be those who evaluate you the same way as I did.” Rotmiller said that as long as I couldn’t reveal the blessing I had been given, I should try to lay low as much as possible. This would prevent issues in the future. “As someone who has lived an ordinary life, I really wanted to tell you this.”
“...I see. Thanks. I will take your advice to heart, always.”
“Hmm, this conversation went on longer than I intended. Let’s wrap up this meeting here. I will carry Murad.”
That was how Team Half-Wit’s final drinking party ended. And unlike usual, we parted ways without scheduling our next gathering.
“I hope that the path you are walking on will be full of light.”
Team Half-Wit. I really learned a lot from them.

The conversation with Rotmiller was informative, not because of the advice he gave, but because the situation itself set off alarm bells. Although things had worked out this time, it could happen again anytime. And there was no guarantee it would be the same next time, so I thought about it. If a teammate, and one I was attached to, ended up convinced that I was an evil spirit and even had proof of it, then what should I do?
I didn’t bother to voice the answer out loud. That wouldn’t change anything. I would try to survive, even if I had to become a terrible human being to do it.
...I’ll have to be more careful.

In order to prevent that tragedy from coming to fruition, I decided to pay attention to each and every move I made, just like when I first fell into this strange world. I needed to operate under the assumption that I could only trust myself and be more systematic about my plans and actions. If I really cared for them, this was the right thing to do.
“Bjorn, what arrre you thinking about?”
“It’s nothing.”
“I didn’t say something weirrrd while I was drunk yesterday, right?”
The morning after Team Half-Wit’s last dinner, I left the inn with Missha and headed to the Great Temple. We didn’t have to go together, but we had to visit Kommelby later, anyway.
As soon as I arrived at the temple, I called for Krovitz.
“Nice to see you again. Do you have another issue?” The young paladin in his early thirties had a curious look on his face, as I had returned after only two days.
I brought up the matter straightforwardly. “It’s not an issue, but I have a favor to ask.”
“A favor... Let’s hear it, first.”

“I want you to arrange a meeting with the dragon tribe. I decided it would be better to return this as you said and ask for a different reward, after all.” The Dragon Slayer sword was a valuable treasure, but I had determined that the only thing it would do if I held onto it was rust.
“May the blessing of the twilight star be with you. This will be very good news for them.”

Did he think I was doing this for the public good? Krovitz readily agreed and said he would arrange a meeting with them. For me, this was a load off my shoulders. It would be tough for a rank-six barbarian to arrange a meeting with the leaders of the dragon tribe on his own.
And since we’re meeting through the temple, they won’t think about robbing us or stealing the reward.
“When the date is set, I will send a message to the address you left.”
“Thanks for your help.”
Okay, that matter was settled. I left the temple with Missha and boarded the carriage to Kommelby. As soon as we got off, we headed to the Central Exchange for a simple reason.
I have to upgrade the Spirit Imprint immediately.

If word got out that I had received a blessing, there was a possibility that I’d be kicked out of the tribe. So, before that, stage six needed to be undergone. And for stage six, you needed materials on top of money.
“Are you registered for consignment sales?”

“I came because I have something I’m looking for,” I said, submitting the documents I had prepared in advance to the staff. I needed an immortal heart, a raw material that could very rarely be obtained from the remains of a Troll caught with distortion magic. It was expensive, but if you had enough money, it was much better to buy it. Even those who specialized in hunting Trolls could only find one once every few months.
“There is a total of one item that meets your criteria. Would you like to look at the description?”

The look-up fee was three thousand stones, and the confirmed price was eighteen million stones. It was up one million stones from the last time. “...I’ll buy it.” It was a little depressing, but I just bought it nonchalantly anyway. This item was so understocked that the entire exchange only had one. If this one got sold, there was no telling when it’d be in stock again.
If the sixth stage costs this much, from the seventh on, I’ll probably have to find the materials myself.

Arriving at the storage room with that thought in mind, I checked the item for defects and took it. With this, I had accomplished my goal for today. It was Missha’s turn next. “Let’s change your sword again.”

“...Is that why you brought me herrre?” Missha shot me a look that seemed to ask why I was the one deciding that, but she didn’t really resist. This wasn’t strange. She must have noticed the limitations of steel too.
“With this new party, the goal will be to reach the sixth floor, so don’t think about saving money.”
“...If there is something I like.”

Since it was a weapon that Missha was going to use, I searched for a suitable item while taking her opinion into account. It took longer than expected. We agreed to purchase a grade-three Iril long sword made of mithril and steel, but choosing a design was the problem.
“Ugh, it’s not about choosing the prettier one!”
“Yeah, let’s just go with that. Anyway, go ahead and choose. By the way, I think this one looks good.”
“Oh, well, guess who isn’t a barbarrrian. You just think that all it needs to be is heavy.”

Despite grumbling, Missha chose her sword carefully. Apparently, you had to be attentive to things like weight distribution and reach. While explaining that, she even listed off the names of famous blacksmiths that she had memorized, which surprised me. It seemed she was also an adventurer, after all.
“Wow, to think the day has come that I can use a sword worrrth twelve million stones...”
“If you took off the enchantment on it, you could’ve saved at least four million.”

“Still, if you’re going to buy it, you should buy a good one! I will use it for the rest of my life!” Missha declared resolutely after she finished picking up the items from the storage room, hugging the sword like a baby. “Ughh, I rrreally need to save the remaining money...”
I cocked my head. “Why are you saving money? Leave only the money you need, and use all the rest to buy and consume Beast Blood.”
Where a barbarian had a Spirit Imprint, a beastperson had a Soul Beast. Soul Beasts developed over time, but Beast Blood was able to shorten that length.
“I told you earlier. Don’t even think about being frugal.”
“...Is it really okay to spend it rrrecklessly like this?”
“It’s not reckless, it’s an investment in the future.”

Missha asked if it wouldn’t be better to buy an essence instead, but that didn’t seem reasonable to me. Essences of rank five and above cost tens of millions of stones. And there was no need for her to buy anything below that.
“You haven’t unlocked the power of your Soul Beast yet. I think it’s right to focus on that for now.”

In the end, with my powerful persuasion, Missha used all her money (excluding her emergency fund) to purchase Beast Blood. She said she’d take it home later. We’d know tomorrow if any unique abilities had manifested.
“Then let’s get going.”
After spending our fortune for several hours, we returned to the residential sector. The time was around 8 p.m. when the day slowly got darker and dusk began to fall.
I can do the Spirit Imprint at the holy land tomorrow and be done with that...

I organized the things I had to do before the next labyrinth opened. There were three things left: 1. Meet the dragon tribe and return Dragon Slayer; 2. Get information about Orcules and Noark; and 3. Build a new party.
Oh, come to think of it, I didn’t ask her about that. When I remembered, I did so straight away. “Missha, is there anything you look for or do in particular when looking for a teammate?”

We had already roughly decided what roles would fill the remaining three seats. However, it was necessary to hear Missha out. She was not only an original member, but her career was longer than mine. I figured that I might get advice about something I hadn’t even considered.
“Umm...” After seriously thinking it over, Missha carefully opened her mouth. “I... d-don’t want an elf.”
Well, that was an unexpected requirement.

chapters.title: Chapter 151: Barbarian Chief (3)
paragraphs: We had me, a tank, and Missha, a cold-type melee damage dealer. Now we needed to recruit three more party members that fit this combination.
One priest, one wizard, and one archer or scout.

The first configuration that came to mind was this. You could say it was the fundamental team comp in Dungeon and Stone. Since my vampire essence was gone, the presence of a priest would be of great help to the team.
But I’m giving up on the priest.

Or, rather, it’d be misleading to say I was giving up. I had even asked Krovitz if he could introduce me to a priest, but he refused point-blank. Apparently there needed to be at least three rank-five adventurers in the party and the party had to have a certain number of accomplishments under its belt first.
The basic recruitment conditions are stricter than in the game.

That was disappointing, but not a major problem. Although having a priest would greatly increase the team’s cohesion, I’d also been deliberately pushing it off because of the downside of disadvantageous deals.
I’m starting to get a sense of how to form the party.
That evening, I had learned the shocking fact that Missha was racist. After I finished gathering my thoughts, I got dressed, went outside, and headed to the tavern I had been meaning to visit.
Jingle!

As soon as I opened the door, I saw a woman from the Black Bear tribe who was built like a boulder. She asked if I was alone. When I answered with Mr. Bear’s name, the woman pursed her lips and pointed to a spot with her chin. Mr. Bear, a rank-five adventurer, was carrying drinks and food to some guests with his apron on.
“We don’t even have any customers, yet he always invites his friends.”
I sat down in an empty seat, trying to ignore the grumbling behind me. After Mr. Bear finished serving a round, I quietly raised my hand and waved him over.
“Oh, hold on. I’ll be th—Bjorn Yandel?”
“Let’s talk for a minute.”

At my words, Mr. Bear gently shifted his gaze and side-eyed the counter. I didn’t expect him to be like this, but he was totally whipped by his wife. I was just planning to talk for a bit, but I ended up ordering two snacks and drinks. I figured that this would make things less tense.

“...Ahem.” Soon after, Mr. Bear, who had brought the order over, sat down across from me with an embarrassed look on his face. “It’s not always like this,” he said, coming up with an excuse. “You know that, right? It’s just that the tavern is very busy these days...”
It was pretty quiet for a busy tavern, but I didn’t bother saying that. What was so embarrassing about being a family man?
Soon, Mr. Bear opened his mouth and changed the subject. “So, seeing as you are here, does that mean you’ve left your original party?”
“...The party disbanded.”

“From the look on your face, you must have lost someone.” I neither confirmed nor denied that. However, my silence was enough of an answer. Mr. Bear smiled bitterly and gulped down an entire glass. “It’s a damned thing, that is.”
“Yeah, it really was.” I also threw back the entire glass and ordered two more. Then we finally got to talking.
“How many have you gathered?”
“Only two for now.”
“That must be you and the red cat woman.”
“So, your answer?”
“All right, I’ll join you.”

After Mr. Bear calmly agreed, he started asking questions: what floor we were aiming for, how the loot distribution would work, and how I was going to fill in the remaining two spots. I briefly mentioned the party comp I was thinking of.
“First of all, there has to be a wizard, for sure. And the remaining spot... leaves us no choice but to find a scout.”

Actually, there had also been the option to put Erwen on the team in the archer position instead of Mr. Bear. However, it was unclear how well a kid who’d just started adventuring lessons would do. In addition, Mr. Bear, who had a summon that could serve as a tank, was able to cover for the absence of a priest to some extent, so I had chosen him instead.
“Until a scout is found, we’ll hire one. We plan to distribute the rest equally, except for the scout.”
“I see.” Mr. Bear nodded. “If I play the scout, can you increase my share?” he asked bluntly.
“What?”
“Just as I said.”

What the hell was this old man talking about? Did he just say that he was a scout? If so, there was something I didn’t understand at all. “Didn’t you say you were lost on the first floor for nineteen hours when we met?”
“...Did I even tell you the time?”
“It was around 19:00 on the first day when the Rift opened.”

Mr. Bear had been wandering around the Crystal Cave even then, unable to find the portal to the second floor. No matter where you ended up in the labyrinth, a scout would accurately know the direction of the portal on the first floor. Nineteen hours didn’t make sense when I considered that Rotmiller’s record was six hours.
“Ah, that... You know the path in the Crystal Cave is a bit complicated.”
“Huh?”

“I know where the portal is, but it’s always difficult to find it.” Mr. Bear went on to explain that he only gave directions, and that his other teammates were usually the ones responsible for finding the way.
I didn’t know what to say to that, so I asked, “To put it simply, are you saying you are a scout but bad with directions?”
“Ahem! My former coworkers said so. It’s hard to admit, honestly.”
What was hard to admit? Even an ordinary person could find their way to the second floor’s portal within a day as long as they had a compass.
A scout who is bad with directions...

I didn’t know how that was possible, but I didn’t express those thoughts and wrapped the conversation up. “I will think about the loot distribution. I need to listen to the opinions of those who will be joining later too.”
“That is enough for me.”
“Then our conversation is over.”
We had our first teammate: Abman Urikfried, a rank-five archer with a tank summon, and a guide whose aptitude for navigation was near zero.
“I hope we work well together, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
Our specs may have gone up a lot, but was it just me or were we beginning to see the return of Team Half-Wit?
In commemoration of becoming a team, we even clinked glasses for a while. Soon, Mrs. Bear glared at us. “Honey, how long are you going to play around?”
“D-Dear? No, this is not playing.” Mr. Bear got up in a hurry and headed to his wife, after which they talked in hushed voices. At first, it seemed like a scolding.

“Oh my gosh, you should have said that earlier. The person who will be my husband’s new teammate!” She came up to me and gave me a friendly smile after their conversation was over. “Nice to meet you. People call you Little Balkan, right? Seeing how tall and strong you are makes me a little relieved.”
“I-I’m glad.”
“Yes. To be honest, I didn’t really like his previous teammates. How could they not show their faces here even after working as a team for over half a year?”
“...Previous teammates?” I was sure this man was playing solo, no? I quietly glanced at Mr. Bear. He was shaking his head repeatedly, his face pale. A past conversation came to mind.
“You have a wife, yet you enter the labyrinth alone?”
“The restaurant is in the red these days. I figure I should at least earn some money.”

It was good to work hard, but I never suspected he had been working alone while lying to his wife. Following the revelation of his poor sense of direction, it felt like my first impression of him was crumbling down. I had thought he was going to be a reliable yet wise teammate, almost like a bear. Now I saw that he was just a man living in the moment.
“Anyway, please consider your food today my treat. And although my husband may be lacking, I hope you take good care of him in the future.”
Not wanting to interfere in someone else’s family affairs and get caught in the crossfire, I half ran away from the tavern.

When I arrived at the inn, Erwen had ordered a drink and was sitting in the lobby on the first floor waiting for me. “Oh, Mister. Have you been drinking?” I wondered if she came by to continue her story from last time. Before I had time to say anything, though, Erwen delivered an apology. “I’m sorry!”
“Sorry? What do you mean?”
“I had no idea what happened to your teammate and I—”
“How do you know about that?”
“Your face seemed so dark back then, so I asked your other teammate.”

When I asked who she was talking about, she answered Hikurod. It seemed likely that he’d told her what happened without mistrust because she told him that she was my former comrade. Fortunately, it seemed he left out the blessing and the Dragon Slayer parts.

“You must’ve had a hard time. I know... what it feels like to lose something.” Erwen sniffled and touched my hand. It was very embarrassing, like being comforted by a three-year-old child. It was a little late, anyway. By now, I’d pretty much already finished sorting out my thoughts.
“...Let’s stop talking about that. Anyway, it’s good that you’re here. I had something to tell you.”
“What is it? Uh, I still have something left to do...”
“Left to do?”
“...It’s nothing. So, what did you want to talk about?”
I decided to be blunt. “I’m starting a new team, are you interested in joining?”

Originally, I didn’t plan to include Erwen. Of course, it wasn’t because of Missha’s request. It was just that after much thought, I chose Mr. Bear for our archer, and there was no room left. However, the situation had changed now that I knew that Mr. Bear was a scout. The spot meant for the real scout was now available.
She’s lacking combat power for now, but with enough work, she’ll be able to pull her own weight.
The fact that she was getting scouting lessons from her sister was a great bonus. It would be perfect if she guided the way with Mr. Bear.
“Um...” Erwen only managed to come up with an answer after a long period of silence. “I’m really glad you made the offer, so don’t get me wrong.”
So, it was a no. “Is it because of your sister?”
“No. It’s because of me. I still have a lot to learn from my sister.”

Her response was unexpected. Well, it wasn’t that I couldn’t understand where she was coming from, though. There was no doubt sticking with her sister now would help her develop. It had only been a few months since she started getting adventuring lessons, and I couldn’t teach her about elemental spirit magic, either.
“I see. Okay.”
“Um... you’re not mad, are you?”
“Why would I be? It’s a great choice. You too have become an adventurer now.”

“Ah, I haven’t received a compliment in a long time...” Erwen stared off into space blankly for a minute before clearing her throat and coming back down to earth. Then she spoke in a determined voice. “Please wait for me for just half a year. After half a year, I will have learned everything I can learn from my sister and join your party.”
Well, the thought was nice, but... This now felt like I was hiring someone for corporate espionage.
Crumble.
For some reason, I swore I could hear her sister’s world come crashing down.

The next morning, as soon as I opened my eyes, I headed to the holy land without even washing up. It was a reasonable assessment that there was no need to wash up when going to a place full of barbarians, anyway.
It feels like I’ve come back to my hometown.

I was not even a real barbarian, but there was something comforting about the green bushes here. There was a time it had been uncomfortable because the chieftain was scary, but it at least felt like that now. Maybe that was why...
Goddamn it.
Suddenly, the blessing came to mind and my heart felt heavy. An instinct trained by constant misfortune whispered in my ear. It said a secret that more than ten people knew couldn’t be kept forever.
Even if I finish the sixth stage today, it will take several more years to reach the ninth stage...

Unlike the other races, who had abandoned the old ways, barbarians were close to maddeningly stubborn. If it were known that I had been entrusted with a blessing from a star goddess rather than an ancestral god, super rookie or not, the chieftain would step in and try to kick me out.
I’m going to think about that later...

I walked through the bushes and headed toward the center of the holy land. As I was doing so, I saw young warriors gathered in an empty field, little fighters practicing martial arts while waiting for their coming-of-age ceremonies. This was what I always saw when I came here, but...
Is that... Kharon?

I saw a familiar face among the young warriors: Kharon, son of Tarson. He had once been an ignorant baby barbarian, but he had accepted the world’s dark side and become a full-fledged warrior. He now stood in front of the young barbarians like a drill instructor.
“All together. Humans are...?”
“Enemies!”
“Our hearts...?”
“Must be protected!”

It was rote education that was closer to brainwashing than anything else, but even with this, their chances of survival would be much higher. I looked at them with a pleased smile until I realized one thing.
But what is that?

Kharon and several of the senior barbarians who seemed to have followed him looked strange. For some reason, they were each carrying three or four backpacks. I wondered if it was a fashion trend among barbarians.
“Instructor! What about those bags?” one of the young warriors raised his hand and asked. Apparently, I wasn’t the only one who found the look strange.

Kharon replied with a smile as if he had been waiting for someone to draw attention to it. “Good question, young warrior! This is Robert, this is John, this is Aiden...” Kharon called out the name of each backpack on his left and right as well as his front and back.
“Hahaha! Those sound like people’s names!” the baby barbarian chuckled.
“That’s because they’re all human names.” Kharon was no longer laughing.
“...W-What do you mean?”
Kharon explained in detail how he had obtained the backpacks to the shocked baby barbarians, and again continued his mental conditioning regime.
“Repeat again. Humans are...?”
“Enemies!”
“Our hearts...?”
“Must be protected!”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel is...?”
“A great warrior!”
I watched, rendered speechless. What the hell had I done?

chapters.title: Chapter 152: Barbarian Chief (4)
paragraphs: “Ah, uh... um...”

After staring blankly at the wild brainwashing scene for a while, I came to my senses and entered the village. To be honest, the word “village” was misleading. The barbarians’ holy land was closer to a campsite. Tents were pitched anywhere, without distinction between your land and mine. After passing through that, I headed straight to the shaman’s tent. It wasn’t like I didn’t know the location at this point, so I decided that there was no need to set up a meeting through the chieftain.
What, no one’s here?

When I opened the shaman’s tent, it was empty. In the end, I had no choice but to go to the chieftain’s tent anyway. But in a twist, there was no one in the chief’s tent either. Even if the chieftain wasn’t there, the elders usually took turns overseeing it.
The heck?
As I was walking around in front of it, an elder I had seen a few times before found me. “Bjorn, son of Yandel? Are you also here to attend the funeral?”
There was no need to ask whose funeral it was. It had been exactly half a year since Ainar had been locked away in the holy land.
“...It’s already that day.”
“It is an honor to be able to leave something behind for future generations.”

After asking where the funeral was being held, I headed straight there, to a dark, desolate forest. I had traveled for about thirty minutes when I spotted the barbarians gathered in its depths with solemn expressions on their faces. There were the shaman and chieftain, as well as some familiar elders. Well, the first person I noticed was someone else, though.
“Ainar.”

Ainar stood there listlessly, leaning against a thick tree as she stared intently at the corpse of her master. “...Bjorn?” Ainar’s eyes were blank as she said my name. Then, as I drew nearer, she bit her lip. “If I had known this would happen, I wouldn’t have done it.”
She hadn’t known. I thought for sure they would have told her.
“...Bjorn, did you know?”
“Yes.”

The training that Ainar had been undergoing for six months was called “Forging” among the barbarians, the process of training someone to develop a certain build. In the game, when you finished Forging, your physique stats increased significantly and you were eligible to receive a Soul Succession. Of course, you could stop at just Forging, though.
“I had heard that this elder had a chronic illness,” I said.
When I heard that the lifespan of the elder who had made Ainar his successor was short, I had considered this possibility. But it seemed she herself had been unaware of it.
“That—I didn’t know!”
“It seems the elder cared a lot about you.”

Soul Succession, along with the Spirit Imprint, was one of the unique enchantments available only to barbarians. Through this ritual, a barbarian could pass on one of their essences to future generations. But you could receive it only once, and those passing on the essence lost their lives.
“...Why didn’t anyone tell me? If I had known this was going to happen, I would have stopped right away,” Ainar lamented in a voice full of regret and remorse.
The chieftain, who had been observing us, opened his mouth. “Kiduba was a coward.”
“Don’t insult him! Kiduba was a fearless warrior!”
“Then it must be you who are a coward. That’s why Kiduba couldn’t explain Soul Succession to you.”
“I am not a—!”

As Ainar began to snap, the chieftain cut her off at once. “Then stop whining. If you want to prove that you’re not a coward, face his death without insulting him any further, warrior. There is not a single person in the world who doesn’t feel pain. Even so, you must face it and move on. That is the way of a warrior.”

After that, Ainar kept her mouth shut, and the chieftain did not speak for a long time. The funeral continued in silence. The shaman approached the body, which was leaning against a tree, smeared blood on his face, and rang a bell. Then, a solution was sprayed all around to prevent insects from eating the corpse. The barbarians silently watched the process, and soon the shaman announced the end of the funeral ceremony.
“The spirit of Kiduba, the third son of Tohar, has left its body and settled in the forest.”

Now, the corpse would be left in the forest to rot and become white bones. Then, when that time came, the shaman would break even the bones into small pieces and scatter them through the forest. The warriors standing in front of the corpse all cut off their hair or slit their hands and sprinkled blood around him before leaving. The entire process didn’t take too long.
Now it was only me and Ainar. I approached the corpse first, cut off my hair with a knife, and scattered it around. “Now it is your turn.”
Ainar did not answer. However, rather than pushing further, I just left without a word. As this had been a farewell she hadn’t been prepared for, she needed time to come to terms with it on her own.
“Keke, I knew you would come, warrior.” Soon after leaving the forest, I entered the shaman’s tent. “Did you bring the ingredient?”
“Yes.”
“Come, take it out.”
Following the shaman’s instructions, I took out the Immortal Heart—the heart of a Troll—that I had stored in my backpack. It was resting on a piece of cloth in a box, still pounding lightly.
“Did you get it yourself?”
“No, I bought it at the exchange.”

“For how much?” I didn’t know why he was curious about that, but once I answered, the shaman giggled. “How has a barbarian like you appeared? You are undoubtedly blessed with financial fortune, warrior.”

Most of my conversations with the shaman were like this, but strangely, this comment left me in a bad mood today. Without thinking, I shot back, “Don’t talk about financial fortune when you don’t know anything.”
At my words, the shaman just grinned. “Hmm, since you came back alive and well, the problem probably isn’t you... Have you lost something?”
“I don’t want to answer that.”
“Sure, that’s fine too.” I didn’t reply. “Warrior, the more precious things you lose, the stronger you will become.”
I very much wanted to curse him out, but I just kept quiet. For some reason, the more I talked to this old man, the more I felt like I was losing. “Sure. Can I get the Spirit Imprint today?”
“Of course.” The shaman happily nodded his head at my question. I had thought he might be tired from the funeral ceremony.
Clink.
I put the million stones charged by the shaman into the jar and laid on the floor. I had reached the sixth imprint of the Immortality Path.
“This time, too, there are three paths ahead of you.”

After listening to a brief explanation of each, I chose one. There was no need to think it through. In the first place, I had poured all my money into the Imprint for this one thing. “I will choose the Soul of Battle.”
“Keke, even if you want to change it later, you won’t be able to.”

Soon after, the shaman started stabbing me with needles. Before long, a sharp pain overtook me, but I was able to deal with it better than before. This was for a psychological reason that had nothing to do with the intensity of the pain. I knew that a very big reward lay at the end of this.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 6. Your Soul Regeneration has significantly increased. Your Special Ability stat has increased by +60.]

I had managed to significantly increase the stat that was the hardest to obtain—MP regeneration. Simply put, that meant that I could now use Giantization more often and sustain it for longer. This was nothing compared to the main event, though.
[A Spirit of Battle now resides in your body. Thanks to the special ability Union, Equipment Performance increases in proportion to your Ability level.]

Union, a passive skill that was always paired with the active skill Wild Outburst, was already great on its own. However, there was a hidden aspect to this skill. Perhaps because the whole point of it was the idea of becoming one body in battle, if you had this, your equipment wouldn’t be damaged even while using Giantization. In other words, I wouldn’t have to take off my cumbersome armor anymore. Not only that, but it would also be possible for me to smash enemies with a super-giant mace and shield!
“Ughhh... Behel... ahhh...”
As he watched me cry-laugh even through the lingering pain, the shaman muttered to himself. “Keke, definitely not a sane one, this one.”
Like a barbarian, I let that assessment go in one ear and out the other.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 4
Physique: 555 (New +225)
Spirit: 198 (New +44)
Special Ability: 188 (New +60)
Item Level: 98 (New -770)
General Combat Power: 965.5 (New +23.5)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Orc Hero - Rank 5  Ogre - Rank 3 (New)]

A lot of time had passed since I began imprinting the sixth stage. Beyond the tent, it was still bright out. As I gulped down the water from the kettle on the side table, I asked, “Has it already been a day?”
“Kekeke, are you going to cry to me about how hard it was?”

Jeez, why not just answer with “Yes”? I couldn’t understand his manner of speaking no matter how many times I heard it, but I didn’t bother to argue with him. Or, more accurately, I had no strength with which to do so. I was about to grab my backpack to get up, when...

“Warrior.” The shaman, who always told me to get lost right around this time, called out to me and promptly dropped a completely unexpected bombshell. “How did you come to receive a blessing from a human god?”
My heart dropped, but I let out a long sigh. It was clear that he already knew everything, so there was no point in denying it. “Who did you hear that from? No, how many people know about it?”

“How could I not know? The ring you wear is greatly intertwined with your destiny. Keke, don’t worry, though. The others will never notice.” The shaman jeered, adding that they had knotholes for eyes. That was when I noticed that the shaman seemed to be in a strangely agreeable mood despite the topic of our discussion.
“Are you going to tell the chieftain?” I asked cautiously.
“Why should I do that?”
I didn’t really have anything to say to that.

“It’s just an old custom. Just like what I did in the forest yesterday. Thousands of years ago, we left our homeland and arrived in this city. Because of that, we learned about the existence of gods, and learned how to actually be civilized.”
“What are you trying to tell me?”

“While we rely on and follow the will of our ancestors, why should we reject and hate a being that genuinely helps us? That is just foolish stubbornness, something that truly deserves to be called barbaric.” At his core, the shaman still hadn’t changed, especially in terms of his strange manner of speaking. Of course, I couldn’t say anything that might get me on his bad side while he had such a powerful grip on my greatest weakness.
“...So, what do you think the chieftain will do?”
“If he finds out about your blessing, you mean?”
“Yes.”
The shaman giggled. “Why ask what you already know? That roughneck will brand you a traitor right away and kick you out. Slash! Or maybe cut off your head and burn it.”
So, that was how it was. Goddamn it, did I have no choice but to live in suspense until I finished the Spirit Imprint?
As I pursed my lips bitterly at the thought, the shaman continued. “Warrior, you are worrying for nothing.”
“What do you mean?”
“Beasts, dwarves, and elves all abandoned the old traditions long ago. Why do you think that is the case?”

I didn’t have to think too hard about it. Earth’s history was the same. When new ideas and reforms were needed, there were always those who decided to turn their backs on the old. Later generations then called these people great.
This deranged old man...
It was then that I realized what the shaman was trying to say.
“Are you worried about being kicked out, warrior? If so, the solution to that problem is very simple.”

It seemed this grandpa was also a barbarian, after all. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have dared to think up a solution like this. If there was a problem, destroy the problem by destroying it—that was the barbarian way. So, in other words...
“You just need to become the chieftain of the tribe.”
Take over the barbarians before I could be exiled.
“How about it? Isn’t that a much more warrior-like path?”

I didn’t know if it was a warrior-like path or not. Without thinking, though, I laughed out loud. I was a barbarian less than a year old who was actually an evil spirit. To tell me to become a barbarian chieftain so I could change this society to my liking?
“Those are funny words, shaman.”
It was a rather tempting suggestion, especially since it made sense.

chapters.title: Chapter 153: Barbarian Chief (5)
paragraphs: There were three major advantages to becoming the chieftain. First, I wouldn’t have to hide the fact that I had received a blessing. In addition, I could change the barbarians’ illogical way of doing things, which had been in decline for decades, to my liking. Third, in the future, when I retrieved the Barbarian Genesis Treasure, I would be able to use it as I pleased.

It wasn’t that being the chieftain was the only way. It was just a matter of how tribal policy had changed before that. The fact was that barbarians were a conservative race that valued tradition, but they had made progress (albeit little by little) under certain past chieftains, like using honorifics and showing courtesy to the king.
