They now also acknowledged the existence of evil spirits and sent their corpses to the Great Temple. Considering their long history, it hadn’t been long since it was taken for granted that warriors would live in the city rather than the holy land. Maybe about six hundred years?
In the past, erasing essences at the temple was forbidden by the entire race.

It was actually pretty absurd that only this much had changed over thousands of years. Rather than saying that the chieftain had no authority to make changes, it would be more accurate to assume that a person who could do so had not yet appeared. Not only did the tribe’s chieftain have overwhelming authority in matters of the tribe, but warriors tended to believe and follow most of the chieftain’s words because they thought the chieftain was smarter than them. Well, even so, if reform began there would inevitably be resistance, but that part could be changed slowly with enough time.
It’s not a bad idea.

The shaman’s suggestion only sounded ridiculous for a moment. The more I looked at it, the more it seemed like a very sound option. The problem was that it would take at least a few years to become the tribe’s chieftain the normal way.
I heard that the current chieftain was once an adventurer on the eighth floor.
His exact adventurer’s rank was unknown, but it was clear that it would take a long time to catch up to him in terms of combat ability.
I don’t necessarily have to go all the way to the eighth floor.

My cut-off should be around the sixth floor. Not all tribal chieftains in the past were as strong as our current one. Even if they lacked strength in battle, as long as they had good leadership skills or sound judgment, they were promoted to chieftain of the tribe.
I need to gather my own supporters from now on. Even if it’s not to become chieftain, having influence within the tribe will definitely be helpful.
Just as I finished gathering my thoughts—
“Warrior, you seem to have a lot on your mind. I’m hungry, so get out.”
“Ah, oh... yeah. Sure. Enjoy your meal.”
The shaman ordered me to leave. Jeez, he was the one who had lit the fire in my heart first.
Grumble!
Actually, I was hungry too.
When I left the shaman’s tent around 9 a.m., I smiled bitterly.
Somehow, every time I come here, I end up wasting a whole day.

Still, maybe because I had passed out, my body felt more refreshed than it usually did when I woke up, and I felt ready to start the day like this. In that spirit, I grabbed one of the elders passing by. “Do you know where Ainar is?”
“I haven’t seen her since the Forest of Warriors yesterday.”
Hmm, could she still be there? I was a little worried, so I headed to the forest where the funeral had been held yesterday. A while later, I found Ainar lying in the bushes, drooling.
“B-Bjorn?”
“Did you sleep here?”

“I-I wasn’t planning to, but...” Ainar looked away, embarrassed, as she wiped her spit with the back of her hand. Unfortunately, her eyes landed on Kiduba. “Oh...” As if waking up from a dream and facing reality, Ainar let out a short sigh. After sitting there in silence for a while, she carefully opened her mouth. “Hey, Bjorn?”
“Speak.”
“Do you have anything to eat?”
Now that was a barbarian. I chuckled and set down my backpack. Then, I took out the preserved food I usually ate in the labyrinth and we ate together.
“Are you okay now?”
“I’m a little annoyed, but still better.”
“Annoyed?”

“He deceived me. If he had been honest, I wouldn’t have shown such an unsightly side of myself. Kiduba has made me act like a coward in front of everyone.” Ainar snorted in anger, and I got the sense that she fully believed what she was saying. It was quite fascinating that she could overcome sadness and enter this stage of grief in just one day. “By the way, Bjorn, did something happen to you too?”
“What do you mean?”
“It just feels like something did. Your expression is darker than it was the last time we met. If that’s because of me, I just want to tell you that you don’t have to feel that way on my behalf.”
A darker expression, huh? “...It’s not because of you, don’t worry.”
“If not me, who is it?”
“it’s...” I considered coming up with an excuse but abandoned the idea a moment later. “Probably because a teammate of mine died.”
“...I see. Is it okay if I ask what happened?”

I gave her a brief summary of what had happened on this expedition. Ainar quietly listened without any of her usual energetic interjections. When it was all over, she quietly recited the name as if not to forget it, then briefly expressed her condolences. “Riol Warb Dwalkie... I wish I had gotten to meet him before.”
Ainar and Dwalkie, huh? It was tough to imagine the two together, but Dwalkie had even been best friends with the dwarf. They might have turned out to be good friends. Well, not that it mattered now.

A moment later, Ainar got up from her seat and made a sudden proposal. “Anyway, Bjorn, why don’t you fight me?” she asked. “I want to see if I have become a warrior strong enough not to hold you back.”
“You mean you want to join the party I’m assembling?”
“If you think I deserve it.”
How barbaric. The fact that she didn’t expect any bias from our friendship was a sign of how dependable she was. However, you had to draw a line between your business and personal lives.
“Ainar, aside from the wizard position, there is only one spot left. And I was thinking of having a wizard fill that role as well.”
“Speak plainly.”
I grinned. “What I mean to say is: do your best.”
Ainar answered with a shout of, “Behelahhh!” and suddenly, a greatsword was in her hand and swinging for my neck.

Tank, Melee, Ranged, Wizard—all vital positions within the party had already been selected. However, thanks to Mr. Bear doubling as a scout, the spot that would have gone to a scout had become vacant, a kind of bonus spot. The identity of the team I would create would be determined by which class of character I put in that position. Would we have the instantaneous firepower of two wizards, or the steady damage of two long-range fighters? Or should I instead seek consistency and hunting speed with two close-range warriors? After much deliberation, I had decided to go with two wizards.
“Behelahhh!”
However, as my spar with Ainar began, my uncertainties grew.
She’s definitely gotten a lot stronger.
She’d had half a year of training in swordsmanship, stat increases from Forging, plus the rank-four essence she had inherited from the elder.
I didn’t expect her to inherit that essence. She really is lucky.

Right now, in terms of power, she was almost no different from Missha. Considering the fact that she only had two essences, her potential in the second half was considerable. There was only one thing that bothered me.
This would make the team too melee-heavy.
Thanks to the essence of the Ogre, I was also able to deal damage. So, if Ainar joined, our team would have three melee fighters.
“Let’s stop here.”
“I can still go longer!”
“I know. But I don’t think there’s a point in continuing.”
“...Am I not qualified?”
I firmly shook my head. “That’s not it.” Although I may not have been wearing armor, the fact was that she’d made me bleed even while Giantized. Needless to say, she had passed.
“Th-then can I come with you on your next expedition?!”
“Can you give me some time to think about it?”
“Ahh! Okay! O-Of course. Is one minute enough?”
“...One minute is too short, let’s make it three.”
“I can wait that long! As you know, I am very patient!”
I closed my eyes and ignored Ainar’s subtle attempt to talk herself up. Since I’d already made the decision in my heart, it didn’t take long. I just wanted to review it one more time.
Soon, I opened my eyes and looked at Ainar. I didn’t have a necklace to put around her neck. “I hope we will work well together.”
“W-Wait. That means...?”
“It is what you think.”
Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin: Pass.
The reason Ainar had passed was simple, and it wasn’t because I had fond memories of beating up Death Fiends with her. I had made my decision after looking a little further into the future.
I’ll have to roll out two teams on the sixth floor, anyway.

On the sixth floor, operating in a small clan rather than a single party was ideal. The scale of the monsters and the strategies needed to survive were too much for five people to handle. I had assessed that it would make sense to send Missha or Ainar to the other team when the time came, since her potential for growth was obvious.
“Ainar, have you gotten an Imprint?”
“Not yet. As you know, I have no money...”
“I see. That’s fine.”
I’d explain the Imprint route to her in detail later. I concluded the conversation there. Ainar headed to the elder’s tent to pack her things, and I waited outside to get my thoughts in order.
One wizard to go...
Actually, this was the biggest challenge in creating a party. Wizards were all snobs. Anyone who wasn’t was bound not to be a proper wizard.
Whew, I’m already tired just from thinking of doing all of that legwork.

I was once again reminded that it was a good idea not to go with the two-wizards strategy. I was acquainted with two wizards, Raven and Ragna, but it wouldn’t be out-there for both of them to turn me down.
Once I get back, the first thing on my to-do list is raising Missha’s and Ainar’s adventurer ranks.
While I was concocting a plan and wandering the holy land, a barbarian spotted me and called, “Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“Kharon, son of Tarson?”
“Nice to see you! But what are you doing here?”

When I told him I came for business, Kharon said this was a great coincidence and asked me to say a few words to the young warriors. I thought about it for a while and replied that I would. Wasn’t I in the middle of seriously pursuing the chieftain position? I did not intend to pass up on the opportunity to attract support. It seemed Ainar needed some time too.
“Really?! The young warriors will be delighted!”
Soon, I followed Kharon into an empty clearing. Dozens of young warriors had already gathered, and as soon as I announced my name, they exploded into fervent cheers.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“A great warrior!”
“Whooo!”
Although I knew this was a result of Kharon’s brainwashing, it still gave me a weird high. I guess I’m a man like any other, huh?
“Behelahhh!” I felt like screaming, so I screamed.
The baby barbarians followed suit. “Behelahhh!”
This was a kind of ecstasy I had been unable to experience since Ainar left the team. Yeah, that was the stuff.

I tried my best to hide my satisfied smile and started to play the role of a guest lecturer in earnest. It wasn’t too tough. Once I had them fight each other like barbarians, I roamed around and provided unlimited tips on how to bash their enemies’ heads in, filling in any gaps in Kharon’s lessons.
“When you get money, the first thing you should do is purchase a video recorder. It will come in handy if you are accused of being a looter.”

I had no intention of putting a stop to Kharon’s money-duplicating bug. It was a bit much even for me, but the victims were plunderers anyway, right? Fewer of them existing would make the world a better place.
“Now, all together. A good plunderer?”
“Is a dead plunderer!”
“The Adventurers’ Guild?”
“Shouldn’t be trusted!”
“If you meet a Hans in the labyrinth?”
“No! Go away! Unless you want to die!”
As I was drilling the things every barbarian adventurer needed to know into their heads, suddenly, goosebumps ran down my spine.
...Murderous intent?

Soon, I stopped teaching and turned around. Standing right behind me like a ghost, I saw a familiar barbarian with a large scar on his face, a long, braided beard, and even the distinct scent of sweat that suggested he hadn’t washed in several days.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.” It was the chieftain. “Recently, I have received a lot of summons from the guild. Is this all your doing?”
I slowly shifted my gaze toward Kharon, who had assured me that the chieftain would not come to find us during training. He was already distancing himself from me, his face pale.
“Explain fast. Before I misunderstand you.”
Ah, uh... um... Goddamn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 154: Barbarian Chief (6)
paragraphs: The chieftain had an ax clutched in his hand, the same ax that had cut off the head of the man next to me at my coming-of-age ceremony.
“Teaching them to kill humans instead of monsters to earn money. Do you think this is the way of a warrior?”

My heated head cooled down. This was unexpected. I thought I might have to face this someday, but I didn’t know that would be today. I calmly caught my breath and made a snap judgment. I could 1) admit that I was wrong and apologize, or 2) come up with excuses. But I immediately dismissed both options from my mind. I knew what kind of race barbarians were. Even if an option seemed easier and more reasonable to the average person, I couldn’t get this wrong. There was only one way through this.
“Chieftain, this is what you should have done.”
Just collide with the problem headfirst like a barbarian.
“...That’s funny.” The chieftain’s mouth twisted. “Tell me, what do you mean?”

It felt like the moment I opened my mouth, that ax would swing. But I proudly straightened my shoulders. What was wrong only became wrong when you admitted it was wrong. But what if you didn’t? Then it became a conviction. Whatever the crux of it was, there was a possibility I could package this like that, which was exactly what I needed to do.

“It is as I said. What I did today was something you should have done a long time ago!” On behalf of a cause, rather than self-interest, I raised my voice in front of the chieftain instead of giving in. I decided that the safest route would be an angry outburst where I pled for the future of the tribe as a young warrior concerned for his people, because the chieftain cared about warriors. “Chieftain! Do you know how many are dying in the labyrinth every month?”
“You cannot become a warrior if you are afraid of death.”
This was now a clash of different values.

“Bjorn, son of Yandel, you should know that the only warriors who become strong are the ones who are able to survive.” Still, believing my actions were truly for the sake of the tribe, the chieftain’s voice softened a bit. But stopping here would get us nowhere.
“Only the warriors who survive become stronger?” I asked.
“You are proof of that!”

He was not wrong. Half of the barbarians died on their first trip into the labyrinth, then another half the next time. By the time half a year had passed since the coming-of-age ceremony, a total of 90 percent of the barbarians in that age group were dead. It was a demented system that was difficult to even call survival of the fittest. To survive it, you had to be strong even if you didn’t want to be.
“Chieftain, did this many die when you first became a warrior?”
“No, they didn’t.”

That was what I thought. It was not that I had particularly studied up on past records, but if this trend had lasted even ten years, the barbarians wouldn’t have even been able to afford to hand out weapons at the coming-of-age ceremonies.
“Then is it because we are weaker than them that so many are dying? Chieftain, do you really think that?”

“That is... also not true.” He could’ve avoided saying anything that damaged his argument, but the chieftain just answered my questions honestly. Well, he was probably also well aware of what the actual reason behind our current state of affairs was.
“In the labyrinth, there are monsters in human skin. They treat us like goblins. Why do you think that is?”
“Wizards take our hearts—”
I sternly cut him off. “No! Because you didn’t do anything!”

If it had been any other race being targeted like this, they would have asked the royal family to make a law to prevent the trade of hearts. Of course, the failure to do so could have been because our race was weak. But our chieftain hadn’t even made the slightest effort, instead using the tradition of survival of the fittest as a shield. He just watched as we all raced to the bottom.
“You should have at least warned them about the dangers! You should have told them what kinds of monsters lurk in the labyrinth and how to deal with them so they could prepare!”
“This is a tradition passed down from the time of our distant ancestors. I cannot change—”
“Our ancestors wanted us to be strong!”

There was no way to interpret the chieftain’s decision as wise. There was no animal anywhere in the vast expanse of nature that chose to die. They all chose evolution and to adapt to their new environment. However, the chieftain had failed to do the obvious.
“Chieftain! Look at us now! In the labyrinth, we’ve become prey as easy to hunt as goblins because we have been taught that only monsters are our enemies! But you say our ancestors wanted this?”
“...Calm yourself.”
“If I were you, I would have at least sent our people off with a pair of leather boots. And given them a pouch to hold mana stones. And taught them how to use a compass in advance—”
“Didn’t I tell you to calm down!?”
Oh, did I cross the line a bit? The cry of the tribal chieftain who had been beaten with facts by a warrior less than a year old shook the forest.
It seemed his rage was skyrocketing because he couldn’t refute me with logic, but he also didn’t want to sit back and listen quietly. “Spit it out!” he demanded. “What do you want to say!”
“If you don’t do it right...” I gulped before delivering my last line. “I will do it, Chieftain.”
For myself, and for the barbarian race.
After I finished proudly expressing my aspirations, the chieftain did not speak for a long time. He just stared at me like he was mulling what I had said over. Then, out of nowhere, he swung the axe.
In an instant, I moved back to dodge it. Then, using Giantization, I reached out and grabbed the axe, and a power struggle began.

It was a landslide victory for the chieftain. My large body of well over ten feet was promptly suspended from the axe and dangled in the air. So, I dropped the axe and charged at him. Then I thrust my fist into the chieftain’s face. However, I did not feel the usual satisfying jolt run through my hand, and when I came to my senses, I saw the chieftain’s large fist appear right in front of my eyes. That was the last thing I remembered.
...So I must be in the chieftain’s tent.
Once I calmly finished piecing together what had happened, I slowly opened my eyes. As expected, I was in a tent and I could see the chieftain.
“You woke up fast.”
“...Chieftain, your nose is inside your face.”
“So is yours.”

Really? No wonder I couldn’t breathe well. I could taste a bit of blood in my spit too. I opened my backpack next to the bed, took out a bottle of potion, took a few sips, and handed the rest to the chieftain. “You drink too.”
“...It’s fine. Why waste a potion? If I leave it, it will be better by tomorrow.”
Well, if you say so.

After roughly popping my nose back in place with my hand, I swiped at the pooled blood like I was blowing my nose and wiped it on the bed. Then I got straight to the point. First, the most pressing matter I had to address. “Are you done being angry?”
“...I wasn’t angry to begin with.”
“Then why?”
“You were a little cocky, so I just felt like hitting you.”
Um, the rest of the world would call that being angry. Anyway, I didn’t have to say anything else because I could sense that his anger was gone now. There were other important matters to deal with.
Good thing that went well.

I had declared that I would become the tribe’s chieftain in front of the tribe’s chieftain. It wasn’t that I had just blurted the words out impulsively, either. I had just wagered that the chieftain wouldn’t kill me over something like this.
“Do you covet my position that much?”
“Yes.” Ambition and aspirations were nothing for a barbarian to be ashamed of—all the more so if conviction and a noble cause were mixed in with them.
“As expected, you are different from the other warriors.”
“What do you mean?”
“Other warriors have wanted the position of tribal leader for the sake of honor. But you are only focused on our tribe.”

Fortunately, I didn’t think he suspected me of being an evil spirit. It seemed the chieftain didn’t actually hate this side of me, either. I was sure if I hadn’t argued with him so much, I wouldn’t have been beaten up at all.

Anyway, the chieftain had some excuses to make too. He brought up something a little out of the blue. “If I had to compare, you’re similar to the last chieftain. If it was for the tribe, he always went out of his way. Do you know what happened afterward?”
“Are you talking about the War of Sacred Relics?”
“Yes.”

The War of Sacred Relics was the name given to the war we fought with the elves ten years ago, a tragedy that had started when a barbarian picked up a holy relic belonging to the elven tribe in the labyrinth by coincidence. The elves arrested and interrogated the barbarian who took the relic, and the barbarian stubbornly resisted their methods and died.
“Before the royal family interceded, we fought against the elves for over a year. The previous chieftain also died in that battle.”

The War of Sacred Relics was the biggest reason behind the barbarian’s declining authority. Countless warriors who were supposed to lead the next generation had died. To add to that, the Magic Tower announced right after that barbarian hearts were valuable magical ingredients.
“We even met with the lord of the Tower, but they just asked why they should have to give up on magical ingredients for us.”
Wow, so they didn’t just sit back and take it.
“But we couldn’t wage a war against the Magic Tower.”
“So, like I said—”
“Yes, I’m sure things would have been better than they are now if I had taught the young warriors the dangers you spoke of.”
“What?”
When I flinched in surprise, the chieftain chuckled. “But you’re still young, warrior. What you’ve done was instill hatred toward humans in the young warriors.”
“They are plunderers, not human beings.”
“If you really believe that distinction can be made, then I pegged you wrong.”
“...But why can’t we hate humans?” I asked out of pure curiosity.
The chief paused for a moment, then answered. “Because if we hate them, we have nowhere to live.”
“You are afraid of the Rafdonian monarchy.” It was not that I didn’t understand. I knew very well how great the power of the royal family was.
However, the chieftain just muttered bitterly, almost to himself. “There is no living being in this world who is not afraid of him. If there comes a day that you meet him, you will understand.”
It was almost as if it wasn’t the army under the royal family that he was afraid of, but the king himself.
After that, he cut the conversation short.
“I’ll forgive you for teaching the warriors about plunderers. But if you go any further, I won’t sit idly by. Do not let the warriors harbor a deep hatred toward humans.”

He hadn’t chosen me as his successor, but he acknowledged my ambition and would tolerate it even if I increased my influence within the tribe. I had received a warning to stay in my lane, but this was a boon I would not have been given if I had admitted my mistakes or made excuses.
“If you want my position, become stronger, warrior. And prove you are worthy. I will watch over you. Oh, and one more thing. Your fist is quite strong.”

Look who was talking. With that parting compliment from the chieftain, I left the tent. The sun was setting beyond the castle walls, and the area around the tents was filled with barbarians. Everyone was staring at me, from the baby barbarians to even the elders, who must have been fairly good fighters in their youth.
“You’re all right.”
“I heard the chieftain has a bloody nose...”
“Then does that mean...?”

Upon seeing me return alive and well from the tent, they radiated deep curiosity. I merely adjusted my backpack and walked through them. They watched but did not approach me. Apparently, they thought I’d earned the chieftain’s ire.
A few steps later, Ainar came up to me. “Bjorn! Are you okay?! I heard you fought with the chieftain!”
“Ah, I am fine.”
“So what happened? I heard that you declared that you would become the tribe’s chieftain?”
The moment Ainar asked this straightforward question, about a hundred barbarians’ ears perked up at the same time. It would be impossible for me to just slip away from here.
So I smiled and replied. “He told me to get stronger and prove my worth.”

Immediately, a buzz filled the clearing. Some were surprised, and some said it would be impossible even for me. There were also those who had surprisingly realistic reactions and said that it would take several years. The chieftain probably thought the same way.
“And? Bjorn, what did you answer?”
At the time, I answered, “That it won’t take long.”
On the way back to the city with Ainar, we ran into Kharon. I drilled firmly into his head that he shouldn’t teach the baby barbarians to hate humans too much.
“B-But! Didn’t you say that humans are our enemies?”
“Not everyone is an enemy.” I was pretty much going against my own advice, but when I told him about Dwalkie, Kharon agreed.
“A noble man even among humans... Can I tell this story to the other warriors?”
“About Dwalkie?”
“It will be a very good example! We love warriors like him!”
“Didn’t you hear me? He was a wizard, not a warrior.”
“Haha! You say strange things. He fought to the death to protect your teammates. How is he not a warrior?”
Well, I had nothing to say to that. I just ended the argument and conversation there. “Then I’ll be going now.”
“Okay! See you next time, Bjorn, son of Yandel! The great warrior who will lead us in the future!”
Somehow, it felt like my title had gotten longer.
Still, I guess this worked out well.

I decided not to bother with the issue of robbing plunderers. The chieftain was only concerned about hatred for humans escalating—he told me that this was within the bounds of what was permissible. The killing and robbing of plunders would end in a few months, anyway. The reason why plunderers targeted barbarians so much was because it was low risk, high return.
If rumors start to spread that we’ve changed, none of those bastards will risk their lives.
If a goblin dropped millions of stones’ worth of materials, anyone would go crazy. But a rank-three monster doing the same? Any sane bastard would make a run for it.
Drag!
After leaving the holy land, I led Ainar to my inn, and after finishing a tearful meal on the first floor, I booked her a vacant room next to mine.
“C-Can I really sleep in a place like this...?”
“Of course. You don’t have to pay me back later. This much isn’t—”
“Bjorrrnnn! I will follow you for the rest of my life!”
“...Quiet. This is not the holy land.”
“Oh, right!”
While I was giving Ainar the heads up, my room, which should have been empty, opened from the inside. “...Bjorrrn? Who is that woman with you?”
“Oh, you’re here?”

Since Ainar was a party member who would be joining us in the future, I gave Missha a brief introduction. But since I had mentioned each of them to the other several times in the past, there was no need for long explanations.

“Nice to meet you, Missha Karlstein! I’ve heard a lot about you! Any teammate of Bjorn’s is a teammate of mine! I hope we work well together!” Ainar seemed nervous about meeting Missha for the first time. She practically screamed each word as she held out her hand.

Missha was just as bewildered. “Oh, um... Nice to meet you...” She shook hands with Ainar almost like she was possessed and approached me once she came to her senses. Then she whispered in my ear. “Th-this is the Ainar you mentioned? You said she was a barrrbarian!”
“And?”
“How is she a barbarian?!”

Wasn’t it clear she was a barbarian? I didn’t understand her reaction at first, but then when I thought about it again, I understood her surprise. Most people imagined barbarians as at least six feet tall.
The problem was, Ainar had heard this too. “Missha Karlstein! A-Are you insulting me for being short?! I sincerely thought of you as a precious teammate...!”
“Ahh! No. You heard wrrrong!”
“I have good ears!”
“S-sorry! Th-that’s not what I meant. Hm? It’s just that you’re so prrretty... yeah! That’s why I—”
“Whaaat?! Missha Karlstein, how much more will you insult me? A duel! I demand a duel!”
Ainar started shouting as soon as her trauma button was pressed and Missha tried to calm her down. Watching this gave me a powerful headache.
“Ugh... my head...”

It was clear my head hadn’t totally healed yet from being clocked by the chieftain. Yeah, that had to be it. After all, all five members of the party hadn’t even gathered yet. There was no reason for me to already see a rocky road ahead.

chapters.title: Chapter 155: Male Lion (1)
paragraphs: I was drinking something similar to green tea at a tea shop near the administrative office.

The people accompanying me were some rank-seven officials from the administrative office: Shavin and her best friend, Ragna. This was not our first meeting. After becoming acquainted with the sewage commission, we had met a few times under Shavin’s decree to have a tea or a meal. In terms of frequency, this happened about once a month.
“Oh! Share these with your teammates when you get back later. They are sold at a new cookie shop near our office, and are very popular these days.”
“...I will. Thanks for this.”
Most of our conversations were about trivial things, but the reason I kept coming to these gatherings was simple. Sometimes, there was useful information.
“Oh, right! Did I already tell you about this? I think the system that charges mana stone exchange fees according to seniority is going away.”
“How certain of that are you?”
“Our chief sees the law as pretty much passed already.”
Goddamn it. For an adventurer with less than a year of experience, this was no different from a bombshell. “When do you think it will be implemented?”
“Well, maybe next year at the earliest, or the year after that at the latest?”
“That’s fortunate, at least, I guess.”

As always, after exchanging useful information, the conversation turned to the usual stuff. And around the time I started to get bored, Shavin would spit out another useful tidbit. By our second gathering, I realized this wasn’t a coincidence.
It’s like I’m being trained or something.
Shavin definitely knew that without bait like this, I would have no reason to participate in these boring gatherings.
She must be doing all this for this kid.
“And you? Ragna? Anything happening with you?”

I didn’t realize this at first, but the librarian, Ragna Litaniel Peprok, had the social skills of a rock. Was that why Shavin wanted me to be good friends with her? Did she think she was her mother or something?
“No, nothing.”
“Is that so? Anything you want to say to Mr. Yandel? You’ve been so quiet since earlier.”
“Something I want to say... There might be something, actually.”
“Oh, yeah? Then let it out. You two are already friends, right?”
Shavin glanced at me, and I let out a silent sigh and nodded. “Yes, we are friends.”

It was a friendship that had been ratified with a handshake during our first gathering. Honestly, I didn’t know how meaningful that could possibly be but, what could I do? Working at the administrative office, Shavin had a lot of information that could benefit me. Not only that, but she also commissioned me for sweet, non-sewage jobs, so all I could do was flop around like a caught fish in her net.

“Friends...” Did my words give her courage? Ragna, who had been sitting in silence throughout the conversation, stared at me with an expressionless look as usual and then spoke in an almost scolding tone. “B-Bjorn Yandel. You shouldn’t stay away from books.”
“Oh, I’ve been busy these days.” That was true. I hadn’t had a day of proper rest since coming out of the labyrinth.
“Then... are you coming tomorrow?”
“If today’s work goes smoothly.”

I still had the Dragon Slayer’s sword, but I couldn’t really do anything about that until Krovitz got me a meeting. So, once I finished recruiting a wizard, I would be able to take it easy for a while.

“Ragna Litaniel Peprok.” In that spirit, it was time to get down to brass tacks. It would not be an exaggeration to say that this was the reason that I had participated in this gathering even though I was busy.
“If you have something to say, say it. Go ahead. We’re f-friends, right?”
“Of course!” When Ragna used the word “friend” first, Shavin smiled happily and agreed.
Okay, that should be enough groundwork. “Are you interested in becoming an adventurer?”
“...This is the same proposal you made back then.”
“Yes.” I’d made the same offer before, but the situation was a little different than it used to be. Our party had become much more diverse, and we were now friends.
As I waited for Ragna’s answer, Shavin let out a shriek. “N-No! What are you talking about!?” I hadn’t expected this. “Ragna? You’ll refuse, right? Of course you will. You know how the labyrinth is!”

This had been a mistake. I thought that Shavin would help me out and tell Ragna that being an adventurer was also a social experience since it seemed she was friends with several adventurers. I had misjudged, thinking she would be less resistant to adventuring. That was why I had brought it up while the three of us were together in the first place. I never thought she would be the one to spoil my plan.
“...Shavin, don’t be so scared. I’m not going anywhere.” Ragna gently grabbed Shavin’s hand. Only then did Shavin regain her wits and sit down again, looking embarrassed.
That left a bitter taste in my mouth. “So you’re rejecting my offer.”
“Yes. I like the library job.”

She liked being a librarian, huh? To believe that, I’d need to ignore a clear memory of her looking into the distance and saying, “Who would be interested in this place?” It would be more prudent to accept that she couldn’t leave for some reason.
Recruiting her was a failure.
I was a bit disappointed. After meeting with them a few times, I learned that her wizard ranking was very high. She was at least rank five, but also young and had room for future growth.
Well, the fact that a kid like this is working as a librarian means there’s some sort of backstory there.

I let go of my disappointment. She would have been a great recruit, but there was nothing I could do right now. At our current level of acquaintance, even if I asked her what her story was, I didn’t think she’d tell me so easily.
Shavin, now back to normal, asked, “Uh, but isn’t there already a wizard on your team, Mr. Yandel? The administrative wizard...”
“He is dead,” I answered.
That was the end of today’s gathering.
After the meeting, I headed to the Magic Tower. It was my first visit in about two months. Wow, so it had already been that long since our research agreement ended.
“Huh? Mr. Yandel?”
“Long time no see. Can I come in?”
“Well, sure.”
Raven’s personal laboratory had remained unchanged since then. Documents piled up like mountains and magic materials were scattered everywhere. I wished she would clean up a bit.

“Don’t put that down just anywhere—give it to me. I need to remember where I put it.” Mmm, or was this a system that didn’t need cleaning up because she remembered everything? Maybe there was more of a method to this madness than there seemed to be. “So,” Raven said sharply once I handed over the document that had been sitting on top of my chair, “what’s happened? You haven’t visited in two months.”

She used to at least bring me some water in a flask when I visited. Did we not even have a business relationship anymore? Well, I welcomed the opportunity to get straight to the point. No matter how much I flattered her or led up to it, that wouldn’t change this woman’s decision. If it wouldn’t affect the outcome of this conversation, I might as well save time.
“I have a suggestion for you.”
“Tell me.”
“There’s a vacancy for a wizard on my new team.”

“In other words, this is another recruitment offer.” Raven laughed. Her attitude was completely different from the last time I asked, when her expression had gone flat the moment the words left my mouth. Well, that had been back before I earned the nickname of Little Balkan. “Mr. Yandel, do you remember what I told you back then?”
“You said it would be nice if all the members of the party were above rank six and there was a priest.”
“And? How did that go?”
I gave truthful introductions for each of the members, starting with the fact that there was no priest and that Missha was a rank-seven melee damage dealer.
“Hmm, rank seven?”
“She’ll be promoted to rank six within the month, so don’t worry about that.”
Noticing her skepticism, I recited Missha’s essences and their ranks, and Raven’s expression relaxed. “If you say so.”
Next was Ainar. Since we had cleared the Bloody Citadel together, there was no need for a long explanation of who she was.
“You made that offer so confidently, yet she’s rank nine? No, more importantly, why is she still rank nine? She consumed an essence of a Bone Knight back then.”
“She’s in the same boat as Missha. There was no time to apply for a promotion.”

This wasn’t an excuse, but the truth. Right around now, those two, who had had an epic battle yesterday, would be at the Adventurers’ Guild applying for a promotion. Ainar would receive at least a rank-seven evaluation. She currently had one rank-seven essence and a whopping rank-four essence.
“She inherited a rank-four essence? Well, that changes things.”
“Her evaluation might end up being rank seven, but it’s safe to say that she’s rank six. I fought her and judged that for myself, so there is no need to doubt it.”
“I can see that for myself. And the last person?”
“Abman Urikfried, a rank-five adventurer from the Black Bear tribe. He uses a large crossbow as a weapon.”
When I told her about his tank summoned beast, Raven’s expression changed. “That’s enough for him to be welcome anywhere. Why did he join your team?”
“We’ve met before. He said that I at least won’t stab a teammate in the back.”
“Well... You are trustworthy in that sense.” Surprisingly, Raven readily accepted that and moved on. But after hearing the party composition, she seemed to have her doubts. “What about a scout?”

The long-awaited question had come. Because people interpreted information differently depending on how it was presented, I brought it up as if I had just remembered it. “Oh, I didn’t tell you. Urikfried is a scout.”
“...Is that true?”
“Do I need to make an oath for you to believe me?”
“No, but...”
I chuckled, straightened my shoulders confidently, and threw away the remorse that was starting to squirm to life in my conscience.
Well, I didn’t lie, did I?

Mr. Bear was a scout. It was just that he was bad with directions. Anyway, after revealing Mr. Bear’s ability, the rest was a breeze. Raven just pretended to think it over since her pride was on the line.

“It will be a good opportunity for you too. Don’t you always say you don’t have enough money? For now, our goal is to get to the sixth floor, so there won’t be a shortage of money once we start exploring in earnest.”
“Hmm.”
“And as you can see from our party’s composition, it can’t be just any wizard. We need a skilled mage like you.”
“Hmm?”
“Oh, and one more thing. Since we have a scout, we might enter Rifts or discover hidden areas of the labyrinth on several occasions. A wizard like you should know the value of that, right?”

“Hmmmm.” When I came at her more convincingly, Raven let go of her pride and nodded. “Alright. Since you’re so determined.” I sort of expected this, because she hadn’t immediately rejected the offer when I made it. If she didn’t already have exploration in mind, she wouldn’t have even heard me out. “But, I have one condition.”
“...Speak.”
“Exploring will always be my second priority. The first will be my research.”
“Speak plainly.”
“If I have a topic to research, I may take a break for a month or two, or even leave the party altogether. I hope you can understand that.”

I was secretly nervous, but her demand wasn’t an unreasonable one. It wasn’t like we were an official clan. Sudden vacancies were common in this industry, especially for a lofty wizard. Yeah, this wasn’t bad at all.
“Fine. But tell me in advance. If you’re going to leave for good, I’ll have to find a new wizard. We can use mercenaries for month-long absences, though.”
“Okay. That’s it, then.”
That was how the last member of our party was decided: Arua Raven, a rank-six, conventional wizard under the Altemion school.
“I guess we’re really colleagues now.”
“I’m counting on you.”
Recruitment success.

After that, we chatted for a bit. The foundation for our party had been laid down, but the party itself was not yet ready. “We’re all going to gather together to register the party at the guild and talk about loot distribution. When would be a good time?”
It was common for parties to collapse during the initial meeting stage, so I wanted to have a meeting as early as possible. Time was running out to find new members if we needed to.

Unfortunately, our meeting was immediately delayed by over a week. “My thesis on the vampire guardian is in its final stages. Next week, everything including being published in the academy will be over, so maybe we can gather around that time.”

I decided to look on the bright side. If the research had been scheduled to end next month, she wouldn’t have even thought to listen to my proposal. The timing was good in many ways. With her specs, she could actually find a better team than us.
“Then let’s meet on the 17th. I’ll discuss the location and time with the rest of the party and send you a letter.”
“I would appreciate that.”
After that, I left the Magic Tower and met with Missha and Mr. Bear individually. After deciding on a place and time, I went back to my inn and rested.
The next day, I visited the library, and after that, my daily life continued without any incidents.
“Whoa! I have never seen such a huge mace!”
I sparred with Ainar and practiced True Giantization mode.
“You’re buying me this even after you bought me cotton candy? Bjorn, are you some kind of shaman’s pot?”
“I’m not buying it for you, it’s an invest—No, a loan. When you earn money later, you have to pay it back.”
With Missha, we visited Kommelby as a trio to upgrade Ainar’s equipment. Missha moved into the room next door, which happened to coincidentally be vacant.
“What about your original accommodations?” I asked. “There aren’t many inns that let you cook.”
“It’s fine. I’m going to buy everything now. She steals all my food anyway!”
We visited Mr. Bear’s shop, and almost got him killed after Missha ran her mouth.
“Honey, have you been lying to me and entering the labyrinth on your own this whole time!?”
“D-Dear? I-I’m sorry. Don’t kill me...! Think of the baby!”
Peaceful days passed just like that.
With just one minute left until midnight on the 15th, I lay comfortably on the bed.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
That time had come once again.

chapters.title: Chapter 156: Male Lion (2)
paragraphs: A community of evil spirits, Ghost Busters, was a source of information I had that Missha and Ainar did not know about.
Okay, let’s do it.
Forcing my eyes away from Hansu Lee’s plush-looking bed, I turned on the computer first. This community was only active for twelve hours. There were things I needed to learn in that time.
Orcules, Noark, Dragon Slayer.

In the past, this had just been rumors of a distant land, but now it was closely related to my survival. Library books had their limits. The medium of books itself could be slow when it came to providing up-to-date information.
[1-140,000 GP] All information related to Orcules.
First, I put up a post seeking information and decided to join a chat room. I figured that this might be more helpful than the Exchange.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 1 person is online.]

Baekho seemed to have entered his chat room as soon as the community opened. True, he had been really sad when he logged out last time. He even seemed worried that I might not come back, like a child who didn’t want to be separated from his parents.
Whew, still, he’s not a kid you can easily meet up with.

It left something of a bitter taste in my mouth. He was a symbol of misfortune brought here on the day of his discharge from the military, and a veteran who had survived in this world for nearly ten years. Baekho viewed me in a very good light, but... I couldn’t fully trust him. He told me last time that he was in hiding. Warning me that he wasn’t up to date with current events, he introduced me to the Watchers of the Round Table. I had let it slide then, but I couldn’t rule out the possibility that he could be a member of Orcules or the underground city of Noark.
Whether we’re both Korean or not, here, we’re just strangers who don’t even know each other’s faces or names.

Soon, I got my thoughts in order. Maintaining a relationship with Baekho had more positives than negatives. So, while I dug into his true identity, I should try to feel out some information about Orcules without overdoing it.
“Brooo!”
The moment I double-clicked the mouse, I was once again in a large room reminiscent of an aristocratic mansion. Before I could get a proper look around, Baekho ran toward me.
“Bro! What took you so long!?”
“I came here straight away...”
“Do you know how anxious I was that you might be dead!?”

This seemed to be the truth because his eyes were sharp and his hair messy, as if he’d been tugging at it. It hadn’t even been five minutes since the community opened and this was his reaction? How starved for affection was he?
“Brother, you can’t die yet! We haven’t even talked about K-pop singers yet, or cussed out politicians and the military. I can only do that with you! We have to talk about Dungeon Fighter, too!”

Oh... So that was the problem. Well, expecting a normal person’s sensibilities from a guy who’d survived this place for ten years would be laughable. I smiled and sat down in the chair. “Stop it. I’m not going to die.”
“Okay. Then what should we talk about first? Oh, Lovel Lovel’s third full album? That would be best, right?”

Wait, who the heck was Lovel Lovel? Since I had no interest in the entertainment industry, I smoothly changed the subject. I had a feeling that if I confessed to not knowing them, he’d get irritated. “...Let’s talk about the military.”
“Absolutely! Huh? But now that I think about it, weren’t you in public service?”
“I still went to the training center, man.”

“Mm...” Perhaps talking about our trainee days wasn’t so appealing to him. A strange look appeared on Baekho’s face, and the next time he spoke, it was hesitant. “Bro, maybe we should just talk about Dungeon Fighter.”
“I haven’t tried that.”

“What?! Didn’t you say you were in public service?!” Baekho screeched like he was shocked. He came back to his senses a beat later. “Ahhh! I’m sorry, bro. I didn’t mean anything by that. You know that, right?”
“Yeah... let’s just go with that.”
“Okay...”

The air between us instantly grew awkward. Baekho scratched his cheek, looking somewhat dispirited. It was not that I couldn’t understand his thought process. He was so happy to meet a fellow Korean, but was now realizing that we didn’t really have much in common.
“Pffft! Hehehe...”
“Why are you laughing?”
“No, bro. Isn’t it funny, though? The conversation we just had.”
Was it? I wasn’t sure exactly which part was so amusing.
“I can’t really explain it, but for some reason I felt like I was just back in Korea.”
Oh, that. “...I think I know what you mean. And roughly what it feels like.”
“Right?” Baekho chuckled and leaned back in his chair.
Rather than trying to force a topic, we let the conversation flow naturally. Starting from our original jobs, we exchanged stories and somehow ended up talking about the military.
“The training center was so funny. I didn’t know there were so many wackos in our country.”
“I guess it’s just the environment. And then everyone returns to normal outside.”
“Well... that’s true. We never knew we’d end up here, either. Once we get back, we’ll probably have to go to a mental institution.”
“I think it would be best not to talk about that.”

“No. Haven’t you thought about it? Killing people if they get in the way, killing them if they’re suspicious, wondering whether every person we meet is going to harm us or not. Human life... just feels like a game here. We’re madmen.”
As if the humorous atmosphere from earlier had never existed, the air grew heavy.
“You’ll adapt quickly. Just like when you got here.”
“...You think so?”
“Yeah.”

A moment of silence passed after that. Baekho was the first to speak. “Anyway, that’s why I’m grateful to you. To be honest, these days I’ve started to wonder whether I really need to head back or not. Not that I like it here, but... You know what I mean?”
“Yeah.”
“You might think it’s no big deal, but it motivates me, at least. Laughing here gives me faith that I’ll be able to do it when I get back too.”

Faith, huh? I got the strange sense that that word was out of place, but I didn’t examine the feeling too closely. I wasn’t sure of anything yet, and I decided that there was nothing to gain by looking into it.

“Oh, by the way, do you know about Orcules?” I brought up the main topic on my agenda in a nonchalant tone as if I was just mentioning it to put an end to the tension. After I threw out that question, I focused on examining Baekho’s expression for any changes.

There were none. “Orcules? Why do you want to know?” Baekho asked the reason first. Until now, he had answered everything easily no matter what I asked. That created more questions. Who was this guy, really?
“You know how you need a Genesis Treasure to get to the last floor? I was wondering if they stole it. Oh, you know about the theft, right?” I recited the lines I had prepared without pause.
Baekho nodded. “Yes. I do. So that’s why you asked... I’m relieved.”
“Relieved?”
“Oh, it’s nothing.” Baekho glossed over that and continued. “Anyway, you managed to think that far ahead too, then. I actually used to think the same.”
“You mean you don’t anymore?”
“Yes. I’ve done some research, but that doesn’t seem to be the case. Makes sense, since the Genesis Treasures were all stolen half a year ago.”
“All of them?”
“Oh, you didn’t know that. All six races were robbed. On the same day too.”
Huh, the elder had said that the other races might be in a similar situation. He had been right.

“Realistically, though, it makes no sense. I don’t know about the other races, but how could Orcules steal from the dragon people? No matter how skilled the thief, it’s not possible. Well, I tried to investigate just in case, but I couldn’t find any clues.”
“So you don’t know who stole them?”
“No. If you learn anything, let me know too. Since there’s no other way to get back home without one.”

I asked the question because I was curious about Orcules, but I had learned something unexpected instead. This guy knew nothing about the Genesis Treasures, either. I had even had some momentary delusions that he might be the final boss.
“Bro, you’re not having weird thoughts, are you? Like that we have to compete or whatever. You can open the door with up to five people, anyway. I can help.”

“No, it’s not that...” Because I couldn’t tell him what I was thinking to his face, I brushed it aside. “It’s just that it’s a little weird for you to say that to me. How can I find clues that you couldn’t even find?”
“Uh, I don’t really have much to say to that... But for some reason, I have a feeling that you’re special. Actually, I’ve had that thought since I first saw you.”
“That leaves me with nothing to say...”
“Come on, didn’t you say you beat the game at Times Ten? In ten years, you’ll be like me. Realistically, I have no more areas to improve.”

Apart from saying that he had no more room to become any stronger, Baekho’s resolve shone through in those casual words. This guy really thought it’d take another ten years to find the Genesis Treasures, but he still wasn’t giving up. How did someone become so tenacious?
“Oh, right. Wanna hear something interesting? I’m sure you don’t know this, either. It’s a setting that didn’t exist in the game.”
“What is it?”
“There is a huge underground city under the sewers called Noark.”
“...Noark?” I tried my best to keep my composure. I hadn’t dared to bring it up, but I had wanted to. To think he would mention it first.
“Yes. Talking about Orcules reminded me of it. That’s actually their home base. You know the Ormi Revolutionary Corps, right?”
I laughed at the slightly unexpected name. “Those guys that appear sometimes as special events. They approach you to ask you to start a revolution with them as soon as you get some fame.”

Accepting the event always resulted in your character ending up dead. I had tried countless times to see if there was a hidden condition to get around that, but there was nothing I could change because the problem lay in the structure of the game itself.
“Noark was created by those bastards. Their rebellion failed and they fled underground.”
“That’s interesting. And then?”
“That’s it. They have similar goals, right? That’s why they’re partnering together.”

The existence of an alliance between Noark and Orcules was something I had discovered from the letter left behind by High Priest Ludwig. In other words, everything from now on was important. Was there a way for me to ask for information about the Dragon Slayer without being suspicious?
“Bro, I’m just telling you this just in case, but if a commission related to this comes down from the palace or guild, don’t even go near it.”
“I think I need to hear the reason behind that first.”

“Ah, that makes it a long story...” Baekho sighed but quickly continued. “There’s this bastard called the Dragon Slayer who did something really stupid recently. He kidnapped a High Priest but lost him. Apparently, someone picked up his letter and brought it to the temple or something.”
I gulped. “But how?”
“I don’t know the details. I heard that he lost his memory and doesn’t know what happened to him.”
Lost his memory? Could that have something to do with the vine that fell off? I wanted to ask for more details, but Baekho steamrolled forward and didn’t give me a chance to.

“Anyway, what I wanted to say is their alliance has broken up, so they might end up getting taken over by Rafdonia. So don’t ever participate. They’re not doing so well down there. Getting caught up in it will only get you hurt. Okay? Dang it, time’s up already. Bro! See you next—” A moment later, Baekho’s voice cut off and he disappeared without a trace.
“Goddamn it.”
In other words, he had bounced because his time was up.
After Baekho disappeared, I returned to my room and took a moment to get my thoughts in order. To be precise, I mulled over one particular sentence he said again and again.
“I don’t know the details. I heard he lost his memory and doesn’t know what happened to him.”

Considering the pill that deranged bitch fed me, this was a very plausible turn of events. The problem was, I didn’t know if that was true. It was possible that Baekho had heard rumors created by Orcules itself and passed them on to me. But if it was true...
It makes sense that the vine broke.
To some extent, the logic was sound. This ring did not actually stop ill-fated meetings with the bastard—it only postponed them.
After all, it’s only a matter of time before I get caught.

If he looked into who had delivered the letter, he’d find out about me someday. There was also the issue of disposing of the sword called Dragon Slayer. And even setting that aside, the possibility that Noark had a way of restoring memories was also on the table.
My job will remain the same.

I sat down at my computer again and did what I had to do. I checked for posts selling information and, when there were any, met up with the users to purchase it at a reasonable price. Assuming that anyone could become my enemy, I gathered more and more information, not just about the Dragon Slayer.

Eventually, it was 3:09 a.m., just about time for the Watchers of the Round Table to open. I deliberately waited until there was only one minute left to enter the chat room. The beauty of performing a character lay in the details.
Creak!
When I put on the lion mask that was on the table, the closed door opened. A red carpet led up to the Round Table’s room. As I moved slowly, I could hear the sound of conversation in the distance.
“That man, is he not coming this time?”
“That wouldn’t be strange. Someone like him has no need for us.”
“Who the hell is he that you guys are acting like this?”
There was a new voice in their midst. It seemed to be a member who hadn’t attended the last time.
“It’s hard to explain.”
“He’s kooky. So if you ever meet him, watch what you say. Otherwise, you will have a very hard time.”

In response to their senior’s experienced advice, the newbie said, “Ha, I really don’t understand. You’re all making messing with me, right? Physical strength doesn’t work here, and he can’t even learn our identities, so what are you so afraid of?”
“Psh. There’s one thing: murderous intent.”
“What... No matter how strong he is, we’re strong enough to defend against it,” the newbie muttered incredulously.
I kept walking and made my presence known.
Step.
At the sound of loud footsteps, the members seated at the Round Table turned their heads in unison. I quietly passed behind them and sat down in the seat I had used last time.
“Long time no see, Mr. Lion.”
Except for Clown, they all looked at me silently.
Apparently, this vibe was not to their liking, because the newbie acted like a newbie and laughed awkwardly. “Oh, um... I-I guess there really is a newcomer. Haha.”

I quietly stared at the newbie and released the murderous intent I had put so much effort into practicing. If there was a newbie, it was important to cut them off at the pass. Wasn’t that tradition here?

chapters.title: Chapter 157: Male Lion (3)
paragraphs: The newbie was wearing a goblin mask. Strictly speaking, I was the newbie here and this person was a returning user, but... Sorry. Since it had been a while, they needed to be caught up on what had changed, right? Or they needed to listen carefully to the patch notes from their seniors.
“S-Stop...”
When Goblin spoke with obvious difficulty, I immediately dropped my murderous intent. However, if I left off here, I’d just be branded as a temperamental asshole.
“That’s it?”

I decided on today’s lines by recalling my parting words from last time. When putting on an act, the important thing was consistency. “I heard there was a newcomer inside, but...” I muttered with disappointment, as if I’d had certain expectations but everything had gone predictably. As if to imply that this hadn’t just been bullying, but me trying to learn what level this person was at. “How boring.”

Like that was my only goal, I took my eyes off of Goblin and scanned Fox, as well as Crescent Moon and Deer, to show them that I would be very disappointed if this meeting failed to entertain me like last time’s.
“Keke, don’t worry, Lion, I have something that will interest you again.”
I didn’t even answer, just sat there with my chin on my hand.
If Clown is saying that, then it must be really important information.
Was this why people pushed around their subordinates? I kept pretending to be indifferent.
Rattle.
When the time came, the door to the Round Table closed. This meant that no more members would be joining. However, there was one thing to deal with before the meeting began in earnest.
“Goblin, snap out of it.”
“How funny. They’ve always pretended to be so great.”
“Keke, but unlike last time, Mr. Lion was being considerate! Ha! I’m starting to get embarrassed for you.” At Clown’s words, Fox and Deer laughed in agreement.
“This is definitely... not like back then.”
“Yeah. I was even able to endure it this time too.”
As the two of them glanced at me as if to thank me for being considerate this time around, I flinched inwardly. The reason for that was simple.
That was my maximum output...

This was the maximum amount of murderous intent that I could turn on and off freely. I had practiced countless times after watching the head of the Karlstein family use it in real life, but it turned out that when I used it seriously, I couldn’t turn it off at will. Well, it was good that they had interpreted this as me being considerate. This was why people should try to at least seem powerful.
“S-Sorry. I’m fine now.” Anyway, Goblin also came to their senses. Although as soon as our eyes met, they turned away, apparently traumatized by what had just happened.
This one definitely seems inferior to the other four.
Just look at Fox—she had taken my true murderous intent for a lot longer but was just cautious and wary of me, not afraid.
“So, who should start?” Fox asked, glancing at Clown.
Clown just shrugged. “You should enjoy the best delicacies at the end, right? How about starting with Mr. Goblin?”

“Ahem, why not.” Soon, Goblin cleared their throat and relayed their information as if to make up for their unseemly behavior earlier. “Everyone already knows that Ludwig, the High Priest of the Stars, was missing.”
“And?”
“The culprit was Orcules. They kidnapped him and used him like a slave.”
Was this prick a priest? Was that how they knew? The thought occurred to me, but the light emitted by the jewel on the Round Table was red.
“Keke, I guess more than half of us know that already.”
This left a bitter taste in my mouth. It hadn’t even been two weeks since I brought the letter to the temple. Everyone who knew, including Baekho, must already know about me...
“You’d better get used to it. If you want to satisfy those two, ordinary information won’t cut it,” said Fox.
Huh?
“I didn’t know about this. Perhaps this will cause the temple to offer their support to the palace.” From what Crescent Moon was saying, it seemed the two weren’t aware of this information.
So the red light came on because Clown, Deer, and I knew about this?
I clicked my tongue unwittingly. Had these two been watching me this whole time?
Clown jumped to his feet and freaked out at the other three. “Hey, do the unspoken rules mean nothing? I thought we decided not to openly reveal whether we knew the information or not.”
“Sorry. I just felt bad for Goblin.”
“We looked past it when it was just us. But there’s a newcomer, right? So let’s all be careful. Okay?”
“O-Okay.”

Oh, so that was the original rule. It made sense—if things kept proceeding in this way, the people who did and didn’t know certain information would inevitably be revealed. That was something that had been bothering me, but thanks to Clown, it was sorted out.
But for some reason, I don’t think he spoke out because of me...
Something like this had happened at the last meeting too.
“Crescent, don’t be too discouraged. Most wouldn’t know the information you just shared.”
And back then, Clown had been the first to say it.
Did he determine that that last bit of information could be used to infer his identity?
I wasn’t certain, but it seemed possible.
However, if that assumption is true, Clown is either a priest or a member of the underground city. It must be one of the two.
The latter seemed more likely. I couldn’t imagine Clown working in a temple. Well, it was possible that he was putting on an act like me.
That’s not important right now.

Soon, I returned my attention to the meeting and listened to the next bit of information Goblin revealed. Perhaps it was a shock that the previous information gave off a red light. “The Goddess of the Stars has given a blessing.”
At the next announcement, a green light came on right away. Was this something that even Clown didn’t know about?
“I want to buy information on who the blessing was given to,” said Clown.
“I’m not sure...”
“Keke, information even a paladin doesn’t know? I guess the temple is really keeping it hidden?”
“You said you wouldn’t talk about things like that!”

“Oh, my bad. But this is something everyone knows already. Why are you being so sensitive?” At that, Goblin glanced at me, and Clown laughed like they were being ridiculous. “Do you think he cares about you?”
Goblin huffed in displeasure but didn’t argue. I impassively made a mental note.
Goblin Mask = Paladin.
In any case, the meeting continued. After Goblin was Fox beside them. “There will be a double-digit Numbers Item at the Sky Auction House next month.”

A double-digit. In other words, a numbered item between eleven and ninety-nine would be put up for auction. But I wondered if the clown’s warning to keep to the rules had been effective. No one spoke after that, but the air grew heavy like everyone was sizing up their competition.
Whew, I need to reach the Sky Auction House too.

The Sky Auction House was located in Karnon, the royal capital. To enter Karnon, I needed to gain more fame or raise my adventurer ranking and accumulate accomplishments. That would take at least a year.
I don’t even have the money to buy a double-digit Numbers Item. I’ll have to pass on this one.

I neatly tucked that thought away. Not only did I not know what kind of item it was, but even if I had the money, it would be better to use it on Garphas’ Necklace, which I got at the count’s banquet.

“The royal family is coming up with a plan to conquer Noark.” After Fox, Deer offered up some information, and a green light appeared. So Baekho had been right about the conquest. As advised, I planned not to go anywhere near that.
Next came Crescent Moon. “Equipment allegedly owned by the Dragon Slayer, a member of Orcules, was put on the black market. Even though it wasn’t his sword, it’s clear he has run into misfortune.”

The green light came on once again. I barely managed to keep my composure as I continued to rest my chin in my hands. His stuff was on the black market? But I only stole the sword. I was taken aback at first, but I quickly pieced things together in my head.
It would be correct to assume that what Baekho said was true.

The Dragon Slayer had lost his memory, probably thanks to the same drug that woman had used on me back then. The person who had collected the remaining equipment and sold it on the black market would have been the same one who fed him the drug.
Since we were going clockwise from Goblin, it was finally Clown’s turn next. Everyone’s eyes were full of high expectations after the tone he set earlier. “Hmm, Lion, would you like to go first?”
“You must be pretty confident.”
“Of course. If we only say boring things that we all know here, Mr. Lion might not come back next time.”
I chuckled and nodded, signaling that I had no intention of going along with his games, so we should go in order.

“Well, that leaves me with no choice. Mr. Lion’s information could be more interesting!” Clown shrugged flippantly. Then, bending his body to a bizarre extent, he stretched and announced in a playful tone, “Within the next three years, a spell capable of binding up to six people will be created.”
These words were followed by silence. Everyone shifted their gaze to the center of the round table.
“It’s a green light...”
That meant that Clown’s words were true. Or at least, he believed they were.
“Holy... I didn’t know that was possible.”
“The guild, the royal family, the clans... everything will change.”

Despite the tacit rule the clown had mentioned earlier, everyone openly expressed their astonishment. That was to be expected. Not only would this widen the range of floors an adventurer could be active on and change basic team composition, but it was also the same as increasing someone’s chances of clearing the game by several times.
Six people will be able to enter the last floor?

Five and six were completely different. Whether it was Times Ten mode or Times One Hundred mode, this meant that combinations and strategies that had been impossible in the original game were now possible.

In the middle of all this, Clown stared only at me, like he didn’t care about the reactions of the others at all. “So, what do you think?” The eyes hidden beyond the small holes in his mask met mine. The emotions contained in them were very clear.
He’s like a child asking to be praised.
I chuckled and opened my mouth, though only to the point that it didn’t harm the character I was crafting. “This is rather interesting.”
One compliment sticker earned.

There was a saying that praise bred willingness. Well, getting whipped several hundred times would do the same, but in terms of efficiency, there was a huge gap. What truly made people passionate was the future. They desperately longed for rewards.
“Ahem. So, it’s your turn, Mr. Lion.” Clown, having received a gold star, awkwardly averted his eyes and changed the subject.
As if they had been waiting for this, all eyes turned to me. Thanks to the bomb Clown just dropped, everyone’s eyes were shining.
...What to choose?

In truth, I had already prepared some information to release here in advance, but the quality of the information offered had gone up too much. Perhaps thanks to the words I had parted with last time, it felt like everyone was pulling out all the stops today. The clown in particular had come with a clear goal in mind. Information about the six-person binding spell? I would never have gotten to hear about that if it hadn’t been for my mysterious act.
Whew, I mean, it’s a good thing, but...
It created more of a burden on me. What should I tell them? Of course, it wasn’t that I didn’t have information that would meet their sky-high expectations.
But if others know about these things, it will affect me too.

The problem was choosing information that was useless even if they knew it, like the Vamdemon. Besides, bringing up the labyrinth while everyone else was talking about the outside world would be kind of weird in terms of flow.
Hmm, that would be best.

Soon, after carefully weighing the consequences of releasing this information, I made a decision. “You were curious about the blessing earlier.” I looked at Clown as I spoke, implying I was giving him a reward for being the one to entertain me.
“I don’t want to reveal the reason—”
Clown misinterpreted my intentions, so I cut him off. “The blessing came with a holy relic.”
“Sorry?”
“A new holy relic has appeared in the world through a blessing from the Goddess of the Stars.”

Clown, who sat there dazed for a moment like he didn’t believe what he’d just heard, came to his senses. Peering at the jewel’s green light, he cautiously asked, “...Can we hear what kind of holy relic it is?” Unlike his usual playful tone, his voice was now cold and subdued.
So, the holy relic is what’s important to you. Not who received the blessing.
I laughed happily and answered, “If you bring me another interesting story.”

“Keke, still, I’m glad to hear you’ll be returning.” Clown laughed frivolously as usual, but I could sense it. The next time I came, I’d be able to hear more interesting information, although I couldn’t imagine what it would be.
“I’ll look forward to it.”
And when that time came, I would probably say this: No fun.

chapters.title: Chapter 158: Male Lion (4)
paragraphs: The reason I brought up the holy relic at the meeting was simple. Except for the part where it was closely related to me and concerned me, there were many advantages.
For now, it’ll help with my whole mysterious vibe.
Wasn’t it only proper, after Clown had established the right atmosphere? Rather than suddenly mentioning the labyrinth, this seemed like a better choice.
You were curious about this earlier, right? Here, let me tell you. Your reward.

If I framed it like that, I judged that the other members who were also anticipating what I had to say would have nothing to complain about. And indeed, my prediction was correct. Far from being disappointed, I could see at a glance that their expectations for me had climbed even higher.
“...Could it be that you also know where the Master is?”

I shrugged at Fox’s words, which said, If you bring me something interesting, there’s nothing I can’t tell you. Thankfully she understood, and Fox squeezed her small hands together in apparent determination as she made up her mind to hear that information.
I’ll tell them it’s no fun no matter what they bring me, though...
My pang ran through my conscience, but I quickly brushed it off. Wasn’t this just a business relationship conducted while wearing a mask, anyway? It only made sense to care solely about my own gain.
Still, I think that bit of motivation worked well.

This was the second advantage I had predicted. Structurally, the Watchers of the Round Table made it difficult to guarantee complete anonymity. Having information others didn’t know meant you somehow had to have access to that information.
Crescent Moon has talked about elves a lot, and Fox seemed more up-to-date with the latest information about people and events than the hidden elements of the labyrinth.

Of course, unlike Goblin (whose identity as a paladin had been exposed), the other masks seemed to stay in their lanes. But in order to bring me interesting information, they would have no choice but to reveal their cards. If I played this right, it would be of great help to me in inferring their identities.
I don’t know about the others, but I’m curious about Clown.

To that end, this was a good opportunity. I was sure they were curious about my identity as well. Since I would have no choice but to continue revealing information about the labyrinth, I couldn’t pass up an opportunity to look impressive. I didn’t know about the first few times, but if I continued like that, they might get suspicious that I was actually an amateur who just knew a lot about the game.
Anyway, here was the third advantage.
“I want to buy information on who the blessing was given to.”

Clown had already shown a strong interest in the blessing, and I decided that it was reasonable to use information like that which would come out anyway. Of course, I had no way of knowing how much he could find out on his own, since I didn’t know how tight-lipped the people at the temple were.
Rather, I can confirm that through him.

If this ended up being information Clown, who was considered high-level even in the Watchers of the Round Table, was unable to find out, then I could rest easy. That would mean that my secret was well kept. I was turning the gears while resting my chin on my hand.
“Now then, shall we do one more round?” The second round started under Fox’s prompting.

Goblin went first once again, but there were some hiccups from the start. After receiving a red light, they just barely managed to receive the green light on their next attempt, but the members all objected.
“The saint’s real name? I’m sure that might be useful in some places, but...”
“You’re free-loading.”
“Maybe that would have been enough before, but it’s going to be difficult to let something like this slide now.”

In the end, Goblin had to bring out new, useful information that the other members approved of, and it moved to the next person after that bit of chaos was resolved. The information was temple-related, as expected.
The second Captain of the Paladins is the woman who was beside Krovitz during the blessing, right? To think that woman is gay.

This was more a scandalous piece of gossip than anything else, but surprisingly, the members did not object to its use. I could understand their general thought processes. They probably thought this was important information that, with proof, could give them an upper hand against the captain. Homosexuality was classified as a great sin in this world.
“Now, me next.” Fox revealed what the double-digit Numbers Item that would appear at the Sky Auction House was.
“You’re using the same information twice.” Deer expressed his dissatisfaction but did not go so far as to object. He must have known that the double-digit Numbers Item was worth that much.

The round continued like that, and secret information spilled from the members’ mouths. Deer told us information about palace politics, and Crescent Moon mentioned that the successor to the elves’ tribe committed a mortal sin and had been stripped of their title.

“Hmm, is it my turn now?” Clown, who had dropped the bomb of the six-person bonding spell last round, relaxed a little this time and spilled some normal information instead. Well, I guess it couldn’t really be called normal. “The masks we are wearing were not chosen at random.”
“What do you mean?”
“The Master said that when you first choose a mask, you choose the one that most closely resembles your destiny.”
That was a very interesting statement. It was a little too vague to be called useful, though.
“That’s why I treat Mr. Goblin as lesser. It means that despite his weakness, he is fated to be cunning.”
Goblin trembled in anger at being Clown’s no-fucks-given example. But I wondered if they did seem a bit pitiful.
“I don’t know about Goblin, but Clown, I can see why yours is like that since you’re such a douchebag,” Deer muttered caustically. Clown did not seem bothered by this and just laughed.
“But this doesn’t sound like very important information.”
“Yes. It’s a bit fascinating that the Master said that, but...”
“Bring forward something more useful.”

Clown clicked his tongue at the backlash. “Tsk. Even after I gave you clues about your fate... This is why they say not to give pearls to swine,” Clown grumbled, casting a quick glance at me. I once again didn’t answer, staying put. Silence would always get you halfway to wherever you wanted to go. “Then I suppose I should talk about something more on your level.”

Soon Clown pulled out new information. It was about the Adventurers’ Guild and this time it passed without objection. Then it was my turn again. I revealed one of the things I had picked out beforehand. It was advanced information, but so advanced that it was useless to have.
“The Stone of Revival exists.”
As soon as I finished speaking, everyone’s eyes focused on the Round Table. The moment the jewel at the center emitted a green light, silence fell.
“Um, what is the Stone of Revival...?” Goblin was the first to speak.
At their careful question, Fox answered, “It’s an item that can resurrect someone. Well, those are the rumors, at least.”

Even in the game, the Stone of Revival was only ever spoken of as a legend. That made sense. To consume it, you had to meet some crazy conditions that bordered on divine intervention. The first time I got my hands on it was pure coincidence, and I wasn’t able to obtain it again afterward even though I knew the conditions for acquiring it. There was no way these guys who had beaten the cheat version of the game could possibly know it actually existed.

“Th-then can you really bring the dead back to life with it?” Crescent Moon asked carefully. They couldn’t hide the excitement that dripped from their voice. Could it be that they had someone they wanted to save?

“Yes.” In exchange for hearing lots of useful information today, I threw in a little extra. “With the Stone of Revival, it is possible to resurrect the dead.” There were complicated requirements attached to it, but its effects were as rumored.
But was this not enough to satisfy them? “Then who has the item—”
“Enough.” I cut off Crescent Moon’s words coldly. If they wanted to hear more, they would have to bring me information worthy of it.
Crescent Moon soon came to their senses. “Then at least tell me what kind of information interests you. I need that item.”

Hmm, I didn’t expect that. I thought about it for a moment. An oddball in a male lion mask who was bored and tired of everything, and who attended these meetings looking for amusement... how would a guy like that answer here?
Before long, an appropriate line came to mind. “I don’t know what I’m interested in.”
