The lion didn’t even know. It was kind of a cringey character set-up, but aside from that it was a pretty good concept. If I framed things like this, not only would they bring me a wide range of useful information, but it would make it easier for me to dismiss whatever they told me as no fun.

“It won’t be easy to please someone like you.” Crescent Moon let out a long sigh. Their eyes were filled with the determination to find out, though. That pricked at my conscience, so I averted my eyes to stare out into space, my chin still propped up.
Did I look solemn like that? A moment of silence ensued, with no one speaking.
After, Fox assumed the role of moderator again and led the conversation, “Ahem! So, what do we do now? If everyone is okay with it, shall we do another round?”
Goblin raised their hand. “I’ll stop here. I have no more information that will satisfy you all.”

“I will stop too. I prepared several more just in case, but I’m not very confident considering the quality of the information today.” When Deer announced he was backing out like Goblin, the meeting naturally came to an end.
Ha, again?

However, everyone stayed put and quietly watched me. Come to think of it, the same thing happened at the last gathering. They all pretended not to be but were curious to hear what I had thought, I guess. Well, it probably hurt their pride a bit. Last time, I had shown my disappointment by asking, “That’s it?”
So what should I say this time?
After a moment’s consideration, I made a decision. I scanned the various masks one by one and smiled as if to say their efforts were at least praiseworthy. “I’ll look forward to the next one.”
Thanks for the information.
At the Round Table after Lion left, Goblin blurted out the question they had been holding back, sounding drained. “Who... the hell... is that man?”
Deer clicked his tongue. “Certainly not a regular person.”
Goblin let out a long sigh.
All I wanted was to infer his identity. Why am I always treated like this?
Soon, Goblin confessed what they were thinking. “...He might be someone from my side.”
“Keke, what do you mean, Goblin?”
“There are less than ten people in the church who know about the blessing. Each one is at least a high priest or a captain. If that man is one of them, that might explain—”

“Ha, is that what you mean?” Clown fired back irritably, abruptly cutting Goblin off. “This is why everyone looks down on you. Why are you thinking so small? That man is a cardinal? A captain? That’s the best you can think of?”
“But there’s no other explanation! It hasn’t been more than two weeks since the blessing was received...”
“Tsk, how pathetic. You don’t think there could be a spy among them?”

“That’s nonsense...” Goblin trailed off, finding the thought absurd. After all, they knew how faithful the temple’s dignitaries were. They were absolutely not people who would work for outsiders. But what was this? “Wait, do you all think that way?” Everyone except for Goblin was accepting this nonsense.
“There is no other explanation.”
“To be honest, I had thought he would be kind of an isolated hero. But that doesn’t seem to be the case, either...”
“Perhaps we have made a connection with a figure more powerful than we could ever have imagined.”

At this point, even Goblin started to have doubts. Could it be that that man’s influence had even reached the core of the church? Of course, they didn’t know anything for sure yet, so Goblin focused on the conversation that followed.
“Then let’s put our heads together for the remaining time. We may not be able to discover his identity, but we can deduce what kind of person he is, right?”
“Good idea. Maybe we can find out what he’s interested in.”
At Fox’s suggestion, they pooled their collective intelligence together to investigate. The goal was to find out the identity of the lion.
“I’ll go first. That man wasn’t even interested in the double-digit Numbers Item. That must mean he’s powerful enough to not be intrigued by an item like that.”
“The same goes for the plans for conquering Noark. He didn’t even flinch after hearing it. It’s clear he has eyes and ears on the palace.”
“Kekeke, I can’t be sure, but he’s probably killed at least thousands of people. He doesn’t even know what he’s interested in. Even I haven’t seen someone that broken.”
Each time they brought up their observations, they essentially participated in group brainwashing. The finishing stroke was Crescent Moon’s assumption. “Perhaps... he knows all of our identities.”
“What do you mean, Crescent?”
“When he first brought up the Stone of Revival, he was looking right at me. As if he already knew my story.”
Goblin unknowingly scoffed. Lion may have been extraordinary, but wasn’t that too much of a leap?
It seems more likely to be a coincidence... He was sitting right across from him.
Of course, Goblin did not say this out loud, because everyone was taking Crescent Moon’s words seriously.

“Hmm, I was wondering why he suddenly brought up the Stone of Revival, but that explains it.” Clown was completely convinced, and the others believed the possibility was worth considering. Gradually, Goblin also grew unsure. Hearing all of these smart people say the same thing, they started to think it might be true.
“Oh!” Just then, Fox clapped her hands and shouted. “Masks! We have masks.”
“Masks...?”
“Yes. Maybe we can get a sense of what kind of person he is based on his mask.”
“Hmm, if Clown’s words are true, there’s a possibility we might be able to figure out his personality.”
“A lion, huh?”
One by one, the members listed the things that came to mind when they thought of a male lion.
“Umm, when I think of lions, I remember the story that they drop their cubs off a cliff as soon as they’re born.”
“You mean the story that they only raise the survivors? Those are all just myths. Though, to become that strong, he must have gone through something worse than falling off a cliff.”
“Keke, nothing comes to mind other than the king of beasts. Could it mean that Mr. Lion will become king one day?”
“Hmm, he certainly didn’t look like someone who would work under anyone.”
“I heard lions are symbols of emperors in the East.”
“A symbol of an emperor! How exciting!”
Goblin just listened quietly as they spoke. A thought came to mind.
I’ve heard lions are polygamous... Maybe this just means he’s fated to have a lot of luck with women.
Of course, once again, this thought remained unspoken. They knew for a fact that if they said it out loud, the others would look at them like they were pathetic.

chapters.title: Chapter 159: Negotiation (1)
paragraphs: On the evening of the 17th, all the members of our newly formed party gathered. The meeting place was a three-story bar that had opened not too long ago. At first, we were going to meet at Mr. Bear’s tavern, but he very flatly refused.
“Hmm, our shop isn’t good for secretive conversations.”
“That’s okay. Instead of expedition plans, we’ll be talking about loot distribution—”
“Stop, there is a place I know. Let’s go there.”
Geez, I was just trying to help raise his profits. Was it the habit of a married man to refuse such things with disgust? I swear, this guy was an odd one.
“Am I the last one?” By the time Raven arrived, everyone was gathered.
“Don’t be sorry, sit down.”
“I came on time, why should I be sorry?”
Oh, that was true... but why was she being more snippy than usual? Ah, was she trying to come out swinging, since they were all strangers?
She’s very shrewd when it comes to these things.
I had a feeling that she might have come right on the hour on purpose, but I didn’t bother saying that. None of them had signed the contract yet. “Then let’s briefly introduce ourselves.”
After ordering a few dishes and drinks, we had time to get familiar with each other. Ainar started us off. “I am Ainar, the second daughter of Fenelin! Nice to meet you!”
“Um, Ainar? I think that’s too shorrrt...” Missha, who had grown quite close to Ainar these past few days, said.

“D-Do I have to say more...? Sorry. I’m not used to these gatherings...” Ainar scratched her head in embarrassment. No one criticized her for it, though. Ainar was already acquainted with the entire team. She had been with Raven at the Bloody Citadel, and she had met Mr. Bear at his shop a few days ago.
“Miss Ainar... you’re exactly the same.”
“Thanks for the compliment. Wizard, you seem the same too.”
Anyway, in the end, I took the liberty of introducing Ainar myself, things like her adventurer ranking, her role in the team, etcetera.
After my briefing, Mr. Bear made a short comment. “Then there are two swordsmen?”
Before I could answer, Ainar interrupted to point out his supposed error. “Urakburak, I am a warrior, not a swordsman.”
“My name is Urikfried... No, I said this last time, but can’t you just call me Abman?”
“...I will try. The pronunciation is difficult.”
“Pronunciation?”
“Is there a problem?”

Mr. Bear looked like he had a lot to say to that, but he ended the conversation with a deep sigh. He was slowly learning how to talk to a barbarian—namely, that the best thing was to not talk to them at all. “You’re the only one I haven’t met. I heard a lot from Bjorn. Abman Urikfried.”
“Arua Raven. You’re a scout, yes?”
Missha interrupted. “Ah, I am Missha Karlstein.”

Afterward, the remaining three introduced themselves and conversed about their respective roles like professionals. With this, half of the first meeting was over. The food we ordered arrived then, so we continued our conversation over meals and drinks.
“This place is clean and has good food.”
“If only my wife cooked like this...”
“Are you married, Mr. Urikfried?”
“Oh, I didn’t mention. It has been three years now.”
“Bjorn, this is called squid, would you like to trrry it? The texture is very unique.”
The overall atmosphere was friendly until the topic of the labyrinth came up near the end of the meal.
“Anyway, let’s get to the point now, shall we?”
“Yes, that’s a good idea. Bjorn, how are you going to distribute the loot?”
When the problem of money came to the surface, the looks in everyone’s eyes changed. Well, everyone except Ainar.
“Can’t we just take what Bjorn gives us?”
“Maybe you can, Miss Ainar. But not us.”
The wizard was quick to judge and Mr. Bear had a family to protect. Both were nice people in private, but when the time came, they openly defended their rights.
“Missha is fine, but I think there’s a problem with Ainar getting the same share. Of the five of us, she’s the most lacking.”
“Urakburak...! I-Is that what you think of me?! I-I trusted you! I thought you were a valuable comrade!”
“Be quiet. Bjorrrn will take care of it. Hm? Be nice.”
Ainar trembled at the betrayal and Missha covered her mouth just in time to quiet her. However, seeing her like that must have made it a little hard for Mr. Bear to keep talking.
“Ahem...” Mr. Bear coughed and averted his gaze.
Raven smoothly took the baton and started her own appeal. “I don’t really mind Miss Ainar or Karlstein. I’m a wizard, after all.”
“...Speak.”
“With me, you can store an essence in a test tube and sell it. And since I know high-class distortion magic as well, even if we want to get remains, we can obtain them much more easily.”
“Are you asking to raise your share?”
“Yes. I want 30 percent.”
Whew, right from the start, this was not easy. Dwalkie had accepted an equal share with a laugh and a smile. “...30 percent is too much.”
“Of course not. All my seniors say they take that much.”
Hey, who are you trying to fool?
There was no doubt wizards were treated well in the labyrinth—assuming everyone was equal. “Those seniors must have joined teams with lower rankings than themselves.”
“Hmm, are you saying I haven’t?”
Since Raven was a rank-six wizard, it was appropriate to treat her as a rank-five adventurer. Considering that Missha and I were rank six and Ainar was rank seven, Raven was clearly a higher rank.
“We’ll find out once we start our quest.” I was confident. Regardless of ranking, there was no world where she would end up carrying us single-handedly. “Isn’t that why you wanted to join the team?”

“Well, that is true.” Surprisingly, Raven readily admitted it. Was she just setting the stage for her next argument? “Still, it’s also true that Miss Karlstein and Miss Fenelin are less crucial than the three of us.”
“They’ll pull their weight soon.”
“Yes. I think so too. In one year... No, at the earliest, they will do their part in a few months. But why should I suffer a loss until then?”

Raven proposed the team revise our distribution scale again later, once the two of them could proudly claim their share, and I accepted that logic to some extent. “The ratio is 20 percent for everyone. Instead, you’ll have 40 percent of the special loot obtained through magic.”
“All right.”

Like that, Raven ended up taking the offer that a wizard belonging to a five-person party would normally receive—an equal share plus a bonus limited to magical loot. One person down. All that was left was Mr. Bear.

“I’ll take 5 percent from Ainar and give it to you.” In truth, considering he was a scout, it wouldn’t be unreasonable to give him 10 percent more. “Since we haven’t even gone on our first expedition yet, for now, be satisfied with that.”
Mr. Bear readily agreed. Well, I was sure it would be a bit awkward for him to proudly claim his share. He may have been a scout, but his navigation ability was zero.
“Then this matter is settled.”

Thus, the final distribution rates were determined: 20 percent for me, 20 percent for Missha, 15 percent for Ainar, 20 percent for Raven (along with 40 percent of any special loot), and 25 percent for Mr. Bear. This was just the case for general loot. We agreed to split anything obtained from getting rid of a plunderer and things like that equally.
Whew, what a waste.

I could see why explorers were so hung up on promotions. I needed to reach rank five or something soon. If the three of us had all been rank five, those guys wouldn’t have even brought up distribution in the first place.
Well, this much is to be expected.

I took a sip from my drink and let go of my regrets. I had even had a scenario in mind where they were even greedier than this, but they instead stayed in their lanes. If I weren’t the leader and this were another team, the members would have been more outspoken about their profits.
I guess the most important hurdle has been crossed.
Now that the distribution negotiations were over, the party was pretty much set in stone, although there were still countless issues left to discuss.
“Oh right, what about the party? When are you going to register it?” asked Raven.
“I will do it tomorrow.”
“Then I can’t go. I thought that would be the case, though, so I brought a power of attorney with me. Please go without me.”
“...Sure.”
We had to discuss things from simple administrative tasks to all sorts of issues.
“Are we going to make a separate team fund? Or just collect what’s needed each time?”
“We will collect a regular amount each month.”
“How much?”

How much would be used for the team funds? If there ended up being a shortage in the funds, how would we make up for it? If we entered a Rift or discovered a mysterious treasure in the labyrinth, would we still use the same distribution rates? Were we going to acknowledge individual claims over items people acquired single-handedly? Were there incentives? Etcetera, etcetera, etcetera.
Team Half-Wit wasn’t like this...
When I zoned back in, I noticed that Raven and I were the only ones still actively engaging in the conversation.
Honnnk!

Ainar was asleep with her head hanging. Mr. Bear just downed a drink like he was enjoying a bit of long-awaited freedom, and Missha was scribbling in a notebook. She wasn’t taking notes or anything, it was just her hobby. Apparently, her hands were itching to do something now that she wasn’t able to cook. She had started drawing a few days ago.
“...What did you draw?”
“N-Nothing.”
“An orc?”
“Pffft!! Yes, it’s an orrrc. An orc. Hahaha.”
Her reaction was somewhat strange, but Raven called my name before I could press Missha for details. “Um, Mr. Yandel, we’re still talking...”

Oh, right. After using my brain for the past several hours, my concentration was failing. I wasn’t sure about the important topics, but having to decide on so many little things was leaving me in this state. Before long, I checked the time and said, “Raven, let’s stop here for today.”
“Sorry? But we’re not finished going through the things on my list.”
“List?”
“Points that should be addressed before forming the party. I made a list of them beforehand.” When I asked her how many points were left, Raven answered with thirty-one.
...What we’ve done so far isn’t even half of it?

Just thinking about the rest of the points already left me bored out of my mind, but with her personality, getting through them would be at least a little helpful. “Still, it’s too late now. Let’s do the rest next time.”
“Okay.”

We arranged a meeting for two days from now and all left. For some reason, my body and mind were both exhausted. I had always thought my personality was similar to a wizard’s, but after seeing a real one, I was certain. I was glad I chose a barbarian.
The morning after the first meeting, four of us gathered and visited the Adventurers’ Guild. Submitting Raven’s power of attorney from yesterday, we officially finished registering the party.

“The party name is Bjorn? Isn’t that too half-hearted?” Ainar muttered in dissatisfaction, but I was just doing as was customary. Team Half-Wit’s official name had just been “Murad.” Normally, everyone just used the team leader’s first or last name.
“If we find something more suitable, we can change it. So don’t be too disappointed.”
“C-Can I think of one too?”
“Of course you can.”
“Really!? I will think hard!” I was sure she’d forget about this in a few hours, but it didn’t matter if she did. The name of the party wasn’t important.
“Abman, what are your plans?”
“I have to get back to the tavern. My wife is waiting for me.”
“I see.”

As soon as the team was formed, Mr. Bear left and we had a simple meal out before returning home. All three of us lived at the inn now—me in room 201, Ainar in room 202, and Missha in room 207 across the hall.
“Oh, Bjorrrn. There’s something in your mailbox.”
“Mail?” I checked it at Missha’s comment, and there was a letter inside with the seal of the Church of Reatlas.
Is it a meeting with the dragon tribe?
I hurriedly entered my room and checked the contents. But what was this? When I opened it, there was only one sentence written on the note.
He will call you.
The heading—Paal Krovitz, Third Captain of the Paladins—was longer than the actual message.
What is this?

While I was looking at it in confusion, the letter caught on fire and turned to ashes in an instant. I was thankful that he’d taken care to be secretive like I’d asked... but it was hard for even me to understand his message.

I sat on the bed for a moment to get my thoughts in order. I had a rough idea of the “he” Krovitz was referring to. He must have been talking about the leader of the dragon tribe, the elder dragon. There was just one thing I didn’t quite understand.
He’s going to call on me?
It would have made more sense if he had written a time and place down instead, since I was the one who had asked him to arrange a meeting with the utmost secrecy.
How will he call me? Is he going to track me down to set up a rendezvous?
Just as I flopped back into the bed with these thoughts in mind, a magic circle appeared on the wooden floor below me in blue light.
“Huh?”
Without giving me any time to figure out what was going on, the magic circle flared, blinding me. When I came to, I was in an unfamiliar place.
It’s like I was summoned to another world.
In front of me was a building reminiscent of a Greek temple supported by huge pillars. I quickly took stock of my current situation.
This is the Dragon Temple. Did they use a teleportation-type Dragon Speech? And the letter served as a medium?
I roughly grasped what was going on. This wasn’t bad. It’d be much easier to maintain secrecy this way.
“You are not surprised.”

Soon, I looked forward. There was a man with all the characteristics of the dragon people gently looking down at me from his seat on a throne. Scales sprouted from his skin and his pupils were reminiscent of a reptile’s. The throne was enveloped by fog, but dozens of eyes were shining from beyond it. Were they all dragon people? How many did he gather?
Geez, those eyes.

They carried a different kind of pressure from murderous intent. It felt like I was weaponless and facing another species that I could never defeat, a natural predator. This was Dragon Fear, something all dragon people were passively equipped with.
And they’re using it on me, huh?
I smiled sharply. I thought I knew what their intentions were.
“Did you know? You are not the first barbarian to visit this place. However... You will be the first to return alive, if you manage it.”

It was a kind of stalling. Due to the nature of their race, they wouldn’t steal the Dragon Slayer sword without compensating their benefactor, but they probably decided it was best to break my spirit beforehand. After all, they didn’t know what kind of unreasonable demands a barbarian like myself would make.
The Dragon Fear grew stronger, which made me break out in a cold sweat. But, so what? I wasn’t raised to be a fool whose mind went blank just because of a little sweat.
Why do these people like psychological warfare so much?
Thanks to that, it became clear what I had to do right then. I never dreamed that I would start with this before I even introduced myself, but letting them know this now would save more time.
Whether they tried to subdue me with Dragon Fear or not, this was all a waste of time.
“Behelaaah!”

chapters.title: Chapter 160: Negotiation (2)
paragraphs: A strange silence fell. It would have been good manners to ask why I had suddenly screamed out of nowhere, but Mr. Dragon just kept his mouth shut, stone-faced, after my outcry.
Geez, this is making me embarrassed.

Once the silence was starting to feel uncomfortable, the brown-haired Mr. Dragon deactivated his Dragon Fear and asked, “...Why did you shout out of the blue?” It was hard to read his reptilian eyes, but this seemed like pure curiosity. So, this man could get curious.

“I just felt like doing it,” I answered without hesitation. “Why, is there a problem?” When I was too flustered to give a detailed explanation, this was my barbarian cheat code that I could apply to anything.

Mr. Dragon seemed lost in thought for a moment before he smiled. “No, there is no problem. Barbarians are as interesting as I’ve heard.” His was an imposing and dignified voice. Soon, he waved his hand in the air.
Shhhhhh!

A gust of wind billowed out and the mist disappeared. The scene beyond the mist was rather different from what I had expected. There was no one there. I thought it would be full of dragons because of all those shiny eyes I saw.
When I looked at him for an explanation, he averted his eyes sheepishly. “Let it be known that I was against this childishness.”
“Against what?”
“Ah, apparently, negotiating is easier after you crush the opponent’s spirit? Or so they say.”

Put simply, the shining eyes had all been an illusion. To be honest, if I had thought about it calmly, I could have noticed that earlier. Not only had I stressed a need for confidentiality to Krovitz, but the dragon people were a race with an extremely small population. Logically, there was no way dozens of them had gathered in one place just to pick on me.

“Anyway, I’m sorry about that. Tsk, I don’t know what we’re doing, trying to save a few pennies. I told them we cannot forget our duty and treat our benefactor like this.” His voice was still imposing, but the way he spoke and the atmosphere around him were noticeably lighter than before. Was everything before just an act, and this was his real self? If that was the case, I thought we might be able to see eye to eye. Still, I couldn’t let my guard down. This could be an act too.
“First, let me confirm. I am Bjorn, son of Yandel. Are you the chieftain of the dragon tribe?”
“Chieftain... In your culture, that would be accurate, although it hasn’t been that long since I took over the position.”
“It hasn’t?” I involuntarily cocked my head. I heard it had been more than thirty years since the Dragon Slayer had killed the elder dragon and received a curse.
“Time means different things to different people.”

Oh, right. The dragon people had had long lifespans in the game. It wasn’t critical information so I had forgotten about it for a moment. Anyway, that wasn’t important, so I should just get to the point.
“Chief.”

“Feel free to call me Pirsearaidormus.” Was it possible to say that freely or easily? As I was pondering what my reaction to that should be, Mr. Dragon laughed and gave me another name. “That was a joke. Just call me Lapir. It is my second name for public use.”

For reference, second names were a culture unique to the dragon people. Since their true names were so long, they needed second names in order to make living in the city more convenient. Regal Vagos’ real name would be much longer too.
Whew, I’m glad, though.

I let out a silent sigh of relief. This was an official meeting, and if he had requested I call him by this long, true name, it would’ve been a hassle. “Lapir, then. If my name is too long, you can call me Yandel, or Bjorn—whichever is easier to pronounce.”

“I like Yandel better.” Anyway, introductions were over. Right when I was about to speak up, Mr. Dragon spoke first. “Before we start talking, can I see the Dragon Sword first? I heard the story through the church, but I still can’t believe it.”
As soon as I heard that, I let out a derisive chuckle. He may have spoken softly, but the implication of those words was very explicit.
Telling me he can’t trust me to my face...

Well, it wasn’t that I didn’t understand where he was coming from. Vagos was a member of Orcules and a huge criminal with a bounty worth hundreds of millions of stones. I was sure it was hard to accept that a fourth-floor adventurer like me beat him up and stole his sword.
Stab!
There was no need to drag this out, so I took the Dragon Sword out of my bag and stuck it in the ground.
Ow, that hurts.
I only held it for about three seconds, but my skin was already peeling off.
A moment later, Mr. Dragon came down from the throne and pulled out the sword, holding it in his hand. “So it was true,” he murmured in a low voice.

In that short sentence, I could sense a whole range of complex emotions. He seemed somewhat determined, yet wistful at the same time. Well, considering the story behind this sword, he must have felt differently about it than I did.
Mr. Dragon held the sword and stood there like that for a long while before stabbing it into the ground again. “How was he? You’re the last person to have seen him. I wish to hear more.”
I told him about what happened that day, leaving out the parts I didn’t want to talk about.
“I see. So he ended up... Thank you for telling me. As you requested, I will keep the fact that the Dragon Sword has been returned a secret.”
“Were you close with him?”
At my question, Mr. Dragon smiled sadly. “He is... my younger brother.”
“What?”

“Which is why... I couldn’t stop him myself.” I wanted to speak with him a little longer to learn more information about the Dragon Slayer, but Mr. Dragon changed the subject in a way that told me he didn’t want to talk about it. “Come to think of it, I haven’t said this yet. Bjorn, son of Yandel, thank you for returning this sword. Unrelated to the reward you seek, we will consider you a benefactor of the dragon people.”

I could tell from the look in his eyes that those words were sincere. His reptilian eyes were a bit hard to read, but still. As I had only done this for the reward, I was pretty self-conscious, but there was no need to refuse this treatment. Later, I’d ask about the exact benefits that came with being a benefactor, but for now I focused on the current conversation.
“So, what would you like?”

That was, in truth, the crux of this meeting. I’d been thinking a lot about this. What should I ask in return for a weapon made of a grade-six material and an item that had the same significance to the dragon people as a holy relic?
“What can you give me?” I asked just in case, figuring that he might make an offer that could change my mind.
Mr. Dragon had some things prepared, and spoke without much preamble. “The first is wealth.”

Money. Not bad. That was one of the three options I had been considering before I made my final decision, anyway. If I considered that grade-six weapons started in the hundreds of millions, I should be given enough reward money to cover my entire body with high-quality equipment.
“I don’t need money.”
At my response, Mr. Dragon gave me a strange look. I guessed he didn’t think I would turn down this offer. “Hmm, that’s probably because you don’t know how much money—”
“I’ll say it again, I’m not after money.”
The amount didn’t matter. It wouldn’t be more than the Dragon Sword was worth, anyway. I’d rather get something else.
Sensing my resolve, Mr. Dragon offered up the next possibility for my reward. “The second is a teammate.”
“Teammate?”
“I heard from Sir Krovitz that you are building a new party.”
“Your point?”
“I will have one of my clan members work with you for two years.”
This was a reward I hadn’t even considered. He was offering to give me a teammate? This was definitely a race that knew their worth.
It’s certainly appealing...

As I could tell from the battle with the Dragon Slayer, Dragon Speech made possible things even a wizard or priest couldn’t pull off. In addition, dragon people had high base stats that made them good at close combat, and they could use magic that only certain humans could use.

However, once again, my answer was the same. “I have already found all my teammates.” I wasn’t inclined to take in a teammate who would be gone after two years. What I wanted was a party held together by a bond.
“She is very pretty.”
Umm, and what does that have to do with anything?
When I shot him a look, Mr. Dragon coughed in embarrassment and opened his mouth again. “...Then this will be the final offer.”
“Speak.”
“I’ll give you the arc-made weapon that will be forged next year.”
As expected, this was the last option. Arc metal and dragon people were closely related and even considered synonymous. Only dragon people could handle the arc.
And the rule is that only one weapon can be made each year through a ritual.
In that sense, this reward was the one that made the most sense—an arc longsword that I could use in exchange for one that I could not. This was a win-win.
But if that was the case, I would have just taken the money.

My answer this time was the same. “I don’t like that, either.” Mr. Dragon clearly didn’t expect that I would turn this offer down as well and pursed his lips. He didn’t seem to have anything else to offer, so I decided to speak first. “I don’t need those. Just give me a tattoo,” I said like it was no big deal.
“Tattoo?” Mr. Dragon cocked his head before his eyes widened horizontally. He seemed to realize what I meant a moment later. “You mean the Dragon’s Blessing?”
Yes, that.
When I nodded, Mr. Dragon’s eyes changed in an instant. “Yandel, where did you hear about that?”
Whew, now came the real test. The Dragon’s Blessing, along with Dragon Speech, was the thing that elevated the dragon tribe into the ranks of OP characters.
“The elders were right. You people are too greedy.” The smile disappeared from Mr. Dragon’s face, and he reactivated his Dragon Fear. “I should have done this earlier.”

The air around me grew so heavy that it became difficult to breathe. Was this his real serious mode? It seemed he had been telling the truth when he said he was opposed to the childishness from earlier because the intensity of this was entirely different.
Not to the extent that I can’t endure it, though.
It was the same as last time again. Scary to the point of making me shudder? So, what? As long as their ancestral gods were with them, a barbarian never backed down from psychological warfare alone.
“Behelahhh!”
When I relaxed the stiff muscles of my neck and summoned a shout from low in my belly, Mr. Dragon’s jaw dropped. “What the...?”
“Is there a problem?”

“...Are all barbarians like you?” Soon enough, he pulled back Dragon Fear. Yes, he may have used serious mode, but it wasn’t because he was really irritated with me. “Hah...” Mr. Dragon dropped the grim look on his face and let out a deep sigh. “I will offer you a sizable sum of money on top of the arc weapon. How about that?”
Having concluded that the stick wouldn’t work on me, he handed me a carrot. FYI, I hated carrots.
“I refuse!”
“You don’t understand. This will be dangerous for you too. If your people find out, you will be treated as a traitor.”
I’d already received a blessing, so that wasn’t new.
“So calm yourself—”

“Lapir! Aren’t you a descendant of a dragon?! Don’t be petty and do it for me! You call me a benefactor yet you can’t do this? That is low!” He’d probably never had someone childishly scream, “Gimme!” at a negotiating table before, because he just stared at me blankly. I used the opportunity to aim for his Achilles heel. “The goddess of the stars told me that Regal Vagos and I will meet again. We are connected by a strong, ominous fate.”
“...The goddess of the stars said that? Is that true?”
“I must get stronger if I don’t want to lose another teammate to your brother.”
It was a dirty move even for me, but what could I do? Negotiations were won by the ones who didn’t hesitate to use even the dirtiest of tricks. And technically, I didn’t say anything untrue.
“Lapir, you said earlier that you couldn’t stop your brother with your own power, right? Invest in me. I will finish what you couldn’t do.” After that, I didn’t press him anymore.
Mr. Dragon entered thinking mode for a long time. “...I suppose this is karma,” he muttered, sighing.
“Will you do it?”
“...First, I’ll have to confirm with the temple that the prophecy you mentioned is true. I will call you after that. This is not something I can decide on my own.”
If you say so. “How long do you think it will take?”
“I don’t know. One month? Two months? I will make a decision as soon as possible and let you know.”
“Until then, I’ll hold on to this.”
“Sure.”

He’d accepted that much more easily than I had expected. After that, I pulled Dragon Sword out of the stone and put it back into my bag. Then, after asking how I should contact him again and getting answers to a few other questions I had, I concluded today’s negotiations.
“This is a message stone. When I contact you, tear the paper I just gave you. Then I will know where you are.”
“I will.”
Soon after, Mr. Dragon sent me back to the inn by using his teleportation-based Dragon Speech again.
Like I thought, Dragon Speech is such a cheat.
With that thought in mind, I threw off my equipment and was about to lie down on the bed.
Knock, knock, knock.
A knock rang out. That meant I had a visit from a stranger. Missha would have just opened the door, and Ainar’s knock would’ve sounded more like bang, bang, bang.
“Nice to see you.” When I opened the door, I saw a familiar woman.
“Julian Urbans?” It was the daughter of the district chief, a truly dishonorable daughter who wished for her father’s downfall in order to gain her freedom.
“So, have you changed your mind?”
“What do you mean?”
“I heard your party was disbanded. That wizard is dead too. It was that Rotmiller man’s doing, right?”

Ah, so that was why she hadn’t given up and had come back. From an outsider’s perspective, her explanation was definitely plausible. “He’s not ‘that wizard,’ but Riol Warb Dwalkie. And it’s true your father tried to pull one over on me, but Rotmiller wasn’t bought.” I pointed out only the facts. After doing that, I realized I needed to resolve this issue now. Even if the district chief tried something else, I didn’t think Mr. Bear or Raven would fall for it so easily, but ignoring the problem would only make it more of an issue in the future.
I should do it while it’s already on my mind.
“Where is your father now?”
“Uh, I don’t know. He’s probably at the District Seven headquarters at this time.”
Obtaining just the necessary information from Urbans, I issued her an order to leave. “You go back now. And don’t return. I refuse to get entangled in your family’s affairs.”
“Pardon? What do you m—”
“It is just as I said.”

When she first came to see me, I thought she had harbored ill will toward me because of the prison break incident. But now that I was thinking back, the timing was just right. The reason the district chief had suddenly become hostile toward me a few months ago was because of her.
“I told you. Our interests are aligned.”
“Uh huh, leave.” I forced Urbans out and put on the equipment I had just taken off.
Creak.
When I stepped out the door, she was still standing there. “Are you going to see my father?”
“Yes. I’m going to negotiate.”
“But why the weapon?”
I cocked my head. Why wouldn’t I take my weapon to a negotiation?

chapters.title: Chapter 161: Negotiation (3)
paragraphs: I walked through the city at a fast clip, wearing light armor and with a shield and mace in hand.

“No, wait! Just wait a second!” Behind me was the young lady Urbans, practically running after me to try to stop me. “I know what you’re trying to do, but doing that won’t help you right now. I-I’ll resolve it. Of course, I’ll need your help, but... You can lend me your strength and I’ll use my brain. What do you think? Won’t we make a pretty good team?”

What was this kid talking about? Ignoring her chatter, I continued walking. Miss Urbans, who I was treating like she was invisible, kept trying to stand in my way and grab my arm. Did she really think that was going to work?
“Ugh!”

Dragged along without any resistance, Miss Urbans threw the parasol she was carrying on the floor, vexed. But the momentary show of anger didn’t last long. Within three seconds she picked up her parasol and started following me again. “I, um... s-sorry. It might be because of me that you got involved in this. If I hadn’t approached you, Father might have left you alone.”

“At least you’re not unrepentant.” I spoke up for the first time to respond to her honest apology, though I of course didn’t stop walking. This and that were two different things. Plus, her words didn’t seem that sincere to begin with.
“I even apologized!”

When I just increased my speed, Miss Urbans, who clearly grew up an indoor girl, did her best to follow me while wiping her sweat with her handkerchief. I guess she thought there was still room for persuasion.

“Hoo, hoo, hoo...” Even while letting out rough exhales, Miss Urbans chattered incessantly. “Give me a chance to make things right. I know it’s a brazen request. B-But once I inherit my father’s position, I’ll repay you many times over!”
She was slowly reaching her physical limit. Miss Urbans’ voice started to grow distant. After some consideration, I slowed down a bit. Of course, I hadn’t changed my mind on helping her.
But it might be better for her to be by my side while I meet with the district chief.

Now that I thought about it, her reactions would make it easy for me to prove my innocence. However, if I walked too slowly, she was bound to talk my ear off, so I adjusted my speed to keep her at a certain distance. About thirty minutes passed like that, and we finally arrived at our destination.
[Adventurers’ Guild District 7 Central Branch.]

There was a headquarters located in each district of the city. I’d seen this one a few times in passing, but it was much bigger than the other branches. Since there were matters that could only be settled at headquarters, there were a lot of adventurers inside too. I stood in front of the doors to think for a moment.
Do I break this or not?
Did I seem like I was hesitating? Miss Urbans, who looked like she had bathed in sweat, quickly spoke up. “Yes. It’s not too late—”
You wish.
“Okay, I’ve decided.”
“Sorry?”
“I’m going to break it.”
Yes, that was more to my liking.
Crashhh!
I kicked the door with all my might. I needed to show them that I was a crude barbarian so that they thought, Oh, this guy will fuck me up if I mess with him, and think twice about doing so.
If this negotiation goes well, he won’t be able to ask me for the money to repair it anyway.
And besides that, he had enough money for repairs. Though, did they use good quality wood at headquarters or something? It didn’t break as dramatically as I thought.
“Kyaaa! W-What are you doing—!”
Ignoring Miss Urbans, I pulled out the leg that was penetrating the door, calmly gripped my mace, and just smashed the door straight-forwardly.
Crunch! Crunch! Crunch!
The door transformed into an open doorframe that let the breeze in to improve air circulation. Beyond it, I could see staff and adventurers.
“...A robber?”
“Shouldn’t a robber be at the bank...?”

There were those with reasonable concerns, those who looked dazed, others who looked like they had just seen a lunatic, and lastly, those who, like real adventurers, saw this situation as an opportunity.
A bald man who was standing next to a female employee stretched his arms as a warm-up as he approached me. “Miss, if I handle this, do I get some accomplishment points?”
“Pardon? Yes! As I remember it, that by-law was made half a year ago!”
“Good.”
Come to think of it, there was a guy like this last time too, six months ago when I became a free barbarian.
I didn’t think a rank-five adventurer would step forward first. Are the adventurers at headquarters higher-ranking?

The ID badge Mr. Baldy was wearing proudly on his hip told me he was a rank-five adventurer. Still, there was no reason for me to back down. Instead, I thought he would be the perfect opponent to assess my combat strength.

“I am not here to fight you. Move.” However, as a modern man who had arrived in this world not too long ago, I tried using words first. I judged that there wasn’t necessarily a reason to fight an adventurer here.

Mr. Baldy didn’t seem to want to pass up the opportunity to gain accomplishment points, though. “Hey, barbarian. It looks like you have some complaints to make with the guild. If that’s the case, you should have gone through the process of lodging a formal complaint, eh?”
“Complaint?”
“Ah, you don’t know what the procedure is, huh? Makes sense for a savage.”

A sharp smile appeared on my face. A savage, huh? He certainly wasn’t wrong. Even barbarians considered themselves savages, but only we could call ourselves that. How could he not know something that simple?
“...There’s something wrong with your head. Perhaps that’s why you went bald.”
“What? You son of a—!” As expected, he must have shaved his head because of hair loss since he rushed toward me indignantly. Or at least, he was about to.
“E-Everyone stop!” Miss Urbans shouted, stepping between me and Baldy.

Unable to injure a civilian, Baldy stopped right away. “Get out of the way. That man is a criminal who just caused a commotion at the guild. I don’t know who you are, but if you do something as careless as to side with him—”
“...Miss Urbans?” While Baldy was steaming through his nose intimidatingly, another employee recognized her status and the situation took a new turn.
“What? Urbans? The daughter of the district chief?”
“Why is a woman like that defending a barbarian...?”
Realizing how important she was and that something had gone wrong, Mr. Baldy took a step back. Maybe it was because he was a rank five, but he was definitely quick on the uptake.
“Is my father upstairs?”
“Pardon? Yes! That’s right...”
“Then we’ll go up together. Is that all right? As for what happened here... Please take care of it.”
“Yes! Of course!”
Thanks to Miss Urbans’ status, the ruckus on the first floor was smoothly dealt with and I was able to go up.
Creak, creak.
The wooden staircase was not able to handle the weight of a barbarian wearing heavy equipment without creaking. I stopped for a moment to ask, “Why did you help me just now?”
“Because you’re not going to change your mind anyway.”
Well, yeah, but... That makes it even harder to understand.
If she had figured out that I was impossible to recruit as an ally, why did she help me?

“I thought that a side effect of my offer would be that it would help you as well, Mr. Yandel. But since you don’t want it, it’s only right to do this. I’m sorry you’ve had to suffer because of my family’s affairs. Once we get inside, I’ll make sure to properly explain the situation to my father.”
Hmm, I did sense more sincerity than earlier. “I see.” I nodded nonchalantly and kept moving.
“Eh? That’s it?”
What, did you think I would change my mind?
“Fulfill your ambition with your own hands.”

I refused to get involved in something troublesome. To be honest, I didn’t sympathize with the position of a daughter deprived of freedom by her father, either. If she truly wanted independence, she would have given everything up: the perks that came with the status of being the district chief’s daughter, the responsibilities, all of it.
“Miss?” When we arrived at the district chief’s office, we saw a guard blocking the way. “Who is the man next to you?” the guard asked professionally.
Miss Urbans brushed the question off. “He is a guest of my father’s.”
When the guard knocked on the door and notified the district chief of the situation, permission soon filtered through the wood. “Tell them to come in.”
“You cannot bring any weapons inside. Please hand that to me.”
I raised my mace as if to follow the guard’s instructions, then entered the office with brute force.
Crunch!

The door to the office also transformed as I introduced an open floor plan. When I stepped beyond it, the district chief was sitting at his desk, frozen in place with a pen in hand. He glanced between his daughter and me, back and forth. “What is this?!” After a moment of silence, the guard sprung into action. “Stop, you can step out,” said Urbans.
“There is nothing to worry about. He is not that reckless.”
“All right, then.” The guard seemed well-trained because he left without another word. Of course, there was no need to shut the door, because it was gone now.
Sigh...
In a daze, he watched the guard pace the hallway, and then go downstairs. The district chief got up from his desk and sat on the sofa, so I also seated myself in front of him.
Squelch.
The sofa collapsed, unable to bear the weight of a heavily-armored barbarian. But like any barbarian, I did not apologize. “This sofa is old.”

A blue vein pulsed on the district chief’s forehead, but I guess he decided that the sofa wasn’t important. “...Tell me why you’re here. There must be a reason why you’ve come here holding my daughter’s hand and done this.”
“Um, Father, that’s—”
“I didn’t ask you.”
At those words, Miss Urbans went as still as stone. Although she had bold plans to go against her father, I guess she was still scared of him.
“Figure out family affairs amongst yourselves,” I said bluntly. That was the first reason I was here today.
“Does that mean you’re betraying my daughter?”
“There’s nothing to betray because we were never working together. And we never will.”

The district chief looked at me with an unreadable expression on his face, clearly trying to discern my true intentions. I didn’t offer any explanations. It was up to him to decide whether he believed me. “Then why did you come with my daughter?”
“She kept bothering me, so I decided it would be better to say it to you directly. But she kept following me, like a goblin.”
“Th-that was so I could stop you before you caused any trouble!” Julian got riled up at the word “goblin” and, as I expected, her reaction was helpful.

“I see. I will believe you.” That checked off my first goal of clearing up that particular misunderstanding. “But if that is your purpose here, why are you acting so rude?” the district chief asked after a moment as he looked at the smashed door. “That had nothing to do with my feelings toward you. What will people think of me when they see that broken door?”
I don’t know, that you’re a righteous chief who values communication with his employees and has nothing to hide?
At the thought, I smiled. I could see what he was really trying to say. He was saying I’d ruined his reputation by causing a scene.
“No one would be able to object if I were to arrest and detain you right away.”
He wasn’t wrong, but I wasn’t scared. I knew he couldn’t do it, which was also why I was behaving like this. “Arrest me. Then everything you did to me will also be revealed.”
“...You trust that scout?”

“No way.” I firmly shook my head. I had no intention of getting Rotmiller involved in this incident. I had a better card to play than that in the first place. “I have a video copy of you trying to win over the wizard after my prison break.”
“Then the lady of Altemion lied to me.”

“She said she wouldn’t show it to anyone; she didn’t say there wouldn’t be copies.” I cocked my head indifferently and added, “I don’t know if you know this, but she became our party’s wizard not long ago.”
To put it simply, that meant, “Forget about trying to win over Raven.” The district chief’s eyes darkened.
Still don’t get it? I’m not the same rookie barbarian I was when we first met.
“A district chief who tried to frame and kill the heir to the barbarian tribe. I heard there’s going to be an election next year. Sounds like the perfect gossip for people to chew on.”
“...Heir?”
“Your information channels are slow. It happened not long ago.”
The district chief pursed his lips for a moment. “What do you want?” he finally asked.

A complete declaration of surrender. It was time to move on to my second reason for coming here. The district chief had tried to use Rotmiller to hurt me. Normally, this was a serious crime deserving of three skull smashes. Of course, in order to punish him for his sins, I had also had to go through numerous obstacles. We would end up becoming arch nemeses at this rate, which was why I left off with a warning today. The Dragon Slayer alone was headache enough.

“Whether there is another misunderstanding or if you just hate me, it doesn’t matter. If you pull something like this one more time... I won’t talk anymore.” I glared at him while releasing murderous intent, and he stiffened. It wasn’t as dramatic a reaction as at Ghost Busters, but that should be warning enough.
When I was done with my business, I got up from the sofa right away. The district chief blurted out a question. “Aren’t you going to wait to hear my answer?”
I don’t know, is that necessary?
I chuckled.
Snap!
I grabbed the table between us with both hands and folded it with brute force alone. “This table is also old.”
That ended today’s negotiations.
“Then I’ll go now. I’m hungry.”
If I had to come back here one day, it wouldn’t be something like a door or a table he’d lose.

chapters.title: Chapter 162: Exploration (1)
paragraphs: The day after my negotiations with the district chief, the whole team gathered for our second meeting. After getting through the thirty-one points of discussion that we couldn’t last time, we came up with a plan for our quest together.
“Hmm, if we want to go to the fifth floor, there will be a lot of preparations to make.”
“Can I leave that part to you? If you bring back the receipts, I’ll take it out of the shared funds.”
“All right. I have business at Kommelby, anyway.”
The name of the team was decided at this meeting. I thought “Team Bjorn” was good enough, but Ainar wasn’t the only one with fantasies about our team name.
Raven suggested one first. “Um... I thought about it, but how about the name ‘Narak?’”
“Narak?”
“It means ‘those who walk in the darkness’ in an ancient language. It’s nice, isn’t it?”

I didn’t know about that, to be honest, but I did get the sense that a black flame dragon used to live inside the right hand of this edgy twenty-four-year-old wizard. Those who walk in the darkness... “You... have a unique taste.”
“...Are you making fun of me?”

Anyway, I was just about to choose the party’s name based on Raven’s claim that her suggestion was a hundred times better than something as half-assed as Team Bjorn when Ainar, who was dozing off, rushed to join the conversation. “N-No! I came up with a team name!”
“Pardon? Oh, do you have another idea?”
“Our team name is Apple Pie!”
“Apple pie...? Like the dessert?” Raven asked, half-dazed. Without hesitation, Ainar replied in the affirmative. Apparently, it was her favorite thing. “What nonsense...”
“How come!?”
Raven sighed at Ainar’s stubbornness before suggesting a vote. Apparently, she was convinced that we would never give credence to a name like that.
Mr. Bear abstained. “I don’t care what our team name is, so you guys figure it out.”
Unexpectedly, Missha voted for Ainar’s suggestion. “Mm, I think Apple Pie is fine too... It’s sweet and delicious.”
“That’s—! W-What about you, Mr. Yandel? You’re not going to use such a ridiculous name, are you?”

To be honest, this was a dilemma. If I took Raven’s side, it would be a draw. Deep down, I wanted to take Ainar’s side and wrap this up as soon as possible, but showing favoritism as the party’s leader would hurt the wizard’s feelings. I suggested a compromise out of necessity. “Let’s just combine them and name it Apple Narak.”
Raven was speechless.
“Oh, is Narak Pie better?”
“...I’ll take the first one.”
“Ainar, you?”
“I think that’s better too! I like how it sounds!”
Just like that, Apple Narak was chosen as our official team name and the second meeting was over.
After that, peaceful days followed. My daily routine consisted of reading books at the library and meeting with the entire party every morning to practice working together before our expedition.

On our third day of practice, Hikurod dropped by for a visit out of the blue. “Hahaha! Long time no see, Ainar! Miss Raven!” The dwarf seemed to be visiting after hearing the news from Missha. We exchanged some conversation about current events. The construction to convert his home into a forge was already underway, and apparently he was busy recruiting a blacksmith these days.
“Oh, your wife runs a tavern? I’ll have to check it out later.”
“Yes, come and try the honey wine. My wife makes it herself, and it’s our shop’s unique delicacy.”
Since they both liked to drink, it seemed he and Mr. Bear would make surprisingly good friends. They weren’t going to become best friends later, were they?
Anyway, time marched on like that and the day arrived before I knew it.
“I should get ready.”
The labyrinth would open today.
“Bjorn, arrre you ready?”
“Oh, just a moment.” I put on my full armor for the first time in a while and lifted the backpack I had packed yesterday onto my shoulder.
Creak.
When I walked out the door, Missha and Ainar were waiting for me. “Have you forgotten anything?”
“No!” Ainar answered loudly.
Missha sighed from beside her. “She couldn’t be, anyway. Everrrything important is in my backpack.”
“I see.” This thought had been growing more and more pronounced recently, but I was glad I at least had Missha. This would have been more tiring if I were alone.
“Oh, Bjorn. Therrre’s something in your mailbox.”
“Huh?” Right when I was about to step away from the door, Missha pointed at the mailbox next to it. When I opened the box, there was a letter inside.
The sender is... Niall Urbans?
It was a letter from the district chief. Since when was this in my mailbox?
Rip.
I tore it open and read through the contents. Well, “through” may not have been the right word.
I will not ask you to pay the bill.

The letter was just one line. I could practically sense the district chief’s arrogance in it, but it was still a gesture of reconciliation. If he wanted to continue his war with me, he would’ve sent a fine or a bill with it.
It was a good idea to break the door.

Truthfully, when he had asked me what I wanted, I also had the option of asking for money. But I didn’t breathe a word of that and just busted the door down like a thug. That was because I wanted to get it through his head that if he did me wrong, he’d pay the price, and that price could not be paid with money.
Then it looks like I won’t have to worry about that now.

I had revealed that I had neither joined hands with his daughter nor had any intentions of doing so in the future. I also implied that if he was hostile toward me, there would be very annoying consequences. Getting back at me in a blind rage? It was safe to say that nothing like that would happen at least until the end of election season next year.
“What’s the letter about?” asked Missha.
“Oh, nothing to worry about.” I tore up the letter and threw it in the trash can on the first floor on my way out.
We headed to the meeting place, the central plaza of District Seven. As it was a location often used as a meeting place, it was crowded with adventurers waiting for their teammates.

“You’re one minute late.” As soon as we arrived at the alleyway on the right, Raven grinned at us. However, she didn’t seem bothered by our lateness. No, she looked to be enjoying it. “Come on, pay the fine. You promised, right?”
“Oh, yeah. The fine...” For reference, the fine was one of the thirty-one discussion topics she had raised at the second meeting. “How much was it, again?”
“One thousand stones per minute. Since there are three of you, that’ll be three thousand stones.”

I obediently opened my wallet and paid the fine for three people. If I hadn’t wasted time reading the letter, we wouldn’t have been late. “But Raven, where’s your bag?” I noticed while paying the fine that Raven wasn’t carrying anything on her back. When I asked about it, I got a strange response in return.
“Oh, that?” The corners of Raven’s mouth lifted and she tapped the ring on her index finger twice. It began to glow, and a small portal opened in the air.
“A subspace...?”
“Yes. I thought it might be necessary for the labyrinth. I sold all my unnecessary possessions and treated myself with that money.”
Right. Someone like you can treat yourself to things like this. A subspace, just for you.
Jingle.

Raven stored my payment in her subspace as if to flaunt it and then closed the portal. That made my heart burn a bit for some reason. Was this what some might call ‘feeling deprived’? And she was always whining about having no money... I thought she really didn’t have any.
“Anyway, Abman is rrrunning late.” While I was trying to shake off my envy, the topic of conversation changed.
“You’re right. He’s not going to ditch us, right?”
“I am not worried! He must have lost his way!”
Raven laughed like that was ridiculous. “How can a scout get lost?”
“Mmm, isn’t it possible? I hearrrd it’s a useless ability in the city.”
“But he lives near here.”
“That’s... definitely true. Then why is he late?”
“M-Maybe he has a stomachache?!”

The three women started chattering about Mr. Bear’s tardiness. I just stayed silent. The plan was to reveal Mr. Bear’s poor sense of direction inside the labyrinth. Anyway, after a long while, the crowded plaza quieted down.
Right when we started to sincerely worry, Mr. Bear showed up. “Sorry I’m late. Did you wait long?”
“Pay the fine first. You are exactly forty-five minutes late.”
“Oh, I forgot about that...” Thanks to the fine, Mr. Bear was robbed of forty-five thousand stones before even entering the labyrinth.
“But why are you late?”
“It’s the first time I’ve come here at night. My surroundings looked somewhat unfamiliar.”
“Pardon? What do you mean—”
“Okay, let’s go. We’ll be late.” I quickly interrupted and stopped the conversation there.

After Raven cast the binding spell, I led the group to Dimension Square. When we arrived, it was way past 12 a.m., and the portal was slowly decreasing in size. In just a little while, the timing would be right to use my experience points cheat, but...
I’ll decide whether or not to let them know about that after this expedition.
We pushed onward into the portal.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
The Crystal Cave was a much too familiar sight now. As soon as I opened my eyes, a shout from Ainar echoed and pounded against my eardrums. “Behelaaah!”
“Kyaaa! Y-You scared me! Why are you screaming all of a sudden?” Raven asked.
“I just felt like doing it!” Ainar answered.
Yes, I knew that feeling. I nodded in understanding. This was her first time back here after an entire six months. For Ainar, who was a born barbarian, that must have a special significance.
“Yeah, there really is another barrrbarian on the team...” While Missha glanced between me and Ainar and sighed, Mr. Bear was surprisingly nonchalant.
“It’s better than being quiet.” Since he’d been working alone for a long time, it seemed he didn’t hate our noisiness.
Anyway, enough chit-chat. “Abman, what’s closest?”
Mr. Bear pointed off into the distance at my question. When I checked it against my compass, it was south. In other words, our starting point this time was the ghoul zone.
Caught on the opposite side again.

“Since we’re going to the Goblin Forest, we can head this way instead. I’ll lead.” Mr. Bear put away his compass and led the way. I wondered if it would be better for me to just use his initial instructions and guide the party myself, but...
Well, I need to know how good he is.

Knowing how severe Mr. Bear’s poor sense of direction was would let me decide whether it could be corrected through effort or not. If there really was no other option, I was planning to just use Mr. Bear as a compass to find the way myself. I’d learned a few things from watching Rotmiller.

Anyway, heading north, we inevitably passed through the center of the first floor, a dark zone where four different types of monsters appeared together. Without needing to take out a torch, Raven lit up our surroundings with solar magic. “Leait.”
Whoom!
Unlike a torch’s gloomy red light, this spell lit up the area in pure white. I could comfortably see, like back in the city, but there was one concern.
“This is only the first floorrr—don’t you think it’s better to save your mana?”
“This much is fine. It charges pretty fast.”
“O-Oh... I-I see?”
“Yes. And don’t worry. Maintaining this won’t interfere with my ability to cast other spells.”
Soon, Missha clamped her mouth shut. She was clearly seeing the majesty of a real wizard, which Dwalkie had dejectedly described for us countless times in the past.
“It’s fascinating that your mana recharges so fast. The wizard I was with in the past wasn’t that skilled,” Mr. Bear said, stroking Raven’s ego.
“Ahem, I’m confident when it comes to mana, if I must say so myself. You’d be hard-pressed to find another wizard like me in the same class.”
“Oh, really? Well, now that I’ve seen this, I can tell you are a superb wizard.”
“I’m flattered. You’re also a rank-five adventurer and a scout, Mr. Urikfried.”
While the two of them were buttering each other up, a cavity with a radius of about thirty yards appeared in the cave.
“Ah, this is that Rift!”
“Ainar.”

When I tersely said her name, Ainar clasped her mouth shut with her hand. That made her look even more suspicious, but luckily everyone’s attention was focused on the monument in the center of the cavity.
“I’ve only heard about this before.” Like a typical wizard, Raven approached the monument with academic curiosity.
As a fifth-year adventurer, Missha also had some insight. “Is this it? The monument rrraised by the Immortal King, in honor of the arrrchmage who first discovered the labyrinth?”
“Yes. It is commonly known as such.”
“Commonly?”

“The theory going around in the academic world is that the archmage didn’t discover the labyrinth but created it. Oh, to put it simply... The theory is that the great sage did not create the portal by discovering coordinates to another dimension, but that they created the labyrinth dimension itself.”
Like the know-it-all she was, Raven’s explanation got longer. Ainar was not even listening and Missha just seemed to be going along with it, but I was curious. “Why do the wizards think that?”
“Because of this monument.”
“The monument?”

When I gave her a reaction, Raven immediately followed up with an explanation. “The labyrinth remains constant. Even if the terrain is destroyed, it will return to its original form the next time the portal opens. That is why there are theories out there that travel between the dimensions includes not only space but also time in its coordinates...”
“Ugh... my head...” Ainar moaned in pain after hearing so many complicated words in quick succession.

Raven pouted and gave a short summary. “This monument is proof that space-time magic was at least several times more developed back in the era when the labyrinth was first discovered than it is in the modern day. Space creation that is impossible now may have been possible then.”
Even the summary was long, but I got the gist of it. “I see.” To sum it up, wizards thousands of years ago were capable of casting dimensional magic.
I should look into the great sage.
Perhaps there was another way to return to Earth besides the Gate of the Abyss.
“Are you finished talking?” Mr. Bear had been standing off to the side until now like he was uninterested in this topic.
“Oh, yeah. Let’s go.”
At his urging, we resumed our expedition. Then—
“Oh, the monument!”

We ended up in the same location about fifteen minutes later. Despite the fact that I was watching him at work, I still couldn’t understand the method he was using to find the way. “How did this happen, Mr. Urikfried?”
“Oh, that was my mistake. I thought it would be faster to go that way...”
I immediately threw away my plans to develop Mr. Bear as a scout. This was not something that could be fixed.

chapters.title: Chapter 163: Exploration (2)
paragraphs: Arua Raven had shiny blonde hair and a short height, just over 4′9″. Add her scrawny body on top of that and she almost looked like a kid, but there was nothing scarier than this kid when she was mad.
Like right now. “Did you know about this, Mr. Yandel?”

“I didn’t know it was this bad.” When I answered honestly, the look in Raven’s eyes grew deadlier. However, I just scratched the nape of my neck like a barbarian. We were already inside the labyrinth. What was she going to do? “I will find the way from now on. Abman, just keep telling me where the portal is.”
“...All right.” It seemed Mr. Bear was also intimidated by Raven’s look because he handed me the steering wheel without argument.
Alright, what happened next was what was important.

“Ha, honestly...” Judging by her face, she seemed to realize that she had been scammed, but Raven decided to withhold her rant until she saw how this played out first. I had to show her clearly during this expedition that even if our scout had a poor sense of direction, it wouldn’t be detrimental to us. Before severe curse words flew out of that mouth.
“Then let’s go.”

Using Mr. Bear as a compass, I quickly found the way. I could feel Raven’s doubtful look burning into my back, but I wasn’t too worried. As long as you knew north from south and west from east, you could find your way to the second floor.

He said that taking the wider passageways at the crossroads will get you halfway there. And to avoid hilly places, as they are likely to be dead ends. And from the outskirts, always go toward the path with fewer crystals.

These were the various tips I had acquired from working beside Rotmiller, who was a completely self-taught scout. Using these, I limited wasteful travel such as turning back from dead ends to a minimum.
“Oh, we’re here fasterrr than I expected.”

As a result, we reached the outermost edges of the dark zone in short order. It was much easier from here on out. Normally we would locate the portal by searching our surroundings instead of using a compass.
“That way.”

However, we had a scout who could sense the location of a portal without any special instruments on our team. So, we just had to travel in that direction, and the end. Of course, the portal had been opened by another adventurer a long time ago.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
After reaching the second floor, Raven’s expression grew considerably less harsh. “Twelve hours to reach the second floor... Not bad.”
Okay, safe. Since we had set the time needed to clear the first floor to thirteen hours during the planning stage, there was nothing for her to complain about.

“No wonder you budgeted for such a long time even though there was a scout.” Raven eyed me like she had been suckered, but surprisingly, that was all. Was she okay with anything as long as the results were all right?
Reasonable.
To that end, I tried to make sure the plans we had made for the second floor did not go awry, although the constraints were tight. We wanted to clear it in twenty-four hours. “Abman, what direction?”
“That way.”

There were eight portal headstones in the Goblin Forest. However, once one opened, the rest simply turned to stone. Therefore, it was customary for teams that arrived later to just search for the portal by traveling around the outskirts. This apparently took two to three days on average, assuming there was no scout on the team.
If there is a scout, one day is enough since you don’t have to go in circles.
Without having to take out the compass, we headed straight for the opened portal.
“Raven, can you increase the number of light spheres?”
“Three is no problem.”

The absence of a professional scout was no problem, either. The fact that the area was covered in traps? As long as our surroundings were bright enough to look like broad daylight, this wasn’t even an issue. Goblins flocked toward the light, but now, even if dozens of goblins attacked at once, I could handle them on my own.
“Then let’s rest here for today.”
We set up camp around 9 p.m. at the outskirts of the Goblin Forest where hobgoblins started spawning.

“...Do all adventurers operate on such a rigorous schedule?” This must have been a pretty tough day for Raven, who had never been on a proper expedition, but a good biorhythm should be set on the first day while you still had stamina left.
“We will continue setting up camp around this time so things will go more smoothly from tomorrow on.”
“...Well, it is interesting being on a real expedition.”
“Stop talking and go to sleep. We still have to get moving tomorrow.”
“Okay. Wake me up if anything happens.” As was customary, Raven was excluded from the night watch. Just installing the alarm spell alone was considered one person’s share.
“Hey, Bjorn... About Ainar. Is it okay to leave herrr to do watch on her own?” Missha expressed some concerns about Ainar, who was taking watch after her.
I just smiled. “It’s okay. She won’t fall asleep or anything like that.”

Ainar was surprisingly reliable when it came to these things. She was untrusting of humans, and barbarians considered it shameful to fail to fulfill one’s duty. When we explored just the two of us, she kept watch well enough, and our night watch back then had been four hours long and more tiring thanks to the fact that we couldn’t sleep much.
“Oh, I see... I guess I was a bit biased.”
After eight hours of camping outside and switching which of the four of us was on watch every two hours, we resumed our expedition early in the morning. Before the afternoon, we found the portal.
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]

After reaching the third floor, the quest went smoothly. The battles were too easy to be considered combat practice, and finding the way wasn’t a problem. Mr. Bear didn’t get lost like on the first floor or in the city now that there were no roads.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – The Witch’s Forest has activated.]

The Witch’s Forest, which I was worried about, was the same as usual. After connecting ourselves with rope like a bunch of fish out to dry, Mr. Bear led the way while the rest of us followed, and we easily cleared it. A while later...
“Oh, it’s a tower! Bjorn! There really was a tower in the middle of the forest!”
“Haha, I told you. There arrre many fascinating things in the labyrinth.”
“Behelaaah!”
“...You just felt like screaming, huh?”
We were in front of the fourth-floor portal and it was only the afternoon of the eighth day.
Our speed is almost the same as with Rotmiller.
While that fact was satisfying in some ways, it was also bittersweet. Was it impossible for hard work to trump talent after all?
“Mr. Yandel, what are you thinking about?” asked Raven.
“Oh, it’s nothing.”
“Th-then, can we go in already? My stomach is churning from the ominous mana this entire forest is emanating.”
Was it because of her innate mana sensitivity? Raven may not have vomited, but her nausea was much worse than Dwalkie’s had been. I wanted to fix that for her as well, but not yet.
“Just wait a little longer. We can only enter after the color of the portal changes.”
“Oh, right. I’ve heard about this. It’s because there might be another team already inside, right?”

“If we don’t wait, we might get mistaken for plunderers and attacked.” After I gave her a reasonable explanation, Raven waited patiently. Before long, the color of the portal changed. “Okay then, let’s head in.”
Now it was time for the actual climbing.
[You have entered the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.]

The Tower of Heavens was a unique floor where random combinations of monsters appeared at each stage. Since this place was commonly referred to as the Tower of Training, I had planned to properly calibrate our teamwork here.
But it would be pointless with this much of a difference in power.

After our first battle, I realized that this party’s combat power was in a whole different league from Team Half-Wit, to the point that it would be impossible to use our maximum strength on the fourth floor.
[You have cast Giantization.]

Thanks to Union, my mace greatly increased not only in size but also in performance. With the attack skill Swing added to that, a rank-seven monster really just felt like a goblin. And the key here was that there was a separate major damage dealer.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Hazardous Material.]
Rank-five archer Mr. Bear’s powerful damage went beyond just a one-shot kill and completely wiped out the surrounding area, along with his high-rank tank of a summon, Iron Bear.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-six attack spell Fire Baptism.]

This was how crazy useful it was to have an experienced wizard like Raven, who of course possessed attack magic from each of the four major elements as well as more than a hundred curse and support spells.
Yes, there should definitely be three people who can carry the team.
The quality of the party had risen dramatically. No matter what bizarre combination spawned, as long as the monsters were under rank six, we could clear them out in under three minutes.
They may be lacking compared to the three of us, but Ainar and Missha are also pulling their weight... As expected, the fifth floor should be fine even in this state.

Therefore, rather than coordinating our moves through practice, we focused only on climbing the Tower of Heavens. However, our time did not improve as I had predicted. The reason for that was simple. The speed with which we fought was incomparable to Team Half-Wit’s, but our team didn’t have a professional scout.
Everything is good, but it’s a pity it takes so long to clear the Stairway of Wisdom.

The Stairway of Wisdom was a kind of shortcut. Instead of having to go through a maze full of traps and monsters, it let you skip five floors at a time. Not only that, but unlike the Stairway of Courage, there was no forced cooldown of four hours before taking the next set of stairs. It took Rotmiller about one hour to clear Wisdom. Just now, it took us almost five times that.
“Bjorn, can’t we just fight monsters?”

I was just as frustrated as Ainar, but there was no choice. It would take more than sixteen days to reach floor one hundred with just Courage. Getting through the fourth floor before the labyrinth closed would be impossible.
“It’s already late today. Let’s rest and climb the rest tomorrow.”

We’d only managed to clear one ordeal of Wisdom since entering the Tower, yet it was already past 10 p.m. so we prepared camp. Of course, this camp was quite different than usual. Without needing to set up a watch, everyone just spread out their sleeping bags where they wanted to and that was all.
“No night watch in the labyrinth! Missha, my head is spinning right now!”
“Haha, I know how you feel. The firrrst time I came here, I couldn’t get used to it and couldn’t sleep well—”
Hooonk!
“Hey, I’m talking to you!”

Ainar passed out as soon as she laid down on her sleeping bag. Missha looked at her and sighed before wiping herself off with a wet towel to get ready to sleep. “Bjorrrn, why do you keep glancing this way?”
“I’m not.”
“Now, now. Turn your head. We’re teammates! There’s no point in having rrregrets now.”
I’m telling you, I didn’t look.
I just sighed and focused on wiping the blood off my mace. But I guess she wasn’t pleased with that, either. “Tsk.” Missha clicked her tongue deliberately for me to hear.

This was a change that had occurred after she moved into my inn. Despite saying that she wanted to forget that day ever happened, she kept jokingly bringing it up more often. Well, I had no complaints about that.
Maybe it’s better this way.

Missha revealed her feelings to me and I firmly drew the line. No matter how much we wanted to pretend it didn’t happen, that was impossible. That was probably why she had decided to do this. It was much less awkward this way, rather than being overly conscious of it and careful with our words all the time.
“Then I’m going to sleep firrrst.”
“Sure.”
Soon, Missha got into her sleeping bag and closed her eyes. I could see Mr. Bear had set up his sleeping bag in a corner and was getting ready to go to sleep.
Hooonk!
While I was fixing up my equipment, I grabbed Ainar’s greatsword and quickly wiped it down too. That was when Raven quietly came up to me. “Do you have something to say?”
“Yes.”
“Say it.”
“I’ve done some calculations, and at our current speed, we won’t have long even when we reach the fifth floor.”
So you calculated that, huh? Oh, you wizards.
Of course, it was not that I couldn’t understand her concerns. The more time we wasted here, the less time we’d have on the fifth floor.
“And our profit will be that much lower than other teams’.”
“...This is our first expedition. It may take long now because we don’t have a professional scout, but we’ll get faster and faster.”
“If you say so.”

After that, Raven didn’t say anything else and returned to her sleeping bag. This was not because she had fully accepted my assurances, though. If it continued to take us more than five hours to get through the Stairway of Wisdom, she’d come to find me again with extreme solutions.
Whatever, time for sleep.
I set down the well-polished greatsword next to Ainar and lay down in my sleeping bag. After a bit of shut-eye, I woke up to the sound of Raven’s voice ringing in my head.
“Mr. Yandel, just listen.”
This was a spell called Secret Voice. What reason did she have to use magic to wake me up?
“I cast a detection spell while washing up because I sensed something was off and... There’s someone else besides us here. So, do not move.”
It turned out the reason was quite straightforward. I was honestly not sure how she could say all of this so calmly.
“They are right behind me.”
One wrong move and our wizard was going to die.

chapters.title: Chapter 164: Exploration (3)
