paragraphs: My just-woken mind froze, stone cold. It was a similar principle to a cooling fan that ran before any work that would severely overheat the computer.
So there’s a rat...

My heart started to pound at a low, steady rhythm and my thoughts accelerated. The Tower of Heavens was an independent floor. Once the color of the portal changed, it was impossible for anyone to follow. No item or cheat code could get around this, to my knowledge.
Did they enter before the color of the portal changed?

The bastard had entered with us from the beginning. Of course, we had also waited to make sure no one followed behind us to be safe, and ran a detection spell in case of a stealth ability before departing.
If they have a stealth ability that’s rank two or higher, it’s possible we didn’t detect them. Ordinary magic can’t detect things like that.

Of course, that was just the worst-case scenario. It was unlikely that this guy was really a giant with a rank-two essence. In the end, even they got caught with detection magic. It would be more plausible to assume they had avoided our detection spell immediately upon entry using an item or skill.
The fact that they’ve just been following us all the way here probably means they’re not confident in combat.
Okay, suddenly my courage revived. Given how Raven was calmly briefing me on the situation, she didn’t seem too frightened, either. Now. How should we solve this problem?
“I don’t think they’ll hurt me right away. So think carefully about what move you’ll make. My life is in your hand—”
The answer came to me quickly. “Behelahhh!” I called out the name of my ancestral god, quickly got up, and ran straight to Raven.
“You deranged—!”

Raven screamed right into my head out of shock, but this was the best option. Doing something stupid that would end up with her getting taken hostage would cause a real headache. Plus, they didn’t know that we’d noticed. By nature, humans were incapable of making rational decisions when they were really surprised.

“Raven! Are you okay!? You appeared in my dream!” Tossing out a possible explanation to make them think even for a second that they hadn’t been caught, I ran. Let them get their hopes up. Of course, I couldn’t be certain what kind of decision the bastard would make in that short moment.
“Kyaa!”
Thankfully, they did not drop their concealment by the time I reached Raven.
“What is going on!? Is it an enemy!?”
“What... I was having a good rest.”

The trio woke up in shock at the nighttime commotion, the second effect I was hoping for while shouting for my ancestral god. This made it possible for all of us to be prepared even if the rat ambushed another teammate or tried to take them hostage.

But had she heard my shout in its entirety even in her sleep? Missha met my eyes and lowered her head like someone who had been hit in the heart by an arrow. “Appeared in your dream... s-so the two of you are that close, huh? I-I didn’t know. Yeah... I didn’t know, and I... haha, hah, ha...”
What was this kid saying? Without any preamble, I just yelled, “Prepare for battle! There’s a rat in here!”

For adventurers, the sentence, “Prepare for battle” was absolute. On a well-conditioned reflex, the trio immediately drew their weapons and gathered in a tight formation to stay alert to their surroundings. I quickly moved around them.
“Bjorn, a rat? Do rats come out on the fourth floor?”
“...What I mean is that there is an adventurer hiding among us.”
“I-I see? I was scared it was a real rat!”
Shouldn’t you be more scared about the other thing?
There were many things I wanted to say, but I held back. That was not what I should be doing right now. “Raven, where are they?”
“Th-they’re gone. I can’t sense them with detection magic.”
Yes, so you’re on detection null mode again.
I didn’t know if it was an item or a skill, but if it was an active ability rather than a passive one, there had to be a limit to how long they could use it.

“Keep casting the detection spell until they appear.” I sent Raven behind me and gave out orders. “The rat has a stealth ability, so pay attention. They’ll definitely show themselves when they attack.”
Finally grasping the situation, our party members stood on alert, with serious looks on their faces. Things continued on like that in silence for several minutes.

The bastard still hadn’t shown up, but I was sure they were not planning to hold out forever. They probably just needed time to figure out what to do, although they wouldn’t be able to come up with anything.
“Mr. Yandel...”
“Don’t be nervous. Time is on our side.”
In a stone chamber with all four doors firmly closed, there was nowhere to run. Having the Stairway of Destiny available could change up the situation, but that wasn’t the case either.
“Just come out. I will kill you painlessly,” I muttered into the void.
“I found them!”
“Where?”
“By the door over there!”
So that’s where you were.
“Can the effect be lifted?”
“Since I’ve identified the target, it’s possible.”
“How long will it take?”
Raven didn’t answer. She just extended the wand in her hand.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-eight support spell Track Down.]
The jewel embedded at the end of her wand started glowing.
Shaaa!

A cloud of blue light appeared, clung to something transparent, and formed the shape of a person. When the cluster of light disappeared, the figure of the hiding bastard was finally revealed—a masked assailant dressed in a tight, dark suit.
“Looks just like a rat. Behelahhh!”
The moment our eyes met, I kicked off the ground and dashed forward.
Rattle.
Apparently making up their mind, the rat slammed the door open and climbed the stairs.
“Bjorn! They’rrre getting away!”
“Don’t panic and pack your things for now.”

Instead of chasing after them right away, I took care of our stuff scattered on the floor. If there was no one left here, the door would close, and then we wouldn’t be able to come grab our things again.
Well, there is the option to leave one person here, but is that necessary?
There was no need to rush. The door the rat had opened was the Stairway of Courage. Until we all went up, no monsters would appear. In other words, they were a rat trapped in a cage.
“I got everything.”
“Then let’s go.”

I stuffed everything including my sleeping bag into my backpack and pursued them. When all of us entered, the stone door closed with a bang. I climbed the stairs in the lead with my shield protecting my torso.
Judging by the look in their eyes earlier, I don’t think they chose just any random door.

I was a little nervous. What were they after? Since I had no clues at the moment, I kept my guard up even higher as I ascended. Soon, the stairs ended. Beyond the open door, I could see the next floor, empty. Well, maybe empty was not the right word.
Welp, I didn’t expect this...
In the center of a stone chamber of about five square miles, a corpse was melting.
Bang!
Once everyone in the party entered the chamber, the door closed and a group of monsters appeared.
“Nothing showing up on the detection spell?”
“No.”
“Fight assuming that the rat is hiding nearby.”
For now, we maintained a defensive formation and cleared out the monsters. This all took about six minutes. When the battle was over, all eyes naturally turned to one place.
“Bjorn, that corpse...” Missha trailed off. I thought I knew what she was trying to say, so there was no problem. She was asking if it was real.
I called on the expert. “Raven?”
“It’s not fake. I can feel the remnants of mana.”
“Simpler.”
“It means they just died.”
“Could it—”
“It can’t be someone else, either. It’s faint, but the wavelengths of the mana match perfectly.”
...So it is. Goddamn it.

The rat committed suicide before we could even have a proper conversation. That made me uncomfortable. It was like how in a novel, the members of a secret society would take poison before being captured.
It’s my first time experiencing this, so I didn’t even think of it.

I’d met a lot of scum in the past, but they had all wanted to live until the bitter end. This was my first time seeing one run straight off and kill themselves. It was not like we’d had a proper fight, either.
“...We should check it out first.”

I slowly approached the body and removed the mask. However, neither gender nor race could be determined by their features. All the muscles on their face had melted and flowed down the bone like an egg yolk.
“Mr. Yandel, maybe you should remove their clothes just in case.”
As instructed by the wizard, I stripped the clothes off the corpse. Then an even worse scene than before unfolded.

“Like I thought, their whole body melted. It’s not acidic, either. Their clothes are intact...” Raven approached without hesitation and poked the corpse with an iron stick here and there to take a look. “The bones are still attached. No abnormalities in the hair, either. Looks like it’s a substance that only breaks down proteins...”
Watching her handle the corpse without batting an eye, I couldn’t help but ask, “Are you okay?”
“Pardon? With what?”
“Didn’t you vomit when you saw the Corpse Golem—”
“Ahh! That’s because the smell of rot hit me mid-cast. I’ve seen worse things during experiments, so this much is nothing.”
“...I see.” Her personality was very different from her appearance.
Even the ten-year veteran adventurer Mr. Bear had to turn his head. “Yandel, are you sure they’re dead?”
“It looks that way for now.”
“Then I’m going to take a break over there. Cheese is my favorite food.”
“Cheese?”
“If I look any longer, I don’t think I’ll be able to eat cheese ever again.”
That was a rather valid reason so I told him to do that. Then Ainar and Missha left for similar reasons.
“Ch-cheese? I don’t know what that is, but it’s probably delicious.”
“Bjorn? I don’t think I’ll be much help eitherrr...”
Yes, there was no reason for all of us to go through the trouble. “You both go and rest.” I focused on my conversation with Raven. “Is it poison?”
“Yes. I don’t know which alchemist made it, but it’s a very unusual poison. The components of the potion are released through the sweat glands as soon as it’s consumed and it melts the skin.”
“Perfect to commit suicide.”
“That’s right. Especially if you have to hide your identity.”
The feeling of discomfort grew. Who the hell was this bastard? They didn’t seem like a regular plunderer at a glance.
Click.
I took off the gear they were wearing. It was loot, but I thought that it might be able to help me infer their identity as well. “There’s no identity card.”
“...That’s strange.”
It wasn’t just strange. Without an identity card, you could not pass through the checkpoint back in the city.
Were they sent by the Dragon Slayer?

If this person were from the underground city, it would make sense that they didn’t have an identity card. With that thought in mind, I rummaged through their expandable bag. The items I managed to produce weren’t many—just some exploration supplies and food.

“Wow, this guy must be an expert. There’s everything from sleeping plants to basilisk paralysis poison.” The rest were all consumables for battles against other people. Among them were items rare enough for even Raven to covet.
This bastard really planned to kill someone.

Although I hadn’t exchanged a single word with this masked person, the thought gave me chills. It was a wicked plundering method to use the distinct characteristics of the fourth floor. If it weren’t for Raven, this situation could have ended with us in big trouble.
“But what were you doing at that time?”
“...I was cleaning myself off.”
Oh, that’s right. “Why didn’t you do it while everyone was awake?”
“...Excuse me, this is only my second time in the labyrinth. It hasn’t even been a month since I met Mr. Urikfried.”

Right, this was still an adjustment period for her. Since she was so on the ball, I hadn’t even thought about it. Anyway, Raven finally realized how she looked right now in her thin dress. She frowned and took clothes out of her subspace to put on.
“Tell me next time. I’ll pitch you a tent or something.”
“It’s fine. I’m an adventurer now. I don’t plan to make a fuss about something like that.”
“If you say so.”

Afterward, I exchanged a few more words with Raven while examining the corpse, but nothing much came out of it. After covering the masked person who had been turned into pudding with a cloth, we gathered in a corner and all went to sleep.

Of course, we decided to take turns on watch just in case. The first watch was mine. As I was reviewing what had happened today in the silence, I heard a groan from Raven’s sleeping bag. Was she having a nightmare? I was wondering if I should wake her up when Raven slowly opened her eyes.
“...Mr. Yandel.”
“Are you awake? Don’t worry and go back to sleep. I’ll guard the area.”
“It’s not that. I want to ask you something.” When I told her to go ahead, Raven paused before finally blurting, “If I hadn’t used the detection spell back then, what would have happened?”

Her tone was completely different from her usual dignified one. Then I realized that no matter how calm she acted and how well she appeared to control her emotions, there was no way she wouldn’t be shocked by something like that.
“You want an honest answer?”
“Yes.”
“If we were unlucky, we all would have died. If we were lucky, it would’ve ended with one or two of us dead.”
There was a moment of silence. “Is... exploring the labyrinth always like this?”
I smiled bitterly and nodded. “Yeah.”
Not knowing when or where you’d meet a scoundrel, the fact that your life could disappear at any moment, that was adventuring.
“Don’t worry, though. It’s not always difficult and terrible things.”

I didn’t know if it would comfort her, but I told her about Team Half-Wit: how Dwalkie had been discouraged after running into a plunderer for the first time, and the beautiful scenery Rotmiller had shown us on the third floor to cheer him up.

“My seniors told me that that’s a meaningless phenomenon caused by mana supersaturation,” Raven whispered, chuckling. I wondered if this was how traditional wizards saw the world. “Still, I hope I see it next time.”
“Okay, next time I’ll wake you up before twelve.”
It wasn’t long before I could hear the sound of easy breathing from Raven’s sleeping bag. That was how the eighth day came to an end.

chapters.title: Chapter 165: Exploration (4)
paragraphs: An expandable backpack worth a substantial two million stones, an iron dagger and other miscellaneous equipment, a bundle of consumables more effective against humans than monsters, and a spoonful of discomfort that settled in my stomach like a stone—these were the things the masked stranger had left behind for us.
“I wonder what kind of person they were.”
“No matter how I think about it, I don’t think they were an ordinary plundererrr. They were all alone, and the way they died is also...”

When the situation had taken a turn for the worse, the person in the mask committed suicide. This was far from normal. However, the truth had already been buried in the darkness. “Don’t worry about it anymore. There’s nothing more we can learn now.” We had no other option but to take what we needed and move on. That was how adventurers were.
“Bjorn. How many cotton candies is this?” Ainar asked, practically salivating.
Before I could answer, Raven said, “Altogether, this will be about 3.5 million stones.”
“...You have expertise in this area too?”
“Obviously you’d have to sell it to know for sure, but the margin of error won’t be very big. I got a certification as a regular appraiser in the past.”
So that’s a thing, huh?

When asked for more detail, Raven explained that a regular appraiser was different from a special appraiser. Apparently, you could only be certified based on pure knowledge and not skill. “You should study for it later when you have time, Mr. Yandel. If you just show people this, you won’t have to needlessly bargain and intimidate them. Trading broker licenses may be difficult to obtain, but—”
“It’s okay. I’m good at intimidating people.” I cut off her words before she could follow them up with more self-praise and resumed the quest.

Our progression was not much different from Team Half-Wit’s. Choosing the Stairways of Wisdom as our first priority and the Stairways of Courage as our second, we focused solely on climbing the Tower.
“...Ugh, are we wanderrring the maze all day again?”
“We have no choice since we don’t have a professional scout.”
Each time we took the Stairway of Wisdom, it was a lot of work trying to find the way, but I had to give my all to do so. I had a mother-in-law right next to me.
“Four hours and thirty-four minutes... Four hours and eleven minutes... Three hours and fifty-nine minutes.”

Each time we got out of a maze, Raven reported the time. Thankfully, the higher we climbed, the more the duration decreased. It was thanks to the know-how I acquired from acting as a half-scout. I had a long way to go to catch up to Rotmiller, though.
“Four hours and thirty-five minutes. It increased a lot this time.”
“That’s because Ainar stepped on a trap.”
“Considered.”
Days passed quickly. From the twelfth day on, we all slept without anyone on watch duty.
“Are we going to set a night watch today too?”
“...It seems like a waste.”

“Whew, this is all because of that bastarrrd. Isn’t this crossing the line? Ambushing us here of all places...” Missha was angry as if her sanctuary had been invaded. Actually, I felt similarly. This was the one and only place where I could rest in peace.
Goddamn it.
Despite these and other happenings, our expedition went smoothly and by day sixteen, we reached floor one hundred. From there, we could search for the portal to the fifth floor.

“Two hours and forty-one minutes... It’s gotten really quick.” Even Raven, who had been acting like a mother-in-law every day, now had a satisfied smile on her face. For reference, the same went for me.
Could it be that I’m in fact a gifted scout?

Even fighting tooth and nail, the three-hour wall was hard to penetrate. However, I was able to shorten our record after coming to one key realization: destroying the traps was easier and faster than solving them.
“Ah, Mr. Yandel. How long did you say it took to get here when you had a professional scout on your team?”
“It took about twelve days.”
“Four days’ difference is not bad, considering the fifth floor will be much more comfortable without a scout.”
I agreed. Although we had lost four days due to the absence of a scout, our party was, as a result, composed of all combat characters. We just had to make up for the lost time in battle.
But jeez, can’t you just give a compliment?

Such feelings of dissatisfaction lingered within me. Missha came over and patted me on the shoulder. “Good work, Bjorn. I really didn’t know things would turn out like this. We’re prrrobably the only team with a barbarian scout.”
You’re the only one I can rely on, after all...

“Ahem.” Mr. Bear cleared his throat at Missha’s words and stepped forward. I guess he was somewhat embarrassed about entrusting the role of scout to a barbarian when he was one himself. “Looks like it’s time for me to step up.”
I obediently handed over the steering wheel. This was because the doors had to be opened in the correct order to reach the fifth floor. “Which door should I open?”
“That one.”

This was why scouts were such OP characters. Even if their sensory stats did not exceed a certain level, they could recognize the mana of the portal with just natural talent. Like that, we used Mr. Bear as a compass and advanced toward the portal that was hiding somewhere in the Tower.
[You have chosen the Stairway of Courage.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Courage.]
The process of opening a door and clearing the corresponding ordeal was repeated over and over. After spending another night there, we resumed our expedition and opened ten more doors.
“Finally, the last door.”
We had reached the floor with the portal. It was already nearing the end of day seventeen. Soon it would be time to set up camp, so part of me wanted to take a break and open the door tomorrow.
“I think I can concentrate better now.”

However, considering the fact that Raven was vulnerable in the morning, we decided to proceed today. The portal room was a boss room too. The better the wizard’s condition, the better it was for all of us.
“As I said before, there is most definitely a rank-five monster here.”

“Like that vampire monster.” Ainar gripped her greatsword with eyes full of excitement and anticipation. It seemed she wanted to confirm how much she had changed from how helpless she had been in the past.
Heh.

I couldn’t help smiling. Don’t lose concentration. The survival rate of potential graduates who reach this point is less than 50 percent. This was what I originally planned to say, but it didn’t really mean much.
“Um, why did you stop talking?” asked Raven.
Besides, it wouldn’t even be barbarian-like. “I forgot.”
“Sorry?”
“Let’s go kill ‘em.”

I opened the door, climbed the stairs, and headed to the next level, a stone chamber with a familiar headstone embedded in the center. Once all five of us entered, the door closed and monsters appeared.
“Gaaah!”
That made me laugh. I had wondered which bastard would come out.
“It’s a Troll!”

Yes, nothing like a Troll to make it a real graduation ceremony—the bastard that had made me break my keyboard one year into Dungeon and Stone and the same one that had driven Team Half-Wit to the brink of near annihilation.
“Should I start with distortion magic? I heard that Troll remains are very expensive.”
Wow, this kid was bold, even though rank-five Fear was quite strong. “It’s fine. The essence is just as expensive.”
“If you say so.”
As I was exchanging brief words with Raven, the Troll let out a scream and extended its foot forward.
Boom!
I also kicked off the ground to play the role of a tank.
[You have cast Giantization.]
The difference in our weight classes narrowed in an instant. When the physical distance between us decreased as well, the Troll swung its huge fist.
Bang!
A heavy shock jolted through my giant shield, but having consumed the Ogre essence, it was low-res.
The shield is still intact too.

The lithinum shield that used to dent with each punch did not budge this time thanks to the effect of my level-six Imprint, Union. Now, the performance of the equipment I wore would be enhanced in proportion to the sum of my stats. Yes, this was the perk I had spent all that money for!
“Behelahhh!”
After blowing up my stats with Wild Outburst, I brought down the mace with all my might.
[You have cast Swing. The destructive force of any blunt weapons you use will increase significantly in proportion to your muscle strength.]
My target was the head. However, the bastard twisted its body so my giant mace ended up slamming it in the shoulder.
Crunch!
The deformed shoulder dropped with an audible crack. It was dislocated in just one shot. In the past, it used to take at least six blows just to break through the flesh and get to the joint.
“Gaah!”
Of course, as befit a Troll’s healing factor, the bones reattached themselves within seconds. However, that had been enough to measure my combat power.
Let’s take a look.

I focused on defense and observed my teammates. First the original member, Missha. She hadn’t absorbed a new essence since our time with Team Half-Wit, but her swinging sword sliced through the Troll’s skin all too easily.
Slice!
This was the power of money. That was a longsword made of Iril that cost a whopping twelve million stones. If it hadn’t been able to do that much, we would’ve had to demand a refund.
“Behelahhh!” Ainar shouted. She immediately joined the ranks wielding her greatsword, probably jealous of Missha, who had gotten to play an active role first.
Whoom!
A powerful gust of wind followed the sword’s trajectory through the air, leaving an afterimage. Ah, maybe afterimage wasn’t the right word.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Repeated Slash.]
This was the active skill of the rank-four essence she had inherited from the elder. The effect was simple: one cut did the same damage as two.
Slice! Slice!

Of course, this meant nothing against a Troll. Even though the weight of the greatsword had been coupled with superior strength, the sword only dug in about an inch. This was because Ainar’s skill was Repeated Slash, one difficult to perform well with a normal hit.

“This guy’s skin is tough... ahh!” Taking the Troll’s fist, Ainar fell backward. She got up quickly but blood dripped from her mouth. It seemed she had organ damage. “Behelahhh!” Instead of taking a potion and resting in the back, Ainar clung to the Troll again and swung her greatsword. This was a rational decision rather than stubbornness. This time, the greatsword glowed with a red light—the active skill of the Bone Knight’s essence that she had earned at the Bloody Citadel.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Vitality Absorption. If damage is inflicted on a living creature, your healing factor temporarily increases.]

When Ainar struck an enemy, her blood replenished, a great quality to have as a backup tank. By using Repeated Slash together with Vitality Absorption, Ainar returned to her original state in just a few strokes.
Her ability to deal damage is lower than Missha’s, but her tanking is much better.
While observing both of their battles for a while, I checked up on their pros, cons, and areas of improvement for the future.
Ainar needs a good attack skill soon. Missha needs to consume more Beast Blood to bring up the level of her Soul Beast.
With that in mind, I was half-heartedly dealing with the Troll. Mr. Bear spoke up from behind me. “Can we join now?”
“Ah, were you waiting for them?”
“I was curious to see how well those two ladies would fight.”
“I am not a lady!”
Ignoring Ainar’s shout and with my permission, Mr. Bear joined the battle.
[Abman Urikfried has summoned the Iron Bear, Iradun.]
However, did he determine that the frontline was already overpowered? Mr. Bear sent the Soul Beast to the back to serve as a bodyguard and started firing his crossbow.
Shoop! Shoop! Shoop!

Each time an arrow was shot, it released a huge whipping sound and pierced deeply into the Troll’s body. I could tell how experienced he was from the locations of the direct hits. His attack strategy was to restrict the Troll’s movements by driving arrows into joints such as elbows and knees.
Slice!
Missha and Ainar worked together to cut off the Troll’s arm and start the Super Regeneration pattern. Raven had already cast an Aggravate spell, so its healing factor was slow.
Nothing left to see now.
Just when I was about to crush the Troll’s head with my mace, Mr. Bear stopped me. “Stop! The third lady should also play an active role.”

“...Could you not call me a lady, please?” Soon, Raven grunted and waved her wand. She didn’t even warn us to stand out of the way like Dwalkie used to. Rather than being inconsiderate, though, it was more that she’d figured there was no need for that.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-five attack spell Thunder Spear.]
Zig-zagging to avoid us, white lightning shot forward. Everything flashed white. Then came the sound.
Bang, bang, bang!
By the time I processed what was happening, the Troll’s head was already blown off.
Slump.
The Troll collapsed to the floor and disappeared into a glimmering light on the spot. Of course, there was once again no essence.
We had killed a Troll, and it was as easy as toying with it. Of course, that didn’t mean the fifth floor wouldn’t have dangers, since several rank-five monsters could appear together there.
Whooom!

A portal opened when the Troll died. However, we did not go up to the fifth floor right away and camped out instead. Even if we went up now, it’d be time to sleep, so it would be better to get at least one more comfortable night.
Is this finally the beginning?
After tossing and turning for a while with anxiety and anticipation, I fell asleep. The next morning, around 7 a.m. on the eighteenth day, we finished packing and entered the portal.
“Wow, I’m really going to the fifth floorrr...”
[You have entered the Great Demon Realm on the fifth floor.]
With this, I’d graduated from the first half of the game. It was time for some real adventuring.

chapters.title: Chapter 166: Great Demon Realm (1)
paragraphs: The fifth floor, the Great Demon Realm, was where you slowly reached the limits of what a team could accomplish and where clan-scale hunting began to become a better alternative. As soon as I set foot there, my heart pounded, not metaphorically but literally.
“Huh? Bjorn, did you feel that too? I think my Dignity of Soul has gone up!” Ainar immediately grew animated, but it wasn’t a level-up, just an increase in Soul Power.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Reach the fifth floor.]
[Reward: Your Soul Power has permanently increased by +20.]

Did this mean all the achievements we had accrued until now had been exceeded? It seemed likely, but I couldn’t be sure. Well, it wasn’t like I could see the status window, nor was Soul Power a stat that you could feel.

Anyway, Raven, who liked to explain things, kindly explained what was going on to Ainar while making it easy enough for her to understand. “Calm down, Miss Ainar. It’s not a promotion but a phenomenon called Baptism, a blessing bestowed by the labyrinth on adventurers who reach this point. Or, that’s how most people think Baptism works. Wizards think differently, though.”
“Oh, I see! That’s kind of romantic!” Ainar, who had a fondness for superstitious things, didn’t ask a single question about what the wizards thought.
However, Missha started to have questions of her own. “Isn’t Baptism meaningless to wizarrrds since they can’t consume an essence?”
“No. Our mana increases instead. Now that I’m experiencing it, the amount is quite significant. If I knew this was the case, I would’ve listened to other people’s advice and come here sooner.”
“Oh, I see...” Missha trailed off, but somehow, I felt like I knew what she was thinking. She must have been reminded of Dwalkie, who had always lacked mana.
“Oh, I heard priests gain more divine power. And to add one more thing—”
I cut her off before the explanation became never-ending. “But doesn’t something seem strange?”
“Sorry?” Raven cocked her head like she didn’t understand what I meant.
On the other hand, Mr. Bear, who had often been to the fifth floor, nodded in agreement. “There are a lot of people. It’s not usually like this.”
Right, so this wasn’t common, then. I took a look around and gulped. The starting point of the fifth floor’s Great Demon Realm was a safe zone, which was why this place always looked like a campsite.
But why are there so many tents?
At this point, the camping grounds were the size of a village. Not only that, but as I looked at the flags planted near some of the tents, more than half of them were adventurers belonging to a clan.
What is this? Why are they staying here?

Usually, most of the adventurers who used this place as a base traveled in parties. It was kind of a necessity for them. But clans with a large number of people could camp out on their own even in the middle of the fifth floor just fine.
“Bjorn, it seems everrryone is staring at us... Is everything all right?”

Fifth-floor adventurers, those skilled enough to belong to a clan, were watching us from afar and whispering amongst themselves. It couldn’t just be because they were being cold to rookies. Really, what the hell was this? I was trying to figure it out when...
“Oi!” A man in the distance waved his hand and quickly approached us. “Abman! That’s you, right?”
“...Karal?”
“Nice to see you. I see you finally changed your mind and found yourself a party?”
“It just so happens that’s the case. And you? Are you still working there?”
“A man has nothing without loyalty, right? I need to devote myself.”

Mr. Bear greeted the man, who seemed to be on quite friendly terms with him. Soon, he noticed my stare and explained, “Ah, this is Karal Larveger. He was a colleague of mine until he abandoned me and joined a clan on his own.”
“Abandoned you? I begged you to come with me, but you ignored me.” Seeing how Mr. Bear spoke in a lighter tone with him than with us, it seemed they were pretty close. That was good.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

“...Ohhh, are you?” I guess he’d heard of my title Little Balkan because he looked intrigued. “I heard it hasn’t yet been a full year for you, but you’re already here. I’m starting to feel a little shabby.”
“I was just lucky. But there’s one thing I want to ask you.”
“I think I know what you’re curious about. You want to know why we’re still here when we should be heading up.”
Well, to be more accurate, I was curious why they were giving us the stare-down. But I nodded for now.
“It’s simple. More than half of the people who were supposed to join us didn’t make it. Our schedule has been... interrupted.”
Half didn’t make it up? How could that be? I intuitively sensed the seriousness of the situation.
“So, I want to ask,” Karal began cautiously before saying something completely unexpected. “Were you guys attacked on the fourth floor too?”
That masked bastard... They weren’t just after us.

After thinking over it for a second, I replied honestly that we had been attacked. Karal asked a few questions about what had happened and we answered truthfully to earn the necessary information in return.
“Right, so you noticed them through a detection spell...”
“It was purely coincidental. When I first used the detection spell, nothing showed up.”
Afterward, when we told him that the masked assailant had committed suicide when they were caught, Karal’s face hardened. “Ha, suicide, huh?”
“Do you have any idea who it could be?”
“Only that it was thoroughly planned out. Anyway, thanks for telling me. If I learn anything... I will deliver the news through Abman.” Soon after, Karal left to report the news to his clan.
We also took time to debrief a bit. “...So it wasn’t a simple plunderer after all.”

There was more than one masked assailant, and they had all committed acts of terror against the adventurers on the fourth floor without discrimination. Apparently, we were the third team to survive the ambush and come up. I could understand why. No one set up a night watch in the Tower of Heavens.
“So we were rrreally lucky...”

Apparently, those who survived just barely managed to get rid of their assailants after the death or serious injury of a teammate. We were the first team to discover them in advance and drive them to suicide. I could understand the looks coming our way now. They would have initially been watching the portal in anticipation of their long-awaited clanmates. Then they would have been curious whether we’d been attacked too.
“Mr. Yandel, could his words be true? That at least three hundred people would have died from these ambushes...”
“Well, we’ll know for sure back in the city. They might have survived but stayed on the fourth floor because their scout or guide was killed.”
“Ah, right...”

Of course, my words didn’t mean much. There was no doubt that hundreds of adventurers had died—not low-level adventurers who hunted on the first and second floors, but veteran adventurers who had climbed the Tower for several decades.
“Whew...”

While this giant red flag scared me, it almost made me relieved. At least they weren’t sent by the Dragon Slayer. I’d even had the delusion that the assassin might have been sent by the district chief or the dragon tribe.
“What bunch of brazen bastards could have planned something this outrageous?”
I was careful to hold my tongue at this point. The information on the royal attack on Noark had not yet been announced.
I suppose this is a sort of declaration of war against the royal family.
I was certain in my mind that the perpetrators of this act of terror were adventurers from Noark.
This is going to blow up.

A headache crept in. A war would break out between the palace and Noark. No, it had pretty much already begun. But the biggest problem here would come if the conquest failed, if Noark locked its doors and the war ended up getting dragged out.
Then I’d be fucked. Because the next battlefield after that would surely be the labyrinth.
Whether it’s Noark or Rafdonia, they need mana stones to maintain the city.
Goddamn it. Why had I been pulled into the game at a time like this? If I had come at least a year earlier, then I would’ve had more time to prepare.
Then, if I didn’t deliver that letter to the grandpa priest, does that mean there wouldn’t have been a war?

The thought came to mind, but I brushed it off. Why was this my fault? This was all that Dragon Slayer scum’s fault. Usually, the three religions were neutral in order to keep the palace in check. No one had forced him to kidnap the high priest and use him as his slave.
“Bjorn?” Missha called out to me.
“Oh, I was just thinking about something.”
“So what arrre you going to do now?”

As I was drawn out of my thoughts, I found that everyone was looking at me. That was because these guys saw this as a simple terrorist attack. Their thoughts weren’t as complicated as mine. “There are no changes to the schedule. Resume the expedition.”
Soon I made a decision, and Raven cautiously expressed her concern. “Even though there are people like that in the labyrinth?”
“It will be fine. There are a lot of clans here. If those people have brains, they won’t do anything here.”
Rather, this was the safest time for us. Next month, those moles might be running around on the fifth floor too. It was also possible that entering the labyrinth would be prohibited outright.
“Now, stop thinking, and let’s go make some money.”
The fifth floor would close after the thirtieth day, so we had lots to do before then. There was no telling how long we’d be out of a job.

The structure of the fifth floor’s Great Demon Realm was simple. Just think of a flat, tray-shaped boulder with slides stretching in four directions. The problem was that these slides were divided into dozens of branches, and some were cut off in the middle or connected to another road.
Whoosh.

When we left the starting point, which was illuminated red like a butcher’s shop, the darkness and heat of the labyrinth welcomed us. Not all of the four roads were like this, though. This was the characteristic of the specific route we chose.

[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Hellfire Gorge has activated. Status effect Ember Mark is now active. All of your consumption values increase by 1.5 times, and Flame Resistance decreases by -30.]

All consumption values—to put it simply, Soul Power, mana, divine power, and energy—were consumed 1.5 times faster than normal here. But that wasn’t bad. Compared to the other routes, this was pretty generous.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-eight support spell Cold Blood. Your Flame Resistance has significantly increased.]

As cold mana seeped into our bloodstreams, our heated bodies cooled down. In that state, we slowly continued our expedition. We hadn’t encountered a monster yet, but just walking here was more stressful than I thought.
Walking through clouds wouldn’t be this bad.
The road was about ten yards wide. The darkness of the labyrinth obstructed our vision, and the abyss below us emitted a strong heat.
“Ainar, stop looking down.”
“I-I was just wondering what’s below us...”
“I heard that there’s lava flowing there.”
“Lava? What’s that?”
“Uh, it’s hard to explain...” Raven faithfully answered Ainar’s curiosity. Ainar frowned every time a difficult word came up but still listened earnestly.
In that respect, they kind of suit each other.
It was a rather nice sight to see as a team leader, but I couldn’t just stand by and watch. “Ainar, stop bothering Raven and look straight ahead.”
“O-Okay!”

I kept my nerves sharp as we descended the slope. There was a fork in the middle and I took out a notebook to draw a map, unconcerned with scale or measurement. I had no intention of using the safe zone as a base camp and just picking at the surrounding area, but I knew that we needed to be able to return if something were to happen. As we reached the third crossroads, I realized in real-time just how great Rotmiller was when the ground shook with an explosion.
Bam!
Soon after, a swirling pillar of fire passed us by.
Spatter.
Small embers flew and landed in front of us before forming a densely packed shape—a beast whose entire body was covered in blazing fire.
“They’re Ifrits.”
“Two rank-five monsters from the get-go.”
As soon as the battle started, Raven cast the Cold Bestow spell on us. Ifrits were spirit-type monsters, so they were immune to physical damage.
[Your weapon will now deal Cold damage.]
A frosty light hung around my mace. I activated Giantization, rushed forward, and smacked the bastards with it. The sensation felt off.
Smack!

This mace had shattered a Troll’s shoulder in one strike when we were on the fourth floor just last month, but the Ifrit didn’t budge. This was why I hated spirit monsters. Unlike Property Change magic, which could transform physical damage into another attribute of the same level, Cold Bestow could only grant additional damage.
“Isir Faist.” With Raven’s rank-six curse spell Rapid Freeze and Missha’s Ice Crush combo, in the end, they finished off the battle while I held out.
[You have defeated an Ifrit. EXP +5]
Mr. Bear summoned Iradun as a tank aid, but Ainar just watched. Such was the fate of a physical warrior.
Roll...
A mana stone dropped where the Ifrit disappeared. Again, there was no essence.
[You have leveled up.]
[Your Soul Power has increased by +10. The maximum number of essences you can absorb has increased by +1.]
I had finally reached level five. This would only be useful if an essence came out, but, oh well.
“Keeekk!”
There was just one monster left now. The flame beast that had lost its precious comrade roared at us.

“...An Ifrit?” At that moment, a group of five adventurers appeared on the other end of the road. It looked like they were headed back to the safe zone after their hunt. And really, how awful was this behavior?
“This is clearly going to take more than five minutes.”
“Ugh, I’m tired as hell. Let’s just take it down.”
A huge ball of water fell from the sky and soaked the Ifrit’s body. The fire was extinguished in an instant.
“What are you—”
Before I could say anything, an arrow pierced through the Ifrit’s head.
Shaaaaa.
The last monster dissolved into light. When I noticed what the bastard had left behind, I let out a big sigh.
“...An essence!”
It was the essence of a rank-five monster.
Goddamn it.
I mean, come on. Why now?

chapters.title: Chapter 167: Great Demon Realm (2)
paragraphs: The moment the glowing red essence floated up, the looks in the eyes of the group of adventurers, which had previously only been filled with the thought of getting some rest, sharpened. It was like a mirror, since our expressions couldn’t have been much different.

A heavy silence fell, but as suited quick-thinking adventurers, it didn’t last long. The first to open his mouth was the hammer-wielding warrior on the other side. “An essence has appeared from the monster we took down.”
“Um, Mr. Nelbo...”
“You can stand back, Mr. Wizard. I’ll take care of this.”
So, you’re the leader.
It seemed this guy had already decided what stance he would be taking in this situation—claiming ownership of the essence.
Chuckle.
I honestly hadn’t even expected anything else. These were the same bastards who couldn’t even wait a few minutes and interrupted our fight. “Prepare for battle,” I muttered.
I said that more for the other side to hear rather than my teammates, a warning that blood would be shed if they were unreasonable here.

“Um, Mr. Yandel...” Raven said, concerned. It was similar to how the wizard on the other side said, “Um, Mr. Nelbo...” to the hammer warrior. Wizards really did seem to be reluctant when it came to these sorts of things. Was it because they grew up with affluence?
I summarized the situation in one sentence. “Don’t panic. It’s just five more monsters in the form of humans.”
With that, the other side recognized that I was the leader too. The hammer-wielding warrior fixed his eyes on me and spoke, the words carrying with them a strange weight. “You’re that guy from...?”
“Do you know me?”

Instead of answering, the warrior lifted the visor of his helmet. The problem was, I still didn’t know who he was. Had I met him before? I was sure I would remember those awfully thick brows. When I looked at him with zero recognition in my eyes, the hammer warrior took off his helmet in frustration.
Flash!
A pure white scalp glistened under the light of the white magic spheres floating in the air. Then I remembered. “...Baldy!”
It was the guy I met when I went to negotiate with the district chief. He had tried to farm accomplishment points off of catching me. To think he would be disguising himself with a helmet.
“Pft!” For some reason, the opposing party’s members burst into laughter.
Embarrassed, Baldy turned red. “...Do you want to die, savage?” Baldy put on his helmet again and said, “You’d better watch what you say from now on. There’s no district chief to protect you here.”

What now? If he knew what my relationship with the district chief was, he wouldn’t be able to say something like that. Well, it didn’t matter. “And you’d better get lost. Unless you want to lose that head too.”
“So, you want to do this, huh?”

When I took a step forward, Baldy did the same. The distance between us narrowed, the essence in the middle of us both. The air grew heavy and a chill that couldn’t even be warmed by the heat of the canyon took over.
Zippp.
Ahead of us, Baldy’s archer pulled his bow.
Click.

From behind, I could hear Mr. Bear loading his crossbow. In the silence, we could almost hear each other’s breathing. It was like a thread pulled taut. The moment the thread snapped, there would be a bloodbath. Baldy and I both knew this.
“Baldy, if you leave now, we’ll give you the mana stone.”
“I see math isn’t your forté, savage. We took the monster down. Of course, the mana stone and essence are all ours.”

No one backed down. Only adventuring parties in the top 30 percent made it to the fifth floor. Even if we got our hands on that essence, the death of even a single party member would be more of a loss.
Squeeze.
Yet we gripped our weapons and narrowed the distance anyway. Cold sweat ran down my back.
Stupid, greedy, bald bastard.

According to custom, we had ownership. He had probably intended to follow that custom at first, handing over the mana stone coolly. Their interference in our battle was likely just the result of wanting to rest as quickly as possible. The problem was that an essence had appeared.
...Is there no other option but fighting?

Gradually, I let go of my uncertainty and assumed the worst. The current situation was kind of like a game of chicken. Whoever backed down first would lose. And if everyone wanted to be the winner, this would end in catastrophe.
“Baldy, this is your last warning.” I didn’t like just running my mouth, but I attempted using words this time.
“Wow, I’m scared out of my mind.” That was a no, then.
With this, I made up my mind. If he really wanted it, I’d see this through to the end. Without that amount of determination, I wouldn’t be able to survive in this heartless world of adventurers.
Now that it’s come to this, I’ll have to consume the essence for now.
The original plan had been to store the Ifrit’s essence in a test tube and sell it. This essence didn’t suit me, Ainar, or Missha.
Step.

However, an essence was always helpful if consumed. I’d rather absorb it myself than give it to that bastard. The cost of erasing an essence was still low for me, so I’d milk it to the bone, then toss it.
We’ll fight by shoving them off. We won’t be able to take their equipment, but winning comes first right now.
Okay, I’d pretty much finished gathering my thoughts. Time to put them into action. But just as I was about to step forward—
“Everyone, stop!”
“Yes. Mr. Yandel, put down your weapon.”
The wizards on both sides stepped forward and our confrontation entered a new phase.
“Mr. Wizard? I thought I told you to stay put.”

“Mr. Nelbo, quit talking like that. It doesn’t make you seem as important as you think it does.” Baldy was silent. “Answer me.” Still nothing. “If you keep acting like this, I’m not entering the labyrinth with you next month.”

“...I’ll stop.” Baldy immediately lowered his tail at the scolding of the wizard, who looked like a young boy. No wonder this dignified and sassy wizard had stood back. He had just been playing along.
I couldn’t hide my disgust.
Bald and a phony?
Now I didn’t even want to speak to him anymore. Anyway, the tension faded after Baldy lowered his weapon and stepped back.
“The pattern on your robe. Altemion School, right?”
“Yes. You’re from the Warton School?”
“Haha, that’s right.”

I knew about the Warton School too. Not only was it a fairly large school, but I could distinctly remember that what made it unique was that they poured all their resources into water-attribute magic.
“I’m Efrain Bello.”
“Arua Raven.”
First, the wizards introduced themselves. Then, unlike the adventurers, who had immediately pulled out their weapons, the two of them shared brief pleasantries.
“How is the Master of Altemion? I saw him a year ago at the academic conference.”
“Well, Master is the same as usual. And Warton’s master? Still researching?”
“Haha, of course. It is our earnest desire.”
It was a sort of, We’re family! conversation. It was like seeing high society in action. It was probably an effort to not complicate things since wizards all knew each other one way or another.
“So, what are you going to do now?”
Soon, Raven got to the point. “You’re aware that staking your claim on the essence of the monster we were hunting is far-fetched, right?”

“Hmm, I don’t think it’s entirely far-fetched. Customs are just customs, after all. You can’t deny that we got involved. So it’s highly likely that the committee will recognize this as a personal dispute between adventurers.”
Unlike the rest of us, who were about to fight like beasts, the wizards tried to find a solution to the problem through conversation.

“Although it may just be customary, it’s hard for those who broke said customs to be seen in a good light. But to go all the way to the committee over one essence... I think it would be more reasonable for your side to just give it up.”
“That’s...” The opposing wizard trailed off. That meant our wizard had won the argument. “Yes, it is. So we’ll forfeit it. I didn’t want to do something like this in the first place.”
So things could be resolved like this too.
I guess I really was fated to be a barbarian.
I lowered my mace. I didn’t end up using it today, but there would definitely come a day when I would have to. That was how the labyrinth was.
“M-Mr. Bello?”
“Stop being a bad sport.”
“Well, in this industry, we all have our own methods...”

Baldy implored him to reconsider, but the wizard’s authority was unshakeable. “Then I don’t know you well at all, Mr. Nelbo. This isn’t defending our rights—it’s greed. I think I’ve shown you enough respect as the leader. But how is this any different from being plunderers?”

Baldy couldn’t say anything in response to the wizard’s valid remarks and groaned. That didn’t make me feel that good inside, though. I was starting to get curious about how it would feel to crush that shiny head.
“Mr. Yandel, what are you going to do with the essence?” While Baldy was getting scolded by the wizard, we discussed how to dispose of the essence.
“Ahem!” Ainar’s eyes clearly said look at me, but I went with my original plan.
“We’ll put it in a test tube and sell it in the city.”
“Nice and neat.”
I was going to feed Ainar a better essence later.
I don’t have the money to feed her an essence right now, anyway.

Typically, when a party member took an essence, they paid the party half of its selling price. Well, Missha and I could leave our part as debt, but it wasn’t clear whether Mr. Bear and Raven would agree to that.
“Ainarrr, cheer up. If we sell that one essence, you can buy tens of thousands of cotton candies. Hmm?”
“T-Tens of thousands?” Ainar stumbled at the overwhelming unit of measurement before rallying her strength. I guess she didn’t think this option was all that bad anymore.
Even still, she’ll have to start with paying back the money I lent her first.

Anyway, once our discussion about the essence was over, Raven stored the Ifrit’s essence in a test tube and we made way for the other party to pass. That would have been the end of it if they had just passed us by.
“You, what’s your name?” Baldy asked, stopping in front of me.
The heck? Is he threatening me right now?
When I eyed him up and down, he cleared up the misunderstanding. “No, I mean... you could argue this is a fated meeting, after all. I can at least ask for your name.”
Fate, my ass. Still, I gave him my name. “It’s Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel?” Baldy cocked his head as if he’d heard the name somewhere. He revealed his name in turn. “I’m Meltasen Nelbo.”
So, it wasn’t Hans Nelbo. That set my mind at ease a bit. “Then goodbye.”

It would be weird to shake hands here, so I ended the conversation. Baldy smiled sharply and continued walking. Starting with him, his colleagues passed us by one by one—shieldsman, swordsman, wizard, and archer, in that order.
The archer froze right in front of me. The reason was simple—because I glared at him, hard.
“Ugh, I’m tired as hell. Let’s just take it down.”
If it weren’t for this bastard, this bullshit wouldn’t have gone down in the first place. In some ways, he irked me more than—
“Hans! What are you doing? We’re leaving.”
Soon, the archer averted his eyes and walked away. I froze like a statue. So there was a Hans.

The twenty-first day dawned. It had already been four days since we’d entered the fifth floor. We continued to follow the road downward, hunting monsters as we went. In the middle of that, Ainar also reached level four.
She hit level four after entering the labyrinth just three times?

In some ways, she’d grown even faster than me. I wished someone would give me a free ride too. Anyway, there were a few times we found ourselves in rough spots while fighting monsters, but the expedition itself was going smoothly. I had been worried that something might happen because of Hans.
Maybe it ended with the essence...

This was an optimistic thought. If you looked at it closely, it even seemed plausible. Even though we ended up getting through the situation all right, we could have ended up fighting five against five, a battle where the losers would have to delete their characters. Put simply, it was possible that the Hans effect ended with the essence drop.
No, what the hell am I thinking? Goddamn bastards.
I’d never really believed in jinxes until I met Hans.
“Mr. Yandel, do you really still have to do that?” When I temporarily stopped to update the map, Raven carefully spoke up.
“What do you mean?”
“...I get that you’re working hard, but we won’t be able to get back by reading that anyway.” Spoken like a wizard who valued results over effort.

I had no rebuttal to make. In truth, I wasn’t confident we could return to where we started with this map, either. That was how complicated the roads of the Great Demon Realm were. It wasn’t just made up of several paths—there were some spots that had to be climbed over with a rope too.
“If I keep going, I’ll get better. It will be better by the next time.”

I was Team Apple Narak’s guide. Although I wanted to live solely as a barbarian warrior, harsh reality had forced me down this path. Therefore, I had to practice doing this. I was sure Rotmiller hadn’t been all that good in the beginning, either.
“Well, I can’t say anything to that... But, isn’t it hard?”
“Well, it is annoying. But it’s also fun in some ways.”

I wasn’t just saying that; I was being sincere. First, this could be considered a qualification, so it felt like I was growing and developing. It was better to be safe than sorry, after all. If there ever came a time when I was stranded like back in the Witch’s Forest, this ability I was honing now would help me.
More importantly, if I become a scout, leading the team to where I want will become easier.
“So, are we just going to continue down today too?”
“There isn’t any other option.”

Just like how the third floor consisted of several areas—Orc Colony, Witch’s Forest, Ironrock Hill, etcetera—the fifth floor also had named areas. Between these narrow, maze-like paths were wide, disk-shaped terrains just like the starting point. There was also a place where you could enter through a cave on a cliff. We’d discovered three areas like that so far, but all three already had owners.
It seems there are more clans controlling hunting grounds than there were in the game.
As someone who had just entered the fifth floor, this was very frustrating. To think my growth would be hindered not because I didn’t have the ability to take down monsters, but because of people.
Damn this reality-patched game.

In order to kill monsters that only appeared in those areas, you had to pay a fee to the clan occupying it. And even if you paid the fee, you only got the right to a one-time hunt for experience points. I suppose properly capturing human nature in a video game was impossible. In reality, the ladder kick was several times worse.
Kick as much as you want. You think I won’t be able to climb higher because of that?

After spending ten years on one game, I’d learned all kinds of tricks and hidden features. I’d also spent an entire year stuck on the fifth floor, so there wasn’t a single nook or cranny I didn’t know about.
Since we’ve come down this far, we should be able to see it now...
The road to strength was here.

chapters.title: Chapter 168: Great Demon Realm (3)
paragraphs: Adventuring was a job that involved entering a labyrinth, hunting monsters, and gathering mana stones. Ordinary people believed that battling monsters was the greatest hardship involved in this career. But when you actually asked the adventurers themselves, you got completely different answers. There was the absence of light, not being able to sleep when you wanted to, food that tasted like animal feed, sexual frustration, getting stained in sweat, and dirty beds.
“It’s not as bad on the lower floors where the expeditions are shorter. But the higher the floor, the more difficult adventurers say these things become.”
“Hmm, I see.”
“Yes. They say it’s normal for large clans, starting from the seventh floor on, to take two to three months off after a trip into the labyrinth.”

As someone belonging to this occupation, that made perfect sense to me. But... so what? What was the point, on the afternoon of the twenty-second day, of bringing up this topic during mealtime right when I was about to take out some jerky? Raven wouldn’t be talking about this for no reason.
“If there’s something you want, just say it.”
When I shot her a look that told her to get to the point, Raven answered with a voice full of determination. “Let’s eat something decent today. Not dried meat, but a meal that uses fire.”
Huh, so that was her objective. She sure was a wizard. She could have just said that she wanted to eat something tasty today.
I thought about it briefly and then answered, “Okay, sure.”
“You may be the leader but you should still take everyone’s opinions into—Wait. I beg your pardon?”
“I said yes.”
“Oh, really?” Raven’s eyes widened. It seemed she expected to be rejected.

Well, I was sure she knew what an unreasonable proposal she was making. This wasn’t the fourth floor. There, we cooked our meals every day and sometimes even ate grilled meat preserved with magic, but the fifth floor’s Great Demon Realm had an open-world structure.
“Can we really?” she asked. “If the smell spreads, there’s a high chance that we won’t even be able to eat it because of the monsters.”
“You... What is it that you want?”
“I-I mean... I’ve thought about it, and I think I can solve the smell problem with magic.” It seemed like this was what she had wanted to get at from the start.

Anyway, when the decision was made to cook food, Ainar, who had been nervously eavesdropping on the conversation, let her mouth fall open in shock. “So this is a wizard...” She seemed to be impressed that Raven had gotten my permission with just a brief exchange.
Now that we’re on the fifth floor, I’ll need to improve on this too.

I had actually already been thinking about this. The total length of our expedition was now about a month. I needed to take steps to manage the team’s stress levels. People tended to get prickly when they were sensitive.
“Then, Miss Karlstein, please let me know if you need water or fire.”
“Umm, then can you light a firrre?”
“Is this enough?”
With that, our party’s official chef, Missha, started cooking with Raven’s help. The menu was tomato stew with lots of meat.
“Delicious again! Missha! You should marry me in the future!”
“What are you talking about, Miss Ainar? Miss Karlstein will be living with me.”
“Um, I’m glad you guys enjoyed it, but both of those options arrre kind of...” Missha trailed off and glanced at me.
While the others were eating, Mr. Bear and I stood guard. But by the time the three of them emptied their bowls, not a single monster had appeared.
“Hmm, it really doesn’t smell. What kind of magic is this?”
“I applied an air control spell and a combustion spell. It gathers the scent in one place and burns it.”
“Hmm, I see.”
Mr. Bear was delighted, marveling at the fact that it was possible to have a decent meal on the fifth floor. I felt the same way. To be honest, I was sick of jerky.
“Okay then, you two can eat. We’ll stand guard now.”

Soon, the two of us sat down and helped ourselves to the stew. As we were a barbarian and a macho man from the Black Bear tribe, five minutes was more than enough. No monsters appeared while we ate. It wasn’t just because of the effectiveness of the odor-removal magic, either.
The overall number of monsters has decreased.
I had been getting this vibe for the past few days, but the number of monsters on the fifth floor was much lower than in the game. Of course, I had a guess as to why.
Fucking clans.

In the Great Demon Realm, monsters spawned from mirrors located in each unique zone and were then released into the canyon. However, the clans had monopolized those areas to hunt the monsters as they spawned, so fewer monsters inevitably crawled out of their respective zones.
Well... thanks to that, I managed to find this early.

I glanced at the moss growing in the corner of the path and smiled. It was different from the other moss we’d passed by. Its color was half red and half green, and a batch of black moss the size of a bead formed at the point where the two different kinds met.
The problem is how to make this look natural...

While I was thinking this, some monsters appeared straight ahead: eight rank-six Hell Hounds. They were basically wild dogs the size of tigers with four eyes. As a bonus, their bodies were completely engulfed in black flames.
“Grrrrrr!”
“Prepare for battle.”
Since we’d hunted more of these than we could count over the past few days, we jumped into the fray without needing to coordinate. It took about ten minutes for us to wrap up the battle.
“So, are we going further down now?”

Raven asked what our plan was, and I thought it over for a moment. There was still a long while before it would be time to make camp. How could I get them to stay put here without making it seem strange?
Welp, if it weren’t for that scent-hiding spell, we would be stuck here fighting monsters right about now.
While I was biting my lip in disappointment, the black moss on the corner of the road disappeared.
...Huh?
It was almost as if something invisible had picked it up.
It’s already here?
I quickly gave orders. “Raven, I think there’s something here with us.”
“Sorry? What do you—”
“Cast a detection spell.”

Was this a side effect of being stalked by that masked assailant on the fourth floor? Raven didn’t hesitate to cast based purely on my hunch. “Dire Tanib Karsachi.” Waves of mana rippled out in a circle. Raven’s expression soon grew serious. “There is something. It’s in front of us.”
“Is it a person?” I asked, pretending not to know, and Raven cast Track Down instead of answering.
Whooom!
A cluster of lights appeared and began to stick to the air like clay. Before long, the lights faded and the figure of our invisible guest was revealed.
It was a squirrel the size of about a six-or seven-year-old child. It was sitting curled up in front of the moss, gnawing on the piece of black moss with its front teeth.
“Kyuu?” Sensing our eyes, the squirrel cocked its head.
“Oh...! I-It’s cute!”
“It looks delicious!” Missha and Ainar both exclaimed at the same time.
Raven let out an excited shout of her own. “It’s a Mila Roden! We have to kill it right now!”
So you know how rare it is to run into this guy.
“Ahh, right... it’s still a monsterrr...” Missha raised her sword with a somewhat sad look on her face.

On the flip side, Mr. Bear loaded his crossbow with a bolt faster than ever. It seemed more than one of us had recognized this creature’s value. “We’re lucky, finding a Mila Roden on our first expedition.”

“W-Wait. Distortion! I haven’t used a distortion spell yet!” Raven stopped Mr. Bear and quickly cast a spell. It wasn’t just any distortion spell, but a high-class one. Now, when we took down the targeted monster, there was a higher chance that the corpse would remain intact.

“Kyu, kyuut!” As soon as it was struck with the distortion magic, the Mila Roden went into a frenzy. Perhaps it was an instinct imprinted in its DNA. Most of its ancestors would have been killed in the same way.
“Abman!”

Just as I shouted, the crossbow fired. However, as one of the few herbivorous monsters in the labyrinth, the Mila Roden managed to avoid it with quick movements. I immediately dove forward and grabbed it by its tail.
“Pii! Piiii! Piit!” The creature struggled and let out a scream. This felt a lot like I was hurting an animal but, well, what could you do? This was the law of the jungle.
Slide.

Just as I was reaching my hand out with the intention of squeezing its skull, Raven stopped me. “Wait! Can’t we keep it as whole as possible when we kill it? I heard its skin is sold at a high price.”
Spoken like a true wizard who sought the most sensible course of action. I obediently agreed and grabbed the Mila Roden by the neck and tail to secure it in place. “Missha.”
“Uh, huh? D-Do I have to do it?”
“Your sword is the thinnest.”

Ainar used a greatsword and Mr. Bear’s arrows were too big. My mace wasn’t even worth mentioning. And since this creature was still a monster, it would be hard to kill it cleanly with a regular knife.
“Stab it in the forehead.”
“Ugh...” Missha seemed reluctant, but in the end, she pulled out her sword to give the creature peace.
“Kyuu...” The Mila Roden went slack like someone had pulled its plug. I gulped and counted the seconds.
One, two, three...
This was usually the amount of time it took for monsters to turn into light after dying.
“Bjorn! It’s meat!”
The body did not disappear.
The rank-seven Mila Roden, a squirrel that carried a mirror on its back, was categorized as a rare species along with the Mimic because it was ridiculously hard to encounter one.
“Haha, we caught a very rare monster thanks to you, Mr. Yandel. Do you have experience with these, Mr. Urikfried?”
“This is my first time seeing one too. That’s how rare it is.”

Mr. Bear had been active on the fifth floor for a long time, yet this was also his first time hunting one of these. Well, considering the monster’s nature, that was understandable. It was a pacifistic monster that had the ability to conceal itself at all times. To add to that, when detection spells were cast around it, it refused to even step within range. It was a monster that you could only encounter with god-like luck—assuming you didn’t know about the black moss.
If you just wait here and use a single detection spell, you can always find one.

Of course, that was easier said than done. It took me over a year of being stuck on the fifth floor to learn this method. This was a game full of hidden features. I had looked through recorded playthroughs with the conviction that there might be a condition for making the Mila Roden appear, and I noticed the moss disappearing from the map in one of the recordings. At the time, I thought it might be a bug.
This sick game...

I soon confirmed it wasn’t a bug but a hidden feature. If you ran a detection spell as soon as the moss disappeared, the chances of a Mila Roden appearing were 100 percent. Of course, whether the distortion spell succeeded or not was another matter entirely.
“I guess this is beginner’s luck. Even the distortion spell succeeding is—”
“It’s high-class distortion. Not just distortion.”
“Oh. Right, high-class distortion...”

In the game, the success rate of using distortion magic on a Mila Roden was 20 percent. Even a high-class distortion spell had less than a 30 percent chance of succeeding, which was why I thought we would have to catch at least three or four before we managed to preserve one.
“Anyway, could you hand it to me?” asked Raven.
“Do you know how to butcher it?”
“I did this every day during my apprenticeship.”
The limp corpse was quickly dismembered into leather, intestines, and bones by Raven’s butcher knife. Her technique was much faster and more sophisticated than Rotmiller’s.
Wow, experts are on a whole other level.
“But what’s expensive about this guy?”

“Its hide is in high demand because of its rarity, and its tendons are used as magical ingredients. But... its real value lies elsewhere.” Soon, Raven cut out the mirror attached to the skin on the creature’s back, marking the end of the butchery process. “It’s this mirror.”
“Mirror?”
“Yes. It can’t be taken out to the city, but it can be very useful here.” With that, Raven explained the purpose of the mirror in detail. I watched her do so, pleased.
Is this why you need a wizard in your party?
Things had become much easier for me. In the past, I had to explain everything from A to Z myself. Whew, could I finally live like a normal barbarian?
“But you also have good instincts, Mr. Yandel.”
“Huh?”

“There’s no way you sensed the Mila Roden’s presence.” Raven shot me a strange look but seemed to let this pass without getting suspicious. Since she herself recently went through something similar on the fourth floor, I guess she thought it wasn’t impossible that I managed to do the same. That was that.
“So, how do you use it?” In the game, you simply equipped the mirror to the wizard and pressed a button. So, how did it work in real life?
“Um, I’m not really sure, either. That wasn’t written in the book. Maybe injecting some mana into it would work?”
“...Try it. Oh, but before that, cast a binding spell first. Just in case.”

“Good idea.” After casting the binding magic, Raven held the mirror and closed her eyes. It seemed she was pushing mana into it, but as a barbarian with no aptitude for mana, I couldn’t sense anything special. We waited for a while, when—
Flash!
Suddenly, the mirror engulfed us in a radiant light. When I came to, instead of a labyrinth filled with darkness, we were standing at the top of a wide wilderness.
[You have entered the Mirror of Fire.]

“Everything has changed, like a Rift!” was Mr. Bear’s impression. However, this place was completely different from a Rift. To start with, there was no guardian or final boss, and this place didn’t take the form of a dungeon. This was just an open-world structure crawling with monsters.
“Go somewhere else, barbarian. This is our clan’s territory.”
In other words, this zone was the world beyond the mirrors that all of the clans were camped outside of, snatching up all the monsters as they spawned.
“Bjorn! Monsters are coming in from all sides!”
“Prepare for battle!”
[Field Effect – The Hidden World has activated. The drop rate of mana stones has significantly increased. The drop rate of essences has slightly increased.]
Let’s get just two essences—no more, no less.

chapters.title: Chapter 169: Burning (1)
paragraphs: The world beyond the mirror was a hidden map like The Labyrinth of Larcaz. Its difficulty was quite high right upon entry because monsters flooded in from the start.
“Bjorn! Another wave is coming!”

As soon as one battle was over, another horde of monsters rushed in. The scale this time was on a whole other level. There were eight rank-seven beast-type Flame Wolves, five rank-six natural-type Salamanders, and three rank-five plant-type Redwoods.
“Raven, how long ‘til the spell!?”
Just as I shouted that, blue light shot out of Raven’s wand. “Nara Brigianu Toon!” This was the rank five wide-range ice spell Blizzard: Freezing Rain.
Crashhh!
Gray clouds formed in the sky above, and sharp shards of ice poured out of them.
Bang, bang, bang!
More than half of the monsters were obliterated with a single spell. Of course, the rank-five monsters were unaffected even by this wide-range skill.
“Behelahhh!”
Thanks to my increased Threat Level from Wild Outburst and Giantization, monsters flocked to me on their own. This was why a tank was as important as a wizard in this place.
“Gaaaaaa!”

Blocking the Redwood’s stem whip with my shield, I focused solely on defense, also known as Barbarian Turtle Mode. I could take down at least one of them with Swing, but it was better to save my MP since my Threat Level would drop once Giantization ended.
“Kill the Salamanders first!”
While I was taking on three Redwoods, our wizard prepared a spell for the next wave. This time, it was the damage dealers’ turn to play their part.
Clashhh!
Receiving long-range support from Mr. Bear, Ainar and Missha began eliminating the monsters in earnest. It took less than three minutes to take out the trash mobs.
Cleaning up trash mobs is quick with three close-combat damage dealers.
Afterward, the five of us teamed up to defeat the rank-five monsters, but there was no time to rest.
“...Another one.”
No sooner did we finish the battle than another herd of monsters came looking for the source of the sound. We repeated this process over and over again.

After we had finished about ten battles, Raven said, “Mr. Yandel, I don’t have much mana left.” Raven was using wide-range spells without holding back, so her mana had been reduced to less than a third of her usual levels. Of course, that was no problem. The first wave was almost over.
“Don’t use attack magic and just provide support.”
“Okay!”

Raven’s remaining mana was used to cast curses on the enemy or give the team buffs. My Giantization ended around then too. It seemed Mr. Bear, who had been firing explosive arrows, didn’t have much MP left either.
“Behelahhh!”
As the three of us started to struggle, the importance of the melee sisters Ainar and Missha increased accordingly. After all, melee was the best way to deal average DPS.
“Oohhhh! This is the battle I wanted!” Ainar’s excitement peaked as she dealt with our endless enemies. Like a true barbarian, who was deemed the warrior tribe, her enthusiasm was rather beneficial.
Was she always this good at fighting?
Although it looked like she was swinging her greatsword crudely, she still avoided everything that needed to be avoided. It was like she was fighting on crack.
Well, she did train her swordsmanship there...
Her battle instincts even seemed to be superior to Missha’s. Anyway, the battle was approaching its end, so I changed up the formation. “Abman, now, send him this way!”
Iron Bear Iradun, Bear for short, was the team’s tank assist.
Whoom!

Even Bear, who was protecting our long-range fighter in the back, joined the front line and lent us his strength. That was because it really seemed like everyone was at their limit now. Our wizard’s mana was completely exhausted at this point, so even support had come to an end.
Crunch! Crunch! Whiiish!
Pushed to our limits for the first time in a while, we cleared the monsters with normal attacks that didn’t involve skills—just a mace, sword, and giant crossbow bolts.
“Looks like it’s over...” Once I finished it off by crushing the latest monster’s flaming skull, the battle ended. Hundreds of mana stones decorated the ground.
“But were mana stones always this darrrk?”
“It’s what makes this place special. The density of the stones is about double.”
Simply put, a double event was at play. It took several minutes for Raven to collect the stones with what little mana she had left. Oh, and there was an essence.
“I saw that! It came from the guy wearing human heads on his body!”

“You mean Headhunter.” That was a rank-seven fire-type undead monster. I coolly abandoned the essence. It could be useful if consumed, but now that we were going to hunt rank-five monsters every day, there was no point in taking it.
“Mm, we’re leaving it...?” Ainar stared at me with obvious disappointment, like a child who had dropped her candy on the floor.
I told you no. Bad.
“It’s not a good essence for you. So deal with it.”

“...Okay!” Picking up just anything would end up costing you more money if you tried to erase it later. But I supposed throwing away loot bothered her. “But can’t we just sell it in a test tube?” Ainar shouted.
That particular suggestion was dealt with by the wizard. “No. Anything below rank six won’t even pay for the test tube. And on top of that, I heard you can only take one item from this place.”
“Hm? Only one? What do you mean by that?”

“I don’t know the reason, but the items obtained in here have to be distorted with magic to take out, and I heard there can only be one.” That was a characteristic of this map that I would’ve had to explain had Raven not already known about it. “We have to choose carefully what we’ll take with us. Essences are useful... But I’ve heard of some people finding a really valuable item here.”
“A valuable item...” The item we were going to take with us was already decided, but that piqued my curiosity. Did someone else know about the item already?
I asked for more details but Raven stopped me there, saying that that was all she knew. “Information on these things is hard to learn from books. I only heard about it from other people.”

True, information on the fifth floor and above was classified as advanced. Even trivial achievements were treated as intellectual property and not freely shared. Some clans even prohibited their members from mentioning the work they’d done in the labyrinth. This kid hadn’t been hung up on The Complete Book of Rifts for nothing.
“First, get some rest. I’ll take watch.” After a fierce battle, we decided to take a break. As we settled down, we took stock of our current state. “Raven, how long until your mana is fully charged?”
“With meditation or sleep, twelve hours. If I don’t get that, it’ll take more than a day.”

“I see.” This was what I meant about melee damage dealers being better than wizards on the fifth floor. Wizards required a considerable amount of time to recharge their mana. “From now on, save your mana as much as possible.”
“You’re going to continue the expedition like this?”
“This isn’t a place that’s easy to reach. We should explore as much as possible. We might find that valuable item you were talking about.”
“That is certainly true. There’s no telling when we’ll get to come here again...”

So that problem was dealt with. After replenishing our stamina for fifteen minutes, we resumed our quest. It was a forced march, but no one complained. They had already seen the amount of mana stones and essences that this place spat out.
