“I’ll finally get to hold my head up in front of my wife.” Mr. Bear grinned from ear to ear. No matter what happened, he was a family man.
“Abman, do you sense a portal anywhere?”

“I can feel one faintly—it’s very far away, over there.” In this map where compasses did not work, we relied on our scout’s ability in order to navigate. “...If you’re going to go the opposite way, why did you ask?”
Because the place I want to go is this way.
Of course, I couldn’t say that. Instead, I improvised a plausible explanation. “That portal is likely to be the exit. We’ll have to go the opposite way if we want to find something.”
Nothing I said was wrong, so I quickly gained Raven’s support. “Ah! That’s right. I read there was a portal leading out of the mirror.”
Whew, this was why there needed to be a decently smart character on the team. “Okay then, let’s go.”
It was around 7 p.m. on day twenty-two. Since the day was almost over, we had about a week left now. In order to milk it to the bone, we had to hurry.

This map, the Mirror of Fire, had one distinct peculiarity: it took one day for monsters to regenerate. Thanks to that, the hunting grounds temporarily became a safe zone. This was fortunate. If monsters were constantly crawling out in the hundreds, we wouldn’t have been able to even sleep.
[You have defeated a Hell Guard. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Gremlin. EXP +2]
[You have defeated a Doom Warrior. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Chaos Worm...]
[You have defeated a Doomfire Fairy...]

Killing monsters we weren’t able to hunt before because of the control the clans had over their respective territories, we escaped the forest surrounding the starting point after three days. Progress was much slower than I had expected.
The map is sizable, but the main issue is that there are too many monsters.

Once a battle started, monsters in the surrounding area all gathered thanks to the sound. Of course, it was much better than them converging on us from all sides like at the very beginning. Now, we only had to worry about our enemies coming at us from the front, and it was possible to retreat backward if necessary. However, as our forced march dragged on, stamina and mana bottomed out and our hunting speed slowed down. That led to a few dangerous situations. In the end, we had to take periodic breaks.
Still, the rate we’re collecting mana stones is wild.

I didn’t call this place the Burning Zone for nothing. With the ability to win large-scale battles using magic and a doubled mana stone drop rate on top of that, I really started to feel like I was making money through mana stones after coming here. Prior to this, our jackpots were all from catching plunderers and obtaining their equipment.
Big battles are the best type of hunting, after all.
On the morning of the twenty-sixth day, after camping out in front of it, we officially entered a new area.
Whoosh!

The Burning Forest, as the name suggested, was engulfed in black flames that burned 365 days a year. However, the fire damage we suffered was negligible thanks to the trees being quite far apart from each other and Cold Blood raising our flame resistance. There were three reasons I chose this place. First, it had the lowest battle difficulty.
“Hmm, there’s nothing special.”
“Yeah, I was a little worried, but I think it’s easierrr than the last area. No rank-five monsters, either.”

Although there were a lot of monsters, they were just rank six or seven. Of course, easy prey meant fewer rewards. However, the Ashen Mountains and Lava Lake on the other side were quite challenging for characters of our level, and there was nothing to be gained from entering the Altar of the Dead where the portal was.

Second, we needed to get something to make things more comfortable for us, an item hidden in the center of the Burning Forest. With that thing, it would not only be possible to clear the other zones next time, but we’d also be able to enter a certain island on the sixth floor.

“Don’t get too relaxed. You never know what might show up.” I issued a warning out of habit, but once we entered the forest, I sped up too. Since our trip here took more time than I expected, it was unclear whether we had arrived in time.
“The trees here are all burnt.”
“Let’s rest here for today.”
After an endless, all-day cycle of battle and travel, we only unpacked our sleeping bags at our campsite when the day was coming to an end. The next morning, we encountered a monster.
It’s finally here.
“Arua! What’s this thing’s name?”
“Uh... I don’t know, either.”

Only one of these existed in the Burning Forest—a monster that even Raven, who spent her whole life reading books, didn’t know the rank or name of. A rare monster that even the clans who controlled the territories on the fifth floor may or may not meet once a year.
“Kwohhh!” This was the rank-five rare-type monster Berthas, and my third reason for choosing the Burning Forest.
“Behelahhh!”
This guy was guaranteed to drop an essence.

chapters.title: Chapter 170: Burning (2)
paragraphs: About thirty adventurers were gathered under an enormous mirror that was glowing with red light. The blue wolf symbol on each of their chests meant that they belonged to one particular clan.
“Shift change!”

At one man’s shout, one of the teams lined up in front of the mirror and changed spots with a team who had finished their break. They began mechanically hunting the monsters that appeared from the mirror. This was a sight all fifth-floor adventurers had seen before.
“...Let’s go somewhere else.” The party of adventurers who happened to arrive at this place saw them and dejectedly changed course. They were used to this. The entire fifth floor was like this.
“Halt! From this point onward is the domain of the Nevis Wolf Clan. Please go somewhere else.”

It would be impossible for any ordinary party to argue. Most large clans on the fifth floor were made up of adventurers skilled enough to be active on the sixth floor. These skilled individuals were killing time on the fifth floor for one reason: the sixth floor was dominated by even bigger clans. As a result, they made more money this way.
“Deputy commander, what’s our total profit today?”
Mana stones were obtained by hunting in twenty-four-hour shifts, and any passersby with complaints were driven out by force.
“We obtained the essence of a Doomfire Fairy. Who wants to buy it?”

If a rank-five essence appeared, it was stored in a test tube and sold in the city. Anything below that was sold to nearby adventurers at a cheaper price. An adventurer looking for experience points was treated like a customer to maximize profit.
“I’ll cast a binding spell for you, so stand back and don’t engage in battle.”
Like that, they hunted around the clock, reaping the fruits of the labyrinth as usual.
“Commander! It’s a Berthas!”
“What?”
The man who was resting in the back and commanding the clan quickly got up and approached a mirror. A monster was visible beyond it.
“Kwohhh!” Two horns sprouted from its forehead, and its muscular body stood over ten feet tall. Berthas was a devil-type monster with a torso covered in black wings and four arms.
The corners of the man’s mouth curled up. “This must be our lucky day.” It was their first time seeing this monster in a year.
How much did it sell for last time?

It was only rank five, but since its rarity was recognized, he remembered the essence sold to the Magic Tower for a high price. The mana stone pool was actually lagging below average on this expedition, but this should be enough to make up for the deficit.
“Everyone, stand in formation!”
The man pulled out his own weapon for the first time in a while and stood in front of the group. Then, they waited for the Berthas to fully emerge from beyond the mirror.
“It’s coming!”

A giant foot slowly emerged from the mirror. The eyes of the clan members shone with anticipation. None of them were worried about the battle. The wizards had readied their greatest firepower spells. It may have been rare, but it was still just a rank-five monster, so the battle would undoubtedly be over as soon as it appeared.
At least, that should have been the case.
“Behelahhh!”
A human roar was heard through the mirror. At the same time, the monster that was about to step outside turned around and pulled its foot back in.
“...Who the hell are they!?” The leader couldn’t understand what had just happened at all.
“Behelahhh!”
The Berthas turned its head the moment I unleashed Wild Outburst in full force. Soon, the mirror that had formed under its feet disappeared. Thankfully, I had drawn enough aggro.
Phew, I thought we lost him.
The monsters in the Hidden World used mirrors to travel to the labyrinth. To put it simply, if I had been a second late, someone else would have gotten to kill this bastard instead.
“Kwohhh!” As soon as I raised my shield, the monster rushed at me.
Bam!
As it collided with me, I noted that its strength was below a Troll’s. As expected, this guy didn’t live up to its scary face. Judging by appearance alone, you’d assume it was at least rank three.
“Mr. Yandel, are you okay?”
“I can handle it, don’t worry about me!”
“Everyone except Mr. Yandel, step back. We need to figure out what abilities it has first!”
We had encountered an unknown enemy. Raven, flustered, gave out orders for the first time.
You don’t have to be that careful... But it would look strange if I acted like I know what this thing is.

I was confident that I could hold it down for hours, so I decided to observe the proceedings without saying anything. To be honest, a part of me was curious too. What kind of decisions would a wizard make in the absence of any prior knowledge?
“Marde Guarjour.” The first spell Raven used was Mana Assess, the same spell used at the checkpoint to convert mana stones. “Fortunately, it’s about rank five!”
First, the monster’s threat level was assessed. However, that was all she was able to find out. The rest would have to be inferred through live combat.
BOOM!
The monster’s fist met my shield and exploded—an ability called Blast Scars.
“There was no sign of it gathering energy. I think this is a passive ability...”
First of all, passive was right. So, what was the trigger, then?
Bang! Slam! BOOM!

While explosions continued to ring out from beyond my shield, Raven scrutinized the battle from the rear with keen eyes. Then she reached a conclusion. “The same spot! The explosions occur when it hits you in the same spot!”
Correct. I didn’t think she would figure it out so quickly. “So how long are you going to just watch?”
“Uh... You seem fine on your own, so shouldn’t I observe some more? Miss Karlstein or Ainar could get seriously hurt.”
Hmm, did that mean I wouldn’t? For some reason, I felt a mix of both sadness and pride as a tank at that moment.
“If things get dangerous, I’ll throw you a potion right away!”
“High-rank?”
“Yes, high-rank!”
If you say so.
Maybe it was more based on how I was already feeling, but from what I’d experienced, high-rank potions hurt less. Having pain resistance didn’t mean you couldn’t feel pain.

“Oh, it uses its feathers as arrows too. Seeing as its energy isn’t moving while it does that either, I think that’s just a unique trait!” Anyway, Raven’s voice became much lighter once she concluded that this wasn’t a very dangerous enemy for our level. “Mr. Yandel, try hitting it with the mace. You might have to strike it to trigger it...”
I guess being able to analyze a new monster was fun for her. Since it was the first time I’d seen our wizard so excited, I obediently followed her instructions.
Crunch!
When I slammed down on one of its four arms with Swing, the joint bent. Its wings instantly spread.
“That’s a special ability!”
This was one of Berthas’ three active skills, Wings of Greed.
Shaaaaaa!
The surrounding air was quickly sucked into the wings like a whirlpool down a drain. After about three seconds of suction, the wings folded with a clicking sound, and its broken arm healed.
“It’s a healing ability!” Raven apparently had no intention of twiddling her thumbs while watching because she immediately cast Aggravate.
Whew, I really hoped that would come out...
This guy’s true value lay in the passive skills, but as long as we were going to absorb an essence, it was better to pick an active one that was useful too.
[Berthas has cast Legion of Hatred.]
[Berthas has cast Destruction Ray.]
After all, demon summoning and light beams didn’t suit a barbarian.
Whooom!
Avoiding the Destruction Ray, which took an entire three seconds to cast, I attempted Giantization after receiving permission.
“I think all of its abilities have been confirmed!”
“Uh, then should I go fight now?”
This was our long-awaited moment of triumph.
“Behelahhh!”
While Ainar gripped her greatsword and obliterated the devils Berthas had summoned, Mr. Bear and Raven whipped out their finishers and took aim.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Hazardous Material.]
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-five attack spell Thunder Spear.]
This was an ultimate combo that not even a Troll, the epitome of resilience, could withstand.
Kaboom!
There was a giant explosion and the monster’s body turned into light.
[You have defeated a Berthas. EXP +5]
Light particles interspersed with black smoke. Curious about the outcome, Raven used wind magic to remove the smoke. At that moment, a white essence appeared before our eyes.
“A-An essencee!”

The Wings of Greed that I had been longing for had appeared. The odds were only 33.3 percent, but it had really shown up in one attempt. Suddenly, I was a bit nervous. The essence of a rank-five monster had appeared. Therefore, there were two options: store it in a test tube and sell it or have one person on the team pay for it and absorb it.
“What will you do?”
“I think Ainar should take this.”
“Eh? Me!?”

Everyone ignored Ainar’s gushing. Although I was just a party to this negotiation, I was a man who would become the ruler of the barbarians in the future. Put simply, I could represent all barbarians.
“Hmmm... Even though we haven’t even confirmed what kind of essence it is?”

The skills the monster possessed had been confirmed during the battle. However, what skills the essence contained could only be known for sure after consumption. Plus, the basic stats attached to the essence were just as important as the skills.
“With that in mind, I hope you’ll make it cheaper.”
“How much?”
“Sixteen million stones.”
When I made an initial proposal, Ainar jumped. “Sixteen million stones?!”
“Ainar, please be quiet. Hm? Bjorrrn is talking.”
“O-Okay!”

Raven didn’t even smile at the interruption, her expression serious as she continued the conversation. “When that’s divided by four, I only get four million stones.” As expected, it didn’t work. That was why I had suggested sixteen million in the first place. “I think the amount is too low. That was a monster rare enough that even I didn’t know about it. More importantly, if I store this in a test tube and sell it, 40 percent of the profit is mine.”
“...Instead, I’ll let you research it.”
“A-Are you selling me to the wizard!?”
“Hmm, just like how you did before?” Now Raven looked interested. After all, to a wizard, research was worth more than money.

Gaining momentum, I stopped testing the waters and played the cards I had up my sleeve in succession. “Plus, if you store this in a test tube and cast distortion magic on it, you can’t take anything else.” In other words, wouldn’t it be a waste to use distortion magic here when you might discover another treasure?

Raven seemed interested in that and nodded. “Although there’s only a few days left... The possibility definitely cannot be ruled out.” Nice, it seemed like I was done persuading her. Next was Mr. Bear’s turn. “What do you want to do, Mr. Urikfried? I can make up for the loss with research, but—”
“I do not care. Haven’t I already earned enough? The only reason we’re here in the first place is because Bjorn discovered that creature.”
“Well, that’s true, but... Are you sure about that? We don’t know how much this will sell for.”
“That’s why I don’t care. If the barbarian girl gets stronger, that’ll benefit us as well.”
“Okay, then we’re done here.”

Ainar would now have to pay four million stones each to Mr. Bear and Raven back in the city. She’d made a lot on this quest, but she’d have to return to being broke again. “Now, hurry up and take it before it disappears.”
Still, Ainar seemed happy about having a new essence as she took it without resistance.
[The Essence of Berthas has seeped into Ainar Fenelin’s soul.]
As soon as it came into contact with her skin, the pool of light instantly slid in. Raven’s eyes lit up with curiosity. “Well, how does it feel? What is the most notable change?”
“Uh... I feel stronger, I think...”
“Hmm, ambiguous. I’ll have to look into the data back in the city. Why don’t you try using its special ability?”
“S-Special ability?”

“Oh, it might be hard to visualize it.” Raven then advised her to recall the three abilities the Berthas used earlier and focus her energy. “You can try saying something too. That’s how we first learn magic.”

“Uh... then I’ll give it a try.” Under Raven’s guiding hand, Ainar attempted the Berthas’ skills one by one. The summoning skill, Legion of Hatred: “C-Come out! Devil bastards!” The long-range-attack skill, Destruction Ray: “Arrrgh!” And then, Wings of Greed: “Wings!”
Flap!

Wings of light spread out behind her back—aka, Barbarian Valkyrie mode. “H-Have I become a Valkyrie?” Ainar looked around and down at her appearance for a while, then let out a delighted shout. “Behelahhh!”
Well, it was good that she liked it.

chapters.title: Chapter 171: Burning (3)
paragraphs: After Ainar won Wings of Greed in the lottery, Raven treated her like a puppet and tested the essence’s performance. First came the most important issue.
“I-I can’t fly...!”

You couldn’t fly with them. Since the wings were made of light, not only was it not possible for her to attack or defend herself with them, but it was also impossible for the wings to grant her flight. They just moved according to Ainar’s mood.
Flap, flap!
Oh no, bad mood. Still, you had to take balance into account. If these could fly, that would be a total cheat.
“...Still, it suits you very well.”
“Yeah, yeah, you look really strrrong.”
“Really?!” At Missha’s compliment, the wings started to flap again.
Flap!
Hmm, that clearly meant happiness. Well, even I had to admit the wings looked sick. The air-sucking effect that accompanied each healing session was pretty flashy too.
“If we had known it did that beforehand, you could’ve taken it, Mr. Yandel. You’re not regretting it?”
“Huh?”
“Now that the Vampire essence is gone, you don’t have an ability related to stamina regeneration.”

Ah, that was what she meant. But this wasn’t an essence that suited me. First off, passives didn’t suit tanks. You could get good regeneration through stats anyway, and there were tons of better essences in the labyrinth.
More than anything, it’s compatible with Ainar.

The effect of Blast Scars was simple: two strikes in the same spot created an explosion. In the game, it acted almost as a critical hit, and just exploded a little better against dark-type monsters or if you increased the swordsman’s accuracy. But when you combined it with Repeated Slash, it was a completely different story.
“Then let’s keep moving.”
Soon after we resumed our expedition, a monster herd appeared and everyone was able to see Ainar’s growth with our own eyes.
Bang!
An explosion occurred as soon as she used Repeated Slash. A rank-seven monster’s head immediately blew up and disappeared into the light.
Even Raven was startled by the force. “Is this why you gave the essence to Miss Ainar? Because of my assumption that it creates an explosion from repeated strikes?”
Well, it was not just an assumption to me but a fact. Of course, I couldn’t say that, so I came up with an excuse. “You are the team’s wizard. Of course I trust your judgment.”
“Uh... Well, thanks, but...” As expected, Raven couldn’t respond to that and kept quiet.
Meanwhile, Ainar couldn’t rein in her excitement and continued shoving through monsters. “Behelahhh!” Explosions occurred each time she swung her sword.
Bang! Bang!

Thanks to the twin stats (Strength and Agility) attached to the Berthas’ essence, her movements were much smoother and more powerful than before. Of course, since I wasn’t at the front of the group drawing aggro, she continued to accumulate injuries.
“Wings!” When Vitality Absorption and Wings of Greed were cast together, her wounds healed quickly.
That pretty much sets her character build.

She’d be a Berserker Barbarian. I didn’t bother hiding my delight as I watched Ainar in battle. I was also a bit envious. Before I developed Shield Barbarian, I always built my characters like that. Exciting battles were a man’s dream.
Increasing her strength stat so she can use her sword with one hand isn’t a bad idea.
I thought about it for a moment. A barbarian warrior swinging through the battlefield like a whirlwind with a huge greatsword in each hand, and also wings on her back? Oh, shit.
Hella cool.
It might even be possible to be vicariously satisfied with that.
“B-Bjorn!”
“Got it. I will help you now.”
However, she wasn’t perfect enough to overcome a lack of numbers, so I joined the battle and helped finish it. Was that alone impressive enough, though?

“Wow, so you can become that strong with one essence...” Missha followed Ainar’s movements with slight envy in her eyes. After all, this kid didn’t have an essence higher than rank five yet. Watching Ainar, who had both a rank-four and a rank-five essence, might make her feel depressed. Ainar was in her first year of adventuring like me too.
“Don’t worry. You will get stronger too.”

“Yeah...” Missha was suddenly dejected, but there was nothing else I could say to her. I planned to obtain everything we could from the Hellfire Gorge before finding her an essence anyway. I suspected it would take half a year, and it would take several years to acquire the sword that served as the core of an ice-type double swordsman build.
Now that I’m on the fifth floor, there’s a lot of work to be done.

After that, we collected the mana stones and continued our quest. The vast forest of flaming trees exuded a desolate beauty. Clearing monsters, time flew by and the thirtieth day dawned before we knew it. It was 8 a.m., just sixteen hours before the labyrinth closed.
Finally here. It was a close call.
A huge tombstone appeared between the trees. “Everyone, stop!”
“Uh, is it a trrrap?”
“I don’t know. But it could be.” As soon as she saw the man-made carving, Raven was on high alert.
That’s a good habit, but... It’s just a tombstone.

The tombstone had no function in the game. The areas in the other directions had the same one, and it served as a sort of landmark, a sign that this was the center of the area. Well, it was possible there were hidden features I hadn’t discovered yet, but the chances of that were low. I’d tried all sorts of bullshit out of suspicion but nothing came out of it.
“So what are you going to do?” I asked Raven.
“Prepare for battle first. It might summon something when you get within a certain radius.”
“Sure.” Ignoring the wizard’s instructions in this situation wasn’t a good call, so I obediently followed them.

Fortunately, Raven, while cautious, was not the type to pointlessly waste time. “I don’t sense any mana. But just in case, I’ll approach it slowly.” We gradually closed the distance and soon stood in front of the tombstone. Of course, no monsters appeared. “Mr. Yandel, try touching the stone.”
You always make me do these things.
Knowing it was safe, I put my hand on it without argument. Again, there was no response whatsoever.
“Can we stay here a while and check things out?”
“If you want.” I agreed to Raven’s request too. Since this was the real version, I figured we could find some clues I couldn’t in the game. Half an hour passed like that. “Raven, let’s go.”
“N-No! A man-made structure in a forest like this? There must be something behind it!”
It looked like she’d fallen into the same trap as I had. How many months did I lose to that suspicion again?
“Ugh... I feel I’ll be able to learn something with just some more...”
Some more what? “We don’t have a lot of time. If you’re really curious, search for relevant records once we’re outside.”
When I drew the line, Raven set aside her lingering disappointment and did as I said. Whatever the case, she hated being a nuisance. Simply put, she was easy to handle. “Okay then, let’s go.”
After that, we searched around the tombstone, the reason being that there might be something nearby. We couldn’t travel far with our remaining time anyway, so no one complained.
It should appear sometime around now...
After we had spent about two hours searching, Missha pointed off into the distance and shouted, “Bjorn! Look! Look over there!”
“...A house?”
In the middle of a forest full of monsters where everything was on fire was a two-story brick house.
Phew, we won’t have to come here next time.
This was exactly the place I was looking for.
The blackened wooden door swung open effortlessly.
Creak.
Geez, that sound. It was annoying me so I just tore the door off and tossed it to the ground.
“Um, can you please not break everything?”
“...Nagging.”
“I’m not nagging—”
“Got it. I’ll be careful.” Just for breaking one door...
“...This place is spooky.”

The interior was little more than ruins. We confirmed that there were no monsters with magic, but because there could be a trap, we carefully searched the place. Still, it didn’t take long. Everything from the sofa to the outer wall was burnt down, leaving just the skeleton of the house. We finished searching the first floor in an instant and went up to the second floor. In a room that looked like it used to be a bedroom, we found a book.
“Raven! It’s your favorite thing!”
The book was relatively intact, probably because it was inside a drawer. Of course, the outside was completely charred, but there were some normal pages inside too.
Was this always here?
This was an item I hadn’t ever found in the game.
Stars in her eyes, Raven took the book from Ainar and opened it. “It is written in the ancient language.”
“Can you read it?”
“Yes. This is my specialty. It looks like a diary.” As if to show off her knowledge, Raven started reading down the page. The contents were quite interesting.
Day 192. The rescue team did not come today, either. Now there are only three of us left in the expedition. Tarvian suggested building a house, and I agreed. Devil meat tastes disgusting, as usual.

Day 271. We finished building a decent-looking house. The three of us drank the wine we had saved. I don’t know how long it has been since we laughed and chatted like this. God damn it, if only Zephyros didn’t get drunk and start saying weird things, I’d still be in a good mood. What’s the point of living when the world has ended, you ask? Even if everything burns down, there is still hope. The fact that we are still alive is proof of that.
Day 467. Tarvian is pregnant. Whose child could it be? Neither I nor Zephyros asked. Ah, Tarvian. The wisest and most pitiful woman of all. I am desperate for a drink today.

Day 672. No, 673? I don’t know, but something big happened. The Orb of Fire began to lose its power. Already the outer walls are getting scorched by fire. Only our wizard, Tarvian, can fix it. But even if she sacrifices her life to prolong its duration, what is the point?

Day 711. Zephyros and I have agreed on something for the first time in a long time. Today, we die. If the world has not yet ended by the witch’s hand and if someday someone finds this place, I hope you use the object in the basement to save the world.
The writer’s name was missing from the diary and only four pages were still intact. However, as Raven read the last words, she was seized with shock. “Witch...”
“Why are you so surprrrised?”
“I wondered if this could be the case since it’s written in the ancient language, but... The person who wrote this diary is from our dimension!”
“Hmm?” Missha gave her a look that seemed to say, So what?

Raven didn’t have the presence of mind to kindly explain it to her. “Why? Ah, is it because this is another dimension? Is that why these records from back then are still here? No, but how did these people get here?” Raven muttered to herself as if to organize her thoughts. Surprisingly, however, that wasn’t the case for long. “Basement! Let’s go underground immediately! If these words are true, there must be something there.”
“Good idea.”
Going back down to the first floor and clearing out the collapsed furniture revealed the way to the basement. It was quite dark, so we used light sphere magic.
Trudge, trudge.

When we descended, we found a small space of about one hundred square feet. It looked like it had once been used as a warehouse for food and storage, but there was a box that clearly looked valuable inside as well.
“I’ll open it,” I offered.
“Ah, will you?”
Finally, being put in charge of things like this was paying off.
That seemed natural, right?
As I thought that, I opened the box. Inside was a single marble. Before Raven could say anything, I put my hand on it.
[You have been registered as the user of the Orb of Fire.]
This was a bound item.

chapters.title: Chapter 172: Burning (4)
paragraphs: Twinkle!

Once it registered its user, the Orb of Fire began to glow. However, after that, no matter what we did, there was no reaction whatsoever. Even Raven gave up after poking at it for a while. “I think... this will have to be appraised by a special appraiser back in the city.”
“Are we taking this?”
“Sorry? What do you mean?”
No, I mean...
I decided to be honest. “I thought you might suggest taking the book instead. Saying it has great historical value or something.”

“Well, it’s not that I don’t want it.” Instead of getting angry, Raven readily agreed with my assumption. “But the writer of the diary said themself that we should take this and use it. It’s clear that this orb is more valuable than the diary. Plus, I already memorized everything and made a video recording just in case.”
“Uh... I see?”
“Yes. So don’t worry about that.”
Afterward, Raven cast distortion magic on the Orb of Fire. Now, even if the team discovered the bind on it before we left this place, Raven wouldn’t be able to undo the spell.
I should only let them find out what this thing is once we’re back in the city so it won’t seem suspicious.

Yes, that was the best course of action. As far as they knew, I didn’t know anything, so any binding that may or may not have happened was a complete accident. Although my conscience was pricked... It wasn’t like I took this item for my own good. The Orb of Fire was an item for the entire team. Therefore, the benefits would be shared by all of us for as long as we were still members of the same party.
“...It doesn’t seem like there’s anything else.”
We searched the house for about thirty more minutes but there wasn’t anything notable inside, even though I figured there might be another feature that hadn’t appeared in the game like the diary.
“So, what should we do?”
“Isn’t it obvious? We should continue hunting.”
“...I thought you’d say that.”
Like the money-grubbing adventurers we were, we spent our remaining time frugally hunting monsters. And after a while...
[You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
It was time to return.

Sunshine for the first time in a month. As if to photosynthesize, I took some time to bask in the warmth before moving on to the checkpoint dedicated to mid-level adventurers ranked six or higher. As I waited there, everyone except Mr. Bear gathered.
“Where is Urakburak?”
I mean, do you really need to ask?

Since we had been hunting right up until the moment we left the labyrinth, I didn’t have the energy to answer that. After a short wait, Mr. Bear finally arrived. Beside him was an unfamiliar adventurer.
“Here.”
“Ah, thanks. Thanks to you I was able to find it.”
“Haha, and thanks to you, I got to experience all sorts of things.” After that questionable bit of praise, the adventurer casually headed off to their own party.
Mr. Bear smiled, embarrassed, and joined us. “Haha, the line is quite long now.”
That’s because we’re late thanks to you.

The sighs kept coming but I didn’t say anything. I was the party’s leader. Everyone had their pros and cons. I had to try and embrace their flaws as well. I also had a somewhat higher tolerance for this stuff thanks to my Team Half-Wit days.
He does fight brilliantly, this guy.
Anyway, as we all got in line and waited, Missha and Mr. Bear started chatting. “Standing here all togetherrr like this, I feel like I’ve really made it.”
“Haha, I guess I can see why you might feel that way. Parties are recognized from rank six on.”
“Yes. I feel like I’m a full-fledged adventurrrer now. It feels really strange...”

Actually, I was feeling the same thing. In the past, we all had to gather after passing through different checkpoints for each of our individual ranks. The line dedicated to rank six cleared out quickly. The number of adventurers passing through this checkpoint was far fewer than the number at the rank-nine checkpoint, but there were double the staff. There were even individual rooms for privacy.
“Team Apple Narak... is that right?” The administrative staff member looked down at our team registration with an impressive poker face.
After going through some simple administrative procedures, we handed over the bags of mana stones we had collected—about seven of them, and all of them hefty.

When the staff member opened all the bags to confirm that they were full of mana stones, their eyes widened. Of course, before long, those same eyes narrowed significantly. That almost threw me back to the time I was dragged into the guild’s prison, but Raven handled the matter, as she was pro-conversation.

“All of these mana stones were obtained fairly by killing monsters. There are video recordings to prove it. Of course, if you want to confirm that, you’ll have to pay appropriate compensation for disclosing our achievements to others.”
“I believe... that won’t be necessary.”
“Then can you hurry up and exchange those, please?”

Perhaps she was tired, or the staff member’s look had pissed her off, but Raven was more irritable than usual. It seemed that the staff member might have picked up on the menace radiating from her because they worked quickly and finished the exchange in no time. “25.19 million stones.”

This was an amount that only clans could achieve. Divided by five, that was five million stones each. If we continued earning like this every month, our annual salary would be a whopping sixty million stones!
God bless the Burning Zone.
Even if we took down dozens of monsters each battle, it would be impossible to earn this much without that x2 bonus.
“Ha...” Air left my lungs in a rush. That was how strange this felt. It felt like just yesterday that I exchanged my first mana stones for 180,000 stones and earned the respect of my barbarian peers.
“S-So, how many cotton candies is that?”
“Uh... You won’t go bankrrrupt even if you eat ten every day for the rest of your life?”
And the fact that this amount had come not from the equipment of plunderers but purely from mana stones was inspiring. Well, it’d be hard to earn this much every time, though.
We found it very early this time.

I had discovered the black moss earlier than expected and hadn’t had to wait long before a Mila Roden appeared. Not to mention, the distortion spell succeeded in one try. It would be unrealistic to expect our next expedition to run this smoothly.
“...We’re doing the loot distribution tomorrow, right?” Raven asked as soon as we left the checkpoint. From the look in her eyes, the answer was already decided.

“Let’s do it the day after tomorrow while we’re at it.” I had no intention of doing it today, either. Not only had we cut back on sleep to hunt, we stayed awake until midnight on the last day. Considering our usual routine was to set up camp at 9-10 p.m., it was way past our bedtime.
“The day after tomorrow?”
“Yes, because we have to sell the equipment and remains too.”
“Oh, that... Could you sell those for us, Mr. Yandel? I really don’t think I can wake up tomorrow.”
“I thought we could leave the appraisal part to you since you’re certified?”
Raven pursed her lips. It seemed she had never dreamed that her bragging would come back at her like a boomerang.
“It’s not just equipment, but magical ingredients too. That’s something only a wizard can handle.”
“...Then you’ll come with me. Even a barbarian can handle being a porter for a day, right?”
Porter, my ass. From someone who carried a subspace ring, the request was absurd, but I just said yes. I was curious about how a wizard navigated the marketplace, anyway.

“Then I’ll see you then.” After setting up a meeting time, we decided to split up to head to our respective lodgings. “Then I’ll be going first.” Raven yawned and left for her personal laboratory in the Magic Tower.
“Abman, can you find the way?” asked Missha.
“Don’t worry. I know the way home from the checkpoint.”
“Wow, so you can at least find your house.”
Mr. Bear headed to the tavern, where his wife was waiting.
“All rrright, let’s go too.”
“Missha, can’t we eat something before that? I-I’m so hungry...”
“Let’s eat together after we wash up first.”
“Ugh, I’ll try to survive until then.”
We went off to our nest.
At 1 p.m. the next day, while Missha and Ainar slept in at the inn, I prepared to go out. I had to go sell the loot with Raven.
“Ah, then drop my equipment off at the rrrepair shop for me.”
“...Can you do mine too?”
I even brought their equipment with me. It was a bit disappointing that neither of them offered to come with but, well, I was the party’s leader. I could suffer this much for the sake of the team.
“You’re one minute late.”
“Shall I pay the late fee?”
“Do I look like a beggar?”
Why was this one so prickly?
Ah, because she couldn’t sleep longer.
I decided in my infinite generosity to let it slide. Raven was not the party’s leader, yet she had been dragged here just for being a wizard, so of course she wasn’t pleased.
I wonder if she likes sweets. I’ll have to try feeding her some later.
As I recalled this bit of worldly wisdom I had learned from my ex-girlfriend, we got on the carriage headed to Kommelby. On the way, there wasn’t a hint of friendly conversation. We both passed out.
“That was a good nap...” Raven yawned.
When I woke up, the carriage had arrived. Because we didn’t meet early in the morning, we decided to move fast. Ah, but first, I put something sweet in her mouth.
“Mm, I ‘on’t like ‘weet stuff...”
“Look me in the eye if you want to say something like that.”
“Ugh, this hurts my pride.”

Anyway, today’s agenda was simple: sell the Mila Roden’s remains to a magic shop, visit the forge in the center to drop off some equipment for repair, get rid of the masked assailant’s equipment, put the expandable backpack and the Ifrit’s essence up on the Exchange, and, while there, call for the special appraiser and get an appraisal of the Orb of Fire.
“This... is a very valuable item,” the appraiser told us. “Only a few large clans have one in their possession.”
“So what is it?”
“It is an Orb of Fire. When activated, it reduces fire damage within a fifteen-yard radius without consuming Soul Power.”
“How do you activate it?”
“There is an activation word. I’ll write it down here so you don’t forget.”

The cost of the special appraisal was a whopping three hundred thousand stones. As soon as I heard that, my stomach hurt. Seriously, these guys just sat back and raked in the cash. “So, what is the appraised value?”
“Oh, I didn’t mention, but only the one who first acquired the orb can use it.”
“Sorry? I beg your pardon?” Raven shifted her gaze to me. But what could you do? It was an accident, I tell you.
Sigh...
Her sigh seemed to contain many emotions.
We were about to leave after finishing our business when the appraiser made a request. “Oh, would it be possible to learn where you found this?”
“No. We have no intention of disclosing our achievements,” said Raven.
“Well, if you change your mind, please come find me. It just so happens that the clans that acquired the orb are also keeping their mouths shut. I will pay a fair price.”
“Okay, we will.”

Once we left the auction house, our to-do list for the day was complete. Given how methodically we handled things, there was still a lot of time left until the last carriage, so we had a quick meal near the platform.
“Raven, I’m just letting you know, I didn’t know about the orb.”
“Did I say otherwise? What, you thought I was going to make you reimburse me?”
Uh... you’re not? I most definitely thought that.
“It’s fine. Even the appraiser said so himself that it’s a magic item that’s used more as a communal asset than a personal item.”
“Yes, I will only use it for the party.”
The issue I had been worried about had been easily resolved, so I settled in to eat comfortably and brought up something I was curious about. “But why did you decline that offer earlier?”
“You mean telling them where we found the orb?”
“Yeah, it sounded like they were going to pay a good price.”
“Not really. If we tell them, they’ll probably make several times more on the information. I refuse to let that happen.”
Well, vendors everywhere always had the easiest jobs.

“Most importantly, if the place we acquired it becomes common knowledge, more people will learn about that book. That can’t happen either. I’m going to do proper research into this in the future and turn the academic world upside down.”
Now I saw there was another reason she had made the decision she had. What was so important about reputation? I couldn’t relate to her motive, but I supposed everyone had their own goals.
“Anyway, I hope we continue to work together in the future.”
“What’s this all of a sudden?”
“I think an ancient secret related to that witch is hidden in the labyrinth for some reason. I’ve decided to look for it.”
“Hmm... so?”
“I’m going to continue working as an adventurer. By your side.”
I didn’t know why she was emphasizing the fact that she’d be working alongside me like that. When I stared at her, Raven grinned.
“I got this feeling in the Bloody Citadel, too, but you’re blessed when it comes to these things, Mr. Yandel. I feel like things are about to get more interesting in the future.”
She wants to experience interesting things by staying by my side, huh? I chuckled.
“You can count on me. A wizard’s intuition is more accurate than you think,” she said.
I suppose she was right. When it came to a wizard’s intuition, you could count on it.

chapters.title: Chapter 173: Choice (1)
paragraphs: The day after I went to Kommelby with Raven, the entire party gathered at the tavern for the final payout.
“We really made a lot of money.”
Mana stone income: 25.19 million. Expandable backpack and miscellaneous equipment: 3.01 million. The Ifrit’s essence minus the test tube: 9 million. The Mila Roden’s remains: 750,000.
A total of 37.95 million stones.

Of course, it wasn’t fair to divide this into five equal parts. For the mana stones, it was agreed that Ainar would take 15 percent and Mr. Bear would take 25 percent. The essence and Mila Roden’s remains were special loot, so Raven took 40 percent.
Let’s see, then my share is... 7.1 million and 2,500 stones.
For the record, my share was exactly the same as Missha’s.
“Miss Ainar gets 5,843,000 stones.”
“Ooh!”
“Now, what are you going to do about the cost of the essence?”
“Uh, the essence...? How much was that?” Her delight about the ridiculously high number was short-lived, and Ainar soon wore an expression of confusion.
“...I’ll pay with her.” I took 2,157,000 stones from my share and gave them to Raven.
“What about Miss Karlstein?”
“Ah, I’ll let Ainar pay me back laterrr.”
“Well, if you say so. Uh... wait, then Miss Ainar gets paid nothing today.”

Was that a problem? Although she had worked hard in the labyrinth, her debt had only increased. She owed 4 million to Missha and 7.5 million to me (if you included the cost of the equipment I had bought her last month) for a total of 11.5 million stones.
“I-Impossible...! I had money but now I don’t! S-Something is wrong!”
“That’s how the worrrld works. Still, you’re much stronger now with the essence.”

Unlike Missha, who comforted her with words, I decided to give her a tangible reward. “Anyway, I hope we can raise Ainar’s share soon.” She had a rank-five essence now. It was hard to argue that Ainar’s combat power was below average anymore.
“Ah, I don’t mind.”
“...From the next expedition on, I’ll only take 20 percent.” Mr. Bear readily agreed, so Ainar’s share of the mana stones was raised to 20 percent. It was now an even split.
Whew, I wish I could adjust the ratio for the special loot too... But Raven will definitely go into a rage if I suggest it, so I’ll do that another time.

Actually, now that I thought about it, this was a bit unfair. I was the tank, the leader, and now even a scout despite not having experience. Plus, I spoon-fed them all the hidden features. Shouldn’t I get at least 30 percent?
“Ah, then, once everyone pays the team fund, today’s business is over.”
“How much was the team fund?”
“Three hundred thousand stones per person.”
“Are you taking more money?!” Ainar’s debt increased by another three hundred thousand stones. Well, that didn’t matter considering I fed and housed her, anyway.
Three days after splitting the loot, while Missha went out with Ainar to apply for a promotion to rank six, I lay down on my bed to get my thoughts in order.
I’ve already earned another ten million stones, excluding the money lent to Ainar and the money in the shared account with Missha.
My growth had accelerated now that I’d reached the fifth floor. Now that I could play proactively, I could leverage my knowledge of the game to the fullest. I sketched out a rough plan.
I’ll lay the foundation on the fifth floor and then climb up to the sixth after just one year.
Of course, once I reached the sixth floor, it would be difficult to advance as quickly since you couldn’t clear it with combat power alone. Starting from there on, I’d be in for a long slog.
But on that floor, I can absorb that essence.
As long as I had a formidable enemy like the Dragon Slayer gunning for me, I needed to become stronger as soon as possible.
Even if that wasn’t the case, considering the social climate these days, my current status isn’t good enough.
Recently, the air in the city had grown heavy. To be more precise, the adventurer industry was tense and on edge. Which made sense, considering what had happened.

Four hundred and seventy-one people had died on the fourth floor during this expedition alone. You couldn’t even compare this tragedy to the deaths caused by the Lord of the Floor on the third floor months ago. These people had died at the hands of plunderers, not monsters, in a large-scale terrorist attack targeting veteran adventurers who had been in and out of the labyrinth for nearly ten years.
“Bjorn!” Just as I was thinking that, Missha rushed into the room after running here from the guild, a piece of paper in hand. “L-Look at this! The palace issued a notice to adventurers!”

I quickly took the paper and read it. The announcement stated that the kingdom had drawn up a war plan and that rewards would be given to adventurers rank six or higher who participated. The target of their conquest was Noark.
There will be an uproar.

The underground city was something of an open secret. The people who knew about it knew about it, but 99 percent of people didn’t even know it existed. However, the palace had now mentioned it in an official notice.
“Bjorn, what are you going to do?”
“I don’t know.”

The reward was quite attractive: a custom amount of money per person and a three-year exemption from taxes. Plus, the palace would bestow one essence in their possession on one lucky person based on their achievements, so many would be tempted.
Looks like they’ve already recruited super-mega clans too.

The announcement also included the names of clans that had already agreed to participate. They’d probably been given a much greater reward. It was a sort of publicity stunt. Just the participation of large clans alone would increase the trust of ordinary adventurers. No, they’d even consider it a good opportunity and think it foolish not to participate.
“Anyway, what I want to say is, don’t participate.”

Recalling Baekho’s advice, I made up my mind. “We are not participating.” I refused to play monkey in the middle. Besides, weren’t we already progressing at a good rate? It was hard to see the merit of participating in a conquest.
“I see... I’m glad. I don’t have a good feeling about this...”
“Just to be sure, I’ll meet with Raven and Abman to tell them. Oh, how did Ainar react?”
“She was looking forward to the opportunity to rrrise to fame. Don’t worry, though. I’ll make sure to properly explain it to her.”
“Then I’ll leave it to you.”
After speaking with Missha, I headed to the Magic Tower. What would a wizard think of all this? It turned out the answer was rather straight-forward.
“Ah, that announcement... I heard it last night too. I was going to ask, but I’m glad you won’t participate.”
“Are you against it too?”

“Yes. I’m curious about the underground city, but however they package it, this is just a war. I don’t want to get involved in a fight over rights like that.” Whatever the reward may have been, Raven was not particularly interested in it. That was fortunate for many reasons.
Afterward, I received a similar answer at Mr. Bear’s tavern. “Everyone has been talking about that all day here, but I have my doubts. Well, the reward sounds nice, but...”

Mr. Bear admitted that if he had still been working solo, he might have joined the fight. Well, this man was almost forty years old. Three years’ worth of tax exemption was huge. He was practically taking care of his wife’s share of the taxes alone right now.
“Haha, but our child will be born next year. My taxes will be reduced for twenty years thanks to the childbirth tax credit, so I’m not in a hurry.”
“I see.”
“If you guys are sitting this out, I have no intention of joining, either.”
Okay, so our team had officially passed up on the conquest.
I’ll learn about the details at Ghost Busters once it opens.

For now, there was nothing I could do. I was about to head back to my inn to review my list of things I had to do in the city this month when Mr. Bear made an unexpected suggestion. “Yandel, how about a drink later?”
“A drink?”
“You’re the leader of a party now. From the looks of it, you don’t seem to have any connections in this regard.”
“So?”
“There is a meeting of fifth-floor adventurers this evening. Why don’t you go with me?”
Hmm, networking... To be honest, I’m not up for it.
However, it was common for adventurers to hang out and exchange information. It wouldn’t be bad to try it out at least once.
Plus, since the Watchers of the Round Table only have high-level information, it’s hard to learn about this side of the job from them.
“Fine. When and where is it?”

After getting the time and place, I headed to the library to pass the time. Ragna greeted me, looking as aloof as usual. I wondered how she’d heard this news, given she was in the library all the time.
“Do you have something to say to me?”
“Are you... joining the conquest?”
“No, our party has decided not to participate.”
Ragna’s expression brightened a bit. “I see. That’s a relief...”
The comment seemed strangely suspicious to me, so I flat-out asked, “Relief? Do you know something about Noark?”
“I... don’t know much about that. But I know what kind of people the royal family are... Enormous sacrifices are sure to follow,” Ragna answered, her voice dark.
“The royal family?”
Ragna suddenly looked like she had said something she shouldn’t have, and withdrew her statement. “Please ignore what I just said.”
I didn’t bother pressing her, though. I knew how dangerous it was to slander the royal family. “Thanks for your concern.”

“Concern...” Ragna chewed on that word. What followed was unexpected. I thought she would correct me and say she wasn’t worried about me, like she usually would. “Yes. I was concerned, but I’m really glad.”
“Uh... right.” This baffled me. However, after she blurted that out, her neck reddened in embarrassment. I pretended not to notice. “...So, can you cast the spell? I want to go read now.”
“Oh, right. Magic. Sure.”
I didn’t want to make this more awkward.

Ten at night was normally the time I would have washed up and gotten ready for bed. However, I was instead at a bar I’d never been to, not in District Seven where I lived, but across a wall in District Eight.
“Abman! Long time no see! How have you been?”
“About the same. And you?”

“Haha! Still living as long as death evades me!” We entered a private room that had about a dozen adventurers inside. It seemed this man with the warm vibe was the organizer of this meeting. “Who is your friend next to you?”
“He is the leader of our party.”
“Oh? I wondered who might have taken you in. I guess the lucky guy is right here?”
As soon as we entered the room, our host kicked off a brief round of introductions.
“I am Perpe Derves. Call me what you want. You can just call me Pepe too. It’s a nickname only used by my close friends.”
Pepe... That was an overly cute nickname for a bearded man. “...I’ll go with Derves.”
“Sure.”
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Can I call you Bjorn?”
“Do as you wish.” Our titles were agreed upon with adventurer-like speed.

“Wait, Bjorn Yandel? That sounds familiar.” One of the adventurers tilted his head and a moment later recalled where he had heard it. “Ah, Little Balkan! The barbarian who made his name against the Lord of the Third Floor! Am I right?”
“That’s right.”
When I readily admitted it, Derves’s gaze shifted to one of surprise, and slight doubt. “Oh, so this is only your first year?”
“Don’t focus on that. We were on the fifth floor this time.” With Mr. Bear’s assistance, the doubts were totally cleared and only admiration remained.
“Reaching the fifth floor in less than a year... how amazing.”
Afterward, Derves introduced the other participants one by one. With Little Balkan’s fame and my explosive growth behind me, everyone’s reception was positive. Except for one person.
“I’m Jack Johnsonville, belonging to the rank-five Nevis Wolf Clan.” The tanned, blond man introduced himself with a somewhat aggressive look on his face.
Why is he opening his eyes like that? Does he wanna die?
My body itched to act on my barbarianized thoughts, but I endured it with superhuman patience. After all, I was one of the few modern people in this world. Of course I should be able to handle that.
Sensing the chill in the air, Derves dispelled the tension with a toast. “Haha, then let’s drink.”
The meeting started like that. Everyone drank casually and exchanged friendly or business-related conversations.
“How is it? Not bad, right?” Mr. Bear whispered in my ear.
I chuckled and nodded. I had assumed there would be a lot of trash-talking since it was a gathering of adventurers, but this wasn’t that bad. Well, there was one bastard stirring the pot, though.

“Why don’t we meet somewhere other than an old bar next time?” asked Jack Johnsonville. “There is a tavern affiliated with our clan, and the drinks are amazing. Of course, it’s much more expensive than here. Hahaha... The conquest? We should all participate. Oh, perhaps it’s scary for party units like you guys. Work hard, though. You never know. Maybe you’ll catch a talent scout’s eye and get to join a clan.”

He was the only person in this gathering who was a member of a clan, and the bastard continued to brag about it. This son of a bitch also ruined the conversation every time any attention landed on me.
“I can’t help but ask. Yandel, what is your secret? How did you rise up the ranks so quickly?”
“Isn’t it obvious? He found a good party.”
“...Haha, finding a good party is a skill in itself.”

Every time a silence came over us, Derves tried his best to put a bow on it and brush aside any disputes. “A-Anyway, Bjorn. How about you? I would like to hear your impressions of our meeting since this is your first time attending.”
Should I tell them the truth or not? I thought about it for a while, but I had already decided on an answer. “I like it.”
“Pft, of course he does. He’s a rookie who just reached the fifth floor.”

I was a K-barbarian with the spirit of a modern man, the philosophy of a Confucian, and the boldness of a savage. If I had to, I could be patient. I was confident in my ability to withstand insults even worse than this.
“What the hell is this stupid son of a bitch going on about?”
“W-What? Are you talking to me right now?”
“Is there another stupid son of a bitch here besides you?”
However, when I didn’t have to be patient, I was not. That was how a K-Barbarian operated.

chapters.title: Chapter 174: Choice (2)
paragraphs: Elders first—this was one of the three fundamental principles and five moral tenets of Confucianism that outlined the hierarchy between children and adults. But when in Rome, you had to do as the Romans did.
Age means nothing in this world.
In Rafdonia, hierarchy was determined based on individual strength, and separated the weak and the strong. According to that law, I had zero reasons to put up with this man.
“...It seems the chick doesn’t know his place.”
“Do you want to be beaten up by a chick?” When I stood up, the air in the room instantly turned murderous.
“What?” The tanned blond was startled, as if no one had ever come out swinging like this before.
Mr. Bear quietly put his hand on my arm, a gesture to stop. “Yandel.”
At this, the chicken regained his triumphant smile. “Why don’t you listen to your teammate? If you apologize on your knees, I’ll let this slide.”
What was this prick talking about? I just challenged him to a duel instead. “Shut up and let’s fight.”

This was the only type of personal dispute permitted by the city. If you agreed to a duel and it was fought fairly in the presence of a notary, it was not classified as assault. Although if he died, it would be a headache. But to prevent that, I just had to rein in my strength.
“...Do you realize what a duel means?”
“I don’t care. I just want to crush your head.”

“Deranged bastard...” I guess he’d never met such a savage adventurer before because Blondie looked completely lost. Well, I was sure he didn’t suspect he would be challenged to a duel today after coming to a party to brag.
“What are you thinking so hard about? Are you afraid this chick will beat you up?”
“...I have no reason to deal with a madman.” Blondie snorted and stood up.
So that’s the tactic you’re going with.
The mental high ground of not wanting to stoop to a madman’s level, huh... The method for handling that was simple. “Chicken.”

With one word, the blood vessels on Blondie’s forehead stood up. I guess he didn’t want to speak to me, though, because he took his anger out on Derves, who was next to him. “Pepe, you should be more picky about who you invite. Hanging out with a barbarian like that will drag your reputation down too.”
Derves made no reply. To be exact, he didn’t have the chance to. The tanned blond whipped around and headed to the exit after saying that.
Trudge, trudge.
His back was straight and his gait cocky, but I noticed visible proof that Blondie was feeling both humiliation and contempt.
“Abman, did you see? His face is red.”

“Yeah, I guess he knows shame.” Even Mr. Bear, who tried to stop me at first, didn’t hesitate to dunk on him with me. If you couldn’t beat ‘em, join ‘em—this was a highly desirable mindset for a teammate of mine to have. However, I guess this insult was hard to bear.
Step.
Soon, Blondie’s feet stopped in front of the doorway.
“Oh, he stopped. I wonder if he’ll accept my duel.”
“Of course he won’t. It’s obvious this punk is nothing without his clan.”
Blondie whipped his head around and looked at me. When I glared at him tauntingly, he spoke through gritted teeth. “Barbarian, don’t think you can act up just because you’ve gotten some petty fame.”
“Okay, and?”
“With that attitude, you won’t ever get higher than the fifth floor.”

I laughed without meaning to. Who did he think he was? “That’s funny,” I said, slowly walking forward. “I don’t know how long you’ve been an adventurer, but you’re the idiot who chickened out against a newbie like me. You’re the one who can’t hunt on the fifth floor without a clan, and who’ll spend the rest of his life picking up breadcrumbs on the fifth floor. I’m the one who reached the fifth floor in just eight months. I’m the one with a nickname, unlike you, and who formed my own team to climb even higher. I’m the one who’s already recognized for my potential and talked about as the successor of the barbarian tribe’s chief.” Standing right in front of him now, I patted him on the shoulder. “Now, which one of us will be on the upper floors in a few years’ time?”
Blondie couldn’t say anything to that. Standing at his average human height of 5′7″, he could only look up at me.
I kindly lowered my face so I could speak into his ear. “Now, get lost. If you want to go tattle to your clan, that’s up to you.”
When I opened the door for him, Blondie left in a daze.
Slam.
I closed it immediately. When I turned around, everyone was looking at me. I went back to my seat and sat down. “Problem solved. Let’s keep drinking.”
Strangely, no one said anything.
Geez, you’re making me embarrassed. Have you never seen a barbarian solve things with words before?
The silence was short-lived. The surprise at the sudden incident subsided and we chatted while clinking glasses. The main topic, of course, was Jack Johnsonville, that cowardly wimp.
“Hahaha, did you see his face when you challenged him to a duel? I’ll never forget it as long as I live.”
To my surprise, no one berated me. Well, if he was aggravating someone he’d just met, he had to have been even worse to them. “But why did you keep inviting him?”
“He may be condescending, but he told us information that only a clan member could know.”
Hmm, I guess his loose lips were useful in some ways. If so, I felt a bit bad.
“Don’t worry too much. We haven’t been playing along with him much recently so he’s been coming less. He would’ve gone somewhere else soon enough.”
“If you say so.”
“Oh, and one more thing. You won’t have to worry about him. He’s at the bottom of his clan, so he won’t dream of retaliating against you.”
“Haha, Pepe. That’s not the problem. With his personality, he’ll be too mortified to say anything and keep it to himself.”
“Hmm, maybe. Well, if he does say something, it’ll just get him treated like a fool by his clan.”
Nice and neat. Impatience was the right answer here.
Even if the clan does retaliate, what are they going to do? Ambush us in the labyrinth?
If a large clan was ever caught doing that, they’d be severely punished. They would never cross a line like that for a low-level grunt.
All they can do is try to limit experience points at worst.

They could abuse their power to prevent us from gaining experience points in a certain area. I didn’t know about one specific zone, but the fifth-floor clans had close relationships with each other. Therefore, ending up on their blacklist would result in enormous restrictions on your ability to level up. This didn’t apply to me, though. To start with, I had no intention of paying for experience points, anyway. Why would I pay the clans when I could just hunt in the mirror?
“Come on, let’s drink, then!”
As the drinking party continued, talk about Blondie gradually subsided. What replaced him was the topic of Noark’s conquest.
“Bjorn, your party won’t be participating?”
“Yes, I have a bad feeling. Derves, what are you going to do?”
“We’ve already decided to put one foot in. The labyrinth is just as dangerous.”
“I see.”
“Most of us here will probably do the same. The rewards are enticing. If you do the math, it’s money you’d only be able to earn after over a year of adventuring.”
“I wish you a safe return.”
“Haha, thank you.”

I didn’t bother saying anything about that decision. There was no one here with less adventuring experience than me. They were not going to change their minds because of a stranger’s advice, and it went against etiquette too. Even a barbarian should stay in their lane when it came to certain things.
“It’s getting late. Let’s start going home. Abman, you’ll be in trouble with your wife.”
“...I told her I’m with Yandel, so it’s okay.”
“Oh? Your wife seems to have a very good opinion of this guy, then.”
The meeting ended after 2 a.m. Actually, one or two people left before that for their own reasons, but I stayed until the very end.
“Will you come again next time?”
“If you invite me.”
“Okay, I’ll let you know through Abman.”

I wasn’t able to get any useful information right away. All I got was a glimpse into the mindset and logic of regular adventurers. But I planned to participate next time, too, assuming they returned alive. I was curious how the conquest would go.
“Thanks to you, I drank well!”
When we got out onto the street, the chilly night air wrapped around my skin. When I first got here, it was early spring. Now, autumn was coming to an end. “Let’s go.”
“Haha! Yes, let’s go!”

Mr. Bear was much more cheerful than usual, probably because he’d chugged down all that alcohol. In fact, he had drunk so much that it was surprising he could even stand up properly, but his mind seemed sober. That didn’t mean he could find his way home, though.
I feel like I’ve gotten closer to him tonight.
The carriages had stopped running by now, so I walked all the way to District Seven to drop Mr. Bear off.

Mrs. Bear was infinitely kind to me, perhaps because of all the money her husband had earned from this expedition. “Thank you for bringing him home. Would you like to stay and rest for a bit? I have something perfect for a hangover.” After being treated to hot honey water, I headed home.
Home, huh?
The word stuck to my mouth now.
Click.
As I unlocked the door, the one behind me opened at the same time: Room 207, Missha’s room. “Mmm, you’rrre back now?”
“Oh, were you awake?”
“Why werrre you so late? Why do you smell like alcohol?”
I lingered in the hallway for a while to tell her about the gathering I attended with Mr. Bear.

“Oh, right... You must be tirrred. You’re like a real leader now.” Exchanges like this were part of the job for adventurers. Missha patted me on the shoulder for my hard work. “But what’s that paperrr bag in your hand?”
“Oh, I bought some apple skewers at the night market on the way back.”
“Hm? But you don’t like those.”
“Don’t you two like them?”
Missha chuckled. “Nyaha, you’re like a dad.” Missha took a skewer from the bag and returned to her room with it in her mouth. I’d give the rest to Ainar tomorrow.
Click.
I set the bag down on the table and quickly washed up. Cool air slid in through the window, and I sobered up a bit.
Not bad.
This was one of those days when I started to have that thought more often.
After the gathering, slightly busier days followed. Now that we had money, it was time for an upgrade.
“Ainar, go get an Imprint from the holy land.”
“I don’t have money.”
“I will lend you some.”

“Th-that’s...!” When I first lent her money, Ainar had acted like she was receiving free cash, but as the number grew bigger, she was beginning to realize the size of her debt. “How much longer will I be broke!?”
Well, maybe a year or so? After that, I still planned to tell her what to spend the big money on every step of the way. Anyway, it took three days for her to get the stage three Imprint.
“You look better than I thought. Didn’t it hurt?”
“It hurt!”
“But?”
“But pain is natural for growth!”

Oh, right... that was right. Barbarians had a different mindset than ordinary people. Ainar’s imprint was Slayer, a typical imprint for warriors that bolstered various battle stats. For the third-stage Imprint, she chose Predation, a well-performing passive skill that restored a certain amount of Soul Power when you killed your opponent.
For now, let’s stop at stage three and raise it to stage six once we earn more.
Missha made progress in the meantime too. Ainar’s terrifyingly rapid growth was probably making her impatient. As a result, Missha spent most of the money she earned this time on Beast Blood.

“Bjorn! I finally did it!” She had finally achieved her first awakening with her Soul Beast. Her newly obtained power was Glacier Blessing, a top-notch, overpowered ability that reduced the energy consumption of ice-attribute skills and items by half.
I didn’t expect her to get that before the sword...
Were these reparations for past hardships? Ever since we reached the fifth floor, everything was going smoothly.
“But are you still going to use that equipment?”
“These are fine on the fifth floor.”

It wasn’t like I didn’t spend money, either. I sold the expandable backpack I’d been using up to now and used almost all of my money to purchase a subspace ring. A person’s heart could be so devious. Even the expandable backpack had started to feel uncomfortable now.
Well, I was going to change it later anyway, so I might as well buy it in advance.
Personal storage was a necessity in the labyrinth. You never knew if you’d be separated from your team. More importantly, it was possible to store divine items in subspace too.
There’s nothing in the world that can’t be done with money.
Determined to continue earning more money, I got ready to go out. I had a meeting with Rotmiller.
“Thankfully, you came on time today.”
“Well, I’m a scout now too.”
“Haha, I like your attitude.”

Since a few days ago, I’d been meeting up with Rotmiller every day to receive scout training. Of course, not for free. Like with blacksmiths and other skilled professionals in the Middle Ages, asking for free classes was straight-up theft. I’d been paying a considerable fee every day.

“I haven’t been to the fifth floor myself, so I can’t teach you how to get around there. But I’ve studied up on it a lot, so I can give you some advice. Oh, learning how to make a map would be a great help.”

I learned the basic knowledge required for a scout and a few tricks and bits of know-how that only experienced practitioners could tell me. On top of that, I was given special training to develop a better sense of direction. Little by little, I learned everything Rotmiller had worked hard for years to create.
“...Teaching you like this makes me think that it might not be a bad idea to set up a training center.”
“Good idea. Anyone would want to learn from you.”
“Haha, your flattery...”
After class with Rotmiller, I headed to the inn to have dinner with the others. Erwen joined us today.
“How do you always find me here? I might have gone out.”
“Mm... I just know. It’s an elf’s instinct, I guess.”
“You wish. You just keep coming until you find him.”
“Missha is right! You liar!”
“...Both of you, stop.”
Every time Erwen came around, these two got snippy. It wasn’t that I didn’t understand why. Barbarians hated elves, and Missha just didn’t like them.
I wish they’d get along since they might be teammates one day... Am I asking for too much? I might have to reconsider adding Erwen to the party.

As we ate, we learned what Erwen had been up to recently. Apparently, her sister had decided to join a clan as a contractor for a few months. Afterward, she said she would be hunting on the fifth floor. The life of a rich family, I guess.
“I’ll leave now! See you next week!”
After dinner, I headed up to my room, washed up, and spent time resting. It was late, but I didn’t bother sleeping.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn to a different world.]
After all, it was that day of the month.

chapters.title: Chapter 175: Choice (3)
paragraphs: In Hansu’s room was a double-sized bed, a wardrobe, a desk, and a computer.
I turned the computer on first and entered the chat room.
[Long Live Korea’s independence - 0 people are online.]
This was the same guy who thought I was dead just for logging in a few minutes late.
And we only have an hour together too.
Since something rather big had happened recently, I planned on getting as much information out of Baekho as possible.
I got here first today.

Before I could even sit down on the sofa in the spacious room full of antique furniture, Baekho logged in after me. Nothing out of the ordinary up to that point. “Bro!” But what was this? Just one look at his face and I could tell he was in a hurry. “I’m in battle right now, so I have to leave right away.”
“What?”
“I don’t have time to explain.”
“Wait—”
“You heard about the war of conquest, right? Don’t join it under any circumstances, even in the future. I’m just here to tell you that.”
“What do you m—”
“See you next month!”
That was the end of our conversation. After only a few seconds of showing his face, Baekho disappeared in a flash.
“What the...?” For a moment, my mind went blank. But if I sat down and thought this through... He was in battle?

One hour in the community was one second in reality. If he felt he had to leave in such a hurry, that meant that he must be fighting a strong enemy. One second in here would only be 0.02 seconds out there, which indicated that he felt he couldn’t waste even a short moment like that.
What the hell is he fighting against?
I didn’t know. Just one thing was for certain—that he was closely related to the conquest of Noark.
This punk, is he in the underground city?

It was late at night and we were not in the labyrinth, but he was fighting an enemy? No other possible explanations came to mind. It was only yesterday that the Rafdonian army had headed off to war. From the alliance between the king’s army and the adventurers to the battalion of paladins sent by the temple, the sight of them entering the sewers in formation had been quite a spectacle.
And his last words... must mean he believes the conquest will fail?
He told me not to join under any circumstances. I took this to mean that he thought that the first conquest would fail and a second army would be formed.
Ugh, this is so frustrating...

I wouldn’t get anything out of being here so I went back to my room. There were three hours left until the Watchers of the Round Table opened. With nothing to do, I started surfing the web. First, I checked the Exchange, then poked around the chat rooms that had no entry restrictions. They were all the same. Everyone was talking about the conquest of Noark.
...It’s already chaos down there.
The number of players who were participating in the takeover was many.
“I’m in the back so I can’t really tell but things aren’t looking good at all. I keep hearing explosions at the front but the fucking commander won’t tell us anything...”
“Why are there so few soldiers today? Are they all dead?”

Based on what they were saying, it seemed that even at this moment, a fierce battle was unfolding underground. I honestly couldn’t even imagine how intense things were there, especially after reading the posts on the community bulletin board.
[I’m about to die. Taking questions.]
I was stabbed in the neck, but when I opened my eyes, I was here. I’ll be alive for twelve seconds, right? Fuck this.
EdwardBless77: I hope this isn’t an eternal dream. I hope you wake up in your home.
└OP: I really hope so.
godFLEXyou: You did well. Get some rest.
└OP: Thanks for your compassion.
StevenCastle: I guess you were with a frontline unit. I heard it’s a living hell there right now. Have you run into anyone from Orcules?
└OP: I don’t know. I heard someone shout that something arrived but I don’t remember. Maybe they saw wrong. We couldn’t see a yard ahead of us thanks to those fucking dark wizards.
Teckmonkey: What do you want to do most?
└OP: Breed.
└Teckmonkey: Oh, um... I’m gonna keep my mouth shut.
Tunaboot: Where are you from?
└OP: I don’t know where you’re asking about. On Earth, Canada. Here, Aribeten Clan. I was executive level.
└Tunaboot: Of course I meant hometown. But Aribeten executive? You were a big man.
└OP: Doesn’t matter now that I’m about to die. Goodbye.
└Ionboii: Wow, if you’re revealing this much information, I guess you’re not a troll. I sincerely hope you rest in peace. Good work. And just ignore the idiots saying garbage above.
There were dozens more under that too. Even as the comments piled up, the original poster answered each one. As if in a trance, I read through all the comments and made one myself.
Elfnunna: Why are you giving up already? You should be trying to log out and live out this moment.

As long as you didn’t give up, there was still a chance. Although the possibility may be infinitely small, it still wasn’t zero yet. I was proof of that. But after posting that, I realized it might sound rude, so I added an explanation.

└Elfnunna: I’ve been stabbed in the neck, too, and entered a countdown state like in the game. But my body still moved. I finally killed my opponent and just barely survived. So why don’t you try that too?
With my experience in the Land of the Dead and Bloody Citadel, I wanted to give this stranger hope.
└OP: I know what you mean. But I’m an archer. I won’t be able to use the method you mentioned.
The answer that came back was one of complete resignation.
└Elfnunna: Can you give it a try, though?
I commented in that same trance. The answer came back quickly.
└OP: Sorry, if I have to die anyway, I want to die as myself. Not in this cursed body, but as my parents’ child.

My mind went blank as soon as I saw that. I took my hands off the keyboard. What could I possibly say here? That even if that were the case, this wasn’t his real body? That it was just a manifestation of his inner self? Well, no one could question the poster’s decision. They shouldn’t, either.
Without thinking, I turned to stare at the armoire. Or, to be more precise, at the mirror hanging next to it. I saw Hansu Lee.
Type, type.
I began typing again. I hope you rest in peace and I hope you wake up in the real world—I typed and deleted consolations like these repeatedly but I couldn’t bring myself to press Enter.
Type, type.
Even while I was slamming on the keyboard, unable to send anything, players continued to add comments and the OP answered each one.
Branbran_Helmet: Fucking garbage flop game.
└OP: Ikr, this fucking garbage flop game!
After that comment, there were no more. I hit refresh. Before I knew it, the OP’s nickname at the top went blurry. That meant he was dead.
I didn’t know why. I didn’t know his face, and I’d never talked to him in person, but my heart beat wildly.
Thump, thump.
I’d seen death countless times since waking up in this world. The weight of it felt heavier today, though. Why was that?
Drag.

As if in search of the answer, I scrolled up and read it all over again from the top. Thanks to all the people who had asked about his real self, it was possible to get a glimpse into this person’s life.
Drag.

He was from Canada. Born into a family of farmers, his real name was Mac Davis. His first kiss had been at seventeen... with his girlfriend’s best friend? He seemed like an oddball, but he hadn’t done anything in his life worth getting killed over.
Drag.

His dream had been to be a veterinarian. Seeing his childhood dog choke on its vomit had been the catalyst for that. But because he didn’t have the brains for it, he failed. He ended up helping his parents with their farm work and occasionally played games.
Drag.
Yes, he was a normal person, moderately nice, but occasionally remembered as a bad person to some... an ordinary human being no matter how you looked at it.
Drag.
