Soon, I stopped scrolling at one particular spot. I saw that there was a new comment below mine.
└OP: I keep thinking about what you said. Somehow, I get the sense that you’re a strong person. I hope you can clear this game and return home. Of course, that’s your choice, though.
He had left words of encouragement for me while I was repeatedly typing out and erasing those few sentences of condolence. I could feel how thoughtful this person was by his use of the word “choice.”
Type, type.
I typed out a new comment on the keyboard, although he wouldn’t be able to see it now.
└Elfnunna: If I go back, I’ll be sure to write a letter to the address you wrote above.
└Elfnunna: You worked hard.
Leaving behind meaningless comments, I left the post. Then I lay in bed for a while and let my mind wander in a daze. Time seemed to slip by.
Soon there were only three minutes left until the deadline to enter the Watchers of the Round Table. But what was this?
Creak.
As I rushed in, I found the room was empty. Crescent Moon, Goblin, Fox, Deer, and Clown were not here. I was the only one seated at the round table.
Did they all join the conquest?
No other explanation came to mind. Three hours in the community was only three seconds outside. What could be keeping them from spending those three seconds here?
I didn’t think I’d be ditched here too...
After Baekho, I’d been left alone once again. I didn’t even have time to be disappointed—my surroundings flashed and when I came to, I was back in my room.
[Minimum number of participants has not been met. This meeting has ended.]
A message floated on the monitor. So this was what happened if the entry deadline passed without enough participants. With that, the value of participating in the community today vanished.
Still, I should look around before I leave.
In the end, I had no choice but to surf the web and read through trivial news. Time passed like that and the time came to log off.
[You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
The familiar room and body of Bjorn felt a little unfamiliar today. Was I just tired?
Just go to sleep.
I cleared my head and lay down on the bed.
Creak.
As always, the bed caved in with a groan. Thus, another day came to an end.
Three days later, the troops that had headed for Noark returned. “Bjorn! C-Come out quickly! The army has returned from underrrground!”
Only about a third of them had survived. Soldiers passed us by on the street silently and with sinking shoulders. That was enough to tell us how things had gone.
It really failed.
Things were getting messy.

chapters.title: Chapter 176: Doppelganger (1)
paragraphs: Standing in front of the mirror, Amelia tucked her shoulder-length red hair behind her half-cut ear, revealing the scar on it—a wound that would surely become a flaw if she wished to live a typical woman’s life. At the time, she didn’t have the money to buy a potion, so she had no choice but to leave it alone. Of course, she could easily treat it today, but she didn’t bother. Besides, it suited her lean, muscular, 5′6″ physique and matched the tattoo under her eye.
“Almost there.”
This wound always reminded her of who her real enemy was.
“Amelia, the lord is calling you.”
She slung her packed bag over her shoulder and stepped outside. A figure was waiting for her. “I didn’t expect you to come.”
He was a member of Orcules, the most infamous evil spirit both above and below the surface, and a big-name criminal they called the Corpse Collector. “The situation is urgent.”
“How bad is it?”
“The palace has made an incredibly bold move. I never thought they would release that madman from prison.”

“...He’s out?” Even Amelia, who was always expressionless, could not hide her surprise. If the Corpse Collector was a well-known evil spirit, this man was the opposite. Few people knew his name, but anyone even faintly familiar with him could only feel fear at the thought that he was free.

“Yes, he is here. Thanks to that, things have gotten a little messy. Our side is dying off en masse too.” The man in the spectacles grinned and patted Amelia on the back. “So, let’s go. Everyone’s already gathered—you’re the only one left.”
“...All right. Let’s move.” Amelia followed the man into a quiet hallway, their quick footsteps the only sound to be heard. “Is the Dragon Slayer involved in the battle?”
“Hm? Oh, him... his arm is crippled, so what can he do? He’s probably resting in his room even now.”
“...I see.” Amelia cautiously raised one more question. “Has there been any improvement?”

The man stopped in his tracks and turned around. “Why are you curious about that?” As someone famous for his intelligence, he may have been forming a connection between Amelia and the Dragon Slayer’s equipment being found on the black market.
That was a mistake.
Amelia realized her mis-step a moment too late, but she answered as calmly as possible. “If he’s no longer useful, I’m going to kill him.”
“Huh? You two are unfriendly?”
“I don’t like his eyes.”

A moment of silence followed Amelia’s answer. It wasn’t long. The man burst into laughter. “Ahahaha! True! His snake eyes are kind of annoying. Especially because he doesn’t know his place.” The man started walking again. “Be patient, though. It looks like his body will heal in half a year to a year.”
“And the Dragon Sword? Isn’t he useless without it?”
“Ah, that. We’ll have to look for it. The alchemist grandpa said restoring his memories isn’t impossible.”
“...I see.”

A way to restore memories; she wanted to ask what exactly that was, but she held back. She wasn’t typically interested in others. This smart guy was sure to sense that something was wrong if she asked too many questions.
I should look into that later, though.

After traveling through the corridor for about three minutes, a big door appeared before her eyes—the white door that lead to the great hall. Stepping inside, she saw the lord of the castle sitting on the throne. “It’s been a while, my lord.”
“Come, Amelia Rainwales.”
After a brief salute, Amelia inspected the other four figures in the hall. Three were familiar, and one was not.
“An adventurer from Orcules. But since we don’t have much time, introductions can come later. Let’s move on to why we’re here.”
She shoved aside her curiosity and awaited the lord’s commands.
“As you can already tell, I’ve gathered you all because the situation isn’t good.”
“Hehe, I heard! I heard that madman is down here?” a woman asked.

“That’s right, Miss Carmila. The captain is dealing with him now, but he won’t hold out for long,” the lord of the castle continued with a tight smile. The city would finally be sealed off. No one would be able to enter nor leave Noark for the next two years. “As soon as you all exit through the secret passage, the sealing magic circle will be activated. Do you have any questions?”
“No, my lord.”
“See you in two years, my handsome lord!”
“Carmilla, show some respect.”
“Shut up, smelly man.”

After that brief exchange, Amelia moved to the secret passage with her four companions. It wasn’t long before they reached the spot where the red flag was planted. They exchanged communications with their lord over a message stone.
“We have arrived.”
“I wish you good luck.”
A moment later, an immense barrier of blue mana surrounded the entire city.
“Wow, so cool. We really can’t go through it.”
I didn’t think I’d end up leaving the city like this.
Amelia did her best to shake off her mixed emotions and recalled the objective of this mission.
“I heard you’re the commander. What do we do now?” Carmilla asked.
The mission was very simple: gather information in Rafdonia. That was their main objective.
Finally. I’ve made it here.
Recalling the second mission their lord had given them, her lips curved.
If possible... kill a certain adventurer.

Rumors of all kinds circulated in the city, from the conspiracy theory that the failure of the conquest was orchestrated by the palace to the apocalyptic theory that the city would soon be wiped out by the war with Noark.
This world is no different than Earth, huh.

For the past few days, I’d been going around taverns and hearing these ridiculous stories over and over again. It was a boring yet stressful operation, but it was also one I couldn’t avoid. It wasn’t as if I was Lion of the Round Table right now. What could a barbarian on the ground do except move his own body?
“Bjorn, are you going drrrinking today too?”
“Yes, I’m going to be late, so don’t wait up for me.”

There was less than a week left until the labyrinth reopened. Today as well, as soon as the sun started to set, I headed for the streets and had a glass on my own. Just by doing so, information reached my ears.
“I heard that death gratuity payments are delayed until next month.”
“Makes sense—even the palace can’t pay for all those deaths.”
“Haha, it’s the opposite. They have enough money, but it’s taking a long time to count all the bodies.”
In a way, it was similar to my early days here. Back then, I didn’t have the money to go to a tavern, so all I could do was keep my ears open during meals.
Nothing special today, either.
After the conquest failed, the palace did not make any official announcements, leaving endless rumors to propagate from mouth to mouth. There were a few agreed-upon facts, though.

First, Noark had also suffered considerable losses and had narrowly escaped defeat by sealing off the city. This was confirmed as there had been many witnesses. No matter how hard the palace tried to keep it quiet, how could they when the number of people who had participated in the battle was so high?

Second, the palace had a super adventurer who lived out of the public eye. This I heard directly from a drunk survivor—namely Mr. Derves from the fifth-floor gathering, who had managed to return alive. Apparently, this mystery adventurer had fought on equal footing against the head of Orcules. Well, it wasn’t strange that the palace would have a champion like that.

Third, three of the ten biggest clans had been disbanded thanks to this conquest—or rather, they were completely annihilated. Not even 10 percent of their members had survived, making recovery virtually impossible. This wasn’t just the case for the ten clans, either. The smaller clans active on the fifth and sixth floors had had more than half of their members reduced to ashes.
Thanks to that, limitations on hunting will be lessened.
That was the only positive in this situation, but the costs that came with it were too steep to be happy about it.
If this battle drags on, I’ll eventually have to face it inside the labyrinth.
This was what I had been worrying about since the first signs of war had appeared. To be honest, this situation was ridiculous.
An Unlimited Player Kill storyline...

I hadn’t even experienced this in the game. If the labyrinth turned into a battlefield, a person like me, who had to make money and level up my character inside of it, would have no choice but to get involved.
If the supply of mana stones decreases, inflation is bound to go up too.
Sadly, no one was talking about this in the cheap taverns. I supposed anyone already worrying about inflation was bound to be an evil spirit.
I’ll have to make a decision soon.
It was nearing the time for me to choose: should I stop adventuring until the situation deescalated, or should I enter the labyrinth as usual? To be honest, my answer was already decided.
Going in would be the right choice.

There was no telling when this confusion would end. Just hitting pause would be a bad decision, since my misadventure with that Dragon Slayer son of a bitch was not over yet. I had to get stronger before the ring of vines broke off. That was the only way I would survive.
If I get force-conscripted down the line, I’ll have to participate in the war anyway.

More importantly, Noark had suffered considerable losses in this battle. Put simply, they’d need time to bounce back too. Even if that weren’t the case, we were in a better position than other adventurers. That was to say, we could crack the first floor with a bug, the fourth floor was independent so I didn’t even need to worry about it, and as long as we entered the mirror on the fifth floor, we would be safe from TPK-ing.
The problem is how I’m going to convince those two...
I couldn’t be sure yet that Raven, the wizard, and Mr. Bear, the ten-year veteran, would want to enter the labyrinth.
I have no other choice but to deal with this head-on.
As soon as I reached a decision, I emptied my glass and left the tavern. A barbarian had their own barbarian way. I made my way to Mr. Bear’s tavern instead.
Mrs. Bear greeted me. “Sorry, we’re closed—oh, Mr. Yandel. What brings you here? Is it my husband?”
“Is Abman here?”

“He’s probably knocked out from drinking. Wait here. I’ll bring him to you.” I wasn’t sure if it was because she had received some proper financial therapy, but Mrs. Bear seemed several times nicer than before.
I sat and waited at the half-cleared table until Mr. Bear was dragged in, rubbing his eyes. “Yandel, what are you doing here in the middle of the night?”
“I have something urgent to talk to you about.”
“Hmm, do you? Wait, let me sober up first. Honey?”
When Mr. Bear called for her, Mrs. Bear served him honey water. “Drink up.” Based on that heartwarming show of hospitality, it seemed he’d regained his authority as the head of the family.
“Ugh, that hits the spot. So, your urgent matter?”
“I’ll get straight to the point. Are you going to join the next expedition?”
“Hmm, looks like you’ve already made up your mind?”
“I’m going in.”
As I nodded without any pretense, Mr. Bear chuckled. “Is that so? Then I will join as well.”
“That was fast. Do you know something I don’t?”

“No, but we’re a team. If our leader has made a decision, I should trust it.” I hadn’t expected that at all. To think he would respect the authority of a leader! This man was more traditional about stuff like this than I thought.
“End of conversation, then.”
“Why not have a drink while you’re here?”
“No thanks. Your wife needs to rest too. Now that you’re awake, you can help her clean up.”
The conversation ended in an instant and I left the tavern. It looked like I had earned some points with her thanks to that line because I noticed Mrs. Bear’s eyes became much softer as I headed out.

It was past three o’clock in the morning, but I headed for the Magic Tower without hesitation. To Raven, this was practically daytime. As a matter of fact, she was locked up in her lab working on an experiment when I arrived.
“Hm? Mr. Yandel? What are you doing here?”
“I came to ask you something.”
“Is that so? Let me just finish this. You can sit anywhere while you wait.”

I thought she would call me out on my rudeness for coming to see her at this hour, but surprisingly she didn’t. Was it because we were teammates now? At least she wasn’t treating me like a stranger like she did a while back.
“So. What do you want to ask?” Raven tidied up the area around us and sat down.
“The labyrinth,” I said bluntly. “Are you going?”
“Oh, that... Well, we did need to talk about that. What did the others say?”
She asked that like it was obvious that I would come to ask her last. It hurt my pride a little, but she was right. “Everyone except you has agreed to enter.”
“Is that so? Then I will go with you guys.”
“That was fast. Do you know something I don’t?” I repeated the same thing I said to Mr. Bear and this time I received a different answer.
“Yes.”
“...What is it?”
“Nothing major. Just that the palace didn’t send an official notice to the Magic Tower yet.”
“An official notice?”
“Normally when something dangerous is going on, the Magic Tower is notified first. Like, ‘don’t go into the labyrinth this month.’”
My mind went blank for a moment, but this VIP treatment made sense. Since wizards were considered high-quality human resources, the palace was directly ensuring their safety.
“So, don’t worry. They’re the ones who led the conquest, so if there’s still no official announcement? That means the palace has assessed the situation and has decided that it isn’t dangerous.”
“...I see. If you ever hear anything like that, tell me in advance.”
“If our leader commands it,” she said with a teasing smile.
I left the Magic Tower, returned home, and woke Missha and Ainar up from their sleep.
“Ugh, what is it? I was sleeping.”
“Ugh, I smell alcohol! Did you go drinking without me again!?”
“Uh huh, just eat this.” I handed them both chicken legs and notified them of the verdict. “We’re going into the labyrinth.”
Ainar reacted like she hadn’t even considered not going in an option. Missha let out a big sigh. “I already knew that, you ridiculous barrrbarian.”
Hah, it would be nice if the rest of the team was like them.
“So, is that it?”
“Yeah, that’s it. Go to sleep.”
“Ugh, just tell us these things in the morrrning!” Missha complained and went back to her room.
So did Ainar. “Good night, Bjorn!”
I took out my key as well and inserted it into the groove. However, just as I was about to unlock the door, I heard footsteps coming up the stairs.
Click, clack.
This bit of white noise was not particularly strange considering this was an inn, but for some reason, the sound pricked my ears today.
Click.
In the end, I subconsciously turned to the stairwell and made eye contact with the person coming up. I thought maybe I was mistaken because of the skirt, but of course not.
What’s she doing here?

This was the unsurmountable wall I had faced twice before, once in the Land of the Dead and once in the sewers—the eighth-floor adventurer from the underground city, otherwise known as the deranged bitch.
Gulp.
As soon as I saw this face that was imprinted in my mind, I swallowed subconsciously. But it seemed she might have been just as surprised.

“To think I would see a familiar face here... This is kind of a problem.” The woman looked at me, frowned, and pulled one foot back to take up a stance. It looked like she’d already decided how she was going to handle this. “Well, I’ll just have to beat you up and erase your memory like last time.”
God damn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 177: Doppelganger (2)
paragraphs: Always think before you act—that was the advice I gave to Ainar on my first day here. They were not just empty words then, either. In fact, this motto had saved my life in the face of countless hardships.
God damn it.
So to that end... after taking a moment to curse my luck, I took stock of my current situation.
“To think I would see a familiar face here.”
First, one thing could be gleaned from this line: she hadn’t come here looking for me.
“This is kind of a problem.”

Second, she was just as bewildered by the situation as I was. However, unlike the last piece of information, there was a different nuance here—it was almost like she was suggesting there was another reason she needed to hide her identity other than the obvious.
I thought Noark was sealed off... Then is she here as a spy or something? And she was made to leave before it was sealed off?
Well, it was hard to be sure yet. There could be other hidden factors. Right now, only one thing was for sure.
“Well, I’ll just have to beat you up and erase your memory like last time.”
Even despite all of this, she had no intention of killing me. In other words, I could at least rest assured in that sense.
As long as I don’t accidentally step on a mine.

I just had to be careful so that she wouldn’t find out that the memory removal pill didn’t work on me. That way, the situation wouldn’t take a turn for the worse. Thus, my basic approach here was decided. Although I had no intention of willingly taking the pill and incapacitating myself, with that bit of insurance, I had nothing to lose.
What did I say in the sewer again?

It was a few months ago, but I could easily remember it. When we were accidentally reunited in the sewer, this was the first thing I had asked. “...Why are you here to kill me? I kept my promise, didn’t I?” If I wanted to pretend my last memory of her was from the Land of the Dead, I had to ask the same thing again.
“That’s the same thing you said back then.”
“...Back then?”
When I looked at her uncomprehendingly, the woman shook her head and continued. “But your face looks much calmer this time.”
I ended up chuckling.
Calmer, huh?
Was it that obvious? “Our oath is still valid,” I said bluntly. “Why not pretend you didn’t see me?”

“Then take this.” The woman took a pill out of her pocket, entirely dark and somewhat damp, and threw it at me. “That pill erases a person’s memories. If you take that, then you won’t remember anything that happened today.”

For a second, I had the thought that taking this pill might be the neatest way to resolve this situation. But no, it had to be a last resort. “How can I trust you?” Taking this would render me unconscious. What if this woman wanted my equipment? What if she opened it up and found the Dragon Sword in my sub-space ring? That was a land mine in itself.
“Do you have another option?”
“Why do you think I don’t?”

Compared to when we met in the Land of the Dead, I was several hundred times stronger. Even compared to my sewer days, I was at least ten times stronger than I used to be. Above all, this was not a dark cellar with no one around to help me. It was an aboveground city with law and order.
“With just one shout, my teammates will wake up. You can’t handle all of them on your own.” There was no reason for me to give in to this woman.
“...I see it was arrogance, not calm.”
“You can see for yourself.”

Despite my bold words, the woman was silent. She may have called me arrogant, but she knew that things were different than they used to be. A sudden, heavy silence fell in the empty hallway as the day began to dawn.
The first to speak was the other side. “Barbarian.” The woman took a step forward and called out to me.
Instead of answering, I turned around. There, sure enough, I saw her clone. This was the Doppelganger ability, Self-Replication.
Dash!
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Asura’s Kick.]
The doppelganger that had silently appeared behind me leaped into the air and swung a heavy foot. It was the same move that struck my head last time. I immediately raised my arms to protect my face.
Bang!
The tingling blow jolted through my wrist, but that was all.
With my current physical resistance?
Well, the hit did seem to have cracked a bone, but actually, I couldn’t tell for sure. I couldn’t even feel pain as trivial as that because of my Pain Resistance stat.
“Behelahhh!” Calling out the name of my ancestral god, I slammed a fist the size of a watermelon into the clone’s face.
Pop!

As soon as the clone took the hit, it disappeared into a puff of smoke. I hurriedly turned in the direction of her original body in anticipation of a simultaneous attack, but the woman just stood there. “How did you know?”
Oh, she never thought I’d be able to stop that move. “Sound,” I answered honestly.

At some point during our conversation, all sounds in the hallway had disappeared. Although it may have been late at night, it was a markedly strange phenomenon. Since Ainar’s snoring easily penetrated through wooden doors, as soon as the sound disappeared, I knew the woman was planning a surprise attack. And as soon as she stepped forward, I figured out the trick. Self-Replication was something I had suffered through once already.
The radius in which the clone can be summoned is five yards.
She had obviously been too far away to summon one right behind me without stepping forward. Since we’d fought each other twice already, I was able to counter it.
I repeated what I said earlier. “My offer is still valid. Just pretend you didn’t see me and disappear.”
As expected, I got a different answer this time. “...How can I trust you?”
I smiled and threw her own words back at her. “What other option do you have?”
I didn’t know what ability she had used, but it seemed like it only lasted for a short amount of time. I had started to hear Ainar’s snoring again a few seconds ago. Now, if I really screamed...
Creak.
The door opened at that moment. “Bjorn? Who arrre you talking—” Missha appeared through a crack in the door, rubbing her eyes.
“I’ll explain later. Go inside.”
“Ah!”
I reached out and closed the door before it could fully open.

“Hey! You horrrible bastard!” Missha flew into a rage after banging her head on the door, but it couldn’t be helped. That wasn’t important right now. “Hey! Open it! I said open! It’s a girrrl, isn’t it? Erwen? Is she back again?!”
I put my weight on the door and stared silently at the woman. The message in my eyes was very simple: Now what will you do?
I got my answer after a brief pause. “If I say I’ll leave, will you believe me?” In other words, would I not try to retaliate?

I answered without hesitation. “I’ll believe you.” After all, this was the same woman who let me go on an oath and oath alone, and I hadn’t reported her either. I had even stopped Missha from coming out of her room. “I just want to let you know, I don’t care what you do. I just don’t want to get mixed up with you.”
“...I’m sure,” the woman muttered in a slightly melancholic tone, but that wasn’t the response I was seeking.
“So, your answer?”
“I will go.”
“And promise to never come looking for me again?”
“I didn’t come for you. But... if you want, I will promise that too.”
At those words, I lowered my guard a little. Although a mere promise didn’t mean much in this world, not everyone was like that.
“I don’t want to kill a barbarian with my own hands if I can avoid it... That was our agreement in the first place.”
Even in the Land of the Dead, she had saved me because of a promise. The weight of a promise was different to her.
I thought of her as a lunatic back then, but it turns out she isn’t entirely like that...
“Then go, human woman.”
At my words, she nodded quietly. Then she turned around and descended the stairs.
Click, clack.

The further away the sound of her footsteps got, the more relieved I felt. I was really glad this had ended without a fight. I was not entirely ready to withstand someone’s aura yet. City and teammates or not, if she had truly wanted to kill me, I would have had to see blood too.
“Phew...” I would only be able to sleep if I saw her leaving for myself, so I headed to the stairs.
Click.

The woman was on the last step, about to step down to the first floor. But it seemed she’d noticed my presence. “...I’m not a human woman.” She swung around and looked into my eyes. “Amelia Rainwales.” Leaving behind those words, she disappeared like smoke.
My mind went blank for a moment. “What the...” That made it seem like we’d meet again.
Knock, knock.
I knocked on Ainar’s door first, but the sound of snoring was the only response I got and the door did not open. Unlike Missha’s door, which swung open right away.
“Hey! Who was that woman out therrre?!”
“A peddler.”
“What?”
“Let’s just go to sleep. I’m tired.”
“Huh? Oh? Uh... uh? Sleep? Here? Why?”
I tossed a pillow onto the bare floor and laid down. I really didn’t want to do this, but...
“R-Right. B-Because you’re tirrred. S-S-Sleep up here, though. Not on the floor...”
“That’s a bit... I’ll just sleep here.”
“Hm? Then, w-why are you here?”
Because I was kind of scared to sleep alone tonight.

The days passed and it was once again time to enter the labyrinth. We had an hour and a half left until the portal opened. At exactly the scheduled time, Raven arrived. With that, everyone was gathered.
“Fortunately, no one is late this time.”

We first cast the binding spell then got moving. Our meeting spot this time had been Mr. Bear’s tavern. We decided that just taking him with us from the get-go would be easier for all of us than waiting an hour for him there.
“...There are definitely fewer people than usual.”
The road leading to Dimension Square was oddly quiet. I could understand why. Since the times were what they were, everyone probably wanted to take a break and assess the situation.
But what’s this?
When I arrived at Dimension Square, I froze. The scene here was completely different from the quiet alleys we’d just walked through.

“Everyone please line up!” The number of civil servants present was several times higher than usual. I could also see soldiers. Hundreds of groups comprised of one knight and four soldiers were scattered all over the place.
Are they trying to restrict entry into the labyrinth?

The thought came to mind, but fortunately it wasn’t like that. “Here you go.” Standing at the end of the long line, a government official hurriedly approached us and handed out two items. One was a video recorder, and the other... honestly, I had no idea.
“What is this necklace?”
“It’s an identification tag that shows you’re on our side.”
“Identification tag?”

“Yes.” The official explained a few new precautions they were taking in the labyrinth and warned us that we could not lose the tag. It was a lengthy lecture, as was typical for someone who worked in administration, but the gist was simple.
If we lose it, we’re fucked.
Without an identification tag, we would become kill targets. Conversely, killing someone without a tag carried no punishment.
No wonder they’ve been so quiet. It’s because they were plotting this.

Seeing as they were only telling us this just before the labyrinth opened, it seemed the government had managed to maintain thorough secrecy. As a resident of Rafdonia, that wasn’t necessarily a bad thing.
“B-Bjorn... arrre we going to be okay?”
“Why wouldn’t we be? This means the army is going to protect us in the labyrinth.”
“Oh, does it?”
“Still, one thing is for certain. The rumor of there being a portal in the underground city is true.”
We chatted and waited, and the portal opened after about five minutes. The soldiers entered first, then it was time for the adventurers to wait in line.
“...We might not get in.”
“Come on, Mr. Urikfried. That won’t happen,” Raven said, but as time passed, her expression hardened.
The portal shrank as the line got shorter. I was actually more than happy about this turn of events.
Hmm, if things play out like this, I won’t have to explain anything.

Originally, I intended to confess to the incident from my first trip into the labyrinth so I could use the experience point copy bug. After watching him for a month, I knew Mr. Bear was someone who placed great value on trust, and Raven was trustworthy in a different sense. The incident with the special appraiser played a big part in my decision.
“If we tell them, they’ll probably make several times more on the information. I refuse to let that happen.”
She never did anything that benefited someone else, so I had planned to reveal this method and accumulate free experience points starting this month.
“What are you doing!? Get in, quick!”
“If you’re not going in, get out of the way!”

With the way things were currently going, I thought it was possible to take advantage of the bug naturally. Even I thought the current situation was risky. It helped that actually seeing the soldiers here frightened some adventurers, making them hesitate to enter and slowing down the line.
“No more! Everyone, please stand back!”
“What!? W-What do you mean?! I waited for over an hour!”
Admission was cut off when there were about ten people left in the queue.
“A-Are we going to have to go home like this!?”
“Huh, I didn’t think they’d really cut us off.”
“It’s because you jinxed it, Mr. Urikfried.”
“...Are you blaming me for this?”
Raven sighed. “Whatever. Let’s just go back.”
Everyone seemed resigned.
Now, you’re all making this barbarian sad. You’re just going to give up already?
“Bjorn, what arrre you doing? Is something up ahead?”
“Now.”
Eventually, the portal’s light began to fade. Normally, this was around the time when someone would have shouted, “The portal will be closed soon!”
“Everyone, get on my back.”
“Huh?”
There was no time to explain, so I activated Giantization. My body grew in an instant.
“W-What are you doing!? It’s illegal to activate a superhuman ability outside specified locations!”
Paying a fine was no problem. It wasn’t even that much. Unless you injured someone, it was only about three hundred thousand stones.
I’ll take this out of the team fund.
I immediately scooped the four of them into my arms and started running blindly ahead.
“Hey! What are you doing!?”
“Stop!”

I ignored all the cries of the civil servants. This would end with just a small fine, anyway. There was no reason not to go in. Just think of how much we would earn after just one day of hunting on the fifth floor.
“Kyaa!”
“No way—are you just going to enter?”
“Behelahhh!”
Was my shout answer enough? Ainar started cackling from her place tucked under my left arm. “Hahaha! Yes, Bjorn! Great warrior!” Now that was a barbarian.
Boom! Boom!
I sprinted through the empty plaza with a satisfied smile on my face.
Shaaaaa!
The light of the portal shrank to the size of a person and began to fluctuate. Soon, the light flashed and embraced us.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
Safe.
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]

chapters.title: Chapter 178: Doppelganger (3)
paragraphs: In the pitch-black darkness, Raven cast a light sphere spell. “Leait.” Before it blinded me, I reflexively closed my eyes. “Mr. Yandel, what are you doing?” she asked.
When I peeked an eye open, I saw that the sphere of light was emitting a faint and subtle glow, unlike usual.
Oh, so you can adjust the brightness too.
“Nothing.”
As I set my embarrassment aside and looked around, Raven scolded me. “Anyway, if you’re going to do something like that, please tell me in advance next time. You surprised me.”
“Yeah. What if security comes to arrest us when we leave?”
“Then we can just pay the fine.”
“Don’t think you’re going to pay with—”
“It was for the team.”
When I cut her off, Raven let out a deep sigh but didn’t say anything else. I wasn’t exactly wrong, and that wasn’t what was important right now anyway.
“Isn’t it strange? We’re already in one of the dark zones.”
“It’s not just a dark zone. Do you see that?” Raven pointed out a tombstone on one side of the wall to Mr. Bear.
Time to get into the main topic of conversation, then. “It’s a tombstone. Do you know how this happened?”
“I think it was the dimensional instability phenomenon.”
“...What’s that?”
“A portal is a kind of dimensional magic. I heard this can happen sometimes. It’s caused by an error that occurs when your starting coordinates are being decided.”
“So... it’s just a coincidence?”
“Well, there is an unsubstantiated account that suggests the possibility that dimensional instability might increase right before the portal disappears.”
Uh, I think that’s the same book I read.
My mouth was itching to speak, but I just kept quiet. Since this one was going to explain it all anyway, there was no reason to step forward and raise suspicion.
“Bjorn, this is...” I shot her a look and Missha clammed up. Just in case Ainar had a slip of the tongue too, I stood next to her. Okay, that settled that.

“Hmm, so you’re saying this happened because we just barely managed to enter at the end?” The corners of Mr. Bear’s mouth rose slightly. As an adventurer, he seemed to have realized the overpowered nature of the experience point copy bug.
However, Raven shook her head. “That is a little ambiguous.”
Hm? What is?
I impatiently joined the conversation. “Ambiguous? What do you mean?”
“Even if the coordinates were incorrectly chosen, we shouldn’t have landed in the outermost area like this. After all, if this happened every time, why would anyone ever go in early?”
Hmm, that was true. Actually, I was also wondering about that. Dimensional instability was surprisingly well-known to many people. Why was no one using this freeloading bug?
“The dimensional instability phenomenon was made known 130 years ago. At that time, there was a big issue with the dimensional magic circle, so the frequency increased exponentially.”
“So?”
“The Magic Tower repaired the magic circle on a commission from the palace. After it was stabilized, the phenomenon rarely occurred again.”
Put simply, the XP bug must not have been usable for the next hundred years after that. “Then how did this happen?”
“...Maybe it’s time for another repair?” Raven came up with a plausible hypothesis and carefully added a suggestion. “Which is why I think we should keep this a secret.”
“Explain.”
“I don’t think anyone knows that there is a problem with the dimensional magic circle yet. However, as time passes and the phenomenon worsens, other adventurers will also start to experience it.”
Mr. Bear listened quietly and nodded. “You mean we should use it exclusively until they find out.”
“Yes. It’ll reduce our expedition time and allow us to accumulate experience points—how great is that?”
I joined in. “Wait, I thought experience points didn’t matter to wizards.” Wizards couldn’t absorb essences, which was why XP was useless to them. Why was she being so proactive?
Raven smiled. “I’m personally interested. The same goes for that headstone no one’s touched yet. On that note, may I open it?”
“Do as you like.”
Once I granted her permission, Raven touched the tombstone.
Whooom!

A portal opened, radiating five colors of light. Raven closed her eyes as if to concentrate on the flow of mana in the air and the sensation on her fingertips. Then she murmured, “It feels very strange.” This was a sensation that I would never know as a barbarian with zero innate aptitude for mana. However, even I felt one thing for sure.
[The portal has been opened for the first time. EXP +2.]
Yeah, this was it—what freeloading felt like.
[You have entered the Den of Beasts on the second floor.]
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]

We came right back to the first floor after heading up. The Den of Beasts was a hopeless endeavor for us. Because there were so many forks in the road, without a scout of Rotmiller’s caliber, we’d just get slowed down.
Even Rotmiller said it’s better to give up on the Den.
It wasn’t that we couldn’t find our way with a scout. But while there was a faster route available, there was no reason to go through this place.
“Then let’s get going.”

I took out my compass and held it in one hand as I led the way. First, we got out of the dark zone and headed northwest. We didn’t end up getting lost too often. For what it was worth, Rotmiller taught me how to find my way around the first floor really well. Of course, I wasn’t an expert yet.
“Abman, where is the portal?”
“That way.”
“Then we only need to go north from now on.”
Thanks to the fact that we had a scout on the team, it was possible to find the optimal route with just a compass. In other words, I was making up for my inexperience with a cheat code.

Around three hours into the expedition, while moving from outskirt to outskirt, people appeared for the first time—a knight with the royal family’s crest engraved on their chest and four soldiers. The knight stopped us. “Do you have an identification tag?” he asked curtly.
It was evident that they had already fought one battle because their weapons and armor were splattered with blood. It wasn’t monster blood. There were no monsters on the first floor that bled red.
“I will ask you one last time. Identification tag?”
“Ah, here it is. You guys get yours out too.”

Momentarily hesitating in the face of the knight’s intimidation, we took out the tags we received back in the city. Then the knight made way to let us pass, offering a word of advice as we did. “Be careful not to let it get stolen. Some clever ones are already after them.”
I see. Well, they weren’t idiots. They would know that was the only way for them to survive. Passing by, I asked him something I was curious about. “Is there any way to identify stolen tags?”
“No.”
“Then why aren’t you suspicious of us?”
Did my question bother him? The knight frowned slightly but still answered it. “Blood.”
“What?”
“If it was stolen, it would have been stained with human blood. Above all else, I know your face. I am a knight of Count Ferdehilt.”

Oh, he saw me at the banquet. Anyway, I didn’t know what that count was up to. He told me very ominously that he would call me when things were ready, but there had been no contact yet. Well, no news was good news for me.
“Hmm, it certainly is nice to have a celebrity on the team,” said Raven.
“Don’t mock me.”
“I’m sorry? I’m not mocking you.”
Man, did she think I was a real barbarian or something? “Wipe that smile off your face, then.”
“...Jeez, so quick.”
“Anyway, let’s speed up from now on. Let me know if you’re tired.”
“What are you going to do if we are?”
“Ainar will carry you.”
“Eh? Me?”
Both Ainar and Raven seemed displeased, but it couldn’t be helped. We had to head up as quickly as possible to run into fewer people.
About thirty minutes after speeding up, the couch potato wizard Raven chose to abandon her pride and get carried. “...Miss Ainar. Please carry me.”
Thankfully, our speed increased after that. Bored from just being carried, Raven began massaging the parts of Ainar’s body she could reach.
“D-Don’t touch me!”
“Wow, Miss Ainar. Your body is softer than I thought.”
“...Are you mocking me?! If so, then get off!” Ainar freaked out and flailed. Right when I was about to tell Raven off, I saw something blocking my way and stopped.
“Bjorrrn, why did you stop?”
“There are dead bodies.”
There were five corpses in total, four men and one woman. Their equipment had all been stripped off so they were pretty much naked, and the bleeding indicated they’d been dead for quite a while now.
“Miss Ainar, will you let me down?” Raven got off her personal carriage and inspected the bodies as well. “It doesn’t look like this was done by a knight.”
“Your reasoning?”
“The wounds. One with a blunt weapon, one with an arrow. The rest were burned, and I don’t think it was magic. It must have been a special ability.”
A knight used a sword, because it was the best weapon for using an aura. But with no sword wounds...
“Maybe they are adventurerrrs from Noark? Another adventurer could have taken them down because they didn’t have a tag.”
Raven smiled grimly at Missha’s words. “Or it could be the opposite.”
“Opposite?”
“The knight said so himself earlier,” Mr. Bear said. “These adventurers might have been targeted for their tags.”
“Besides, whoever did this left their faces unrecognizable. Normally, that’s not necessary, is it?”

Of course, we couldn’t know what the truth was, but these corpses rang alarm bells for all of us. They had to, because these were adventurers who had reached the outskirts of the first floor this early into the expedition. They must have been strong enough to speedrun, but they had still been killed within a few hours of the labyrinth opening.
“...We really need to be careful.”
“Yandel, it looks like these bastards went to the Goblin Forest. Shouldn’t we go somewhere else?”
“It won’t make a difference.”
“Well, that’s true.”

In the end, we made our way to the Goblin Forest without making any changes to our schedule. I wasn’t sure how long it had been, but we reached the portal to the second floor at 6:47 a.m., much earlier than our previous expedition. Even compared to Rotmiller’s time trial attempt, there was only a thirty-minute difference.
“Mr. Yandel, you can be a real scout now.”
“Nyaha, a barrrbarian scout? No one will believe this!”
“Bjorn is the hope of the barbarians!”

Everyone showered me with compliments after checking the time, but this was hardly a result of my skill. This expedition had a different starting line. We’d moved from outskirt to outskirt, which was bound to save a lot of time. “...Anyway, let’s go up.” I dismissed their chatter and stood in front of the portal.
“You’re embarrassed.”
“Yes, yes, you arrre.” Abman and Misha teased.
Yeah, right.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]
[You have entered the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.]
On the morning of the seventh day, a day faster than with Rotmiller, we reached the fourth floor.
At this rate, we might be in first place.

This was the result of combining Abman’s scouting ability with my rapidly growing navigation skills. As a matter of fact, we rarely came across any adventurers, just two large-scale clans, and maybe ten parties. Each time we did, we parted ways only after showing each other our tags, weapons up. The atmosphere in the labyrinth had gotten really scary.
“Raven, what are the results?”
“Nothing.”
As soon as we cleared the first stage of the Tower, she spent about an hour running detection magic, wary of the masked assailant incident from last time.
Geez, look what that bastard is making us do.
It pissed me off worse the more I thought about it, but what could I do? We had to look out for ourselves given the current state of affairs.
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]

The first stairway was none other than Wisdom, a maze full of traps and monsters. Most of the training I had received from Rotmiller was in this field, so my clear time was reduced by about forty minutes.
“Raven, how long did it take?”
“One hour and fifty-eight minutes.”
Considering that it took five hours the first time, that was ridiculously fast.
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Courage.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Wisdom.]
[You have chosen the Stairway of Courage.]
Even after that, we continued to overcome trials and focused on climbing the floors.
Floor twenty-seven on the first day...
We actually succeeded in clearing a quarter of the Tower in one day. This speed would have been impossible had the Stairway of Wisdom not appeared multiple times in succession.
“It’s a bit early, but let’s take a break ahead of schedule today.”
The Stairway of Courage we had cleared last would only let us leave after a four-hour wait, so we just set up camp.
“What should we do about night watch?”
“I don’t think there’s any need for that.”
There was no night watch. After using detection spells periodically throughout the day, we hadn’t found any other adventurers.
“Well, even if someone really is hiding here, a night watch would be pointless. If we can’t even find them with detection magic, what difference would staying awake change, right?”
“That’s exactly what I was going to say.”
“Then shall we eat before bed?”
“Sure.”
Everyone gathered for a quick meal, headed to their sleeping bags, and laid down. A comfortable bed could only be found on the fourth floor. At least, that should’ve been the case.
Goddamn it.

Maybe it was because of the masked assailant incident, but sleep didn’t come easily to me that night. In the end, only after tossing and turning for a while did I manage to close my eyes. But it wasn’t long before I was forced to wake up.
Dddddd!
Vibrations spread through the ground under my back. The entire Tower was faintly trembling. I quickly got up. There was only one thing in the labyrinth that caused a phenomenon like this.
“Mr. Yandel, is this...”
“Yes, it’s exactly what you think.”
A Rift had opened on the fourth floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: Doppelganger (4)
paragraphs: Rifts were instance dungeons that existed on each floor, such as the Bloody Citadel and Glacier Cave. A Rift had two main characteristics: the drop rate of essences increased exponentially, and a special monster called a guardian gave players special rewards that could not be obtained in normal areas.
“Abman, where is the Rift located?”
Mr. Bear closed his eyes to focus his senses before opening them again. “Over there. It doesn’t seem far.”
In that case...

I smirked. The odds of being able to successfully enter had just increased. It was only thanks to five Stairways of Wisdom appearing on the first day that we were already able to reach floor twenty-seven. It was fifteen minutes to midnight; the seventh day still hadn’t ended. It was safe to say we had barely any competition since Rifts on the fourth floor only formed above the twenty-fifth floor of the Tower. And the portal also happened to be nearby.
“Mr. Yandel, we’re going to look for it, right?”
“Of course.”

Rifts were the crown jewel of the labyrinth, an opportunity no adventurer would pass up on. Roused from our sleep, we unanimously cleared our campsite and stood in front of the door leading in the direction Abman had pointed to.
Voom!
After waiting a few minutes, the engraving on the stone gate began to glow. That meant that the four-hour wait time was over and the door was now ready to be opened.
“Ugh, I don’t like this...”
“I really hope there won’t be hallucinations.”

Missha and Mr. Bear, who had previous experience under their belts, groaned as we walked through the door. On the other hand, Raven and Ainar couldn’t seem to understand what they were so distressed about.
“I would rather deal with hallucinations. I heard they’re not very effective against people with strong willpower.”
“Hahaha! Then I will have no problem!”

Come to think of it, this would be the first time these two would ever be dealing with this particular stairway. I was also a little curious. A wizard armed with logic and a fearless barbarian warrior—how would these two react? If I saw how they handled things, I might be able to tell if I was a unique case or not.
[You have chosen the Stairway of Patience.]

A straight corridor about a hundred yards long stretched out ahead of us. As soon as I set foot inside the place, my teammates disappeared and a new background appeared: the pediatric ward where I spent most of my childhood. The sky beyond the window was clear, and the face of the child lying on the bed was also bright.
It’s a visual hallucination.

As I took a step toward the child, my surroundings changed. Beyond the window, the sun had begun to set. In front of the bed, a young college student had pulled up a chair. This was someone I had once trusted more than my parents.
Ha, starting with this again?

I chuckled and took another step forward. Then the conversation between the child and student began. As they played games together, the child asked if the student could stay and play a little longer, but the student refused. It could have ended there, but the child was young. As he continued to push, the student’s face hardened. Like an explosion, he jumped up from his seat and unleashed a flood of abuse, words that hurt more than any hospital treatment back then ever had.
Step.

I took a step further, letting it flow in one ear and out the other. I was an adult now. The same words didn’t hurt me anymore. I didn’t point the arrow at myself, either, telling myself that he must have had a bad day that day. It was something that could happen to anyone. It could have been someone’s fault, but then again, it could not have been. That was all.
Step.

Inside the car right before the accident; an apartment that was burning red; sitting there left alone at an amusement park; my very first apartment after being hired at my office job... Each time I took a step, my surroundings changed and the cast of characters changed accordingly.
Step.
My mom, dad, uncle, and ex-girlfriend—at each location, a new person appeared and spoke words that left deep scars on me. But, so what?
It’s still easy.
I didn’t need a hallucination to see these things—they were scenes I could vividly picture in my head. This was nothing new now. Pain came with tolerance.
What is this?
However, when I kept walking, new characters appeared that never had before.
“Oh! Ah, you’re here too, Bjorrrn?”
“Haha, why are you so late?”
Missha and Dwalkie were smiling at me happily, arm in arm. But despite the warm welcome, their faces contorted grotesquely when I took another step.
“If it weren’t for you, everrryone could have been happy.”
“Are you happy that you survived instead of me?”
This was a plotline I had often seen in cartoons and movies. Geez, didn’t they have anything original?
Yup, it’s not my fault. Go complain to god.
Without looking away from them, I continued walking in silence.
“Bjorn, great warrior and son of Yandel!”
“Give me back my friend’s body!”

In addition to Ainar, who appeared next, the connections I had formed as Bjorn Yandel appeared one after another and said strange things to me. None of these interactions were based on real memories, but they didn’t feel unfamiliar, either. These were all things I’d thought to myself at least once.
Yup, still not working.
I pushed forward without stopping. I didn’t cover my ears, or close my eyes.
[You have completed the Ordeal of Patience.]
Soon, the hallucinations were over. I had been in front of the door, but before I knew it, I had reached the end of the hallway and the stairs were in front of me. The rest of the team was there too.
“B-Bjorrrn...!”
“If you cry again, I’m really going to leave you behind.”
“Hnng...”
Turning away from the teary-eyed Missha, I checked on the rest. Mr. Bear had a calm expression on his face. He had an offended look in his eyes, but that was all. Ainar was unexpectedly fine too.
“Are you all right?” I asked her.
“Huh, oh... it just felt kind of unpleasant.”
Well, come to think of it, barbarians were all mentally strong since they were a race taught to fight their problems instead of running away from them. So what about a wizard?

Raven was staring out into space with a blank expression on her face. Even from a distance, I could tell that she was trembling like a leaf. What did she see? I was curious but didn’t bother to ask. I didn’t think she’d answer, anyway.
“It’s all over now.”
“Oh... yeah. Right...” Raven came to her senses once I approached and patted her on the shoulder. Cold sweat had formed on her forehead.
“We’ll take a break upstairs, so hold on a little longer.”
“Okay...”

I consoled my teammates and climbed the stairs. Then we took a ten-minute break. In truth, I avoided choosing the Stairway of Patience for this very reason even in the game. It drastically cut down on a party’s stamina. I hadn’t suspected this was the reason, though.
“Abman, where should we go from here?”
“That way.”

After the break, the expedition resumed. I had decided that the Rift was our top priority right now. We selected the Stairway of Wisdom next and cleared the maze in about two hours. Then came the next stage after that.
“It’s the portal!”
A Rift was open in the empty stone chamber. The color of the violently shimmering portal was green.
Doppelganger Forest, huh?
Bloody Citadel, Glacier Cave, and now this—the third Rift I would ever explore.
[You have entered the fourth-floor Rift.]
There were two types of Rifts on the fourth floor—the Golden Ruin where money practically fell into your lap, and Doppelganger Forest.
So it’s not Golden Ruin.
Dismissing my disappointment, I called forth our wizard. “Raven.”
“Leait.”

When the light sphere floated into the air, I could see the new environment that surrounded us. We were locked inside a massive iron cage. Nothing beyond the bars could be seen due to the darkness of the labyrinth.
“Bjorn! What is going on!?”
Um, should I explain?
As I was wondering this, Raven opened her mouth. “Don’t be startled. It’ll open on its own in time.”
“Huh? What do you mean?! Explain!”
“It’s because the number of participants hasn’t been met yet. Up to three parties can enter this place.”

This was how this Rift differed from the one on the first floor. Doppelganger Forest could be entered by up to fifteen people through three different portals. If the former was a collaboration between individuals, this was a collaboration between parties.
“Is this place written about in that book too?”
“Yes. We’re lucky. I don’t know much about the Golden Ruin.”
Hmm, since she’s read The Complete Book of Rifts, she can take care of the hidden feature... Wait, should I leave everything, including the strategy, to her?
I made a snap judgment. “That’s good. Then you can give the orders this time. I will follow them all.”
“You mean I should take on the role of leader?”
“Isn’t there a proverb about following the wizard in places like this?”
“Heehee, sure. Just leave it to me.” With a little flattery, Raven squared her shoulders and declared that she would take on all the troublesome tasks. She was definitely easy to handle, this one.
If there comes a problem, I can step forward then.

As per Rotmiller’s advice to hide my uniqueness from my new party as much as possible, I felt a need to be careful. Running wild like I used to in the past was bound to make Raven and Mr. Bear pick up on the fact that something was wrong.
“Then here are the things you need to be careful of. First, all the monsters we meet here will be doppelgangers...”

After that, Raven’s briefing continued. Except for Ainar, everyone listened intently. I already knew all this, but I listened with the thought that there might be parts I didn’t know or parts I needed to correct.
After who knows how long of that, I cut her off. “That sounds like enough.”
“Pardon? I haven’t even told you about the herbs that grow here...”
“You can tell us as we go. Rest comes first.”

I stopped Raven’s endless infodump in its tracks and we took a break. After the Ordeal of Patience, we had found the Rift so soon that we hadn’t gotten any sleep. We had to conserve our stamina for the main event.
Honnnk!
Ainar started snoring right away. Missha and Mr. Bear also sat against the iron bars.

And Raven... For some reason, she was chattering next to me. “It’s kind of strange. Obtaining the mirror on the first expedition and then reaching a Rift on the second...” It seemed that her excitement about entering a Rift had not yet faded. “I feel very lucky. I got to go to the Bloody Citadel too.”
Ah, so that’s how it is?
“Yes, you are completely right.”
“...Are you making fun of me?”
“No way.”
“Wipe that smile off your face before you say that.”
She was too quick for her own good. “Anyway, I’m going to rest so you should too.” I ended the conversation there and closed my eyes.
Time passed before I knew it, and it became the morning of the eighth day. It was just after 7 a.m.; in other words, about five hours since we’d entered the Rift.
Clunk!
The tightly sealed iron bars slid up. This meant we were at full capacity.
“Okay then, let’s go.” When I stepped out of the cage, the quest officially began.
“Leait.” Raven increased the number of light spheres to three to ensure she could see. Then, the shape of the cave beyond the darkness became visible.
Ainar cocked her head. “Huh? Didn’t you say forest?”
“I thought I explained this earlier.”
“Oh, sorry. I wasn’t listening at all.”
It was such an overly honest answer that Raven couldn’t even get angry. “...The forest appears just after this cave. After all the parties that have entered join together in one place.”
“I see!”

Raven just clenched her fists and vibrated with annoyance. I felt empathetic for some reason, but right then I was in Normal Barbarian mode where all I had to do was follow orders. Yes, there needed to be days like this once in a while.
“Mr. Yandel, what kind of life have you been leading?”
“...Let’s go.”
“Ah, yes. Let’s go. We don’t have time.”

Following Raven’s instructions, we moved along the path at a slightly faster pace. The reason for our haste was simple. The first stage of Doppelganger Forest was the Shadow Cave. The layout was such that each party started from a different location and met with the others in the center.
“We have to get to the center as quickly as possible. That way we can take the rewards from the other routes too. If we’re late, it’ll be the other way ‘round.”
Although we’d be fighting the final boss together in the end due to the structure of the Rift, until then, this was no different from a competition. Who would get the most? That was up to us.
As we were running through the straight passageway, Mr. Bear suddenly sensed a presence and stopped us. “There’s something up ahead!”
After a brief pause, a person emerged from the darkness.
Step.
He had messy brown hair, a bushy beard, a breastplate made of lithinum that covered a muscular body over six and a half feet tall, and even a giant shield and mace.
“It’s Bjorn!” Ainar looked between the two of us with obvious confusion.
Raven noticed and snapped, “I already told you it’s a doppelganger!”
“D-Doppelganger?!”
“Ugh, honestly! It doesn’t matter anymore. Prepare for battle!”

I think this was the first time she’d ever shouted like this. Was there truly no one in the world who could defeat a barbarian with words alone? I was laughing to myself at the thought when the doppelganger dared to call out the name of our ancestral god.
“Behelahhh!”
At the same time, his body inflated like a balloon. We would have to be careful
[The Doppelganger has cast Giantization.]
[The Doppelganger has cast Wild Outburst.]
I was pretty strong.

chapters.title: Chapter 180: Doppelganger (5)
paragraphs: Boom! Boom! Boom!

The doppelganger let out a war cry and sprinted forward. I could understand now how the apprentice knight felt as he threw away his pride and ran off the stage back then. So that was what I had looked like...
Makes sense that he ran away.

Because of his increased Threat Level stat due to Wild Outburst, just looking at him sent shivers down my spine, a result of the almost violent intimidation coupled with his large physique. First things first, though, I had to match his weight class.
[You have cast Giantization.]
[You have cast Wild Outburst.]
My eye level instantly changed. Flexing my abdomen, I shouted with all my might, “Behelaaah!” It was my original battle cry that no doppelganger could truly recreate.
Covering my torso with my shield, I ran forward. The doppelganger did the same. Our shields collided and a roar not unlike two dump trucks crashing echoed through the space.
Kwaaaaaang!
Since he was a doppelganger, our difference in strength was zero. Our next moves were exactly the same too.
[You have cast Swing.]
[The Doppelganger has cast Swing.]
Our maces crossed paths like mirror images.
Kwaaang!

Another explosion sounded and the ground shook. This was akin to a fight between two large-sized monsters. At this rate, the battle was bound to go on all day, but this guy and I had one crucial difference between us: teammates.
Even in the game, having a good team is considered a skill in itself.

Without even needing orders, magical support soon began. Curses with a relatively short casting time played the main role. In just a few seconds, the other me’s Strength, Agility, Physical Resistance, and other stats were cut down. Puzzled, the doppelganger stuttered, “Your m-mom!”
You’re really going to insult my mom right now?
My mind went blank at the unexpected line.
Bam!

When I came to my senses, the doppelganger’s mace was grinding against my shield. If I’d reacted just a second later, it would be embedded in my head right now. “You freaky doppelganger asshole!” I hurriedly recovered my wits and retaliated.
It looked like he’d even inherited my trait of using dirty tricks when at a disadvantage. As expected, he was not an opponent to be underestimated. That is, I wasn’t.
Whiiip!
While the bastard shielded himself from Mr. Bear’s arrow, I took advantage of the opening to bring my mace down on his shoulder. Then, blood sprayed from his mouth.
Did he bite his tongue?
What a classic. This was a strategy I had anticipated, so avoiding it was no problem. That was because it was something I would definitely do, even more so if I was in a tough spot.
Chhhhh.
Acidic blood sprayed the ground and started bubbling. Missha let out a surprised shout at the sight. “Wow, how is he exactly the same as you?”
Yeah, right.
“Stop standing around and help already.”
“Okay.”

Soon, Missha and Ainar joined me on the front lines. To save time, I grabbed the guy’s mace and hugged him from behind. Now, all that was left to do was shove a knife in his head while he was restrained.
“Keeeeeek!”

The doppelganger wearing my face let out a screech like nails on a chalkboard. At this, Missha stiffened. It wasn’t for long, but just as she corrected her stance to thrust her sword forward, a battle cry erupted from behind us.
“Behelahhh!”
It was not Ainar’s. Even if her voice was on the deeper side, it was different from a man’s.
“Bjorn! There are three Bjorns!”
But why was I the only one who got doppelgangers?
The second doppelganger had already cast Giantization, breaking our formation by protecting his torso with the shield and charging at us like a beast, a.k.a (True) Shield Charge.
“Don’t bother trying to block it, just avoid it!”

Following my advice, Missha and Ainar stepped back without argument. It was a pity I couldn’t finish this one off right away but, well, what could you do? This must have been karma for absorbing the Ogre essence and becoming an off-tank.
[The Doppelganger has cast Swing.]
Ainar stopped the mace with her greatsword and went flying back in true Lü Bu-like fashion. I wondered if I should join in now.
“Mr. Yandel, keep holding that one! We’ll take care of things on this end!”
For now, I decided to follow Raven’s orders. We couldn’t possibly lose a one-on-four fight. So, I focused solely on marking the original doppelganger.
Ha, this is really annoying. What’s he so sturdy for?

Although I was in a more advantageous position thanks to the curse spells affecting him, it was hard to wrap up my own fight and go help them. Even if I was a secondary tank, I was still a tank. This clash was as never-ending as a fight between Trolls.
I might as well just watch.
I half-resigned myself to my fate and went into spectator mode. To be honest, what I saw was really interesting.
“Ugh, why won’t the knife go in!?”
“This is Bjorn, all right! A great warrior!”

The doppelganger was overwhelming our two melee fighters on his own. Mr. Bear’s long-range support? Even the bolts fired with the incredible tension of his super-mega crossbow could not pierce the doppelganger’s shield. Raven’s magic wasn’t much different, either.
Chwaaaaa!
When the melee sisters stepped back for a moment, a Fire Baptism shot forward. The timing was so perfect that even the doppelganger couldn’t avoid the flames and was promptly engulfed by them.

“Behelahhh!” However, the other me just ran right through the flames and swung his mace. She had picked the wrong spell. My Flame Resistance was my second highest resistance stat after Physical Resistance, and I’d pretty much finished the Mana Resistance part of my build too.
“...I never realized you were this strong,” Mr. Bear exclaimed. Although we’d been fighting battles together this whole time, I guess actually facing me was different.
Raven felt the same. “Why are you still rank six?!”

That was because to reach rank five, you needed to accumulate experience points. Although my teammates were being attacked, I couldn’t help the way my shoulders perked up a bit. I really was strong now, huh?
“Mr. Yandel, don’t just watch and say something. Do you have any weaknesses?”

They weren’t really weaknesses, but things to target. Should I call it the Bjorn Yandel Fighting Style? Still grappling with the doppelganger I was marking, I shouted out the most important points. “Missha, Ainar! Don’t slash, stab!” Ironskin multiplied a user’s Physical Resistance by four, but only for slashing damage. In fact, cuts of a certain level were unaffected. “Abman, aim only for the legs!” My lower body was weaker than my upper body. I still hadn’t gotten fitted for leg armor. My arms were totally exposed too, but my upper body could be covered with the shield.
“Take out the knees first, huh? It really is like fighting a large monster.”
“Yes. It doesn’t have any regeneration abilities, so don’t worry about killing it in one blow and focus on the long game instead. Raven, use lightning magic instead of fire magic!”

Ice blocked bleeding, and wind and earth spells were considered physical magic. Lightning, on the other hand, would work best here because it dealt elemental damage and specialized in penetration and instantaneous firepower.
I can’t believe I have to teach my teammates how to kill me.
It was a strange thought. Still, my advice was effective, and the tide of the battle slowly turned until the doppelganger was brought to his knees. Seven crossbow bolts were stuck in his leg.
“...What a monster.”
“I agrrree. So much that I never want to fight it again.”

Even though we had secured victory, my teammates shuddered, apparently fed up, and just hearing them made me flinch. A big reason for those reactions was because the doppelganger even resembled me in personality. It really fought like a madman.
“Look at that. It’s still trying to get up. What kind of person does that?”

If he bled, he sprayed it at his enemies; if both his hands were tied, he used his teeth. If a hand-off between teammates was about to happen, he latched onto the opportunity like a ghost and charged toward his attackers to take his pound of flesh. The bastard did everything he could to survive, and he was still doing just that.
“Mi... ssha...” The doppelganger gave Missha a desperate look. Since winning the fight was impossible, it was employing one last trick. Without thinking, I chuckled.
You really think that’s going to work—
“Uh... huh?”
“I... like... you...”
“R-Rrreally?
Oh... it’s working.
It was a dirty trick, manipulating Missha’s emotions like this. I tightened my hold on the other doppelganger’s neck and let out a loud sigh. “What are you stopping for?! Kill it already!”

“W-Wait! I want to ask something!” Missha jumped up and waved her hands before turning to the doppelganger with a serious look on her face. “B-B-But why did you reject me then? If you like me.” Missha averted her gaze to stare at the ground in embarrassment.
“Oh my gosh!” Raven’s eyes lit up at the sudden unfolding of a love affair.
But had his aggro been redirected by that comment? Instead of answering Missha, the doppelganger turned his attention to Raven. “Ra...ven...”
“What, is it me this time? What are you—”
“I... like... you...”
Raven’s expression contorted grotesquely at the second love confession. “Uh, Mr. Yandel...?”
I was overcome with shame. How much lower would I stoop? “...Ignore it. It’s just saying that to live.”
“...You mean you would confess your love to anyone in order to live, Mr. Yandel?”
Uh, no, but... No, is that true?
I just owned up to it. “...Looks like it.” I figured that copping to it would prevent any misunderstandings.
However, even as we were saying that, the doppelganger’s eyes moved elsewhere, in the direction of Mr. Bear. “A-Ab... man...”
This crackpot doppelganger!
“I-I li—”
Thankfully, that sentence did not get a chance to reach its end. Mr. Bear shot an arrow through its forehead.
Stab!
That final blow preserved my last remaining dignity. “I’ll pretend I didn’t hear... No, I didn’t hear anything.” It was official: my friendship with Mr. Bear would last forever.
The first doppelganger round had ended. After defeating one of them, we all ganged up and killed the remaining one. Missha dealt the final blow.
“Mi... ssha...?” The fucking doppelganger tried the same trick again when it was cornered, but Missha’s angry determination was unyielding.

“Die, you awful barbarian bastarrrd!” Thrusting her sword into an exact copy of me seemed to be stress-relieving for her. I just stayed silent, although looking back, I hadn’t actually done anything wrong. It was best to shut up when the vibe was off like this—then at least you wouldn’t step on any land mines. This was a survival tactic I had learned from my ex-girlfriend.
“Urakburak! There’s no mana stone!”

The doppelgangers and their equipment dissolved into light, but they didn’t leave behind any mana stones. In truth, the only real Doppelganger that existed in Doppelganger Forest was the final boss. The ones we had just killed were just low-level entities the real one had summoned through its Self-Replication ability.
“All right, let’s keep moving.”

Afterward, we continued hunting doppelgangers and resumed the quest. They usually came in groups of one or two. Only once did three appear at the same time, but they were easier to handle than the first time. Thankfully, I didn’t appear again. After traveling for about half a day like that, the straight-corridor part of the map ended.
“Finally, we’ve reached a fork in the road.”
The road was divided into five different branches. This meant that we had finally reached the center of the area.
“From now on we could run into the other parties, so be careful.”

To add some context to that, it was now possible for us to run into not only our doppelgangers but doppelgangers of another party. It was safe to say that the difficulty had risen significantly. There was no enemy more difficult to face than one you had no information on.
Please be around our level.

With that thought in mind, I proceeded down the crossroad Raven chose. A long while passed. Unfortunately, we did not find the room with the hidden treasure we were looking for. However, we encountered a strange adventurer instead, a thin man with a height of around five feet.
“Please state your name. Otherwise, we will treat you as a doppelganger and kill you.”
At Raven’s request, the man took off his hood. He was far away and hard to distinguish in the darkness, but as soon as I saw him, I had déjà vu, along with an unfamiliar unease.
Why is that?

While I was worrying about that, the man spoke. “...s, cree... sen...” It was the typical speech pattern of a doppelganger. I had already guessed when I saw that he was alone, but this confirmed his identity.
“Mr. Yandel, please take care of this one on your own.”
“Is this for analysis purposes?”
“Yes. We don’t know what kinds of people they actually are, right? We need to figure it out in advance. If it gets dangerous, I’ll step in right away.”
I was actually thinking the same thing, so I followed her orders without question. Meanwhile, the doppelganger kept muttering like a broken record player. “I. Am... not. A doppel... ganger...”
I covered my upper body with my shield and slowly approached.
“C-Chris... en.”
He had no visible weapons. He didn’t seem like a priest, so he was probably a special ability user.
“Hans... Chrisen...”
“...What?”
“That... is... my name.”
Chills ran through my entire body.

chapters.title: Chapter 181: Jinx (1)
paragraphs: Hans Chrisen. The name was familiar somehow.
“Uhh! Bjorrrn! That guy is...!”
Even without Missha telling me, I suddenly remembered. All sorts of summoned creatures were surrounding him.
“He’s a summoner!” said Raven.
The formation of the summons comprised of one attack type and three support types, averaging about rank seven. Once I identified each of them, I sighed.
No wonder he looked so familiar.

With this, the possibility of it being a similar-looking guy was null. This was Hans G, the guy I had determined to be a player based on his knowledge of Riakis’ attack patterns and the appearance conditions for a Death Knight.
God damn it.
What happened when I ran into him last time, again? A Troll showed up on the fourth floor and almost killed everyone. Player or monster, every Hans in this world was a plague.
Step.
My heart grew cold.
I have to kill him.
That single thought dominated my mind.
“Mr. Yandel? Why are you so quiet—?”
I sprinted forward with more power than ever before. The pause right before that was only to gain momentum.
Boom!
Leaving clear footprints on the hard surface of the ground, I closed the distance between myself and the bastard in an instant. But Hans G didn’t just sit back and watch, either.
“Kyaaaaaa!” A nearby lizard screamed and spewed fire at me. To be precise, it was a summoned beast of the fire attribute by the name of Naimpi.
Whooosh!
As a rank-seven summon its flames were not very threatening, but when enhanced by buffs from the support-type summons, its firepower increased explosively.
Chhhhhh!

The heat sizzled on my skin. But who cared? “Behelahhh!” My upper body was covered with a shield and the rest of the damage was offset with Flame Resistance. As I ran through the fire, it burned off some skin, but I had to prioritize.
Crunch!

The mace, full of the power of an Ogre, made a satisfying sound as it struck true. Simultaneously, Hans G’s head exploded and he collapsed. The death had to have been instant because he turned into light before his body even touched the ground.
“W-What are you doing!” Raven shouted, as my actions were different from my promise to let her observe.

It was not that I couldn’t understand why she was pissed, but I could explain later. “Don’t come any closer!” I shouted authoritatively, moving swiftly toward my teammates. Then I let go of the breath I’d been holding. “Hup!”
Done. I may have run into a Hans, but I hadn’t breathed in its polluted air. So it would be fine. No, it should be fine...
“No way, is it poison?”
Uh, no, but... How should I explain this?
“Yes. Let’s give up on this path.”
“Pardon? Wait, it’s really poison? There was nothing to suggest—”
“Enough. Let’s go.”

With a somewhat domineering attitude, I led the team back the way we came. It seemed Raven was unfamiliar with this side of me. She started following without question but had an unhappy look on her face as she did so.

“This is far enough.” After walking for about five minutes, I stopped. Just as I was about to turn around and explain what had happened, I tripped on a jagged stone and stumbled. “Uhh!” Managing to regain my balance somehow, I didn’t fall, but even this didn’t feel like a coincidence. Could it be that the Hans effect had begun? But that was just a doppelganger, not the real Hans. Maybe the misfortune would end here...
“Yandel! There are more ahead!”

At Mr. Bear’s shout, I quickly looked around again. Two doppelgangers were approaching. I knew for a fact what they were as soon as I laid eyes on them for one simple reason: the two people who emerged from the darkness were wearing the exact same face.
God damn it.
I squeezed my eyes shut, then opened them again, but the scene in front of me remained unchanged. Was this hell?
“I’m... C-Chri... sen.”
“H-Hans... Chri... sen...”
Hans was being copy-pasted.
It was just like the first time. Heedless of the flames, I rushed forward straight away and crushed his head. In this case, teamwork was just a bonus, not a necessity.
“Everyone hold your breath. We’re going through!”
“Huh? What?”
“There is no time to explain!”
Since there was no other way to go, I held my breath and sprinted through the passage. When we finally got far enough away, I turned around and checked on my teammates.
“Bjorn, your eyes are scary!” cried Ainar.

“What the hell is going on? No matter how I look at it, I don’t think there was poison there. Was that someone you know?” Raven demanded. My teammates could not hide their confusion at my strange behavior.
“Yes. I knew him.” I calmed myself down and explained everything: that the name of the doppelganger we just met was Hans, and all of the bad things that happened each time I met a Hans.
“Th-this is a big problem! But, what do I do? I breathed!” Having heard the Hans Education lesson I gave to the barbarians, Ainar listened to my personal story and bit her nails anxiously.
“...Sounds like it’s not just a coincidence.” Like any adventurer who believed in superstition, Mr. Bear also looked concerned.
“Pardon? What do you mean by that?” Raven stood there, her expression clearly saying, What kind of nonsense are you all talking about? Then she burst into laughter. “Pft, Puhahaha!”
Was she a madwoman? How could she laugh in a situation like this?
“I guess you really are a barbarian after all, Mr. Yandel.”
“That is a racist statement.”
