“Oh, I’m sorry if it sounded like that. But... P-Pffft! If you’re really worried, do you want a Wizard’s Protection?”
A Wizard’s Protection? That hadn’t existed in the game.

When I cocked my head, Raven explained calmly as if speaking to a child. “Whenever a wizard visits a poor neighborhood, kids come running up to ask us to give them luck. That’s a Wizard’s Protection.”
...So it’s just empty words?
“I don’t need it.”

“Why? It’ll at least help calm you down.” Raven cackled and said she wasn’t just joking around. She started by explaining a study that showed that strongly believing in something could affect the physical body.
It sounds like she’s referring to the placebo effect... Who do you think I am?
“Do it.”

“Okay. Sure? Oh, how was this done again? Can you bend down for a moment?” When I slumped down on the ground, Raven tapped my shoulders as if to knight me with a rather reverent expression on her face. Then she spoke in an uncharacteristically warm tone. “Everything will be fine. You have inherited my luck.”
I didn’t know about luck, but I felt my sense of reason coming back. When I thought about it, this was only a jinx. Had there been a Hans around when I ran into the Dragon Slayer?
“Ugh, honestly! Get it together! You’re the team leader!”

As per Raven’s words, I needed to snap out of it. Even if the Hans effect really did exist, as long as we were inside the Rift, meeting Hans’s real self was inevitable. All I could do was be more careful than usual.
“Me too! Do me too!”
“Can you... do me afterrr?”
“Ahem, me too.”
When my expression relaxed, my teammates gathered in front of Raven like baby birds.

“Ha... Fine. Make a line, everyone.” Even as she sighed, Raven bestowed protection on each one of us, even adding words of blessing. Was she always like this? I felt like I was witnessing an unexpected side of her. “Now, tell me. I’m sure you didn’t kill him without thinking of the consequences. You know about him already, right? About that Hans, or whatever.”
“To some extent.” After the blessings had been doled out, I took time to share the information I knew, namely what essence Hans Chrisen had and who his teammates were.
“So, his party is an elven archer, a human warrior, and a wizard?”
“The last I saw it.”
“Only four people?”

“Since they’re in the Rift, it’s highly likely there are five people now. He probably put a scout in the remaining seat.” The fourth-floor Rift opened somewhere above the twenty-fifth floor. Without a scout, finding the Rift before it reached full capacity was virtually impossible.
“That does seem likely.”

When I told them what I knew about his teammates too, Raven nodded in relief. I had a feeling I knew what she was thinking. Unless there had been a major change, Hans G’s team was clearly inferior to us.
“We won’t have to worry about any funny business when it comes to splitting the loot with them.”
“Funny business is our job.”
“If the situation requires it. We don’t know anything about the last team yet.”
Finishing off our information exchange there, we resumed our expedition. Thankfully, we seemed to be out of their range now, because after that we only ran into our own doppelgangers.
Too bad. I was hoping to learn about the last team in advance.
It seemed our paths hadn’t overlapped because the unidentified team showed no signs of appearing. But there was no use being disappointed.
“Oh! Another mana stone box!”

We wandered the cave all day and occasionally opened the boxes that appeared in our path. This was the main reward for the first stage, the Shadow Cave. Since the doppelgangers didn’t spit out any mana stones, this was how we could strike a balance.
Still, it’s a bit strange.
I thought it was just a feature in the game, but now that I was experiencing it in person, it felt strangely out of place. It almost felt like a real game.
“The hypothesis going around in the academic world is that the archmage didn’t discover the labyrinth but created it.”
Perhaps Raven’s words back then were true. If someone made the labyrinth, this setup made sense.
What even is this world in the first place?

Was this a game, or another reality? The questions I’d had since the first day I woke up in this world lingered in my mind, but as always, I folded them up and shoved them in a corner again. I wouldn’t be able to find an answer in the clues I had right now. Wasting energy on something useless was foolish.
“All the boxes are open now. Almost no doppelgangers, either. What are you going to do?”
“Aren’t you supposed to be making the calls here?” I shrugged and handed the reins over to Raven.
What she said was what I was going to say, anyway. “Um, I think we should rest here and head to the center tomorrow.”
There you go.
“Why?”

“Because there is a high chance the other teams have already gathered in the center. There’s no need to camp together, right?” It was a wizard-like, safety-focused decision. I especially liked the underlying distrust for others in said decision. “What, is there anything you want to say about my judgment?”
“Not at all.”
“Hmm, the look in your eyes is weird, though...”
“I was just thinking how glad I am to have a wizard like you on the team.” This was sincere. She’d never know how much easier things had gotten since she joined the team.
“...Flattery will get you nowhere.”
Yeah, yeah, your shoulders are already at your ears, though.
After that, we set up a rough camp and took turns taking watch as the eighth day came to an end.

That was how day nine started. Waking up a little earlier than usual, we headed to the very center of the cave. We didn’t get lost on the way. We had stayed here because of the boxes, but the way to get there was actually really simple. You just had to follow the passage with weeds.
Trudge, trudge.
The closer we got to the center, the more weeds and moss appeared on the wall. Soon, a wide cavity appeared in front of us.
“Finally, the latecomers are here!” Ten adventurers had already gathered inside.
“Oh! Y-You’re here, Mr. Yandel!” Oh, of course, Hans G was there too. Did they spend the night here? When we arrived, the adventurers were cleaning up a chaotic campsite. I quickly did a scan.
Hans G’s team is as I expected.
None of the members had changed and all four of them were the same as the last time I saw them. The unfamiliar woman with them must have been the newcomer.
The other party is...

I wasn’t sure. They were a dwarf, a beastman, and three humans. Their equipment looked roughly on par with ours. The only peculiarity was their sharp eyes. But considering the setup of the Rift, that wasn’t especially peculiar, either.
“Who is the leader there?” The dwarf came up to us. He was the guy who had called us out for being late as soon as we arrived.
“O-Oh, Mr. Yandel is probably the leader. H-He’s the one I told you about.”
“Little Balkan?”

“Y-Yes.” It looked like they’d already said their hellos. Hans G said something to the dwarf, then greeted me in a friendly tone. “N-Nice to meet you again. To think I’d see you here. Y-You have no idea h-how surprised I was t-to see your doppelganger.”
“Enough.”
“...Pardon?”

“Don’t come closer.” I lowered my voice and stopped Hans from approaching. The way I saw it, this much distance was just right for us. There was no need to mask your feelings in this world, right? I turned away from Hans G and spoke to the dwarf. “Identification tag?”
For some reason, it was Hans G who replied. “Oh, haha! I-I already checked their t-tags, so you don’t have to—”
Yeah? The way you’re acting, it’s only making me more anxious.
“Identification tag.” I ignored Hans’s words and repeated myself.
The dwarf smirked and shot back a request of his own. “You guys take yours out first.”
Did he want to kick off a psychological war or something? I didn’t particularly feel like avoiding it, but identification came first so I just gave in and showed him. “Now it is your turn.”
At my request, the dwarf showed us his. “Now, are we done?”
“...We’re done.” I nodded.
At that moment, Raven’s voice sounded in my head thanks to a transmission spell used to secretly convey messages. “Mr. Yandel. These people are not from the city.”
Yeah, you noticed too, then. These bastards are from underground.

chapters.title: Chapter 182: Jinx (2)
paragraphs: You could only have received an identification tag before entering the labyrinth. They were called identification tags, but they were really just pendants engraved with the emblem of the royal family. Before we started our journey, Raven did a general appraisal and valued each at less than three thousand stones.
“So it’s just an ordinary necklace,” I’d said back then.
“Even the palace can’t produce and distribute magical items in such a short period of time.”

The tags didn’t even have our names on them, so it was impossible to discern if one had been stolen. However, upon closer inspection, the tags had a hidden trick. It was nothing special, but something both the civil servant and the knight on the first floor had neglected to tell us.
“What’s this written here?”
“...It’s in ancient script.”

Inside the symbol of the royal family was a small number written in ancient text. The number on our tags was two. Raven and I came up with several hypotheses about this and, after comparing ours with various other adventurers’, came to a conclusion.
“The tag numbers on those clan members earlier were all three.”
This ancient number signified the adventurer’s rank. Not their exact rank, but one for low rank, two for middle rank, and three for high rank.
“So that’s why they asked our rank when they handed them out.”
“Why didn’t they tell us then?”
“Because they’re concerned that Noark might abuse the system.”

Of course, the system was crude and easy to figure out as long as you could read ancient script like us. But in terms of bang for your buck, it wasn’t bad. Stamping an extra number while embossing wasn’t that difficult, and we were benefiting from it now.
Goddamn Hans effect.

I focused on keeping my expression under control and gripped my shield tighter. The number on the dwarf team’s tags was one. That meant they were from Noark and had stolen the tags. Just a glance at their equipment told me there was no way these were low-rank adventurers.
What should I do now? Destroy them right away?
That was the first option that came to mind, but upon close review, it was the worst possible option. Raven seemed to be thinking along the same lines.
“They don’t know their identities have been exposed yet. So we should pretend we don’t know anything either and start our quest for now.”
Yes, that was the best option.
When I nodded in response to the transmission, the dwarf eyed me with a strange look. “Is there a problem?”
“No, there isn’t. Let’s introduce ourselves. I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel. You are?”
“Jagurth Martin.” It was a dwarven name, but obviously a pseudonym.
“Ah! I am H-Hans Chrisen.” Hans G also revealed his name and with that, the introductions between the party leaders were over.
“Identification tag?”
“Ah, here it is. What are you all doing? Show yours too, quick.”
Just in case, I checked Hans G’s team’s tags too. All of them were two except for the newcomer, who had a one.
“Um... s-since we have to work together now, w-why don’t we introduce everyone?”
“Hmm, work together? Do you know about this Rift?”
At the dwarf’s question, Hans G nodded confidently. “Yes, to some extent. I like books.”
It was kind of funny seeing it in action. “I read it in a book”? That was my go-to excuse too.
“Explain. What happens next?”
“Since we are all gathered, if we put our hands together, the path ahead will open. And if we follow the path, we’ll reach the forest.”
“...You are useful.”
“Haha... I’m glad to be a h-help. On that note, why don’t we take time to share what everyone does best and get to know each other?”
Afterward, following Hans G’s suggestion, we briefly introduced each party’s comp. To summarize, it was like this:
Team Hans G: Summoner, Wizard, Blunt Weapon Warrior, Scout, Elven Archer.
Team Dwarf: Dwarf Warrior, Beast Swordsman, Sorcerer, Archer, Priest.

“Oh! There is a priest!” Upon hearing the composition of the dwarf’s team, Hans G’s expression suddenly brightened. Now that we had to run a raid, he seemed to be glad about the presence of a priest... But it was obvious it was just a priest of Karui.
“So, about the loot distribution...”

Like any adventurers meeting in a Rift, after the introductions came a discussion about the loot. We decided that any party that defeated a trash mob would take its loot. For loot from joint hunts, we agreed to roll a die. However, it was not a fair die.

Raven went into negotiation mode, where she wheedled her opponent with a soft voice. “Shouldn’t the team who contributes more get more? Mr. Chrisen, am I right? It’s obvious your side is going to be the least help.”
“A-As I said before, we have information about the Rift—”
“I’m well informed about Doppelganger Forest too.”
“Wait a minute. Aren’t you being too rude?” In the middle of the conversation, Team Hans’s elven archer got triggered, but it didn’t change anything.
“Miss Meirin, please stop. S-She’s not wrong,” Hans said.
“Yes, let’s admit it. We were in hot water against that barbarian’s doppelganger earlier. Asking for equal distribution when the difference in our skills is this wide would be unfair to them.”
When the leader and wizard said the same thing, the elf clammed up. Then, Hans G turned to us, resigned. “We will subtract one from any rolls we make.”
“Subtract two. Instead, we’ll use a die that goes up to ten.”
“...All right. But instead, p-please increase our share if we make an assist.”

“That is a reasonable proposition. While we’re at it, why don’t we make that a rule? If any party makes a mistake, subtract one from their roll, and add it to the party that assisted them. How about that?” Raven looked straight at the dwarf.
He nodded obediently. “Sounds fine to me.” Because I’m going to stab you in the back, anyway.
Or did I just imagine that last line?
As we all gathered at the altar located in the center of the common area, the vines blocking the passageway unfurled to reveal an uphill path.
“We’ll go in first. I hope you won’t follow too close behind.”
“Well, of course.”
Keeping a safe distance between the teams, we reached the forest before too long. Now, the second stage began.

[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Doppelganger Forest has been activated. Status effect Distrust is now active. The damage you deal is doubled when attacking other members of your expedition.]
The contents of this stage were very simple: go around the forest, defeat the three mini-bosses, and find the altar somewhere.
“Then which party leads the way?”
“I think it would be better to take turns.”

Adventurers were distrustful by default, so we moved in separate teams rather than one big group. From a bird’s eye view, the formation would look like an isosceles triangle. Our system was to take care of monsters coming our own way in each direction and provide support if others were in danger.
“Cast a voice control spell first.”

Although the other teams were quite a long way from us, we used voice magic to communicate. Defeating the doppelgangers that appeared every few minutes, we continued our quest. We passed quite a bit of time like that.
“Nyaha! What is that dwarrrf?! He acted so tough, but fighting him is nothing special!”
Naturally, we hunted doppelgangers of the other two groups and acquired information on them. Hans G’s team was easy, as expected, and the dwarf’s team wasn’t as strong as I thought.
About rank five, I presume.
For me, who had left the possibility that he might be a Dragon Slayer-level opponent open, this was extremely fortunate news.
“Raven, turn on voice control.”
“Pardon? I already did?”
Oh, I forgot to mention. “Just you and me.” This was a sensitive subject.
“Hm? Why just you two...?” asked Missha.
“I will explain everything later.”
Openly left out of the conversation, the other three expressed their curiosity but nodded after seeing the look on my face.
“...It’s done,” said Raven. “But you don’t want to tell the other three?”
“I don’t think they have a talent for acting.” It wasn’t particularly intentional, but our gazes both automatically shifted to Ainar. “...Let’s not get into that.”
“Yes. That would be best.”
I got straight to the point instead. “So, how do you think that group will act?”
“I’m seeing a fifty-fifty possibility. They might just want a peaceful expedition and leave... Or they could be greedy.”
The answer was kind of surprising. “Fifty-fifty?” I thought for sure she would see the greedy outcome as more probable.
“They have fewer people than us. And after actually fighting them, they are weaker than us too.”
Hmm, that was true.
“Still, one thing is for certain. Even if they get greedy, it won’t be right now. It’ll probably be after the guardian is defeated.”
That aligned with my own suspicions. Doppelganger Forest was a Rift with a full capacity of fifteen for a reason. It was difficult to clear as a single party unless you were extremely skilled.
“You know what that means, right? On the flip side, that means that we also can’t take down those guys first until we defeat the guardian.”
“Yes, I know.”

This was the most goddamn annoying part of the current situation. Nip it in the bud. The root of all evil had to be uprooted immediately in order to bring peace, yet we couldn’t make the first move! My mace was itching to swing.
“Then how about them?”
“The team with Hans?”
“Yes. Did you notice anything suspicious?”
“I don’t know. He seems a little dorky, but doesn’t seem like a bad person.”

“Doesn’t seem like a bad person, huh?” It certainly did look that way, but I knew that Hans G was the same person who had led more than a hundred adventurers to their deaths while trying to save himself from being trapped in the Evil Rift. We couldn’t just see him as an idiot. He was also a player. “Hah...”
I sighed involuntarily. Hans G and adventurers from Noark. Why did things go into hard mode every time I entered a Rift?
“Bjorn, doppelganger!”
“...Watch that team carefully along with the dwarf’s. If you notice anything strange, tell me right away,” I told Raven.
“All right.”

I finished the conversation there and focused on the expedition. Despite what I was expecting, no one inquired deeply into our conversation. There was no way they weren’t curious... They probably just trusted it was necessary and were waiting for us to tell them when we were ready.
You’re making me feel guilty.
“R-Requesting support!”
Anyway, aside from Hans G’s team occasionally asking for help, time passed without incident. By nightfall, we found one of the three mini-bosses.
“I-It’s a Manticore!”
This was one of the few non-doppelgangers in this Rift, and one rumored to have good bang for its buck in terms of remains and essences.
[You have defeated a Manticore. EXP +5]
Thanks to the information from Raven and Hans G, the fight itself was not difficult. However, the problem was... well, I guess it wasn’t exactly a problem.
“Everyone, stop!”
An essence had dropped, the first essence in a long while that I could absorb.
“Raven, get out the die!”
We had to win this.

chapters.title: Chapter 183: Jinx (3)
paragraphs: The Manticore was a rank-five monster with the body of a lion and the face of a human. This guy’s essence was quite peculiar.
[Manticore]
[Discernment: +40
Appetite: +30
Leaping Power: +30]
Its stats were mainly just thirty points to Leaping Power. In a way, they were lower than the essence of a rank-nine monster, but its passive ability was related to stats as well.
[(P) Heredity—Mana stone consumption will permanently increase the user’s stats.]
Heredity was a skill that let the user increase their stats by eating mana stones. That description alone sounded extremely overpowered, but there was an important constraint in place.
The sum of the absorbable stats is two hundred or so.

The total number of stat points you could obtain from the skill was two hundred. At first, I wondered what kind of trash essence this was. Among rank five monsters, there were many essences with a total of over three hundred stats attached. But for this one, you had to use its passive skill to get even basic stats. The active skill wasn’t that great either, unless it came with the Manticore’s core ability, Random Skill Rampage, but that was a unique ability that couldn’t be acquired with an essence.
“Everyone, stop!”
However, the moment this essence came out, the looks in everyone’s eyes changed.
Yeah, so you all know the true value of this essence.
“Raven, get out the die!”
In time with my shout, the dwarf let out a growl. “I think it’s best you take a step back first, barbarian.”
What, you think I’ll steal it if I lose?
It was ridiculous, but nothing good would come out of arguing right now. “...Let’s all step back at the same time.”
“Fine.”
“Y-Yes! I think that would be good.”

Starting with me, everyone stepped back together and began to settle the situation as quick as lightning. Essences only stuck around for an average of thirty minutes. So, I asked the question I couldn’t ask earlier, just in case. “Are there any teams that will be giving up their bid?”
Hans G and the dwarf both shook their heads. “W-We will participate,” said Hans. “Except the wizard or priest, a-anyone could use this essence.”

Damn player bastard. Where the Manticore’s essence truly shined was after it was erased. Even after it was gone, the user retained 20 percent of the extra stats. It was essentially the same as taking an elixir with forty bonus stats.
“Why would I give up on this expensive essence?” the dwarf asked.
“...Expensive essence? Are you thinking of selling it?”
“None of us have room for one.”
Hmm, that made sense, but suddenly a possibility came to mind.
These bastards are from the underground city, right?

For adventurers of Noark, erasing an essence from the temple was a tricky procedure, especially if the city was locked down. Holding onto it and secretly selling it after the lockdown would make more sense. However, the biggest question still remained.

“...But your party doesn’t have a wizard?” There were no wizards on the dwarf’s team. The sorcerer, who had used all their essence slots on attack-type essences, played a similar role in terms of firepower, but you couldn’t replace a wizard skills.
The dwarf’s reply was flippant. “But you guys do. We’ll pay for the test tube and the cost of labor.”
Who are you trying to swindle?
“And if we refuse both?”
The dwarf laughed at my suggestion to stop being greedy. “The die will be rolled anyway. And if we win, we’ll watch until the essence disappears.”

In other words, that meant that they’d choose to intervene if they couldn’t have it. That left a bitter taste in my mouth. Underground or above, adventurers were still adventurers, it seemed. In this respect, both cities were remarkably similar.
Do we just ambush and kill them here?
Of course, such extreme methods came to mind, but I managed to regain my composure. Raven’s help played a big part. “Mr. Yandel, there’s no choice.”

Yes, we hadn’t even rolled the die yet. It was not even a core essence in my build like the Orc Hero’s, which had Giantization. Once I was able to get rank three essences, it would have to be erased anyway, and there were better alternatives.
“So how long are you going to stand there?”

I came to my senses at the dwarf’s insistence. “Let’s have a representative from each team.” And so, the leaders of each team gathered in one place. I briefly explained the rules. “One person throws the die at a time, and the person with the highest number gets the loot. However, if two people roll the same number, only those two will roll again.”
“Are we going to use that wizard’s die?”
“This is a genuine Adventurers’ Guild die. I don’t care if we don’t use mine. Of course, I’ll have to check before we roll in that case.”
“Really? Then it doesn’t matter to me.”
The dwarf nodded coolly, and after Hans G’s wizard came over to confirm the die was fair, we were ready to begin.
“Hans, as promised, your rolls will be reduced by two. So if you have something to say, say it now.”
“...W-We’ll be content with just having the opportunity.”
“That’s that, then. Now, who will start?”
Should I go first or later? Not that it really mattered, but everyone gulped and carefully eyed each other.

Unexpectedly, Hans G was the one who stepped forward. “I-I will go first.” He picked up the die. Although they had the handicap of needing to subtract two from the roll, his teammates cheered him on with obvious hope in their eyes.
“Mr. Chrisen, you’ve got this!”
“Hans, you’d better be prepared for an ass-whooping if you don’t roll properly.”
“Chrisen, it’s okay to lose, so don’t feel too pressured.”

Hans G met his team’s eyes one by one: the rookie scout, the human warrior, the middle-aged wizard, and the elven archer. The elf nodded without a word. Anyone could see that the relationship between the two was very special.
Geez, are we in a shonen manga or something?
That made me laugh. The scout saw that and bit her lip in anger.
“Then... I’ll roll!” Hans G gave the die an enthusiastic roll.
Roll...
The die rolled across the dry soil, the small and large numbers on each side flashing at us in turns.
Tap.
In the silence, the die stopped rolling. The number written on the upturned side was a whopping ten, the largest number that could be rolled on the die.
“Kyahhh!”
“That’s crazy! Unreal!”
“Average market price! Mr. Parteian, what’s the average market price according to the guild?”
Cheers erupted from his team. On the other hand, we fell into stunned silence.
The dwarf stepped forward, apparently disapproving of how fired up they were. “You speak as if the essence is already yours. You didn’t forget you have to subtract two, did you?”
“Ah, yes... I’m aware.” The celebratory mood subsided significantly, but Hans G’s team was still festive. Eight was still a high number.
“I’ll go next.” The dwarf walked up to Hans G and snatched up the die. He hesitated for a moment before scowling and tossing it crudely on the floor.
Roll...
The die stopped moving before long on a nine. Was this real life?
“Ahhhhhh!”
“Fuck!”
“I believed in you! You son of a bitch!”

Beastly shouts erupted from the dwarf’s team. On the other hand, Hans G’s team froze, unable to rein in their expressions. The dwarf looked at me and Hans G and sneered. He spoke the sequence of words I’d probably uttered least in my entire life. “Luck is on my side.”
What the hell was wrong with this bastard? An overwhelming feeling of despair swallowed me whole. However, I could not just lie down and accept defeat. I had too many things going for me to do that.
“Yandel! Don’t be so dejected. It’s not like you.”
“I believe in you, Bjorn! You can do it!”
“Yes, yes, Bjorn! You can do anything, rrremember?!”
“I won’t talk probabilities. Things like that mean nothing to you anyway, right?”
I still had teammates who believed in me. And I also had myself, someone who never gave up. For that reason, I grabbed the die.
Squeeze.

The dwarf let out an arrogant laugh at the sight. The situation was pretty familiar. Hans’s number was eight. The dwarf’s number was nine. I just had to roll a ten. Probability was just probability—it was meaningless. This kind of dramatic setup showed up in movies and cartoons all the time. Yes, judging by the way the scene was progressing, this would work!
It had to work.
“...Bjorn’s eyes look different.”
That strange certainty flowed through my hand. It felt like something invisible was giving me a warm embrace. Before that feeling could leave me, I threw the die.
“Go! Great warriooor!” Ainar shouted as the die began to roll. Surprisingly, my mind was calmer than ever as I watched.
Thump.

My heartbeat was steady. The air touching my skin was moderately cool, and as if time was passing slowly, every second of this scene was engraved in my mind. And with that pleasant sensation still blanketing me, I noticed the moment the die stopped.
Tap.
The air changed instantly. Silence descended, cold and downcast. Instead of the die, I was looking at the people around me.
“Holy...”
The arrogantly smiling dwarf, my teammates who had watched and believed in me... even Hans G, whose defeat was already confirmed, could not hide his astonishment. His jaw dropped.
Did it really happen...?
I finally checked the die. It had landed on a one.
...I should’ve gotten Missha to throw it.
A loser had to stay silent because anything they said would just be an excuse. They could only take it on the chin, just like I was right now.

“Hahaha! A one with that expression! Did you see it? Did you? I was so scared there. His eyes were so confident.” Sharp mockery erupted from Team Dwarf. A feeling of contempt covered me from head to toe. “I just want to ask. How the hell did you manage to get that look in your eyes? Ahahaha!”
“Don’t make fun of Bjorn!”
“Go! Great warrior! Pft! Pft! Ahahahaha!”
“...I’ll kill you!”
I grabbed Ainar, who was about to charge. “Enough.”
“But! If I don’t crush that head of his...!”
Yeah, that snout of his would never shut. I knew the feeling better than anyone, but now was not the time. The other team knew that very well too.

“You guys stop too.” When I stared at him in silence, the dwarf also stopped his teammates from making any more taunts. After all, the winner was decided. I let go of my disappointment and shifted gears. “How much will you offer?”
“Fifteen million stones for a test tube.”
That was just the standard price. “And the cost of labor?”
“I’ll give you five million stones.”
Earning five million stones for casting one magic spell was a profitable business. However... “Seven million.”
“You are greedy.” The dwarf eyed Hans G’s team. Since there were two wizards, he could just ask the other one.
“W-We don’t have a test tube.”
What? I had highballed my price to split the cost of labor with them, but this changed things.
At Hans G’s words, the dwarf accepted my proposal without hesitation. “I’ll give you seven million.”
However, that train had already left the station. “It’s too late. It just went up to fifteen million.” In effect, the cost of labor had become equal to the cost of the test tube.
“Don’t be unreasonable, barbarian,” the dwarf sputtered, appalled.

It wasn’t that I didn’t get where he was coming from. Being so short, it must have been hard for him to see the bigger picture of how the world worked. Thus, it was only natural that he was unaware of the most basic principle of the market—aka supply and demand.
“Unreasonable? I think this is a reasonable price. Especially since you won’t reject it.”
“...Ten million stones.”
“There is no negotiation here. If you don’t like it, don’t take it.”
“Think this through rationally, barbarian. Are you going to throw this money away?”

“It is your choice. Throw away the essence, or just pay us, store it in the test tube, and sell it.” I boldly stuck to my guns to the bitter end. This was the reason why monopolies were able to cruelly throw their weight around in the capitalist market. Business deals still happened, even like this.
“...God damn it.” The dwarf trembled in anger, then parted his lips. “I’ll offer you fifteen million stones.”
“That’s a good choice—”
“I’m not talking to you.” The dwarf looked at Hans G. “I’m talking to them.”
“Pardon? I-I don’t know what you mean...”
“If you pay us that amount, I will pass ownership of this essence onto you.”
On-site sales, huh? So that’s how you’re going to play this.
This was a purely emotional choice that abandoned all logic. I’ll admit it made me flinch for a moment, but it turned out not to be a big issue.
“W-We don’t have that kind of money right now.”
“You can pay in kind.”

“Let me discuss it first...” Hans G took a moment to talk it over with his teammates. Judging by the way their mouths were moving with no sound, it seemed they had activated a voice control spell as well. It didn’t take long, and the conclusion they reached was also not all that different from what I had expected. “A-As we thought, we need our equipment...” The quality of Team Hans G’s equipment wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t that great either, and at least three of them would have to toss in their main pieces of equipment to match the price. Exchanging their equipment for an essence that was useless right now was nonsense. “W-Which is why... how about we p-pay you in the city?”

“...That’s not an option.” There was no way these guys from the underground city could sell to Hans G on credit. Driven into a corner, the dwarf let out a rough sigh. Then he looked at me and said in a super unwilling tone, “Barbarian, at the price you mentioned—”
“Twenty million stones. It just went up again.”
“You mother—”
“Or we can buy the essence from you at fifteen million stones, would you like to do that instead?”
“...I will pay the twenty million stones.” The dwarf cursed me, but that didn’t change the result. Even after having to pay me, he would still make a good profit of about 11.7 million stones.
No, wait. Then we earned a bigger profit?
Indeed, this was the taste of monopoly. Even though our number on the die was the smallest, we were the ones receiving the greatest share. Quite ironic.

After the negotiations were over, things proceeded quickly. First, we received twenty million stones in kind from the dwarf’s team. Obviously, they wouldn’t have money like that on hand. They tried to hand us equipment, but I refused because they started taking out a pile of unused equipment from their backpacks. Just how many people had they plundered?
“Give us potions so that we can calculate the cash amount more easily.”
“...We can’t pay you that much money in potions.”

“Then I’ll take the remainder in equipment.” Even after hearing their reasoning, I demanded as many potions as possible. Since we might end up battling these guys, I decided it was best to reduce their maximum power as much as possible before that. Taking the equipment they had on them would make them easier to deal with too.

“Seven bottles of advanced potion and one high-rank potion. Plus the rest of the equipment... sounds about right.” With the help of Raven, who was a certified general appraiser, the spot transaction ended without argument and we set up camp in a suitable spot after that.
One person from each team was selected to join the night watch, so a total of three stood guard each shift. The first watch was Hans G, the dwarf, and Mr. Bear. Next in line was me.
“Yandel, it’s your turn.”
“Has anything happened? Like a suspicious conversation between them?”
“It was mostly the Hans guy talking to himself. I was even starting to think it would be more comfortable and enjoyable to stand watch alone.”
“Right, good job. Get some rest.”
My night watch group consisted of an elven archer named Meirin and a beast warrior from the White Wolf Tribe. It was an uncomfortable few hours in many ways.
I can see why he said he would have been more comfortable alone.
The wolf warrior was silent, and the elven archer kept shooting me icy looks the entire watch.
“Do you have something to say to me?”
“Everyone is sleeping, how about being a little quieter?”
Oh, you tree-hugger.
What was there to hate about kind barbarians? These guys clearly had a personality problem. Oh, except for Erwen.
Whatever, just stand guard.

I was more wary of these guys betraying me than a surprise attack from a monster because the odds of them stabbing us in the back were now much higher. I didn’t know about Hans G, but the dwarf bastard clearly had a knife ready for us in his heart.
That’s probably why they paid us so generously.
Even considering the monopoly we held, twenty million was practically extortion. But he had paid the amount incredibly coolly... almost as if he thought there was a way for him to get it back.
Well, I’m in the same boat, I guess.
I still hadn’t given up on the essence in that test tube yet. I was just biding my time.
“Missha, get up. Shift change.”
After my shift—which was unpleasant, to say the least—was over, I switched with Missha and fell asleep.
The next morning, the quest resumed again. Except for the occasional meal break, we spent all of our time searching the forest and as a result, were able to defeat the two remaining mini-bosses.
[You have defeated a Duocorn. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Culves. EXP +5]
Unfortunately, no essence appeared.
“Huh? Isn’t that it? The thing you guys told us about beforrre!”
However, we succeeded in finding and reaching the third stage, which I predicted would take another day.
[You have entered the Shadow Altar.]
As soon as we found the altar, a black shadow enveloped us. A huge barrier formed around us before we could blink. The concept of this stage and my duty here were clear.
[The sealed doppelganger now resides in the body of one of the members of your expedition.]
Okay, time to use some good old-fashioned politics, starting with this bastard. “Dwarf, your face looks off. Is there something wrong with your head?”

chapters.title: Chapter 184: Jinx (4)
paragraphs: The rules of the third chapter, the Shadow Altar, were simple: find the member of your expedition possessed by the doppelganger and offer them to the altar. That was it. If we were correct, the doppelganger residing in their body would be removed. But if we were wrong?
They will be incapacitated until the Rift is cleared.
In other words, if I played my cards right, I could get rid of someone who could get in my way.
“Dwarf, your face looks off. Is there something wrong with your head?”

“Hmm, seeing as you’re trying to oust me from the get-go, you’re the one who is more suspicious here.” My first target, the dwarf, did not panic and counterattacked. Just as I thought, he was not an easy one to handle.
But the real attack started now. “Suspicious? That’s strange. When I first met you, you clearly sounded like you knew nothing about this place. But now you speak as if you know?”

“Oh, you’re right.” When Raven agreed, Hans G’s teammates also began to grow suspicious. This made sense. We had just gotten here, and we hadn’t yet discussed what the third stage entailed. So how did the dwarf know to defend himself?
“That’s...” The dwarf thought it over for a moment, then without hiding his displeasure, spat out, “I heard from Hans.”
“...Lying to get out of trouble, huh.”
Hans G stepped in just in time to assist the dwarf. “I-It’s not a lie. I told him.”
“Told him? When?” Since I’d kept an eye on them throughout the entire journey, I couldn’t accept this explanation.
“Y-Yesterday, during watch.”
He was indeed out of my sight at the time, but I had assigned Mr. Bear to them for this exact reason. “Abman, is that true?”
“Of course not. The two of them didn’t have that kind of conversation.”
“Says Abman, who was with you. Hans Chrisen, why are you covering for the dwarf?”
As I took a threatening step forward, Hans G frantically waved his hands. “I-It’s not a cover-up. It’s the truth! We used a magical item t-to talk... So Mr. Urikfried couldn’t tell!”

A conversation had with a magical device... It didn’t sound like a lie. Goddamn it, when did they get so close? I would have been in big trouble if I hadn’t figured that out here. “What did you talk about?” I had to find out.
“Th-that’s...” When I intentionally expelled murderous energy, Hans G trailed off, unable to overcome the pressure.

Just when I was about to cut it out, the dwarf stepped in as if to protect Hans. “Why should we tell you that? It was a private conversation. And that seems to have cleared up the question of how I know of this altar.” With that skillful argument, he left no room for rebuttal and resolutely put an end to the conversation.

Of course, so far there had been no disruption to my plans. Even without this, I had countless ways to attack these guys. “From now on, let’s talk about ourselves.” The dwarf was an adventurer from Noark, and Hans G was someone this world considered an evil spirit. If I aimed for these weak points, there would inevitably be inconsistencies in their answers. “Dwarf, what’s your adventurer ranking? Do you have family? Siblings?”
“...I don’t want to talk about myself.”
“So you refuse.” I smirked. They had a right to remain silent, but they had a responsibility to answer. In this place right now, all questions were justified.

“Excuse me, I think it’s best to do as Mr. Yandel says. I’m not saying that because he’s our team leader, but the fact is that there’s a doppelganger here, right?” Raven provided supporting fire with logic.

Agreeing that this method was the best, Hans G’s wizard also supported our opinion. “Let’s do that. We can’t just blindly offer someone to the altar. Let’s discuss this together. Then we’ll know who it is. There are ways to discern even a doppelganger.”
The public opinion was swayed in an instant. In the end, the dwarf had no choice but to back off. “...Fine. Then how should we do this?”
It was Hans G who answered the dwarf’s question. “I suppose verification magic would be best?” Like a player, he presented the most classic strategy.
But at that moment, the blunt weapon warrior on Hans G’s team carefully raised his hand and expressed a concern. “Um, but I heard verification magic doesn’t work on everybody?”

It was a sharp question that didn’t seem to match his average-looking face. He was right—verification spells didn’t work on everyone. For example, me. It hadn’t worked on me when I was in the guild that one time. According to Raven, mana resistance was one thing, but it seemed I also had an innately thick mental barrier.
“It doesn’t matter if it doesn’t work. I heard it doesn’t work on doppelgangers, anyway.”
“Y-Yes! That’s right! We can at least use it to reduce the number of suspects.”
“True, even that will be helpful enough.”
When the brainiacs Raven and Hans G combined their voices, there were no more objections. And so, the official hunt began.
“Are you a man?”
“...Why are you asking that?”
“Haha, I’m just making sure the spell is working properly, so you can just answer however you want.”
“As you can see, I’m a man.”
“That’s the truth.”

The two wizards went around and attempted to verify everyone’s words with magic. As a result, nine people were identified as being immune to the spell: on Hans’s team, Hans, the wizard, and the elven archer; on the dwarf’s team, the dwarf, the archer, the sorcerer, and the priest; and on my team, me and Raven. As a side note, the number far exceeded my expectations. I figured this would be the case for wizards and sorcerers who had high mana resistance and willpower, but there were others here who were also immune to truth spells? Was it because everyone here was a rather experienced adventurer?
I didn’t think it would be more than half the group...
Thanks to that, I now had a headache, but my job remained the same.
“Are you a doppelganger?” First, the same question was asked to those on whom the verification spell was working, and everyone answered “no” to greatly reduce the list of suspects.
“So the doppelganger bastard is hiding among the nine of us.” Everyone’s eyes were much sharper as we all looked at each other. The situation was quite favorable for me, though. “I’ll go first.”
Once those who answered “no” were removed from the list, I brandished an executioner’s sword. I had just two targets: the dwarf and Hans G, who were also the leaders of each team.
“Where did you get the equipment in the backpack?”
“Why are you asking that?”
“Answer the question.”
“...I won’t tell you.”
Exercising the right to remain silent, huh? That’s fine with me.
“Hans Chrisen, it sounds like you know a lot about this forest. Where did you get that information?”
“I-I read it in a book.”
“What is the title of the book?”
“That’s... I won’t tell you.”

As my questions continued, the no-comments stacked up. This was all part of my plan. Technically these weren’t questions relevant to finding a doppelganger, but anyone who was hiding something would only look suspicious.
“...We may be immune to the verification spell, but I see no one wants to answer truthfully?”

The dwarf burst out laughing at my suspicious muttering. “Like you’re any different!” It looked like I had properly attracted his aggro. After taking a beating from my hostile personal attacks, the dwarf refused to hold back anymore. “What essences do you have?”
“...I cannot say.”
“Because you can’t remember because you’re a doppelganger?” When the dwarf opened fire, his teammates joined in and attacked me for doing the same to their own leader.
“Come to think of it, this guy was the one who started drilling people without evidence.”
“Almost as if he doesn’t care who ends up on the altar...”
“Not only that, but he’s too logical for a barbarian.”

I just remained silent throughout the assault. Then, Hans G’s team began throwing questions at me too. “I heard doppelgangers have flawed memories. Do you remember the last time we met, back in the Land of the Dead? What happened then?”
“That... I don’t remember very well.”
“Hmm, are you saying you forgot?”
“...I am a barbarian.”
“Pft, what a convenient race.” When I couldn’t answer, the elven archer let out a caustic laugh. It seemed my attack on Hans G earlier had gotten on her nerves... Oh, these newbies.
“The fact that you’re insisting that I’m the doppelganger must mean you are the doppelganger! Missha, Ainar! Don’t you think so too?”
“Huh? Uh, yeah...”
“B-Bjorn, the great warrior, must be right!”
Even my teammates had a lukewarm reaction to my forceful assertion and did not play along. Thus, the gazes on me grew colder. Then, finally, the moment I had been waiting for arrived.
When the hands of the clock overlapped at midnight, white light began to emanate from the altar in the center of the space.
[The Stone of Truth has formed.]

This was this stage’s key item. Without needing any prodding, Raven explained it to me. “It’s the Stone of Truth. It makes it so a person can only speak the truth, but only once. Even if it’s the doppelganger speaking.”
“...Does it show up again after?”
“I heard it appears every night at midnight. However, the doppelganger’s powers grow stronger each time you use it.”
“So we have to be careful.”
I kept my mouth shut, like someone who was anxious about something. I inspected everyone’s faces and met the dwarf’s eyes.

“Let’s decide by vote. I choose that barbarian. He’s obviously suspicious.” The dwarf smirked and threw me to the wolves. Without the need for a ballot box, several people raised their hands and eight votes were collected in an instant. That was more than half of us.
“...Think again carefully. I am not a doppelganger.” I gave them my sincere advice, but it was ignored.
“How do you use this? Oh, like this?” The dwarf rubbed the Stone of Truth and it emitted a white light. “Barbarian,” he asked, “are you a doppelganger?”
My reply was immediate. “I am not a doppelganger.”
Pzzzzz.
The Stone of Truth lost power and crumbled.
“Wizard, why did this happen?”
“Why do you think? It means he spoke the truth.”

Now that I had what I wanted, it was time to quit the idiot act. I stretched my arms up and loosened my tight neck. “I told you to think again.” I had now secured the citizenship I needed for my plan. To put it simply, no one would be able to doubt or attack me from now on. “Dwarf, why did you insist I was the doppelganger? Are you the doppelganger?”
Time to get down to some serious politics.

“That’s! Because you acted suspiciously...!” The dwarf shouted like he was making excuses. I got where he was coming from. I was the one who had started attacking left and right from the get-go and had made several seemingly sloppy moves, but that didn’t mean I had to go easy on him.
“What suspicious act? I answered everyone’s questions.”
“...You didn’t tell us your essences!”
“You act like you’re from another world. Don’t you know how rude it is to ask an adventurer about their essences?”
“Then how about earlier?! What’s your explanation for that? The elf asked you—”
“I told you, I forgot.” I straightened my shoulders without the slightest hint of shame. The barbarian forgot. What was he gonna do about it?

Realizing he had been fooled by my trick, the dwarf clammed up. Except, I guess it was difficult to watch their leader go through such humiliation because another member of his party chimed in. “That’s enough, barbarian. The votes speak to your suspicious behavior.”
Correct. They speak to a beatdown from an ignorant barbarian!

“That’s because you were all ganging up on me!” the roar of the wronged barbarian echoed through the chamber. The dwarf team’s archer tried to say something but their words were buried under my overwhelming voice. “Did you give me time to explain? You’re the one who stole the stone Raven was holding and used it!”
“No, that’s—”
“I think you guys are suspicious! Own up to it and go to the altar!”
“I’m telling you, I didn’t steal it—”
“Own up to it and go to the altar!”
Only then did the archer shout as hard as he could. “Then we’ll use the Stone of Truth tomorrow! Is that enough for you!?”
It looked like these guys had started to realize the benefits they could get out of the Stone of Truth. But, uh-oh. They were too late.

“Yes, it is you!” As the line I had been bidding for came out, I reined in my excitement and stomped forward. The air grew tense and hostile in an instant. “Say that again, archer! Not only did you waste it on me, but you’ll use it again? Are you the doppelganger?”

I switched targets from the dwarf to the archer. This had been my plan from the beginning. No matter how much of a fuss I made, I knew it would be impossible to get the dwarf or the priest, the key members of their team, on the altar.
“Come to think of it, it was you! Every time I said something, you kept egging the dwarf on!”
“It wasn’t just me, everyone—”

“Take responsibility and get on the altar! It’s not like it’ll kill you. Clearing the Rift with one less archer is not a problem!” The furious shout rendered rational thinking difficult. As his attempt to argue with me backfired on him, the archer’s face turned white.
But did that seem strange to some of the others? A few on Hans G’s team started to switch sides. “Certainly, that might be a more reasonable route than using the stone.”
“...And it won’t kill you, either.”
In the end, the dwarf had to step in. “Fine, get on the altar.”
“Sorry? What do you mean—”
“Enough. Do as I say. Unless you’re the doppelganger.”
It appeared the leader’s authority was quite strong in his party because the archer couldn’t make a single sound.
“Martin! Are you really going to put him on the altar?”
The dwarf nodded his head resolutely despite the uneasy look in his colleagues’ eyes. I could clearly see what he was thinking.
He’s trying to use this to turn public opinion in his favor.
He was doing exactly what I had done. If he put the archer onto the altar at my insistence, but he was not the doppelganger, then they would have the right to accuse us instead.
Since he can’t attack me, he’ll probably aim for Raven.

His strategy was to sacrifice his archer in order to force our wizard, an important part of our party, onto the altar. This could be a boon to them later since wizards performed incredibly well in PKs.
Idiots.
They probably thought they had nothing to lose. After all, if the archer really was the doppelganger, things worked out for them either way.
However... You think a doppelganger would willingly go to the altar?
I wiped the smile off my face and watched the archer get dragged over to the altar by his leader.
“Don’t worry. Once the guardian is defeated, you will be released safe and sound.”
“...I’ll be waiting here.”
Eventually, the archer stood in front of the altar. Everyone watched in silence.
Shaaaaa!
When the archer touched the altar with a determined look on his face, light burst forth.
[The soul of expedition member Arka Petray has been sealed.]
The soul that was pulled out of the archer’s body floated in the air, connected to the altar. His movements and expression clearly looked pained.
“Wizard. No, Hans Chrisen. What does this mean?”
“...H-He’s not the doppelganger.”

The dwarf let out a long sigh and opened his eyes after a beat. Even though this was his decision, it seemed he was feeling mixed emotions after seeing that. But did he figure that this wasn’t the time for all that? “Barbarian, are you ready to take responsibility for your words?” the dwarf growled.
I answered immediately. “No, why should I take responsibility?”
“That’s... because of you... my teammate ended up like that! Following your logic, it’s time to check your side too!”
Tsk, tsk.
I shot him a look that clearly told him how pathetic I found that logic. “How childish.”
“...What?”
“Is finding the doppelganger a joke to you? Stop being emotional and think rationally.”
The dwarf did not respond to my calm rebuttal. Well, I was sure he probably hadn’t expected he would hear this from a barbarian who had been screaming bloody murder just a moment ago.
“Grow up, dwarf.”
Even though your height will stay the same.
“What the fuck!?”

As he cursed, I calmly reached out my hand and stopped him. “Wait, you’re not trying to attack me, are you? Unless you’re a doppelganger, you have absolutely no reason for that, no?” The dwarf’s body began to tremble. And so, I stopped provoking him. “I’m sorry about your teammate. To think he would go like that. He seemed like a nice guy...”
“Enough. Get to the point.”

“I made a mistake in a moment of excitement. But why don’t we forget the past and focus on clearing the Rift? If we lose any more people, there’s no telling whether we’ll even return alive.” This was the reason why I could troll to my heart’s content. No matter how angry he got, the dwarf was likely well aware that a fight between us right now would only lead to total annihilation.
“...So, what’s your plan?”
“I’m starting to think your priest is—”
“Everyone, stop!” Hans G’s wizard shouted then. His name was Parteian, a man who had his own middle-aged charm. “Let’s end this meaningless destruction here. I have a way to find the doppelganger.”
None of us had expected to hear that.
“What way?” There was no way he was lying given the determined look on his face. “Speak.”

When I urged him, the wizard pulled out an item from his sub-space. It was a small disc the size of a compass. As soon as I saw it, I knew what it was: No. 7234, Misplaced Trust—an item that prohibited all lies within a radius of ten yards when activated.
“Y-You had s-something like that this whole...?” Player Hans quivered like he had just encountered his natural enemy. This was a sentiment that I alone could relate to 100 percent.
“This normally isn’t an item that gets much use. Well, I figured it would come in handy one day. So this is the day. I’m sorry I didn’t bring it out sooner.”
I haven’t gotten rid of the priest bastard yet...

I let go of my disappointment. Unable to watch our dispute any longer, the wizard had pulled out his prized possession. Not using it at this point would just be strange. Unmasking the doppelganger early on had its own advantages, too, which sounded good to me.
“Fine by me.”
“...Same here.” The dwarf also set aside his hostility toward me for a moment and made overtures toward peace. It looked like we were thinking the same thing.
“Good choice. Then, shall we all gather over here?”
Everyone whose name had not yet been cleared gathered in the middle and the wizard used Misplaced Trust. The effect lasted only ten minutes. “Then who will start?”
“I will.” The dwarf kicked things off. I supposed he really wasn’t the doppelganger because he didn’t look nervous at all. However, that didn’t last long.
“Then I’ll ask you a question to check whether it’s working.” To verify that the magic was active, the wizard casually asked, “What city are you from?”
He had stepped on a land mine.
Goddamn it.
There was no way the dwarf could answer that question. A cold silence fell. The dwarf’s curved mouth twitched involuntarily.
“Why aren’t you answering? Is there a prob—” The wizard cut himself off and shut his mouth. He had just realized why the dwarf couldn’t answer. “Hold on, are you—!”
The moment the wizard’s jaw dropped, I shouted with all my might. “Prepare for battle!”
We were fucked.

chapters.title: Chapter 185: Jinx (5)
paragraphs: Anyone who’d ever been hit by a car could tell you that it all happened instantaneously and could never be undone. Just like what was happening now.
“Prepare for battle!”
At the exact same moment my shout cut through the silence, the dwarf’s sword swung at a breakneck speed and dug into the wizard’s shoulder blade.
Crunch!
The disturbing sound of tearing flesh was one that woke you up to what was happening around you. By the time the sound reached my ears, my body was already moving forward.
Dash.
My goal was to rescue Raven.
“Kyaa!”
Crossing the distance between us at a great speed, I pulled Raven into my arms and quickly retreated. Hans G’s tank did the same to their wizard.
“Both of you, look alive!”

The blunt weapon warrior who had been standing a distance away pulled Hans G and the elven archer behind him by their necks. We naturally took up defensive formations. Numerically and qualitatively, we had the advantage. With that being the case, how would the dwarf approach this unfavorable situation?
While everyone stood there on high alert, waiting to see how this would shake out, the dwarf, who had pulled out the ax stuck in the wizard’s shoulder, called someone’s name.
Shoop!
“Hans Chrisen!”
We all grew tense as our eyes converged on Hans. However, Hans G remained silent and trembling.
“Do you want your secret exposed!?” the dwarf shouted again, accusingly.
It felt like my head was vibrating. The secret Hans G was hiding could only be one thing.
The dwarf pressed on. “Fine, if that’s what you want, I’ll expose you myself. Hans Chrisen is an evil spirit! I have proof of that in my backpack—”
“You guys! Get away from him!” I immediately issued a warning. If the dwarf had definitive evidence, Hans G’s betrayal was inevitable.
“E-Evil spirit? You think I’ll believe—”
I was a second too late.
Whooosh!
Hans G’s lizard summons unleashed a fierce jet of fire at the blunt-weapon user.
“W... hy...” He collapsed to the ground, covered in flames.
“I-I’m sorry.” Hans G winced, walked to the dwarf’s side, and then turned and said something I couldn’t understand. “W-What are you doing? M-Miss Meirin, come here, quick!”
“...W-What are you talking about?! You want me to walk over there after you’ve done such a terrible thing?!”
“Y-You’re not thinking of abandoning me, are you? W-We’re from the same place. W-We have to go everywhere together! I-I’ve handled all the dangerous parts for us!”
This was a very sudden turn of events. “Ha, you awful bastard!” As soon as I saw the way the elven archer’s expression crumpled, I easily pieced the situation together in my head.
I can’t believe they’re both players.
Considering even the dwarf looked surprised, it seemed he hadn’t known that. He had probably just discovered some evidence during night watch and threatened Hans G with it, and that was it.

When Hans G screwed her over, leaving her with no options, the elven archer stomped over to the dwarf’s side. “Dwarf!” she shouted in irritation. “You’d better keep your promise and take me to Noark!”
“...Of course! Come on, help me!”
This is a proper mess now.

A headache crept in. We’d clearly had the upper hand in numbers up to this point. But now, we were on the side with one less person. Team Hans G’s scout had passed out from the shock, but even if they woke up, their combat ability was zero. Besides, overcoming adversity and defeating them wouldn’t solve all of our problems. A bleak future would await us after that when the five of us were forced to fight the boss battle alone.
Fuck, and there’s a doppelganger among us.
We had a long and winding road ahead, to say the least. Various curses came to mind far too naturally.
Even considering the Hans effect, isn’t this a bit much?
The complaints also popped into my head involuntarily but... Well, what can you do?
“Behelaaah!”
We had no choice but to try. There was no need for a lengthy exchange. The time for conversation was long gone.
Boom!
The moment I activated Giantization and ran forward, a gray vortex swirled into existence and surrounded me.
Shaaa!
This was one of the sorcerer’s many attack skills. As the damage it dealt wasn’t physical, even I couldn’t white-knuckle my way through this without injuries. But we were a team too.
“Teirun Sheardiem.”

A veil of mana covered my skin, a spell referred to conveniently as Mana Shield in the game. This was why wizards were important in Player vs Player battles. They may have been inefficient with their mana and thus wasteful while hunting, but that wasn’t the case when fighting against people. Mana consumption would be high on both sides.
Whooom.
When my vision cleared, the dwarf was in front of me.
Boom.

He jumped high with his short legs and slammed his shield into my face. The damage itself wasn’t significant, but my Giantized body was helplessly pushed back thanks to his skill, Polar Shield. It gave the user a knockback bonus for pushes and reduced impact for blocks.
Drip.
Immediately after I was pushed back, leaving behind long footprints in the ground, the beast warrior came out stabbing. The most likely target was my delicate eye.
“Oh no you don’t!” Missha, who was hidden behind me, jumped out and parried the beast swordsman.
Okay, then I’ll leave him to Missha.
Whiiip!
Blocking the arrows flying in from the front with my shield, I brought my mace down on the dwarf’s head as he landed on the ground. But what was this?
Klang!

I had activated Swing for this blow. Even if he was protecting his head with a shield, the shield should have been crushed entirely. That was what had happened with his doppelganger too. So why was his shield intact?
Goddamn it.
I quickly identified the cause. His earrings emitted the same light as the shield.
Of course—it was only natural that the attack had worked differently on the doppelganger. A numbered item could not be copied. With a premium item like that, the difference was like night and day.
Bang!

Just then, a blast occurred at the rear of the dwarf’s camp thanks to an explosive arrow from Mr. Bear. Hans G summoned an Earthberg right on time, avoiding any casualties, but as their defenses began to crumble, Raven’s magical onslaught continued.
Dddddd! Kablam!

A lightning bolt split into dozens of smaller lightning bolts which all proceeded to fall to the earth. One of them struck Hans G and knocked him off his feet. But not for long, of course, because there was a priest over there.
Whooosh!

In just a few seconds, Hans G regained consciousness and used his summoned beast to fire a jet of flame. The target was our back line. Raven had just used a spell and I wasn’t at an angle where I could stop the attack either, so Mr. Bear’s summoned beast, Bear, just absorbed the blow with his body.
“Woom!” Bear howled like this was no big deal to him. Soul Beasts had high Mana Resistance stats.
Whew, at this level, team battle is on a different scale.
Afterward, the priest of Karui finished his preparations and began calling forth summons in earnest.
“Grrrrrr...” An army of undead began pouring out of an ominous-colored portal that appeared in mid-air. Coincidentally, we had the perfect person to handle this.
“Behelaaah!” Without needing any orders from me, Ainar rushed forward wielding her greatsword.
Bang! KABLAM! Bang!

Each time she used Repeated Slash, explosions followed and sparks flew. Plus, if she was injured, she healed herself with Wings of Greed. Of course, using skills without restraint like this would usually leave her with no MP, but...
[Ainar Fenelin has killed an opponent. Satiation has activated and Soul Power is restored.]
The Slayer Imprint Ainar had gotten specialized in massacres, you see.
Bang! Ddddddd! Whooom!

Attacks were hurled from all directions, causing a cacophony of sounds. Each person wasn’t just facing one specific opponent. We at times had to step back to help out our teammates. Thus, a fierce battle where the winner was indiscernible raged on.
“You know something?” I took another knockback blow to the face from the dwarf as he spoke to me for the first time this entire battle.
I wanted to just ignore him, but I replied anyway. “That you’re going to die soon?”
“No. You are the core of your team.”

Wasn’t that obvious? With each chance I got, I ran from side to side, destroying formations and inflicting damage on the enemy while shielding against all arrows and spells that crossed my path. The dwarf, on the other hand, just followed me around as I did that to keep me from going too wild.
“In other words, if you and I disappear at the same time, we’ll have the advantage.”
“...What?”
The dwarf grinned and shouted, “Jainen! Now!” Jainen was the priest of Karui’s name. The dwarf always shouted out loud to give orders as their team had no one to cast a voice control spell for them.
[You have entered the special terrain Crossroads of Fate.]
My surroundings, which had just been full of firework-like flashes, grew dark. In addition, the sound of fierce combat vanished as everything grew quiet. That made me laugh.
I was wondering what you were going to do. Did you use Crossroads of Fate? You dwarven bastard, do I look that easy to you?

Crossroads of Fate, a unique ability only a priest of Karui could use, was simple. It sent two designated targets to a separate dimension. For reference, this skill could only be activated when the designated individuals were enemies, and only when one person was victorious or the power was cut off from the outside could they return.
Click.

A switch clicked and the space around me lit up. I was standing on top of a stone statue the size of a building dozens of stories tall. Well, to be more precise, I was in the statue’s palm. When I looked up, I could see the statue’s face looking down in my direction—the face of the evil god, Karui, which I had only ever seen in books.
“You’re not surprised,” the dwarf muttered about ten yards away from me, his tone sedate.
I couldn’t stand it, so I had to ask. “What kind of confidence did you have to bring me here?”
“...Do you know about this place?”
Of course I did. This was a sort of dueling ground, a location cut off from the outside world where you had to fight using only your individual skill. And he brought me here?
“How ridiculous.”
Spotting the look on my face, the dwarf frowned. “You think too highly of yourself, barbarian.”
So, you genuinely assumed that surviving against me was doable. That if you kept me tied up here, the team you have outside would eventually be victorious and let you back out.
Smirk.
I thought about saying something but doing so would be a waste of time. I couldn’t find any reason to, either. I could just show him with my actions like any other barbarian.
“Behelaaah!” No need for questions and answers. Ending the chitchat there, I charged at my opponent.
Dash!

The dwarf stepped back, suggesting he had made up his mind to hang out here. It was a pointless endeavor, though. How fast could he possibly run with those short legs? Even he seemed to realize that that wasn’t an option and picked up his shield.
Voom.
He swung the shield with the intention of pushing me away, but the only reason I let that move hit me earlier was because his teammates kept distracting me.
Whip.
Twisting my body slightly to avoid him, I slammed down my mace.
Clang!
A clear ringing sounded as it met the shield the dwarf had raised above his head. Of course, that was no problem.
Clang!
If once wasn’t enough, then twice.
Clang!
If not twice, three times.
Clang!
Wow, this was like playing whack-a-mole or something. No matter how many times I slammed my mace down, the dwarf’s shield remained sturdy.
“I told you... I can hold out.”
Your breath is getting choppy, though. Anyway, I guess this is where you placed your bets. How unfortunate. I never thought you’d actually get baited by the feint.
Clang!
After I slammed the mace down thirteen more times, I faked like I was going to do it again and swiftly reached my hand out.
Voom!
I pulled on his earring. There was no way a numbered item could be damaged by a force like this, but flesh didn’t count.
Riiip.
The fragile earlobe tore and the earring came off.
No. 2988: Mark of the Guard Corps.
It didn’t come with special stats or effects, but wearing it increased the shock absorption of a shield by a whopping 50 percent. I never thought I’d get this critical item here.
“...Give it back!” The dwarf reacted a beat later and rushed at me like a madman. Of course, all I could do was offer him a big, strong macing.
Bam!
An exciting clanging rang out from the shield that was reflexively protecting his head. Whew, that was more like it. I could feel my sinuses clear up, like a breath of fresh air.
On that note, let’s do one more.
Bam!
The dwarf staggered considerably, holding the half-crumpled shield.
Crunch!

Taking advantage of his lowered guard, I brought the mace down on the crown of his head. The dwarf dropped like a fly, marking the end of our fight. However, seeing as this pocket dimension hadn’t disappeared yet, it wasn’t an instant fatality.
Did he pass out?
Whatever the case, he had one hell of a sturdy body.
Anyway, that’s good.

I dug through the dwarf’s bag and pulled out an item. It was none other than the test tube containing the Manticore’s essence. Looking at this, I was suddenly reminded of the line this guy said during the dice roll earlier.
“Luck is on my side.”

That was a line a guy like me could never say. It was a bit ironic, though—the guy who had said that line was now doomed to die soon, while I was in the opposite position. Perhaps luck foreshadowed incoming misery.
“To think the test tube remained intact in the expandable bag.” I smirked. “Luck is on my side.”
This much luck should be fine. Everything else, I’d worked hard to achieve myself. I chugged the essence into the test tube.
[The Essence of the Manticore is being absorbed into your soul.]
Dddddd!
Right at that moment, I felt vibrations run through the entire space. No wonder—he hadn’t died yet. But he was finally dead.
The corpse will return to its original place, so I can clean that up later...
When I closed my eyes and reopened them, I saw a familiar forest. I quickly scanned my surroundings. Not even five minutes had passed since I was whisked away.
Kwaaang! Craccck! Pop!

The battle was still raging. However, it seemed a retreat had taken place since my disappearance because the battlefield had moved slightly to a location about seventy yards away from where I stood. I could tell with a single glance that I needed to join my struggling teammates as fast as possible.
Hmm, this distance looks just right.
Thus, I activated my newly acquired ability, the active skill found in the yellow Manticore essence.
Leap.
Feeling my body grow lighter, I jumped up in one vigorous bound.
[Your Jump Power stat increases by x10 for one jump and you inflict a powerful shockwave on the surrounding area upon landing.]
My body flew in a steep parabola and aimed for the middle of Team Dwarf’s formation.
CRASH!
I finally got myself a transportation ability.

chapters.title: Chapter 186: Overgeared (1)
paragraphs: The dwarf had said that without me, his side would have a much greater advantage. I was now seeing with my own two eyes that he wasn’t just talking big.
Pababababat!
My body shot up like a cannon ball despite the drag. Looking down from above, I could see the entire battlefield at once.
“We just have to hold out until Mr. Yandel gets back!”

No one was seriously injured or dead, but my teammates were struggling. With the party’s wall (me) missing, the burden on my teammates had multiplied by several times. While Bear’s summoning period had ended, the undead summoned by the priest of Karui stampeded at them from all directions.
“Huh?” It was then that Missha met my eye. “Uh, huh?”

“Miss Karlstein! What are you looking a—huh?” So did Raven. I was quite a distance away, but judging by her gaping mouth, she seemed to be thinking something along the lines of, Why is a barbarian flying?
To make one thing clear, I was not flying. “Falling down” would be the correct phrase. Or as I liked to call it, Barbarian Meteor Mode.
CRASH!
I tensed my back and found my balance before landing on both feet. Footprints more accurately described as craters were engraved deep into the ground.
Sting.
A sensation akin to electricity buzzed through my legs. Jeez, if I hadn’t adjusted my Bone Strength stat, I might’ve just shattered my bones. With that thought in mind, I scanned my surroundings.
Whooom!
Dust billowed out from the point of impact in the form of rings. This was the side effect of a transportation skill.
[Your Jump Power stat increases by x10 for one jump and you inflict a powerful shockwave on the surrounding area upon landing.]

Damage had been dealt to the terrain around me. Of course, the amount of damage was negligible. I didn’t classify it as a transportation skill for nothing. Except for the small area that I had crushed down with my body, it was safe to say there was no wide-range damage.
Shaaaaaa!
The undead army fell over from the wind pressure. Team Dwarf, meanwhile, was just taken aback by my sudden intrusion; they remained standing despite the strong winds.
[Your total weight is over 1100 lbs. Special terrain effect Recoil is applied to your total damage.]
Wait, sorry, I was in Giantization mode.
Boom!
Just like thunder comes after a lightning strike, as soon as the wind dissipated, the ground shook and flung everything standing on top of it.
“Kyaa!”
“What...!”
Hundreds of undead flew into the air along with Team Dwarf. My mouth curled into a wide grin at that overwhelming high.
Thankfully, it looks like it was enough weight.

I’d been a bit worried. With Union, Giantization applied to my equipment, too, but I still had a lot of pieces of equipment to get fitted for. But even without this weight bonus, the Leap skill had another big advantage.
[Your Threat Level has temporarily increased significantly.]

A Threat Level bonus was bestowed on the user for a short period after landing. This was important to me because it meant that aside from Giantization, I now had another skill that could increase my Threat Level.
“I-If that guy is here...”
“The dwarf! Is that bastard... dead?!”
“You said you could handle him!”
As the remaining members of Team Dwarf already lost their fighting spirit just from seeing me, I shouted, “Behelaaah!” That was the activation code for Wild Outburst, after all.
[Your Threat Level has temporarily increased by x3, and your physical stats increase in proportion to that value.]
With a Physique bonus proportional to Threat Level, yeah, this was it. I felt like I’d really become an ogre.
“Grk!” Summoned beasts flocked to me like madmen. On the other hand, the intellectuals were different.
“R-Retreat! Everyone, retreat!”
“R-Run!”
As if they had fallen into a state of Fear, they abandoned formation and ran away. Or was this just a result of common sense rather than Threat Level?
Slam! Slam! Whoom! Smack!
With a giant mace and shield and two legs as dangerous as living weapons, I crushed and flung summoned beasts and pursued Team Dwarf.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The sound of a large monster’s footsteps that seemed to accompany my run was a bonus.
“Block him! Block! You’re the warrior!”

“Shit, how am I supp—” The elven archer stabbed a dagger into the beast swordsman’s thigh. “Ahh! You deranged bitch!” The swordsman tumbled through the dirt from the inertia. And then he was in my hand. “Uh, huh...?” My grip was roomy, even while holding a human head between my fingers. “...S-Surrender. I surrender—”
Slowly, I applied force. Was it because of Wild Outburst? I was sure this guy had Physical Resistance, but his head felt softer than a watermelon.
Crunch!
Moving on.

Before long, Wild Outburst ended and my fired-up vigor also disappeared, but the chase was no problem. We hadn’t even finished the third stage, after all, so there was a barrier with a radius of about five hundred yards surrounding us. Plus, I now had a transportation skill.
Kwaaang!

Using Leap, I blocked their path. Team Dwarf dropped their weapons without hesitation and surrendered. I supposed they decided it was better to submit themselves to my mercy. Well, there was a sort of logic to it.
“P-Please don’t kill us. We’ll do anything. Y-You’ll need us t-to take down the guardian. Right?”
I’d have to think about this one. First, with the help of my teammates who were following behind me, we disarmed the group. Now was a good time to turn off Giantization.

“Bjorn! What the hell was that!? Me too! I want to do that too!” I wondered if it was a barbarian instinct. After seeing Leap in action, Ainar’s eyes exhibited a powerful hunger. Even the way she looked at cotton candy couldn’t compare.
I didn’t hide my amusement and made her a promise. “Haha, I’ll find you something similar next time.”
“Really!? Remember, you promised!”

“Yes, it’s a promise.” The cultivation tree I’d drawn up for Ainar had something similar to Leap on it. Though it was a rank-three essence, so it’d take some years to get it... but a barbarian really should be able to jump this high.
“E-Excuse me! P-Please help!”
Hm? The call came as we were taking the equipment off Team Dwarf. When I turned my head, I saw a woman.
Right, I forgot she was alive.
Team Hans G’s rookie scout’s name was... I couldn’t be bothered to ask, so let’s go with Scout Lady.
“Potion! Please lend us a potion. I gave him one of mine but...” When I turned to where Scout Lady was pointing, I could see the blunt-weapon warrior on the ground.
“Is he alive?”
“Y-Yes!” Apparently seeing a glimmer of hope, she nodded enthusiastically.
I pondered this for a moment. Saving him was the logical thing to do, but a potion might be a waste. Before long, I grabbed the priest of Karui.
“E-Eek!”
Don’t be a chicken. Who said I’m killing you?
I dragged the priest with me and dropped him in front of the blunt weapon user. “Treat him.”
“Y-Yes!” Although they worshipped an evil god, priests of Karui seemed to be capable of divine magic too. Blending in would be impossible otherwise.
Shaaaaaa.
As divine power filled his body, the burns on the blunt-weapon warrior slowly disappeared. His breathing quickly became much more stable.
“Thank you. Thank you. Really...”
“But what happened to the wizard?”
“H-He passed away.”
“Are you sure?”
“Yes. W-When I checked, his heart was already...”
“I see. We’ll take care of the other side, so stay with this guy until he wakes up. He’ll be very confused.”
“Y-Yes! Thank you...!”
When I returned to where my teammates were, they had finished taking Team Dwarf captive. They were pretty much down to their underwear.
“...Where did you get the mouth gag?” I asked Raven.
“It’s from my own possessions.”
What? A gag? Why?
When I asked the reason out of pure curiosity, I received an unexpected answer. “I’m interested in this area of study as well.”
“Uh... I-I see?” I was genuinely perplexed. However, a reaction like that could hurt Raven’s feelings. “Yes. That’s not... n-not bad?” I expressed my opinion to avoid any misunderstandings.
But, huh? “Not bad? Mr. Yandel, are you also interested in Monsterology?”
“Monsterology?” When I asked this in confusion, Raven also tilted her head. Suddenly, a thought came to mind. “Is the gag... for monsters?”

“Yes, why? If I got the chance, I had a mind to catch one alive and study it. Wait, then what did you think I used these for...?” Raven trailed off, then her face quickly flushed red. “...Don’t come near me any longer.”
