“How close can I get?”
“One yard.”
“...All right.” We half-jokingly agreed on a distance and I approached our group of captives. Then I loosened Hans G’s gag. There was something I was curious about. “I wanted to ask you something.”
“Pardon? Ah, yes! A-Anything!”
“How did the dwarf figure out you’re an evil spirit?”

“...Pardon?” Hans G looked at me like he found the question strange. But to avoid getting on my bad side, he answered meekly. The truth was truly unexpected. “H-He is also a p-player... No, an e-evil spirit.”
The dwarf was from Earth. That was why he had been able to deduce Hans G’s identity just by his actions. “Tell me exactly what happened between you two.”

I listened to the details. Minus his constant stuttering, it wasn’t a long story. The dwarf had instigated a conversation with Hans G through a magical device during night watch and revealed something no one from this world could know. Hans G happily participated in the exchange, but it was a trap. What the dwarf had used was a magical device that recorded conversations. Threatened with his weakness, Hans G received an offer to take the guardian down with the dwarf and make good money. As a side note, the stick came with a carrot. Apparently, the dwarf offered to share the loot equally and if things went wrong, he would take responsibility and take Hans G to Noark.
“I-I r-refused. B-But—m-mm!” A lame excuse was going to follow, so I ended the conversation and put the gag back in his mouth. All my questions had been answered, anyway.
How the hell are four out of the fifteen of us players?

The elven archer, Hans G, the dwarf, and me... It was ridiculous, but in the end, I was the winner. However, the final battle remained. With that in mind, I moved on to a new item on the agenda after establishing a team voice link.
“I want to hear your opinions.”
“About what to do with these people?”
“Yes.”
I didn’t mean a majority vote. If I made the decision, my teammates would follow it, but I wanted to hear their opinions before that.
“They attacked us! Of course they should die!” said Ainar.
“Hmm, I don’t know. If we can clear the Rrrift on our own, we should obviously kill them, but...”
“Will these people really cooperate with us?” said Raven.
Their opinions were mostly similar. It was hard to trust them.
“They say that an unreliable ally is more dangerous than an Ogre.”
Even if we fought together, if we could not fight properly out of fear of betrayal, it would completely upend our plans.
“Still, the Noark team is better,” claimed Raven.
“What about them is better?”

“Once we leave the Rift, we’ll never see them again. If we agree to save their lives, there’s a chance they’ll put their faith in that.” Raven turned her gaze to the elven archer and Hans G. “But those two are different.” An evil spirit was a creature that felt even more sinister and threatening than an underground adventurer.
“Right! The chieftain said so too! Evil spirits must be killed as soon as they are found!” said Ainar.
“Yeah... I didn’t know this before but after today, I know it for sure. Why everrryone says not to trust evil spirits...”

“They will do anything to keep their identities hidden. It’s wise to get rid of them as soon as the opportunity presents itself. That man is a testament to what happens if you trust an evil spirit,” Mr. Bear said.
Each word was like a knife to my chest. How would they react if my identity were uncovered? Would they look at me with the same look in their eyes?
“So what do you think, Mr. Yandel?”
I brushed off those meaningless thoughts and gave them my decision. “I think it’s better to kill them now.”
I had no intention of letting them live in the first place. It was just a question of whether to kill them now or after we killed the guardian. I was already perfectly acclimated to this world.
“Can we kill the guardian by ourselves?” Raven asked.
“We’ll have to try.”

It may have sounded irresponsible, but it wasn’t a totally unreasonable decision. The blunt-weapon warrior, at least, had survived. Our manpower had increased to six people. Also, in addition to the Guard Corps Token, there could be more items we might be able to use right away. Above all, if my predictions were correct, we would have one more wizard.
“Then we just have to find the doppelganger.”

“Yes. The Stone of Truth won’t show up for a long while and since we decided not to cooperate, I think we can just kill them all. If we offer them to the altar, they’ll just end up being released later.”
“Turn off Voice Control.”

After asking Raven to turn off the team communication spell, I approached the group of prisoners. The silence seemed cold yet strangely warm. Eyes full of hope mingling with anxiety focused on me. Well, I was sure they were aware that the meeting was over and a decision had been made. No lengthy explanations were necessary.
“It won’t hurt.”
Probably.

“Mm—mmp! Mmm!” As soon as I opened my mouth, the prisoners wriggled and tried to say something, like flickering candle flames struggling to stay alight. I swung the mace without hesitation, starting with the priest of Karui at the end.
Crunch!
Then the sorcerer.
Crunch!
Hans G.
Crunch!
And even the elven archer. I struck hard enough to kill them instantly, even if the doppelganger dwelled inside of them.
Crunch.

The entire process took only about five seconds. Their violent wriggling stopped as if it had never happened in the first place. Four bodies with crushed heads fell to the ground. At the sight, just one thought filled my mind.
Good thing they were gagged.
“Mr. Yandel! You can’t just hit them like that!” Raven exclaimed.
Hm?
“Even if they’re for monster use, you could break the gags like that!”
Ah... Is that important right now, though?
“You’re rather calm.”
“Pardon? What do you—”
“You’re the only doppelganger candidate left.”

There had been nine people on whom verification magic did not work. Among them, Raven and I were the last ones standing. And since I had used the Stone of Truth, I had been eliminated as a possibility.
She belatedly realized what was going on. “Ah...!” Raven’s eyes went wide and she shouted, “It’s not me! Why would I be a doppelganger? No, it can’t be... There must be a mistake...”
So, that’s how you’re going to play this.
“Raven is the doppelganger. Everyone get back!”
At my cry, the trio next to Raven jumped back in surprise.
“Y-You’rrre the doppelganger? I never dreamed of it.”
“Give back Aruru! She may be human and a wizard, but she’s my precious teammate!”
The melee sisters couldn’t hide their astonishment.
“I-It’s really not me. Please believe me. I’ll confirm it with the Stone of Truth as soon as it appears tomorrow! Okay?”
“Even now, after everything is over, you’re still trying to take the Stone of Truth... you really are a clever monster.” Mr. Bear quietly raised his crossbow and stood alert.
Raven looked like she was going to cry at any moment. “I-I’m not...” So she could make an expression like that too, huh? “I-It’s really not me!”
Come to think of it, hearing her scream this loud was a first, too.
This... is rare.

Since this wasn’t something we got a chance to see often, I was tempted, but any more of this and she might really cry. So enough joking around. “The only one left is you. But if not you, who the hell is it?”
“Th-that’s...!”

“Didn’t you tell us that if the host is killed, even without being offered up on the altar, the doppelganger will be released?” Pretending to drive her into a corner, I dropped a hint, judging that our wizard would be able to use this to come up with an explanation.
“M-Maybe someone is still alive! Pretending to be dead is a doppelganger’s specialty!”
That was the line I’d been waiting for. “Still alive, huh?”
When I started moving, Raven let out a bewildered shout. “W-Where are you going?”
Step.
Soon, I paused where Parteian, the unfortunate wizard whose shoulder had been destroyed by the dwarf, lay on the ground. First, I bent over and tried to find a pulse.
“...I-is he alive?”
“Hush.”
His heart wasn’t beating. His breathing had also stopped.
Tap, tap.
I got up and kicked the wound with my foot. He didn’t even flinch. Hmm, was this bearable, then? I took out a bottle of potion and poured it on him.
Chhhhhh.
The wound boiled and began to heal.
“Keeeeeek!”
Yeah, even you can’t stand a potion.

chapters.title: Chapter 187: Overgeared (2)
paragraphs: In this stage, Shadow Altar, the doppelganger pursued just two objectives: to make the expedition waste the Stone of Truth, and if that didn’t work, to create disorder in order to reduce the size of the expedition. In that sense, there was one prime suspect.
“What city are you from?”

Kyleman Parteian, the wizard from Hans G’s team who had successfully cut the expedition in half. At first, I thought he’d stepped on the landmine by accident. It had seemed to me that the wizard’s team, including Hans G, was not aware that Team Dwarf was from Noark.
“Dwarf, are you a doppelganger?”

I had attacked Team Dwarf relentlessly about where they had obtained the equipment in their backpacks, what exactly the civil servant said to them as they handed them their identification tags, etcetera. I asked countless questions the dwarf couldn’t answer in order to make him seem suspicious. However, at the time, there was one thing I had overlooked. How did the dwarf, stumped by such an easy question, look to the doppelganger?
It must have seemed strange. And after that, the doppelganger would have questioned why.

The doppelganger was inside the body of an intelligent wizard. It would have pieced together the Noark thing through the questions the dwarf couldn’t answer. Maybe it got greedy too. Not only did its host happen to have a perfect item for the situation, but if used properly, it would become even easier for it to hide its identity.
“H-He passed away.”

Doppelganger bastards knew how to play dead. That was how they had beaten me many times in the game. If you didn’t make sure their deaths were clean and instant, these sons of bitches went into hibernation and stayed alive to trick players, just like this.
“Keeeeeek!”

As soon as the potion was poured on it, the doppelganger flailed violently. If I hadn’t been right about this, our only option would have been to use the Stone of Truth on Raven even after already beating the other candidates to death.
“It’s a doppelganger!” With her name finally cleared, Raven let out a more joyful shout than ever.
The doppelganger denied it even as it screeched. “N-no! Hey! I! am! Kiyeek!”
How much could you possibly look down on someone? It was absurd, but arguing with a monster was just as ridiculous. I just grabbed him by the hair and walked to the altar.
As the altar got closer and closer, the doppelganger’s struggle intensified. “How—?!” Finally, he gave in, making excuses and blurting out apologies.
I chuckled. Actually, the real reason I had figured it out was something else.
Why don’t you practice your acting?

A wizard’s greatest weakness was close combat, but this bastard had managed to avoid the dwarf’s ax as it swung straight for his head and took the blow with his shoulder instead. Unless he had anticipated a surprise attack, that wouldn’t have been possible. The idea that he would have died instantly from something like that was just as ridiculous. Maybe I could have bought him bleeding out, but how could he have stopped breathing before Scout Lady could even feed him a potion?
[You have successfully discovered the doppelganger dwelling in the body of an expedition member.]
As soon as I shoved the doppelganger’s head onto the altar, it began to glow with a pure white light. At the same time, the forest vibrated like there was an earthquake.
“Keeeeeek!”
A shadow-like creature was pushed out of the wizard’s head and shot through the trees, releasing a terrifying scream.
“Oh! It’s getting away!”
It disappeared in a certain direction. There was no need to worry, though. That meant that the third stage was over.
[Only one Stone of Truth has been used. Seal Unlock Percentage: 10%]
[Please track down and kill the Doppelganger before they regain their power.]
Now, it was time to fight the final boss.
“Bjorn, let’s follow him!”
“Stop. We have to do something before that.” I calmed Ainar, then checked how Parteian was doing. Well, Raven did. Not me. “How is he?”
“His injury is almost healed, so he should wake up soon.”
“I see.”
As soon as I called for her, Raven inspected Parteian. After that, she finally slumped. It looked like her sanity had returned and her legs grew weak. “Whew...”
The melee sisters and Mr. Bear approached with bashful looks on their faces and offered a few words.
“Wow, so that guy was the doppelgangerrr...”
“I told you. It wasn’t me!”
“Ahem, still, you’re not a wizard for nothing. Who would have thought someone might still be alive in a state like that?”
“Ha... what were you going to do if it really was me?”
“Aruru! You know me, right? I believed in you!”
“Yeah right... and what the heck is an Aruru?”
“What?! Could it be that you don’t like Aruru?” Ainar seemed really hurt by that.
Of course, that wasn’t going to work on Raven. “Then would you like me to do the same to you? Arua Raven! Please call me properly either by my first or last name. I hate this kind of—”
“I-I wanted to call you by your first name, but it is difficult to pronounce...”
When Ainar dropped her head, Raven finally clammed up. “You want to call me by name?” she asked hesitantly. “What do you mean?”
“You’re a human wizard, but you’re also a precious teammate of mine.” Ainar uttered those sickly sweet words without so much as flinching.
“Ha, that weird pronunciation...” Raven sighed incredulously but whipped her head away from Ainar. “It’s fine. Call me whatever.”
“Really!?”
“Yes. They call me by something similar at the school anyway, so I shouldn’t really be getting mad at you.”
“Thanks, Aruru!” We were treated to the heart-warming sight of friendship between teammates strengthening after overcoming adversity. As I watched, I had the following thought:
This kid, although she doesn’t look like it, is weak to these things. I should use this next time I make a mistake.
After making that mental note, I ended the conversation and started organizing our equipment. There was a mountain of things to do before the boss fight.
“Both of you, stop doing that and come here.” First, I called over the scout woman and the recovered blunt-weapon warrior. “I assume you heard about the situation?”
“...We did.” It seemed the fact that Hans G and the elven archer had been evil spirits was quite a shock to them, as their eyes were still blank.
“Snap out of it. You can deal with all that after you get out of here.”
“What can we do?”
“Tell me what you can do.”

I checked the blunt-weapon fighter’s combat power—what essences he had, what forms of combat he was capable of, etcetera. Normally this was information you would never tell an outsider, but as things had reached this point, he cooperated with me very submissively.
“Okay, then what about you?”
“E-Except for finding the way, I won’t be any help in battle. I’m sorry.”
We had one rank-six fighter and one unranked guide.
“Still, Parteian will be of great help to you. He’s a rank-five wizard.”
“What? Rank five?”
“That’s right. Although he specializes in other fields than attack magic. He was the one who played the most roles on our team. You should hear the details for yourself when he wakes up.”
I was genuinely surprised because Raven was still a rank-six wizard. How the hell did Hans convince such a prime talent to work with him?
Then that means we have to beat the guardian with a total of seven people, including a rank-five wizard...
I still couldn’t get a proper idea of how the battle would go. I didn’t have enough paint to draw the picture I wanted. So, while Parteian recovered, I dug through Team Dwarf’s spoils.
“Check every single thing. If anything stands out, get Raven to inspect it. Anything that can be used must be used.”

I looked at the things belonging to Hans G, the elven archer, the beast swordsman, the dwarf, the sorcerer, and the priest of Karui. The archer we had offered to the altar had been transformed into a spirit, and we’d only be able to look through his belongings after the Rift was cleared, so pass.
“Arururng! How about this?”
“I sense mana here. But I don’t see any magic formulas so it can’t be a regular magic item... It is highly likely that it’s a Numbers Item.”
“Oooh! These shoes! They fit me perfectly!”
“These boots are made from half-troll leather. They also have Acceleration magic on them. These are expensive, so wear them with care. We’ll have to add it to the settlement later.”
As they had all been seasoned adventurers, each person’s bag revealed useful items. It was like opening a treasure chest.
“Raven, can you check this too? I know it’s made of lithinum, but why is it made into a necklace?”

“It’s for mana conductivity. You could cast the same spell twice and the efficiency will be different. So, let’s see, this necklace...” Apparently hitting her stride, Raven determined the values of all sorts of items with lightning speed.
Even still, this process took more time than expected and soon, Parteian woke up. “Uh... Umm...”

Taking in the sight of the forest littered with the bodies of his teammates and various pieces of equipment, the middle-aged wizard fell into a state of confusion. I sent the blunt-weapon warrior to explain to me.

“Y-You mean the doppelganger was in my body...? Noark... Yes, no wonder their bags were full of unused equipment. It makes sense if they are from there... Chrisen and Meirin were evil spirits...?” As the explanation continued, the wizard’s complexion paled. But even in this situation, he came up to me and offered words of thanks. Maybe that was just a wizard’s nature. “Thank you. If it weren’t for you, something truly terrible would have happened.”
“If you’re grateful, go and help Raven. This is not the time to relax.”
“I will.” After Parteian joined in, the pace of the sorting accelerated. Surprisingly, he was also an expert in this kind of thing.
“...Appraisal magic? Are you from the Narman School?”
“Come to think of it, we haven’t even introduced ourselves. That’s right.”
“I’m Arua Raven from the Altemion School.”
“Haha, I’m aware. There’s only one school with such an impressive symbol on their robes.”
“Our Master can go a bit overboard...”

When Parteian, a wizard from the School of Narman who was capable of special appraisal, joined in, it was possible to classify numbered items, of course, and also items that we couldn’t clearly identify earlier. We passed a long while like that.
“It looks like we got all the useful stuff. Let’s stop and gather around.”
After finishing the sorting work, we got together and established a temporary pact.
“I’ll tell you this in advance, but everything you guys take now will be written down and paid for properly later. If you want to keep using it, you’ll have to pay for it then. Understood?”
“Okay!”

“Then Ainar, come here.” I looked at the list we’d created and transferred the items we’d obtained to each person. My criteria was but one thing: who the item would be best suited for. “Give your shoes to Missha.”
“N-No way! They won’t fit her feet anyway!”

“Don’t worry. I made sure that it came with an adjustment spell.” My dogmatic ruling didn’t pass without complaints, but things like these were what I should use my authority as a leader for. “Ainar.”
“Okay. I’ll give them to her...”

Starting with Ainar, the rest of my teammates took usable equipment, as few as one piece and as many as five per person. Jeez, how much money could we get for all of this? Once you fought another adventurer, you understood from the bottom part of your heart why it was that everyone plundered so much.
“That’s it, then.” The remaining loot was divided and stored in Raven’s and my sub-spaces. It wasn’t just for safety reasons—there was just too much.
Grin.
Looking at my new equipment, I couldn’t help the smile that kept creeping up on my face. Indeed, this was the flipside of Hans’s Law.
[You have equipped No. 2988: Guard Corps Token. Your total Item Level has increased by +1485.]
[You have equipped No. 8667: Outlaw of the Wilderness. Your total Item Level has increased by +315.]
[You have equipped Idium Gaiters. Your total Item Level has increased by +400.]
Doppelganger bastard, you’re dead.
[Bjorn Yandel]
[Level: 5
Physique: 555 (New +5)
Spirit: 198 (New +15)
Special Ability: 191
Item Level: 3068 (New +2200)
General Combat Power: 1731 (New +570)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Orc Hero - Rank 5  Ogre - Rank 3 / Manticore - Rank 5 (New)]

chapters.title: Chapter 188: Overgeared (3)
paragraphs: I was walking through a dark forest in the direction where the doppelganger had disappeared from the Shadow Altar, the path ahead seemingly endless. Every step I took seemed weight down by the tension in the air. As for our formation, I was at the very front and the rest were following a few yards behind. It was far from our usual setup, but... Well, what could you do? Such was the life of a tank who carried the team.
“Prepare for battle!”

The moment I sensed a presence ahead of us, dozens of doppelgangers untouched by the glow of the light sphere spell revealed themselves. This was the change that occurred at the start of the fourth stage. After the Doppelganger’s seal was removed, the number of clones on the field increased exponentially.
“Enemy... enemy of the Empire...!”
“...Kill, them!”

They no longer transformed into us, and it would stay that way until we found the main body. I didn’t know why. This was a part I had overlooked in the game. I was sure I could find some hidden explanation for this phenomenon if I looked, but now was not the time to think about stuff like that.
[You have cast Leap.]
Before the distance between us could narrow any further, I threw myself forward and landed in the middle of them.
Kwaaang!
As I landed, the ground beneath me shook and the special terrain effect Recoil activated. Dozens of doppelgangers were flung through the air at once.
Crunch!
I swung my mace like a baseball bat to strike one out and promptly cast Wild Outburst.
“Behelahhh!”
My Threat Level tripled. Doppelgangers in the forms of soldiers rushed at me like crazed beasts. As long as they were monsters, they couldn’t ignore my provocation. “For... the Empire...!”

Doppelgangers had no skills but were tricky enemies nonetheless because their default stats were high. As indicated by the way the shield soldier withstood my macing, each of their stats was at least above Ainar’s. Plus, the fact that our formation was made up of a variety of arrow, spear, sword, magic, crossbow, and shield fighters played a part in raising the difficulty of the battle.
Crunch! Crunch!

However, although I blocked what needed to be blocked, I never avoided an attack. There was no point in the first place. Enemies were all around us. All I could do was get beat up like the tank I was and await my teammates’ support.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-five attack spell Lightning Bolt.]
Soon, the long-awaited spell was completed. The lightning struck a wide range.
[Kailman Parteian has cast the rank-five support spell Spell Enhance.]
Thanks to Parteian’s support, Raven’s attack was twice as powerful as usual. I paused so as not to get caught up in the spell.
Boom, boom, boom!
The Lightning Bolt, equal in power to a natural disaster, lasted only about five seconds, but it was enough to half-destroy the doppelganger corps.
Large-scale combat really is the best type of hunting.
The remaining monsters were taken down by my teammates, who were waiting in the rear. Just like that, the first battle came to an end.
“Parteian,” the blunt weapon user murmured as he brushed the blood off his weapon, “will Miss Sarman be all right? I keep getting worried.”
“You saw it for yourself. The doppelgangers don’t come near the altar. As long as she doesn’t go outside, she’ll be fine.”
“I can’t stop wondering if we should’ve just brought her...”

The blunt-weapon warrior continued to be troubled by Scout Lady, who had been left behind. But there was nothing I could do. Using a scout against a doppelganger may not have been impossible, but that was only if I wanted a sacrificial pawn. If she had come along as someone in need of protection, the cons would have far outweighed the pros.
“That’s enough. Miss Sarman agreed to it. If we fail, everyone will die anyway.”
Reading the expression on my face, Parteian ended the conversation there and I resumed our expedition without saying anything. Nothing good would come from wasting time.
Dddddd!

After that, as we fought several more battles and continued to advance through the dark forest, we felt a slight vibration beneath our feet. That meant the Seal Unlock Percentage had reached 20 percent. Since it went up 1 percent every ten minutes, it was about time.
“Mr. Yandel, can we go a little faster?”
“Sure.” I increased my speed as I raced against the clock. “We’re here.”

We finally reached our destination—a sinkhole we hadn’t noticed while wandering the forest looking for the mini bosses earlier. If we headed down there now, the boss battle would begin. But, before that, we had things to do.

“Let’s search the surrounding area first.” Following Raven’s instructions, we circled the sinkhole in search of something. It didn’t take long to find it. “As expected, it is just like the book said. It mentioned there would be one hidden near the entrance.”

“It” was a white tombstone that emitted an eerie sound. In the game, it had been named the Sealing Stone and appeared throughout the forest once the fourth stage began. But this alone couldn’t be considered the hidden reward we were looking for.

“Just like the book?” asked Parteian. Information on the Sealing Stone could be found in Memoir of the Sacrifice, which appeared at the Shadow Altar after the end of the third stage. The book just told us to find it and activate it, though. “There was nothing like that in the memoir.”
“Not the memoir, but another book.” Raven did not answer Parteian’s question in detail and placed her hand on the Sealing Stone.
Shaaaaaa!
Black light shot up into the sky in the form of a pillar.
[The Sealing Stone has been activated. Seal Unlock Percentage: 10%.]

With this, the Doppelganger’s Seal Unlock Percentage was reduced by 10 percent. Of course, if things went according to our plan this number wouldn’t matter too much anyway, but since it was on the way, there was no reason to skip it.
“Those are all the preparations we can make up here.”
Soon, we returned to the sinkhole again.
“Is everyone ready?”
It was time to fight the boss battle.
[You have entered the Doppelganger’s Hideout.]

A boss battle was the crown jewel of a Rift. However, the boss fight in the Doppelganger Forest had a slightly unusual format. First, the expedition had to be divided into two. One team had to fight the boss, while the other team had to find the Sealing Stone located in the forest riddled with doppelganger soldiers and manage the Seal Unlock Percentage. This was also the standard strategy described in Memoir of the Sacrifice.
The concept is super annoying.

Here, everyone had to trust each other and do their part to succeed. If that landmine hadn’t exploded earlier in the altar room, we probably would have chosen two or three people from each team and created two different teams to fight the boss.
We can’t use that method anymore, though. We only have seven people now.

The expedition had been cut in half and things had gone awry. Our number was nowhere near enough to split the team up. So what could we do? Looking through the dwarf and Hans G’s teams’ loot, I quickly came up with an answer and gave Raven a hint to lead her to the same one. Rather than split the already small team into two, which would render us useless on both fronts, the plan was to focus all of our manpower in one place. Put simply, it was a strategy for experienced players.
“It might be a little dangerous, though. Will everyone be okay?” she had asked.
“There is no other way.”

Thus, the basis of our strategy was laid. My guess was that our probability of success was 90 percent. Of course, probability was nothing more than a number, so the only way to see if this worked was to try it for ourselves. And when did life ever work out according to Plan A?
Boom!
Like the barbarian I was, I jumped down the tunnel first to check that it was safe. Then when I sent up a signal, the rest of our party members descended.
“The air is chilly.”
The temperature of the cave was cool.
“Kyaaargh!” The monsters inside sensed our presence and erupted in bizarre howls.
I chuckled. This was one of the roles of the barbarian: breathing courage into the team. “What are you all frozen for? Let’s go kill ‘em.”
When I went straight in without the slightest hint of hesitation, the few intimidated members of our group also came to their senses and followed along.
Trudge, trudge.

After about ninety steps or so, the fog scattered throughout the entire cave lifted and the boss room—a cavity with a huge magic circle drawn on it—was revealed. Stones of Truth were scattered on the floor like toys, and something in the form of a person sat squatting with their back turned to the center of the room. We heard the sound of sobbing.

“Are you... here to kill... me too...?” The figure turned its head and looked back at us. Its face was not any of ours. It was just an ordinary kid—or it would have been if it weren’t for the fact that its eyes, nose, and mouth were flipped upside down. “I... didn’t do... anything wrong...” The child glared at us like we were being unfair. Soon, the emotion in its eyes transformed into anger. This was a typical boss battle intro. “I’m like y—!”
I decided to skip the dialogue before it could get its next line out. “Behelahhh!” This wasn’t a good environment to use Leap, so I just dashed forward and swung my mace.
Smack!
The sitting child’s head was promptly bashed in, but I didn’t feel the usual sensation I got when I hit something. It instead felt like I had just hit a punching bag full of water.
“Keeeeeek!” A scream coming from an unidentified place filled the entirety of the cave and the child turned into black slime.
Bubble, bubble, bubble!
The black form repeatedly contracted and expanded into spikes that looked like sea urchin thorns.
Is it starting with me?

When the process was over, another me stood there. Imitation: the Doppelganger’s unique skill, which couldn’t be obtained even from its essence. However, it was a bit different than it had been during the first stage.
“Keeeeeek!” The monster no longer copied my words and actions.
[The nameless extorter has cast Swing.]

It didn’t stop with simple imitation; it became stronger than the original. On top of having the stats and skills of the individual it was copying, it also basically had the stats of a rank-five monster. Doppelganger wasn’t a rank-four monster for nothing.
Whooom!
As a test, I backed away and avoided it. Its mace slammed into the ground.
Kwaaang!

The mace left a crater behind, and the entire cave shook. It was the kind of force that required a Strength stat of at least two hundred to achieve. When I thought of this as my future self, I was almost a little proud.
I can stop this, no problem.
The stats I lacked could be compensated for with items. To make sure the Doppelganger swinging the mace indiscriminately couldn’t get near my teammates, I stopped him with my shield.
Kwaaang!
The sound wasn’t crystal clear like I had hoped, and the force slamming into the shield was greater than I expected. That was a 50 percent reduction in impact?
“Raven!” Like the dishonorable adventurer I was, I called for support. A spell flew in right away. Since our opponent was a high-rank monster, we started off with curse magic instead of attack magic.
Clang!
It became a bit easier to bear the doppelganger’s attacks after that, but this only set up the first basis of our strategy. The official first phase started now.
[The nameless extorter has cast Self-Replication.]
The Doppelganger with my appearance flung black slime from his body indiscriminately, which splattered on the ground. The number of tiny beads was too high to count.

“Iherno Heindar!” Raven’s wand released a jet of flame that melted the beads of sludge, but it was impossible to dispose of them all. The beads stubbornly crawled across the floor and clumped together. Then, after going through a series of transformations, they began to copy our appearances. Raven calmly relayed the information to me. “Four in total!”

I quickly made a decision. Since these were just clones, they wouldn’t perform on the same level as the original body. Thus, I promptly set the plan in motion. “Don’t worry about me and get rid of them first!” I left the clones to my teammates and just decided to focus on facing the main body.
“They’re all Hans Chrisen!”
At Raven’s briefing, my body stiffened reflexively.
What?
I doubted whether I’d heard her right and, even though I was in the middle of battle, I took a moment to look. Of course, Raven hadn’t given me faulty information.
...God damn it.
How could they all show up as Hans G? Alive or dead, didn’t they randomly transform into one of the fifteen of us? So what the hell were the odds of this happening?
Oblivious to where my mind was at, Raven shouted like this was good news. “It’s a relief that Mr. Yandel isn’t among the clones! Let’s sort this out quickly!”

It wasn’t that I couldn’t understand why she felt that way. Not only was Hans G relatively inferior in combat power to the rest of us, but four summoners was also a shitty combination. There was no doubt this worked out well for us.
Thump.
But my heart started pounding like crazy anyway.

chapters.title: Chapter 189: Overgeared (4)
paragraphs: A doppelganger clone was not the same as the original Doppelganger body. It could only use the abilities of the individual it was imitating. Plus, monsters that were just summoned in the boss room lacked intelligence. No, should I say skill? Unlike Hans G, who had been able to summon all of his creatures at the start of the battle, the clones lagged as they summoned one creature each.
“One guy for now.” Before the clones could even do anything, Mr. Bear’s crossbow pierced one in the forehead. The rest soon met a similar fate.
“We destroyed them all!”
Victory came in less than thirty seconds. I had been worried that something shitty might happen since there were four Hanses, but it had gone smoothly—for now.
“Everyone, now!” Before it could summon more clones, we had to hurry up and damage the original body. It wouldn’t be easy, though.
“Keeeeeek!” While everyone was dealing damage, the main body began screaming and running amok with Leap, Swing, and Giantization.
[The nameless extorter has cast Flesh Burst.]

It even had the skill I stopped using after losing my healing factor. With my physical ability on top of the average stats of a rank-five monster, this guy truly boasted the grandeur of a boss monster.

“Everyone, get back!” In the end, Raven had to pull the close-range fighters back. It wasn’t a bad call. With two mages and one archer, there were more than enough damage dealers. There was no need to take on risk by pushing our close-range fighters to the forefront. Plus, while the Doppelganger was using my form, there wasn’t much of a point to dealing damage, anyway. “You three, please protect us!”
Once the three close-range damage dealers—Missha, Ainar, and the blunt-weapon warrior—took defensive positions, the team’s back row were able to fire at ease and thus sent more ranged shots forward.
Where do you think you’re going?

As high-powered, long-range damage continued, the monster’s main body ignored me and tried to retreat back. Each time it did, I managed my Threat Level with Wild Outburst and drew its attention back onto me. This went on for who knows how long.
Pzzzzzz!
A Thunder Spear sunk into the Doppelganger’s head. Its body was tattered from repeated Flesh Bursts, and the monster transformed back into black slime.
Looks like we cleared the first hurdle.
Of course, the first phase of the fight was far from over yet. The first phase only ended once every character who entered the boss room had been cloned in turns.
“Oh! This time it’s me!”

Whoever appeared, they wouldn’t be as difficult to handle as me. As a matter of fact, Ainar was designated as the next doppelganger but the battle was over before the clones even got a chance to fight us. Now, there was no reason for the close-range damage dealers to remain in the back.
“Keeeeeek!”
We had just defeated Ainar’s doppelganger when...
Ddddddd!

The magic circle drawn on the floor radiated light and the entire cave began to tremble. Ah, but it wasn’t an ultimate finisher move or anything. This just meant the Seal Unlock Percentage had gone up another 10 percent.
[Seal Unlock Percentage: 20%.]
Although only a few minutes had passed since the start of the boss battle, this was an unavoidable part of it. Once the battle began, the speed at which the seal was unlocked increased dramatically.
If I remember correctly, it was about 5 percent per ten summoned clones.

This was the most annoying part of this stage. No matter what you did, it was impossible to stop the Doppelganger from summoning clones, so an increase in the unsealing rate was unavoidable. Well, if there had been a second team outside who could activate the Sealing Stone, that would have made things easier, but that wasn’t the case.
We have no choice but to finish this fight before then.

If it reached 100 percent and the seal was fully unlocked, it would be game over for us. From that point on, each clone would become as strong as the main body. The clones would even be able to proliferate through Self-Replication.
“It’s me this time.”

Next up was Raven. Unexpectedly, it was a close call. Casting time was essential for magic, so I intended to finish this as fast as possible, but the clones summoned during this fight proved to be a problem. Two of the four were me.
“Behelaaah!”
“Behelaaah!”

I didn’t know what kind of spell the Doppelganger was trying to cast, but sensing the way the mana was gathering, Raven shouted that we’d all end up dead at this rate. I was sure it would’ve been a big problem if the spell was completed. I blew off its head before that, though.
Crunch!

Afterward, the doppelganger transformed into Missha, the blunt-weapon warrior, Parteian, and Mr. Bear in that order, and we did our best to get rid of them as quickly as possible. Finally, the first phase was over.
Dddddd!
No sooner had the first phase ended than the magic circle lit up again.
A 40 percent unseal rate in the first phase...
It was the exact number I had predicted. But I still wanted to reduce it as much as possible.

“Everyone, get in the formation we discussed!” I let go of my disappointment and doled out orders. Now that the first phase was over, the Doppelganger was once again transforming, repeatedly contracting and expanding in the center of the cave.

“If it is... a lie... no one knows...” The Doppelganger’s voice echoed through the entire cave, signaling the start of the next phase. “Is that... not the truth?” Soon, the doppelganger completed its transformation.
[The nameless extorter has cast Swap.]
It was time to begin the second phase.

Swap was one of the Doppelganger’s special abilities. Its effectiveness was truly intuitive. This skill swapped the location of the main body with the location of a clone created with Self-Replication. However, that was just if you obtained the skill through an essence.
“...Why is it starting with me?”
“...Why is it starting with me?”
Raven doubled. Their faces were the same, and there were no differences in their tones of voice or expressions. And it was now impossible to distinguish between them by location.
This is how the wizard I had trained so hard to get died way back when.
I remembered the first wizard I had ever successfully recruited while playing Dungeon and Stone. My shock had been immense back then.
Slide.

I shifted my gaze and scanned the Stones of Truth rolling around the ground like toys. Usually, the standard strategy was to use these to distinguish whether someone was a doppelganger or not. But if we did, the Seal Unlock Percentage would go up. Without the external support of a Sealing Stone team, we could not use these. So, how would we distinguish the real from the fake?
Smirk.
I smiled and stared at the two Ravens. Although their first lines matched up, their words and actions differed from here.
“D-Don’t shoot!”
“What are you all doing? She’s the fake one!”
One said defensive lines and the other defended herself with a rather aggressive stance.
“What are you doing?” I said curtly. “Shoot it.”
Click.
I could hear Mr. Bear pull his trigger behind me.
Pop!
A large arrow no different from a siege weapon was fired, shattering Raven’s small skull.
Slump.
The body collapsed lifelessly. Everyone, including Missha, froze. “W-Was it... the real Aruru...?”
“Murderer! You killed Aruru!”
“Of course not. Calm down, everyone.”

Before long, Raven’s body turned into black slime and floated up from the ground. That meant I had been right. For reference, the aggressive Raven had been the real one. “Okay, you go to the empty spot now.”
I sent Raven to the wall, as her position had been swapped with the Doppelganger, and approached the slime in the middle of its transformation. “So it’s you this time.”
As I waited with my mace held up, the Doppelganger finished transforming. “Eek! P-Put that down, you boneheaded barrrbarian!”
You wish.
Smack!
Without further ado, I clocked it over the head with my mace. Once again, it was the right answer. A doppelganger couldn’t copy a numbered item, and the real Missha had No. 5991: Serpent’s Fang.
“Uh, shouldn’t you still take a second to think about it firrrst? I mean, it was me...”
“Oh, Miss Karlstein, what do you expect from a barbarian?” Raven, who had received the used-up Misplaced Trust from Parteian and had been holding it in her hand for the entire boss battle, said.
“It’s finally my turn. I will handle it.” Mr. Bear had the Deceit of the Necromancer.
“Behelahhh!” Ainar was wearing the Fox Flame Knot from the elven archer. It wasn’t a useful item, so it’d be sold once we got outside.
Crunch!
As such, we could breeze through the second phase with the power of items. Did it just realize that now?
[The nameless extorter has cast Swap.]

The Doppelganger transformed into the blunt-weapon warrior and immediately started attacking. The target was the wizard with the lowest Defense stat. If we had been standing in a dense formation like before, this attack would have been difficult to avoid.
“I will stop it!”
However, as soon as we entered the second phase, we distanced ourselves and stayed close to the wall. As a result, we had more than enough time to react to a surprise attack.
Bang!

Ainar’s greatsword clashed with the Doppelganger’s war hammer and exploded. Taking advantage of the opening, Missha slid in from behind and thrust her sword forward. Afterward, Mr. Bear and Raven swept in and finished it off.
“Everyone to their positions!”
After each round, the team members who had already been imitated were all sent to one place to gather in a dense formation.
“Why aren’t you going?”

The blunt-weapon warrior came to his senses at my words and hurriedly moved to his position. A dim light shone from his shoes. This was an inexpensive Numbers Item in the nine-thousands range called the Footsteps of Abundance. It was rather useful for a warrior. It hadn’t been loaned to him from the loot, either—the shoes were his. Apparently, he had worked hard to save up for them.
[The nameless extorter has cast Swap.]
Anyway, next was the middle-aged wizard Parteian. He had lent his Misplaced Trust to Raven, but this wasn’t particularly a problem. After all, this guy’s magic wand was a numbered item too.
Crunch!
Since the imitated individual was a wizard, it didn’t take long to defeat it. Now all that was left was me.
“Mr. Parteian.”
“Are you talking about that? I will prepare it straight away.” Having suffered greatly at the hands of my doppelganger in the past, the wizards had already prepared their strongest spells.
“Behelahhh!” As soon as the Doppelganger finished transforming, I shoved him back with my shield.

“The one in the back is fake!” In an instant, the wizards made their call and aimed the spells they had prepared. Of course, a tank wouldn’t die in one blow, but since there were no summons in the second phase, they were able to cast uninterrupted.
Pzzz! Bang! Shwooop!
The high-powered attack spells literally rained down. Soon, the Doppelganger couldn’t take any more damage and collapsed. The sight was kind of bittersweet.
I should fix up my Mana Resistance soon.
I still had a long way to go as a tank.
We finally reached the third phase, aka the last phase of the doppelganger fight.
“Everyone, come over here!” Without needing any orders from me, Raven commanded everyone into a new formation. Right at that moment, the labyrinth began to shake with what felt like an earthquake.
Dddddd!
The ceiling made a crumbling sound and grains of dust fell to the ground.

“Ki-hee-hee, hi-hee, ki-hee-hee, ki-hee-hee!” The Doppelganger had returned to its slime-like form and let out a strange peal of laughter. Honestly, it wasn’t even creepy anymore. All I wondered was how the hell it was speaking without a mouth.
“Be careful! Mr. Yandel, if you go down—”
“Don’t worry. That won’t happen.”

Raven’s worries were summarily dismissed. It wasn’t because I was confident in our ability to win. It would be a lie if I said I wasn’t nervous. Assuming the worst and being wary of unforeseen circumstances was my go-to, after all. But a leader had to lead the team with confidence from time to time too.
Squeeze.

Only maintaining enough tension to keep my body on its toes, I gripped my mace tighter. The final phase was a sort of frenzy. From now on, every minute and second was critical because the summons would appear on a scale that far outstripped the first phase.
Pop!

As the slime expanded to the point that any onlookers would assume it had reached its limit, it exploded. Black balls of sludge covered the cave. On cue, the two wizards shot fire to eradicate them, but they couldn’t even get rid of half of them. Meanwhile, the explosions continued.
[The nameless extorter has cast Self-Replication.]
[The nameless extorter has cast Self-Replication.]
[The nameless extorter has cast Self-Replication.]

The balls clumped together to form shapes and soon mimicked our forms. Even at a glance, there were dozens. From Hans G to the elven archer, the dwarf, and more, people we’d never see again after today began to appear from all over. The wide cavern was filled in an instant.
“Don’t be afraid. The clones in this phase are not as strong as before!”

As per Raven’s words, these guys were much weaker than the ones we saw earlier. If I hit them one or two times they’d probably explode and disappear into dust. However, the Frenzy phase was scary for another reason.
[Seal Unlock Percentage: 50%.]
[Seal Unlock Percentage: 60%.]

The magic circle on the ground continued to glow, updating us on the status of the seal. If things kept going like this, the seal would unlock in just a few minutes and the Doppelganger would regain its full power. And so, it was time to take that out.
[You have used Outlaw of the Wilderness. The Physical damage you deal in close combat temporarily increases in proportion to the number of humanoid monsters present.]

This was the item that had planted the confidence in me that we could beat the shit out of this Doppelganger, and the thing that had made it possible for me to predict a whopping 90 percent probability of success.
[Current rate of increase: 112%.]
[Current rate of increase: 157%.]
[Current rate of increase: 278%.]
[Current rate of increase: 342%.]
“Behelahhh!”
Items were a skillset too.

chapters.title: Chapter 190: Overgeared (5)
paragraphs: No. 8667: Outlaw of the Wilderness was the numbered item Team Dwarf’s beast warrior had been wearing, and there were no stats attached to it. That was expected of a low number, and it was also relatively cheap. That was because its effects were a little ambiguous. Close-combat physical damage increased against humanoid monsters, and the rate of increase was proportional to the number of monsters. There was bound to be little demand for this item among adventurers. Humanoid monsters were scarce in the labyrinth, and even those didn’t typically move in flocks.
Plus, it takes a day to recharge.

Honestly, unless you were aiming for a Doppelganger or a specific monster on the fifth floor, it was a hard item to find a use for. But thanks to this item, our odds of victory had really jumped. If it wasn’t for this, it probably would have been half and half.
[Seal Unlock Percentage: 70%.]

Just then, the magic circle let out another burst of light and announced that the seal wasn’t far off from unlocking now. Since the rate rose by 5 percent per ten monsters, according to our calculations, the number of summoned clones had already surpassed sixty.
[Current rate of increase: 401%.]
However, it was still a long way off. Consequently, we kept to the walls as planned and formed a dense formation.

“Barhatun Wiar.” Raven summoned a stone wall with magic. Our thought process was that we could hold out until the right moment came. However, we didn’t barricade the entire wall, but left a gap that would allow about two or three people to pass through on one side. This was Raven’s idea. If it were completely blocked, the Doppelganger would try to penetrate it, but if there were a path it could use, it would head there instead.
It really worked.

I set up camp there, blocking the only available entrance. In my current state, it didn’t matter if the doppelgangers were in my image or not—if I smacked them with my mace, they would depart this world in a single blow. I made an effort to suppress that particular desire. Our objective was not to hunt the clones.
Bam!
The clones apparently took exception to this, because they pushed each other aside to charge at me. Of course, not all of them were like that.
“There’s a hole over here!” A clone broke down the stone wall and cleared a path. When I turned around for a moment to check, the clone was none other than a copy of me.
“Mr. Yandel, focus on that side! We’ll take care of this!”
The close-range damage dealers and Iron Bear rushed to form a human barrier to stop the clones, but it wasn’t easy. We had a very big disadvantage working against us.
“Ah! Don’t kill them!”

Blocking without attacking was tough for non-professional tanks to pull off. From behind, I could hear an arduous battle ensuing, but there was nothing I could do. Going to assist them would only make our plan backfire.
Dddddd!
About two minutes later, the cave shook again.
[Seal Unlock Percentage: 90%.]
It was finally time to finish the match.
“Mr. Yandel!”
The ceiling wasn’t very high, so I jumped in place with just the slightest force in a move I called Low Jump.
[Your total weight is over 1100 lbs. Special terrain effect Recoil is applied to your total damage.]
The clones, including my colleagues, went flying through the air. As soon as I landed on the ground, I stomped on the clones and quickly rushed forward.
[Your Threat Level has temporarily increased significantly.]
Thanks to the increased Threat Level, the clones hurriedly stood up and charged at me like zombies, and soon I felt a tremendous weight pile up behind my shield.
“Behelahhh!” I shoved through the clones like a bulldozer and reached my destination within ten seconds.
Pop! Pop!
The main Doppelganger was Self-Replicating by repeatedly blowing itself up. Uninterested in seeing more, I swung my mace.
Smack!
It felt like smacking tofu, but it was enough to tell the damage had been done.

“Keeeeeek!” The main body stopped its infinite Self-Replication loop and transformed into me. Since it was in Frenzy mode, the transformation was a little different from before. The number of heads growing above the shoulders was two.
Me and Ainar... Goddamn it, why her?
It was a doppelganger with my skills that could also use Ainar’s essences.
[The nameless extorter has cast Swing.]
[The nameless extorter has cast Repeated Slash.]

The momentum of the fight was different. If it weren’t for the Guard Corps Token, I would for sure have fallen backward. And that wasn’t even taking into consideration the clones attacking and suffocating me from all sides.
Whooom!
I completely ignored it all and swung the mace. The two barbarians on the main body smiled doubtfully as if to say, You think that’ll work?
I just stared back and smiled too.
[Current rate of increase: 771%.]
You’re not the only one who has a buff. Namely, Barbarian Extreme Damage Mode.
Kwaaaaaang!
When I cast Swing, the Doppelganger blocked it with its shield as usual and staggered. With that, I had an opening. Not allowing it any time, I swung the mace again.
Crunch!
In one blow, Ainar’s head was crushed. Since it had two heads, this wasn’t enough to fell the bastard. That wasn’t a problem, though. I just had to deal it another blow.
Crunch!
After losing both heads, the doppelganger immediately returned to its slime state. Then, it hardened.
[The Doppelganger has cast Crystallization.]
This was its frantic, last-ditch attempt at avoiding death. Well, to be fair, it was a considerably tricky move.
[Magical damage has been reduced by 99%. Physical damage has been reduced by 90%.]

It was virtually immune to magic damage in this state, and the fucking cheat skill also reduced 90 percent of all physical damage. But if I couldn’t kill it in time, I’d have to repeat this all over again. It was funny, but that was the standard approach: mass summoning, transformation, crystallization. The usual strategy was to repeat this sequence over and over and accumulate enough damage to the crystal to finally destroy it.
Kaboom!
However, we had to bet everything on this one sequence, which was why we had left the clones alone.
“Raven!”

At my shout, Raven and Parteian immediately activated their magic. It wasn’t an attack spell, but one they used while PKing the dwarf’s team earlier—Mana Shield. “It won’t last long!” Raven shouted urgently.
I knew that already. As this was a spell that required a huge amount of mana consumption, within a minute, our two wizards would run out of mana.
Kwaaaaaang!
Trusting in the thick mana covering my skin, I focused solely on destroying the Doppelganger in its crystalline state. How many clones were around me right now?
Kwaaaaaang!

If it wasn’t for Outlaw of the Wilderness, I would never have gone with this strategy. Instead, I probably would’ve cleaned up the clones in advance before we dealt damage to the main body as a team, worrying the entire time whether it would be enough to actually damage it.
Crunch!

With the fourth Swing, the crystal was scratched for the first time. It was quite fascinating. Although I’d experienced this Crystallization move many times before, I was already this strong? How much damage was I dealing right now? I couldn’t know the numbers for sure, but it was amazing because there was still one thing I hadn’t used yet.
[You have cast Leap.]
Once again, Low Jump.
[Your Threat Level has temporarily increased significantly.]
“Behelahhh!” I followed it up with Wild Outburst right away.
[Your Threat Level temporarily increases by x3, and your physical stats increase in proportion to that value.]
Robust power radiated from my body. Of course, the duration of this high was very short, but according to my calculations, this would be enough.
[The destructive force of any blunt weapons you use will increase significantly in proportion to your Muscle Strength.]
Threat Level was converted to Strength, and Strength into destructive force in a miraculous law of exchange.
[Current rate of increase: 771%.]
When you added Outlaw of the Wilderness on top of that, even 90 percent Physical Immunity was pretty much negligible.
Baaaaaang!
After all, my damage was being copied right now.
[You have killed a Doppelganger. EXP +6]
[Guardian kill bonus. EXP +3]

How many times did I slam down my mace on the crystal like a man possessed? I couldn’t be sure, but around the time Mana Shield’s effects faded and injuries began to quickly accumulate on my body, the crystal cracked like a broken mirror and soon shattered like a grenade.
Crackkk!
I couldn’t even say it was a close call.
About a minute, huh?
It broke a lot faster than I expected. I had even considered that we might need everyone to attack it together. But in a surprise twist, there was no need to even use Plan B.
Yes, there need to be days like these too.
An unease came over me. No one could say it was good luck that something hadn’t unexpectedly gone wrong.
No, it’s still too early to feel relieved.
I shook myself from my thoughts. After all, four Hans Gs had appeared right after the boss battle began despite ridiculously low odds. Just like the Bloody Citadel, this could be a variant Rift.
Shaaaaa!
Just then, fragments of the shattered body turned into light and scattered through the air. It was the same for the clones filling the cave.
Whooom!
A portal connecting to the fourth floor opened in the center of the cavity. That meant that the Rift really had been cleared.
“Oh! What?! Did we kill it?!”
“Ahh, I thought I was going to die. Arurrru, can you give me a potion?”
“Later. It’s not even a big injury, right? We have to check something first! Essence? Numbers Item? Rift Stone? Did anything appear?”

Oh, right. We had to confirm that too. I had been so wary of something else showing up that I didn’t even get a good look. Now, it was time to collect the highlight of the Rift, the guardian’s reward. I gulped and looked to where the Doppelganger had been standing.
There was nothing there.
Could this be the Hans effect?

The thought did come to mind, but it was not good practice to blame everything on Hans. The drop rate of an essence or numbered item was only 33 percent, after all. Well, it broke my heart a little that even a Rift Stone, which had a drop rate of 66 percent, hadn’t shown up, though.
...This is a common thing.
It was often like this in the game. I would put my all into clearing a Rift and receive no rewards for it.
“...Mr. Yandel, snap out of it. These things happen.”
“Y-Yeah! We got a lot of other stuff already.”
When I stood there in silence, my teammates offered me words of comfort. I mean, I wasn’t mad or anything.
Are the PK rewards all of it?

It felt a bit anticlimactic, but it was funny to feel disappointed about that when I thought about it. I couldn’t even fathom how much money we’d earn from selling all that equipment. We’d pretty much guaranteed our all-time highest income, and I even consumed the essence of the Manticore.
Yeah. This is already on par with a Doppelganger essence.
Hmm, was this the effect of positive thinking? I felt more energized all of a sudden. “Missha, how’s your injury?”
“Huh? Fine. It’s just a scrrratch. A scratch!”
“Drink a potion first.” Leaving behind my disappointment, I took care of my teammates and started the after-battle cleanup.
Raven chuckled at the sight. “You really are a leader at times like these.”
“Are you mocking me?”
“Nope, that one was sincere.”
“Aruru, don’t be like that. Bjorn will be embarrassed.”
Yeah right. “Then I guess we’ll have to go back up.”
Once the cleanup was pretty much done, I led the group back into the forest. The doppelgangers above would have disappeared by now.
“You are all safe! I’m so glad!”
“Sorry to have kept you waiting, Miss Sarman.”
We picked up Scout Lady and deposited her with the blunt-weapon warrior. With that, the business between us was over.
Incidentally, the archer from Team Dwarf we had sacrificed at the altar was already dead.
“But what happened to this guy...?”
“Oh, that... I was worried he might wake up...”

It seemed she’d killed him before he could regain consciousness. It was somewhat impressive. Despite everything, she was also an adventurer. Just in case, I checked the archer’s equipment and backpack, but it didn’t seem like the elven archer had secretly taken anything. With that, the business between us was over.
“Oh, don’t forget to take this. It came in handy.”
“You keep that.”
“Really?”

Parteian gifted Misplaced Trust to Raven. Although it was out of charge, it wasn’t a worthless gift. There were, after all, ways to recharge it. Even selling it as is would earn us some hundreds of thousands of stones.

“Thank you for saving us. If you ever need my help, come find me anytime.” Just as I was wondering if those were empty words, Parteian handed me a visitation pass with the symbol of the Narman School on it.
Hmm, I guess they weren’t. I’ll keep this and go find him as soon as I need him. This feels like I’ve cleared some side quest or something.
Afterward, we said goodbye to the blunt-weapon warrior and scout woman and escorted them to the portal.
“But aren’t you guys leaving?”
“It’s a Rift, after all. We want to look around some more and do research.”
“Hmm, is that so?” Parteian nodded in apparent understanding and Raven laughed sheepishly. “Then I’ll be leaving.”
Before long, they rode the portal back to their original place.
“They... should be fine, right?”
“Worrying is unlike you.”
“Wizards always worry and care for each other, okay?”
“I meant you’re worried for nothing. It’s the fourth floor.”

Hans G and the elven archer may have been dead, but on the Tower of Heavens, you could stay put as long as you wanted. Those three would probably pass the time like we did way back when before returning to the city.
“True... you’re right.”
Turning away from the forest, we headed up to the top again. There was still something left for us to take.

chapters.title: Chapter 191: Bifron (1)
paragraphs: At 7 a.m. on our eleventh day of traversing the labyrinth, after sending the other three out of the Rift, we returned to the forest.
“Umm, why don’t we eat something firrrst?”
“That would be best.”
Finally noticing how hungry we were, we gathered and cooked a meal. And of course, it was human nature to feel drowsy when you had a full stomach.
“...Let’s sleep for today and do the rest tomorrow.”

Fatigued, we set up camp and all fell asleep. We hadn’t just stayed up the entirety of last night—we had played a game of mafia in the third stage which had wasted our energy, and had even participated in a PK. Not to mention the ensuing Doppelganger boss battle.
Hooonnnk!

Sleep came as soon as I closed my eyes. When I opened them again, a whole day had passed. Even though I fell asleep at 8 a.m., when I checked the time, the hand had moved back an hour to 7 a.m. again. That meant I had slept almost twenty-four hours.
“Oh, are you awake?”
“...Why didn’t you wake me up?”
“We just woke up too.”
So you weren’t being considerate, I see.
Quickly washing my face with some bottled water, I caught the scent of something delicious nearby.
“If you’re awake, grrrab a plate and sit. Oh, wake Ainar before that. She’ll listen to you, at least.”

After waking Ainar and eating together, we wandered the brush and picked up what we needed, a wild herb that grew exclusively in Doppelganger Forest. “Don’t just follow me and check the ground as you go. These are ten thousand stones per root.”
Along with that...
“Mr. Yandel.”
Kwaaang!
Crushing the Seal Stones, which were now useless, now had a certain probability of dropping Fragments of Sealed Evil.
“How much do these cost?”
“Around one million stones each.”
“I see. I’ll buy five of them when they appear.”
I took five of the seven total fragments, because the effects were null after that.
[You have taken a Fragment of Sealed Evil. Your Mana Resistance permanently increases by +1.]
For reference, Missha bought the remaining two pieces. “Eh? Me?”
“You made a lot of money anyway. Don’t hoard it.”

“I’m not, but...” Missha eyed Ainar with an apologetic look. She should really be more selfish, like a real adventurer. Ainar would eventually be consuming an essence with plenty of additional Mana Resistance, so it made more sense for Missha to eat this. It wasn’t like she wasn’t paying for it.
“Whew, looks like that thing’s not showing up.”
“We can spare one day. Let’s keep looking.”

Although there were no monsters, it took an entire day to search this vast forest. However, we invested even the day after to search the entirety of the forest one more time, at which point we finally found what we were looking for—a mandragora root, an ingredient that went in an elixir.

“Everyone, cover your ea—no. Just stand far back. I’ll take this one out.” Once Raven shielded herself with magic and pulled it from the ground, all our tasks in the Doppelganger Forest were complete. However, she asked, “I’m really sorry, but could you give me a little more time? I want to see more of this place.”
“Why?”
“It’s purely personal curiosity.”
At Raven’s request, we decided to stay here longer. Surprisingly, no one objected.
“Right, the Complete Book of Rifts. The perrrson who wrote that can’t know everything about this place!”
“If we’re lucky, we might discover something.”

The prospect made everyone’s eyes light up. Well, I thought the possibility that we’d find a hidden feature that I was unaware of was close to zero, but at least she’d asked. When we first met in the Bloody Citadel, she hadn’t bothered with requests. Raven just used the dwarf and me as her servants and made us help her with her research.
“Then where are you going to look first?”
“The cave at the very start.”

Starting from Shadow Cave in the first stage, we moved all the way to the Doppelganger’s Hideout and searched meticulously. Well, to be more accurate, we smashed anything that seemed suspicious as we searched. As expected, there were no hidden rooms or items. However, numerous questions cropped up along the way.
“Why did it have to be a steel cage?” Raven said.
“Isn’t it because we had to wait for the other teams to enter?”
“Then it would make more sense to just make it a timed entry. Just like when we enter and exit the labyrinth.”

Why was it that Doppelganger Forest began with us imprisoned behind bars? What was the Memoir of the Sacrifice we had obtained from the altar, and why was it described as a sacrifice? Why did the clones turn into imperial soldiers after the third stage? No, what even was the Empire they mentioned?
“Now that I think about it, it’s a pity. Although it was inarticulate, it could still speak. We might have learned something if we captured one...”
We discussed the topics Raven raised as a team but couldn’t come up with any answers. And so, our Rift expedition ended there.
“I’m sorry, everyone. We wasted two days for nothing because of me.”
“Don’t apologize. You are the party’s wizard. It was a fair request. We’re the ones who agreed to the search.”
“He’s rrright. And it was fun, I felt like a real adventurerrr. Right, Ainar?”
“Huh? I thought it was boring.”
“Please, take a hint. Hmm?” Ainar followed Missha like an older sister these days, so when she scolded her, Ainar turned sullen.

Raven smiled at the sight. “Thank you, everyone. But now that I think about it, I don’t think there was anything to be sorry about. Even if we sell just one mandragora root, that’ll balance out a few days of hunting, right?”
“It seems our wizard has returned to normal.”
“Normal? Mr. Urikfried, what do you mean by that?”
Mr. Bear just shrugged his shoulders and avoided answering. Raven eyed him suspiciously but did not press further.
[You have entered the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.]

On the afternoon of the fourteenth day, after returning to the labyrinth through the portal in the boss room, we continued our quest. It took about six days to reach the fifth floor. After that, we took the Hellfire Gorge route as planned and pretended to be focused on hunting while we actually looked for a Mila Roden. Oh, for reference, once you found the black moss, everything after that was a breeze. I didn’t even have to cue Raven to use detection magic. Having enjoyed our previous expedition into the mirror, Raven cast a detection spell every five minutes.
“...It didn’t stay again.”

As a result, we were able to hunt a total of three Mila Roden, but none of them had been winning tickets. Actually, this was the norm. The possibility of the distortion spell succeeding and Mila Roden’s corpse remaining intact was 20 percent.
That’s out the window this time.

Since there were only five days left until the labyrinth closed, we didn’t bother looking for any more Mila Roden. Even if we got into the Mirror of Fire, we wouldn’t have time to do anything. That was too bad, though, because I had planned on using the Orb of Fire to try out a new area.
[You have defeated a Stoneburn. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Fire Zombie. EXP+2]
[You have defeated a Red Mud. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Hell Flame. EXP +5]

Still, the hunt itself wasn’t bad. This was the only bright side of the failed attempt to conquer Noark. With more than 90 percent of the clans occupying the map now gone, the entire fifth floor was overrun with monsters. Of course, this situation wouldn’t last long. In a few months, clans who had recovered would return, and a lot of clans likely hadn’t entered this time around in the first place because the situation was unstable.
More time passed like that, and the day of our return soon dawned.
[You have been transported to Rafdonia.]
Warm sunlight blanketed my skin. As always, I stood there absently enjoying the warmth for a while. Looking around, I could see some other adventurers doing the same.
Okay, let’s go.
When I headed to the checkpoint for our rank, I could see my teammates had arrived before me, all except one person. “I see Abman is not here yet.”
“Oh, there he is now. With someone else. Again.”
It was a strange sight every time. No matter how large the plaza was, how could he get lost there?
“Haha, the line isn’t too long this time,” Abman said.
“Not because you managed to get here any faster. I think it’s because the number of adventurers who entered the labyrinth this time was smaller than usual,” Raven said.
“Ahem, I didn’t say otherwise.”
Anyway, as we waited in line together, our turn soon came. Our mana stone income was much lower than before.
“7.08 million stones.”

Divided in five, that was about 1.41 million per person, almost four times less than last time. But that was unavoidable. Not only had we been unable to enter the mirror world, but it was difficult to get mana stones in Doppelganger Forest, where we had invested a lot of our time.
“Is that all?”

“Yes, congratulations on your earnings.” Since it wasn’t an outrageous amount of money, the employee didn’t send us suspicious looks. However, as we were about to leave the checkpoint, the employee urgently stopped us. “Oh, please wait!”
“...Is something wrong?”
“Team Apple Narak, and team leader Bjorn Yandel,” he said quickly. “Is that right?”
“Yes, and?”
“...You’ll have to wait here for a moment. That includes your team members.”

A security guard hadn’t come to seize me like in the past, but the request was enough for me to realize something was wrong. It was the same for our party’s wizard. “Excuse me, shouldn’t you explain what’s going on first?” Raven spoke aggressively on my behalf as I was on the verge of having my PTSD triggered.
“Inspector, is this them?”
“Ah, yes, yes! That’s correct!”
Then a knight entered the checkpoint. Raven’s expression darkened. “Why is Mozlan...?”
Mozlan: an executive body made up exclusively of knights with noble backgrounds, and an organization with an infamous reputation.
“Bjorn.” Missha, who had seen Dwalkie get arrested right in front of her, shuddered.

However, the knight was surprisingly kind, at least more so than those high-handed bastards from back then. “Nice to meet you. I’m Elmeras from Mozlan’s executive board.” Although even his casual speech was that of a lord, that was to be expected of a nobleman. That wasn’t the main issue here anyway. The most important thing was that he was offering a handshake. For now, this man wasn’t being all that hostile toward us.

“...Bjorn, son of Yandel.” Inwardly, I sighed in relief and reciprocated the handshake. However, my anxiety wasn’t fully gone. Why had the inspector stopped us and for what reason had Mozlan come to find us?
“Hello.”
“Hmm, and you are, young lady?”
“I’m Arua Raven from the School of Altemion. I want to hear why you came to see us, Sir Elmeras.”
The knight answered Raven’s question with a laugh. “There is only one reason why the inspector would detain you. Someone has put an arrest order on your team.”
It was truly out of left field. “Sorry? What do you—”
“Don’t be too alarmed. Judging by the details of the order, it doesn’t seem to be very serious.”
“But what are we being arrested for?”
The knight grinned and replied, “The activation of a special ability within city limits, and entering the labyrinth without permission against the instructions of the guards.”
Oh, that...
Everyone including Raven shut up. After everything we went through in the labyrinth, we had completely forgotten about that. We thought that would end with just a fine in the first place.

“I don’t understand. Isn’t the standard punishment a fine?” I couldn’t help but ask in an argumentative tone. No matter how I looked at it, there was no reason for an arrest order to get dropped on us nor for Mozlan to get involved. So how did this happen?
“We have to look at what you did in context. Rather than committing a simple misdemeanor, it could be argued that you have all violated royal orders.”
So, that was it. The situation pretty much made sense now.
It seemed Raven had figured it out too. “...You’re saying they’re making efforts to rein the adventurers in.”
“I can’t hide anything from a wizard. It’s just as you say. Although only a day has passed, news of your team is already spreading among the adventurers.”
“News of us?”

“They’re all calling themselves stupid for following orders instead of running blindly into the labyrinth. The higher-ups have determined that a similar event will occur again if this ends with a simple fine.”
Put simply, they were using us to set an example, punishing one person to instill alarm in the minds of a hundred.
“If control over the city’s adventurers loosens now, it might lead to bigger issues. I hope you understand.”
I could see why they chose me. As I had some previous fame and had become a hot topic due to our unauthorized entry into the labyrinth, they probably figured that news would spread fast.
“So, what happens to us now?”
When I cut straight to the point of this conversation, the knight clarified one thing before answering. “To be more precise, it’s what happens to you, not them.”

The only one who would be punished was me. The rest would end up with fines. Apparently, it seemed from an outsider’s perspective like the rest of them had just been dragged into the situation because of me, and since this punishment was just meant to make a statement, we didn’t all have to suffer.
“Oh, that’s reasonable! Yes, that makes sense!” Seeing Ainar delight in that hurt my feelings.
Raven didn’t step forward and call it unfair, either. Mr. Bear was just relieved that he had managed to avoid a beating from his wife. Was I the only one who would stand up for myself?
Just as I started to feel a lack of trust toward my teammates, Missha asked, “Umm, Mr. Knight? If it’s just for show anyway, can I rrreceive the punishment instead?”
Correction: Missha was the only one who stood up for me.

“What are you saying, Missha?” I chuckled and nudged her away. I was grateful, but it was unlikely that would work. If you wanted to get nitpicky, I was the culprit behind this incident anyway. Besides, it sounded like the punishment wouldn’t be too severe from the way he was talking. “It’s fine. I will take responsibility. So tell me. What will become of me now?”
The knight’s response was utterly nonchalant. “Go live in Bifron for twenty days.”
In other words, I was being temporarily exiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 192: Bifron (2)
paragraphs: Although once a mere colony, the world’s sole stronghold, Rafdonia, had transformed into humanity’s final home as survivors flocked to it following the apocalypse. This stronghold consisted of fourteen districts.

To start, District One was the royal capital of Karnon, where the royal family and the nobility resided. Its most prominent trait was that no commoner was allowed to enter without permission. Districts Two to Five were Kommelby, a commercial area commonly referred to as the free market. Located on the outskirts of the royal capital, expert artisans and profitable shops were concentrated here. Districts Seven to Thirteen were Ravigion. Occupying the largest area of the capital, about 70 percent of the total population resided in this city. Its key feature was that a Dimension Square, where the portal opened every month, existed in each district.

Finally, District Fourteen was Bifron. Unlike Gnome Tree in District Six, which had been classified as a special district from the moment the city was designed, this district was a very different case. Originally, it had been part of Ravigion, but now it was designated as a prohibited area that didn’t even have a Dimension Square of its own.
Creaaak!
This place’s gates were now opening so that a single prisoner could be tossed in.
“What are you doing? Get in.”
“...Is that it?”

“Haven’t you been briefed already? Unless you try to escape, it doesn’t matter what you do.” The knight who brought me here turned his back on me, apparently uninterested in sticking around here any longer.
Boom!
Before long, the castle gates closed. Only then did I turn around to examine my surroundings.
“A prison, huh?”

As its nickname suggested, this place gave off a different vibe from the other normal districts. If District Seven, where I lived, was abandoned for a hundred years, it might look something like this. There were old buildings in various states of disrepair or demolition scattered around, and the outer wall was covered in filth and graffiti. The streets weren’t much different. Waste materials were piled up haphazardly.
Welp. I guess I have to spend twenty days here.

I didn’t want to linger by the gate so I just started walking. I could feel wary stares at me. These looks were from the residents of this district, who were wearing shabby clothes over their skinny, bony bodies. Or should I say, inmates?
Scoff.

I couldn’t help laughing. How would modern man Hansu Lee from the twenty-first century have reacted to this? He would have surely shriveled up from those stares alone. Along with disapproval, those eyes were filled with greed. I was sure he would be busy looking for a place to hide, unable to utter a word.
“What are you looking at?”

But right now, I was a barbarian of this era with a six-foot-tall, muscular body clad in heavy armor. Even if dozens of those skeletons attacked me, I was confident I could turn them into watermelon porridge in a matter of minutes.
“Behelaaah!”
When I unleashed a Wild Outburst carrying that confidence, the residents watching me from the shadows looked as if they had seen a ghost and gone on their way.
“It’s fine! I won’t bite!” Watching them, I laughed dramatically and continued walking.
“W-Why is that man screaming out of nowhere...?”
“...Seeing as he came all the way here, he can’t be sane.”
“Unhinged bastard. It’ll be best not to get too close.”
