I could hear these faint whispers as I walked. It was just the reaction I was hoping for. I refused to attract flies in the middle of all this mess.
This feels like entering a beginner’s level.

I had been quite worried because this place was called a lawless land. Or, that was what Missha called it, at least. Now, I was convinced. The stronger man had the upper hand in lawless places, and it could even end up being more comfortable for him than a society where laws did exist.
I can just think of it as taking a nice break.
This barbarian body was sensitive to the natural order of things and was already realizing that I wouldn’t have a hard time here.
I was walking around and exploring my surroundings when a little boy about ten years old boldly jumped in my way. “Excuse me, Mister New Guy!”
“Did you follow me from the gate?” I asked, just to confirm.
“No? I saw you just now.”
“Then how did you know I’m new here?”

“Because I’m seeing you for the first time today. Whenever someone like you comes here, rumors spread fast.” That made sense. You just had to glance around at the frail people walking down the street to see why I would stand out.
“What do you want?” Conscious of our surroundings, I spoke in a low voice.

However, this kid did not back down and spoke his mind clearly and loudly without avoiding my eyes at all. “If it’s your first day, you haven’t found a place to stay yet, right? Let me guide you. I might not look it, but I’m a native here, born and raised.”
Put simply, he wanted to be my guide. Of course, it wouldn’t be for free. I was sure he hadn’t mustered up the courage to stand in the way of a giant barbarian for charity. “Your price?”
“Just give me one hundred stones.”
That was pocket change that seemed to be missing a zero at the end. “Fine. Lead the way.”

When I coolly accepted, the child took the lead, saying he’d take me to the best place in this area. As I followed the kid, I asked him some of the questions that popped into my head. I had read a few books on Bifron at the library, but it would be conceited to assume I knew everything about this place just from that. First, out of personal curiosity, I asked, “Were you born here?”
“Yes.”
“Parents?”
“They passed away.”
“I mean, were your parents born here like you?” The child looked like he didn’t want to answer that, but he gave in to money in the end. “I’ll give you one hundred more stones.”
“...Only Mother. I heard Father come from outside.”
“For what crime?”
“...Possession and distribution of seditious books. And before you ask, it was a book on whether the taxes paid to the palace are fair or not.”

“He was a man of intellect, then.” It wasn’t that surprising. The nickname Prison Camp had been attached to Bifron in the first place because those who slandered the royal family were banished here. You want to complain that bad, then try living someplace out of reach from our divine protection—that was the gist of the logic behind the banishments, but for the royal family, it was a very clever move. It was a way to drive out rebels while solidifying the position of the sovereign. There was a lot more to gain this way than with hangings.
“How old are you?”
“I’m eleven.”
“So you can leave in three years.”
“If I prove I’m skilled enough.”
I cocked my head. “Skilled? I heard children can leave once they turn fourteen?”

“You only heard half of it. Freedom is only available to a small number of people who show promise in whatever field. Well, they say whatever, but most people aim to be adventurers. It’s a lot easier that way and they choose more people.”
“Are you aiming for the adventurer side too?”
“No. Scholar.”
A scholar, huh? No wonder this kid was so well-spoken. It seemed he’d managed to keep up his education even in this environment.
“You’re an adventurer, right? How did you end up here?”
Soon the child started asking me questions too. It seemed he thought it was unfair that he was the only one answering them.
“If you’re willing to earn one hundred stones less, I’ll tell you.”
“It’s not even that much money...”
“Adventurers never leave money on the table, even if it’s a small amount.”

“Oh, so you are an adventurer?” It was too childish of a trick to say he really bested me. But realizing I could hurt him, the kid quickly continued talking. “All right. I’ll take a smaller payment. So tell me why you are here.”
“I made a small mistake in the city. They told me to come live here for twenty days.”

“Twenty days...” Was this an infinitely short amount of time for a boy who grew up here all his life? The little boy chewed his lip and was silent for a moment. Then he asked one more thing. “What rank are you?”

This was personal information I didn’t really want to answer. “That wasn’t the question you asked. You can keep the one hundred stones. Just answer my questions thoroughly from now on.” Like the cowardly adult I was, I dodged that conversation and changed the topic to questions on things that were hard to grasp through books alone, like the prices in Bifron, the social structure, etcetera. Like a true native, he answered each one without much difficulty, but one piece of information made an impression on me: the source of their food.
“The palace sends rations every month?”
“Yes. But the big guys take it all and use it as leverage against the rest of us.”

The thugs he had mentioned didn’t bother me. A hierarchy was bound to exist, even among the lowest of the low. That was all part of being human. What caught my attention was something else. “This place is more and more contradictory...”
“Pardon?”
“Nothing.” My interest in Bifron had been piqued. It felt like this district, which in the game was normal like the rest, had an interesting hidden backstory.
“We’re here.”

After walking and talking for a bit longer, we arrived at the inn the kid told me about. The first floor was a tavern and the second floor an inn, just like many other shops in the city. Usually, these kinds of shops were occupied and run by thugs.
This is the best place?
I chuckled and opened the door to the inn, which looked to be infested with bugs.
Creaaak.
Surprisingly, there were quite a few people inside, men and women with sturdy physiques drinking alcohol and wearing tattered clothes.
Jingle.
When the rusted bell rang, all eyes inside turned to me. The emotions in them varied: wariness, confusion, curiosity, greed. I ignored it all and approached the counter.
“Innkeeper, how much is it for one night?”
“Fifty stones.”
Once again, that number was missing a zero. “How about a meal?”
“Two hundred fifty stones.”

“Two hundred fifty stones...” This was chump change to me, but now that I was actually experiencing it for myself, I realized how different this place was from the outside world. To think the price of food was five times more than the price of housing. These prices were unimaginable in Rafdonia, where the housing crisis was severe.
“I’ll sleep here tonight.”
“The meal?”
“I’ll take it straight away.”
“We take advance payment here.”
Paying three hundred stones for everything, I sat down.
“I’ll get going now, Mister.”
“You haven’t gotten paid yet.”
“Oh, right!” I handed a thousand stones to the child, who had just remembered why he was there. “I... don’t have any change...”
“Keep the change. Come sit next to me.”
“Pardon?”
“Keep me company until my meal arrives.”
After giving me a strange look, the kid collected himself and sat next to me. He answered every question I asked. We passed the time like that.
“Here’s the food you ordered.” Finally, my long-awaited meal arrived. With no meat to be seen, it was just bread and translucent soup.
“Then...”
I stopped the kid as he tried to get up. “Sit.”
“What? But you said until your food gets here.”
Geez, did barbarians look like fools to these people? Adding murderous energy to my voice, I said imperiously, “Sit.”
Sensing the heavy shift in the air, the child clammed up and sat back down. He pretended not to, but I could feel him trembling even across the table.
I scooped up a large spoonful of soup. “Eat.”
“Pardon?”
“I said eat.”
“Th-thank you, but I’m not hungry...”
So, that’s how you’re going to play this?
“If you eat, I’ll give you ten thousand stones.”
I made an offer the kid could never refuse. What choice would he make now? The answer was really simple. “P-Please spare me...” Like a child born and raised in a shitty environment, he was quick.
There were two reasons why I was able to see through the kid’s tricks.
“Did you follow me from the gate?”
“No? I saw you just now.”

One, the kid had calmly answered my question with a lie. Well, he had been good enough to not make the lie obvious, but I was fairly confident in my memory. This kid had been hanging around near me ever since the castle gate opened.
“Just give me one hundred stones.”

Two, the amount of money he had requested was too low. This was very strange. Tourist destinations always scammed people left and right, but this kid and even the innkeeper didn’t think to overcharge me. Of course, this could just be a coincidence.

“P-Please spare me...” But instead of eating, the kid dropped to his knees. I wasn’t surprised because I had kind of expected it. This was not the first time the people of this world lacked the creativity needed to pull off a good scheme.
If you want to stab someone in the back, make it a little less obvious next time.

I flipped the table along with the soup I wouldn’t eat even if they paid me and got up. At first, I was going to interrogate him to get him to spill the name of his accomplice, but it seemed that wasn’t necessary.

“Stop right there,” I said to the thugs quietly shuffling toward the door, attempting friendly conversation for a change. Unfortunately, the four men and women—including the innkeeper—were rather busy speeding up their escape.
“Damn it!”
“Run!”
I watched and clicked my tongue in irritation.
Do you really think that’ll work?
“Aaagh!”
In a series of fluid movements, I first picked up the kid with one hand, then smoothly activated Giantization mid-step, and then kicked off the ground with Leap.
Smashhh!
My body crossed a distance of dozens of yards in an instant and landed on the ground. With the Recoil effect, the men and women trying to escape were sent flying.
“Behelaaah!” When I followed that up with Wild Outburst, the foursome no longer dared to get up and run away.
Crunch.

To prevent them from escaping, I broke one foot each. It was broad daylight and also in the middle of the street, but oh well. This was a lawless land, after all. No security guards would come running because I used a special ability, either.
“Agh, ah!”
Only then did they come to their senses. Among the four, the man with the face of a rat shouted what sounded like a prepared line. “W-We’re from the Western Alliance!”
The Western Alliance was one of the four gangs that controlled Bifron. Apparently, their leader was an adventurer.
“I-If you let us go, we won’t retaliate for—”
You wish.
Crunch.
I crushed his other foot to shut him up, but apparently, that made him even more desperate. “O-Our boss is a rank-six adventurer!” Even while screaming in pain, the guy wouldn’t stop talking.

I couldn’t help but tilt my head in confusion. “Your boss? What do you mean?” He tilted his own head at my quizzical tone like he couldn’t understand what the hell I was talking about. I pasted on a friendly smile and bent down to pat the man’s head. “From now on, your boss is me.”
I had always wanted my own subordinates.

chapters.title: Chapter 193: Bifron (3)
paragraphs: On the third floor of the tavern where Team Apple Narak always assembled, Raven let out a sigh. Said sigh was the result of a lack of a certain person’s presence thanks to unforeseen circumstances. “Well, we’ve all gathered as promised, but we won’t be able to divide the loot like this.”

It had already been three days since they had returned to the city. On behalf of their absent leader, Raven visited Kommelby and sold all of their loot on her own. The payout was a whopping 152,400,000 stones.
“A h-hundred million?! I’ve never heard of that unit before!”
“Woah, that’s the amount even after subtracting the equipment we took?”
“Well, we sold equipment we collected from seven intermediate adventurers, after all. And the numbered item Fox Flame Knot was just registered at the auction house and hasn’t even been sold yet.”
“...I expected a high number, but this is really incredible.”

As soon as they heard the amount, everyone gasped. It was just the reaction she was hoping for, but why did it feel like something was missing? Raven subconsciously glanced at the empty seat at the table.
I didn’t notice when he was here, but things are kind of boring without him.

Bjorn, son of Yandel, leader of Team Apple Narak and the barbarian warrior who served as the team’s tank. If he were here, they would be engaged in a war of attrition on the distribution ratio by now. The conversation would progress something like this:

“You should get 40 percent of the Manticore essence because it’s special loot? What strange math. Maybe if we had won the dice roll that day, but I got this from the dwarf, so it’s only fair to distribute it evenly.”
“Then what about the twenty million stones we received as a labor fee?”
“You’ll definitely get back the cost of the test tube. But 40 percent of the labor fee? I recall the distribution agreement for special loot had no clause for labor fees?”
As always, she would laugh and offer a new compromise. At the time, she thought it was all just for her profit, but maybe that wasn’t necessarily the case.
“Aruru, what arrre you thinking about?”
“It’s nothing.” Raven brushed off her thoughts and ended the meeting. “If no one is urgently in need of money, I’ll hold on to this until Mr. Yandel gets back.”
“Okay. Sure. Ainar can just borrrow money from me.”
“Again? I have to borrow money again!?”
“You have a lot to pay back, anyway. Taking the money in advance will only make the math morrre complicated for Aruru. So just wait until then. Okay?”
“Okay!”
“Hmm, it was twenty days, right? It’s a little over two weeks left now.”

For some reason, Raven felt a strange emotion. She was the one who had suggested it, but was it normal to agree that one person should hold onto goods worth over one hundred million stones this easily? Normally, no. Like the wizard she was, Raven couldn’t resist asking. “Aren’t you all worried? I said I would hold onto it.”
“Hmm?”
“Worry? Why would we do such a thing?”
They reacted like she was asking something bizarre. That made her feel even more strange. It wasn’t a bad feeling at all, but also hard to define with words.
Is this why that guy used the Awakening combo?

When she first heard that story from Bjorn, she thought the man he was talking about had been too naive. That was because a wizard from the Magic Tower would never do such a thing. But now, she could sort of understand his decision. Not completely, but maybe 1 percent.
“Anyway, that’s it for today’s agenda.”
After the point of the meeting was over, they ate together and chatted about various things. Naturally, most of the conversation centered around their absent leader.
“Aruru, what kind of place is Bifrrron?”
“...A sinister place. Even virtuous people turn vile there.”
“That’s what poverty and hunger will do to someone.”
“Mr. Urikfried, have you experienced them?”
“...Three years into my career, there was an incident where I lost all my equipment. I just barely managed to save my money back up by living on stone bread alone. I only narrowly paid my taxes too.”
The atmosphere got a little heavier. Missha spoke cautiously. “He should be fine, rrright? Bjorn?”
“What are you worried about, Miss Karlstein? He’s strong and has money. What issues would he have? He’s probably on vacation mode right now.”
“Mm... I hope so...”
Raven chuckled and shook her head. What could you say to a woman in love to console her in a situation like this? Missha seemed extremely cute to her at that moment.
She’s a year older than me...
For some reason, she was even envious.
Will I ever make that face about someone?

It wasn’t easy to imagine it now. Missha turned her head, embarrassed about being stared at, and pinched innocent Ainar’s side. “Ainarrr, stop eating meat and say something. Aren’t you worrried about Bjorn?”
“...Huh? Bjorn? Why would I worry about Bjorn? Bjorn is a great warrior! Without the law, he’ll live a better life!” It was a truly barbarian-like answer.

Normally this was the time when everyone would shake their heads in disapproval, but on an unspoken agreement, everyone kept their mouths shut. The reason was simple. It really seemed like he would. This was the same man who skillfully evaded the law and did as he liked, after all.
I shouted louder than ever, “Behelaaah!”

Currently, I was on the terrace on the fourth floor of District Fourteen’s old administrative office. A total of 514 subordinates stood in a line at ground level, and there was only one thing these guys had to do right now. Since I had made the first shout, their task was to shout back.
“Behela!”

These were the fruits of my labor three days into my stay here. I had become the boss of the Western Alliance, which occupied the western sector of Bifron. It wasn’t hard to pull off. Following the natural order, strength became authority in a lawless land like this. By which I meant I crashed their camp and destroyed everything.
“Too quiet!”
“Behelaaah!”
“Louder!”
“B-Behelaaah!”

Now that I had subordinates, I taught them the barbarian battle cry, which wasn’t quite there yet. I supposed it was because there was not a single barbarian among all these people. It would take some time for me to be satisfied. If someone asked the basic question of why I was even teaching them this, I only had one answer to give: I was a K-Barbarian with a humanitarian spirit. Of course good things should be shared.
“Behelaaah!”
It still didn’t meet my standards so I tightened my grip on my mace. In response, the cry grew louder.
Okay, that’s good enough.
“That’s it for today! Go have fun! Oh, but don’t do anything that harms others!”
“Yes sir!”

Finishing off our first-ever morning gathering, I dismissed my subordinates. Quite a few of them were on crutches because of broken legs, but they were able to leave the premises safely with the help of their colleagues. Now, it was time for me to start my morning too.
“Your tea is ready.”

Upon entering the room, a man with a jellyfish haircut and a giant bald spot on the top of his head bowed and served me brunch. This guy had been the boss of the Western Alliance until yesterday. He was suffering from severe circular hair loss so he normally wore a wig, but I told him to stop wearing it from now on. A subordinate shouldn’t hide anything from his boss, right?
“Tea and bread, huh?” Seeing the breakfast on the table, I couldn’t help but sigh. “Are you joking? Bring me wine and meat.”
“Sorry? Ah, yes! S-Sorry. I didn’t know what you would want, so—”
“It’s because you eat things like this for breakfast that your hair is already falling out.”
“Th-this is because of the witch’s poison!”
Yeah, right. If that were really the case, everyone here would be bald.
“Don’t make embarrassing excuses.”

After a brief wait, crispy grilled meat was set on the table. As usual, I just ate it with my bare hands. Having thick skin on my hands and high Flame Resistance on top of that, this much was no problem.
“You, what was your name? I don’t remember.”
“Because you didn’t ask—” Was this treason? Just as that thought was about to enter my mind, he realized his mistake and quickly rectified his statement. “Jingkasar Feljain.”
“That’s unusual. Where does it come from?”
“It comes from the south-central region.”

Oh, so his ancestors were desert people. No wonder his skin was so dark. “Hmm.” I studied him for a moment and contemplated this. Jingkasar Feljain? That was too much work to pronounce. It should be shortened for practical reasons. Okay, since he was Mr. Jing... “Jingjing. Yes, Jingjing sounds good.”
“...Pardon?”
“From now on, I will call you Jingjing.”
The reply only came several moments later. “...Okay.”
“Okay, boss.”
“Okay, boss...” Jingjing didn’t seem to like his new name at all, but what was he gonna do about it?
If you don’t like it, you should’ve won, or supervised your subordinates better so they didn’t start a fight with me.
“Water.”
“Sorry?”
“Water.”
“Ah, yes!”

After the meal, I swallowed the antidote the knight had given me with water. I was uneasy about it since I didn’t know what it was made of, but since Raven guaranteed it was safe, I was sure it was fine.
The idea of not taking it makes me more uneasy.

Bifron was a district where the protective magic circle was damaged. The witch’s poison that had driven the world to its end was leaking in even at this moment, and all the residents here were being exposed to it. The witch’s poison was easy to think of as radiation, but since this was a fantasy world, it had one peculiar trait.
It doesn’t affect you until the age of fifteen. After that, the probability of it affecting you increases depending on the length of exposure.

To explain it in game-like terms, Bifron was a place covered with probability-type terrain that was capable of causing instant death. For adults, the life expectancy following deportation was eight or nine years, and that was only because the protective magic circle was still half-working. If they left the castle walls, they would die within the day.
Well, no one has ever gone outside, though.
The world outside the city was also unknown to me. Even in the game, it had been completely blocked off by the system.
“I’m full. Let’s go on a walk.”
“...I will accompany you.”

I took Jingjing for a walk and, while walking aimlessly in one direction, asked some questions I’d been curious about. As he was once the head of an organization, he was more knowledgeable than the kid who had guided me on the first day and even answered my weird questions with sincerity. He was devoting his whole soul to my boss act.
“Ask me anything you want to know. Jingkasar Feljain will answer them all.”

Well, his ulterior motive was too obvious. He probably figured he just had to endure this for twenty days, after which I’d be gone. Making any attempt to stab me in the back was sure to get him killed.
Should I be thanking that kid?

Of course I hadn’t planned to get exiled to Bifron or take over the Western Alliance, but it wasn’t like I didn’t have a plan, either. Whether I liked it or not, I would be staying here for twenty days. I figured that there would be less hassle if I established a home base here. There was also something I now wanted to check out. Well, I couldn’t say I wasn’t bored, either.
“But boss, how far are we going? We’re already in the eastern territory.”
“Just follow me.”
Once our morning walk hit the two-hour mark, Jingjing started to get curious. “But any further and it’s just the castle wall...”
“That is our destination.”
An empty castle wall? Why? The question clearly crossed his mind, but Jingjing did not ask. Within a day, he had learned how to talk to me.
Step.
We arrived at a street near the castle wall. I got up on a rooftop that looked to be higher than the rest and studied the wall.
It’s the same here too.
As in the other districts, there were soldiers standing guard on the wall. I’d always wondered this: why were the soldiers watching this side instead of the outside?
I asked Jingjing, but received the following answer: “I’m not sure. I guess it’s in case someone tries to go outside.”
To be honest, I once thought the same. That was what everyone else believed too.
But is that necessary in Bifron?

From the royal family’s perspective, it would be better for these people to disappear anyway. Moreover, if these people died from the witch’s poison while trying to climb over the wall, it would only help solidify the legitimacy of the monarchy.
It’s so strange.

This was a contradiction I had noticed the moment I arrived here. Bifron’s protective magic circle was broken, which was why even the sentries on the castle walls had to be fed an antidote. Yet they were wasting their resources to position sentries here?
There’s something here.

That was my intuition, the same intuition that had allowed me to discover countless hidden features in the past. But no matter how long I stared up at the castle walls and sifted through my thoughts, the answer did not come to me. I did have a plausible hypothesis, but there was still insufficient evidence to support it.
“Let’s head back. I’m hungry.”
“Yes, boss.”
Soon, I took my eyes off the wall and turned around. Just then, a group of dozens gathering in the street below caught my eye.

“Those Eastern bastards. Looks like they heard you were here. What will you do?” Although he posed it as a question, Jingjing’s eyes showed just how eager he was for me to crush them just like I did his group. Too easy to read.
“It’s fine. Guide me back to our territory. It’s best not to run into th—” Just as I was about to walk away, I froze. There was a familiar face among the Eastern bastards.
Amelia Rainwales?
What was she doing here?

chapters.title: Chapter 194: Bifron (4)
paragraphs: Including today, I had run into her a total of four times: once in the Land of the Dead, once under the sewers, and once by chance at my inn after Noark was sealed off. At this point, we were strictly past the point of coincidence. Therefore, it was time to alter my approach toward this woman.
“...Aren’t you going?”
“Nah, I changed my mind.”

As the saying goes, knowledge was power. I may have tried to shake off my curiosity up to this point to avoid getting entangled with this woman, but we had already ended up learning each other’s names.
“...I’m not a human woman. Amelia Rainwales.”
Avoidance was no longer an option.
I need to find out now who the hell this woman really is.

If someone kept hanging around near your house, of course you should find out what kind of person they were. Whether they should be reported to the police or were scary enough that you should abandon your house and bounce... It was only once you had that information that could you respond appropriately.

“Jingkasar Feljain!” After waiting for a while, the door to the rooftop flew open. The person who came in was a bald man wearing a black blindfold. It looked like this guy was the leader of the Eastern group. “You dare enter our territory without a word? I’m sure you came prep—wait, what happened to your hair...?” Baldy, who had barged in with vigor, didn’t finish his sentence. Apparently Jingjing’s jellyfish cut was quite a shock to him. “...It was a wig?”
Jingjing did not respond, instead dropping his head. An awkward silence fell.

It seemed there was too much built-up resentment between them for sympathy, though. The confrontation resumed a moment later. “Y-You think I’ll take pity on you for that? As of today, I will end my wretched rivalry with you!”

“Pft, puhahaha! You think a loser like you who’s never even been in the labyrinth can defeat me just because you have more numbers? A rank-six adventurer like me?” Jingjing followed up Baldy’s declaration with exaggerated laughter and confidence.
In reality, he wasn’t even rank six. When I interrogated him about it earlier on account of him being so weak, Jingjing confessed that he was actually rank seven.
There’s no way a guy like that could be this relaxed against a group of dozens. Is he confident because I’m here?
That was kind of funny, but Baldy was serious. “Yes, I know you used to be a rank-six adventurer. But that’s why I brought someone impressive with me. Make way, kids!”
When Baldy said that, the dozens of thugs behind him stepped aside and revealed a woman: Amelia Rainwales, an eighth-floor adventurer from Noark.
“Barbarian? Why are you...?” Her annoyed expression as she appeared in the middle of the group of men turned into a frown when she spotted me. It was kind of satisfying.
You don’t know how surprised I was to see you too.
“That’s my line. Why on earth are you here?”

Amelia ignored my question as she tried to get her thoughts in order, and Baldy looked back and forth between us and cautiously opened his mouth. “...Do you know that barbarian?” He must have been worried that she seemed to know me since he had placed all his faith in this woman.

“Quiet.” When Amelia muttered curtly, Baldy flinched and clammed up. About three seconds passed. “Bjorn Yandel, hand over the man next to you.” Seemingly finished sorting herself out, Amelia suddenly made a request.
Of course, there was no way I would agree to that. “This guy is my subordinate.” Barbarians did not abandon their subordinates. At least not if there was no reason to do so.
“...Boss!” When I answered immediately without a moment’s thought, Jingjing looked moved.
On the other hand, Amelia didn’t seem to follow. “Subordinate?” She looked like she didn’t understand why a rising star in the adventuring industry was here, acting as a gang leader.
“I have my reasons,” I said shortly.

Amelia nodded coolly. “I see.” You’d think she would ask what those reasons were, but this was just how she was. “Then I’ll take him by force.” When the negotiations fell through, Amelia immediately took out a dagger and got into an offensive stance. Did she think she was a barbarian or something?
I quickly continued. “Wait, let’s talk first.”
“Talk?”
“Yes.”

Things were different from when we met at the inn. I had no teammates to help me and Bifron was a lawless land. Talking it out was best. I didn’t have the character stats to stop an aura yet. And if your body was weak, your mind was bound to suffer.
“Interesting. I didn’t think you would be the one to try talking it out first. Are you planning an ambush?”

“Ambush? I don’t do anything cowardly like that.” I didn’t hide that this was insulting to me. Of course, I may have thrown my mace at her mid-conversation in the sewer, but I doubled down. My memory of that time had been erased—at least as far as she knew.

“...That’s almost laughable.” She couldn’t argue with me over it, though, and she moved on without a hint of frustration. Her body was still preparing for an ambush. Was she finally recognizing me as a worthy adversary?
“First, take away the men.”
“Fine.”
An agreement was made and, when given a look, Baldy took the thugs back down. Next was Jingjing’s turn. “Um...”
“Don’t worry. I won’t abandon you.”
“Yes, boss!” He seemed anxious, but he still trusted me and headed downstairs. Before long, it was just the two of us on the rooftop. Thus, it was time to have a heart-to-heart.
“Amelia Rainwales. What are you doing here?”
“Why should I answer that?”
“It’s funny for adults to get involved in a children’s fight.”
“...Didn’t you just turn twenty?”
Come on now, details weren’t important here. I was sure Jingjing and Baldy were older in terms of age, but in this industry, the strong were the ones with seniority.
“Anyway, your answer?”
Amelia thought it over for a moment before opening her mouth. “You first. Why the hell are you in Bifron?”
“I was arrested for using a special ability in the city. I thought it would end with a fine, but they told me to come live here for twenty days. Today is the third day.”
“And the subordinate?”
“He tried to mug me, so I beat him up in return and took over his gang.”
Amelia smirked. “You really do whatever you want, don’t you?” Her tone wasn’t tinted with sarcasm. Instead, there was a hint of envy.
“Your turn. Why did you come here?” I had already asked the same question several times.
Finally, Amelia gave me a brief summary of her story. “I’m looking for an adventurer who might be here. In return for their help, I agreed to help them with something.”
“I see.” The situation roughly made sense now. I had been wondering why she would make a deal with guys so weak.
She probably wants to handle this quietly. A commotion like the one I made will inevitably leak outside.
This might go more smoothly than I expected.
“I’m telling you just in case, but I’m not here to break my promise.”
Huh?
When I tilted my head, Amelia continued to offer up what sounded almost like an excuse. “I... didn’t think I’d run into you here.”
Oh, that—her promise never to come find me again. I never dreamed she would care about that in a situation like this, and before I even thought to. Did she have some sort of obsession with promises?
“Don’t worry. I didn’t think you broke your promise.”
“I see...”
Now that I had a grasp of the situation, I got straight to the point. “Anyway, I’m glad. If that’s the case, we have no reason to fight.”
“You mean you’ll give him up?”
“No, there is no need. Aren’t you in need of subordinates? I will lend you my men.”
“I heard the Western Alliance has the least authority here.”
“You’re quicker than I thought.”
“Because it’s already been over ten days since I got here.”
I nodded. “I see.”
As she said, the Western Alliance was a small elite, although they were too weak to be called elites. But at the very least, they’d be better at tracking someone down.

“Never mind the small number.” This wasn’t a problem. Rather, I almost couldn’t understand why she hadn’t thought to do something so simple. Not enough subordinates? Why worry about something like that? “Because starting today, the eastern sector is also my territory.”
Subordinates just had to be copy-pasted.

I had wondered if she was the inflexible type considering how much value she placed on promises, but she was surprisingly similar to me in this sense. That was to say, Amelia was an efficiency freak too. “That’s not a bad idea.”
“You mean you agree?”
“Before we get to that, what do you have to gain from helping me?”
“...Do me a favor sometime.”
“Then I refuse. For some reason, I get the feeling you’ll ask me for something I won’t be able to pull off.”
Welp, that didn’t work. Fine, no matter. The favor wasn’t the important thing here. “Then consider it charity. It’s better than wasting my energy fighting you.”
I guess that seemed plausible enough, as only then did she agree to the deal. I headed down to the first floor.
“W-What happened to that woman?”

“You forgot to add ‘boss.’” I kicked Baldy, who was standing in an awkward confrontation with Jingjing, in the stomach. It was customary to cut your opponent off at the pass when you were taking a promotion.
“Urgh!” Kicked right in the stomach, Baldy dropped to the floor on the spot. “You bastard!”

With this as the trigger, the Eastern guys filling the entire first floor charged at me. Swords, hammers, spears, skewers—thugs jabbed at me mercilessly with the weapons in their hands. There was no need to stop them.
“W-Why is this...”

Even though they aimed at exposed skin, the weapons bounced off without even leaving a cut. That was only natural. These were guys who had come out in the dozens to catch one Jingjing, and they thought attacks like that would work against my current Physical Resistance?
“Are you done?”
“Behelaaah!”

It didn’t take long. After implanting fear in them with Wild Outburst and wrecking a few guys as an example, the battle was over. Dozens of men didn’t even dare to run away from the overwhelming difference in power.
I grabbed Baldy by the collar and lifted him up. “What is your name?”
“P-Philippe Lazere!”
“From now on, I will call you Baldy.”
Okay, that concluded the introductions. Just as I was about to move on to the next step, Baldy asked blankly, “W-Who are you?”
I corrected the error there. “Boss.”
“What...?”
“I’m your boss.”
“Boss...?” Baldy’s confused gaze shifted to Jingjing, who was hiding in the corner. Finally, he understood the situation.
Yeah, that’s how I beat him too.
“You came right on time,” I said to Amelia when I noticed her. “Give me a potion.”
“...Potion?”
“My subordinate is injured. I need to treat him.”
Amelia eyed me like she was looking at a strange creature but then took out a potion bottle and handed it to me.
Chhhhhh.
Baldy screamed and wriggled as I fed him the potion. After a moment’s wait, he regained consciousness in a cold sweat. He still appeared to be dreaming.
Enough sticks, time for the carrots. “I will be leaving in seventeen days.”
“Sorry?”

“I’m just saying.” To put it simply, just consider this bad luck you’ll have to deal with until then. Afterward, I ordered Baldy and Jingjing to go gather everyone. “Since it’s a lot of people, Dimension Square will do. Is five hours enough?”
“Th-that’s nowhere near enough—”
“Yes, boss! That’s enough!” Jingjing forcibly cut Baldy off. That was experience for you. Answering “yes” to anything was a subordinate’s greatest virtue, especially if your boss was a barbarian.
“Okay then, get on it.”
As time was running out, my subordinates quickly rushed off to carry out their missions. It was a rather satisfying sight.
Is this why everyone is so obsessed with power?
I smiled and shifted my gaze to Amelia, keeping my tone deliberately nonchalant. “Now, tell me. Who are you looking for?”
I’d been curious since earlier. This woman was from Noark, after all. She might have been looking for someone not of her own volition, but on Noark’s orders.
Someone the underground city has sent her to look for at a time like this...

This could be an important clue. Any information others didn’t know about was always helpful. Even if the information was irrelevant to me, I could use it to seem important at the Round Table. Either way, I had nothing to lose.
But despite what I had been hoping, Amelia only answered with the individual’s description. “Looks like an elderly person but could be in disguise.”
“You mean they can’t be identified by appearance? Then how will you find them?”
“The tattoo on their back. I heard it is impossible to hide it with any spell.”
Hmm, so we have to check every single person’s back?
“Any other useful traits?”
“No.”
“You don’t even know their name?”
“...It’s useless information since they’ll be using a pseudonym, anyway.”
“You never know. Let’s hear it.”
When I prodded, Amelia hesitated for a moment. But she must have determined that I wouldn’t know it, anyway, because she soon answered with a name. “Auril Gavis.”
What?
“Auril Gavis?!”
“...Do you know him?”
“No, I just pretended to know.” I improvised a response and put on a poker face.
Thump-thump-thump!
But despite my calm outward appearance, my heart pounded like crazy. That was a given. Auril Gavis? That was the name of the author of the Complete Books series—and the creator of Dungeon and Stone!

chapters.title: Chapter 195: Bifron (5)
paragraphs: Auril Gavis was a figure from at least 150 years ago. When I once asked Raven to discern the age of a scrap of paper I gave her from the Complete Book of Rifts, that was the time period she came up with, which was why this was even more surprising.
That bastard is still alive?

I thought for sure he was dead. Of course, now I had no idea why I thought that. This was the creator of Dungeon and Stone, and most likely the culprit who had brought countless players including myself to this world. This place was literally a fantasy world—the word fantasy was in the name itself. Of course there was a chance that he was alive. Those of the Dragon Tribe even lived for hundreds of years.
Thump!
When I realized this, my heart began to race. It was a different emotion from the first time I heard that name, a palpitation full of anticipation rather than shock.
Thump!

If that son of a bitch really was alive and if I could just find him, there might be a way to return to my original world. A clue to guide me on my murky road home was dangling right in front of my eyes.
...Calm down.
I reined in my beating heart and found my cool. I could overinflate my expectations and run hopeful scenarios in my head before bed later. Right now, I needed to pay attention.

“Barbarian, you really are unique,” Amelia said enigmatically, staring at me. For a moment, I thought she might have seen through my lie. “Or should I say brazen? To think you can joke around in front of me after everything... Aren’t you afraid of me?”

Now that I was looking closer, it seemed she was just fascinated. Or she felt uncomfortable about the fact that we were having this conversation, having never met someone like me before. The important thing was it was a nice save. This was why people needed to live with one of their screws a little loose at all times so that no matter what they did, no one would look at them strangely.
“What are you talking about, human woman? I am Bjorn, son of Yandel, not Barbarian.”
“Okay, Bjorn Yandel,” Amelia snickered. To me, that felt like a sign that I could relax.
To that end, my next question was, “Is Aruil Gavis a man or a woman?”
“He’s a man.”
“Could he be disguised as a woman?”
“I don’t think so. The records show he was a man with a severe male supremacy complex.”
“So he wouldn’t do something like that even if he had the ability to. Then what about a child? Could he disguise himself as one?”
“...He wouldn’t turn himself too young.”
“Your rationale?”
“Because he was a person who put a lot of value into appearance.”

I nodded and decided to prod a bit. “I see. But why are you looking for him?” This was a follow-up question to the easy questions that she would have no choice but to answer. I read this in a book somewhere. Posing questions in this order increased your chances of getting an answer, although it was unclear whether it worked in practice. Still, there was no reason not to try.
I got an answer a moment later. “...It is a personal matter.”

Modern people often used that excuse to shut a conversation down when they didn’t want to answer or wanted to avoid forming a relationship. It was also used to dodge a question. But since Amelia was the one saying it, it was hard to tell.
“That’s not for you to know.”
“Why should I answer that?”

She sometimes refused to answer like that, but she had never lied or tried to cover anything up. As a result, I started to wonder if perhaps this really wasn’t an order from Noark, but truly a personal matter.
Well, that’s not important right now.
If Auril Gavis really was in Bifron, I had to find him. I had a mountain of questions I wanted to ask.

After our conversation, Amelia said she would drop by the city and return at night. She had business there in the afternoon. At first, that seemed so natural that I nodded without thinking. “Wait a minute, how are you going to get into the city? Is there a way to avoid the guards?”
“There is a secret passage under the sewers.”
I would have regretted it if I didn’t stop her and ask. A secret passage leading to the city! “Can you teach me where that is too?”
“Hmm.”
“What are you thinking so hard about? You’re acting like it’s a tough request.”
“...Fine, I’ll tell you.”
When I reminded her that I was currently helping her search for Auril Gavis, she readily filled me in on the passage. She looked relieved to do so. Did that mean her debt was now paid?
Thanks to that, I learned something useful.

I had a ticket to Bifron that I could use whenever I wanted. Of course, I didn’t intend to use this during my exile. I was aware that I stood out in a crowd. If I ended up getting caught, it’d be a headache. The knight who brought me here had even warned me. He said I could do whatever I wanted except escape.
“Then, see you later.”
“Huh?”
“Didn’t you say you would come back later tonight?”
“Right, I did...”

To see the location of the secret passage for myself, I went with Amelia under the sewers and then said goodbye. Glancing at the time, I saw that it had already been three hours since I had made the order for everyone to gather. And so, asking for directions on the way, I headed to the rendezvous place, the Dimension Square that once would have been crowded with adventurers.
“Hey, do you know anything? Why did the boss call everyone all of a sudden? And what are those Western Alliance bastards doing here?”
“I am not ‘hey.’ I’m your boss.”
“What are you—”
“Talking back is not allowed.” I made my way through the crowd to the center.
On the way, members of the Western Alliance recognized and greeted me. “Salute!”
Yeah, this was more like it.
“The heck...?” The Western Alliance members knelt before me and the Eastern guys stood there with puzzled expressions. They at least had the sense to make way so it was easier to get to the center.
“Boss, the stage is over there.”
After reaching the center, I headed up to the podium with Jingjing’s assistance. Apparently, he prepared it in advance, thinking I might need it.
He’s good at his job.

Maybe it wouldn’t be a bad idea to use him as my butler outside. Now that I had the secret passage, it’d be a waste to only make use of him over here. Although it wouldn’t just end with a fine if I were caught. With those thoughts in mind, I was about to climb the podium when...
Crunch.
The stairs made of wooden planks snapped. These thin slabs of wood could not bear the weight of both me and my equipment. Unable to hide my devastation, I said, “Jingjing, how did this happen?”
“I’m sorry.”

An apology was made immediately without a word of excuse. That alleviated my mood a bit, but the maker of this podium was a barbarian hater. If not, they would have designed these stairs to be able to hold one. “This podium is dangerous.”
“Yes, boss. I will burn it straight away.”

Jingjing pulled out a torch and lit up the podium. When he poured a liquid I presumed to be oil on top of that, the flames soared and instantly covered the three-story structure. Now it looked like we were having a campfire or something.
Whooosh!
My heart warmed with the heat of the fire. Just a while ago I hadn’t had anyone on my side, but now? I had more than a thousand subordinates.
“So what will you do?”
“The inauguration ceremony will go on.”
“Inauguration ceremony... Yes, I see. That’s why you gathered everyone...”
“Isn’t that obvious?”
“I’m sorry.”
As a sign of forgiveness, I patted Jingjing on the shoulder and used Leap. My destination was the rooftop of a nearby four-story building.
Kwaaang!
A crack formed on the rooftop, but fortunately, it didn’t break. I was glad. If I had fallen through the roof after that cool jump, that would have been way too embarrassing.
So this is why they say the position makes the person.
I was trying to maintain my dignity without even realizing it.

“Ahem.” Anyway, as I headed toward the railing, I could see the tightly packed crowd filling the plaza, creating a spectacular view. Now it was finally time to start the inauguration ceremony. I began. “Behel—aaah!”
“Behel—aaah!” The Western Alliance members immediately chanted back. The Eastern guys just blinked blankly, as if wondering what kind of deranged sight they were witnessing.
I clicked my tongue. “Tsk.” There was still a lot left to teach.

After the inauguration ceremony to show off the face of their new boss was over, I called forth Jingjing and Baldy to give orders. “Check the backs of everyone in Bifron. And bring all the tattooed ones to me.”
Of course, this excluded women, along with children under the age of fourteen who didn’t have credentials yet. A total of thirty-seven suspects were dragged before me before the first day was over.
“This is not the tattoo.” When she returned that night, Amelia checked each one of them and shook her head.

Yeah, it couldn’t be this easy. To increase our efficiency, I berated the deputy leaders of the “Behel-a Alliance,” Jingjing and Baldy, and many more suspects were captured on the second and third days. Of course, the person we were looking for was once again not present.
Plus, while the quantity of suspects increased, the quality declined.
“It’s a birthmark, not a tattoo.”
“So he says. How did this happen?”
“I will fix this.”

Put simply, these guys were going to berate their subordinates to raise the efficiency too. And I guessed the berating worked because the tattoos started to look more like tattoos after that. Still, after another two days, we hadn’t made much more progress. It was ridiculous to think we’d be able to find Auril Gavis with such a simple and unimaginative method, anyway.
But what can I do? I have to try something. It’s not like there’s a better way.

Looking for a needle in the desert, if that needle would take me back home, was worth a shot. So, I continued my search. Of course, I changed my methodology a little. Not much, though—I just added a reward.
“Anyone who fails to meet their daily quota will receive mental training that night.”

You might wonder how this was a reward, but happiness was always relative. Put simply, being better off than others was a reward in itself. What, do you think cavemen weren’t happy just because they ate raw meat and slept naked in caves?

Three more long days went by. However, Auril Gavis showed no signs of appearing and I started to pack away my expectations too. I would be lying if I said I wasn’t disappointed since this was the first real clue I had about how to return, but the real reason I was helping Amelia was something else, so I decided to focus on that: none other than Amelia Rainwales herself. Who the hell was this woman? Using Auril Gavis as a point of contact, I gathered information from her every day. Surprisingly, she answered my questions thoroughly, although it was limited to information of little importance.
“I don’t eat food that contains wheat. It makes my skin itchy for some reason.”

Such information included the fact that she had a wheat allergy or that the only thing she did for fun was read. But while she answered those questions without trouble, she avoided questions like who the barbarian she was indebted to was.
“That you don’t need to know.”
“But I’m curious. For a woman like you to be hung up on him, he must have been a great warrior! Tell me what kind of person he was!”
“...If I had to describe him, he was a little like you.”

Although she uncharacteristically tossed in that bit at the end, the information wasn’t useful. We were both barbarians, after all. Of course, there was a resemblance. Anyway, our casual chitchat continued, and she lowered her guard a bit.
“Why do you plunder? To be honest, it doesn’t suit you at all.”
“It doesn’t?” Instead of getting angry at a question that could be a bit sensitive, Amelia answered with a question of her own.
I smoothly recited the lines I had prepared. “I have met many plunderers besides you since then. Thanks to that, I’ve become more certain. You are not the type to kill people for money.”
“...That’s laughable. What do you know about me?”
“Nothing. But at your level, I know there are many other ways for you to make money.”
Amelia was silent for a moment and briefly explained herself. “...I don’t normally do it.”
“What about back then?”
“Those guys... committed a sin deserving of death.”
“You mean it was a personal grudge?”

“Yes,” Amelia answered while staring out into space, lost in a memory. I was curious and wanted to delve deeper into the backstory there, but I couldn’t dig that far. Amelia had come to her senses. “Why am I even telling you this?”
“Don’t make a big deal out of it. We’re going our separate ways in a few days, anyway. There are things you can only tell strangers.”
“Things you only tell strangers, huh?” She pondered the words which seemed to leave an impression on her before she smirked and got up. “It’s late. I should go now.”
“Are you coming at the same time tomorrow?”
“Maybe.”

Amelia disappeared from sight, just as silently as she came. Was that it for today? I went out to the terrace to give my mind a bit of a break. The view at night in Bifron was completely different from the districts outside it, its streets and buildings buried in darkness without a single light to be seen.
Only a few days left now.

I sat blankly on a rocking chair on the terrace, staring out into the darkness as I got my thoughts in order. I wasn’t sure how long I spent out there, but after checking my watch, I headed to the bedroom. It was 11:57 p.m.—time to lie down for bed. It was going to take a long time for me to fall asleep, though.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
Hopefully, everyone had logged in today.

chapters.title: Chapter 196: Master Key (1)
paragraphs: As soon as I entered the community, I turned on my computer, checked the usual chat room, and froze.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 2 people are online.]
Why two people? Was there a new Korean around? Wait, but it didn’t make sense for a newbie to have found the chat room this quickly.
Click, click.
Dubious, I moved the mouse and double-clicked on the room’s name. Then, an unusual message popped up.
[Participation in this room is temporarily restricted. Remaining time: 9 minutes and 51 seconds.]

What was this, now? It was confusing at first but I soon managed to piece together what was happening. Restricting participation was one of the inherent privileges of the host who opened the chat room.
In other words, it means someone came to find Baekho as soon as the community opened, and Baekho locked the door to speak with them.
This was the most probable explanation. This person was likely an acquaintance of Baekho’s. If they had been strangers, he wouldn’t have locked the door but instead kicked them out.
An acquaintance of Baekho’s, huh?

It made me curious. Baekho was an old user who had taken the pill in the early days, which had the side effect of restricting his access to the community to one hour. He must have been in this community for ten years, easy, and would have many acquaintances. He was the one who gave me the invitation code to enter the Watchers of the Round Table in the first place.
But this person has to be someone who’s been around for as long as Baekho.
“Welp.”
I wished I could at least see the nicknames of the participants. Kind of disappointed, I watched the time tick down and before long, the number of participants dropped to one.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence – 1 person is online.]
When I checked, the participation ban was lifted as well. Had the person already left? With that question in mind, I entered the chat room.
“Are you the person from Mr. Lee’s home country?”
What the fuck was this? I hurriedly turned my head at the strange voice and came face to face with an unfamiliar Caucasian man. Wait, maybe not completely unfamiliar.
[Elfnunalove]

When I checked the nickname above the man’s head, my mind went momentarily blank. Surprisingly, I had met this person before. Back when I heard rumors of a dimensional collapse and was asking around about a wizard named Shernal Fergang, he had been one of the users who sold me information.
“Come to think of it, it’s all right. You seem to be a fan of theirs too.”

After watching him decline the twenty thousand GP I had offered as compensation, I realized that I really was a rookie here, and I grew determined to rise to the top as quickly as possible. But to think this guy was acquainted with Baekho...
Wait, but where is that guy?
I quickly came to my senses. This man was also sending strange looks at my nickname. “Hmm, we’ve met before, haven’t we?”
Okay, so you recognize me too.
Seeing as he was using a nickname as unpleasant as Elfnunalove, it seemed that my nickname, Elfnunna, was memorable to him.

“Yes. We meet again.” Something about this situation was making me uneasy, so I held my tongue. I had a lot I wanted to ask, but sometimes you could accidentally leak information of your own just by asking questions. For now, I waited for the man to speak first.
After a moment, Elfnunalove scratched his head, looking sheepish. “I’m sorry about this.”
“What do you mean?”
“I feel I have taken away the friend you haven’t seen in a while.”
“...Are you talking about Baekho?”
Elfnunalove nodded. “Yes. As you know, there aren’t many Koreans here. I know very well how important it is to have people from your hometown around.”

“I don’t understand. What do you mean by taken away?” This wasn’t my usual noob performance—this was genuine. I had no idea what he was talking about. Could it be that Baekho had had to leave the chat because of him? But, how? Surely the moderator of this chat room was Baekho?

As all sorts of questions ran through my head, the white man continued, “It’s just as I said. You won’t be able to meet up with Mr. Lee here from now on. I’ve been leaving him alone up to this point thinking he might serve as a key, but... Unfortunately, he made a big mistake.”
“What?”

“I was actually just going to leave, but I’m letting you know so you don’t waste your time waiting for him. Have a good day.” Before I could say anything, Elfnunalove left the chat room. I just stood there, staring blankly at the spot he was just standing.
Goddamn it. What the hell is going on?
Before long, I was left alone in the empty room.
Made a mistake? He can’t come here again?

My thoughts were all jumbled, but at times like these, it was important to calmly organize them. Who the hell was Elfnunalove? As I ran through the conversation I just had line by line, I quickly came to a conclusion.
It’s still just a hypothesis, but I’m pretty sure he’s one of Ghost Busters’ admins.

Like Soul Queen, whom I met when I entered for the first time, he must be someone who oversaw the newbies and managed this place so that the community didn’t become a mess. I couldn’t explain what had just happened any other way.
“Unfortunately, he made a big mistake.”

Elfnunalove wasn’t even the host, but he had still kicked Baekho out of the room. He must have been the one to restrict entry to begin with. At least on the bulletin board, admins had considerable authority. Only an admin could permanently boot someone from the community. In all likelihood, he wasn’t just an ordinary admin, but...
Hold on.
When my thoughts reached that point, I hurriedly returned to my own room. Then I quickly opened my inbox.
[Elfnunna’s transaction history has exceeded 50. EXP +50]
[Your member rank has been adjusted: Orc -> Troll]
[From: Ghost Master]

Ghost Master was the top administrator of Ghost Busters who was referred to as the Game Master or GM by users of the community and whose identity was unknown. I suddenly remembered a conversation I had had with Baekho.
“Do you know who the Game Master is here?”
“Ah, I don’t know that. In fact, I only found the pill after robbing the Ministry of Security’s headquarters in the early days.”
“Then they won’t know who you are, either?”
“They probably have an idea. I also have a guy I’ve been suspicious of...”
“Who?”
“There are three. Should I tell you all of them?”

Baekho had told me the names of three suspects then. They were all wizards and each was famous enough that everyone in the city knew their names. Since Baekho was the one doing the speculating, there was no way his theories were completely groundless.
The GM is a wizard.
This wasn’t 100 percent confirmed, but assuming that premise was true, I recalled the first time I met Elfnunalove.
“...Is it okay for you to just tell me all of this?”
“What does it matter? It’s not like I’m the master of that school.”
As I listened to him divulge the inside scoop on the Tarutein School, which had spread rumors about a potential dimensional collapse in the labyrinth, I thought this: This guy talks like a wizard.
I gulped nervously as the puzzle pieces I’d collected began to form a very distinct picture. This might have been a leap on my part, but if my speculations were correct, I may have just met the GM.
“Holy shit.”

A strange shudder ran through my body, but before long, I was back to normal. Even if Elfnunalove was the GM, that didn’t pose a serious problem for me. That nickname did bother me a bit, but at least it was a sign that he wasn’t hostile toward me. Even if my identity were revealed, he wouldn’t be coming for my throat or anything. Probably.
Okay, let’s erase that ASAP.

I went to the message board and deleted the comment I had left on my Canadian friend’s now-blurred post. It would be impossible to deduce my identity just with that, but just in case. While I was at it, I erased any and all of the other traces I had left here. Aside from some comments left on a funny post, there wasn’t much: that one post from when rumors of the dimensional collapse were going around, and another post I had made on the Exchange to gather information about Orcules after my battle with the Dragon Slayer.
Does this mean I can’t see Baekho anymore?

After I finished cleaning up my digital footprint, I thought of Baekho. I was kind of disappointed. Aside from the fact that I wouldn’t be obtaining valuable information through him anymore, to be honest, I had fun hanging out with him.
But what did he even do for the admin to come kick him out personally?
As of now, I had no way of learning the truth, but it wasn’t hard to speculate that it was closely related to the conquest of Noark. That had been the only big event as of late.
Type, type.

After that, I spent time wandering around the bulletin board, mostly just surfing the web. I checked to see if there were any posts left by Elfnunalove too, but there wasn’t a single one. The same went for Baekho.
I should refrain from posting too.
A true veteran stayed far away from the community and silently did his own thing. Taking this incident as a learning experience, I set in stone a new rule for using the community.

After browsing around for a long while, it was time to enter the Round Table. However, this time, I didn’t bother waiting until right before closing and just entered. With everything that had happened recently, I figured that I could obtain information from the small talk before the gathering too.
Everyone is here today, right?
Starting in the customization room as usual, I hurriedly donned the navy suit I always wore and put on the lion mask.
Creaaak.
After I finished getting dressed, the door opened on cue and I walked down the carpet to the Round Table.
It was Clown who greeted me first. “You came early this time, hehehe.”
Since he skipped last month, it had been two months since I’d heard that distinct laughter. I approached my usual seat and scanned everyone.
Crescent Moon, Deer, Fox.
Including Clown and me, there were a total of five people participating in this rally. Fox met my eyes before looking away and saying to everyone, “Anyway, Mr. Goblin is late today.”
“Hehe, maybe he’s dead. I heard the losses on the paladin side were significant.”
“...We should hope not.”
As expected, the main topic of conversation even before the official meeting was the conquest.
“I’m just amazed this many people came back alive. If there is a hell, it would have been that place. I participated without much thought and regretted that decision.”
“I agree. I never imagined Noark would be hiding so much power. When the conquest army was first formed, I felt like we could attack even the royal palace.”
“Hehe, yet everyone suffered a huge blow.”
“Clown, you speak as if this doesn’t pertain to you.”
“Of course it doesn’t. The number of people who die is irrelevant to me. Isn’t that right, Mr. Lion?”

“I’m not interested in the conquest.” I rested my chin on my hand like I was bored and just listened to the conversation with perked ears. The dark wizard of Noark, the priests of Karui, the inside scoop on a large clan that had suffered huge losses, other races, etcetera—information too lacking in scarcity to bring up during the official meeting continued to flow out under the guise of small talk.
Good thing I came early.
Hiding my satisfied smile, I was listening to them discuss the latest situation when Goblin appeared through the open door.
“Oh, Mr. Goblin!”
“So you are alive.”
“Oh, yes. It was really dangerous, though. God was truly on our side.” Goblin naturally brought up his god even though he wasn’t from this world.
Clown laughed mockingly. “What god? It’s obvious you were hiding in the back like the goblin you are, hehe.”
“Clown, why are you always so mean to me?”
“Because you’re too easy.”
Despite being openly mocked, Goblin simply sat back in his seat, letting out a hollow scoff.
He’s scared.

At first, I didn’t understand why Goblin was taking such a weak stance, but maybe it made sense. Goblin’s identity as a paladin had already been exposed. He could never openly make an enemy of Clown, who was clearly strong.
Boom!
Once Goblin sat down, the door clicked closed. That meant it was time to start the meeting.
“Lion, is your promise still valid?” Before we even decided on the order, Crescent Moon tossed me a question.

There was context missing but I understood it well enough. He must have been talking about my promise to provide information on the Stone of Revival in exchange for interesting information. When I nodded, Crescent Moon’s expression grew determined.
“Hehe, looks like you’re really confident this time.”
“Just desperate. I need that item more than anything.” His answer was accompanied by an obvious resolve to learn more about the Stone of Revival at any cost.
“Then who will start?”
Just before the game of wits to decide who would start could begin, the door, which had been firmly closed, opened.
Creak.
This had never happened before.
The heck? Another member? I thought no one could enter the meeting once it started. Surely that must have been the rule?
Given how everyone else also looked confused, it seemed I was not the only one who found this strange.
Boom.

Soon, the thick wooden door flung open, and a figure appeared through it. It was a man wearing a featureless white mask. The only skin exposed on his hands was wrinkly. “Haha, this place hasn’t changed a bit.” An old man’s voice came from behind the mask.
For a moment, silence filled the hall. The first one to come to their senses was Fox. “Master...?”
From that single, murmured comment, it hit me. This was the Master, the creator of the Watchers of the Round Table.
“That’s a mask I haven’t seen before. Who are you?”
At his question, Fox, who had been baited by me many times, tilted her head. “Didn’t you invite him, Master? I’m certain that’s what he said...”
Strictly speaking, I didn’t say that. I had just cleverly avoided answering so as to create a misunderstanding. But that excuse wouldn’t work here.
Goddamn it. What should I do?
One wrong move and my act would be exposed.

chapters.title: Chapter 197: Master Key (2)
paragraphs: The Watchers of the Round Table was a secret community created for the exchange of high quality information. When I first came to this place, the existing members were curious about my relationship to the Master. The reason for this was simple. The Master, who had been recruiting members through the private messaging function, had apparently disappeared one year ago. The members believed they could hear recent news about the Master from me, and once my character concept for Lion was established, our supposed acquaintanceship was assumed to be fact. For my part, I had consistently answered any related questions with “no comment.”
“I refuse to answer.”
If I said I knew him, I was worried about possible repercussions in the future. If I said I didn’t, that wouldn’t match my mysterious vibe. But had I gotten greedy without realizing it?
“Could it be that you also know where the Master is?”

At our second gathering, I had shrugged at Fox’s question, as if to say, Bring me something interesting, then I’ll tell you. I had rested my chin on my hand and acted utterly relaxed, like some sort of all-powerful being. Everything I did in that moment had clearly been intended to cause a misunderstanding.
“Didn’t you invite him, Master? I’m certain that’s what he said...”
And I seemed to have pulled it off because Fox sounded very confused. The other masks also seemed to be wondering what was going on.

“Hmm, I invited him?” The Master touched his chin, clearly trying and failing to remember doing that. As a result, the other masks turned to me with eyes full of questions and curiosity about my identity.
“If not for Master, how did this guy get in here?” Fox murmured.
Goblin presented a theory. “Perhaps he used the invitation code from last time.”
Clown refuted it. “Idiot. Don’t you know that the invitation code expires after just one month, so you can’t reuse it?”
“Is that true, Master?”
“What Clown said is true.”
“Then...” When their master agreed, the looks directed toward me turned sharper. “Mr. Lion, why did you deceive me into thinking that you were acquainted with Master?” Fox asked in a cautious tone.

I held my breath for a moment and closed my eyes. It would be a lie to say I wasn’t taken aback by the Master’s sudden appearance, but losing my composure would ruin everything. I quickly decided on the stance I would take. “I didn’t deceive you.” After all, I never claimed that I knew him with my own lips. They just misunderstood. If I pushed forward with this approach, they wouldn’t be able to say anything against me.
Well. They’ll sense that something is off, but...
From my murderous energy to tidbits of information, hadn’t I offered them enough? They wouldn’t be able to reach the truth—that I was a cybercriminal—with this, anyway.
“You didn’t?”
Opt for the most shameless method. That was what this Lion character was about. “It’s just as I said. Is there something wrong with your ears?”
“N-No... it’s not that...” I didn’t release any murderous energy, yet Fox was clearly spooked.
I chuckled out loud and was about to point out that I didn’t say anything and that they were the ones who had misunderstood.
But just then, the Master looked at me and spoke. “Everyone, stop. I don’t know the details of what conspired here, but he did not deceive anyone.”
Huh?
“I see it now. Who you are.”
For an instant, my heart skipped a beat. Of course, the sensation was only fleeting. He knew who I was? That was impossible. Even the Master was just the host of a private chat room, so how could he?
“Haha, although, I thought you would choose a tiger.”
That laughter shut me up, not because he had hit the nail on the head, but because I had no idea what he was talking about. I just chose silence. Not talking would get me at least halfway there.
“Or a soldier.”
That interpretation was not wrong.
A soldier, huh?

I now saw who this old man was mistaking me for—Sergeant Lee. A literal sergeant, and the nickname of the unfortunate player who had been dragged into this world on the day of his discharge from the military, Baekho Lee.
“Haha, there’s no use pretending otherwise. You are the only one who received a non-expiring code from me.”

Come to think of it, it made perfect sense for the Master to reach this flawed conclusion because Baekho had transferred the code to me. With a mask on, there was no way he could tell me and Baekho apart.
Should I consider this a good thing?
I wasn’t sure yet. The key issue was how close Baekho and the Master were.
“I never thought you would come here. When I first came to see you, you mocked me and said what I was doing was pathetic. I am a little curious. Why did you change your mind?”
I easily came to a conclusion.
They weren’t that close.
Mocked? Fine. There were plenty of bickering friendships in the world.
“Oh, I didn’t tell you. The pill I took was a prototype, so I can only stay here for an hour.”

However, Baekho could only log into the community for one hour. Therefore, it would be impossible for him to participate in this gathering in the first place considering the entry time was between 3:00 and 3:10 in the morning. And yet this guy didn’t know this, something Baekho had told me the first day he met me?
I can see the basic picture.
The Master didn’t know much about Baekho. Thus, it was possible for me to pretend to be him.
“Although I was the one to suggest it first, there really is nothing for you to gain by participating.”
Clown grumbled at that. “Hehe, nothing to gain? Master, aren’t you looking down on us too much?”
“Oh, sorry if I offended you. But this fellow is an incredible man, you see.”
“Hmm, is that so?” Clown’s eyes began to glow as the Master praised me.

I quickly scanned the other masks. Their gazes weren’t much different from Clown’s, filled only with surprise—perhaps even more than when I told them high-quality information, like the Stone of Revival’s existence.
“I’ve never seen Master recognize someone like that...”

“I didn’t think he was that influential,” Crescent Moon exclaimed while Deer looked somewhat angry. Fox flinched as soon as we met eyes and dropped her head. It seemed she felt guilty about suspecting me earlier.
What should I do?

As I watched the situation unfold, my apprehension mounted. There was a saying that said that a crisis was an opportunity, as could be seen by the change in everyone’s looks already. If I pulled off pretending to be Baekho, it would be a big help to my act in the future.
More importantly, I think I can learn about Baekho through this old man.
The returns were obvious. But what about the risks?
There really aren’t any.

Come to think of it, if this didn’t work out, I could just reveal that I was Baekho’s friend. After all, birds of a feather flocked together. While the Master had mentioned that Baekho was a big man, as his friend, I would seem like I was on a somewhat similar level.
Okay, just do it.
Making my decision, I broke my long silence and spoke to the Master first. “What should I call you here, sir?”
“Hmm?”
“I can’t call you what I usually do.”
“Why not? Just call me Gramps like back then. And get rid of that honorific too.”
“Okay, Gramps.” Even as I smoothly changed my demeanor, my head was spinning.
I almost screwed it up from the start.
To think they spoke so casually to each other. Thanks to that, I realized one more thing. Baekho was a proud Korean Confucian, but he had spoken so casually to an older person?
Forget not being close, looks like they didn’t get along.
I had a sense of how to approach this guy now, and so, I made up for my earlier misstep. “You have strange tastes. I was trying to help you save face,” I said like I really didn’t get him.

I didn’t know if I properly pulled it off, but the Master let out an eager laugh. “Haha! Yes, that’s more like you. Anyway, let’s end this conversation here. It’s nice to see you after so long, but I don’t have much time.”
“Master, what do you mean?” Fox asked.
“Due to certain circumstances, I don’t have much time in here.”
“Pardon? What on earth has happened to you since—”

“Enough,” The Master cut her off and dismissed the question. “I understand that Miss Fox would like to ask me many questions, probably to do with why I disappeared without a word and what I mean by running out of time. But I cannot tell you those things.”
“Are you really in such a rush?”
“No, it has nothing to do with time.”
When the Master firmly put his foot down, Fox did not push further. Instead, she asked one last question. “Then... when will you return?”
“Well, I don’t know about that. But I’ll come back in a year. If there is something I need to inform you of before then, I may come sooner.”
“Hehe, that means you came to tell us something urgent today, Master?”
“Clown, it is as you say.” At the Master’s declaration, all the attention that had been focused on me turned to him again. This was perfect for me—even the contents of his speech itself.
Come back in a year...
To put it simply, that meant that I didn’t have to worry about my lies being exposed at every gathering. But my curiosity outweighed my relief.
I don’t think he’s lying that he doesn’t have time... What kind of situation is he in? And what’s this urgent news?

With many questions buzzing through my mind, I focused on listening and watching the Master. It wasn’t just me—all the masked members of the Round Table did the same. As a result, a foreign silence fell.

“Hey, don’t be so nervous. Rather, it is safe to say that this is good news.” The Master waved his hands as if to dispel the tension in the air and slowly parted his lips. “In two years, a binding spell capable of binding up to six people will be created. That means the number of keys to open the Gate of the Abyss will increase to six!”
The silence turned oppressive. The members glanced at each other awkwardly and said nothing.
The Master tilted his head at this. “Huh, why do you all look like that? I thought you would be more surprised...”
That’s because you’re one step behind.
A six-person binding spell was information valuable enough to shake up the entire city for at least several months. However...

“...You revealed this news already? Eh, no wonder your reactions were so bland.” Realizing that Clown had mentioned this in the last summit, the Master sounded somewhat disappointed. “But that’s kind of a surprise. Clown, I didn’t expect you to tell them something like that. Have you taken a liking to the people here now?”
“Hehe, of course not. I was just curious about how a certain someone would react.” Clown looked at me with his characteristic laugh.
Following his line of sight, the Master glanced at me with a look that seemed to be full of meaning. I was nervous that he was going to say something to me.
Zzzzzz.
But just then, the Master’s body began to shimmer like a hologram. “Darn, it’s already time for me to leave.”
“Master!” Fox shouted in disappointment, but he just shimmered even more in response.

But even in a situation like this, the Master looked solely at me. It was a very unpleasant and uncomfortable gaze. We were only looking at each other, but it felt like he was seeing right through me.
In the end, I couldn’t stand it and asked, “Do you have something to say to me, Gramps?”
“It’s not Gramps, it’s Old Man.” A voice resonated through my head like a Secret Voice spell. It was clear who the owner of the voice was. “That’s what that damn kid called me.”
God damn it. No wonder he let that slide so easily.
He knew from the start?
Without realizing it, my body stiffened slightly. Of course, the movement was so insignificant that it was difficult to capture with the naked eye, and it only lasted an instant.
“Hmm, in truth, your response was so smooth that I’m confused even now. But judging by your rapid increase in heart rate, I guess you really aren’t that kid.”
What the—he was just feeling me out?

“Don’t worry. I feel no reason to interfere with whatever you’re doing here. I am just curious. But unfortunately, I don’t have time today. We will talk about who you are next time we meet.” With that, the Master’s body dissipated before my eyes like fog.

“Ha.” I laughed out loud, the nonsensical kind of laugh that came out when one experienced something too ridiculous to process. There really wasn’t a single son of a bitch in this world that was easy to deal with, huh.

chapters.title: Chapter 198: Master Key (3)
paragraphs: When the Master, the person who first created the private chat room called the Watchers of the Round Table, disappeared without a trace, everyone made sounds of disappointment.
“Huh, he really is gone.”
“...That was different than just leaving a chat room.”
“Yes, it was almost like he was logging out.”
Their voices were full of questions. Well, I felt similarly.
“I thought you could only log out when you returned to your room?”
“I think, based on what he said, it was more like he was being kicked out.”

It was very different from Baekho’s situation. To start, Baekho took a prototype pill which limited his time in Ghost Busters to one hour. But what about the Master? As far as I could tell, this was a problem that had arisen for someone who was normally fine using the community. Did everyone else have similar thoughts?
“What on earth is Master going through?”
“Hehe, I don’t know, but one thing is for sure.”
“What is?”
Clown lowered his voice at Fox’s question. “His one-year disappearance has something to do with the GM.”
There was a moment of silence, not because this information was shocking, but because everyone took a moment to reflect on it. The general verdict was in agreement with Clown’s theory.
