“Well, that’s probably the most likely explanation.”
“But there’s one thing that doesn’t make sense. If Master really is under the GM’s control, how did he show up here again?”
“He’s a mysterious guy. Since this space is created by magic, maybe he found a solution through magic?”
“Th-th-that means our master could be a wizard more powerful than the GM who created this community!”
“That’s definitely plausible. Hehe.”
Afterward, the members exchanged all sorts of theories and I just listened quietly to all the interesting content. Of course, that didn’t last long.
“...Um, Mr. Lion, do you know anything?”
Before long, their attention naturally turned to me. This was to be expected. After all, I had pretended to be Baekho and called him Gramps. They were probably wondering if I knew anything.
“Not sure.”
How would I know? I was just as curious about his identity as they were. Of course, I had no intention of telling them that. That was so not cool.
“Oh, I see. You don’t—”
Saying “I don’t know” didn’t suit Lion, so I decided to go with a better option. I cut Fox off. “But I have a hunch.”

That was when Fox’s disappointed tone brightened considerably. “A hunch? I-Is that true? I’m not doubting you, but...” Through the crack in her mask, I could see Fox’s eyes fill up with a blossoming anticipation. It was the same for the other masks.
Actually, I don’t even have a hunch.
My modern-man conscience squirmed, but I ignored it.
“P-Please tell us. What happened to the Master—?”
I cut Fox off again. “Enough.”

“Eh?” Fox, who had apparently believed I was going to tell them, stared at me blankly. However, there was no need for me to explain myself in detail. A slight shrug was enough. There was no one here who didn’t know the meaning of this gesture anymore.
“Hehehe, you want us to bring you something interesting.”
If you want something from me, you need to bring me something adequate—that was the ironclad rule Lion had established for the Round Table. So how would Fox respond?
“All right.” Just as expected. She was the one who was almost obsessive about the Master’s current situation. “Still, my hurdle is a bit lower, right? Since it’s just a hunch and not a fact...”

I didn’t answer, and Fox let out a deep sigh. I guessed she never expected to find herself in this situation just like Clown, who had taken the bait of the holy relic, and Crescent Moon, who was obsessed with the Stone of Revival.
“Somehow, it feels like I’ve gained a comrade. Fox, you’ll be in for a hard time too.”
Fox just let out a harsh, resigned laugh at Crescent Moon’s attempt at consoling her. This meant that the quality of her news would go up in the future.
All that’s left are Deer and Goblin.
Setting aside my satisfaction, I spoke in a purposefully nonchalant tone. “How boring. Isn’t that enough small talk?”
“Yes, let’s start the gathering.”
I had planted enough seeds; it was time to harvest them. So, after the third month, when no one was present, the fourth month of our gathering began.

Goblin kicked us off. “The wizards of the tower are working together to look for a way to break Noark’s barrier.” When he first said that, everyone else reacted as if that was obvious, but they were soon convinced by his additional information. “It seems that a fixed amount of divine power is required for the process, and they believe they can at the very least reduce the time it’ll take for the barrier to come down.”
“I guess that means there has been some degree of progress in the research.”
“Yes, that’s right.”
To sum it up, the magic curtain protecting Noark might be ripped off soon. Well, I didn’t know how soon it would be, though.
Raven said it will take at least two years.
Finishing off with news that the Magic Tower had set a goal of shaving off six months, Goblin’s turn was over.

Next was Deer. “The palace has produced a new type of identification tag. It’s a magic device in the form of an engraving that cannot be counterfeited. It seems that preparations were made a while ago, but it will be supplied to adventurers starting next week.”
“Next week, huh? That’s not helpful at all. It’s not like this is information we can benefit from knowing in advance.”
“Then one more. The palace is keeping an eye on clans that have stopped adventuring and are playing it safe.”
“What do you mean by ‘keeping an eye’?”
“If I had to guess based on the political climate, it seems a significant disadvantage will be given to them, though I can’t be sure.”
“...I see.” She tried to hide it, but Fox seemed relieved by Deer’s follow-up. I noted that reaction down.
Fox likely belongs to a clan. She wouldn’t be a regular member, though. Maybe a clan master?
Of course, I could only speculate at this stage, so I tuned into the next person. It was Fox’s turn. “Mega clans are preparing a large-scale boycott.”
“Boycott?”
“Boycott. They won’t be entering the labyrinth as a group. They were already very dissatisfied after the conquest, and then a recent incident lit a fire in them.”
“Oh, that. I know what you’re referring to.” Crescent Moon jumped in, apparently familiar with the subject. “Bjorn Yandel, right?”
Huh? Why was my name coming up here?
“Yes. That’s right. The palace banished an ordinary adventurer to Bifron for something that originally would have ended with a fine.”
Oh, that...
“Law enforcement is under their domain, of course, but most clans interpreted this as a warning.”
“Public opinion must not be great.”
“Yes. There’s talk that if clans give the palace any more power, they could be forcibly drafted next time there’s need for an army.”
My hands stiffened and my lips went dry the moment my name was mentioned, but luckily no one seemed to notice my reaction. No one seemed particularly interested in Bjorn Yandel, either.
Whew, I nearly had a heart attack.
Anyway, after Fox answered Deer’s additional questions, the third turn was also over.
“Okay then, who wants to go next? Should we continue clockwise?”
“...Clown, can you go first?”

“Well, if you want.” At Crescent Moon’s request, Clown readily took the fourth turn. He was the one I was most looking forward to, but it seemed he hadn’t been able to find any interesting information this time. “To be honest, I don’t think this is something Mr. Lion will be interested in, but I’ll give it a try anyway.” Unlike when he told us about the binding spell, Clown spoke almost like he’d already written his turn off entirely. “Right before Noark went into lockdown, they sent a few people aboveground. Their goal is to kill one specific adventurer! Shocking, huh?”
“Assassins... Do you know who the target is too?”

“I’m not sure. I don’t know that much either, hehehe!” The fourth turn ended with an elusive smile. Clown didn’t even ask if I was intrigued. Well, how would he know that out of all the things I’d heard today, this was the most interesting?
An assassin from Noark...
Immediately, a person came to mind: Amelia Rainwales. Could she be one of the assassins sent up? Judging by her abilities, she would be perfect for the role.
Then does that mean the target is Auril Gavis?

The thought did come to mind, but somehow I didn’t think that was the case. It hadn’t sounded like she was lying when she said that her search for him was her personal business. Anyway, I’d have to think this all through later.

“Now it’s my turn.” The long-awaited fifth turn began. The main character of this turn was Crescent Moon, who desperately sought the Stone of Revival. He seemed confident, considering he had asked a few minutes ago if my promise was still valid. I wondered what he had prepared. “Does everyone remember what I said before about the traces of the Relic Thief?”
“Of course.”

When Crescent Moon carefully started, the other masks all nodded, except for Goblin, who had been absent at that gathering. “Sorry? What relic thief?” Goblin tilted his head, but no one paid him any mind.
Fox didn’t hide her curiosity at all. “So, what? Is this information related to the Genesis Treasures again?”
Crescent Moon nodded and proceeded to say something utterly shocking. “The Genesis Treasures no longer exist.”
The Genesis Treasures, besides being holy relics, were the keys to reaching the last floor, where the Gate of the Abyss was located.
“What do you mean they don’t exist? I don’t understand what you’re saying at all.”
“Is this reliable information? Or is this just what you believe?”
“Hehehe, that’s a bit of a shock.”
“H-H-How could they disappear?”
As these were all players wishing to return home, it took only a moment for chaos to fill the hall.

But I guessed he had expected a reaction like this. Crescent Moon just pressed on, his tone hollow. “How nice it would be if I were mistaken. But this is the indisputable truth. The Genesis Treasures do not exist anywhere in this world.”
“Y-You mean they were destroyed?”
“That’s the conclusion we came to, at least.”
“B-But those things are indestructible!” Goblin was apparently in quite a panic because the volume of his whining rose significantly.
Shaaaaaa.
A green light emanated from the jewel embedded in the center of the Round Table. That meant that what had just been said was true.
“So... the Genesis Treasures might really have disappeared,” Deer murmured in an empty voice. There was silence after that for a while.
The first to open their mouth was Crescent Moon. “So, how about it? Was that interesting?”

That was a very difficult question to answer. I wanted to say it was boring, but how could I say that here? Crescent Moon had had his eyes fixed on me the entire time he was filling us in. He would’ve caught me flinching as soon as he dropped that bomb.
What should I do?

After a short period of deliberation, I made a decision. It’d be a bad choice to call this news boring. “You have skills.” I’d rather admit it. Instead, I should try to mitigate the damage on another front.
“That must mean...” Crescent Moon’s breathing grew rough, almost like he thought the Stone of Revival was practically in the palm of his hand.
“To be honest, I am quite impressed,” I said simply.

Of course, there was a lot to lose by admitting that. Aside from having to share information on the Stone of Revival with someone else, once he got what he wanted, Crescent Moon would no longer be as eager to bring me information. In addition, it didn’t suit the image I’d created of Lion. Clearing the “make the lion laugh” achievement on the first try? I’d lose face.
Smirk.
However, this was not a problem. Right now, I was not Bjorn Yandel but a veteran wearing the mask of Lion.
Okay, this should be enough chit-chat.
As soon as I did one last run-through in my head, I asked Crescent Moon, “How did you find that out?”
What surprised me was not the fact that the Genesis Treasures were gone but something else. To be more precise, it was a pity because this was something I already knew.
“There are only a few people who know that the Genesis Treasures have disappeared.”

Picking up on the meaning behind my words, Crescent Moon’s eyes widened. I guess he didn’t realize that I was cheating him. “...Right, so you knew.” He didn’t suspect me at all—he just looked resigned, his voice weak as he spoke. What would it take to please me? Even I could feel the thick despair in the air, and it wasn’t ideal.
“Pshehe...”

Just look at the awkwardly smiling Clown. This would affect all the members I had baited before now. So, in that spirit, I laughed out loud and said, “The Stone of Revival can be obtained on the ninth floor.”
I could provide at least some encouragement, after all. To be honest, I felt a bit sorry for him.

chapters.title: Chapter 199: Master Key (4)
paragraphs: It was actually next to impossible to find the Stone of Revival based on the singular clue that it was on the ninth floor. I was sure Crescent Moon knew that too. He was also a user of this sadistic game. But to him, this information was like a storm after a long drought.
“W-Why...” Pushing aside his joy, Crescent Moon asked me, “Why are you doing me this favor?” He couldn’t help being curious about the reason.
There was only one thing someone like Lion had to say here. “Because it seems more fun this way.”
Crescent Moon fell silent for a moment, turning my words over in his mind, before shuddering. “You... are definitely a scary person.”
Huh? What now? I didn’t know what he meant so I just stared at him, unmoving, with my chin on my hand.

He belatedly noticed his mistake. “Forget what I just said. That was idle talk. It doesn’t matter what kind of person you are. If it means getting that item, I’d give up my soul,” Crescent Moon said resolutely. Then, he tossed in some self-deprecation. “Well, I’m sure you know my situation already.”

That statement was completely incomprehensible to me. How the hell would I know that? What was he misunderstanding? I tried recounting the events of previous gatherings, but I couldn’t figure it out so I just stayed silent. As always, that got me halfway there.
“Of course... I guess you really knew.”
I didn’t deny it. It would be weird to deny it at this point, anyway. I just changed the subject like I wasn’t interested in whatever the hell he was talking about. “Now it’s my turn.”

When I started, all the masks turned to me. They seemed to look forward to what I was going to tell them this time. Feeling embarrassed for some reason, I tossed out one of the pieces of information I had prepared, something as fascinating as the Vamdemon but also functionally useless. It wasn’t as exciting as the Stone of Revival either.

“Hehe, this time, I already knew that.” Although the Round Table’s jewel glowed green, Clown seemed somewhat disappointed. Of course, that wasn’t my problem. He seemed to be blaming himself for not bringing something more interesting too.
“If it’s okay, I would like to continue. How about everyone else?” Fox said.

They seemed to have a lot prepared considering the break last month so the gathering continued after the first round. For round two, I offered up similar kinds of information steadfastly and as a result, the third round began before I knew it.

“I-I will stop after this round.” Goblin, who went first, spent a moment struggling to come up with something, but eventually waved the white flag and reluctantly passed his turn. But it seemed everyone else was in a similar boat.
“Hmm, I should stop here too.” Even Fox forfeited, making this round the final round of this meeting. I wasn’t particularly disappointed, though.
Looks like I heard everything that could be heard.

I hadn’t been able to figure out how the state of affairs was shifting since the confrontation with Noark, but I was getting a sense for it. It was the opposite of the rumors that were spreading in the city.
As expected, the palace has the greater advantage here.

The failed conquest had come with great losses on our end, but the same went for the underground city. Just based on what these guys had said, Noark’s lockdown was more of a last-ditch effort on their part to survive.
And now that the identification tags can’t be duplicated, I won’t have to drastically revise my plan. Looks like there aren’t any pressing issues at the moment, either.
I discreetly shifted my gaze to the Round Table. The green light was on for the information about Orcules that Crescent Moon had just offered up.
“Now it’s just you, Mr. Lion.”
Naturally, attention shifted to me. For some reason, everyone’s eyes were bright.
Geez, no pressure.
Tap, tap.

I tapped the armrest with my finger and pondered what to say. What kind of flourish should I add for the finale? I already had something in mind, but there might be something that better suited the current vibe at the table. It wasn’t long before I came up with something fitting.
Tap.
I grinned and stopped my finger. This wasn’t a piece of information I’d prepared in advance for this occasion, but... “Goblin.”
“Y-Yes?” Goblin was incredibly startled and even stuttered.
I stared right at him. “Come to think of it, you mentioned something like this earlier. About Gramps possibly being a wizard more powerful than the GM, who created this community.”
“A-Ah! Yes. I did...”
While Goblin seemed like he didn’t understand what I was getting at at all, Fox’s eyes lit up. “Is this information about Master?” She was at least better than Goblin, who seemed truly clueless.

“Wrong.” I ignored Fox and spoke to Goblin, like I had let his comment pass earlier but wanted to let the group know they were fundamentally wrong about one thing. “This community was not created by the GM. To be exact, it was an existing place that was then remodeled to its present form.”
I recited the information I had gotten from Baekho word for word. Everyone then directed their eyes to one place—the gem embedded in the center of the Round Table.
“...It’s green.”
I already expected this so I wasn’t surprised. Not that I’d checked it out myself or anything, but I had no doubts that this information was true.
“To think this place wasn’t created by the GM...”
“Hehehe, it’s the first time I’m hearing this too.”
“Then who on earth created this place?”
The members of the Round Table all clammed up as if on cue, and again turned their eyes to one person—the only one here who could answer that question.
Okay, this should be enough aggro on me.
I cut through the tense silence, my tone nonchalant and emotionless. “I hope things will be more entertaining next time.”
That was what I left off on. That way, they’d come back with something more useful.
“He’s... gone.”
When Lion left the Round Table, a heavy silence dominated the room for a long while. The reason was simple: his last words. Or to be more precise, the emotion contained in his tone.
“Do you think he’s mad at us?”
Clown laughed at Fox’s whisper. “Hehehe Fox, you think too highly of us. Do you think we’re worth getting angry over for a guy like him?”
“That’s—” Fox’s mouth shut mid-rebuttal as she remembered what the Master said earlier.
“There is nothing for you to gain by participating.”

This was a secret gathering that ordinary players knew nothing about. Fox had been using the information obtained here to good effect, which was why it was hard to accept it at first. However, having heard what the Master said, there was no point in denying it. Lion had nothing to gain here.
Well, I guess there isn’t exactly nothing.
Fox smiled a wry, involuntary smile.
“I hope things will be more entertaining next time.”

Entertainment—something that could soothe one’s boredom even for a little while. To put it simply, a pastime. If there was anything Lion wanted from this gathering, that would be it. But how had they done so far? They hadn’t even been able to provide that. To demand a one-sided transaction...
“...We must have looked pathetic to him.”
“I’m sure. That man is a different type of person from Master. Although they are a bit similar.”
Fox tilted her head at Deer’s words. “Similar?”
Crescent Moon answered her question. “Since he showed up, we never really noticed Master’s absence.”

She slowly started to understand what they meant. That was how special Master’s presence at the Round Table was. He was the one who had gathered the current members and taught them valuable knowledge no one else knew about.
“If there is a difference between them, it’s that Mr. Lion isn’t the type to run a charity. Hehehe.”
“Charity?”
“Why, am I wrong? Or Fox, do you think Master created this place to obtain information?”

Fox did not attempt to argue. She couldn’t, because everything Clown said was true. The Master always knew everything and divulged his information generously, like he was a teacher in a classroom with his students.
“Hehehe, that’s why you follow Master so eagerly in the first place, Fox.”
Fox did not deny that, either. “You’re right. If I hadn’t thought of it as a charity, then I wouldn’t have thought of him as a benefactor, either.”

It was all thanks to Master that this gathering could exist. Just look at how things used to be not long ago. Before Lion joined, there were only four regular members. This was because once Master disappeared, attendance drastically fell. The other members, like Goblin, only ever dropped by from time to time to see if the Master was back.
But if they knew someone like this was here, they would continue showing up, just like Mr. Goblin did.

The thought was strange. However, Fox set those feelings aside and focused on the conversation that the remaining members were having. The topic of conversation was the person who had returned after a year-long absence, the Master. Well, strictly speaking, it was about Lion, who seemed to be familiar with him.
“Lion has to be someone we have heard of at least once. If even Master thinks he’s incredible, he must be one in a million.”
“True, he even treated the notorious Corpse Collector like a child.”
“A child... Right, he did say that. Hehehe.”
Once again, the time for deductive reasoning had come. “The last thing he shared was a s-shock. To think this community wasn’t created by the GM... How could he know such a thing?”
“Perhaps he’s acquainted with the GM.”
“With the GM who’s only rumored to exist?”
“Maybe to people like us, but he called Master ‘Gramps.’ There must be a whole other world we don’t know about.”
“I see...” Goblin said admiringly.
“But why are you acting like this today?” Clown asked him. “Last time, you acted like everything I told you about him was far-fetched.”
“That was when I didn’t know him very well.”
“Hehehe, I guess your eyes aren’t just for decoration after all.” Goblin scoffed at Clown’s mocking tone and averted his eyes.
That was when Deer parted his lips. “But am I the only one who sensed it?”
“Sensed what?”
“When Master left, I sensed an intentional thought.”
“Oh, I sensed that too.”

“Hold on, both of you. What intentional thought? You mean Master left someone a Verbal Message?” Fox was genuinely surprised. A Verbal Message was a kind of telepathic ability that could only be used in this incorporeal world. It was similar in principle to murderous intent, though instead of the urge to kill, you conveyed an intentional thought to the target. “Even Master said that’s difficult to use...”
“Hehehe, why are you surprised, Fox? Did you think Mr. Lion wouldn’t be able to pull something like that off?”

Clown’s tone was annoying, but she didn’t exactly have anything to say to that. As he said, when you thought about it rationally, it wasn’t that big a surprise. This was the guy who had radiated all that murderous intent during his first meeting. It would be weird if he couldn’t use a Verbal Message.
“Anyway, that means Master exchanged conversation with Mr. Lion before leaving?”
“Yes. It’s clear the two of them had something to talk about in private.”
“And you don’t know what that would be either, Mr. Clown?”
“Obviously. Master and Mr. Lion are both pretty much monsters!”
Fox pursed her lips in disappointment. If only she could learn what they had talked about, she could figure out what kind of situation her master was in.
“Hehehe, still, it wasn’t a complete loss.”
At Clown’s words, Fox came to her senses. “Pardon? What do you mean?”
Liking her perked-up ears and enthusiastic attitude, Clown chuckled. “I didn’t sense it at all.”
“Please include explanations when you speak.”
“Mr. Lion’s Message! I tried really hard, but I couldn’t sense it at all. Unlike Master’s, which I could sense at least faintly.”

Fox, who had some knowledge about how Verbal Messages worked, froze on the spot, and rightfully so. Even though Clown was speaking in his usual playful tone, the contents of what he was saying were by no means light. “Wait a minute. That means...”
Finishing her sentence for her, Clown shared what they had gained from today’s gathering. “Yes. Mr. Lion might be more of a monster than Master.”
The truly shocking theory left everyone speechless. Then came silence.

Goblin cautiously opened his mouth. “Um... Isn’t it possible that Master was the only one who said something? That would explain why Mr. Clown didn’t sense an intentional— W-wait, why is everyone looking at me like that? I’m just saying. Just saying. I don’t actually think that!”
The silence continued some more after that.

chapters.title: Chapter 200: Master Key (5)
paragraphs: The player nicknamed Elfnunalove, who more often used the name Ghost Master publicly and whose identity was the subject of many rumors, slowly opened his eyes and checked the time. It was just past midnight. His location was a private laboratory located on the upper levels of the Magic Tower. As always, he sat in his chair to get his thoughts in order.
What will he do now?
Today, as soon as he entered the community, he placed a permanent ban on a player. The target: a Korean user with the unique nickname of Sergeant Lee.
I’m sure that by now he’s on a rampage looking to kill me.
He hadn’t wanted to make an enemy of Sergeant Lee. He wasn’t just the person closest to the key, but the player who possessed the most influence, at least among those from Earth.
He’s the one who doesn’t listen when you talk to him.

The man was a bit worried that he may have plucked a nose hair from a sleeping tiger, but it had to be done. Sergeant Lee was the one who had refused his last attempt to smooth things over before banning him. Of course, the man understood Sergeant Lee’s situation, which was why he had left him alone until now, but he couldn’t be that considerate forever. He too had to make a choice.
Still, that’s too bad for him.
As he let his mind wander, it naturally landed on a certain man—a Korean user who used the nickname Elfnunna.
Looks like he’s a fan of his too.

Having encountered several Korean users before now, he knew how small their number was. The number of Koreans among the player population was less than 1 percent. It wasn’t for nothing that Sergeant Lee, who had desperately searched for someone from his homeland for years, begged for a chance to say a few words to him before he left.
He’s a funny man, now that I think about it. If he misses his homeland that much, he should be looking to team up to beat the game and return together.

The man smiled and rose from his seat. His crystal ball was vibrating, announcing an incoming call. “I never thought you would call me first at this hour. I guess something has happened on your end, Soul Queen.”
“Yes. I was getting ready to leave work, but I noticed something strange in the connection log.”
“A strange connection?” The man’s posture straightened. This woman’s understanding of this place was as deep as his, so nothing she said here would be trivial.
“The log shows someone connected, but it doesn’t state who they are. And more importantly... the connection time is recorded as 3:00 a.m.”
“So they entered the community in the middle.”
“Yes. I thought that was very strange too.”
“Can you give me some time to think this over?”

The man cast a spell on himself while still on the line. Meditation was a combo spell he had created himself by adding several spells to Thought Acceleration. Once he cast it, one person immediately came to mind.
“The Watcher of the Round Table.”
“Oh! That suspicious man who was banned a year ago!”

They had learned of his existence a year ago. His username was 0720. None of the guides who helped newcomers enter the community ever recalled helping him. When the admins stepped into his inner world, they saw him dressed in clothes from this world, so they deemed it suspicious and banned him. That was because most people wore modern clothes in their pocket dimensions. They deduced that he had to be a spy from the palace who had secretly infiltrated the place by obtaining a pill from somewhere. If not, he was possibly a player from someplace other than Earth.
Above all, he looked like an old man.
Most players were young, which made sense. These were people who had enjoyed a sadistic game like Dungeon and Stone, after all. It was hard to imagine an old man over seventy clearing it.
“Perhaps the Watchers of the Round Table is a gathering he created to avoid detection.”
“But didn’t you deem the remaining members normal back then?”
“Yes. I did then. But just in case, Soul Queen, will you go check for me?”
“I believe that is a private chat room.”
“Don’t worry about the invite code. It will take a few months, but there are ways for you to get in.”
“Well, in that case...”

Soul Queen accepted the task, and with that, the man moved to end the call. More detailed instructions would follow after figuring things out next month. There was nothing that could be done right now. Then he paused. For some reason, a certain nickname popped into his head, and he found himself involuntarily asking, “Soul Queen, do you remember the player Elfnunna?”
“Oh, him? He joined a few months ago, but I remember him clearly because he was unique. Not only his nickname, but there was something else about him that left an impression on me.”
“What was it?”
“I couldn’t see his inner world at all. I’ve never seen someone with such a thick mental wall in my entire career.”
“...I see.”

The man felt like something was off. A strangely thick mental wall could be written off as everyone being different, and Soul Queen also hadn’t been a guide for all that long. However, he still had the feeling that he was missing something. His Intuition stats rose when Meditation was active, so he didn’t attribute this feeling to just his current mood, either.
“Please excuse me for a moment.”

The man excused himself to run through the notes he had made in his head. Or, to be more precise, he checked the list of people who had been sent letters around the time Soul Queen mentioned Elfnunna joining.
They were all newbies.

Considering the possibility that Elfnunna took the pill later than he’d received it, he increased the range to three months, but the results were the same. None of those players had gone beyond the fifth floor, either. So how could his mental barrier be that high?

“...Bjorn Yandel?” Widening the range even further, one name stood out in his eyes, a barbarian who peculiarly chose a shield. He had sent him a letter in hopes that he may be a certain person, but he suspiciously did not join the community.

“Soul Queen.” The man handed out new instructions. “Investigate the user called Elfnunna, what posts he’s made, how much GP he has, and what information he’s purchased. Even if you have to restore everything that’s been deleted.”
There was reason to check this out.
The morning after the community opened, Amelia woke me up.
“...What’s going on? It’s only morning.”
“Morning? It’s already noon.”
Geez, can’t a barbarian wake up late?

I poured a glass of water down my parched throat and asked, “So, why are you here?” Amelia usually came in the evening. That was when we had agreed to see each other yesterday too. So why was she here to see me now?
The answer that came out of Amelia’s mouth was rather simple. “I thought I should give you a heads-up before I leave.”
“So you’re leaving.”
“Yes, so you can stop your search now.”
Based on what she was saying, it didn’t seem like she was leaving because she had found Auril Gavis. I tried casually probing her. “Looks like you have something to do.”
Amelia didn’t answer, but even that was enough for me. This woman was always scurrying around in the city.
“Right before Noark went into lockdown, they sent a few people aboveground. Their goal is to kill one specific adventurer! Shocking, huh?”

Maybe the assassination operation Clown had mentioned was beginning today. I had no intention of intervening—not that I could stop her anyway. Instead, I made a friendly offer. “Are you going to come look for him again? I can leave word here if you need.”
That was because she was sensitive about favors and grudges. I had a feeling that clearing my debt with her would help me in the future.
“There’s no need. It’d be difficult to find him this way, anyway.”
“I see.” I didn’t bother offering again after she refused. The conversation came to a natural stopping point, and I gave her a brief farewell. “Then I’ll see you next time.”
Amelia stared at me silently for a moment. Then, she asked, “When you say you’ll see me next time, what do you mean?”
Oh, so that’s what you were curious about.

Well, I was the one who had been making such a big deal about never seeing each other again. I was sure this sounded a bit strange to her. I decided to answer honestly. “Somehow, I have a feeling we will meet again.” How many times had we already run into each other by chance? I had no idea how long it would be before I could return home. I was sure I’d run into her again at least once before then.
“...You weirdo.”
After that, Amelia disappeared from sight swiftly as usual. Now, then, it was time for me to start my day too.
Ding!
First, I slammed my hand down on the bell I had made next to the bed.
“Did you call, boss?” My right-hand man, Jingjing, appeared in less than a minute.
To start, I gave him orders to stop the search, then had a light lunch before going out with him. This was my daily after-lunch walk. In Bifron, there wasn’t much else to do.
“Let’s go to the distribution center.”
“The distribution... center?”
“Is there a problem?”
“No, boss. I will guide you to the nearest one.”

Today’s destination was one of the twelve distribution centers in Bifron. When we arrived, there was a long line of people waiting to receive the food rations provided by the city every morning. Even just a few days ago, this had been a rare sight. Originally, the distribution centers were occupied and monopolized by each faction.
“As you ordered, minors are free to take as much as they please.”
“Good, keep this going.”

I watched the line of children with a satisfied smile before turning around. Then I wandered around the city, going wherever my feet led me. As I did, I spotted a familiar little boy—the kid who had acted as my guide on my first day in Bifron and brought me to the inn.
“Come here.”
“Yes, sir!” The kid, who had begun to shuffle backward as soon as our eyes met, soon stood at attention in front of me.
“Where are you going?”
“I-I’m coming back from the distribution center...”
“You’ve gained a little weight since the last time I saw you.”
“Yeah...”

Was it because I was now the top dog in Bifron? Even on that first day, I never did anything to hurt him, yet the kid continued to shudder when he saw me. Well, I was just happy to see him again. Was this the loneliness that came with being on top?
“How are you doing these days?”
“I-I read books in my free time. I-In the library that you made...”

I hadn’t made the library; it was more like I’d revitalized a library that was gathering dust. Many of the books had been used as kindling so there were still more empty bookshelves than filled ones, but since I’d given my underlings instructions to collect as many books as possible to fill the shelves, that would get better with time.

Growing anxious about the way I was staring at him, the kid started offering excuses for things that I didn’t even ask about. “I-I’ll never do anything like I did back then again, I promise! Now if I need money, I register at a labor camp and earn it myself!”
“Come to think of it, your dream is to be a scholar.”
“Y-Yes!”
I smirked and offered him some advice. “Keep living like this, then. If you stab people in the back for money, you’ll end up having problems with your head, and one day it’ll disappear.”
“...Pardon?”
“If you don’t have a head, you can’t be a scholar.”
“Sorry? Ah, yes...” Although he looked like he didn’t understand what I was talking about at all, I didn’t bother launching into a lengthy explanation. I refused to be a boomer barbarian.
“Let’s go.”

After that, I continued my walk with Jingjing through different distribution centers, libraries, residential facilities, labor camps, etcetera. With nothing else to do other than look for Auril Gavis, I tinkered with some silly projects here and there, leaving the city much livelier than when I first arrived. The dissolution of the gangs was the biggest contributing factor.
It’ll go back to normal once I’m gone, though.
On that note, I led Jingjing to the sewers. He began to tremble, and his voice came out strange as he asked, “Um, boss, why are we...?”
Wow, you’d think I came to kill and bury you here.
“I’m going to the city for a while, do you need anything?”
“...Pardon?” Jingjing, who rarely repeated the same words twice, asked, looking puzzled. “G-G-Going to the city...?”
“Oh, didn’t I tell you? There is a passageway leading to the city.”
“Th-th-that’s... not possible?”
“Why are you stuttering? Is there something wrong with your head?”
“No... Boss.” Jingjing’s head, which must have been filled with the thought that he’d be free in a few days, now dropped miserably, but I guessed he belatedly realized it could be a bluff.
“Anyway, since you don’t need anything—”
“No! I do!”
“Really? Tell me.”
Jingjing requested one thing from the city: a skewer from a shop in District Nine.
“It will be cold by the time I bring it back.”
“That’s fine!”
I smiled and nodded my head. It was clear what this guy was thinking. He was trying to check whether I had a way to get into the city. “Then you head home.”
“Yes, boss.”
Afterward, I let Jingjing go and entered the sewer. Then I headed toward the secret passage Amelia told me about.
Bzzzzzz.

It was then that the message stone I carried in my clothes, outside of sub-space just in case, started to vibrate. It was the one I had received from Mr. Dragon. A while back, he promised to contact me if a decision was made as to whether they’d give me the Dragon’s Blessing or not.
He said it’d take a month or two and it took exactly two.
I wondered what their answer was. When I clicked on the button that protruded from the bottom of the stone, a voice rang out from it. “Tear the paper I gave you back then.”
“I want to know your decision before that.”
“The elders will decide when they see you.”
“I see.” I tore the paper that I had thrown into my sub-space as instructed.
Decide when they see me, huh?
That wasn’t the yes I was hoping for, but I wasn’t too worried. Making things happen even when they didn’t work out—that was the spirit of a K-Barbarian.

chapters.title: Chapter 201: Blessing (1)
paragraphs: A magic circle blossomed on the ground of the sewer. As I stood there, taking in the light it was radiating, the musty scent of filth vanished into thin air.
“You’re here.”

It was the Dragon Temple I had visited last time. I could see Mr. Dragon in front of me with six members of the dragon tribe standing behind him. Those must have been the elders he mentioned earlier. They had reptilian eyes that split vertically, but it wasn’t hard to tell that their gazes weren’t all that friendly.
That called for a battle cry. “Behelaaah!”
I didn’t use Wild Outburst since I didn’t come to start a fight, but that was enough to attract aggro. The elders frowned as they watched me, seemingly wondering what the heck I was doing.
“Oh, sorry. I just wanted to do that.”

When I scratched the back of my head and apologized, Mr. Dragon, the only one here with previous experience dealing with me, began our meeting with a strange look in his eyes. “You... haven’t changed.”
Was that a compliment? Now that my self-introductory shout was over, I got straight to the point. “So, what do I need to do now?”

Could the Dragon’s Blessing be bestowed upon me, a barbarian? Mr. Dragon said that the elders would be deciding that after meeting with me, but that wouldn’t be because they were curious about what I looked like. What kind of verification did they want from me?
“It’s nothing,” said Mr. Dragon. “Before coming to a final unanimous decision, the elders will take turns asking you questions or making requests.”
“I understand the question part, but what do you mean by requests?”
“Well, I don’t know yet either. But you should know you can refuse if you want to.”
Yeah right. Then they’ll just vote no. Is this because it’s a Dragon’s Blessing? They’re being ridiculously strict.
“How about it? Will you do it?”
I grumbled inwardly but nodded, although I was starting to think they were asking a lot from someone who was returning the Dragon Sword... but a Dragon’s Blessing was worth it.
“Okay, that’s decided, then. There’s no point in wasting time, so shall we start straight away?”
“Fine.”
Upon receiving my consent, Mr. Dragon glanced at the elders behind him to start the verification process. The first to step forward was one of the only two female dragons present.

“I will start.” Due to the nature of the dragon tribe, it was pointless to guess her age based on her appearance, but I got the sense she was the youngest of them from the look in her eyes and tone of voice. “Bjorn, son of Yandel. What is your greatest wish?”

As soon as I heard that question, I got a sense of the purpose of this hearing. It was truly an evaluation, in the strictest sense of the word, to learn what kind of person I was before passing on the secret art of the Dragon’s Blessing to someone of another race.

Contemplating this for a moment, I gave my honest answer. Was it to return to Earth? No, despite it all, that was only a secondary goal. “To survive.” My utmost priority had always been survival, though that had changed a bit. Survival remained a top priority of mine, but there was something else too now. “If possible, with my teammates.”
Even as I answered, I felt a strange emotion well up inside of me. Since landing in this strange world, this might have been my biggest transformation. So, how was my response received?
“...I see.” The dragon woman gave me a meaningful look and asked one more question. “If your sacrifice could save a teammate, what would you choose to do?”
“I thought you were each asking one question.”
“You don’t have to answer if you don’t want to,” the dragon woman said in a tone that implied she didn’t care.

I just answered honestly again. “I don’t know yet.” If you asked me if I would make the same choice Team Half-Wit’s wizard, Riol Warb Dwalkie, had made, this was the only answer I could give. Anything I said or any resolutions I came to before I was faced with that situation was meaningless. Death always put humans to the test. “But when that time comes, I will choose what I have to choose.”
The dragon woman gave me a curious look. “...Then you could have just answered that you’d save your teammate.”
“I didn’t want to answer the question like that,” I said dismissively.
That wouldn’t be fair to him, either.

The dragon woman, who had no idea what I’d gone through, stared at me for a moment before stepping back. “My questions end here.” It was hard to discern whether or not she’d liked my answer just from her expression.
Before I could even catch my breath, the next round began. “I’m Geornavehanuteres.” A middle-aged man with a body almost as bulky as mine made a request instead of asking a question. “Fight me.”
The proposal was accompanied by an underlying burst of Dragon Fear. I answered without a moment’s hesitation. “Fine.”

As a barbarian warrior, it would be ridiculous for me to turn down that offer. Besides, this was also a good opportunity. An elder of the dragon tribe would at least be equivalent to a seventh-floor adventurer. If I could fight him without running the risk of dying, there was no reason not to do so. That was my verdict.
“Everyone, stop,” Mr. Dragon interrupted. “We agreed not to make such requests.”
“What is more reliable than hand-to-hand combat? Don’t you agree, barbarian warrior?”
Uh, I was going to use a mace...
I personally thought equipment should also count as a skill, but I decided to just back him up. “Of course.”
“Hahaha! I like you!” I guess my answer must have satisfied him, as the macho dragon man burst into laughter. “I didn’t think he would agree to a request like that without hesitation, though.”
The other elders seemed to find my response interesting too. “So, what will you do?”
“I will ask a question before moving on, then,” the macho dragon man conceded, obvious disappointment in his tone. “Barbarian, what are you most afraid of?”

The first thing that came to mind was death. However, giving the same answer as I did for the first question wasn’t good interview etiquette for many reasons. So I answered this with a bit more specificity. “Fighting someone stronger than me.”
“...What?” The macho dragon man tilted his head as if he’d misheard me. A moment later, he realized something. “You think I’m weaker than you?” he growled.
I shook my head. “No, I don’t.”
“But you just—”
“You didn’t intend to kill me, did you?”
“No, but—”
I cut him off curtly. “I must fight because I am afraid. More and more so every day.”
I knew that this might sound un-barbarian-like to some, but, so what? This was the real essence of a barbarian.

Thankfully, it seemed I’d managed to properly convey what I meant. “Preparing for that moment rather than running away because you are afraid... that’s a sound answer indeed.” The macho dragon man smirked. “Interesting. Are all barbarians like you?”
“Somewhat.”
It was in fact Ainar who’d taught me how warriors lived their lives, and the advice she gave me back then showed me the path forward whenever I was driven to a dead end.
“I see. My questioning ends here.” Soon, the macho dragon man returned to his position with a satisfied smile on his face. One thing was for certain: I definitely had one vote.
The third round was also a question, not a request, and a pretty strange question at that. “You, are you in love with anyone?”
“Your answer was a little late. I guess there is someone you have in mind.” The drowsy-looking dragon woman went back to her position without any further questions.

The fourth turn started like this. “I will test your insight.” A grey-haired dragon grandpa handed me an item. I could tell what it was for as soon as I saw it. It was a ring puzzle. “Now, take it all apart.”
Huh, I never thought this would be one of the tasks.

“To give you a little help, there’s a specific order and method you have to use to separate them.” When I took the ring puzzle from him, the dragon grandpa grinned and even gave me a hint. He probably thought I’d never be able to solve it. Geez, did he think I was a real barbarian or something? I used to play with a lot of ring puzzles back in the hospital as a kid. “I will give you as much time as you want. Sometimes it is possible to arrive at the truth through persistence.”
I grabbed the ring puzzle and checked the setup first by looking it up, down, left, and right. Given enough time, there was no way I couldn’t solve this.
Well, that should’ve been the case.
“Haha, it has been five minutes.”
Goddamn it. What the hell is this thing?
“It has been ten minutes. Any closer yet?”

I admitted to myself that receiving more time was not likely going to lead to an answer. And so, there was only one method left: Giantization. My body expanded in an instant. I grabbed the rings with my enlarged hands and pulled them to the side.
Crunch.
I finally succeeded in separating the seven rings.
“W-What are you doing!”
“I separated it.”
“...Th-th-that is nonsense!”

“You never told me not to break it,” I answered confidently. That was because I had already realized what the trick to this puzzle was. This old man told me at the start that he was testing my insight, not my intellect. He also hinted that the solution was something you could only arrive at through persistence. That meant that this ring puzzle was impossible to solve, to begin with!
He probably gave me this to see how I solve problems that don’t have solutions.
“L-Like this! You can solve it like this...!” The dragon grandpa dropped to the ground numbly and fiddled with the puzzle that now had a few extra pieces. His eyes looked very sad for some reason.
“Ahem.”
“Th-this can’t be obtained anywhere else...”
“Who’s next?” I did my best to ignore the dragon grandpa and turned to the elders, who resumed the interrogation.
The fifth question was about my past. “How many people have you killed so far?”

I recalled each person in my mind and gave them the exact number. Then the elder asked why I had killed them. The answer wasn’t complicated. The methods I’d used to kill them varied, but my reason for doing so was just one. “Because they tried to kill me.”
“I see.” The elder who asked the question nodded and stepped back, which ended the fifth turn. Before long, the confirmation hearing reached its final stage. I couldn’t tell if it had gone well.
Well, the old man who gave me the puzzle is probably opposed... The macho dragon man will likely vote yes. The rest? Well, I’m not sure.
“Then it is my turn now.” Soon, a handsome man who looked like he was in his mid-to-late twenties stepped forward and asked just one question. “Have you only told the truth?”

The way he asked made it sound like he could discern the truth. That had me feeling cagey, but I’d answered every question with the truth up to this point. Plus, I figured that if I got a failing grade here, it wasn’t too late to start the negotiations KB-style, short for K-Barbarian. “I did.”
“Then we’re finished.”
That was the end of the hearing. Mr. Dragon exchanged looks with the last man and opened his mouth. “Looks like we’ll have to discuss amongst ourselves some more, so you can rest a bit.”
“Do I have to wait long?”
“Well, it looks like we’ll be done in an hour.”

Well, in that case, guided by the dragon woman who had asked the first question, I headed inside the temple and arrived at a room. Since they mentioned getting some rest, I was sure I was being guided to a guest room.

“Are you the barbarian who was supposed to come today?” However, the room had a previous occupant, a dragon kid with the appearance of an early teen. She looked at me and laughed. “Wow, you’re super ugly!”
What the hell? Who was this rude kid? My mind went blank at the sudden blow but I calmly laughed it off like the adult I was. “Haha, looks like you don’t have a mother.”
“If you were raised right, you wouldn’t be telling such strange lies!” Bjorn Yandel was manly-looking, but by no means ugly.

chapters.title: Chapter 202: Blessing (2)
paragraphs: Before you embark on a journey of revenge, dig two graves. These were the words of Confucius.

But the book I had read only had those words written inside—his intended meaning wasn’t included. So what did Confucius really want to say? That it was important to forgive? Or just how self-destructive and dangerous it was to choose revenge? Twenty-first century me had had no way of knowing, so I just chose to interpret it in the way that resonated with me more. Yes, Confucius knew that when you went to kick someone’s ass, you had to be prepared to get your ass kicked too.
But I guess she didn’t know that.
I stared down the kid who dealt me a personal blow the very first moment we met. She was currently staring out into space in a daze.

“That... what does that mean? I don’t understand...” I hadn’t used any difficult words there, so what she couldn’t understand must have been the situation itself, not what I had said. Well, maybe not? “I-I have a mom!” the kid shouted, glaring at me.
“You do?” I replied.
“I mean, she passed away, but...” The little girl flinched as she trailed off. To be honest, I was a little taken aback too. I didn’t think my insult would be so spot-on.

However, that was no problem. “Of course.” I nodded as if I knew that already. She didn’t have a mom? So what? The same went for Bjorn Yandel, who grew up without a mother. Moreover, considering the physiology of the dragon tribe, this kid was only young in appearance. She was probably older than me in real life, meaning there was no reason for me to stop punishing her for that preemptive attack.
“B-But how... did you know...?”
“It shows.”
“It... shows?”
“Yes. If you were raised right, you wouldn’t tell such lies.”

When I responded like that was obvious, the kid ground her teeth. Although cursing someone else’s parents wasn’t a customary insult in this world, one couldn’t help being sensitive about topics related to family.
Uh, or was I wrong?
“Apologize, barbarian! Lie? I didn’t lie!” The kid, who had recovered mentally to some extent, let out an angry shout at the fact that she had been accused of telling a lie.

For some reason, a corner of my heart died as soon as I heard that. To think she would deny it so vehemently. That was how sincere she had been when she called me super ugly. Bjorn Yandel would have been hurt by this, but this wasn’t a problem, either. A K-Barbarian always repaid an insult tenfold. That was me.
“Not even realizing you’ve lied, huh?” I gave the girl a sympathetic look. “How sad, to think you don’t have a father either—”

“I do! I have a dad! You weird bastard!” The kid cut me off with a scream. I decided to stop provoking her here. This should be enough to convey that messing with a barbarian could lead to big trouble. Plus, this was the dragonian homeland.
Wait, but why is the elder staying silent?
Suddenly noticing the silence behind me, I turned around and spotted the dragon elder watching me in amusement. “Incredible.”
Huh?
“I have never seen someone make Miss Penitaseauros this angry.”
That told me that she was an overly emotional kid. Even at this moment she was huffing and glaring at me, except I was focused on something else.
Miss?
The elder had attached an honorific to the name. That meant this kid’s status within the dragon tribe was notable.
“Wait, is this the shaman?”
The dragon shaman served a similar role to the one and only barbarian shaman. To put it simply, the Blessing could only be done by her.
“Oh, you didn’t know?”
How was I supposed to know?
When I slowly turned back around, the kid was glaring at me even more aggressively. “What? You want to apologize now?” There was an obvious sneer lingering on her lips.
After thinking it over for a while, I decided to stick with my guns. “Kid, why should I apologize?”
“...Don’t you want to get the Blessing?”
That was true, but even a shaman was below Mr. Dragon, the chief. If he gave the go-ahead, this kid would have no choice but to bestow the Blessing on me.
“That’s for the elder dragon to decide.”
The kid smirked at those words. “Oh, you mean my dad?”

I froze mid-laugh. She was Mr. Dragon’s daughter? The tribe’s shaman and the daughter of the ancient elder dragon... Indeed, she could not have a loftier status, but the option of apologizing was already erased from my mind. That was not barbarian-like. More than anything, if I apologized, I’d just be admitting that I was super ugly.
“...What are you looking at?”
“Nothing? I’m not looking at anything?”

After the kid’s shocking identity reveal, she and I engaged in a bout of psychological warfare in awkward silence. After a long while, the elder arranged a truce on our behalf. “That seems to be enough.”
No, it would be more accurate to call it a scolding.

“Bjorn Yandel, your remarks to the shaman earlier were very rude. The place where you stand is the temple in which our spirit dwells. Even if you are a barbarian, you need to show respect.” The elder pointed out my mistakes calmly and logically, then shifted her gaze to the kid, who was snickering to herself. “The same goes for you, Miss.”
“...Me too?”
“Bjorn Yandel is the elder dragon’s guest and the savior of our tribe. It was disrespectful to criticize his appearance during your first meeting.”
“But I didn’t lie!”
“There are times when one should remain silent. Even if what they say is the truth.”
The kid lowered her head despondently. However, I didn’t derive any satisfaction from it.
What is this? An indirect insult?
“Be silent even if what you want to say is true”? That meant she agreed that I was super ugly, but just thought it was wrong to say it out loud.
“I must attend the meeting, so...” Soon, the elder left me and my wounded pride behind.
It was awkward to keep standing there so I just flopped down on the ground. A suffocating silence promptly fell.
It was the kid who finally broke it. “Tell me...”
“What?”
“I heard you’re an adventurer. Any interesting stories?”
“...Why should I tell you?”
At my question, the kid shot me an annoyed look. “Words have power. And I can sense the nature of that power.”
“I don’t understand.”
“Ugh, I need to get used to your wavelength so that I can bestow the Blessing on you later or not. That’s probably why my dad sent you here early.”
This was my first time hearing about words having wavelengths, but there was something else that caught my attention more. “You speak as if a decision has already been made.”
“If they were turning you down, you wouldn’t have been brought to this room in the first place.”
“Then what are they discussing over there?”
“I don’t know. I guess they thought they’d look like pushovers if they didn’t do something.”
Somehow, I thought that might be the case.
“Anyway, so say something. You have to keep talking for me to read your wavelengths. That way the process will be less burdensome on your body.”
I couldn’t get used to this logical attitude because it differed from my first impression of her, but I obediently played along. “Anything you’re particularly curious about?”
“Why you became an adventurer.”
“You say strange things. We are born warriors. If we don’t fight, we die.”
“You mean you had no choice because of taxes?”
Well, sure, to put it another way... “Our status is not as great as yours.”
“Oh, I see...”
The dragon tribe did not pay taxes. This was because they had made a big contribution to the war thousands of years ago. The other races, on the other hand, struggled to pay their taxes every day.
“I heard that you can borrow money based on your race, though. Is that not the case for barbarians?”
I smiled bitterly at the genuine curiosity behind her question. “Yes, it’s not the same for us.”

Dwarves got a tax cut when they became blacksmiths. Beast people and elves had financial security because they helped with agricultural and livestock work in Gnome Tree. The palace handed out interest-free loans for adventurers up to their second year in the trade so they weren’t put to death for failing to pay their taxes. But barbarians? Well, they had awesome weapons, for one.
Once I become chief of the tribe, the first thing I’ll do is round up donations and fix everything.
Objectively, barbarians were the furthest behind. Improvements were needed in many areas. And I guess that not-so-great vibe showed on my expression because the kid changed the subject.
“...Enough of this, now tell me about that.”
“What?”
“I heard you fought Uncle—no, the Dragon Slayer?”

Oh, that. That was my sole point of contact with the kid, so I slightly dramatized what happened back then and told her about it. I didn’t make that many changes—I just removed the parts that could put me in a tough spot, like how we got the Ogre’s essence, things that could make her suspect me of being an evil spirit, etcetera. It was an interesting story even without all that.
“Riol Warb Dwalkie... That’s a name I think I’ll remember for a long time.”

Like everyone who heard this story, the kid focused the most on the part about Dwalkie. This sort of reaction made me feel proud because it felt like he was finally being recognized by other people too.
“The sword... So that’s how you got it. You truly are ridiculous. Anyway, and then? What happened after that?”
When the story about the Dragon Slayer ended, I naturally brought up the part about finding a new party member. At this point, I heard some interesting news.
“Did you know? My sister could have joined your party.”
It sounded like she was talking about the two-year teammate contract Mr. Dragon had proposed. “What kind of person is your sister?”
“She’s kind. But she’s so busy I don’t see her often.”
No, I’m asking how strong she is, not her personality.

I was always a bit curious about stuff like that so I moved to ask some more questions, but ended up not being able to. The door opened just in time. “I heard you fought, but you two seem to be getting along.” Mr. Dragon entered and smiled at the sight of us chatting. Thanks to that, I learned one thing: the elder didn’t tell him what I said to her earlier. If he’d heard about the whole ‘being raised right’ thing, he wouldn’t have been able to smile at me like that.
“So, is the verdict in?”
“It is.”
Geez, you could’ve just started with that.
“What is it?”
“We have decided to grant your request.”
“I see.” I nodded and glanced at the kid. She might’ve been right on the money earlier—the decision had already been made but they had held an hour-long meeting purely because of pride.
Is this why they asked those weird questions?
Reasonable suspicions filled me, but before I could examine them, Mr. Dragon spoke softly. “However, there is one condition.”
“Condition?”
“It was confirmed through the Church of Reatlas that you have received a blessing. One day, you will probably be reunited with Regal Vagos, the Dragon Slayer.”
“Okay, get to the point.”
“If you can kill him when that time comes, bring me his heart.”
“...Heart? Why do you need that?” Since this was a weighty condition, I decided to ask for the reason behind it first.
The answer came from the kid. “It’s because of me. When all that happened back then, I was the one who cursed Uncle.”
“Curse...”

That curse, which had made it so that the dragon Regal Vagos was no longer a member of the dragon tribe, was the reason why his use of Dragon Speech was restricted and he could not even properly use the Dragon Sword he had stolen by betraying his own people.
“Wait, wasn’t the curse left by the previous elder dragon?”
“That’s the story that has been told to the public. But in truth, it was my daughter who placed that curse.”
“...I see.” I felt like I was hearing the secret history of the dragon tribe, but that wasn’t important right now. “So, what does the heart have to do with the curse?”
“As payment for placing the curse, I’ve been frozen in time. I’ve become unable to step out of this temple for the rest of my life.”
“You mean you’ll be able to go back to normal if you have his heart?”
The kid didn’t answer my question. “At least, that’s what we believe,” Mr. Dragon said, his voice soft and sorrowful.

I suddenly had a thought. Perhaps this was why he had proposed providing me with a teammate for two years, so that she could follow me around and, once the Dragon Slayer appeared, kill him and bring his other daughter the heart.
Then how old is she?
At first, I figured she was a few years older than me, but now that I knew what I did, I didn’t think so, since the former elder dragon had died more than thirty years ago.
Well, her words and actions still don’t match her real age... but if she’s only ever lived in a temple, that makes sense.
“So, what will you do?”
“All right. If I kill the Dragon Slayer, I will make sure to take out his heart and bring it to you.”
“Then it’s done.”

This wasn’t a particularly difficult condition, so I skipped further negotiations and accepted the offer. Now it was time to receive prepayment of the reward. “Then, when will it be possible to receive the Blessing?”
“You can do it tonight if you want,” the kid said in response to my question. “But I must ask this before that. What kind of Blessing do you want to receive? I need to know that so I can prepare.”
“What are the Blessings?” I asked just to confirm, figuring that there might be a difference from the game.
“You don’t know? I thought you asked for it because you already did.”
“I only know one for sure.”

“Really? Then I guess I’ll have to explain the rest.” The kid looked annoyed yet still explained each one in detail. Based on what she was saying, it seemed there were no significant differences from the game.
“The first is the Earth Dragon’s Blessing.”

When you got this essence, any additional stats you got from an essence rose by 20 percent. The Earth Dragon’s Blessing had good compatibility with me since default stats were important to me. Though in truth, there were no options here with bad compatibility.
“The second is the Volcano Dragon’s Blessing.”

If the first one was good for stats, this was a type of Blessing that increased the performance of all skills. From what I could remember, it was about 30 percent. If I chose this, my Giantization size would grow even larger and the performance of Ironskin and Swing would significantly improve too.
“Lastly, there is the Sea Dragon’s Blessing.”

Unlike the other Blessings, this was the only one in which a specific stat went up. The effect of the Blessing was +100 Soul Power. Bearing in mind that Soul Power rose by ten each time you leveled up until level five, you could get a sense of how high that number was. If I chose this, the duration time of Giantization would go up several times at once. This meant that I wouldn’t ever run out of MP until I absorbed a few more core essences.
“Okay, that’s the end of the explanation. So, what will you choose?”
Which of the three would I choose? The kid even kindly offered me more time to think, but I firmly refused. “I’ll go with this one.” I already had something in mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 203: Blessing (3)
paragraphs: Dragon’s Blessing was one of the traits that made the dragon race so OP. Unlike Dragon Speech, this Blessing could be bestowed on other races. However, the number of times this had happened could be counted on two hands. You had to build up a certain amount of friendship with the dragon tribe and beat a hidden side quest in order to pull it off.
If you choose a dwarf, whom they don’t get along with, as your character, you won’t even get the chance to try.

Of course, I was a barbarian, not a dwarf, but in actuality I had given up on the Blessing. The conditions of the hidden quest were already insane in and of themselves, but according to my research, these quests were virtually gone in this era. A hundred and fifty years had passed since the setting of the game. The problem that had been such a headache for the dragon tribe throughout their history had supposedly been solved by a certain hero.
Wait, if I can do this one like this, does that mean the others aren’t impossible, either?

I recalled a few of the hidden routes that I thought were closed to me and thought them over. Perhaps it was still possible to take those routes. Even if that wasn’t the case, there were things that had been completely blocked by the game’s system that I could try.
“Just telling you this in case, but you can’t choose multiple blessings. As a barbarian, your body wouldn’t be able to withstand it.”
“What do you mean my body can’t withstand it?”
“Just as I said. You’d die.”

Hmm, so that wouldn’t work. She might give it a try if I insisted, but I had no intention of being so stubborn. The price was my life, after all. I heard the number of people that received more than two Blessings was very few, including Mr. Dragon. That was how much of a toll it took on the body.
“So, your decision? I can give you more time if you want.”
“No, it’s fine. I’ll go with this one.” I shook my head and smiled. That was because I had made the decision before I even got here.

The Blessing of the Sea Dragon? Not this one, that was for sure. Soul Power was an important resource, but if I rationed it appropriately for a hunt, I wouldn’t end up lacking it. It wasn’t like I was a sorcerer or something. I just needed the minimum.

The Blessing of the Volcano Dragon wasn’t bad. As the skill buff was set to keep pace with your growth, the performance enhancement wouldn’t just stop at 30 percent and would work even better as time went on.
“I will receive the Blessing of the Earth Dragon.”

However, I ultimately decided that it was better to raise stats than skills. The reason was simple. Many of my skills were dependent on stats anyway. If the stat went up 20 percent, the performance of any accompanying skills would be enhanced by that much too.

“Good choice. I guess you’re being cautious about him.” Mr. Dragon nodded at my selection. He seemed to think I was taking the Dragon Slayer into account in my decision so I just agreed. It wasn’t that the thought didn’t cross my mind, after all.

Silence of the Soul, Vagos’s goddamn overpowered Dragon Speech, reduced the target’s MP to zero and prevented them from using their skills, which was why I had had to fight him with my bare fists. However, if you asked if this was the deciding factor in my decision, it wasn’t. The Earth Dragon Blessing had a hidden ability.
But there’s no way these guys don’t know that...

I narrowed my eyes at Mr. Dragon and the kid. I wasn’t particularly insulted, though. They wouldn’t have enough loyalty to me to tell someone of another race about something like that. I didn’t need that kind of consideration from them in the first place.
“That’s it, then. I will leave you to it.” Once the decision was made, Mr. Dragon stepped aside with a delighted smile. “Have a good time with my daughter.”
Dude, that just sounds wrong.
After Mr. Dragon left, the kid and I talked until nightfall. The main topic of conversation was my quests so far.
“Do I have to talk about myself?”
“That would be best. I told you earlier, there is power in words. The more you talk about the path you’ve walked in life, the easier it is for me to detect your wavelengths.”
“If you say so.”

This was more comfortable for me than rambling nonsense, so I told her my story while filtering out some things. It hadn’t even been a full year since I became an adventurer, but I had more things to tell her than I thought. Maybe that was why...
“It’s getting dark now, how much longer?”
We even had a meal during the conversation and it was already evening, but it seemed this wasn’t enough to bestow the Blessing yet.
“...Not yet. Your wavelengths are strangely difficult to read. Yeah... so keep going with what you were saying.”
“Where did I leave off?”
“Doppelganger Forest. You told me up to meeting the other adventurers and realizing some of them were from the underground city.”

Since I had arrived at this place during broad daylight and spent all day talking, I had already reached recent events. After this, I had nothing left to talk about. I was a little worried, but when I honestly admitted that, I learned that there was apparently no more need to read my wavelengths.
“Hmm, I think this is enough.”
“That means?”
“Follow me. I will bestow the Blessing on your body now.”
When I followed the kid inside, I spotted a cave hidden behind a thin cloth.
A cave connected to the wall of a building, huh? It feels like I’m on a quest or something.

After walking through the cave for a few minutes, we reached a cavity of about forty square yards containing a bed and a few pieces of furniture. The jewels embedded on the ceiling created a soft light and smoke, giving the impression of a mystical space.
“Now, lie down here.”
“The bed is too small for me to lie on. I’ll just lie on the floor.”

When I lay on the ground coolly, like the barbarian I was, the kid chuckled and started preparing to bestow the Blessing on my body. It didn’t take long. It did take the form of a tattoo, but ultimately the core of a Blessing was the special ability of the shaman.
“Where do you want it?”
“How big is it?”
“About this big.” The kid spread her palm wide and showed me. It was much smaller than I thought.
“Does the location matter?”
“No, it doesn’t matter. Why do you ask?”

“I want to put it somewhere others can’t normally see it.” It was the Blessing of another race, after all. Until I became chief and changed the rules of the tribe, I’d be in trouble if I got found out.

“...Somewhere others can’t see it?” Something came to the kid’s mind and her gaze subconsciously slid to one place in particular. A grimace appeared on her face. “That’s... going to be a bit difficult.”
When I followed her line of sight, I genuinely freaked out. Jesus Christ. Who the hell got a tattoo there?
“...I-I can do up to the butt area.”
Yeah right. “It’s fine, do it here,” I told her the spot I had had in mind from the beginning.
“The sole of your foot? Oh, I see...” This society was similar to a Western culture. Since they wore shoes indoors, there was almost no reason to show their bare foot.
The kid seemed to accept this but then frowned. “But can’t I just inscribe it between your tattoos? I don’t think it will show much. Don’t you always wear armor on top?”
“The shaman will notice.”
“Ah, I guess.”

Of course, considering the shaman’s personality, he wouldn’t bother me about it. But I still wanted to hide it as much as possible. There was no telling how things would turn out in the future, and the shaman was strangely suspicious.
“That’s it, then. Can I get started?”
“Of course.”
“It will hurt quite a bit.”

“It’s okay. Finish it quickly if you can.” Despite the kid’s warning, I didn’t worry too much. Could it be as painful as the Spirit Imprint? Even if my Pain Resistance didn’t help me, though, I wasn’t afraid. “I am a barbarian.” Barbarians were those who always bounced back up after getting knocked down.
“Hmm, is that so?” The kid shot me an enigmatic grin before lighting a white flame over her finger.
Chhhhhh!
As she seared the sole of my foot with the fire, she spoke. “You can scream.”
Oh, is that so?
[The Earth Dragon’s Blessing now dwells in your soul. All additional stats increase by 20%.]
I shouted with all my might—“Aaaaaargh!” This was not the time to care about the barbarian race’s reputation.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 5
Physique: 555
Spirit: 198
Special Ability: 191
Item Level: 3068
General Combat Power: 1907.6 (New +176.6)
Acquired Essences: Corpse Golem - Rank 7  Orc Hero - Rank 5  Ogre - Rank 3 / Manticore - Rank 5]

The process of receiving the Blessing of the Earth Dragon on the sole of my foot was short in and of itself. Did it take maybe three minutes? Compared to the Spirit Imprint, which could take hours, it was only a moment. However, the total time it took ended up being similar. That was because as soon as it ended, I lost consciousness.
“Are you awake?”
When I slowly peeled my eyes open, I could see the kid sitting against the wall, reading a book. “...I must have fallen asleep.”
“Not passed out? You’re hilarious, really.”
I ignored her ridicule and checked the time. It was 9 a.m., time to start a new day.
“Drink.”

I chugged the water she gave me and got up. I was very mentally tired but felt a great vigor in my body. Well, considering my stats had risen by 20 percent, I couldn’t not feel the difference. I was already looking forward to seeing how it worked. Aside from the Corpse Golem, my number of rank-five or better essences was currently only three. Just filling in these blanks would raise my stats as much as a high-rank essence would.
“Kid.”
“It’s Penitaseauros.”
Don’t wanna be called a kid?
“Okay, Penetasaur.” Even as I recited her name, as she asked, it felt strange. Was this supposed to be a human’s name or a dinosaur’s?
“...Just call me Pen.”
“Okay, Pen. Anyway, is it over now?”
“Yeah. Fortunately, it went well. But just in case, come visit again whenever you can. I’ve never bestowed a Blessing on another race before so there could be some side effects.”
“Okay, if I have time.”
“Make time. I already told Dad about it.”
After giving her a half-hearted “okay,” we both left the cave. I asked for Mr. Dragon’s whereabouts so I could get back to where I was before I was summoned.
“Dad will be where you first arrived. Want me to guide you?”
“I can find the way myself.”
After receiving scout lessons from Rotmiller, I was confident in my ability to memorize directions. Just as I was about to leave, her voice came from behind me. “Sorry.”
“Huh?”
“I said sorry. Yesterday... For being honest and calling you ugly.”
I chuckled. I was confused whether this was an apology or an attempt at picking another fight, but like an adult, I decided to just point out the facts. “I’m not ugly.”
“What?”
“I am handsome, like a man.”
Pen studied me quietly before nodding slightly. “...Okay.”
It seemed I’d succeeded in instilling the correct beauty standards in her before she was tainted by the world. “See you next time. I’ll tell you more stories then.”
“...Okay.”

Saying goodbye to Pen, I went looking for Mr. Dragon. Then, after finally handing over the Dragon Sword, I returned to the sewer I had originally been in through Dragon Speech. The familiar scent of filth made my appetite disappear entirely. I considered for a moment whether I should just go back and get some sleep, but ultimately decided to hurry along.
It really is connected to the city.

Just as Amelia said, when I followed the secret tunnel, an exit leading to the city appeared. It was in District Eight, right beside District Seven where I lived. Originally, I was planning to meet Missha and Ainar to hear what was going on with them, but I was too tired for that.
I’ll see them in a few days anyway.
I covered my face with the hood I brought with me, then bought the skewer Jingjing asked for before heading back.
“Here’s the skewer from the shop you mentioned. I asked them for the spiciest, manliest flavor.” He just stared. “Why aren’t you saying anything? Aren’t you happy?”
“...I am happy.”
“Too quiet.”

“I am very happy!” Jingjing rejoiced enthusiastically, making it worth dragging my tired body all the way over here to bring it back. This was a weight off my shoulders. Now that I’d warned him that I could come back at any time, Bifron wouldn’t go back to its former state overnight.
“Are you crying?”
“It’s... because the skewer... is so spicy...”
“Tsk. It’s because you cry so easily that your hair is falling out.”
“Right...”
“I’m going to sleep now, so don’t wake me up.”
After sleeping for almost an entire day, I spent even more time sleeping as if to enjoy the last bit of my vacation. Soon, the day finally came.
“Behelaaah!”
It was the end of my short, yet long, exile. Receiving an enthusiastic send-off from all the members of my organization, I headed to the city wall. I shared a brief farewell with Jingjing too.
“I will visit from time to time.”

“Yes, boss! We’ll be waiting for you!” Still, Jingjing’s mental state seemed to have recovered a lot since the first day. After once again instilling in him to keep the secret passage a secret between the two of us, I called for the guard on the wall.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel. Confirmed.”
Then I entered the checkpoint and went through a simple identification process. Once that was over, the guard opened the door from the other side of the double-door structure.
“A knight of Mozlan left you a message. He said to stay out of trouble.”

What trouble? It was their fault that I got locked up here when it should’ve been handled with a fine. I grumbled as I entered the city and took a deep breath. Even the air felt different here. Strangely, even the sunlight felt warmer today.
...But where is everyone?

Returning to the city after twenty days of exile, I absently stood there on the street for a while. Even after a few minutes, none of my teammates showed up. I was kind of hoping they would come out to greet me.
Well, they wouldn’t have known the time.
I hurriedly grabbed a wagon and headed for the inn. As soon as I returned, I knocked on Missha’s door.
Bang, bang!
Even after several knocks, the door did not open. I couldn’t hear anything inside, either.
Huh? Is she out?
We might have missed each other on her way out to greet me. That was what I was thinking when a door opened.
Rattle.
It was the door to Ainar’s room, not Missha’s. “Bjorn...!” Ainar greeted me urgently, looking like she’d just woken up. For some reason, alarm bells started going off in my head.
What the...?

At first, it started in the subconscious, but I soon realized what the cause of this strange feeling of wrongness was. If Missha had gone out to greet me, Ainar wouldn’t be here alone, because she would’ve brought her with her.
“Why—! What took you so long!?”
