“Calm down and tell me what happened.” Forcing down my mounting anxiety, I first asked what was going on.
“Missha...! Missha was kidnapped!”
Something had gone wrong while I was away.

chapters.title: Chapter 204: Blessing (4)
paragraphs: Missha had been kidnapped, and in the city too. Just hearing this made it sound like something big had happened, but I calmly awaited more details. If what she was saying was true, it was strange that Ainar had been sleeping peacefully in her room before I arrived.
“Kidnapped? Explain in more detail. What happened, and when did it happen?”
“It happened yesterday!”

The incident happened only a day ago. Apparently, Ainar and Missha had been on their way back from a simple meal out, but upon returning to the inn, they found beastmen in black clothing waiting for Missha.
“Ah! It sounded like they came from Missha’s home!”
That meant they had been sent by the head of her family.
“What do you mean ‘and’?! The beastmen whispered something to Missha and took her by force!”
Hmm, could you really call that by force? “Did Missha say anything to you?”
“She said she’d be back tonight so I just needed to spend today alone. Oh! She also told me to go greet you, Bjorn... but I was so worried that I couldn’t sleep and ended up oversleeping!”
I couldn’t help but laugh. Aside from the oversleeping part, Missha had even had time to give Ainar instructions before leaving, so how could this have been a kidnapping?
When I asked that, the answer I got in return was passionate. “As she said that, Missha looked like she really didn’t want to go! If that’s not kidnapping, what is?!”

Taking away someone who didn’t want to go? That sounded like common barbarian logic—except, I was also one of those barbarians. “Okay, so it’s true that Missha was kidnapped.” I knew just how pointless it was to argue with a barbarian over whether something was a kidnapping or not.
“Right? I was so surprised I went to Aruru too, but I got mad because she acted like it was no big deal!”
“What did Raven say?”
“That I shouldn’t do anything funny and to wait at home until you got back, Bjorn. That’s why I haven’t even reported it to the Public Peace Agency yet!”
Ok, that was a good move on Raven’s part. It was best to leave a barbarian to a barbarian. And if that didn’t work, it was best not to bother talking to one at all.
“So! What are you going to do, Bjorn!? Of course we’re going to break in, right? Missha is our teammate!”
And do you know what will happen if we do that?
“Missha is also a warrior,” I said bluntly. “You have to give her time to figure this out on her own.”
“That’s... I see!”
“She said she’ll be back today, so if she’s not back by tonight, I’ll go looking for her.”
“Okay!” When I explained the situation in a barbarian-like way, Ainar readily agreed without being stubborn.
“It’s morning, are you hungry?”
“Of course I am hungry!”

First, I took Ainar out for breakfast. Then I listened to what had happened while I was away. There was nothing particularly notable, just repetitive days of training, eating, and going home. It seemed the usual meetings with Raven and Mr. Bear had been put on pause until my return.
“Oh, Missha also complimented you back then. She said that even if it doesn’t seem like it, Bjorn is the team’s heart so we can’t get together without you!”

“Oh... I see.” Embarrassment crept in from nowhere. Well, on the bright side, that was a hundred times better than trash-talking me behind my back... I changed the subject. “Did Missha give you money for food?”
“Oh, yeah, but I used it all up.”
“...I’ll leave you money, so use it to buy food until tonight.”
“Are you leaving? Without waiting for Missha?”
“Staying home won’t change anything. I need to do what I have to do. Missha would want that too.”
After the meal, I deposited Ainar in her room and went out. My first stop was the Magic Tower.
“Oh, you’re here? How are you feeling?”
“Thanks to the antidote from Mozlan, everything seems fine.”
“That’s good. You must be tired. Anyway, did you hear about Miss Karlstein?”
“Yes. I plan on checking it out for myself if she doesn’t come back today, so don’t worry.”
“I wasn’t worried to begin with. It’s Miss Ainar who’s acting weird. Why is she freaking out over Miss Karlstein going to her parents’ house?”

I smiled ruefully but kept quiet. Unlike Raven, I knew the backstory surrounding Missha and her family, which was why I had no choice but to worry. “Anyway, I heard you couldn’t divide the loot since I wasn’t there. Let’s meet up tomorrow.”
“What if Miss Karlstein is late?”
“Then I will come back and let you know.”
After that, I briefly asked about what had been going on with her lately, set up a time, and parted ways. The next stop was Mr. Bear’s tavern.
“Oh, you’re back at last. You must be tired.”
“Did anything happen while I was gone?”
“Nothing in particular. But shouldn’t I be asking you that? How was staying in Bifron?”
“It wasn’t bad. It was a comfortable place to live.” Just like with Raven, I exchanged brief updates with Mr. Bear and informed him of the place and time to meet.
“We can finally split that money,” he said.
“Sorry to keep you waiting. You could have asked for your share first.”
“No, those kinds of things have to be done officially in front of everyone to prevent conflict. Besides, it’s not like you were off on vacation.”
“Thanks for understanding. Then I will head out.”

After leaving the tavern, I debated what to do. There was still a lot of time left until dinner, so how should I fill the time? After thinking it over for a while, I headed for the library. Not only was this the perfect place to kill time, but I had to report my survival to someone there.
“...Bjorn Yandel.” As soon as I arrived at the library, Ragna stiffened.
“Long time no see,” I said with a casual smirk.

I was about to explain why I hadn’t shown up for the past twenty days, but before I could do that, Ragna spoke first. “I heard. Not only did you use a special ability in the city, but you violated the rules to enter the labyrinth and were exiled as a result.”
Oh, so she knew. Well, judging by what was said at the Round Table, it sounded like it was common knowledge as much as it was a political issue.
“I am glad that you seem to have returned safely. And I’m sorry.”
“Sorry?” Her apology didn’t make sense in this context at all.
When I tilted my head, Ragna cautiously continued, “I inquired with the steward in case I could help you, but he said there was nothing I could do...”

I still couldn’t understand. Why was she apologizing and who was this steward? When I asked her, Ragna clammed up like she hadn’t meant to say that. I didn’t dig, either, because I figured there was no way she’d tell me about any of that, anyway.
Sounds like she’s talking about her family situation...

My dormant curiosity about Ragna surged to the surface again. She was a wizard in her twenties who was at least rank five, with the stench of wealth emanating from her clothes and wand, and she had even just mentioned a steward. There were times I was unsure considering she was working as a librarian, but she was most definitely a noble.
That’s a bit strange too.
I’d looked into it out of curiosity in the past. There was no noble family with the surname Peprok. So who was she?
“...Are you going to read?”
“Oh, yeah. I intend to.”
Uncomfortable with my stare, Ragna changed the subject. And so I just headed in to read some books.
Well, I’m sure I’ll get the chance to figure it out later.

It wasn’t like she’d ever done anything to harm me. It wouldn’t be good for an outsider to dig into someone else’s family affairs when they didn’t want to talk about it. Whoever she was, our current relationship wasn’t bad.
Anyway, I didn’t find the Complete Books series today, either.

Reading until the sky turned dark outside the window, I slowly cleaned up my spot and got up. After discovering one of the Complete Books by coincidence I continued looking for them on occasion, but I didn’t find any this time, either.
“Are you leaving?”
“There is someone waiting for me.”
“...I see.”
After returning to the inn, I had dinner with Ainar and asked her what she had done that day.
“Today? I took a nap and visited the holy land because I was bored.”
“Holy land?”
“It is fun to teach the young warriors. It makes me nostalgic for the old days too.”
The way I see it, she’s no different from the old days... Well, her combat power did rise tremendously.
“Let’s visit together next time. Everyone wants to see you. It’s already been twenty days.”
“Okay, let’s go together next time.”

Since declaring that I would become the chief of the tribe, I had been visiting the holy land whenever I had time to provide early education, so I agreed without much hesitation. I needed to raise my approval rating in advance, after all.
“Haha, the young warriors will be delighted.”

Since we were both barbarians, by the time that conversation was over, so were our meals. We didn’t head back to our rooms and instead waited on the first floor, which doubled as a restaurant, because Missha wasn’t back yet.
Did something really go wrong?
I grew more worried as the night grew darker, but thankfully Missha appeared about an hour later. In sharp contrast to her usual bright clothing, she was dressed in black. “Huh? Bjorn?”
“It’s Missha! Missha is back!” Ainar ran straight to Missha and hugged her.
“Ah! Don’t. I’m not in the mood for that!” Missha sighed and peeled Ainar off of her. Then she came down and sat in front of me. “...Sorrry. I was planning on waiting for you therrre.”
“It’s fine. I’m not a child. Anyway, how did things go on your end? From what Ainar said, it sounds like something’s happened.”
“Oh, that...” Missha trailed off and glanced at Ainar. “Ainar, you go up and sleep.”
“Eh? How come?”
“Hush.”
“Fine! I’ll go sleep!”
First, she sent Ainar up, and then we talked.
“So, why did your family call you?”
“Well... one of my brothers died so I had to go. After all, I am still a memberrr of the family.”

“It was because of a funeral.” Despite what I was worried about, it didn’t seem like they had really taken her by force. However, one thing was suspicious. “How strange. At this point in time?” The labyrinth had closed weeks ago, so a funeral at this time meant that there must have been a fatal incident in the city.
“Don’t worry, it’s nothing strrrange. He was always sick. The priest had to be called in every day to trrreat him.”
“So it’s not the guy from the Lord of the Floor incident. Then who was it? Judging by your dark expression, was it the big brother who used to be nice to you?” I asked bluntly.
“...You prrrobably don’t know him. I’ve never talked about him to you.”
“Really?” That probably meant it was one of those guys who had bullied and ignored Missha. Then why did she look so gloomy? “Something other than the funeral must have happened, then.”
“...How did you know?”

It was nothing special. If I said I could tell just by the look on her face, though, she’d probably get mad so I beat around the bush a little. “If it was just about the funeral, you wouldn’t have sent Ainar off.”
“Honestly, why arrre you so smart?”
“...Tell me. What happened?”
“Well...” Missha sighed and continued. “Father... No, that man wants me to brrring you home again.”
Why couldn’t everyone just leave me alone? The head of the Karlstein family wanted to see me again. I wondered if there was a new clue about the Ring of the Frost Spirit.
“Anyway, that’s that. You don’t have to go. I already put my foot down and turrrned him down.”

Since Missha took care of it, I didn’t think I’d have to worry about this issue anymore. Apparently, she told him to come visit me himself instead of ordering me to come to him. If there was no news, that would mean whatever he wanted wasn’t a big deal.
If he really comes to find me... I’ll hear him out then. It feels like there’ll be trouble if I go over there myself.
So, that was that.
“Ahh, the more I think about it, the more it pisses me off. What the hell does that man think of me? Funerrral or not, I’m not listening to him anymore.”
Afterward, I chatted with Missha, who was burning with the determination to become independent. I told her about the past twenty days before going to bed.
The next afternoon, we had our meeting.
“It’s been a really long time since we all got together. How have you all been?” said Raven.

All the members of Team Apple Narak were gathered. The location was the three-story tavern where we had been holding meetings since the first day. The goal was to distribute the loot, which hadn’t been paid out yet.
“I heard it yesterday, but I want to hear it one more time. What is the total income?”
“Including the Fox Flame Knot that sold a few days ago, it’s 159 million stones.”
“Is that including the cost of your labor?”

“Yes. I thought about it, but in the end, we killed everyone on that side. It seems funny to claim sole responsibility for the labor now. So the only thing I took out in advance was the cost of the test tube.”

Well, even if it weren’t for that, the loot would have ended up in our hands after the battle. Still, I was surprised. Honestly, I thought she’d claim it all as hers. She’d gotten a bit softer these days, at least compared to when we first met.
“Anyway, I’ve compiled the details of the final settlement here. Please refer to this—it’ll make things easier.”

Reading through the document Raven had prepared with even the receipts attached, we began the official settlements. Mana stone income was evenly distributed. Even equipment and combat income were split equally. However, the herbs harvested in Doppelganger Forest were classified as special loot, so Raven took 40 percent. The potions were not sold and were instead classified as shared items. As the documents were organized in an easy-to-read format, the complicated payments went smoothly.
“Thirty million stones, huh?”
Aside from slight discrepancies, a huge sum of thirty million stones landed in each lap, our highest income ever. But now we had to start the repayment process.

“Now then, all that remains is the settlement for the loot we’ve kept. Actually, I have some spare time these days so I’ve organized these a bit too. As customary, the payment is set at about 70 percent of the average market price so it will be much cheaper than actually buying them.” Raven spoke while looking at each one of us. “First, Miss Karlstein. The leather boots augmented with Acceleration and Adjustment magic are 2.1 million. The lithinum necklace with Cold Reinforcement is 2.7. That’s a total of 4.8 million. But since your share is being subtracted here... You just have to pay 3.84 million stones.”
“Miss Ainar’s expandable backpack is 1.5 million... That’s it. Just pay 1.2 million stones.”
“Ugh.”
“Mr. Urikfried’s sub-space quiver is 2.1 million. The steel breastplate is 550,000... But why did you take the breastplate?”
“...I’m going to get an Adjustment spell placed on it and give it to Iradun.”
“That’s not a bad idea. Although it will be cumbersome to put it on him each time you summon him... Anyway, you can pay 2.12 million stones.”
Aside from Raven, who did not take any personal loot, everyone placed their payment on the table. Then it was my long-awaited turn. How much would I have to cough up?
“And finally, Mr. Yandel. First, 3.1 million for the idium gaiters. Then 3.3 million for No. 8667: Outlaw of the Wilderness.”
“Wait a minute, leave out Outlaw of the Wilderness. I intend to keep it as a team item, not personal loot.”
“...A team item?”
“It might be useful against that guy on the fifth floor. It’ll be a good idea to hold on to it for then.”

“Hmm.” Raven looked at me like an IRS employee looking at a tax evader. But in the end, she agreed. “That sounds reasonable. Although I feel like I’m getting the short stick here. Let’s move on to the next one.” Before I could even feel relieved about saving some money, Raven moved on to the final items, those which could be called the crown jewel of this settlement. “The Essence of the Manticore, and No. 2988: Mark of the Guard Corps. To start, the Manticore essence averages 50 million at auction, but the value of the test tube was already subtracted, and the value was also calculated based on the official guild price.”
“So, what’s the official price?”
“32 million stones.”
Goddamn it. Then if I add a 30 percent discount here, as is customary, and subtract a fifth since I’ll be receiving 20 percent back as my share after I pay for it...
“For the Manticore, you’ll be paying 17.92 million stones.”
That was still expensive, though. “...What about the Mark of the Guard Corps?”
“That’s 52 million stones as per the average auction price.”
That wasn’t much different from the price in the game. Likewise, if I added a discount here, things came out to a final value of 29.12 million stones.
“And then if you add the idium gaiters to that, it’s a total of 48,776,000 stones.” Raven grinned and continued, “Have you saved up some money?”
I kept my mouth shut and looked at Ainar.
“Huh? Why are you looking at me all of a sudden?”
“Ainar, how much money did you borrow from me again?”
“A-Are you stealing my money...!?”
No, I’m just getting it back.

Indeed, this expedition brought in a record-breaking income. However, after paying for everything that needed to be paid for, even my savings so far weren’t enough. Even if I included the money I lent to Ainar, the amount was too large to pay off all at once. Of course, that was no problem for me.
“Ainar, while you’re paying back your money, lend me some more.”
“Hmm? I was told teammates shouldn’t give each other mon—”
“Oh, I’ll pay you back.”
“O-Okay...!”
“Missha, I’d like you to lend me some too.”
“Geeeez, how much do you need?”

The thirteen million I lacked was made up for with loans from Ainar and Missha. As a result, I was in debt. When was I going to be able to pay this off? Should I be hoping to run into a plunderer in the labyrinth or something?
“I am rich now!”

Her depression from lending me money was short-lived. Ainar, whom Missha and I had been taking care of up until a few days ago because she had no wages, started spending her money like no tomorrow. Well, maybe that was an exaggeration. She did buy snacks generously, but because the prices were so cheap, it wasn’t an expense that stood out.
“Bjorn, what should I do with this money?” asked Missha.
“Just hold on to it. You can get a new set of equipment once we’re back.”
“Okay.”
“Oh! Me too! I want new gear too!”
“Be patient this month. Some items will be custom-made and they won’t be completed before the labyrinth opens.”

Because of how much the payout had been delayed, I decided to put off spending until next month. Now that a big sum had come in, I planned to custom order equipment that would get us to the seventh floor, even if that meant only getting one or two pieces of gear at a time. Of course, I couldn’t tell her to spend all her money on that.
“Still, since you earned a lot, don’t save all of it and use it where you want to. Isn’t that why you earned it in the first place?”
“Huh? C-Can I do that?”
What did this kid think of me? Getting stronger was important, but I didn’t intend to make her sacrifice her life for it. “Looks like there’s something you want to do, then?”
“Yeah.”
“What are you looking at me like that for? You’re spending your own money.”
“Well, it’s not just that...” When I shot her a questioning look, Missha cautiously opened her mouth. “Can we move somewhere else?”
“...What?”
“Now that we’re earrrning a lot of money, I was wondering if we can move somewhere better... I can’t even cook here.”

Hmm, no wonder she was studying our reactions like that. I thought it over for a while and agreed since this inn was starting to feel cramped. Besides, Missha’s food tasted much better than the restaurant food here and was healthier to boot.
“Then let’s look into where we can move soon. For now, we have to prepare for our next trip into the labyrinth.”
“Okay!”

After that was our first normal day in a long time. It was a peaceful time. We gathered together to plan for the expedition, I met up with Rotmiller to receive my usual scouting lessons, which had been put on hold, and sometimes I visited the commercial district to see if there were any items to buy. As always, those days passed by like a bolt of lightning.
“If everyone is here, let’s start heading over.”
We met at Mr. Bear’s tavern like last time.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
It was time to enter the labyrinth.

chapters.title: Chapter 205: Instant (1)
paragraphs: Inside a palace located deep within Noark’s fortress, a man was talking to someone through a crystal ball. “Amelia Rainwales. Have you found the adventurer?”
“Not yet, my lord.”
“I see...”
This was the first scheduled report he was receiving since the city’s lockdown. It was only natural that there hadn’t been any progress yet, but the castle’s lord fell into silence nonetheless.
More bad news soon came his way. “But I have one more thing to tell you.”
“What is it? Tell me.”
“It is said that the palace will be distributing specially manufactured identification tags to adventurers starting this month.”
“...Are they magical devices?”
“Yes.”
“Explain in detail. I’m sure you’ve learned more information about them already.”

The lord of the castle listened to Amelia’s intel on the identification tags that were scheduled to be distributed by the palace. The more he listened, the more depressing the contents became. The identification tags had been designed by the palace’s wizard.
“It’ll take at least several months for us to come up with something similar.”
“Yes, I think so too.”
“Thank you for letting me know. Don’t worry about us and focus on your mission. See you next month.”
After that, the lord of the castle closed his eyes and fell into deep thought. Much time passed like that.

“Ah, you’re here.” Having called for the quaestor, the first thing the lord of the castle did was inquire into Noark’s current financial situation. To be precise, he asked the following question: “Quaestor, how long can we last without entering the labyrinth?”
“Three months, if things continue to hold steady.”

In the fallout of the battle, things weren’t looking good for Noark. However, there had never been a time when they were ahead of their opponents, so this was familiar to them. Their ancestors had dealt with the same.
“What if we starve and hold out? How long can we last then?”
“...Perhaps twice that amount of time.”
“I see.” The lord of the castle nodded. Then he called for his counselor and instructed, “Until I give orders stating otherwise, seal the labyrinth and make sure no one can enter.”
“...The backlash will be severe. Can we know how long this will last?”

“At least until we can copy the identification tags made by the palace,” the lord of the castle replied, voice firm. If Noark’s people headed in before that, they would definitely be doomed to a disgraceful death. “Until then, we hold out as long as possible and let them lower their guard.”
They had to have patience and wait. Then it would surely come—their one opportunity to change everything.
[The labyrinth is now closed. You are being transported to Rafdonia.]

Light sank through my closed eyelids. When I slowly opened my eyes, the clear sky filled them for the first time in a while. The warm city air circulated through the deepest parts of my lungs with each breath. I was truly sensing the flow of time with my whole body.
Is it already June?
It had already been six months since I had been exiled to Bifron. The winter here, which was a joke compared to Korea, was long over and even its short spring was coming to an end.
Interesting.

It had been March when I first came to this world. It really had been over a year since I got here. It had hit me when I had paid my first year of taxes too, but the strange feeling lingered. To be honest, memories of my life on Earth were starting to fade. That was a given. If you add the time I had spent in the labyrinth, my time here technically amounted to almost two years.
“Hey, are you going back to your inn right away?”
“For now. Let’s wash up and get some drinks.”
“We’re baaack!”
Confirming that everything around me was business as usual, I shook off the thoughts in my head.
Nothing big happened this time, either.
I wondered how the other floors had fared, but judging by the reactions of those around me, it seemed there hadn’t been anything notable. That was making me anxious.
Shaaaaaa.

I looked down and checked my wrists. Although it hadn’t been long since my return to the city, the identification tag etched like a tattoo on my wrist was already disappearing into a burst of light. It was cumbersome getting a new one each time, but it was different from the old identification tags that could be stolen. Coincidentally, since these things had been released, there had been no trace of those underground bastards.
It’s about time they show up...

Earth had a distinctly different ecosystem from this place, which was a world with no flowing rivers or fertile land for farming. To survive, both Noark and Rafdonia had to create food with mana stones from the labyrinth.
But already six months with no news, huh?

Since hearing from Fox that the mega clans had formed an alliance to prepare for an ambush from Noark at the last Round Table, I was even more anxious. Where were they all hiding? It wasn’t like there was a way for them to get food other than mana stones.
“Mr. Yandel! What took you so long?” As I walked and thought things over, I could see Raven waving at me in the distance. Even Mr. Bear, who was always late, was there before me.
“I had something to think about.”
“Hmm, you could’ve done that while you were in line...”

Yep, she only cared about efficiency, this one. Anyway, since I was late, I apologized and stood in line. It only took a few minutes for the line to move up. That was because this was the rank-five checkpoint.
“Team Apple Narak, is that right?”

This was one of many changes that had happened in the past six months. Me, Ainar, and Missha had been promoted to rank five, making the team’s rank go up one level. You had to complete a commission from the guild to become rank five, which was a bit cumbersome, but we did it together three months ago. Having a low rank was bound to get you looked down on, and getting looked down on was bound to attract trouble.
“Wow, they even hand out candy here. Bjorn, did you know?”
“I didn’t know that.” I put the candy Missha handed me in my mouth and sucked on it. “It’s sweet.”
Rafdonia was a city that was unfailingly cruel toward the weak. But slowly, I was starting to feel respected everywhere I went.
“Are we splitting the loot tomorrow?”
“Why are you asking the obvious?”
“Oooh! Then let’s go! To home!”

After exchanging our mana stones, we headed out into the city. The rank-five checkpoint even offered a bathing facility for convenience but we didn’t use it this time, either. Why would we when we could just wash up at home?
“See you guys tomorrow. Honey, I’m back!”

We split up in front of Mr. Bear’s tavern to avoid a lost child incident and then headed straight home, to a four-story building in the center of District Seven which was only ten minutes away from the commercial district of Kommelby. The first and second floors were occupied by us and the third and fourth floors were used by another adventurer couple. The entrances were different so we rarely ever ran into each other.
“Ahh, home!”

Unlike our previous accommodations, which were a single room each, our new home was superior in every aspect. It had been only two months since we had moved in. It was a property that we liked, and the previous tenant left around then. Of course, we were only renting it. The purchase price was insane.
“Since we take a long time to wash up, eat before us if you’re hungrrry!”

Ainar and Missha headed into the first-floor bathroom, which had a bathtub, and I washed myself in the small bathroom on the second floor. Well, I was calling it small, but it was in much better condition than our previous one. Washing myself with soap, I chuckled.
This can be considered a change too.

We had a spacious house with a kitchen, the type of soap sold in artisan shops and not the mass-produced stuff, and even an expensive bed that I had bought as a big investment. Rather than saving each penny I earned to return home, I started to improve my quality of life here. However, I didn’t want to consider this a waste. How many years would I be here? Since the Genesis Treasures had disappeared, I didn’t even know if it was possible to go back.
In the first place... I don’t even know if I have to go back.
As I came out of the bathroom, I scrubbed my hair dry with a towel as if to shake my wavering resolve right out of my head.
Shwaaa!

It sounded like they were still washing up downstairs. I was hungry, but since Missha’s food tasted so much better than anything I could buy, I sat on the sofa and dozed off for a bit. I wasn’t sure how much time had passed.
“You woke up just in time. Come eat.”

Turning my eyes to the kitchen, which emanated an appetizing smell, I saw a whole table was set. Since there were two barbarians present, most of the dishes on it were meat. We exchanged casual conversations while we ate.
“Oh, rrright. Are you taking the equipment over today?”
“I should. You need to take good care of it if you want it to last for a long time. Once we’re done eating, pass everything along to me. I’ll head over alone.”
“Okay. But are you going to Hikurod’s forge again?”
“We should use it often, at least. It’s not like you need a special skill to inspect weapons.”

In the past few months, the dwarf had opened a forge. It had been about three months now, but since this was the type of business where regular customers formed the foundation, it felt like we couldn’t avoid suffering through some mediocrity. It did seem to be getting better, though.
“But, speaking of Hikurod... If his shop fails, he’ll come back to adventuring, rrright?”
“That question... don’t ask that in front of him.”
“What, do you think I’m dense? I have a brain too, you know. I’m just a little worrried.”
“Haha, Missha, what are you so worried about? If he fails, we can employ him as our steward!”
“A steward...?”
“Hikurod is fun!”
What did she think a steward was? I couldn’t tell, but taking something a barbarian said at face value would be a foolish thing to do.
Agreeing that that would be fun, we laughed and chatted about pointless things for a long while.
“Then I’m going to head to the forge, so you guys get some rest.”
“Do you want us to come with you?”
“It’s fine. I’m not going anywhere important.”

Leaving the kids to get a nap, I packed up the equipment and headed to the dwarf’s forge. Then, after leaving the gear there for inspection and repair, I came back home and also lay in bed—an extra-large bed I had purchased for a whopping 350,000 stones.
Yeah, this is it.

Satisfied with its enduring softness, I closed my eyes, reminded of the past for some reason. Was it when we missed the last wagon of the day and I had to sleep in Kommelby with Missha? At the time, I had wondered when I would be able to sleep in a bed like this every day and had sighed that I had a long way to go.

It had now been over a year since I first came to this city. I was no longer fazed by blood splattering all over my body, and rather felt that days without blood were stranger. At this point, I no longer felt anything about harming monsters, or even people.
Before going to sleep, I asked myself: was I living more like a human than back then?
My nap, which lasted until the next morning, ended when Missha dropped in. “You said you werrre planning on leaving around now. Wake up!”
“Ah, thanks.”
“Hungry? You want food?”
“No, I’m supposed to eat out.”
“Oh, rrreally?”

As I washed up and was getting ready to leave, I heard snoring from the first floor. It sounded like Ainar was still sleeping. For reference, Missha and I were each using a bedroom on the second floor. Although there were two rooms on the first floor...
Honnnk!
...That girl snored louder than me. The remaining room on the first floor was just being used as a storage room.
“See you at the tavern later.”
“Okay, see you!”

I said goodbye to just Missha and left the house. Instead of taking a wagon, I headed to Kommelby, which was a ten-minute walk. Crossing the castle wall and walking for thirty more minutes, I reached the public platform where we agreed to meet.
Raven was already there. “You’re late. The wagon arrived a long time ago.”
“I think you’re just early today?”
“Tsk, you’re too sharp for your own good. Come on, let’s go. Before I starve to death.”

After meeting up with Raven, we had a meal at a restaurant we frequented and then headed around the general stores and exchanges to dispose of the loot from our previous expedition. This time our profits were higher than usual. This was thanks to a rank-five essence that had appeared in the hidden world on the other side of Mila Roden’s mirror.
“Looks like it’ll take some time until it’s sold. Let’s use my money for the payout and I’ll receive my share from this later,” said Raven.
“That’s fine with us, but are you okay with that?”
“Why would I not be okay with it? Waiting until it sells and then gathering again to split the pay would be a lot of work for no reason.”
That was true, but we’d been sticking with this method until now since we figured it would lead to the fewest issues.
“...What? What’s with that look?”
“Nothing.”
“Doesn’t seem like nothing.”
“You are mistaken.”
Struggling to hold back my laughter, I walked forward. Come to think of it, this girl had changed a lot too, although she still struggled to be honest about her feelings.
“We finished up faster than I expected. Let’s wait at the tavern.”
After selling all the loot, we headed to the tavern that served as our meeting place. As expected, no one else had arrived yet.
“It’s better this way. I didn’t even have time to make a list last time.”

After ordering just drinks, Raven pulled out a piece of paper and began to write down all the items we were splitting today in advance. It took longer than I expected. Every time I asked about it, she always said it was no big deal.
“Thanks.”
“...Why are you saying that out of nowhere?”
“You’re always taking on troublesome tasks on our team’s behalf.”
“If there was even one other person who could do this aside from me, I wouldn’t be doing it. Why don’t you pay me while you’re at it?”
“Okay, I will. How much do you want? The others will be happy to do so too.”
“...Never mind. It’s not like I can get rich off of money like that.”
Geez, if it weren’t for her tone of voice, she would have been a lot more popular.
“Oh, I thought I would be the last one to get here.” A while later, Mr. Bear arrived. Soon the melee sisters also showed up and the distribution process began.
“It’s 8.5 million per person.”
Thanks to Mila Roden spitting out a mirror this time around, a lump sum landed on our laps. My debt had already been paid off two months ago, so this income all went into my pocket.
“Then let’s talk about something else now.”

After the settlement was over, we casually made plans for our next expedition over food and drinks. Well, it would be more accurate to say I was telling them the plan rather than collaborating with them on it, actually.
“We will not be going to Hellfire Gorge anymore.”
“Excuse me? Why not?”

For the past half a year, we’d been hunting in Hellfire Gorge and had entered Mila Roden’s Mirror of Fire a total of three times. We had finished exploring the Ashen Mountain Range and Lava Lake, which we hadn’t been able to tackle before. It wasn’t too tough. Along with the Orb of Fire, which reduced Fire damage, our combat power was now much higher than when we first entered that place.
“Why would we leave a place we’re compatible with and go somewhere else?” Since she was having fun in Hellfire Gorge, Raven expressed concerns about my decision.

However, I wouldn’t compromise on this. “We can’t stay on the fifth floor forever. It’s time to explore other places now.” We had obtained everything we could from Hellfire Gorge, so it was time to move on to the next stage.
“So where are we going?”
“Frost Canyon.”
“Uh, Frost Canyon...” Missha trailed off and glanced at me. She knew that, unlike Hellfire Gorge, this was an area that could be good for her.
Well, she wasn’t wrong. Frost Canyon dropped several essences that had good synergy with Missha, who was an Ice-attribute adventurer.
That’s one of the things I’m after too. Then, once we get a particular essence, we’ll be done with Frost Canyon.

After that, I planned to collect just experience points from the remaining two areas in the Great Demon Realm and pave the way to the sixth floor. It would take another year just to get there, though.
Still, we’ve come far.
That was what I was thinking when the ring of vines on my finger began to glow.
Shaaaaaa!
“Bjorn, is that...”
Unlike the first time, I didn’t deny it. I didn’t even try rubbing it with saliva to put it back together. It would make no difference.
[The activation conditions for Blessing of the Stars have been met.]
The second vine that was blocking my Dragon Slayer-related death flags snapped.
God damn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 206: Instant (2)
paragraphs: “It’s been a while, Miss Rainwales.”
Upon receiving a call from the city through the crystal ball, Amelia found herself tilting her head. This was not the familiar voice of the lord of the castle. “...The alchemist?”
“Haha, it’s an honor that you recognize my voice.”
“...How are you able to use this communication network?”
“I asked the lord. I have a favor to ask of you and wanted to ask myself. Isn’t that better for both of us? This way we can hear each other’s voices too.”

“I see.” She got it now. The alchemist was more important in Noark than even the lord of the castle. If he requested something, the lord had to listen. Amelia hurriedly got to the point. “So, what’s the favor you want to ask?”
“Oh, it’s nothing big. But besides that, how are you?”
“...You know that question isn’t a good one to ask someone like me.”
“Still haven’t shaken it off?”
Amelia kept her mouth shut and avoided answering. Having known her since she was young, he was one of the few people who knew her backstory.
“Miss Rainwales, I have my guesses as to why you accepted this mission. But you must let go of that now. Your sister would not want you to take revenge—”
“Enough.” Amelia cut him off coldly. “Stop talking about that and get to the point.” Those left behind had their own work to do. She didn’t want anyone to interfere with that, even this old man.
“...All right. Then I’ll get to my business.”

Afterward, the alchemist recited a few items he needed and Amelia recorded them on a piece of paper so she wouldn’t forget. Most of them were alchemical ingredients like magic reagents—nothing special but things hard to come by with the city in lockdown.
“How long will it take to get them all?”
“A few days is enough.”
“Is that so? Then can you get me just the sleeping flower powder a little earlier?”
“I can send you that right now.”
“Oh, do you have some?”

“You already know I do.” Sleeping flower powder had the same effects as a sleeping pill. Although it wasn’t that strong, she often used it because it had the ability to bypass poison tolerance, not for the enemy, but for oneself. “I’ll put it in sub-space once this call is over.”
“Haha, then I guess today’s business is already done?” The old man laughed, but his voice sounded somewhat downcast.
Just as she was about to end the transmission, Amelia stopped when a question suddenly popped into her head. “But... what do you need the sleeping flower powder for?”

Amelia felt awkward even as she asked that. It was a question she wouldn’t have normally asked. She rarely asked questions of others first, especially out of simple curiosity. However... Something was different today. She felt like she was missing something important.
“There are no alchemical formulas that require sleeping flower powder,” she said.

“Oh, that?” Before long, the old man’s voice came through the crystal ball. “The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos. I’m going to use it to treat him. Oh, not in the medicine itself, but because it’ll be more convenient to put him to sleep first.”
“Did you come up with a way to return his memory?”
“No, but I’m going to treat his damaged body first. As you know, we need all the firepower we can get.”
“I see.” Amelia involuntarily let out a sigh of relief. As long as his memories didn’t come back, whether he recovered or not wouldn’t matter to her.
“Haha, but once his body recovers, I plan to restore his memories too.”
Amelia stiffened.
“It’s just that the method for doing so is so intense that it’ll be too much on his body right now. And since the sample size is so small, the success rate is only about half right now.”
A 50 percent success rate—too big a possibility to leave to chance. However, that wasn’t a huge issue. Everything would be fine as long as his body didn’t recover.
“I see.”
After that, Amelia cut off the transmission. As promised, she put the sleeping flower powder in the two-way sub-space... after applying a poison that destroyed living tissue on top of it.
The second vine had torn off. It had been quiet for a while, which had put my mind at ease.
What the hell is that bastard up to?

Unease started to creep in. I wasn’t ready to face him yet. Although I’d grown in many areas, it was only to the extent that I’d gone from a fourth-floor adventurer to a fifth-floor adventurer. To think there was only one vine left now...
The sixth floor. I have to get to the sixth floor as soon as possible.
On the sixth floor, there was a chance I would be able to absorb a specific essence, my second core essence following Giantization. If only I could somehow beat that—
“Mister!”
“Huh?”
“What are you thinking so deeply about?”

The sound of Erwen’s voice jarred me from my thoughts. Was it because the recent bout of peace had lasted so long? It wasn’t like the last vine had broken off, yet anxious imaginings kept cropping up and cluttering my head.
“I’m sorry. What were we talking about?”
“We weren’t... I was asking you what we should order.”
“Oh, right.” Reading through the menu, I ordered a suitable snack and beer.

“But this place hasn’t changed a bit,” Erwen said while watching the worker leave after taking our order. I didn’t have to ask to know exactly what she was talking about. “Even though we’ve changed so much.”

The tavern was called Fidenpus, the same one where Erwen and I had had our return drink after completing our first-ever quest. That was why we couldn’t help this strange feeling of nostalgia. The barbarian who had once had a hell of a time on the first floor because he didn’t have a night companion was now a fairly well-known adventurer in the city. But I wasn’t the only one who had gained notoriety—Erwen had also grown tremendously by the time she reached her first full year. You just had to look at her equipment for proof.
“This is our first time having drinks since a few months ago, right?”
“Ah, when you paid your taxes for the first year?”

For reference, that had been just after I moved. As I was trying to decide where to meet today, I had chosen this place for that reason. Missha obviously wouldn’t like it if I invited her home. Since our home was a space shared by three people now, I couldn’t just do whatever I wanted.
“Did anything happen during this expedition?”
“...Yes, well. Same as always.”

Once the drinks and platters came out, we started talking in earnest. The main topic of conversation was what was going on in each other’s lives. Now that I had fewer meetings with the girl who used to come over every day, we didn’t have anything to talk about other than this.
“How is the vibe in your clan? I’m curious. Any news?”
“I’m not sure. Even if there is, they don’t tell us anything...”

After serving as mercenaries for an acquaintance’s clan, Erwen and her sister resumed their exploration of the labyrinth with other members of the clan. They were active on the fifth floor too, but since our team only hunted in Hellfire Gorge, we hadn’t run into each other in the labyrinth yet.
“Anyway, I’m frustrated out of my mind. I mentioned this before, right? There is someone who keeps flirting with my sister. Now he’s even coming onto me.”
“Sounds annoying.”
“Yeah, and it’s not like I can plant an arrow between his brows since he’s executive level... I guess I just have to be patient. Until I get everything I need and leave.”

The more we talked, the more I realized just how much she had changed. It had been a little over a year since she became an adventurer, and unlike back then, she was no longer innocent. In a way, that made sense. One year in the labyrinth was enough time to see all kinds of things.
“Anyway, you said you had something to tell me?” Figuring that the time was ripe, I brought up the main reason we were meeting today.
“Oh, that...” After a moment’s pause, Erwen parted her lips. “Do you remember? When I said I had a lot left to learn from my sister...”

“I remember.” She told me that she would absorb everything like a sponge for half a year and then come join my party. Well, it had already been more than half a year since then, but I never brought it up first. Not only were there no empty slots on our team... “Since you haven’t said anything since then, I thought you changed your mind.”
I had thought that conversation was pretty much over. But was that not the case?
Erwen vehemently denied it. “H-Hey, what are you talking about? There’s no way. We were each other’s first-night companions!”
Technically, my first-night companion was Hans A, and hers was Harts Young or whatever his name was.
“So, what do you want to say?”
“I... think it will take some more time.”
“What do you mean?”
“Y-You’re all rank five, right? As of right now, there is no room for me to squeeze in... To be honest, it almost feels like there’s no hope. W-Well, you even l-live together now...”
“What are you saying? Stop mumbling and speak up.”
At my words, Erwen gulped down the rest of her drink. “I regret it. Back then... why didn’t I just accept your offer? I thought I could close the gap quickly, but it’s only getting wider...”

Those words were more of a lament than an actual statement, but I thought I knew what she was trying to say. She wanted to join our party but she didn’t want to ask me to remove someone. It wasn’t like her specs were better than those of the current members, either. Hmm, still, it seemed she hadn’t changed her mind.
“Anyway. So, what I want to say is...”
“Enough.” I stopped her there. First of all, there was a misunderstanding that needed to be cleared up. “I had no intention of putting you on my team from the beginning.”

“...Pardon?” Erwen went momentarily still. It took a while for her eyes, which were staring blankly out into space, to focus enough for her to shoot me a baffled look. “W-What do you mean? You never mentioned anything like that back then. I-I thought it was guaranteed...” Erwen’s eyes bounced around, unable to settle on one place, almost like her mind was short-circuiting.
Whoops, that was not what I meant. I cut her off before the misunderstanding could grow any worse. “Erwen, I’m going to form a clan.”
“C-Clan?!”
“Not now, of course—it will take a few more months. But if that’s still okay with you, I want you to—”
“Yes! I want to join!” The answer came before I even finished speaking.
“No, first I should explain in more detail—”
“It’s okay! I’m joining anyway!”
“...If you say so. Anyway, this is a secret. I haven’t told anyone in my party yet.”
“Uh, so I’m the first one you’re asking...?”

I cocked my head. “Yes, of course you are.” I hadn’t even told them I was making a clan, so how could I have asked? Considering our relationship, I didn’t even have to ask Missha and Ainar. As a member of the Magic Tower, Raven would probably refuse. And Mr. Bear I wasn’t sure about.
He seems to have a bad history with clans.
As I was thinking this, Erwen let out a strange burst of laughter. “Hehe, hehehe!”
My drinking party with Erwen, which started early in the evening, lasted longer than expected. Originally, my plan was just to hear out why she asked to see me, listen to some news, and part ways.
“What? The clan master is bald?”
“Yeah, I’m telling you. You have no idea how hard it was for me to hold back laughter when his wig came off during the hunt.”
The conversation with Erwen was more fun than usual. Was it because I was drinking for the first time in a while? I didn’t know why something so trivial was so funny to me.
Oh, the others will be waiting for me at home...
The thought occurred to me a few times, but each time it did, Erwen brought up an amusing story so I couldn’t find the right time to slip away. Still, it was time to go back now.
“Um, we should—”
“Oh, right!”
“Huh?”
“Did I mention that I absorbed a new essence this time?”
What? She got a new essence? I couldn’t just ignore that.
“It’s a very unique ability. It suits me too.”
“Stop stalling and tell me. What did you get?” I straightened my back and refocused on what Erwen was saying.
To start with, it was rank five. As it was an essence recommended to her by her veteran sister, it was a very compatible one for an elven archer like her.
She won’t have to erase this one later.
Already planning to map out a cultivation route for Erwen once I got back, I asked all kinds of questions about her newly acquired essence.
“Wow, Mister, did you know your eyes just got really bright?”
That was a given. Regardless of what happened, I used to be a player who had been more in love with this game than anyone else.
“It’s an essence people say is super unique. Of course I’m curious how it works in real life.”
“Still, I am at a loss as to how to explain it. It’s not like I can show it to you...”
Hmm, that was true. I was about to nod in agreement when—
“Um, actually, about that...” Erwen trailed off and glanced at me. A red tinge lingered on her face, probably because she was tipsy. “Do you want to see my special ability upstairs quick?”
...What should I do?

chapters.title: Chapter 207: Instant (3)
paragraphs: Most of the taverns in the city doubled as inns.
“Do you want to see my special ability upstairs quick?”
She was offering to grab a room to show me her ability. This had happened once before so it wasn’t all that strange. However...
“That won’t work.”
“...Pardon?”
To Erwen’s bewilderment, I firmly refused the offer. “It’s late. I have to get home.” I had a cat waiting for me. “Show me later when you get a chance.”
“Oh... okay!”
I knew myself well. As a gamer more interested in this world than anyone else, if I saw that special ability now, I’d spend all night experimenting with it.
“Ah, you’re herrre?” When I parted with Erwen and arrived home, Missha walked over from where she was reading a cookbook in the living room and sniffed me. “Smells like you didn’t drrrink that much.”
“I didn’t feel like it.”
“Hmm, is that so?”

I hadn’t committed a crime or anything, but for some reason, it was hard to meet her eyes. Was it because I hadn’t told her I was meeting Erwen? Hmm, that was probably the reason. But if I told her she wouldn’t have liked it... I had no choice.
I smoothly changed the subject. “Anyway, where’s Ainar?”
“Sleeping in her rrroom.”
“...I see. You should sleep too.”

As I ended the short conversation and was about to head upstairs, Missha stopped me. “Wait, go sit over there.” Had I been caught? “It’s good to let your stomach digest beforrre bed. I’ll boil some stew for you.”
“Ah... thanks.” As instructed, I sat down at the kitchen table. Missha put on an apron and started cooking, and I silently watched her back. Her tail was moving.
Swish, swish.
It felt like I had done something wrong. I didn’t have to think for long. “I met Erwen today.” I decided to confess it before I missed the golden opportunity.
“...Rrreally?” she answered a beat later but she didn’t seem too surprised.
“Are you mad?”

At my question, Missha chuckled. “Why would I be? Stuff like that is rrreserved for those who actually stand a chance.” With that, Missha tossed the pot full of stew in the trash. Her words did not match her actions.
“Why did you...?”
“Oh, it didn’t taste rrright.”
“I-I see?”
“Wait, I’ll cook you another one.”
Soon, Missha boiled up a new pot of stew and served it on the table. Then she went up to her room, saying she was tired.
What was that just now?
Despite the strangeness, I ate the stew in the bowl. As always, it felt perfect on my taste buds and went down easily. Yet the other one didn’t taste right?
No way.
After finishing my meal, I cleared the table a bit and opened the trash can. I froze in a daze, holding the lid.
...Good thing I decided to be honest.
The stew in the trash was full of carrots. She already knew, from the moment she came up to sniff me, who I had met with today.

Time was like flowing water. You couldn’t stop it with your hands, and what flowed through your fingers slipped downstream, impossible to get back. We had only one option—to get on this boat called life and row toward our goal, whatever it took.
Yes, let’s start another day.

Getting up from bed, I studied the mirror for a moment to motivate myself. This was a bit of know-how that came with being a gamer. You had to do things like this so you didn’t get tired of all those repetitive quests.
“Bjorn... Oh, you’re awake? Then go wake Ainar for me.”
“Okay.”
And as this was a repetitive quest, my life these days was exactly the same every day. Wake up at 7 a.m., wake Ainar, have a meal Missha cooked for us, and get ready to go out.
“Librarrry again?”
“Why, do you want to come with me?”
“No, that’s okay. I’m going to take Ainar to the trrraining center later.”
Once breakfast was over, Missha and Ainar headed to the training center where they’d bought a monthly pass to stretch their legs and I headed straight to the library.
“Are you here to read that book again?”
“It was more interesting than I thought.”
“Haha, be grateful. I thought that would be the case so I took it out in advance.”
Recently, I was reading an ultra-long novel series. It was a recommendation of Ragna’s and it was more interesting than I expected. Since it was set in the labyrinth, the worldbuilding was rich too.
Though, the characters are all too nice so it’s not realistic at all.
Still, as a novel, it wasn’t unbearable. If I were being honest, this was good entertainment. Aside from drinking, there weren’t too many hobbies to enjoy in this world, which was a problem.
“Have a nice day.”

As always, around 1 p.m., I closed the book I was reading, left the library, and had lunch. The menu was a meat-filled lunchbox Missha had prepared. Once I finished eating it at the fountain, the time soon came for me to meet with Rotmiller.
“You are late today. About thirty seconds. To become a great scout, you have to know just how important time is. Since you were late, let’s start class right away.”

It had already been over a year since I’d started scout training with Rotmiller. To be honest, I thought it would be over in a month or two. But Rotmiller’s knowledge was like the sea—the more I learned, the more I realized there was yet to know.
“Now that you seem to know all the basics, let’s move on to the intensive course.”
“Before that, what happened to the thing I mentioned yesterday?”
“You mean setting up a school?”
“Yes.”

It was Rotmiller who had first mentioned the idea of setting up a school, but the more training I received from this man, the more I thought the school would be a huge hit. Even if you didn’t have hearing as great as an elf’s, a nose as good as a beastperson’s, or an inherent talent for navigation, it was possible to acquire the skills of a scout with his help. The master of hard work—that was the essence of who Rotmiller was. This alone was attractive enough, but having started from the bottom himself, even the man’s teaching skills were first-class.
But he doesn’t know his own worth yet.
Honestly, it was a wonder why he still hadn’t done it. Unlike the dwarf’s forge, he didn’t even need any initial capital to get started.
“Seriously consider it. You’ve been screwing around for months since then.”
“I’m not screwing around, I’m taking advantage of the free time I didn’t have before to train.”
“If that’s the case, shouldn’t you do even more of this? Sometimes teaching can help you learn.”
“That’s... hard to argue with. I actually have learned a lot while teaching you.”
“So, your answer?”
“I still don’t feel like it.”
I quietly clicked my tongue. It seemed Rotmiller didn’t want to officially retire from the adventuring profession yet. “Really? Let me know when you decide. I will help.”
“Thanks for the sentiment, at least.”
“They’re not empty words. I’m being sincere.”

In fact, I already had a rough plan in place. First, he could rent out a training center, in the beginning, to use as a classroom and market the class toward human kids who hoped to become adventurers. Once he established that, he could advertise to the Adventurers’ Guild and operate a separate, adventurers-only class. That would make more money, anyway. Of course, it’d take considerable time for him to reach that point.
But Rotmiller is human.
Humans paid fewer taxes. If he secured a job and got a certain amount of profit, he wouldn’t have any problem putting food on the table for the rest of his life.
All of that means nothing if he says no, though.

If capital was an issue, I was willing to invest to some extent. The concept of a stock market was still new in this world, but it was not completely nonexistent. It was a perfect way to manage my money too.
“Today’s lesson is finished.”

Anyway, after receiving training for a few hours after that, today’s class reached its end. It was about 8 p.m. Maybe it was because this was an intensive course, but the explanations were longer than usual so we ended an hour late.
“Then tomorrow... No, I won’t be able to come tomorrow,” said Rotmiller.
“Let’s say three days to be sure.”
“Let’s do that. Take care of yourself this time around too.”

Anyway, my structured daily routine ended there. In the evenings, I normally had a drink with other adventurers introduced to me by the dwarf or Mr. Bear and listened to industry trends, or met with the rest of the party to socialize, but I had no one to meet up with today. Since I’d already completed my own special routine that occurred every midnight on the 15th, my schedule was completely empty. It had been a long time since I had free time to myself.
Should I go to the library again? Or go warm up at the training center?
I debated it, but I just went into a tavern I saw on the way home and ordered a drink by myself. Yes, there needed to be days like this once in a while.
Clink.
Tossing back the lukewarm beer, I organized the thoughts floating around in my head.
There really isn’t anything going on these days.

These kinds of repetitive days weren’t boring to me. To be honest, they were comfortable and enjoyable. But on the other hand, my anxiety grew and grew because I knew these dream-like days wouldn’t last forever.
Still, maybe it won’t end yet. I didn’t hear anything at the Round Table, either.

The Round Table I attended two weeks ago didn’t indicate any big signs of change. I offered up information and acted tough as usual, the others all looked at me with awe, and I pretended to be bored while actually focusing on the news the members were sharing. That was all that happened that day. There wasn’t any information that intrigued me, and the gathering itself ended after two rounds.
Oh. I guess there was one strange thing that happened.
If I had to pinpoint something from this gathering, there was one thing.
“Then see you next month. Hehehe.”
At the end of the meeting, Clown said goodbye for the first time—not to me but to the other members, and in a somewhat mysterious tone of voice too.
Does that mean something interesting will happen next time we meet?
Well, I didn’t know about that. It could have been a simple whim on his part. That was Clown’s personality, after all. It wasn’t like I was a prophet or a mind reader, either.
I should get going.

After sitting alone in the bar for about an hour, looking pathetic, I got up and headed home. When I got there, the melee sisters were already back from the training center and bickering. Well, it was closer to a one-sided scolding, to be honest.
“Ainar! Didn’t I tell you to keep your laundrrry in one place?! Do you think you’ll be able to become a great warrior like this?”
“That... I was going to do it later! I really was! I wasn’t being lazy, I swear!”
“This is the last time. If you do this again, you can do your own—Oh, Bjorn. When did you get back? Did you have dinner?”
“Not yet.” Although I drank, I didn’t order any food on the side on purpose.
“Really? I’ll prrrepare some soon, so go wash up. Hey! Ainar! Where do you think you’re going? I’m not done talking to you!”
“Tsk! You caught me!”

Ditching Ainar, who was being scolded by Missha, I went to the bathroom to wash up. When I got back, the table was set with a generous spread. Since it was going to be hard to eat like this tomorrow, I guessed she was being more liberal than usual.
“Thanks, as always, Missha.”
“It’s nothing new...”
After the meal, we played a card game Missha bought at the market and spent time together until late into the night. That was because it was better to sleep late today.
“The sun is starting to rise.”
“We should invite Urakburak and Aruru next time!”
“That again? I don’t know about Aruru, but Abman should stay home. He has a wife.”
“Then we can ask his wife to come too!”
What was this kid talking about? This was bound to turn into a pointless argument if I left them alone so I stepped in and sorted it out. “Okay, okay. Let’s go to bed. Wake up as late as possible.”
Tomorrow night, the labyrinth would open.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]

It was hard to see even an inch ahead in the darkness. Considering we had just entered the labyrinth, this was an anomaly, but no one on my team was startled. Since that first time, we’d been through this several times already.
“Leait.”
A dim sphere of light floated up above our heads, illuminating the surrounding area. The first thing we saw was the headstone located on the wall of the dead end.
“We arrived at the right place again. At this rate, it seems like this isn’t a special phenomenon but something you can think of as a rule.”

To be more accurate, it was a dimensional instability bug with a 100 percent success rate. As always, Raven stepped forward first and put her hand on the stone. The way the magic flowed when the portal was activated was so unique that she hadn’t been able to get a good sense of it after only one or two tries. Of course, I didn’t know where she planned to use this information, either. Was there any use for it?
[You are the first to open this portal. EXP +2]
Anyway, when we entered the portal, we were greeted by the flat air and ground unique to one particular area. God damn it.
[You have entered the Den of Beasts on the second floor.]
Why this, of all places?
“Mr. Yandel, what are you going to do?”
“...Let’s head down again.”

Although I’d been taking Rotmiller’s classes for over half a year, this place was hopeless. There were too many crossroads and complicated rules to remember. It was so bad that even Rotmiller only ever managed to clear this area with his enhanced olfactory stats and had advised me it was better to just give up.
“So Goblin Forest again?”

Did I even need to say it? Once we were back on the first floor, we headed to Goblin Forest, which we tended to use the most. Finding the way to the Land of the Dead or Rock Desert wasn’t too difficult, but still, this route was the fastest.
“We might earn portal opening achievement points there. We’re going to move quickly, so follow close behind.”

I pulled out my compass and started to find the way in earnest. We got out of the dark zone without getting lost once, and after that, we crossed the border between the dark zone and the central area and traveled down the shortest route. I didn’t have to ask Mr. Bear for the direction of the portal once. That was because I’d mastered the Crystal Cave by now.
Trudge.
A little over two hours had passed since we had entered the labyrinth.
“Mr. Yandel.” Raven, who was on Ainar’s back, suddenly stopped me. “S-Something’s weird.”
“...Weird?”
“Mana is swirling in the center of the cave, almost as if dozens of people are casting a joint spell...”

Joint spells were when wizards used high-ranking magic or linked their unique manas to amplify the force of a certain spell. For reference, the technique was often used in large-scale raids. But it was not often that it was used on the first floor.
“...Black magic. I can also sense cursed mana.”
To think they’d even use black magic. This was starting to look serious. “Must be Noark, right?”
“Yes. It’s common knowledge that there are many dark wizards on Noark’s side.”
“No wonder they were so quiet. This is a headache.”
“W-What are you going to do?” Scared by the current situation, Raven looked uncharacteristically shaky. Yeah, it seemed I needed to be the vigilant one here.
“This changes nothing. Let’s speed up some more. We’re getting off of the first floor as fast as possible.”
Quickly giving orders, I got us moving again. And about five minutes later...
“Something is coming at us from behind!” Raven suddenly shouted at the top of her lungs.
Voom!
A red cluster of light rushed past us from the back of the passageway and disappeared down the other side in a flash. There was no time to avoid or react to it.
“...What on earth was that just now?”
“I-I don’t know. I think it was mana, but...”
That was ridiculously ominous. A type of magic that even Raven didn’t know about?
“Hey, Bjorrrn... Shouldn’t we keep moving?”
As per Missha’s advice, I took the lead in paving the road again and tried to figure out what was going on. There was no clear answer. Maybe that was why...
“We... are okay, right?”

Even knowing the leader’s role in a situation like this, I couldn’t answer that question. At this moment when everything was murky and confusing, there was only one thing that was clear. Those times that felt blessed, and felt all the more fleeting because of it... Those peaceful days had come to an end starting now.

chapters.title: Chapter 208: Leader (1)
paragraphs: I advanced slowly while being vigilant of my surroundings. This was a change that had occurred a few minutes ago. Once we stopped running toward the second floor, we inevitably became more careful about our safety because a sight-obscuring fog began to fill the entire cave.
“...I’ve heard of this. It’s black magic. Something dark wizards used in past conquests.”
My heart began to pound, low and steady.
Thump!

Even as Raven removed the fog around us with wind attribute magic, visibility was limited to a five-yard radius. It was difficult to fend off danger in such an environment. Because I was not currently inside a game made up of HP and MP, a single mistake could lead to death. There was no Try Again button here.
Thump!
I had to be alert to get back alive without losing anyone.
“Mr. Yandel...”
In the past, we had been too weak to defend ourselves, and we had to lose a teammate. There hadn’t been any other way out of that crisis. But what about this time?
Yes, I’m much stronger than I was back then.
To ensure my body didn’t grow stiff from tension, I stayed focused on the positives.
“Mr. Yandel!”
“Don’t shout.”
“Then answer the first time.”
“What did you want to say?”
Raven, who was still on Ainar’s back, asked a cautious question. “Is going to the second floor the right choice?”
“What do you mean?”
“There are a lot of knights from the palace down here. Plus, there are a lot of large clans. Wouldn’t it be safer to join them instead?”

It was a fair suggestion. If we were near the starting point, I would’ve chosen that option too. But in the current situation, well, it didn’t seem like a particularly good choice. There was one thing I should clear up too.
“Raven, more than half of the large clans did not enter the labyrinth this month.”

This was something I’d heard from Fox at the Round Table. Large clans that were dissatisfied with the palace had launched a massive boycott. The few that had realized that the palace was keeping track and adding those clans to a hit list had backed out, but that wouldn’t have been many of them.
“...Why now?”
This was probably the best time to do this.
“Abman, what direction?”
“That way.”
I confirmed the location of the portal with Mr. Bear and continued guiding the way. This was also a change that had occurred since the fog took over the cave: the compass had stopped working.
“...Will we be fine as long as we find the portal?”
“The second floor won’t be all that safe, either. But we just have to get to the fourth floor.”
The Tower of Heavens was an independent floor. If we could get there, it would be possible for us to return to the city safely even in the midst of this war. That was our best option.
“No. What I meant was that they may have set up defenses near the portal.”
“What do you mean?”
“Exactly what I said. If I were a tactician on Noark’s side, the first thing I would do is look for a way to eliminate the way up to the second floor.”
That was... true. But, so what? We had to at least try. Thanks to us taking advantage of the dimensional instability phenomenon, we were already in the outermost region anyway.

“If going up to the second floor is impossible... What are you going to do then?” Unlike usual, Raven kept asking me more questions. I got the sense that she was anxious too. Well, I was sure she needed someone to depend on since she wouldn’t have much experience with situations like this.

“Then we’ll join the people from the city like you suggested. There aren’t any other options anyway.” I tried my best to speak calmly. I had no way of knowing if this was the best plan, but one of us should be calm, at least. “If that’s enough explanation, let’s keep going.”
“Okay...”
While moving as fast as we could toward the second floor, we encountered other adventurers.
“Finally, a person. Do you guys know what’s going on?”

The party was composed of three humans and two beast people. Their equipment level was similar to ours or above it. Well, a group that had already made it this far into the first floor couldn’t be made up of lower-floor adventurers. If they joined us, our combat power would rise significantly. However, I needed to check something before that.
“First, identification tags.”
Were these bastards really trustworthy?
“It’s real.”
“Did you think it was fake?”

As soon as we met, we each confirmed that we were from the city with the identification tags on our wrists and then began to exchange conversation. If things were normal, we would’ve been on our separate ways after confirming each other’s identities, but this was an emergency.
“Do you know anything?”
“Not much. Except that Noark has done something.”
“Noark, huh? Of course.” The leader on their side nodded at my words.
I narrowed my eyes. “Are there no wizards on your team?” The fact that there were few normal wizards on Noark’s side was common knowledge.
The leader just confidently shrugged his shoulders. “As you can see, we are a team aiming for achievement points. We do not need a wizard.”
Fuck, that made sense too. Wizards rarely participated in speed runs. Not only were they dead weight because they were slow, but wizards couldn’t obtain any experience points from a speedrun anyway.
Thus, I attempted introductions, figuring that the other side might have heard of me with my nickname of Little Balkan and all. “Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
“Hansen Calders.”
“Hansen?”
“Oh, do you know me? We might have mutual friends—”
“I don’t think so.” I shook my head, feeling an ominous shiver go down my spine. This was the first time I’d heard that particular name. So what should I do?
Just as I was worrying about this, Hansen and his teammate exchanged whispers. “Little Balkan? Oh! The barbarian from that time with the Lord of the Floor!”

It seemed someone on his side knew my name. Hansen’s gaze became a little more appreciative as it flicked back over to me. “I see now that you’re a celebrity. Why don’t we travel together? I don’t think this is a time for either of us to be exploring.” Hansen offered to join forces first.
“Can you give me some time?”
“A few minutes. I’m too anxious to be in one place for too long.”
After asking for Hansen’s patience, I took time to talk it over with my colleagues. After all, collective intelligence was a thing—there could be something I missed that stood out to someone else.
“I don’t know about this. It does seem safer with more people, but... Still, Bjorn, I think it’s betterrr to trust your judgment.”
“I agree with Missha!”
First, the melee sisters expressed their intent to fully go along with whatever decision I made. Mr. Bear was on the opposing side.
“Something is off. At their level, they should be pretty well known, but I’ve never heard their names before. They may not be from the underground city, but there’s a chance they are plunderers.”
This concerned me a bit, since among us, Mr. Bear had the most connections.
“Raven, what do you think?”
“I-I don’t think there’s anything off. Wouldn’t it be better to just join them? Their identification tags were fine too.”
Hmm, I see.

I’d been inwardly relying on Raven the most, but I think I had to rethink that. Maybe it was because this was the first time something like this had happened to her, but her gears weren’t turning as usual.
“Don’t think about the identification tags and think strictly about the people.”

“Pardon? What do you—ah!” Raven realized what I was getting at. Now that things had devolved like this, it was foolish to put our trust in identification tags. There was a possibility that they’d made fakes.

Actually, there were two possibilities: either they didn’t manage to replicate the tags and just bit the bullet and came back to the labyrinth anyway, or they did successfully replicate them and were using that as a cover to cause trouble. I didn’t know which it was yet, which was why I had to trust solely in my intuition to decide. It was just like in Dungeon and Stone, where one mistake meant game-over.
“I-I don’t know. Just decide for us, Mr. Yandel.” Feeling disoriented, Raven left everything to me. Why was she so out of it?
“Raven, snap out of it. You were fine even when there was an assassin hiding next to us in the Tower of Heavens.”
“Th-that was different from now. Right now, if I make a mistake, others will suffer for it.”

Oh, so that’s what it was. I was learning something new about Raven. I never thought she would be the indecisive type when it came to having more responsibility. I got it, though. Someone could die from the choices I made. Overcoming that pressure to make a decision was never an easy task, because this was not a game. The choices you made didn’t just end with the death of your character.
God damn it.
Ultimately, the decision was in my hands. That was nothing new, though.
What a headache.
I sighed and studied Hansen’s group at a distance. If there were a wizard among them, or if they were well-known adventurers or part of a famous clan, then I could’ve trusted them a little easier.
But they aren’t.
Unfortunately, I wasn’t given much time.
“Have you made your decision?”
“Yes.” Soon, I made up my mind. “Sorry to keep you waiting, but I decline your offer.” My final decision was that there was no need to gamble.

“Is that so? That’s too bad.” Surprisingly, Hansen nodded without seeming too displeased. It seemed he already understood why I’d decided what I did. “It’s the careful man who lives the longest. I hope to meet again someday.”
“What are you guys going to do?”
“We’ll first go to the second floor, although I’m not sure that place is safe either. Has to be better than here, though.”
“I see. If there’s any luck, I’ll see you in the city.”
“What are you doing? Let’s move.” After our brief exchange came to an end, Hansen’s group headed off first and disappeared into the fog.
Did I make the right choice just now?
Smirk.
I forced a smile in an attempt to erase my doubts and anxieties. When had I ever made a choice while knowing the outcome?
“Let’s get going.”
I just had to trust it and move on.

About five minutes after parting with Hansen’s group, we discovered five dead bodies. They were not the bodies of Hansen’s party, who had headed off first. Their equipment was completely stripped, but it wasn’t difficult to figure out who they were.
“It’s a knight.”
“...A knight?”
“Yes. The tattoo on the back of his neck here. It’s the symbol of Viscount Terten.”
“That’s a family crest? It’s almost like a brand.”

To be more precise, it was like he was more an object than a person. The realization left a bitter taste in my mouth. The fact that even knights were treated as consumables in this world had suddenly sunk in.
“...Not all nobles are like this.”

Leaving behind Raven, who seemed to be trying to defend them, I sorted through my thoughts. The corpses of one knight and four soldiers, and the fact that the surrounding area showed no signs of struggle, could mean only one thing.
“There’s some kind of monster here. And not a literal one.”
“Yes. Looking at the wounds, this was all done in one blow. Seeing as all the injuries are the same, it doesn’t seem like it was multiple people, either.”

Knights, who could use auras, were the strongest when it came to human versus human warfare. In a world like this where magic and special abilities existed, they were the blades that protected the vested interests of the rich. To think one had died without fighting back... I realized we were in the eye of a storm all over again. A knight who had spent his entire life holding and wielding a sword and would have enjoyed immense power had died like an extra. No, more were continuing to die off even now, just like during the conquest of Noark that occurred underground several months ago.
“Time of death?”
“It’s been about twenty minutes.”
So whoever or whatever killed them wouldn’t be too close. That was a good sign for us, but it was too early to be relieved. Anything could happen from now on.

“Those guys... are they really planning on starting a war?” Mr. Bear muttered, frowning. Now that he was staring at the knight’s dead body, it seemed to finally hit him exactly what kind of situation we were currently in.
To be fair, it wasn’t like we’d fought anyone ourselves yet. I decided to be blunt. “They’re not planning it, Abman. We are already at war.”
We were fortunate enough to have been in the outskirts when it started, so we hadn’t experienced the consequences yet. But it was just a matter of time now.
“What will you do?”
I sighed at Raven’s question. I didn’t know how many times she had already asked it since we came back down to the first floor. We were at a crossroads once again.
“...The only thing in this direction is the portal.”
“You don’t have to explain. That means that whoever killed this knight headed that way.”

The second-floor portal was the only way out I could think of, and now a monster was lurking there. However, even if we turned around, the situation remained bleak. The battle that had already started in the center would soon cover the entire first floor.
Fuck, Den of Beasts or not, we shouldn’t have come down to the first floor.
