I couldn’t help regretting it. To think that trivial decision would land me in this rotten situation. It was as if this heartless world was testing me: Choose whatever you want, but the responsibility for that choice is all yours.
My eyes shifted to my teammates. Missha, Ainar, Raven, and Mr. Bear were all looking at me, too, like the decision was entirely mine.

“...Let’s head back.” I soon made a call. I didn’t know who was in front of me. It could be a member of Orcules since someone strong enough to kill a knight like this would be rare in Noark too. I was about to turn around when—
“Ha, are you really just going back?” A voice rang out from beyond the fog.
Step.
Footsteps followed.
Shaaaaaa!
Immediately, Raven sent forth a gust of wind to push back the fog, revealing a man wearing no equipment—just simple black clothing and a skull mask on his face.
“What kind of barbarian is this timid? Huh?”
My body stiffened at that voice. I had never heard it before, that was for certain.
“Hehehe.”
But it was somehow familiar.

chapters.title: Chapter 209: Leader (2)
paragraphs: It’s a coincidence. It’s just someone with a similar laugh. This world is so big, there has to be one other person out there with a similar quirk.
Those thoughts didn’t even occur to me. As soon as the sense of déjà vu hit me, I accepted it as reality.
Clown.
A member of the Watchers of the Round Table and the guy who seemed to be the most knowledgeable and skilled out of all of them—this was that man’s true identity.
I’d already guessed that he was from Noark, but to think we’d meet like this...
I was face-to-face with the clown I’d been so curious about, but it wasn’t at all nice to see him.
We’re fucked. What do I do? He looks hella strong. If I reveal I’m Lion, will he let us go? No way.

I cast aside the weak thoughts that started to pop into my head. Not only would that be the equivalent of revealing that I was an evil spirit, but the person Clown respected was Lion, not this barbarian sucker. The moment my identity was revealed, Clown would lose interest in me and get angry.
And so I shouted, “Prepare for battle!” If I could overcome the fear, which could become my greatest asset, at any moment, anywhere, that was a win.
Clown looked amused. “Now you sound like a barbarian!”

Did that bring her to her senses? Raven immediately cast a spell. “Derva Timunes.” It was a team communication spell. Since we were facing a human, not a monster, she must have thought to turn this on as soon as she heard me shouting.
“Tsk, how boring.” Now that he’d lost his source of entertainment, Clown seemed displeased. That wasn’t my problem, though.
“Everyone, get behind me!”

As I fired off orders, I used Giantization to block the passage. This was the advantage of the first floor’s Crystal Cave. Although each passageway was different, they were mostly narrow enough to be blocked by one giant barbarian.
Click.

“Behelaaah!” In an attempt to shake off the fear, I called out the name of my ancestral god. Holding the shield just low enough to not interfere with my vision, I focused all my attention on this guy’s movements.
Thump!
My warrior’s heart started beating at just the right speed. Hot blood circulated quickly through my veins, invigorating me. I had a feeling I at least wouldn’t go down without a fight.
“Mr. Yandel, we can’t attack if you do this!”
Our wizard’s concerns were firmly dismissed. “Then don’t.”
“Pardon?”
“We don’t know who he is. We need to first learn his abilities. Until then, don’t step forward.”

The most important thing in PvP warfare was information. Out of the tens of thousands of special abilities and items, how had our opponent combined them and in what class had they cultivated their character? Without knowing that, it would be difficult to respond in the right way.
“That’s...! This monster killed a knight. Yet you’re going to figure him out on your own?”
What else could we do? “This is the best way.” I was a tank. I could take a mystery attack, but not these guys. The moment they were struck unprepared, their game was likely to be over.
“Since I can’t hear what you’re saying, this is no fun,” Clown said coldly. Without giving us time to discuss our strategy any further, he reached out his hand. Suddenly, there was a weapon there.
It’s mithril.
His awl pike emitted a blue-silver light. “Just die.” A low voice resounded through the passageway, and at that exact moment, Clown’s form disappeared right before our eyes.
We didn’t lose him for long, of course. This was a straight corridor, after all.
You think you can use stealth-play?

When I lowered my shield slightly, I spotted Clown taking a stance from an angle that had previously been obscured by its bulk. With my instincts having been hardened by numerous live combats, I quickly identified where he was aiming.
The thigh...
In combat, everything was informative. The time for swinging weapons without thought was over and each action was bound to have justification and intention. So why did he aim for the thigh?
As I thought, is he an assassin?
Compatibility-wise, he must have figured it was too much work to try to get through my shield. It was the first thing I’d upgraded with the money I saved after paying off my debt.
If he had a brain, he would’ve realized as soon as he saw it.
A large shield crafted from the grade-four metal moonstone was strong enough to even withstand a few blows from an arc sword.
Hack!
And it was impossible to pierce with mithril, which was grade five.
Clang!

Not stopping at shielding myself, I tensed my arm and applied force. Clown was pushed back without resistance. I recorded one more piece of information in my head. Well, actually, this went without saying.
His Strength stat is below mine.

I was starting to think this was doable. I was not the same person I had been six months ago. Starting with equipment, I’d made significant improvements in many areas. By the looks of it, he wasn’t at the level of the Dragon Slayer either.
Well, I’m sure he hasn’t shown me everything he’s got yet.

Staying vigilant, I studied Clown, who had stepped back. I managed to block the first attack, but if I allowed even one, it was very likely to be trouble. He did confidently tell me to die, after all. That wasn’t a line someone would say while aiming for the thigh.
Is it poison, then?

It was highly likely that the weapon was poisoned. It could also be that his special ability was related to poison. I didn’t know anything for sure yet, so I left all possibilities open, even while operating under the assumption that that was the case.
I think it’s about time now...
All we’d done so far was exchange simple physical moves. Since those had been blocked, it was time to start using skills.
“Ugh, honestly! I wanted to save my MP as much as possible!”
I couldn’t help but laugh. Aside from his classic over-the-top tone, to flat-out say “MP”?
“...Mr. Yandel! That man is an evil spirit!”
This deranged bastard had no intention of hiding his identity, huh?
Are people from Noark all like this?
Well, now that they were openly opposing the palace, there was no reason to hide it.
“No, wait a minute. If he’s an evil spirit...”
Those words made me flinch. I could guess what Raven was thinking: someone from Noark who could kill a knight on his own, the most notorious player in the city...
“The Corpse Collector...?” Raven said numbly.
“Kyaaa!”
I hurriedly turned around to look behind me.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Puppet.]
The bodies of the knight and soldiers scattered behind me stood up and attacked Raven.
Damn it, she was right.

There was no point in denying it any further because the Corpse Collector’s character build was famous. It was a good character class I had also played a few times, specializing in curses and summoning—a class that emphasized high Agility stats to compensate for their weakness in close combat.
An APN, or Agile Poison Necromancer, was my opponent today. Since he had been aiming for my vitals with an awl-like weapon, I had thought he was an assassin, but that had obviously been a mistake.
A necromancer, huh?
He had simply underestimated me and tried to use an ordinary attack to take me down. His real specialty lay elsewhere.
He didn’t happen to be in the area—he came looking for us.

Now that I knew his identity, I started to see the situation in a different light. This guy probably left the corpses there on purpose for one simple reason. If he pretended they were corpses and left them there, he could use them like CCTV to alert him when anyone walked by. Not that it mattered now.
There won’t be any need to test the waters.
I decided to focus on the positives. Having gathered information on Orcules after the battle with the Dragon Slayer, I also knew quite a bit about the Corpse Collector.
He has six known essences.
Of course, he probably had three unidentified essences, and considering this guy’s notoriety, that would be disastrous for us. But at least I’d figured out his class.
“All of you, don’t fight and step back!” I hurriedly gave my team orders. If this were a battle against a normal summoner, the standard strategy would have been to defeat the summons.
“Don’t fight?”
“Keep your distance first!”
But when it came to APNs, every summon was the equivalent of a bomb. Widening the distance was the key to survival.
“Aruru, come here!”
“Okay!”
The moment Ainar, looking out for Raven, prepared to step back, gray light burst through the eye holes in Clown’s mask.
Flash!
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Curse of Stone.]
My nerves started to numb from the feet up. I realized what skill it was as soon as it hit me: the essence of the rank-four monster Medusa.
Dash.
Perhaps he wanted to kill me first because he picked up the awl again and lunged at me. It was an overpowered skill.
It’s probably because of this skill that there were no signs of a struggle here.
Even a knight would have a hard time fending off a rank-four essence, since an average knight was level five. It would be hard to keep up in terms of Mana Resistance.
Well, not me, though.

Over the past six months, I had filled all two hundred available slots of the Manticore’s passive skill, Hereditary, with Mana Resistance. Usually, you used it to improve miscellaneous stats, but Mana Resistance had been the most practical option for me.
“Behelaaah!”
As a result, my battle cry had evolved to replace the Fortitude skill.
[Your Mana Resistance is over 400.]

I had +20 from stage two of the Immortality Imprint, +80 from the Ogre’s essence, and +200 from Hereditary. The boost I got from Giantization and Wild Outburst was about +40, and if you added the additional 20 percent increase from the Earth Dragon’s blessing...
[The Suppression Immunity effect has been activated. The status effect Curse of Stone has been nullified.]
My Mana Resistance temporarily surpassed 400 and I became immune to any skills that tried to restrain me!
As soon as the numbness in my feet disappeared, I grabbed my shield and ran forward. My opponent looked very taken aback. Perhaps it would be more accurate to say he was dumbfounded.
“Ha! Suppression Immunity? Just how much did you invest in Mana Resistance?!”

Save the high praise. The reason I’d paid all that money to consume the Manticore essence had been for Mana Resistance in the first place. Regardless of whether the stats remained after you erased it, +200 Mana Resistance was enough to milk the essence until the second half.
Anyway, he’s fast as fuck.

Although I pushed forward like the tank I was. this guy easily kept his distance like a classic APN. This was why these bastards were tricky. In general, a summoner’s actual body was bound to be vulnerable, but catching APNs was a whole ordeal. Still, I was glad he wasn’t an assassin.
“Raven! Freeze the corpses!”
“Pardon? Okay!”
“And Abman, when I give the signal, fire off a bit shot! To give us an opportunity to escape!”
“Escape? Is that possible?”
Well, the odds were fifty-fifty, but we had to try. We had a higher chance of getting away than we did of being victorious in battle.

“I guess I need to pour everything into one blow. Okay!” Fortunately, Mr. Bear obediently followed orders. As soon as he heard the name Corpse Collector, he must have pieced together that our odds of winning in a fight were slim, and that even if we did, it would inevitably come at a cost.
Why the Corpse Collector of all people?
This guy was among the upper echelon even in Orcules. He was above even the Dragon Slayer.
But I have a chance now.
Due to the nature of their class, necromancers weren’t very good at chasing people down. Not only that, but this guy was trying to conserve his resources.
Since he has to keep fighting until the labyrinth closes, I’m sure he wants to save as much energy as possible.
With that in mind, I quickly backpedaled.
Shaaaaa!
A chill slid over my back. It seemed Raven had used ice magic to freeze the corpses, as instructed.
“They’re frozen!”
Okay, that was all set. “Abman!”
“Ah, just say the word!” Mr. Bear seemed to be ready too.
Once I sounded the alarm for a surprise attack, I asked one more thing of Raven. “Raven, turn off the communication spell.”
“Pardon?”
“Hurry.”
“It’s off.”
Once the team communication spell was deactivated, I spoke to Clown. “Hey.”
He gave me a curious look. “Hm?”
I continued regardless. “Do you know the top two ways to piss someone off?”
“I’m not sure. I’ve never heard of them.”
Oh, foreigners. I knew he wouldn’t have. “The first is to stop talking in the middle of a sentence.”
Clown nodded in understanding. “I see. What’s the other one?”
“That’s...” I trailed off and deactivated Giantization.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Enhancement.]
[Abman Urikfried has cast Hazardous Material.]
An arrow containing all of Mr. Bear’s power shot across the open passageway.
CRASH!
The cave shook as if struck by an earthquake.
Whooosh!
As the other side was obstructed from view by a sudden wall of fire, I bellowed, “What are you doing? Run!”

chapters.title: Chapter 210: Leader (3)
paragraphs: Thick bones covered his whole body in an instant.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Bone Armor.]
The man smirked and stared straight ahead. The flames that hit the bones were quickly extinguished but the remaining flames in the passage became a wall and blocked the way.
“Hmm, I didn’t think he’d run away.”
Should I follow?
Contemplating this as he stared out beyond the blazing flames, the man soon decided to call it quits. How to piss someone off... He wasn’t exactly curious about that.
“...Captain, it’s the body of a knight.”
“As expected, they’ve already gotten this far. Everyone, be vigilant. The enemy has to be nearby.”

About twenty adventurers appeared as if on cue from one of the passageways connected to the second-floor portal. Seeing as they were all wearing the same symbol on their tops, it looked to be a small clan.
“Tsk.”

The man clicked his tongue in displeasure and moved on. His mission for this insurrection was to be in charge of the second-floor portal and stop people from escaping. It was originally a mission that the Dragon Slayer was supposed to take on.
“That snake-eyed bastard is no help whatsoever.”
If that guy had just recovered in time, he could have focused on using his talent for mass murder to help out in the center of the floor as planned.
“Well, I’m sure they’ll take care of the escapees on their end.”

After all, there was no reason to chase and kill a guy who had bounced. Just the thought of it alone was tedious. All he had to do was his own job. With that in mind, he was about to move toward the second-floor portal.
Bzzzzzz.
The message stone in his pocket vibrated.
“Necrapeto, what’s your situation? Have you reached your destination?”
“Oh, Deputy Commander! Don’t worry. I arrived a long time ago and the portal’s blocked off so well that not even a rat can escape through it. Hehehe!”
Although he spoke confidently, there was a long beat of silence before the commander replied. Strictly speaking, it wasn’t even a reply. “...What is that tone? And what is that strange laugh?”
“Strange laugh?” The man tilted his head at first, but soon realized what they meant and chuckled. “Oh, it’s just a habit. Don’t worry about it, Deputy Commander.”
“A habit?”
“Yeah, something that happens when I put on a mask.”
“...I don’t know what you’re talking about. Anyway, if something goes wrong, contact me immediately.” With that, the transmission ended.
The man tapped the skull mask he had been given with his index finger. Suddenly, the members of the Round Table came to mind.
Fox and Goblin will for sure be here.
How many of them would be alive and well at the next meeting? He was already looking forward to it.
I ran with all my might, worried that Clown may be coming after us.
Huff, huff.
After we had been sprinting down the passage for about ten minutes, Mr. Bear muttered, “Did we lose him?”
It was a death flag kind of line, which made me nervous for a moment, but I didn’t bother saying anything. I was wondering the same thing.
To be more precise, we didn’t lose him—he just didn’t chase after us.
Either way, it was clear that we had time for a breather now. “Let’s slow down from now on.”
“...We’re not going to run some more?”
“That man isn’t the only one we have to be careful of.”

We were currently in a fog-covered Crystal Cave. If we sped up too much, it would be hard to respond appropriately to unexpected danger. It was safe to say that the entire first floor was already a minefield.
“Bjorn, maybe the right thing would have been to fight.”
“What do you mean, Ainar?”
“The Corpse Collector... This was a chance to make your name even more widely known! But you abandoned that opportunity and ran away!”
Yeah, no wonder she’d been quiet this whole time. So that was what she was unhappy about. This girl tended to look up to me like some ancient heroic barbarian. But, the chance to earn fame?
I’m just thankful that no one got hurt.

A necromancer’s true abilities became obvious the moment they took a body out of sub-space. Moreover, the Corpse Collector had a numbered item that had earned him his fame, a signature item similar to the Dragon Slayer’s sword. If he had had a chance to pull that thing out, some of us would have been killed or badly injured.
“Ainar, don’t be foolish.” Without needing to step forward, Missha gave Ainar a warning that caused her to shrink back.
“I’m okay with it! As an adult, I can understand why you did it. But, h-how do I explain this to the young warriors?!”

Ah, now I saw the real problem. Ainar always went to the holy land and told them all about the quests she had been on with me. It was a level of hero-worship that was almost embarrassing, but I just left her to it since it could raise my approval rating in the tribe.
“You can just make something up.”
“That’s—! Warriors don’t lie!”
“Tsk! Stop talking back!”
When Missha harshly reprimanded her, Ainar clammed up. Her slumped shoulders made me feel bad. Unshakeable confidence was a barbarian’s charm.
After a moment’s thought, I answered, “Ainar, we didn’t run away just now.”
“Huh?”
“That man ran away from us.” It was a classic barbarian-style mental victory.
“W-What do you mean? Don’t make fun of me... I’m not that dense!”

Hmm, I didn’t know about that. I pressed on, my expression serious. “I’m not making fun of you. Ainar, a wise warrior must also know when to pick and choose their battles. What we just did was run toward a battleground that was more in our favor and knowing that, he ran away.”

Ainar frowned in discomfort. “Is that... true?” she asked cautiously. I had been a bit worried, but luckily that seemed to have worked. When I nodded firmly, Ainar returned to her usual cheerful self.
“Mr. Yandel, you really are...”
“What, do you have something to say?”

Raven shook her head at me with a strange look on her face. “No. Just... I was just thinking that a leader should be someone like you.” Hm, it seemed that my method of consoling Ainar had been quite impressive.
“Anyway, let’s keep moving.”

The chatter ended there, and I proceeded cautiously down the passage, keeping a careful eye out. My destination was the center of the first floor, the very place that was likely covered in blood right about now.
“Wouldn’t it be better to try to head through another portal?”
“It’ll just be the same thing there too.”
I abandoned the option of heading to the second floor. After all, the Corpse Collector was standing in the corridor leading to the Goblin Forest.
He’s probably trying to block the portal.
I assumed that individuals of similar strength would be waiting at the other portals.
“In that case, I will defer to your judgment. Yandel, you have good intuition when it comes to these things.”
Like that, we pushed through the fog for a while.
Rattle, rattle.
About ten people appeared in front of us. By the time we noticed each other’s presence, we were already within sight of each other. Fortunately, they didn’t seem like enemies.
“...They’re knights.”

Not only was everyone in the group wearing the armor of a knight, but each piece of armor carried the symbol of the family they belonged to. Well, even that could be replicated if Noark tried his utmost...
“Explorer, raise your wrist and reveal your identification tag.”

Judging by that arrogant tone alone, it seemed his armor was the genuine article. As instructed, I first showed them the tag on my wrist and then I asked, “Is there any point in showing the identification tags in this situation?” That was the thing I was most curious about.
“To some extent,” the knight replied curtly.
“I want to hear more.”
“There was a person who ambushed us with identification tags that looked real. Due to that, we took some damage.”
“I see.”

“If your curiosity has been sated, put down your weapons and stay close to the wall until we pass,” the knight said harshly, and I obediently followed his instructions. Things were really dangerous here. The knights seemed to have fought many battles to get here as they were all drenched in blood.
However, I should still find out what I needed to know. “Can you tell me exactly what the situation is?”
“...What a strange question.”
“We ran to the second floor as soon as we arrived. We don’t have information about what happened down here.”
“Hmm.” The knight stopped walking and stared at me as if to discern whether what I was saying was true or not. As those menacing eyes met mine, I started to think I shouldn’t have asked.
“Hello. I am Arua Raven, a wizard from the School of Altemion.” Raven stepped forward and introduced herself. “If you are doubting our identities, I can use magic to prove—”
“Stop. Don’t come any closer unless you want to die.”
“No, I—”
“Do you think there are no wizards in Noark?” the knight asked, his voice low.
Raven couldn’t say anything to that and kept her mouth shut.
A heavy silence settled between us.
“Sir Garfizel, these people cannot be on Noark’s side, so you don’t have to worry about that.” The situation took a turn when a knight in the back row spoke up.
“How can you be so sure?”
“He’s a pretty famous adventurer.”
“Hmm, this man?” The knight who seemed to be the leader shot me a dubious look.
I felt the same way. “...You know me?”
“Of course I do.” The knight who answered my question raised his helmet, revealing a familiar face.
“Carls Erimor?”
“What an honor that you remember. Long time no see.”

Carls Erimor was a knight from the House of Baron Martoin whom I met at the count’s estate. He was only an apprentice, but still. He was a rare adventurer-turned-knight, so we got along quite well. To think I’d run into him here.
“So, who is this man?”
“His name is Bjorn Yandel, and in the city, he’s more famous as Little Balkan.”

Once Carls verified my identity, the knight looked at me in a different light. “Little Balkan, huh? I’ve heard your name in passing as well. In high society, you are called the Knight Crusher, correct?” His gaze was still far from benevolent. However, since his suspicions of me being an enemy had been cleared, it was a lot better than before.
“So, can I hear what’s going on now?”

The knight briefly explained that as soon as they entered the labyrinth, adventurers from Noark attacked them from all sides. Some were camouflaging themselves with fake identification tags as well, so the initial causalities were considerable. After the fog appeared, the knights gathered in the dark zone in the center of the map to protect as many adventurers as they could and prepare for battle.
“By the dark zone, are you talking about the place where the monument is located?”
“Yes, head there. You’ll be safe as long as you get there.”
That was good news. I carefully spoke up in an attempt to stop him from leaving right away. “Are you guys going to the portal?”
“...Why are you asking that?”
Geez, so aggressive.
“Because we’re coming from over there.”
“Interesting.”

I told the interested knight what I knew. We were on the same team right now—I couldn’t let them die in vain. “The Corpse Collector is near the portal. So if you see a dead body in the passageway, be on guard. That means he has found you too.”

In sharp contrast to what I had been expecting, the knight listened intently and nodded without question. “Every piece of information is valuable in wartime. The Corpse Collector, huh? Thank you for telling me.” Surprisingly, he even thanked me and handed me a ring. “If you run into a knight who doubts who you are, show them this and tell them about me. Then your identity will be verified.”
“...I’ll take good care of it.”
“I’m running out of time, so goodbye.”

As soon as he handed over the ring, the knight led his group away and disappeared into the fog. He didn’t look so arrogant to me anymore. Now that I was looking again, I could see that he was a dutiful guy.
I guess it doesn’t come with size adjustment magic.
After trying to put the ring on my little finger, I gave up and handed it to Missha.
“Eh? Me? You want me to wearrr it?”
“It doesn’t fit on my hand.”
“...Th-then it can’t be helped.” Missha elegantly extended her left hand to me. What? Did she want me to put it on? “Ahem...”
I turned her hand over so that her palm was facing up and placed the ring on top. “You wear it.”
“Hmph, you’re embarrassed.”
...She was talking nonsense.
After running into the knights, we increased our speed some more. The further from the outskirts and closer to the center we got, the more the scent of blood intensified.
“Here too...”
“Stop looking and keep moving.”
No matter where we went, we ran into a dead body every few minutes. Almost all were naked.
Even in the middle of all this, you’re taking what you need, huh? Well, the feeling’s mutual.
“Yandel! It’s an ambush!”

We also ended up involved in quite a few battles as we pushed forward. Did this make nine? One time, it was only after we checked their identification tags that they suddenly attacked, while the rest attacked us as soon as we saw them. They were mostly around rank five, like us, but there hadn’t been any major issues so far.
“Behelaaah!”
On average, we were a pretty strong team. We were slowly reaching sixth-floor capabilities, and because we didn’t have a professional scout, our combat power was pretty high.
“Bjorn, what arrre you going to do about the two who escaped?”
“Leave them. We don’t have time, so take the equipment from the rest and let’s go.”
The further we traveled, the more equipment piled up in our sub-space. It felt like being in an infinite Player Kill dungeon.
I never thought I’d experience excitement like this on the first floor.
My anxiety slowly mounted. So far things had gone smoothly, but how long could this possibly last?
“Bjorn...”
“Don’t worry. We’re almost there now.”
I pushed down my paranoia and continued leading the team.

After a long while, at a crossroads divided into several forks, we encountered a group of about thirty unfamiliar adventurers. They seemed to be resting after an arduous battle and lifted their weapons as soon as they saw us.
Thump!
My heart began to pound. If these guys were from Noark, then we were fucked.
“Huh...? M-Mister?!”
That was when I heard a familiar voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 211: Leader (4)
paragraphs: “Mister!” Erwen jumped out from the group of adventurers and hugged my arm. “What a relief! I was so worried!”
Huh, I didn’t expect to see this kid here. That wasn’t to say it was a bad thing, of course. I relaxed a bit and glanced around at my surroundings. Her sister, Daria, was also there.
They don’t all seem like members of the same clan...

At first, I wondered if this was the clan that Erwen had joined as a mercenary, but that didn’t seem to be the case, either. Most of them were wearing the mark of a clan, but not all of them did. Also, each clan mark was different. If that was the case, how on earth had this group been formed?
“Miss Erwen, who is that?” a human woman who looked to be in her mid-thirties asked and lowered her weapon.
Erwen finally released my arm and turned around. “Don’t worry. I know this man! Oh, so does my sister! Right, sis?”
“...That’s right. We know for sure who they are so you won’t have to worry that they’re on Noark’s side.”

“That’s the first bit of good news I’ve heard in a while.” After hearing Daria out as well, the woman ordered the wary adventurers to lower their weapons. Hmm, was this woman the person in charge here? “Nice to meet you. I am Versyl Gowland, the deputy commander of Clan Larer.”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

“Little Balkan...?” When I shrugged, the woman looked happy to see me. “Wow, we’ve come across someone very incredible.” A flattering compliment naturally followed. An ordinary barbarian would get conceited here and act arrogant. Were these the conversation tactics of a real leader?

“You flatter me. Rather, I should be saying that to you,” I answered, studying the woman. I wasn’t saying this out of politeness, either—it was the truth. “Clan Larer is a fairly large clan, to my understanding.” It wasn’t one of the top ten, but it was big enough for them to call themselves a large clan. And what made it unique was that 80 percent of the clan members were women. “The deputy commander, huh?” I had run into a considerable big shot in an unexpected place, although I had no interest in small talk in a situation like this. “So, what are you all doing here?”
“Let me explain.”

As soon as our introductions were over, Versyl gave me a quick rundown of what was going on. It sounded like we were all in the same boat. As soon as they entered the labyrinth, these guys quickly moved toward one of the second-floor portals.
“Then the incident happened.”

In an attempt to assess what was going on, Versyl led her team back to the starting point. However, by then, that place had already been no different from a living hell. And so she began gathering a makeshift army.
“The people gathered here are all people we met in the area. Their identities have been confirmed too.”
“Confirmed?”
“I’m not acquainted with each one of them, but they’re all people with mutual acquaintances. We unfortunately made a point of excluding those who weren’t, so you can rest assured.”

As they were unable to trust identification tags anymore, this was the method they had ended up using. Just like Erwen had vouched for me, the rest of the group had vouched for each other and established a minimal level of trust.

“Our goal is simple.” After explaining the group’s current state of affairs, Versyl presented the goal they were working toward. “Combine forces to protect ourselves. Penetrate the enemy, and ultimately reach the safe zone.”
“By safe zone, do you mean the dark zone in the central region?”

“Yes. Since you know about it already, this will be quick. Will you join us, Mr. Yandel?” Was it because she was the deputy commander of a successful clan? The way she spoke, it definitely felt like she was used to managing people. She seemed like the cautious type too.
And a deputy commander must be considerably skilled.

After briefly thinking it over, I accepted Versyl’s recruitment offer. “Okay, I hope we work well together.” In the middle of all this chaos where the future was uncertain, we established a temporary safe haven.
“There’s no need for you to stand guard, so get some rest. We’ll be leaving soon, so I’ll let you know when.”

I accepted Versyl’s kindness with gratitude. We were desperate for a break, anyway. Between the fog obscuring our vision, having to battle people rather than monsters, and the havoc that made it difficult to predict even what the next step forward would bring, our physical fatigue was one thing but the mental stress we were under was also enormous.
“What are you doing? Let’s rest.”
I led my team members, who were acting awkward around the unfamiliar adventurers, to an empty spot. Then came rest.
“We got lucky. To find these people herrre... I guess there is always a light at the end of the tunnel.”
The others finally seemed to relax a brief moment later. My teammates, who at first had been wary of their surroundings, enjoyed a short break with obvious relief.

Erwen had stuck by her sister’s side while we were speaking, but sat down next to me afterward. “Mister, you made the right choice. That deputy commander over there is really strong. So are the others. Anyway, I guess we really are fated to meet. I was just thinking that I missed you and then you actually showed up! Hahaha.”

“Tsk.” Ainar and Missha, who normally didn’t see Erwen in a good light, frowned slightly but didn’t start a fight or anything. They probably knew, too, how foolish it would be to cause trouble over personal grudges in a situation like this.
Raven, who had never met her, seemed curious and joined the conversation. “But how do you two know each other? I heard that elves and barbarians don’t get along. Oh, I didn’t introduce myself. I’m—”
“I know! I’ve heard a lot about you from Mister. He said a very talented wizard joined his team.”
“...Did Mr. Yandel really say that?”
Well, not exactly like that, but...
Figuring this was Erwen’s way of building a social life, I just watched quietly.
“I’m Erwen Fornacci di Tersia. You’re Miss Arua Raven, right?”
“Just call me Raven.”
“Then please call me Erwen too.”

Finishing off their introductions in a friendly tone, Erwen proudly told her the story of our first meeting. He pretended not to, but Mr. Bear also listened closely, apparently curious about my relationship with the elf.
“Your first return drink was with a pretty elf... Yandel, I’ve been thinking this more and more, but you really have good luck with women.”
What was this guy talking about?
“Mr. Urikfried? Hehe, thank you for the kind words!”
“...Call me Abman.”

“Okay, Mr. Abman!” Erwen made friends with the group in an instant with her youthful energy on full display. To be honest, I was quite impressed. “So, how do you use this crossbow? It doesn’t seem like a normal person would be able to pull it because of the tension.”
“Oh, this? It’s nothing fancy. Do you want to try pulling it?”
“Can I? Ugh... wow! It’s completely different from my bow.”
“Haha, that’s because it’s made of Troll tendons.”
Was Erwen always this friendly? It seemed almost like she was trying to please her mother-in-law.
Ah, that’s not a completely inaccurate comparison.

Come to think of it, I had told her I was going to form a clan. Raven and Mr. Bear were the number one contenders. Since they may all belong to the same clan one day, she must have thought it necessary to make a good first impression.
Well, she seemed to be earning the dislike of the two other members, though.
“Urakburak. Stop smiling. Is this the kind of situation to laugh about!?”

“...Huh?” Upon receiving an unprovoked blow from Ainar for the first time in his life, Mr. Bear froze, stunned. Then he belatedly put two and two together and blurted out an incomprehensible excuse. “A-Ah! I’m on the cat’s side, of course.”
“Right? I almost doubted you! So, come over here already and look at my greatsword. Talking about bows is no fun!”
“Oh... it’s not?”
“Of course not!” Ainar yanked Mr. Bear over to her like she was kidnapping him.
It was right about when this ridiculous scene was unfolding that Daria, who had been carefully watching us from a distance, approached. “Erwen.”
“Ah, sis.”
“Sorry to interrupt, but I have something to say.”
“Oh, to Mister?”
“Yeah.” Since she had something to say to me, I was about to get up, but Daria stopped me. “You’re resting, you don’t have to do that.”
“Yeah? If you say so. What did you want to tell me?”
At my question, Daria just stared at me awkwardly. For some reason, she seemed uncomfortable about approaching me. Said reason soon became clear. “You... I heard you’re a rank-five adventurer now?”

As far as I knew, Daria had also been rank five when we met and that hadn’t changed since then. But me, on the other hand... Back then, I had been a rank-nine rookie, but within a year I had grown into a rank-five adventurer in charge of my own party. It made sense that she’d be uncomfortable around me.
“And? Is that it?”
“...I have a suggestion.”
“Say it.”
“Why don’t you travel with us for the time being?”
“Elaborate.”

At my words, Daria continued in a strictly business-like tone. Apparently, there were a total of seven parties gathered here in pursuit of a common goal, but in the end, they were still strangers. In actuality, most of the parties were forming groups with other teams they were already acquainted with.

“If you agree, our two teams will position ourselves close to each other as we move so that we can join forces right away if something happens.” Wherever people gathered, factions were bound to arise. Daria was offering me an alliance.

“Not a bad suggestion.” The offer itself was quite attractive, so long as one condition was met. “But do you have permission from your leader?” Daria was a member of the Blue Wall Clan’s fourth team as a mercenary. Naturally, her team leader was one of the clan’s executives. Had they finished discussing this already?
“That man... You don’t have to worry about him. I can convince him. So, your answer?”
“All right.”
“Okay, then I’ll come back later. Erwen, come with me for now.”
“Okay...”

Afterward, I watched Daria lead her sister back to where her team was. I felt a strange feeling wash over me. The first time we met, she treated me like a childish barbarian and a guy skulking around her sister. I never thought I’d receive an offer like this from her first.

After a few more minutes of rest, Versyl announced it was time to depart. “Everyone, finish up your preparations. We’ll be leaving soon.” She also relayed where in the formation our team would be positioned at this time, which was three spots from the front. Right behind us was Erwen’s team.
This feels like we’re being taken advantage of.

Our formation had each team following behind one another like a train. Of course, there were no complaints here. Due to the nature of the Crystal Cave, it made sense to move in a single file, and the team paving the way at the forefront was Versyl’s team, which was the strongest.
“I heard from Daria and Erwen that they call you Little Balkan?” said Erwen’s team leader, Big Jaw. “I hope we work well together. Yes, I’ll leave the front to you.”
Why were we ahead of Erwen’s team? Was this really a coincidence?
Of course it’s not.

Third from the front may have been similar to fourth, but it was an indisputable fact that being closer to the front was more dangerous. It was a minor thing, but it was also true that we were the ones who were in a worse position.
Raven seemed to think so too. “Hey, this isn’t sitting right with me.”
“Hm? Which part?”
“The formation. You don’t think this is permanent, do you? I think it would be better to alternate front and back.”
Big Jaw laughed good-naturedly at Raven’s objection. “Haha, we have a lot of long-rangers on our side, and you guys have close-rangers. It’s just a logical setup.”
“That’s—”

Big Jaw cut Raven off, his voice firm. “Aren’t you located in the center, which is the safest spot to be, in the first place? Who do you think that’s thanks to?” Even the logical Raven couldn’t say anything to that. If our position was thanks to him, she must have figured that it was fair for us to stand in front since we hadn’t done anything. You could argue these guys had helped us out.
A mere team leader of a medium-sized clan influencing the deputy commander of a large clan?
It sounded like bullshit to me. I needed to keep a close eye on him.
“Now, let’s finish this conversation here and get moving. It seems the first group has already left.”
Oh, don’t rush us.
I left my doubts behind and moved forward.
Step, step.

And so our journey officially began. The journey itself was smooth in the beginning, to the point that I was starting to think it was divine intervention that we had encountered these people by coincidence and Erwen happened to be there to vouch for me.
“Deputy Commander! Dark wizards!”
“Stall for time. I will take care of this quickly.”
The combat power of the team to which the deputy commander belonged was truly amazing.
I’ve heard that their clan is mainly active on the seventh floor.
Having them pave the way made things very comfortable for us followers.
Is this what being carried feels like?
Aside from the few surprise attacks launched from some side roads, I could count the number of times I had to wield my mace on one hand.
About an hour into our journey, Versyl stopped and spoke to us. “I have good news and bad news. The good news is that we’re almost there. We can reach the dark zone in twenty minutes if we run.”
Yes, I knew that already. “What’s the bad news?” one of the adventurers asked.
“Not everyone will reach it,” Versyl said matter-of-factly.
A chilling silence filled the cave.

chapters.title: Chapter 212: Discarded Hand (1)
paragraphs: “W-What do you mean not everyone will be able to reach it?!” a man shouted into the ensuing silence. His voice clearly conveyed an anxiety that this kick-ass party might be on the verge of abandoning us.

“Let me explain,” Deputy Commander Versyl calmly continued. “Our scout tells us that adventurers from Noark are camped out in every passageway leading to the dark zone so that no one can get out—or get in.”
A troop of a size unlike any we’d run into so far were camped out ahead. At that, another man shouted, “So what you mean is that sacrifices are necessary in order to pave the way!”
That was the true meaning behind the statement that not everyone would reach the dark zone. I, too, had a similar interpretation to that man.
“Something like that.”
However, the moment I heard those light yet heavy words, my heart started pounding uncontrollably.
Thump!
Versyl continued without pause, not bothering with excuses, just the cold, hard facts. “We will be using a mass teleportation spell.”

Mass Teleport was a high-level spell that could only be used by wizards from certain schools who were rank four and above. Now it made sense why not everyone could go. An even heavier silence weighed down the cavity this time.
“B-Bjorn? Isn’t it possible to get through here without fighting if we use a teleportation spell? So why is everrryone’s expression...”
The reason was simple, and Raven explained it. “Mass teleportation magic can only be used on up to twenty people at a time.”
Just as Raven said, Mass Teleport was only usable on up to twenty people, and our group currently numbered thirty-five.
Fifteen people.
Simply put, a total of three teams were about to be abandoned in a situation where the safe zone in the center region was right under our noses.
“I-If you were going to abandon people, why did you suggest joining forces in the first place!?” someone shouted in anger.

Versyl didn’t so much as flinch as she offered a brief, concise apology. “I apologize for that. We didn’t know things would turn out like this, either.” Her voice seemed soft but did not leave room for argument.
I sighed quietly. There was no point in trying to persuade this type of person. No matter what anyone said here, this woman wouldn’t change her mind.
“So, how are you going to choose which fifteen people to abandon?”
Versyl shot me a strange look at my question. I supposed a barbarian who could remain calm in a situation like this was peculiar to her. “Each team will draw lots.”
“Everyone but your team?”
“No. Us and one more team.” Versyl’s gaze shifted toward the party who had fought alongside them throughout the entire journey as they paved the way forward.

“Sorry about that. Deputy Commander Versyl and I have been acquainted for a long time.” The leaders of each party looked utterly unsurprised as they apologized to us as if they already knew this would happen.
Yeah, so you agreed on this in advance, huh? Well, it’s not like that’s unexpected. Those guys are from a large clan too. Except... Goddamn it.

A headache crept in instantaneously. Now there were only two tickets left on the teleport. On the other hand, there were three lots for stragglers. If we did this by a draw, there was a higher chance of being abandoned than there was of being taken along.
Picking up on this, the expressions of the remaining parties all changed into ones of desperation.
“Please take us.”
“Five million... no, we’ll pay ten million stones per person.”
Some offered money.
“We are a team under the Blue Wall Clan. If you take us with you, Master will surely give you a big reward...”
Some promised a future partnership with their clan.

“W-We don’t have a clan yet. We all happen to be women too. We may be active on the fifth floor now, but we’re originally from the sixth floor. I heard Clan Larer is recruiting members due to their recent losses...”
Some even positioned themselves as tools to trade away. No one willingly agreed to draw lots. That was to be expected. After all, no one wanted to leave their precious lives to chance.

“Yandel.” Mr. Bear grimly called my name. He was probably asking if we should do something too. I just watched things unfold for now, figuring that it wouldn’t be too late to make an offer after seeing what Versyl decided.
“I’m sorry. It wouldn’t be right to do it that way.”
“Th-that means...!”

“Yes. The rest will be decided fairly by drawing lots. Please, I hope you understand my decision.” Making an exception for just one team, as promised, Versyl adhered to the rules she had outlined at the get-go.
“Versyl Gowland, deputy commander of Clan Larer. She’s just as I heard.” Raven admired that pride of hers but I couldn’t sympathize.
More like there wasn’t an offer that appealed to her.

If she were truly a fair person, she wouldn’t have excluded that other team from the draw in the first place, especially when it was obvious what situation the people left behind would find themselves in.
Anyway, drawing lots, huh?
I didn’t know if this was a good thing. I’d never once been picked in something like this.
“We’re running out of time, so let’s start right away.”

Versyl put five stones into a pouch and finished preparations for the draw. The rules were simple: whoever got one of the two white stones won. Pulling one of the three black stones meant you’d be dumped here without hesitation.
“Which team would like to go first?”

“I will.” The first to step forward was the party that said they would pay ten million stones per person. “To think that my fate would depend on a damned stone.” A dwarven warrior dressed in fancy gear nervously put his hand in the pouch. “H-Hahaha... We got it!”
He’d succeeded on the first try. Laughter spread through the dwarf’s team while the faces of the other teams darkened.
“Come stand here. Then who’s next?” In this intersection between joy and sorrow, no one wanted to be the first to step forward. Now there was only one winning ticket and three to hell.
“Mr. Yandel, we need to wait. In terms of probability, if you draw now, you have a greater chance of drawing a black stone.”
We currently had a 25 percent chance of winning and a 75 percent chance of losing, but as always, probability meant nothing.
“Hah, we’ll just go for it.” The all-female team who was awkwardly studying the room stepped forward. “Kyahhh!” They pulled the remaining white stone.
God damn it.
“Then that’s that.” With just two draws, the fates of all five teams had been decided. The other three teams hadn’t even had an opportunity to leave their fate to chance.
“Kyahhh!”
What had I been doing while the women’s team pulled out the white stone? Contemplating who out of Missha, Ainar, and Raven should pick ours. I didn’t think this would end in two rounds.
How does that make sense?

Just when the thought came to me, Versyl turned the pouch upside down and scattered the three black stones on the floor as if to prove that no deceit had taken place. “Then gather around, everyone. We’ll be casting the spell as soon as we’re ready.”
At Versyl’s words, those selected quickly gathered in one place.
“W-Wait!” The leader of one of the three parties that had mentally clocked out in this situation, Big Jaw from Erwen’s team, hurriedly ran up to them. “T-Take us with you! Please, we’ll do anything!”
A groveling plea wasn’t going to work on this woman. “All of the spots are already full.”
At Versyl’s emotionless rebuke, Big Jaw directed his pleading elsewhere. “If you yield your spot, ten million stones! No, I’ll pay twenty million stones!”
Trying to buy a seat with money, huh? It seemed he was more of a coward than I thought. Seeing as he made no mention of his team members, he wanted to survive on his own.

Daria, who was on his team, frowned like she was looking at a bug, but Big Jaw didn’t stop there. When talking at them from a distance didn’t work, he approached each person one by one and asked if they were willing to accept the deal, but they all turned him away.
“Th-there’s really no one?”
Did you really think that would work?
Money wasn’t the problem. The moment you sold your spot for money, you’d get separated from your teammates.
“If you’re done talking, can you please step back?”

At Versyl’s curt request, Big Jaw turned back to his party, drained. With that, the commotion came to an end. The wizard on Versyl’s side began drawing a magic circle on the floor to use Mass Teleport.
“Bjorn...”
“Let’s talk later.”
I ignored Missha’s call and spoke to the deputy commander. “Versyl Gowland.”
“Yes. Go ahead.” Her voice was kind but otherwise emotionless, with no sympathy or curiosity in her inflection. Maybe she thought I was going to make a pathetic plea like Big Jaw.
I smirked and asked a single question. “On the journey, why did you place us in the safest position of the formation?”
Versyl tilted her head, but it seemed she wasn’t particularly curious as to why I was asking this question. She just answered, “I drew lots. To be fair.”
Right, so everything he had said was a lie. Not that I didn’t already know this, but it definitely wasn’t thanks to Big Jaw that we had gotten placed in the middle.
Okay, that confirms that that guy is a selfish bastard.
Like it or not, the abandoned three teams would have to work together now. It was becoming clearer how I’d have to deal with Big Jaw.
“Is that the last of your questions?”
“No, one more.”
“Sure.”
“You said enemies were camped out in the passageway? I want more information. What is the layout and how many troops?”
“...Do you intend to barge through them on your own?”
What, did you think we were just going to die here?
“If needed.” We may have gotten this far with more ease by coming with them, but the center had been my destination from the start. This changed nothing. “So, your answer?”
At my urging, Versyl paused and stared at me. “...You are just like the rumors say. All right. Xenia?”
“Yes, Deputy Commander.”
“Go on and tell him everything he wants to know.”
“Okay.”

Versyl provided a scout from her own team and I was given a general lay of the land through her. After about five minutes, all preparations for the activation of the spell were finished, and Versyl left with just one last word for us.
“Xenia, come here... I hope you won’t resent me.”
From now on, we would have to overcome this trial with our strength alone. Well, there was nothing new about that.
“...They’re gone.”

With more than half of the people in our group now gone, the vacancy felt even bigger than it would have otherwise. But because of that, I had to focus even more on one thing: what should I do now? Well, it certainly wasn’t wasting precious time brooding over this strange emptiness.
“Mr. Yandel, what are you going to do now?”
“Let me think.”

We had two options: charge through the route that Versyl gave up on and head for our original destination of the central region, or turn around and find another place. The latter wasn’t a bad option, either.
We can survive if we just stick to the outskirts.

War was in full swing in the center of the map, and in the outermost parts, Noark’s strongest warriors were blocking the way. On the other hand, there would be relatively few people in the outskirts. Since it was also a wide area, we would likely be able to survive as long as we hid ourselves well.
However... We wouldn’t be able to find out how things are going.
That was the biggest downside. In this chaotic situation where each minute and second counted double, we wouldn’t be able to obtain information about the situation if we stayed in hiding.
Besides that, the Lord of the Floor will show up on the third day.
We couldn’t defeat the Lord of the First Floor on our own. If it got summoned while we were holding out, we would be annihilated.
“We have to figure out our combat power first.”
“Pardon?”

“Everyone, gather around.” I withheld my decision for now, brought the other two parties who were in the same situation together, and immediately got to the point. “Each person will take turns revealing their ranking, essences, and specialties.”
“You want us to tell you everything about ourselves?”
“Is that important right now? We have to join forces.”
“You speak as if you are the one in charge here.” Big Jaw frowned at my suggestion. The others didn’t seem pleased that I was talking like the leader either, although they didn’t show it.
How annoying.
“Does it matter who’s in charge? I’ve never met an idiot who cared about something like that even in a situation like this.”
“...W-What? What did you just—”

“If you want it that bad, fine—let’s choose the captain first. What, you want a vote?” I naturally steered us toward a vote. That was because Erwen was there. I figured that if at least one member of another party cast a vote for me, I couldn’t lose.

However, things took a slightly unexpected turn. “I don’t think that’s necessary. If we do a vote, our team will vote for you.” So said the remaining team’s leader. “Including your own team, that makes ten votes already. There is no need to waste time.”
Oh, it’s going to work out just like that?

To be honest, I was a little taken aback. However, it seemed Big Jaw was in the same boat. He kindly asked the reason for that in my stead. “What do you mean by that? You want a barbarian as your leader? Are you crazy?”
“First of all, I’m not skilled at leadership.”
“Then you should pick me instead of the barbarian—”
“If I had to choose one of you two, he’s the more reliable one.”

I had a feeling I knew what he was thinking. He probably thought I was at least better than Big Jaw, who had tried to abandon his team to survive on his own. However, as he continued, I learned that there was an additional factor.
“More importantly, while everyone else was in denial, this man was the only one who asked the woman for information.”
...This is kind of embarrassing.
“Your name?”
“Takelan Arbenon.”

“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.” After exchanging formal introductions with Takelan, I returned to the topic at hand. “Anyway, that’s decided, then. Now, tell me your adventurer rankings, essences, and specialties one by one. That way I can choose our next move—”
“Wait a minute, what’s decided?”
Ha, you son of a bitch.
“Do you have a problem?”
“Of course I—”
Not wanting to waste any more time, I cut him off and spoke firmly. “Then get lost. Our two teams can travel together without yours, then.”
“...God damn it.” Big Jaw clenched his fists in anger but did not leave our side. Well, where was he going to go now?
I smirked. “If you interrupt me one more time or disobey my orders, it’s over. Understood?”
He was silent.
“Answer me.”
“...All right.”
Okay, that set up the hierarchy. After that, I quickly executed my original plan of action to figure out who had what positions and what essences.
Hmm, this is kind of ambiguous.

Although I managed to figure out our approximate combat power, my worries deepened. I guess you could say I was still unsure. So, to be safe, I went through an additional verification process. “First, let’s introduce ourselves. We should be able to call out to each other in an emergency.” I even threw in a logical reason and listened to everyone’s names. To be honest, it was hard to remember all of them.
Still, there’s no Hans.
This was a fairly positive indicator. It meant that whatever decision I made later had a slightly higher probability of success.
“What will you do now?”

At Raven’s question, fourteen pairs of eyes honed in on me. It was nearing the time to make a decision. I parted my lips, erasing any regrets about the choice I had made. “We will head to the safe zone.”
“What are our chances, do you think?”
I answered Takelan’s question with a bitter smile. Although we had just seen how meaningless probability was, one thing was certain: even if we were successful, not everyone would survive.
About half of us will die.
To reach the place some were easily able to travel to with a single spell, we would have to risk our lives.

chapters.title: Chapter 213: Discarded Hand (2)
paragraphs: Inside the fog-covered Crystal Cave on the first floor, where corpses littered the ground and the metallic scent of blood filled the air, a man cackled as he chatted with his comrades. The topic of conversation was nothing special: wasn’t that woman we just killed pretty, wasn’t it kind of a waste? Those kinds of obscene comments. As always, it ended with complaints.
“Tsk, there’s nothing fun to do here.”
“Haha, in other words, it’s not all that dangerous.”
“...You’re unnecessarily positive.”
“I’m not wrong, though.”
“Well, that’s true...”

The man pushed down his displeasure and chewed on a piece of jerky from his pocket. As a mere footman, this was the first piece of meat he’d had in a long time. After not being able to enter the labyrinth for six months, Noark, where he came from, was suffering from severe food shortages.
...We can win, right?

The man shook his head at the sudden anxiety that filled him. It was not a matter of whether they could win or not. They had to win. Only then could they eat and live like human beings—even if in an underground city that didn’t see the light of day.
“Lex, focus on your mission.”
The man resting against the wall sighed at his captain’s words and fixed his posture.
“You look frustrated.”
“We haven’t sighted anyone for over two hours,” the man said truthfully.
“So?”

“That means no one will come anymore. All the bastards going inside have already gone in, and all the bastards who haven’t either kicked the bucket or run away.” The area they were assigned to was around the central region, but quite far from the dark zone at the heart of it. That meant they wouldn’t be coming across anyone from inside.
“Still, stay vigilant just in case.”
“Yes, yes.” The man half-heartedly accepted his captain’s orders and stood at one of the intersections. He couldn’t see far because of the fog, but he felt no anxiety.
Who cares what shows up? How many of us are here again? It’ll just mean some more loot to take back to Noark.
At least, that was what he had been thinking when a comrade who was standing at the other intersection shouted, “Captain! A presence!”
The man grabbed his weapon and moved toward him.
Someone came?
This was a surprise, but he wasn’t worried about it, either.
Do they not realize what’s going on?
They probably didn’t. If whoever it was knew what the situation was like here, they wouldn’t have thought to pass through. They must have made their way here without knowing anything.
“Huh?”
The man tilted his head. No, wait, there was something else. Everyone listened with confusion on their faces.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
What the hell is that sound?
“Footsteps?” someone suggested, but that didn’t make sense either. How could these be the footsteps of a person? It would have to be a large monster like a Troll.
Wait, but there are no monsters like that on the first floor.
At the strange, out-of-place sound, the man gripped his weapon tighter.
“Behelaaah!” The thing let out a wild cry as it appeared from beyond the fog.
“W-What the hell!? Who is this bastard!?”
“Stop him!”
It was a barbarian and a very large one at that.
To live was to let go. What would you give up to survive? This process operated strictly based on prioritization because humans were rational creatures.
Thump!

It was a common trope in movies. For a helicopter to fly, or to keep a ship from sinking, people threw out more and more cargo to escape enemy pursuit. The more they threw away, the better their chances of survival.
Thump!
However, reality and movies were entirely different. Reality wasn’t nearly as kind. What we had to throw out to survive was not baggage, but something else.
Thump!
Perhaps Versyl knew that which was why she had abandoned us without hesitation, leaving only the words “I hope you won’t resent me” behind.

I didn’t resent her. I knew it was a thoroughly logical decision on her part. She had her priorities, and for that, she had discarded anything unnecessary that she was carrying, just as I was doing now.
“Behelaaah!”

With a cry, I dug my toes into the dirt with all the strength I had. Behind the shield I was gripping tightly with both hands, I felt an opposing force unlike any I’d ever felt before. It felt like going against a tidal wave with just one shield. That might not have been an inaccurate description, even if it was a bit exaggerated.
“W-What the hell?! Who is this bastard!?”
“Stop him!”
I was paving the way at the forefront to clear the path for our twenty-minute run to the center. I was pushing through the enemy infestation like a tank on the battlefield.
“Bjorn!” Missha was following right behind me. Her role was simple: get rid of the enemies who were tossed aside by my charge.
Slice!
It didn’t matter if she couldn’t kill them in one shot. Reducing their numbers wasn’t our main objective and we had backup right behind us.
“You bitch—!”
If Missha provided the first sweep, the second was conducted by Raven on Ainar’s back, along with Mr. Bear.
Kwaaang!

Crossbow bolts and spells flew at the enemies Missha failed to kill before they could even get up. Of course, it didn’t matter if they didn’t manage to finish some of them off. There were a lot of sweepers remaining.
“Erwen, be careful!”

We had a long-range damage-dealing duo made up of sisters Erwen and Daria, then Takelan’s team with an average rank of five following right behind us, and even Big Jaw’s team located at the very back. It was similar to a medieval cavalry.
“Ahhhhhh!”

Our only goal was to charge forward. Enemies not slain in the front were dealt with by those picking up the rear. It didn’t matter if some enemies survived the last sweep. That was for Mr. Last Place to figure out.
You reap what you sow.

When choosing the formation for this strategy, Big Jaw insisted on being in the very back, even giving us the long-range elf sisters. His thought process was obvious. He probably figured the frontlines were the most dangerous place to be in charge. If something unexpectedly went wrong, he could run away. He was treating the mercenaries Erwen and Daria as discardable hands.
Brainless bastard.

In reality, the riskiest location in this strategy was the very back. Right now, they may have been able to freeload since we were taking care of them from the front, but this status quo wouldn’t last forever. I didn’t know that catastrophe would strike so quickly, though.
Boom!
A heavy blow thudded through my shield. Even when I applied force on the tips of my toes, I couldn’t move another inch forward. I lowered my shield slightly to check the view up front.
“Never have I ever seen such a madman.”
A warrior from the Black Bear tribe like Mr. Bear was standing in my way. His body was half as large as mine in Giantization mode.
God damn it.
How high was this guy’s Strength stat? Even as it struck me that adventurers from Noark were considerably strong, though, I wasn’t too pressed.
“Barbarian, you think you’re some hero from the stories—”
Ignoring the bear bastard’s jabbering, I shouted toward the back, “Raven, now!” I was not an all-powerful hero. However, the same went for our opponents.
“Everyone, get back!” In time with Raven’s warning, an explosive shockwave slammed forward from behind me.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-six support spell Oxygen Explosion.]
It was a whopping rank-six wind attribute support spell. The reason she activated it behind me was simple. It didn’t deal much damage, but it came with great knockback.
“Ugh! What the...!”
Ending our tense wrestling match, I shoved my opponent away like a sail that had just caught a strong headwind.
“N-No!”
Crunch.
The bear bastard lost balance and fell back. I stomped on his face with Leap and dashed forward. Well, he seemed like a tank too, so he wouldn’t die from just that.
Stab!
Before long, I heard the squelch of flesh being pierced behind me. Geez, it was like stabbing tofu. His Strength stat may have been high, but it seemed his Physical Resistance wasn’t.
“Behelaaah!”
While we had been momentarily slowed down by the bear bastard, our enemies had started closing in on us from behind. So I used Wild Outburst to dope up my physique stats and resumed the charge.
“We need to move faster!”

However, we weren’t moving as quickly as before. This was a very big problem. One of the weak points of the cavalry was that they ended up getting surrounded when their opponent managed to stop their charge.
“You unhinged bastards!”
“Kill them!”
The enemies who had been knocked down rose like zombies and rushed at my comrades. While we had been penetrating enemy lines one-sidedly earlier, now we would have to hack through this melee.
Slice, stab, crunch! Kwaaang!
The overlapping, chaotic sounds of intense battle rang out behind me. Of course, I couldn’t see exactly what was going on. Because of that, I kept most of my focus on the front lines.
“Bjorn, don’t worry about the rear!”
I was worried. Humans dropped like flies during war. I was worried that someone would get seriously injured by an unseen knife.
Slice!
Because I couldn’t know whose flesh that sound had come from, dark thoughts kept popping into my mind. Could that have been Missha? Ainar? Raven or Mr. Bear? But, so what?
“Behelaaah!”
Stopping here would only make things worse. Embracing the fear I couldn’t shake off, I focused everything I had on the role assigned to me.
“W-What kind of strength—?!”
Just clear the way. Leave the rear to my comrades and push forward dependably. That was what I had to do in this moment, and something only I could do.
“The good news is that we are almost there. We can reach the dark zone in twenty minutes if we run.”
Time seemed to drag on. Sweat, blood, and screams all filled the cave.
Has it been three minutes?
It felt like an hour had passed, but in reality, it would only have been about that long. Now I could tell where we were on the first floor just by looking at the walls.
God damn it.
It felt like I was trapped in a cave where time itself was distorted. I checked my location in real-time to infer how much had passed.
Seven minutes.
The first fatality occurred at that exact moment.
“Kaiyen! Kaiyen is hurt! Help me. W-We need to help him...!”
“Let go, Lena.”
“What? But...!”
“He’s... already dead. Leave him here.”
Kaiyen was an archer on Takelan’s team. That was all I knew about him, but he had left a good impression during our introductions.
Eight minutes.

The road ahead was blocked by a barrier someone had summoned. I immediately took the fork next to me and adjusted our route. This bit of improvisation would’ve been impossible if I hadn’t received scout training from Rotmiller.
It’ll take at least thirteen more minutes to get there.
The bad news didn’t end there, though.
Nine minutes.
Another person died. This time it was a member of Big Jaw’s team, who was following us from the very back.
And one more thing.
“Bjorn, Missha is hurt!” cried Raven.
Missha was injured. “What part of her body and how badly?”
“U-Under the left side of her chest! No internal injuries—”
“Feed her a potion while you run. Ainar, carry Missha too!”

Fortunately, her life wasn’t in danger, but Ainar, who had been carrying Raven in one hand and helping us out in battle with the other, now had to serve solely as transportation for two members of our party.
Ten minutes.
Without fail, more bad news came in from behind me. “Mr. Yandel! The people in the back are gone!”
Big Jaw’s team had run away from their positions in the rearguard. It seemed they had deemed this an impossible undertaking after seeing the deaths on the frontlines... I had miscalculated.
To think he’s this brainless.
I never thought he would still think it possible to escape from this situation alone when enemies were surrounding us.
Fuck, if you’re going to kill yourself, at least die for us.
Anyway, with those bastards gone, the burden on Takelan’s team grew much heavier. Was that why?
Thirteen minutes.
Two people died this time—the wizard belonging to Takelan’s team and the warrior who had been running with her on his back.
“Damn it! All because of a stupid goblin—!”

The main cause of death was a spawning goblin. Amid the confusion, the goblin had flown at the warrior and blocked his line of sight, and in a split second, an ice-type sorcerer had turned them all into an ice statue.
Fifteen minutes.
A dark wizard jumped out from a side passage and cast a wide-range explosive spell. There were no deaths, but...
“Sis!” Daria threw herself in the way to protect Erwen, who was standing in the center and was rendered incapable of combat. Fortunately, it wasn’t an instant kill.
“Snap out of it and keep moving. I’ll carry your sister!” Abman carried Daria, reducing our combat power even more.
Seventeen minutes.
After abusing Leap for stat boosts and sustaining Giantization throughout the entire battle, my MP finally bottomed out.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has ended.]
As planned, the empty spot next to me was quickly filled with Mr. Bear’s tank summon, Iron Bear.
Eighteen minutes.
Iron Bear was soon unsummoned. However, Missha had recovered thanks to the potion and reentered the fray.
Nineteen minutes.
Hope was in sight. Now we just had to go a little further. Although nearly half of us were dead, none of the people I was determined to save had died yet.
Twenty minutes.
A high-ranking adventurer, likely at least rank four, suddenly blocked my path. He was a swordsman holding a greatsword made of adamantium, a grade-five metal.
“You’re gonna be fun to slice up.”
And he used an aura.

chapters.title: Chapter 214: Discarded Hand (3)
paragraphs: The old me would have thought of a rank-four adventurer who used an aura as a lethal enemy to run into.
Whooom!
He hadn’t finished activating his aura yet. With a grade-five adamantium greatsword and an aura, it was clear he’d turn this moonstone shield of mine into scrap metal in an instant.
“You’re gonna be fun to slice up.”

However, Dungeon and Stone was not simply a game based on HP and MP and Item Level. Rank-four swordsman, rank-three tank, or whatever have you—in this sadistic game, a single slip-up could lead to your character’s death.
“You wish.” No matter how strong you were, a critical hit killed you just the same. In that sense, the enemy in front of me wasn’t impossible to defeat. “Come.”

Although we were handicapped in the sense that we had to finish this fight in a short time because of the enemies swarming us from behind, this was a problem that could be resolved by throwing something of ours away.
“You barbarian bastards never know your place.”

All I could do was hope desperately that this bastard wasn’t too durable. I didn’t have time to feel this guy out and learn what skills and equipment he had. Who lived and who died would be determined in an instant, just as it always was.
“Behelaaah!” I let go of my fear.
Dash.
Just then, I heard the sound of feet kicking off the ground.
Whip!
In the foggy passageway, the human, who had the audacity to be over 6′2″, charged forward.
Whooom!
The human swung a greatsword.
Dash.

Instead of blocking it with the shield, I hurriedly dodged to the side, not because I thought this shield was too expensive to let this guy slice it up, but because it’d be pointless. When you gave something up, you stood to gain something in return—like this.
Slice!
The greatsword came down above my left elbow.
“M-Mr. Yandel!”

In an instant, I became a one-armed barbarian. This was my second time experiencing this after the battle with Riakis, the Lord of Chaos. I wasn’t particularly sad about it. I had thrown away the complacent thought that I could win against this guy in one piece the moment I saw him.
Chhhhhh.
I aimed my severed limb at him and sprayed acidic blood like a fountain.
“Aaaaaaa!” Luckily, it hit his eyes.
Hell yeah.

In exchange for an arm, I had managed to block this guy’s vision. Of course, that wouldn’t last for long, so I quickly followed my attack up with an order. “Raven, use Lava Eruption!” I clung to my opponent, figuring that since this guy used a greatsword as a weapon, he wouldn’t be able to harm me with his aura at this distance. If I hadn’t wrecked his sight, I would’ve had to give up something even bigger to get this close.
“But if I do that, you’ll—!”
“It’s okay, just do it!”
“Okay—!”
I hurriedly held my breath and flexed my muscles. This felt similar to the time I wrestled that Troll on the fourth floor.

“You son of a bitch!” As he fought fiercely against my grip, scales sprouted all over his body. This was one of the effects of Test Specimen, which temporarily increased Physique stats. I had expected this since he used an aura.
You’ve got some wild stats, huh?
Coincidentally, so did I. “Stay still.” I used Giantization again, hoping that since I hadn’t used it for a few minutes, my MP had recovered enough for thirty seconds of juice.
“Ugh.” The man released a pained groan, his back buckling under the sudden increase in weight.
Voom, voom!
Carrying me on his back, the bastard swung his greatsword randomly. Passageway, wall, or whatever have you—his aura sliced through everything.
“Are you scared because you can’t see?”
“I will kill you!”
“Everyone, get back!”

Because of his sword dance, Missha and the others couldn’t get close enough to deal additional damage. However, this worked better for me. Thanks to his struggling, our other opponents couldn’t come to help him either.
“Moronic bastard.”

“Aaaah!” He tilted his upper body in an attempt to throw me over his shoulder, but it made no difference to me. Staying right on top of the enemy like a pervert was one of the basic hallmarks of a tank.
Booom!
We collapsed and fell on top of each other. It was a far cry from any scene in a romance movie, though. Rather, it was more like a dog fight in a thriller.
Smack! Smack! Smack!
Finally, the bastard let go of his greatsword and slammed his fist into my ear. Of course, that was no problem either. You couldn’t use an aura with your bare hands, after all.
Smack! Smack! Smack!

Physical attacks could be endured with Physical Resistance. As someone who used an adamantium greatsword, his Strength stat seemed to be considerable since my brain was rattling around in my skull, but compared to my severed arm, a concussion was minor.
“Kesial!” When his erratic sword dance begrudgingly ended, the enemies who hadn’t been able to approach us until now rushed at me. However, they were one second too late.
“D-Do I really shoot...?!”
“What are you waiting for!?”
The spell was complete.
“Iherno Wature Tunbar!” It was the rank-four Fire attribute spell, Lava Eruption.
Whoosh!

The dark-red lava spewing from Raven’s wand descended on us. I immediately adjusted my grip so that instead of pressing him down from above, I was now strangling him from below, his body on top of mine.
“Let go, you barbarian!” the bastard shouted. It looked like his sight had returned because it seemed he’d spotted the lava crashing down on us.
“Why, you don’t like hot stuff?”
Then you should have raised your Flame Resistance, moron.
“No!”
I squeezed my eyes shut. At that moment, I experienced a heat that seemed to melt everything.
Whooosh!
“Ahhhhhh!”
At the same time, I felt something flowing down my skin. The fluid quickly cooled and hardened.
[Your HP has fallen below 50 percent. All Resistance and Resilience stats have increased due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]
I had Flame Resistance thanks to the third stage of the Immortality Imprint, a Manticore’s Mana Resistance, and the Orb of Fire.
Yet it’s still this bad...

My whole body was hot and itchy, almost like I had drunk a potion. The pain even cut through my resistance. But, so what? Not wanting to be in pain? I shook off the idea like a passive effect. Again, this was not a kind world.
Should I have asked her to use Cold Blood too?
I quickly dismissed the weak thought that suddenly popped into my head. Raven’s mana was shaky as it was. We had to conserve our resources.
“Krrgggh.”

I pushed away the enemy, who had turned into a lump of charcoal, and stood up. My intestines were so cooked I felt like a Korean blood sausage and something crunchy seemed to flake off of me each time I moved. Was this what you called soft on the inside and hard on the outside?
“M-Mr. Yandel? A-Are you okay?”
“...I’m just a little burnt.”
“A-A little burnt?”

I had to endure at least this much to take down a bastard who used an aura. Besides, the bleeding at my elbow had stopped. It had been cauterized by the fire magic. In many ways, I’d gained a lot from that one spell.
“Ugh.”
Fuck, why is this asshole still alive? Does he have Flame Resistance too?
As I noticed him getting up with me, I hurriedly turned around to reach my remaining hand toward the shield I had tossed aside earlier. And at that moment...
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has ended.]
Giantization was deactivated and I lost my balance. The distance between my hand and my shield widened dramatically.
Thump!

Even as heat radiated from my entire body, a chill went down my spine. If this guy’s greatsword... no, if he pulled out even a dagger and stabbed me in the neck with it, it would be game over for me. I could picture the worst-case scenario in my head.
C-Cough!
However, when I turned around and hurriedly checked behind me mid-fall, I saw the bastard’s back getting farther away. He staggered but moved at a fast pace.
I momentarily stiffened at that unexpected sight, then breathed a sigh of relief.
I got lucky.
The bastard couldn’t shake his arrogance, which was why he had blocked me all alone even though he had comrades with him.
Huff, huff, wheeze...
He could not give up the hope that there would be another opportunity later, which was why even though he had the chance to kill me, he chose to escape with his life. I understood the feeling.
“You... barbarian son of a... bitch...”
To him, fighting me wasn’t a matter of survival. There was no reason for him to risk his life for this fight. That was why our positions were now reversed.
“Where... are you... going?”
