Instead of a shield, I lifted the greatsword he had left behind in my hand. The Strength stat I had gotten from the Ogre’s essence was enough for me to be able to handle the adamantium greatsword with one hand.
“...S-Stop him!”

I hurriedly pursued him, narrowing the distance between us in an instant. It seemed he’d taken a lot of damage because his steps had no strength behind them. Before long, the sword was within cutting distance.
“Leave... your head.”
Being a swordsman wasn’t too bad either.
Slice!
I grinned at the sensation and shouted. “Behelaaah!”
I had survived, at least for now.

The time it took to cut off the head of a rank-four aura user was about two minutes. That was how battles always went. It didn’t take long for the winners and losers to be decided. A knight who spent their whole life training, or an adventurer who’d been in and out of the labyrinth countless times... in this world, anyone could lose their life in an instant.
“Ainar!” Without time to savor the victory, I tossed the greatsword I was holding to Ainar.
“Huh? Huh?”
What are you confused about? You gotta take what you gotta take. I thought of you the moment I saw it. What a pity.

Picking up my shield with my now-empty hand, I dragged my eyes away from the corpse. Hah, I was sure I could loot more useful things from him, but there was no time for that. I let go of my greed and faced forward.
“Kesial got hit!”
“Kill him!”

The enemies that had stopped in their tracks thanks to Lava Eruption came to their senses and attacked. I forced my tattered body forward because that was my role. I used Shield Charge, holding the shield up with my one remaining arm and putting all my weight on my shoulder as I ran. Maybe it was because we were nearing our destination, but the level of the adventurers here was much higher than it was outside, including the aura bastard from earlier. I guessed this was their frontline.
Shatter.
I hadn’t given a command, but a potion flew at me anyway. It was a rather gentle pain like my flesh was being scorched with fire rather than being stabbed repeatedly with an awl.
“That’s your favorite high-grade potion!”
Oh, no wonder. I feel a bit more energized. Let’s liven up and go again.
There was really not far left to go now. The finish line was right in front of us.
“From now on, I’ll help!” Ainar came up next to me.
“What about Raven?”
“I left her to Urakburak!” That was a good call. Raven had probably told her to do that.
“Behelaaah!”
I stopped using the terrain to check how far we had left to go. I focused only on the present moment.
“Missha! Stay right behind me!”
Just a little farther.
“Erwen! Now! Use that thing!”
Yes, just a little farther.
“Ack! N-No. Not now...”
“Yandel! Raven’s mana ran out!”

Just then, the magical support Raven was providing from behind Mr. Bear came to an end. That meant that it was no longer possible to use Oxygen Explosion to clear the path when it was blocked or when our speed was reduced.
“N-No! Lena...!”
As we slowed down, another person died—the sorcerer on Takelan’s team. She was a support-type sorcerer who specialized in defense and had been securing the rear.
“We’re so close...!”
Things would be tougher from now on. I gritted my teeth and brushed off the pang in my chest.
“God damn it!”

I didn’t have the luxury to plug my ears. Even if I could, I wouldn’t have done so. This was the decision I had made. Now I needed to concentrate and decide what I was willing to let go and what could absolutely not be discarded—what I was determined to protect.
“Missha!”
“Don’t worry! I can still fight...!”

In this fierce battle where another one of us could die at any moment, everyone paved the way with a single-minded passion. And after what felt like an eternity, a dark passageway finally came into view.
“This way!” As soon as I saw it, I immediately turned and entered the passageway. “Erwen, light!”
“Y-Yes!”

In place of Raven, whose mana was exhausted, Erwen summoned a fire spirit to illuminate our surroundings. The passageway was sparsely lined with monochromatic crystals. There were no adventurers from the city out here to greet us.
“Bjorn! They’re not following us!”
Our pursuers had stopped like this was the beginning of a new territory. So this was the boundary that divided the armies.
“Be alert and keep moving.”

It was still too early to be relieved. I kept moving forward without slowing down, figuring that it wouldn’t be too late to take a potion and regroup after we reached safety. And about three minutes later...
“Halt.”
We encountered a group we had longed so very much to see—a squad of ten knights.
Our surroundings were full of naked corpses, probably from Noark’s side. It was a good thing we’d risked our lives to get here. The fact that these guys were on our side was already relieving enough.
Hmm?
The knight whose eyes met mine drew his sword and took a slow step forward. The sword was overflowing with aura.
“We are not the enemy!” I shouted urgently. “Here is my identification—”
Oh, my arm... I left it back there.
“Well, I don’t have it, but everyone else does!” I hurriedly continued, but his reaction was cold.
“Now you’re trying all kinds of tactics, huh? That pathway is occupied by Noark, yet you speak of identification tags?”

Well, it did sound hard to believe. We probably looked like spies disguised as Rafdonians to infiltrate their line. So what should I do? Would they believe me if I told them that I was called Little Balkan?
After thinking it over for a moment, I realized that there was a better way. Coincidentally, I had been given something to use in this very situation. “Missha, take off your ring and show them.”

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Discarded Hand (4)
paragraphs: The knight who gave us this ring told us that showing it and providing his name would confirm our identity. Yeah, that was all he said.

But before I could even say who gave it to me, one of the knights recognized it. “That’s a Verbal Message ring. And... it belongs to Sir Garfizel, who left to scout out one of the second-floor portals.”
“Verbal Message ring...?”
When he saw my reaction, he chuckled. “Looks like you didn’t even know what this was. Just wait. Whether your words are true or not will now be revealed.”

When the knight twisted the jewel embedded in the ring, blue light leaked out and entered his body. The knight closed his eyes in silence as if to enjoy the afterglow. Then, about three minutes later, his mouth opened.
“The Corpse Collector is near the portal, huh?”
With that one sentence, everything clicked in my mind. Fuck, so that was why this was called a Verbal Message ring. No wonder he gave it to me when I hadn’t even asked for compensation.
I can see why he wanted me to have it.
The knight named Garfizel had wanted to use me, someone he had run into by chance, to deliver information. That was probably why he told us about this place too.
“By the dark zone, are you talking about the place where the monument is located?”
“Yes, head there. You’ll be safe as long as you get there.”
If the message ended up being delivered, that was good. If not, no harm was done. Still, he could have just been honest. Now I really felt like a sucker.
Why are there so many bastards in this world that treat people like puppets?
It left a bitter taste in my mouth, but the fortunate thing was that this ring confirmed our identities.
“Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel.” I had never revealed my name to him but the knight said it anyway.
“Did that clear your suspicions?”

“It’s safe to say you are not from Noark’s side. Although it’s unclear how you guys managed to get through their defenses on your own... come in. We will head to our temporary Central Headquarters to discuss this in more detail.”
“Glad to hear that. Do you have a priest too?” There was no way there wasn’t a priest here, but I was mostly just beating around the bush.

Fortunately, the knight seemed to understand what I was getting at. He noticed the state we were in and nodded. “Yes, I suppose you need treatment first.” That was a bit of a surprise. I thought he’d be inflexible and insist the debrief came first. “Your comrades will be taken to a makeshift infirmary.”
“...What about me?”
“The debrief comes first.”
Ha, well, I guessed in some ways he could still be considered a gentleman. “I can wait, so go on and take a break.”
“But...!” Missha protested my decision, but I silently turned my gaze somewhere else, to where a patient whose condition was more critical than my missing arm was lying.
“Is Daria okay?”
“I-I’m not sure. Rrraven used a curse-removal spell but she hasn’t woken up...”
“The priest will treat her. You should take her over there.”
“...I’m sorry,” said Erwen.

What was there to be sorry about? She was acting like she’d committed a sin or something. I smiled and patted her on the shoulder. Then I headed over to Raven for a brief exchange. “You are the leader when I am not around. I know it’ll be tough because of your mana exhaustion, but I’ll leave you to it.”
“...Don’t worry about the team. I’ll take care of it. I may be worn out, but not as much as you.”
Hmm, that line probably didn’t sound right coming from a one-armed bastard, huh?
“If you’re done, follow me,” said the knight. “My subordinate will take your comrades to the infirmary.”
“Okay.”

After that, I was separated from the group and followed the knight inside their makeshift HQ. The sight I was greeted with was an unfamiliar one. The dark zone, which was usually free of light, was all lit up thanks to the torches they had installed.
Looks like a temporary shelter.
If the outer area was composed of guards and adventurers, the inside was a bit different. Adventurers were packed inside the narrow passageway, all of them either sitting down or lying down to rest.
“There’s no fog here.”
“We’ve put a defensive magic circle in place.”
“Defensive magic circle...?”
“Ah, you wouldn’t know yet if you came from the outside. The fog is a poison-type dark spell, although it’s not very potent considering the wide range.”

A poison-type dark spell, huh? Was it Evil Supper, then? Since breathing it in didn’t seem to cause any harm and there was enough of it to cover the entire first floor, I had assumed it had to be a fog spell cast solely to block our vision.
Just how many dark wizards did they grind for that?
A chill ran down my spine. What would have happened if we had decided to head to the remote outskirts and hold out on our own?
...We would’ve been fucked.

No matter how weak the poison, after a few days of exposure, symptoms would have appeared. Only then would I have realized what the fog was and started coming up with a countermeasure. And considering how late in the game that would have been, we would have had way fewer options.
“Hey, you, you can rest but stick to the wall.”
“Ah, yes... Sorry.”
We walked through that narrow passageway for about twenty minutes. Finally, the center cavern appeared. No, it would be more accurate to call it a square.
“...How did you do this?”
“We used wizards to demolish the nearby walls and expand the area. We couldn’t accommodate everyone in a small space.”

Huh. Was this military-style civil engineering? I supposed there was nothing you couldn’t do when so many people were gathered. The cavern, which used to have a radius of about thirty yards, was now hundreds of times larger in size. The expansion contained barracks that housed different clans.
“Come in.”
The knight brought me to a large barrack located in the very center. At the entrance was the flag of the imperial family of Rafdonia, and inside, I saw people having a meeting around a round table.
A meeting of the leaders, huh?

Although this was the palace barracks, it wasn’t filled with just knights. Adventurers wearing the marks of famous clans were also present and passionately discussing something. There was a familiar face among them.
“Oh, you’re—!” The woman looked like she had just seen a ghost.
I smiled viciously and said hello. “We meet again, Versyl Gowland.” I didn’t realize we would meet again so soon, either.
“How are you... Did you find a wizard capable of teleportation?”
Of course not. Instead of answering, I waved my arm, which stopped at the elbow.

Judging by her expression, she seemed to understand what that meant. “...You got through there?” Versyl muttered in disbelief. After all, we had just cleared the route these guys had given up on. It seemed she hadn’t expected us to succeed. “How did you do it?”
Well, I wasn’t proud of it, but I’d used a method similar to hers. I discarded what I needed to discard, as per my priorities.

In the middle of my reunion with Versyl, a man interrupted and commanded silence. “Enough chitchat.” So this guy was the big man here. “Sir Ergos, you should be on the frontline. What are you doing here? And who is this barbarian next to you?”
“I had something to report to you, so I temporarily left my post.”
“Tell me.”
“I have obtained Sir Garfizel’s Verbal Message ring.”
“...Sir Garfizel’s?”
“Yes. This man is an adventurer named Bjorn Yandel. He delivered the ring to me.”

When the knight handed over the message ring, the man activated it. After some time, he spoke, keeping his eyes on me. “I am Marco Elbern. I am the head of the Third Royal Guard.” It seemed he was finally interested in me. “I’m going to ask you a few questions. Can you answer them honestly?”
“...I will.”
“First, if the contents of this ring’s message are true, that means that the Corpse Collector is positioned north at the portal leading to the Goblin Forest.”
Some of the adventurers at the table let out exclamations of “Corpse Collector!” but not loud enough to disturb the conversation. I didn’t have to worry about them right now.
“What are you trying to ask?”
“Is this reliable information?”
“It’s reliable. I did escape him, but I also engaged in battle with him for a brief time.”
“You fought him? May I know what your rank is?”
“...Rank five.”
When I revealed my ranking, the head of the guards touched his chin with a strange look on his face. “If those words are true, it’s safe to say that the man let you go.”

“Probably.” I readily admitted that. To be honest, the Corpse Collector seemed solely interested in blocking off the portal to the second floor. If it weren’t for that, we would have had a lot of trouble getting away. “Are those all your questions?”
“No, one more. It sounds like just now you entered through the path assigned to Sir Ergos. Is that true?”
“That’s right.”
“I want to hear about that in more detail. Was there a way to avoid the enemy?”
“If there was, do you think I’d look like this right now?”
“...That’s fair. Then tell me in more detail how you got all the way here. It may be beneficial to our strategy.”

Although I had already sufficiently proven that I wasn’t an adventurer from Noark, there wasn’t a point in refusing this request and causing trouble. I explained the twenty-minute battle as concisely as I could. And it seemed it had been enough to convey what a desperate road we had just traveled.
“A moving story.” Marco’s gaze became a little friendlier. The clan members who were also listening to my story looked at me in fascination as well. “I see the qualities of a commander in you.”
“If I were one, more than half of us wouldn’t have died.”
“That’s why I said ‘qualities.’ Your teammates are all alive. A great commander is not a person who makes the perfect choices. They’re a person who makes the necessary ones.”

It didn’t seem like he was mocking me or anything, but I didn’t want to talk about this. Even if it was a compliment, I wasn’t that pleased about it. I changed the subject. “If there are no more questions, I want to go soon.”
“I have one more question for you. The man you ran into at the end. Did he have a scar on his chin?”
A scar? “He did.”
When I nodded, the knight laughed, amused. “I had my doubts since you spoke of an adamantium greatsword, but it was the Snake Knight.”
“Snake Knight?”
“A bastard who stabbed his master’s child and escaped to Noark. He’s rather infamous, but I guess it was too long ago for you to know about him.”
No wonder he used an aura. He had been a knight. And given how the adventurers around us were murmuring, it seemed he once had a bit of a reputation.
“Anyway, congratulations. Since you killed that man, your reputation will go up.”
“My reputation, huh?”
“What, don’t barbarians like that?”
You’re not wrong, but I’m not like normal barbarians, you see.
Of course, there was nothing wrong with a good reputation. I had to get permission to enter the royal capital of Karnon, after all.
“I like it if I return alive.”
It wouldn’t be too late to think about stuff like that later. It hadn’t even been one day since the labyrinth opened.
“I’ve kept an injured man for too long. Go rest. Sir Ergos will tell you the rules of our settlement.”
With that, I headed out of the barracks and, guided by a knight, headed to the temporary infirmary to join my teammates.
“Mister!”
“How’s Daria?”
“The priest healed her and she’s all better now. She is sleeping... But it’s all thanks to you!” Now that her sister had been treated, Erwen had regained her composure and livened up again.
Missha came up and removed Erwen from my person. “Hey! Stop botherrring him and go away.”
“Excuse me?”
“‘Excuse me?’ Can’t you see Bjorn is hurrrt?”
“Let me see. Are you okay? Is there anywhere else that hurrrts? You must be tired, getting called there even after all that. Let’s go show your arm to the prrriest.”

It looked like everyone else’s injuries had been treated already, so I followed Missha to the priest. Oh, for reference, everything was free of charge because this was a wartime situation. All adventurers had to follow the orders of the king. This infirmary was probably a gathering of priests from a bunch of different parties.
“You won’t recover your full strength for about a day and it’ll feel strange. I need to go treat the other patients. May the brilliance of the sun be with you.”

With one heal, my arm grew back in just a few minutes. I once again realized how important it was to have a priest. If I had tried to heal myself with an advanced potion, it would have taken at least two or three bottles. This went beyond regrowing a severed arm—the higher the person’s physical ability, the weaker the effect of a potion.
If I form a clan, I’ll have to find a priest somehow.
After receiving treatment, I rejoined my teammates. “Raven, do you have any information on the situation here?”
“They assigned us a spot, kind of.”
“Assigned us a spot?”

“Where we’ll be sleeping from now on. We all received a map, and it looked like we were in an outer passageway, I guess because we got here late. I think the innermost part of the safe zone is already full.”
I laughed silently at Raven’s words. The innermost area was full of the barracks of large clans. Had they been assigned there because they arrived early?
“Anyway, let’s head over there quick. We have to take turns on guard shifts starting tomorrow.”

Geez, it was like being in the military. Picking up on the tension in the air, a question suddenly came to mind. “...But where is Takelan?” Takelan Arvenon, a rank-five adventurer, had been the only other survivor of my plan.
As soon as I mentioned Takelan’s name, everyone froze.

“Oh, him...” Raven tried to paste on a smile as she answered. “He left as soon as he got his assignment. Anyone who is here alone or in a team of two or fewer is used to fill vacancies in other parties.”
“Really?”
Then couldn’t he just have added himself to our team? The clans were moving as a unit too. There were a lot of teams made up of more than six people walking around, anyway.
When I expressed that, Raven smiled awkwardly. “He wanted to go. So you don’t have to worry about it.”

“If you say so.” I nodded nonchalantly, but inside I was thinking, Something happened while I was away. An incident occurred. I didn’t know why they were hiding it from me, though. Well, I could just ask Ainar or Missha about it later.
“Erwen, you’re joining up with the Blue Wall Clan, right?” I asked.
“Yes... I d-don’t want to but Daria said we had to... She said it could lead to problems down the line because of our contract.”

Well, the contract was one thing but Daria probably also thought it would be much safer that way since Blue Wall included a whopping six parties. Of course, one of those parties had disappeared on the way here, though.
“Then we’ll get going. Take care of your sister once she wakes up. And always be wary of your surroundings.”
“Okay...!”
After leaving Erwen, we headed to our assigned spot. It was a passageway located on the outskirts and not even two yards away from the team right next to us.
“It’s been a long time since I’ve slept on the first floorrr...”

Like the adventurers that we were, we spread our sleeping bags out on the floor without complaint and lay next to each other. All of us knew that we should be very thankful that we could even sleep like this.
Honkkk!

As soon as she laid down, Ainar started snoring. I didn’t know why, but at the sound, I remembered everything I had to do: check out the loot from today, inspect the equipment that got covered in lava, and wash my body, which was soaked in blood and sweat. Oh, I should also look into what happened to Takelan. My to-do list was mountainous, even though we’d done all that work already.
Ugh, whatever. Do it tomorrow.
When I closed my eyes, the strength left my body. It was like I was sinking.
Just when my consciousness was slowly drifting away, I heard Missha’s voice from beside me. “Bjorrrn, you did well today.”
Then I heard Raven’s voice from my other side. “Yes. You really went through a lot.”
Abman also chuckled bashfully and added, “Get some rest, Yandel.”
Honkkk!
Only then did it fully hit me that our exceptionally long first day was finally over.

chapters.title: Chapter 216: Discarded Hand (5)
paragraphs: Orcules was a group of famous criminals who rebelled against the king. Though not older than a few decades, this group has gained notoriety by committing numerous crimes and acts of terrorism since its inception. The palace had placed enormous bounties on its members and launched a manhunt, but had only been able to eliminate seven of them so far due to their stealthy operations.
“And there are seven of them here, huh?” After hearing his subordinate’s report, the head of the Third Royal Guard Marco Elbern could not hide his groan.

As soon as disaster struck, he immediately responded and formed a safe zone in the center of the first floor to declare a state of war and seize command. The first thing Marco did was gather information. He sent search parties toward the portals to the second floor, which could be plowed through at any moment. He stayed up all night accepting report after report.

As a result, seven members of Orcules had been identified. Three were prowling around near the safe zone committing massacres—the Wailing Witch, Black Claw, and the Lighthouse Keeper—and the other four were blocking the second-floor portals.
So that was their goal from the start.

Elbern clenched his fists in a show of frustration. The first three were a problem too, but those four were the biggest stumbling blocks. The Corpse Collector, who was all the more so for being an evil spirit, was a man infamous for his grotesque and brutal acts. The Fallen Scholar, once the head of a great school of magic, had become a criminal after tampering with forbidden magic. The Blood Knight started as a soldier born in Bifron and gained notoriety for killing the head of the First Royal Guard.
And finally... Traitor.

The man who had gathered those deranged bastards to create the group known as Orcules had single-handedly written a history of countless wrongdoings and massacres. Seven representatives of that group were all here, but it wasn’t just Orcules they had to be wary of. Countless big-name criminals had escaped to Noark. With all of them working together against them, Elbern couldn’t guarantee they’d win even at their full strength.

Eventually, after a long silence, Elbern opened his mouth. “I’m canceling the plan to fight through the bastards and get to the second floor.” Another heavy silence accompanied those words, weighing down the air in the room.
After struggling with himself for a moment, one knight spoke up. “...Day three will begin soon.”
“I’m aware. But as long as the Fallen Scholar is also here, the portal is very likely to be useless anyway.”
“Then...”
Elbern blinked slowly in an attempt to shake off his thoughts. A commander had to make decisions. “Gather wizards who can use portal magic as stealthily as possible.”
So he had to make the necessary decisions, no matter what sacrifices they resulted in.
I opened my eyes and checked the time—12:17 a.m. Another day had passed before I knew it and it was already the third day.

Nothing big had happened yesterday. I sorted through the loot we’d obtained on the way here, located an adventurer with repair-related abilities and fixed some broken equipment, stood guard with the rest of our team on our shift, and, as soon as guard duty was over, went around the neighborhood and collected information. I also heard what happened with Takelan.
“...Uh, that perrrson?”

I worked hard to pry it out of Missha but after finally hearing what had happened, it didn’t seem like a big deal. Seeing that we were all alive, he snapped and lost his mind for a moment. He blurted out some cruel things, but he didn’t get very far.
“Aruru was no joke. She shouted back, saying how could he say that when you were dragged away in the state that you were in... Geez, it even made me sweat.”
Hmm, Raven was quite fierce when she was mad. It was still a mystery how that small body could hold so much gusto.
“Anyway, that’s all. Ainar got mad too, but he disappeared beforrre she could draw her sword.”

I was thankful for my teammates’ actions on my behalf, but the more details I heard, the more my jaw tightened. These guys didn’t know that I had purposely placed them behind me to increase our chances of survival even the slightest bit.
“Huh? Why are you making that face?”
“It’s nothing. I’m just hungry.”

Takelan’s anger was justified. If the formation had been designed solely with efficiency in mind, more people could have survived, but I hadn’t done that. Although they might have been better suited to taking up the rear, I had placed my teammates where it was relatively safer—right behind me. Takelan must have realized that afterward, which was why he had reacted that way.
It’s probably best to keep that to myself.

After taking a moment to fully wake up, I slowly got up and folded up my sleeping bag. Although it had been busy enough, day two had been much calmer compared to our intense first day. But that ended now.
“Mm, Mr. Yandel...?” Raven woke up at the sound of me moving around and poked her head out while rubbing her eyes.
“Did I wake you? Sorry.”
“No, I just couldn’t sleep...”
“Are you done sleeping?”
At my question, Raven dragged her upper body out of her sleeping bag and sat up. “And what about you? Are you done sleeping?”
“I can’t sleep, either.”
“Is that why you were going to stand guard alone?”
I smirked and readily admitted it. It would be funny to try to claim otherwise when we were in the same boat. “It’s already the third day...”

On the third day, the Lord of the Floor spawned if five or more people were gathered in one place. Of course, there was a fixed probability of it appearing near us. Since ten thousand adventurers were already gathered on the first floor, the possibility that it would be summoned right in front of us was low, but...
You never know.
I was the tank of this team. Even if the Lord of the Floor dropped down right in front of our eyes, I could make time for my teammates to escape.
Whooom!
At that moment, the ground began to tremble and the monochromatic crystals embedded in the cave walls emitted a brilliant light. The color of the glow was blood red.
“Mr. Yandel, this is...!”
This meant that the Lord of the Floor had appeared somewhere.
“W-What is it?!” Starting with Ainar, the rest of my teammates woke up one by one. The same went for the other groups of adventurers who were sleeping nearby.
I calmly placated my teammates. “Don’t be too freaked out. Luckily, I don’t think it appeared nearby.”
Where the Lord of the First Floor was, there was bound to be a loud sound. Since there was no such sound, it was safe to say that it had spawned somewhere far away.
“Everybody get back to sleep.”
“I’ll wake you up if something happens. It hasn’t been long since our guard shift ended.”
“But you’re tired too.”
“I dozed a little so I’m fine.”

I wasn’t sure if they would be able to sleep right away, but I forced my teammates to get back into their sleeping bags and close their eyes, deciding that recovering their stamina was our top priority.
Whooom...

About twenty minutes later, as if their battery had run out, the crystals that illuminated our surroundings went dark. That meant the Lord of the Floor had been eliminated. Of course, it was still too early to be relieved. Unlike the lords of the upper floors, which took months or years to respawn, this guy could be resummoned multiple times.
“We’ll be okay, right...?”
“Don’t worry. Thirty proper adventurers can take down the Lord of the First Floor. In our current situation, no matter where it appears, it’ll be quickly dealt with.”

That was also the biggest reason why I wanted to charge down that gruesome passageway to join the palace’s forces. Here, we’d be safe from the Lord of the Floor. Even if it showed up right under our noses, help would come if I could just hold out.
“Then I’ll leave this place to you.”
“Where are you going?”
“To obtain some information.”
“Then I’ll go w—”
“It’d be a waste of manpower. If you really can’t sleep, stand guard with the rest of them.”

As soon as the Lord of the Floor was defeated, I left our assigned area and headed to the center region. The respawn time of the Lord of the Floor was six hours. In the meantime, I was going to look around and see if there was anything unusual because there was nothing else to do.
While I advanced using the marks drawn on the walls by the imperial troops, I also kept an ear open to the nearby conversations of other adventurers.
“Hey, did you hear? I heard it was the south passageway.”
“You mean where the Lord of the Floor appeared?”
“Yeah, I heard about twenty people died by the time support came.”
“Damn it, I’d rather those underground bastards come at us instead.”

This was the idle gossip of adventurers in a similar situation to me, so the things they said weren’t very reliable, but I couldn’t just ignore them, either. Still, it was more than useful to learn public opinion.
“I don’t know how much longer we’ll have to stay here.”
“I know. In the last speech they gave, they said they would clear the path to the second-floor portal soon. But it’s already the third day.”
“It’s making me nervous that they’re so quiet.”
As expected, adventurers were showing distrust toward our leadership, which had not announced anything since the first day. The same went for me.
They should be making a decision soon...
If the Lord of the Floor was killed every six hours, that meant a total of eight Lords would be killed in two days. That meant that on the fifth day, that thing would most definitely appear.
With a large clan and even the head of the guards here, they can’t possibly not know that...
But why hadn’t they taken any action yet? I was incredibly curious about the conversation that had been held at that meeting the day I got here.
They must know that that’s what Noark is after too... But why are they just holding out?
I thought for sure they would choose to clear a path somewhere and advance to the second floor.
Trudge, trudge.
The more worried I grew, the more I increased my walking speed. Then a familiar face appeared—the guy who had first discovered the backpack copying bug and spread it far and wide within the tribe.
“Kharon...?”

“Bjorn, the great warrior and son of Yandel!” When I recognized him first and spoke to him, Kharon got up immediately and rushed toward me with his usual intensity. “To meet you here! As expected, you are destined to lead us!”
I was a bit taken aback but I accepted the greeting in true barbarian form since I was glad to see him too. I asked the question on my mind. “But who are those people next to you?”
“The warriors I met here!”
“You met them here?”

I couldn’t understand this at all. The barbarian backpack copy bug had been blocked a long time ago. That the technique had been widely spread among adventurers was one contributing factor, but the biggest factor was that the stream of lower-level adventurers had dried up after the magical identification tags were created since it cost seventy thousand stones to get one tag. That was why I heard Kharon had joined a third-floor team not long ago.
“What happened to your team?”
“Oh, they died on the way here! So the soldiers introduced me to some warriors who were left alone like me!”
Damn soldier bastards. A party of five barbarian warriors... It was obvious they just put these guys together because they were fed up with them.
“A-Are you really Little Balkan! It’s an honor to meet you! I-I am Devan, the second son of Verox!”

“Oh, hey. Nice to meet you too.” Greeting the barbarians who were excited at my name, I continued my conversation with Kharon. Maybe if I hadn’t noticed him in the first place it would have been different... but I couldn’t just leave him now that I had. “Why don’t you join us instead of staying here?”
“I-Is that all right?”

The identification tags and the equipment they were wearing alone were enough to tell me they were warriors active on the third floor or higher. Having them with me would definitely be a help. More importantly, I could trust them.

“Of course you can,” I told Kharon, who was greatly appreciative of what area our team was assigned to. “I’ll let the administrative officer know on the way, so you guys can head over first. If you see a wizard, be polite and say that I sent you.”
“Okay!”
“Ah, if you don’t know which way to go, ask the adventurers nearby. If you shout and wake them up, they’ll let you know even if it’s annoying.”
“Ooh! I see!”
I sent Kharon’s group off and was about to leave when I stopped at the low sound of a man’s voice. “Bjorn Yandel.”

When I turned around, I saw the last person I wanted to run into. “Takelan Arvenon.” He was among a group of adventurers I had never seen before. That was a given. He had lost all his comrades on the way here.
In the silence, Takelan studied me. The twitch in his chin proved that he was holding something back with great difficulty.
I spoke first. “I heard what happened while I was gone. Do you resent me?”

Takelan didn’t nod nor shake his head—he just stood there like it was all he could do to survive. It took a long time for him to answer me. “No, I do not resent you.” That was an unexpected response. Takelan spoke slowly, emotion in every word. “I kept thinking about it because that was all I could do. How did things end up this way? Lena is dead, but how can you guys smile and laugh? If those bastards didn’t run away in the middle, maybe Lena could have lived. No, above all, I kept wondering... Did you not know things would turn out like this?”
“So, did you reach a conclusion?”
“I don’t know. The fact is, you are the one who was the most injured. And you are the one who had the hardest job. And it wasn’t a situation where you could guarantee even your teammates’ survival.”

Was there such a thing as a situation where anything was guaranteed? I only did my best to raise our chances of survival even the slightest bit. That was why it felt like a sharp knife was scraping at something inside of me.

“I shouldn’t have followed you. However,” Takelan continued, “I was the one who chose to. I was the one who voted for you as the leader too. I was the one who just watched silently when that woman said they’d use a teleportation spell...! It was all me.”
Watching him direct all the blame on himself in self-hatred, I was seized by an indescribably painful feeling.
“So I don’t resent you.”
“...I see.”
What could I possibly say in this situation? I couldn’t even offer up clumsy words of consolation. But did my hesitation tell him everything I needed to know?
“Don’t pity me.” Takelan ended the conversation there and sat down again. “There will come a day when you feel the same way as I do.”
His eyes were no longer directed at me—only at the floor. I sensed that all the words we would ever exchange had been said.
Trudge, trudge.

So, I continued on my way again. Takelan did not speak up as I left, and a while later, the passageway widened and a wide central cavern appeared. I first located an administrator and let them know that Kharon’s group had joined ours.
“Team Apple Narak... Oh, you’re at a passageway outside the Northern District. Okay, it’s been registered.”
That ended my business, but just as I was about to turn around, a knight came out of the barracks, walked up to the administrative officer who had helped me, and glanced my way.
Murmur, murmur.
He named a total of six schools.
“Oh, yes. A wizard from that school? Let me check the list.”
As if priests weren’t enough, now they’re trying to conscript wizards?
That was my first thought, but as I turned the names of the schools the knight mentioned over in my head, I noticed they all had one thing in common.
“Derta, Sperys, Jacquard...”
Portal magic.
Wizards of those schools who were above rank four were able to open a portal that could carry up to thirty people. The moment I realized this fact, my heart pounded uncontrollably.
Thump!
There was no point in denial. A conversation I had not too long ago flashed through my mind.
“A great commander is not a person who makes the perfect choices. They’re a person who makes the necessary ones.”
That man would without hesitation discard what he deemed to be low priority. All of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 217: Ruler (1)
paragraphs: A portal was a kind of innate magic that only a few schools dealt with. In this game riddled with all kinds of death flags, I didn’t have to explain how much of a cheat this spell was. Making it possible for you to return to the city without having to wait for the labyrinth to close? That was an unbeatable survival tool in itself.
Well, it doesn’t come without its limitations, though.

The way to counter it was widely known so it wasn’t easy to use it as an escape during battles against other people. In addition, it could only carry a maximum of thirty people at a time. This was also the reason why upper-floor expeditions were almost always composed of groups of thirty.
More importantly, once they use it once, a wizard can never use the spell again.

Note that this was different from in the game. Originally, only an archmage who had reached rank one could use the Portal spell, and once used, that wizard would die. However, this was 150 years into the future from the time of the game. The six schools that possessed the formula for the Portal spell had come together for a joint study and created a way for even lower-ranking wizards to use this magic. I didn’t know the details since I wasn’t a wizard, but I knew that it was only possible for someone to use it once in their life.
I’m sure there won’t be any wizards who will refuse to use the spell in this situation, either...

So how many of them were in the labyrinth? Well, it would be quite a few. Finding a wizard who could use Portal magic was the top priority for large clans, and the schools offered up wizards who could still use the spell to support expeditions.
Still, even if you gather everyone and their mother, it won’t be more than 150.
That meant that, realistically, fewer than 4500 people would be able to escape this hell through the portal.
Official palace knights, and the elites of large clans that had their own wizards... In actuality, it’s safe to say everyone else will be abandoned.

The more concrete the numbers became, the more I realized what a ridiculous thing they were planning to do. These numbers were different from that time with the Lord of the Third Floor. At the very least, tens of thousands of adventurers would die here.
Yet this is the decision they made, huh?

Shoving aside the dizzying feeling, I continued walking through this logically. What may have been the most important thing at this moment was why the commander of the Royal Guard had made this decision.
He probably determined that the path to the second floor was blocked or no different.

It was impossible to get out of the first floor. No, it may have been possible, but it would cost more lives than just a few fleeing through the portal. And so, the commander had made this decision. It seemed he felt that preserving his troops as much as possible and returning to the city was strategically the right thing to do.
“I see you are here again.”
I turned around at the sudden presence behind me and froze in place.
Geez, you surprised me.
“Was it Bjorn Yandel?” I didn’t know when he’d shown up, but the commander of the Royal Guard was right behind me. His name was...
“Marco Elbern.”
“You have a good memory for a barbarian.”

Normally I wouldn’t back down here and would fire back at him, but I replied delicately this time. “Thank you for the compliment.” He was the most powerful person in this place, after all. Even if it was short, the chance to speak with him alone was a godsend. After thinking it over for a long moment, I asked him something, deciding to be straightforward like the barbarian I was. “I see you’re looking for wizards capable of portal magic. Are you planning on running away?” First, the most important question that would confirm whether I was right or not.
As soon as he heard the question, Elbern’s eyes hardened. “You are very much a barbarian in this sense. No one else would have dared to ask me directly.”
Well, as you can see, I am a barbarian.
When I just stared back in silence, Elbern asked a question of his own this time. “Where did you hear that?”
That was enough for me. So, it was true. I had wondered if maybe he had some other plan in play here.
“I heard the knight give instructions to the administrator.”

“...He’s not vigilant enough. Or was careless for being near a barbarian.” From the look in his eyes, it seemed the knight would end up being punished for that, but that had nothing to do with me. I was just about to get us back on track when the commander continued, giving me an unreadable look. “Hmm, or I guess you could also be smarter than I thought. I should just tell you at this point. The administrative officer gave me information about your team’s composition.”
“...You looked into me?”
“I had a feeling I’d be interested soon enough.”
Interested, huh? Is this a good thing or the opposite?

It ended up being both. “I can take you and the wizard if you promise to serve the Imperial Army for just one year.” He was offering me a ticket to ride the portal back home. The problem was that it only had two seats.
“And the rest?”
“You know already what the choice I have to make is.”
Fuck, so they’re below his standards. I thought I leveled them up enough over the past few months.
“So, what will you do?”
I was at a crossroads.
“I want you to answer me now. I don’t have much time.”
Should I choose my and one other teammate’s lives? Or gamble with everyone’s?
“Can you... win?”
“Don’t worry. We will definitely return home alive.”
A fleeting conversation I had had in the past flashed through my mind.
“I...” I answered without hesitation. “I will not abandon my team.”
Perhaps my brain had turned into a barbarian’s too.
[The second Lord of Terror has been slain.]
[The third Lord of Terror has been slain.]
[The fourth Lord of Terror has been slain.]
[The fifth Lord of Terror has been slain.]
Time passed. I kept quiet about the conversation I had had with the commander.
“Keep the news about the portal to yourself, if you value your teammates’ lives.”
His threat was a factor, but I also didn’t feel the need to mention it. The news would spread quickly enough on its own. And it indeed did.
“Mr. Yandel, have you heard the rumors?”

It was impossible to keep thousands of people quiet, especially if they were not a tight-knit group. The commander’s portal escape plan was spread by word of mouth and it didn’t take long for it to reach Raven’s ears.
“Yes, I know.”
“...What are you going to do? Do you think it’s just a rumor too?”

Mr. Bear and Missha turned toward us at that question. I guessed they had discussed it among themselves already before asking me. Well, there were probably only a few people who hadn’t noticed the oppressive air filling this cave.
“Kharon, you can’t even lift that greatsword? How can you call yourself a man!?”
“I-I can lift it! Look!”
“Ohh! Then you’re half a man!”
The barbarians had been playing around with a single adamantium greatsword for almost an hour. Sometimes I envied their lack of concern and the way they could keep moving forward with no worries.
“Uh, Mr. Yandel...?”
“Oh, sorry, I was thinking about something else for a second.” I tried smiling as cheerfully as I could and patted Raven’s shoulder. “Don’t worry about the rumors! Everything will be fine!”
It will work out. I will make sure it does.
I just wanted these guys to keep on going without concern. We only needed one person to be constantly suspicious and anxious about the traps and enemies that lay ahead.
“Ugh, why are you being so unnecessarily positive?!”
“That’s what being a leader is.”
“Ugh, okay, stop slapping my shoulder!”

I ended the conversation there and closed my eyes again, falling into thought. They had all revolved around the same thing as of late: how could we all survive and get back to the city together? I cycled through the same problem thousands of times, made countless plans and discarded them, and with each plan I came up with, checked each numerous times for variables and miscalculations.
It has to be perfect.
If plan A didn’t work, plan B. And if that didn’t work, plan C. Whenever there was time to spare like this, I ran simulations from start to finish and assumed the worst in each one.
Whooom!
As if to remind me that the tipping point was nearing, a weak vibration began to run through the ground beneath me.
“That’s already the eighth.”

That was the eighth Lord of the Floor to appear. This had happened multiple times over the past several days, so Raven and the others didn’t seem particularly concerned about it. That was because they didn’t know what happened when the ninth Lord of the Floor was defeated.
That’s probably why there have been no protests despite the rumors. Most will think the idea that the knights are going to portal out is nonsense.
From the perspective of the average person, there was no reason for leadership to use portals to escape. They didn’t know about that special event.
“Anyway, I guess it’s nearby, judging by the screams...”
“It may come this way, so be on guard.”
We waited until the Lord of the Floor was defeated, staying alert just in case. Just then, I sensed a presence from behind us.
“Please make way!”
A group moved quickly through the passageway, pushing through adventurers like a dispatched ambulance. Sticking to the walls, they soon ran past us like the wind.
“It’s the Eramel Star Clan.”
Judging by how they were moving toward the screams, it seemed this group from a well-known, large clan was on their way to defeat the Lord of the Floor.
“Since support is on its way, it will get dark again soon.”
The Lord of the First Floor could be taken down with just thirty adventurers. With the proper strategy, it was possible with even fewer. I smiled bitterly.
I don’t know why they keep going after the Lord of the Floor when they’re going to abandon us anyway.

The Lord of the First Floor had no loot, dropped no essences, and even if you managed to preserve its remains through Distortion magic, they weren’t all that valuable, either. The only reward you got for defeating it was that you could then be promoted to a rank-four clan, where the real benefits began. That was why this guy was mostly used as a test. Like a rite of passage for reaching a certain level, it was a monster that most people defeated just once.
Is it guilt? Like, “We did our best ‘til the end”?

The thought came to mind but there was probably a more realistic reason. They had to seem like they were doing their part until right before they were about to leave so that those left behind wouldn’t notice.
“Kyaaaaaa!”
About twenty more minutes passed and we heard a loud scream in the distance, after which the red-hot crystals turned off. That meant that the Lord of the Floor had been dealt with.
“It’ll be day five tomorrow, so we just have to hold out for two more days.”
I checked the time every once in a while and continued to revise my plans. Soon, it was 10:07 p.m., around two hours after the eighth Lord of the Floor had been defeated. No, in other words...
“God damn it!”
...About four hours before all hell would break loose.
“Everybody get inside! The rumors were true!”
“Those bastards from the palace are running away and leaving us! Stop them!”
A commotion erupted inside the cave.
“You bastards! Get out, get out of the way!”
“Back off, adventurer. If you come any closer, I will cut you down.”
“Either way I’m going to die so—!”
Slice! Thud, roll.
At that exact moment, in the central zone where the barracks of the imperial knights and large clans were located, an adventurer’s head fell to the ground.
“Anyone else coming closer?”
Their hesitation at the knight’s murderous threat only lasted so long.
“What are you doing? Push!”
“I’m getting out of here! I said I’m going!”
“Ahh! My arm! My arm...!”
Adventurers rushed like moths toward the blinding light of life. This was a scene that was playing out in all the passageways connected to the central cavern simultaneously.
“The real enemy is out there, yet they are eager to shed unnecessary blood.”
The commander of the Third Royal Guard and the cause of this situation, Marco Elbern, clicked his tongue and asked his lieutenant, “What is the current percentage?”
“A little more than half have escaped.”
“Half, huh? This will take much longer than we planned.”

If they had been able to use the portals to escape to the city all at once, this commotion would not have happened. However, portal magic tended to suck in mana from the surrounding area, so the only option was to cast the spells sequentially.
“It is our turn soon. Leave this to the remaining knights, Commander.”
Elbern followed the lieutenant to the center. A new portal was opening just in time, emitting a dazzling light.
Whooom!
Elbern let go of all his regrets and slowly approached the portal.
“Please, take me too!”
“Aaagh!”
With every step he took, he heard a mixture of emotional screams and the clang of weapons.
Rattle, rattle.
Elbern paused in front of the portal, suddenly remembering a conversation he had two days ago.
“I will not abandon my team.”
He was an impressive man in many ways, very much a barbarian, yet not at the same time. And he was also a bit disappointing.
“I misunderstood you, it seems. I never thought you would make the wrong choice.”
He had lost interest in the barbarian at that moment. It was on a sheer whim that he had made that offer in the first place, but to think that man wouldn’t take advantage of his good fortune...
“Keep the news about the portal to yourself, if you value your teammates’ lives.”
He intended to leave after that threat, but at that moment, the barbarian said something strange.
“You feel guilty.”
“Guilty...?”
“That must be why you’re disappointed that I refused.”
At first, he couldn’t understand what he was talking about. But soon, a cold voice filled the space between them.
“You wanted me to convince you that your choice was the right one, no?”
Elbern hadn’t been able to argue. Even he hadn’t noticed it himself, but for a split second, he thought that the man might be right.
“Knight, I am different from you. So don’t use me to placate yourself.”
The conversation with the barbarian had ended there. They would probably never talk face-to-face ever again.
“Commander, we must go.”

Elbern looked up and stared ahead. Unlike the dark labyrinth around him, the sliver of the city he could see through the portal was bright. It was the only city in this cursed world, the place he had to protect, the last stronghold.
“For Rafdonia.”
He pushed himself through the portal. This was the choice he had to make.
Finally, the moment of truth was here. I closed my eyes for a moment, gathered my breath, and repeated my mantra.
Do what you have to do.
I opened my eyes. “Everyone, follow me. We’re moving toward the center.”
“Pardon? What are you going to do there?”
What else was there to do? By the time we arrived, all kinds of talents abandoned by their various groups would be drowning in despair.
First, we’ll need to match their weight class.
We had to gather our forces. That was the first step toward survival.

chapters.title: Chapter 218: Ruler (2)
paragraphs: “No! Take me with you—!”
“...I’m sorry.”

Once one last adventurer squeezed his eyes shut and entered the portal, the battle finally came to an end. The reason was simple. There were still knights all over the passageways blocking the other adventurers.
“Surrender,” said their commander.
“Sorry? But our portal hasn’t been cast yet—”
“That portal was the last one. I’m sorry, all of you.”
“C-Commander, what do you—! Ahhh!”
As soon as one of the knights lowered his sword, adventurers rushed in from all sides to trample him and beat him up.
“Speak! What does that mean? Why is that the last portal?!”
The knight simply endured all the violence. He answered questions even as his teeth were kicked out and the veins in his eyes burst. “It is as he said.”
“Y-You deranged bastard! Then you knew you would be abandoned and still...!”
“Someone had to stay behind. Your anger is justified, so take it out on me. This body of mine is still worth that much, at least.”
“I will kill you!”
“For... Rafdonia...!”

Some knights surrendered while others had their swords drawn to the end, but the outcome was the same. The adventurers overpowered them with numbers and broke their lines, ruthlessly and blindly venting their anger and despair. Of course, the adventurers knew that the knights were in the same boat as them, and would serve as valuable forces for what was to come. However, they needed someone to take out their emotions on.
Similar scenes were occurring all over the central cavern.
“Ahh! Who are you? Don’t push—!”
A barbarian easily pushed through the crowd from one of the passageways and made a scene. “Hey, knight.” He grabbed the arm of an adventurer beating a knight and spoke. “Killing people...”
“L-Let me go!”
“...Is a problem.”
“What!? These bastards abandoned us. Are you on their side—!”
At that moment, the barbarian slammed his fist into the protesting adventurer’s face.
Punch!
The adventurer collapsed into a heap.
“I said... it’s a problem...” the barbarian gritted out. Everyone immediately went still. There were no more adventurers attacking knights, at least in that particular area.
The situation in the center wasn’t all that different from what I had been expecting, except for one thing.
I didn’t expect so many knights to stay behind.

It was a happy miscalculation. They wouldn’t follow my commands, but at least they were still high-level personnel. Just traveling around this cave with their lives intact would make them good bait for me.
“Mr. Yandel!” A beat later, my teammates appeared through the path I had cleared.
“Oh, can you take care of these guys?”
“Pardon?”
“I mean, protect them so they don’t die.” Entrusting the half-dead knights to my team, I left the passageway and headed to the square in the center.
“Ahh! S-Stop...!”
With every step, screams rang out in all directions. They were mainly from the knights.
Yeah, you guys are human too, huh? Those who are hurting tend to gang up.
“...God damn it!”
Hot tempers erupted. On the other hand, there were also those slumped on the ground a few feet back in a daze of despair. Even anger felt pointless to these people.
“W-We’re all going to die.”
“Cecilia... Sorry, I...”

These people were accepting their deaths as inevitable. Among them were even those wearing the marks of large clans. There were some party units and some people on their own or in duos. Well, even a large clan couldn’t take everyone with them. Even knights got abandoned in situations like these. They would’ve excluded lower-ranking members first because spots were limited.

Occasionally, I heard voices trying to quell the anger. “Please stop...! This changes nothing! They’re in the same boat as us!” This group was divided into two categories: those who appealed thoroughly to emotion and raised their voices to preserve morality and humanity, and those who still held on to hope.
“Have you all gone mad!? At this rate, we’ll all die!”
They set aside their anger and tried to stop these atrocities with logic. In a way, I probably fit into this category. These were the people who would be of most help to me in this situation.
Step.

Eventually, I stopped walking. In front of me was the monument I’d seen many times before—the Last Great Sage. It was the only structure ever erected in the labyrinth to commemorate the achievements of Diplan Groundel Gabrielius.
In honor of his great first step.

There was a hidden element to this monument, something that allowed it to open the Rift on the first floor. However, it would be impossible to enter the Rift and avoid the battle. Not only did we not have a rank-eight mana stone, but even if we did, the last Rift opened a month ago so there was no point. I deliberately avoided opening it the past few months thinking it was more beneficial to explore the fifth floor, so it opened naturally. Well, not that disappointment changed anything.

“Ahem, ahem.” I coughed and cleared my throat. Even still, I wasn’t particularly worried. If barbarians had any prominent trait aside from their outstanding physical stats, it would be their distinctly loud voices. “Stoooooop!”

A thundering cry released in Giantization mode was enough to pierce everyone’s eardrums even in a chaotic situation like this. For a moment, everyone stopped and turned their attention to me. Of course, it didn’t last for long. They looked at me for a moment with eyes that seemed to ask, Who’s that bastard? then stopped caring.
So that isn’t enough for you, huh?

To be honest, I hadn’t had high expectations. Could such a cartoon-like thing happen in real life? “I am Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel!” But whether I was ignored or not, I continued to shout and shout. One rule for being a barbarian was this: if people couldn’t hear your voice, it was because it wasn’t loud enough. “If any fellow countryman knows who I am, do as I say from now on!” I requested support because I wasn’t the only barbarian here.
“Little Balkan, Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“Great warrior!”
“These are the orders of our next chieftain! We must follow them!”
“Behelaaah!”

Starting with Kharon and Ainar, the barbarians scattered throughout the cave shouted on cue. They had been watching me since I first yelled. Although they didn’t know what I was planning, they probably figured they should help out a fellow countryman.
“I repeat! Everyone stop!”
As I shouted, echoes followed.
“I repeat! Everyone stop!”
“I repeat! Everyone stop!”
“I repeat! Everyone stop!”

Again, the crowd paused and turned their attention to me. Maybe if I shouted all alone until my vocal cords gave out they wouldn’t have, but as the same cries kept repeating all around them like a radio broadcast, they couldn’t help being curious.
“Who are you to tell us to stop!?”
“This is all because of these bastards, but you want us to put up with it?!” The amount of negativity was still too great. Many were still beating up knights, blinded by anger.

And so I kept shouting, “I repeat! Everyone stop!” Like a simple, boneheaded barbarian, I just yelled the same thing over and over, intending to keep going until my request was fulfilled. And when my shouts reached something like the tenth verse... “I repeat! Everyone stop!”
“Somebody shut that bastard up!”
The anger that wouldn’t subside no matter how much it was expressed eventually turned on me.
“If you’re going to take the palace’s side, then die!” One of the adventurers even charged at me.
“Protect the future chieftain!” The barbarian warriors who saw this rushed to protect me.
However, I stopped them. “Stop! We must not fight amongst ourselves!”
The simple barbarians halted at my command, but not the adventurers charging at me.
Whip.
One of them was wielding a sword like he was facing down an enemy.
Khak!
I figured this would be the case considering their lower-quality equipment, but it didn’t leave a single scratch on my body. After all, how could normal iron penetrate all this?
“Uh. Um...”

I didn’t try to block at all and just took the blows, unmoving. That was enough to make our difference in skill clear, and he noticed it a beat later. With a newly cool head following all the excitement, the adventurer backed away almost in fear.
Hey, where do you think you’re going?

I grabbed him by the shoulder and pulled him toward me. “Do you want to live?” I asked. He didn’t answer. “I asked if you want to live! If you think you’re going to die anyway, why are you running away!?”
When I shouted threateningly, the adventurer’s face turned pale.
“Tell me, do you want to live!?”
Like a cornered rat biting the cat back, the adventurer couldn’t take the pressure, met my eyes, and shouted, “W-Who would want to die, then?!”

That was the line I wanted to hear. Everyone was already looking this way at the scene this guy had made. I let go of the adventurer’s shoulder. “Then run away. If you think you can survive like that.”

The adventurer, now free, did not turn around to escape. To be exact, he couldn’t. He seemed to have lost all strength in his legs as he slumped to the ground with a dull thud. But apparently, he still had a bit of energy left—enough to shout up at me in anger. “Then what do you want me to do!?”
What else was there to do? I’d said it several times already. I took my eyes off of him, looked around, and shouted again, “I repeat! Everyone stop!”
Life as a barbarian had taught me well that your frustrations could become tenacity someday, as long as you didn’t give up first.

Although it was only for a moment, everyone finally went still. It was kind of a miracle. The only thing the barbarian did was scream. He did not use violence—just shouted relentlessly. At first, he thought it was folly because he thought that no matter how many times the man cried out, this current chaos could not be subdued. Figuring that everyone would regain reason once all the knights were dead, he and his clan members had stepped back from the situation.
“Incredible.”

The one-sided violence against the knights had almost entirely stopped, something brought on by a single barbarian. How was this possible? The exact reason was still unclear. It could only be guessed at. They often said words carried weight, so perhaps that barbarian’s words carried more than usual. Just as one action left a bigger impression than a hundred words, perhaps that foolish single-mindedness of his had sparked people’s curiosity.
Smirk.

Or, maybe they just came to their senses after watching something ridiculous over and over again, like how the vibe of a serious conversation completely changed when someone said something stupid. Of course, this was all just speculation. He did not know what the actual reason everyone had stopped was. It could have been that they just got curious about what this barbarian wanted to say.
Nevertheless, one thing was clear. That barbarian had managed to achieve something he couldn’t. Rank-five adventurer Little Balkan, although inferior in terms of power and faction size, had done it.
“Deputy Commander.”
“Yes, go ahead.”
“No more watching quietly. If anyone attacks a knight nearby, stop them,” the man commanded before walking forward.
“Commander, where are you going?”
“I want to hear what that barbarian caused all this commotion to say. If he’s just a fool, or...”
The deputy commander tilted his head, but the man didn’t elaborate. He could admit it was rather strange himself.
“Everyone stop! He’s right. Just stop for now! Let’s calmly put our heads together!”
Just as he did just now, other bystanders from all around the cavern began to raise their voices and stand up.
Thump!
For some reason, his heart raced. The man stared in the direction of the monument.
“I repeat! Everyone stop!” The barbarian was still shouting, and the people who supported him were shouting back.
“Everyone stop!”

Now, even those who had nothing to do with the barbarian were raising their voices. At the sight, the man was struck by an unwitting thought that everything that was happening now was like a scene from a hero’s story in a folktale he used to read as a child.
“Anyone who causes trouble from now on will be considered the enemy!”
Someone approached me. “I am the commander of Clan Nartel, Melter Fend. If you have a plan to get through this situation, I would like to hear it.”
A woman came up next. “I’m Lacey Nareth of Heindel Church. I am here to thank you for preventing this tragedy.”
The third was a wizard. “I’m a battle mage from Rafdonia. Oh, I wasn’t abandoned but chose to stay behind of my own free will. I didn’t like that commander at all.”

More and more people continued to gather: a priest, a wizard, the head of a clan, the deputy commander, a party leader, and even individuals—those who used to belong to a group but had been abandoned or had voluntarily stayed behind.
“I think you can stop shouting now. Everyone is waiting for you to speak.”
“Tell us. Do you really have a way? Or did you stop the bloodbath out of pity?”
As expected, you couldn’t beat a barbarian who wanted to get something done. Having achieved my objective, I turned off Brainless Repetition mode. “Nice to meet you all. I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
The requirements for a conversation had finally been met.

chapters.title: Chapter 219: Ruler (3)
paragraphs: Before deactivating Giantization, I took a look around at my surroundings, the cavern in the center of the dark zone that had been expanded to the size of a plaza, one more time.
Right now it kind of looks like Gwanghwamun Square.

A group of adventurers easily numbering in the thousands looked my way, all packed like sardines. I wondered exactly how many there were. I didn’t dare count. Including the people who were still out in the passageways due to the crowd in the center, the number would be ridiculous. I realized now that the numbers you heard and read about were different in real life.
If he saw this, would that bastard have made a different decision?
The thought came to mind but I quickly dismissed it. It was pointless to consider and not something to concern myself with right now.
“Behelahhh!”
“...We wanted you to speak. Why are you shouting all of a sudden?”
“I just felt like doing it!”
To be honest, the crowd was making me kind of nervous. Screaming made me feel a bit better. I was a barbarian—there was nothing in this world that I could not do.

“Listen up, everyone!” In a silence that was hard to imagine coming from this many people, everyone’s attention locked on me. It was making me shy, but I stayed stone-faced and continued. “Let’s put our heads together! With so many people, there must be some smart ones here!”
I already had plans in place from A to Z, but I figured it would look suspicious if I revealed all of that in front of this many people.
“Eh?”
“That’s it...?”
Those who had awaited my announcement while holding their breaths stared at me blankly. Some of them also looked disappointed.
“What was I expecting from a barbarian?”

That was the only downside to being a barbarian. You couldn’t come off as an intelligent character and take the lead. Well, without a barbarian, it would have been impossible to stop the fight earlier in the first place.
“Th-then why were you shouting so passionately earlier!?”
“A wise warrior directs his anger to the right place. It is not here that we should be shedding blood .”
“No, I know what you want to say but...”

The adventurers didn’t know what to say. I adhered strictly to playing dumb. After all, I’d achieved my goal of saving the knights for now. No, not only that, I had even succeeded in creating an environment where everyone could gather and talk, leaving a deep impression on people. I’d managed to do everything I had set out to do for phase one.

A middle-aged wizard who had introduced himself as a war correspondent defended me, shifting the tone of the conversation. “He’s not wrong. Everyone has their own role to play. Since this fellow has stopped the meaningless bloodshed and allowed us to gather like this, he has already done more for us than anyone else.”
I guessed I’d left a good impression.
“Roles, huh? That reminds me of a passage from The Book of Monarchy. ‘The role of a ruler is not to fight, but to create the desire to fight.’”
“Haha, I never thought anyone actually read that book. Nice to meet you. Was it Melter Fend, of Clan Nartel?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Oh, do you know me?”
“You are quite famous.”

The two conversed briefly and exchanged friendly glances. That was bad. Not only did we not have time to socialize, but these were adventurers who had already been abandoned by their leaders once. If they saw us bonding all alone, they were sure to get anxious.

“Enough of that, let’s get talking! Does anyone have any information we don’t know about?” I played dumb and intruded on their conversation to make sure it didn’t get off-topic. These guys needed to discuss for my plan to work, and we needed to reach the conclusion I came to earlier, even if it was a bit more cumbersome than me just flat-out saying it.
When no one else came forward, Fend got the ball rolling. “First, we need to determine why the palace’s troops abandoned us.”
“Exactly! They haven’t had any issues holding out so far, so why...?”
This was the biggest enigma here. Those who were angry at being abandoned regained their logic and expressed their confusion. Since many people were gathered, we reached the right answer quickly.
“It’s probably because of the Lord of the Floor.” This came out of the wizard Kyle’s mouth.
“...The Lord of the Floor?”
“But we’ve been dealing with it fine so far!”
“Until now we have. But the commander was probably afraid of the thing that appears after the ninth Lord of the Floor is defeated.”
“...The thing?”

“The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak. Another Lord of the Floor called by that title.” Most were confused at this name they had never heard before, so Kyle provided a brief explanation. “It is because of this monster that adventurers have to report to the guild before planning a raid against the Lord of the First Floor. That’s how much of a calamity it is if it appears.”
“It’s bad enough that even hundreds of knights and large clans cannot defeat it together?”
“No, not that bad. But...” Kyle trailed off and stared into the distance. “We’re not the only ones in the Crystal Cave.”
Noark and Rafdonia were both here, and soon even the Lord of the Abyss, Berzak.
“The commanders made a judgment call. If a battle with Berzak begins, Noark is sure to attack us.”
“Come to think of it, there have been no raids since the first day...”
“Damn it, they planned this from the start!”

It was a kind of war of elimination, a strategy of mutually assured destruction in which Berzak was used to inflict tremendous damage on us. That was why the commander of the Royal Guard had chosen to retreat because high-ranking adventurers and knights were valuable forces that were difficult to replenish in a short period of time. He wanted to protect them, at least, for that goddamn king.
“Wait! Isn’t that a bit odd, then? If they knew something that dangerous would appear, why didn’t they try to go upstairs before then?”
One of the adventurers pointed out a contradiction. This was also something I had thought carefully about, but the answer was really simple.

“I think I can answer that.” This time, it was the priestess from Heindel Church who spoke up. “On the first day we entered the labyrinth, a search party was sent to the second-floor portals. This is information I learned while treating a knight who returned alive.”
“Tell us already!”
“The western portal connecting to Rock Desert is unfortunately no longer usable.”
“No longer usable?”
“The Fallen Scholar... That cursed wizard has apparently destroyed it.”

The Fallen Scholar was a criminal who was rumored to be an executive member of Orcules. When his name was mentioned, the crowd erupted into chaos. As they all shouted and made a commotion, I quietly got my thoughts in order.
West, huh?
So now our odds were one in three? That was valuable information.
“If west is blocked, then we just need to go to another portal!” someone in the crowd shouted, but few even bothered responding. That was because that was common sense.
“The other portals have not been checked, but the knight said that it is highly likely the Fallen Scholar has already gotten to them.”
“Then...”
“Yes, we are completely trapped here.” When the priestess finished speaking, a heavy silence fell. Regardless, however, the discussion continued.
“Those bastards from Noark are really going for it this time.”
“So what are we going to do now?”
“Aside from the monster Berzak, if they find out that our main forces are gone, they will definitely invade.”
The other adventurers were participating in the conversation more actively than before, but they made little progress. There weren’t enough clues to come up with a proper countermeasure.
Whenever that happened, I interrupted and provided hints. “Everyone is thinking too narrowly. A skilled warrior always anticipates the enemy’s next move before acting.”
“These guys spent months planning for this specific day. Surely they prepared for the possibility of us escaping through a portal.”
“...To be honest, I think it would be stranger if they actually expected that.”
Hmm, that was true. Certainly, it was something the average person wouldn’t even consider.
Kyle and a select few did not take my words lightly. “That makes sense. Maybe their plan was to corner us and force us to use portal magic.”
“Yes. Then the real battle may not be this one, but the next. From now on, there won’t be many wizards in the city who can use portal magic anymore.”

“They may be aiming to cause friction between the palace and the adventurers too. If this news gets out to the city, distrust toward the palace will surely hit an all-time high. Well, all of that is assuming we return alive.”
These were all questions I’d had at one time or another, as we were in a situation where any and everything needed to be carefully considered.
“I just don’t know what they’re after...”
Since no one was coming up with an answer, Kyle turned to me. “What do you think? It seems to me that your opinion is important.”
“What do you mean?”
“You pointed out the heart of the issue just now too. I am curious about your warrior’s intuition.”

I pondered this for a moment. Having asked many questions and come up with many theories up to this point, I had already reached a conclusion. Of course, I wasn’t sure if it was the right one. “I think we were the target from the beginning.”
“Oh? Not the knights and large clans?” Kyle chimed in with interest, but not everyone agreed.

“That is nonsense. If they knew the knights were going to use a portal, why would they use this strategy? If the cream of the crop have all escaped already, mutually assured destruction would only hurt them, not help them.” The speaker was a bastard who had been very polite to all the other talented people over the course of the discussion, yet treated me with a particular brand of hostility.
I didn’t know why he was acting like that toward me. Was it because he had no hair? I smirked. “Why do you assume they plan to die with us? They can just go upstairs.”
“Like I said before—”
“They just have to leave one portal active and escape through that.”
This was the conclusion I had reached. After all, wasn’t this world full of efficiency fiends? If I were the leader on the enemy’s side, this was the only plan of action that would make sense.
Because this is the most lucrative for them.

They could burn through over a hundred high-ranking wizards’ portals in one go and then just wait for the next opening to strike. Not only that, but they could also reduce the king’s influence in the city... and more importantly, though the cream of the crop may have been gone, they could wipe out ten thousand adventurers without shedding a single drop of their own blood. With our main forces gone, we would never be able to defeat Berzak in this lifetime.
But I guess it was tough to admit that. The guy was speechless for only a moment before coming to his senses and making an ignorant rebuttal. “It can’t be that simple—”
Or, well, he tried to. Kyle nodded slowly. “So you think the same thing I do.”
The heck, he already figured it out yet still asked me?

That made me a bit uncomfortable but I decided not to comment on it. Geez, this was why I never wanted to stand out too much. Still, it seemed more like he was testing my abilities rather than suspicious of me.
Just then, we heard a commotion outside. I couldn’t hear it because it was far away but it didn’t take long for the news to reach us.
“Commander!”
“What is it?”
“The Noark bastards blocking the passageways have all disappeared!”
Kyle smiled ruefully at me. “It seems you and I were right.”
Now we really needed to hurry.
Now that we’d figured out Noark’s plan, it wasn’t difficult to come up with a countermeasure. Even if it may not have been a perfect solution, it was obvious what we had to do.
“We have to go up to the second floor as well.”
“But do you know through where?”
“We at least know it’s not west. Let’s divide into three teams and search.”
The group would split into three and run to the second-floor portals. Of course, that wasn’t the end of it.
“Even going up will be a problem! Those guys will definitely be there!”
Out of the frying pan and into the fire. More adversity awaited us at the end of our journey, but so what?
“Isn’t that better than dying here? From now on, it’s your own choice what you do,” Kyle said calmly, and at least around us, no one chose to stay.
“Then how will we divide our forces?” one of the adventurers asked to iron out a more detailed strategy.
Before Kyle—who was starting to lead the conversation now—could speak, I jumped in. “I think we should divide ourselves into groups of three hundred.”
“Only three hundred? When we’re already low on manpower?”
Ugh, this asshole again.

“Even if we put more people in each group, this terrain is difficult to fight in properly. This is for the best.” In technical terms, this meant guerrilla warfare. I didn’t bother saying that, but everyone picked up on the implication.
“Hmm, you have a point. A battle is one thing, but more importantly, the bigger the group, the more people will survive. Our numbers will distract the monster.”
“Most of us will die if we come across that monster anyway, so you’re saying you want us to serve as bait to raise each other’s chances of survival.”
It was truly a heartless strategy. However, everyone agreed without dissent. This was the good thing about the adventurer industry. No time was wasted discussing things like approval.
“Then how should we divide up the groups?”
