“Let’s figure that out on our own. I have no intention of working under anyone.”
“Yes, we don’t have time, anyway.”
Once we had a rough plan set up, one of the adventurers—the leader of a small, unknown clan—ended the conversation and stepped away. Chaos promptly ensued.

Some recruited comrades to join them. “This is the Red Light Clan. I’m looking for those who want to get out of this goddamned place with me! Anyone above rank six, whoever you are, and however many!”
Some looked for shelter in the storm. “One of our party members is rank seven. Can’t you let it slide?”
In the middle of all that commotion, the commander of Clan Nartel, Melter Fend, immediately set out to recruit the wizard. “Sir Kyle, I know you are on your own. Would you like to join our clan?”
Welp, I had planned to do that first but seeing how friendly those two had been acting earlier, I didn’t think the man would refuse.
Then I should act fast before everyone is snatched away.

“I’ll be going now. See you on the other side.” After briefly saying goodbye, I turned around, intending to return to my teammates, who were in the crowd somewhere, and gather some talent. It was going to be quite a challenge for a barbarian sucker like me to gather three hundred people, though.
I was about to get moving when the battle mage, Kyle, stopped me. “Wait, what are you going to do? I’m sure you’ll take on the position of leader?”
“Of course.”
“Then take me too.”
Huh?
“Why?”
“I’m just following my gut. I have a feeling that people will come together for you.”
“...You’ll trust your intuition when your life is at stake?”
When I glanced at Fend, who had offered to recruit him first, Kyle grinned. “What, you think a wizard who willingly chose to remain in this chaos is sane?”
Uh, that’s definitely fair.
“All right. I hope we work well together.”
I had a high-ranking wizard now. This was a huge win. Using this, I could recruit better team members.

“Take us with you.” Before I could take a single step, a group of knights approached me. Inspecting the familiar face of the knight at the forefront, I realized it was the same man who had resigned himself to getting beaten up when I first got here. “Four official knights and six apprentice knights. We won’t slow you down.”
What, are you trying to repay the favor? That works for me.
“All right. Follow me.”
The group of knights moved to stand behind me. But before I could take another step, someone called out to me. “Wait.”
It was Fend. What was this? Was it because I stole the wizard from right under his nose? He didn’t look like that kind of sore loser, but...
“Which direction are you going?”
“East.” Since the west was blocked, the east was good. That way, even if our first attempt failed, we could turn north or south depending on the situation.
“Coincidentally, that’s also the direction I’m going in. Why don’t we travel together?”
“I have no intention of working under you.”
“Don’t worry. I will follow your orders.”
“What?” This was also unexpected. He didn’t seem like the type of guy who would work under anyone, either.
What is this? Is there a hidden camera somewhere?
“So, your answer?”
“...If you agree to follow my orders to the letter.”
“Then it’s decided.”
Soon, Fend and his clanmates took up a spot behind me. To be honest, I was dumbfounded. I hadn’t even made any offers yet. How were this many gathered already?
“Behelaaah!”
“Follow the next chieftain!”
Before I could take more than a few steps this time, the barbarians all ran up and fell into step behind me. Well, that was to be expected.
“Mister!”
“Erwen? Where is your clan?”
“My sister thinks it will be safer this way! Will you take the two of us too?”
“Of course.”
The elf sisters, who had apparently been watching things unfold from somewhere nearby, also joined in. And they weren’t the only ones.
“If it’s all right, I’d like to travel with you,” said the leader of a rank-four party that was active on the sixth floor.
A priestess who had stayed behind to save as many people as possible said, “I believe you’ll be able to save the most lives.”
“Haha, in times like these, steadfast people like you are the most reliable people out there. Take us with you too.” Even a dwarven clan that was quite famous in the city spoke up.
All I was doing was walking, but numerous people came up to me and asked to go with me.
Kyle gave me a big grin. “Didn’t I tell you? I knew people would gather around you. A wizard’s intuition is usually right.”

chapters.title: Chapter 220: Ruler (4)
paragraphs: Team Apple Narak’s wizard, Raven, was standing with the rest of her teammates in a nearby passageway. The reason for this was simple. When the assault against the knights stopped, she had tried to get to her team’s leader, but thanks to the thousands of people packed so tightly together, she couldn’t even think to get through the crowd.

“Miss Ainar, I hope you can help me. I can’t see well from here.” As someone far below the average height even for women at 4′9″, Raven sat atop Ainar’s shoulders and watched the events in the center of the square unfold. Although it was too far to hear, that was no problem. That could be fixed with magic.
“What arrre they saying?”

“It’s almost over. I think they’re agreeing to break off into groups of three hundred and pave the way.” Raven relayed what was happening in the center to her teammates in real time. Many other teams here were doing the same. They each had at least one person with magic or enhanced hearing.
“And Bjorrrn? What’s Bjorn saying?”
“Ah, well... I think he’s trying to get over here before he does anything else. Oh, a wizard started talking to him. I think Mr. Yandel is trying to form a team.”
“Oh, I see...” Missha nodded worriedly at Raven’s words. Raven could understand why.
“We are going north!”
“Is there anyone who wants to come with me?”

Numerous clans and teams were already crying out for comrades. That included famous and well-known adventurers, and even leaders of clans with great reputations. Three of those groups had already formed an alliance as well.

However, Raven tried to stay upbeat. “What are you all worried about? You all know Mr. Yandel is second to none when it comes to fame. Even if it takes some time, we’ll be able to find three hundred people.”
Her behavior was definitely out of character. Normally, she analyzed the situation with cold logic and only ever told the truth.
Mr. Yandel would have done something like this, though.
She had learned something from following that barbarian around. A leader could not always act as they pleased.
“Huh?” Raven suddenly, involuntarily froze.
“What’s wrrrong? Did something else happen?”
“The wizard just said he wants to follow Mr. Yandel.”
“Wow, really? You said he’s a rrreally great wizard, right?”
“Yes, but...” Raven was stunned. This was good news, but she felt uneasy not knowing the reason behind his decision.
Someone like that could definitely join an even better group...
Why did a wizard like him want to join them? She couldn’t figure it out. This time she decided to be honest with her teammates and ask their opinions.
“Hmm, that wizard said that people will come together for Yandel? I think I know what he means.”
“You do?”
“Yandel... that guy is special. You know that too, Raven.”
“I do?” Raven said, confused.
In response, Ainar let out a loud shout. “Bjorn, son of Yandel is a great warrior!”

A Great Warrior... For some reason, hearing that made her recall the events of the Bloody Citadel. Fewer than ten barbarians had officially received that title from the king since ancient times. But back then, as she watched that two-month-old barbarian adventurer sleep like the dead after finishing all his hard work, she had had the thought that that title might indeed be his one day.
“Isn’t that why you joined his team too?”
“...That’s right.” Raven nodded readily. Urikfried wasn’t wrong. If she hadn’t sensed anything special about that barbarian, she wouldn’t have joined this party in the first place.
“He has a strange ability to pull people in.”
As the conversation with her team ended, Raven turned around to look toward Yandel again. It hadn’t been too long since she’d last checked on him, and yet...
“If it’s all right, I’d like to travel with you.”
“I believe you’ll be able to save the most lives.”
“Haha, in times like these, steadfast people like you are the most reliable people out there. Take us with you too.”

Before she knew it, numerous adventurers were following behind him as he walked. But was it because of what Urikfried said? The sight no longer seemed strange to her, and she did not doubt the intentions of the wizard who had been the first to tag along.
“It wasn’t... just me.”
There were some people in this world whose backs just made you want to follow them.
“Didn’t I tell you? I knew people would gather around you. A wizard’s intuition is usually right.”
Most of them left great footprints behind.

I had expected it to take at least an hour or two. Even if the cream of the crop had escaped through the portal, there were still adventurers here who were more impressive than me. I thought that I would have to do my best to compete with them to build my troops up to the level I wanted.
It’s probably because of this man.

The wizard Kyle possessed both knowledge and power, and the charisma of a natural leader. The tides turned when he joined me. Then, rank-three adventurer Melter Fend brought his entire clan under my command and this created a buzz. It was like how people started hoarding certain products when nonsensical rumors went around that there would be a shortage. Even if they didn’t think of doing so themselves, they started to think that maybe they should when others started to do it.
“Behelaaah!”
“The hope of the barbarians!”
“Follow the great warrior!”
I ignored the cries of the fired-up barbarians and pushed forward. I was experiencing something I’d never felt before.
“Please take us with you! We won’t slow you down!”

Was this how a superstar felt when he arrived at an airport? Every time I took a step, a new party, clan, or even individuals approached and asked me for my approval. So I raised the bar for one simple reason. According to the basic economic principle of supply and demand, I was now the one with the power in this exchange.
“Tell me your role and rank.”
“Rank five. I’m alone now, but I was once my team’s protector.” A protector was the warrior who stood at the forefront. Rank five should be skilled enough as well.
“Your name?”
“Pell Akabird.”
Pass.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel. Come with me.” As I moved, I was strict about only choosing the people I needed.
Almost all the priests left through the portal, so I don’t see any.
That was too bad, but it couldn’t be helped. I just had to fill up the slots with as many warriors and wizards as possible. Oh, and a knight would be even better.
From time to time, I ran into people I was acquainted with. “Carls Erimor.”
“Is there space for me and my colleagues, perhaps? Three apprentice knights and one official knight.”
“To think you were abandoned too.”
“I suppose apprentice knights aren’t that high on the food chain.”

Erimor, a knight of Baron Martoin’s whom I had met at the count’s home, had a good personality and was once an adventurer, so he should be able to pull his own weight. Plus, there was a knight who could use an aura with him too.
“Follow me.”
“Thanks.”

One step, then another. Each time I stepped forward, the number behind me grew. Just the barbarians who decided to follow me alone were enough to exceed our quota of three hundred, but I continued to bring more people into the fold.
We’ll just need to divide ourselves into groups of three hundred if we have to.
If we traveled along the same route, we could help each other out in an emergency. I hadn’t expected to reach a number where that was actually possible, though.
Okay, this is going well.
I continued to advance like that and spotted a familiar face even in this crowd of people.
“Takelan.”

The man was standing alone. He didn’t seek out a team like last time, nor did he show any desire to create one. Perhaps he had given up on everything. When our eyes met, he avoided my gaze. It was clear he wanted me to pass him by, but I was a barbarian who had to do what I wanted to do.
So I approached him and said, “Follow me.” I didn’t know why I did it. The words just came out of me. “Come on, if you want to live.”
“You think... I want to live?” he muttered like he couldn’t believe what he was hearing. “Lena was my wife.” So she was. “Why should I live?”
“Because someone needs to deliver the news,” I replied.

Those were just empty words. Even at that last moment before ending their own life, everyone yearned for survival in a deep, dark corner of their heart. Although Takelan had lost all his teammates, he had followed us until the bitter end. Was there really a reason for that? Well, I wasn’t sure.
“Yes, I forgot about that...”
However, when they had a reason, it was easier for people to pick themselves back up and move forward.
“If you’ve come back to your senses, come with me.”
“...Why are you helping me like this? You won’t need me now.”
I gave my honest, selfish answer. “If you survive, that’ll ease my mind at least a little bit.”
Using others to relieve my feelings of guilt; in a way, I was just like the commander of the Third Royal Guard. The only difference was that I was well aware of how cowardly I was.
I didn’t know what he thought about that statement, but after that, Takelan stepped behind me and joined our team.
That took longer than I intended.
I continued to lead the group. Before long, I spotted one of my teammates near a passageway. “Bjorn!”
As soon as I was within range, Missha and Ainar greeted me enthusiastically. I pushed them aside and spoke to Raven. “Raven, did anything happen here?”
“Good. Did you hear what we said inside?”
“Yes, I heard...”
Okay, so I wouldn’t have to repeat all of that. “But why do you keep averting your eyes?”
“What? I’m not doing that. See, look!”
Hmm, is that so?
For some weird reason, it seemed like she was uncomfortable. Oh, was it because of all the people gathered behind me? Well, even I had to admit Barbarian Commander Mode was sick.
My teasing brought her back to her normal self. “Anyway, with this many people... we can probably just figure out the numbers and leave right away. You did a good job. We were running out of time.”
Running out of time. She wasn’t wrong. But before that, there was just one thing I had left to do—something that might be the most critical thing for surviving this crisis.
Kyle Pevrosk, a rank-three battle mage known as the Iron Sorcerer, let out a hearty laugh as he observed his new leader.
I was wondering what he was doing...
The more he watched him, the stranger this man became. After gathering all these people, the first thing he made them do was introduce themselves.
“Your name?” He approached each person and asked for their name, then after hearing it, shook hands briefly. “Nice to meet you. I’m Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
Some even asked the barbarian, “Why are you asking for names when there is no time?”
The answer they got in return was truly a spectacle. “There are still many people whose names I don’t know.”
“But why does that—”
“It is important to me. So don’t interrupt me.”

The barbarian continued to ask everyone for their names like he was conducting some kind of sacred ceremony. Most considered the exercise pointless. The same went for Melter Fend, the head of Clan Nartel, who had his own years of experience and insight under his belt.
“...Could there be some kind of a hidden meaning?”
Kyle laughed at that question. “Melter Fend, why did you decide to follow him?”
“That’s...” Fend hesitated before opening his mouth. “To be honest, I figured there was a reason why you chose him, Sir Kyle.”
“Yes, that can be one of your reasons. But that can’t be the only one. You have people you’re responsible for.”
“...You know about what happened?”
“I heard about it in passing. You refused the commander of the Royal Guard, saying you couldn’t leave behind your fellow clan members, right?”
“This is kind of embarrassing.”
“Nothing to be embarrassed about. I think it’s a sign of loyalty. But to rally those members simply to blindly follow the decisions of another... Even I can’t accept reasoning like that.”

Fend laughed sheepishly, then chose his words more carefully this time. “This might sound strange, but I got the feeling that somehow, standing behind that man might be the safest thing I could do...”
“Followed your intuition, huh?”
“It’s quite common in this industry. After all, this is a place where you die without luck.”
“I am not criticizing you. I believe the other people here aren’t all that different from you.”
“Excuse me?” Fend tilted his head, but Kyle’s next statement was equally cryptic.
“Just watch. Whether this was all pointless or not, we’ll soon find out.”
With that, the two observed the barbarian without much conversation. He was still taking turns asking for names one by one.
“...Hans?”
“No, Hanvus.”
“Oh, is that so? Nice to meet you! It’ll be short, but I hope we work well together.”
“I should be saying that to you!”
It was the process of asking names and exchanging brief greetings, that was all, but something was very different than it had been at the beginning.
“Nice to meet you, Teterudra. That axe is nice.”
“Haha, that’s the highest compliment you can pay a dwarf.”
“Please take care of the rear later.”
“Don’t worry about a thing.”
The tension loosened more and more. In the face of a battle where their survival was entirely up in the air, the thorns around these people’s hearts went slack.
“Wait, why are you skipping me?”
“Didn’t I already ask you when we first met? Davers, right?”
“Ha, you remember all of that?”
“We’re comrades who have to fight together.”
Only then did Fend realize what had caused this change. That barbarian was easily earning the trust of all these people just by asking their names.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel. Are you really going to hear out the names of all these people?”
“Is there a problem?”
“Just as I thought, you’re a stubborn guy. I am Humble Albertine. Let’s grab a drink if we get out of here.”
“Humble Albertine, I’ll remember it.”
“I can’t miss out on an opportunity like that. Me too! Let me join!”
Not to mention this wasn’t just building up trust between the two people speaking. These brief exchanges were heard by the people around them too.
“We’re... no longer strangers.”

Fend was genuinely astonished. Although they had to work as a group for now, these people had all been strangers until moments ago, but now they knew each other’s names and faces. Just by hearing these short conversations, they could understand to some extent what kind of people the others were too based on the way each person connected with that barbarian. And, like a spider’s web, these snippets tangled together and intertwined to form a bond.
“Bjorn Yandel, he... did he really plan all this...?”
“No, I don’t think so.”
“But it wouldn’t make sense otherwise.”
“What wouldn’t?”
“...People don’t normally do things like this without a reason.”

Kyle chuckled. Certainly, that was usually the case—the things this barbarian was doing here would normally result in a completely different outcome. “Don’t try to apply logic here. If you’ve studied history, you should know. Every era is bound to have people like him.”
Taking action ordinary people couldn’t understand and getting results was why these people were considered great.

The long introductions were over. The moment the group of one thousand was split into three under Kyle’s direction, I let out a roar containing all my respect for the protection my ancestral gods provided me. “Behelaaah!”
“Haha... My friend, why did you shout this time? The other barbarians are following you already.”
Oh, sorry about that, but... I can’t help it. To think there wasn’t a single Hans among all these people.
Was this not a miracle from the ancestors themselves?

chapters.title: Chapter 221: Like Fireworks (1)
paragraphs: One rank-three adventurer, nine rank-four adventurers, fourteen official knights who could use auras, and one rank-three wizard—these were the people who would act as the core of this plan. And considering the danger ahead of us, even these numbers couldn’t exactly guarantee our safety.
Still, it’s close to a miracle that this many have gathered in one place to begin with.

The cream of the crop had already escaped through a portal, so logically there was a shortage of top-notch personnel. How many people would willingly throw away their ticket to safety and stay behind? Realistically, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say this was all of them.
Not bad.

With that thought in mind, I glanced to the side. A black-haired Caucasian man in his forties and wearing a robe was standing there. This was the person I was most suspicious of: Kyle Pevrosk, a rank-three battle mage affiliated with the palace. When I learned his rank, I was really surprised. In this industry, it was customary for a wizard’s rank to be treated as one higher than an adventurer’s. Of course, this wasn’t just out of courtesy for the wizard. The fact was that Raven was only rank six, but she did the most work in the team after me. It would be accurate to say that the criteria for counting our ranks was different. But rank three?
A rank-two adventurer is in actuality the second strongest.
To be honest, I didn’t know why that shitty commander had left this man behind. A rank-three wizard was someone you had to take with you no matter how much he refused.
Or was it because of his status that even the commander couldn’t force him? Hmm, that could very well be the case.
For the palace, the death of this one man would be more of a loss than the deaths of thousands of adventurers. The commander probably tried to take him somehow but was unable to.
Like I thought, it must be a grudge.
Before departing, I had asked Kyle why he stayed behind. “I can’t run while he’s here,” he had replied coldly, his voice sharp. “This is the first opportunity I’ve had in a long time.”
Unfortunately, Kyle didn’t tell me who “he” was, but it hadn’t been the right time to dig into it. Plus, whatever his motive was, it worked out in my favor. So I immediately kicked off our journey.
Now, in the present, I was running at the forefront of hundreds of people.
Rattle, rattle.

Our formation was simple. After splitting over a thousand adventurers into three groups, I had them follow behind at certain distances. Our forces were distributed appropriately, but the core team I mentioned earlier was placed in the group at the forefront. There was no resistance from the rear group. They, too, had accepted that if the monster emerged, the ones clearing the way through all those dangers would be them.

Aside from the sound of running, there was a tense, focused silence. Normally I would have exchanged a few words with my teammates to calm my nerves, but that was impossible right now. The members of my party were somewhere else.
Rattle, rattle.

Behind me were only warriors and knights, heavily armed just like me. We had only one mission: when something happened, clear the way. This was, of course, the most dangerous position, so I sent my teammates back. This situation was different from the one we were in the other day in many ways. Because there were more people now, the rear was much safer.

As I was running like that, I heard a voice from the message stone hanging on my waist. “Anything strange up there?” It was Kyle, who was about seventy yards behind me. For reference, my party was all placed near him.

“No.” Even as I responded, I felt awkward. This kind of communication was essential considering so many people were being forced to move through a wide terrain together, but I’d never used it before since I usually traveled in a party. Perhaps I’d get used to this once I made a clan.
“All right, I’ll send the message to the back. Let me know straight away if anything goes wrong. It’s going to start soon.”
“I will.”

I ended the transmission and stared straight ahead. The thick fog from a few days ago was completely gone and there was no sign of a single adventurer from Noark. Only bloodstains and corpses served as a testament to the past few days.
Is it starting soon?

As more time passed, my heart began to pound erratically. That was a given. It had already been over thirty minutes since the ninth Lord of the Floor had appeared and the crystals on the cave walls began to emit their red light.
“This way.”

Suddenly, the road forked off and I turned right. At the same time, one of the warriors following me left a mark on the wall. This was also the reason why I had taken the lead—to have someone on the frontline with scout abilities.

“Halt.” My mind went blank and I stopped everyone. The crystals that were glowing bright red were losing light and beginning to fade to black. About three seconds after that, the entire cave was plunged into darkness.
Whoosh.
I lit the torch I had prepared and said, “Everyone, be on guard from now on.”

For some reason, I was reminded of a quote from Einstein: “I know not with what weapons World War III will be fought, but World War IV will be fought with sticks and stones.” Of course, this quote didn’t exactly sum up my current situation, but one thing was clear.
[Special Condition – Nine Horrors has been fulfilled. The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, has begun to wander the floor.]
It was time to get back to the basics.

[Field Effect – Abyssal Fog has activated. All active skills have been disabled. Mana Efficiency has been reduced to 25%. Any monsters exposed to the Fog of the Abyss will evolve into superior beings.]
Click.

I inserted my torch into the groove of my helmet, entering Barbarian Candle Mode. I hadn’t used this mode in a while, but it wasn’t particularly embarrassing, because the other warriors all did the same.
“Haha, I don’t know when I last used a torch.”
“Same here.”

Everyone put their torches on their helmets and vision was restored. Then, the Black Fog surrounding us became clearer. It was like the darkness that appeared starting from the second floor of the labyrinth—a darkness that ate up all light.
Visibility is about two yards.

It was a shorter distance than expected. True, in the game I had always been accompanied by several Great Sorcerers to take down Berzak. Because it was only ever summoned after careful planning, I had never ended up in a situation like this.
“We were told this would happen, but it seems more dangerous than I thought.”

The skilled warriors grew tense. That was how important sight was in battle. For example, in the United States, twenty-one feet was considered the ideal distance when confronting an offender. Anything closer than that and it was hard to fend off a criminal coming at you with a knife. The same went for a gun. Twenty-one feet was the distance required to aim and pull the trigger at a human sprinting at you at full speed. But two yards...
As I stopped momentarily to prepare myself, Kyle’s voice came through the message stone. “We have to move quickly,” he urged.
“I was fixing the torch. We will depart now.”
I notified the warriors and started walking again, shielding my upper body.
Rattle, rattle.

I increased my walking speed little by little. This was one of the reasons why our current situation was a pain in the ass and why the frontline was composed of sturdy warriors and knights. To think we had to run while only seeing two yards ahead of us...
“Behelaaah!”
In an attempt to shake off my fear, I roared and took off. How long would it take us to arrive at our destination if we walked this slow? Yeah, we already knew things were dangerous, right?
“L-Let’s go!”
When I leaped into the darkness first, the warriors gathered their courage and followed suit. Well, it’d be easier for them since I was lighting the way.
“Kyaaah!” A beast howled in the darkness and charged at me. It was too big to be from the first floor. Well, that also had to do with the fact that I was not using Giantization like I usually did.
Punch!
I cuffed the beast’s jaw with my shield. Immediately, the warrior to my right slashed its neck with a double-edged axe.
Khak!

It dug into the hide, but the blade got caught in the bone. That left a bitter taste in my mouth. The dwarf who just swung the axe was a rank-four warrior, and not a tank but a close-range damage dealer. Yet a one-shot-kill was impossible even for him.
“Kyaaah!” The beast charged toward us again despite the deep cut in its neck. I smacked its head with my mace.
Smack!
It probably wouldn’t die with that, either, since I hadn’t used my one and only attack skill, Swing. Well, I couldn’t use it, to be precise.
[All active skills have been disabled.]
Active skills were sealed in Fog of the Abyss. The Corpse Golem’s Acid Fluid was still there, but I couldn’t use Flesh Explosion. That was why I couldn’t use Giantization right now, either.
It really feels like I’m back in the old days.

A strange sense of loss filled me inside and out. It reminded me of the early days when I had nothing. That was probably why the other warriors were so afraid of what was beyond the darkness too, because one of their greatest weapons was gone.
“What are you all doing!? Follow me!”

However, the base stats left by our essences remained the same. We could use our passives and we also had equipment we’d customized with hard-earned cash. We couldn’t use the equipment’s abilities or scrolls, but permanent features such as the 50 percent Shock Reduction provided by Mark of the Guard Corps were still active.
“Leave the ones still alive to the next group!”
We ignored the monster and plunged into the darkness again, knowing that if we tried to kill each one, we’d never get there on time.
“Kyaaah!”
Woof! Woof!

Every few steps, beasts appeared in groups. They were about half as big as lions, but looked similar to the Blade Wolves that commonly appeared in the eastern district of the first floor. However, the difference in strength was like heaven and earth.
[You have defeated the Abyssal Blade Wolf. EXP +5]

We had to clear the way by defeating rank-five monsters with the same difficulty rating as Trolls without any active skills. That was also why I mainly recruited warriors. Sorcerers, summoners, necromancers, and other extremely skill-dependent characters were inevitably useless in this situation. On the other hand, most warriors tended to have high base stats.
“Agh, my arm...!”
“Priest, heal them quickly!”

Even so, the more we cleared the way, the more casualties accrued. Just like how my fighting power plummeted drastically after losing Giantization, the other adventurers were not used to fighting in this state. The Abyssal Blade Wolves also played a role.
[The Abyssal Blade Wolf has cast Inner Madness.]

Inner Madness was an active skill given to Blade Wolves that evolved through Fog of the Abyss. The effect was simple. All of the user’s defense-related stats disappeared, but bonuses were added to stats related to attacks such as Cutting Power, Destructive Power, and Penetrating Power.
“Kyaaah!”
Shaking off my thoughts, I quickly covered my face with the shield.
Kak-kak-kak!
There was a grinding sound on the other side of the shield as I blocked the claws. However, I was more concerned for my body than the repair costs.
This is the strength of grade-four moonstone, huh? Even I’d have a tough time surviving this without a weapon.
It was only natural for casualties to continue to pile up. These claws were able to tear through grade-two metal-like paper.
Whew, if an essence comes out, I’m eating it right away.

Normally this event opened in the very end stage of the game so the Abyssal Blade Wolf essence had never been all that attractive to me, but right now, things were different. First, not only were the base stats high for rank five, but its skills were pretty good too. One of these skills could temporarily transform me from an extreme tank to an extreme damage dealer. It was an unusable skill in this situation, though.
Still, their base stats are high, at least.
Any stat increase would be of great help. An essence could be erased at the temple later. One million stones didn’t even feel that expensive to me now.
“Behelaaah!”
Hoping it would improve morale, I let out a shout. I wasn’t the only one doing this either. Everyone was calling out to whatever it was they believed in to fight through their fear.
“For Rafdonia!” Loyal knights cried out unwaveringly to the palace that had abandoned them.
“Ailee!” Some called their spouses’ names.
“May the stars be my guide!” Some asked for help from their gods.

After a long while, I heard Kyle’s voice come through the message stone. “It’s time to change shifts.” The warriors and knights who were conserving their stamina in the backline switched with those in the front.
“...Will you be all right?” the dwarven warrior who had been fighting diligently by my side asked with concern.
Of course, if I was being honest, I wanted to take a break too. “Someone needs to lead the way.”
“You can call another scout for that.”

“Another scout...” I chuckled. Most scouts weren’t all that great in combat. To call someone like that up here, where even warriors and knights were liable to end up with tears in their flesh and their intestines spilling out of them? “Don’t worry. I’m fine.”
“...I will be back soon.”
Geez, so much loyalty for such a short battle. “I’ll be waiting.”
When the dwarven warrior stepped back as well, new faces filled the spaces behind me and next to me. They didn’t feel like strangers, since we’d already introduced ourselves before departing.
“Albertine, Davers, Karkin, nice to see you. I’ll leave my flank to you guys.”
“Haha, you already look like a mess.”
“Why don’t you rest in the back? We will clear the way from now on.” The warriors were considerate of my tattered equipment and still-dripping blood.
“I can still take it. I’ll let you know if I change my mind later.”
“That’s absurd.”
“Well, it’s because he’s like that that this many people are gathered here.”
“Damn it, these guys don’t even want to give us time to say hello, huh?”
Before we could finish our short chat, we had to hurriedly get moving again when a beast appeared in front of us.
“They’re different from the average Blade Wolf, so be careful.”
“We know.”
“More than enough have been popping out of the side roads.”
“Not as much as here, but it was fierce back there too. Many have died already.”
“Died...?”
“There are no priests back there.”
I see.
The priests had all been placed on the frontlines, but I didn’t think that made it safer here. No matter what, there would be fallout.
Their divine power will run out eventually.

To conserve as much divine power as possible, I ordered the injured to be sent to the back to be given potions, but even that was just prolonging the issue. Once we hit the tipping point, this place would turn into an even worse hell.
Missha...
I shook my head. I was worried about my teammates in the rear, but if something had happened, they would have contacted me through a message stone by now.
I should just focus on what I need to do.

I cleared my mind and hefted my shield onto my shoulder. If necessary, I wielded my mace. At times I cried out, and sometimes I even lost my balance and fell to the ground before quickly rolling back onto my feet.
Punch! Punch! Slice! Kwaaang!
The beasts spewed black blood from the blows of blunt weapons, swords, or even the auras of knights. Their bodily fluids continued to cover my body. More time passed in a haze.
Huff, huff.

Warriors who had invested all their stats in Physique were breathing harshly and groaning. That was our struggle. Even I, who prided myself on having experienced all kinds of chaos, was having a hard time remaining lucid. Was that why? When I came to my senses, another warrior was standing in the position to my left. Since when?
“Davers, when did Albertine head back?” The man didn’t answer. “Is he dead?”
“Yes.”
...I see. We promised to have a drink later.
“Behelaaah!”

Like pouring fuel on a fire, I burned even these fleeting emotions and pushed forward. I also ordered the priests to cast heals on everyone but me. Since I had Pain Resistance, I only needed a potion.
Smirk.

No, to be honest, I didn’t even know anymore. Was my judgment clouded after so much fighting? Or was it because I was surrounded by warriors that the barbarian instincts buried in this body were waking up? Or was it because we knew each other by name? I didn’t know. Maybe it was because I’d seen too many deaths.

To some, I was as discardable as a bad hand in poker. And to me, others were just as discardable. Up until a few days ago, that was an inarguable fact. I neither resented it nor thought it unreasonable. That was how the world worked, and I chose to conform to it.
Thump!
What was this feeling? This wasn’t who I was. But...
Thump!
A hot heart and head, the burn of coursing blood, the stickiness of my skin...
Thump!
Yeah, maybe it was only natural that I wasn’t in my right mind right now.
“Ahhhhhh!”
I stopped searching for a reason. I didn’t know why, but each time someone behind me died, I felt something stir in my heart. It was a desire I’d never felt before.
Thump!
Myself, my teammates, and the countless people behind me, I wanted to get them all back home alive...
[Your HP has fallen below 20%. All of your Resistance and Resilience stats have maxed out due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]
...Even if I had to burn everything I had to do it.

chapters.title: Chapter 222: Like Fireworks (2)
paragraphs: The old me hadn’t been like this. So what kind of person had I been?

Little Hansu Lee, who spent most of his days in the hospital, had been an ordinary kid. He admired heroes and believed he would be someone special one day. However, the kid had learned as he grew up that dreams were just dreams. In the end, the ones who had the last laugh were the people who lived their lives rationally.
Missha, Ainar, Raven, Mr. Bear.
I solidified my top priority in my mind. No matter what happened, I would get them back home alive.
Clang!
Even as I made that resolution, I blocked the claws of the beast aiming at one of my comrades with my shield.
“Are you all right?”
“A-Ah! Thanks...”

I did not want to let go of this burning desire to save every person I could who was coursing through me. My head and heart felt hot, as hot as the breath I was exhaling right now. Had I always been such a hot-blooded person?
“Davers, if you’re tired, go back and rest.”
“...That won’t happen. Not until you rest.”
Why were all warriors such fools? In moments like these, I had the fleeting thought that I shouldn’t have asked their names, but at the same time, I was glad I did.

With that, I let go of all doubt and all regrets. As if I had really become a character in a game, I focused on just one thing. A Shield Barbarian was designed to protect his comrades, and Bjorn Yandel had followed that character build to a T. What was the thing that he did best? No, what was it that he had to do? I already knew the answer.
[Your body is rapidly regenerating due to Recovery (Greater)‘s effects.]

I narrowly maintained my tattered state through just potions. Even while knowing I’d probably be in much better shape if I received a priest’s care, I did not request healing instead. The lower my HP was, the higher the defense stat of Orc Hero’s passive skill rose.
“Behelaaah!”
The more I burned through my life force, the stronger I got. Then I could save more people, and those people who survived would help us overcome any remaining hurdles.
“Almost there!”
This was a reasonable choice. Let’s trust that and move forward.

About nine hours had passed since we left the center of the map. The first two hours were spent sprinting like we were doing a speed run, and the remaining seven were spent clearing the way through the Fog of the Abyss. We’d taken a lot of damage. There were horrors we’d faced that were difficult to summarize in just a few sentences.
“We’re here.”
Eventually, we reached our first destination.
“How is it, is the portal open?” asked Kyle.
I swallowed a groan and made sure my voice was calm as I answered, “No, the portal has been destroyed.”
The place we arrived at past countless corpses and puddles of blood was in ruins. In the spot where the headstone and opened portal should have been was absolutely nothing.
Squeeze.

Truly, it had been a long time since irrational sentiment had fueled my anger. So many warriors had died. Each of those people had had a family, and each was a precious life that should not have been discarded.
“So this was a pointless trip... Snap out of it. There are still two portals left. You need to decide where to go.”
Forcibly pushing back the tide of emotion, I cooled my head as much as possible and got to thinking. North or south?
“Make the decision as quickly as you can.”
I didn’t even have the luxury to take my time and think it through. Even at this moment, a battle was being fought.
“Yandel, don’t feel pressured. How can you choose something like that? It’s just luck.”
“Haha, a warrior always makes decisions with the heart, not the head!”
“Whatever choice you make, we will follow you.”
“And even if it’s the wrong choice, no one could blame you. If anyone does, I’ll crack their skull open with my axe.”
The warriors who’d teetered on the brink of death with me several times in that short time spoke words of comfort. These were fascinating people. How could they laugh while looking like that?
Smirk.
I closed my eyes.
We only have one shot now.
Realistically, it was impossible to check all three portals. Based on the time we had, we had determined that we had up to two opportunities and set east as our first destination.
There were several reasons for this:
1. If we chose east, we could then choose between north and south if the first portal was a bust. It was also possible to change routes during the expedition based on new information.
2. The Abyssal Blade Wolves weren’t as tricky as other monsters, making this the path that would deal us the least amount of damage.

3. In the Den of Beasts, it would be difficult for Noark to set up a blockade. If a battle broke out, we determined this area would be best for us since we could use the simple strategy of using the walls to protect us on three sides, hold out until the very end of the seventh day, and then head down to the first floor.
...God damn it.
As I sifted through my thoughts, I realized something.
It was the wrong choice from the start.
From my point of view, it made sense to choose the east. But what about from the point of view of the other side?
I was too quick to choose.
I made plans to head in the direction that I favored because if that succeeded, it would have been best for me. I acted with the best-case scenario in mind. Anyone else would have done the same.
What direction would those bastards have chosen?
I asked myself again: which portal was the most advantageous for Noark? The answer quickly came to me.
North.
No matter how I thought about it, there was no better option than the Goblin Forest. There were three reasons for this:
1. The Abyssal Goblins were the trickiest out of the four monsters on the first floor. If we wanted to take that portal, many sacrifices would follow.
2. Since there was nothing in the terrain that could act as walls up there, it would be possible for them to set up a blockade. They’d have the advantage in combat.

3. Above all, the Goblin Forest was the shortest distance from the third floor. This was the most important part. These guys had stopped adventuring for six months, which meant they would be suffering from food shortages. They would’ve planned to mine mana stones after they pulled this whole operation off. After all, everyone in this world was obsessed with efficiency.
Stupid bastard.

I already knew about their food crisis, which was why I assumed there wouldn’t be many troops waiting in front of the second floor. That was what I had placed my faith in for this plan. However, I had failed to make the connection to the Goblin Forest even though I had run all those simulations in my head.
One of three options? No, I just wanted it to be the easiest one.
I cursed my own foolishness. But instead of blaming myself even more, I grabbed the message stone.
Squeeze.
Now was not the time to retreat into myself and crumble. Blood had already been spilled, so what was important now was what we did next.
“We are going north.”
When I announced my decision through the message stone, I heard Kyle’s voice. “Goblin Forest, huh?”
“Is there something you want to say?”
“No. In fact, if you couldn’t choose, I was going to recommend that first. The thought only occurred to me now, but I’m suspicious of that direction.”
So this guy had the same thought as me. If only I had realized it sooner. Me or this man.
Enough complaining.
I started moving, leading the group that had followed me here. “Get ready. We’re leaving again.” Our destination was the Goblin Forest in the north.
“Ha, that ends our break.”
“Let’s go. We can rest once we’re out of here.”
Instead of breaking formation and heading back the way we came, I turned to take a detour.
“Grrr...!”
“Kyaaah!”
Beasts appeared without fail as soon as we left the portal’s vicinity. Fighting more bloody battles with these bastards, we cleared the path for the rest. And a long while later...
“Grk, grrk!”
Slowly, Abyssal Goblins began to appear. That meant we had traveled a considerable distance from the eastern district where the Blade Wolves spawned.
“Grrk.”
It was as small as usual, but a goblin with ominously black skin stared back at me.
“Kreuk, kreuk!” The bastard was laughing, just like the first time I fell into this cave.
“Prepare for battle!”
From now on, we would walk the hard road.
Goblins were rank-nine monsters, nothing special. You just had to be careful of their traps, and even those traps were nullified with a pair of proper boots.
[You have defeated the Abyssal Goblin. EXP +5]
However, rank-five goblins with “Abyssal” in their names were different. These sons of bitches turned into trickier monsters than even Trolls.
[The Abyssal Goblin has cast Random Trap.]
The effects of Random Trap were simple.
Click.
When stepped on, a random skill below rank five was cast on the target. Oh, for reference, buffs were excluded. You only ever got hit with attack and curse-type skills.
Whooosh!

The moment a trap activation sounded, a nearby warrior’s body was swallowed up in flames. I knew what it was as soon as I saw it: Extermination. Among the rank-five skills, this was the one that dealt the greatest amount of single-target damage.
“God damn it! Priest! Priest, priest!”
The priest being called provided heals as soon as the flames appeared, but it was useless.
Slump.
The warrior who had been clearing the way on the frontlines for over two hours collapsed in a charred heap, a truly pointless death. That was the damned thing about Abyssal Goblins.
“Krr, kreureuk!”
No matter what class you took or the cultivation method you used, there was bound to be a counter to it. And a random attack? If you got unlucky, you’d die without a prayer.
“Fuck, this is driving me crazy.”
And on top of all that, an Abyssal Goblin’s trap was impossible to detect in advance with the naked eye or magic. You just had to step on it.
“I-I can’t go any farther. I’m sorry.” The warrior who had come back up to the frontlines laughing even after receiving heals for an arm that got ripped off by a Blade Wolf shuffled back in fear.

It wasn’t that I didn’t get where he was coming from. Being too weak and getting injured because I couldn’t avoid my opponent’s attack was one thing, but getting killed for being unlucky? Even a warrior who had overcome a myriad of hardships would have a hard time getting over the psychological fear.

“I will go first,” I decided, not because I wasn’t afraid, or because I had some kind of noble mindset that allowed me to sacrifice myself for others with a smile. “You guys follow behind me.” The fact was, if everyone got scared off, there would be no end to this. In the end, that would kill everyone including me, which was why this was necessary.
Click.
At least one person needed to overcome fear and take the first step forward.
“Behelahhh!”
So I shoved my fear aside and sped up.
Click.
The traps were triggered at intervals of twenty steps. I hit a curse-type debuff.
[Your energy is greatly reduced.]
Then I triggered a continuous flame spell, Leech Flame.
[Your body is burning and any healing abilities are temporarily sealed.]
Then water damage, and actual lightning.
[Any ice damage you take is significantly increased for a certain period of time.]
Kablam!
All kinds of effects piled up on me, but I continued, relying on my +200 Mana Resistance from the Manticore. I stood by the first step I took—it was not meaningless.
Click.
I continued running. Suddenly, I heard people’s voices in the distance, but that didn’t last long.
“Stop making a scene and step back. I will go next.”
“Damn it, why! Why am I...?”
Those who passed by the others who had stopped or fallen followed behind me, starting with the barbarians. “We will follow the great warrior!”
“Behelahhh!”
“Haha! You said you have a family. This is a job for a single man like me,” said a leader who had lost his party.
An abandoned knight stepped up to bat next. “...This, too, is a way of fulfilling my pledge to the palace. I will go next.”
“This is insane. I’ve never seen something like this before.”
“Ha, how are we supposed to back out here?”
“I’ve been thinking this since earlier, but you’re a real wild bastard, huh.”

The murmurs grew louder. I suddenly felt the presence of comrades right behind me, but I didn’t look back. They didn’t need someone who doubted and worried in front, but someone who pushed onward silently and steadily.
“A-All of you have lost your minds! You think others will recognize you for this?! Huh? As heroes?”
Not blaming those who dropped to the ground, we pushed forward with those who got up again.
“Goddamn it... I’m still going. After all, someone has to do it.”
Click.
We pushed forward so we wouldn’t have to leave anything else behind.

When I came to my senses, Ainar was carrying me. I didn’t ask what had happened. This was already the third time I had stepped on traps over and over again and passed out after not being able to bear it any longer.
“How long has it been?”
“Please... rrrest more, Bjorn... Okay?”
Brushing off Missha’s concerns, I got off of Ainar’s back. I spotted Kyle. That guy would tell me. “How long has it been?”
“We’ll be there in two hours.”
“Yes, I see.”
I’d passed out for about thirty minutes, then. The priests’ divine power had already run out. I wondered how many more had died while I was gone.
“Mister...” I was about to walk forward when Erwen grabbed my wrist. “Can’t you stay...? Other people are clearing the way now. Okay?”
It was a terribly selfish yet tempting offer. The old me might have even thought it rational.
“I have to go.”
“Why... do you have to push so hard?”
“Because I’m sick of seeing people die.”

I had high Mana Resistance, so even after stepping on hundreds of traps, I only ended up passing out. It was only a rank-five ability, after all. Even without Giantization, my body was strong. Something I had realized in the middle of all this was that I wouldn’t die from this madness.
“Move.” I pushed Erwen away and ran forward. My teammates no longer held onto me. When I sped up some more, I was able to rejoin the frontline in no time.
“Still not sick of it?”

Almost two hundred warriors were clogging up the passage. This was what happened after all of the warriors from that huge initial group we’d originally split in three spontaneously reassembled. This was different from the district of the Blade Wolves, after all. As long as the traps were stepped on at the front, the enemies that appeared from the side roads weren’t all that dangerous.

The requirement for being up here was that you had to be above rank five, and had to have high Defense stats as well. Close-range warriors were accepted too, but long-range fighters were strictly excluded. That was because the Abyssal Goblins’ specialty was not just their traps. These guys also threw weapons called Monster Bags. They exploded when thrown and a random monster below rank five appeared right in front of you. This wasn’t an environment that spell casters and archers, for whom distance was everything, could survive in.
“...Is that a priest on someone’s back?”
“Oh, we told her to take a break but she kept using her divine power and lost consciousness.”

The priestess wasn’t the only one being carried. Warriors with serious injuries who were grappling with the effects of potions were being carried by other warriors. And once they came to, they would probably carry other warriors.
“I see. When she wakes up, stop her with force if you have to. We have to save her for when we really need her.”
“But that priestess is so stubborn, she won’t listen to us at all.”
“Then knock her out before that.”
“Oh, that’s doable.” Although that meant committing sacrilege against a priest, the warrior nodded in acceptance. He knew this wasn’t the time to judge.

“Then I’ll head up.” I nodded to the warrior and was about to move forward when the others bumped me back. Wait, did these guys just shoulder-check me? This was my first time experiencing that since waking up in this body. “...What is the meaning of this?”
The warriors shrugged nonchalantly at my question. “Can’t you see we’re waiting in line here?”
“Even if you are the captain, you have to stay in line.”
“Bjorn Yandel, do you think you are some kind of hero?”
What? Wait, what is this bullshit?
I was incredulous but the warriors’ expressions were sincere. “Get some more rest, Yandel.”
“You deserve it.”
Huh, I didn’t know whether to be happy about this or not.
“S-Stop!” While I was quietly observing the others at work, there was a commotion up front. Stop? In this situation? Something had to have happened.
“Move.” I hurriedly pushed through the warriors. This time, the puzzled group did not stop me.
“Uh, huh?”
“Wait!”
“Yandel? Why are you here?”
“We clearly told you to rest...”

When I reached the front, familiar adventurers greeted me, but there was something we had to deal with before I could answer their questions. What was the commotion about? But without me needing to ask, the answer was right in front of me.
“Anyway, welcome. Yandel, this is what the wizard was talking about, right?”
Beyond the passageway, in the darkness that swallowed all light, a giant eye blinked and watched me.

I sighed and nodded. “Yeah, looks like it.” What was denying it going to do? The second I’d met that eye, our encounter with the Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, became pretty much inevitable. Honestly, it was a miracle we hadn’t run into him until now.
“Now what are you going to do?”
What else can I do? Follow the plan.
“Everyone, get back.” I held up my mace and moved forward. Although I was approaching it with a weapon, that giant eye just continued to blink without backing away. It was a pretty creepy sight.
Is this your first time seeing a barbarian?
I chucked the mace into the eye as hard as I could.
Chomp!
Like the token rank-nine monster it was, the eye disappeared into a flash of light with just one regular hit.
[You have defeated the Watcher of the Abyss. EXP +1]
[The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, is starting to take a strong interest in you.]

Whew, it hadn’t been long since I had woken up, but it looked like I was in for another hard time. I pulled out the message stone and immediately reported this to Kyle. “I just killed the Watcher of the Abyss. I need you to come here now.”
It was time to move to Plan B.

chapters.title: Chapter 223: Like Fireworks (3)
paragraphs: The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, was actually less powerful than Riakis on the third floor, but he was several times harder to fight. That was because Fog of the Abyss was a cheat. It nullified active skills and various special effects, caused a three-quarter reduction in mana efficiency, and caused rank-five abyssal monsters to appear throughout the raid as trash mobs. Because of these terrible conditions, it was difficult to even attempt to take this guy down unless it was in the second half of the game.

On top of that, you had to prepare a lot to plan a proper raid: high-ranking numbered items that bestowed not special effects but regular effects, powerful tanks who could hold their own, damage dealers who could use an aura or fight at an equivalent level, as many priests as possible, and several sorcerers who were still powerful despite the reduction in mana. It was recommended that all participants in a raid had equipment of at least rank five or higher, and on top of all that, if you didn’t make sure to get a few special consumables, the damage you took increased exponentially.

But, even if you did manage to prepare everything, it was all considered a bust on day seven. From then on, regardless of the phase, additional attack patterns were unlocked. Simply put, in our current state, we’d never be able to beat this guy.
“So we’ve ended up in the monster’s sights. I’ll be there soon.”

However, we could stall for just enough time. I checked my watch while waiting for Kyle to join me. It was day five, 7 p.m. After a fierce battle to clear the path, we’d confirmed the existence of the eastern portal, and now there were only two hours to go to reach the Goblin Forest. This valuable outcome had been achieved through the sacrifices of countless warriors, but it would be a lie to say we hadn’t had a bit of luck on our side too.
“Yandel, are you all right?”
“What’s not to be all right about? I knew we’d have to run into it at least once.”
Rather, it was closer to a fluke that we were only seeing it now. One of the expedition teams who had chosen a different direction than us was probably experiencing great suffering in our stead.

How many more had died in vain? The thought left me cold but I didn’t wallow in guilt. We were all in the same boat. We had promised to be each other’s bait. On the other hand, if we had run into this guy earlier, the other teams would have been able to travel a little more easily.
“I’ve made you wait.” After about five minutes, Kyle arrived with the troops needed for Plan B: six rank-five wizards, three knights, and three warriors.
Quickly verifying the troops, I couldn’t hide my confusion. “How is this everyone?” The number of wizards was the same but the other numbers were extremely cut down. What could be the reason why?
“Everyone else is dead.”
Yeah, okay, they weren’t just hanging around in the back. We were six people short. So, who should fill those vacancies?
“Oh, your teammates offered to follow, but I stopped them. You’ll be hearing some complaints later.”
Complaints, huh? But they still wouldn’t make six. Oh, maybe the elf sisters offered to come along, too.

“...Thanks.” After thanking Kyle, I scanned the warriors around me and forced myself to speak cheerfully. “As everyone has heard, we are short six people. I’m sorry to ask this while you all look worse for wear, but is there anyone willing to join?”

Before I could finish talking, someone answered. “I will go. I’ll follow you.” Rank-five warrior Alexandro Bell was affiliated with a large clan but had been abandoned here after being pushed down the ranks.

“I was getting bored of stepping on traps, so that works for me!” Karak, the third son of Tion, was a barbarian in his thirties who was active as a member of a ten-person clan. I had been amazed at first to see a fellow countryman who was rank four.

“You, you’d better keep your promise about buying drinks once we’re out of here!” Milton Teterud was the head of a clan made up entirely of dwarves. Instead of his clan going on quests together, they apparently lent their services to affiliated teams as mercenaries. It was more of a guild than a clan.

I should have said thank you here, but for some reason I was speechless. To be honest, I hadn’t expected this to happen. The situation was different from before. There were now only two hours until we reached the portal. Although this hope could be extinguished the moment it touched despair, hope was still hope. Just because these people had been paving the way while treating their own lives as insignificant, that didn’t mean they didn’t have a desire to survive. Since we’d suffered this much damage fighting just trash mobs, I hadn’t thought anyone would volunteer to serve as bait for the boss.
“Oh? If I come too, does that mean I can join the drinking party?”
“I’m interested in something else. If I follow you guys and survive just this once, I think I’ll earn the ultimate achievement I can brag about at drinking parties for the rest of my life.”
“Behelaaah!”
“Take me with you. I’m curious what that Berzak, or whatever his name is, looks like.”

Numerous adventurers spoke up and volunteered. Was it because they believed in the plan Kyle and I had concocted? Or because their brains were secreting endorphins and they were getting swept up in the energy of the rest of the group? Well, I was sure that was a factor too. Even so, one thing was certain.
“You all... have something wrong with your heads.”
This wasn’t a choice that someone of sound mind would make. But I guessed they found this statement strange because a moment of silence ensued.
Some accepted my accusation. “...You’re not wrong. When this story is told outside, everyone else will probably say the same thing about us.”
Some laughed it off like I’d just said something ridiculous. “Is that really coming out of your mouth right now?”
There wasn’t anything in particular I could say to that. I only did what I did because it had to be done.
I guess the same goes for these guys.

My heart grew hot and I started to think something was wrong with my head. I needed to cool it. I selected six of the numerous volunteers. There was only one criterion: who were the most compatible fighters? Because these were comrades I’d been fighting alongside all day, I had no trouble choosing. I already basically knew their fighting styles.
When the decision was made, Teterud, the leader of the dwarf clan, protested. “You! Why are you leaving me behind?! Are you afraid I’ll slow you down?”
“No way.”
“Then why? I won’t let you go until you tell me why!”
Geez, the stubbornness of this small man. It looked like Kyle was almost done with the magic circle, so I offered a brief explanation. “I need someone to lead this group while I’m gone.”

Teterud was a rank-four adventurer. He was skilled and led a clan of his own so he knew how to manage people. If I had to leave the frontlines to someone, this guy was the right person. I heard that he had been taking the lead whenever I passed out.
“...Tsk.” Though dissatisfied, he seemed convinced by my logic and stopped arguing with me.
“Yandel, everything is ready. It’s time for him to show up too.”
Hah, I see.

As soon as I heard Kyle say that the magic circle was complete, I sent the rest of them away. “You guys leave now. This scout Kyle has brought along will show you the way. I heard he’s quite strong, but make sure to keep him alive.”
“You talk like you’re our father or something. All right, we’re going. See you later. That’s a promise. Okay?”
“You’re the one who sounds like the father here.”
“I do have a kid in the city. Now, let’s go!”

As we moved closer to the wall so as not to block their path, Teterud took up my mantle of stepping on traps at the head of the group and the other warriors followed. Everyone offered up parting words as they passed.
“Don’t die.”
“Hmm, strangely, I don’t think you’re going to die. See you later!”

Most were words of encouragement and support. Those comments continued for a while even after the group of warriors passed. As the rest caught up, some said thank you, and others offered words of apology, not once or twice, but again and again.
“Why is everyone doing that?”
Kyle laughed at my question. “That’s because your message stone has been turned on this whole time. Everyone already knows about the situation up front.”
Oh, so it was.
“Bjorn...”

As the procession continued, members of Team Apple Narak also appeared. Upon seeing the state I was in, Missha looked like she was going to burst into tears. Raven and Mr. Bear wore complicated expressions too.
“Stop that and keep moving already. The people behind can’t pass if you’re blocking the way.”
“I swear... if you come back injurrred, I’ll kill you.”
Hmm, telling a tank not to get injured? Wasn’t that pretty much a death sentence? I kept those thoughts to myself.
It’s not that bad.
So what if I got scolded a bit? All of this was so that we could get back to our daily lives.
“I’ll leave it to you,” I said to Raven.
“Yes, don’t worry. Even without you there, I will make sure to protect our team. Now, Miss Ainar, let’s go.”
“Ugh, o-okay! Don’t pull my hair!”

With that, Raven rode Ainar, who was trying to insist on following me, down the passage. Even after that, the procession continued. They all looked like refugees fleeing through a tunnel in the middle of a war.
Whoosh.

There were lit torches, the groans of the wounded on the backs of their comrades, broken equipment, bloodstains, sad and weary eyes, and beads of sweat dripping down the skin as everyone limped after the people ahead of them. I didn’t have to ask Kyle what had happened. Considering how many things had happened to me too, I knew this day had been particularly long for everyone.
“Okay, then, everyone is gone.”

Including Group One, which I had been leading, Groups Two and Three, which were following along using the marks on the passageways, all passed us by. It didn’t take long. That was because they were running at a sprint. Our numbers had also decreased considerably since the start.
“This feels kind of creepy.”

Once everyone left, our surroundings grew very dark. Was it because the swaying torches had been lighting the cave as the procession was passing us? Their sudden absence was stark. It felt like we were the only people left in the world.
Anyway, it should be here by now...
I raised my shield and stared down the passageway. “It’s here.”
Current visibility: two yards. But in the darkness of the labyrinth beyond that, hundreds of eyes were watching us.
The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, was here.

If I had to pick what I had been most worried about when first making the plan, it was Berzak. No matter how I approached the issue, the fact was that it would be impossible to escape this bastard with hundreds of people. It was safe to say that this would turn into a massacre the moment we encountered him.

Well, if we split up and ran, the aggro would bounce around and more people would be able to survive, but what could we do while scattered apart? If we broke off into smaller groups, we wouldn’t even be able to penetrate the trash mobs and reach the portal, let alone fight Noark on the second floor.
“Can you use the magic circle right away?”
And so we made a Plan B. But with our resources, this strategy could only be used once.
“I’ve double-checked the magic circle several times, so don’t worry.”

If Plan B failed, everyone would die. Even if we succeeded, if we encountered the Watcher of the Abyss one more time, we wouldn’t be able to avoid getting annihilated. This was also one of my reasons for assuming the maximum number of portals we’d be able to check was two. In that time frame, many of the teams led by the others would have disappeared. Even if we made it through the first encounter, I predicted that the possibility of running into Berzak again would be too high.
“Prepare for battle.”
The moment the eyes appeared in the darkness, everyone drew their weapons and prepared to fight. They knew from Kyle’s explanations what these eyes meant.

These disembodied eyes were an effect that occurred around Berzak. For reference, the radius of the effect in the game was about 1.2 miles. And it wasn’t just simple wallpaper. All of these eyes shared sight with the bastard. In other words, Berzak was already watching us.

“As you all know, our goal is to hold out as long as possible until the others escape his line of sight.” Kyle seemed nervous as well and repeated the same explanation he had already given several times.
“Do you take us for fools? We remember the plan. You also said that if your predictions are correct, we just have to hold out for ten minutes.”
“I see. I’m sorry. But I will say one more thing. I forgot to mention this earlier... but no matter what happens, protect Yandel.”
“Hm? Yandel? Will do.”
“Are you not going to ask why?”
“Everyone knows even without you saying it. This guy has to survive for the rest of us to get back home.” Everyone nodded at the warrior’s words.

“I was going to say that if Yandel dies after killing a Watcher of the Abyss, it might target the main team next...” Kyle laughed, sheepish, and decided to stop there. “Well, no matter. It seems I didn’t even need to tell you to protect him anyway.”
“Haha! Yes, whatever the reason, what matters is that the results are the same, no?”
“Indeed, you are right. It seems wizards and warriors are no different in this respect.”
The light conversation made the tension relax a bit. Unfortunately, it didn’t last long.
Whiiip!
A shadow shot out of the dark, as sharp as a spear.
Bang!
The moment I blocked it with my shield, I felt a pain in the back of my hand. It wasn’t deep, and had just scratched the skin.
Whew, I’ve never encountered this guy so unprepared like this, so I couldn’t even calculate the damage.
To think my moonstone shield would be pierced with one regular attack. Was it because I wasn’t in Giantization mode?
At the sight of my perforated shield, the faces of the warriors around me hardened. “Just hold out for ten minutes,” Kyle said in an attempt to inspire morale.
Ten minutes already felt so far away. Still, for some reason, that made me laugh.
“Why do you laugh?”
“Warriors laugh when they’re tired.”

I faced forward. A shadow shimmered in the dark. The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, was a boss that you could only attempt to defeat in the second half of the game, a monster of monsters that would only end up pummeling us at our current level. But, so what?
“Behelaaah!”
Despite all that, this guy was just one hurdle—one that after an exceptionally long day like today would allow us to see tomorrow.

chapters.title: Chapter 224: Like Fireworks (4)
paragraphs: We were just a few steps away from the darkness. Relying on the shimmering torchlight, we stood in a dense formation. Everywhere we looked, displeased eyes followed us.
What are you staring at?

Hundreds of eyes filled the darkness. It felt like we had stepped inside the setting of a cruel, twisted fairy tale. Of course, that was just the setting. The storyline was up to us. If we overcame this adversity, this would become a story of hope. If we fell here, it would remain just a cruel tale.
Whiiip!

The spear-shaped shadow embedded in my shield pulled out and returned to the darkness. This had already happened several times. This bastard had to be shy or something because the only thing he was doing was shooting potshots from a distance.
I guess that works for us, though, considering we’re only here to stall.
With that thought in mind, I checked the condition of my equipment. The shield had holes all over it. “You’ll need to get a new shield once you’re out,” the warrior next to me said.
A statement that assumed that I’d return alive. I grinned. “Oh, I should definitely buy a new one.”
We would survive, at least one more of us.
Slide...
After those four regular shots, I heard a sound from the darkness.
So, done testing the waters?
Slide.

Soon, on the whistle of a spooky breeze, it appeared. It was about six feet tall and wore only a robe that looked like something the dead would wear. It didn’t even have a weapon. Its outline looked humanoid, except for the fact that, like a ghost-type monster, the parts of its body not covered by the robe consisted only of billowing, dark blue smoke.
Flash!

The place where its head should have been above the neck was covered by a hood. A red eye flashed from underneath it. It was unquestionably different from a human. First, there was only one eye emitting light, and even that was located in the center of the face, not on the right or left, making its proportions strange. On top of that, the eye was huge, as if its entire head was made up of a giant eyeball.
“Avoid eye contact as much as possible,” said Kyle.
As soon as I confirmed the monster was there, I fixed my eyes on his shoulder. The reason was simple.
“Do not be afraid.”
The moment you met that eye, you had a certain probability of being affected by the Fear status condition.
“Look at me.”

When Fear stacked up nine times, the character in question became a servant of the Lord of the Abyss forever. Just like the countless monsters in the labyrinth, they’d turn into enemies and attack us.
It’s an awful attack pattern.
In reality, it was safe to say that it was essentially an Instant Kill, since the Monsterization effect wasn’t reversed even after the boss was cleared.
Well, our objective isn’t to clear it but to last ten minutes...

I doubted anyone would reach Monsterization in ten minutes, but we couldn’t let our guards down yet. We hadn’t come here fully prepared, after all. There were no fear-related fail-safes in place. In other words, the status condition Fear itself was threatening enough on its own.
“Ugh...” A warrior next to me gripped his head and groaned. It looked like he’d met the monster’s eye. If he was set off by Fear he would’ve either dropped his weapon and fled or attacked us.
“Bjorn!”
“Be careful!”

While I was checking on my comrade, a shadow shot out from Berzak’s chest. The awl in question had struck my shield time and time again. However, it was using a slightly different pattern from before.
Whiiip.
The terrifyingly threatening shadow split into dozens of different strands and swept over me like a net.
Splat.

The shadow clung to my body like octopus suckers. I could feel it pulling at me from all over. It was obvious what his plan was. Since regular hits were going to take too long, he must have been planning on dragging me into the darkness.
Ha, we’re not that unprepared.

“Ecovir Iheran Ifoun.” Kyle shot the spell he had prepared in advance, the rank-seven support spell Attribute Bestowal. For reference, the attribute in question was naturally strong against Dark-attribute monsters.
Whoosh!
A pure white flame combining the Fire and Divine attributes swallowed everyone’s weapons except those of the knights. The reason he didn’t use it on them was simple.
Slice!
With an aura, it was possible to inflict damage on the monster without Attribute Bestowal.
“Save Bjorn!”

The moment I was shackled by the shadows, warriors ran forward and cut or smashed it with weapons engulfed in flames. My body was freed in an instant. However, before I even had a moment to catch my breath, dozens of shadows jumped out of the bastard’s body again.
Whiiip!
It was a new attack pattern again. This time, the bastard was aiming not only for me but for everyone. I hurriedly adjusted my grip on my shield.
It’s begun.
The real battle was getting started.

The eye monster I killed earlier, the Watcher of the Abyss, was a summon used by Berzak to select its next victim after a battle ended. When cast, it appeared all over the entire cave and roamed around looking for a sacrifice. Once you ran into it once, that was it. There was no way to break the aggro on you, and so I killed the eye without hesitation. If no one attracted the main aggro, it was impossible to lure Berzak out.
As was evident from how it had been acting up to this point, until my comrades attacked the monster first to save me, I was the only one the bastard had seen as his enemy.
While we had been strategizing, someone had asked, “Then wouldn’t it be better for a single person to step up and sacrifice themselves?”

Realistically, there was no chance of that working. Aside from the question of who would fill that role, Berzak’s line of sight had a radius of one mile. If we couldn’t hold out until the rest of the group escaped that radius, it would all be for naught.
Ten minutes.
Kyle estimated the time it would take to be about ten minutes. If we were defeated before then, it would pursue the expedition team and commit a senseless massacre.
Boom!
That was why I held out, not on my own, but with the wizards and warriors who had followed me here.
“Behelaaah!”
Wielding flaming weapons, we resisted the darkness. It wasn’t an easy task.
Whiiip!

Constant attacks flew at us from sharp shadows that could punch through almost anything. Normally, I could’ve handled this without trouble. Although I had no way of knowing how long it would last me, as long as I blocked it with my shield I wouldn’t be seriously injured.
This goddamned game.
The problem was that I couldn’t see in front of me. Since my gaze was fixed lower down to avoid eye contact, I wasn’t able to react in time. For reference, it was like this in the actual game too.
[Do not look into Berzak’s eye.]
If this command was applied to the character, no matter how high their Agility stat, their evasion rate and defense success rate plummeted, just like right now.
Stab!
The shadow dug deep into my shoulder.
[Your body is rapidly regenerating due to Recovery (Greater)‘s effects.]
It was getting to the point where potions weren’t enough. Even though the aggro was dispersed somewhat, most of it was focused on me.
“Agh, ah!”

And the shadows weren’t simply stabbing at us, either. They were also flying out in the shape of nets and dragging my comrades into the darkness. We’d been diligently slicing the shadows and blocking them until now, but we couldn’t hold out forever.
God damn it.
Eventually, the first sacrifice occurred.
“Sillian!”
Sillian Neroff was the guy who had come along saying that it would be cool to tell this story at drinking parties later.
“Arghh! Agh! Ahh!” Terrible screams rang out from the darkness he had been dragged into. It made me feel very strange. In the game, I thought it was just a sound effect to set the mood.
Anger boiled in me, but the more it did, the more I focused on remaining vigilant. Once again, there needed to be someone doing that.
“Stop.”
“But—!”
“If you go in there, you will die too.”
He’d already been sucked in, so saving him was impossible. At our current level, at least.
One of the warriors vented his anger. “God damn it!”

It wasn’t that I didn’t get it. We couldn’t even witness the death of a comrade we’d fought alongside all day with our own eyes. We could only listen to the sounds from beyond the darkness. I felt helpless. It was something I’d felt countless times just today. But whether I felt helpless or not, the battle continued.
[Your body is rapidly regenerating due to Recovery (Greater)‘s effects.]
Berzak activated a skill called Call of the Abyss. It gathered all the trash mobs in the bastard’s line of sight into one place.
“Grk! Greuk!” The Abyssal Goblins that had received the call released a bundle of monsters, summoned more, and set traps far and wide. Another person died as a result.
Shooop!

Traps went off and monsters jumping out of the Monster Bags ran wild, initiating a melee battle. An awl-shaped shadow pierced the body of a comrade. Even the wizards who had been casting Mana Shields on occasion to prevent fatal injuries couldn’t react in time.
Slump.
One more died like that.
“Kyle! How much longer?!”
“Four minutes.”
What, four minutes left?
