“Four minutes have passed.”
Geez, I almost got excited there.
Crunch!
Just then, the first disaster struck.
“It’s a Troll! Push it back!”
One more died. The cause of death was a Troll summoned right under our noses. But the problem wasn’t the Troll—it was that the deceased was a wizard.
God damn it.
The death of a warrior was inevitable, but a wizard was different. They had been placed in the middle so we could protect them in whatever way we could.
That means mana will run out soon...
This was the worst-case scenario. But even as I thought that, I continued to move, and time continued to pass.
“Five minutes left... four minutes!” As if to boost morale, Kyle announced the time with each minute that passed. “Now we just have to hold out for three minutes!”

Since the wizard’s death, there had been no more victims. Like the veteran adventurers they were, they gradually accumulated experience as the battle continued. However, something happened at the eight-minute mark.
“I can no longer use magic. I can just barely maintain the Bestow spell,” Kyle reported.
So we’ll have to survive without support from a wizard, huh?
This was sooner than I had expected, but it couldn’t be helped. One wizard had already died. To leave enough mana to activate the magic circle, we had no other choice.
“Keeek!” As the wide-range spells dried up, the monsters emerging from the Monster Bags piled up.
And in this grueling situation, dealing with reduced numbers and the absence of magic, Berzak continued to shoot arrow-like shadows at us without pause.
Shoop!
Like that, another person died.
I don’t think I’ll be able to keep that promise.

You couldn’t give your final will and testament in the middle of such a fierce battle. Whether the enemy was a monster or a human, they wouldn’t be so kind as to give us time for that. So we had discussed it beforehand.

“If you guys can grab my equipment, take it to my teammates.” That was the will left behind by the guy who had just died. But just as I’d told him back then as well, there wouldn’t be time to do that.
“Ahh! H-Help me!” The guy right next to me was grabbed by the shadows and disappeared into the darkness. “Ahh! Ahhh!”
Listening to the resounding screams, I bit down on my lip.
“Deliver the news to my son. You will definitely be famous by the time you get out of here. That boy will wish to meet you.”
I thought I could keep that promise if I could just get back alive.
“I’m going to charge the magic circle now!”

There was one minute left until we hit our target of ten minutes. The wizards activated the magic circle they drew earlier. I swung my mace frantically. My shield was nowhere to be seen. Oh, right. I tossed it aside earlier, announcing I did not need it. It would be impossible to repair anyway, so I didn’t feel all that bad about it.
“Yandel, come here!”
Oh, it’s already done?

Suddenly, a bright light emanated from the ground. Berzak seemed to be startled by that, as he stopped attacking and just watched us. The same went for the other monsters. It was only for a moment, but the battle had stopped.
I quickly scanned my surroundings. I couldn’t see all the dead bodies, of course. Some had been dragged into the darkness.
It has to be nearby!

At the border where the light met the darkness was the body I was looking for. I quickly ran toward him and retrieved his sword and shield. I had to use quite a bit of strength. Even dead, his eyes were still open and his weapon was clutched in his hand.
“Bjorn!” someone shouted, and I rolled through the dirt to get inside the magic circle. The warriors didn’t even ask why I did that.
“That’s... yes, we did promise.”
“His teammates will be grateful.”

When I sprung back up to my feet, I could see monsters approaching us in the distance. They had been momentarily scared off by the light the magic circle was emitting, but they soon seemed to decide it wasn’t a threat.
“Bothering us until the end!”
“Hey, wizard! I think we should go now!”
“Just a little longer!”
I stared straight ahead. I could see Berzak.
“I saw you.”
What the fuck did you see, huh?
I fixed my eyes on the bastard and recited the names of the deceased in my head.
Silian Neroff. Neil Feymez. Paul Agmus. Garfen Gulan. Matt Elvans. Refrey Siaberus.
Six people in total.
Yeah, I’ll see you again someday.
Riakis, the Lord of Chaos; the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos; and Berzak. I hoped these bastards knew that I wouldn’t be running from them forever.
[Kyle Pevrosk has cast the rank-four spatial spell Mass Teleportation.]
When I opened my eyes, there were people around me. So we had reached the right place.
“How much distance have we cleared?”
“It should be close to two miles. Now that we’re totally out of sight, he won’t be able to follow us. Well, if we run into a Watcher of the Abyss again, that will change things.”
I checked behind me like a man possessed. I saw none of those fucking eyes in the darkness, thankfully. That meant we really had succeeded in teleporting that long distance.
“Incredible.”

“Not really. If we hadn’t entrusted the coordinate designating device to this team, even I would have been unable to teleport us this far. Oh, and the other wizards shared some of their mana with me.”

Well, even if he wanted to be humble about it, that wasn’t something just anyone could pull off, no matter how much help they had. It wasn’t easy to use magic like that in a place where Mana Efficiency was reduced to a quarter.
“...Then I’ll start moving.”
“Without resting?”
“I can rest as I go.”
I opened a bottle of potion and poured it over my head. While the other warriors were receiving treatment, I started walking.
Before long, I found the people I was looking for—Garfen Gulan’s teammates. They were very tight-knit, enough so that they had come to the frontlines to try to take him away from the danger there.
“You are...” They recognized me, too, and froze. Their eyes were on the sword and shield I was holding.
“Take them.”

“...Is he dead?” an adventurer asked tearfully, and I remained silent. It took a while for her mouth to open again. “This... I’ll take it. But take this.” After picking up the sword, the woman handed me the shield. “You will need it, I think.”
“...Thank you.” I didn’t refuse and accepted the shield. I had lost mine, after all. Refusing this would only make this more painful for them too. “Then I will go.”
I continued forward and soon reached my teammates.
“Anyone injured while I was gone?”
No one answered my question. They just stared at me blankly. Missha’s hands even trembled.
Oh, is she going to scold me for getting hurt? I should run, quick.
“If you’re not hurt, then I’ll just go—”
“Stop. Please, stop and get some rrrest. You’ve done enough. Okay?”
“Yes, Mr. Yandel. Do as Miss Karlstein says. If you go up there in the state you’re in, you won’t be any help, anyway. You said there could be another big fight later on, right?”
I decided to stop being stubborn. Raven was right. Even after going through all that, I still had a mountain left to climb. I’d better conserve my energy.
Trudge, trudge.
While other warriors cleared the way in the frontlines, I followed the procession with my teammates and recovered my stamina.
After a long while, instructions to stall the procession came through on the message stone. “Stop!” I sensed intuitively that we had reached our destination.
“Is the portal open?” asked Kyle.
His voice was followed by that of Teterud, the leader of the all-dwarf clan, whom I had entrusted with the frontlines. “It’s open.”
So we’d come to the right place. My legs felt strangely weak. If this place had been destroyed, too, I would’ve really lost it.
“Raven, take care of things on this end.”
“Yes, go. You’re going to even if we stop you, anyway.”
I passed through the crowd of adventurers and headed to the front lines. As soon as I arrived, Teterud greeted me. “Now what are you going to do? Will you go in straight away?”
“As soon as preparations are finished back there.”
“Are you going to go first again?”
“Is there a point? You guys are going to follow right behind me, anyway.”
“Haha, that’s true.”
I soon stood in front of the portal. After about ten minutes, I got a message from Kyle through the message stone. “The preparations are complete. You can go in now.”
I closed my eyes and took a breath. Even I could tell my breathing had gotten rough, but the rougher it got, the more I thought of the positives.
There might be no one there.
Noark’s side probably would have assumed that even if someone managed to come up alive, it would be a small number.
Plus, it’d be more beneficial to them for us to return to the city, testify to what the royals and their knights have done, and create disorder.
Of course, that was just one possibility. They also could have decided to be thorough and deployed troops near the portals to finish off even the few survivors.
I’m sure they didn’t leave that many behind.
Regardless of how much equipment they had grabbed on the first floor, they couldn’t live off of that. Their main forces would have gone straight up to other floors to mine for mana stones.
God damn it.
Even as I thought that, I found myself feeling uncertain. However, I still put my foot forward.
This isn’t the first time.
How many times had I been certain before? We didn’t have any other options, anyway. Even if we waited here patiently, we’d just end up getting picked off by Abyssal Goblins.
Trudge.
I took one more step and entered the portal.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
My vision went black for a moment. It wasn’t long before I felt my body floating. When I opened my eyes, I saw a green forest.
“God damn it.”
There was good news and bad news. The good news was that there weren’t many troops nearby. And the bad news...
Fuck, they’re still here?
My expectation that their main forces would have headed up to mine for mana stones was wrong.
Splat.
Finding my balance and landing on the ground, I studied the three people in the forest. I could tell who they were just by looking at their clothing—two of them, at least.
“The first survivor.” This was the person who had destroyed all the portals, the Fallen Scholar.
“Haha, I told you someone would definitely show up if we waited here. Hey, barbarian! Congratulations. It was a rough journey, eh?” asked an unknown beastman.
“Oh? We meet again.” The last man was still wearing that white mask from before. “I guess we’re meant to be? Pshehe.” With his eyes on me, the Corpse Collector grinned.

chapters.title: Chapter 225: Reversal (1)
paragraphs: The Goblin Forest was on the brighter end of the second-floor areas you could travel to. It was still dark, but the countless stars embroidering the sky acted as a source of light to some extent. It still wasn’t as bright as this, though.
Whoom!
Dozens of light spheres floating in the air illuminated our surroundings and made it look like daytime. It was like being at a lit stadium at night.
Just how much mana do they have left?
This display alone made the difference in our power levels glaringly obvious and clawed at my chest, but now was not the time to dwell on it.
“Yandel, those guys...”
“The Fallen Scholar and the Corpse Collector. And I don’t know the other person.” Even as I briefly filled in the warriors who had followed me, I stared straight ahead.
“Oh, I guess you didn’t come alone after all?” The beastman whose identity I had not yet deduced chuckled. He seemed to be in a good mood. “This will be quite a bit of money even split in three.”
His greedy eyes scanned us as if we were a trash mob he’d found on a sweet hunting ground. Ha, I had even been toying with the idea that they might just congratulate us and let us go.
“How uncouth.” The gray-haired elderly wizard, the Fallen Scholar, clicked his tongue in apparent displeasure.
“Why? Isn’t this why you insisted on staying behind too?” the beastman asked. The Fallen Scholar didn’t answer, as if annoyed by the accusation.
Just then, the Corpse Collector laughed and joined in. “Pshehe, you still don’t know anything about this old man, huh? Spoils of war or not, he probably just wants to get home as soon as possible.”
“Hmm, is that so? Then I guess we’re the only two uncouth ones here.”
“Ha, what are you saying? You think I stayed behind to get some equipment?”
“...Then why did you?”
The beastman tilted his head at Corpse Collector’s—Clown’s—words. I also listened in while pretending not to, figuring that learning their individual motives and goals could increase our options.
Yeah, that was what I thought.

“Because it seemed like fun, of course!” Clown shouted dramatically, just like at the Round Table. “The chance to kill adventurers who managed to fight through that hell on just a shred of hope! What could be better?”
The Fallen Scholar frowned again. “What is that tone? It’s as if you are acting all of a sudden.”
“Ahh, this? I thought, if I’m lucky, someone here might know! Pshehe.”
“Someone might know...?”
“Never mind. I’ve always wanted to kill them, but it’d be no fun to kill them so easily, right? But the ones who are dying should at least get to know who I am to make it fun!”
“I have no idea what you are talking about. Do what you want. I will rest.” Fallen Scholar looked like he had no idea what Clown was talking about, but I was different.
You maniacal bastard.

This guy was hoping that a member of the Round Table was here to recognize him, which was why he had even worn a mask and revealed who he was. In a way, it was a gesture that showed just how determined he was not to let anyone here live.

“Hmm, but there’s a lot more of them than I thought,” the beastman noted, his voice calm even as more of my comrades entered through the portal. He did not seem the slightest bit nervous. These were the dregs left behind by the royal troops, after all. No matter how many of them were here, he was confident he could take care of them.
Even better.

I decided to interpret this as positively as possible. If these guys had decided to start mowing us down as soon as we came up, the situation would have been even bleaker. It was good that the enemy was underestimating us.
“Pshehe, I guess that’s all of you?”
Whether that was arrogance or not, we just needed to take advantage of it.
“If there were more, it would have been trouble. This worked out.”
“Pshehe, what trouble?” Clown, a high-ranking necromancer who was considered by many to be a one-man army, snapped his fingers.
Whoom!
A huge sub-space opened up in mid-air.
“Gruhhh!” Hundreds of corpse soldiers poured out.
“Behelaaah!” This was what I had waited so long for. It was time for the final battle to begin.
The corpse army charged at us head-on. They seemed to be in good shape, as they were properly equipped. The threat they posed was considerable.
“Hey, if we just win this battle, we can go back, right?”
However, no one ran away, at least around me.
“Whew, now we can finally fight properly.” The warriors, who were already exhausted as it was, laughed as they drew their weapons.
“Finally, I can save a little face. Remember, I’m a higher rank than you.”
It was very different from when we had been clearing the way on the first floor. Various weapons such as swords, hammers, axes, and maces began to glow.
[Alexandro Bell has cast Fire Fury.]
[Ralph Kell has cast Breeze Blade.]
[Milton Teterud has cast Fighting Flag. The amount of energy consumed during battle is greatly reduced.]
These were skills that we hadn’t been able to activate until now due to the field effects downstairs.
“Woahhh!”
“Let’s gooo!”
Like people who had just been waiting for this moment, the warriors charged at the zombie army. I also used Giantization and joined the ranks. Yeah, we may not have had stamina, but we had MP.
Kwaaaaaang!
There was an explosion as the frontline collided with the zombie army, a sound that should rightfully accompany a battle of adventurers.
“Geuuuu...” As soon as the corpse army’s charge was stopped in its tracks, support flew in from the rear: flying arrows, attack magic of various attributes, and long-range special abilities.
Of course, the other side didn’t just sit idly by, either.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Curse of Stone.]
During the battle, bodies turned into stone statues.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Corpse Explosion.]
Corpses designated for self-destruction burst through our line and blew up.
Pop!
The force of the explosion was about the same as a rank-six fire spell. It wasn’t enough to kill these warriors instantly now that they were strengthened and sharpened by their active skills.
Chhhhh.
However, as the corpses were being controlled by a Poison Necromancer, those nearby who were drenched in their blood instantly began to dissolve.
“Ahhh!”

In the middle of all that, one of the trio, the beastman, took a massive leap and landed in front of me. “Hey, barbarian! Are you the leader here?” His appearance was completely different from earlier. With ferociously protruding fangs, fur covering his entire body along with a blue mane, and a height and frame on par with me in Giantization mode, the bastard had transformed into a beast reminiscent of a Lycanthrope.
No wonder he had no equipment.
I scanned the man and quickly analyzed him.
Is it a strengthening type?

Each beastperson had a unique ability called a Soul Beast. It seemed that his was a strengthening type like Missha’s. One of the powers he had obtained during the process of leveling up his Soul Beast over and over again must have been some kind of transformation skill.
So which essences has he absorbed?
Since I’d figure that out later, I set my curiosity aside and shielded my face. The bastard was swinging his huge front paw at me.
Bang!
There was a heavy, bone-chilling shock.
His Strength stat is higher than mine.
As expected, this wouldn’t be an easy fight.
Whoom!
Just as I was about to disengage from the power struggle and step back, a sword swung not toward me, but the wolfman.
“I’ll take care of this guy, so you back up!” It was Melter Fend, the leader of Clan Nartel.
“You’re taking over?”
“Sir Kyle’s orders.”
If you say so.

I obediently conceded and stepped back. A round peg should go in a round hole. Fend was the sole rank-three adventurer in our group, and he had been conserving his strength up to this point in preparation for the battle on the second floor.
He said he once served as an apprentice knight. He will be much better at fighting against people than I am.
“Yandel, can you hear me?” The moment I left the wolfman to Fend and turned around, I heard Kyle’s voice from the message stone.
“I hear you.”
“Sorry. I was delayed because I was splitting the troops.”
“No need to apologize, tell me what you need.”
“You focus on leading people against the Corpse Collector. Fend and his comrades have volunteered to take care of Blue Mane.”
“Blue Mane?”

“Oh, you didn’t know? He made a name for himself during the conquest of Noark. He used to be the heir of the Blue Wolf tribe, but it seems he went into hiding in Noark after committing a crime and running away.”
Hmm, so he wasn’t a member of Orcules, then. No wonder I didn’t know who he was. “Okay. I’ll handle it.”
“You are reliable. Then I will give my all to stopping that old man.” By “old man” he must have meant the Fallen Scholar. Perhaps he was the one Kyle wanted revenge against.
“Okay, then I’ll entrust him to you.” I ended the conversation and swung my mace at the corpses riddling the forest.
But just then, I heard Kyle’s voice again. “Oh, and one more thing. Your teammates will reach you soon.”
“What?”
There was no answer.
Crunch!
I was in the middle of crushing the head of a corpse that was covering itself with a shield, when...
Slice!
An adamantium greatsword lodged itself into the temple of a zombie that was aiming for my side.
“From now on, we will help you!”
“Bjorn!”
It was Ainar and Missha. The close-range damage dealer sisters smoothly took up stances on either side of me. It was a formation Team Apple Narak often went with when fighting.
“You’re not going to be stubborn and try to fight alone again, are you?” When I turned around, I could see Raven atop Mr. Bear’s summoned beast, Iron Bear.
No, wait a minute, if Iron Bear is here...
As expected, a quick glance around confirmed that Mr. Bear had come up too.
“You should be in the rear, why are you all...?” I could buy the melee sisters, but why were these two here too? The back would be much safer.
Mr. Bear answered while nocking an arrow on his crossbow. “Shooting at high angles is not my specialty.”
Well, that was true, but there was no way that was the real reason.
I’ll have to get him Leap Sight once we’re on the sixth floor.
Thinking of an essence I could give Mr. Bear later, I swung my mace. However, the zombie collapsed before I even hit it.
Whoosh!
A firey arrow had buried itself between its brows.
“Mister!”
So you’re here too.
It looked like her sister, Daria, was there as well. She had been trying to protect Erwen from the danger earlier, but maybe she had a change of heart? I wasn’t sure, but I wasn’t complaining.
“Protect the commander!” Fend and his clan members had carved out their own territory on the battlefield and were diligently pummeling the wolfman.
“You annoying bastards...!” Judging by that rave review, it seemed their strategy was working well, although it bothered me a bit that things on the Fallen Scholar’s end were quiet.
Trust him. I’m sure Kyle will be able to handle whatever happens. I just have to do my job.

I scanned the surrounding area. It wasn’t difficult to spot Clown while I was Giantized. The bastard was sitting on top of a giant corpse monster, watching the battlefield like it was incredibly entertaining to him.
There’s a limit to how much you can underestimate people.
I couldn’t help but laugh. Come to think of it, the Dragon Slayer had had the same look in his eyes when I first met him.
“Missha, Ainar. We’re clearing the way from now on.”
I started fighting through the corpse army in earnest and advanced. The target was the Corpse Collector. The objective? Crush his skull and check if there was something wrong with his head.
“Yandel! Yandel is trying to do something again!”
“Is he aiming for the Corpse Collector?”
“Follow the great warrior!”
“Let’s gooo!”
Adventurers began to gather around me.

chapters.title: Chapter 226: Reversal (2)
paragraphs: The worst had been averted. Although the famous veterans had stayed behind, the number of troops waiting for us wasn’t overwhelming. We only had to face three enemies. Not to mention, as a result of their confidence or something, these guys didn’t shoot us point blank as we came up through the portal and took up formation.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Puppet.]
However, things still weren’t looking good. Although we were able to fight on par with them right now, we’d be at a disadvantage if the battle dragged on. That was how necromancers worked.
“Gruhhh!”
It was a large-scale battle where the death toll went up rapidly every second. Flesh was torn by the hands of corpse soldiers, and the headless bodies of our comrades rose up again to attack us.
Crunch!
Even at this moment we diligently destroyed zombies’ heads, but at this rate, we would be the ones outnumbered.
Ha, what a combination.

I couldn’t help groaning. Although there were only three of them, they worked way too well together between the Corpse Collector’s troops, Blue Mane’s hand-to-hand combat, and Fallen Scholar’s wide-range spells and overwhelming ability to create openings. If these veterans were just great fighters, our odds would have been much higher.
Rather, it must be because of this synergy that the rest have all gone upstairs.

I shook off the regret that brushed through my mind. No one in the world was without their flaws, and not everything about this was necessarily bad. Rather, because our opponent was the Corpse Collector, some things about this situation were advantageous for me too.
[You have used Outlaw of the Wilderness.]
I didn’t think I would be using the item I had obtained in Doppelganger Forest here.
“Behelaaah!” At the forefront of the frontline, I once again did what I had done countless times today—cleared the way.
Crackkk! Kwaaang!
Each time I swung my mace, corpses wearing various kinds of equipment were swept away like autumn leaves. The reason for this was simple. Outlaw of the Wilderness was a necromancer’s kryptonite.
[The Physical damage you deal in close combat temporarily increases in proportion to the number of humanoid monsters present.]
My close-combat damage rose in proportion to the number of troops around me. I was sure I’d reached the maximum buff by now. The max was... what, ten times?
[Current rate of increase: 1000%]
Crunch!

Was this how Lü Bu of the Three Kingdoms felt? I didn’t even need to use Swing since they were exploding with each smack of the mace. Well, using it would help some more, but saving my limited MP and investing it in Giantization was the best plan of action.
“Ha, what kind of rank-five adventurer...?”
“A Great Warrior!”
“Follow him!”
Once I started my mindless assault, other adventurers naturally fell into step behind me and took up a siege formation.
Okay, that takes care of anyone attacking me from the rear.
“It’s a suicide bomb!”

Corpse Explosion had dealt a lot of damage at first but that was slowly being dealt with. That was because these were veteran explorers and raids were daily occurrences to them. Even without any instructions from me, they naturally worked out how to deal with it.
“Wizard!”
“Dertu Teiran!” That was the rank-eight support spell, Gust.
Bang!

As soon as a suicide soldier’s body started to swell up, they got knocked back or pushed away with magic or skills. Of course, even so, damage to our formation occurred from time to time, and I was taking the brunt of it.
Chhhhhh!

The suicide soldiers’ acid clung all over my body. However, it didn’t sting that badly. It wasn’t because I had raised my Poison Tolerance particularly high; it was just that Dungeon and Stone was a team game.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-seven support spell Neutralization.]
This was a buff spell that reduced poison damage by half.
[Rebecca Eisel has cast Share.]
Share was an active skill that allowed the user to take a third of the target’s damage for them.
[Khan Algon has cast Collective Immunity.]
That was an aura-type skill that shared half of the caster’s tolerance-related stats with everyone within a fifteen-yard radius, regardless of whether they were friend or foe.
[Folton Cassel has cast Blood Fountain. You will now create a regeneration orb whenever you receive damage.]

Now there were healing tokens that burst out of my body whenever I took damage and replenished the blood of my comrades. With hundreds of adventurers averaging rank five in one place, there was no lack of talent.
Whoom!
Just then, the dozens of light spheres filling the sky above the Goblin Forest disappeared, plunging the surrounding area into darkness. I intuitively sensed what was happening.
“Careful, he’s going to make a move soon,” said Kyle through the message stone.
Yeah, the Fallen Scholar wouldn’t just sit back and watch forever.
Whoosh!
The sky darkened as if a solar eclipse had occurred. On top of that, a red orb appeared and began to rapidly increase in size.
“It is the Orb of Destruction.”
This was an attack spell I had never heard of in the game, and rightfully so. This invention was the Fallen Scholar’s signature spell, every part of it his, right down to the formula.
He said it was rank two?

My heart squeezed. I knew just how much of a punch top-tier attack magic could pack. Of course, that didn’t really mean anything. Even if I didn’t know that, I would have been able to guess roughly how dangerous that spell was when I saw their reaction.

“You deranged old man! Are you going to kill me too!?” The wolf bastard shuddered at the orb in the sky and attempted to flee. Even Clown seemed to be in a similar state. He was shouting something in the distance, looking gobsmacked. I couldn’t hear what he was saying, but it wasn’t difficult to infer, because the corpse army located on the outskirts was retreating.
God damn it.
They were the Fallen Scholar’s comrades, and they had determined that if that spell fell here, everything would disappear without a trace, friend or foe. But, so what?
“I’ll stop it, so you guys keep going!”
I fought through my anxiety and focused on clearing the way for now. “What are you doing?! Don’t just stand there and keep moving!”
“B-But if that thing falls...!”
“And where will you run? Fight!”
Now, without even needing me to say anything, the adventurers all encouraged each other and bolstered their fighting spirit.
“It’s coming...!”
I raised my head at someone’s whimper. Already, the ominous orb that had grown large enough to fill the entire sky was falling vertically toward the ground.
[Kyle Pevrosk has cast the rank-three attack spell Piercing Steel.]
At that moment, Kyle completed the spell needed to mark the Fallen Scholar.
Shaaaaaa!
He must have drawn the magic circle in advance to prepare for this, as an intense gray light burst from behind us.
Flash!
When the momentary flash of light faded, a giant arrow pierced the massive meteorite.
Kabooom! Shaaa!
There was a deafening explosion. A strong gust of wind tore across the earth.
“R-Run!”
Hundreds of large and small flaming rocks poured down like rain. The adventurers fled, scared out of their wits, but not many of the fragments touched the ground. This was also thanks to Kyle.
Bang! BOOM! Bang, bang, bang!

The falling rubble was blocked by a translucent barrier, and upon touching it, the hundreds of shards exploded and disappeared in the air. Even a rank-three wizard could not spread a shield over such a wide area, though.
Did he contain them all?
Reading the trajectory of all the shards, he had successfully blocked each one with minimal mana. That would be the most logical explanation. Raven was watching the sight with her mouth wide open.

“Is that... possible...?” As a wizard herself, she was likely even more acutely aware of just how high-level the technique she had just seen in action was. But unfortunately, the opposing wizard was not an ordinary one, either. No, rather, the Fallen Scholar was a Great Sorcerer considered even more powerful than Kyle.
“Damn old man.”
The falling meteorites broke off and adjusted their orbits, avoiding the barrier and hitting the ground.
Boom!

The meteorites did not discriminate between friend and foe. Whether at the center of the zombie army Clown had unleashed or behind and to the side of me after crushing my comrades, they then took the shapes of golems and stood up.
The rank-five summon spell, Fire Giant.
“Mr. Pevrosk!” Raven shouted incredulously. “How did this happen? There wasn’t any kind of summoning circle...!”
“He used his remaining mana to create and bestow a new formula on the boulders that remained.”
“A rank-five spell, in that short moment... and dozens of them...?” Raven murmured with a mix of shock and admiration.
However, Kyle didn’t appear to have the luxury of kindly answering her questions. “Yandel! I need to prepare for the next attack, so take care of the rest!” The transmission abruptly cut off.
Whew, he said he’ll take care of the Fallen Scholar, but I guess clean-up is my job. Well, even that guy can’t possibly take on a monster like that by himself.
Not to mention Kyle had used Mass Teleport on the first floor and was low on mana. I was beginning to realize we were still at a disadvantage.

Melter Fend was in charge of Blue Mane, Kyle had volunteered to take on the Fallen Scholar, and I was leading hundreds of adventurers in an assault against Corpse Collector. The moment one of these three sides lost, it was game over. Our precarious balance would collapse and everyone would be annihilated in an instant. But, in other words, the same went for our opponents.
Slide.
I charged at the Fire Giant, who had fully stood up and was looking down at me, a gigantic mace in its hand.
Dash.
I Leaped high and used some of my precious MP as I brought down my mace. One strike was enough to destroy the core of a rank-five Fire Giant summon.
Kwaaang!
The Fire Giant turned into mana particles and drifted away. I turned my attention to what was beyond that. In the distance, I could see Clown.
Still laughing, that bastard.
If I could just kill him, I’d have the advantage. Step by step, I walked forward slowly, crushing, stomping, and at times shoving corpses away with my shield.
Crunch!
I was paving the way for our survival.
Shaaaaaa!
From the sky, a rain of fire summoned by the Fallen Scholar was falling nonstop.
Kablam!
Kyle diligently applied defense magic and fought back fiercely, but it wasn’t enough to block all of it.
“Aaaaaah!” Screams sounded from everywhere. Bodies that had chased survival desperately enough to get all the way here collapsed on the damp ground, as charred as charcoal.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Puppet.]
Then, in that state, they stood up and swung their weapons at us. At the sight, I couldn’t help but think if there was a hell somewhere in this mortal realm, perhaps it was right here.
Bang!

A pile of corpses shot out like a cannonball from somewhere in the distance and broke our formation. This was a change that had occurred a few minutes ago. Corpse Collector had started pulling out more summons from the sub-space.
Damn it, I thought we were almost there too. Just how many has he stocked up?

Curses filled my mind, but even still, my feet did not stop moving. Although I was already far removed from the main forces and surrounded by the corpse army, I kept moving forward. I didn’t know how many people were left. Many had likely died.
“Behelaaah!” But despite that, when Ainar cut down a corpse and cried out, echoing chants sounded from all directions.
“Yes, Behelaaah!” That wasn’t a barbarian. Humans, dwarves, and even beastpeople shouted along. Yes, there was a certain addictiveness to it.
Boom!
A pile of five conjoined corpses flew in and got to their feet in front of me. Frowning at their grotesque appearance for a moment, I quickly located a familiar face in the pile.
Hansen Calders.

This was a man I had met while wandering the passageway on the first day. That was before I even ran into Clown, when I didn’t realize what had happened yet. At that time, he had offered to join forces and I had declined because I couldn’t trust him.
“It’s the careful man who lives the longest. I hope to meet again someday.”
Even though he had been rejected, the man had smiled as he left.
“Gruhhh...”
This is how we meet again... So he really was on our side.

Hansu Lee would have thrown up everything in his stomach just from laying eyes on this gruesome sight. Swinging my mace toward it, I thought to myself, What if I had trusted him back then? And what if we did travel together... Would he be fighting on our side instead of the enemy’s?
Crunch!

Yeah, possibly. Only one thing was for sure. I had been wrong back then. The decision I had made wasn’t even the best option there was. I hadn’t made an effort to figure out if he was trustworthy, making the excuse that he was a stranger. If I had put more work in, I might’ve found reliable evidence that I could.
“I’m sorry.” Stepping on the pile of corpses, I sprinted forward. As I did, another thought struck me. I wonder what kind of person he was. If he was alive, what could he have done?

There was no way of knowing anymore. He might have possessed an extraordinary potential that could have been of great help to me. Even Dwalkie’s first impression had just been so-so. At first, I thought he was a weirdo. But in reality, he had been the kindest one of all of us and the greatest wizard of any I have ever seen.
I shook off those thoughts at the sound of Kyle’s voice. “Yandel, how much farther?”
“Not long now.”

It truly wasn’t long. Just a little farther and I would reach Clown, although he was an Agile Poison Necromancer so close combat wouldn’t be all that easy. Even so, necromancers had an obvious weakness. Besides, after summoning an opposing army of this size, the amount of MP he’d burned through would be no joke. As long as Kyle kept the Fallen Scholar in check and Fend held down that wolf bastard, this shouldn’t go off the rails.
“Please move a little faster. Something doesn’t feel right.”
Doesn’t feel right? Is this another case of wizard’s intuition?
With that thought in mind, I was about to swing my mace again.
“Gruhhh...!” From between the corpses with rotten breath, a group of strange adventurers appeared. One team, two teams, three teams... Too many to count.
“We came to see what the fuss was all about, but what is this...?”
“We’ll help too!”
“Survivors from Rafdonia! Kill them!”
“Woahhh!”
They were adventurers from Noark who had been hunting on the second floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 227: Reversal (3)
paragraphs: Takelan Arvenon could not believe this.
What am I doing?

He was swinging a sword. With all the strength he had left in his body, he moved his arms to kill the enemies in front of him. Even still, he constantly asked himself why. His most precious wife was dead, so why should he live?
In response to that question, the barbarian had answered, “Because someone needs to deliver the news.”
“Yes, I forgot about that...”

In a state of desperation, Takelan had embarked on this arduous journey because of those words. To tell bereaved families what had happened? He knew very well that wasn’t the real reason. The barbarian, unlike him, had managed to protect everything important to him.
“I repeat! Everyone stop!” Shouting like an unwavering fool, he had prevented a senseless tragedy.
“I am the commander of Clan Nartel, Melter Fend.”
“I’m Lacey Nareth of Heindel Church.”
“I’m a battle mage from Rafdonia.”
He had been recognized by renowned adventurers.
“Behelaaah!”

And, leading this arduous journey from the most dangerous position in the forefront, the great barbarian had brought them to their destination. This man was a born leader. Just as Takelan had first thought, he had the power to move people.
But because of that, Takelan had wanted to see this great man collapse in despair after losing something precious to him.

Only that would be able to ease his pain even a little. Yeah, it was inevitable. Even that man couldn’t do it. It was only natural that he couldn’t save all of these people. With a sickening motive of seeking comfort through another person’s misfortune, Takelan had tagged along on this journey.
Slice!
Yes, that had been the case, but now he was wielding his sword to save people other than himself.
“Ah, thank you. It was Takelan, right?”
He didn’t reply.
“You’re a quiet guy.”
As someone who had recently lost his comrades of numerous years, here he was, fighting with all his might for someone he had never met before. Takelan couldn’t understand it at all.
Slice!
Why am I still fighting? Because I haven’t seen that barbarian’s despair yet? No. But if not that, why?
“Ha, reinforcements, in a situation like this?”
“We’re going to die, huh?”
“Ha, this is driving me crazy. And we came all this way.”
“Enough small talk, fight!”
“Yes, I refuse to die like this!”
How were these people still fighting to the bitter end even while predicting their own deaths?
“Woahhh!”
Glancing around at the looks in these adventurers’ eyes, Takelan soon realized the reason.
Kaboom!
Beyond the place where constant explosions rang out, the place where numerous enemies were flocking from, a giant man was fighting, still clinging to hope.
“Behelaaah!”
The situation was grim, but the grimmer it got, the more I noticed the positives.
Equipment is second or third-floor level.

There were a lot of them, but their strength was considerably lacking. Well, if they were talented enough, they would have headed upstairs a long time ago. The dredges of Noark attacked us alongside the corpse army, but it didn’t make much of a difference to us right away. At our level, a single corpse summoned by Clown was more threatening than these guys.
The only problem is that it’s going to take a little longer to clear the way.

That was the most troublesome thing. Time was not on our side. If we wanted to have a chance at winning, we had to fuck up Clown and then gang up on Blue Mane or Fallen Scholar as soon as possible. These assholes from Noark showing up now of all times?
The rear will collapse at this rate...
More and more time was running out. As impatience surged through me, I gripped my mace tighter.
Crunch!
Once again, it was a one-shot kill.
“Ahhh!”

Even as I cut through the enemy, even at this moment, the number of allies I had was decreasing. In the face of death, people were more truthful than ever. Some cried out for their families and proclaimed their love, some cursed the king, and some even revealed things they never would have otherwise.
“Look... at your face... Hey, I’m an evil spirit.”
“...What? W-What are you—?!”
“Sorry for lying... Thanks for every—cough! Finally, home... a-ahh, Mom... I’m late...”
Yeah, there was no way there weren’t players among all these people.
Thump!
It occurred to me that nothing about this made sense. We had overcome all that adversity to get here. Was it going to end in vain like this?
No, it can’t.

I pulled together my crumbling heart. I could let it break later after I collapsed. My arms and legs were still moving, after all. Until my lungs finally stopped breathing and my blood finally ran cold, it was only right to keep struggling again and again.
Crunch!
Swinging my mace, I thought to myself, just like I did on the first day I got here, What do I need to do to survive? First, take stock of the situation.
“Kyle! How are things on your side?”
“We’re managing to hold on so far but it’s not looking good.”

It seemed there had been a significant amount of damage at the rear where the wizards, archers, and long-rangers were gathered. I supposed that was only natural. I was sure the adventurers from Noark had ambushed their forces as well. Since most of the warriors were on my team, it must have been difficult to handle their assault.
I guess we’re surrounded on all sides.

Surprisingly, there was an escape route: the portal we rode up. Kyle hadn’t mentioned it for morale reasons, but I was sure some people had escaped down to the first floor with it. Running away was always an attractive option, especially if your life was at stake.
“Yandel, how about heading down and regrouping a bit?” a warrior shouted to me, offering advice.

Did Kyle hear that through the message stone? “Absolutely not. We’ll have to come back up again to avoid Berzak, and these guys won’t be so kind as to give us time to get in formation again,” Kyle said firmly, shutting down any ridiculous ideas.

And it was a ridiculous idea because I hadn’t even considered it an option in the first place. There was a difference between zero and one. If my and Kyle’s assessments were correct, no matter how you looked at it, this was the one—our shot at survival. We had to end the battle here, whatever it took.
“How is Melter Fend doing?” I asked about another battlefront that could potentially turn the tides, for better or for worse.
The response I got this time wasn’t optimistic either. “He’s handling him well, but it seems a quick victory will be difficult.”
In that case...
“Bjorn!” I turned in surprise and saw a suicide soldier had approached within arm’s length of me. “Dertu Teiran!” Thankfully, Raven used Gust to push it away.
Pop!
The soldier exploded with a loud sound. The other corpses weren’t really affected, but the same couldn’t be said for the adventurers from Noark who had arrived as reinforcements.
Chhhhhh!

Those nearby melted into pools of acid on the spot. As for the rest, just one drop of its bodily fluids was enough to turn their faces white and make them stumble. It left a bitter taste in my mouth. Rafdonia or Noark—they both treated people like consumables just the same.
“Then what about the Fallen Scholar?” I continued the conversation without taking a moment to catch my breath. This was information that could be critical right now. “Can you kill him?”

“Now that the magic circle is complete, I’ll try. But...” Kyle trailed off. It seemed he wasn’t confident. “I’m sorry. I thought I had caught up to him, but the gap between us has widened since then.”

I had no intention of blaming him. If this guy had left through one of those portals yesterday, we wouldn’t have gotten this far in the first place. Besides, the Fallen Scholar was a ridiculously powerful wizard even by my standards.
“But as I said, I should be able to buy some time. I’ll make sure to deal a blow in that time, whatever it takes. Even at the cost of my life.” Those words suddenly reminded me of Dwalkie.
“Are you referring to that Awakening spell?”
“...Something like that.”
“Will you be all right?”

“If I was afraid of the consequences, I wouldn’t have stayed in the labyrinth in the first place. This is a moment I’ve been longing for. And since I’ve been improving this technique for a long time now, there’s no guarantee I’ll lose my life.”
“...I see.” I didn’t offer up empty platitudes and say there was no need for him to do that. Not only was that just pretense, but who here was not fighting with their life on the line right now?
“Ahhh!”
Even I was. If I dropped dead right now, people would be sad but not surprised. That was the war we were waging.
“Then what will you do now?”
I laughed at Kyle’s cautious question. Did he really have to ask that?
“It might be better for you to come back and fight here instead—”

“No need,” I said firmly, cutting him off. Although we were being driven back now that Noark’s adventurers had arrived as reinforcements, I answered, “The plan remains the same.” Kyle Pevrosk had the Fallen Scholar, and Melter Fend had that wolf bastard. “We will take on the Corpse Collector.”
“I thought you would say that.” I could hear a chuckle through the message stone.
“Why do you laugh? Do you think we can’t do it?”
“No, that’s not what I meant. I just remembered something you said earlier. You said warriors laugh when they’re tired. Please add wizards to that too.”
Hmm, us warriors laughed a little more energetically than that. “Maybe if you give me a more manly laugh next time.”

“Next time, huh?” Ah, maybe this wasn’t an appropriate time for a joke. I momentarily regretted it, but before long, a much lighter voice rang out from the stone. “Yes, having a next time to look forward to isn’t a bad thing. You know something? If I get back, I’m going to start writing a book. A book about my life. It was my childhood dream.”
“I’ll read it if I get a chance.”
“It would be an honor. Oh, if I do write the book, can I quote you in it?”
“Quote what?”
“That thing you said, that warriors laugh when they’re tired. Oddly, those words keep lingering in the back of my head.”
Uh, I just said that without thinking.
I felt a bit embarrassed about how seriously he was taking all that. But there was little I wasn’t willing to agree to if we could only get back home. “Write it or not, do as you please.”
Kyle laughed out loud at my answer. “Haha, is that so? Then this will be a breeze.” It was a much more cheerful laugh than before.

The current structure of the battle was a bit complicated. First, the expedition’s long-range damage dealer line was concentrated around the portal. Warriors were shielding them nearby. At first, we’d only had to fend off the corpse army at the front, but we had to change formation because adventurers from Noark ambushed us from behind.
Those guys must be going through hell too.

As I regrouped, Fend and his clan members were in the middle of the battlefield raiding Blue Mane. I was sure they were having as arduous a time as us. Since we were also currently separated from the main team to capture Corpse Collector, you could call us a kind of detached unit. With that in mind, it was time for a mid-way check-up.
“Raven! How many people?”
“Pardon? Oh, I think there are about forty!”
Geez, a lot have died. I’m pretty sure there were more than a hundred of us at first.
Shaaaaaa!
Just then, a light burst from the ground. A giant red magic circle covered the entire battlefield in an instant.
“...It’s a spatial magic formula!” Raven was the first to read the formula, but that was all she managed to figure out.
Kyle’s calm voice rang out from the message stone. “Don’t be startled. It was bound to happen at some point.”
“Then the plan is still on track?”
“Yes, I knew that old man would use this spell.”

I was relieved by that. Apparently, if the Fallen Scholar used spatial magic, Kyle could turn the guy’s mana against him to cast another spell. That was the basic gist, but I didn’t really get the details since I wasn’t a wizard. This wasn’t an ability that had been implemented in the game, either. It must have been a limitation of the 2D game format.
I should get ready too.
Either way, I had to keep moving under the assumption that it would work. Otherwise, there was nothing else we could do.
Shaaaaaa!
Soon, the light shining from the magic circle reached its peak and everything in sight turned pure white. Right at that moment, I heard Kyle’s voice once more. “I’ll be back.”
Flash!
A dazzling flash covered the battlefield.
[Kyle Pevrosk has cast the rank-two spacetime spell Parallel Universe.]
There was a ringing in my ears. When I opened my eyes, the battlefield appeared in my blurry vision, unchanged. “Kyle, did it work?” I asked, clipped.

There was no answer. That must have meant the spell was successful. Right about now, Kyle would be initiating a one-on-one fight with the Fallen Scholar in a pocket dimension that looked like the Goblin Forest.
I hope he comes back victorious... but I’ll have to prepare for the other possibility.
Kyle thought he could at least buy some time. So at that time, we had to do something on our end as well.
“What are you all doing?! Run!”

After stopping for a moment at the pure white flash, I led the detached unit once again and continued charging. Without attacks from the Fallen Scholar flying in at every moment, the march was much easier.
This should be enough.

After who knows how long, we finally reached our destination. There was no need to risk our lives breaking through these guys anymore. I entrusted the detached unit to Teterud, who had been clearing the way with me. “Teterud, you take the rest back now.”
“Then I’ll leave him to you.” The path was already cleared and we had said everything that needed to be said.
“Did you hear that? We’re stopping here and going back!”
“But that doesn’t look all that easy, either.”
“Well, I’m sure Yandel will take care of this part!”
“Let’s go!”

Soon, Teterud withdrew the remaining group back to where Fend was. The initial charge might have been difficult, but I was sure they’d make it over there. And as long as they did, they would be able to help in catching the wolf too.
“Come on, everyone, get on me.”
As soon as I said that, Missha quickly jumped up and landed on my Giantized shoulder. “Are we rrreally going alone?”
Then came Ainar. She didn’t fit on my shoulder so I wrapped my left arm around her waist. “Oh! I can see why Aruru rides on top of me now!”
“Please excuse me.” Getting down from Iradun, who disappeared as his summon ended, Raven sat on Missha’s lap.
“...This feels very strange.” The biggest, Mr. Bear, wrapped his arms around my neck and hung on.
“Now it really feels like we’re one team!” Finally, Erwen sat on my right shoulder.
Ha, now I’d really become a means of transportation.
Just as I was about to leave, Daria stopped me. “Wait.”

I had a guess as to what she was going to say so I decided to cut her off at the pass. “As I said before, I can’t let Erwen stay behind.” No matter how much she pulled the older sister card, I couldn’t give her up. Erwen was the key to pulling this strategy off.
“That’s not it. I’m coming too.”
“What?”
So you are capable of guilt.
“...What’s with that look?”
“Nothing. Come here.” I extended my remaining arm and wrapped it around Daria’s waist.
“Geuuu...!”
“Kill him! Kill him and it’s over!”

In addition to Clown, amateur second-floor adventurers from Noark were quickly gathering. I bent my knees slightly and looked forward. More than a hundred adventurers from Noark stood between me and Clown, and an even greater number of corpses were lined up.
It looks like about sixty yards.
Checking the distance one more time, I bent my knees even more like I was pressing down on a spring. “Hold tight.” This time, instead of jumping low, I jumped as hard as I could.
[You have cast Leap.]
My body flew up in an instant and the entire battlefield unfolded beneath me.
“Flying! I’m flying!”

Fend was raiding the wolf in a siege formation. Teterud was running in that direction. Our main forces were gathered in the center. The finishing stroke was that Clown bastard, who was cackling at me from a safe spot in the distance.
“U-Uh...” The moment I reached my peak height, someone pulled my hair as hard as they could. Geez, I’d need to make a handle on my armor for next time.
“Kyaaa!”
I flew in a parabola and quickly crashed back down to the earth. Clown, who was sitting on top of a corpse monster, spotted me and turned his summoned beast around.
You think that’s going to work now? If you’re going to attempt a hit-and-run, try harder.
Crashhh!
I slammed down on the ground like a cannonball.
[Your total weight is over 1100 lbs. Special terrain effect Recoil is applied to your blast radius.]

Due to Recoil, the remnants of Noark and the corpse soldiers nearby all flew into the air at once, except for the corpse monster Clown was riding on. Its weight must have exceeded my 1,100 pounds because it didn’t even budge. Of course, this was just a minor issue.

“I didn’t think you had the essence of a Manticore. Pshehe!” Clown still looked unconcerned as he met my eyes. Rather, he looked to be enjoying this. If I could, I wanted to exchange a few words with him, but I hurriedly ended Giantization. My body shrunk in an instant.
“Kyaaa!”
As he watched the comrades who were clinging onto me fall off, Clown spoke in an exaggerated tone. “Oh, dear! Did you run out of MP? And you just managed to make it this far. What a shame.”
Yeah, right. Well, once I give him a good roughing up, I’m sure he’ll stop with that stupid voice.
“Erwen.”
“Ah, yes!” As soon as her name was called, Erwen cast her special ability.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Elementalization.]

Elementalization was the special ability of the rank-five monster Evan, and a skill that was quite unique even in Dungeon and Stone. Its effects were simple. The caster essentially turned into a spirit and became temporarily immune to physical damage.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has proposed a contract with you.]
Then they could contract with one other person to temporarily share multiple abilities.
“Mister, hold my hand.” Her voice sounded not of this world. Like a man possessed, I grabbed Erwen’s outstretched hand. And just then—
Whoosh!
A powerful flame burst from her hand and swallowed my body whole as if to protect me. Elemental Barbarian (Fire) Mode.
“Erwen, turn off the fire.”
“...Pardon? Oh, right!”
Only just remembering the instructions I gave her, Erwen quickly changed attributes.
Crackkk!
My already thick skin cracked like dry dirt and became thicker.

[The Spirit of the Earth now dwells in your body. Damage received from Fire attribute attacks is reduced by half. Damage received from Water attribute attacks is doubled. Poison immunity bonus. When using blunt weapons, the Strength effect is added to attacks. Your Physical Resistance has increased significantly.]
A real man chose rock.

chapters.title: Chapter 228: Reversal (4)
paragraphs: In Dungeon and Stone, there were several essences that were better suited for certain races. A typical example was the Elementalization skill Erwen had just used. When used by a human who had no spirits to summon, all it did was turn them into an attribute-less spirit. A skill buff was also added to Elemental and Natural Power, which were stats that allowed the user to manage spirits. In truth, this essence was for elf-only use.
Rustle...
Every time I moved my arm, flecks of dirt fell from me. It was as if I’d become a rock giant. Oh, but “giant” wasn’t really the right word, though.
Ha, I wanna use Giantization so bad right now.
It was a pity I wouldn’t get to see that magnificent sight, but it couldn’t be helped.
Dash.
I let go of my disappointment and sprinted forward.

“Kweeek!” At that moment, the corpse monster that Clown was riding on spat venom from its mouth. Without lifting a shield, I took it with my body. Elemental Barbarian (Earth) Mode was immune to poison.

“Oh, I forgot about that effect.” It looked like this bastard had beaten the game on cheat mode because it was only now that he realized the state I was in. However, he was still relaxed. “Okay, you used your brain a bit. Pshehe.” Even though his main ability—poison damage—had been rendered useless, Clown was still laughing. Well, he would. This guy wasn’t just a Poison Necromancer but an Agile Poison Necromancer.
Dash.

The bastard got off the corpse monster he was riding and retreated. I was also running at full speed, but the distance between us was still widening. This was because of the price attached to Elemental Barbarian (Earth) Mode.
[Your Agility-related stats have significantly decreased.]
It felt like my body was moving at half speed. In truth, this was the biggest downside, not the doubled Water damage or drastic reduction in Mana Resistance.
“What? Didn’t take this into account?” When poison became useless, Clown gave up on close combat and started maintaining a distance, something a proud person would never do.
I didn’t turn off Giantization for nothing.
Seriously, a top-tier adventurer with the nickname of Corpse Collector was running away from a rank-five barbarian?
Thought you’d do that, asshole. Leap.
I muttered the name of the skill in my head and kicked off the ground.
“Kyaaa!” As she was unable to stray more than five yards from me in spirit form, Erwen was dragged along with me. That ended up being unfortunate.
I should consider the maximum distance as thirty yards.

I calmly assessed my current state of affairs. Considering I had once been able to jump seventy yards even in Giantization mode, the distance had drastically reduced. It was hitting me how heavy this body really was. I weighed less than half as much when using Giantization. Still, the speed of the jump itself was similar.
“Behelahhh!” Activating my transportation ability, I narrowed the distance between us in an instant.
Kaboom!

The ground undulated around the landing place. The effect itself was the same as before, but there was an obvious difference. The corpse monster’s massive body hadn’t even budged earlier, but this time...
“Gueeek?” It couldn’t take the shock and got thrown into the air.
[Your total weight is over one ton.]
Yeah, looks like I’m heavier than you now.

Clown was scrawny, so he wasn’t even worth mentioning. His body floated up mid-backstep. Before he could land on the ground, I waddle-ran to close the distance and then took up the kind of stance one would use to swing a baseball bat.
At that moment, my eyes met his in mid-air. He no longer looked to be smiling. Geez, that hurt my feelings. “Crack a smile,” I demanded. He didn’t reply.
Well, if you really don’t want to, I’ll crack you instead.
Whooom!
I swung my mace with perfect timing and enough momentum to split the bastard’s skull. Just then, thick bones sprouted from his skin.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Bone Armor.]

This was the ability that had blocked Mr. Bear’s ultimate finisher with no difficulty, but I wasn’t too worried about it. Outlaw of the Wilderness was still activated, and paired with Elemental Barbarian (Earth)‘s destructive blunt weapon buff and a Swing containing the soul of an Ogre on top of that. With all that synergy, it was impossible to stop this attack, even with a rank-four skill.
Crackkk!
The moment the mace touched it, his Bone Armor shattered like a nut getting cracked with a hammer, revealing the soft skin underneath.
“Erwen!”
Erwen, who was flying next to me in spirit form, fired a flaming arrow. The target was, as always, right between the brows.
Kwaaang!
The flaming arrow sunk into his mask and exploded, but that mask appeared to be some kind of piece of equipment too. The first hit was blocked and did not deliver much damage.
Tap.
Clown went flying back from the force of the explosion, then found his balance and landed. And at that moment...
Shatter.
Fine fissures like spider webs spread across the mask before it cracked into pieces. As I took him in, I smirked.
So, that’s what you look like.
“Ugly as hell.”
If that little dragon Penn had gotten to see this face, she would’ve freaked out. But did that trigger him?

“You stupid NPC bastards, you don’t know anything!” I got high praise in response to my comment. The bastard was no longer putting on a clown act. Abandoning his exaggerated tone, he spoke like your run-of-the-mill asshole adventurer. “Don’t think I’ll give you a quick death.”
Huh, that Dragon Slayer son of a bitch had said the same thing. He’d yammered something like, “Even death can’t save you.”
“I’ll bestow unimaginable pain on you.”
Was this kind of dialogue popular in Orcules? I wasn’t sure, but our epic battle soon continued. I wouldn’t have expected anything less.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Puppet.]

A necromancer’s true worth lay in battles of numbers, but the majority of the corpse army was fighting the main team and a lot of them were dead. This bastard wouldn’t have much MP left, either. More importantly, I had a more advantageous combo going for me too.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Curse of Stone.]
A curse skill that prevented someone from charging at you? While the skill’s attribute was Earth, too, it was pointless.
Yeah, I’m an Elemental Barbarian now.
Even despite the drastic reduction in my Mana Resistance stat, Earth Resistance easily ensured immunity against attacks like that.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Bone Armor.]
I countered Bone Armor with Swing.
Crunch!
Each time a shell was peeled off, Erwen, who was in spirit form next to me, shot an arrow.
Thunk!
Damage steadily accumulated as the battle continued.

“Gruhhh!” Clown began taking out high-level zombies with high individual combat power from sub-space to attack Erwen. This was an excellent move. If Erwen received a certain amount of damage, Elemental Barbarian Mode would also be undone. From that point on, poison damage would come my way as well.
Okay, so no mage?

His summons strictly specialized in poison and physical damage, so they couldn’t harm Erwen, who had immunity to physical damage. Well, some elite zombies with elemental weapons popped up from time to time...
Crunch!
But I crushed them before they got too close. Of course, it was difficult for me to block all of them by myself. But I wasn’t here alone, you see.
“Dertu Teiran!” Raven pushed away the enemies with Gust spells, and if that didn’t work, deployed a Mana Shield to protect Erwen.
In terms of usefulness, wizards can’t be beaten.
The rest of the group followed from a distance and focused on protecting Raven. It was perfect teamwork where everyone was watching each other’s backs.
“How long do you think you can hold out!?” Spitting out bloody saliva, the bastard continued to provide rave reviews of our work, but his words contained a threat I couldn’t laugh off.
This weasel-like son of a bitch.

The battle itself seemed to be unfolding in our favor, but it was our side that was in a hurry. Even if we minimized the amount of damage Erwen took, in time, Elemental Barbarian Mode would inevitably end. Besides, I didn’t know how long Kyle would be able to hold out.
Whew, I need to end this before Fallen Scholar returns.

As time passed, our urgency increased. My Physical Resistance had risen from turning into an Earth-attribute barbarian, but my Mana Resistance had decreased proportionally. Erwen or not, my actual body wouldn’t be able to withstand a proper magical blow, especially if it was a Water-attribute attack that dealt double damage. Honestly, if it weren’t for the Fallen Scholar’s existence in the first place, we could have gotten all the way here on our own, without the need for a detached unit of over a hundred people.
“...The corpses are retreating!”

To make matters worse, the bastard began putting nearby zombies into sub-space one by one. This was a very big problem. However, it did come with the advantage of lessening the burden on my comrades following behind me.
Hack!
The Bone Armor, which I used to be able to crush in one blow, could now withstand up to two hits. This was because the increased damage I was dealing thanks to Outlaw of the Wilderness had depleted.
“So, was that it?” Damn player bastards. I had kept a tight lid on it yet he’d still noticed. Clown’s eyes curled into a smile.
“Don’t laugh. You look ugly.”
“...When this is all over, the first thing I’ll do is pull out that tongue of yours.”
Try to, if you can.

“Behelahhh!” I let out a yell and shoved against him even harder. The resistance was fierce. It seemed he had finally acknowledged me as an enemy since he activated an essence the public didn’t know about.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Ephemeral Immortality.]
This was the skill of a rank-four monster, Death Lord.
Whoosh!
The bastard’s clothing was promptly swallowed up in black flames and his skin burned off until only bones remained, leaving him with the appearance of a Lich.
No wonder he had no armor.

I’d feared this, but to think he would actually have this skill... The way Ephemeral Immortality worked was really simple. When you used it, no matter what you did, you couldn’t die for one minute, and your Spirit and Special Ability stats were converted to Physique stats.
A high-level adventurer with stats focused on physique...
I spoke calmly, even as I gulped. “You look much better now.”
The guy didn’t even respond, just rattled his bony jaw and rushed toward me.
Bang!

It was a simple push, that was all, but my body, which had even launched that massive corpse monster into the air with Recoil, got shoved back. Whew, just how high was his Strength stat? The fortunate thing was that I didn’t take any damage thanks to Physical Resistance.
God damn it.
However, my comrades were a different story. It was only logical that one regular hit with that monster-like body would easily knock them over.
“Everyone, get back!”
In an instant, my goals became the complete opposite of what they were. Instead of stopping him from running away, I now had to block him.
Dash.
Clown shoved me aside and charged forward like a bull. The distance narrowed truly in the blink of an eye. This was like a max-level Skeleton.
Dash.
I quickly caught up with Leap.
Bang!

As I landed, the bastard bounced up with Recoil, but that didn’t even buy us time. Even though I’d timed the landing perfectly, he easily pushed me off within a second and continued his charge. And that instant was enough for something to go wrong.
“Miss Ainar!”
As she blocked his fist with her adamantium greatsword, Ainar toppled over and collided with Mr. Bear.
Bang!

Missha took a blow to the stomach and went down hard. Raven rushed to raise a stone wall with magic, but it shattered with a single punch. It was all too clear what this guy’s objective was. He must have been planning to use his limited time to defeat the most bothersome member of our party—the wizard.
“Protect Raven!” I shouted, activating Leap. At the exact same time, the bastard ignored Missha and ran forward again.
Boom!
With one punch, our tank-summoned beast Iron Bear was reverse-summoned.

“Kyaa!” Raven, who had been riding on Iron Bear, hung in the air for a breathless moment. The fist swung again before she could even land on the ground, but Mr. Bear pulled her behind him just in time.
Kwaaang!

I landed on the ground and the bastard was sent flying up again. In the meantime, I used Giantization and got on top of my fallen comrades. Realizing what I was trying to do, Mr. Bear and Daria rushed under me.
Bang! Bang!
At that moment, the bastard landed on my back like he was trying to stomp me into dust.
Are these guys okay?
No, I don’t think so. And I honestly thought this would be enough. Plan B.

I changed my mind in less than five seconds, quickly got up, and punched him in the head with my fist. I guessed he hadn’t expected the blow because it sent him toppling back despite his weighty frame. Yeah, the best defense was a good offense. I dove on top of him.

“Behelahhh!” I pressed him down with my overwhelming weight and he took it. But it seemed Elemental Barbarian’s weight was a lot even for him as he had a tough time pushing me off. How much longer now?
“...Damn barbarian.”
So, it’s finally over. Ha, I thought we were all going to die.
At the sight of his naked body, flesh now covering the bones, I smirked. “How small.” It would be a lie to say I didn’t feel sympathy for him, but feelings like that didn’t have a place here.
Dash.
I immediately ran forward and swung my mace at him. As expected, Bone Armor burst forth.
Crunch!

Since I was using Giantization, it was destroyed in one blow. Erwen also didn’t miss the opportunity to shoot an arrow. Although she aimed for the head, the bastard rolled over and avoided it like the agility character he was. However, the arrow hit his leg dead-on.
Nice.
Now that there was a hole in his leg, that cockroach should slow down. I quickly sprinted forward again. That was the moment.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has ended.]
My MP ran out and my body shrank. Well, it was about time, since I’d used Leap and Swing a lot. That wasn’t a problem, though. It looked like this bastard was almost out of mana too.
“Mister, all the corpses near the portal fell over!”
He’d maintained that zombie army using Puppet even while fighting us, but now he’d turned it off? That showed just how cornered he was.
Just a few more hits now.

I ran toward the bastard as he scurried away like a rat. There was no Leap this time, but it unfolded similarly to the battle thus far. When he was caught mid-run, Bone Armor. Once I whacked it several times with my mace, Erwen shot an arrow. Things went on like that for a while.
Just how big is his pool of MP?
I’d just managed to catch up to him once more and was about to start macing his Bone Armor when—
“Ah-ah, Yandel. Can you hear me?” Good news and bad news came at once. “Blue Mane has been eliminated. We’ll come help you soon.”
Melter Fend and his clanmates had finally succeeded in their raid against Wolf Man. The disappearance of the corpse army was probably a major contributing factor. This was great news.
“And one more thing. I think... Sir Kyle has lost.” But Kyle had been defeated. “Be careful. The Fallen Scholar may come to you.”
Fend’s warning ended up being pointless, though, because he was already here. “Haha, Mr. Necrapeto. You’re looking in a bad way.”
God damn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 229: Reversal (5)
paragraphs: Crack!

Another layer of Bone Armor was torn off, revealing Clown’s face, which was full of bewilderment. In my experience, this expression was no different than a signal that a long fight was coming to an end. However, the moment I was about to bring down my mace with all my might, a cool breeze blew toward me from somewhere to the side.
Whip!
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has exceeded her damage threshold. Elementalization has deactivated.]
My body grew lighter before I could even register the change. In no time, my rock-like skin was back to its original state. My hearing was on a hair trigger like an alert animal.
Slump.
I heard something drop to the ground behind me.

“Erwen!” An urgent cry from Daria quickly followed. That was enough to infer what was going on. Erwen had been hit, so Elemental Barbarian Mode had ended. But if that was the case, what had hit her? Before I could even turn my head in the direction of that first gust of wind, I caught sight of the answer.
“Haha, Mr. Necrapeto. You’re looking in a bad way.” He was an elderly man with the appearance of an archetypical wizard: lush gray hair, a white beard, and kind-looking features.
Fallen Scholar.
He was here.
Already? How? What happened to Kyle?
The moment I was faced with that fact, numerous questions popped into my mind.
Slide.
I tried my best to rid myself of them and moved my arm. It was an unconscious decision made in the blink of an eye.
If not now... I won’t have any other opportunities.
Elemental Barbarian Mode was now over. Since I could no longer block poison damage, if I let this opportunity pass me by, I’d have to face both Clown and this old man at the same time.
“You’re in a hurry.”
God damn it.
The strength left my left arm and my mace fell to the ground.
Boom!
A red light penetrated my wrist.
I’m actually going to lose my mind. What kind of crazy hit...?

There had been no casting time needed. That meant that to Fallen Scholar, the spell he’d used just now was no different from a basic attack spell like Magic Arrow. And a regular hit of that caliber had pierced my body when Elemental Barbarian mode was over and my Mana Resistance was back?
No, think later.

I once again shook off my questions, because they weren’t what I needed to focus on right now. Dropped the mace? Just fuck him up with a shield. If I didn’t have that, I’d channel my K-Barbarian spirit and chew him up with my gums if I had to.
Smack.
The moment I dropped the mace, I struck Clown’s face with my shield. Since one hit didn’t do it, once more.
Smack!
Since twice didn’t put me at ease, one more time.
Voom!
I was just about to slam it down a third time.
“What an interesting fellow.” I froze. It felt as if something invisible was pressing down on my whole body with tremendous force.
“You said it yourself. I’m in a hurry.”

The only thing I could move was my eyes, which I shifted to the side. Fallen Scholar had his own eyes fixed on me. His face was expressionless by default, but it also seemed amused for some reason, as if he’d just discovered something that had piqued his curiosity.
“What is your name?”
So, you’re curious about me.
“You can’t be an unnamed adventurer considering what you’ve done to Mr. Necrapeto.” There was no malice in his tone.
Just then, Melter Fend’s voice sounded from the message stone. “Is that man already...!?” Fallen Scholar frowned, displeased with the interruption. “Just wait. I’ll be there s—”
The message stone attached to my waist exploded.
Pop!

I mean, what kind of wizard was this guy? It wasn’t like he’d waved a wand or anything—there wasn’t even the usual hand movement that accompanied using mana. Just what was this old man’s rank? The only thing I’d been told was that he’d been rank three before he was banished.
“Are you not going to answer me?”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.” I decided to respond for now. Since Fend would lead the main team here as soon as possible, I figured I should stall with conversation until then.
“Nickname?”
“Little Balkan.”
“Hmm, this is my first time hearing it. So what rank are you?”
“...I recently got promoted to rank five.”
“Rank five, huh? I’m getting more interested.” Fallen Scholar looked at me with a twinkle in his eyes and moved his hand as if to manipulate mana.
Shaaa!
Colorful light rose from the ground. Oh, I knew this spell; it was the unique rank-five spell Memory of the Earth, a spell that replayed anything that happened in a specified area for the caster.
He even uses the specialty magic of completely unrelated schools with ease.

Memory of the Earth was a spell unique to the Earthrin school. According to my research, Fallen Scholar had been affiliated with a school pursuing a completely different type of magic before being banished.

“Pffft.” Fallen Scholar let out a light chuckle, apparently watching the replay. “I see now that you are an even more interesting fellow than I thought. To think you would say something like that to Mr. Necrapeto.”
“Something like that,” huh? I didn’t know if he was talking about my comment on his looks or the “how small” remark, but it didn’t matter either way.
“What happened to Kyle?” It seemed the other side was interested in conversation, so I decided to also sate my own curiosity.
To my surprise, he answered obligingly. “That fellow is still alive. He’s not the kind of person who should die here.”
“...You mean you kept him alive on purpose?”
“He has achieved many things through revenge. If he abandons even his human emotions, he will likely be able to reach an even higher realm.”

His words were eloquent and well-pronounced, befitting a wizard, but I had no idea what I was hearing. How was that a reason not to kill him? If your opponent had great potential, wasn’t that more reason to kill them? I didn’t say any of that out loud, but it seemed my confusion was written all over my face.

“Individual or group, friend or foe—what does it matter?” Fallen Scholar said. “As a person who wants to see the limits of magic, I am just curious what kind of magic that man will create if he does manage to reach that level.”
“Even if that magic can kill you?”
“Don’t worry. Rising to the top means discarding any and all unnecessary things over and over again. By then, he will have no human emotions left.”

I just gave up on trying to understand him. People called this old man inhuman and driven mad by magic, and they were right. His way of thinking was totally different. But because of that, anticipation stirred inside of me, a faint hope that that peculiar way of thinking might spare my life today.

“Now, let’s end our conversation here. I have slightly overdone it today.” I noticed only then that there were bloodstains on Fallen Scholar’s beard. It seemed he’d tried to wipe them off but the traces remained.
That means this bastard isn’t in his usual condition either.
Whatever the outcome, this was a positive.

Just as I was thinking this, Fallen Scholar spoke up as if to bid me goodbye. “Thanks to you, I’ve had fun for the first time in a long time. I still have need of Mr. Necrapeto, so I’ll be taking him with me.”

Still half-unconscious from being beaten with my shield, Clown’s body floated up into the air. I was forced to watch because my own body wouldn’t budge. It left me with mixed feelings. I really just needed a little more time. Was this really how this was going to end? Well, if he was going to let us go, this was still a good deal for us...
“So, die.”
Yeah, of course not.
Slide.
Fallen Scholar extended his hand toward me, and an ominous red mana formed around it. I let go of any and all regrets. This was nothing new at this point. It was always like this.
“Behelahhh!” I had to fight if I wanted to live.
[You have cast Giantization.]
Squeezing out the last of my strength, my warrior’s body once again increased in size.
Crunch, crunch, chhh.

When I put strength into my feet, I heard the invisible mana covering my body cracking. I pretty much expected this. “Wizard” was practically a synonym for “efficient,” right? Since his body wasn’t in peak condition, I was sure he’d only used minimal mana on me.
Dash.
My body was finally freed. I kicked off the ground and ran.
“Yandel! I see Yandel!”
But I did not go to the place in the distance where my allies were running over from, but toward the enemy.
Leap!

“Hmm.” Fallen Scholar gave me a curious look. He must have been wondering why I wasn’t running away even though he’d released Crowd Control, but that was just the way it seemed from his point of view.
How long can I last with ten minutes’ worth of MP? Twenty seconds, and that’s if I’m generous.
After that, Giantization would deactivate, which was why this was the best I could do for now.
Leap!
