I closed in on Clown, whose body was being dragged away. My reason for doing so was simple. The old man who seemed disinterested in anything other than magic had just said it himself.
“I still have need of Mr. Necrapeto, so I’ll be taking him with me.”
He still needed Clown. This meant that if I stuck close to Clown, he couldn’t use magic. That was probably why he’d tried to drag Clown toward him in the first place.

“You are wise.” The crimson spell in Fallen Scholar’s hand was still there, but it didn’t fire at me. “It’d be a waste of mana to just throw it away.” His open palm changed directions, aimed not at me, but at my comrades.
Flash!
There was a flash of light, and a red orb shot out from his palm.
“Barhatun Wiar.” Dozens of stone walls appeared in its path, courtesy of Raven. No wonder she’d been so quiet up to now; she had been secretly preparing a spell. But it didn’t mean much.
Bang! Bang! Bang! Bang!
The red orb flew at them at high speeds, destroying the stone walls all too easily.
“Get down!” Just as I did earlier, Mr. Bear covered everyone with his body and even summoned Iron Bear on top of that.
Kwaaang!

The orb exploded in mid-air, right at the midpoint between me and my comrades in the distance, expelling thousands of individual jets of flame. No, to be more precise, it exploded right where Erwen had collapsed after Elementalization ended, as if she had been his target from the start.
“No!”
Poppp!
Like fireworks made with CGI, countless sparks flew out and explosions followed one after another.
Whooom!

A strong gust slapped against my skin. Even in the midst of all this chaos, Fallen Scholar’s expression remained unchanged, and when he spoke, his voice was calm. “That young lady was born with the most destiny after you.”
I couldn’t understand what he was talking about, but one thing was for sure. He really had been aiming for Erwen.
Grit.
My jaw hurt. It felt like someone had hit me on the back of the head with a huge, blunt weapon. Was Erwen really dead?
Thump!
Blood pooled in my heart and paralyzed all reason. The more it did, the more just one thought filled my mind: What do I have to do to protect the rest?
I at least have to kill this bastard.
I extended my hand toward Clown’s head, trusting that my soon-to-arrive allies would take care of Fallen Scholar somehow.
Smack!
My shield came down on Clown’s face again, but it seemed he was still conscious. “Pooh!” Clown spewed the blood pooled in his mouth onto my face.
Chhh!
There was a sizzling sound. I felt no pain, but even with my dulled senses I could feel something continue to flow down my skin. I somehow managed to open my eyes, but my vision was blurry.
Hydra Venom.

His passive skill had a similar effect to that of Acid Fluid, but there was a huge difference in terms of performance. The suicide soldier zombies had probably been modified using his own blood. Of course, none of that mattered. I reached my hand out beyond the darkness in my vision.
Squeeze.
Luckily, I grabbed his hair. Okay, with this, I wouldn’t miss it.
Grit.
Instead of using my recently stabbed left arm, which had no strength left in it, I bit him like an animal.
“Aaah!” I could feel soft cartilage. Was this his ear?
Spit.
Spitting it out, I lowered my chin some more. What I wanted was his neck. If I chewed off the blood vessels leading to his brain, even this asshole wouldn’t be able to survive.
“You really are a beast.” There was disgust lining every word.
Slice!
Something sharp cut through my right arm. In truth, this was my first time feeling pain in a long time. Maybe that was why the corners of my mouth turned up.
“I think I know why barbarians are called savages now. Each one of you is positively unhinged. Are you not afraid of death?” the Fallen Scholar asked.

This guy knew nothing about barbarians. They weren’t fearless beings. They just learned how to overcome fear and move on because there was no other choice. They could only laugh and choose the sole option available to them. Some called them savages for that, but these were people who fought with themselves every day. They called them warriors.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has deactivated.]
Giantization ended just in time.
Choke!

With nothing to hold on to, my body was pushed back. It rolled round and round. Maybe it was because I’d been in many dogfights, but standing up without being able to see in front of me was no problem. The problem was the lack of direction.
“Impressive.”
There you are.
Dash.
I charged in the direction of the voice.
Stab!
Something stabbed me through the stomach, but in that moment, a warm energy embraced me.
Shaaa!
It was divine power.
“Yandel! Protect Yandel!” I could hear Teterud the dwarf, who I’d sent to help Melter Fend earlier. He was quite close.
“Belbev Ruingenes!” I could also hear Kyle’s voice, amplified by magic and filled with anger. He was shouting the Fallen Scholar’s real name.
Bang!
Something exploded in front of me. Did he step back to avoid it?

“So that fellow managed to get over here. If I knew this would happen, I wouldn’t have made conversation.” Fallen Scholar’s voice moved a little further away. “You know something? I wasn’t being overconfident. It’s just that for the first time in a long time, I miscalculated. I thought I had enough time.” His voice was still calm. “Well, I’ve been miscalculating from the moment you first appeared. Because I thought no one would get up to the second floor.” The bastard’s voice grew fainter and more distant. “Congratulations. On being the sole victor.”

After that, I did not hear the voice again. From that point on, my blurry vision blackened. I couldn’t even sense the dim light of the labyrinth through my retinas anymore. It felt like I was all alone in the universe.
Tap.
Just then, I felt someone approach me and I reflexively swung my severed arm.
Tap.
My blow was stopped mid-swing, but there was no counterattack like I’d been fearing.
“It’s me.” I heard the voice of Teterud. “My friend... it’s all over...”
Ah.
“So... rest now.”
Ahh... What about Erwen...?
I had to ask, but my voice wouldn’t come out.
Slump.
Today was such a long day, and that was the last bit of it that I remembered.

chapters.title: Chapter 230: Reversal (6)
paragraphs: “Are you awake?”
With the distinct tang of potion still lingering on the tip of her tongue, Missha Karlstein opened her eyes. The first thing she saw was Abman.
“...W-What happened? Did we win?” Missha asked the moment her vision cleared, trying to recall the answer. Her memory wasn’t perfect and seemed to cut off intermittently.
“Protect Raven!”
Corpse Collector had transformed into a skeleton and charged at her. She had been unable to withstand a single attack and got knocked out.
Bang! Bang!
Then, she had been awoken by a thunderous boom in time to see Bjorn lying face down with both hands planted on the ground, struggling to protect them. That was her last memory.
“I don’t know if we won, but we’re safe for now, at least. Our enemies have all retreated.”
“Really? That’s a rrrelief. But is anyone d-dead...?”

Abman’s face fell in a way that suggested that someone really did die. When he spotted the look in her eyes, however, he quickly backtracked. “Ah, don’t freak out. Everyone on our team survived. That elf was the one who died.”
“Elf...?” She flinched at those words. “Was it Erwen?” Although it couldn’t be said that they had a good relationship, the question carried a genuine sadness from the very depths of her heart.
“No, it was her sister who died. She shielded Erwen in the end and protected her from the explosion.”
“...Then what about Erwen?”

“I heard she would have died if she had been treated any later. I don’t know if ‘fortunately’ is the right word here, but she’s unconscious right now. I worry how her mental state will be once she wakes up.”
“I see...”
Missha listened as he filled her in on the status of the rest of the team. Raven had also lost consciousness and Ainar had woken up early on, heading off to find Bjorn.
“Don’t go, though. I wanted to stay by his side, too, but the priestess kicked me o—You’re not going to listen anyway, huh. It’s that way.”
Missha asked Abman for the right direction and headed off. Now that the battle was over, Goblin Forest was very bright thanks to the flames floating everywhere.
Step, step.

Missha walked and walked through the adventurers. She saw some sitting on the bare floor to rest, and others crying. Some were gleefully gulping down alcohol, and others were busy carrying motionless corpse soldiers and tossing them into the flames.
“Oh! It’s the cat lady from Yandel’s team!” As she walked along in silence, adventurers struck up conversations with her.
“Are you going to see Yandel? He should be over there.”
“Hmm, I would advise you not to go, though.”
“Yes, you must be worried about your teammate.” Some made strange comments.
On the other hand, some spoke with ease. “Oh, don’t worry. That guy can’t possibly die.”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel is immortal!”
“I heard he half-killed Corpse Collector too. And that if it weren’t for Fallen Scholar, he would’ve won. He’s going to be incredibly famous once he’s outside.”
All kinds of adventurers acknowledged Bjorn’s greatness. The more she heard, the faster Missha’s feet moved. Before long, a tent appeared. Several other adventurers were gathered there too.

“Ah, Miss Karlstein is here.” The first thing she spotted was Ainar arguing with Kyle Pevrosk in front of the tent. “Please excuse me for sitting down. In truth, even being awake is overdoing it right now.”
“Why won’t you let me in!?”
“I told you. The priestess is even risking her life to save him. So please lower your voice if you really want to help him.”
“Ainar, stop it!” Missha hurriedly moved to stop Ainar. She wasn’t sure what was going on, but it was clear Ainar wasn’t helping.
“M-Missha! You’re awake!” Ainar excitedly greeted her, but Missha rushed to Kyle to ask about Bjorn’s condition.

It was terrifying just hearing about it. Apparently, the poison had been sprayed all over his face and his eyes, dissolving everything in its path. “It seems the poison melted his bones and has slipped a little into the brain.”
She felt suffocated and dizzy. The whole world seemed to swim before her eyes like she was drunk.
“...You may come in now.” The priestess came out of the tent sporting a pale complexion.
Missha stepped inside, not able to even say thank you. “Bjorn...”

She spotted him asleep on top of a makeshift bed made of several layers of sleeping bags. Outwardly, he looked fine. Although he had been left with burn-like scars on his face, none of it looked serious at least.
“The scars will gradually fade with time. I didn’t have enough power for that...”
“Truly... Thank you...”
“It’s nothing. Compared to what he did, I did nothing. Anyway, I should go rest now...”

The priestess left and Missha knelt next to Bjorn. She stroked his face. For some reason, she was reminded of the time they had been chased by the Lord of the Third Floor, but this was completely different from back then. Back then, he’d slept comfortably, as if he had done everything he’d set out to do. She remembered thinking he looked like a hero. After that day, there had been a lot of the same. Bjorn accomplished many things and was acknowledged by new people accordingly. There were times Missha was rather pleased and proud of that.
“Why do you...”
But his face right now? It looked sad and distressed. It seemed like he was blaming himself.
Squeeze.

Missha clenched her fists, unable to finish her sentence. She thought she already knew the reason for that expression of his. She couldn’t possibly not know, since she had been by this man’s side, watching him, for a long time now.
Erwen... He probably thinks it’s his fault.
Slide.

Missha removed her hand from Bjorn’s body. He hadn’t even regained consciousness yet, but each time her hand touched his skin, his body flinched like he was convulsing. How much must he have suffered for this iron-like man to be in this state?

Missha closed her eyes and prayed fervently. God had never listened to her prayers, but she brought her hands together and prayed nevertheless that the man lying before her never got acknowledged again.

When I opened my eyes, the whole team was gathered. As we greeted each other, the priestess came in and checked how I was doing. I could see well. My sense of smell was also normal. But the rest of my body wasn’t able to move all that well. My nerve endings were all alive, but strength didn’t come properly to my arms and legs, and if I forced it, they started to shake.
“This is a common phenomenon for those who suffer brain injuries. If you take it easy for about a month, you will be fine.”
“I see. Thanks.”
“It’s nothing. Now that you’re awake, I’ll bring Sir Pevrosk in.”
While the priestess left to find Kyle, my teammates filled me in on what had happened in the aftermath of my collapse. There was less than one hour until the end of Day Seven now.
“Any ambushes?”
“None.”

They told me that Fallen Scholar and Clown hadn’t returned while I was unconscious. Well, what would they be able to do on their own? It’d take time for them to recover, and the corpse soldiers Clown had left behind had all been burned with fire, so they lacked numbers. Also, it was hard to call for reinforcements since it took a day just to get up to the third floor from here. Going up and back down again would take two days.
Fallen Scholar, with his personality, wouldn’t go in the first place no matter how much Clown insisted. He’s not someone who acts out of vengeance.
No, wait. As I was talking with my teammates, I remembered something I had forgotten. Why hadn’t I remembered this until now?
“Ah! Erwen. What happened to Erwen?” I hurriedly asked, and a moment of silence followed. My teammates stared back at me with grim looks on their faces. “...So she’s dead.”
“No, her sister was the one who died.”
“Her sister?”

I heard the details from Mr. Bear, a short recounting of Daria using short-range teleportation just before the explosion to sacrifice herself for her sister. The weight of death touched me again. This was truly a fast-moving world indeed. It had all happened in an instant. No one could have stopped it, and Daria hadn’t even been able to leave a will at the moment of her death. It was a good thing I’d heard it in advance.
“Where is Erwen right now?”
“...She’s there.”
“There?”
“Yes. There.”
I wanted to go there, but the moment I tried to raise my body, my strength faltered.
“Give me your arm.”
Eventually, with the help of Mr. Bear, I managed to leave the tent. As if on cue, Kyle appeared. “You’re awake.”
While speaking with Kyle, I slowly moved to where the battle had taken place. “There are a lot of people here, what happened?”
“These are people who came up after the battle. About a thousand people in four separate groups.”
“A thousand...?”
“We left marks along the way, remember? Once their teams were formed, they followed us east and then the rest of the way.”
I see. I wish they had come a little earlier. If they did... What are you thinking right now?
I continued walking, shaking off my regrets and resentment. What was the use in getting bitter over the past?
“Oh, it’s Bjorn, son of Yandel!”

As I walked with Kyle, adventurers recognized me and came up to speak to me. They wanted to go out and have drinks later, or pay back debts on behalf of their clans. Some even promised to be the first to aid me when I was in trouble and thanked me. But none of them offered a single word of consolation.
“...Don’t think too badly of them. They say heroes aren’t the type to be comforted by others.”

I hadn’t known that such a proverb existed in this world too, but I didn’t think badly of them anyway. They had all made a lot of sacrifices too. It was because they were hurting that they could laugh as they spoke.

“Mister...” When I arrived at my destination, I saw Erwen. She was on her knees, clinging tightly to her sister’s body, which was stiff and covered with burns. Her cheeks, full of blood and dirt stains, had clear marks of something flowing down them.
“Come here.”
Erwen shook her head.
“It’s almost time to go down. Are you going to stay here alone?”
“I’m... not alone.”
Removing my arm from Abman’s shoulder, I staggered toward Erwen and patted her on the back. “Listen to me. I am your guardian now.”
“...Pardon?”

I told her about the will Daria had imparted to me. It wasn’t a long one. That woman had asked that I take care of her sister in the case of her death. For reference, she told me this before the royal guards had even escaped through the portal, but she might have had a hunch even then that something like this would happen.

“Mister... my sister, my sister is...! She isn’t moving anymore. She can’t speak. She’s cold, and hard. And I-I haven’t done anything for her yet...” Soon, Erwen threw her arms around me. “What do I tell my little sister, that kid? That after mom, even our big sis is dead? A-And because of me?”

I stood still and listened as the words fell out of her. I didn’t console her and say it wasn’t her fault, or that Daria chose to do what she did. I just waited until she was done. I wasn’t sure how long we were there.
“Yandel, we have to go now.”

It was time to go down to the first floor. Together with Erwen, I recovered her sister’s body. It was better than with Dwalkie. At least this time, there was a wizard around who could use distortion magic. The funeral could be held in the city.
“Let’s go home.”
I led Erwen back to my team. Missha and Ainar, who were not on good terms with her, said nothing. They seemed like they wanted to approach her but couldn’t out of fear that it would hurt her.
I’ve never seen Ainar like that.
Soon, we stood in front of the portal in the center of Goblin Forest. It was 23:50. The clock was pointing to the end of a long journey.
“Come on, let’s go home!”
“Woahhh!”
Starting with the teams in the center, we headed down to the first floor one by one. Even though Berzak was scary, I was sure it wouldn’t appear within ten minutes.
“Yandel! I’ll see you in the city!”
“Do you remember my name? I’ll definitely come find you again.”
The adventurers in front of me entered the portal, and then it was our turn.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]

The cave seemed even more eerie than before. Even as I moved forward to allow adventurers behind us to come down, I continued to check the time. Only one minute left until the labyrinth closed. It didn’t feel real. Was it really over?
Thump!
Yes, it had to be over. With one minute left now, what could Berzak do?
“Goddamn royal bastards.”
“Once I get back, I’m not even going to piss in their direction.”
Anger toward the palace erupted from the mouths of adventurers who were convinced of their survival.
Uh, you should still watch your mouth.
“You guys, don’t say anything weird even after you get back.” I cautioned my party members not to curse the emperor in front of anyone.
[The labyrinth is now closed. You are being transported to Rafdonia.]
A pure white light appeared beyond my eyelids, the light of the outside world I’d longed so desperately for.
Thump!
Soon, the light disappeared and a clear sky came into view. I studied my surroundings blankly.
They’re really all dead.
Dimension Square, which was always crowded, was unprecedentedly empty. Wow, how many people were dead?
“Woahhh!”
Even as I listened to the cheers erupting around me, my gaze naturally slid in one particular direction.
“It’s a portal!”
“Damn, you bastards!”

In the center of the plaza where the portal had opened, hundreds more were opening, and those who had abandoned us appeared one by one. All of them looked exactly as they did days ago. With the way time worked in the labyrinth, even through separate portals, everyone came out at the same time.
They will never be able to imagine what we’ve been through.
At the sight of their all-too-normal appearances, I let myself vent some of my grievances. And at that moment—
Shaaaaa!
A huge magic circle bloomed in the center of the square where the portals had opened.
“Uh—huh?”
For a moment, time seemed to pass in slow motion. But in truth, it all happened in an instant.
Thump!
Sensing something strange, bewildered knights, clan elites, and top adventurers quickly tried to put distance between themselves and what was to come.
Baaaaaang!
An explosion.
Shaaaaaa!

A gust of fire slammed into me and pushed me back. Falling to the ground and quickly raising my head up, I saw a red-hot pillar of fire soaring into the sky. It was like watching the end of the world.
Suddenly, a voice played in my head, the last words Fallen Scholar had said to me. “Congratulations. On being the sole victor.”

chapters.title: Chapter 231: New Era (1)
paragraphs: The absolute monarch, called the First and Immortal King, was Ravigion III. Following his death after his thousands of years ruling over Rafdonia, King New World implemented many policies to shake off the deep-rooted remnants of his predecessor. The best example of this was his changes to the calendar.

To more conveniently calculate the cycle of the labyrinth, one month was set as thirty days, and a thirteenth month was created to hold any extra days. In addition, the labyrinth’s cycle was changed to thirty-five days at the end of the year by updating the portal. Of course, this led to controversy among scholars. They claimed it wasn’t practical to waste five days a year. However, the immovable King New World held a grand festival every thirteenth month and won over the public, and the controversy died down as the years went by.

The name of the era also changed twice. At first, it was referred to by the king’s true name, but because of its long and difficult pronunciation, the public began to call the king by a nickname which the royal family started to use as well: New World.

On May 2nd of year 154 of New World, seven pillars of fire burst from each Dimension Square and covered the sky above Rafdonia. It was a disaster that would be recorded in the history books for years to come.
“God damn it.”
Using whatever was nearby to support my weight, I struggled to my feet. Then I walked out of the room with the crutches that were resting by my bedside. Oh, these damned stairs.
“Bjorn! You should’ve called me when you woke up. Why are you sufferrring alone?” Missha, who was cooking on the first floor, spotted me and helped me out.
Now I really felt like a patient. Oh, I guess I was one. They did tell me I’d have to recuperate for a month. My arms and legs still felt weak.

“Come, sit. This is your first prrroper meal since getting out, right? I prepared one for the firrrst time in a while.” While Missha went to get Ainar, I took a moment to catch my breath, spoon in hand.
It’s been three days.

Three days had passed since that day. It hardly felt real. On the first day we returned, all of the survivors were dragged to the palace to testify as to what had happened inside the labyrinth. Afterward, I slept for days.
Deranged bastards.

I still felt chills go down my spine when I recalled the moment the pillars of fire exploded. To think they had been aiming to sneak in while we were away. I had never dreamed a trap would be set in the center of the square where the portal opened and in all seven squares at that.
What’s going to happen now?

The damage suffered by those of us who came out of the labyrinth the normal way was minimal, but the Third Royal Guard and numerous large clans had been practically annihilated. Of course, there were survivors among them too. Some whose portals had formed on the outskirts of the Square had backed away as soon as the magic circles lit up and managed to save themselves with sheer luck—maybe one hundred or so? That was the total from all seven squares. It was a bit ironic.
“A great commander is not a person who makes the perfect choices. They’re a person who makes the necessary ones.”

The ones who had made the necessary choice were all dead, and those who had been left behind fought without rest for days and survived. Our situations had flipped overnight. If I had accepted that guy’s offer back then and left without my teammates, what would have happened to me?
“I would be dead.” The words unknowingly left my mouth.
I heard Missha’s voice from behind me. “Hm? What did you say?”
“Nothing. Where’s Ainar?”
“I slapped her on the back but she still won’t budge.”
“She must be very tired.”
“Yeah. I’ll just serrrve her once she wakes up later.”

Geez, Missha must have been tired too. While the two of us just slept, she had woken up several times to serve us meals and help us focus solely on resting. She even found crutches somewhere. She was a teammate I could rely on in many ways.
“Why arrren’t you eating?”
In the middle of staring blankly at Missha, I came to my senses and brought the spoon to my mouth. The taste seemed to herald the end of a hard day.
“...What arrre you going to do about Erwen?” Missha asked when the meal was almost over. After the interrogation on the first day, Erwen took her sister’s body to the elven holy land.
“I don’t know. She said she’d visit after the funeral, so I plan to discuss it more then.”
“Hmm, is that so?” Missha said, her voice completely neutral. “Why don’t we just brrring her home?”

What? Was she feeling me out? Or saying no in advance? Many thoughts along those lines crossed my mind in a split second, but her tone didn’t seem to indicate that was the case at all. “What do you mean by that?”
“Well... you said she lived with her sisterrr? It’ll be hard for her to keep living there. But I’m too worried about her living alone.”
“So?”
“Unfortunately, we can’t enter the labyrinth as six people, but I think we should take carrre of her until she gets back on her feet again.”
Right, I forgot this was just how Missha was. Her intentions were praiseworthy, which made me want to tease her. “Didn’t you hate elves?”

“Eek, what do you take me forrr? Spit out the meal I just worked hard to prepare. Spit it all out!” Missha snapped as she looked me up and down. How strange. Just a moment ago, it felt like my heart was being weighed down by all kinds of thoughts. “Why are you laughing? It’s getting on my nerrrves.”
“I’m just grateful.”
“...Ugh, out of nowhere again.” Missha averted her gaze in annoyance and gulped down her water.

I studied her silently. In truth, except for the ears on top of her head and her tail, she looked just like a normal human being. Her short red hair had grown a bit since we first met. She had a sharp nose and eyes that were angled slightly upward. You could tell she was down-to-earth and kind just by exchanging a few words with her, but when I first saw her face, I thought she would be the feisty and cool type.
Belatedly, I realized the room had gone quiet. A strange, awkward silence lingered in the kitchen.
“Um...” Missha parted her lips.
Knock, knock.
We heard a knock at the front door.
“I’ll go see who it is.”
“...Okay, I’ll clearrr the table.”
Walking on crutches and opening the front door, I saw a familiar person standing there. “Kyle Pevrosk.”
“Haha, nice to see you. Did you get a good rest?”
“I fell asleep as soon as I arrived and only just woke up.”
“Then does that mean you have time for a short conversation?”
“Of course. Come in.”
As I stepped aside, Kyle came in. He exchanged greetings with Missha, who was clearing the table.
“Oh! Mr. Kyle?”
“Sorry, Miss Karlstein. It looks like I’ve interrupted your alone time.”
“Eek, don’t tease! He and I arrre not like that.”
“Hmm, no? Sorry about that, then.” Kyle apologized as if he really hadn’t realized.
Missha shot me a look, then whipped around and started doing housework. And so, we sat on the sofa in the living room.
“I meant to come find you earlier, but as you know, I had a lot of work to do.”
“I understand. After what happened...”
“Yes, yes...”

An uncomfortable silence settled between us at the mention of that incident. Before long, Missha placed the cookies she’d bought earlier on the coffee table and headed back to her room so that we could talk freely.
“Oh, this is from Lanemouth Bakery.”
“Is that so? It must be a famous spot.”
The mood lightened thanks to the cookies. I spoke more comfortably then. “If you have time, I want to hear everything from the beginning.”
“I have quite a bit of time before my next appointment, but what do you mean by the beginning?”
“Fallen Scholar. What happened with that old man?”

This was something I was curious about but hadn’t had the chance to hear the backstory of. By the time I woke up in the labyrinth, it was just before the end of Day Seven and even that was spent taking care of Erwen. Not to mention what had happened after we returned to the city. Dimension Square had been a literal hell on Earth that day.
“Oh, that...” Kyle bit into a cookie and started talking.

There were some things I couldn’t understand since it was a battle between wizards, but the gist of it was simple: he had lost one-on-one. Before he could even use his modified version of Awakening, which he had been preparing for years, he got driven into a corner by an overwhelming sequence of spells. Activating the spell in an incomplete state, he took damage.
“I thought that I had finally managed to catch up to him with all my effort, but that had been my mistake. No, on the contrary, the gap between us seems to be wider than before.”
Kyle had faced a wall that could never be climbed no matter what. And what was even more humiliating was that he had still survived.

“...He said my talent was a waste. Isn’t it funny? I wasn’t even a match for him. If he hadn’t decided to spare me, I likely wouldn’t have even dealt the amount of damage I did.” By the time he finished talking, Kyle’s face was dark.
“That must have been a hard topic to discuss, so thank you for telling me.”
“I thought you should know this as well: after what happened, they might end up targeting you.”
Hah, so this guy thinks so too.

“Thanks to this incident, the palace has raised the threat level of the Fallen Scholar to another rank, right below a commander. To be honest, as someone who has faced him, I think he should be placed on the same level as a commander... But no matter how many times I say so, everyone else disagrees.”
“They won’t know until they experience it for themselves.”

This was a wizard who could pierce my Mana Resistance, which I had struggled to grind, with a regular hit. How many of these monsters could there be out there in the world? If we ran into each other in the labyrinth by coincidence under normal conditions, I wouldn’t be able to avoid getting annihilated within minutes.
“Anyway, that’s why I wanted to tell you to be careful.”
Hmm, but personality-wise, I don’t think he’ll bother to come to track me down out of revenge. Unlike Clown.
“What happened to Corpse Collector?”
“No news yet. I heard he took a critical hit from you before he left, but he’s probably still alive.”
“...I see.”

At least the Clown situation was better, because he’d lost a corpse army of thousands during the battle. It would take a huge amount of time for him to recover that, so I at least had time to level up.
“Oh, so how many survivors were there?”
“Are you referring to those who used the portals to escape?”
“Of course. I think I heard that about a hundred people lived.”
Kyle sighed at my words. “There are 103 to be exact, although I don’t know if they can be considered alive.”
“What do you mean?”
Once again, Kyle used professional wizard jargon to explain this and that. To summarize, it was like this:
“So, it was a unique spell imbued with black magic, so even treatment with divine power isn’t working properly on the wounds?”
“That’s right. They are all unconscious now. As for when they’ll wake up—no, it’s unclear whether they’ll even wake up or not.”
“That’s one hell of a mess.”

After discussing the survivors, we had a conversation about the incident itself. Just what was going on? Kyle, who was a rather high-ranking member of the palace, was open with me about everything he knew.

“At first, we were confused too. How did they manage to prepare a spell that requires several months of preparation to even activate in the square in one day?” This was the question all adventurers that had been there that day had, including me. The answer was really simple. “As it turns out, they drew the magic circle in the sewers to avoid prying eyes.”
Like the tunnel people they were, they worked from below.
“Our investigation found that the barrier on Noark hasn’t undergone any changes. That means that either these guys have a way to come outside or manpower that they sent out in advance.”
I laughed awkwardly at his hypothesis. It was probably manpower that was sent out of the city in advance.
For example... Amelia.
A spy from Noark had infiltrated the city. Until now, I was on the fence about strictly calling her my enemy. I had thought her hatred was only directed toward the royal family and not me.
But it would be smart to see her as the enemy now.
That woman would continue to work under Noark. And if I got unlucky, I could end up losing my life because of that unless I decided to join Noark’s side.
“Then let’s get to the main topic at hand here.”
“Main topic?”
“Currently, the situation in the city isn’t good, because a great number of the important figures that maintained the city are dead. At this rate, the economy will collapse soon.”

That was pretty much what I had been thinking. Adventurers were miners who gathered resources from the labyrinth. The knights may have been strong, but they were nowhere near as important as adventurers in this sense. The high-ranking adventurers were all dead—well, aside from some large clans who had been boycotting. High-ranking adventurers who didn’t feel safe going in even after the identification tag system was introduced had survived too, but the real problem lay elsewhere.
“Those people likely won’t enter the labyrinth anymore. That is, until they are convinced that the labyrinth is safe.”
A “safe labyrinth” was a funny thought, but understandable. The number of survivors from this month was less than two thousand. Who would want to mine mana stones in a situation like this?
“...It’s inevitable. Until now, the identification tags and presence of the Third Royal Guard had reassured adventurers, but the truth has been revealed.”
The knights who had vowed to protect us from Noark had stooped to opening portals with the large clans and fleeing, leaving ten thousand adventurers behind.
“I’m embarrassed to say this, but someone said during the meeting that it might have been better if there were no survivors at all.”
I laughed bitterly at Kyle’s words. The more I went through, the more I realized how cruel this world was.
Well, complaining won’t change anything.
“So, now I have to watch out for Fallen Scholar, Corpse Collector, and the palace?”
“Haha, of course not.” Kyle waved his hand at my half-joking concern. “You may not know this because you’ve only been at home, but you have become a very important figure to the palace.”
“...Elaborate.”

“Even at this moment, stories about you are being spread through the mouths of the survivors who journeyed with us that day. In a few more days, there won’t be anyone left in the city who doesn’t know who you are. You are the rising star who single-handedly left Corpse Collector in that state, after all!”
“...Please don’t spread rumors that I did it on my own anywhere.”
“You’re a humble guy.”
No, it’s not about being humble, it’s an actual burden.

Being just a good guy who had led the way and worked harder than anyone else was enough, but this reputation Kyle described was hard for me to bear. The one fighting single-handedly had actually been Clown. Even as he fought our party, that guy had been pushing back the main team composed of senior adventurers with an army of corpses.
When I think of it that way, he really is a monster.
I sorted out the thoughts that briefly passed through my mind and returned to the topic at hand. “So what does that have to do with the palace? Adventurers of my level would be common there.”
“But few as iconic as you.”
“I don’t know what you mean.”

“There was already mounting distrust toward the palace brewing. It is inevitable that this incident will become a catalyst. The king has assessed the situation as follows: if you become the heart of the movement, it could lead to a bigger—”
God damn it.
“...Huh? Why do you look like that?”
I answered honestly. “For some reason, all I heard was that they are going to get rid of me.” This was my 100 percent sincere assumption.
I wasn’t sure if he was aware of where my mind was going, but Kyle chuckled. “Don’t worry about a thing. The palace’s approach to you was already decided during the meeting.”
Decided? Oh, is that why he said I don’t have to be careful?
“Stop stalling and tell me. I see now that this is why you came today in the first place.”
When I prodded him, Kyle smiled as if he was the one who was more pleased between the two of us. “Congratulations. Soon, you will receive a very, very, very big reward.”
So the king had decided to hand me a carrot.

chapters.title: Chapter 232: New Era (2)
paragraphs: There was a very, very, very big reward to be bestowed on me by the king. I hadn’t heard the details yet, but my mouth was already watering. But in my experience, moments like these were always the most dangerous. If you received a gift, the unspoken rule was that you would have to return it one day. I had to check if I could accept this in advance.
“What exactly is the reward? And what do I have to do?”

Kyle kindly answered my questions one by one. The specific reward hadn’t been determined yet. Besides, I was not the only one receiving something; all the survivors from that day were as well. Apparently, the palace would be inviting us to a party in celebration.
“What I can say for sure is that there will be a bestowal of rewards and your achievements will be the ones honored as the most valuable.”
“I see. Do you have any guesses?”

“I have something in mind, but...” Kyle trailed off, then asked me to take the following list as just his opinion. “The first is a noble title. Of course, the chances of being awarded a title are very slim. Even if you get it, it won’t be an inheritable title. And there will be no fief, either.”

I wasn’t expecting much, anyway. That was how the world of nobles worked. It wasn’t something you could become a part of just because you achieved one or two things. If I were to make a guess as to the reward I would be receiving, it would just be an entry into the royal capital.

“The second is an essence. The palace is said to open even the Gold Soul Repository in situations like this, so you can look forward to that.” The Gold Soul Repository was the palace treasure vault where treasures up to rank three essences were stored.
“The third?”
“Equipment.”
“The most typical one.”
The third guess was high-grade equipment or Numbered Items. The fourth was just money. “It’s highly likely that aside from the title, the rest will be distributed according to merit.”
I thought I understood what he meant. The people with the fewest achievements would end up with just some money. Those with a few achievements would receive equipment or a rank-five essence.
A rank-three essence based on merit, huh?
That got me drooling more. Rank-three essences were normally farmed starting on floors seven or eight. But I could even choose which one I wanted? That would definitely boost my stunted growth.
“So what does the king want from me? You haven’t said that yet.”

I hadn’t heard the most important piece of information. What did I have to give in return for this gift? Surely, sooner or later, the palace would try to regain the trust of the people by defeating Noark. If they wanted me to enlist in the military and participate in the battle when that moment came, refusing this gift was the right thing to do, no matter how attractive the reward.
“Nothing big. You just have to show that you are on amicable terms with the palace during the reward ceremony. The rest will be taken care of by them.”
“...That’s an easy yet difficult request.”
Kyle grimaced at my answer. “As expected, it seems you don’t see them in a very good light.”
I responded with silence, and rightfully so, because how could I like them? Without trying to come up with another solution, the palace elites took the easy way out and all ended up dead.

“But just know that not everything that happened that day was the palace’s intention. Even the commanders of the Royal Guard each have different values. I’m sure the results would have been different had a different commander been there that day.”

Kyle seemed to be trying to defend them, but my feelings of unease did not fall away. Maybe it was that I felt a sense of responsibility. Playing nice with the palace almost felt like betraying those who had fought with me after being abandoned by these people, like I was climbing the social ladder during enemy occupation.
“...What do you think of the palace?” I asked cautiously.
It was a question that could potentially be considered blasphemous. Kyle flinched, then responded with a grin, “To be honest, not that positively.”

I didn’t think he was saying that just for my benefit. This man wasn’t the type to do something like that in the first place. Still, I never thought a rank-three battle mage would say something like that even in private.

“But the palace is a necessary entity to keep this world going. Well, that’s probably not something someone who turned their back on the Magic Tower and enlisted for their self-interest should be saying, though.”
“Self-interest?”
“You already noticed, didn’t you? What kind of relationship I have with Fallen Scholar.”
Hmm, yes, but...
“Can I ask you to explain further?”
“He is my master’s enemy. One day, he slayed my master, who was his research partner, and completed a forbidden spell.”
“So you enlisted in the military for revenge?”
“That’s right. As soon as I heard that that man pledged himself to Orcules, I saw a dark road ahead of me. But I couldn’t do anything on my own.”
In his youth, Kyle decided that he needed help from the military and the palace to seek revenge. So he went under their wing, judging that the enemy of his enemy was his friend.
“So don’t think too hard. So what if you don’t like them? If there’s something you can use them for, it’d be rational to do so.”

Kyle’s advice was 100 percent correct. Realistically, what would I get by making an enemy of the palace? That went for the other survivors who had negative feelings toward the palace. If you were going to go through all that hardship, at least get something out of it.
“Your expression looks a little better.”
“Thanks to you.”
“It’s getting close to the time for my next appointment. I’ll get up now.”
“Thank you for coming. I can’t send you off with my body in this state, though.”
“Haha, did you intend to see me out? It’s okay, rest. You’ll be busy from now on.”
“Busy?”
Kyle, who was heading toward the door, turned around at my question. “You will find out soon.” He left with a mysterious smile.
[Your Reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +10.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +10.]
The day after Kyle left, there were visitors—Raven and Mr. Bear.
“If everyone has rested, let’s settle the loot.”
“Shouldn’t you ask how I’m doing first?”
“You clearly look fine. And you’re the one who foolishly ground his body into dust, but we have to worry?”
Uh, is that how that works...?
That hurt my feelings as a tank, but that all disappeared when she continued.

“So please stop getting hurt.” Her tone was harsh, but Raven looked embarrassed as she pressed on. “Seriously, what did Miss Karlstein do to deserve this? It seems she’s always taking care of you all alone.”
“Uh, me? I’m okay... Mm, I do wish he’d stop getting hurrrt, though...”
“Miss Karlstein, your problem is that you are too nice. If we leave this man to his own devices, he’ll die prematurely.”
“...Anyway, let’s get to business. Loot settlement? Did you sell all the equipment?”
“Yes. I was tired as heck but gritted my teeth through it and forced myself to sell it all, so you should thank me.”

I was informed that on the first day back from the labyrinth, as soon as the interrogation was over, Raven went to sell the spoils instead of going home. The reason for rushing to sell to the point of straining herself was simple.
“That’s because we had to sell it all quickly to earn as much as possible.”

Huge losses had been incurred in the overall adventurer population. The fact was that equipment prices would fall since demand had decreased. Besides, 99 percent of the loot from the survivors was equipment apparently, so there would be a surplus.
“Thanks. I hadn’t even thought that far ahead.”
“...If you could think that far ahead in a situation like that, you would be a superhuman, not a barbarian, Mr. Yandel.”
I mean, you could have just answered with “You’re welcome.”
“Aruru! What do you mean?! Bjorn is a super-barbarian!”
What was this kid saying? Was it because this past expedition was so depressing? I couldn’t get used to this everyday chaos.
“Then let’s all sit down.”

Before the conversation could drag on too long, I stopped them there and sat my teammates on the sofa. The loot settlement began. Thanks to Raven’s thorough organization, it didn’t take long. All we had to do was hear the details of the settlement and get paid. The payout ended in the blink of an eye and we spent time chatting with each other.
Mr. Bear brought up a new topic. “Oh, I don’t know if you’ve heard since you’ve been home, Yandel, but you have a new title.”
“Oh, really!?”

After Ainar, who was very excited, and Missha, of course, even Raven seemed curious. It seemed the nickname wasn’t widely known yet seeing as Raven didn’t know. I guessed information came quickly to a tavern owner.
A new nickname... Am I finally growing out of Little Balkan?
“What is it? Spit it out,” demanded Missha.

“Huhu, what do you think it is?” Mr. Bear avoided answering and relished in the attention. Various theories were exchanged among the team, and soon Mr. Bear asked me for my opinion. “You? Yandel, can you think of anything?”
“Well, anything but Big Balkan would be good.”
Unsatisfied with my reaction, Mr. Bear pouted and told me my new epithet. “Giant.”
“Huh?”
“It’s Giant. Your new nickname.”
Hmm, that was simpler than I thought. Then was I Giant Bjorn, son of Yandel now?
While I was chuckling at that silly thought, Missha expressed her own opinion. “It suits you. It covers one of Bjorrrn’s essences, Giantization, too.”
“Yes, that’s what I thought as soon as I heard it. Ah! But why did you have that other nickname before? Did you not have an essence then?” Mr. Bear smiled warmly and raised a question.
It was Raven who answered. “No. I heard he had one then too. Rather, he was much bigger than he is now. Right?”

I nodded. At the time, using the skill of a Vampire, Master of Blood, I borrowed Missha’s brother’s The Unclean and was 1.5 times bigger than I could get with Giantization now. But in the end, the nickname I got in return was Little Balkan.
Mr. Bear tilted his head in confusion. “Hmm, bigger? Then how did that happen?”
Again, the reply came from Raven. “I think... I know the answer.”
“Hm? You do?”
“Yes. Surely... it didn’t seem so big in the eyes of the people who were there back then. Mr. Yandel’s back.”
My face heated up when I heard that, especially because everyone else was seriously convinced.
“His body is smaller, but his back looks bigger now... Yes, that could explain it.”
“Yeah, I think I know what you mean.”
“Bjorn is a great giant! I’m sure someday he’ll leave the biggest mark on this world!”

Ugh, I really wished they wouldn’t do things like this. I hastily changed the subject to the conversation I had with Kyle. As it was related to the palace, everyone except Ainar forgot about the nickname Giant and listened with interest.
“A party in our honor, huh? I wonder how many will attend.”
“You are naive, Mr. Urikfried. It’d be quicker to count how many won’t be attending.”
“What?”
“They may curse the palace behind its back, but who would want to make an enemy of them? Especially when they’re even rewarding their hard work.”
“S-Still, adventurers have pride. Yandel! Say something!”
“Actually, I agree with Raven.”
“...What?”
“If they’re not planning to defect to Noark’s side, of course they should take what they can get from the palace.”

Adventurers never lost out. Not usually to this extent, but most of them were sensitive to losses. Anyway, since we discussed everything there was to discuss, we all ate together and eventually our guests left.
“Then I’ll be heading home.”
“See you soon. Call me if you need something.”
Raven and Mr. Bear left. Ainar went to the holy land and Missha also left to get groceries. The house was suddenly quiet. But before long, I heard a knock.
“Teterud...?”
“Haha! I came because I heard you were still recovering. Can you drink?”
“...Keep it a secret from Missha.”
Although it was broad daylight, this was a friendly face, so I let Teterud and his clanmates inside and we had a drink together. Just as that was nearing a close, another visitor arrived.
“Oh, you’re here too?”
“Melter Fend.”
“Just call me Melter. Long time no see, Bjorn. I wanted to come see you earlier, but I was delayed by the funerals of members of my clan who passed. Oh, can I come in?”
“Of course.”

Teterud and his clanmates left after a while for business, so after that, things turned into a private meeting with Melter. The main topic of conversation was the battle with Blue Mane. There was an incredible story behind that.
“You awakened an aura...?”
“Haha, not awakened, exactly. But I can see the path sometimes and use it a bit.”
Melter, a former adventurer and apprentice knight, had manifested an aura during the battle.
Well, it still seems unstable, but a rank-three adventurer who can use an aura?
I could picture Melter’s name becoming infamous throughout the city. It probably wouldn’t take too long, either. After all, many high-ranking adventurers had died.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Anyway, the visitors didn’t end with Melter.
“Yandel! Are you inside!? I heard you can’t even walk properly yet!”
The warriors I met that day and adventurers who came to say thank you lined up at my door. We drank. Missha served meals.
“It would have been nice to have Albertine here as well...” At times, we held a moment of silence.
Those weren’t the only visitors. Hikurod and Rotmiller came after hearing the news.
“So, you’re called the Giant now? How sad the lives of dwarves are. Hahaha!”
Ragna and Administrator Shavin came over for a friendly gathering.
“I see you won’t be able to come to the library for a while... I’ll bring you some books to read next time.”
The chieftain even came all the way over from the holy land.

“I heard you’ve done a big thing this time. I am proud of you.” The chieftain seemed to know about the party in our honor and offered me a warning. “The king’s laughter can be poisonous. Don’t get too close to the royal family.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
“Good. Then, let’s drink!”
Such visits continued over several days. There were also several return visits. That was because invitations to the party had been sent out in bulk from the palace not too long ago.
“...Are you going to fight this?”
“We must fight! If we let this pass, they will look down on us forever!”
While some came to talk about fighting back, others offered me serious advice. Ratio-wise, there were a lot more of the latter.
“Set aside your anger for a moment and think rationally.”
“You are the one who suffered the most that day. If you want to accept the reward, what can they say?”
“If they cancel the reward ceremony, the dead adventurers will not receive any compensation at all. Think of the bereaved families.”
“To say it coldly, this is a great opportunity for you. I hope you don’t pass up on it. I’m really saying this for your own good.”

My conversations with them brought to mind many things. Now, my choices impacted not only myself but a lot of people. With that sense of responsibility in mind, I listened to each one of their opinions.
That was until Missha finally exploded. “Hey! Tell them to stop coming! Or, no, just meet them somewhere outside of the house!”
Yeah, she was well within her rights to be irritated.
On May 10th, a little over a week after the disaster, we woke up early and got ready to head out. Today was the day of the appreciation party.
“Agh! T-Tighterrr!”
“Y-You’ll die, Missha!”
“It’s okay, just—hissss!”
As I waited quietly on the sofa, Missha came out of the room wearing the dress Ainar helped her put on. She looked somewhat embarrassed.
“...Uh, i-is it weirrrd?”
“...No, not at all. It suits you.”

I was being 100 percent sincere. The fancy dress was totally different from the tight-fitting pants and fluttering everyday skirts she normally wore. Red accented the otherwise white canvas of fabric and it was around knee-length, so she didn’t seem to have problems moving her tail. Was this out of consideration for beastpeople?
I should thank whoever made it later.
“S-Stop staring.”
“Ah, sorry.”
“Is that it...?”
“The pin in your hair is pretty,” I quickly added.
“Um, what about the necklace?”
“That too.”
“Hmm, rrreally?” I guessed I had passed the test because Missha didn’t say much after that.
The vibe was awkward so I changed the subject. “Where’s Ainar?”
“Oh, right. Ainar! What arrre you doing? Come out!”
“B-But...! I’m embarrassed too! Can’t I just wear armor?”
“I told you, you can’t wear armorrr or bring weapons into the palace! Come out already. You don’t look strange at all!”
In the end, Ainar got dragged out by Missha. She wasn’t in a dress but a slim-fit men’s suit that fit her perfectly, almost as if it were custom-made.
It looks like a uniform.

The tight-fitting white pants, shirt, and coat coming down to her thighs were made of high-quality fabric. The coat and shirt were full of all kinds of insignias and embroidery, giving them a luxurious feel.
“I-It’s strange, isn’t it?! Yes! Th-there’s no way clothes like this would suit a warrior like m—”
“It suits you well, what’s wrong?”
“Ugh, don’t make fun of me...” It had been a while since I’d seen her like this.

“I’m not making fun of you. I have similar clothes too.” Ainar and I had been gifted similar outfits. The base for mine was navy blue with brown accents like my hair color, and the color arrangement, shape of the embroidery, and other details were much more masculine. Well, the biggest difference was something else, though.

“It’s tight.” I adjusted my tight-fitting clothes and checked the mirror: Barbarian Tailcoat Mode. In some ways, I looked more intimidating now than I did in armor. Were suits always this muscle-defining? I looked like a gangster.
“Bjorn! There’s a carriage outside!”
“Really? Then let’s go.”

When we finished our preparations and headed outside, the driver who was waiting there greeted us cordially. “Nice to meet you. Mr. Bjorn Yandel, Ms. Missha Karlstein, Ms. Ainar Fenelin. My name is Jack Haynes, and I have the honor of escorting you all to the palace today. If there are any inconveniences, please feel free to pull this rope and let me know at any time.”
It really felt like I’d become someone important.
“Wow, so this is a personal carriage...”
“Oooh! Candy! The candy is free!”
As the wheels rolled, the carriage began to move toward the very center of Rafdonia, where the king resided.

chapters.title: Chapter 233: New Era (3)
paragraphs: In a study filled with the faint scent of old books, a nervous young man was making a report to a middle-aged man wearing glasses. “As a result of the final analysis, the team has determined that it was likely Belbev Ruingenes who installed the magic circle and Lyranne Vivian who activated it.”
“You mean both are in the city?”
“Yes. Judging by the fact that Noark’s protective barrier is functioning normally, it is highly likely that they are inside Rafdonia.”
“Their stealth is definitely shocking.”

“They are relentless. Then I will move on to the report of the casualties that was compiled this morning.” In a melancholy tone, the young man reported the total damages incurred in the recent incident.
However, the middle-aged man just listened nonchalantly. “Yes, many have died.”

Seventy percent of the adventurers who frequented floors four and above had died. The 1600 survivors were either those who had been abandoned or adventurers who hadn’t entered the labyrinth at all. To be honest, it was a huge loss equivalent to a dimensional collapse.
“It’s better this way.” The prime minister of Rafdonia, Marquess Tercerion, smirked and let the contents of the report go in one ear and flow out the other.
At this, the young man tilted his head. “Sorry?”
“It’s nothing. I need to think. You may leave.”
“...Yes, Father.”
“Refer to me by position, in the palace.”
“Yes, Prime Minister.”
Soon, the man gestured with his hand and his son bowed politely before leaving the study.
I’ll have to contact the Magic Tower soon.
Tercerion got up and headed to the window. He could see servants rushing around in preparation for today’s event.
Shaaa.
When he opened the window wide, a strong wind blew in. The sun was warm and the sky was clear without a single cloud in sight. “His Majesty will like this.”
It was the perfect day to start a new era.
The royal capital, Karnon, was a special district that commoners could not even enter without permission.
“Ohhh, is that the royal palace!?”

As we passed through a giant gate engraved with the symbol of the royal family, a road leading straight to the royal palace appeared before us. Petals were scattered all over the ground. On the boulevard, crowds of onlookers were watching the parade. Of course, very few were nobility. Even if the royal capital was called the city of nobles, 90 percent of the population was made up of servants who worked or resided there.
“Wow! A parade of heroes!”
“Sprinkle the petals!”
I didn’t know how much they were being paid for this, but the servants lining the boulevard greeted us passionately as we passed them by.
After a long while, the carriage stopped at the outer wall of the palace. “We have arrived. Were there any inconveniences during your journey?” The same went for the hundreds of other carriages too.
“Let’s get off.”
“Oh, wait! Let me catch my brrreath, okay?”
Are you nervous now?
Well, this was her first time in the royal capital, after all. “...Let me know when you’re ready.”
“Ahhh, I think I’m rrready.”

When I got off the carriage, I saw familiar faces, survivors who’d stood on the line between life and death with me during the latest tragedy. Because of the distance between us, we could only exchange glances.
“I am Fert, the guide for today’s heroes. Please come with me. I will lead the way.”

After a simple identification process at the castle gate, we followed the guide into the palace. Its official name was the Palace of Glory, a palace used to receive guests during banquets or royal family events.
Befitting the name of “the palace,” the interior was splendid. Ainar turned to me, cowed. “B-Bjorn...”
Geez, this kid always acted like this in the strangest of places. “Stand tall. You’re here as a guest, remember?”
“...O-Okay!”
“Come this way.”
Following the guide, we arrived at a private reception room of about sixty square meters.

“It is an honor to greet our heroes.” As soon as we entered, ladies-in-waiting swarmed us to tidy our hair and fix our clothes. In the meantime, the dedicated guide informed us of simple etiquette and the order the banquet would proceed. After who knew how long of that, Raven and Abman, who had arrived ten minutes earlier, came to our reception room.
“Mr. Yandel!”
“Oh, I almost didn’t recognize you all like that.”
They, too, were dressed differently than usual, Raven in a long, traditional dress that dragged on the floor and Mr. Bear in a clean suit.

“Ha, it looks a bit awkward, doesn’t it?” Mr. Bear scratched his cheek, embarrassed. Apparently, his wife helped him dress, but they insisted he change once he arrived. It was surprising they had something in his size.
“Ah, all tailcoats for guests are enchanted with magic.” According to the guide, thousands of magic clothes would adjust to the wearer regardless of their size.
Enchanted clothes?
It was a logical yet outrageous waste. How often did guests without banquet attire like us ever visit the royal palace?
“Then Raven, did you change your clothes here too?”
“No, I’m wearing my own.”
“...I see.” As a wizard belonging to the upper class, it seemed she had at least one set of formal clothes.
“Wow, so prrretty. How much does something like that cost?”
“Uh... I’m not sure. To be honest, this was a gift from Master.”
“Oh, really? Anyway, you look like an elf wearrring that. Not the elf tribe, but the old elves from fairy tales.”
“You mean pixies?”
“Ah, yeah. Those.”
“Hmm, you’re not making fun of me for being short, right?”
“Of course not! It’s rrreally pretty!”
Missha and Raven’s girl talk quickly kicked off. Mr. Bear, Ainar, and I stepped back and held a different conversation.
“Hey, Yandel. Have you heard anything more about the rewards? There’s a rank-four essence I’ve been wanting for a long time and I was wondering if it’ll be possible for me to get it.”
“I haven’t heard much, either.”
“Anyway, Bjorn, I’m hungry. When are they feeding us?”
“If you can’t wait, eat some jerky.”
“Oh, did you bring some?”
“Give me one too. I want to chew on something.”
As we sat side by side chewing on jerky, the guide, who had left for a bit, returned. “Preparations for your entrance are complete. Let us go.”

The hallway outside the guest room was bustling with people, and the guides lined us up in an orderly fashion. For reference, our party was located at the very front, with Melter Fend on the left of us and Kyle on the right.
“Oh, you’re here.”
“You look good in a suit too.”
“Now, stand over here.”
...Geez, no pressure.
“Why am I in the middle?”

“Haha, wouldn’t it be weird otherwise? All of us are just people who followed your lead.” I couldn’t argue with that, but this man really had a tendency to put me on a pedestal. As I was about to say something, Kyle looked straight ahead and spoke again. “It’s beginning. Look ahead.”
“The heroes are entering!”
The door opened to the sound of a loud shout.
Bwoooooo!
With the blare of a trumpet, a spirited musical performance began.
“Go ahead.”
When I stepped past the threshold at Kyle’s prompting, countless adventurers followed behind me.
Step, step.

The space beyond the door was a rectangular hall wide enough to accommodate thousands of people, and a red carpet was spread all the way to an empty throne. I continued down the carpet. Walking without crutches was agonizing, but I suffered through it for the sake of my pride as a barbarian.
Step, step.

As I continued walking, knights drew their swords to pay their respects and priests didn’t hold back on using their divine power to bestow blessings. As for the nobles, they applauded us from afar. It was treatment too extreme for an adventurer just a year old to be receiving. It didn’t feel particularly great. The others probably felt the same.
We’re not some spectacle to watch. Or are we?
Tap.

When I stopped walking, the adventurers behind me also stopped in a line. It was different from the orderliness of soldiers. Since they hadn’t learned the drills, the lines and rows didn’t match up and our clothes also gave off a chaotic vibe.
“Pffft.”
Was that funny to them? A nobleman could be heard laughing in the distance, and that laughter gradually spread. At the same time, I heard the sound of something tearing.
Squeeze.

When I turned my head slightly to look behind me, an adventurer was clenching his fists. It was a warrior who had cleared the way with me in the cave. He had been unstoppable when crushing monster heads.
He has more restraint than I thought.

This was another side of warriors I hadn’t known about. I didn’t know why, but I didn’t like it. Maybe that was the reason I released an involuntary cry that echoed through the vast space. “Behelaaah!”
This hadn’t been my intention, but answering shouts echoed behind me. “Behelaaah!” It was the cry of other barbarians, as well as other warriors who were now addicted to our battle cry.
“These ridiculous bastards, even inside the palace...”

Most of the other adventurers looked stunned or let out unamused sighs. The nobles, on the other hand, were a little different. Did they think this was some kind of performance? The nobles went silent for a moment out of surprise, then applauded and whistled.
These guys are funny sons of bitches.

It was kind of amusing, but the tension eased. The adventurers who had been uncomfortable with this place—the luxurious palace, the countless looks of nobles who hardly showed their faces in public, the awkward tailcoats, etcetera—regained their cool a bit.
Mm-hmm, this is how bold adventurers should act. Especially after everything we went through to survive.
Kyle grinned in satisfaction at the sight. “I told you. Who else could stand in front if not for you?”
Well, maybe he was right. Who else would do something like this, if not a barbarian?
“Q-Quiet! Please be quiet! His Excellency Ageni Lawton Tercerion, Prime Minister of Rafdonia, has arrived!”

The prime minister appeared in the middle of all the excitement. He appeared to be in his early fifties, with a kindly impression and gray hair. The prime minister, who evoked the air of a principal, stood in front of the empty throne and began his speech, starting with a light joke. “Haha, I apologize. I arrived late. Please don’t be angry with me, heroes. It is such a beautiful day, after all.”

The speech naturally drifted to the topic of the weather and smoothly continued to the next topic. There was nothing particularly interesting to note. After reciting our achievements one by one, he explained to the nobles why we had been invited here today.
“These people achieved something that not only famed clans but knights could not achieve. If it weren’t for them, we might never have known what happened in the labyrinth that day.”
Coming back alive with information on Noark was our nominal feat. That was because they couldn’t outwardly say we were being given carrots to suppress an adventurer resistance.
“And so, I, Ageni Lawton Tercerion, praise their achievements on behalf of the ailing His Majesty, the king!”

The long speech ended and the prime minister began to deal out rewards according to merit. First, all survivors were given ten million stones and the right to access the royal capital of Karnon. From there, additional rewards would be bestowed based on achievements. And we were the first in the order.

“Melter Fend, commander of Clan Nartel, step forward. You made a great contribution in leading the battle to victory by defeating the criminal Blue Mane of the Blue Wolf tribe.” Apparently, they’d already managed to collect all the information they needed, as the prime minister mentioned our achievements in detail. “The Silver Soul Repository will be opened for you. You may choose one essence and one other item. Also, you will be given a reward of twenty-five million stones.”
“Thank you.” Melter had obtained a ticket to the treasure vault containing rank-four essences and equipment of the same caliber.
Can I look forward to my turn?
In truth, Melter’s accomplishment was the smallest out of the three of us. The reason why he’d been able to defeat Wolf Man in the first place was because I took down Corpse Collector.
Unfortunately, I had to wait, as next was Mister Kyle. “Iron Sorcerer, Sir Kyle Pevrosk, step forward.”
“It’s been a while, Prime Minister.”
“Forgive my absence due to governmental affairs.”

There were three achievements the prime minister mentioned for Kyle: using his wisdom to suggest a way for the expedition to survive, throwing off Berzak with Mass Teleport, and inflicting damage against Fallen Scholar during the battle in Goblin Forest.
“I hear you have been requesting permission to study magic forbidden to you for a long time, correct? Starting today, you are a proud royal sorcerer of Rafdonia.”

“You have no idea how happy I am to hear that, Prime Minister. Thank you very much.” Kyle had been promoted to royal sorcerer. In other words, he now had the chance to learn and master all kinds of magic to his heart’s content.
“Barbarian warrior, Bjorn, son of Yandel, step forward.”
It was finally my turn. Perhaps I was a different case than Melter and Kyle, who already had reputations, because the prime minister seemed to take a moment to study me before reciting my merits.

“Your merits are as follows: nobly stopping an internal conflict and allowing many knights to return to their families; fighting most courageously on the dangerous frontlines and inspiring others; acting as bait to buy time from Berzak so that other adventurers could survive; and driving Abed Necrapeto, a soul cursed by another realm, to an impasse and making a decisive contribution toward victory.”
When he put it that way, it sounded like nothing had really happened.

“These words alone cannot truly capture your hard work. But nonetheless, I commend you on behalf of the palace! The Gold Soul Repository will be opened to you. You will be able to select whatever essence or item you desire, and you will also be granted fifty million stones. Moreover!” The prime minister continued, “You will be awarded the title of baronet.”
...Huh?

chapters.title: Chapter 234: New Era (4)
paragraphs: Baronet was a title directly above an ordinary knight.
“What in the...”
“Baronet!”
The prime minister’s declaration left the nobles stunned, and rightfully so.
“This is unprecedented! To give a barbarian an inheritable title!”

A baronet could pass down their title. Not perpetually, of course—just to their son and grandchild. But in some ways, a baronet could be considered better than an honorary baron, whose title only existed temporarily.
It’s not like I deliberately chose a nobility path. I didn’t expect to earn a title.

To be honest, I was dumbfounded. In the game, you could clear quests for marquesses or above to accumulate the accomplishment points needed to become a noble. This route had as many cons as it did pros. You were a nobleman, but in truth, you were closer to the vassal of a noble, and so there were restrictions to what you could do. So what had happened to those restrictions?
Well, since commoners and nobles can’t refuse the king’s orders anyway, aren’t restrictions virtually nonexistent? Hmm, that seems to be the case, but...
That was when the prime minister shouted, “Everyone, quiet!”
“This is His Majesty’s command.”
The commotion that seemed unlikely to settle any time soon was instantly calmed by that one sentence. That was how much weight the king’s name carried in this country.
“You will be informed of the date that your title will be awarded as soon as it’s decided.”

Anyway, that ended my bestowal of rewards. The prime minister didn’t even ask if I would accept the title. He probably never considered otherwise. Well, I had no intention of rejecting it. This wasn’t just a game. In other words, becoming a noble came with all kinds of conveniences and new potential plays.
“Portyan Miriant from Clan Nartel, step forward!”

After my turn, the process of handing out rewards according to merit continued for a while. At this time, my teammates stepped forward one by one as well and received decent rewards. Missha, Ainar, and Mr. Bear got ten million stones each as reward money and had the option to select either a rank-five essence or equivalent equipment. At her request, Raven received the right to learn palace magic instead of an ordinary reward.

In Erwen’s case, she received a rank-four essence or an item equivalent to that—the greatest reward among my comrades. She was recognized as the second greatest contributor in the battle against Corpse Collector, and was also receiving compensation as a bereaved family member. Even though she hadn’t been able to attend this event, today was just the announcement and the actual reward would be given later, so that wasn’t a problem.
“Mr. Yandel, is Erwen still at her holy land?”
“Sounds like the funeral is over, but she must still have a lot on her mind.”
“I see...” Raven, who asked for news about Erwen, trailed off. I asked if she had something to say to her, but I didn’t get an answer.
After a long while, the long reward ceremony came to an end and the banquet began. “What an amazing day. Everyone, please enjoy this event with the heroes of the new era with a happy heart!”

Because there were so many people in attendance, the banquet was being held in two different spaces, the grand inner hall where the reward ceremony had taken place and the outdoor garden where all sorts of delicacies were laid out. It wasn’t compulsory, but most adventurers enjoyed the banquet outdoors. That was what the vibe was like. The interior was quiet with classical music playing. Because more than half of the nobles chose to enjoy the banquet there, it was awkward for the adventurers to stay.
“Mr. Yandel, what are you going to do?”
“Of course I’m going outside.” We also chose the outdoors.
“If we stay here, we could expand our network.”
Since my baronet title was confirmed anyway, networking didn’t necessarily have to be done today. I didn’t want to do that today, either.
“Yandel! Yandel is here!”
“Huh? What’s a nobleman doing out here?”
“Hahaha! Yandel isn’t like that!”

That I had been bestowed a title had perhaps evoked a sense of distance, because the adventurers greeted me warmly when I came out to join them. Whew, good thing I did. No matter how I looked at it, my relationships with these guys felt more valuable than the ones I could have with those noble bastards.
“Everyone is looking at you. Why don’t you say a few words? We heard more than enough inside, but I think it’ll sound different when you say it,” Kyle said from beside me.
So, a short toast, huh? I wondered what would be best.
Just go at it like a barbarian.
I didn’t have to think for long. Was there a need to? We’d already heard enough pretentious praise.
“Good work, everyone!” This should be enough for today. “Now, let’s drink up and enjoy!”
My toast ended super quick. The barbarians, who preferred to keep things brief by nature, shouted in response, “Behelaaah!”
The same went for the adventurers.
“To think the day would come when I’d get to drink inside the royal palace!”
“Yandel is going to be a baronet, what are you worried about?! Let’s enjoy ourselves!”
“Woohoo!”
The adventurers let go of their discomfort about being at the palace and began to enjoy the banquet to their hearts’ content. This applied to us as well.
“Wow, Bjorn! Try some of this! I don’t know what kind of meat it is, but the bones are crispy and delicious!”
“Uh, you’re not supposed to eat the bone...”
“Huh? Why?”
“...Never mind. As long as it’s tasty to you.”
The greasy food here was a different kind of delicious from Missha’s home-cooked meals. Drinks went down easily, and there were numerous comrades around to drink and chat with about past struggles.
This feels like an after-party or something.

A pleasant time befitting a banquet followed. The atmosphere darkened whenever talk of a deceased comrade came up, but after a brief moment of silence, everyone regained their spirits. Time marched on just like that and soon it was nearing sunset.
“You look like you’re having fun.” Melter, who had been enjoying the banquet with the nobles indoors, came out.
“Did you have fun inside?”
“Of course not. I had to stop myself from running out of there.”

“Looks like you’re going through it too.” I could understand Melter’s decision to enjoy the banquet with the nobles inside. He led a clan, after all. I was sure he didn’t want to miss the opportunity to network with nobility, because one day he may need their help. “Since you’re here, take a bottle.”
“A bottle...?”
“Why bother using a glass?”
“Haha, if I had known things were like this, I would have come out sooner. But where are your teammates?”
“Except for Abman, everyone got tired of us and wandered off.”
“Really? I thought that barbarian girl would be different.”
“Oh, she can’t drink that much.” To be more exact, she could drink, but after getting drunk on the atmosphere and downing continuous bottles, she had passed out.
“Yandel, there’s an empty bottle here. You’re not drunk yet, are you?”
“Of course not.”
Now that Melter was here, I continued drinking with the warriors around me. This was one of the pros of having Bjorn Yandel’s body. He handled alcohol incredibly well.
As I continued chugging down drinks and testing the limits of this body for the first time, Missha returned. “Ugh, the smell of alcohol...”
“Oh, Missha. Did you have a good time?”
“Yeah. There’s something like a perrrformance over there. It’s fun. It would have been great if you came too...”
“There will be more of that later. But where’s Raven?”
“She’s drunk and talking about complicated stuff with the wizarrrds.”

Discussing complicated topics while drunk? Wizards definitely weren’t to be trifled with. “I’m going to walk around for a while.” I excused myself from Melter, got up from the drinking party, and walked the garden with Missha. While not as much as the drinking party of warriors I was just a part of, everyone here was having a good time. Nobles were mingling here and there too.
“Oh? I can’t even imagine an army of thousands of corpses.”
“Me neither. That must have been so scary. You’re amazing.”

Just like the time I was the star of the count’s banquet, the nobles were the first to approach the adventurers around them with interest. Well, not all of them had big heads like the titled nobles. Young, borderline aristocrats were in truth no different from middle-class commoners.
Huh? But why didn’t anyone come over to us?
That was strange, but I soon understood. How could anyone approach dozens of rugged, rowdy warriors?
“Bjorn, should we sit and rest for a bit?”
“That would be good...” I wasn’t that drunk but because of the effects of the last battle, it was hard to walk for too long.
“...Why are you sitting on the floorrr? Sit beside me.”
“I think that thing will break.”

Missha sat on a bench and I sat on the grass, and we just quietly passed the time. Was it because I drank so much? For some reason, the loud banquet sounded like background music in the distance, and thoughts of all kinds passed through my head.
“Yandel! You’re Sir Bjorn Yandel who just received the title of baronet, right?”

As I was enjoying the comfortable silence, some nobles recognized me and approached me. But Sir Yandel? Were they already treating me like a noble? I didn’t want this time to be interrupted so I turned them away with appropriate excuses, but I couldn’t use that method on everyone.
“Haha, so you’ve been here.” This was a non-collateral, titled aristocrat, someone with whom having an awkward relationship could lead to trouble in the future... Dwalkie’s half-brother.
“...Baron Martoin.”

“In truth, I tried to come see you a few times earlier, but I didn’t approach you because you seemed to be having a good time.” Excuses. It was obvious he just couldn’t bring himself to go through the warriors to get near me.
“Thank you for your consideration.”
“Haha, it’s nothing. You are the star of this banquet, after all.”
