After a formal greeting, I had a brief conversation with Baron Martoin. It was a more fruitful conversation than I thought. Apparently, when commoner-born nobles were made there was bound to be tension, but I was going to be a different case.
“How so?”
“Because your title was bestowed by the king himself. An adventurer whom the king has a close eye on? Who would dare to touch you? Everyone will be anxious to befriend you.”
The king, huh? I always felt this, but every time the king came up in conversation, I felt uneasy, including when the chieftain came to talk to me.
Anyway, if this is true...
Deciding to joke around a bit, I greeted the butler who was seated next to the baron. “Anyway, long time no see, butler.”

The butler’s face turned white at my greeting. Well, it made sense that he’d be scared since the barbarian who used to crush heads and chew bones now had great fame and power. “P-Please e-excuse my behavior back then...”
When I grinned at him, the butler trembled and apologized. It didn’t feel particularly satisfying.
Now I just feel like I’m bullying a weak kid.
Even a sandbag needed to provide some moderate impact to make it fun. I stopped teasing the butler and continued talking to Baron Martoin. Naturally, Dwalkie’s name came up.
“Anyway, where is my brother?”
The baron brought up his brother, whom he hadn’t given a second look back then like he wanted to use him to get closer to me. Missha and I both froze at the same time.
What the fuck? Is he joking right now?
“Where... is he...?”
As I echoed him while barely schooling my expression, the butler’s face paled even more. One thing was clear: this guy knew the situation. “My Lord, as I said before, Riol Warb Dwalkie is...”
The baron already knew too. He’d just forgotten.

“Oh, right. My memory is not what it used to be at my age. Haha.” The baron gave a hearty, embarrassed laugh. My insides, which were fine even after countless bottles of alcohol, were seething. Was that why?
Squeeze.

When I came back to my senses, Missha was squeezing my arm tightly, a worried look on her face. I patted the back of her hand to say, Don’t worry, and removed it. I wasn’t someone who had nothing to lose anymore. There were too many things I was responsible for.
“Yes, I understand. Don’t worry. As you get older, you may develop issues with your head.”
“...Huh? Oh, I guess you could phrase it like that. Hahaha.”
I reached out and offered to shake the baron’s hand. “I have somewhere to go, so I have to leave. It was nice seeing you.”
“Really? That’s too bad. See you later,” Baron Martoin said in disappointment, reciprocating my handshake. Then he asked one last question. “Oh, but where are you going?”
I brushed off the hand I had used to shake the baron’s as if to remove the dust on it and answered, “Oh, I just suddenly want to wash my hands.”
Dirty things should be washed away, after all.
Baron Martoin was thickheaded. “...Is that so? Anyway, I’ll call on you sometime soon, so don’t refuse. Now that you are a noble, there is a lot you have to learn.”
The baron casually sent me off. Maybe the problem was with me. You wouldn’t normally imagine that a barbarian would make a sarcastic remark like that.
It might be one of the few disadvantages of being a barbarian.
“You were verrry patient.” Missha petted my hair like she was proud of me.
I slowly got up and headed inside too. Washing my hands was something I could ask any passing wizard for, but I also wanted to use the bathroom.
“Are you surrre I don’t need to go with you?”
“...Do you think I’m a child?”
I parted ways with Missha and headed to the bathroom with the help of a guide. Coming back out, I was about to return to the banquet when someone who recognized me came up to me.

“Oh, there you are.” It was Count Ferdehilt, the organizer of the banquet I attended last time. He had said something strange to me as he awarded me the winning prize of the tournament, No. 7777: Garphas’ Necklace.
“I will call on you privately when you are more ready.”
Up to today, he had never called me once.
“You speak as if you were looking for me.”
“That’s because I was. Why don’t we go over there and have a drink? It won’t take long.”
“If you say so.” Since he was a man with an amount of power that could not be compared to the likes of Baron Martoin, I obediently followed him inside.
“Here.” When I sat down at the table, the count poured me a drink and I downed it at once.
“My team is waiting for me. Can I hear your business with me?”
“Haha, of course.” Thankfully, the count seemed to understand and got straight to the point without irritation. “Arabella, my youngest daughter. You’ve met her once, correct?”
Something’s off here...
“What do you think? Isn’t she pretty?” Sure enough, the count wrapped his arm around his daughter’s shoulder and pushed her in front of me.
“I-I’m Arabella...” The count’s daughter, who appeared to be in her early teens, trembled as her eyes met mine.
Ha, I never thought this would happen to me.

“How about it?” My brain shut off at this shocking turn of events and for a moment, I couldn’t say anything. But to him, I must have looked like I was thinking it over. “Oh, if you already have a woman, don’t worry. You can just take her as a concubine.”
“...Concubine?”

“Oh, didn’t you know?” The count laughed at my muttering and said, “It is a noble’s duty to produce as many descendants as possible to aid this country. If you become a noble, you’ll be able to take in three concubines.”
Duty, my ass. I felt like going to the bathroom again.

chapters.title: Chapter 235: New Era (5)
paragraphs: Take my daughter as your wife and your lover as your concubine. Upon making that sudden proposal, the count continued. “Limenin, the first Abyss Seeker to reach the tenth floor. Great Pikma, the adventurer who journeyed to every district of the vast sixth floor and created a map. Juggernaut, the Iron Hero. Besides them, there have been countless heroes. Do you know what they all had in common? Their journeys were always backed by strong sponsors.”
In the end, I had no choice but to ask. I fully got what he was trying to say, but still. “What do you gain by sponsoring me?”
“There is always a shortage of talent in this city. I was already planning on sponsoring you even if this incident hadn’t happened.” Those didn’t sound like empty words.
“What exactly do you mean by that?”
“It is common for nobles to sponsor promising adventurers, because it helps their reputation.”
I already knew about that. You could say it was a highbrow hobby of the upper class. To put it in modern terms, it was a lot like collecting luxury cars, but I didn’t know this next part.

“Sometimes, this becomes the measure of a family’s power. If they don’t have any sponsored adventurers they are shunned, and if their adventurers have no significant achievements, they’re seen as having bad judgment.”
Now I was seeing that this went beyond the realm of a mere hobby. For noblemen, the social sphere was a political arena and the opinions of others were powerful.

“The wealth of the Ferdehilt family is not inferior to that of any great noble line or Order of Knights. But there is one thing we are missing.” I didn’t know much about the count but I did know this. “Despite our efforts, we have not had a prominent adventurer for a long time.”
“So that’s why you said you’d call on me when I was ready.”

“I see no reason to hide it. At the time, I didn’t have confidence in you. If my sponsored adventurer died soon after I chose them, that would damage the reputation of my family as well.” Yet, not wanting someone else to snatch me, he warned me not to accept the invitations of other nobles. An act of calling dibs. “If I knew this would happen, I would have sponsored you without hesitation back then.”
I smirked at the regret dripping from his tone. If he did, the count’s reputation would have risen as much as my stock price, and he wouldn’t have had to offer his daughter to me like this.

“I have no doubts now. You are going to be an even bigger figure in years to come. Many adventurers have died, but this won’t be the end. As always, time will pass and the vacancies will be filled, and you will surely become the figurehead leading this new era.”
“...You flatter me.”
“Well, we’ll find out in time. Anyway, that should be enough to explain what I gain from this. Will you give me an answer now?”

I silently pondered this for a moment. Or, rather, I pretended to, since he’d be upset if I refused right away. “Sorry, but a relationship like that would be tough.” It was a refusal with as little room for negotiation as possible.
“Think carefully about this. Everyone will want to be on friendly terms with you, but who will want a blood relationship? I can do more for you than you can imagine.”

My conversation with the count ended there. After briefly saying goodbye to his daughter, I returned outdoors. As soon as I came out, Missha found me. “Bjorn! Wherrre did you go?! I went looking for you because you took so long and you werrre gone!”
“Ah, there was a nobleman who wanted to talk.”

I didn’t need to tell her what just happened. Making an excuse, I returned to where I was earlier and had another drink. But the more I laughed and chatted, the more I remembered what the count had said.
“You will surely become the figurehead leading this new era.”
The banquet came to an end.
The performance ended and the cacophony stopped. The damned banquet was finally over.
“Fuckers.”

At first, he hadn’t known what kind of banquet this was. As his only source of information had dried up, he was no different from blind. Communicating with the outside world was impossible. However, thanks to the conversation with the prime minister he’d had a little while ago, he came to learn about what had happened recently.
“It’s been a long time since we’ve met face-to-face. Those scoundrels from Noark dealt us a blow. There has been a lot of damage.”
“A lot of damage? Just how much...?” the man had asked, trying to hide his rising anxiety.
The prime minister had answered, “Whatever you’re imagining, even more than that.”

Seventy percent of adventurers on the fourth floor and above were dead. Of course, the part that was important to him was something else. Most adventurers active on the seventh floor or higher, large clans that could easily live without climbing for the rest of their lives yet pushed themselves to go even higher, were also dead. How long would it take to repair the damage that had been done?
Ha, I’m gonna freak the fuck out, he’d thought. I should’ve bashed that skull in when I had the chance.
The man gritted his teeth. When he heard the news, the first thing that came to mind was, They got me.
“Was this... what you were aiming for?” he asked, barely suppressing his murderous energy.
The prime minister answered with a smile. “We didn’t know this would happen, either. If you want, you can use that ability of yours to check if it’s true.”

It seemed true that he hadn’t known, but he’d been tricked by that clever tongue more than once. “Piss off. It’s obvious things would’ve ended up like this even without this particular incident happening.”
“Well, what do you think?”
“Shut the hell up. If you had let me kill them all during the conquest, this never would have happened.”

It felt like his question had finally been answered. At the time of the conquest, Rafdonia had a much more significant advantage. They’d taken a lot of damage, but if they’d pushed a little further, they could have ended the battle decisively. However, Rafdonia did not do so. They took their time, and in the end, Noark activated an ancient barrier and locked their castle gates.
“Why don’t you be honest? That you had no intention of keeping our promise from the start.”
“Don’t be disrespectful. His Majesty the King placed the honor of the royal family on the line for that promise. Do not doubt that it will be seen through.”
“Don’t doubt, my ass.”
That was when it had hit the man—or more like when he had finally admitted to himself—that these bastards had no intention of letting them go.
He’s probably acting so arrogantly because he thinks we have no way of escaping, he thought.
On that note, the prime minister had left. The reason why he hadn’t bashed his skull in and instead let him leave was simple: because night inevitably had to fall.
Ha... where should I look now?

He had thought the palace would have some kind of clue, but he hadn’t been able to find any. Rather, he only just realized there were no answers here. It was safe to say he had lost ten years on that hunch, but the man did not give up.
If I have nowhere to go, I’ll just go to Noark.
Although weaker than Rafdonia in terms of power, they would have the determination to clear it.
Ugh, whatever. I’ll think it over outside.

The man closed his eyes, stretched his hand out into the air, and slowly started the visualization process. Dissolution of Stars was the skill of the Dark Lord Dead Red, whose essence he had obtained in his last trip into the labyrinth. And with no witnesses around to see him obtain it, it was one even the palace didn’t realize he possessed.
Crackle.
A dark sphere spun above the man’s hand and absorbed the mana around it, including the mana in the sealing magic circle located in his room.
Crackkk.
Eventually, the magic circle broke.
Bang!
The dark sphere promptly exploded and dissolved everything within a hundred-yard radius.
Ding! Ding! Ding!
In time with the explosion, he could sense the knights stationed in the surrounding area approaching. Geez, so quick.
“J-Jailbreak!”
“Stop him!”
The man grinned. “Hey, take another step and you’re dead.”

The knights flinched at the murderous intent radiating from the man. Even though they shouted about the king and loyalty like fanatics every day, they seemed to be aware their lives were precious. The sight made him feel a bit better.

“Foolish bastards.” The man sneered and leaped high into the air. Then, as if to relish in his freedom, he used Spatial Interference to step on air and all too easily escaped the palace. He reached a height of hundreds of meters in less than a minute.
This damned city hasn’t changed a bit. Castle walls strangling it in all four directions like iron bars... Oh, wait. I can’t enter Noark right now because of the barrier.
After traveling for a long while, the man belatedly came to that realization and stopped to think in mid-air.
Should I go to Bifron? That’s the best place to hide. Yes, that would be best. But... Let’s stop by the Magic Tower first.

Before going into hiding, there was somewhere he needed to visit. He had to restore his information supply route so he’d be able to at least know what was going on in the world while he was in hiding.
I’m curious about what happened to him too... He should be alive, right?
He really hoped so. Thinking those thoughts about someone for the first time in a while, Baeko traversed the night sky.

Five days had passed since the end of the banquet. At that time, I didn’t do much. I just stayed at home and took time to recover, and when I woke up feeling much better than I had yesterday, I went to find a certain family. That was because I had promised.
“Deliver the news to my son. You will definitely be famous by the time you get out of here. That boy would like to meet you.”
His family consisted of a ten-year-old child and a young wife. Despite what he’d said, the child did not smile when he saw me. Yeah, how could he?

“I’ve heard a lot about you. Thank you for coming...” Although I’d traveled four hours by carriage to get there, I ended up only having a brief conversation with the wife. Apparently, she planned to open a shop with the money the bereaved families had received. She said it had been the couple’s longtime dream.
“If you encounter any trouble raising your child or with your finances, feel free to come find me anytime.”
“Why... are you doing so much for us? I heard you only met my husband for the first time that day...”
“Because if we had met somewhere else, we would have been friends.”

“I... see...” The resolute woman who had pulled herself together within ten days for the sake of the child that had been left behind shed silent tears. “Ever since he was young... he always had a childlike side. He always admired heroes. Thank you very, very much. He will be delighted too. If someone like you remembers him...”

And who was a person like me supposed to be? Those words rose up in my throat but I swallowed them down. Whether true or not, I had to. If that was what they wished, that was something I had to do too.
“Bjorn!” As I was quietly reflecting on these thoughts the next day, Missha burst through the door. “Erwen! Errrwen is here!”
So she’s sorted herself out too.

When I promptly went downstairs, I saw Erwen standing blankly in the living room. This was our first reunion since that day. I wondered what I should say before finally blurting out, “I’m glad you’re here.” If I had led a better life, I would have been able to offer better words of comfort at times like these.
Seeing Erwen’s grim expression, Missha scurried toward her. “D-Did you eat? Are you hungrrry?”
“I’m all right. Thank you, Miss Karlstein.”
“Miss! Just call me sis—ah!” Missha promptly stepped on a mine. “No, no, yes! Missha is enough...” She quickly corrected her title.
At that, Erwen winced. Then she slowly opened her eyes and pasted on a strained smile. “You don’t have to be so accommodating. Really. Thank you though, sis...”
“Ah, yeah... Oh, right. Come this way. I cleared this rrroom thinking you might come—”
“Pardon? Cleared a room?”
“It’s not like you have anywhere else to go. You can stay here as long as you want, so stay until you get back on yourrr feet. It’d be hard to be alone...”

Erwen’s eyes widened at Missha’s words as if she’d just received an offer she hadn’t expected at all. “C-Can I really do that...?” Soon, Erwen moved to look at me as if to ask for my opinion and I shrugged.
“I told you. It was your sister’s wish. I’m your guardian now.”
Erwen clenched her small fists and spoke like she had to force the words out. “...Thank you for your consideration. I really don’t... have... anything left... so—”
“Of course you do. Missha, hurry and take her to her room. Since you added the furniture yourself, you’ll know it better than I do.”
“Ah! Okay!”

Soon after, Missha led Erwen away to give her a tour of the house and things like that. It seemed Erwen hadn’t been sleeping at all lately. After mentioning she wanted to get some rest, Erwen laid down and fell asleep right away.
“...Whew, fighting a monster would leave me with more peace of mind.”
“I agree...”

Afterward, the two of us ate the meal that Missha prepared alone, as Ainar was going to spend the night at the holy land. Then, after dinner, I spent the time chatting with Missha and when it was around midnight, headed to bed.
I could feel my heart racing. I wondered how many people were going to be there today.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
Clown—is that son of a bitch here? I really hope he is.

chapters.title: Chapter 236: Awl (1)
paragraphs: A woman stood in a cramped room with a dark-themed interior and wood-tone blinds letting in white light. There was a two-hundred-dollar single mattress and a work desk with a laptop on top. A tea table for one person was pushed next to the wall with space for only one chair. The woman looked around, a very confused expression on her face.
“This is...”
She knew this place. It was the first apartment she’d rented after moving to New York for a job and the place she was called to every month on the 15th.
“Why am I here?”
The woman experienced a headache as she tried to recall. The memories slowly came back one by one.
“Dark wizards!”
“Stall for time. I will take care of this quickly.”
War had broken out on the first day in the labyrinth. She had gotten to safety with a Multi Teleportation spell, a heartless choice that had had to be made after a long meeting between the leaders.
“Those bastards from the palace are running away and leaving us! Stop them!”
While the knights had been dealing with the adventurers, she and her clanmates ran through the portal.
Shaaa!
A magic circle on the ground had emitted a brilliant light.
Baaaaaang!
And then a huge pillar of fire had covered the sky.
“N-No way...” It finally made sense why, after returning to the city through the portal, she was here. “Fifteen days have passed...?”

The woman hurriedly turned on her laptop and, looking around the bulletin board, tried to figure out exactly what had happened. As someone who had done this often, it didn’t take long for her to get the information she wanted. Among the adventurers who came out through the portal, only 103 survived. All of them were unconscious, and even the High Priest of Tovera Church, nicknamed the Agent, had given up on them as there was no way to treat them.
“N-No...” Faced with reality, the deputy commander of Clan Larer, Versyl Gowland, turned white as a sheet.
As soon as the computer turned on, I checked the chat room first.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 0 people are online.]
Once again, Baekho hadn’t returned. Well, I was sure there was nothing he could do since the Ghost Master had banned him. Hah, it had definitely been nicer when he was here.
Are the Watchers of the Round Table my only source of high-quality information then?
I dismissed my disappointment and moved the mouse. The Round Table didn’t open until three hours after the community opened. Until then, I planned to look around and check out the vibe here.
As expected, tons of players died.
Normally, players who had been waiting for this time of the month would be flooding the Exchange and bulletin board with posts. But now?
Nearly one-third.
Not only the board, but the chat rooms too. Even the large chat rooms, which always had more than fifty people inside, had barely over ten.
Every time I encountered these changes, I sighed. It was like a great flood had covered the world. People had been swept away everywhere, leaving no place untouched.
Will this place be filled with newbies in time? Hmm, probably.

Even Korea had nothing left after the war but managed to make it as far as it did. When that time came, I would no longer be a newbie but a high-ranking player. Oh, was I already? Yeah, I was pretty sure there were no players with the title of a nobleman yet.
Click, click.

Letting my mind wander, I browsed various bulletin boards as if surfing the web. Every bulletin board I went to was full of talk about the recent incident. Looking around, there was some—no, a lot—of talk about me.
[Bjorn Yandel, what the hell is that guy?]
I heard he’s rank five so I thought he’d be in his thirties but apparently he only finished his coming-of-age ceremony last year? What have I been doing for five years?

I had been mentioned a few times during the incident with the Lord of the Third Floor, but that was nothing compared to the mentions I was getting now. The number of posts in which I was the subject was countless, and each one had dozens of comments.
These99: He’s not rank 5 to start with. How can he be rank 5? If it weren’t for the guild’s accomplishment point system, he would’ve reached rank 4 by now, easy.
└OP: Wow, he’s that strong? Within a year? I feel even more ashamed.
└NExtlevEL: Rank 4 is a huge reach. OP, you don’t have to feel ashamed. You can reach rank 5 within a year as long as you get a good essence.
└NExtlevEL: Oh, and it doesn’t seem like he has a lot of essences. From what I’ve seen, he’s just barely made it into rank 5.
└These99: Rank 5 in one year is easy? What, are you playing solo? How can you even say that bullshit? He already wrecked Corpse Collector and proved himself.
└NExtlevEL: Are you American? That’s clearly hero-worship. Do you really believe that? And even if he did win, you think he did it alone? It was all thanks to his team.
└Pnec: He’s right. Corpse Collector was fought a hundred to one. How can you call that wrecking someone? Are you stupid?
Players gave their opinions like they were arguing about celebrities on the internet. Several comments made my heart skip a beat.
fliccolo: The way I see it, he must also be a player.
└OP: Oh, maybe. Why didn’t I think of that?
That sort of speculation was inevitable when one gained fame in a short period. Still, my past actions helped me out.
└arolf5205: What player? If you guys ever saw him yourself you would never be able to say that lol.

└stevencastle: Anyone who says something like that is lucky enough to have never entered the labyrinth. If they saw him bite off Corpse Collector’s ear at the end while he was blind, they could never call him a player.
└cherylvander: A true man’s man.

└Ykbell: His shouts as he stepped on goblin traps got even my heart pounding. Less than one year or not, that was something a modern person could never pull off. Everyone who was there at the time would agree.
└COOOOL75: Behelahhhhhh!!!!!

It was a very strange feeling to see both slanderous and praiseworthy things being written about me. I guessed I’d grown enough to become a hot topic. While on one hand, the strong interest in me was an issue, I decided to think of it as a bridge I had to cross to go higher. That was because I was going to keep going up. Floor number and reputation were inevitably proportionate.
It’s almost time.

I looked around the bulletin board for quite a while, and soon it had been three hours since I entered the community. In the past, I went in as late as possible to attract attention, but this time I just entered as soon as the time came. I was curious about the small talk before the official gathering.
Everyone aside from Clown is still alive, right?
Letting go of a bit of anxiety, I quickly double-clicked the mouse.
Flash!

A light flashed before my eyes for a moment and when I came to, I was in the familiar customization room. Wearing the same suit I always wore with Lion’s mask, I headed into the main room where the round table was.
Creaaak.
Three people were already there: Goblin, Fox, and Deer.
I guess Clown isn’t here yet.
When I entered, the three of them glanced at me and let out surprised exclamations.
“I’m glad you made it today.”

These guys were like this every time I came. Like the Lion on my mask, I sat down in my designated seat pretending not to care, and propped up my chin in my hand. If I did this, they’d start playing dialogue on their own. I just had to close my eyes and listen.
“The number of survivors is already four,” Goblin muttered to himself like he found the stillness in the air uncomfortable.
“Interesting. I thought you of all people would be most at risk. How did you survive?”

That was the part I was curious about too. Aside from certain priests, most religious figures in the labyrinth that day took the wizards’ portals out. That meant they’d all kicked the bucket. So what was the deal with Goblin?
“Well. Since it’s related to my identity, I’ll just say I was lucky.”
“Tsk, like it’s a big deal.” When Goblin avoided answering, Deer clicked his tongue. Then the two of them made small talk.
Strangely, Fox didn’t participate in the conversation. And it seemed the other two noticed too.
“Fox, you are acting strange today.”
“Yes. You’ve been staring into space this whole time...”
Deer and Goblin expressed their concerns.
Fox flinched a beat later, then tilted her head. “...Sorry? What did you just say?”
“See? It’s strange.”
Goblin started acting friendly then. “If something’s happened, tell us. I don’t know about the others, but I can help you, Fox.”
Fox let out a long breath and shook her head. “Thanks for your concern, but it’s nothing. So please mind your own business.”
“Oh, right. If you say so...” Goblin changed the subject, embarrassed, at Fox’s harsher-than-usual tone.
“By the way, I don’t think the others are coming.”

There were only five minutes left before the room closed. The remaining participants were two: Clown, whom I’d been waiting all this time for, and Crescent Moon, who desperately longed for the Stone of Revival.
“Could it be that they are both dead?”
“Hmm, I don’t know about Crescent Moon, but I don’t think Clown is dead.”
“...R-Right? Surely?” Goblin answered, though he sounded somewhat disappointed about that.
Creaaak.
Then the customization room by the hallway opened and a presence appeared.
Is it Clown?
I pretended to be indifferent and turned my head to check.
“Huh?”
Goblin and Deer also froze because that wasn’t the mask we were expecting.
A queen?

Her mask was studded with colorful jewels. The eyes were decorated with various gold pieces that looked almost like makeup and the forehead was in the shape of a crown. The outfit she had chosen was a fancy red dress.
Is she a returning member?

The thought came to mind but after Queen’s elegant greeting, I realized that wasn’t the case. “Oh, hello. This is my first time here, so there’s a lot I don’t know, but I hope you will all help me out.”
She was a new member, the first new member since my arrival. Naturally, everyone’s attention was focused on her.

The most enthusiastic one among us was Fox. “First, how did you get in here? Could it be that you also met Master?” Unlike earlier when she was blank and absentminded, Fox couldn’t hide her excitement and questions.
“Yes, well... Something like that?”
When Queen half-affirmed her theory, Fox’s voice grew even more excited. “Master! Where is he? I just need to see him. There’s something I must ask of him—”

“Oh, my. I’m sorry. I don’t think I can honor that request.” Queen firmly put her foot down. Then, smiling, she led the conversation with a relaxed air that didn’t seem to suit a newbie. “Anyway, why don’t we introduce ourselves?” Despite it being her first meeting, Queen spoke like she was right at home.
“The rule is to not use names,” Deer replied, disgruntled.
“I see! Then you are Goblin, this is Fox, and then Lion. Hmm, then what should I call you?”
“Deer.”
“Not Antlers?”
“Your mask should have had a name on it too.”
“Ah! It did. So I’m Queen? Huhu.”

While the attention was on her and Queen chatted with the other members, I continued to study her. A mask didn’t cover every part of a person’s face. Goblin had copper-colored skin, so I figured he was from Southeast Asia or South America. So what about this woman?
She’s definitely a Westerner.

She had flowing blonde hair and blue eyes. Her skin was white like a Caucasian. Of course, that was all I could tell from her appearance, and even that was unhelpful when it came to inferring her identity in this world. But I still couldn’t take my eyes off of her.
I feel like I’ve seen her somewhere before.
A feeling of déjà vu came over me out of nowhere. Why was I feeling this way?
“Anyway, Ms. Fox. It’s so nice to meet you. As you know, there aren’t many female players, right? Oh, and Mr. Goblin. You have a very nice voice. Mr. Deer seems very kind too. And Mr. Lion is—”
When Queen, who seemed to have the power to drain people’s energy, turned to me, Fox quickly warned, “Excuse me.”
“Yes?”
“I can see what type of person you are, but I think you’d be better off not getting too friendly with him.”
“Pardon? Why not?”

When Queen tilted her head, Fox looked at me with unease. Did she think I was going to exert my dominance like with Goblin? Well, I might have if things were normal. If I could free myself from that excessive energy of hers with a blast of murderous intent it would be a win for me.
“Mmm, you are very reserved, Mr. Lion. Let’s talk a lot more once we get to know each other better!”
I just ignored her and didn’t do anything. The reason was simple. I had to preserve my energy.
Looks like he came just in time.
With one minute left until the room closed, with a creak, another door in the hallway opened.
“Oh, I guess there are more members than I thought?”
The attention on Queen was short-lived. Everyone’s eyes turned in the direction of the sound.

“Wow! A lot of you survived!” As he walked in, Clown struck up a conversation in his characteristic asshole tone. “Mr. Goblin, I thought for sure you were d—Hmm?” Clown looked at Queen and tilted his head.
“Hello. Shall I call you Mr. Clown? I’m very excited to meet such an interesting person!”
“...Who is this? This ditzy woman?”
“A new member. It seems she has come at Master’s recommendation.”
“Hmmm... Is that so?” Clown stared at Queen as if to study her and sat down. Then, dismissing his interest in her, he spoke to me. “Pshehe, how are you, Mr. Lion?”
His repertoire was the same as usual. This son of a bitch always pretended to be friendly with me like I was his only equal here.
“Just you wait. I’ve brought many interesting stories with me this time.”
What is this idiot saying?
I slowly raised my level of murderous intent. Normally I had to fall into a trance and make myself feel the desire to kill someone for that, but I didn’t have to do that this time.
If it weren’t for this bastard, Daria would not have died, and many more adventurers could have returned to their families alive.
But how was this son of a bitch acting now?
“Pshehe, I guess Mr. Crescent Moon is dead?”
Cracking himself up like usual. Yeah, so...
“But why are you so quiet today, Mr. Lion?”
Filling myself with one intentional thought—True Murderous Intent—I opened my eyes.

“Are you—!” The moment our eyes met, Clown grasped at his neck with both hands. Struggling to breathe like he had been thrust into the vacuum of space itself, he soon fell to the floor, where his body twitched.
The other members panicked, not knowing what was happening. I slowly got up and walked toward Clown. Then I looked him up and down.
“S-Stop...”
It was kind of funny. He was always treating people like idiots with his stupid tone like he was someone important.
“You look like a bug.”
From now on, I ban you from acting like you know me, asshole.

chapters.title: Chapter 237: Awl (2)
paragraphs: Murderous intent was an affirmed desire to kill someone. Usually, it only resulted in a shiver down your spine, but in this imaginary world, that effect was amplified dozens of times. Since the feeling wasn’t transmitted through a physical form, in severe cases one experienced extreme shock accompanied by permanent side effects that spilled over into real life.

Players called this phenomenon Mind Pollution. When they reached this state, the subject suffered from speech impediments such as stuttering and, in the most severe cases, their mind collapsed and split into fragments.
“You look like a bug.” I stared at Clown with even more deliberate intent.
“W-Why...” Clown asked, even as he choked on his own spit.

The reason was simple. Clown was a necromancer. It would take a long time for him to recover the summons he’d lost during this battle, and until the barrier around Noark was released, he could not come out into the city to harm me.
Orcules.

However, he belonged to the same group as the Dragon Slayer, who killed Dwalkie. In the end, this guy was also an enemy I would have to defeat someday. If I could screw him up in advance, it was only logical to do so.

“...Uhh, ha!” As the murderous intent dragged on longer, I felt a sharp pain in the back of my head. Since this was a skill that used willpower as payment, that was unavoidable. I’d probably have to sleep all day tomorrow—maybe even two days. But the more it hurt, the more I increased the pressure. This son of a bitch probably already considered Bjorn Yandel his enemy by now and was planning his revenge.
It’s best to screw him up here.

This bastard was more dangerous than the Dragon Slayer. Unlike that guy, who lost his memory, he harbored clear hostility toward Bjorn Yandel. If I didn’t take him down now, one day, he would harm my comrades.
The murderous intent had become so thick that the others aside from Clown could now feel it on their skin.
God damn it.
As the oppressive energy continued, a sudden feeling of stiffness occurred in my brain. I had experienced this before, the sensation of exhausting all my willpower from using murderous intent.
“S-Stop. Please...”
I could’ve finished this if I had a bit more in me. Despite my disappointment, I squeezed out my last bit of murderous intent to the bitter end.
Gasp!
After holding out for a few more seconds like that, Clown took a deep breath like a man surfacing from the ocean. Then he coughed and vomited. “Khak, ughhh—!”
Although he looked pathetic, I wasn’t in good shape, either. I felt like I might pass out the next time I closed my eyes.
“Why... Why...?” Coming to his senses, Clown struggled to stand up and looked into my eyes. His breathing was a bit rough, but it didn’t seem like there was a problem with his speech.
So, I didn’t even get near Mind Pollution. Huh, so it’s like this...

I kind of expected this. In the past, when I released my murderous intent on Fox, my willpower bottomed out before I could reach that point too. Clown, who had killed countless people, must have had a thicker mental barrier than Fox.
Hm. Just judging by the energy, I thought I had gotten a lot stronger, but it’s still not enough.
Feeling bitter, I carefully studied Clown’s eyes. In those trembling pupils, I sensed more worry than resentment, a fear that filled him because he couldn’t understand the reason for my actions.
I continued to stare at the trembling Clown. So, what should I do now? That wasn’t even a concern in my mind.
What, just because my sudden surprise attack had failed, I need to have an acceptable reason? It’s pointless to worry about stuff like that. That’s because I’m not Bjorn Yandel. I’m Lion.
“That’s it?”
It wasn’t because of mental exhaustion that the murderous intent ended. It was because I pity you.

Repeating that until I believed it myself, I turned around indifferently. “If the rumors were true, I thought you would be at least a little useful,” I spat, seemingly annoyed, like I had just been testing something out.

The plan to screw up Clown with murderous intent had failed, but I wasn’t too disappointed because this outcome had its own advantages. As the age-old adage went, “Keep your friends close and your enemies closer.”
Now that this has happened, I’ll resort to milking him dry for as long as possible.
Clown was an executive of the criminal organization Orcules. As long as he had Noark as his base, he would continue to be a source of useful, quality information.
“Um... are you okay?” Queen, who had been watching the situation with bated breath, cautiously approached Clown and extended her hand. But did that hurt his pride?
Slap.

Clown pushed her hand away in a fit of anger, grabbed onto a chair, and sat down on his own. Then he looked at me as if the whole scene he’d made earlier didn’t matter. His eyes fixed on my face, he asked a question I didn’t understand. “...Lion, are you him?”
Huh? Who’s him? Like some kind of villain who must not be named?
I didn’t know so I just kept quiet, as always figuring that would get me halfway to where I wanted to go.
After a moment of waiting, Clown started muttering to himself like he was puzzling something over. “...No, that’s not possible. You aren’t him.”
Deer seemed to know something, because he said, “Yes, he is unable to participate in this gathering due to restrictions.”

Queen, who was watching things unfold with interest, also opened her mouth. “This place is more top-of-the-line than I thought. Yes. He cannot possibly be here. This chatroom doesn’t open until three o’clock, after all.”
Someone who couldn’t possibly join because it was three o’clock? It sounded like they were talking about someone I knew.
Are they talking about Baekho?

The thought suddenly came to mind, but there was no way to confirm. This was one of the few downsides of being Lion. Even if I had a question, I could never ask first, especially if it was low-level information everyone else knew. Lion had an image to maintain.
Anyway, I’ll look into it later.

It was time to step in. Everyone was already saying I wasn’t, so there was no need to stay silent. I chuckled. “Yes. I am not that guy,” I said as if to reward them for using their brains. Not “him”, but “that guy.” Whoever it was, I chose a word that implicitly put him and me on the same level. But did this strategy work?

“Who are you...?” Despite having been reduced to that state, Clown looked at me with awe. There was no sign of resentment in his eyes at all. He probably hadn’t even considered the idea of being hostile toward me.
“Do you want to know who I am?”
Clown gulped and nodded, but then immediately flinched as if he hadn’t meant to do that. He didn’t backtrack, though. It seemed getting beaten up had made him really wonder who I was.
I shrugged slightly, a gesture that everyone except for the new member, Queen, would recognize.
“...What does that mean?”
Like a dutiful subordinate, Clown answered Queen’s question. “It means we’ll be told if we bring him entertaining information.”
“Oh, right. That’s the concept of this secret chatroom, right?”
“Yes, that’s right. On that note, who is the ‘him’ everyone was talking about earlier?” Goblin asked, but Queen ignored the question as if she didn’t hear him.

“Are you serious about revealing your identity...?” Clown asked in a daze, and I didn’t bother answering. I just stared straight at Clown like there was nothing I couldn’t tell them as long as they entertained me, even if it had to do with my identity—like even that would be amusing to me.

“I’ve been thinking this for months, but I just can’t understand it.” Deer spoke like he had grown weary of me. “I don’t know how long you’ve been in this world, but you’ve been properly broken. If you keep this up, you won’t be able to live a decent life even once you’re back home.”

Worrying about a stranger’s life? He was a sweeter man than I thought, but this and that were two different things. When I pretended not to hear and did not even look at him, Deer clammed up in anger.
That was when Queen stepped forward. “Anyway, this is interesting. If I bring you information, can I hear who you are too? I’m getting curious.”
“If you can entertain me.”
Queen grinned at my answer. “Just wait. I may not look it, but I know quite a few interesting things. Huhu.”
Hmm, that did make me look forward to it, since this woman was a stranger too.
Seeing how she managed to get in during a time like this, it looks like she’s here on Master’s recommendation...
I hadn’t been able to pay her much attention at first in favor of educating Clown, but I’d have to keep a close eye on her going forward.
“Then why don’t we get started...?”

A silence fell as no one opened their mouth. Then Goblin spoke up and the confusion was somewhat sorted. “True, the door closed a while ago so we can’t sit like this forever. Crescent Moon didn’t make it in the end.”
“If he isn’t here at a time like this, that must mean he wasn’t able to avoid dying.”
It seemed everyone thought Crescent Moon hadn’t survived this incident. And he had been the one with the most initiative here too...
“So, who will go first this time?” Normally, Fox would have taken on the role of moderator herself and begun the gathering, but Goblin took the lead considering the strange state she was in.
“I’ll go later. This is my first time, so I think I’ll need some time to get used to how things work.”
“Sure. Then who will go?”
“If no one else will, I will go first.” The first speaker was Deer. “Let’s go with this since he was brought up earlier. He escaped into the world five days ago.”
“What? He did...?” Clown seemed surprised as if this was new information.

“Um... If we want to be fair, shouldn’t you tell us who he is first...?” Goblin hinted that he wanted more information on what was going on, but Fox’s eyes remained the same. No, was she even listening?
Vooom.
Anyway, the jewel at the center of the Round Table gave off a green light. That meant that the information was true and that more than half the people here were unaware of it.
“But I don’t understand. How can you release such valuable information like this?”
Deer answered Clown’s question with nonchalance. “Most people who don’t know will know in a week anyway. I should at least use it here.”

“Then may I try next?” Queen raised her hand just slightly. Normally, going clockwise was the rule, but everyone allowed it because they were curious about just what information this woman would share. “Huhu, it’s my first time at a gathering like this so I’m a little nervous.” Her voice didn’t sound nervous at all. Queen met eyes with each person like she was relishing in their attention, then slowly parted her lips. “He is in the Magic Tower as we speak.”
Hah, this again?

Because I couldn’t be sure who “he” was in the first place, I wasn’t particularly impressed by this information. But I guess these two were different. The moment the words left Queen’s mouth, Clown’s and Deer’s eyes turned to the center of the Round Table, to the jewel that could discern authenticity.
“It’s true...”
“The first place he goes to since reentering the world is the Magic Tower? Doesn’t that pique your interest?”
When the opportunity came, I’d have to make sure to find out who “he” was. If these guys were acting like this, whoever it was must be an extraordinary person.
...If it really is Baekho, who the hell is that guy, really?

While I was thinking that, I felt eyes on me from Queen’s direction. I didn’t know when she’d started, but she was staring intently at me. “Mr. Lion, you don’t seem surprised to hear that. As if you already knew.”
Uh, is that what you think? I just don’t know who he is, so where he is doesn’t matter to me.
“I guess you have someone in the Magic Tower too?”
“Well, that could be the case.” Queen tried to feel me out, and I ignored her like I thought her attempts were cute.

“Next... I’ll go.” After that, it was Fox’s turn. Fox hadn’t said much since the gathering started and promptly received three red lights in a row. The first two things she shared were recent pieces of information that everyone knew already, and the third was judged to be pointless information to have.
“To think the Clan Master of Clan El Capard was a player. That’s quite interesting. But isn’t that useless? I remember hearing he died as soon as he stepped out of those portals this month.”

“...Value is relative. For example, neither I nor Mr. Goblin know who ‘he’ is. That means that was pointless information to us.” Fox’s logic made sense, but this was a Round Table where the majority ruled.
“Still, at least now you know someone interesting exists out there. Pshehe.”

“...Are you all of the same opinion?” Everyone was silent in response to her question, and that silence became the most effective answer. In the end, Fox had to try for the fourth time with information about a single-digit numbered item. “The Clan Master of Clan Tavern has No. 9.”
“Tavern’s Clan Master, huh...?”
“It’s like putting a pearl necklace on a pig. Pshehe.”

The Round Table’s jewel emitted a green light and no one disagreed this time. A single-digit Numbers Item was worth that much, at least. To be honest, it seemed like Fox was just now revealing information she had been saving up.

“I will go this time.” Next up was Goblin. Like the paladin he was, he revealed information connected to religious society. “Ultimately, all denominations have decided to withdraw their support for the king. In a few days, they will begin to keep their distance again just like they did in the past.”
Since this was information you couldn’t know unless you were a key figure on the religious side of things, it passed with flying colors.
“Pshehe, then it’s my turn.” As soon as it was his turn, Clown made a shocking declaration. “I live in Noark.”

Just what was going through this bastard’s head? Did the murderous intent screw up his mind? This was information that revealed part of his own identity. Everyone, including me, was stunned by this incomprehensible decision.
Or, rather, that was true for everyone except Queen. “Noark! You must be a very interesting person too, Mr. Clown!” she remarked innocently.

Clown’s eyes were fixed on me and showed no signs of moving. For some reason, I was reminded of a certain evil spirit hunter. That bastard had also studied me with an expression like this after tossing out some bait.
Is he trying to feel out how much I know?
The thought came to mind, so I studied Clown’s eyes closely too. I thought I could even see relief in them.
“Judging by your surprise, I guess you didn’t know who I was? Pshehe.”
What are you talking about, you deranged bastard?
“Mr. Crescent Moon said it seemed like Mr. Lion knew all of our identities. I guess that’s not the case.”
He was testing the waters. Lion was extraordinary, but how extraordinary was he? Did he only have personal power and influence, or was he a superpower with an enormous faction plus information?
“Was that entertaining for you?”
And if he could rack up some additional entertainment points in the process of finding out? Well, it was definitely an effective play on his part.
“Certainly,” I said with a smirk. “It was an entertaining ruse.”
At that moment, the green light on the jewel turned off, indicating that the previous turn had passed. It was time for my long-awaited turn. The information I would reveal had already been decided.
“Clown is the Corpse Collector.”
Who do you think you’re messing with?

chapters.title: Chapter 238: Awl (3)
paragraphs: The moment I said that, Clown took in a deep, sharp breath, revealing a sense of shock that could not by any means be hidden by a mask. His reaction alone confirmed that what I’d said was the truth. But was the announcement itself too shocking?

“Corpse Collector...?” The members urgently turned their disbelieving eyes to one place in particular, where the Round Table’s jewel was located. Before long, the jewel began to glow a specific color—a very vivid green.
“...It’s true.”

Now, everyone’s eyes shifted again, not to the jewel that had done its job, but to Clown, whose brain appeared to be malfunctioning. With eyes full of wariness and hostility, Clown did not say anything at all. Of course, it wasn’t because their gazes were causing him discomfort. If he were that type of person, he wouldn’t have revealed he was from Noark in the first place.
He must be surprised I knew his identity.

I hadn’t actually intended to flaunt that fact, either. It would be next to impossible to deduce I was Bjorn Yandel from this piece of information alone, but I had determined that revealing it would just put me at risk.
But to think the cards would fall right into place on their own.
If I had revealed his identity first, Clown might have assumed I obtained that information recently. But now?
“Mr. Crescent Moon said it seemed like Mr. Lion knew all of our identities. I guess that’s not the case.”

Clown had provoked me and created the perfect setup. No, not only that, but this guy had even revealed that he was from Noark with his own lips. To put it simply, even if his identity was exposed, he was not the kind of person who would leave the gathering.
Well, since it’s already known to the whole world that he’s a player, his identity won’t be as important to him as the other guys’.

Thanks to that, nothing was stopping me. I could still have my Plan B of keeping him by my side to extract information and expose his identity and give him a middle finger. Doing so even came with several additional benefits. Since he had revealed that he was from Noark, the other members would openly expect information from their side from him. In addition, I could solidify Lion’s character in front of the other members and leave room for newbie Queen to jump to her own conclusions. This was also a very important aspect for me. The more Lion appeared like a veteran, the harder it would be to associate him with Bjorn Yandel. I’d truly hit the jackpot.
“...A secret chatroom with the Corpse Collector. I’m glad I joined,” Queen murmured, ending the brief silence.
“...Pshehe, you got me good.” Coming to his senses then, Clown pretended he hadn’t lost his composure and faked a laugh.
Goblin hadn’t been able to meet Clown’s eyes ever since he heard the words “Corpse Collector,” and Fox and Deer shot me even warier looks than they were giving Clown.
“...You really know everything.”
“Just who are you...?”
Ahhh, nice... That’s the stuff.
I tried my best to keep the corners of my mouth fixed in place and ignored their questions as nonchalantly as possible. Thanks to that, everyone’s attention shifted to Clown again.
“Now, how does it feel to have your identity exposed, Corpse Collector?” Deer snarled in a way that implied he had a past with Corpse Collector.
But Clown didn’t miss a beat. “Pshehe, I don’t know. How am I feeling? Only like Mr. Lion is more dangerous than I thought.”
“You’ll keep pretending to be unshaken until the end, huh.”
“Tsk, it takes one to know one. You think I care about the likes of you guys and what you think of me? It’s not like I’ve spent my days hiding myself like all of you.”
He wasn’t exactly wrong, but did Deer pick up on the nuance hidden in those words? “...You’re still going to keep attending the gathering after all this?”
“Of course. Ah, but I hope you don’t misunderstand and assume that I’m staying because of you guys. The reason I want to stay is all because of Mr. Lion.”

To be honest, this kind of reaction was a bit surprising. I couldn’t believe he could still act friendly toward me after the murderous intent incident followed by me exposing his identity. Was this bastard a punching bag or something? Even while I was inwardly marveling at him, the battle of wills between Deer and Clown continued.
“Anyway, Mr. Deer. You should watch your mouth. What are you going to do if I come looking for you?”
“I don’t think there is anything to worry about. I’m not stupid enough to expose my identity wherever I go like you.”
“Pshehe, are you sure about that? I already have about four candidates in mind. I’m sure I’ll figure it out if I kill them all.”
“Pffft, try it if you dare. You think that’ll scare me? Not too long ago, you were almost beaten to death by a barbarian. I guess that arrogant personality of yours came out unscathed, though.”
“You... do you really want to die?”
Judging by that rave review, the winner was Deer. Clown then pressured him with murderous intent but I guessed they were around the same level, because Deer didn’t even flinch.

“Now, now. Stop it. Members should be friendly with each other. No?” Queen stepped in to arbitrate. It was kind of funny. What kind of newbie was she? “Let’s do another round instead. I didn’t realize it before, but this is so much fun.”
I guessed Queen’s absurd network was an impressive enough draw because the battle of wills stopped there. But the moment the next round was about to start, Fox forfeited.

“I will stop here.” I guessed she had no more information to use. This happened once in a while so it wasn’t so strange. Except that instead of leaving the chatroom, Fox went through the door and waited. “I’ll wait outside until it’s over.” This was the first time this had happened since I became a member. “Please make some time for me once this is over. I have something to tell you, Mr. Lion.”
Something to tell me, huh? Is this related to her absentmindedness earlier?
“...You might already know it, though.”
Fox left with that mysterious statement and the second round started right after.

The first turn was Queen’s. She must have liked the system of the gathering because her voice was cheerful as she whipped out her information. “Everyone knows the GM, right? But let’s see if you know this. Huhu! This is a common misconception, but this community was not actually created by the GM!” Her tone implied she was sure that this was a free pass, but the light emitted by the jewel was, of course, red. “Eh...?”
“That is information Lion has shared before,” Deer informed a startled Queen.
“...Mr. Lion knew about that?” Queen stared at me. It seemed her curiosity about me had grown even more. Well, the same went for me too.
Who is she, really?
This was high-quality information that no one else at this summit had known about before I’d told them.
It could be someone from the moderator team. No, wait...

The moment that thought came to me out of nowhere, although I’d only met her once, a face buried in my subconscious flashed through my mind—the woman who’d acted as a guide and filled me in when I first entered this community.
Come to think of it, her nickname was Soul Queen.
Coincidentally, this woman had chosen a queen mask. Clown said we always chose the mask that most resembled us. Was this really a coincidence? Even though she was also a Caucasian with blonde hair?
Her voice seems similar too. Why didn’t I realize it immediately?

The realization was late, but this was actually normal. A person was bound to look totally different without their nose. If it weren’t for the fact that she was using the name Queen, my subconscious wouldn’t have even thought of Soul Queen.
It’s not confirmed yet, but I’d better operate under the assumption that I’m right for now.

While I was in the middle of processing this new possibility, Queen revealed new information and promptly received another disqualification. “Hmm, I guess I should opt for recent information, then. Within a few years, a six-person binding spell will be invented. It’ll completely change the structure of quests. How about that? Isn’t that amazing—”
Ha, how many people were going to beat that dead horse?
“Eh?” Seeing the red light, Queen looked bewildered. “Are you sure there’s nothing wrong with this jewel?”

“Of course not. That is information that has already been mentioned before. Since half a year has passed, there should be about a year and a half left until the binding spell is released to the public.”
“Wow, you even know the time frame? This place is really high-level,” Queen remarked innocently.
Clown laughed arrogantly. “Pshehe, your level is just too low.” He probably wasn’t being serious. The presence Queen carried had been unrivaled by any other members thus far.
He must be doing this so that she’ll reveal more valuable information.
Goblin had been keeping his mouth shut ever since Clown mentioned the word “level.” He knew how to read the room, for once.
“Hmm, this one’s a bit sensitive...” Sounding completely unaffected, Queen went for a third try. “The king isn’t sick. It was all a lie.”
...Huh?

The jewel responded to Queen’s words with a green light, which caused even more havoc at the Round Table. The reason was simple: the exact opposite information had been stated several meetings ago by Clown.
“The king of Rafdonia’s illness is getting worse.”

In a way, this could be said to be the Round Table’s key weakness. If the speaker was 100 percent confident in what they were saying, the gem emitted a green light. It did not discern between fact and fiction, but lies and truth. If it weren’t for that, people would have been able to use the system to ask about all kinds of information.
“This has become a headache.”
“Excuse me? Why is it a headache?”
Deer sighed and explained the situation to Queen. “Hmm, neither one of us has lied, but one of us has it wrong?”
“Exactly.”
“Then wouldn’t it make sense for my words to hold more weight? Everyone here thinks that the king is sick, but I’m the only one who is convinced it is a lie.”
“Pshehe, and where did you hear that nonsense?”
“Hmm, is this your limit, Corpse Collector?”
Clown was triggered by Queen’s provocation. “...What did you just say?”
Queen fired back with a witty retort. “Then where did you hear the information, Mr. Clown? I met with the king in person. But you’re still surer than I am?”
“...Anyone could say something like that.”

“I never thought the Corpse Collector would be so uptight. Here, I’ll place my hand on the jewel. Is that good with you?” Queen proceeded to state that she met with the king and the jewel glowed green.
Clown couldn’t argue with that. How did this guy end up in this situation? He was getting beaten down from all sides today.
“Another monster like Lion. A player able to contact the king...”
“It’s not like that. I just happened to get the chance.” Queen, as her mask implied, established a strong first impression from her very first gathering.
“Why are there more and more people like this here?” As a bonus, Goblin was humbled.
“Then enough about this matter. Let’s move on to the next! Mr. Goblin, you go!”
“M-Me?”
“Yes!” Queen, with that powerful aura of hers, naturally led the round. Goblin couldn’t refuse and obediently went next.
“The Magic Tower discovered a way to penetrate Noark’s barrier yesterday. It appears they’ll be able to do it at any moment. Oh, thirty High Priests will have to gather to offer a prayer, though.”
So, there was finally a way. Perhaps a second punitive expedition would be formed in the near future.
“So he says, Corpse Collector.”
“What are you gloating about? Sounds like the temple will withdraw support from the palace, anyway.”
“You think a mere religious body can rebel against the king?”
“The palace no longer has him, either.”
“Damn it, if I knew you were on their side, I would never have brought that up.”
Deer and Clown started bickering again.
“Um... are you not stopping them this time?” Goblin asked Queen pointedly, but she just watched with amusement.
“Why? Now that I’m taking a closer look, this just adds to the fun.”
“I-I see?” Thus, even Queen remained a spectator in their battle of wills and the conversation seemed to be nowhere near reaching its end, but surprisingly, the winner was quickly decided.
“Oh, right. Congratulations. I heard you got a new nickname.”
“...What do you mean?” Clown reacted like this was news to him.
“Oh, didn’t you hear? Your new nickname is Toy Collector.”
“Oh my, how vulgar.” Queen covered her mouth like she knew exactly what the moniker was referring to, and Deer continued explaining without hiding his amusement.
“Toy Collector. It’s because you’re like a baby.”
“I’m like a baby...?” Clown didn’t seem to understand what he meant.
Expecting this, Deer gave an exaggerated tilt of his head. “What? Are you not? Bjorn Yandel has infamously been talking about it every day at drinking parties.”
“Th-that bastard...?” Clown’s voice shook as he slowly remembered something.
This was the perfect moment to land the finishing blow. “You, you’re small.” Like the longtime player he was, Deer didn’t miss his shot and stabbed the dagger right into his heart.
Crackkk.
The sound of something shattering could be heard from Clown’s mouth. I took a moment to offer an internal apology.
Oh, sorry, sorry. I specifically told them to keep that a secret.
“Pfft.”
But somehow things had just ended up like this.

chapters.title: Chapter 239: Awl (4)
paragraphs: “Pfft.” When Goblin cracked up, cold eyes turned his way. “Ahem, ahem!” Clearing his throat and acting like he hadn’t laughed at all, Goblin avoided those eyes.
Deer intervened and defended him. “Why are you bothering innocent Goblin? It’s not his fault you were put in a small body.”
Clown couldn’t even reply to that sarcastic remark. He just glared at the both of them as he quaked in humiliation.
Is he still going to come here after this?
I was worried for a second, but thankfully Clown was first-class. “...Pshehe.” In a situation where it would be understandable for him to burst into tears, Clown forced a laugh. “How childish.”
I thought I knew what he was trying to do, the only way of turning things around when you’ve been unilaterally wrecked.
“This isn’t even my body. You think those words can affect me?”
A mental victory. He’s in a class of his own.

Clown’s words were spoken coolly, but hot resentment spilled into his tone. As for Deer? Those eyes of his were filled with pure joy. In truth, the victor had already been decided, but Deer was a ruthless man who lacked the mercy of a magnanimous winner.
“Hmm, so you admit you’re small?”
Was this man the devil?
Clown took a blow to the chest at the very end and eventually chose to remain silent. He had apparently realized that talking only got him hurt.
“Men will be men.” When the affair came to an end, Queen chuckled.
I was embarrassed for them. I was sure it was pathetic to watch grown men fight back and forth about something like this. Anyway, the short snafu passed and the gathering continued.

“The conversation got off track. I’ll go next.” Deer heralded the resumption of the gathering and revealed his piece of information. “Three days ago, the palace captured a spy from Noark. It seems a few were sent out before the barrier was activated.”
A captive spy... I wondered if it was Amelia, but for some reason, I didn’t think it was. She wasn’t the type to be easily captured.
“They plan to kill them once they extract everything they need from them. Oh, after they torture them to the verge of death first.” Deer spoke as if to provoke Clown, who was from Noark.
I think it’s basically confirmed that Deer is from the palace.
This was another thing brought about by the confrontation with Clown.

“Pshehe, how naive. You think I’d bat an eye at the death of one or two bugs that couldn’t even protect themselves?” His voice was full of displeasure. Regardless of whether the spy lived or died, he probably didn’t like Deer’s smug attitude. “Then it is my turn.” As soon as Deer’s turn was over, Clown immediately retaliated. “Soon, an assassin will be sent after Bjorn Yandel.”
...Huh? What now?
“I heard he’s being paraded around as a hero. It’ll be so fun to see him die right after he receives his noble title. The palace’s reputation will go down the drain!”
Ha, why are we suddenly playing monkey in the middle with my life?
I was startled for a moment at the sudden mention of my name, but annoyance soon crept in.
An assassin when my body hasn’t even fully healed yet...
The silver lining was that I learned that this was going to happen in advance. And I guess Deer felt the same.
“Idiot,” Deer replied, clicking his tongue. “You couldn’t control your emotions and even kindly warned the enemy? You really are a baby.”
“Tsk, why are you so confident that this is something you’ll be able to stop just because you know about it?”

The battle of wills between them was about to start up again. It was fun at first, but it was slowly getting annoying so I interrupted and cut it off there. “I’ll go next.” When I opened my mouth for the first time in a long while, the hall went quiet in an instant. I glanced around at the members. Fixing my eyes on Queen, I said, “The one who created Ghost Busters was an evil spirit from another world.”
Dang, I was going to save that one.
In truth, it was more of a fascination than anything. Originally, I had saved it to use as a reward if someone told me something entertaining.
“This community was not actually created by the GM!”

But if Queen already knew that, she must also know that the entity that created this community was an evil spirit from another realm, so I figured I’d better use this tidbit before it became useless. I was starting to run out of cards I could use to build up Lion’s reputation.
“Created by an evil spirit from another world...”
Huh?
“Yeah, that must have been it.” When the jewel turned green, Queen nodded as if I’d just confirmed something for her.
What, she didn’t know that already? I thought an admin would definitely know.
Then was she not Soul Queen? The thought came to mind, but I didn’t know anything for sure yet. It was possible the GM just hadn’t told her about that.

As I was thinking this, Goblin spoke up after a short pause, clearly surprised. “W-Wait! An evil spirit from another world? What do you mean by that? You mean there are players here from somewhere other than Earth?”
There was only one thing I could do for him. “The interpretation is up to you.”
If you want me to open my mouth, bring me something entertaining. Though even if he does, I’ll probably judge it as no fun.
“...I have heard that such people existed. But I always thought it was just a rumor,” Deer, who had been lost in thought for a long while, exclaimed like he’d just heard an amazing secret.
This proves that Baekho really is amazing.
As was the case with this tidbit, most of the top-of-the-line information contributing to Lion’s image today had come from Baekho Lee’s mouth.

“Pshehe, like I thought, it was a good idea to stay.” Even Clown, who had been getting kicked around the entire gathering, seemed to think my information was interesting and nodded in satisfaction. He must have thought it was a good idea to put on an iron façade.
“...This makes me more interested.” Queen suggested we do another round with a zealous look in her eyes, but unfortunately, the gathering ended on that note because Goblin raised a white flag.
“I’ll stop here as I have nothing more to say.”
“Then I’ll stop here too. I think it will be difficult to find something all four of us don’t already know...” Deer also declared his intention to opt out and the gathering naturally came to an end.

“Then, if you’ll excuse me.” Clown, who normally stayed behind after to chat with the other members, left as soon as the gathering was over. Well, I was sure it would be uncomfortable to stay and talk while everything about him was on display. “Pshehe, I’ll make sure to bring something fun next time.”

Even after all that, Clown still acted friendly toward me. To be honest, I was a bit dumbfounded, but his subservient attitude toward the strong was worth learning from. I guessed there was a reason some people survived for so long.
“Then I’ll be leaving.”
When I got up and opened the door, I could see Fox waiting for me, leaning against the wall of the empty hallway. “Ah, is it over?”
When I nodded, Fox led me to a room, not the main room with the Round Table, but a nearby reception room. So there were rooms like this here too.

As we sat on the sofa facing each other, a strange silence settled between us. However, whoever opened their mouth here first would be the weaker of the two of us. When I waited patiently, Fox parted her lips first. “Um... thank you for making time for me.”
“Your reason?” I asked curtly.
Fox flinched with a whimper, then spoke up cautiously. “Do you know why I called you aside today, Mr. Lion?”
I didn’t know, but answering honestly would also be a weak person’s move. “Are you trying to sound me out?” I muttered coldly.
“I—no! Th-that’s not it...!”

“Looks like you’re not that desperate yet.” With that, I pretended to get up. That was because she was the one whose business was urgent. I didn’t know the exact reason, but I knew that for sure. If it weren’t, there would be no reason to set up a separate meeting like this.
I’m sure she needs Lion’s power or information for something.

I had gotten my thoughts about Fox in order while the Round Table was still in progress. Ultimately, I figured that if I used this opportunity well, I might be able to learn her identity. So how was that playing out?
“Please, I beg you. If you know my situation, please help me,” Fox begged earnestly, but even that conveyed an implication that she couldn’t fully trust me.
If I know? So, she’s asking me to help her after seeing that I knew Clown’s identity.
If her identity was already exposed, she had nothing to lose so she’d take my help. If not, she’d think it over more and decide what to do.
Oh, you wicked...
“You mock me to the end.”

I got up from my seat like there was nothing more for me to see here. There was really nothing I could do right now. The truth was, I only knew Clown’s identity. I didn’t know anything about Fox’s circumstances.
“You are not desperate yet,” I said. This wasn’t the right way to ask for Lion’s help. “When you are more desperate, come find me again.”
When I reached the door, Fox called out urgently, “J-Just tell me! At least tell me if you know my situation or not!” Her voice was tinged with regret.
I chuckled at that unexpected naivety. “Why should I do that?”
“That’s—”
I cut off Fox’s answer and said, “This is more fun for me.” This was Lion, after all.

In a spacious room reminiscent of a hotel suite, a white man lying on the bed mused to himself and got up. “I wonder what those two are talking about right about now. Eh, no use being curious. They never tell me anything, anyway.”

He was used to this. Ever since his school days, he was often left out by his friends for some reason. He had been lucky, though. The virtual currency that he bought out of boredom ended up being a jackpot that had allowed him to live in a house like this—not that that mattered now.
“Whew, less than five hours left.”

Checking the time, the man sat on the table in the living room and clicked on the laptop’s keyboard. This was the only thing he looked forward to every month. When he was chatting in this virtual space, it made him feel like he was back in the real world.
“Bjorn Yandel, huh?”
The bulletin board he was browsing through was only filled with posts about that guy. So this was the main plot point for today?
[Did you hear that Bjorn Yandel is now a nobleman?]
I’m seriously jealous. There’s a lot of talk that he’s a player, but what does that matter? Player or not, at that point, I would just want to live here forever.
The man spent his free time commenting on various posts.
Bling0_0: Agreed. A nobleman can have several wives too. I would live here too. I heard his teammates are super pretty.
└arolf5205: The official wife would be Missha. I saw her from a distance and she’s really cute.
└Ykbell: I’m for Erwen! I like that elf.
└cherylvander: Isn’t a barbarian woman best suited for a real man?
Going into various posts with many views and attracting aggro accordingly, the comments poured in. The man read them all the way through and frowned.
└Pnec: Dumbass. Seeing as you envy that fucking noob, it’s obvious you’re also a loser.
Okay, I’m going with you today.
The man grinned because he knew those who hadn’t been brought up with proper manners were the most fun to take down.
Thinking back, that type of insult seemed to work pretty well.
Remembering the incident that happened earlier, the man chuckled and left a comment.
└Bling0_0: Okay, 1 inch. Yours is 1/10 of Bjorn’s. Hands and feet trembling in envy much?
Ding!
It wasn’t long before a notification of a new comment popped up.
└Pnec: ...Fuck, you wanna go?
Okay, that was kind of unexpected.
└Bling0_0: What? Is it actually 1 inch?
└Pnec: Why are there so many weird bastards here? Just get lost.
└Bling0_0: You wish. That’ll be your future wife. Even a nice woman can’t stand 1 inch. Even if you became a noble, you wouldn’t be able to keep a concubine around.
└Pnec: ...Hey, where do you live?
As expected, rave reviews exploded on his screen soon after. The man grinned and swarmed to the chaos relentlessly. His opponent also made personal attacks of his own in the middle.
└cherylvander: I was wondering what all the notifications were about. What the hell are you two doing here? lol
└Ykbell: Stop, you guys. I graduated from MIT and my professional opinion is that 1 Inch got totally wrecked.
└1spring: But look at how he’s talking. I think he really is 1 inch.
Users who had been watching the fight as spectators joined in on dragging them and soon the user deleted all their comments and ghosted.
Loser.
With victory in his hands, the man stretched, feeling refreshed. After passing the time like that for a long while, the time came for the community to close.
“Mr. Parav, Mr. Parav!” When he opened his eyes, a priest sitting next to him was whisper-yelling and shaking his shoulder. “You can’t fall asleep here!”

“Oh, sorry...” The man quickly apologized and continued to listen to the bishop standing at the pulpit. Or, to be more precise, he pretended to. This was not the world inside the community where he could show off his true nature. It was time to put on his faithful paladin act.
Ha, if I knew it was going to be this hardcore, I would’ve chosen another class.
After about an hour, today’s nighttime prayer was over. But before returning to his room, the man took the time to chat with his comrades and build up his relationship with his peers.

Was it because he had just come back from the community? As he listened quietly to their conversation out of exhaustion, one of them turned to him worriedly. “Parav, are you okay? You don’t look so well.”
“Is it because of that? Shake it off. How is it your fault that you weren’t able to enter the labyrinth that day because of an upset stomach?”
“I’m just glad you’re alive.”
“God was on your side.”
His comrades appeared to be greatly mistaken, but Parav didn’t correct them. He just nodded his head in sorrow. “Yeah, I should shake it off.”

To be honest, it hadn’t even been an upset stomach. He had just had an ominous feeling that day and made up an excuse to be lazy. The next day, when the pillars of fire erupted in the different Dimension Squares, he felt lightheaded.
“Why don’t you go get some rest?”
“No, I will stay here with you all. I think that will be better.”
“...If you say so.”
Afterward, his comrades continued to chat. Even here, that barbarian was a hot topic. “That man, I hear he’s going to become a nobleman?”
“I think it’s a good thing. From what I heard from the priest who was with him that day, he is a truly virtuous man.”
Like religious figures who valued humility as a virtue, the man’s comrades praised the new hero without any hint of envy or suspicion.
So boring.
As expected, it was hard to find the carefree nature of the community out here. Feeling claustrophobic for some reason, the man blurted out unwittingly, “Isn’t that man a bit suspicious?”
“Suspicious?”
“It’s not common to build such a reputation in the first year, is it?”
“That’s true, but...”
“Maybe he is an evil spirit?”

It sounded like a joke, but he was actually being sincere. Public opinion in the community was leaning in the other direction, but Parav thought everything Bjorn Yandel had pulled off so far was impossible unless he was a player. But what were his comrades’ opinions?
Silence followed his suggestion. Of course, it did not last for long.
“Hahaha!” His comrades laughed in unison.
“Evil spirit, how can that be?”
“He is a fellow Captain Krovitz has taken a liking to. It’s no good to be so suspicious.”
“No evil spirit knows how to sacrifice and lay down their life for their comrades like that.”
“My friend, you are joking too much today!”
Parav felt his face grow hot. Of course, it wasn’t an unfamiliar sensation to him. Ever since he was young, he’d always been teased like this and left out of the group.
Yeah, I’m sure I’m just jumping to the wrong conclusions again.
Parav sighed and headed back to his room. This always happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 240: Awl (5)
paragraphs: “How was it?”
In a library filled with a faint scent of books, the blonde woman, Soul Queen, answered after a moment’s thought. “It was a very interesting place.”

That was the most fitting description. A place where Corpse Collector was one of the members and where even someone like him was out of his element? She never realized such a chatroom existed in the Ghost Busters community.

“I’m sure my personal opinions aren’t what you’re most interested in,” Soul Queen teased, and the man did not deny it. That was because there was another reason for her infiltrating the Watchers of the Round Table.
“Perhaps the Watchers of the Round Table is a private gathering created to avoid our detection.”
Whether a spy from the palace, or perhaps a player from another realm, the man had sent her there to look into both possibilities. But what was the verdict?
Soul Queen smiled. “It seems you were right again, Mr. Love.”
“In what sense?”
“The Watchers of the Round Table definitely seems like a space created by a player from another realm.”
