“I should hear about it in more detail then.”

Soul Queen slowly explained what had happened there: Lion, who exerted an overwhelming presence; Clown, whose identity as Corpse Collector had been revealed; Deer, who was presumed to be affiliated with the palace; and Goblin, who was so average he seemed almost out of place there.
“Hmm, I don’t know about Ms. Fox. I don’t think she’s reserved but I wasn’t able to converse very much with her.”
Still, Fox was worth keeping an eye on, and rightfully so, because she had requested to speak with Lion at the end. What if that had been some kind of secret rendezvous?
“You are suspicious of the member called Lion.”

“Yes. If there really is a player from another realm among them, he’s the only one it could be.” The man asked for her reasoning and Soul Queen answered without hesitation, “He drove Corpse Collector close to the verge of Mental Pollution with murderous intent alone. And seeing as he pulled back right before reaching that point, I think he had more to spare.”

That fact alone made it obvious. A feat like that was impossible with an ordinary human mind, unless he was a player from another dimension who had been dropped in this world and survived here for over a hundred years. That wasn’t the only reason, either. In the second round, Lion had said this:
“The one who created Ghost Busters was an evil spirit from another world.”

In response to her statement that it wasn’t the GM who had created the community, he brought up information that only a few knew about almost flippantly, as if he knew her identity too. She was sure of it then.
“Yeah, that must have been it.”
This man, who already seemed incredibly dangerous, was not a simple player.
“Come to think of it, you said he knew Corpse Collector’s identity from the beginning?”
“Yes. To clarify, the other members already suspected Lion of knowing their identities.”

“...That is very strange.” Security within the community was flawless. Even he, who had taken over admin rights and created the modern version of Ghost Busters, was unable to learn the users’ real world identities.
“How do you think he knew who they were?”

“I don’t know. If he really does know, there are two possibilities.” The man provided two possible theories in response to Soul Queen’s question. “One, Lion is on par with the archmage from another realm who created this sub-space, or he has a comrade who is. And two...”
“Two, Lion is in the same party as the creator of the Watchers of the Round Table. Right?”
“Yes, that’s right. Up to this point, the current members were gathered by that Master person, so if they told him who the members were, that would make sense.”
“But then it wouldn’t make sense for him to know who I am.”
“But we’re not sure about that yet. Next time, throw in some bait to confirm whether that guy really knows your identity or not.”
“I will.”
“Anyway, information about the Master is what’s important now. Did you find out anything?”
“I haven’t met the Master yet. But I was able to learn from Mr. Goblin that on the day of the foreign connection shown in the log, he had visited the Table.”
“Then that means that the person who snuck into the community that day has the nickname 0720.”
“I suppose that’s the only thing that makes sense. I wanted to find out more, but it seems like Mr. Goblin is still wary of me...”

Even after that, the two of them conversed for about an hour. Their topic of conversation was not only the Watchers of the Round Table, but the recent incident, the deaths of far too many players, what the most efficient way was to increase new member recruitment in the future, and even the biggest problem to crop up recently.

“What will you do about Mr. Baekho? He’s turning the Magic Tower upside down looking for you. Right now, you may be just one suspect out of many, but I don’t think it will be easy to keep your identity hidden forever...”
“I’m still debating it. For now, it seems he is hostile toward the palace, but... we have to be careful. It could be a trap.”
“Yes, I will leave that part to you, Mr. Love.”
“Meanwhile, Elfnunna. How is the investigation into him going?”
“All of his posts have been deleted, so it will take a little while to recover them. But he has quite a lot of GP.”
“Is it all from Mr. Baekho?”

“No, he made almost all of it on the first day by selling a few pieces of quality information.” Soul Queen went on to explain that these were things one could know by playing the game to some extent, and that the other posts and comments left by him were all deleted so it would take some time to recover them.

“Hmm, I see...” Love tapped the armrest with his index finger, mulling this over. There was one reason why he was looking into Elfnunna: because he theorized that Bjorn Yandel and Elfnunna could be the same person.

Bjorn Yandel was a barbarian whose rise through the ranks had been meteoric. Strangely, he had picked a shield during his coming-of-age ceremony. Elfnunna, meanwhile, had easily acquired GP by selling in-game information within the community. Also, he was a Korean Baekho Lee looked to like an older brother. That was a very important thing about this man. If these two were the same, there was a possibility that he was also the person Love had been eagerly awaiting.
Hold on.
A thought flashed through his mind and Love parted his lips. “Soul Queen.”
“Yes, go ahead.”
“Did you say Lion was Asian?”
“Yes, even with a mask, you can’t hide the color of your skin.”

As it was a Western game, the percentage of Asian Dungeon and Stone players was very small. Just look at Baekho Lee. He had opened a chatroom waiting for Koreans, but it took several years for him to meet a fellow countryman, and that countryman had been Elfnunna, the same person now suspected of being Bjorn Yandel.
Love straightened his posture. “Lion has only openly mentioned one identity: Clown’s. Correct?” he inquired.
“Uh, it’s hard to say since this was my first visit, but that’s what I think judging by the atmosphere when he brought it up.”
“In that case...” he murmured and fell into thought.

Bjorn Yandel had most recently fought against Corpse Collector. Could all this really be just a coincidence? Of course, since they had no way of finding out if he was the same person as Elfnunna, this all remained a huge leap. But because of that...
“When is Bjorn Yandel’s conferment ceremony?”
“I remember it being in three days.”
“Three days...” Soon, Love made up his mind. “I’m going to go out for the first time in a long time.”
Rather than ruminating on it for another hundred days, he may as well meet him in person.
“Hey, wake up, wake up! Wake up!”
The morning after spending time in the community, I woke up to a Back Smash from Missha. I was tired as hell from using murderous intent for the first time in a while.
“What did you do yesterday that you’re so exhausted this morrrning!?”

After community nights, it was better to wake up on time, even if you had to overdo it. To anyone who knew about that place, sleeping in could look suspicious. There were more eyes on me now than ever too.
And a goddamn assassin is on their way...
Yesterday, I had collapsed out of sheer exhaustion, but I didn’t think I’d be sleeping well from now on. Ha, so annoying.
Why can’t everyone just leave me alone?

I wouldn’t be able to fight like usual in my current state, either. The sighs came to me naturally, but I quickly washed my face and headed downstairs to share a meal with the others. It was a bit of a strange sight. That was because there was one more person at the breakfast table than usual.
“Y-You’re up?”
“Of course. Don’t just stand there, sit down. The food will get cold.”
“Y-Yes!” Erwen sat down, her expression nervous as she began to eat.
An uncharacteristically awkward silence fell over the table. Fortunately, Missha noticed it and asked enthusiastically, “So, how is it? My food.”
“I-It’s good... thank you...”
“Let me know if you want to eat anything. I’ll make it for dinnerrr later. Oh, and tell me if there’s anything you can’t eat too.” As always, Missha was considerate of even the minor details.
“Carrots! I can’t eat carrots!” Ainar jumped in at that point and received a Back Smash of her own.
Do you really think that’ll work? I’ve tried the same thing ten times, but every attempt has ended in failure.
Apparently, we had to eat those since we ate meat every day.
I am grateful, but... A barbarian has to live a barbarian lifestyle.
“I-I’ll do the dishes!”

After the meal, Ainar left for the holy land as always and the rest of us spent time together. The vibe was not as bad as I thought it would be. I guess you could say it felt like the hierarchy had been fully settled.
“Erwen, come sit over herrre. We should talk.”
“Y-Yes!”
“It might be a bit earrrly to ask this, but what are you going to do from now on? Our party is alrrready full, as you know.”
“That’s...” Erwen trailed off and glanced at me. She must have been asking if it was okay to talk about the clan.

Well, there was no reason she couldn’t. But I didn’t have the energy left to discuss it at length right now, so I just glossed over it. “It’s too early, Missha. We don’t even know if we’ll be able to enter the labyrinth next month.”
“That’s... trrrue.”
To be honest, unless this situation was declared resolved, it would be wise to stop exploring the labyrinth for a while. It wasn’t like we were hurting financially right now.
The irritating thing is that the city isn’t all that safe, either.

Between the Dragon Slayer, Corpse Collector, Noark’s mystery assassin, and even the actions of the palace, which were all too enigmatic, there were countless reasons for me to get stronger as soon as possible.
Still, it’d be better to keep an eye on the situation until it calms down to some extent.
I tried to let go of my impatience. As the saying went, “Even when you are in a hurry, take the long way around to be safe.”
That part I’ll have to discuss with Raven later.
Anyway, after that we ate snacks and talked about this and that. At first, Erwen looked downcast and uncomfortable, but because Missha treated her with kindness, she soon relaxed.
Still, it looks like she finished processing what happened to her sister before coming here.

That was a weight off my shoulders. In the future, she would inevitably have to shoulder even more heavy burdens, but Erwen was currently standing under her own power. There was no doubt she would be able to go even further.
“Huh? You have a youngerrr sibling?”
“Yes, she’s still young and living in the holy land. When she gets older... I’ll have to take care of her. Just like my sister did for me...”
“Nyaha, don’t worrry too much. You still have a long way to go. By then you will have much more wiggle room.”

“You think so...?” Surprisingly, their conversation was friendly. But Erwen suddenly bowed at her out of nowhere. “I-I never apologized for back then, did I? I-I’m sorry, something must have been wrong with my head that day...”
“Don’t apologize. It’s fine. Something good came out of all of that too.”
I cocked my head. “Back then”? Did the two of them have something to apologize for?
“B-But are you okay, sis...?”

“What’s not to be all rrright about? My thoughts have changed a lot since then too... It’s not like I’m qualified for the thing we talked about in the firrrst place.” Missha looked me up and down. For some reason, I shivered.
Knock, knock.
A knock sounded from the front door.
“I’ll go see.” I quickly got up and headed to the door. Normally I would’ve opened it straight away, but I learned yesterday that an assassin might be sent after me. First, I asked who it was.
“My name is Rayman Keplow, a knight of the Second Royal Guard.”

The knight politely revealed his identity, I guessed because I was due to receive the title of baronet. When I checked through the peephole, the armor looked legit, and other knights were standing behind him, surrounding him.
This doesn’t seem like a trick.
I opened the door because I had a guess as to why they were there, and I confirmed the reason they came face-to-face. It was the first bit of good news I had received in a while.
“An order has come down from above.”
“An order?”
“We’ve received instructions to protect Lord Yandel from any dangerous people that intend to harm him.”
So, Deer had made a move.

chapters.title: Chapter 241: Turning Point (1)
paragraphs: A total of twelve knights had been dispatched as my bodyguards. Eight of them stood guard outside the house and three stood guard indoors just in case of anything unexpected. The remaining one followed me wherever I went, even inside the house, and provided a close, dedicated escort.
“Did you say your name is Rayman Keplow?”

“Yes, sir.” The knight responded politely to whatever I said. This was new to me, but not all that unexpected. I was due to receive a title soon, so he must just have been treating me accordingly in advance.
Plenty of knights of the Royal Guard would have titles, too, but if all the guys he sent are like this... it would be fair to take it as a thoughtful gesture.
The first thing that told me was that Deer seemed like a meticulous person. I’d have to look more into that at some other time, though.
“You said earlier that this was an order from your superior. Who exactly gave you that order?”
Keplow answered my question. “To be honest... I don’t know that, either.”

I watched his expression carefully as he answered. It didn’t seem like he was lying. When I pressed further, I learned he had been dispatched having only been told it was on the orders of his immediate superior.
Yeah, if he has a brain, he would try to hide his identity.
It was kind of a shame. Considering this involved the palace, I might’ve been able to reach Deer’s identity...
...No, wait.
Suddenly, a possibility flashed through my mind.
“I heard he’s being paraded around as a hero? It’ll be so fun to see him die right after he receives his noble title. The palace’s reputation will go down the drain!”
I had at first assumed this was just an emotional outburst because there was so much resentment in his voice.
“You couldn’t control your emotions and even kindly warned the enemy? You really are a baby.”
Deer also thought the same.
But had that bastard actually been aiming for this?
It was possible that what Clown really wanted was to dig up Deer’s identity. Of course, since the jewel had turned green, the existence of an assassin was undeniable.
But if he can use this as bait to dig for clues about Deer, too, I’m sure he would have seen that as a win.
That made more sense. Clown may have been beaten up at the Round Table, but he was actually one of the big fish in this world. The “mistake” he had made was more than likely intentional.
Deer must have also had that possibility in mind to some extent, which is why he sent these men my way as discreetly as possible. Ha... there really aren’t any straight-forward bastards here, huh.

While the urge to sigh was almost overwhelming, on the other hand, this was motivation to remain alert in the future. Just look at today. If I’d kept sleeping out of exhaustion, Deer would have been able to realize something was strange from the knights’ report.
“Come drrrink this, Mr. Knight.”
“I cannot receive private favors from civilians—”
“Hey, this isn’t a favor. You’re going to have a hard time protecting Bjorn, arrren’t you?”

Missha went around serving tea to the knights like she was the lady of the house. Did this girl assume that a private escort was just one of the services that came with a title? Hmm, maybe, because she didn’t know anything about the assassin.
“Mr. Rayman Keplow, was it? I don’t know how long you’re going to be herrre, but make yourself at home in the meantime.”
In the end, Missha managed to seat Keplow at the table and serve him tea. “...I will call you Lady Karlstein.”

“Hm? It’s just Missha, but... if you want to call me that, I can’t forrrce you to stop...” Missha smoothly borrowed my soon-to-be-conferred title and led Keplow into using an honorific for her. Of course, I didn’t think that was intentional.
It must have just happened accidentally.
Anyway, Missha briefly introduced Keplow to Erwen and also Ainar, who was not here today.
“Should I call you Lady Erwen?”
“U-Uh... That’s...” Erwen trailed off awkwardly.
Sensing Erwen wasn’t comfortable with that, Missha came to her rescue. “That’s not necessarrry. Can’t you see she’s uncomfortable? Just call her Erwen.”
“Y-Yes! That would be good...”
“Then I will inform my subordinates to do so.”
The titles were decided at lightning speed.
Knock, knock.
Then there was another knock at the front door, despite it still being early in the morning.
“A teammate of Lord Yandel’s has arrived.” A knight informed us that the visitor was like a house servant. Was this why everyone was so obsessed with power?
“What teammate?”
“A wizard named Arua Raven.”
Keplow looked at me in askance and I nodded. That was enough.
Creak.
The door was opened by Keplow’s hand. Still sitting on the sofa, I raised an arm and greeted the visitor elegantly. “Ah, you’re here.” This was Barbarian Noblesse Mode.
Raven scoffed at the ridiculous greeting. “‘Ah, you’re here?’”
“A cup of tea?”
“Black, please.” Raven glanced at Keplow, who stood behind me like a bodyguard, and immediately sat on the sofa across from me. “So what’s with this situation?”
“It’s exactly what it looks like.”
“...I’m going to get pissed.”
What could this tiny girl do to me, anyway? Still, I quickly answered her. “The palace sent me knights as guards in case something happens before the conferment.”

“Hmm, that makes sense. You have a surprisingly high number of enemies, after all.” Raven readily accepted that explanation. Well, it was already well known that the Corpse Collector wouldn’t be leaving me alone. The large clans seemed disapproving too.
“Raven, my enemies are also your enemies.”
“...Why are you bringing that up so early in the morning?” As the morning was not usually when she was at her most active, Raven wasn’t in that great a mood.
“Here, black tea. You know where the sugar is, rrright?”
When Missha brought her a cup of tea, Raven sipped on it and shifted her gaze to Erwen.
“H-Hello, Miss Raven...”
“Ah, yes... Hello...” As their eyes met, the two exchanged awkward greetings.
I involuntarily cocked my head. “Didn’t you call each other by your first names before? I’m pretty sure that was the case.”
“Mr. Yandel, just shut up.” When my mouth clamped shut, Raven led the conversation as the elder of the two. “How are things these days?
“...All right. You don’t have to worry about me.”
“If you’re okay, I won’t. By the way, are you going to stay here from now on?”
“Yes... Thankfully, Sis gave me permission...”
“Hmm, is that so? That’s interesting.”
A few more exchanges followed and the conversation ended when Erwen returned to her room to get some rest.
“...Um, Mr. Keplow, are you going to keep standing there?”
“I’m used to these kinds of jobs, so don’t mind me and feel free to converse as usual.”
“If you say so...” She may have said that, but Raven’s expression was full of discomfort. She showed no signs of opening her mouth first.
Therefore, I decided to just ask the question on my mind instead of letting the awkwardness drag on. “What was that?”
“Can you please use nouns?”
“I mean with Erwen. I’m sure you’re not suddenly shy around her now.”

I had definitely sensed it during their conversation. Raven was having a really hard time dealing with Erwen, and I didn’t think it was simply because Erwen had recently lost a family member. So what was the real reason?
“Is there something I’m missing here?”
“Ugh, honestly, you’re way too quick when it comes to the weirdest things.”
“So, are you going to answer?”
Raven hesitated for a moment before opening her mouth with a sigh. “It’s just a little... I sort of feel like it’s my fault.”
“Your fault?”
“The spell that your wizard Dwalkie used. I know how to use it too.”

The gist of what Raven was saying was simple. When Fallen Scholar appeared, Raven had intuitively sensed the truly overwhelming difference in their abilities as wizards. And she knew that without using the Awakening technique, she wouldn’t be able to overcome that gap.
“I had no problem with the formula or mana, but the spell wouldn’t come out of me.”
I could understand. It was an easy spell that any wizard could cast, but not one everyone could actually use when the time came.
“It happened when I was hesitating.”
Fallen Scholar’s spell had fired, and the stone wall of mana Raven had erected was shattered all too easily. And as a result...
“Sometimes, when I’m alone in my empty laboratory I think that if I had used that spell, maybe her older sister would have survived.”
I smiled bitterly. I never dreamed that she would be thinking something like this.
“The same goes for you, Mr. Yandel, and everyone else on our team. We all could have died. But even knowing that, I...”

What was she talking about? I cut her off before the run-of-the-mill self-loathing rambling could start up. “Enough. Stop talking. It’s unfortunate what happened to Erwen, but none of us died, right?” That might have been a bit cold-hearted.

“You’re right.” Raven nodded and agreed. Regardless of ifs, ands, or buts, her time spent with Erwen and Daria had been short, meaning she couldn’t prioritize them over her actual party. “But the reason why things ended the way they did was because you did what I couldn’t, Mr. Yandel.”
I laughed light-heartedly and said in a joking tone, “Haha, that’s because I’m the leader.”
However, Raven just let out another small sigh. “Yeah, that’s exactly why...”
“Huh?”
“...I’m just trying to say that being sentimental like this isn’t like me.”

I nodded subconsciously at that. Well, when I first met her, my impression of her was completely different from what it was now. Anyway, Raven didn’t seem to want to talk at length about this as she changed the subject.
“Mr. Yandel, what are you going to do about Erwen? The party is full and there is no room for her to join.”
“I’m thinking.”
“Then what about the labyrinth? Are you going in?”
“I’m going to keep an eye on how things are developing for now. If things continue like this, it’ll be tough to go in.”
“...That’s true.”
“So, is that all you’re here for today?”
“No, I have different matters. I have something to tell you.”
I was a believer that no news was good news, so Raven’s words were enough to activate my anxiety alarms.
“I’ve decided to take lessons from Sir Pevrosk.”
“What? Surely you’re not going to leave the party to take classes?”
“Sorry? Of course not. Why would you think that?”
That was because the exact same thing had happened to me several times before.
“But what are you going to learn in the class? Don’t you have a school already?”

“I can’t learn court magic at Altemion.” Right, she had earned the right to learn court magic as her reward. “I was hoping someone could help me lay the groundwork, and thankfully Sir Pevrosk agreed.” Raven proceeded to explain she would be staying at an inn near the palace instead of the Magic Tower and that I should come to find her there if I needed to. “That’s the end of my business. I’ll get going. See you later.”
That was apparently really all she had to say because Raven left as soon as she finished the tea Missha brought her.

On May 18th, Team Apple Narak, excluding Raven, visited the palace again. There were still two days left until my conferment, but apparently, we needed to come in advance to decide what I’d receive as a reward.
Yeah, I’m sure it’ll look better to reward it where everyone can see.
There wasn’t a banquet so we didn’t need to dress as formally as last time. However, equipment was still prohibited in the palace so we were in clean everyday clothes.
“Oh, Yandel! Are you here today too?” Upon entering the palace, some adventurers I was acquainted with immediately struck up conversations. Like me, they were set to receive their rewards today.
They mentioned they started going down the list and calling everyone a few days ago.
The monetary compensation had already been paid in bulk, but those who had the opportunity to choose essences or equipment had had to wait on a waiting list.
“Then we’ll head in firrrst, Bjorn!”
After arriving at the palace, I got separated from my team because their rewards were different from mine.
“S-So it’s just us two...” I was in a waiting room with one of my knight escorts, a royal guide, and Erwen. “Mister... is it okay for me to accept something like this?”
“If not you, who will? Have confidence. These people are not kind enough to hand out rewards to people for no reason.”
Why was she acting like this after we’d already come all this way? “You have to get stronger. You and me both. That way we won’t lose anything else.”
“...Yes, you’re right.” Erwen nodded, looking more resolute.
As we made small talk, another guide arrived to take Erwen to the Silver Soul Repository, where rank-four essences and items of that ranking were stored.
If the Gold Soul Repository were open to her, I would’ve been able to feed her her final essence right away.
It really was a pity. It wasn’t that there weren’t any core essences for an elven archer among the rank-four essences, but one rank higher and she could’ve had that.
I’m sure she’ll get it someday. It’s about time to head up to the sixth floor.

I shook off my regrets. After these rewards, our combat power would rise significantly. There was no need to keep wandering around on the fifth floor, building up strength. The problem was those bastards from Noark, though. But considering the moves the assholes in the palace were making, it seemed they had some sort of solution to that too.
“Lord Yandel, please come this way.”

As I sat there organizing my thoughts, my personal guide arrived and led me to the Gold Soul Repository. It was a basement with no windows, but because of the bright flames everywhere, it didn’t feel dark at all. Rather, it was so bright it was hard to think of it as underground.
Feels like we’ve gone down to at least the fifth underground floor... the architectural technology in this world is strangely advanced.

When we arrived at our destination, a knight greeted me with great vigor. There was also a wizard next to him. He gave me brief instructions. The time limit was three hours. I could choose my desired essence or item, and if I attempted to steal or break anything, it could lead to severe punishment. He was basically telling me to be careful.
Geez, so intense.
After that explanation was over, the huge iron door opened smoothly like gravity didn’t affect it at all.
Whistle...
Thousands of essences in test tubes and displayed in glass cases greeted me. Each was on par with an Ogre essence. Although I could only take one, I felt my lips curl into a smile.
This makes it feel like I used some sort of cheat code.
It was time to get stronger.

chapters.title: Chapter 242: Turning Point (2)
paragraphs: Upon entering the Gold Soul Repository, I knew for certain why the other races couldn’t exert their power in front of the king. I guess you could say I saw what they were capable of. Precious rank-three essences filled half the vast treasury, and it wasn’t even just one of each.
There are seven or eight each of easy to obtain and rarely used essences.
Most of them had spares. Even difficult to acquire essences only obtained in Rifts had at least one of each color.
Shit, even the essence of Nibaroque?

That was the essence of a rare monster that only appeared in Rifts, although it wasn’t really an option for a barbarian warrior. Still, in terms of sheer acquisition difficulty, it was better than a rank-two essence.
How did they collect all these?
The more I looked around, the stronger the thought grew. Though maybe this kind of thing became possible when a single royal line was around for thousands of years?
I thought in the game you could pick whatever you wanted because it was just a game.

I dismissed the thought that the palace could be brought down by Noark. How could you consider the possibility of losing after seeing this? There were thousands of rank-three essences here. I didn’t know what their current troops looked like, but this meant the palace could produce a ridiculously powerful army if they wanted to.
If you feed five rank-three essences to a knight who can use an aura...
It was wild to even think about, and it didn’t end with rank three. In the repository one rank higher, I was sure they had rank two essences too.
...Maybe even rank one.
What was scarier was that it didn’t end with essences. There were also Numbers Items.
Since the Gold Soul Repository has triple digits, the one above will have doubles and then singles.
Though they were lower priority than an essence, they were the easiest ways to bring up your stats when you hit a limit development-wise.
I do have something I want, but not as much as an essence. Hmm, should I still look around?
Since there was time left, I looked around at the items inside the Gold Soul Repository with interest. Though I already knew all the options and quickly lost said interest.
“Um, touching is...”
“It won’t wear it out, so what are you worried about?!”
It was quite fun seeing the wizard who came as my guide turn white as a sheet every time I touched an item.
Enough touring around.
It was now time to make a decision, and so I did a final check. I’d already decided which essence to take, but just in case.
All right then, let’s start with this one.

Bellarios was a Chinese dragon, a monster reminiscent of an Imugi and basically a higher-level version of the Manticore. Its basic stats were heavy on Mana Resistance and it even had Circulation Ring, which was an unusual passive skill that allowed the user to accumulate stats.
Well, the passive will be almost impossible to use in my current state.

Circulation Ring was only effective once you reached a level where you could hunt at least a rank-three monster. It was really thanks to its active that it became a core essence of my build in the first place. When used, Scales of Greed temporarily grew scales on the user’s skin and their Magical Resistance rose in proportion to their Mana Resistance. For reference, when Mana Resistance surpassed 1500, you unlocked Magical Immunity, which then made it possible to kill wizards like bugs. That would make Barbarian Dragon Mode possible.
Usually, this essence wouldn’t be worth eating right now.

If it weren’t for Fallen Scholar, it wouldn’t have even made my list. When it came to going on expeditions, the Manticore essence was more than enough. I had to absorb it someday, but how fast I developed would depend on which essence I consumed first.
Anyway, on to the second option.

Vol-Herchan was a super-huge monster whose entire body was covered by a shell. As could be told just from its outward appearance, it possessed a defense-related skill. The passive worked well with Ironskin and the active made the user’s body able to withstand even an aura. Put simply, it was an essence you should get in preparation for dealing with an aura, which made it an essence with an ability I didn’t have yet. If I’d had this, my arm would’ve remained intact against the aura-using adventurer from Noark.
Amelia... that woman used an aura too...
Since Clown said he would be sending an assassin, this essence had gone up on the list. To be honest, Amelia was the scariest assassin I could imagine.
Besides, I’ll be fighting against more people in the future.

That wasn’t to say that it was useless against monsters. Being able to counter an aura was only an added bonus. More importantly, it came with super-high Strength stats, making it the most balanced of all the candidates in terms of offense and defense.

Then, finally, came Bayon, the sole monster classified as small among rank three, which was dominated by large monsters. It was also one of the few humanoid monsters, along with being undead. In other words, it was immortal. According to the game, Bayons were ancient heroes who had died and came back to life, which might have been why they had a very unique ability. These monsters fought with essences like adventurers. The combination of essences was different for each Bayon, but all of them had one thing in common—the skill linked to the essence—Transcendence.

What was unusual was that if you consumed its essence, you only got this one skill. The passive and active pretty much became synonymous. However, the basic stat increase the essence provided came with an additional boost to the super-rare Soul Power stat, so the advantage was that you wouldn’t have to worry about MP after taking it.
Then what should I choose?
I had to consume each of these essences at some point. It was just a matter of which to take first. Thinking it through for the last time, I made a decision.
Yes, if I can only consume one, this should be it.
I was looking forward to the conferment day.
“Hmm, you mean this essence?” When I chose my essence, the wizard’s expression went strange. “It is a good essence. Then I will report that to the Prime Minister.”
“Oh, can you add in a Numbers Item? Looks like they’re just gathering dust—”
“I cannot.”
Geez, so snippy. I was half-joking. After going through an additional full-body search and returning to the reception room, I found my teammates, who had arrived before me.
Mr. Bear greeted me with a smile. “I guess the Gold Soul Repository took longer.”
“What essence did you choose?” I asked.
“I just chose the one you mentioned. It didn’t seem like a bad choice, and you said it’s secret lore, right?”

Secret lore, put simply, was a tried and true combination of essences, like ones a historical hero or great adventurer once had. Of course, the essence combinations of those people were well-known but mostly made up of higher-ranking essences, so it was difficult information to use unless you were a high-ranking adventurer. The useful lower-level combinations were publicly known as well. For example, Hikurod had known to use Emergency Restoration to reset the cooldown time of his numbered item. That must have been a bit of secret lore circulated among the dwarves.

“I should sign up for a training ground once I get back.” Mr. Bear had chosen an essence on my recommendation and was filled with the desire to leave the palace quickly to use his newly acquired skills. And it seemed everyone else was in the same boat.
“Bjorn, let’s go home! The power of a warrior is overflowing within me! I have to let it out quickly!”
The three of them had only obtained rank-five essences, unlike me, but I was jealous. After all, I had to wait until my conferment day to get mine.
“Ugh, be patient, will you? Erwen hasn’t come back yet.”
“Tell that elf to get home by herself!”
“Hey, what did I say about talking like that?” Missha scolded Ainar and defended Erwen.
“I-It was a slip of the tongue. No more carrot soup, please...”
It was reassuring when the eldest sister had your back, huh? After a little while’s wait, Erwen returned from selecting hers as well.
“You’re late. Was there a problem?” I asked.
“No. I chose the one you picked for me. But I couldn’t adjust to it right away so I had to take a break...”
Hmm, that made sense. A high-ranking essence usually came with a big change to the body.
“S-Sorry. Did you wait long?”
“No need to be sorry, as long as nothing’s wrong. Now, let’s get back.”

Afterward, we took the carriage provided by the palace and returned to District Seven, which felt like home now. We headed straight to the training grounds, the only place in the city where the use of special abilities and skills was permitted.

“Then let me go first.” Mr. Bear summoned Iron Bear, Iradun, then placed a pig he had purchased at the entrance of the training ground on the target. “I can’t make myself do it. Missha, can you help me?”
“Me? Uh... okay.” Missha used her sword to make a cut on Bear and the preparations were complete.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Starving Claw.]
Soon, the arrow he was holding began to emit a red light. Mr. Bear notched it on the bow and aimed it at the pig’s thigh.
Plunk! Squeal!
The pig let out a braying squeal and went into a frenzy. However, it did not take long for that energy to disappear.
Slump.
Despite the fact that the arrow didn’t even hit its vitals, the pig soon collapsed and stopped moving. No blood flowed out from the wound because the arrow embedded in it was absorbing it.
Shaaa!
Even at this moment, the arrow stuck in the pig was extracting its life force and delivering it to Mr. Bear.
Here comes the best part of the combo.
[Abman Urikfried’s Vitality is currently maxed out. Any additional Vitality will be transferred to the target his soul is connected to.]
The excess vitality passed through Mr. Bear and on to Bear again.
“Woom?” Bear’s injury was healed in no time.
“I was skeptical, but it really is able to heal a Soul Beast.”

“The book said that this ability will treat you as the first priority for healing if you get hurt too, so keep that in mind.” Even though I was saying that, Mr. Bear was unlikely to get hurt as a long-ranger, so it was safe to say our tank line had gotten stronger. And the perks didn’t end there. About three minutes after the arrow was shot, the pig’s corpse dried up like a mummy’s.
That’s not bad for a sustained damage deal.

Mr. Bear also had Hook Arrow so once one of his arrows was embedded in something, it was hard to remove. That meant that once it was stuck inside you, it would continue to damage you and absorb your blood.
Once he gets Altruism later, he’ll be able to treat our wounds too.
Of course, that was just a convenient side effect of his development. I didn’t plan to make Mr. Bear a healer, since every essence slot was precious. Heals were best left to a professional healer.
It’s about time to find a priest too...
Anyway, next was Ainar.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Wildness Control.]
A rank-five essence couldn’t be used as a final essence anyway, so I picked out something with the best immediate effects that could be used for a long time.
[All effects applicable to her next attack will be converted into Cutting Force.]

Thanks to Wildness Control, the effects of both Blast Scars—which created an explosion when the user hit the same spot twice—and Vitality Absorption—which increased the user’s healing factor upon attacking an enemy—were converted into slashing damage.
Slice!
Though it may have been an adamantium greatsword, it still sliced through the steel bar like butter.
“Can I try it with another sword?”
“Why not? Have at it.”
Unlike the pig, steel bars were free. These could be restored with magic.
“Then...” Skeptical, Ainar tested the ability again with a cheap steel sword provided by the training grounds. The results were the same.
Slice!
The steel bar was halved with a single stroke.
Great, this gives us more options.

She’d fight by using explosion and blood absorption attacks against multiple enemies and then, when it came to strong, singular opponents, raising her Cutting Force. To put it simply, she was no longer a smurfing, one-trick barbarian.

“Then is it my turrrn now?” After that, Missha tested her newly obtained essence too, followed by Erwen. Both of them wore looks of satisfaction as the compatibility of their essences exceeded their expectations.
...Leaving me a sad barbarian.
Why was I the only one without a new essence?

Two days later, I visited the palace again. To be honest, I wasn’t as nervous as I was the first time anymore. How many times had it been this month alone? Of course, today’s visit was a little different from the previous one.
“Since you’re so tall, could you bend down a bit?”

The attendants were not satisfied with the banquet clothes Kyle had gifted me and swarmed me, intending to dress me up to the fullest. Also, my team wasn’t around. That was because I was the only one who had been invited today. Even a renowned figure could not attend a conferment ceremony unless they were nobility—it was a long-held tradition of the palace.
Things are already noisy in there.

I was currently inside the Palace of Glory, where I had been once before. Musical instruments could be heard from the inner hall. It seemed the banquet had already started. It’d probably be reaching its climax when we entered.
“Oh, you look much better in those clothes.” As I waited there all dressed up, Count Ferdehilt came to see me with his youngest daughter from our last encounter.
“I-I’m Arabella Ferdehilt.” The daughter still seemed afraid and couldn’t make eye contact with me.

I guessed the count didn’t plan to bother me with talk of an arranged marriage on a day like today because he left me alone after some basic chitchat. Or, well, it may have been more accurate to call it a warning.
“There are a total of three people, including you, who are being awarded titles today. One is a viscount and the other is a marquess.”
I’d heard that. Unlike me, it would be more accurate to call their new titles promotions rather than bestowals.
“I don’t mind the viscount, but the prospective marquess from the Kudou family is famous for his petulance and for being extremely competitive.”
“In a word, he’s immature.”

“...That’s an accurate description. So be careful. Today is a once-in-a-lifetime event. They might be thinking you stole their spotlight. Ah, but if they try to provoke you, have restraint. Now that you’re a part of this world, you can’t just do as you please. All right?”
“I will remember your advice.”
“Yes, that should be enough. Then I’ll stop bothering you. See you later.”
The count took his daughter and casually left, just like that. It seemed his only purpose was to make friends with me.
Politics, huh?

It reminded me of the events in Doppelganger Forest and made me laugh. Would barbarian-style politics work in aristocratic society? As I passed the time with silly daydreams, the day quickly fell into night.
Wow, have I really been in this small waiting room for over ten hours?
When I stepped out into a hallway laid with red carpet a long while later, two men were waiting for me, also dressed to the nines for conferment day.
That little one over there must be the viscount.
I studied the other man, who had a fairly good build for a human. Judging by those sharp eyes, he was obviously the marquess.
“Nice to meet you. I hear you’ll be bestowed the title of baronet today? Congratulations, indeed. Having a hero like you as a part of our society is a blessing to the palace.”

The prospective viscount offered up various platitudes he didn’t mean, but the prospective marquess said none of those things. He scoffed like he didn’t even want to speak to a commoner savage like me.
Well, that’s easier for me.
I wasn’t interested, either. I had no intention of wasting my time with politics. What I wanted was a rank-three essence and an advantageous noble title.
“Today’s honorees are entering!”
Soon, upbeat music rang out and the door opened.
Come to think of it, this is the second time I’ve passed through this door this month.
With nothing to be nervous about, I casually walked the carpet. Our formation was the prospective marquess in the middle, me on the left, and the prospective viscount on the right.
Step, step.

We walked forward to cheers from the other nobles and stopped in front of the empty throne, where the prime minister stood. He threw out some ceremonial lines and we bowed on one knee as instructed. And that was when...
Hmm?
Just as I was about to squat down, the prospective marquess prick started tipping toward me.
The heck? Did he lose his balance?

My first thought was that I should probably help him steady himself, but I soon realized that wasn’t necessary. My subconscious caught a dark emotion in his movements—malice. It was truly ridiculous. It seemed like he intended to push me by “accident” and make me crash to the floor.
Is he fucking crazy?

Putting aside the fact that he was pulling such a dirty move right in front of countless nobles and even the prime minister, who was the palace’s second-in-command, did he really think that would work?
The best defense was a good offense. I subconsciously tensed my body and we collided at the same time.
Smack!
What followed unfolded according to the laws of physics.
“Aaagh!”

The prospective marquess was flung forward with a heavy thud and rolled in a complete circle across the carpet. As a bonus, his fancy suit wrinkled right up. The music stopped at the horrifying show of impropriety and silence fell. Suddenly, the count’s advice came to mind.
Oh, right. He told me to have restraint.

chapters.title: Chapter 243: Turning Point (3)
paragraphs: The moment the prospective marquess’ body leaned toward Bjorn Yandel’s, a man watching the situation from a distance smirked.
The rumors were true.
Even “thug” wasn’t a strong enough word to describe this guy. To think he would try to play a trick like that in front of the prime minister...
No, maybe he believes that the prime minister and the other noblemen won’t blame him.

Hmm, it was an understandable assumption when you thought about it more carefully. There was clearly a difference between a born nobleman who would soon be a marquess and a barbarian adventurer who was only now being given the title of baronet. Due to the exclusive nature of aristocratic society, even more blatant bullying was common, and it was implicitly tolerated. It was a kind of hazing process.
You have to admit he’s bold, though.

The prospective marquess wasn’t a knight. He had taken a few essences for the sole purpose of appearing more intimidating. To pick a hand-to-hand fight against the adventurer who was known to have defeated the Corpse Collector...
Ah, come to think of it, he’s injured, right?

Belatedly, the man remembered that Bjorn Yandel was still suffering from the side effects of the previous battle. Apparently, the poison had infiltrated even his brain. They said that at the recent banquet in his honor, he had been dripping sweat just from walking. That was probably the reason the marquess felt comfortable trying something like this.
...This is just going to ruin my mood.

At the potential future that came to mind, the man frowned. Malice hidden behind the splendor of nobility, a hero suffering humiliation in front of everyone... that wasn’t something he wanted to see in his first outing in a long time.
“Huh?”
The man tilted his head as something completely unexpected happened. The barbarian’s body didn’t budge despite the prospective marquess’ dirty trick.
Has he already recovered somewhat? That’s good.
Just as he was thinking this, the barbarian’s shoulder muscles, which could not be concealed by clothes made of cotton, twitched.
“Aaagh!” Right at that moment, the prospective marquess bounced backward. Even the music stopped and silence fell. His brain struggled to process what had just happened.
...Did he just push that asshole marquess?!

That barbarian would never have done something like this if he had remembered the consequences. For some reason, the man’s secondhand embarrassment spiked and he felt rather dizzy. He was glad that the barbarian’s condition had improved enough that he wasn’t subject to lowly manipulations, but...
You should have pretended you didn’t notice.

If it were him, he would’ve said, “Haha, did my legs give out? I should work out more,” and gotten the marquess back later. It was less risky that way. Well, you could say he acted like a typical barbarian.
If it were really him, he wouldn’t have pulled something like this.

Then was he really a native barbarian as suspected? The man was disappointed, but kept an eye on the situation. Still, you never knew. This guy may have been another big deal, even if it wasn’t him. After all, Bjorn Yandel was suspected of being a player due to his meteoric rise.
Let’s observe for now.
He refocused on the situation with those thoughts in mind.

“Bjorn, son of Yandel.” The prime minister called out the barbarian’s name in a troubled tone. He already knew about the prospective marquess’ trick, of course, and also how the barbarian had reacted to it.
Now then, how will you get yourself out of this?
The man’s anticipation didn’t fade as he waited for the barbarian to open his mouth. It didn’t take long.

Soon, the barbarian shouted, “I-I did nothing wrong!” like everything about this was unfair. It was a protest that lacked any logical defense, like a child throwing a tantrum. “It’s true! I was just standing here when he used me to roll forward!”
He even went as far as blatantly placing the responsibility on the marquess. The man found himself growing disappointed.
“Marquess! Speak up too! Tell him you just felt like doing forward rolls!”
He recalled the people who had met Bjorn Yandel commenting in the community that he could not possibly be a player. Only then did he finally understand what they all meant.
This is supposed to be a modern man...?
The man’s eyes dimmed as he stared at the barbarian.

The conferment ceremony was over. To be honest, I didn’t really remember how it went. It was boring. The prime minister used all the rhetoric in the world to drone out a speech and with the words, “I confer this title on behalf of the king,” I became an official nobleman of this country. And so the banquet began.
God damn it.

It was different from the appreciation party. Back then, many nobles had come up to me to make friends or out of pure curiosity. There was no one around me now, though, Baron Martoin included. Even the count who had tried to pursue an arranged marriage only glanced at me from a distance. The treatment I was getting was completely different from the treatment of the marquess and viscount, who were surrounded by many people.
Well, it wasn’t that I didn’t get it. I’d been properly targeted by the marquess after what had happened.
Ha... all because of one weirdo.
Now that things had come to this, I tore through the piece of meat I was holding in my hand and recalled what happened earlier.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

How was I meant to navigate a situation where even the prime minister was looking at me with disapproval in his eyes? The solution I decided on was this, the thing that always served as a big help to me in times of trouble: Brainless Barbarian Mode.
“I-I did nothing wrong!”
Everyone already knew that the fault lay with the marquess, anyway. I just decided to be shameless. Political maneuvering didn’t suit a barbarian in the first place.
“It’s true! I was just standing here when he used me to roll forward!”
As expected, the prime minister couldn’t say anything in response to that.
“...Roll forward?”
Guys who spent all day holding pens and sitting at desks were like this. No matter how smart and quick-witted they were, they were bound to have zero experience with conversations like these.
“Marquess! Speak up too! Tell him you just felt like doing forward rolls!”
Even the nobles who had interpreted my actions as a challenge changed their minds as Brainless Barbarian Mode continued. They had realized that barbarians were literally a different race from them.
“...Speak, Kariot Kudou. Is that true?”
The prime minister stared the marquess down, his eyes cold, and the marquess replied in fright, “O-Of course not, prime minister! That barbarian dared to push me without knowing his place—”
“Stop.”
Cutting the bewildered marquess off, the prime minister plastered on a warm smile without a word. It was an unspoken threat to not turn this into a big scene.
“Yes... that’s... right.”
In the end, the marquess had no choice but to admit that he wanted to roll forward, because the prime minister’s response indicated he was siding with me. Any nobleman would be able to tell.
That prime minister guy makes me uneasy too.
Anyway, whatever. The conferment ceremony resumed as if nothing had happened, and it ended with the essence I had chosen two days ago being delivered to me in a luxurious box. Cut to now.
Should I just go home?
Sitting alone at a round table munching on meat, the desire to return home began boiling inside of me.
Hmm, one more dish, then.
Decision made, I asked the attendant placed at my table to bring me another plate filled to the brim with meat.
Hmm?
A while later, I turned around upon sensing a presence, but what I saw was a man instead of the meat platter I was waiting for. “Haha, nice to meet you, Baronet Yandel.”
This was the first nobleman to approach me after hours of mistreatment. As soon as our eyes met, my barbarian intuition spoke to me. Something was off.
“I am Hans from the House of Baron Ifreia.”
This man is dangerous.
Hans Ifreia. In short, Hans I.

“...You are more reserved than I thought.” As the youngest of the baron’s family, he didn’t have a title, but his presence was still suffocating. An aristocratic Hans? This was a type of Hans I’d never seen before!
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel.” My plan was to briefly introduce myself and leave, claiming to be busy.
But just then, the meat platter I ordered earlier arrived. “Huff, huff. Here it is, Baronet Yandel.” Considerate of my appetite, the attendant brought me mountains of meat on three different plates.
“...Thanks.” The words of gratitude came out of my mouth absentmindedly. But what was this?
“This... is the first time...” The attendant looked at me, clearly touched. “No one has ever said that to me since I started this job...”
Oh, these aristocratic bastards. The attendant asked me to request whatever I wanted without hesitation, then stood behind me in wait.
I was just going to go.
For some reason, I got the sense that would hurt his feelings, so I grabbed a piece of meat with one hand.
“It seems you are still eating. If it’s all right with you, may I join you?”

Had I been an ordinary noble, I would’ve readily granted that request or beat around the bush to reject it, but I was a barbarian from the city. “That’d be kind of awkward.” I straight-up told him I was uncomfortable.
Hans I’s eyes narrowed. “Hmm, you’re different from what I’ve heard.” His tone and the look in his eyes were somewhat peculiar.
“Different?” I asked.
“Oh, please excuse me. I just thought that you wouldn’t be uncomfortable with something like this.”
Who the hell was this bastard? For the youngest member of a baron’s family and someone without a title, he was strangely relaxed. Also, his name was Hans.
...Why did he come up to me?
It looked like I should suss him out. After a moment of thought, I spoke casually. “You should have a plate. It’s awkward eating alone.”
“Aha, that’s what you meant.” At my words, Hans I ordered the food he wanted from the attendant. That was how our alone time began.

“Nice to meet you. I was bored sitting here by myself.” I held out the hand that had been holding the food without wiping it down. Hans I hesitated for a moment before grabbing it. Ah, that disgusted expression...
Ha, this makes him even more suspicious.

What reason did he have to stay in this seat, going so far as to shake my greasy hand? I opened my mouth to find out, wide enough that it wouldn’t be strange if the pieces of meat I was chewing on landed on his face. “So! Hans Ifreia? I like you! Let’s be friends!”
Hans didn’t answer.
“Why, do you not want to be friends?”
At my question, he laughed awkwardly as he removed flecks of meat from his face one by one. “No, of course not...”
“Haha, I’m glad!”

Soon, the meal he ordered arrived, and we ate and chatted together. Congratulations on the title. The weather is nice today. Most of it was small talk like that, and at some point, Hans I stopped touching his plate. That was because the meat chunks flying from my mouth ended up on it.
“Why aren’t you eating?”
“...My stomach doesn’t feel well.”
“Hmm, it’s awkward eating alone.” That meant, get to the real reason you’re here quickly or get lost. So, how would this guy react? The answer was really simple.
“If you are uncomfortable, then I will take my leave.” Hans I rose from his seat without hesitation. “Have a nice meal.” He immediately left the table.
What was that?
Did he really just want to be friends? The fact that he just left made me more uneasy.

By early evening, the sun was slowly starting to set. After sending away Hans I, I half ran away from the palace and boarded the carriage heading home. That was because I had met a Hans, and I had no idea what kind of trouble I might end up in while spending time in a place riddled with nobility.
Let’s start with the essence first.
As soon as I got out of the palace, I greeted Keplow, who started guarding me again, and opened the test tube bottle.
Come to think of it, this is the first time I’m absorbing one without breaking the bottle.
Corpse Golem, Orc Hero, Manticore—each situation was different but in the end, I had to crack the bottle open to take them. Well, it wasn’t like they could be reused either way.
Whoop.
Putting the test tube to my nose and breathing in deep, the essence flowed into my body like smoke.
[The Essence of the Bayon is seeping into your soul.]

There was one reason I had ended up choosing this guy. In fact, right now it would have been more advantageous to take the essence of Vol-Herchan to prepare for auras and increase my combat power, but... there was a vast difference in how difficult it was to acquire each.
Now that I have this, I can just take the experience points from the Land of Immortality and skip it.
Vol-Herchan traveled in groups and was easy to run into, while Bayons were hard to even come by and their area was very tricky. My choice this time around was made with the future in mind.
The only difference between them is the characteristics of the essence—there’s no significant difference in terms of stats.
Besides, considering the effect of the next Spirit Imprint, this choice made more sense.
[Your Soul Power has increased by +100. Your Soul Regeneration has increased by +30. Your Strength has increased by +25.]

A sensation of fullness rose from the depths of my chest, a new feeling of vitality delivered by smaller, rarer physical stats. After enjoying the afterglow for a minute, I opened my eyes. Keplow smiled and offered words of congratulations.
It’s late today, so I’ll have to wait until tomorrow to go to the training grounds.
Disappointed about not being able to use my newly acquired ability right away, I closed my eyes again. A long while passed.
Creak.
Suddenly, the carriage stopped in the middle of the street. Did a wheel fall off?
Just as I was thinking that, Keplow, who was a human-born knight with an aptitude for mana that my barbarian self lacked, shouted, “I can sense mana below us! You have to get off—!”
There was a huge explosion and flames surrounded us from all sides.
CRASH!
The carriage shattered into pieces in an instant.
Beeeeeeep!
Through the ringing in my ears, I could hear the knights shouting. “Assassin! The assassin is here!”
Damn it all.

chapters.title: Chapter 244: Turning Point (4)
paragraphs: Hans Ifreia—or the man who borrowed his name and appearance to attend the conferment ceremony—washed his face with cold water.
Splash!
Each time the water touched his skin, bits of meat washed away and down the drain. The sight was enough to make him want to throw up.
...It’s been a while since I’ve been this disgusted.
Upon falling into this familiar, yet unfamiliar world, he had experienced far worse things from the get-go, but those days were already far behind him.
Instead of approaching, I should just observe from a distance.

After returning to the banquet hall, the man looked to the table where he spoke to the barbarian earlier. For some reason, it was empty. When he approached the nearby servant and exchanged a few words, he learned that the barbarian had already left in a carriage.
I don’t feel like going back to the Magic Tower like this...
The man thought it over for a moment and left the palace. Then, using both an invisibility spell and a hovering spell, he flew over the city in Stealth Flight Mode.
There he is.

He looked down at the street from his spot several yards in the air and soon spotted the carriage carrying Bjorn Yandel. It would have been hard not to spot it, considering the knights on horseback surrounding it.
Looks like he’s going home.

Inferring the carriage’s destination from the direction it was traveling, the man started to tail it. Although his hope that that barbarian was the person he was looking for had largely faded, it was still possible that what he had seen was a facade. He was the first barbarian he had ever seen act that brainless. And there were even more suspicious things about him.
With his understanding of the game, he would have figured out how he was meant to act in this world before anyone else and begun to play his role perfectly.
As such, the barbarian’s actions up to this point could be interpreted either way, positive or negative, so the man needed more information. What kind of person was Bjorn Yandel?
They say he’s living with three women...

Ignoring a rising envy, the man eagerly chased after the carriage. If they were living together, it wouldn’t be any regular relationship. He’d be able to find more decisive clues by taking a peek into the barbarian’s home life.
Kabooom!
While he was in the process of following the carriage with that thought in mind, it exploded.
The explosion brought to mind the pillars of fire from that day, but the force of it was nothing compared to back then, fortunately.
[Your HP is below 50%. All Resistance and Resilience stats have increased due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]

My vision was blurry, likely due to retina damage from the heat. Also, reddened skin was peeling off of me and my whole body was itching and throbbing. I seemed to have suffered a lot of muscle damage too.
“Assassin! The assassin is here!”
But I hadn’t died in one blow, and my body could still move.
Damn it all.
Suppressing the curses clawing up my throat, I quickly gripped the ground and stood up. Then I activated the sub-space ring I’d retrieved upon leaving the palace.
Man, I should have put on equipment first thing.
Regret always came a moment too late. I first took out my shield and secured it to my forearm. Then, something else exploded with a burst of black smoke.
Is that a smoke bomb?
Since I had already experienced my vision being blocked in battle several times before, I quickly focused on my sense of hearing without panicking or missing a beat.
“Kyahhh!”
Since this incident was happening in the middle of the city, I could hear the screams of civilians all around me.
“These insolent—!”
“Down with these wicked rebels!”
The knights responded to the threat and sounds of weapons being drawn were heard, but I had to focus on something else. Through all the noise, I had to distinguish the one threatening my life.
Dash.
For example, that one. As soon as I heard the sound, I turned my body in its direction and shifted my posture, lowering my shoulder. At that moment, a heavy blow jolted through my shield.
Bang!
Whew, so you guys can see where I am even through the smoke.

That meant I no longer had a reason to keep quiet. “Keplow! Are you alive!?” Shouting at the top of my lungs, I tried to confirm the safety of Keplow, who had been next to me right before the explosion. There was no answer. Was he dead? Or just unconscious?
Slide.
I quickly slid a hand into the sub-space and took out my mace. At that exact moment, I heard what sounded like something slicing the air.
Whooom!
In my experience, this kind of sound usually came from a slash. Trusting my subconscious’s judgment, I twisted the shield diagonally.
Boom!
An instant later, something collided with the left side of the shield. If things kept going this smoothly, being blinded wouldn’t be a problem.
Voom!
I swung the mace with all my might in the direction where I believed the enemy to be.
Crunch!
The resulting blow felt satisfying.
Hmm, can’t avoid that? I thought an assassin would be a High Agility type.
“Kurgh!” Something in the smoke released a scream like a death throe as it was launched somewhere far away.
Shaaaaaa!
A clearly artificial gust of wind blew through the street and pushed back the black smoke.
Magic? Whose is it?
There were no wizards on our side. That said, the assassin wouldn’t have cleared the smoke themself. So who had cast the spell? Dismissing the short-lived question, I scanned my surroundings.
“Lord Yandel! Are you all right?”
The number of knights left standing was only four. On the other hand, the number of masked people surrounding the shattered wagon was over thirty.
Is Amelia... not here?
I examined the masked people to see if there was anyone with a build similar to Amelia’s. There were about three candidates, but I wasn’t sure.
“No one mentioned there’d be wizards!”
“What are you hesitating for? Kill him already!”

Briefly bewildered by the spell that drove away the smoke, the assassins resumed their assault. I was sure they were well aware that since this was a surprise attack in the middle of a busy street, the longer they took to finish, the more trouble this would be for them.
“Protect Lord Yandel!”

The knights, who were each fighting their own battles, confirmed my location before converging and standing in a protective formation around me. I could see why nobles were so obsessed with training knights. How loyal and trustworthy were they?
I don’t think I have time to put on armor.

After taking stock of the situation, I neatly dismissed my disappointment and manifested a special ability, the one I had originally planned to use at the training grounds tomorrow. Bayon’s ability, Transcendence, was a unique skill that was both passive and active. When activated, the performance of all passive skills was enhanced by 1.5 times. Acid Fluid became more powerful, Path of Heroes and Ironskin’s stats increased, and Manticore’s Heredity was similarly affected. That alone was already great.
[You have cast Transcendence.]
However, where this skill truly shined was when it was used actively.
[The next skill you use will be strengthened.]
It was not a simple enhancement ability, either. A unique additional effect was temporarily added to each skill.
[You have cast Giantization. By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
There was a reason why a Shield Barbarian’s core ability was rank-five Giantization, and it lay in this skill.
[Your Physique will grow in proportion to your Strength stat.]
Transcendence applied a Physique bonus in proportion to the user’s Strength rather than a fixed value.
Will it be about fifteen feet?
This was Giantization (Transcendence) Mode.
Yeah, at this size... I’m roughly the same size as during the battle with Riakis.

I estimated my height based on my new eye level. It was about the same as the time I grew 1.5 times thanks to Missha’s older brother’s skill The Unclean. I had the Vampire’s essence too back then, but I wasn’t satisfied with it because the settings weren’t where I wanted them yet.
“Behelaaah!”

I couldn’t deny I’d become much stronger. Giantization increased Physique and Threat Level in proportion to height, and Wild Outburst caused Threat Level to rise again based on Physique stats. Both were active at the same time, making raw power pulse through my veins.
Leap.
I kicked off the ground as hard as I could and leaped up. My expected landing site was right near the masked assailant aiming an arrow my way.
Bannng!
The moment I touched the ground, the masked assailant and their bow were both sent flying high into the air.
[Your total weight is over 1100 lbs. Special terrain effect Recoil will be applied to your blast radius.]
Fortunately, it looked like the weight limit had been met thanks to my increased height. I had been worried since I wasn’t wearing armor.
“Huh?” Not realizing the situation they were in, the masked assailant released a stunned sound.
What, didn’t think I’d make the first move?
When I swung the mace like a baseball bat, their neck snapped at a bizarre angle.
Crack.
Okay, got one... Hmm?

Just as I was about to turn my head to look for the next target, a man jumped out from the lower right corner of my eye, an excellent angle that would have been my blind spot. However, I easily spotted and avoided him thanks to the base stats of my new essence.
[Bayon]
[Soul Power: +100
Soul Regeneration: +30
Strength: +25
Pain Resistance: +30
Bone Strength: +30
Mana Resistance: +20
Vision: +25]
The Vision stat improved the user’s field of vision, not their eyesight. In the game, it came with a bonus to Evasion according to the detailed stat logs.
Crunch!

Kicking the bastard flying up at me in the abdomen, I prepared for another Leap. But did the knights finally come to their senses? They shouted in alarm when they realized what I was doing, as I was meant to be under their protection.
“C-Come over here!”
Who was protecting who? Pretending not to hear them, I Leaped to my next destination. With the same combo as before, I took our opponents out one by one. None of the enemies were all that strong yet.
Crunch!
I noticed this when I crushed that guy in the smoke earlier, but these goons were strangely low-level.
Is there really no one in Amelia’s league here?

I had planned to use Leap at the slightest hint of danger, but that guardedness soon disappeared. As I faced these guys down, I grew even surer that if it weren’t for that first explosion, they could have been defeated by the knights alone. But what was this?
“...I-I thought we only had to deal with knights!”
As I started to go on a rampage and the knights pushed their opponents back in their battles, the masked assailants’ assaults began to splinter.
“You said that one explosion would kill him!”
“I’m going back. No one said he fought this well!”
Once one or two fled the battlefield, all the other masked assailants chose to flee too. It was ridiculous.
Who are these guys?
They didn’t seem to have any sense of purpose whatsoever.
...Were they really sent from Noark?
I was beginning to doubt that, but for now, I rushed to capture the escaping masked bastards anyway. I managed to catch a total of four. Unfortunately, the rest all got away.
“...Well done, my lord.” Judging by the awkward salute he gave me, I guessed this knight had never had the noble he was escorting carry the team like I just did.
“Ah, you guys did a good job too. Is anyone dead?”

The knight replied that three were dead. Thankfully, Keplow wasn’t one of them. Although he had been caught up in the explosion with me at the very center, I guessed he was durable enough to survive. Since he’d taken a potion in time, he’d regain consciousness soon.
Then let’s go do some interrogating.
The battle was over, and guards were probably on their way, so I grabbed one of the captured men and took off his mask. The face hidden behind it was one I had never seen before.
The man trembled, apparently picking up on the fact that he was screwed. I reached out and shoved my hand in his mouth.
C-Cough, cough!
I searched diligently, but there was no poison inside.

Hmm, I guess reality is different from cartoons. But shouldn’t an assassin carry at least one, just in case of capture? Though, if these bastards had had that much dedication, they wouldn’t have tried to run away.
Just who the hell were these guys? I wiped off the saliva left on my hand from shoving it in his mouth on his clothes and asked, “Who sent you?”
The man didn’t answer. Not that that meant much. A little beating and that mouth would open soon enough.
Flash!
Just as I was thinking that, a white flash of light burst from the dark sky.
Booom!
Something came flying in like a meteorite and hit the ground. At first, I thought it might be a catapult shot by the assassins who escaped.
Choke...!
But it was a man. Surrounded by a spherical, protective shield, his face was all too familiar to me. That was because I had met this bastard before. “Hans Ifreia...?”
Seriously, what’s going on? Why did he fall from the sky?
As I was momentarily taken aback by this unexpected development, another man jumped down from the sky from the direction Hans I fell from.
Dash, dash, dash.

Without paying me any mind, he approached Hans I. Neither I nor any of the knights dared to utter a single word at the strange sight. The air around us changed the moment the man arrived, leaving no room for us to speak.
“Let’s not make this difficult, old man, okay?”
“I told you, you mistook me for—”
“Ha, I told you those lies won’t work on me.”
The man then stretched out his hand and the protective shield around Hans I was torn away with ease.
Rippp.
Hans I’s face turned white as a sheet from that overwhelming act of intimidation. The man grabbed him by the collar. “It’s you, GM. Lift the ban, now. If you don’t, you’re going to die here.”

chapters.title: Chapter 245: Turning Point (5)
paragraphs: Ghost Master, the administrator who controlled the Ghost Busters forum and someone considered a legendary veteran among players.
“It’s you, GM.”
For a moment, I couldn’t breathe.
Hans I is the GM?
I was baffled. If that was true, why had a fish as big as the GM approached me while hiding his identity? Because I was famous these days and he wanted to meet me in person?
No, that can’t be it.

The GM suspected me of being a player, which was why he had approached me during the banquet to feel me out, and even went as far as following me. Yeah, that was a far more plausible hypothesis, even if it wasn’t particularly convenient for me.
Then he must have been the one who cast that wind spell.

Once I established that hypothesis, that particular question naturally got answered. While on my tail, he had watched as the carriage and smoke bomb exploded, blocking his view of me. He would have been curious whether I had lived or not.
I’ll think about this more later.
I redirected my focus to the most important part of all this. The man who fell from the sky and called Hans I the GM was intimidating enough to make even knights tremble. Just who was this man?
“Lift the ban, now. If you don’t, you’re going to die here.”
Huh? Lift the ban?

A chill ran down my spine. There was only one person I knew who would make such a request to the GM: a proud son of Korea, Baekho Lee. Of course, there was a possibility it wasn’t him. I was sure the number of people banned by GM was far more than just one or two. It made sense that one of them would hold a grudge and show up to cause a scene.
“Do you hear me, old man?”
For some reason, I kept seeing Baekho.
...Is it really him?

Thinking that, I took in the guy’s appearance again, committing it to memory. He was around 5′7″, dressed in a neat suit with no equipment, and unless he was wearing a disguise, he was human. His skin was pale without any visible scars and he had platinum-blonde hair in a pomade style. The guy had features anyone would say were good-looking, but perhaps because of the sharp look in his eyes, he exuded a vibe more similar to a bad guy than a charming gentleman.
“Lord Yandel.” As I was studying the guy, a knight came up to me and whispered, “You mustn’t try to run away.”
“...What do you mean?”
“He’s not the kind of person that will work against.” His voice was clearly nervous. Could it be that he knew who this guy was?
“Who is that man?” I hurriedly asked.
“That man—”
The moment the knight was about to answer, the man’s gaze shifted to us. “Oh, right. You guys are here too.”
Huh, how did he hear that whisper from all the way over there?

“Bjorn Yandel.” Seeing as he was calling me by the right name, he seemed to know who I was, but perhaps not all that well. “I heard you beat up that angsty teen bastard? And only in your first year too.” The guy gripped Hans I tightly by the neck and spoke with obvious curiosity as if he’d just accidentally stumbled upon something interesting. “I’m just asking this just in case, but... Are you a player?”
Ha, no wonder I’d felt so anxious about the fact that he knew my name. Gut feelings like that were never wrong. I had only one answer to give him.

“...So you’re an evil spirit.” I didn’t pretend to not know what he was talking about, but drew a line in the sand by calling my opponent an evil spirit. Whether this guy was Baekho or not, it didn’t matter. After all, what could I say with so many people watching?

“Hmm, that’s strange. You’ve made a name for yourself, but not enough for the GM to be interested unless you’re a player...” the guy muttered, then narrowed his eyes. “Hey.” His mouth was smiling, but he spoke in a voice that held no emotion. “Just answer yes or no.”
“Don’t answer... ugh!” The knight trying to give me advice was hit in the stomach by something invisible and sent flying. It was obvious whose handiwork that was.

“Ah, are you worried there are too many people around? Don’t worry. If you’re a player, I’ll kill and get rid of them all. Mm-hmm. I can do you that much of a favor if you sate my curiosity.” The guy grinned and once again demanded I choose. “Yes or no.”

I just barely stopped myself from answering “no.” That was because the question itself was questionable. Asking the same question over and over again with only yes or no as options? It was almost like he had the ability to discern whether I was telling the truth...
An essence like that does exist.
Since I didn’t have any information, it would be wise to be careful here.
“If you don’t want to answer, just say no. You just have to say one word. I’m just curious.”

The more he obsessed over an answer, the more my suspicions grew. And so I had only one viable option. “I’ll ask the questions here.” Instead of just keeping quiet, I changed the subject in a way that implied that I didn’t want to give my enemy the upper hand over me. After all, if I stayed silent, that would just look suspicious to both this guy and the knights. “Evil spirit, are you one of the assassins?”
I tossed out a question that a barbarian who knew nothing about the GM would ask.

Of course, this guy wasn’t going to back down so easily. “I told you to answer with yes or no.” The moment he spoke, the air became heavier. My body tensed like an animal that had just encountered one of its natural predators in the wild.
Is this murderous intent...?
I was reeling. Was it really possible to emit such a high concentration of murderous intent outside of Ghost Busters? I had no idea. Right now, only one thing was for sure.
“Wow, you’re holding up well.” This guy was a tyrant, one who was clearly volatile, yet achieved whatever he wanted to achieve regardless of time or place. “Answer already.”

My mind went blank. Was this how Clown felt at the Round Table? My breathing stopped and my vision went hazy like the blood vessels leading to my brain were being obstructed. A thought suddenly came to me.
...What happens if I say yes?
I couldn’t stop the thought, even knowing it was a vain hope born of a weak mind.
If this guy is really Baekho... can’t I just reveal my identity?
Maybe that would actually help me here. We were both Koreans, after all. If what he showed me in the community was his real personality, he might treat me like a real older brother.
Yeah, just maybe...

Depending on my answer here, there was a scenario where I could be carried by Baekho as I grew stronger so that we could one day escape this world together. But the moment that potential future came to mind, I instantly sobered up.
There were several reasons. To start, I didn’t know if this was actually Baekho or not. Also, the moment I revealed my identity, the hundreds of civilians here would be reduced to corpses.
“...Bjorn!”
“Missha?”

When I turned in the direction of the sound, I saw Missha running toward me in a hurry. Right, this was happening near my house. She probably came as soon as she heard the commotion just in case. However, this wasn’t good.
