“Oh, your girlfriend?” Upon spotting Missha, the man grinned like he’d just caught sight of a useful weakness. The pressure temporarily constricting my body disappeared and I could move freely.
Dash.
I immediately threw my body in front of Missha and blocked her path to protect her from a possible surprise attack.

“The Red Cat Tribe is definitely cute.” The man nodded sagely. Then for some reason, he once again asked his earlier question, but to Missha this time and not me. “Answer with yes or no. Red Cat, are you a player?”
“Hmm? F-Frayer?”
“An evil spirit.”
“N-N-No, I’m not!” Missha answered, startled by the sudden question. The guy nodded.
“That’s the truth.”
“You don’t have to answer to him. Missha, get behind me.” I quickly hid Missha from his field of vision.
The guy laughed at the sight. “Ha, a player wouldn’t take care of an NPC... It’s so strange, though. Why won’t you answer me?”
Cold sweat had been pouring down my back since earlier. If I answered, he’d find out I was lying. If I didn’t, that would look suspicious too.
So I decided to offer up a barbarian-like explanation, completely avoiding the question. “Why should I do what my enemy says?”
“Oh, that’s true.” The guy nodded, apparently accepting my logic. When he spoke again, his tone was amused. “But you, are you really going to be my enemy?”
Ha, look at that glare. Is this what people mean when they say someone is smiling with their mouth but not with their eyes?
“If you don’t answer, I’ll kill that Red Cat.” Before long, he had me in checkmate. I knew it wasn’t an empty threat as soon as I heard it.
God damn it. What should I do?
My gears were turning frantically but I couldn’t come up with a good answer. That was the moment...
“...Mr. Baekho Lee.”
“Huh?”
“See you later.”
Despite the fact that Hans I had been held up by the neck this whole time, only able to move his eyeballs, a light burst out of his body.

“Ha, that son of a...” Baekho cursed and got up. He was in the middle of a vast farm with a refreshing fruity scent. It didn’t take long for him to figure out where he had fallen. There was only one place in the city that could have a farmhouse like this—Rafdonia’s District Six, Gnome Tree. “Ugh, so annoying. Now that bastard will never come out of the Magic Tower...”

Baekho readily admitted to himself that he had lost the guy. Even if he ran straight there right now, there would be nothing left for him to find. He’d misjudged the situation. He had been wary of the wizard escaping using Teleport, which was why he’d gripped him by the neck so that he couldn’t cast a spell. But a wordless Teleport, and on him at that?
“So, you’re not a nobody either, huh?”

He regretted underestimating his opponent, but he quickly brushed it off. It had already happened. Dwelling on the past didn’t suit him. Plus, it wasn’t like it had been a total loss. He’d confirmed that that bastard was in fact the GM.
All I have is time, so I just have to run around a bit more.
Baekho scratched his head and soon turned his attention elsewhere.
“I didn’t get an answer in the end.”
Bjorn Yandel, the barbarian he’d met by chance while chasing the GM...
“...Well, whatever.”

Baekho decided to stop worrying about whether that barbarian was a player or not. Not only was he likely not a player, but Baekho’s interest in the barbarian had already completely cooled. Even if he was a player, he wasn’t particularly interested anymore. Bastards who were satisfied living in this world and sucking up to NPCs were of no use to his plans.
Slump.
Baekho flopped back on the ground carelessly. Using the skill of Spatial Interference, he picked the grapes hanging from a nearby tree and floated them into his mouth.
“Natural grapes are the best.”
Good air, delicious food, and the GM wouldn’t be coming out of the Magic Tower for a while now...
I’m too lazy to go all the way to Bifron.
It might not be bad to stay here for a while.

Two days had passed since that incident. The title conferment ceremony, the assassins, the GM, and even Baekho Lee... A lot had happened in just one day, and the past two days had been spent sorting it all out. First of all, the assassins.
“We will take them in for interrogation.”

The captured assassins were escorted to Mozlan. According to the report I got from the knight today, they had been hired by an anonymous client. Apparently, the bomb that killed three knights had also been supplied by that mystery person.
“Their orders appear to have been to kill you and steal the essence you were given.”

Many things about this explanation were suspicious. The essence? Fine. The box containing the test tube was more than sturdy enough to survive an explosion. It was also more than possible to kill me and take me by surprise.
“But what was their plan if I absorbed it before then?”
“We didn’t understand that part, either.”

That, not to mention the large bounty the contractor had placed on my head, meant that the essence was just an excuse. Otherwise, there was no reason to put a price on my head, which was why Mozlan surmised that the contractor was from Noark—at least until yesterday.
“...So it’s likely one of the large clans?”

Mozlan concluded that the culprit behind this incident was one of the large clans. Apparently, Noark would have sent more reliable fighters. This sort of shoddy execution wasn’t like them. More importantly, the large clans had more than enough motive.
“That’s right. After harming you, they probably planned to lay the blame on the palace. In fact, several such traps were uncovered in various taverns that same night.”
It was a reasonable explanation, but I had questions. Why did Clown say all that during the meeting, then? Was it because he’d heard about this plot in advance?
Well, he did only say there would be an assassin. He didn’t say they would be from Noark...
He might’ve judged that since they hadn’t sent the assassins anyway, there was no harm in giving us a heads-up.
...Or it could be that there are really none coming after me.
A sense of resentment washed over me. Ha... why did I have to live in fear even in the city? Anyway, enough about the assassin.
To get straight to the point, the GM was not Hans I.
“The Hans Ifreia you met that day had to have been someone in disguise.”

When they stormed his house, the real Hans Ifreia was unconscious. Just in case, they investigated for traces of mana as well, but the real Hans had not an iota of magical talent. Simply put, someone had borrowed his identity.
That was the disappointing part. I had hoped this investigation might help reveal the GM’s identity.
Still, it wasn’t a total loss.
There were a few consolations. First, I learned that the GM suspected me of being a player. That meant I at least had some time to prepare.
Since he saw that I didn’t answer, he’ll be even more suspicious of me now. He’ll probably make a move the next time the community opens.
Fortunately, I had a guess as to what would happen, so I came up with a way to deal with it. Anyway, on to the next positive.
Baekho Lee.
To start, that guy had been Baekho for sure. The GM had even called him that at the end.
“...Mr. Baekho Lee. See you later.”
This had been said through magic, not his voice, as his windpipe had been in the process of being crushed at the time. Well, not that the information meant much.
“He... I’m sorry. I am not authorized to tell you.”

When I asked the knight from back then who Baekho was, that was the answer I got in return. I guessed this was why life was all about timing. If Baekho hadn’t cut the knight off back then, I was sure he would’ve told me.
He sure is a dangerous one...

Even if I got to see Baekho again someday, it’d be difficult to be as friendly as we used to be, not after learning he had two completely different personalities. I had thought the sincerity he had shown me in the forum was his true self, but the disparity was far too stark.
He was a real thug...
Anyway, I moved on from Baekho to Missha. In truth, this was the most troublesome and suffocating part of this whole situation.
“Bjorn, don’t take this the wrrrong way and just hear me out, okay? Y-You’re not going to disappear out of nowhere, r-right...?”
Missha started anxiously watching my every move.

chapters.title: Chapter 246: Turning Point (6)
paragraphs: Just what kind of mistake had I made that Missha was acting like this? Thoughts like that didn’t even occur to me. That was because Missha had been by my side the longest. A barbarian who read books, a barbarian who knew how to take on the role of a scout, a barbarian who pretended to be ignorant but was actually clever, a barbarian who always knew something others didn’t like it was all just obvious to him—there must have been plenty of suspicious things about me. Until now she would have overlooked them, saying that was just the kind of person I was, but the events of that day would have made her fully realize. After all, she knew me best.
“Why should I do what my enemy says?”
I may have avoided answering with barbarian-like reasoning, but that probably would have seemed strange to Missha too. If nothing else, she knew I always had a reason for being stubborn.
“If you don’t answer, I’ll kill that Red Cat.”
When I heard Baekho say that, I felt a deep sense of despair. Perhaps Missha had sensed, too, that I had been driven into a corner and was desperately holding back an answer.

“...Disappear? What do you mean?” In the middle of the night while everyone else was asleep, Missha came up to me cautiously and voiced her anxiety, and I pretended to have no clue what she was talking about. “Why would I suddenly disappear?”
“W-Well, that’s... I had a nightmarrre. Yeah.” Missha made up an excuse about a dream. It seemed she believed revealing her hidden fears might make them come true.
“Dream? If you’re that scared, you can sleep beside me!”

“I-I’m not that scared! Hmph, fine! If you’rrre just going to make jokes, go to sleep, you boneheaded barrrbarian!” Missha left in a fit of frustration and I let out a sigh in the now-quiet room. My chest felt tight.
Disappear suddenly...

I knew why she had asked that because I snuck into her room yesterday and saw the book on her desk. It was a book I had read at the library before—one that listed some behaviors and habits of evil spirits.
Evil spirits are clever and good at acting. Also, they do not get attached to people. In the event of a crisis in which their identity may be exposed, they choose to sever all ties and hide.

It was a description I could relate to a decent amount. I was destined to die if my identity were exposed, after all. At first, I would try to distance myself from the people around me as much as I could, and if that didn’t work, eventually change my identity. If even that option didn’t work...
I’d probably go to Noark.
In fact, Noark was a city made up of people like that. Criminals who couldn’t remain in Rafdonia any longer and evil spirits alike hid in the sewers, and Noark took them in.
Even Clown is famous for joining Orcules as soon as he was exposed as an evil spirit.
I lay on the bed and stared blankly at the ceiling. My head was all jumbled up.
If they find out that I’m an evil spirit...

How would the team react? Would they feel betrayed and angered by my deception? Well, I wasn’t sure. Missha, at least, seemed more anxious about the idea that I might disappear from her side if I was an evil spirit than the idea of me being an evil spirit in the first place.
Damn you, Baekho.

I admitted it to myself. I was afraid of my true identity being revealed to them. More than the guillotine I might be dragged to, I was afraid of everything I built crumbling down, even if what I built may have just been a sandcastle.
Voom.
I pulled out a magical device from sub-space that allowed the user to have secret conversations with others.
“Fine, if that’s what you want, I’ll expose you myself. Hans Chrisen is an evil spirit! I have proof of that in my backpack—”
For reference, it came with a recording function. The dwarf I met in Doppelganger Forest had used this to drive Hans G into a corner.
Click.
When I pressed the groove at the bottom of the device, the conversation the two had had back then began to replay in rich detail.
“What is there to think about? They’re NPCs anyway.”
“But they are comrades who have been with—”
“What a joke. You think those guys will think like that once they find out your identity?”
Hans G couldn’t say anything in response to that, because he knew the truth.
“The person your comrades thought of as a friend was the real Hans. And as you know, the real Hans is no longer in this world.”
We were evil spirits. No matter what kinds of relationships we built here, they could only be precarious ones built on lies.
“But... I consider them to be my real comrades.”
Hans G had replied like that that day, but how had he actually acted when the chips were down?
“I-I’m sorry.”

When the dwarf ended up in hot water and forcibly exposed his identity, Hans G flung flames at his party’s warrior and took the dwarf’s side. The truth was, he knew that they could no longer go back to their old relationship. The comrades who were once precious to him now considered him the enemy.
Click.
I pressed the button again to turn the sound off. Suddenly, Takelan’s words came to mind.
“There will come a day when you feel the same way as I do.”
He was wrong. If such a moment of despair were to come to me, it would have a much more terrible and miserable ending.

Another two days passed. In the meantime, nothing significant happened. There were no more clues about the large clan that was suspected to be behind the assassination attempt, and the events of that day were obscured and buried in oblivion. There was nothing else to dig into. Thanks to that, though, the number of knights guarding me increased. Once it had been proven that there was a faction with malicious intent toward the palace targeting me, the idea that I needed more protection gained more momentum. A little too much momentum.
Ha, thanks to this, I can’t go anywhere.

There were already three bodyguards on me. Of course, that was just inside the house—there were more than thirty knights standing guard outside. If I went out, all those people followed me. They even got someone to taste my food.
“I’ll try it first, in case it’s poisoned.” At each meal, a knight with increased poison tolerance tasted a bite first.
“Th-there’s no need! W-Why would I harm Bjorrrn...?”
“It’s best to be certain. Mmm, that’s delicious. You are a great cook, Lady Karlstein.”
“Th-that’s no comfort at all!” That did nothing to improve Missha’s mood since the tester said that every meal, but still, their inflexibility did make them seem more reliable.
Even if Noark does send an assassin, I won’t have to worry about this, at least.
Once breakfast was over, Ainar headed to the holy land, and Erwen left to meet her younger sister. I had similar plans.
“...You’re going out?”
“I should start getting work done.” Now that I’d rested enough, it was time to start working hard again and do the things I’d been putting off.
“Are you going shopping again?”
“No, this is another business.”
“Hmm?”
Normally I spent our time off going shopping, but today’s mission was different.
Although I made a lot of money this time, my purchasing power will go up even if I do nothing. There’s no need to shop now.

To start, the cost of equipment had already started to plummet as a result of a large chunk of adventurers dying, leading to a decrease in demand. Meanwhile, food prices had risen. Concerns that the supply of mana stones might decrease next month had led to hoarding.
I should try to avoid using cash as much as possible.

The currency here was not a simple piece of paper whose worth was determined by social consensus. It had real value. This world ran on mana stones that could be turned into iron or wheat by the hands of alchemists. Unlike the value of labor, the currency here never depreciated.
I wonder if Hikurod will be okay...?

Suddenly, the dwarf came to mind. It seemed business in his forge was going well these days, but I was sure that at a time like this, it was a ghost town. I felt bad for him. He’d used all his money to open that shop, only for something like this to happen.
I should go see him later when I have time.
I dressed and headed out with Missha. Outside stood a carriage prepared by the knights. I found it completely unnecessary.
“Please get in.”
By now, though, I was used to this treatment and got on the wagon. It wasn’t like it cost money anyway, and they said it was much easier to guard me like this, so what could I do?
“Where shall I take you?”
“To the Great Temple of Reatlas.” As soon as I told the driver my destination, the carriage started off.

“...Reatlas? Why are you going therrre all of a sudden?” Missha gave me a somewhat uneasy look. I could understand her sentiment. The religious factions here were pretty much natural enemies of evil spirits.
Welp, looks like her suspicions haven’t completely disappeared yet.

Missha had spent a day or two reading books about evil spirits and saying peculiar things to me, but that had all stopped just a little while later. At first, I thought I had just been overthinking things and that she had concluded I couldn’t really be an evil spirit.
At times like these, it’s probably best to not press and leave her alone.
And so I continued the conversation casually. “I’m thinking of asking them whether there are any priests available.”
“...Available prrriests? A-Are you thinking about l-leaving the team?”
“What are you talking about?”
“But even if there is a prrriest available, there’s already five of us—ah! Are you thinking of kicking one of us out...?”
Honestly, what was she saying? I sighed and cut her off. “I am not going to leave the team, nor is anyone else leaving the team.”
“Hm? So why a prrriest...?” Missha trailed off, apparently still confused.
I told her my future plans. “Because now we have to prepare to go up to the sixth floor.”
“Eh, the sixth floor? Oh, I see. But what does that have to do with this?”
“I’m going to make a clan.”

The time had come for our five-person party to graduate. Even if it may have been small, any party with more than five people was classified as a clan. That was because it would have to be divided into two or more teams when traveling into the labyrinth.
“Clan? So from now on, we’ll be working with ten people?”
Well, it looked like it would be that way eventually, but not right now.
Since Erwen can serve as a scout, we just need a single priest for now.
From the sixth floor onward, we also needed another adventurer to fill a special position. That made a total of eight for now.
At our level, we’ll have no problems getting to the fifth floor even if we split into two groups of four.

Well, I wasn’t actually worried about that part. If that didn’t work out, meeting up on the second floor and then traveling together was a viable strategy. Of course, depending on our starting location, it would take time to find each other, and we’d also be slowed down on the fourth floor thanks to the maximum member penalty.
But it’s not like we’re a large clan.
Unless our purpose was to control hunting grounds, a difference of a day or two was not significant to a small clan. Rather, the problem lay elsewhere.
When will the labyrinth return to normal?
If there was no hint of it returning to normal any time soon, I planned to wait a few more months. It would take that much time for me to finish preparing to go to the sixth floor anyway.

“We have arrived.” As I was getting my thoughts in order, the carriage stopped in front of the Great Temple. Most of the knights waited by the carriage. I headed inside with just three personal guards and Missha.

“Captain Krovitz is out on business.” Another paladin greeted me instead of Paal Krovitz, whom I was acquainted with. His name was Sven Parav, and he was the deputy commander of the Second Order of the Paladins of Reatlas. “It is an honor to meet you, Baronet Yandel. On what business did you visit our church today?”
I gave him a brief summary of my plans for the future, that I planned to make a clan and if possible, I wanted to take a priest with me. To be blunt, I was rejected outright.
“Hmm, even for a baronet, that will be difficult.”
My recently acquired reputation as the Giant and my noble status of baronet had no pull in the church. Those were the bare minimum. To recruit a priest, certain achievements were required.
Whew, why are they just as inflexible as in the game?
Since I had known this was likely, I asked about the ways to increase my achievements and got a detailed answer.
Except for a few things, everything is like in the game.
In the end, the answer lay in labor. Welp, should have done that in advance.
“Parav, right? Thanks for today. I’ll come back soon.”
“Yes, we are always waiting for a visit from a hero.”

After wrapping up my business here, I said goodbye to Parav and turned around. The moment I was about to exit the chamber, the last vine protecting me from an ill-fated encounter with the Dragon Slayer snapped.
[The activation conditions for Blessing of the Stars have been met.]
God damn it.
The problems just kept coming.

chapters.title: Chapter 247: Gnome Tree (1)
paragraphs: An alchemist was a person who could transmute mana stones into materials. Not many people held this job even in Rafdonia, so they were considered the city’s most important resources. As for Noark, which was in much rougher shape, it went without saying how they treated their alchemists.
“Good morning, Miss Marlene!”
“Are you on an errand for the alchemist? That looks heavy. I’ll carry it for you.”

It was for this reason that everyone in the city was kind to Marlene. She was the alchemist’s one and only apprentice. When the day came that she inherited all his knowledge, she would be in charge of this city from then on.
Grandpa isn’t the same as usual these days...

To be honest, it would be a lie to say this role wasn’t burdensome, but there was really no one else to take over for her, so her only choice was to shoulder the responsibility and push forward. It wasn’t just a role she had taken out of duty, either.
“Grandpa!”
“I told you to call me Master.”
“Alright, Master! So what about the stuff? Is it here?”
“It is. There’s quite a lot, so you can look through it and take what you need.”
The alchemist tossed her a two-way sub-space and Marlene took it to confirm the contents that were inside. It contained the things she had ordered.
“Please say thanks for me!”
“Will do.”

Marlene whistled and moved the items into her personal bag. This was an unmistakable privilege. Without the title of alchemist’s apprentice backing her, it would have been impossible for her to use this two-way sub-space, which was supposed to be used strategically, for personal gain. Not to mention that the infiltrators outside the city wouldn’t have listened to her request in the first place.
“Wow, Grandpa! Try some of this. They make some good cookies!”
“I told you to call me Master. Oh, these cookies are delicious, though.”
“But what’s that? It looks like an elixir on the outside, but I’m sure it can’t be one...”
“Haha, well spotted.”

“Huhhh? I-Is it really an elixir?” Marlene, who was munching on the cookies without much thought, jumped to her feet, and rightfully so. With the ingredients being so expensive and the production process so difficult, even her master had only made five bottles of elixir in his lifetime.
He already used two bottles too...
Now there were only three elixirs left in Noark, and one of those bottles was currently in her master’s hands. For what reason?

When Marlene’s eyes lit up with curiosity, her master smiled and explained the situation. “You’ll need to know this in the future, so I’ll tell you. Today, I’m going to feed this elixir to the Dragon Slayer Regal Vagos and attempt to restore his memory depending on how well he recovers.”
“To Regal Vagos...?” Marlene frowned subconsciously.
“Why, you don’t like him?”
“...He just looks scary.”
“Don’t judge people by their appearance. It’s because of an injury. I heard he was quite handsome before the burn. Well, I have another reason not to like him, though.”
“R-Right? It’s not just me, is it?”
“Haha, you always pick and choose what you want to hear.”
“That’s because it’s not just his looks for me, either. That man is so mean. The way he speaks with no manners to you as well...”
“What a kid.”

A moment of embarrassed silence ensued, after which Marlene heard the details from her master. The reason why the precious elixir was being delivered to that dragon man was very simple, at least on the surface.
“The Corpse Collector’s power was greatly reduced recently, so apparently our forces need to be supplemented.”
“Is that man that strong? I heard he was weakened by a curse.”
“Still, his Dragon Speech is special. Not that he can use it however he wants... But they expect him to be able to use it once or twice after taking this elixir.”

The head of Orcules had made the request directly to the lord of the castle and he had granted it. It was a one-sided request, but he hadn’t had a choice, because he was partly responsible for what had happened to the dragon man. Although they had tried to treat him, for some reason, Vagos’s health had deteriorated further.
“Tsk, it’s a mystery, though. I’m certain nothing I did could have caused that.”
“The way I see it, it’s all an act! To frame us somehow and scare us!”

“...I don’t think it’s an act, but I know what you’re trying to say. The lord of the castle can’t be swayed by them forever.” Orcules was like a poisoned chalice, especially in that they were impossible to put down even knowing they were detrimental. “Now then, the preparations are complete, so let’s go.”
Afterward, Marlene followed her master to the dragon man’s room.
“Gruhhh...” Lying on the bed, he was unable to even speak properly. His limbs were locked and the only parts of his body he could move were his eyes.
“Since you have no problem hearing, I will just speak. This will be good news for you. The lord of the castle has bestowed an elixir on you.”
“Guhhh...”
“Then let’s start right away.”

The process of treating him wasn’t all that complicated, and rightfully so, because the elixir wasn’t just any regular item. The only requirement was to make sure to feed the elixir carefully so as not to spill it. After about ten minutes had passed, the dragon man was able to lift up his torso and speak.
“God damn it, what the hell did you guys do to me before?” That was the first thing he said. “What the hell kind of treatment put me in that condition!?”
Marlene wanted to say something back, but she remembered her master’s words earlier and held her tongue.
“Haha, that’s why we brought you the elixir. I hope you’ll be kind enough to understand.”
“Ha... if you weren’t the alchemist...”
“Now, seeing as you are looking better, let’s move on to the next thing.”
“Next?”
“What you were going to say back then. You collapsed so suddenly that you couldn’t finish your sentence. You should be able to recover your lost memories now.”
“That won’t cause any complications, right...?”
“The procedure may fail, but it won’t harm your body or anything like that.”
“...I’ll trust you.” The dragon man nodded condescendingly like he was the superior here. Marlene was displeased with that, but she couldn’t say anything while her master was keeping quiet.
“Eat. This is a secret medicine called Lethe’s Curse. Oh, and it may hurt a little, but in your current state, you should be able to endure it, so don’t worry.”
The dragon man accepted the medicine with obvious suspicion but swallowed it in one gulp. “...It’s bitter.”
“The pain will come soon, so lie down.”
The dragon man obediently followed the alchemist’s instructions and lay on the bed again. A long while later, Vagos, who was suffering and sweating profusely, opened his eyes again.
“So? Are your memories back?”
“...I don’t know. I think they are.”
“It may take a while.”
“It is a very strange feeling. I can vividly remember things that happened when I was young.”
“It’s that kind of drug.”
“Before we get into that, do you have anything sweet? I want something to chew on...”
At the dragon man’s request, the alchemist looked at Marlene. The look told her that she should give him something if she had it.
“...I’ll bring something.” Marlene hurried back to her room and fetched the cookies she had left behind earlier. However, when she returned, her master wasn’t in the room.
“Your master was summoned by the lord. So, the snack?”
“Here...” Marlene handed over the few remaining cookies. She didn’t want to, but what could she do?
Those are from Miss Amelia...

The dragon man was greedy and didn’t stop with one cookie. He chewed on several at once. A while later, he suddenly gripped his forehead as if the forgotten memories of that day had suddenly slammed into his mind. “Ugh... my head! Y-Yes...! It was that bastard...!”
Soon, the dragon man let out a sharp, pleased exclamation as he stared out into space, but his moment of joy did not last long.
C-Cough!
He began to cough loudly, his expression growing distressed. It was obviously not due to something stuck in his throat. Before she knew it, the dragon man’s skin grew bizarrely swollen.
Grandpa never mentioned this side effect!
Unaware of this possibility, Marlene’s mind went totally blank.

“You!” Suddenly, the man stretched out his hand toward Marlene with obvious hostility. Marlene, who had spent her whole life learning alchemy, had no hope of reacting in time. “Krr!” However, his hand never touched her body. The man tried to jump upright but lost his balance and fell off the bed.
Choke!
Saliva continued to drip from his open maw. If her eyes weren’t playing tricks on her, there also appeared to be flecks of blood. How had this happened?
“You... what did you put... in the cookie...?”
“W-What? It’s just an ordinary cookie...” Marlene replied, rattled.

The man completely collapsed to the floor. “...You d-damned bitch.” Even in the middle of what seemed to be a poisoning of some kind, the dragon man strained to look up. Of course, this also didn’t last long.
Plop.
Vagos dropped his head weakly. “D-Dragon blood... reacts with cinnamon...”
This was all thanks to a cinnamon allergy.
[The activation conditions for Blessing of the Stars have been met.]

The third vine was gone. I didn’t know why. If I had to guess, the guy must have been tirelessly plotting another evil plan before getting punished by god for it, because this was a holy relic imbued with divine power. Anyway, the reason wasn’t important.
God damn it.
Now, the Dragon Slayer could come after me at any time. That meant that I had to be even more on guard in the future.
The second vine only broke off last month.
How could this happen? A sigh slipped from my lips automatically, and rightfully so because I couldn’t say I was fully prepared yet.
I think I can mess him up on his own...
The problem was that there was no guarantee that he would come take revenge alone. What if he came with Clown? And if not him, what if he was accompanied by numerous subordinates?
Looks like the barrier will break open soon too.

The palace had even found a way to demolish Noark’s barrier. If it became possible to travel between the underground city and its aboveground counterpart, it would be possible to encounter the Dragon Slayer in Rafdonia too. Of course, even that wasn’t something to worry about right now.
Why here...?
I let out a silent sigh and glanced around.
“Bjorn, is that...?!” Knowing what the vine ring meant, Missha was horrified. The knight, on the other hand, just seemed to be wondering what kind of weird thing was going on now.

But the paladin was different. “...It’s a holy relic from our temple. And one I’ve never seen before.” Sven Parav, the deputy commander of the Second Order of the Paladins of Reatlas, narrowed his eyes. Like the religious man he was, he had recognized this was a holy relic. “Could it be that the prophecy that was given back then—”
“Stop.”
“Ah... sorry.” When I cut him off, the paladin realized his mistake and shut his mouth, but it was already too late. “Then the subject of that prophecy was...”
“Confidentiality is essential to escort operations, so you don’t need to worry.”
Don’t worry, my ass. They may say this is all classified but they’ll go rat me out to their superiors anyway. Ha, so annoying.

Three knights and one deputy commander. Although only four people knew my secret, the fact was that that number would gradually increase in the future. How long would it take for it to reach the chieftain’s ears?
...He won’t actually kick me out of the tribe, right?

Well, I didn’t know about that, but it was clear that there would be trouble. The chieftain had even seemed displeased about my new title. Convincing him that it was for the sake of the tribe had been a whole other ordeal.
It’s going to take me a long time to get to stage nine of the Imprint...
It was suffocating, especially in that there was nothing I could do right now. Even if I asked them to keep it a secret, they’d only say yes to my face.
“Then I’ll be on my way.” So, I just left the temple without saying anything. What could I do when the cat was already out of the bag?
I have no choice but to take over the tribe as soon as possible.
This could all be resolved if I became the chieftain and changed the traditions of the tribe. And in that sense... I had work to do.
“Missha, you can go home now.”
“Hmm?”
“I’m going to stop by the holy land for a while.”

They said to strike while the iron was hot. I immediately parted ways with Missha and headed to the holy land. The knights joined me only up to the entrance and did not come inside. That was because barbarians still subscribed to the tradition of forbidding entry to other races.
“Then we will wait here.”
“I’ll be out by evening, so take a break somewhere nearby.”
“Yes, my lord.”

When I entered through the open castle gates, a forest landscape that you’d be hard-pressed to find in the city appeared. I wasn’t sure if this was a remnant of the warrior whose body I was in, but for some reason, this place smelled more like home than Hansu Lee’s room.
The air here is definitely nice.
Walking along the overgrown, weedy road instead of the paved ones of the city, I soon arrived at the residential section of the holy land. There were huts built without any criteria whatsoever.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel is an invincible warrior blessed by the ancestral gods!”
“God and invincible!”
“Now, I’ll tell you the story of Bjorn slaying the world’s most wicked Corpse Collector, so take heed!”
“H-Heed? What does that mean!?”
“It means open your ear holes and listen!”
In a nearby clearing, young warriors could be seen receiving early training. The instructor was... Ainar.

Ainar was different at home and outside. Her shoulders, which never opened up in front of Missha, were wide, and her expression was overflowing with confidence. She was carrying four backpacks. That was because the number of backpacks one carried was a symbol of success to the barbarians. She must have just wanted to show off in front of her juniors. I guessed she really liked her position here because her daily routine consisted of coming to the holy land every morning.
...Let’s pass by quickly.

I debated heading over to say hi to Ainar, but I stopped myself because I had a feeling the interaction would drain me of my energy. I came to the holy land today for another reason. I needed to conserve my strength.
Whip.
When I arrived at the chieftain’s house, I threw open the tent flap and entered. That was one of the benefits of being a barbarian. You didn’t have to knock.
“Oh, are you all better?”
“Yes.”

“What business did you come here for?” Like a man who served as the pinnacle of the barbarian race, the chieftain got straight to the point. I liked that things here were always straightforward. That meant I had nothing to worry about.
“I have something to say.”
“Speak.”
In barbarian society, honesty was considered a virtue, so I said what I wanted to say. “I have come to succeed you as the chieftain.”
“Succeed...” The chieftain picked up an ax resting against the corner of the tent and said, “Don’t use complicated words. Fight me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 248: Gnome Tree (2)
paragraphs: Back then, the chieftain told me, “If you want my position, become stronger, warrior, and prove you are worthy. I will watch over you.”
If I proved I was worthy, he would hand over the position to me. So how should I prove it? I hadn’t bothered to ask, because based on the barbarians I knew, there was only one answer.
“Wait, let’s move somewhere else!”
“...You really are a wise warrior.”
The fight, which almost broke out indoors, was moved to an open field thanks to my insight.
“Behel—aaah!”
“Behel—aaah!”
The battle began with us each charging at each other with a shout.
Bang!
The chieftain swung the ax that had once mercilessly decapitated Oreum, son of Kadua, and I used my hard-earned skills to fight back. But in terms of outcome...
“I won.”

After about an hour of fighting, I was defeated. One of the key factors behind my defeat was a lack of variety. The chief and I were the same type. If our tactics had been completely different the fight would have been more up in the air, but since he overwhelmed me on strength alone, there were no surprises.
As expected, I’m not ready yet.

I accepted defeat gracefully. Of course, the outcome could have been different had it not been a sparring match. You couldn’t spray Acid Fluid in your opponent’s eyes or speak nonsense to confuse them before surprise-attacking them when sparring. The fact was, when I was pinned to the ground and my hands and feet were bound, I didn’t bite off his neck with my teeth. Put simply, this was a fight where our ultimate finishers were sealed. But how did the test go?
“You are still lacking,” the chieftain said to me. “If you want my position, become stronger.”
Jeez, I thought the cutoff would be the sixth floor. Wasn’t I there yet? I had been sure he wouldn’t do something like refuse to give me the position of chieftain until I defeated him...
“To the extent that you’ll be able to defeat even an old man like me.”
Oh, maybe it was like that.
To win against an eighth-floor adventurer... that will take a bit more time.

I let go of my impatience. This was also one of the strengths of the barbarian race. Even if I failed to succeed, there was nothing to lose. Rather, there was a lot to gain. Although my body had been pummeled to the point that I had to chug a few bottles of potion as soon as the match was over, I had still made a lot of progress. This was different from last time, when I got knocked out by a single punch. The battle had lasted nearly an hour.
The number of essences I know for sure he has is six.
I had confirmed several of the chieftain’s essences. Not only that, but I had also learned his fighting style to some extent. Next time, I would be able to take him on much more easily.
Barbarians are definitely good fighters.
I’d have to fight him some more to accumulate more experience, but through this battle I was naturally able to learn the tendencies of the chieftain, who was once a warrior on the eighth floor.
“He fought against the chieftain for an hour!”
“Look! That stingy chieftain is drinking a potion!”
“He may look fine on the outside, but his insides must not be. As expected, Bjorn, son of Yandel, is a great warrior!”
Furthermore, when the sparring match was over, my fellow barbarians filling the field didn’t seem particularly disappointed about my defeat either. Well, I was only in my first year still.
“I thought it would take at least five more years.”
“Hmm, perhaps the tribe will change hands much sooner than expected.”
Even the elders nodded in satisfaction. And so I may have lost, but I’d gained a lot. The chieftain, on the other hand, had gained nothing.
Yeah, so I think it can be said that I won.

As I was winning the mental battle, my motivation returned. Soon, I stood up and stared at the chieftain. He seemed curious about what I wanted to say considering I had been silent this whole time. “Are you feeling hopeless?”
“Of course not.” I chuckled and said, “Again.”
After all, it was rare to get the chance to face an opponent with no stakes to worry about.

I fought the chieftain a total of three times and each ended in my defeat. However, as the number of fights went up, the length of our spars got longer. This was thanks to Hansu Lee’s strength, not Bjorn’s. I was good at self-evaluation. That was because I had experienced many failures in my life, and each time, what I desperately sought was the reason behind each failure. Finding that reason was my specialty.
He definitely knows a lot of little techniques thanks to all his experience.

The differences between the chieftain and I lie not just in our stats, but in our skill as warriors, in our ability to make snap judgments, and in our instinct for picking up on the barest hints of an opponent’s weakness even in a battle where thinking before you acted slowed down your reaction time. These were all things I had to learn. It wasn’t enough to be satisfied with the role of a meat shield even though I’d now consumed the essence of an Ogre.
I needed to be able to fight better. This was also the best way to protect my comrades.
If my allies are in danger, I just have to get rid of the enemies so they no longer are.
That was my fate, my new fate as a tank that I had to work toward from now on.
“...You look like you’ve realized something.”
“Ah, yeah, thanks. I learned a lot.”
“Haha, that’s what the chief of the tribe is for!”
What was this man talking about? He didn’t seem like it, but he was really weak to compliments. “Can I come back soon?”
“Anytime.”
It was slowly approaching sunset. After my spar with the tribal chief finally came to an end, the barbarians who had been enjoying the entertainment all scattered to do their things.
“Bjorn! Are you going home?!”
“Not right away. I plan to look around for a while.”
“Really? Can I come with you?”
No reason you can’t.
After the spar, I walked with Ainar. We didn’t have a particular destination in mind. We just walked in the opposite direction of the city’s walls.
“It’s been a while since I last came here.”

After leaving the campsite, we were greeted by a thick, wild forest—the same forest where the souls of countless warriors, including the elder who performed the Soul Succession ritual for Ainar, would be roaming. But I kept walking.
“There’s nothing but the barrier in that direction. Why are you going there?”
“I’m just curious about that barrier all of a sudden.”
After increasing my speed and walking for about an hour, I soon reached my destination.
Tap.
An invisible wall appeared before me, signaling that this was as far as I was permitted to go. The forest continued beyond it, sprawling into the distance.
When I knocked on the wall with the back of my hand, Ainar jumped and stopped me. “Eh! Bjorn! W-What are you doing?! If the protective barrier gets broken, it’ll be a disaster!”
True, this is a world where everyone would die without a barrier protecting them. Or that’s what they say, at least.
This was a question that had popped into my head after I visited Bifron: was the outside world really in the state the palace said it was?
“Hehehe, warrior, it’s been a while.” When I turned around at the presence behind me, I saw an elderly barbarian with a bandage over his eyes.
“Shaman!”
“Yes, it’s been a while for you too, Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin.”
It was fascinating to me every time. How could he make his way around so well without eyes?
“What are you doing here? Few warriors come this deep into the forest.”
“I just came because I was bored. And you? What are you doing here?”

“Hehe, what else would a shaman be doing in the forest?” The shaman showed me his hands, which were smeared with white powder. Upon closer inspection, it was powdered bone—and it was human, not animal.

“You were carrying out a funeral.” When the dead bodies left in the forest finally turned into bones, the shaman crushed the bones into dust and scattered them throughout the vast forest as the last step in the funeral process.
“W-Was it Kiduba, third son of Tohar’s turn today?”
“He has a long way to go before being returned to the forest.” Put simply, that meant that the elder who had acted as Ainar’s mentor had a long while to go before he ended up a skeleton.
“...I see.”
“I’m going back to the village now. Why don’t you both come with me?” the shaman asked us.
I replied that I would go back later.
“Really? If that’s what you want.” The shaman turned around without hesitation. “Everything has an order, warrior. It is not yet time to wonder what lies beyond it.”
With those cryptic words, he left.
“Haha, come to think of it, it’s been a while since we’ve been alone together.”
“Has it?”
“Why don’t we have a bout for the first time in a while? You don’t hang out with me these days because you’re recovering.”
Oh, she meant sparring. It looked like my match with the chieftain earlier had aroused this kid’s fighting spirit too... these barbarians.
“Not today. Let’s do it tomorrow.”
“All right. You probably know this already, but I’m pretty patient.”
Uh-huh, sure.
I nodded absently and spent some more time studying the protective barrier. Maybe it was just because of the shaman’s parting words, but something felt strange. But I couldn’t figure out what it was.
Ha... if I were a wizard instead of a barbarian, would I have been able to learn something here?

In the end, I turned back having gained nothing. There was quite a distance between the protective barrier and the castle wall, but the journey back wasn’t boring. After all, Ainar was a chatterbox. She especially liked barbarian talk—talk about equipment, who fought with whom and won, and which place had the clunkiest and coolest backpacks these days.
“Oh, did you hear? Kharon is going to be a father soon.”
“What?” I was genuinely surprised. “How? He never mentioned that in the labyrinth?”
“Haha, it seems that once he reached the third floor, he started meeting women. Oh, and I only heard about the pregnancy from the woman a few days ago, so he probably didn’t have time to tell you.”

Afterward, Ainar explained the situation in detail. The woman was one of the warriors of the tribe, which made sense. Humans couldn’t give birth to barbarians. It wasn’t impossible for different races to conceive together, but in the end, a human child was born. Barbarians preferred their own people anyway. Their standards for what made someone attractive were different from other races’.
More importantly, this way there are no ideological issues with the pregnancy.

In human society, getting married and then having children was the right way to go about it, but that tradition didn’t exist in barbarian society. The child was raised by the holy land, and the woman considered giving birth to a child a matter of great pride. Not only that, there were also practical benefits to giving birth. It was small compared to the package humans got, but the palace gave the parents two years of tax relief.
And the pregnancy itself is short.

Each person was different, but it took an average of four months for a barbarian to give birth, and the recovery time was also very short. Perhaps that was the reason why barbarian women were so tolerant of childbirth. It was kind of hard to say this, but childbirth wasn’t just a noble process. Pride or not, if the economic factors weren’t dealt with, that would only lead to a low birth rate.
“Come to think of it, what are your thoughts, Bjorn?”
“Children. I heard the female warriors of the tribe have their eyes on you too...”

Oh, so that was what “have their eyes on me” meant. No wonder they kept poking at my body and complimenting it. I had genuinely thought they were complimenting my muscles and had been flexing the heck out of them each time.
“I don’t want any yet.”
“Oh, why? Not that I’m one to talk, but we’re on the late side. Some warriors went through their coming-of-age after us have given birth already!”
Was it because it was my first time having this kind of conversation? For some reason, I was starting to feel afraid for the first time since entering this barbarian body.

As I tried to hide the fact that I was inwardly quaking in my boots, Ainar seemed to come to some sort of realization. “Ah! Could it be because of Missha? Don’t worry! Missha will understand. We are barbarians! She can only give birth to beastpeople!” Ainar seemed like a different person to me at that moment. To think she would tell Mr. Bear she preferred cats yet have these thoughts in her head.
“I’m good. And you?” I changed the topic, feeling awkward. To put it in Wuxia terms, I was employing the method of redirecting your opponent’s attack toward another enemy.
“M-Me!?” Yet when the arrow turned on her, Ainar couldn’t hide her bewilderment. The reason was simple. “I-I couldn’t even if I wanted to. W-What warrior would like a small woman like me...?”
Oh, damn those beauty standards. I’d unwittingly ended up hitting one of Ainar’s sore spots.
But the moment I was about to apologize for that, she said, “And... I don’t want any now, either.”
Huh?
“O-Of course! The more I spend time with you, the more young and unmanly the other barbarians look!” Ainar shouted almost in exasperation.
I found myself just as perplexed and suggested she look for a countryman who had accumulated years of seniority. But her response was unexpected.
“I don’t like older men!”
She doesn’t like elders, and people our age feel too young...
She was awfully picky, but to be honest, that was a good thing for me. If she suddenly got pregnant and could not enter the labyrinth for a few months, I’d have to deal with the aftermath.
Hold up, how did the conversation end up like this?
Twenty-nine-year-old Hansu Lee aged another year in this strange world and became thirty.
“Anyway, let me know when you do! I will introduce you to a good warrior!”
But these kinds of conversations remained as troublesome as ever.
Two days later, after breakfast and a warm-up spar with Ainar, I set out on my own. Oh, I guess I couldn’t call it “on my own.”
“You have reached your destination. The store has been searched, but be on your guard regardless.” I was now accustomed to the faithful escort of the knights.
“Right, thanks.” Quickly thanking them for their work, I got off the carriage and entered the meeting place. It was a tea shop I had visited about three times before.

“Oh, Mr. Yandel! Here, over here!” Shavin Emoor, the rank-seven administration clerk, was perched in the corner and waving at me. Beside her sat Ragna, the librarian, in silence. When I sat down with them, all the members of our usual friendly gathering were officially here.
“First, thank you for coming. After you received the title of baronet, I thought long and hard about whether or not I could ask you to come.”
“You worry about strange things.”

“That’s right, Shavin. Do you think this man will change just because he’s a nobleman now?” Ragna sipped her tea, her tone aloof. Well, she was right about that. I had no intention of showing off my title everywhere I went.
Yeah, so the title of baronet is not a particularly big deal to you, is it?

Her casual reaction told me that she was a part of a really prestigious family, though I didn’t know exactly what family that was. The fact that she wasn’t acting any different even in the face of my convoy of knights made me even more curious. Who could it be?
I turned my gaze to look at Shavin. Unlike Ragna, she was glancing at the knights out of the corner of her eye. Well, anyone would be uncomfortable.
Let’s just get straight to the point.
“So, what’s your business today?”
“Huh, since when did we only meet for business?”
“You have a habit of crinkling your nose when you lie.”
“Huh? R-Really? I never knew!”
Of course you didn’t.
“I lied.”
At the sight of Shavin’s dumbstruck expression, Ragna let out a quiet laugh. “This is a really rare sight.”
“Maybe to you. This is nothing to barbarians.” In actuality, if I started acting like a barbarian in earnest, most people made that face. “Anyway, so? Hurry up and tell me your business.”
When I picked the conversation back up where we left off, Shavin came to her senses and brought up her business. “I want to commission you, Baronet Yandel, on behalf of the administrative office.”
Hmm, a part-time job? It wasn’t like I was low on money right now, but you could never have enough money in this world.
“Tell me, what kind of commission is it?”
I should hear it out first.

chapters.title: Chapter 249: Gnome Tree (3)
paragraphs: The commission Shavin brought me was very simple. “You just have to deliver this letter to Baron Nertovin.”
The task was to deliver a letter. The reward was three million stones. But it came with one condition.
“Oh, for reference, this letter must be handed to the baron himself before he leaves Gnome Tree.”

That was the reason why a whopping three million stones were attached to a commission that otherwise only involved delivering something. There were almost no adventurers who could enter Gnome Tree. Actually, aside from the workers who worked on its farms, it was a district only nobles could enter.
“I understand the contents of the commission. I want you to tell me the details.”

It already smelled like a sweet commission, but I didn’t get ahead of myself and calmly went down my list of necessary questions. What was this letter? Why pay such a huge amount for this commission when you could just wait to send it to the baron by mail once he returned to the city?

Shavin answered my questions openly. “I cannot tell you the contents of the letter. And the reason I am making this request is because the baron definitely won’t read our letters even if we send them to his home.”

The administrative office had something they had to relay to the baron, but the baron was ignoring them. And so the administrative office had gotten word that the baron was on vacation in Gnome Tree and devised a way to get the letter directly into his hand.

“Gnome Tree is like a resort for nobles. On top of that, each noble is only permitted three escorts. You can just approach him casually and not have to worry about his knights while you deliver the letter, which will be easier for you too.”

Hmm, that was true. I nodded in understanding. It was definitely troublesome for a noble to visit another nobleman’s house in the city. You had to have a meal with them and say hello to their family. It would be impossible to keep the meeting brief and just hand over the letter.
Then was the condition that it had to be delivered in Gnome Tree added specifically for me?
The thought suddenly came to mind, but it probably wasn’t the only reason. They wouldn’t have made it a condition if they were just being considerate.
“So, what will you do?”

Shavin tossed the ball in my court and I replied only after pretending to think about it some more. “I accept.” Getting paid three million stones for delivering one letter at a moment in time when it was impossible to earn money anywhere? There was no reason not to take the job.
I planned to visit Gnome Tree at some point, anyway.
“Ah, I’m just letting you know in advance, but I’m going to deliver the letter regardless of whether he reads it or not.”
“Okay. As long as you fulfill the commission, you will have no issues getting paid, so you don’t have to worry about that.”

Okay, then that resolved my last concern. I signed the contract Shavin brought and took the letter I was meant to deliver. With that, our official business was over. After an hour or so of informal chitchat, the friendly gathering parted ways and I returned home.
“Missha, pack your things.”
“Huh?”
“Let’s go on a trip.”
We decided on two nights and three days. Although Gnome Tree wasn’t so far away that this couldn’t be a one-day trip, I needed time to find the baron there.
Not only that... There are places I need to visit there too.
If I could have, I would have scheduled a leisurely trip of five nights and six days, but the labyrinth would open again soon.
Well, my team and I agreed not to go in this time, but it’s best to see firsthand how many troops the palace is sending in.
“G-Gnome Tree! Wow! I never thought I would get to go therrre!”

Although I had sprung the trip on her, Missha packed her things excitedly once she found out that the destination was Gnome Tree. For reference, I was permitted to bring three people, so I decided to take Ainar and Erwen as well to make it a family trip.
“I-Is it really okay for me to come?”
“What are you talking about? You don’t have to if you don’t want to.”

“I want to! I’ll go and pack my things! How long did you say we’re going for?” Though she momentarily pretended she was going to decline the invitation, Erwen quickly got up and headed off to pack her things. Her face was bright for the first time in a while. Well, there wasn’t much to be happy about lately.
“Hey! Didn’t I tell you to stop messing arrround and pack properly?”
“I wasn’t messing around...”

“Just underwearrr and that’s it? What about your toothbrush? Towels? Huh? Are you going to ask to borrow mine every night?” Before long, Missha gave in and helped Ainar pack her things, and our preparations progressed smoothly.
Early the next morning, we traveled toward Gnome Tree under the warm hospitality of our convoy of knights. “We will take you to the entrance.”
It was well after noon when we arrived.
“Baronet Bjorn Yandel. Confirmed. Come this way.”

We went through a simple identification process at the castle gates and then stepped foot beyond them. The knights didn’t follow. This was because there was a rule in Gnome Tree that stated you could only bring three companions.
That’s unfortunate.

In truth, the knights wanted to fill all three slots themselves, but I stubbornly refused and filled the spots with Missha, Erwen, and Ainar instead. Having knights with me would make it hard for me to move around freely, and this was a place where I didn’t have to worry too much about assassins.
“Do not hesitate to use the whistle if there is a threat to your safety inside. Gnome Tree’s militia will come to help.”
Since Gnome Tree was the second most secure area in the city after the royal palace, the knights only expressed their concerns rather than try to forcefully cancel the trip.

As we stepped through the double gates, even I was dazzled by Gnome Tree’s scenery. A long road stretched straight out into the horizon, a wide-open green landscape sprawling out on both sides of it. The breeze that gently blanketed my skin carried the scent of unripe grains and fruits.
“Oh! Look over there! There are elves!”

As we were transported by the carriage, we continued to sightsee. Mostly what we saw was elves farming. That was because they were farming specialists. The elves sent those who knew elemental spirit magic to Gnome Tree and received huge amounts of money from the palace in return.
So jealous...
The huge supply of goods from Gnome Tree was also the reason why elves could offer interest-free tax loans to their tribe members, unlike barbarians.
“Erwen, how many years do you guys get loans?”
“For us, it’s three years.”
“Wow, I envy you. We only get loans until the second year. They don’t force us to pay it back, but after that, we have to figure things out on our own, whether we live or die.”

For reference, these tax loan policies were commonplace for everyone except barbarians and humans. It wasn’t just elves making money this way. The dwarves were recognized for their unique construction skills and metallurgy, and had signed a formal contract with the palace. The windmills and waterwheels we saw in the distance were all probably made and managed by them. Oh, and as for beastpeople...
“Moo—!”
“M-Missha! What is that strange-looking monster!?”
“Oh, I guess you’ve never seen one beforrre. It’s called a cow.”
“Cow?”
“Remember that meat you said was the most delicious? Well, I’ve neverrr eaten it from the wild, either...”

Beastpeople were active in the livestock industry. Not only did they have a natural rapport with animals, but there was a special ability-type Soul Beast that increased the growth and reproduction of livestock.
But the ones who make the real money are the dragonians.

The other races were all working class, but the dragonians were a little different. It was safe to say that they were landed gentry. In fact, the farming region commonly referred to as Gnome Tree was located in the holy land of the dragon tribe.
...Why are barbarians the only ones with nothing?
The more I thought about it the more unfair it felt, but what could I do? Fighting was our race’s only talent.
Rattle.

The carriage soon arrived near the mountain in the center of Gnome Tree and began to circle it and head east. A long while later, the coachman assigned to us at the gates of Gnome Tree informed us that we had reached our destination. “We have arrived.”
Said destination was a residential district named Kiarbis, a resort for nobles with such a long history that it had even existed in the game’s setting 150 years ago.
“Please come this way.”
With the help of the man who was serving as both our coachman and guide, we headed into our inn. The administrative office had booked it for us in advance.
It’s nice.
The place was much better than I expected. First, we had our own separate building, and five hired servants came with it. I wondered how much it cost to spend one night here.
“Please start off your stay here with a meal. We have already prepared it.”
Since we were hungry anyway, we ate first.
“There’s a hot spring...?”
When the servant informed us of an outdoor hot spring, we immediately went there to alleviate our travel fatigue.
Oh, yes, this is it.
I should come back later in the winter, even if I had to spend my own money to do it. After I enjoyed the hot springs for about an hour, I found Ainar waiting for me inside alone.
“Bjorn, how long does it take you to wash!?”
“Where are Missha and Erwen?”
“They are both still outside. I don’t understand it at all. It seems like plain old warm water to me...” Ainar didn’t seem to have understood the true purpose of hot springs. Oh, these barbarians.
“Anyway, get some rest, and then you can play with the others once they come out.”
“Huh? What about you?”
“I should start doing my work. Why, do you want to come with me?”
“N-No... I will rest here!” Ainar jumped away at the mention of work and I chuckled before exiting the inn.
At first, I just walked around.
This is the definition of luxury.

I guessed because this place was originally designed as a resort for aristocrats, it was filled to the brim with high-end facilities: hot springs, riding arenas, fishing grounds, etcetera. If this were the modern world, I would’ve called this extravagant, but here it was on a whole other level.
They don’t just eat wild meat, but also use it for recreation?

Almost 99 percent of this city ate meat and bread made with mana stones. As you could tell just by looking at Ainar, most had never even seen a real cow. But this place even had a field where pheasants and deer were released for hunting purposes.
Hmm, I think that’s enough looking around...

I took the letter and headed to my destination. There was no need to go to great lengths to find out which inn the baron was staying at. No other titled noble in this city would be staying in rented lodgings like I was. Most spent their vacations in the villas they owned.
“You can come in.” When I arrived at the villa and announced myself, I was soon granted permission to enter. Whew, thankfully he didn’t tell me to get lost.
“I’ve been wanting to meet you myself. Haha, pleased to make your acquaintance, Baronet Yandel. But why have you come to see me?”
“Oh, I have something to give you.”
“Give me?” When I delivered the letter, the baron opened it right away. Then a strange look crossed his features. “These administrators sure are riled up, huh? To ask something like this from you...”
“Well, I don’t know what this is all about.”
“Hmm, and you still accepted the request? Why would someone like you do that?” the baron muttered like he couldn’t understand my logic at all.
To be honest, I’d readily agreed to it because they’d offered me three million stones as payment... but because that wouldn’t make me look too good, I made up an excuse. “I owe them a debt.”
“Haha, you could have just pretended whatever it was never happened.”
Wow, was this the mind of a nobleman? It made me kind of admire him in a bad way, but I couldn’t say that to his face. “A warrior never forgets a favor.”
“Hmm... that’s true. Haha! How interesting. A nobleman who’s guaranteed to be loyal? There’ll probably be many nobles who will want to be on friendly terms with you.”

After the delivery was complete, the baron invited me to have a meal with him, but I declined and left. In this much-too-small aristocratic society, you were bound to face repercussions if you were friendly with just anyone.
Anyway, with that, the commission’s over.
I completed it so easily that I wondered to myself whether I could actually get three million stones just for this.
That means I’m free for the rest of the trip. I’ll visit that place later in the evening.

After deciding on my schedule, I headed home. It was then that, among the knights following around their young noble masters, I noticed a familiar symbol. As soon as I spotted it, I broke out in a cold sweat.
The House of Baron Ifreia.
It was the same house that the man whose identity the GM had stolen just to meet me belonged to.
It can’t be. Wasn’t he the youngest? It must be his older brother.

And even if I was wrong about that, that didn’t change anything. Quantum mechanics itself said so. You couldn’t know anything for sure until you opened the box. Whether or not the cat inside was alive or dead could only be verified with observation. And luckily for me, I hadn’t checked inside the box yet.
I should get out of here fast.
I fixed my eyes on the ground and increased my speed. But at that moment...

“W-Wait! Aren’t you Baronet Yand—” The man just had to recognize me, his familiar voice ringing out behind me. “P-Please wait! I-I heard you were terribly hurt because that wicked wizard disguised himself as me. I must apologize—”
It was (True) Hans I.

chapters.title: Chapter 250: Gnome Tree (4)
paragraphs: At first, I thought it might be the GM again, but if it was, he wouldn’t be using a face he’d already used before to approach me again. Also, the vibe being given off by the knights and the man himself was completely different. Simply put, this guy was the real Hans I, not the GM pretending to be him. And so, I had just one option.
“I must apologize—”
Holding my breath, I gritted my teeth and pretended I didn’t hear him.
Dash.
“W-Why are you running away?!”
“Ooh! I just felt like running!”
“Th-that’s...!” When I took off in an oblivious sprint, (True) Hans I was extremely startled, but that wasn’t going to stop my feet from moving.
“Behel-aaah!” Our distance widened in an instant and he didn’t follow me, either. Thankfully, it seemed he didn’t have that much tenacity.
Did I lose him?

Quickly arriving in front of our inn, I tried to calm my pounding heart. I’d only heard his voice—I didn’t even see his face. Thanks to that, no eye contact was made, and since I held my breath, the possibility of airborne contamination was low.
...This should be enough. Yes, I should be fine.
“Welcome back.” As I was taking a breather in front of the door, a servant greeted me. I followed him inside.
“Nyaha, Bjorn is herrre!” A very red-faced Missha greeted me. She was in High Energy (Alcohol) Mode.
Erwen, who was sitting gracefully next to her, was in a similar boat. “Mister... hehe, hehehe!” She called out to me in an eerie tone and promptly burst into a creepy laugh.
What’s going on here?
Our surroundings were full of empty bottles and the smell of alcohol was wafting through the living room.
It hasn’t even been an hour since I left...?
Just what had happened here in the meantime? Putting on a detective’s hat and scanning the room, it was then that I noticed that Ainar was nowhere to be found.
“Where’s Ainar?”

“The lady warrior got drunk and fell asleep a long time ago.” The person who answered my question was one of the building’s servants. When I asked for her location, I was directed not to a room but a yard in the middle of the building.
Honkkk!
Ha, honestly.
I tossed Ainar into her bed and headed back down. Missha was drinking from the bottle, seemingly overjoyed about something. “Mm...!”

Sensing some sort of danger, I cautiously approached Missha. “Did something happen while I was gone?” There were occasions when she took small sips of alcohol and got drunk, but I’d never seen her knock back entire bottles like this.
“Happen? Nyaha, nothing happened!”
“Then why are you drinking like that?”
“I was just in a good mood!”
“I-I see?”
Drinking because she was in a good mood? I guessed I was worried for nothing. After a refreshing dip in the hot spring and with free drinks on tap, there was no real reason not to drink.
“Yeah, at firrrst.” Missha wiped the alcohol from her lips with her sleeve, all traces of laughter disappearing from her face.

I subconsciously turned my head to avoid her gaze. Naturally, Erwen’s disheveled form on the sofa caught my eye. She was staring out into space and for some reason kept giggling to herself. “Hehehe...” Was she a giggly drunk or something?
Missha suddenly grabbed my wrist. “Hey, Bjorn.”
“Yeah, speak.”
“Your rrrejection that day.”
Uh... you’re going to bring that up now?
It was an uncomfortable topic, but the mood wasn’t right for me to avoid it. As soon as I shut my mouth and waited, Missha bit her lip and asked, “Is it because I can’t give birrrth to a barbarian?”
Huh? What? Did Ainar say something weird?

My brain malfunctioned for a moment, but a barbarian’s body was good in a crisis. “Of course not.” My mouth opened without an inkling of hesitation. It wasn’t exactly a lie. The reason why I had rejected Missha that day wasn’t because I didn’t feel any attraction to her or because she was a beastwoman. There was a reason that was mine and mine alone.

“I see...” As if to discern whether I was lying, Missha stared straight into my eyes before opening a new bottle and pouring it down her throat. “Then it must be...” She looked into my eyes again and then avoided them, her lips opening and closing before she finally, quietly continued. “You... one day, disappear... disappearrr...” Missha trailed off before her head finally dropped. “Nyahang...”
No wonder she seemed far past her usual drinking limit. I let out the breath I had been holding and picked her up. Then I took her to her room and laid her on the bed.
When I returned to the living room, Erwen was looking at me with the corners of her lips quirked up. “Finally, everyone... is asleep...”
What was this kid saying? “Go to sleep if you’re drunk.”
Neck slice.
“Kehk—”
I knocked her out and tossed her next to Missha.

It was slowly approaching midnight. I wondered if I should clean up the bottles rolling around but decided to just leave them alone. This wasn’t even our home. I was sure they’d take care of it once I left the room.
“Whew...”
I slumped down on the sofa, which was a bit small for me. My thoughts were all jumbled because of the last thing Missha had said.
“You... one day, disappear... disappearrr...”

It was obvious what she was trying to say in the end. Because you’re going to disappear someday... She was probably going to ask if that was why I rejected her. Of course, I doubted she knew for sure that I was an evil spirit. No, rather, she probably considered it more likely that I wasn’t. She saw me receiving a blessing in a city where evil spirits were known to be enemies of the gods. The idea that one of the said gods would help an evil spirit and bestow a holy relic on them was absurd. This was probably just a bud of anxiety that had been rooted in her mind for a while now and had come out thanks to the alcohol.
Still, what’s fortunate is I don’t think she’ll hate me even if I am an evil spirit.
I was relieved by that fact. I was grateful and even pleased that I had not spent my time here in vain. But the greatest emotion I was feeling was shame.
What do I really expect?

When I first woke up in Bjorn Yandel’s body, my greatest goal had been survival. After somehow surviving and adapting to this world, I decided to try to find a way to return to my original world. But.... Wasn’t it all right to just live like this? Did I really have to go back there? To be honest, there was less to look forward to there than here.

Lately, this thought had been growing in my mind. Somehow, I was starting to understand why players called the residents of this world NPCs to differentiate them. There was a need to draw a line, to remind ourselves that this world was not the world we belonged to, that we had a place to return to.
Stop.

I forcibly stopped that speeding train of thought. Would I go back home? Or stay here? Neither decision could be made yet. Didn’t I make a vow to myself after seeing those inmates on death row die for not being able to pay their taxes? I was determined to at least get to the sixth floor.
There’s no use wondering about all that now anyway.

This wasn’t just a matter of taxes. The Dragon Slayer, Clown, Noark, the palace—this world was full of things that could threaten my life. Like it or not, I had to become stronger. No matter what I wanted or decided to do, I needed to be alive for it to happen. So, on that note...
“Where are you going this late at night?”
“Oh, I’m going for a short walk. No need to wait for me.” I let the servant know I was heading out and left the building. It was approaching a time when there would be no people around.
When I got outside, the cool night air filled my lungs. Perhaps it was because we were right under the mountain, but it was a little chilly.
Step, step.

As expected, the street was sparsely populated, but it wasn’t completely empty. The brightly-lit gambling hall was still buzzing with noise. Well, that didn’t really matter much to me because my current destination was outside of town.
It’s dark.

As soon as I left the town, a darkness comparable to the labyrinth filled my field of vision. The countryside in Korea was like this too. If I moved even a little bit away from the light, nature’s pitch-black embrace greeted me.
Anyway, it should be out soon.

I debated lighting a torch but decided to just walk carefully, just in case. I didn’t know how long I was out there by the time the cave marked on the map the inn had given me finally appeared. This place was a tourist attraction here.
No one’s guarding it.

As soon as I cautiously entered the cave, my surroundings slowly began to brighten up. That was because this place was similar to the first floor, a mysterious cave full of crystals on the walls that glowed with blue light. I moved without hesitation. There weren’t any other paths—in the game, you just had to walk straight from the entrance.
Whooom!
Before long, a wide cavity appeared. At its center was a boulder that pulsed at regular intervals.
Rignaracia.

The map-slash-pamphlet from the inn said that the origin of the name was an ancient word which literally translated to “blessing of the land.” Touching it brought good luck. It was probably a superstition. After all, the object that actually had a hidden feature here wasn’t that boulder.
Slide.

I opened the sub-space bag and pulled out my mace. Passing by the boulder in the center of the chamber, I pressed the interact button on the wall where a mural was painted. Oh, and by that, I meant I hit it with all my might.
Banggg!

The wall collapsed as it was shattered by a macing with the power of an Ogre behind it, but I wasn’t too worried about that. This cave had a self-repairing magic circle. It would fix itself after five minutes or so.
Let’s go, then.
After that, I pushed myself into the passage that appeared behind the collapsed wall. Inside was a small space just like in the game.
Seeing as it’s hidden like this, the one outside is probably fake and the one here is real.

I placed my hand on the boulder in the center. Unlike the one outside, it was an ordinary rock that didn’t vibrate at regular intervals or give off a mysterious vibe. But as time passed, another feeling came.
[The energy of the Earth Dragon dwells within you. (1/3)]
A feeling of satisfaction flowed into my body through my fingertips.
[Your Soul Power has increased by +10. Your Earth Resistance has increased by +20.]
It was a rather sweet hidden feature. Although it came with the condition that you had to become a noble and be able to come and go within Gnome Tree, it gave you almost thirty stats for free.
Most people who played the original version even a little bit should know about this, because they would have hit the interact key everywhere they went.
This was my guess, but I suspected quite a few players knew about this hidden element. I was sure they didn’t know about this particular part of it, though.
[The blessing bestowed on your soul has resonated. Additional stats have increased 30%.]
Upon receiving the Earth Dragon’s blessing, the stat buff was upgraded from 20 percent to 30 percent.
I didn’t think that I would be the first to unlock it, though.
It was definitely a far cry from a normal playthrough. Becoming a noble at only level five? If this were the game, I would’ve thought this was a bug.
Anyway, I should head back soon.
Now that I’d gotten everything, I turned to the exit, at which point I froze.
Swoosh.
In front of the hole in the wall, which had begun to repair itself as if in defiance of time, stood a man.
“Wow, so you really were a player?” It was Baekho Lee.

All sorts of thoughts ran through my mind. Why was Baekho here? I hadn’t seen a hint of him since that day. Could it be that he’d been following me this whole time? The truth, it turned out, was far simpler than that.
“This is a strange coincidence. I came here because I thought the GM was here in disguise, but to think you’d show up.”
It all went back to Hans. Baekho had run into Hans I by coincidence at Gnome Tree and while following him, discovered me.
From then on, he must have followed me around.
I was able to piece together a rough timeline of events. So, how should I act now? There was pretty much only one option.

“There you go again. Aren’t you tired of saying that?” I didn’t think it was a good idea to reveal my identity to Baekho. He was clearly a volatile guy. Even if we stayed friendly, he’d probably pull out a knife and force me to make a choice the minute shit hit the fan.
“Looks like that cat’s noticed it too. Wouldn’t it be better to kill her?”
Yeah, like that. I felt like I’d been cornered, but I stubbornly pretended to have no clue what he was talking about. “I see now why the chieftain calls evil spirits wicked beings.”
“Wow, I admit you have a good head on your shoulders. To think you’d even try to weasel your way out of a situation like this.”
I used all the acting chops I possessed to put on a questioning look. “Situation like this...?”
Baekho chuckled like I wasn’t fooling him. “Yes, a situation like this. The fact that you’re here is proof that you’re a player, right? How else would you know this was hidden here?”
Okay, I thought you’d ask that, asshole.

I replied on cue, cleverly remixing the truth. “I am a benefactor of the dragon race. After returning the Dragon Sword to their people, I became close with the ancient elder dragon, Lapir.
