Even the dragon priestess, his daughter, gets along with me well.” This reply neatly implied I would have heard this information from them.
As soon as Baekho heard this, he tilted his head. “...What the hell? You’re telling the truth.”
Of course I am. Because I didn’t lie.
“Then were you the one who messed up that dragon bastard? Wow, this is epic!” Baekho exclaimed, apparently finding this somewhat interesting.
I sighed internally. Although I’d had to reveal some of my secrets to get out of this mess I was in... to be honest, it wasn’t really a loss.
Yeah, the ring broke off anyway.

Now that the holy relic was no longer active, like it or not, the day would come when I ran into the Dragon Slayer again. That meant I had no reason to guard that information with my life like before.
“Yes.”
Baekho studied me for a moment and then nodded. “Makes sense. Yeah, with an accomplishment like that, it makes sense they’d tell you about this. This is nothing special.”
Does that mean I’m in the clear? No, of course not. It’s too early to let my guard down.
I waited patiently for whatever he said next, remaining alert. After what felt like a year, Baekho grinned and asked, “But hey, why are you answering all my questions?”
My mind went blank.
“Last time when I asked if you were a player, you stubbornly refused to answer. So why are you being so nice all of a sudden?”
That damned prick.

chapters.title: Chapter 251: Gnome Tree (5)
paragraphs: There was no point in making up excuses anymore. No amount of clever words was going to trick him. He was going to try to get a definite answer by any means necessary.
God damn it.

Setting aside my displeasure at being forced to make a choice, my brain was already starting to run through the options available to me and the fallout of each one in detail. What was really the best option for me?
“Excuse me? Aren’t you going to speak? I asked why you’re being so nice?”
Ha, this annoying prick. I wished I could say something like, I just wanted to, you got a problem with that? and go back to Brainless Barbarian Mode.
But then I could really die.

I was weaker than him, and so even though the guy kept voicing his suspicions, I couldn’t default to my usual strategy of claiming there was something wrong with his head and following it up by swinging my mace. If I did, it’d be my head that got cracked open.
Baekho sighed in frustration and glared at me with his blue eyes. “Ha, look at you, acting rude again.”
“Why do you keep asking? You have no intention of believing me anyway.” I didn’t bother to hide my huff, but it seemed he was just as annoyed with me as I was with him.
“Yeah, but it’s different hearing it from your own mouth.”
Yeah, I know what you mean. That’s why I’ve been trying to hide it this whole time. So, you insist on hearing an answer?
It was time to admit it. Too many things had already gone wrong for me to be able to get through this without sacrificing something. I had to give up what I had to give up.
“They say manners make the man.” I may have been suspected many times in the past, but I’d never confessed my identity to anyone until now.
“Huh?” Baekho looked puzzled by my sudden change in attitude, but I had nothing holding me back now that I’d made up my mind.
“Wouldn’t it be good manners to pretend you didn’t see anything just now?”
“Hold on. Really? You really are a player?” Upon actually hearing the truth from me, Baekho’s eyes gleamed in fascination.
So, it really was just a matter of curiosity for you.
Anger burned inside of me. Did he even have a clue that this was the first time I’d ever spoken in this tone with Bjorn Yandel’s body?
Still, it feels a bit refreshing.
Feeling a strange mix of liberation and resentment, I glared at Baekho. But it seemed this guy’s empathy gauge was nonexistent.
“Wow, and you’ve seen that movie too!” Even in the midst of all this, he focused only on the topic he was interested in and wanted to talk about. Did he have literally no social skills?
“...You should apologize before anything else.” I was sure we painted a bizarre picture, a barbarian lecturing a human on social common sense and morality.

“Oh, sorry. But since you watched that movie, suddenly you don’t feel like a stranger anymore. I like that movie.” Baekho blurted out a flimsy apology before cautiously asking one more thing. “...But did you also see the second one?”

Just what was wrong with this guy? At this point, this conversation was confusing enough to make even a barbarian cry. “...I saw it.” I decided to answer his questions for now because if I ignored them, he might do another one-eighty.
“Hm. Why are you talking down to me?”
Huh?

Suddenly riled up, all traces of laughter disappeared from Baekho’s face as he released a wave of murderous intent. “Why do you keep talking without honorifics? Don’t you know a thing about mutual respect? What, do you think a player somehow won’t die if they get stabbed in the stomach?”
I felt like I was going to lose my mind. “...I’m not used to talking like that.”
“Oh, you’re a Westerner!”
That was another way that statement could be interpreted. I had been speaking with barbarians in mind.
“Then let’s both speak casually. Okay?” A bright smile returning to his face, Baekho requested a handshake. At first glance, he seemed utterly unpredictable.
This has sobered me right up.

It kind of cleared my mind. Perhaps his seemingly erratic speech patterns were more strategic than they seemed, a way to seize the upper hand by skillfully draining the opponent’s energy and leaving them with no time to think.
Did he ask if I watched the second movie to figure out when I came here, and the last question to check if I’m from Asia?
Maybe that was a leap, but it would be best to be careful.
I should definitely hide that I’m Hansu Lee.

That was my biggest concern. At first, I had thought it might be better to reveal both the fact that I was a player and who exactly I was to be on friendly terms with him, but I put that on hold for one reason.
“Looks like that cat’s noticed it too. Wouldn’t it be better to kill her?”

Earlier, he had offered that as a bit of simple advice, the same way someone might meddle in the life of an acquaintance. But the moment I revealed that I was Hansu Lee, he would make it his business. This guy was the type to be fiercely protective over one of the few Korean players in this strange world.
“But about me being a player...”
“Ah, I promise I won’t tell anyone! What, do you think I don’t have basic common courtesy?”

The word “yes” sat in the back of my throat, but I swallowed it back. Now that I’d talked to him some more, I had a better understanding of him. Baekho was like a ball that was liable to bounce anywhere at any time. I could never get involved with him, at least not until I was confident I could control him.
“Anyway, I’m really glad you answered honestly. I heard you became a nobleman recently. If you were an NPC, I was planning to kill you here before you could join the palace’s side.”
That nonchalant statement made my heart skip a beat. “...What?”
“Why are you surprised? It’s not like I just enjoy PKs or something. Well, as long as you’re not an NPC born with a destiny it’s fine. Those guys are a headache for me too.”

I couldn’t understand a word he was saying. A little curious, I tried to ask about it indirectly, but Baekho just glossed over it. Was it because I was Westerner Bjorn Yandel? I felt like he would’ve answered Korean Hansu Lee.
“Oh, and one more piece of advice just in case. It’s a bit ridiculous to say this to someone who is already a nobleman, but don’t get too involved with the palace.”
“Your reasoning?”
“The palace is not interested in opening the Gate of the Abyss. No, instead, they’re more intent on stopping that from happening. It might be their fault that the Genesis Treasures are gone too.”
The palace? But why?

It was common knowledge that the key to saving this world was located in the deepest part of the labyrinth, but was that all a lie? I was filled to the brim with curiosity and questions. However, no matter what I asked him, Baekho just looked at me in annoyance and said: “Why do you need to know?”
Well, if that was how he felt, I doubted he’d tell me who the GM was, either.
While I was licking my lips in disappointment, he asked, “So, you’re in that camp?”
“That camp?”
“You know, people who want to keep living here. When I saw you risk your life for that NPC, I figured you were one of those guys, but judging by your growth rate you might not be. Which is it?”
“What will you do if I say I want to stay?”
“What do you mean what will I do? Of course there are bastards like that out here. I’m not that inflexible. As long as it doesn’t affect me, I don’t care.”
I quietly stared into Baekho’s eyes, not that there was a point in doing so. I couldn’t tell what was going on behind those blue eyes at all.
I don’t think he’s just sounding me out...

I let go of my worries and parted my lips. “I don’t know.” It was the most honest answer I could give. “At first, going back was my goal. But these days, I’m starting to wonder if I should really have to risk my life to go back.”

“Because of that red cat?” I didn’t answer, but I guessed that was enough for him. “I feel like I’m looking at the old me,” Baekho said with a smirk. “I’m telling you this because you seem promising, but don’t expect too much from an NPC. You’ll definitely regret it.”

I could sense a cold emotion hidden behind his laughing tone and suddenly questioned what had happened to him. Just what had he experienced in this world that he’d become such a broken monster who only wanted to go back? I had no way of finding out right now.

“Then since I asked all my questions, I’m leaving.” Before long, Baekho turned around like he was done here and brought down the wall, which had just finished repairing itself. Actually, I wasn’t sure if you could call what he did “brought down.”
Crumble.
All that remained of the wall when he was done was dust. And when Baekho waved his hand again, even that dust was blown away by the wind.
...Good thing I didn’t use Brainless Mode.
At the realization that it could’ve been my head that was turned to dust, I felt faint.
Just when I was watching Baekho leave, he turned around, looked at me, and delivered some parting words. “Oh, right. By the way, we’re strangers the next time we meet. Got it?”
“What do you mean?”
“If we happen to run into each other by chance, don’t pretend to know me. I don’t do friends in this world.”
Oh, that bastard. How cold.
After Baekho left, I exited the cave without looking back and returned to our lodgings. I spent the entire next morning resting with the trio, who were suffering from hangovers.
“Ughhh, Mister... I’m dying...”
“Bjorn... But when did you get back? How did the work yesterrrday go?”
By the way, Missha seemed to have forgotten everything that happened last night, as she didn’t remember me coming back at all. Which was for the best.
“Is it because I can’t give birrrth to a barbarian?”
If she knew she said something like that to me yesterday, she wouldn’t have been able to face me.
“If you’ve finished the commission, can you just have fun now?”
“Of course.” I’d planned for two nights and three days just in case, but all of our business at Gnome Tree had been concluded on the first day. The rest of the trip was free.
“Oooh! Let’s go have fun!”
In the end, we spent the second day having fun until late at night. It was a rather enjoyable day, except for the drowning at the end.
“Ainar! I told you not to move like that!”

It happened at a fishing spot. We had been fishing at night with the lanterns on when Ainar freaked out after being bitten by a fish, causing the boat to capsize. The problem was that none of us knew how to swim. Well, the three of them had probably never been to waters this deep.
I really thought I was going to die.

Still, I learned one thing thanks to that whole mess. When I fell into Glacier Cave way back when, I’d assumed I’d been on the verge of drowning because of the armor but that wasn’t it. Barbarians could not swim. It wasn’t a question of technique, but because we had no choice but to sink if we fell into the water. Luckily, I had been able to use Giantization (Transcendence) mode to bring my head above the surface and call for help.
Once I get back, I should look around for swimming classes. Ainar may not be able to, but these guys should learn to swim.
Anyway, that was how our second day ended. The next day, after drinking all night and falling asleep, we woke up at noon and got on the carriage that would take us back home.
“Ugh, I wish we had just one more day. I guess we’re rrreally leaving, though.”
“I agree. Since Mister doesn’t drink much at home...”
“Oooh! Missha! There are horses running over there!”
We spent a few hours admiring the natural scenery that was hard to come by in the city. We soon arrived at the southwest exit of Gnome Tree and returned the whistle we had received upon entry.
I forgot about that.

The whistle was a pride of the Gnome Tree and could summon a militia whenever and wherever it was blown. I wondered what would have happened if I’d blown it when I ran into Baekho, but I was sure it wouldn’t have changed much. I didn’t think he would have given me the time to do so, either.
“Then I’m going to rest. Let me know when you guys are hungry laterrr.”
We arrived home in the evening and headed to our separate rooms to rest, and the next day wasn’t all that different. It was a period of peaceful relaxation. As always, times like these flew by.
“I’m going out for a while.”
The day had finally come. Two hours remained until midnight when the labyrinth would open. I finished getting ready and headed to Dimension Square.
They said the palace has really prepared for this one.

Rumor had it that the palace was building an army. Since they’d suffered a blow, apparently they planned to fight back properly and seek revenge. The scale of their efforts was unknown. That was because it seemed there hadn’t been any official letters requesting cooperation from clans sent out like for the last conquest. That meant they intended to handle this with the power of the palace alone.
I’m sure I’ll get a sense of it once I get to the plaza. Just how big their forces are.

I could actually see adventurers here and there heading to the plaza to scout out the situation. Everyone must have been curious about the palace’s true potential, which had only ever been speculated on but never properly witnessed.
“Oh, Bjorn! Are you going to the square too?”
“I want to see for myself.”
I spotted some familiar faces on the way, so we chatted while we walked together. A while later, all the adventurers who made their way over, including me, were tilting their heads in confusion.
“...Now I didn’t expect this.”
“To think there would be no one here.”
It wasn’t exactly no one. Guards from the Public Peace Agency were occupying the plaza to prevent adventurers from entering, but that was it.
“Where’s the army?”
No matter where we looked, there was no sight of the rumored army.
“Are they not here yet?”
“My friend, do you really think that’s likely? The labyrinth opens in five minutes. If they’re still not here, that means the army never existed in the first place.”
“How anticlimactic. To think the rumors about them putting up a proper fight were false.”
The adventurers gathered near the square and started to leave one by one, making no effort to hide their disappointment. The same went for the adventurers I’d run into on the way here.
“Yandel, are you not coming?”
“I’m going to wait a little longer.”
“Hmm, then I’ll be going first.”
Figuring I might as well just in case, I waited there until the portal opened and stayed for some time after it closed. To be blunt, there really was no army.
The heck? Are they aiming for the next opening?
I was full of questions, but staying here any longer wouldn’t answer them. I gave up and turned around. And that was when it happened.
Booom!
Somewhere in the distance, I heard the faint sound of something collapsing.
Dddddd!
Before long, the ground beneath my feet began to shake.
“W-What is this? An earthquake?” The officials and security guards who filled the square froze, stunned looks on their faces.

The few knights in the square were different. Their expressions looked more resolute than anything, remaining unchanged as they began to whisper amongst themselves. Like something they had been waiting for had finally begun.
Yeah, so that’s what it was.
I shifted my gaze to the ground. For some reason, I had a feeling I knew where the royal army was, even if I couldn’t see it with my eyes right now.
Sneaking in right under everyone’s noses.
The war had already begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 252: Open World (1)
paragraphs: It was a small earthquake. Tables vibrated but the cups on top of them did not tip over nor was the sound of something breaking heard. The most that happened was the pile of chips falling down.
“An earthquake?”
Although momentarily surprised by the sudden natural phenomenon, when the shaking stopped, the nobles went back to gambling as usual—except for one person.
“Wait, young master, where are you going?”
“I just remembered something I had to do. I’ll just fold this round.”

The man flipped over the cards in his hands and took his chips as he bowed out. Then he took off the mask he was wearing. The concept of a gambling house you could enjoy while wearing a mask was quite fun.
No matter how I look at it, that couldn’t have just been an earthquake.

Baekho walked out into the dark street and sat on the first bench he saw to calmly assess the situation. The other nobles didn’t seem to notice because of how noisy the gambling hall was, but he had heard the huge wave of energy rolling through the ground beneath his feet.
It was like a mixture of mana and divine power.
He wasn’t a wizard, but he had highly attuned senses and considerable aptitude for mana, so there was no way he was mistaken.
If that’s the case... They were always talking about breaking the protective barrier, but I guess they really did.
Before long, Baekho reached the truth. These bastards couldn’t be more relentless if they tried. It couldn’t be a coincidence that they’d made their move at midnight right when the labyrinth opened.
Sneaking in under their noses, huh?

Now that he’d left the palace, he had no way of knowing for sure, but Noark’s side would have entered the labyrinth. They’d probably dedicated all their energy into preparing for this month’s expedition, never imagining that they would fall victim to their own tactics.
This could end up wiping out all those assholes down there.
To Baekho, that wasn’t a good thing. He had been considering clearing the game with the bastards from Noark if he ran out of options later.
I have nothing to do anyway... Should I go down and help?
The thought came to mind, but Baekho smirked and shook his head. That didn’t suit his play style. Instead, he had a better idea.
The palace must be empty right about now, no?
Baekho’s smirk deepened.
The forehead of the Guardian of the Palace and Knight of Light, the Commander of the First Royal Guard Jerome Saintred, was covered in deep wrinkles due to the news he’d just received.
“The palace is under attack...?”

At first, he thought it might be a counterattack from Noark, but that made no sense. The palace had gathered troops, pretending that the labyrinth was their aim, and had taken so much care to be secretive that they’d only revealed that the true target of this campaign was Noark two hours before departure. That, coupled with the fact that the protective barrier around Noark had only been opened just now, meant there hadn’t been nearly enough time for enough troops to escape and attack the palace.
“Have we received orders to retreat?”
“Not yet.”
“Then the plan remains unchanged. The battle will continue.”
Jerome quickly led the army down the sewers and as time passed, he received news about the identity of the person who had dared to attack the palace.
To think it wasn’t a group.
He briefly wondered if this was the work of the Fallen Scholar, whose danger level had been elevated recently, but even that hypothesis proved to be incorrect.
“Baekho Lee.”

Once a more promising adventurer than anyone, he had brought on a catastrophe once he was discovered to be an evil spirit. Of course, very few people knew about said catastrophe. The incident was thoroughly covered up by the palace, who valued his talent, and he had been given a new identity.
What a headache. How the hell did he know that even I would be out with the rest of the troops for the military campaign?

As far as he knew, Baekho currently had no means of obtaining information. In the past, he had communicated with an outside collaborator at an evil spirit gathering, but he was currently banned from the gathering. This was also the work of the palace. They had slipped information about Baekho’s identity to the evil spirit named the GM, and when there had been no signs that he’d been ousted, they sent him to Noark to make him an enemy.
Then did he just guess on his own?

Jerome groaned. He had heard an earthquake had occurred aboveground after the protective barrier was destroyed, but there was one part he didn’t understand. Inferring what was going on from the earthquake? That much was understandable, but taking action was another matter. If he had guessed wrong, he could have been caught again, so why would he take on a gamble like that?
...That man is the type to do things like that.

It hurt his pride, but Jerome could admit it. Baekho was a beast-like man. Whenever an opportunity presented itself to him, he was the type to snap his jaws around the enemy and not mind the risk of getting bitten himself.
And it had to be now, when the Order of the Rose is vacant...

Jerome worried about the situation aboveground, but there had been no call to withdraw yet, so there was only one thing he needed to do now: fulfill his duties as a knight and execute the palace’s orders.
“We have arrived.”

Passing through the underground maze, the army finally reached the final gateway to get to Noark, a stone gate enchanted with dozens of ancient spells. How many hours had it taken to break down this wall alone during the last campaign?
“Luckily, it looks like they haven’t properly fixed it yet. Begin.”
At Jerome’s orders, the Wizard Corps began to draw a massive eight-pronged magic circle on the floor.
Kabooom!
A long while later, the magic circle flared with a powerful light and shot pure waves of mana at the stone gate.
Shaaa!
Beyond the cloud of dust, the underground city was once again visible.

“Come on, let’s go. It’s time to defeat these wicked rebels and restore peace and stability to this city.” Jerome pulled out the Sword of State the king had bestowed on him and, before anyone else, stepped into the beyond. “For the eternal prosperity of Rafdonia.” There wasn’t a hint of hesitation in his steps.
The portal in Dimension Square had closed. However, I stayed there for a long time after that in the hopes that I might be able to get some useful information out of those knights.
Welp, I just wasted my time.

The knights refused to engage in even the most trivial small talk with me and disappeared as soon as the clean-up in the square was complete, so I gave up and left. Instead of heading to the inn right away, I planned to stop by a tavern to hear what the other adventurers thought of the incident.
Should I go to Mr. Bear’s place while I’m at it? Hmm, that would be a good idea.

Adventurers often visited his tavern too. It also didn’t have partitions or rooms like more popular taverns so it was perfect for eavesdropping on conversations, although he’d get angry if I said that to his face.
“Oh, Yandel. What are you doing here at this hour? And without Missha.”
“I was out and got bored. You seem pretty busy today so don’t mind me. I’m going to drink quietly in the corner.”
“...Can’t you just call me over to chat? If it’s you, my wife will probably say it’s okay,” Mr. Bear pled once he spotted me in the tavern, apparently sensing an opportunity to slack off.
Geez, don’t you feel sorry for your pregnant wife?
“I want to just sit quietly today.”
“...If you say so. Do you just need some snacks and drinks?”
“That would be great.”
While I sat at an empty table and waited, Mr. Bear prepared a platter made of just meat for me. The drink of choice was the signature drink here—salt honey wine.
At first it tasted strange, but the more I try it, the easier it goes down.

Anyway, this was not my main reason for coming here. As I sipped my drink and kept my ears open, I could hear the conversations of nearby adventurers and ordinary citizens. Word spread fast in taverns, and as a result, most of the conversation in the room centered around the army the palace had formed.
Nothing of particular value.

That the palace had deliberately spread false rumors, that Noark was sure to be afraid—this was all information without substance that they’d cooked up in their own imaginations. Well, I hadn’t expected information on par with the Round Table from a tavern, so I wasn’t disappointed. My objective here was just to learn what public opinion was, anyway.
These days, even ordinary city dwellers don’t view the palace in a good light.
After that I closed my ears and drank as I got my thoughts in order. A long while later, the tavern became less busy so Mr. Bear came over and took a seat in front of me.
“Yandel, what do you think?”
“About the army?”
“Yeah, you have unbelievable instincts when it comes to these things.”

I thought it through before telling him about my hypothesis that the army might be stealthily infiltrating Noark right about now. I still wasn’t sure I was right. I wondered what veteran adventurer Mr. Bear thought about the idea.
“...So was that what the earthquake was about?”
“Do you believe I’m right?”

“Isn’t your explanation much more plausible? Definitely more than that bullshit idea that the palace is afraid of Noark.” Having seen the palace’s treasury once before, Mr. Bear was quick to accept my logic. He knew that the palace’s potential was far greater than he’d imagined. “...It’s possible that we might be able to enter the labyrinth next month.” Before long, Mr. Bear voiced his prediction that the cold war might end much earlier than expected and also expressed his worries about the city’s economic problems. “Yandel, doesn’t that mean you should spend your cash instead of saving it like this? If the situation in the labyrinth settles down, the prices will return to normal.”
I was a bit touched by the question. Was it because he was a veteran adventurer with a family to take care of? It seemed like Ainar and Missha didn’t think about things like that at all.
“Let’s just keep an eye on it for now. Tomorrow, we’ll have a better sense of what’s going on.”
“Yes, I was too hasty.”
Drifting away from that particular topic, I drank and chatted about various things with Mr. Bear.
Gong! Gong! Gong! Gong!

Then the alarms outside began to ring. This was the first time I had seen this happen in over a year of living in this city. Even when my carriage had exploded and the GM and Baekho made a mess, the city’s alarm bells did not go off. But they were ringing now?
Clunk, clunk, clunk.

When I got outside, I could see guards from the Public Peace Agency running somewhere in their heavy boots. I grabbed one and asked about the situation. The guard told me he couldn’t talk to civilians about it but his tune changed when I revealed my identity.
“My name is Bjorn, son of Yandel. I am an official nobleman who was bestowed the title of baronet by the palace. So tell me. What is going on?”
“...W-We don’t know, either. We just received orders to provide support in Karnon. According to my colleagues, there was a big fire.”
A big fire in Karnon at a time like this... It can’t be a coincidence.

Could it be that Noark had invaded the city? Well, I wasn’t sure about that, but it was possible. If they had somehow learned about the palace’s surprise attack plan in advance, they could have chosen to go with a war of attrition strategy.
Ha, those bastards from the palace can’t do a single thing right.

As I quietly sighed to myself, Mr. Bear spoke up from where he was standing beside me, watching the guards run by. “A fire in the royal capital? This doesn’t seem like an ordinary situation... I wonder if Raven is okay.”
Hm? Raven? Why bring her up all of a sudden? Oh, right. She said she was staying near the palace to learn magic. God damn it.

I had been fine up to this point but the second that realization hit me, my heart began to pound. An ominous feeling instantly welled up inside of me. These premonitions were never wrong, which just added to my anxiety levels.
“I hope it ends up being a simple fire—”
“Abman, I’m going to go.”
When I got up, Mr. Bear stopped me. “Where are you going in the middle of all this? Yandel, listen to me. It’s best to stay home at times like these.”
“Don’t worry. I’ll find her soon and bring her back.”
“Then I’ll go with y—”
“What are you talking about? You should stay with your wife.”

I told Mr. Bear to close up shop and head to my place with his wife, since Missha would be worried about me too, and I figured I should give her a heads-up. It would put me at ease to have everyone together too.
“...Be careful.”

Afterward, I parted ways with Mr. Bear and got on the roof of the military carriage heading to Karnon, the royal capital. The soldiers riding below kicked up a fuss, but when I revealed my identity, everyone quieted down.
After what felt like hours, the carriage finally arrived at its destination. “Baronet Yandel! We will be arriving in Karnon soon!”

Without realizing it, I stiffened. Even in the middle of the night, the sky was red. The tall, pristine castle walls were stained with black soot, and the surroundings were cloaked in an acrid, fog-like smoke. Beyond the hot flames, or perhaps outside the flames’ reach, wails and screams overlapped.
Jesus Christ, what the hell happened?
Karnon, the city of nobles, was in flames.

chapters.title: Chapter 253: Open World (2)
paragraphs: Fierce flames rose around the wall of mana. There were screams and wails of grief for those who had been lost. Watching all of this with blank eyes, Nebarce Greenhope thought to himself, Where... did it all go wrong?

The answer wouldn’t be found out here. The one at the heart of it all was the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos, who had kidnapped the high priest against Noark’s advice and treated him like a slave, and whose evil deeds had led the palace to draw their swords when they were revealed to the world.
...Was it me?
Nebarce accepted the blame. What was the use of turning to the past to escape the present? In the end, even the former lord of Noark’s castle, the one who took Orcules in, should be held accountable.
“How about it? Did everything turn out the way you wanted?”
That was why he accepted that he was to blame for what was happening today.
“Stay close.” Nebarce ran tirelessly so as not to fall behind and out of range of the sphere of mana. In front of him stood an elderly man who was casting a hovering spell as easy as breathing.

This was Belbev Ruingenes, the old man who had gained the moniker of the Fallen Scholar in his later years, a wizard who had longed for knowledge his entire life and had driven countless people to ruin in his pursuit of it. After hearing from Amelia that there was nothing they could do, it fell to Nebarce to go seek the wizard despite his displeasure. Because back then, he’d had a powerful conviction.
It was a great cause.

The palace was in the wrong. They had to be brought down and a new world had to begin, one where the people above and belowground were united. That was the right thing to do. At least, that should have been the case.
“I-It’s hot...”
“Please, save me. I can pay you whatever you want...”

People were burning alive and dropping like flies. Each time one did, the beliefs that had made Nebarce into the man he was today slowly crumbled. Was this really the right thing to do? To trample over those who didn’t even have the strength to defend themselves for the sake of a great cause? Was this really the path to a new world?
Nebarce finally couldn’t take it any longer and opened his mouth. “Stop...”

Only then did the old man stop and glance back, frowning like Nebarce had just said something strange. “Stop? I also came here hoping to avoid destroying the balance of power, but you were the one who requested my help in the first place. If we stop now, the army headed for Noark will never turn back.”
He was right. “But... I didn’t ask for this.”
“Really? Then what did you want to happen?”
He was rendered speechless. What had he expected after seeking out the Fallen Scholar, who was the greatest villain of this era?

“This is an opportunity that will never come again. Even I didn’t expect that man to appear. I don’t understand what the problem is. As long as he is drawing attention toward the palace, we won’t be in danger.”
“You think I’m saying this because I fear for my life? I just... I just...!” Nebarce couldn’t finish his sentence.

Then, apparently finding this conversation to be a waste of time, the old man mercilessly turned back around and began walking forward. “You look like you’re having a hard time.” Even at that moment, hundreds of flames were flying indiscriminately from his hands with the sole purpose of destruction, dyeing the city red. “Throw away your emotions and think only about your goal. That’s better than losing both.”
It was an extremely calculated, wizard-like remark.
Whoosh!
The bubble of mana followed the old man and before long, Nebarce felt a scorching heat begin to sear his skin. He picked up his frozen feet and continued walking. Each step was full of questions.
“M-Mom... I-I c-can’t b-breathe...”
“It’s okay, baby... Momma is right here. To the end.”
What would be at the end of this road?
Rain fell that night. It was the achievement of the wizards of the Magic Tower.
Chwaaa!

The guards who came from all over the city to provide support weren’t resting, either. A long line had formed in front of the well. They were passing buckets tirelessly down the line and throwing them toward the flames. And it wasn’t just the guards.
“If you’re tired, don’t be stubborn and step back! Being pigheaded will only do more harm than good!”

Joining them were adventurers who lived nearby and civilians who had heard the news and rolled up their sleeves to see if they could be of any help. People came together to overcome the calamity in front of them.
“My goodness, my house is going to catch fire at this rate!”
“Hey, bro, are you seriously saying that right now? There are people with families in there right now!”
“If you two have the strength to bicker, pass down a bucket!”
Of course, not everyone was helping out with noble intent. Like me.
Raven.

When I actually arrived at Karnon, the situation was bleak. The fire was on a whole other level from several modern-day factories burning down. I wondered if Raven was holding up all right. Or if maybe...
Maybe what?
I slammed my fist into my chin to wake myself up.
Smack!

A healthy mind dwelling in a beat-up body. There was no time to worry. Raven was a wizard, after all. With her personality, she’d be holding out well right about now and even taking care of the people around her. Yeah, with luck, she might even have decided to stop by the Magic Tower tonight and avoided this whole mess entirely.
“Hey, wizard.” I approached a wizard who was helping to suppress the fire and revealed my identity.

Even though I’d bothered him at a busy time, the look in his eyes was friendly. “‘Hey, wizard?’ It’s been a long time since someone’s talked to me that way. Haha!” Aside from my noble title, it seemed I’d made a good impression. “So, what does Bjorn Yandel need from a wizard?”
“Can you cast Cold Blood?”
“Is there any wizard who can’t?” At my request, the wizard chuckled and cast the spell on me.
[Your Flame Resistance has significantly increased.]
Whew, it was less hot now.
“Are you thinking of going in there?”
“I have a teammate inside.”
The wizard who cast the spell on me nodded and chuckled. “But will you be all right with just that?”
Huh? What is this? Is he mocking me?
The thought came to mind, but I was left ashamed by what he did next.
Click.

The wizard took out a message stone and asked someone for a favor. “Ah, ah, can you all hear me? Sorry to bother you while you’re all busy, but I want to ask a favor. A man called Bjorn Yandel, who you’ve probably all heard of, says he needs to go into the fire to save his teammate. If any of you have an item or potion that can help with fire resistance, please send it to the coordinates of my personal lab. I’ll summon it out here.”
What was this, a wizard group chat? This was an unexpected stroke of luck so I kept my mouth shut and just waited. Before long, replies rolled in one by one.
“Bjorn Yandel has a noble title so his credit shouldn’t be a problem. But still, I’m going to charge you for any damages, just so you know.” The first to speak was a stern-sounding old man.
“All right. Most of my disciples have gone to Karnon to offer support, but I’ll ask anyone still here and send everything that matches your description,” said the voice of a young woman.
“My dear disciple came home alive thanks to him. I’m going to send a scroll along, but tell him he doesn’t have to pay for it.” This man sounded benevolent.

“Bjorn Yandel... it’s not a bad idea to have him indebted to me at this juncture. If he’s not next to you listening to this, tell him this for me: the Fire Dragon’s Ring was sent by the School of Ioni. Don’t forget that,” said someone with a calculating tone.
One of the voices was even familiar. “Aru? Is that the teammate you’re referring to?”
That voice is... Old Man?
If I was remembering right, the one who had just spoken was called Old Man, the Master of the Great School of Altemion and also Raven’s teacher.
“Hmm, that seems to be right. He is nodding.”
“I will send everything I have right now.”
With that, the transmissions all ended. To be honest, I was dumbfounded.
What just happened?

All I had done was strike up a conversation with an easygoing-looking wizard to get Cold Blood cast on me. But I could now see that this was no ordinary wizard. The people in his group chat each sounded like the head of a different school and I knew for a fact Old Man, who was the Master of Altemion, was in it.
That means this guy is no ordinary wizard, either.
“Who are you?” I asked out of pure curiosity.
I guessed he’d never intended to hide his identity as he introduced himself with a smile. “Oh, come to think of it, I didn’t say. My name is Leven Arfegan.”

It was my first time hearing the name, but I had heard of the school of magic he subsequently mentioned. It was a school belonging to the middle ranks of the Magic Tower. To think the master of that school would be this young.
“I will make sure to repay this debt someday.”
“If that will put you at ease.”
A few minutes later, we heard word through the message stone that the items had been delivered, and Leven Arfegan used magic to summon all the items to this spot.
That really is the Fire Dragon’s Ring.
Starting with a high-ranking Numbers Item, there were various rare items. As I looked through them one by one, I felt a strange feeling well up inside of me.
“Luck was on my side.”

To be honest, good luck wasn’t enough to explain it. What were the chances that the wizard I had happened to speak to was the head of a school of magic and would be kind enough to use his personal group chat to help me?
“Luck? That’s not right.”
Huh?

“I’ve never seen those people take direct action to help a stranger. You think something like that can be attributed to luck alone?” When I tilted my head in confusion, Leven smiled. “I don’t know what they saw in you to so readily help you rescue your teammate, but... It’s a testament to your own achievements.”
It was the kind of wordy explanation you’d expect from a wizard, but I could understand what he was getting at. Although it was kind of embarrassing for him to say it to my face.
Swipe.

As I scratched my ash-stained nose out of embarrassment, Leven laughed and patted me on the shoulder with a delicate hand. “So don’t talk about how lucky you are and just do what you have to do. You should hurry and save your teammate.”
Yeah, this was not the time to be sentimental. “Thanks.” After thanking him sincerely, I activated or put on the summoned items.
[You have consumed Lye of Eternity. Your Flame Resistance has temporarily increased by +50.]
[You have consumed Tears of Spirit. All of your Elemental Resistance stats have temporarily increased by +15.]
[You have consumed Pure Flame. Any Flame Damage you take will be reduced by 10% and your Flame Sensitivity has increased by +15.]
First, I drank the doping potions.
Rip.
Then I tore open a scroll.
[You have equipped No. 4819: Lava Shield. Your total Item Level has increased by +985.]
[You have equipped No. 760: Fire Dragon Ring. Your total Item Level has...]
I equipped myself with a triple-digit numbered item and various fire-specific magical artifacts.
Whoosh!
The air no longer felt hot. As a test, I reached my hand out toward the flames and found it felt the same.
“It’s cool,” I said unwittingly. Of course, this was a sentiment a non-Korean like Leven could never understand.
“Hmm, no matter how high your Flame Tolerance rises, you shouldn’t physically feel cold...”

“I was just talking about how it felt.” I brushed that aside before he could get into magical theory with me and stared into the flames, which showed no signs of diminishing. I asked Leven one thing. “What did you see in me?”
Leven said earlier that he wasn’t sure what, but the others had seen something in me, which was why they were willing to help. So what did he see?
His answer was something completely unexpected. “It was the rumors.”
“Rumors?”

“Rumors I’ve heard about you. I only saw you for the first time today, but I knew as soon as I met your eyes that it was all true.” It was an ambiguous response with a lot of room for interpretation. Just as I was about to ask for a more detailed explanation, Leven gave me a shove with his noodle arms. “...Your body is like iron.” He let out an embarrassed laugh at the way I didn’t budge at all and then asked me for a favor. “Oh, come to think of it, I didn’t ask earlier. If you have strength left after saving your teammate, please save the others as well.”
That wasn’t a particularly difficult request. Okay, got it. “I will try my best.”
“The fact that you’re the one saying that makes me believe it. Anyway, I won’t keep you here any longer. Go ahead.”
Soon, I finished my preparations by activating the Orb of Fire I acquired months ago.
[You have activated the Orb of Fire. All Flame-type damage within a radius of 15 yards will be reduced by 50%.]
This was Barbarian Firefighter Mode.
“Behelaaah!”
Charge.

chapters.title: Chapter 254: Open World (3)
paragraphs: Huff, huff.
I ran through the flames, inhaling smoky air through my nose.
Boom! Boom!

I sprinted through the rubble of a building that couldn’t take the fire and collapsed. Oh, the reason my footsteps sounded like this was simple. I’d turned on Giantization to raise my Flame Resistance if only a little bit.
How far in have I gotten?

I tried to somehow figure out where I was while running, but I couldn’t know for sure. The palace, which always served as a way to measure distance whenever I came to this part of the city, was invisible because of the smoke. All I could do was keep running.
Whoosh!
Anyway, in the hour I spent running around, I learned two things.
Whooosh!

First, no matter how I looked at it, these flames tearing through the city couldn’t have been caused by a simple spark. Flames that didn’t stop at just spreading and continued to explode at regular intervals?
It must be magic.
Kwaaaaaang!

I stopped that thought in its tracks and quickly moved my shield in the direction of the explosion—a red shield with an entirely different price tag than the shield I’d temporarily borrowed from the knights after hearing about the assassin.
[The Lava Shield has absorbed the flames. Your Soul Power is restored in proportion to the amount absorbed.]
No. 4819: Lava Shield. I brought it along because it came with a passive +30 Flame Resistance bonus when equipped, but it was really coming in handy now.
Ha, it would have been a big problem if I came in with nothing.

In life, it was always better to be safe than sorry. Since this was an item that only reacted to attack skills and magic, I thought the Soul Power part of its abilities would be useless. But without this, I would’ve had to save my energy and conserve Giantization for later.

The second thing I realized was that everywhere I went, things were quiet. Buildings were collapsing and the sounds of flames roaring and burning down the city filled my ears, but I encountered no survivors. Not a single scream was heard, let alone a call for help.
...Still, what’s fortunate is there aren’t many corpses.

The corpses I encountered were all lying face down and pointing in the opposite direction I was. They had fled further into the capitol to escape the fire, which had started from the outskirts because the palace was there too.
I hope Raven got there safely...

While I hoped she had escaped this catastrophe, I continued to run through the flames because that might not have been the case. According to what the guard had told me, the entirety of Karnon’s southern neighborhood was engulfed in flames. Raven’s inn was in the very center of South Karnon.
It should be somewhere about here...
Tap.
I stopped in my tracks. In front of me was a stone structure covered in hazy smoke.
Banggg!

I was injured all over by the explosions going off even now, but because it was such a big building, it wasn’t hard to recognize it as the Third Public Platform of the royal capital of Karnon. I quickly glanced around and was left dazed.
God damn it.
The address Raven gave me was right around here, but of course, I didn’t know the exact location. But what did that matter? No matter where I looked—north, east, south, west—nothing was intact.
I tried holding my breath to focus on the sounds around me as well, but I still heard nothing but the goddamn fire. What happened to Raven? Had she managed to escape like I’d been hoping?
“Arua Raven!”

Just in case, I screamed as loud as I could, figuring that someone in the area may have been waiting for help. But despite several calls, there was no response. I was just about to keep moving toward the palace when a voice rang out in my head.
“...Mr. Yandel?”
Secret Voice was a basic spell that all wizards could do.
“What? What are you doing here, Mr. Yandel?”
So she really was nearby. What would have happened if I’d left like I was planning to? Feeling dizzy, I hurriedly cried out, “Where are you?!”
“Come a little further down the road on the other side of the platform. Then you should be able to see me.”
When I followed Raven’s instructions, a plaza appeared. Raven was by the fountain in the center with ten survivors.
Slide.
When I stepped into the sphere of mana keeping the fire at bay, I could see Raven’s small form standing proud. “Why on earth are you here, Mr. Yandel?”
Um, can’t you give me a little welcome?
It seemed reality was different from the movies after all. Normally in the movies, they came running in for a hug.
“Did you... come all this way for me? Through that fire?”
You wish.

“I was on a walk,” I blurted, feeling embarrassed for some reason. I was really glad that she was safe. “But why are you still here and not near the palace? If there is a fire, you should run away immediately. Have you lost your mind?”
After joining Raven, I first stopped to hear her side of the story. Why was she still here near her house and not the palace? The reason was really simple.

“Well...” Raven had been testing her newly acquired knowledge in the temporary lab she had set up in her inn. That was why she didn’t hear about the fire in time when it broke out. “It’s convenient being near the platform, but it tends to be noisy. I usually block out that noise, so...”
By the time Raven noticed the change, the surrounding area was already covered in flames, but it hadn’t been as late then as it was now. She could have gotten out.
“If I just left then, everyone would have died.”

However, the moment Raven saw a woman lying on the street with a child in her arms, she decided to stay there. She may have been a fan of cold logic, but she tended to stick to her morals as much as she could. She had probably been unconcerned at the time, assuming that the fire would be extinguished soon with just a bit of patience. She probably hadn’t expected the situation to turn this serious.
“...Let me apologize first. I never dreamed you would come looking for me, Mr. Yandel.”
I told you I was on a walk.
“Don’t apologize.” This tiny thing was pretending to be an adult. “Well done.”
“...Pardon?”
I glanced around at the survivors gazing at us with anxious eyes and said, “You have to save whoever you can.”
No matter how I looked at it, these people didn’t just look like NPCs to me. They were people, same as me—even if people like them called people like me evil spirits.
But looks like there are no nobles.

Taking a quick look around, I realized that most of them looked like ordinary lower-middle-class citizens. That made sense. After all, even if this was the royal capital, 90 percent of the population of Karnon were commoners, people who lived and worked here to make the lives of nobles easier.
“But where did you get that equipment from?” As the situation began to sort itself out, Raven questioned my firefighter equipment and Lava Shield.
Was it because she was a wizard? Even in the middle of all this chaos, her curiosity came first. I briefly filled her in on the source of my equipment.
The look in Raven’s eyes grew strange. “That’s unbelievable. Master I understand, but the others are not the type of people to do that.”
“You can say that even though I didn’t tell you who exactly I was talking about?”
“To an extent. The wizard community seems big, but it’s small enough that everyone knows each other.”
Oh, I see. But since we can’t stand around talking about this forever, let’s change the subject.
“So how’s this barrier of yours? Can you keep it up while moving?”
When I got down to business, Raven’s expression also shifted, growing serious. “I can. Although it’ll be much weaker.”
“So, what’s your opinion? You think you can hold it?”
“You’re using the Orb of Fire, right? If I use Cold Blood here, I think I’ll be able to hold out.”
“And you’re good on mana?”

“...I’ll have to try it to find out.” Raven, like any proper wizard, didn’t offer false assurances willy-nilly. Simply put, that meant this could go either way, but neither of us mentioned abandoning anyone.

“Did you all hear that? We’re going to get moving so if you have any objections, please tell me now.” Raven explained the plan to the survivors once again, and there were naturally no objections. “Then let’s go.”
Once Raven finished transforming the barrier into its mobile form, we stepped into the fire.
“How is everyone? Doing okay?”
“I-It’s bearable, Ms. Wizard.”

The survivors were sweating profusely but the air within the barrier wasn’t hot enough to burn. They appeared to be having difficulty breathing because of the smoke, but Raven periodically used wind magic to push the smoke away and replenish our oxygen.
“Stay close so that you don’t fall behind.”
The radius of the Orb of Fire was fifteen yards. Adjusting our speed to make sure the survivors didn’t fall out of that range, we started at a canter.
Banggg!
I blocked the explosions in front and Raven was in charge of the back.
“Mana?”
“Still plenty, don’t worry.”
Aside from the fact that Raven’s mana was being consumed in real-time, we were moving at a fairly steady pace. After traveling for a long stretch, we got our first bit of good news in a while.
“The flames have definitely gone down.”
“Does that mean we’ll be able to get out of here soon?”
“If my predictions are correct.”
Even the survivors, who had reached their physical limits, showed surprising tenacity now that they had hope fueling them. But where there was good news, bad news was sure to follow.
“Mana ahead!” Raven suddenly exclaimed, urgently cutting through our conversation. In response, I hurriedly faced forward. And at that moment—
God damn it.
A huge fireball appeared in front of me. I reflexively raised my shield to block it.
[You’ve exceeded your single absorption limit. Your Soul Power is consumed in proportion to the amount absorbed.]
In sharp contrast to the boost the shield had been giving me thus far, I felt a huge amount of energy drain right out of me.
Shit. A Fire-attribute attack that can’t be blocked with a Lava Shield? What kind of bastard...?
I raised my head. The first thing I saw was the ruins of buildings floating in the air.
Crumble...
The flaming chunks of stone were packed densely together and were turning into the shapes of golems.
Raven’s distraught voice rang out behind me. “Mr. Yandel. This spell is—”
“Stop, you don’t have to tell me. I know.”
It was the rank-five summon spell, Fire Giant. A spell I remembered seeing once before.
...No wonder the fire was strangely hot.
I gripped the mace tighter and continued to stare straight ahead.
Step, step.
I couldn’t hear the sound of footsteps, but an old man with another man following behind him soon appeared through the flames.
“I never thought I’d see you here.” The old man stopped walking and said, “Luck is on my side.”
Yeah, there was no way things could go this smoothly. The Fallen Scholar, Belbev Ruingenes.
To think I’d run into him here.
Already, a corner of my heart felt tight, but this at least told me one thing.
So it really was those bastards from Noark.
These guys were the culprits behind the fire. Well, it made sense when you thought about it. Who else would wreak havoc in the city like this?
“Raven.” I set that all aside for now and gave orders. “You take the people outside. Since you said we’re almost there, you can do that without me, right?”
Oh, you and your smart mouth.
“Do as I say. When have I ever been wrong?”
The answer came after a moment of silence, not with her physical voice but in the form of a Secret Voice transmission. “...I’ll bring help here as fast as I can.”

Afterward, Raven used a wind spell to push the flames away, creating a path and leading the survivors through it. Surprisingly, Fallen Scholar let her be. I was prepared to stop him as soon as he tried something funny.
Yeah, it’ll be easier for you to deal with me without a wizard, eh?
I could roughly guess what he was thinking. Not that it didn’t seem out of character anyway, but I figured there was no reason he would let them go so easily if not that.
“When?”
Huh?
“I heard you were in the palace. When did you get here?”
What the hell was he talking about now? Before I could even tilt my head, the answer appeared before my eyes.
“Just now.” A man in his twenties emerged from the flames like he had been there from the start. “Hey, Dentures.”
“...Dentures?” I asked.
Baekho furrowed his brow at Fallen Scholar. “Who said you could set a fire without my permission?”

chapters.title: Chapter 255: Open World (4)
paragraphs: Adventurers aged much faster than normal people. That was because the higher up in the labyrinth you went, the more time you spent in there. On the upper floors, a single quest could last half a year.
But why is he so young?

That question suddenly popped into my head at the appearance of the platinum-haired man with pomade-style hair, but before long, I swallowed it down. Rather than wasting my time wondering about the secret to his youthful looks, there was information I needed to sort out first.
“I heard you were in the palace. When did you get here?”
While the city was on fire, Baekho had been in the palace.
“Who said you could set a fire without my permission?”
The Fallen Scholar really had been the one to set the fire...
“You wanna die?”
And Baekho was furious about it. But why?

Even the Fallen Scholar, the target of his wrath, frowned like he had no idea what was going on. “I don’t understand. Why are you being hostile toward me? I must have made things a lot easier for you tonight.”
“Easier? Yeah, right. It’s not like that bastard of a king will come outside just because you’re burning this place down.”
“Oh, so the king really was your target?” Fallen Scholar’s eyes twinkled at Baekho’s answer. Even at a time like this, he was baiting him.

“What? The king is my target?” Baekho scoffed like the very idea was pathetic. “You really don’t know anything, Grandpa. Well, whatever. I can’t be bothered to explain.” Baekho waved his hand dismissively like he was batting away an annoying fly.
“...You are more disrespectful than I heard.” I guessed this was his first time being on the receiving end of this kind of treatment because Fallen Scholar couldn’t hide his displeasure.

Of course, Baekho didn’t even bat an eye. “Yeah, yeah, the disrespectful one here is you, you naggy, rancid-smelling grouch. Honestly, buy a new pair of dentures or something. I can smell something rotten from all the way over here.”

“W-What did you say...?” Fallen Scholar took an uppercut for one clapback. “You shameless...” Judging by that quivering beard and rave review, it looked like the winner of this fight had already been decided. Well, I couldn’t imagine a world where this old man could beat Baekho Lee, who carried with him the spirit of a K-Gamer, in a war of words.

“Now, let’s get down to business.” Baekho ignored Fallen Scholar’s irritation and got to the point. “So, how are you going to take responsibility? My favorite beef soup restaurant. It’s burned down because of you.”
That was the real reason why this guy had charged over here in a rage.
“B-Beef soup...?” Fallen Scholar stared at him uncomprehendingly, but Baekho continued to vent his anger anyway.
“He may have been an NPC, but he made it perfectly just based on my description. Ha... He was going to make me kimchi next time too...”
“...Was there an alchemist workshop in Karnon?”
“Screw alchemy.” Baekho spat on the floor like a delinquent. “This is why I can’t talk to fucking NPCs. Hansu would have gotten mad with me.”
I flinched when my name suddenly came up out of nowhere, but I probably would have gotten angry alongside him. To think there was a place in this city where they made beef soup!
If a place like that existed this whole time, you should have told me earlier! I didn’t even get to try it!
Anger welled up in me toward both of them. Of course, there was nothing I could do about it except pretend to be a barbarian who didn’t know anything and keep watching.

“So, what do you want? I don’t want to make an enemy of you. If this incident has caused damage to your workshop, I will compensate you.” Fallen Scholar attempted to negotiate. It was a rather surprising sight. The demon who set fire to the entire southern part of Karnon trying to solve an issue with diplomacy? Just how infamous was Baekho that this old man was acting like this? I couldn’t be sure, but I knew one thing for certain.

“Take out your dentures. You said you’ll compensate me, right? Well, if you’re really sorry, pull out those nasty-smelling dentures with your own hands. Then I’ll let it go.” When he was your enemy, Baekho was trickier than anyone else, but as an ally, he really was a reliable guy.
“...I don’t know how you came to this misunderstanding but these aren’t dentures—”
“Bullshit.” As if to announce the collapse of the negotiation, Baekho took a step forward and said something that no one here could understand. “Then what is this?”
Just a second was enough.
Dash.
I heard the light tap of feet kicking off the ground and between one instant and the next, Baekho’s body disappeared.
Whip.

I couldn’t tell how high his Agility was, but what I could confirm with my powers of perception were short, fleeting flashes of movement: Baekho clenching his fists, Fallen Scholar’s stunned expression, a veil of mana falling between the two.
Shaaaaaa!

It was a combo of Danger Detection Assistance and Protective Shield, an essential sequence of moves for wizards trying to survive in this roguelike universe. Judging by the purple color of the shield, its mana density was basically maxed out. It was strong enough to withstand even an Ogre’s punch.
Crackkk!
But it couldn’t withstand Baekho’s fist.

Soon, the veil of mana shattered like shards of glass. As if to offset that, the blue energy on Baekho’s knuckles also lost its light. Not that this was some grand achievement on Fallen Scholar’s part, because bare fists proved to be more than enough.
Smack!
The split-second exchange ended, and Baekho’s fist cracked against Fallen Scholar’s jaw. I saw a flash of something white stained with blood.
“See, you were lying.” Baekho snatched it from the air and tutted. “If they’re not dentures, why do they fall out?”
Yeah, no matter how I looked at it, this guy was unhinged.
“Do you really intend on giving up here?” he asked.
Fallen Scholar, who had taken a hit, got up surprisingly quickly. Without any emotion, he glanced at Baekho. “If I want to keep going, this won’t prevent me from doing so.”

“Wow, I’ve never heard a wizard say something like that in close combat.” Baekho laughed as if Fallen Scholar had just said something hilarious, but apart from that, he didn’t seem to be looking down on his opponent. That was because Baekho was injured just the same.
Why is he injured?

I couldn’t figure that out yet. After the Danger Detection safeguard was broken, Fallen Scholar had used an additional safeguard and Baekho had broken even that with his bare fists before punching his teeth out. Those were all the moves I saw exchanged.
Spit.
Baekho spat bloody saliva on the floor and asked, “What was that at the end?”
“It was a simple curse spell.”
“There’s no way I was cursed.”
“You should be familiar with the trick. Our bodies touched temporarily. I connected the circuit then and completed the spell using your body as a medium.”

“Oh, so that’s why my Mana Resistance didn’t work.” Baekho nodded in understanding. Now that I thought about it, it seemed most pro wizards from this world knew how to use this trick. Ha, there hadn’t been an overpowered ability like that in the game. “But that doesn’t make sense, either. You did that in that brief moment? The other guys all take at least a few seconds to connect.”
“I’m the one who created this technique. I should at least be able to do this much.”
“Ha, so you’re the one who made that damn skill?” Baekho narrowed his eyes at the Fallen Scholar, acknowledging his opponent’s abilities.
The same went for Fallen Scholar. “I know your situation. I also have a guess as to why you ended your affiliation with the palace.”
“So?”
“Since we’ve met here, I’ll make you an attractive proposal.”

“What is it? Tell me,” Baekho demanded, apparently intrigued. It seemed this was more entertaining to him than seeking revenge for the beef soup restaurant. The vibe here was getting weird so I quietly took a step back.
Fallen Scholar’s gaze shifted to me. “Why don’t we finish that man off first before we converse?”
Uh, I didn’t expect that... God damn it.

My heart pounded. My life would already be hanging by a thread facing Fallen Scholar alone, but if Baekho decided to back him up, there would be nothing I could do other than reveal that I was Hansu Lee and appeal to his nostalgia.

“That’s not an option.” I already had the worst-case scenario in mind, but thankfully Baekho rejected Fallen Scholar’s proposal. Was it because he knew I was a player? No, it wasn’t some kind of emotional reason like that he couldn’t bear to watch me die. “Then it’ll seem like I’m following your orders.”

It was simply a matter of asserting dominance. But I guessed Fallen Scholar must have found Baekho’s attitude frustrating because he spoke like he was addressing an unruly child. “That man is a nobleman.”
“So?”
“As long as you are at odds with the palace, he is a potential enemy.”
That was a pretty reasonable argument to me too, but thankfully, Baekho didn’t even listen to it. “So what? I can take care of him on my own, so don’t even worry about that.”
It was obvious what the source of his conviction was. He knew I was a player. He was likely confident that no matter how close I got to the palace, he could incapacitate me at any moment.
Does this mean it’s a good thing that he knows my identity...?
“Then... we should relocate.” In the end, even Fallen Scholar couldn’t wear down Baekho’s stubbornness and let go of his selfish desire to kill me. Well, to him, Baekho was more important than me.
“Ah, just warning you in advance, but I’m not getting on a telpor.”
“Telpor...?”
“Teleportation. You take the lead instead. I’ll follow. You can try something funny if you want, but be prepared to die in that case.”
“...Then I’ll head off first.” Soon, Fallen Scholar flew into the air with the servant-like man behind him. It was floatation magic.
“What are you looking at? I’ll follow, so you can go first.”

Fallen Scholar stared at Baekho for a few seconds before disappearing beyond the flames. That took care of one of my problems, but it was too soon to let my guard down. One thing about Baekho was that you could never be sure where he would bounce next.
“Hey.”
“...What?” I didn’t bother trying to hide my fear.
Baekho smirked. “I’m only saving you just this once.” With that parting line, he left.
My mind went blank for some reason.
What, does that mean he didn’t just tell Fallen Scholar not to kill me as a power play? I don’t know, I still don’t know which it is. But if that really is the case... I might be a little touched.
I wiped the ash-stained bridge of my nose with my finger.
“Hm.”
Oh, that bastard. I thought he didn’t do friendship.
Not long after Baekho and Fallen Scholar left, Raven returned. “Mr. Yandel!”
Thanks to the mention of Fallen Scholar, behind Raven was a large battalion of knights and battle mages.
“We came to save y—huh? Why is no one...?”

Raven looked bewildered by the fact that Fallen Scholar was nowhere to be seen. The troops from the palace that had followed her here wore similar expressions. Before any misunderstandings could come about, I quickly explained the situation.
“You mean that the same man who appeared during the assassination incident came and attacked Fallen Scholar?”
“Yes, the two of them suddenly started fighting and disappeared in an instant.”
“Do you know the reason why that man decided to attack Fallen Scholar?”
“No, I’m not sure either!”
The reason why I simplified the situation as much as possible was in case someone interpreted what had happened to mean that Baekho had helped me.
“You were really lucky.” Since the incident involved such formidable individuals, the knights did not doubt the authenticity of my statement.
“Then we should get out of here as soon as possible.”

The troops from the palace stayed behind to search the surrounding area and Raven and I watched them for a while before heading back out. The first to greet us were the survivors who had been evacuated earlier, the ten lives Raven and I had worked so hard to save. Everyone bowed at me with dark, ash-stained faces. Of course, not for long. Ignoring a thank-you wouldn’t kill anyone, right?
“Huh? Where are you going?” When I turned around, the question slipped from Raven’s lips.
To be honest, I was exhausted after what happened earlier and all I wanted to do was rest, but... “I made a promise.”
“...A promise?”
In return for receiving the Fire-attribute equipment and consumables, I told the wizard named Leven Arfegan that I would try to fulfill his request to the best of my abilities.
Raven’s expression went blank, but she didn’t stop or scold me or tell me that what I was doing was pointless. “Be careful. I will be helping people here.”
What, let’s each do our best in our roles?
I looked Raven up and down in a show of respect and then stepped back into the fire. Twelve hours later, a deluge of rain poured in, and the fire was finally extinguished.
Shaaaaaa!
A total of seventeen more lives were saved. It was the kind of low number that would never be used as an A-plot in a movie or a comic, but...
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
It was my best.

chapters.title: Chapter 256: Open World (5)
paragraphs: Fallen Scholar’s signature flame spell was as relentless as his reputation implied. Even with countless helpers gathered from all over the city, all they could do was keep the flames from spreading further. In the end, the fire was extinguished only after the masters of seven different schools came together to cast a spell.
Shaaaaaa!
Rain poured down as if a hole had opened up in the sky.

“Woohoo!” Some cheered at the sight of the fire finally losing its strength, others were silently relieved, and others slumped down to the ground like they had no energy left to even shout. For reference, I was in the latter group.
“...Goddamn it.”
It was finally over. My overheated body quickly cooled and the tension in my muscles instantly released. I collapsed on the spot, flopping onto the ground, and immediately regretted it.
“Ha.”

The ground was lukewarm and wet. The ash that had been flying around all night had mixed with the rainwater, turning into a sticky mess. It was a habitat any human would be uncomfortable in. However, I couldn’t be bothered to get up again. How long did I stay like that with my eyes closed?
“Oh, what the heck! I thought you were hurt!” When I opened my eyes, I saw Raven above me. “...But you’re not actually hurt, are you?”
“I’m just exhausted and resting, so don’t talk to me.”
“If you’re going to rest, you should go home and wash up properly—”
“Later.”
“...Okay. Since you worked hard...”
After lying down for a few more minutes, I got up. The water was up to my ears now. The drainage wasn’t very good here.
“...You look like a mess.”
“I don’t think you’re one to talk, Mr. Yandel.”

We made our way to the city’s untouched district with dark lye dripping from us. I could see people here and there. There were those desperately searching for people they’d lost, and those combing through the wreckage for any survivors. Everyone was in a similar state to us.
“What time is it, by the way?”
“It’s almost noon.”
Noon on June 2nd, huh? It was kind of funny. Normally the only people in the city who looked like this at this particular time were adventurers.
“The rain stopped.”
The wizards appeared to have released the spell as the dark clouds that filled the sky broke up and warm rays of light began to shine through.

“Bjorn!” I caught sight of Missha in the distance. Ainar and Erwen were by her side. They must have come here after hearing the news in the middle of the night. Seeing as they were in a similar state as us, it seemed these guys had also been working hard all night to put out the fire. “...You’re not injured, rrright?”
I was worried she would nag me a bit but Missha surprisingly didn’t say anything. It was probably because of the people around her.
“B-Baronet Yandel...!” These were the few survivors I had rescued last night. I was sure she couldn’t bring herself to ask why I did so in front of these people.
“Why are you still hanging around here?” I asked in confusion. “You should all be resting.”
At my question, the survivors hesitantly thanked me and left. What, did they really wait here this whole time just to say those few words?
Then at least don’t be afraid of my noble status.

I chuckled and kept walking. Before long, the eastern district, which hadn’t been swallowed by the fire, appeared. First, I got an inn nearby. We couldn’t take a carriage home looking like this, could we? Plus, it’d take at least a few hours to get home and I just wanted to rest for now.
I wonder how much it costs to stay a night in Karnon...
Since this was the royal capital, I expected it to be much more expensive than the commercial district of Kommelby, but I wasn’t able to learn the price today because our room was free.

“Our manager has instructed us not to accept money from anyone today.” All nearby inns were offering rooms free of charge for citizens and adventurers who had come to fight the fire. “Before you head up, I’ll need you to sign in... Baronet Bjorn Yandel...?!”
“Yes?”
“I’ve heard a lot about you. That you worked the hardest out of everyone today... I want to thank you on behalf of the city.”

I didn’t know if it was because of my title or reputation, but the staff at the counter reserved the biggest remaining room exclusively for me. Apparently, the unit on the other side of the hall was being shared by fifteen people. Because our accommodations included one living room, three bedrooms, and two bathrooms, we could share it comfortably between the five of us.
“Bjorn, you should go ahead and use one of the bathrooms firrrst. We’ll take turns using the other one.”
“Thanks.” I didn’t turn down my team’s generosity and went to the bathroom to wash up. Even though I showered as quickly as I could, it still took about an hour.
I’ll wash and return the equipment I borrowed later...

I gathered the equipment I took off in a corner of the room, lay down on the bed, and closed my eyes. Like you would expect from a hotel in the royal capital of Karnon, the bed was soft. Fatigue set in at once.
Anyway, I wonder how things went in the labyrinth. Did the army win? I’m curious about things on that end too...

Well, I was sure I could look into that tomorrow. That was my last thought before sleep came to me, and by the time I opened my eyes the next day, the royal army that had ventured underground had already returned.
“It’s the army!”
And as a result, my mind was boggled.
What exactly happened down there?
As I stared down at the army marching down the road toward the palace from my window, I couldn’t find any evidence that they’d been in a battle at all.
In an area deep underground that was untouched by the light of day, thousands of people were walking in a line, relying on torches. All were inhabitants of Noark.
“This way.” An unfamiliar old man was at the front of the pack leading the way, and the ruler of the city, the lord of the castle, was following right behind him.
“My Lord, we do not know who this man is. We need to leave now while we can—”
“Watch your mouth. Right now, this man is the only person we can trust.”
“But how could he know a shortcut even we didn’t know about? It’s much too suspicious. This could be a trick from the palace—”

“Stop.” The lord of the castle sternly cut the vassal off. It was understandable that they would be suspicious of the old man, as well as incredibly anxious, but a trick from the palace? That was too much of a leap. If it weren’t for this old man, everyone here would have disappeared along with the city of Noark. “We have no choice. Just trust him,” the lord of the castle muttered, clearly drained as he recalled the events from earlier.

It had been just after midnight when Rafdonia’s troops attacked, right when all of Noark’s troops had left for the labyrinth. The royal army destroyed the barrier that had been protecting the city all this time and began their advance.
“My lord, the royal army has invaded!”
“Take all civilians to the shelter.”

Stunned for only a moment, the lord of the castle gathered everyone remaining in the city and hid in the shelter under the fortress. The shelter had been built by a royal in the distant past to be a refuge that could accommodate thousands of people. At the time, Noark’s castle had functioned as the home of the royal family, back around the same time the witch’s curse brought destruction upon the world. Humanity had come together from all corners of the continent, established a city under the ground and, using a protective barrier, survived there for a long time until they eventually ventured back out onto the surface. That was also the origin of why there was a portal to the labyrinth underground.

For better or for worse, the palace’s troops showed little interest in their shelter. Their reasons were understandable. Once the portal opened at noon, adventurers would come out. The palace’s top priority was to defeat Noark’s adventurers. They would have no issues destroying the shelter afterward.
“Yes, they have set up camp in the square and aren’t making a move. It seems they are waiting for the portal to open.”
“Send word aboveground.”
In the end, the lord of the castle requested support from aboveground, at which point the Fallen Scholar started burning down the royal capital to draw their attention.
Stubborn bastards.

The troops did not retreat to the city. Even their last hope, the Fallen Scholar, lost contact at some point. Time continued to pass in a similar fashion until there were about twenty minutes left before the portal opened and the forces sent into the labyrinth returned.

The lord of the castle commanded his remaining troops with the spirit of a man who had been driven into a corner. At the time, that had been the best he could do. He had no idea how many people would be killed, but this was the only way for at least a few more people to survive.
“Open the gate!”

Just before the hour hand pointed to twelve, the lord of the castle led his troops out of the shelter. Ferociously breaking through the line of soldiers lying in wait for them in front, they headed toward the square. It was even more hopeless in person. Thousands of knights, even more soldiers, and wizards and priests were in position everywhere, but it was already too late to turn back. Soon, blue light gathered in the center of the square and a portal opened, spitting out a stream of adventurers.
“The portal is opening!”
“Prepare yourselves!”
“W-What the hell!?”
“Army! It’s the royal army!”
“Damn it! No wonder no one was inside!”

The adventurers from Noark had been shocked by the troops greeting them upon their return to the city, but the sense of wrongness they’d noticed inside the labyrinth allowed them to quickly get up to speed.
“What are you doing!? Are you going to die like this?”
“Hurry up and take out your knife, you bastard!”
The adventurers immediately took out their weapons and prepared to retaliate, and the lord of the castle led his troops as close to the outskirts as he could. As he did, he gave only one order:
“Run! Aboveground!”
The best plan of action he could come up with was to save his own skin, to save as many people as possible for the sake of the future. But it seemed that got someone’s attention.
Before long, a knight appeared in front of him. The dazzling aura covering the knight’s sword was a testament to his identity.
“So, this is what the head of the insolent insurgents looks like. I’m surprised. You’re more normal-looking than I thought.”
“The Knight of Light...!”
It had been the Commander of the First Royal Guard, Jerome Saintred. Possessing the nickname of Guardian of the Palace, he was a talented knight who was a very significant figure in Rafdonia.
“Don’t worry. You’re not going to die here. I will cut off your limbs just in case and take you with us alive.”
The Knight of Light swung his sword. The lord of the castle, who had only spent a few years as an adventurer in his twenties and had reached the fifth floor, could do nothing more than watch.
Whooom!
