A flash of light marked the sword’s trajectory and stained his vision white. But when the flash died down and he opened his eyes, the lord of the castle found that nothing had happened to him. His arms were moving and his legs were still intact and standing. But how?
Just as the question formed in his mind, the mysterious old man appeared several feet up in the air.
“You still have work to do.”

The battle around him had stopped at some point, and not voluntarily. The Knight of Light still had his sword aimed at the lord of the castle’s neck, but his hands were trembling as he fought against some invisible force. No one in this space seemed to be able to do anything to harm another like it had suddenly become law.
“Then since everyone is here, let’s get going. Fortunately, this thing still works fine.”

When the old man flicked his wrist, a huge, city-sized magic circle etched into the ground began to glow. This was his first time feeling such a powerful mana in his life. As the old man began to murmur, the world around the lord of the castle blurred.
Flash!
When he came to, he was in a dark underground passage, and he wasn’t the only one there. Everyone on Noark’s side who had been in the square was in the passage as well.
“W-What have you done!?”
“Mass Teleportation? But it’s impossible to transport so many people at once...”
Although very few, some knights ended up coming along with them.
“Looks like I made a mistake while trying to move so many people at once. Ah, I didn’t bring them on purpose, so don’t mind me and just kill them.”

Like a man possessed, the lord of the castle had complied with the old man’s suggestion and ordered his people to slaughter the knights. He started following the old man, who just smiled mysteriously at his questions about where they were. Hours passed.

“Are you the person I think you are, sir?” The lord of the castle was jarred from his thoughts by the sound of a man’s voice. Surprisingly, the leader of Orcules was talking to the old man in a respectful tone.
“Well, without questions, there can be no answers.”
“So you’re saying I should think for myself. All right.”

The leader who had torn Noark in half and clashed with them on many occasions meekly bowed his head and withdrew. While that was a strange sight in itself, it further raised the lord of the castle’s suspicions about the old man.
Who is this man?

He even debated asking the leader of Orcules. The moment they were teleported to this place, Orcules’ leader immediately ordered his members to stay put and not do anything rash. That had to be because he knew something.
But there’s no way this man will cough that information up willingly.

Instead of asking the leader about the old man’s identity, the lord of the castle approached the old man himself and actively attempted to engage him in conversation, something he hadn’t been able to do before out of a strange sense of unease. Surprisingly, the old man was very friendly.

“Oh, you mean that teleportation spell? I just borrowed the power of an ancient magic circle that was already in the city, so don’t think so highly of me. The same goes for being able to temporarily stop the battle. That’s just how well-designed Noark is as a city.”
“I had no idea something like that even existed...”
“Haha, it would be strange if you did, so don’t be too hard on yourself. So, are those all your questions?”

The lord of the castle asked the old man whatever came to mind and the old man answered every question he had except for the question of where he was leading them. A long while later, the narrow passage they were in gradually widened and a sloped road appeared up ahead.
“We have arrived.”
“Where are we...?”

As they climbed up a hill, the outside world appeared before them. The lord of the castle could say with conviction that he had never seen something like this before—the shining sunlight, the forest, the flowing stream, the chirping birds, the worms squirming on the moist ground. And above them...
“No walls...?”

The castle walls that should have been visible no matter where they looked were not there. Put simply, that meant they were not inside Rafdonia, which was commonly referred to as the world’s last stronghold.
“W-Where is this place...?” the lord of the castle breathed, turning back to the old man.

Through the sliver of his chin visible under his hood, he could see the old man smiling. “Congratulations. You will now go down in history as the first people to leave the city in thousands of years.”
June 2nd, New World 154: the age of living trapped within the castle walls had finally come to an end, and a new world had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 257: Clan (1)
paragraphs: After the royal army’s return, the people of the city learned that the army was indeed real, and that the reason they were not at Dimension Square was because they had traveled underground for a stealth mission.
What happened?

No one knew how things had gone, and so, speculation ran wild. Conspiracy theories flourished, from ones debating whether they had won or lost, to one claiming that the palace was actually just pretending to fight the underground city. New hypotheses were crafted by the gossip every day.

A few days later, the palace put posters up all over the city. To briefly summarize their contents, it was as follows: our awesome army won, and even conquered Noark. So stop worrying. I couldn’t tell how much of it was legit, but assuming that the posters were to some extent grounded in truth, and compensating for a few holes in the story...
I’m sure of it. There was no battle.
It had been difficult to find evidence of a battle on the knights returning to the palace.
Those bastards from Noark probably escaped.

But where to? The world was blocked in on all sides by walls. The idea that they could be hiding aboveground didn’t make sense either. If that number of people came from aboveground, there would obviously be evidence.
Then that means they are still underground...
“Bjorn! Stop messing around and come move these!”
Yeah, I should just focus on moving. Continuing to worry about it won’t give me an answer. It’s wiser to wait for the opening of the Round Table, since Clown is a member.
And so I ended that train of thought and moved my body.
“Oh, could you put the bed down over there?”

I was currently in an orphanage affiliated with the Church of Reatlas, carrying things around like a mover. It was time for me to start racking up achievements. So, occasionally, when a commission that could be done for the church popped up, I headed there with anyone who was free to complete it.
“Ainar! You thought I wouldn’t notice you sneakily taking a brrreak?!”
“I-I’m not taking a break, I’m playing with the kids!”
“Waaah! She broke my doll! Doll murderer!”
“That’s... I was trying to teach you where the weak points are and accidentally...!”

There was some chaos today as usual, but after an hour or two, the move was complete. And so today’s commission came to an end. Afterward, we had a simple meal at a restaurant near the church, where I learned a strange fact from Missha.
“Did you know? The orrrphanage we went to today is that orphanage.”
“That orphanage?”
“You know. The place Dwalkie spent a small porrrtion of his childhood. The old building that’s scheduled to be demolished tomorrow is that place.”
“...I see.”
“Anyway, I was just saying! I’m leaving now! Oh, and I’m going to be home late today so both of you take care of dinner on your own.”
After eating, we immediately dispersed. Missha left after informing us she had an appointment with one of her old teammates, and Ainar headed for the holy land.
“Hehe, it’s just the two of us now.”
“I have to stop by somewhere, so you head home first.”

Sending away Erwen, who had nothing to do, I headed to the guild alone. The knights who used to shadow me every day were no longer at their posts because they had all left at the end of last month. Apparently, their superior had recalled them.
At the time I didn’t think much of it, but they must have been called back for the raid against Noark.

If everyone in Noark got away safely and were somewhere underground the knights might return, but I decided not to bet on that. Still, having spent a month together, one of the knights had taken a moment to offer me a warning before leaving.
“Please take care of yourself. If more assassins appear, the higher-ups have determined that it is more likely to be the work of a large clan than Noark.”

It seemed even Deer, who had assigned guards to me, thought the assassination attempt was the work of a large clan rather than Noark. I could see why—it had already been a month since Clown had claimed the assassin was coming soon.
“Then shouldn’t you be protecting me more? After all, this means the large clans will be targeting the palace.”
“...You don’t have to worry about that.”

Besides, based on the nuances I could pick up on in my conversation with the knight, it seemed the palace had finished all necessary preparations to stop the large clans without issue, even if they attempted to manipulate public opinion. Which was why they didn’t have to protect me anymore.
Well, part of me feels more comfortable without them around, anyway.

Since I was lost in thought during my walk, I arrived at the Adventurers’ Guild before I knew it. There was no need to take a number like last time. There weren’t a lot of adventurers in the first place now, and...
“Baronet Bjorn Yandel, your identity has been verified. We will guide you to the branch manager’s office.”
Yeah, I should at least enjoy the perks of having a title like this.
“Not the branch manager. I want the district chief.”
The employee asked if I made a prior appointment, but I just bulldozed over that trivial concern with the power of a nobleman.
“Are you guys rebels?” A barbarian on whom words didn’t work mixed with a noble who had no intention of listening to anyone: aka, Barbarian Noblesse Mode.
“...We’ll guide you straight there.”

When we got to the fourth floor, the employee knocked to announce my presence and before long, a loud sigh was heard from inside. As the door swung open, I immediately went in and sat down on the sofa. Then, putting my feet up on the table, I spoke arrogantly. “Greetings.”
The man didn’t respond.
“Go on.”
As soon as the words left my mouth, the district chief, who had been working at his desk, got up and greeted me. “Baronet... Yandel... you’re here...”
Shouldn’t you be used to stuff like this by now?
“Okay, sit down.”

When I gave him permission to sit, only then did the district chief sit down across from me. It had happened several times already, but it was still thrilling every time. Was this what real power tasted like?

“...What business do you have with me today?” The seventh district chief of the Adventurers’ Guild, Niall Urbans, who had had a bad relationship with me from our first meeting, was now speaking to me in a polite tone. Of course, our conversation hadn’t started this way. At first, he tried to use mildly respectful language to put us on the same level, but when I got angry with him and asked if he was insulting me, a nobleman, he ended up settling on this tone.
“I came to check if there are any adventurers who have responded to my recruitment posting.”
“That’s something that the branch manager could handle for you...”
What was this guy saying? I specifically came to the guild headquarters in the Seventh District for him. “Talking back... to a noble?”
“...I will check on that right away.”
“Since there could be a mistake like last time, do it personally. Don’t get someone else to do it.”
“Right...”

The district chief headed down to do as I instructed and I munched on the snacks laid out on the table as I waited. I wasn’t sure how long I had been sitting there when the district chief finally came back holding some papers.
“Here they are.” When I ripped them out of his hands without so much as a thank you and began to read, I found that nothing had changed since my last visit two days ago.
“One more applicant, but they aren’t even all that great.”
“I’m sorry.”

“There’s nothing you need to apologize for.” Showing a rare bit of generosity as his superior, I read through the document again. The number of people who had applied to the teammate recruitment posting I put up a few days ago was exactly thirty-one. It was fewer than I had expected. This was because fewer adventurers wanted to enter the labyrinth these days.
Still, since the clans are so broken up, I thought more would apply than this.

I set my disappointment aside and put the paper down. There were no adventurers on that sheet that I was interested in taking to the interview stage. I hadn’t been able to find the special class that I’d been looking for, either. I guessed all we could do was wait indefinitely.
“Um, but...”
“Don’t waste my time and speak.”
“Is there a specific class you’re looking for?”
“Not really, I just need someone who is capable. Why do you ask?”

“Because I spotted a famous name among the applicants.” The district chief went on to rave about how skilled, loyal, and promising said adventurer was. It seemed like this guy wanted to find me a teammate soon so I’d stop coming here.
“Enough!” I threw the paper on the floor and stormed out of the office. “You just do what I tell you to do!”
No matter how great his resume may have been, to put a Hans on my team? Was this guy out of his mind?

Nearly two weeks had passed since the fire broke out. I could sort what I’d been up to since into a few categories: grinding for achievements at the temple, stopping by the holy land to spar with the chieftain, going around Kommelby to get a feel for the prices, and then heading to the guild every three days to relieve stress by tormenting the district chief. Although my schedule was rather productive, it didn’t yield any immediate results. The value of currency would probably continue to rise for the next while, so I wasn’t making any moves money-wise.
And it looks like it’ll take another two to three months before I have enough achievements to get a priest...

The same went for recruiting a teammate. There was no sign of the special class of adventurer required for the sixth floor appearing anytime soon, and the three other spots I needed to fill to reach ten people were still vacant.
Will we have no choice but to climb it with only six people in the end?

The idea was disheartening. Normally, when a clan was split into two parties or more, the team met up on the fifth floor. This was because when the number of people traveling together exceeded five, the fourth floor ended up taking considerably longer, a painful loss for adventurers who treated time as money.
But there are still a lot of things about the idea of going up in groups of three that make me uneasy. It’ll be much safer to just meet on the second floor.

Of course, it was a bit too early to worry about that. If our return to the labyrinth ended up being delayed a few more months, all of this would be pointless. What was important was when the situation would stabilize again.
There’s a chance I might be able to figure that out today.
It was the 15th, the day when Ghost Busters opened. This morning, I headed to the holy land in preparation for my trip into the community. That was because I couldn’t just go in like usual this time.
GM.
Even the GM suspected me of being an evil spirit now. It was highly likely that the GM would make a move today because that was what I would do if I were him.

Twelve hours spent in the forum was twelve seconds in real life. I’d always thought this, but this brief moment was a huge weakness for community users because you were totally cut off from reality. Since even getting stabbed in the neck with a knife wouldn’t wake you, if someone were to take proper advantage of this twelve-second stretch, they would be able to tell if you were a player or not.
But not going in would be worse.

I decided to enter the community anyway, making the call that after Noark and the palace’s recent encounter, the amount of information I’d be able to get this month would be huge. Besides, the GM’s right-hand man, Soul Queen, had also entered the Round Table as a new recruit last month. If Lion were absent during this meeting, it would be possible for them to connect me and Lion together in the future.
...Is that too much of a leap?

Anyway, the point was this: in life, it was always better to be safe than sorry. I didn’t know for sure whether the GM would aim to check during those twelve seconds, but there was no reason not to be prepared.
“Bjorn, you called for me?”
“Ah, I have a favor to ask of you.”
“Favor?”
“Can you try putting this on your face?”
When I arrived at the holy land, I called over Kharon and handed him the Golden Mask, the hidden item I had obtained in the Bloody Citadel.
“What is this? I like that it’s shiny, but...”
“It’s a magic item that transforms your face for thirty days.”
“Huh? But why are you giving it to me?”
“Because you’re the person whose build is most similar to mine.”
I proceeded to ask Kharon to drink in the city until midnight tomorrow while wearing my face.
“That’s not a difficult request, but why?”
“I have somewhere I need to go tonight that’s a secret from my teammates.”
“...Looks like that beastwoman is not very understanding of you.”
Huh? Why was he bringing her up here? I was confused as to what he was talking about, but I soon realized what he was getting at.
“It is a warrior’s instinct to want offspring. Is that why you came to the holy land today?”
I took this in for a moment before nodding. Now that I thought about it, this seemed like a much better way to keep my secret than the excuse I had prepared.
“Anyway, don’t worry! I will do my best so that even if that beastwoman shows up, she won’t suspect a thing!”
Actually, he would most definitely be found out if she showed up, which was why I had told him to spend all night drinking. “I’ll trust you. You are the wisest warrior here after me, after all.”
“Y-You think that too, huh?! I’m flattered!”
After filling him in on the precautions he should take and his itinerary for the night, I gave Kharon, who had turned into me, my equipment and sent him into the city.
[You have used Golden Mask. Your appearance will change for 30 days.]

I also put the mask on and took it off in order to adopt Kharon’s appearance. That was because my face stood out in the holy land. If there were eyewitness accounts of me being in both places at once, there would be no point in all the effort I went through today.
I should get back to the city too.

Since it would be possible for Kharon’s friends in the holy land to figure out who I was, I quickly put on Kharon’s equipment and left the bushes to return to the city. Then I found a room at a random inn and locked myself in.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn to a different world.]
Whew, I just hope he doesn’t do anything strange while wearing my face...

chapters.title: Chapter 258: Clan (2)
paragraphs: I was inside Hansu Lee’s room once again.

Coming here was beginning to feel a lot like returning to your hometown after moving away. Even though it was all comfortable and familiar, it still felt oddly unfamiliar at the same time—even this room I had once called home.
Click.

First, I joined the community by pressing the power button on the computer console. I waited for a moment for the posts to come up, because there was nothing else to do until the Round Table opened at three o’clock.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 0 people are online.]

Baekho was once again not here. Judging by the way he’d been trying to threaten the GM into undoing his ban, it looked like he was looking for a way to get back somehow, but it seemed that hadn’t happened yet.
He said going home was his ultimate goal...
Remembering the aspirations Baekho had shared with me in the past, I thought about the GM. What was the GM’s goal? Was it to return as well?
...Then why did he ban Baekho? Hmm... I don’t know.
There were things at play here that I didn’t understand or even know about.
Anyway, it’d be nice if all my hard work wasn’t for nothing.

Hoping that the plan to use Kharon as a standin worked to clear me of any suspicion, I made a list of the things I knew about the GM. There wasn’t much. First, he was a wizard. He was also a big fan of Elfnuna, to the point that he used the nickname Elfnunalove on the messaging boards.
No, wait... What would happen if he found out I’m him? Would he help me out?
For a second, I even considered the idea of using this to secure a powerful sponsor, but ultimately, I defaulted to my previous approach.
Absolutely not.

This was in line with the way that I’d tried my best not to reveal my identity to Baekho until the end. I didn’t know what the GM’s intentions were, not to mention the GM had even sent a community invite pill to Bjorn Yandel once before. Put simply, that meant that even if it had been with good intentions, he had invited me to this community on the off chance I was a player, which meant I had to go to great lengths to protect myself. No one knew how interpersonal relationships could turn out. When it came to some people, the act of revealing I was an evil spirit was tantamount to giving them a noose with my neck already in the loop. I’d seen some examples of ways things could go wrong with my own eyes too.
“Fine, if that’s what you want, I’ll expose you myself. Hans Chrisen is an evil spirit!”
If the same thing that happened to Hans G happened to me, what choice would I make then? Could I avoid being forced into making a choice like that?
Click, click.

I emptied my head and moved my mouse. Since it’d already been a few minutes, several posts were popping up on different bulletin boards. I spent time surfing through them. Soon, about thirty minutes had passed since the community had opened, and a new post appeared.
[I’m from Noark and I have something to tell you guys.]
The post began as follows:

I thought this over a lot, worried that I might get banned for being from Noark, but I’m making this post because everyone needs to know regardless of whether they live aboveground or underground. We are outside right now. Not inside the walls, but the real outside world.
Its shocking contents contradicted the very foundations of this world.

I’m sure you guys are thinking this makes no sense, but it’s true. We escaped the palace’s forces and got out, and we’re still alive and well. To be honest, I don’t know if the witch’s curse disappeared over time or if there was no such thing from the beginning, but one thing’s clear. The outside world is perfectly fine. Plants are growing and if you get close to them, you can see bugs eating grass. Same with wild animals.

The poster then devoted many words to describing what the outside world was like, and then documented what had happened in a journal-like fashion. I slowly read through the entirety of that long text. My first impression was that it didn’t seem like a simple joke.
This can’t just be someone spewing bullshit to try and troll people...
After all, no one would take the risk of getting banned just to make a joke like this. Still, the comment section went wild.
Brutalizer X: Here is the attention you were begging for.
arolf5205: I was wondering what this post was but I just read the beginning and immediately came down here. Surely no one is stupid enough to believe this?
I started with the comments at the top dismissing the post as lies made up by an attention whore.
ryanzeus31: But if this is real, isn’t the palace fucked? If there really is a world outside where people can live without mana stones then there’s no way this goddamned city can compete.
└furryking1955: Maybe that’s why they hid it. No way they didn’t know about this.
Those who believed in what the poster was saying even a bit were concerned about what this meant for the future.
Gareth: Wow, I was wondering where that old man appeared and disappeared to. He went outside?
Others left comments as if they knew something.
└NIKAMOTO: Old man? Who are you talking about? Respectfully, please share your information.
└Gareth: We were waiting in front of the portal to cut down all those fuckers from Noark as soon as they came out but an old man suddenly appeared and teleported them all away.
└Kni8htofroom: If you’re going to lie, at least put some effort into it. How could someone move all those people with Mass Teleport?

└Gareth: I don’t know. And I don’t want to bother trying to convince you. Anyway, what do I do now? Ugh, I thought the palace would be more comfortable and chose the knight route. Is the palace ruined now?
Starting with this comment, public opinion slowly shifted toward the sentiment that the post was true. Soldiers who participated in the attack on the palace’s side began to testify one by one.
└amulet: It might be hard to believe, but they really did escape via teleportation. I was there too so I can confirm it.
└kongkong2: This person has been exclusively posting from a knight’s perspective for a few years now. Does that mean all of this is real?
The post was designated as trending and witnesses from the palace’s side poured in, and even some people from Noark made an appearance.
EXBlunt: Wow, the fresh air is nice. Are we the winners here for going underground all those years ago?
xxfblz: Yeah, we can live good lives without mana stones. You guys have fun slaving away for taxes.

I started to get confused too. I had already thought it plausible that the outside world was fine. In fact, I had gotten the sense that something was off seeing the guards standing on top of the castle walls. But there was something about this that I couldn’t understand.
Why are they telling us this?
It wasn’t strange to have someone from Noark post in the community, but why was this person sharing what was going on? Because they thought it was their duty as a player?
No, that can’t be it.

If that really were the case, I wouldn’t have ended up stuck on the first floor just a few weeks ago, knocking on death’s door as I cleared the way for hundreds of others. These guys had been utterly silent then. They didn’t disclose Noark’s plan for a surprise attack even as a joke, and as a result, most of the adventurers aboveground were killed. And a good chunk of them were obviously players.
...Then it would make sense to assume that they were ordered to do this by Noark.
They had a good enough motive for that too. If they lied about escaping outside, that would help them evade the palace’s attempts to track them down.
But if the outside world weren’t fine, the palace wouldn’t fall for the lie anyway.
Immediately confronted with a contradiction, I let out a big sigh.
Ugh, just what is going on?
Eventually, I couldn’t stand it and left a comment.
Elfnunna: I have one question for the people of Noark. If the outside world is truly fine and you guys are there right now, why are you revealing that here? When you’ve been quiet all this time?
Before long, a notification dinged, signaling someone had replied.
└FIREWORK: Woah, are you really Elfnuna? I’m building a fire-type archer. Please give me some advice.
└bigfisher: You really fell for that huh. It’s Elfnunna, not Elfnuna.
└Bling0_0: But it could be the real one. I heard the original nickname was taken by someone at the beginning and can’t be used now since they died.
None of the comments had any substance. Geez, I was only asking people from Noark.
Welp.

I clicked my tongue and checked the time. Surprisingly, there were only about ten minutes left before the Round Table opened. As the comments were constantly being updated in real-time, the night had just flown by.
Yeah, I’m sure there will be some useful information there.
I stopped reading the comments and lay on the bed for a while. Then, as soon as the time came, I entered the Round Table.
He’s going to be here, right?
I was worried that Clown would be absent this meeting since he’d gotten dunked on for the entirety of last month’s gathering, but thankfully the guy was resilient.
“So you’re here too, Mr. Lion. Pshehe.”
Acting friendly again? I let that greeting go in one ear and out the other and sat in my usual seat. The current participants were Goblin, Deer, Clown, and Queen. For some reason, Fox wasn’t here.

“That’s strange. She’s always the first to show up,” Goblin commented, studying my reaction. That was fair. Since I had spoken with Fox separately at the end of the last meeting, he must have been wondering if something had happened.

Because I also didn’t know anything about Fox’s absence, I just kept quiet. After a while, the time soon came for the gathering to start and Fox still hadn’t appeared. But instead, Crescent Moon, who had been the subject of much speculation after not attending the last gathering, made an appearance.
“Oh?”
“So you aren’t dead, Mr. Crescent Moon.”
Thanks to that, the attention people had been paying to Fox’s absence shifted to him.
“A new face. Nice to meet you. Last month was my first time attending a meeting and I still have a lot to learn.” Like the talented extrovert she was, Queen approached him to say hello first.
Crescent Moon was in a strange state. He should probably have been curious about Queen, whom he had never met before, but he just sat down without a word. Had this guy always been like this?

“Pshehe, acting all full of yourself. What happened to you? At least tell us that. Can’t you see everyone is curious?” Clown asked, and the other members didn’t say anything about how rude he was being. They were curious, too, about what the hell had happened to Crescent Moon.

“...I wasn’t in the mood last month.” All the attention on him must have been uncomfortable as Crescent Moon offered a brief explanation. Although he gave no details, it wasn’t hard to figure out what he meant. After all, moods like the one he was talking about usually corresponded to certain events. The same went for that low, empty tone of his too.
“Looks like he lost someone,” Deer clicked his tongue and muttered. Crescent Moon did not respond.
At that, Goblin eagerly looked between Clown and Crescent Moon. The reason was simple. “Then it’s a good thing you came. Your enemy may be right here.”
“What do you mean by that...?” Having not been here last time, Crescent Moon didn’t know Clown’s identity.
“Clown is Corpse Collector.”
When Deer revealed that information without making any effort to hide his hostility, Crescent Moon froze. There was a short silence.
“I see. Clown is... So, you are...” Crescent Moon then turned to Clown. Did he really lose someone to Noark? In that gaze, I felt a rather piercing murderous intent.
But as someone who had experienced worse, Clown only laughed it off as usual. “Pshehe, how are you going to kill someone with that?”

Crescent Moon stared Clown down silently, then released his tightly clenched fists. All of a sudden, his murderous intent was also gone. Crescent Moon had realized it too. Even though the enemy was right in front of his eyes, there was nothing he could really do here. “I will find you someday,” he said, his voice calm and restrained.
After a brief pause, Clown sneered. “...Pshe, I’ll be waiting.”
Anyway, that ended their personal exchange.

“Now, since the door is closed, why don’t we start soon? I’ve been looking forward to this for a month!” Before long, Queen took up a forced, bubbly tone and rallied the troops. We took time to decide on the order.

“Now, now. Then I’ll go first today.” Clown claimed the first turn. No one said anything but I could sense they were all waiting to hear whatever would come out of his mouth. “This might get a little interesting,” he told us before fixing his gaze on Crescent Moon. “While we’re on the topic of you coming to find me, just how do you plan to do that? You’ve all seen the post on the bulletin board, right? The one saying that the outside world is perfectly fine and everyone who used to live in Noark is now outside.” Soon Clown put his hand on the jewel and said: “All of that is true.”
As proof, the jewel at the center of the Round Table gave off a green light.

chapters.title: Chapter 259: Clan (3)
paragraphs: Even though the light on the jewel turned off, the silence dragged on. Just as I had been in the middle of wondering if that post was true or not, Clown had confirmed its authenticity, which made the weight of what had happened that day all the more evident to us.
So, the outside world really is fine.
What would happen to the city once the community closed for the night? Rumors would surely spread like wildfire.
Those damn bastards from Noark.

Hearing the truth from Clown’s mouth, I could clearly see Noark’s intentions. That post was not a confession borne of personal defiance. It was a planned move to spread this information through the city using the community.
Which is why this asshole is telling us about all this so easily.

Clown always hid behind a frivolous mask and spoke in a theatrical tone, but he wasn’t actually a fool. For example, he maintained his silence during all of Noark’s previous plans. And even though he was one of the top members of Orcules, he never used them as information fodder here.
“Soon, an assassin will be sent after Bjorn Yandel.”

The last piece of information he had mentioned was similar. Although he spoke as if Noark was going to be the one to send an assassin, he had in fact been referring to an assassination plot by a large clan. And what he stood to gain by doing so was obvious.
“Anyway, Mr. Deer, you were very zealous.” Clown had made Deer make a move in real life. “Pshe, I didn’t expect you to actually send those knights like that.”
He had laid the foundation for tracking down Deer’s identity in exchange for tipping us off. Even if the assassination against Bjorn Yandel failed, from his perspective, that was way more important.
“Asshole.”

It was possible that the reason why Deer had suddenly called the knights back was because he had belatedly realized what Clown’s aim was. The longer the tail, the more likely he was to be caught by it.

“It’s fun watching you two fight, but please do that on your own later! Um, Mr. Clown, if it’s all right, may I ask a question?” When Clown and Deer showed signs of starting a brawl, Queen skillfully cut through the tension and tossed out a question. “So, who is the old man? The one who carried over ten thousand people with Mass Teleport at once and disappeared. Sounds like he was the one who guided you all outside too.”
“That’s...” Clown trailed off and laughed awkwardly. “Pshe, it’s a secret. If I just tell you, that would be no fun, right?”

It was clear he had no idea who the guy was. That was not how you pretended to know something. With the experience I’d racked up thus far as Lion, I saw an opportunity to toss in my two cents and took it. “There’s no way that old man would have revealed his identity.”
I topped the act off by shooting Clown a look as if to scold him for trying to pull a petty trick. Clown flinched like I’d caught him red-handed. His eyes seemed to say, How did you know that?
Queen, for her part, shifted her gaze to me, giving me a curious look. “Hmmm, does that mean you know something, Mr. Lion? Who that mysterious old man is?”
No, how would I?
Maintaining eye contact, I didn’t answer, Lion’s signature gesture that you had to bring him something interesting if you wanted to hear something from him.
Queen grumbled, “Hmph, then can you at least tell me what you’re interested in?”
Hey, that would reduce the variety of information.
There was only one thing I could say, exactly the same line I’d used in a similar situation in the past. “I don’t know.” Lion didn’t know himself. “What I’m interested in.”
At my words, Queen looked at me like I was an unfamiliar beast.
Okay then, I think I’ve met my quota for today...
I pretended not to be interested in the conversation that followed despite listening intently. The gathering, which had momentarily been on pause, resumed.

“Then I will go this time.” Goblin took the second turn. He revealed information related to one of the churches. “Do you remember me telling you about a blessing that was given to someone a few months ago? I finally figured out who it was.”
What? Out of the blue? Having not expected this to come up here, I tried my best to keep my composure.

“You’re finally useful. Pshehe, so, who is it? And what’s the holy relic they received?” Clown, who had shown a strong interest in the blessing and holy relic at the time, straightened up in his seat. Perhaps something like this had never happened before.
Goblin puffed out his chest and said, “Bjorn Yandel. The one who received the blessing back then is the same barbarian who recently gained fame as the Giant.”
Things were getting interesting.
“Bjorn Yandel.”
Not to toot my own horn, but it was the hottest name in the city these days.

“He’s the one who received the blessing...?” Having suffered much at my hand, Clown laughed in apparent shock. “Hey, is this information confirmed? That man isn’t even human. How could he receive a blessing?”

“Well... I thought it was strange, too, but when I looked into it, it’s not completely unprecedented. There have actually been a few people of different races who have received blessings in the past.”
“Most left a big mark on history.” Deer stepped in to back Goblin’s explanation up. “So stop doubting Goblin without even knowing anything. Didn’t the jewel turn green?”
“That...” That didn’t always mean the information was accurate. That was obviously what Clown wanted to say, but he couldn’t finish his sentence. That was because he was the prime example of that.
“Now, now. Let’s stop this. You, too, Mr. Clown. Since this information is 100 percent accurate, unlike Mr. Clown’s from back then, you all don’t have to worry. I saw it for myself and confirmed it.”

Huh? Goblin saw and confirmed it was true himself? Well, that changed things. At first, I thought it was highly likely that Goblin had obtained information after it had already become widespread. But he was saying he saw it for himself?
...Then he was there too?

When the third vine broke off, there had been a total of five people around me: three knight bodyguards, Missha, and Sven Parav, the deputy commander of the Second Order of the Paladins of Reatlas. Naturally, I could immediately narrow the suspect list down to one, since it was pretty much established fact that Goblin was a paladin.
How interesting. To think he’s really him.
The image Goblin presented at the Round Table and that dignified paladin from back then were incredibly different. Well, it probably still wasn’t as jarring a difference as me.
...Is this actually a good thing?
Clown and Queen’s, and now even Goblin’s identity had been revealed to me. There might come a day when this information would be extremely useful.
“Then what’s the holy relic? If it’s the Goddess of the Stars, it must be a relic related to destiny, right?”
“To be honest... I don’t know that, either. I’m not in a position to be asking around...” Goblin then confessed that he knew nothing about the holy relic’s abilities, and his turn ended.
Next was Queen. “The day the returning adventurers were being rewarded in the Palace of Glory, the palace sent an official notice to the Magic Tower.”
“An official notice?”

“Yes. It was a request for them to repair the portal to the labyrinth. When they checked, they found it was in a very unstable state.” After that, Queen shut her mouth and waited for the jewel to glow. It was a green light, indicating a pass, but the other members weren’t pleased.
“This may only be your second time, but come on. Pshehe, what use is there in garbage information like that?”

Despite Clown’s dig, Queen did not budge. “I don’t know. I think this information will mean different things to different people depending on their level,” she retorted. “If the repairs were even a little late, there could have been a dimensional collapse.”
But even Deer was on Clown’s side this time. “It’s not like you’re saying that a dimensional collapse is going to happen, though; information that repairs have already been done is a bit subpar.”
Well, there was nothing they could gain from this information, but the same couldn’t be said for me.
...If the repairs are finished, it would be correct to assume that the EXP copying bug has been fixed.
Man, did that mean I’d need to speed-run to gain portal-opening EXP from now on? Still, just in case, I decided to test it out one more time the next time I entered the labyrinth.
“I have nothing more to say. I sincerely believe that this information is not inferior to the information I heard today.” Queen remained firm with the other members and received a pass.

“Oh, you can do that...?” Goblin, who had received many rejections in the past, seemed to be in awe of this novel method. But knowing you could do something and making it work were two different things. Even if Goblin tried to say the same thing Queen did, things wouldn’t go the same way for him. A barbarian-like stubbornness wasn’t something everyone could pull off. It had to be backed by the confidence that you were the best.
This woman is really strange too.

Anyway, after Queen was Deer. He spoke of a royal treasure being stolen while Karnon had been engulfed in flames. I had never heard of it before, but judging by these guys’ reactions, it seemed like it was a pretty important item. I’d look into it later.
“Now it’s you, Crescent.”

It was finally Crescent Moon’s turn. Because he was silently keeping to himself and acting out of character, I was looking forward to what kind of information he would spit out. But when I actually heard it, it was nothing special.
“The elves have decided to replace the next pureblood with someone else due to circumstances within the tribe. They are currently looking for a suitable candidate.”

Since this was information on the inner workings of one of the six races, it helped get a sense of the current state of affairs in the city, but it was otherwise just ordinary information that ended there. However, I couldn’t take my eyes off of Crescent Moon. That was because he was staring straight at me.
“Next time, I will bring something more entertaining.” By that, he meant that while he may not have had anything useful for me this time, he was determined not to give up on the Stone of Revival.
That wasn’t bad. In truth, the information itself wasn’t all that bad for me either.
If they’re selecting a new pureblood candidate, would Erwen be able to take the role? If she could consume that, that would be a game-changer.

As I was getting my thoughts in order, I could feel everyone’s eyes on me. Oh, it was my turn now. Instead of the few bits I prepared, I pulled out something else. “If you use the Stone of Revival, you can revive up to two people.”
So, keep working hard.

The Stone of Revival was an item that had been considered a mere legend until I mentioned it, but one that had now become a reality. Naturally, information about this item was valuable. However, I figured the members who were not desperate for the Stone of Revival would find this dissatisfying since this wasn’t information related to how to acquire it. It was just an extra tidbit saying it could save two people, and this was already the third time I’d used this particular topic too.
However, the other members did not voice their dissatisfaction. The mood wasn’t right for that.
“Two people... I see...” Crescent Moon, who appeared to have lost someone important not too long ago, muttered blankly at my words. There was a deep longing in his voice. A moment of silence ensued.
“Why, Mr. Crescent, you just lost us one chance today.” Clown lamented that my turn had been wasted on the Stone of Revival and suggested we move on to the next round.

“I have nothing else prepared, so I will stop here. If it weren’t for Lion, you all wouldn’t have come, either.” Crescent Moon didn’t even look at Clown and asked the other members for their understanding before leaving the Round Table.
The same went for Goblin. “Uh, my curiosity is sated... I don’t have anything to use, either, so I’m going to leave.”

Once even Goblin left, Deer also felt it too tough to continue with just the four of us and opted to leave. That was fair—once you got down to four people, the gathering got a bit grueling. Excluding the speaker, you could only pass with information that two or three other people were unaware of, and the amount of information you could obtain in return in each round was reduced.
“Then what about this? The three of us.”
“I don’t mind.”
Clown and Queen agreed to go on. Ultimately, the choice was mine.
These two are bound to have valuable information...

The thought made me want to be greedy, but in the end, I decided not to push it. If I wasn’t careful, they might find out that I was nothing but hot air. So the gathering ended after the first lap. “If there was something interesting, it would have been said already.” With that arrogant, Lion-like line, I turned around and returned to Hansu Lee’s room.
After spending more of my time looking through the forum, it soon became closing time and I returned to my original body.

“Oh, right. This isn’t my house.” I was in a room at an inn in District Seven that I had obtained using Kharon’s face and name. As soon as I opened my eyes, all the worries I had momentarily put aside came flooding back.
I wonder if Kharon is doing all right.
Kharon was my alibi. If the GM had really decided to make a move today, he would probably be watching Kharon right now to see if he was a player.
Inhale.

I wanted to check how things had gone as soon as possible, but if I went to where Kharon was now, there was a chance this would all go sideways. And so I decided to exercise patience and endure my burning curiosity.
The morning after what turned out to be a near-sleepless night, I met Kharon again at the holy land as agreed.
“Bjorn!”
Because the appearance change lasted thirty days otherwise, we put on the mask again to return to our original selves.
“Hehehe, considering the dark circles under your eyes, I’m guessing you had a great night?”
Oh, right. That was the excuse I was using. “...Thanks to you.”

I glossed over that and interrogated Kharon about everything that had happened yesterday, reasoning that I couldn’t risk ‘not remembering’ something big later. To be honest, though, I was just curious as hell. Although I’d entrusted this task to him, my imagination had run wild all night.
“Oh, you mean yesterday?”
I wonder what could have happened?

chapters.title: Chapter 260: Clan (4)
paragraphs: A barbarian warrior had just left the holy land. At the sight of Bjorn Yandel, one man breathed a sigh of relief.
“Fortunately, he came out right away.”

If Bjorn had intended to stay at the barbarians’ holy land overnight, he would have had to try for the 15th of next month instead. Trying to infiltrate the holy land with this body would have been a bit...
Twist.
The man, who was following after Bjorn Yandel, lost his balance and staggered. Because this was his first time connecting his senses to this golem, some of the controls were still unfamiliar.
“Excuse me, are you okay?” When the man caught himself in a bizarre pose, eyes started to turn to him.
“I’m all right.” The man felt a strange sense of embarrassment and quickly left the area. With a creaking gait, he followed after Bjorn.
“Mom, that man is funny...!”
...Baekho Lee, if it weren’t for that man...

The reason why the man had had to leave behind his perfectly fine body and link up to a golem he was not familiar with was all because of Baekho, because he couldn’t know when he would appear again. It was too dangerous to leave the Magic Tower as himself.
So, where is he going now?
It was still early morning and the sky was blue. The man continued to walk behind Bjorn Yandel.
He’s going to drink this early in the morning?
Finally, he arrived at a famous pub in District Seven, a bar that operated twenty-four hours a day with three shifts of staff on rotation.
“That man... is Bjorn, son of Yandel?”
“Oh, that man?”
“We got lucky. To think we get to see the man from the rumors in person.”
As soon as Bjorn entered the bar, the people around him turned to look. He was now famous enough that people recognized him wherever he went.
Smirk.
As if relishing in his fame, Bjorn grinned and sat at a table in the center of the room on his own. He then started tossing back drinks.
“Um, what would you like to order...?”
The man, who entered the pub at the same time and found a table nearby, ordered some food and kept a close eye on Bjorn. There was nothing significant to note.
Just drinking, drinking, and more drinking. The table beside him, which had been empty, was now filled with drunkards who had followed the scent of alcohol.
“Haha! To drink something that strong in one go, you really must be a giant!”
People who at first just came over to talk to a celebrity eventually sat down once he proved to be more entertaining than they thought. Oh, there were quite a few women among them.
“Um, can I touch your arm?”
“...O-Of course!”
“Wowww, it really feels like iron! Oh, I’m Amy.”

Interested in the body of a famous adventurer, these women who approached pretending not to be scared began trying to seduce the barbarian warrior. It wouldn’t work, of course. That was because Bjorn Yandel already had three lovers and was known to cherish all three fiercely.
“I... am B-Bjorn, son of Yandel! Nice to meet you...!”
Huh?
“Ahem...!”
“Oh my! How manly.”
As the women’s hands got bolder and more mischievous, the barbarian warrior made no move to stop them at all.
“Can I touch your thighs too?”
“Ahem! If you want...” Although he acted like he had no other choice, the slight curl at the corners of his lips proved that he was enjoying this too.
This guy is supposed to be a hero...?
The man was incredulous, but none of the people seemed uncomfortable with his behavior at all. They didn’t necessarily see it as an ethical problem. Anyway, their drinking continued into the evening.
“Behel-aaah! Drinks! Bring me more drinks! I have plenty of money!”

The closer it got to midnight, the more he was beginning to hope Bjorn was not a player. He couldn’t not feel that way. Breaking tables by arm-wrestling out of the blue, trying to smooth it over by declaring he had a lot of money, threatening a drunken customer who shot him a glare for being too loud, etcetera. This went far beyond just a perfect barbarian act. This guy was the very definition of a brainless barbarian warrior.
This... cannot be Elfnuna...

Even with that thought in mind, the man still waited until midnight. He’d wasted too much time here today to leave without checking on the final result. A long while later, there was only one minute left until the community opened. That barbarian was still chugging down drinks with other people, something a community user would never do.
Tick.
Soon, the minute hand moved to midnight. Having made arrangements in advance not to enter the community this month, the man was able to observe Bjorn Yandel without missing a beat.
...So he wasn’t.

Even though it was midnight, Bjorn was still laughing and chatting. No matter how quickly someone logged in and out, there was bound to be a brief moment of pause, but there was no such thing here. That at least meant he was not a part of the community.
If he’s not a member even after the letter I sent back then... that must mean he’s not a player, either. If he could read the letter, there’d be no reason for him not to join.
Soon, the man got up from his seat with a weight off his shoulders. Bjorn Yandel was not a player, and he felt a strange sense of relief at the thought.
Yeah, there’s no way this guy is a modern man.
According to Kharon’s account, his day yesterday was simple. That was because he’d spent all of it in a pub, drinking since morning.
No wonder he reeked of alcohol.

Of course, I didn’t intend to scold him about that. I was the one who told him to go drink in the first place. I figured that if Kharon spent the day at a bar, that guy would be conscious of the fact that other people were around and wouldn’t be able to try anything funny.
“So, what happened while you were drinking?”
“Oh, that? It’s kind of a long story... But it was so much fun!”

I tuned out the story of a drunkard he’d made friends with at the pub, and how he accidentally smashed a table and had to pay for it, because I’d expected that much. The price of the table and the drinks didn’t bother me as long as my goal had been achieved.

“Was there anyone strange at the bar? Hmm...” Kharon seemed to comb through his alcohol-soaked memory before giving me the answer I wanted. “Come to think of it, there was a weak-looking man sitting in the corner all day. He was a strange guy and kept ordering stuff without drinking or eating.”
As soon as I heard this, I knew it was him. “So, what did you do? Did you speak to him?”
“Of course not. He seemed kind of empty in the head so I didn’t go up to him first.”
“When did that man leave the pub?”
“I don’t know about that... I think it was around midnight.”

A smile appeared on my face. He was at the pub all day and left as soon as midnight came and went. It seemed my trick had worked. The sight of Kharon having a good time with the pubgoers must have cleared all of his suspicions about me. That meant my plan had gone off without a hitch.
“Mm, yes. Midnight should be about right. Because it was around one o’clock that I saw that shifter woman.”
Huh?
“...Shifter woman?” Anxiety rose inside of me. And as always, it was well-founded.
“That daughter of Karlstein!”
Missha had run into Kharon in my body. “What happened when you saw her?”
When I urgently asked what happened next, Kharon explained what went down. “She may be a shifter, but she was a fierce woman. I can see why you like her.”
To summarize, it went down like this: Missha had dragged Kharon out by the neck while he was flirting with the women and they exchanged a brief conversation.
“Sorry. No matter what I said, nothing worked.”
Before long, Kharon got caught. Of course he did—how would he hide the fact that he was an entirely different person from her? But the important bit started here. So, what had happened?
“She asked what you were doing so I just answered honestly.”
“...You answered honestly?” I bit out through gritted teeth.

Kharon flinched at my tone, but he must have really wanted to say this because he pressed on. “Bjorn, you are the hero of our tribe. You are just doing your duty. Why do you have to hide that? So I just told her honestly! That Bjorn is fulfilling his duties with the female warriors of the tribe, so don’t even think about interfering!”
I didn’t respond.

“Haha, she didn’t seem to know what those duties were so I explained it to her in detail. And then it seemed like she finally understood and left. You should thank me! Now you can fulfill your duties in the holy land whenever you want! But... why are you so quiet?” Kharon asked cautiously, and I once again responded with silence.
I just didn’t know what I should say here. Damn it, how did things end up like this? Even getting angry at Kharon would be pointless.
“Kharon, son of Tarson. Make a warrior’s oath that you will keep everything that happened today strictly confidential.”
“Oath? If you want, I can do it a hundred times.”
Inwardly whimpering, I asked him to make an oath and Kharon agreed without an inkling of hesitation. That was the reason why I couldn’t get angry at the guy.
“Oh, but what does ‘confidential’ mean?”
“...It means do not tell anyone.”
“That’s not difficult! I am famous in the tribe for being tight-lipped!”

Yeah, what would getting angry at him do? Like a natural disaster, it was wiser to consider what had happened an inevitability. No one got angry at storm clouds for bringing rain, right? Kharon had already done his job. Thankfully, we were able to successfully trick the GM.
Now I have no choice but to deal with the aftermath.
After parting with Kharon, I headed home.
Trudge, trudge.
Unlike usual, my steps there felt very heavy.
When I arrived home, Missha was sitting on the sofa in the living room. I couldn’t see any hint of emotion on her face. Yeah, none at all.

“Oh, you’re herrre?” Missha asked as if nothing was wrong. But her fingernails, which were always neatly trimmed, were jagged, and her eyes were bloodshot. Did she spend all night on the sofa like that?
“Y-Yeah...” My heart constricted. I couldn’t bring myself to say any of the lines I had prepared and just stood there.
“Okay, then. Go sleep.” As if to give me time to say something, Missha took a moment to look at me in silence before turning around and going into her room. Even then, I just watched.
What could I say? That what Kharon told her wasn’t true? To explain that, I’d have to tell her about the GM. Of course, I could possibly make up another excuse, but...
It could make the situation worse.

Maybe if this had happened a few months ago, I would have gone that route. But now, Missha already suspected me of being an evil spirit. This was better than being suspected of that. Fulfilling the duties of the tribe? At least that didn’t sound like something an evil spirit would do. This was for the best.
...My ass.
I quickly climbed the stairs and knocked on Missha’s door. There was no answer. Did she not want to speak with me?
“I’m coming in.” I ignored her wishes and did what I wanted like the barbarian I was.
Crack!
Thankfully, the door wasn’t locked as it easily flew open. I could see a Missha-sized lump on the bed with the blanket over her head.
So you don’t want to even look at me.
It was a good thing I came after her, because everything had its proper place. A tank was a person who protected their teammates, not harmed them.

“If you don’t want to talk, just listen,” I said. I still didn’t have the courage to reveal I was an evil spirit. With no plan in mind, I opened the mouth of my borrowed barbarian body. “Nothing happened at the holy land.”
Missha pulled down the blanket a bit at my words. “...Why are you telling me this?”

She asked like she was confused like I had no reason to make excuses, whether she believed them or not. She wasn’t wrong. Missha and I were only teammates. There had been an opportunity for us to have a more intimate relationship, but I had been the one to push her away. I thought it would be difficult to make rational decisions at future crossroads if romantic feelings got in the way.
“Bjorn, is this because you think I’m uncomforrrtable? If that’s why you’re being considerate, you don’t have to—”

“It’s not for you. It’s for my own peace of mind. Unlike Dwalkie, I’m a selfish bastard.” I cut Missha off and spoke. “Missha, nothing happened last night at the holy land, and I don’t want you to misunderstand that.”
“Why don’t you want me to misunderstand...?” The eyes poking out of the blanket were filled with a distinct brand of hope and desire, one I couldn’t ignore forever.

I took a breath before continuing. Even if I may just have been a wicked evil spirit dwelling in Bjorn Yandel’s body, this was a truth I couldn’t run away from forever. “Because I don’t just consider you my teammate anymore.”

chapters.title: Chapter 261: Clan (5)
paragraphs: The last time we spoke of it, I told Missha that I considered her a valuable teammate, pushing her away with cowardly words. I had thought that was the right thing to do, and in fact, it was. At the time, I had still been burning with the desire to return. Not to mention... I didn’t even have the right to cross that line, because I was an evil spirit. No matter how many sweet-nothings I whispered through Bjorn Yandel’s lips, I figured it would only ever mean deceiving the other person.
“W-What does that mean? That you don’t just considerrr me a teammate...?” she asked with wide eyes.
I answered without hesitation. “You should know what I mean by that.”
It was something I had realized after visiting the community this time around. More than Hansu Lee’s dark room, I considered this, this place where I was now, my home.
“You didn’t even say it properrrly...” Missha slowly shifted her eyes from the wall, which she had been staring at to avoid my gaze, to me. “So how can I know...?”
Perhaps this was what Baekho was wary of. The moment you formed a deep connection with an NPC, your desire to stay in this place became stronger. But, so what?
“Missha Karlstein, I like you.”

I didn’t care about returning anymore. The fact that it became difficult to make rational decisions when romantic feelings got in the way was also a factor, but it was already too late for me anyway. I considered my teammates, including Missha, to be precious, and I couldn’t prioritize myself above them.
This was a trace of the legacy Dwalkie had left behind. What else could I do after he left us the way he had? I could never think of these people as NPCs.
So, what was Missha’s answer? I felt nervous for the first time in a while, but I didn’t express this outwardly in order to avoid influencing the results. There was a long beat of silence.
“Bjorn.” Soon, Missha parted her lips and cut through the quiet. Before I knew it, she was out from under the blanket and standing in front of me. “...Let’s go out.”

Missha grabbed my hand and led me out of the house. I didn’t ask where we were going. The time was early morning, when people were just starting to wake up and start their days. Without even bothering to put on coats, Missha and I left the house and found a room at an inn thirty yards away, where we pressed our bodies together.
“Bjorn, gently—! It hurrrts when you squeeze too tight...”
Concerned about causing her pain, I forced my rough barbarian body to move carefully and conscientiously. “Are you really sure about this...?”
“...Anything for you.” The hug Missha gave me was clumsy yet warm. That was how the two of us spent our time until evening, sharing in each other’s heat.
So that’s where her tail goes.
That day, I got to learn with my own two eyes the answer to a question that had always been on my mind. But as the saying went, happiness was fleeting.
“Bjorn.”
“Get some more rest. Don’t worry about Ainar and Erwen. I’m sure they’re fine—”
“That’s not it. I have something to say.”

Before I could even tilt my head in confusion to ask what she meant, Missha sat up on the bed and looked at me. When she spoke again, she sounded resolute. “I think... it’s best for us to just stay teammates.”
She rejected me.
It felt like she was in a dream.
“Missha Karlstein, I like you.”
The moment she heard those words, her heart began to pound like crazy and the whole world seemed brighter. That was why.
“...Let’s go out.”
Missha had taken Bjorn and practically run out of the house with him because she was anxious. It felt like if she took her eyes off of him for even a moment, she was going to wake up from this dream.
“Bjorn, Bjorn, Bjorn...!”
“Don’t worry, I’m not going anywhere.”

That was how they’d passed those dream-like hours. The two exchanged body heat and in the moments in between, they talked. They talked about everything from the moment they met until now, laying bare their thoughts and feelings. It was a time for them to share with one another.
Did I fall asleep for a little bit?

A dream was a dream because you had to wake up one day. Missha slowly opened her eyes. She could see a dark sky out the window and the man she had wanted so badly sleeping next to her. The profound happiness that filled her at the sight was short-lived. The world was dyed the color of reality and she sobered up.
As I thought, Bjorn...
He was an evil spirit. Unable to say it even in the privacy of her own head, Missha let the sentence go unfinished because it broke her heart just thinking about it.

She felt choked up. She’d had her doubts, but she became sure about his identity today. That was because after hearing about the duties of the barbarian tribe from Kharon, she had asked Ainar some questions. Only barbarians could give birth to barbarians. This was something she had known from the start.
“Be in a relationship? Haha, isn’t that obvious? Of course we can. As far as I know, there are quite a few barbarians who are!”

Barbarians were still people, after all. The longer they lived in the city, and the longer they adventured with people other than their fellow countrymen from the holy land, the more their values gradually began to change.
“According to the chieftain, any warrior is bound to change after living in the city for a few years, even if just a little. I think he called it ‘urbanization.’”

Because they were kind, their personalities meshed well with others. Affection accumulated from spending a long time together. There were definitely barbarians in the city who were attracted to people romantically, regardless of their race, but they all had something in common.
“But I heard it’s difficult to find someone, because most of them don’t understand our duty.”

Even those barbarians inevitably wanted to have children. Ainar explained that duty was an intrinsic part of their race, imprinted on their souls. And so, Missha had tried to be understanding. That was the reason she had headed up to her room without saying anything, even though she had waited there all night, unable to sleep thanks to the pain in her heart.
“Missha, nothing happened last night at the holy land, and I don’t want you to misunderstand that.”
However, she had instead been told not to misinterpret the situation.
“Because I don’t just consider you my teammate anymore.”

She’d even gotten to hear something like that from Bjorn. At the time, she had been so lost in her happiness that she couldn’t even think of them, but when she woke up again, everything was full of contradictions. Of course, she believed him when he said that nothing happened in the holy land.
But if that’s true, why did Kharon lie?
Why did Bjorn tell Kharon that he was going to fulfill his duties? Thinking about it now, the answer was obvious.
Because he had to.

The only barbarians who hadn’t yet fulfilled their duties were the ones at the start of their careers who hadn’t established themselves. It was strange for a warrior who even had the nickname Giant to avoid his duties, which was why Bjorn had used Kharon. Kharon’s words yesterday were proof of that.
“Bjorn is fulfilling his duties with the female warriors of the tribe, so don’t even think about interfering!”

Without even needing to be coerced, Kharon had given her the full story. If Bjorn really wanted to keep that a secret, there was no way Kharon would have done that—he would’ve made Kharon make an oath. Considering how thorough he always was, this could only be interpreted as intentional. Bjorn had wanted Kharon to spread rumors in the barbarian community that Bjorn Yandel was fulfilling his duties.
Even still, the reason why he had to go to the trouble of changing his appearance...
Missha dropped her head.
Because... he likes me...

Bjorn wanted to be seen as a barbarian who fulfilled his duties to his countrymen but for that same information to not reach her ears. If she hadn’t stopped by that pub out of a gut feeling that night, she would’ve also thought that Bjorn had just been out drinking all night. Anyone she asked would’ve said the same.
Now I...

Now faced with the truth, her hands and feet trembled. Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit, but that hadn’t affected her feelings for him in the slightest. This was natural. The person she had fallen in love with was not Bjorn Yandel, but the man who had saved her and had been by her side throughout many adventures.
So... what do I do now?

The fact that he was an evil spirit was not important. Even if everyone pointed fingers and said that it was wrong, she just had to do what she wanted to do, just like he’d taught her. But even still, there were logistical problems that remained.
If we do this, he will be caught someday...

Love made it hard to make logical decisions. Missha knew that better than anyone. And in truth, Bjorn had made the wrong decision. Rather than pretending to fulfill his duties, actually fulfilling them for real would have been much more advantageous when it came to concealing his identity. And there was just one reason he hadn’t done so.
Yeah, because of me...
So Missha made up her mind. If this relationship continued, Bjorn would one day make a bigger mistake.
I’ll shoulder this alone...

This was the best course of action. Although even just imagining it made her heart ache, she was great at enduring hardships like these. Before she met the man she knew as Bjorn Yandel, she had lived her whole life that way.
“Bjorn.” She called her sleeping lover’s name to wake him.
“Get some more rest. Don’t worry about Ainar and Erwen. I’m sure they’re fine—”

“That’s not it. I have something to say.” She forced a smile even though it hurt, and spoke even though the only thing that lay down this road was pain. “I think... it’s best for us to just stay teammates.”
Surely, for this man, she could do this.
“Y-You come in a little laterrr. I-I-I’ll make an excuse to the others... Okay?”
Before I could understand what the hell was happening here, before I could get a full rundown of the situation, Missha left.
I froze on the spot, as still as a stone—Barbarian Statue Mode.
“I was rejected...?”

My head felt numb. What did I do wrong? Did I make a mistake today? I racked my brain for some time, but the only things that came to mind were made-up worst-case scenarios. Yeah, what was the use in working myself up? If I had a question, I just had to ask. And if I did something wrong, I just had to fix it.
“Oh, you’re herrre? Come eat.” When I finally got home, Missha greeted me as if nothing had happened. Erwen and Ainar, for their part, thought I only got home just now.
“You’re here, Mister?”
“Bjorn, out all night and only coming back now? Take me with you next time you drink!”
For now, we all got together and ate. I wanted to ask Missha what she meant earlier, but I couldn’t ask her here.
“Th-then, I’m tired so I’m going to rrrest now!” As soon as the meal was over, Missha fled to her room.
“Erwen, Missha is acting weird today, isn’t she? She’s walking weirdly too.”
“Hm, I don’t know why she’s acting like that, either. Something doesn’t feel right, though...”
As the two questioned Missha’s behavior, I chimed in that she must have been sick and quickly followed her upstairs to “check on her.”
“B-Bjorn...?!”
Finally, we were alone again. I asked her to tell me if I did something wrong and why she wanted to stay as teammates, and her answer was the same as before.

“L-Let’s just pretend nothing happened today. I think that would be best.” It was a stubborn refusal to offer a proper explanation. Determining that now was not the time, I decided to back off and wait for the right moment to ask again. But...
“Oh, sorrry! I have somewhere to go now!”
“Ainar! Laundrrry! Let’s go hang the laundry!”
“...I’m tired today.”

After that, Missha continued to avoid situations where the two of us might end up alone like a plague, and if I somehow managed to corner her and press her for an answer, she always gave the same one. After a few days, I gave up too.
“...I see. Then let’s just pretend that day didn’t happen.”
Even I couldn’t keep being so tenacious when the other party was acting like that. That would only be coercion. And to be honest, backing off was a subconscious defense mechanism.
Wow, I want to smoke.

I couldn’t even remember the last time I’d felt so out of it. Even when I’d stepped on those goblin traps and had to crawl through Crystal Cave, or when those pillars of fire exploded in the square, it hadn’t been this bad.
Yeah, just focus on what you have to do.
I couldn’t continue being so distraught forever, so I wiped the incident with Missha from my mind as much as possible and focused on my work. Thankfully, there were other things to occupy my time.
“Mister, did you hear the rumors?”
“That the outside world is fine?”
“Yes. It’s all anyone talks about these days.”

Information about the world beyond the castle walls that had first been revealed in the community started spreading throughout the entire city. Well, it was still just being treated as a rumor for now, but as more time passed, it was bound to grow bigger.
I wonder how the palace will react.
Contrary to my expectations, the palace had yet to respond. I had to keep a closer eye on the situation—while still doing my own work, of course.
“Anyway, you know about today, right?”
“Meeting at the District Seven headquarters at 3 p.m. today, right?”
“Yeah.”

As soon as I finished lunch, I headed to the Adventurers’ Guild early and prepped the paperwork in advance. These were the various documents required to create a clan. That was because Raven and Mr. Bear, who had said they wanted to think about it some more, finally decided to join my clan.
“Raven?”

As I was filling in the paperwork, Raven showed up before the designated time. “This is an important matter. I didn’t want to leave it all to you.” She tried to make it sound like she didn’t trust me, but in truth what she really meant was that she came over early to help me. “How far have you gotten? Let me see.”
Raven proceeded to take a few of the papers and scribble on them with the pen, quickly jotting down the essentials. She was three times faster than I was and made fewer mistakes too.

“These rules are too ambiguous. These things have to be clear-cut. The same goes for the conditions for leaving the clan. You can make exceptions, but you have to clearly state who you’ll be making those exceptions for.”
“I-I see...?”
“Show me the paperwork you’ve already done. I have the feeling I’ll have to fix everything, anyway.”
“Here.”
Anyway, with Raven’s help, we were almost done with the paperwork by the time our other teammates arrived.
“This is my first time forming a clan myself so this all feels new. Did you do all this, Raven?”
“Yes. You all just need to sign here. But if you want to read through the documents before that, go ahead.”
“Haha, it’s all right. I’m sure you did a good job filling it out.”

Starting with Mr. Bear, the remaining members of our party signed the paper and once we submitted it, our application for creating a clan was complete. It’d probably be officially registered in the guild by tomorrow.
Then that solves that problem...
The structure of a clan would go beyond uniting us as a group—it would carry us to new heights.
“Did everyone clear their schedules?”

In that spirit, we left the guild and headed to a tavern. There were still only six of us, but this was our first meeting as a clan instead of a team. Ordering a few dishes and some drinks, we took time to share our plans for the future. Hmm, it’d probably be more accurate to call it ‘announcing’ rather than ‘sharing,’ though.
“We will be entering the labyrinth this time.”
Now that we’d officially created a clan, it was time for us to charge forward again.

chapters.title: Chapter 262: Bug (1)
paragraphs: When I announced we would be entering the labyrinth, Raven quietly asked, “I guess that means you believe the rumors, Mr. Yandel?”
It wasn’t a matter of believing it—I knew it was the truth. The outside world was fine, and all of Noark was out there.

“I don’t fully believe it, but I think it’s more than possible.” However, since the source of my information was a community of evil spirits, I couldn’t act too confident, so I told them about the strange feeling I got when I saw the guards atop the walls of Bifron looking inward. “I felt something was off then, but if the rumors are true, that would explain it.”
“Hmm, to be honest, I’ve been suspicious of that too. Even the Magic Tower doesn’t have any windows.”

The Magic Tower was a high-rise building that stood taller than the castle walls. When the palace approved the construction of the building, they demanded no windows be included. On paper, the reason was so that the Magic Tower could not look into the royal palace.
“What? Wait... then is the outside really fine like they say?”

“It’s just a story with the potential to be true for now.” Raven cut Mr. Bear off before he could start freaking out. Then she looked at me. No words were spoken, but it was easy to understand what she wanted to say. She wanted to know if I was really going to bet on that possibility and enter the labyrinth.
I offered the answer I had prepared. “To be honest, I don’t think it matters whether the rumors are true or not.”
“Your logic?”
“I see it as an indisputable truth that the palace has occupied Noark’s castle.”

Whether the bastards were outside or still underground, what did it matter? The army was already occupying Noark’s fortress, where their portal was located. That meant there was no need to worry about running into anyone from Noark inside.

“I thought the same thing. All right. I’m in.” It seemed Raven had just been curious about my opinion and actually thought this was a good opportunity, as she cast her vote in favor of my plan. That naturally kicked off a round of voting from everyone else.
“Well, if you two say so, then I’m sure it’s all right. I will follow your lead.”
“Ohh, are we finally entering the labyrinth again?!”
Mr. Bear and Ainar were excited, and Missha and Erwen also agreed to go in. From there, it was time to move on to the next order of business.
“Then what are we going to do about the number of members? Including Erwen, there’s now six of us.”
“We will split into groups of three and meet up on the second floor.”
“Hmm, that means the fourth floor will take up quite a bit of time.”
At Raven’s comment, Erwen paled and hurriedly apologized. “I-I’m sorry. I’m inconveniencing you all...”
“N-No, that’s not what I meant. Really.”
No buts. Before things could get more awkward, I stepped in. “Still, it won’t take as long as you think. Unlike me, Erwen is a proper scout. It’s possible the total time will be similar.”
“Oh, then there are no problems.”
This ended the conversation about Erwen. After that, we talked about future plans, and a unanimous decision was made.
“Yeah, I don’t think I’m ready yet, but...”
“We’ve gotten a lot strrronger now.”
“Haha, we should get ready. It’s been a while since I’ve been up there.”
Our target was the sixth floor.
After the clan meeting, my busy daily life continued. It was finally time to use up the money we had been saving.
“If any of you have a piece of equipment or item you’ve been wanting, buy it now. Ainar, you consult with me before you buy anything.”
“Wow... I heard it was like this, but it’s rrreally bad. Lithinum equipment is seven hundred thousand stones?”

While the price of food and items essential to daily life had skyrocketed, the price of equipment, consumables, and labyrinth-related items had plummeted. This was because 70 percent of the demand had vanished. As the majority of adventurers had been killed, all related items left in the city had become dead stock.
Still, this will be the lowest point.

That was because the value of the money we had collected so far, including the money we received from the palace, rose on its own. I had saved all that money until now, but it was time to use it. Once the situation in the labyrinth stabilized, prices would gradually rise.
“This is the recent transaction history you have requested.”
“Ah, thanks. I’ll take a quick look at it and give it back.”

A quick look at the market prices at the Central Exchange these days showed almost no changes. Even just a few days ago, the market had been crashing again and again. The reason things were different was because there were people like me gradually starting to use their money. Vendor anticipation that the market would soon recover was also having an effect.
