If things had stayed like this for a few more months, it could have been possible to graduate to the next level with items on the Exchange alone.
Even though I felt a bit disappointed, I went to the Exchange every day with my teammates and made several reasonable purchases. I bought a total of three items.
[You have equipped a Large Battle Shield made of adamantium. Your total Item Level has increased by +1750.]

First, I replaced the shield that was destroyed in the last battle. While I was at it, I got it in a grade-five metal. The price was unbelievably cheap. The fact that it wasn’t made to order was a factor, but it was even cheaper than the grade-four metal moonstone usually was.
[You have equipped No. 8820: Iron Wall. Your total Item Level has increased by +310.]

The second item was a pair of steel boots. As it was an item that doubled the user’s Physical Resistance and Mana Resistance for three seconds upon activation, it was a great match for a Shield Barbarian. Of course, that didn’t mean it was a top-class item. There were better boots among the higher numbered items than that.
Still, these boots should be good enough for the second half.

The last item I purchased was an ingredient named Soul of the Dead. It was the most expensive item of all the ones I purchased to receive the seventh stage of the Spirit Imprint. It could also be used as an ingredient in alchemy and magic. The price for this had plummeted like everything else, but only by a relatively marginal amount.
I can’t guarantee when I’ll be able to get it again.

The cost wasn’t the issue—it was just that these materials were harder to come by than equipment. That was because the supply itself was limited. For that reason, I decided to buy it as soon as I saw it.
Mm-hmm, it’s better to buy this thing with money than try to find it myself.

Soul of the Dead was an item that had a certain probability of dropping when you hunted rank-four monsters with a distortion spell. That meant there was no way of knowing how long it would take to get it yourself. I could use my time in much more productive ways.
“Bjorn, then I’m going to the training grounds!”
Anyway, when the time came to leave the auction house, Ainar ran to the training grounds again. It seemed she was very happy with the two numbered items she bought.
“Missha, what about you?”
“I’m going home. I need to prepare dinnerrr.”
“Then you can take Abman home.”
“Huh? Are you not going home?”
“I’m going to stop by the holy land for a bit. I might not be able to come home today.”
Missha flinched at my words before turning to stare straight at me. “Holy land...?”
Ah, it was because of that particular keyword. I hurriedly offered an explanation. “I bought those ingredients, remember? I’m thinking of getting the Spirit Imprint.”
“Ah, yeah. I see. Yeah, right...”
Ever since that day, there had occasionally been awkward moments like this. I knew we agreed to pretend nothing happened, but there was no way that would be easy.
“T-Then have a good trrrip. I’ll take good care of the girls.”
“Yeah... I’ll leave it to you.”

I parted ways with Missha and boarded the carriage heading toward the holy land. On the other side of the street, I could see Missha sitting on a bench still waiting for her carriage. When our eyes met, Missha hurriedly averted her gaze, then looked back and waved stiffly.
Ugh, honestly. This is so uncomfortable.

I nodded awkwardly and drew the curtain on the carriage. A moment later, I wondered to myself what the hell I was doing and felt a sense of shame, but even this was a lot better than before. As the saying went, time healed all wounds. If I kept pretending that nothing was wrong, one day that would really be the case.
“Then we are departing.”

The carriage soon left the platform, and after resting my eyes for a bit, I arrived at my destination before I knew it—a platform on the outskirts of District Seven close to the holy land. After crossing the castle gates and walking down the forest path, the barbarian camp appeared before my eyes. First, I entered the tent of the chieftain and said hello.
“Long time no see. Spar?”
Whew, looks like he hasn’t heard about the blessing yet, thankfully.

I had been a bit worried after Goblin, that fucker, talked about the blessing at the Round Table, but it didn’t seem to have reached the chieftain’s ears. Well, that was only a matter of time, though.
“I came to see the shaman.”
“Shaman? Then you have bad timing. You can’t meet with the shaman right now.”
“Why?”
“He is in the middle of a Soul Receival.”
“Soul Receival...?” This was a term I hadn’t even encountered in the game.

“You don’t know about it?” When I tilted my head, the chieftain narrowed his eyes. That wasn’t a huge problem, though. In the past I would’ve flinched, wondering if this was common knowledge that only I didn’t know about.
“I forgot.” Now, after living as a barbarian, I had come to realize that it wasn’t strange for them to lack common sense.

“I see.” As expected, the chieftain readily accepted this excuse and explained what a Soul Receival was. “Soul Receival is a ritual that must be performed by the shaman every few years to be able to make incantations.”
“Then how long do I have to wait?”
“Since the ritual started at the beginning of the month, you should be able to see him next month.”
Hmm, next month, huh?
“Okay. I’ll come back then.” I left my regrets at the door and turned around.

It was late evening, around the time when drunk people began to appear all over the city when we gathered at Mr. Bear’s tavern. Oh, for reference, the closed sign was up today so we were the only ones there. Mrs. Bear was healthy enough to work at the tavern even in her third trimester, but now she was really close to her due date.
“Is it really okay for you to leave her side?”
“Stop fussing. We’ll only be gone for a day—what could go wrong? I’m going to have a baby soon. I need to make more money. My wife agreed to this, so don’t worry.”

“If you say so.” My argument was half-hearted anyway so I said nothing more. To be honest, if Mr. Bear decided to stay behind now, we were the ones who would be screwed. “Then let’s get a binding spell done.”

After a quick meal at Mr. Bear’s tavern, Raven divided us into threes and cast the binding spell. The way we’d divvied our forces was simple. Me, Mr. Bear, and Raven were Team A. Erwen, Missha, and Ainar were Team B. Not that it meant much—we were only traveling separately on the first floor and meeting on the second.
“It’s almost time. Let’s go.”

“Oh, wait.” As we finished our preparations and were about to head to Dimension Square, Raven stopped us. With a somewhat embarrassed look on her face, she took out a few small items from her sub-space. “Um... we’re a clan now, right? I had some free time recently so I made us an emblem.”
Emblems were the symbols adventurers in clans always wore on their armor.
“I did some research while I was making it, and they say the symbolism behind a clan’s emblem is very important. So I borrowed Mr. Yandel’s nickname and made it a Giant...”
“But this looks like an Ogre, not a Giant.”
“Ugh, then never mind!”
“I never said I didn’t like it. Once we get back tomorrow, let’s officially register it as the clan’s emblem at the guild.”

When I said we should register it as our clan’s emblem, Raven’s expression went from stoic to bright. It looked like she was looking forward to that. “Now, everyone, gather round. I’ll attach it for you.”
Raven proceeded to attach the emblem to everyone’s equipment with magic. When we actually put it on, it looked rather cool. Should I say it felt like we’d become well-off adventurers?
“Thanks, Raven. You took care of this without being asked.”
“...Well, it is my clan, after all.”
“That’s what I’m thankful for.”
“Empty flattery. Whatever, let’s just go. We’re going to be late at this rate.”
Oh, so embarrassed.
After we finished installing the emblem, we hurriedly headed to Dimension Square. There were quite a few people around to watch the proceedings, those looking our way from a distance.
“Hey, Bjorn Yandel is there too.”
“He’s going in again already after going through all that?”
“I heard he made a clan, but there’s six of them.”
“But what’s that emblem? Is it an Ogre?”
“The Ogre is one of Bjorn Yandel’s essences.”

The area around the square was crowded with more people than expected, but the number actually waiting to enter was not many—three or four hundred at most. Most of them were low-level adventurers who had no choice but to put on their equipment and come because they were short on cash.
If the other squares in the city are like this, the upper floors will be almost empty.
I spent the rest of the time going through my plans for this quest one last time and before long, a portal opened in the center of the square with a burst of light.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
This time, there were quite a few things for us to get done in the labyrinth.

chapters.title: Chapter 263: Bug (2)
paragraphs: This cave was covered wall to wall in brilliantly-glowing crystals, a place I’d been to many times in the past, but it felt unfamiliar today. Well, maybe that was only natural since it had been two months since I saw it last.
But the other factor must also play a role in that.

Scanning my surroundings, I swallowed my disappointment. First, unlike usual, there were only three of us. Also, while it wasn’t as bright as broad daylight, the area we were in wasn’t dark enough to require a separate torch.
“This isn’t the dark zone.”

Simply put, the experience point copy bug was in fact locked. That meant it would be impossible for us to use the dimensional instability phenomenon to start in front of the portal to the second floor now.
“Do you know anything?” Pretending not to know what was going on, I asked Raven and she carefully came up with a guess.

“I did hear the palace recently put in a big commission to the Magic Tower. I didn’t hear much because I haven’t been around there these days... But now that I think about it, it might have been a portal stabilization job.”

Whew, so that really was what had stopped the bug. Still, Soul Queen had given me time to mentally prepare so I was able to quickly throw away any lingering regrets. Well, what could you do? We’d just have to go classic from now on. We had it easy for several months there, right?
“Let’s get moving.”

Taking a moment to examine the terrain at our starting point, I quickly took out the compass and tried to find our bearings. That was because the number of people entering the labyrinth this month wasn’t that high. If we played our cards right, it might be possible for us to get EXP for opening a portal.
“Abman, summon Iron Bear. We’re going to move a little faster than usual.”
When Mr. Bear called out his summoned beast, Raven automatically got on top of it. “If only Miss Ainar was this soft...”
Oh, these wizards. They’re way too used to riding things.
“Whooom!”

Anyway, as I took the lead and ran, Raven and Mr. Bear followed behind. Our formation had Mr. Bear positioned at the rear, as he was rather sturdy for a long-range damage dealer. Goblins weren’t that much of a threat to me now, but still, you never knew. The most dangerous things in the labyrinth had always been the people.
It looks like there are no bastards from Noark for now...

At first, I was tense as I ran through the cave, but before long, I lowered my caution level one notch. We ran into several adventurers as we sped up, but most were lower-floor adventurers wearing low-ranking equipment. And even that number was small.
It might actually be possible to open the portal.
As time passed, hope gradually grew within me, but it was destroyed the moment I arrived at the start of the dark zone.
“Looks like someone got here first.”

A rank-nine mana stone was on the ground in front of us. It couldn’t have been Missha’s team who passed through here. Maybe Erwen could have led them here fast, but I never taught Missha and Ainar to be so wasteful.
“...Why are you picking it up?”

“A rank-nine mana stone is still a mana stone.” Thinking of the day I crawled down this long passage on all fours, I couldn’t accept throwing away a mana stone. Back then, this little mana stone had been my only hope.
“No, I meant I could pick it up with magic.”
Oh, that’s true.
Did that mean that the party that passed through here hadn’t had a single wizard? At this speed, I had assumed whoever got here first had to be a top-tier team.
“Leait.”

Instead of torches, we lit up the darkness with a light spell and continued running. After about forty minutes, a portal appeared. I hadn’t been betting on it, but the portal had already been opened, just as I expected.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
I left behind my disappointment and threw myself into the portal. Our agreement was to wait upstairs no matter who arrived first.
“...I felt this way in the cave earlier too, but this feels... strange.”
“Right? Things were so intense back then.”
The Goblin Forest was where bastards from Noark and Rafdonian adventurers had engaged in a bloody battle two months prior. But now, our surroundings were quiet and there was no one in sight.
“Looks like Missha’s team isn’t here yet, so let’s take a break for a while.”
After that, we had free time to look around and were able to find traces of people nearby.
“Looks like it’s from the people who got here first. But why are you studying it so intently?”
“It’s just bothering me.”
“Uh, the fact that you’re the one saying that is making me nervous, Mr. Yandel.”
What was this kid talking about? “Don’t just stand around, rest a little. The other team could show up at any time.”
So we each took out our own chairs from sub-space and sat down. Occasionally, goblins approached us, but they did nothing to interrupt our break. Iron Bear could take care of them.

“Excuse me...” In a forest bathed in soft moonlight, a woman who appeared to be in her early twenties opened her mouth to complain. “Now that we’re on the second floor and since there’s no one around, can’t we summon Yongyong?”
“No. With that size, it will surely leave tracks.”
“Come on, Sis. Don’t be like that. We’re not the only summoners here, right?”
“Carmilla, stop it. Ms. Rainwales said no.”
“Hey, Mister. You keep your mouth shut.”
“Then stop acting up so I won’t have to open my mouth. Why are you so tired, anyway? You were sitting on my shoulder the entire first floor too!”
“Ugh, you smell like a widower, okay? It’s making my clothes smell. It’s hurting my nose!”
“...What did you just say?” The warrior carrying the woman paused at the brutal verbal attack, but only for a moment. He let out a sigh that implied he was used to this treatment.
“Huh? What could I possibly say to you?”
“Then don’t say anything in the first place!”
“Carmilla, I get you’re sensitive these days, but stop acting like a child. You’re not the only one on this mission.”

“Ugh, you and your scolding...” The woman named Carmilla pouted. She wasn’t pleased with this entire situation. “But why do we still have to carry out our mission, anyway? When everyone’s left us behind to escape outside, what difference is killing that adventurer going to make?”
“...I’m sure they have their own circumstances to worry about. They contacted us a few days ago.”
“Oh, right. The call that cut off in ten seconds after they just said what they wanted to say?” Carmilla spoke caustically and the archer frowned.
“They asked us to be understanding about that. It’s impossible to maintain a call for long because of the barrier. But they said they have a way to get us out too, so we just have to do our job—”
“How naive. You don’t think that could be a lie?”
“...Then why did you come all this way, Miss Carmilla? Why not stay in the city?”

“That’s...” Carmilla trailed off and bit her lip. How could she admit it? In truth, she had followed them because she had been too scared of how that woman would react if she made a fuss about not wanting to go.
Ugh, just what is happening?
Irritated for some reason, she returned her attention to the archer, her tone sharp. “Anyway, Nebarce. What happened to the Fallen Scholar? You were the one who was with him until the end.”
“I told you. The Fallen Scholar was talking to that guy before he disappeared somewhere—”
“Everyone, stop.”
When the woman clearing the way stopped walking, the archer also stopped and smoothed out his expression. “Amelia, is something wrong?”
“The trap set near the portal is gone.”
“That means someone has come up to the second floor. Judging by the time, it must be a high-level adventurer... It could be that more adventurers have entered than we expected.”
“Nebarce, any teams you can think of?”
“I’m not sure. But it can’t be a large clan. They wouldn’t make a move when things are still uncertain.”
“I see.”
Carmilla butted into the middle of their conversation. “But does it matter who it is? I don’t know why you’re all curious about that.”
“...You’re definitely not wrong.” At her words, Amelia seemed to fall deep in thought for a moment. “But it’s bothering me for some reason,” she muttered.
“Sorry? What did you say?”
Amelia shook her head. “...It’s nothing. Let’s keep moving.”
“Did you wait long, Mister? I’m sorry. It took some time because we ended up starting in the southern district.”
After we waited about two hours in the forest, Missha’s team arrived on the second floor and we quickly got moving. That was because while we had been waiting, more than ten teams passed us by.
It’s not as empty as we thought.
The third-floor portal we eventually arrived at was, of course, already open. The same went for the one to the fourth floor, which took us six days to reach.
“But at least we can have a proper meal now.”

Having spent the entire time running without proper food, we replenished our stamina as we cleared the fourth floor’s trials. We were a party of six now, but our speed was slower than usual. That was because once you had six people or more, the difficulty of the trials increased. The fact that more monsters were spawning was great, but in the case of the Trial of Wisdom, where you had to pass through a maze, the map got even bigger and it ate up a lot more time.
I guess race still plays a role. She’s definitely better at finding the way than I am.

Having received scout training from her sister, Erwen found the way better than I ever expected. If my navigating abilities were rooted in knowledge and experience, Erwen found the way by relying on her senses. Her night vision was also much better, so she could spot traps from afar.

“From here on, I know it even without Mr. Abman’s help. It’s this door, right? I can hear the ripples of mana beyond the door.” Erwen had high sensory stats, to the point that she could find the portal leading to the fifth floor even without a scout’s innate abilities. I knew for a fact that none of her essences came with additional hearing stats.
Was she just born with it?
Anyway, when we arrived in front of the portal on the fifth floor, it was around the start of the nineteenth day.
Are we about a day later than usual?

If there were seven of us, the fourth floor would have taken much longer. From then on, the waiting time between each trial increased in proportion to the number of people present. There was a reason large clans were divided into teams of five and chose to meet on the fifth floor.
“But why don’t they meet up on the second floor and hunt like we did, Aruru?”

“They’d have to divide the loot into an extra share and it’s just not worth it on the lower floors. Besides, if you split a team into two, it’s important to have a scout on each side. There are many non-combative adventurers on the lower floors, right?”
“Hm! I see!”
“I... see what you’re doing now! You didn’t understand what I said at all but you still nodded anyway, right?”
“Oh, you really are a wizard!”
“Both of you, stop fooling around and go to sleep.”
It was time to camp out anyway, so we all entered the fifth floor early in the morning after resting on the fourth floor, where it was safe.
[You have entered the Great Demon Realm on the fifth floor.]
The fifth floor looked a little different than usual even from the get-go. Which was exactly what I had been hoping for.
“It’s nice and quiet.”
There weren’t any of those clans who always arrived first to secure a spot and control the hunting grounds.
“Oh! Over there! It’s an Istoltos!”
Monsters you wouldn’t have even been able to catch sight of in the past unless you paid a clan now roamed the map freely.

“So this place was originally filled with this many monsters,” Mr. Bear said simply. True, this guy had been active on the fifth floor for a while now. As much as he harbored ill feelings toward clans, it must have felt strange for them to not be here. “Yandel, what do you think? Things won’t be this way for long, will they?”

“Yeah, it probably won’t last long,” I answered honestly. Even starting next month, large clans would probably begin entering the labyrinth one by one. And after a while longer, newly-created clans would fill the vacancies the old ones left behind. “So let’s stop gawking and get moving. Opportunities like this don’t come often, after all.”
There was a monster that would be difficult for us to get our hands on if not today.

chapters.title: Chapter 264: Bug (3)
paragraphs: I was walking over a precarious canyon. I was in the lead, my tank assistant Iron Bear was heading up the rear, and the rest were clustered together in the center.
“Keeek!”
With every step we took, I could hear the shriek of ghost-type monsters beyond the darkness. This was a distinct feature of one of the four routes connecting to the sixth floor, the Canyon of Ghosts.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Canyon of Ghosts has activated.]
The ground beneath us shook vigorously every few minutes and the eerie moans of ghosts served as background music on our journey.
[Status effect Restligeist is now active. Your Dark Resistance and Physical Resistance have decreased by -100.]
And that wasn’t even mentioning the strange, unpleasant feeling that our skin had grown thinner.
It seems creepier now that I can’t see other adventurers.
It had already been one day since we’d entered the Canyon of Ghosts but we still hadn’t run into anyone else from the industry yet. The only things we’d encountered so far were monsters.
[You have defeated a Curse Stone. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Corrupted Creature. EXP +2]
[You have defeated a Bloodshot Ghost. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Dakirion. EXP +5]
[You have defeated an Ancient Spider. EXP +2]
Well, still, that was more a pro than a con. We were able to obtain most of the experience points available on this route in just one quest.
I think we’ll just need to pass through here one more time to find the ones we couldn’t this time around...
“Be careful not to fall.”

Aside from stopping each time the ground shook, we invested all of our time in combat and travel. We only rested when we made camp. It was a bit of a tight schedule, but oh well. Since we’d recovered quite a bit of stamina on the fourth floor, we would be fine for a few days.
“That’s fascinating. I thought the next district would be Frost Canyon.”
“Back then, we weren’t ready to move on to the sixth floor. This route is the most direct route to the sixth floor.”

“Hmm, I did hear something like that... But if that’s why we’re going this way, wouldn’t it be better to pass through Hellfire Gorge, which we’re familiar with, instead of this place we’ve never been to before?”
“But we’ve collected all the achievements there.” I’d given Raven all kinds of explanations for why I’d brought us here, but in truth I had a different reason for taking this route.
Because I already got the essence I wanted from Frost Canyon.
The essence I’d originally intended to give Missha had been awarded to her by the palace.
And more importantly, that guy spawns here.

The monster we’d have to track down and overcome if we wanted to enter the sixth floor appeared on this route. Of course, I couldn’t flat-out say that guy was our objective. If I did, I’d have to answer the question of how we were going to find it, and I didn’t have a good explanation for that. It was best to let them write it off as luck.
“Mister.”
Huh?
“We have to go this way.”
Setting those thoughts aside and looking ahead, I saw a three-pronged fork in the road in our way. Actually, it would be inaccurate to call it a “road.”
“The gap is bigger this time. I’ll go over first and throw the rope.”

Jumping over thirty yards in one go using Leap, I tossed the rope I had prepared to the opposite side of the cliff. This was the fun thing about the fifth floor’s Great Demon Realm. The number of available routes increased depending on your character’s abilities.
“It’s secure! We’re coming over now!”
When they finished securing the rope, the other members of the party crossed the canyon to where I was. Thanks to the slope, it was no sweat. You just had to hook onto the rope and slide down.
“Then I’ll be back.”

Once everyone had crossed over, I used Leap to jump back over to the other side and retrieve the rope. You couldn’t just use these like they were disposable, after all. It cost a lot of money to get a specially-made rope of this length.
“Erwen, how far down are we now?”
“About one-seventh of the way.”
“So we’ll be able to reach the sixth floor in a week.”
“Yes. As long as we can maintain our current speed.”
With Erwen’s continued guidance, we quickly progressed down the trail. Her approach to navigation was different from mine—she didn’t make any maps, but she also never got lost or wandered in circles.
“The elf girl is very good at finding her way.”

“I haven’t been to the sixth floor myself yet, but I went down all four routes while working with a clan. And this is the bare minimum of what I should be able to do considering you’re directing us to the portals, Mr. Abman!”
“Please, knowing the location of a portal means nothing on the fifth floor. You should have more confidence in yourself.”
Although they never thought badly of her, Erwen proved her own worth, making the team see her in an even better light. Lately, her relationship with Missha had improved quite a bit too.
“Sis! Come more inside. It can be dangerous walking on the outside...”
“Okay, thanks.”
Anyway, following Erwen’s directions and moving along the shortest route, it soon came time to find a campsite and rest.
“This looks good.”

The location I chose for our camp was near the edge of a cliff, a spot where you only had to guard one side and where even if something went wrong, you could just jump over to the side road about fifteen feet away. Oh, and of course, the order of the night watch didn’t really matter.
“Bjorn, wake up.”
“Another monster?”

Because monsters appeared every twenty minutes with regularity, we had to pick up our weapons mid-sleep. This included Raven, who lacked stamina. We tried to avoid waking her up for the smaller groups as much as possible, but when dozens of monsters rushed in at once, we had no choice.
“...I’m going back to sleep.” Raven yawned.
“Yeah, you worked hard.”
Raven didn’t answer with anything other than a quiet snore. It was kind of funny to watch. She’d become a real adventurer now.
“Ha, she doesn’t even wake at the slightest sound anymorrre.”
“No, I think she does wake whenever there is a sound. But if it doesn’t seem like a big deal, she just falls asleep again.”
“That’s kind of cool. That’s actually the hardest thing to do.”
“Even if it’s hard, it’s about time she adapted.”
“Yeah, that’s rrright... In the end, you can adapt to anything...”

Just like my relationship with Missha. Just like how it had been awkward for a while after entering the labyrinth but we could now have a conversation without too much discomfort, you could get used to anything with enough time.
“Anyway, you should sleep too. I’ll stand watch.”
“There’s still a few minutes until your turrrn, though.”
“It’d be more annoying to wake up again.”
“Mm, but I feel bad, though...”
What was there to feel bad about? We had to wake up in twenty minutes to fight again, anyway.
After that, the expedition continued and ten days had passed since we entered the fifth floor. However, we were still on the fifth floor.
“How long until we get to the sixth floor?” I asked.
“I think it will take about a day,” Erwin answered.
“At this speed?”
“Yes.”
“Let’s call it two days to be safe.”

Unfortunately, the longer the expedition got, the more our speed decreased. That was because we were gradually reaching the limits of our stamina. Well, it would have been stranger if we were somehow fine despite fighting all day without proper sleep. Adventurers were not superhuman. They were just much more capable than ordinary people.
Well, still. We managed to take that guy down yesterday.

Although we were taking longer than expected, we’d already achieved one of the sub-goals of our quest. The rare rank-five monster Soul Eater was a very unique monster in many ways. For one thing, only one of these guys appeared each time the labyrinth opened.
[You have defeated a Soul Eater. EXP +177]

For another, the experience points it gave you was ridiculous. When I saw the XP log after killing one for the first time, I assumed it was a bug. How could I have known that there would be a monster that randomly gave you between one hundred and two hundred EXP the first time you killed it?
I wonder how much I received.
Thanks to the fact that Soul Eater gave you a random value, I wouldn’t be able to accurately track my XP from now on, but I had no regrets. With this, I finally hit level six.
[You have leveled up. Your Soul Power has increased by +30. The maximum number of essences you can absorb has increased by +1.]

Between the Corpse Golem, Orc Hero, Ogre, Manticore, and the essence of the Bayon I had gotten as a reward from the palace, my essence slots were full with a total of five essences. But there was a reason I had entered the labyrinth without erasing the Corpse Golem’s essence to free up a slot—since I’d been doing quite a bit of EXP copying lately, I figured I’d be able to level up just by catching this guy.
“No matter how few adventurers there are up here, I never dreamed we would run into this guy. We were extremely lucky.”
“Haha, I’ve told you several times. Luck follows this team.”
What luck? You don’t know how much effort I put into fulfilling all the spawn conditions without you guys knowing.
“Aruru, this is not a team anymore, it’s a clan!”
“Ah, right... Sure, sure.”
“Cut the chit-chat and focus.”

As the party’s leader—no, clan chief, now—I ensured everyone stayed relatively on task as we kept moving. Excluding the delay, the expedition seemed to be proceeding smoothly, but it wasn’t without its fair share of close calls. Our forces exceeded fifth-rank thanks to the rewards from the palace, but when had stats ever been the end-all and be-all?
“Miss Karlstein, looks like we’ll need to repair your armor as soon as we get out.”
“Ah, rrright... Ugh, honestly. It hasn’t even been long since I bought it. Such a waste.”
There was an incident where Missha was struck head-on by a spear summoned by the Soul Eater. Of course, she got out completely unscathed, but...
“Missha, in what way is it a waste? If it weren’t for your armor, you would have died yesterday.”

The blade sunk deep into Missha’s armor right around her heart. If it had penetrated even the width of a finger deeper, the injury could have been life-threatening. Even just remembering it left me lightheaded. If she were still wearing the grade-two leather armor she had obtained from killing Jencia, who was our first Player Kill opponent, she wouldn’t have even lasted long enough to heal.
I’m so glad I spent the extra money to get rank-five leather armor instead of rank-four leather.
“I mean, a waste is still a waste...”
Huh, she still hasn’t seen sense.
“Enough. Don’t even think about skimping to save money on equipment in the future.”
“Okay...”
This was why low Physical Resistance equipment was unacceptable. You just couldn’t rest easy.
“Ahem, this is heartwarming and all, but why don’t we keep moving?” said Mr. Bear.

After a brief moment of awkwardness following the scolding I gave Missha, we resumed our expedition. About a day later, we traversed the entire Canyon of Ghosts to reach the bottom level, and after traveling down there for another half a day, a portal appeared.
“Wow, we’re really going to the sixth floor...”
“This will be my first time up there too.”
“I’m getting really excited for some reason. I’ve heard so many things about this place.”
As was appropriate for the moment right before you first stepped foot on a new floor, everyone let out exclamations of excitement. I of course felt the same way.
I finally made it to the sixth floor.

The first time I ever saw tax delinquents getting executed in the square, I thought this: in order to live in a house with a kitchen, receive medical treatment when needed, and be able to live a leisurely life with three puppies following retirement at age fifty, I needed to get to the sixth floor. Even here, I’d have to work and save up like a dog until I retired. That was why... As for how to get home, I’d need to worry about that later.
I didn’t expect to get here before two years were up, though.

I was over three years ahead of schedule, but I wouldn’t say that I had been lucky. It’d been thirteen months since I’d woken up in this body. You could say that wasn’t all that long, but too many things had happened to me in that time. I’d struggled hard but still lost someone, and with that legacy on my shoulders, I’d grown into the person I was today.
“Bjorn?”
“Oh, I was just lost in thought for a second.”
“You go in first. You’re the one who brought us here.” Mr. Bear patted me on the shoulder.
Raven poked me in the side with her wand. “Yes. He’s right. If it weren’t for you, Mr. Yandel, I wouldn’t have entered the labyrinth in the first place.”
Oh, don’t rush me.
“Then let’s go in.”
I started walking toward the portal.
[You have entered the Great Sea on the sixth floor.]
Blue sky and beating sun, the smell of salt carried on the wind, and the sound of crashing waves.
Shaaaaaa!
When I found my balance in mid-air and landed, the first thing I saw was a wide, sandy beach. The sand was almost white, and beyond the water-soaked sediment stretched an emerald-colored sea.

Everyone was mesmerized by the sight. I wasn’t much different, either. That was how beautiful it all was. But unlike my teammates, who were seeing the sea for the first time, I was moved in a different sense.
We stood there in a daze, gazing out at the horizon like people who had lost all sense of time. Or, well, I actually came to my senses a while ago.
There’s no need to interrupt the moment, though.

Taking my eyes off the sea, I looked around and studied our surroundings. The starting point on the sixth floor was Laemia, the Island of Beginnings. In the game, it had always been full of people, but there was no one around now.
Well, by this time, they would have already set sail.
I turned my head to the sea again and walked over to Missha to speak to her. “Missha.”
A brief call of her name was enough. “Ah, yeah. Rrright. We need to start with that...” Realizing what I was asking her for straight away, Missha pulled out an item she had been holding dear.
Raven tilted her head. “What’s that stored inside the glass bottle? Looks like an adventurer’s badge...”
“An adventurer’s badge is right.”
“Oh. Could it be...”
“Yes, it’s Dwalkie’s.”
When Team Half-Wit held our simple, private funeral for Dwalkie, we burned most of his belongings but left this intact. It had been the dwarf’s suggestion.
“I heard that place is so mysterious that time flows separately there and it even has seasons, even though it’s inside the labyrinth. Please, do this for him. I’m sure he’ll be grateful.”
“...Even though he’s never been there before?”
“That’s why he’ll like it. Dwalkie definitely will.”
Now, I wondered how he’d really feel. I couldn’t be sure, but here I was.
“Could you wait a minute?”
“Of course. Go ahead.” Raven didn’t argue and stepped back with our other teammates to give us privacy.
“Missha.”
“Yeah.”
Missha and I made our way past the sandy beach toward the sea.
Chwaaaaaa!
Like a beating heart, the waves rose and fell rhythmically. Missha bent over and dipped her fingers in the ocean. “It’s colderrr than I thought it would be...”
“I see.”
“It would’ve been nice if we could have all come here together...”
“Yeah.” It really would have. Even when we first got to the third floor, he had been as giddy as a child.
“...I think I can sort of understand now why adventurers always call it a big world.”

Just a little longer. If only he’d gotten to spend a little longer with us, then he could have seen the real night sky spreading for miles in all directions instead of a Milky Way projected on a rock ceiling.
“Give it to me.”
“Huh? But...”
“If we put it down here, it’ll definitely sink down.”
“Oh, that’s trrrue...”

Without needing any scientific explanations, Missha understood what I was talking about just by looking at the waves. And so I took the specially-made glass bottle from Missha and waded into the sea. The shallow water gradually deepened, and I moved as far away from the island as possible.
“...This should be far enough.”
Even after turning on Giantization, the water rose to right under my neck. I threw the glass bottle as far as I could.
Splash!

Before long, the bottle dropped into the water and bobbed to the surface before beginning to ride the waves to the other side of the island. Okay, got it on the first try. If that didn’t work, I was going to take a boat out.
“Anyway, I tried to make it work with Missha, but it didn’t,” I said, watching the glass bottle float away. Then I chuckled because it was kind of funny. What was I doing? “Get some rest.”

I swallowed all the words bubbling up in my throat and turned around. It wasn’t like he would hear any of it, anyway. But even as I told myself that, I thought this: what would Dwalkie think of me now?
He probably would have been happy.

Even if this may have been an act more for those left behind than anything else, that guy would have smiled. No, he would’ve liked it even more because we were doing it for ourselves. That was the kind of guy he was.
Chwaaaaaa!
Feeling the waves pushing against my back, I glanced back again and said a brief prayer. I didn’t know where that glass bottle would end up.
Chwaaaaaa!
But I prayed that these rolling waves would lead it wherever he desired.

chapters.title: Chapter 265: Bug (4)
paragraphs: “Sorry for taking up time.” When I got back, the first thing I did was offer an apology. That was because these guys had never even met Dwalkie. I thought it was only natural to apologize considering I had consumed quest time for personal reasons. Of course, my teammates’ reactions were considerate.
“There’s nothing to be sorry about. What do you take us for?”
“Yeah, Raven is right. You worry about strange things. Any one of us could be in the same situation as that man someday.”
Uh, I don’t think you should say something like that...
As I was thinking this, Raven addressed Mr. Bear on my behalf. “...Mr. Urikfried, could you please not jinx us like that?”
“Raven, you don’t even believe in superstitions.”
“I’m an adventurer now.”
“Oh, right.” Mr. Bear chuckled and the heavy atmosphere lightened.
Did she purposefully make a joke?
“What are you looking at?”
...Probably not.
At the sight of the defiant look in Raven’s eyes, I chuckled and slowly got us back on track. “Now. If you’ve all rested up, let’s go explore the island.”
It was time to start exploring.

The Island of Beginnings, Laemia, was the first island you arrived at no matter which route you took, but it wasn’t just for this symbolic reason that Laemia was called the Island of Beginnings. There were essential materials for exploring the sixth floor here—at least in theory.
“It’s already been emptied out.”

After climbing to the summit of a mountain nestled in the center of the island, we looked around in frustration. Normally there was a special tree that grew here. It was as hard as grade-three metal and was light enough to float on water.
“Well, no matter how fast this tree grows, there’s no way it’ll fully grow within a month.”
However, when we reached the summit, the only thing we found were thousands of stumps. Well, it wasn’t like there weren’t any trees that were at least somewhat grown...
“Most of these can’t be used.”
“Still, there are some that can. Let’s at least take those.”

Soon we took out the axes we had prepared, picked just the trees that were big enough to be used as material, and packed them into sub-space one by one. It took about thirty minutes to get it all done.
“If all goes well, we should be able to take this much again next month.”
“Yeah. If there are no people then just like this time.”

Man, it would be nice if the sixth floor were reset every month too. It was disappointing in a lot of ways. From the first floor to the fifth, everything was reset when the labyrinth opened the next month, but not from the sixth floor onward. Here, time flowed separately, as shown by the way the marks carved on that huge boulder didn’t get erased from month to month.
“Wow, something is written on the rock! It looks like text... what does it say?”
“Aren’t you going to the holy land every day to learn how to read?”
“Haha, I gave up on that a long time ago!”

Letting out a brief sigh at Ainar’s unnecessarily cheerful reply, I approached the boulder and read the words scribbled on it. Most of it was just rubbish. So-and-so was here, please make me successful, I like you, so-and-so, etcetera.
Looks like people here write graffiti too.
I chuckled and looked away. The vast sea spread out beneath our feet. There may not have been many trees on this island, but this high up, I could see an island that wasn’t visible from below.
“Oh, that must be Farune Island.”
Farune Island was the second island on the sixth floor, located to the north of the Island of Beginnings. It was also the place we would be going next.
“Abman, I’m just asking in case, but can you sense the location of the portal?”
“No, only the one on this island.”
“I see.”

When I nodded, Raven jumped in to defend Mr. Bear. “Don’t be so disappointed. It’s because this floor happens to be incredibly big. I heard if you get near the portal, you’ll be able to sense where it is again.”
What disappointment? Unlike the lower floors, there wasn’t a lot a scout could do on the sixth floor anyway, especially just after entering.
“Anyway, since we got everything we need, let’s go down.”

Finishing my business at the summit, I headed down to the shore again with my party and moved in the direction of the island we saw on the mountain. Originally, the traditional strategy was to make a ship on the Island of Beginnings by uprooting a few more trees.
But the rule of thumb is to skip the labor with money.

I then took out the boat I brought with me from the sub-space and floated it on the water. I’d purchased it with a portion of the amount we’d contributed to our shared fund once the clan was founded. Although I had to spend most of our shared funds to get my hands on it, if it weren’t for the current economic situation in the city, I never would have found it at this price. The timing was good in a lot of ways. Any trees we acquired in the future could be used to upgrade the ship or could be sold as logs to buy a better one.
“Bjorn... th-this won’t sink, right?”
Why you... We even got a boat back in Gnome Tree and fished on it... Oh, that boat did flip over though.
“Don’t worry. I tested it back in the city. It’ll be fine as long as we don’t move too much.”
“B-but... Ack! I-It’s shaking! S-Something’s wrong with the boat! It’s so different from last time!”
“That’s because we were on a lake back then and now we’re on an ocean.”
Actually, the biggest problem was that this boat was twice as small as the one we were on at the time. Anyway, once her freakout was over, we got onto the boat one after another.
“Now, set sail!”

Just as we practiced on the ground in the city, we rowed hard against the waves. That was because our ship had no sails. If I’d bought one with a sail, it would have been too small for even four people, and I didn’t have enough money to buy a big one. There was always something charming about being a newbie, no?
“I-I think the boat is going backward...?”
“You’re mistaken! Paddle harder!”
“One, two. One, two!”
There was a bit of trial and error seeing as it was our first time paddling for real, but like adventurers who were used to forcing the impossible to become possible, we quickly got used to it.
“Oh, the island is getting closer!” It looked like the sailing was getting her hyped up because Raven reacted to every little thing, unlike her usual self. However, her excitement did not last long.
It’s taking a lot longer than I thought...

It didn’t look that far away from the summit but now that we were actually paddling on the boat, it felt like we were moving at a snail’s crawl. Or was I the only one who felt that way? To think we would be faced with a new challenge so soon after entering the sixth floor.
“Blargh.”
“B-Bjorn? What’s wrong!?”
“‘M-Motion sickness...”
It turned out Bjorn Yandel wasn’t made for the sea.
As she watched me half-die from seasickness, Missha asked with worry, “M-Motion sickness? Doesn’t that only happen in carriages?”
I wondered how she could even ask that, but that was probably just my modern point of view. The question made sense if you’d only ever lived within castle walls your whole life.

Raven only seemed to know about sea sickness in theory too. “Motion sickness refers to dizziness caused by a disparity between one’s vision and their sense of balance. That means it doesn’t only happen on carriages.”
“Oh, I see...” Missha nodded and spoke in a tone that clearly implied she didn’t understand anything that was just said. “No wonder my stomach has been feeling nauseous since earlier...”

Although Missha was doing better, barbarian-warrior-from-birth Ainar was even worse off than me. “M-Move! Blargh!” Unable to paddle at all, Ainar grabbed onto the railing and started to empty out her insides.
“Kyaaa!”
“S-Stop! Miss Ainar! You can’t move like that!”
She was vomiting so fiercely that she was making the boat teeter back and forth. Truly, it was so violent that it felt like the boat could flip over at any moment.
“Bleh, blargh!”
“S-Stop!”

As the boat was too small to even stand and walk around in, there was no way for any of us to physically stop Ainar. Plus, four of the six people here couldn’t swim. Excluding Erwen and Missha, no one knew how. And since we were quite far from the island, even if I used Giantization like last time, my feet wouldn’t be able to touch the ground.
Wait, isn’t this a really dangerous situation, then?
When it occurred to me that this couldn’t be passed off as no big deal, I quickly assessed the situation and gave orders. “Raven! Knock her out with magic!”
“Ah, right! Seretara Bayreon!”
“Uh, whoop, huh...? Hnng...” Thankfully Ainar didn’t have proper Mana Resistance stats yet so she lost consciousness with one shot of magic.
“U-Um, Mister... I-I think I’m going to die.”
“Uh, me too. I should do that, too.”
Unable to withstand the force of nature that was Ainar, our party members were incapacitated one after another.
“Still, Mr. Urikfried is surprisingly okay—”
“...Bleghhh!”
“U-uh... Mr. Yandel is all—”
Of course I wasn’t.
“Grrruh!” I vomited while grabbing the guardrail as gently as possible while someone sighed behind me.
“...Why is there not a single normal person here?” Surprisingly, Raven did not get sick.

The concept of the sixth floor was simple: sail the vast sea and pass through various islands to head to the seventh floor. That was why a navigator was essential on this floor, a specialized party member who could steer a boat and map out seaways and had even consumed an essence to help with sailing.
Well, the applicants for that position will flood in as long as we have a proper boat so there’s no need to be impatient.

Stepping off the bow, I pulled the boat to shore myself and put it in sub-space to make sure I couldn’t lose it. It was a method that I could only use now while we were sailing a small boat. If we wanted to cross this damned ocean and its many calm areas and seas of ice, we’d need a big boat.
That’s another reason why it’s recommended you travel in a clan from the sixth floor onward.
Since boats were so expensive, adventuring on a team scale on the sixth floor couldn’t be anything but a financial burden.
“Whew, land! Land!”
The sun was starting to set in the distance. Arriving at Farune Island, we had a simple meal and immediately got ready to set up camp.
“So the sunset can look like that...”
“Yeah. For the first time today, I’m glad that I became an adventurer.”

Having only ever seen the sunset over the castle walls, seeing it over the mountains left a great impression on my teammates. Actually, I felt the same. Being on a sandy beach like this really made me feel like I was on an island somewhere on Earth. I’d never actually visited an island like this, though.
Why didn’t I go back then...?

For the first time, I regretted the way I used to spend all my time holed up in my room, playing games. At the time, I had been living in what was undoubtedly an even greater world without any castle walls.
“Ainar, you go to sleep. We’ll wake you at the end.”
“C-Can I?”
“You did have the hardest time...”
“Thanks, Missha!”
Giving Ainar, who’d had a hard time with seasickness, the last turn, the rest of us decided on the watch order.
“I don’t think we need to stay up in pairs. I heard only monsters below rank eight appear on this island.”
“Okay. Let’s take turrrns on our own and wake everyone else up if something happens.”
“Um, but if we’re going to do that, why didn’t we just sleep on the island we were at? There were no monsters there.”
“At the time we didn’t know it’d take this long to arrive.”
“Oh... right.”
Because it was a moderately warm day, we just placed our sleeping bags on the sand and laid down, although we’d brought a tent with us because it often rained here.
“It’s prrretty.”
“Yeah, you’re right.”
As we looked up at the Milky Way stretching across the sky, we all came to a wordless agreement to stargaze tonight.
“...My wife would have liked this too.”
“You make it sound like she’s dead. I’m going to tell her you said that.”
“...W-What are you talking about? I-I just meant I’m sad about her quitting adventuring! That’s it!”
“Stop the chitchat and go to sleep. We’re going to explore the island as soon as the sun rises tomorrow.”
Was it because it was our first night on the sixth floor? It seemed everyone felt restless, and it took a long time for us to fall asleep.
“I want us to take a look around the coastline first before heading inland.”

The next morning, waking up early, we cleaned up our campsite and trekked around the island in a full circle. Not for any big reason—I just wanted to see with my own eyes how big the difference between the game and reality was.
The island is bigger than I expected.
That was the thought I had when we were halfway around the island.
“Oh, Bjorn! There’s a boat over there!”
We discovered a boat anchored on the shore. It wasn’t at the level of a large sailboat, but it was still about three times the size of ours and it had everything it needed.
“With this, the calm zone and even the icy seas would be no problem. Ah, but of course, it’s branded by the owner.”
“Oh, does that mean we can’t take it?” Ainar tilted her head innocently at Raven’s explanation.
“Hey, barbarian. What are you doing in front of our boat right now?” The owner of the boat appeared from further inland. “No, wait, hold on—are you that barbarian from back then?”
I recognized that face. “Long time no see.”

chapters.title: Chapter 266: Bug (5)
paragraphs: He laughed when I said, “Long time no see.”
“I didn’t think you’d remember me.”

I guessed he was surprised that I recognized him. True, it had been a short encounter, after all. We hadn’t had an opportunity to have a conversation one-on-one, let alone properly introduce ourselves.
“Memories like that are not easily forgotten.”
But how could I forget the time I had to crawl through a dark cave on all fours while one foot was fucked up and bleeding everywhere?
“Patzran, will you hand me a potion?”
“I was keeping it handy for when I can’t use divine power.”
“You have a lot anyway. I will pay for it when we get out.”
“Tsk.”

This guy, who was the swordsman of the group that saved me, had tossed his leader a potion with a displeased look on his face. It was a novel experience. How many times in your life did you feel humiliated and grateful at the same time?
“I like this aspect of barbarians. Your iron rule is to repay a debt, isn’t that right?” The guy interpreted my words to mean what he wanted them to mean, a pleased smile on his lips.
I didn’t bother to correct him. Well, it was true I was grateful. “Still, what a surprise. I didn’t think you would remember me, either.”

“There aren’t many people who could crawl that far a distance in a state like that.” The guy looked me up and down. “Anyway, to think you were that Bjorn Yandel.” With no need for introductions, this guy inferred my identity just from my appearance. Hm, I didn’t know if I should considered that a good thing or a bad thing.
As I chuckled, Raven approached me from behind. “Long time no see, Mr. Patzran.”
“Who... Ah, Miss Raven?”
I was just as surprised as the swordsman. What, they knew each other?
“Right... yes. I did hear you joined this team.”
“We’re a clan now, not a team. But, anyway, wow! I had no idea you and Mr. Yandel knew each other. Is this fate?”
“What fate? We don’t even know each other’s names yet.” When I jumped into the conversation, the swordsman laughed and revealed his name.
“Malmern Patzran.”
“What a strange pronunciation.”
“My house is one that still insists on a traditional naming style. Call me Patzran. That’s what everyone calls me.”
“House? Are you a noble?”
“Noble? Maybe thousands of years ago.”

I understood what he meant immediately. There were cases like this from time to time, people from families who had once been nobility or royalty in countries before the end of the world. But after entering this city, they were degraded to mere commoners. They didn’t have titles, but still sustained their own internal legitimacy by deciding on the heads of their house and the like.
“So, what were you doing in front of our boat?” Once introductions were over, Patzran got to the point.
Because I hadn’t been doing anything in particular, I answered honestly. “We were just looking around the whole island.”

“I see.” My fame was one thing, but since he was acquainted with Raven, Patzran did not doubt our claim at all. “Nervio Pertia.” He activated the magic circle engraved on the ship and reverse-summoned it into sub-space. It was a small act, but one that really bothered me.
“Where is your team from back then?”
“They are exploring the island.”
“I guess that means you’re looking for something?”
“Well, I don’t think we’re well acquainted enough to discuss that.”
Geez, so defensive.
It was a firm answer that set clear boundaries, but I had a general sense of what they were doing.
They docked it on the shore, then sent just one person to put it away...

That had to be because they were looking for something. Most summoning engravings had a cooldown period, after all. If they’d determined there was nothing to look for, they would have left on the boat right away instead of waiting again.
But deactivating the summon means they found what they were looking for.
If so, what could they have been looking for? There was one thing that came to mind. I’d also run up to the sixth floor aiming for it.
If that’s the case, that derails my plans...
Even as I subconsciously licked my lips in regret, I made sure to control my expression so that my feelings didn’t shine through. But it seemed the same went for my opponent.
“Yandel, how long are you guys going to stay on this island?” Patzran asked casually, his tone nonchalant.
Huh, is he trying to feel me out?
“We’ll probably stay here.”
“Stay? There’s nothing special here.”
“This is our first time up here.”

“Hmm, it wouldn’t be a bad idea for you to head to at least the next island...” Patzran said hopefully before suddenly shifting his tone, apparently realizing he’d gone a bit too far. “Well, no matter. I’m sure you’ll figure that out yourselves.”
Yeah, who are you to decide where we’re going?

“Anyway, if you’re going to remain on this island, we might meet again. See you later, then, Yandel.” Soon, Patzran ended the conversation. It was obvious what he was thinking. He probably wanted to hurry off and inform his teammates of our presence.

“Wait,” I said shortly, and Patzran turned around. He seemed curious about why I suddenly called out to him. I couldn’t just let him leave like this, though. To be honest, something had been bothering me the whole conversation. “It’s not just Yandel, it’s Baronet.”
“...What?”
He tilted his head like he might have heard me wrong, so I spoke more clearly this time. “I said it’s Bjorn, son of Yandel, Baronet.”
Who does he think he is, sneakily trying to act friendly? Does he think I’m still the barbarian on the ground from back then?
“Then I’ll get going. Ahem! B-Baronet Yandel...”
When Patzran scurried away from our line of sight, Raven sighed. “...Mr. Yandel, did you have to do that?” It was obvious what she was talking about. She must think I was too harsh.
But I proudly straightened my shoulders. “It’s not like I asked him to speak with the highest honorifics.”
I didn’t ask him to call me Sir Baronet Yandel. Nor did I criticize his casual speech. So what do you mean, ‘did I have to do that’?
“Raven, I’m the one who doesn’t understand you. What other nobleman is this generous?”

“Uh, I don’t have anything to say to that... Still, you’ve never done anything like that before. What on earth happened between you two?” Raven seemed to regard this as some kind of personal vendetta on my part, but that was not the case. I was honestly more grateful to him than anything. But this and that were two separate things.

“Raven, there’s a big difference between speaking to me casually because I told him to and speaking casually first when I never told him he could.” Even when I became a noble, my teammates and acquaintances did not change how they spoke to me. That was because I told them not to. But Patzran? It was probably hypocritical of me to point this out as a barbarian, but he spoke casually to me as soon as he saw me.
“Hah, so you’re saying you did it for your pride as a nobleman? You’re a total noble now.”
What was this kid saying? “Not as a noble, but as a clan leader.”
“...Pardon?”
“Wherever I go now, I represent you all. But should I have just laughed and moved on out of consideration of an adventurer I don’t know well? Just because it’s someone I know?”
“That’s...”

More importantly, their team’s objective appeared to overlap with ours, so we’d run into each other again in the future. That was why I turned on Barbarian Noblesse Mode—I determined that letting ourselves get looked down on from the start wasn’t wise in the long run.
“Sorry for being critical. I didn’t think that far ahead.” Raven lowered her head and apologized. This was one of her strengths: admitting a mistake and apologizing honestly.
“That’s all I need. I’ve already forgotten it.” I waved it off with a generous heart like the barbarian I was and instead asked the question on my mind. “But Raven. Do you dislike nobles?”
“No? Not at all.”
Hmm, really? Your tone was very sharp earlier. Oh, is she close friends with that man? And that’s why she got angry when she saw me bullying him?
I asked her outright because I figured this was a plausible theory, but Raven shook her head again. “Uh, that’s definitely not it. I’ve only run into Mr. Patzran a few times at banquets...”
“Hmm, then why were you so angry?”
“I wasn’t angry.”
“But you were definitely different than usual.”

Raven had a hard time answering my question. Rather than that being because she was uncomfortable, it felt more like she didn’t know the reason, either. “It just bothered me a bit. While other nobles are like that, I hoped you wouldn’t be the same, I guess... No, wait. What am I saying? Ugh, I don’t know, either.” Raven looked confused.

I chuckled. I thought I knew what she wanted to say. Even I would feel weird if Ainar suddenly changed and started acting like an authoritative figure. Mm-hmm, a barbarian’s charm was their mind, which was as simple as stone.

“Ahh, both of you, stop! What is this weird vibe?!” Not liking the awkward air, Missha interrupted and the topic naturally changed. “So, what are we going to do now? There’s still a lot of the island left to explore.”
“Oh, I’m thinking of ending the island tour.”
This should be enough to measure the size of the island, and we’d already confirmed that there were other people here besides us—competitors who may have come to this island for the same reason.
“Then what are we going to do now?”
My answer to Raven’s question was brief. “We’re going inland.”
You couldn’t be an adventurer if you were going to back down just because of some competition.

Farune Island, the island located closest to the Island of Beginnings, was a popular hunting ground. The monsters were all ranked eight or lower, but it was an advantageous spot profit-wise in that insect-type monsters spawned here in large quantities. Yeah, that was if you just looked at the profits.
“Erwen, fire! Fire! Fire! Hurry!”
“O-Okay!”
“Ahhh! I think one went in my mouth!”
“Miss Ainar! A mana stone just came out of your mouth! Did you seriously just chew the monster to death?!”
Krungby was a rank-eight insect-type monster larger than a person’s face that could summon swarms of bugs.
Whooosh!
Each time Erwen and Raven unleashed their wide-range area of effect abilities with magic or fire spirits, we were showered in mana stones, but no one looked happy about it. I was no different.
It’s grosser than I thought.

Even though I considered myself someone with a strong stomach, this was still proving to be a challenge. Thick bodily fluids covered me completely, and the smell of bugs being roasted was repulsive. Man, I wished I didn’t have to know a smell like that existed.
“I never heard there were so many monsters here. But I guess since there are no people around—Kyaaa!”
“Don’t speak! It’s going in your m—mm!”
Even as my clanmates were experiencing the worst moments of their lives, they didn’t ask to go back. The reason for that was simple.
“Bjorn, it looks like you were right.”
“Yes. There has to be something on this island. If not, those people would not have come here with such a big ship.”

Of course, I wasn’t a freeloader, so I didn’t plan to tail them enough to figure out what that was. Not only did I already know what it was, but no one in our clan was morally bankrupt enough to agree to such a plan in the first place. So we decided to look for it on our own under the assumption that something was hidden on the island.
Thanks to that, it won’t seem suspicious even if we find it later.
The problem was Patzran’s team because the hidden feature here was a kind of event that targeted the entire island.
If there’s no one else on the island besides us, there are a total of eleven people.
That still didn’t exceed fifteen people, which was the condition for unlocking the highest difficulty level, but eleven was already difficult enough.
That’s probably why he tried to send us off too. The event would be much easier to get through without us here.
That made me kind of curious. How did he know about this Easter egg? Could there be a player among his party members? Or was he a player?
I’m sure I’ll get a feel for that when we meet—

While I was walking with these kinds of thoughts in mind, Erwen stopped us. “Mister, someone is fighting over there.” She pointed in the direction of the center of the forest. Since this was someone with hearing several times better than ours talking, I was sure she didn’t mishear.
“Looks like Mr. Patzran’s team is hunting,” said Raven. “Hmm, if we run into him here, I think he’ll misunderstand and think we followed him—”
“No. They are not hunting.” The look in Erwen’s eyes was sharp.
“Sorry? What do you mean they aren’t hunt—”
“I mean that’s the sound of people fighting other people.”
In other words, there was a Player Kill in progress.

chapters.title: Chapter 267: Farune Island (1)
paragraphs: People were fighting each other. Those words instantly put me on high alert. It was possible I had gotten a little complacent without even realizing it.
Thump!

There were no adventurers from Noark in the labyrinth. No, there weren’t a lot of adventurers to begin with. But the labyrinth was a place where anything could happen. So, let’s quickly confirm what we knew.
“How many in total?” I lowered my voice to ask.
Erwen answered without a moment’s pause, “At least eight.”
“That means at least two teams are fighting.”
“For now.”
“Anything else I should know about?”
Hmm, that’s not what your tone of voice is telling me. It’s not good to overlook these things. You know how it is in movies.
“Anything else I should know about?” I asked more firmly this time, and Erwen cautiously answered.
“...I don’t have a good feeling about this for some reason.”
Oh, I see.
“Sorry. I shouldn’t have said that...”
I chuckled at Erwen’s uncertain tone. “There’s nothing to be sorry about.”
I felt the same. As soon as I heard that adventurers were PKing each other, an ominous feeling crept up on me. I contemplated how to proceed.
“Yandel, then what should we do now?”
“Arrre you going to save them again...?”
I cocked my head. “Again?”
“That’s what you did on the first floor and when the rrroyal capital caught on fire. Since you like saving people...”

What was she talking about? This situation was completely different from back then. At the royal capital, I just had energy to spare, and had also promised to do so if I had enough strength left. And on the first floor...

“I think I see what the misunderstanding is, but let me set things straight while I have the opportunity.” As a side effect of my actions, I had cleared the way, leading thousands of adventurers and undeservedly ending up a hero. To be honest, it was true that doing so had thawed something inside me, but... “The people I was really trying to save back then were you guys.” My priorities had not changed. I was a selfish person who didn’t deserve to be called a hero. I had enough on my plate just protecting my own people.
“You mean...?”
“There’s no need to get involved when the situation is giving off bad vibes. We are leaving the island.”
Mr. Bear looked uncomfortable. “But is that okay? We don’t know what’s going on—it’s possible they might need help.”
I don’t think he was always like this... Looks like he’s still drunk on the heroism he felt on the first floor.

“Those people are adventurers too. They are in this profession because they’re prepared to face situations like this.” I spoke firmly with the authority of a leader and Mr. Bear accepted this without further argument.
He did raise a belated concern, though. “Raven, are you okay? You seemed acquainted with that man earlier.”

“Mr. Patzran? Well, if the fight is over there, there’s a good chance he’s caught up in it...” Raven trailed off, unable to finish her sentence. Then she looked straight into our eyes and made a firm declaration. “But it doesn’t matter.”
“Doesn’t matter?”

“We’re not that close, anyway. What if we go help and something happens?” It was an extremely adventurer-like, selfish answer. We all fell silent at the words that followed. “...My team is more important to me.”
Wow, she can say something like that with a straight face? This girl has gotten bolder now that she’s a year older. She still looks like a kid, though.
“Then it’s decided.”

As soon as the decision was made, we turned around and ran toward the beach. Our estimated time of arrival was approximately one hour. Since it wasn’t a very big island, we shouldn’t have any issues as long as we got out quickly.

It’s unfortunate we have to leave behind the Easter egg... But we can try again after we observe the situation from outside the island. Yeah, running away is the best thing to do when you’re getting a bad vibe.
I threw away the last of my regrets.
“The beach!”
Arriving at the shore an hour later, we hurriedly pulled out our boat and set it afloat on the waves. Then we got onto it one after another and paddled away from the island.
“B-Bjorn!” It was right when we were starting to let our guards down that the valiant barbarian warrior Ainar let out a fearful shout. “W-What’s happening? T-The sea is...! The sea is rising!”
The calm seas changed in an instant and began to shake the boat violently.
[The offering of Farune Island has been destroyed. The Fury of the Sea engulfs the island.]
God damn it.

The hidden feature of Farune Island was simple: when the offering hidden in the center of the island was destroyed, you proceeded to an event called the Fury of the Sea. It was a kind of siege-themed event. A sea monster rushed toward the island from the shore, and you had to fend it off from inland. What I had been after was the essence of the event’s boss, the rank-four monster Elfrot. It was an essence that either Missha or Erwen could use during the second half. Well, whether it dropped or not was a separate issue. Anyway, that wasn’t something to worry about right now.
At least eight people over there. And six people here...
The highest difficulty level might have been unlocked. No matter what Easter eggs I was after, that meant getting off this island was our top priority.
“W-What is this?”
“The waves are surging all of a sudden. I’ve never heard of this happening before...”
“Paddle! Hurry up and paddle!”
Taken aback for a moment by the rough waves that seemed to be declaring that no one was allowed to leave this island, we hurriedly started rowing. We were almost out.
We can get out of here if we just get a little further.
In the game, even after the event was triggered, it wasn’t impossible to get off of the island, system-wise. It was just that most ships sank before getting that far.
“One, two. One, two!”
We chanted and worked hard to push the boat over the waves.
I should’ve spent more money on a good boat.

It still didn’t feel like we were getting anywhere. It wasn’t just that we were at a standstill—it felt like we were gradually being pulled toward the island no matter how hard we rowed. In fact, that wasn’t just a feeling. It was actually the case.
“B-Bjorn! T-The island is getting closerrr!”

The boat kept getting pushed back even as we tried to break through the waves. It left a bitter taste in my mouth. If only I’d installed a magical propulsion device on the boat, we might have been able to get out.
“Bjorn! The boat is filling with water...!” Ainar cried.
“W-What do we do? It must be leaking somewhere!” Raven called.
When the boat even started filling with water, panic spread among the party. It was nearing time for me to make a decision.
After a moment’s thought, I quickly gave orders. “We’re giving up on getting off the island. Everyone, sit with your backs turned! We’re going to ride the waves as close to the island as possible!”

That was the advantage of a small boat with a maximum capacity of six. It wasn’t that the boat had no distinction between front and back, but that didn’t matter much, especially when it was getting tossed around by the waves like this.
“Place all heavy equipment in sub-space!” In addition to reducing the weight of the boat, I made them remove their equipment in case we capsized. Then all preparations that could be made were made.
“Right!”

Our boat skipped over the ocean with relentless speed, the waves throwing us forward. The oars were now used more to keep the boat from tipping over and capsizing than to move it. But about three minutes later, when the island in the distance had gotten noticeably closer, a huge wave crashed over us.
“T-There—!”
“Kyaaa!”
It completely flipped over.
“Pffft!” My body was submerged in water in an instant. For now, I focused on clinging onto the overturned boat as best I could. “Is everyone all right?!”
“Yeah, for now!”
“I’m all right too!”
At my shout, reports of survival rolled in, but there was one noticeable exception. “What about Raven?” What happened? Did she get swept away?
“Puh, here! I’m over here!”
Jeez, that scared me. Floating on the water while holding onto the overturned boat, we quickly brainstormed.
“What now?”
“Can’t we just stay like this?”
“Uh, it does look like it’s going the right way...”
It wasn’t a bad idea. A boat made of this special, incredibly buoyant wood would never sink even if it was flipped over.
This actually seems more stable than being inside the boat...
Because the waves were crashing toward the island, the boat would head straight to shore without any special maneuvering on our part.
“Hold tight, everyone!”
We held onto the handles of the boat so that the waves wouldn’t carry us off. But about a minute later, we were faced with a new crisis.
Uh, I didn’t think this through...
“There, a boulder! It’s a boulder...!”
As we approached the shore, the boat neared a reef. It would be impossible to change our trajectory at this point.
“Meet at the center of the island if we get separated!” I shouted urgently, preparing for the worst. And right at that moment, the boat hit the reef.
I opened my eyes to the sound of crashing waves. Everything looked blurry like I had something in my eyes, and the distinct, salty tang of the sea was strong in my mouth.
Kakak, kakak, kakak.

For some reason, I heard the sound of gnawing coming from somewhere around my feet. Wondering what it was, I lifted just my head to glance at my lower body and froze in place. A crayfish monster the size of a large dog was scrambling to somehow chew through my foot.
“You have to be kidding.”
You really think that’s going to work? With my Physical Resistance?
Smack!
I used my free foot to shove the Sterrap away, hurriedly got up, and struck it in the head with the plank I was holding.
[You have defeated a Sterrap. EXP +1]
Like the rank-nine monster it was, the crayfish burst into light with one hit.
But where did this plank come from?
I only realized then that I had been holding onto a plank from the moment I woke up. Where did it come from? Without me having to think too hard, the memory came flooding back to me.
Oh, right. The boat got smashed...

The boat had hit the reef and smashed to pieces. I’d grabbed onto the biggest plank I could find and hugged it as tight as I could, figuring that even a barbarian wouldn’t sink with a flotation device.
Did I survive thanks to that?
Having finished processing the situation, I quickly looked around. There wasn’t a single person on the empty shore.
I wonder if the others are all right.

I was sure Raven was fine. She may not have been able to swim, but I saw her use a floatation spell toward the end there. Missha and Erwen could swim, which was a weight off my shoulders. The problem was Ainar and Mr. Bear, who couldn’t swim.
Hah, I hope they safely washed up on shore.

No matter how much I tried to reassure myself, I continued to worry. But even as I did, my hands did not stop taking my equipment out from sub-space and putting it on. A swarm of monsters would soon descend on the island. Seeing as Sterraps were still crawling around, it looked like it hadn’t been long since the event started, but we had to be prepared.
She said there were adventurers fighting each other. What on earth happened that they triggered the event?

There were a few things about this situation I didn’t understand, but they were the kinds of things that weren’t currently answerable. Ha, if I’d known this would happen, I would have just gone to help them. Then at least I’d know what was going on.
Trudge.
I was about to leave the beach and enter the forest when I stopped. That was because I’d heard something from beyond the bushes.
Dash, dash, dash.
It was the sound of someone running.
That’s not a monster.

The monsters on Farune Island were all flying insects that could glide. That meant that it couldn’t be a monster running. It was also highly unlikely it was one of my clanmates because we were planning to meet inside the forest. There was no reason for one of them to run in the opposite direction.
Then is it one of the adventurers who were fighting earlier?

I slowly raised my mace and waited for the figure in question to appear. The reason I decided to wait was simple—there was only one set of footsteps. Even if a fight broke out, I was confident I could get myself out of it. And so, making contact and extracting information was my top priority.
Now.
Measuring the distance through the sound of their footfalls, I abruptly threw out a hand.
Huff, huff.
“Kyaaa, mm—!” My prey was instantly subdued and wriggled in the air.

“Stay still. I won’t hurt you.” My original plan had actually been to swing my mace and subdue them a little more permanently, but I decided to put that on hold. That was because I recognized this face. It looked like the other party didn’t remember, though. “I’ll let you go, so be quiet.”
“W-Who are you...?”
“Didn’t I tell you to be quiet?” I snapped back gruffly, and the priestess in pure white robes trembled. Man, now I felt like the bad guy. “I am Baronet Bjorn Yandel.”
“Ah...!” When I revealed my name, the priestess visibly brightened. She didn’t seem to doubt me at all. It seemed Patzran had told her about me.
“So calm down, Ersina. I am not your enemy.”
“H-How do you know my name...?”
How do you think? Because we’ve met before. I keep saying this, but it was an unforgettable memory.
“Priestess Ersina, could you heal this man?”
“I refuse.”
When this woman refused to treat me, it felt like my world had come crashing down. Welp, whatever. That wasn’t important.
“We can talk about that later. Explain. What the hell happened inside that forest?”
Assessing the situation came first.

chapters.title: Chapter 268: Farune Island (2)
paragraphs: The account of Lairin Ersina, priest of the Church of Tovera, went as follows.
“While we were exploring the center of the island, an unknown team suddenly attacked us.”

They had been ambushed by a team of five people. Each one of them was strong, with equipment from at least the seventh floor, and these guys had been on the verge of annihilation before they could even mount a proper counterattack. The biggest factor was that they lost their wizard right at the start. Well, it sounded like they still fought hard under those adverse conditions.
“The situation continued to deteriorate, and in the end, Mr. Drous couldn’t take it any longer and made a decision.”
One of the team members inevitably made the call to sacrifice himself to save his party. But it was a distinctly different sentiment from the time with Dwalkie.
“...So while your teammate bought you time, you all ran away?” I scoffed.
The priestess blushed, then came up with an excuse. “I was against it. I told him over and over that I could never abandon him, but...”

What was this woman saying? If she had really been against it, she wouldn’t have even been out here for me to run into. “Stop. Enough explaining, just tell me the important parts. What happened after that?”
“...I don’t know what happened to Mr. Drous, but someone started chasing me soon after. As a result, I got separated from my team.”
