No wonder she had been running around all alone. I now got the gist of the situation, so it was time to focus on the details, starting with this one. “But who’s Drous?”
“Guardweaver Drous. He was the blond-haired swordsman who gave you the potion and saved you that day.”
Oh, so his name was Drous. I was finally learning the name of the blond after over a year but there was no time to relish in it. “Who are the guys who attacked you? Describe them in detail.”

Then I inquired into the unidentified team of five and the priestess told me everything she could remember, from their appearances to the abilities they’d revealed in battle, and even the names they called each other. I was listening attentively to every tidbit, knowing that this information could end up saving me, when one thing she said knocked me off my axis.
“Wait, red-haired woman?” The description of one of the attackers matched someone I knew.
“Yes. That woman seemed like the leader of the group. But is there a problem...?”
God damn it, of course there is. How many human women in the city have red hair and use a dagger?
When I asked for more information, even the position of her tattoo and the fact that her right ear was almost cut in half matched up. This meant it couldn’t just be someone who looked similar to her.
Amelia Rainwales, again?
A suffocating feeling began to balloon from deep within my chest, and rightfully so, because Amelia was from Noark. It was highly likely that the other four people with her were as well.
Simply put... that means this isn’t a simple case of looting. Ugh, it looks like I’ve gotten caught up in some real trouble here.
When I unwittingly sighed, the priestess studied me cautiously. “...Have you heard of that woman?”
“Maybe.” Half-heartedly glossing over that, I asked a few more questions. “Now that that’s done, let’s continue our conversation. Ersina, was there anything special about them?”
“By anything special, you mean...?”
“Like, was something strange about them? Do you have any idea why they ambushed you?”
“That’s...” The priestess trailed off and continued after a moment’s thought. “I was in a hurry so I wasn’t able to stop and think, but now that I think about it, there was something strange.”
“Stop dragging it out and get to the point.”

“Mr. Drous said something to us when he stepped forward to buy us time. He said this was his responsibility and that there was no need for us to get involved. At the time, I thought he was just speaking as our leader, but...”
“That certainly is strange.”
“Yes. And he seemed to be acquainted with the people who ambushed us. When they first attacked us, they called Mr. Drous a traitor... and told him to give them something I didn’t recognize.”
What?
“Why are you only mentioning that now?” That was clearly the reason they were attacked.
When I stared at her, dumbfounded, the priestess faltered. “I-I was just so distracted earlier...”
Ignoring the priestess’s frustrating behavior, I found I was starting to get a clearer picture of what was going on in my head.
“Right before Noark went into lockdown, they sent a few people aboveground. Their goal is to kill one specific adventurer! Shocking, huh?”

According to Clown’s statement at the Round Table the month before last, Amelia and a small number of infiltrators had been assigned an assassination mission. Of course, until now, I didn’t know who their target was.
It’s possible this guy was the target.
Then who the hell was this Drous guy?
“But why are you...”
“Baronet.”

“Ah, right... Anyway, why are you alone in a place like this, Baronet Yandel?” This was the priestess’ first question after my interrogation. It seemed she had belatedly grown suspicious of my own circumstances.
“I was trying to leave the island when my boat sank and I was separated from my comrades.”
“Pardon?”
Pardon what? The gist of it was that the two of us would have to work together for a while. “Let’s walk and talk.”
“Pardon? What do you mean... Are you saying you want to go in there?”
“My comrades and I promised to meet up in the middle of the island if we got separated.”

“I-I see. But over there is...” The priestess looked resistant to my suggestion. It was clear what she was thinking. It must have felt like walking into a tiger’s den, but she was separated from her team just like I was.
Geez, this priestess only thinks about herself.

“Don’t if you don’t want to. I’ll go alone.” Instead of politely persuading her, I spoke firmly and the priestess had no choice but to go along with me. Rightfully so, because what could a priestess do on her own? Not only were there no boats in the water for her to use, but even if there were, the sea was in a state like that.
“...But do you know why the wind is blowing like this? Like there’s a sudden storm.”
Actually, that’s what I want to know.
“I don’t know, but monsters are gathering on the shore.”
“...I see.”

This was as much a mystery to me as who the hell Drous was. I knew there had been an ambush, but who had triggered the island’s event and why? If it was someone who knew the triggering conditions, they would have known how dangerous things were about to get too.
Well, I’m sure I’ll find out later.
Like it or not, I was trapped on this island. I would run into Amelia or her comrades eventually.
For now, I’m just going to focus on meeting up with my clanmates.
Shaking off the bad thoughts as much as possible, I headed inland with the priestess. At first, I took the lead and the priestess followed behind.
“This is going to take several hours at this rate. Come here.”

I eventually put the priestess on my back and started running. The monsters we encountered along the way were not a problem. If I were alone, I would have been able to get through scot-free anyway, even barehanded, and priests had a unique skill.
[Lairin Ersina has cast Non-Aggression.]

This buff-type divine spell prevented monsters below rank seven from attacking a designated creature first. It was a bit funny, though, because the Church of Tovera, one of the three churches of Rafdonia, had a very specific rule. The damned rule stated that their divine power could not be used on barbarians.
Ugh, that narrow-minded god.

Apparently, a barbarian got drunk thousands of years ago and peed on Tovera’s statue. As far as I knew, this rule came about after that. It was probably for this very same reason that she hadn’t treated me back when I was crawling through the cave.
“Looks like the sun god is understanding when it comes to breaking the rules at times like this?”

“I understand how you feel, Lord Yandel, but please do not insult him,” the priestess retorted, her tone growing a bit sharp at my barb. “Breaking the rules is my own problem. If you need to condemn someone, condemn me.”
Jeez, so blunt.
“There’s been a misunderstanding. I had no intention of condemning you.”
Yeah, no, you’d better use it if you want to live. No matter how much you love your god, I’m sure you don’t want to go meet him so early.

“If you were hurt by what happened back then... I apologize. But the reason why I insisted on following that rule that day was because it was an issue that could be solved with a potion. It really wasn’t to forsake you.”

That did make me feel a bit better. “It’s fine. I understand your situation too,” I replied, brushing off any lingering resentment. What could an individual do against the decision of a group? “Anyway, let’s stop talking about this. That’s not important right now.”
“Yes.”
The chitchat ended there and we focused on moving from that point on. A long while later, we arrived at our destination at the center of the island.
“H-Here it is. The plunderers attacked us here—”
“Be quiet.” There was nothing around. All that was left were traces of a battle from a little while ago. “...I think you can drop your divine power.”
First, I got the priestess to terminate her divine spell. Then I slowly searched the area. It looked like I was the first to arrive, as none of my clanmates were there.
“There’s really no one here...”
I couldn’t even see the corpse of the wizard who had apparently been the first casualty, not to mention the team leader, Drous, who had opted to sacrifice himself. What really happened here?
“Then what are you going to do now?”
I answered the priestess’s question without hesitation. “We will wait until someone arrives. Friend or foe.”

“Right, I see. All right.” Contrary to my expectations, the priestess did not complain about my decision and accepted it. When I asked why, this was the answer I got in return: “I have to reunite with my teammates as well.”
“What do you mean?”
“It’s impossible to get off the island, anyway. If my teammates escaped and ran into your comrades on the beach, they are likely on their way here now.”
So, that was how far ahead she had been thinking when she decided to follow me. “Ersina, are you not afraid that all your teammates are dead?” I asked nonchalantly.

“Of course I am afraid,” the priestess answered. “But all I can do is have more faith the more afraid I become.” Oh, right. She was a priestess. For a moment, I wondered if I’d asked a pointless question. “That is all that’s permitted to us.”
But she wasn’t exactly wrong.
Please, I hope everyone is safe...
That was about all I could do right now.
The harsh sound of crashing waves pounded against her eardrums.
“B-Bleghhh...!” Missha opened her eyes, regurgitating the seawater filling her stomach. Then she hurriedly scanned her surroundings. “A-Ainar!”

Her heart dropped. Ainar had been right next to her until the very end, after the shipwreck. Missha had clung onto Ainar through those raging waves with the single thought of taking care of her, as Ainar couldn’t swim.
“I lost herrr.”
All kinds of anxious thoughts filled her head. Was Ainar okay? What would she tell Bjorn when she saw him later? No, was Bjorn even—
Slap!
Missha slapped her cheeks with both hands. That sobered her up.
“Think positive, positive...”
She had woken up on the shore in one piece even after losing consciousness.
Everyone will be fine. Yeah, so...
“Meet at the center of the island if we get separated!”
Missha thought back to Bjorn’s shout earlier and brushed the dirt off her hands and face. She slowly walked toward the forest.
Tap.
Then she heard something nearby.
“...Ainar? Is that you, Ainarrr?” Missha shouted despite her raspy voice. She ran in the direction of the sound and soon encountered a stranger.
“You.”
“H-Huh?”
“You are Bjorn Yandel’s comrade.” It was a red-haired human woman who was missing half of her ear, a scar her only memento.

chapters.title: Chapter 269: Farune Island (3)
paragraphs: There was a woman glaring at a particular spot. At the end of her line of sight was the body of a man, Guardweaver Drous—a piece of trash who had tried to avoid karma and live a second life under a new name.
Or at least, she should have been glaring.
“Amelia, why do you look so down?”
Amelia bit her lip involuntarily. This didn’t feel as therapeutic as she thought it would.

“Because his teammates ran away? Come on, don’t worry so much. The other two went to look for them, right? They’ll catch them soon.” Even her immature comrade who had spent the entire journey complaining was now tiptoeing around her, but Amelia did not have the presence of mind to care.
“This is my responsibility. There’s no reason for you all to get involved. So, go!”

The image of this guy sacrificing himself for his comrades kept lingering in her mind’s eye. At first, it was ridiculous. What the hell was this guy saying after betraying them like that? And for people who had no idea what kind of person he was?
Her molars ground together. If he had been capable of that this whole time, why hadn’t he done it for them?
“Still, we got our stuff back, right? Even if those guys escape alive, our mission is a success.”

Only then did Amelia clear her mind and shift her gaze to the jewel in her hand, an artifact left behind by the Great Sage Gabrielius, and a treasure protected by the lords of Noark’s castle for generations. Come to think of it, she was unsure about this thing too. To be precise, she kept thinking about what Drous had said as she took it away from him.
“Amelia, this won’t change anything.”
How could he say that when he knew what this object meant to her?

Amelia used some of the poison in her possession to dissolve the man’s corpse. Then she placed the jewel she was holding into sub-space. All of Noark’s leaders had left for the outside world and couldn’t be communicated with, anyway. She would be the one to hold onto it for the next while. There was no rush, so she planned to go back and find a way to use the gem later.
I finally have it.
Regardless of any uncertainty, her long-cherished dream was nearing fulfillment. With that thought in mind, Amelia shook off her unease.

“But, Amelia.” Carmilla, the team’s summoner and also the woman who was in possession of their mode of transportation on the sixth floor, latched onto Amelia’s side. Her eyes were full of curiosity. “Is this really it?”

It wasn’t that Amelia couldn’t understand how she felt. This item was talked about like a legend within Noark, and in some ways, it was considered more fictional than the Stone of Revival. That was why Amelia didn’t want to confirm anything.
“I don’t know.”

Of course, she knew that the stories about this item were not simply made up and that the item she had just placed into sub-space was unmistakably genuine. But to see something was to covet it. It would be foolish to tell Carmilla the truth and invite trouble.
“Ah, don’t be like that. You knew who that man was too. I’m pretty sure you know whether that thing is real or not.”

Amelia once again shut her down. “Again, I don’t know. And whether this is really that item or not is none of our business. Our mission was only to reclaim what he had on him and get back to the city.”
Just as she was about to turn around, Carmilla grinned. “Judging by that reaction, I guess it really is that thing? Wow, I didn’t think it really existed.”
The words might sound like a lighthearted comment to some, but having seen all kinds of ugly things in her life, Amelia instinctively reached for her dagger. And at that moment—
Stab!
—warmth began to radiate from her back.
“I’m sorry, Lady Rainwales.”

It had been a mistake to only be wary of Carmilla. By the time she came to her senses, the warrior’s sword had penetrated her stomach. But, so what? In the time it took to reflect on her misstep, Amelia made a decision.
“Good job, Mister!”
The blade was buried under her ribs.
“When will you start calling me Brother?”
Her organs were damaged, but it wasn’t an instant-death kind of injury.
“Whatever, we’re only half-related!”
Amelia quickly pulled out her dagger and thrust it forward. Her target was Carmilla, the woman she’d fantasized about killing time and time again.
Whip!
Unfortunately, her reach was a bit short. Of course, that didn’t really matter. She’d picked up on a little trick while fighting that barbarian in the past.
Whooom!
As soon as an aura was imbued on the tip of the blade, it could compensate for the gap.
Stab!
“Aaagh!”
The tip of the dagger punctured Carmilla in the eye.
“Pity.” If it had just gone a little deeper, it could have stabbed her brain.
Pluck!
Before she could feel disappointment, the blade in her stomach was pulled out. The recoil made her stagger, but there was no time to rest.
“God damn it!”
The warrior’s sword immediately swung for her vitals. Judging the attack too difficult to avoid, Amelia raised her arm. That was because her arm wasn’t vital.
Slice!

The sharp longsword cut through her arm. She managed to preserve her life but suffered a great loss. This wasn’t all that big a problem, either. If her main body was busted, she’d just have to fight using clones.
Dash.
Amelia used Doppelganger’s Self-Replication, created a clone right behind the warrior, and immediately aimed a kick at his head, a combo most enemies couldn’t even react to.
“B-Behind you!”
The clone’s foot came into contact with her opponent and an explosion sounded.
Bang!
But the sound didn’t come from her target, the head.
“Ugh!” Her foot had landed on the warrior’s shoulder. The timely warning had allowed the warrior to twist his body out of the way.
Stab!
The price for her failed assault was the warrior’s sword sinking into her stomach once again, although her clone’s interference made it so the sword didn’t dig in too deeply.
I could die if things keep going like this.
This was dangerous.

“What are you doing?! Grab the arm, quick!” The moment the thought popped into Amelia’s mind, the warrior rolled onto the ground and picked up her severed arm. It was wearing a sub-space bracelet. Frustrated, Amelia used her clone to quickly chase the warrior down.
“Let’s go, Yongyong!”
She was three steps too short.
“Kwaaaa!” The warrior got on top of the Drake Carmilla summoned before the clone could reach him.
Whoom! Whoom!
The Drake soared up into the sky in an instant. She could hear the conversation the two were having under the loud flap of its wings.
“...Amelia Rainwales. She’s a terrifying woman. I never thought she could be so menacing even in a state like that.”
“Whatever, just give me a potion!”
“First, we need to talk. What now? We couldn’t even kill her properly.”
“Ugh, what does that matter!? She’s going to die anyway...”
That was the extent of the conversation she could pick up on with her advanced hearing because they had completely disappeared into the sky.
“Damn it.” Amelia let out a curse for the first time in a while, but it changed nothing. Taking action was the only way for her to save herself from ruin.
Trudge.
Amelia used her intact clone to carry her main body and quickly left the area, judging that if those guys decided to come back down and make a confirmed kill, that would really be the end of her.
Trudge, trudge.
Amelia continued to move, not quite sure which direction she was headed. A while later, she was sent sprawling after her MP bottomed out and Self-Replication came to an end.
Tap.
She froze at the sound of a nearby presence. If it was one of her comrades, she would live, but if it wasn’t, she would die. It was an either-or situation that would decide between life and death.
“...Ainar? Is that you, Ainarrr?”
Surprisingly, both of Amelia’s predictions were wrong. “You.”
“H-Huh?”
“You are Bjorn Yandel’s comrade.” She lifted her head, and a glance at the sides of the woman’s skull confirmed her suspicions.
Slump!
It was a cat.

“Ahhh, who is this lady!?” Missha was confused. That made sense. Anyone would have been if a woman with a severed arm and a hole in her stomach collapsed in front of them. “U-Uh... is this one of the adventurers who were fighting? PPotion. Yeah, potion first...”

The woman was unfamiliar, but Missha opened her water-soaked expandable backpack anyway and pulled out a potion. Whether this woman was good or bad... No. There was no intel as to whether there had been any good people here in the first place.
“You are Bjorn Yandel’s comrade.”
But the woman’s last words before she collapsed removed any hesitation Missha may have felt. Yes, she might be acquainted with Bjorn. Missha decided to treat her before anything else.
Pong!
Removing the potion’s stopper, Missha hurriedly poured it on the woman’s wound.
Rumble.
She didn’t hear the characteristic hiss of a potion boiling on someone’s skin. The potion just flowed down the wound like cold water.
“Eh? I bought this from an authorized general store!”
It was confounding, but having had the misfortune of purchasing counterfeit potions in the past, Missha took another potion out of her bag. The same thing happened again.
...Uh, why isn’t this working?
Was this one fake too? Missha then poured a little bit of the potion on a cut she’d gotten after falling in the water.
Chhh!

Seeing as it itched like crazy, the potion was fine. So why wasn’t it working on this woman? She had no way of knowing, but Missha didn’t give up. She’d learned from Bjorn that the barbarian way was to chew with your gums when you didn’t have any teeth left.
I haven’t used these in a long time...
Missha took out herbs and bandages. These were first-aid supplies she’d kept to use on the off chance she ever ran out of potions.
“This is going to sting a little... Oh, you can’t hear me, anyway.”

Washing the wound with an antiseptic first, Missha applied the herbs and bandaged it. Then she laid a blanket on the ground and laid the woman on top. That ended her first aid. Since she had done all she could, the rest was up to the woman.

“At least she’s brrreathing all right...” After taking a moment to observe, Missha confirmed the woman’s breathing had stabilized and squatted down next to the blanket. Then she let out a sigh. “Ugh, I can’t just leave her herrre...”
If she were just unconscious, Missha would have carried her, but because her condition was so grave, that was impossible.
“Bjorn will be waiting...”
Missha sulked, but she couldn’t leave the woman like this. She passed about ten minutes pouting.
Squeak, squeak, squeeeak!
Missha turned her head at an unpleasant sound. “Ugh, what’s going on now?”
Monsters were crawling out onto the shore.
The sound of flesh colliding with flesh rang out periodically. I just couldn’t keep my body still, so I kept messing with my hands incessantly.
Two hours.
It had already been that long since I’d arrived at the center of the island. No matter how fast I got here, one of my clanmates should have shown up a long time ago.
Why is no one coming?

Even if I tried to have faith, dark possibilities kept filling my head. Missha, Raven, Mr. Bear, Ainar, and Erwen... Were they really okay? If I knew this would happen, I would have searched the coast, not come to the center.
“Do you intend to stay here?” the priestess asked carefully as I vibrated with anxiety. To me, she looked like a fucking cult member at that moment.
You told me to have faith earlier.
“You’re a priestess. Why are you so quick to give up?” I grumbled, but I knew in my heart that even taking her class into account, her reaction wasn’t out of left field.
Squeak, squeak, squeeeak!

As if to validate that, marine monsters that only ever showed up after the event started began appearing here as well. They had walked all the way over here from the shore, at a pace less than half the walking speed of a normal person.
In a little while, this place will be filled with stronger guys. The coast will already be riddled with them.
Even still, no one arrived.
“Ersina.”
“Yes, go ahead.”
“We’re moving. Waiting really doesn’t suit my personality.”
“Looks like your faith hasn’t faltered.”
What was she saying? She was the one who told me that all we could do was have faith.
“If you were born human, you might have been a great religious figure.”
A religious figure, my ass. That felt strange to hear as a proud modern-day atheist, but her tone was closer to admiration than sarcasm, so I didn’t argue with her.
“Enough nonsense. Get up.”
“Okay.”
I pulled the priestess to her feet and prepared to leave. Just as I was about to go, our first visitor in two hours arrived.

Unfortunately, it was not one of my party members. His skinny body was covered in minor injuries, probably from an arduous battle that took place just a short while ago. A longbow was slung over his shoulder. Even his green hair was covered in dirt.
“...Lord Yandel.” Friend or foe? It wasn’t hard to figure out, considering the question that left his mouth the second he spotted us. “You two... What have you done to Lady Rainwales?”
This was all very coincidental.
You see, I actually had a question for you too.
Ignoring the sudden ringing in my ears, I asked, “Hey, why do you have Raven’s sub-space ring?”
You’d better have a good answer, or else you’re dead.

chapters.title: Chapter 270: Farune Island (4)
paragraphs: The sea surged with powerful waves. Arua Raven was currently flying above the chaos, screaming at the top of her lungs for the first time in a really long time. “Mr. Urikfried! You’ve got this! We’re almost to land!”

She looked down from the sky; Abman was in the water getting swept back and forth, relying on a single plank to stay afloat. Every time the waves crashed over the board Raven’s heart constricted, but there was nothing more she could do.
I have to take care of at least Mr. Urikfried...
The moment the ship capsized, everyone separated and disappeared, and the only one she found while searching the area was Abman. She kept following him so as not to lose track of him.
“Huh?”
Abman apparently lost his grip on the board, because his body disappeared beneath the surface of the water. Raven hastily dropped her altitude but Abman was nowhere to be seen.
“Mr. Urikfried! Mr. Urikfried!” she screamed as she searched the area for a while, but there was no reply. Raven trembled, a chill running through her. “...No, he’ll be fine.”
Forcing the trembling down, Raven steeled herself and moved toward the shore.
“Found you!” Scouring the coast, she finally found the person she was looking for. Abman had been washed up by the waves and was passed out on the sand. “Whew.”
He was breathing all right, and his body temperature hadn’t dropped that much. Raven quickly used a flame-type support spell to dry Abman’s wet clothes and body, then waited for him to wake up.
It was then that a man emerged from the woods.
“You’re not the one I was looking for... But this isn’t too bad, either.”
Blood rushed to my head. Why did this guy have Raven’s ring? No matter how positively I tried to think, I couldn’t come up with an explanation that was anything other than bad.

“Hey, why do you have Raven’s sub-space ring?” I asked, still clinging to a last shred of hope. “Explain.” Praying there was some kind of misunderstanding at play here that I couldn’t see, I exercised superhuman patience. But the answer I got in return wasn’t what I expected.
“I’ll ask the questions first.”
Don’t want to give me the upper hand in the conversation? Then you chose the wrong time to show up.
“Really?”
“Let me ask again. What have you guys done—”
“Then die.”

I kicked off the ground and sprinted forward, figuring that we could ask questions after we established the pecking order here. When I used Leap to jump up and Giantization to balloon in size, he backstepped to widen the distance between us.
[Your total weight is over 1100 lbs. The special terrain effect Recoil will be applied to your blast radius.]
That bit of distance won’t save you from this.
Crash!
The ground rippled out from my landing point.
“Ah...!” The slender man bounced up like a spring. I didn’t miss that opening and immediately dove forward, my massive barbarian hand outstretched.
[Nebarce Greenhop has cast Emergency Escape.]

The man suddenly disappeared from right under my nose like a mirage. But there was no cause for confusion. Like moving the camera in a 3D game, I scanned my surroundings and caught sight of him about twenty yards away. Ah, so he was a Blink user. He didn’t get far, though.
Dash.
I adjusted my trajectory in mid-air. Since this guy was a top-tier archer, an arrow was already flying in.
Whip!
The white light enveloping the arrowhead told me the arrow was layered with a skill. That wasn’t a problem, though.
[You have cast Transcendence. The next skill you use will be strengthened.]
I hadn’t chosen Bayon’s essence as my royal reward just because it worked well with Giantization, after all.
[You have cast Leap. By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
Transcendental Leap, for short. Its effects were simple. The ability became usable and castable in mid-air, significantly increasing its utility.
[Travel time is significantly reduced.]
You also got fast. Really fast.
Flash!
The moment my foot kicked into the air, I was already in his face with the full force of Leap driving me.
Crash!
His body flew into the air again, unable to handle the recoil. I quickly reached out and gripped his neck.

“Urgh!” The man moaned in pain. There was no room for sympathy, though. Maintaining distance was a matter of life or death for a long-range fighter, after all. Since he hadn’t been able to do that, he deserved to die.

“Die.” I tightened my grip on his neck. I wasn’t too worried he would run away. Not only was the cooldown time for Blink considerably long, but even if he escaped using another skill, I’d just have to catch him again.
“Ugh...!” His wriggling intensified. If I applied a little more strength, his neck would probably snap right then and there.

That was when I came to my senses. “Hey.” Breaking his neck here wasn’t a good idea. I should at least hear him out. If the story I heard wasn’t the one I wanted, just snapping his neck wouldn’t be enough.
Thud.

When I loosened my grip on his neck, the guy fell to the ground. I stomped on his stomach to make sure he didn’t pull any funny business and lowered my torso to lean over him. Then I grabbed his wrist.
Snap!

I twisted his wrist instead of his neck—the wrist with the hand wearing Raven’s ring. The guy couldn’t even moan at the horrible pain and his eyes rolled back. But that wasn’t my problem. I’d been very patient until now.
“Where did you get this ring?” I asked the same question again. Earlier we’d run into a bit of a debacle in which we both ignored each other’s questions to ask our own, but this time was different.
“W-What on earth are you talking about?!” Although it wasn’t a proper answer, it was an answer.
“Just answer the question.”
“This ring, where did you get it?” I scanned his paper-thin body. His wrist was already crushed, but there were still plenty of parts that could be broken.
It seemed he’d come to the same conclusion. “K-Kerman’s Magic Workshop in District Seven!” he shouted urgently. “Kerman’s Magic Workshop, that’s where I got it!”

That was an answer I hadn’t expected at all. “...What?” I expected him to say he picked it up by accident or stole it, but that he didn’t kill her. I was planning on moving onto the next phase of my interrogation as soon as he tried to feed me a vague line like that, but I instead froze. “You bought it...? You didn’t steal it from Raven?”
“I don’t even know who Raven is!”
He sounded genuinely wronged. It didn’t seem like he was lying... but you never knew. He could be clever enough that he came up with a lie on the way over.
“A-Agh!”

I grabbed his dangling hand and took off the ring. Then I opened the ring’s sub-space and searched inside. It was filled with equipment, consumables, and items that appeared to be personal. Checking a few of the items, I let out a deep sigh.
What, it really wasn’t Raven’s?

It wasn’t Raven’s ring. As proof, it wasn’t full of magical ingredients like it should have been. There was no way this guy stole the ring and tossed all the expensive spellcasting components on the ground, either.
Oh, come to think of it, Raven said she bought it at a magic workshop too... Yeah, I believed in her the whole time. Mm-hmm, she’s not just any regular woman. There’s no way she went down so easily.
“D-Does that clear up the misunderstanding?”
Oh, uh...

“So it turns out this is your ring.” Like any barbarian whose honesty was his greatest strength, I coolly admitted I was in the wrong and took my foot off the guy who was squirming on the ground with broken wrists.
“B-But why are you putting it in your pocket...?”
Mm, because that’s a whole separate issue? This ring is mine now. People from Noark are the original treasure hoarders, right?
“Do you have complaints?”

His silence told me just how displeased he was by my actions. Simply put, the transfer was approved. Now that I had permission, I stripped him bare of his weapons and equipment, thus completing the necessary preparations for a nonviolent conversation.
“Who are you?”

Starting with his name, I interrogated the guy about his background and the events that took place on this island. He must not have wanted to die yet because the words came out easily. His name was Nebarce Greenhop.
“Your face looks familiar for some reason...”
“It should, considering we’ve met once before.”
“What? You and I? When?”
“When the royal capital of Karnon caught on fire.”
As soon as I heard that, I remembered him. When I ran into the Fallen Scholar that day, there had been a dork following behind him.
To think it was him.
Anyway, that wasn’t important. It didn’t look like this guy knew anything about what Fallen Scholar and Baekho talked about after they left, either.
“Now, tell me everything that happened today.”
After that, I was able to hear the side of the story that I hadn’t been able to get from the priestess. First, it really was the blond these guys were after.
“That man was originally from Noark. But he betrayed the lord of the castle and ran away with a treasure.”
“W-Wait. Mr. Drous is from Noark...?”
“That’s a fake name in the first place. It was very difficult to find him because he changed his face and went into hiding.”
Having trouble believing it, the priestess stared out into space in a complete daze. Well, I would feel the same if someone told me that Missha was an evil spirit or something like that.
“So, what happened to him?”
“He died.”
“Are you certain?”
“It was right over there. You can see where Lady Rainwales got rid of the body.”
The place he pointed to still had traces of acid. Geez, so brutal.
“So what were you doing this whole time that you only showed up now? And where are your teammates?”
“Me and one other left the group to track down the people who ran away. That’s when I got separated from my partner in the middle.”
Hmm, sure. So you were pursuing them when you turned back empty-handed and ended up here. Wait, then who triggered the event?
It suddenly occurred to me to ask who broke the island’s offering, but I didn’t get the answer I was hoping for.
“How the sea ended up like that...? I don’t know, either. The ground suddenly started shaking during the chase and then my surroundings went dark.”
Huh, he doesn’t know, either? That makes this even more suspicious...
As I stood there trying to get my thoughts in order, the archer cautiously asked a question of his own. “So, what happened to Lady Rainwales? Was there no one here when you arrived?”

He’d asked the same question when we first met. Hmm, was this why he’d answered all of mine so honestly? Because he wanted to know where she was? I couldn’t be sure, but right when I was about to reply, two figures emerged from the bushes.
Dash.
“Erwen! There! It’s Bjorn!”
“M-Mister! You’re here!”
It was Ainar and Erwen.

chapters.title: Chapter 271: Defense (1)
paragraphs: After treating her injured eye with a potion, Winix Carmilla looked at her stepbrother in irritation. He had also healed his severed arm with a potion. “Ugh, none of this would have happened if you didn’t mess things up!”
“You don’t think you were being hasty?”
“...Hasty? Did you think we’d get another moment alone with that woman? I did nothing wrong! It’s your fault for not stabbing her properly!”
The man simply sighed at Carmilla’s accusations. What was fighting here going to do? “But this is the right item, right?”
“You and your worrying. Can’t you feel it? This gem is overflowing with mana.”
“...If I had that level of mana aptitude, I would have become a wizard.”
“You wish. Don’t you know you’re too stupid to be a wizard?” Carmilla grumbled at her stepbrother as usual, but the corners of her lips were twitching up. “I wonder how much this will sell for.”

This was the reason she could smile even after getting stabbed in the eye not that long ago. After all, Noark was virtually gone now. Even if it meant putting her life on the line, she’d judged it was wiser to take a piece of the pie here, and that judgment had proven correct.

“Come on, let’s go. Once we stop to rest at any island here, it’ll be over. We’ll be able to live like nobles for the rest of our lives.” Carmilla steered the Drake, which was gliding away from the island.
The man stopped her. “Wait.”
“What is it?”
“We have to make sure Rainwales is dead.”
“What? We already have the item, so why?” Carmilla tilted her head, but the man remained firm.

Having now fought her himself, he was surer than ever. The word “monster” was not strong enough to describe Amelia Rainwales. If his surprise attack hadn’t been successful, they wouldn’t have been able to escape alive like this. “If that woman survives, even if we get back to the city, we’ll have to live in fear for the rest of our lives.”

“If she survives? Can you stop jinxing it? How can she survive in that condition? After you stabbed her in the stomach like that with a poisoned knife!” Carmilla shrieked at the man’s warning. But even as she did, she also had her doubts. “...If you’re so anxious, then you go check whether she’s alive or dead. Of course, I’m certain she’s dead, but since we were in too much of a rush to even take her equipment...”
After coming to an agreement, the two rode the Drake back to the island. Thankfully, their other two comrades who had left to chase down the others had not yet returned.
“...Looks like she managed to get out of here even in that state.”
Amelia was nowhere to be seen, but she couldn’t have gotten far.
“There’s more bloodstains over here. This way.”
The two of them followed the trail of blood she left behind, but the trail continued for much longer than they expected before suddenly ending.
“...She intentionally erased her tracks. To think she would have the mind to do that in her state.”

“W-What do we do, then?” Only then did Carmilla begin to pale. Now that she’d seen for herself that Amelia had had the awareness to erase her tracks, she was starting to think the woman really might have survived. But there was nothing they could do.
“The chase ends here.”
“E-Ends here?”
“Yeah, it’s not like we have an expert scout among us. Staying here would only be a waste of time. Let’s go back.”
Afterward, Carmilla and the man moved to the area where they’d just done battle.
Crack!
The man destroyed the stone situated on the altar at the center of the island.
“W-Why did you break that thing all of a sudden? A-Are you mad at me...?”
“I’m not mad. It’s for a reason. I’ll explain it later, so let’s focus on leaving now.”
“Wait, what do you—” Carmilla could not finish her sentence.
Rumble!
Dark clouds were gathering and thunder roared overhead. The wind seemed to be getting stronger too.
[The offering of Farune Island has been destroyed. The Fury of the Sea engulfs the island.]
This man seemed almost like a stranger to her today.
The moment Ainar and Erwen showed up, I wanted to run and greet them right away, but I held myself back to preserve my dignity as clan chief. “Ah, you’re here.”
Mm-hmm, the leader of a clan should have some gravitas.
“You’re late.”
“I’m sorry. But where are the others...?”
“Not here yet.”
“Excuse me? What do you mean not here yet? I thought we were going to be the last ones. Are they—”
“Stop.” I cut Erwen off. “Everyone should be fine, so don’t worry. They must be late for a reason.” After all, Erwen and Ainar had arrived late but were completely fine.
Oh, on that note...
“So, why were you guys late?”
“Well, actually...”

I listened to the reason for their tardiness, thinking it might help me figure out what was going on with the others who weren’t here yet. Their explanation was nothing special. Apparently, Erwen managed to swim to shore without losing consciousness but lost her bow on the way.
“I spent some time looking around the beach in case the waves carried it to shore. That’s when I ran into Miss Ainar by chance.”
Hmm, no wonder she doesn’t have her bow on her shoulder. But thankfully she was able to find Ainar so I guess it worked out?
“So that’s what happened. Don’t worry too much about the lost bow. You can use this for now.” With that, I pulled a longbow out from the sub-space and handed it to Erwen.
“Huh? A bow made of bortal wood? Where did you get something so valuable?”
Wow, this thing is grade-four bortal wood? No wonder the color’s so nice.
“I picked it up by chance.” Erwen tilted her head at my succinct explanation, but she pieced things together before long.
“But who is this person...?” she asked, glancing at the man on the ground, who was dressed in casual clothes after being stripped of all his equipment by me.
“He’s from Noark.”
“Wow, I see! I’ll use this gratefully...!” Erwen excitedly replied, obvious glee on her features. She was definitely a sweet kid.
Anyway, as we were chatting, the priestess joined the conversation. “I’m glad you were reunited with your comrades. I’m happy to see your faith was not in vain.”
I introduced her while I was at it. “This is the priestess from the team Patzran belonged to. Her name is Ersina. I ran into her by chance as I was coming this way and we traveled here together.”
“I am Lairin Ersina.”
“Ah, right...” Erwen awkwardly acknowledged the priestess’ greeting and asked me, “Mister, did anything else happen?”
“Anything else?”

“...Never mind.” Erwen shook her head, then looked at Nebarce. “But why did you break this man’s wrists instead of killing him?” It must have seemed strange to her that I had left someone from Noark alive.
“He might be useful.”
“Hmm, really? He doesn’t look it... Well, if you say so, Mister!”

I laughed woodenly and that particular topic thankfully ended there. To be honest, I had another reason for keeping him alive. I had a feeling that if I killed this guy, it might do something irreversible to my relationship with Amelia Rainwales.
Looks like their target was just Drous too.

Based on what Nebarce said, it sounded like Amelia’s team had run into some kind of issue too. It might even be possible to form a temporary alliance with them since the waves of monsters would start picking up soon. Considering how the last wave was bound to go, the more people on our side, the better.
“Then let’s move.”

Anyway, we got ready to leave since we couldn’t stay here forever. Our destination was the east coast, where the first boss would appear. However, I never would have thought the team would still be scattered even after the first wave had started. Just what the hell was everyone else up to?
It’s making me worried...
“I’ll clear the way, so Ainar, you keep an eye on this guy to make sure he doesn’t try anything funny.”
Just in case, I kept Ainar out of the battle and ordered her to watch Nebarce. Then I picked up the pace as much as possible.
[You have defeated a Ranemut Warrior. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Conch Horn. EXP +3]
[You defeated a Garbel...]

Because monsters from the sea were covering the entire island, it was hard to make headway. Well, the monsters were still only around rank seven, so travel was still possible, but the urgency continued to mount.
We’ll have to find them all before the next wave.
Starting from the next wave, the difficulty of the monsters would go up dramatically, to the point that even I wouldn’t be able to handle them alone.
“...Everyone will be okay, right?” Erwen muttered, obviously concerned by the large amount of monsters we were encountering.
I quickly answered, fearing she would jinx things. “Don’t think anything weird. It’ll be fine.”
“But there are so many monsters...”
It’ll be hard to survive alone—is that what you’re thinking?
“Didn’t I come all the way here with Ersina?”
Missha and Raven might have joined forces with Ersina’s teammates somewhere else on the island. Well, that wasn’t without its issues, either.
God damn it.

I recalled the conversation I had with Nebarce earlier. Even if my clanmates ran into Patzran’s teammates by luck, that wouldn’t necessarily be a good thing. I had asked how Amelia’s team had known they would come to this island.
Nebarce had replied, “There’s a traitor among them who passed their plans for this expedition on to us. Although only Lady Rainwales knows who it is.”
There was a traitor among them too.
Arua Raven turned to the bushes and her eyes went wide.
“You’re not the one I was looking for... But this isn’t too bad, either.”
Thankfully, the face she found was a familiar one.
“Miss Raven, we meet again.”

“Mr. Patzran!” Raven, who had just been on pins and needles, breathed a sigh of relief before hurrying forward. “What on earth happened? Why are you so injured? Who’s that on your back? Are they dead?”
Patzran flashed her a pained smile and set down the wizard he was carrying. Then he began to answer her questions. “He’s just unconscious, don’t worry.”
“T-That’s a relief. So, what happened?”
“...Plunderers ambushed us.”

There had been an ambush, and they’d managed to escape, but the group ended up separated after being pursued. Now they were searching the island for their teammates. After providing a summary of the situation, Patzran cautiously continued. “Although you’re not the teammates I was looking for, I’m so glad I ran into you, Miss Raven. If you don’t mind, could you help us out?”
“What do you mean?”

“One of our teammates is in the middle of the island. She stayed there all alone to give us a chance to escape. We have to save—oh, come to think of it, I don’t see that barbarian.” Patzran then noticed that Raven wasn’t in top shape either and tilted his head. “Miss Raven, did something happen to you too? What happened to that beastman archer? He looks like he fell in the water.”
“Well, we were about to leave the island when a storm suddenly brewed... It capsized our boat so everyone got separated.”

After that, when Raven told him about their agreement to meet up in the middle of the island, Patzran’s eyes lit up. “In the middle of the island? That’s good, then. Why don’t we head over there together? Since those awful bastards are still roaming the island, that will be much safer for all of us.”
Put simply, he was proposing a temporary team-up. Raven thought it over for a moment before giving her answer. “Okay, let’s do that.” After all, there was no reason for her to refuse.

chapters.title: Chapter 272: Defense (2)
paragraphs: On the eastern shoreline, reefs poked up out of the water here and there. These were the same reefs we had been pushed into by the rough waves, smashing our boat.
“We’re here.”

The sandy beach was already half underwater and filled with monsters. The standard marine monsters on the sixth floor were Ranemut Warriors and Shamans. Conch Horns spat venom from a distance. Garbels had the unique characteristic of spawning up to three more Garbels when killed.
“Bjorn, I’ll help too.” Ainar took a step forward, expressing her concern at the hundreds of monsters.
Just stand watch, will you?
“No need.”
“What? But...”
No buts. Oh, come to think of it, I never got the chance to show this to her after I got this essence.
“Don’t worry. I can handle this much on my own.” I slung my mace over my shoulder like a hitter with a baseball bat. “Erwen.”
“Yes, what shall we do this time?”
“Wind.”
I whipped out Elemental Barbarian (Wind) Mode.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Elementalization.]
A sharp wind wrapped around my body and began to swirl around my skin.

[The Spirit of the Wind dwells in your body. All damage you take will be adjusted for by improved dodging. Damage received from magic is doubled. You have received a bonus against Penetration and Cutting Damage. Your Agility stats have risen significantly.]

The abilities of this mode were simple. You got a speed boost and it allowed you to take on the role of a dodging tank. For a damage dealer, it increased your DPS a whole lot. Of course, the biggest benefit lay elsewhere.
[The range of all of your attacks is tripled.]

This was the biggest distinction of Elemental Barbarian (Wind). When this mode activated, normal hits were swapped out for wide-range damage. Put simply, that meant even a Blunt Weapon Warrior like me could make area-of-effect attacks.

“Kweeek!” Sensing something off, the monsters around me went into a frenzy and started swarming me, but I held my position and waited for the right moment. There was no need to swing twice, right? Just one proper hit should be enough.
Transcendence.
The moment I determined that enough monsters had gathered in one spot, I immediately used Transcendence.
[You have cast Swing.]
In the same way a skilled swordsman might swing his sword, I swung my mace in a controlled arc.
Whiiip! Whooom!

With a gust of wind, the mace in my hand lengthened like a Yeoui Staff and increased in size proportionately. This was Transcendental Swing with its tripled damage range and the reason why truly ridiculous plays became possible toward the latter half of Dungeon and Stone. The damage for most moves was multiplied.
Kwaaang!
Whew, that’s a ringer.
When I finished my Swing, I scanned my surroundings with satisfaction.
Yeah, that’s the stuff.
There were no monsters standing.
“Bjorn! How did you do that? Teach me too!”
“Ask Erwen to help you next time.”
“I can do that as long as Erwen is there?”

“Yeah, something similar, at least,” I absentmindedly answered Ainar, who was impressed by my new combo, before looking out at the sea. Thanks to that effective blow, most of the monsters on the beach had been cleaned out.
“Mister, the waves! The waves are rolling back!”
As we waited on the empty shore, the waves suddenly rose high like a tsunami.
[The first Fury of the Sea has begun.]
This happened when the mini-boss of the first wave appeared.

“Siren! It’s the Siren Queen!” Priestess Ersina shouted upon catching sight of the monster surfing down the waves. As an adventurer who had been active on the sixth floor for a long time, it seemed she knew about this monster as well. “Why is a rank-four monster here on this island?”
Why do you think? Because one of you guys triggered the event.
“Everyone, get behind me. Erwen, you get ready to fight.”
“Okay.”
“What about me? Do I just keep watching?”
“For now. I’ll call on you if necessary, so wait.”
“Okay!”

After doing another basic tune-up on our formation, the Siren Queen was finally in front of us. “Kyaaah!” With a pretty face and a screech that was very much the opposite, she stabbed the trident in her hand forward.
Bang!
Since she was a rank-four monster, even a regular hit from her was quite heavy. There was another reason she was rank four, though.
[The Siren Queen has cast Song of the Sea. Your stats have decreased.]
She had an aura that reduced your stats the longer you were exposed to it.
[The Siren Queen has cast Vortex.]
Also, every time this monster dealt a regular blow, it threw out a vortex that stole a set amount of MP from you.
[The Siren Queen has cast Proof of Loyalty.]
And then, each time that ability was in cooldown, it summoned rank-five monsters—not just one or two, but dozens at once.
It’s a typical shaman-type debuff boss monster.
As I thought, it wouldn’t have been an easy fight—if we hadn’t encountered her right here, that is.
“Behel—aaah!”

The main challenge posed by the Siren Queen lay in numbers. Usually, it was normal for there to be hundreds of sirens guarding her. However, she was alone when she first arrived on the island. Of course, she could make copies of herself if left alone.
I didn’t come all the way over here for nothing.
To defeat her before she evolved into a raid boss, I abandoned my search for my clanmates to come here.

“I-I will help, so give me a weapon! A rank-four monster is impossible for you guys to handle alone!” It seemed we didn’t look all that trustworthy considering the suggestion we got from Nebarce, but I just let it go in one ear and out the other.
The same went for Ainar. “What are you saying!? Bjorn is a great warrior!”
“Great or not, that is not a monster that three people can kill on their own—”
“Bjorn, can I rip off this guy’s mouth?”
“If he talks smack again.”
“Okay!”

Ainar’s threat must have been effective because Nebarce shut his mouth. Thanks to that, I was able to focus solely on the fight. The battle was being handled with just the following trio: a priestess for whom heals and blessings were second nature, a spirit archer, and a tank barbarian. Nevertheless, the boss fight went smoothly, which made sense considering our team was made up of a damage dealer, a tank, and a healer.
[Lairin Ersina has cast Blessing of the Sun. All debuffs of rank five or lower are removed, and stats temporarily increase in proportion to the debuff.]
The stat reduction spells were dismantled by the priestess at regular intervals.
Whiiip!
The Vortexes that stole MP upon landing a hit could just be dodged with the joystick.
It really is nice having high Agility.

The summoning move wasn’t all that tricky to deal with, either. Erwen hovered around my head in Elementalization mode and kept killing the monsters off before their group could even reach ten in number.
“Behelahhh!” Plus, because my Threat Level was so high, there was no situation in which they ignored me and ran to the back of the group.
Crunch! Crunch! Crunch!
So all I had to do was put on the tank/damager hat and beat the queen up to end it all.
“Keeeeeek!”
The battle took about twenty minutes in total.
[You have defeated a Siren Queen. EXP +6.]
The Siren Queen had to be bashed nearly thirty times in the head before she finally disappeared in a burst of light. The essence I’d been hoping for did not appear.
If one with the summoning ability showed up, it could have sold for a lot of money. Ah, I guess it doesn’t matter without a wizard or a test tube, anyway.
I let go of my disappointment and set down my mace. Erwen deactivated Elementalization and we both headed to the spot where the rest of the group was.
“...To think three people really can take down a rank-four monster.” The priestess Ersina was still somewhat in disbelief.
Nebarce was in the same boat. “I’m sure I heard you were a rank-five adventurer...” He trailed off and gave me a curious look. “So, you were hiding your abilities...”
What was this guy talking about? I laughed as soon as I heard that, but I didn’t bother to explain myself.
Funny. It’s just that the ranking standards are super lax.

This was one thing I’d felt very strongly about ever since the game became my reality. Adventurer rankings here represented a very limited view of a person’s abilities. The guild only gave out rankings based on the average rank of a person’s essences; it didn’t take the synergy of the essences into account. Nebarce himself was a prime example of that.
He is rank four.

This guy had the badge of a rank-four adventurer. Since he was from Noark, it wasn’t a real badge, but he must have gotten to rank four himself. Even still, I’d owned him in ten seconds. Although my cultivation strategy was strong against people (especially long-rangers), all of that aside, he was just weak. In fact, most of the adventurers here were. Even though their ranks were high, their performances were poor.
In hindsight, the Dragon Slayer was similar.

Having been going on quests for a long time, his level was high and his essences were many, but that was all. There was no logic behind the essences he chose. To be honest, he could even be called a failed character by my standards.
He felt exactly like those guys who only played the game for a few days before calling it a flop and quitting.

More so than possessing high-ranking skills, in this game, you were stronger if you had lower-ranking skills that worked well together. Choosing a core skill like Giantization and evolving it in different ways until you were overpowered was a basic strategy of the game too.
The person with the strongest combination of essences was Corpse Collector.
While I was in the middle of getting my thoughts in order, I hurriedly turned my head in the direction of a sudden voice. “M-Mr. Yandel!”
Huh? Wait, that voice is...
“Raven! Abman!”
“Mr. Patzran, you’re all right!”
Four men and women emerged from the tree line. Whew, all that was left now was Missha.
“Yandel, Erwen, Ainar, I’m glad you’re all safe.”
“Urakburak! I’m glad you’re safe too!”
After running toward each other with grins and sharing a brief reunion, we quickly exchanged information.
“What happened?”
“Oh, that.”

Raven’s report was simple. She and Mr. Bear had linked up with Patzran and his team’s wizard to travel to the center of the island together. Upon arriving, she spotted my memo saying that I was heading east and switched directions.
“But why did you arrive so late? I waited there for over two hours.”
“Sorry. We got so lost on the way there...”
The reason was truly absurd. To think not a single one of those four people could find the way.
Well, two of them are wizards. And aside from using a sword, that guy doesn’t seem to know much about anything else...
Mr. Bear wasn’t even worth mentioning. Yeah, it was only natural to end up lost with a team like this.
“But... Miss Karlstein?”
“Not here yet.”
“Pardon? Not here yet...?”
“Don’t worry too much. Aren’t we only meeting just now too? She’s fine somewhere else on the island.” I tried to shake off my worries somehow and shifted my gaze.
Just like us, Patzran had finished greeting his teammate, Ersina, and approached me. “I heard from Ersina what happened.”
“What happened...?”
“...Baronet Yandel. That you protected her this whole time. Thank you.”
“We should help each other in times of trouble. Anyway, the blond—no, Drous. Did you hear about his identity?”

“Oh, about that... I did hear. It’s hard to believe that Drous was from Noark. Regarding that, do you mind if I confirm a few things for myself?” Patzran then asked politely if he could speak to Nebarce, and I readily agreed.
“Make good use of it and then return it.”
“Of course, I’ll take good care of it.”
Okay, then that’s that sorted.
Keeping an ear on Patzran’s conversation with Nebarce, I went up to Raven and whispered quietly, “Raven, no need to answer, just listen. Someone here has been conspiring with Noark.”
Someone had betrayed their team and told Amelia they would be coming to this island today, someone whose identity only Amelia knew.

“I don’t think they’ll try to stab us in the back now, but just be aware. Let me know right away if you notice anything odd.” As soon as I finished speaking, Raven nodded, her expression stiff. Well, then, now that the information exchange was over, I approached the wizard who was lying on the ground in exhaustion. “Hey, wizard. What’s your name?”
I figured that I might be able to detect something strange about him if I talked to him. Yeah, that was what I was thinking.
“Ah, nice to meet you. I’m Aulock.”

As the wizard stretched out his hand with a friendly smile, I froze. Priestess Ersina, swordsman Patzran, and even the female archer I hadn’t met yet—although I didn’t have any concrete evidence to help me determine who might be the traitor among the many suspects, a sudden certainty surged through me.
“Hans Aulock. Feel free to call me Hans.”
Got you.

chapters.title: Chapter 273: Defense (3)
paragraphs: Hans Aulock would henceforth be known as Hans J.
“His name is Hans...?”
The moment he revealed his name, Raven and Ainar flinched and turned to stare at us. They both knew what the name Hans meant to me.
“...I-Is there a problem?” Hans J looked startled by the sudden attention on him. I squeezed my thigh hard.
Not now. Be patient.
Frankly, I wanted to bash his head in right now and turn him into a nameless corpse. The desire dominated my mind.
Squeeze!

But I didn’t have evidence that he was the traitor yet. All I had was a suspicion. Even if I explained the ominousness of the name Hans, Patzran and Ersina would not be able to accept my logic. At least right now, they were still thinking of him as a teammate.
“No, no problem.”

And so I couldn’t make any moves yet. Even if he was the traitor, if he had a brain, he’d just try to keep quiet until he could get back to the city. I determined that observation was my top priority.
“Huh? It didn’t seem like that...”
“I said there is no problem.”
“Hmm, if you say so...” Hans J touched his chin, looking uneasy. I did feel kind of bad since it felt a little like we were bullying him. “So, are you going to leave my hand hanging?”
Still, a handshake crossed the line.
“Oh, Patzran! Are you done talking?” I took my eyes off Hans J and changed the subject. It looked like those two had finished talking just in time.
“Kind of. Sounds like Drous really was from that place... I always did think there was something strange about him.”
“I see.”
“So, what are you going to do about that man?”
“I’m bringing him along for now.”
“All right.”
Surprisingly, Patzran had no objection to Nebarce’s presence, although he’d almost died because of him. Was he not arguing because he thought he was my loot?

“Anyway, can we all gather around?” Anyway, once the reunion was over, Raven called everyone together. Then she started sorting through the situation with me. “The seaway is blocked by the waves so it’s impossible to escape the island. It’s no wonder monsters keep appearing.”
“Speaking of monsters, they seem to be getting stronger. Not long ago, a Siren Queen appeared.”
“Yes. I don’t know what happened on this island today, but it seems we’re caught up in something unusual. On that note, Mr. Patzran, do you know anything about this phenomenon?” Raven asked.

Patzran paused for a brief moment before answering. “Since it sounds like you already have a theory, I’ll be honest with you. This was the reason that we visited this island.” Apparently, he had heard some things from their leader, Drous, even if the others hadn’t. “I don’t know all the details either... But I heard we just have to hold out until the sun rises in two days.”
“Luckily, that means this won’t last forever.” With that, Raven presented us with two choices. “Our first option is to find a good, defendable spot and hold out for two days.”
“And the second?”

“Wander the island and look for our comrades. Our team hasn’t found Miss Karlstein, and Mr. Patzran’s team hasn’t found their archer yet. If both of them are alone right now, it will only become more dangerous for them as time goes on.”
I ended up chuckling at Raven’s words. Why did she bother saying we had two options?
“So what will you do?”
“Of course we should go find our comrades,” I answered without a moment’s hesitation, and Patzran was no different.
“If I escaped safely, I’m sure Heina escaped safely too. We have to go rescue her.”

We would search the island and look for our comrades first. But right when our future course of action was practically decided, Hans J rolled his eyes and joined the conversation. “Vote! Why don’t we decide with a vote?”
Unbelievable.
Even if your name is Hans, you’re really going to say something like that in an atmosphere like this?
He cleared his throat. “Ahem, well, it’s possible there are people who don’t want to do that but can’t speak up.”
“If you say so. Let’s vote. Raise your hand if you think we should go find our comrades.”
The vote proceeded straight away without a moment’s hesitation, and when everyone raised their hands, Hans J reluctantly raised his too.
“That’s that, then.”
Barbarian democracy was invincible.
Step, step.

I walked at a slightly faster pace to clear the way. Behind me followed eight individuals—all my clanmates except Missha, and Patzran, Ersina, and Hans J, with whom we had made a temporary alliance. There was even the strategic prisoner Nebarce Greenhop.
At least it’s eight people for now.

Assuming Missha and Patzran’s team’s archer joined us, it might be possible for us to clear this level somehow. The presence of a priestess was huge. If she weren’t here, it would have really been impossible.
“Miss Karlstein! If you can hear me, please respond! Miss Karlstein!”
“Heina!”

Once we left the shore, we focused on finding our comrades, who had to be somewhere on the island. It wasn’t an easy task. The island itself wasn’t that big, but because of the dozens of monsters appearing wherever we went, we couldn’t move any faster.
Crunch, chomp! Kabooom!
Currently, we were practically fighting at a standstill.
[You have defeated a Sea Giant. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Naga Archer. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Snake of Palpus...]
This was a change that had occurred thirty minutes ago. The ranks of the spawning monsters rose sharply, to the extent that it was difficult for even a party of eight to take them down efficiently.
Our mood was also darker than before. No one wanted to say it out loud, but the reason for the gloom was obvious.
“With so many monsters...”

There was no way our lost comrades would be all right. Even if Missha and the archer lady had been lucky enough to run into each other, the two of them alone would not be able to withstand this wave of monsters. But, so what?
“Behel-ahhh!”

Unbothered by the terrible conditions, I cleared the path with more vigor. Even if I had to swing my mace several times just to take a few steps forward, that was not a reason to stop moving. As of now, we didn’t know anything for sure.
Chomp, chomp, chomp!
I kept going.
Pop!
Blood gushed. I heard the rough breathing of my weary comrades.
Slice! Stab.
There was the disgusting squelch of monster skin and intestines being pierced. Under the din came a mutter.
“...I-Isn’t it about time we stop now?” It was Hans J’s voice. “Why isn’t anyone saying it? Because they don’t want to be the bad guy? But e-everyone already knows!”

My feet stopped on their own. Monsters were spitting saliva and charging at me even at this moment, but I turned around and headed toward the man. “Know what? Speak properly. Before I misunderstand you.”
“Think logically! Don’t you see that it’s already too late?”

Yeah, so you wanna play the wise wizard, huh? Fine, then. I wanted to break your neck the moment I saw you, anyway. Since you’ve decided to spout nonsense in front of a barbarian, that should be justification enough.
Cough!
I gripped him around his neck.
“M-Mr. Yandel!” Raven screamed, alarmed by my actions.
Patzran left behind the monster he was fighting on the front lines and ran toward me. “What do you think you’re doing!?” Since I was assaulting his teammate, Patzran no longer called me by my title.
“Take another step and I’ll kill you.” At the sight, Ainar also entered battle mode and blocked Patzran’s way. Erwen was similar.
Slide.

She didn’t say anything, and she continued to fire arrows at the monsters just the same. But at some point, Erwen positioned herself behind the priestess to signal that she would kill her if a fight broke out.
Raven went into a panic. “E-Everyone, stop it!” she shouted.
“Yandel, snap out of it.” Mr. Bear shoved away the monsters with his large crossbow and stopped me. All of this happened in the three seconds after I grabbed the wizard by the neck.
God damn it.
What was I doing? This wasn’t like me.
Slump.
I relaxed my grip on Hans J’s neck and dropped him to the ground. The front line had already collapsed thanks to me, and monsters were beginning to flock toward us.
“Sorry. I got worked up there.”
“...Let’s talk about this later.”
When I returned to the front line, Patzran didn’t say another word to me, silently dealing with the monsters by my side.
“Whew...”

Just like that, we returned from the brink of civil war, but it couldn’t be said that things were the same as before. While we still fought together, everyone was wary of each other. Thanks to that, our speed slowed even more. Well, at least Hans’s trap stayed shut.
Missha...
Still, this was bad news for me, since I had to find Missha as soon as possible.
God damn it.
“M-Mister! It’s a body!”
While we were searching the island at the speed of a snail’s crawl, we encountered the dead body of a person we were looking for.
The moment I came face-to-face with the corpse, my heart dropped. I felt faint and my mind went blank. But before long, that emptiness turned into relief, because it wasn’t Missha.

“Heina...!” It was the archer belonging to Patzran’s team. Patzran, who was clearing the way beside me, ran toward her, gutted. “God damn it!” After checking to see if she was breathing, he slammed his fist on the ground.
Just then, white waves of energy rippled from the center of our formation.
[Lairin Ersina has cast Destruction of Evil.]
Destruction of Evil was one of the core abilities of the priest class. You could think of it as a kind of barrier. It couldn’t stop people, but while it was up, monsters couldn’t get through.
“Keeeeeek!”
Put simply, we were safe for the time being. I lowered my shield and approached the body—but not the body of the archer woman. There was one more body here.
“Who is this person?” When I dragged a startled Nebarce over and asked him, he answered that it was his comrade. Thanks to that, my mind went blank again.
Just... what the hell happened?
I could accept that the archer was dead, but it didn’t make sense that this guy’s body was right next to hers.
“Raven, cause of death?”
“There are too many bite marks to be sure. But... It has to be the fatal stab wound on his abdomen.”
So that’s what did him in.
“Evidence he was stabbed by a sword, huh?” Heina was an archer, but the man had been stabbed to death? This really didn’t make sense. “What about the woman? Can you tell exactly what killed her?”
“I don’t know. Her side is even worse...”
“If you had to guess.”

“...First, there’s a wound that looks like she was slashed by a large claw. But that’s also a bit strange. I haven’t seen any monsters here that could leave a mark like that. It’s as if she was torn apart by a large creature...”
“Any monsters come to mind?”
“There are three claw marks and there is a deep indent near the end. That’s usually a wound pattern that appears when someone is attacked by a flight-type monster like a Wyvern.”
“I see.” This situation was getting more troubling. “That means it couldn’t have been a monster.”
“Yes... it seems so.” Raven nodded in agreement, which was only logical, considering the bodies had also been stripped of all equipment.
“Patzran, does the woman still have whatever item her sub-space was in?”
“No, she doesn’t. Someone took it.”
There were two possibilities now.
Either there’s one other adventurer on this island we didn’t know about... or Noark’s side is facing some internal conflict too.
Slap!
Nebarce looked like he was losing it so I slapped him across the face. “Snap out of it. I have something to ask you. Can you guess who did this?”
“Carmilla and Belverson. This has to be the work of those bastards.”
“Explain.”
Nebarce told me that the man named Belverson used a sword, and the woman named Carmilla had a Drake as a summoned beast.
“But why did they hurt your comrade too?”
“I-I don’t know. Perhaps they coveted the treasure. Maybe they even got to Lady Rainwales...”
I don’t have time to take care of your mental health.
I pulled Nebarce’s head up by the hair to keep it from dropping and asked a question I had glossed over earlier. “Tell me about the treasure.”

His explanation wasn’t particularly informative. “I don’t know anything other than the fact that it’s an item that’s been passed down by the lord of the castle’s family for many generations. Oh, oh! And legends say that it can change the history of the user!”
Change their history? Was it really an item with that much power? Since he said that part was a legend, I’d have to take it with a grain of salt.
Anyway, it’s clearly an object important enough that they sent a woman like Amelia to find it.

As such, those two had more than enough motive. Noark had also left for the outside world, after all. Procuring a big haul, creating new identities, and living in the city didn’t sound like a bad plan.
“Mr. Aulock, please take care of Ms. Heina.”
“Ah, leave it to me...” Hans J cast a preservation spell on the archer’s corpse. Then he put the body into sub-space, wrapping up the embalmment process.

“...Yandel, so what are you going to do now?” Like the adventurer he was, Patzran swiftly shook off his grief and asked what my plans were, but I couldn’t bring myself to answer. “Are you going to continue looking for your comrade?”
I knew I shouldn’t, but I just couldn’t say it.
“We still have some energy, but the situation will only get worse from here.”

I knew that logically. Our forced march was consuming our stamina, and we now had to be wary of Carmilla and Belverson. At this point, the right thing to do would be to find a defendable spot on the island and preserve our stamina.
Then what’s Missha supposed to do...?
It continued to be hard for me to make rational decisions.
Maybe this is why...

Suddenly, I had a thought. It was possible Missha knew this would happen, which was why she had pushed me away that day. If our relationship had had the chance to develop into something deeper back then, I wouldn’t have even been able to think like this right now. I would have been in a frenzy, swept away by my emotions, just like with Hans J earlier.
“Mr. Yandel...”

I took a deep breath, exhaled, and slowly looked around. Raven, Erwen, Ainar, Mr. Bear—my precious comrades were looking at me with worry in their eyes. It was now time for me to make a call as their leader.
“Everyone, put down your weapons. We will rest while the barrier is up.”
But even as I said those words, it felt like my insides were rotting away.

chapters.title: Chapter 274: Defense (4)
paragraphs: Once I came to my senses, the first thing I did was apologize. “Wizard, sorry about earlier.”

Hans J, who had almost been strangled to death by a teammate during a battle, looked dubious but accepted the apology at face value. He was well aware that a division in this group right now could endanger his own life. “...Since you apologized, I won’t comment any further on this matter.”

When the wizard accepted my apology, Patzran stepped forward to help clear the air as well. “Bjorn Yandel, I don’t blame you. It’s not like I can’t understand how you’re feeling. To be honest, Sir Aulock was tactless earlier.”
“Patzran, what do you mean by tactless? I only said what needed to be said.”
“...But the way you said it wasn’t great.” Surprisingly, Patzran took my side.
Well, how could you tell someone desperately searching for their comrade to give up since they were clearly dead already? What kind of barbarian wouldn’t get angry after hearing something like that?
“Ahem, let’s stop talking about this now.”
“Yes, I think that would be for the best.”

I subconsciously gnashed my teeth in irritation, which ended the conversation. I had a feeling that was a good thing, though. If we talked about this any longer, we’d likely end up having a repeat of earlier.
“Then what will you do?” At some point, Patzran had started speaking casually to me again, but I didn’t nitpick since I messed up earlier too.
“As I said, we will rest here until the barrier disappears.”
“After that?”
“We will find a better spot and hold out there. Just like Raven suggested.”
“I see. Okay.”
Once our rough plans for the future were decided, everyone laid their tired bodies on the ground to replenish their stamina.
“God’s protection will soon end.”
“I see. Good job. Everyone, get up.”

Time passed and after Destruction of Evil was lifted, we searched the area as planned and found a suitable spot to set up base. We had a cliff at our backs, making it a spot where we’d only need to worry about defending ourselves on three sides.
“Behel—aaah!”

We fended off the monsters from there. Despite my concerns, we didn’t run into anything too dangerous. Since the event had been activated on the highest difficulty level, I had been picturing an even worse scenario, but the wizards were performing great.
“Bertia Sevnu Hellhavens!”
To be more exact, Hans J’s performance was great. Of course, wizards normally shined in battles of numbers, and Raven was also doing her job.
[Hans Aulock has cast the rank-5 attack spell Chain Lightning.]
However, you couldn’t compare her performance to Hans J’s.
Chhhhhh. Puff!
Each time a spell was cast, at least a dozen rank-five monsters either died or fainted.
He can cast Chain Lightning in fifteen seconds? Who is this guy?

Momentarily stunned by the explosive high-level magic, I soon learned something surprising from Patzran, who was fighting alongside me. “Oh, you didn’t know? Aulock is a rank-four wizard from the School of Benocton.”
Benocton was a school that primarily focused on the study of elemental magic, and it seemed he was a rank-four wizard in a rather high position there.
No wonder his equipment looked expensive.
When I learned that he was a more skilled wizard than I thought, I worried that might have annoying implications in the future but ultimately decided to think about that later.
Yeah, what’s he going to do to me if he gets mad? I’m a noble. I’m high status too.
“Ersina, cast a barrier.”
“Okay.”
Anyway, Hans J’s performance was one thing, but if I had to choose the MVP of this siege event, it would have to be the priestess.
[Lairin Ersina has cast Destruction of Evil.]
Without her, we would have had no time to rest.
“Whoa, Mister. Come over here. I put my sleeping bag here.”
“Thanks.”

Whenever we started to run out of strength while fighting off the monsters, we immediately activated a barrier and replenished our stamina and bottomed-out MP. After some recovery, the barrier was lifted and the hunt resumed. We had been repeating this for about four hours when the time finally came.
[The second Fury of the Sea has begun.]
The second wave began.
Pitter, patter.
Rain started to fall from the sky in drops that soon turned into powerful streams of water.
Shaaaaaa!
A strong downpour not unlike the ones that fell during monsoon season began.
“...Rain?”

Everyone was bewildered by the change in the weather—they’d experienced rain in the city, but never in the labyrinth. Of course, having been active on the sixth floor for a long time, Patzran’s team was different.
“Why, at a time like this...?” They weren’t affected by the rain itself.
“This will make things harder.”

They clicked their tongues and frowned. Everyone knew just how dangerous it was to deal with rain in the labyrinth. The rain itself obstructed your vision, while the rainwater ran down your eyelids and made it difficult to concentrate. Also, because of the cold temperature, long-term exposure could lead to hypothermia, and it became easier to drop weapons when your hands were wet. There wasn’t a single good thing about it.
“What a headache...”
Everyone sighed at their shit luck, but not me. The reason was simple. I knew this had nothing to do with luck.
It’ll be here in about thirty minutes.
The fact that it had begun to rain was evidence that the second wave had begun. The mini-boss would appear soon. This particular guy’s MO was to target the area with the most people.
“Everyone, don’t fan out too much and stick together!”
After I gave out instructions, we spent our time fighting monsters and adjusting to the new climate.
Shaaaaaa!
Rain in the labyrinth was something I had never experienced before, either.
It’s much more troublesome than I expected.

The ground was slippery, and in some places, you sunk thanks to the mud. While that alone was already distracting in a lot of ways, the water-attribute monsters took to the change in climate like fish in, well, water, slashing at us without pause.
Squeeze!

In case I dropped the mace, I made sure to keep a tight grip and swing it several times harder than usual. Time passed and just as I was getting used to fighting in the rain, a great big lizard appeared in front of us.
“M-Mr. Yandel! There! Over there!”
“Kwohhh!” It was a Guano Sea Serpent, a rank-four monster that had moss-covered scales, a plump tail, and walked on four legs. Its defining feature was Stench.
[You have been exposed to Stench. All effects that deal sustained damage are doubled, and you are immune to Purification while in Stench’s range.]
This was the passive skill that had acted as my foundational essence when I was building a Witch Doctor.
Gag! Gag...!
