As one would expect from a monster that was colloquially referred to as the Poop Lizard, everyone started retching the moment it appeared.
What kind of smell...?

The stench was strong enough to make even a barbarian with a strong stomach feel faint. I held my breath and fought hard to keep my focus. To start, it was a rank-four monster like the Siren Queen, but this situation was already completely different.
...I should be careful not to make any mistakes along the way.

Monsters flooded our surroundings. And unlike the Queen, who needed summoned monsters to show off her strength, this guy was strong all on his own. We’d have to distribute our forces. I quickly split the group into two. “Patzran, Ainar. Don’t worry about things on this end and focus on standing your ground!”

As the close-range damager and frontline fighter, the two of them marked the trash mobs on either side of us. Just in case, I told Hans J and Mr. Bear to focus on taking down the hordes of monsters too, rather than on the boss battle.
“Everyone, get behind me!” The rest of us formed a kind of attack squad. Our goal was to kill this bastard while the trash mob squad held out.

“Kwohhh!” After testing the waters from a distance, the monster charged at us, the horns on its forehead angled forward. When I received the charge with my shield, the battle began in earnest. The fight itself wasn’t anything out of the ordinary.
[Guano Sea Serpent has cast Plague of the Sea.]
Erwen and Raven ran interference, taking out the self-destructive spirit it tried to summon.
Pop!
Well, when the spirit exploded and spattered blood everywhere, it did give me a status effect.
[You have been infected by Scurvy. All healing effects are reduced by half and you will receive continuous Poison damage.]
However, that much could be dealt with by the priestess’ heals.
[Guano Sea Serpent has cast Origin of the Deep Sea.]
[Guano Sea Serpent has cast Sink.]
[Guano Sea Serpent has cast Rainmaking Ritual.]
This guy’s other attack patterns weren’t all that different, either—some magical, some with divine power.
“Behelaaah!”

With the stubborn body of a barbarian at the helm, we weathered the attacks just like that and the battle continued. Of course, there may have been no major incidents, but that didn’t mean it was all smooth sailing.
“M-Mr. Yandel! You have to avoid that!”
The Guano Sea Serpent was famous for its great stamina. So naturally, as the battle dragged on, there were several close calls.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has exceeded her damage threshold. Elementalization has been deactivated.]

Toward the end, Erwen suffered an injury and was rendered incapable of combat. Having used half-heals throughout the entire battle, the priestess’ divine power was practically exhausted. But that was nothing to worry about now since we managed to take it down.
[You have defeated a Guano Sea Serpent. EXP +6]
In the end, even Hans J joined the attack squad and fired off a lightning spell. With that, the monster’s massive body staggered and fell, and soon scattered into particles of light.
“D-Did we get rid—huh?”
Everyone tilted their heads in sync.
“H-Huh?! M-Mr. Yandel!”
“It’s an essence!”
An essence had dropped.

Rank-four monsters weren’t common, even on the sixth floor. They only appeared if you took your boat far into the ocean, and even then there weren’t many of them so it was impossible to hunt dozens of them a day like you could with rank-five monsters. In other words, that was how tough it was to acquire their essences.
“It’s been a while since I’ve seen a rank-four essence.” A light appeared in Patzran’s eyes, as he was a veteran of the sixth floor.
Geez, it’s not even his essence. And man, why did this one have to come out?

I clicked my tongue in disappointment and took a moment to shake off my regrets. This essence didn’t suit anyone in my clan, but the price of the essence itself wasn’t so bad. It’d make us a lot of money if we sold it.
“Raven, store the essence in a test tube.”
“Ah, right!” At my instruction, Raven quickly moved to pull out a test tube from the sub-space.
Just as she was about to place the essence inside, Patzran stepped forward and stopped her. “Wait, shouldn’t you first ask if anyone wants to claim it?”
I hadn’t expected that since their team was otherwise just a priestess and a wizard. The only one of them who could even make a bid was Patzran.
“I’m only asking this just in case, but you’re not assuming we don’t get a share, are you?”
Oh, so that’s what you were getting at. Yeah, there’s no way a swordsman would want to take an essence like this.
“Don’t worry. The essence will be sold and the funds will be split evenly based on the number of people.”
“Hmm, if you say so.” When I finally told him what he wanted to hear, Patzran backed off without another word. That ended the distribution problem.
“Um, I’m going to store it now, then.” Raven did a final check-in, test tube in hand, and everyone nodded. And that was when it happened.
“Anyway, the rain has stopped.”
“That’s a pretty big coincidence. It’s possible the Guano Sea Serpent had something to do with the rain.”

I absentmindedly raised my head at Patzran’s and Hans J’s conversation and completely froze. The Guano Sea Serpent had been defeated and the rain had stopped. None of that was a problem anymore, but...
“Wait... what’s that? It looks like it’s getting closer...”
Through the dark clouds that were only just starting to roll back, a flying shadow swooped down, spewing out flames.
“I-It’s a Drake!”
God damn it.
Swearing inwardly, I shouted, “Prepare for battle!”
The scumbags were here.

chapters.title: Chapter 275: Vortex (1)
paragraphs: Bewilderment and surprise—setting those emotions aside, my brain analyzed the visual information it was gathering.
Drake.
First, Drakes did not spawn on this island. So how was this possible? The answer lay in a conversation I’d had just a few hours ago.
“Carmilla and Belverson. This has to be the work of those bastards.”
Two plunderers from Noark had likely betrayed Amelia because they coveted a treasure she was in possession of. Of the two, the woman named Carmilla was said to have a summoned beast.
Hmm, then since I’ve identified the enemy...
Whoosh!
Judging by the fire the Drake was breathing at us, it was clear they had malicious intent as well. So there was only one thing for me to do now.
“Prepare for battle!” I shouted, gripping my mace tighter. As we’d already been in several similar situations lately, this cry once again served as a trigger that spurred everyone into action.
“E-Everyone, gather round!” Raven, who had been staring blankly at the sky, hurried to cast a spell before she could even put the test tube in sub-space. “Alerbeth Wiar!”
The rank-seven support spell Mana Barrier was the most used non-elemental defense spell for wizards. However, the translucent barrier that surrounded us was covered in a blue frost.
Did she just layer an ice spell on top of it in that split second?
One thing was for certain—her casting had gotten really fast since she’d become an adventurer.
Whooom!

While I was taking a moment to admire Raven, the flames the Drake was spewing met the mana barrier and fanned out like rainwater running down an umbrella. In any case, it bought us time to catch our breath.
Erwen is incapable of combat. Ersina is out of divine power. Raven likely doesn’t have much mana left, either. Even my MP is at its limit.

I updated my alllies’ stats in the short moment we were afforded. The situation wasn’t looking good in a lot of ways. Thanks to the battle with the Guano Sea Serpent, almost all of our biological resources including stamina were at rock bottom.
This won’t be easy.
Just as I was thinking this, the flames suddenly stopped and the Drake crashed into the mana barrier.
Kwaaang!
Body Slam, the foundational skill of a tamer.
Rippp!
Since it slammed down on us with all the speed and strength of that giant body, there was no way a rank-seven defense spell could hold up.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Hazardous Material.]
The moment our enemies emerged through the broken mana barrier, Mr. Bear fired an explosive arrow at the Drake’s forehead.
Kwaaang!
The Drake blocked the attack without much damage by shielding its body with its large wings. Well, that didn’t matter. We never expected it to be a one-shot kill.
“Behel—aaah!”
I activated Giantization, which I had been carefully rationing, and kicked off the ground to run toward the Drake, which was hovering in an effort to block Mr. Bear’s arrows.
Dash.
The distance between us rapidly narrowed.

“Carmilla, I will take care of that barbarian.” Just then, the man riding on the Drake’s back leapt off of it, aiming his sword at me. The blade was surrounded by a white aura. It wasn’t the type of aura used by knights.
Oh, that looks like it’s going to hurt.
My tank’s intuition told me that just ignoring this and charging forward would be dangerous. And so I raised my shield and blocked the sword.
Bannng!
A heavy shock rattled the shield.
Good thing I blocked that.

A flying barbarian akin to a cannonball had been stopped by a single sword. It looked like my shield was scratched as well. If I’d chosen to take the hit with my body, I would have suffered considerable damage.
“I thought... you were... rank five.”
Anyway, what was this bastard talking about? I had only one thing to say. “Go to hell.”

I wielded my mace with a flourish, and he responded by stepping on my shield, backflipping, and widening the distance before even landing on the ground. Jeez, did he think he was a flying squirrel or something?
Dash.

After returning to the ground following that brief exchange in mid-air, I immediately sprinted at him. At the same time, the Drake’s throat gurgled before it released another stream of fire. But that wasn’t a problem. I wasn’t alone, either.
“We’ll handle it!”
Once again, Raven’s defense magic shot out to block the Drake’s flames, and Mr. Bear fired a quick arrow to keep the Drake in check.
Dash.
I kept running.
Whooom.
At first, the man went to block my Swing without avoiding it, but apparently sensing something was off, he pulled his sword back and retreated. Jeez, he had good instincts.
If he blocked it, it would have completely destroyed him.
Biting my lip in annoyance, I heard Mr. Bear cry out from behind me. “Yandel, I’ll leave him to you!”
“Yeah, and I’ll leave the rest to you guys.”
That was how the structure of the battle naturally took form. Summoner Carmilla was tackled by Raven, Mr. Bear, Patzran, and Hans J together.
“Woohoo! Leave the monsters to me!” Even in the middle of all this drama, Ainar couldn’t read the room and launched herself at the trash mobs to clean up shop.
“Why do you keep running away? You attacked me first.”

I dealt with the swordsman named Belverson. Well, I did have one order to give out before we started fighting in earnest. “Raven, use a team communication spell!” I closed the distance between me and the swordsman and ordered Raven to turn on team communication magic, but with one more condition.
“Just us? But why—”
“Did you do it?”
“Yes. Our conversation can only be heard by us now.”
Okay, in that case... After confirming that the spell was working, I speedily conveyed my message to the others. Everyone except Raven seemed confused by my instructions.
“I don’t know why you’re saying that, but okay. If the time comes, I’ll do as you say.”
I didn’t think I had to worry about them not following instructions. Put simply, that meant that we each just had to focus on doing our jobs.
Dash.
On that note, I ran at the swordsman again, closing the gap.

His comrade and the owner of the Drake tried to help him several times, but found herself interrupted by Raven and Hans J until she was eventually dragged into a full-fledged battle with that part of the team. “Ugh, so annoying. I’ll kill you if you lose!”

From then on, our fight became a one-on-one matchup, but it wasn’t as easy as beating up their archer earlier. There were several reasons for this. First, this guy was not a glass-cannon long-range fighter, and he was overall on a higher level than the archer.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has deactivated.]

More importantly, due to the battle with the monsters beforehand, my MP had run out and it was impossible to use my abilities to subdue him. Man, if only I were in top form, I would have owned him a long time ago.

“You’re good, but this ends now!” When Giantization deactivated, the swordsman closed the distance and swung his sword at me. As a citizen of Noark, he seemed to be well-versed in fighting people because his timing and sword’s arc were difficult for me to block with my shield.
But this guy doesn’t know about Ironskin.
The Ogre’s passive skill, Ironskin, had the side effect of raising the user’s Physical Resistance by a multiple of two exclusively against slashing damage.
Clang!
The sword dug into my forearm, but that was all. It was my turn now.
Whoom!
As a foreign sensation spread through my skin, I struck his temple with my mace.
Crunch!
A pleasant crunch resounded.
“Ugh.” Unfortunately, what the mace shattered was not his skull but his left arm, which he raised just in time.
Well, better an arm than a head. I guess you’re smart enough to realize that, at least. So, one more.
Just as I was about to exploit this opening by swinging my mace again, I was forced to step back as a monster came at me from the side.
“Kyaaagh!”
Ha, my precious opportunity.
“...So, an Ogre essence.” This guy also seemed to be aware of Ironskin now. From that point on, he only pretended he was going to cut me and attacked mainly with stabs.
Looks like a short battle is out of the question.

When a more difficult battle ensued, the number of wounds on my body went up. The wounds weren’t even healing with a potion from Raven, perhaps because the sword was poisoned. However, I refused to get impatient.
Just refill your MP first.
Change of plans. I was now going to fight as defensively as possible and figure out what essences he had, then end the match.

As I was preparing for the long haul, I heard a woman let out a shout from somewhere across the battlefield. “Hans Aulock!” It was the voice of the woman firing off various attacks from the Drake’s back. “Stop interfering and help us!”
A feeling of déjà vu crossed my mind. Coincidentally, many things about this situation overlapped with the events of Doppelganger Forest.
“W-W-What are you talking about!?”
“Ha! I’m the one who did your background investigation and gave it to that bitch. You think I don’t know who you are?”
The fact that our enemy was from Noark was the same.
“D-Don’t listen, everyone! This wicked woman is just trying to cause infighting—!”
“So, is that how you want to play it? Everyone, listen! Hans Aulock is the scumbag who killed the daughter of Count Montraina twelve years ago and concealed it!”
Said enemy was openly revealing a man named Hans’s secret and encouraging them to betray their party.
“What a cunning tongue! Do you really think we’ll believe that?”
One of Hans’s comrades even denied the betrayal, but Hans had been driven into a corner. It was all exactly like back then.
“Iherno Kar Verdei...”
However, it played out completely differently.
Stab.
Before Hans J could finish casting, a dagger skewered him in the lungs.
Choke!
It was the kind of quick reaction that could only be achieved by someone who was already lying in wait.
Slump.
When Hans J dropped, the eyes of the woman who had tried to appeal to him went wide. “H-How...?”
How do you think? I prepared to stab him just in case there was the slightest hint of him screwing around.

It was Erwen who’d stabbed a dagger into Hans J’s back. Even though she was badly injured enough that she couldn’t participate in battle, killing a wizard was easy, especially if she had been preparing to do so right behind him.
“Y-You! Why did you...?!” On the other hand, having never anticipated this, the priestess stared at us with her jaw dropped. It looked like she was still unable to accept Hans J’s betrayal.
“Why do you think? He’s a traitor.”
“That’s just her trying to turn us against each other! It hasn’t even been confirmed yet...!”
“But he suddenly cast a spell.”
The priestess’ face hardened at Erwen’s harsh words. “It’s possible the spell wasn’t aimed at us...!”
She wasn’t wrong. We couldn’t know for sure if Hans J’s spell was actually aimed at us, but humans were rational creatures.
“You really think that?”

Hans J would have realized it right away. We may have been able to write that woman’s words off as a tactic to turn us against each other for now, but if and when we got back to the city, we would have had questions. Because there was a possibility we could look into his background, the smartest thing for him to do was kill and silence everyone.
Anyway, this bastard really was the traitor.
I thought it was possible he wasn’t since there was no basis for my hunch aside from his name, but it seemed the Hans effect was scientific fact.
“Bjorn Yandel! Say something!” The priestess directed her arrow of criticism from Erwen to me, but I already knew how I would respond.
“Good job, Erwen.”
“It’s nothing. I just did as I was told.”
Yeah, but it’s the fact that you followed through and did it well that’s important.

Both Mr. Bear and Raven had gotten the same instructions, too, but they hadn’t been able to act as speedily as Erwen. The moment you killed someone, there was no going back. No matter how prepared you were mentally, there was still a psychological barrier to entry.
It’s possible she’s the one I can trust the most when it comes to things like this...
Entering another evaluation for Erwen in my mental database, I raised my shield. The moment I did, a pure white blade embedded itself in its metal face.
Bang!
Dang, not even a second to think, huh?
Well, since their trump card ended up misfiring, I was sure he felt a sense of urgency.
“Mr. Patzran! Mr. Patzran, say something! That elf struck down Mr. Aulock...!”
“Ersina, let’s discuss this later. It’s possible he really was going to betray us.”

Thankfully Patzran was not as naive as the priestess and postponed this conversation for later. Judging from his tone, it sounded like he had been surprised at first, but seemed to accept I’d made the right call.
Yeah, that’s how it should be. Anyone can see he was going to betray us sooner or later. Okay, then the betrayal plotline ended without trouble...
It was right when we returned to our original positions, each fighting our respective battles, that there was a setback.
“Mr. Yandel, Mr. Urikfried is—!”

chapters.title: Chapter 276: Vortex (2)
paragraphs: The line between life and death was at times drawn slowly, and at other times it was drawn in an instant. In the adventuring industry, it was usually the latter. Most injuries could be treated with potions or divine power, after all. Unless you suffered an injury that led to instant death or your entire team was wiped out, normally you would survive.
“Ahh, please wake up.”

However, there were cases like this, too, where potions and divine power did not work, like with wizard Riol Warb Dwalkie of Team Half-Wit. As he approached death, that man had given his last testament to those he was leaving behind, causing Missha and her comrades to feel a great sense of loss. Of course, there was a distinct difference between back then and right now.
“Hello? Woman whose name I don’t even know? Please...”

This was a stranger, not a precious comrade. Besides, her death wasn’t even certain like Dwalkie’s had been. There was a chance she could overcome this and survive. At the crossroads between life and death, it was completely up to this red-haired woman—and Missha—to decide which way she’d go.
“Ugh, just wake up alrrready!” Missha shouted and swung her sword harshly to vent some of her frustration. At the end of that sword were some of the monsters that were coming up from the sea.
Slash!

Enemies continued to appear no matter how much she cut, stabbed, and cut again. Missha was at her wit’s end. Unless she got out of here right now, she might never see Bjorn again. But it’d be impossible for her to carry this woman with her. Her injury had healed to some extent now and her breathing had stabilized, but in a situation where they were surrounded by monsters on all sides, how could she carry someone?
Slice!
She could only bring her along if the woman came to her senses and was able to follow along, no matter how slowly.
“I’m at my limit too, you know!” Missha shouted again, hoping her prodding might reach the woman’s subconscious.
“You...” The woman, who had been lying there like a corpse, finally opened her eyes.
“Y-You’re awake!” Missha said, delighted. “How are you feeling? Can you move?”
The woman just muttered to herself like she was trying to piece things together in her mind. “So, you protected me this whole time...”
“Yes! But I can’t go on doing that anymorrre. Okay? We need to get somewhere saferrr. Can you do it?”
There was a very brief pause. Then, “I can’t move.”
“What?”
“But I can take care of these monsters. I need you to take something out from my pocket for me.” Her voice was calm, so much so that it didn’t seem to be coming from the mouth of a dying person.

At that, Missha stopped fending off the monsters and rushed over to open the expandable pouch on the woman’s belt. Then she pulled out the item the woman spoke of. “A scrrroll? What kind of scroll is this?”
“Destruction of Evil.”

Missha was genuinely surprised. It was a scroll imbued with divine power and not just regular magic? Scrolls like these weren’t even produced anymore. How did this woman come across something so precious? Many questions filled her head, but they didn’t matter.

“Ahhh, why didn’t you tell me about this beforrre you passed out?!” Missha hurriedly tore the scroll open, and a translucent barrier imbued with the energy of the divine immediately obstructed the monsters. It was her first genuine break in a long time. “Ah, I can breathe now.” Now that she had a moment to recover, Missha quickly went up to the woman and asked one of the questions that had been on her mind since earlier. “Hey, so what’s your relationship with Bjorn?”
“That barbarian and I...”

“...Yeah, you and that barbarian... What? No. You don’t get to sleep yet, okay? Ah! Finish your sentence firrrst!” Missha went to shake the woman’s shoulder and stopped when she realized midway through that she was injured. Then, sighing, she slumped down to the ground. Now that her body could rest, concerns about her missing comrades rushed into her mind again. “...Everrryone is fine, right?”
Just then, a strong wind blew in from the sea, a chilly breeze that carried with it the scent of the ocean and was humid enough to feel sticky.
Shwaaa.
For some reason, Missha felt strangely anxious today.

It was a clash of weapons with the express purpose of killing the other party. Injuries were common in such battles, even if everyone was at the top of their game and made no mistakes. That was why adventurers were so often superstitious. They knew it too. Injuries during battle were inevitable, and the severity of those injuries at times depended on luck.
“Mr. Yandel, Mr. Urikfried is...!”

That was what happened to Mr. Bear today. The Drake’s claw broke Patzran’s sword as he was fighting on the front line, and that broken blade flew off and embedded itself in Mr. Bear’s body through no mistake of his own. If he’d been more agile it might have been possible for him to dodge it, but most people wouldn’t interpret what had happened as a mistake. It would be more accurate to say he had gotten unlucky.
“Bleeding...! The bleeding won’t stop!”

Some people survived falling down a ten-story building by luck, but others lost their lives just by slipping. Dungeon and Stone was a game that faithfully adhered to reality’s irrational side, which was something that had been very attractive to me until I woke up in this body.
“Priestess! Please, treatment...!”

Anyway, the problem was where the blade struck. Although it missed his heart, the sharp fragment did not stop at just slicing his lungs and ended up penetrating one. Puncture wounds caused the most bleeding, and one of his internal organs was injured.
[Lairin Ersina has cast Healing.]
The priestess used up her remaining divine power to heal him, but it was pointless.
[The target has been designated as a Dragon’s Offering. All healing effects have been nullified.]
That was the active skill of the rank-five monster, Drake. That damned summoner bitch must have cast it on Mr. Bear the moment she saw his injury.
“What are you looking at, barbarian?”
God damn it.
Bang!
I wanted to run and check on Mr. Bear right then and there, but I didn’t have that luxury. The same went for the others.
“I’ll watch over Mr. Abman. Everyone, focus on fighting!”

Realizing there was nothing they could do for Mr. Bear, who was teetering between life and death, they had no choice but to entrust him to Erwen and continue to fight. But the situation was not looking good.

The absence of wizard Hans J was a death sentence in itself, but while Patzran had been trying hard to fill that empty spot, he’d lost his weapon. That stroke of bad luck was then compounded by more bad luck and a fragment of that sword had stabbed Mr. Bear, further reducing the number of combatants on our side.
“Your name is Nebarce, right?”
“Here’s your bow back. You fight too.”
“...Is that okay?”
“I’m sure you don’t want to die here, either.” Erwen made the tough call to give Nebarce a weapon, but it didn’t change anything.
“Let’s go, Yongyong! Just a little longer!”

Even at a glance, a fight against a clearly buffed-up Drake and a summoner who had doused herself in supplemental essences to act as long-range support was rough. At that point, fighting a rank-four monster would have been no better, and “dogshit” wasn’t a strong enough word to describe our current state of affairs. Erwen was out of MP and Soul Power, and the priestess’ divine power was being consumed faster than she could recover it. Even Patzran, who was in charge of the vanguard, had lost his sword. The addition of one archer could not drastically turn the tide.
It’ll be tough to ask those guys for support.

It was a bittersweet feeling, but I had to admit it now. Things had changed, and so my strategy needed to be revised again. Originally, I intended to play things as safe as possible and wage a long battle, confirming my opponent’s essences one by one.
There’s no time.
Mr. Bear wouldn’t last that long. I had to finish this battle as quickly as possible to ensure that Dragon’s Offering was lifted.
And to do that... I’ll need to make the necessary sacrifices.
It would require a bit of determination. What could you give up and what could you gain? I’d already done the math. So what about my opponent?
“You’ve gotten antsy now that your comrade has been hit, barbarian!”
What could this guy—who was laughing like he’d already won—give up to stop me?
I guess I’ll find out soon.
I kicked off the ground with a roar. “Behel—aaah!”

I didn’t feel the usual burst of energy wrap around my body. That was only natural since I didn’t even have the MP left to use Wild Outburst. However, the protection of my ancestral gods would still be with me since they favored warriors who ran with wild recklessness in their hearts.
Whip!
Mm, or not.

As soon as the distance between us narrowed, the guy thrust his sword at me. This had already happened several times throughout this battle. Whenever this guy took a stab at me, I raised my shield to block it. That forced me to waste my turn while giving him the opportunity to jab a blade into my forearm or thigh before retreating to safety. That had been his attack pattern until a little while ago.
Yeah, I won’t stop you.
As he thrust his sword at me, this time I swung my mace instead of raising my shield. That meant it was his turn to make a choice. What would he do?
The swordsman was confused by the sudden change in battle rhythm and hurriedly took a step back before withdrawing his sword. Why couldn’t we exchange blows like men?
I knew he’d do that, though.
I expected this to happen so as soon as he widened the distance between us, I kicked off the ground and altered my trajectory, turning toward the Drake and its summoner.
Leap.
I used my MP, which had recovered just enough for one move, and used Leap.
Booom!
A cloud of dust spread across the landing zone. Because I wasn’t in Giantization mode, Recoil didn’t apply. That wasn’t important, though.
“Grk?” The Drake noticed me appearing on its other side near the forest and opened its mouth.
Your breath stinks, asshole.
Smack!
As soon as our eyes met, I smacked its muzzle with my mace.
“Gweeek!” Its head turned sharply, but a strike like that wouldn’t do much against a large-sized monster. But, so what? My real target was that irritated woman on top of it.
“Ugh, honestly! Can’t you stop this one guy!?”
I kicked off the ground again, bouncing up like a spring. But right at that moment, a blade dug into my back.
Stab.
It was clearly that bastard from earlier. Man, did he get all the way over here already?
“What took you so long?!” the summoner shrieked, even as she watched the swordsman stop me in my tracks with a sword through the lung.
I couldn’t help but question her actions. “Why...”
Do you think I can’t move or something? It’s not like there’s a hole in my neck.
Slide.
I took a step forward with the sword still inside me. Then I slammed the mace I was holding down.
Whooom!
The target was that whiny summoner’s head.
Stab!
The sword in my back withdrew, which made me flinch, but my arm did not stop moving. But right at that moment, he stabbed me again.
Whooosh. Stab!
This time, it dug into the elbow of the arm holding the mace. The joint was shattered, not just the skin and my grip on the mace loosened.
Bastard, showing off your fighting experience, huh? Well, I guess the same goes for me. Flesh Burst.
I decided to sacrifice the arm that was already useless.
Pop!
He had noticed that I had Acid Fluid while fighting me, but it seemed he never expected my body to explode.
Chhhhhh!

“Ahhh!” Covered in my blood and flesh, the guy moaned in pain and stepped back. This was the good thing about the Corpse Golem’s essence. Since it was a rare essence, no one knew about it. The fact that it used HP instead of MP was useful in this particular case too.
Clunk.
Just then, the mace in my hand rolled to the floor. That was fine. Although not as good as the mace, my hand was an excellent weapon.
Smack!

I then thwacked the summoner with my shield and she fell off the saddle and onto the ground with a shriek. I could see one of her arms was bent at an odd angle. That was a little disappointing. If I had gotten her in the head, I could have killed her in one hit. The Drake just had to jerk right as I was about to hit her, making it so I couldn’t crack her dainty skull.
I just need to hit her one more time.
Channeling the spirit of a barbarian who got knocked down seven times and laughed eight, I went to jump off the Drake’s back. But what was this?
Voom!
My falling body was suddenly sent flying upward. The Drake had thrown me up with the back of its neck. The summoner quickly moved out of sight, but it wasn’t all bad news.
Stab!
Patzran took advantage of the Drake’s flashy move and stabbed his broken sword into its chest.
“Keeek!”

Did the sword pierce somewhere around its heart? The Drake struggled violently before disappearing in a flash of light. Its summoning had finally been lifted. And now that the status effect on Mr. Bear had also been lifted, it would be possible to heal him with divine power. My first wish had been fulfilled.
Bang!
With that thought in mind, I hurriedly picked myself up off the ground. And that was when...
Ssshing!
A sharp sword was held against my neck. “You monster.”
Despite not minding the compliment, I had no energy left to block or avoid his sword. However, there was a silver lining. This guy couldn’t kill me right now.
“Everyone stop! Unless you want to see him die!” the bastard shouted at my comrades.
My comrades angled their own weapons at the unconscious summoner’s neck. “No, you drop that sword. Unless you want to see this woman die.”
Much like a hostage exchange, a tense silence ensued.
Trudge.
At that moment, two women emerged from the forest.
“B-Bjorn...?! What the hell is going on?!” One was Missha, for whom I had been searching so desperately.
“You look like you’re in a pickle, barbarian.” The other was Amelia Rainwales.
How were these two together? Just what had happened? Many questions popped into my head, but I focused solely on one thing. Their appearance was a net positive.
“Amelia Rainwales, so you were alive,” the man said to Amelia, sword still pointed at my neck. “That’s for the best. Help us.”
“The fact that you can say that to me after what you did must mean you have some kind of reason I should?”
“Of course. We’ve hidden that item somewhere on this island. If we die like this, it will be lost forever. Do you really want that?”
Amelia frowned at those words. Having met this woman several times already, I knew what that meant as soon as I saw it.
God damn it.
That was the expression she wore when she was thinking something over, and whatever conclusion she came to would probably decide our fate. I stared at Amelia, unable to speak.
“Belverson Erfner. Have you heard of the top two ways to make someone angry?”
“...What?” The swordsman let out a baffled noise at that totally random question.
Either way, Amelia pressed on. “The first is to stop talking in the middle of a sentence. Unfortunately, I didn’t get to hear the second. But if I were to hazard a guess...”
“...Yes?” the swordsman asked, too curious not to take the bait. The same went for me. Did this woman know the answer?
Anticipation mounted in the uneasy silence. Amelia continued without batting an eye. “It’s... stabbing them in the back mid-speech.”
Ah.
Dash.
The moment Amelia finished speaking, I sensed a presence behind me. It was obvious what—or who—it was.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Self-Replication.]
The swordsman belatedly realized what was going on and shoved me away before whirling around.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Asura’s Kick.]
But it was already too late.
Bam!
Amelia’s doppelganger appeared behind him and landed a blow on the swordsman’s temple.
Slump.
The swordsman dropped to the ground, his eyes already losing focus. “Why...?” he mumbled. “That item... to you...”
“Yes, it’s something I’ve sought my whole life.”
“Then why...?”

Amelia approached us in an instant, pressed down on the swordsman’s head with her foot, and said, “It doesn’t matter if you hid it or not. I can just learn where it is from your sister. There’s no way that bitch can handle an interrogation.”
She was a very sensible woman.

chapters.title: Chapter 277: Vortex (3)
paragraphs: “N-No...!” Those were the man’s last words, but Amelia paid them no mind and slammed her foot down, crushing his head like a dropped watermelon.
Chomp.
It felt a bit anticlimactic, such a fierce battle ending like this.
“Barbarian.” Soon, Amelia’s attention turned to me. “You’re very injured.”
“And you’re missing an arm.”
“Didn’t have enough time.”
What’s time got to do with it? Are we having two different conversations?
Just when those questions popped into my head, Amelia searched the man’s corpse and found a severed arm in his sub-space. “To think he kept it.”
The heck? Why is that in there?
I frowned involuntarily but Amelia just calmly brought the arm to the stump it had been severed from.
You think that’s going to stick?

“It’ll take a day for the nerves to return to normal.” All she did was press it there for about ten seconds, but her arm adhered to her body like she’d glued it on. Seeing as the proportions were just right, it seemed to be her own arm.
Come to think of it, she did say she can’t take potions.
I recalled a short conversation I’d had with Amelia in the past, in the sewer.
“...Did you not take a potion?”
“It’s because of my body type.”
So, she does have that essence.

Source of Youth was a passive skill that made the body unable to tolerate any healing effects, including potions, but greatly increased the user’s natural healing factor. It was a skill that offered a lot of bang for its buck as it could heal even severed limbs if given enough time.
“B-Bjorn! Arrre you okay?! Why are you so hurt again?!”
Ah, right. Now isn’t the time for that.
I belatedly came to my senses and pushed myself off the ground. I was ridiculously curious about what had happened to Missha, but that could wait until later. “I’m okay. Help me move.”
“Oh, okay. Come here!”
I hobbled over to my comrades with Missha’s help. Everyone gathered in one place.
“Miss Karlstein... I’m so glad you’re okay. Mr. Yandel was so worried...”
“Ah, sorry I’m late. There was an incident. But who’s that lying on the grrround...?” Then, after seeing the fallen man’s face, Missha jumped. “A-Abman?! I-Is he dead...?”
Raven did not answer. She just looked down at her feet, her eyes full of sorrow.

When I removed my hand from her shoulder, Missha hurried over to Mr. Bear and checked him over. “He’s... not brrreathing...” Missha turned to me with wide eyes and quickly moved her hand to Mr. Bear’s heart. “There’s... no pulse either. I-Is he really...?” She dropped her head, unable to finish.
“...Yes,” Raven said through a tight throat, sounding like she was about to cry.
You couldn’t write a better comedy if you tried.
“Yes” what? Ugh, I’ll end up dying first at this rate.

“Why are you killing off someone who’s alive and well?” I dragged my tattered body over to Mr. Bear and turned the bracelet on his wrist over so it was visible—No. 7611: The Deceit of the Necromancer. When the wearer took fatal damage, they fell into a state of suspended animation and became immune to all damage for a specified period of time. Of the three jewels on the bracelet, there was now only one that gave off light. “Looks like... it worked fine.”
But did Raven not know about this item or something? “Excuse me? What do you...?”
I didn’t have the energy for a lengthy explanation, so I just took the stopper off a potion and poured it over Mr. Bear’s body.
Chhhhhh.
His slightly dried blood began to boil and form bubbles. That was proof that Mr. Bear was still alive. Potions did not affect someone who had already departed.
“Ersina, what... are you doing? Treat him, quick.”
“A-Ah... yes! I will!” When the priestess threw in healing on top of the potion, Mr. Bear’s wounds quickly began to close.
Whew, it’s safe to say he should survive now.

It was truly a relief that I managed to get to him before the item’s effects wore off, that I’d fought through the desire to pass out immediately and stayed awake. Without me, everyone would still have been crying over what they thought was a dead body.
Erwen approached me. “Mister, you come here too. You need treatment quick...”
But it seemed to ensure Mr. Bear’s survival had caused all tension to leave my body. “Ah.” Yeah, I needed treatment too.
“Huh?”
Just as I was about to take a step forward, the ground began to tilt.
Slump!
That was my last memory of that day.
When I woke up, my surroundings were dark. Above me, I could see a sliver of a night sky between the dense trees and dark leaves.
Crackle, crackle!
I heard the sound of a bonfire nearby. The strange sense of coziness made me want to linger in this moment for a little longer.
First thing’s first, take stock of the situation.

I dug my fingers into the ground and forced my upper body up off the floor. From my shoulders to my back to my calves, there wasn’t a single part of me that wasn’t sore. Thanks to my Pain Resistance, though, it was a different sensation from pain.
“Phew.” I let out a long breath.
Did she wake at that small sound? The tree-hugger in the sleeping bag beside me rubbed her eyes and poked her face out.
“...Mister! You’re awake!” It was Erwen. “Are you feeling okay?”
“...For now,” I replied, glancing around at our surroundings. There were several sleeping bags laid out, and it looked like everyone was sleeping.
I guess we’re camping out.
When I checked, I could see a translucent barrier holding back a hoard of monsters, a sign that Destruction of Evil was active. Oh, and of course, there was also someone on watch.
“Looks like you’re finally awake.” Amelia Rainwales was a woman I’d encountered several times by chance before, though I was still unsure whether those encounters were ill-fated or not.
“...What happened?”
“It’s been about a day since you fell unconscious. That’s all.”
Hmm, I don’t think I was asking how long it’s been.
“I meant why were you with Missha, why were you betrayed by your comrades, and is there anything else I need to know?”
“I see.” When I rephrased my question in a way that even a three-year-old child could understand, Amelia nodded. “Ask your teammates, then.”
Ha, feisty.
“Erwen, tell me.” I redirected my interrogation to Erwen and got the basic rundown.
“I-I don’t know where to start... First, I’ll start with what happened after you collapsed.”

Apparently after I passed out, my comrades were a mess because I had been impossible to treat. Mr. Bear had been unhealable because of the Drake’s skill, but the swordsman had gotten me with a poisoned sword, and the wounds were tough to deal with.
“H-He’ll definitely die at this rate.”
“What? We can just use magic!”
“Detox spells are general fixes—they’re not specialized to specific types of poison, so they won’t work.”
“Th-then what about divine power?”
“This poison is so potent that it’s miraculous he even managed to stay on his feet for this long. In my state, I don’t have enough divine power to drive it out.”
“Bjorn is not the kind of warrior who should die in a place like this! Save him!”
Neutralizing the poison using magic was too difficult, and the priestess was completely drained, making heals impossible. That was when Amelia stepped forward.
“Use this. It’s probably an antidote.”
Amelia found the antidote in the swordsman’s bag and handed it to us, and the poison was neutralized with that.
“Thankfully, the medicine worked great. When we gave you a potion after that, your wounds started to heal.”

That ended the recap of my health problems, but what followed was still chaotic. Monsters were still flocking in from all sides, and everyone was in the worst condition possible. Meanwhile, they had to take care of an unconscious me and Mr. Bear, making things even harder.
“Still, thanks to her help... we were able to hold out until the priestess could use Destruction of Evil again.”
“Cut to now,” I assumed.
“Huh? No. This is our third time taking a break like this.”
When Ersina first activated the barrier, apparently things got basically as bloody as when they were fighting the monsters because of none other than Patzran and Amelia.
“We may have had no choice but to join forces until now, but this woman is a plunderer from Noark. She cannot be trusted. She was the one who attacked us in the first place.”
“E-Eh?! N-Noark?!”
“You didn’t know that while you were traveling with her? You were lucky in many ways.”
Patzran did not hide his animosity toward Amelia, and Amelia was no different. She wasn’t the one to instigate the hostility, though.
“You’re a talkative man. If you want to fight, let’s fight.”
Confronting his animosity head-on, she poured fuel on the fire of conflict. But just when murderous intent began to fill the barrier, Missha defended Amelia.
“S-Stop it, all of you! I didn’t know this woman was from Noark, but... still, she’s not a bad perrrson!”
Raven assessed the situation rationally as well and tried to mediate.

“What are we going to do without her? Mr. Patzran, think logically. She was betrayed by her comrades too. I’m sure she won’t attack us while there are only two of them left. If she wanted to, she would have done so a long time ago.”
Of course, the parties in question did not even try to listen to logic.

“You mean I should let go of my grudge just because things are different now? That woman hurt Drous and even went as far as to send people after us. If we hadn’t managed to handle it, we would be dead.”
“How unfortunate. If you’d died then, I wouldn’t have had to hear this whining of yours now.”
“What did you say? You plunderer bitch...!”
Patzran drew his second sword, which he carried as a backup, and Amelia drew her dagger and faced him.
“Yes. Wise choice, Mr. Patzran.”
Patzran did not end up swinging his sword. I didn’t know him that well, but I knew he wasn’t that stupid.
“I’m keeping my eyes on you, so don’t even think about pulling something funny.”

After that, an uncomfortable break followed. Once the barrier was lifted, they fought monsters again, and once the cooldown time of Destruction of Evil passed, they took a break. It was during the second break that Mr. Bear woke up.
“Haha... keep today a secret from my wife. She’ll definitely make me stop working as an adventurer.”
Mr. Bear worried about the fallout of today’s events as soon as he woke up but quickly recovered his energy and joined the front line.
“From that point on, the monsters showing up suddenly changed.”

While I was unconscious, the third wave had begun. The mini-boss was a rank-four monster. The priestess got hit by the boss and knocked out, and there were some other close calls, but Amelia got us through it by playing the role of main damage dealer.
“Essence?”
“None.”
Hah, of course. Is it just the final boss left now? I really hope that guy will drop an essence. Well, before that, I should probably worry about whether we’ll be able to kill it or not.

Many thoughts filled my mind but I set them all aside and continued listening to Erwen’s story. There wasn’t much else to it. Her explanation was long-winded, but in the end, all that happened was more fighting, breaks, and continued tension between Patzran and Amelia.
“So that’s how we got to now.”
“Yes, did that sate your curiosity?” asked Erwen.
“Somewhat. Thanks. You must be tired too. Get some rest.”
“...It’s okay. I’ll stay by your side.”
Mm, I mean, that’s not really necessary, but...
It would probably be weird for me to say something here.
“But, Mister, um... Shouldn’t you wake Sis?”
“Missha? It’s fine. She knows I’m alive and physically all right, so why wake her up? Let her sleep.”
Just look at how no one is waking up even as we’re talking right next to them.
They must have been exhausted from the arduous battles. We could talk later. It was time to listen to the other side of the story now.
“Long time no see, Amelia.” I got out of the sleeping bag completely, sat down in front of the campfire, and expressed my thanks. “Earlier... No, thank you for helping me yesterday.”
“You talk a lot for a barbarian. Just ask me what you want to ask.”
Barbarians can talk too, you know...
Well, whatever. Getting straight to the point was always a welcome change. “What happened with Missha?”
“Did you not hear about it from that elf?”
“I thought I should hear it from your own mouth.”

“...Tsk.” Amelia clicked her tongue in apparent annoyance, but surprisingly did not complain much and told me what happened. She had been betrayed by Carmilla and Belverson and, while running away, had encountered Missha and gotten help from her. I was very surprised by what followed.

“What? A Destruction of Evil scroll? You had something as valuable as that?” The techniques for crafting these divine scrolls had disappeared a long time ago and they were no longer made. They were priceless treasures.
Where the hell did she get— Oh. She probably looted it.
“Ahem, sorry for interrupting. Keep going.”
“That’s a nasty look in your eyes.”
“You’re just imagining things.”
Thanks to the Destruction of Evil scroll, Amelia and Missha were able to survive the wave of monsters. After that, they had physically recovered enough to move.
“I still don’t understand. How did the two of you get through all those monsters and get this far?”
“...There’s an essence. One that prevents monsters from attacking you first.”
Oh, you have that essence? But why absorb that one if you’re a scout? You could just bring along a priest to handle that... Ah, wait, there are no priests in Noark.
And come to think of it, she was a plunderer. That essence would have been very useful for wandering alone in the labyrinth.
“So, is that the last of your questions?”
“No, I have a few more.”
“Ask.”
“Do you know what caused the island to become like this?” Who had triggered the special event on this island?

My question was a bit vague, but Amelia gave me an answer. “Carmilla and Belverson messed with the Arrangement of Gabrielius. When I got away from them alive, I guess they figured they had to trap me here somehow and eliminate me.”
Hmm, so that’s the story.

One of those two might have been a player as well. The Arrangement of Gabrielius denoted a hidden element, but it seemed that few players even knew about the secret event on this island in the first place.
“Is this what that summoner woman told you while you were interrogating her?”
“Yes.”
“What did you do to her?”
“I don’t believe in being merciful toward traitors.”
So she killed her. Ugh, why kill her after barely managing to capture her alive?

I couldn’t hold back my sigh of disappointment. After all, that woman was a rare kind of adventurer who could summon and control a flying beast. We could have used her to escape this island right away.
But what’s done is done.
Instead of blaming Amelia and hurting our relationship, I turned my attention elsewhere. “Anyway, did you find what you were looking for?”
Amelia went silent as if she was debating whether to answer me or not.
“Hey,” I wheedled, “what’s there to hide between the two of us now?”
“Hmm? Between us?”
“I saved your life, after all.”
“What do you mean by that?”
“Do you think Missha would have saved you if we didn’t know each other?”

Amelia seemed to agree with that logic as she didn’t argue. She just clicked her tongue and answered my question. “The item was retrieved. Contrary to his claim that it was hidden, it was right in his sub-space.”
“Somehow, I had a feeling it would be. There’s no way those guys would let that treasure out of their sight.”
“Then is that the last of your questions?”
No, of course not.
“Just one more,” I said before finally asking, “What is the item? From what I’ve heard, it sounds like it’s powerful enough to change history—”
“Stop.” Amelia cut me off firmly, her forehead creasing.

Oops, was this a touchy subject? “Don’t answer if you don’t want to. I was just asking out of curiosity!” Noticing the tight corners of Amelia’s mouth, I quickly made an excuse insisting that I didn’t intend to pry. But did I misread the situation?
Amelia stared off into space and made a random remark. “Monster.”
...Monster?
Shaaa!

As soon as I tilted my head, a powerful wind blew through our campsite from all directions, shaking the nearby tree branches. Only then did I realize what she was talking about. Jeez, and I had wanted to rest a little longer.
“There’s a monster in this area. At least rank three. Go wake your comrades.”
So, the last wave had begun after all.

chapters.title: Chapter 278: Vortex (4)
paragraphs: Farune Island’s hidden Easter egg was the Fury of the Sea. The difficulty of this special event, which was triggered when the altar was destroyed while fewer than twenty people occupied the island, was determined by the number of people present. With five to nine people, there was an increase in the number of ordinary monsters that spawned. With ten to fourteen, a fourth wave of monsters was added and the final boss appeared. With fifteen to nineteen, some of the final boss’s restrictions were removed.
I didn’t think I would be raiding a rank three while so unprepared...

The longer I thought about it, the more I wanted to sigh. What I had been aiming for was the boss of the third wave. If we’d managed to trigger the event with only six people, the fourth wave wouldn’t have even started. My plan had been to take down large trash mobs and collect a bunch of mana stones and essences to sell, and if possible, secure a rank-four essence for Erwen. But nothing had gone as planned.
...Why does my life always turn out like this?

It wasn’t enough that the event had been triggered on the highest difficulty level. The number of people on the island had gradually decreased to the point that we were now facing the last wave with ten people. Even the Elfroth’s essence hadn’t appeared as I hoped. Of course, if the final boss were to cough up an essence, I could happily bounce back from that.
But it’ll be hard to take down.

In this situation, survival was more important than loot. That was what rank-three monsters were like in this game. We may have been adventurers who had reached the sixth floor, but as ten people who had never fought together as a team, this was a beast that was virtually impossible for us to hunt.
But what can we do? We have to try.
I lifted myself up.
“The blessing will soon disappear.” The priestess spoke as if she had been waiting for this to happen.
“Exactly how much time is left?”
“Ten minutes.”
So, ten minutes...
I nodded and looked around. I could see Patzran and Amelia conversing a short distance away.
“A rank-three monster, are you sure?”
“The truth won’t change just because you don’t believe it.”

“You speak as if you saw the monster with your own eyes. Danger Detection isn’t that accurate an ability. I heard the information you get from it is conveyed in the form of shapes and sensations, and it often ends up either exaggerating or underestimating the strength of a monster.”
It was a tedious doubt and a tedious conversation. I turned away from them and approached someone else: Missha Karlstein, my oldest comrade, who had been with me in the labyrinth for the longest.
“Bjorn...”
The one thing I can’t call her is my lover, though.
I smiled ruefully and asked, “How are you holding up?”
“I think I should be the one asking you that...”
“I’m okay. A little under the weather, but that’s probably because I slept so long.”

After that, I took the time to talk to Missha. It wasn’t to tell her a secret plan I couldn’t tell anyone else or something, but because I hadn’t had a proper conversation with her yet. Right after we reunited, I spent the whole day knocked out, and now that I was awake, the last wave was beginning, leaving us no time.
“I was really worried.”
“I’m... sorry. That woman seemed to know you so I couldn’t leave her—”
“You’re supposed to say, ‘I won’t make you worry anymore.’”
“Okay. I won’t.”
Okay, that solves that problem. What do we talk about now?
“Anyway, I’m glad everrryone is all right. I was really worried, to be honest. For some reason, I had a strange feeling...”
“Strange feeling?”
“...Nothing to worry about. Now that I think about it, I was just anxious after being separated from you guys.”
True, that was generally how people worked. Negative thoughts were usually more vivid than positive ones.
“...But is it okay for us to be chatting like this?”
Why not? That priestess is just sitting there praying too.

Mr. Bear was even writing a letter. Was it because he’d already come back from the dead once in the past two days? As soon as he heard that a rank-three monster had appeared, it seemed he remembered some things he wanted to say to his wife.
“Urakburak! Why are you doing something so silly!? You can tell her the name of your child yourself once you get home!”
“Whatever, just tell me, what name do you think would suit a girl? You’re... ahem, a woman yourself.”
What, was he seriously naming his child right now? This was freaking me out... I wished he’d stop raising all these flags.
“...This rrreminds me of last time.”
“Oh, when we were trapped on the first floor?”
“Yes. The mood was just like this back then.”

Like this? Compared to back then, this was nothing. Even Raven took the time to make a will and asked us to bring it back to the city if she didn’t survive. Most of that will dealt with the issue of money.
“Anyway, Bjorn, you’rrre the same now as you were then.”
“About not leaving a will?”
“Yeah.”

I ended up chuckling. There was no one outside the labyrinth to whom I could bequeath a will in the first place, and even if I died, I didn’t want to reveal my identity. That would leave behind a much better memory.
“But Missha, you didn’t leave a will, either.”
“Yes, but...” Missha trailed off.
It seemed there was something she wanted to say to me, so I cut her off. “Let’s stop with all this depressing talk. We got home alive last time, didn’t we? It will be the same this time.”
“...Yeah. You’re the one saying it, so I believe it.”
Afterward, we stopped worrying about the present and moved onto lighter topics.
A while later, Amelia called out to me. “Barbarian. It’s time.”
Peaceful moments like this always flew by.
“Haha, a rank-three monster. How exciting!” Ainar was already holding her greatsword, which she had been rigorously sharpening with a whetstone in our downtime.
“Honestly, Miss Ainar... Is now really the right time to get excited? When we might all die?” Raven scolded.
“Now, now. Stop fighting. Everyone, take this.” Mr. Bear handed out letters covered in crooked writing to each of his teammates.
The priestess also stood up after a long prayer. “May the light shine on the path we take.”
“Missha.”
“Yeah.”
After sending Missha back, I stood at the front of the formation, lifting up my mace and shield. Before long, the barrier surrounding us shattered.
[Destruction of Evil has deactivated.]
It was time to roll the dice.
“Keeeeeek!”
As soon as Destruction of Evil lifted, the group of monsters camped out in front of the barrier began to attack, and Raven called out the trigger for the magic circle she had prepared in advance.
“Sartum Ebehel!”
This was a military spell that ordinary wizards were not permitted to learn due to its abnormally high lethality for its rank.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-4 attack spell Collapse.]
The moment the magic circle began to glow, red targets appeared on the vital points of the hundreds of monsters rushing toward us.
Crackkk!

About two seconds later, explosions rang out, and numerous monsters were torn apart. A horde of rank-six monsters was practically swept away with one shot of magic. Of course, these incredible results weren’t obtained without a price.

“...I’m going to rest now.” With this one spell, Raven had consumed almost all of her mana and we could no longer expect support from her. Her role was now to conserve her mana and replenish MP until the final boss showed up.
“Behel—aaah!”
Therefore, the remaining enemies were up to us.
“Keeeeeek!” The dense group of monsters had been annihilated, but more monsters flooded in from all sides, filling the gaps.
Chomp, chomp, chomp!
Only activating Giantization, I focused solely on fulfilling my role as a shield for my comrades so they could comfortably deal damage. We already had enough firepower for a trash mob, anyway.
Whiiip! Stab! Kwaaang!
The three-person long-range damage team consisted of Erwen, Nebarce, and Mr. Bear.
[Ainar Fenelin has killed an opponent. Satiation has activated and Soul Power is restored.]

Ainar showed off her true worth while facing multiple weak enemies. Rank-four adventurer Patzran also pulled his weight, and Missha used her characteristic speed to pass me by and get rid of the enemies making a break for the rear.
She really fights well.
The most impressive was Amelia. She refused the position I tried to assign her, saying she’d handle things herself, and she really was capable of doing just that.
Slice!

Ten monsters disappeared into bursts of light with a single stroke of her dagger as she danced through them like a one-woman army. If you counted the doppelgangers she’d summoned through Self-Replication, that number went up to at least fifteen. I was a little worried about that, though.

“Wouldn’t it be better to conserve a bit of strength?” MP was one thing, but the thing I was most concerned about was Mana, another resource consumed when using an aura. If she used all of it now, she might not be able to use it against the boss later.
“I know my own limitations best, so stop ordering me around.”
“...If you say so.” What could I say to that? If she had a brain, she’d be able to pace herself. She had more live combat experience than me, anyway.
I just need to do my job well.

Holding my shield, I focused only on blocking the incoming monsters. I swung my mace at times, but only enough to push our enemies back out of the assessment that my MP should be conserved for later. Unless I used Swing, I had to hit the monsters at least ten times to kill them.
“The monsters are gradually decreasing too.”
The more mana stones began piling up around us, the more the number of monsters flocking us decreased.
“Maybe that means the priestess’s prayer worked!”

Mr. Bear and the others looked delighted by that suggestion, but I remained quiet. That was because I knew that all the monsters we’d been fighting so far were the ones left over from the third wave that we hadn’t managed to kill. The fourth wave didn’t have regular monsters. Yeah, that was the least this game could do if it had any conscience at all. How would we have been able to take down a rank-three boss monster if this place was riddled with trash mobs too?
“Let’s build up some more steam!” Anyway, the positive news boosted the group’s morale.
“Looks like there are no more in the area now.”
Time passed and the trash mobs were finally cleaned up. We quickly picked up the mana stones, reorganized our formation, and took a short break as we waited. It lasted for only about ten minutes.
“It’s here,” Amelia said, her voice low. No one asked which direction. Everyone raised their heads and turned to one spot in particular as soon as she spoke.
Boom.
Beyond the bushes, we heard heavy footsteps. Then, the monster smashed through a tree and showed itself.
Boom!
“Kwohhhhhh!” This was the first rank-three monster we were facing.
Upon sighting it, Raven screamed out the information she knew. “...I-It’s a Storm Gush!”

Storm Gush was a rank-three aquatic monster nicknamed the Ogre of the Sea. To describe it in more detail, it was similar to a crustacean, though that didn’t mean it had a lobster-like appearance. Its fifteen-foot-tall body was covered in thick, hard shells, but its basic form was that of a Lizardman.
Boom!
Its long tail served as a counterweight and its snout protruded. It walked on two legs and wielded a weapon even with its ridiculous physique.
Boom!
When the monster fully revealed itself, everyone gulped.
“That’s a rank-three monster...”

It was an uncommon monster that clans on the seventh floor had to fight in the dozens. I’d fought many monsters of this size before, but this guy exuded a menace that was in a whole other league. Still, it wasn’t anything compared to the Lord of the Floor.
I hurriedly shouted, “Prepare for battle!”
What are you all blanking for? We’re already within his range.
“Kwohhh!”

With a massive harpoon in his hand, the boss charged at us, moving with an incredible agility that that bulky body didn’t seem capable of. I immediately turned on Giantization (Transcendence) Mode. You needed to be in the same weight class to fight with a guy like this.
[Your Physique will increase in proportion to your Strength.]

My warrior’s body began to grow in an instant. The look in the charging monster’s eyes slowly began to change, from that of someone looking at easy prey to someone facing an enemy. That was fair—the last time I measured my height in this state, I was just over fifteen feet. He probably never thought there could ever be a human tall enough to meet his eye.
“Behel—aaah!” Soon, with Wild Outburst, my Physique stats jumped and I ran forward. If he overpowered me in terms of strength in our very first exchange, I would definitely be looked down on.
Kwaaang!
A few steps later, his trident struck my shield. “Heavy” wasn’t a strong enough word to describe the blow.
So, even in this state, I’m outmatched.

Bumping into him flung my body back. I hadn’t experienced that since receiving the passive skill Union with one of my Immortality Imprints. Not that it came with a knockback bonus or anything, but ever since my equipment started growing with me when I Giantized, it had become much easier to talk about my weight in units of tons.
“What are you all doing? Attack!”
As soon as I was thrown back, Ainar swung her adamantium greatsword.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Wildness Control. All effects applicable to her next attack will be converted into Cutting Force.]

This was one of the various conversion-type skills that converted the effects of bonuses into Cutting Force upon landing a hit. And that was on top of the weight of the greatsword itself and the kinetic force of the downward strike.
Khak!

However, Ainar’s greatsword only penetrated about half an inch into the monster’s carapace, leaving a dent in the shell. Instead of interpreting this as a lack of ability on Ainar’s part, it’d be more accurate to call that monster horrifying. It was not for nothing that he was called the Ogre of the Sea. His Physical Resistance was insane. Well, that didn’t matter, though, because she wasn’t our main damager.

“I’ll be borrowing this.” A second later, Amelia jumped off my shoulder and leaped, stabbing the dagger into the monster’s shoulder. The dagger was covered in an aura that had the effect of disregarding Physical Resistance by 90 percent.
Stab!
Amelia’s dagger sank into the handle before coming out.
Shooot!

A dark green fluid shot from the wound due to the creature’s blood pressure, but it wasn’t a critical hit. This monster wasn’t weak enough that a wound like that could hurt it or interfere with its ability to move, and also, it had high Regeneration.
Whoom!
The boss monster then slashed at Amelia with its sharp claws. It moved at easily twice my speed, but it wasn’t fast enough to catch a true Agility-based fighter.
Dash.

As soon as Amelia evaded the monster’s counterattack by stepping back, I closed the distance to avert a further rampage. The fact that I lacked the strength to mark him one-on-one wasn’t a huge problem right now.
Pushhh.

I may have been the main tank, but it wasn’t like I had to block him on my own. A single push of his spear may have been able to shove me back, but there were several other warriors here who could distract him from the sidelines.
“Shell lizard! Get away from Bjorn!”
I quickly fired off orders. “Missha, Patzran! You guys help too! Keep your distance and only approach when he’s attacking me!”
This was the first priority for close-range damage dealers in a raid. As soon as the front line got set up according to my instructions, the battle began.
“Kwohhh!”

I was in charge of the big hits. If I got pushed back, the close-range damage dealers came in to distract him. Then, using that opening, I closed in on him again to attract aggro while Amelia attacked. We repeated this process over and over.
“The wound is already healing. Raven, start casting Aggravate! And tell us everything you know about this monster!”

Raven unleashed support magic while briefing us about the monster in real-time. “T-The ground! When the Storm Gush stomps its feet, you have to get far away! It does that when using a special ability called Eye of the Storm.”

It wasn’t enough information to be called a strategy, but even that tidbit was something I hadn’t explained to my comrades beforehand. After all, how could I have given them a strategy? Even though I knew exactly which monster would show up thanks to the game, all they had known at that point was that the monster was rank three, and nothing else.
But since Raven knows about it, I won’t need to step forward.

If Raven weren’t here, I would have had to handle the briefing because things were way too dangerous for me to do my usual routine of pretending to learn as I went. In a fight with a monster like this, a single blow could lead to a fatal injury. For example...
[Storm Gush has cast Eye of the Storm.]
Yeah, like this thing that Raven just told us about.
Boom.
After the monster stomped the ground with its foot, within a second, a vortex with a radius of fifteen feet appeared and sucked everything in for five seconds.
Whiiip!
The wind pressure could even be felt from one step away.
“Get back!”
Just in case they got swept up in it, everyone took another step outside of the blast radius. Of course, I was the opposite.
Dash.
Instead of backing away, I thrust my body right into the whirlwind.
“B-Bjorn? Where arrre you going?!”

Because Eye of the Storm was an aurora-type skill, the whirlwind was centered around the monster, not the location where it was created. Put simply, if the monster decided to charge at us, the vortex would move with it, and there was a chance someone would get caught up in it. Someone had to take charge of blocking it just to be safe.
Whiiip!
As soon as I entered the vortex, the wind roared and surrounded my body, but it didn’t suck me in toward the monster like a magnet.
[Your total weight is over 2000 lbs. Special ability Eye of the Storm has been bypassed.]
Yeah, it would have been weirder if this huge body could be blown away by a little wind.
Whip!
The real problem was him thrusting the trident at me in an environment where it was difficult to even open my eyes. To be honest, I didn’t even see it coming.
Bang!
My hand moved of its own accord and blocked the spear. Was this a side effect of risking my safety over and over until today?
Wow, I managed to react to that?
Now, my body reacted before my head.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
I relied on intuition to block the spear three more times, and the whirlwind subsided before I knew it.
Okay, then I should be able to widen the distance now.
Dash.
When I moved back, I could hear Raven’s shouts, which had been drowned out by the wind. “Mr. Yandel, what are you doing!? I just told you about that!”
It was a tongue-lashing meant for a teammate who refused to follow directions, but as a barbarian, I had only one thing to say to that. Since “I forgot” was a bit much even for me...
“Oh, sorry. I felt like I needed to do that.”

You’re the wizard, you should have been the first to tell me that heavy people might not get sucked in, so I should go inside and hold back the monster. Tsk, these local wizards. Don’t your books explain basics like that?
To me, that was a travesty.

chapters.title: Chapter 279: Vortex (5)
paragraphs: “Felt like you needed to? What nonsense!”
Uh oh, I think that set her off.

Before the conversation could drag on, I cut her off and changed the subject. We could give each other feedback on our performances later. “Ah, so what’s next? What should we look out for?” I asked, hurriedly marking the Storm Gush, my shield up.
Raven had no choice but to stop berating me and continue explaining. “Next is a special ability called Ley Line. When activated, the ground turns red—ah, now! Mr. Yandel, get out of the way!”
Booom!
Large lines formed under the targeted area and a column of air exploded moments later, just like that.
Shoooooot!
Whew, that almost came out of nowhere.
“Everyone, get back! A Vortex will soon come out of that hole.”

Anyway, Ley Line not only dealt powerful instantaneous damage, but it also generated a Vortex right on top of the hole in the ground it created. For reference, Vortex was the exact same skill used by the mini-boss Siren Queen.
Whoooom!

If I got hit by that, I would be airborne until my comrades managed to rescue me and my MP would be drained in proportion to however long that took. Well, at my weight, I was immune to ending up airborne.
My MP would still be stolen, though.
You had to avoid Vortex, unless you were as heavy as I was.
“Everybody, don’t stick together and spread out!”

The first Ley Line had struck the ground near us, increasing the difficulty of the battle significantly. In the middle of all this, we also had to avoid a tornado, limiting our movement. But even this combo had a quick and easy solution.
“From now on, we will fight on the move!”

We just had to move over. After all, this bastard was the only monster left on this island now. The entire island was its boss lair. There was no reason not to take advantage of the wide area we’d been given.
Actually, this method won’t get us very far, either.

This was one of the tricky things about dealing with this monster in a situation where we lacked heavy hitters. If this guy kept using Ley Line, our map would eventually shrink. And on top of all that...
“Huh? Why is the sea water here?”
As per the nature of Farune Island, the sea level gradually started rising at the beginning of the fourth wave until everything but the center of the island was submerged.
“Mr. Yandel! There’s a big problem! The water is rising! W-What do we do?”
What do you mean what do we do? We have to keep moving as we fight.
“Maintain formation. We’re heading toward the center!” Thankfully, no one questioned my instructions. It wasn’t like they could come up with a better strategy themselves.
[Storm Gush has cast Tyrant’s Roar.]
Even as we fought and moved, Storm Gush whipped out new skills.
“Priestess Ersina! That’s the one I mentioned earlier! Hurry, purify it!”

Although its effects were weaker depending on a target’s Mana Resistance and Spirit stats, Tyrant’s Roar was an area of effect skill that stunned creatures within a ridiculously wide radius of thirty feet for up to two seconds. Thankfully, this was easily countered with a Purification from the priestess.
[Storm Gush has cast Storm’s Kin.]
A berserker move that temporarily boosts Regeneration and Physique stats?
“Everybody, stay away!”
I took the entire hit and shouldered the damage. In return, I was left with holes all over my shield, armor, and body, but that last one could be dealt with by heals from the priestess.
The equipment, on the other hand... will break the bank a bit to repair.
I’d be lying if I said that didn’t leave a bitter taste in my mouth, but I could put up with it considering we were in the middle of a rank-three monster raid. Living was more important than money.
“Stomping! Everyone, get away!”

The Storm Gush cycled through four skills repeatedly, and over time, the team became more accustomed to his attack patterns, but it was too early to let our guards down. This guy had three more skills left that he hadn’t used.
Damn rank three.

This was the decisive difference between ranks three and four. Basic stats aside, the number of skills they had was different. Monsters of this level not only had skills from another monster’s essence, but also unique abilities, like a Vampire’s Black Magic, for example.
For this guy, it must be Weapons Expertise.

In-game, there were things like Critical Hits, Accuracy, Dodging, Defense Success Rate, etcetera. Weapons Expertise was one of many unique abilities on the list of battle features that could adjust stats, and Storm Gush clearly had a lot of it. Was that why?
Damn, he uses that spear well.
The thrusts of his spear were very intense for a monster. It felt like he wasn’t just applying force but some sort of deeper technique.
Anyway, he’ll probably use his remaining moves when he runs out of stamina.
“Mr. Yandel, did you hear that? Once that guy starts using the ability I just mentioned, everyone will be in danger. We have to think up some sort of plan now!”
Oh, stop screaming, will ya? I’ve already thought it through.

It was just that I’d been waiting because I’d look suspicious if I presented a countermeasure the minute she was done explaining. Once again, I had two plans thought up—Plan A and Plan B. A was best, and B was second best. The only problem was that these plans were impossible to coast through. From now on, we would have to engage in an intense battle unlike any we’d ever fought against a lower-level monster.

Those who got unlucky would get hurt, or even die. I could only hope, knowing this was selfishness disguised as selflessness, that if someone had to suffer through that misfortune, it wouldn’t be one of us.
Patzran, Ersina, Nebarce, Amelia.
While I was reminding myself of my priorities once again, Patzran shouted, “T-There’s nowhere left to run!”
Shwaaa!

Water was rising in the direction we were moving away from. It was impossible to escape by boat even if we wanted to because hundreds of tornadoes sprang up around the island once the first wave ended.
At this point, more than half the island is probably already underwater.
We didn’t have much time now.

“Let’s go over there!” I led the group toward the center of the island, taking the largest, most roundabout route we could, and asked my comrades for just one thing: to fight harder, even though it would be tough. “The monster needs to take as much damage as possible.”
“Do you have a plan?” Amelia asked, and I explained the plan I had laid out.
“...You came up with that just by listening to the wizard?” Patzran shot me a strange look at my explanation.
The priestess, on the other hand, expressed a concern. “But will that be enough? From what I can tell, it sounds like a far-fetched and risky plan.”
“Bjorn is a great warrior! He knows how to fight better than anyone!” Ainar did not miss the opportunity to gas me up.

“You’re... going to play that rrrole again?” Missha said sadly before announcing she would join me. Of course, I didn’t allow it. Even disregarding my affection for Missha, this was the most efficient formation.
So what did Raven, the poster child for efficiency, think? “It’s not a bad plan. Especially in that it prepares for failure.”
So, you’re giving the green light too.

“You don’t sound like you’re trying to trick me. Fine, I’ll do as you say.” Amelia was the one I had been most worried about, but when she also agreed to my plan, that took some of the weight off my shoulders. That surprised me a bit. I never thought she would accept her role so readily.
When I admitted to my slight doubts, Amelia said something unexpected. “Your words hold weight.”
Huh?
“I see what you mean.” Patzran, who had been arguing with Amelia this whole time, nodded. “You didn’t panic even when you learned a rank-three monster had appeared.”
That’s because I knew from the start that that would happen...

“The people who decided to follow you that day must have felt this way too.” The priestess also brought up the war with Noark on the first floor. “Bjorn, son of Yandel. A giant who opens the way in the forefront, and one who was born with the spirit of the times.”
I still didn’t get it even if they worded it like that, and that made me uncomfortable. It wasn’t like I’d been all that noble in front of them.
“In a situation where we can’t be certain of anything, seeing you safely reunited with your comrades gave me confidence. Destiny is with you.”
Oh, these religious freaks.

“...What are you talking about?” I let out an involuntary sigh. Of course I did, because regardless of whether they wanted to call me a hero, I knew my true nature. Just a moment ago, I had been praying for my people to be safe even if these guys had to die.
Why are you doing this to me?
The warrior’s heart in my chest pounded heavily. Was this some kind of barbarian instinct to want to live up to expectations?
“Behelaaah!”
Whatever, let’s fight.
Before I could feel a greater sense of responsibility toward these people, I entrusted my body to the battle and emptied my head.
[Storm Gush has cast Eye of the Storm.]
This again.
“Everyone, get back!” The moment the whirlpool appeared, I stuck to the boss monster right away and kept him in one place.
Whiiip!
