It was hard to see even an inch in front of me in the violent storm. Suddenly, this thought came to mind: wind was wind, no matter what. And no matter how much I prayed, I could not decide who died and who survived.
Kwaaang!
Much like this tornado, what would be on the other side of this storm was up to the gods.
“Mr. Yandel, there is nowhere left to retreat.”

Once we finished guarding against the Eye of the Storm pattern and moving again, we reached the center of the island, an empty lot tucked away in the bushes with a white stone pagoda in the center. There were still dark flecks of blood staining the ground. Just yesterday, I spent time praying here for what felt like an eternity.
“W-Water is rushing in from all sides!”
As the rest of the island sank, the sea was now visible in all directions.
[Storm Gush has cast Ley Line.]
Vortexes erupted from the holes in the ground the Storm Gush had created on the way here, mixing with the water and swirling around us.
Shaaaaaa!
If this were the game, I would have felt that this was the kind of glorious setting worthy of a boss fight.
Boom!
The Storm Gush appeared in front of us and slammed the staff part of his trident on the ground.
[Storm Gush has cast Rainmaking Ritual.]
This was one of his three remaining skills, which he only used once his HP dropped below 70 percent.
Okay, looks like we managed to chip away at his stamina as planned.
It was slowly becoming time to end the match.
Rainmaking Ritual was one of Storm Gush’s three core skills. Its effects were simple.
Pitter, patter.

It was raining. While contact with this rain increased Storm Gush’s Regeneration and overall Physique stats, player characters suffered various debuffs. Of course, that alone was a minor issue. The real problem was the next attack.
“What are you all doing!? Do as we planned!” With my cry kicking things off, everyone except for the rear guard rushed at the monster. As did I.
“Kwohhh!”

Unlike earlier, I really did not hold back in this assault, because that was our plan: all or nothing. We agreed that as soon as this guy used Rainmaking Ritual, we would hit him with everything we had to kill him in one go. As a result, there was no reason to hesitate. Every injury that accumulated on my body just made it all the easier for my team to deal him damage.
Stab!
Mr. Bear’s arrow dug deep into the monster’s hard shell. It likely barely pierced the flesh underneath, but that didn’t matter.
[Abman Urikfried has cast Starving Claw.]
Those arrows dealt continuous damage. The more arrows that stuck in that shell, the worse things got for Storm Gush. Next up was Missha.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Strengthen.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Cold Condensation.]
As always, Missha buffed up Cold Condensation to raise her Cold Sensitivity stats, which determined Ice damage. She even unleashed her Soul Beast Skadia’s active ability and power.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Absolute Zero.]
After receiving the reward from the palace, she’d drank dozens of bottles of Beast Blood and acquired this second ability.
[Missha Karlstein’s first blow causes the status condition Frozen, without fail.]
White frost formed on the sword that Missha was swinging at the monster. Her target was his right arm—the one holding the trident.
Rippp.
His forearm was frozen solid. Of course, because of his high Mana Resistance and large body, what was Frozen was only his arm, but all of this was just foreplay anyway.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Ice Crush.]
This active skill increased damage to any enemies who were Frozen. From there, she threw in the rank-five skill she had obtained as a reward from the palace.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Mutation. Her Agility stats are temporarily converted to Strength.]
This was a skill that Missha, who lacked Strength stats, could benefit from throughout the second half.
Bang!
Dual-wielder Missha’s second blade struck the monster’s arm, but it seemed all that it froze was the outer shell.
Rippp.
It cracked, raining down icy fragments, but the monster’s thick arm was still intact. Yeah, even if she gave it her all, it would be weirder if she could cut a rank-three monster’s arm off.
“I’m next!” Right when the monster started going after Missha in a rage, Ainar rushed forward and brought her sword down on the wrist with the broken shell.
Khak!
But even with her Cutting Force at its peak thanks to Wildness Control, it was not enough. Although the blade dug deep into its flesh, it soon got caught on bone.
“Koooooo!”
“A-Ainar!”
The monster twisted its body in an effort to protect its arm and swatted Ainar away with its tail.
God damn it.
Even Ainar had a hard time getting up after that. That was the scary thing about rank-three monsters. Even without actively using a skill, each blow from them was potentially lethal.
[Storm Gush has cast Eye of the Storm.]
Damn it, you’re using that again?
Dash.
As I sprinted forward, my comrades backed away. From there, I held my ground even if it meant death.
“Behelaaah!”
The exceptionally long five seconds passed and the tornado dissipated.
“Mister, step back!”
Ah, you’re ready now.
I quickly stepped aside so as not to get in Erwen’s way. And at that moment...
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]

The rank-four essence Erwen had obtained as a royal reward had a skill that consumed MP exponentially in proportion to casting time—basically, the longer you charged it, the more MP it burned, and the more damage it dealt. It looked as if she’d put all her MP into this one attack. The intensity of the cluster of light that formed around the arrowhead was incredible.
Whip!
Just then, Erwen let go of the string and the arrow shot forward in a flash.
Kabooom!
The point of impact was the monster’s upper abdomen. It seemed she was aiming right where the heart would be, since the head, while also a vital, was difficult to hit.
“Kwohhh!”

The Storm Gush roared in agony, but he could still move normally. Unfortunately, it seemed the arrow didn’t manage to pierce his heart. Still, I wasn’t too upset or anything. Even if she did hit it, it probably wouldn’t have killed him in one blow. Rank-three monsters didn’t immediately die from getting stabbed in the heart.
“Huh?”
Then, for the first time, the Storm Gush made a new move.
[Storm Gush has cast Storm Call.]
It was a skill it only used when its HP was at 40 percent.

chapters.title: Chapter 280: Vortex (6)
paragraphs: The monster raised its spear high into the sky. As soon as I saw that, the following thought came to mind first:
Wait, already?
No matter how many dents in its shell we’d made on the way here, and despite the arm we’d half cut off and stomach we’d pierced with an arrow, it was already at 40 percent HP?
When I raised my head to confirm it, everything suddenly made sense. I didn’t know when she’d gotten there, but Amelia was hanging from the monster’s back, burying a dagger in its neck.
Should’ve hit the back of the head, not the neck.

I allowed myself to be disappointed for a moment, but I didn’t think someone like Amelia would have aimed for the neck on purpose. It probably ended up there because the monster moved to avoid the attack. I focused on something else.
I’ve never seen this skill before.
A black aura was radiating from the hole in its neck.
Oh, wait, is it that one?
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Power of the Abyss.]

As if the Doppelganger’s essence wasn’t enough. To think she had something like this too. It was almost a miracle that I hadn’t died screwing around with her until now. Anyway, I could worry about that later.
“Don’t stop!”

I called out orders as I approached the monster again, but was this too harsh of a demand to make of comrades who didn’t know what was going on? Everyone froze, unable to concentrate on the battle. It wasn’t that I couldn’t understand where they were coming from.
[Storm Gush has cast Storm Call.]

In truth, all Storm Call did was suck in the wind in the surrounding area to recoup MP, but in a situation where the area was full of rainwater due to Rainmaking Ritual, this combo could also recover a large amount of HP. Usually, that would be it... but on this goddamned island, the skill came with an additional side effect.
“Th-the water is as high as a wall!”
“It’s a tsunami!”
Guided by the tugging wind, the rising water rushed in like a tidal wave.
Shaaaaaa!
Like a rolling snowball gradually increasing in size, waves rushed in from all directions and formed a wall of water.
“N-No!”
This show of violence from nature was the type that made you close your eyes on instinct. There was no need to worry about it, though.
Shaaaaaa!
Finally, the waves rushing at us from all sides swallowed us whole, but there was no damage.
[A sanctuary has appeared on the island.]
“H-Huh?”
“H-How on earth did this...?”
I didn’t know exactly how it worked, either. In the game, I’d always figured this was just a part where they’d put a lot of effort into the direction.
“Raven, light up our surroundings!”

The seawater soon covered us, turning the surrounding area dark, so we secured a light source first. When we did, we could more clearly see the environment we were now in. It was a very strange feeling, almost like we were trapped inside a reverse fishbowl. We were still in danger, though, so the sightseeing ended there.

“Everyone, move! This is our only chance!” When I gave orders again, my stupefied comrades quickly returned to their senses and got moving. The battle, which had entered a new phase, proceeded with unparalleled urgency.
[Storm Gush has cast Ley Line.]

First, Mr. Bear, unable to avoid it, was hit by the Vortex that rose from the ground. Still, it seemed he’d managed to dodge to some extent because he thankfully escaped its clutches and avoided getting thrown out of the sanctuary.
“Mr. Urikfried...!”
“P-Priestess. I-I can take this... help Yandel...” Mr. Bear was rendered incapable of combat. Since he had Starving Claw active, the wound would heal over time, but it would take a few more minutes.
“Whoom?!” When Mr. Bear got injured, Iradun the Iron Bear, who was barely managing to hold his own on the front line, was unsummoned.
Our bad luck did not end there. The Vortex that sprang from the hole where Ley Line had been cast began fanning out in what limited space we had, hampering us.
“Don’t get hit by that thing!”
From this point on, it would be best to treat Vortex as an instant kill. The moment we got caught up in that thing, we would be thrown into the sea enveloping our sanctuary.
Slice!
Soon after, Amelia cut off the monster’s dangling arm with an aura-imbued dagger.
Boom.
The bulky arm fell to the floor with the trident made of bone still in hand. But even without a weapon, the monster was a threat.

“Kwohhh!” Storm Gush swung its left arm in a counterattack and ripped open Patzran’s stomach, flinging him away. Because of the Vortex restricting our movement, he wasn’t able to dodge as quickly as usual.
It’s not a fatal wound.

One man was down, but I calmly assessed the situation and shifted my gaze. One of the few advantages of this world was that it was possible to recover with a potion or heal as long as you were still alive.
Dash.

Vortex sliced through our formation and came right at me so I had no choice but to retreat. Just then, Amelia’s team archer, Nebarce, was hit. Using a skill to try and avoid the Vortex flying at him from behind, he ended up reappearing right in front of the monster’s mouth.
Oh, right. He has that random Blink ability...
In the end, Nebarce couldn’t even blurt out his final words before getting chewed up by the monster.
Crunch, crunch.
It was the battle’s first casualty. Apart from taking a second to grieve, I felt no particular guilt. Who told him to use a shit skill like Emergency Escape here?
Anyway, as long as my team is fine...
“...Ugh!” Just then, Missha got hit.
Slice!
Although she dodged to the side to avoid a slam, she lost an arm in return.
“Missha!”
“D-Don’t worry! I can fight with one arrrm!”

Fight with one arm? This girl had gotten very tough since she started following me around. I didn’t have the luxury of telling her to stay back, so I just put a little more viciousness into my next attack to avenge her.
[You have cast Swing.]
I used all of my saved-up MP and swung my mace. The target was that protruding snout.
Smack!
This guy seemed to hold a grudge because he immediately twisted his body and came after me.
Bang!

Even though I blocked it with a shield, the shock penetrated my bones. Was it because of the sharp increase in Physique stats it had gotten from Rainmaking Ritual? When I’d blocked the same attack earlier, it hadn’t been this bad.
God damn it.
Forget dislocation—my arm was bent with the shield still in hand. Since I had kept my arm tight against my body to put more weight behind it, even my ribs tingled. But a heal came in soon after.
[Lairin Ersina has cast Healing.]

A warm yet mysterious power reconnected my severed tendons and pieced my fragmented bones back together like a puzzle. This mysterious power seemed to say that now that I was healed, I should go fight for my comrades.
“Behel—aaah!”
A fight that could not be explained with words like “arduous” promptly ensued. The monster was as strong as you’d expect a rank-three monster to be, and tough.
Stab.

While its flesh was being stabbed repeatedly by an aura user, dozens of arrows were lodged in its shell, draining away its Vitality. Curse spells were being piled on it, causing dark green bodily fluids to drip out of its wounds. But while the dagger Missha stuck in its eye was wobbling, the bastard continued to fight and fight again, as if we were evil incarnate and he was justice itself. He moved tirelessly, and every time he did, someone got hurt. Most of the time it was me.
Scratch.
Sharp claws tore through shields and armor, and sometimes dug into flesh.
Stab!
No heals came in, signaling that the priestess’s divine power had probably run dry. But, so what?
You think I’ll break down before you?
I held out, wielding my mace nonstop and at times sacrificing myself to a Vortex in order to save my comrades. I endured and endured.
“Kwohhh!” A minute later, the monster let out a shriek and stared at me as if to demand why I wasn’t collapsing. So, we were thinking the same thing. High praise for a monster.
Please just move on to the next attack pattern, you bastard!
I struck him in the neck with my mace, that exact sentiment in mind.
Smack!
That made him flinch for a moment but didn’t leave a dent.
Stab.
In the meantime, Amelia lodged a dagger in his temple.
“Kyaaa!” The monster howled in pain and at that moment, a thick curtain of wind enveloped his body almost protectively.
Whooom!
[Storm Gush has cast Priest of the Storm.]
This was the last-ditch survival skill it used when it only had 10 percent HP left. This was the moment I had been waiting for this whole time.
“Raven!” I called the name of our wizard, who had only been casting curse spells from the sidelines this whole time, but the spell was already being cast.
Shaaaaaa!
A vivid magic circle appeared on the ground, radiating light.
Dash.

Not stopping at just dodging to the side, I got as far from the monster as I could. I wasn’t the only one who did; Missha and Amelia, still on the front line, did the same. They knew what was coming next.
“Felz Askar Bier.” Among the military magic Raven had worked hard to learn, this was the only spell specifically designed to kill a single powerful enemy rather than multiple at once.
But despite that, its range is too wide.
I gulped and looked forward.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-4 attack spell Divine Punishment.]
From the seawater-covered ceiling, thunder shook the heavens. A second later, everything turned white.
Flash!
It wasn’t blinding, though. The pure white light, which would have been refracted multiple times before reaching this place, was dim as it filled our vision.
Kablam!
The long-awaited Divine Punishment landed right on top of the bastard’s head.

High Physical and Mana Resistance, Strength, and Agility that rivaled that of an Ogre were the traits that had earned it the nickname Ogre of the Sea, but a Storm Gush’s Vitality stat was very low compared to that of an Ogre. Because of the skills it had under its belt, it was smarter to aim for a short fight. Its attack patterns and combos meant that engaging in a long battle with this guy would gradually put the challengers at a disadvantage. And so, I had also aimed for a short fight, conserving 70 percent of our MP and only dealing regular attacks. The plan was to start cramming in more damage at an increased tempo after Rainmaking Ritual, and critical hits starting at 40 percent when Storm Call was used. Then, at 10 percent, a level-clearing move with bullseye aim.

It was a fairly straightforward strategy, except for the fact that we didn’t have any counter skills to neutralize some of the monster’s attack patterns, which increased the risk. We had consumed almost all of our resources to reach 10 percent HP, and so our wizard had to handle the final blow alone. Yes, it was definitely a plan worth trying. The only question was, how did it turn out?
Kablam!
Before long, Divine Punishment pierced the seawater in the form of a thunderbolt and I was able to see the results with my own two eyes.
It failed.
It was such a miserable failure that we couldn’t even pretend it was a success.
Chhhhhh.

The monster’s shell was now steaming like that of a cooked lobster, but it was still alive and moving. The tornado swirling around it, protecting it, remained unchanged. The reason was clear. It wasn’t that we’d waited too long and the spell had been fired after the monster had activated its invincibility.
The damage just wasn’t enough.
It was just that Raven’s finishing move had been lacking, and by a lot.
I thought that spell would be worth a try.
It might have been my fault for not considering the terrain. Perhaps if it was in a normal environment, that lightning wouldn’t have had to pass through the seawater and lose some of its power.
“I-It’s alive! What do we do?”
What do you mean, what do we do? We have to move on to Plan B now.
“Patzran! Bring out the boat!”
At my cry, Patzran looked up, his abdomen still shredded. “...What boat?”
Hmm, did I not tell him about Plan B? No, I’m sure I did. Did he forget because of all the chaos?
I didn’t really like repeating myself, but I reiterated the key part of Plan B which I had explained earlier. “Let’s bounce!”
If we stayed here, everyone would die.
[The Energy of the Storm has entered Storm Gush’s body. Storm Gush has become temporarily immune to all damage.]

We had to default to Plan B in the end, but there was a lot to feel good about. No one had died. Although the archer from Noark met his doom today and Missha’s arm had been severed, Ainar had passed out, and Mr. Bear had also suffered a serious injury, everyone on my team had survived. That was all that mattered.

“Ah, boat...!” Finally, Patzran seemed to remember what Plan B was as he hurriedly touched his sub-space ring where the boat was stored. But suddenly dubious, he took a moment to question me. “B-But even if we take out the boat now—cough!” He paused to cough up blood.
Raven picked up the slack and finished his question. “Mr. Patzran is right. How can we float a boat when everything is covered in water?”
How do you think?
“Don’t you remember? His boat is made of Arthene wood.”

Arthene wood was the highest-grade material for ships. It was obscenely sturdy and was also buoyant enough to make a life jacket weep. Even if you filled the whole boat with water, it’d still float to the surface on its own.
“What are you doing, Mr. Patzran!? Hurry, get the boat out!”

When Raven pressed him, Patzran cradled his torn stomach and summoned the boat. The boat was large enough to accommodate ten people. I carried the unconscious Ainar and injured Mr. Bear onto the boat and tied them to the pole with rope.
“What are you all doing? Secure yourselves. You could fall off like this.”
“Ah, right!” Those who could take care of themselves attached themselves to the boat with rope.
Just then, Missha, clutching her severed arm with one hand, spoke. Hm, I tied it up securely, so she really didn’t have to hold it so tightly...“Bjorn, I have something to tell you.”
Huh? Tell me?
“Let’s do that later.”
“But—”
“Why? You don’t trust me?”
Missha paused at that and shook her head slightly. “I trrrust you.”
Okay, then we’re prepared to set sail.
Once everyone boarded the boat, Raven turned to me with great confusion. “But how do we get all the way over there?”
Oh, that’s also true.
How could a boat that had been summoned on land set sail? This was a conundrum I hadn’t considered when coming up with the plan.
If I didn’t think of it, it must mean there was no need to. Hmm, yes.
That seemed to be the case, considering the fact that my body started moving automatically as soon as I heard her question.
“W-What are you doing? You’re not thinking of lifting this whole boat...?”
If you already know what I’m doing, keep quiet. You’re making me lose steam.
“Ahhhhhh!”

Releasing a yell that was closer to a shriek, I lifted the boat with both arms. Then I took big strides toward the edge of the water. Since it was difficult even for me to hold this thing up for too long, I offered them final words of advice right before plunging the boat into the sea. “Hold your breath, everyone. Go.”

Being made of highly buoyant wood, the boat began to rise as soon as it entered the water. With Priest of the Storm turned on, they shouldn’t have any issues once it got up there since there wouldn’t be any vortexes like before. In the actual game, escape by boat was not blocked at this stage of the event.
...They’re gone.

Only when the boat was out of sight did I turn around. There stood the one and only comrade—no, should I say fellow soldier?—who had decided to stay behind. Anyway, Amelia was looking at me with open fascination.
“You really cherish your comrades.”
“They are small and precious.”
“...I see.”

Come to think of it, this lady had a habit of answering most statements with “I see.” What was annoying was that no matter how many times I heard her say it, it was still hard to discern what kind of “I see” it was.
So I just decided to say what I wanted to say. “You surprised me too. I didn’t think you would be so willing to play this role.”

Our mission now was to play the part of bait. When this guy finished charging, he would start using an indiscriminate wide-range skill, and this was not the kind that could be blocked with a shield. It had been clear that a frail wizard, priestess, and multiple injured warriors wouldn’t last even a few seconds against it, so we decided to move onto Plan B at this stage: retreat. But unfortunately, not all of us could go. Without someone to stall him, this guy would just chase after us, tail whipping through the water. And we would never be able to defeat the bastard on a boat.

“This role, huh?” Amelia chuckled. “It’s definitely not something I would normally do.” It seemed she could admit even to herself that she was acting strange. Then why did she decide to stay? “But I can’t stand being indebted to anyone.”
Wow, so that was really why. I was genuinely amazed. Showing such loyalty to someone just because they saved her from near death once? Wasn’t this the best type of personality to manipulate?
I should make sure to occasionally make her indebted to me if I get the chance.
“What is that? That look?”
“Oh, you caught me. I was just thinking highly of you for honoring your oaths.”

“...Empty words.” Amelia frowned in displeasure. “Whatever, don’t look at me like that. Your escape method seemed foolproof. If I’d done the math and decided that it wasn’t worth a shot, I would never have stayed.”
“Hmm, I see.”
“Barbarian, what do you mean by ‘I see’?”
“That’s... Ah, I think it’s ending soon.”
When I shifted my gaze, Amelia ended the conversation and looked straight ahead.
The tornado around the monster was gradually fading. That meant the final phase would soon begin.
Squeeze.
I gripped the mace tighter. But it seemed she found that strange for some reason.
“Wait, I’m sure the plan was to hold out until we can escape?” Amelia questioned my combative attitude, which also made me tilt my head.
“...I am planning to hold out?”
“...Then it’d make more sense to put your mace away and carry just the shield.”

Huh? What was this girl saying? What did that have to do with anything? “A mace is a great defense!” I insisted. I always said this, but the best defense was a good offense, especially when you were dealing with a guy who was almost dead anyway. “So, you lift your weapons too! Don’t think about dodging half-heartedly like a bad sport to kill time! You’re living with the life Missha saved, anyway!”
“...I see.”
Letting up was not allowed.

chapters.title: Chapter 281: Adrift (1)
paragraphs: The effects of the skill Priest of the Storm could be divided into three main bullet points.

1. Until the skill was fully charged, the caster was immune to all damage. In some ways, it was a high-value skill. Even if it was impossible for the user to move while charging it, an invincibility skill was still an invincibility skill. In the game, incredible plays were possible if you used it well.

2. Once it was done being cast, the caster acquired a huge boost to their defense stats across the board. When you coupled this with the temporary invincibility it offered, it wasn’t a stretch to call this the highest-quality survival skill in the game. But that wasn’t all.

3. The skill caused wide-ranged damage in a certain area around the caster until Priest of the Storm ended. The greatest defense was a good offense, after all, and the damage it dealt was too high to write it off as a simple survival skill.
“It’s coming soon.”
The moment I raised my shield to right below my eyes and crouched down, the storm wall around the monster gradually expanded and enveloped the entire sanctuary.
This change signaled that the skill was done charging.
Shaaaaaa!

Strong winds whipped around my body. It wasn’t as difficult to see an inch in front of me as it had been when I was inside Eye of the Storm. However, as if blades were hidden in the raging winds, what seemed like shining white daggers struck my armor and body.
[You are taking damage.]
[You are taking damage.]
[You are taking damage.]
[You are taking damage.]
This was the reason why I got my comrades out first. This type of area of effect skill was impossible to block, even with a shield.
Kakak, kakak, kak! Bang!

Arms, back, shoulders, waist, thighs, calves—to the extent that it was basically impossible to identify which part was getting hit at any given point, simultaneous blows struck me all over my body. It was as if dozens of people were throwing snowballs filled with rocks at me from all sides and without stopping.
Hmm, yeah, that sounds about right.

To be fair, considering my Physical and Mana Resistance, it wasn’t like I was at a risk of a one-hit KO; this kind of continuous small damage barely left a mark on me. But what about Amelia? Her Physical Resistance wasn’t as high as mine.
What the hell is this girl?
Surprisingly, she was avoiding every single hit.
Wow, how high does your Agility stat have to be to get you eyes and reflexes like that? I asked her to come because she said she could do it, and I guess she really can.
Oh, I wasn’t jealous, of course. Why would I be?
“You look busy.”
Amelia didn’t answer me. Was she trying to tell me to focus up rather than chitchat with her?
“Kwohhh!”

Just then, the one-armed shelled monster roared more menacingly than ever and charged at me. This was a side effect of my Threat Level. If I were a human using Wild Outburst, it would have still tried to kill Amelia first.
Kwaaang!
The moment I took the bastard’s ridiculously large body with my shield, I got shoved backward. But a big move like that was bound to leave an opening.
Stab!
Amelia thrust a dagger into its back. Because of the jump in its Defense stats, it didn’t sink in as deeply as before.
It doesn’t even flinch now.
Even after being stabbed, the bastard swung its front foot at me without hesitation.
Voom!

This was the tricky thing about Priest of the Storm. As if to prove my assertion that the greatest defense was a good offense, the fact that its Defense stats went up essentially translated into an increase in its attack power. It could now focus the time it would have spent on defense solely on attacking.
Dash.

I promptly dodged to the side and widened the distance between us. A little while ago, it would have used Ley Line or Eye of the Storm next. Now, there was no need to worry about those follow-up attacks. Since this world was a heartless place where you had to give something up in order to gain something else, Priest of the Storm had a penalty too.
“Kwohhh!”
Sure, scream. You can’t use your skills right now, anyway.

The use of other skills was not permitted. A Storm Gush that reached this phase had to fight while relying only on hand-to-hand combat and that wide-range attack. In the game, this lasted for ten minutes.
If we can’t kill him in that time, let’s run away without looking back.

As soon as it could use its other skills again, the raid would be a failure. Not only would it start throwing all kinds of crap at us again, but its injuries would slowly start to heal once Priest of the Storm ended. And with Amelia as our sole damage dealer, it would be able to recover faster than we could damage it.
[You have cast Swing.]
Not caring about preserving my remaining MP, I used my skills like there was no tomorrow, figuring that regular hits wouldn’t even be able to distract him.
“Amelia!”
Whether we could take this guy down or not depended on how well our main damager performed.
“...Tsk.” At my shout, Amelia clicked her tongue and swung her dagger again. From the look on her face, it was very clear she just wanted to stall.
Tsk, you people with nothing to lose.
I couldn’t understand it at all. Like it or not, we had to fight this guy for ten minutes either way. Why just hold out?
If we can kill him, it’ll be a jackpot and—Oh, right. She wouldn’t get anything out of an essence drop.

It made sense that Amelia wasn’t showing any enthusiasm for my plan. Her essence slots were all filled, anyway. But since the wizard had already escaped, the essence couldn’t be stored in a test tube. And even if it could, it’d be difficult to split the loot once it was sold since she was from Noark. She probably hoped never to see us again after today.
With that in mind, I decided to give her some different motivation. “If we kill him, I won’t claim ownership of Belverson’s equipment!”
But, what was this?
“...You were thinking of claiming ownership?” Amelia asked innocently.
Then did you plan to take it all for yourself? When all you did was show up at the end and take the last shot?
“...You guys get Carmilla and I get Belverson. We already decided on this.”
Hmm, I did hear that was how the agreement went down, but I hadn’t been the one to make it.
“I didn’t hear anything like that!” I shouted while dodging Storm Gush’s claws.
“...I see,” Amelia quietly muttered.

Somehow, I felt like I knew what she meant by that this time. She must have seen the stubborn, barbarian-style logic that she’d be forced to contend with in the near future. Thanks to that, a little enthusiasm appeared in her eyes. As her employer, that was exactly what I wanted to see.
Boom!

With that, a more active battle ensued. Although we were already getting ahead of ourselves with talk of loot, the possibility was in actuality fifty-fifty: either we defeated the monster in time, or failed and dealt with the challenge of escaping and all its related losses. It was hard to judge which way this would go yet. We could only hope for the former as we worked our butts off.
“Behel—ahhh!”

Sweat and drops of blood ran down my skin. Still, there was no time to rest. The more I bugged this bastard, the more helpful it would be to Amelia, who was dealing damage on a razor-thin tightrope as it was.
Stab!
The monster’s claw landed on my shoulder.
Click.
Losing its seam, my breastplate split open and fell to the ground.
Damn repair costs.
My hands shook, but I decided to think positively. That armor was already as destroyed as it could get. Even if I avoided that last hit, it wouldn’t have made a big difference.
“Amelia!”
The Storm Gush ignored me and swung its tail at Amelia.
Dash.
Fortunately, she avoided it by hurriedly jumping up.
Stab!

A dagger hidden in the storm plunged into her body. This wasn’t a surprise. At first, she had managed to avoid each one, but as the battle dragged on, small and large injuries started accumulating on her body.
“Ugh.”

The location for this particular wound wasn’t great—none other than the thigh. It seemed to have touched a vein because an unbelievable amount of blood gushed from her sliced leg. However, the real problem lay elsewhere.
Dash.
It was the fact that Amelia’s mobility had been hampered.
God damn it.
As I feared, Amelia couldn’t attack as actively after the injury and this resulted in a drop in DPS.
We won’t be able to finish him at this rate.
My mind was all jumbled up. Should I change our strategy now? Should we just hold out and then bounce? Then what about my repair costs? Who was going to compensate us for our struggles?
...Let’s stay a little longer.
I quickly wrapped up my internal debate and made a decision. While our state had taken a turn for the worse, this bastard was clearly cornered too. His HP should have been nearing rock bottom.
“Human.” That was when it spoke for the first time, its eyes full of hate. “Human!”
My body stiffened at its strange, sudden intensity.
That line... wait, was this monster always able to speak?
I had no memory of that, no matter how hard I racked my brain. Then was this a change that came with the reality patch? Anyway, I could think about that later. That wasn’t important right now.
[You have deactivated Giantization.]
[You have cast Giantization.]
I quickly switched to Giantization (Normal) Mode. That was because I couldn’t use Transcendence during Giantization (Transcendence) Mode.
[You have cast Transcendence. The next skill you use will be strengthened.]

It was really just the slightest difference. And in order to compensate for this difference, what we needed now was not a tank but a damage dealer. Of course, I didn’t have a great number of skills. So which one of them should I use?

Not Leap; maybe if I were facing a lanky long-range type it would have come in handy, but an ability that made me faster wouldn’t let me whittle down even 1 percent of this guy’s HP. The same went for Swing. Turning on Transcendence only increased the range, not the damage itself. That was useless. However, there was an essence that I’d never included in any of my cultivation plans that I had consumed by chance, and which funnily enough had helped me countless times on my journey so far.
[You have cast Flesh Burst.]
Yeah, maybe this one.
[By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
After activating the skill, I jumped forward. The skill wasn’t instant anymore and now had a three-second delay, but in return, the damage it could cause had increased greatly.
Hmm, it was about thirty-five times, I think?

I’d only calculated it once or twice while studying Transcendence but my memory should have been accurate. There hadn’t been many other skills in the game that increased damage to this extent. Of course, the pure damage Flesh Burst itself dealt was low. This skill was just used to spray acid—it didn’t have much explosive power. Even multiplied by thirty-five, it would be hard for this ability to take off even 3 percent of a rank-three monster’s HP. Well, I would be satisfied with that for now.
Dash.
I dashed forward once more and clung on to its neck with both arms: Barbarian Trojan Horse Mode.
“Human!” The monster roared as it struggled to buck me off of it. Oh, to think it would willingly open its mouth for me.
Slide.
I dropped my mace and shoved my hand into its snout.
Chomp!
The bastard immediately bit my hand with its thick teeth as if to punish me for doing something so irrational, but it was wrong about one thing.
I’m a barbarian, not a human. Anyway, time’s up.
When I finished counting down in my head, an explosion erupted from the hand in its mouth, although there were none of the sparks that would have accompanied a classic explosion.
Kabooom!
Yeah, if this wasn’t an explosion, then what was? The moment the blast occurred, I was thrown back into the air. That was how strong the force was.
Boom!
My heavy body immediately plummeted to the floor, and I hurriedly raised my head and stared at the spot the bastard used to be. I realized it when I saw the wind had died down.
Shaaaaaa!
The Storm Gush’s body was disappearing into a cloud of light.
[You have killed a Storm Gush. EXP +7」
So, I’d gotten him.
[Achievement Unlocked
Condition: First rank-3 monster kill.
Reward: Permanently increases your Spirit stat by +1.]

Was it because I’d lived as a barbarian for so long? A sense of satisfaction filled me just from the fact that I had been victorious in battle. But unfortunately, that satisfaction did not last long. An indescribable pain soon took over my entire body. The cause was clear.
[All Defense stats have been temporarily nullified.]
Ha, I didn’t even consider the fact that Pain Resistance would go away after a Transcended Flesh Burst.
Oh, fu—
I hadn’t experienced pain like this in so long that I couldn’t even scream.
“Barbarian, are you okay?” Amelia’s face entered my blurry vision. She then said something strange. “You’re lucky.”
I didn’t think she said that simply because we’d survived because we’d succeeded in defeating that monster.
Oh, could it be...?
“Essence...?”
“Yes, it appeared.”
What, really?
I raised my head a bit more and looked above me. Then, I saw an ultramarine-colored essence floating in the air. I probably didn’t see it earlier because my eyes weren’t focusing right.
Hallelujah.
I immediately crawled toward the essence on my stomach. The pain tearing through me? What about it? Humans were creatures that could be blinded by greed regardless of circumstance.
“...Shouldn’t you treat yourself first?”
Treatment could come afterward. Besides, it wasn’t like this was the first time my arm had ever been pulverized.
“Ehhhssence...”
“Strange guy.”
I pretended not to hear Amelia and crawled toward the essence like a possessed man.

[The Essence of the Storm Gush is being absorbed into your soul. Strength has increased by +90. Agility has increased by +55. Physical Resistance has increased by +75. Natural Regeneration has increased by +50. Lung Capacity has increased by +40. Lightning Resistance has decreased by -30.]
Strength filled me up from the inside out. While I was savoring that pleasant fullness, Amelia opened her sub-space bracelet.
“Anyway, take a potion now.”
That was the moment.
Shaaaaaa!

A brilliant light began to leak from the sub-space’s opening. This seemed strange even to someone unfamiliar with magic, like me. A sub-space item didn’t light up just because you put something inside or took something out.
Then... what is it?
It seemed Amelia was just as confused because she hurriedly put her hand inside and rummaged around. Then she pulled out an item.
“Why is this...?”
It was a stone that was emitting pure white light.

chapters.title: Chapter 282: Adrift (2)
paragraphs: I suddenly had a thought. That stone that was in Amelia’s hand right now—perhaps it was the lord of Noark’s treasure. Of course, that was only baseless conjecture for now.
“...What is that stone?” I asked bluntly, like the barbarian I was.
Amelia’s answer was stone cold. “Don’t worry about it.”
Jeez, then don’t make me curious. Judging by that reaction, I think it is that treasure...

Even if I asked more questions here, I doubted she’d answer any of them. So I shrugged off my interest in the stone and shifted my focus. Right now, there was something that took precedence over idle curiosity.
Pshoot!
Almost like glass in an aquarium, a crack formed in the barrier that was preventing the water from entering, and it soon sprung a leak.
[The sanctuary will soon disappear.]
That meant we had to start preparing. I first picked my mace and the broken pieces of my breastplate up off the ground and put them in sub-space. Additionally, I pulled out a rope.
“What are you doing? Come here. Unless you want to be swept away by the water.”
Realizing what I was planning, Amelia frowned. “Aren’t you going to use the scroll?”
“Oh, are you talking about the Multi Teleportation scroll?”

This scroll was the key to Plan B, an item I’d asked Kyle to make for me after the events with the Lord of Abyss Berzak left their mark on me. However, the maximum number of people the scroll could transport was two. It was also impossible to designate coordinates, and could only teleport the user to the coordinate transmitter registered at the time of its making.
If its performance hadn’t been stripped down in those ways, it would have been impossible to put the spell into a scroll like this.

For reference, Raven had the coordinate transmitter. Normally she carried it in her sub-space, but since I gave her a heads-up in advance, she would have taken it out. In other words, I could get to my clanmates just by tearing this scroll.
“The monster is defeated and we’re not in danger. Why use that expensive item?”

Using this thing just to make things a little easier was absurd. Kyle said he could make a scroll like this for me again anytime as long as I provided the materials, but when would I get those materials again? Aside from being expensive, most were rare items that were difficult to acquire.
“So, sit already. Once the water recedes, our comrades will come save us anyway.”
“What do we do until then?”
Why are you asking such an obvious question? We have to hold our breaths. It’ll only take a few minutes. You can’t handle that?
“...Never mind, I’ll tie myself.” Amelia pulled a stake out from sub-space and drove it into the ground. Then she took the rope from me and connected it to her own body.
“Oh, if you’re done, come help me. I only have one hand.”
“...How pathetic.”
I know you’re going to help me anyway.
When I raised my free hand, Amelia tied a rope around my torso to secure me in place. That wrapped up our preparations.
Pshoot!
As we watched the water pour through the holes in the sanctuary, we chatted for a while. Surprisingly, it was Amelia who started the conversation. “I guess your pain is gone now.”
Oh, I was just starting to forget about that.
“...Ugh.” A hallmark of pain was that it got worse the more attention you paid it, so I quickly changed the subject. “Enough talking about me. Can’t you tell me now?”
“Huh?”
“That stone. What is it used for? It looks like that was the treasure those bastards were after, no?”
“Barbarian, I told you not to worry about that,” Amelia said, her voice cold as she put her foot down.

But one thing about barbarians was that we weren’t able to tolerate curiosity. “I can’t not worry about it when it keeps glowing like that next to me! I’m not asking for much, so just tell me why it’s glowing, at least. You seemed startled earlier too.”
“That’s...” At that question, Amelia trailed off and squeezed the stone in her hand. “I don’t know why.”
“Huh? You don’t know?”

When I stared at her in obvious bewilderment, Amelia clicked her tongue and glared at me stubbornly. “Yeah, I don’t know. Is there something wrong with that? There’s not a lot I know about this item in the first place. Just that with this...”
With that?
My ears perked up, and I was careful not to interrupt her.
[The sanctuary has disappeared.]
But a moment later, the barrier keeping the seawater out shattered, and water began to rush into the space like something out of a disaster movie. It just had to be now.
I could have learned more about it if I had more time.
It was a pity, but what could I do? I’d have to ask her more questions later when I got the chance.
“Hold your breath! And hold the rope tight!” The moment after I shouted at her and took a deep breath, cold seawater swept over us.
Shaaaaaa!
From now on, it was sit-tight time. If we just held our breaths and waited, the water would drain on its own. Then our comrades on the boat would come back and find us.
Ten minutes will be easy.

Was it because of the Lung Capacity stats that came with Storm Gush’s essence? Even though I was holding my breath, I didn’t feel much discomfort. It was a stat that wasn’t all that useful in the game. Which made sense, because if there was a need to have an underwater battle, all preparations were made in advance. There was no need to know how to hold your breath longer or anything like that.
But this might surprisingly be a good thing...?

Unlike the game, this was a world where you had to fight with your body as your weapon. Lung Capacity stats would be useful in battle. I was no longer Hansu Lee fiddling with his keyboard. I knew how important breathing was in real combat.
I think my body is slowly getting better too.

The distinct tickling sensation that coincided with an injury healing started to spread all over my body. The water here was salty, so it wasn’t like it carried the properties of a potion or anything. It was just the effect of my newly acquired skill.
[The energy of the sea fills your body. Due to the passive skill Origin, Natural Regeneration has significantly increased.]

The effect of Storm Gush’s passive skill, Origin, was simple. My healing factor rose whenever I came into contact with seawater, and the longer I was exposed, the more the rate of said increase compounded like interest. From what I could remember, it took about ten minutes for a severed arm to sprout again.
It’s useless outside of the sixth floor, though.

I once tried to store some seawater in an empty bottle and use it like a potion, but the experiment was a massive failure. Even after an hour, the water lost whatever potency it had and the skill wouldn’t work.
Just what’s so great about the energy of the sea? Anyway, I finally got my regeneration back.

A smile spread across my face. The most disappointing thing about losing the Vampire’s essence had now been rectified. Plus, this was a whopping rank-three essence, and not one solely focused on regeneration, either. Origin had other effects too.
I can replace this one later when I start farming for a rank-two essence...
Unable to hide my delight, I watched my body recover in real-time.
Hmm?
I belatedly realized that the torch we were using while killing the Storm Gush had been put out when the water rushed in, and everything in front of me was blurry from being underwater.
So why can I see in front of me at all?

Once again, the cause was Amelia’s mysterious stone. Even in sub-space, the thing was radiating a brilliant light and serving as a torch. As soon as I noticed, I started to wonder. Aside from the question of how light could leak out of a sub-space, which was by definition its own pocket dimension, somehow the light seemed like it had gotten stronger.
I cocked my head and pointed at Amelia’s sub-space bracelet. The gesture conveyed the following question: Hey, is that thing okay?

At my question, Amelia smacked me in the chest with her fist. Mind your own business. I figured that was what that meant. But it seemed she also found the growing intensity of the light peculiar, because she opened her bracelet and took out the stone. You couldn’t even compare its brightness now to its brightness while in sub-space. This was clearly not normal...
Poke, poke.
Feeling anxious for some reason, I hurriedly poked Amelia’s side with my finger. But is this really okay, though?
The meaning behind my gesture should have been obvious, but Amelia did not answer. As if it wasn’t blinding at all, she just stared blankly at the stone like a woman possessed.
Dang, this is making me anxious...
The moment I instinctively sensed something was wrong, the stone released a burst of light almost like an explosion and dyed everything around us white.
Flash!
That was where my memory ended, much like the day I was first dragged into this world.
Ack, my eyes!
With that, I blacked out.
[An error has occurred.]
[Character location cannot be logged.]
[Character transmission log has been temporarily suspended.]
[Administrator must promptly...]
When I opened my eyes, there was light beyond them—a red glow as the sun set over the horizon.
“Shit!” Realizing what time it was, I hurriedly sat up. “It’s been a whole day?”
The battle with the Storm Gush had taken place at night, but the sun was setting. That meant I’d been unconscious for at least a day.
Uh, what’s this now?
Soon, I was confronted with a problem much more serious than losing a day.
Where the fuck did all my equipment go?

Noticing the void a beat later, I saw I had no equipment. Actually, not just equipment—I had nothing. My sub-space ring, earrings, acid-immunity-enchanted magic panties—all of it was gone. I was in a completely, primordially naked state.

Did someone see me unconscious and loot everything? Hmm, but don’t they usually kill the unconscious person before they do that? Wait, there was no one else on the island besides us in the first place. What have the others on the boat been doing this whole time, then? Ugh, just what is going on?
“I’m going to lose it.”
“Jumbled” was not a strong enough word to describe my mental state right now. This situation couldn’t be explained with common sense alone.
“Hey.” I shook Amelia, who was lying next to me. Of course, I kept my eyes directed elsewhere. Like me, all her equipment had been stolen too. “...Amelia, wake up.”
Hmm? Please, wake up. That stone was yours. How did this happen?
“Ha...” I desperately tried to wake Amelia, hoping for an answer, but she didn’t stir. Judging by her breathing, she wasn’t dead.
Damn it.
I gave up trying to wake her for now and took in our surroundings. They were full of contradictions from the moment I opened my eyes, but there were things I hadn’t noticed yet.
Arm.
Okay, my arm was now intact because it had been regenerated thanks to the seawater.
Stakes and rope.

The stakes and ropes we had fastened to the ground to keep us from being swept away by the water were gone. It wasn’t like we had been transported to another island or anything. This was the same spot where we fought the Storm Gush earlier.
The ground is already dry.

The entire island had been submerged in seawater, but the grains of sand under my feet right now were crumbly. Was this physically possible in one day? I didn’t know, but the important thing was, if the ground had been naturally dried by the sun, why were Amelia and I still wet?
Buzzz!
Just then, I heard the distinct sound of insect wings in the distance.
Oh, yeah?
The rank-eight insect-type monster Krungby was the main creature native to Farune Island.
Why the fuck are you coming out now?
Baffled didn’t cut it. The event had ended a day ago but these guys were already spawning? Monsters that would usually only be regenerated the next time the labyrinth opened?
Anyway, let’s deal with the rest later.
I hurriedly got up. Then I picked up a suitable tree that was on the ground nearby. The grip couldn’t compare to a mace, but it was enough for a rank-eight monster.
It’ll work fine as a one-time weapon.
Dash.
Kicking off the ground, I charged at the insect monster emerging from the bush.
Swing.
I started angrily whipping at it.
Smack!
There was of course no system message or anything, but the sensation in my hand was the same as usual, which was relieving.
Well, at least my essences are fine.

chapters.title: Chapter 283: Adrift (3)
paragraphs: Thud.

As the insect-type monster Kronby disappeared in a burst of light, it dropped a mana stone. I didn’t bother picking it up, though. What would I do with it when I didn’t even have a pocket to store it in?
I’m going to lose it.
In a way, this was even worse than when I first fell into the labyrinth and had to crawl on three limbs. At least back then I had underwear.
Let’s think about what’s going on later and find something to cover up first.

Momentarily overwhelmed by the strange situation I’d found myself in, I quickly compiled a to-do list and resolved each item one by one. First, clothing, one of the necessities of life. Although this was an island that only had trees as far as the eye could see and where monsters disappeared as light the moment they were killed, it wasn’t difficult to fulfill this requirement. To start, I was a barbarian anyway.
“...I really get to try everything here, huh?”

First, I picked up a vine that looked like it would fit. Then, securing some pumpkin-sized leaves on the vine, I wrapped it around my waist and, ta-da. With this, the piece of equipment I decided to call Protection of the Tree Spirit was completed.
...This is more durable than I thought it’d be.
As I put on the item I created and moved around, I was surprised by the high quality. I guessed the basics weren’t basics for nothing. There was a reason the first humans preferred this look.
I should make her one too.

While I was at it, I made Amelia one as well. Rather than just bottoms, which was enough for me, Amelia’s required two parts. But because she was much smaller than me, it didn’t take much more time to craft both.
Since it’s roomy, the size shouldn’t be a problem.
This was one of the few advantages of Protection of the Tree Spirit. Because it was so primitive, it wasn’t a problem if it was a little too big. All you had to do was tie the stems tighter.
How long is she going to sleep?

I went up to Amelia and tossed the Protection of the Tree Spirit (F) on top of her body. It was not like I hadn’t considered putting it on her, but it’d just make things even more awkward. No matter how I looked at it, putting it on for her would be crossing the line. There was a reason they said that a boy and girl shouldn’t sit together after the age of seven.
Anyway, since I’m not hungry right now, I should make a place to rest.

After fulfilling our clothing requirements, I immediately began preparations for our shelter requirements. This, too, wasn’t all that difficult. After digging a pit the size of a hovel, all I had to do was stuff it with the same kind of leaves I’d used to make Protection of the Tree Spirit. I also picked up dry wood and made a bonfire in the center. Surprisingly, lighting the fire was easy.
Is it because my body is overflowing with strength?
When I rubbed some pieces of wood together without pause, it soon began to smoke. There were surprisingly few things in the world that could not be done by force.
Anyway, when does this girl plan to wake up?

After lifting Amelia up and placing her on the bed of leaves, I looked up at the sky. It was already night, but it didn’t feel cold thanks to the fire. With a light source secured, I should be able to fight any monsters that came our way without issue. At this point, I moved on to the next item on the agenda.
The problem is food...
That was the third necessity of life and, in terms of survival, the one that always came first.
“Ha, honestly...”
The sighs came freely. It wasn’t like this was my first time in the labyrinth. I didn’t think I would have to worry about this again.
Growl.
...Where do I get food from?

There were no mountains on Farune Island. With the exception of the coast, everything was a flat forest, which meant there were many natural walls preventing the light of the bonfire from spreading too far.
These moth-like bastards.

However, the light of the bonfire was still enough to attract nearby monsters. Thanks to that, I had to deal with monsters all night long. Well, I still didn’t put out the bonfire, though. Monsters appeared even without light, after all. I determined that it was smarter to fight with my sense of sight secured than without it.
It’s not like I’m going to sleep in this situation anyway.
I spent a few more hours fighting back hunger before Amelia finally came to her senses.
“You’re finally awake.”
“...How did you know?”
“Your breathing got quiet.”
This girl was a weird one. It was obvious that she’d woken up but she kept her eyes closed without saying anything. I guessed she wanted to take stock of the situation first? “...Where are we?”
“Wait, put that on before you get up.”
Raising herself up on her elbows, Amelia frowned at the leaves laid on top of her bare body. “Barbarian... did you undress me?”

This was one of the questions I’d expected Amelia to ask me when she woke up, so I was able to answer without missing a beat and without panicking. “Can you really say that after seeing the state I’m in? My clothes were completely gone too.”
“...I see.” After I turned around, I heard the sound of leaves rustling behind me. Fortunately, I didn’t need to explain to her how to put it on. “It’s on. You can turn around now.”

When I turned back around, Amelia was wearing all the pieces of Protection of the Tree Spirit (F) I had made. It was a very strange feeling. Now that both of us were wearing something like this, it felt like some sort of costume. I wondered if we’d receive a Costume Effect buff if we fought together.
“So, what is this place?” Amelia didn’t seem embarrassed about her clothes at all as she repeated her earlier question with a straight face.
Well, I should have been the one asking that. “This is Farune Island. I don’t know how much time has passed, and when I opened my eyes, we were completely naked.”
When I gave her a brief summary of the various questions I’d had the moment I opened my eyes, Amelia fell silent. It seemed she needed time to get her thoughts in order.
After giving her about a minute, I asked, “Now then. Tell me why we are in this situation.”
“...Why are you asking me?”
What, pretending not to know?
“The stone you were holding flared back then. I’m certain that has something to do with this.”
“Yeah, that...” Amelia reached into the air, but the object that had been gone since I opened my eyes did not suddenly appear again.
Oh, right. I should make this clear too. “Just saying this in case, but I didn’t touch that thing. I don’t know where it disappeared to.”
“Don’t worry. I don’t doubt you.”
Hmm, so I had that much credibility? “So, your answer to my question?”
“...I have a guess, but it’s not confirmed.”
Tell me what you’re thinking, woman. Do you really have to restrict information even in a situation like this?
“Just speak freely. What is that stone and why are we in this situation?” I asked, not bothering to hide my irritation.
“That’s...” Amelia trailed off.

The moment she finally parted her lips again, her expression determined, we heard the snap of a nearby branch. We simultaneously lowered our stances and turned in the direction of the sound. That was because there were only insectoid monsters on this island. In other words, it was highly likely that sound had been made by a person.
Except for the crackling of the bonfire, there was a suffocating silence. Because of that, I grew more uneasy. If there were another sound, I might have just assumed it was a random passer-by.
“How long are you going to spy on us? Come out,” Amelia said into the dark woods, her voice low.
We got a response about five seconds later. “Haha, you make us sound like bad guys.”
Five adventurers straightened up from where they were crouching and made their way through the bushes.
What the hell, they were really watching us? Since when? God damn it.

I felt wrong-footed, but I immediately scanned the group in front of us. They were all human and male. Their equipment level seemed about fifth floor, but there was a clan emblem on their chests. It was an emblem I’d never seen before.
Did they come to the sixth floor with a clan and split off as teams on this island?

Even that explanation seemed a bit iffy, though. Considering recent events, very few adventurers had entered the labyrinth this month. Plus, their presence would have meant that the occupancy requirement of twenty people on this island had been hit. But we were only running into these guys now? Something was fishy here.
As I was thinking that, Amelia openly expressed her wariness, which signaled the start of the conversation. “Why were you spying on us?”

“Don’t jump to the wrong conclusion. We spotted a fire in the distance and thought it was our clanmates. When we came to say hello, we saw the state you two were in and just observed you a bit out of surprise. We only found you just a little while ago.”

It was a somewhat convincing explanation. Even I would have been curious about a man and woman wearing leaves like primitive people in the center of an island. I would have wondered what their story was too.
“So, what happened to you?”
“None of your business.”
“Haha, don’t be so on guard. It’s clear you two aren’t in a good spot—”
Amelia cut the man off. “I said it’s none of your business.”
But did he find that charming as well? “Haha, how feisty.” The man laughed good-naturedly, without a hint of displeasure. To be honest, he looked like a clown to me. Was he asking to be killed?
“Amelia.”
“I’ll make my own decisions here, so you just stay quiet.”
Yeah, okay.

When I called her name to warn her against escalating the situation, Amelia also softened her tone a bit. “The boat we were on capsized. Before parting ways with our comrades, we promised to meet them here. Is that enough of an explanation?” She had obviously adapted the story from my own real-life experiences.
“Hmm, then where did all your equipment go?”
“We put our equipment in a backpack before falling into the water and we ended up losing it. We threw away our clothes because they were wet and dirty.”
“I see.”
Afterward, the man asked Amelia a few more questions, clearly curious. Amelia offered him a plausible story. Of course, the more he dug, the more contradictions there were.

“Oh, so that’s what happened! It must have been quite frightening.” But as if those contradictions didn’t matter, the man scanned Amelia’s bare body and his eyes lit up. “This is, well, very fortuitous—”
Smack!
Amelia landed a high kick on the man’s head.
Slump.
Ha, this woman. When even the barbarian was keeping his mouth shut...
Who taught you to throw the first punch?
Even as I inwardly sighed, I immediately moved as if on cue.
“What the hell are you doing!?”
The blood had already been spilled, after all. I could debate things like right and wrong later. For now, we had to work together. “Behel—ahhh!”
Releasing Wild Outburst, I activated Giantization and, using Leap, landed in the center of their formation.
Swing.
I swung my club to take down the wizard first.
Okay, the wizard’s done.
I then twisted my back and used the centrifugal force to swing my club at the archer beside him.
“You!” The shield-holder beside the archer blocked the attack properly, rendering my second surprise attack a failure.
Crunch.
As a bonus, the club broke after smashing the shield. Damn, if I had had my mace, I could have crushed him with the shield.
Plop.

I tossed the broken club to the ground and grabbed the shield with both hands. “Gimme.” I yanked at it forcefully, but taking it was difficult. No matter the difference in strength, shields were usually secured to a person’s wrist with a belt. Of course, that wasn’t a major issue. If his arm was the problem here, all I had to do was break it.
Crunch!
“Aaaaaah!”
After using the shield to pull him toward me, I brought my elbows down to shatter his joints. Next, I kicked the guy away and took his shield.
Clang!
I immediately lifted it to the side to block the arrow flying at me. And that was the end of the battle.
Stab!
In that short period of time, Amelia had sorted most of it out. When the archer dropped, spurting blood, there was no one left standing. Not all of them were dead, though.
“A-An aura...?” Upon noticing Amelia’s aura coating the blade of the stolen knife, everyone lost their fighting spirit.
“Do you... know who we are...!?” The man who had taken the high kick in the beginning looked up at us with murder in his eyes.
Ha, why did things turn out this way?
“Be quiet.” It’d be a hassle if this guy started screaming, so I hurriedly gathered leaves from the ground and stuffed them in his mouth. I looked at Amelia. “What are you doing?”
I took part in this because I had no other choice, but what we did just now was no different from looting. If word reached the city, it would definitely cause a lot of problems.
“Tell me why you suddenly did this in a way that I can understand.”
When I looked at her, giving her a chance to explain, Amelia averted her eyes. “...I only attacked first before we ended up at a disadvantage since we had no weapons.”
That was ridiculous. “In that case, wouldn’t the normal approach be to try to solve things through conversation first?”
“I thought that wouldn’t work on these guys.”
It was like talking to a wall. Jeez, was this how everyone who met me felt? For some reason, talking to her felt like trying to reason with my past self.
Does she think she’s a seer like Nostradamus or something?
I abandoned the conversation there with a sigh, and Amelia spoke in an almost consoling tone. “Don’t worry. The situation you’re fearing won’t come to pass.”
“What do you mean by that?”
“Check their backpack.”

I didn’t know what she meant, but I opened their expandable backpack as instructed. The first thing I saw was snack-sized beef jerky. I had been close to dying of hunger too. It seemed our food problem had been solved, then.
Munch, munch.
I first stuffed the jerky in my mouth and then went through the rest of the bag. It wasn’t long before I noticed something odd.
Who the hell are these bastards? They’re not part of a clan...
The backpack was full of various equipment, and it was hard to write it off as emergency back-up equipment. Not only were they all different kinds of items, but most had blood on them.
“These guys... they’re plunderers.”
Then were the clan badges for camouflage? But why did they look familiar... Where had I seen this emblem before?
Combing through my memories, I soon remembered. “...Clan Elbis.”

It was a clan I’d read about in a book at the library. A gathering of dozens who had committed heinous crimes, in the end, they were all executed when their misdeeds were exposed. If memory served, that had been about fifteen years ago.
No sane bastard would carry this as a fake clan emblem, even if they were in disguise...
Something felt majorly wrong here. And in that moment, a breeze blew in from the cold sea and brushed down my spine.
Shaaaaaa!
No, wait...
When I hurriedly rifled through the backpack to find their identification tags, I froze in a daze.
“Holy shit...” The IDs listed various names, races, and ages, but they all had one thing in common.
“The renewal date is the 134th year of the New World...?”
For some reason, the date written on them was from twenty years ago.

chapters.title: Chapter 284: Adrift (4)
paragraphs: Is this for real? It’s not some sort of prank?

I stood there frozen for a long time, seized by a sensation that could only be explained as shock. My fingertips faintly trembled, and my breathing grew increasingly rough. But even so, I was quick to accept what had happened.
Time travel.

This was the only thing that could explain all the contradictions I’d been noticing since waking up on this island. Denying it was pointless. Yeah, why would time travel be impossible when it was also possible to suddenly wake up in a barbarian’s body while playing a computer game?
Still getting my thoughts in order, I looked at Amelia. “You already knew.”

Amelia gave a slight nod. “I suspected to some extent.” She then explained she had only been sure after running into these guys. I’d only heard about them in a book, but apparently they were very famous at the time.
...No wonder she was acting so strange. She’s not the type of person to throw the first punch like that.

I guess that was the perk of being a time traveler—being able to see through the hidden intentions of bastards like these, and bashing their heads in before they could try anything. It must have seemed incredibly bizarre from the victim’s point of view, though.
“F-Famous? W-What are you talking about?”
Whatever, I didn’t have time to explain. It would be pointless anyway. “Are there other clan members besides you here on this island? If yes, nod your head.”
I quickly moved on to an interrogation. After answering a few questions I had, I took time to think.
“Twenty years ago, huh...?”
First, we were twenty years in the past. Put simply, we’d just met people whose crimes would be revealed and who would be executed five years from now.
This situation is worse than I thought.
What we discovered through interrogation was that more than thirty of them were on this island. Amelia warned me that the commander of Clan Elbis was an especially dangerous adventurer.
“...We should get moving.”
“We should.”

I exchanged brief glances with Amelia, and that was all the conversation we needed. Surprisingly, she and I meshed quite well when it came to things like these. We didn’t have to waste time trying to convince each other.
“Let’s strip their equipment first.”
“Oh, I’ll take care of these guys here.”
We skillfully stripped their gear and stole their backpacks.
Stab.
Then we killed them all. And rightfully so, because how could we send them back alive when they’d come chasing after us with their comrades as soon as they reunited with them?
They deserve to die in the first place.

They wore the emblem of a clan whose crimes would be revealed in five years. Not only was there clear evidence of their looting in their backpacks, but they’d said things over the course of our interrogation that left no question of their guilt.
“What about the bodies?”
“We’d better bury them.”
“Then let’s get digging.”
I followed Amelia’s suggestion that we bury the bodies without objection. You needed to adhere to the expert’s advice in these situations.
“Now I’ll erase our tracks over there.”

While I was digging a hole to bury the bodies, Amelia returned to our camp and took apart the bonfire and bed of leaves I had laboriously created. My short-lived life as a caveman thus came to an end. Time to get back to civilization.
“It’s a dagger. Will you use it?”

Throwing off our Protections of the Tree Spirit, we pulled on the equipment we obtained from killing these bastards. It couldn’t be compared to the equipment I usually used, but I could work with this. Asking for more here would only be greed. After burying the bodies and covering them with dirt, I chewed on jerky and drank water from one of the canisters. Then I used the compass to situate us on the island.
Whew, now I feel like a person.
It was a familiar sensation.
“There’s this cave I spotted earlier. Let’s head there.”

The sky was slowly brightening and turning blue. I followed Amelia for about thirty minutes, and we found a small cave. Apparently, it was a place she had discovered while heading to the center of the island with Missha.
“It’s wider inside than I thought.”
“...You didn’t come in?”
“I just saw it in passing. I thought it would be a good place to hide.”
But you remember the exact location?
“What a great memory you have.”
As I was innocently admiring her skill, Amelia grimaced and said it was just a habit.
“Jeez, a grown adult getting embarrassed about a compliment.”
“...I’m not embarrassed.”
“Ah, I see.”
“Barbarian, what do you mean by ‘I see’?”
“I see” is just “I see.”
Anyway, enough chitchat. “I want to talk about that instead. What on earth is that stone?” I asked the same question I had been asking for hours, and was finally able to get an answer.
“It’s the Fragment of Records Stone. A relic left behind by the Great Sage Gabrielius, and a treasure protected by the lords of Noark’s castle for generations.”
So, that was the official name. It was clearly related to our situation.
“Then is it because of this stone that we were transported to the past?”

“Probably.” Amelia willingly acknowledged the possibility. She then went on to explain that the Fragment of Records Stone was a legendary item that was rumored to have the power to change history by sending the user back to the past, which was why she had been trying to obtain it her whole life.
“But why did you activate it while you were with me?”
“That... wasn’t my doing.”
“What?”
“I don’t even know how to use it in the first place. I planned to study it properly once I got back to the city later.”

According to Amelia, it seemed even the lord of Noark didn’t know how to use it. The family had just been keeping it safe until, as Auril Gavis said while handing it over, “the one who has answered the call of the times” eventually appeared.
God damn it.
Supposedly if you sighed too much, you chased blessings away. But the sighs just kept coming.
“Then you don’t know how to get back, either?”

“...That’s right,” Amelia answered apologetically, but her eyes continued to twinkle. Well, it wasn’t like I didn’t get it. From her perspective, she had achieved her life-long wish. Rather than trying to find a way back, her main concern would be how to change the past.
If I’m over here, what’s happened to me back there? Am I just frozen?
My mind grew even more scrambled, but I wouldn’t get any answers by worrying about that right now. For now, I decided to sate my curiosity.
“So, what happened to you?”
“What do you mean?”
“I’m curious what happened that you want to return to the past so badly.”
Amelia just kept her mouth shut at my question.
If you don’t want to answer, just say so.
After that, an uncomfortable silence fell between us that lasted for a long while. Well, thanks to our sudden trip to the past, we both had a lot to think about.
“The sun is rising.”

Time passed and the day dawned, and we just stayed in place, figuring that rashly wandering around could mean running into that clan and finding ourselves in a sticky situation. Man, if the bastards we killed earlier had a boat, we could have escaped the island on it.
To think they were controlling the entire island.

Something I found out during the interrogation earlier was that Farune Island was their clan’s domain. Apparently, they used this place as a base and plundered any clan-less adventurers who showed up. The reason why the five of them were wandering the island in the first place was in search of adventurers who might have entered while the clan was away.
But thankfully that means we just have to get through today.
The sixth floor closed on the sixtieth day of the labyrinth. Surprisingly, today was that day. I wondered if that was something to be surprised about when time travel existed, though.
I wonder what happened to the others... There will be another month left until the labyrinth closes there. Will they get by all right without me?

I suddenly worried about the comrades I left behind, but I didn’t let myself go too far down that rabbit hole. I needed to worry about myself first, considering I didn’t even know if I could get back.
It won’t all return to normal when the labyrinth closes, will it?
While I was thinking those idle thoughts, Amelia called out to me. “Barbarian.”
“My name is Bjorn, son of Yandel, human.” She didn’t answer. “So, what were you going to say?”
“I was going to tell you to pick out one of the tags from the backpack in advance.”
Huh? Ah...

At first, I was confused as to what she was talking about, but I quickly understood. As we were now, if we went back to a past version of the city, we wouldn’t even be able to cross the checkpoint. Soon, I rummaged through the backpack and compiled all the identification tags. There were almost forty.
“...But why did these guys collect tags like this when they could end up being used as evidence that they’re looters?”
“It’s a common practice. Identification tags are worth some money.”
Apparently, many people who weren’t from Noark also searched for new identities in the city.
That’s fair—if your backpack gets searched, you’ll get caught for looting anyway. So it’s more profitable to take the tags and sell them.

Before long, we went through the tags one by one and picked out the ones we could use. Unlike Amelia, who was human, I didn’t have a choice. Out of the many identification tags, there was only one belonging to a barbarian.
“Amelia Berrywells? You picked a good one.” Amelia chose a tag with the same name as hers. The race was human and the sex was female. “The age is twenty-one? Have you no shame?”
“...I-It’s not like I picked this one by choice.”
Huh? What was with that reaction? “Wait, Amelia. Just how old are you?”

“...Don’t pry into my life, Bjorn Yandel.” Amelia quickly returned to her normal self and cut me off cold. I wanted to tease her since it was the first time I’d ever seen her stutter. “I just chose the one where I would have to pay as few taxes as possible since that’s what we’ll be doing if we have to live here for a prolonged amount of time. The fact that we have the same name is just a bonus.”
So, you’re already assuming we might be stuck in this time for over a year. Jeez.
I licked my lips and scanned the tag in my hand to memorize what I needed to know.
The name is Nivelles Enze, age twenty-one. A sixth-rank adventurer.

That was all the necessary information. As he had been rank six, some of the essences in his possession would have been registered in the guild, so it would be wise not to use Giantization in front of people.
“If you’ve looked it over, give it to me.”
“Huh?”
“You told me not to call you ‘barbarian.’ I can’t call you Yandel in front of others.”
Oh, that was true. I handed Amelia the identification tag I would be using for the next while. But what was this?
“Nivelles Enze...?” Amelia froze, her fingers tightening around the tag like the name was familiar to her.
“Is he someone you know?”
Amelia shook her head at my question and didn’t elaborate any further, claiming it was just a coincidence. Ugh, she really had a knack for driving people up the wall.
Then don’t react like that in the first place.
Anyway, after that we passed the time until the labyrinth closed in the cave. While we talked only occasionally, there was one conversation that left a deep impression on me.
“I’ll take responsibility for finding the way back, so don’t do anything that makes you stand out. It could result in something irreversible.”
“Something irreversible?”
“It’s something I overheard a wizard say once. If you could hypothetically go back in time, even the slightest of changes could lead to the destruction of a country.”
It sounded like she was talking about the butterfly effect. You know, that one flap of a butterfly’s wings could cause a hurricane across the ocean.
...Wait, then what happens if the Bjorn in this time dies?

The thought suddenly popped into my head. Since I was twenty years in the past, Bjorn would still exist in this time. He must have been just old enough to be snacking on a baby bottle. What would happen to me if that child died?
I might end up in a very tight spot.
Once I got back to the city, it would be best to keep a low profile and watch how things played out, just as Amelia advised.
“Okay, I won’t cause any trouble so don’t worry.”
“...I’ll trust you,” she said, obvious distrust in her eyes. Then she soon fell into a contemplative mood.
More time passed. Some clan members looking for their missing comrades passed us by, but thanks to Amelia’s meticulous camouflage, we were able to go unnoticed.
Finally, the clock’s hour hand ticked as it moved to midnight. It was time for the labyrinth to close.
Shaaaaaa!
