“How about this instead? If the Gate of the Abyss opens, you’ll be able to return to your original world. How about that? It’s not what you asked, but isn’t that enough?”
Auril Gavis threw that tidbit at me almost like it was a reward. It was obvious that this was how he had always been planning to answer if I asked him why he wanted to open the Gate of the Abyss.
But that can’t be all of it.
I got the feeling he was hiding the actual important part. If the only thing the Gate of the Abyss did was allow us to return, he’d have no reason to bring us here.
Welp, this is why I wanted to check his motive... If this is how he wants to play this, I can just pass on things that are difficult to cover up from now on too.
“Fine, it’s your turn now.” I casually handed him the reins like I was satisfied with his answer. We proceeded to exchange rapid-fire questions.
“What year are you from?”
“Year 154.”
“Twenty years from now.”
He slowly interrogated me about my personal information and I did the same.
“Is your relationship with the palace hostile?”
“...You could say that.”
“What do you mean? I want you to be clear.”
“We are adversaries.”
Hmm, is that so? So you aren’t all in one boat.
“The one who sent you the invitation must have been me from the future—no, wait, let me rephrase the question. Who gave you the invitation?”
“An evil spirit from Earth nicknamed the GM.”
“I don’t know anything else about him, either.”
“I see. It’s now your turn.”
“Why is the palace hiding the fact that the outside world is normal?”

“Hmm, I guess that information’s spread that far in the next twenty years?” Auril sneakily tried to feel me out but when I didn’t respond, he gave me an answer. “The palace believes that is the best way to protect this world.”
“You mean it’s not because of a simple lust for power.”
“Unfortunately.” Taking up the next turn, Auril asked what difficulty I beat the game at.
I answered, “Times Fifteen.”
“...You’re lying.”
Geez, so stone-faced. But that confirmed one thing: there really was a lie detector running.

“Anyway, I don’t understand. Why would you lie about this and not the rest...” Auril trailed off like he’d come to a realization. “The original! Could it be that you cleared my original version?” He raised his voice in excitement.
Damn it all.
It was checkmate. The moment I answered in the negative, it would become another answer entirely.
Jeez, and he said my questions were unfair?
It was ridiculous, but what could I do? This was a world where the strong got everything, after all. A small fry like me could only swallow it. I kept my mouth shut, unable to honestly say “no.”

The old man took my silence as confirmation. “You did, you did! Right, there is no way the Fragment of Records Stone would react to someone who crossed over from a rubbish, mass-produced product like those other versions!” he rambled feverishly and mostly to himself. As I listened, I felt a little awkward. “Tell me, how did you beat it? How long did it take? No, what did you originally do for a living?”

It suddenly seemed like the old man was desperate. However, because the elderly tended to have extreme emotional ups and downs, I felt a need to verify whether that was actually the case. “I want to drink something.”
“Huh? But you can’t feel thirst here...”
“Then are you saying I’m lying?”
When I took off my mask and frowned, the old man quickly made a cup and filled it with water.
Hmm, this won’t cut it.
“Soda.”
“...Soda?”
“I want it to be soda, not water.”

“Ahh! You mean that?” The old man quickly changed the liquid in the cup. It was clear, but it was definitely soda given the bubbles that shot up from the bottom. I couldn’t stop myself from chugging it down.
“Aah...” Unlike the tasteless and odorless drinks that I usually found in Hansu Lee’s bedroom in the community, I felt the refreshing sensation of carbonic acid slide down my throat.
Burp.
“Haha, you drink heartily, like a man. Anyway, if you’ve finished, I want you to answer me now. Are there many others who have beaten the original in twenty years, like you?”

At that question, a smile spread across my face. Rightfully so, because my barbarian instincts that were finely attuned to hierarchical structures were telling me something. I didn’t know what was so important about clearing the original, but maybe I had the upper hand now.
“Hmm, are you that curious?”

chapters.title: Chapter 291: Big Fish (3)
paragraphs: Funnily enough, this was how all human relationships worked. Most of the time, the more desperate side became the side at a greater disadvantage in any given interaction, just like right now.
“One more cup.”
“Ah, here you go.”
“Haaah...” I drank another glass of lemon-lime soda. The old man looked like he wanted to stop me and finish the conversation now, but not a chance. “Can I have some cola too?”
“Haha, I guess you really miss your home.”

“Haaah...!” Yeah, this was the stuff. My whole body shivered at the refreshing sensation of carbonic acid, a sensation I hadn’t gotten to experience in so long. However, I decided to stop my drink-based power trip here.
Since he knows what these sodas are, I guess he really has been to our world. But then how did he cross over? I’m sure he hasn’t opened the Gate of the Abyss...
Many questions swirled through my head.
If I can figure out how he does it, can I go home without having to climb the floors?

Of course, it was just a thought. I wasn’t that desperate for it to work. To be honest, my biggest concern these days was whether I really needed to go back or not. I had already adapted to life here very well. It was an uncomfortable world in some ways, there was no doubt about that, but it was a good enough place to live. Yeah, even without soda.
“Haha, seeing you so happy puts me in a good mood too. How about it, would you like another?”
“No, that’s enough for now.”
“Really?” Auril cocked his head and then asked me the same question he did earlier.
“I’m sure it was my turn?”
When I rebuked him, Auril cleared his throat. “Ahem, ah, sorry. I got ahead of myself. As you said, it is your turn this time. Ask me anything.”
Are you joking? You haven’t actually answered any of my questions.
“The questions end here,” I said firmly.
“Huh?”
What do you mean ‘huh’? You really have no shame.
“Is there any reason to go on? I can’t even discern whether what you say is true or not.”
When I criticized how shady it was of him to run a lie detector behind the scenes, the old man protested like I was the one being unfair. “But I have not told any lies!”
Yeah, I’m sure, because you didn’t tell me anything important.
Actually, the fact that he didn’t was what gave me faith that he hadn’t lied to me.

“It’s true that this is unfair, though.” All this old man had to do was change the subject when he wanted to avoid a topic, but I couldn’t even hold my tongue without giving something away. “...What can I do?”
Hmm, I don’t know.
I pretended to think it over and waited until the exact right moment to open my mouth. “How about I get to ask ten questions for every one of yours?”
“What?” the old man said, clearly aghast.
Hmm, was that a bit harsh? I hurriedly whipped out the excuse I’d prepared. “I’m already taking a great risk by talking to you.”
“Risk?”

“Since I don’t know how this will change the future.” That line simultaneously reminded him of the amount of risk I was taking on right now and how valuable information from twenty years in the future was.
“What? Hahaha!” Auril burst into laughter as if I’d just told him a genuinely hilarious joke. The laugh was so joyful that it pissed me off. I wasn’t trying to be funny.

“Ah, sorry for laughing out of nowhere.” When I glared at the laughing old man, he coughed and reigned his expression in. “It’s just that I hadn’t even thought of that. Of course it would be natural for you to assume something like that... But the Fragment of Records Stone cannot change anything.”
That was the reason he’d laughed at my statement.

I experienced a temporary mental blue screen. But even after I rebooted my brain and tried to process what he’d just said, I still couldn’t understand it. So I asked outright. “What do you mean it can’t change anything?”
“Oh, is that your question?”
I felt both speechless and out of breath.

Just when I was getting desperate for another sip of lemon-lime soda, Auril laughed in amusement and provided an answer to my question. “Haha, that was a joke. Since explaining the concepts of time and cause and effect to you would be too complicated, here’s what you need to know. It doesn’t matter whether the chicken or the egg came first. The universe only has one single history regardless.”

History of the universe or whatever... I still didn’t get it. But while I may not have understood the theory behind it, I got the gist of what he was trying to say. “Whatever I do here, it won’t change the future?”
“That’s right. A timeline once observed cannot be changed.”
“Simpler.”
“That means that whatever you do for whatever reason, whatever conversation we have here and now, has already happened in the future you’re from.”

Understanding and accepting were two different things. I got the theory he was operating under, but... then what about Dwalkie? The letters I left at the holy land? In the end, nothing would change no matter what I did.
No way.

I decided to carefully hear the old man out but not to trust him too much. Even an old man like him couldn’t know everything. He didn’t even know I was the only person to clear the game on the original setting.

“Looks like you don’t believe me. Well, you’ll find out once you finish everything you have to do here and get back to your present. What it means to answer the call of the times.” Then Auril changed the subject and returned to our original topic of conversation. “So, in terms of fairness... Ten is absurd. How about three?”
Geez, badgering me right when I was overwhelmed. I set the whole “history of the universe” thing aside for now and focused on the negotiation. “Three is too little. Maybe five.”
“...Have you no conscience? Although information from twenty years from now is valuable, the things I know aren’t inferior either.” Auril frowned like I was hurting his pride.

Well, it wasn’t that I couldn’t understand where he was coming from. If you asked a hundred players from Earth, every single one of them would be interested in the information Auril had and would think it was more valuable than any they could offer.

“If you really think that, then you don’t have to agree.” However, the value of water was dependent on the environment you were in. A handful of water was more precious to someone dying of thirst than a hundred pounds of gold. “The questions are five to one. Take it or leave it.” I presented my final offer on cue.
Which was when something happened.

“These damned bastards...” The old man’s expression suddenly hardened. For a moment, I was terrified I may have crossed the line. Thankfully, though, it seemed I wasn’t the cause of his anger. “Oh, sorry. I wasn’t talking to you. It’s just that those people from earlier broke the rules again,” the old man continued, looking concerned about me misconstruing his expression. “Looks like I should leave for today. Why don’t we continue this conversation next month? I will think about the issue of fairness in the meantime.”

Although this was sudden, I didn’t let my disappointment show. The moment I gave away my true feelings, the terms of the negotiation we were about to conclude would go down the drain. “Fine.” I nodded like I was in no rush at all, and in response he waved his hand.
“...I’m back.”

When I came to, I was lying on my bed at the inn. It was midnight on the 15th. I headed back to bed after checking the time. Of course, sleep did not come easily to me. Countless thoughts, worries, and anxieties passed through my mind in a chaotic whirlwind. Regardless, morning came like it always did.
“...Nothing changes.”

As soon as the day dawned, I got dressed and headed to the library. The fact that the future wouldn’t change after this anyway? That no matter what I did, it would be meaningless because it had all already happened? So what? That couldn’t become an excuse to do nothing, because there was a possibility Auril was wrong. If I did nothing, that just meant that the possibility would really become zero.
She’s not here today.
I stopped by the library with that thought in mind, but Raven was nowhere to be seen. Where did that little kid go? Did she get a beating for shocking people with electricity while I was gone?
She didn’t come after all.
I even waited until the time Raven usually headed home but she didn’t show up. The next day was more of the same.
...Jeez, this is worrying me.
Although I was beginning to regret not finding out where her house was, I continued to visit the library. It wasn’t until what looked like another unsuccessful day that Raven appeared.
“Why weren’t you here?”
“I had something to take care of. You?”
“Just ‘cause,” Raven blatantly lied, sat down, and started reading a book.
But what was this now? “Why do you keep turning your head away?”
“I didn’t turn my head.”
You’re turning it now too. And your hair is suspiciously messy.
“Come here.”
“No.”
“Then I’ll come to you.” I stomped over and brushed Raven’s bangs to the side. When I saw what was underneath, I barely managed to keep my cool.
So, this is what you were trying to hide.
There was a large bruise around Raven’s eye.
“Who was it?”
“...It’s none of your business.”
Ha, how was I going to get her to cough it up?

As I sighed and contemplated how to handle this, Raven carefully studied my reaction. “...Don’t worry about it,” she said, her voice low and consoling. “My mom just caught me coming home late from the library.”
The explanation left a bad taste in my mouth. Even setting aside the fact that this little kid had been beaten by her mother, this was also a kid who never failed to head home right on time.
Got home late, huh? Why?
“Were you late because you were waiting for me?”
Raven kept quiet, and her silence spoke volumes. A beat later, she said, “No.”
It’s already too late for that, kid.
“Enough about me. Tell me about the labyrinth. You didn’t finish your story last time.”
“...How far was I?”
“Doppelganger Forest. You said that Doppelgangers specialize in playing dead. But that’s not very interesting, so tell me something else.”
I told Raven about the labyrinth as she asked, pretending everything was fine until the time came for her to go home.
“I’m leaving now.”
“Sure.”
“Are you... coming tomorrow?”
“If I don’t have anything going on.”
Once she had my answer, Raven hurriedly left the library. I left too.
Should I follow her?
I began to follow Raven. I wanted to avoid sticking my nose in someone else’s family affairs wherever possible, but...
It’s not like she did something worth getting hit for.
This had gone a little too far.

chapters.title: Chapter 292: Big Fish (4)
paragraphs: Ravigion was home to more than half the kingdom’s population. People of the upper class grouped these people together and called them all commoners, but a wealth disparity existed in Ravigion too. Adventurers and self-employed people who ran prosperous businesses found homes in the city center and on main streets near the square. Those places were generally safe, nice places to live.
So this is where she used to live when she was young.

Things were different in the large neighborhood a block down from the main road, which you could only reach through a dark alleyway. There was poor security away from the eyes of the guards. The buildings were old and run-down. Each one was divided into dozens of rooms, and every room was rented out. Bathrooms were shared, as were the kitchens. Even the barbarian inn that cost five hundred stones per night was on the outskirts of the city center, not in a place like this.

When I entered the alley after Raven, the wary eyes of the residents all honed in on me. It was a similar experience to my time in Bifron. Everyone was on guard around me, but no one approached me first to pick a fight. Rather, they all looked away.
Jeez, have you never seen a barbarian before?

While this once again reminded me of all the pros of being a barbarian, I was also realizing what a terrible neighborhood Raven was living in. This wasn’t a busy street with lots of people. It would be obvious to anyone watching that I was following her.
But none of these bastards are coming forward to stop me, huh? So it’s none of your business, huh? Well, whatever. I don’t intend to let Raven stay here for too long, anyway.
Creak. Thud.
A short while later, Raven headed into a building and closed the door. At first, I didn’t even realize that it was a house. It was really just a wall with a door hanging on it.
Then should I wait here a bit?

After reaching her home, I passed the time leaning against the wall. About twenty minutes later, Raven’s birth mother returned from work. It wasn’t hard to recognize her. Her hair was far from her daughter’s shiny blonde and she was a lot taller, but her face, at least, was exactly the same as Raven’s.
“Are you Arua Raven’s mother?”

“I am... Wh-who are you...?” The age gap between the two of us wasn’t big enough that I could say something like ‘she would have been a beauty in her prime.’ She looked to be somewhere in her late twenties at most. Did that mean she had had a child in her early twenties?
As I stared at her, feeling weird about that, Raven’s mother grew anxious. “Did my child cause another incident...?”
“This is not the place. Let’s go talk somewhere else.”
“...All right.”
I headed to the main street with her mother and entered a tea shop that also served as a café in the present day.
“Don’t worry. I’ll pay.”
“Right...”
I felt incredibly odd talking to her. Her face was the same as Raven’s, but her manner of speaking and things like that were completely different.
“Order anything you want to eat. If not, I’ll order it myself.”
From experience, it wasn’t difficult to order off the menu here without much help. Our food arrived quickly, fitting for a tea house. Of course, neither I nor the woman touched any of it.
Jeez, where should I start?
“First, let’s clear up a misunderstanding. I’m not here to complain about something Raven did.”
“Sorry? Then—”
“I am Raven’s friend.”
“Friend...?”
“Barbarians don’t care about age.”
“I-I see...” The mother nodded, although she still looked confused. I thought I had a rough idea of what her personality was like. She was just the exact opposite of Raven.
“I saw her for the first time in a while today. She had a bruise on her face.”

“Ah...” Finally realizing why I came to see her, the woman’s face turned white. But then she took a moment to think it over again and apparently came to the conclusion that it was unfair of me to call her out. “That’s... none of your business.”

Despite being scared to even speak this whole time, she chose to put her foot down here. By all means, my remark was rather foolish. This was a ridiculous world where you got sentenced to death if you couldn’t pay your taxes. A parent beating their disobedient child wasn’t an issue here. No—rather, it would be even weirder to criticize them for doing so.

“Business? Don’t use complicated words.” However, I was a proud member of the barbarian tribe who didn’t know anything about stuff like that. “All I care about is getting bloody revenge for my friend.”

When I said this calmly without any emotion, the woman froze. That was fair—when would she have ever had cause to hear something like “bloody revenge” in normal conversation? From what I heard, she just worked in a kitchen.
“...So what do you want from me? For me to stop hitting her in the future? Is that enough for you?”
“No, let her go.”
“What do you mean by that?”
“You should already know. Raven has the potential to become a powerful wizard.”

“...She does have his blood, after all.” The woman pressed her lips together. There was a clear glint of hatred in her eyes. She seemed to be thinking of the husband who abandoned his family after having an affair... but that was none of my business.
“Send Raven to the Magic Tower.”
“I can’t afford that.”
“I will pay all the necessary expenses.”
“...Why would you do that?”
“I just feel like doing it.”
The woman was silent for a long time at my answer. Then she said something strange in a low voice. “That child will abandon me.”
Huh?
“She’ll become a great person one day and look down on me. Then, in the end, she’ll leave me behind for that world of hers. Just as he did that day since she’s his blood...”
Ah...

“Isn’t this unfair? Why is that child’s life so easy? I gave birth to her, but no one in my entire life has ever helped me for that reason. But... why that child...?” After that, all kinds of sorrows fell from the woman’s lips in an unorganized jumble. “Come to think of it, I didn’t have any talent. I was slow to read too. But that girl is learning and using magic at her age.”

Her husband and daughter were the topics of conversation, but ultimately the underlying thread was regret and dissatisfaction about the life she had lived. I listened to her in silence. Her trauma was caused by her husband’s affair; her hatred was too complicated to be resolved with brief platitudes and went beyond festered.
After who knows how long, I asked, “Are you finished?”

“Fine,” she answered. “I’ll send her to the Magic Tower. The only thing she gets from me is her face, anyway. It’ll be easier for me if she completely disappears from sight. Sure. I also... want to be comfortable now.”
“That’s it, then.” As soon as the conversation was over, I got up from my seat and paid the bill. Then, before leaving the shop, I tried to hand the woman some money but she refused.

“I don’t need it. Someone came from the Magic Tower a few days ago. They said they’d support her fully and that I should at least send her there to take the test. I guess using magic everywhere she goes at such a young age caught their attention.”
“...I see.”
“Isn’t it strange? Everything I’ve accomplished in life is in a single room in this dump.”

With that, Raven’s mother staggered toward her house in the back alley like a person with no energy left in her body, and I watched her go. It wasn’t because I felt sympathy. But despite that, the woman’s last words kept lingering in my head.
“What was the point of my life, then?”

Time passed quickly after that. Raven’s mother took her to the Magic Tower as promised, and Raven’s potential was noticed over the course of several days. For reference, I was able to hear about the process in detail from Raven, who came to the library once every two days.
“You got to join the School of Altemion?”
“Yeah, I like the old man there. He doesn’t look down on me for being a kid.”
Was it just like that old man Auril Gavis said, then? I thought that her future would change if she was sent to the Magic Tower at a young age.
Come to think of it, I don’t even know when she entered the Magic Tower...

I had been confident it had been above the age of ten. That was because when I first met little her, Raven said she intended to become an administrative wizard. I had assumed she must have had a change of heart sometime in the future.
“But what’s with your expression?”
“It’s nothing. Anyway, it’s good that you got into the Magic Tower.”
“...I’m a little worried. I don’t know if I can do a good job.”
“You will be a great wizard. I guarantee it.”
“Hehe, really?”
Anyway, my conversation with Raven wasn’t limited to the Magic Tower but also her family. Apparently, her mom suddenly turned nice. It sounded like her mother hadn’t told her about meeting me.
After chatting for a long while, the time came for Raven to go home. “Then I’m going. Oh, and I can’t come here anymore. I have to go live in the Magic Tower from now on.”
“I probably can’t come here after tomorrow, anyway.”
“Why?”
“Something’s come up.” Tomorrow, I had to head down to Noark with Amelia. I probably wouldn’t come back here until we achieved our objective.
“...I see.”
Before parting ways with Raven for the last time, I offered her one piece of advice. “Once you get to the Tower, be careful—don’t be as rude as you are now.”
“Huh?”
“That goes for everyone you talk to. There’s no need to go around making enemies.”
“...I’m not afraid of anything like that.”
“Even if you aren’t, do as I say. Not only will you make enemies, but you’ll scare off people who are trying to be your friend. With that kind of attitude, you’ll only end up alone.”

“Did... I offend you too?” Raven asked carefully and after a moment’s pause, I admitted I had been a little offended. It seemed that made her come to some sort of realization. “Okay. I won’t do that anymore.”
“Do what?”
“...Tase people.”
Yeah, now you sound like a pouty little kid.
“But don’t you have to go now?”
“Yeah...”
After that, we ended our last conversation, left the library, and parted ways without making plans for our next meeting.
“Then, see ya!” It was a promise that set neither a time nor place for fulfilling it. Hey, where did that polite, formal manner of speaking go?
I smirked and answered, “Yeah, see you later.”
Although you won’t even remember me then.
After sending Raven off, I headed in a certain direction without hesitation. I’d kind of accepted it now.
Yeah, Dwalkie... cannot be saved.

I headed to the orphanage run by the Church of Reatlas. Arriving in front of it, I stood frozen for the longest time, unable to open the door. The reason was simple. Though I was flooded with the desire to go in and talk to Dwalkie one last time, I also wondered what the point of doing so was.
After who knows how long, someone called out to me from nearby. “Mr. Enze...?”
“Emirn?” It was the woman I had met while working as a volunteer the other day. At dinner, she and I had exchanged an odd conversation asking me for courage. “What brings you here?”
“To be honest with you...my son is here.”
...What?
“Thankfully, things worked out so I was able to bring him home. Thank you so much. If it weren’t for you, Mr. Enze, I would have hesitated forever.”
I stiffened at the instinctive realization that washed over me, but I had to check.
“Is... your son’s name Riol?” Riol Warb Dwalkie and Warb Emirn.
“Oh, yes, that’s right,” Emirn blurted in obvious surprise. So, Dwalkie had taken his middle name from his mother. “But, how did you know?”
“Just... because you look sort of like him.”

“Haha, is that so? True, I noticed you often talking to him.” Emirn smiled happily at my words. But did she want to get Dwalkie home as soon as possible more than she wanted to speak with me? “Then I’ll be going now.”
“Oh, right...”
Emirn hurriedly bade me farewell and entered the orphanage. I stood there at the entrance like a statue, unable to move for several minutes. All sorts of thoughts ran through my mind.
Dash.
I climbed over the orphanage’s fence and entered. Dwalkie was sitting where he always sat, reading a book. “Oh! Hello.” Dwalkie greeted me.
“Yeah... It’s been a while.”
“What brings you here?”
“I... just came.”
Dwalkie tilted his head like he thought I was acting strange, but he didn’t seem wary, perhaps because of all the time we’d spent together.
Slide.

I turned my head and glanced into the building through the window. I could see Emirn hand a stack of documents to the staff at the desk. It was then that I realized that Dwalkie would go live with his biological mother now and hear about the ocean. He’d become an administrative wizard, but he wouldn’t be able to give up on his dream and would someday enter the labyrinth.
“Everyone, thank you for being my teammates.”
He would die.
It’s... all because of me?

I felt a deep sense of responsibility. At the same time, I also felt like a speck of dust in the vastness of the universe. A sense of helplessness filled me, followed closely by a desire to defy fate. Maybe it wasn’t too late. If I acted now, I might be able to prevent that future from coming to pass. Yeah, if I kidnapped this kid right now, something would have to change.
God damn it.

Even as the thought came to mind, my body didn’t move. The same scenes kept running through my mind: Emirn’s face as she came to ask me for courage; and Dwalkie’s voice as he recalled his birth mother during our Team Half-Wit days. I kept seeing and hearing them both.
What... am I meant to do? Would the future really change if I took him? What if my actions have no effect and I just reduce the amount of time he gets to live in peace with his mother?
Squeeze.
A small hand patted my clenched fist. It was Dwalkie’s. “It’s big... Oh, I’m sorry. For suddenly touching you.”
“...You don’t have to be sorry.”
“Will my hands be that big someday? Big enough to protect the people I care about?”
To that question, I replied, voice rough, “Don’t worry. You’ll become a big man.”
Even though your body may be skinny and short, you’ll be bigger than me. Actually, bigger than anyone I’ve ever met.
I jumped the orphanage walls like I was running away from something. Then I hid in an alleyway and watched.
Creak.
After some time, I could see Dwalkie and Emirn come out the orphanage door.
“How come you’re my mother?”
“That’s... a long story, Dwalkie. Let’s go. I’ll tell you everything at...”
The two of them left, holding hands much too awkwardly to be considered mother and son.
“Goodbye, Dwalkie.”
I just watched on.

chapters.title: Chapter 293: Newbie (1)
paragraphs: It was evening when I returned to the inn.
“You’re late.”
Oh, geez, you scared me. I’m sure I locked the door behind me—how did she open it? At least turn on the light or something...
When I lit the lamp, I could see Amelia sitting on the bed in my room. Hmm, what should I say in a situation like this?
She looks like she’s kind of in a bad mood... But since when did I care about that?
I was feeling rather down too, so I just glared at her to hurry up and say what she had to say. Amelia slowly got up and passed me by. “We need to get to the location by midnight, so get ready.”
So, it was time to leave. I should quickly get my gear on.
Slam.
After Amelia left, I put on the pieces of equipment I’d been keeping in a corner of the room one by one.
Slide.
Boots made from the second-grade material Wyvern leather.
Click.
A belt with expandable pockets that could store potions and scrolls.
It feels empty.

I didn’t buy gaiters or a breastplate because it was impossible to purchase a full set of armor just by stripping five plunderers. I decided to invest all my money in a shield and weapon instead. And so, I chose a custom-made mace entirely made of the grade-three metal idium and a large battle shield made of the grade-five metal adamantium.
The grip feels good. Yeah, this is how big a shield should be.

Since they both weighed quite a bit, these two purchases exhausted all the money Amelia gave me, which was why my helmet was just plain iron. Well, you couldn’t expect iron to provide more than a minimal amount of protection.
I didn’t buy it to use as armor, though.

Back when I ordered this equipment three weeks ago, I was very concerned about the future, so I got a helmet made completely out of iron. The shape was similar to the one I used in my early days, with a T-shaped opening just so I could see. Of course, it had its differences. For one, the design was different since it was made at a different forge.
Is it because the opening is narrower than the first one I used? It’s really uncomfortable.

The amount of my face left exposed was significantly reduced. My judgment was that exposing my face to the countless people I would be running into in the labyrinth from here on out could lead to problems in the future.
Actually, I don’t know if there’s any point to this now, but...
I sighed and shook off my concerns and then, after glancing in the mirror, left the room.
Amelia was finished getting ready and waiting for me in a chair at the end of the hallway. “Finally, you’re here.”
What do you mean by ‘finally’? It didn’t even take ten minutes.
“You...” Amelia turned around to look at me and flinched. “That helmet, where did you get it?” she demanded.
“I got it custom-made. Is there a problem?”

“...Custom made?” Once she heard my answer, Amelia simply stood there for a while, totally silent. Her face was cold and stony and the look in her eyes was intense, just like when she saw Nivelles Enze’s identification tag on Farune Island. Of course, things were different now than they were then.
“Why are you silent when you’re the one who asked the question?”
“...It’s nothing.” Both back then and right now, this selfish woman never gave me a proper explanation. “We don’t have much time. Let’s go.”
But I knew the reason now.

In front of the sewer that was serving as our rendezvous point, the broker was waiting for us in black robes. It was a very strange feeling—I felt almost like I had become a smuggler. The broker didn’t say hello, and neither did Amelia. When they extended their hand forward, all she did was put a pouch of money in their palm.
With the payment handled, the broker gave a cursory warning. “I’ll say this one last time, but once you get down there, it won’t be easy to come back up.”
I was kind of amazed.
If you’re going to say that, at least say it before you get paid.
It was clear they wouldn’t give us a refund.
“That’s something for us to figure out.”

“Hehe, if you say so.” At Amelia’s stone-cold response, the broker laughed ominously and took out a key to open the steel bars leading to the sewers. Then they guided us inside. “Follow closely so you don’t fall behind.”
The journey to Noark was longer than expected. It was only after hours of walking through the maze-like sewers that the entrance appeared.

“Now, this is as far as I go. If you go inside and follow this map here you will reach a door. Once you get there, show this tag to the security guard and they will let you in.” The broker then handed over what would serve as our IDs and placed something that looked like a magical device near the wall to open the entrance.

What looked like a stone gate and an ordinary wall was pushed aside to reveal the stairs leading to the basement. But just as we were about to head down, the broker, who had not opened their mouth this whole time except when necessary, asked, “Can I ask just one thing? It’s not common for a barbarian to go down to Noark. What’s the story? You don’t seem like runaway lovers—”
“Stop.” Amelia shut them down. “If your job is done, you can go now.” The tone exuded an air of professionalism. It looked like there was some murderous intent mixed in too.

“...Excuse me. That was out of character. Go ahead. I have to confirm that the door closes.” When the broker backed off with their tail between their legs, Amelia strode down the stairs and I slowly followed.
Boom!
Before long, I heard the sound of a door closing.
Man, it feels like I’m entering hell or something.
“Wait, hold on. We should check the map first.” After descending the stairs, I went to open the map but Amelia stopped me.
“There’s no need. I already know how to get to the castle.”
Oh, right. She’s from here.

Anyway, after giving up my role of scout for the first time in a while and just following her, we reached our destination, a cavity so vast that it was hard to believe we were underground. I could see a stone gate much larger than the gates of Rafdonia in the distance.
“Hahaha, don’t just stand there and come on over!” One man stood in front of the castle gates, a human with a body as stocky as a barbarian’s.
Amelia leaned in to whisper to me. “Don’t do anything to attract his disapproval. Despite his cheerful tone, he’s one of the strongest fighters in this city.”
“Do you know him?”
“If you’ve lived in Noark for a while, you can’t not know him.”
Hmm, is that so? He doesn’t seem that strong...
Anyway, after that, we handed the man in front of the gate the ID tags we received earlier.

“Oh, ho! Looks like that guy has finally found some proper ones. Nice to meet you. I am the Gatekeeper, Lek Aures! Oh, I guess you don’t want to reveal your real name. Don’t worry. No one here uses their real names, anyway. Have you decided on your new names yet?”
Lek Aures, who introduced himself as the Gatekeeper, then asked us for our names and we gave him the ones we chose in advance. Amelia was Emily.

“Bjon, son of Thor.” I just went with a pseudonym I’d used in the past. “Nivelles Enze” was also a pseudonym, but I figured it was better to create a new one just in case. Of course, it didn’t matter much. This was just to engrave names on the tags, but I had been told no one in the city asked for names.
“Haha, I think it’s been almost five years since I’ve engraved a barbarian’s name on a tag.” When the gatekeeper returned the tags, they were engraved with the pseudonyms we’d given him.
“Is there anything else left to do?”
“No, the admissions process is over. Head that way.”
“...It’s not that door that opens?”
“Hahaha, don’t you think it’d be a waste to open that big door when it’s just two people entering?” Lek the Gatekeeper then opened the side door.
As I watched the stone door slide open, I was reminded of the day I first came to this world. Yeah, it was just like this then too.
Boom.
Then the door opened completely and an unfamiliar city came into view.
“Emily and Thor Bjon.”
“Thor is my last name, my first name is Bjon.”
“Hahaha! Ah, that’s right. Anyway! Welcome to Noark, you two!”
So, I’ve ended up all the way here.

People often thought of Noark as a den of criminals. That was natural because this was the place where those who had committed sins far too grave to live aboveground ended up. This was also Orcules’s lair.
“It’s surprisingly normal.”
There were no bloodstains on the walls, the streets were clean, and the faces of the people walking by weren’t all that scary.
“I don’t know what you were expecting, but this is also a regular place where people live, you know.”
Geez, can’t a newbie be surprised?
“Follow me.”
First, I followed Noark native Amelia around to take a look at the city and ask her whatever questions crossed my mind. “What are those stones embedded on the ceiling?”
“Magical devices. They use mana stones to emit light.”
“What about that moving doll-like thing?”
“Golems called patrols. They all belong to the lord of the castle.”
“Oh, and is there a market here too?”
“There is, but it’s not big since there is only one alchemist in the city. Most food products are rationed by type.”
Hmm, I see.
“Then what if you want to eat something specific?”
“You can hand in mana stones at the alchemy workshop and apply. But it takes about two days and the price is much more expensive than aboveground. Are you finished asking questions?”
“...For now.”
“Good. Because it looks like you’re drawing attention.”
“Huh?”
“We’re being tailed. Let’s speed up.” Amelia then sped up without asking for my opinion so I hurriedly followed after her.
“Tailed? It’s been less than ten minutes since we got here.”
“Barbarians are not particularly common in this city. They would have noticed you came from the overworld as soon as they saw you.”

I had a feeling I knew what she was getting at. In Noark, it was rumored that devils inhabited the overworld. I could only imagine how much they coveted the wallets of newbies fresh from the overworld who still had all their money from aboveground with them.
“Weren’t you just saying this is a regular place where people live?”
Amelia tilted her head at my question. “And what’s strange about that? Isn’t it natural to have people like this in a place where people live?”
Uh, is it?
“I guess that’s fair.”

Not being able to logically refute this, I just casually accepted it. It wasn’t like Rafdonia was all that different in the first place. Even in Rafdonia, three types of people roamed the outskirts at night: criminals, adventurers with the strength to defend themselves, and if neither of the above, those who believed in forced minimalism.
“Then what now?”
“We’ll go to the back alley where the patrols can’t see us.”
“Huh? Back alley?”

For a moment I wondered if I heard her wrong but Amelia gave me a logical reason for the move. Harming an ordinary citizen born in Noark was considered taboo, and you’d be hunted down by the lord of the castle for punishment, but apparently hurting everyone else was okay.
“These are guys who specialize in targeting newcomers so they’ll have a lot of things with them.”
Ha, you should have led with that. I guess native citizens have a totally different thought process. Yeah, farming always comes first no matter what.
Trudge.
After entering the alleyway and wandering for a bit, we came to a natural stop at a dead end and turned around.
“Where are you going like that? When you know you won’t get far.” As if on cue, a group of fifteen plunderers appeared before us.
“Did you think you could escape into the alley?”
“To think you would walk in here on your own two feet. This is why newbies don’t last long.”
“We all experienced this as newbies too, so don’t resent us too much.”
The city’s old guard was clearly excited at the thought of robbing some newbies. It was like watching a game flop just before the end. Tsk, this was why you should welcome newbies with open arms.
“Huh?” Looking around the group, I caught sight of a human man and flinched. But because I didn’t know for sure yet, I needed to confirm. “You there.”
“Are you talking to me?”

When I singled him out, the guy stepped forward as if his curiosity was piqued. The man, who had a physique large enough to be mistaken for a barbarian, was wearing a shiny breastplate. It was made of a material I couldn’t not recognize.
“...That’s lithinum.”
“Ha, what about it?” he asked.
What do you mean, what about it? Haven’t you ever heard of put-pocketing?
It was common sense for a veteran to donate an item to a newbie. I had actually just been getting embarrassed about being naked from the waist up so this worked out perfectly.
“Take it off. Before it ends up with blood on it.”
It was time to evolve into a civilized person.

chapters.title: Chapter 294: Newbie (2)
paragraphs: These guys were probably somewhat on guard too, since they had no information on how strong the new kids in town were. That was probably why they flocked to us as a group of more than ten people like this—luckily for me.
“Take it off. Before it ends up with blood on it.”

The moment my words echoed through the alleyway, the man stared at me uncomprehendingly. But before long, understanding began to dawn on him. Everyone, including him, clammed up. This was common in the animal kingdom. When prey ran away, you chased it, believing it to be weaker than you. But conversely, if said prey came out strong, you instinctively realized that something was wrong. Experience told you that you were in danger.
Slide.

The men who had slowly been closing in started widening their distance, wary of a surprise attack. Not that it mattered to me. We were in an alleyway blocked in by three walls. Although it was too cramped for me to use Giantization, it was still fine. There was nothing above to get in the way of me doing this.
Leap.
I jumped over their heads and landed on the other side of the alley. Okay, that blocked their escape route.
“...Kill that guy first!”
The group panicked and rushed at me. Finding their escape route suddenly obstructed, they seemed to think they had to get through me as fast as possible.
Whoom!
Pricks. They’re good at dodging.
“Don’t just block, avoid!”
“Who’s going to get hit by something as slow as that?”

The three people in front of me dodged my mace like eels and swung their own weapons. I could withstand most attacks with Physical Resistance, but some of the attacks fueled by skills succeeded in penetrating my thick hide.
Stab.
Geez, that stings.
If only I had Giantization activated, I wouldn’t have bled a single drop. Well, defense wasn’t my only way of protecting myself.
Transcendence.
I raised my mace up high and entered the command in my head. My selection for Transcendence was, of course, already decided.
Swing.
This combo was effective when dealing with large groups of enemies thanks to the fact that it tripled my reach.
Whooom!
When my mace slammed down on the ground, it lengthened like a Yeoui Staff and grew in size. Its reach was much shorter than when it was used with Giantization, though.
“H-Holy shit...!”
“Watch out!”
Where are you planning on going in this narrow alleyway?
Kwaaang!
The men hurriedly retreated but the three at the very front couldn’t get out of range in time.
Ah, so refreshing.
Step.
When I stepped past the trio I just turned into minced meat, the rest of the men shuffled back.
“Woman! Get the woman!”
They’re just marching straight to their deaths, huh?
It seemed they figured their best bet at this point was to take a hostage because they rushed at Amelia with outstretched arms and swinging weapons. Of course, they had no hope of touching her.
Smack, smack, boom!

Amelia instantly subdued two with punches and kicks, then pulled out a dagger from her thigh and swung it at the neck of another. Although her opponent defended himself by raising his wrists, which were clad in iron guards, that wasn’t going to work against a woman who could wield an aura.
Slice! Plop. Plop, thud.
The cleanly severed wrists and head fell to the ground almost simultaneously.
“A-An aura...?”

That was the end of the battle. The moment Amelia used her aura, everyone dropped their weapons. Now that they realized this wasn’t an opponent they could defeat, they decided to leave their fates up to our mercy. But it was much too late for that.
“P-Please don’t kill us. We’ll give you everything we have...”
“What will you do?” I asked.
“Kill them, obviously,” Amelia answered without hesitation.
At this, even those who had dropped to their bellies in submission picked up their weapons and began to fight back. “Die!”
You really think that’s going to work? It looks like they’re only about rank six on average too.
Smack, crunch. Slice!
Amelia and I quickly wiped the group out like we were a two-member plunderer party who had been working together for ages. It took less than five minutes.
It’s nice having a strong damager.
I felt reassured in a way I had never experienced on other teams. Was there a way to add her to our party later? Even as I thought that, I made sure to keep moving, swiftly farming the corpses.
“Ugh...” As I was taking off the lithinum breastplate that I had been eyeing from the get-go, the guy stirred and began to tremble. What, he was just unconscious?
Smack!
After hitting him on the back of the head to put him down, I turned to Amelia. “Why did you leave this guy alive?”
“...You said you didn’t want it to get bloody.”
Ah...
“Th-thanks?”

There was a brief awkward moment, but we wrapped up the looting a few minutes later. For some reason, the farming took longer than the actual battle. Still, the earnings-to-labor ratio was higher than ever.
I think this would be worth seventy million stones in the overworld.
As I gave the loot a cursory scan before shoving it into the expandable backpack, my heart felt full. These were the results of a few minutes of fighting?
I never imagined such a sweet hunting ground was hidden underground.
Perhaps Noark was a good place to live.
Click.

After putting on the breastplate, I also put on some miscellaneous equipment including the matching gaiters. The sizes were perfect, just like the breastplate. Mm-hmm, it was incredibly important for a warrior to wear proper armor.
“Then let’s go.”
“Oh, right.”

The stares of the nearby residents watching through curtained windows were growing uncomfortable, so we quickly left the alley and got back onto the boulevard. Then, following Amelia, I got to take a good look around. I figured that making it obvious that I was new in town could result in another loot-mining opportunity.
Well, that was the plan, but even after walking for quite some time, no one took the bait.
“Anyone on our tail?”
“No.”
“Still?”
Why was this happening? When I cautiously expressed my disappointment, Amelia sighed like I was being ridiculous. “Noark is a small place. Word spreads fast.”
Ah, since none of the guys following us earlier had returned alive, no one was going to come after us guns blazing again.
“...Ugh.” I clutched my chest and slumped to the ground with a pained expression on my face.
Amelia, startled by this, stooped down. “Are you hurt? I didn’t notice any external wounds earlier—was it poison?”
As Amelia hurriedly moved to administer an antidote, I whispered, “Don’t worry. I’m pretending I’m hurt.”
“...What?”
“Someone might come at us if I do something like this.”
“Barbarian, you really...”
I saw disgust appearing in Amelia’s eyes, so I quickly got up.
Jeez, you enjoyed farming too. And now you’re trying to shame other people for it?
“Just follow me. We might end up having to sleep outside if we’re any later.”
“Okay.”

Anyway, after heading to the city center, we found an inn in the area. Oh, of course, we got one room instead of two. Apparently, if someone were to target us despite the rumors that were spreading, they would be skilled enough to do so.
“Thankfully there’s more than one bed.”
“All lodgings in Noark are like this, so that’s not a surprise.”
“Huh?”
“No one in the city would come to sleep somewhere like this alone.”

From what she told me, unless you purchased a house with your family, it was common for most people to live with their comrades and party members, which made sense to some degree. Living in groups would be safest in a place like this.
“Yandel, you wash up first. I’ll go through the loot in the meantime.”
“Ah, I’ll be quick.”
Once I was done washing up, Amelia went into the bathroom next. After that, we talked for a while.
“What are you going to do with the loot?”
“For now, I’m going to keep it. It’ll be worth three times the amount of money if we sell it aboveground later.”
“That’s a larger difference than I thought.”
“It’s only natural, considering the supply down here is significantly higher than the demand.”

Hmm, that was true—plunderers collected more equipment than mana stones. “But from what you’ve told me, there’s a merchant company that crosses between above and underground. Can’t you just sell it to them?”
“Sounds like you’ve misunderstood something. When I said the equipment was three times less valuable down here, I was referring to the merchant company’s rates.”
“...I see.”
“So if there’s anything you need, don’t even think about selling gear. That’s not how this city works.”
Anyway, the discussion about what to do with the loot ended there. After that, we got down to business.
“So, what’s the plan now?”

Infiltrating Noark had gone according to plan. We now had two goals we needed to achieve here: 1. Seize the Fragment of Records Stone that was being kept by the lord of the castle and use it to return to our time, and 2. Fulfill Amelia’s wish.
I hadn’t said this out loud, but it would be difficult to achieve the second goal because fulfilling this woman’s wish would mean that the past would have to change.
From the grim expression I saw on her face earlier, I think she’s aware of this to some extent...
I wondered what decision Amelia would make when the time came.
“Why are you asking that?”
“In case you changed your mind.”
Amelia answered my straightforward question without the slightest hint of hesitation. “You say strange things. Our plans haven’t changed,”
So you’re not going to give up.

Day and night existed in the underground city of Noark, too, but there was no dawn or dusk. During the hours of the day when people were active, the jewels embedded in the ceiling glowed bright, and when it was night, they switched to minimum output.
“It’s daytime.”

After staying the night, we left the inn once the world outside the window brightened. That alone made me very aware of the fact that I was in a strange city. It wasn’t at all typical to see all the doors in sight open and people pour out of buildings as soon as day broke.
“Stop looking around and come with me. We’ll be stuck waiting a long time if we’re late.”
“Oh, all right.”
Following Amelia, we arrived at the castle located in the center of Noark. I only saw them in the distance yesterday, but today the castle doors were wide open to welcome a large number of people in.
“Why is everyone going over there?”
“Most of the jobs available in the city are in the castle. Those who don’t enter the labyrinth are assigned work there and live off those wages.”
Was this a communist country? Well, it was probably because they could survive in a place like this that everyone from Noark was so tough.
[Labyrinth Management Office]
Arriving at our destination, we entered the building. The interior was similar to the Adventurers’ Guild and the procedures weren’t all that different, either.
“Then see you later.”
“Oh, right.”

We each stood in a different line to save time. To enter the labyrinth from Noark, there were more hoops to jump through than I previously thought. First of all, not only did a newcomer to the city have to register here, but it looked like they had to pay an entrance fee every time they entered.
How can this place be even worse than Rafdonia?
It was almost absurd to think that Noark had been founded by the Ormi Revolutionary Corps, who had once called for the royal family to be overthrown.
But when is this line going to get shorter? They should at least make you take a number like in Rafdonia. What are they doing, getting all these people to line up?
After complaining inwardly about the slow administration and outdated system for thirty minutes, a group of five adventurers swaggered up to me.

“Hey, brother! Judging by the registration papers you’re holding, you must be a newbie, right?” Then, acting friendly, one of the men placed a hand on my shoulder. “We’re a little busy today. Can you give us your spot? Hmm? We’re all on the same side now. We should be helping each other.”
For a moment, I didn’t understand what was going on.
What the—? Is this another attempt at put-pocketing?

chapters.title: Chapter 295: Newbie (3)
paragraphs: I turned my head to look at the hand on my shoulder. It bore a ring with an unusual pattern on the index finger.
“A sub-space ring.”
My heart began to pound. What could be inside that ring? It was like looking at a loot box that hadn’t been opened yet.
Slide.
Subconsciously, my hand gravitated toward the ring. My precious...
“...What the hell, you bastard?!” As soon as my hand touched his, the man jumped and removed his hand from my shoulder. “Barbarian, you son of a bitch! Are you...?!”
Judging by the startled look in his eyes, I could see what the misunderstanding was here. His comrades each offered their two cents.
“No wonder there’s a barbarian down here.”
“No normal person would come down to this city.”
“So he was kicked out of his tribe because of his preferences—”
What were these assholes talking about? I had to hurry and clear up the misunderstanding, so I quickly threw my fist forward.
Smack!

The first punch landed on the face of Buck Tooth, who had dared to put his hand on my shoulder and act friendly. Something white popped out of his wide-open mouth. His buck tooth had been completely cured with a single punch.
“Behel–ahhh!” As soon as I released my battle cry, the other adventurers crowding the space all stepped back and made space.
“It’s a fight!”
“Woahhh!”
“The newbie and Rex’s gang are fighting!”
Was this a high school classroom? The workers sitting at the windows just sighed, looking unfazed.
So, no one’s going to stop me, huh? Even better.
I was starting to like Noark more and more. Maybe I’d secretly wished to live in a macho society like this even if I pretended not to.
“You bastard!” One of Ex-Buck Tooth’s comrades, Beardy, drew his weapon in anger.
Okay, let’s switch to team-battle mode.
I had been refraining from using a weapon just in case, but I now took out my mace and swung it like I’d been waiting for the opportunity.
Whoom!
Beardy ducked to avoid the hit. Right at that moment, a ball of electricity flew at me from the man behind him.
Pzzzt.
It doesn’t look like magic... He must have a special ability. But my shield is made of adamantium.
Adamantium was a grade-five metal that reduced all attribute-based damage by fifty percent.
Buzz!
An electric current flowed through the shield and into my body, but I could shrug it off with my Mana Resistance. It seemed like these guys had never experienced something like this before, though.
If you wanted to take down a tank, you should have cursed me first, you bastards.

When I swung my mace, unaffected, Beardy looked flabbergasted. I got it. He’d expected me to end up paralyzed, which was why he had closed the distance even more, leaving himself at just the right angle to get whacked.
Smack!
Okay, that was two down.
Boom.

Beardy’s body cracked the ceiling and then landed on the floor. If this were baseball, that would have been a foul. I tapped my shoulder with my mace and stared straight ahead. “What are you doing? Come.”
The trio who had just lost two of their teammates for trying to cut in line surprisingly made the rational choice. “Rex, let’s leave.”
“I think I just heard someone say that Kalte’s entire gang was found dead after following a newcomer who came down yesterday.”
Oh, you guys hadn’t heard the rumors yet.
It seemed they were just starting to realize I wasn’t an easy opponent from the whispers of nearby onlookers.
“But if we back off like this...”
“We’ll be laughingstocks, I know. But that’s still better than dying. I don’t know if it’s true, but I also heard there’s a woman with him who uses an aura.”
“An aura...?” The man named Rex frowned.
Right at that moment, Amelia, who had been waiting in line elsewhere, came over and stood next to me.
“Ah, you’re here,” I said.
“You seem to be the talk of the town wherever you go.”
“It wasn’t my fault this time.”
“...I’m aware. I saw it happen.” Amelia’s hand drifted to the dagger on her thigh. It seemed that was rather persuasive to our unfortunate trio.
“...Why don’t we call this here?” Rex suggested.
Hey, that’s not how you negotiate.
“Your apology?”
“I’ll do it. I apologize for looking down on you and making an unreasonable request.”
It seemed like the culture of this city was that once you decided to take something lying down, you lie really low. Surprisingly, this guy went fully submissive.
Now, then. What should I do?
Contemplating this, I glanced to the side and saw Amelia give a slight nod. That meant I should let them go. “Fine, I accept your apology.”
“Thank you. Then...” Once I verified that their apology had been received, Rex began to tend to his fallen comrades.
Hmm, what the hell is this now?
“Stop. Leave behind everything those two have.”
“But I apologized...”
Those are two different things, man. What use is an apology that’s nothing more than pretty words?
“We’re on the same side now. We should be helping each other.”
Mm-hmm, that’s that neighborly feeling that comes with being in a community, no?
Rex thought this through for a long time before he finally sighed and stripped the equipment from his unconscious comrades. “There, is that enough?”
“The ring?”
“...Here.”
Whew, how much did this make? I was practically copy-pasting money at this point. Why did these bastards from Noark all live in poverty?
Anyway, I’ll find out what’s in the ring later.
“Go.”

After sending off Rex and his minions, I stored all the stripped equipment in my new sub-space ring. The expandable backpack was getting uncomfortable, so I had actually just been thinking that I really hoped to get my hands on a sub-space item.
“They may not have looks going for them, but they’re warm-hearted.”
Amelia said nothing.
“What are you looking at? Let’s get in line again.”
After that, we headed to the window again. Other adventurers had taken our place since we stepped out of line, but that was no problem. I’d already adapted to this city.
“Oh, human.”
“...W-What is it?”
“As you saw earlier, we had extenuating circumstances. Can you yield your spot to us?”
“...Of course.”

Thanks to the consideration of a kind adventurer, we were able to stand at the very front of the line. Since we had been in the middle of the line before the fight, we were essentially saving thirty minutes.
“The people here are very kind.”
“...Anyone looking at us would think you’re the one from Noark, not me.”
Haha, don’t flatter me like that, I’ll get embarrassed.
“I’m just quick to adapt. Not a genius.”
“I never said anything remotely like that.”
“Haha, you’re too shy to tell the truth, huh?”
Anyway, since we were at the front of the line, our turn soon came and we were able to get our registration done ahead of schedule. That was because we skipped the rank adjustment application.
“Didn’t you say you were planning to get your rank raised to five?” I asked Amelia.
“Doesn’t matter. By now, news of us will have reached the lord of the castle.”

Since we’d managed to achieve our objective quickly thanks to me, there was no reason to adjust our rank and publicize the essences in our possession to the whole town. “Good thing I did as I pleased.”
“...Things may have turned out fine just now, but be more careful from now on. Little fish aren’t the only ones in this city.”
“Okay. So have we finished our mission for today?”
“Yeah, let’s head back and rest.”

Returning to the inn we found yesterday, we changed the terms of our stay to rent the room long-term and then waited there, refraining from going out. I wasn’t sure how long we stayed put. Contrary to Amelia’s expectations, the lord of the castle did not show any interest in us for several days. Which was a problem, as phase one of our plan involved working under him.
“Amelia, what’s going on?”
“...Looks like he’s taking his time trying to figure out what we’re like since he has no information on us.”
“And?”
“Let’s keep waiting for now. He’ll get in touch someday. With his personality, the lord of the castle won’t be able to leave two independent, high-ranking adventurers alone.”
Time continued to pass and soon it was time for the labyrinth to open.
“Wooo!”
“How long has it been?”
“Let’s go make some money!”

The square was packed with people like there was a festival taking place. It was always like this on labyrinth entrance day, but the people gathered in the plaza today looked especially excited. It wasn’t like she couldn’t understand why. After the small number of people who entered the labyrinth last month had returned alive, public opinion was that the labyrinth was safe again. To those who had been struggling, that couldn’t have been better news.
Swish.
Arua Raven passed the square on a wagon and drew the curtain bitterly. It had just hit her.
“So, it’s already been a month...”

It had been a month since Bjorn Yandel had died. Although it had been the death of a man largely considered a hero by the adventuring community, the world kept turning, unchanged. The only things that had changed were the things around her.
Sigh...
Raven briefly recalled the past month.

“So, Bjorn is dead,” Ainar, who was surprisingly the most composed member of the group, had said. “What are you doing? Let’s all head home and rest. We’re all tired, so let’s talk about what we’re going to do from now on tomorrow. As for the guild... I will go there by myself.”
Facing reality head-on and accepting it, she tried to do what had to be done immediately: sustaining this team Bjorn Yandel had created. Of course, that wasn’t going to work out how she wanted it to.
“What do you mean... from now on? What do you mean by that?” the elf asked.
“Since Bjorn is dead, the five of us will have to enter the labyrinth together from now on.”
“The labyrinth?” the elf shot back aggressively. “Is that really the problem we should be concerning ourselves with right now?”
“Then what problem do you think we should deal with?”
“We have to get revenge!”
“Revenge?”

“On Noark! It’s all because of those people that the event on that island was even triggered! And that red-haired woman was also suspicious. If that bitch is alive and has something to do with what happened to Mister...” Murderous intent gleamed in the elf’s eyes. “No, even if she has nothing to do with it, it doesn’t matter. I’m going to find and kill them all.”
It was understandable that she’d lose her reason to anger. The recent loss of her sister had also been at Noark’s hands.

“Erwen, we get how you feel, but calm down,” Raven said. “The people of Noark are outside now. How are you going to get revenge on them in the first place? Let’s go home for today and come back tomorrow—”
“Yeah, that’s all he was to you people.”
“Excuse me?”
“I feel bad for him. For staying back to protect the likes of supposed comrades like you.”
“...What did you say? Say that again.”

“R-Raven, stop it! Don’t act like her too!” Ainar, their warrior, stopped her. Normally their team’s beastwoman would have stepped forward to intervene, but she didn’t seem to have the presence of mind to do that.
But did that catch the elf’s eye? She marched up to the beastwoman. “What about you? You’ll join in on it, right? Revenge?”
“I-I...” The beastwoman trailed off.
After a while, the elf, who had been quietly waiting for an answer, left with the words, “Beastly bitch.”
“I-I’ll meet up with Erwen tomorrow. So let’s... all go home too,” Raven said.
With that, the party scattered and went home. The warrior woman intended to head to the guild and report the death of Bjorn Yandel, but the wizard stopped her.
“Miss Ainar, please take care of Miss Karlstein. I’ll... do this.”
“But—”
“You can’t even read, Miss Ainar.”
“Okay. I’ll leave it to you.”

The beastman archer, who had a family of his own, did not say a single word until the moment they parted. Like someone who had been through this many times before, he just watched the splintering of his team with grief in his eyes.

“Let’s see, the deceased... Baronet Bjorn Yandel?!” When Raven submitted the death report, the guild went into an uproar. Nearby adventurers and staff alike seemed to have a ton of questions, but they didn’t dare approach Raven after seeing the expression on her face.
A day passed.
“Did you hear? Baronet Bjorn Yandel is dead.”
“To think that giant would go like that...”
“What a shame that someone like him left us.”
News of Bjorn Yandel’s death spread through the city as quickly as word of his feats spread in life. Those who knew him visited his home.
“Ainar! Missha! Open the door! Is Yandel really dead? W-Why... Open the door!” shouted former teammate and dwarven warrior, Hikurod Murad.

“...Murad, stop it. I just came back from seeing the death report for myself at the guild. We shouldn’t make things even harder for them. Let’s just go and come back another time,” said Brown Rotmiller.
Many other adventurers who were indebted to the hero named Bjorn Yandel visited his home.
“Thank you for saving us that day.”
“Now you won’t... be coming to the library anymore.”

Flowers piled up in front of the door. Countless people mourned his death, and the barbarian tribe, who had seen him as their next leader, even locked the gates to the holy land and held a funeral for several days, praying for his spirit, which had come to rest in the labyrinth, to return to the forest. But even still, the world remained unchanged. It was only the things around her that were different.
“...Let’s not think about going on quests for a while and just rest.”
All plans for future expeditions were suspended. What could the four of them do when they weren’t all in their right minds? They needed a break. And the same went for Arua Raven herself.
But a break won’t change anything.
The day that elf stormed out like that, Raven intuitively realized that the saying “time is the best medicine” was a lie. As the days went by, everything became more of a mess than ever got fixed.
“I need to find it.”

Raven was unable to sleep properly for several days and spent her time buried in books. Even today, she was on her way back to the palace’s library. That was because what had happened that day was still veiled in mystery. In the city, his cause of death was understood to be the Storm Gush.
“I can’t accept that.”

But he had succeeded in killing it. He’d even had the energy to secure his body to the ground with stakes so as not to get swept away by the ocean. So where had he disappeared to in that short amount of time? And if he had really just been washed away, why had his equipment been left behind?

“There’s something else... Some big mystery at work here...” Raven clutched at her chest like a person struggling to breathe. Although she perhaps wasn’t being very wizardly and logical right now, she needed something to cling to. “There has to be something else.”

chapters.title: Chapter 296: Newbie (4)
paragraphs: Noark was a city full of warm-hearted people. But if you decided to interpret that statement another way, you could also take it to mean that it only had warmth going for it. Prices were so all over the place that I couldn’t get used to them, and the administrative services were old and outdated.

Just this morning when I headed to the labyrinth management office to receive a binding spell, the administrative wizard in my line took an hour break because he was tired. Though, to be fair, I did get to the front of the line after that by ‘convincing’ someone to yield their turn out of anger.
“How long are you going to stand there like that?”
“Oh, I just felt weird for a moment. This place really is no different now than it is twenty years in the future.”
“Why are you stating the obvious?”
Jeez, so unromantic. Even if it’s entirely the same, we’re still in the labyrinth twenty years in the past.
“Follow close behind.”

After looking around and indulging in sentimentality for a moment, I ran after Amelia, who had started running ahead of me. I frowned. It looked like she was leading me the right way, but how could she find the way without looking at a compass?
Oh, could it be...?
“Are you a scout?”
Amelia glanced back at my question, then resumed running without a word. That was answer enough for me.
Holy...
A human character who used an aura, had a Doppelganger’s essence, and had the abilities of a scout? The world was so unfair. It made me feel a little greedy and desperate.
It would be so reliable to have someone like her on the team...

If we got to know each other better here, would she let herself be recruited once we got back? We still had a lot of seats left to fill before we hit the ten-member clan threshold... Anyway, I wondered if my clan was operating well without me.

While I was running behind Amelia with these thoughts buzzing through my mind, a group of adventurers we encountered along the way struck up a conversation. “Oh, are the two of you a party?” This was a group that was running toward the second floor to cut down on travel time like we were, not some low-level adventurers.
This is quite nerve-wracking.
Currently, I was affiliated with Noark, not Rafdonia. Maybe that was why I found myself worrying that they might find us suspicious. It ended up being an unnecessary fear, though.
“None of your business.”
“Haha, feisty. Take care!” The group laughed merrily at Amelia’s cold response and disappeared down another path.
“Why did you freeze?” she asked me.
“Just... nothing. I was just thinking I would have a hard time living a life of crime.”
“...What did you say?” Amelia asked like she couldn’t believe her ears, then burst into genuinely hearty laughter. “Ha, puahahaha!”

To be honest, from my perspective, this was extremely random. It wasn’t like I’d said something funny in the first place, and it was my first time ever seeing her laugh so loud. “...Haha, I guess you like jokes like that?”
I felt a sense of pride, but Amelia stopped laughing at my question, wiping all traces of emotion from her features. “Don’t be mistaken. I only laughed because you are ridiculous.”
Uh-huh, say that without smiling, then.
I guessed her sense of humor was odd, being from Noark. Was it so funny to her that my anxiety was giving me jitters?
When I asked that, protesting her treatment of me, Amelia opened her mouth. “The people we just saw were from Noark.”
“What?” That person who looked so pleasant was from Noark? “How do you know that? I heard it’s at the discretion of people from your side whether to wear faction emblems or not.”

Amelia was quick to answer my questions. Apparently, what had tipped her off was the fact that there wasn’t a wizard or priest on their team and that the color and design of their equipment weren’t uniform, as if they were wearing items they’d stolen from multiple different people. “And more importantly... Only people from Noark would bring along a kid whose face is covered with a robe.”
“Kid? Oh, are you talking about that small adventurer in the back?”
“Yes.”
“Hmm, I just thought it was a short girl or a dwarf... How can you be sure?”
Amelia’s tone was slightly wooden as she replied, “I just know it when I see it.”
“What?”
“Enough, let’s move.” Amelia ended the conversation like she didn’t want to talk about this anymore. This was one of this woman’s bad habits. She made people curious.

“Amelia. If what you say is true, why are people from Noark bringing children into the labyrinth?” Instead of asking how she was able to recognize the child in an instant, I asked a slightly different question.
It seemed this much was okay because Amelia answered me. “First, children can be enslaved for a pittance.”
“Hmm, I still don’t know if that’s a reason to bring them along.”
“They are surprisingly useful. They can be used for cumbersome tasks like cooking and night watch, and are even helpful for looting.”
“They’re helpful for looting...?”
“As bait. If a child comes to ask for help, even the wariest of adventurers will at least listen to their story.”
Hmm, really?
“Strange. I think I would be even more wary if a child came up to me. In Rafdonia, minors are not allowed to enter the labyrinth.”

“That’s because you’re from twenty years in the future. That law is already on the books now just like it was then, but even civil servants in Rafdonia implicitly permitted the practice in this time period.”
Wow, she really sounded like an old person when she talked like that. Back in my day.
“Hey, Amelia, how old are you?”
“...Get moving instead of spouting nonsense.”

Anyway, we continued to chat as we headed up to the second floor, and since we ran, we soon arrived at our destination. As expected, the portal had already been opened by someone else. That was too bad. We got here pretty fast too.
“Let’s go up.”
When we entered the portal, we were greeted by a gloomy yet soggy ambiance.
This place always puts me in a bad mood.
This was the Land of the Dead, a district where Ghouls, Death Fiends, and various undead monsters appeared, and also the place where Amelia and I first met.
Whew, I thought I was going to piss my pants back then.
As I looked at it now, I realized you really never knew how things would turn out in the future. Who knew the two of us would come back here again, and as comrades this time?
“Amelia, I have a question.”
“Don’t ask.”

“You told me back in Bifron that the people you killed here in the Land of the Dead that day committed sins that were deserving of death. Is that related to something you’re trying to fix here in the past?”
“You... have a lot of questions about me.”
“Of course.”
When I nodded, unaffected by her irritation., Amelia clicked her tongue. “...Yes, it’s related.”
Hmm, so it is.
I wanted to hear the backstory behind that too, but I stopped because it looked like she was going to get mad at me. I’d have to ask about that another time.
“If you’re done, let’s move.”

Entering the second floor in earnest, we continuously slaughtered monsters as we moved without pause. Was it because there were just two of us? It reminded me of the time that Ainar and I used to work as a duo. Back then, each battle had been a struggle. Time sure flew by.
Smack!
To think I could now beat a Death Fiend to death with my bare fists.
“Behel–ahhh!”
My shout was met with pointed silence.
“Oh, sorry. It’s a habit,” I said.
“Whatever, sit. Let’s rest here for a bit.”

We traveled all day and then found a place to settle down at nighttime. After having a simple meal, we agreed to sleep just three hours before we got moving again. To clarify, no one was on night watch. Apparently, she just needed to summon a clone through Self-Replication to handle night watch for us.
“...You can do that?” In the game, the Doppelganger’s essence hadn’t come with an auto-hunt mode. So how could that be the case here? The answer ended up being simple.
“Don’t worry. I haven’t slept properly since becoming an adult.”
Her mind was always half-awake as she slept so she could control her doppelganger around the clock. At least, that was what this woman claimed. I didn’t know if that was biologically possible.
“Tsk, no wonder your eyes always have bags under them.”
“Are you picking a fight?”
“I’m saying you should get some sleep.”
Anyway, Amelia admitted that she did end up having a little less energy than usual while using the auto-hunt mode, but that it should be fine on the lower floors.
“Rest.”

So I lay down on the ground without complaint, but sleep didn’t come right away. It wasn’t because I was anxious there wasn’t a night watch or anything. After all, I was a tank. Most types of beatings wouldn’t kill me straight away.
I wonder if the others are doing all right...
Camping in the labyrinth kept bringing thoughts of my clanmates to mind. That was how the night of Day One passed us by.

On Day Two of entering the labyrinth, we arrived on the third floor, right on schedule. It was now time to commence fulfilling our mission for this trip into the labyrinth: return with achievements worthy of being noticed by the Lord of Noark.

“Ever since the first day we arrived in Noark, we poked around the city and proved we were capable. But even still, the lord of the castle hasn’t approached us,” Amelia had said. As for why, she explained it like this. “He is clearly being careful. The palace has sent many spies underground before.”
So, in other words, what we needed to show off in the labyrinth was not our capabilities but our character. Were we really suited for Noark?
“The easiest way to prove ourselves is looting. If we return from the labyrinth with looted items, his suspicions will lessen.”
Amelia spoke of looting as the top method and I agreed, on one condition. We would plunder, but by targeting plunderers, not ordinary adventurers.
“Is that your condition?”
“Yes. I don’t place too much value on other people’s lives anymore, but I won’t kill anyone for my own gain.”

“...But how will you tell plunderers from adventurers?” Amelia had been flexible, agreeing she would do as I requested as long as there was a way. I replied that it was difficult to explain, but I’d show her how later.
Time passed and now, we had arrived at our destination of the third floor.
“Now, what are you going to do?”
Plunderers couldn’t do anything on the fourth floor, and it would be hard to operate as a duo on the fifth. Thus, the third floor was perfect for plunderer farming.
“If you really have a way to identify plunderers, go ahead.”
Jeez, so impatient.
I then asked Amelia for a few things.
“First, Amelia, use your stealth skill.”
“...Stealth?”
“Don’t act like you don’t know exactly what I’m talking about. The skill you used in front of me back then, when you suddenly disappeared into the darkness.”
Amelia disappeared as instructed without another word. Whew, I really couldn’t sense her presence at all. I had the thought that I should look into getting a detection-type Numbers Item I got back.
“Now, what’s next?”
