It was really strange hearing a voice appear out of thin air, but I played it cool and didn’t let it show on my face. “Nothing special. You just have to follow me in that state. I’m going to find a plunderer.”
“All right.” This was one of the good things about having Amelia as a comrade. Whatever I did, she refrained from asking pointless questions and just watched.
Well, at least, that was usually the case, but...
“Barbarian.” Amelia abruptly called out to me. “Why... are you suddenly taking off your equipment?”
Oh, couldn’t bear your curiosity, could you? True, I’m sure it’d be hard for an ordinary person to see what I’m doing here. But I was hoping that you of all people would recognize my strategy.

“It’s hard to explain. Just watch.” I then took off a few pieces of equipment and stored the rest in sub-space. After that, I took out the beginner’s set of armor I had been angling for from the very first day and put it on.

Seeing as my surroundings were silent, it seemed Amelia still had no idea what I was trying to do. However, just as a picture was worth a thousand words, seeing it once would be better than hearing a hundred long-winded explanations.
“We’re starting now. Follow closely.” I started running forward mindlessly and shouted with all my might, “I-I’m lost and my comrade is gone! I-I can’t see! Is anyone there? Help!”
This was a barbarian’s secret skill, one developed to protect the heart: Call Forth the Bad.
“Help me! I have a lot of money!”
He who answered the call would not be a good person.

chapters.title: Chapter 297: Evil Spirit (1)
paragraphs: After running for about thirty minutes, I came across a five-person party made up of three humans, one dwarf, and one elf. Judging by their equipment, I figured they were fifth-floor adventurers or higher.

“You lost your way? Calm down and catch your breath here.” When they saw me approaching their camp, they sat me down and gave me beef jerky instead of getting defensive. My first thought was that the jerky might be poisoned.
“Hmm, what to do? We don’t have time to wander the entire third floor looking for your party.”
Not one of them expressed any ill intent over the course of the conversation or asked for equipment in exchange for saving my life, even though that was pretty much the norm.
“Haha, you want to give us your weapon? It’s fine. If you give us all your equipment, what will you do during this expedition?”
“It’s okay. If it really bothers you, pay it forward by helping another person in a similar situation instead of being stingy.”

These were people with character too solid to merely call them good people. That kind of made me even more suspicious, so I sat by the bonfire and pretended to doze off to give them an opening to attack me.
“He must have been very tired.”
“Jess, what should we do? The thought of leaving this guy like this bothers me a little. It’s the same as leaving him to die.”
“Why don’t we roam the area for just a few hours and see if his comrades are around?”
“And if we can’t find them?”
“Hmm, then why don’t we take him upstairs with us for this expedition? It may make things harder, but we can’t leave him to die in a place like this.”
There was no point in testing these people any longer. It seemed I would only cause them trouble. So I gave the signal we agreed on earlier to Amelia, who was nearby, to come pick me up.
“There’s a lot of people coming to find us today. Who are you?”
“...Sorry to disturb you. I’m looking for my comrade.”
“Comrade? Oh, could it be?”
When Amelia approached the campfire, I jumped up and ran to her. “Oh! Emily! I missed you! What took you so long?”
“S-Sorry... But this is a bit...”

“Emilyyy!” I hugged her tight to keep our act from being exposed, all the while taking care to watch my back. They seemed like good people, but I worried they might change their minds after seeing Amelia.
“I’m glad you’ve reunited with your comrade.”
But there was no plot twist.
“Haha, stay close to your teammate from now on.”
“You have a good comrade. It’s not easy to find people who get lost in the labyrinth like this. You should treasure each other.”
These people had ended up being nice from start to finish, and so it was time for their uninvited guests to leave.
“Come on, let’s go. Everyone... is worried... about you...” Amelia led me away, saying something about how our ‘team’ promised to meet us elsewhere, and the people sent us off with warm smiles.
I... really came back without a hitch?

While on one hand I was stunned, on the other, I was extremely touched. Was this what you called healing? What kind of life had I been living this whole time? It turned out there were still so many wonderful people in the world.
“Unfortunately, your plan didn’t work.” While I was busy being deeply touched, Amelia looked at me, clearly wondering what my next move would be.
Jeez, you’re making me embarrassed. It’s not like I knew things would turn out like this.
“Are you going to continue?”
At Amelia’s follow-up question, I started to seriously think my plan over.
Then five adventurers emerged from the darkness. “Hey there, did you get separated from your comrades? What are you two doing? If that’s the case, come on over. We’ll help you.”

They were all smiling brightly, like people who had just found a golden nugget on the side of the road. I finished waxing lyrical about mankind then and there and approached them with a smile. “Oh, really? We were just in need of help!”
Yeah, the rule of thumb was that guys like these came to find you, even when you didn’t go looking for them.
The second party we encountered was much more obvious than I thought they’d be. As soon as we approached, we were not-so-subtly surrounded.

“Oh, isn’t that a sub-space ring? That’s a valuable item compared to the rest of your low-grade equipment.” As I reached my hand toward them to touch the sub-space ring, the group went into intimidation mode.
“So, where are your comrades?”
“I don’t know.”
“Hmm, is that so?”
It seemed that after obtaining that bit of additional information, they concluded we weren’t much of a threat. Soon, one of them approached Amelia and went to place his hand on her exposed thigh.
Stab.
Her dagger sunk into the back of his hand before he could touch her.
“Aghhh! You bitch!”
“Kill her!”
Just like that, the battle began not even a full three minutes after meeting each other.
Whip!

Seeing as he retaliated without the slightest hint of hesitation as soon as he was stabbed, it seemed he was quite experienced in interpersonal combat. Of course, that wasn’t a problem for us because we were the same.
“Behel–aaah!”

Giantization, Swing, etcetera—as soon as I started using my skills and rampaging in earnest, the match was quickly decided. The fact that they had conveniently placed themselves in a siege formation to prevent us from escaping worked in our favor.
Crunch!

That may have been an effective way to kill goblins after capturing them, but not Trolls and Ogres. Targeting the back row’s bow and staff users from the get-go, we had them all flat on their backs before long.
“Did you trick us...? Fuck.”
Crunch!

The moment I crushed the head of the guy who seemed to be the leader, a pleasant silence descended. Now it was time to pick up these poor, abandoned items. Stripping their equipment and opening their bags, there was evidence of looting everywhere. There wasn’t much equipment inside since it was only the third day, but they had sleeping pills, poison, psychological scrolls, and more. The bag was full of consumables that could be used on people, not monsters. Several IDs appeared to have been stolen.
But was it because we’d raised our income in one fell swoop? “We just need to do this about ten more times.”

Amelia no longer questioned my methods. She realized, too, that there was no more effective method than this. Killing a plunderer who recently looted other people got you several pieces of equipment as well as several IDs, meaning you got much greater results in terms of time versus effort.
“Then let’s just wipe off the blood and keep going.”
Anyway, after that, we continued to pull the same act and ran into several teams. The reactions were varied, but to sort them into broad categories...
“Not interested, keep moving.” When it was just me, the percentage of people who refused to let me approach at all was near 90 percent.

“Since you’re in a tough spot, we’ll let you stay with us for a while.” Those who listened to my story and asked for a reasonable amount of compensation in exchange for letting me rest with them accounted for 5 percent of the population.
“...How suspicious. Take out your ID.” Those who mistook us for plunderers and whipped out maces of justice were 3 percent.
“No matter how precious an item is, it’s not more precious than a life.”
“Sorry. My policy is to prevent any potential issues later.”
Those who tried to strip me of my equipment even if that meant I’d get killed by monsters and those who tried to take my life just because I saw their faces were about 1 percent each.
Our batting average is much lower than I expected.

We ran into maybe one team out of a hundred that was useful. So why had I run into so many of these bastards before today, the one day I actually wanted to run into them? People often said that even the most common fixtures in your life tended to disappear right when you needed them. I didn’t know if that was true, but after wandering around for a long while with no luck, we were met with a new type of team on the eighth day.
“Oh, nice to see those famous new recruits here.” It was a team of plunderers from Noark.
To speak in terms of outcome, there was no battle. It was not that we didn’t have any intention to fight—it was more so that our opponent didn’t give us a chance.

“Haha, it’s nice to see you here, but I hope you stay in your lane.” The plunderers did not even allow us to get close, and Amelia didn’t necessarily show any hostility, either. Rather, they warned us. “We work under the lord of the castle, so I wouldn’t do anything reckless if I were you.”

Jeez, I didn’t even think of doing anything. But we needed to at least pretend to be on the same side, right? If we attacked first and any one of them returned to the city alive to testify, our plan would be ruined.
“Wait, can we talk?” the team from Noark suggested.

“Fine.” Amelia agreed without hesitation. It didn’t take long for me to figure out why she was acting like this. Since we needed to join forces with the lord of the castle, this was an opportunity for us to make an appeal.
“I’m Beck.”
“We’re...”
“I’m aware. You’re Emily, and you are Iron Mask, right?”
“Iron Mask?”
“Oh, you didn’t know? That’s the nickname people have given you.”
I didn’t know I had a nickname like that. Well, it did suit me considering I constantly kept my face covered with a thick helmet while in Noark.
“But your face is more handsome than I thought.”

Oh, right. I had been in the middle of fishing so I wasn’t wearing a helmet. That unsettled me but I didn’t bother putting one on. What difference would it make to show my face to a few of them? It wouldn’t change anything either way.
“But was that your guys’ strategy? I was very impressed. You made good use of the stereotypes about barbarians.”
“...What do you mean by that?”
“Oh, it was just a compliment without any particular meaning behind it, so don’t give me that look. We might end up as comrades, no?”
Amelia interjected at that. “Comrades?”
“Oh, right, I didn’t tell you. I didn’t mention it earlier because I’m sure you need some time to adjust to the city, but the lord of the castle thinks highly of the two of you.”
In other words, we seemed capable, but he was keeping his eyes on us because he didn’t know what kind of people we were.
“The lord of the castle likes bold people. Especially ones who are unbound by morals, like you.”
That meant there would be no need for any more tests.
“They’ll be in touch by the time you get back so make sure to carefully consider it in the meantime. It is a strange city, after all. You at least need a place to lay your head, right?”
“...I’ll think about it.”

“Haha, that’s it then.” The man then turned to me with a bright smile. “Oh, and you. It doesn’t seem like you’ve been out in the human world for all that long, but it seems it’s rubbed off on you, eh?”
“And you must have been out in the world for too long, seeing as all your hair has fallen out.”

“...What?” It seemed like he was paying me a backhanded compliment, which was why those words just came out of me. But was that not his intention? “Ah! It was a compliment, a compliment! I apologize if you took it the wrong way.” Instead of getting mad, the guy just apologized.
And so it was my turn. “Oh, mine was a compliment too. I apologize if you took it the wrong way.”
“...I-I see?” The man laughed awkwardly and I followed suit. Even still, I kept looking at him. I had a strange feeling.
His name was Beck, right? Why do my hands keep itching when I look at him?
Fueled by a mysterious discomfort, I shifted my gaze and spotted the only adventurer in the group wearing a cloak. They were small in stature—like a child.

“Oh, I guess you guys don’t know.” Beck seemed to misinterpret my staring as a sign of curiosity because he whipped off the child’s cloak. “It’s a similar tactic to the one you used, in a way. We use this kid as bait. Most people lower their guards that way. If we send her in beforehand, it becomes a way to confirm how strong our opponents are in advance. She’s surprisingly useful in battle too. Most people have a psychological resistance to killing kids like her.”
Beck described the child like he was trying to sell me on a product, but his explanation didn’t even reach my ears. I’d already heard all of that from Amelia, anyway.
Huh? Where have I seen her before?

When I looked at the expressionless child standing under the cloak, I had a strange feeling of déjà vu. But did he misunderstand my staring? “Hmm, looks like you’re not curious. You just like what you see, then?”
Beck said some absolute bullshit. Normally I would have bashed his head in and cleared up the misunderstanding right then and there, but I decided not to argue and asked, “What is her name?”
“Name?” Beck tilted his head like that was a strange question. He seemed like he had no idea why her name might be important to me, but he answered anyway. “Jencia Nephrin.”
So, it was you. No wonder I felt weird.
“W-We’re real p-people, right? Wouldn’t that be murder?”

I met this child in Glacier Cave and she was the first evil spirit I ever killed. Of course, the Jencia I killed was a different person from this child. Evil spirits only ever took over the bodies of adult natives of this world, and no evidence suggested otherwise yet.
Wait, that means...

The moment I registered this, I realized one thing. As a child born in Noark, it was highly likely that Jencia was living underground even as an adult. In other words, it finally made sense why that woman—the woman in Jencia’s body—had been so miserable.
“I want to go home. I can’t die in a place like this. You have no idea... what I’ve had to do to survive in this fucking world. Yeah? Please...”

Human characters tended to have it easier when it came to survival. Their taxes were set much lower than the other races so they didn’t have a problem getting by for at least a few years even without doing adventurer work. That was why I couldn’t really sympathize with her claim back then. All I saw was a woman looting others for an easy life.
“M-Mom...”
But she had started from this hell. I’d always thought that barbarians had the worst start. It turned out there was a bottom below rock bottom.

chapters.title: Chapter 298: Evil Spirit (2)
paragraphs: I felt weird. Not because I was sympathizing with her months later, nor because I regretted bringing down my mace at the time or anything. But I felt somehow uncomfortable and suffocated.
“You don’t look well. Do you know that child?”
I shook my head at Amelia’s question and asked her about something that had been on my mind. “What happens to those children when they become adults?”
“They become adventurers.”
“Are there no other options? Like working in the castle or something like that.”
“That’s impossible. Those children promised to work under the lord of the castle in the first place.”
“Promised?”
“In exchange for the castle fostering them, they do whatever they are told.”
I was dumbfounded. “Leaving them all the grunt work and using them as bait while looting is fostering them?”
“Children who survive hell grow up strong.”
As soon as I heard that, words the chieftain once said to me flashed through my mind.
“You should know that the only warriors who become strong are the ones who are able to survive.”

The context was similar—the labyrinth was an environment structured in a way that people had no choice but to become strong in order to survive. The lord of the castle deliberately placed these children in said environment.

“Still, aside from when they’re young and serve as bait, the mortality rate improves after that. The same goes for the child’s treatment in their assigned team,” Amelia continued. After surviving for about three years as a decoy, they were recognized for their contributions and started to learn how to use weapons. In addition, they were apparently given unclaimed essences during hunts. “Children who undergo that lifestyle become useful fighters as soon as they become adults.”
“What if they want to quit once they become adults?”
“That doesn’t happen. They start receiving constant ideological education from a young age. By the time they become adults, they’re servants who are more loyal to their lord than anyone.”
“But what if they still come to their senses and want to quit?”

Amelia frowned at my persistence, then said, “The castle commences making corrections. To make them loyal again.” I was speechless. “Don’t worry too much. No child goes to work under the lord of the castle without knowing that.”

The conversation ended there, but my wheels kept turning. What kind of life did the player who entered the body of Jencia Nephrin have to lead? Well, it might not have been so bad. They didn’t kill evil spirits without mercy in Noark.
They still wouldn’t have let them roam free, though.

From the lord of the castle’s point of view, the evil spirit would have taken over the body of a high-achiever he had been cultivating on leftover essences for several years. Whoever the evil spirit may have been, the lord of the castle would have made it so that the woman now known as Jencia would continue to live the same life as the original, even if that required correction that was a bit stronger than usual.

Anyway, whether her identity was exposed or not, she would have had to start looting from the start. So treating everyone as NPCs instead of people could actually have been a defense mechanism... Wait, why am I concerned about this? Stop thinking.
I cut my train of thought off there. It didn’t matter to me what environment that player had had to survive in. That woman tried to kill me.
Yeah, so... I just did what I had to do. That’s all there is to it.
Whew, laying it out like that made my chest feel less tight.
“What are you doing, Amelia? Let’s go. We need to do our job.”
“Why... are your mood swings so intense?”
“I’m a barbarian!”

Shaking off any unpleasant emotions, I continued to fish for plunderers using the secret skill Call Forth the Bad. A few more days passed like that. I was sorting through the equipment of another plunderer team as usual when...
“Oh, another sub-space ring.”
Rumble...

“...Huh?” The moment I looked up in confusion, the ground under me began to shake with what felt like an earthquake. To be honest, I was shocked. I didn’t consider for a moment that something like this might happen.
Booom!
A Rift had appeared on the third floor.
That a Rift had opened on the floor we were on was a little sudden, but not something particularly surprising. That was something that could happen during any expedition. The problem was, why now?

We did not enter the labyrinth to embark on a normal expedition. There were no essences for me in the third-floor Rift, either. Plus my essence slots were already full, so it would be impossible for me to absorb another one unless I erased the Corpse Golem’s essence.
What about the Numbers Item and Rift Stone, you may ask? Those couldn’t be brought with us twenty years into the future anyway.
Well, the money from a Rift would be helpful for surviving here, but... Stop getting ahead of yourself and check it out first.
I quickly cut my inner monologue off. Having a Rift open on your floor and managing to enter it in time were two separate things.
“Amelia, the location.”

Talented scouts could determine the location of a Rift once it was generated. So where had this Rift formed? If the closest portal was several hours away running, we wouldn’t be able to get in anyway, so there was no need to even bother.
“Five minutes north.”
What the—? It’s right under our noses. You should’ve said that earlier.
Last time a Rift had formed on the fifth floor, it had been located in a completely different district, so my party and I had to admit defeat.
“What are you doing?! Let’s go!” I shouted with enthusiasm and intent to start running right away.
“You want to go in?” Amelia asked bluntly.
Um, obviously. If you can enter a Rift, it’s always best to do so. Essences, items, and whatnot are always a win, and there are experience points you can only acquire in particular Rifts... No, wait.
“Amelia, have you been inside the third-floor Rift?”
“Once before.”
So she’d already gobbled up the experience points here. No wonder she had no enthusiasm.
“Not me! So let’s go!”
Silence.
“We’ve pretty much succeeded in getting the lord of the castle’s favor! That won’t change just because we don’t bring back a little more loot!”
“But if something goes wrong in the Rift...”
“It won’t! And we’re comrades! Help me out this once! I’ll just collect the achievements and come out!”
After a beat of silence, Amelia sighed. “...All right, follow me.” She began to lead the way.

I was sure she hadn’t changed her mind because of the word “comrade.” She probably just judged that it was better to deal with a few days’ annoyance rather than have a falling out with her collaborator. She was a woman who valued rationality above all else.
She surprisingly meshes well with barbarians.

Since she was the unemotional type, a barbarian’s naive pleading worked well on Amelia. To this woman, it would make more sense to just do this for me than continue to be bugged for the next few days.
Dash.
Anyway, as we were running, the portal appeared in our line of sight
“Yandel, think this through one last—”
Think what through?
“Behel–ahhh!”
I threw myself into it without hesitation.
Flash!

When I opened my eyes, we were inside a pure white temple. The ceiling was tall enough for me to Leap to my heart’s content. White marble columns and a hundred stone statues ran along the length of the wall.
Since no one’s here, I guess we entered first.

Once I confirmed there were no other adventurers yet, I slowly looked around. Rather than being an attempt to figure out where I was, this was out of pure curiosity. That was because there was only one Rift on the third floor. This was the Hundred-Color Temple, a temple that carried a hundred colors. It was also a place that you had to drop by at least once during a playthrough, because the supply of EXP here was enormous.
“Yandel, do you know of this place?”
“To some extent.”
“Then there’s no need for me to explain.”

The Hundred-Color Temple had three main characteristics. First, elite monsters that didn’t appear in normal areas like Corpse Golems poured out. No matter what you took down, you’d be able to get points for first kills as long as it was your first time here. Second, it was not a cooperative raid like regular Rifts. Those who entered had to compete with each other, and only one team could enter the boss room. If the team that entered first failed, then another team got a chance.

Oh, but that didn’t mean Amelia and I would have to compete with the other teams on our own. The third characteristic: when a Rift was created, a total of five portals opened on that floor, and those who entered through the same portal became a team of five. That had always been the most challenging part of playing the game. That was a given. What happened if you found a Rift while working as a five-person party, only to find two people were already inside?
Well, two characters from your team would be left behind, just like with this team of adventurers who just came in.
“Damn it, someone was already in here.”
The portal in the air spat out three more adventurers and closed. It looked like their teammates had been left outside.
“Oh no! Lemud and Hans didn’t get in!”
Oh, nice.

“Calm down! They may be separated from us, but Lemud and Hans should be able to hold out on the third floor without us!” Soon, the human swordsman finished soothing his panicked comrades and approached us. “Nice to meet you. Did you two come in together?”
“Yes, and?”
The man laughed good-naturedly despite Amelia’s curt response. “Haha, we’ll be together for the next while. Since it’s fate that we met like this, let’s introduce ourselves first. I’m Carlton Drek.”
“Emily.”
“Bjon.”
When Amelia and I revealed our pseudonyms, Carlton cautiously asked me a question. “Bjon, are you a barbarian?”

It was only natural that he’d be wondering. After all, I was in full plate metal armor right now. Since I was covered in iron plating from head to toe, no one could check whether I had a barbarian’s tattoos or not.
“What does that matter?” I asked stubbornly.
Carlton backed off and apologized. “Sorry. I was just curious, but I see how that could sound rude to you.”
Looks like he thinks I’m just a large human. Fair. It’s mostly narrow-minded people who react sensitively to trivial questions like that.
Anyway, after we revealed our names, an elf guy hanging in the back of the group called out to Carlton. “Carlton, will you come here for a second?”
I can’t hear them.
They whispered something to each other. It looked like they were discussing something.
“They are calling us suspicious.”
“Huh?”
“I can hear what is being said as long as it’s at distances like this. That’s without magic, of course.”
“...I see?”
So she had good hearing. I never knew that. I should be careful not to even whisper in front of her.
“So what are they saying? They look serious.”
The contents of the conversation intercepted by Amelia were as follows:

The elf pointed out our peculiarities. “They only revealed their first names. Plus, there’s the fact that there are only two of them on the third floor on the thirteenth day. They could be plunderers. One even has his face covered.”
“Yes, but there is no other way,” Carlton replied. “We can’t just stab them in the back because they’re suspicious. Let’s not play our hand yet and find out what kind of people they are as we go.”
It seemed the discussion ended on that note.

“Ah! Sorry! My friend was worried about the teammates we left behind.” Carlton laughed heartily and came up to us. Then he revealed the names of the other two and gave them a chance to introduce themselves.
“Now, this man from the elf tribe is—”

“Stop, I’ll do it. I’m Eimbern Berta Garcia. As you can see, I specialize in archery.” Eimbern ended his introduction by briefly revealing his name and main weapon. It seemed he didn’t want to give us more information than that.

Anyway, next was the barbarian warrior. “Hahaha! Nice to meet you all!” Like the barbarian he was, the warrior had been left out of his two comrades’ whispered conversation and approached us with a bright smile. Then, without bothering to keep his guard up at all, he introduced himself. “I am Yandel, third son of Jarku!”
“...What?”
My mind went blank as soon as I heard that. If I didn’t hear him wrong...
“Ah, is that a little too hard for humans? Just call me Yandel Jarku!”
...that meant he was my biological father.

chapters.title: Chapter 299: Evil Spirit (3)
paragraphs: Barbarians had a very laid-back approach to naming. If the child was a son, he used his father’s name as his surname, and if it was a daughter, she used her mother’s name. As such, there were no family names in the tribe and all barbarians treated each other like kin. Well, not that that was important right now.
Yandel Jarku.
It was very unlikely it was someone else with the same name. How many Yandel, third son of Jarkus could there be? It was only logical to assume he was my biological father.
“Hahaha! How long are you going to leave my hand hanging?”
Okay, let’s come to our senses first.
My biological father? So what? I could be shocked and bewildered all I wanted, but this wasn’t something to be mind-blown over. It wasn’t like I was actually Bjorn Yandel.
“Ah, my mind wandered for a second.” I accepted the handshake and stepped back. That concluded our introductions.

Carlton laughed awkwardly and got straight to the point, the first thing any adventurer should do when encountering someone who wasn’t in their party in a Rift. “Haha, that’s enough introductions. Since we’ll have to work together from now on, let’s discuss how to divvy up the loot.”
Once he brought up loot distribution, Amelia pulled me back by the wrist. “I need to talk to my comrade for a moment.”
Huh? Talk?

I followed along obediently, even though I was confused. Once the two of us were alone, I quietly asked, “Why do you want to talk all of a sudden? Didn’t we already decide how to distribute the loot?”
“I didn’t bring you over here to talk about the loot.”
“Then what?”
In a cautious tone, Amelia asked, “Are you okay...?”
Only then did I realize why she pulled me aside. Right, she would know why I froze back there. “I’m fine. I was a little surprised, but I won’t cause any incidents, so don’t worry.”
“I’m not asking because I’m worried about an incident...”
Huh? Then what is it?
When I stared at her, Amelia dropped it. “...Never mind. Since you say you’re fine, I shouldn’t worry about it. Let’s get back. As for the distribution, we will go with what we decided earlier.”

Pretending to finish our conversation, we returned to the center and began our official discussion of the loot, which went quickly and without a hitch. That was because we were not here to obtain an essence.
“Are you really fine with just taking mana stones?”
In return for giving all the essences to their team, it was decided we would take all the rest. “Not just mana stones—Numbers Items and Rift Stones too.”
“But we don’t even know for sure if we’ll be able to face and defeat the guardian.”
“That’s for us to figure out. Don’t worry.”
“Hmm, if you say so.” Carlton looked bewildered by the fact that our conditions were so in their favor, but he didn’t argue. That ended the issue of loot. “Yandel, come over here!”
Jeez, I really couldn’t get used to that. Every time that name was called, it made me flinch.
“Huh? I want to speak with these two...”
“You can do that later. It looked like the blade of your axe was dull earlier, so you should go sharpen it with a whetstone.”
“Huh? I think it’s fine... but okay!”

As soon as the conversation about loot was over, Yandel Jarku was called away by a comrade and we didn’t dare approach them. We passed the time in awkward silence, keeping a distance between our two groups.
“What are they talking about over there?”
“They’re trying to guess our rationale for not taking an essence.”
“Rationale?”

That seemed like a trivial matter to me, but now that I thought about it, it was only natural that that was what they were worried about. Saying we didn’t want any essences could be interpreted as us saying that we were strong enough not to need an essence from the third floor. That must have been nerve-wracking to them since they weren’t sure what kind of people we were.
“Bjon, what kind of people were your parents?” Amelia asked me out of the blue.
Her motives were so obvious that it made me laugh. Parents? “Are you curious about my father?”
“A little.”
“Then I’m sorry. To be honest, I don’t really know anything except that he died in the labyrinth when I was very young.”

This wasn’t a made-up explanation but the truth. And not just because I was an evil spirit, either—the original owner of this body knew very little about his father too. This was common in barbarian society. About 99 percent of the members of this tribe made a living by exploring the labyrinth, after all. It was only natural that our mortality rate was high.
“Let’s stop talking about this.”
At my firm suggestion, Amelia didn’t probe any further and began chewing on beef jerky.
A while later, the door in front of us, which had been sealed shut, began to open.
“Looks like the other portals have closed too.”
It was time to start exploring the Rift.

The Hundred-Color Temple was a competitive-type Rift. Only one team could enter the boss room, and that was determined on a first-come, first-served basis. In that sense, we were off to a good start. Thanks to us fulfilling the five-person requirement early on, we were able to discuss and deal with issues like loot distribution in advance.
“Okay, let’s go then. Ah, but who will go first?”
Jeez, if you were going to waste time on the formation, you should have done it earlier.
“I’ll go first.”
“Ah! Then I’ll take the next—”
“Yandel! Come over here. There could be monsters that come at us from the rear.”
“O-Okay!”

When I took point, our battle formation naturally took shape behind me. Jarku was in the very back, and the other three were in the center. Of course, the formation didn’t matter much. This was the third-floor Rift, after all, and with a difficulty of five people.
I should clear it quickly and leave as soon as possible before something troublesome happens.

I marched through the open door with that determination driving me, and a stone chamber with the same structure as the temple from earlier appeared. The size of the room was similar, but this time there was only one stone statue inside.
Shaaaaaa.
The light pouring from the blue jewel in the statue’s hand began to spread through the chamber like fog.
A boss-type monster from the get-go.
After using the color to confirm what kind of room this was, I cracked my neck and stomped into the fog of light.
Carlton was startled by this and shouted out a warning. “H-Hey! You don’t know what’s going to come out!”
Hmm, so. You guys don’t know all that much about this Rift.
Seeing as they knew there was a competitive element, I’d hoped they would know this too. But given their reaction, it seemed they’d only heard about what kind of place this was in passing.
Boom.

Just then, a huge shadow appeared from beyond the fog. It was bipedal, and almost fifteen feet tall—a Blue-Armored Colossus. Normally, this was a mid-level boss-type monster who should only be hunted down by five third-and fourth-floor adventurers. But when all was said and done, this guy was just a third-floor Rift monster. The experience points it provided were no greater than a rank six’s, and its Strength was lower than a rank five. Even if it was a mini-boss, it was nothing compared to an actual rank-five monster like a Troll.
“Behe—”
Oh, right, I can’t say that.
“Oohgahhh!” I let out a primitive cry and dashed forward.

“Wait! We need to fight together—” Carlton was saying something back there, but I had no reason to pay him any mind. Rather than try to hide my strength, it would make things easier for both parties if I openly flaunted it.
Giantization.
First, after matching my opponent’s weight class, I jumped up and closed the distance between us in an instant.
Leap. Swing.
Then I sent a full Swing at it with all my might.
Chomp!
This basic combo snapped the Blue-Armored Colossus’ neck, leaving it at a crooked angle.
“W-What power...!”
Praise poured in from the newbies behind me, but I had a bitter taste in my mouth. Was this the pain of a tank? Even at my current strength, I still hadn’t been able to get a one-hit kill.
Jeez, so embarrassing. I should’ve just left it to the damager.
“Emily!” Just as I was shouting for her, I sensed a presence behind me.
Stab.
A dagger brimming with aura pierced the heart of the Colossus.
Chomp!
Then the Colossus disappeared in a burst of light, and the fog filling our surroundings cleared up. The entire thing was over within three seconds of the battle starting.
“A-An aura...”
“Why are these people on the third floor...?”
The newbies from twenty years in the past started to expose themselves as the newbies they were. It seemed they were only realizing then and there that they’d just boarded the express bus.
“What are you doing? Hurry up.”
“Oh, c-coming...!”
The third-floor Rift had a stage structure. Clearing one room opened up another, and only the team that got through all the stages the fastest earned the right to enter the boss room.
Chomp!

After clearing the first room in three seconds, Amelia and I exerted our true skills to clear the rest of the stages at high speed. Unlike the first stage, though, we were rarely able to finish everything in a few seconds. For every boss-type monster, there was also a quantity-type.
“Oohgahhh!”

Monsters poured out for a set period, laid down traps, and used psychological abilities on us. As rooms of various concepts flew by, the difficulty of the stages went up. This was what made the Hundred-Color Temple unique. Occupants were bestowed status conditions each time they cleared a stage, or permanent buffs were given to the monsters that would appear in the next stage. You normally wouldn’t charge through it blindly like this.
“Wait! I’ve heard about that symbol before. There’s something hidden in this place that can lift the curses on us...”

As per Carlton’s advice, the standard strategy for clearing the Hundred-Color Temple was to activate the hidden features in each room to get rid of the status effects. There were hints like that placed openly in each room too. At each fork in the road, you could use the symbols to find the rooms where you could lift the curses.
“Never mind, I’m not in the mood for that.”
“What do you mean ‘the mood for that’? What kind of bizarre—”
“You talk a lot. Just follow.”
Anything that took even the slightest bit of extra time was skipped. I judged that we’d have no problem clearing it even with a few extra hurdles. I was steamrolling through the Rift like a beast.
“Emily, why won’t this door open?”
“It’s a characteristic of the Gold Room. I don’t know the reason, but you have to wait three hours for it to open.”
“Oh, is that so?”
It was only when we arrived at the Rift’s midpoint that we regrouped to rest.
“Are you going to rest here?” My question carried the underlying suggestion that it might be more comfortable for us to sit far apart from each other, as we’d been doing earlier.
Carlton smiled ruefully. “It’s not like there’s any point.”
Hmm, that was true, but I honestly didn’t expect him to come out and admit it.
When I chuckled, Carlton apologized. “I’m sorry. At first, we considered you suspicious. We thought you might stab us in the back.”
“But not anymore?”
“That’s right.”
“Your reason?”

“If you two had bad intentions, we would have died a long time ago. It’s not like you don’t have the ability to get through this Rift without the three of us.” Carlton gave a logical reason, then added, “More importantly, you don’t seem like people who would do that.”
“Is that a gut feeling?”
“That’s right. Not mine, but Yandel’s.”
Carlton’s gaze landed on the barbarian warrior sitting on the ground munching on beef jerky. Looking at him now, I noticed his side profile looked kind of like mine.
“Get some rest.” After concluding my short conversation with Carlton, I got up from my seat and went up to Jarku.

“Oh, what brings you here? Ah, do you want some?” Jarku smiled innocently as soon as I arrived and handed me some jerky. I accepted it and shoved it in my mouth. There was no need to take off my helmet. I had it made so that the mouth visor could move up and down in anticipation of this very situation.
“Isn’t that thing uncomfortable? I don’t think I could last a day in that since it’s so stuffy.”
“It’s fine once you get used to it.”
“Haha! That’s the adaptability of a human everyone keeps talking about!” Jarku laughed heartily, then lay down on his backpack. Then he asked me an unexpected question. “Bjon, do you have children?”
“Is that so? I do.”
“What’s their name?”
“Bjorn. Bjorn, son of me, Yandel.”
So, you really are the father of this body.
More importantly, as the clear evidence was laid out in front of me, I felt my heart tightening.
“What do you think? Isn’t it a pretty good name?”
“...I think so.”
After that, Jarku led a one-sided conversation for a long while. Most of it was about his child, and I silently listened to him go on.
Thump.

As I listened to his tone get brighter and brighter, I ended up not being able to maintain eye contact, so I averted my gaze. When I did, I spotted Amelia watching me from a short distance away with a pitying look in her eyes. Thanks to that, I was finally able to identify the emotion weighing down my heart.
“Hehe, he’s going to become a great warrior. A child of her blood and mine—”
“Stop!”
“Huh?”
“Stop. I need to go...”
It was guilt.

chapters.title: Chapter 300: Evil Spirit (4)
paragraphs: I was suddenly reminded of my first day in this world.
“An evil spirit resided in the soul of Oreum, son of Kadua.”

That day, the tribe’s chief decapitated the player standing next to me with a terrifying axe, and my struggle to survive began. Of course, at the time, I didn’t know what I knew now. Because this whole world was my enemy, I had to be wary of everyone I came across.
“I thought you were an NPC. I never would have done all that if I had known.”
Just like Jencia, who regarded everyone as an NPC, I didn’t have room in my heart to sympathize with their hatred.
Squeeze.
But I got it now.
“So, it was you...”
The emotion in the chieftain’s eyes as he looked at Oreum, son of Kadua, had been sadness.
“Isn’t it disgusting that these evil spirits are among us, pretending to be people?”

The anger burning in the citizens gathered in the plaza to watch the execution of evil spirits had been born of anxiety. Of course it was. Imagine if one day, suddenly, an evil spirit took over the body of one of your loved ones and they became a completely different person. Could there be anything more terrifying than that? It was only natural to hate them. Even for me, if an evil spirit entered the body of Missha, Raven, Mr. Bear, Erwen, or Ainar, I would feel devastated too.
“Bjorn, it’s almost time.”
“...So it’s already that time. Okay.” I slowly got up from my spot in the corner. The feeling that there was a stone weighing down my heart remained unchanged.
Don’t be foolish now. This changes nothing. Feelings are fleeting. I need to finish my job as soon as possible and get out of here.

When the time came, the stone door that wouldn’t budge earlier opened up and we were able to continue exploring the Rift. White-Armored Guards, Green-Armored Vanguards, Silver Prophets—new types of monsters appeared in each room, and experience points continued to accumulate. Essences also dropped occasionally, but it seemed Amelia hadn’t been able to memorize all the hundred or so essences that could be obtained in the Hundred-Color Temple.
“Do you know what kind of ability this essence holds?” Every time an essence dropped, Carlton and his team asked us for advice.

Surprisingly, Amelia kindly explained what she knew. “It’s the essence of the Judge of Blue-White Palace. From what I can remember, it’s one of the rare bow and projectile-related essences that have high Strength.”
“Hmm, so she says. Eimbern, what will you do?”
“Strength, huh? I actually wanted to increase my bow’s tension, so this works out. I like the skill it comes with too. I think I can make good use of this. I’ll take it.”
Eimbern took one this time, and Carlton and Jarku each took one earlier. They had already picked up three rank-six essences just by following behind us, but I wasn’t necessarily upset about it.
“Haha! Thank you! This has been easy thanks to you guys!”
“...No need to thank us.”
Not only were they useless items to us, but this wasn’t nearly enough compensation to make things up to him, anyway. It also didn’t change the fact that he would one day die in the labyrinth.
“Anyway, I think we’re gradually nearing the end.”
After continuing to carry out our raid for a long while, we eventually reached the boss room. Seeing as the jewel in the statue’s hand wasn’t lit up, it seemed we had arrived first.
“But how do you open this door?”
“Step aside.” Amelia destroyed the statue in one blow. Rather than a random act, this was one of the quickest ways to progress. If you did this, the door opened, and an angry voice rang out.
Who did she come here with to know all this?

While I once again grew curious about Amelia’s past, an imposing voice resounded from beyond the stone gate. “This is the resting place of the noble sacrifice. Intruders will pay for their sins with blood.”
What did you say, Mr. Rank Five?
I’d seen this intro several times during the game so I just listened disinterestedly while chewing on jerky as the stone door began to open.
“C-Can I go in?”
“Someone just spoke! I-Is it not a monster?” The trio was greatly intimidated by the voice just now and showed clear signs of nervousness.

Well, it wasn’t like I didn’t get it. The guardian of the Hundred-Color Temple was a rank-five high-rank mutant who even had a random monster’s essence. Since there were almost no high-rank mutants below the third floor, it was unlikely they’d ever run into a monster that could speak like a human.
“Bjon, how long are you going to stand there like that?”
“Oh, I was distracted for a second.”

To be precise, I was remembering the Bloody Citadel. The Vampire I encountered back then was also a rank-five high-rank mutant bastard, but that had been a time I’d had no essences. Of course, the boss here was still much stronger than that Vampire. We had just fought through an entire labyrinth to reach it and even got cursed along the way, while this boss would be equipped with all kinds of buffs.
Anyway, I wonder which essence we’re dealing with here.
When we stepped beyond the stone door, it closed with a bang.
Boom!
“A forest...?”

Unlike the previous rooms, which were stone chambers made of marble, the ground here was covered in bushes and the trees scattered around bore fruit. That was not to say the landscape beyond the door was the outside world. No, it was a large dome-shaped interior decorated with an artificial garden. There were a total of five doors on the circular outer wall including the one we just entered. If we ended up losing the fight, one of those doors would probably open for another team to take on the challenge. Well, I was sure that wouldn’t happen, though.
“You guys stay back.”
“This is a guardian, will you two be okay on your own...?”
“We’ll call you if we need you.”
“...All right.”
Okay, that settled that problem. Now that the passengers on the bus were all seated, Amelia and I made our way to the cabin located in the center of the forest. I guessed that triggered the alarm.
Boom!

A knight in gray armor and on horseback fell from the sky and blocked our path. His name: Knight of the End. Although he was on horseback, he wasn’t classified as a large monster. His height was about 5′9″, and he had the proportions of an ordinary human. He was much smaller in size than the Colossus we met earlier, but this wasn’t a monster to be underestimated. In most games, the smaller enemies were the more intimidating ones.
Whip.
Soon the knight on horseback swung a weapon that looked like a cross between a spear and greatsword in the air, acting tough. “Wild dogs of the empire, seized by greed. I will punish you today.”
Still saying gibberish, huh?
“Emily, do you know what that means?”
“I don’t know, either.”
Is that true?
Step.

I first used Giantization to match his weight class before taking a step forward. Right at that moment, the Spirit Horse, the rank-seven beast-type monster that the Knight of the End was riding on, huffed and charged at us.
Neigh!
Well, a Spirit Horse is usually a trash monster that can be taken down with just one Swing... but its stats are inflated here.
The Spirit Horse in the boss room was given the Knight of the End’s stats. Put simply, it wasn’t a monster that could be killed with one or two hits.
Ah, and I can’t even use Swing right now.
I’d received various curses on the way here and Swing ended up getting sealed. Of course, this was a minor issue. We had a damager who was much more efficient than me, so why would I need to attack?
Boom!

Determination fueling me as I lifted my shield, I blocked the knight’s attempt at stabbing us from atop the horse. It was quite a heavy hit. I was starting to see why the cavalry were considered the best soldiers in the Middle Ages. There were no superhumans with Giantization there back then, right?
“Doable.” Having not conceded an inch of ground to this guy, I cried out, “Emi—!”
Ah, she’s already in the air.
Slice!
Before I could even finish speaking, a shimmering aura sliced off the horse’s neck, and that was all.
An aura is definitely a cheat.
The Spirit Horse helplessly turned into specks of light and vanished.
Slump!
It was time to start Phase Two.

The Knight of the End fight was divided into three phases. In Phase One, he ran rampant on the Spirit Horse he’d summoned with the active skill Servant. Then, after the Spirit Horse was released, a ground battle unfolded. Starting at Phase Two, the Knight of the End used the skill of a random essence under rank five.
...But why isn’t this bastard using his skill?

No matter how long we waited, he didn’t whip out the skill from his extra essence. So we just continued the boss fight like normal and moved on to Phase Three once Amelia shoved a knife in his throat.

“Immortality is a choice and a promise.” The Knight of the End was resurrected with a cringey line. This was the effect of the passive skill Chivalry, a high-risk skill that destroyed all equipment you were wearing at the time you took lethal damage and restored your HP in proportion to the amount of time the equipment was worn.
At first, I wondered what kind of useless skill this was.

Left with no equipment, the Knight of the End was weaker than usual at the start of Phase Three, but the same usually went for the player too. If their specs were on par, their MP likely also bottomed out around Phase Three after taking all sorts of damage. During my first attempt at clearing this Rift, we continued to attack each other with regular blows in what ended up being a long dogfight, and my team eventually got wiped out.
Well, with our specs now, this will be a piece of cake.
“I cannot lose.”
Uh, what?
Just then, the Knight of the End suddenly grew in size. I was a bit stunned.
To think it would be Giantization.
I never imagined the high-rank mutant essence he had would be the essence of an Orc Hero.
No wonder he didn’t use it earlier.

Only then did it click for me why this guy hadn’t used his skill in the previous phases. Giantization was not an ability you could typically use while wearing equipment. The stat boost it gave you was huge, though.
“I cannot lose...!” Using Giantization, the guy started attacking me in a mad frenzy. Of course, that wasn’t going to work.
What is growing bigger going to do for you? Your stats and size are still inferior to mine.
Squeeze.
After grabbing his fist, I pulled him in and grappled him down.
Stab.
Amelia’s dagger dealt the finishing blow.
Shaaaaaa!

Then the guy turned into particles of light and fluttered away without so much as a parting line. It was always like this, but this was the tensest moment for me every time. I stared straight ahead without blinking.
Please, something come out.
Despite my hopes, there was no floating essence.
Plop.
No Rift Stone fell to the ground with a thud, either. Instead, a piece of equipment came into view.
“A numbered item...” After confirming that the equipment on the ground was a hammer, I froze.
Wait, what is this? ...Holy, this showed up here?

Flinching for a moment, I rushed over and picked up the hammer. I wasn’t sure about the grip, but looking at its masculine color and rugged design, I was certain. This was No. 87: Kraul’s Demon Grinder.

This was an expensive double-digit Numbers Item you couldn’t even hope to get a glimpse of outside the Sky Auction House in the royal capital. Not to mention it was the final weapon I had decided on for myself after I took the Ogre’s essence. And this thing decided to appear on the third-floor Rift? ‘Jackpot’ wasn’t even a strong enough word to describe it.
God damn it.

If only this weren’t twenty years in the past. As an efficiency freak, I was disappointed, but this was still a good thing, my first stroke of luck in a long time. Yes, that was indisputable. Except, as soon as I grabbed the hammer, my brain started to buzz with loud thoughts.

Ha... how do I take this with me? If I dig a hole in the ground where no one will find it, will it still be fine twenty years in the future? Wait, what if someone takes it? Then I’m just screwed. Hmm, should I just sell it? Yeah, I can just sell it and use that money to buy an expensive essence or something at the auction house before I leave. That’s the reason why I was gathering all that equipment in the first place...

While these thoughts ran through my mind in a continual loop, Carlton came up and congratulated me. “Congratulations. It’s a pity it wasn’t an essence that came out, but that must be our greed talking. Actually, this makes me feel a lot better! I’m glad you guys got something out of all this too!”
Uh, this item is too valuable to call just “something.”

It would be best not to say that, though. From the looks of it, even Amelia didn’t suspect I was holding a double-digit Numbers Item. I decided to worry about that later, though. The portal had just opened too.
Whooom!
Carlton glanced at the portal that had appeared in front of the cabin in the center of the forest and asked, “So what are you guys going to do now?”
“We’re going to leave after a bit. We want to look around for the remaining time.” To be precise, there were a few things we wanted to take with us.
But did he catch my drift from that alone? “I guess you’re going to look for the Arrangement of Gabrielius, then.”
“Yes.”
“Then what about the white fruit on the tree over there? It clearly looks out of the ordinary.”
Oh, that... He was right about it being a hidden feature, but it was more like a joke item. How could I say this in a way that he wouldn’t try to eat it?
While I was pondering this, Amelia explained in my stead. “It’s a white fruit. When consumed, it takes the stats of an essence in the person’s possession and randomly changes them.”

Her explanation was short but not wrong. White fruit changed the nature of an essence upon consumption. The skills remained the same, but the base stats attached to the essence changed to a random value that matched its rank. It wasn’t an item anyone in their right mind would consume because there were thousands of tiny, intricate stats in this game. There was a significant chance that good stats such as Strength and Agility would become almost useless or get switched out with low-value stats like Greed or Obsession.
“So, what will you guys do?”
“We’re going to head straight out. I’m sure our comrades that got left behind will be waiting outside.”
“I see.”

After saying goodbye to Carlton, the elven archer approached me. “First, let me say thank you. We undoubtedly couldn’t have gotten all the way here on our own. We would have suffered a great deal more.”
“You guys just got lucky.”
“Luck, huh? Well, it’s definitely extremely difficult to meet adventurers like you in a Rift. Please excuse our initial wariness. We’ve experienced a run of bad luck lately.”
“Bad luck?”
“It’s hard to explain. It’s not that anyone’s done anything wrong, but no matter what we do, our bad luck keeps getting in the way and turning things into a mess.”
Hmm, really? There’s only one possibility that comes to mind.
I debated whether to say this or not before biting the bullet and opening my mouth. “You said there’s a guy named Hans on your team.”
“I did.”
“Take him out. You will have some better luck that way.”
The elven archer looked momentarily dazed, then let out an awkward laugh. “Haha, that’s a funny joke.”
Nope, I’m being 100 percent sincere right now.

chapters.title: Chapter 301: Evil Spirit (5)
paragraphs: “Bjon! I may have only stood back and watched this time, but this was a fun expedition! Let’s meet again if we get the chance!”
“...Yeah.”
After a brief farewell, Carlton’s group exited the Rift. It was time for us to get back to work as well.
“Now, let’s go. There could be something more!”
“...Are you thinking of wandering around without a plan?”
No, I plan to pretend to wander around without a plan and get everything I want.
“Follow me. I know a few things.”
Oh, if you say so.

I followed the experienced Amelia out of the boss room and traveled back through the other stages. At that point, we located two hidden items: the Fragment of Earth, which raised the user’s Earth Resistance and Physical Resistance by one point each; and the Book of Souls, which gave the user three additional experience points. Amelia said she already used them so I took them for myself, thus ending our search for hidden items in the Hundred-Color Temple, as those were all the spirit-type items there were. The rest required distortion magic if you wanted to take them outside of the Rift to sell.
Then since I’ve got everything I need...
“Amelia, why don’t we stay a bit instead of leaving immediately?”
“Why?”
“To be honest, I am quite tired from sleeping only three hours every day. Why don’t we get a good rest here?”

Amelia looked at me with disapproval. It was obvious what she was thinking. At a point when a lot of time had already elapsed and the labyrinth would close tomorrow, she must have been wondering if we really needed to rest now.
Tsk, we already achieved our goal days ago. Why is she so greedy?
But since whining wasn’t my style, I gave her a reasonable excuse for a break. “My head is all jumbled up, so I need some time.”

“Ah...” Amelia gave me an understanding look and yielded to my request. “Fine. We’ll rest before we leave. Let me know when you’re ready.” After all was said and done, Amelia was rather kindhearted when it came to things like these.
“Thanks, Amelia.”
“Just rest.”
Amelia took out her sleeping bag and lay on the floor, and I made a spot for myself about ten feet away from her. Then I began the official count.
Let’s see...

I’d obtained 156 experience points for first kills in the Hundred-Color Temple. When you added the one-point kill bonus for a high-rank mutant, a Guardian Kill Bonus of three, and three more for Book of Souls, that number went up to 163. Of course, even adding all that EXP up, I still had a long way to go to get to level seven.
If all goes well, I’ll reach level seven in the mid-to-late portion of the sixth floor.
I couldn’t deny that my character was getting closer and closer to completion. I’d also already gotten the Demon Grinder.
I need to figure out how to take this with me...
Just as I was thinking this, Amelia said, “Yandel, there’s something I want to ask you.”
“Ah! Is it about the numbered item? I-I don’t know what it is either, but I liked the weight of it so I’m going to use—”
“It’s a different question.”
Oh, that’s not it?
I had been worrying about what to do if she asked to split the hammer.
“You... don’t want to change it?”
“What do you mean?”
“What happened to Yandel Jarku, your father.”
Oh, that... Well, I was trying my best not to think about it.
“It’s possible you might be able to save him.”
“How can I, when I don’t even know how and when exactly he died except that it happened when I was young?”
“If you want, after I finish up my work here, I can go back to Rafdonia and help—”
“No need.” I cut her off, voice firm. “I don’t want that.”
“How come?” Amelia asked, sounding genuinely curious.

Well, this probably seemed strange from her perspective, since she didn’t know that I was an evil spirit. “If the future could be changed by something as simple as that, the fact that we met here would have changed his fate as well.”

The future couldn’t change. Amelia seemed to be aware of that to some extent too. But since Auril Gavis had confirmed it for me and I had also confirmed it through Raven and Dwalkie myself, she was likely giving the idea less weight than I did.
Amelia jumped up. “Could be changed? What do you mean by that?”
I thought it over for a short moment before answering honestly, telling her about my attempts to change Dwalkie’s and Raven’s futures, and how they all ended up as failures.
After hearing my explanation, Amelia pursed her lips in denial. “Impossible...”
I decided to be blunt. “Amelia, didn’t you kind of sense this too?”
“Sense what...?”

“If you didn’t, then what was that about the other day? Why were you surprised when you saw the name Nivelles Enze, and what was with the strange look you gave me when I came downstairs wearing this helmet?”
“That’s...”
“Didn’t you already realize it yourself? No matter what we do, the past won’t change. No, rather, all of these events flowed the way they did because of us.”

Amelia said nothing. She just clenched her fists, clearly holding something back. There was a brief beat of silence before her lips parted again. “So, you’re going to give up? Without even trying, when you may be able to save your father?” Her voice sounded the same as usual, but I picked up on a hint of aggression below the surface.
Maybe that was why I got a bit aggressive back. “I’ve never seen my father’s face before, anyway.”
“So, you don’t care about him enough, is that what you’re saying?”
“...Yeah.”
“I see.” But despite her supposed understanding, Amelia tutted. It seemed she was disappointed in me.
Ha... maybe I shouldn’t have brought this topic up to begin with. It seemed like we’d gotten closer these past few days and now it’s all ruined.

After that, we just took our break without saying a word. About five hours later, I got up after a restful sleep and proposed we leave, figuring that would be better than walking on eggshells like this in here.
“Wait, can we stop by there?” I asked.
“If you want.”

Once we arrived back at the boss room to take the portal outside, I approached the hut located behind it out of simple curiosity. In the game, this hut was part of the terrain and couldn’t be entered.
Oh, the door opens.

The hut opened with a creak, and I scanned the interior. I had a strange feeling of déjà vu. There was one bookshelf, a dining table, a carpet, and a stove. By all accounts, there was nothing special about the space. It was an ordinary, stereotypical hut. But the room’s size, structure, and the layout of its furniture reminded me of somewhere else without my even needing to take a closer look.
It’s almost exactly the same as there...?

The place I was referring to was the only safe zone in the Witch’s Forest on the third floor: the Witch’s Hut. The same place where Missha and I took a break and summoned the Lord of Chaos after offering up human firewood.
“You can choose to look around if you want to, but I didn’t find an Arrangement of Gabrielius when I searched the place last time I was here.”

Since Amelia was urging me to hurry up, I just briefly checked the books on the bookshelf and came back out. The books were all blank, by the way, and the titles were all written in an ancient language so I couldn’t read them either. Maybe if I brought Raven back later, she’d be able to find something.
“If you’re done, let’s go,” said Amelia.
“Oh, I’ll go out first, just in case.”
We stood in front of the portal. Once we went through it, we would return to the same spot we were at when we first entered the Rift.
Step.
As the tank, I set foot through the portal first.
Shaaa.
The light of the portal enveloped my body and the world around me went white. Then slowly, my sight returned. But what was this?
“Nice, you’re finally here!” A group of adventurers was standing in front of the portal like they’d been waiting for us.

“So, did you get a Numbers Item—” The group and I made eye contact and both sides flinched simultaneously. “Uh, what the heck? Iron Mask?” This was the team of adventurers from earlier that worked under the lord of Noark.
“Ha, what a coincidence! I never thought you were the one these three bastards ran into inside.”
“Three bastards...?” Subconsciously following Beck’s line of sight, I immediately froze.
Beep...
For some reason, my ears were ringing.
What is this?

My mind went momentarily blank, but my brain continued to perceive and analyze the incoming visual information in real-time. Carlton Drek, Eimbern Berta Garcia, and Yandel, third son of Jarku... the bodies of the three men who’d exited through the portal several hours ago were lying on the floor. No, it wasn’t just those three. There were two more bodies. I could guess who they belonged to.
“Oh no! Lemud and Hans didn’t get in!”
Those must have been the two people who had been waiting outside. So how did this happen?
“...Bjon.” Amelia came out of the portal a moment later and gripped my wrist once she realized what was going on. Was she telling me to suppress any volatile urges? That seemed to be the case.
Beeep.
Ugh, so noisy.
I closed my eyes for a while, trying to somehow restore my usual calm. When I opened them again, everything in front of me remained the same.
“Since this is our second time running into each other during this quest, I guess we’re meant to be!” Beck smiled good-naturedly and got up from the body he was sitting on like a chair.
“What are you guys doing here?” Amelia asked Beck.

“Well, we started searching the area as soon as the Rift opened and saw these two here.” Beck poked what seemed to be Lemud and Hans’ bodies with his foot. “I captured them and found out only three of their comrades made it inside. Then, after waiting a while, these three came out.”

Beck then shrugged, omitting what happened next, and Amelia did not ask any further questions. It was obvious, anyway. They probably killed these three after getting the necessary information out of them, like the fact that the guardian had dropped a Numbers Item at the end. Things like that.
Beeeeeep...
Amelia and Beck conversed. This place was too noisy, though, making it hard for me to hear. All I could do was stand there blankly, remembering.
“Ah, is that a little too hard for humans? Just call me Yandel Jarku!”
I knew he was going to die, but... I didn’t know it would be because of me.
If it weren’t for me...

Yandel Jarku and his teammates would have all entered the Rift together, meaning his other comrades would not have been found by these guys while waiting for the rest of their party. As a result, he... no, they wouldn’t have died. They would have continued on their journey. And perhaps...
“Hehe, he’s going to become a great warrior. A child of her blood and mine...”
Yandel Jarku would have seen his child grow up. It was even possible they could have entered the labyrinth together as adults.
If it weren’t for me.
Then there would never have been an evil spirit dwelling in Bjorn Yandel’s body.
Beeeeeeeeep...
The ringing in my ears grew worse. It was a kind of coping mechanism, a way of drowning out the voice echoing inside me, even if only just a little. An alarm system for a coward.
Squeeze.
Although I put all my strength into my balled-up fists, blood still rushed to my head.
Beeeeeep...
If only it weren’t for me...
Dwalkie wouldn’t have died. Even if he became an adventurer in the future, he never would have gone somewhere as dangerous as that place on the fourth floor.
Beeeeeeeeep...
If I hadn’t come...
Dwalkie’s love story may have come true. One day, the two of them might have met as teammates and naturally progressed into a relationship in which they healed each other’s hurts.
Maybe.
Perhaps.
If I weren’t here.
Beeeeeeeeep...
My ears—no, my head was numb.
“But why is Iron Mask so quiet?”
“Bjon.”
It was like homework I had been putting off all this time, always saying feelings were nothing more than feelings instead of dealing with them head-on.
“Bjon, snap out of it.”

Numerous emotions that I had been burying in a corner of my heart and ignoring came flooding back to me all at once. I had to do something. Knowing it would be hypocrisy to say this was for someone else, I knew I had to do this for myself.
I forced my lips to part. “Amelia.” I said her real name, not the pseudonym “Emily.” Was that enough for her to figure out what was about to happen?
“These are men who work under the lord of the castle. Restrain yourself,” she hissed, her grip on my wrist getting stronger. Of course, it didn’t make much of a difference.
You’re an Agility character.
“Bjon...”

When I shook off Amelia and stepped forward, Beck smirked. “Haha, looks like Iron Mask is angry. I’m not asking you to give it to me for free. I’m just asking for a look at what you’ve got. We’ve been waiting here for a long time, after all.”
Although I didn’t really hear the conversation the two of them had, I could figure it out through context clues.
So, you’re curious about this, huh?
Click.
I took out the hammer I was keeping in sub-space—No. 87: Kroul’s Demon Grinder.

“A hammer? There’s a numbered item like this...” Beck mumbled to himself before trailing off. Then his expression changed. “W-Wait. Can I take a closer look? I just want to see if it’s the item that I’m thinking of.”
“Go ahead.” I took another step forward and Beck took a cautious step as well.
Just when the distance was perfect, he stopped and said, “I-It really is that item! Did that really appear in there?”
“Yes.”
I’m glad that sated your curiosity.
Smack!
Now die.

chapters.title: Chapter 302: Evil Spirit (6)
paragraphs: Smack!
Immediately after I struck Beck’s bald head with the Demon Grinder with all my might, his skull and scalp burst at the same time, leaving blood spurting from all kinds of holes.

It was a successful surprise attack. However, as you’d expect from a group that had been through all sorts of hardships, the rest were quick to react even though their leader’s head had been blown off.
The archer stepped back and widened the distance between us. “You bastard!”
The close combatants approached quickly and blocked my left and right sides in unison, like a pair of annoying cockroaches.
Whooom!

I used Giantization and brought my hammer down on the shield-bearing warrior in front. Surprisingly, the guy didn’t even try to dodge. He just raised his shield following the hammer’s trajectory and shouted, “Stab!”
So, your plan is to block me while the others stab me in the side?
Now that I was getting a better look at it, the shield had a pretty nice sheen.
It’s adamantium.
It looked like he was relying on that expensive shield to protect him, but there were better items than that in the world.
Suffer, then.
The hammer and shield collided, resulting in an explosive bang. The guy’s shield was slightly dented, but otherwise fine.
Crunch!

Meanwhile, the guy actually holding the shield was spurting blood from every hole like a can of soda that had been punctured by a needle. That was because, since I didn’t use Swing just then, I couldn’t show off the full potential of my new double-digit Numbers Item. With Swing, my damage would increase by 500 percent when using blunt weapons, and my Soul Power consumption would be reduced by half. Plus, when brought down, I’d get a 50 percent bonus to Armor Penetration.
Plop.
The guy dropped to the ground with his eyeballs popped out thanks to the force of my blow.
Who’s next?
Flick.

When I shifted my gaze to my third target, he took a step back. Taking a quick look to the side, I saw the archer doing the same. Were they trying to run? If so, that was a bit funny, because I had zero intention of letting them go.
Transcendence.
I quickly recited the command for the active skill I had acquired from Storm Gush.
Eye of the Storm.
Boom!
When I stomped on the ground, a vortex began to swirl around me, but it was different from the vortex the Storm Gush used. That was thanks to Transcendence.
Whooom!
Eye of the Storm no longer pulled in enemies within a fifteen-foot radius. Instead, it attacked a designated target within a sixty-foot radius. I pulled in one right in front of me.
“Aghhh!”
Just like that.
Crunch!
That made three. But I wasn’t satisfied with that and looked to the final target trying to flee, the archer. If he got too far, I planned to follow with Leap.
Stab.
But Amelia took care of the archer. She was a very practical woman. Like it or not, since things had already gone sideways, she would have determined it was best to kill and silence everyone.
“Ah, ugh, uh, h-help...”
Smack!
Amelia then struck the child next to the archer, Jencia, on the back of the neck and knocked her out before coming back over to me. “That was a foolish thing to do,” she said shortly.
“Because they work for the lord of the castle?”
“No, because now we have to kill that child because of you.”
...Is that how it works? But she was definitely alive in the future?
“We would have had plenty of opportunities to kill them, even if it weren’t today. Even if you didn’t step forward now, I was planning to kill them someday too.”
“...You were?”
“I feel responsibility for this incident as well.”
Responsibility, huh? Ugh, I don’t know. My thoughts are all jumbled up.
Beeeeeep.
Although I’d beaten them all to death, the ringing in my ears remained. Rather than feeling refreshed, I felt even more suffocated.
“Why did you do something as rash as that? You said you’d never even seen your father’s face before.”

That was true. I had also been well aware the entire time that even if I beat all these bastards to death right now, that wouldn’t make up for what had happened to him. Honestly, I couldn’t have been more hypocritical if I’d tried.
“Just because.” There was no better way to express it. “I just... felt like doing it.”
“...I see.” Surprisingly, Amelia didn’t get angry. She just stared at me in silence.

I turned my head to avoid Amelia’s gaze. In doing so, I saw Yandel Jarku’s body. Besides the injuries he suffered in battle, his corpse looked like it had been messed with, like it had been treated like a toy.
Squeeze.
I clenched both fists and recalled the short conversation we’d had inside the Rift.
“Did you say your name is Bjon? Well, Bjon, you should have a child as soon as possible. It’s a sad thing, the thought of leaving nothing behind.”
“...Is it?”
“Yeah, I didn’t realize it before I had a child, either.”

Jarku then said that a child of your blood was like another you, which was such a mysterious thing. After having a child of his own, he began, for the first time, to wish for something other than just becoming an excellent warrior himself someday.
“Hehe, he’s going to become a great warrior.”
And so I ran away.
“Stop!”
“Huh?”
“Stop. I need to go...”

I’d realized something profound from that single sentence—that even if I lived with the name Bjorn Yandel, saved countless people, and became a revered hero in the city, I could not be forgiven. Even if none of this had been my intention.
No matter what anyone said, the facts of the matter wouldn’t change. In the end, I was an evil spirit—one that had robbed this barbarian warrior of his most precious wish.
“Looks like you’ve calmed down a bit,” Amelia said as I continued to stare at Yandel Jarku’s dead body.

She wasn’t wrong. As the saying went, time was the best medicine. Before long, the ringing in my ears subsided and the tremors stopped. It was now time to figure out how to fix the situation I’d put us in.
I looked at Jencia’s unconscious body. “Do we really have to kill her?”
“Is there another way? If this child returns alive, the lord of the castle will know what we did.”
Ha, goddamn it.
When I let out a sigh of frustration, Amelia asked, “Is there a reason not to kill her?”
“She’s... still young.”

Even as I gave that answer, I second-guessed myself. Why was I looking for a way not to kill her? After all, I knew the future. After living a hellish life, this child would become an adult whose body was taken over by an evil spirit. So it was actually better to kill her now.
God damn it.

The curses came freely. What the hell was I thinking? That since she was going to die someday anyway, killing her now changed nothing? Or was it actually that killing her would prove Auril Gavis was wrong?
I firmly shook my head. “We can’t kill her. Let’s find a solution.”
“That’s unlike you.”
“What do you know about me?”
You don’t even know I’m an evil spirit.

I didn’t mean to be so harsh with my reply, but deep down I knew the truth. There was no doubt that if I were my usual self, I might have made a different choice here. But at least today, I didn’t want to do that. Today had already been particularly hard. Even if this decision meant complying with fate, I couldn’t bear to do anything else.
“It’s as you said. I guess I don’t know you very well. I didn’t know you were so weak. If you can’t do it, I will.”
“Stop.” I grabbed Amelia’s wrist.
“...I’d advise you to let go.”
“I said we should look for another way.”
“Another way? There is no surer way than this.”
Ugh, honestly! That’s why I’m saying we should come up with a way together... Oh, right, that!

A solution occurred to me and I quickly opened my mouth. “Wait, the pill! If we give her the medicine created by Noark’s alchemist, we can erase her memories! You said they work for the castle lord? They might have one!” I spoke with the same passion as a philosopher shouting, Eureka!
Amelia just snorted. “In the current year, we’d be in the early stages of when that medicine was developed. There’s no way these guys have something that precious on them.”
“But we should at least look!”
“...Okay, if that will make you give up.” Amelia shook off my hand. “And I’m warning you, do not grab my arm without permission again.”
Jeez, so sensitive.
With that, Amelia approached the bodies and started looting.
Okay, whether the pill turns up or not, that buys me time to think... Oh, wait.
I belatedly realized I’d made a mistake. It looked like Amelia hadn’t noticed yet, but...
That was pure foolishness.
Was it because I lost my head there? It was a mistake my normal self would have never made.
...I’ll deal with it later when she brings it up herself.
I squatted down as well, took the equipment off the corpses, and checked their backpacks. As I did so, I continued to worry about what would happen if we couldn’t find a memory removal pill.
“...She’s lucky. To think they would have something like this at this point.” A pill appeared from their bag.
Once we found the pill, everything went smoothly. Amelia hurriedly put the pill in Jencia’s mouth and we waited until she came to her senses.

“A-Ahhh! W-What is this...?!” After some time, Jencia, whose hands and feet were tied and who even had a blindfold on, regained consciousness. We quietly observed her reaction from a distance, judging that a drug from the early days could be defective. “Mister Beck! Mister Beck! H-Help me!”

Seeing as she was looking for Beck, it was clear her memory had been erased. So how much of it was gone? We were able to obtain that information through Jencia, who was muttering to herself, properly unhinged.
