“To think she forgot everything since the moment she entered the Crystal Cave. Maybe it’s because it’s in the early stages of development, but it seems like it’s more potent compared to the mass-produced ones.”
Amelia then went over to the flailing Jencia, knocked her out again, and even dosed her with sleeping pills to prevent her from waking up. That was that, then.
“The labyrinth will close soon. We just have to stay with her for a few hours.”

After moving locations, we passed the time with the sleeping Jencia. After all, you couldn’t leave a child on her own in the labyrinth. Once the labyrinth closed, Jencia would be retrieved by the lord of the castle’s men. They would try to dig up information about what happened, but she wouldn’t remember anything.
“...Um, Amelia. Sorry about earlier.” I apologized to her while we were waiting, but Amelia just ignored me like she didn’t hear anything.
After a long, awkward silence, white light rushed in from all directions and the labyrinth closed.
Shaaa!
There was no warm sensation of sun on our skin, or the usual cool breeze winding around our bodies in greeting. Only the drab underground city welcomed us.
“You’re back.”

Noark’s Dimension Square was located in the western region of the castle. From here on there were differences with Rafdonia. In the overworld, you had to pass through a checkpoint at the end of the expedition and exchange your mana stones, but currency exchange here was up to the individual.
“Come, let’s go drink!”
“What the—isn’t that the kid from Beck’s gang? Why is she here alone? Did the others kick the bucket inside?”
“Iron Molars will welcome that news. He was waiting to get at Beck, anyway.”

The adventurers who appeared in the square all dispersed to their respective destinations and the area grew quiet. Jencia, who was lying on the ground in the distance, was found by the lord of the castle’s men as expected and transported somewhere.
“We should go too.”
“Oh, right...”
We left the square as well and headed to Melta Merchant Company, Noark’s one and only merchant company and the underground plunderers’ most preferred vendor for getting rid of their equipment.

Unlike the mana stone exchange, where the line was quite short, the street in front of the merchant company was bustling with people. That was because mana stones themselves were money here, so there was no need to exchange them. The mana stone exchange here didn’t even exchange stones for money anyway, but rather food or other desired items.
“Hmm, Iron Mask and Emily. The hottest topic in town these days.”

When our turn came, we took out all the equipment we had in storage. Oh, for reference, we had removed Beck’s equipment from the pile since they’d know that we killed those guys if we pulled that out.

“...You obtained all this during this expedition?” As we began to shake out the backpacks, the worker’s expression turned increasingly blank. Although Noark was full of plunderers, I figured it wasn’t common for someone to steal so much stuff. “This will take some time. Could you please wait?”

Afterward, the staff member called over several more appraisers from the merchant company and they started settling our account together. After about ten minutes, the appraisal was done. Along with the equipment, we had twenty-one rank-four mana stones, one rank-five mana stone, and seven rank-seven mana stones. Geez, I couldn’t even get a feel for how much that was when it was worded like that.
“How much is that based on the Rafdonian Currency Exchange Office?”
“Oh, I guess you’re not familiar since this is your first time in Noark. Based on last month’s exchange rate, the total is 21.57 million stones.”

I did hear as much from Amelia, but these guys really were thieving bastards. No matter how low-quality the equipment may have been and despite not including any of the sub-space items or expandable backpacks, this was highway robbery. “Sold in the overworld, this would be worth well over seventy million stones.”
“Yes. It would, in the overworld.”
So, you have an attitude, huh?
“It’s fine. Emily, let’s take these and leave.”
“Does that mean you won’t sell?”
“Yes, I have no intention of handing these things over at that ridiculous price.”
“If you say so.”
With that, we gathered up the equipment and headed out. The staff looked disappointed, but they didn’t stop us. They probably thought we’d have no choice but to sell it to them in the end anyway.
“Let’s go to the inn, then.”
Coming out of the merchant company, we headed to the inn we were staying at. Then we took turns washing up and sat facing each other to talk.

“Since we stopped by the merchant company to show off our looted equipment, the lord of the castle will express his interest in us.” This was the reason we headed there with equipment we had no intention of selling. In truth, the lord of the castle was pretty much the owner of the merchant company. The blood-stained equipment and IDs and the numerous other pieces of evidence of our looting would soon reach his ears.
“Then we just have to wait until then.”
“Yes, for now.”
After discussing a few more topics, we changed into our everyday clothes and lay down on the beds. “If we’re done talking, I’m going to sleep. I’m tired.”
Of course, sleep did not come easily. While I was tossing and turning in bed, Amelia suddenly spoke up. “Are you sleeping?”
“No. Why?”
“I wanted to ask you something.”
A question, huh? I had a guess as to what this could be about. While reflecting on our expedition, she must have noticed that mistake from earlier.
“Ask.”
“How did you know about the Blessing of Amern?”

Oh, so that was what that medicine was called. It was my first time hearing its actual name, but I made sure not to let that show as I answered her. “Oh, that? You told me to swallow it when we met at the inn.”
“But I didn’t say that it was made by an alchemist in Noark.”
“I was curious what it was so I captured an adventurer from Noark and made them tell me before I killed them!”
“Hmm, I see. Yes, I see...”
Uh, what was that tone? It was making me anxious.
“Barbarian, first of all, the name of that pill is the Blessing of Lethe. Not the Blessing of Amern.”
Huh?

“Which means my theory was correct.” Soon, a shadow hung over the bed where I lay. When I slowly turned my head, I could see Amelia standing over me, looking down. “You didn’t lose your memory back then.”
That was checkmate. It seemed like she even continued to play ignorant despite already being aware of my mistake so that I would lower my guard. What kind of person was this manipulative?
I sighed and coolly owned up to it. “Yes. Somehow, I was the only one who was fine.”

How was it my fault if the medicine was defective? What was she going to do about it? At the time I hid the truth, worried she would come assassinate me if she found out, but there was no need for that anymore, right? Noark’s presence in the city had already been exposed.
Yeah, what do I have to hide now?

When I thought about it, this wasn’t anything to worry about. I quickly raised my upper body and stared confidently at Amelia. Yeah, my body language said, if you have something to say, then say it. But what was this? The look in her eyes was strange. It felt somehow... cold.
“...Why are you looking at me like that?”
Amelia’s voice was frigid as she replied. “Bjorn Yandel, the only people who don’t lose their memory from that medicine are evil spirits.”
Ah. Uh. Um... goddamn it.
I didn’t know that.

chapters.title: Chapter 303: Rainwales (1)
paragraphs: Noark did not reject evil spirits, so unlike aboveground, many lived there openly, their identities exposed. Judging from our previous conversation, native Amelia did not view evil spirits in a negative light either.
But the moment I admit to it, it will become my weakness for the rest of my life.

Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit. To say that was my Achilles’ heel was an understatement. It was a bomb that could destroy my entire social life and even threaten my actual life, and the button to that bomb was currently in Amelia’s hands. Of course, Amelia and I had a friendly relationship now, but no one knew what would happen later. What if things went wrong for some reason? Not only would I never get a restful night of sleep again if that were to happen, but it would definitely become a cause for anxiety even if there were no particular problems in our friendship. If she ever decided to blackmail me, I would be summoned like a servant and worked like a dog.

“Amelia Rainwales, are you insulting me?” I spoke in a low voice, like the growl of an animal. And rightfully so. Evil spirits didn’t lose their memory? That could have been a lie she made up just to feel me out. And even if that medicine really did work like that, I had to make it seem like I’d gotten a defective dose.
“And what if I am?”
“...Huh?” I’d never had anyone respond to me so confidently.
While I was busy being momentarily stunned, Amelia said, “Are you going to attack me? Without my help, it’ll be harder for you to get the items in the lord of the castle’s possession.”
“...Do not test my patience.”

Amelia snorted at my words. “The fact that you’re saying that is proof that you aren’t too angry. Otherwise, you would have rushed at me long ago, like all other barbarians do. Come to think of it, you were strange from our first meeting. I told you to beg for your life despite your honor as a warrior and you didn’t even think twice. But now I’m insulting you? Don’t you think it’s funny to say that now?”

Ha, was this karma? When she laid it all out like that, I had no way of arguing. There was only one approach still available to me. “There must be something wrong with your head for you to laugh at a barbarian like this.”
It was an ultimatum. Hesitating any longer would definitely leave me at a further disadvantage here.
As I was puffing myself up with that thought in mind, she said, “Why, are you really planning on attacking me? Just like you attacked the evil spirit hunter who approached you back then?”
Huh? She knows about that too?
“...You—did you investigate me?”

“You’re more than a little suspicious. Most people would have done the same, not just me. Well, I’m sure everyone let go of their suspicions after you received a noble title.” Amelia continued talking without giving me a moment to interrupt. “But to think you really are an evil spirit. You have talent. How on earth did you get a title? Even if the Ministry of Security cleared you of charges, the palace would have made sure to do a separate verification for something like that.”
Oh, there hadn’t been anything like that. I didn’t know how but it had all worked out. I could use that to my advantage now. “You don’t think that might be because I’m not an evil spirit?”
I spoke confidently, my back straight and my shoulders high, but Amelia answered without missing a beat. “As I said before, only evil spirits retain their memory after taking that medicine.”
“It was defective—”
“That can’t be the case.”
Was she a ruler? Because she was rigid. Her guard was so high that nothing I said was working. What should I do?
As I was contemplating this, Amelia muttered, “Hmm, now that I think about it, it’s possible the palace kept quiet on purpose. Since you were nothing short of a hero in the city at the time.”

What was she going on about now? I was curious about what she’d say next but I felt like asking would only be admitting she was right, so I swallowed back the urge. But it must have been visible on my face.
“Looks like you have no idea what I mean.”
“Yeah, not at all. Why should I care about what you’re saying in the first place?”
Amelia grinned at my denial. “So you’re not going to admit it until the very end?”
“Of course. Because I’m not an evil spirit.”
“Well, that’s just like you. It’s fine. There are ways.” Amelia proceeded to pull a compass-sized disc out of her sub-space. It was an object I couldn’t not recognize.
Holy—why is this thing here?

When activated, No. 7234: Misplaced Trust made it impossible for anyone within a thirty-foot radius of it to tell a lie. It also happened to be the same item that caused that whole mess in Doppelganger Forest.
“I didn’t see that when you unpacked the bag at the merchant company earlier.”
“Because I bought it when I was living in the city on my own. I thought it would come in handy being in a city like this. I didn’t think you’d be the first person I ever used it on, though.”
So that’s what this was. You already ran a simulation of exactly how you’d corner me by combining all the cards you had.
“Judging by your expression, I guess I don’t have to explain what this is. Well, there’s no way an evil spirit wouldn’t know.”
Click.
Amelia pressed the button at the top of Misplaced Trust. Then she placed it on the nightstand between the beds. The second hand began to move slowly, making a ticking sound.
With the stage set, Amelia turned to me and spoke. “Bjorn Yandel, are you an evil spirit?”
It was checkmate. A suffocating silence followed in which I desperately racked my brains.
What should I do?
The question wasn’t whether or not to reveal I was an evil spirit. That cat was already out of the bag the minute she whipped Misplaced Trust out.
It’s not a fake.
Unfortunately, the Misplaced Trust was genuine. I tested it the moment she activated it. When I tried to tell the lie “I am a woman,” it wouldn’t leave my lips at all.
“You have five minutes now. Are you going to stay silent, then?”
This item meant that silence was an answer in itself. The fact that I was an evil spirit had already been established. And so, my concerns lay elsewhere.
Do I kill her?
As this was my most important secret, extreme measures seemed appealing.
...Stop thinking crap like that.

I shook off that thought. Killing her would be impossible in the first place. To be honest, it wasn’t like I had no chance of winning in a fight against her now, but if Amelia chose to run, the chase wouldn’t be easy. Also, if our partnership went sideways here and now, all my plans would be in jeopardy too.
Besides, she’s clearly the type who would be a huge pain in the ass to have as an enemy.

In that case, there was only one option, although it wasn’t a barbarian-like solution. Since this woman was into black-and-white thinking, I had no choice but to be her friend if I didn’t want her to be an enemy.

“It would be a shame for this item to go to waste so I guess I should speak instead, if you won’t. What I said earlier about evil spirits not losing their memory to the medicine was not a made-up statement—it’s the truth.”
I put an end to my lengthy panic. “Yes, I am an evil spirit.”

This was my second coming out after Baekho. Amelia didn’t look particularly surprised. She’d only pulled that thing out to make me admit it out loud; she must have already been convinced a long time ago.
“That’s a strange expression on your face,” she said.
“...You’ll never know how relieved and suffocated I feel right now.”
“For some reason—” Amelia suddenly stopped mid-sentence. At first, I wondered why, but I soon understood what was going on. Misplaced Trust had recognized a lie and silenced her.
“You weren’t about to say sorry or something like that, were you?” Was she serious? A rage momentarily surged through me but I barely managed to push it down.
Yeah, we can’t turn into enemies now, can we?
Now that I’d been caught out as an evil spirit, I had to become best friends with this woman, so I should confirm something first. “But are you okay? With the fact that I’m an evil spirit.”
“If you’re asking if I hold a negative opinion like the people in the city, the answer is no. I once worked on the same team as an evil spirit for over a year.”
“...Then why were you so persistent?”

“Because I was curious.” I was immediately faced with a second obstacle. Just for a reason like that, she dug into something someone clearly wanted to hide? Right when steam was about to come out of my ears, she averted her eyes. “Strangely, I keep getting involved with you. That’s why I was curious. Whether you had anything you were hiding, and whether I could trust you.”
Seeing as Misplaced Trust is activated, I don’t think she’s saying something she doesn’t mean... Ha, this makes getting angry kinda—
“Oh, of course, I also figured you wouldn’t be able to betray me so easily if I knew your weakness.”
That would have been best left unsaid. Well, what could you do with a woman like this?
“I have a question,” she continued.
“If you’re an evil spirit, why were you so angry over the death of Yandel Jarku? Was it guilt?”
“That’s...”
I don’t know, either, was how I wanted to answer, but the words wouldn’t come out. So I just honestly admitted it. “Yes.”
“Hmm, you’re actually a very soft person.” Amelia looked at me with amusement. “Is your goal to return like the other evil spirits?”
“...I don’t know.”
“Because of your comrades? I guess the real you was an affectionate guy as well.”
Ugh, why was she so interested in me? I needed to change the topic ASAP.
Click.
At that moment, the needle on Misplaced Trust stopped moving. That meant that it was no longer active.
That’s much better.

I quickly changed the topic of conversation. Like it or not, I’d already been revealed as an evil spirit, right? I should start by asking the questions I had been avoiding asking before now to hide my identity.
“But Amelia, why were you looking for Auril Gavis back in Bifron?”
“Oh, I guess you would know about him if you’re an evil spirit.”
“I don’t just know about him. I even met him in person not too long ago.”
“You met him?”
“Let’s talk about that later. Answer my question first.”
“...Because the day my older sister died, he was there.”
“What?”
“I figured he must have been involved in some way. Which is why I wanted to meet him and hear the truth. That’s all.”
Hmm, it was actually nothing special. I thought there would be a bigger secret to it.
No, the fact that the old man was there that day isn’t useless information. Perhaps I can figure out what his goal is from this quest.
“Now, then. Tell me. Where did you meet him?”
“Do you know about Ghost Busters?”
“If you’re talking about the gathering of evil spirits, yes, to some extent.”

Okay, then there was less to explain. “I was sure I wouldn’t be summoned since this is twenty years in the past, but I was summoned in my sleep. I met a man claiming to be Auril Gavis there.” After going on to explain that I got exposed as a time traveler throughout our conversation, I said, “The important bit starts now, so listen carefully. That old man said that no matter what we do here, the past cannot be changed.”
“...He said that?”

“Yeah, at first, I found it hard to believe so I put it to the test. And it went exactly how I told you it did in the labyrinth.” Dwalkie and Raven. I tried to change their futures, but even those actions were already a part of this timeline’s cause and effect. “So I will ask again, Amelia. Are you still going to try?”

Amelia didn’t answer. When I told her this last time, she didn’t even flinch, but now that the additional explanation of Auril Gavis had been added, it seemed the weight of my words was different. She quietly gathered herself before opening her mouth. “I will. It’s too late to give up now.”
Too late, huh? She sounded like someone who bought stocks during a bubble that was about to burst.

“I see. Then I will help.” Instead of arguing with her, I expressed my intent to join her. She was a very compassionate woman, after all. If I kept building up our goodwill and ingratiating myself to her like this, she wouldn’t consider toying with my weakness.
“...I’m tired. I’m going to sleep.” Amelia ended the conversation there and laid back down on her bed. I was a bit stunned.
Huh? Sleep? Shouldn’t she be saying thank you right now? That she can rely on me, or that she’s glad to have me?

I wasn’t expecting anything of the sort, but I never thought she would just lie down without acknowledging my offer. Yikes, that called for a change of plans, then. How could I get brownie points with her?
“Amelia, are you sleeping?”
“I-I was just thinking I could give you a m-massage if you’re tired.”
Silence.
“Ah, right... That’s a bit much, right? Sorry to disturb your sleep.”
I lay on the bed across from Amelia. Although I closed my eyes, there was no way I’d be able to sleep.
In the middle of a long silence, a question suddenly came flying at me without blinkers. “What was your original name?”

I didn’t know why she was suddenly curious about my real name, but I found myself answering honestly. “It’s Hansu Lee. Oh, Lee is my last name.” Since I’d already been found out, something like my real name wasn’t important. Besides, I figured that refusing to answer could affect her goodwill toward me, which was the last thing I wanted. Hmm, yeah, that should have been the case.
“Hans? Then is your name Hans? That’s a surprisingly common—”
“What the fuck did you say?” A curse flew from my lips unwittingly. That had crossed the line.

chapters.title: Chapter 304: Rainwales (2)
paragraphs: After I jumped up and cursed as if she’d just said my trigger word, a short, awkward silence followed. It didn’t last long though.
“Did you... just say ‘fuck’ to me?” Amelia asked, almost as if to double-check, and I hurriedly began damage control.
Of course, I didn’t blindly apologize. This issue was important to me. “Ahem-hem, my name is Hansu. Not Hans.”
“So?”

“I want you to be careful about the pronunciation. You know. This is a very sensitive matter for me...” Even as I said that, I worried this incident would further diminish her goodwill toward me, but Amelia was surprisingly generous and understanding.
“...All right. I’ll be careful from now on.” It seemed she acknowledged she’d crossed a line even if she didn’t know why I was reacting like this over something like pronunciation.
Okay, then that settled that. Since she started the conversation, I decided to ask her a question on my mind too. “Um, Amelia?”
“Speak.”

“What did you mean earlier? That the palace could have knowingly kept quiet about the fact that I’m an evil spirit.” This was a question that I’d been forced to hold back before my coming out, even though I had been dying to ask it.

“It’s still just a possibility.” Amelia offered a disclaimer and gave me her rationale for it. “To start, if the palace figured out you were an evil spirit, your identity would have been exposed long ago.”

Hmm, that was true. If they just used one Numbers Item like the one Amelia used today, there would be nothing I could do. “I get that, but how does that turn into them willingly keeping quiet? In that case, wouldn’t it make more sense to take the fact that they haven’t said anything to mean that the palace must completely trust me instead?”
“That could be the case. But you were the most famous hero in the city at the time. I thought there was a possibility the palace just felt it couldn’t touch you.”
Uh, I still don’t get it. No matter how famous I get, I’m still only a small fry from the palace’s point of view.
“Explain.”
“Hmm, I guess you’re not the type who’s good at politics.”
Please stop with the analysis of Hansu Lee.

When I stared at her without responding, Amelia smirked and continued. “Think about it. There’s a hero who sacrificed his life to save his comrades and fought a bloody battle to bring back thousands of adventurers from certain death, and then it comes out that that hero is actually an evil spirit? What kind of problems do you think will arise from that?”
“Uh... confusion?”
“Yes, there will be confusion. Because the palace, along with the city’s three religious sects, has described evil spirits as evil beings and designated them as targets for extermination.”
Only then did I understand why this woman thought the palace might have kept quiet about my identity despite figuring it out.
“Because evil spirits must always be evil...”
“Luckily, you’re quick.”

I was different from the other evil spirits. I helped uplift my barbarian compatriots despite our race’s weak influence and even went as far as fighting at the forefront of a major battle, risking my life. That was why the palace had to be cautious. The moment they executed me for being an evil spirit, the citizens would start to think, But he saved thousands of people? Yet he is being killed for being an evil spirit?

“Of course, even if they reveal you are an evil spirit and put you on the execution scaffold, there won’t be any riots or anything like that. As always, things will be noisy for a while for a bit before getting quiet again. But...”
“The palace won’t want to leave even the slightest precedent suggesting evil spirits might perhaps be useful.”

“Again, this is all just speculation,” Amelia finished, but her ‘speculation’ left me very uncomfortable. Her reasoning wasn’t outlandish. It had a basis. And the problem was that said basis sounded plausible to me.
Huh, what if this is really true? Will I need to create a whole new identity and live in hiding as soon as I return?
All kinds of thoughts jumbling up my mind, I asked, “Amelia, are you sleeping?”
“No. And from now on, call me Emily even if we’re alone. I will call you by your pseudonym as well.”
“Uh, all of a sudden?”

“We could make another mistake in front of other people.” She was probably referring to the time we beat up Beck’s gang. “So it would be good to make it a habit to avoid doing it again. If everything goes according to plan, we will soon come into contact with the lord of the castle.”

With that, I wiped all other thoughts from my mind. Yeah, it doesn’t matter how much I mull over my whole situation with the palace—I wouldn’t be able to find a proper solution in this era anyway. I should focus on our work here first.
The next morning, a visitor came to the inn we were staying at.
Knock, knock.
“I’m Rick Omanus. Are you Emily and Bjon, son of Thor?”
Surprisingly, he was a knight. Not an adventurer who just used a sword as a weapon and wore plated armor, but a real, genuine knight under the lord of the castle’s purview.
I guess there’s an order of knights here too.

Now that I thought about it, that was probably why Amelia could use an aura. It would have been difficult to build up the mastery needed to achieve a natural awakening at such a young age alone. I was sure she learned from someone.
“What’s your business with us?”
“The lord of the castle thinks highly of your capabilities and has decided to provide you support.”
His arrogant choice of words brought to mind some high-ranking people in Rafdonia. I guessed he just couldn’t imagine we’d ever say no. Well, not that we were going to.
“What kind of support are you talking about?” Amelia asked, pretending to be oblivious.
Rick Omanus held out a piece of paper instead of answering. “The details are all written here, so will you give me your answer after you read it?”

The contract listed what support we could obtain from the castle and, conversely, what we would have to give up in exchange for taking the recruitment offer. The conditions alone weren’t bad. Members of the team received support, a right to go up to Rafdonia as a reward for accomplishments, and many opportunities to receive benefits with the lord of the castle’s seal of approval. In exchange, we had to follow his orders in the case of emergencies.
“This is recruitment, not support I see.”
“I told you. The lord of the castle thinks highly of your capabilities.”
“I need time to think.”
“I will wait out here. But I hope you won’t take too long.”
This was what we had been waiting for, but since responding too quickly could arouse suspicion, we dragged out our ‘deliberation’ for a long while.
When we opened the door again, I asked, “...Have you been in that position the whole time?”
“Since I’m on official duty, naturally.”
Still, I didn’t think he’d be doing that for over two hours. “Here, take it.”
Afterward, we handed the knight the signed contract and he told us to come visit the castle any time, as everything had already been arranged. I guessed he really didn’t think we’d refuse.
“But does a signature even mean anything?”
“It’s a mere formality. After all, if you defy him, living a normal life in this city becomes impossible.”
Trying to intimidate the newbie, huh? There was also always the option of moving to the eastern part of the city and teaming up with Orcules.
“Then see you later.” The knight, having finished his business, left without looking back. It was our turn to start our day.
“Emily, what’s your plan now? We’ve attracted his attention, but not enough for him to want to meet us in person.”
“That’s not a problem. We just have to keep attracting his attention in the future.”
“Well, that’s true.”
Not to brag, but I was pretty good at drawing attention. With this barbarian body of mine, I got caught up in all kinds of stuff even if I stayed put.
“Now, let’s go out.”

After that, we packed up all our equipment and headed to the castle. Last time we were here, we only took care of administrative work in the outer bailey, but this time we were able to enter the inner walls, which required permission.

“Ms. Emily and Mr. Iron Mask. I received word from Sir Omanus that you would be coming. My name is Mel. From now on, it is my job to assist the two of you whenever you visit the inner bailey.” The administrator who greeted us with a bright smile welcomed us to the family and briefly explained the structure of the inner bailey, along with its layout. None of what was said was of much interest to me because I’d already heard all of it from Amelia. “Since this is your first day, registration will come first. Ah, what are your plans for the future, if I may ask? Most people end up in their original parties—”
“We have no intention of joining an established party.”
“I see. Then I will guide you through the process of creating a new party in your name.”

We followed him to the Labyrinth Administrative Center in the inner bailey, which was only accessible to adventurers who worked directly under the lord of the castle. We registered ourselves as a two-person duo named Iron Mask. More so than Emily and Bjon, apparently nicknames like that were memorable.
“What will you do with the three available slots for additional comrades? If you tell me the roles that you want—”
“Pause.”
“Sorry?”
“Until we find someone we like, we will work as a duo. So I don’t want you to allow any membership applications.”
“Yes, I will do as you wish.”

Amelia finished adjusting our party’s settings like the local she was and then confirmed one piece of information with the labyrinth management’s staff. “How many herders can we choose from?” A herder was a child in a position like Jencia’s, someone who entered the labyrinth at a young age and took on all kinds of dangerous tasks.
“There are currently thirteen available.”
“What if you include those who are already affiliated too?”
“One hundred seventy-three.”
“I want to see them all.”
Amelia carefully read through the information provided by the staff, taking care not to miss a single detail. Then she found the names she was looking for. “I want to take these two children.”
“If you’re talking about the Rainwales sisters, they are already associated with a team, so that will be impossible...”
“You can at least contact the team they belong to. Tell them they will be generously compensated if they are handed over.”
“...All right.”
That ended our official business for today. Before we returned to our inn, Amelia took me to a place located in the inner bailey. That place was a tavern.
“A tavern? There’s a place like this in the castle?”
“It is one of the benefits available for those who have gained access to the inner bailey.”
“But why did you...?”

I had never seen Amelia take a sip of alcohol before, so I couldn’t understand why she would bring me here until I saw the sign for the tavern: Rainwales. It couldn’t be a coincidence that the tavern’s name was the same as Amelia’s last name.
“Aren’t you coming in?”
“A-ah. Uh...”

The interior was relatively clean and there were not many people inside, probably because it was daytime. We took a seat in the corner, ordered drinks and appetizers, and sat quietly without saying a word to each other.
Why did you bring me here, then? It’s clearly a historical site...
“Are you curious?”
I thought it over for a moment before nodding.
“It won’t be a very interesting story.”
“Life can’t just be all interesting things.” I tossed the drink down my throat in one go. Ugh, it was strong. And it tasted so bad. I guessed Noark was a city of real men after all.
“...Weirdo.”
“Huh?”
“I didn’t say anything.” Amelia then gulped down her drink too.
Oh, what’s gotten into her? Throwing it down the hatch? Is this too hard to talk about sober?
The moment Amelia brought the glass she had finished down on the table, I heard a bang.
Jeez, that scared me.

I hurriedly turned my head in the direction of the sound and heard the deep shout of a man from the kitchen. “You ungrateful bitches!” The man’s voice was full of anger, and before long, the sound of something breaking was heard, along with a distinctly female scream.
Smack! Smack!
Even a blind man could tell violence was taking place in that kitchen, but the few customers inside the tavern seemed used to it.
“The owner is going after his daughter again.”
“Hehe, I feel sorry for those kids. Having to call a man like that their father.”
What, owner? Daughter? Then is the person getting beaten over there...?
Whip.

The moment I realized, I quickly turned my head to check on Amelia. The hand she had curled around her glass was shaking, and she looked too small and pitiable for me to write it off as a sign of timeworn anger.

chapters.title: Chapter 305: Rainwales (3)
paragraphs: Amelia was a strong woman, and I didn’t think that just because she knew how to use an aura and had several rare, high-ranking essences. I had not once seen this woman afraid of anything. But now, that same Amelia was shaking in front of me, even though no matter who that father in the kitchen over there was, she had no reason to be afraid of him anymore.
Is it trauma?

It wasn’t that I didn’t get it. I’d also experienced something similar in the past. Although I knew in my head that it was safe, I hadn’t been able to ride in cars for several years and the smell of something burning often woke me up from sleep and had me wandering the entire building to find the source. It wasn’t a matter of self-control—it was an instinct engraved in the subconscious.
Smack!
This was fear.
“...Are you all right?” Amelia didn’t answer my question so I grabbed her trembling wrist. “Emily.”
She finally came to her senses. “Oh, sorry. I didn’t hear you... What did you say?”
“I asked if you were okay.”
Yeah, you’re not okay.
It was only after the noise in the kitchen quieted down that Amelia spoke again. “...How unsightly of me.”
“Huh? What are you talking about?” As far as I was concerned, I didn’t see anything. And even if I did, I would never think it was unsightly.

Just then, a man appeared from the kitchen. “Whew, those bitches get me worked up every day.” Although he had a somewhat stout and stocky build, his height was around 5′6″. Contrary to what I had been imagining, he looked extremely ordinary.
“Aren’t you being a little harsh today?”

“Harsh? Those ungrateful bitches don’t know when to be thankful. Enough talking about those annoyances, let’s drink.” The man sat at the table with one of the customers and started drinking and chatting.
Amelia watched him for a long time from her corner seat, then said, “That man was my adoptive father.”
“Adoptive father?”
“It’s a familiar story here. There are children without parents who need a place to stay, and there are people who want to take in such children all over the city.”

“All over the city, huh?” I had a feeling I already knew the reason why. It wouldn’t be for a motive as noble as providing a home for children who were all alone. Amelia said it was a common story, and stories like these were usually extremely cynical.
“It’s a kind of symbiotic relationship. The children are protected until they are old enough to work and the adoptive parents get cheap labor out of it.”

In this city, the adoptive father had full control over the adopted child, and that right was absolute, at least until the child grew up and became an adult. Killing the adoptive parent or escaping was impossible because it would set a dangerous precedent. The child in question would be called ungrateful and be punished accordingly by others.
“...I see.”
“But my sister and I were a little better off. We were physically healthy, and we were hardy enough to never get sick. That’s why we were able to avoid getting split up.”
“How old were you at the time?”
“Five. My sister was three years older.”

Amelia said it wasn’t bad at first. Unlike when she had been going into the labyrinth with her weak and injured father, she was fed on time and didn’t sleep in the cold. She was bullied into doing all kinds of chores even at that age, though.

“But that wasn’t so hard, either. Everyone lives like that. I even considered myself lucky to have an older sister to rely on.” At the time, Amelia had had a vague dream that once she grew up and became an adult, their lives would finally begin in earnest.
“But I guess it didn’t work out that way.”
“...It’s all because of me.”
It had happened when Amelia was around nine years old. While she was helping out at the tavern, a drunkard had tried to strangle her. The reason? Because she dropped his food.
“That was when my sister stepped in.”

Amelia’s sister saw it happening while she was serving the customers and ran into the kitchen. Then, picking up a knife, she slowly walked over and pounced on the drunkard’s back, slicing his carotid artery with incredible precision.
“I learned this later, but not one of the adventurers in the tavern sensed my sister’s presence until she had already grabbed a knife and reached the bastard’s back.”
The drunkard did not die that day. He was treated with a potion just in time to save his life. However, through that incident, the girl’s talent was exposed to the world.
“The next day, someone came from the castle. They said they would cover up this incident if we handed over my sister.”

Surprisingly, their adoptive father rejected that part of the offer. He used all his money to cover the cost of the potion, offered an apology to the drunkard, and smoothed over the incident on his own.
“From that day on, my sister became a herder.”
But their adoptive father had decided that since she was a talented child, she could be taught to make a lot more money than she would by working in a tavern.
“My sister was talented too. Within less than a year of joining a team of plunderers, they recognized her contributions and she started receiving a small cut of the loot.”
When that happened, the adoptive father had figured that since these children shared the same blood, Amelia might have had talent too.
“It wasn’t long before I became a herder and was pretty much sold to a team of plunderers. And it wasn’t long before my talent was recognized too.”

Amelia glossed over what happened next and moved on, and I didn’t dig too deeply. I didn’t have to ask to know what kind of life the Rainwales sisters had lived as herders. They would have just borne it all, solely relying on the only blood they had left in this world.

“Anyway, that’s how we ended up a part of a gang of telekinetics, and also enslaved to work in this tavern in the city.” Amelia wrapped up the story of her life from childhood to her teenage years. “How about it, does that sate your curiosity about me now?”
“Yes, that’s enough.” As we made plans, I got a rough idea of what happened next.
The sisters’ hopes of becoming free as adults would be trampled in about five months thanks to a mundane tragedy.
Noon soon passed and the number of people entering the tavern slowly increased.

“...Excuse me.” A girl in her early teens with long, red, curly hair approached our table. Her face was slightly bruised, but she was using her messy hair to cover it up. “Would you like some more alcohol...?”
This was usually what workers said if you stayed in one place for too long. It meant, “Order more stuff or get lost.”
Amelia was unable to meet the young girl’s eyes. I could understand why.
“What’s your name?” I asked.
“...Amelia Rainwales.”
Yeah, anyone was bound to feel awkward facing their younger self. And since she knew what was going to happen, she must have felt guilty too.
“Let’s go.”
Amelia attempted to leave, but I stopped her. “Just a moment.” I was finally face-to-face with Fetus Amelia. I couldn’t let this opportunity pass me by. “Kid, how old are you?”
“I’m... fourteen...”
Oh? If she was fourteen years old twenty years ago...
“So you’re thirty-four,” I muttered, and Amelia whipped her head around to glare at me. It seemed she was annoyed that her personal information had been leaked.
“Thirty-four...?” The young Amelia looked like she didn’t understand what we were talking about, but she still kept her expression friendly in front of customers.
“And this is what you look like when you smile.”
“Pardon?”
“Ah, I meant it’s nice to see. You should smile more.”
“Ah, right...”
While adult Amelia looked like she’d just stepped on dog shit, young Amelia looked puzzled and didn’t know what to do. And so the fooling around ended there.
“We’ll pay and leave now.”
“Ah, right!”

I didn’t think I would survive the consequences if I continued, so I hurriedly paid the bill and left the tavern. Right when we got back to the inn, Amelia, who had on a sour expression the whole way here, suddenly spoke, her voice low and pained. “Perhaps it’s as you say.”
“What do you mean?”
“When you spoke to her, I remembered that I had that conversation before.”
Ah, the sour expression was my fault. I definitely thought she was just annoyed with me.
“Amelia?”
“Emily.”
“Ahem, yes, Emily. Do you want another drink?” I took out the drinks I had stored in sub-space. All plunderers carried some around.
“No. There’s no point in me drinking, anyway.”
“Because of your essence?”
“Yes.” Put simply, her Poison Tolerance and Psychological Resistance stats were too high for her to get drunk.
“Then why did you drink at the tavern earlier?”
“That’s... because you look suspicious if you don’t drink at a tavern.”
“You never waste a single moment, huh?”
“What?”
“Don’t get all serious. What’s so hard about having just one drink? It’s lonely drinking alone.”
“Why do you want to drink in the first place?” Amelia asked as I pulled out a glass and poured into it.
Did you really think I just wanted to drink?
“We still have things to talk about.” I’d heard about her childhood at the tavern, but there was actually something else I wanted to know now that I’d come out and all.
“Things to talk about?”
“Why are you pretending not to know? It’s not like we have secrets anymore.”
“...Don’t act friendly. It’s annoying.”

“Really? Then tell me this and I’ll stop. When we were making plans at the very beginning, you never said anything about Nivelles Enze. Yesterday was also my first time hearing that Auril Gavis was there.”

At the time, Amelia had refused to communicate with me. Although we were working together, we didn’t even consider telling each other everything and relying on each other. But seeing as she was now willing to tell me about her past, it was safe to say I’d garnered some trust.
“What difference would it make? You were already convinced nothing could change, anyway.”
That was true, and that conviction remained unchanged. “But yesterday you cried and told me that it was too late to give up.”
“...I didn’t cry.”
Tsk, that’s a minor detail.
“Did you not? Anyway, since you said you won’t give up, I plan to help you.”
“That way I’ll help you, right?”
“Well, that’s part of the reason.”
“Then there’s another part?”
I decided to answer honestly. “I want you to be indebted to me.”
Amelia looked like she didn’t understand. “...Why?”

There were too many reasons to list them all for her. First, Amelia knew my weakness. I needed her somehow beholden to me to keep her quiet. Also, she was strong. Based on the time I’d spent with her so far, she seemed to have a good heart, and her years of experience meant I could rely on her in certain ways.
To sum all that up, I said, “To be honest, our first meeting was not great, but I like you.”
“...What?”
“Ah, don’t take that the wrong way. I don’t mean I like you romantically.”
“I... didn’t take that the wrong way.”

“Then I’m glad.” I cleared my throat and continued, “Anyway, I know what kind of person you are now. If I make you indebted to me, you will definitely repay it. So, if I can, I want to save your sister too. Since you’ll grant any favor I ask you for if I do.”
“F-Favors?” Amelia stepped back, giving me a wary look. “What kind of favor are you planning on asking of me?”
Jeez, I’m not going to eat you. This is just going to lead to misunderstandings.

For every step she took back, I took a step closer. “Amelia Rainwales.” Originally, I didn’t plan on revealing my desires this early, but it should be fine to call dibs at least. “If I succeed in saving your sister and take care of the logistical hurdles once we return to our time...”
“Then join my clan.”
Yeah, any good quest has to have a reward.

chapters.title: Chapter 306: Rainwales (4)
paragraphs: Was my recruitment offer that unexpected? Amelia studied me carefully, apparently trying to gauge my intentions. But after not being able to figure them out, she spoke up in a somewhat bitter tone. “I... am a plunderer.”
“Naturally, since you are from Noark. But I know better than anyone that you’re different.”

The fact was, Amelia had let me and Ainar live during our first meeting. The same went for when we ran into each other in the sewer. Not just me, the barbarian, either. Hikurod, Rotmiller, Missha, and even Dwalkie—she fed all of us the Blessing of Lethe and sought an alternate way to resolve the situation.
“My description is registered in the Adventurers’ Guild. The palace will know it too—”
I cut Amelia off sternly. “A new identity can always be created.”
“That’s not as easy as it sounds. And if I’m working with you, a nobleman, there will no doubt be people who dig into who I am—”
Wow, you have a lot to say today.
“That’s why I said once I resolve all those problems, come join my clan.”
“There’s... no way something like that would ever happen. And if your plan is to be your usual bullheaded self when shit hits the fan, we’ll both be screwed—”
“So, I need to set up safeguards, huh?”
“Safeguards...?”
“Never mind, I’ll figure out whether that’ll work or not so you just have to answer.”
It was a yes or no question. When I outlined the situation neatly for her, Amelia hesitated for a moment, then sighed. “Ha... why do you always put me on the spot...?”
“So, your answer?”

“All right. If there ever comes a time where I wouldn’t cause any problems working alongside you...” Amelia trailed off and avoided eye contact, but it seemed she didn’t like her own subconscious actions.
Slide.
She raised her head again, looked into my eyes, and said, “Then I will be your comrade.” The quest was thus established.
[Quest Name: Save My Sister!
Objective: Sister’s survival (0/1), Solve identity issue (0/1)
Reward: Amelia Rainwales (SSR) Recruitment Contract]
At least, that was the basic gist of it. As I was mapping out this new quest in my mind, Amelia gulped down the contents of the bottle on the table.
“I thought you don’t drink because you can’t get drunk?”
“I’m thirsty.”
Oh, I see. But saying something like that while chugging down alcohol makes her seem very macho.
Tap.
Amelia grimaced as she put the bottle down. At the sight, I couldn’t resist asking, “Does alcohol taste bad to you?”
“How could you ever think it tastes good?”

“No, just checking. I think it tastes bad too.” I’d heard people say that going through hardships made alcohol taste sweeter, which was why I was wondering. I felt like I’d been through enough hardships myself, but it still just tasted bad to me.
“...Enough with the nonsense, let’s get back on track.” Amelia sat across from me. “You wanted to hear about Nivelles Enze, right? I’ll tell you. Your opinion might help me think of another way.”
“Okay.”
“Oh, and one more thing. I’m warning you in advance, but I will only be your comrade if you keep all the promises you made earlier. Got it?”
“But I didn’t ask you to be my comrade, I asked you to join my clan.”
“Oh, uh...” Amelia flinched at my words. “That’s... certainly the case. I... thought that meant the same thing. But if those are two different things, I’ll rephrase—”
“It’s fine. I think comrade sounds better than clanmate, anyway.”
“...Were you messing with me just now?”

How quick on the uptake. “Of course not.” Amelia shot me a suspicious look but she couldn’t say anything to that because she didn’t have any proof. So, it was time to change the subject. “Hurry up and tell me about everything I don’t know, including Nivelles Enze.”

When we got back on track, Amelia’s playfulness disappeared as well, and she began combing through her memories. “Nivelles Enze was the name of the man who saved my life that day. And Iron Mask was the nickname he used in Noark.”
“So it was.” The thing I had been most uncertain about was now clear: I was this woman’s savior. No wonder she’d been particularly nice to me ever since I arrived in Noark wearing that mask.
“Which was why I kept wondering whether to tell you this or not. I came here to change my past, but now that I’m actually here, everything seems to be flowing exactly as intended.”
“I see.” I had nothing to say to that since this was something I’d experienced once before. “But you said you won’t give up. Anyway, tell me when you met m—no, when did you meet Nivelles Enze?”
“I don’t know the exact date. But if memory serves, about three weeks from now. We met at the inner bailey...”

After that, I continued to converse with Amelia for a while and acquired the information I needed to know. Amelia was no longer guarded or putting me to the test, and she answered all my questions honestly. In a way, this was the first instance of perfect communication between us. Of course, that didn’t mean she always answered straight away.
“Do you have any more questions?”
“No, I think I’ve heard everything I need to hear.”
“I see. Then...”
“Sorry. To be honest, I’m not sure if I have any ideas yet. Let me think it over some more.”
“I see...” When I replied that I couldn’t think of anything concrete, Amelia looked disappointed but didn’t argue. “True, I’m sure you won’t be able to come up with something right away.”
“Sounds like you didn’t expect anything from me at all.”
“...Weirdo. If I actually didn’t, I wouldn’t have told you all of this.”
“Hmm, does that mean you trust me?”
“...To some extent.”

“Some extent, huh?” I chuckled. Normally I would’ve considered that a shifty answer, but perhaps because it was coming from Amelia, I instead felt somewhat proud. You know, like how a compliment from your parents usually went in one ear and out the other, but a compliment from someone who was usually picky made you feel accomplished.
“Anyway, if you have no other questions, it’s my turn.”
“Huh?”
“Why are you surprised? It’s... only natural that I’d have questions for you too.”
“Oh, I guess so. Ask away. What do you want to know?”

“What exactly did you talk about with Auril Gavis? I couldn’t ask you in detail earlier.” I was sure she was going to ask about the kind of world I lived in or something like that, but that turned out not to be the case. She really wasn’t one for idle curiosity at all. Well, that made things easier for me, anyway.

“To be honest, I already told you everything you might be wondering about. But since you want to know, I’ll start from the beginning. When I woke up, I was in a mansion that gave me a strong sense of déjà vu. Ah, explaining why I felt déjà vu is going to be a long story...”
“It’s okay, tell me. We still have a long night left ahead of us.”
“Uh... If you say so, all right.”

After that, I told Amelia everything that happened in the spirit world when I visited last month. As a result, I even mentioned some big names: the head of Orcules, the Fallen Scholar Belbev Ruingenes, and the unidentified man called Kagureas.

“Kagureas? This is my first time hearing that name too.” Unfortunately, Amelia knew nothing about the man. That wasn’t the case for the other two, though. “The head of Orcules was there, huh? There were rumors that he might be an evil spirit, but to think those rumors were true... Then did you come from the same place as him?”
“No. Not all evil spirits are from the same dimension.”
“Is the same true for Fallen Scholar?”
“Probably. It was around this time that people from our home started to get dragged here.”
“Is that so? Sounds like I’m hearing some surprising secrets thanks to you. I don’t know about the commander, but that old man Ruingenes wasn’t rumored to be an evil spirit at all.”
“While we’re on that note, can you tell me some more about those two?”
“I don’t know much, but if you’re okay with that, sure.”

Once again, Amelia gave me a disclaimer before sharing the information she had. It was more useful than I thought because I didn’t know much. Whether you were talking about the head of Orcules or the Fallen Scholar, there was little that was publicly known about them. There was bound to be a difference in the knowledge I had and the knowledge that Noark native and member of Orcules Amelia had.
“So, will you be called there again on the fifteenth?”

“Probably. He said he’s going to fix the fairness issue or something like that, so I’m curious how that’ll turn out. Oh, is there something you want to ask him? I will ask him for you when I get summoned.”
“...I’ll think about it.”
There was nothing left to talk about so we stopped there and I lay down in bed. Having almost spent the whole night awake, the day ahead felt particularly long.
It seemed lying in bed brought a new question to mind, though. “Bjon, what was your world like?”

Amelia started asking me various questions, which was unlike her, and I answered them one by one. Democracy, science, cars and planes, missiles—each answer required a long explanation but it wasn’t tedious or annoying. After all, this was my first time sharing stories like these in this body. Unlike the rest of the time, when I had to think twice about each word I spoke because I had to hide that I was an evil spirit, there was no need for that with Amelia. Time flew by.
“That was quite an interesting story. Although I knew most of that already.”
“What? You knew? But how?”
“There are many evil spirits whose identities have been exposed living in Noark. You’re bound to hear various stories as you move through life.”
“I see... Then why did you bother asking me?”
“That’s...” Amelia trailed off and did not speak for a long time.
“Did you seriously fall asleep...? Stop pretending to be asleep. I know you only sleep halfway like a dolphin.”
Was the student surpassing their master? I didn’t think she would turn one of the two ways to make someone pissed back around on me.
“...Are you really sleeping?”
Would you look at that? She’s even snoring now. Ha, ridiculous. Is she acting or what?
I couldn’t be sure, but after that, I stopped talking and closed my eyes. The reason was simple. If she was really sleeping deeply for the first time in a long time, I didn’t want to bother her.
“...Good night.” I rolled over, turning my back to her, and soon fell asleep.

After that, the time passed quickly. Well, that might not be the best way to describe it. To be honest, it was a very boring period. Because we rigidly refrained from going out to not cause any problems, we killed all of our time at the inn. That wasn’t to say that time was all a waste, though.
“Bjon, go wash up.”
“But we’re not even going out.”
“...You smell.”

We talked all day. The topics we covered were many. Sometimes we talked about my home, Amelia’s memories with her older sister, or stories from the labyrinth. Having conversations about various subjects, I got to learn more about the person Amelia was. The biggest takeaway, though, was that I finally got to hear about Amelia’s essences.
Has she never operated in a real party? I don’t see how she couldn’t get to the eighth floor with those specs.
Amelia’s stats were much better than I expected. To be honest, if it weren’t for his arc-made longsword and Dragon Speech, she could even be considered a higher rank than the Dragon Slayer.
But it’s not just combat. She has talent as a navigator too.

With this as a foundation, she was able to fill the position of scout, on top of being a nuker whose aura could quickly cut down monsters with high physical resistance. In turn, she had the disadvantage of being a bit of a glass cannon, but that could be resolved by my tanking hits for her at the front.
“Oh, right. How did it go out there today?”
“As expected, it was rejected,” Amelia answered as she dried her hair with a towel, fresh from a shower.
Huh, so that’s how that played out.

“Hmm, maybe the problem was that we offered too little...” Our attempt to take in the Rainwales sisters, who were working as herders for another party, was a failure. “How were they? Do you think they would change their minds for more money?”
“I don’t know. Can’t be sure, but it’s best to not go that route. If they know we are overly interested in them, they will not only be on guard but try to take advantage of us.”
“That’s true. Everyone here is cunning.”
“Still, we succeeded in approaching them casually. Thankfully, they are showing interest in us first.”
“Interest?”
“They asked if we were willing to join their party.”
In some ways, things were going according to plan, but we both wore grim expressions at that realization. Whatever the reason, all of this had already happened in the past.
“Everything fits so well that it’s almost nauseating.”
In the original timeline, we joined that party and, after undergoing all sorts of things, were faced with that incident in about five months.
“What are you going to do?”
“...Join the team as planned. It may be a little unpleasant, but this is the best way for us to be nearby when something happens.”
“Really? Then let’s do that.”

I didn’t necessarily disagree. No matter how I looked at it, it seemed impossible for us to change the past this way, but it wasn’t like I could think of any other way. For now, I decided to follow Amelia’s plan—at least until a better one came along.
I checked the time once more at five minutes to midnight. Amelia noticed and said, “Ah, come to think of it, today is that day.”
“Yes.” After a drink of water, I lay on the bed.
“Have a nice trip.”
Seeing me off? This is very weird.
“There’s still about five minutes until I go. It’ll only be a short moment here, anyway.”
“Ah, that’s true.”
After that, I spent the time exchanging meaningless chatter with Amelia. Was it because this was Auril Gavis we were talking about? I was a little nervous.
Tick.
Just then, the second hand of the clock ticked into place and my vision grew blurry.
That Sprite from last time was really delicious. I wonder if he’ll give me some more?

chapters.title: Chapter 307: Round Table (1)
paragraphs: The study gave off the soothing scent of wood.
It doesn’t look like there’s anything particularly different about it.
I was looking around with that thought in mind when a change caught my eye. The white mask I wore during my last visit was hanging on the empty wall.
Does he want me to wear it out there?

I smirked and put on the mask. When I entered through the door, sure enough, I saw an old man walking in from the far end of the hallway: Auril Gavis, the mysterious man who perhaps had all the answers to my questions.

“Haha, you’re here. I’ve been waiting for you.” This was a man who hadn’t even thought to hide his emotions when he heard that I cleared the original game. “Have you had any issues since then? Ever since I sent you off that day, I’ve been very anxious about the possibility of something happening to you.”

Even if he started things off with a cheerful laugh and induced an amiable atmosphere, I couldn’t let my guard down. I saw it the other day. The head of Orcules, the Fallen Scholar, and other powerful individuals who were undoubtedly on the same level as them had been unable to make a peep when this man had dressed them down.
“I’ve been all right. But what happened to the people from back then?”
“Huh? What people?”
“You said they broke another rule and then left before the night ended.”
Only then did Auril nod in understanding. “Ah, you must be talking about those failures.”
Failures, huh?
At that nonchalant statement, I realized the battle had begun. The reason why the cryptic old man used “failures,” a word that would set me on high alert, without hesitation was obvious.
I guess he doesn’t like that I jerked him around last time.
It was a kind of variation of the carrot and stick technique. The only difference was that the stick wasn’t being swung at the target, but at someone else.

“The failures you speak of will be gathered in that room, so no need to worry. I made it very clear to them what will happen if they kick up another fuss.” While showing off his superiority by wielding his whip mercilessly against others, he simultaneously showed his target infinite kindness—just like he was right now. “Ahem, anyway, that was inconsiderate of me. I’m sure that must have been been a bit disturbing for you to hear. But don’t worry. I know better than anyone that you are different from them.”

The kindness contrasted with the coldness he just showed. The recipient of that kindness had no choice but to think, I don’t want to end up on this guy’s bad side. To avoid that, I have to match his benevolence. That was the conclusion that your subconscious naturally reached.
I was immune to underhanded techniques like these, though.
“You are special. Aren’t you?”
I smirked at the old man’s question and answered, “I don’t know.”
“Huh?”
“Enough with your foolish tricks.”
I’m tired of carrots, you see.

“...Tricks? That’s a bit harsh, isn’t it?” At my provocation, the old man’s expression shifted, and he stared straight at me. Although there was no accompanying sting of murderous intent, the look in his eyes was intense and full of roiling energy.
But I didn’t back down. You had to show these kinds of people in advance that you weren’t at all afraid of ending up on their bad side. “I didn’t come here to talk about that with you.”
“If you’re going to make small talk like this, send me back. Actually, in that case, I want you to make sure that I don’t ever come back here again.”
The old man looked rather flummoxed. “S-Small talk?!” he sputtered, like he was the one who had been wronged. “You were the one who asked what happened to them!”
Ah... that’s true. This situation took a funny turn. But what is he going to do about it?

“Then are you saying this is all my fault?” As a barbarian who farted wherever he wanted, I had learned the importance of belief—a powerful belief in oneself. That strong conviction helped you build the confidence to go through life without being intimidated no matter what challenges you faced.
“No, I’m not saying it’s your fault...”
“Apologize,” I demanded boldly.
“Wait, calm down. What on earth did I do to make you so sensitive?”
Even if I was being unreasonable, even if I was currently in the body of Hansu Lee and not a barbarian, I said, “So you won’t apologize?”
“...Haha, I guess you also think I’m a pushover.” The old man frowned at my repeated demands, and I noticed our surroundings begin to warp in a peculiar manner. To be honest, it was fucking scary.
“Apologize.” But this changed nothing. What were he and that poker face of his going to do? Was he going to kick out the user who cleared the original game?
“...Hah, why are you being like this?” the old man asked with a sigh.

Before long, the room around us stopped distorting, just as I expected. It was perfectly clear to me that he was playing up his anger to get out of this. I got the feeling the anger was genuine, though.
“Why do you keep provoking me? I’m sure you weren’t this ill-mannered last time.”
“You speak as if you know me. And a pushover? Aren’t you the one who underestimated me first?”
“What are you talking about? Underestimated you—”
“Did you think that if you used the word ‘failures,’ I’d fall in line and do whatever you want?”

Surprisingly, the old man didn’t refute my accusation to claim that I was mistaken, that it wasn’t intentional. I was sure there were a lot of excuses he could have made, but he just thought it over for a moment and then nodded. “Indeed, you are definitely different from the others... I apologize. I treated you too familiarly even though someone who cleared the original game, which was considered a failure, could not possibly be an ordinary person. I will be careful from now on.”
Uh, I wasn’t expecting such a sincere apology...
I was a little bewildered. If he had given me an empty apology, I planned to use that to take the upper hand in the conversations that followed.
Perhaps this was an intentional move on his part too.

“...Since you put it like that, I will let it slide.” Normally I didn’t accept apologies that only consisted of pretty words, but I made the call to do so here, figuring that continuing the barbarian act would really make our relationship fall apart.
The tension eased after that. “Now, why don’t we have a drink and talk in that other room instead of standing here like this? Ah, is there a type of tea that you want?”
Why are you asking the obvious?
“Sprite.” That was the only thing that had been on my mind for weeks.
We reached the point when I would normally be thinking, Yeah, that’s the stuff. Yeah, that should have been the case.
Why does it taste so bland? Is it because I asked for ice?
Rattle.

I set down the glass, which had only ice left and lost myself in thought for a moment. It wasn’t that it wasn’t refreshing at all, but it felt like there was less carbonation than usual. It tasted noticeably worse than the last time I had it.
Is this old man holding a grudge...?
When a plausible explanation occurred to me and I shifted my gaze to him, Auril Gavis spoke. “So, I want us to slowly get the ball rolling...”
It was kind of funny. This wasn’t the type of guy who should be tiptoeing around a noob like me.
I guess that’s how important I am to this old man.

Although it took some effort on my part, as his treatment of me improved, I made sure to increase my vigilance as well. After all, no one in this world treated someone well without motive. I also quit agonizing about the soda so I could think through the actual problem more thoroughly.
Just why is the user who cleared the original game so important? Hmm... I don’t know. I honestly have no idea.

The fact that I had more in-game knowledge than other players did was true, but that couldn’t be the reason. The man in front of me here was Auril Gavis, the creator of the game. All the knowledge I had, he would have as well. If what he wanted was a player with knowledge, all he had to do was share it with them.
So why is he being so obsessive? I guess that’s what I have to try to figure out from now on.
“Ahem-hem, what are you thinking so hard about?”
“Ah, sorry. My mind wandered for a moment.”
“Ha! With me right in front of you?” Auril was astonished by the absurdity of that statement. Of course, that rudeness of his didn’t last long.
“Hah, are you starting up again?”
“Ah, no, I’m not. I just meant it’s refreshing to hear something like that for the first time in a long time.”
“Ah, I see. I almost misunderstood you.”
“...Are you perhaps a barbarian?”
Huh? Ah man, did I make it too obvious?
Although on the inside I flinched, I didn’t let my unease show on my face and brushed his accusation off like he just said something distasteful. “Is that supposed to be a question?”
“No, of course not. It was a joke.” His expression made me think it really was a joke, but I needed to be more careful from now on. “Anyway, speaking of questions...”
“It’s okay, talk freely.”
As soon as my permission was given, the old man quickly got down to business. “Didn’t we talk about fairness before we parted? I have been racking my brain hard these past few days—”
“Shorter and more to the point.”
“I created an item that can solve the problem.”
See, you can sum it up in one line.
“Hmm, item?”
“It’s this.” Instead of explaining at length, Auril took out a fist-sized jewel from his inner pocket. It was an item that was very familiar to me.
“This is...”

No matter what angle I looked at it, there was no doubt about it. It was the jewel that was embedded in the center of the Round Table. I didn’t know this was its origin story. Then was this old man the Master?
“...Are you reacting like that because you know what it is?”
“No, it just looks expensive.”

“Expensive... haha! This is an item whose value cannot be converted into real-world capital—ahem, I almost got carried away again.” It seemed that after just a few lessons, Auril had learned to cut off his rants on his own. He quickly explained the item. “This is an item that holds some of the powers I have in this spiritual space.”

I didn’t understand the principle behind it at all, but I didn’t dare open my mouth. Not only would I not understand his explanation in the first place, but when you weren’t sure about something, it was best to stay quiet.
“It’s really simple to use. If you speak the truth in front of this jewel, a green light turns on, and telling a lie will turn on the red light. Would you like to test it out?”

I had let go of the suspicion that this item could be fake the moment he pulled it out, but I didn’t bother letting that show. That was because he’d practically given me a chance to ask a question for free. “Auril Gavis, are you over three hundred years old?” I deliberately mentioned a specific time frame. If I simply asked how old he was, he could just answer with “one” to prove that the jewel would turn red when he lied.
“...I am not,” Auril responded in a tone that suggested he saw through my scheme but was letting it pass.
Shaaaaaa.
The jewel turned red.
“That means that what was said was a lie.”
Wow, so he’s over three hundred years old? Since The Complete Book of Rifts was written 150 years ago, I just threw out a random number... What the hell kind of monster is this guy?
Although I was inwardly shocked, I didn’t let it show.
“How about it? Won’t things be fair if we use this to ask each other questions?”
“Hmm, but isn’t this a bit unfair? Since you made it, you might be able to decide what color the jewel glows.” It was a very valid concern.
Surprisingly, Auril chose to tackle this accusation head-on. “I swear on my name, that is impossible.”
You swear, huh?
That was a word I had very much missed. I’d had enough of backstabbing. “It’s going to be hard to believe you with just that. Maybe if you swear on your parents.”
“P-Parents...?”
“Seeing as you can’t, I guess you were lying.”

“Of course not! It’s just... such an absurd suggestion that it caught me off guard. How can I swear on people who are no longer in this world?” It seemed he hadn’t considered that a swear made on his own name wouldn’t convince me in the slightest. He took a moment to think. “It’s up to you whether you believe it or not, but I will say this. The vow I just made is the truth, and now, without this item, I cannot discern whether you are telling the truth or not either.”
“Huh?”
As I tilted my head, a green light appeared. “I told you earlier. A significant portion of my power was used to create this item. I can no longer read your soul in its totality.”
“My soul in its totality...?”
“That means I cannot read what essences of what rank you possess.”
The green light turned on again. But did this old man realize that the more it did, the more my faith was fading?
It makes me even more suspicious that he’s talking about his weaknesses so openly like this... What if it really is rigged?
Just when the look in my eyes began to darken, he asked, “Do you remember the people you saw the other day?”
“The people you called failures?”
“That’s right. I may have said that earlier, but those are in fact individuals who are treated with respect wherever they go, based on their reputations and abilities alone.”
“Reputation and ability are two different things.”
“...It’s a figure of speech.”
“Anyway, so what are you trying to say?”

Auril sighed and made a new proposal. “Why don’t we have this conversation where they are? They may not know everything, but they should be fully capable of recognizing an outrageous lie and objecting to it.”
“...What?” My mind went blank as soon as I heard his suggestion. Was this the Round Table beta version?

chapters.title: Chapter 308: Round Table (2)
paragraphs: “You know, a kind of jury system,” Auril Gavis said, before launching into what sounded like an excuse. “Of course, I don’t like this approach either, nor do I think it’s a very good option. I’m only suggesting it since you can’t trust me, so you can refuse it if you don’t like it.” Seeing how he was tiptoeing around me even as he said this, it seemed he’d interpreted my stare as a disapproving one.

“A round table, huh?” To be honest, that wasn’t a bad suggestion for me. If we were going to do it, though, it would require some modifications such as having them all sit at a round table instead of emulating a jury. Playing Round Table with this group, which included the head of Orcules and Fallen Scholar, was bound to give me useful information. But...
“I refuse. I don’t feel like parading this information in front of others.” For now, limited-edition information from Auril was my top priority. Ironing out the rules of the Round Table came after.
“A refusal... Actually, I thought you would say that. From your perspective, it could look like I’m colluding with the rest of them.” Auril sighed and asked, “Then what will you do now?”
I chuckled. What else was there to do? We needed to get back to where we started. “One question for three.”
“Hmm, I guess my end of the deal has gotten better than five.”
“Since you made this item,” I said, my eyes on the jewel.
Auril noticed and smirked. “Thank you for recognizing my efforts, but wouldn’t it make more sense for us to take one turn each if that’s the case?”

True, this might seem unfair to him. As long as the lie detector was operational, you could argue we were both on equal footing. “Think of it as the price of my faith.” However, because I was treating it like this was my first time seeing this jewel, I couldn’t be sure that the old man didn’t manipulate its truth-telling abilities. That was because he was its creator. It wouldn’t be strange if he had a hidden cheat code in place.
“How contradictory.” Auril laughed incredulously. “You’re already well aware, aren’t you? If I was lying to you, there would be no point in asking additional questions no matter how many you asked.”
Of course I know that. So what? “So, are you refusing?”

“Haha, of course not. Strangely, even though it seems contradictory, it makes sense. At least you’re throwing yourself into an uncertain situation just the same.” He accepted my terms with a cooler head than I had expected. I thought the negotiations would proceed more messily than this. “In exchange, may I take the first turn? You did ask for my age earlier.”

“Fine.” This time, I gave him an inch. I was sure that he had a motive for asking, but it was also true that he’d been very considerate so far. Plus, taking a question wasn’t necessarily a bad thing, since that question could also be used to understand the other person’s intentions.
Thus, our game of true or false began. “Then let me ask.” Soon, Auril parted his lips and spoke. “How many people clear the original in the next twenty years?”

That was his first question? That was the thought that popped into my mind, but it was too early to let my guard down. Since he’d chosen to ask this particular question despite the unfavorable exchange rate of three questions to one, this wouldn’t be idle curiosity on his part.
The reason why he’s curious about that...

He must have been curious whether there was anyone available to replace me if need be. And so I just answered honestly. “The only person who came over after clearing the original game was me. At least, as far as I know.” This was an answer that set me up to have the upper hand in this relationship, yet left room for him to not fixate solely on me.
“Hmm, I see.” When the jewel lit up green, Auril simply gave a slight nod, his expression unreadable.

Then it was my turn to ask the questions. I already compiled a list of questions beforehand so there was no need to come up with any. Though I’d need to make some tweaks to them now that this jewel was in front of me.

“Have you used the Fragment of Records Stone before?” I intentionally worded this in a way that he would only be able to answer with yes or no. Of course, this method reduced the amount of information I could obtain, but at least I could fact-check properly. Then, as long as the facts were established, I could infer the rest. That would be more trustworthy to me than anything a third party could say.
“I didn’t think I’d be asked that from the get-go... You really aren’t an easy customer.”
“Your answer?”
“I have used it before.”
So I was right. Confirming the green light came on a brief moment later, I calmly selected the next question.
It was then that Auril asked, almost fascinated, “But how on earth did you know that?”

The answer was simple: because there were little hints of that in our last conversation. To be honest, I just wanted to test it to see if I was right. But in the world of competition, nothing was free. “If you’re curious, ask me later.”
“Ahem...”
“Then let me ask my second question.”
“Go ahead.”
I took a moment to take a breath before launching into the second piece of information I needed to confirm. “Did you create this spiritual world?”
Auril flinched slightly before giving me a strange look. “...I can’t get a sense of your strategy at all.”
“What do you mean by that?”

“It’s hard for me to understand why you would want to know that. If you were just asking out of curiosity, I could understand. But you don’t seem like the type of person to do things from a place of emotion.”

I thought I got what he was trying to say. To this old man, that question would not have seemed cost-effective. Although I hadn’t gotten a definitive answer, the implications were clear. It would have seemed a waste to bother checking that.
But these sorts of things have to be clearly addressed.

This space to which I was summoned on the fifteenth of each month was unique. As the palace and Magic Tower were aware of its existence, much research had been done into it, yet no one was able to figure out the method by which this place had been created. To this day, the Tower’s wizards could only theorize that a wizard much more powerful than they could ever imagine had created this place. So could this old man really be such a great wizard?
“So, your answer?”
Before long, Auril gave me a response. “It is as you think. I created this place.”
“It’s red.” The jewel judged that claim to be false. Just as Auril was wincing, I was busy being puzzled. I didn’t expect a lie to crop up here of all places. My eyes narrowed. “Why?”
“Well...” Auril trailed off. “I guess the jewel deemed my response a bit vague.”

Vague, huh? Because I had previous knowledge about the jewel, I had a general guess as to how this happened. Since the jewel based its responses on how the speaker felt, if the speaker lacked confidence in the claim themselves, the light wouldn’t turn green.
