The standard asking price was several million stones.
His armor looks like it’s good quality too...
“What are all of you standing around talking for? You said you’d help me find my teammates!”
“Jackson, you go over there and calm that barbarian bastard down.”
“That’s easy. Hey, barbarian! Are you hungry? Have some beef jerky!”
“Oh! Beef jerky! But... do you not have alcohol?”
“Haha, here it is. If you’re bored, let’s drink together.”

Droff assigned one of his party members to the barbarian and exchanged glances with the rest. As their eyes met, everyone nodded silently to indicate their agreement with the plan. Unanimity was achieved in an instant.
“Ugh, I’m so tired from running all day... You guys have something to discuss, right? Can I nap while you do that?”
“Haha, do as you like.”
As if on cue, the barbarian announced he was tired and lay on the ground, and soon the sound of snoring could be heard.
Honk! Hooonk!

At the sight, Droff let go of the last of his guilt. This was the guy’s own fault. Who could resist when he was pretty much begging to be mugged? Droff exchanged hand signals with his teammates and they slowly crept up to the barbarian.
Now.
Weapons were fired from all directions at once. But... what the hell?
Khak!

The tip of his sword was obstructed by something hard. His blade bounced off like he’d just tried to stab some kind of barrier, and the noise it made was also strange. Unlike the sound he usually heard when he slashed through flesh and leather, a sound not unlike scraping a stone wall rang out.
“...W-What the—?”
While everyone was busy scrambling, the barbarian jerked up without a single drop of blood on him, raised a fist, and then shouted like he’d been waiting for this: “We have a problem!”

“Ha... I didn’t think that would actually work.” After their first plunderer hunt succeeded, Felic Barker huffed a laugh. He had been hesitant while he was playing along with it, but after seeing the results, he had to admit it paid off.
“Commander, there was no loot in the bags, but they have a substantial amount of equipment.”
“I’m sure. Looks like this ain’t their first rodeo.”

This was the unfair thing about this world. Rather than hunting monsters to undergo organic growth, stabbing fellow adventurers in the back got you much further ahead. Though if you did it wrong, you could end up getting a little too ahead of yourself and dying before your time.
“Now, what do you think? About my strategy,” I asked, straightening my shoulders with pride.

Felic nodded charitably. “It’s not bad. No, to be honest, this is innovative.” He was greatly impressed and went on to praise me for a long while. “To start, having someone like you act as the herder and infiltrate the teams already cinches it. Who can react to both an ambush from the inside and an attack from the outside?”

As a matter of fact, during the battle just now, every member of that party had their fronts turned to me. As soon as the clan members hiding in Reed Forest attacked, they all fell like dominos. The entire battle took around ten seconds.
“Anyway, the barbarian race is truly amazing! People are bound to be suspicious of a child in the labyrinth, but nothing like that happened this time!”
Was that meant to be a compliment? The question popped into my head, but I just tossed it away. It wasn’t like I was a real barbarian, so I could just take it as high praise.
Anyway, that should be enough to prove how great this method is...

It was now time to move on to the next stage of my plan. There was one sole reason why I shared this strategy with them. “I’m glad you like it! Then will you guys use my method too?” I would likely have to work with these guys for the next while, but I didn’t want to loot good, innocent adventurers. And being a bystander while they got murdered didn’t sit right with me, either. That was why I was trying to persuade these guys to hunt plunderers instead.
“I wish we could, but...” At my question, Felic expressed his concerns. “Unfortunately, this method has a fatal flaw.”
“What is it?”
“You are the only barbarian here. It is a good strategy, but it’s not efficient for all of us to flock together every time—”

“Don’t worry. I already have a solution for that. Hey, you, and you there.” I grinned and called forth the men I’d scouted out in advance from Teams One and Two, ordering them to take off their clothes.
“Um, why are we getting undressed...?”
What do you mean why? I’m trying to check your muscles. Okay, there’s quite a bit of water weight to them but they should be big enough.
Slide.
When I took a step forward, the two undressed men stepped back, covering their upper bodies with their arms. What, did I imply I was going to do something bad?
“Um, if you could tell us what you’re going to do...”
“I am going to turn you both into warriors.”
I took out the items I brought with me. Did they finally realize what I was trying to do? The two men’s eyes went wide and they shouted, “That’s—!”
“No way!”
It was a brush and dye.

The surrealist painter Salvador Dali once said, “I am not strange. I am just not normal.” The impressionist painter Vincent Van Gogh once said, “I know nothing with any certainty, but the sight of the stars makes me dream.” Pablo Picasso once said something as well: “Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up.” I wondered if there too would come a day when I could leave such famous words as theirs behind.
I had no way of knowing for sure right now, but I spoke anyway. “Stay still! Unless you want to die!”
The two of them kept squirming. Ugh, how ticklish could it be? The lines kept ending up crooked.
Brush, brush.

The more external distractions there were, the more I focused. Using four common colors—red, green, blue, and black—I channeled the wisdom of my predecessors in my heart and focused them on my brushstrokes, expressing them in a form of art that the ordinary person could not hope to understand. Rather than paper, human skin served as my canvas.
Brush, brush.
The ordinary people surrounding me kept muttering.
“Looks like some kind of graffiti.”
“So crooked...”
Tsk, how barbaric. They don’t even know what modern art is.
“Ahem!” When I coughed to show my displeasure, they shut up.
Whew, that’s much better. I should have done that ages ago.
I continued my work in silence. It didn’t take long. It was fun at first, but the more it dragged on, the more boring it became.
“All finished! You can stand up now.” When I haphazardly wrapped things up and patted the two guys on the back, they timidly stood up.
Jeez, you’re killing the creator’s muse.

“Why are you covering the tattoos with your arms?” I removed their arms, which were covering their upper bodies out of shame so that my art was on full display. I was quite satisfied, although they weren’t nearly as good as the tattoos on my body.

“...It’s less obvious than I thought.” The clan leader, who had been looking at me like something was wrong with me earlier, seemed surprised by the finished product. In the dark labyrinth, minor inaccuracies weren’t that noticeable. But as the artist, I couldn’t help but notice the flaws in my creation.
“Why are you looking down at the ground?” I demanded. “Are you ashamed?”
Look at those meek expressions and attitudes. No one will buy that they’re barbarians if they act like that.
“Come here. I will turn you into real warriors.”
I asked the clan leader for his understanding and started correcting them. It wasn’t too hard. It took about thirty minutes.
“B-Behelahhh!”
“Louder!”
“Behelahhh!”
“Good. And what do you say when you run?”
“I’m lost! Help me!”
“Snore!”
Honk! Hooonk!
“Sit!”
Slump.
Okay, now you’re a bit like barbarians.
In the middle of the night, the crescent moon high in the sky, Erwen Fornacci di Tersia knocked on the door of a house.
Knock, knock.

The door opened about a minute later with a creak. The elf man who opened the door froze when he saw Erwen’s face. Her grim expression told him exactly why she came to visit him at this time of night. “...You’ve made a decision.”
“Yes.” Her short answer showed not even the slightest hesitation, which made the man sigh sadly. It wasn’t that he couldn’t sympathize with how this child felt.
“The process of gaining the power of a pureblood is much more terrible than you imagine, and it’s also not something you can achieve just because you want it.”
“I know.”
“Please, why don’t you reconsider one last time?” the man asked, unable to watch this happen. He could already clearly see the path this child would end up walking in the future.

But Erwen’s resolve remained unchanged. “Sorry, but I’ve already made my decision. Please help me. Help me become a pureblood.” Erwen raised her lowered head. Her amber eyes, which were once always bright, now contained only a thirst for power.

The man’s chest felt tight. He had seen people with eyes like hers reach their end far too many times. However, he could not dare refuse Erwen’s request. “All right. I will help you.” Regardless of how powerful he became or whether his clan called him a hero or not, he would still always be a villain to the di Tersia sisters.
“Thank you. I’ll be going now.” Erwen turned around and began to slowly walk away.
As he watched her, the man found himself stopping her. “Wait.”
“...Is there something you want to say?”
“If... yes, if...”
If there were a way to bring that man back to life, what would you do?

The man wanted to ask this question but couldn’t bring himself to continue. “Nothing. I just had a foolish thought. It’s late, you should go home. I will relay word of your decision to the council of elders.”
“Yes.” Erwen, who had stopped for a moment to tilt her head, turned back around to leave. This time, the man did not stop her.
No, he couldn’t stop her.
Not only had that man, the one who knew about the Stone of Revival, been absent from the gathering this month, but the person the stone would be used to save had already been decided.

chapters.title: Chapter 315: Inheritance (4)
paragraphs: “Now, now, everyone, have a drink! I’m buying, so don’t even think about sitting this out! Hahaha!”
Time passed and once the labyrinth closed, Amelia and I joined the after-party. The location was the tavern run by the Rainwales sisters’ adoptive father.
“Haha! Iron Mask! Do you remember what that guy said while his intestines were spilling out of him? ‘H-Help me!’ Uh... you don’t think it’s funny...?”
“It’s not funny at all.”
“I-I see...?”
I gave Dumbo, who was pretending to be friendly out of excitement, a stony look before getting up from my seat. Then I headed to Felic Barker.
“Hey, Iron Mask!”
“Barker.”
“Haha, I told you to call me Fel.”
“No, this is easier.”
“A drink?”
“Sure.”

When I sat beside him to drink, the guy started talking nonstop. Most of the talk was flattery directed at me since the Fashion Barbarian strategy worked just as well as I expected. No, it actually exceeded expectations. According to him, the “warriors” who received training from me and were split between each team had even higher batting averages than I did. Well, that couldn’t be helped, since I was constantly covering my face with a helmet as per my nickname. People who showed their faces were bound to look less suspicious.
“This is a masterstroke! For some reason, they trusted you more than the child herders!”
“Then you won’t need herders from now on?”

“Hmm, I don’t know. I think it’s still too early to decide. I don’t know how long this strategy will last us, either.” Although I casually threw that out there just in case, the clan chief showed no intention of letting the sisters go. He may not have looked it, but he had good judgment. “Besides, I don’t know about the others, but I think the Rainwales sisters are very talented. After a few years, they’ll become great additions to the clan.”
So, you’re not going to let them go so easily, huh? Ugh, and it’s not like I can slit his throat here either.

I just quietly sipped my drink. To be honest, Felic Barker was the biggest obstacle to our plan. Well, to be more precise, the problem was one of the essences in his possession—the rare rank-four Sea Merchant. It was a neutral monster that you had an extremely low probability of encountering while sailing around the ocean on the sixth floor. In most cases, it never attacked first, and when encountered, if you threw a certain amount of mana stones into the ocean it swam in, it threw you back something called bluestone, a high-grade material used for equipment. Of course, since it was a monster, it was also possible to hunt it, and if you happened to overcome the extreme odds and obtain its essence, you were able to acquire a unique active skill called Unhealthy Contract.
The only one currently bound by the contract is the sister.
It was this Unhealthy Contract that was the problem. This man had created a heinous contract, and we had to release Laura from it first in order to save her.
Ha... how did this precious essence end up in the hands of a guy like this?
The thought pissed me off so I flat-out asked Felic. “How did you obtain the essence of a Sea Merchant? I heard that’s a very rare essence.”
“Oh, that? Why are you asking all of a sudden?”
“I was always curious. I just couldn’t ask before because we weren’t close.”

“Hahaha! Then are we close now?” When I shrugged to avoid answering, the guy interpreted the gesture in whatever way he wanted and started explaining. “It was back when I was still active in a clan aboveground. I was young back then too...”

Without all the extra, unnecessary information, his story could be summed up as follows: while on a quest with his clan, a Sea Merchant dropped an essence, and this guy was so money-crazy that he stole the test tube containing it.
“I was planning on listing it for auction to make a quick buck once some time passed and things quieted down. I figured I could live the rest of my life without worrying about money!”

But despite his high hopes, Felic’s crime was discovered before long. And so he fled to Noark. In the process, he apparently ended up unable to sell the essence in the test tube and absorbed it himself.
“Bjon.” We’d just gotten to that point in the story when Amelia came up to me.
“Ah, Emily...”
“I’m thinking of leaving soon.”
“Really? Then I’m going to head out now.”
When I excused myself from his company and got up, Felic flashed me a wicked grin. “Keke, have a nice time!”
Taking in that smile, I thought, I can’t wait for the day I get to bash this guy’s head in.
Tap.

Arua Raven closed the book she had been reading all night. Then she stretched and got up from her spot. When she did, the items she had pushed into a corner of the lab caught her eye. They were Bjorn Yandel’s belongings.
“I should... get rid of those now...”

Raven let out a long sigh. Time was truly a cruel mistress. She had searched through various books, convinced there must be some big secret, but she’d discovered nothing. As the days passed, Raven was growing less and less able to ignore reality.

Perhaps this was the kind of person she was. Emotions were temporary. No matter how angry or sad she got, as time passed, she inevitably found herself thinking logically again. Bjorn Yandel was dead, and so it was now time to sell these items and divide what remained in accordance with his will. Instead of sifting through books until late at night, that was what she should do.

But the more she thought that way, the more an inexplicable sense of shame crept up on her. That was why she had been reading until just now. Bjorn Yandel’s death had changed Missha’s and Erwen’s worlds. Those two would never get to go back to how things were before. But her?
Sigh...

Not long ago, she started eating at every meal again, worried that her body would break down at this rate. She was no longer as desperate about searching through books to solve the mystery, either, and sometimes found herself thinking that it wouldn’t make a difference anyway. And that wasn’t all—she even drank tea and could force herself to smile when the seniors from her school struck up conversations with her. Raven knew that if time continued to pass like this, eventually, she would return to her everyday life. She was like a match—she could burn hot, but couldn’t burn for long.
It’s not like... I didn’t care about him too...

She had also liked Bjorn. She may not have seen him as a romantic interest, but she felt the most amount of human affection possible for him. She had learned a lot from him, and being around him was fun. He was probably the first person to have had as much of an emotional impact on her since that woman. But just as she did back then, she was recovering from his loss, and that fact brought her guilt.
“...I should just go through it for now. I can sell it another time,” Raven said, almost like she was trying to convince herself. Then she started officially organizing Bjorn Yandel’s belongings.
She appraised the equipment and wrote down the market prices, then she went through the items in sub-space. As she was doing this, something caught her eye.
“Huh? This has to be...”

The Golden Mask was an item that could be obtained in the first floor’s Rift, the Bloody Citadel, but the method for doing so had been erased from the copy of The Complete Book of Rifts in her possession.
“How did Mr. Yandel...?”

When she watched Yandel defeat the Vampire with the Tears of a Goddess back then, she had theorized he had his own copy of The Complete Book of Rifts. But when he made a warrior’s oath and claimed it was a coincidence, she had let go of her suspicions.
“...Was that all a lie?”
Perhaps he had owned The Complete Book of Rifts or had read it once. Just as she was thinking this, though, she recalled her master suspecting him of being an evil spirit.
Come on, what kind of ridiculous thought...?

Raven chuckled and continued organizing the backpack. “What... is this?” Raven discovered a magical device of unknown origin. Judging by the symbols on it, it seemed to both record conversations and allow the user to use Secret Voice.
Click.
Raven pressed the groove at the bottom. Then voices began to flow out.
“What is there to think about? They’re NPCs, anyway.”
“But they are comrades who have been with—”
“What a joke. You think those guys will think like that once they find out your identity?”
Neither of those voices were Bjorn Yandel’s. Then who were the two people in this conversation? The answer came to her quickly.
“The person your comrades thought of as a friend was the real Hans. And as you know, the real Hans is no longer in this world.”
“But... I consider them to be my real comrades.”

It was a conversation between Hans Chrisen and the dwarf from Noark they met in Doppelganger Forest. This must have been the weakness the dwarf had been talking about. She never thought Bjorn would still have this. Anyway, if they wanted to sell it, it probably had to be reset.
Shaaaaaa.
Raven channeled mana into the device to figure out how its mana circuits were structured. To someone who specialized in magical devices, this was an easy task.
So you have to press it twice and then press and hold it once.

Although she had learned how to reset it like she wanted, Raven did not retract her mana and instead continued to explore the circuit structure. It was unusual, so she wanted a closer look. She went further and started reading the residual mana.
What, the maximum number of times a recording can be played back is fixed? Did they use a cheap core or something?
Raven’s hand then flinched. “Huh?” This magical device could only play back a single recording up to one hundred times, and when that limit was exceeded, it was automatically reset.
There are only two plays left?

The number of times it had been listened to was a bit strange—a bit too strange to write off as a simple error. So she channeled more mana into it to take a closer look. Then she checked the playback history.

“What the...?” Except for the first two replays, the rest were from after they left Doppelganger Forest. Put simply, that meant that the person who had replayed it the remaining ninety-six times was Bjorn Yandel. “Why did Mr. Yandel listen to this conversation so many times...?”
She had no idea, but Raven instinctively sensed something was off.
Knock, knock.
Someone knocked on the door to her laboratory. Raven stopped what she was doing for the moment and opened the door. A completely unexpected person stood before her. “Miss Missha...?”
“Yeah... can I come in...?”
“Ah, yes! Of course. Come in! Wait a minute, I need to clean up the room...”
“You don’t have to put in so much effort.”
“Right... but what brings you here all of a sudden?” Raven was flustered by the sudden visit.
“There’s something I have to tell you...”
She suddenly got an ominous feeling.
“Drinking again?”
“Ah, there was nothing else to do, so...”
When Amelia returned to the inn, she glanced at me as she hung her coat on the hanger. Jeez, why was she judging me? Did she know how boring sitting here alone was?
“Did you get our share of the loot without issue?”
Amelia chuckled at my question. “What, you think I can’t even calculate something like that properly?”
“That’s not it, but you never know. They could have played a trick behind your back...”
“Don’t worry. I made sure we got our share. Well, not that it matters.”
“That’s true.”
Our objective wasn’t money. Although it was hard to say it was an entirely meaningless pursuit, only once we saved Laura and found a way to return to our original world would it become meaningful.
“So, what are you going to do next? Judging by the conversation I had with him, it seems terminating the contract and getting her out of it before the incident in a few months will be difficult.”
“Nothing changes for now. We will keep trying. At least until a better method comes to mind.”
“Sure...”

It had already been about two weeks since we got back to Noark. Since leaving the labyrinth, we continued to brainstorm amongst ourselves about how we could save Laura. But even after several days of talking, we still hadn’t been able to reach a suitable answer.
Ugh, I feel like I might be able to come up with something, but...

The more stifling our situation grew, the more I looked forward to midnight on the 15th. I was hoping that by meeting with Auril Gavis again and obtaining information from the other members, I might be able to cook up a good idea.
“Is it today?”
“In two hours, to be exact.”

Amelia nodded at my answer and went to wash up, and when she came out, we just chatted out of boredom. Before long, the time came, and there were about ten seconds left until midnight. I closed my eyes and concentrated on the sound of the second hand.
Tick, tick, tick...
Before long, I heard the tenth tick.
“...What the...?”
I immediately opened my eyes.
Tick, tick, tick...
The ticking of the second hand continued to punctuate the silence.
“...Are you back already?” Amelia asked, but I just stared blankly at the clock.
Tick, tick, tick...
What the—why can’t I go?

chapters.title: Chapter 316: Memory (1)
paragraphs: Tick, tick, tick...

The second hand of the clock made a full circle, marking the beginning of the next minute, but I still didn’t get called to the spiritual world. After checking the date and time again, I even waited until morning just in case my clock was broken, but nothing changed. How did this happen? I discussed the possibilities with Amelia all night and narrowed the list down to three explanations.

First, that this incident was a singular, random error, completely accidental and not the result of someone’s handiwork. There was a nonzero probability of this. Whether a device was electronic or magical, it was ultimately created by a person. Although rare, there were times when even sub-space rings malfunctioned and the items inside could not be taken out. The possibility of that was still minimal, though.

The next one made more sense: Auril Gavis had banned me from the spirit world. This was a more likely hypothesis than number one. If you just looked at how the old man treated me, anyone would say he had no reason to banish me, but then again, you could never read someone’s mind. I couldn’t rule out the possibility that this was some kind of trick on his part.

Finally, something beyond his control could have happened to Auril Gavis. This was also a very plausible theory. Actually, I decided this was the most likely of the three. Although I couldn’t even imagine what would have had to happen for that inhuman old man to run into trouble, this was a world full of monsters, after all. Even he could have people he considered a threat, the prime example of this being the palace.
Whatever, let’s go to sleep.

Since I had no way of figuring out the answer, it was pointless to spend any more time worrying about it. And so I decided to wait until the 15th of the next month to deal with this and, as the days passed, I entered the labyrinth once more.
“Hahaha! It went well again! If we keep this up, we’ll all be rich soon!”
Nothing of note had happened in the labyrinth. All I did was spend my time looting plunderers until the labyrinth closed like last time.
When midnight on the 15th rolled around again, things went the same way as last time.
“You didn’t go this time, either?”
“...Yeah.”
My mind remained in my body again even though it was time.
Ha, this is so frustrating...
Just what the hell was going on? While the walls continued to close in on us more and more, time continued its relentless march forward.
Wow, time flies.
I wiped the bitter smile off my face and folded the calendar in my hand before putting it in my pocket. It had already been six months since the day I came to the past.
Slide.
When I got up and picked up my coat, Amelia asked without even looking in my direction, “Are you going today too?”
“There’s nothing to do here, anyway. You?”
“I’ll stay here.”
After that dry conversation with Amelia, I left the inn. Most of our conversations were like that these days—short, shallow, and always on an invisible edge.
Ugh, so damn uncomfortable.

It was bearable at first, but now that there were just a few days left until D-Day, it had gotten much worse. That was because we still hadn’t found a good solution. The community hadn’t opened once since it closed all those months ago.
...Did he really ban me?

I was starting to think that was the case now, which made me want to check it out. The head of Orcules was in this underground city. If I asked him directly, I would be able to find out if I was the only one who got kicked out or if the community server itself was down.
What am I even thinking? It’s not like that’s going to change anything.

I sighed and walked the streets of the underground city. I’d become quite familiar with this place. Aside from the eastern district, which was the home of Orcules, I’d pretty much memorized the main streets.

“Oh, Captain! You’re here!” When I arrived at the clan’s base located inside the castle walls, Dumbo greeted me. Having gone into the labyrinth with me for some months, he was no longer as afraid of me as before. Rather, he was acting no different than a henchman. “Come, come, sit here! Would you like something to drink?”
“Something light.”
“Haha, just wait a moment! I’ll get it straight away!”

As I sat on the empty seat, acting all arrogant, Dumbo quickly brought me a drink and sat beside me. Like a jukebox, he began a one-sided conversation. Most of the chatter was about rumors and recent events in the city, and the way he talked was entertaining enough not to be boring.
“Oh, right, Captain. Did you hear that news about barbarian hearts?”
Suddenly, a topic I couldn’t ignore popped up. “Hearts? What about them? Tell me.”
“Ah, I guess you didn’t hear? Well, they say that word has already spread in the overworld that barbarian hearts are being sold at a high price because they can be used as magical ingredients.”
“...What?”

The Magic Tower’s announcement about barbarian hearts being a precious magical ingredient was supposed to be made in about ten years, a long while after the war between the elf and barbarian races. But that story was already going around?
Did the future change because of me? No, that can’t be possible...
I pressed Dumbo for the details because I just couldn’t believe it, and he quickly clarified.
“Ah, it wasn’t the Magic Tower that announced this. It was actually just a false rumor.”
“False rumor?”
“Apparently, our commander put in a request some months ago for the Melter merchant company to spread that rumor around in the overworld.”
What? What the...

Without needing any further explanation, everything clicked into place for me. That was natural. There was only one reason why Clan Leader Felic Barker would make that request of Noark’s one and only merchant company and connection to aboveground.
“I guess the commander thought spreading those rumors would make plunderers more susceptible to our tactics. Ah, but I don’t think he expected the rumors to spread this much.”
Dumbo seemed to think I didn’t understand because he threw in details I didn’t even ask for. In addition to rumors spreading in the overworld, apparently, the rumor was even circulating in Noark now.
When I heard that, a curse flew from my lips. “God damn it.”
“...Sorry?”
“Quiet.”
Dumbo clammed up at a single word from me and I calmly organized my thoughts, which were all jumbled. It would probably be revealed to be a rumor soon.
But perhaps this was the start of it...

This thought wouldn’t leave me. Maybe it was because of these rumors that Felic Barker spread that some wizards began doing research into the subject, which then led to a price tag being placed on barbarian hearts ten years in the future.
Then that means I could be the cause of all that insanity...?
It was still just a thought, but the problem was that it didn’t feel like a logical leap at all.
“Dumbo, I’m leaving.”
“Sorry? Okay!”

I was not in the mood to be socializing at the clan house, but when I left, I found there was nowhere for me to go. I was walking around the interior of the castle when an old man who was passing by suddenly stopped and started talking to me.
“You must be Iron Mask.”
It was hard to ignore. Since this world was particularly unkind to the elderly, a person had to have some level of skill to survive to that age.
“And who are you?” I asked cautiously.

The old man chuckled and took out a mana stone from his pocket. “This is the kind of person I am.” As soon as he opened his mouth, the mana stone glowed and turned into bread. He was an alchemist—a transmutation-type wizard who had the ability to change mana stones into bread or iron.
I never thought I’d run into someone like this in the hallway.

In a way, an alchemist was a bigger fish than the lord of the castle or the head of Orcules. At least, that was the case in Noark. As far as I knew, there were only two alchemists here. The city wouldn’t immediately fall into ruin if the position of lord of the castle wasn’t filled for a while, but if the position of alchemist became vacant, the city would collapse. This wasn’t an exaggeration, but the reality.
“Haha, judging by your surprise, I guess this is your first time seeing alchemy?”
First time seeing alchemy or not, I couldn’t understand it. Who would have imagined I would meet someone who could be considered the very foundation of this city in a corridor?
Wait, even if this is the castle, the alchemist wouldn’t be foolish enough to wander around alone...
When I carefully glanced around in disbelief, I sensed gazes on me from all sides. Since they were difficult to see with the naked eye, it seemed that all of them had a concealment essence.
“You are more perceptive than I thought. Don’t worry too much. They’re just this old man’s guards.”

Perceptiveness aside, they were the ones who were letting me sense their presence like they had no intention of hiding it to begin with—almost like some kind of warning for me to not even think about doing something foolish.
“Ah, anyhow, I haven’t even told you my name yet. My name is Marfa Ipaello. You can call me whatever you prefer, but if I had to choose, I’d prefer you call me by my last name.”
“...Iron Mask.”
“I’m aware. It’s fate that we met like this. Why don’t we talk for a moment?”
“All right.” I accepted his offer without much hesitation. He could have been another alchemist famous for his foul temper, but I knew this old man’s name through Amelia.
This is the person who created the Blessing of Lethe.
That alone was worth talking to him about.
“Hmm, you are as hardy as they say. Come, let’s go.”
As they say, huh? So this meeting wasn’t a coincidence, then. He came to see me.

Ipaello started walking down the corridor first, and I followed behind. Even though we were heading up to the third floor where access was restricted, no one stopped me because this man was next to me. That was how we arrived at the alchemist’s workshop.
“We’re okay from here, so everyone can step out.”
It’s kind of similar to a wizard’s lab, but kind of different.
I started scanning my surroundings as soon as I entered, and the old man kicked out the guards who were in hiding before offering me a seat. “Sit. If you want something to drink, let me know.”

“I’m fine.” Normally this was the moment I’d stubbornly demand meat and assert my dominance in the conversation, but I skipped that this time. If I were caught being rude, I was certain to get an earful from Amelia. This old man was the savior who took Amelia in at a young age. Even without taking his position into account, I couldn’t treat him poorly. Well, I still couldn’t use honorifics, either, since I had to save face as a barbarian. “So, why did you call me here?”
“I just wondered what kind of person you were. This is the first time I’ve heard those children have so much fun while talking about the labyrinth.”
“Those children?” I asked, feigning ignorance.
“I’m talking about Laura and Amelia. Sweet children. Sometimes when I feel lonely, I call them over to my workshop, give them snacks, and ask them to chat with me for a while.”
“...I see.”
“I was quite worried, but now that I’ve met you, my worries have disappeared. They are unfortunate children. I hope you take good care of them.”
“I will,” I said with a nod. Then, after a moment’s thought, I carefully asked, “But if you’re going to ask a favor like that, wouldn’t it be better if you just took them in?”
“Haha, that’s not easy for me to do at the moment.” He spoke vaguely and omitted the details, but I knew his situation to some extent.
At first, he was only able to provide snacks for them, but after the death of the other alchemist, he took Amelia out of the team completely and raised her himself.

Previous attempts to take them out had likely failed because there were currently two alchemists in the city. So long as there was someone out there who could replace him, he couldn’t enjoy absolute power.
“How are those girls these days?”
“They are well. I’m trying to prevent them from doing dangerous work as much as possible.”
“...I see.”

After that, the natural topic of conversation was the Rainwales sisters. Alchemist Ipaello asked how the children were doing and I answered him honestly. Then, waiting for the right moment, I began to speak. “But can our conversation be heard over there?”
“If you’re talking about the guards, you can speak without hesitation. They won’t hear it. Is there something you want to ask?”
“Is there a way to remove the effects of an essence through alchemy?”

“Effects? If you’re talking about a poison, that’s possible...” The old man answered my question without much thought before trailing off for a beat. “...Are you talking about the Unhealthy Contract?”
“Maybe.” I shrugged. Was that enough of an answer?
“...That is beyond the realm of alchemy.”
“I see.”

“Yes, unfortunately.” Ipaello smiled a bitter smile. I was also disappointed but I didn’t let it show. Yeah, it made sense that something that didn’t exist in the game wouldn’t exist in the past either. “Is there anything else you’re curious about?”

Ipaello seemed to really like me considering how friendly he was being, and so I asked about the pill called the Blessing of Lethe while I was at it. But his reaction to my question was a bit strange.
“Blessing of Lethe? What is that?”
“The... medicine that erases memories.”
“Ah, that! But that medicine doesn’t have a name yet...”
Uh, I didn’t expect that...
“But Lethe, huh? It doesn’t sound bad. It’s also very romantic, comparing oblivion to a blessing.”
I let out a silent sigh of relief at that. No wonder it was called Lethe.
“Okay, I was just wondering what to name it, so I guess I can go with that.”
I never thought this would be the backstory.

chapters.title: Chapter 317: Memory (2)
paragraphs: To be honest, the name Blessing of Lethe stood out to me from the moment I heard it. It couldn’t be a coincidence that a medicine that could wipe someone’s memory would have the same name as a river in Greek mythology, a mythology that didn’t even exist in this world. Of course, I didn’t think much of it at the time. That was because this was a city where evil spirits lived their lives openly. There would be nothing strange about that name coming out of a player’s mouth at some point.
But to think that player would be me...
From the false rumor spread by Felic Barker earlier to incidents like this, the blows kept coming one after another and it wasn’t even funny.
While I was sitting there blankly, Ipaello eyed me suspiciously. “Wait a minute... How did you know about that medicine? So far, it has only been distributed to less than twenty people.”
Oh, that.
“I heard Felic Barker received it from the lord of the castle.”
“Hmm, is that so?”

Despite his slightly skeptical look, I proudly straightened my shoulders. I wasn’t exactly lying. Felic Barker really did have the Blessing of Lethe. Of course, he didn’t exactly flat-out tell me that, instead just dropping hints that he had received a secret medicine the alchemist supplied to the lord of the castle as a reward.

“True, the lord of the castle seemed to be watching him with interest recently, so that could be the case.” Ipaello accepted this without further argument, but I guessed he was curious about one last thing. “But where did you hear the name Blessing of Lethe?”
“I don’t know, I think those guys said it. I may have misheard it.”
“Haha, I guess they’ve already created slang for it?” Soon, the suspicion disappeared from his eyes. That was one issue sorted, at least.
Now that I was in the clear, I snuck in a question of my own. “But is that medicine okay to use? I heard it was only made recently. It doesn’t cause any other issues?”
“Not to worry. Aside from some irregularity in the amount of memory that gets erased, there are no side effects.”
Irregularity, huh?
It seemed the research needed to mass produce the medicine with consistent performance hadn’t been conducted yet.
“But when you take into account what most people would be using it for, a side effect like that doesn’t really matter, does it?”
“That’s true, but it could be defective or not have any effect.”
“There’s little chance of that happening. If anything, it’s overly effective. And after the first test, there have never been any defective batches.”
“Overly effective?”

Like the scholar he was, the old man seemed excited when the conversation shifted to his field of study. Ipaello asked me to wait a moment, then brought out a box that was stored in a corner of the workshop. “Now, this is the first dose of this secret medicine that I produced.” The box he opened contained a pure white pill. Although there were more than ten storage spaces, except for the one, they were all empty.
“It looks twice as big as the one I saw.”
“Haha, it’s not just the size that’s big. One pill and almost all of your memories will be erased.”
“...What?”

An entire lifetime of memories would disappear if you took this thing? Then wasn’t it weird to call it defective? Wait, why was he even making a mass-produced product when he had a prototype with better performance in the first place?

When I asked this out of pure curiosity, Ipaello’s answer was typical of a researcher at a large company. “Ah, that’s because it costs tremendous amounts of money to produce even one of these pills. The lord of the castle said we wouldn’t break even.”
As an office worker, this was a completely understandable explanation.
True, since the medicine was originally made to be used on people who witnessed things they shouldn’t have, a few days’ memories would suffice.
After that, I spoke with Ipaello for about five more minutes, and that marked the end of our conversation for that day.

Time continued to pass, and soon it was the day before D-Day. We ran through our plan one last time. Well, after everything was said and done, the question as to whether it could be called a plan remained, but what could we do? Sink or swim, we had to try. Anyway, to summarize the major parts of the plan, it went like this:

First, we would infiltrate the castle and seize the Fragment of Records Stone. This was my sole responsibility. There wouldn’t be any troops in the castle tomorrow, and Amelia seemed to think me capable of robbing an empty house just fine. Anyway, while I was busy in the castle, Amelia would be sticking close to her young sister. The problem with our plan arose here.

After joining Amelia, we would run away with the sisters. At least, that was what we were saying we’d do, but we hadn’t properly ironed out how exactly we’d do so. Even if that old guy found a way to break the Unhealthy Contract Felic Barker placed on Laura, everything else would have to be left to improvisation.

Third, the Rainwales sisters would obtain new identities above ground and live happily ever after. This was the extent of our plan. To be honest, I didn’t think it would go well at all. The problem wasn’t that it wasn’t detailed enough. The problem was that the most important component was missing.
“A timeline once observed cannot change.”

No matter what you did in the past, the future remained the same, and there had been ample evidence of that so far. Dwalkie and Raven, the barbarian hearts, and even the Blessing of Lethe; if I already had this many examples, Amelia would have even more. She would have been feeling déjà vu several times each day we lived through, recalling her old memories.
Tap.
Just then, something touched my forearm. When I turned my head to the side, I could see Amelia holding out a bottle of alcohol.
“...For me?”
“Yes.”
“Out of the blue?” I asked incredulously.
“Tomorrow is D-Day,” Amelia answered, expressionless.
“I mean, still...”
“I also have something to tell you.”
Ah, you should have said that from the start.

I took the bottle and uncorked it, laughing as I did so. Since she couldn’t get drunk, she wanted me to have a drink in her stead. Well, even if you were sober, it was easier to talk if the other party was drunk.
“Hah...” I chugged down half the bottle in one go, then said, “So what do you have to say? Is it important?”
“Not exactly. But... I feel like I haven’t been able to talk to you properly recently.” Amelia avoided my eyes as she spoke. Was she embarrassed right now?
“Uh... R-Right...” That also made me embarrassed for some reason. Was it because of the alcohol?
Whew, this drink is really strong. And super bitter too.
Just as I was about to ask where on earth she got this drink, Amelia called my name. “Yandel.”
“I thought you wanted us to use pseudonyms even at the inn.”
“That ends today, anyway. Even if anyone hears, it won’t be a problem.”
“...So what do you want to talk about?”
“There is something I need to tell you,” Amelia said, before quickly correcting herself. “Actually, it’s more of an apology.”
“...An apology?” I got an ominous feeling the moment I heard that. And as always, my instincts never led me astray.
Thud, roll.
The half-empty liquor bottle fell from my hand and rolled onto the floor. Ha, no wonder the drink was so bitter.
“What did you put in it?” I asked, placing my practically paralyzed arm on my thigh.

Amelia’s face was still expressionless as she answered. “All the medicine I have that is not life-threatening.” Saying something like that with that look on her face made her really look like a serial killer. But despite the shiver that went down my spine, I was able to learn one thing.
So, she isn’t trying to kill me.
I swung the small emergency hammer that I carried in my thigh holster like a dagger as hard as I could. Unfortunately, the attack failed.
Whoom!
Amelia leaned her upper body back and the hammer hit empty air. “I knew you would do that the moment you moved your hand down.”

Considering I used a surprise attack every time we fought, it seemed she was able to figure out what I was trying to do just by the look in my eyes. “Goddamn it.” My muscles lost their strength and my body staggered when I stood up, but Amelia prevented me from falling to the ground.
Yeah, I knew you would do that.

“Ah...!” Taking advantage of the fact that she was supporting my weight, I quickly moved my arm to put pressure on Amelia’s neck. The technical term for this move was the Triangle Choke. But this woman wasn’t that easy to beat, unfortunately.
Bang!

A powerful blow landed on my temple and my body was thrown back. As my head spun, I saw two women in front of me. It seemed she’d managed to summon a doppelganger in that brief moment to deliver a high kick to my head.
I’m done for.
In addition to being drugged, my head was also injured and my body wouldn’t move at all.

“...You really never make things easy.” Amelia let out a scoff, then picked me up and laid me on the bed. Then she started a one-sided monologue. “Sorry. It seems I won’t ever be able to be your comrade.”
I used the last of my strength to grab Amelia’s wrist as she turned around. “You... what are... you trying... to do?”
Amelia did not answer. She just pried my hand off, then put on her equipment piece by piece with a grim look on her face. She looked like she was about to go to battle.
“Open the drawer when you wake up.”
That was the last thing I remembered.

Amelia Rainwales looked into the mirror. Then she straightened her clothes and brushed back her hair. That revealed the scar on her ear, which had been cut a long time ago. It was a wound that would definitely have become a flaw if she wished to live a typical woman’s life, but as it stood, she couldn’t even call this a loss. She’d had to sacrifice much more than this to stand here today.

For some reason, however, she was finding it difficult to leave. Why? Amelia stood in front of the mirror and took stock of her emotions. It wasn’t because she was afraid. After that fated day, life became nothing more than a means to an end for her—and that was still the case even if today changed nothing, meaning decades of effort in pursuit of a single goal would be for naught.

She was not afraid of failure. Rather, that in itself would be almost salvation. While she had been sprinting toward the future without stopping, she had desperately looked forward to this day. At the very least, she could hold onto the fact that she never gave up trying to protect her. Then what was it? What on earth was holding her back?
Amelia turned around, and there was the sleeping barbarian. The strained expression he wore as he asked her what she planned to do was gone and he was even snoring, dead to the world.
Step, step.

Amelia walked over to the bed and opened the drawer to the nightstand. Then she placed the note she had written earlier inside and turned around. At that moment, she remembered a conversation she had a few months ago.
“If I succeed in saving your sister and take care of the logistical hurdles once we return to our time...”
“Then join my clan.”

Even the memory of his offer was absurd. It made no sense realistically. But if she were to let herself imagine it for a moment... it would have been quite enjoyable. Every day she spent exploring the labyrinth with this foolish man would have been full of all kinds of surprises. Yes, no doubt...
It was then that Amelia realized why she couldn’t move her feet. It was out of regret—a lingering regret about a future that would never come to pass.
But feelings were just feelings. If her feet were heavy, she just had to apply more force to move them. She couldn’t stop walking.
Creak.
She took a moment to catch her breath in front of the door and then turned the doorknob hard. When she stepped out, she could see the chaos had already begun.
“F-Fire!”

Flames were rising in the eastern district. Amelia quickly moved through the crowd of people that filled the street. Although she had lied to that man and said that it was tomorrow night, D-Day was actually today.

chapters.title: Chapter 318: Memory (3)
paragraphs: “Motherfuck!” As soon as I opened my eyes, I jumped up from the bed. Everything in front of me was hazy and an acrid scent filled my nose. Outside the window, things were particularly noisy.
Threatening shouts rang out through the glass. “Anyone on the streets will be considered a traitor. Everyone, get inside a building!”
“Kyahhh!” I heard screams split the air at irregular intervals, and each time a loud boom erupted in the distance, a subtle vibration shook the bed.
What the hell is going on? I need information.
Step, step.
I forced my weak body over to the window. The moment I threw it open, black smoke poured into the room and a dry cough burst from my throat.
Cough, cough.
Even as I coughed, I scanned what I could see outside the window. Soldiers were roaming the smoke-filled streets, corralling the citizens.
“It really is a fire.”

I could see a neighborhood engulfed in flames in the distance. It was the eastern district, the home of Orcules. Although it was quite far from my current location, a fire breaking out in an underground city with poor ventilation was bound to fill the entire city with smoke.
Bang! Kwaaang!
Seeing as strange roars were breaking out intermittently, it didn’t appear to be a simple fire.
“Jesus... what the hell is going on?”
I pressed a hand to my throbbing head. It felt like my gears were turning several times slower than usual. It was possibly a leftover side effect of the poison Amelia dosed me with.
Oh yeah, I took poison...
That woke me right up, and what happened before I lost consciousness scrolled through my mind like a panorama.
What the hell is she thinking? And where has she disappeared to?

I didn’t know. But the less I knew, the more I focused on one thing. This was the same as the day I woke up in this body. Putting everything else aside, what was the thing I had to do right now in this moment? The answer came to me quickly.
“Drawer.”

Amelia told me to open the drawer. Perhaps there was an explanation for this situation there. I closed the window and headed to the side of the bed. The drawer on the nightstand thankfully contained a note with only a few lines inside.
The note started off with a short apology. It didn’t take long to read the whole thing, and as soon as I finished, I tore it to shreds. But even then, my anger didn’t fade.
To think today was D-Day.

Amelia had tricked me. It wasn’t written in the note, but the reason why was obvious. She probably wanted to prevent me from interfering with the past any further, thinking that that might change the future.
Ha, I never thought she was someone who could do something so impulsive...

The back of my head still tingled but I tried to center myself and checked the time. It was four-thirty in the morning. Since it had been a little after ten when I drank with Amelia, I had been asleep for about six hours.
Now, then. What to do?

I closed my eyes for a moment and gathered my thoughts. The note Amelia left told me to find the Fragment of Records Stone when I woke up and then go back, saying she would handle the rest on her own. Given the current state of the city, it didn’t seem like it’d be difficult to infiltrate the castle.
Don’t make me laugh. Then what, she’s going to stay here alone?
I didn’t like this plan. But despite those feelings, I also had this thought: What would happen if I really didn’t do anything? How would the future change then?
“...Whatever, let’s get out of here for now.”
I stopped ruminating there and quickly put on my equipment. Since time was running out, I decided I could worry about the rest while I moved.
Creak.
I quickly headed to the castle.

Passing by the soldiers tirelessly herding the civilians through the acrid smoke, I soon arrived at the castle. The gates were already tightly closed and even with the tag that marked me as a member of the lord of the castle’s faction, I wasn’t able to get them to open.
“The lord of the castle has prohibited anyone from entering. They deployed the teams a long time ago. Why are you only here now?”
“...I was sleeping.”
“Then head to the eastern district, even if you’re late. It looks like your clan left to join the campaign ages ago.”
Ugh, so annoying.
“Okay. Good luck.”
I turned around without hesitation, away from the gate. Just because the door was closed didn’t mean there wasn’t a way inside. Barbarians did not ask for permission.
There’s smoke in the air, so they won’t be able to see me.
After moving along the castle wall for a moment, I confirmed no one was around before Leaping high over the wall. But unfortunately, there was a person beyond it.
“W-Who are you!?” The soldier was understandably startled to see me falling from the sky during his patrol.
Smack!

Before he got too noisy, I quickly quieted him and ran toward the inner bailey. Just as Amelia predicted, the castle was a ghost town on D-Day and there was no one around that could pose a threat. All of them were just patrolling soldiers. By now, the core troops would be fighting in the eastern district occupied by Orcules.
“Enemies!”
Smack!
“Enemy invasion!”
Smack!
Thanks to that, I was able to skip through this part of the map quickly. The problems started at the inner bailey.
Kwaaang!
The moment I broke down the doors to the inner bailey and entered the first floor, fearsome-looking adventurers surrounded me.
Yeah, no matter how empty the house, you had to leave something behind, huh?
They were an elite military unit bestowed knightage by the lord. Thanks to the fact that I had visited the castle countless times over the past few months, I knew some of them.
“...Iron Mask, why are you here? You should be at the eastern district where the fight is.”
“Ah, I have something to discuss with the lord of the castle.”
“I never imagined you were one of Orcules’s henchmen.” A bald man whose name I didn’t even remember glared at me with the rage of someone who had been betrayed by a trusted friend.
I didn’t feel any remorse at all. Not only was I not one of Orcules’s henchmen, I never once considered these guys my friends. “Whatever, fight me.”
“I don’t know what kind of reckless bravado you must have to crawl all the way here, but this is your—”
What are these rank-five minions saying? I said let’s fight, not talk. If you’re not coming to me, I’ll go to you.
Kwaaang!
Without wasting any more time on a pointless conversation, I immediately activated Giantization and Leaped into the middle of their formation.
“Behel–ahhh!”
I made my hammer, which was already monster-sized thanks to Giantization, three times larger by combining Transcendence and Swing.
Whooom!

Then I spun like a top and swung my hammer. This was a move called Whirlwind. It was taken from the game that used to be my favorite before I fell into Dungeon and Stone. The special thing about it was that you could enjoy a cool battering sensation along with a cool sound, just like this.
Kwaaang!

Their bones snapped like twigs the moment they were struck by my hammer, and even some of the sturdier guys flew straight into the wall. This made sense considering the hammer I was holding was not a normal weapon.
I’m definitely built to be a tank, but somehow I do better damage than one.

This was No. 87: Kraul’s Demon Grinder—a double-digit Numbers Item that could increase damage by 500 percent when a blunt-weapon skill was active. Put simply, just holding this weapon increased the power of rank-three Swing by five times. There was no way anyone could survive a blow from it.
Ah, none of that matters if they dodged it, though.

“W-What the hell...?” The guys who dove for the floor the moment I swung my hammer and escaped the line of fire stared up at me with dumbfounded looks on their faces. Among them, there was one who managed to come to his senses and fight back.
Arrow, fire, lightning, ax—I checked each of their weapons and smiled.
How is it that not a single one of them uses a sword?

That was the funny thing about Noark. Just because you were a knight didn’t mean you knew how to use an aura. These guys were only recognized by that title for their loyalty. True knights who used auras were probably about one in a hundred.
And as I thought, those guys were all taken to the front lines.

After that, the fight devolved into me striking each one manually with the hammer. Even the warriors covered in heavy, full-body armor couldn’t handle it and dropped like flies when I activated the 50 percent Armor Penetration buff with Down Thrust. About five minutes later, after the remaining few fled, the battle was over. I didn’t bother following them, and I skipped out on looting too. Not only did I not have time for that, but there was no room in my sub-space ring after all the loot we’d stockpiled for the past several months.
...Ugh, I have to take this hammer back with me somehow.
I hurriedly got moving again. My destination was not the study in the castle or the upper floor where the office was—it was the underground shelter Amelia told me about.
Sprint.
I managed to locate the stairs leading down to the basement and started to run down the steps before suddenly stopping in my tracks. Someone was coming up from below.

“I wondered what that commotion was up here...” Coincidentally, it was someone I had met once before, the knight who came to recruit us under the lord of the castle’s instructions. “Iron Mask, what are you doing here?” His name was Rick Omanus. When he spotted me, he drew his sword.
I... accidentally took a wrong turn? There was no time to make an excuse like that.
Voom!

The knight’s judgment was so quick that as soon as he saw me, he immediately imbued his sword with an aura to enter battle mode. An attempt at conversation was only made after that. “Answer, Iron Mask. Why you are here, and in addition, how you know about this place.”
Amelia told me not to answer that question. Although no one knew about this underground shelter now, that would not be the case in the future.
“Are you saying you won’t answer?”
My heart started pounding violently at that.
Thump!

Knights were essentially a tank’s counter. Tanks were strong but slow, and auras ignored all manner of defense. Not to mention a tank usually didn’t deal much damage, making it difficult to inflict any on a knight. I’d already seen this for myself during the battle with the knight-turned-plunderer named Snake Knight we ran into in Crystal Cave. He cut one of my arms off like it was tofu. All I could do was take advantage of that gap and pounce, clinging onto him like a cicada. The main reason we won that battle was Raven’s magic.
Thump!

Not to mention the situation now was completely different from the one back then. This was a one-on-one battle without any comrades around to help me. I hadn’t even touched on building the stats I’d need to handle an aura.
Thump!
The cycle of my heartbeats got shorter, and my grip on my weapon tightened. This wasn’t a physical reaction born of fear. It was natural to feel this level of tension before a battle.
“So, you’re not going to answer? I’ll cut off your arm first, then.” Rick Omanus made the opening move.
I answered, “Do it, then, if you can.”
Yeah, it’s about time to take down a knight.

chapters.title: Chapter 319: Memory (4)
paragraphs: How strong had I become? This was a question I had been asking myself for the past few months. In the game, I could get a sense of my growth through stats, but in real life, it was hard to tell based on that alone. This wasn’t just a game.
In that sense, he might be the perfect match for me.

Even an ordinary knight capable of harnessing an aura was on par with a rank-six adventurer, and when it came to interpersonal battles, they would be ranked even higher. But my specs weren’t all that shabby, either. Of course, my Spirit Imprint was still at stage six and my level was still so low that I had an overwhelmingly small number of essences compared to the strongest fighters of this era. But from Ogre to Bayon to Storm Gush, I had a whopping three rank-three essences. The combination of said essences also had thought behind it and was specially designed with synergy in mind. More importantly, the main reason a tank couldn’t compete with a knight was because they lacked in the damage department, but in this case, Demon Grinder could make up for that.
So in other words... we’re on a level playing field. One hit, and we’re both dead.
A tense silence fell on the dark steps. I supposed he was also uneasy about how confident I was acting.
Did I come on too strong for no reason?

My opponent spent so much time measuring the distance between us that this question came to mind. The more he did, the more I honed my concentration. Just as they said that a battle between swordsmen of old was decided in one breath, this battle was likewise decided in an instant.
Slide.

The one to make the first move was the other side. He took a single step. The moment he climbed one stair to compensate for his lack of reach, I sprayed the acid blood I had been storing up in my mouth by biting my tongue.
“Puhuuup!”

The bastard didn’t dodge it. Like a boxer who didn’t even blink an eye when a punch was thrown at him, he took a neutral stance and thrust his sword. This was the reason why Corpse Golem essences were so overpowered. Not a single son of a bitch knew about Acid Blood. He must have figured getting covered in blood was no big deal.
Chhh!

The acid blood reached him before his sword reached me. There were no screams—just the sizzle of something melting. But even if he was trained to handle things like this, no human being could have perfect control over their body. He reflexively closed his eyes, which made the tip of his sword waver. Taking advantage of that opening, I twisted my body to the side and pounced.
Dash.
The hovering sword grazed my side. It wasn’t an injury worth worrying about, but did he realize what was going on just from the sensations he felt through the sword?
Slide.

He raised the shield in his left hand. Since his first move had failed, it seemed he was choosing to use defense to get through this round. Judging by the white light forming on the surface of the shield, it looked like he had at least one defense-related ability. However, this was his second self-mate. This hammer had Armor Penetration.
Clashhh!

The moment I mercilessly brought the hammer down on him, his mouth fell open and he spewed out blood. “Kurgh!” His eyes were full of shock. Well, I was sure it must have been hard for him to understand why his body had been pulverized when he had blocked the attack with a shield. But understanding something and accepting it were two different things.
Dash.
Accepting that he was in a tight spot, he retreated down the stairs. The attempt to somehow buy time to regroup was his third self-mate, because I also had a grab ability.
Whoom!
Using Transcendence followed by Eye of the Storm, I stopped him from getting away from me.
Yes.
Crash, crash, crash!
I brought down the hammer again and again until his head was turned to paste.
“Ugh, I’m sweating.”

After hitting him enough to kill him three times over, I wiped the cold sweat from my forehead. Although the battle had only lasted a few seconds, it consumed considerable mental energy. The rewards were still unmistakable, though.
Wow, what kind of equipment starts at grade four?

I guessed the lord of the castle had invested quite a lot because the knight’s equipment was very good. I couldn’t bring myself to leave it behind, so I quickly stripped it and threw it in sub-space. I had to abandon the least valuable items that were in there because I was out of space, but that was unavoidable.
Suddenly, I remembered the note Amelia left behind.
Take the Fragment of Records Stone and leave on my own? Leave where? I still haven’t found a place to bury the equipment yet.
How could I leave this all behind after all that work? I couldn’t go anywhere until I dealt with that first. I didn’t even know how to use the stone in the first place, anyway.
At any rate, an opportunity like this will never come again so I have to take it fast.
When I finished looting, I left the naked body behind and went down the stairs.
Tap.
The stairs themselves were very wide but when I traveled to the bottom, a passageway big enough for twenty people to easily pass through appeared. There was a large door at the end.
It’s slightly open.

There was no one visible in my immediate surroundings so I approached the door, making as little sound as possible. Beyond the door of what seemed to be a shelter, only one person was seated. His hairline had been peeled back by the ravages of time. He had a fat, lumpy belly, a fancy outfit that clearly looked like it was made of quality fabric, and eyelid creases deep enough to leave you feeling uncomfortable. This had to be the lord of the castle, whom I had only seen from afar once before.
The lord seemed to sense my presence at that point, as he spoke up in an anxious voice. “...Sir Omanus?”
Hmm, what to do?
After thinking about it for a moment, I just revealed myself.
“You are... Iron Mask?” The lord of the castle flinched when he spotted me. “Where is Sir Omanus? He went to check on what’s happening...”
“Omanus is dead. Ah, just to be clear, I killed him.”
When I calmly relayed this information, the lord’s eyes widened and he started to back away.
What a useless thing to do. You think you can run away like that?

When I quickly walked over and lifted him by the back of the neck, the lord of Noark’s castle started to flail around in a fit of rage. “Ugh! Let go! I said let go! How dare you!? Do you know who I am!?” It was an extremely bad look for the ruler of a city.
Welp, then you should have brought more guards to your secret panic room.
“W-What do you want...?! S-Stop! Use your words!”

I lifted him with one hand and gave him a simple pat-down to search him. Before long, I found what I was looking for. Amelia said he would most definitely have it on him and she was right. I didn’t know it would be in the form of a necklace, though.
Tap.

I forcefully ripped off the necklace and released the lord of the castle. He let out an angry shout about a treasure left behind by his predecessors getting taken away from him, but he did not fight me.
Okay, I have it now.
Worried that just touching it might activate it somehow, I held onto just the chain of the necklace and placed the Fragment of Records Stone in the sub-space.
“You...! Do you know what that is!? Give it to me now! I said give it to me!”
“Ugh, so noisy. Want me to rip out your teeth?” Once I got the lord of the castle to shut his mouth, I calmly asked, “Do you know how to use the Fragment of Records Stone?”
“You! That’s what you were after—!”
“Just answer the question. It’s just you and me here.”
“...You think I have anything to say to you!?”

The lord of the castle was a surprisingly tough nut to crack. At first, he got angry, then he said he didn’t know, and it was only after a beating that he revealed the story that had been passed down by his predecessors.
“There’s no way to use it?”
“A-At least according to all known records, y-yes... But it is said that when a person who will answer the call of the times comes near it, a light will shine.”
I wasn’t expecting that at all. Amelia told me that even the lord of Noark’s castle himself didn’t know how to use it, but in reality, he seemed to know everything about it.
So it won’t activate unless a condition is met.
It was a good idea to ask just in case.
“If that answers your question—”
“Uh huh, just tell me this. What does a person who ‘answers the call of the times’ have to do if he wants to go back?”
“What...? Why would you ask—” I guessed he must have had more than zero brain cells after all because the lord of the castle’s eyes went wide. “Wait, are you...!?”
Well, you would have to be a moron not to figure it out after all those hints.
I had no intention of hiding it so I just nodded. “It’s as you think. So tell me what I need to do to return to my original time period.”
“N-No wonder... I was wondering how you reached this place no one knows about. I guess that was how...”
“Another thing I didn’t ask.”

When I reprimanded him, the lord turned pale and hurriedly answered my question. “I-I heard you leave the same way you come. That after you complete all your work here, the stone will call you forth again...”
“How bothersome.”
“...Can I also ask a question?” As I was wondering what to do now, the lord of the castle spoke to me. “W-what kind of person am I in the future?” he asked, his eyes sparkling unpleasantly.
Did he expect to leave his mark on history like a hero? “Why are you asking that?”
“I-It’s just curiosity... Although now that you’re here, that future won’t exist... I can still be curious.”

So, he actually didn’t know anything. Well, I was sure that was why the rumors all said this was a treasure that could take you to the past and change history—even Noark’s leadership didn’t know how it really worked.
“Ah, how does the operation today end up going? Orcules, did we succeed in driving those bastards out of the city?” the lord asked.
“Are you that curious about the future?” He nodded at me. “Then close your eyes.”
“...They’re closed.”
“What do you see?”
“I don’t see anything.”
That was a relief. It would have been a problem if he said he saw something.
“That’s your future.” I brought down the hammer with all my might.
Slump.

The lord of the castle’s body slumped and a red pool of blood began to collect where he fell. I looked away without much interest. If even half the things I heard and saw while living in this city for the past few months were true, he fully deserved to die.
He was fated to die on this day too.
The murder of the lord of the castle would be known as the work of Orcules to the public, and that was what Amelia believed as well. But as it turned out, the real culprit was me.
Well, that’s not surprising anymore.

In truth, I debated whether to kill him or not until the last moment. Still, there was only one reason why I finally brought down the hammer. Even if I just up and left, the lord of the castle would be killed by someone today and history would come to pass. That would most definitely be the case no matter what. Unless, by the slimmest chance, the one I killed was a fake and the real lord of the castle fled and completely fooled the entire world for twenty years or something. Unless it was a scenario as ridiculous as that, the results wouldn’t change.
“Huh...?” At that moment, my feet stopped on their own. “Wait.”
I thought I could understand how the philosopher who shouted Eureka! felt.
“...Fool the entire world?”
It felt like an electric current was flowing from my head to my toes.

chapters.title: Chapter 320: Memory (5)
paragraphs: Clunk, clunk.

On top of the ten-person carriage that was shaking as it sped through the streets, there was an out-of-place presence among the solemn-looking adult men—a fourteen-year-old girl who was staring off into space with blank eyes. Her calm expression gave no indication of how nervous Amelia Rainwales felt right now, except to her sister, Laura.
Slide.
Amelia flinched from where she was sitting tensely, her hands on her knees. Her sister’s hand was folded on top of them.
“What’s wrong? Are you really worried?”

Introverted Amelia nodded. Not only was it meaningless to lie to her older sister who knew her as well as a parent would, but Laura would have noticed just how much she was trembling right now, no matter how shaky the carriage was.
“...It’s okay, nothing bad will happen.”

When she felt her sister’s warm hand on her skin, Amelia felt her tension release little by little even though they were practically being dragged into a battlefield. When she closed her eyes, the conversation between the adult men began to enter Amelia’s ears.
“What about Iron Mask and Emily?”
“I heard the lord of the castle is going to send someone to their inn, but I don’t know if the message will reach them given what’s going on.”
“Hah, what a mess. If they were planning something like this the whole time, at least tell us in advance, right? What is this, in the middle of the night?”
“That’s just how top secret it was. I never thought the lord of the castle would join hands with the palace to attack Orcules.”

The sisters had been working at their adoptive father’s tavern like they did any other day when they were summoned by Felic Barker. He looked to be in a rush, did not explain anything, and told them to prepare for a fight. As soon as they picked up their equipment, he put them on a military carriage with the members of their clan who had arrived.

“Wait, attack Orcules? I didn’t hear about that. I just heard we were being sent as backup for a riot in the east. And the palace? What kind of nonsense is that? How could the lord of the castle work with the palace?”
“Sounds like the palace made contact with the lord not long ago. I didn’t know at the time what was discussed at that meeting... but I think we all have a decent guess now.”
“Well, those bastards from Orcules would be a thorn in the palace’s side too. I guess their interests aligned.”
“Mhm, if not for that, what reason would knights that were sent here from the palace have to be fighting Orcules?”
“...That must be why the lord didn’t tell us until the day of.”
“That’s right. Because they’ll be the core troops anyway. We just have to focus on making it out of here alive.”
“Ha, if I knew this would happen, I would have made sure I was sleeping outside the castle like Iron Mask. Staying in the castle only got me dragged into this.”
“Durbon, watch your mouth.”
“Ah... forget what I said.”

“And you guys, stop complaining so much. Once this is over, we’ll receive proper compensation.” Clan Leader Felic Barker eased the tension. A long while later, the carriage finally stopped at the entrance of Noark’s eastern district.
“I guess we have to walk from here.”

The eastern district looked like it had already been the site of several battles. Beginning right at the border, the scent of blood was thick and the remains of collapsed buildings and tattered corpses filled the streets. There were sounds of explosions all around, and human screams more desperate than those of banshees filled the air.
“What are you all doing?! How long are you going to block the road? Get off quickly! Can’t you see there are more carriages behind you?”
Amelia followed them out. Her body, which had calmed down during the journey, was trembling again.
Her sister lovingly grabbed her hand. “Don’t worry too much. I’ll protect you.”
Her trustworthy sister never broke a promise. Even still, Amelia wasn’t able to calm down all that easily.
Squeeze.
Instead, the stronger her sister gripped her hand, the more Amelia got a strange, ominous feeling.

Amelia finished reminiscing and slowly opened her eyes. It was clear where she had to go: the eastern district of Noark that had slowly escaped the influence of the castle and its lord once Orcules made it its home base.
“F-Fire!”
Today, most people simply assumed a fire had broken out in the area, but in reality, a war was going on there.
We’re probably traveling east by carriage right now.

Although it was a memory from twenty years ago and the first large-scale battle that she had ever experienced, Amelia remembered even the trip over. It wasn’t a memory she could forget even if she wanted to. It was no exaggeration to say that her life over the past twenty years had been one which she had looked back on and regretted this day countless times.
Dash.

Amelia picked up the pace and headed toward her destination. The eastern district, which she had been running over to for a long while, was occupied by hundreds of clueless adventurers who were called up that day. Scanning the area, she soon found the person she was looking for.
“Found you.”

“Who... huh, Emily?” When Amelia struck up a conversation, Felic Barker, who was standing by for battle, went wide-eyed. “How are you here?” Although he was happy to see her, he seemed a little suspicious.
“I went to the castle when I saw the commotion and they sent me here. I heard about the situation from other people on the way.”
“Ah, I see... But where’s Iron Mask?”
“He’s drunk and asleep, so I just left him.”
“Hmm, I mean, still... how could you leave such a valuable military asset behind?”
“What of it? He’s so drunk that he can’t even wake up.”

Felic seemed disappointed, but he didn’t argue. He didn’t find her excuse itself strange thanks to the fact that that barbarian often gave the excuse that he had too much to drink the night before whenever he was late. “Well, I’m sure that guy didn’t realize something like this would happen today, either. Then I’d better assume he’s not coming.”
After that, Amelia stood next to her younger self and older sister.
The sisters greeted her awkwardly. “Hello...”

Unlike the barbarian, whom they were both familiar with, Amelia hadn’t interacted with these two beyond what was strictly necessary over the past several months. For some reason, whenever she stood in front of them, she couldn’t bring herself to speak.
This time, she forced herself to open her mouth. “Stay close to me.”
“...Sorry?”
“That way I can protect you.”

“Ah, right...!” The sisters weren’t all that close to Amelia but they knew she had outstanding skills, so their faces brightened at her words. Although they also seemed to be wondering why she was suddenly being nice to them.
“Prepare for battle!”

Once the formation was established, it wasn’t long before it was her group’s turn to go to the front lines. Divided into dozens of teams, the idea was that they would take turns on the front line and alternate breaks. There was no imminent danger. Sweeps were currently being carried out by the troops from the palace and the lord of the castle’s elites who had been informed of today’s plan in advance.
“The bastards are trying to escape! Kill them!”
The goal of the troops gathered in this particular spot was not to sweep but to seize. How strong could the leftovers escaping the burning neighborhood be? A one-sided massacre followed.
“The lord of the castle seems completely resolved.”
“Looks like 70 percent of these people are ordinary citizens; is it really okay to kill them all like this?”
“Ugh, you idiot. We can’t go through them one by one to check who they are. What if a member of Orcules gets away disguised as a civilian?”
“That’s true, but...”
Some expressed skepticism about the one-sided battle, but they were just a minority. Everyone here specialized in killing people.
“Does anyone remember what the commander said earlier? How much was it for two?”
“I can’t really remember, but at this rate, I think this is worth more than going on another expedition.”
“Hey! Did you hear? Herders! Stop fighting and collect! Ah, and if anything they’re wearing looks expensive, strip it!”

Most were delighted by the opportunity to earn a high income for easy work, but as she heard this, Amelia’s expression hardened.
