Although she was born in this city and grew up with these people, not only did this way of thinking make her feel sick, but she knew that this festive atmosphere was only temporary and hell would soon be unleashed.
“What the—? Someone is walking over here.” Even amid all the noise, that muttered comment seemed overwhelmingly loud.
Amelia hurriedly turned her head. “...Is he out of his mind?”
A lone man walking straight toward them caught their attention. Considering the hundreds of escape attempts that had been made so far, it was a very strange sight in comparison.
Step.
As the man got closer, those watching him approach began to feel uneasy.
Step.

He wore a black military uniform drenched in blood. However, while he was wet, there was not a single scratch on his clothes. Judging by the fact that they were dyed red with blood, it seemed he hadn’t been lucky enough not to run into trouble on the way here.
Step.

The sword on his waist was also peculiar. This crowd was made up of plunderers who could recognize the value of an item. As such, the closer they got to it, the more everyone realized the sword was no ordinary weapon. The sword itself was very plain, but the name of the man carrying it was very famous in this city.
“...Hey, this isn’t what I’m thinking it is, is it? Please tell me there’s something wrong with my eyes.”
“Does anyone know his face?”
There was a stir among the adventurers on standby. Some fell back on their instincts and backed away, while others were busy dealing with denial.
Step.
The man narrowed the distance to fifty yards.
Whippp!
A fire flung by a fire-type expert sputtered and died before it could even reach the man. Then came silence. This was a very famous ability.
“N-Nullification...”

Nullification was the unique power of the Lord of the Fifth Floor, the Lord of Tranquility. This incomprehensible power nullified special skills and abilities, which were the bedrock of every adventurer. It had been held by less than ten people in all of history, and as far as they knew, only one in the current era.
“T-Traitor...”

He was an unrivaled criminal with the nickname Traitor, the man who founded the group called Orcules with his own hands, and an undefeated swordsman: Ricardo Lüchenprague. The appearance of this man caused chaos.
“Why is this man...?”
“Palace! They said the palace’s soldiers would be fighting him!”
The man did not answer any of their questions. He simply raised his sword silently, utterly disinterested.
“R-Run!”
From there, the adventurers that were gathered turned their backs and began to run away. However, the moment the sword was swung, there was a flash of light.
Flash! Slice!
The memory Amelia had replayed countless times over the past twenty years began to unfold once again.

chapters.title: Chapter 321: Role (1)
paragraphs: The Commander of the First Royal Guard, Jerome Saintred, was a young knight in his mid-twenties who took up the position following the Blood Knight’s slaughter of the former commander.
“If we hadn’t learned about this ancient shelter in advance, it could have ruined our plan.” Jerome brushed his short silver hair back out of his face and headed down the dark stairs.

The reason this man was in the basement of Noark’s castle and not in the eastern district, which was currently a battlefield, was simple. The offer the palace made to the lord of the castle to keep quiet about this city if he helped them exterminate Orcules was merely an excuse to bring Rafdonia’s troops here. The palace’s objective had been something else from the very beginning: the Fragment of Records Stone, an item that, according to the information provided by a close confidante of Noark’s lord, was always worn by the lord in the form of a necklace. Of course, Jerome was not well informed about what this item was, but since he had been given his orders, he had to return to the palace with it somehow.
Tap.

Jerome, who was walking down the steps, stopped in his tracks. He had discovered a body lying on the stairs. The cause of death was a blow to the occipital region, which he believed had been caused by a blunt object. Even his equipment had been stripped and the man was practically naked.
Jerome bent down and touched the wound.
And the time of death... thirty minutes ago at most.
His face hardened. Someone had infiltrated this place first, and there was a high chance that their target was the lord of the castle who was hiding below. Was the intruder still down there?
Dash.

Jerome quickly ran down the stairs. Before long, he reached a wide-open stone gate and a big passageway, but the only thing waiting for him there was the corpse of a bloated, middle-aged man. Once again, the body showed signs of being struck by a blunt object.
I don’t know who it was, but I’m a moment too late.

Jerome bit his lip in frustration but speedily inspected the scene of the incident. The most important thing, the Fragment of Records Stone, was not there. Judging by the cuts on the lord’s neck, it seemed it had been pulled off with force.
To think there was someone else after it.
Momentarily stunned by this unexpected turn of events, Jerome quickly went back the way he came. It was still too early to give up.
They couldn’t have gotten far in thirty minutes.
He had to find them.

Auril Gavis had said, “A timeline once observed cannot change.” Certainly, as he said, it might be impossible to change the future completely. But what if the observation itself was wrong? For example, what if I could make young Amelia believe her older sister was dead? And then, what if I could make Laura hide her identity for twenty years? Wouldn’t it be possible to save her then? The idea sent shivers down my entire spine, but before long, I was met with a major obstacle.
“That day, my sister died in my arms.”

Amelia saw her sister’s death firsthand. Just as I had with Dwalkie in the Labyrinth of Larcaz, Amelia watched the light leave Laura’s eyes. How on earth could I fake that? I had no idea. It wouldn’t be easy to convince Amelia, someone who had already killed countless people despite her young age, that her sister was dead.
Well, I’m sure it’ll work out somehow.

It felt like I was back to square one, but the thought didn’t feel as daunting as before. That was because the lord of the castle said so himself that once all of our work here was done, the Fragment of Records Stone would activate on its own. In other words, there was still work for me to do here. So what was the role I had to fulfill? That was obvious.
Kwaaang!

I ran all the way to the alchemist’s place and busted through the door with my shoulder. There was a chance that the door was already open, but so what? Probability was just a number. And so I decided to put my all into every moment.
“A-Agh!”
“What the—?” When I smashed through the door, I found a startled old man in a corner of the workshop. But it wasn’t Marfa Ipaello, the owner of this room. “Who are you?”
“I’m...” The old man frantically averted his eyes in a very transparently suspicious way.
Huh?
When I inspected the old man’s attire, an unusual brooch at the front of his robe caught my eye. “Are you an alchemist?” The old man flinched at my question, which was answer enough.

Just in case any guards were hiding nearby, I remained on guard as I stepped forward. In turn, the old man stepped back and blurted out an excuse. “Ah, this is a misunderstanding! It’s a misunderstanding! I never meant to steal anything...”
“I see.” No wonder he was startled like someone who had been caught red-handed doing something he shouldn’t be. This man had taken advantage of the chaos to come steal something.
“I-If you keep this matter a secret, I will surely—”
There was no reason to prolong this conversation. It looked like he’d given even his own guards the slip to pull off this heist.
Smack!
As a non-combatant, the alchemist had no hope of defending himself as I lunged forward and slammed the hammer down on the top of his head.

“Wow, you even have a sub-space.” I didn’t have much time so I just stole the alchemist’s ring before hurriedly searching the workshop, soon finding the item I was looking for: the prototype of the Blessing of Lethe. When consumed, it would cause you to forget all of your memories.
Okay, that’s the first item on my checklist.

It was now time to go find Amelia. This was a world without phones, but although we hadn’t established a set meeting place or time, that was no problem. Since six hours had passed since I’d fallen asleep, she was probably busy being chased right about now. I had to hurry.
“Found you.” I quickly turned around at the sound of a voice from the doorway and saw a silver-haired knight. “Give me the Fragment of Records Stone.”
What was this son of a bitch talking about?

The Traitor, Ricardo Lüchenprague, was once called the Sword Master. Anyone who had seen him wield a sword or dealt with him in person all said the same thing: that his swordsmanship was different from that of an ordinary knight.
Whooom!

An aura fluttered at the tip of his sword. That in itself was not special. The aura was spread thin to reduce energy consumption and gave off a certain sharpness, but that was all. The aura did not boast a mountainous vigor like the Knight of Light’s nor change its form like the Knight of Moon’s. But despite that, this man’s sword was superior to theirs, not because of the aura but because of his technique.
Slice!
“Agh! H-Help me!”
Not a single one of the hundreds of adventurers blockading the eastern district could withstand a singular strike of his sword.
“We have to run—! Agh!”

Anyone standing in his way was cut down. If they dodged, the sword seemed to reach their escape route before they did. Anyone could see it was a crude technique. The elaborate techniques favored by most knights were nowhere to be seen. But Amelia still could not take her eyes off the sword.
“M-Miss Emily. W-We need to run...”
Something about his swordsmanship felt unnatural. It was a swordsmanship that had been tirelessly optimized for one thing and one thing only—to kill.

“What are you all doing?! Get over here!” When the one-sided massacre began, Clan Leader Felic Barker began preparing to flee with his clan members. Amelia could not sit back and watch this happen. The reason she had hung around these people for the past several months was this very moment.
“Felic Barker.”

“Huh?” The moment Felic turned his head at the sound of his name, Amelia embedded a thin needle in his neck. “...Uh, huh?” His body went as rigid as a stone statue, head still turned. Amelia hoisted him onto her shoulder. “What is the meaning of this...?!”
The clan members belatedly realized what was going on and aimed their weapons at Amelia, but that wasn’t a big problem.
“How dare you betray us?!”
It was not a betrayal, because she never thought of them as her comrades in the first place.
Slice!

Amelia decapitated the clan member who came closest. Then, sure enough, the enraged adventurers slowly shuffled back and seemed to weigh their odds before finally running away, leaving their captured clan leader behind.
“Ugh, whatever!”
“Never mind, let’s just go!”

She’d expected them to react like that. The Traitor was carrying out a massacre and getting closer and closer. Those men would have no reason to risk their lives for the clan leader, unlike these two here.
“...Please let go of that man.” The moment the young girl who used to be her past reached out to her, she heard the sound of something slicing through the air behind her.
Whip!
Amelia twisted her body to the side to move out of the way, then used the rotational momentum to kick her attacker’s wrist away.
Clang!
The dropped sword skittered across the ground, and she saw a girl holding onto her numb wrist in pain. It was her older sister, Laura Rainwales.
“Amelia, let’s run!” As soon as she deemed the situation too dangerous, Laura took her younger sister and ran, and Amelia just watched.

She felt her chest tighten. She knew why these girls were trying to save Felic even though the other clan members had fled. It wasn’t out of loyalty, but due to the shackles Felic had placed on Laura. Unhealthy Contract involved all kinds of unfair conditions, but there was one critical one. The moment Felic Barker received a wound that put him in near-death condition, he would receive all of Laura’s life force. That was why those two had stayed behind.
But when even that failed, the reason Laura ran without looking back was Amelia. In that brief moment, her sister accepted her death if it meant Amelia could escape.
Grit.

Her jaw subconsciously tightened. It was only a three-year age difference. When she was young, her older sister felt even bigger than an adult, but now she knew. Even then, her sister was only seventeen. There was no way Laura didn’t feel burdened by her lot in life, and there would definitely have been times she wanted to give everything up and run away.
Dash.
Amelia ran forward with Felic stiff as a log on her back.
Slice!

She headed toward the place where a particular man stood like a beast in a crowd of herbivores. He was pursuing the hundreds of people running away in a panic, swinging his sword methodically. For the first time, however, an emotion appeared on his expressionless face. That emotion was curiosity. True, it must have been strange to see someone walk toward him while everyone else was running away, and with a strong man slung over her shoulder, at that.
Whooom!

The aura in Amelia’s dagger turned black. This was an effect of a conversion skill called Power of the Abyss she had obtained from the rank-four monster Grabanich. When this skill was activated, all of her abilities, including Spirit Power and Dragon Power, were converted into Soul Power, which then became twice as efficient to use. The same went for auras, which used mana. This ability had served Amelia, who was born with low mana reserves, quite well.
Swish.

The moment she got within a certain distance, her blackened aura returned to its original color because of the special ability that Traitor had absorbed from one of the Lords of the Floor. This ability rendered all active and passive skills within a certain radius useless.
Yeah, so to put it simply... It’s over now.
Even the Unhealthy Contract was inactive in here.
Tap.
When Amelia threw Felic from her shoulder, Lüchenprague cut him in half in a single breath.
Slice!
The body split in two with the quick squelch of bloodshed. She was a bit worried, but the Unhealthy Contract did not activate and heal his injury.
I guess I cleared one hurdle...

Because Amelia had escaped with her sister before seeing how Felic died back then, it was relieving to see for herself that her sister’s life was no longer in his hands. But there was no time to think about things like that.

Having achieved her goal, Amelia quickly retreated. When she did, the traitor who hadn’t uttered a single word while massacring dozens immediately chased after her and said, “I don’t know what that was, but I do know that you used me.”

It seemed he understood the gist of what had happened. For some reason, a word the barbarian once told her about popped into her head unbidden. It wasn’t a particularly pleasant-sounding word, but unfortunately, there was no concise way of expressing the same sentiment in Rafdonia.
That place has a truly amazing vocabulary.
Amelia said the word without realizing it. “K-Kimochi...”
Apparently, this was a way of expressing gratitude toward an enemy who helped you.

chapters.title: Chapter 322: Role (2)
paragraphs: “Laura, we need to go back!”
“Weren’t you paying attention? That woman uses an aura. And that man named Lüchenprague is an even bigger monster.”
“But—!”
“We won’t be able to do anything even if we go back. This is the smartest choice.”
Amelia gritted her teeth as she ran, Laura dragging her by the arm. For some reason, she felt like crying. “Smartest choice? Are you crazy? How is you dying and me living a smart choice!?”
When Amelia shook off her sister’s arm, Laura stopped running. Laura sighed. “Amelia, listen to your sister for once. We don’t have time to—”
“What’s with that? Stop talking like these are your last words!”
“...That’s not it.”
“Then what is it? Why are you just running away instead of at least trying?”

“Because this gives us a higher chance of survival!” Laura shouted angrily at her disobedient younger sister before plowing on. “Amelia, that woman didn’t kill Felic. She used a needle to paralyze him. She carried him like she was on some kind of mission. That means she’s not planning on killing him right away. And I’m still alive and well too.”
“Ah...” Amelia involuntarily let out a surprised sound. Even in the middle of all that danger and chaos, her sister had managed to consider all these factors before making a decision.

“I may feel uneasy about it, but this is still the best option. Rather than getting killed for attacking that woman, this gives us better odds. Now, if you understand, follow me.” Laura got moving again like she considered even this conversation a waste of time, and Amelia hurriedly followed suit.
After who knew how long of that, the Rainwales sisters encountered familiar faces.
“Huh? Laura, Amelia? You guys were alive?”
“...Mr. Durbon.”
It seemed something had happened along the way or they got separated, because only about half of the clan members who ran away were there.
“Hey, I’m glad you’re here. You guys are lucky. We were just about to get out of this city.”
“Pardon...? Get out?”
“Can’t you see? Lüchenprague has come out of the eastern district. What do you think that means? The fight’s already over and he’s on his way to get to the lord of the castle. This city is finished.”

When Durbon finished his explanation, the two men next to him threw in their own two cents, looking haunted. “That man isn’t human. Did you see how his expression didn’t change once as he slaughtered dozens of people? I still get goosebumps remembering it.”
“I heard if Traitor sticks out his tongue, that means he’s really angry.”
“If this city falls into his hands, it will be our heads and the heads of everyone on the lord of the castle’s side that get cut off.”
Although this suggestion was coming out of the blue, Laura calmly collected the information she needed to make a decision. “But how do you plan to escape? The front gate—”

“Yes, the Gatekeeper is guarding it. But it looks like there is a hidden side road. Apparently, it’s the road the Melta Merchant Company uses to travel aboveground, and one of our guys knows about it.”
“...I see.”
“Do you want to come with us?”
Laura accepted the offer without asking any further questions. “We will go.”
“L-Laura?”

Their original plan was to head to the relatively safe western district and hide out until the danger had passed, but this changed things. If she died, her younger sister would be left alone in this world. At the very least, Laura wanted Amelia to be able to live like a human being. This might be her last chance to ensure that.
“Ah, I’m just telling you this in case, but in exchange for taking you with us—”
“I know. If anything dangerous happens, I will step in.”
“Ahem, right... I’m glad we’re on the same page.” The man nodded in embarrassment, then started leading the group away.

With his shiny silver hair, pale skin, knightly armor with the symbol of the palace on it, and longsword that was one and a half times larger than normal, I recognized this man on sight despite never meeting him before.
Jerome Saintred.

He was the head of the First Royal Guard and the strongest knight of royal blood in the kingdom, known to the common people as the Knight of Light. The most pressing question at present was why the hell this bastard was currently here. This guy never came up once in the stories Amelia told me.
“Give me the Fragment of Records Stone.”

With that one sentence, I was able to get a rough idea of why the Knight of Light, who should have been sweeping the eastern district right now, was here. It became very clear to me at that moment that the palace’s goal was not to exterminate Orcules.
Defeating him... won’t be easy.

He was on a whole other level from Rick Omanus, the knight I faced on the stairs earlier. He would have undoubtedly reached level five, the maximum level you could get to with the secret medicine knights took. Given that he was a commander, he would also have completed the level seven Awakening, not to mention the level six Breakthrough event. And that wasn’t all.
Considering the palace’s wealth, it’d be safe to say all seven of his essences are at least rank three.

In terms of number of essences and average rank, I was outclassed. That wasn’t even mentioning the difference in our stats as a result of said essences, plus I was also at a disadvantage as a tank going up against a knight. However, if I had to choose one thing I might be a match for him in, it would be equipment.
Whoooom!
Starting at double digits, Numbered Items were lowkey indestructible.
Kwaang!
I parried his sword wordlessly with my hammer.
Whew, I’ve never been in a fight like this before. I’ve always blocked with a shield first and then attacked with a weapon.
Seeing me block the blow, my opponent frowned. As a knight who could cut down anything, I guessed he never expected his sword to actually get stopped by something.

“Wait.” I used the brief opening after that strike to make an attempt at conversation. I didn’t think it would work, but there was no harm in trying, right? “There’s a misunderstanding here. The Fragment of Records Stone? I don’t know anything about whatever that is.”
“You lie. I’ve gotten testimony that you came from underground and headed here.”
Hmm, I see...
The you-have-the-wrong-person strategy didn’t work, but I ended up getting some unexpectedly useful information out of it.
“But... you may have taken it without knowing what it was. Give me the necklace the lord of the castle was wearing.”
That wording gave me a foothold to latch onto. “If you’re talking about what the lord of the castle was wearing, do you mean this necklace?” I asked, pointing to the necklace I was wearing.
The knight nodded. “Yes. If you hand it over, I promise there won’t be any unnecessary bloodshed.”
This was a big win. I had shoved the Fragment of Records Stone into my sub-space ring ages ago.
Which means this guy doesn’t know what the Fragment of Records Stone is.

The necklace I was wearing was just an ordinary necklace with a large, refined stone embedded in it. All it did was reduce the casting time of any wizard who wore it. It was something I secretly swiped during a past looting session and now wore around my neck as an accessory.
Interesting that I get to use it like this.
Humans were a social species. It was a good thing I attempted conversation.
Rip.
I yanked off the necklace. “Well, if you want it, I can give it to you. I only took it as a souvenir anyway.”
“Souvenir?”
“It was the lord of the castle, after all. He ordered us to go out and fight, yet he went to hide in the basement. I followed him, but there was nothing to take other than this necklace.”

“Hmm, so you were just after money,” the knight muttered, apparently buying that explanation. On his way to the lord of the castle, he must have happened upon Omanus, who was stripped of all his equipment.
“Isn’t that how guys like me operate? Of course, seeing as someone like you wants it, this necklace must be pretty valuable... But I can’t see how it’s worth risking my life for.”

Talkative bastards usually had ulterior motives, but this young knight who had probably spent his whole life doing nothing but swing a sword did not think me suspicious. He just looked at me with disdain. “Enough excuses. Give it up.”
“Ah, but I need a guarantee before that.”
“Guarantee?”
“A guarantee that you will let me go if I give you this.”
“I do not break my promises.”
What, because you’re an honorable knight?
If he really didn’t know how to lie, he wouldn’t have been here in the first place. Even as he was bleeding out, the lord of the castle hadn’t realized he’d been tricked by the palace.
Leap.

I broke the window on the wall and Leaped up high. Since I jumped out from the fourth floor, I had a bird’s-eye view of the city from the castle at its center. The eastern district where the battle had broken out was burning brightly, while the west was relatively calm.
Flash!

I didn’t have the luxury to take it all in though, because a moment later there was a flash of light behind me right before the knight appeared. The skill he used was instantly recognizable: Gateway of Light. It was from a rank-three essence, and sat at the top of the tier list of transportation skills you could get in Dungeon and Stone. This wasn’t a half-assed teleportation skill that sent you to a random location, but an overpowered ability that allowed you to specify a destination.
Man, it’s been a while...
I’d used that skill a lot before starting my barbarian build.
“Did you think you could run?” As soon as I turned around in mid-air, the bastard swung his sword and I once again blocked it with the hammer.
Jeez, so impatient. It’s not like I said I wouldn’t keep my promise. Anyway, this is my first mid-air fight.
Using the recoil from blocking the sword to my advantage, I allowed myself to get pushed back up into the air once more. With that, the distance between us widened.
Flash!

The moment the knight used Gateway of Light to close the distance again, I threw the necklace in my hand as hard as I could. He quickly stretched out his arm, but he didn’t have enough reach to catch it. For a brief moment, I could see the debate currently happening behind his eyes. He was trying to decide whether to kill me here or not. That confirmed one thing, at least.
Not break your promise? Yeah, right.

This guy had been planning from the start to kill me as soon as I gave him the necklace, probably to get rid of any witnesses. Well, it didn’t look like he was going to follow through on that plan now, though.
Smack!
I kicked the knight in the stomach while he was distracted by the necklace. He didn’t even flinch, but that didn’t bother me. That wasn’t the reason I kicked him to begin with.
Voom!

In accordance with the laws of physics, the distance between us widened again. Even as he was falling, the guy looked at me and asked, “What is your name?” His voice spoke to a pure curiosity about his opponent.
All I could think in response was, Why would I tell you that?
“Are you a moron?”
“...What?”
Oops, I said it.

I caught my slip-up immediately, but luckily the knight didn’t use Gateway of Light to come at me again. There was a maximum number of times it could be used in one go. After the third use, you would have to wait out the cooldown.
Flash!
Soon, light wrapped around his body and he disappeared from sight. Without needing to look too far, I could see him reappear in the same direction I threw the necklace.
Okay, got rid of that guy...

I activated Transcendent Leap after that, and what felt like an invisible platform formed under my toes. When I kicked off of it with all my might, my body shot forward like an arrow. My destination rapidly approached.
This makes me feel like Superman.
I chuckled and replayed the brief mid-air fight that just occurred. The more I thought about it, though, the more antsy I felt.
I should get stronger soon.
I approached the center of a cemetery on the outskirts of Castle Noark and proceeded to land in style.
Kwaaang!
“Whaaa!”
In other words, that meant I smashed all the tombstones in the surrounding area and went tumbling through the dirt for several hundred yards.
“...Jeez, I almost died there.”

I had gone directly from the castle located in the middle of the city to the outskirts, and the price I paid for cutting down on travel time was unmistakable. Was it because I accelerated and got propelled from up high? Beyond the numbness, I could feel a prickle of electricity running through my legs. Considering my Pain Resistance, that meant they must literally be destroyed.
...Still, I don’t need to use a potion.

The downside of an Ogre essence was that it came with a -40 to Natural Regeneration. Thanks to that, my wounds barely used to heal if I didn’t take a potion. But the essence of the Storm Gush, combined with the Natural Regeneration stats I received from the Immortality Imprint, easily compensated for this drawback. Now minor injuries healed naturally with a mere lick of the wound.
Slide.

After a short break, I stood up. I was able to locate the place I was looking for from a quick glance around because I had visited it before. It was a passage hidden beneath a giant tombstone, tall and wide enough for a single carriage to pass through. The first thing that caught my eye was a corpse.
It’s the cemetery’s guard.
The man who had been here serving as the security guard for the secret passage was now dead, his body covered in stab wounds.
Since I slept for a whole six hours, Laura’s group would have passed through here a long time ago... By now, Amelia would have joined them.
It seemed the only way I’d be able to reach them before it was too late was if I got a move on, so I quickly entered the passage. Or, rather, I was about to enter.
...Huh?
I stopped walking.
Step, step.
I could see an old man in fine clothes walking toward me from the other direction.
Thump.
The moment I made eye contact with the old man, my heart started pounding. It felt like I was dreaming.
Upon meeting my eye, the old man said hello. “Haha, nice to see you.”
It was Auril Gavis.

chapters.title: Chapter 323: Role (3)
paragraphs: The man had long, white hair, fine wrinkles, a friendly air about him, a straight back that didn’t seem to belong to someone of his age, and blue eyes that seemed capable of seeing right through you.
“Hmm, this place is as dull as ever.”
When I saw the old man, who looked exactly like he did in the community, I felt my heart sink.
Auril Gavis...?
Of course, I figured we could run into each other today. Amelia did tell me that the day her older sister died, this old man was there too.
Wait, why is this old timer here, then?
No matter how I looked at it, there was only one reason this old man would be here and not at the center of the incident.
He... came looking for me.

My heart started to pound faster and my mind was jumbled. How did he find me? Had he also figured out that I was Bjorn Yandel? And why had the community been closed for months? No, more importantly, what was he planning to do with me now that he’d found me?

As these questions ran through my mind, cold sweat started to trickle down my spine. It was at that moment that Auril Gavis cleared his throat and drew my attention. “Ahem.” It seemed he didn’t like the fact that I had just stopped and stared at him without saying anything. I had to do something.
Ugh, but what do I say? Okay, first, I need to act natural and greet him.
“Now, will you get out of the way?”
Huh?
“If someone as big as you is blocking the road, I cannot pass, can I?”
What did you say? Does he not know it’s me?

This unexpected plot twist left me reeling, but luckily, this mouth of mine had told countless lies before and was thus able to respond on autopilot. “Ah, yes... You can pass, sir.” That was an honorific I had not used once since inhabiting the body of a barbarian.
Auril Gavis smiled happily at this. “What a polite fellow. Or perhaps you’re quick on the uptake? Either way, you’ll live long.” When I stuck to the wall to let him pass, Auril walked by, chuckling.
Step, step.

His footsteps got farther and farther away. Suddenly, a thought occurred to me. I may have instinctively gotten myself out of that interaction, but was it actually a good idea to hide my identity? Of course, it was just a passing thought. It wasn’t like we were in the community right now; we were meeting in person. If I could hide my identity, of course I should. If Auril learned that I was Bjorn Yandel, that would invite all kinds of trouble once I got back to the future.
Yeah, I handled that well.
At the thought, my tense shoulders began to relax and I slowly began to process what just happened.
“Ah, I didn’t ask one thing.” Auril, who was walking away, abruptly turned around and gave me an intent look. “What on earth happened today that this place is such a mess?”
“The lord of the castle teamed up with the palace and attacked Orcules.”

“Oh? What a turn of events...” Despite his seemingly intrigued tone, I sensed no genuine interest in his voice. “Ah, and let me ask you one more question. A new barbarian came to the city recently, right? About five or six months ago...”

For a moment, I thought I was just imagining things, but upon hearing the second question, the difference in attentiveness became clear. Although his tone was casual, there was a deep, undeniable undercurrent of interest in his voice.
Composure, composure...

Calming my racing heart, I identified the best answer I could give here and smoothly opened my mouth to respond. “Yes, there was.” It wasn’t smart to lie here. Anyone in the city could answer this question anyway, so there was no point in deceiving him.
“Oh? Is that right? Can you also tell me where I can find him?”
“If memory serves, he was a part of the lord of the castle’s faction. So he’s probably fighting in the east right now.”
“Haha, you weren’t just polite but also very friendly. And the name?”
“Pardon?”
“Ah, not you, that barbarian’s.”
“Bjon. I heard it was Bjon, son of Thor.”
When he heard my answer, Auril nodded, and then gave me a friendly pat on the arm. “Thank you for responding. You seem busy, you should go now.”
“Yes, I hope you also succeed at whatever you’re after, sir.”
Jeez, why does it feel so cold here?
Once the conversation seemed to be over, I gave him a brief nod and entered the passageway.
Step, step.
I could hear the old man walking away behind me, and as soon as the sound faded, I started running with all my might.
Whew. Almost pissed my pants.

Meanwhile, across the city, the silver-haired knight Jerome Saintred listened to a report from the royal army’s adjutant wizard and nodded with satisfaction. “What’s the situation on the eastern front?”
“As ordered, we are investing only minimal troops for the purpose of buying time, and we can withdraw at any time if contact is made with the enemy.”

Jerome was pleased by the successful execution of his first-ever special mission as commander. He’d secured the Fragment of Records Stone, which was the primary goal of this mission, and he’d also achieved his secondary goal of reducing Noark’s power by causing internal strife.
“Send word to the battle mages immediately. In ten minutes, we will rendezvous at the agreed-upon meeting place and return to Rafdonia.”
“Yes sir.”
If the royal troops stationed in the east were withdrawn, Orcules would direct their anger at the already-dead lord of the castle, and the civil war would begin in earnest.
Jerome nodded at the deputy’s voice, signaling for him to continue if he had something to say.
Permission acquired, the adjutant asked in a cautious yet polite tone, “May I ask what the necklace you are holding is for?”
“You are not authorized to know that information,” Jerome answered sternly, putting the necklace in sub-space.
The adjutant lowered his head to acknowledge his mistake. “Please excuse me. I saw you were holding a refined stone necklace and... I swear I had no idea it was related to your classified mission.”
He was clearly trying to convince Jerome that his question was one of pure curiosity and nothing else, but Jerome flinched at his explanation. “Refined stone necklace...? What do you mean by that?”
“...Sorry?”
“Elaborate. Are you saying this necklace is made of refined stone?” Jerome pulled the necklace back out and showed his adjutant.

The adjutant’s answer remained the same. “Yes, I’m sure of it. It’s a magical device made entirely of a high-ranking, refined stone. Ah, a refined stone is a specially processed Rift Stone that makes it easier to cast spells—” The adjutant clammed up mid-sentence when he heard a disturbing grinding noise from his superior’s jaw.

“So, I was deceived...” The adjutant involuntarily ducked his head. That was to be expected. Normally, Jerome was the type of person to laugh off paying one million stones for something worth ten thousand. “...Adjutant Avex, you lead the army back to the city first.”
“Sorry? But, Commander Saintred, you—”
“I have work to do.” Jerome stormed off without waiting for a reply.
The adjutant could only watch him go without a word. He had never seen his commander so angry.

An underground sewer system supplied Rafdonia’s water and drainage. Anyone who had been down here thought the same thing. First, to say the stench was terrible was a massive understatement, and second, it was more complicated than a maze.
This place is just as nasty every time I come here.

After running down the straight passage for a long while, I climbed the ladder to reach the sewer. When I slid the steel disk that resembled a manhole cover to the side and headed up, a road that split off into four branches greeted me. Of course, I had no problem figuring out the right way. One of the paths still showed signs of the dozens of people who had already gone down it. I just had to use those tracks as a guidepost and follow their lead. The problem lay elsewhere.
Goddamn sewer.

Perhaps this was a section that was designed to only allow water to pass because, unlike the section I did my commission in, there were no walkways on the sides for people to use. Actually, strictly speaking, it wasn’t that there weren’t any at all, but the footpath was too narrow for a barbarian over six feet tall to walk on.
Even the sewer design is discriminating against barbarians now.
Splash, splash.

In the end, I had no choice but to walk through filthy water that reached up to my shins. After who knew how long of that, I began to notice remnants of a recent battle left on the walls. Most were sword marks carved into the stonework. They were all different depths, but all the marks had one thing in common: the cuts were very clean, almost as if a high-precision machine had been used to make them. As a result, I was able to pretty much infer the identities of the people who left the marks—the shallow ones would be Amelia, and the deep ones would be him. The head of Orcules, the Traitor—Ricardo Lüchenprague.
“Tsk.”

It left a bad taste in my mouth. In the original plan that we were supposed to execute together, our goal had been to somehow shake this guy first and then enter the sewer afterward. That was because based on what she could remember, when Amelia was reunited with her childhood self in the sewer, she was being chased by this guy.
But it looks like she wasn’t able to get rid of him in the end.
Judging by the marks on the walls, it seemed she wasn’t successful. Why did she do such a foolish thing, drugging me? The future wasn’t something that would change just from something like that.
This girl is strangely straightforward when it comes to things like this.

In some ways, Amelia was similar to a barbarian. Though she was human, she was so stubborn that she never knew when to give up. And that wasn’t all. Although she pretended to be logical, she wore her heart on her sleeve.
Kwaaang!
Just then, there was an explosion in the distance and the entire sewer system shook.
Dash!
I picked up the pace.

The human body had limits. No matter how much you exercised or how strong you became, there was a maximum amount of power your muscles would be able to produce. That was why essences were the bedrock of the adventuring profession. Because they existed, adventurers were able to fight against even giant monsters using powers that surpassed their natural limits. However, none of that mattered here.
“Finally decided to fight?”

Amelia was seized by a feeling of helplessness. The boosts her essences gave her still coursed through her body and improved its performance, but all of her special abilities were sealed—Source of Youth, a skill that greatly increased the user’s Natural Regeneration in exchange for not being able to benefit from the potion or healing effects; Self-Replication, a skill that always gave her a numerical advantage in one-on-one fights; Power of the Abyss; Asura’s Kick; etcetera. All the abilities that served to uplift her in battle had been rendered useless by this one man standing in front of her.

“...Why are you so obsessed with me?” Amelia finally asked the question she had been holding back. And it was a fair question because she couldn’t understand it. She ran around the city for over two hours trying to get rid of this man, but he’d pursued her relentlessly, even into this sewer and its foul stench.
“Were my actions unexpected?”
Amelia nodded at the man’s question. “Yeah, I really can’t understand it. Instead of chasing after me, going after the lord of the castle should be much more important to you, no?”

The palace and lord of the castle had joined forces to wipe out Orcules. But this man, their commander and strongest fighter, had left the front lines to chase after a woman he had no connection to? Even setting aside how that would turn out for her personally, she couldn’t accept how this was playing out.
“What a ridiculous question.” The man’s smile was terribly cold. “A human woman with an awl-shaped aura that appears to specialize in daggers... All characteristics of the Order of the Rose.”
“...Order of the Rose?”
“Are you going to deny it?”

Amelia was truly confounded. She knew what the Order of the Rose was, of course—a unit directly under the palace that was responsible for special missions such as assassination, infiltration, and covert operations. There were rumors that the unit was entirely made up of women, but that had never been confirmed.
“I guess you’re a new recruit? Well, that’s probably why you asked a question like that.”
“I do not belong to the Order of—”
“Abandon the thought of living.” Amelia made an attempt at reasoning with him, but it didn’t work. “Because I have no questions for you.” A sword flew at her, cutting off all conversation.
Amelia quickly activated her aura to block it. No, she thought she blocked it.
Slice!
Her right hand got cut off at the wrist and fell into the sewer, still clutching one of her daggers.
Whip!
The sword rushed at her again. The target this time was her left wrist. The blade seemed to sing with a cruel determination to cut down everything in its path.
Kwaang!

Amelia used her aura-filled dagger to parry the sword and then stepped back. But did he anticipate that too? Taking advantage of the recoil, he swiftly switched targets, twisting his blade in a snake-like motion to dart at Amelia’s neck instead.
“Ah...!” Between one moment and the next, Amelia found herself pushed against the wall, cool metal pressing into the skin of her throat.
Press.

When the man pushed the blade in, blood dripped down her neck, accompanied by a burning pain. “What a nice expression.” Because her airway was blocked, Amelia couldn’t breathe, let alone piece together a reply. “It suits you.”
As she ran out of oxygen, her mind went blank.
Am I really going to die here? Then what will happen to Laura and my childhood self? If things were to unfold as I remember them, I should meet up with them injured but alive...
Amelia frantically scanned her surroundings as if searching for someone who could get her out of this.
...Yandel.

When she realized who she was looking for, Amelia found herself chuckling. There was no way he could be here because she had personally dosed him with a medicine that would knock him out for at least six hours. By now, he must have woken up, read the note, and arrived at the castle. Or, if he ended up waking up a bit earlier, he might have obtained that stone and returned to their original time already. No, there was a high chance he had already returned. This wouldn’t make sense otherwise.
“Are you looking for a way out?”
No matter how hard she searched, she saw no way for her to escape. The moment his sword dug in a little deeper, her torturously prolonged life would finally come to an end.
“Pfft...”
In other words, history had changed. She was going to die here today.
The cause being... Bjorn Yandel’s return.

She had excluded Yandel from this plan. There were several reasons she had done so. To start, she did not want to be indebted to that barbarian. Plus, she thought if he used the Fragment of Records Stone to return to their original world, he could alter the established timeline. After all, there had to be a reason that the legends said it was possible to change history. Surely, as an object of unknown origins and mysterious abilities, the stone would be the solution to her problems.
No, rather, she had just hoped it was. She was no different from a castaway on a lifeboat drinking seawater to quench her thirst. But surprisingly, it had worked.
“Why are you laughing?”
Press.
The man pushed the sword in a bit further out of displeasure. Death, which had always seemed to hang over her ever since she was a child, now felt a little closer.
So, he really succeeded in going back.
Amelia closed her eyes and began thinking.
“Suffer more.”
What will happen to the Rainwales sisters once I die? Without me, someone will definitely get killed... Or, maybe it will all end well because I’m not there.
She’d never know how it would turn out. The thought made her both happy and somewhat sad at the same time.
The sword dug into her flesh a little more. She couldn’t breathe, and her mind began to dull. It occurred to her that none of this mattered. She did her best, so she should be able to rest now.
But the moment she made up her mind to do just that, she heard a familiar voice from beyond the passageway. “Behel–ahhh!”

chapters.title: Chapter 324: Role (4)
paragraphs: I ran through the sewers.
Splash, splash.
The filth that was up to my shins splashed all over the place, but my eyes were locked straight ahead. There was a man and a woman. The man was forcing the woman against a wall, a sword at her neck.
Jeez, if you’re going to leave me, at least be doing well.

I tightened my grip on the hammer and shouted with all my might, the sound echoing through the passageway. “Behel–ahhh!” I decided I had to do whatever I could to draw attention to me and get the sword away from Amelia.
Shoop!

The moment the sword pulled back, a fountain of blood erupted from Amelia’s neck. I thought he was just holding it against her skin, but it seemed it was already inside. It looked like he even dug it in deeper right before pulling it out.
“...Barbarian?” the man muttered, turning toward me.
Although I was wearing an iron helmet as usual, it seemed he’d inferred my race based on my large frame and the contents of my shout. I used my keen vision to check on how Amelia was doing.

“K-Krr... ugh...!” Amelia had a hole in her neck. She used one hand to cover the bleeding and the other to barely support her staggering body. I could tell even at a glance that she wasn’t doing well.
Well, as long as she hasn’t died...

Worrying wouldn’t help anyone. The most important thing when it came to saving someone was having good judgment and the ability to execute on it. With that in mind, I kicked off the ground once more and sprinted forward.
Splash!
The distance rapidly narrowed. As soon as we reached a radius where we could touch each other’s weapons, the man’s flared with a bright aura and swung at me.
Kwaang!
I blocked the aura with my hammer. At that moment, his eyes filled with confusion. I guessed he took for granted that he’d be able to slice through my weapon with his aura.
But like you’d expect from a veteran who had faced all kinds of adversity, he soon figured it out. “That’s a Numbers Item.”
How sharp.
Still, I decided to focus on the positives in this situation. His blabbering had created an opening.
Whip.

While engaging in a tight power struggle, I extended an arm to pull Amelia toward me. She barely had the strength to remain standing, so it was easy to drag her into my arms. Did I have everything I needed, then?
“...You’re her comrade.”
“Isn’t that obvious?”
“That means... you are my enemy too.”
Why do you keep stating the obvious?

At that moment, our brief clash of arms came to an end. Lüchenprague put more force behind his sword to shove me away. It was a very strange feeling since I hadn’t been overpowered by anyone recently, but there was no need to be discouraged.
His strength is slightly superior to mine.

As I was pushed backward, I was able to shuffle back even more. Of course, the man lunged at me right after. He was much faster than me too. When it came to the most important part of close combat—stats—I was inferior to him. Not to mention the passive and active skills I’d worked hard to stock up and create good combos with were sealed. In the midst of that, my opponent was handing out auras, which were my natural enemy, like candy.
Has he no conscience?
Despite my complaints, I quickly made a decision. I was facing a truly overwhelming difference in stats. Even under normal circumstances, running away would be a challenge.
But I won’t have to default to that right away.
This wasn’t a huge deal. I just had to create unusual circumstances.
Kwaaang!
Yeah, for example, underwater warfare.
Shaaa!
In a dark sewer illuminated by flickering torchlight, there were fifteen men and women divided into two groups glaring at each other like enemies.
“What are you talking about? Say that again, Dumbo.”
“It’s Durbon, not Dumbo.”
“Tom-ay-to, tom-ah-to. Based on the way you always laughed like an moron in front of that barbarian, you liked it, anyway.”
“What...? You bastard!”

There was clear hostility on both sides of the exchange. Caught in between, Laura Rainwales held her sister’s trembling hand and thought to herself that she wouldn’t have followed these people if she had known this would happen.
Why are these guys like this even in a situation like this?

Laura just could not understand it. It had started off as what was clearly a minor argument. One of the adventurers, a former worker of the Melta merchant company who knew of the secret passage, was having trouble navigating them through the sewers. Someone made a scathing comment. That alone was enough to sow the seed of discord.

Durbon, the man who was implicitly acting as their leader, had defended their guide. “Jeez, you’re grumbling way too much for someone who’s doing nothing but tagging along for free.” No, he went beyond defending and threw in some threats. “And now that I think about it, this is kind of unfair. If you’re going to say something like that, at least pay up. Ah, if you don’t have money, you can pay with equipment.”
“What?”
“Or you can go back if you want.”
Those few exchanges instantly divided the group in two and led them to the present moment.
“This is my final offer. Either give up your equipment and follow us, or go back.”
“Ha, do you think I’ll just do as you say?”
“Stop acting high and mighty just because you’re friends with the guide. The only thing we need to find our way out of the city is that guide, anyway.”
“...So you insist on bloodshed.”
“Um... let’s calm down, everyone...” Laura opened her mouth, figuring she had to stop them somehow, but Durbon cut her off mid-sentence.
“Laura, you stay quiet. This is for the best.”
“Excuse me? W-What’s for the best...?”
“We’re going to need a lot of money from now on if we want to find our place aboveground.”
At Durbon’s words, the man who stood opposite him nodded in apparent agreement, conceding the point. “Yeah, if half of us die here, the rest will be able to live more like proper human beings.”

Those words made Laura realize that there was never a seed of discord to begin with. Unlike in the overworld she had only ever heard about in stories, this way of thinking was natural for people from Noark. Picking a fight over someone not being able to find the way was just an opportunity to start something. Perhaps they purposely took advantage of it.
This is why I wanted to get Amelia out somehow...

Noark was a place where beasts resided. Laura trembled, once again disillusioned by the city she was born in. Then she put her hand on her sword belt. If this battle was unavoidable anyway, Durbon’s faction, to which she belonged, had to win. That way she would be able to get out of here and live like a real person. Well, maybe not her, but at least her sister.
“Amelia, get ready.”
“Okay.” At Laura’s whisper, her sister also touched her weapon. Somehow, someway, the sisters were also beasts that had successfully survived in this world of the fittest.
“Now then, let’s get started—”

The moment their opponent took a step forward with a weapon, Durbon’s group fired an arrow and the battle began. Then, several minutes into this clash, a strong current of water gushed forth from beyond the dark passageway and engulfed them.
Shaaaaaa!
Bang, bang, bang, bang!
As I ran away from Lüchenprague, who was charging at me with a ferocious aura covering his sword, I made exactly four strikes at exact intervals.
Crack, crack, crack, boom!
The ceiling, cracking like spiderwebs on a mirror, collapsed after the fourth.
Shaaaaaa!
Like a broken dam, a torrent of water began to pour down through the hole.
There really is water flowing above us.
To be honest, before I started swinging the hammer, I wasn’t sure about that. I just thought that, given the events young Amelia had lived through, it was highly likely.
“At that time, a disagreement broke out in the group, resulting in a battle. Then, suddenly, water poured into the passage. Everyone was swept up in it and lost consciousness. And when I woke up...”

I wiped the distracting thoughts from my mind and hugged Amelia tighter. If I’d been an ordinary person, I would have already been swept away by the torrent. But both my opponent and I were far from ordinary people.
Kwaaang!
When I instinctively defended myself with the hammer, a tremendous shock jolted through the handle. Even though the water was rising and already up to our heads, my opponent had swung his sword.
Persistent bastard.

It was hard to keep my balance due to the rapid current, and I was pushed back five or six steps before I finally just closed my eyes. Vision didn’t mean anything now, anyway. Whether there was a source of light or not, it was impossible to see anything in this muddy water.
Oh, is this real, live mud wrestling?
The thought randomly popped into my head, but I quickly dismissed it. I had more important things to worry about right now.
One, two, three, four, five, six...

With my dominant elbow against the wall, I quickly walked back the way I came. This left my back defenseless but I wasn’t too worried. He likely made his last attack by relying on his senses to swing his sword at the spot I was last standing.
Slice!
Just then, a tingling sensation arose on my thigh. It seemed he was following after me and swinging his sword blindly.
Ugh, this asshole is unreal.
Still, it was fine, because we had arrived at our destination.
Fifty-one, fifty-two... whew, we’re at the right place.

Walking with my eyes closed and feeling along the wall, I reached the fork in the road I had seen earlier and hid myself down one of the other routes. This was a trick I’d learned from Rotmiller. Having made maps in the past, I was able to accurately measure the length of my strides, and I had gotten much better at memorizing a route I’d taken before. There was no way this guy had that ability.
Okay, it looks like he’s passed the fork in the road without realizing it even exists.
But I didn’t let my guard down as I continued moving down the road.
Giantization.
I finally got a bit of reprieve once I got farther away from the guy and was able to confirm my skills were in working order again.
She still has a pulse.

Amelia was still alive, and the passive skill that gave her a cockroach-like survival rate, Source of Youth, would have activated by now. I wouldn’t have to worry about the wound on her neck anymore. It may have hit something vital, but the injury itself wasn’t too serious. The skin over the injury should regenerate in a minute.
The problem is oxygen...

In my case, I had no major issues with air thanks to my increased Lung Capacity stat from the Storm Gush’s essence. But Amelia’s situation was a bit different. Because of her neck injury, oxygen wasn’t being supplied to the rest of her body properly. I didn’t know how long she would last. I was pretty sure she just needed to hold out for five minutes... She told me that after the passage flooded, the source ran out and the water soon started to drain.
Ugh, whatever.

After taking a moment to think it over, I adjusted my hold on Amelia. Fumbling around her body, I finally found her nose and covered it with one hand before putting my mouth to hers. It was underwater artificial respiration, just like in the movies. I didn’t know if this would really work, but I figured it was better to at least try. It wasn’t like I had anything to lose, either.
Did she come to her senses? The moment our lips met, Amelia’s limp body flinched. Then she started to struggle, almost like she was trying to push me away.
Squeeze.

I pulled her in closer by the waist to tell her to stay put. The resistance then faded. Was that consent, then? I couldn’t be sure, but I moved to press my lips as close to hers as possible to prevent water from getting in through the gap.
Blow!
I exhaled as hard as I could.

After about five minutes of repeated underwater rescue breathing, the water level began to drop at a rapid rate. When the water pouring in from above ran out, the water below began to distribute itself evenly throughout the vast sewer system.
Surprisingly, Amelia was still conscious at this point. “L-Let me go...”
Jeez, it was a rescue operation, no need to make a big deal out of it.
When I let go of her waist, Amelia plunged into the water. Oh, right. She was short. The water was still up to my shoulders so she had no hope of standing on her feet.
Gasp!
The moment I was about to reach out and grab her waist again, Amelia’s head bobbed up to the surface on its own. She knew how to swim.
“I’m... just letting you know... but that was pointless.”
“Huh?”
“Holding... my breath has... been my specialty since I was little...”
“What are you saying?”

Since she was still gasping for breath and talking at an inaudible volume, I couldn’t understand her at all. It seemed she didn’t want to repeat herself, though. Or, maybe she felt there was something more important for us to focus on. I couldn’t be sure, but Amelia changed the subject.
“Never mind that... why are you here?” Her breathing was more stable than earlier and her voice returned to normal.
Hmm, I don’t think I have to worry about her anymore.
“What do you mean ‘why am I here’? What does that even mean?” I asked, uncomprehending.
Amelia frowned. “I told you to go back. Did you not see the note?”
“Ah, I did see that.”
“Then... why didn’t you go back...?”
Jeez, why are you scolding me so much?

Well, to be honest, I couldn’t go back just because I wanted to, anyway. Remembering all the trouble she caused me with her trick earlier, I spoke curtly without really meaning to. “Because there’s work left to do.”
“Work...?”
“I can’t go back before then.”
“What? Why on earth are you so...?”
What was she mumbling about? That was the only way we could go back. I was about to say so when Giantization suddenly deactivated.

“Ugh, prick.” Put simply, this meant that bastard was within a hundred-foot radius of us. It looked like he just went straight and doubled back when he realized he lost me, and I didn’t think he’d let us go all that easily. Therefore, I made a decision. “Hey, you go first.”
“...What?”
“Go save your sister. I’ll take care of this guy somehow.” I’d send Amelia to the sisters while I stopped this guy.
Amelia frowned at my simple plan. “That’s suicide. He is not an enemy you can handle—”
“Then what about your sister? Are you going to give up?”
“...If I can’t change anything anyway, it’s better—”
“Stop.” I cut Amelia off. I didn’t know when she became so weak-willed. “Trust me, Amelia. I have put some thought into that so go and save the sisters first. Got it?”
“But—”
“Hush.” No buts. I laughed a bit at her surprising reaction to my offer. Having someone worry about you wasn’t a bad feeling. “Why do you think I’m going to lose in the first place?”

The ability that came with the essence of the Lord of the Fifth Floor, Nullification, was definitely a great skill. It was also unbelievably rare. The number of people in the entire history of Rafdonia who had obtained it was less than ten, and as far as anyone knew, there was only one person who possessed it now. It was no wonder people were afraid of it. With no information on it available, it would look to anyone like a completely overpowered skill. But I saw it in a very different way.
It’s not a particularly difficult one to deal with.
I’d devoted all of my free time in my twenties to Dungeon and Stone. Of course I’d hunted the Lord of Tranquility. “Three hundred times?” Hmm, something like that.
Amelia didn’t understand what I was talking about. “Three hundred times...?” she asked.
“I’ve taken that essence more than three hundred times,” I replied.
There was no such thing as a skill without a weakness.

chapters.title: Chapter 325: Role (5)
paragraphs: The Lord of Chaos was Riakis; the Lord of the Abyss, Berzak. The lords of each floor had both a true name and nickname, and their essences were usually referred to by their second name—essence of Chaos, or essence of Abyss, for example. That was usually how it went.

My assessment of the essence of Tranquility that Lüchenprague had was that looks could be deceiving. As the essence of a Lord of the Floor, it was powerful and oppressive, but the concept behind it was riddled with issues. This was evident just by looking at its active skill, Nullification, a wide-range silencer that nullified all skills within a hundred-foot radius. This included passive skills, and any skills used outside the radius disactivated the moment you entered it, rendering long-distance intervention impossible.
But that did not mean it was invincible. There was a reason I didn’t consume things like that.
It can’t dispel magic and divine power.

And the downsides didn’t even end there. Nullification did not work on a monster. Put simply, the essence of Tranquility was basically an essence that was only useful in interpersonal combat, and its passives were even more ridiculous. With its passive skill Tranquil Control, the skills of all essences you absorbed aside from this one were disabled, and the stats you gained from the essence were doubled. It was an extremely high-risk skill that forfeited the skills of all other essences you acquired in exchange for doubling your stats.

Thanks to that, I hardly ever took this essence. That was because my goal was always to clear the game. The reason I took it three hundred times in the first place was because I wanted to attempt a different route.
[“I have heard of your reputation as an adventurer. Why not turn the world upside down with us?”]

There was a route that occasionally opened up in the game when you gained fame. So, back when I joined forces with the Ormi Revolutionary Corps to clear the Treason route, I always started off by taking the essence of Tranquility. There was definitely no other essence like this one when it came to interpersonal combat. I never succeeded at beating the game that way, though. After running into countless dead ends, I came to the tentative conclusion that there was a problem with the game itself and clearing the Treason route was impossible. After that, I never absorbed the essence again. Just in time, I realized that the essence of Tranquility had a fatal flaw.
Squeeze.

I gripped the item I had prepared for this very scenario, the key to defeating Lüchenprague the Traitor. Actually, I had debated using it earlier, but at the time I decided taking care of Amelia was my top priority so I saved it.
Whew, if I knew she was going to lie about D-Day, I would have given this to her in advance.

The reason I didn’t bother sharing this information with her was because I thought we were going to be working together, as planned. Of course I did, because how could I ever have predicted that she would take me out by mixing paralysis medicine into a drink? It never even occurred to me that it would probably look cooler to whip it out in the middle of a crisis, just in time.
...Really, it didn’t.
Slide.
The water level was going down every second now.
Now that it’s down to the waist, he’ll be able to see again.
I stared down the passageway Amelia had disappeared through. I remembered the conversation we had before she left and laughed to myself.
“I’ll trust you.”
“Yes, trust me. The matter with your sister—”
“I didn’t mean with my sister.”
“Not my sister. That you won’t die. That’s what I’ll trust. So... don’t die.”
“U-Uh... Okay...”
I avoided her eyes because it was embarrassing to hear something like that said to my face. Amelia seemed to feel similarly because she quickly left me behind.
“Then I’ll go first—”
You’re here.
I could hear the splash of water in the distance, so I shook off the distracting thoughts and focused on the sound.
Splash, splash.
The distance closed quickly. I tensed and crouched my upper body.
Rip.
Then I tore open the scroll I had in my fist.
Shaaaaaa!
Glowing flecks of mana particles burst out and settled on my skin. The light emitted by the mana particles was weak, but it was enough to draw someone’s attention in the darkness of the sewer.
Splash.
The sound that had been getting closer stopped.
Thump.

My heart pounded like I was a child caught in the middle of planning something naughty, growing louder as the silence dragged on. Apart from the running water, there was no other sound for about three seconds.
Splash!
When I heard him start to run, I crouched down and dove into the water. Then, the moment the guy appeared at the crossroads, I stood up abruptly and rushed at him.
Kwaaang!

The aura and hammer came into contact, throwing water in all directions from the impact. Perhaps because my concentration was at its highest, all available visual information was easily cataloged by my mind. The water droplets had broken into thousands of particles, and my opponent’s face was visible through them. After meeting my eye, the guy shifted his gaze to the side.
Is he looking for Amelia? Jeez, you’re making a barbarian feel left out.
Dash.

As soon as my feet touched the ground, I jumped up again and closed the distance between me and the enemy. The guy was already swinging his sword sideways. It seemed he was planning to keep me in check so I couldn’t get any closer, but thanks to that, I ended up in the middle of the sword’s trajectory. This was a good thing for me.
Dash.

I sprinted forward without stopping. At this rate, it was clear that the sword would reach me before my hammer, which got pushed behind my shoulder in the first exchange, could hit him. But, so what? I hadn’t been planning on hitting him with the hammer in the first place.
Slide.

I reached my other hand forward. It was free because I had placed my shield, which was a useless item against an aura user, in sub-space. But I guessed a sword wasn’t the only weapon in a swordsman’s arsenal. My opponent didn’t bother redirecting his blade’s trajectory. He just shifted to swat my hand away with his free one.
Tap!

Soon, his hand bumped my wrist. Since this guy was not inferior to me in terms of strength, my arm was pushed back. In the middle of all that, he swung the sword to slice my waist, and because my two feet were in the air, it was impossible for me to step back and avoid it. When you looked at it that way, his assessment of the situation definitely wasn’t bad. It was just a little complacent.
Skin touched skin and the conditions of the pre-torn scroll were met.
Shaaaaaa!
Blue-colored mana particles burst into being. If this were the game, this would have been the message that appeared on the screen:
[You have been Bound to Ricardo Lüchenprague. You are no longer affected by Nullification.]
I immediately ran through the combo I had prepared.
Transcendence. Leap.
Dash.
The moment I stepped into the air, my body darted forward in a straight line, splashing water everywhere.
Dart!
I wasn’t running to get out of the sword’s orbit, but further inward.
While I’m at it... Giantization.
Now that I had the weight of an eight-ton truck that had someone’s foot on the gas, the rest was history.
Kwaaaaaang! Choke...!
The resulting body slam was incredible.
Amelia was sprinting through the half-submerged sewer when she felt herself unwittingly freeze as a vibration ran through the water.
Kwaaaaaang!
She could faintly hear the loud bang even from afar. It seemed a battle had started back there too.
Splash, splash.

Amelia quickly refocused herself and started moving her feet again. The boom was loud enough to make her wonder if a section of the sewer had collapsed. What could have caused a sound like that? Could something have gone wrong? Several questions came to mind simultaneously, but she shook her head. She said she would trust him. In a way, that was a promise in itself.
But if Yandel won against Lüchenprague, how was Lüchenprague able to appear before the sisters at the end? Amelia shook off that thought too.
Splash.

She continued to jog. Although the sewer was as complicated as a maze, it wasn’t very difficult to reach her desired destination. As someone whose achievements had been recognized several times and who had risen to a significant position within Noark, she had taken this path many times. Naturally, she had memorized it all for this day.
Left here. And until the next three-way fork in the road, straight ahead.
Amelia continued to run, pushing her body to limits that far exceeded those of an ordinary person. And after a while...
Tap.
Amelia stopped. She had arrived at her destination, a crossroad with five passages. She could see water-logged bodies floating everywhere. They were all faces she remembered.
“Laura! Amelia! What are you doing?! If you’re awake, hurry up and fight!”

When she regained consciousness after being swept away by the water, the battle had still been raging. At the time, Amelia had taken out her weapon and tried to fight as ordered, but her sister stopped her, pointing to the side. The adventurer who once worked for the Melta Merchant Company, the only one who knew the way, was taking the equipment off the corpses and getting away. And so the two hadn’t participated in the battle and just followed the disappearing guide.
Here.
Recalling the right passage in her memory, Amelia hurried inside and was soon able to find the person she was looking for.
“I-I’m just hiding here for a moment...” the guide stuttered out an excuse, looking terrified.
“Whatever, I don’t care about you.” Durbon glared at the man, then whipped his head around. “How dare you two betray me and run!”

The man then slapped her sister’s cheek. Laura took the hit, not even thinking of stopping him. She had come to the conclusion that making him angrier was not a good idea because Durbon was not alone. Ironically, he had drawn his weapon and sided with the people he was just fighting.
Since the numbers have decreased just like he wanted, he probably figured there was no point in fighting anymore. The guide disappearing would have been a factor too.

He was truly an animal. Even after all of this, he and his temporary allies would probably betray each other at the last minute and try to steal each other’s equipment. There was no way to know that for sure, though.
Squeeze.
Amelia gripped her dagger with her remaining hand.
“I-It’s all my fault.”
“So you know what you did wrong.”
“M-My sister just followed me... ugh!”
“Yes, don’t worry. I’ll make sure to send her the same place I’m sending you!”
The moment the man choking Laura was about to bring down the axe, his arm fell into the water, still clutching his weapon.
Slice!
While the man screamed, his body twisting from the pain of the amputation, the others in the vicinity were shocked to see Amelia.
“Emily...?!”
“H-How are you here...?”
They were not worth speaking to. Amelia plunged her dagger into each of their necks, utterly emotionless.
“Uh, w-wait! I-I know the way...!”
That included the guide, who tried to argue that he was essential. Since she knew the road that led to the city anyway, there was no reason to save him.
Slice!
With that, she cleaned up the area. The Rainwales sisters trembled, wary of her, but it seemed one of them had a curiosity she couldn’t ignore.
“Amelia—!”
Her younger self ignored her older sister’s urgings to stay quiet and finished her question. “W-What happened to Felic Barker?”
“He is dead.”
“I-Is that true? B-But how...”
“No more questions.” Amelia ended the conversation there. “There is no time for this. Follow me, quickly.”
This long tale was nearing its end.

chapters.title: Chapter 326: Ouroboros (1)
paragraphs: Bind was a support spell that, when used, designated certain individuals as your comrades and made it possible for you to travel through the labyrinth portal together with them. It also allowed you to share experience points upon defeating monsters.

It was during the Traitor route that I realized this spell was the perfect counter for Nullification. After once again taking the essence of Tranquility, I finally managed to reach the depths of the palace after about three hundred tries. During that attempt, I had been filled with the hope that I would be able to see the king’s face if I just went a little further.
[You have been Bound to a member of the Guardian Knights.]

Then the palace NPCs used this strategy on me and flushed all my hard work down the drain. It wasn’t long before I found a counter to this counter, but I still never got to see the king’s face, and in the end, I gave up on the Traitor route. That had probably been my first time calling it quits since starting the game, but I didn’t consider it a waste of time. At times, there was something to be gained from the process of failing—like this.
Choke...!

I followed up Bind with a huge body slam. Lüchenprague was hit head-on, tossed into the air, and thrown backward. However, sitting back and enjoying the show at this point would be a bad move. Just look at martial arts games. If you threw an enemy into the air and rendered them incapable of blocking, you had to follow through with a combo, no matter what.
Transcendence.
I activated another ability before the bastard’s body got out of my twenty-yard range: Eye of the Storm, the grab skill I had obtained by consuming the essence of Storm Gush.
It just so happens that I’m perfectly optimized for PVP.
A strong gust kicked up down the long stretch of the sewer, and the bastard’s body changed directions in mid-air, coming back toward me. I took up a smashing stance.
One, two, three. Now.
At the exact right time, I put all my power into a well-placed Swing.
Crack!
The crunch of flesh and bone sounded as the hammer connected, but I wasn’t particularly satisfied. That was because the sound didn’t come from the spot I was aiming for.
Welp.

My target had been his vulnerable temple, but unfortunately, the guy raised his arm. Even while being dragged toward me by the gust, he had managed to come to his senses and protect one of his vital points.
I still took out an arm, though.
Although it wasn’t a fatal blow, I decided to look on the bright side. His arm was bent at an odd angle and left dangling. That alone showed that he’d suffered considerable damage.
Dash.
The bastard was sent flying toward the wall by my whack, but he managed to get his bearings and kick off the stonework with one leg.
Looks like this guy has a lot of combat experience too.
Instead of trying to put distance between us, he ran toward me and swung his sword.
Whiiip!
Up close and personal, that aura of his was even more brutal. Because his Agility stat was much higher than mine, it would be tough to stop that with a hammer in the stance I was in.
If he had run backward, I would have continued chasing after him and kept up my momentum, but this time I chose to retreat.
Splash.

Once there were about ten yards between us, there was a momentary lull. The bastard rotated the sword in his one remaining hand, seemingly warming up for the next round, and asked, “How... did you know?”

Seeing as he was out of breath, it seemed the damage from the body slam and arm smash hadn’t faded. Wait, then had he started a conversation to buy himself time to recover? I paused in my analysis of his condition to laugh.
“No one... knows about... this essence...” He was clearly looking for an explanation for this unexpected turn of events.
So, you were just curious.

Well, he probably made a concerted effort to hide his weaknesses from others. That was likely why he always worked alone too. Even if he did decide to team up with other people, he would never use Bind with them. The moment he did, Nullification’s fatal flaw would be revealed to the world.
Now that I’m thinking about it, Nullification was probably why he was nagging Fallen Scholar so much in the community.

In order to overthrow the royal family, Lüchenprague would need a comrade who would not lose their powers around him even without needing Bind, like a wizard or a priest for example. However, since a priest wouldn’t cooperate in killing the king, Fallen Scholar’s relative value must have risen. Not only was he a top-tier wizard, but he was also an evil spirit.
“So, you must be an evil spirit...” the guy muttered, watching me intently. I didn’t say a word, but he seemed to have jumped through the hoops and hurdles needed to reach that conclusion on his own.
Well, he isn’t wrong, but more importantly... He doesn’t know the reverse counter method.
Through this conversation, I became convinced that he did not know of the counter to my counter. If he did, he would have had no reason to insist on working alone. I gripped the hammer tighter.
Good thing this is twenty years in the past.

Of course, I had no way of knowing what would happen in the future. Perhaps when we met again someday, this particular problem of his would be solved. He could have gotten a ton of new essences over twenty years, too, and his swordsmanship may have reached a stage of perfection. What I knew for sure was that considering his notoriety twenty years from now, there was a high chance he would turn into an enemy I had no hope of defeating.
But that’s not the case today.
I made my next move. There was a reason I’d been staying put until now.
Transcendence. Eye of the Storm.
While we were talking, the cooldown period had come to an end.
From there, the battle unfolded in a pretty straightforward way.
Bang, bang!
The aura and double-digit Demon Grinder clashed nonstop, exchanging blows.
Shit, why is he so good at fighting?
I was hitting my limit for the first time. I’d been overpowered in terms of stats many times, but I’d never felt this way when it came to pure martial arts technique.
Slice!

The moment I hesitated, my opponent sliced into my flesh. His sword moved as fluidly as a snake, and at times was as hard as steel. That wasn’t all, either. Even to my untrained eye, the amount of technique that went into every form and thrust of his blade was clear. Put simply, this was a completely new type of enemy for me. Even in a fight against a knight, the winner was bound to be decided by split-second decisions if I managed to force them into a dogfight to the death.
Slice!
