The wounds accumulated on my body faster than my Natural Regeneration could heal them. Even still, I didn’t have any fatal injuries yet. That wasn’t because I was good at avoiding them, but because I was periodically using potions.
Chhhhhh!
Bubbles boiled from the deep cuts and flesh filled the gaps. I took stock of my condition for only a brief moment before back-stepping.
Transcendence. Eye of the Storm.

I used my grab skill which had just finished recharging and dragged my opponent in again. However, it turned out basically the same way as last time. As if to prove that it only worked the first time because I caught him off guard, he didn’t miss a beat and used the speed with which he was being dragged toward me to put more force behind his next swing.
Whippp!
Whew, even his timing is scary now. From now on, I should table Eye of the Storm.
Dash.
I took a step back to dodge the sword again. In response, my opponent kicked off the ceiling, instantly closed the distance between us, and said, “Who are you?”
Kwaaang!
“Seeing as you’re that woman’s comrade...”
Kwaaang!
“Were you sent by the palace?”
Jeez, so noisy. You talk a lot.

On one hand, the bastard’s nonstop, uninterrupted chatter was pissing me off, but on the other hand, it made me wonder what he was talking about. Sent by the palace? What’s the palace got to do with anything?

Of course, it was a question that quickly slid out of my mind. After all, the palace and lord of the castle had teamed up to invade the eastern district occupied by Orcules. It wasn’t strange that he’d assume that I was with them, though there was one thing I was still wondering.
So, what now?
I didn’t even consider the possibility of me killing this guy here. According to history, he was going to appear in front of Amelia not long from now.
Still, although winning may be hard, I don’t think I’d necessarily lose.
I had no way of knowing for sure, but I felt like if I put my mind to it, I could stall him here for hours if I wanted to. Unless something unexpected happened, I felt like I could do this all day.
Huh?
So of course, something unexpected happened. You had to be careful what you wished for.
Splash.

I thought I heard someone in the distance. Both I and my opponent put distance between ourselves and quickly looked toward the source of the sound. I hadn’t misheard it—there really was someone there.
God damn it.
That “someone” was a person I recognized, and by the looks of it, it seemed Lüchenprague also knew of him. “...Jerome Saintred,” he muttered.
As soon as his name left Lüchenprague’s mouth, the silver-haired knight on the other side of the tunnel spoke up as well. “Ricardo Lüchenprague.”

The greeting was far from friendly. Hatred and murderous intent filled both their eyes and voices. Well, that was exactly what you’d expect when the Traitor who wanted to kill the king was faced with the protector of the palace. I quickly finished assessing the situation.
Okay, I should leave these two to fight and bounce.

I was the reason the Knight of Light came into the sewer in the first place, but considering the two were enemies, there was a chance I could turn this disaster into an opportunity. With that thought in mind, I started looking for a way out of there.
Unfortunately, someone was quicker to make up their mind. Lüchenprague said a strange word. “Two.”
He took the fork in the road next to him and started to flee. It was only after that that I realized what he meant by “two.”
...Shit, are you serious?

That guy thought this bastard and I were on the same side, likely because he already mistakenly assumed I was from the palace. Even I would have found it tough to fight two on one in this situation if I were him. I understood the sentiment, but I didn’t have room to empathize with him right now.
Ah... I should scram now too.
Momentarily startled by Lüchenprague’s escape, I quickly came to my senses and got moving. Deep down, though, I was desperately begging.
Please, please, please... Please follow him, not me. Please? Come on, that’s the nutjob that wants to kill your king.
Dash.
When I started running, I heard a sound behind me. It seemed Saintred had finished deciding who to follow.
Splash.
Ha, that tracks. There’s no way things would go that smoothly.
Splash, splash!
I could hear him chasing me. It seemed this guy had decided that retrieving the Fragment of Records Stone came before the Traitor. That, or he had a deep grudge against me for what happened earlier.
Flash!
As Lüchenprague fled, Nullification was lifted and the knight used Gateway of Light to block my path. I didn’t notice because of the distance earlier but he seemed different.
What the, what’s with the serial killer eyes?
The bossy vibe I got when I met him earlier was gone and before me stood a knight with the eyes of a merciless executioner.
“Did you think you could survive after making a fool out of me?”

Perhaps this was karma. You know, running down the quick and easy path when you realize you’re surrounded on all sides by enemies. Of course, this didn’t mean I regretted it. Things like this were the fault of the person who got fooled in the first place.

“Before I punish you, I will ask you one thing.” The knight pointed a sword covered with a twisting aura at me and spoke. “Lüchenprague. What is your relationship with that man? Is he the one who ordered you to bring the Fragment of Records Stone to him?”

This was a bit of an ironic situation. Lüchenprague thought I was in cahoots with this guy, and this guy thought I was on Lüchenprague’s side. I felt like an innocent bystander caught up in this mess, but what could I do? I had to wriggle my way out of it somehow.
“You noticed?” Instead of clearing up the misunderstanding, I simply affirmed his assumption. I decided this was my best bet for now.
In fact, when I nodded, I saw something in the knight’s gaze shift. “Did you already hand the item to him?”
“I don’t know.” Donning the Lion’s mask had taught me this: to tell a good lie, you had to convince yourself first. “What do you think?”
When I shrugged and let his imagination run wild, the knight started to shake with barely restrained energy. “...So that’s why you split up.”

“I guess you didn’t earn the reputation of Knight of Light for nothing. Your gears appear to be turning well.” When I used this time to compliment him, the knight went quiet. I did my utmost to harden my expression. Then I sprinkled an extra bit of seasoning on the already finished dish. “I won’t let you get to the commander. Fight me.”

It was the heartfelt declaration of someone determined to somehow buy more time for the greater cause. However, in front of Jerome, that determination was meaningless. No matter how much I tried to stall him, all he would have to do was use Gateway of Light to pass me by. Which was exactly what I was hoping for.
“Kekeke...”
What the fuck? Why is this guy laughing all of a sudden? Has he lost his mind?
When I frowned, the knight’s laughter instantly died as he stared me down. “Almost got fooled again.”
“...What?”
“It doesn’t matter whether your words are true or not. I just have to kill you first to confirm.”
“But then it would be too late—”

“It doesn’t matter. Arrive at the destination one step at a time without being overly ambitious.” The knight looked at me coolly. “That is the way of a knight.” It seemed this guy had figured out his own way to navigate this world of con artists.
...Do I have no choice but to fight?
I wordlessly lifted my hammer. It didn’t seem he would change his mind even if I kept talking.
Silence fell, marking the part of the match where breaths were exchanged just before the swing of weapons.

Suddenly, an old man’s laughter rang out behind me. “Hahaha...” Since Jerome was right in front of me, I couldn’t turn around to check, but it wasn’t difficult to identify who it was. “You are very adept at deceiving others,” said Auril Gavis.
However, it seemed Jerome had never met him before. “...Reveal your identity, old man,” the silver-haired knight said in an authoritative tone.
“What a rude fellow.”
As Auril’s voice echoed through the sewer, the Knight of Light suddenly wrapped his free hand around his own neck.
...Choke!
The strained look on his face suggested he couldn’t breathe. His eyes were locked behind me, and the emotion in his pupils was one of astonishment. “Y-You... who on earth...”
“I don’t sense any particular value in you.”
Cough...!
“Begone.” The moment Auril finished his sentence, tone utterly dry, Jerome’s limp body floated up into the air. Goosebumps ran down my spine.
Is he dead? The strongest royal knight gone, as easy as killing a fly?
As if to answer my question, the voice behind me spoke up again. “He is probably not dead. He will likely wake up in the palace.”
Ah, was he talking about that essence? I slowly turned around, shaking off the thoughts that flashed through my mind.
“Finally you look at me.” The sight of the old man and his kind smile was disturbing. That was because his lips were clearly curled, but his eyes were not.
Just how much does he know?

I swallowed involuntarily, and Auril opened his mouth. “About the barbarian we were talking about—Bjon, son of Thor. When I asked around in the city, a kind young man informed me that he is also known as Iron Mask because he always covers his face with a thick helmet. Just like you.”
So, you came here already knowing everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 327: Ouroboros (2)
paragraphs: It was like watching a monster die.
Shaaaaaa!

Jerome’s body, which hung limp on the floor of the sewer, broke up into little flecks of light and fluttered away. Some items were left behind as it did, but most were things without value. His expensive-looking sword, armor, and other items were all covered in light and disappeared with him.
Is it Iblus...?
I had a guess as to which essence was at play here, but that wasn’t important right now.
The silence was filled only by the sound of flowing water. Auril Gavis, who was still grinning like his face was stuck that way, spoke again. “Let me ask. Are you an evil spirit?”

It wasn’t so much a question as a statement. Well, if he came all this way, he must already be convinced that the rank-six adventurer Nivelles Enze, who he hadn’t been able to find anywhere in the city above, was Iron Mask.
Still, the reason he asked is probably because he wants to hear it from the source...

Having just seen him render the palace’s greatest knight incapable of combat with a flick of the wrist, I decided to activate Barbarian Confucian Mode. “Evil spirit? I don’t know where you got that impression but I am not, sir.”
“You’re lying,” Auril said, distrustful despite my polite tone.
Ha, I guess he can use his lie detector here as well.

I sort of expected that, but it still rubbed me the wrong way when my attempt ended up being in vain. However, there was no time to waste on despair. After all, we were not inside the community right now. If I wasn’t careful about how I handled this, it could lead to problems down the line.

“Haha, I guess I can’t fool you. You’re incredible.” I quickly changed my tune. Since any further deception would come across as arrogance, I decided to acknowledge and own up to the bare minimum. “Yes, I am the person you are looking for. I never thought I would run into you out here, so I was startled and couldn’t be honest with you.”
“Startled, huh...?”
“Yes, startled. And I didn’t actually lie, did I?”
Auril scoffed at my bold question. “Haha, yes... come to think of it, you did not lie.”

That was right. I didn’t lie back then. His question about the state of the city? I answered honestly that the lord of the castle had teamed up with the palace and attacked Orcules. I’d responded yes when asked whether a barbarian had come to the city about five or six months ago, and when asked for his name, I informed him it was Bjon, son of Thor.
“Yes, I couldn’t bring myself to lie to you—”
“But do you want to know something?”
“...Sorry?”
“Do you realize that being deceived in that way feels a lot worse than being told an outright lie?”
“Ah...” That was a good point, not that there wasn’t a way to counter it. I started off with an apology and decided to offer him an explanation. “...I’m sorry. I have a problem.”
“...A problem?”
“Yes. Living in this world, I’ve been forced to deceive others against my will. I know I really shouldn’t live like this, but...”
I wasn’t going to take the full blame here. If my environment made me like this, the one who pushed me into the said environment was this old man.

“Haha...” Suddenly called out and assigned partial blame, Auril laughed incredulously. Luckily, though, his eyes were smiling as well as his mouth this time. It seemed he was rather amused by how bold I was being.
Okay, now that things have gotten less tense...
“Anyway, did you come here because of me?”
“That’s right.”
“Hmm, it doesn’t feel that great to have a background check done on you...” I trailed off and eyed him, making sure to make my discomfort known.
Auril cleared his throat. “Ahem, but if I didn’t do that, I wouldn’t have been able to meet you.”
“What? Ah... Right. Why did the community suddenly close? I thought you might have banned me.”
“Ah, there was a reason for that.”
“Reason?”
“Let’s just say there was some royal intervention. But the space has been recovered now to some extent.”
“Oh, then will I be able to see you there starting next month?”
“No. I recently transferred ownership to a friend. I’ll be difficult to reach from now on.”
“By friend... are you talking about the GM?”
“That will probably be the case.”
Curiosity piqued, I asked who the GM was, but Auril did not answer. Rather than it being top-secret information, it seemed more like he was sulking and didn’t want to tell me.
“Well, there is no particular reason to keep it a secret... But try and figure it out on your own.”
“Sorry?”
“If you only see me as someone you have a transactional relationship with, I have no choice but to treat you the same.”
“Ah, right...”
Jeez, a man over three hundred years old is going to pout over something like this? It’s your fault for getting tricked while holding a lie detector.
“So, how long are you going to keep speaking that way?”
“Sorry?”
“You didn’t talk to me like that there. You sound like a different person here. It’s quite strange.”
“Haha. That was just an act.”
“Act?”
“Yes, another character. Let’s call it an attempt by the weak to not be looked down on. There’s no way I would be rude to you in real life unless I’ve lost my mind.”

“Hmm, I guess I can see what you’re trying to say.” Auril quietly nodded and didn’t say much more for a while, a moment of silence settling between us. It was some time before his mouth opened again. “Anyway, I came to find you because I wanted to give our relationship a fresh start.” He sounded like someone who wasn’t over their ex-boyfriend.
“...I’m sorry?” I wasn’t able to hide how baffled I was.

The old man quickly offered an explanation. “I want to be on friendly terms with you. It is clear we can be helpful to each other, but continuing to go around in circles will be frustrating for both of us.”
“That’s why I even prepared a gift for you.”
“A gift...” I subconsciously flinched at that word. While I was excited by the prospect, I was also worried. I couldn’t figure out his angle.
“Don’t be nervous. It’s nothing bad.”
“Could you give me more information?”
“As you know, I want you to open the Gate of the Abyss. In that sense, I called it a gift, but it is also something that benefits me.”
Ugh, what’s with the lengthy explanation?
“I see. So?”

“It is an ability that will be of great help to you when it comes to keeping your identity hidden in the future,” Auril then gave me a summary of the gift. In short, he was going to use his power and expertise to grant me a buff.
“So, if I accept this, I won’t be affected by spells like Verification or other interrogation-type items like Misplaced Trust?”
“Exactly. It only applies a protective shield to the body, though, so it won’t be effective on the mind when it’s in a pure state.”
“A pure state?”
“Like it is in the place you are sent to every month, for example.”
Ah, so it doesn’t work in the spirit world. Then telling straight-up lies at the Round Table won’t be possible, I guess.
“How is it, my gift?”
I thought it over for a brief moment. First, there was no doubt it was a very helpful ability. He said it himself: with this power, I wouldn’t be at the mercy of things like Misplaced Trust anymore.
But when you look at it objectively, it seems like he could be secretly scheming behind my back.
I didn’t know much about magic. If Auril planted a tracking device on the gift, I would have no way of finding and removing it.
The problem is, I can’t refuse it.
This was the old man who sent the Knight of Light to his grave with a single wave of his hand. Put simply, if he intended to harm me, he could make it happen—even by force.
“All right. Are you going to give it to me right now?”
“Well... I actually already did it. The moment I found you again here in the sewer.”
“What? But I didn’t feel anything of the sort.”
“Because that’s my specialty.”
Ah, I see. I already knew I had no choice, but it feels like I’ve been violated.
No wonder he had been speaking in the past tense ever since earlier.
Once talk of the gift concluded, Auril decided to be blunt. “I’m saying this just in case, but I have no intention of forcefully controlling you.”
That was good news. Although I couldn’t be sure how long that promise would hold, it was better than being strangled with magic and threatened right now. “That is very like you, sir. Much respect.”
“Haha...” Despite my flattery and the old man’s humble laugh, we both knew this was all crap. However, sometimes charades like this were considered good manners in social settings.
I laughed cheerfully as I gathered my thoughts. From here, I had two options. The first was to somehow get rid of Auril and go rescue Amelia.
“Haha, it was nice to see you. You said you wouldn’t use force against me, right? Then I’m actually busy right now, so I have to go... Stay healthy!”

The second option, exploitation of the elderly—get help from Auril directly. It didn’t take long to make a decision. After all, I tried to avoid him once but I’d ended up running into him again like this. It would be impossible to stealthily get rid of him. Even if I chose the first option, this stalker-like old man was sure to follow me.
If this old timer puts his mind to it, the iron mask covering my face could ‘fall’ right off... And at that point, figuring out my name will be a piece of cake for him.
If I was going to end up giving it to him anyway, I figured I should at least get something in return.
Might as well milk him dry.
Making my decision, I cautiously opened my mouth. “Um... sir.”
“Ah, speak.”
“Can I ask you a favor? If you grant this for me, I will reveal my name and face to you.”
“Name and face...?”
“Yes, haven’t you been curious?”
“That is true...”
“So why don’t you do this one job with me?”
Auril did not respond to my suggestion. He just stared at me with a look in his eyes that seemed to ask, What is this bastard trying to pull this time?
Meanwhile, Amelia was running through the sewer with the sisters when she abruptly stopped in her tracks.
“W-Why are you suddenly stopping...?”
There were no presences nearby. However, one of her skills, which she had been keeping active since earlier, had shut off out of nowhere.
“He’s here.”
In other words, Ricardo Lüchenprague, the Traitor, was nearby.
So this is how it’s going to go... In that case, what happened to Yandel?
That was the first thought that popped into her head, but Amelia shook off her concerns. She said she would trust him. That wasn’t what she needed to worry about right now.
Laura flinched at Amelia’s words. “By him, you mean...” In response to an earlier question about her severed arm, she had told the sisters that Ricardo Lüchenprague was chasing her.
“Yes, him.”
When Amelia confirmed it, the two girls began to tremble. They could still remember the sight of him cutting down hundreds of adventurers a few hours ago.
“Amelia, Laura.”
“Y-Yes!”
“Listen carefully. We’re almost there now.” Keeping her explanation as short and concise as possible, Amelia gave them directions to the city. “Go. I’ll do my best to stop him.”
The sisters had two conflicting reactions to that. “Why are you helping us like this...?” Her younger self was at a loss. She also seemed worried about leaving Amelia alone.
However, her sister Laura was different. “Amelia, come quickly.”
“B-But—”

“Hurry!” Though there seemed to be a mix of both suspicion and gratitude on her face, she cool-headedly led her younger sister down the passage Amelia told them about. Laura had something more important to worry about than her own feelings.
Amelia watched the two sisters run away holding hands. Without even needing to close her eyes, she could vividly remember the end of that dark passageway, and what she experienced there.
Could she really change the future? She couldn’t be sure yet.

“They seem to be precious to you,” a deep male voice said softly. “Good.” When she turned around, Ricardo Lüchenprague was there smirking at her. “That means I’ll be able to show you what loss feels like.”
Amelia gripped the dagger in her hand tighter.

chapters.title: Chapter 328: Ouroboros (3)
paragraphs: Some would think her foolish. Everyone died someday, and everyone experienced loss at least once in their life. It was an all-too-common tragedy. Some would probably be surprised that this cold-blooded woman would willingly walk toward certain destruction just because she had been unable to deal with the death of a family member. Some would consider her weak because, for twenty years, she hadn’t been able to get over something everyone else could. Amelia thought the same.
Stab!
Nevertheless, her sister would have brushed her hair—Amelia being younger and requiring more care—and said: “It must have been very hard for you.”

Not bothering with pity, not even bothering to reprimand her for doing such a thing, her sister would have hugged her tight and told her she did a good job. Even if everyone in the world considered her terrifying, even if they pointed fingers and called her a cold-hearted woman, to Laura, she would always just be her crybaby younger sister. She had been the only person in the world to ever treat her that way.
Yes, she definitely would have...
“Sorry...”
“Who are you apologizing to?”
Amelia closed her eyes, ignoring the pain radiating from her abdomen. “Laura...”

In the end, she’d achieved nothing. Although she had spent the past twenty years getting stronger in preparation for this day, it hadn’t been enough to defeat this man. Even though she’d tried to speak to him to clear up the misunderstanding, tried to explain that she was not a part of the Order of the Rose, the man would not listen. In the end, a battle broke out, and she desperately bought time for her sister to escape. But that was over now.

“What, are you seeing a hallucination?” The man sneered and twisted the sword. A burning pain radiated from her injury. “Did you think I’d let them escape?” The excruciating sensation brought her back to reality. “You need to see what I had to go through.”
The sword slid out and Amelia collapsed to the ground, at which point the man began to drag her along by her hair. The events that were about to unfold were very clear to her.
“That way I can show you what loss feels like.”
This man was going to slay her sister right before her eyes, just like he did that fateful day.
Splash!
With every step he took, her heart dropped more and more. Her consciousness faded and each time she opened her eyes, the scenery around her was different.
“As I expected, they didn’t get far,” the man muttered.
“L-Laura...”
“You go first! I’ll take care—!”
The same conversation had happened that day as well.
“Amelia...!”
The sword was aimed at her younger self.
Stab!
Her older sister hugged her.
“Laura...!”
The man’s sword ran through her sister’s chest, just like it did back then.
In the end, I changed nothing...

That was when Amelia realized that this was what twenty years of hope had gotten her. The happily ever after these two girls sought only existed in fairy tales. In reality, all that was left was a weak, foolish human woman.
“That’s a nice look.”
Stab!
The man pulled out the sword embedded in her sister’s body. At that moment, her consciousness faded and the scenery changed again. The dark sewer reeked of blood.
Kwaaang!
A roar filled the passage, and she felt a warmth on her cold skin.
“Jeez, why are you crying? It’s not even over yet.”
Not over yet? What could that possibly mean? She couldn’t figure it out.

“You did a good job. Now leave it to me and get some rest.” At those words, the tension in her body disappeared and her eyes fluttered shut on their own. “When you wake up, it will all be over.” That was the last bit of awareness her consciousness allowed her.
As Amelia lost consciousness, I shouted, “What are you doing?! Take your sister and run!”
The shout was directed at Amelia Fetus—Amelia F for short.
“A-ah—!” Amelia F seemed momentarily confused by my instructions, but she quickly draped her sister over her small shoulders and started running.
Whew, then I can leave the rest to the old man...
I shifted my gaze.
“You...!” Lüchenprague, clearly stunned, looked around. It seemed he was trying to check if the Knight of Light was with me.
What a comedian.
“If you were going to run, then just run. What did you come all the way here for?”
He did not answer my question—he simply avoided my eyes, a strange look on his face.
A thought suddenly popped into my head, and I decided to ask just in case, even though I was sure it couldn’t possibly be true. “You... did you end up here while trying to find your way out?”
His response was brief. “...Destiny led me here.”
“Ha, destiny, my ass.”
I laughed at how ridiculous that was, but come to think of it, I realized destiny wasn’t that far off. If things went a certain way no matter how hard you fought, how was that not destiny?
As I was thinking that, the guy asked me a question of his own. “Anyway... did you come alone?”

“Yes.” The Knight of Light and I weren’t even comrades to begin with, so I confirmed it—I didn’t see a point in hiding it anyway. “Hey, let me ask you one more question. Why are you so obsessed with this woman?”
“...You don’t need to know.”

“Rude,” I said and slid my eyes over to check on Amelia. Her injury was visibly recovering at a rapid rate thanks to the fact that I tore one more Bind scroll before intervening. Put simply, as the three of us were now bound together, Amelia was no longer affected by Nullification, either.
This would have been easier if she was fully awake.
That was a bit of a letdown, but what could you do? If it was for the right to recruit a clanmate (SSR), this was nothing.
“Move. If you give up that woman, you—”
“What are you saying, you one-trick pony?” I beckoned with a finger. “Shut up and fight me.”
This would be the last battle of my time travel journey.
Huff, huff...
The girl running down the sewer huffed out hot breaths. Her overheated muscles showed no signs of cooling, and even more heat radiated from her wet back.
“L-Laura... a-are you okay...?” Even as she ran with all her might, to the point that she couldn’t even breathe properly, Amelia continued to talk to Laura on her back.
There was no answer. However, Amelia ignored the spike of fear she felt and kept moving. But it seemed she had hit her physical limit while carrying Laura on her back.

“Ugh...!” Amelia was running at a gallop when she lost her balance and fell. Her foot hadn’t caught on anything—her legs had simply given out. “L-Laura! Are you okay? Huh?” Before worrying about her twisted ankle, Amelia checked on Laura, concerned the injury had been made worse by the fall.
The shock seemed to have woken her sister up. A small voice escaped Laura’s mouth. “Amelia...”
“L-Laura! I-It’s okay! We’re not far now. Don’t speak and—”

“Your own...” The weak voice petered out before it could reach the end of the sentence, but Amelia knew what would come next. Laura was probably telling her to leave her behind and keep going. If she had the energy, she would surely have added all kinds of reasons, pointing out she was already done for and that it would make more sense for Amelia to go on her own.

“Sorry, I don’t know what you’re saying.” Amelia pretended not to understand and propped Laura’s limp body up as there was no way she had enough strength to do so on her own. Laura, who was six inches taller than her, felt particularly small in that moment. And maybe it was just her imagination, but Laura also felt lighter than before.
“Blood...”

It was because of the blood that she had lost. As the life that once filled Laura’s body escaped, she became that much lighter. Amelia leaned her sister’s body against the wall and tore off her clothes to apply pressure to the wound. Then she poured out all the potions she had on her. She hadn’t had the presence of mind to do it earlier, too overwhelmed by the sole thought that she had to get out of there, but she should have done it ages ago.
Why am I such a moron?
She felt ashamed. Her ever-calm sister would have been able to do exactly what needed to be done even in a situation like this.
“Ugh...!” As her wound began to heal from the potion, Laura writhed in pain. Thick veins protruded from her neck and forehead.
“L-Laura! Please hold on...” Amelia lifted Laura’s body again. But just as she was about to stand up, the passage shook with a loud rumble.
Kwaaaang! Crumble.
The ceiling above them collapsed and rocks poured down. At that moment, Amelia’s body lurched forward. Someone had pushed her from behind.
Boom!
Clear of the debris, Amelia hurriedly whirled around, and there was Laura. The sight of her beloved sister’s lower body crushed under a giant rock didn’t seem real.
“Amelia...”
“L-Laura...” Amelia reached out to her like a girl possessed. When she did, Laura swatted her hand away. “W-What are you doing?!”
As Amelia cried out, Laura’s eyes feebly shifted toward her. “I once... resented you...”
“I-I know. E-Even someone like you would have felt that way. But stop being stubborn and—”
“Listen!” At Laura’s shout, Amelia bit her lip. Her voice was wheezy and it couldn’t even be called a shout, but Amelia was rendered mute by the overpowering command it carried.
Tap.
Laura placed her hand on Amelia’s cheek and, unlike before, spoke in a soft tone. “You... wished. You always... wished for this...”
At those words, something flowed down Amelia’s cheeks. She couldn’t tell if it was sweat or tears, but she knew one thing for certain.
Thump!
Amelia’s heart began to race like it was broken. Perhaps even if her mind tried to deny it, her heart knew what was happening here.

“W-Why... are you talking like that?” Laura’s words were missing one key thing—herself. She was speaking like this moment was her last. “L-Laura... don’t give up. You took a potion, right? We just have to go a little farther... D-Don’t worry about the rock. I-I’ll clear it soon. I-I’ll make sure to do it... Huh?”

At Amelia’s plea, Laura pursed her lips with a pained expression on her face. Of course, it lasted only for a short moment. “Forget... all the painful memories here. A normal life... this is the start for you.” Laura forced her twitching jaw muscles up to give her a bright smile.
From there, it all happened in an instant.
Tap.
Laura reached out, pulled out the dagger strapped to Amelia’s waist, and inserted it into her own neck.
Stab!
“N-No...!” Amelia hurriedly pulled out the dagger. Pouring the remaining potion onto the wound, she pressed down on it with both hands in an attempt to somehow stop the bleeding. “N-No. No, no...”
It wasn’t enough. The blood choking Laura stopped.
Chhhhhh.
The same was true for the blood that had been sizzling in reaction to the potion. The warmth flowing through her fingertips disappeared. The blood was sticky, but no longer hot.
“Ahh... A-Ahh...”
Amelia realized at that moment that her sister was no longer there.
“Ahhh!” Amelia let out a terrible, gut-wrenching scream and hugged Laura’s upper body to her chest. Right at that moment, the ceiling began to collapse once again, dropping an avalanche of rocks.
Dddddd!
Amelia saw it coming but did not avoid it. She intended to stay with Laura like this until the end. However, this cruel world wouldn’t even allow her that.
“...Ugh!” Her body flew back as if someone had yanked her by the back of her neck.
Boom!
The back of her head must have hit the wall because Amelia’s vision blurred. As her consciousness drifted further and further away, Amelia stared at her sister, still buried in the rubble.
Step.
She heard a footstep nearby and reflexively turned toward the source of the sound. An old man was walking toward them.

At Amelia’s murmur, the old man looked at her impassively. When she took a closer look, however, she noticed that he seemed to be worried about something. After a moment of silence, he sighed, then opened his mouth. “Whew, so many requests. Auril Gavis. That is this old man’s name.”

chapters.title: Chapter 329: Ouroboros (4)
paragraphs: My battle with the Traitor, Ricardo Lüchenprague, shocked me in many ways. After all, this was my first time realizing that weapons proficiency—as opposed to specs such as a precious essence, high-stat skill, or an aura—could have such a big impact in battle.
Whip!

Even his sword, which seemed almost like he was swinging it willy-nilly, seemed to have a hidden purpose and flowed naturally from one move to the next. This went beyond just being a good fighter. Of course, that was not to say things were hopeless.
I don’t need to beat him, anyway.
As long as I could buy time, this would be my win. With that thought in mind, I studied my opponent’s swordsmanship closely.
I think I can see it a little now.
At first, I may have had to rely on my senses and reflexes to dodge his sword at the last second each time, but as time went by, I started to see how each move led into the next.
Whip!
When he aimed for the wrist, it was because he wanted to keep me in check.
It would be best to dodge backward, but that’s probably what he’s aiming for. Because that leaves my throat vulnerable.
In any other situation, that would be checkmate. Assuming Nullification was working as usual, at least.
Slide.
When Giantization deactivated, my body shrank and my opponent’s sword grazed my wrist. But did he anticipate that too?
Whip!
The bastard twisted his sword like a snake to aim for my thigh.
Dash.

I quickly retreated, but it seemed this guy noticed even as he was swinging his sword because he altered the trajectory once again without a moment’s hesitation. This time, the blade flew toward Amelia, who was unconscious.
Motherfucker...
I quickly followed up Transcendence with Eye of the Storm and dragged him back in front of me. With this, Amelia was safe.
Shaaaaaa!
As if he’d considered even this scenario, the bastard expertly swung his sword as he was being dragged in by the wind. I managed to somehow dodge it, but...
Is this asshole’s brain some sort of supercomputer?

The longer this went on, the more I felt like I was being toyed with. It felt like he was seeing through all my moves. I was starting to understand how modern Go players felt playing against machines.
If I can figure out how he’s doing it, that would be a big help.

Although this wasn’t a level of martial arts I could learn just by watching, since it was rare to participate in a life-or-death battle with such a highly skilled swordsman, I stalled for time with the goal of learning as much as possible.
I think things on the old man’s end should be wrapping up now...

A long while later, just as that thought was running through my mind, a moan escaped Amelia’s mouth. “Ugh...” She hadn’t yet regained consciousness, but that was a sign that her injuries had recovered to a certain extent.
Okay, once Amelia wakes up, we can beat him up two on one.

That was probably why the bastard targeted Amelia whenever he got the chance even in the middle of our fight. Unlike the Knight of Light’s honorable swordsmanship, this guy didn’t have a single drop of pride as a warrior. If the situation took a turn for the worst, he would bounce without even looking back, no hesitation.
Yeah, just like right now. “...I won’t forget this day.”
It seemed he figured that if he was going to run away anyway, it was best to do it now before Amelia woke up.
Dash.

My opponent reeled off a cliche line about future revenge before stepping back and putting distance between us. I didn’t follow. Although I didn’t show it, I was almost out of MP. In order not to be overpowered in terms of strength, I had been using Swing each time I blocked the sword and had fired off Transcendence, Leap, and Eye of the Storm throughout the battle.
Hmm, then that finishes that...
I went up to Amelia. Her breathing was quite steady, though her severed hand would probably need some more time.
“Haha.” Just then, I heard a sound behind me. When I hurriedly turned around, Auril Gavis stood there, watching me with pride. “You really defeated that man by yourself.”
“If you had helped me, it would have been much easier, sir.”
“I didn’t want to face that man yet, you see.”
“I see...”

It was clear he wasn’t going to tell me the reason, so I broke eye contact. To Auril’s left, there was an object floating in the air thanks to his telekinesis. No, I shouldn’t say object—a person. It was an unconscious Amelia F. Seeing as she was here, it seemed things had gone off without a hitch.
But I should still check.
I shifted my gaze to Auril again. “So... how did it go on your end?”
“It went well. Like you asked, I made sure to tell her my name at the end as well.”
“And Laura?”
“Hmm, you seem to be getting shorter and shorter with me...”
“Haha, how could that be? You’re mistaken. Mistaken.”

The old man looked at me suspiciously for a brief moment but laughed it off like he didn’t really care. “Anyway, the same goes for this child’s sister. As you asked, I gave her medicine, treated her, and sent her to the overworld.”

This old man sure was good at getting things done. Apparently, he threw her into the first carriage he saw in the overworld, crashed it, and made it look like an accident. That would serve as an excuse for her losing all her memories. He also left behind the ID of someone with zero connections and a similar age.
“I believe I have a sense as to what it is that you want. You’re not thinking of doing anything foolish, are you? Haha.”
“Of course not.” There shouldn’t be any problems on the sister’s end now, so I checked on the other item on our list. “But what happened to the younger sister?”

“Don’t worry. Didn’t I tell you? Discreet magic is this old man’s specialty. This child will never in her life realize she was hallucinating. Aside from the fact that her sister stopped breathing, everything else actually happened.”

Laura getting crushed by a rock and driving a dagger into her own throat were all real things that happened. It was just the sensation of her heart stopping and the potion no longer bubbling that had been illusions.
“But let me ask this. Did you really have to reveal this old man’s name?”
“She said that was what you said in her memory.” We had to stick to the script to avoid contradictions.

“Hmm, that is true. Anyway, you have a good head on your shoulders. To think you came up with such an ingenious idea.” The old man looked at me, impressed, but I actually had a bitter taste in my mouth. When you actually thought about it, you’d be hard-pressed to find a production as over-the-top as this. I really did feel like an actor on stage following a script.
It’s too inefficient.

Even after everything was over, I still couldn’t accept it. If it were just me, I wouldn’t have done all this. There would have been no need to pretend Laura was dead, no reason to take Amelia to Noark. I could have just ended it all by sending her and her sister to the overworld together. Everyone could have had a happy ending. Yet I had chosen this convoluted plan that required one girl to live in grief for twenty years. Because I had met Auril Gavis after returning to the past, I realized there was no way to undo what had already happened. Since the result was fixed, I put the rest of the pieces together any way I could. In some ways, what I had done was no better than hypocrisy.

Worrying about whether the chicken or the egg came first was pointless to start with. What did it matter? Whichever one came first, the egg laid by the chicken would eventually go through the process of becoming a chicken anyway.
“You don’t seem very pleased.”
At Auril’s statement, I decided to honestly share my thoughts with him. Although it was a long story, he listened intently before patting me on my forearm.
“It’s not that I don’t understand how you feel, but don’t think too deeply about it. You must have gained many things over the course of this journey as well.”

It wasn’t a particularly comforting consolation. Still, there was definitely a lot gained: information that could only be learned in the past, the buff Auril Gavis had placed on me, the double-digit Numbers Item Kraul’s Demon Grinder, and a ticket to recruiting Amelia (SSR).
“The reason the world lived on, the country lived on, and society lived on was because everyone did their part here. Just consider this yours.”
Hearing that made me feel even more uncomfortable. Just what was the Fragment of Records Stone? I wanted to ask for more details, but I didn’t have the luxury to do so right now.
“Anyway, if we’re all done here, I’d like to get what I was promised—”
As Auril tried to subtly change the subject, I decisively interrupted. “It’s not over yet.”
“Hmm?”
“Give her to me.”
There was one last thing to do.
When Amelia came to her senses, she was traveling through the sewer on someone’s back. Even through the haze shrouding her mind, she wondered who it could be.
“Looks like you finally came to.”

That voice woke her up completely. No wonder her arms were sore from his large, metal back. “Mr. Iron Mask...?” It was Iron Mask, the person who, unlike the other clan members, had always been generous and kind to the sisters.
Ms. Emily’s comrade.
Although she didn’t know the reason why, Emily had looked out for the sisters all day. Amelia wasn’t oblivious enough to not see that.
Why are these people helping us?
Amelia had no way of knowing, but one thing was for sure. If it weren’t for their dedication, she and her sister would have already...
Already...?
When her thoughts snagged on that word, the memories came rushing back to her. “L-Laura! W-What happened to Laura? She w-would have been next to me... Did you not see her?”
“...You were the only one I saw in the rubble.”
“Ah...” Amelia clenched her fists unthinkingly. “A-Ah...”

She felt lightheaded. Iron Mask was explaining the situation, but his voice sounded far away. “We’re on our way back to Noark. The path leading aboveground has collapsed—what, did you fall asleep?” The deep, male voice swam through her fading consciousness. “...Sorry for not saving her. See you later.”
That was the last thing she remembered.
Time passed and when she opened her eyes again, Amelia was in an eerie cemetery. “This place is...” She could see Noark’s castle in the distance and smelled an acrid scent.
There was no one around. Not Iron Mask, not Emily, and not her precious sister.
Slide.
Amelia pulled out her dagger as if she were possessed. It was covered in thick blood.

“L-Laura...” As she stared at the blood on the dagger, she was forced to accept that the events that transpired today were not a dream. “A-Ah...” Amelia collapsed to the ground and stayed there for a long while before there was a loud commotion.
“Here! There’s someone here!”
“Who is this kid?”
“Looks like Felic Barker’s herder?”
“Let’s take her for now, she might know something.”

It was as she was being led into the city by the guards that Amelia realized she was completely alone. Her sister, her protector, was no longer there. From now on, she would have to survive in this city alone.
As I watched Amelia get dragged away by the guards, I heard a sound behind me. “The sight of her like that leaves me with a heavy heart. I feel like I’ve done something wrong.”
What, you want to cosplay as a benevolent grandfather now? You don’t even actually feel that way.
“Why are you alone? Where is my comrade?”
“That woman is still back there.”
“You left an unconscious woman—”
“Don’t worry, she would have woken up as soon as this old man left.”
Hmm, if you say so.
I shook off my concern. Whatever happened, Amelia was a woman who could protect herself. I had just one question. “Then why didn’t you come with her?”
Auril looked at me like that was obvious. “You and I have something to talk about.”
Ah, that... I can’t go back on my word now.

It was basically a natural law that people felt different when they entered the bathroom versus when they left it. So even though I’d made up my mind to make a necessary sacrifice, when it actually came time to do so, I had trouble opening my mouth.

“Are you not going to keep your promise?” Auril’s voice was gentle but there was a strange, oppressive weight to his words. When I subtly averted my eyes, the old man took a step closer, his eyes glinting. “Tell me your name. Or you can take off that mask first. Hmm, yes... it would be best to see that face of yours first.” The sight of his breath steaming out of his nose was truly terrifying.
“W-Wait!” I quickly raised my hand and stopped Auril. Then I put my hand into my sub-space.
As I did, he asked, “Why are you rummaging through your sub-space?”
Because there’s something I want to try.
“The Fragment of Records Stone?” He tilted his head when he saw the item I pulled out of the ring. “Why did you pull that out?”
Why do you think? Because it’s the last trick I have up my sleeve.
The lord of the castle had said it himself.
“I-I heard you leave the same way you come. That after you complete all your work here, the stone will call you forth again...”

The way to return to my original time was to finish all my work. I figured the only work I had left was rescuing Laura, and that job was now done. Put simply, I could flee into the future without paying his wages. At least, that should have been the case.
Why isn’t this working?
The Fragment of Records Stone did not so much as twitch. And I supposed my disappointment was obvious.

“...Haha, so. That’s what you were after.” The old man seemed to have figured out my intentions because he glared at me. “I wasn’t lying when I said I want to be on friendly terms with you. That’s why I granted all of your cumbersome requests... But to think you were planning to stab me in the back in the end.”
“This is... a misunderstanding. If we calm down and discuss this—”
“It’s fine. I now know exactly how to deal with you.”
God damn it.
When I subconsciously backed away, Auril waved his hand in the air.
Whoom!
Like someone had turned on Eye of the Storm, my body was dragged forward by a physical force. When I came to my senses, I found myself standing in front of him.
“Now, shall we have a look at that face?” Auril reached a hand toward my helmet.
Ha, if I knew this was going to happen, I would have taken it off myself.
I belatedly regretted this, but it was already too late to turn back.
Tap.

Still, as the saying went, there was light at the end of every tunnel. The moment Auril’s finger touched my helmet, the Fragment of Records Stone in my hand suddenly began to emit white light in all directions.
Shaaaaaa!
Yeah, that’s what I call exploitation of the elderly.
As my world turned white, I smiled. “Sorry about that. I wanted to keep my promise.”
“You—!”
“Please don’t shout. What’s the use? My work here is complete.”
“Name! Hurry and tell me your name at least—”
Flash!
A flash of light burst in front of my eyes, cutting off Auril’s voice.
Tap.
The light dissipated and my feet, which were floating slightly, touched the ground. It was a close call, but it seemed my plan to exploit the unpaid elderly had been a success.
“Uh...” But how did this happen? “Uh...?”

As I went to take in my surroundings, I froze in a daze. Everything was the same—the destroyed graveyard, the dead cemetery guard, and even the smell of smoke blowing from the burned-down city. If I were back in my original time, there should have at least been some changes, but everything around me looked the same.
“What the— Where did that old timer go?”
Auril Gavis was the only one gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 330: Ouroboros (5)
paragraphs: As the static buzzing in the back of my mind started to spread throughout my entire body, I blinked back to awareness at the sound of something falling.
Tap.

When I checked, it was the Fragment of Records Stone. I was sure I had been clutching it tightly in my fist even when light was bursting from it, so how did it fall? I quickly walked over and picked it up. That was when I noticed there was something else on the floor.
“Clothes...?”

The robe was made of a high-quality fabric. The important thing wasn’t the material but the owner, though. It wasn’t just a high-quality robe—it was the robe Auril Gavis had been wearing, now on the floor in the exact spot where the old man had been standing just a moment ago. It was as if his body had been sucked somewhere, leaving this behind.
“Don’t tell me...” I looked down at the Fragment of Records Stone in my hand. “This activated for the old man?”
I was starting to understand what had happened, although I was momentarily dazed by the unexpected twist. The Fragment of Records Stone had reacted to Auril, not me.
Ugh, I can’t wrap my head around it.
I forced myself to focus and started running through this from the beginning. There were two possibilities. First, Auril had received a ‘call of the times,’ just like I had.
“Have you used the Fragment of Records Stone before?”
“I have used it before.”

Second, Auril had already used the Fragment of Records Stone. Which meant the old man had been living in this era after answering the call, just like me. That was how he met me, and once the work he needed to do—the role he needed to fulfill—was completed, he returned to his original time.
If it’s the former, that means he was sent to the past. And I guess the latter would mean the opposite.
That was how the puzzle pieces in my head started to come together.
No, it’s still too early to jump to conclusions.

Then I realized just how much information I was lacking and changed my mind. I didn’t know enough about the Fragment of Records Stone to make any inferences. It was wise to keep all possibilities open. It was possible that the call of the times wasn’t always a call to the past—it could also be a call from the future.
I should think about that later.
I put the Fragment of Records Stone back into my sub-space and picked up the robe from the ground. Then I rummaged around excitedly.
Looting!
After all, this was a rare drop item from Auril Gavis. Chances were that he carried around something interesting.
Are you joking?
As a result of my enthusiastic rummaging, I found nothing much besides the robe. Just ordinary socks, shoes, and luxurious panties made of pure white silk.
“Ahh, fuck!” Realizing the piece of cloth I was touching was underwear, I hurled it on the ground. Annoyance overtook me.
What kind of old man has nothing?
I had been getting my hopes up because this man gave off the air of a final boss. What a massive bust.

“Ah.” Belatedly, I remembered seeing Auril take water out of his sub-space. At the time, I figured it was a sub-space ring. “But I guess it was a subordinate sub-space.” A subordinate sub-space could only be used by top-tier wizards. In such cases, there was no physical object; it was directly connected to the user’s soul by a tattoo or something like that.
Uh, no, wait a minute...

Then if I used a subordinate sub-space, would that mean I could take all of the equipment I collected here back to my time? The thought suddenly occurred to me but it was nothing to shout Eureka! over. I wasn’t a wizard. Unlike a magical device, a subordinate sub-space could only be opened by the wizard’s unique mana.
Ha, then it’s another bust...
I sighed and let go of any regrets. Getting angry and venting my disappointment would change nothing. I had something else I had to do right now.
First, I should meet up with Amelia.

I picked up Auril’s belongings and put them in sub-space before walking through the sewer again. It was clearly ordinary clothing, but since I might have missed something, I figured I could check one more time later.
Splash, splash.
As I retraced my steps, I came across five or six corpses.
This is where the infighting broke out.

Since I had the common sense to take unclaimed equipment with me, everything was looted. I guessed because these people were trying to migrate to the overworld, they were all carrying expandable bags or sub-space rings, so inventory was a non-issue.
Wow, how much is all this?

Using my shoulders, neck, arms, and everything, I carried all the bags and continued moving. Before long, I arrived at the location I left Amelia and found she wasn’t there. Judging by the traces of the battle with the head of Orcules, this was definitely where she passed out. Where did she go while I was gone? There was no need to think for long.
She must be there...
Unable to ignore the acid in the back of my throat, I quickened my pace.
A collapsed ceiling blocked more than half the passageway. I could see Amelia clearing away the debris. She was clawing at it so frantically that she didn’t even seem to notice I was there.
“Aaaah!”
What the—why are you screaming all of a sudden? It’s scary.
The sight of her grasping her head was brutal so I quickly walked over and grabbed her wrist.
Tap.
The moment my skin touched hers, Amelia shuddered and turned around. “...Yandel?” She seemed surprised to see my face, then tried to shake off my hand. “Let go. I need to find—”
“Even if you look, you won’t find anything.”
“What?”

I grinned. “That’s why I told you. It’ll all be over when you wake up.” Despite those words, Amelia still stared up at me with a blank expression on her face. It seemed she wasn’t picking up on what I meant. “Just follow me.” It would be easier to let her see it with her own eyes.
When she came to, Amelia was filled only with despair. She was alone in the dark sewer and the familiar silence told her that everything was over.
Yeah, it’s all over...
Amelia got up and started to trudge. There was somewhere she had to go, something she hadn’t been able to do that day.
“Forget... all the painful memories here. A normal life... this is the start for you.”

She had had to leave her sister’s body behind. When she came to look for her sometime later, Laura’s body was already gone. Apparently, the workers restoring the passage cleared away all the corpses. This became a source of painful regret for her.
“I have to find it.”

She had to find her, even if she may just have been a corpse. She had to retrieve it, not leave her sister’s body in this dirty sewer. Now that she’d traveled twenty years into the past, she could at least do that much. No, perhaps that was the only thing fate had been willing to allow her from the very beginning.
“Ugh, heugh...!”

Soon reaching the site of the tragedy, Amelia started to clear out all the rocks she could find. She was so desperate as she did so that she looked almost deranged, and that wasn’t all that inaccurate a description, either.
Her sister was nowhere to be seen. She had to be in here somewhere.
Could it be that I’m not even allowed this?

“Aaaah!” For the first time in a long time, Amelia let out a scream. Even when her flesh was cut and her bones were broken into pieces, she could swallow back her groans, but she couldn’t this time. It felt like her heart was being torn apart.
Tap.
At that moment, she felt the warmth of another person. “...Yandel?” It was a person she had seen every day for the past six months, someone all too familiar to her. “Let go. I need to find—”
She immediately tried to shake him off, but the barbarian refused to let go, as always. After saying something incomprehensible to her as she resisted, he forced her to stand.
“This place is...”
They walked for ages to reach the overworld—the giant city of Rafdonia, a place where the palace’s influence reached every corner.

“Ugh, my eyes...” Midday in the city was too bright for eyes that had just emerged from a dark sewer. But before her eyes had time to adjust, the barbarian dragged her forward by the wrist. “W-Where are we going?”
“I told you you’ll see when you get there.”

Amelia scanned her surroundings even as she was being dragged along by force. Pedestrians were passing by on the street, smiling children and parents, merchants touting their wares, and pure white marble buildings reflecting the sunlight. It was a place she had once longed for desperately, a world filled with warm sunlight where she could live a normal life, unlike Noark. Of course, she knew now that even the overworld was not a paradise, that it was a place where beasts even worse than those who roamed Noark lived, and where mundane tragedies occurred every day.
“Just once...” Nevertheless, she had wanted to see it just once, her sister and herself living a normal life, at times crying and at times laughing.
“Huh? What did you—”
“Yandel, go on your own from here. I have something to find below—”
“Ugh, I told you, you won’t find her.” When Amelia stopped walking, the barbarian looked at her with frustration and said, “She’s alive, your sister.”
“...What?”
Alive? But how...?
“I’ll... explain that later, so just follow me, okay?”
The barbarian tugged the confused woman along and continued walking. Amelia did not resist. She didn’t have the presence of mind to do so.
“Whew, it took a while because he never mentioned which first-aid station it was.”
After who knew how long, Amelia arrived at a first-aid station located in the overworld. Then, after explaining why she was there to a staff member, she found the hospital room.
Drag.
When she opened the door, the figure of a girl lying in bed entered her line of sight. Warm sunlight was shining through the window.

“L-Laura...” It was an unbelievable sight, the kind she never thought she would get to see in her life. Amelia approached the bed like a possessed woman. Then she grabbed Laura’s hand. She could feel her sister’s heartbeat through the place where their skin met. “How did this happen?”

In response to Amelia’s question, the barbarian told her everything that happened so far. He had made a deal with Auril Gavis. In order to eliminate potential paradoxes, the Blessing of Lethe was used to erase Laura’s memories, and then they staged a carriage accident to explain her amnesia.
“When she wakes up, your sister will probably remember nothing. She will live her life thinking that the name on the identity tag is her own.”
“But don’t be too sad. Once we get back to the future, there shouldn’t be any problems. You can reveal your identity then and live as friends.”
Her heart pounded. It was then that it hit her.
“Besides, you said the Dragon Slayer is trying to regain his memories too. Let’s look for a way together once we get back—see if we can recover her lost memories.”
He had really done it.
“Okay? So please say something. You’re making me anxious...”
The sight of him eyeing her cautiously despite the fact that he’d just accomplished something miraculous, clearly not sure what to do with himself, made Amelia laugh. “No need.”
“Huh? What do you mean?”
“It means you don’t have to worry about it anymore. I won’t be trying to get my sister’s memories back.”
“Eh? How come?”
Amelia smiled at his question. As she didn’t smile often, the muscles of her face felt awkward as they moved into place. “It’s better to not remember.”
From now on, her sister would be different. The life she had longed so desperately for would begin, and painful memories would only get in the way of that life.
“...Goodbye, Laura.”
I’m okay. Even if I’m not with my sister. Even if the life I lead is far from the normal life I wished for. Even if it’s still awkward to even lift the corners of my lips.
Her sister would have nothing to worry about.
“Let’s go, barbarian.”
“It’s Yandel, not barbarian.”
“Yes, Yandel.”
She was not alone anymore.

chapters.title: Chapter 331: To the Future (1)
paragraphs: Sunlight and a cool breeze slid in through the window. As I drank rum paired with the grilled meat from the store across the street, I couldn’t help but exclaim, “Yeah, that’s more like it.”

How long had it been since I’d been able to enjoy a normal day like this? Maybe it was because I’d been in drab Noark for several months, but the change was unbelievably satisfying. Not that I didn’t have any worries on my mind, though.
It’s already been a week.
Seven days had passed since that chaotic night all those big names crawled out of the woodwork to keep me busy: Auril Gavis, Lüchenprague, and Jerome the Knight of Light.
Sigh.
I was still stuck in this time period.

“When is this thing going to activate?” I took out the Fragment of Records Stone and fiddled with it out of habit, but there were some good things about having extra time. At the very least, I had time to dispose of the equipment I collected.
I also have a few guesses as to why this thing is still silent...

Anyway, for that reason, we decided to take a break and found a place to stay aboveground. Just one room, by the way. I tried to find two separate rooms, but Amelia scolded me and said that there was no need for that, and to be honest, I accepted her reasoning. After all, we had lived as practically a single unit for several months already. It was much too late to argue for a separation of sexes.
“Drinking again...”
“Oh, you’re here.”

“I told you to keep the door locked when I’m not here.” Amelia returned from her outing and unceremoniously threw her coat on the coat rack. I didn’t bother asking where she’d been since early morning. It was obvious. She probably went to stalk her sister to see how she was doing again.
“Nagging as soon as you get in?”
“I’m not nagging—”
I quickly changed the subject. “So, how’s Laura?”

Perhaps because of the powerful effects of the Blessing of Lethe’s prototype, Laura had only opened her eyes three days ago. After being diagnosed with memory loss by the priest who was volunteering at the first-aid station, she started to believe the name on the identity tag was her own.
“It’s not Laura, it’s Shannon.”
“Ah, right.”

Shannon Ellaura was the new name we created for her. We were a little reluctant to use the tag that the old man had given her. Swapping the old tag with a new one in the patient’s box of belongings and even correcting the patient records written at the first-aid station one by one, Amelia had been quite busy the past few days.
“So, how is she?”

“Unfortunately, she has attracted the attention of the priest who was there as a volunteer. She was taught to read for the first time today and she’s learning really fast. The priest seems to think that’s a sign that her memories will return soon...”
“Don’t worry. That won’t happen.”
“I’m not worried about that part. It’s just that since the priest is from the church, his attention bothers me.”
At first, I was confused about what she meant, but I quickly understood. “Because of her essence?”
“Yes. It’ll come off as suspicious for a child who isn’t even an adult yet to have an essence.”

If left alone, Laura-slash-Shannon would probably live her whole life without ever knowing that the power of an essence resided in her body. Her stats could be explained away as her being a naturally fit person, and without her memories, she would never be able to activate her special skills.
“That definitely makes me nervous too. Catching the attention of the volunteer priest wasn’t in the plan.”

If she lived a life closely linked to a religious denomination, that would change things. As churches were places that had the power and authority to erase essences, that raised the possibility that the existence of her essence would be discovered.
“...Since losing one’s memory is a rare occurrence, it seems she has unexpectedly caught their attention.”
“Then what will you do now?”

“What can I do? It’s not like I can forcefully remove it.” Amelia bit her lip unhappily and said she would just keep an eye on things for the time being. I agreed with her opinion. With that, that conversation came to an end.
“Anyway, don’t you think you should change the way you talk?”
When I started in on her, Amelia gave me a wary look. “...What about it?”
“Your tone is too stiff for a conversation between clanmates.”
“Clanmates?”
“Why are you looking at me like this is the first you’re hearing of it? You’re not thinking of pretending you forgot or something—”
“No, I remember. Just... I don’t know what that has to do with how I speak.”
“Hmm, it doesn’t have anything to do with it, actually. I was just curious how you’d sound in a different tone.”
“...What?” Amelia gave me a long-suffering look before letting out a deep sigh. “You... really...”
“What, I can be curious, can’t I? Given the way you spoke when you were young, it doesn’t sound like you always spoke this way.”
“That’s...” Amelia trailed off, which I wasn’t expecting. In the past, she would have just ignored me or asked if I was making fun of her. “I will try to work on my tone.”
“Huh?”
“No, I will... work on it. Are you satisfied? No, is...that good?”
What do you mean good?

I genuinely got goosebumps, which was why I was still speechless when Amelia began to contemplate her tone with a serious look on her face. “Hmm... does ‘okay’ sound nicer than ‘good?’ Which do you think is better?”
“W-Wait. Aren’t you changing it too easily?”
“You’re the one who told me to change it, Yandel.”
“Yeah, but still.”
“Don’t misunderstand. This is an issue I’ve been thinking about recently too.”
“You’ve been thinking about it?”
“...Laura would have wanted this for me. Besides, since you brought it up as well, that must mean there really is a problem with me.”
Ah... I was just joking around with her before we got down to business to lighten up the depressing vibe in here...

I decided to quickly sort this out before it got to be too late. “Now that I think about it, I don’t think you have to force yourself to change anything. Who cares about the way you talk? What’s important is what’s within.”

Amelia didn’t seem particularly moved by my speech at first, but when I told her she could trust me as someone who had a romantic history with Missha, who talked differently than most people, she nodded.
“So that’s the relationship between you two.”
Why did I say that? I haven’t told anyone that.
“Hmm, since speeches like that are hard to find fault with, I’m sure it’s not empty words this time. All right. For now, I’ll put the issue on hold.”

“...Okay, good idea.” This was a rather uncomfortable topic for me so I quickly moved on to the point I had been trying to get to earlier. “Anyway, since we’ve rested long enough, I think it’s time for a serious conversation.”
“Conversation... all right.” Amelia sat in the chair across from me and we began the meeting we had been postponing for a week under the guise of a break.
The first item of the meeting was this. “Do you really have no connection to the Order of the Rose?”
“I don’t. And that conversation was over a long time ago.”

I learned several days ago that the reason Lüchenprague had pursued Amelia so persistently was because he believed she was a member of that group. It seemed he held some sort of grudge against them that was not known to the public.
“That way I can show you what loss feels like.”
Considering the guy said that at the time, he must have lost someone precious to him. But that didn’t matter.
“Why are you bringing this up again?”

At the time, I looked past it as a strange coincidence, but now that I was taking a moment to think about it, a possibility came to mind. “You said you learned how to use your aura from a woman you met by chance at Castle Noark, right?”

“Yes, she taught me a few things, saying she liked the look in my eyes. Of course, she only helped me build a basic foundation—it was much later that I actually awakened the aura. But... I’m sure we’ve talked about this already too.”
“That is true.” Earlier in the week, we concluded that this woman must have been a member of the Order of the Rose, but... “Is there a possibility that that woman was you?”
“...What?”
“It just suddenly occurred to me. There’s no way a strange woman would show you such kindness.”
Amelia, who had been quite perceptive ever since she was a child, understood exactly what I was trying to say this time. “Are you thinking that that is the task we still have to complete?”
“Yes.” Creating the basis of an aura for Amelia F, who had been left alone in this world, might have been our remaining homework.
“Don’t worry. That can’t be the case.” Amelia flatly rejected the possibility. I asked her to provide evidence but she just told me to trust her on this one and didn’t go into detail.
The way she’s talking, I guess I really have it wrong...
If that was true, that was good news for me. If we had had to follow history as it unfolded, that would have meant we would have had to stay here another two years.

“Then let’s get on to the next item on the agenda.” The second topic that I brought up was Auril Gavis. What kind of variable would this suspicious old man be going forward? We discussed this for a long time, and to little avail. It ended with me getting scolded.
“Why did you do such a dangerous thing? It could have been a good thing to part on good terms.”
“What do you mean? Are you saying I should have revealed my name and face?”
“Even if you didn’t, I’m saying there was no need to mock him in the end.”
“Ah...” That was true. At the time it felt good, but thinking about how furious the old man must have been afterward did make me shudder a bit.
“You’re great and all, but you need to behave yourself better.”
“...All right.”

“Since you’re agreeing, I won’t say any more on the subject... But be careful. Becoming your comrade also means I’m entrusting my life to you.” I was very pleased by that declaration, which went beyond trust.
...But didn’t she say she wouldn’t say any more?

“Ahem.” I broke up the conversation with a cough and moved on to the next item on the list. It was none other than the point of this meeting: how to activate the Fragment of Records Stone. “To be exact, I want us to discuss what exactly the homework we might’ve been given is...”
“You sound like you have something in mind.”

Of course, I wouldn’t have brought this up without any thought. Aside from providing the foundation of an aura for Amelia F two years from now, there were a few more potential assignments. The first was this.
“The Genesis Treasures...?” Amelia seemed confused as soon as the Genesis Treasures were mentioned, but I couldn’t shake the possibility.

Well, I couldn’t be the one who would steal the Genesis Treasures twenty years from now, but I may have a little bit to do with it in the future. Like the barbarian heart fiasco, for example—the fallout would come much later, but I could end up being the catalyst.
“True, you said the Genesis Treasures are particularly important items to evil spirits. In that respect, that makes sense. You’re also an evil—”
“Shh.”
“Ah, my bad. You told me not to mention that.”

Although this was a sore spot for me, since Amelia apologized right away, I let it slide with a yellow card. On to the second possibility. “The GM... that’s the nickname of the man who took over the gathering from Auril Gavis.”
“Yes. But what about him?”
“This is exactly around the time he took over the community.”
You could say it was a bit too coincidental. Perhaps I needed to meet with him in the past and do something to get back to our original time.
“That seems plausible too. Do you have a third?”
You think I don’t?
I immediately told her my last theory. “Hide everything I collected here so that I can deliver it to the future. Perhaps that is my final task.”
“That’s... just something you want to do anyway, no?”
Uh, I don’t have anything to say to that...
“Then have you come up with any ideas?” I asked. “On what it is that we have to do?”
“W-Well... I’ll tell you when I think of something.”
I thought she might have a good idea. This was a bit disappointing, but embracing the shortcomings of a comrade was a mark of good leadership. “Anyway, so did you sell all of the equipment?”
“More than half. At a reduced price, I could sell it all sooner—”
“No, it doesn’t matter how long it takes. Sell it for full price.”
“There were some valuables among them—isn’t it best to keep a few of them?”
You really don’t know?

When it came to equipment, maintenance was essential. The value decreased over time. Besides, trying to sell equipment from twenty years ago in the future would only invite suspicion as to its origins, so aside from Demon Grinder, it was best to get rid of everything.
The problem is where I can hide this to keep it safe...
I was about to run through potential solutions for the millionth time when Amelia said, “Ah, I have something to tell you.”
“Huh?”
“I heard this when I went out today. They say a rank-three essence will be auctioned off at the Central Exchange.”
“Huh, a rank-three essence? Why not at the Sky Auction House?”
“It seems the Alminus Trading Company is trying something new.”
Hmm, are they trying to gentrify the Central Exchange? Even if they are, they won’t be able to beat Sky Auction House.
“So what essence is it? Ah, or is that also kept quiet until the day before the auction, like at Sky Auction House?”
“It is, but I already know what essence it is so it doesn’t matter. It was a very famous auction at the time.”
Yes, this was the benefit of being a time traveler.
When I urged her to speak, Amelia opened her mouth. “It’s the essence of Vol-Herchan.”
Is this what they call fate?
Coincidentally, this was an essential essence of my cultivation method.

chapters.title: Chapter 332: To the Future (2)
paragraphs: Vol-Herchan was a super-huge monster that appeared on the seventh floor. Because it lived in groups within a designated area, as long as you had the specs, the acquisition of the essence itself was on the easier side. This was why I chose the essence of the Bayon as my reward from the palace; it was a little harder to obtain later.
But if you look at combat performance alone, this one is superior.

If Bayon’s Transcendence gave you buffs, improved unpredictability, and made unconventional skill combos possible, Vol-Herchan specialized in just one thing: Physical Resistance, the stat that all tanks had to prioritize over Strength. Besides, among Vol-Herchan’s active skills was one that could block an aura, so this damned essence was one that was essential to develop into a reliable Shield Barbarian.
The problem... is the color of the essence.

Depending on the color of the essence, the active skill varied. This was the biggest reason why growth became tougher the higher level you became. Not only was hunting high-ranking monsters difficult, but starting at rank three, droppable essences appeared in five or six different colors. As such, I couldn’t get ahead of myself yet.
“Amelia... do you know what color the essence is?”
“Hmm, it was probably green.”
What? Green?!
“Hallelujah...” The word flew from my mouth unknowingly and Amelia frowned. True, she must have been confused since this was her first time hearing it.

“Is that a word used in your homeland?” Without any religious connotations, I explained that it was simply a phrase you used when you got lucky, to which Amelia nodded and said, “I see.” Then she gave me a somewhat brooding look. “And you had so much to say earlier when I said that phrase...”
Ah... right. I had been pretty stern with her when she said “evil spirit.” It might have seemed hypocritical of me.
Welp, normally I would have just shouted hallelujah inwardly.
Was it because she was the only ally I had in this world who knew I was an evil spirit?
I offered her a genuine apology. “I wasn’t trying to be harsh with you. I just think I might be getting too comfortable around you. I’ll be careful too.”
“...If you say so.” Amelia coolly accepted my apology, resolving the matter there.
Picking up where we left off, I decided to ask the most important question. “But, Amelia...”
“Stop giving me that strange look and just say it.”
Well, if you say so.
“Um... do you happen to know how much it sold for?” When I asked this, trying my best to stop vibrating in my seat, Amelia snickered and got up from her chair.
Click, clack.
She came all the way up to me, bent down, and whispered in my ear. As soon as I heard the amount, goosebumps rose all over my body. Why the hell was it so expensive?

I almost passed out after hearing the price, but if I wanted to get nitpicky, it wasn’t that unreasonable. This was a rank-three essence, after all. And since it was released on the exchange instead of Sky Auction House, there would have been a greater number of bidders after the item. After all, there were tons of rich people who had the money but not the qualifications needed to enter Sky Auction House.
Anyway, that wasn’t important. “Um... Amelia.”
“Speak.”
“Well...” As I trailed off, Amelia returned to her seat and sat cross-legged, her arms crossed. It was harder to ask her this when she looked like that. “Uh... it’s...”
When my hesitation continued, Amelia sighed and threw me a bone. “Are you curious how much we’ll get for selling all the equipment?”
“Yep.”
“Probably... only 70 percent of the top bid. And that’s assuming we sell it all slowly and for the proper price.”
Hah, I see.
“...I guess I’ll have to give up on it.”

Being just 30 percent short of the price wasn’t a huge problem. However, that was after I’d been collecting looted equipment for half a year and had gathered the entirety of ten people’s earthly possessions. Raising the money needed to make up for the 30 percent in such a short period of time would be next to impossible.
Judging by her expression, Amelia seemed to think so too. “...Was it an essence you wanted?”
“Yeah...”
“Don’t be too discouraged. We can obtain the essence on our own later.”
That’s true, but...
Sigh...

Even Amelia’s words of comfort made me sigh. If I had known the price was so high, I would have preferred not to find out about the essence at all. It felt almost like someone had handed me a birthday gift before taking it away again. After all, even the color of the essence was perfect. In that brief moment, even I felt the tug of fate.
“Well, it’s not that we’re totally without the means...”
At the sound of Amelia’s voice, I raised my lowered head. “Means...?”

Amelia avoided my gaze. At first, I thought maybe the look in my eyes was making her uncomfortable, but it didn’t seem like she was just staring off into space. It felt more like her eyes were fixed on something.
What is she staring daggers at?
I followed her line of sight and then jumped to my feet—and rightfully so. There, leaning against the wall, was Kraul’s Demon Grinder in all its glory.
“N-Not that!”
“Why? It’s not something that we can take back to our original time, anyway.”
“I’m going to bury it and hide it!”
“That still has an element of risk to it. It may be more logical to dispose of it and exchange it for an essence.”
