Amelia wasn’t wrong. No matter how well I hid it, there was no guarantee that it would still be there twenty years later. An essence, on the other hand, could come back with me no matter what. But...
“Are you seriously nuts?! Telling a warrior to sell his weapon!”
“You sound very barbarian right now.”
“Ah, it’s a habit...”
“I figured that was the case.”

But why did our conversation suddenly go off the rails? I returned to the matter at hand, resolute. “Anyway, I’m never going to sell this, so don’t ever talk about selling it again! I would rather give up on that essence!”

I wasn’t merely being stubborn. Even a rank-three essence couldn’t compare to a double-digit Numbers Item in terms of rarity. Double digits were so rare that they didn’t even appear at Sky Auction House. Depending on the demand, the difference in price between the two might not be very big, and the essence could even sell for more at times, but when you looked at their acquisition difficulty alone, Kraul’s Demon Grinder was dozens of times harder to get your hands on. Put simply, if I sold this thing now, I had no way of knowing when I’d be able to get it again.

“Hmm, if you say so.” When I explained the reason in depth, Amelia accepted my logic without objection, and that was the end of that conversation. Amelia went out to check on her sister again, and I drank at the inn by myself to soothe my queasy stomach.
“Ugh, the alcohol... is sweeter today...”

How long would it take to obtain this essence? I couldn’t be sure, but it would take years at least. To start, I’d need to return to my original time, reassemble the clan, painstakingly upgrade our ship, and get through the sixth and then the seventh floor to encounter a Vol-Herchan. Then, after all that, the laborious grind required to get the right color of essence would begin.
“Ugh... Vol-Herchannn...”

I was drinking alone crying woe is me when the door opened with a creak. “Have you been drinking this whole time?” It was Amelia, who had devotedly stayed by her sister’s side all day and only returned after sunset.
“Haha, you’re here? Amelia...”
“I told you to keep the door locked.”
“...Sorry.”
“...You’re apologizing?”
“I’ll be better about locking the door from now on. After all, it’s not like I have that essence. If an assassin with an aura comes after me, I’ll have no choice but to squeal and die...”
Was it because it had been a while since I’d been drunk? I was suddenly so overcome with emotion that I couldn’t speak.

At the sight, Amelia let out a deep sigh. “You reek of alcohol.” That was my bad as a roommate so I accepted the criticism as it came, my head hanging morosely. There was a pause before Amelia cautiously opened her mouth. “But Yandel. That essence... do you really want it that bad?”
“Huh...?” At that moment, I instantly sobered up. She sounded like a mother about to give into her son who was throwing a tantrum in the toy aisle. “Do you have a way...?”
At the sliver of hope in my voice, Amelia huffed out a sigh that almost sounded like a laugh. “Don’t get your hopes up too much.”
“Y-You mean...!” I was moved to near tears.
“I told you not to get your hopes up too much. All I’m saying is that there’s something we can try.”
So this was how it felt to have someone older and dependable on your side. I had never felt this way before.

Since that day, Amelia went out every morning and returned at dusk looking tired, but she didn’t answer any of my questions asking what she was up to. She said she’d tell me when the time came since she didn’t know how things would play out.
“If things go well, I think I can solve our money problem. So until auction day, be proactive. Don’t just stay at home all day.”
“Amelia...!”

There was no way I could go against Amelia’s orders so I started wandering outside after that. I had just one goal in mind: finding a place where Kraul’s Demon Grinder could be safely stashed for twenty years.
Hm, I think the forest in the holy land would be perfect, but it might be disturbed during a funeral ceremony...
Finding the perfect spot was a lot trickier than I thought. Even if it seemed like I found a good place, whenever I examined it objectively, it was never 100 percent ideal.
The sewers can’t be trusted because vagrants gather there... And I can’t enter the holy lands of the other races, so that’s a bust...

If Amelia failed to gather the money needed for the essence, I would have to choose a more secure place that could hide our large sum of equipment-related money as well. Well, that wasn’t my only concern, though.
What happens if she really finds the money?

My current level was six. I could consume a total of six essences, and all six slots were currently full. In order to take the essence of Vol-Herchan, I’d either have to level up or erase one of the essences I had. But to reach level seven, I’d have to clear more than half the sixth floor, so it was a no-brainer.
What would be the best one to erase?

Orc Hero, Ogre, and Bayon were my core essences so I didn’t intend to remove them, and Storm Gush was a rank-three essence so it would be a waste to erase it. Just the base stats alone made it worth keeping. So, I had two options: Manticore, my sole transportation skill and a rank-five essence I already planned to erase someday, and Corpse Golem, the rank-seven essence I had been forced to absorb to survive. Although it had the lowest rank of all my essences, that didn’t mean it was an easy decision.
I feel like I’ll be empty without this...

There was no need to explain how vital this essence had been in words. I’d received immense help from its Pain Resistance stat. Plus, Flesh Burst and Acid Fluid—which I had once considered trash skills—actually played a useful role in battle.
It’s about time to graduate, though. I never intended to use it this long in the first place.

If I had to choose between the two, it was better to keep the Manticore. The reason was simple: even if I got to keep 20 percent of its stats thanks to Heredity, that would still mean my current +200 Mana Resistance would be reduced to +40. If I erased it now, I would have to consume another essence that could boost my Mana Resistance to balance things out until I obtained the essence of Bellarios.
Well, this is all pointless to worry about if Amelia can’t find the money.
At the reminder that my hiding spot would become even more important in the case of failure, I diligently explored various parts of the city, and time flew by.
Only three days left now.
With about three days left until auction day, I set a clock on the table and lay in bed.
I wonder what will happen this time.
It was midnight on the 15th.
“Oh, I’m here this time.”

Waking up in a familiar room, I first put on the mask hanging on the wall. Then I hurried outside. Only silence filled the empty hallway, but if my hypothesis was correct, the GM who inherited this space would be around here somewhere.
Should I take a look around first?
I wandered the hallways and carefully inspected the mansion. I didn’t see any of the existing members of the community, like the head of Orcules or Fallen Scholar.
Come to think of it, I wonder what happened to them...

It was when those questions slowly began to arise that I spotted a white guy standing blankly in the first floor’s main hall. Even at a glance, I could tell he wasn’t an evil spirit from the same realm as Auril. He was wearing sportswear with a logo that was familiar to me.
Is that the GM?
In order to get a closer look, I took a step forward. But did he sense my presence too?
The man looked around and flinched when he made eye contact with me. “A-A person!?”
I studied the man in the silence that followed, and he did the same.
That’s unexpected.
His facial features were somewhat dopey, with eyes full of confusion. It almost looked like he was afraid of me, as well.
“Um... w-who are you? I heard the original members were all banned...”
The existing members were all kicked, huh?

Seeing as he was revealing information I didn’t even ask for despite the fact that he was clearly on guard, I thought I caught the heady scent of a newbie, which was impossible to hide even if you tried.
Yes, even the GM wouldn’t have been here more than a year at this point. He would be inexperienced.
How should I prepare this meal? My mouth was already watering. Maybe that was why.
“A-Are you... sir! Is that you?”
At that question, asked with such an innocent look on his face, I almost licked my lips without realizing it.

chapters.title: Chapter 333: To the Future (3)
paragraphs: What was I doing now, and for what purpose? In order to become an excellent gamer, you had to be constantly aware of your goals and the means you had to achieve them. By doing so, you could reduce the amount of time you wasted unnecessarily. That was how to have an efficient gaming life.
Lick.

Even as I licked my lips, I was busy running through my list of what I wanted to achieve on this trip to the community. I didn’t need to think for too long, though, as it could all be summed up in one sentence. My goal was to find out the GM’s identity.
Hmm, this would be best.

Lion Style Form Four: Possession. Going beyond method acting, this was a technique that allowed me to smoothly carry on a conversation like I’d been possessed by the person I was embodying. I made it up just now.
“Haha, did I surprise you?” When I laughed like the old man, the white guy’s eyes widened.

“A-Are you really him, sir?” His voice was welcoming, but did he sense something was off? His guard, which seemed to have lowered a bit, went up higher again. “But your height is different... Your skin as well...”
Haha, you have a lot of doubts for a newbie. You’ll be a big boy one day.
I spoke like I was rather happy to be on the receiving end of his suspicions. “I could say the same to you as well.” My tone was that of a grandfather kindly teaching his grandson something new.
The man glanced around at his surroundings as if he’d just realized something, then checked his reflection in the glass window on the wall. “Ah, then is this your true self?”
“That’s right.”
“But why the mask...?”
“I don’t want to show my real face to others.”
‘Ah’ what? It was quite funny to see him nod like he understood my logic, but I made sure to keep a straight face. I was not Hansu Lee right now.
“Haha, so how is it here?” I decided to start with a light question and gather information bit by bit.
“Ah, right... I’m not sure yet. I’m not really sure how to do the thing you told me about, either...”
The thing I told him? I had no idea what he was talking about, so I whipped out Form Two: Sit Tight. Using the secret skill that always got me halfway through, I soon felt a tug on the line.
“The... materialization you mentioned? Even that isn’t all that easy...”
Ah, that.
Thankfully, that was something I was familiar with. It was an essential function to master if you wanted to be active in the Ghost Busters community.
Normally it only works in a person’s inner world. But since he took over the Master’s position, I guess it would work for him here too.
I quickly took stock of the situation and smoothly continued the conversation. “Haha, it’s natural to have a hard time at first. I will help you a little. Is there something you want to eat?”
“Close your eyes and imagine it in your head in detail. Imagine it is in your hands. Yes, good job. You’re a quick learner.”
“Sorry...?”
“Would you like to open your eyes?”
“Yes... H-Huh?” The man opened his eyes, which went wide at the hamburger in his hand. He took a big bite. “...I can’t taste it.”
Oh, that? Sorry, that function was removed when the Round Table got made before you came... But there’s no need to tell him such a cruel truth.
“That is unavoidable, so don’t be too down on yourself.”
“Right...” The man nodded in acceptance but still couldn’t hide his dismay.
It wasn’t like I couldn’t sympathize. When I first came to Ghost Busters, I couldn’t hide the disappointment I felt after trying the can of Coke in the refrigerator, either.
“Ah, um.”
“Speak.”
“But what happened to you, sir? You told me I would never see you again...” Judging by his tone, he wasn’t suspicious of me but simply curious.
It wasn’t a very difficult question so I was able to easily answer it. “I was worried about you. I thought I should meet with you here at least once and provide you some help before I leave.”
“Ah, I see...!” Like the naive newbie he was, the man trusted this without a hint of suspicion.

As soon as I saw this, I knew the timing was perfect. Since I’d managed to gain some of his trust, it was time for some digging. “Don’t worry too much.” I patted the man’s shoulder nonchalantly like someone with no ulterior motives. “With magical talent like yours, you will be able to quickly improve at materialization.”

The GM was a wizard. I already knew this after meeting him in person months ago, but the reason why I deliberately chose the words “magical talent” was simple. It was best to be cautious about everything. Since he was only in his first year, it was possible that he wasn’t officially a wizard yet.

“Ah, magic... that’s why you chose me, sir.” Judging by his tone, it sounded like he’d already selected the wizard route. “Still, there is something I don’t quite understand. There would be many people more capable than a half-wizard like me, so why...?”

“Do not belittle yourself. How many of those called to this world have established themselves as quickly as you? You will surely become even greater with time.” When I started innocently praising him, the man looked away in obvious embarrassment. At this point, I attempted to dig for his identity one more time. “By the way, what was your rank again?”
“Rank six.”
What? I was genuinely surprised. It wouldn’t have even been a year since he was called here, but rank six? Was that possible in such a short time?
As those questions were filling my mind, the man muttered in a self-deprecating tone, “Luckily my rank is high, but I still can’t use magic properly, so I live on edge every day...”

That answered my questions. Combined with the fact that he called himself a half-wizard earlier and told me he couldn’t use magic just now, that had to mean that the character he possessed when he got here was already a wizard. Statistically, evil spirit possession only happened when the possessed person was twenty years of age. However, unlike adventurers, who could only enter the labyrinth as adults, wizards were able to select their class at a young age.
Ha, so while I started from scratch as a barbarian...
Even as I found myself getting jealous of someone else for the first time in a long time, I carved that vital piece of information into my head. So there were cases like these among evil spirits.
“Um... what’s the matter?”
I laughed. “It’s nothing. I’m just proud of you.”
“Please don’t be like that. It makes me embarrassed...”
“Embarrassed? How is knowing your shortcomings and working hard to fix them something to be embarrassed about?”
At the warm words that almost gave me a toothache just from saying them, the man looked at me, moved. “Sir...!”
Okay, in the game, he’d be in the Confused state right about now.
I snuck in another question. “But... what is your name?”

It was about time I learned the identity of the GM, which was shrouded in mystery. I knew he was a wizard, but I didn’t know his name or face yet, so I wanted to use this opportunity to figure it out.
“Pardon? My name? Why...?” The man looked confused at my question. Suspicion showed signs of emerging in his eyes, something I’d worked hard to mitigate by building his trust up to this point.
Welp, I guess it’s not going to work out like this.
I quickly made a decision and whipped out Plan B. Plan A had just been to test the waters anyway. “Haha, I was asking for your real name,” I said cheerfully.
“R-Real name?” The man looked taken aback for a moment before exhaling in relief. “Ah... no wonder. I was wondering why you were suddenly asking my name. You have no reason to ask that...”
“Haha, I was only asking out of curiosity, so you don’t have to answer if you don’t feel comfortable.”
“No. There’s no point in hiding my real name. It’s Oliver Wiseman.”

“What a nice sounding name, haha...” I laughed like the old man and filtered the name “Oliver Wiseman” out the other ear. As he said earlier, what was the point in knowing it? Real names were useless here.
“But, sir?”
“Hmm?”
“Could I ask for some advice?”
“Of course. Go ahead.”
“You told me to turn this place into a place for evil spirits—no, players—to interact.”
Uh, did he?
“I did.”
“I think I can produce the pill you spoke of with a bit more research, but I’m clueless about the other aspects. Could you give me some advice on those?”
“I don’t know how to start decorating this place.”

Oh, that. After thinking it through for a while, I gave the GM what I knew would end up being great advice. Since I’d decided to play along, it wasn’t hard at all to help him out. If he didn’t know how to run this community, I just had to tell him what I saw in the future.
“As this world classifies people like you as evil spirits, the others will be reluctant to enter this place. There should be a system in place to maintain complete anonymity.”
“Ah! I do have an idea for that part! I think I can create something like an internet forum...”
“Internet forum?”
“Sorry. That would be an unfamiliar term for you.”

The GM explained internet communities in an easy-to-understand manner like someone teaching an old man about pop culture. For someone who had lived with the internet my whole life, this explanation was completely redundant. However, I learned one thing from this.
So, Auril didn’t introduce himself properly.
Judging by how this guy was talking, it seemed Auril had only introduced himself as an evil spirit from another world and not the creator of the game. Anyway, that wasn’t important.

“Oh, that sounds like a good idea. But while you’re at it, I think it would also be a good idea to use those ‘computers’ you mentioned earlier. It suits the form of a community, and it would be easier for people to adapt to something they are familiar with.”
“Oh... you’re right!”

“It would also be a good idea to create something like an exchange for different parties to help each other. A place to exchange real-life information and items without revealing their identities will be an attractive prospect to many.”
“And when you send out those pills, send them a letter in your mother tongue to explain what kind of place this is.”
“Incredible...! It’s amazing enough that you grasped the concept of computers and communities right away, but to think of all this as well...!”
I spent a while describing the final form of Ghost Busters to the GM like it was all my idea. With each section, the GM let out exclamations of admiration.

But it seemed something had belatedly occurred to him. “Just from what you’re describing, it’ll be an extraordinary place. But how can I create all that?” the GM asked, tilting his head. To that, I had nothing to say.
How, you ask? That’s for the engineer to figure out. How would I know the process?
“If it’s you, you can do it,” I said firmly.
“Sorry...?”
“You may still be inexperienced in materialization, but you will slowly get used to it. I believe in you.”
“Ah, right...” the GM answered half-heartedly. He looked like he still lacked confidence, but that wasn’t my problem. That was how things turned out in the future, anyway.
I ended the debate about feasibility there and resumed my design work. “Oh, and one more thing. How about writing an entry code at the bottom of the letter?”
“You mean a password?”
“Yes, if you use an insult to the palace as the password, you should be able to filter out spies to some extent.”

The PS after the letter actually served as a password. Not that it mattered much, of course. Whether you got the password right or not, Soul Queen had to approve your membership after a verification process. Since I was a perceptive person, I’d figured out the trick hidden in the letter and entered the password before she even arrived.
Oh, come to think of it, though, the abbreviation for ‘password’ is PW, not PS.

How did that happen, then? Had it just been a stroke of luck on my part? It suddenly occurred to me that there might have been another way to figure out the password, but that wasn’t something to worry about right now.
“Sir, are you unwell?”
“Ahem, no. Where was I?”
“You were talking about a way to identify spies.”

“Ah, right.” After that, I rattled off information on everything from the contents of the letter to the concept of everyone having individual private spaces, along with measures to filter out and eject spies.
Those should be enough instructions.

Although I was bound to have missed some details conveying this verbally, I wasn’t particularly worried. This wasn’t the first time I’d experienced this since coming to the past. Whether I said everything or not, this mansion would slowly turn into the community I knew.
Hmm, maybe this was the task I had left to do in this era...
As the thought popped into my head unbidden, I suddenly began to worry I might be sent back to the present as soon as I left the community.
No, come on. That won’t happen.
I tried to shake off my concerns.

“But, sir...” the GM said cautiously. “This isn’t certain, but the person you mentioned at the end last time. I think I know who they are. Um... when you found out I cleared the game at Times Fifteen mode, do you remember you said there would one day be a user who would clear it on the original difficulty? The person who would make every player’s long-cherished wish come true?”
When I understood what he was getting at, I flinched. Ah, so that was what they had talked about.
So he doesn’t pass on information about the future to just anyone.
I could now see that the GM had been assigned a position of surveillance. The GM himself didn’t seem to be aware of this, though.

But what’s this about a long-cherished wish? Is he talking about the Gate of the Abyss? Hmm, perhaps that old man just said whatever he needed to say to motivate the GM—that I need to show up for them to all go home.
Anyway, I decided to think about that later. “Yes?”

When I prompted him, the GM continued speaking. “I’ve thought about it since then and I have a guess as to who it could be. He was very famous in our forum, which was called Stone Iven... and someone I respected very much. While I was clearing the game at Times Fifteen mode, I received a lot of help from him.”
I knew who he was talking about without him needing to say it, but I was currently disguised as Auril Gavis so I leaned in with fake anticipation. “And who is that?”
“It’s someone who went by the username Elfnuna.”
“Hmm?”

“I don’t know for sure, of course, but in my opinion, there’s no one else out there who could beat the original difficulty besides him. And didn’t you say last time that this user would be a barbarian? Coincidentally, it seemed he mainly used Shield Barbarians.”

“I see... all right. But since nothing is confirmed yet, it would be best to leave as many possibilities open as possible. There is a chance that that person is not a barbarian at all.” I casually tacked on that last bit to make it a little harder for him to track me down. But was that a mistake on my part?
“Pardon? Not a barbarian?”
Uh, why are you triggered all of a sudden?
Though I was startled, I let out an easy laugh. “Haha, I just meant that it was a possibility.”
“I see...” The GM spoke as if he agreed, but his eyes said otherwise. “Sir?”
“Speak.”
“May I be so bold as to ask you one more question?” The GM stared intently into my eyes, which were the only things visible through my mask, and asked, “What is my name?”
Oh, what a mess.

Upon reflection, perhaps I underestimated him too much. Even if he may have been a newbie now, this was a veteran who would end up running the community for over twenty years, keeping his identity thoroughly hidden the whole time. Although he may be lacking the quick judgment he would one day have in his prime, he wouldn’t be wanting for intelligence.

The fact was that my appearance was different here than in the outside world, yet I was still wearing a mask and had also asked for his name. Although I’d provided valid explanations for each action I took to make him accept them, even still, the discrepancies would have built up. No matter how hard I tried to act like the old man, I wouldn’t be able to do it perfectly. This man must have sensed that something was off about our conversation from the start, and my statement just now was a critical mistake.
“...Why aren’t you saying anything?”
At his question, I laughed ruefully and silently. But now that things had come to this, this wasn’t the time to be asking how things went so wrong.
“Is it because you don’t know my name—?”
I quickly spoke up, interrupting the GM. “Zerkif Elmen Mackinder.” That wasn’t just a random name I blurted out in haste.
“There are three. Should I tell you all of them?”

This was the name of one of the three wizards Baekho suspected of being the GM. As such, the probability that it was the right one was 33.3 percent. The odds were good enough to at least give it a shot before throwing in the towel. So how did that work out for me?
There was a moment of silence. Then, the GM spoke in a voice that radiated hostility. “You... who are you?”

chapters.title: Chapter 334: To the Future (4)
paragraphs: The best-case scenario had been the GM not suspecting me at all until I got all the information I wanted. But, as expected, it seemed that hiding it until the end wasn’t feasible.
Well, it can’t be helped now.
I shook off the small bit of disappointment that lingered. The information I’d uncovered so far made pulling out Form Four worth it, anyway.
I don’t know what school he belongs to, but he’s twenty years old and a rank-six.
Besides that, the number of potential candidates had now been reduced to two. There was no way Auril Gavis had met with him without knowing his name.
And judging by that reaction... This can’t be Zerkif Elmen Mackinder.

That 33.3 percent probability I mentioned earlier had just become 50 percent. This was as much information as I could uncover while keeping my identity hidden. Well, I still wasn’t going to give up, of course.
If I look into the other two candidates, I think I can find him based on that information alone...

However, there was no need for that when the easy way existed. The reason I had been willing to dig around for information more assertively than usual in the first place was because I had this to fall back on.
“Tell me. Who are you? How did you get in here and why did you pretend to be him?” The GM, who now saw through my act, forcefully pressed me for answers like he was some sort of top dog or something.
Cute.
I smirked. I had been planning to reveal I was a different person before I left anyway. “Auril Gavis.”
“...What? That’s the name of the game’s creator—”
“That is the name of the old man you met.”
When I cut him off, the GM frowned. He heard me right but it seemed he didn’t understand what I was saying at all.

As a player who cared about newbies, I kindly offered up an explanation. “That is the man who summoned you all to this world and who only intends to use you. He also doesn’t hold the slightest guilt for what he’s done. Beware of him.”
“Saying something like that while hiding your identity—”
Whatever.
“It’s your choice whether you believe me or not. I just came here to warn you.”
“...Then why did you pretend to be him?”
“I wanted to know what kind of person you were before I told you.”
Of course, I didn’t think the GM would trust this completely. I wasn’t telling him the entire truth to begin with, and the GM seemed to be studying me closely to figure out what my intentions were.
What’s important is how plausible I sound.

People were so sensitive that when they were told something like this, it didn’t matter how much they trusted the person in question—they would start to feel antsy. Just like how, even if it was very small, you couldn’t help being concerned about a crack in the wall. Maybe, if, perhaps. Planting these keywords in the GM’s head was enough for now.
That should drive enough of a wedge between them...
There were countless reasons to be wary of Auril, but I decided to stop there. Rather than going on and on, I figured letting his imagination run wild would be more effective.

“...Do you think I’ll be swayed by you?!” Of course, since figuring out who I was was more important to this man than Auril Gavis right now, the GM raised his voice. “If you don’t reveal your identity—”
What a joke.
That’s not how you ask questions, especially to someone who seems stronger than you.
I took a step forward and fired back, “And if I don’t reveal it?”
Having been interrupted, the GM tried to open his mouth to say something, but no sound came out. He just choked on air.
...Cough!
[Lion Style Form Three: Disrespect for the Weak]
When I took another step forward, the GM began to tremble, his eyes going so wide I could see the whites. I didn’t realize his backbone was this flimsy. “You’re weak.”
When I was your age, I dominated the Round Table, punk.

I lowered the intensity of my murderous intent since he wouldn’t even be able to understand what I was saying in this state, and murmured in a low voice, “Aika Teratios.” This was the name of the second candidate Baekho mentioned.
The GM’s reaction was not what I expected.
What is this man talking about? Is he casting a spell or incantation or something? his wary eyes seemed to ask.
Welp. Not that one either? Then there’s only one possibility left...
“Yurven Havellion,” I continued without missing a beat. And it seemed Baekho wasn’t completely barking up the wrong tree, though I had been starting to have my doubts.

His reaction was noticeably different from before—temporarily dilated pupils, shallower breathing, and stiff facial muscles. He was even trying to act casual and not break eye contact. I had literally just been considering the possibility he might be a master at the poker face.
“So that was your name.” While on the one hand, I was filled with joy at finally discovering the GM’s name, I felt somewhat troubled on the other.
To think I would only succeed on the third try.

Both 33 percent and 50 percent were odds worth playing but the successive failures had left me unsettled. It seemed one of them had been a winner after all, though. Well, that was how it always went for me.
“Yurven Havellion.” I chewed over the GM’s name and slowly wound back the murderous intent.

When I did, the GM, who was frozen and unable to breathe, collapsed to his knees and began to gasp for breath. His eyes were glued to me the whole while. “W-Who are you...?” His gaze was filled with fear rather than hostility now, but once the murderous intent constricting his body and mind disappeared, it seemed he was able to think rationally again.
Flash!
A light burst behind my eyelids, dyeing the entire world white. This was a phenomenon I’d experienced countless times so it didn’t come as a surprise.
“See you later,” I called mockingly.
Using his authority as the moderator, he had shut down the server.
“Are you awake?”

When I opened my eyes, Amelia was sitting next to the bed. There was only one reason this girl who was usually busy roaming the city all day and night was beside me. While I was in the community, I was incapacitated. She thought it was possible something could happen while I was gone.
What’s going to happen in the span of less than ten seconds?
It felt like she was being a bit overprotective, but I also felt grateful for it.
“Here.” I was thirsty and reaching for the water bottle I left on the nightstand when Amelia picked it up and handed it to me.
“Ah, thanks.”
“So, how did it go?”

After taking a sip just to quench my thirst, I filled her in on what happened tonight. Amelia listened with obvious interest, but she didn’t make too big a deal out of it. “Yurven Havellion. To think that hermit wizard was an evil spirit. The city would be turned upside down if this got out there.”
“Hermit wizard?”
“You don’t know? He’s famous for holing himself up in the Magic Tower and rarely spending time outside. Most of his current reputation was established during his time as an adventurer years ago.”
“I see.”

This was my first time hearing he was a homebody, but thanks to some research I’d done on him in the past, I did have some general information on him. After an explosion occurred at the school he belonged to, he established his own school. During his adventurer days, he mainly used wind-attribute spells. In his specialty, the field of magical device manufacture, he was unparalleled.
Which is why his nickname is the Magic Engineer.
Anyway, that was how the story started, and it ended with me expressing relief that the Fragment of Records Stone didn’t activate.
“...Relief?”

“Ah, in the middle, I started to think that this could be the task I still had to complete in this era. If this was my final task, I wouldn’t be able to hide the equipment and would have to return as soon as I woke up.”
“Ah... that’s... t-true.”
“Huh? Amelia, what’s wrong?”

“Nothing. So, did you find a place to hide the equipment?” Amelia was acting strange but it wasn’t to the point where I felt like it was worth interrogating her. Besides, this topic was more important anyway.

“Well, I don’t know. I did a lot of exploring all over but none of the spots I checked out feel secure. I wanted to see if you had any advice.” After listing the places I had visited so far, I asked Amelia for her opinion.
“They certainly all have their issues.”
“The forest in the holy land would be perfect, but I’m nervous about that shaman who wanders there all the time.”
“Then why not leave it in a bank vault?”
“Bank vault?”

That was a method I hadn’t even thought of. In order to use the bank, I’d have to use the identity of Nivelles Enze. Not only was there a possibility that a problem would arise when I tried to recover the contents as Bjorn Yandel, but more importantly, Nivelles Enze was an identity that would be expunged next year for failure to pay taxes. Put simply, anything deposited in the vault would be returned to the National Treasury.
But it’s not like I can pay twenty years’ worth of taxes in advance, either.
This method had many pitfalls that made it unrealistic, which was why it hadn’t even been on my list.
But she wouldn’t have suggested it without knowing all that...
“Explain in detail.”
When my back straightened, Amelia spoke. “Bank Alminus has something called an unassigned, fixed-term safe.”
“I’ve never heard of it.” This wasn’t a policy that existed in the game. That meant it must be an update that had been added within the past 150 years.
“It makes sense that you wouldn’t know about it. It’s a little-known policy even to adventurers who frequent the bank.” Afterward, Amelia gave a brief explanation of the unassigned fixed-term safe.

To summarize, if I pay money, the items will be stored for a set period of time without me needing to even reveal my identity. Until I retrieve the item, I just need to hold on to the key. Hmm, not bad.
The next day, I left the inn with Amelia for the first time in a while to visit the bank and confirm whether the policy in question had any harmful clauses or causes for concern I was unaware of.
This is even better than the Swiss Bank.

I decided this was at least safer than burying the weapon in the ground, so I ended up putting Kraul’s Demon Grinder into the anonymous personal safe. The period was set at a generous twenty-two years. Well, the fee was no joke, all things considered.
“Don’t worry, an amount like that is more than doable.”
As I had been given Amelia’s blessing, this kind of chump change was no big deal. Fortunately, it seemed things had worked out well.
“Uh, you found leftover money...?”

Amelia, who for two weeks had been working night and day to earn money, did indeed make the promised capital. When I asked what kind of witchcraft she had performed, her answer was this: “Nothing special. I just sold information.”

Taking advantage of her privilege as a time traveler, she sold information. Her main customers were those interested in this auction. It sounded like she sold information on the names and colors of the essences that would be put up for auction in a few days.
“But that’s strange. Why would they trust you as a source?”
“Ah, I used the head of the Central Exchange’s name.”
“Used? How?”
“I followed him twenty-four-seven to look into him and found something to blackmail him with. Then I used that to threaten him.”

It seemed the Exchange had put a lot of effort into maintaining secrecy because even the Exchange’s head did not know what the essence in question was. Of course, that was just a minor issue for us. What was important was making the customers think this was a trustworthy internal source.
“When I visited them as a member of the head’s office, no one questioned the authenticity of the information. They probably figured they could hold him liable if the information was incorrect.”
Upon hearing all of this, I couldn’t hide my amazement. This was the kind of resourcefulness that could have made her a successful businesswoman. Was this the prestige of an SSR teammate?
“Amelia...!”
“W-What...! Don’t cling to me!”
As a result, finding a place to stash my equipment, selling the rest, and finding the money to buy the essence were all taken care of by Amelia.
“Whew, it’s today...”
Time passed, and auction day arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 335: To the Future (5)
paragraphs: The Alminus Central Exchange’s first auction house, which was never more than half full even during regular auctions held with decent items, was currently flooded. And the people there weren’t nobodies, either.
“Nenma’s clan leader is here.”
“He probably intends to give it to the adventurer Iron Wall rather than use it on himself. Didn’t his first squadron’s protector die not long ago? It’s probably to fill the empty slot.”
“Oh? Is the Lagman Company also after that essence?”
“Is there anything a merchant wouldn’t be willing to buy when the price is right?”
“Hmm, but it’s tough to find an item in an auction that sells for the ticket price...”
“The value of an item doesn’t just lie in its cost. After all, Duke Kudo’s birthday is coming up soon.”
“True, if you can use this auction to impress enough nobles, you might be able to attend the banquet.”

From adventurers with shiny equipment to people who weren’t adventurers but clearly gave off an air of wealth, I couldn’t see anyone who was only here as a spectator. That was only natural. As the auction became a hot topic, tickets apparently started getting sold for high prices too.
Valuable essence aside, getting tickets was already hell in itself.
If Amelia hadn’t told me about the auction before the information was released to the public, I would have had trouble getting even one ticket and coming alone.
“Stop looking around like that. Nothing good will come from attracting attention.”
Spotting the beginnings of a scolding a mile away, I smoothly changed the subject. “Have you been to places like this often?”
“...I’ve come often enough.”

True, she’d been an adventurer much longer than I had. “Then I can ask you all my questions.” I scanned our surroundings out of the corner of my eye. “There are a surprising amount of people wearing masks like us. I heard the winner of the auction will be processed anonymously anyway.”
“There will always be people who won’t want their participation known to the public.”
“Oh, who is that guy in the suit over there? He doesn’t look like a merchant or an adventurer.”

“He’s an agent sent by an influential family. He may be dressed well, but he’s probably not from a noble family. A nobleman would protect the family’s reputation above all else, even when it comes to things like this.”
“Oh, really?”
Was she an encyclopedia or something? Every question I asked was answered without delay. While I was busy asking more questions to test her performance, the auction began.
“Amelia... can we buy that?”
“...If you give up on the item coming later.”
“That’s a no...”
The other items appeared to have been carefully selected too. Including the first item exhibited, those that followed were also of a very high standard.
What kind of Exchange auction has a triple-digit Numbers Item?
It wasn’t even a shabby triple-digit either. Although it wasn’t all that useful to me personally, any damager who used a blade could make good use of it.
Man, if I had the money, I would buy that too and put it in the safe.
Each time a new item came up, I watched the competition heat up and swallowed back my disappointment.
“That’s 140 million stones! We have 140 million stones. Are there any more bidders? The item goes to the anonymous bidder!”

Auctions in this era were very refreshing. Rather than a system in which bids could only be raised at regular increments determined by the moderator, it was a free bidding system that allowed you to bid high immediately. And for a system like that, the way they took bids was surprisingly modern.
Beep, beep, beeeeeep.

On the right armrest of each chair, there was a magic item that allowed you to punch in a number. Once you set your bid and pressed enter, the amount appeared on the electronic display board on the podium. Thanks to that, each bidder’s identity was kept anonymous.
True, if you didn’t have a method to protect anonymity like this, there could be fights later.

For reference, this system was first deployed by Sky Auction House. I learned this during my studies at the library. Apparently, there was an incident where some prestigious nobles were bidding against each other using their real names and things escalated into a brawl.

“Now, here is the seventeenth item!” A new item appeared on the podium as if on cue. It was a test tube stored in a luxurious box. Many essences had appeared so far, but this one was different in many ways.
“Yandel.”
“I know.” Unlike the previous essences, there was a large picture next to the box. It was a drawing of a massive beast covered in a thick shell, roaring at the viewer—Vol-Herchan.
They even prepared that? They really put a lot into this auction.
The participants of the auction buzzed at the dynamic drawing that seemed like it could come to life at any moment.
“Oh...? Curious...”
“I thought this essence would appear at the end.”
“Yes. It’s strange. There were a total of thirty-five items on the docket today so there should still be more than half left...”
Some questioned the fact that the essence was being presented in the middle of the auction, but I didn’t think it was strange at all. No, on the contrary, it was a praise-worthy tactic.
“The Alminus Company was smart about this.”

If the essence were the final item in the auction, those who saved up their money for it would have had no choice but to hold off until then. That meant fewer bids on the other items. But if this was auctioned in the middle to determine its owner early on, that changed things. Since the item they had intended to use their remaining capital on would have disappeared, they would be able to bid on other items they liked without any resistance.

“This item is the essence of Vol-Herchan, obtained by Clan Marel’s Thunderfire in the last expedition by personally slaying said ferocious beast...” The moderator officially began to explain the product and the story behind it, and the air in the room changed.
“Ahem...”

People who had been holding easy conversations and networking with each other started to get quiet. Desire burned in the eyes of the adventurers, and the eyes of the merchants showed a keen interest, like that of a wild cat waiting to pounce. They may not have been holding swords, but they looked like they were about to go to battle.
Tsk, who do you think you are, trying to win?
Beep, beep, beep-beep, beep.
I typed in the amount in advance.
“Now, the starting price is fifty million stones.”
As soon as the auction began, I pressed enter.
Beep.
In response, a number appeared on the electronic display board: 870 million stones. This was the reason this auction became famous enough to reach Amelia’s ears in the future.

There was only one bid. After a momentary silence following the truly brutal raise, the moderator exhibited professionalism and spoke with forced calm. “That’s... 870 million stones...! We have 870 million stones.”
Then the chaos began.
“870 million stones?”
“What kind of unhinged bastard...”
Some were incredulous, and their jaws dropped.
“Who would bid an amount like that immediately?”
Others were curious about my identity.
But while those who had already given up on the competition simply watched, thoroughly entertained, the people who were seriously after this essence were different.
“You must decide quickly before the bidding closes.”
Their expressions changed as they hurriedly began to discuss. The reactions were mixed here too.
Some had already exceeded their budgets. “Eight hundred seventy million stones is unreasonable...”

There were those making their decision based solely on cost-effectiveness. “It’s not that it’s not doable, but... paying that much money for an essence only used by protectors is crazy. We forfeit the bid.”
There were even those beginning to suspect the auction house itself.
“Why are you telling me not to bid?”
“It could be a trick on the part of the Exchange.”
“Are you saying it’s a fake bid to get us to bid higher?”
“It’s possible... but the Exchange could also have used the essence as bait to attract customers despite having no intention of selling it from the start.”

Some even voiced the possibility that the essence of the Vol-Herchan was a fake listing used to tout buyers, but none of that mattered to me. Even as their heads all spun at the dizzying amount of money, and even as they struggled to come to a clear decision on whether to make a bid or not due to the whispers around adding to the confusion, time continued to pass.
Tick, tick.

“Any... more bidders...?” The moderator, who had been bringing down the auctioneer’s gavel without hesitation up to this point, dragged things out three times longer than usual before finally opening his mouth. Seeing that the crowd was just eyeing each other, he declared the end of the bid.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
When the last, clear thwack signaling a failure to bid rang out, I nodded to myself several times with a satisfied smile.
Mm-hmm, the best part of an auction is making an immediate purchase.
Once the whirlwind-like auction came to a close, we went to the item retrieval room, paid the amount, and received Vol-Herchan’s essence.

“That’s 870 million stones... confirmed.” The staff member who handed the goods to us seemed to be quite high up the food chain, but apart from giving us an unkind look for spawning all those unflattering rumors about the auction house, she seemed to be extremely curious. But I guessed this was what you called professionalism. “Goodbye.” She occasionally glanced at us but did not ask us who we were or make any unnecessary comments.
“What are you doing? Let’s go.”

When we came out of the retrieval room, I felt eyes on us from all directions. Everyone seemed curious about what we were taking with us, but because there was no way for them to know which item we purchased out of the thirty-five, no one was eager to approach and start a conversation.
“Anyone following?”
“Not anymore. Judging by their level, they were just following out of curiosity.”
“Is that so?”
“Where are you planning to go?”
Where was there to go except there? “To the temple.”
After getting on a carriage heading out of Kommelby, we immediately entered the Church of Reatlas. It was nearing time for them to close their doors to the public but we made it just in time.
“I see you’ve come to erase the mark on your soul.”
“Here, a donation.”
“Yes. Will your comrade wait outside?”
“I will...”
I paid all the money we had left and removed the essence. The erased essence was the Corpse Golem, just like I decided in advance.
Come to think of it, I haven’t erased any essences at the temple yet.
I’d heard about it from others but the actual essence removal process, which I was experiencing for the first time that day, was much stranger than I expected.
Look at these mechanics! In the game, you just had to hit a few buttons on the keyboard.

A white light enveloped me and I woke up in a pure white space, naked. The blue dagger the priest had just handed me was in my hand, and around me were giant monsters. They were all locked in thick iron cages: an Ogre, an Orc Hero, a Storm Gush, a Manticore, a Bayon, and even my target for today, a Corpse Golem.
I stared at them for a while before using the dagger to cut the thread of light that connected the Corpse Golem to me.
Shaaaaaa!
When I came to, I was back in the temple.
“I feel very strange.”

“That is natural. One of the connections latched to your soul has fallen away, after all. Most people feel this way the first time, so no need to worry too much. After a few days, you will get used to the emptiness.”

“A connection has fallen away, huh?” It sounded like the exact kind of thing a priest of Reatlas would say, but I still found myself nodding. It wouldn’t be enough to say this listless feeling was simply a feeling of emptiness caused by a reduction in stats.
“Are you all right?” Amelia asked.
“Ah, it’s nothing to worry about. I’ll be fine after eating some meat.”
After finishing my business at the temple, Amelia and I returned to our inn. Then I took out the test tube I won at the auction.
“Amelia, are you ready?”
Amelia looked like she didn’t understand what I meant.
“The Fragment of Records Stone could react the moment I take this, so I’m just warning you to be prepared.”
I had met the GM and deposited my equipment in a safe. Amelia had followed her sister around and even took economic measures to make sure she wasn’t killed over taxes in the future.
So, if my hypothesis is correct... This should be the final piece of the puzzle.
I took out the Fragment of Records Stone from my sub-space and absorbed the essence.
Nice... this is why I swallow essences.

The feeling of fullness was so potent that it was difficult to feel the empty space left behind by Corpse Golem. As the light contained in the test tube was absorbed into my body, strength began to surge through me. Of course, it was much less intense than the time with the Ogre. Essences with that much default Strength were rare even at rank two.
Still, it’s the skill that’s important.
Relishing in the sensation, I slowly opened my eyes. Then, seeing the Fragment of Records Stone still sitting there, inert, I bit my lip in disappointment. “...This wasn’t it, either?”
Then what did I have to do now? Was I going to be stuck here for years? I wasn’t even able to relish in the joy of obtaining a new essence thanks to the anxiety.
“Yes, it’s about time we go back...” Amelia breathed out a sigh.
“Huh?”
When I tilted my head, Amelia smiled as if in reassurance. “Don’t worry, we will be able to return tomorrow.” She looked somewhat saddened by that fact.

chapters.title: Chapter 336: To the Future (6)
paragraphs: “We’ll be able to return tomorrow? What do you mean?”
Amelia avoided my eyes at that question. “It’s not a guarantee, but there’s something that’s been on my mind from the beginning.”
“From the beginning...?” My mind went blank for a moment.
Is that why she always looked uncomfortable every time we talked about how to get back?

It hit me that the feeling of wrongness I’d felt in previous conversations hadn’t just been my imagination, but there was still something I didn’t get. “If you had an inkling from the beginning, why didn’t you tell me earlier?” When I stared at her, Amelia glanced at me again and averted her eyes. In the end, I had no choice but to be blunt. “Is it... because you don’t want to go back?”
“That’s...” Amelia trailed off before shaking her head. “That’s absolutely not the case. I just thought it wouldn’t be bad to stay here a little longer...”
“What? But why?” My head tilted involuntarily, but when I thought through it calmly from Amelia’s perspective, it made sense.
“Th-that’s—”
“Ah, I see. Okay.”
“Okay...?”
“You felt bad about leaving your sister.”

When we left, Laura would have to live on her own for the next twenty years. It was natural that Amelia would want to do what she could from the sidelines to help her live a better life and at least see what kind of life it would be before she left.
“You could have just been honest with me. But I guess I might not have been trustworthy enough to you.”
“We’re comrades. Just tell me these things.”
“...I will. I’ll tell you first thing from now on.”

“Okay.” I quickly resolved the misunderstanding between us and moved on to the next item on the agenda, which might have been the most important part of this conversation. “So what’s your hunch that you think we can return so quickly?”
“Ah, that.” Amelia was brought back to reality by that question and explained what she was thinking. I listened intently, even asking some questions in the middle, and nodded.
Hmm, definitely...
It was plausible. No, to be honest, as soon as I heard it, I had a gut feeling that this was it—our last remaining task.
The next morning, after checking out of our inn early, we headed to a nearby restaurant. There was a place Amelia wanted to go. As for me, I just wanted to finish our job and hurry back.
“This restaurant closes down in twenty years... Ah, of course, if you think it’ll be inconvenient, I don’t mind returning right away.”
How can I not go if she’s going to put it that way? Yeah, we won’t have time to take a break once we get back. And she’s been busy working hard every day.

Amelia even looked embarrassed by her own request. It seemed she was self-conscious about expressing such a mundane desire, but in my mind, it was a positive change worth celebrating. It meant our bond had gotten strong enough that she felt like she could ask something like this.
“Let me know if there’s anything else you want to do.”
“Then... can we stop by the Arandeje Art Gallery in District Nine?”
“...Art gallery?”
“There’s a piece of art I want to see. Um... I’ve been wanting to see it but I couldn’t in the future. It seems it was sold to a wealthy nobleman.”
Anyway, for that reason, we headed to the museum after our meal. Amelia stood in front of the artwork she had been wanting to see and stared at it for over thirty minutes.
“...Do you mind if I look at something else?”
“Of course.”
Then we walked around the gallery and admired the other paintings and sculptures. To be honest, this was a bit unexpected.
I never suspected she had a hobby like this.
Just by the look in her eyes, I could tell she was genuinely having a good time. Well, that was a separate issue, though.
“Amelia, this is nice and all, but I’m starting to get hungry...”
A look around told us it was already midday, so we had a meal at a nearby restaurant.
“Yandel, can we stop by one last place?”
At Amelia’s request, we rode the carriage again. The place we arrived at was the Church of Reatlas’ orphanage, where Dwalkie stayed as a child.
This place and I have a strangely deep connection.

Rather than enter the building, we sat on a bench across from it and watched Laura through the window. Recovering from her stint in the hospital, she sat at a desk doing paperwork. Apparently, she had gotten a job at the orphanage through the priest.

“I thought she was just helping with chores but seeing as she’s doing paperwork, it looks like she’s already reading,” I said, before wondering aloud if there was a chance she hadn’t lost all of her memories.
Amelia just smiled ruefully and shook her head. “That couldn’t be the case.”
“How are you so sure?”
“Laura... didn’t know how to read.”
“...What?”
Then after just a few weeks of learning from the priest, she can already do administrative work?
This was a surprise but not something I couldn’t wrap my head around. People like her did exist.
“...She’s a genius.”
“I didn’t know my sister was this smart, either. I knew she had an extraordinary memory, but...”
“And the priest? Didn’t the priest who taught her find this strange?”
“That woman simply considered it a sign that her memories are coming back. My sister thought so too.”

Perhaps these sisters’ true talent didn’t lie in something like killing people. It was just their environment that made them that way. I wondered what Amelia would have grown up into if she had been born into an ordinary family. It seemed she liked art, so maybe she would have become famous for it.
“What is that look?”
Ah, was I staring too hard? “...It’s nothing. Anyway, how long are you going to watch? Looks like your sister is finishing her work now.”
“We should... go now.”
Once Laura finished her paperwork and put on her coat, we stood up.
Creak.
Then we picked the lock on the sewer system and walked down. This was the only way to Noark.
“I didn’t think I’d be heading down here again. Nothing bad will happen, right?”
“It should be fine. There’s another way to sneak in besides the cemetery.”

In the past, we went the official route and entered the city through a broker because we needed legal identities in Noark, but there was no need for that now so we instead entered illegally through a path Amelia knew about. Apparently, this path was connected to the castle.
“But what’s going to happen to Noark now?”
As we walked, we talked about Noark. After the big incident involving the palace, Orcules, the lord of the castle, and even the fourth faction (us), I was curious how things would play out.
“The new lord of the castle will be busy smoothing things over right now.”

“Smoothing things over?” Of course, I knew that this all ended up somehow being swept under the rug, but I was curious about the how. “They were the ones who teamed up with the palace and lost, how can they smooth that over?”
“Because Orcules needs this city too.”
I questioned why Orcules couldn’t just seize the city for itself, but it sounded like there was logic behind its decision not to.
“In order for the portal connecting Noark and the labyrinth to open, it requires the blood of the lord of the castle’s line.”

That was why the new lord of the castle killed everyone in his family as soon as he learned of his father’s death. It seemed he was worried the group would take over the city by turning his weaker brothers into their puppets.
He really is one heck of a dude. To think he could make that call at a moment like that.

After that, the new lord of the castle conceded a part of Noark to Orcules to bring about a truce, and gradually stabilized the city. This was according to the full account that would exist in twenty years.
“We’re here.”

After traveling through the sewer system for a while, we arrived at the castle and snuck away from the eyes of the guards to leave its walls. Passing through city streets that still smelled like smoke, we arrived in front of a small mansion.
“Yandel, will you wait here a moment? I will go alone.”
“I will.”
It was Amelia’s house.
There was no reason to knock. Back then, she never lived with the door locked. She had given up, had wanted to let whatever was going to happen just happen.
Creak.

Amelia opened the door and glanced around the house. Although it only had basic, simple furniture, that made it feel more like home to her. The house the alchemist grandpa provided for her remained in this condition up to the day she left it as an adult.

Sensing a presence, the girl huddled against the wall raised her head and looked at her. “Miss Emily...?” Her dull pupils began to shine. Amelia didn’t have any mind-reading abilities, but because this was her past self, she could clearly see what this girl was thinking, could see the rising hope that maybe her sister was alive. “I-Is...”
“Your sister is dead.”
“Ah...” When Amelia spoke sharply, the girl’s head dropped. The light that had appeared in her eyes disappeared.
Amelia forced the girl to stand her ground. “Before long, you will enter the labyrinth. And you will continue to live a life in the gutters, encounter many people, and kill them.”
“...So?” It seemed the provocative words had the desired effect, as the girl who looked like an empty doll raised her head in defiance.
Amelia reached out a hand toward her. “Promise me that you won’t kill any barbarians.”
“...Why should I do that?”
Amelia’s response left no room for doubt. “Later on, a day will come when you will think to yourself that choosing to keep this promise was the greatest stroke of luck in your life.”
At those words, the girl pursed her lips. Although she had no outward expression, Amelia knew what her younger self thought after hearing that.
I don’t know why this woman is telling me this but... I don’t think she’s lying. No, I think she’s actually giving me sincere advice. Like my sister, who’s no longer here...
Squeeze.
Amelia took the girl’s hand and clasped it. Then she squeezed and released it three times. It was something the sisters used to do when making promises.
“This... how did you...?”
Amelia did not answer the girl’s question. She just released her hand, turned around, and walked to the door.
Step, step.

When Amelia stood in front of the door again, the girl spoke up in an exhausted-sounding voice. “If... What if my life ends up in danger because I don’t kill that barbarian? Do I still have to keep my promise then?” It was a question typical of her younger self. Thinking of her older sister, who always told her how important promises were, she was not going to make a promise she could not keep.
But Amelia said confidently, “Then you can do as you want.”
Because that won’t happen anyway.
Then Amelia opened the door and left. “Ah, one last thing. Keep the door locked.” With that, she quietly closed the door and turned around.
She could see a barbarian waiting for her in an alley a little distance away. “Are you done talking?”
“Yes.”

The promise would be kept. Though her younger self did not know why they had worked so hard to keep her sister from dying, the fact that she had been on the receiving end of their help still remained. And her sister had taught her to always repay someone for their help.
“Amelia, that blond kid has been looking at me since earlier... Should we deal with him?”
Amelia followed the barbarian’s gaze and saw a boy with a familiar face. “Ah, no wonder he looked so familiar. Is that Guardweaver Drous?”
“Yes, that’s him. His real name is something else, though.”

Even as she spoke, Amelia felt strange. That boy would later tell her about the existence of a treasure called the Fragment of Records Stone. After seizing it, he would betray her and run off alone, turning into an enemy. That was when the scar on her ear was made, too, and was also the reason why she had been forced to make an oath to not commit murder inside Noark to the lord of the castle. Well, that agreement had an exact range of dates so it didn’t apply to this era. Anyway, that wasn’t important.
I feel nothing, almost to the point that it’s bizarre.
Even as she stared into that face, she did not feel angry. It was like the old fury and hatred in her heart had disappeared.
“Shouldn’t we do something?”
At his concern, Amelia realized what the source of her serenity was. “No, it doesn’t matter. Leave him.”
“Leave him?”
Looking back, even the pain she went through after getting entangled with that boy was all part of a single, continuous journey to meet this man in the future.
“...What the, why are you laughing all of a sudden?”
“I didn’t laugh.”
“You did laugh.”
Amelia ignored the barbarian’s persistent questions and walked forward.
The barbarian hurriedly caught up. “Hey, but why is it not activating?”
“I don’t know. I’m sure it will soon.”
“But what if it still doesn’t work?”
“Then we’ll have no choice but to live here together. I don’t mind that.”
“Uh... that’s kind of... Not that I don’t like you, but...” The barbarian trailed off like she had cornered him.
Amelia found herself chuckling again—not the awkward, stilted laugh she practiced in front of the mirror, but a real one.
Whip.
When Amelia stopped walking and turned around, she collided with the barbarian following behind her. At that moment, the world was dyed with white light.
Flash!
Iron Mask...?

It was a complete coincidence that the blond boy happened upon them. Wandering around the streets looking for a drunkard he could rob, these people entered his line of sight. Although he wasn’t wearing an iron helmet like the stories said, there was no other person in this city with such an enormous form. No, there were probably only a few in the whole world, unless they were barbarians.
More importantly, the red-haired woman next to him...

It was definitely the famous Iron Mask and Emily. The boy saw the woman enter a house and hid nearby to watch them. Before long, the woman came out of the house and rejoined Iron Mask. But did they sense his gaze?
The boy felt like their eyes met and ducked out of view. That was the moment a brilliant light burst out and brightened this underground city.
Flash!
The flash lasted a fleeting moment. When the light subsided, chaos overtook the deserted streets. Drunkards jumped up, and people inside nearby buildings hurriedly opened their windows.
“W-What was that?! That light!”
“...Magic?”
“It didn’t do something weird to my body, did it?”
Everyone looked around in bewilderment trying to figure out what had happened, but the blond boy who hid in the alleyway was different.
Iron Mask disappeared...
They disappeared, but the boy did not question why. The boy, who had had to survive in Noark from the moment he was born, ran forward, relying purely on instinct.
...This stone! The light came from this stone.
The boy picked up the rock that had fallen on top of their clothes and quickly hid in the alley.
“There! The light was from over there!”
“I saw it from that window over there. There was a light and people disappeared!”

The guard who came to see what the commotion in the middle of the night was all about started hearing witness statements. With them, he was able to figure out the identities of the man and woman at the center of the light.
“A man who looked like a barbarian and a woman with red hair?”
“Iron Mask! It was Iron Mask! The man the lord of the castle is looking for! Look through their belongings!”
“Identity tag! There’s an identity tag among the clothes!”
“Rank-six adventurer, Nivelles Enze... Is this Iron Mask’s real name? What about the woman’s ID?”
“Unfortunately, it wasn’t found!”
“Captain, they say some kid stole something that was left behind.”
“What? Where did they say they went?!”
The guards rushed to the alley the boy had disappeared into, but they were unable to find him.

chapters.title: Chapter 337: Snowball (1)
paragraphs: There was a strange chill running up my spine. When I opened my eyes at the sensation, my surroundings were dark.
Beep!
I heard something like a beep from somewhere nearby.
What is that? I don’t think I heard it wrong...
Slide.

I first lifted myself up. The surrounding area was very dark, but not to the point that it was hard to see what was up ahead. This was thanks to the white light coming from a jewel on the ground where I lay.
The Fragment of Records Stone?
That thought occurred to me so I quickly picked it up.
What, it’s just a light gem?

When I took a closer look, though, it was just an ordinary magical device, the kind every adventurer either saw or used at least once in their career. Its only function was to emit light. But why had it been left here? Even as I thought that, I held the light gem up high so that the light could reach further.
Shaaaaaa!
When the radius of the light broadened, my surroundings became more visible.
[Your location has been confirmed.]

Around me was a stone castle with no signs of life. Unlike Rafdonia, the road was not paved with stones. All the structures and shapes matched the exact spot I was in just a moment ago. If there was a difference, it was that it seemed that a lot of time had passed between then and now.
Hmm, it does look like we returned to the present... Then what about Amelia? Why isn’t she next to me?

Unlike the first time we went to the past, Amelia wasn’t there. Did she wake up first? True, I woke up before her on Farune Island. It was possible Amelia found this magical device somewhere and turned it on before leaving me. Which meant there was a good chance she was nearby.
“Ahem.” After coughing a few times to clear my throat, I shouted with all my might, “Amelia!”

The shout of a barbarian gifted with vocal cords of steel was powerful enough to reverberate and echo through the whole city. But even after waiting several minutes, there was no answer. The silence felt ominous somehow. Was I the only one who had been returned to our original time period through the Fragment of Records Stone? The possibility suddenly flashed through my mind.
I should wait for a while first.
I decided not to make any hasty moves for now and wait here.
But since it’s boring to just sit tight... I should check on my physical condition.
I started a self-inspection.
[Information Accuracy Rate: 83%]
[Your character information needs to be updated.]
[Updating and synchronizing...]

As expected, the essence I took in the past had remained unchanged. However, I calmly continued the inspection. Right after taking the essence, I stayed at the inn and hung around in the city for a day before coming straight down to Noark. There had been no time to take proper stock of it.
[The Essence of the Corpse Golem that was absorbed into your soul has been removed. Your Pain Resistance has decreased by -70. Your Strength has decreased by -15.]

As Pain Resistance dropped, some of my dulled senses recovered. Thanks to the +30 attached to the essence of Bayon, my Pain Resistance wasn’t completely gone, but a stat decrease of about 70 was something you could feel in the day-to-day. Of course, this wasn’t a huge problem. Aside from Pain Resistance, my overall stats had increased significantly.

[The Essence of Vol-Herchan has been absorbed into your soul. Your Physical Resistance has increased by +75. Your Natural Regeneration has increased by +40. Your Poison Resistance has increased by +120.]

Physical Resistance and Natural Regeneration were two essential stats for a tank, plus Poison Tolerance. Though there wasn’t Strength attached to this essence, it had more superior stats that could replace it.
[Your Muscle Mass has increased by +15.]

Muscle Mass was an ultra-rare stat that could only be obtained from certain monsters ranked three and above. Its effects were simple. For every point of Muscle Mass, your Strength value rose by 1 percent.
An additional 20 percent on top of my current stats means my Strength must be a little over 60.
With an additional +30 to Endurance, +20 to Vision, and +80 to Bone Strength, my total stats had been raised tremendously with just one essence. Conversely, some stats had been reduced.
[Your Agility has decreased by -30. Your Flexibility has decreased by -50.]
[Synchronization complete. Character log transmission has been resumed.]

Surprisingly, the decline in Flexibility was more noticeable than in Agility. My body felt much stiffer than before. Just the drop in Flexibility limited some movements that used to be possible for me, and the drop in Agility had slowed me down.
Still, compared to what I gained, you can’t even call that a drawback.

Stats were one thing, but the biggest advantage of Vol-Herchan’s essence lay in its skills. Its passive, Evolving Shell, granted different effects when your Physical Resistance stat reached 70, 350, 750, and 1500. For reference, the effect of stage one was as follows:
[Your Physical Resistance is over 70. You have been granted a 50% resistance against sword-type weapons thanks to Evolving Shell.]

This was an effect I used to call Sword Invulnerability and the reason why this essence was useful for countering auras. An aura was unconditionally classified as a sword-type weapon. With this one skill, auras’ absolutely wild ability to slash through 90 percent of your Physical Resistance was reduced to 45 percent.
Anyway, I need to turn on Giantization to reach stage two.

Taking just one more essence would unlock stage three when I was in a fully doped-up state, and stage four was detrimental to the mind in a way that I couldn’t even imagine now. That was because most magnifying buffs like this came with limits. As a key example, the Orc Sorcerer’s Frenzy ability, which tripled a user’s Physical Resistance for ten seconds, didn’t increase it above 300.
But... is she really not nearby?

After taking some time to check on my character development, I was starting to get anxious waiting for Amelia. I couldn’t be sure but it felt like almost two hours had passed, and I still hadn’t heard a single peep nearby.
“Hmm, this makes no sense...”
It didn’t add up for several reasons. By the time I opened my eyes, the light gem had already been emitting light. Even if it weren’t Amelia, the person who activated the device had to be nearby.
...I should look around first.

At this point, it would be foolish to stay put out of fear of missing each other, so I used the light gem to illuminate the way as I slowly walked. Come to think of it, there was something else that was strange here.
It’s kind of weird that this city is so empty in the first place.

In the present, the people of Noark had fled outside the castle walls to avoid an invasion from the palace, and the palace had occupied the city. But right now? It was so quiet that you’d be hard-pressed to hear an ant crawl.

“Could it be...?” A not-so-great thought came to me but this was not the time to jump to conclusions. I decided to focus on what I could take care of right now—for example, finding something to cover myself with.
Bang!
Entering the first inn I saw, I dusted off a tablecloth and wrapped it around my waist. There wouldn’t be clothes around here that fit me anyway.
Still, now I look like a civilized person.
This made me feel more like a human, but human greed knew no bounds.
...Is there anything to eat?

Once the “clothing” part of food, shelter, and clothing was resolved, hunger set in. I went around each room rummaging through drawers and cupboards. Lodgings like these were mainly used by adventurers, so I was able to find preserved food to satiate my appetite.
This is like being in some post-apocalyptic world.
Looking for food in a building that was basically abandoned felt weird.
“Then... should I look around some more?”
Now that my stomach was full, I exited the building and roamed the eerily quiet city. A long while later, I arrived at an empty Dimension Square, where a single barrack came into view.
The palace...?
The military barracks, which had a large rendering of the royal family’s emblem on the side, looked like it had been set up by the army that occupied Noark.
Slide.

I didn’t sense any presence anywhere nearby so I carefully pushed the cloth aside and headed in. But did they take everything with them when they retreated? Besides one large desk, the interior of the barracks was filled only with dust.
“Motherfu...”
That was the biggest red flag for me. I abandoned the possibility that time could have stopped in the present while I was in the past the moment I saw that the city had turned into a ghost town.
“But to think it wasn’t even a one-to-one ratio.”
I swept the desk with my index finger. There was at least an inch of dust. Considering Noark’s climate, this wasn’t an amount that could accumulate in just six months.
“...When the hell am I?”
My ominous premonition had become a reality, and a shiver was running down my spine when a familiar voice rang out behind me. “Finally...”
When I reflexively turned around, the face I had been so longing to see was standing there. “Amelia...!”

Amelia Rainwales, my SSR-Rank comrade I had just managed to recruit after twenty years. Okay, thankfully, I didn’t come back alone. It looked like she really did wake up first and had simply gone somewhere.

“Where on earth have you been? I thought you disappeared.” Glad to see her, I was about to start in on a lecture when my brain suddenly sputtered to a stop—and rightfully so. “What is that...? That equipment?” Unlike me, who woke up naked, Amelia was clearly not in the same boat. She was fully decked out in custom-made equipment.
Is it possible to farm equipment of this level just by waking up a little earlier?
Just as I was overcome by that strange feeling again, Amelia grabbed my wrist, her grip forceful. “I’ll explain as we go. Just follow me!”
If a car suddenly skidded to a stop by your side, the door opened, and someone shouted at you to get inside, what would you do? My answer would be “SAY YES.”
There must be a reason.
Even if it were an unfamiliar stranger, I would still at least consider it. But if that someone was my comrade, of course the wisest course of action would be to listen to them.
Huff, huff...!

So, although this was a little out of the blue, I ran down a dark street with all my might to keep pace with Amelia. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t curious, but it wasn’t like I couldn’t ask while running.
“Amelia... What is going on? At least give me a brief explanation!”
At my request, Amelia really did give me a brief answer. “Someone is chasing us.”
“What?”
“One of the members of the Seven Powerful, Blood Spirit.”
“What?”
“Sorry. This was my mistake. I didn’t know she’d already progressed to a point where she could deceive my sensors and track me down...”

My head was spinning. I didn’t understand a word she was saying. What the hell were the Seven Powerful? And who was Blood Spirit? I had a lot of questions, but time was limited, so I decided to ask about the most important thing first.
“Is she strong enough to defeat both of us?”
“She’s strong. If we fight her head-to-head, I will inevitably lose.”
“What? Who the hell is this person...?”

“I guess it’s only natural that you wouldn’t know. You knew that woman before she signed with the Elemental Ruler and went on her rampage.” As Amelia ran, she turned around and looked at me. “Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.”
“The reigning master of the pureblood and the ninth contractor of the Elemental Ruler. That is that woman’s name.”
My mind momentarily went blank. Pureblood? Elemental Ruler? “...Erwen?”
She’s gotten that strong? No, before all that...
“Just how much time has passed?” The question left my mouth without conscious thought, but I guessed she heard even that small whisper as she ran.
“Two years and six months,” Amelia answered in a bitter tone. “It’s been two and a half years since your alleged ‘death.’”
Holy shit...

chapters.title: Chapter 338: Snowball (2)
paragraphs: Two years and six months. Since I was in the past for about half a year, it was safe to say that time had passed at roughly a five-to-one ratio. The problem was that this ratio didn’t seem to be consistent.
“Amelia, did you arrive before me?” I asked, even though I was already half-sure that was the case, and she answered without missing a beat.

“Yes, it was a long wait. The magical device you’re holding now is one I left behind to immediately send a signal to me when you returned. Well... I didn’t know at the time that it would take more than two years for the signal to come.”
No wonder there was a beep when I woke up. That was the sound of the device turning on.

“Anyway, I’ll explain everything you want to know later, so hurry up and run for now.” Amelia seemed to want to stop chitchatting and focus solely on getting out of here, but I couldn’t abide by that so easily. I just couldn’t understand it.
