“Wait, if Erwen is the one chasing us, why do we have to run?”
“I don’t know about you, but that woman will definitely try to kill me. If we fight in this city, where my oath is active, I will inevitably lose.”
I get that you’ll lose, but...
“Why on earth would she kill you?”
“Because she thinks I have something to do with your death.”
“Ah...” At those words, a few more puzzle pieces slotted into place in my head. Nevertheless, I couldn’t make sense of Amelia’s actions. “But I can just talk to her and persuade her—”
“Persuasion won’t be easy.”
“...What?”

At my obvious confusion, Amelia stopped walking. Then she looked at me, her expression deadly serious. “Yandel, that woman isn’t the elf you used to know.” Her face looked like the face of someone remembering some kind of monster. Amelia seemed convinced that even I couldn’t control Erwen.
“Just what happened while I was gone...?”

“A lot of things happened. There is no time to explain at length.” Amelia firmly cut my muttering off at the pass and continued, “I doubt that woman still has the desire to do so anyway, but there’s only one thing in this situation that matters.”
“W-What’s that...?”
“That woman can’t protect you.”
It had been a really long time since I’d felt like this. No matter how much time we spent talking through this, it felt like my brain was making sense of none of it.
“...Protect? Me? From who?” I asked in a daze.

Amelia’s reply was once again curt. “From everything in this world.” What on earth did that mean? Just as I was about to ask a new question, Amelia called my name and stopped me in my tracks. “Bjorn Yandel. This is what happened two years ago.” Like a doctor giving her patient a terminal diagnosis, she said in a firm yet grim tone: “The palace announced you were an evil spirit.”
...What now?
It was a lazy afternoon in an office with warm sunlight streaming through the windows. However, the interior of the office was far from peaceful.
“...That is all.” After reaching the end of his regular report, Alex Halo, assistant to the deputy commander of the Third Magic Troop, kept his chin stiffly raised as he studied his superior’s face.

She was reading the document with a frown. “Hmm...” Once finished, his superior raised her head and gazed at him with that usual tired look in her eyes. At the sight, he quietly breathed a sigh of relief. He knew from past experience that that meant that, at least this time, he’d managed to pass muster. “That was well written. The contents of the report were good as well. The part about movement in Noark was especially interesting. Although it is just an assumption, it was still clever. It was at least better than the trash you’ve brought me thus far.”
Was that an insult or a compliment? Alex couldn’t tell, but his next line was the same either way. “Thank—”
“Is that what you thought I’d say?”
Oh, damn.
Gulp.

Her sudden change of tone made him swallow. His superior’s eyes were no longer riddled with fatigue. Or rather, they still looked fatigued, but they weren’t sleepy. They were the eyes of a predator that was staring at an herbivore right before chewing it up. If he kept quiet here, he’d really be screwed.
“If you tell me what needs to be corrected, I will correct it.”

“First, your writing style is an issue. Especially this part. I’m sure I pointed it out last time, but you made the same mistake. Don’t you know this gets sent to Commander Pevrosk upon getting my approval?”
“...I will correct it.”
“No, the contents themselves are the main problem in the first place. People from Noark might be living in the labyrinth? Why don’t you become an author instead? I don’t think you’ll sell, though.”
“I will correct it.”
“Are you a parrot? How are you going to correct it? That’s what you should be telling me.”
Whew, it’s finally over.
“...I will rewrite it.”

“Okay, then.” Her eyes finally shifted to another document and Alex turned around, struggling to hold the pieces of his shattered soul together. Then he closed the door carefully so as not to disturb his superior, who was already concentrating on a different task.
Creak.

He could see his superior through the gradually narrowing gap in the door. There was something about her tired yet hardworking air that captured people’s attention. Perhaps that was why, although the soldiers in the corps feared her, they for some reason didn’t hate her.
If she was just a little kinder, she would be much more popular...
She was the Golden Wizard, the deputy commander of the Third Magic Troop, though she was more famously known by the name Little Devil to her soldiers.
She definitely is good-looking—
“What are you doing? Aren’t you leaving?”
“E-Excuse me. Nia Rafdonia!” The startled man saluted and hurriedly slammed the door he had been carefully closing shut.
“Ha... when will he stop being useless?”

Staring at the closed door for a moment, the Golden Wizard Arua Raven sighed. Of course, it didn’t take long for her attention to shift. Moving her pen again, she tackled the pile of tasks on her desk one by one.
“That’s all for today.” After a while, Raven stretched her stiff muscles and glanced out the window. The world beyond the glass was already dark as the sun had set.
Since I finished all the important tasks today, I can come in early tomorrow to finish the rest...

Raven was unfastening her uniform button by button when she paused, laughed ruefully, and buttoned them all up again. She was going to wear these clothes to work again tomorrow—was there a point in changing? Just putting her officer’s coat on top, she tidied up her desk and finally checked the calendar.

It was December 2nd, New World 156. She still felt strange every time she looked at the calendar. It was about time things improved, but she still had moments like these where she suddenly froze and her heart sank. Because she had experienced loss, the short time she spent adventuring with him and his comrades seemed painfully joyful and brilliant by comparison. But those days would never come back.
It’s already been more than two years...

Even a few days wouldn’t be enough time to explain all the things that had happened in the last two and a half years in detail. But if she had to summarize it regardless, it had been a very long time, long enough to tear apart friendships she’d desperately tried to maintain, and long enough for a rank-six wizard from Altemion to join the Royal Military and climb the ranks to deputy commander of a corps.
Rattle.
Raven walked over to the window and opened it wide. A chilly winter breeze quietly blew in.
Shaaaaaa!
She recalled the last time she saw each of her comrades: the barbarian warrior woman Ainar Fenelin, the normally-not-reliable-but-trustworthy-when-it-mattered Abman, and even Missha.
It’s been more than half a year since I saw them last...

The comrade she had met with most recently was Abman, but even that was over half a year ago, and their conversation wasn’t as comfortable as before. They ran into each other by chance on the sixth floor and talked about what they were up to before awkwardly parting. Well, she did see Erwen two months ago, but she couldn’t exactly call her a comrade anymore. They only made eye contact and didn’t even say hello.
Still, it seems Mr. Abman and Miss Ainar are doing well...
Thinking of her old comrades, she quietly closed her eyes. Then she suddenly remembered the sorest spot.
“Miss Missha...”

She wondered where and how she was living now. Raven held out her hand to the open window. As she caught some falling snowflakes on her palm, she remembered the last conversation she’d had with Missha.
“Therrre’s something I have to tell you...”
It had been about two years and four months ago now, the end of that summer.

Intuition, what adventurers jokingly called their sixth sense, was surprisingly useful in day-to-day life. Although there was no clear data or basis, ducking because of an ominous feeling and having a claw pass right over your head a moment later was a common occurrence in this industry.
Thump!

But this wasn’t an innate sense. The more experience you had, and the higher your intelligence, the more likely your intuition was to be correct. Intuition was a product of hundreds of thousands of scraps of information accumulated like grains of sand in the subconscious. The difficult part was explaining to others how you reached the conclusion you had. The reasoning clearly dwelled in the unconscious mind.

“Something to tell me...?” At the time, Raven had ignored the ominous feeling she was getting and responded with a question. She didn’t know anything for sure yet, after all. It was common for intuition to simply end up being an error in judgment. No, you could argue it was much rarer for it to actually correspond to a genuine threat.
“Yeah... I have something to inforrrm... I mean, inform you...”
“Um, your speech...”
“Ah, that...? I’m going to try changing it. I can’t talk like this forrrever...”
“Ah... really? You’ve thought this through. Th-that’s good? I’ll cheer for you.”

On the surface, Missha’s change was a positive thing. Raven knew a bit about Missha’s situation. Apparently, she had damaged her tongue in the past and though the scar had healed over time, she’d ended up talking like that as a result of a psychological issue. Yes, she should have been happy for her.
Thump!
But why was her heart beating faster? It was making her more anxious. “...So, what did you have to say to me?”
“Well, actually...” Missha trailed off and averted her eyes before seemingly making up her mind and forcing the words out. “I want to leave the team.”
It was a retirement announcement. Raven did not bother asking for the reason. This wasn’t much of a surprise to begin with. “I see...”

To be honest, she figured this would happen. No matter who joined their clan, no one could fill the void left by that barbarian. Labyrinth exploration was suspended indefinitely anyway, and it was only natural that the team would eventually disband.

“Okay. If you think that’s for the best, there’s nothing I can say to that.” She didn’t really care about the team disbanding. What mattered was their friendship. Just because they weren’t going to enter the labyrinth together anymore, that didn’t mean their friendship had to end there. “So, what do you plan to do from now on?”
“I’m going to return to my family.”
“Ah, if you’re planning to take a break without a specific plan in mind, I agree that that’s—”
“And then I’m going to enter the labyrrrinth. No... enter the labyrinth.”

“...Sorry?” Raven couldn’t wrap her head around that. She said she was going to leave the team, but still enter the labyrinth? The back of her mind began to prickle with an inexplicable sense of betrayal, and she bombarded Missha with questions. “The labyrinth? With who? Did you already find a new team?”
But Missha did not answer them. She just changed the subject, a slightly sad tinge to her tone. “Before that, that’s not all I have to say...”

At those words, Raven felt the ominous feeling she had barely managed to subdue intensify again. Was that why? Her volume, which had risen as she got worked up, evened out to normal levels. “...Go ahead.” Perhaps because her head had cooled, her voice also came out sounding somewhat cold.

Missha kept avoiding her eyes and ended up fixing her gaze on the floor. When she spoke, her voice was incredibly quiet. “Just so you know, soon... there are going to be rumors that Bjorn is an evil spirit...”
“...Sorry?”
“Ah! I-It’s just a rumor! D-Don’t believe what anyone says! I-I just wanted to tell you that...”
Just what on earth is Miss Missha talking about? Has she lost her mind as a result of Mr. Yandel’s death?

While Raven was starting to wonder if they were having a rational conversation right now, on the other hand, another thought began to gain traction in her mind. This was her intuition, that sixth sense that had a way of reaching the truth before rational thought could. “So you’re saying you’re going to spread those rumors. Although I don’t know why you would do that.”
Instead of answering, Missha shuffled backward.

“Which is why you came to tell me in advance. Because you wouldn’t want us to remember Mr. Yandel as an evil spirit.” Raven took a step forward. “But you know what I think?” She had already figured out the source of this ominous feeling that had been gnawing at her since earlier. “You said there are going to be rumors that Mr. Yandel is an evil spirit... but it won’t just be a rumor, will it?” she demanded, grabbing Missha by the wrist.
This was an uncharacteristic oversight on her part, as there was no way a wizard could stop a martial-type adventurer with force.
“...Ugh!” Missha shook off her hand and ran away, and the next day, rumors that Bjorn Yandel had been an evil spirit spread throughout the city.
“Where on earth did she disappear to...?”
That had been the last she’d seen of Missha.

chapters.title: Chapter 339: Snowball (3)
paragraphs: My mind went momentarily blank. The world around me seemed to narrow like a crushed can, and the words Amelia left me with a moment ago kept ringing in my head.
The palace has announced you are an evil spirit.
The palace has announced you are an evil spirit.
The palace has announced you are an evil spirit.

The shock was not unlike how I imagined it would feel if dozens of strong men stood in a circle around me and bashed me over the head with hammers. If it weren’t for Amelia, I would have stayed there frozen for a long time.
“Yandel.”

“...Are you okay?” When I came back to myself, Amelia’s face was a few inches from mine. Her right hand, which looked incredibly small to me, was on my chest, and she was looking up at me with worry in her eyes.
“I get how you feel, but this is not the time.”
“Ah, sorry...”
Amelia snatched my wrist and dragged me forward. I started absently moving my feet behind her. Even I could see that her call was the right one here.
“I doubt that woman still has the desire to do so anyway...”
Erwen also knew I was an evil spirit. That meant it would be naïve of me to hope that she’d still see me as her comrade. The same likely went for the others. My jaw subconsciously tightened.
Yeah... So, the day has finally come.

Despite accepting this, I also had the following thought: You never know. Erwen was chasing Amelia because she was under the incorrect assumption that she had killed me. Whether I was an evil spirit or not, she might treat me the same way she did before. Yes, that possibility definitely existed.
“You don’t have to pull me now.” I removed Amelia’s hand and started running on my own.

No matter the possibilities, it was definitely as Amelia said. Erwen couldn’t protect me now. Even if she wanted to, Erwen was a part of the elf tribe. If she tried to help me, that would mean hurting her race, and Erwen was more likely to choose her people rather than make a decision for personal reasons.
...But that’s probably just an excuse.

Even as I ran, I smiled ruefully. That was because no matter how clever and cowardly you were, you couldn’t lie to yourself. The truth was, I didn’t want to see Erwen yet. To be more exact, I was afraid because I didn’t know what I’d hear when I did.
“Right! The chieftain said so too! Evil spirits must be killed as soon as they are found!”
Those were words Ainar once spoke to me.
“Yeah... I didn’t know this before, but after today, I know it for sure. Why everrryone says not to trust evil spirits...”
Missha’s words.
“It’s wise to get rid of them as soon as the opportunity presents itself. That man is a testament to what happens if you trust an evil spirit.”
Mr. Bear’s words.
Squeeze.

Each one had been a knife to the chest. Even just remembering it was making me feel this way, but experiencing it firsthand? If I had to see them doubt my sincerity, had to watch them hurl abuse at me for my deception with my own two eyes, what would the look on my face be then? If I could somehow avoid that situation now, I might be able to prevent that day from ever coming. And so I ran after Amelia.
“Yandel, this way!”

Leaving the empty square, we passed through the dark, underground streets and headed for the castle located in the center of the city. In addition to the one in the cemetery, there was another secret passageway in the castle. Getting there and heading aboveground as soon as possible was critical.
Screech!
We arrived at the castle and forced the gate open.
“Yandel, watch out.”
“Huh?”
In that short moment, Amelia shoved me through the crack in the gate from behind.
Stab.
An arrow that had been flying toward us without a sound sank deep into Amelia’s back. Her mouth fell open and she staggered from the impact, collapsing on top of me. I felt her hand touch my cheek.
“I’m... glad...”
“Glad? What are you—?”
“Her face... I don’t think she’ll... hurt you...”
I couldn’t understand what she was saying at all, but there was no time to ask. I hurriedly picked her up and stood.
“The... safe...” Amelia continued saying something to me, but she never got to finish her sentence.
Pop!
Because she exploded in my arms.
Plop, plop, plop, plop.
Dozens of pieces of her fell to the ground. The sight didn’t seem real at all.
“Ame... lia...?” Her weight disappeared from my arms, but I couldn’t even move my now purposeless arms down. I could only stand there, my mind struggling to catch up.
Amelia’s... dead? Like this...? And... because of Erwen...?
I was frozen for only a moment before I noticed something odd.
“Blood.”
There was no blood. An explosion that could blow a person to bits like this should have sent blood flying everywhere, but there wasn’t a single drop on my body.
Shaaaaaa!
Right when this hit me, Amelia, who had turned into hundreds of bits of flesh, disappeared in a flash of light like a dying monster.
[Amelia Rainwales’s Doppelganger has suffered too much damage. The summon has been dispelled.]
So, it had been a doppelganger made with Self-Replication.
Jeez, that startled me... I thought you really died. If you were going to come meet me as a doppelganger, you should have just told me that from the start.
Still unnerved, I started to grumble at Amelia, but I quickly set those thoughts aside. Now wasn’t the time for that.
I should think while I move.

I kicked off the ground and continued running. Because I memorized the route when I first followed Amelia into Noark, I knew the location of the secret passage. The problem was whether I’d be able to get there safely.
Dash.
There hadn’t been any arrows yet, but I wasn’t sure how long my luck would hold out.
If I fight... can I win?
I decided to assume the worst: the possibility that Erwen would be hostile and try to kill me. With that premise in mind, the memory of Amelia’s body exploding naturally entered my mind.
That ability...

The explosion had differed from ordinary explosions. There were no sparks and chunks of her did not fly in all directions like they would have with a grenade. Her body had just collapsed into hundreds of little pieces like a game of Jenga.
It has to be Rupture...

The effects of Rupture were simple. Regardless of whether it was an arrow, sword, or axe, as long as a blade could penetrate the target’s flesh and inflict a certain amount of damage, it dealt a fixed amount of additional damage proportional to key stats possessed by the caster. Much like with an aura, which was exclusive to humans, this ability ignored things like Physical Resistance and Mana Resistance..
On top of that, she said Erwen became a pureblood and signed a contract with the Elemental Ruler...
Whether that attack involved Rupture or not, I was starting to think my chances of winning in a one-on-one fight were low. With specs like that, she would have equipment on a similar level.
How can I beat her with my bare fists and no weapon?
Whoom!

As I sprinted forward with these thoughts rattling through my mind, the gem that had served as my light source in this dark, underground city lost its light. That wasn’t normal. I’d used light gems several times before. This magical device gradually lost its light when it ran out of mana—it didn’t go dark out of the blue like this.
...Is this a spirit of darkness?
I never thought she would be able to harness that attribute too. I soon stopped running.
Tap.

I was confident in my ability to memorize a path I’d once taken. If I paid close attention to my stride as I traveled, I would be able to find my destination even in the dark—if there weren’t someone chasing me, at least.
This escape is a failure.

The moment I came to that conclusion, I closed my eyes. Abandoning vision, which had become useless to me, I decided to focus on my other senses. Soon my sensitive hearing caught the sound of footsteps.
Step.
That was kind of a surprise. I thought for sure the first thing I would hear was an arrow flying at me.
True, she must want to speak with me, even if I am an evil spirit.
Even as I kept my weight on my toes so that I could book it at any moment, I also thought about one of the things Amelia said earlier.
“Her face... I don’t think she’ll... hurt you...”
She probably did see her face. Amelia was able to see at distances several times longer than I could. She could have made eye contact with Erwen, who had fired the arrow from beyond the darkness.
But how can you be so sure just by looking at her face?
I had no way of telling what Erwen was thinking as she walked toward me in the dark.
“Is that you, Erwen?”
There was no answer. The sound of footsteps stopped.
Thump!
There was a silence where all I could hear was the echoing boom of my heart.
“Mister.” The light gem flickered on again as a name I hadn’t heard in a really long time rang out from the dark.
Shaaaaaa...
The light spread in all directions and illuminated my surroundings. Thanks to that, I was able to see for myself why Amelia said she was glad, why she was so certain this girl wouldn’t hurt me.
“Is that... really... you, Mister...?”
She had been able to tell just from her expression, at least in that moment.
“Yes.”

The moment I answered in the affirmative, the look in Erwen’s amber eyes seemed to shift violently, fragments of countless emotions flickering through them: joy, gladness, anticipation, anxiety, fear... and distrust.
“H-How... Th-they clearly said you died...”
“Ah, it just happened.”

“W-What do you mean ‘it just happened’? You can’t just stop there for something like...!” Erwen’s voice momentarily rose as she grew heated,, but she suddenly went silent as something occurred to her. “...Is this that woman’s doing?” she murmured. The look in her eyes turned sharp. “Who are you?”
Uh, I didn’t think her mood swings would be this bad...
It was at that point that I started worrying that she might genuinely harm me, but I answered her anyway, making an effort not to let that show. “Who else would I be? It’s me, Bjorn Yandel.”
“Liar.”
“What, will you believe me if I use Giantization?”

“Yeah, try it.” Her terse tone of voice was incredibly foreign to me, but I cast Giantization without argument. “W-What... is it really you, Mister?!” Erwen’s tone returned to normal. That only lasted a short moment, though.
“I told you—”
“No, I won’t trust you on that alone.”
“Try something else.” The tearful and happy Erwen instantly toggled back to Cold Mode and I quickly used Leap. “R-Really you...!”
“Yes, I’m glad you believe me now—”
“Did you think that’s what I would say? That’s not enough.”

We repeated the same process several times. It seemed Erwen was only going to be satisfied after checking all my essences, as she continued to make demands. When she told me to use Flesh Burst, a chill ran down my spine.
“...So you were fake after all?” Those eyes filled with mania and murderous intent genuinely made my stomach churn.
I told her that I erased that essence and instead proved my identity using information only the two of us knew.
“What you gave me when we first met.”
“A Licho leaf.”
“The inn where we spent our first night together.”
A pause.
“You can’t... answer that...?”
“I-It was an inn called Garlic and Salt.”
“Too late.”
“No, you started with ‘our first night together.’ We only went there to test out an essence...”
“Hmm.”

After walking down memory lane for a while, stories only the two of us knew flowing between us without hesitation, her mood swings lessened until she completely let go of her doubts. Of course, it was impossible to know when she’d get pissed off again and nock a bow between my eyes, but that was the case for now.
“M-Mister...!”
“Long time no see. I heard it’s been two and a half years already?”

It had taken a while to finally be able to greet her properly. Erwen lowered her bow as if she’d never raised it in the first place and clenched her fists in apparent frustration. “What... took you so long?! You were alive the whole time...! Why didn’t you come to see me?”
Ah, I guess it could look like that from her perspective. It’s not like I didn’t want to come back...
“I had extenuating circumstances,” I quickly replied, worried she might get angry again.
“By extenuating circumstances... are you talking about the declaration?” Erwen asked cautiously. “That you’re an evil spirit?”
This was perhaps the most critical part of this conversation. It was a hurdle that had to be overcome at some point or another.
But just as I was wondering how to approach the problem, Erwen spoke, her voice soft. “Idiot,” she murmured. “There’s no way I would care about that...”
“...Does that mean you don’t believe the royal declaration?”
Even as I asked that, I felt both guilt and relief. Of course Erwen would have decided that she didn’t believe it. The fact that she was talking so casually in front of me right now was proof enough.
“No? I meant whether the declaration is true or not, that doesn’t matter to me,” she said like I was being deliberately obtuse.
I couldn’t help but tilt my head. “Huh?”
It seemed she realized an explanation was necessary at that point. Erwen began walking me through it step-by-step. “Mister, we met as adults, right?”
“Uh, right?”
“And evil spirits appear on the day someone becomes an adult.”
“So what does it matter if you’re an evil spirit or not?”
“...I-Is that how it works?” I asked, unable to hide my nerves.

Erwen suddenly came up to me and grabbed my hand in a tight grip. “When you risked your life to save me in the cave, taught me all the things I didn’t know, and after Daria died... the person who helped me back on my feet was you, Mister. It was all you.” The sensation of her hand against mine felt particularly warm. “No matter what anyone says, you are Bjorn Yandel to me.”
So, there are people who can think this way.

Many things I could say came to mind, including thank you, but I couldn’t bring myself to voice any of them and just kept my mouth shut. Erwen probably didn’t know how much comfort she had just given me with a few short words.
“But...” Erwen then let go of my hand. When she spoke, it was with a look in her eyes and a tone that seemed to suggest we were back at square one. “Are you really Mister?”
I felt like I was going to lose it.

chapters.title: Chapter 340: Snowball (4)
paragraphs: In a mountainous area on the seventh floor called the Dark Continent, shrouded in the black fog that characterized the region, five adventurers were preparing camp.
“Scholar Gramps, how long will the blocking magic circle take?”
“It will take about ten minutes.”
“Still? Ugh, this is why we need a priest.”

At the blond man’s grumbling, there was a subtle change in the old man’s expression as he drew the magic circle. Although it wasn’t too noticeable, that emotion was displeasure. “If you’re that dissatisfied, why don’t you put a priest in the remaining slot?”
The blond man smirked at the old man’s words. “Gramps, you think a priest will join our team?”
“There are priests of Karui too.”
“I refuse to take halfway healers,” the blond man muttered, taking his eyes off the old man to stare into the fog.

Although a pitch blackness was blocking his view, the man could see the shape of a monster cutting through it and coming toward them—the rank-five beast-type Dieville Wolf. Although these monsters usually travelled in packs, it seemed this one had lost a battle for dominance and fell behind.
The blond man spoke to the woman in his characteristic light tone. “Kitty, you take care of that.”
“I told you not to talk to me like that.”
“Touchy. Your answer?”
At the man’s question, the red-haired beastwoman, Missha Karlstein, raised her swords without a word.
Woof, woof...!
She leveled her swords at the monster that emerged from the fog. Two cuts were enough.
Stab!
The moment the sword in her left hand pierced the monster’s skin, a chill swirled around it and froze the monster’s body solid starting from the stab wound.
Bang!
Then, the sword in her right hand shattered the frozen monster to pieces.

“Oh, rank fives can be taken down with a one-hit combo now?” Missha didn’t reply and returned to her original spot. The blond man grumbled at her like she was being unfair. “Hey, why are you only cold to me?”
“You really don’t know?”
“You think I would? I take you around with me and feed you essences, grow your skills, and even teach you how to save your husband. Why do you have so many complaints—”
“Stop.”
“Just look at the way you speak. You were cute when you used to purr—”
“I said stop.”

When Missha shot him a cold look, the blond man shrugged and sat in front of the bonfire. “Ah, talking about your husband is off-limits, right? Sorry.” After giving an apology that had no sincerity behind it at all, the blond man started chatting with their other comrades as if nothing had happened.
Missha quietly contained her boiling rage.
...Baekho Lee.
That was the name of the blond man seated in front of her, the only person the palace was wary of, and a talented man who always outsmarted Noark.
Crackle, crackle.
Watching the sparks fly from the fire at random intervals, Missha thought back to their first meeting.
It had been like a hand extended to her by the devil, especially in that it was an offer she couldn’t refuse.
“What if I told you there’s a way to bring Bjorn Yandel back from the dead?”

That day, Baekho told her that there was something called the Stone of Revival on the ninth floor. With it, it was possible to bring back someone who was lost. Of course, it wasn’t a well-meaning offer made without the expectation of getting something in return.
“In exchange, there’s something you need to do for me.” Baekho gave her two conditions. “First, testify that Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit.”
“...What?”
“I heard you were pretty much lovers? If you testify, it won’t sound like complete nonsense.”
She couldn’t understand the logic behind the first condition at all. “Don’t be ridiculous! That means Bjorn will have nowhere to return to even if he comes back alive! Why would I—?”
“So, you’re not going to do it?” Baekho cut her off with a smirk.

Even as she was seized by the desire to get out of there immediately, Missha suppressed it by biting her lip. The reason was simple. She had a gut feeling that if she said one more word here, he would take the offer off the table and leave.

“Good girl.” Smiling at Missha’s patience, Baekho continued speaking in a more generous tone. “Now, I get you must be confused, but I’m not just making a thoughtless suggestion. If my plan goes well, I can completely destroy the palace.”
“...The palace?”
“To get through the Gate of the Abyss, it looks like I’ll have to sort out the palace first, and the first step is revealing that Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit.”
This bastard.
Those words threatened to fly from her mouth, but Missha held them back.
“Anyway, so what I’m trying to say is... once the palace disappears, it won’t matter whether he’s an evil spirit or not.”
“...And if that plan fails?”

“Then I’ll take responsibility and help you escape the castle walls. I heard it’s a better place to live than people think. Well, if you don’t want that either, I’ll make you new identities so that you can live together secretly on the outskirts of the city. Don’t you think it’s a pretty good plan?”

It didn’t matter whether it was good or not. If what he told her about that stone was true, she didn’t have a choice. It was better to be alive than dead, and in a world without Bjorn, she was as good as dead.
But Missha wasn’t foolish enough to sign on right away. “...Tell me the second condition.”

“Ah, that? It’s simple. I need you to help me. I’ve been needing a dual-wielding ice swordsman.” Missha flinched at the man’s calm response. He was definitely smiling, but the look in his eyes made it seem like he regarded her more as an object rather than a person.
“...Why does it have to be me?” Missha felt an inexplicable pressure and had to fight to get the words out. She was curious about this man’s hidden intentions.
The answer she received was different from the one she expected. “Just a whim.”
“...A whim?”

“Yeah, it doesn’t actually have to be you. It’s not like I can’t create rumors that Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit without you, and I’ll even have to find you the Stone of Revival, which makes it an even bigger hassle...” He spoke like this was all a huge inconvenience for him. Just when contempt was boiling from the tips of her feet to the top of her head, Baekho grinned at Missha. “Ah, but you do have one pro to you. You have a reason not to betray me.”
That was the reason he had come to this place.

Erwen’s question nearly drove me to drink as it seemed I would have to start verifying my identity again, but it wasn’t too hard to dispel her suspicions this time. I just had to tell her the truth from the very beginning. I told her about the Fragment of Records Stone activating on Farune Island, arriving in the city twenty years in the past, and my six-month struggle to return to my original time. For reference, any mention of evil spirits was thoroughly omitted from this explanation.
“No matter what anyone says, you are Bjorn Yandel to me.”
It wasn’t easy to lie to the first person to ever say this to me, but I had no choice. This was best for both of us.
“It is an ability that will be of great help to you too when it comes to keeping your identity hidden in the future.”

I had received a gift from Auril Gavis. If it worked properly, it wouldn’t be impossible for me to “prove” to anyone who asked that I was not an evil spirit. But if Erwen were interrogated instead and the fact that I had confessed to being an evil spirit were revealed to the world? Things would get very troublesome. No one could know for sure how things would unfold in the future. And so, it was absolutely appropriate to keep these scenarios in mind and exercise caution.
But did Auril gift me this because he already considered the possibility of this happening?
The question came to mind as this was the first bit of news I’d heard since I returned to the future, but there was no way of finding out for sure right now.

“Hmm... then you’re not an evil spirit?” It seemed Erwen was telling the truth when she said she was not interested in my status, as she didn’t pry into the matter. But she instead stubbornly pursued another line of questioning. “Um, then...”
“Hmm?”
“You and Amelia Rainwales, you two were together for over half a year...?”
“Th-that’s right?”
“And she, like, fell in love with you for saving her life and said she’ll be your comrade?”
“She didn’t fall in love with me or anything like that, she was just repaying—”
“If she was just repaying you for a favor, then I guess you can abandon her now, right?”
Abandon? Amelia? Why is that suddenly the conclusion you jump to?

Unlike before, the conversation with Erwen was now a bit difficult to follow. While I was carefully choosing my words, Erwen spoke first. “Even if there were special circumstances, she’s still a plunderer from Noark. How can you trust a woman like that?”
“But Amelia is a very useful talent...” I trailed off, then clammed up.

For some reason, Erwen was smiling at me with a peculiar look in her eyes. “Haha, Mister, you’re cute...” This was probably my first time hearing that compliment since entering the body of a barbarian. It was only when I stared that Erwen noticed me looking and covered her mouth with her hand like she was embarrassed. But I guessed she had something she really wanted to say. “Mister, don’t worry about that woman. You have me. I’m really strong now, enough that it doesn’t even matter if she’s gone. I make good money and I also have subordinates I can mobilize with a single word.”
“Oh, really...”

“Yes. Of course, I know what you must have been thinking. Placed in a situation like that all of a sudden, you would have needed someone to rely on.” She spoke as if she thought I couldn’t live without a woman. While I was wondering whether I was just being sensitive, Erwen grabbed my hand and said something that clearly indicated her memories were warped. “It’s possible that woman was quite trustworthy there. L-Like I was when you first met me... But don’t worry. You have me now.”

Honestly, her words only left me dumbfounded. It was true that we were close, but were we this close? Enough to say something like that without hesitation, despite meeting for the first time in two years and six months?
“I’ll protect you from now on. Yeah, so...”
“So...?” I asked, an ominous feeling coming over me, and Erwen grinned.
“Next time you see her, make sure to kill her.”
“Rainwales, that woman!”
I was starting to understand why Amelia said what she did earlier.
“Yandel, that woman isn’t the elf you used to know.”
That innocent twenty-year-old elf was no more. All that was left was an elf with extremist tendencies who seemed to have a loose screw in her head.
If I let her jerk me around here, it’s all over.
I instinctively realized that laughing her suggestion off would be the same as signing my death warrant.
“Behel—aaah!”

The first thing I did was shout, because whenever I did I felt like I could do anything. I didn’t know what Erwen had gone through in the past two years, but she didn’t even blink despite my sudden yelling. No, on the contrary, she clapped happily.
“Yay! It’s Mister!”
...Jeez, so anticlimactic.
I forced myself to ignore Erwen’s reaction and spoke in a firm tone. “Erwen, I’m not going to kill Amelia.”

But as expected, Erwen wasn’t going to take that lying down. “Pardon? Why not? Secrets are best kept between fewer people, right? The Fragment of Records Stone too. I think we need to hide the fact that you’re alive for now, so there’s no reason to keep that woman alive—”

“Stop.” When I cut her off, Erwen tilted her head with an expression that told me she really couldn’t understand my logic. “I’ll take care of the matter with Amelia, so don’t say anything like that again. Got it?” Sticking to my guns, I stared Erwen down until she answered.
Erwen looked around with a somewhat startled expression, almost like she was trying to figure out who I was scolding before her shoulders dropped. “...Okay. I won’t.”
Whew. Based on this, I think I can control her somehow.
After settling the matter of Amelia, I discussed a few things with Erwen before taking the secret passage leading aboveground.
“Don’t worry. No one will see you.”

Once we reached the overworld, Erwen used a spirit of darkness to conceal me and we headed to an inn. There weren’t a lot of people out on the streets in the middle of the night, especially those skilled enough to detect Conceal.
“It’s small, but please stay here tonight. I’ll get you a better place by tomorrow...”
“Better place...?”

This was already a penthouse suite with four separate rooms attached to it. It was hard to believe those words were coming from Erwen, who once traveled an hour to have a thousand-stone meal just because it was cheap and tasty, but I guessed this was what you called the passage of time. It would be best to adapt to the changes as they came.
“Okay then, let’s go in!”
“...You too?”
“Of course? I booked it with my own money.”
Uh, that’s true.

While I was rendered speechless by her logic, unable to come up with a retort, Erwen shoved me into the room. “Mister, do you remember this?” She suddenly pulled a bottle of alcohol out from her sub-space. I felt like I was being given a new test.
Remember...? Ah, I remember.
“Our first return drink.”
Thankfully, that seemed to have been the right answer, because Erwen laughed and said, “I knew you would remember!” But then she said something I didn’t want to hear. “Isn’t this so romantic?”
“Romantic...?”
“This drink. I’ve been saving it to drink by myself once I kill all the bastards and bitches I need to kill. Ha, but to think I’ll be drinking it with you...”
What on earth has happened to this girl? If this is the state she’s in, I’m starting to worry about the state of the others...
“Okay, let’s have a drink.” Since keeping my head on straight after a drink was my specialty, I accepted Erwen’s offer.
She still can’t hold her liquor all that well.
Before long, Erwen was drunk and lying on the bed. At the sight of her sprawled out defenselessly, I worried whether she was like this in other places too.
No, I shouldn’t worry about her.
I chuckled and sat on the chair by the window. I could now see why husbands craved alone time so much once they got married.
It’s peaceful...

Taking a moment to relish in the silence in front of the moonlit window, I officially began sorting through my thoughts. The amount of information I had gotten during my conversation with the drunken Erwen was considerable, so now I had to organize it.
Raven was in the Third Magic Troop. Mr. Bear had joined a clan to make a living. She didn’t know anything about Missha. And Ainar...
If all goes well, she will be the easiest to bring back.
I sighed and shook my head. Actually, there was a much more important hurdle than reuniting my scattered clanmates. All quests had to be completed in a certain order, after all.
She said the palace confirmed that I am an evil spirit a few months after the rumor spread...
Let’s take care of that first.

chapters.title: Chapter 341: Snowball (5)
paragraphs: Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit. It had only been a rumor at first, but as time passed, even the palace acknowledged that fact. Of course, refuting it wouldn’t be too hard. I just had to set up a forum for me to prove myself and use Auril Gavis’s gift there. Then I could salvage my reputation and my status as a baronet.
But... Something is off.

The more I thought about it, the warier I felt. And rightfully so, because a dead person had immunity; not literally, but in moral terms. Since there was no point in asking the dead to answer for their sins, people didn’t usually dig deeper into or pay much attention to said sins. Yet it had happened anyway, a situation where a dead person was rumored to be an evil spirit and the palace had confirmed it.
I should lie low for a while...

This wasn’t normal. I didn’t see it as an act of god or something coincidental like that. The reason the rumors had spread was because someone wanted something. And since the palace acknowledged it, it would be smarter to assume they had done so for a reason.
But the problem is, I have no idea what that reason is.

I didn’t have enough information, and so it was dangerous to go to the palace and say, “I’m back alive,” and take the stand to defend myself. Not everyone would welcome the news of my survival. In fact, there could be someone out there who would see my survival as unfortunate enough to want to neutralize me altogether. If that person was in the palace, I was as good as dead.
...Standing on that stage can come after I at least figure out what’s going on.

Soon, I decided on my plan for the time being. First things first: collect information without informing anyone of my return. Clearing my name and restoring my noble status and reputation would come after that.
“Hah...” After getting my thoughts somewhat in order, I let out a long breath and checked on Erwen, who was laying on the bed.

It seemed I would need her help for the time being. Right now, I didn’t have the money to even buy clothes, let alone find a place to stay. It was impossible to conceal my very recognizable appearance to go out and gather information in the first place. To be honest, her attitude today was very uncomfortable...
But seeing as she’s passed out after drinking so little, it seems her old self hasn’t completely disappeared.
Just as I was watching Erwen sleep like an angel with that thought in mind, her eyes opened. “How long are you going to stare out the window like you’re waiting for someone?”
Huh...? She wasn’t sleeping?

The particularly calm, peaceful moonlit night had passed and as soon as it was morning, Erwen put on her jacket and got ready to leave. Clearly anxious, she issued the same warning several times. “You cannot go outside while I’m out. I have a way of finding out if you take even one step outside. Okay...?”
I was curious what that method of hers was, but I just nodded and asked where she was headed. “Are you going back to your holy land?”
“Yes. I should stop by.”
True, I heard she became the pureblood of the elves and made a contract with the Elemental Ruler. She had tribal duties and responsibilities—
“Because I’ll need more money from now on.”
“I’ll get rid of everything I need to there and find a better house for you within the day. This place... is n-not the best, is it?”
“...In what way?”
“I mean... it’s not that I don’t like it, either... but it’ll be better to start off in a better place...”
...You know, I’m just going to interpret that as this inn having too many cons to use as a hideout.
“Then... I’ll be back?”
“Ah, wait. Can I ask you for a favor?”
“Sorry? Favor? Do you want me to buy you meat?”

“No, not that... Not that you shouldn’t buy meat. Anyway, this is a different favor.” I asked Erwen to stop by the bank and check on my safe, and if something was inside, to bring it to me with no questions asked.
“Okay. See you later, Mister!” Erwen readily accepted my request and left. She didn’t seem all that reliable, though.
She’ll bring it back all right... right?
I felt oddly anxious, but there was nothing I could do. If I went out, someone would definitely recognize me.
Still, I’m glad Amelia came back to the present first.

It was only last night that it hit me that the safe’s storage period of twenty-two years had been exceeded, much to my bewilderment. Thankfully, it seemed Amelia had taken appropriate action. Otherwise, she wouldn’t have left me that command.
“The safe...”
She probably went there in advance and extended the storage period. She was truly a trustworthy woman.
Looks like she’s gotten even stronger in that time too.

The summon radius of a doppelganger created through Self-Replication was typically five yards, and once summoned, its range of motion was a hundred yards from the original body. But it didn’t seem like Amelia’s main body was in the area during the fight yesterday at all. Simply put, she must have acquired a new skill. For reference, three skills worked well with Self-Replication and could get rid of the above restrictions. But considering Amelia usually heeded my advice in the past, there was a high chance she’d absorbed the one I recommended.
Dual Rule.
So it would be logical to assume she took the essence of a Twin Hydra and gave her doppelganger independence since I explained the cons of the other possible skills to her at length.
Anyway, I should get some sleep...
I was very tired since I stayed up pretty much the whole night, so I headed over to the bed and closed my eyes.
“Mister, wake up.”
“Ah... you’re here...”
When I opened my eyes again, I saw Erwen. The sun was slowly setting outside the window. A glance at the clock told me that about eight hours had passed.
“Did anything happen outside that I should know about?”
“Were... you worried about me?”
No, I was sleeping.
“Of course.”
“...Hehe, this is kind of nice.”
“Ahem, so, how did it go?”

“Ah, that? I had some money saved up so I was able to find a suitable house! Since there wasn’t much time, there were some things about the house I didn’t like, but don’t worry! I made sure to fix those parts.”
“Really? That’s good.” I didn’t really care about the house so I cut off that particular conversation there and checked on something more important. “But... what about the bank? How did it go there?”
“Ah... the bank...?” Her response was very vague.
That made me nervous. Was she unable to open the safe? I was sure I told her the right code. Or wait... did Amelia not get an extension?
Just as all sorts of scenarios were running through my mind, Erwen handed me a piece of paper crumpled into a ball from her pocket. “Here.”
“Uh...” I subconsciously took it, but I didn’t really understand what it was. “What’s... this...?”
“What was in the safe. You asked me to get it for you.”
“Was there a hammer in there? About this big—”
“There was nothing like that. There was only that letter.”

“...Letter?” Only realizing what the paper ball was right at that moment, I carefully unfolded it. Although there was no sender, it wasn’t hard to figure out who wrote it: Amelia Rainwales. “...Can I read it?”
“As you wish.”
After asking Erwen to give me a second, I read the letter as quickly as possible. Despite it being full of wrinkles, it wasn’t hard to read. To briefly summarize, the letter read as follows:

I’ve taken some measures but in case something goes wrong and we can’t meet, I’m leaving this letter. I extended the storage period, so if you leave me a note with your current location here, I’ll come find you. Oh, and one last thing. Kraul’s Demon Grinder is...
Unfortunately, the letter ended there. It seemed the last sentence had torn off as it was crumpled.
You left out the most important part!
I asked Erwen if she knew what the missing bit was, but she just answered that she didn’t know. Apparently, she just skimmed it so she didn’t remember.
My hammer...!

My heart broke, worried something might have happened while I was away, but I decided to think as positively as possible. Yes, the future wasn’t set in stone yet. It could simply be that Amelia had it. If that wasn’t the case, I’d be able to find out what was going on once I wrote her a reply.
“Um, Erwen...” After burning the letter to maintain secrecy, I called for Erwen. I was going to ask if she could put the reply in the safe for me.
“It’s okay. It’s not your fault that you received a love letter, Mister. You can’t help who you are.”
“Huh?”
“Ah, by the way, I made sure to dispose of the safe just in case.”
“You’re not sad, are you? That you can’t contact that woman.”

I should have been angry and demanded to know why she did such a thing—I was someone who knew how to get angry when I needed to. Yeah, that was what I should have done, but for some reason, I found myself agreeing with her instead. “O-Of course not!” It was an instinctive reaction. If I were to tack a reason onto it in hindsight, it could have been that I was worried about what would happen if Erwen and I had a falling out.
“Hehe, right?”

Anyway, after that, I ate the food Erwen brought for me and soon it was nighttime, the best time to use the power of the spirit of darkness. We concealed ourselves like last time and headed to the house Erwen had found.
“You... found this place in one day?” It was a single-family home with high fences and a private yard.
“I told you. I have a lot of money.”
I mean, still, if she managed to buy a mansion like this in one day, that means she bought it at full price without even bargaining... If that’s the case, can’t she just buy me a new Demon Grinder?
I followed Erwen into the mansion.
Boom.

As the thick iron door closed and the bright lights of the mansion turned on, I realized there were no windows. No, to be precise, anything remotely window-like had been covered with thick boards. I had noticed it looked dark from the outside, but I thought she had just drawn the curtains.
“Um... Erwen...?”
“Yes?”
“Why are the windows...”
“Ah, these? It’ll be an issue if someone peeks in from the outside...” Erwen said with a smile. “And you won’t be going outside anymore, anyway.”
Gulp.

“Still... was it necessary to put up planks...? If people looking is the problem, there are curtains, and the fence outside looked very high...” Sensing something had gone wrong over the course of this conversation, I hastily offered a sensible rebuttal, but my logic fell on deaf ears.
“No, you don’t really understand, Mister, what a great—no, dangerous situation this is! I’m not just talking about you. What will happen if I get caught hiding you?”

“...That would be a huge problem.” That was such a valid response that I had no choice but to agree with her. Not only would it be an issue, but she could lose everything she’d worked so hard to achieve up to this point.

But did my reaction boost her confidence? “Right? So this is an unavoidable measure! Because you’re a troublemaker, Mister. I have no choice but to watch over you.” Erwen’s voice grew louder, though not for long, of course. “Oh, no... your shoulders are drooping...” When I hung my head, Erwen stamped her feet like someone who had just seen something incredibly sad and carefully proposed a compromise. “It must be tough, but cheer up... I’ll let you take walks in the garden at night sometimes. Okay?”
“Really...?”
“Yes! Of course, assuming I’m next to you.”
That was how my life in isolation began. Time passed, and soon it was midnight on the 15th.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]

chapters.title: Chapter 342: Comeback (1)
paragraphs: Hansu Lee’s room felt familiar yet unfamiliar at the same time.
It... feels like it’s been a long time.
Glancing around for a moment to see if anything had changed, I sat on the chair and moved only my toe to turn on the computer.
Whirl!
My goal in the community today was simple. As always, gathering information was a top priority. The difference was that, unlike usual, said information had been accumulating for two and a half years.
I should check the bulletin boards first.

The Round Table, which could be said to be the main event of my nights at the community, would only open in three hours, so I used the mouse to check various bulletin boards instead. It was quite a cumbersome task. To get the gist of what had happened while I was gone, I had to go through the long list chronologically.
[Wow, anyone been to Bjorn Yandel’s house?]
I went there with some people he helped on the first floor and it felt strange to see the flowers piled up. It really hit me that he was dead too. His comrades are totally mourning.
When I saw that post, I paused. Hmm, since there’s a lot of talk about me here, I can probably start reading from here.
tetyys: Why the fuss over one dead NPC?
└Sogeking33: Fair, no one would care if a punk like you died, right?

└SoDamnToxic: Candidate for the next barbarian chieftain, first adventurer-turned-nobleman in ten years, and rumor has it that the palace is going to send knights to hold the funeral procession to commemorate the death of a hero... It makes sense why bastards with inferiority complexes would flock to this.
Ki11Humans77: What a waste. I heard he created a new clan and was curious how it would grow.

After checking the comments on the first post I clicked, I pressed the back button. Then I moved through the pages slowly to read through the posts one by one. One month, two months, three months... as time passed, the bulletin board was flooded with posts focusing on the hottest topics at the time.
Just look at the stories about my ‘death’ that used to be all over the bulletin board.

It took barely a month for the frequency of those mentions to not only decrease but stop entirely. However, starting the next month, I started popping up in posts again. Someone had added new fuel to the fire.
[Is the rumor that Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit true?]
Wherever I go these days, that’s all I hear. They wouldn’t be saying that if it was complete nonsense.
[Three reasons why Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit]
Click thumbs up while you’re here~
[Do you logically think he can be an evil spirit?]
If you argue with me, you’re a newbie who’s never even seen Bjorn Yandel. If you agree, you get a beastwoman girlfriend.
arolf5205: He’s right. All the people saying Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit are probably newbies.
1spring: Bjorn Yandel is not an evil spirit. Do I get a shifter girlfriend now?
Bling0_0: Hmm, but I still think he’s an evil spirit...

Bjorn Yandel’s Life After Death, two months in: the bulletin board was plastered with discussions about whether I was an evil spirit or not. Up to this point, most people thought it was a rumor. There was a comment in the middle that bothered me, though.
teckmonkey: It’s possible that’s not a rumor but a fact. Some say that the rumors were first started by Bjorn Yandel’s closest comrade.
When I saw they described them as a comrade and didn’t refer to a specific person, though, I lost interest. I was used to trolls flocking to every hot topic.
Click, click.

Three months after my death, my name was barely ever mentioned. Then, six months later, my name, which was slowly being forgotten, suddenly blew up on the bulletin board. The palace had made an official statement that Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit.
[Hey, was that declaration made by the palace real?]
[Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit?]
[He was a candidate for chieftain and even received a noble title. How can he be an evil spirit? Something has to be wrong.]

Everyone seemed confused at first, but gradually evidence began to emerge and the vibe shifted to acceptance. If you assumed I was an evil spirit, there were several suspicious things about me that you could point to as proof.
[Thinking about it, it was kinda weird]
How is it possible to go up the ranks that quickly? It’s too strange to even just write him off as an outlier.
tunaboot: Counter-argument 1: even if he was an evil spirit, it still doesn’t make sense.
└BrutalizerX: Counter-argument 2: Bjorn Yandel was living with three women.
└WingPizza: Counter-argument 3: Bjorn Yandel is known as a giant who’s well over eight inches. I’m talking about his kidney, of course.

Of course, my name wasn’t a hot topic for long. Aside from it being shocking news, there was not enough fuel to keep the fire burning. Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit? How surprising—but, so? How long were they going to talk about a dead guy? That was the vibe. Well, some people hypothesized that there must be some big motivation behind the fact these rumors were being spread about a dead person and that the palace was just now revealing they were true, but unfortunately, that was the extent of their theories. There was no way insider information would make rounds on a free bulletin board.
Click, click.

I continued to read the posts after that, but there wasn’t another topic that served to fire up the entire bulletin board until several months later. It was just business as usual, people saying what they wanted to say.
Then, one year after my death, there was an incident that set fire to the community.
[Guys, did you hear about Clan Nartel?]

Clan Nartel was the clan headed by adventurer Melter Fend, whom I had worked closely with during the battle against Noark all those years ago. Apparently, almost 90 percent of the clan had perished in the labyrinth—and the cause was already widely known.
godFLEXyou: Yeah, I heard they were attacked by Noark and only a few came back alive.

Bastards from Noark, who were last known to have left their castle walls, were discovered in the labyrinth. All kinds of speculation circulated: there was a portal outside the walls, or perhaps they may have created a new portal through some ritual. One person even said they were likely people who snuck into Rafdonia right under our noses and hid their identities.

Then, one year and one month after my death, a medium-sized clan was wiped out in the labyrinth. It was a clan active on the Dark Continent, where Clan Nartel suffered its catastrophe. Because there were no survivors, the cause of their annihilation was unknown.

At one year and three months, the number of clans disappearing on the seventh floor without a trace rose rapidly, and there were even several eyewitness accounts citing the presence of people from Noark. Most of the sightings were on the seventh floor.

At one year and four months, the palace recognized the gravity of the situation with Noark and started distributing identity tags again. Knights were also sent into the labyrinth to patrol the lower floors, but nothing improved. Despite verifying the identities of all entrants on the first floor as soon as the labyrinth opened, none of them were found to be from Noark.

One year and six months: Mindful of the fact that Noark’s faction only appeared on the seventh floor, the palace made an alliance with several large clans to form an expedition team. After suffering countless losses, they returned. Still, they did get something out of it.
[Breaking News: Latest News on Noark]

This is trustworthy information obtained from a prisoner taken captive during the expedition. The guys from Noark opened a portal outside the castle walls and apparently, it takes you straight to the seventh floor. Of course, even the asshole we captured doesn’t know how that’s possible, nor does the palace know anything.

New information came to light. More time passed. After one year and eight months, the palace forbade ordinary adventurers from entering the Dark Continent and formed a second expedition team. As a result of flooding the floor with countless troops, they achieved a pyrrhic victory.
[It’s really war now]

With the seventh floor as the stage, a full-scale power struggle began. They decided that if the bastards from Noark were able to stay holed up on the seventh floor and expand their power, it would lead to major issues in the future. Numerous adventurers participated in the battle for the enormous reward offered by the palace, and new war heroes gained fame every day. A prime example was the Seven Powerful—seven heroes who did not have much fame before but made a name for themselves by playing a major role in this war.
[Now that I’m thinking about it, Bjorn Yandel’s party had an insane talent pool. How can two members of the Seven Powerful come from one party?]

Time passed, and once I finished checking the most recent post made ten minutes ago, I took my hand off the mouse. Even just skimming it, looking through two years and six months’ worth of material had taken more than two hours.
Why don’t I take a break and process this?

I got off the chair and lay on the bed. To start, I had learned very little new information while looking around the forum. That was natural. I’d heard all kinds of stories from Erwen during the ten days I’d spent stuck at home. I was already aware of the major events in the timeline of the past few years, including the stories about Noark.
Still, it was nice to get a feel for how people were feeling at the time by looking around...

Besides, there were posts with trivial information Erwen hadn’t told me about—for example, the adventurers who had been declared brain-dead due to the pillars of fire that fateful day in Dimension Square were all cured.
Anyway, should I check the Exchange for information this time?
After taking a short break, I sat in front of the computer and started combing through the backlogged posts one by one. Time passed, and at 3:09 am, it was time to enter the Round Table.
Creak.
Goblin entered through the opened door and cheerfully said hello. “Oh, Ms. Fox! Long time no see!”
“Yes, hello.”
“I guess we’re the first ones again today?”

At Goblin’s question, the woman in the fox mask, Versyl Gowland, offered an unenthusiastic chuckle. She knew this question wasn’t being posed to check, but to make personal conversation. Versyl had nothing she wanted to say to Goblin.
“...Haha, it looks like you have some more things to think about? I’ll be quiet.”
“Thank you.”
A while later, Deer and Crescent arrived almost at the same time. When she checked, the time was 3:05. There were still five minutes left for people to enter.
“Looks like those two haven’t arrived yet?”
“...I’m sure they’ll come soon.” She answered Deer’s question with a rueful laugh.

The members who had not yet joined the gathering were Clown and Queen. They would probably participate today. Well, rather, they’d probably just check who had come and then turn around and disappear again, just as they had been doing for the past year.
“Still, since there are four of us, we can hold a proper gathering today.”
“...We couldn’t even do a round last time because Deer wasn’t here, right? Why didn’t you come then?”
“Goblin, do I have to tell you the reason why?”
“Well... no. Yes. I was just curious.”

As they exchanged meaningless chatter before the gathering, the door opened again. This time it was a woman. “Oh my, it’s been a while, everyone.” Although her presence could not be compared to Lion’s, Queen crushed even Clown in terms of useful information and had proven her worth at this meeting.
“Are you just going to leave again this time?”
At Crescent’s polite question, Queen laughed awkwardly. That was answer enough. Everyone knew what she was thinking.
She thinks participating in this gathering is pointless without that man here.

Even after Lion stopped coming, she attended the gathering for a while and shared various pieces of information. But at some point, she started simply checking who was there and leaving before it even began. The same went for Clown.
“Pshehe, are you all gathered again?”
“Clown...”

There were two minutes left until the gathering began. Everyone’s eyes turned to Clown as he arrived. Most of their reactions were not favorable. There had been many run-ins with Noark recently. Though most of their reactions weren’t as intense as Crescent’s, they couldn’t be cordial to a member of Noark.

“Looks can’t actually kill, you know.” Clown chose an empty seat and sat down, not minding the glares. Instead, he stared at the clock on the wall, waiting desperately for one particular person to arrive. This was a very familiar sight to the other members by now.
“Hah... looks like he isn’t coming today, either.”
“...I heard there have been sightings of Noark trying to crawl down to the sixth floor. What is the reason for that?”
“Eh? Why would I tell you that when the gathering hasn’t even started?”
“That’s... because you don’t participate in the gathering...”
“Oh, Mr. Deer... then you should have brought me something more entertaining a long time ago, don’t you think? It’s because it’s so boring that I leave every time.”
“...Do you think acting like that will make you look like Lion?”
“Pshehe, that wasn’t my intention.” When Clown laughed mockingly and got up, Queen also stood up as if on cue. “Anyway, since it looks like he won’t be coming today either, I’ll leave.”
“Me too...”
Fox stared at their backs and sighed quietly. As much as their absence was a loss, she was once again reminded of the necessity of one specific person’s presence.
Jeez, where has Lion disappeared to?

At first, Clown and Queen had joined in on coming up with all kinds of theories as to his disappearance: he lost interest, the GM banished him from the community, etcetera. There were many other hypotheses, but the most memorable was Goblin’s: that he might have been Bjorn Yandel. If he had died, the timing was all very coincidental.
“Pshehe, Mr. Goblin, why don’t you quit being a paladin and become a writer instead?”

Goblin was only laughed at for his hypothesis, however. Although no one else said anything harsh, the other members did not take his suggestion seriously. That was because when Lion first appeared at the Round Table, Bjorn Yandel hadn’t even been an adventurer for a year yet. Someone active on the third and fourth floors at best could not possibly behave like he had.
However... Maybe he guessed right...

Fox was beginning to think that the hypothesis could be correct. Although there were many holes in the theory, if that really was the case, it would explain why Lion hadn’t been seen for two and a half years.
Creak.

Just as she was thinking that, the tightly shut door slowly began to open, and everyone jumped. The reason was simple. Clown, who was stomping away from the table, hadn’t even reached the door yet, and there was no one who hadn’t arrived yet. Or there shouldn’t have been, except for one person.
Tap.
Beyond the open door, a man appeared. The man, who could freeze everyone in the room with his mere presence, spoke as if he had just stopped by out of boredom.
“Long time no see.”
Lion was back.

chapters.title: Chapter 343: Comeback (2)
paragraphs: Before entering the Round Table, I ran countless hypotheticals. This was because of the two-and-a-half-year gap. It was clear the other members would be curious about my absence.
It’s possible some have correctly arrived at the conclusion that I’m Bjorn Yandel thanks to the fact that my disappearance was around the same time.

Of course, I wasn’t too worried about that part. Only Amelia and Erwen knew that I was back. Just showing my face at the Round Table would put that suspicion to rest. The problem would come after news of my survival broke.
Well, there’s ways to get around that too.

My immediate concern lay somewhere else. How was I going to explain my two and a half years of absence? It was because of this that I ran various simulations and assumed various different premises before coming to a conclusion.
“Lion...”
“...You really were alive.”
Even if these people looked at me with surprise and doubt, there was no real reason for me to explain.
“Aren’t you going to move?”

“Ah... yes...!” When I spoke, Clown flinched away from in front of the door and retreated toward the wall, as did Soul Queen. Of course, she was in a better state than Clown, who was completely out of it.

“...You seem the same, Lion.” Even as she made way for me, she watched me with interest in her eyes. Her relaxed tone bothered me, but I didn’t show it. I just ignored her, walked by, and sat down at the table indifferently.
Tap.

After that, there was a silence that could only be described as bizarre. The members stared at me intently and also glanced at each other. It was obvious what they were thinking. They probably wanted someone to bite the bullet and ask me everything on the group’s behalf.
It’s been a while, huh.
Was it because I’d been sadly hiding at home these days? An addictive feeling of freedom came over me. A few more seconds of silence ensued.
Boom!
The doors connecting to the Round Table shut with a bang. That meant 3:10 had passed and people could no longer enter. In other words, that also meant we could start the meeting now.
“Are you going to keep standing?” I said to Clown and Soul Queen. “Sit.”
I have a lot I want to hear from you guys. A lot to say too.

“Pshehe, I’ve embarrassed myself.” Clown, who was standing in a daze against the wall, came to his senses and sat down. He looked at me with eyes that betrayed his joy. “We sincerely welcome your return, Lion.”
What is this prick saying? Did he forget what I told him last time about not acting friendly? Well, I guess that can happen in two and a half years.
When I just ignored him without responding, Clown snickered like he knew I’d do that.

The next to speak was Deer. Showing his macho side, he jumped up from his seat and confronted me head on. “You haven’t shown your face for over two years. Why have you come now?” Of course, my answer was already decided. “Well? Are you saying you won’t answer?” Deer’s voice went up an octave when he saw me exercising my right to remain silent. I was pretty sure the palace guys sounded just like this when they interrogated someone. What a shame. Just because I’d been away for two and a half years, he’d forgotten his place.
“How rude,” I said as coldly as possible, slowly raising my level of murderous intent.
Whooom!
Since it had been a long time, I decided it was necessary to discipline these guys at least once.

“...Ugh.” Exposed to my murderous intent, Deer clenched his fists in pain. This should have been enough to prime a courteous listener, but I wasn’t satisfied and continued to pile it on. As I did, the veins on Deer’s neck began to rise. Deer was better than Clown, who once writhed on the floor from this, but he ultimately wasn’t much different.

“Never look down on me again.” When I unleashed the full extent of my murderous intent, Deer slowly bent over as if something heavy was pressing down on his shoulders. As he stared up at me, strained, I made sure to sound pleased. “Yes, just like that.”

Before long, Deer was on his knees and looking up at me from the ground. Judging by the way his arms trembled on the table as he struggled to support his weight, he seemed to be at his limit. But I was in the same boat.
Ugh, my head.
The moment my head throbbed, the murderous intent that was weighing down the hall disappeared.
...Gasp!
Deer sucked in a deep breath as soon as his lungs were unfrozen.

At the sight, Clown sneered. “...Pshehe, foolish human. Have you forgotten what to do if you want to ask Mr. Lion something? Bring something entertaining! Entertaining!” Even as he said that, Clown glanced at me out of the corner of his eye as if to ask, Right?, clearly hoping for a compliment.
Naturally, I ignored him again.

“Lion.” After a beat, Crescent, a man I believed to be an elf and who longed for the Stone of Revival more than any other, ended the silence. “I don’t care what you’ve been doing all this time.” Swallowing back the anxiety and questions that must have been brewing in his head for over two years, he said, “Thank you, for coming back.”
It was just the reaction I had been hoping for, but actually hearing it, I felt a bit bad. This guy must have been super anxious while I was gone.
Should I give him a clue this time?

As I was thinking that, Soul Queen spoke up in a cheerful tone in an attempt to break the tension. “Hmm, then I guess it’s all sorted now? Shall we get started? I think we’re going to have a lot to say to each other in today’s gathering.”
That was how the gathering began. The process of deciding the order was quick.
“So Ms. Fox is first, then?”
“...I guess so.”
The order was clockwise as always, but it had to end with me.
“Why did I sit here...?”

That had been our tacit agreement in the past. Listening to the information that was brought by the others first, evaluating it, and then relaying information of an equivalent value—that was how the Round Table usually went for me.

“...Since I haven’t prepared anything special today, I’ll say what I originally planned to mention.” Fox was the first to relay her information. Right from the get-go, things were quite interesting. “The Dragon Slayer, who went inactive after kidnapping a high priest three years ago, reappeared for the first time on the Dark Continent. According to witness accounts, he looked much stronger, and it seems he has dealt with the Dragon’s Curse to some extent.”
It was news about the Dragon Slayer, who I had forgotten about for a while there.
So he’s lifted the Dragon’s Curse, huh?
Though that was unfortunate news, I decided not to get too fixated on it. Being able to use Dragon Speech didn’t change anything. I was no longer the old me, either.
Shaaaaaa!
The Round Table’s jewel emitted a green light, announcing the successful end of the first turn.
“Pshehe, you are clever, Ms. Fox,” Clown cackled.
“...What do you mean?”

“That can’t be what you originally meant to say here since it’s something we can use to infer your identity. Judging by Mr. Deer’s reaction, it seems even the palace hasn’t received this information yet. So that must mean you met him in person yourself.”
“I won’t answer any personal questions.”
“Well, that’s fine. I can just ask that salamander son of a bitch who he met in the labyrinth later.”
Fox pursed her lips at Clown’s crass behavior and the baton naturally passed to the next person.

“Then it’s... my turn.” It was Deer this time. Before sharing his information, he made eye contact with me, then awkwardly averted his eyes. It seemed the lingering effects of the murderous intent earlier were still going strong. Perhaps he was too proud to show it, though, as he did his best to appear unaffected. “The palace will soon issue a conscription order for titled nobles.”
As he spoke, Deer turned his eyes to Clown, as if to check how Noark would react to that.

“Pshehe, do you think that’s going to scare me? All I’m hearing is that you’re cornered with your back to the wall.” Clown just sneered as usual, and Deer did not react to his attempt at provocation, ending his turn.

When the green light turned off, Crescent opened his mouth from beside him. “It’s my turn now.” I was looking forward to whatever he’d say since he had been the most enthusiastic about bringing me information ever since he latched onto the Stone of Revival. Having not expected me to attend today, though, he made a disclaimer in advance. He seemed worried I might be disappointed and stop coming again. “Unfortunately, I couldn’t prepare anything special. This is related to Blood Spirit.” Surprisingly, a rather interesting piece of information came out of his mouth. “A few weeks ago, Blood Spirit took most of the financial support funding bestowed on the elves from the palace for herself, claiming she needed the money. She did not disclose the reason.”

This incident was practically a scandal within the tribe. Soul Queen, who was listening intently, expressed her doubts. “But can she really take an amount like that without disclosing the reason? Even if it is Blood Spirit? A support fund from the palace certainly wouldn’t be small.”
“It’s definitely unprecedented. But the elders had no choice as she threatened to sell off the Sacred Bow if they didn’t give her the money.”
“...Sell the Sacred Bow?”
“It’s shameful, but yes. Since she said the money was vital, we have no choice but to trust she has some justification she cannot reveal.”
At Crescent’s explanation, the other members could not hide their discomfort either. “Pshehe, what is that wild woman planning?”
“I can only imagine one reason a woman like her would need a large sum like that.”
“I don’t know, but it looks like there will be more bloodshed.”
I felt very uncomfortable for some reason. If these guys were reacting like this, what was Erwen’s public image like?
No, before that... She told me not to worry because she had plenty of money, but it was all stolen from her tribe?
I was stunned. I had wondered how she had the capital to buy a mansion in one night, but to think this was what happened.
What’ll happen if the elves find out? If it were me, I’d be devastated.
As I was thinking this, Goblin cautiously spoke up. “Th-then... can I go now?”
Ah, it’s his turn now. He was the paladin from Reatlas, right?
Since I knew his identity for sure along with Clown’s, I was a little curious about what piece of information he’d reveal.
“The Church has decided to send all forces except the First Order of Paladins to the royal army.”
What, war again? Even though I was disappointed, I ended up chuckling.
The Church? I guess he has no intention of hiding it anymore. Either that or his identity has been revealed within the last two years.

Even as I wondered what kinds of conversations were exchanged at the Round Table while I was away, I kept my ears open. Once a brief conversation about how the Church’s actions would affect the war ended, it came time for the next person to speak.
