“Pshehe.” This time, it was none other than Clown’s turn. “Why is everyone talking about such boring things when Mr. Lion has come after all this time?” Clown tilted his head exaggeratedly before the look in his eyes sharpened and he shared his piece of information. “Baekho Lee has the Stone of Revival.”
...Huh?

The ripple effect from the information Clown casually dropped was huge, and the one who showed the most violent reaction was Crescent. Crescent, who always held hatred in his eyes whenever he looked at Clown, could not hide how off-balance he was and muttered, “Baekho Lee... the man whom the palace has secretly ordered to be killed? Has the Stone of Revival?” Crescent mostly seemed surprised to hear about the Stone of Revival, but I was different.
Why is Baekho being mentioned here...?

Not only was his a name I hadn’t expected to hear here but when did he get so famous in the first place? Two years ago, only a small number of people even knew his name. And how did he get the Stone of Revival? That was something you could never obtain without luck, even if you knew the method for acquiring it. Unfortunately, I didn’t get too much time to process this bombshell.
“How was it? If it’s related to Baekho, I thought you might be a bit interested too.” As soon as the green light came on, Clown subtly asked for my opinion.

After thinking it over for a moment, I answered. It was of higher value than the information I’d heard thus far. I was more curious about this than anything war-related, but it would be suspicious to seem too surprised. “It’s certainly not bad.” I expressed my feelings on the matter just enough without going overboard. After all, you needed to give reviews like this once in a while so that people would bring similar information in the future.
I should ask Erwen if she knows anything about Baekho once I get back.
I made a mental note and then stared straight ahead.
“Clown, is what you just said true?”
“Can’t you tell?”
“G-Give us more details, even a little—”
“Pshehe, I don’t want to.”

Crescent, who had become a beggar in an instant, was being mocked by Clown. It was a pity, but there was nothing I could do about it. This was also my first time hearing that Baekho had the Stone of Revival.
Hmm, this makes it inconvenient to use the Stone of Revival as my tidbit this round... What should I bring up later?

While I quietly sat back and observed the situation to decide which information to reveal next, Soul Queen clapped and drew everyone’s attention. “Now, is it my turn?” Of the numerous members at the table, she looked directly at me and spoke in an intrigued tone. “There has been no record of Lion accessing Ghost Busters for the past two years and six months. Where on earth have you been all this time?”
Haha...
On the 15th, all community members were forcefully summoned to this spiritual world. Well, you could log out as soon as you entered, of course, but...
“What do you mean no record of access?”
“It’s just as I said. There is no record of him accessing it whatsoever.”
The fact that my login records had disappeared altogether was strange in many ways. She probably confirmed this through the GM.
“Which was why I thought you must be dead...”
Beyond simply assuming I was dead, this woman would have been convinced I was Bjorn Yandel because I had been the only famous death during that time.
But did he pick up on some kind of contradiction in Soul Queen’s statement? “D-Dead?” Goblin asked. “But I thought you were waiting for him this whole time?”
“No, the person I was waiting for was Master. The one who created this Round Table. I’ve been visiting regularly to check to see if he’s returned.”
“Ah...” Goblin, now convinced, turned to me, as did everyone else. It was clear what they wanted.
Shaaaaaa!
Since the Round Table’s gem was glowing green, it was true that I had not logged into the community for two and a half years. They must have been hoping for an explanation from my own lips.
“Ah, are you going to avoid answering? True, this must not be entertaining information for you—”
I cut her off and said, “How bold.”
“Oh? Is there a reason I should be nervous?”

As she met my eyes, her expression was utterly relaxed. The look in her eyes seemed to be saying that even if I hit her with the same murderous intent that paralyzed Deer, she had a way to deal with it.
“Funny.”
“Oh, then will you tell us? What happened to you, that is.”
I glanced at the jewel that had already lost its luster before replying. “It’s my turn now.”
“Are you ignoring my question?”

“Well.” I was not ignoring her question. To be more exact, this was her punishment for it. “The Magic Engineer, Yurven Havellion.” To maintain Lion’s authority going forward, I had to properly teach her a lesson, even if the subduing wasn’t done with something like murderous intent. “That is the GM’s name.”
Those who dare to rebel will be punished.

chapters.title: Chapter 344: Comeback (3)
paragraphs: “There has been no record of Lion accessing Ghost Busters for the past two years and six months.”
When I first heard that, I was quite surprised, but thinking about it, there was no cause for concern. I knew at least one thing for sure.
All she probably found out is that my nickname is Elfnunna.

Even Auril Gavis hadn’t been able to dig up my real-world identity from inside the spirit world, but I was supposed to believe a GM who had inherited only half his powers had managed to do that? Ridiculous. Instead, the main problem was that he could ban me if he learned my nickname. But that wasn’t such a huge issue when I thought about it, either.
It’s not like not being able to participate in Ghost Busters would kill me.
On the other hand, I had a lot to lose if I rolled over and took this treatment. The moment I did, that woman would conclude that this was my Achilles’ heel.
“Where on earth have you been all this time?”
After that, even more explicit questions would be directed at me. If I kept avoiding them, it would only be a matter of time before the Lion mask came off.
A good offense is the best defense.

So, I would rather stick to my guns and leave things up to chance. That was because in the past, the GM banned Baekho and then almost got beaten to death in real combat. Just as a nuclear weapon could be seen as a deterrent to war, I concluded that bold exaggeration might be my only viable solution here.
Well, I can’t be sure what the outcome will be yet... But I’ll soon find out.

I glanced around at the rest of the room, which was so silent it seemed no one was even breathing. All eyes were focused on one place, the jewel located at the center of the Round Table, which distinguished truth from lies.

But I looked elsewhere, at Soul Queen, the GM’s ally who participated in the Round Table wearing the mask of a queen. Her constantly collected facade was starting to crack, and every part of her being seemed to be asking, How did this happen? She’d clearly never expected things to turn out like this.

“...Uh. Eh—uhh.” Her mouth wanted to say something, but all that came out were puffs of air that amounted to nothing. Her hands twitched with the same impulse. “U-Uh...?” One of her hands quickly darted forward with the intent to stop me, but it was only in the air for a moment before falling weakly back onto the table. She knew that no hand gesture could stop this, that the tea had already spilled.
Shaaaaaa!
Like it was enjoying the attention, the jewel glowed green after a beat. Then, the short silence came to an end.
“The GM... is Magic Engineer...?”
“W-Wait... I can’t keep up. H-How is he an evil... no, how can someone like that be the GM?”
“...Pshehe, it was worth waiting two years for you. To think you’d start out with a secret like this.”
The members each spoke and the chaos continued. There was nothing among the murmuring worth listening to.
“Actually, I’m more surprised by Queen. I speculated she might be from the admin team, but...”

Yeah, no wonder she spoke about the access logs in front of everyone. There was no reason to hide it. It seemed at least part of Queen’s identity had been exposed to some extent during my absence as well. Considering the woman’s personality, perhaps it had been intentional? Of course, that wasn’t important right now. No matter what everyone else was saying, I kept my eyes glued to one thing and one thing only.

“Can...” Soul Queen, who was standing with her hands on the table and head bowed, was glaring at me. It didn’t feel particularly scary. The reason was simple. “C-Can you handle the consequences of this...?” When she stuttered like that, who would be afraid? “I don’t know how you found out, b-but after what you’ve just done—”
I cut her off. “You said earlier that there’s no reason for you to be nervous, yet you’re shaking.”
Soul Queen quickly glanced down at her hands. They were shaking violently, like someone suffering from tremors.
Slap.

She grabbed her shaking wrist with her other hand and glared at me again. With a determined look on her face, she took a deep breath. “So. That’s how you want to play it. I’ll go first this time.” She placed her hand on the jewel and told anyone who wasn’t going to participate in this round to beat it. Naturally, no one was going to leave in a situation like this. “Lion is Bjorn Yandel.”
Before long, the jewel lit up.
1. Lion was Elfnunna.
2. Elfnunna did not log in to the community for two years and six months, and neither did Lion.
3. Therefore, Lion was Bjorn Yandel.
As this conclusion had been drawn through clear logic, she was 100 percent certain of this fact. At least, she had been, until she entered the Round Table today.
Shaaaaaa.
This went beyond tension. The jewel lit up in a silence so powerful that it could cut you with a knife if you weren’t careful.
“...It’s red.”

As expected, there was no green light. This jewel did not determine the truth—it just relayed whether the speaker was saying what they thought was true. It looked like Soul Queen had wanted to deal me a blow, but as long as her own certainty had been shaken, that was a pointless undertaking.
The problem is, this woman doesn’t seem like she’s lost it to the point that she wouldn’t realize something as simple as that.
Then what was the reason for this pointless undertaking? That answer came in the form of Goblin’s question.
“Um, isn’t Bjorn Yandel dead? And Mr. Lion is alive in front of us... But why would you ask...”

“There are many questions surrounding his death. Even his teammates did not see his body.” This woman had made that announcement with this in mind—that there was a possibility Bjorn Yandel was alive. Well, the red light she received suggested she lacked faith in that conclusion, though.
“Pshehe, you would have known the red light would come on, though.”

“...I won’t answer that part,” Soul Queen said, then took her eyes off of me. That was when it occurred to me that she had just been feeling me out. No, actually, that had to be it. Looking back, that woman had stared solely at me the whole time, even as the light came on.
To think she’d think to feel me out in return in a situation like that. How is it that nothing in my life is ever easy?

Though I worried about what kind of conclusion she reached upon seeing my reaction, I didn’t show it. But perhaps her confidence grew as my silence continued. “...Anyway, since the red light came on, I guess I’ll have to go again.” Soul Queen casually declared a redo and then glanced at me again. “I can prevent Lion from setting foot in Ghost Busters at any time.”

Then she revealed information that confirmed her identity as a member of the admin team and received a green light. This behavior was somewhat within the range of what I expected. Though she asked if I could handle the consequences to come, unlike me, that was the only threat she could make.
“Pshehe, I hope you won’t do something like that. Ah, you can’t, anyway.”
“...What do you mean?”
“If you can ban him, why have you left me alone? I’m from Noark, a place all of you hate so much. Isn’t it because you’re curious and want information about what we’re up to on our side?”
“...What does that have to do with this?”

“Pshehe, was I right? Anyway, that’s all the more reason Mr. Lion shouldn’t be banned. We don’t know what kind of information this man will tell us next...” Clown said bluntly. “And it’s best not to do anything that might have consequences you can’t handle, right?”
“...Can’t handle?”
“Yep. He knows the GM’s identity. What kind of trouble are you trying to get into?”

His words scratched my itch. It wasn’t cool to say stuff like that yourself. If someone stepped up like this for me, I could save face, too—similar to how bullies always had a bootlicker at the front of the pack. When Queen pursed her lips and turned away, I met Clown’s eyes. The guy was smiling. Did I do well? his eyes asked. It seemed Clown thought this made up for his mistakes in the past.

“Pshehe. Well, I’m just giving you my two cents, but it’s probably not my place to meddle.” Clown finished saying what he wanted to say then continued in a light tone, “Anyway, if we’re going in reverse, is it my turn this time?”
That was how the second lap officially began. The first item on the agenda was already one that couldn’t be overlooked.
“Since we’re talking about Bjorn Yandel, that son of a bitch... It’s possible he’s not actually an evil spirit.”
Huh?
“Pshehe, because I heard the person who spread that rumor was Baekho Lee.”
...Baekho? He exposed me?
While I was inwardly shocked, Deer casually blurted out even more shocking information. “But the original source was that woman Missha Karlstein.”
...Huh? Missha?
“That means the same thing in practice. That woman is now Baekho Lee’s teammate.”
Wait, what on earth? Why is Missha Baekho’s teammate?
“Pshehe, thankfully it’s a green light. I figured that no one knew that woman from the Red Cat Tribe is now Baekho Lee’s teammate.”

I felt lightheaded as I was force-fed information that was hard to swallow, but I managed to endure it with difficulty, firmly telling myself that I could not let how I was feeling show on my face. That was when the next turn began.

“...Jeez, like I thought, this isn’t easy.” Goblin received two red lights on war-related information before succeeding on the third try, which had to do with the internal affairs of the Church of Reatlas. This guy had always had the habit of selling out his church whenever he was in a tight spot, so that wasn’t a huge surprise.

“It’s me again.” That was how Crescent’s turn arrived. I was interested as he mentioned Erwen in the previous round, but unfortunately, the information that he provided was so-so because it was related to the war. The same went for Deer, who was next.
“Pshehe, looks like the palace has really sharpened their swords this time.”

I guessed the information was quite important seeing as Clown, who always mocked Deer, was saying something like that, but the war didn’t matter to me. With my scattered comrades, clearing my name after getting accused of being an evil spirit, etcetera, I had plenty of homework to get through before that.

In that sense, Fox’s information interested me quite a bit. No, should I say it worried me? “A few months ago, a double-digit Numbers Item was obtained by the Alminus Central Exchange. It’s said that an unknown woman borrowed a large sum using that as collateral, and the repayment date is just around the corner. It’s possible we’ll see that item at the auction house soon.”
That... isn’t my Demon Grinder, is it? Yeah, it can’t be. Kind Amelia could never do something like that.
While I was struggling to convince myself of that, I suddenly felt eyes on me.
Ah, it’s already my turn.

I’d already decided on what to say so there was no need to think. I slowly glanced around at each member of the Round Table. Everyone seemed to look forward to what I was going to say, except for one person. Perhaps because of the mess she created earlier, Soul Queen looked more anxious than curious. She had high self-esteem, but was more timid than she seemed.
Anyway, I think that’s enough suspense.

After tapping my fingers against the arm of my chair twice for dramatic effect, I looked at Soul Queen. “You asked if I can handle it.” It was now time for me to answer that question. No, rather, it was my turn to ask the same one.
Then are you, as Clown said earlier, really ready to handle it?
Gulp.

The moment Queen’s throat moved, I continued without hesitation. “Queen’s username is Soul Queen.” As soon as I finished, the eyes of all the members turned to the jewel. I couldn’t help laughing at this.
Jeez, I’m not done talking yet.
“And Soul Queen’s real name...”

To be honest, I didn’t know it either, but I intentionally trailed off while staring at her. If she didn’t react, I decided I could just say something like, I’ll tell you next time to make it entertaining, and pretend to be merciful for now.

“Oh?” When I paused once more, the interest in everyone’s eyes grew stronger. Clown’s was the most obvious. True, he’d been humiliated by this woman once before. “I hope she’s not the type that stays holed up in the Magic Tower like Magic Engineer. Because that’ll make her harder to kill. Pshehe...”
With Clown’s creepy laughter, the muscles in Soul Queen’s throat jumped once more.
Tap, tap.
I idly tapped the chair again.
“...S-Stop!” The words I wanted to hear finally flowed from her mouth. “P-Please don’t... reveal my identity, I...”
Tsk, should’ve said that from the start.

chapters.title: Chapter 345: Comeback (4)
paragraphs: Soul Queen finally waved the white flag. It seemed she had realized how foolish it was to try and gain the upper hand against me.
“Pshehe, what a funny woman. You were so bold when he revealed the GM’s identity, but you’ll lower your tail now that it’s about you?”
Queen did not respond to Clown’s insults and instead took them. Considering the reputation I remember her building for herself in that short time at the Round Table, this was kind of sad.
It would be a shame to stop here.

Accepting her surrender here would be foolish. Because Soul Queen seemed to care a lot about hierarchy, it would probably be a good idea to drive it home for her for good at this opportunity, just as the goblin I met on my first day in this world did to me: who was above, and who was below.
“Why...” I said, tapping the chair with my index finger once more, “Should I do that?”

Soul Queen flinched at the short question before answering in a quiet voice. “...If you stop here, we will not antagonize you.” Including not banning me from the community, of course, that meant she wouldn’t blame me for revealing the GM’s identity earlier.

I laughed coldly at her uncharacteristically quiet voice. After all, it almost sounded like she was making an offer to someone on even footing as her. “You still haven’t learned.” I tapped the arm of the chair with my index finger again. However, if there was a difference from earlier, it was that this time I did not hide my displeasure.
“...If there is something you want, please tell me,” Soul Queen pleaded.
“I don’t want anything from you people.” She didn’t seem to understand what I was saying so I decided to make things clear. “Nor am I afraid of you.”

At least, that was true on the surface. If I was at all uncomfortable with making an enemy of the moderators, would I have attacked them with no fucks given like this? To these guys, I probably just looked like an uncontrollable loose cannon.
“I will ask for the last time,” I said, before asking Soul Queen again, “Why should I do that?”

“Th-that’s...” Of course, she couldn’t give me a reason. Everyone she ever saw as a business partner would have had some kind of desire for her to appeal to. It was natural for an eloquent tongue to freeze at the sight of a new species. “I...”

She was a smart woman in many ways. Threats didn’t work, and I wasn’t even asking for compensation. I was only trying to drag out her punishment, like this was just a fun pastime to me. What could she do to persuade an opponent like that?

Pondering this for a long moment, she reached an answer: let go of the thought of persuasion and hope for mercy. “I’m... sorry...” It was the last resort of the weak when they had nothing to offer the strong. “Please, forgive me...”
“Looks like that foolish woman has finally realized her place. Pshehe.”

Soul Queen was not fazed by Clown’s ridicule and bowed her head just as I made Deer do earlier. Then she looked up at me, struggling to force an apology from her throat. “I will... never do anything... to offend you again... So please, forgive my mistakes today...”

To be honest, I was very impressed. I didn’t expect her to be so submissive off the bat. Was it so shocking that I knew their identities? When I looked around, I saw the other members glancing back and forth between me and Soul Queen without a word. They seemed curious about whether I would actually accept her apology.
That’s enough for sorting out the hierarchy...
I looked down on Soul Queen and said, “Much better.”
Yeah, that’s the stuff.
“Queen’s nickname is Soul Queen. And I will not say her real name.” I placed my hand on the table again to end my turn and received a green light.

“Whew...” With that, the tension eased and the other members who were watching the situation unfold exhaled loudly. The same went for Soul Queen. “Thank... you...” That expression of gratitude probably felt like peeling off her own skin to her. I didn’t bother replying to it and an awkward moment ensued.
It was Deer who cautiously ended the silence. “...What’s going to happen to the meeting? Is it going to continue?”

Once I finished my turn, the second round ended. On the longer days, there were times we went four or five rounds, but it wasn’t strange to end the gathering here either. What decision would these guys make?

“I-I’ll stop here...” Soul Queen, who had gotten a good scolding for getting aggressive, glanced at me as she said that. If I told her to stay, she’d probably remain, but it wouldn’t change anything if she did.
“Then I’ll stop here too...” Goblin, who barely managed to pass the last round after two red lights, declared he was opting out and the gathering naturally came to an end.
Welp, it’s already over...
It was unfortunate that the first Round Table I’d attended after two and a half years ended after two rounds, but there was nothing I could do.
But since I showed my face today, I’m sure they’ll bring something more interesting next month.

“Pshehe, then let’s all prepare harder for next month. Ah, of course, assuming Mr. Lion comes back again!” Clown glanced at me even as he pretended to speak to the other members. It could have been considered kind of cute. What he really wanted to ask was whether I was going to come back next time.
Slide.
It wasn’t cool to do something as nice as answer that, though, so I didn’t answer at all and left the Round Table then and there.

“Whew...” As soon as I returned to Hansu Lee’s room, I immediately took a deep breath and lay back on the bed. I was considerably fatigued, probably as an effect of the murderous intent I used earlier.
I’ll probably sleep like a log until tomorrow evening.
Of course, since that was my future self, the present me decided to do what he could without taking time to rest. First, sorting through the information I’d gotten.
I don’t think anyone will think I’m Bjorn Yandel after what happened today...
I reviewed the events of the Round Table. Although I made a good comeback, it didn’t go perfectly. I couldn’t pretend to be dead forever and live in the shadows.
The moment my return becomes common knowledge, the same suspicions will arise.
Of course, there were quite a few ways for me to deal with this. After traveling to the past, I had plenty of cards I could bluff with.
I’ll cross that bridge when I get to it...
The real issue was something else entirely. To be honest, it almost made me lose my mind at the Round Table.
“But the original source was that woman Missha Karlstein.”
“That means the same thing in practice. That woman is now Baekho Lee’s teammate.”

Missha Karlstein. Why did she start that rumor, and how did she become teammates with Baekho? No matter how much I strained my imagination, I was having trouble figuring out the A to Z here. But, if I were to make a guess, another thing said at the Round Table would probably be key.
“Baekho Lee has the Stone of Revival.”
For example, it could be possible Missha felt that she had to join up with Baekho to save me.
...Is that too much wishful thinking? Ha, why couldn’t that thing have brought me back even a year earlier?
That two-and-a-half-year gap once again felt incredibly big, and my frustration with it increased. But what could I do? Things had already reached this point.
Anyway, if Missha’s goal is to save me... What’s Baekho’s goal?

Well, I didn’t know. There still wasn’t enough information to go off of. The only thing we had in common was that we were both Korean, but Baekho and I had actually only had short conversations. We’d never even had a real, genuine talk.
...I’ll think about this again after I learn more about Baekho.

I closed my eyes and continued sorting through my thoughts. The GM, Auril Gavis, Amelia, Noark, and the palace—there were more than enough things to think about regardless of which one came first. As the gears in my mind continued to turn, I sat in front of the computer again and spent my time reading through the posts I hadn’t checked earlier.
I thought the GM or Soul Queen would send a message or something, but there’s nothing like that.
I moved the cursor without hesitation. It didn’t seem like anything interesting was going to result from careful scrutiny here, and there wasn’t much time left until the community closed anyway.
Click.

When I clicked “log out,” there was a flash, and soon darkness fell. In a bedroom where all the windows were boarded up and not even a single ray of moonlight streamed in, Erwen was staring down at me.
“Hehe, you’re awake...”

Erwen Fornacci di Tersia was now the reigning Master of the Pureblood and the contractor of the Elemental Ruler. As a token of these positions, she had been bestowed the Sacred Bow. She was also a member of the Seven Powerful, who played a big role in the war against Noark, earning her the nickname Blood Spirit.
“Pshehe, what is that wild woman planning?”
“I don’t know, but it looks like there will be more bloodshed.”
She was the only one of my clanmates who had sacrificed everything for revenge.
“No matter what anyone says, you are Bjorn Yandel to me.”

This woman told me it didn’t matter whether I was an evil spirit or not, but it was hard to be grateful and moved by her dedication. It was overly excessive. Why was she so obsessed with me? My immediate thought was the Obsession stat. All three of the essences Erwen had consumed—Goblin Archer, Iron Hill Chaser, and Carnivaro—had the Obsession stat attached. Since another person close to her had died not long after her sister, I figured that could have been a catalyst for her behavior.
“Mister... if you’re done sleeping... do you want to go for a walk? Th-the moon looks beautiful today...”

But that had been the Erwen of two and a half years ago. The Erwen who had received enough financial support from her clan to make even the children of aristocrats pee themselves had changed most of her essences. The problem was that these changes were not necessarily positive.

She now had the essence of a Patrolman Ertes from Golem Island on the sixth floor, which had a +45 to Defense Mechanism. With wolf beast Kalban, which had the unique trait of being passive during the day but aggressive at night, Impulse was +30 and Distrust was likewise +30. From rank-four monster Metcrow, she had gotten a +24 to Possessiveness, and from her two other essences, she had -30 Control and +40 Craving.

If you looked at each one individually, they weren’t stats that would cause major psychological issues, but when this much piled up, there would inevitably be an impact. After realizing this, I was as careful as possible not to provoke Erwen. If she lost it, the situation could deteriorate beyond her control.
Yeah, that had been my strategy until now.
“Ah, right...! I also bought a necklace... With this, I can know where you are at any time!”
I can’t put this off forever. That isn’t my style, either.
Tap.
I roughly pushed away Erwen’s hand, which was already touching my chest without hesitation.

“...Uh?” Erwen was clearly confused. “M-Mister... a-are you mad? But... why...?” Her eyes darted around in confusion as she looked for the cause of the shift in my mood. “Come to think of it... the boards... in the living room were a bit torn.”
I had been considering just tearing them off out of frustration a while ago, but did she interpret that in a different way?

“Amelia Rainwales. It was that woman, right...? That woman came, right? That’s why you...” Erwen constructed a ridiculous fantasy and started to tremble, murderous intent gleaming in her eyes. To be honest, seeing something like this in the middle of the night was making me shiver.
“Amelia didn’t come.”
But, so what? Running away because I’m scared or uncomfortable goes against my beliefs.

Even when I had been framed and imprisoned in the guild’s underground prison, even when I had encountered the Dragon Slayer in the Labyrinth of Larcaz, even in the battle with Noark where I gained the reputation of Giant, I had always faced my problems head-on. That was the reason I was able to survive.
“Why... why... are you still calling her by that name?”
I answered without hesitation. “Because she’s my comrade.”
Erwen’s reaction came after a brief pause. “Th-that’s! I-I told you repeatedly that you don’t n-need a woman like that because I’ll be with you from now on...!”
Yes, you did say that.
“Why do you get to decide that?”
“Th-that’s...” Erwen was at a loss for words.
I didn’t particularly feel bad. Maybe because I had been wearing the Lion mask just a few hours ago, my response flowed out of me naturally. “Disrespectful.”
Erwen’s eyes widened. At that moment, I woke my sleeping muscles. What would someone who wasn’t quite right in the head do now?
“...Who are you?”
“I’m Bjorn Yandel.”
“L-Liar... you’re an evil spirit...”
A black aura soon began to swirl around Erwen’s body. This was Erwen’s specialty, the spirit of darkness.
Thumpthumpthumpthump.
Sensing a threat, my heart pounded like crazy. I had been prepared for this, but actually being faced with it was very intimidating. But the scarier it got, the more I thought back.

Who was I? A barbarian warrior who had overcome all kinds of hardships. The Giant, Bjorn, son of Yandel. The only user to clear the original game. The absolute ruler of the Round Table with the lion heart.
Squeeze.
As soon as I reminded myself of my identity, which I had lost sight of for a while, my heart swelled and courage welled up in me.
“I-It’s not too late, so just say it. S-Say that was a mistake you made in your sleep—”
“Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.” Before my determination could ebb, I spoke. “There’s something wrong with your head right now.”
Yeah, and if there was a problem, the only solution was to fix it the way I did best.
“Stop talking and fight me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 346: Seclusion (1)
paragraphs: Objectively speaking, her specs were slightly superior to mine, and her equipment was overwhelmingly superior. Besides that, since she’d apparently spent over a year cutting off the heads of Noark’s adventurers in the war, she’d have more battle experience than me now. But there was no need to be scared because Erwen had made one mistake.
Slide.

That was distance. Contract with the Elemental Ruler or not, as long as she was an archer whose life depended on maintaining a proper distance, I had the advantage at close-range. The fact that this was a hidden room where all four windows were blocked off was also a point in my favor, not to mention that my opponent wasn’t in her right mind right now.
“F-Fight you? How can I, with you—th-that’s not possible...”
Jeez, and you were saying all kinds of things about me being an evil spirit earlier.
I didn’t intend to give her long to think. If we both started exerting our full power, it’d be tough to end this quickly.
Squeeze.
After making a fist with my watermelon-sized hand, I kicked off the floor and dashed forward.
Whoom!
My punch, which was supposed to be a surprise, crossed empty air. I guessed she was an agility character after all.
Well, I expected things to go sort of like this.
Boom.
The moment I skidded to a stop with a stomp on the ground, a vortex swirled to life around me and began throwing things all over the place.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm.]
Since it wasn’t being used with Transcendence, the radius was only five yards, but it was enough to cover the room we were currently in.
Whiiiiiip!
Bed, blanket, pillow, bookcase, table, carpet—anything weighing less than a thousand pounds was blown around by the strong wind. Of course, Erwen was included in that.
“...This is—!”

Erwen, who had once fought a Storm Gush on Farune Island, was staring at me with obvious shock in her eyes. She must be wondering why this skill was suddenly popping up here. I deliberately didn’t show it to her when I was verifying my identity since it wasn’t a skill I originally had.
Whooom!
But Erwen hadn’t been sitting around twiddling her thumbs all these years, either. She immediately started to adapt. She called forth a wind spirit and began resisting the pull of the vortex.
“S-Stop...!”
Stop what?
“I told you. There’s something wrong with your head.”
Maintaining Eye of the Storm, I jogged forward and threw my fist at her.
Whooom!

Of course, even as I did that, I didn’t think the fist would reach Erwen. She would definitely step back to avoid it, then I could use Giantization to instantly lengthen my arm. Well, that should have been the case, anyway.
Plop.

Once Eye of the Storm ended, the various pieces of furniture and fixtures fluttering in the air fell to the floor all at once. Erwen was standing in front of my outstretched fist with her eyes screwed shut.
“Why...?” At this point, I had no choice but to ask. If I hadn’t managed to stop it midway, my fist would definitely have hit Erwen. But why? “Why didn’t you avoid it?”
Erwen slowly opened her eyes and said, tearfully, “Because... then you’d get hurt...”
Huh?

I was busy feeling lightheaded at the sudden turn of events when Erwen continued woefully, “You’re right, Mister... To be honest, I’ve noticed as well... that there’s something wrong with me... But, still. Yes, still... How can I hurt you?”
Uh... I see?
Plop.
As I watched her tears flow down her cheeks and to the floor, I was rendered speechless. This made me look like the bad guy.

After that, I had an honest conversation with Erwen. At times the conversation got too wordy, and at times we got off track and spent a long while talking about something off-topic, but to sum it up briefly, it went like this:

She hadn’t been in her right mind since I ‘died.’ She had been able to endure a long, painful period fueled by a single-minded drive for revenge, and she took up the mantle of pureblood of her tribe. As soon as she got stronger, the war broke out, and considering it an opportunity to get revenge, she sought dangerous battlefields without sparing a thought to her own safety. That was around the time she made a contract with the Elemental Ruler.
“I admit it was excessive, but I never meant to keep you prisoner, Mister.”

The reason why she boarded up the windows and only let me take walks at night was because she was so worried. A rumor that I was an evil spirit had already spread through the city, after all. It was a kind of obsession. Apparently, she couldn’t shake the thought that she might lose me again.
“Then Amelia?”

“...Same for her. I can’t trust her. I’m confident that I would really never betray you under any circumstances... but I don’t know about that woman, so, I was anxious... But I-I won’t do anything like that from now on. I won’t stop you from making her your comrade. Though it still makes me anxious, to be honest...”
“...Since you don’t want me to interfere...”
Hmm, is she being sincere? It doesn’t seem like she’s lying or anything...

I was worried she might suddenly blow a fuse again and lose her mind, but she seemed like she was being genuine right now, especially given what she said next. “The essences. I don’t care if you tell me to erase them at the temple tomorrow. But... that will mean I can’t protect you anymore...”
Most of Erwen’s essences had been acquired through her war achievements. Did it really not matter to her if I told her she had to erase them all?
“...Why would you do all that?”
“Because... I don’t want you to hate me.”

I still couldn’t accept that explanation. Was our connection so deep? Honestly, there was only one possibility that came to mind, but I couldn’t really say something like that in this situation, so I didn’t bother to voice it aloud.
“...It would be best not to erase those essences.”
“...I’ll do as you say.”
“Instead, consider erasing some if something like this happens again.”
“Yes, if you want—”
“I’m not saying this for me, I’m saying it for you.”

That statement was me being 100 percent sincere. Erwen was not normal right now. If I whispered her sweet nothings every day and cleverly played on her desire not to be hated, it wouldn’t be difficult for me to use her to my liking. But, again, that was not right. That was not how a relationship between comrades was supposed to work. I’d learned that from a wizard in the Labyrinth of Larcaz.
“For... me?”
I spoke firmly. “Yes, for you... no, to be more specific, for the sake of our relationship.”
“O-Our relationship...”
“...Got it?”
When I noticed she looked somewhat dazed, I grabbed Erwen’s shoulder to confirm she was paying attention, and she answered, “Y-Yes... hehe.”
...She properly understood me, right?

After that conversation, my day-to-day didn’t change drastically. I continued to live a secluded life. I only went out to the yard at night to get some air and did not remove the boards on the windows. The only thing that changed was Erwen’s attitude.
“Mister, this is the equipment you used.”
Before, she alluded that hiding out at home was not a problem, but Erwen now began to help me out more actively. That started with equipment.

“This is...” Though No. 2988: Mark of the Guard Corps had no special stats or effects, when worn, it provided a whopping 50 percent boost to a shield’s Shock Absorption, making it a core item for a Shield Barbarian. “...You had this?”
“Yes, there was no way I could sell it.” Apparently, Raven took charge of distributing my estate, but after receiving the earrings in the mail, Erwen had held onto them instead of selling them.
“But, why are you giving this to me now? I’m sure I asked you about my equipment before.”
“Sorry... I hid it because I didn’t want you to go into the labyrinth.”
So, I wasn’t just imagining things. If I hadn’t hashed things out properly with her, I might have really been trapped in this house...

The thought gave me chills, but would she really have done that? I threw away my discomfort and looked into something else. I figured all of my equipment had been sold on the market a long time ago, but now I was starting to change my mind. The other guys might have kept things too.
“...I’ll have to look into that in detail. But what I know for sure is that Abman Urikfried would have sold everything.”
“Abman?”
“Yes. I heard he took relatively meaningless items instead of the equipment you wore. Like the sub-space ring.”
Hmm, I see.
Since he was hesitant to sell the things I wore, it seemed he made a point to take only the equipment he could sell without guilt. That was a little disappointing, but not critical.
If these earrings and that item are in good condition, that means I can just acquire the rest again, anyway.
Only the shield and armor would need to be remade. The other Numbers Items I used to have weren’t that expensive, either.
“Do you know who took my necklace?”
“Ah, the thing that transforms mana stones into strange things?”

“Yeah.” The official name was No. 7777: Garphas’ Necklace. This necklace had the ability to convert a mana stone inserted into the necklace into something random. You could call it a gacha version of alchemy, which turned mana stones into bread, water, metal, etcetera. It wasn’t a particularly valuable item—at least, not until you had enough money to hold a hidden special event.
“To be honest... I wanted that as well. So I sent that wizard—Arua Raven—a letter about it.”
“And? Who took it?”
“Missha Karlstein.”

“Ah...” As soon as I heard the name, air whooshed out of my mouth. She was the only one of my old clanmates whose whereabouts were unknown. Well, I did hear she was with Baekho from the Round Table, but that really only made me more confused. It all felt like a puzzle.
Still, I decided to look on the bright side as much as possible. Missha and I had quite a fond relationship, after all. There was a good chance she hadn’t sold it.
Hmm... or, maybe that’s not the case, either?
I couldn’t be sure as it had been two and a half years. I decided to think about it later.
Anyway, I think Ainar would have taken the armor and weapons... Then I guess the rest went to Raven?
As I was contemplating the whereabouts of my scattered equipment, one item soon came to mind.
Ah, the Orb of Fire... I wonder what happened to that?

That was the sole binding-type item in my possession. If the orb had recognized my disappearance from this time period as a death, it would have been possible for them to sell it, but if that wasn’t the case, there was a high possibility they just kept it.
If it’s the latter, Raven is also the one who’s most likely to have it...
“Whew...” The more I thought about it, the more I sighed. Though I’d gotten some things out of my trip to the past, I’d gotten a lot of present issues I had to sort through in return.
“Mister, aren’t you eating?”

“Ah... I was just thinking about something.” I stopped my train of thought there and had a spoonful of the takeaway Erwen brought back. Finishing my meal quickly, I took time to discuss some things with Erwen.
“What are you planning to do next?”
“I have to quash the false accusations of me being an evil spirit first.”
“Should I... pull some strings to prepare a meeting...?”

Erwen suggested I prove myself in front of all the royals, but I refused. My reasoning was that it was too early. I’d have to do it one day, but I still couldn’t shake the feeling that something political was at play in my case.
“I think I have to approach that part more carefully. Plus, if anything goes wrong, it could end up implicating the entire elf tribe.”
“...Y-You’re so kind.”
“Ahem. Anyway, that is why I want to ask. Instead of worrying about Raven and Abman, can you dig up some information about that?”
“Yes! I will.”
After the discussion was over, Erwen left for her people’s holy land and I lay on the sofa to take a nap. Which was when it happened.
Knock, knock.
Someone knocked on the front door. Erwen had no reason to knock.

chapters.title: Chapter 347: Seclusion (2)
paragraphs: Sweat beaded on the forehead of Magic Engineer Yurven Havellion, a wizard who was the head of a school and respected by many others in the world of innovation. That was how tricky his current task was, trying to defy the laws of the spiritual world.

“Damn it,” the robed man muttered at the jewel laying on his workbench. It was the one he’d received from an old man he met shortly after coming to this world, an object that could be considered the server and system for the spirit world now named Ghost Busters. “What on earth went wrong?”

An infinite number of magical circuits, large and small, were intertwined inside this small jewel. The man had proven himself by analyzing and studying this thing, and had created the Ghost Busters of today by modifying each of the circuits he identified.
“...As I thought, this method will never work.”

The man continued to inject mana into the jewel, modifying the circuit for a long time before sighing in apparent defeat. Actually, it was kind of funny to be disappointed. There was no way something that he hadn’t been able to achieve for decades could suddenly be achieved in a few days. His biggest achievement as of late was updating the system to secretly view the nicknames of players who had entered anonymous chatrooms using his admin privileges.
Ringggg.
Just then, his personal pager vibrated. There was no need to even check who was calling.
“Yes, Soul Queen? Were there any issues related to me?”
“No... there is no talk about you anywhere yet.”

“...I see.” The man felt both annoyed and relieved at the same time. This was because his identity, which he had kept secret for twenty years, had been revealed in such an unexpected place. “Please continue to keep an eye on that. These rumors must be suppressed before they grow bigger. I will continue to look for a way to learn the identities of the other members.”
“All right. And... I’m sorry.”

The man fell silent at the apology from the woman in the crystal ball. He couldn’t say there was nothing to be sorry about, even just as empty words. “Then... let me know if any issues arise in the future.”
“All right, get some rest.”
The man finished the call and headed for the workbench again.
I think it could be possible by changing the circuit to store people’s location information when they connect to the server...
The man analyzed the jewel’s complex internal circuitry. As always, the answer to his problems lay within this jewel.
Knock, knock.
The moment I heard the knock, I immediately sat up in bed.
Who is that? Erwen wouldn’t be knocking, so I’m sure it’s an outsider... But why would an outsider knock on that door and not the main one? God damn it.
Holding my breath, I kept myself low and crept over to the door as quietly as possible.
Drag, slide.
Right at that moment, there was a rattling sound on the doorknob before the lock was released.
Creak.
The door opened slowly. Whoever my opponent was, I balled up my fists with the intention of taking them down first, but I froze when I spotted the intruder.
“...Luckily, you were inside.”
“Amelia!”
“Ugh! I-I told you not to run at me out of nowhere...!”
It’s because I’m glad to see you. Jeez, making me embarrassed.
“...Come in, quickly.”
“Excuse me...” Amelia didn’t seem to like the reunion hug so I skipped over it, and she hurried into the house.
There were so many things I wanted to ask, but I decided to go in order. “How did you know I was here?”
“I waited in front of the bank and followed the elf.”
“Huh? But then why...?”
“There was no opening to approach you.”
Eh? That girl is always away at the elven holy land during the day.
When I told her this, Amelia shook her head. “No way. That woman was always near the house.”
Chills ran down my spine. “...Uh, then she never went to the holy land?”

“You... didn’t know? But it seems she’s had a change of heart recently and she’s been disappearing somewhere. I didn’t come right away because I watched the house for a few days to make sure it wasn’t a trap.”
That put me somewhat at ease. Said change of heart must have been the conversation we had not long ago.
“So... how did it go with Blood Spirit? I’m sure it must have been hard for her to accept that you came back alive. Same for the evil spirit issue.”
“Ah, that worked out fine.” I briefly summarized what happened with Erwen and told her just the important parts.
Amelia looked a little surprised. “It doesn’t matter to her if you’re an evil spirit or not, huh? What an uncharacteristic way of thinking for an adventurer from the overworld.”
“She’s gotten a little... weird. Back when I first met her, she probably wouldn’t ever have thought that way.”
“Well, I don’t think so.”
“Huh?”
“She didn’t stop seeking revenge for you even after the announcement. She must have come to the conclusion a long time ago that it doesn’t matter what your identity is.”
Hmm, that’s possible.
“Anyway, I hammered it into her that I’m not an evil spirit. You never know what will happen later.”
Amelia chuckled. “Then I’m the only one in the world who knows your identity?”
“No, there is one more person.”
“...I thought Missha Karlstein doesn’t know you are an evil spirit?”

“It’s someone else. He’s not even a local to begin with. He’s from my home country.” There was no reason to hide it and there was plenty of room for it to become an issue in the future, so I told her about Baekho.
Her reaction was a little weird. “Baekho Lee...? That man is from your home country?” It was like she had just heard something about someone she knew quite well.
Hmm, come to think of it, there were quite a few people who knew about Baekho at the Round Table too.
I had intended to sneak the question in with Erwen, but it was better to just get the information from her. “Do you know him?”
“...Of course.”
“True, since you came to this time period much earlier than me, you might have heard of him. Ah, but how long has it been since you got back?”
“It was two years ago.”
“Oh, then you were there and back on a one-to-one ratio—”
“But when I returned doesn’t matter. I knew about that guy a long time ago.”
Huh? You knew Baekho from before that?
When I looked at her for more information, Amelia opened her mouth. “Do you remember that I told you I used to work on a team with an evil spirit for over a year? That evil spirit was Baekho.”
Who the hell is this guy? He’s literally everywhere.

Amelia had met Baekho about five years ago. Apparently, she deliberately approached him aboveground under orders from the lord of the castle. At the time, there had been suspicion he was an evil spirit, so this mission had been to confirm that. If he were an evil spirit, it would be possible to use that to control him.
“Adventurers who could use auras were rare, so joining his party wasn’t difficult. I stayed on his team for about a year.”

Amelia said she obtained Self-Replication from Doppelganger Forest and cleared the Hundred-Color Temple on the third floor all around that time. Wow, no wonder she knew about all the hidden features. If she was with Baekho, it made sense.
“So? What happened after?”

“Nothing special. When I couldn’t find substantial evidence after over a year, the lord of the castle lost interest. I received a new mission and left the party with an excuse. Then... I heard the news later.”
“News?”

“I don’t know the details. At the time, the incident was thoroughly concealed by the palace. All I know is that his identity was revealed by a teammate’s betrayal, and many people died in the labyrinth that day. That was all I could find out.”
Afterward, Amelia said the palace destroyed all their records of Baekho and controlled the flow of information for several years to ensure his existence was forgotten by the city.
One question here. “Then how did you know the name Baekho Lee?”

“That was a relatively recent thing. It seems he really had a falling out with the palace. He’s been showing up everywhere and introducing himself as Baekho Lee. Ah, for reference, he used to use a pseudonym, or was just called ‘him’ by everyone else.”
I see... I never thought someone around me would know so much about Baekho’s past.
“What was he like before?”
“Well, we weren’t very close. I didn’t like his loose tongue and behavior. Instead, he had a very close relationship with the others.”
“Close relationship?”
“Yes, like the team you made.”

The more I listened to stories about Baekho out of curiosity, the weirder I felt. “What? Everyone on his team was female? And he even dated all of them? Wow, was this bastard running some harem in the labyrinth?”
“Harem? I don’t know what that is, but aren’t your teammates all women?”
What was this girl saying? Mr. Bear’s spot was firmly established. Besides, during our Team Half-Wit days, everyone had been a guy except Missha.
“If you say so. Let’s just go with that.”
“I’m not just saying that, that’s the truth. It just so happened that the team ended up like that because I selected people based on capability and aptitude. I never saw them as romantic interests—”

“You don’t have to explain. I don’t care at all. You’re from a different country in the first place. I don’t know what kind of place Korea is, but I suppose that part is similar to the aristocratic culture there.”
Korea is a normal monogamous culture... What does she think Korea is?

For some reason, I felt like Baekho and I had properly ruined Korea’s image, but I just decided not to make any excuses. It didn’t really matter that much, after all. Now that I’d heard enough stories, it was time to move on to the next topic.
“Anyway, Amelia. What was written on the note you left at the bank?”
“What do you mean? It was just as I wrote.”
“Ah, the letter Erwen handed me was ripped at the bottom. I could only read, ‘The Demon Grinder is...’ and couldn’t read the rest.”
“...I-I see.” When the topic turned to my big and precious hammer, Amelia looked noticeably dismayed. “No wonder you didn’t mention that... It was because you couldn’t read it...”
“That’s why I’m anxious. Tell me. What happened to the hammer? Is it okay—”
“The hammer is fine.” Amelia firmly cut me off.
Slide.
Avoiding my eyes, she added meekly, “...In the vault of the collateral loans department of the Alminus Exchange.”
Ha...
A heavy silence fell between us. Even Amelia, an ever-unflappable woman, was aware of her wrongdoings and was avoiding my gaze. In the end, I was the one who spoke first. “...So why did you sell it?”
I’m sure there was a good reason for it. This is Amelia we’re talking about—
“I should make a correction.”
“Hmm?”
“I didn’t sell it, I used it as collateral to borrow money.”
Are you being serious?
When I glared at her, Amelia cleared her throat. “I need to make that clear so that it doesn’t lead to misunderstandings in the—”
“Uh huh, just answer my questions. Why did you sell—no, give my hammer away as collateral? For what, exactly?”
“...To protect you when you returned.”
Ha, I knew she was going to say that. I don’t know what it is, but there has to be a good reason why she had to—
“I bought an essence at the auction house.”
There was a long silence.
“...What?”
“Don’t worry,” Amelia rushed to explain. “As long as I repay the money by the date the loan is set to mature, I can get it back.”

That revived me a bit. True, you could do stuff like this if you needed money. It was obvious she’d got the Twin Hydra’s Dual Rule with the cash from the loan. It was a good enough essence to get if it could be bought with money.
But I needed to check what I needed to check. “...When’s the repayment date?”
“In two months.”
“And the money?”
“I don’t have it right now.”
“And your plan to raise the money?”
“...I had one.”
So, we were talking past tense. A new quest was added to my already busy schedule.

chapters.title: Chapter 348: Seclusion (3)
paragraphs: Everyone was bound to have their own plans, though there was no guarantee they would work out. Amelia was the same way.

“There was an organization I’ve always had an eye on. These people disguise themselves as a health care station and sell opium at a high price in the shadows... I was originally planning to rob them for the cash.”
“And?”
“While I was tracking down their base, the Public Peace Agency barged in.”
I had nothing to say. Should I have said this was very like her? Should I have been glad this was still much more wholesome than robbing a bank?
When I chuckled, Amelia snuck in an apology. “...This was my mistake, so I’ll figure out a solution somehow.”
What was this girl saying? “It’s fine,” I said firmly. “Why would you solve it on your own?”

If she hadn’t extended the storage period of the vault in the first place, the item would have disappeared into thin air a long time ago. Amelia had about half the share of that hammer, too, since we had been in the middle of hunting as a party when it dropped. More importantly, it was ridiculous to hold her responsible when she was the one who found the money to purchase Vol-Herchan’s essence for me.
“We’ll solve the money issue together. Got it?”
“...Because we’re comrades?”
Oh, she knows to say things like that?
“Yes, because we’re comrades. If there’s a problem, we look for a way to solve it together, not decide who’s to blame.”
“...Okay.”
On that note, we discussed solutions after that. It was a difficult amount to raise in two months by normal means, but it wasn’t impossible. The stocks I had bought two and a half years ago paid off.
“Borrow money from that elf, huh? Certainly, if she had enough money to purchase a mansion like this, that could be a possibility. But is that okay?”
“Huh? Is what okay?”
“That elf is also one of your comrades.”
“Ahem...”
Jeez, hitting me where it hurts.
“Amelia, it looks like you don’t know this because you’ve been alone for a long time, but comrades help each other when they’re going through a hard time. Got it?”
“So... that’s how you treat your comrades.”
I never said I’m just going to take her help. I’ll pay it back, with interest on top.
“Anyway, enough about that. Let’s talk about something else.”
“You decided the conversation wasn’t going in your favor.”
“Am I wrong? That’s how I remember it usually was whenever you changed the subject.”
It was such a sound argument that I had nothing to refute it. But was her personality always like this? Why did I get the nagging feeling she was making fun of me?
“Whatever, just say what you were going to say, Yandel.”

Seeing as she wasn’t giving me the chance to argue, I suspected she was intentionally teasing me. But since I only had an assumption backing me up, I just let it slide for now. There were more important issues to address, after all.
“Ah, it’s nothing special, I wanted to talk about how to introduce you to Erwen.”
I refuse to let a Party Kill happen on my watch.
Tap-tap, tap-tap, tap-tap.
As I tapped a steady beat on the table, Amelia clicked her tongue. “That’s very annoying. Why don’t you calm down? Is that elf so scary?”
“W-Who said I’m scared? Erwen listens to me.”

I was just a little nervous. I told Erwen I was going to take in Amelia as a comrade, but a person’s impulses couldn’t always be controlled. I didn’t want to see Amelia explode again, especially if it was her main body this time and not a doppelganger.
Tick, tick.
Time passed and right when I was starting to feel hungry, I heard the main gate in the yard closing.
Clunk.
Erwen was home. Her hands were probably full of food to feed me for dinner tonight.
Step, step.
The sound of an elf’s characteristic light footsteps crossed the yard and quickly approached.
Tap.

She stopped in front of the front door. It was kind of a strange thing. There was definitely a rattling sound and the doorknob turned, but why was the door not opening? And why did her excited humming stop?
The moment the question popped into my mind, Erwen murmured, “Open door... A woman’s scent.”
At those words, I immediately stood up. I had a feeling that if I launched into the surprise event I had prepared like this, it would end up being a disaster.
“E-Erwen! You’re home!” When I quickly went to meet her at the door, Erwen ignored my greeting and glanced around the interior.
Then her eyes honed in on Amelia inside. “Amelia Rainwales.”
“Long time no see, Blood Spirit. Is this our first meeting in the city?”
“...How are you here?”

“I followed you from the bank. You’ve gotten better at stealth magic but it looks like you don’t use it often in real life. You’d better be more on guard in the future since you don’t live here alone.”
“...Should I kill her?” Erwen mumbled to herself.
“Um, Erwen?”
“Ah, sorry. I forgot to say it in my head.”
“Uh... r-really? Yeah, that happens. First... let’s sit. We’re going to work together from now on, so we can’t be so awkward around each other.”
“Okay.” Surprisingly, Erwen quickly calmed down and sat at the table as requested. In a casual tone, she said, “So I just have to get along with this woman from now on?”
“Call her by her name, not ‘this woman.’”
“Then I’ll use her last name. It’s Rainwales, right?”
“That’s right. I’ll call you Tersia too.”
“Okay.” When Erwen gave a one-word answer, the conversation ended there.
It was my turn to step up. “Erwen, as I said last time, Amelia will be working with us from now on.”
“What about the identity issue?”
“You don’t need to worry about that part. I’ve prepared one that will work while waiting for Yandel to return,” answered Amelia.
“...Why didn’t you tell me he was alive sooner?”
“What a ridiculous question. How could I trust you with that?”
“What? You’ve only been with him for half a year at most.”
“Hmm, from what I understand, your time with Yandel in the labyrinth was less than half a year?”
Why are you guys talking without me again?

“Now, everyone, calm down.” I quickly intervened in the conversation. “I don’t know what exactly happened between you two in that time, but since it was all a misunderstanding, why don’t we clear the air right here and now?” I shot Amelia a look that told her to stop being touchy and start yielding to Erwen.

“I don’t know, I have no grudges. Of course, thanks to her, I once got my legs blown off on the sixth floor and had to cling to a board for three days because I couldn’t swim. But I survived in the end.”
...So, you had a reason to be touchy.
“...I wondered how you escaped from the boat in that state.”
“Erwen.”

“Don’t worry. I don’t particularly hold any grudges, either. It’s just that the body of an adventurer from Noark that I finally defeated after all kinds of trouble got snatched from right under my nose. Ah, should I mention how my arm got sliced when I followed her?”
“But I didn’t kill you.”
“You’re saying that like you could have. You were the one who ran away as soon as support showed up for me.”
“Well... I did achieve my mission. I was in a tight financial situation but thanks to selling that man’s equipment, I was able to buy this dagger here.”
Okay, let’s give up on being on good terms. No one said that a team has to get along, right?
I forced a smile and ended the conversation. “Haha, you fight over really trivial things! Now, shake hands quickly and make up.”

In whatever case, it was always the person who smiled who was top-notch. After Erwen and Amelia shook hands with sour looks on their faces, I moved on to the next item of business—straightforward, like the barbarian I was.
“Erwen, can you lend me some money?”
“Money for what...?” I told her about the Demon Grinder, no holds barred, and Erwen’s expression hardened. “So, you want me to pay for the essence this woman bought with my own money?”
“I guess you could look at it that way?”
“...Sorry, but that’s going to be difficult.”
“Huh?”
“Don’t get me wrong. It’s not because I don’t want to.”
Then what is it?
When I gave her a questioning look, Erwen quietly admitted, like a sinner at a confessional, “I... don’t have much money now... Really.”
Ah, makes sense... Come to think of it, she mentioned she barely managed to buy this house with the money she extorted by threatening the chief of her tribe.

Still, I asked just in case, “Then what about using this house as collateral to borrow money?” I felt like trash for even suggesting it, but what could I do? I had to prepare for the worst-case scenario.
“...Th-this house? Th-this house is full of memories...”
“We just have to pay it back on time, right?”
“Yandel, you really—”
Erwen interrupted. “Don’t say anything to him. This is all your fault in the first place. How shameless.”
“What?”
“Got it? So you don’t have to be sorry, Mister. A house... can be b-bought again later...”
But your hands are shaking...
“...I’m sorry.”
“I told you not to say that. This is for you, after all, Mister.”
Anyway, it was decided that the Demon Grinder would be recovered using a reverse collateral-blocking technique. It was time to devise the next part of our plan.
“Whatever we do from now on, we’ll need to secure funds first.”
“Yes. If you’re going to enter the labyrinth again, you’ll need new equipment too. If we have money... we’ll be able to keep this house...”
“Wait, labyrinth? I’m sure lifting the false accusations comes first?” asked Amelia.
Oh, that...

“I’m going to put that off for a while because there’s something suspicious about it.” When I told her about the questions and concerns I had, Amelia nodded in understanding. It seemed she picked up on the strange vibe too. “Anyway, that’s why I want you to find me a suitable identity.”

“Finding an identity won’t be difficult, but it’ll be like trying to hide an elephant in a room. It may have been more than two years since your death, but there are still many people who remember you.”

In other words, that meant there was a high probability my identity would be exposed even if I used an iron helmet. This wasn’t like twenty years ago when I was a nobody. The second I used something like Giantization, people would think of Bjorn Yandel.
“Hmm, I still think I just have to be careful in the labyrinth...”
“Maybe for one or two months, but if it goes on much longer, there will definitely be those who recognize—”
“Wait, why don’t you take an essence?” Erwen interrupted.
“An essence?”

“Like the one Miss Ainar took. There are essences that reduce your height. If you shorten your height a bit and introduce yourself as a human, I don’t think anyone will notice.” Erwen studied Amelia’s reaction the second the words left her mouth. It seemed she was on guard against any criticism Amelia might send her way.

Contrary to her expectations, though, Amelia acknowledged Erwen’s idea and even magnanimously praised it. “Certainly, if this is going to go on longer than one or two months, that would be a much safer way to hide your identity in the long term. You came up with a pretty good solution.”

It seemed the praise felt a bit strange to Erwen. “...That’s because it’s related to Mister,” she responded coldly, turning her head. It was a sight that would warm any spectator’s heart, but I had no choice but to interrupt.
“Um... Sorry to say this all of a sudden but, I don’t have space to take an essence.” I still had a long way to go to get to level seven, and I didn’t have an essence I could erase.
As soon as I explained my situation, Amelia chuckled. “Manticore. I’m sure you’ve mentioned before that that’s an essence you’ll have to erase someday.”
...You’re going to take my jump button?

chapters.title: Chapter 349: Seclusion (4)
paragraphs: I definitely took the Manticore essence with the thought of erasing it someday. When I purchased that essence at the auction, I even contemplated whether to erase this one or Corpse Golem.
“Um, Amelia... if I get rid of this, my Mana Resistance will drop and I’ll be vulnerable to things like magic...”

At first, I was reluctant about my sole movement-related skill Leap disappearing, but that wasn’t the real problem. It was the absence of Mana Resistance. Until I got my hands on the essence of Bellarios, my ability to tank would be greatly hindered.
But I can’t erase the Storm Gush.

The Storm Gush was a whopping rank-three essence. I’d have to erase it someday, but that time would come after the Burrow Island event at the earliest. It’d be possible to use that essence to skirt through it, and my second core ability besides Giantization would appear there.
Man, then what do I do?

My worries deepened. Rather than giving up an essence, giving up on a disguise seemed like an option to me. It was clear there was something fishy about the moves the palace had made, but it might not turn out to be a big hurdle to clearing the accusation on my name.
I’m sure they won’t kill me to keep me quiet or anything.
“Ah, I didn’t say this because I’m sure you know, but even if it’s proven that you are not an evil spirit, the palace won’t just take kindly to that,” said Amelia.
“Hmm?”
“Why do you look confused? That will be the equivalent of leaving a blemish on the palace’s credibility since they confirmed the rumor.”
Ugh... now I have to think.
I asked for Erwen’s and Amelia’s opinions as it was difficult to make a decision. “What do you guys think I should do?”
Erwen suggested I take the essence. “I... think it would be best to stay as hidden as possible.”
“Your reason?”
“...Just a feeling.”
So, an intuition. When I turned to Amelia, she shared her thoughts too.
“I agree with Tersia.”
“Your reason?”
“It’s not like there’s much to be gained by clearing your name right now.”
Of course there is. I wouldn’t have to erase my essence.
Just as I was about to say this, Amelia continued, “It’s been two years. You’re not thinking your former clanmates will come back right away, are you?”
Erwen agreed with that. “I don’t know about Miss Ainar, but it will definitely be hard for Arua Raven to come back even if she hears of your return. She belongs to the royal military now, after all.”

Mr. Bear would be in a similar situation. Since he joined another clan, it would be difficult for him to leave. I didn’t even have information on Missha aside from the fact that she was now Baekho’s teammate.
They’re not wrong in that sense.
I paused the conversation there and repeatedly cycled through the pros and cons of both options. It didn’t take as long as I thought.
According to the information from the Round Table, the palace will soon conscript the nobles.

Most would send mercenaries they had stockpiled in their stead, but coming from an adventuring background, I’d have no choice. I would have to join the war straight away and follow the instructions of my superiors.
I soon made a decision. “I... will erase my essence.”
My jump button...

Now that my future course of action had been decided, it was time to move on to the next item of business. What essence should I take? Something I realized over the course of this discussion was these two had one thing in common.
“I think an Imp’s essence would be good. It’s small, but it comes with Mana Resistance too.”
“But that’s a rank-seven essence so it’s actually harder to find at the Exchange. The Dwarf Eater’s essence would be better. Plus, it raises Bone Density like Miss Ainar’s, so it’ll suit you too.”
“And, what, you have the money to buy a rank-four essence? I think the rank-five Altsmoror would be better.”
“Ah, Altsmoror? That won’t do. That has a fatal side effect,” said Erwen.
“Side effect?” Erwen glanced at me before whispering something to Amelia. I couldn’t hear what she said, but Amelia looked at me afterward and dismissed that option with a, “That could be an issue.”
Why are they so interested in my essence situation?

I chuckled and cut off their conversation. “Stop. I’ve already decided on something.” Among the essences that could reduce the size of my body, I had selected three main candidates based on which had the best stats and skills. “Erwen, find out how much money you can borrow from the bank with the house as collateral tomorrow. Amelia, you go to the Exchange and see if the essence I mentioned is there.”
“Okay.”
“Then let’s eat. I’m starving.”
Wrapping up the conversation there, the three of us shared the dinner Erwen brought.
“...You’re going to stay here starting today?”
“Looks like there are plenty of empty rooms. Is that a problem?”
“I’d prefer you draw a line between your work life and your personal life.”
“Hah, you guys, stop it. I’m tired, let’s just sleep. Amelia, you can use any of the spare rooms over there.”

There was a small snafu when Amelia came back to the house with all her stuff instead of staying at her inn, but it didn’t turn into a major issue. That was how what was a strangely difficult day came to an end.
“Mister! I’ll see you later!”

Starting the next day, Erwen and Amelia went out each morning to do their part, and I spent my days living a secluded life in this dark house. Simply put, that meant I spent most of my time sleeping. Thankfully, however, a collateral loan that was just the right size hit our bank account three days later, and I was able to use that money to retrieve the Demon Grinder the bank was holding as collateral.
“...Heh, do you like it that much?”
Of course I do. This is my number one treasure from now on.
[You have equipped No. 87: Kraul’s Demon Grinder. Your total Item Level has increased by +4800.]

Anyway, the good news didn’t end there. Just in time, the essence I was looking for came on sale at the Exchange. Well, it was my second choice, not my first, but it didn’t make a meaningful difference. It wasn’t an essence I’d be using for all that long, anyway.
The price is just right too.

I used up almost all the money I had left over after retrieving the Demon Grinder to purchase the essence. The order for the custom-made shield I’d be using in the labyrinth had already been put in by Erwen, and the rest of my equipment would be made cheap with tier-one materials, so I figured there wouldn’t be much money spending going forward.
...Ah, I guess there’s one thing left. Please, no one recognize me.
Once the essence was purchased, I visited the temple the next day. It was the Tovera Church, one of the three religions. I was nervous about going to Reatlas since I’d been there so many times.
“If we go in together, we’ll stand out more.”
“Go ahead, Mister...”
“Don’t draw attention to yourself,” said Amelia.

This was a small temple where 90 percent of the visitors were ordinary people, unlike the Great Temple which had decent attendance. Still, I was quite worried about revealing my face to erase the essence.

Thankfully, the old priest in charge of the removal process didn’t recognize me. “Haha, you were born with an excellent build for a human. You would have achieved great things if you had been a knight.”
[The Essence of the Manticore that was absorbed into your soul has been removed. Some stats obtained through the passive skill Inheritance are permanently acquired.]

The essence removal I had been so worried about went off without a hitch. I paid exactly twice as much as I paid last time and hurried back home. Then I opened the stopper on the test tube I had purchased earlier.
[The Essence of Gachabone has seeped into your soul.]
The default stats that came with the essence of the rank-six monster Gachabone were simple.
[Your Sixth Sense has increased by +40. Your Physical Resistance has increased by +15. Your Dark Resistance has increased by +30. Your Accuracy has increased by +45.]
They were ambiguous stats if you wanted to play a specific class.
[Your Bone Density has increased by +110.]
The Bone Density stat would give me a human physique. However, there was a penalty.
[Your Luck has decreased by -50. Your Control has decreased by -30.]

Luck increased the probability of random factors like critical hits. Control was helpful for preventing status effects like the psychological spell Fear. Now that they had gone down, they’d have the opposite effect, though.
“Oh.”

When the essence finished absorbing, the two people with me had strange reactions. To be honest, I was the one feeling the strangest. Our eye levels were not that different now. Amelia was around 5′6″, I believe? Then did I shrink to around six feet? As I wondered this, Erwen averted her eyes.
“...Do I look that weird?”
“N-No. That’s not it...”
“Then what?”
“I-I think... it will be quicker for you to see for yourself...” Erwen pointed to the mirror and I moved toward it, holding my baggy pants up with my hand.
There was no longer a strong barbarian warrior standing there, only a tall, handsome human man. “...Is that me?”
I could see why Ainar had been so depressed back then. I looked so weak, like I’d break something if I got hit with a hammer.
This essence... should I erase it?
That was how dreadful my reflection in the mirror was. No wonder Erwen had averted her eyes when she saw me.
“Um... Mister, what’s wrong? Your shoulders suddenly dropped...”
As I was busy feeling depressed, Erwen asked why and I answered honestly. How could I go outside like this? Even Erwen couldn’t look at me properly.
“H-Huh? Y-You’re mistaken! That’s not why I was averting my eyes!”
“Huh? Are you saying it’s not because you were holding back your laughter at my pathetic appearance?”
“No! Why would I do that?!”
“Then why did you do that?”
“B-Because,” Erwen replied quietly in an embarrassed tone, “you’re handsome...”
“What?”
Jeez, her taste is so conventional.

So the reason why she obsessed over me while I was a barbarian was not because she saw me as a man, but because she thought of me as her protector? To get a bigger sample size, I asked Amelia. “Do you think so too?”
“Well...” Amelia stared intently at my face before smirking and turning her head. “Well, it’s nice that my neck doesn’t hurt looking up at you anymore.”
Surprisingly, no one felt negatively about my current appearance. Had I been too influenced by a barbarian mindset?
Thinking about it more carefully, I suppose I’d be considered handsome by modern beauty standards.
Of course, even if that was the case, I had absolutely no desire to keep this appearance. Giantization was relative to your base size. A small body like this wouldn’t be efficient.
“Anyway, I’m going to check my new skill. Can you help me?”
I couldn’t keep wallowing about my shrunken body forever, so I decided to do what I needed to do. First things first: practicing using my skills.
Since I can’t exactly go out in the yard in broad daylight, I should just do this in the living room.
“Yes, I’ll help you, Mister. What should I do?”
“Oh, just hit me. Using a spirit or a special ability.”
“...Sorry?”
Uh... does this kid not know this essence’s passive?

That seemed to be the case, so I briefly explained the passive skill Probabilistic Retaliation. When you received damage that used some kind of resource, the damage had a certain probability of being ignored and reflected back. Whether magic, divine power, or spirits, this passive skill applied to anything that used a person’s resources. To be honest, the reason I chose this essence was largely because of this skill. Of course, it would be hard to make up for my reduced Mana Resistance with this alone, but this essence was the only one that had this kind of performance at this price. My first choice had actually been this same essence in a different color.
Anyway, the probability was about 10 percent...
For reference, this was a figure based on my reduced Luck stat. My default Luck stat—which I had no way of knowing for sure—could cause some margin of error, but it wouldn’t be huge.
“Um... then I’ll go ahead.” Once I finished explaining, Erwen summoned her spirits and started attacking me.
[You have taken Cold damage.]
[You have taken Cold damage.]
[You have taken Cold damage.]
“Erwen, change the attribute.”
“Okay!”
[You have taken Fire damage.]
[You have taken Fire damage.]
[You have taken Fire damage.]
What the—?
“W-Wait! Amelia, you try.”
“If you want. Your height is just right now.”
[You have been hit with Asura’s Kick.]
[You have been hit with Asura’s Kick.]
[You have been hit with Asura’s Kick.]
What is this? No, really, what is this?
“Aghhh! S-Stop!”
Why isn’t this working?

chapters.title: Chapter 350: Dark Continent (1)
paragraphs: The odds of Probabilistic Retaliation activating lay more or less at 10 percent. For reference, this probability didn’t go up just because you had Transcendence. That was because the 1.5 times increase in performance was instead applied to the amount of damage reflected back.
I mean, but still.
[You have been hit with Asura’s Kick.]
Just when I started to genuinely worry that I had been scammed and had taken a weird essence, the passive activated nearly a hundred kicks in.
[The Luck dwelling in your body has blocked the damage.]
