Probabilistic Retaliation activated, and a transparent veil sprouted over the target area as if to protect me.
[Your powerful luck reflects 150% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
A skeleton summoned right next to me imitated the kicking stance exactly and landed an Asura’s Kick on Amelia while releasing a roar, even though it didn’t have vocal cords.
“Gahhhcha!”
Hey, that’s the sound that it makes when there’s a critical success. Wait a minute, then this could really injure her.
I rushed forward but it was already too late.
Smack!
Startled by the sudden attack, Amelia wasn’t able to dodge the strike flying toward her and took it on the shoulder.
Shaaaaaa.
The skeleton disappeared in a burst of light after landing exactly one kick.
“Are you okay?!”
When I ran toward her in shock, Amelia took her hand off her shoulder and pushed me away. “Don’t be dramatic. I was just a little surprised.”
Surprised? Your shoulder is totally shattered.
“Erwen, bring me splints and bandages.”
“Ah, right...!”
Giving Amelia a potion was pointless because of her Source of Youth, so I adjusted the bone with my hand, and then bandaged it with a splint.
“I told you to dodge once the ability activated. If you can’t dodge it, at least kick gently.”
“...I did kick gently.”
Yeah right. And a critical success meant it reflected 100 percent of the original damage.
Ah... it would have been 150 percent because of Transcendence.

For reference, the amount of damage usually reflected was only 10 percent. Even if you factored in Transcendence, that was 15 percent. Since this skill summoned a skeleton to deliver the attack, it was possible to dodge it, so it wasn’t a very useful skill.
“Anyway, Amelia, you take a break.”
“Yes! I can help you now, Mister! I’m good at dodging. And blocking too!”
“...All right.”
When Erwen summoned a spirit again, Amelia slunk over to the sofa to sit, looking dejected.
[You have taken Fire damage.]
[You have taken Fire damage.]
[You have taken Fire damage.]
This time, the skill activated after ten tries.
[The Luck dwelling in your body has blocked the damage. Your ordinary luck reflects 15% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
A cute little skeleton once again popped into existence beside me and shot out flames. Since it wasn’t a critical success, it didn’t come with a unique sound effect.
Pop!
As Erwen dodged to the side to avoid the flames, the sparks hit the wall and flew everywhere.
“Oh, fire.”
“E-Erwen! Water spirit!”
“Ah, yes!”
That day, we almost lost our collateral house.
After experiencing a near-fire, we headed out to the yard at night to test my skill and obtained important data.
To start, it looks like there isn’t much of a margin of error in terms of the probability...

Unlike the first attempt, where success only came after nearly a hundred tries, after that, the skill activated an average of fifteen times later. The problem was that averages were just averages. There were many cases where it suddenly stopped activating even though it was working normally, and in those cases, I really had to get beaten up for a long time. I was pretty sure our record was 198 times.
How is that possible?
Even if the probability were 1 percent, those statistics wouldn’t make sense. And even after accumulating that huge stack, I didn’t end up getting a critical success.
Well, it feels like it’s working more often, though.

Anyway, after testing the passive followed by the active, the three of us spent every day planning for our quest. The number one objective of said plan was money. We took a short-term loan of six months to make up for our insufficient budget. The interest rates were high and if we didn’t repay this money on time, the house would be taken over by the bank. Was that why?

“Mister, I’m okay... you don’t have to overdo it...” Erwen seemed to have given up on keeping this house the moment it got used as collateral for the loan. She probably thought it would be difficult to raise the money in six months.
“I told you. I’m going to work as hard as I can.”
I had a conscience too. Since Erwen really liked this house, it was only right to try and protect it no matter what it took.
“But to raise that much money in such a short period of time... There would be no other option but the war.”
“Rainwales is right. None of us have boats. That means we can’t go to the sixth floor and we’ll have to stay on the fifth at most...”

“You don’t have to look at me like that. I think it’d be better for us to join the war too. Though I may be noticeable, as long as I don’t use Giantization, no one will think of Bjorn Yandel when they see me now.”
Without needing to talk it over for long, we decided to join the war. If we joined the royal military, we could travel straight to the seventh floor on a big ship.
At our level, seventh-floor monsters won’t be a problem, either.

All three of us were good at interpersonal combat, too, so we should be able to perform well in the war and collect bounties. No, bounties weren’t the main appeal. Our enemies would also be upper-middle-floor adventurers, so if we stripped their equipment and sold it, the income would be enormous.
Not only that... If all goes well, it might be possible to kill some seventh-floor monsters and reach level seven too.
Originally, gaining that amount of XP would only have been possible by clearing more than 60 percent of the sixth floor. This made things a bit easier.
Once I reach level seven, I can get an essence from Burrow Island.
After that, I could erase the Gachabone’s essence and move on to defeating a Bellarios.
If I reach level eight and get another essence, I’ll have to erase Storm Gush too. And the essence I’ll be consuming at level nine will be easier to farm after I grind for the Lord of the Floor.

As I was mapping out the direction my cultivation would take in the future, it made me feel strange. I was sure the middle act of the game was definitely over at this point. I couldn’t believe I’d already come this far.
While I was momentarily in my feelings about that, Amelia asked Erwen a question. “But Tersia, is that okay with you? I thought the elves worked with the executive board.”
“Oh, that’s true. Is that okay, Erwen?”
“That’s okay. I took vacation leave.”
“Vacation?”
“Yes. I told them I wouldn’t be entering the labyrinth for a while, and even if I did, I’d be working separately. So you don’t have to worry about that issue.”
“...If you say so.”
After that, I listened to Erwen and Amelia recount how the war had progressed so far and devised plans accordingly. Time passed until the labyrinth day dawned.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
Inside the Crystal Cave, which was glowing a soft purple, Amelia took point and started leading the way as soon as we opened our eyes. “Come this way.”
“Wait a minute, I’m better at figuring out directions—”
“Amelia is a scout.”
“...She is?”

Erwen had received high-level training from her sister equivalent to that of a professional scout, but she stopped insisting after my explanation. Her pride did seem to have taken a hit, however. To be honest, I couldn’t understand that. I also had navigation software installed in me, but I wasn’t disappointed about not being able to use it.
It’s much easier to just follow, so why bother?
It was interesting, though. There were only three of us on this team yet we all had scout skills. Was this what you called being one of the elite few?
Sprint.

Anyway, I just had to follow Amelia, so I continued to glance around as I ran. The vibe inside the labyrinth, which I was entering for the first time since my return, was much different from what I had expected. I expected to see knights wearing the seals of noble families and adventurers from clans everywhere.
“There are more lower-floor adventurers than I thought.”
I could see adventurers reeking of newbie energy here and there. In general, their faces were on the brighter side. They were nervous about being inside the labyrinth, but not trembling in fear.
“Oh, that? The palace implemented a lot of policies for lower-floor adventurers. After all... many high-ranking adventurers died that day.”

Hearing it out, there was a reason why there were more people on the first floor than there were during my newbie days. The royal policy was one factor, but the major thing was that most large clans had disintegrated. Now that there’d been a reshuffling, the labyrinth had transformed into a land of opportunity where all you had to do was stick a flag on the ground to stake your claim. The most prominent example was the fifth floor.
“No one is in charge of the fifth floor?”
“There will be some control, but not as bad as it used to be.”

In the case of the Great Demon Realm, it used to be common for clans to occupy and monopolize areas where monsters appeared, but that was rare these days. Apparently, it was better to join the war effort instead. Since the pay for participating was sizeable and the palace bestowed an essence you desired on you in return for war achievements, it seemed that was the trend these days.
“We were a bit too late.”
Although we arrived extremely early, the first-floor portal had already been opened by another adventurer. Our official portal speedrun was another failure.
[You have entered the Den of Beasts on the second floor.]
There was no way we could get the second-floor speedrun after the first floor was a fail, so we started to move at a more leisurely pace. Our schedule was wide open, anyway.
The deadline is the 25th.

The way the palace recruited troops was very simple: arrive at Laemia, the Island of Beginnings, by the 25th day. Though the deadline was tight for a team that had just reached the sixth floor, it was a different story for the three of us since we had a free pass up to the sixth floor.
Our speed isn’t slowing down since we have no wizard.
In the past, this would usually be the time we’d stop and rest, but no one suggested stopping.
We’re already on the third floor...?
By the end of the first day, we arrived on the third floor. We didn’t even run as fast on the second floor as we did on the first.
“Mister, you must be tired. Here, drink this.”
Surprisingly, these two still had energy after all that, so we could probably have moved faster if we really wanted to. True, these guys were agility characters.
“Erwen, I told you not to call me Mister in the labyrinth.”
“Ah, right. I’ll be careful...” Erwen smiled shyly and nodded.
After that, we prepared camp. There was no night watch. We were only at the beginning of the third floor, anyway.
“I can just leave my doppelganger in position, so rest easy.”
Thanks to Amelia’s Self-Replication, there was no need to waste someone on a task like that.
“Wow, Amelia. It’s definitely convenient to have you around.”
“Don’t be dramatic. This is nothing.”
Ha, sassy. I was just saying thanks, since even if it is a doppelganger, it’s you doing the work.
“Yes, that’s right. It is nothing.”
“Huh?”

“W-Well, I can do something similar...” With that, Erwen immediately summoned a spirit. It wasn’t hard for her to keep it summoned while she slept, unlike before. It didn’t put a dent in her mana consumption, either. “And if I use the spirit of darkness, I can make it harder for monsters and other people to see us. What do you think? Isn’t mine much better? Hmm? Don’t you think?”
“Y-Yeah... yours is better.” I wanted to refrain from comparing teammates, but a strange feeling of intimidation made my head nod on its own.
But was that the answer she wanted? “Then... tell me the same thing.”
“...Hmm? Tell you what?”
“That. What you said to that woman...” Erwen twisted her body from side to side. “Th-that it’s more convenient to have me here... Th-that... I’m the best... a-and the greatest...”
Um, I never said those things.

chapters.title: Chapter 351: Dark Continent (2)
paragraphs: Grains of sand heated up under the sunlight shining down on them. The cool yet somewhat damp wind smelled slightly of salt in this place, the Island of Beginnings, Laemia. However, the vast sea stretching along the horizon wasn’t visible this time.
[You have entered the Great Sea on the sixth floor.]
The first thing I saw when I crossed through the portal was over a hundred super-huge sailing ships lined up along the coastline. The number was so big that even the vast sea felt cramped.
“Now, now, if you’ve passed through the portal, quickly move to the side! The others have to come up!”

Without a moment to look around, I left the vicinity of the portal under the instructions of an adventurer wearing an Adventurers’ Guild badge. His tone of voice was so light that I asked Erwen about him, and she informed me that he wasn’t a regular employee of the guild. Apparently, these were adventurers commissioned by the guild. The guild had received a request for cooperation from the palace to manage adventurers, but not having the manpower to send, they had resorted to outsourcing.
True, it’d be hard for ordinary guild staff to get to the sixth floor.
As the war had been going on for over a year now, the rigidly organized process went naturally and smoothly.
“Come this way! First, you’ll register for war and be designated a unit!”
After waiting in a long queue that stretched down the eastern coastline, I submitted my ID tag and finished registering for the war. Then there was a bit of a commotion. Erwen had become too famous.
“Erwen Fornacci di Tersia... Uh... uh, B-Blood Spirit...?”
“Is there a problem?”
“N-No... there isn’t! Sorry for the fuss!”
They could have questioned Erwen on why she was registering as an independent, but the registration clerk was uncomfortable even making conversation with her and just wrapped up the process quickly.

“Rank-five adventurer Emily Raines. You have a previous record of participating in the war. Registered.” Amelia went after Erwen, and this time the registration really ended in one second. As her identity had been made two years ago, her age on her ID was twenty-two. Apparently, she started off as a rank-nine adventurer and went through the slow process of raising her rank. She even went as far as paying taxes among other things to completely create a new identity. Unless she encountered someone who knew her face like Erwen, her new identity got her off scot-free.
Unlike me, who was receiving some peculiar looks.
“Rank-five adventurer Riehen Schuitz. You have no record of participation. Would you please take off your helmet?”

The identity Amelia found for me, Riehen Schuitz, was an adventurer who was active five years ago. Of course, the broker had paid his taxes faithfully that whole time, so there were no issues with the documentation.

“Hmm.” The reaction I received was mixed, probably because my face looked younger than twenty-nine years old. I felt like a minor trying to buy cigarettes. Still, I managed to get through safely, perhaps thanks to my hair having been dyed light brown as written on the ID card. I made sure to choose an identity with the same eye color as mine.
“What, is there a problem?”
“No, it seems you are returning from a long break. I wish you the best of luck.”
“Thanks.”

I did have to raise my helmet once, but fortunately, the registration process ended without any real incident. There were many cases of people returning from retirement for the war, so there wasn’t much suspicion, just as Amelia told me. Two of the Seven Powerful had done the same as well.
“Then we just have to be assigned a unit now.”

After completing registration, we moved to the bulletin board on the side. On the board, there was a brief list of the ships currently on standby and the number of people on board. Deciding which ship to board was quite important in war. This was because the adventurers on the same ship formed a single unit once they arrived on the seventh floor.
“There’s no need to think it through. Since this is your first time participating, you can only take a third-class ship,” said Amelia.
“Third-class ship?”

“It’s a ship mainly crewed by adventurers without war achievements or those that don’t come from a big team like a large clan. As a result, they’re located in the rear as support since their combat power is lacking.”
Haha, so newbies have to claw their way up from the bottom? Well, it would be troublesome to have a newbie holding you back on a dangerous battlefield.

“Then I’ll ride that one.” We chose the least crowded ship among the third-class ships and the three of us boarded together, deciding that it would be advantageous to choose a room with as few people as possible.
“Luckily, we were able to get a three-person room,” said Amelia.
“Why, is it difficult to get a three-person room?”
“Not really, but it is the most popular.”
I was able to figure out the reason for that without having to ask.
Ah, right. The binding spell was updated while I was away.
In this era, six-person parties were common. Three-person rooms were a popular way to split into two groups to sleep.
“Then let’s all take time to rest until departure tomorrow.”
“Okay! What should we talk about now?”
“...I said let’s rest.”
“Yes, exactly. That’s what I’m doing.”
I looked at Amelia in search of help, but she had already finished organizing her belongings and was laying in bed.
Jeez, pretending to sleep.
“Then should we talk about the war...?”
“Okay! Do you have any questions?”
“I heard participants on the third-class ships are usually placed on rear support. What exactly do they do?”
“Uh... I’m always at the front so I don’t really know... But I think I heard they are in charge of securing retreat routes or escort missions.”
I wasn’t particularly tired so I talked with Erwen, listening to various war stories. A while later, we suddenly got a visitor.
Knock, knock.
It was someone we all knew well.
“...I heard you were on the same boat so I came to say hello. It’s been a while, Miss Tersia.”
I didn’t expect to be reunited so soon.
“Whew...” The blonde woman standing in front of the closed cabin adjusted the collar of her uniform. Then she let out a deep sigh.
Why does this woman have to be so unpredictable?

Blood Spirit, Erwen Fornacci di Tersia, was the reason why Raven was standing in front of this cabin right now. For some reason, this member of the Seven Powerful was on a third-class ship instead of a first-class ship.
Honestly, they always make me do the annoying tasks.

The Third Magic Corps, the corps she belonged to, was scheduled to board a third-class ship as well because a corps made up of wizards was essential for defense. However, this was not that ship. Somehow, she had ended up getting reassigned here on orders from her superiors.
We’re not even that close anymore. And we weren’t that close in the past, either.

Her superiors assigned her to this ship because they were once a part of the same clan, but Raven was not confident in her ability to keep Erwen in check. How could she control that wild woman when she had no idea what trouble she’d cause in the future?
But since I’ve been ordered, I have no choice but to at least talk to her and get a sense for what she plans to do...
Sighing, Raven knocked on the door.
Knock, knock.
The door opened about ten seconds later.
Creak.
The hinges rusted from the sea breeze opened with a creak, and the closed cabin came into view. In keeping with the information she received, there were three people in total inside.
Rank-five adventurer Riehen Schuitz, and Emily Raines.

One was wearing a helmet even indoors, and the other had her eyes and ears covered with a black cloth that came down to her nose. This made Raven even more curious. Who were these people, if Blood Spirit was suddenly working with them?
“Stop staring at Mister and say what you want.”

At the borderline cold and aggressive voice, Raven stopped studying the cabin and looked at Erwen. Then she tried to put on a customer-service smile. “I heard you were on the same boat so I came to say hello. It’s been a while, Miss Tersia.”
“Yes. Then if you’re done, can you please leave?”
Tsk, when will she fix that attitude of hers?
Even as she tutted inwardly, Raven did not let it show and continued talking. That was because she had too many questions to leave like this. For example...
“Did you just say Mister?”
Why did this woman refer to this man as Mister? Wasn’t that nickname reserved for that man?

Unfortunately, Erwen offered no reply. She simply glared at Raven, her eyes clearly conveying that that was none of her business. But there was also a somewhat nervous tint to them, almost as if she’d let Raven see something she didn’t want her to see.

“Hmm.” Raven moved her eyes from Erwen to the man. He was a stranger and she couldn’t even see his face because it was covered by a helmet, but for some reason, the air he gave off was very familiar. She just couldn’t put her finger on how.
No, even if they had nothing in common, nevertheless, he strangely resembled that man.
“A-Are you—? This man...” Soon, Raven’s jaw dropped and she looked between Erwen and the stranger frantically.
The longer the silence dragged on, and the longer Raven’s eyes were glued to me, the more I got to thinking.
What? She caught on already? Then what happens next? Can I convince her that I’m not an evil spirit? Even if I can’t convince her, the news will definitely reach the palace...
As I shifted my eyes over to Erwen, I saw she was also looking at me as if to say, Mister, what do we do now?
I was kind of amazed. I mean, she was the one who made that slip of the tongue.
“Could it be...” Just then, Raven opened her mouth and ended the uncomfortable silence. “I didn’t know you were this damaged.”
...Huh? Say what now?
While Erwen and I were both confused, Raven continued in a tone tinged with sadness. “Miss Tersia... no, Erwen... it’s not right to look for someone to replace him.”
“There’s no way someone like that exists. It must be hard, but the only thing you can do is overcome it.”
Only then did I get what was going on. Raven had misunderstood. She thought Erwen missed me so much that she had found a similar man and covered his face to roleplay.

“And you.” Wearing her small uniform, Raven whipped around to glare at me. “I know what you’re thinking, so you’d better give up on using Miss Erwen. Because I’m not going to let that happen. I’m going to keep an eye on you, and if you cross the line even a little...”
When Raven trailed off, I found myself making excuses. “Wait! I don’t know what you think this is, but I’m not thinking of—”
“Your voice...”
“My voice?”

When I tilted my head, not understanding, Raven flinched and avoided my eyes. “Your voice... is... similar.” It looked like she now sympathized with Erwen. “So that’s why...” Raven muttered, rueful, before turning to Erwen. “Still, you shouldn’t. Something like this... he wouldn’t want this, either.”

Fierce sincerity colored her tone, and it went beyond offering advice and was almost in begging territory. However, that wasn’t going to work for Erwen. Raven had the wrong idea about all of this in the first place.
“W-Who are you to interfere? You don’t know anything!” Erwen came to her senses and chose defense. Simply put, that meant she went on the attack. “Get out, and don’t come back!”
Erwen forced Raven out and slammed the door shut.
After Raven’s visit, time passed quickly. On the day of departure, not only did the warships floating on the coastline unfurl their sails, but the role of this ship was also determined.
“Escort for the Magic Corps, huh?”

As soon as this ship arrived on the seventh floor, the adventurers on it would participate in battle as escorts for the Third Magic Corps. For reference, battle formations and tactics were taught on the deck.
So this is why they tie troops to each ship. Because there’s time to teach them to work together as they go.

The estimated length of our voyage to the seventh floor was approximately fifteen days. Aside from training, most of my time was free but I spent most of it on deck. The reason was simple. I was once again realizing that barbarians were weak to the sea.
“Blaaargh!”
Even though the ship was big, I couldn’t stay in the cabin because of my seasickness. Here, I could just throw up anywhere.
Anyway, since I was spending so much time on the deck, there were times I ran into Raven, and with considerable frequency. For some reason, it was always when Erwen wasn’t there.
“...Even the motion sickness is the same. How annoying.”
“...Blargh.”
“Why are you hiding your face? Because Erwen told you to?”
“True, your face is too different from his. Why are you hiding your face like that? Don’t you have any pride? I swear, if you make one mistake. I won’t let it slide.”
Ugh, I’m already having a tough time as it is. Why won’t this kid leave me alone?

chapters.title: Chapter 352: Dark Continent (3)
paragraphs: Raven’s harassment ended when we reached our destination after a fifteen-day voyage: a continent with vast plains. As if to prohibit intruders, there was a dark purple barrier spread along its borders and even a portal located in the sea in front of it.
“Woahhh!”
“We’re here!”

As soon as this long-awaited sight unfolded over the horizon, the adventurers all gathered on deck and cheered. True, the voyage had been boring, although I personally had no time to be bored between suffering from seasickness and looking around the islands when I was feeling all right.

“It’s Riehen Schuitz,” I warned Erwen once again as soon as she came up next to me. She lowered her head. It seemed she realized she’d made a mistake. Hopefully, this would prevent any more. “Anyway, why did you come up here? It’ll take a while for us to enter the portal.”
“Just because... I just wanted to be with you...”
At first, her directness had burdened me a great deal, but she had eased up on me a lot lately. Or should I say I had gotten used to it?

“...But what are those boats? I don’t think I saw them when we set sail.” I pointed off into the distance. The portal we’d arrived at was packed with boats that had already arrived, and among them was a different kind than the sailboat we came on.
“Ah, that? It’s a speedboat. They send those who arrive on the sixth floor first out in advance.”
“To stop Noark from coming down?”

“Yes, there has been more of that recently. But seeing as there are no signs of battle on the ships, I don’t think there was an attempt this time... I heard it was intense not long ago, to the point where more than half of the speedboats got completely destroyed.”
I see. Anyway, since they arrived earliest, these guys would have killed the Gatekeeper already. I wonder if there was an essence.
While I looked around, I could feel eyes on me. This was a change that had occurred as the voyage dragged on.
“That woman is Blood Spirit...”
“But do you know who the man beside her is?”
“I don’t know. When I asked a friend who joined the Magic Corps, they said this is his first mission back after retiring a few years back.”
“Hmm, yet he became teammates with one of the Seven Powerful right away... I guess he has some kind of ace up his sleeve.”

Thanks to Erwen’s popularity, Amelia and I received attention wherever we went. For now, the emotion in people’s eyes was 99 percent curiosity. Although this war had no-name adventurers appearing in it all the time, they were probably interested in my identity and capabilities as I was working with Blood Spirit from the get-go. The other 1 percent was hostility.
“Schuitz.”
“Ah, Raven?”
“She’s doing that thing again,” said Amelia.
Even as we gathered with the rest of the corps to talk about our plans since war was just around the corner, Raven’s eyes were glued to us.
“Um... should I get rid of her when the opportunity presents itself...?” asked Erwen.
What was this girl saying? When I knocked Erwen on the forehead so she wouldn’t get any ideas, she gave me a resentful look.
“But what if she recognizes you?” she asked. “I’m anxious.”
Actually, I was thinking the same thing. Of course, not about getting rid of her, but whether or not to reveal my identity to Raven and ask for her to help us.
It just seems like a pointless hassle.

First, convincing her that I was not an evil spirit would take some work. Even if she did accept, there was no guarantee she’d keep my secret and cooperate. I knew Raven could get attached to people, but she also knew how to distinguish between public and private affairs.
And even if she does keep it a secret, the fact that she belongs to the palace now would just cause trouble later on.
My final decision was that it would be best to explain everything to her myself once everything was already dealt with.

“If I get caught, though, I’ll have no choice but to be honest and tell her everything.” Regardless of how I was hoping this would go, if I were discovered before that, I’d have no choice but to ask for her cooperation.
“Ugh, that makes one more person.”
...Is that what you were anxious about?
Bwoooooo!
The moment the horn sounded from the ship in the lead, our ship also came to life.
“Everyone to your positions!”

Finally, our short wait was over, and it was time for all of us to enter the battlefield. The adventurers who were waiting around on deck moved to their assigned positions at the command of a palace affiliate. We didn’t need to move because our assigned position was the deck.
“Mis—no, Riehen, I’ll tie you up!”
“Huh?”
“I’m good at these things!”

Soon, we tied ourselves to the boat with the rope we were given. This was a measure to make sure we didn’t fall off. Once our preparations were complete, the horn sounded from the flagship again and our ship began to move.
“I’m kind of nervous...”
“Don’t worry. Riehen... I’ll make sure to protect you.”
Um, isn’t that supposed to be my line as the tank?
Even as I thought that I didn’t bother continuing down that line of conversation.
“Ship entry complete!”

The ships in the lead crossed through the portal and as our ship moved closer to it, I could feel my muscles tensing with barely contained energy. That was because we were headed toward a battlefield right now. The other adventurers were also stiff and solemn-faced, unlike earlier. The sight gave me PTSD as I was reminded of a certain event on the first floor.
“Main unit, entry complete!”

It was time for me to ditch my light-hearted attitude too. This was my first time entering the seventh floor in this body. Moreover, the said floor was full of adventurers from Noark who were more dangerous than monsters. Even if I was planning to get something out of my trip up here, I could just as easily lose something.
“Erwen and Emily.”
“Yes.”
“Speak.”
Holding onto the railing with one hand and my new shield with the other, I said, “Do not leave my side.”
Flash!
Before long, our ship entered the portal.
Boom!

The large sailing ship soared through the air for a moment as if thrown by a giant before hitting the surface of the sea and sending streams of water flying everywhere. It was an incredible experience, but there was no time to be distracted. We were not currently on a peaceful sea under a blue sky.
[You have entered the Dark Continent on the seventh floor.]
The sea was black as if covered in oil. Although this was only the entrance to the continent, the surrounding fog was already affecting our visibility.
Bang! Bang! Pop!
Explosions from all sides pounded on our eardrums thanks to the mana cannons being fired by the troops Noark had stationed on top of the canyon.
“Their welcome is very intense today,” said Erwen.
“Where did those guys get mana cannons?”
“They must have taken them from our ships.”

Even as we conversed, mana cannons, black magic, and various special abilities flew toward the ship. I could tell the firepower was considerable just by the sound, but the damage to the royal fleet was nonexistent. There was nothing you couldn’t achieve with money.
Shaaaaaa!

The moment we entered the seventh floor, all incoming attacks were immediately blocked before they could reach us. Although the ship rocked significantly on occasion, there was never any damage. This was proof of the large-scale investment the palace had put into all their warships after initially suffering heavy damage during the landing process. Apparently, mana stones in the tens of millions were consumed per minute just to maintain the magic circles on board.
So how much money is that just to get to the continent? Ah, maybe it’s still a bargain compared to the cost of the ship?

Of course, this wasn’t the time to be worrying about the country’s financial situation, so I shoved aside those distracting thoughts and focused on the present. Taking the warm welcome head-on, the fleet steadily advanced and soon broke through the adjacent coast before changing formation into a single-file line to enter the narrow canyon.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Canyon of Vengeful Spirits has activated. All Healing and Regeneration effects are disabled. All Divine Power is sealed.]

The Canyon of Vengeful Spirits was a section of the map that you had to pass through in order to enter the Dark Continent, as the entire coastline was made up of cliffs. As the warship we were on followed the ship before it into the canyon, the ominous, gloomy fog thickened even more.
“Prepare for battle!”
Undead monsters began crawling up the outer walls of the ship. Their ranks were as varied as their types.
[You have killed a Deadburn. EXP +3]
[You have killed a Red Eye. EXP +4]
[You have killed a Banshee Queen. EXP +6]
[You have killed a Teeth Skeleton. EXP+ 4]
[You have killed a Cliff Demon...]

More than half the monsters that appeared here could be hunted on the sixth floor too, but since we skipped that floor, we racked up XP no matter what we killed. Erwen’s contributions as a long-ranger were considerable. Almost 70 percent of the monsters were dropped before they could even get on the ship, and the sea monsters had no chance of attacking us at all.
[You have killed a Chaosseaman. EXP +6]
[You have killed a Malder Elephant. EXP +5]
[You have killed a Skeleton Mermaid Queen...]
Since I was Bound with Erwen, the XP flowed my way even if all she did was fire off a basic attack. Of course, that didn’t mean I spent my time freeloading.
Smack!
The deck was also full of Spirit monsters that had no need to climb, so I had to swing my weapon unendingly.
[You have killed a Ghosties. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Soul Drinker. EXP +6]
[You have killed a Canyon Ghost. EXP +3]

Given the fact that there were so many people on the ship, the spawn rate was no joke. And even as a fierce battle unfolded on deck, those vicious bastards from Noark added to the chaos by firing cannons at us from on top of the canyon. This was neutralized by a defensive magic circle.
“Ahhhhhh!”
However, there were still cases of adventurers whose lines were cut during battle falling off the rocking deck into the sea.
“What the—why isn’t the ship moving?”
“The ship ahead has sunk!”
“Huh? But it was moving forward just fine!”
“It looks like a Deadrect appeared and damaged the warship’s magic circle!”
As I listened to the battle updates, it seemed there were cases of some of the ships’ defensive magic circles getting broken by monsters, causing the entire ship to go down.
Welp, the persistent bombardment from above is worth it, I guess.

Not only would it be a plus for Noark if they were lucky enough to destroy just one ship, but as long as they continued to attack, the ships could not turn off their defensive magic circles. Thus, as we advanced through the canyon, we had no choice but to keep the magic circle on, consuming a lot of our firepower.
“Amelia, behind you!” At my urgent shout, Amelia shattered the skeleton trying to ambush her with a back kick. “No need to thank me. We’re comrades after—”
“It’s Emily.”
“Huh?”
“I’m sure no one heard you in the middle of all this, but I want you to be careful.”
“Ah, I’ll be careful...” Even though it was the same pseudonym she used back in the past, it wasn’t sticking for some reason. Which meant I had no right to scold Erwen for her mistake.
“Mister—! Look over there!”
“It’s Riehen.”
“Ah... right... anyway, there! We’re almost there!”
I looked where Erwen was pointing, but all I could see was fog.
[Field Effect – Canyon of Vengeful Spirits has been deactivated.]
A while later, however, the narrow canyon opened up to reveal a wide lake. There was a waterfall on one of the sides, and the water here was as red as blood.
“Whew, it’s over!”
“I can finally catch my breath.”
As the constantly spawning monsters disappeared, the bombardment from Noark also came to an end. This meant we had safely cleared the first hurdle.
So this is when the real challenge begins...
As I stared at the fog-covered water, I gulped. Maybe I was only imagining it, but I thought I could already smell blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 353: Dark Continent (4)
paragraphs: “Riehen! Here, water!”
“Ah, thanks.”
While the adventurers, including me, took a short break and quenched our thirst with either water or alcohol, palace personnel walked the interior of the ship to inspect those on board.
“Once we disembark, the ship will be de-summoned, so make sure to not leave any items behind!”

Once the inspection was over, we were transferred to small boats one by one and traveled by water toward shore. At the water’s edge, troops who had already disembarked were standing in orderly rows. Well, it was still a mess compared to modern times, where soldiers marched with their left feet aligned.
“Luckily, it looks like they weren’t waiting for us here.”
“It seems Noark’s forces are trying to avoid a fight with the main units as much as possible,” said Erwen.
“True, if we face ‘em head on, it’ll be harder for us to lose with an army like this backing us up.”

Anyway, we waited as instructed. It wasn’t long before the lead troop started marching, though we didn’t follow, of course. That was because we had been on a third-class ship. On paper, the mission of ship 3-21 was to escort the Third Magic Corps. Unfortunately, said corps was the Third Corps, whose main mission was to secure a safe way out in case of retreat. Put simply, once the main unit left, their role in this war was simply to build a garrison and protect this place.
“Now, now! Let’s set up the barracks first!”

Once the remaining ships of the Third Corps disembarked, it was officially time to build the stronghold. The adventurers set up the barracks supplied to them, and the wizards rushed around to draw various magic circles. This went on for hours.
Shaaaaaa!
Thanks to magic, the deafening sound of the waterfall quieted down and the fog obscuring our vision finally cleared.
“Whew, that’s much better now.”
“Everyone, have some of this food and rest! Barracks will be assigned and jobs will be announced soon!”

Once the garrison setup was pretty much complete, we were assigned the barracks we would be staying in. Ours was a six-person barracks located on the eastern side of the lake. We may have been under military purview at the moment, but the three of us were not separated due to the custom of grouping party members together.
“Haha, let’s introduce ourselves since we will be working in the same group from now on.”
Three people I’d never seen before joined us as well. Apparently, we weren’t just sharing the barracks but would have to move as a group on guard duty and patrol from now on too.
I guess this happened because there are three of us.

Whether a clan or a party, five people—no, after the binding spell was updated, six people—was the minimum unit size. Since there were only three of us and the numbers didn’t add up otherwise, we were automatically matched with others.
Looks like it wasn’t totally automatic, though.

I looked at the man who was smiling good-naturedly and leading the conversation. He was wearing a stylish uniform and even had a sword at his waist, but he was a wizard. The emblem of the Magic Corps on his chest attested to this.
“Ah, speaking of, I didn’t introduce myself yet. I am Alex Halo, assistant to the deputy commander of the Third Magic Corps.”
“Assistant to the deputy commander?” I muttered quietly.
Amelia whispered in my ear. “That means he reports to the deputy commander.”
Oh, so he’s Raven’s right-hand man?
It was obvious why she sent her right hand here: to keep us in check and surveil us—or more specifically, Erwen.
“The six people assigned to these barracks will belong to Group 3-17 from now on and carry out various missions together. I, as the team leader, will help—”
“Team leader? Says who?” Erwen made no effort to hide her displeasure with that announcement and a crack appeared in the man’s smile.
“Haha... I was aware there may be discontent with that bit. But since it’s an order from up high—”
“You smile like you’re relaxed but you’re very nervous.”
“...Sorry?”
“Why, do I make you uneasy?”

The man flinched at Erwen’s question but shook his head. “...Of course not. On the contrary, I feel safer with you here.” Anyone could tell that response was pure politeness. If he really thought that way, he wouldn’t have had reason to avoid Erwen’s eyes as he spoke.
“Stop it, now.” Knowing that man was only here on orders, too, I quickly intervened.
“But the three of us are enough...”
“It’s good to have more people to help.”
“But team leader?”
“Someone from the military could be our team’s leader. Why are you so outraged about that?”
Erwen pursed her lips. “...Okay. I’ll stop.”
Did that interaction leave an impression? Only then did the man shift his gaze to me. “You are...”
“Riehen Schuitz.”
“Ah, yes... I’m aware. Nice to meet you. And the person next to you is Ms. Emily Raines?”
“Yes.”

The man came up to me to say hello, then introduced us to the other two people blankly watching us interact a short distance away. “These people were aboard the third-class ship that sank on the way here. Thankfully they were rescued, but unfortunately, their other teammates were not.”
No wonder I wasn’t getting the vibe these two had been taken from another team. So, that was why. When our eyes shifted to the other two people, they introduced themselves a little nervously.
“I-It’s an honor to meet you, Blood Spirit. Ah, o-of course, the rest of your teammates too. I am rank-five adventurer Lykion Elt.”

He didn’t give off a bad first impression. He seemed polite, and seeing as he had stayed quiet until he was given a moment to introduce himself, he seemed to be quick on the uptake too. Rank five meant he would do his fair share as well. Besides that, he seemed to be coming from a rather unfortunate situation.
“I-I’ll do my best not to be an inconvenience!” said the other man. “I’m H-Hans Caesar.”
“What...?” I blurted involuntarily.
The man kindly repeated his name again for my benefit. “Hans Caesar!”
Are you kidding me?
I took a moment to reflect. What happened the last time I ran into a Hans? I quickly remembered. Hans J, whom I met on Farune Island, had been a traitor.
And after I met him, I got sucked into the past.

I spent an entire six months there, and when I got back, two and a half years had passed in my original time period. And that wasn’t all. Not only were my clanmates now scattered, but I had also been branded as an evil spirit.
“Haha...”
When I let out a bark of incredulous laughter, Hans K tilted his head and asked, “Um... what’s the matter?”
There was no reason for me to go as far as exchanging words with him. That would only bring me bad luck. “Erwen.”
“Yes, go ahead.”
“You said the three of us were enough, right?”
“I did.”
Yes, you did.
“Hmm...” I genuinely mulled this over. If I gave her the command to go ham, Erwen would let out a war cry and tear this group to pieces.
But if I do, news will reach Raven.
That was the part that bothered me. Raven knew of my hatred of the name Hans. Once she heard about why I got rid of him, her suspicions toward me could end up growing.
Hm, that means I just have to make it look like I kicked him out for something other than his name. Come to think of it, that’s a good idea. Okay, I’ve decided.
“You’re all trash.”
“...Sorry?”

“I said, having you guys here will only slow us down.” When cold words of contempt left my mouth, their expressions hardened. I guessed they never thought I’d be the one saying something like this and not Erwen.
“Haha... what do you mean? Mr. Schuitz, you just said it’s better to have more people.”
Ah, about that.
“I changed my mind.” A Hans was a serious matter. When I asked for him to remove those two or take us out of the group, Alex looked flummoxed.
“How ridiculous. What, do you think you’re someone special now?”
“Forget it, we’ll leave,” announced a member of the Hans Group. “There is no reason for us to stay after being treated like this. Instead, tell your superiors that the blame lies with them, not us.”
It seemed I really hurt their pride since they declared their withdrawal from the team and walked out of the barracks of their own volition.
Whew, that solves that—
“How dare they say that? Should I follow them?” Erwen asked.
“It’s fine, don’t even speak to them.”
“Okay!”

Anyway, as we conversed, Raven’s right-hand man, Alex, shot me a disgusted look. I was sure he had been filled in on Raven’s mistaken assumption. I must have seemed normal at first, but now I likely came off as a pathetic bastard who only cared about how much power a person had.
“So, what are you going to do now? Our group of six is now a group of four.”
“...I will first report this to the Deputy Commander and then inform you of how we’ll handle you.”
“If you say so.”
When Alex left the barracks as well to relay the situation to Raven, Erwen turned to me and carefully asked, “But why did you do that all of a sudden?”
“His name was Hans.”
“...What about it being Hans?”
Ah, does she not know about my Hans jinx? Hmm, I guess I don’t remember telling her...
Just as I was about to explain, Amelia smirked and spoke for me. “You were his clanmate and don’t even know that?”
“...So you know?”
“Of course I do.” Amelia shrugged and provided a brief summary of my Hans jinx. In Amelia’s case, she knew the weight of the name because of that fiasco where she called me Hans Lee.

Erwen seemed furious about being the only one out of the loop. “Hans...” She muttered the name in a truly murderous tone, then balled her fists up in determination. “Come to think of it, the traitor on Farune Island was Hans Aulock. Sorry. I won’t forget to keep an eye out from now on.”
“Uh... s-sure.” I was now concerned she would end up embedding an arrow in every Hans she encountered, but I decided not to worry about it too much.
So what? They’re Hanses, anyway. No matter how you look at it, they’d definitely end up doing something bad. The problem right now is that I already ran into a Hans...

Although I’d quickly kicked him out of the group, I was in the same space as Hans K for too long, and the barrack was poorly ventilated. And considering we were in the middle of a battlefield on the seventh floor...
“Mister, your hands are shaking...”
Ugh, I’m going to lose it.
What on earth was going to happen to us? While my hands were shaking from anxiety, Alex came back and told us how our team’s problem would be resolved.
“It’s been decided how you’ll be dealt with.”
Nothing much had changed. We were going to continue forward as a group of four, and he would take on the role of team leader just the same.
“After this, you—no, we will be on personnel escort duty instead of external patrol or sentry duty.”

Our group’s job was changed to guarding Raven, the deputy commander of the Third Magic Corps. Of course, that wasn’t a problem. As long as Sir Kyle, the commander, was busy supporting the special forces of the First Corps, Raven was the most important person in our unit. But while we may have been called escorts, I suspected her real goal was probably to keep an eye on us so we couldn’t cause any more issues.
Anyway, things went smoothly for a while.
Kabooom!
Until a mana cannon sounded from somewhere nearby.
Beeep! Beeep! Beeep!
The alarm spell activated and rang throughout the garrison.
“A-Ambush!”
“Everyone, prepare for battle!”
This happened less than two hours after my encounter with Hans K.

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Isolation (1)
paragraphs: The lakeside where the garrison was located was one of the few safe zones on the Dark Continent. That didn’t mean total safety, though—that just meant monsters didn’t spawn naturally here. And monsters weren’t the only dangerous things in the labyrinth. Case in point:
Beeeep! Beeeep! Beeeep!

The alarm spell detected an enemy and sounded an emergency siren. It was clear who the intruder was. Even if a monster happened to enter the safe zone by chance, said monster wouldn’t also fire a mana cannon.
“It’s Noark!”
“An enemy invasion!”

However, there was another problem here. We knew who the enemy was, but how did they get here? The main unit, which had gone ahead, should have conducted a thorough search of the area before advancing.
There’s no way the main unit was attacked.

I decided to operate under that assumption because of the size of the main unit. There was no way that many troops could have been annihilated in that short period of time. If they were in such a tight spot they would have contacted us, and if they did, the Third Corps we belonged to would have immediately provided support.
They ambushed us away from the eyes of the main unit.

The above possibility was the most plausible and based on this premise, the intruder’s troops were likely to be few in number. In order to avoid the eyes of the main unit, it made more sense to move in small, elite units. Of course, I had no way of knowing what was actually going on for sure.
“Mister! What are you doing? Let’s go!”
Jeez, it’s Riehen. Though I guess there’s no need to correct her since Raven’s misunderstood our situation anyway.
“Okay, let’s go out now.” I stopped my train of thought there and rushed out of the barracks.
Immediately, I saw a cannonball made of pure mana coming at us from straight ahead.
Whew, good thing I took the lead.
Kwaaang!

When I blocked it with my shield, the remnants of the mana exploded and scattered in all directions. The shock was significant but not enough to push me back. That was because the Mark of the Guard Corps absorbed 50 percent of the blow.
“A-Are you okay?” a voice behind me stuttered.
Don’t be a chicken.

Was this because the Magic Corp were always in the rear? “I’m fine.” I reassured Raven’s aide, who was surprised by the cannonball that just exploded in front of his nose, and quickly gave orders. “Alex, right? Stay close behind me.”
“Y-Yes!”
“Emily, Erwen, you two follow behind too and protect this man.”
“Okay!”

Our formation was established in an instant. Normally, this stuff should have been done by the team leader, but well, it looked like he was the type to only ever do what he was told. Even if I was the one giving the orders, I didn’t think he would argue.
“Alex, where is the deputy commander’s barracks?”
“O-Over there!”
“Then let’s head there first. Stay close.”
“Yes!”

While adventurers rushing out of barracks headed toward the outskirts in their groups, we moved further into the camp because the objective of our group was to escort someone. Well, to be honest, that was an excuse. I just figured I could learn more about the current situation if I went to the command center.
And Raven could be in danger too...

I picked up the pace and arrived at the barracks where Raven would be. Raven was standing outside. Around her was a crowd of uniformed wizards belonging to the Magic Corps. It looked like they were performing some kind of incantation by drawing a magic circle on the ground.
“Deputy Commander Raven, what is the current situation?” I asked.
Raven furrowed her brow at my quick approach and question. “Why are you guys—”
“Obviously we came to carry out our assigned mission since it’s an emergency.”

“Ah...” Raven nodded in understanding. It seemed she had just remembered that our group’s assignment was changed to escorting her. But apparently there was one thing still bothering her. “Alex Halo, why is this man making the report you should be making? Aren’t you the team leader here?”
When Raven glared at him, Alex froze, unable to hide his dismay. “A-About that...” It was only then that he realized that I had naturally begun leading the group. That was still no defense, though.
“About that?”
“No, I... I will correct this!”
“How are you going to correct that...? Ha, it’s fine. I don’t have time for this right now.”
“Deputy Commander, we’ve finished charging it with mana!” One of the wizards shouted. Raven ended the conversation there and walked between the wizards.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-two defense spell Wall of Gold.]
A big iron wall barricaded the entire lakeside. To be honest, my jaw dropped as soon as I saw it.
Wow... she uses rank-two magic now?

Dozens of wizards had poured their magic into Wall of Gold, but it was ultimately Raven who stood at the center of it all and cast the spell. Put simply, with enough mana, she had advanced to a point that she could use a rank-two spell.
This feels weird...

With her nickname of Golden Wizard, I had expected her to be quite strong now. But could I even bring a kid like this back to my clan? Being the deputy commander of a corps meant she already had a solid life ahead of her without having to live as an adventurer.
“This will buy us time for now. Good job, everyone.”
“No problem, Deputy Commander!”
“Everyone, follow me.” As Raven started walking away with the air of a leader, the wizards of the corps followed suit.
I sped up to stick next to Raven. “Where on earth are you going now?”

I was worried about her reaction even as the words left my mouth, but thankfully Raven glanced at me and answered with an annoyed expression on her face. “We received a missive from the command center of the Third Corps: activate the defense spell first and then go to central headquarters. If that answers your question, please don’t ask me anymore. I have enough to think about as it is.”

I fully understood how annoying it was to have your thoughts interrupted so I just shut up and followed along. When we arrived at the central headquarters not long after, Raven entered alone. I tried to follow her.
“...Why are you following me?”
“Our group’s mission is to protect you!”
“Stop talking nonsense and stay outside. That’s an order.”

I had no choice but to take a step back in the face of Raven’s stubbornness. I was curious about the conversation the leaders would have inside. I wondered if there was a way to eavesdrop. I asked Erwen and Amelia about this, but they didn’t seem to have a solution.
“Deputy Commander!” After about thirty minutes, Raven came out of the barracks. I quickly went to her side to ask how it went, but all I received was a cold reply that she couldn’t tell me.
Ha... she really is ruthless to people she’s not close with.
I missed the old Raven. She did everything I asked her to even with a disgusted expression on her face.
“Emily, can you find out?”

“I was planning to already.” Information was priceless at times like these, so I collected it through Amelia. Because of her expertise in this area, it didn’t take long, and she came back with a report a while later. “First, communication with the main unit is blocked.”
“Then does that mean we can’t receive support from them?”
“Well, not exactly. They normally contact each other at regular intervals. If that communication stops, they’ll realize something has happened on our end.”
“Then the main issue here will be how long we can hold out until the main unit returns.”
Nearly ten hours had passed since the main unit departed. Even if they retreated and came back to help due to the loss of contact, it would take considerable time for them to return.
“How’s the reaction on the adventurers’ side?”
“Not too bad. They all believe in the Golden Wizard. They seem to think nothing will happen this time either, just like the last.”
“Last?”

“Ah, I know about that too!” Erwen, who was looking for an entry point into the conversation, jumped in to explain. Apparently, the garrison had been attacked just once before, in the early days when no one really had any information on each other. “That woman infused mana into a magic circle she set up in advance and summoned this wall at that time too. Noark tried to penetrate it for hours but was unsuccessful and ended up fleeing.”

This was the incident that had earned Raven the nickname of Golden Wizard. Afterward, Noark realized Raven was always around protecting the garrison and never attempted anything like that again—until today.
“Something is off.”
“Definitely...”
Unlike Amelia, who agreed with my muttering, Erwen tilted her head. “Off?”
“Yeah, you guys said they never made the same mistake again after failing last time.”

If they were reusing a strategy that had failed once before, it was safe to say they had prepared a workaround. Those pricks from Noark were not stupid. The guys who once prepared a large-scale explosive spell in anticipation of our main troops escaping to Dimension Square through a portal were just poking around this time? That made no sense.
The problem is how they’re going to penetrate that...
I thought back to the spell Wall of Gold. It was high-level magic that could only be used if a wizard had maxed out on mastery of Earth and Lightning magic.
It’s not a concentration spell, first of all.
Unlike other spells that required a continuous flow of mana to sustain, the duration of this spell was determined in proportion to the amount of mana used in the initial casting process.
Also, if the wall is damaged, it’s possible to repair it by infusing more mana.

I could see why the other adventurers weren’t feeling all that bad about our current odds. To start, there was a corps of wizards here. Repairs could be done if anything broke down, and the spell could be recast at least twice.
I just don’t see it playing out like that.
After all, I just met a Hans, didn’t I? Operating under the assumption that the enemy had some kind of trick up their sleeve, I vigorously brainstormed.
“Um... Mister?”
“Leave him. It looks like he’s thinking about something.”
How are they planning to break through this wall? Did they bring along a high-ranking wizard like Fallen Scholar? But in the first place... do they even need to penetrate it?

If I were them, I would have closed the distance and induced a melee instead of shooting cannons from afar, but these guys didn’t do that. They launched long-range attacks and gave us time to use Wall of Gold... as if they were waiting for us to do just that.
In other words, they wanted us to use Wall of Gold.

If so, what was the reason? When I thought this through from their perspective again, I quickly came up with an answer. “Because they’ve already snuck in.” There was nothing easier than destroying an enemy whose guard was down from within.
But it seemed Erwen and Amelia didn’t understand what I was saying. “What do you mean by that?”
Instead of answering Amelia’s question, I looked at the Wall of Gold surrounding the lake and asked, “Do you know how long this wall has stayed up in the past?”
“It would have been... about eight hours. I heard it remained intact long after the main unit arrived.”
So it is. Eight hours, huh?
That was how long we would be confined within these walls.
The moment I fleshed out Noark’s plan in my head, I went straight to Raven’s barracks. “I have something to tell you.”
“I’m sure I told you to wait outside the barracks. Did that woman tell you to imitate his rudeness too?”

Raven scowled at me, but it wasn’t like this was my first time seeing that expression on her face. Unbothered, I passed on all the information I had for her. Even Raven, who at first questioned what this conversation was all about, experienced a noticeable shift in expression as the story progressed.
“Why Noark is repeating such a fruitless attempt... We were curious about that as well. And you have a point. I will compile this theory and immediately relay it to my superiors—”
“Not relay, you need to prepare measures right away.”
“...I’ll take care of that. You can leave.”
I even cut her off and spoke firmly, but unfortunately, it didn’t work out all that well. Was it because I wasn’t speaking like a barbarian?
“I guess that didn’t go well.”
“I can only hope Raven passes it on to the higher-ups.”
A while after I had come out of the barracks and spent some time guarding it from the outside, out of nowhere, something dark soared through the air and landed in front of us.
Thwack!
Then, it slowly stood up. “Gruhhh!” It was a corpse with squelching skin.

chapters.title: Chapter 355: Isolation (2)
paragraphs: The corpse rose from the ground. Its skin was red and bumpy, like it was on the verge of bursting at any moment, and there were stitch marks scattered all over it.
“No way... Corpse Collector...?” Amelia murmured.
I let out an involuntary sigh.
So, you were thinking the same thing.
There could only be one necromancer from Noark here.
Yeah, if it was really an elite few that snuck in, there’s no way that bastard would get left out.

Abed Necrapeto was a criminal belonging to Orcules with the nickname of Corpse Collector. He specialized in many-v-one combat. I could already feel a headache gathering at my temples. If this guy was here, that meant Noark was going all out.
Ha, there hasn’t been an ambush on the rear corps since that one failed attempt months ago, but of course as soon as I get here...
I couldn’t help taking a moment to complain, but I knew I should probably put that off until later.
Dash.
I immediately sprinted forward and brought my hammer down on the corpse’s skull. There was no need to even use Swing.
Smash!
The corpse was instantly crushed and blood exploded everywhere. As was par for the course for a close-combat warrior like me, I had no choice but to get coated in it.
Chhhhhh!
Jeez, judging by the poison, I guess it really is him.
“Are you all right?”

“Don’t worry. I’m fine,” I answered Amelia. I didn’t need an immunity bonus from Elementalization for something like this. The +120 Poison Tolerance I got from Vol-Herchan was enough to handle the contact poison on my skin. It was a bit itchy, though.
“Anyway, it looks like it’s slowly starting...” I said. While I was pleased that my hypothesis was correct, I noticed that Erwen had gone as still as stone next to me. “...Erwen, are you okay?”
“...Pardon? W-What did you just say?”
“I asked if you were okay.”
“Ah... ah! Yes...” Erwen nodded, but she still sounded distracted and her eyes were locked on the mangled corpse. “Corpse... Collector...”
Ah, right. Come to think of it, this was basically an encounter with her sister’s killer. The one who had killed Daria was Fallen Scholar, but this guy had played a significant role.
When Erwen spoke again, her voice trembled. “...Can we kill him?”

I contemplated this for a moment and answered, “Maybe.” If all went well, it might be possible for us to kill him. “But our survival comes first today,” I added firmly. If she got carried away trying to avenge her sister and ended up losing something again, it’d be a no-win scenario.
I didn’t know if she realized that herself or not, but Erwen stared at me blankly for about five seconds. Then she bit down on her lip and balled up her fists. “...Okay. I’ll do as you say, Mister.”

That left me ill at ease. I went up to Erwen and put a hand on her shoulder, even though I wasn’t sure if I could provide her any comfort right now. “Erwen, don’t worry. I’m also the type who needs to give people a taste of their own medicine. I haven’t forgotten what they did to me, not once.”

It started as an attempt at consolation but all of that was sincere. The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos; the Corpse Collector, Abed Necrapeto; the Fallen Scholar, Belbev Ruingenes—I hadn’t forgotten my grudges against those guys, either. I was simply waiting for the right time to strike.
“Just wait a little longer. It won’t take long.”
“...Okay.”
Okay, then I think she’s emotionally recovered at this point.
“Emily, where did that guy go?” As I shook the blood off my arm, I asked after Alex’s whereabouts.
“He went back into the barracks as soon as the body dropped down in front of us.”
Hmm, did he go report this to Raven? Then why isn’t he out yet?
Meanwhile, more corpses were falling from the sky.
“You were right.”
Jeez, speak of the devil.

When I turned around, I could see Raven coming out of the barracks with Alex. Her expression had grown much grimmer in the short while between our last conversation and now. “I should have put my foot down when the command unit decided to ignore our concerns.”
What the—? Regretting stuff like that isn’t like you.
There was no greater waste of time than dwelling on the past. “But what are you going to do now?”
“I’ve just received orders from command. All troops from each unit are to gather at the lake. It looks like they’re planning to use the magic circle on the hull of the flagship to fight back.”
A rally instead of a fight, huh? They must have chosen the most conservative strategy since they didn’t know anything about the enemy’s forces yet. “Then are we moving right now?”
“No. We will wait here a moment. I’ve contacted the other wizards within the corps, so they should gather here with the adventurers soon.”

So we were going to go to the lake once everyone got here. After that, we would get on the ship there and activate a magic circle to buy time. I didn’t know if this was a good plan, but it wasn’t like there was a better way.
“Personnel status report.”
“There are three confirmed deaths and the whereabouts of two individuals are unknown!”
“Two missing... we can’t dawdle here any longer because of two people who haven’t been confirmed dead or alive. Let’s move.”
We cleared out the zombies and waited for the wizards from the corps to gather along with their escort adventurers. It was now time to head to the lake.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-seven support spell Neutralization.]

Close-combat adventurers like me cleared the way with support from wizards and long-rangers. The process of relocating went off without a hitch. That was because there were only animated corpses for now, and even they couldn’t stop hundreds of tanks who had the support of dozens of wizards. But, as we were moving steadily toward the lake, the ground suddenly shook with a bang that sounded like a nuclear bomb going off.
Kaboom!
“Looks like there’s been damage to the magic circle.”

The fog that had been dispersed by magic began to gather in the air again, blocking our sight. Well, there was a plus side. The alarm spell that had been ringing like an emergency siren seemed to have been damaged as well, as it became much quieter.
“What are you all doing? Don’t stop moving!”

Soon, Raven used Wind magic to remove the surrounding fog and the group got moving again. Before long, once the blood-red lake was close enough to see with the naked eye, the wizards summoned small ships and set them on the water. And at that moment...
“Board the ships one by—”
“Aaaagh!” The scream of a dying man echoed from the back of the group. Because no one had been injured in the battle with the zombies up to this point, the scream sounded particularly loud.
Tap.
Raven, who had been about to step into one of the ships, retracted her leg. “...What’s going on?”
“We still need to confirm. It’s probably not a big deal, though, so—”
“No. I have to know. Halo, you stay here and lead the rest aboard.”
Raven ordered the others to board the ship first. It seemed she didn’t want to board when she had no information about what was going on.
Wow, is this the responsibility of a military commander?
I’d heard Raven was held in high regard by the corps and I thought I could see why. Raven was a conscientious and trustworthy leader.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you following?”
The problem was that our mission was to escort her. If she didn’t get on the boat, we couldn’t, either. “...Where are you going to go?”
Raven’s answer to my question was short. “The rear. Something doesn’t feel right.”
If something doesn’t feel right, shouldn’t you be running in the opposite direction?
Just as I was thinking this, another scream rang out from the back. “Aaagh!”
“Deputy Commander! We’ve identified the enemy!”

Finally, we got a report on what was happening back there. Surprisingly, there was only one enemy, but no one took the current situation lightly. That was because the enemy described was one of the most famous in the city.
“...An old knight in dark red armor?”
“Yes. It has been confirmed he is wielding an aura.”
Blood Knight was a criminal belonging to Orcules who had been born in Bifron and made his start in life as a knight. He later became infamous for murdering the previous commander of the Royal Guard.

“Emily, do you know anything?” While Raven was talking to her subordinate, I also snuck back to get information from Amelia, but there was nothing particularly useful. Apparently, they’d had no contact because he was never active outside the city. She had only seen him a few times in Noark’s castle, and even then they apparently never had a conversation.
“Deputy Commander! You must go quickly while they hold him off in the rear!”
“No. If we really have encountered Blood Knight, it will be nearly impossible to mitigate the damage.”
“But—!”
“No buts. If someone has to stop him, it’s only logical that I be the one to do it. Get on the boat before me. That’s an order.”

“...Yes ma’am!” The wizard on the receiving end of Raven’s orders saluted her with a worried but touched look on his face. It would have been a very heartwarming scene if we weren’t the ones being forced to act it out.

“On that note, Miss Erwen. Could you help me until the corps board the ship?” After she finished convincing her subordinates, Raven made a sincere plea for Erwen’s help. “You just need to buy me some time. After that, we can use Multi Teleportation to escape.”
What? I’m sure her school isn’t allowed to learn that spell.
“Multi Teleportation...?” I echoed aloud without thinking.

Raven answered me without so much as glancing in my direction, instead keeping her eyes on Erwen. “I was fortunate enough to have the opportunity to learn it. If I had this back then... there might have been another way out that day. Of course... it’s already far too late to be thinking things like that. I’ll entrust this to you.”
In response to Raven’s persistent request, Erwen glanced at me. It looked like she wanted me to decide what to do for her.
“Why are you looking at him?” Raven shot me a scrutinizing glare as Erwen delegated the decision-making process to me. “To think you would imitate even this part of their dynamic...”
Well, Raven seemed to be fine with it despite her complaints, so I ignored her continued misunderstanding and quickly checked something else. “What will you do if we don’t follow?”
“You will be disciplined for violating military law. You will never be able to partake in royal campaigns again.”
Uh, is this a threat? But that wasn’t what I asked...
“I was asking what you will do. If we say that we won’t follow you regardless of disciplinary action, do you plan on going alone?”
“Ah...” Raven thought this over for a moment and answered, “It’d be impossible on my own. I’d probably go with other adventurers.”

So, not going wasn’t even an option on the table. Somehow, this kid had gotten stubborn about the strangest things. Though I supposed it wasn’t like she hadn’t had her altruistic tendencies in the past, either. “Okay, then let’s go together.”

After coming to a decision, there was no need to waste time. The rear wasn’t even that far away. When we arrived at the spot the screams were originating from, the first thing I saw was a defenseless wizard on the ground about to be hit with a ferocious aura.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-four support spell Trajectory Interference.]
Instead of blocking the aura with an ordinary defense spell, Raven cast support magic and redirected the sword’s trajectory.
Whooom!

The greatsword passed over the top of the man’s head instead of his neck. As soon as I saw this, I immediately sprinted forward and pulled the panicked wizard out of danger. “Ah...! Th-thank you for—D-Deputy Commander?!”
“Raymond, you did well. Leave the rest to us and lead the rest of the adventurers to the main unit. That’s an order.”
“...Yes ma’am!” The wizard led the adventurers away as instructed by Raven. Surprisingly, the enemy just watched all of this happen from afar with a look in his eyes that gave me goosebumps.
That man is Blood Knight...

First, I covered my upper body with my shield and took my position in front. Then, facing him, I looked him up and down. My first impression was that he was shorter than I thought he’d be. He had to be 5′4″ at best, but he didn’t seem like he’d be an easy enemy at all.
Why does he give off such a strange air?

His stockiness was apparent from his build. Coupled with his unique aura, the amount of intimidation he radiated from that small form of his was considerable. The biggest contributing factor was probably his voice.

“The Golden Wizard, Arua Raven.” His voice went beyond scratchy; there had to be something wrong with his vocal cords. There seemed to be gravel in his throat as he slowly spoke. “One of the targets to be killed.” With that, he raised his greatsword in a businesslike manner.
So, you don’t even care about us?
Staring at his blood-red aura, which suited his nickname of Blood Knight, I muttered, “Erwen, Elementalization.”
“Which one should I use?”
Which one do you think? Is there anything else to whip out against a knight?
“Earth.”
As soon as I answered, Erwen’s body turned translucent. The moment we joined hands, I could feel the power of the earth flow through my skin.

[The Spirit of the Earth now dwells in your body. Any damage received from Fire attribute attacks is reduced by half. Any damage received from Water attribute attacks is doubled. Poison immunity bonus. When using blunt weapons, a Strength bonus is added to attacks. Your Physical Resistance has increased significantly.]
Whew, it’s been a while since I’ve used Elemental Barbarian (Earth) mode.
[Your Physical Resistance stat is over 350. Any stabbing damage taken will be reduced by 50%.]
Anyway, at this point, the second stage should have activated even without Giantization.
“What a pointless thing to do.”
Jeez, don’t be so arrogant just because you know how to use an aura. Woe is to the tanks.
“Die!”
Watching the old knight rapidly close the distance between us, I grinned.
Who’s dying? Do you know why I even came all the way here?
[You have cast Iron Fortress. The effect of Evolving Shell has increased by 1.5 times.]
My nickname had once been Knight Crusher. The day had finally come for that to truly shine.

chapters.title: Chapter 356: Isolation (3)
paragraphs: The effect granted by stage one of Evolving Shell was a 50 percent resistance to swords. Starting at stage two, stabbing damage was reduced by half. So what would happen if those effects were multiplied by 1.5? The answer was simple: Sword Resistance went up by 75 percent and Stab Wound Reduction got a 75 percent boost as well. Essentially, when you used Iron Fortress in combination with Sword Resistance, you reached a state where you were virtually immune to taking any penetration damage from swords.
If it weren’t for the limit, I would have received a Sword Immunity achievement.

The limit of any Sword Resistance buff was about 85 percent. And so, even with the passive strengthening effect of Transcendence, I couldn’t reach total immunity. In essence, I was pretty much only immune to getting stabbed. Although slashes would get through, I had the Ogre’s passive skill, Ironskin, covering my bases there.
Ironskin on top of my current Physical Resistance means...
Well, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say I’d become a knight’s worst nightmare at this point.
However, she must have been worried since she didn’t know that. The moment Blood Knight’s feet kicked off the ground, someone shouted, “Watch out!” It was Raven’s voice.
Showing her would be quicker than explaining it to her, right?
Slide.
With that in mind, I blocked the enemy’s thrust with my shield.
Khak!

Perhaps it had been a long time since he heard that sound from the tip of his sword. As he took in the fact that my shield was blocking his aura, my opponent’s face displayed utter bewilderment. “How...?”
How do you think?

The ability Union, which I’d obtained from the sixth stage of the Immortality Imprint, was all about a warrior’s weapons becoming one with the body. This essentially meant that when I used abilities like Giantization, my equipment benefitted from the effects as well. The same went for Evolving Shell.
Ah, maybe that isn’t what he’s wondering, though.

He probably wouldn’t be worried about the minutia. He would only be curious how I managed to block an aura. Well, there was a whole long backstory to that, but in this world of survival of the fittest, it could be summed up in just one sentence.
Shoving his sword back with my shield, I spoke. “I am stronger than you.”
What else was there to say in this world of winners and losers?
Whoom!
As if to engrave that in his mind, I swung my hammer with all my might.
Dash.
As expected, my enemy quickly backed away. That wasn’t anything to be disappointed about, though. After all, nothing was easier than catching a guy who was running away.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm. By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
I linked Transcendence together with Eye of the Storm.
Whiiip!
The gust that blew in out of nowhere dragged the enemy over to me. No, to be more precise, he was dragged right into the path of my swinging hammer.
Swish!
Unfortunately, just before my hammer could touch him, his body went as blurry as the fog around us and he quickly maneuvered in mid-air to avoid it.
So, you don’t just have an aura, huh?

I adjusted my grip on my hammer with that thought in mind. Raven, apparently unable to shake off her old habits, hurriedly shouted, “Blood Penetration! It’s a rank-four ability that allows a person to temporarily accelerate and move through the air!”

I’m grateful, but I knew that as soon as I saw it. Besides, your explanation is too basic. This isn’t simple acceleration but an increase in Agility. You also omitted the fact that it decreases the user’s Strength stat and temporarily gives them the attributes of a spirit-type, meaning physical damage can’t be dealt to them.
I watched the blood-red blur move through the air like a fly and bit my lip. Now that I had the Demon Grinder, I had been hoping to get a taste of combat this time.
But since he has that ability, it’s best to leave damage to the others.
It was unfortunate I couldn’t get rid of him myself, but I didn’t intend to be stubborn.
Teamwork was fundamental for a tank.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Element Synthesis.]

Five elemental attributes combined into one arrow to pursue the blood-red fog: Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, and even Darkness, which had become Erwen’s main attribute after signing a contract with the Elemental Ruler.
Auras are definitely overpowered.
The arrows were all destroyed by the enemy’s sword. However, it seemed he thought these arrows were a threat to him regardless.
Shoooooot!
Despite the fact that he was just running away, the enemy turned around and flew straight at Erwen. I guessed he figured he should deal with the long-ranger first.
But do you really think that will work? You’re making the tank feel bad.
“Erwen, get behind me.”
The moment he started flying in, Erwen hid behind me. This was why tanks were so important inside the labyrinth. They could become walls for damagers to hide behind anywhere, any time.
Whoom!
