Even though Erwen disappeared behind me, our opponent did not give up and swung his sword. It wasn’t a blind redo of his earlier attack, though. I guessed he assumed it was my shield that had blocked his aura last time, as he aimed for the seams of my armor this time. In other words, he targeted the joints where my skin was exposed. Of course, the results weren’t much different.
Slice!

It was a slash, not a stab. As a consequence, I didn’t get the benefits of the Evolving Shell buff, but Ironskin was activated, so I was only slightly cut. Put simply, I just withstood an aura with my bare skin. My enemy’s eyes widened at the unexpected sight.
Jeez, you’re surprised again? What, you didn’t believe me earlier when I said I was stronger than you?

“Sheter Ebon!” Raven shot a curse spell at the enemy, who had stopped for a moment to attack me. Since I’d seen this spell countless times during our quests together, there was no need to wonder what it was. Materialization was a rank-eight curse that forcibly stripped spirit monsters of their Physical Immunity.
Yeah, this is what you call teamwork.
When I lived in Noark, there were a lot of frustrating moments thanks to the lack of a wizard on our team.
Whooom!
As soon as the enemy’s body, which was a blur, became clear again, I slammed down the hammer. However, perhaps because I had low agility, I missed again.
Whew, I’m confident I can keep him from getting up again if I just get one hit in.
“I’ll help.” Amelia joined the battle, summoning her doppelgangers to tackle the corpses, which were coming at us from all directions even now.

“...Who are you guys?” our enemy wondered, looking at us. It seemed he was too curious not to ask, despite the fact that he couldn’t hold his own against my vicious attacks. Obviously, I was not obliged to answer. “People like you aren’t—”

“Woahhh!” I shouted out a war cry instead of the name of my ancestral god, who I could no longer call on unless I wanted my identity revealed, and swung my hammer repeatedly. The enemy swallowed his question and focused only on dodging.

As the battle raged on, he fought back with all kinds of skills. However, he was quickly put on the defensive. That was to be expected. Dungeon and Stone was a team game, and even if you looked at us individually, our current team members weren’t lacking in any way. That much was true even if you just looked at Erwen.
“Erwen, back!”

She did hide behind me each time she was targeted, but that didn’t mean she was weaker than the enemy—if she were alone, she could just use her natural gift for agility and various, versatile spirit abilities to widen the distance again. Even if this were a one-on-one fight, she wouldn’t lose. The same went for Amelia.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Power of the Abyss.]
The Blood Knight’s aura could be blocked by another aura, and her physical specs weren’t inferior to his, either. Raven was a bit different, though.
“Arhen Hail Tun... Kyaaa!” She wasn’t really useful here. It didn’t make sense for a wizard to 1v1 a knight in the first place.
“Even if you’re scared, stay right behind me. It seems he’s determined to target you.”
“O-Okay.”
Erwen and Amelia were both strong enough to take care of themselves, so I focused on protecting Raven throughout the battle. As it dragged on, however, I started to sense that something was off.

Why isn’t he running even though things have reached this point? He should have realized by now that he’s inevitably going to lose if this continues, so why is he not retreating? Is he waiting for my MP to run out?

If that was the case, that wasn’t really an issue. Although Iron Fortress did drain MP by the second, I purposefully didn’t activate Giantization for that reason. I’d sooner see the end of the match than run out of MP.
Something felt ominous so I checked on our last remaining insurance. “How’s the Multi Teleportation coming?”
“If I start preparing it again now, it’ll take about five more minutes.”
“Again...?”
“Actually... I stopped preparing it earlier...”
You thought we wouldn’t need it considering our overwhelming upper hand.
“Start preparing it now. You never know if things will take a turn.”
“...Okay.”
The moment that order left my lips, Amelia let out an urgent shout. “Schuitz, magic!”
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-three black magic spell Falling Star.]
A giant black sphere plummeted from the sky and through the fog.
God damn it. So, you were waiting for your comrade.

When the spell activated and I realized I couldn’t avoid it, my body froze on the spot. I hadn’t optimized my build for magic yet. My aura setup was pretty much done, but in return, my Mana Resistance was much lower than before.
Looks like she noticed it too late too.
It seemed even Raven, who was busy casting Multi Teleportation, was going to have a hard time blocking this one.
What can I do? I have to counter it with what I’ve got.

I made my decision in what felt like a split second. That spell was coming toward me, and Erwen and Amelia were quite a distance from me. But if I avoided it, Raven, who was right behind me, wouldn’t be safe. And so, there was only one option.
Pulling Raven’s small body into my arms, I dragged us both to the ground and covered her.
Giantization.
“M-Mister...!”
“Shuitz!”
Immediately after I managed to activate Transcendence and bulk myself up even more, the magic came down on us and struck my back.
Baaaaaaaaang!

The first thing I felt was a spine-breaking jolt. Next, my organs were concussed by a shockwave that moved through my bones and muscles, and a tingling sensation akin to electricity sizzled through my blood. Was it because the Corpse Golem was gone? Why the hell was this so painful?
“Uh...” As I grimaced instinctively at the unbearable pain, I heard a sound below me.
“How... even Giantization...?”
Yikes, has it all gone down the drain now?
This was why I had been saving Giantization. Unlike Swing, which had almost no visible effect, this skill was immediately noticeable to anyone watching.
“Are... you...”
Jeez, this is not the time for that.
“Let’s... talk later.” As soon as the shock running down my spine subsided, I hurried to stand up.
Clunk.
Something fell behind me. It was a completely shattered piece of armor.
Ugh, so dizzy.
My vision was blurry, not because of the fog, but because of the smoke. Smoke that was coming from my body.
Chhhhhh.
Wow, how long had it been since my body was wrecked like this? Even as I forced myself to my feet, each of my joints screamed at me in protest.
Tsk, exaggerating much? Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. It’s been a while.
Trying to keep my thoughts flippant, I stood up completely and set Raven down. Then I sent her behind me. It was only then that she saw the state I was in. “Your... b-b-back...!”
What about my back? At least finish your sentence.
Just then, Amelia came up next to me and reviewed the situation on my behalf. “It would be best for you not to know the state you’re in.”
“...That bad?”
“Yes, it’s a wonder you’re still standing.”
Ah. Um, well... If you say so.
“...Whatever, just pour a potion on me.”
“We... already poured one.”
Huh? But I didn’t feel anything. Ah, is my backside completely paralyzed? Come to think of it, it did stop hurting at some point...

I figured that, at least, was a positive and directed my attention forward. The first thing I saw was Blood Knight standing a distance away from us. He looked like a train wreck after being beaten four-on-one, though from the sound of it, he seemed to be in better condition than I was. Anyway, none of that was important.

“Grandpa, why are you pushing yourself like this? Do you know how surprised I was when I heard the news from Necrapeto?” A robed woman was standing next to Blood Knight. Since she was holding a wand, she had to be a wizard. So was she the one who cast the spell just now? Sensing my gaze, the woman smiled brightly and waved her hand. “Ah! Hello! I don’t know how you survived that, but it’s nice to meet you!”
Erwen trembled with rage at this.
“Erwen, I’m fine, so don’t fall for her taunts.” Even as I said that, I dragged Erwen to my side by her wrist before directing my attention to Amelia. “Emily, who is that woman?”
“The Wailing Witch, Lyranne Vivian.”
Ah, so that’s her. This is my first time seeing her in person.
“Then what about the man standing next to her?”
When I glanced at the second of the three newcomers, Amelia answered immediately. “The Lighthouse Keeper. His real name is unknown.”
Ha, this bastard is also famous. One of the few support-type special ability users in Orcules.
“And next to him...”
“It’s fine. I know who he is.” I cut her off and shifted my gaze.
As soon as our eyes met, I could see his widen through the opening in his mask. “So! Do our numbers match up now? Mr. Fake?”
The Corpse Collector, Abed Necrapeto. Jeez, why is this son of a bitch everywhere?

chapters.title: Chapter 357: Isolation (4)
paragraphs: Even among Orcules, the most wicked criminal organization in this world, these four people had quite a reputation. Maybe that was why I felt so strange in that moment, because the difference was starker than ever.
“Schuitz, what do you want to do?”

What else was there to do? In the battle in the Goblin Forest on the second floor, there had only been three of them. To fight those three people, over a thousand adventurers had sacrificed their lives.
“We have to fight. At least until the spell is complete.”
The situation now wasn’t as hopeless as it had been back then, though. No, with this team, my first thought was that this was doable.
“Is that so? Okay.” Judging by Amelia’s reaction, it seemed I wasn’t the only one who thought it was worth a shot.
Erwen looked like she hadn’t even considered running away in the first place. “...Abed Necrapeto.”

The moment Corpse Collector appeared in the distance, murderous intent began to radiate from Erwen’s body. I considered warning her to reign herself in, but there was no need. This was better than her being scared. Besides, seeing as she hadn’t run at him immediately, it didn’t look like she’d lost her senses yet, either.

“What are you doing? You stopped casting.” She had the presence of mind to tell Raven, who was frozen in a daze, to continue casting the teleportation spell. She seemed to remember what I said earlier about survival coming first. I was oddly proud of her.

“Oh... O-Okay.” Raven had been unresponsive since she saw my back but she came to her senses and carried on with her work. I guessed she concluded this was not the time to sate her curiosity about me.
Welp, I’m sure she noticed, right?
While I was worried about how this would play out in the future, on the other hand, I was still hopeful. Even Corpse Collector had called me Mr. Fake.

“Pshehe, aren’t you staring a little too hard, Miss Elf? Even I feel uncomfortable. Hmm, anyway, I’m surprised! I heard you borrowed a large sum from your clan, but... I didn’t know you used it to make a counterfeit like that!”

Even after seeing Giantization, he didn’t make the connection that I was Bjorn Yandel. True, he was probably convinced I was dead. Since Erwen’s eccentric nature was so widely known, it probably made more sense to think she created a knock-off.
I wish Raven thought that way too... Ugh, whatever. If I’m caught, I’m caught.

I was sure she wouldn’t tattle because she ‘couldn’t betray the palace’ or whatever now that I’d sacrificed this body to save her. I decided to stop worrying about this starting now. I didn’t think the enemy was going to give me more time to think, anyway.
The dark wizard on the other side noticed our insurance plan. “Necrapeto, the spell that woman is casting over there, I think it’s Multi Teleportation.”
“Pshehe, then we should hurry. A dance of blood, bones, and despair—”
“Ah, can you quit talking like that? Why did you develop that strange habit all of a sudden? Not to mention that mask you started wearing whenever we go on expeditions...”
“Um... Miss Vivian, there are people watching...”
“That’s why I’m telling you not to do that stuff! Ugh, honestly, why does he get so weird whenever he comes outside?”
“...It’s a hobby. A hobby.”

There was a brief delay as the Wailing Witch scolded Corpse Collector, but it didn’t last long. “Both of you, stop it and do your job.” The large man in the robe, Lighthouse Keeper, stopped their conversation, and their banter naturally dried up.
I guessed our attempt to fill the teleport gauge would have to stop here. “How long until you can use the teleportation spell?”
“...It will take ten minutes. When the spell was canceled earlier, the mana dispersed.”
“Then what about using another spell while you cast it?”
“It’s possible. High-level magic would be pushing it but I should be able to help when needed.”
Okay, that took a weight off my shoulders. “Focus on finishing the spell for now, but support us when you see fit.”
“Okay—wait, why are you in charge?”

That was nothing new. “What a foolish question. Is that important right now?” I quickly steamrolled past that and continued giving orders. “Erwen, Emily. You two focus on protecting her for now. That spell has to be completed as soon as possible.”
“Okay.” Surprisingly, Erwen agreed without a moment’s hesitation.
Amelia had a question, though. “Isn’t it better to give up on the spell entirely and work together to fight them?”

That wouldn’t be a bad plan, honestly, but I couldn’t ignore the possibility of reinforcements. “We don’t know when another one of them will show up.” Also, even if support didn’t come, I was reluctant to see this match through to the end. The odds were good enough, but it would be a tough fight. There was a high chance one of us would get hurt or die in the process.
“...That’s true. Okay. I’ll do as you say.” I guessed that was enough explanation because Amelia didn’t say any more. Hmm, or should I say we no longer had the luxury for chitchat?
“Gruhhh!” The battle began when the legion of corpses surrounding us charged at us all at once.

On paper, the situation was simple. The corpse legion was running in from all sides and we took up a defensive formation to stop them. The problem here was that the corpses, which used to explode with just one hit, were now much more of a threat.
“Gruhhh!”
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-five black magic spell Rage of the Dead.]
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-four black magic spell Dark Baptism.]
Dark wizard and necromancer was a powerful combination that was once my favorite too. Black magic was filled with highly efficient buffs for undead. They had good synergy.
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-four black magic spell Lamp of the Underworld.]
Whew, so you’re using that one too. Well, you can’t go without that spell in this combo.
Whooom!
The moment a black flame appeared in the sky, the corpses we’d worked so hard to beat up to this point regenerated and came back to life.
[Lyranne Vivian has summoned Erimian, Queen of Pain.]
A vengeful spirit studded with thousands of thorns soared through the sky with a shriek. It was the signature summon that had earned the dark wizard Lyranne Vivian the nickname of Wailing Witch.
[Your Pain Resistance has decreased by -200.]
[When any target who hears the scream takes damage, a fixed amount of the summoner’s dark magic is restored.]
Mana was a wizard’s most important resource.
Well, we just have to be careful not to get hurt.
As long as we were fighting in small, elite teams, this wasn’t such a tough summoned beast to deal with.
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-three black magic spell Voodoo Doll. The accuracy rate of curses targeting you increases to 100%, and their strength significantly increases.]
After completing her basic preparations, from buffing the corpse legion and pulling out her signature summoned beast, the Wailing Witch officially began casting spells.
[High-Level Decay remains in effect. The speed at which your wounds are healed is significantly reduced.]
[Lethargy remains in effect. Your Strength is significantly reduced.]
[Invisible Threat remains in effect. The chances of you missing an enemy attack have increased.]
Jeez, why is she only placing curses on me?
It reminded me of that priest of Karui, Elisa, and almost triggered my PTSD from that incident. But what could I do? I had to buck up.
Deciding to scream at the top of my lungs since I couldn’t scream for my ancestral god, I roared and swung my hammer. That was the only thing a warrior could do in a situation like this. “Aghhhhhh!”
Crunch!
Dedicating my every movement to protecting my allies, I left the long-range attacks to Erwen. Thankfully, Erwen offered a great return on investment.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Element Synthesis.]
She fired off an attack of pure, concentrated power to keep the enemy in check.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast High-Speed Fire.]
Fire poured down from the sky like rain.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned Dicloe, the Elemental Ruler of Darkness.]
Even the Elemental Ruler of Darkness, the summon that had earned Erwen the nickname Blood Spirit, joined the party.
K-K-Kablam!

The Elemental Ruler was only summoned for about five seconds but in that short period, half of the enemy’s large legion were despawned—literally despawned. Even the Lamp of the Underworld couldn’t revive corpses that had disappeared without a trace.
“N-No! Do you know how long it took me to collect those?!”

Even Corpse Collector had some high praise for that overwhelming show of brutality. However, in return for summoning the Elemental Ruler, Erwen’s Soul Power was depleted. She was still able to use various skills that used Soul Power as a resource, but she would not be able to use spirits from now on.
“You did well.”
“It’s... nothing.”

Erwen’s secret weapon had disappeared, but the situation wasn’t looking too bad. This was thanks to the respite we were given as a result of the large gap in the corpse legion that had been flocking in. Unfortunately, that respite didn’t last long.
“Schuitz, he’s coming.”
“I’ll take care of that guy, so you step back.”
Blood Knight, who had been sticking to the rear even as the battle kicked off again, got healed by Lighthouse Keeper and rejoined the fight.
I guess a support-type special ability user would also have a heal skill.

That was frustrating. It wasn’t long ago that his entire left arm got blown off by Erwen’s Rupture, but it was already better? Even an advanced potion would have side effects that lasted for a long while after the fact.
Slice!
Huh?

“Ugh.” The bastard was aiming for the seams of my armor again, and I was about to counterattack when I suddenly froze in place. Since my Pain Resistance had dropped by two hundred, it was only natural I would feel pain for even a small wound, but this one was much deeper than before.
“Now I can cut you.”
The bleeding was relatively minor and a burnt smell filled the air. What was the cause of it? It wasn’t hard to piece together.
It’s not an aura.
My opponent’s sword was still covered in red energy, but it was different from the aura he was using before. The heat radiating from it was so powerful that it warmed the air around it.
Ha, you enchanted it with fire in that time?

This had to be Lighthouse Keeper’s doing. With the intel that I had been annihilated by magic just a few minutes ago, Blood Knight’s normal attack was exchanged for something that would deal magical damage.
That clever bastard.

Of course, even if he changed his weapon to fire, the buffs I had against swords and slash attacks didn’t change. This wasn’t too difficult to deal with, it was only that the battle had gotten a little harder.
I can withstand this much.
As expected, a power struggle ensued from there. It wasn’t without its close calls, but speaking in terms of results alone, time passed without either team racking up any significant wins.
“I-It’s done!” Finally, Raven completed the Multi Teleportation spell. We could now run from this battle any time we wanted to.
Okay, we’re officially subscribed to the insurance plan.
“Don’t use it yet. Just wait.”
“Sorry?”
What do you mean, sorry? You think I’ll be able to sleep at night after that beating I just took? If I have to leave, I’m taking at least one of them with me. So who should I choose?
Without needing to think for long, I decided on my first target.
“Hey! They finished their spell!” The dark wizard was flying on a broomstick, so pass.

“Vivian! Do something! If we let them go like this, my losses will be too big!” The Corpse Collector prick had high Agility stats and even a skill that made him virtually invincible, so he’d be tough to kill.
Whip!

The same went for Blood Knight, who was swinging his sword at close range. How could I take down a guy who dodged like an eel even during four-on-one? Unless I fought him solo in a closed room, that would be difficult.
“I’ll see you again someday.”
I smiled at Blood Knight, who spoke as if our escape was already a sure thing.
Jeez, who said we’re leaving like this? Yeah, he would be best.
Lighthouse Keeper, name unknown. His defining trait was that he was one of the few support-type special ability users in the city.
And trinkets are usually pricey.
He was also wearing rings on all ten fingers.

chapters.title: Chapter 358: Isolation (5)
paragraphs: His height was around 6′3″. Somehow, Noark’s special ability bender, Lighthouse Keeper, had a build better suited for a warrior than Blood Knight. Looking at him, I smacked my lips.
Whew... this would have been so much easier if I had Leap.
The distance between him and me was about 130 yards. It was a distance that could have been narrowed with just two uses of that skill.
Well, what can I do? It’s gone now.

I left my regrets behind. What was the point of missing something that was already gone? If I didn’t have a movement skill, I had no choice but to move with my own two feet. That kind of thinking was more aligned with the spirit of a barbarian too.
“Erwen, Emily. You two hold your positions here.”
“...What about you, Mister?”
“I’ll be back.”
“Back? Where—”
Where do you think?
[You have used Wild Outburst.]
Releasing a roar, I ran forward. “Ooowoah!”

It didn’t feel the same as yelling for my ancestral god, but it couldn’t be helped. I wasn’t certain Raven had caught me yet. Just as with Corpse Collector, there was a chance I’d simply exacerbated her earlier misunderstanding.
Dash.

When I ran forward, leaving the formation for the first time after solely playing defense for my comrades throughout this battle, there was an immediate reaction. It started with Blood Knight. He was standing far away so as not to enter the range of Multi Teleportation, but when he saw me coming, he charged at me.
Khak!
Do you really think that’s going to work? A sword using fire instead of an aura? I can just block that with a shield.
Dash.
Ignoring Blood Knight, I sprinted forward again. Of course, it was difficult to shake him off with my agility, which left my back exposed.
Slice!

I didn’t necessarily have to block the blow with a shield, though. Even if I decided to just take it with my body, the most it would do was cut slightly deeper—it wouldn’t lead to a serious injury like a lost limb or anything. It simply hurt a lot because of my low Pain Resistance.
Ugh, it’s like he slathered the sword with salt.
I grimaced at the surging pain, but it didn’t stop me from moving. If I were the type of person to stop what I was doing because of pain, I wouldn’t have gotten this far.
Dash.
Like a salmon swimming up the river, I kicked off the ground again.

As I did, I got some high praise from Blood Knight. “This—what the...?!” I guessed he was impressed by the sight of me continuing to run forward without any consideration for the fact that I had been stabbed in the back. “Stop...!” It was a bit dull compared to the rave reviews I’d received so far, but the shock in his voice was quite satisfying.
Yeah, when would you have ever experienced something like this before? With that aura of yours, you can usually cut down anything, including a tank.
Slice!
The bastard stabbed me again without pause. Of course, it made no difference. Cuts or not, I ran forward like a runaway train. There was nothing he could do to stop me.
Dash.
It was time for him to finally learn. He may not have realized it yet, comfortably resting on his laurels thanks to that aura of his, but...
Slice!
Damagers were helpless creatures in front of tanks.
Whiiip!
Just in time, supporting fire came in from behind me in the form of an arrow shot by Erwen.
Stab.

The arrow sunk right into the bastard’s arm. He had been dodging so well when they had us on the defensive—did he want to beat me that bad? I wasn’t sure about his logic, but he’d made an obvious mistake, and given the way his expression was already contorting, he knew it as well. Getting hit by a single arrow may not have been a big deal, but the follow-up attack was a different story.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
This was the skill that blew Amelia’s doppelganger to pieces.
Splat!
When she activated the ability, Blood Knight’s arm crumbled into dozens of pieces and dropped to the ground in chunks.
Okay, that gets rid of that annoying mosquito.
Dash.
Leaving behind Blood Knight, who collapsed from the shock of his arm exploding, I continued running. Of course, before long, the next obstacle appeared in my way.
“Wow, he’s like an Ogre!” It was the dark wizard, Lyranne Vivian, who was watching me without a care from dozens of feet in the air. She cackled and shot magic at me.
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-four black magic spell Corrupting Flame.]

It started with black flames pouring down from the sky like raindrops, but as was the case with most wide-range area-of-effect abilities like this one, the damage itself was bound to be less intense. I kicked off the ground, covering my head with my shield like an umbrella.
Well, it’ll do some damage to the shield... but that’s nothing new.
Had there ever been a time my shield was left intact after a difficult battle? I could make up for the repair costs with loot.
Dash.
With that in mind, I kicked off the ground once more and sprang forward. Perhaps that made my opponents feel the need to change their strategy.
[Lyranne Vivian has cast the rank-four black magic spell Tombstone of Pain.]
The rain of fire stopped and instead, a pitch-black fog appeared and swept over me.
Judging by the effect, it looks like this is that ability...
If my hypothesis was correct, there was no way to avoid this skill other than withstanding it with Mana Resistance.
In other words... my opponent won’t be able to avoid it, either.
The moment the fog clung to my body, I quickly recited the command in my head.
[You have cast Liability of Risk.]

The effect of my newly acquired active skill from Gachabone was simple. While active, the amount of damage you received was doubled, but the amount of damage you could reflect through Probabilistic Retaliation also increased.
[By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
When used in combination with Transcendence, it had an interesting effect.
[In exchange for the temporary deactivation of Probabilistic Retaliation’s Damage Immunity effect, the odds of activation have been set at 100%.]
It was a guaranteed Gacha.
Whooom!
As soon as the skill activated, the black fog clinging to my skin began to harden. This was the function of Tombstone of Pain: temporary movement restriction.
Shoop!
While trapped, you couldn’t avoid any attacks.
“Waaaaaah!”
Jeez, that hurts like hell.
Crunch!

I let out a shout and held out for about two seconds, and the hardened fog shattered like porcelain a moment later and fell to the ground. The inner surface of each chunk was riddled with sharp, protruding thorns.
Ha, what is this, a medieval torture device? But I suppose I’m glad that I’m the only one getting mangled.
Once the hit was registered, Probabilistic Retaliation was activated.
Drag, slide.
A skeleton rose beside me, its joints cracking. Perhaps it wasn’t a critical success this time as there wasn’t a fun sound effect.
[Your Ordinary Luck reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
It still did 30 percent, not 15 percent. Plus, since I had taken double the damage, I was in effect able to deal four times the usual return fire. Well, even that seemed kind of unfair to me, though.
“U-Uh...?!” Still, my opponent was a squishy, fragile wizard, right? I supposed this could work as payback. “W-What is this?!”
The moment the skeleton reached its hand out into the sky, a pitch-black fog blanketed the witch on the broomstick.
Shoop!
The disturbing shriek echoed all the way down here. “Kyaaaaaa!”
Jeez, what a pair of lungs. Is that why she’s called the Wailing Witch?
Dash.

I dragged my body, covered in big and small holes, forward again. Perhaps because it dealt a fixed amount of damage, the wounds weren’t doubly as deep even though the damage was doubled. It still hurt like hell, though.
Maybe that’s why she’s not dead, either.
As soon as the spell was lifted, Vivian plummeted to the ground screaming before getting a grip and using a floating spell to narrowly escape hitting the earth.
Looks like her wounds weren’t even that deep...
I had been hoping that even 30 percent damage would end up being a wombo combo on a wizard.
Maybe she managed to reduce the damage to some extent by activating something like a mana shield in the split second before the spell hit?
That was definitely disappointing.
“Arghhh...”
The attack still fulfilled its purpose, though. Seeing as she was busy curling up in pain, she wouldn’t have the energy or presence of mind to bombard me with magic for the next short while.
“Gruhhh!”

After I solved the problem of the dark wizard and started quickly closing the distance with the rear of their group, the Corpse Collector used some corpses he pulled out of his sub-space to block my path. There were seven in total. It seemed he whipped out undead specifically designed to stop tanks from handling me because each of them was big enough to make a large monster cry.
If I have to crane my neck this much to look up at them even while using Giantization... then they’re maybe about twenty-three feet?

Once again, I thought about how much easier this would have been if I still had Leap, but it wasn’t a major issue. I wasn’t just any tank. A wall standing in my way? There was no need to go around it.
[You have cast Swing.]
All I had to do was get rid of it.
[The range of all of your attacks is tripled.]

With an elongated hammer, I clobbered the head of the giant zombie standing at twenty-three feet tall. Despite it likely being an undead for tanks, this strike was enough. That was because Swing was based on your Strength stat, and with the Demon Grinder’s special effect, the damage it dealt went up 500 percent. Not to mention it was a downward strike, which meant I got a 50 percent Armor Penetration bonus on top of that.
Kwaaang!
How could a summoned beast stand up to something like that?
Shooot!
With one wallop, the corpse giant was reduced to a pile of rotten meat, blood shooting from it like a large fountain.
Whew, this poison is a bit strong.
[You have been Poisoned (High).]
[Your Poison Tolerance stat is over 100. The Poison’s rank has been adjusted to Low.]
The poison sank into my skin and got absorbed. It hurt, but it wasn’t enough to make me stop, especially when my target was right in front of me.
I’m almost there now.
I quickly ran through the opening left behind by the fallen corpse giant and stared straight ahead. The distance to the target was about a hundred feet.
What the—? Why is this prick so close?

Did he come all the way over here to summon the corpse giant? Standing about fifteen feet away, I could see Corpse Collector. Even at a glance, he looked very confused, and it would have been rude to just pass him by.
[You have cast Swing.]
[The range of all of your attacks is tripled.]
Without wasting a single second, I brought my hammer down on him. Instead of dodging, he opted to defend, using a skill I hadn’t seen in a long time.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Bone Armor.]
It took more than a few hammerings to break it last time. I wondered how it would be this time. And I was soon able to find out.
Crunch!
The shell surrounding the caster’s body was stripped away with just one blow of the hammer, exposing the skin underneath.
[Abed Necrapeto has cast Ephemeral Immortality.]

In an instant, the bastard was engulfed in flames and turned to bones. A rank-three essence, this was the highest-grade invincibility skill out there, one that converted your Spirit and Special Ability stats into Physique stats to make you immune to damage for one minute.
Wow, I didn’t think you would pull out the invincibility skill after one hit.
Since that had come into play, there was no longer any need for me to waste any strength on him, so I simply grabbed one of his arms and threw him far away.
Dash!

After that, I jumped high as if Leaping, allowing me to get a lay of the land. The stakes my target had planted in the vicinity were shooting out various special abilities like turrets in a war game. The effect of Lighthouse Keeper’s core skill, Noble Idol, was as follows: by planting totems on the ground, he could alter the abilities he possessed. For example, single-target buffs and curses could be converted into wide area of effect abilities.
I guess he was desperate.
Seeing as the totems were shooting flames and mana bullets, it seemed he had turned off support abilities like Acceleration and Soul Regeneration and quickly switched to attack mode.

“...You monster.” Even after watching me come all this way despite the attacks pummeling me from all sides, the enemy didn’t run. It must have been more risky for him to go outside the range of his totems. Soon, he shouted in a desperate tone, “Come!”
The hell? No way I’m going inside that.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm.]
[By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
At this point, I figured I was within range, so I used my grab technique.
Shaaaaaa!
A gust of wind rushed toward me.
“A-Aaagh!” My opponent got caught up in the gust and was sent flying in.
You sounded so posh when you were talking earlier, but I guess you scream like that when you’re in a tight spot.
Squeeze.
With my shield-covered hand, I grabbed the guy’s neck in mid-air. He struggled for a bit but quieted down when I applied more strength like he should have from the start.
Boom.
Dropping my opponent to the ground and looking down at him, I cut to the chase. “Those rings. I hope they’re expensive.”
The journey here had been tough.
Smack!

Grabbing my opponent by the neck again, I slammed my forehead into his face. Not only was this a bad angle for bringing down the hammer on him, but now that I was up close, I could see he was also wearing a necklace. If I hit that with the hammer, it’d get crushed.
I was about to headbutt him again when his body went limp. Was he dead, or just unconscious? I was hoping it was the former, so I headbutted him two more times.
Crunch, chomp!
Oh, how disgusting. Anyway, that should take care of him. Now, what should I do?
Now that I’d achieved my first goal, it was time to rethink things.
Since I’ve beaten Lighthouse Keeper, I think we can beat up the rest of them, four against three.
Should I retreat now and use teleportation, or continue fighting and beat the rest of these bastards up? I didn’t have too much time to think it through.
Boom, boom!
Even at this moment, the corpse giants were closing in on me.
Yeah, let’s dip for now.

I’d been stabbed countless times, struck by magic, and even poisoned on the way here. Things like that could be overcome with willpower, but my MP was holding on by a thread. I’d been maintaining Iron Fortress to face the aura user and even used Giantization just now. And that wasn’t all. I’d been firing off various skills willy-nilly and even linking them with Transcendence. If my MP bottomed out, it’d be hard to stop an aura, which would make it more difficult for me to protect my comrades from Blood Knight.
And it would be a problem if reinforcements showed up on top of that.
After making my decision, I turned back the way I came, still holding my newly-acquired loot by the throat. But what was this?
Why is no one attacking me?
The corpse giants who had been charging at me formed a wall as if to protect something, and no spells came at me, either.
“Necrapeto! What on earth are you doing?! Stop him! It’s not like it’ll kill you, anyway!”
Judging by the shouting, it seemed their wizard had recovered as well. So what was going on? The answer soon became clear.
“If you want to stop him, do it yourself, Miss Vivian!” a relatively intact undead shouted on behalf of Corpse Collector, who was currently just bones. “Looks like your magic works well enough!”
“What...? Were you not paying attention earlier? My spell was bounced back!”

Now that I was taking a second look, I could see they weren’t too eager to touch me after what they each went through. That was fair—they didn’t have any information on me, and I was sure they didn’t want to get snapped up and have their skulls shattered like Lighthouse Keeper. Thanks to that, the path ahead was clear as I ran, dragging his body along behind me.
“What, you’re going to fight me?”
Blood Knight, who had activated one-armed mode, now stood in my way. Then he asked, “Name?”
Huh?
“What is your name?”
That’s all you wanted to know?
I had only one thing to say to that. “If you’re going to fight me, then fight. If not, get lost. I need to get back and eat...” I paused for a moment and waited for a response. “Cat got your tongue?”
When I started running forward again, Blood Knight moved to the side. “I’ll learn it soon enough.”

Surprisingly, Blood Knight didn’t try to stab me in the back and let me go instead. It seemed he’d learned from the taste of helplessness he got earlier. True, how was he going to stop me when I could just ignore him and keep running even as he drove a blade into me?
Sprint.
I picked up speed in the final spurt and soon arrived at my destination. The magic circle on the ground was glowing like it was ready to go at any moment, but the wizard herself was frozen.
“What are you doing? Let’s go.”
At my prodding, Raven raised her head and looked at me. For some reason, her eyes seemed to be shaking violently.
What is it?
When I looked around in confusion, I noticed Erwen and Amelia were also wearing similar expressions on their faces.
Jeez, and I even came back with loot. They look like they’re staring at a monster.

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Interrogation (1)
paragraphs: The Wailing Witch, Lyranne Vivian, slowly descended from the sky and started shrieking the minute her feet touched the ground. “Necrapeto! Have you lost it? Why did you just let him go?!”
The man whose bones had just started to grow flesh scowled at the sound of that hysterical voice. “I’m still older than you, you know...”

“Ha! Is it really the time to argue about that? Let’s hear it. Why did you just let those bastards get away? If our leader finds out about this, you’re not getting off the hook!” Vivian’s fuse was short as she shouted at him and jabbed her index finger at a spot across the field, where a magic circle that had lost its light sat on the ground.
The man responded to this with annoyance. “Ha, why should I get in trouble? It’s already unreasonable to ask a necromancer to engage in close combat, and you saw what happened.”

The woman flinched as she was faced with a more thoughtful counterargument than expected. But it seemed her main issue was something else. “...But you didn’t even use the Staff of the Underworld!” Vivian regrouped and brought Corpse Collector’s core equipment into the fray.
“Why should I have used that?” the man asked in obvious disbelief.
“Because if you used it, Lighthouse Keeper wouldn’t have been cornered!”
She wasn’t wrong. If he had used the Staff of the Underworld, which was high-ranking even among double-digit Numbers Items, it was true he could have forced the enemy to flee the battlefield.
“If I used that, either he or I would have had to die. But you wanted me to use that on someone I have zero information on when I had a 100 percent chance of survival if I just left him alone?”
“But you also have your new ability.”

“And if it becomes common knowledge, the palace will prepare countermeasures for it. Who will that benefit? If I’m forced to rely on that ability in a dangerous situation, are you going to be the one to save me? Huh? Please keep your nose out of my business. I know for a fact that the reason why you didn’t use magic isn’t much different from why I didn’t use Staff of the Underworld.”

When the man began to argue in earnest, Vivian could only listen in silence. Everything he was saying was true. She hadn’t tried too hard to stop that monster for the same reason: because there was insufficient information. Since she had used a spell and had it rebounded back on her in kind, she had been hesitant to use an even stronger spell.
“Ugh, so annoying...”

In the end, all of them were responsible for their defeat. Even though they worked together as a single unit, the fact of the matter was that no one here was noble enough to sacrifice themselves for someone else. They all cared more about their own gains and losses than any threat to their comrades.

While Vivian pursed her lips in an attempt to reign in her anger, Blood Knight returned and joined the group. “...Is everyone okay?” The old man whose arm got blown off looked the most miserable of the three.

Vivian didn’t seem to care, though, and quickly redirected her ire at him. “We would have been if you fought properly, Grandpa. Instead of stopping that monster, you should have aimed for our other opponents in the rear!” Lyranne wasn’t saying this to find fault in him—she genuinely believed every word. “It’s not like you could have stopped him anyway, so why do something so useless...?”

If he had spent that time targeting the rest of their enemies instead, things would have gone differently. After all, that monster had spent the fight shielding his comrades from various attacks with his body before breaking off from their formation.

“Killing Blood Spirit, a member of the Seven Powerful, would have been a good enough achievement on its own. Not to mention the Golden Wizard. Not only was she one of our targets for this ambush, but the teleportation spell would have been voided the moment that woman died.” Blood Knight had made a bad call.

Necrapeto, who was watching this dressing down play out from the sidelines, sounded genuinely impressed as he exclaimed, “Wow, you... you’re going to blame Gramps right now? You’re even bigger trash than I thought. I can’t believe you would say that to the person who was trying to protect us.”
“What, I can’t even speak my mind? It’s not like I’m wrong.”
“Well, that’s true. Pshehe.” The man nodded and glanced at Blood Knight.

He had suddenly fallen prey to the wolves, but surprisingly the old knight made no excuses. He simply grumbled in his usual dry, scratchy voice, “Call the leader, quick. Tell them that we lost the Golden Wizard.”
“Why can’t you do it, Grandpa?”

Blood Knight answered with a cold look, and Vivian eventually lowered her head. Not only had they lost their target, but Lighthouse Keeper, who was a valuable resource within Orcules, had been defeated. What’s more, they had had to sit back and watch as the enemy used teleportation to escape because if they made a move, they might have been the ones to end up dead next. How could they tell their leader that?
While everyone was hesitating, Corpse Collector urged her to do it. “I get how you feel, but you should contact him first. There’s more information we need to relay even besides Golden Wizard.”
“...Are you talking about that monstrous bastard?”
“That too, but...” The man trailed off, then continued. “Anyway, just relay this: I don’t know how she got here, but... we found Amelia Rainwales.”
[Arua Raven has cast the rank-four spatial spell Multi Teleportation.]
When the light from the active magic circle faded, the first thing I could see were iron bars.
“Stand down. We’re in the right place.”
“...What are you talking about?”
“This is an installation inside every warship. When transportation type abilities are activated, it always directs the caster here as a protective measure against intruders.”
Ah, I see. But teleport guidance? I think I’ve heard about this somewhere before...

“I am Arua Raven, deputy commander of the Third Magic Corps. This is my ID. We have returned with teleportation magic from a battle with the criminals of Orcules.” Raven revealed her identity to the soldier stationed outside the cage, and soon after her identity was verified, the cage opened.
Clunk!
What the—why are you leaving us in here?
“...What is the meaning of this?”
Raven avoided my eyes—and my question—and said to the soldier, “These people will be kept here for the time being, so keep a close eye on them.”
“Yes ma’am.”
Uh... I didn’t expect this plot development.
Just as my mind was going blank, Erwen lunged at the bars and shook them. “I’ll kill you!”

It was hard to say she was just losing control as usual, because I felt like I was losing my control too. For some reason, this reminded me of the guild’s dungeon, and it made me want to destroy those bars immediately.
“I get how you feel, but please remain calm. It’s impossible to escape that cage by force anyway.”
“...What?”
“No. 399: Cage of Silence. Skills are sealed inside it, and you can’t use magic, divine power, or an aura, either.”
No wonder I felt a chill down my spine. After confirming my skills weren’t activating even after I recited a command in my head, I sighed and released the bar I was holding.

“Here... this is a potion. Please heal your wounds.” Raven handed a few bottles of potion through the bars and left after giving instructions to the soldier. To summarize the important points: Be courteous. No matter what happens, do not open the cage. If there is an emergency situation or enemy invasion, make sure to release us so that we can fight back.
“...She got us. Tersia, don’t waste your breath and come over here.”
“What? That woman just locked us in here! How can I—”
“What else can we do?”
I quickly regained my composure and spoke. “Erwen, she’s right. Calm down and come here.”
“...All right.” Erwen abandoned her stubbornness and came over to me.
“It... would be best to use the potions first.”
It seemed like it would take me a long time to recover through my natural healing factor alone, so I enlisted Amelia’s and Erwen’s help to pour the potions all over my body and stop the bleeding.
“Are you okay?”
“...Yeah, I’m used to it now.”
To be honest, I felt like I was going to die. The only Pain Resistance I had left now was the +30 attached to the essence of the Bayon. But what could I do? I had to treat the wounds somehow.
“Um... will you give us some water?”
“Ah... A-All right!”

When Erwen made a request to the soldier, he rushed to bring us water. I’m sure part of it had to do with Raven’s instructions to treat us courteously, but I figured it must also be hard for people to mistreat Erwen thanks to her status.
“Um... are you okay?” Or maybe he was just worried about me. “You look like you’re sweating more than bleeding...”
“I’m okay, don’t worry.”

This always happened whenever I took a potion. After I gulped down the water brought over by the kind-hearted soldier, I stood near the bars on the opposite side of the cage as the entrance. That was because the conversation we were about to have was confidential.
“Anyway, since we’ve dealt with first aid, let’s talk. Both of you, come here. And lower your voices.”
“Don’t you think your face is too close, Rainwales?”
“What’s the problem? It’s just to have a conversation.”
“...Th-then I’ll get close too...”
“Hmm, I’m sure I heard elves have good hearing?”
“W-What’s that got to do with you?”
“I’m just saying—”
Ugh, what was with these guys now? “Stop it, both of you. This is not the time for that.”
“Okay, Mister...”
Before we could really get off track, I hurriedly settled their quibbling and got down to business. The first thing on the agenda was this. “Why do you guys think Raven did that?”
Why did Raven lock us up here? Even their bickering selves easily reached a consensus on that point.
“I guess she’s figured out your identity.”
“Yes, that’s the only possible answer, Mister. People know you as an evil spirit now, so she must think the same. Even though you saved her life so many times, that ungrateful...”

Did murderous intent flow through this kid’s bloodstream now or what? I didn’t know, but I was worried about the condition of Erwen’s teeth if she kept grinding them like that, so I brought up the second most likely explanation. “Emily, what are the odds she did it because she figured out your identity?”
“Well, that could make sense too. Since that woman was on that island.”

Raven and Amelia were acquainted. They fought together on Farune Island, and Raven also knew that Amelia had the Power of the Abyss, Self-Replication, and Asura’s Kick. Using a dagger as her main weapon on top of that? Even if it had been more than two years and Amelia’s face was covered, Raven would have noticed the similarities.
“True... she might suspect we’re spies because of this woman. Ha, I knew this would happen.”
“Wait, what exactly did you know?”
“What do you think? That you would hold Mister back.”
“Pfft, you talk really well for someone who can’t even use your head.”
“What...?”
Wait, why was the conversation taking a turn like this? I quickly changed the subject. “Anyway, Emily, are you okay? There’s a good chance Noark recognized you as well.”
“They... probably did recognize me. Blood Knight I never had much contact with so he may not have, but at the very least, Corpse Collector would have.”
I felt a bit bad about that. She had been in complete hiding since changing her identity. Now, she’d become the enemy of both the palace and Noark.
“Don’t worry too much. I already prepared for this. I will leave as soon as there’s a risk that my presence will cause you harm.”
“I guess you still have your conscience?”
“More like I have common sense, unlike you.”
Ugh, again.

All three of us might end up in trouble. Actually, I had a feeling Erwen would still be okay even in the worst-case scenario. I may get targeted for execution by the palace and Amelia may get accused of being a spy for Noark, but Erwen wouldn’t. Even if worst came to worst, the elves would protect her.
“...So what are you going to do now?”
I took a moment to gather my thoughts before answering Amelia’s question. “I don’t know. We have no choice but to wait for now.”
There wasn’t much we could do locked up in this cage. Once Raven got back, the best we could do was assess the situation then and respond appropriately.
“Mister?”

I ended the conversation there and stood up. Then, still holding the water I received from the soldier earlier, I walked up to the corpse lying nearby whose face was covered with a cloth. I didn’t know what would happen in the future, but it would be better to do what I could right now.
“...What are you trying to do?” Amelia asked.
“Check for loot.”
“What? In a situation like this?”
What, is there anything else to do?
I shrugged and crouched down to start looting Lighthouse Keeper’s body.
Ten rings, one necklace, and I couldn’t grab the staff he dropped when I pulled him toward me, so...
The sub-space could be opened once I got out of this cage later since magic devices didn’t work within these bars.
Wow, how much is all this, anyway?

The more difficult the situation, the more important it was to learn to smile even at the little wins. Although it was impossible to estimate exactly how much income we’d earned, one thing was clear. If we sold all of these, it’d be roughly enough to pay off all our debt.
The problem was whether we would be able to safely take these out with us.

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Interrogation (2)
paragraphs: Raven climbed the stairs to the deck and hurried to the ship’s gunroom. By the time she arrived, the assistant to the deputy commander as well as the platoon leaders of the corps were all gathered.
“Deputy Commander Raven! You’re back! What a relief! We were actually forming a unit to back you up since you were taking so long to return—”
“I need to make a report. Please leave, everyone.”
“...Sorry? Ah, yes ma’am!” The leaders that were gathered followed Raven’s urgent command. The room emptied out in a matter of seconds.

Raven placed her hand on the military-use message stone located inside the cabin with a troubled look on her face. “Nia Rafdonia. This is Arua Raven, Deputy Commander of the Third Magic Corps. I have been delayed in securing a retreat route for the troops and have just returned. Please update me on the present situation.”
“Nia Rafdonia. This is Eltora Tercerion, Chief of Staff of the Third Corps. I was worried when I heard you had gone to stop Blood Knight, but I’m glad you’ve returned safely.”
“...Please excuse me, but how come the chief of staff is at the other end of this transmission instead of the commander?”
“Because in times of war, I am the second in command and take over in the absence of the highest commanding authority.”
“Absence... Sir?”
“Count Ramleonde was killed in battle. After he gave the order to gather all units, he was ambushed by a group of criminals led by the traitor Ricardo Lüchenprague while on the move.”
“That can’t be...”

“The ambush ended once all troops retreated to the lake, but as we cannot be certain what might happen next, I want you to command your unit to stay in the area and be on guard until further instructions are given.”
After that, they clearly and concisely shared information on the casualties and damage they knew about and the enemies that had carried out this attack.
“I think I’ve conveyed everything you need to know. Now it is your turn. Was it really Blood Knight?”

In response to her superior’s question, Raven summarized everything that had transpired in the form of a report: how she had stayed behind to stop Blood Knight, how the enemy’s reinforcements had joined the fight, how Lighthouse Keeper had been slain in battle, and that she had used Multi Teleportation to retreat. The events were concisely relayed in a few sentences, omitting all else. It wasn’t simply to save time, though. If it had been, she wouldn’t have had to finish her report so awkwardly.
“Lighthouse Keeper was slain, huh? This is good news. Well done. Be sure to inform Blood Spirit of the reward she’ll receive for her achievements in battle.”

Her superiors believed this achievement was thanks to the contributions of Blood Spirit, but the reality was entirely different. The reason no one had been harmed by the notorious Blood Knight was thanks to that man, Riehen Schuitz, and he had been the one to kill Lighthouse Keeper in the end as well.
“Then I will end the transmission here.”
Raven found herself unable to relay that, even as the conversation came to an end. No, that wasn’t all.
Amelia Rainwales.

She also had not mentioned the woman who had played as active a role as Blood Spirit in the battle, even though it was obvious to her that this was the same woman from Noark she had met on Farune Island. Raven intentionally withheld information. She may not have lied, but it was undeniable that she had forsaken her duties as a soldier.
Sigh...
As someone who always dutifully fulfilled her role, Raven felt a deep remorse. But what could she do? She needed time to get her thoughts in order first.
Riehen Schuitz...

Until now, she had assumed the man who introduced himself by that name was someone who Erwen was merely dragging around because of his resemblance to a certain someone. Once she saw Giantization, she hoped against hope. If he wasn’t just similar—if that was the reason why Erwen called him Mister—that meant that that certain someone was actually alive.
“...I don’t know.”

She was overwhelmed. It was hard to be sure of anything. Though it really seemed like him, she still wondered if he was just someone with a strong resemblance. There were many clear differences, too, like his height and face.
“Your... b-b-back...!”
When she touched his wound reflexively, his blood was just hot and sticky to the touch. If it was that man, his blood would have stung. Also, there was another difference.
...He’s too strong.

He had a body that could block Blood Knight’s aura, a unique skill that reflected magic, and on top of that, the ability to pull in enemies using wind. The Yandel she knew could not have displayed such power against such strong opponents.
But time has passed.
It was possible he had gotten stronger from taking new essences. Even Erwen, who was a member of the Seven Powerful, had changed a lot in the past two years.
In that case...

The more she organized the numerous pieces of information she’d been bombarded with in such a short period of time, the more Raven found herself leaning toward the thought that Bjorn Yandel was alive. The decisive factor was Amelia’s presence. Though she had been unable to uncover anything in the end, it was true that there had been uncertainty surrounding his death. If the person who went missing with him was alive and well, that as good as implied that he could be alive too.
If it really is Mr. Yandel, what do I do?

Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit. The palace had already officially announced that, and she knew that was the case even before the announcement. That was because she had seen Missha’s expression that day.
“You said there are going to be rumors that Mr. Yandel is an evil spirit... but it won’t just be a rumor, will it?”
Missha, who had the longest and deepest relationship with Yandel, did not answer her, but her wavering eyes held the truth.
Snap, snap.

Raven bit her nails for the first time in a long time. It was a habit that only came out when she felt cornered. In sharp contrast to her usual self, she could not look at this situation objectively at all. While she hoped that the man was Yandel, she also found herself hoping he wasn’t.
“Well, what can I do? I have to check.”
Soon, Raven made up her mind. She knew that no matter how scared she was, she could not put off and run away from something that needed doing.
No. 399: Cage of Silence was a trap-type Numbers Item that activated when a transportation-type ability was used within a certain radius of it.
“That woman... she’s not going to leave us in here forever, is she?”
“She’ll come. And probably soon.”
“How can you be so sure?”
“Because this cage won’t last forever.”
To be more precise, its effects lasted two hours upon activation, and the time it took to recharge was extremely long.
Besides, she can’t beat us up while we’re locked up.

This was Cage of Silence’s biggest weakness. It was an item solely for containment. Once this item was activated, all attacks from the outside were obstructed. Therefore, most people usually used it in conjunction with a siege formation, ganging up on the target once the cage disappeared.
Tap.
The moment footsteps echoed down the hallway, the soldier in charge of guarding us saluted in that direction. “Nia Rafdonia!”
So, you’re here.
“Thank you for watching over them. I have something to discuss with them. Could you give us the room? Ah, and please keep everything that happened here a secret.”
“Yes ma’am!”

Raven returned after about an hour, alone. She even sent away the soldier and got rid of any potential eavesdroppers. This was a good sign, but it was still too early to relax. Raven stood in front of the steel bars and quietly stared inside at us for a while. I was the first to break the silence.
“...What are you going to do with us?”
“Are you still going to use that tone with me?”
Coming out swinging, huh? Would it be better to just reveal my identity and ask her to help us?
While I was debating this, Raven continued. “Your helmet. Take it off.”
I’d already shown her my face once before anyway, so I obediently took off the helmet stained with Lighthouse Keeper’s blood.
Surprisingly, there was no change in Raven’s expression. “And the armor you’re wearing too.”
Who do you think I am? They say boys and girls shouldn’t even sit next to each other after the age of seven.
“I can’t give in to inappropriate sexual demands. If I were a woman, would you request such—”

“What are you talking about?” I tried to explain logically why I couldn’t take off my armor, but Raven just stared at me, utterly stone-faced. She was kind of scary like that. “I haven’t included anything about you yet in my reports. Or about Miss Rainwales next to you. But if you don’t do as I say, that will change.”
“I’ll take it off.”
“Your tone... it’s sharper now.”
It was not like I had a way out of this now. Instead of wasting my breath on replying, I took off my armor, which was wrecked in the back.
Then, for the first time, there was a shift in Raven’s expression. Something stirred behind her eyes as they locked on the tattoo hidden under my armor.
Whew, it’s actually a relief that it’s turned out like this.
“It’s been a while, Raven. What, didn’t you already suspect this?”
Raven bit her lip and glared at me. “Still... I hoped I was wrong.”
“Because I’m an evil spirit?”
“Yes. It would have been better to not ruin your memory...” Raven trailed off bitterly. My heart tightened.
So you can’t accept that I’m an evil spirit.
“Wait! Raven, that’s a misunderstanding.” I quickly launched into an attempt to sway her.
“Misunderstanding?”
“Yes, I’m not an evil spirit.”

“Then why are you in that state?” Glaring at me, Raven balled up her fists. “Looks like you shrank your height with an essence like Miss Ainar’s Bone Knight... If you’re not an evil spirit, why would you have to hide your identity?”
Yeah, I knew you would ask that.
“By the time I returned, the palace had already made that announcement. When I looked into it, it seemed fishy. That’s why I’m hiding my identity for the time being.”
“...I admit there were many suspicious things about that announcement. But ‘time being’? And ‘returned’? What does that mean?”
Okay, I think I’ve succeeded in arousing her curiosity.
“It’s a long story. There’s something called a Fragment of Records Stone—”

“Wait!” Just as I was about to explain what happened to me, Raven jumped in and interrupted me. “You don’t need to explain in detail. This will be enough.” With that, a familiar object appeared in Raven’s hand. It was No. 7234: Misplaced Trust, an item that prohibited all lies within a radius of ten yards when activated. “You should know what this is, Mr. Yandel. It’s an item I received from Mr. Parteian in Doppelganger Forest long ago. A while ago, the military had some leftover budget, so I made sure to recharge it with a few uses.”
Oh my, how prepared.
Whooom!
She clicked the power button and the compass-sized disc began to move. Then Raven stared daggers at me as she asked, “Okay, tell me now. Is it really a misunderstanding?”
...It should work, right?

Even as I thought this to myself, I was quite nervous. I hadn’t actually checked whether Auril Gavis’s present was working properly or not. My plan had actually been to purchase Misplaced Trust or a similar item to confirm this before taking the stand to defend myself to the palace.
“Raven, it really is a misunderstanding. I’m not an evil spirit.”
Well, since I can talk, I guess the present really is working...
Click.
Just then, the watch hand that had been smoothly circling the disk stopped.
“...What did you just do?”

“Uh...” When I trailed off, the hand started moving again. Was it a momentary malfunction? “I’m not sure...” I quickly doubled down on the “I don’t know” method, and the hand on Misplaced Trust once again stopped with a click.
Tick, tick.
A moment later, it resumed.
“...Why is Misplaced Trust stopping every time you speak, Mr. Yandel?”
I gulped at that.
He said I wouldn’t be affected by these things in the future... That damned old man. You should have told me it was going to be like this!

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Interrogation (3)
paragraphs: In some ways, this was like a cliché plotline in a mystery novel. All circumstantial evidence was pointing to a culprit, but a critical piece of physical evidence was missing. That was exactly the position I was in right now.
What kind of gift is this?!

Maybe if this were before the notion that I was an evil spirit had already been established, this would be useful. But to prove my innocence in this situation, I needed adequate concrete evidence. I’d only look more suspicious otherwise—just like right now.

“Repeat after me. I am a woman.” This was the request Raven made of me after Misplaced Trust’s strange malfunction. Her objective was clear. She wanted to figure out why Misplaced Trust was stopping when I spoke, and though she had no way of figuring out the truth, she was going to run different experiments until she got close to it.
There was only one thing I could do right now. “I—! Ugh, my voice...! I don’t think I can say it because it’s a lie—”
“Stop screwing around!”
Uh... that was a genuine attempt. As expected, that strategy won’t work.
“Whatever, just say anything.”
“...I’m really not an evil spirit. Believe me, Raven.”
When I repeated the same words, the hand once again stopped. The only difference was Raven didn’t miss that brief opening and quickly said, “I am a man. What the... I was able to say it?”
So, the anti-lie effect stops working on everyone else when it freezes up too. Just learned something new. Damn it.
Tick, tick.
But despite the fact that it kept stopping, it started working normally again a moment later, the needle on the disc continuing to move.
“I am a m— Hmm, now it’s not working anymore. Mr. Yandel, you did something, didn’t you?”
Wait, why are you automatically blaming me? Well, I am the one causing it, but...
I had to deny this thoroughly. “Th-that’s unfair! Why are you accusing me when you bought a defective product?”
“Defective product? How can it be normal that this happens every time you open your mouth?” That was definitely strange. If I were Raven, I would have used the same reasoning.

But I couldn’t just admit that, could I? I raised my voice. “I didn’t do anything! It’s true! Believe me!” The fact that it was now impossible to distinguish truth from lies with Misplaced Trust meant the chances of the person with the loudest voice winning the argument had gone up.
“...Please shut up. You’re too loud.”
Jeez, why are you getting all stone-faced? So scary.
When I clammed up reflexively, Raven also paused for a moment, lost in thought. “...Tell me.”
“Huh?”
“What you were about to say earlier. Tell me that.”
“Ah...” In a way, this was like ancient times when there was no magic or science, a time when just talking to someone was enough to trust them. Whew, what a wonderful world that was.
“What do you mean you ‘returned’? What on earth were you doing before then?”
“I’ll tell you everything.”
With that, I ran through what happened after Amelia and I were left alone on Farune Island in chronological order. In the end, the two of us defeated the Storm Gush, and an essence appeared.
“Then you pulled in Lighthouse Keeper earlier with...”
“Yes, I used it in conjunction with Bayon’s Transcendence.”
“I guess everything up to that point is true. Go on.”
Before I got into the next part, I told her about the treasure Amelia and her team had been after, the Fragment of Records Stone that had once been in the possession of the lord of Noark’s castle.

Raven was convinced surprisingly easily. “I’ve heard of that item before. But I had no idea that was the treasure that man Drous ran away with. Anyway, legend says you can use it to change the past, right?”
“It wasn’t a legend but a fact. Well, it was impossible to change history, though. You’ll understand in a second.”
I told her about how the Fragment of Records Stone activated and how I woke up twenty years in the past.
“...That’s impossible, but if something like that really did happen, I guess that explains how only your equipment was left behind on the island.”
The more the conversation progressed, the more doubts Raven started to have. But she didn’t interrupt me, probably planning to judge the veracity for herself once my explanation was over.
“Nivelles... Enze?” When I got to the part about how I borrowed my identity from IDs we got off a plunderer on the island, Raven tilted her head in confusion.
Oh, does she remember what happened back then?
I started to hope, but reality remained ruthless.
“...That sounds familiar, somehow.”
Well, she was like five years old back then. How could she even remember my name? Anyway, after that...
It was Dwalkie’s turn to make an appearance. I told her about how I tried to change his destiny but soon realized that no matter what I did, history would always flow in the same direction.
“Everything I did had already happened in the original timeline.”
“The study of time has been around since ancient times. This is the single-dimensional timeline theory... Don’t worry about it, please keep going.”
“Sure.”
Then I told her how I went down to Noark and explained in detail the efforts I made there for six months to save Amelia’s sister. Of course, I left out everything that had to do with evil spirits.
“When I got back, it was only a month ago, and I was in Noark. At that time, I ran into Amelia and Erwen, and Erwen believed me.”
“And the reason why you didn’t announce your survival right away was because the announcement made by the palace was suspicious...right?”
“That’s right. I don’t know if you’ll believe that, though.” I’d said everything I needed to say now. So what conclusion would Raven come to?
I was filled with half anticipation and half worry as I waited for Raven to speak. When she did, her voice was hard. “What a ridiculous story. The kind children would like.”
I expected this reaction to some extent. After all, she was a wizard, not an ordinary person. The more intelligence someone had, the more absurd my story would have sounded to them.
“Do you have proof that your words are true?”
I knew you would ask that so I prepared something. Do you know why I didn’t tell you about our meeting? Normally, these things hit better when they’re brought up at dramatic moments.
“Proof... of course I do. You said the name Nivelles Enze sounds familiar to you, right?”
“Yes, and?”
“Of course it’s familiar. Because you and I already met twenty years ago.”

At Raven’s confusion, I explained those events in detail: our first meeting in the library, how I saved her from getting in trouble as she went around electrocuting anyone and everyone, and how we met almost every day after that to chat.
“That person... was you...?” Before long, Raven’s eyes filled with astonishment.
“I guess you finally remembered who Nivelles Enze is.”
She may not have remembered the name, but she remembered who I was. That was a very fortunate thing. Raven was silent for a while, staring at me with a mix of wonder and bafflement.
“No way... How could that happen...?”
“I know how you feel. But it really did happen. You remember the conversations we had, right?”
“Faintly. I just remember someone like that existing... I was really busy after I entered the Magic Tower. And then that happened not long after...”
“That?”
Raven flinched, her voice growing cold. “You don’t need to know that, Mr. Yandel.”
Haha, and I was so nice to you when you were little. How did she grow up like this? Ah, I guess she was actually even feistier back then. At least now she speaks more politely...
“Anyway, are you considering believing me now?”
Raven didn’t answer my question and kept her mouth shut.
Tick, tick.

As the silence dragged on, the spinning hand on Misplaced Trust sounded particularly loud. There were less than two minutes left on it now. It may have stopped every time I spoke, but it wasn’t like I talked without stopping at all.
Tick, tick.
Time marched on.

“It doesn’t matter what I want to believe. Amelia Rainwales, you answer. Are all of those stories true?” Only remembering then that she could validate my unbelievable tale through someone else, Raven’s attention shifted to Amelia next.
Tick, tick.

Even though Misplaced Trust was operating normally, Amelia had no issues answering. “Everything Yandel said is true.” Yeah, I may have omitted a few details, but the experiences themselves were facts. “Yandel and I traveled twenty years to the past and went through a lot. Those were all things that actually happened.”
That was the final blow. Even if it was a hard story to believe, there was no way she couldn’t believe it at this point.
Okay, I think I’ve finished persuading her...
With that thought in mind, I lowered my guard a little.
“But...” Raven said, squeezing the words out. “That... doesn’t prove Mr. Yandel isn’t an evil spirit.”
“...Huh?” I just couldn’t understand it. Why? Wasn’t my story believable enough? Why was she still digging into this so persistently?
Could it be... she has another reason to suspect me as an evil spirit other than the announcement from the palace?
That possibility made my mouth dry up.
“Amelia Rainwales, I will ask you one last question.”
“...Speak.” Amelia nodded.

Raven hesitated for a moment, but when she finally asked her question, she left no room for ambiguity. “If you are uncertain in the slightest or you don’t know for sure, please tell me so. Is Bjorn Yandel an evil spirit?”
God damn it.

Amelia didn’t answer Raven’s question. No, she couldn’t answer, to be more exact. How could she? You couldn’t even utter a lie in front of that Numbers Item. The only thing you could do was sit there in silence.
So, a heavy silence fell. The only sound was the click of Misplaced Trust’s needle moving around the disc.
Tick, tick, tick.
However, that didn’t last long.
Tick.

Once the needle completed a single revolution and stopped, the light from the disc also faded. Misplaced Trust was deactivated. However, the tension in the air persisted. That happened sometimes, in situations where a beat of silence provided a clearer answer than ten thousand words.
“I guess there’s no point in answering now,” Amelia said quietly a moment later.
Raven’s mouth showed no signs of opening. She also didn’t reactivate Misplaced Trust to repeat the same question. I didn’t ask, but it probably wasn’t because she was out of uses.
“Raven...”
“Please, don’t say anything. At least... not now...”
Raven stared at me from her spot in front of the bars for a long while. It seemed she was quietly sorting through her thoughts. But perhaps that process didn’t go as smoothly as she hoped?

Raven started muttering to herself. “I am the deputy commander of the Third Magic Corps and I take pride and responsibility in my role. I have no intention of abandoning the duties of my position, either. Which is why I have to report this. Because if I don’t, that won’t just be treason against our country, but also a betrayal and deception of those who have placed their trust in me.”
It was not hard to figure out who those words echoing through the dark room were meant to convince. It wasn’t me, Amelia, or Erwen.
It was herself.
“I mustn’t do that. No, I can’t do that...” Raven mumbled, clenching her small fists as she tried to detangle her jumbled thoughts. Then she turned around and headed toward the stairs.
Trudge, trudge.
She looked like she was walking a tightrope.

“Yandel, if you let her leave like that, you’ll be in big trouble,” Amelia advised me from over my shoulder, but I couldn’t really hear her. Of course, I knew that logically. If Raven left now, next time, she’d bring men.
Grit.
What could I say to stop her? My comrade, who had tried to believe in me, eventually figured out the truth and decided to walk away from me.
Thump.

My heart tightened. At the same time, I had this thought: if I weren’t an evil spirit, if I had been born in Bjorn Yandel’s body, met these people, and became their teammate, how would things have been?
Ridiculous. If that were the case, we would never have become teammates.
I tried to shake off the pointless fantasy, as well as the guilt I felt about Raven. This was not the time to think about that.
I guess I have no choice but to go to Plan B.

Now that the situation had taken a turn for the worst, I had to focus on getting out alive, regardless of my current predicament. After all, it wasn’t just my life at stake. I had to take responsibility for Amelia and Erwen too.

When the troops arrived and the steel bars opened, I’d have to use Giantization to keep them out of the room and stall for time. Instead of going out onto the deck, I would need to smash open the floor to escape down into the lake. The issue of breathing could be taken care of using a water spirit... and from there...
While I was putting together Plan B, Raven stopped walking and slowly turned toward me again.
Tap.

“Earlier... why did you save me?” She looked right into my eyes as she asked, as if this was the one thing she was still stuck on. “If you didn’t use Giantization, your identity wouldn’t have been exposed. Why... did you still save me? Even... getting hurt like that. There must have been a reason.”
So, that’s what you were wondering.

I could understand why she was asking, but that only deepened my sadness. Raven would have never asked something like this in the past. The reason she was asking now must have been because I was an evil spirit. All of my sincerity up to this point was in question, and the time we spent together had been negated.
I guess this is what Baekho must have felt like.

The emotions he must have felt once upon a time saturated my entire body to the bones. The walls around my heart sealed shut as if they had never been opened. I doubted that anything I said here would mean anything.
Nevertheless, I spoke. “Yes, I had a reason.”
“...I see. As I thought, there was something else driving you.”

I may have looked to her like a monster who had stolen someone else’s body, and all of this may have seemed like a lie. But, while I knew it wasn’t my place to say something like this, if there had been something driving my actions, it was one single thing.
“Raven, it was because you were in danger. That’s why I saved you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Interrogation (4)
paragraphs: Arua Raven turned back around. Even after she took her eyes off of him, she could still feel the man’s lonely, pitiful gaze on her shoulders. It felt like a blade was digging into her chest.
Why is he looking at me like that? I’m the one who was betrayed...
Evil spirits deceived the entire world. That was what she had been taught from a young age, and what she’d heard from countless stories growing up.
You saved me because I was in danger? That’s not possible...

Raven shook her head, but it took more effort than it should have. Ignoring the way her heart protested, she tried to drill this into her skull: he was simply saying what she wanted to hear. He had to have some sort of angle. She couldn’t be fooled by this. With that in mind, she began to take heavy steps forward.
Trudge.
With each step she took, however, memories of going on expeditions with him flashed through her mind. It started with their first meeting in the Bloody Citadel.
“What the hell is that?! Why is there a Vampire here?”
“You better run instead of whining, dwarf.”
A Vampire had appeared as the guardian of the first floor’s Rift. The man naturally took charge of their group and threw himself into battle before ultimately achieving victory.
The holy water he used toward the end... he only knew about that because he’s an evil spirit.
