Ultimately, that was how it was. Behind every precious memory, she found moments where she was deceived and fooled. How stupid and easy she must have seemed.
Trudge.
Of course, when all was said and done, she had ended up owing her life to that man in the Bloody Citadel. However, Raven assessed the situation rationally.
That doesn’t mean he sacrificed himself to save us.
If he hadn’t done what he did, he would have died too. That was why that man had risked his life in that fight.
Trudge.

The next scene that came to mind was the time they were trapped in the first floor’s Crystal Cave. The knights and large clans had discarded them like a bad hand and escaped through a portal, leaving them in dire straits. That was the same day that man became known as a hero in the city.
“Then what do you want me to do?!”
“I repeat! Everyone stop!”
The man had been resolute almost to a fault, and in response, adventurers who had been pointing swords at each other joined forces. Then progress began.
“Fuck, this is driving me up the wall.”
“I-I can’t go any farther. I’m sorry.”
While warriors who must have crossed the boundary between life and death countless times before faltered and lost their courage, that man continued forward.
“Behel-ahhh!”
That man took on the most dangerous role and fought more desperately than anyone else. However, Raven made a call.
That... was also to save himself... That’s all there is to it...
She took a step.
Trudge.

Each step took her farther away from the steel bars. The things that she had experienced with the man inside, big and small, and all the help she had received from him flashed through her mind. And each time they did, Raven thought to herself:
That wasn’t even that difficult... He didn’t risk his life that time... I gave him at least as much help in return.
Most were things she could gloss over with thoughts like that, but...
“Did you...come all this way for me? Through that fire?”
“I was on a walk.”
What happened on the day the royal capital was set on fire...
“W-What are you doing? You’re not thinking of lifting this whole boat...?”
“Ahhhhhh!”
How he sent everyone away from Farune Island and stayed behind to fight the enemy.
“Your... b-b-back...!”
Even the way he blocked the spell flying toward her with his body...
That... was for his own good...?
Raven soon found that no matter how hard she tried to deny it, it was increasingly difficult to do so.
There’s... no way...

Although she had been in life-threatening danger at the time, she could still clearly remember it. That man, even as he writhed in pain so intense that the veins on his neck were sticking out, had endured it all while hugging her carefully so as not to crush her. There was no point in lying to herself any longer.
“Raven, it was because you were in danger. That’s why I saved you.”
Though she tried to refute it several times, he had been speaking the undeniable truth.
Creak.
The door on the other end of the hallway beyond the steel bars closed.
“She’s gone.”
Eventually, Raven left. I now had to abandon the hope that she would come back and open this cage.
“Evil spirit.”
Huh?
When I glanced to the side, I found Erwen. Her head was lowered and all I could see were her eyes, which were locked on mine. “...You were an evil spirit?”
Yeah, I was wondering why you were quiet.
Like I thought, she was shocked by this news. And it made sense that she’d be angry. She probably assumed I didn’t tell her because I couldn’t trust her.
“Erwen, calm down. I’ll explain—”
“This woman knew already. So I was the only one who didn’t know.”
“About that, I—”
“I told you I didn’t care. I told you...! But why did you deceive me? Because you couldn’t trust me? What will it take for you to trust me?”
I think this is the first time I’ve ever seen her this mad...
I glanced at Amelia for help, but she just shrugged and avoided my eyes.
Are you trying to say this is karma and that I have to deal with it myself? But on the bright side... she really doesn’t seem to care that I’m an evil spirit.

Was it because she just saw Raven leave with her own eyes, unable to accept the fact that I was an evil spirit? While on the one hand, I was left lightheaded by all the murderous intent Erwen was radiating, on the other I was relieved and grateful.
Well, this and that are two separate things, though. How can I calm her down?
I didn’t have to think for long.
“And Raven, what about her?! You h-hid it so thoroughly from me, but just because that woman was in d-danger—! Protecting her at the cost of your identity is—!”
Tap.

Before Erwen could seethe even harder, I snatched her wrist out of the air. “Erwen, I would have done the same if you were the one in danger.” Every word I spoke was sincere. I definitely would have done the same for Erwen.
But was that hard for her to believe? “L-Liar... Y-You didn’t even tell me in advance... Y-You think she’s more trustworthy than me.”
“What...? Why on earth would you think that?”
“Because... I-I’m like this... Because I only took those kinds of essences... I’m treated like an unstable bitch...”
Huh. I didn’t know you were thinking thoughts like that about yourself.
It looked like Erwen had secretly been feeling a lot of shame about her condition. “Erwen, that’s not true.”
“Then... why did you only hide it from me...?”
Jeez, that’s why I told you I would explain.
I sighed inwardly.
“Because he wanted to protect you.” For some reason, the answer came out of Amelia’s mouth, not mine. “That’s reasonable, isn’t it?”
What was this girl talking about? I ignored her and studied Erwen, who paused as she took that in.
“...Uh, huh?” Her shoulders jerked and began to shake after a beat. “M-M-Me?”
Okay, it sounds like she’s calmed down a bit...
Just in case she had misunderstood something, I quickly jumped into explain. “You saw it too. Raven interrogated Amelia.”

Even if I had Auril Gavis’s gift, I couldn’t prevent truth magic from being used against other people. That was why I wanted to keep the number of people in on my secret as small as possible. Of course, this decision was also to my advantage, but it wasn’t made solely for my own benefit.

“I wanted to give you an out if there ever came a time when you got into trouble because I’m an evil spirit. If you didn’t know, you would just be seen as a victim. But if you knew and still helped me, you would be treated as an accomplice.”
“Th-then it’s because you care about me more than Rainwales...? S-Since you kept it from me on purpose. To... protect me...”
“Uh...” My eyes naturally shifted to Amelia. She chuckled in a way that seemed to ask what I was stressing about, then nodded.
I think she’s telling me not to worry about her and to take care of this first... Whew, she’s so trustworthy.
“Yes, that’s why I kept it from you.”
“I-I knew it!” When I agreed with her, Erwen was overjoyed and balled up her fists. Then she looked toward Amelia, her shoulders straight and the corners of her mouth curled up.
“...This is a bit annoying,” said Amelia, frowning.

Erwen didn’t pay her any mind and turned her attention back to me. “Mister, I’m grateful but... don’t do that again. There’s no way I would want to leave you to fend for yourself.” Erwen glared beyond the bars in the direction Raven left. “I’m different from that woman, who knows no shame even after you saved her life multiple times.”
Uh, are you...?
“So, just trust me! Okay?”
Once that was just about sorted, Amelia stepped in and changed the subject. “Anyway, what are you going to do now?”
Oh, that... I should start getting ready.
“Let’s pack our stuff first.”
“Stuff?”
“We can’t leave the equipment behind.”

I crouched over the items I looted from Lighthouse Keeper. Gathering the equipment on his stretched-out robe, I wrapped it up like a bundle, then tied it around my neck tightly—Barbarian Peddler Mode. I’d carry it around like this for now and then put it in sub-space when I had the chance.
“If you’ve got everything, tell me now: what are you going to do? I’m sure you have something planned.” Since Amelia was asking again, I shared the Plan B I had been cooking up in my head.
Then, I waited patiently until the time came. A long while later, the doorknob at the end of the hall started turning, before slowly opening with a creak.
Rattle. Tap.
Raven once again appeared—without anyone accompanying her.
“She’s alone,” said Amelia.
“What is she planning? She must have reported it to her superiors by now.”
Amelia and Erwen stared out of the cage, clutching their weapons as if on guard. At that, Raven flinched and stopped.
“Why are you alone?”
“To check something,” Raven responded quietly.
The exchange was held from a distance of twenty-three feet. Perhaps it was because of the way our voices echoed in the hallway, but every inch between us felt wider than ever.
“Check what?”
Raven did not answer me. She just kept walking and closed the distance.
Step, step.

The closer Raven got to the bars, the more I could see her expression without darkness obstructing it. She was wearing a complicated look, one that could not be summed up in just one emotion. But one thing was obvious just at a glance.
“...You didn’t report me?” I asked, and Raven once again answered with silence.
Step, step.

Her feet continued without pause, and it didn’t take long until the only thing between us was the steel bars. Raven stared at me through them with her clear blue eyes, and I looked back at her without a word. I wasn’t sure how much time passed before—
Clunk.
Raven wordlessly took the keys out of her pocket. What kind of change of heart had she had? Earlier, the walls around her heart had been so high up that nothing I said was working.
Could this be... an attempt to trick us?

That was plausible. Our combat power would have been included in her report. Since it would be troublesome to turn us into enemies while on the boat, she may have been pretending to help us for now only to arrest us later in the city.
“Why are you doing this all of a sudden?” I asked bluntly. “Like you said earlier, what you’re about to do now will betray everyone who placed their trust in you.”
As I spoke, I focused on Raven’s eyes. I was convinced her poor acting skills would tell me whether she was telling the truth or not, but Raven only chuckled.
“Why are you laughing...?” It didn’t sound like mockery. Rather, the laugh felt more self-deprecating, more tinged with sadness. But why would that be?
“It’s just, this reminds me of earlier.”
Huh?
“If I didn’t know you were an evil spirit, you wouldn’t have even asked that.”
“Ah...” For a moment, I was rendered speechless. It seemed Raven had made her decision before she even came down here because there was no hesitation in her movements.
Slide.

The key slid into the lock and turned. The steel bars between Raven and I shined in the torchlight and reflected our images like mirrors. For some reason, I felt flustered. To be honest, I had thought I was done for, which was why I thought up Plan B.

“...My answer is the same as yours. If you stay here, you’ll be in danger, Mr. Yandel. I’ve decided to help you for now, not caring about what happens afterward. So...” The key finished turning with a click. “Come out quickly. I need to hear what you plan to do next too.”
The tightly closed door had opened.

chapters.title: Chapter 363: Responsibility (1)
paragraphs: Once we exited the cage, we moved to the gunroom located at the center of the ship because the talk we were about to have had to remain secret.
“You can speak freely here. This place is designed for private conversations.”
Oh, in that case.
“I want to hear about the current state of affairs. What happened with the ambush?”
This was what I had been most curious about while locked in the cage, so I decided to get caught up on the information I had been thoroughly cut off from. How did Orcules’s ambush go?
“Count Ramleonde was killed in action. He was attacked by the Traitor, Ricardo Lüchenprague, during his retreat.”

My heart dropped when I heard that the commander of our corps had been assassinated, but upon closer inspection, it seemed the war situation wasn’t as dire as I thought. Apparently, as soon as the dozens of boats on the lake were essentially turned into fortresses, the attacks stopped. They’d been in a standstill for going on two hours now.
“Command assumes that the goal of this ambush was to take advantage of the confusion and assassinate key figures.”
Assassinate key figures, huh?
“That’s highly plausible.” After all, that was what Blood Knight had said as soon as he saw us.
“The Golden Wizard, Arua Raven. One of the targets to be killed.”
Raven must have been one of the key figures on the hitlist. I could roughly piece together their strategy for this attack in my head with no issue.
Have Corpse Collector spread his undead over a wide area and use that to locate the assassination targets.
The number of undead grew drastically over the course of the battle with Blood Knight, and before long, a three-person team arrived to provide reinforcements.
“Anyway, the situation isn’t that dire right now, so let’s talk about you first. What is your plan from here on out, Mr. Yandel?”
Hmm, a plan, huh? I have to start thinking about that now... I never expected the old man’s gift to work that way, either. Thanks to that, my head is—
“Um, and...” Just then, Raven spoke up again, trailing off. “I’m going to warn you in advance. I may have helped you this time because I had no choice, but I can’t keep it up.”
Huh? We’re not back to being comrades...?
When I shot her a look of betrayal, Raven avoided my eyes. “It’s no use looking at me like that. I think I’ve taken on enough risk just by not reporting this incident. I’ve done my part.”

That was disappointing, but nothing I couldn’t understand. She may not have reported it because she couldn’t bring herself to let me die like this, but I was sure she wasn’t prepared to throw herself into the pit with me. That was what it meant to help evil spirits in this world. The moment you were caught, execution was guaranteed.

“Raven, I don’t blame you, so don’t make that face. I’m grateful that you helped me out this time. If something goes wrong in the future, I’ll do my best to make sure you don’t get dragged into it.” I laughed like a barbarian and patted Raven on the shoulder.
Smack! Smack! Smack!

What was up with this? Normally she would have yelped in pain and glared at me, but Raven didn’t do that this time. She simply pursed her lips and looked down at the ground. “Mr. Yandel... how can you be like that even in a situation like this?”
Ugh, that’s what’s bothering you? You’re needlessly emotional. I told you, I get where you’re coming from.

“The fact that you tried to help me despite knowing the truth... that’s already enough for me.” I didn’t blame her—on the contrary, I felt apologetic. After all, this kid who was doing well for herself and had a stable life ahead of her was risking everything because of me.

An awkward silence ensued after that. Once Raven came back to her senses to some extent, she returned to the original topic of conversation with a bashful look. “Anyway... so what are you going to do now?”

“Well, I think you shouldn’t hear it. If you hear my plan and get more involved with me, it’ll be hard for you to distance yourself from our actions later. You said this will be the last time you help me anyway, right?”
Raven flinched when I tried to establish boundaries, but I guessed she had an opinion on that. “Mr. Yandel, you said you’ll do your best to keep me out of it, but you never know what will happen.”
“That’s true.”
“For now, you not getting caught is our best bet. And to do that...”
“To do that...?”
“I’m willing to help. To some extent.”
I knew she was going to pull through in the end. When I grinned, Raven glanced up at me, looking somewhat annoyed.
“Whatever, so just tell me what you plan to do now. I’m sure you had a plan, which is why you came out onto the battlefield with your identity hidden. You would have known you would stand out.”
I answered after some thought—honestly, like the barbarian I was. “I have none. For now.”
“...Excuse me?”
Even if you look at me like that, the plan still doesn’t exist.
I truly never imagined Auril’s gift would turn out like that. I came to the labyrinth because I needed money, but I hadn’t been planning on doing anything that could attract attention.
I guessed she hadn’t expected that answer at all. “...By none, you mean... So you have no plan at all?”
Raven confirmed this with a stammer and I reaffirmed it like a man. “Yes.”
“Really? If people find out I helped you, I could be dishonorably discharged from the military and even kicked out of the Magic Tower.”
Wow, you could end up getting kicked out of the Magic Tower too? Did she really risk all of that for me?
Once again grateful for Raven’s decision to help, I changed the subject. “Anyway, I’m hungry after being locked up for so long. Can I take out some beef jerky—”
“Don’t change the subject!”
“I-I’m not, I’m just really hungry—”
“What are you saying?! You’re not even a real barbarian!”
Huh, come to think of it, that approach wouldn’t work on her anymore. The thought was kind of bittersweet.
Sigh...
A sigh echoed through the quiet room. As an uncomfortable tension settled between us, I sneakily pulled out some beef jerky and gnawed on it.
“What... are you eating right now?”
I wasn’t lying about being hungry. My body was a barbarian’s, after all. It needed to be supplied with nutrients at all times.
“...Do you want some?”
“No... Ha, how could I have realized you were an evil spirit when you’re like this all the time?” Raven sighed again, but I decided to take that as a compliment on how thorough I was.
Chew, chew.
Whew, I feel more energized now that I’ve eaten something.
“Raven, did you know already?”
“Know what?”
“It seemed like you had another reason to suspect me other than the royal announcement.”

“Oh, that...” Raven’s expression instantly darkened, but it seemed she decided that whatever was making her react like that wasn’t something she had to hide. “The magic device that contained the conversation between Hans Chrisen and the dwarf from Noark.”
Ah, so that recorder ended up with her. But what about it?

When I shot her a questioning look, Raven slowly continued with her explanation. “Maybe it was because it used a cheap core, but that recorder had a maximum number of times you could listen to the recordings on it.”
“So?”
“The limit was one hundred, but there were only two plays remaining. I started to wonder why you would have listened to that over and over again.”
“...I see.” To think that ended up being a clue. I never would have imagined.
“To be honest... there was something much more decisive than that, though. Miss Missha came to see me at the lab about fifty days after you died, Mr. Yandel.”
“...What did she say?”
“She said that there were going to be rumors circulating that you are an evil spirit.”
Was it because the topic of conversation was Missha? I felt my heart go cold. “And?”
“Because of the thing with the recorder, I got the feeling something was off. I asked her if that wouldn’t just be a rumor.”
At the time, Missha had avoided answering, but ironically, that served as a clearer answer than anything.
Erwen jumped in. “Was—so it was that bea—no, that woman who started the rumor?”
Raven looked slightly uncomfortable and lowered her head. “Probably. Although I don’t know what her circumstances were.”
Erwen gritted her teeth when Raven confirmed her suspicions. “What circumstances? That woman... I knew she would do something like this one day...”
“Calm down, Erwen. No one knows what happened to Missha yet.”
“But...! No matter what her circumstances were, I would have never done something like that to you! Aren’t you angry, Mister? You were betrayed!”
“I’m telling you we don’t know that yet.”
To be honest, I was more worried than angry. After all, there was the matter of that intel I had gotten at the Round Table. Missha was with Baekho.
“Baekho Lee has the Stone of Revival.”
She might have made some kind of deal with him to revive me. Well, that was just a working theory on my part. Whether or not that was true, her decision was ultimately detrimental to me.
Jeez, what is that girl doing right now?
“Honestly! Mister, you... why are you so ridiculously kind?!”
What was she saying? “Anyway, Raven... then you don’t know why the palace acknowledged the rumor and made it public, either?”
“No. But... I did hear something from Commander Pevrosk.”
“Hear something?”

“As soon as the announcement was made, he came to me and said that no one can know the truth about a man who’s already dead. Of course, I thought he was just saying that to comfort me, but... Now that I’m looking back on it, there seemed to be a strange hidden meaning behind his words, almost as if the commander knew the truth? You might find something there.”
“Can you look into it when you get back to the city?”
“Sure, I can do that much...” Despite my concerns, Raven nodded. Fortunately, it seemed this kind of favor was included in “to some extent.”
After that, we all conversed and made plans for the future, and we soon came to a conclusion.

“Then it would be best to hide your identity for the time being.” Now that we knew how verification through Misplaced Trust worked, we decided it was necessary to be more careful about revealing my identity. “But... why did it only malfunction for you, Mr. Yandel?”
I glossed over the gift I got from Auril Gavis. “I don’t know. Maybe it’s because of the Fragment of Records Stone.”

This was yet another lie, but it couldn’t be helped. I was the only one immune to Misplaced Trust. This may not have mattered considering she already knew I was an evil spirit and was fine with it, but who knew what would happen in the future? That was also the reason why I hadn’t told Amelia yet.
Plus, if I tell Raven about this, I’d have to mention Auril Gavis.
Auril Gavis was an enemy of the palace. If it became known that I had received a gift from him on top of being an evil spirit, I’d be in an even tighter spot. There’d be no room to even negotiate.
“Still... I’m glad. If this isn’t a one-time phenomenon, this means you’re a little safer now.”
“Yeah, I think so too.”
“But... Mister, do you really have to reclaim your identity? I like the way you look even now...” Erwen offered her two cents, but my ultimate goal of clearing the rumor didn’t change.
“If I don’t, I’ll never be able to receive another Spirit Imprint.”
Do you know why I cultivated a barbarian? If I want to create more synergy with the essences I’ve consumed so far, the Spirit Imprint is essential.
But I guessed Erwen couldn’t empathize with that logic. “But... you can live without that.” She sounded kind of sad. “Mister... why are you so hellbent on getting stronger...?”
At that question, everyone turned to me.
“Come to think of it, Mr. Yandel, you were like that in the past too... Only interested in climbing the labyrinth’s floors.” Raven’s eyes held some unease.

“I’ve heard rumors before that evil spirits might be able to return to their original world after reaching the end of the labyrinth.” Amelia calmly summed up my predicament, but I wasn’t particularly grateful to her for doing so.
Don’t say it like that. That’s bound to create a misunderstanding.
“No way, Mister, is that why...?”
“I guess Mr. Yandel has a reason to go to those lengths to get back, then. Well, it’s his home, after all...”
“Mister... can’t you just live here...? I-I’ll do better... and I won’t make any trouble...”
Ugh, what were they saying? “Erwen, calm down. I think there’s been a misunderstanding.”

Return? Returning hadn’t been my primary goal in the past, and it wasn’t right now, either. My number one goal had always been survival. But after meeting people, exploring, and experiencing so many things, said number one goal had changed a bit. It was still to survive, but not just on my own. With everyone together.
“Why am I so hellbent on getting stronger...?” I continued without any hesitation. “So that I can protect you guys.”
I’m no longer protecting just myself with this shield.

chapters.title: Chapter 364: Responsibility (2)
paragraphs: When I thought about it, it wasn’t such a bad idea to keep living with the name Riehen Schuitz. With my current specs, even if I hid some of my powers, I could earn enough money to retire with just a few more years of work. Of course, I’d have to give up on returning in that case...
But so what?

I’d already adapted. This world was no longer as terrible to me as it used to be, and in recent days, I’d even started to think it was better than my old life. Here, I had people I could trust and people who believed in me—connections I never had while living as Hansu Lee.
But... There’s no guarantee that I can hide my identity forever.

I wondered how long I could live as Riehen Schuitz. No matter how careful I was, it wouldn’t be forever. Not only was life unpredictable, but there were already too many witnesses. In the end, word of Riehen Schuitz would spread. Even if Raven made a false report, Clown had been there. He’d probably yap about it at the Round Table, about the interesting guy he met. And since Deer was also part of the Round Table, news would inevitably reach the palace.
Besides, I showed him the Gachabone essence.

Although it was a lesser-known essence, after some research he’d be able to identify this essence and find out about the increase in Bone Density it gave users. At that point, he’d realize I was originally much taller. Well, the most decisive factor was something else.
Auril Gavis.

I still didn’t know what that old man did to me as he handed me this superficial gift. Put simply, even if I hid my identity and lived in the shadows, I couldn’t guarantee my safety that way. So the conclusion I came to was the same one as always. Just as the shaman told me when he predicted my chaotic fate, I had to get stronger so that I could handle whatever came my way.
Whooom!
While we were busy discussing the future in the office, the crystal ball on the table began to vibrate.
“It’s a military-use message stone directly connected to the command center. I guess we’ll have to finish this conversation another time.”
Well, Raven couldn’t dedicate all her time to us during a war. Honestly, I had also been starting to wonder if it was okay for us to be sitting around talking like this.
“We’ll be outside.”
“No. There’s no need. You are my escorts, after all. Please just stay quiet while I’m on the line.”
“If you say so.”
Raven picked up the call from command and conversed with them in a businesslike tone, then summoned all the officers in the unit.
“Deputy Commander, those people are—”
“Don’t worry about them. They are my escorts.”
“But, we’re in a meeting...”
“Are you going to make me repeat myself?”
Wow, she was really born to be a commander. It’s a wonder how a voice so harsh can come out of someone so small.
“Then let’s begin the meeting. I’ve just received orders from Command. They say they haven’t detected any signs of enemy life within the walls.”

Anyway, as we stood at Raven’s side, we were able to get the gist of how things were unfolding. First, it seemed the enemy troops surrounding the lake had up and disappeared. This happened two hours after the entire corps retreated to the warships.
“It could be a trap. To get us to leave the ships of our own volition.”
“I’m not sure. I think there’s more weight to the theory that they retreated.”
“Everyone, please be quiet. Theorizing is pointless. Command has decided to mobilize troops from each unit to conduct a search.”

It seemed Raven had already thought about who to send because, without hesitation, she selected the members and sent them off to join the search team. A while later, new information came in from the newly-formed squadron.
“There’s nothing visible on the lakeside.”
First, the lakeside, which had been full of Clown’s undead creatures just a few hours ago, was completely empty.
“The second search team has discovered traces of large-scale magic in the area.”

Confirmation soon came in that it was a Multi Teleportation circle. Once Wall of Gold activated, people couldn’t teleport inside, but the reverse was still possible. The command center came to the conclusion that the enemy had retreated.

“Another standby order has been issued. It may be uncomfortable, but we will wait on the ship until the Wall of Gold disappears and the main unit returns. Our state of alert will also remain at this level.”
“Yes ma’am! I will convey that to the adventurers as well!”
Under Command’s orders, all troops remained on board and did not venture out to the lakeside.
Shaaa!

Eventually, Wall of Gold ran out of juice and disappeared into mana dust, and we reunited with the main unit once they came back from their expedition. Only after that did we go out to the lake to clean up the battlefield. The main unit waited about a day to confirm the area was safe, and left behind some additional troops as they headed off on another campaign.
“The main unit’s objective is to find Noark’s base, right?”

“Yes. The entrance, to be exact. It’s most likely to be connected to a specific area, like the center of the Crystal Cave. If we can find that place and occupy it, we can study how it was possible for them to get here in the first place.”
Jeez, being part of the main unit must be hectic, too, if they’re going to search the seventh floor as such a large army.
Just as I was thinking this, Raven let out a long breath. “Still, I’m glad this ended without any major casualties.”
It wasn’t without major hiccups, but at least no one had died or anything. Now that this particular mess was resolved, I was starting to feel that it was finally over.
“I really hope nothing else goes wrong before we return to Rafdonia.”
Hey, be careful what you say out loud.
Raven’s grumble left me uneasy, but I was sure nothing else would happen. We had a lot of troops now.
Just then, a line written on one of the documents on the table caught my eye. “...Patrol squad?”
“Ah, that? I guess the higher-ups had a lot of opinions about this incident. Even if it was a small team, no one noticed the enemy until they already infiltrated our base.”
“So they decided to deploy patrol squadrons?”
“Yes.” Raven provided a short answer since she was busy, then went back to her paperwork.
Huh, doesn’t she get bored staying holed up here? I’m getting so sore that my saliva is starting to taste sweet.
“Mister, are you bored?”
“A little?”
“Then do you want to go on a walk together?”
“Then who will protect Raven?”
“There won’t be a problem. That woman will stay behind, anyway.”
Erwen’s words triggered Amelia. “...Says who?”
“How touchy. You can go take a break once the two of us get back.”
Ugh, they’re going to end up fighting again.
“Both of you, stop it. I don’t want to go on a walk.” I mediated between the two and then slumped back into my chair to pass the time. Boredom set in even more.
Anyway, a patrol squad, huh?

It may have been an impulsive idea, but it seemed better than sitting here like this. At least I’d be outside walking around while on patrol. And since I’d run into a ton of monsters, it’d give me the XP I’d been missing.
I might even end up hitting level seven.
I didn’t have to think it over for long. “Raven, what do I have to do to join the patrol squad?”
“...You can’t.”
“Huh? Why?”

“We’ve already chosen all the members. Besides, in general, a mission can’t be changed once it’s assigned—it’s a matter of principle. Otherwise, everyone will only ever try to take the easy missions. There’s also the issue of fairness.”
Oh, I see.
I nodded and asked another question. “But isn’t there still away?”
“...Mission reassignments are possible at the discretion of the unit commander.”
What the—were you just messing with me? How mean.
“That commander is you. You can just change it—”
“I said no. I’m not going to do it.”
“I said I’m not going to do that for you. Who knows what trouble you’ll cause out there?” Raven put her foot down without so much as glancing my way.

Of course, that wasn’t a big problem. I wasn’t the type to give up like that. “Haha! That’s what you’re worried about?” When I laughed like none of what she said was a big deal, Raven looked confused.
What is that look? This is the problem with nerds. It’s like their brains are so dense that they can’t do any flexible thinking.
“The problem is you wouldn’t be there. So we can go together!”

When I offered a solution, Raven narrowed her eyes and looked me up and down. Then she posed an unexpected question. “I’m only asking this because I’m curious, but is there a similar race to barbarians in your world?”
Ah. Uh. Um...
In the end, I did get to join the patrol squad. This was because Raven was a pragmatist.
“Let me join!”
Silence.
“Let me join! I promise not to cause trouble!”
More silence.
“Let me join!”
This was Barbarian Parrot Mode. Once I employed the technique to which I owed a lot of my success in the Crystal Cave all those years ago, Raven was forced to stop ignoring me and gradually react.
“Ugh, why are you so stubborn about the weirdest things?!”
“Then let me join!”
“I said no! And if I haven’t said yes in over four hours, you should know to take a hint and stop!”
“I don’t know about any of that, just let me join!”
Sigh...

Once your opponent stopped expressing their anger and instead sighed, that was a promising sign that they were growing resigned. I continued to exploit that opening and eventually Raven gave her permission, likely concluding that this was better than being distracted from her work for the rest of the mission. That didn’t mean she succumbed solely to my tenacity, though.
“Ugh, honestly! Why are you being so stubborn?! You just have to stay put for a few more days!”
“...Because there are monsters outside.”
“What?”
“I told you. I have to get stronger.”
“Ugh, honestly... What am I supposed to do if you say that?”
And that was how I was given the OK. Of course, I did not manage to get Raven to come along with me. I told her I preferred to go with her, but Command wouldn’t allow it.
“I’m the only wizard who can use Wall of Gold here. I have to stay behind just in case something happens.”
Come to think of it, she was a valuable resource. “Then I’ll leave Emily or Erwen here.”
“If that’s to guard me, there’s no need. I was already doing fine without you, Mr. Y—I mean, Mr. Schuitz.”
Hmm, I’m still worried, though...
“I’m fine, really. Just don’t cause any trouble out there. In particular, don’t use Giantization. And don’t neglect your patrol duties just because you’re killing monsters. And...”

I had to sit through a long list of warnings like some kind of trainee before Raven finally contacted her higher-ups to change my mission. It was only then that I was able to leave the barracks. Coincidentally, there was a patrol squadron about to head out.

“You must be the new additions. It’s an honor to meet you, Miss Tersia.” When we arrived at our destination, the leader of the patrol squad started by confirming our specs. “Blood Spirit, since archery and elemental spirit magic are your specialties, you can stand in the center of the formation... Are the two of you close in combat?”
“That’s right.”
When I nodded, the team leader asked about our abilities in more detail. Amelia, who was an Agility-based damager, was placed on the left wing of the formation.
“Hm. Judging by your heavy armor and shield, it looks like you were in charge of the vanguard.”
Excuse me, how could this small body ever take a beating?
Before I could be branded as a tank, I hurriedly cut him off. “I’m usually the one destroying things.”
“...Sorry? Then your shield?”
“It’s just for decoration.” I put the shield in the sub-space and grabbed Kraul’s Demon Grinder with both hands. “I will stand on the right.”
After all, it wasn’t like I could let loose and use Giantization if we got into a fight. So I deserved to sit pretty and enjoy a close-range damage dealer position at least once, right?

chapters.title: Chapter 365: Responsibility (3)
paragraphs: The Canyon of Vengeful Spirits was the Dark Continent’s barrier to entry. When you got out of there, the lake where we were currently stationed appeared, and after that was a map divided into three main zones. The first was the Aribeona Estuary. This route followed a river to a waterfall lake, and if you went down it, it got you to the Dragon Mountain Range located in the center of the Dark Continent the quickest.
That’s also where the Bellarios spawns.

The place where I could acquire the essence responsible for my Mana Resistance in the final stages of my cultivation strategy was found in that mountain range. We wouldn’t be patrolling all the way there, though.

The second area was a wide jungle to the east of the estuary called the Great Forest. Because it was so large, the forest was subdivided into several zones, but that was the official name. Third was the Panthelion Ruins located west of the estuary, the destination for the Fourth Patrol Squad, which was made up of about thirty people including me.
“All troops, march!”

The patrol squad arrived at the entrance to the ruins, adjusted our formation, and then officially entered the area. Of course, the purpose of creating a patrol squad was to proactively defend against possible ambushes, so we didn’t travel deep into the ruins.
“Front line, march!”
“Raise the shield wall!”
There were a lot of monsters here anyway.
“Krrr...!” It started with modified beasts whose bodies were made of steel, like Golems.
Boom! Boom!
Giant, magically engineered Golems.
Whirl!

Flight-type monsters flew around like drones. Monsters that were asleep throughout the ruins sensed the presence of intruders and came running out. These monsters were not able to penetrate the shield-wielding front line to reach us.
Kwaaang!
The monsters were obstructed by a huge wall of people. The sight was strange. I never thought the day would come when I’d see someone else’s back from this angle.
This is what the others would have seen when they looked at me.
Even as I was seized by an uncanny feeling, I pounded the monsters that managed to escape to the sides with my hammer.
[You have cast Swing.]
[You have killed a Gigawolf. EXP +4]

Even if this was the seventh floor, the average rank of the monsters at the entrance to the Panthelion Ruins wasn’t very high, meaning there wasn’t a monster that could survive more than one single blow. Maybe because they were converted from machines, the feeling when you hit them was also odd.
Kakagak, rip, smash!
Whew, but it’s so convenient to just swing a hammer.
“Front line to the side!” the patrol commander soon shouted, and the tanks and their shields moved in unison, opening up a path in the center. As a result, the monsters broke through the front.
“Leona er epura!” But a joint spell was already ready to go in the rear.
Swoop!

Something a lot like a laser cannon fired from the center of the formation and blew holes in about fifteen large monsters, disrupting their charge and allowing the remaining monsters to be quickly cleared out.
It’s definitely easier to hunt in a raid team format. The front line is also stable with the priest here.

Although the average rank was admittedly low, it didn’t take more than ten minutes to clear out almost a hundred rampaging monsters. That was only natural since there were over thirty of us here. Even if we killed a hundred, the profits from this battle wouldn’t be that big once you divided by the number of people.
“There was no essence, so we’ll just collect the mana stones and keep moving!”
The patrol squad continued hunting—no, patrolling—and followed the pre-planned route circling the entrance to the ruins.
Wow, the amount of XP I mined today alone has to be over a hundred.
The number of new monsters I had already killed during this patrol exceeded twenty. The spawning monsters were low-rank, but there were many unique creatures here that only inhabited this zone.
“Good work, everyone.”

After patrolling for about ten hours, we let the next team take over our shift and returned to the base. There, we received a ticket from an administrative officer. Apparently, it confirmed our share of the loot from today’s hunt. It looked like we could receive our payment by submitting it to the Ministry of Merit later in the city.
“Hey there.” When I turned around with my ticket, a shifty man started talking to me.
I could only tilt my head in confusion. “...Who are you?” Not only did I have no memory of making a friend like this, but I’d never seen this guy before.
“Why are you acting like we’ve never met? I was beside you the entire fight.”
Oh, really? Come to think of it, he was...
From experience, it was best to gloss over stuff like that and change the subject in these cases. “Ah, so, what did you need?”
When I asked why he came up to me, the unnamed man patted me on the shoulder like he was my boss. “You were fighting real good there.”
Hmm, did he come over to socialize?
With that thought in mind, I decided to be humble for now. “You say that’s good? You have low standards.”
“What?”
For some reason, the man frowned. That wasn’t my problem, though. I removed his hand from my shoulder. It was annoying me.
Tap.
If you want to make friends, choose a better way to approach them.
“So, what do you want?”
When I asked again, the man’s fake smile disappeared, and the next thing that came out of his mouth was something unexpected. “I thought I’d give you some advice.”
“...Advice?”

“Looks like you’ve ignorantly poured everything into Strength. If you keep taking essences like that, you’ll be in great danger someday.” He took out a dagger and cut his arm. “See that? Even if I apply tons of force, it’s hard to cut. Adventurers should be well-balanced like me, rather than just relying on Strength—”
“Oh, what, you were just an idiot? Ah, sorry. I forgot to say that in my head.”
Even though I apologized like a man, his expression went stony and he glared at me.
Jeez, you look like you could be knocked over by a single tap. Who do you think you are, bragging about your measly Physical Resistance to me?
But just in case, I asked his name first. “By the way, what’s your name?”
“Melliver Eltain.”
What, you’re not even a Hans?
“I see. See you around.”
“Mister, what are you doing over there?”
“As you can see, someone’s calling me,” I told the man. Then, erasing the name I just heard from my memory, I walked away.
So, the name was Melliver... What was it again?

I couldn’t remember it and unfortunately, I never got to see the man again. I continued to take on patrol duties after that, but I joined a different patrol unit each time. The reason was simple. Each patrol unit only patrolled a single zone. This was a sensible strategy from Command’s perspective. If each patrol squad was in charge of an area, they would get familiar with the terrain and work better as a group. Normally, it was impossible to change teams every time... unless you had the support of a higher-up in the military.
“Raven, I heard the Eleventh Patrol Squad is going in deep this time...”
“Okay. I’ll write you a recommendation.”
“Thanks.”

Thanks to Raven’s help, I was able to visit the Aribeona Estuary and Great Forest in addition to the Panthelion Ruins to accumulate XP. Of course, I only ventured to the entrance and hadn’t encountered most of the monsters yet, but I still amassed XP each time I changed teams and time flew by to today.
[You have leveled up. Your Soul Power has increased by +30. The maximum number of essences you can absorb has increased by +1.]
Finally, I reached level seven, which I had been striving for, and added a new essence slot. This meant I could add new synergy to my current combo.
Since our money problem is essentially solved, I won’t have to join the war effort next time. Starting next month, I should farm for an essence. Ah, do I need a boat first?
As I was idly mulling over various things, I suddenly noticed how quiet things were. “Raven?”
“What is it?”
“Where are Erwen and Emily?”
“Emily left the barracks earlier to get some sleep and Erwen... I don’t know. She followed that woman not long after.”
“Hmm, I see.”
“So, is that all the questions you have?” Raven had already taken her eyes off me and was reading a document.
Jeez, at least give me time to answer. Come to think of it... It seems I’m alone with her.

As I stepped back and stopped talking so as not to disturb Raven’s work, I realized how strange this moment felt. That was because Amelia and Erwen had constantly been by my side ever since our reunion with Raven.
I should take this opportunity to ask her the question on my mind.
“Um, Raven.”
“What is it this time?”
“That ‘thing’ you mentioned before... what was that?” I asked cautiously.
Raven’s pen flinched and stopped moving. She lifted her eyes to glance at me. “What do you mean?”
Jeez, pretending not to know?
“What you mentioned in front of the steel bars. You said ‘that thing’ happened not long after you went to the Magic Tower.”
“...I don’t really want to talk about it. It’s not important.”

“Really? That’s too bad, then.” No matter how much effort I put into pretending to be a barbarian 24/7, I had no intention of being my usual rude self right now. I readily backed off. “Then how’s your mother? Is she doing well?” I just decided to chat instead. This may also have been a sensitive subject, but it wasn’t completely out of left field for me to ask.
“Did... you know something already...?”
“Huh?”

When I tilted my head at her strange reaction, Raven quickly blurted, “It’s nothing. But... why are you asking about my mother all of a sudden? I don’t see how that’s something you’d be interested in.”
Haha, I knew you would say something like that.
“Why wouldn’t I be? I was the one who convinced your mother to send you to the Magic Tower.”
Raven flinched. “W-What did you say?”
“I don’t know if you remember, but there was a time you came to the library after being beaten by your mother. At the time, you cried like a child and begged me for help—”
“I-I never did that!”
“Huh? I thought you don’t remember much of what happened back then?”
“Still, I... am confident I would never have done that.”
“Oh, really?”
“I’m not in the mood so stop joking around and tell me. Is it true what you said? That you... persuaded my mother?”
“Yes.”

While I was at it, I told her more about what happened in the past. I just skipped over it in the cage because I hadn’t had time to get into it. I’d wanted to have a moment like this with her at least once, though. To be more exact, I wanted to know how much of a positive impact my presence had on the overall chain of events. You never knew. There could come a day when I had to use the Fragment of Records Stone again.
Ah, but I should leave that part out.
As I talked, I made sure to omit parts of the conversation I had with her mother. The reason for that was simple.

“That child will abandon me. She’ll become a great person one day and look down on me. Then, in the end, she’ll leave me behind for that world of hers. Just as he did that day, since she’s his blood... Isn’t this unfair? Why is that child’s life so easy? I gave birth to her, but no one in my entire life has ever helped me for that reason. But... why that child...?”
How could I relay something so dark, and to the person in question herself?
“Forget about what happened in the library and tell me already. That day... what did you talk about with my mother?”
“Nothing special. I tried to persuade her to send you to the Magic Tower by saying I would pay all the expenses, but she refused.”
“Refused?”

“Ah, she refused the money, to be exact. Apparently, someone had visited from the Magic Tower a few days before. I guess you caught someone’s eye, electrocuting people with magic everywhere you went.”
“I see... that’s why she suddenly changed her mind...”
“Ahem, not to toot my own horn, but I’m kind of your savior in a way...” I implicitly lobbied for that interpretation but Raven just ignored me.
Jeez, you’re embarrassing me.
“So... what happened to your mother? Are you getting along now?”
When I changed the subject again, Raven’s response was frigid. “We can’t even if I wanted to.”
“She’s already dead.”

I was rendered momentarily speechless, and silence fell. “Ah, uh... r-really? That’s unfortunate. She didn’t seem like sh-she had any health problems...” It had really been a while since I had been this flustered so I tried to calm down and sort this out, but it wasn’t like I could put the genie back in the bottle.
“It wasn’t a health issue. It wasn’t even an accident. And she wasn’t at the end of her lifespan, either.”
“...Then?”

“She hung herself. It was about a month after I left for the Magic Tower. I was able to go home for the first time in a week because of some homework from Master, and...” Raven’s tone was calm as she spoke, like she was simply reading an entry in an old diary she’d found hidden in the corner of a storage room—like it wasn’t her story at all. “There was a rotten smell in the bedroom. And that was my last memory of my mother... Don’t look at me like that. I already worked through it a long time ago. People die. It’s nothing new.”
Raven ended up being the one to offer comfort instead of the other way around, while I ended up unable to speak at all. The memory got clearer and clearer.
“Isn’t it strange? Everything I’ve accomplished in my life is in a single room in this dump... What was the point of my life, then?”
That was the last conversation I had with her mother. After that, I watched her stumble into the back alley like a person who had been drained of all life.

chapters.title: Chapter 366: Responsibility (4)
paragraphs: Raven was the one to end the awkward silence. “Are you going to keep making that face? This isn’t even your fault, Mr. Y—I mean, Mr. Schuitz.”

She probably wasn’t saying this knowing the entire context, but she wasn’t wrong. It would be unrealistic to say this was all my fault, but I couldn’t shake the thought that I had been the one to give a person standing at the edge of a cliff the final push. If I hadn’t gone to see that woman, perhaps she wouldn’t have made that choice.
Dwalkie... Bjorn’s biological father, Yandel Jarku...
When I thought of these two cases, I was forced to acknowledge the possibility even more. My presence had changed the future.

“Ha... if I knew this was going to happen, I wouldn’t have brought it up,” Raven said. It began to hit me that I could no longer play the oblivious card and keep my mouth shut anymore, couldn’t deceive her yet again.

On the other hand, I also thought this: was it okay for me to pick at a wound that had finally healed just because I didn’t want to turn a blind eye to the part I’d played in causing it? That thought made it hard for me to open my mouth and speak.
“What a strange tension. Are we interrupting something?”
“Strange? That can’t be possible. But... Mister... what were the two of you doing...?”

When I turned toward the entrance at the sound of voices, I could see Amelia and Erwen lifting the tent flap and walking in. When I turned my head again, Raven had already returned her attention to the documents in front of her.
Yeah, this isn’t the time to have this conversation.
In the end, I couldn’t say anything that day.
[The labyrinth is now closed. You are being transported to Rafdonia.]
On day seventy-five of the quest, the closing date for the seventh floor, we returned to the city.
Wow, it really feels like it’s been a while.
After spending over two months in the labyrinth, the city felt alien. I had heard some upper-floor clans tended to rest for a month or two after an expedition, and I was beginning to understand why.
“Are you going home straight away, Mister?”
“For now. Let’s rest, and then we can eat some good food.”
“Okay!”

After leaving the currency exchange, we headed straight to the mansion. We didn’t actually exchange a lot of mana stones. After we got to the sixth floor, all loot was received in the form of vouchers with the seal of the royal family. Apparently, these could be exchanged for money at the Office of Merit, but since it would be crowded for a few days, I decided to wait a while before heading over there.
“Whew, finally home.”
‘Home’ was a mansion with a small garden, and anything that could be called a window boarded up. I never thought I’d be glad to see this place.
Anyway, let’s eat the takeaway after washing up...
“Then who’s going to wash up first?”
We were trying to decide on the order when Amelia said to me, “Schuitz, you use the second-floor bathroom.”
“Huh? That’s fine with me, but you’re okay with me going first?”
“The first-floor bathroom is bigger than the second. The two of us can just use it together.”
I didn’t quite understand. “...What? You guys are going to use it together?” For some reason, I couldn’t really picture it. “You guys... when did you get so close?”
At my obvious shock, Erwen waved her hands, extremely flustered. “C-Close? That’s not true! You! Say something! Why would I take a bath with you?”
“Because it’s more efficient. Well, if you don’t want to, I’ll take a bath first.”
“What? Why do you get to decide—”
“Then I’m going in.”
“...Wait, stop!” When Amelia headed toward the bathroom, Erwen ran after her with a shout.
How is it that they never have a quiet day?

I turned away and headed to the second-floor bathroom. I was a little curious about who was going to use the bathroom first or if they’d wash up together... But what did it matter either way? At this point, I was at least sure they wouldn’t draw their weapons on each other.
“Whew, that feels much better.”
As soon as I poured hot water on my body, I felt all the fatigue I accumulated melt away. It felt like the expedition was finally over.
Considering everything that happened... things ended up going quite smoothly.

There weren’t any noteworthy incidents after that initial ambush. I continued to join patrol duty until I gained enough XP to reach level seven, and that peace persisted. It seemed something happened to the main unit in the middle of our stay because they requested our support, so we joined the troops for a while. Of course, that didn’t affect me very much. Raven had to remain in the rear because of her strategic role, and that also applied to us as her unit.
For this loot settlement, I’ll have to first sell the equipment and exchange the vouchers for money...
As I was cataloging our gains from this expedition while washing up, it all felt very novel.
“Level seven, huh?”

I was now at a level where I could proudly say I’d entered the mid-to-late stages of the game. Not to mention the number of rank-three essences I’d obtained despite still technically being at the beginning of the second half. It seemed like just yesterday that I was crawling around after stepping on goblin traps.
I’ve become much stronger.

I was starting to feel my growth. After all, the reason why I could say that this expedition had ended smoothly in the first place? I’d had to fight four members of Orcules: Corpse Collector, Wailing Witch, Lighthouse Keeper, and Blood Knight. In the past, someone would have had to make a sacrifice to get us out of that encounter, and I also would have had to put my life at stake.
I have to get even stronger.

Rather than feeling satisfied, though, I felt my own inadequacy even more. I still had a long way to go before I could guarantee complete safety for myself and my comrades from the palace and monsters like Auril Gavis and Baekho.
I have to hit level nine somehow. And I have to resolve the issue of the Spirit Imprint as soon as possible...
Just as I was thinking that, I heard, “Mister, are you almost done? I’m thinking of reheating the food now.”
“Ah, I’ll be out soon.” Realizing I had been in the bathroom for a lot longer than I thought, I quickly finished up and exited. Then, eating the reheated food, we talked.
“Schuitz, what’s your plan for dealing with the guild issue?”
“Guild issue?”
“What Raven mentioned. That if you want to avoid the palace’s attention, you should make sure to deal with the information the guild has on record first.”

The last time rank-five adventurer Riehen Schuitz entered the labyrinth was about five years ago. If the palace were to look at the documents stored in the guild, my fake identity would quickly be exposed. The team Schuitz worked with and the essences he was confirmed to have would all be written down there.
“Plus, if they find his old colleagues and ask them a few questions, they’ll be sure to notice something is off. Not to mention if they’re brought in to meet you personally.”
I had to either burn Schuitz’s records or modify them to make them inconspicuous. This was something only a guild insider could do.
“Is there someone who can help?”
“I don’t know, I’ve never been close to the guild.”
Of course, even as I said that, there was one person who came to mind: Julian Urbans, the precious daughter of the district chief whom I once took as a hostage to clear my name.
Hmm, maybe ‘precious daughter’ isn’t the right description.

Thinking back even now, she had been an unusual woman, wishing for her father’s downfall because she didn’t want to live like a puppet. I wondered what happened to her. If I had helped her back then, could I have cashed in that favor now?
The day after we returned to the city, Amelia headed out to dispose of Lighthouse Keeper’s equipment and Erwen left to drop by her holy land.
“Then should I head out too?”

I also got dressed and went out. After some discussion, we concluded it was okay. Even Raven, my former clanmate, hadn’t recognized my face, as it was unfortunately next to impossible to look at this face and think ‘Bjorn Yandel.’ So it would be weird for me to stay holed up at home.
I should have met that dragon tribe kid with this face instead.
Even the dragon shaman, who claimed I was ugly as hell the first time we met, wouldn’t be able to tell such a lie when she saw my current look.
Tsk, what’s so great about a scrawny face like this? Anyway, I should go there first...

This was my first proper outing since returning to the present. As I walked along, leisurely taking in my surroundings just like I did twenty years in the past, I soon arrived at my destination: Carcia Romne, a forge with a fancy, ancient name that didn’t seem to suit the trade. Apparently, it meant “magic flame.” It was the forge Hikurod Murad built after he left Team Half-Wit.
I heard business was good these days. I guess that was true.

I’d heard this from Raven but I didn’t expect things to be going this well. Seeing as he had apparently added a floor on each of the nearby buildings, it seemed business had been booming in the two and a half years I’d been gone.
Should I take a look inside?
I was curious so I went into the forge and slowly looked around at the equipment on display.

“Hahaha! The items on display are not for sale—they’re samples of custom-made items. If you’re looking for something in particular, let me know!” When I turned around at the familiar voice, a familiar face stood there.
“Hikurod Murad.”
“Oh, do you know my name? Hahaha! I guess I have become famous.” Hikurod laughed heartily and looked up. Then he flinched as his eyes met mine. “...Huh?”
“What is it?”
“Ah, it’s nothing. Just a strange feeling. Why, you’re a tall and handsome fellow.”
I thought he might have recognized me but it seemed he didn’t.
Okay, then this proves no one will recognize me even if I don’t cover my face. But... why am I sad?
Pushing the inexplicable feeling aside, I had a conversation with the dwarf. “Is it okay for the boss to be out on the floor?”
“Haha, I don’t do blacksmith work.”
“Why?”
“Well, why would I when the hired blacksmiths do it for me? They make it better than I do.”
“...I see.”
“This may even be my calling. I’ve found my talent late. So, tell me. If you’re looking for something, I can match any price.”
Now I could see that the dwarf seemed to have given up on his dream of becoming a blacksmith and switched to a sales job instead. No wonder business was doing well.
Oh? He’s even wearing a mithril necklace.

To be honest, this was quite a shock. Between the fact that he’d given up on his dream and the clothes he was wearing, he didn’t seem like the guy I once knew. The cherry on top was the last thing he said.

“Ugh, tsk... how unlucky. And he seemed like he had a lot of money.” When I told him I was only there to look around, all traces of laughter disappeared from his face and he kicked me out. “If you’re not going to buy anything, get out! Other customers can’t get in because of you!”
Even as I was kicked out, I was flabbergasted. What happened to this guy that he’d become so obsessed with money?
...I guess it doesn’t matter since he seems to be doing well.
After leaving the blacksmith, I headed to the training center I tracked down. It was a center Rotmiller ran to teach scouting skills to adventurers.
It’s closed. I just wanted to catch a glimpse of his face, even from afar.
For some reason, they weren’t open for business today.
So where should I go?
I considered going home, but there was nothing to do there anyway, so I decided on a new destination and got moving. When you had nothing else going on, there was no place like the library.
When I entered through the wide-open doors, I saw a familiar desk.
What the...?
The people sitting at the desk were all different. Normally, there would be just one sleepy-eyed librarian sitting at that wide desk.
“Hello, welcome.”
Instead, more than twenty employees were working the desk, much like the library from twenty years ago.
“Um... what happened to the original librarian?”
“Who are you talking about?”
“Ragna Litaniel Peprock...”

One of the librarians tilted her head in confusion at my question before heading over to the desk to ask the others. “I asked my seniors and they said that person retired before the library was restructured,” she reported.
“...Can you tell me when she retired?”
“Since it was just before the restructuring, it must have been two years ago.”

Two years ago, huh? Well, she wasn’t the type of person who should be a librarian for the rest of her life. She was using a huge amount of mana to manage a library that should have been maintained by dozens of people all on her own.
“Is there something else I can help you with?”
“It’s all right. If you just cast the detection spell on me, I’ll take care of the rest myself.”
“The Book Recognition spell costs three thousand stones!”
What, you have to pay for it now?
It hit me that there had been a lot of changes while I was gone, but I paid for now, grabbed a few books, and sat down. I wasn’t sure how much time passed like that.
Honkkk!
Who is that?
Honkkk!
I couldn’t stand the sound of the snoring that kept echoing through the stacks at random intervals and raised my head.
“Um... we received a complaint... could you please wake up...?” One of the librarians was shaking a giant, snoring barbarian’s shoulders.
Honkkk!
Ugh, what a disgrace to barbarians... Huh?

The moment the barbarian woke up, wiping her mouth, I couldn’t help but jerk back in surprise. “Ah, sorry! I guess I fell asleep for a second!” She had blonde hair that was half braided and half left down, and gold eyes that carried a hint of stubbornness.
“Ah, right... Then will you be leaving...?”
Huh, I never thought I’d see her at the library.
I almost didn’t recognize her with her newly-large frame, but the moment I saw her face, I knew.
“Haha! No need to kick me out. I’m apologizing! Don’t be callous. Ah, was ‘callous’ too difficult a word to understand?” It was Ainar, the second daughter of Fenelin.

chapters.title: Chapter 367: Responsibility (5)
paragraphs: She was almost six feet tall, but thanks to her good proportions and lean muscles, Ainar didn’t look too bulky.
It’s strange to be looking up at her.
She must have erased the essence of the Bone Knight.

It was strange to see Ainar again after so long. After all, I was used to the way she looked after her body shrank all those years ago in the Rift. Well, if I combed through my memories, I could still see remnants of the old Ainar in this woman’s face.
She looked so young back then.
Ainar had become much more mature than she looked in my memories. Though maybe it was more a difference in the way she held herself than a change in her face itself.
“Haha! It’s not weird to fall asleep while reading a book. Are you discriminating against me for being a barbarian?”
“Um... th-that’s not it. R-Really—”
“I’m joking! Joking! I promise not to cause any more trouble, so let me off the hook, okay?”

I sensed an ease in her hearty laughter, and her speaking skills had improved considerably. She was messing around with the other person and even naturally fostered an atmosphere that made it hard for them to scold her. I was honestly impressed. She was now able to use the characteristics of the barbarian tribe to her advantage.
“...Okay, if you say so.”
“Haha, thanks! Ah, do you want some beef jerky?”
“...It’s all right. And food is not permitted—”

“I know! It’s just that you’re so skinny. Now, go! You must be busy!” Ainar practically pushed the librarian in the back to shoo her away and opened a book, likely as a way of keeping her promise not to fall asleep.
She... reads now?
For some reason, I felt my heart swell. I spent some time pretending to read while secretly observing her from across the library.
“Mm...” Ainar frowned. It seemed she was stumped by a part of the book. But even this served to prove how much she had changed. “Hey, friend!” She called out to me without hesitation.
“...Are you talking to me?”
“Haha, you’re strange, friend! Is there anyone else here? Can you come here and read this for me?”
Huh, to think she would call a human her friend and go so far as to ask one for help. Do... I look like a barbarian to her?
“Don’t be scared! I won’t hurt you!”
“It’s not because I’m scared, I’m just surprised. I thought barbarians hated humans.”
“That’s all prejudice! Well, I was like that at one point, but I slowly realized there’s no reason to dislike you.”
Hmm, I don’t think she mistook me for a barbarian.
I didn’t think she made any connection between me and Bjorn Yandel, either, so I headed over to her table as requested.
“I’m reading this part here and I just can’t understand this word. Can you tell me what it means?”
“This reads... logistics. It refers to a branch of the military that manages and supplies goods.”
“Branch? What is that? It sounds interesting.”
Why is she reading a book on the military if she doesn’t even know that?

It was ridiculous, but I decided to answer her question. When I looked at the pile of books stacked next to her, I saw there were various genres other than military nonfiction. Most were history books.
She’s reading these?
“Anyway, thanks! I can finish the rest thanks to you!”

When I finished explaining the word to her, Ainar returned her attention to her reading and I returned to my seat as well. Some time passed, and eventually, I couldn’t stop myself from asking, “Why are you reading that book?”
“Huh? Are you picking a fight with me?”
“No, that’s not it...”
“Haha! Don’t make that face. I know I must look strange!”
Jeez, she’s really screwing with people now.

As I watched, Ainar’s bright laughter soon dried up as her expression shifted to something more serious. “The warrior I respected most in the world often read books. Well, I’ll never be able to follow in his footsteps... But I have to do something.” There’s a slight, lonely tinge to her tone.
I recalled what Erwen and Raven informed me Ainar was up to.
After I died... she declared that she would become a chieftain.

I had been considered a strong candidate, but once I died, she had boldly expressed her own ambitions to the tribesmen. At first, they were skeptical, but as time passed, more people began to support her, and now she was practically considered the next successor.
Suddenly, Ainar looked at me. “Anyway... this is a little disappointing.”
“What is?”
“If you were born a barbarian, you would have been quite handsome.”
“...Is that so?”
“Anyway, it’s fate that we met here, so why don’t we introduce ourselves? I am Ainar, the second daughter of Fenelin. You are?”

“Riehen Schuitz.” When I revealed my pseudonym, Ainar seemed to think it over for a moment as if to commit it to memory. Then she handed me some of the books from her pile. “Why... are you giving these to me all of a sudden?”
“It’s a gift for a new friend.”
Who gives library books as a gift? It’s not like I can take these with me.
“...Thanks.” I was flabbergasted, but I still did the polite thing and thanked her. But what was this?
“No problem. This is nothing for a higher species.”
“...Higher species?”

“Ah, is that too difficult a term for you? You wouldn’t know, being human, but...” Ainar stole a glance at our surroundings and then leaned in so that only I could hear. “Barbarians are the most superior race in the world.”
...Huh?
“Read that book and you’ll see for yourself whether I’m right or not.”
I instinctively checked the titles of the books I was handed.
Secret of the Heart: The Selfish Superiority Factor
Barbarians III: Why Wizards Covet Their Hearts
Seven Reasons Why You Shouldn’t Provoke a Barbarian, Learnings from the War of Sacred Relics
Those were the book titles.
“Aren’t you reading?”
“...I’m reading.”
Ainar kept prodding me so I had no choice but to read the books I was given. To be honest, I was also curious. Sure, the titles may have been odd, but the contents could end up being normal...
...Never mind.

I didn’t know who wrote these books, but they were all the same: texts praising barbarians as a superior race. What on earth were they thinking when they wrote these things? Seeing as they were capable of writing books in the first place, the authors couldn’t have been barbarians. And if they were in their right minds, they wouldn’t have published these with a barbarian target audience in mind.
Tap.
I gave up trying to figure it out and closed the book. When I did, Ainar looked at me from across the table with sparkling eyes. “How was it? Wasn’t it a good book?”
“...It was definitely an interesting story.”

“Haha, don’t look so dejected. Humans aren’t all that inferior. We’re just special. Did you know? The barbarian illiteracy rate is ninety-nine times that of humans, but we still maintain and pass on traditions that go back thousands of years. That’s something no other race has ever managed to do. Ah, also, do you know why barbarians don’t float in water? That’s actually because the density of our souls is significantly higher than other races.”
“Um, do you know what density is?”
“...Ahem, there’s also a reason why Spirit Imprints only work for barbarians!”
So you don’t know, huh?
“It’s because there are no souls as clean and pure as ours.”
I got up from my seat.
“Hmm? Where are you going? I’m just getting started.”
“Sorry, but I just remembered something I need to do. Maybe I’ll catch you later.”
“...Really? That’s too bad. Goodbye.”
It was nice seeing Ainar again, but I was getting the vibe this lecture would last the rest of the day, so I booked it.
I won’t be noticed here.

I moved to another corner of the library and started reading a new book. Most of the ones I chose were books on current events. There were quite a few aggregated newspaper archives published over the course of the year.
I heard the palace implemented a lot of policies for lower-floor adventurers. I guess these are some of them.
In the middle of my research, I turned to the next page and my hands froze as I came across a familiar name in an article from a year ago.
Niall Urbans, Seventh District Chief of the Adventurers’ Guild, Voluntarily Resigns For Personal Reasons, Not Politics
That guy retired?
My interest was piqued and I took a closer look at the article, which didn’t take long to get through.

As for his sudden decision to retire, many acquaintances of the district chief, who ran for guild master just two years prior, believe the decision may have been brought on by a change of heart following the death of his daughter one year ago.
“...Was that girl his only kid?”
I wasn’t sure. We weren’t particularly close.
Still, I should check.
I combed through the books containing articles from a year prior, and before long, I was able to find what I was looking for.
Eldest Daughter of the Urbans Family, Julian Urbans, Announces Marriage to the General Manager of Alminus Company
It started with an article about an engagement.
Julian Urbans Found Dead On The Night of Her Wedding
Then, three months later, an obituary was posted. The cause of death was a nasty fall. Apparently, she was drunk, lost her footing, and fell headfirst from a third-floor terrace.
In his insurance claim, Niall Urbans once again firmly insisted the death was not a suicide, but an accident.
For some reason, there was a bitter taste in my mouth. We didn’t have a close relationship but knowing what I knew about her situation, I almost felt like I had some responsibility for what happened.
Anyway, let’s go back for today. Maybe I shouldn’t have looked into that...
One day, two days, three days, four days...

As always, time passed very quickly in the city, especially since there were a lot of things to do at the beginning of each month. As I exchanged the vouchers for money and sold the equipment, time really flew by, and soon the time came to divvy up the loot.
“There should still be some money left over even after we pay off the debt.”
“Th-then we don’t have to sell the house!”
“About that, I actually want us to postpone paying off the debt.”
“That’s because there’s still plenty of time until the money is due, and there are things we need to invest money in right now.”
“I-If you want to do that, Mister... th-then I can’t argue with you... But where are you thinking of spending all that money?”
“I’m going to buy a boat.”
“A boat?”
While Erwen looked confused, Amelia picked up on where I was going with this and nodded. “True, unless we plan to keep fighting on the war front, it would be best to have at least one ship.”
“Exactly. And I want to go somewhere on the sixth floor next.”

We had joined the war as mercenaries because we didn’t have money, but we managed to hit our target amount in just one expedition. There was no reason for us to go to war again. Though it’d make us good money considering the payout we received this time, there was something more important to me than that.
“Where do you plan to explore?”
“Burrow Island.”
“...Burrow Island? Where is that?”

As Amelia’s reaction implied, it wasn’t a well-known island. Only someone like Raven would know about it. However, when I offered a brief description of the island, recognition bloomed on Erwen and Amelia’s faces.
“An island hidden under the sea... I know the one you’re talking about now.”
“I think my sister told me about that place before!”
“But can we go just the three of us? We don’t even have a navigator.”
“That’s why we have to start looking now.”
“Looks like we’re going to be busy for a while.”
Thankfully, the two agreed to follow my plan without much argument, so starting the next day, we went around looking for a ship and navigator. Time once again flew by.
“Where’s Erwen?”
“Sleeping.”
“Really? You didn’t have to come with me, you know.”
“...You never know. But if you don’t want me to, I won’t come next time.”
Uh, I never said I didn’t want her to...
“Ahem, I was just trying to say thank you.”
“...How was that a thank you?”
Jeez, just accept it, will you?
I chuckled, then checked the clock on the table. “I’ll be back.”
“Sure.”
As soon as I closed my eyes, the whole world was dyed white.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
Now, then. Shall I turn on the computer?

chapters.title: Chapter 368: Black Star (1)
paragraphs: Click, click.
I used the mouse to navigate to the chatrooms first. This was one of the first things I did every time I came to the community.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 0 people are online.]
As expected, no one was in the Korean chatroom where I first met Baekho.
Man, a part of me wants to just meet and have a candid conversation with him...

After briefly checking the chat, I switched over to the bulletin board. Normally, people started posting explosively once the community opened. There was no better time to get a quick overview of what had happened in the past month.
[Breaking News: Count Ramleonde dead during expedition.]

I heard the leader of Orcules and four other members destroyed him. Rumor has it there’s a high chance the vacant position of Third Corps Commander will go to the chief of staff, who performed the duties on his behalf during this expedition.
these99: Now that Wall of Gold’s weakness has been revealed, the rear will no longer be a good place for freeloading.
└SecureId7: Why not? It doesn’t even look like a lot of people died. At most, they’ll just increase the number of patrols next time.
stevencastle: But isn’t the chief of staff that prick Eltora Tercerion?
└OP: Yep. The prime minister’s son.
└stevencastle: Ugh, I’m never going to the Third Corps now. I’ve never had an encounter with that bastard that ended well.
As expected, most of the posts on the bulletin board were about the war.
[Has anyone heard the news about Blood Spirit?]
I heard she killed Lighthouse Keeper, or whatever that member of Orcules’s name is. Is that true? From what I hear, Blood Knight, Corpse Collector, and Wailing Witch were on his team.
marcelone: This is a fact that everyone in the know already knows, but just so you’re aware, I heard she didn’t kill him alone but joined forces with the Golden Wizard.
└OP: Wow, really? I heard they were colleagues a long time ago. I guess they don’t have bad blood, contrary to the rumors.
└marcelone: Still, there’s a lot of speculation since their opponents were so strong. Even Blood Spirit couldn’t defeat Lighthouse Keeper while fighting all of them at once.
Tsk, so there are people who are suspicious.
If doubts were being expressed here, there might even be investigations in motion elsewhere.
Click, click.
I continued to read the posts, my mind wandering. A long while later, I suddenly received a message.
Ding!
[From: Ghost Master]

The GM’s nickname was written as the sender, but that wasn’t particularly noteworthy. System messages and announcements within the community were always sent under this name. More than 90 percent of the messages in my inbox were from the GM.
But I’m worried that my karma’s about to come back and bite me.
Sensing I was about to reap what I’d sown, I clicked on the link. It was exactly what I expected.
[I wasn’t able to contact you last month. If you have time, we should meet.]
I had received an invitation from the GM. This wasn’t particularly surprising. I expected him to contact me. In fact, the bigger surprise was that it took him so long to do so.
To be honest, I thought a message would come right after the last meeting.
I exposed the GM’s identity at the Round Table, and Soul Queen would have reported this to him immediately.
But the fact that he contacted me a month later...

There were two possibilities: either he wanted to carefully take his time before meeting with me, or he for some reason wasn’t reachable the last time the community was active. Well, that didn’t matter.
Then what should I do...?

Leaving the message on the screen, I took some time to think this through. It wasn’t like the GM would ban me or something if I declined the invitation. I’d been diligent about crafting the persona of a big shot while in Lion’s mask. If he had a brain, he wouldn’t try to go against me, especially when he almost died after banning Baekho.
Yeah, let’s meet him at least.
