Now that I’d made my decision, there was no reason to hesitate. I closed the window, found the secret chatroom, and entered the password he included in the message.
The password is 0720? Is that some kind of anniversary?
The thought occurred to me but even if my hypothesis was correct, it wasn’t like that was relevant information.
Shaaaaaa!

Soon, the monitor lit up with a flash. When I opened my eyes again, I was in an old-fashioned study, the faint scent of books in the air. This place gave off a calming vibe for some reason, and it was also somewhat familiar to me. I’d been here once before. At the time, rumors of a dimensional collapse had been circulating. While asking around to see whether the rumors were true or not, I obtained information from a man here.
It had been Elfnunalove, the man with that strange nickname above his head. At the time, I never suspected he could be the GM. I figured he was probably feeling the same way.
“Long time no see, Elfnunna. Or do you prefer Mr. Lion?”
“Either one, I don’t care.”
“Your tone of voice has changed a lot since last time. Or is this your true self?”
I had no reason to answer that so I just ignored him and sat on the sofa across from him.
When I did, the guy plastered on a fake smile. “Anyway, this is our third meeting. Isn’t it strange? Life is so unpredictable.”
It was definitely strange. During our first meeting, I was in the position of a newbie seeking info, and the second time we met had been in a chatroom with Baekho.
“It’s just as I said. You won’t be able to meet up with Mr. Lee here from now on.”

This guy had given me a brief summary of what happened to Baekho out of respect for Baekho’s countryman, and that was the end of it. To him, I had just been a rare Korean player. Nothing more, nothing less.
“You have become much quieter since we last met. Then let me be direct. I don’t believe in fate or coincidences. What do you want from me?”
What do I want, huh?
“What makes you think I want something?”
“Our first meeting, at least, was definitely intentional.”
So, that’s how you’re interpreting this. Although it really was a coincidence.
“You were the one who invited me to the chatroom back then,” I pointed out.

“Yes, I did. But now that I think about it, it’s strange. The fact that you mentioned the wizard named Shernal Fergang from Tarutein School in your forum post as well. No matter how I look at it, I can’t help but think you were trying to reel me in. You intentionally posted something I would find interesting, didn’t you?”
He was a funny guy. What would I gain from that?
“The thought makes me shudder because it means you knew me well enough to pull something like that.”
It was a ridiculous leap to make, but there was nothing to gain by saying so out loud so I decided to stop this line of questioning here. “...I’m sure you didn’t call me to talk about that.”
“Are you avoiding an answer?”
Avoiding? Well, I can’t tell him the truth.
“Think whatever you wish.”
“I will.”
“So, the reason you called me here.”
When I took the reins and steered the conversation where I wanted it to go, the GM smirked. “What a weird question. You were the one who called me.”
Huh? Where did that come from?

I fell silent in response to this strange plot twist, and he was happy to talk to himself. “I have no idea how you found out my real name. But wasn’t the reason you told Soul Queen so that you could meet with me?”
He was so confident yet so wrong that it gave me secondhand embarrassment. I was suddenly faced with a new conundrum, but as always, I didn’t let myself get caught up in the little details.
“I see.”
Since he already thinks this way, let’s change tactics a little.
“So you aren’t a fool,” I said.
“So you mean...” The man trailed off, staring at me.

I responded with a shrug. This guy was probably feeling me out too. It was obvious this was a ploy to get information out of me. If I played along with whatever he was accusing me of, he would take it as fact, but if I denied it, he would be able to eliminate at least one theory. In fact, it didn’t hurt this guy to take all the shots in the dark he wanted, just to see what landed.
So I’ll make sure he misses.
Soon, I opened my mouth. “Yes, there is something I want from you.”
When I thought about it, this wasn’t a bad place to be. I wasn’t just saying that; there were some things that I wanted that only a GM could get.
“In that case, you could have contacted me discreetly.”
Oh, that...
“That’s no fun,” I replied vaguely.
He once again cooked up his own interpretation. “...I don’t know, it seems to me that you only did that to intimidate me.”
Well, you can think whatever you want.
I got back to the point. “So, are you not going to ask?”
“...About what?”
“What I want from you.”
He stared at me in silence for a moment, then sighed. “All right. Let’s hear it. What is it that you want from me?”
I answered after a short pause. “Lift the ban on Baekho Lee.”

If there was something I wanted that I really needed the GM’s power for, this would be it. If Baekho came back to the community, we could talk. I also needed to dig up information on my cat, who he was temporarily fostering.

But it seemed he’d anticipated this request. “I see, so this is what you were after.” Surprisingly, the GM was unshaken. Well, it wasn’t unusual for players to form factions based on nationality. “Then was it Baekho who told you my identity?”
He already seemed convinced Baekho and I were in cahoots, so there was no reason for me to confirm or deny. “Who knows?”
“What... are you two planning?”
“Well, there’s no reason I can’t answer that...”
“...Really?” He looked dumbfounded. It seemed he hadn’t expected me to actually answer his question.
Jeez, you have to let people finish their sentences.
“If you bring me something worthwhile.”
The GM frowned. “Are... you talking about an interesting piece of information?”
So, Soul Queen told you about that too.
When I maintained my silence instead of refuting him, the guy tapped his knee with his index finger. “Hahaha...” Then, suddenly, he started to laugh like a deflated balloon.
What the—? That’s scary.
“I guess you are quite confident in yourself, huh?” This cold question was a complete one-eighty from the amiable, polite tone he was using earlier.
“I wouldn’t say I’m not.”
“I’m very similar.”
“Does that mean you refuse my terms?”

He answered without hesitation. “Yes. There is no reason for me to share my information in a one-sided exchange just because you demand it. If you want the ban on Baekho Lee lifted, you bring me something worthwhile.” The GM got up from his seat and immediately looked at me in a way that told me he intended to have the last word in this conversation.
Hmm, well, I’m glad he gave me time to throw in my two cents.
“How unfortunate,” I said with sincere disappointment. “To think you thought I was making a deal.”
The guy tilted his head at my words.
Don’t pretend like you don’t understand what I mean. Even if you’ve been pretending not to be, you’ve been scared of me from the get-go.
“Your tone of voice has changed a lot since last time.”
This guy had maintained a polite attitude despite my rudeness.
“...I don’t know, it seems to me that you only did that to intimidate me.”
He felt noticeably threatened by my actions.
“In that case, you could have contacted me discreetly.”
And rather than voicing his anger at the things I’d done, he first expressed disappointment instead.
“I’ll give you three months,” I said.
“...Are you threatening me right now?” I neither confirmed nor denied that. As always, the interpretation was up to the listener. Soon, he said, “...Even Baekho Lee couldn’t touch me.”
Wow. You know, if you say it in such a small voice like that, it only looks like you’re trying to give yourself a pep talk.

Anyway, there were a few things I had to set straight. “Actually, I seem to recall you almost died at his hands. Do I look as soft as him?” He didn’t answer. “Remember. Three months. After that, I’ll go find you myself.”
It was now my turn to stand up.
“Whew... I feel much better here.”
Leaving the chatroom and returning to my bedroom, I collapsed on the bed. This was something I’d experienced countless times since first putting on the Lion mask, but it still drained me every time.
I didn’t know things would play out like this.
Originally, I planned to meet up with the GM and ask him how much he knew about me, that kind of stuff. If possible, I’d bring up Baekho too. Yeah, that had been the original plan.
But to think he was that afraid of me.

Throughout the conversation, the plan changed. The Magic Engineer, Yurven Havellion, now had an unknown, powerful man who knew his identity. It seemed that had served to cause the GM considerable anxiety, and being able to pick up on that quickly worked to my advantage.
Still, even though his identity was exposed, he didn’t seem wary of the palace.

As I slowly replayed our conversation, a question that hadn’t occurred to me earlier came to mind. If I spilled the fact that he was an evil spirit to the palace, I could guarantee the GM’s downfall without even having to lift a finger against him. So why did he only seem concerned about direct threats?
Does he have someone in the palace who can sweep the issue of him being an evil spirit under the rug?
If so, I wanted to share that person.
...That couldn’t be possible, though, right? Even the end of our conversation is bothering me...
I recalled the request he made of me before leaving the chat.
“Password. Don’t say anything about the password.”

It was a rather off-putting exchange. What about the password? Seeing as he was bringing it up, I figured it had to have some kind of significance. I kept quiet because I couldn’t figure it out, which apparently was answer enough for him.
“Perhaps you don’t have anything to do with him, then... Sorry for keeping you. I’ll see you again soon.”
Man, that just made me more uneasy. The password, 0720... What was the GM trying to find out from me with those numbers?

chapters.title: Chapter 369: Black Star (2)
paragraphs: My concerns about the GM did not last long. It wasn’t like worrying would help me figure anything out, right? Rather than wasting my time on something pointless, it made more sense to do what I could right now—for example, surfing the web.
Click, click.
Unlike in modern times, web surfing wasn’t simply a fun pastime here. It was a valuable opportunity to gather and aggregate information to survive the next month.
“...Hehe, hehehe.”
Ugh, why is this stuff so funny? It’s hurting my pride.
Click, click.
As my mouse flitted back and forth, scrolling through the posts, hours flew by.
Is it almost time?
The time had come to enter the Round Table.
A white man sitting inside an old-fashioned library threaded his fingers together, lost in thought.
“To think that man was working with Baekho Lee.”

It wasn’t that he hadn’t consider that possibility, but it definitely wasn’t an ideal situation. Baekho, who could only be described as out of control, was stressful enough alone, but this just added to that.
“...Just where did this guy come from?”
Elfnunna joined the community about three years ago. Lion appeared at the Round Table around the same time.
He joined, pretending to be a newbie.
Why did the man enter the community? His combat power was likely no lower than Baekho’s, and judging by the superior information he had access to, it seemed he had established his own faction too.
...Watchers of the Round Table.

At the time, the GM had tentatively concluded that this man’s objective was simply to enter the secret chatroom. The user nicknamed 0720 was an evil spirit from another realm who had secretly infiltrated the community. He was also the whiz who had created the club called Watchers of the Round Table and filled it with big names like Corpse Collector himself. The GM had concluded that Lion must have something to do with that man.
He didn’t seem to know him, though.

He had thought Lion would have some kind of reaction to seeing that chatroom password, but in reality? He had gotten no reaction until the end of the conversation. And when the GM finally mentioned it himself, it made no difference. The man seemed unable to even take a stab at why he was bringing it up.
Well, that may have been another act... But if they really aren’t connected, did he join the community just to be able to contact Baekho more easily? Hmm, that could be the case.
The man reviewed and reconsidered various possibilities.

“I’m sorry. There was a problem on the bulletin board, so I wasn’t able to come immediately when I got your message.” A white woman appeared in the study, the nickname Soul Queen above her head. “So, why did you want to see me?”
The woman sat on the sofa across from him, and the man gave a brief summary of what had just transpired. “Lion. I met with him.”
“...I see. How did it go?”
“He threatened me. To lift the ban on Baekho Lee.”
“So... what are you going to do?”
“Thankfully, he said he would give me three months. I plan to make a decision within that time.”
“But... do you really think he has that kind of power?” she asked cautiously.
This was something the GM had also been debating and worrying about. He knew nothing about the man except for the fact that he was a player from Korea.
Squeeze.
The man subconsciously clenched his fists.
Goddamn Koreans.

It was ridiculously unfair. The GM had only met a few Koreans since creating this community. That was because there were very few who played this game—in terms of numbers alone, their proportion of players was significantly lower than in most Western countries. But when you looked at their performance? Though he had entered the game much later than the GM, Baekho Lee had become a force to be reckoned with. And then there was the new addition of Elfnunna.
Not to mention the chances of Elfnuna being Korean are very high.
At this point, he was even starting to wonder if they were born with special genes or something.
Anyway, I didn’t get to ask why he chose a nickname related to Elfnuna. Well, I guess he wouldn’t have answered, anyway.

The GM believed that whoever cleared the original version of the game before coming into this world was likely to be Elfnuna. While everyone else took the easy way out and enjoyed the modded versions, that person kept slogging through the original.
“Master?” the woman called.

“Ah, I was thinking about something else.” The man returned to the present and gave her orders. “It is as you say, Soul Queen. We don’t have any information about him yet. So, I want you to look into it more actively. Provoke him as little as possible.”
At the man’s instructions, the woman paused for a moment. She usually handled things with confidence, but in that moment her voice was full of reluctance. “...I’ll try.”
Putting on my mask as usual, I crossed the quiet hallway and arrived at the room that housed the Round Table. Everyone was already inside by the time I entered.
“...You’re here! I was worried, pshehe!” Clown, who had apparently been anxious that I might skip the Round Table this month, stood up and welcomed me.

When my eyes met Queen’s, she awkwardly glanced away. Well, considering what happened last time, and since my meeting with the GM earlier would have already reached her ears by now, I got it. When I sat down, I noticed Fox was across from me. She acknowledged me with a look as soon as our eyes met.
“Tsk.” I felt a constant disappointment when I looked at her. If I hadn’t suddenly been transported to the past, I could have used that situation she was in to uncover her identity.

“Um...” While I was busy trying to bite back my displeasure, Fox cautiously spoke up. “Did I do something wrong...?” At first, I wondered what she was talking about, but I quickly realized what it was.
Oh, it’s because I clicked my tongue.

Just like how if you threw stones willy-nilly, sometimes you killed a frog by accident, it seemed like Fox and the others were scrambling to figure out why I was mad at her. I made no effort to clear up this misunderstanding.
“Hm.” It was an ambiguous answer that neither confirmed nor denied anything. Fox gulped at that. She seemed to think she’d made some kind of mistake without realizing it.
Welp, that makes me feel a bit bad... Let’s just change the subject.
“Then let’s begin.”
Just in time, open entry came to an end and the door to the Round Table closed, so the others stopped worrying about whatever mistake Fox supposedly made and focused on the present.
“I’m already looking forward to how interesting the discussion will be this time, pshehe.”
“Then I guess we’re starting over there?”

At Crescent’s question, all eyes turned to Deer, who was situated on my left. This was an unspoken rule of the Round Table. The round had to start from my left so I would go last. These guys revealed their information first, and my job was to listen to it, judge it, and then reveal corresponding information.
Whew, I really did establish a good position for myself.

“...I’ll go first.” Deer kicked things off by calmly presenting the information he had prepared. “The National Incorporation of Evil Spirits bill was brought up in a royal assembly again for the first time in 150 years. Of course, the motion was immediately removed from the agenda due to overwhelming opposition.” It was a short tidbit that was difficult to understand unless you’d worked in public office.
What does that mean?
I had no clue. Of course, that wasn’t a problem. Whenever I faced a lack of knowledge, there was always a guy who took the initiative to help me out.
“National Incorporation bill...?” Goblin asked, his voice small.

Soul Queen stepped in to explain. “The proposal is to not condemn evil spirits as the enemy, but rather embrace and accept them as subjects. It was proposed once 150 years ago, but struck down for various reasons.”
“I-I see... But it’s very surprising to hear something like that from the palace...”
“Pshehe, it sounds to me like they’re low on manpower—”
“I don’t know. At the very least, this proves you know nothing about the palace’s manpower.”
“...Why are you always picking fights with me?”
“Oh my, so self-conscious. I only spoke the truth.”
When Soul Queen laughed breezily, Clown shut up. He was strangely weak against her. Was it because she already gave him a couple of verbal beatdowns?
That bastard is the embodiment of a coward...
Anyway, Deer’s information received a green light on the first attempt, marking a promising start to the meeting, and we immediately moved on to the next person.
This time, it was Goblin. “Ahem, a few days ago, the Church of Reatlas received a prophecy.”
“You’re... not finished, are you?”
“Haha, of course not. Anyway, when I looked into it, the contents were quite strange.”
“Why don’t you stop dragging it out and just get to the point? It only makes you look ridiculous, pshehe.”

At Clown’s accusation, Goblin glanced at him as if to ask why he always bullied him before finally getting to the point. “‘The king’s blood bears a black star, so help the one who will become its master.’ That was the prophecy.”
Reatlas was the Goddess of the Stars. As this was a prophecy from a god who governed fate and the future of souls, there was plenty of room for interpretation.
“A black star, huh? Could that be referring to treason?”
“I think it could be interpreted as the king having secret communication with Noark.”
“But... ‘help the one who will become its owner?’”
“Perhaps it means the queen is pregnant. And the kid is Black, pshehe!”
“...Must you always be so offensive?”
“Why? What’s wrong with being Black? Was I being racist?” Clown cackled like he’d told a hilarious joke, but the reactions of the people around him were cold.
This son of a bitch clearly never had any friends. That’s why he was playing Dungeon and Stone... God damn it.

I stopped that train of thought there because I sensed that it could wreck my self-esteem. Just in time, the conversation around the prophecy wrapped up. Most prophecies were like that—no matter how much effort you put into interpreting them, in the end, you only found out what they really meant later.

“It’s my turn now.” The third turn was Crescent’s. He used to bring us epic information about the Genesis Treasures, but there hadn’t been anything like that recently. Unfortunately, today was more of the same.
Jeez, he always tries to get through his turn with information on the war. Well, I guess it’ll still come in handy someday.
Since I wasn’t leading a clan, though, it was difficult to get much out of this information. In that sense, next.

“The palace has begun passing on military ship manufacturing technology to the civilian population. It seems it was unavoidable since they needed help to repair damaged military ships in a timely manner. There’s a chance we’ll see large clans traveling on military ships soon.” Fox’s information was just like Crescent’s. It was in line with her interests and she explained its implications logically, but that was all.
This round was mediocre, though maybe it’s because it’s the first.
If there was anything of interest, it was the information about the prophecy and the motion raised in the palace meetings.
Accept evil spirits, huh? Will that ever happen?
Even as I entertained the thought, I didn’t have high expectations. Deer said so himself: it was mentioned only once and quickly disappeared from the agenda thanks to the opposition.
“Pshehe, then it’s my turn.”
We were now halfway through the round, meaning it was Clown’s turn. Unfortunately, his information was not helpful to me, either. Rather, it made my life harder.

“Lighthouse Keeper is dead.” Starting with something everyone here knew about, Clown proceeded to rat on me to the Round Table. “The public thinks it was the work of Blood Spirit, but in reality, that’s completely wrong. It wasn’t Blood Spirit, but a strange man that wild woman brought along with her.”
“...Strange man?”
“Yes, at first I thought she was just dragging him along as a replacement for Bjorn Yandel when I saw he had Orc Hero’s Giantization.”
“Riehen Schuitz. The palace is also keeping an eye on him.”

“Pshehe, was that his name? Anyway, I want information about this man at the next Round Table, so I’ll go into more detail. I don’t know where this guy came from, but he is an outrageous monster that even the four of us couldn’t kill together. Pshehe.”
“...Someone like that exists?”
“Wait, the Golden Wizard didn’t say anything like that in her report. Are you certain?”
“If not, would the green light have come on?”
The members of the Round Table were astonished and expressed a deep interest in Clown’s words.
Ugh, what should I do about these bastards who all want to investigate me now?
I sighed inwardly.
What the—why is this woman looking at me?

I felt eyes on me, and when I discreetly glanced in the direction I sensed them, I could see Soul Queen had her gaze locked on me. For some reason, she was muttering something to herself at a volume only I, the person beside her, could hear.
“Giantization... joined three years ago... Blood Spirit...”

Had she noticed something? No, it was likely she’d hit the final stage of puzzle solving where you put the last pieces in place, the solution almost within your reach. But it seemed she wasn’t the only one who was picking up on the fact that something was off here.
It started with Goblin. “Wait, what if it’s not a substitute but really him? Giantization is not a common skill. You said he even had an Ogre’s essence...”
Fox nodded. “Even someone like Blood Spirit wouldn’t go so far as to hire a standin and call him the same name she called him...”
Clown laughed their suspicions off. “Pshehe, what are you all talking about? Bjorn Yandel is dead.”
“What if he’s alive? And has grown stronger without anyone knowing? Then it would make sense that the Golden Wizard omitted this from her report,” Deer said, almost to himself.
“That makes sense. After all, he was exposed as an evil spirit not long after his disappearance. It’s possible he faked his own death for that reason,” Crescent theorized.
“If Bjorn Yandel really is alive...” Queen glanced at me. “That period overlaps with the period during which Mr. Lion disappeared.”

At that moment, all eyes turned to me. Are you Bjorn Yandel? they wanted to ask, but having had bad experiences with me in the past, they couldn’t bring themselves to open their mouths and openly question me.
Well, I’d considered the possibility of this happening. Now that it was, I didn’t feel particularly cornered. That was because all I needed was one good alibi, right?

“That again?” I placed my hand on the Round Table’s jewel and said, “Since it seems everyone is curious about me, I’ll go before Soul Queen this time.” My tone was mocking, like I found their suspicions amusing. “The first time I came to this community was twenty-two years ago.”
The green light came on.

chapters.title: Chapter 370: Black Star (3)
paragraphs: Lion was Bjorn Yandel. This idea was first raised at the Round Table by Soul Queen. The basis for the theory was the fact that Lion had disappeared immediately after Bjorn Yandel’s death.
So, to put it simply... I just have to find an alibi.
Lion was not Bjorn Yandel. The moment this sentence became fact, all of those suspicions would lose most of their weight.
“You said he even had an Ogre’s essence.”
“Even someone like Blood Spirit wouldn’t go so far as to hire a standin and call him the same name she called him...”
“Then it would make sense that the Golden Wizard omitted this from her report.”
“It’s possible he faked his own death for that reason.”
In the end, these suspicions were all derived from the possibility that Lion was Bjorn Yandel. Clown’s reaction was proof of that.
“Pshehe, what are you all talking about? Bjorn Yandel is dead.”
Because he believed there was no way Lion was Bjorn Yandel, he was the only one not to give credence to the theory.
Huh, this guy really has two sides.
When I ran into him outside all I wanted to do was bash his head in, but surprisingly he was almost cute at the Round Table.
Ah, now’s not the time to be thinking about that. Looks like these guys are slowly coming to their senses.
Fox was the first to open her mouth and break the heavy silence. “...Twenty-two... years ago?” Her voice contained an immense shock that couldn’t be described in words alone. Well, that made sense.
“Um... i-is that possible? That means Mr. Lion has been in this world for over twenty years...”
When Goblin trailed off, Deer smoothly offered his two cents. “It’s not unfounded. The general consensus is that the GM was brought to this world around then as well.”
That meant that in their minds, it was safe to say that I had been here about as long as the GM, who as far as everyone knew was the player who had been here the longest.
“Pshehe, so if I kill people for ten more years, can I become like you, Mr. Lion?”
Hm, so I guess Clown has been here for about ten years already. And it looks like the others are in a similar boat.

“But Queen, why are you so quiet? Pshehe.” Clown mocked Soul Queen for barking up the wrong tree. “Shouldn’t you bow down and apologize? For spreading the ridiculous rumor that Mr. Lion is Bjorn Yandel?” Clown seemed to be enjoying being the only person who was right, and he glanced around at the other members. “You guys are the same! Bjorn Yandel? Even if that bastard is still alive, do you think he’s any match for Mr. Lion? Huh?”
“Hahaha... it was just a thought. We didn’t actually think that...” Goblin laughed awkwardly.
Deer, on the other hand, didn’t shirk responsibility and instead reflected on his actions. “Now that I think about it... it would be a big leap to assume Bjorn Yandel is alive.”
“To be honest, I still can’t believe that man was an evil spirit. There’s something a bit suspicious about the royal family’s proclamation... I’ve seen that guy in person.”

Fox has met me in person? In that case, she would have to have been one of the high-ranking people who escaped through a portal that day, no? Hmm, or maybe she just ran into me by coincidence some other time?
I’ll think it over later...
Clown backed Fox up. “Pshehe, I agree with you there. How could that blockheaded barbarian be an evil spirit? How does that make sense?”
This time, even Deer, who was on bad terms with Clown, expressed his assent. “True... it’s hard to interpret what he did at the title bestowal ceremony as an act.”
“You mean how he pushed Marquess Kudo in front of the prime minister and so many nobles?”
“Haha, I heard about that afterward. I heard he yelled something about how the marquess used him to do a somersault, right?”
How embarrassing. How am I supposed to react to receiving such high praise straight to my face? Anyway, I think that should have dispelled all the suspicions...
As I was looking around the table, I could see Soul Queen had tuned out the conversation around her.
What is she thinking so hard about?

As I was studying her, Clown changed the subject. “Ms. Queen, how long are you going to just sit there? It’s your turn now. Can’t you see Mr. Lion is waiting?” It seemed that was how he had chosen to interpret the way I was staring at Soul Queen.
Man, he’s like a professional minion. Why is he so eager to speak on my behalf?

“A-Ah! Yes. Right... I should go...” Anyway, I guessed Clown’s prodding worked because Soul Queen seemed to come to her senses as she took a breath and slowly parted her lips. “The palace already knows the GM’s identity.”
Well, that was an interesting piece of information.

The Magic Engineer, Yurven Havellion, was the head of a magical school and a role model for many construct-type wizards. But that was only who he seemed to be on the surface. In reality, he was the GM, the head of a community of evil spirits called Ghost Busters, and a legend among players. That was his true identity.
Shaaaaaa!
The light on the Round Table turned green, confirming that Soul Queen’s information was accurate and the majority of the people in the room hadn’t been aware of it.
“The palace knows his identity, huh?”
That could only mean one thing. Not only had the palace intentionally let the GM off easy...
“That means it’s highly likely that the GM and the palace are working together in some capacity.”

It could definitely be interpreted that way. That would also explain why he seemed to disregard the threat of the palace entirely while confronting me. So why did Soul Queen reveal this at the Round Table? The reason for that soon became clear.
“Pshehe, so the GM was one of them the whole time. No wonder rumors about him never seemed to spread in the city, no matter what kind of fuss people kicked up.”
This was probably a way of advising and warning me that there was no point in spreading rumors, so I shouldn’t waste my breath.
“Wait, but isn’t that strange? The GM himself called the palace our enemy, right?”

When Goblin pointed out that contradiction, Crescent responded with a cynical smile. “There is nothing more foolish than believing in forever. Especially when it comes to people.” Maybe Goblin’s statement would have been true if this were the GM in the early days, but now, no one could know if he was still an innocent party.
“If this gets out, the community itself could disappear,” Deer lamented.

“Yeah. If news gets out that the GM has joined forces with the palace, all players will live in fear. Including me.” When Fox looked at Soul Queen, the other members naturally shifted their attention to her as well. “Ms. Queen, tell us. You are part of the admin team, right? Why did the GM join forces with the palace?”
“I can’t tell you that.”
“Then I’ll take that as you saying we should come to our own conclusions—”

“But I can tell you this one thing with confidence.” Soul Queen cut Fox off. “If this round is over, I’ll start this time.” She placed her hand on the Round Table’s jewel. “The GM is someone who puts players above all else. He would never sacrifice another player to the palace. Such a thing isn’t possible with the way this community functions in the first place.”
The moment she finished speaking and took her hand off the jewel, a green light began to glow.

“Haha, I feel a bit relieved now that you’ve said that.” Goblin laughed, breaking the silence like he was uncomfortable with the awkward tension in the air. With that, everyone stopped interrogating Soul Queen.
“It’s a good thing it’s functionally impossible.”

In fact, that was probably the most decisive factor. The GM could change his mind later, but their anxieties were abated by the knowledge that the worst could be averted thanks to the systems in place.
“True, if the GM had the ability to learn our real-world identities, this conversation wouldn’t be happening in the first place...”
“It seems he has a give-and-take relationship with the palace rather than one where he works for them.”
“Then it’s your turn now.” Soul Queen did not seem to want to keep talking about this, and she hurriedly ended the conversation by passing off the baton to Clown.

“Pshehe, it’s been such an interesting start...” Clown made a show of trailing off like he was going to pass, but it seemed he came up with something suitable soon enough. “Aha, this should be good!” Clown clapped his hands exaggeratedly and then placed one of them on the jewel. “I also learned this recently and it’s quite a surprising tidbit.”
“Earlier, you called me ridiculous for dragging things out.”
“Pshehe, but you and I are different, Mr. Goblin.” Clown waved him off, and even Deer nodded.
“Why are you nodding?” Goblin whined, clearly hurt, but no one at the Round Table paid attention to him. That was because Clown had begun speaking, finally breaking the mounting tension.
“The Dark Continent is a real place.” The information Clown provided was hard to wrap my head around.
“...It’s a green light.”
“But what does that mean? I don’t understand what you mean by that.”

“Pshehe! It’s just as I said! Literally! After leaving the city and wandering around outside for a while, it hit me. There may be differences in the topography and structure, but the land we are standing on looks exactly like the Dark Continent on the seventh floor!”
This was information that piqued the curiosity of the gamer in me for the first time in a long time.
“...If that’s true, then that means that theory may be true as well.”
“The theory that the labyrinth isn’t a passage connecting to another dimension, but one purposefully crafted by someone?”
“The Crystal Cave and the Rock Desert... perhaps they were modeled after real places.”
If that was true, it was a bit ironic. Someone designed this labyrinth based on this world, and that labyrinth was then used to design a game.
I want to know about the outside world too...
I wondered if there would come a day when I could explore out there.
The second round proceeded smoothly in reverse order without any red lights, but unfortunately, that was all I could say about it.
Queen’s and Clown’s were good, but the rest of the information was so-so.

Regardless of objective value, the information was not personally useful to me. Just look at Fox. She received a green light for sharing the fact that Blood Spirit purchased a mansion for a large sum and that that mansion was used as collateral to borrow another large sum. Crescent? He sighed and said that it seemed Blood Spirit used that money to purchase an essence.
“She got him a happy home and even an essence... Pshehe, that woman is dedicated! It’s not like she can bring Bjorn Yandel back to life by doing all that.”
The reactions of the others were a bit hurtful.
“...Riehen Schuitz. I’ll have to look into him, but I don’t think he’s normal.”
“I-I heard he’s strong, though. It’s not easy to get that strong with just a few essences...”
“It’s always the people who have more power who are worse. Using a woman’s pain for his own personal gain is a blight against all men.”
“My, you’re a romantic, huh, Mr. Deer?”
“Ahem...”
“The elves will have to look into it as well. We only knew she bought an essence, but we never thought she’d give it to a total stranger...”

Ugh, they’re going to conduct all sorts of investigations into me after this. I’ll be able to rest way easier if I can just get my hands on those documents from the Adventurers’ Guild... It seems I’ll have to find a solution to that as soon as possible.
“Haha, it’s already my turn!”
Anyway, Goblin and Deer, who went after that, were similar in terms of usefulness. Their information wasn’t related to me, unlike the previous two, but I didn’t deem it helpful.
Well, it can’t always be useful.

I glanced around, letting go of my regrets. Was it because it was already my turn? The mood in the hall was a little different from before. Eyes gathered on me in anticipation of what information I’d bestow on them this time. Even the sound of breathing couldn’t be heard in the deathly quiet room.
What should I do?
I thought it over one last time, but I decided to stick with what I had already decided to share. I opened my mouth. “I have met Auril Gavis, the creator of Dungeon and Stone.”
Mm-hmm, it was best to hammer things home so that no one would ever think Lion was Bjorn Yandel.
“Whew, I’m tired...”
As soon as I returned to Hansu’s room, I threw myself on the bed and replayed what happened at the Round Table in my mind.
It’s been a while since we’ve done three rounds.
Even after completing two rounds, another round had ensued. There was some useful information, but most wasn’t.
“It’s not like Mr. Goblin leaving makes a difference, so why don’t we continue?”
“I don’t think anything interesting will come of that.”

Ignoring Clown’s disappointed look, I heartlessly stood up. That was because, without Goblin, the ratio needed to get the majority would go down. Even if I wasn’t the one to take the initiative, one or two of the others would have bowed out, as always. So I had decided it was best for me to leave first.
...There wouldn’t have been any quality information, anyway. Okay, my brain’s finally working after that break. I should spend the remaining time surfing the web.
Click, click.
After getting up from bed, I roamed the community and read forum posts.
“Heh, these weird assholes...” Why were these trolls so funny? What the hell was going on in their brains? “Hehehe...”
I was in the middle of surfing the web, one leg propped up on the table, when I saw it.
I quickly sat up. Even after I rubbed my eyes and moved my face close to the monitor, the text on the screen didn’t change.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 1 person is online.]

Online? Who is it? Could it be Baekho? No, the GM couldn’t have dropped the ban already... Even if he did, it’d be impossible for him to come online right now. Is it just a bored person? Or a real Korean? There could be a Korean in the recent batch of newbies. Whatever the case, I’ll find out once I meet them.
With that thought in mind, I double-clicked the mouse.
Click, click.

Everything went white and my surroundings changed. Unlike the default chatroom skin, which was an empty lot, the interior of this one looked like an elaborate mansion. This place had been decorated by Baekho, the chat’s moderator, himself.
What, it’s a woman?

I could see the back of a woman sitting in front of the fireplace. It was hard to determine her nationality from the nickname above her head—HS123—but based on her hair and skin color alone, she was definitely Asian.
Hmm, then is she really Korean? Well, I’ll find out once we talk.

I was more comfortable with men, but that didn’t mean women weren’t welcome. And if it really was someone from home, I was also willing to extend something of a helping hand just as Baekho did for me. With that in mind, I announced my presence.
“Ahem.”

“Kyaaa!” The woman sitting down jumped, her shoulders flying up to her ears. It looked like she hadn’t even noticed I was in the chatroom. The tell-tale air of a newbie radiated off of her, impossible to imitate. “...Huh?” The startled woman turned around, and we made eye contact.
“Uh.”
The woman’s eyes went wide. Actually, my eyes were probably no different.
“Huh?!”
What is this? Is this a dream? Why is she here?
My brain shorted out. My jaw hung there like a goldfish’s, and none of the sounds that tumbled out of my mouth were coherent enough to be classified as ‘language.’ The same went for the woman.
“U-Uh.”
“Uh?”
Still, she was quicker to recover. “Hansu...?” The woman looked more shocked than happy to see me.
“Hyeonbyeol...?” I asked in a daze, my eyes automatically sliding down. She was wearing a formal skirt that went down to her knees, a neat blouse, and... “Ha...you’re exactly the same.”
She was wearing black stockings.

chapters.title: Chapter 371: Black Star (4)
paragraphs: Hyeonbyeol Kang was four years my junior, and my ex-girlfriend. She confessed to me first while we were both struggling in our job search, and we dated for about three years. Well, none of that was important right now.
Slide.
I lifted my gaze again and faced Hyeonbyeol head-on. For some reason, she had a cold look in her eyes. The reason for that was probably...
“You’re really going to look down there in this situation?”
“Ahem...”
It was a reflex, what can you do?
I quickly came to my senses and rushed to set the record straight. “Don’t get me wrong. I was just checking.”
“Checking?”
“The default clothing here is based on how you picture yourself.”
“Then... are you saying this is how I think of myself?”
“Yeah.”

If you wanted to put on different clothing, you had to purchase it with GP. That was how I purchased the athletic wear and short-sleeved shirt I was wearing right now. The default clothing had been a bit uncomfortable.
“Then what about you? What was your basic outfit?”
It had been a tight-fitting navy suit, clothes that my ex-girlfriend—so, Hyeonbyeol—bought me.

“What I’m wearing right now. This was my default outfit.” It would be kind of embarrassing to tell her the truth. If I told her I was wearing that suit even though we had broken up a long time ago, it would seem like I still had feelings for her.
“...Hmm, that’s very like you.” Thankfully, Hyeonbyeol didn’t doubt me and easily accepted my answer. But that raised more questions.
“Like me? What about it is like me?”
“Why are you being so sensitive? I just meant you look comfortable.”
“R-Really?”
Ugh, I can’t relax around her. Is it because of my past sins?
“Anyway... don’t you have something to say to me?”
“...It’s been a while, Hyeonbyeol!”
“That’s it?”
What more could there be? Ah, wait, I didn’t ask her about that.
“So, how did you end up here?”

Hyeonbyeol glared silently at my question before sighing in resignation. “You still haven’t fixed your habit of running away.” I just pretended not to hear that. “It’s fine. None of that is important now...”
“Right. The past isn’t important. I think there’s even a saying that says the present is more precious than gold—” The air in the room seemed to get colder and I shut my mouth.
“Why did you stop? Keep going.”
“I just... think I should apologize first. I’m sorry about back then. Truly.”
When I apologized, erasing all traces of humor from my tone, Hyeonbyeol looked slightly surprised. “You’ve... kind of changed.”
“Well, yeah... So, are you going to accept my apology?”
“I don’t need an apology. Like I said earlier, none of that is important now. It’s not something either of us need to apologize for, either...”
“That’s...true.”

After that brief exchange, an awkward silence fell between us. I mean, it made sense considering I’d been reunited with my ex-girlfriend, who I broke up with over a year ago in the real world, in this faraway one.
“But I’m really surprised. I never dreamed of seeing you here.”
“Really? I always thought we would run into each other someday.”
“I’ve been thinking about it ever since I woke up here. That you must be somewhere in this world too. It was a bit of a relief.”
“A relief...?”
“Because of the news about your disappearance. I was really surprised when I heard you were gone. I wondered whether you had gotten a bad idea stuck in your head...”
Ah, I could see how it could have seemed that way. But I was kind of touched that she worried about me even though we had been broken up for over a year at that point.
“So... how did you end up here?” This was already my third time asking this because the conversation kept going off the rails. “You’re the furthest thing from a gamer...”
Fortunately, Hyeonbyeol answered properly this time. “Um... I started to get interested after we broke up. I was wondering how good this game could possibly be that you were so obsessed with it.”
That was new. Back when we were dating, she used to scold me for using three monitors to play the game.
No, wait.
“Then... you beat the original?”
“Come on, how could I beat that thing? After you went missing, I found the modded version and played that.”
“Then... what version did you beat?”
“Thirty times.”
“Thirty times...?” That was considered first-rate. There were plenty of people in this world who couldn’t even beat that. “Looks like you worked pretty hard on it...”
“Oh, no, I think I beat it after ten tries. Maybe because I switched over from playing the original version. I learned a lot watching you play in the past too.”
“Ah...” Come to think of it, I always bragged to her when I found a hidden feature. Since she was a smart girl, she would have remembered it all.
“Why did your face darken all of a sudden?”
“...You can tell?”
“Of course. We were together for a long time.”

I thought it over for a moment before deciding to be honest. “It’s nothing. It’s just that now that I think about it, you constantly listened to me talk about something you wouldn’t have been interested in and you never complained...” I trailed off awkwardly.
It was only after a short pause that Hyeonbyeol answered. “...You’ve really changed a lot.”
“It’s been a long time.”
“That’s... yeah, true...”

There was another beat of awkward silence, but it was short-lived. When I asked if she knew what happened after I went missing, Hyeonbyeol filled me in. To give a brief summary, it was like this: a month in, my company reported me as missing and the police came to talk to her, which was how she found out.
“You met my mom?”
“Yes. At the police station.”
“What did that woman say...?”
“I didn’t speak to her directly.”
“But something happened. It’s okay, tell me.”

Hyeonbyeol seemed to consider her words carefully before hesitantly opening her mouth. “She talked about the inheritance for a while... then she asked the police if there was a way to report someone as dead before the missing persons report expired.”
“Ha...” I had pretty much expected that, but it still felt shitty. It wasn’t like I had that much money saved up anyway. This was probably my own fault for getting my hopes up.
Grit.

As I tensed my jaw without realizing it, Hyeonbyeol offered words of comfort. “S-Still, you have five years. Since it wasn’t an accident and there was no evidence of a crime, it wasn’t classified as a special disappearance.”
“What’s the difference?”
“In a special disappearance case, the inheritance can be transferred after one year.”
“I see.” That did comfort me a little. And as soon as I had the thought, I was struck by how funny this was.
Chuckle.

This kind of reassurance was very like Hyeonbyeol. Come to think of it, she always comforted me by pointing out the concrete positives in a situation rather than just expressing words of sympathy. She played a significant role in shaping my current personality.
“So what next?”
“I don’t know. After you went missing, I was brought here three months later.”
“What...?”

I was genuinely surprised. Though the Fragment of Records Stone had complicated things in my own personal timeline, if you ignored that and looked solely at the calendar, it had been four years and one month since I became Bjorn Yandel.
Since the time ratio is five to one... that means nearly ten Earth months have passed since I went missing.

In other words, Hyeonbyeol would have been summoned here around the year New World 154. That summer was eventful in many ways. For one thing, it was around the time those pillars of fire exploded in Dimension Square.
As I took this in, a thought occurred to me. “But why did you only join the community now? If you were summoned back then, that means you’ve been in the city for almost three years.”
“I’m not an adventurer. I guess I wasn’t noticeable.”
“You’re not an adventurer...?”
“Yes. How can I fight monsters like that in real life just because I beat a game? I found a job at a decent place to make money.”
“If you’re saying that, that must mean you’re human.”
“I guess that means you’re not?”
I was rendered mute by Hyeonbyeol’s question. I was worried about sharing personal information like this.
It seemed she sensed my brief hesitation. “So, you don’t want to tell me.”

Hyeonbyeol’s eyes creased. This was a look I had seen several times when we were dating. Whenever it appeared, that meant I had to do whatever I could to soothe her anger, but there was no need for that anymore. Strictly speaking, we were strangers now. There was no way Hyeonbyeol, who had always been a logical person, wouldn’t be aware of that.
“For the record, you drew the line first, okay?”
“Okay.”

“...Fine. I won’t ask you anything like that from now on. Okay?” Hyeonbyeol accepted my refusal with her usual cool. But it seemed she was still kind of disappointed. “In exchange, don’t even think about asking about me. I won’t tell you anything.”
Welp, yeah, that’s fair.
I couldn’t argue with that so I nodded without hesitation. Hyeonbyeol pursed her lips at that. “I guess you really aren’t curious, then.”

“If you tell me, I’d have to tell you mine too.” Instead of trying to sidestep, I gave her an honest explanation. The fact was, she knew my exact date of entry. If I told her even just my race, she’d be able to narrow down the list of people I could be drastically.
Silence stretched between us as we stared at each other.
“...Let’s sit for a bit.”
“...Yes, that’s a good idea.”
It was awkward to keep standing so we sat on the nearby sofa. Once we sat, there was nothing for us to really talk about, so I just started with something light.
“This is your first time in the community, right?”
“Yes.”

If she lived a normal working life in this world, how had she received an invitation? I was curious about that but I swallowed down the urge to ask. “I can give you some GP if you need it. You can exchange it for cash if you want.”
“It’s fine. I can earn enough on my own. Besides, if I cash it out, real-world money will be moved. That runs the risk of my identity being revealed, no?”
“That’s... true.” To be honest, I only said that as an icebreaker—if she actually agreed and expressed a desire to cash it out, I would have stopped her from doing so immediately.
“You... must be an adventurer, then.”

“I am.” Though we decided not to say anything that could reveal our identities to each other, I confirmed it. If I refused even a vague question like that, we wouldn’t be able to have a conversation at all. “But why are you smiling?”
“Just ‘cause. I... can’t imagine you in a bloody fight against monsters.”
“You get used to it.”
“It must have been tough.”
“And you?”
“I’m all right. Work is easier here, actually.”
True, she was the smartest person I’d ever met. She must have adapted quickly.

“Really. Since they’re not properly digitized, it was easy to raise capital in the early days.” By ‘raise capital,’ did she mean embezzlement? “Maybe it’s because the market itself is poorly designed, but when I officially started investing money, the rate of return was pretty good. Wait.”
“Now that I think about it, why don’t we stop beating around the bush and just get together?”
“Haha, get together...? We already—”
“No, not get back together—let’s join forces. I can give you both material and emotional support.”
“You’ll help me?”
“My next goal after ensuring my financial freedom was to gain power. And recently, I’ve made a connection with a powerful person. I can use that to support you.”
“What do you want in return?”
“Isn’t that obvious? When you figure out a way to return, I want in on it. I’m sure your goal is to get home too, right?”
“Return, huh...?”
When I trailed off, Hyeonbyeol’s expression shifted as she picked up on the fact that something was off. “...Are you thinking of staying here?”
I saw no reason to deny it. “Even if I go through hell and back to return, there’s nothing waiting for me there.”
“What about your mother?” she demanded.
“Huh? My mom?”
“If you stay here, all the deposit money for your apartment will go to her!”
Oh, that’s what you meant.
“Woah, that’s actually kind of motivating.”
When I laughed, Hyeonbyeol raised her voice. “Don’t try to make a joke out of this! Are you really going to live here?”
“Why are you getting so worked up? It’s not like I can’t live here. You know something? I’ve made more friends here than I ever did in that world.”
I was only trying to lighten the mood, but Hyeonbyeol’s mouth snapped shut and all she did was stare at me in shock. Then, after a long pause, she finally pried it back open to shout, “Friends? You?”
Uh... That reaction is hurtful even by my standards.

chapters.title: Chapter 372: Black Star (5)
paragraphs: Surprisingly, talking to Hyeonbyeol was easy. Considering our relationship and the fact that we were both hiding things, I thought it would be much more awkward.
She never crosses a line once someone draws it, which is very convenient.

The economy, culture, politics, and administration—there were plenty of topics we could connect on without figuring out each other’s identities, and so we spent a good chunk of time discussing those things freely.
“The library... we might have seen each other once or twice in passing.”
“Do you go often as well?”
“Just when I have time.”
“True, there’s no better way to get information than books.”
When I checked the time, I saw that about two hours had passed since I first stumbled across Hyeonbyeol.
Wow, I didn’t even notice the time. What should we talk about next?
While I was thinking about this, Hyeonbyeol spoke cautiously. “But hey...”
“Yeah, what is it?”
“What kind of people are your friends?”
I tilted my head at her. “...Why are you asking that all of a sudden?”
“I’m just curious,” Hyeonbyeol replied nonchalantly. “Since it was actually your fault that you didn’t have any friends.”
“...Huh? You’re just going to upper-cut me out of the blue like that?” I asked, dazed.

Hyeonbyeol scrambled to clarify. “No, that’s not what I meant... I just meant that your criteria for having friends was always whether you considered them a friend or not. In reality, there were probably a lot of people who thought of you as a friend. You know, those people who message you every New Year’s or on birthdays.”
“Hey, those aren’t friends. They’re acquaintances.”
“That’s what I’m saying. It’s your way of thinking that’s the problem.”
I had a lot to say to that but I didn’t argue with her because I could see what she was trying to convey.
“That’s why I was surprised. The friends you have now... are people you consider friends too.”
“Yeah...?”
“To be honest, I don’t know what kind of magic was cast on you that you’ve changed so much. What kind of people are they?”
...Is the fact that I have friends now really so strange that she would say this?
That kind of left a bad taste in my mouth, but I still gave her an answer. “They’re trustworthy. To the point where I wouldn’t worry even if they were standing behind me holding a knife.”
“Hmm, so you were able to build a deep trust because you had to fight together with your lives on the line?”
“I guess so?”
“But isn’t that just colleagues, not friends?”
Uh... Yeah, but...
“Considering the society we’re in, colleagues, or comrades, are considered more than just friends but an even closer relationship—”
“So they’re just colleagues.”
I couldn’t reply. Well, what did it matter whether they were friends or colleagues? The key here was that we were important people to each other.
“...What is that?” she asked suspiciously. “That look in your eyes?”
“Come to think of it, you didn’t have any friends, either.”
“There were tons of people who thought of me as a friend, okay?”
I know that, but you’re like me. Someone who cares more about your own thoughts and feelings than what others think.
“So, have you made any friends here?”
“...I don’t need them. I’m going back, anyway.”
“Really? I guess that’s that, then.”
When I chuckled, Hyeonbyeol shot me an indignant look, but it didn’t last long. “Huh?” She suddenly flinched. “I just heard a ding! in my ears.”
“Ah, looks like you got a message.”
“A message...?”
“Did you post something on the Exchange?”
“No, but I did send in a proposal on a post from someone looking to buy information. I thought it would be convenient to earn some GP. How do I check the message?”
“You can’t see it here. You have to see it for yourself on the computer.”
“...Then I guess I’ll have to check it later.”
“Just go see it now. Seeing as the reply came late, it looks like there must have been a message from another seller.”
When I gave her the okay, Hyeonbyeol’s expression brightened. It seemed she also thought this was the most reasonable course of action. “Then I’m sorry. I’ll be back soon.”
“Huh? You’ll be back?”
“...Are you going to leave?”

“If I wait here, you’ll be in a rush to finish. No need to do that. I’ll see you again next time. Besides, you said this is your first time in the community. Instead of being here with me, you should check out the other pages.”
“That’s... true.” As expected, when I made a logical argument, Hyeonbyeol nodded without objection. “Then I’ll see you next month.”
“Yeah, take care of yourself.”
We even exchanged brief goodbyes. Well, they should have been goodbyes, anyway.
“Why aren’t you leaving?”
Hyeonbyeol didn’t answer.
“Ah, you want me to go first? Then—”
Right when I was focusing my mind on leaving the chat, Hyeonbyeol urgently grabbed my sleeve. “Wait! Um.” She averted her eyes, staring off at a random corner of the room. “How do I get out...?”
Huh, no wonder she was alone in this empty chat. She’s strangely dense about the weirdest things.
“Were you...”
...Stuck here because you didn’t know how to get out, not because you were waiting for someone?
“Twenty-two... years ago?” the pale man asked, pressing his lips together.
“Yes,” the woman answered. “That’s what he said. And the jewel on the Round Table turned green. But how? That was before the community was even created, right?”
The man kept his mouth shut. Actually, his mind was more preoccupied with other things—like the masked man he met after taking over the spiritual world from the old man he presumed to be Auril Gavis.
“It’s your choice whether you believe me or not. I just came here to warn you.”
At first, the man pretended to be someone else, but when his ploy was exposed, he gave the GM advice that almost sounded more like a threat.
“So that was your name.”
Then he forcibly learned his name.
“...Master, your hands are shaking.”

The man reflexively lowered his head and saw that his fingertips were trembling slightly. It had already been twenty years, but still. Of course, he knew now that the energy that had constricted his body back then had been murderous intent.
Squeeze.

The man gripped his knees with shaking hands and forced them to stop quivering. As the saying went, ignorance was bliss. At times, it was more terrifying to know something than it was to not know. He couldn’t imagine how many people someone had to kill to be capable of that kind of murderous intent.
But to think that had been Lion...

It had been so long ago that he hadn’t been able to make the connection right away. Now that he thought about it, it all made sense—the fact that Lion knew his name was Yurven Havellion and the ridiculous murderous intent Soul Queen reported.
He said three months...

The GM felt both scared and relieved at the same time. If he had been prideful and immediately disregarded the threat, he might have made an enemy of that man. However, as afraid as he was of him, he needed to know more about him. If Lion really was the strange man he encountered that day twenty-two years ago, what was he after? That would be the key to figuring this out.
It was three years ago that he reappeared in the community.

His nickname was Elfnunna. He was under the impression that he wasn’t an evil spirit from somewhere other than Earth, but there was no way of knowing for sure. The man was too secretive for him to come to any concrete conclusions.
As soon as he entered the community, he met with Baekho Lee, then immediately joined the Round Table.
If so, what was the reason? A clue to that lay in the conversation they had twenty-two years ago.
“Auril Gavis...”
“Isn’t that the name of the game’s creator?”

After the GM took over the community, that man warned him to be wary of Auril Gavis, the old man who passed on his admin rights. This man had dragged them into this world and didn’t feel the slightest bit guilty about it.
“Excuse me. You’re busy thinking.”
Slowly, the thread began to unravel. Lion was Auril Gavis’s enemy.
And the reason he reappeared in the community after twenty years... was because the Master of the Round Table... was Auril Gavis?
Nickname 0720 was the creator of the Watchers of the Round Table, and someone he had assumed was an evil spirit from another realm.
No, there are too many holes in this theory too.
“Soul Queen, you said the Master of the Round Table has visited the Round Table once, is that correct?”
“Yes. I wasn’t there at the time, but that’s what I heard.”
“And the two seemed to be close friends.”
“Yes. Apparently, all the members were surprised because it seemed like a casual relationship.”
“I see...”

The thread looked like it was finally unraveling, but he soon hit another wall. It felt like the more he dug, the more he sank into quicksand. Auril Gavis, Master, Lion, Baekho Lee—the GM had no idea what any of them wanted. No matter how hard he tried to piece it all together, he ran into contradictions due to a lack of information.
Grit.
Still, he knew one thing for sure. Even now, somewhere out there, giants in a league he had no hopes of ever joining were pursuing their own agendas with great determination.
“...At this point, I have no choice but to admit it.”
“Admit what?”

The man pressed his lips together. The admin of the community? The GM? The oldest player? Even if countless players described him like that and looked up to him, that didn’t change the facts. Ultimately, he was nothing more than a weakling compared to these people.
“Soul Queen, it seems a lot of things are happening out of our sight.”
“Yes, I’ve been feeling like that more often lately too.”
“We will have to work harder in the future.” Rather than despairing, the man accepted his shortcomings and moved on.
Then, as if the heavens themselves had decided to honor his resolve, Soul Queen suddenly said, “M-Master! Lion is in the Korean chatroom, and there are two participants—”
“Who is the other person?”
“A user called HS123. Someone I helped onboard earlier. Th-they were Korean!”
“...So it’s a new member from this go-around.” The man hurriedly doled out instructions. “Send them a message. I need to meet with them.”
An opportunity like this may never come again.
It was a small room with a bed to one side and a computer desk to the other. Hyeonbyeol Kang thought this was kind of funny.
“This space is a manifestation of your imagination and sense of self.”

That was what the guide told her when she first entered the community. Although the woman couldn’t see it for herself since Hyeonbyeol’s mental barrier was so thick, apparently this room was based on the first place that came to her mind. It was supposedly the place she thought she should be, or where she felt the most stability.
How funny. To think that’s here.
Hyeonbyeol smiled cheerlessly. She knew this was the place, but the most important part, that person wasn’t here.
“...Focus on doing what you need to do.”
Hyeonbyeol scanned the room before sitting down at the computer desk. After checking the message she received, she frowned.
What the...? This isn’t a message from the buyer.
Setting aside the annoyance she felt, she combed through the contents of the message carefully. This was because of the nickname of the sender.
Soul Queen... that’s the guide woman I met when I first came in.
Hyeonbyeol didn’t know why, but that woman was requesting to meet with her.
Click, click.
Without much hesitation, she entered the password written on the note and entered the chat. A strange man and a familiar woman were seated inside the room.
Elfnunalove? What’s with that nickname?
Hyeonbyeol felt a visceral discomfort from the get-go but she didn’t let it show.
“Hello. Nice to meet you. I am Elfnunalove.”
“Yes. Hello. How can I help you?”
“I have something to discuss with you, Ms. HS123—”
“Please just call me ‘you.’ It’s a bit weird to be called that out loud.”
“Ahaha, I understand. It can be like that.” At Hyeonbyeol’s request, the man burst into a good-natured laugh. She was dumbfounded.
You understand yet chose that nickname?
She studied the man with cool stoicism and quickly made a call.
Anyway, if he’s going to take an overly accommodating stance despite the obvious edge in my voice... There must be a reason for that.

Hyeonbyeol did not intend to underestimate the man in front of her in the slightest. He seemed a bit dopey for some reason, but judging someone by their outward appearance was a foolish thing to do. The woman nicknamed Soul Queen was an administrator, so there was no way the man she was serving as counsel for could be an ordinary person.
Someone who might be the GM personally called to see me, a newbie...
There was no need to think too hard about it. The timing of the message, that creepy nickname, and the strangely submissive attitude... when combined, there was only one possibility.
This has something to do with Hansu.
Her assumptions were correct.
“You are Korean, yes?”
“Um, excuse me, but can we get straight to the point? I don’t have much time.”
“Haha, I understand. This is your first visit, after all. Twelve hours isn’t enough to check everything out.”
Hyeonbyeol didn’t bother answering. And as always, that method proved incredibly effective.
“I see you are a woman of few words. Then I will get straight to the point. What is your relationship to the user Elfnunna?”
“Why should I answer that?”
“I will give you GP.”
“I met him for the first time today. But what about him?”

“Hmm...” The man with the strange nickname of Elfnunalove seemed to contemplate whether or not she was telling the truth before letting her know the reason why he called her here. “I want to buy information on Elfnunna.”
“Are you telling me to investigate him? We met today.”
“Even trivial information is fine. I heard Koreans have a tight bond. If HS123—no, if you approach him, he will let down his guard a little.”
“...And the payment?” Hyeonbyeol asked carefully.
The man’s response was short and to the point. “Anything your heart desires.”
“...And do you know what I desire?”
“Whatever it is, we have the power to make it happen.”

“Is...that true...?” Hyeonbyeol set aside her indifference, the corners of her mouth rising. That was only natural. She had no intention of stepping away from this conversation for the sake of loyalty. That would be a foolish thing to do.
Hansu is such a klutz... I don’t know what he did, but it looks like he ended up with these two on his trail.
Her eyes crinkled.

chapters.title: Chapter 373: Treasure Hunter (1)
paragraphs: Three days after the community closed, while I was spending my days looking for a ship to use on the sixth floor and a navigator to sail it, I received good news from Amelia.
“Schuitz, don’t worry about the guild anymore.”
“Don’t worry?”
“I found someone to deal with the issue.”
“...What?”

Amelia, as it turned out, had handled things in a very Amelia-like way. Apparently, she discovered a guild official who committed a crime that could ruin their life if they were caught, such as embezzlement or tax evasion or something. Using the evidence to threaten them, it seemed she succeeded in destroying all the information on Riehen Schuitz at the guild.
“It would have been much safer to edit the information to say what we want rather than destroy it, but that would have been too difficult.”
“And what about the possibility that the destroyed records could be a problem?”
“Normally, there’s none. Loss of or damage to administrative materials is more common than you’d think.”
Hmm, is that so?
I nodded, and Amelia added that not all of the documents on Riehen Schuitz had been destroyed and that the forms designating him as rank five remained. Put simply, I could keep my rank-five status.
“You seem vaguely unsatisfied.”
“I’m just worried it might seem strange that my documents suddenly disappeared, no matter how common it is for that to happen.”
“But it’s better than leaving them lying around.”
Well, that was true. Though it might be difficult to dispel any suspicion that came my way, at least now the physical evidence wouldn’t end up in the hands of people who were after me.
“Good job... no, thank you. Amelia.”
“...It’s only natural to do well at something you’re good at.”
“Because it’s more efficient that way, right?”
Amelia nodded and changed the subject. “So, how did it go on your end? Did you read through all the materials I gave you?”
Ah, the ship list. It was a document that neatly summarized the specifications and prices of ships on the market.
“If there aren’t any you like, tell me as soon as possible so that I can look for more.”

“No, there’s no need. As long as the listing is the same as the actual item, there’s something just right.” When I told her which ship I wanted, Amelia asked why and I enthusiastically explained. “It’s the most expensive of the options but in terms of bang for your buck, you could argue it’s cheap.”
“Hmm.”

“Besides, as long as we avoid any special areas, it’s more than enough to take us to the seventh floor in our current state. And if we add customizations later, we’ll be able to sail to special areas just fine, meaning we won’t have to find another ship.”
“I see,” Amelia answered emotionlessly. I wondered why she bothered asking if she was going to react so blandly. “Well, I’m sure it’s as good as you say. This is what you do best, after all.”
I stuttered involuntarily at those words. “Uh... i-is it?”
“We’re already on the same boat and you’re the captain of it.”

Man, that was the kind of statement that could only make the person on the receiving end blush. But besides that, I also thought, Is she doing this on purpose to boost my ego? Well, lately I’d been stuck at home constantly and asking her for all these favors. Maybe she was being considerate.
“Then if you’ve decided on the ship, I’ll go. If I get moving now, I might be able to put in an offer before the Exchange closes.”
I wanted to ask if she really meant what she said, but I couldn’t because Amelia put on her coat and left through the door. Well, it didn’t matter.
Anyway, that gets us a ship.
If we had a bigger budget, we could have gotten a better ship, but I wasn’t particularly disappointed. The ship we got was a pretty good one.
The problem is the navigator...
From time immemorial, the problem had always been people, not things.
Knock, knock.
As I was reading some books I borrowed from the library in bed, I heard a knock on the door.
Hmm, is it already time to eat?
“Come in.”
As soon as I gave my permission, the door opened as if on cue. As always, the visitor was Erwen. Amelia was in the middle of negotiating for the ship with the seller.
“What is it?” I asked, closing the book.
Erwen looked somewhat displeased. “There’s a guest,” she grumbled curtly.
I tilted my head. “A guest?”

As soon as the question left my lips, a woman with shiny blonde hair and blue eyes appeared in the doorway. “It’s me.” Unlike the last time we met, Raven was in everyday clothes instead of the uniform of the Magic Corps, and her hair was down instead of tied up.
Man, she looks like a completely different person all of a sudden.
“Can I come in?”
“Ah, uh...”
Before I could reply, Raven came into the room and sat down. Erwen followed suit, picking up a chair and sitting far away from us.
“Why are you coming in, Erwen?”
“Can’t I?”
No, I mean... I was just asking why... Well, whatever. She won’t disturb us from that distance.
“It’s been a while, Raven.”
“Yes. How have you been?”
“Fine for now. But is it okay for you to come here like this?”
“Don’t worry, I made sure to be discreet.”
“Ah, is that why you let your hair down and dressed like that?”
“...What other reason could there be?”
Jeez, why is she so touchy? I was just trying to ask if something was wrong. I should be careful about the way I talk to her today.
Just as I was about to ask why she came, Raven spoke first. “Your book.”
“What?”
“You were reading a book. Did you buy it?”
“No, it looks like you can borrow them these days.”
“Ah... I heard about that. It’s now possible for people whose identities are verified to take out books, right?”
“Officially, yes. But in reality, unless you’re a nobleman or a high-ranking government official, you are asked to make a deposit.”
“Though you didn’t need to do that, Mister,” Erwen suddenly jumped into the conversation.
Raven nodded, unphased. “Well, with Ms. Tersia’s status, things like that should be possible.”
“So why did you hide yourself to come all the way here? Did something happen?” I hurriedly asked why Raven was here before the conversation could take a strange turn.
Raven wrapped up the small talk and got down to business. “Mr. Yandel... no, sorry. I try to be careful but I can’t seem to get it to stick.”
“It’s okay.”
“Anyway, I have something to tell you, Mr. Schuitz.”
So, you weren’t just visiting.

I had gotten my hopes up because of how long the small talk was taking. “Tell me? Go ahead.” It didn’t seem like this would be a light conversation, so I lowered my voice and gave her my full attention.
“The palace has launched an informal investigation into you.”
“Informal investigation?”
“It usually happens when new figures appear. If an official investigation is conducted without justification, it would look like the palace trying to control and oppress adventurers.”
Hmm, is this like a background check, then? This is a dictatorship anyway, why do they care what people think?
“Anyway, so?”
“The investigators came to me as well so I disclosed a certain amount of information, as we discussed. I picked only the things that couldn’t be kept hidden, like the abilities you showed that day.”
“But if it’s still an informal investigation, I guess that means there aren’t any suspicions about my identity itself.”
“Yes. If there were, you would have been caught a long time ago. Even if it’s informal, there are times when they don’t look too closely into things, though sometimes it’s the opposite.”
After all, the rumors that the palace was training secret special forces in the shadows weren’t actually rumors. The Order of the Rose was a prime example of that.
“So, what happened to you? To the higher-ups, it’d look like you omitted things from your report.”

“That part is covered. I used the excuse of the position of Third Corps Commander being vacant at the time, which meant I couldn’t provide a full report. I also told them I submitted a report separately to my direct supervisor, Commander Pevrosk.”
“Then won’t you be caught lying?”
“It’s not a lie. I really did submit a report to him as soon as I got back to the city. Of course, it’s partly made up.”
“I see...” While it was reassuring that Raven was always on the ball, on the other hand, I felt a bit guilty. “Sorry for getting you involved in my business, Raven.”
“...I thought we already talked about this. I’m just paying off my past debts.”
“I’ll make sure to pay this back too.”

“Yes, you absolutely have to. Otherwise, I’ll take a huge loss.” The mood could have taken a solemn turn just then, but Raven responded with a joking tone that somewhat alleviated it. It was time to move on to the next item on the agenda.
“Raven, have you heard anything about the National Incorporation bill?”
“National Incorporation bill? What is that?”
“It’s a proposal to not condemn evil spirits as the enemy but embrace and accept them as subjects instead. It was proposed once 150 years ago but struck from the agenda for various reasons.”
“Ah, I remember learning about it a long time ago. But what about it?”
“Apparently it was discussed at a royal meeting recently.”

When I explained why I brought this up, Raven looked surprised. “This is the first I’ve heard of it. Mr. Schuitz, how did you know that, considering you’ve been at home most of the time...? Oh, right, it was the full moon not long ago!”

One of Raven’s strengths was that there was no need for long explanations with her. I kept going without stopping to either confirm or deny it. “Look into it, will you? Who brought it up at the meeting, and...”
“If there really is no chance the palace will accept that proposal.”
This could turn out to be a turning point.

The days had been pretty busy since Raven’s visit. Well, to be more exact, it wasn’t busy for me at home, but it was busy for Amelia. Although we invested all of our money into purchasing the ship we selected, we hadn’t found a sailor to sail it yet. Sailors were in limited supply these days. Since everyone was taking military ships to head directly to the Dark Continent, I had assumed there would be quite a few up on the market.
“I guess finding one in under a month was a bit of a stretch...”
“Be honest with yourself. You just can’t find someone who fits your standards.”
Hmm, that’s true.

To be honest, there were sailors and navigators out there. The problem was that most of them were amateurs. If we wanted someone who could take us to Burrow Island, which was our next target, we needed sailing skills more than anything.

“Either lower your standards or give up. Not only are people as skilled as that snatched up the moment they’re put on the market, but none of them will want to join our team as a short-term mercenary.”
“Really? Then I’ll give up.”
“That easily...?”
“Well, what can I do? The labyrinth opens in two days. I’ll have to look again next month.”
“Then are you excluding Burrow Island from this expedition?”

“No, let’s try it on our own this time. I don’t know if we’ll manage, but there’s nothing to do on the lower floors anyway.” Even if we didn’t reach Burrow Island, it wouldn’t be a huge loss considering I hadn’t even collected all the XP available at the start of the sixth floor. But did my announcement bother her?
“...You’re not wrong, but this is annoying. If you had come to this conclusion sooner, I wouldn’t have been so busy all month.”
“I’m... sorry about that.”
After giving Amelia a lackluster apology, I called Erwen over to discuss our plans for our next quest. It didn’t take too long. I also made a Plan B in case we really didn’t find a navigator.
“We’re going into a Rift...?”

“Not for long, just briefly. It’s not like it’ll make a huge difference if we get to the sixth floor a little late. We’re not trying to join the military forces this time, either. And by the sounds of it, you guys haven’t gotten any Rift XP, right?”
“That’s because the Rift isn’t the kind of place you can enter whenever you want...”
That was true. That was why I hadn’t been able to openly share how to access Rifts with Team Half-Wit and the team I personally made after that.
Exposing myself as an evil spirit is really convenient in that regard.
“Anyway, that’s enough planning.”
After I shared the plan, we each spent time on self-care, and two more days passed.
