[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
Finally, it was labyrinth entrance day.
“Mister, why are you smiling?”
“I’m just a little excited. Let’s get to the second floor fast.”
This was going to feel like a real quest for the first time in a long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 374: Treasure Hunter (2)
paragraphs: Thirteen hours after we entered the labyrinth, we were in the first floor’s Crystal Cave. The reason we were still on the first floor, which we managed to clear within a few hours last time, was because this quest started here.
“Hmm, I never knew you could open a Rift like this.”
“Hehe, you know everything, Mister!”

Bloody Citadel, Glacier Cave, etcetera—there were four types of Rifts on the first floor, and these Rifts could be deliberately opened by players. As such, the reason why it took so long was also that we first headed up to the second floor to kill some rank-eight monsters, then came back.
Most people should be upstairs by now...
I took out the rank-eight mana stone I had stored in the sub-space and scanned our surroundings.
Anyway, it’s been a long time since I’ve been here too.

It was a cavity with a radius of about a hundred feet and a gravestone sitting in its center. When the army and large clans escaped through those portals that day, this was the very place where the people who were left behind searched for a way to survive. At the time, the wizards had expanded this cavern so the space was much larger.
“Is everyone ready?”
The two nodded at my question, and I took that as a signal to place the mana stone in front of the monument as an offering.
Dddddd!
Vibrations spread through the entire first floor, starting from the monument itself. At the same moment, a green portal opened.
[You have entered the first-floor Rift.]
Okay, let’s go.
Shaaaaaa!
The portal in the air cast light on the outline of a cave. Railroad tracks covered the floor, and wooden waste was scattered around the surrounding area. It was a bit gloomier than in the game.

Green Coal Mine was one of the four types of Rifts that existed on the first floor. The way it worked was simple. Starting from the spot where the ceiling had collapsed and blocked the road, you followed the railroad tracks until you encountered the boss.
“What are you all doing? Let’s go.”

I quickly led the others, who were reflexively scanning their unfamiliar surroundings, into the tunnel. That was because there would be more people joining us in here soon, and it was best not to run into them. Amelia and I were fine, but Erwen had become very famous in the city, after all. Even if they were lower-floor adventurers, there was a possibility they’d recognize her.
Dash.
It was only after we left the radius of the portal’s light and concealed ourselves with the spirit of darkness Erwen summoned that the additional participants entered the Rift.

“W-Woah! W-What is this?” It started with a man in equipment that was clearly low-grade. He looked around dazedly for a moment before realizing he was in a Rift, at which point he grinned. “Am I the first?”
“Woahhh!” A second person jumped out of the portal and tumbled to the ground. It was another man.
“Hehe, nice to meet you!”
Okay, since they’re both men, nothing bad should happen if we leave them alone.
After I watched them exchange greetings, I quickly dispelled my concerns and turned around. “The sound won’t reach them over there. Let’s run.”
“Okay!”

We began running through the tunnel to officially start clearing the Rift. The very first monster we encountered was, of course, a goblin. This one had a slightly different physique than the guys I was used to seeing on the first and second floors.
“Greuk!”
Its height was similar to that of a normal goblin, but its build was different, with a wide back and firm muscles. Even the hat on its head and the pickaxe slung over its shoulder were unique.
“It’s a Goblin Miner.” This was a rank-eight monster whose XP could only be obtained in the first-floor Rift.
“Kyaaagh!”

The macho-looking bastard rushed toward us as soon as he spotted us, swinging his pickaxe one against three. An ordinary goblin could never hope to match the kind of strength this guy could put behind his attacks.
“So annoying...”
You think that’s going to work? Each of us could easily clear a first-floor Rift alone.
Stab!
Without even having to use her arrows, Erwen used a wind spirit to shoot the monster between the eyes.
[You have defeated the Goblin Miner. EXP +2]
One-shot kill. At our level, that was only natural, but the whole production of pointing at the opponent with her index finger and then firing a blast of compressed air was quite impressive.
Was that a real-life Finger Flick...?
There had been a time in my life when I was obsessed with Wuxia novels.
Man, why can’t I do something like that?
“Schuitz, is there a problem?”
“Yeah, why are you staring at me, Mister?”

“It’s nothing. Let’s go.” I cut that train of thought off at the pass and got moving again. Besides, if I were to describe my own state in Wuxia terms, I would currently be around the level of a Martial Arts Master who had achieved near-indestructibility.
Dash, dash.

Anyway, I led the way from there on out. All we had to do in the beginning was follow a straight tunnel, but still. I made sure to keep a close eye on the ground as I moved, and I stopped as soon as I noticed the tracks were damaged.
“Why did you stop?”
“The tracks cut off. It should be around here.”
Kwaaang!

I smashed the surrounding walls with my hammer. Amelia was startled by this and asked if I was trying to bury them alive, but she didn’t have to be worried about that. Rifts weren’t that flimsy. The places you could break them were usually places where there were hidden features—just like here.
Crackkk!

The wall crumbled like it was made of Styrofoam, revealing a space behind it. It was a narrow side passage just big enough for one person. I probably would have had trouble fitting inside of it in my usual, non-shrunken form.
Thud.
Ugh, my shoulders are still caught.
I had no choice but to walk sideways like a crab into the side passage.
“We’ve earned three million stones in one go.” After picking up a green gem from the box hidden inside a small cavity in the passageway, I retraced my steps to come back out.
“I never knew there was something like this in the coal mine.”
“But, Mister... can we take that out without a wizard?”
“It’s okay. These sorts of things don’t need distortion magic.”

The Bloody Citadel was a good example of this phenomenon. The only things in Rifts that required distortion magic to remove were miscellaneous items such as bricks and building decorations. Valuable things like the Necronomicon were designated as items, so you could just grab them and leave.
Ah, she wasn’t there back then, though, was she?
“Then let’s keep moving. We have everything we need here.”

Anyway, this was the only hidden item in the first stage, so after that, I focused solely on running instead of looking down at the ground. Before long, a cliff appeared. There was a bridge, but more than two-thirds of it had collapsed. The usual strategy for this section was to take the passage next to it as a detour.
If I had Leap, I could’ve just cleared the gap.
It was a pity I didn’t have my mobility skill anymore. Normally this part could be skipped if you had an intermediate or higher-level one.
There are only Goblin Miners down the detour, so it’ll just be a waste of our time.

It wasn’t even a route with a hidden element, but we had no choice but to take the side road anyway. Crushing all the Goblin Miners we saw, we finally exited on the other side after about thirty minutes.
“This is easy. I guess since we’re on the first floor.”
“It’s definitely a bit different from what I expected...”

Erwen seemed dissatisfied with how dull exploring the Rift was turning out to be, but there was nothing I could do about it. That was an obvious consequence of coming to a first-floor Rift with seventh-floor party members. Typical RPG games didn’t even give you EXP for this. Oh, but maybe it was more cut-throat of us to come to a low-level hunting ground for XP?
“Don’t be too disappointed, guys. We’re going to finish this up quickly and leave.”
Everyone seemed bored so I sped up the Rift clearing process. Moving through the passageway beyond the bridge we skipped, we hunted all the monsters in the second stage.
[You have defeated a Hobgoblin Miner. EXP +3.]
[You have defeated a Mineral Slime. EXP +2.]
[You have defeated a Copper Golem. EXP +3.]
Those were the new monsters we encountered in the second stage. Then we hit the mini-boss.
[You have defeated the Goblin Bomber. EXP +4.]
As expected, there was no essence. Well, we didn’t have a test tube or a wizard to take it back to the city, anyway.
The second stage is mainly focused on battle so it went fast.
We cleared the mini-boss in about ten minutes before searching around for the hidden element, something that popped up when you destroyed the minerals near the middle boss’s room: Gobble Quartz.
Oh, there are exactly three.
“We can each have one.” I was about to share the Gobble Quartz I dug up, but Amelia and Erwen frowned.
“You’re...eating that?”
“It smells weird, Mister. And it’s also sticky for some reason...”
“It’s still an elixir. It increases your Poison Tolerance.”
“If you say so.” Amelia, who grew up in Noark and had had no choice but to develop a strong stomach, downed the Gobble Quartz first. Erwen followed suit, cringing.
“Does it taste that bad?”
“...Surprisingly, it doesn’t taste like anything.”
“The texture is very unique,” said Amelia.
“Oh, really?”
The texture can’t be that unique. I guess there’s nothing to worry about.
Snap!

When I chewed up the Gobble Quartz with my molars, it was truly a fascinating texture. It was soft on the outside but felt like chewing stone on the inside. Barbarians usually ate bones with every meal, though, so that was nothing special.
[You have consumed a Gobble Quartz. Your Poison Tolerance has permanently increased by +3. This effect cannot be stacked.]

After that, our strategy for clearing the Rift was essentially more of the same. We moved forward, destroying all visible monsters. Then we stopped for a moment to search for hidden items or features in the area. Once we climbed down a circular staircase at the edge of a cliff, the third stage ended.
“This is the last part.”

We arrived at the deepest part of the coal mine and found ourselves standing in front of a collapsed mineshaft that looked like it was blocked by something. Normally you had to use the explosives hidden throughout the mine to open up a path, but high-level players had their own ways.
Bang, bang!
When I smashed the lower corner of the stone into pieces with Demon Grinder, the shaft came crashing down, creating a gap that was big enough for us to go through one person at a time.
[The sleeping King of Green has woken up.]
At the center of the cavern, which had a radius of approximately fifty yards, a green slime wriggled and howled.
“Kyuiiit!” It was the King Slime, the guardian of the Green Coal Mine.
Meanwhile, at the start of the Rift, two men were trembling in the deep darkness, relying on one flickering torch for light.
“...D-Do we really have to go alone?”
“There’s no other way. The portal is closed.”
“I heard Rifts are explored by five people... How did this happen...?”

The archer sighed at the axe warrior’s words. Even if he asked him, it wasn’t like he had any way of knowing. How could the portal close when there were only two people in the Rift? He actually assumed it was a temporary error at first. Even after the portal disappeared, they waited there for three hours for someone to arrive. But they couldn’t live in denial forever.
“Never mind, let’s go. If we want to clear the Rift between the two of us, we have to start moving now.”
“...O-Okay.” The axe warrior, who had a rather delicate personality despite his size, stood in front. The archer followed behind, supporting him.
Goddamned buggy shit game.

The archer usually felt like luck was on his side. Well, he did also come across said shit game by chance and end up here, but aside from that, his life was on the easier side. That fact hadn’t changed even after he woke up in an unfamiliar world. Just look at his first quest. He was lucky enough to obtain an essence immediately, and starting with his second expedition, he was able to strip equipment off of adventurers fighting each other and plunderers to earn initial funds. With this as his foundation, he was able to make steady progress.
I thought ending up in the first-floor Rift on my third expedition was a great thing, but I never expected something as shitty as this to happen.
Even as the man complained to himself, though, he was on guard. That was the only way he’d survive.
“...Wait, stop for a minute.”
“What is it?”
“Something is off. There should be a Goblin Miner at this point...”
“Huh... do you know a lot about the Rift?”
“Somewhat. I like studying.”

He gave the guy an excuse, but it was a lie. In truth, he had experience with the original version of the game, although he never got past the first half and only beat the game later when he found out there was a modded version. Nevertheless, he knew a lot about the first half because he had played the original. Thanks to the insane difficulty level, reading the Newbie Guide posted by Elfnuna numerous times was essential if you wanted to play properly.
“...Let’s keep going for now. I don’t know why there aren’t any goblins here yet.”
Waiting wouldn’t change anything, so he just wrote it off as a difference between the game and reality and cautiously kept moving.
“Oh, there’s a side road through that collapsed area!”
When he saw the wall at the end of the broken railway track, however, he realized what was going on. “Someone came through first.”
“...What did you say?”
“Nothing.”
Someone had entered the Rift first. At least three someones.
Then... they must have killed all the monsters here.
The moment he realized this, a wave of relief washed over the man, and his legs felt wobbly. Then, once the relief subsided, he started to see this as an opportunity.
If there are no signs of a struggle, that means they’re probably strong enough to just crush everything in their way.

They probably weren’t interested in an essence in the first-floor Rift, and the amount of time an essence stuck around before disappearing was about thirty minutes. If he rushed to catch up to them now, he could obtain the discarded essence at the end. And perhaps he could pick up any hidden items they left behind.
“Let’s go. Don’t worry about the monsters.”
“...What do you mean?”
“There won’t be any monsters up ahead. If you don’t believe me, I can go first.” With that, the archer began running through the dark tunnel without hesitation.
They took the Gobble Quartz.
There was nothing left in the second and third stages. The people who had entered the Rift first were so knowledgeable that he couldn’t find a single thing they didn’t take.
I didn’t even know about that one... but since the wall is broken, I guess there was something inside.
He kept running for a while and arrived at the boss room. All in all, it took about forty minutes.
If the guardian’s essence dropped and they didn’t take it... it might still be around.
Soon, the man entered the boss room with the axe warrior.
Shaaaaaa!
When they spotted the essence floating in the air, a deep hunger appeared in the eyes of the two men. Of course, there was a key difference between them.
“A-An essence...!”
“I know.”
The axe warrior in front of him actually seemed more surprised than greedy, but the man behind him was the opposite.
“I-Is that the essence of the guard—”
Shoop!
The man grabbed an arrow and drove it into the axe warrior’s shoulder.

“Ahhh!” The warrior screamed and dropped to the ground at the sudden surprise attack. He came to his senses a moment later and tried to pick up his axe, but unfortunately, that didn’t go well for him.
Clunk.
The ax slipped and fell from his hand.
“It’s no use. I rubbed a paralysis poison on the arrowhead.”
“...W-Why are you doing this?! I-I’ll give you the essence. P-Please!” The warrior picked up on the fact that he had been defeated and begged and shouted, but the archer’s eyes were cold.
“You’re just an NPC, why do you care so much about your life?”
“N-NPC...? What does that mean? No, but hey, you dragoon! Please have mercy. I have a daughter at home—”
“A dragoon is a protoss.” The man chuckled and pulled out the embedded arrowhead. “Hans Eliburn. That’s my name. Ah, well, that isn’t my real name, either.”
“A-Are you...!”
“I guess you’ve figured it out now. Sorry. I just want to say that in advance so I don’t go soft.”
“N-N—!” The warrior went to shout something, but he never got a chance to finish. He took an arrowhead through the neck before he could.
“It’s no different from killing a goblin.” The man quickly got up and moved toward the essence floating in the air. A sharp smile hung on his lips.
“Luck is on my side.”
[The Essence of the Slime is being absorbed into your soul.]
The man truly considered himself lucky... until he saw the ability he had acquired with his own eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 375: Treasure Hunter (3)
paragraphs: The guardian of the Green Coal Mine, King Slime, had an essence that could come in handy up to the middle stages of the game. None of us would be taking it even if it dropped, though, and it ended up not dropping anyway.
[You have defeated the King Slime. EXP +4]
[Guardian Kill Bonus. EXP +3]
As I watched the King Slime disappear into a cloud of light, I pursed my lips in disappointment. “Wow, really? Nothing?”
I didn’t care about an essence; I was hoping to at least get a Numbers Item. How was there not even a Rift Stone? The individual drop rate of each should have been 33.3 percent.
Come to think of it, there weren’t any essences on the way here, either.
That was why I had had my hopes up, thinking the guardian might spit out a good Numbers Item at the end.
“There was one essence, at least.”
I laughed at Amelia’s words of comfort.
What kind of essence is that? That’s just trash.

When the essence of the rank-nine monster Slime was taken, physical stats like Bone Strength, Physical Resistance, Strength, and Agility dropped, and it only gave you stats with low combat value like Poison Tolerance, Intuition, and Digestion. Even the active skill was so-so, although it could be useful depending on the situation. Normally it wasn’t worth the other penalties, though, so most people considered it one of the worst essences you could take, even among rank-nine essences. The essence popped out while we were killing a trash mob in the middle of our fight against the King Slime.
Welp, it would have been better if nothing showed up at all. Then at least there would have been hope of a jackpot next time.
“Mister, there’s an open portal there! Are we going straight out?”
“Of course.”
I led my comrades to the portal with absolutely no hesitation. This was supposed to be a Rift, but the only thing that dropped was a Slime essence. What the hell was with this trash level?
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
Let’s get out of here quick. If we stay any longer, the bad luck might infect us.
After we left the Rift, we didn’t waste time. Now that we had nothing to see on the lower floors, we headed up and reached our target floor on the twenty-sixth day.
[You have entered the Great Sea on the sixth floor.]

The Island of Beginnings, Laemia, wasn’t crowded with adventurers and soldiers like last time, nor was the coastline filled with warships. The naval force heading for the Dark Continent departed on day twenty-five, so this was natural. That was actually why we arrived a day late on purpose.
“Okay, let’s head to the shore.”

There was no reason to waste time on an empty island, so we headed straight to the coast, then took out our ship from sub-space. Unlike the previous ship I owned, which had to be rowed, this one looked different.
Yeah, this is what you call a ship.

The vessel was of similar size and shape to the fishing vessels commonly seen in Korea. There was a large, square sail at the center of the ship, and in the back part of the hull was a mana propulsion device, so it was possible to increase the speed by inserting mana stones. Put simply, as long as we had enough mana stones, we could get through any windless waters.
Actually, I don’t know if we’ll be going out to the windless areas without a sailor or navigator...

Once we all got on the ship, Amelia gulped and stood at the helm. It seemed she didn’t look all that reliable, because Erwen cautiously expressed some concerns. “Can that woman really sail this ship properly even though she’s not a sailor...?”

“She said she has experience steering a small ship, so she’ll be much better than me since I only have experience with oars. And she apparently learned the basics of how to operate it when she bought it.”
“Right, Amelia?”
“...Don’t talk to me. I’m thinking.”
Dang, I’m kind of getting worried now.

Amelia, wheel in hand, had on a serious expression like she was running simulations in her head. Only after she was done did she officially start giving out orders. “First...we have to row to get away from the island. Only then can we ride the wind, I think.”
“You think...?”
“If you have a problem, you can do it yourself—”
“No, no problem. I’ll do as you say.”

Instead of getting on Amelia’s case, though she was clearly a novice, I faithfully followed her instructions. Of course, I didn’t intend to exert myself by rowing. Why else would we have paid so much for this ship?
Slide!
When I inserted mana stones into the tube connected to the mana propeller, the ship started gliding forward.
“...Ugh!” Amelia was surprised by the sudden speed but she soon regained her composure and turned the wheel to change directions. “N-Now! Sail! Unfold the sail!”
When the sail was unfurled, the ship began to glide forward with the wind.
Whew, it worked out somehow.
“What direction?”
“We’re heading east, so don’t worry.”

“I see...” Amelia sighed in relief, but I noticed she had a white-knuckle grip on the wheel. It was a refreshing sight. To think someone who didn’t even flinch when killing another person would get so nervous about something like this.
“I’m starting to see it.”

After we sailed for about fifteen minutes east, we spotted an island on the edge of the horizon. This was the closest island to the start point after Farune Island, where our fierce battle against Storm Gush took place: Gurkha Island. In reality, there was no reason to stop by this island. The monsters here were all low-ranking and all of them could be encountered on other floors as well. There was little demand for EXP from this place.
But we don’t have a sailor, so we have no choice.

It was next to impossible for us to head straight to our desired destination with our navigation skills, so we had no choice but to go step-by-step, visiting each island one by one. Well, there were other reasons to stop too.
“...Mister, are you okay?”
Jeez, this goddamned seasickness. It definitely seemed a little better than before, but it was still hard to deal with the way my insides were churning.
“Schuitz, if you want, we can take a break.”
“Please.”
After anchoring the ship on the coast, we took a short break. Still, this was the good thing about having a barbarian’s body. The motion sickness may have been bad, but it went away in ten minutes.
“Now, let’s set sail again.”
Once I recovered, we went through the process of setting sail again. Our next destination was the second island on the eastern route, Anos.
“It will take us about three hours to get there—are you sure you can make it?”
“...Don’t worry. I heard we just have to move northeast,” said Amelia.
“According to who?”
“...A book.”

Erwen, who wouldn’t have ever participated in such a reckless voyage before, looked dubious. But Amelia seemed to have quite a talent for sailing as an island appeared in the distance after about three hours.
Amelia clenched her fists in satisfaction. “We came to the right place.”
“But why is the island east of us and not straight ahead?”
“...That is within the margin of error.”

Amelia turned the bow and before long, we arrived at the island of Anos. Unlike Gurkha, which we pretty much skipped, we had business on this island. There were no hidden events or treasures, but we had to get XP we hadn’t obtained yet. Also, we planned to spend the night here since the sun was already setting.
“Blaaargh!”
But before that, I needed to empty my stomach.
[You have defeated a Raffle Monkey. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a War Snake. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Nigel Panther. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Belgaro. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Black Tree...]

Almost 99 percent of Anos Island, excluding the coast, was jungle. After camping out on the coast for a night, we officially began exploring the island the next day. By the time we finished roaming the entire island and collecting EXP, the sun was setting again so we had to camp out for one more night.
Hmm, I thought we’d be able to do a full sweep in half a day and move to the next island.
The monster we hunted last played a big part in messing up our schedule. Even after we searched the entire island, it was nowhere to be seen. We ended up having to look for it until nightfall.
“Mister, aren’t the stars super pretty—”
Honnnk!
“Oh, you’re sleeping...”
The next morning, we set sail toward the next island early and we were thankfully able to arrive in one piece once again. We repeated this process several times.
“We’re already at the seventh island.”
“It’s called Fione Island, right?”

We arrived at the seventh island on the eastern route within ten days. To be honest, this was quite an impressive—and surprising—feat. After all, we got here safely with a sailor who only knew how to move forward, stop, and park.
I thought we would miss at least one island. Is sailing easier than I thought?
With that thought in mind, I watched Amelia sail the ship from the sidelines and learned bit by bit. I was slowly getting used to the seasickness too.
“Wow, the island is just as pretty as I heard.”
“Erwen, is this your first time here too?”
“Yes. Normally I skip past it.”
“True, if you’re unlucky, it’s just a waste of time.”

Fione Island, the seventh island on the eastern route, was often referred to as Treasure Island among adventurers. Compared to the islands with mountains at their center, Fione was relatively flat and on the smaller side. You could walk around the entire thing in about three hours, and there was only one type of rank-four monster that spawned here.
“Are you going to skip it too?”
“The sun is starting to set so we’ll stay the night.”

Erwen looked rather pleased with my answer. Which was fair, as it was safe to say there were no monsters on the island itself. If we did happen to run into one, it would essentially be the equivalent of winning the lottery.
“Mister! There’s still a lot of time until nightfall, so let’s look around the island together! Hmm?”
“...We can do that.”
“It could be dangerous,” said Amelia. “I’ll go with you.”
After we landed on the island, we put the ship in sub-space and walked around to get a feel for the terrain.
Shaaaaa.
The cool ocean breeze caressed my skin. After a short walk, we stumbled upon a wide-open field full of colorful flowers.
“Not bad.”
The comment tumbled out of my mouth involuntarily and Erwen flashed a shy smile in apparent agreement. “Hehe, right?”
“Yeah, since it’s open on all sides we’ll be able to spot any plunderers that come our way easily.”
“...What?” Erwen tilted her head in confusion, but this was important.

This place wasn’t called Treasure Island for nothing. Even if most of the top adventurers were currently at war on the seventh floor, there was almost zero chance there were no adventurers on this island. Aside from Rifts, this island was the only place where you could obtain Numbers Items.
“Enough scouting, let’s set up camp over there. I saw a good spot earlier.”
“Ah, right...”
As we were all seasoned adventurers, we set up camp in good time and went to sleep, leaving Amelia’s doppelganger on watch.
An indeterminate amount of time later, Amelia shook me awake. “Schuitz, wake up.”

When I looked around, rubbing my eyes, I saw that Erwen had also gotten up and taken out her bow. There was only one possibility that came to mind, and it made far more sense than encountering a monster on this island.
“How many?” I asked only for the critical information, omitting any unnecessary chit-chat.
Amelia’s response was just as brief. “Fifteen.”
“It’s a clan, then.”
We had gotten an uninvited guest in the middle of the night.

chapters.title: Chapter 376: Treasure Hunter (4)
paragraphs: I grabbed my weapon but did not aim it. After all, it wasn’t clear what these guys were after. Provoking them could turn an easily resolvable issue into a catastrophe.
“What will you do?” asked Amelia.
“First, talk.”
“I’ll get prepared, then.”
“Sure. Erwen, do not step out unless I give you the signal.”
After a short word with my teammates, I stood in front to shield them from view, and we waited in tense silence.
Step, step.
Finally, a group of fifteen adventurers stopped outside our camp and the man who appeared to be their representative slowly walked forward. “Looks like I don’t need to wake you up.”
“Start with introductions.”
“Haha, you don’t need to be afraid. Nothing you’re worried about will come to fruition.”
Who says I’m afraid? I’m just trying to decide whether I need to bash your skull in or not. Four long-rangers, two wizards, nine close-combat fighters, and... no priest?

The fact that they were fifteen in number was rather notable. Ever since the six-person Binding spell was created, the basic unit of any party became six. Which meant there was a chance three more of them were hiding somewhere nearby.
“You are a very guarded fellow. Let’s calm down and talk for a moment. If we were here with bad intentions, we wouldn’t be talking to you like this, would we?”

That remained to be seen. I glanced at the group standing at the ready behind him, then shifted my gaze to stare at the man. “What do you want? You should know it’s not a good look to wander into someone else’s campsite at night.”
The man revealed his identity. “We are from the Huntsman Clan.”
“I’ve never heard of it.”
“That makes sense. To be honest, it’s not a very famous clan. Recently, we’ve solely been hunting for treasure on Fione Island so we haven’t been active anywhere else.”
“Treasure hunting, huh?” It was only then that I got a rough idea of why this guy had come up to us.
“I don’t know if you know or not, but Fione is split up by six clans each operating in their own territories. It’s a measure to prevent needless disputes.”
“So?”
“You are camping on the territory of the Huntsman Clan. We want you to leave as soon as dawn breaks tomorrow.”

As expected, this was a case of hunting ground control. All adventurers went through this all too often starting from the fifth floor. It really drove home that the labyrinth was a world of survival of the fittest. His first impression wasn’t all that great either, but now I definitely couldn’t see him in a good light.
“I’ve never heard of the palace granting the rights to Fione to any specific group.”
“Haha, despite how sharp you look, you sound rather rigid in your thinking. Adventuring isn’t a by-the-book business.”
With that, the man didn’t say anything else. He just stared at me silently. Whatever words came out of his mouth next would probably depend on what decision I made.

I didn’t have to think for long. “Don’t worry. We were planning to leave when the sun rises.” We really were just here for the night, so I decided there was no need to try to dispute the rights to the hunting ground.

But did my answer make him think I was admitting defeat? “Haha, really? I guess we came for nothing. Thanks for your understanding.” The slightly wary look he had been leveling at us turned into more relaxed laughter. It seemed he had concluded we weren’t dangerous, seeing as he refused to get lost and was now running his mouth like this. “But three’s an unusual number. Did you lose a teammate on the way here?”
“That’s none of your business.”

“Don’t be so on guard. I’m just trying to help. Things could get dangerous if a monster suddenly appears, right? If you want, we could lend you our campsite...” He trailed off, then glanced at Erwen and Amelia behind me.
Ha. This son of a bitch has a knack for pissing people off.
“Thanks for the offer, but I decline.”
“Hmm, really? But the two ladies may think differently, right?” Even though I politely refused him, the man was persistent and only backed down once Erwen and Amelia clearly said no.
“I refuse,” said Erwen.
“We can take care of ourselves,” Amelia agreed.
“That’s a shame. Our clan’s branch office is located in Ravigion, District Eight. If your team disbands and you have nowhere to go, come find us.”
Ha, bullshit until the end.
“Come, let’s get back to camp!”
I barely suppressed a scoff as I watched him lead his group back.
“Mister, why did you hold back?”
“I can’t start swinging my hammer just because I’m a little annoyed.”
“Hmm, can’t you?” Erwen and I ignored Amelia’s question.

“B-But if I stepped forward, that scumbag wouldn’t have been so rude!” Erwen didn’t hide her anger or her confusion about the way I handled things, but it was unavoidable. This girl stood out wherever she went and rumors spread fast. I didn’t want any information on us to leak to the outside world, no matter how trivial.
But it wouldn’t be a good idea to say all that. “Thanks anyway, Erwen.”
“...F-For what?”
“You held back even though you were so angry.”
“That’s because... you told me not to step out unless you said...”
“That’s why I’m thankful.”
“R-Really...? It was nothing. I can do that every day...”
Instead of explaining myself at length, I obfuscated the point instead. After all, expressing sentiment was the most important thing.
“You handled that surprisingly quickly,” Amelia remarked.
“Why are you saying that like it’s a surprise? Whatever, let’s go back to sleep. We have a long way to travel again tomorrow. Okay, Erwen?”
“Okay!”

After sorting out the situation with the Huntsman Clan in record time, we lay down in our sleeping bags again and continued sleeping. What could have been hours or mere minutes later, I heard a voice.
“Schuitz, wake up.” Amelia urgently shook me awake.
What, is it those bastards again?
Whip!
I jumped up and was about to reach for my hammer next to me when she said, “Calm down. It’s not people this time.”
“...What?”
It’s not people? Then what on earth...
“Don’t tell me...” I whipped my head around to scan our surroundings and was finally able to spot what I was looking for with my own two eyes.
“Gigeek, gigig?” It was the only monster that appeared on Fione Island: the rank-four rare-type, Laplaitmimic.

This was a monster that, when killed, had a certain probability of dropping a Numbers Item. When it dropped an essence, rumor had it that it made you billions. This monster appeared in other areas as well, but there was no place it was easier to find than Fione Island. Well, you were considered lucky if you saw it once over the course of a month. Of course, those odds took the entire island into account, not just a territory.
“...To think we would run into this guy while just stopping by.”
Yes, this is the romance of a good adventure.
“Schuitz, what will you do?” Amelia asked in a whisper.
“What else is there to do?” I replied.
You think I’m going to give this up because of those guys?
“Of course we should kill it.”
“...I thought you would say that. I’ll go wake Erwen.” Amelia headed over to the sleeping bag on the side to wake Erwen up as well.
I belatedly realized something strange. “Wait, ‘Erwen’? When did you get so close?”
“Now that I’ve spent some time with her, she’s kind of cute.”
Huh, the human heart could be so unpredictable. Was this the enemies-to-friends trope in action?
“...Cute?”
“I guess I don’t need to wake her up.”
Erwen sat up at the sound of our conversation, rubbing her eyes. “Wake me up...? But what are you two doing right now?”
“There’s a Laplaitmimic.”
“...Really?” She jumped to her feet before her eyes locked on the box rolling around peacefully about twenty yards from us.
“Gigik! Gigigik?! Gigik!” As a non-aggressive monster, the Laplaitmimic just seemed curious about us and didn’t show any hostility.
“Erwen, your role is important here since we don’t have a wizard on our team.”
“I know. You said I have to kill it in one go since there’s no wizard, right?”
“Yes, otherwise it’ll immediately go underground.”
For reference, if this guy hid underground, it was safe to say it was gone. A one-shot kill was critical here.
“Erwen, shoot as hard as you can. If possible, summon the spirit of darkness too. Ah, you know its real body is the box, right? You can’t shoot the stem just because it looks like a body—”
“Don’t worry. I’ll make sure to get it.”
“Yes, I believe in you.” There was no other option than to believe in her in the first place. Erwen had the highest damage output of all of us.
“Then... here I go.” Erwen slowly pulled the bowstring.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Element Synthesis.]
Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, and even Darkness—five elements combined into one and began to emit an unusual energy. Of course, even as all this happened, the Laplaitmimic remained utterly calm.

“Gigik...?” It tilted its head like it was confused by what it was seeing. That innocence evoked a biological sense of guilt, but that was all. We were adventurers, after all. It was our job to beat up both monsters and people for money.
Tap.
Erwen finished concentrating and released the bowstring.
Whiiip!
The arrow shot forward at a speed so fast it was difficult to see with the naked eye.
“G-Gigigik!” Only then did the Laplaitmimic panic, but it was already too late.
Kwaaaaaang!
The arrow flew into the Laplaitmimic’s open mouth and exploded with a bang.

“G-Gigigik...!” Surprisingly, it was still alive even though its box was shattered and its body was in tatters. “Gigigik!” With its last bit of energy, it attempted to burrow into the ground, but Erwen was one step ahead of it.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
As soon as the follow-up attack landed, the Laplaitmimic burst into hundreds of pieces.
Shaaaaa!
Before long, the bits turned into flecks of light and disappeared.
[You have defeated a Laplaitmimic. EXP +6]
As you’d expect from a rank-four monster, the XP increase was noticeable. It was a very pleasant feeling each time, but I focused on something else.
There’s...no essence.
Well, I didn’t really have my hopes up. I’d have to be totally greedy to wish for an essence on top of everything else.
Please, at least 5000 or below.
Soon, two objects dropped where the Laplaitmimic had been standing. One was a mana stone. The other...
“It’s a ring...?”
When I got closer to the loot, an incredulous laugh erupted from my throat. “Huh...”
“Schuitz, do you know what it is?”
Of course, how could I forget? I almost once died because of this thing. It was No. 6111: Destiny Seeker, the ring that Dragon Slayer bastard had been wearing in the Labyrinth of Larcaz.
It’s not a bad item, but it is a bit disappointing...

“What kind of ring is it? I-If it’s good for an archer...” Erwen trailed off with a hungry look in her eye. She was never particularly greedy about things, but I guessed even she coveted Numbers Items.
“It’s hard to say whether it’s good for a specific type of adventurer.”
“Hard to say?”
“If I had to classify it, it’s a detection-type magic device. When something happens near you, you can discern whether it’s positive or negative by the color emitted by the ring.”
For reference, there were three colors: green, red, and yellow. That was why it was nicknamed the Traffic Signal Ring.
“It’s not bad to have one around, so it would be best to keep this rather than sell it.”
“...Then can I wear it?”
“You? But you already have a lot of rings. I’ll just wear this.”
“Ah, okay. Okay! Th-that would be best, right?” With Erwen’s approval, I put the ring on my finger without hesitation.
[The ring has detected your destiny.]
It promptly lit up.

chapters.title: Chapter 377: Treasure Hunter (5)
paragraphs: As soon as I put the ring on, I was momentarily taken aback by the flash of light as it activated. When I saw the color, I pursed my lips.
A yellow light, huh?
That color meant just one thing: that something that could either have a positive or negative impact on my future was nearby.
“Erwen, is anything around?” I asked in a low voice.
Erwen immediately focused on her hearing. “One of those people from earlier.”
“Since when have they been there?”

“I don’t know. But... since they’re hiding in the dark, I don’t think they just arrived. Their breathing is stable too...” Erwen paused to listen. “Ah, they’re even talking now. I think they’re using a message stone. ‘There’s a Numbers Item, how far away are you?’”
No wonder the light on the ring came on. It seemed they had even watched us kill the Laplaitmimic.
“Looks like they left behind a scout. Erwen, you keep focusing on what they’re up to. We’ll clean up our campground.”
“Okay.”
Leaving Erwen on guard, we quickly packed our bags and prepared to leave. However, our opponents were one step ahead of us.
“People have arrived.”
“How many?”
“Eighteen in total. Ah, they’re discussing what to do with us.”
“I see... What did they decide?”
“I don’t know. They must have used magic because the sound cut off in the middle. I’m sorry...”
“What are you sorry about? We’ll find out soon enough.”
In fact, as soon as I said that, artificial light burst out from where our opponents were hiding, brightly illuminating our surroundings.
“Hey there, friend! What was your name again? I think I forgot to ask earlier.”
‘Forgot to ask.’ Yeah right. He hadn’t even said his own name. “I don’t know, I don’t think we’re close enough to formally introduce ourselves.”
“Haha, you’re a lot shyer than you look.” The man laughed, but his eyes were cold. Also, he stood in an angled stance with his hand on his waist, near the weapon on his belt.
“So, what do you want?”
“One of our clan members happened to be on patrol in the area and saw you hunting a Laplaitmimic.”
“What a coincidence.”
“Life works in mysterious ways. Anyway, I’ll just get to the point. Give up your loot.”
“Why should I do that?”
“As I said, this is our clan’s territory. I’m sure you agreed to our terms earlier.”

“Agreed?” I scoffed as soon as I heard that, but I actually understood where they were coming from. They must have roamed this island every day waiting for a Laplaitmimic to spawn, and some adventurers who were just stopping by had managed to steal it from them. But too bad. “The only agreement we discussed was that you wanted us to leave early in the morning and we said we would.” In fact, I didn’t remember loot ever factoring into the conversation.
“That’s a fallacy.”
“It’s not a fallacy, it’s the truth.”

The man’s jaw tightened at that, and I heard an audible grinding sound. I could sympathize. Of course he would have assumed we had reached an agreement. No, in the first place, he never would have even fathomed that the monster would appear right next to us overnight.
“The labyrinth has its own unwritten rules. If you violate our claim, no one can blame us if we harm you.”

This was a very direct threat. I stared at the man to ask if he was serious about this and the guy met my gaze head-on. It wouldn’t have been out of left field for either side to pull a weapon at this point.
Gulp.

As the silence stretched on, the group behind the man tightened their grip on their weapons in a way that suggested they might attack depending on the answer that came out of my mouth. Of course, that didn’t change the fact that I was still going to say whatever I wanted.
“I don’t know about any unwritten rules. Anyone who tries to take what’s mine is a plunderer,” I said firmly.
“...So you’ve decided to make the wrong call.”

I let that go in one ear and out the other, shrugging. “I’ve heard that often enough. Where do you think all those people are now? Anyway, at least we’ve cleared the situation up.” Soon, I gave the final notice. “What are you doing? If you’re going to fight, fight. If you’re here to talk, you’d better get lost.”

This was a completely different confrontation from our first meeting. Earlier, this guy looked down on us and kicked up a fuss until I said we’d leave early in the morning. But now? When I came on extremely strong, he didn’t know what to do. I was sure it made him uneasy. He had no idea how I could be so confident when we had one-fifth of their manpower.
And part of that would be because of Erwen too.

I didn’t think they’d recognized Erwen yet, but the scout would have reported that the elven archer on our team killed a Laplaitmimic with a single arrow. They would have picked up on the fact that we weren’t just nobodies. But he seemed to be having a tough time coming to a decision in front of his clan members.
“If you can’t decide, I’ll help you. If you’re still standing in front of me after I count to three, I’ll take that as intent to harm.”
“...What?” The man looked incredulous but when I actually started counting, his expression changed.
“Three. Two.” Instead of dragging this out, I counted down the seconds faster than was strictly accurate.
The moment I was about to say one, he raised a white flag. “...There’s no need to shed unnecessary blood.”
“Captain! Why did you back down there?”
At his subordinate’s cry, the captain, Ecksher Mellick, frowned. When he did, one of his confidants quickly stepped forward to speak for him.
“They hunted a Laplaitmimic without a wizard. That elven archer has to at least be rank three. If they’re working together, the other two people must be similar ranks.”
“Even if all three of them are rank three, we have numbers on our side!”
“Remilton, have you ever fought a rank-three adventurer? They are monsters.”
“But they didn’t even have a wizard! We still could have won with our numbers!”
“And more than half of us would have died. Do you really think one Numbers Item is worth all that?”
“That’s...” The man who challenged the decision trailed off at the confidant’s logic and the official debate began.
“But if this gets out, we will be mocked everywhere we go.”
“That hasn’t happened yet, and even if it does, I think the captain’s call was the right one.”
“But who is that elf? To be able to kill a Laplaitmimic in one go...”
“A silver-haired elf... maybe that was Blood Spirit?”
“If that really is the case, we could have been in big trouble.”
“Blood Spirit? Did you all eat something bad? Why would that beast be here? She’s such a war fanatic that she must be cutting people down as we speak.”
The sharp voices rebutting each other’s opinions grew louder and louder. Naturally, factions were divided along the lines of those who held the same opinion.

“Captain! The bastards are leaving the island by ship!” a subordinate who was scouting the area reported, and the clan members who were arguing and raising their voices immediately looked to one person. Their eyes all asked what the plan was.
Mellick sighed quietly enough that no one else could hear.
God damn it.

Running a clan was like sailing a ship. Even if typhoons, waves, and lightning came their way, the captain had to show his crew that he could overcome every trial. As such, the man made a decision. “Everyone stop this and pack your bags.”
“Captain, that means...”
“We’re going to chase after them.”
At that, the faces of the people in the radical faction brightened. On the other hand, those who argued for a more moderate response expressed their concerns.
“But their power is formidable.”

Their current estimate was that the three adventurers possessed an average rank of three, but the man wasn’t too worried about that. “I understand your concerns. Perhaps if it was on land, I’d agree. But there’s no way we can lose a naval battle.”

“So that’s why you let them go so easily!” The men in the radical faction were impressed by his decision and the opposing faction also seemed to agree to some extent. That was how confident these people were in naval warfare.
But it seemed there were still some questions. “But... is one Numbers Item worth that much?” one of them asked cautiously.
Mellick answered with a grin. “It’s definitely not worth it for just one Numbers Item.”
“You mean—”
“But that won’t be all they have.”

The Huntsman Clan may have been stuck on this island playing treasure hunt for the time being, but they were once pirates who roamed the sixth floor’s seas. And pirates made their money hunting people.
At early dawn, the day gradually brightened.
Shaaaaaa!

The cool wind struck the sail, pushing the ship forward. Behind us, a cluster of stars shined in the dusky sky. In the east where the bow was located, you could vaguely sense the presence of the sun still hidden behind the horizon. It was a rather picturesque sight. Unfortunately, we had no time to enjoy it.
“Mister, there are ships following us. There are three in total and no emblems or anything like that.”
As soon as we left the island, we were pursued. And it was obvious who exactly was behind it.
So they never intended to let us go from the start.

No wonder the confrontation had ended so easily despite the yellow light—they were probably angling for this very scenario when they let us go. If these guys had three ships, that meant they were quite skilled in naval combat. They probably determined they’d have a greater advantage in a fight at sea. Of course, one question remained.
But why was it yellow instead of red?
If we were going to be attacked anyway, shouldn’t it have been red? What could be positive about this situation?
Those musings were cut off by Amelia. “Schuitz, what do you want to do?”
“It’ll be hard to shake them, right?”
“Probably.”

Their ships appeared to have modifications that made them especially fast, as the distance between us kept growing shorter even though we were using the mana propulsion device. And so, we only had one option now.
“Emily, don’t waste the mana stones.”
“Are we going to fight?”
“Is there any other option?”
Amelia didn’t answer my question. She just let go of the wheel. When she did, the speed of the ship, which was riding the wind, decreased significantly.
Chwaaa!

The three ships riding the current toward us came into my sight too. Among them, the most noticeable was the ship in the middle. It looked about three times heavier than ours, was equipped with mana cannons on the front and sides, and had three sails. That wasn’t all, either. There was even an icebreaking device attached to the bow. A ship of that quality would be just two ranks under a royal warship.

“Schuitz, if those guys fire cannons, our ship will sink in no time.” Amelia expressed her concerns upon spotting the overwhelming grandeur of the small fleet, and I could see why. If this turned into a naval battle, a ship like ours would no doubt be destroyed in no time.
Smack.
I licked my lips and checked the traffic signal ring. The yellow light from earlier had long since faded away, but I thought I knew now why the light had been yellow instead of red.
“That ship... looks very big and sturdy.”
Monsters weren’t the only ones who dropped treasure in the labyrinth.

chapters.title: Chapter 378: Atlante (1)
paragraphs: The three ships stopped about four hundred yards away. It seemed they were wary of Erwen’s arrows.
“Erwen, is it possible for you to attack them from this distance?”
“Yes. But at this distance, most people will be able to counter it.”
True, their clan even has a wizard. They’ll have plenty of time to react before the arrow hits.
Pop!
Just then, the mana cannon attached to the front of the enemy’s command ship boomed and shot mana cannonballs at us.

Jeez, I thought they would at least tell us to surrender first. I guess they figure a conversation can wait until they win the battle. Hmm... or they plan to sink our ship whole and retrieve our drowned bodies later.
Whiiip!
The mana cannonball hurtled toward our ship in what looked more like a straight line than a parabola.
“Shuitz!” Amelia urgently called out my pseudonym, but it was Erwen who answered.
“Mister, I can take care of this.” Without even giving me a moment to ask how, Erwen fired the arrow she had nocked on her bowstring.
Kwaaang!
The arrow, which was loaded with the power of a wind spirit, collided with the mana cannonball on the sea and exploded.
“Erwen, how many can you stop?”
“I think four or five at once should be doable.”
Wow, really? We won’t even need an anti-ballistic magic circle, then.
“I’m proud of you, Erwen. Next time a cannonball comes, block it like that.”
“Okay!” After being recognized for her talents, Erwen eagerly waited for the cannonballs to fly at us again, but unfortunately, they didn’t after the first shot. A period of unease ensued.
“Looks like the enemy is quite perturbed.”
I had the same thought as Amelia, but it seemed our opponent had quickly come to a decision on how to handle this.
Pop! Pop! Bam-bam!
The three ships fired their mana cannons simultaneously and closed the distance between us. Erwen rushed to intercept them, but there were some she missed.
Bang!
A shell exploded at the bottom of the ship, shaking the hull.
Welp, looks like we should get started now. I think the distance is just right too.
“Erwen, Elementalization.”
As soon as I gave the order, Erwen activated the skill without objections. But I guessed she had one thing to clarify. “What attribute?”
“Water.”
When I told her the attribute as well, Erwen carefully grabbed my hand.
Okay, link established.

[The Spirit of the Water now dwells in your body. Any damage received from Water attribute attacks is reduced by half. Any damage received from Lightning attribute attacks is increased four-fold. When using a melee weapon, the damage you deal is reduced by 50 percent. Spring Water’s Blessing Bonus. Any healing and regeneration effects are doubled. The rate at which you recover Soul Power increases by...]
Come to think of it, this was my first time using Elemental Barbarian (Water) mode in real battle.
Slide.
I looked down to check out my new appearance. Visually, there were no significant changes. My skin was just shinier and more moisturized than usual.
“Emily, I’ll be back.”
“Where are...?”
Where else? The best defense is always a good offense. Hmm, but maybe I should still leave her with this.
“Ah, and one last thing. If you think it’s too difficult to protect the ship, just abandon it and jump off.”
“What do you—”
There was no time to waste, so I skipped any lengthy explanations.
Dash.

Stepping on the ship’s railing, I threw myself out into the choppy sea. It wasn’t a diving position. There was no need for that right now. Spring Water’s Blessing was a one-line bonus without any accompanying flavor text. A character who received this bonus could breathe in and walk on water, just like this.
Tap.
My body stood tall on the undulating surface of the sea as if defying gravity.
“Ooowoahhh!”
This was Barbarian Jet Ski (Running) mode.
Sprint.
As soon as I landed on the surface of the sea, I shouted and ran forward.
Pop! Pop! Bam-bam!
Taken aback for a moment by the barbarian running on water, the enemy soon started firing mana cannons at me again.
Bam! Kablam! Kablam!

I was able to protect my vitals with the shield for now, but I couldn’t ignore the mana cannons firing mindlessly in my direction. They were mana cannonballs, after all. The damage reduction I got from my Physical Resistance didn’t apply here. Each time I was hit, my bones ached.
“Erwen, there’s no need to block the cannonballs.”
“Sorry? What do you mean—”
Erwen didn’t finish her sentence. She saw the skeleton clacking as it rose from the water behind me.
[You have cast Liability of Risk.]
[By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
[In exchange for the temporary deactivation of Probabilistic Retaliation’s Damage Immunity effect, the odds of activation have been set at 100%.]
A mana cannon used mana as its resource. So, to put it simply, each time I received a proper hit, I could return a proper one back.
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
Puff! Pop! Pppppp!
Immediately after I got hit by the mana cannon, skeletons appeared like afterimages and fired back. But the bombardment did not cause any damage to the ship.
Shaaaaaa!

A mana barrier wrapped around the ship. This easily blocked my mana cannonball, which was only 30 percent as strong as the original. With it on, the enemy was able to continue their bombardment without stress.
[Your Powerful Luck reflects 150% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
Oh, I got a crit.
“Gahhhcha!” As the unique, exciting sound effect that accompanied a critical hit rang out, the skeleton next to me ignited the fuse of a super-huge cannon.
Poppp!
The mana cannonball flew out with a boom several times louder than usual and shattered the barrier surrounding the hull with ease.
“What kind of monster...!”
“Everyone, abandon the Merina and escape!”
“Come over here, quickly!”
One of the ships began to sink.
God damn it.
To think it would sink after one hit. How much of a loss did we just take?
Flash!
Just then, a light flashed and the ship everyone abandoned was summoned back into sub-space.
Hmm, that can just be repaired later, then.
“Sink the ship!” Determined to solve the easier problem first, the enemy turned their mana cannons toward the ship Amelia was on all alone and fired.
Welp, I figured they would do that.
Erwen did what she could, but she couldn’t stop the ship from sinking. She was too busy avoiding the spells.
“Mister, it’s magic!”
“Get behind me just in case!”

I hid Erwen, who was following me in spirit form, behind me. Although she was immune to physical damage while using Elementalization, she took much more damage from things like magic. And if Elementalization were to deactivate here, the only thing in our future would be a one-way trip to the bottom of the ocean.
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]

Magic flew in along with the mana cannonballs. Taking all kinds of long-range hits with my body, I ran forward. Although Liability of Risk continued to deal out counter-attacks regularly as I took the blows, the enemy’s attacks did not let up.
“Paltan is dead!”
“We have to stop him before he gets up here!”
“More! Fire more!”
“The enemy is on the ropes too! Just a little more!”

It was a full-strength push with both parties putting it all on the line. Of course, they must have thought they had the advantage. In the end, even if I got on that ship, I would be in complete tatters. It was clear they assumed they could overwhelm me with numbers and defeat me once I was tired out.
How foolish.
Shoot!
Just then, a flash of light penetrated my body.
[You have been hit with Thunder Spear.]

The shock was strong enough to make my mind white out for a moment. I felt myself stumble, and though I managed to keep my balance and avoid falling, my physical state was already at an all-time low. The injuries were one thing, but the electric current that just tore through my body seemed to have boiled my guts.
Goddamn lightning magic.

Was it because I had Liability of Risk on top of Elemental Barbarian (Water)? The whopping eight-fold damage was enough to leave me at death’s door. However that seemed to be the case for my enemy as well.
“Gahhhcha!” Just in time, another Critical Success popped up.
[Your Powerful Luck reflects 150% of the damage received back to the enemy.]

The skeleton lobbed a giant Thunder Spear that looked like something straight out of ancient mythology. As the word ‘lightning’ implied, the spear literally flew at the speed of light and totaled the second ship next to the flagship.
That... can’t be repaired.
For reference, I didn’t even hear a boom. That was because my hearing was temporarily incapacitated.
Beeeeeep.
The ringing in my ears seemed to drill through my skull. My legs gave out and I sank into the sea. Well, that was partly intentional, though.
[The Energy of the Sea dwells in your body. Due to the passive skill Origin, your Natural Regeneration has significantly increased.]
I told you. I can’t lose at sea.
Between Storm Gush’s passive skill Origin and Elementalization doubling any healing and regeneration effects, my body began to heal almost as fast as with a potion.
Shaaaaaa!

Crooked bones popped back into place, and burned, stabbed, and bruised flesh knitted itself back together. There was no pain, unlike with a potion, so I was able to perceive the recovery process in more detail and in real-time. Before long, my hearing returned.
“Mister, are you okay?”
I guess she can communicate even underwater when she’s in spirit form. But I can’t speak, you see.
I pointed up with my index finger, then shrugged and tilted my head.
“Are you asking what’s going on up there?”
There you go.
When I nodded, Erwen quickly briefed me. “The attacks have stopped for now. I think they think they got you.”
So, they were excitedly staking their claim on my stuff already.
“Ah, I can faintly hear them talking... I think the wizard is trying to use detection magic.”
Hmm, then they’ll soon find out we’re still alive. I should give them a surprise before that.
When I made a gesture asking to be lifted up, Erwen summoned a water spirit and pushed me.
Chwaaa!
I rocketed to the surface again.
“...H-He’s over there!”
When I grinned like a watery ghost rising straight from hell, my enemies were shocked and piled on the high praise.
“His injuries are all healed too...!”
“What kind of monster is that...?”
Most of them just gaped at me, stunned, but their leader was different. That was what a leader was—the person who had to calmly make decisions in any and all situations.
“Captain!”
“...Turn the bow!”

Soon, the one remaining ship quickly changed course. This was why I hadn’t used my healing powers earlier even though there was plenty of sea water around. I knew that if I came back to life like a zombie and ran toward them, they’d give up and try to run away. Even if I could walk on water, it was impossible to catch up to a ship like that on two legs.
Dash.
But at this distance, I felt like I could just make it.
When I started running, my opponents let out urgent shouts. “He’s coming!”
“Quick! Faster!”

There wasn’t even a cannon to keep me in check. They already knew I could heal myself, anyway, and they seemed to have decided it would be a bigger problem if the blowback from Probabilistic Retaliation made it hard for them to turn the bow.
“It’s all turned now!”
“Mana stones! Pour in mana stones, quickly!”
Finally, the bow was completely turned and the ship began to jet away as if driven by a motor. At this point, the distance between me and the ship was about fifteen yards.
Motherfuck...
I poured every last ounce of my strength into running. If these bastards got away now, the losses would be enormous.
They’re going to escape after destroying our ship? Not a chance. If you’re going to go, leave your ship behind!
“Aaaaaargh!” I accelerated with a shout, and the distance gradually began to narrow. It seemed it took some time for them to pick up speed after turning.
“He’s going to catch up to us like this!”
“More! Toss in more mana stones!”
As the distance narrowed even more, fear blossomed on the faces of the bastards at the back of the ship. They looked like they were being chased by a monster.
Shoot!
Meanwhile, one of the men at the railing was hit by an arrow from Erwen and fell into the sea. It wasn’t an instant death, as she avoided his vitals.
“H-Help me...!” the guy shouted, struggling to keep his head above water, but our opponents did not even attempt to save their fallen comrade. I was also too busy running to pay him any mind.
Dash.
I passed the man and lengthened my stride as much as I could.
Nine yards, eight yards, seven yards, six yards, five yards... The distance was closing little by little, but not fast enough. The ship slowly began to accelerate and soon surpassed my running speed.
Five yards, six yards, seven yards, eight yards... When the narrowed distance began to widen again, relief appeared in the eyes of those watching me from the back of the ship.
God damn it.

This wasn’t anything new, but the absence of a movement-related skill was a major letdown. Originally, my Shield Barbarian build only obtained a movement skill at level eight, but I was lucky enough to get my hands on a Manticore essence before that. If I hadn’t deleted Leap, I would have been on that ship a long time ago!
Is this really how it ends?
I slowed down in resignation. Of course, it wasn’t because I truly thought I lost the ship.
“Erwen, shoot at our ship. You can damage it a bit.”
“...Our ship?”
“Don’t worry about it right now, hurry.”
Erwen didn’t need any more urging. She shot an arrow toward the stern of the flagship.
Kwaaang!
It then exploded.
“...That’s going to cost a lot to repair.”
That was where the ship’s mana propulsion device was.
After the mana propulsion device was destroyed, everything went smoothly. The growing distance quickly closed again, and I soon managed to successfully climb onto the deck.
“Kill him!” Of course, my enemies didn’t surrender as soon as they saw me or anything. A battle began. As they were a clan active on the sixth floor, they weren’t easy opponents.
So what if it’s not easy?

The outcome was already decided. Erwen moved around me, still in Elementalization mode, to kill our opponents one by one, and I protected her as she did. When the injuries on my body accumulated to a serious extent, all I had to do was dive into the water and come back up.
Splash!

After we repeated that about three times, the enemies lost their fighting spirit, dropped their weapons, and surrendered. Since their original fifteen had now been reduced to seven, more than half of them had died.
“Tsk, tsk, you have no appreciation for how precious life is. You’re going to go around wasting it?”
“I was wrong. P-Please don’t kill us...”
What are you talking about? You’re already dead.
Smack!

As soon as they surrendered, the captain slammed his head down on the ground to beg and I brought my hammer down on top of it. Tying the rest of them up, I took control of the ship. “Who’s your sailor?”
“M-Me!”
Whew, the sailor is still alive.
I turned to another man. “Hey, you’re a wizard, right?” The man nodded. “You’re just going to nod? Aren’t you going to answer?”
“Th-that’s right. I-I’m the wizard...” I set the one wizard remaining from the battle aside as well.
“Judging by your tattoo, you’re the son of a bitch who steered the other ship, right?”
“Th-that’s right.” I also appropriated the guys who owned the two other ships.
“The remaining two of you... Just go.”
“Pardon? W-Where do we go?”
Where else?
Crunch, splat!

The remaining two were useless so I immediately disposed of them. After my quick restructuring of the crew, I went to the stern to check out the condition of the ship. Below, I could see the mana propulsion device, which was horribly destroyed.
“Damn it.” I was really upset. “You guys, how dare you ruin my ship like this?”
“...S-Sorry.”
“If you could solve stuff like this just by saying sorry, what’s the point of laws?”
Everyone bowed their heads in silence.
Hah, yeah, what’s the use in getting mad?
Splash, splash.
Just then, I heard splashing water near the bottom of the ship.
Huh? What is that...?

I clutched the railing and looked down, promptly answering that question. “Ah.” It was Amelia. Did she seriously swim all the way here? “...A castaway!” I threw down the rope and when Amelia grabbed it, I hauled her onto the ship.
“Schuitz, you really...”
“Huh?”
“Let me get one free hit.” She sent her fist flying into my stomach.

chapters.title: Chapter 379: Atlante (2)
paragraphs: Once Amelia joined us, we went around and finished farming. That was because one of these guys fell into the sea earlier. It was bad luck to throw money into the ocean.
“Navigator, sail the ship.”
“Where are we going...?”
“To Fione Island.”

Once the naval battle was over, I led the ship back to Treasure Island since I figured that sailing to the next island without maintenance would be next to impossible. Actually, even getting back to Fione was quite a challenge.
The ship’s in worse condition than I thought.

While we were rowing with oars to replace the destroyed mana propulsion device, water began to fill the bottom of the boat. It seemed it wasn’t just the engine system that was broken, so we had to constantly scoop out water until we reached Treasure Island.
“...We can finally rest now.”
“I still think it was a fun experience.”
Huh, fun? This girl has weird taste.

Well, aside from not being fun, it wasn’t all that bad. Erwen had been scooping up water with us at first before realizing she could use a water spirit to make the water flow back out by itself. There would be no need to go through trial and error the next time we were faced with this situation.
Yeah, it’s these experiences that stack up to make someone a veteran explorer.

Anyway, after we got back to the island, we reverse-summoned the ship and then moved inland to summon all the destroyed ships in one go. This time, I did a proper check of their conditions. There wasn’t a single ship in good shape.
“...Emily, which do you think will be more worth it: repairing these or selling them?”

“Well...” Amelia was well-versed in buying and selling things, but she gave up on appraising these. That was how difficult it was to know the market price. “Still, either way, it will make some money. A ship like this is very expensive even if you just take the raw materials and sell it.”
“That’s true, but... Hey, Navigator!”
“Yes sir!”
“Fix the ship.”
Instead of asking them whether the ship could be repaired, I ordered them to fix it. The sailor tilted his head at this.
Haha, haven’t come to your senses yet?
“You can’t do it?” I asked curtly.

The mate flinched, then shook his head and shouted, “I will try—No, I can do it!” The answer exuded determination. He seemed to be under the impression that he’d be following in his comrades’ footsteps once he became of no use to me.
“Good, if you need anything, let me know.”
“...Thank you!” the navigator answered and ran toward the ship to start studying it carefully. He seemed to be trying to figure out how to fix it.
Then I’ll leave the ship to him...
“Wizard.”
“...I’m listening.”
“I want to take ownership of the ship. Can you cast a spell like that?”
“I can.”
Oh, you can?
I did have my hopes up considering he had been hanging around a bunch of pirates, but I didn’t think he actually could. I was sure that was a very rare spell.
“Good, then get ready to use it.”
“All right...”
“Woah, what’s with your tone... you don’t want to do it?”
“No! I want to do it!”
Should’ve said that from the start.

Now that I’d persuaded the wizard, I proceeded to take ownership of the ship. Starting with the flagship, which had lost its owner after the captain died, I next turned my attention to the two men who each owned one of the others.
“This ship is not transferable,” explained one of the men.
“What? Why not?”

“As you can see, the damage is too severe...” It was the ship that had taken the Thunder Spear’s eightfold damage with a 150 percent boost. “More importantly, the central magic circle is damaged. With this kind of damage—”
“The magic circle is broken? But the summoning and reverse-summoning worked fine.”
“To be honest, I’m wondering how that feature still works.”
“Then that’s too bad about this ship.” Since the expert said no, I had no choice but to give up on one of the ships. I’d need materials to repair it, anyway.

The navigator had been studying the captain’s ship, which was caved in at the rear, with a helpless expression when he rushed over at the sound of our conversation. “Um... then can I take the boards off of this one?”
“Go ahead.”
“And I also need manpower...”
“I’ll lend you all three here.”
“Thank you!” After receiving more than enough manpower, the first mate focused on repairing the ship with the wizard’s support to guide him.
Pour.
We poured all the loot we stuffed haphazardly into the sub-space onto the floor and started organizing it.
“This... is amazing.”

We’d have to sell it in the city to figure out the exact amount it was worth, but even at a glance, the equipment was all high-quality. That made sense since these guys were active on the sixth floor.
Anyway, I think this should be enough to pay off all our debt and even buy another mansion... Is... Is it okay to earn money this easily?
My days of hunting goblins and digging up mana stones worth a single loaf of stone bread felt almost surreal now. An indescribable emotion hovered around the edges of my awareness.
“Mister... Then we don’t have to sell the house?”
“Of course not! Let’s change the beds out for nicer ones too.”
“B-Beds?”
Beds were important. They could change your quality of life.
“Then can I change my weapon too? There’s something I’ve had my eye on.” Seeing an opportunity, Amelia also chimed in with what she wanted to buy.
“...Of course.”
“Then that hard work was worth it.”
“But... how much is it?”
When I asked, Amelia glanced Erwen’s way before leaning in to whisper in my ear. The amount was double what I expected. My breath involuntarily hitched, but I didn’t go back on my word.
“Okay, buy it.”
It’s not a waste to invest in your teammates...
“Haha, then I’ll forget about you leaving me on the ship.”
Besides, I’d done her many wrongs.

It took two days to complete repairs to the ship. I didn’t know if this was considered fast or slow, but the ship itself was repaired to perfection. Not only was there a wizard to help out with the project, but it turned out the navigator had also once worked at a shipyard.
A navigator with some maintenance skills...
He seemed like a pretty decent talent.
“Hey, what’s your name?”
“A-Are you talking to me?”
“Who else?”
“I’m Auyen Rockrobe.”
Okay, it’s not Hans, at least.
That alone was enough to pass the screening. “That’s a good name. Good work, Nguyen.”
“It’s Auyen...”
“Ah, was it?”
After praising the sailor’s efforts for successfully repairing the ship, we floated it on the shore.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you getting on?”
“...I am.” The navigator got on the ship like he was being led straight to hell.
Next was the wizard. “You get on too.”
“...All right.”

Once the wizard got on board as well, the remaining two men looked at me with uncertain expressions on their faces. These were the ones who had survived and were brought to this island because they owned two of the ships and thus controlled their summoning. If I had killed them on the flagship earlier, the other two ships in their sub-space would have spawned in the middle of the ocean. Since we needed manpower for the repairs, I had just stripped their equipment and left them alone.
“We’ll get on...”
“Yes, me too...” When I stared at them, the men sighed like they had no choice and started walking toward the ship.
I halted them with my shoulder. “Stop right there. You guys can’t come with us.” They didn’t have anywhere near enough talent to receive my blessing.
Tap.
The men gave me strange looks. “So, we’re staying here...?” They seemed to be wondering whether they should be happy about this or not.
Still, one guy caught on fairly quickly. “...Please, take us with you. We’ll be useful somewhere.”
Hmm, maybe someone with this much intelligence could end up being useful?
The thought came to mind but it didn’t change my decision. “No, you guys can rest now.”
“Damn it...!”
‘Damn it’? How common.
This was probably the phrase I’d heard the most since being dropped into this world.
Crunch, splat!
After making sure to crush both heads equally, I threw the bodies onto the beach. The sea monsters would smell the blood and clean them up.
Now, shall we go?
Splash, splash.
Walking through the sea, which had quickly turned bloody, I climbed the rope ladder attached to the outside of the ship and boarded it. Everyone else was already on deck.
“...Eek!” Having seen his comrades reaching the end of their usefulness and being disposed of like a pair of old shoes, the navigator trembled as his eyes met mine.
Jeez, what a coward. Well, it might be good for him to have a healthy amount of stress.
I went up to the navigator and patted him on the shoulder. Taking out their map of the eastern seas, I pointed at a particular spot with my index finger. “I plan to go here now—”
“That’s possible, of course!” The answer came immediately before I even finished speaking. As a captain, I was quite satisfied with this go-getter attitude of his.
Mm-hmm, a subordinate should by all means have this much enthusiasm. I’ll have to correct his habit of interrupting me, though.
Step, step.
Once the sailor took the helm, I walked toward the deck and stood in front of the bow. Then, I let out a loud shout of, “Set sail!”
I’ve always wanted to do that.
A navigator was like a bed, particularly in that they both changed your quality of life.
“We don’t have to stop by any islands along the way?”
“Yes! Only unskilled navigators need to look for islands to figure out where they are!” Even as he enthusiastically agreed to whatever I said, the mate didn’t forget to insert his own PR.
“Still, I want us to stop by these islands.”
“Then I’ll remap the route!”
“Oh, you’re quite useful.”
“Thank you for the compliment! I will carve it into my bones! Forever!” The sailor then redid the route according to the captain’s orders and began to sail the ship in that direction.
I guessed this displeased someone, though. “Tsk.” The wizard who was captured along with the mate tutted.
What, because you’re different from him? You have to appeal to a wizard’s superiority complex.
Shaaaaaa!
The ship sliced quickly through the open waters, braving the wind. Erwen and I set up folding chairs and parasols on the deck and enjoyed a relaxing break.
Yeah, this is sailing.
The previous ship didn’t have space for this, and I constantly had to help Amelia check that we were moving in the right direction. To think things would be so much easier with a single sailor.
“Emily, why don’t you come rest?”
“...I’m fine.”
“Why?”
“...Just because.”

I called Amelia over, too, but she returned to her spot, not giving me a proper answer. For reference, her spot was next to the sailor. I watched her for a moment to see why she was acting like that and noticed that she was studying the way the ship worked.
“Wait, why did you turn the rudder like that just now?”
“Ah, because the sails were bending slightly. This is called an angled wind, and it’s better to turn the rudder slightly in cases like this.”
Not only was she observing, but Amelia was asking the sailor various questions and engaging in active conversation.
So she can make that kind of face too, huh?
Watching Amelia hang on to his every word, a more serious look on her face than ever, I chuckled.
No wonder she seemed kind of disappointed when I said I’d leave the rest of the sailing to him.
It seemed she’d enjoyed steering the ship. Well, she’d never admit that if I asked. She’d probably just say that she was only learning how it worked just in case.

Anyway, time flew by after that. They were very peaceful days.
