Traveling forward with favorable winds bolstering us, whenever we arrived at one of our destinations, we got off the ship and killed monsters. Then we moved to the next island. Amelia diligently studied up on navigation while on the move, and Erwen and I passed the time by fishing. While we were looking around in boredom, we happened to stumble upon some fishing rods. As the saying went, you should try everything at least once.
You never know, there might come a time when the ship runs out of food and we have to be self-sufficient.
“Oh! The first big catch in a while!” Surprisingly, hanging a fishing rod on a moving ship did get you something.
“Wow... you’re amazing, Mister.”

Most of the catches were ordinary fish, more like unranked monsters similar to the Deadman you could hunt in the Bloody Citadel. They didn’t drop mana stones when defeated, and the corpses didn’t disappear, either.
“It’s a Crab Monster!”
There were also times when a monster bit the bait, which was why I couldn’t stop fishing.
[You have defeated a Crab Monster. EXP +4]

Monsters that only appeared in the ocean were harder to encounter than they were to hunt. Beyond a pastime, fishing came with practical benefits. Anyway, that routine continued for a long while. As we headed east, we left the early waters.
I could hear Amelia’s conversation with the navigator. “Do you know why the compass stops working here?”
“I don’t know. There’s a saying that the Great Sea has a sea god who gets angry at the adventurers that approach them, but that’s most likely just a legend.”
Hmm, is that sea god called Leviathan? I need to hunt him down someday too...

“Anyway, it’s not easy to find the direction from this point on so the skills of the navigator become especially important. This is where beginner navigators struggle the most with their own limitations.”
“Then what’s the method you use?”
“The stars, sun, temperature, weather—all of that becomes information. Of course, the most important thing is experience.”
“Interesting. Can you tell me in more detail?”
“Haha, of course. Ah, we’ve just caught wind. Would you like to grab the rudder?”
“...Can I?”
“Of course. If something goes wrong, I will help you.”
“If you say so...”
When did Amelia get so close to the sailor? She’s not going to ask to keep him later, is she? Nah, Amelia would never do that.
I chuckled and got some shut-eye. When I woke up again, the wind had already stopped. This was the Windless Zone, one of the Great Sea’s special areas.
“The easiest solution is to use the mana propulsion device here.”

Without having to row, we cut through the Windless Zone with the mana stones we’d collected so far. Ah, for reference, the propulsion system that Erwen destroyed had been replaced, not repaired. The other ships had propellers too. We tore them out and moved them here. Since this was a large-sized ship, apparently you needed three small propellers to produce the same output.
“The wind is blowing!”

Once we crossed the Windless Zone in two days, waters with reefs here and there appeared before us. These were far eastern waters where rocky, volcanic land accounted for 99 percent of the islands. Scanning the sea, which had its own unique characteristics here, I smiled.
Somehow we found a navigator to bring us all the way here.
It was time to explore the Burrow Island, Atlante.

chapters.title: Chapter 380: Atlante (3)
paragraphs: Atlante was located in Grand Rock, the far eastern seas. It was also the place where my second core essence following Orc Hero appeared. It wasn’t that difficult to get to this place. You needed a ship capable of sailing to Grand Rock; the ability to dive freely into the deep sea with magic, a spirit, or a skill; and most importantly, the tenacity needed for repetitive labor. As long as you had these three things, it wasn’t very difficult to visit Burrow Island.
It’s all hard work from here on out.
After entering Grand Rock, we carefully led the ship around the reefs. In order to get to Burrow Island, which was hidden beneath the far eastern seas, there was something we needed to do first.
“Would it be possible to know our destination...?” the navigator asked out of curiosity as we were wandering around.
I answered after a brief pause. I decided there was no reason to hide it at this point.
“Sorry? Red Rock Island?” The sailor tilted his head at my answer.
“Yes, it should be just big enough for about twenty people to climb up.”
Every time the labyrinth opened, three Red Rock Islands were randomly generated in this area. You had to complete all unlocking tasks on these three rock islands to reveal Burrow Island.

“...All right.” Surprisingly, the sailor didn’t question my instructions. “So you were trying to go there.” It seemed he knew something about how Burrow Island worked. Most people didn’t know about it, but I supposed he’d had quite a long career. “Then I will plan the route as efficiently as possible, centering it around the search.”
“Ah, I’ll leave that part to you.”
Once he found out what I was aiming for, the navigator sailed the ship more proactively than before, and we located one of the rock islands on the fourth day.
Splash.

The flat, rocky island was submerged in water up to the ankles. When I went to the center of the island and checked the cracks in the ground, I found a neat row of eggs the size of an ostrich’s nestled inside.
“Eggs? What do we do with these?” Erwen asked curiously over my shoulder.
I chuckled. All hidden elements of Dungeon and Stone were the same.
Crack!
If you found anything that looked suspicious, destroy it. That was the first rule of questing, right?
[You have destroyed a Mermal’s Nest.]
How long had it been since we destroyed all the eggs?
“It’s slowly starting to respond.”
“Sorry?”
“Prepare for battle!”
The second the shout left my mouth, sea monsters began to appear from beneath the rocky island. Hmm, maybe ‘sea monster’ wasn’t the best description.
Splash.

I scanned the nearest monster glaring at us, trident in hand, up and down. To start, it walked on two legs with proportions similar to those of a human. The texture of its blue skin was reminiscent of scales and its shiny skin was full of glowing tattoos. The important body parts were covered with cloth and each of the monsters had its own unique hairstyle, differentiating them from other monsters who all looked the same. Their intelligence wasn’t much different from other monsters’, though.
“Kyaaaaaagh!” It was a ferocious howl with no perceivable language behind it. As if on cue, the monsters surrounding us from all sides attacked all at once.
[You have defeated a Mermal. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Mermal Warrior. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Mermal Archer. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Mermal Sorcerer. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Mighty Mermal Warrior. EXP +4]

As the classes were diverse, new XP came flooding in. The battle itself wasn’t all that tough, either. Although this event involved an onslaught of hundreds of monsters, their average rank wasn’t even six.
Smash, smash, smash!

Using Giantization to raise my Threat Level and attracting most of the aggro to myself, the hunt ended smoothly without anyone getting hurt. And it seemed this left an impression on our two hangers-on.
“To think we tried to attack these monsters... Of course we ended up in this situation,” the wizard muttered faintly. The navigator nodded, apparently sympathizing with that sentiment a lot.
Jeez, regrets are always late, no matter how early they come.
“Wizard, go collect mana stones if you have time to sit around.”
“...I will.” Once the battle ended, I made the wizard collect the mana stones that had fallen everywhere. “There’s an essence. What do you want to do with that?”
“Leave it. It’s not worth much, anyway.”
I didn’t bother taking the Mermal’s essence. Although we had a wizard and the test tubes he carried around, it wasn’t worth it. I couldn’t waste our two precious test tubes on something like this.
Rumble!
What the...? Why is the ground shaking all of a sudden?
“Mister?”
“Wait.”

We had been about to get back on the ship, but we waited for a while to see what was going on. The tremors continued to jiggle the surface of the water for about a minute before stopping like magic. And I had a feeling I knew what had caused this phenomenon.
[Somewhere in the deep sea, an underwater city has appeared.]
Who would’ve thought someone else had already cleared the other rock islands? Thanks to that, we didn’t have to waste our time looking for the other two.
“I don’t know if I should call this good luck, though...”

I couldn’t put my finger on what exactly our current situation was. It was nice that the amount of work we had to do had been reduced, but the fact that the events on the other two islands had already been completed could only mean one thing: there was competition gunning for Burrow Island. Of course, we didn’t know that with 100 percent certainty yet. It was possible someone had just cleared the event on their way to another island.
I’ll figure that out later.
I decided to ponder this issue again later. Even if we had a rival, I wasn’t going to change my plans.
Now then, what should I do about the team?

I contemplated this one last time but I decided it was best to take everyone with me. If there was an essence I couldn’t absorb, I’d have to store it in a test tube. So to start, the wizard had to come along. The same went for Erwen, who would solve our underwater breathing problem, and Amelia, whose help I’d need to find the underwater island.
Well, I don’t need the navigator, but... I’m anxious about leaving him alone.
“Wizard, you can use diving magic, right?”
“How long can you make it last?”
“How many people should I assume it’s for?”
“Three including you.”

Erwen and I could handle the issue of water pressure and breathing on our own with Elementalization, so only three of them needed to be buffed with magic. We could use a water spirit to help Amelia breathe, too, but in order to keep Elementalization active, it was better to reduce mana consumption as much as possible.
“If I don’t use any other spells, I can cast it for up to four hours.”
“That’s shorter than I thought but it should be enough. Everyone get ready. We’re all going down together.”
When I gave the order, the sailor and wizard gulped and nodded.
Jeez, you both look needlessly grim. You guys won’t have to fight, anyway.
Splash.

Once preparations were complete, I jumped into the water first. Erwen followed right behind after our Elementalization link was established, so the lack of air underwater didn’t bother me at all. My vision was as clear as if I was wearing goggles too.
Whooom.

Without any particular need for swimming, my barbarian body, which tended to sink in water, quickly descended to the bottom of the sea. When I looked up, I could see Amelia coming down after me. She had tied the navigator and wizard around the waist with a rope and was holding both lines like a leash. For reference, the navigator’s feet were heavily shackled.
Boom!
After sinking for over ten minutes, my feet landed on the ocean floor with a heavy thud. Before long, Amelia and her group arrived as well.
Click.

The seabed was virtually pitch black, so the first thing I did was turn on a light gem and insert it in the groove of my helmet. The reason I didn’t turn it on sooner was simple. If I dove with the light on, monsters could have attacked us in the middle of the water.
Shaaaaaa!
The light covered a much smaller radius compared to the ground.
Whip, whip.

Since being able to breathe didn’t mean I could speak out loud, I waved my hand and gestured for the group to get moving. This was the deep, dark sea where even compasses didn’t work. However, it wasn’t difficult to find our destination. That was because our team had a scout guiding us—Amelia.
[You have defeated a Deep Diver. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Sea Worm. EXP +3]
[You have defeated a Shell Armor. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Mad Clopter. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Marimore...]

Clearing away the various sea monsters that flocked to the light for about two hours, our destination came into sight: a corroded, destroyed underwater ruin. When I set foot inside, the pillars that were still relatively intact began to radiate light, illuminating the surrounding area.
Shaaaaaa...
Just like that, the huge temple located in the center materialized from the darkness.
“Wow...” exclaimed Erwen, the only one in the group who could communicate freely. I may not have been able to speak, but I felt the same.
It’s really incredible in real life.
For the first time in a long time, I felt like I was on a proper expedition. If I had found this place by chance without any prior game knowledge, it probably would have been even more breathtaking.
Whip, whip.
After stopping to admire the building in the distance for a moment, we passed through the empty ruins and climbed the temple’s stairs.
“Huh...?” There was a tiny room located at the top of the pyramid-shaped temple, and Erwen’s eyes widened in surprise when she saw what was inside. “It’s a portal...?”
Ah, didn’t I mention?
I thought she realized when I made Amelia take the lead. I couldn’t answer her anyway, so I just shrugged and walked into the portal.
[You have entered Atlante.]
Please, drop me an essence.

Burrow Island, also known as Atlante, was the hidden island that could be found by completing the Rock Island events and diving into the deep sea. Unlike ordinary islands, you had to cross through a portal to reach it, but this wasn’t a Rift. For one thing, there wasn’t a guardian, which was a defining feature of every Rift. The drop rate was the same as outside too. Because there was no guardian, there were no Rift Stones or Numbers Items. I normally called these places hidden levels. Other examples of hidden levels were the Labyrinth of Larcaz, where I first met the Dragon Slayer, and the Hidden World on the fifth floor, which you could enter through a mirror obtained from a Mila Roden.

[Field Effect – Atlante has activated. Status effect Hyperventilation is now active. In return for being unaffected by water, all resource consumption is doubled. Status effect Challenger is now active. If you engage in battle, you cannot escape.]
As was usually the case for these special areas, adjustments were made to us as soon as we entered. A red glow shimmered along the spot where my feet touched the ground.
This would be the Challenger effect.
As for Hyperventilation, there was no visible effect but it was already active. As proof, I was able to speak now. “You can lift Elementalization now.”
Whew, that’s much better. It was frustrating trying to communicate everything with my hands.
“Excuse me? But...” Erwen trailed off and flinched. “Huh? Mister, you just talked underwater?”
“That’s why I told you you can lift it now.”
“What a strange place...”
When Erwen lifted Elementalization, the wizard kept a close eye on my reaction before lifting the diving spell.

As always, Amelia took stock of her physical condition as soon as she found herself in a new environment. “This is a very strange feeling. It certainly feels like being in water, but it doesn’t feel uncomfortable at all. I can move just as easily as I can on land.”
The wizard and navigator also spoke in reverent tones. “So this is the Burrow Island of Atlante...”
“I’ve been on the sixth floor for over ten years but I’ve never been here in person...”
But did they belatedly start to feel anxious? “Um... so what do we do now? We won’t be much help in battle...” the navigator carefully asked.
I chuckled as I doled out instructions. “The four of you wait here and follow me in five minutes.”
“...Sorry?” The navigator tilted his head like he was worried he heard me wrong. The wizard just frowned.
“Schuitz, I’m sure you mentioned that rank-three monsters appear here?”
“Yes. That’s right. That’s too dangerous even for you, Mister...”

Amelia and Erwen expressed their concerns, which was understandable. The difficulty of Burrow Island was one of the highest of any island on the sixth floor, and the enormous number of monsters that spawned here meant it was standard to explore in units.
“Look, do as I say. Have you ever seen me willingly do something dangerous?”
“...Yes,” said Erwen.
“It’d be harder to find times you didn’t, actually,” Amelia added.
Jeez, way to hit a guy where it hurts.
“Anyway, I’m saying you don’t need to worry. Just because we can breathe and talk here doesn’t mean we aren’t still underwater.”
“Well... that’s true.”
“Call me right away if you’re in danger, Mister! Okay?” When I presented a logical argument, Erwen and Amelia didn’t object any further.
Okay, looks like they don’t need any more persuading.
Step, step.
I slowly walked down the stairs away from where the portal was located.
Shaaaaaa!

The moment I stepped on the last step, dozens of red eyes flashed in the darkness where the light of the gem did not reach. It was a Sea God Stone, a rank-five monster that appeared at the start of Atlante. It was a tower-type monster with high Physical Resistance and slow but powerful long-range attacks, incapable of moving from its specified location.
Step.
I stopped right in front of it. There was no need to even take out a weapon. After all, this was much more effective than hitting it directly.
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[...reflects 30% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
[Due to the passive skill Origin, your Natural Regeneration has maxed out.]
[Your Powerful Luck reflects 150% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
“Gahhhcha!”
[You have defeated a Sea God Stone. EXP +5]
Now, shall we go for a walk in the park?

chapters.title: Chapter 381: Atlante (4)
paragraphs: Atlante, the Burrow Island, was actually the most difficult section for someone trying to perfect a Shield Barbarian build. After all, I didn’t call the essence here my second core essence for nothing. Normally, by the time I reached this point, I only had essences of rank four or lower. Storm Gush’s Origin, Bayon’s Transcendence, and Gachabone’s Liability of Risk would be an impossible combination to achieve at this point in the game. A one-man clear was unfeasible and you had to carry it out with the right teammates and full preparation. It was only after I obtained the essence here that my combat power rose drastically and grinding for a rank-three essence could officially begin.
But somehow the order was flipped.
If I looked back on it now, it all started with the Ogre’s essence. I was lucky enough to obtain a high-level essence early on, and my growth snowballed from there.
[You have defeated a Mermal Priest. EXP +6]
[You have defeated a Lavitor. EXP +5]
[You have defeated an Undersea Guard. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Nagaculos...]

All I was doing was running forward attracting aggro, but the XP just kept rolling in. This was practically a speedrun. Of course, I had to take breaks in between. Even I didn’t have infinite MP, and as long as Hyperventilation was active and doubling resource consumption, that was especially true.
“Mister!” While I was resting for a moment, my teammates caught up to me, collecting the mana stones I left in my path. “There was an essence back there, what do you want to do with it?”
Huh? There was an essence?
I didn’t even notice it since I was just charging forward blindly. I thought it over for a moment before answering, “Just leave it.”

It would have been extremely valuable had it been the rank-four Mermal Priest, but I confirmed that one didn’t drop an essence, so there was no reason to use one of our two test tubes on an unknown essence. If the essence was rank five, we’d get a slight profit, but rank six essences were mostly a loss.
“Schuitz, how far are we now?”
“More than halfway.”
“You’ve only been moving in a straight line since we got here. Is there a reason for that?”
“We’ll hunt the monsters on the outskirts later.”
While I was speaking to Amelia, Erwen joined in. “Ah, is it because of the competition you mentioned earlier?”
That was kind of irrelevant, actually. I simply liked to focus on the most important thing first in order of priority, but I can’t say that had no influence at all. “Yes, just in case.”
Atlante was not a Rift. Once opened, the portal remained open until the labyrinth closed and adventurers were able to travel through it freely.
“What happens if we run into them?” asked Amelia.
“I don’t know.” I gave her my stock response, then added, “If they attack, fight. If not, just pass them by.”
“I see...” Amelia nodded with a somewhat uncertain expression on her face.
I thought about ignoring it, but I ended up asking anyway. “You look like you have something to say.”
“I just... wondered which scenario you would welcome more.”
“Welcome?”
“I said what I said.” When I gave her a look that demanded a more detailed answer, Amelia cautiously continued. “Schuitz, aren’t you secretly hoping the other side attacks first?”
As soon as I heard that, I had a visceral response and came up with countless explanations to defend myself. But I held them back for now. “Why are you suddenly thinking that way?”

“It’s not sudden. I’ve been thinking that more and more as I work with you.” Amelia shrugged and glanced at the navigator and wizard. I turned my head as well, following her gaze. The two people at the end of it hurriedly averted their eyes, fearing they might fall victim to my anger. I didn’t really understand.

“I never thought you of all people would be saying something like that, Emily. Then are you saying I should have let people who attacked me first go?” There was an edge to my tone despite my best efforts.
Amelia shook her head in surprise. “That’s not what I meant. It’s just...”
“Just?”
“...No, it’s nothing. I shouldn’t have said anything,” Amelia mumbled and took a step back, and I didn’t ask any more questions.
Of course, that wasn’t because I wasn’t curious. What else did she have to say after those cryptic words? Since I didn’t ask, I had no way of finding out.

“Haven’t you thought about it? Killing people if they get in the way, killing them if they’re suspicious, wondering whether every person we meet is going to harm us or not. Human life... just feels like a game. We’re madmen.”

A conversation I once had with Baekho flashed through my mind. It was a sentiment I had been able to sympathize with at the time, but the weight of it felt different now, especially the part about a human life feeling like a character in a game. One blow of a hammer could kill a person. Of course, the target was always someone I classified as worthy of death by my standards, but...
“I-I was wrong! Please!”

That had been the man who first made me get blood on my hands. The person I was when I met Hans A was not who I was now. At the time, I felt psychological resistance and had to continuously convince myself that it had to be done as I lifted my weapon. For a while after that, the feeling persisted. The hesitation disappeared, but an unease dominated my whole body every time. I couldn’t shake it even after returning to the city. Their eyes and expressions kept flashing through my mind, and I had to douse myself with cold water and intentionally empty my thoughts. Yes, I was definitely like that once upon a time. But now?
The captain on the boat... what did he look like again?

Now, I couldn’t even remember the face of a guy I killed not too long ago. The only things that came to mind when I thought of him were his equipment and his expensive valuables, and the powerful exhilaration I felt when I obtained them. Was it that I’d gotten used to living this way? Or had I slowly changed into the person I was now?
“Mister, what are you thinking so hard about?”
“It’s nothing. We’re going to rest for thirty minutes before we get moving again. You should rest too.”
I lay on the bare, muddy ground and looked up. The darkness of the labyrinth stretched out endlessly from the point where the light surrounding us ended. It was such a strange thing.

There were only four floors left above me now. If I just passed those hurdles, I could go through the Gate of the Abyss and return to the modern world. But even though I was physically much higher than I had been when I was struggling on the first and second floors, that world felt even farther away than ever.

After resting for about thirty minutes and replenishing our MP, we continued clearing the island using the same method as before. Put simply, I went ahead and wiped out the monsters while the others followed behind and collected mana stones.
If I account for all the monsters on the outskirts I’m going to kill later, our mana stone income will be considerable.

Even as I thought this, it was kind of funny. Despite the fact that we were making a decent amount here, it was nothing compared to the battle we had earlier. Although they were damaged, we now had three ships and the high-quality equipment of ten people. It was the kind of money you could never make just by killing monsters.
[Your Powerful Luck reflects 150% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
When a Critical Success rang out, the last monster chasing me down disappeared in a burst of light.
I’m already in the boss room.

Before long, I had reached the center of Atlante: a vast, vacant plot of land with dozens of pillars the size of buildings circling it. At the center of those pillars was a huge, blue egg, three or four times bigger than me even when I was using Giantization.
It looks exactly like the egg in the game.
I was about to laugh at that thought when—
[You have laid eyes on part of a legend.]
My heart pounded and I felt a strange sense of fulfillment, like I was being filled up with something.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Mythical Discovery (1/5)]
[Reward: Your Soul Power has permanently increased by +10.]
What the...? Did my MP just go up? If that’s true, that means the game’s Achievement system is applicable here too... I must have cleared quite a few Soul Power-based achievements by now.

I hadn’t been sure about this since Soul Power stats weren’t really noticeable, but it seemed I’d have to start hunting for achievements in the future too. There were some helpful achievements on the seventh floor onward.
Wait, then maybe I should have brought the others with me too.

The thought came to mind, but I decided to bring them next time. The probability of us getting an essence on the first try was low, anyway, so we could just test it next month. It was unclear to me whether locals could get Achievements in the first place.
Shaaaaaa!

When I entered the radius of the pillars, a giant vortex wrapped around them and blocked my retreat. This was pointless, in my opinion. Because of the status effect Challenger, my body wouldn’t let me run away even if I wanted to.
Step.
As I headed toward the egg in the center, the vortex outside the pillars began to rattle with even stronger vibrations, as if the sea itself was enraged by my presence.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Booms thundered through the space at regular intervals and the ground shook. The heavy reverberations grew closer and louder.
Boom!

As soon as the ground stopped shaking, I looked up. Two blue eyes were peering down at me from the deep darkness—the rank-three monster, Deep Sea Giant. Aside from in Atlante, this monster could only be found on the ninth floor. Of course, up there, the son of a bitch traveled in packs like trash mobs did, allowing it to cover for its weaknesses with numbers and making it several times more difficult to hunt.

“Serkima Dio Merder.” Just like in the game, my enemy looked down at me and growled out an unintelligible line. I hadn’t been able to tell from reading the text alone, but in real life, its voice was full of contempt.
“Behel-ahhh!” I shouted the name of my ancestral god for the first time in a long while and turned on Giantization. No one else was here anyway, right?
Dash.
Of course, the place I was sprinting toward with a battle cry was the center of the pillars where the egg was. It was the key to taking the bastard down.
Thump!
The egg kicked like it was alive. Or, rather than an egg, it’d be more accurate to call it an egg-shaped heart.
Bang!

As soon as I slammed the Demon Grinder down, the giant released a roar and flung its palm out at me, and I quickly stepped back to avoid the attack. Liability of Risk only reflected skills using resources like mana or Soul Power. There was no reason to take a regular hit that couldn’t even be reflected back.
[The Deep Sea Giant has cast Blade Torrent.]
As soon as I dodged its swipe, the giant activated a skill. Hundreds of streams of water flew at me in straight lines, drawing sharp trajectories like bullets fired underwater.
I should just let this one hit...
[Your Powerful Luck reflects 150% of the damage received back to the enemy.]
What, Critical Success from the get-go?
“Gahhhcha!” As soon as I shielded just my vitals and let the attack hit the rest of me, I heard the excited shout of a skeleton from behind me.
Chwaaa!
The blast the skeleton leveled at the Sea Giant drew a much thicker line through the water than the ones it shot at me.
“Gaaaaaah!” It looked like the damage landed because the monster staggered despite its size. It stumbled and lashed out with another regular attack. Normally I’d avoid a blow like this at all costs.
Kwaaang!
But was it because I had come here after already coating myself in rank-three essences?
This is blockable.
It wasn’t so strong that I couldn’t withstand it with a shield. The blow rattled my bones, but the damage was thankfully immediately healed with Origin.
[The Deep Sea Giant has cast Source of Life.]

In order to recover from the damage done to its body, the Giant drew on the life force stored in its heart. This was one of the Deep Sea Giant’s main skills. The Deep Sea Giants you could encounter on the ninth floor didn’t have their hearts exposed like this. They boasted an incredible healing factor and the imposing power of a rank-three monster, but down here, that didn’t mean much. There was a reason that I usually chose this guy as my first rank-three essence.
Thump.
The heart fluttered weakly, smaller than before.
Bang! Bang! Bang!

Since there was no reason to avoid the regular attacks, I stuck close to the heart and swung my hammer down on it repeatedly. The monster attempted to use various skills to stop me, and they were reflected right back at it, inflicting damage to its main body.
[The Deep Sea Giant has cast Source of Life.]
The vicious cycle repeated itself once again. The heart transferred energy to the main body, and the heart’s defenses decreased thanks to the said transfer. This process continued several more times.
Thump.
I brought my hammer down on the heart, which was now several times smaller than it had been when I first encountered it. The moment I did, I was faced with both good news and bad news.
Crack!
[You have defeated a Deep Sea Giant. EXP +7]
The first bit of good news was that I had managed to hunt a rank-three monster with more ease than ever. The second?
Shaaaaa!
An essence had appeared on my first try. But that brought me to the bad news.
God damn it.

An essence had appeared, but unfortunately, it wasn’t the color I wanted. That wasn’t an issue in this situation, though. I looked beyond the vortex, which vanished as soon as the Deep Sea Giant was killed.
He was wearing attire so casual it was hard to believe he was inside the labyrinth right now. His white skin and slim build gave off a refined air, and his platinum-blond hair was slicked up.
“Wow, what the—did you really kill that by yourself?”
An unexpected encounter awaited me.

chapters.title: Chapter 382: Us (1)
paragraphs: I didn’t even think to wonder why he was there at first.
Thump, thump, thump.
My heart pounded faster than when I had been fighting the Deep Sea Giant. It felt like an eight-ton truck had just crashed into the back of my head. I only came to my senses when he spoke.
“Wow, what the—did you really kill that by yourself?” Though I’d only conversed with him in that form a few times, that voice and that tone were things I could never forget.
Baekho Lee.
The moment I recognized that this was really happening, I realized there was an old man beside him—Fallen Scholar. For now, these were the only two I could see in the area.
He’s working with Baekho now, even though they were fighting each other back then?

My mind was all jumbled up. Aside from the fact that they were apparently teammates now, why were they here? Could it be because of me? No, wait, what happened to Erwen and Amelia, who I left behind? I told them to stay put until I got back.
“How interesting. I’ve never heard talk of anyone like you around,” Baekho said.
“Of course you have,” Fallen Scholar interjected. “You remember the man who was a hot topic not too long ago, don’t you?”
Baekho nodded. “Oh, right. Him. He does fit the description.”
“We don’t know for sure yet, though.”
“Then we can find out now. Hey, are you that guy named Schuitz or whatever?” This was an incredibly rude way to kick off a first conversation, but I was rather relieved.
...So he didn’t come looking for me. And that probably means... He’s here for Atlante itself.
We had been keeping an eye out for the people who cleared the other Red Rock Island events. It must have been these guys.
Then that means this encounter is purely coincidental...
Just as I was thinking that, he said, “When are you going to answer?”
Ha, this rude son of a bitch.
“Why don’t you reveal your identity first?”
At my question, he smiled like he liked my attitude. “Baekho Lee. You?”
“Probably the person you’re thinking of.”
“Wow, how interesting, running into a celebrity here.”
“Celebrity?”

“I heard you fought four-on-one against those bastards from Noark? How could you not be famous when you seemingly appeared out of thin air? Not to mention that elf girl Blood Spirit is looking after you.”

I didn’t have anything in particular to say to refute that. The population of people in the labyrinth decreased exponentially as you went up. Once you got to even the seventh floor, most people knew each other. The appearance of a strange and powerful man whose name and face were unknown must have seemed odd.
“Wait, that means the girl is here too,” said Fallen Scholar.
“Come to think of it, I don’t see any wizards. Looks like we missed them while teleporting over here.”
I once again breathed a sigh of relief at their conversation. If what they were saying was true, that meant Erwen and Amelia were safe.

“So, what’s your business here?” I asked, walking in the direction of the essence. If a fight broke out, I planned to absorb this essence right away. Although the color was different than what I wanted, I figured it would come in handy for now.
Just then, Baekho spoke in a playful tone. “Stop right there. Don’t touch the essence for now.”
Essence?

This was a clue that would help me analyze the current situation. It seemed Baekho was here for the Deep Sea Giant’s essence. Normally that would have been enough of an explanation for me, but my brain, working overtime on pure survival instinct, asked questions I would have otherwise overlooked.
Why come here to find one instead of the ninth floor where Deep Sea Giants appear in groups?
This gave way to one of two potential explanations.
“Come on, didn’t you say you beat the game at Times Ten? In ten years, you’ll be like me. Realistically, I have no more areas to improve...”
One: Despite his claims back then, Baekho’s level wasn’t actually that high. Two: He for some reason was not able to go to the ninth floor right now.
Tap.
I stopped walking toward the essence for now since I had no idea how that lunatic would react if I got any closer. But it wouldn’t be good to come across as meek. “This is my loot.”
At my slightly belligerent tone, Baekho raised his hands in a gesture for me to calm down. “Now, now. No need to be so sensitive. I only stopped you to see if we can make a deal.”
“A deal?”
“What I need is that red essence over there. If you don’t really need it, why don’t we make a trade?”

To be honest, none of what he said really made sense to me. I ended up firing back, “Why would you bother making a trade?” As was evident from his rude attitude, Baekho considered me beneath him. Why was he still proposing a deal, leaving the easier way on the table?

Baekho’s answer was completely unexpected. “So, what, should I kill you and steal it? To be honest, I’m annoyed about coming all this way for nothing... but it’s not like you cheated or anything. Whining just because you got to it first would be trashy of me.”
“...What if I refuse the deal?”
“Well? Then I’ll be disappointed and come back next time.”

This thought process was much too normal. It left me speechless, but looking back, I kind of got it. This guy’s ultimate goal was to return to Earth, right? He probably followed some kind of personal code of his own, just as I had until now.
“Fine.”

Surprisingly, the situation was proceeding more peacefully than I thought it would. In the worst-case scenario, I even considered the possibility of a melee. At this point, however, I didn’t think things would get that far. The proposal of a trade wasn’t bad for me, either.
“What will you give me in exchange for the essence?”
Baekho seemed to contemplate this for a moment before posting the item in the trade window. “Another essence of a Deep Sea Giant. I’ve been killing them regularly these days. I have blue and green—”
I immediately cut him off and answered, “I’ll go with green.” This was even more good news, at least for now.
“What, you wanted that one?”

“Green sells for a higher price on average. Besides, I can save on a test tube.” Baekho nodded in acceptance at my answer and took out a test tube from his sub-space. “But how can I trust that comes from a Deep Sea Giant?”
“If I was going to scam you, I wouldn’t have proposed a deal, would I?”
Jeez, don’t glare at me just for being a little suspicious.
“So, the deal? Are you going to accept it or not.”
“...I’ll trust you this once.”
In response, Baekho tossed me the test tube. Throwing it was an act of disrespect I didn’t quite abide by, but well, I still caught it.
“Now that you have what you want, can you get out of the way? This old man is too scared to go over there.”
When I widened the distance between us, Fallen Scholar stepped forward to put the essence into a test tube. That concluded our trade.
So it wasn’t for Baekho. Then is he planning on feeding it to a teammate?
As I was quietly pondering this, Baekho spoke to me. “Schuitz, was it?”
“That’s correct.”
“So uptight. Speak comfortably.”
“This is comfortable to me.”
“If you say so. Anyway, I want to ask you something, is that cool?” When I gestured with my eyes for him to go on, Baekho decided to be direct. “Are you Bjorn Yandel?”
This guy really doesn’t have brakes, huh?
Thump!
My heart dropped, but I didn’t show it. I reacted like I found the question ridiculous. “Why are you asking that?”

“Someone with an unrecognized name and face suddenly appears out of nowhere, and that elf girl is following that person around, calling him ‘Mister?’ I’m sure she’s not a fool, so that’s strange, no?”
It was sound logic. The members of the Round Table suspected me for the same reason as well.
“So, your answer?” Baekho glared daggers into me. It was obvious what he was doing.
He’s using a lie detector ability. If I keep my mouth shut, he’ll interpret that however he wants. He may even get aggressive.

I quickly got my thoughts in order. There were two contenders for Baekho’s presumed lie detection skill. One gave you the ability to distinguish between true and false, and the other only identified lies. You may argue these were the same thing, but they were completely different because of the gift I had from Auril Gavis. If he had the latter ability and his skill didn’t react to my words, he’d accept whatever I said as truth.
...I might even be able to figure out which essence he has.
It didn’t take long to come to a decision. “I’m not Bjorn Yandel,” I answered, my eyes locked on his.
Baekho chuckled. “Really? That’s unfortunate.”

Based on his voice and expression, he didn’t seem to doubt me at all. Thanks to that, I was able to identify one of the many essences he must have taken. After all, if it were the first option, he wouldn’t have been able to accept my statement so easily. It would only have been natural for him to question why something I said couldn’t be categorized as either true or false.
Well, I expected this, seeing as he didn’t doubt anything I said earlier, but this confirms it.
With this, I’d identified a way to gain an upper hand in conversations with Baekho. But I wasn’t satisfied with that alone. “Can I ask you a question too?”
“Yeah, well, give and take. You can ask.”
I immediately obtained a free pass to pose a question of my own. I took a moment to think it over.
“Aren’t you going to ask?”
There were mountains of questions I wanted to ask.
When are you going to use the Stone of Revival you’re rumored to have? How did you join forces with Fallen Scholar?
And...
“That woman is now Baekho Lee’s teammate.”
Why did Clown say Missha is your teammate? Where is Missha? How the hell did you trick her?

I swallowed back the many questions I wanted to ask right now. The moment I did, he’d show an even greater interest in me than he already was. Now was not the time. After all, I had no idea how he’d react when I told him I was Hansu Lee. I still didn’t know what kind of dots this guy was connecting.
“Baekho Lee,” I called, and he chuckled at my best attempt at pronouncing his name as a local. “Since we’re talking about Bjorn Yandel, let me ask this.”
“What is it?”
“Why did you spread the rumor that Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit?”
Baekho’s mouth tightened ever so slightly. “You... You already knew who I was?”
“Of course. You’re famous.”

“Really? Well, anyone who’s anyone seems to know me these days.” Baekho was momentarily thrown off by my question but he didn’t seem suspicious. “Anyway... I guess Blood Spirit managed to figure that out, huh? That I was the one who started that rumor.”
“So, your answer?”
Baekho tapped a finger on his waist, mulling over my question.
“His comrades are coming.”
Before he could say anything, however, Fallen Scholar spoke up, having finished storing the essence in a test tube. Baekho’s expression shifted accordingly. “Really? Then I guess we have to bounce.”
“Is there even a need for that?”
“It’d be annoying to run into them. Maybe not for me, but they’ll definitely go after your guns a-blazing. Kitty said so herself: don’t touch his former teammates.”
“But how will she be able to find out what happens here?”
At Fallen Scholar’s words, I reflexively gripped my hammer tighter.
Right at that moment, Baekho’s chipper smile dropped and his cheerful voice went cold. “...Gramps, don’t cross the line.”
“...It was a joke. I’ll use a Multi Teleportation spell.”
While I was relieved about that, I was also enraged. “Kitty” had to refer to Missha. I was suddenly hit with a sense of loss I hadn’t felt when I’d only been told Missha had become Baekho’s teammate.
“Wait,” I said, beating all my emotions down. “I want you to answer my question before you go.”
“Oh, right. You asked why I started that rumor, right?” Baekho, who looked as if he had completely forgotten, shot Fallen Scholar a look. Fallen Scholar tutted and nodded his head.

For some reason that tutting sound gave me déjà vu. I felt like I’d been in this exact situation before. Why? Why did it seem familiar? The moment that thought came to mind, a magic circle formed around Fallen Scholar, emitting a blue light.
Shaaaaaa!
What’s happening?
This turn of events was so sudden that it took me a while to figure out what was going on.
Is it an ambush?

Just as that possibility popped into my confused mind, Baekho proceeded to put on the most obvious act I’d ever seen. “Ah! What! Gramps! Don’t turn on teleportation in the middle of a conversation! I can’t answer him then! Schuitz, right? Sorry, I’ll tell you the next time I see you. It’s not because it’s a hard question to answer, really. Okay? Okay—”
Flash!
Baekho’s voice fizzled out and disappeared the moment the light flared. It was so ridiculous that I was rendered speechless.
Squeeze.
Right, I forgot he was Korean. It had been a while since I’d been played. Ever since I arrived in this world, I was always the one playing with someone else.
No, wait...
A thought belatedly occurred to me, and I quickly shattered the test tube.
[The Essence of the Deep Sea Giant is being absorbed into your soul.]
Fortunately, the essence was real.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 7
Spirit: 521.3 (New +78)
Special Ability: 1,807.65 (New +62.4)
Item Level: 8305
General Combat Power: 5866.60 (New +371.41)
Acquired Essences: Orc Hero - Rank 5  Ogre - Rank 3  Bayon - Rank 3  Storm Gush - Rank 3  Vol-Herchan - Rank 3  Gachabone - Rank 6  Deep Sea Giant - Rank 3 (New)]

chapters.title: Chapter 383: Us (2)
paragraphs: “Mister!”
Right when I finished confirming the essence, I saw Erwen in the distance. She was leading the rest of the group over. It seemed she got worried since I was taking so long.
Tsk, I told that girl to stay put until I got back.

“Are you finished? Are you hurt anywhere?” Erwen quickly reached me and inspected me up and down worriedly. Amelia consciously stopped a ways away with the wizard and sailor so they wouldn’t overhear our conversation.
I guess she really wants to save him.

For some reason, that was the vibe I got from Amelia’s actions. I guessed ignorance really was bliss sometimes. The more he learned about us, the less of a chance the navigator had of getting home alive, so she was being careful not to let him hear anything at all. She would have probably realized that was why I was making them follow me at a distance too.
Anyway, judging by everyone’s expressions, it looks like they have no idea Baekho and Fallen Scholar were here.

Thankfully, it didn’t seem they’d disobeyed my instructions to wait, which were made with a potential encounter with an opponent in mind. Or, should I say I was glad they had at least waited to break the rules until this particular moment? If a fight had broken out, the side with one more person would have had a better chance of winning. Because of the field effect Challenger, it would have been impossible for me to run away if a battle began. Erwen and Amelia no longer needed to be protected unconditionally like my former teammates. They were powerhouses capable of carrying their own weight in any given situation.
“But... I sensed mana on the way here. What was that?” Erwen asked, detecting the remnants of the Mass Teleportation spell.
I thought it over for a while before ultimately dodging the question. “I don’t know.”

“Really? Well... I have heard about special mana waves occurring periodically in Rifts and other places like that.” As expected, Erwen accepted my answer without much suspicion. She probably thought she might have been just picking up on a natural phenomenon considering this was a special area with little known information. Or she wholeheartedly believed I had no reason to lie. Maybe that was why I felt a bit guilty.
It’s better this way.

Fallen Scholar was the bastard who had killed Daria, Erwen’s older sister. Unlike Clown, he was directly involved in her death. If I talked about Baekho, I’d inevitably have to discuss the encounter with Fallen Scholar. There was no reason to shake up her emotional state when it was finally starting to normalize.
And there’s no reason to talk about Baekho if I’m going to leave out Fallen Scholar.
After I exchanged a few more words with Erwen, Amelia led the wizard and navigator over. Then she asked a question. “Schuitz, did you get what you wanted?”
“Yes, luckily enough.” I left it at that. I’d tell her about the deal later.

Once the conversation was over, we started exploring again. We hadn’t been able to stop by anywhere else since we traveled in a straight line on the way here. The other regions would be riddled with monsters. Among them were monsters I hadn’t defeated yet, and also ones with essences that sold at a very high price.
Step.
I took the first step. “Then I’ll go first. Follow behind me.”
Our hunting strategy was the same as before. I’d clear the path ahead and destroy the monsters, and these guys would follow behind and collect mana stones.
This time, I should experiment.
Now that I had a new essence, I planned to conduct a performance test as I went this time. My body hadn’t adapted to the increase in stats yet, either.
Since it’s a rank-three, I can feel a big difference.
The Deep Sea Giant’s essence came with a unique stat that made the distinction even more noticeable.
[Deep Sea Giant]
[Strength: +55
Physical Resistance: +35
Natural Regeneration: +35
Mana Resistance: +35
Dark Resistance: +55
Endurance: +40
Adaptability: +70]

The physical stats were average for rank-three essences and most were of high value, but it’d be hard to call this essence rare. These were all great stats, but they were also stats that could easily be found in most essences—save for Adaptability, which was at the end of the list.
All it did in the game was reduce a debuff’s effect in proportion to its duration.
In reality, it felt a bit different. Of course, the aforementioned information was definitely applicable.
Step, step.

The Adaptability stat seemed to have activated and I became more comfortable walking in the water. Not that my movements were restricted in the first place, but now if I didn’t concentrate on the sensation, it didn’t even feel like I was in water. Well, if I had just dived into the ocean instead of coming to this place, which notably allowed people to maneuver around unaffected by the water, the effects probably wouldn’t be as strong.
Should I check the passive skill now?
To use the passive I hadn’t yet been able to test out, I activated Giantization. This was because the Deep Sea Giant’s passive skill only reacted with transformation-type abilities.
[You have cast Giantization. Your Threat Level and Physical Attributes increase in proportion to your increase in size.]
With Giantization, Physique increased by approximately 1.77 times, which raised Threat Level, which then helped attract monster aggro.
[You have used a transformation-type ability. Due to the effect of Evolving Shell, the amount of Soul Power consumed by the ability is reduced by half, and your highest stat increases by 1.5 times.]
On top of that, Evolving Shell got a buff.
[By the authority of the transcendental body, the effect of Evolving Shell has increased by 1.5 times. Your Strength has increased by 2.25 times.]

This was the key difference from the Shield Barbarian build I usually used. Since the Ogre’s essence was filling the slot that usually went to Steel Giant (Rank Four), somehow Strength was my highest stat—even higher than my Physical Resistance.
Welp, that’ll make it tough to reach the third stage of Evolving Shell.

Of course, that was only for now. It wouldn’t pose a problem in the final phase of my cultivation. Once I got my hands on Bellarios’s essence, I’d just need to focus on Physical Resistance when building up my stats.
[Your Physique will grow in proportion to your Strength stat.]
While at it, I switched Transcendence from passive mode to active mode and tried using Giantization.
Slide.
When I looked down to check, I could see the ceiling of the historic ruins I’d had to look up at earlier below me.
I must be over twenty feet tall.

I’d have to take exact measurements later to know for sure, but that was the height I got from eyeballing it. And considering the Gachabone’s essence made me shrink, it was safe to say I was much bigger than before. Even though my Physique had grown this much, however, my Strength values were similar to before I turned on Transcendence. This was because the multiplier applied to Strength had decreased from 2.25 to 1.15 times.
Still, it looks like the other values have all gone up accordingly so it’s not a loss.
The main con of using Transcendence as an active skill was a reduction in Soul Power, not stats. There was a big difference between burning 75 percent and burning 50 percent.
Well, with my current MP, I can sustain Giantization indefinitely even with Transcendence disabled.

In Dungeon and Stone, the time it took for your MP to regenerate was proportional to the total amount of MP you had. I was level seven and had gotten my hands on some MP stats here and there, so my total amount of MP was similar to that of most wizards.
I’m finally on track.
In order to get a chance to adapt to my much higher vantage point, I left Transcendence on. Although we were underwater, the air at twenty feet had the kind of tang that made a man’s heart flutter.
...I wonder how big I’ll become if I erase the Gachabone’s essence?

It was still too early to be fantasizing, but I pictured myself using Giantization with my base height increased from six feet to seven and a half. I couldn’t be sure, but I had a feeling I wouldn’t have any issue wrestling Riakis, the Lord of the Third Floor, with my bare hands in that state.
Smash, smash, smash!

Picturing that future in my head, I continued to swing my hammer. That was because Transcendence only applied to one skill at a time. In my current state, killing monsters using Liability of Risk’s reflex damage and using direct damage took the same time.
[You have cast Swing.]
Even if I got hit, I healed right away, so I didn’t bother with defense and focused only on playing whack-a-mole.
[You have defeated a Riu Moby Dick. EXP +6]

The monsters went ballistic as I swung my super-huge Demon Grinder at them with my increased Strength stat, disappearing into bursts of light. But with how much I was using Swing, I could feel my MP decreasing in real time.
[You have cast Soul Dive.]

So I used my new active skill. Of the seven possible active skills Deep Sea Giants had—including Blade Torrent, Source of Life, and Giant’s Blood—this was the one that corresponded with the green essence, and it was a bit unusual. While active, it consumed no MP. Or, rather, should I say it was just the opposite?
Inhale.
As I took a deep breath in, I felt the emptiness within me begin to fill up again.
[Your Soul Power will regenerate at a rate proportional to the amount of Soul Power you have consumed.]

It was an MP recovery skill that didn’t need to consume MP. Instead, the skill came with a cooldown time, which in the game was about thirty minutes. It may not seem like a big deal, but it was a very good skill. You could use it when you were in a hurry and significantly reduce the amount of breaks you needed to take in the middle of hunting to recover your MP.
More importantly, it can counter that son of a bitch...

The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos, had a Dragon Speech called Silence of the Soul. With this skill, I could counter it. Even in a state of Soul Exhaustion, I would be able to bounce back to my original condition by using it once.
Then I’ve prepared more than enough.
Bashing in the heads of the monsters coming at me from all sides, I grinned as I recalled a vow I once etched into my heart.
“Can you... win?”

The day that I experienced my first loss since waking up in the cold-hearted body of a warrior, I swallowed my helplessness and made a promise. I would survive, whatever it took. And someday, when I no longer needed something like a fluke to win, I would definitely go find him.
“We will meet again, dragon man.”
Smash!
That day had finally come.

On day five of exploring Burrow Island, I finished hunting the monsters whose EXP could only be acquired here. Even after that, we continued hunting on the island. There were tons of islands I still needed to clear outside, but the mana stone profit here was substantial. After all, this was a special level, right? In return for the high difficulty, most special levels had a good payout. On top of that, hunting here had become much easier for me than hunting on the fifth floor.
Still, I don’t plan on wasting time looking for Red Rock Islands just to come back here.
Anyway, as I continued my hunting speedrun, I found quite a few essences. As a result of my slight greed, I was able to store a rank-four essence in one of the two test tubes.
It would have been better if there had been a Deep Sea Giant’s essence...

One rank-four essence was achievement enough, but it was still a bit disappointing. There was more than one Deep Sea Giant in Burrow Island. If you walked around long enough, you had a low probability of encountering one, but none of them coughed up essences. That made sense. Unlike the one I found in the vortex-covered underwater temple, drop rate modifications didn’t apply to regular monsters in the area.

“Schuitz.” As I was running through the events of the previous days, Amelia came and sat next to me. It was clear she had something to say, and I was sure she didn’t come to ask for a longer break. “The labyrinth closes tomorrow.”
Ah, so that’s what she came to talk about.
It was the kind of short statement I’d come to expect from Amelia, but it wasn’t hard to understand the hidden meaning behind it. She was even glancing at the sleeping sailor and wizard as she spoke.
I guessed my silence and lack of immediate response frustrated her because when she opened her mouth again, she was much more direct. “What are you going to do?” she asked.

“The wizard will be killed.” That decision was far too easy, as I had never planned on letting him live in the first place. After all, wizards weren’t morons. They were lofty and arrogant and didn’t easily forget grudges. “As long as the Magic Tower is there, he’ll be hard to control when he’s in the city.”
“I see. All right. And?” Amelia once again glanced at the navigator and I immediately stood up.
Whoom!

Standing by the wizard’s head, I raised my hammer up high. It was a familiar situation I’d been in once before. Hans A, my night companion, had stood over me like this while I was dozing off. Of course, that guy and I were different, in that I didn’t fail.
Smash!
The wizard’s body went slack in his sleep. He didn’t even let out a single sound.

“H-Heek!” The navigator must have woken up to the commotion because he immediately shot up to his feet. “I-I’ll keep quiet for the rest of my life! I-I’ll stop adventuring too!” The man dropped flat on his face in a bow. Considering I was above him holding a bloody hammer, this was a bold move.
...It’d definitely be a waste to kill him.
I glanced at Amelia. She remained silent in a way that told me she would go along with whatever decision I made, but I saw a yearning deep in her eyes.
“Emily.”
“Speak.”
“Can you keep an eye on him so that he doesn’t get up to any funny business in the city?”
“You don’t have to worry about that.”
“Your reasoning?”
“I’ve already mixed poison into his food and administered only a day’s worth of antidote.” Her response was casual, but that only served to make her sound more trustworthy to me.
On the other hand, just now realizing his life was under our total control, the navigator’s shoulders jumped. “Eek...!”
At the sight, I thought it over one last time and soon came to a decision. “Nguyen Rockrobe, right?”
“Do as she says from now on. Got it?”
“Yes! Of course!”
We thus added an experienced navigator to our party, unpaid.

chapters.title: Chapter 384: Us (3)
paragraphs: [The labyrinth is now closed. You are being transported to Rafdonia.]

I felt the sunlight of the outside world on my skin for the first time in almost two months. Perhaps because I had spent the past few days in Atlante deep under the sea, the light felt even stronger than usual.
Humans definitely need light.
Taking a moment to look up at the gloomy sky like the rest of the adventurers around me, I quickly headed to the checkpoint.
“Over here!” Erwen, who had arrived first, waved at me. When I joined her in line, it wasn’t long before Amelia arrived.
“You’re late.”
“It took me a surprisingly long time to find him,” Amelia answered and glanced at the navigator, who was awkwardly standing to her right.
“I guess it was true they entered through the square in District Seven with us.”
“This guy doesn’t lie.”
Jeez, how long has it been since you met, again? How can you be so sure?
I was a little dumbfounded, but I didn’t let it show. “Were there any issues?”
“None. He stayed put and waited until I came to get him.” Amelia’s voice was full of pride. Was she that pleased that he had listened to her?

On the other hand, the navigator Auyen Rockrobe seemed to finally process his situation. “Hehehe...” As soon as his eyes met mine, he put on a business-like smile. I kind of felt bad for him, but since they were the ones who targeted us first, I also thought it was karma.
“It’s our turn now.”

After waiting in line for a while, we soon reached the front, exchanged all our mana stones for money, and passed through the checkpoint. A street full of people appeared before us. From here, we moved in a different formation. Amelia was positioned at the very back and the navigator was right in front of her.
“Haha... I-I’m not going to run away...”
“You could get lost while following us.”

“I’ve lived in District Seven for twenty years...” the sailor mumbled, but he didn’t try to break out of formation as we traveled through the crowded streets and arrived at our home. “This is the place...?” Eventually, we arrived at a three-story mansion. As we walked past the high walls and entered the yard, the navigator gaped in admiration. But I guessed he noticed that something was off as he did. “Why are the windows all...” The navigator wasn’t able to finish his sentence. His eyes were locked on the boarded-up windows.
“Don’t worry about it. It’s a security measure.”
“Ah, right...” He didn’t say much but the navigator’s eyes and expression held a mix of both curiosity and fear. He seemed to be wondering who the hell we were to be living in a house like this.
Come to think of it, I think he’s already figured out who Erwen is... I should check on that later.
Once we crossed through the garden and into the house, we decided to assign one of the remaining rooms to the navigator after some discussion. It was a room located in the basement.
“...Basement? We have a basement?”
When I tilted my head, Erwen blushed shyly. “I deliberately looked for a house with one. Since, you never know...”
Well, I had heard rich people often had panic rooms in their houses.
Creak, creak, creak.

Despite feeling somewhat uncomfortable, I watched Erwen remove the carpet and operate the mechanism to reveal the stairs. As we headed down, a space that seemed to have been designed as a storage room appeared before us. It was completely empty, as we had never filled it with anything. In the deepest part was a thick iron door with a lock.
Rattle.
When Erwen took out the key and opened the door, a room with a large bed appeared. I didn’t know why, but there were also restraints on the wall.

“This... isn’t a room, it’s a prison...” The navigator’s face paled as he took in his assigned room. Actually, I felt similarly. For some reason, chills ran down my spine as soon as I saw the room in the basement. Well, it wasn’t my problem, though.

“...Prison? It’s just an ordinary room. Look, there’s even a toilet and bathroom. It’s nice you don’t have to share it with anyone.” I cleared my throat. “Ahem-hem, anyway, I’m going to head up. I’m suddenly not feeling well...”
Ugh, why is my heart pounding so much? It’s not like I’m claustrophobic.
When I shoved the navigator into the room and closed the door, Erwen quickly locked it.
Rattle.
“W-Wait! Wait!”
Bang, bang, bang!
The navigator banged on the door but all of us pretended not to hear it.
“Can I hold onto the key?” asked Amelia.
“Sure.”
Amelia took custody of the key, thus settling the issue of the navigator’s sleeping quarters. I was sure she’d take care of feeding him too.
There was something else I’d been wondering. “Emily, is that poison real? A poison that kills you if you don’t take the antidote every day? I’ve never heard of it.”

It sounded like something a Poison Witch from a Wuxia novel could do. The typical cliché was that the demonic cult used poison like that to threaten and manipulate members of the righteous sect into becoming their subordinates. If this was a real thing, I could think of various ways it could be useful in the future.
“I guess you have a naïve side to you, too, Schuitz.”
“There’s no way a poison like that exists. Thankfully, that guy doesn’t seem to know much about poison.”
“Ah...” So it was a bluff after all. I was only checking because it seemed kind of possible.

“Whaaat?” Just then, Erwen recoiled. “The poison... it doesn’t exist...?” For some reason, she sounded very disappointed. I couldn’t just ignore that, so I asked if she needed it for something. Erwen averted her eyes. “Y-You never know...”
What exactly don’t I know?
I wanted to ask her to elaborate but I stopped, figuring I wouldn’t get a proper answer anyway.

The first day after returning from the labyrinth, everyone spent time resting in their respective rooms. Starting the next day, however, we got busy. We weren’t just dealing with one or two bits of loot, after all.
“Erwen, you should go with me,” said Amelia.
“Eh? Me? But you can do it alone—”
“Are you saying you can’t do it for Schuitz?”
“...That’s not what I meant.”
From the second day onward, Erwen and Amelia were in and out of the house exchanging the loot for cash, and I spent most of my time guarding the house.
“Schuitz, I’ve prepared the food for him and set it out on the table in order, so just bring it to him on time.”
Aside from going down to the basement every breakfast, lunch, and dinner, my daily routine was nothing special.
On the third day, someone came to see me. “Raven.”
“I was going to come yesterday but I was a little busy. Can I come in?”
“Of course.”
When she entered, Raven glanced around the house and asked, “Where are the other two?”
“They went out to take care of the loot.”
“Hmm...” Her humming sounded a bit strange. When I asked if something was wrong, Raven answered that it was nothing. “I was just thinking about how they’re doing the work I used to do.”
“I’m sorry about back then. You were the only person I could entrust that task to.”
“I didn’t say that to get an apology from you. More importantly... it’s not something that you need to apologize for.”
“Thanks for thinking that way.”
I guided Raven to the living room and sat down facing her. We briefly filled each other in on our goings-on.
“How were things on your end?” Raven asked.
“It all ended up working out somehow. You guys?”
“Same as usual. It’s not like the war will end overnight, after all.”
“I see.”

I felt a wall between us I didn’t feel back when we used to be teammates. She probably felt the same. Since we were both in the labyrinth, we were technically seeing each other for the first time in two months.
Boom, boom, boom!
Just then, thumps rang out from below.
“I think I just heard something from the basement...”
Ah, it’s already past lunchtime.
“We had some work done on the pipes—I think it’s because of that. Don’t worry about it.” It’d be a bit shady to tell her we were holding someone hostage so I just came up with a random excuse.

Thankfully, Raven didn’t seem suspicious. Anyway, our conversation proceeded smoothly after that, and in the process, I was able to learn what happened during this expedition. Well, the most important information came up at the end.
“Ah, and Mr. Y—no, Mr. Schuitz, about that thing you asked about.”
“That thing?”
“The National Incorporation Bill.”
“Did you find out who brought it up?”
“Yes. It was the Countess of Peprok.”

“Peprok...?” I was surprised. After all, that was the surname of someone I used to be close with—Ragna Litaniel Peprok. I wondered if it was just someone with the same last name, but I couldn’t seem to shake a nagging suspicion. Last I checked, there was no noble family named Peprok anywhere in Rafdonia. “Raven, what’s the countess’s name?”
“Ragna Peprok, I believe. Her name was something like that.”
“...What?”
It’s really her? But her middle name is omitted...
“...Do you know her?”
“Perhaps. Can you tell me more about the Peprok family?”
“They’re textbook fallen nobles. They were even erased from the Royal Noble Department, but they were reinstated a year ago without anyone noticing.”
What the—then it’s only natural I couldn’t find her when I looked two years ago. Does that mean Ragna really is the countess Raven’s talking about?

While I was thinking this, Raven lowered her voice and continued. “I looked more into it because that part didn’t make sense to me. It’s not rare for fallen nobles to be reinstated, but how did they build up enough political power to participate in a royal council meeting in such a short period of time? The answer was simple. They had a sponsor.”
“Who was it?”
“The prime minister of Rafdonia, Marquess Tercerion.”
“...What?”
I felt a headache coming on. Aside from the fact that the Countess of Peprok was Ragna, if what Raven was saying was true, the said countess was on the same side as the prime minister.
“Then... that means it was the prime minister who insisted on pushing the National Incorporation bill...” I blurted without thinking.

Raven shook her head slightly. “No. That’s a bit unclear. In fact, they say the prime minister himself shouted that it was nonsense the moment the National Incorporation bill was raised. The other nobles were so surprised that the discussion quickly fizzled out.”
“Maybe he was just putting on a show.”
“A show...?”
“A staged play. Let the other nobles see how angry this makes him so that they don’t get any ideas.”
“Ah...” Raven’s lips parted like she’d never considered that possibility. “I guess you’re well-versed in politics too...?”
“I’m just interested in people.” Of course, this was just speculation and I had no way of knowing the truth. I still had too little information. “Raven, can you look more into Countess Peprok?”
“I will. I still have a lot of questions about her too.”
“Thanks as always.”
“Then I’ll get going now.”
“Sure, get home safe.” My meeting with Raven that day ended there.

A week later, on a sunny afternoon, Erwen and Amelia were once again out in the commercial district collecting the proceeds of our loot sales. Knights wearing the crest of the royal family broke down the front door and invaded our home.
Kwaaang!
“Riehen Schuitz, you are under arrest on suspicion of colluding with Noark.”
Ha, so it’s finally come to this.

chapters.title: Chapter 385: Us (4)
paragraphs: Kwaaang!
Out of the blue, a group of knights burst through the door while I was napping on the sofa. Even half-awake, their words caught my ear.
“Riehen Schuitz, you are under arrest on suspicion of collusion with Noark.”
Collusion, huh?

This was likely just an excuse to arrest me. They probably planned to arrest me on any charge and use that as a jumping-off point to start a full-fledged investigation. No matter how they looked at it, there must have been a lot of things about me that were suspicious.
But they came sooner than I thought.

To be honest, I was mentally prepared for this to some extent. Going around with Erwen attracted attention, and I even ended up involved in a battle with Raven. I figured something like this was liable to happen at any time.
Clunk.

The knights occupied the living room and surrounded me in an instant. They didn’t seem to be underestimating me at all. They kept their distance and leveled their swords at me, their eyes locked on the target.
“Riehen Schuitz, drop your weapon,” the knight who appeared to be the commander ordered me.
While all this was happening, I took stock of the situation.
Now, then... What should I do from here?

First, I didn’t see a wizard. That meant that everyone who came to arrest me was a knight. Considering the reputation knights had in PVP, this could be interpreted as excessive manpower, but it was good news for me. It meant that if need be, I could wreck them all and run away.
The problem is that the moment I do that, I’ll no longer be able to stay in this city...
This was an option I could only choose in the worst-case scenario. More importantly, it would conflict with my ultimate goal of reclaiming the name Bjorn Yandel.
It’s about time to enter the lion’s den.

Ultimately, to get my name back, I had no choice but to make contact with the palace. Of course, my anxiety would be significantly reduced if I had a way to figure out their intentions beforehand, but it wasn’t like I knew nothing.
“...The palace already knows the GM’s identity.”

The GM was the psychological pillar for all players. According to the information that Soul Queen gave us, the palace knew the GM’s identity. No, they didn’t just know it—they purposefully controlled the flow of information so that it wouldn’t be revealed to the outside world. That meant the palace didn’t kill evil spirits indiscriminately. Even in the worst-case scenario where I was exposed as Bjorn Yandel and an evil spirit, there was room for negotiation.
It’s worth getting a feel for how much they know.
Once I was done deliberating, I immediately parted my lips. “Since you say there are charges against me, I’ll participate in the investigation, but let me inform my comrades before I leave.”

The reason for this request was very simple. They should already know that the comrade I was talking about was Erwen. If they refused, there was room to interpret this situation in a more optimistic light. This would mean they deliberately chose a time when Erwen was out, which was consistent with the presumption that they didn’t know enough about me to also want to interrogate Erwen.
“If you’re talking about Blood Spirit, there’s no need. You’ll be able to see her if you come with us.”
My mind momentarily went blank at the commander’s words.
What? Did they take away Erwen too? Then what about Amelia, who was with her? No, let’s first check if he’s telling the truth.
“What’s your proof that Erwen is there?”
The commander answered my question without any hesitation. “I swear on the royal family of Rafdonia.”
Ha, that means he’s not lying...
This wasn’t good. Arresting Erwen, who was beloved by the elves? That meant the palace had enough justification and grounds to arrest us both.
Damn it all...
I wanted to resist arrest and run away right now, but I couldn’t do that while Erwen was captured.
“I will say this for the last time. Riehen Schuitz, drop your weapon. Otherwise, your actions will be considered treason against the palace.”

In time with the commander’s ultimatum, I felt a high-density mana strong enough to be sensed by even a barbarian with no magical talent flare up outside the mansion. So, they did have a wizard, after all. They were just on standby somewhere out of sight.
Thorough bastards.
I lowered my hammer weakly.
Slide.
For now, there was no other option. The only thing I could do was stay on guard.
After I lowered my hammer, things proceeded quickly. I placed the weapon in sub-space as instructed and the knights came forward to collect my sub-space ring.

“The items will be returned in perfect condition once the charges are cleared.” The commander’s demanding tone was now polite. In fact, the treatment I received was far from how you’d treat a criminal. “A carriage has been prepared.”

As soon as I stepped out, surrounded by knights, a carriage was waiting for me. It was visibly different from the ones used to escort prisoners. As opposed to a cart with steel bars, it was the kind of elaborate carriage only a wealthy aristocrat would use.
“Get on. We will be going to the royal capital, Karnon.”

My only companion in the carriage was the commander. The rest of the knights rode on horses, flanking us like an escort. It was the kind of royal treatment I never received even when I was Baronet Yandel.
Drag, slide.
The carriage started to glide down the main road and I studied the commander sitting across from me.
“Is something making you uncomfortable?”
You think something wouldn’t be?
I thought this was a ridiculous question but it wouldn’t be smart to have an attitude here. “What are my real charges?” I asked cautiously.
“As I said earlier—”
“Don’t say collusion. I know if that were true, I wouldn’t be treated like this.”
The commander pursed his lips, troubled, but I guessed he realized I would only continue to pester him if he kept quiet. “There’s not much I can tell you right now.”
“Still—”
“You will find out once we arrive at the royal capital.”
The commander put his foot down and ended the conversation. In the end, I was only able to learn two things.
“What’s going to happen to me now?”
“He will decide that.”
First, someone very high-ranking was waiting for me.
“Was there someone else with Erwen when you took her away?”
“From what I heard, she was alone.”
And second, Amelia’s safety wasn’t compromised.

Afterward, we rode without much conversation. The carriage ran along the main road and stopped after about an hour. The military platform in District Seven had teleportation circles that connected you to each district. Originally it was a facility designed for the speedy transportation of troops during emergencies, but now it was usually used as a means of transportation for nobility. For reference, this was my first time here. I became eligible to use it once I became a baronet, but it was ridiculously expensive.
Interesting that this is how I get to use it.
Without having to get off the carriage, we rode into the teleportation circle and soon arrived at the royal capital’s military platform.
This isn’t the royal palace.

The carriage carrying me instead entered a mansion located near the palace. Thanks to that, I was able to figure out who brought me here, as their family crest was right at the entrance of the estate—a shield with a bamboo-leaf oak tree drawn on it. This was the symbol of the Marquess of Tercerion, and it was safe to say almost everyone in the city could recognize it. For decades, the king had been absent from the public eye. Marquess Tercerion, the prime minister of Rafdonia, had been performing most official duties on his behalf.
The kingdom’s second-in-command, huh?
Since the commander wore the crest of the palace, I had been thinking it would be a high-ranking member of the royal family.
But this isn’t bad. The person I’ll be talking to is second only to the king in terms of power.

Even as I thought that, I grew tenser and tenser. It felt a lot like I’d entered a lion’s den. You could call this a high-risk, high-return situation. If things went well, all my problems could end up solved with only a brief exchange. But in return, I could just as easily end up falling into the pit.
“You may get off.”
When I stepped out of the carriage, a crowd of knights was in front of me, and I accepted their warm hospitality and entered the building.
Rattle.
It was clear a lot of money went into the drawing room.
“...Where is Erwen?” I asked after giving the space a cursory scan.
The commander had a conflicted look on his face. “I lied about her being here.”
“...What did you just say?” Alarm bells started going off in the back of my head. I was sure this son of a bitch even swore on the name of the royal family.
When I shot him a look, he averted his eyes in a way that suggested he’d had no choice. “It was necessary to bring you here as quietly as possible.”
“You won’t get away with using the king’s name if you’re caught.”
“Then I’ll be fine as long as I don’t get caught.”
