Had I ever met a knight that was so quick on their feet? I praised him without thinking. “You would have been a better adventurer than a knight.”
“I don’t care if you’re being sarcastic. I just chose to be practical to fulfill my master’s orders.”
This guy is the type to leave you flat-footed, huh? Damn it all...

In a way, I often did this too. You could argue that using the prejudice against barbarians to make false oaths and deceive my opponents was basically the same thing he just did to me. As it was a clever method, it was incredibly effective. Who would’ve thought a knight would use the king’s name to lie? And a knight who appeared to be a member of the Royal Guard, no less.

I decided not to get too caught up in the fact that I had been deceived. Who cared if Erwen hadn’t been arrested? In fact, if I framed this in a different light, this was a positive. At least this meant Erwen was safe.
Besides, I had to go through this at some point.
The important thing was not what mistake I’d already made, but what I was going to do next.
“Now then, what do I need to do? Just wait again? Until that person you mentioned earlier gets here?”

“There’s no need.” The knight shook his head and placed a crystal ball on the table. Without even having to ask what it was, I immediately pieced together what was going on. No wonder there were no guards in the room. He planned to speak to me through this thing from the start. “Then I’ll leave you.” The knight instructed me to activate the crystal ball and left the room.
I was now alone in the drawing room. Quickly looking around to see if anyone was hiding nearby, I noticed something strange and swept the carpet aside.
Damn it.
Underneath the carpet, colorful, geometric magic circles were drawn. Goosebumps ran down my spine.
Is he planning to blast this whole place sky-high if I try to escape or get on his nerves?
Was it because he was the kingdom’s second-in-command? The firepower I was seeing here was no joke. It pretty much meant this entire mansion was a gigantic execution device in itself.
...Let’s turn on the crystal ball now.
Momentarily appalled by the other party’s thoroughness, I pressed the button to activate the crystal ball.
Shaaaaaa!

Before long, the crystal ball lit up and projected the image of a person. It was a face I remembered: the prime minister of Rafdonia and a high aristocrat with the title of Marquess, Ageni Lawton Tercerion. He was the same person who had hosted my conferment ceremony on behalf of the king in the past.
“It’s been a while,” his deep voice greeted, and I stiffened a beat later.
It’s been a while?
As soon as I picked up on the fact that something was off, my heart started pounding.
Thump!

Was this just psychological warfare? How much did the marquess really know? I forced myself to swallow back the questions bubbling up in my throat. There was something I had to worry about before all that. Right now, what was the best answer for me to give here? It didn’t take long for me to finish deliberating and take action.

“Are you...” I spoke politely yet cautiously, “Marquess Tercerion?” I judged this would be the natural reaction of an adventurer who suddenly got dragged here by a bunch of knights in the middle of a nap.
“I’m sure you haven’t forgotten my face already... You are unusually clever, unlike the rest.” The marquess chuckled at my response and said: “Baronet Bjorn Yandel.”
I hadn’t heard my full name in a very long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 386: Us (5)
paragraphs: Baronet Bjorn Yandel. There wasn’t even the slightest flicker in the marquess’s eyes as he said that name. If Erwen or Amelia looked at me with those eyes, I would have confessed all my wrongdoings before I could get into even more trouble. That was how confident the look was.

But the marquess was different from those two. Nothing was more naïve than believing the eyes of a politician who had been through all sorts of conflicts and had managed to hold onto the position of second-in-command of the kingdom for decades.
“Marquess, I think there’s been a misunderstanding.” I didn’t rule out the possibility that he was just feeling me out and maintained an air of ignorance.
Of course, the marquess didn’t even humor me. “It’s very awkward hearing you speak like this. I still vividly remember the day you were bestowed your title.”
“...Is Erwen the reason you have the wrong idea?”

“I understand the position you’re in so I won’t condemn you for lying to me. But...” On the other side of the crystal ball, the marquess sat forward in his chair and placed his elbows on his tabletop. “For us to have a proper conversation, it seems I have to create a situation where you’ll have no choice but to admit it.”

A situation where I’d have no choice but to admit it? Was he thinking of using a lie detection spell or a Numbers Item like Misplaced Trust? Or torture? Even as I maintained my poker face, I rifled through various possibilities in my head, but in the end, all of those theories were off.
“Allow me to start with this.” The marquess chose the conversation option. “Baronet Yandel, there is no need to be on guard. I am one of the few people who know that you are not an evil spirit.”
So, coming out strong from the jump, huh?
When she first learned my identity, what Amelia had been most surprised about was this: how could I, an evil spirit, receive a noble title?
“Hmm, now that I think about it, it’s possible the palace kept quiet on purpose. Since you were nothing short of a hero in the city at the time.”
That was the hypothesis Amelia came up with back then, and I also thought it had a degree of credibility.
But if what the marquess just said is true, that means he really didn’t know.

Of course, there was also the possibility the marquess was knowingly baiting me. I decided to keep my mouth shut and hear him out for now. In the game, there were times when going second could be more advantageous than going first. I could act after I heard everything he had to say.
“Riehen Schuitz and Baronet Bjorn Yandel. It’s a waste of time to get into the similarities between these two adventurers so I won’t go over them. Is that all right?”
“Yes, well, I’ve been mistaken for him several times, so...”

When I nodded, the marquess ran through the reasons why he was convinced I was the baronet one by one. “First, confirming you were not Riehen Schuitz was easy. I was able to hear the whole story from the employee who happened to damage and discard your file.”
Apparently, they revealed that some woman had come to threaten them. That was when the marquess’s suspicions began to deepen.

“Of course, I thought it was nonsense at first. But do you know what the most important part of administrative work is? Only looking at the numbers. No matter how logical and reasonable an explanation is, if the numbers don’t add up, it’s false. That was exactly the case for you.”
Bjorn Yandel was dead. The marquess explained that when he discarded that premise, all the dots began to connect.

“You were too strong to be Baronet Bjorn Yandel, of course. But given two years and enough resources, it was entirely possible that you could be that powerful. So the question then became how you evaded detection for such a long time. This also made sense if you didn’t stay in the city.”
If not the city, then where? That was much too obvious.
“When you went missing on Farune Island, you came into contact with people from Noark, correct?”

The timing was too suspicious to be a coincidence. In fact, as a result of his investigation, he learned that I had resurfaced two years later in the now-abandoned underground fortress, which was said to have a passage leading to the outside world.
“You appeared just after Blood Spirit headed down there.”

Now that I was looking at this from his perspective, it wasn’t for nothing that the knight broke down my front door and accused me of collusion. At the time, I thought it was just an excuse to get me here.

“Now then, I’d like to hear your thoughts on my theory.” The marquess looked at me from beyond the crystal ball and grinned. It was a theory that merited confidence. After all, it was a far more probable explanation than the idea that I’d been time-traveling for two years.
I only had one thought after listening to his long monologue. It sounded like he was not saying this to bait me, but because he truly believed it.
Should I call this a case of excellent imagination or a lack thereof...? I didn’t realize you could interpret my story like this too.

I didn’t have to think it over for long, because I always prioritized my goals in order of importance. My primary concern was our survival, my second was to take up Bjorn Yandel’s identity again, and my third was to clear up the suspicions that I was an evil spirit. When I came into this conversation, I already had my priorities set in stone.
“As expected, you’re smart, Prime Minister.”

I took off Riehen Schuitz’s mask and revealed my barbarian self. The reason for that was simple. To me, what was more important than clearing the charge of being an evil spirit was regaining my name. Whether he knew me as an evil spirit or a traitor, that didn’t matter. That particular issue could easily be handled with enough negotiation.
If he was going to kill me for being a traitor, he wouldn’t have called me here to talk in the first place.

“Yes, I’m Bjorn Yandel. Long time no see, Marquess.” Not for the first time, it struck me that words had power. If they didn’t, there was no way I could take off my human façade with this much confidence that I’d face any challenges that came my way from here on out.
Whew, that’s much better.
“Haha, thank goodness. It would have been very inconvenient if you continued to deny it.” I chuckled at the marquess’s pointed words.
Inconvenient, huh?

This was the main reason I’d obediently revealed my identity. After this, he would no longer have bothered with conversation, but instead turned to items. And if he learned that items didn’t work on me, it was obvious where his attention would have turned next: to Erwen, Amelia, and Raven. If they were investigated thoroughly enough, it would only have been a matter of time before the truth behind this absurd misunderstanding was revealed. As such, I decided it was better to calmly cop to it so we could get to the real point of this conversation. After all, deceiving others was now my specialty too.
“Now we can finally discuss business.” The marquess cut the chitchat, and his voice grew lower. “Baronet Yandel, why have you sided with Noark?”
“Is that important?”
“That kind of uncooperative attitude won’t do. I know you are a smart man.”
“Can’t really say I sided with them. I was only there temporarily to work toward my goal.”

The marquess stared at me silently. The longer he did, the more proudly I straightened my shoulders. Well, he wasn’t completely off the mark, though. In truth, I went back in time and did in fact stay in Noark, and for six months at that. Not to mention I even bashed in the lord of the castle’s skull.
“...It doesn’t seem like you’re lying—”
Burp.
“Ah, sorry. I’m feeling gassy.” That really wasn’t intentional. I’d actually been feeling bloated since earlier.
“I guess you were nervous.” Did my sudden hiccup change the mood? The marquess didn’t pry and moved on. “Anyway, then can I take that to mean that you are not working with them now?”
“Of course.”
“Even if you say that, I still can’t really accept it. If you are not a spy, why have you been hiding your identity?”
“The palace announced I was an evil spirit. I was planning to find out why they did that first before clearing my name.”
“You were wary of us, huh? I see, that could explain it.” The marquess nodded.
It was now my turn. The best way to get information was to exchange questions, right? “So, while we’re at it, why did the palace make that announcement? I’m sure you would know the reason.”
“I can’t tell you that. Just think of it as a politically motivated move. Besides, we didn’t even know you were alive at the time.”

This was the thing I had been wondering about the most, but I didn’t end up getting an explanation. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t disappointed by that, but I moved on with no regrets. “Then tell me this: what do you want from me? If you really thought I was a traitor, you would’ve assassinated me instead.”
“The palace does not handle things that way.”
Yeah, right. Every time I come back from the palace, my body reeks of all kinds of fishiness.
“Then are you saying you don’t want anything from me?”
“If you were a spy, I was planning to curry favor with you and use you in the war.”
See, that answer came right out without any prodding. “That’s unfortunate.”
“Well, nothing to be disappointed about. Our current situation isn’t too bad either.”
“Not too bad?”
“Wars always need heroes.”
Jeez, did you forget you announced I’m an evil spirit?
To be honest, I was dumbfounded to hear him say something so shameless, but I was sure it was because he was this kind of guy that he’d risen to the position he had.
“Baronet Bjorn Yandel, come work for the palace again.”
“And why should I do that?”
“Because you need us.”
“Well, I don’t know about that.”

When I once again turned him down, the marquess showed his true colors. “Whether you’ve severed ties with Noark or not, the fact is that you once joined forces with them. That’s cause enough for prompt execution.”
“Put simply, you’ll make that all disappear if I join forces with you?”
“Not just disappear. I will help you regain your name and your noble title, of course.”
“What about the announcement?”

“The people will accept any story if it makes enough sense.” It looked like the marquess had already drawn a map of how he wanted to proceed here. “Didn’t you say you only stayed in Noark to fulfill a goal? If you feel emotionally reluctant to do what I ask, think of this as a deal.”
I felt weird. No, should I say uneasy? That was because I came here anticipating the worst-case scenario, thinking I’d entered a lion’s den.
How can things work out this easily...?
Things were progressing so smoothly in my favor that it was actually making me anxious. My heart was pounding.
“Baronet, if you’ve made a decision, will you give me your answer?”

My options were currently limited. Even if the marquess and palace were plotting something shady, what could I do about it right now? I just had to accept this offer and figure out their angle on my own later.

“Fine. Tell me in more detail how you’re going to restore my title and what you want in return.” When I expressed my agreement, the marquess nodded in satisfaction. But the moment he was about to say something, a loud tremor rocked the garden.
Kwaaang!

I wondered what the commotion was all about, and the marquess soon provided insight. “My, it looks like she’s come. I didn’t think she would be quite so unrestrained, though.” It must have been Erwen. “Let’s continue this conversation another time. You should calm her down before things get any more out of hand.”
“...I will.”
That marked the end of our discussion for the day.

chapters.title: Chapter 387: Wild Horse (1)
paragraphs: Shaaaaaa!

After wetting my hair with warm water, I scrubbed my skin hard with soap for who knew how long. It wasn’t until I came out of the bathroom and changed into comfortable clothes that it finally felt real. I was back home.
Step, step.
Toweling off my wet hair as I headed down to the first floor, I found Amelia and Erwen waiting for me in the living room.
“You took your time.” Amelia looked somewhat displeased with my squeaky-clean appearance.
I sat down on the sofa across from her. “Since you’re not writing this out, I guess there was nothing of note?”
“Yes, despite your fears, I couldn’t find any wiretapping devices or anything like that.”
That was a relief. I was worried the knights might have left some behind when they broke into the house—
“Aside from the ones already there, anyway,” Amelia added.
Huh? Already there?
“Judging by your expression, I guess you didn’t know? There has been a recording-type crystal ball in the living room from the beginning.”
Even if she said that like it was obvious, this was the first I heard of it. But if I were to infer from her statement that it had been there a long time...
“Erwen?”

When I shot a suspicious look at the prime suspect, Erwen flinched and averted her eyes. “W-Well... since you never know... A-And if it weren’t for the crystal ball, we wouldn’t have been able to figure out what happened to you so quickly...”
...Well, I can’t say anything to that.
When I asked, she told me the crystal balls with recording capabilities were only installed in the entrance and living room. I decided to consider this a security measure any homeowner might take.
No wonder they found me with the marquess so quickly.
I raised a question I couldn’t ask on the carriage the marquess had arranged to take us home. “Erwen, how did you know I was at the marquess’s house?”
“There was nowhere else you could be! After all, that man came here himself!”
“That man...?”
“Oh, you didn’t know, Mister? Eltora Tercerion, the prime minister’s son, was the commander who came to arrest you!”
“What? Isn’t he the one who was recently promoted to Commander of the Third Corps?”

Is the prime minister crazy? Why would he send his son on such a dangerous mission? What if I bashed his skull in? Though, if he cherished his child in the first place, he wouldn’t have sent him off to battle.
The marquess’s child-rearing approach seemed very Spartan to me, but that wasn’t any of my business.
“But Schuitz, what exactly happened with the marquess?”
“Yes. Please tell us now. You don’t know how surprised I was to see the door broken and you missing when we got back.”
I explained the marquess’s misunderstanding about me and the deal he proposed, and asked them to weigh in. Their reactions differed significantly.
“Oh my, he’ll really return your title? That’s amazing!” Erwen was happy, saying this was good news.

Amelia, who was on a similar wavelength to me, expressed concerns that things were going too smoothly. “The prime minister is the best possible backer you could have, but I can’t shake an uneasy feeling.”
“But what else could I do? If I said no, it would’ve only made things more complicated.”
“...I’ll conduct my own investigation into the prime minister.”
“Yes, I have faith in you.”
“Sorry? What about me?”
“You too, of course, Erwen.”
The only ones you could truly trust were your comrades. This world was too harsh to survive all alone.
Tap, tap.
While he was busy tapping his index finger on the table at regular intervals, lost in thought, the door opened and a man stepped inside. “Did you call, Father?”

Eltora Tercerion was the marquess’s only child and the man who would one day inherit everything the prime minister had built. But the marquess’s gaze was cold as it settled on him. “If you had functional eyes and ears, you would’ve seen and heard that for yourself already. So I’m electing to ignore that. What do you make of this incident?”
“To be honest... I was very surprised. I never thought Baronet Yandel would be alive like you said, Father.”
“Is that all?”

Eltora gulped at the marquess’s follow-up question and chose his words carefully. “His return seems to be advantageous for our family. Although it’s been years, many people still remember him. As a political symbol, he can be put to good use—”

“Enough.” Eltora’s logical observations were interrupted by the marquess. “Is your insight really so limited?” He leveled a look of not just disappointment but disgust at his son. At this, Eltora shifted his gaze to the ground and sighed inwardly.
Why has this old man been acting like this lately?
He was never a kind father, but he was also never this bad. He had gotten a little worse two years ago, though, and Eltora was now starting to feel like an emotional punching bag.
He also brought in that strange woman... Has he noticed something about me?
It was suspicious. Lately, his father never called on him unless he had orders to dole out, nor did he share information with him properly. Just like now.
“Father.”
“Speak.”
“This is my first time hearing that Baronet Yandel is not an evil spirit. Why did you hide it from me too?” Eltora carefully asked, trying to feel his father out.
The marquess’s response was ice-cold. “It sounds like you expect me to hold your hand forever.”
“That’s not what I meant. It’s just, I was thinking I could have been more helpful if I had known in advance—”
“The fact that you believe Baronet Yandel is not an evil spirit is a sign you’re hopeless to start with.”
“Sorry? But Father, you clearly said—”
“Enough. I’d only be wasting my breath trying to explain this to you.”
His words were too heartless to be directed at his own child. Eltora pursed his lips at that but the marquess didn’t pay him any mind, instead bringing up the reason he called him here.
“Tomorrow, I want you to go in person and inform Yandel of the day of our next appointment. I want to continue the conversation we couldn’t finish today.”
“The appointment... what date should I give him?”
“This month’s full moon.”
The meeting would be held in the evening.
It was afternoon on the fifteenth.
“Then see you later, Mister. Take care of yourself!” As I left the house with a send-off from Erwen, the carriage waiting in front of our gate opened.
“Long time no see,” I said.
“Have you decided to stop using polite speech now?”
“I heard you’re the marquess’s son. Then you should already know who I am.”
“That’s true...” The prime minister’s son trailed off with a somewhat bitter look on his face, but that wasn’t any of my business.
“Whatever, let’s go.”
“Sure.”
The carriage traveled down the wide main road. Before long, a military platform appeared. Like last time, we used it to travel in style to Karnon, the royal capital.
“It’s convenient getting to the royal capital in under an hour. How much does one ride cost?”
“One million stones per person. Of course, that’s assuming there’s no carriage.”
“...Then it’s better to just take a carriage.”
“Right you are. There aren’t many nobles who use this place while accompanied by staff, anyway. I heard it’s only used for urgent business.”

As we chatted, the carriage finally arrived at its destination. A huge mansion was visible in the distance. I wondered how much it cost to own this much land in a place as expensive as the royal capital.
“We should hurry. My father is waiting.”
“I guess it won’t be a crystal ball this time?”
“I told you. Father wants to have dinner with you.”
Well, even if he did say that, I kind of assumed the marquess was planning on hosting this dinner over video call.
Creak.

The prime minister’s son led me to the banquet hall located on the fourth floor. There was a large window on one of the outer walls that overlooked the garden outside and offered a beautiful view of the palace beyond it. I didn’t have the luxury to take in the view, though.
“You’re here.” The prime minister, who was sitting at the head of the table, greeted me.
“It’s been a while, Marquess Tercerion.”
“You’ve come a long way. Sit, Baronet Yandel. Ah, Eltora, you may leave now.”
“...Have a pleasant visit.”
When the prime minister’s son left, the empty hall looked even emptier, but there was no better setting for a private conversation.
Tap.

The first thing I did was sit across from him. Perhaps it was to prevent the staff from needing to enter during the meal, but the table was already covered in food. For reference, the amount of food placed in front of me was five times the amount set in front of the marquess. It seemed they had taken into account my needs as a barbarian.
“Don’t worry and eat. I don’t plan to ask you to follow any suffocating rules of etiquette.”
“...If you say so.” The marquess began to cut his meat, and I tore off a chicken leg and shoved it in my mouth.
“How is the food?”
“It’s excellent.”
“I’m glad.”

As we continued our meal, I decided to get down to business. I knew that you weren’t allowed to talk about work during meals according to Rafdonian etiquette, but I was a member of the one race not bound by such empty formalities. “Marquess, the food is great, but I want to hear more about what you were saying the other day now.”
“About how I’m going to help you reclaim your title?”
“Yeah. I’m sure most people won’t be able to accept me suddenly coming back from the dead.”
The marquess didn’t comment on my impropriety and instead answered. “Let me ask you this. How many people knew who you were when you were in Noark?”
“None. I was in hiding there too.”

“That makes things much easier.” The marquess proceeded to explain what he had in mind. “I plan to claim that you were given a special mission by the royal family to infiltrate Noark. Now, after two and a half years, you have completed your mission and returned. What do you think?”
It was a short lie that could be summed up in just a few sentences, but there was no point asking whether it would work. The marquess had the power to make it happen. “Not bad.”
“Of course, it will take some time. I will have to create a paper trail within the palace to substantiate the claim.”
“And what will you do about the announcement declaring I’m an evil spirit?”
“Don’t worry. I can just say the rumors were necessary for your infiltration mission to work.”
I quite liked the scenario he was cooking up in itself. If I made a return like this, I could get my old life back.
But if there’s a problem with this plan...
“And what do you want from me in return?” It was the issue of what I had to give up to get all this.
The marquess set down the knife he was cutting the meat with and raised his hand. “A total of two things.”
“Tell me.”
“I get to create a special forces unit centered around you. You lead them and join the war.”
“For how long?”
“Until the war ends.”
He was trying to turn me into his slave. “Until the war ends? It’s hard to accept an offer without an end date.”

“Then let’s make it a maximum of three years. If the war ends before that, the terms of the deal will still be satisfied. Of course, you will be rewarded for any war achievements you accumulate in that time as well.”
This was a condition I could live with. Most adventurers were making money in the war effort these days, anyway. “And the second?”

“Second...” The marquess trailed off and set down his fork. “I will tell you the second thing I want tomorrow morning. It’ll go faster that way. There are plenty of empty rooms here, so stay the night.”
What is this, the commercial break after a cliffhanger?
After dinner, a servant guided me to a guest room. To be honest, I wanted to go home more than anything, even if it took hours, but there was something shady about the way the marquess was acting.

Given the date and time the marquess had invited me to the mansion, and even the out-of-the-blue request to sleep over, I was beginning to get the picture. But after asking to send a message to Erwen at home, I decided to spend the night here at the marquess’s request anyway. At times, you could turn a crisis into an opportunity.
“Ugh...” This room really was too spacious and luxurious for a single person.
Tick, tick.
Turning only the light on the nightstand, I lay on the bed and checked the time. Then I turned off the room’s mana lights as well and set the clock down.
Tick, tick, tick.
The steady click of the second hand’s march forward punctuated the silence.
Tick, tick.
The sound repeated ten more times, and then it happened.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
I immediately sat up in Hansu Lee’s bed. This time, I’d need to work faster than usual.

chapters.title: Chapter 388: Wild Horse (2)
paragraphs: The community of evil spirits opened at midnight on the fifteenth of every month. Time inside Ghost Busters moved differently than it did outside.
One hour in here is one second out there.
Put simply, even if I used up the entire twelve hours that the community was open, that would only translate to twelve seconds in the outside world.
But he won’t wait that long.
The marquess’s intentions were obvious. He was harboring unsubstantiated suspicions about me and was going to try to confirm them tonight. There was only one problem here.
How much time do I have?

I was hoping for at least four seconds, as that would give me enough time to participate in the Round Table that would be held in three hours. Doing so would help prevent any suspicions that might arise if Lion failed to attend, and also ensure that I didn’t have to miss any information by taking a break this month.
As I thought, four seconds would be cutting it too close.
I suppressed my mounting greed. Yeah, I had to sacrifice what I needed to for this to work.
Tick, tick.
The second I came to that decision, the computer finished booting up. I quickly moved the mouse to check the chatrooms.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence – 1 person is online.]

Without wasting any time, I immediately entered the chat. The player online was Hyeonbyeol. I was wondering if Baekho had returned considering I requested the GM lift the ban on him, but, well, there was still time for that.
“You’re here.” Hyeonbyeol was already sitting on the sofa with crossed legs and simply lifted her head to acknowledge me. Her outfit was the same as last time: a white blouse and suit skirt.

“What’s with that reaction? You’re making it sound like you thought I wouldn’t come.” When I sat on the sofa across from her and fired off a casual reply, a conversation that reminded me of the old days followed.
“I thought there was a chance you wouldn’t. You always ran away whenever things got even slightly uncomfortable.”
Hey.

“Unless it’s something that you need to deal with yourself, you can waste less energy by retreating.” It was common sense to skip side quests that offered low rewards for high effort. Pursuing efficiency meant reducing waste—like right now. I didn’t have time to waste on trivial chitchat so I got straight to the point. “Hyeonbyeol. Did you meet the GM last time?”
This was the reason why I entered this chatroom instead of logging out right away even though I wasn’t going to enter the Round Table this time. I wanted to confirm this.
Hyeonbyeol’s brow furrowed slightly, and after a beat, she parted her lips. “...How did you know?” These were words of confirmation, not denial.
I calmly explained the reason for my suspicion. “I thought it was odd that you got a message in the middle of our conversation. So I looked into it a little.”

I had gotten a strange feeling right after parting ways with Hyeonbyeol. Back in the bedroom, I was fiddling with the mouse when I remembered the GM being very interested in this chatroom. The GM may not have been able to eavesdrop on the conversations happening inside, but he was able to check the list of participants. Suspecting the GM may have been the one to send that message to Hyeonbyeol, I searched for one specific chatroom and kept an eye on the number of participants. It wasn’t long before my suspicions were confirmed.
“The number of participants in the secret chatroom the GM usually uses soon went up to three. I thought the timing was very coincidental and figured it was you.”
“...Then why didn’t you reach out to me then instead of waiting until today?”
“Because the GM can spy on people’s messages.”
“Then you could’ve just written to tell me to come to the chatroom.”
“He might think that strange too.”
“...So annoying.” Hyeonbyeol glanced at me and sighed. “I’m telling you this now so you don’t get the wrong idea, but I had no intention of deceiving you.”
“I know.”
“I was going to tell you today. Of course, I’m sure that’s hard for you to believe—What? What did you just say?”
“I know that you had no intention of deceiving me.”
Hyeonbyeol gave me a weird look. “I’m glad to hear you say that, but... on what grounds?”

My grounds were simple. “If you were planning to hide it, you wouldn’t have answered my question so easily in the first place.” Considering her personality, she would’ve thoroughly covered up the truth. Even if she thought she was caught, she probably would have denied it to the bitter end just in case.
“But I could’ve been acting.”
“If you want to go there, we’ll end up going in circles forever. If you still can’t accept my logic, just take it as me wanting to believe in you,” I joked.
Hyeonbyeol pursed her lips and studied me for a long while. “Hansu, do you have a girl here?” she suddenly asked.
Missha immediately came to mind the second the question left her lips, but I decided to figure out what she was getting at first. “Why are you asking that out of the blue...?”
“Just ‘cause,” Hyeonbyeol said in a strange tone. “It seems like you’ve gotten more eloquent, is all...” She trailed off.

Was that a compliment or a criticism? I decided to take it as the former and changed the subject. Not only was that a topic I didn’t want to dwell on, but I also had no time to do so. “Hyeonbyeol, I don’t have much time.”
“Is this an example of the ‘efficient retreat’ you mentioned earlier?”
“No, I really don’t have time. I just need to check on something before I go, so please answer me this.”
“Okay. What is it?”
“What did the GM offer you?”
“He asked me to be a spy for GP or whatever I want.”
“Of course.”
“What have you been up to that someone like that is so obsessed with you? His nickname was weird too...”
“It’s just a coincidence. I didn’t do anything,” I said dismissively.
Hyeonbyeol thankfully didn’t pry. “...Anyway, so what do you want me to do for you?”
“If I tell you, will you do it?”
“Have I ever not done what you asked?”
Uh... plenty of times?
I supposed the important thing was she almost always did it, even while grumbling the whole time.
Whatever, I’ll just tell her.
“I want you to purposefully leak information for me.”
“Okay. Is there something you want me to tell them this time too?”

“Once I leave the chatroom, I’m going to log out immediately. The GM will probably wonder why. Tell him I couldn’t talk for long because I’m in the middle of a battle and that I left in a hurry with a promise to meet next month.”
“Okay. But let me ask you one thing.”
“What is it?”
“What’s the real reason you’re logging out?”
“That? It’s similar to what you’re going to tell the GM for me.”
“Are you saying... you really came here in the middle of a fight? The labyrinth hasn’t even opened yet!”
“I told you, it’s similar.” Fights weren’t just physical, right? Anyway, that should be enough of an answer. “Then I’m heading out! See you next time!”
I left the chatroom before Hyeonbyeol had a chance to say anything else.
They were in a quiet study with furniture designed and arranged by her.
“If we’re all done here, I’ll leave now...”
“Yes, I will send you the GP we agreed on right away.”
“Right, then...”

As soon as the Asian woman, who gave off an intellectual yet somewhat bumbling vibe, left the chat, the GM muttered, “He is in the middle of a battle, huh? That’s very strange. If a man like him is in a position where he can’t waste a single second, that must mean the enemy he’s fighting is on the same level as him.”
The GM’s voice was full of despondency. Soul Queen, who had been working with him for a long time, knew why—there was no way she couldn’t. She felt the same way.

The Korean woman had asked them to call her Black Star if the nickname HS123 was too difficult to pronounce. And until that woman told them what was going on, they knew nothing. Nothing. Normally they were confident in their information-gathering abilities, but until they happened to collide with this newcomer in the dark, they didn’t even notice the signs that something was brewing.

“...Still, I’m glad we were able to recruit Black Star. If a conflict big enough to cause that man to struggle has occurred, there are bound to be traces of it left behind. For now, let’s focus on finding those traces.”

Even as she nodded at the GM’s words, Soul Queen did not hesitate to ask a question in return. “But there’s something else that’s strange about this. If he was really in such a dangerous situation, why did he enter the chat at all?”
“But this is him we’re talking about. That woman said he didn’t look to be in a rush, either. Perhaps he was simply confident.”
“That’s... true.”

It was a strange thought, but Soul Queen believed that could be the case. No, she definitely thought that was the case. She couldn’t imagine Lion ever looking harried. He was like a giant. Because he had absolute faith in himself, he always walked at a leisurely pace, but still left behind a big footprint.
“Before that... Soul Queen, shouldn’t you get ready?”
“Get ready?”
“It’ll be time to enter the Round Table soon.”
“But Lion won’t be there.”

“Still, there is quite a bit of useful information being exchanged there. More importantly, there is Corpse Collector, who is connected to Noark. You should go. You may get some information about the conflict that is happening wherever Lion is right now.”
“If you put it that way... all right.”
Soul Queen left the chat as instructed by the GM. Then, as soon as the time came, she entered the Watchers of the Round Table.
“You’re early.”
“Yes. I had some spare time.”
Fox had arrived before her. As they exchanged brief greetings, the other members entered one by one. Goblin and Crescent were first.
“Pshehe, I’m surprised Deer isn’t here today.” Clown soon followed.
A total of five people gathered around the Round Table, and there continued to be five until the door slammed shut, signaling the end of the entry period.

“I don’t care if Deer is dead in a ditch somewhere but this is kind of a problem. I can’t believe Mr. Lion isn’t here.” Clown got up without hesitation, grumbling the whole time. “Honestly, it’s because you people never bring anything interesting! Ugh, whenever I think about you acting high and mighty out in the real world...” He kept muttering as he headed to the door, before trailing off and turning to Soul Queen. “Huh? Aren’t you leaving, Ms. Queen?”
“No. I’m going to participate this time.”
“If I leave, you’re going to be left with the dregs.”
Soul Queen chortled, covering her mouth at Clown’s arrogance. “Oh my, what an amusing claim. You’re no different, Mr. Clown.”
“Are you saying I’m on the same level as them?”
“Hmm, seeing as you believe that the reason Mr. Lion didn’t come was because he was unsatisfied with our information, I think you’re on a somewhat similar level, yes.”
“...You make it sound like you know why Mr. Lion didn’t come.”
“I don’t know. I can’t just tell you that for free. If you’re curious, why don’t we do a round?”
“...Pshehe, you and your bluffing. You almost had me fooled. There’s no way you know anything about Mr. Lion.”
“Are you sure? If you are, you can leave.”
Despite her taunting tone, Clown’s feet did not move. This was about what she expected. Clown’s blind interest in Lion wasn’t anything new.
Tap.

Clown turned back around from the door and sat down, then muttered an excuse. “...Well, it wouldn’t be a bad idea to see what absurd thing you have to say before I leave. Pshehe.” Although his tone was rude, he had still played directly into her hand. The fact was that she needed Clown for high-quality information.

When Clown sat down, all eyes naturally gathered on her. As she took in those expectant, curious gazes, she felt the corner of her mouth lift behind her mask. She hadn’t intended to go first, but there was no particular reason not to.
“Pshehe, why are you staying silent now? Well, how can you possibly know something even I—”
She cut Clown off and announced, “Lion is currently battling someone.”

Clown didn’t even make a fuss about being interrupted. Instead, as soon as she finished, his gaze immediately snapped elsewhere, to the place where the jewel that identified the truth was located. It wasn’t just Clown, either—all of the other members looked in that direction with shining eyes.
Shaaaaaa.
Soon, light emanated from the jewel.
“I-It’s green.” Once Goblin broke the silence, a commotion ensued.
“Queen, did you figure out Lion’s identity?” Crescent was so worked up that he kicked back his chair and jumped to his feet.
“It wasn’t Queen,” Fox said softly. “It must be the GM who figured it out.”

“M-More importantly... if Mr. Lion can’t participate in the gathering because of a fight, who could possibly be the opponent...?” Goblin then seemed to pick up on a strange vibe from across the table and trailed off.
Clown, meanwhile, said nothing.
“You’ve gotten very quiet, Mr. Clown—”

“How...How were you able to find out...? Did he tell you? But, then why? W-Why you first, and not me?” Clown’s voice, which was light and casual until just a moment ago, was now filled with emotion. He was glaring daggers at Queen through the cracks in his mask, his eyes full of more fervent interest than ever before.
“Hmm, I don’t know. I wonder why.” She found herself smiling without realizing it. “If you tell me something interesting, perhaps I can tell you more.” It was an almost addictive feeling.
[You are being transported to Rafdonia.]

About twenty minutes in Ghost Busters, when converted to real time, was about 0.3 seconds—too short of a time for anything to happen to me in an empty room. As soon as I finished talking to Hyeonbyeol, I clicked Log Out, making the executive decision not to go to the Round Table today. Even if I stayed, I’d just be scrolling through the bulletin board cackling to myself until it opened. I decided it was better to log out early and prepare for what was about to happen instead.
It’s quiet.
When I opened my eyes, I was greeted by the same darkness from less than a second ago. I couldn’t hear a single sound, and the windows were also sealed tight.
Rattle.
Just then, the locked bedroom door opened. Even as I shut my eyes again, my near-superhuman warrior’s body sensed an unknown entity rapidly approaching.
If I chose to take my time, I would have been screwed.
The time it took for the enemy to open the door and reach my bedside was only about one second.
What is this guy, a cockroach?
My eyes immediately shot open and I threw out a hand.
Grab!
I grabbed their neck in a single move. Then I sat up and confirmed the identity of my uninvited guest. A completely unexpected person was struggling in my grip.
“Eltora Tercerion.”
To think the prime minister’s son himself had come to see me. Of course, this wasn’t cause for alarm. I didn’t care if it was him or his elderly grandfather—my job here remained the same.
“...I hope you came prepared to die.” I planned to collect full compensation for getting called back here and missing out on community activities.

chapters.title: Chapter 389: Wild Horse (3)
paragraphs: In the middle of the night when everyone should have been asleep, an uninvited guest picked the lock on my door. I had two options: first, ask the intruder why they snuck in and express my anger using words.
“...I hope you came prepared to die.”
Second, get angry with my entire body. As a typical barbarian, there was no need to think long about the correct way to treat an uninvited guest.
Squeeze!
I gripped the intruder’s neck harder. This was the normal reaction a barbarian would have to an assassin.
“Did the marquess order you to kill me?”
Ch-choke!
In response, the intruder desperately wheezed, “...I-It’s not...! Wait, let’s talk about this—”

It was obvious what he was going to say—most likely that he didn’t come here intending to kill me. I was sure that was true. It wasn’t like he had been holding a weapon when I opened my eyes. If he really wanted to kill me, the marquess had plenty of better options than this guy. I couldn’t deny that.
“I don’t intend to converse with someone who tried to kill me.”
But I can’t go on a rampage if I admit that, can I? So, get some sleep. I’ll go collect compensation for this from your father.
Squeeze!

I tightened my grip, obstructing his airway to the point where there wasn’t room for even the slightest of sounds to escape. Then I buried my fist in his abdomen, which was bare of equipment of any kind.
Smack!
His back curled up like a shrimp’s from the mild blow. He choked.
Oh, you’re not going to pass out after this? Then another one.
Smack!
Choke!
I guess he’s holding up well since he’s a knight. Do I need to hit him in the jaw?

Just as I was about to change my aim, Eltora sensed that his life was in danger and drew the knife on his waist. “Urgh!” It was about the same size as the dagger I normally used to cut up beef jerky. But the size of a knife in a knight’s hand didn’t matter.
Whooooom!
Using the dagger as a medium, the knight summoned a blue aura that rapidly extended outward.
Whip!

The aura coated the dagger, which then rushed like lightning toward my wrist. It seemed he decided to cut off my hand whole since he couldn’t get me to release him. I could see his logic. Most knights tended to try to cut down anything that got in their way.
[You have cast Iron Fortress.]
[The effect of Evolving Shell has increased by 1.5 times.]
As I quickly activated my skill, his aura touched my wrist.
Kagak!

The aura struggled to slice through my flesh and eventually got caught on the bone. His eyes widened. It wasn’t much different from the look on the Blood Knight’s face when we battled on the Dark Continent. ‘Why on earth isn’t it cutting?’ These bastards who spent their entire lives using auras had trouble accepting the fact that they could fail. Of course, it wasn’t my job to hold his hand.
“Even hiding a weapon?” Blood dripped from my torn flesh but I didn’t budge, my grip on his neck still steady. “So you are an assassin.”
Eltora attempted to violently shake his head, but he couldn’t. He tried but failed because he lacked the Strength stat to turn his neck in my grip. He could only widen his already wide eyes.
Whoom!
The next moment, a large fist broke the bones in his face.
Crack!
Now, shall we go?
Grabbing the marquess’s son by the back of his neck, I exited the room. Unfortunately, I soon ran into a problem.
How do I find the marquess?
I didn’t know where the marquess was, but I couldn’t wake this guy up to ask.
Drip, drip.
Ugh, I want to meet with the marquess before the wound on my wrist heals...
My concerns were short-lived, though. As the saying went, you didn’t have to overwork your mind if you had a tough body.
I’m sure I can figure it out once I go outside.

I was currently staying in a separate building located to the east of the main house. I walked down the empty hallway and headed toward the stairs. The servants who had been everywhere when I first entered my room were now nowhere to be seen. This meant the marquess had restricted their access before sending his son my way.
Well, the first floor looks normal.
The first-floor lobby was brightly lit even at this time of night. Even though no one was on watch in here, a maid standing around on standby noticed me and screamed. “Kyaaah!”
What, is this a biometric alarm or something?

“What is that racket?!” The tightly shut front door swung open at the scream and the knights who were on the night shift rushed inside. “Riehen Schuitz...! What is the meaning of this?! Who is that person you’re holding?!”
Unfortunately, it seemed they didn’t recognize their young master. Maybe I shouldn’t have punched him in the face.
“Judging by the threads on his belt, it looks like a member of the Tecerion Family.”
“You may be a guest of the marquess, but did you think you would get away with something like this?”
“Release that man and surrender!”

A total of four knights surrounded me, their auras active. It was a situation that would make any ordinary adventurer sweat profusely and quake in their boots. These guys probably knew that better than anyone, which was why they were so confident.
“I will say this for the last time, surrender and await Lord Tecerion’s judgment.”
“And if I don’t want to?”
“...Then we have no choice but to demonstrate our prowess.”
“Really? Try it, then.”
When I shrugged at their ultimatum, the knights frowned like they thought I was making a foolish decision.
Tap.

I tossed the son on the ground, opened up my sub-space, and hefted Demon Grinder onto my shoulder. Right at that moment, the four knights exchanged looks with each other and attacked me from all sides.
Dash.
Luckily for me, as soon as I stomped on the ground with my foot, a vortex appeared.
Boom.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm.]
I deliberately didn’t use it in combination with Transcendence because, against a group, it was much more effective in its usual state.
Whiiiiiip!

The knights, who were conveniently within a five-yard radius of me, were swept up by the powerful winds and pulled toward me. Of course, even as they were, the knights swung their swords. After all, a blow from a knight could slice through heavy armor like butter and cut through flesh and bone without resistance.
“Waaaaaah!”

I swung the Demon Grinder again and again, not bothering with defense. This was how barbarians usually dealt damage. Assuming blows were exchanged on a one-to-one basis, I was confident that I’d be the one who came out victorious in the end.
Whiiip.
The knight who charged at me from my front slashed his sword down. I didn’t make any effort to block or dodge.
Slice!
This guy applied so much force that the blade got embedded in my collarbone.
Smash!
I retaliated by driving my hammer into his temple. Right at that moment, the knight rushing at me from the left cut my ankle.
Slice!
Jeez, aiming for the Achilles tendon is low.
I almost lost my center of balance for a moment but thankfully my tendon wasn’t severely damaged.
Ziiip.
I quickly balanced myself on my other foot and used my injured foot to kick him in the face like a soccer ball.
Kwaaang!
The knight was sent flying and hit one of the mansion’s pillars. Just then, I heard a dull thud behind me.
Khak!
So, you didn’t slice, you stabbed.
[Any stabbing damage taken will be reduced by 75%.]
No wonder I didn’t feel any pain.
“W-Who the hell are you...?”
The better question is, who are you, kid? You have something to say?
Smash!
I turned around and elbowed him in the jaw. Just like that, there was only one guy left standing.
“Ahhh!” As if to avenge his fallen comrades, the knight went to slice through my neck with a ferocious, golden aura.
My neck’s a bit vulnerable.
As there was no need for big, energy-intensive moves, I simply raised my left arm and blocked the blow with my shield.
Choke!
Then I kicked him in the stomach.
Shaaaaaa.

At that moment, the timer on Eye of the Storm ran out and the vortex subsided. The foyer was now quiet. Although we exchanged an equal amount of blows, it was clear who the winner was. Except for a few scratches, I was perfectly fine, while the opposing side was currently crawling on the ground.
Cough...!
Two of them were still conscious. I wasn’t sure about the guy I kicked last, but I honestly thought the guy I struck in the temple out of anger would have died.
Did he use some sort of defense skill before getting hit?
It seemed the damage he took to the head was still significant, though, because the knight’s gait as he staggered toward the door was pitiful.
“B-Backup...”
Wow, knights sure are professional, huh?
I was impressed by their sense of responsibility, but as I didn’t want him to get too far, I used Transcendence followed by Vortex to strike him in the head and knock him out.
And I can ask this guy where the marquess is...
I crouched down and grabbed the head of the knight I kicked in the stomach to make him look at me. “I have a question for you—”
Spit!
...Is this son of a bitch off his rocker?
I was always the one spitting bloody phlegm at other people, so this reversal put me in a bad mood. I bit back my anger and tried again. “Where is the marquess?”
“You... will follow me... to hell.”
Who said I’m going to kill you?
I was exasperated, but given how he was spitting curses at me with that resigned look in his eyes, I got the sense he wouldn’t answer my questions anyway.
Bang!
I smacked him over the head and continued to deliberate.

What should I do? Should I go out again? Hmm, I think there are wizards out there, though. I don’t want to make more of a scene in the first place. It would be nice to have a private conversation with just the marquess... Should I just wait until the son wakes up?
Slide.
As all those thoughts were racing through my mind, I sensed a presence beyond the open doors. I raised my head to check, then slowly rose from my crouch.
“...You won’t have to come find me.”

The marquess was standing there, wearing the same casual clothes from earlier. That meant he hadn’t gone to bed. Well, it could have been because he was busy with work. I wondered what the actual reason was, though. I thought it was more than fair to say he was waiting for his cue to show up. The same went for the troops that swarmed in beside him.
Slide.
When I stood up, the woman next to the marquess placed her hand on the hilt of her sword.
“It’s all right, stand down.”
“...Yes.” The guard immediately took her hand off the sword, following his orders. I studied her closely. First off, this woman was not a knight. Auras were exclusive to humans.
And she’s from the dragon tribe.
Confirming her pupils had the characteristic slitted appearance of the dragon tribe, I turned my attention to her equipment.
God damn it.

It hit me what the sword on her waist was. No. 19: Exenith Demon Dragon Sword was a conversion-type longsword that not only greatly amplified physical damage, but converted it into magical damage. Until I finished my Mana Resistance build, that sword could be considered my own personal kryptonite.
I’ve never heard of this woman...
If equipment corresponded with talent, this woman had to be one of the strongest fighters in the city. It was safe to say there were no weak dragonians to begin with.
There was a moment of silence as I took stock of the situation. The marquess was the first to break it. “Why don’t we move this conversation somewhere else?”
“Why should I trust you?”

“Hmm, then at least allow me to take care of those men.” When I nodded, the marquess shot the knights beside him a look, and they took their fallen comrades away. “Aside from Ms. Ravien, everyone leave the mansion.”

The marquess withdrew all his troops from the mansion. All that remained was the dragon tribe woman next to him. But even though the dragonian guard was still present, the marquess didn’t hesitate to say my real name.
“Baronet Yandel. I know why you have done this. There must have been a misunderstanding.”
Misunderstanding, huh?

True, the marquess must have been flummoxed. Even if I wasn’t an evil spirit and just woke up midway through his son’s mission to check, he couldn’t have known things would escalate like this, and in the middle of his mansion no less. Of course, I had no reason to be understanding right now.
“You send an assassin after me in the middle of the night and call it a misunderstanding... You have some nerve.”
“It’s for that precise reason that I’m calling this a misunderstanding. It wasn’t an assassin—I only wanted to check whether you are an evil spirit or not.”

“...Evil spirit?” I already figured out his motive ages ago but I pretended to be oblivious. Ah, would it make more sense for me to get annoyed here? “...Are you saying you suspected me of being an evil spirit?” The question oozed hostility.

The marquess nodded solemnly at this. “It’s better to be certain about these things. As you may have heard, evil spirits are summoned to a gathering every fifteenth day of the month. During that time, they are completely defenseless. I swear, I only intended to check whether you were awake or not.”
“This confirms it. You are not an evil spirit.”
I let out an inaudible sigh. That was my biggest motivation for wreaking all this havoc. “Then why did you send your son, of all people?”
“That’s... because I figured that that way, there wouldn’t be any issues even if you woke up.”
“Go on.”

“First, I didn’t know you would make such a fuss. And second, I thought he would be able to handle himself in an emergency.” In other words, he figured his son could subdue me even if things went sideways.
“Didn’t you worry I might kill him on the spot? Isn’t he your only son?”
“Coddling will only make them grow up weak.”
So, that’s your child-rearing strategy.
Some parts of his explanation were still unclear, but I thought I had a pretty good handle on what had happened.
“Now then, if that clears up our misunderstanding—”

“Just because the misunderstanding is cleared up doesn’t mean there’s no hard feelings. You haven’t completely cleared up the misunderstanding to begin with.” When I interrupted him, the marquess scowled at me.
What, you think that’ll scare me?
“Do you see this injury?” I held out my already half-healed wrist so that he could see the wound. “It’s from when your son ambushed me earlier.”
“...Ambushed?”
“I wanted to talk but he pulled out a knife.”
“I see, then it was only natural you misunderstood and reacted the way you did. He will be punished accordingly.”

“And what about the damage I took?” Not stopping at my wrist, I held out my other injuries from the knights so he could see. Compared to the knights, who were beaten to a pulp, the injuries were extremely minor.
Even as he scoffed, the marquess gave me the answer I wanted. “Since they were caused by a mistake on our part, we’ll be sure to reach an agreement that will satisfy you.”
Okay, that should be enough compensation.
“Then are you willing to clear the air now and talk?” he asked. “I want us to discuss the second condition I intended to tell you about in the morning.”
“Fine.”
When I nodded, the dragonian guard beside him pulled a chair out from sub-space like she’d done it a hundred times. It was an expensive and comfortable chair.
Wow, he makes her carry around a chair like that in sub-space? These nobles...
“As I get older, my body is not what it used to be. Ah, do you need a seat as well?”
“No need.”
“I’m glad.”
“So, what’s the second condition?”

There was no need to drag this conversation out so I got straight to the point. In exchange for helping me reclaim my identity, his first stipulation was that I join the war effort. What could be the second?
“Let me confirm one last thing before I get to that.” The marquess craftily avoided answering and exercised his right to question me.
Ugh, it’s not like I can say no.
“Go ahead.”

With my permission, the marquess continued, but the direction he took the conversation was a bit unexpected. “Aside from my son, the four knights you faced earlier were considered quite skilled even within our household.”
Really? I took them all down before I even got to see their skills so I couldn’t really tell.
“So?”
“I’ll ask plainly,” said the marquess. “How strong are you?”
The question was a bit out of left field but it made sense when I thought about it. Even the marquess wouldn’t know my exact abilities. He just intended to use my reputation to help the war effort.
“Hmm, seeing as you’re not answering, I guess it’s a difficult question?”
“Not really.”

It wasn’t a difficult question—it was simply too open-ended. How could you express a person’s strength in words? How strong someone was was as relative as time itself, and it thus required something to compare it to. For example...
“That woman.”
When I nodded at the dragonian guard, the marquess looked surprised. “Are you saying you’re confident you can defeat Ms. Ravien?”

I shook my head. “No.” Maybe not defeat. It wasn’t like we’d actually fought before, so it was too early to be sure. But the marquess was asking about my combat power, so I answered without a moment’s hesitation. “Strong enough to get past that woman and crack your skull.”
Was that a good enough answer? Probably. I saw a slight tremor run through the marquess’s form, despite the fact that he was usually relaxed even in front of me.
“...He is even more unhinged than the rumor says.” High praise left the guard’s mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 390: Wild Horse (4)
paragraphs: In a way, the marquess’s mindset was similar to that of a person visiting a zoo. These people looked at wild beasts locked up in cages and called them cute and pitiful. However, it didn’t take a genius to recognize this was arrogance. All those iron bars needed to do was disappear. The moment the division between them vanished, humans began to see the true nature of the beast, just like the marquess was right now.

Of course, the marquess was different from ordinary people. Despite my aggressive, if sincere, declaration, he flinched only slightly and quickly regained his composure. Well, it wasn’t like the steel bars had actually disappeared. I couldn’t kill the marquess, and he knew that better than anyone.

“Is that enough of an answer?” As if my statement was purely an answer to his question, I nonchalantly ended our standoff. I would be lying if I said I didn’t want to see that proud marquess’s mask crack, though. For now, I had no choice but to be satisfied with this.
“Don’t worry,” the marquess responded. “I fully understood what you were trying to convey.”
“I’m glad.”
This was a warning. I was willing to accept a mutually beneficial relationship, but if he ever crossed the line, I was prepared to break through these bars and charge at him at any time.
“If I’ve sated your curiosity, I want to hear the second condition now.”
“Ah, about that. This is the second condition.” The marquess glanced at the dragonian woman beside him and then said, “Help Ms. Ravien kill the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos.”
“The Dragon Slayer...?”
“That’s a different reaction from what I expected. I heard from Ms. Ravien that you hated the man?”
I mean I do, but this request is just really unexpected... I guess he knows about what happened between me and the Dragon Slayer because of that lady?

That suddenly made me wonder: what kind of relationship did the marquess and this dragonian woman have? Since killing the Dragon Slayer was his second condition, that meant he definitely had some kind of close connection to her. Was it a business relationship?
“Now, will you give me an answer?”
Curiosity welled up in me, but it was time to give him my verdict first. After I asked one more thing, anyway. “You made me wait until tomorrow just for this?”
“Ms. Ravien was not home at the time. I thought it was only right to have this conversation with her present.”
Hmm, if you say so.
“Fine, I was already planning to kill that bastard with my own hands someday, anyway.”
“That’s that, then.”
“I haven’t reached a satisfactory agreement with you about this yet, though,” I said while holding out my wrist.
The marquess chuckled. “Let’s stop here for today and meet again tomorrow morning. These days, I have such a hard time the next day if I miss my bedtime by even a little.”
“...All right.”

When the conversation came to an end, the marquess got up from his chair and turned around. The dragonian woman put the chair back into sub-space with the air of someone very familiar with this song and dance.
“Baronet Yandel, don’t be too reckless,” the guard warned me in a low voice.
What, is this revenge for what I said earlier?
That was my first thought, but it didn’t take long for me to realize that wasn’t the case.
“If you die again, my sister will be sad.”
“Sister? Ah, are you...?”
The dragonian woman neither confirmed nor denied it. She simply turned around and followed the marquess, but that alone was answer enough.
Huh, no wonder her features looked familiar. Penetasaur.
Pen was the dragon shaman and the daughter of the ancient elder dragon, also known as Dragon Kid for short. So this was her older sister, the woman who could have become my teammate.
When Eltora Tercerion, the only child of the marquess, came to, the first thing he saw was his father.
“Are you awake?”
“...I’m sorry.” Eltora did not ask any questions about what had happened. Instead, the first thing he did was apologize.
The response he received in return was cold. “Do you think I waited by your bedside all night to hear that? Tell me what happened—every single detail.”

At his father’s words, the memories slowly returned to the forefront of Eltora’s mind and he gave a brief summary of what happened at midnight. There wasn’t much to it. He had broken into that man’s room as per his father’s instructions and was immediately grabbed by the neck and beaten so hard that he passed out before he could even explain himself. That was all.
“Pathetic fool.”

Eltora swallowed back his humiliation and said nothing. This time, there was really no room for excuses. Then a question suddenly occurred to him. “But why did you choose to do it like this? If you wanted to confirm whether he was an evil spirit or not, there must have been a surer way...”

At first, he thought it was simply because his father hadn’t wanted to offend Baronet Yandel. After all, he saw the man as a useful tool. But when he thought about it, the method he went with was a little strange. No, there had to be another reason.
“You can’t even figure out something like that yourself?”
“...Please teach me.”
When Eltora bowed his head submissively, the marquess frowned but answered his question. “The enemy’s weakness can only be of real value to us if they do not know we hold it.”
“Because we hide weaknesses that haven’t been exposed yet, but work hard to fix the weaknesses that already have.”
“I’m glad you seem to understand that, at least. Then go, now. I must think.”
“Yes, Father...” Eltora limped over to the door, about to follow his father’s orders to leave, when he stopped. Another question suddenly popped into his head. “Um... Father?”
“If you have something to say, say it quickly.”
“You mentioned the enemy’s weakness earlier... Does that mean you’ve identified Baronet Yandel as your enemy?” It seemed his father had perhaps revealed his hand by accident.
However, Eltora was not able to confirm his theory. “That’s none of your concern. You may leave.”
“Yes, Father...” After Eltora left his father’s office, he headed to his bedroom. Even as he did, though, his mind was loud.
Baronet Yandel is the marquess’s enemy...
Just what kind of dark scheme was the marquess plotting? As he was contemplating this, Eltora’s feet soon stopped in front of his destination.
Tremble.

For some reason, his fingers were shaking around his key. Even though this room was not the same one he had opened earlier but the room he had been living in for several years, it felt as if the moment he opened this door, he’d find a beast sleeping inside. He could even hear it.
“Eltora Tercerion.”
It was a deep, rumbling voice that sent shivers down the listener’s spine, coupled with eyes that seemed to be looking down on you.
“...I hope you came prepared to die.”

He had the strange feeling that if this man wanted to get him, he wouldn’t be able to escape him no matter what he did. The unpleasant sensation of déjà vu caused Eltora to instinctively think of another man.
Well, he could never be him, though.
“The first time I came to this community was twenty-two years ago.”
Bjorn Yandel wasn’t even born back then.
“Even Goblin would laugh at me if he ever found out about these delusions.”
Eltora chuckled and shook his head. Then he inserted the key and opened the door.
Click.
It was a typical nobleman’s room decorated with armor, a longsword, and a stuffed deer head on the wall. As always, it was not at all to his taste.

The next morning, I joined the marquess for breakfast. When I arrived, there were only two people inside the dining room where the food was being served: the marquess, who was seated, and the dragon tribe guard behind him.
“Your son?”
“He will be resting today.”
Don’t these guys usually invite their sons to attend events like this?
The question came to mind, but having fewer people around was better for me anyway. Was he being considerate?
“Let’s eat.”
We started eating and conversation naturally followed. There was something he had to finish discussing with me today—the agreement mentioned yesterday.
“If there is anything you’d like as compensation for our mistake, tell me.”
“Before that, I want to check something.”
“Go ahead.”
“How long will it take to get my name back?”
“I’m thinking about three months. We have to pull this off perfectly.”

Three months, huh? It sounded long at first but I was sure the marquess couldn’t do much about it. He would have to falsify a flawless paper trail showing Bjorn Yandel had been given a royal mission to infiltrate Noark for two years start to finish.
“Until then, you have an important job to do. If your identity spreads before we are ready, others will get suspicious and start their own independent investigations into you.”
“Marquess, can’t you stop that?”
“If things come to that, I will do my best to prevent anything from happening, but I can’t guarantee the information won’t leak. That’s how the palace is. No single person has complete control.”

Put simply, unless you were the king and ruler of this country, it was impossible to have total control over state institutions. This was a weird thing to hear coming from the man who had a bad reputation for turning the king into a puppet, but it wasn’t out of the realm of possibility. In truth, the prime minister was nominally the kingdom’s second-in-command, but that didn’t mean he didn’t have any rivals.

A prime example was Duke Kealunus. His was a great noble family with one branch of his bloodline controlling the Magic Tower. Historically, they had actively participated in labyrinth-related businesses and had secured a strong influence over large clans. To be honest, the duke’s family had much more diverse and broader areas of influence than the marquess’s family, whose only leverage was the position of prime minister.
“If you understand why it will likely take that long, I’d like to hear your request now.”
“I want to meet with the barbarian tribe’s shaman.”
“Your reason?”
Why are you asking such an obvious question? Oh, does he not know since he’s not a barbarian? There is only one reason for a warrior to meet with a shaman.
“To get a Spirit Imprint.”

For various reasons, my Spirit Imprint had plateaued at stage six. I even bought the supplies needed to get to stage seven but I wasn’t able to get the imprint before getting dragged to the past out of the blue. Thankfully, Raven had held onto Soul of the Dead after getting it as part of her inheritance from me, so as long as I solved the identity issue, I’d be able to receive the imprint.
“As I said before, it’ll be troublesome if your identity leaks before the preparations are complete—”
I interrupted the marquess. “That’s why I’m asking you to deal with it. So that I don’t have to worry about it.”
“So this is the compensation you want.”
“Yes, I don’t know what’s going to happen in the labyrinth in the near future, and three months is too long.”

The marquess closed his eyes for a moment and contemplated my request. I guessed he concluded that increasing my combat power wasn’t a bad idea considering he wanted me to participate in a war. “Fine. I will do whatever I can to get you a meeting with the shaman within the month.”

“That’s good.” I didn’t bother asking how he was going to summon the shaman or convince him. That was for the marquess to worry about. Judging by how good he was at getting things done, I was sure he’d manage.
Tap.
By the time we reached an agreement, we were done eating. We left the empty plates where they were and kept talking. After all, there was still a lot we needed to talk about.
“You mentioned you’re forming a unit with me at the center. Do you already have something in mind?”
“I’m going to form a unit of thirty people.”
“So there will be five teams in total. Have you decided who will fill the slots?”
“No, but I have identified some candidates.”

The marquess proceeded to list the names of the prospective members, and as I listened in silence, I was quite surprised. There were many names even I, someone not up-to-date on the latest news, recognized. A member of the Seven Powerful, an ace from a large clan, a renowned paladin, a rumored up-and-comer in the military—was the marquess trying to assemble some sort of dream team?
“But will those people really join the unit?”
“They will. Most of them. Because I plan to promise them a large reward in return.”

“...If you say so.” I did wonder whether that was actually feasible but seeing as he was this confident, that had to mean it was somewhat within the realm of possibility. And so we discussed what would follow.
“Baronet Yandel, you will be in charge of one of the five teams. Among your team members will be Ms. Ravien.”
“Then there’s space for four more people besides me.”
“You plan to bring those two with you, correct?” It was obvious who he was referring to—Erwen and Amelia.
So, he knows about Amelia too. He doesn’t know she’s from Noark, though, does he?
Even as I worried about that, I nodded. “I plan to.”

“Then there are only two spots left. If you don’t have anyone in particular in mind, tell me who you want from the names I mentioned earlier. I’ll make sure to offer the best deal possible if it means I can get them for you.”
Additional members, huh?

The first person that came to mind was Raven. We’d need a wizard on the team and she wasn’t lacking in either skills or reliability. But what about our navigator? I definitely couldn’t fill the remaining spot with that guy. Should I leave him in the basement until the war was over?
I’ll have to discuss it with Amelia later. And I’ll have to ask Raven about her willingness to join before I mention her to the marquess.
After taking a moment to think, I said, “I’ll tell you after some more thought.”
“Sure.” That concluded our conversation today. Or so I thought. Just as I was about to get up, the marquess spoke. “Ah, I have one more thing to tell you. I’m not establishing this unit on my own.”
“What does that mean?”
“In brief, that means the interests of many different factions are at play here. The only thing within my power is ensuring you’ll be able to command one of the five teams.”
“So? What are you getting at?”
“The commander in chief hasn’t been decided yet.”
In other words, the position of party leader was vacant. “Why?”

The marquess met my gaze head-on. “These are not the type of people to obediently follow orders just because they came down from above. And even if they do, that doesn’t mean their supporters will accept them.”

So, it was politics. If even the marquess was limited in the amount of say he had, I guessed there were quite a few influential people involved in the creation of this unit. That was good news for me, though. I was starting to understand what the marquess was implying.

“Anyway... We decided that once all thirty people are gathered and the team leaders are chosen, we’ll have any willing candidates compete to choose the right person. If this unit achieves great things in the war, then the person who sponsored the commander-in-chief will also share in many of those achievements.” The marquess stopped for a moment to study my expression. “What do you think, is it doable?”
This blunt question made his intentions very clear. I found myself chuckling. That was because it was foolish of him to ask whether this was doable.
“No reason it wouldn’t be, as long as there are guaranteed rewards.”
To be honest, the people he mentioned earlier were all great... but I didn’t think any of them could beat me.

chapters.title: Chapter 391: Captain Barbarian (1)
paragraphs: In the first-floor living room under the watchful eye of Erwen’s surveillance camera, three women sat on the sofa next to each other, sipping tea.
“A special forces unit made up of thirty people... This is the first I’ve heard of it too. That must mean it’s extremely confidential,” Raven muttered.
“Since the war is dragging on, I guess the palace is looking for a way to turn things around,” Amelia mused.
“Exactly. Considering the reputations of the candidates mentioned by the marquess, I’m honestly questioning whether they’ll actually be able to get all these big names on a single team.”
“But that part is set in stone according to the marquess.”
“Then I think it would be wise to assume they’re planning something big that will require a lot of firepower.”

While the two of them discussed the situation in serious voices, Erwen didn’t particularly seem interested in the current state of our military. “Mister, you said you don’t like sweets, right? Have some of this. I bought something savory for you.”
“Ah, thanks.”
As I ate the peanut butter cookies Erwen gave me, Raven shot me a displeased look. It seemed she wasn’t happy with me dropping all that information on them and then keeping quiet.
I swallowed what was in my mouth and said, “So Raven, what are you going to do?”
“...About what?”
“I told you. With me, Erwen, Emily, and the dragonian woman the marquess chose, that leaves two spots.”
“I want you to join us.”

When I outright asked her, Raven averted her eyes with a slightly uncomfortable look on her face. “I want to help on the front lines, too, but I think that’d be hard to swing right now.” This was undoubtedly a slightly disappointing response.
“...Really?”

I tried not to let it show, but Raven must have picked up on it because she launched into an explanation without even needing to be asked. “On both the battlefield and in the city, Commander Pevrosk is being summoned everywhere these days. If I leave the Magic Corps right now, there will be no one to help manage it all...”
Jeez, so hard-working. This is why she was so trustworthy as a teammate, though.
I didn’t want to see her so dejected when it wasn’t even her fault to begin with, so I quickly stopped her there. “Why are you explaining yourself? If you’re busy, it can’t be helped.”
“Thank you. For understanding.”
“Understanding or not, this isn’t something you need to make excuses for.”
Anyway, that meant recruiting Raven was off the table. How would we fill the remaining two slots?
As I was pondering this, Amelia spoke to me in a soft voice. “Schuitz, do you think the team needs a navigator?”
“I don’t know, I think it’s unnecessary since we’ll be traveling on a large warship.”
“...I see.” Amelia nodded, but there was something strangely off about her voice even as she agreed. Did she want to take our basement-bound sailor Auyen with her?
Jeez, no matter how fun sailing is, there’s a time and place for everything...
“I think it would be best to leave Auyen where he is for the time being. He may be useful again after the war.”
“All right. I was worried since he’s not eating much lately but I guess I’ll just have to walk him more often than usual.”
“...Yes, that should work.” Then that solved the problem of the navigator. “Raven, do you know anything about the dragonian woman?”
“No. This is my first time hearing about a Ravien. But I’ll look into it once I get back to Command. The commander might know something.”
“Yes, I’ll leave you to it.”

Raven left after that, finishing her tea and bowing out since she had work to do. The rest of us debated which of the candidates the marquess mentioned we should add to the team. Although Erwen and Amelia were constantly at odds, we easily agreed on who our first teammate would be.
“I think we will need a wizard.”
“I agree. It’d be inconvenient not to have one.”
We would fill the wizard position that was still vacant after I failed to recruit Raven.
“What about the remaining spot?”
“Wouldn’t it be best to have a priest?”

If possible, the last slot should go to a priest. If that was too hard to pull off, we decided it would be best to fill it with a support-type special ability user. I had our tanking needs covered, Amelia had close combat, Erwen had long-range, and we’d have a wizard soon too.
