As such, we decided that it would be best to use a supporting special ability user to boost our close-combat capabilities. These were all reasonable arguments so I readily agreed, except for when we got to the last point.

“Then for the wizard, we can go with either this option or this one, this one for the priest, and if we can’t get them, I think this user will be best!” Erwen brightly expressed her opinion, pointing to each of the names on the list of candidates one by one.
“Oh, they’re all men?” I genuinely had this reaction without much thought.
“Well... because there are too many women around you, Mister.”
“...Huh?” Was that a reasonable justification to only choose men? I glanced at Amelia for help, but to my surprise, she just nodded like she completely got where Erwen was coming from.
“I think it would definitely be best to choose a man,” said Amelia.
“...How come?”
“Your judgment is impaired when women are involved.”

What is this girl saying? I’m a cold-blooded guy. Doesn’t matter if it’s a man or woman—if need be, I always chop their heads off equally. The first player I ever killed in Glacier Cave was a woman too.
“Emily, I think there’s been a misunderstanding. Why on earth would you think that?” I asked, feeling wronged.
Amelia answered immediately and without hesitation. “Because... you were like that with me too.”
Just what sort of reputation had I given myself with these two?

There were ten days left until the labyrinth next opened. Amelia had been stopping by the commercial district almost every day since we got back and finally finished disposing of all the loot. In other words, we were finally able to divvie up our haul from our most recent expedition.
“Even subtracting the change, it comes out to 350 million stones.”
It was truly an outrageous amount of money. Not only that, but it was an amount that was difficult for a group of our size to achieve with just mana stones no matter how many floors we climbed.
Well, I guess this makes sense considering we wiped out an entire sixth-floor clan.

I was still surprised when I heard the amount, though. The broken ships didn’t even sell for full price and we decided to keep the largest ship for future use rather than sell it. If we sold that boat, our total income would have tripled.
“Then what do you want to do with the cash?”
Amelia had worked harder than anyone else to dispose of the items. When she asked me what my plans were, I answered without a moment’s hesitation. “Of course we have to share it equally.”

“Then each person will get a little over 110 million stones.” Amelia smiled softly and mentioned that with this amount, she could finally buy the weapon she had been eyeing. But it didn’t take long for that smile to fade.

“Before you get a new weapon, I want you to pay me back first.” Erwen’s voice was too cold for someone talking to their teammate. Of course, the request itself was fair. Although the deal had gotten a little convoluted, Amelia had been the one to pledge my Demon Grinder to the bank as collateral, after all. Amelia used that money to buy an essence, and since she hadn’t been able to pay it back, Erwen was forced to take out a loan using the house as collateral.
“I’m sure there’s still time left to repay the debt...?”
“I’m starting to think we’ll never be able to repay it in time if you keep spending like this. And it’s better to pay off your debts as soon as possible, right?”
“...How much do you need?”
“All of it, of course. If you cough up everything you earned this month, I think that should be enough to pay it off.”
Amelia looked at me like a sad puppy at Erwen’s words. It was obvious she was asking for help, but what could I do here?
“...Let’s buy the weapon next time.”
“When I asked you last month if I could get an upgrade, you promised I could.”
“Things have changed now. I remember you also argued not to sell the biggest ship and to instead use it to travel?”
“That’s... because we’ll need a boat even if it’s not on the sixth floor.”
“Exactly. Just wait a few more months. I’ll help you pay for it then.”
Amelia was so upset that she didn’t even respond, but judging by the way she quietly exhaled and looked out the window, she seemed to have come to terms with the current situation to some extent.
What should I give her at moments like these to lift her mood again? I don’t think she has any particular interest in food...
“Mister, someone’s outside.”
Huh? A person?

When I headed outside, I found it was someone sent by the marquess. Although the guy looked strong, I couldn’t tell whether he was a knight or not from his casual clothing. The conversation we had was extremely short too.
“A letter from the marquess.”
“Ah, thank you for bringing it.”
I quickly went back inside and opened the letter. I didn’t know if this was simply Tecerion’s personality or because the recipient was a barbarian, but the contents were concise.
The shaman problem has been resolved. I will send someone tomorrow morning so go with them.
So, I’m finally receiving the seventh stage of the Spirit Imprint.

The next morning, as soon as dawn broke, I got on the carriage the marquess sent and headed to the royal capital. The trip would normally take at least six hours, but using the military teleportation platform, it was possible to depart in the morning and arrive in the morning too.
It really is convenient...

I arrived at the mansion without even having time to nap in the carriage, but I wasn’t able to meet with the marquess this time. Apparently, he headed to the palace early this morning for business. Well, the marquess wasn’t a deadbeat, unemployed loafer—he was the prime minister of a country. I was sure he was busy all the time. In truth, the reason I had been able to have so many private meetings with him lately was likely because he prioritized me. And even then, all he had time for was a conversation over a meal.
Well, I’m better off not seeing him anyway.

Anyway, I followed my guide into the mansion and arrived at an office located on the third floor of the main building. The prime minister’s son looked uncomfortable as I entered and when the guide left us alone, he said hello.

“...You’ve come a long way, Baronet Yandel.” His tone was polite and he seemed to be addressing me as an equal, but he gave off the vibe that he was intimidated for some reason. Was it because he refused to meet my eyes?
“Not really. I had an easy trip thanks to you. How are you recovering? I see the bones in your face have healed nicely...”
“...As you can see, I’m fine now.”
“I’m glad.”
“Ah, and I didn’t get to say this last time, but I apologize for my rudeness the other day.”

As I listened to Eltora, the prime minister’s son, say sorry to me, I almost burst into laughter. I knew he was only being polite, but still, it was kind of funny that the person who got beaten up in the middle of the night was the one apologizing.
“It’s fine, it’s all in the past anyway. I already worked things out with the marquess so don’t worry about it anymore.”
“I’m glad to hear you say that. That’s a weight off my shoulders.”
“So, the shaman?”
“He is waiting in another room. If you step into the hallway, Renia, the maid outside, will guide you there.”
So all I had to do was go over there and I’d be able to get the Spirit Imprint. There didn’t seem to be a reason to rush so I decided to sate my curiosity a bit.
“How did you get the shaman to come here?”
“I heard Father personally asked the chieftain for a favor, requesting he send the shaman for someone who needed a Spirit Imprint.”
“Hmm, but that must’ve seemed suspicious.”
“Not exactly, according to what I heard. After all, not all barbarians can come and go from the holy land freely.”
“Ah, did he say I’m a warrior who got kicked out of the tribe?”
That was the first possibility that came to mind, but Eltora shook his head. “He said you were a barbarian born and raised in the city.”
“...I see.”

I accepted that without hesitation. Come to think of it, that did happen every once in a while. Barbarians weren’t much different from humans, after all. When you lived in the city for a long time, you found yourself immersed in its culture and were less bound by tradition. I’d heard that in extreme cases, the barbarian parents in question didn’t even send their children to the holy land and instead raised them themselves.
“Well, that should make things easier. Thank you for taking care of that.”
“It’s in our best interest to help you, Baronet.”
“Sure. Then see you next time.”
With all my questions answered, I ended the conversation and left the room. The maid waiting outside immediately guided me to the room where the shaman was.
“I am prohibited from leading you any further.”

In other words, I was the only one who could go inside. When I opened the door and entered, a room completely emptied of all furniture and filled with cigar smoke welcomed me. In the center of the room was a space shrouded in cloth. Through it, I could see the silhouette of a person sitting in an upright position.
It’s been almost three years since I’ve seen the shaman...

As I slowly approached, I found myself nervous for some reason. Even if the marquess made up an excuse for me, the shaman was sure to recognize me as soon as he saw me. Well, considering the type of guy he was, I was sure he’d keep my secret from the chieftain.
“You’re here.” Just then, a voice spoke from beyond the cloth and I stopped in my tracks. “My fellow countryman raised in civilization.”
What’s with this young-sounding voice?
Swish.

When I pulled the cloth aside, I saw a tattooed barbarian wearing an eyepatch. His eyes had both been fine last I saw him, but it wasn’t hard to recognize him: the young disciple I had caught glimpses of a few times during my visits to the shaman.
“Kekeke, are you nervous about meeting the shaman you’ve been eagerly awaiting? I can feel your heart pounding from all the way over here.”
What is this guy saying? I didn’t expect this at all. Where did the old shaman go?

chapters.title: Chapter 392: Captain Barbarian (2)
paragraphs: The trainee shamans who once did odd jobs under the old shaman certainly looked quite convincing, from the eye patch that helped him give off a mysterious aura to the tattoos all over his body. He may have been young, but he was believable as a shaman.
“Now, sit down and take off your top, little warrior.”
The way he lowered his voice on purpose and spoke in a theatrical tone broke the illusion, though. He wasn’t wearing an eyepatch on a perfectly normal eye, was he?
Slide.
Although I couldn’t bring myself to fully trust in his abilities, I sat down and took off my shirt anyway. The young shaman placed his hand on my shoulder.

“You already hold the power of an immortal spirit in your body.” The shaman immediately identified the path I chose, then lowered his hand to my chest and groped me like a pervert. “Then let’s see how far you have gotten.” I could tell just by his tone that he was underestimating me. It didn’t take long for that to change, though.

The hand that started on my shoulder moved down to my chest, then headed toward my side where my lat muscles were located. That was where I’d received the third stage of the Immortality Imprint and the point where you could start specializing.
“Kekeke, you chose the Spirit of the Wild.”
I obtained Wild Outburst then. A proper tank should have the ability to raise their Threat Level, right?

“Already accepting a spirit at a young age, you must have worked hard—” The shaman was yapping away in a proud tone when he suddenly stiffened in shock. Before I knew it, his hand was moving beyond my lats and over my back. At this point, I seriously considered socking him in the face.
This is fine and all, but your face is getting too close.
It looked a lot like he was hugging me.
Slide.

The shaman’s hand traveled up my back and reached the nape of my neck. “Oh? Even your spirit vein is open? Quite...” That was stage four, which increased my Spirit Ability and Soul Ability. The hand moved down the back of my neck and returned to the front, settling on the spot over my heart. “...Th-the qi vein is also open?”

Judging by his startled tone of voice, it seemed he assumed from the marquess’s explanation that he was only here to make a low-level imprint. This was starting to bother me so I forcibly removed the shaman’s hand.
“W-What are you doing? I’m conducting a sacred ritual to read your path—”
And I’m saying that’s a waste of time.
“Spirit vein, qi vein, or whatever, stop groping me. I’ve finished imprinting up to the Soul of Battle.”

“Y-You’ve opened... even the Soul of Battle...?” When he heard I finished imprinting even the sixth stage, the shaman flinched. Then he seemed to realize that was too undignified of him. “D-Did you know? You must make a very precious offering to imprint the next—”

“Ah, I already bought the Soul of the Dead, so you don’t have to worry.” I didn’t know why the warrior led the imprinting ritual instead of the shaman, but he had everything he needed to start. “That’s enough conversation, why don’t we get started?”
I lay down on the cloth that seemed to have been prepared for me. But no matter how long I waited there, the procedure did not start.
“Sorcerer, what are you doing?”
“...Just wait a moment. I need time to center my breathing and concentrate before I start the ritual.”
Concentrate on what? You’re just nervous.

As soon as I picked up on the fact that something was wrong, I raised my upper body off the ground and verbalized my doubts. I was sure this couldn’t possibly be, but... “Sorcerer, are you... You’ve never done a high-level imprint before?”
“...There may not have been any warriors who have asked to receive it yet, but I’ve learned the technique.”
Dang, this is making me anxious now.

I suddenly felt like I’d become a test dummy for a young shaman to gain experience but I had no other choice. It wasn’t like I could tell him to bring the veteran shaman here instead. I was also starting to think it might be better to receive the imprint from the young one since he didn’t recognize me. Besides, he officially held the title of shaman.
I’m sure he’ll do a proper imprint.
That’s what I thought until the first needle pricked my skin.
Stab.
“Ahhh!”
Stab.
“Kaaaagh!”
Stab.
“Why are you tilting your head? Fuck, you just stabbed the wrong spot, didn’t you?”
“...I-I didn’t!”
“Yeah right—”
“It’s going well, just stay still!”
Stab.
“Arghhh!”
Was the Spirit Imprint always this painful? I felt like I was going to lose my mind last time, too, but it wasn’t this bad.
Stab. Stab. Stab. Stab!
Time passed slowly and my brain continued to marinate in a bath of vivid pain. It felt like days later when...
“I-It’s all done...” The shaman finally uttered the words I’d been desperately waiting for, looking exhausted.
[You have activated Immortality Imprint: Stage 7.]

A foreign sensation filled my body, which was drained of all energy. It was a slightly different sensation from when stats normally went up. Based on this, it seemed the imprint itself had worked out all right.
[Your Restorative Power has increased.]

Restorative Power was a similar stat to Muscle Mass. If Muscle Mass increased Strength stats by 1 percent per point, Restorative Power adjusted all healing and regeneration effects in proportion to its value. Of course, it still wasn’t as immediately obvious as a change in Strength.
[Your Special Ability stat has increased by +300.]
Whether it was natural regeneration or a potion, it’d be more noticeable when I tried to use a healing effect.
“Hehehe...” The rewards were great and worth the hardship.
As I laughed to myself, forgetting all about the pain, I heard the shaman make a strange comment. “...This is my first time seeing someone smile after imprinting a new soul on their body.”
“That’s because you’re inexperienced. Warriors usually laugh when times are tough.”
“That’s not true...! I’ve worked on so many warriors—”
Uh-huh, and how many people could you have possibly imprinted in the two and a half years I was away?

“Right, good work.” Energy was slowly returning to my body so I got up from where I was lying. Because the room was filled with candles and the curtains were already shut when I got there, I hadn’t realized it was already nighttime.
I told them I might be late so they hopefully won’t be worried.

The shaman would return to the holy land today or tomorrow morning on his own, so I just put my clothes back on and left. Out front were the staff members who guided me earlier. But what was wrong with their expressions? They looked almost scared.
“Um... Are you all right?”
Ah, they must’ve heard my screaming from out here. Since they didn’t know about the imprint, they must have been wondering what I was doing inside.
“Yeah, I want to go back home now. Can I just leave?” Implicit in my question was a request for them to prepare a carriage for me again just like the one I used to get here.
“Mr. Schuitz,” the guard carefully said, “Lord Tercerion has asked to see you.”
“The marquess...?”

When I spoke without honorifics, the man’s face paled like he was the one who made the mistake. But it seemed he couldn’t point out a guest’s blunder to his face. “Yes, Lord Tercerion is waiting. Let us go.” He emphasized the title and then led me off to another room.
Hmm, I should be more careful about those things around other people from now on. I can’t let them know I’m a barbarian yet.
Creaaak.

We arrived at the study. When I walked in, the marquess took his eyes off his papers and glanced up at me. He only greeted me when the guard closed the door and left. “How was the imprint, Baronet Yandel?”

“Good, thanks to you. But why did you call me again?” I got straight to the point because I was tired, but as always, he didn’t condemn me for my rudeness. He simply answered in kind, just like I wanted him to.

“I had something I needed to tell you right away.” The marquess got straight to the point without showing any displeasure. But I wondered if this guy knew that the more he showed me his friendly side, the less trustworthy he seemed and the warier I became.
“Tell me. What is it?”

“The first thing is that I’ve finished persuading the individuals you wanted to recruit.” The marquess explained that he was able to recruit the wizard I wanted, and because the priest refused, he got the special ability user we chose as our Plan B. Too bad, if the priest worked out, we would’ve had a lot more options.
“Anyway, I’m guessing there’s a second thing?”
“There is. To be honest, the first part could have been conveyed in writing.”
“I’m curious, tell me.”
“Tomorrow, the heads of each team are planning to hold a meeting. If possible, we plan to get them to decide on the position of commander-in-chief then.”
“...Tomorrow, so suddenly?”
“The labyrinth will be opening soon. We may not be able to mobilize you for a big operation right away, but there’s a need to finish finalizing the squadron’s structure. Is there a problem?”
“No, none. As you said, it’s better to deal with things like this as soon as possible. So, how will you decide on the commander?”
“I told you. It will be determined there. Since all five team leaders have their own backers, they will each try to take on the role of commander.”
“Put simply, your plan is to gather us all up in one place and make us decide amongst ourselves.”
“To summarize, yes. Is that all right with you?”

“Don’t worry. I refuse to work under an uptight prick.” This was a special unit going on dangerous missions, right? It was better that I become the commander than watch some brutish moron lead us in circles. Of course, if the right person showed up, it wouldn’t be a bad idea to sit back and enjoy the ride, either.
“So, where are we meeting tomorrow?”
“I have invited them here to my home. We will be having lunch together.”
Lunch tomorrow, huh? If it’s going to be here anyway, it’d be a hassle to go back and forth.
“Can I sleep here today?”
“Of course. If you want, I can help send word to your household right away. I’m sure she’ll be worried.”
“Ah, I’ll leave that part to you.”

After talking for about thirty more minutes, the marquess helped me contact Erwen and Amelia through the branch of the Magic Tower in District Seven. Once that was done, I headed to the room I stayed in last time, washed up, and got ready for bed.
Flop!
A nobleman’s bed was too soft to compare to the bed back home. As it always did the day I received an imprint, sleep came to me as soon as I lay down.
Hooonk!
I was sure I wouldn’t get any strange visitors tonight.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 7
Physique: 1461.40
Spirit: 521.3
Special Ability: 2197.65 (New +390)
Item Level: 8305
General Combat Power: 6256.60 (New +390)
Acquired Essences: Orc Hero - Rank 5  Ogre - Rank 3  Bayon - Rank 3  Storm Gush - Rank 3  Vol-Herchan - Rank 3  Gachabone - Rank 6  Deep Sea Giant - Rank 3]

The next morning, although the meeting was scheduled for lunch, I woke up early and got ready with the help of the servant to uphold Tercerion’s reputation. My hair was neatly combed, and I was dressed in a fitted top and trousers.
It’s been a while since I’ve worn clothes like this... Not bad.
My reflection in the mirror looked pretty good even by my standards. Was it because my body shrank? For once, I didn’t feel too torn up about it.
“Wait a little longer.”
“I saw out the window that some people are already here.”
“Not everyone has arrived yet.”

Since I stayed at the mansion last night, I was able to finish getting ready early, but I was made to keep waiting in my room. I wondered why I couldn’t just wait in the banquet hall but apparently, nobles were prideful about that kind of stuff. It seemed there was an unspoken tension around what time you arrived for meetings.
“Okay, let us go now. Everyone will be waiting.”
Well, I had no reason not to listen to the marquess when it came to these things so I waited until it was time and we headed to the banquet hall together.
Creaaak.
The servant opened the door for us without me even needing to touch it myself.
“Hello, Lord Tercerion.”
“I didn’t know you would also be attending the meal, Prime Minister.”
“What a treat. I am truly honored.”

When the marquess arrived, the three men and one woman who had arrived first all stood up and bowed, and the marquess greeted them once they were done. “Haha, it is nice to meet you all. The food may not be up to the standards of distinguished individuals such as yourselves, but please enjoy yourselves while you are here.”
The marquess sat at the head of the table. As I was instructed to in advance, I sat in the seat immediately to his right.

“Bring out the food.” While the staff filled the table, the marquess led us through introductions much like a blind date. “Since some of you are meeting for the first time, I believe an introduction is in order. What do you think?”

“I agree. May I go first?” The first person to step forward was the man sitting across from me. “Since everyone seems younger than me and there don’t seem to be any nobles, I will speak comfortably.” He had on a crisp uniform with a checkered pattern embroidered on it and neatly brushed red hair. “I am Melend Kaislan.”

I remembered the marquess telling me about him yesterday. He was the youngest son of Count Kaislan and a veteran knight who had entered the military at a young age and had many war achievements. While he may have been the youngest son, he was still over forty and married with several children.

“I’ve spent decades in the military and thanks to that, I’m extremely familiar with combat. But commanding is another thing entirely. I have seen countless talented individuals lose their lives in vain due to incompetent leaders.” This guy had gotten up to introduce himself but instead launched into some lengthy self-promotion. “I am not looking down on you all, but if one of us is to assume responsibility and take that position, I believe no one is better suited than me.”
Was it because he was a veteran with a lot of experience? That military-style speech alone seemed to show off just how narrow-minded he was. And I wasn’t the only one who thought so.

“...Oh my, weren’t we simply introducing ourselves? You’ve put a lot of pressure on the next person.” The dwarf lady next to him offered a soft smile and a passive-aggressive comment before standing up. “In that case, I will go next.”
Wow, look at how smooth that was.
In truth, I knew who this woman was before she even revealed her name. There weren’t many female dwarven adventurers of her age.

“I’m Titana Akurava.” She didn’t seem to have any intention of mentioning her age herself but everyone who knew her knew she was sixty-one. Of course, as it was a trait of her race to age quickly and then maintain that appearance for years, she looked much younger than a human born in the same year would. Age meant nothing to this woman, though.
“...Akurava? Are you really Akurava?” When she revealed her name, the noble knight flinched, his eyes going wide. Rightfully so, because she was a famous adventurer. No, should I say legendary?
“Even I wouldn’t dare lie in front of the marquess.”
“I... right. I was just surprised. I heard you retired ten years ago.”

I first heard about this woman from the marquess, actually. She was a member of a legendary team that used to explore the ninth floor, but after the team suddenly announced their retirement ten years ago, she never appeared in public again. In short, she was from a completely different generation than me.
“Haha, I happened to venture back out into the world again. May I continue, young knight?”
“...Of course.”

She silenced the interrupting knight and took some time to promote herself as he did earlier. “I can guarantee no one knows more about the labyrinth than me. Nor does any adventurer have as much luck. Doesn’t that speak for itself?” It was a short speech that exuded confidence.

As soon as she sat down, another man stood up, unfazed. “Haha, I never expected to meet one of my role models like this. I will go next.” The man gave off a rather lighthearted air. His most notable feature was his height, around 5′3″, which was slightly on the shorter side even among humans. “I am James Calla, the deputy commander of the Sawtooth Clan.”

Sawtooth was one of the super-huge clans that had gone from a Top Ten clan to a Top Four clan. This guy also took a page from the first two speakers’ books and talked up his strengths for a while. Being part of a large clan, he was up to date on the latest information and confident about his ability to synthesize everyone’s opinions and come up with strategies that would satisfy us all. It was clearly an appeal that targeted the old dwarf and stubborn knight, but I wasn’t particularly impressed. My mind wandered to something I had read about him in the papers.
He was an archer, I think?
That was the only thing I had to remember about him.

Once the deputy commander’s introduction was over, the paladin next to him stood up. “I am Jun from the Tovera Church. The surname I once used in the secular world is no more, as I have abandoned it.” In contrast to the previous ones, this introduction was short.
“...Is that it?” the knight asked.

The paladin clicked his tongue with a slightly displeased look on his face but added, “There is nothing more unstable and dangerous than human desire. Everything will go as is planned, according to god’s will.”
“It seems the three churches are being surprisingly selfless about this mission.” The knight attempted to compliment the churches but the paladin ignored him.
“Now... it’s just you left.”

My turn finally arrived and their attention turned to me. Everyone pretended not to be, but their curiosity was obvious. Of course they were curious. I was here as a representative of the marquess, the kingdom’s second-in-command, but my face was one they were seeing for the first time. They must have been wary about the fact that they had very limited information about me.
Creak.
I pushed my chair back, stood up, and told them my name. “Riehen Schuitz.” I could see frowns around the table.
That’s it?

That was what those frowns seemed to be asking. Even the marquess looked like he felt the same. He must have been wondering why I was staying quiet when everyone before me had actively promoted themselves.
Jeez, don’t rush me. So not cool.
I had no intention of going on and on like everyone before me. It was obvious they’d all tune it out anyway, so why bother?
Slide.

I looked around the table slowly and made eye contact with each person, starting with the soldier of noble birth. “Knights, noblemen.” Next was the dwarf lady. “Famous adventurers.” Third was the deputy commander. “Clans.” Finally, I looked at the paladin. “God, or whatever... I don’t follow anyone weaker than me.”
When it came to self-promotion, the shorter it was, the more of a punch it packed.

chapters.title: Chapter 393: Captain Barbarian (3)
paragraphs: Tap.

I sat back down once I finished saying everything I had to say, and a moment of silence fell over the banquet hall. This was only natural. The intention of this gathering was for us to convince others that we were good leaders. It was obvious how my statement was received.
“Do you mean to say you are stronger than us?” The question came from the noble knight, whose displeasure was clearly visible from the way his jaw clenched.
I smirked. “You understood me correctly.” I decided there was no need to deny it. It wasn’t like I said anything wrong.
Despite my bold answer, the table was surprisingly quiet. The knight seemed to want to fire back at me but held back for the sake of the marquess beside him.
Slide.
I glanced at the marquess and we met eyes. Surprisingly, the marquess was looking at me with amusement instead of disgust at my actions.
Hmm, I wonder how the others are feeling.
When I took a look around, I saw different emotions in the eyes that were on me.
“I hope you have at least half as much skill as you do arrogance. Skilled subordinates are always welcome.” The noble knight’s eyes radiated hostility born of offense.
“Haha, men of that age are all like that. I rather like it because it’s manly.” Contrary to her friendly tone, the look in the dwarf woman’s eyes suggested that she found me pitiful.

“Riehen Schuitz... I’ve heard of you. I’ve heard people say you’re the Blood Spirit’s man?” The deputy commander of the Sawtooth Clan, meanwhile, had eyes that seemed intent on picking me apart, a deep curiosity in his gaze.
As for Jun, the paladin of Tovera Church, he looked at me with eyes that were surprisingly barren of all emotion.
What, I’m not even worth worrying about?

I couldn’t be sure but the attention on me scattered and everyone began to study each other. Now that the introductions were over, it was time to make a call. Who would be the biggest obstacle in my path to becoming a leader?

“This is meant to be a happy event but things seem to have gotten tense. Since everyone has introduced themselves, let’s eat.” The marquess stepped forward at that moment to lift the mood and everyone started to eat and chat. Of course, things didn’t get much friendlier.
“One of us will be in the position to lead us all. As I’m sure you all know, it is a position of great responsibility.”

The position required you to take responsibility for the lives of thirty people. However, everyone here also knew that as soon as you took up that mantle, you’d see great rewards. As for me, the marquess already promised a lot of support.
“So, what is it that you want to say, Sir Kaislan? That we don’t deserve it?” The dwarf lady spoke calmly, making it clear she had no intention of giving up the position.
“Ahem, I just wanted to make sure you all really understand what that means,” the knight said, looking almost disgruntled by her refusal. It seemed he regarded her as his biggest competitor.

Not missing this opening, the deputy commander took the opportunity to subtly talk up his career. “Haha, I think I know what you mean. I was also weighed down by countless responsibilities and obligations as I climbed the ranks to my current position.”
Wow, what kind of battle of wills is this?
“Let me ask this bluntly and get this out of the way. Sir Jun, are you after this position as well?”

“There is nothing as fleeting as human emotions. Everything will happen as God wills it.” In a way, that sounded like he was taking up the position of a bystander in all this. The knight’s expression brightened—right until the paladin continued. “But it seems that among everyone here, I am the one who is most aligned with God’s will.” That was a wordy way to say he would also be participating in this competition.
Perhaps because he knew the three churches were backing up the paladin, the knight looked even more concerned. It seemed he saw the paladin as a major player as well. “I see.”
What the—why aren’t you asking me? Jeez, hurting my feelings.

Once the battle of wills to feel each other out came to an end, the knight gave a firm, determined nod and resumed control of the conversation. “There are many who want it, but only one seat. In the end, we will have to decide which one of us is most qualified.”
“Oh, that sounds like you have thoughts on how we should choose.”
“First, why don’t we talk about what we each believe makes an ideal commander?” Put simply, he wanted us to learn more about each other’s personalities.
“All right. We can do that.” The dwarf lady readily agreed to the knight’s suggestion. The paladin and I didn’t object either, and the process went smoothly.

“Since I was the one to bring it up, I will go first.” As always, the first one to speak was the knight, who liked to take initiative. Like the soldier he was, he loudly declared, “A group cannot live up to its true potential if it cannot work as one. I believe the most important quality for a commander is leadership.”
“That’s too abstract. What exactly do you think leadership means?”
“It is the power to create and maintain discipline. From there, you create control. A perfectly controlled unit has no issues working toward a goal.”

I could already picture this guy as the leader, rigidly micromanaging every little thing to create a group without any individuality. The knight went on to give a long, passionate speech about what kind of team he wanted to create and what his strengths were.
“That’s it.”
As soon as the knight’s turn was over, the dwarf lady took the floor. “Thank you for your explanation. I’ll go next.”

Unlike the knight’s speech, which was all very predictable, I was quite interested in what this woman had to say. She was a top adventurer, after all. I wondered what someone like her would place the most value on.
“Since the olden days, problems inside the labyrinth were solved by adventurers. Historically speaking, military intervention like the kind we see today was extremely rare. How come?”
“That’s because the palace respects the ways of adventurers.”

“That may also be the case, but I believe the real reason was because the palace saw it as the most effective solution. Anything can happen in the labyrinth. They needed talent that could deal with all kinds of situations, and that talent was the city’s adventurers. Mobilizing hundreds and thousands of troops inside the labyrinth is too much of a logistical challenge in the first place.”
“So, Akurava, are you saying the ideal commander is an adventurer?”

“That’s not what I mean. I’m just saying that if we need someone to lead inside the labyrinth, that person needs to have abundant knowledge of and experience in the labyrinth, and the ability to make proactive decisions.”

Many of the qualities the dwarf lady listed were ones I could accept. To be honest, I thought it would be much safer to work under this woman than that knight bastard. Her statement wasn’t without issue, though.

“Excuse me, but Ms. Akurava, you don’t have experience leading others, do you?” She frowned at the deputy commander’s words. I guessed she never expected someone who showed her respect to throw her under the bus like this. But even as she glared at him, the deputy commander finished his thought. “I’m sure someone else was in charge of leading your old team.”
“...I have experience leading a team before that.”
“I see. But leading a party and leading thirty people are two different things.”
Wow, this guy has no brakes, either. Well, it’d be weird to worry about the morality of questioning seniority in a business setting like this.
“Anyway, I’m done speaking. I guess you can go next, Mr. Calla.”

“Well, if you insist.” The value Calla embodied by belittling the dwarf woman was this. “No matter what, the most important thing to a commander is information. You said so yourself, Ms. Akurava: the commander has to be able to respond proactively to any situation.”
“Yes, and?”
“With prior intel, it’s possible to avoid being in those situations altogether. And even if you find yourself in a crisis, your options only grow the more information you have.”
It seemed the deputy commander’s main goal here was to keep her in check because he kept staring at the dwarf lady as he spoke. Did that agitate her?
“You’re certainly not wrong. That is, if you have that much access to information,” the dwarf lady responded, sounding more irritable than usual.

The deputy commander immediately opened his mouth like he’d been hoping she’d react like that. “The Alminus Company and Adventurers’ Guild are behind me. Of course, I won’t be able to know about everything going on with perfect accuracy, but... It seems my finger is the closest to the pulse out of everyone in this room.”

The dwarf lady wasn’t able to say anything to that. If the Alminus Company and Adventurers’ Guild were backing him, he’d be able to collect more information than even the palace when it came to the labyrinth, though he may be at a slight disadvantage in terms of top-secret information.
“That’s it for me. Who would like to go next?”

“I will,” said Jun the paladin from beside the deputy commander. He then launched into a long speech like a priest preaching to his congregation. “Everything starts with faith, and that is no different for a commander. Strong faith and trust create a courage that will not give in to any evil...”
Wow, this guy actually talks a lot.

“The world is full of trials. Some overcome them, while others get frustrated and lose faith. But did you know?” Unlike before, his eyes were full of passion. I got the impression earlier that he was a stone-cold guy. “Those who overcome those trials are always those who have kept their faith. Only faith can bring strangers together, and only that united faith can get us through trials.”
Whew, but repeating the same thing over and over again has to get monotonous...
Yawn...
When I let out an involuntary yawn, the paladin pursed his lips and glared at me. “It seems my talk of faith is boring you.”
What, you thought it wouldn’t?
When I shot him a What did you expect? look, the paladin furrowed his brow. “Then why don’t you speak now?”
When the paladin tried to pass the baton to me, the person next to me perked up. “Yes, that would be a good idea.”
“Yes. I’m curious.”
I guessed the others were bored with the faith lecture too.

“Riehen Schuitz, what kind of person do you think the commander has to be?” the deputy commander asked me. There was a subtle undertone to his voice, like he was addressing a citizen who might be swayed to vote for him in the future, rather than a fellow nominee. And he wasn’t the only one.
“Earlier, it sounded like you want a commander who can lead firmly.” The knight subtly promoted himself.
When the knight stepped forward, the dwarf lady also jumped in. “A soldier might want that, sure. But an adventurer would know how important the things I mentioned are.”
It was ridiculous to the point of hilarity. Why were they expecting me to agree with them? I made myself clear earlier.
“...Why are you laughing?”

That was obvious. “It’s just funny that you’re all wasting time trying to debate who the best fit is. Who are you guys trying to persuade in the first place?” While the others had been giving their passionate speeches, I ate my meal intently and was now licking the sauce off my fingers. “When the winner can just take the seat.” I set down my cup after chugging down its contents.
Boom.
The hefty bang echoed through the banquet hall, but no one flinched.
“Ha... I knew he would be like this.”
“Then I guess what you’re looking for, Mr. Schuitz, is power.”
They gave me looks that seemed to suggest they saw me as somewhat pathetic. Either they didn’t know how to read people, or they just lacked imagination.
“Now I see you were just a fool believing in your own petty abilities. Do you think you can convince us like that?”
“Yeah.”
“Traditionally, leadership cannot be achieved by strength alone and—what?”
“Why can’t I convince you?” Now that I was full, I was in the perfect condition to get some exercise. “Stop running your mouth and fight me.”
When I jumped up from my chair, the knight at the other end of my gaze was taken aback. He seemed to be wondering whether this was allowed in front of the marquess.
I guessed he had decided to entrust this task to me, though, because the marquess completely took my side. “I have no intention of interfering with whatever method you all choose.”
I shrugged. “So he says.”

The dwarf lady responded to my blasé attitude in a sharp tone. “Even if you fight him and win, we won’t accept you as the leader. If someone who only knows how to pick fights ends up in that position—”

What was this woman saying? “What, would you have accepted me if I said something else?” This was the fundamental reason why I said that what these guys were doing earlier was a waste of time. I looked at each one of them in turn and said, “Firm control. Experience and good judgment. An extensive ability to gather information. And trust.” These were the qualities of a commander they mentioned. “Yeah, these things aren’t bad.”
And I genuinely meant that, but there was a very serious problem here.
“The fact is, though, we can talk about this all day, but who here will actually accept someone else as the leader?”
There was no way everyone could get what they wanted here by reaching an agreement, especially if what they were trying to sell were fanciful buzzwords like that.
“Are you saying you’re different, then?”
“Yeah.” Power was different. “So, fight me.”
“Don’t be foolish. Even if you defeat him—”
“Who said I meant just him?”

They wouldn’t accept me—I knew that much. But life as a barbarian had taught me that if you ever faced a situation where power alone wasn’t enough to get the other party to bend to your will, that was only because you lacked the power needed to pull it off.
“All of you.” Looking out at the three men and women who seemed to be struggling to keep up with my logic, I grinned. “All of you, attack me at once.”
If we were talking power, there wasn’t a single wizard among them.

chapters.title: Chapter 394: Captain Barbarian (4)
paragraphs: The reason why I said that I would fight all four at once was simple. Even if I defeated all four of them in a one-on-one tournament, they wouldn’t accept it. I determined there was only one way to convince everyone: by tossing them a treat they couldn’t stomach not swallowing.

“Ah, I’ll say this in advance. If I lose, I will give up my claim to the position of commander.” In other words, this was a chance for them to knock a competitor off the stage. “Why is no one saying anything? Are you not confident you can win even if the four of you fight me together?”
When I tossed in some more provocation, my opponents began to react.
“I accept,” said Akurava.
“What? Why should we pit ourselves against one person like this—”
“He’s saying he’ll drop out, so why should we argue?”
“Ms. Akurava is right.” The deputy commander backed the dwarf woman up, turning this into a democratic vote.

At this, the knight nodded with a look of displeasure on his face and the paladin remained silent, which seemed to be his way of expressing his approval. They probably knew it too. This situation might end up being a bit awkward to explain to others, but it was an opportunity to knock a competitor out of the running with ease.
“Riehen Schuitz, right?” asked Akurava.
“Yes?”
“You’re going to have to keep your promise.”
“Of course. If I lose, I will submit myself to the leadership of whoever you choose. But—”
“You want this to go both ways, right? Fine. If by some chance you beat all of us, you will get the position you’re after.”

After that, I asked the three aside from Akurava to make sure they agreed to these terms as well, and just like that, a verbal contract was made. Though it wasn’t in writing, I had a more trustworthy notary than anyone else so I wasn’t worried at all.
“That’s that, then. Lord Tercerion, is there a suitable place?” asked Akurava.
“Of course.”

The marquess didn’t seem concerned about me in the slightest as he lent us the mansion’s training grounds. It probably wasn’t because he trusted me 100 percent, though. It was just that, if I failed because of my recklessness, he still stood to gain something. For example, he could use this failure as an excuse to tighten my leash and micromanage me.
“Then I will be waiting outside,” said the marquess.
Once I reached the training grounds, I put on my equipment.
[You have equipped a Large Adamantium Battle Shield. Your total Item Level has increased by +1750.]
I started with the shield I bought for a large sum once I returned from the past.
[You have equipped an Iron Breastplate. Your total Item Level has increased by +150.]
[You have equipped Iron Gaiters. Your total Item Level has increased by +75.]
[You have equipped War Boots. Your total Item Level has increased by +45.]
This was equipment I bought for cheap because I didn’t have the money at the time. Now that I had money, I should change everything to adamantium.
[You have equipped No. 87: Kraul’s Demon Grinder. Your total Item Level has increased by +4800.]
When I stepped out onto the training grounds in full armor, the other four appeared one by one as they finished their own preparations.
“It’s very strange, no? I feel more comfortable in these than clothes made of cloth now,” said the knight.
“That means your body has gotten used to it since you wear it more often than everyday clothes.”
Their equipment looked expensive even at a glance. But no matter how well it was taken care of, there was noticeable wear and tear and signs of use on the joints. I took in their gear.
Jeez, they even came fully equipped with accessories.
Yeah, I figured they would have brought these in their sub-spaces even if they came dressed in suits. They wouldn’t have been able to call themselves adventurers otherwise.
“But things on the other side look... very different from what I expected.”
“I thought he was Blood Spirit’s man. I guess she didn’t buy him armor.”
“Riehen Schuitz, do you really intend to fight with that equipment?”

The four made strange faces at my ordinary iron equipment. The looks in their eyes were closer to surprise than contempt, though. They probably didn’t expect me to be so shabby-looking when I was here on the marquess’s recommendation.
“It’s not a problem.”

What was the big deal about iron armor? It wouldn’t make a significant difference in this battle. To be honest, their looks were kind of embarrassing me, but when I thought about it, it wasn’t that big an issue.
“Okay, fight me.”
Logically, it was the people who ended up getting their asses kicked that were a bigger embarrassment, right?

There was a popular saying that a battle between masters was decided in a split second. I, of course, didn’t agree. Maybe if it was a life-or-death fight between knights, sure, but I was a proper tank. Where I truly shined was battles that dragged on. But at least in the beginning, this wasn’t much different from the fight between masters that popped into my head unbidden.

All conversation suddenly evaporated. Everyone stood at a distance from each other. Eyelids blinked with less frequency. Eyes crossed paths and a heavy tension settled. Muscles trained through years of real combat were contracted to spring into action at any moment, and beads of sweat gradually formed on hands gripping weapons.
Slide.
Our keen senses picked up on even the smallest of movements. This was one of the reasons why many-versus-one battles were difficult. There were too many things to pay attention to.
Yeah, so instead of that...
“How long are you going to stand there like that?”

The moment I threw that question out there and saw my opponents move to answer, I used that single breath as an opportunity to kick off the ground and rush forward. My first target was the knight who had taken the most aggressive position out front. The guy was forced to swallow back whatever he was going to say and narrowed his eyes. It seemed I’d hurt his pride by choosing him as the first target.
Whooom!

The aura of a skilled knight who was in his prime wrapped around his sword in an instant and swung toward me. Labyrinth or city, it was an aura that would have cut through most armored warriors like tofu.
[You have cast Iron Fortress.]
[The effect of Evolving Shell has increased by 1.5 times.]
I raised my shield to block it.
Khak!

When the sword bounced off instead of cutting through everything in its path like I was sure it usually did, the knight looked startled. But as he was a soldier trained in live combat, that surprise only lasted for a moment.
Whippp!

The knight used the recoil from the bounce to spin in the air and swing his sword at me again. The target this time was my lower body, which was difficult to block with a shield. To be more precise, he was aiming for the area around my calf covered by iron gaiters.
Did he think the adamantium was the problem?
It was a very quick call to make after just one exchange. The problem was, it wasn’t the right one.
Khak!
Are you underestimating iron?
My opponent was using big, flashy movements and leaving a lot of openings, so I took the opportunity to kick him in the chin.
Bang!
His body floated in the air from the blow at just the right angle to hit with my hammer.
[Jun Arshen has cast Light of Protection.]
God damn it.
Kwaaang!

Just in time, divine power came in clutch, a shield of light appearing right above the knight’s head to block my hammer. Using the gap he was given, the knight retreated. Even after almost dying, this guy seemed more preoccupied with something else. “How...?”
Jeez, why are all knights the same? I guess it is pretty surprising to block an aura with iron armor, though.
Anyway, rather than wearing top-of-the-line products, it was more important to make yourself a top-of-the-line product.
“The equipment itself is ordinary no matter how I look at it.”
“Then he must be the reason for this strange phenomenon.”

Correct. Not only did Union increase the Physical Resistance of my equipment, but Evolving Shell and Ironskin were also at play here. Though, while the adamantium shield didn’t have a single scratch on it from the knight’s swing, the iron armor had some deep ones.
“I don’t know what kind of essence he has, but to be able to stop an aura... it seems his confidence wasn’t completely unfounded.”

Akurava and the deputy commander quickly exchanged their thoughts while watching me from a short distance away. “I have a few guesses, although I don’t know why their effects would extend to his equipment. Mr. Calla, will you try firing an arrow at him?”
At Akurava’s instructions, the deputy commander, who was dressed from head to toe in dragon-skin armor, pulled back his bowstring. Did they figure out my resistance to swords already?
[James Calla has cast Piercing Light.]
As soon as light started to gather around the arrowhead, I covered my body with the shield to defend myself. That was because if I tried to rely on sight, I’d already be too late.
Swoop!
The light arrow was fired with a short whipping sound. Since I blocked it with my shield in time, I didn’t take any damage.
“The arrowhead went in.” However, the arrowhead dug deep into the adamantium shield, which hadn’t even been scratched by the aura earlier. At that, Akurava shouted, “Swords don’t work on this man.”
Yikes, I’ll be out of cards at this rate.
Bang!

The paladin, who continued to charge forward even after I pushed the knight back earlier, closed in. This guy’s main defenses were a large shield and mace. Yeah, that was a fundamental combination for any respectable tank.
Kwaaang!
Instead of using his weapon, the paladin made a wall with his shield and tried to stop me in my tracks.
Pushhh.
It seemed his basic Strength stat wasn’t very high, though, because he was pushed back as soon as we collided, his feet dragging through the dirt. Unfortunately, he didn’t go very far.
[Jun Arshen has cast Divine Opening.]
[Jun Arshen has cast Rising Power.]
[Jun Arshen has cast Blessing of the Sun.]
Like the buff-casting, self-healing tanks all paladins were, he used divine power in quick succession, a white light bursting from his body.
“What incredible strength.” As soon as he wasn’t getting shoved backward anymore, he took a moment to compliment me.
Jeez, that hurts my pride. Still, I guess what matters is I’ve reached the distance I was aiming for.
[You have cast Transcendence.]
[You have cast Eye of the Storm.]
My grab skill really shined in PVP. The maximum radius was twenty yards but my reason for getting this close was simple—the shorter the distance, the harder it was to react to it in time.
Whiiiiiip!
A strong gust of wind kicked up despite the otherwise calm afternoon.
“Ah...!” My target was the deputy commander in the rear. When you were fighting one-v-many, it was standard practice to attack the rearguard first.
And that armor makes me want to tear him apart.
In return for granting the wearer considerable Mana Resistance, dragon leather was vulnerable to physical attacks. Put simply, just one hit would put him at death’s door.
[You have cast Giantization. Your Threat Level and Physical Attributes increase in proportion to your increase in size.]
Activating the skill I’d been saving so far, I used my increased Strength to push the paladin away.
Dash.
Then I jumped toward the archer who got flung by the gust of wind. Using my increased reach from Giantization, I brought my hammer down before the archer guy could even react.
[Jun Arshen has cast Light of Protection.]
The paladin I beat once again used the divine spell he used to save the knight earlier.
[You have used a transformation-type ability. Due to the effect of Evolving Shell, the amount of Soul Power consumed by the ability is reduced by half, and your highest stat increases by 1.5 times.]
This was bound to go different than before because the blow he blocked earlier was just a regular hit.
[You have cast Swing. The damage you deal with blunt weapons has increased significantly in proportion to your Muscle Strength.]
Crackkk!
The moment my hammer touched it, the barrier shattered like glass.
Crack!

The deputy commander fell limply to the ground, blood oozing from his cracked forehead. A knight, a tank, and even ninth-floor adventurer Akurava hadn’t been able to prevent this stroke of misfortune.
As an uncomfortable silence settled, I quietly counted, “One down, for now.” There were now three out of four high-level adventurers left.
Hmm, maybe the knight shouldn’t count? Anyway, the real deal starts now.

Though I may have eliminated one of four powerful fighters, I didn’t lower my guard and instead steeled myself anew. I knew this was purely an early advantage. After all, I’d heard a lot about these guys from the marquess but they knew very little about me.

In that sense, this situation was kind of ironic. Although he wasn’t killed instantly, the deputy commander had been seriously injured and knocked out. To think the guy who preached that information was the most important thing during lunch earlier would be taken out first because he didn’t have enough information.
I can’t exactly say he’s been taken out, though.
In the universe of Dungeon and Stone, you could come back to life as long as you didn’t die.
[Jun Arshen has cast Hand of Regeneration.]

A pure white radiance spilled from the paladin’s body and flowed into the unconscious deputy commander. Since I didn’t have any nullification effects as a Shield Barbarian, I already took it for granted that this guy would inevitably be healed.
The short game won’t work.

I promptly abandoned the thought of giving my all to finishing this match before my opponents could recover. I hadn’t been pinning my hopes on such an overwhelming victory in the first place. After all, how could I destroy four top-tier adventurers by myself just because I had a good build? Everything had a price. That was the only truth in this cruel world.
“Aaaaaah!” I ran forward, swinging my hammer.
Bang.
The paladin stopped me.
Whooom!

At that moment, someone flew in and raised the weapon in their hands. It was the knight who got pushed away earlier. It seemed he’d swapped out his gear in that time because he was now holding a hammer instead of a sword. It was kind of funny to see a knight using a regular weapon instead of an aura. This must have been what separated high-talent individuals from the rest—responding appropriately to whatever situation they were in.
Kwaaang!
The blunt weapon struck my shoulder. The physical impact itself wasn’t that bad, but the moment I was hit, a heat seared through my bones. It took less than a second to figure out why.
Who carries something like that as a backup weapon?

No. 761: Loam’s Blast Furnace Hammer was a triple-digit Numbers Item. Its ability was that it piled on additional Fire Penetration damage in proportion to the user’s physical strength. Still, I could deal with it thanks to Flame Resistance.
“Haaaaaah!” With a shout, I activated Wild Outburst. Using my temporarily increased Physique stats, I kicked the paladin once more in an attempt to shove him back.
What the—why isn’t he budging?
My brain, which was pickled from dedicating my twenties to Dungeon and Stone, questioned and answered this at the same time.
[Jun Arshen has cast Holy Descent.]
So, he already activated that. This is definitely going to be tough.
It seemed the rest had fully raised their guards after seeing one of them go down. From here on out, it wouldn’t be easy for me to beat the paladin in terms of strength.
[Titana Akurava has used No. 1911: Fabler’s Broken Pocket Watch.]

Even the dwarf lady, who had been observing the situation, now joined the battle in earnest. For reference, this lady was essentially an attacker. Dwarves, who treated numbered items as must-haves, were as efficient in this position as they were as warriors.
[Up to five minutes of cooldown time has disappeared.]

Case in point, that watch normally only gave you a 70 percent reduction in cooldown time if you weren’t a dwarf. Since she was from the ninth floor, it was safe to say she had all the core items needed for an optimal build aside from this one as well.
So, what was this lady’s crown jewel again?
[Titana Akurava has cast Vampire Awl.]
Oh, right. That.
The rank-two skill consumed little MP, had decent damage, and even sucked out the target’s MP, but it usually lost points thanks to its cooldown time.
Whiiip!
A giant awl flew toward me. Normally it would be best to avoid this, but a paladin and knight were caging me in on both sides.
Kwaaang!

So, I just blocked it with my shield. Though she was functionally a mage, a skill like this was classified as physical damage. My arm was a little sore, but it was nothing I couldn’t handle. The problem was that blocking this left my side unprotected. As soon as there was an opening, the paladin and knight struck me with their weapons.
Kwaaang!
One instantly made me feel like my whole body was on fire.
Kwaaang!
The other tore through my Physical Resistance and even damaged my bones. Well, with Holy Descent, his Strength stat was probably twice as high as mine now.
Yeah, let’s give up on defense.

I made a quick call. If I was going to get hit twice for blocking once, I might as well get hit three times and get at least one hit of my own. Besides, thanks to stage seven of the Spirit Imprint, my healing factor was pretty decent now.
Kwaaang!

I blocked the big attacks with my shield and swung my hammer. My remaining three opponents seemed to take this as a threat as they started throwing new skills my way in an attempt to corner me. To add insult to injury, the deputy commander rejoined the fray thanks to the paladin’s healing.
“If you’re awake, use your bow!”
Kwaaang!
My shield was doing all right, but my iron armor wasn’t all that durable and was damaged in multiple places.
Whippp! Stab!
As arrows penetrated those weak points, my injuries grew.
Whoosh!
After getting hit so many times by the Blast Furnace Hammer, the heat that had been bearable before wasn’t so bearable anymore.
Kwaaang!
Each time the paladin’s mace hit me, it felt like my bones were being ground to dust. Well, maybe that was because they were getting crushed and healed simultaneously. That was probably it.
“You’re smiling?”
The more firepower they threw my way, the more I smiled. I expected it to at least be this tough, after all.
Spew!

I accidentally bit my tongue when I got hit with the hammer earlier, causing blood to gush from my mouth like a fountain. It was a shame I no longer had acid blood, but at least it could block their sight, right?
“...Monster.”
“I have to admit, you are definitely stronger than me.” As the dogfight dragged on, the knight spoke up. “But even you can’t beat four people all at once. Just give up.”
You wish.
I could see they were panting from exhaustion too. Meanwhile, I still had quite a bit of MP left.
[You have cast Soul Dive. Your Soul Power will regenerate at a rate proportional to the amount of Soul Power you have consumed.]
My MP, which was almost bottomed out, filled back up again. The battle continued from there for what felt like hours.
“Why... isn’t he collapsing?” the knight who smugly suggested I give up asked out loud.
“It’s... as if you drank from a holy spring,” the paladin muttered almost to himself.
“Enough of this. Don’t you already know you can’t win?” The dwarf lady seemed sick of my stubbornness.
“We’ll nullify our agreement from earlier, so why don’t we call this here?” The archer seemed to want to end this relentless battle as soon as possible.
“All of you... you’re talking too much. Are you scared of losing?”
As they wasted their breath trying to convince me, I concentrated on just two things: what I could do, and what I had to do right now.
“Just go down already!”
[Titana Akurava has cast Vampire Awl.]
[James Calla has cast Piercing Light.]
[Jun Arshen has cast Hand of Regeneration.]
And as I endured, endured, and endured some more, the moment I’d been waiting for finally arrived.
[Titana Akurava’s Soul Power is insufficient. Vampire Awl has been deactivated.]
[James Calla’s Soul Power is insufficient. Piercing Light has been deactivated.]
[Jun Arshen’s Soul Power is insufficient. Hand of Regeneration has been deactivated.]
Ultimately, the one left standing was the strongest.

chapters.title: Chapter 395: Captain Barbarian (5)
paragraphs: His head hurt. He felt nauseous, his lips were chapped, and his throat felt dry from a lack of moisture. But before all of that discomfort, the first thing that registered in his mind was a question.
Why do I feel like this?

The deputy commander of the Sawtooth Clan, James Calla, gasped like a man coming up for air and opened his eyes. The first thing he saw was an unfamiliar ceiling. A beautiful pattern was carved into the luxurious wood and in the center was a dazzling chandelier hanging from a chain.

While he was trying to figure out where he was, a man’s face appeared in his line of sight. “Looks like you’re awake now.” It was the paladin, Jun. When Calla first saw this man, he wondered how such a handsome paladin could be at this meeting.

“Ah...!” Recalling his last memory before losing consciousness, Calla sprang up. He turned to the paladin, who had thankfully moved just in time to avoid getting hit in the face. “The fight... how did the fight end?”
The paladin awkwardly raised the corners of his lips. “You already know that.”
“Then...”
“Yes, we lost. That man was strong in many ways.”
Unlike the paladin, who didn’t sound disappointed at all, Calla found himself sighing.
“Is it difficult for you to admit defeat, Mr. Calla?”
“That’s... not it. I just... don’t know what to say to the Alminus Company and Adventurers’ Guild after they believed in and supported me.”
“You can just tell them the truth.”
“That four people fought and lost against one barbaric man and ended up having to yield the position to him? How can I say—Why are you smiling?”
“Oh, excuse me. It’s just that your use of the word ‘barbaric’ left an impression.”

At that, Calla admitted to himself that he was in the wrong. He realized how he must have looked, saying such slanderous things after losing. It must have sounded like he was trying to put Schuitz down, just like the countless vile hangers-on he encountered when he ascended to the position of deputy commander.
“Is it still difficult for you to accept him, Mr. Calla?”

“That’s...” The man trailed off, then begrudgingly admitted, “No, it’s not.” That was the honest truth, not a lie. Though he may have said ‘barbaric’ at first, that was only because the first impression the man had left on Calla had been very strong. “That man... is smart.”
The paladin agreed. “Yes, he is.”
“Looking back, we were playing into his hands from the beginning. I thought he was looking down on us. But in reality, that wasn’t the case at all.”
“You’re right. I’m embarrassed to say so, but I did not think we would lose until the very end, either. I must still lack training.”
Calla completely agreed. If he hadn’t laughed the first time he heard the nickname “Blood Spirit’s Man” and instead investigated further, things might not have ended this way.
“The problem is I don’t know how the others will take it. Ah, where are Sir Kaislan and Ms. Akurava?”
“They are in another room. They were unconscious earlier but I don’t know about now. Their injuries were more severe than yours.”
“...It would be best to go see for myself.”
The two of them got up and headed to the other room. Apparently, the others had been healed by a priest, and all that was left was to wait for them to wake up.

As Calla sat by her bedside, Titana Akurava soon opened her eyes. “Judging by the look on your face... I’m guessing we lost?” Unlike Calla, she didn’t ask too many questions, nor did she seem to expect an answer. She remained silent for a short while, an unreadable look in her eyes, before asking where the others were.
“I see you’re awake as well, Ms. Akurava,” said Jun. “How are you feeling?”
“I’m fine, fortunately. But... where is that man?”
“Well, I’m not sure about that, either. Perhaps he is giving us time to wake up and collect ourselves.”
“No way that man is that considerate.” At Akurava’s blunt statement, the gloomy atmosphere in the room lifted a little.
As their conversation continued, Kaislan soon woke up. “...That man! What happened to that man?!”
It was time to discuss what had happened in earnest.
“I see. We lost...” he murmured, his voice full of deep regret, and anger for no apparent reason. Kaislan the knight balled up his fists. “I cannot accept this.”
“That we lost?” asked Akurava.
“No, I am not foolish enough to deny that. However, us losing the battle and him winning the position of commander are two different matters.”
“Oh my, then are you saying you plan to break a promise made in front of the marquess?”

When the marquess was brought up Kaislan flinched slightly, but it wasn’t enough to break him of his stubbornness. “Then are you all going to willingly accept this? We’re talking about thirty people! Not just thirty people, but the top talents who carry the future of this city on their backs! You want to entrust their lives to someone who has nothing but power? For the sake of the greater good, I cannot sit by and watch that happen!”

Calla found himself gripping his throbbing head at that sharp shout. He didn’t realize this man was such a lost cause. “Mr. Kaislan, are you claiming you’re better than Mr. Schuitz in areas other than power?”
“I’m not just talking about myself here; I’m talking about all of us. Aren’t we better than someone who just appeared out of nowhere?”
“I see. Then can you explain why you think that way?”

“I don’t understand why you’re giving me that look. Didn’t we all just have an in-depth conversation about what an ideal commander was earlier? Aside from that man, not a single one of us spoke of power.”
“That’s true.”
“Aren’t we all in agreement? When it comes to leadership, power is the last quality that should be taken into account.”
Even Calla thought the knight was right about that. A commander wielded a great sword—they didn’t necessarily have to be a master swordsman.
But as long as we have the marquess as our witness, we can’t change the terms now. It’s best to call it here.
Calla finished his political calculations and opened his mouth. “I don’t think that man is inferior to us in terms of his other qualities.”
“...What?”

“This might sound strange coming from one of the people who lost, but he wasn’t significantly stronger than the four of us.” Calla truly thought this. If they had time to establish some teamwork beforehand and had fought that man seriously from the start, the battle would have had a different outcome.
But none of that matters now.

“We lost the only match we had, and he won. Do you know what made the biggest difference?” The knight just glared at him mulishly and did not reply. Calla didn’t bother waiting for him before continuing. “We lacked information. As soon as I saw him fight, I knew. He already knew too much about us. What essences we have, and even what equipment we use.”
“So are you saying he fits the description of the ideal commander you were talking about? Wake up! He only obtained that information from the marquess!”
“Isn’t that the scariest part? While we didn’t know anything until we got here, the marquess was different.”

Kaislan didn’t waste any more words on Calla. “Okay, I see what you mean. You’re just going to watch that man stand above us. Are the rest of you of the same opinion?” Kaislan’s eyes then shifted to the ninth-floor adventurer, Titana Akurava.
Unfortunately, he didn’t get the supporting fire he was hoping for. “Even if you look at me like that, that won’t change the fact that I’m of a similar opinion.”
“...Why? Is it because you are afraid of the marquess?”
“I wouldn’t say that’s not a contributing factor at all. But, there’s an even bigger reason than that.”
“A bigger reason?”

“Yes. I don’t think that man will be worse at it than us.” Kaislan narrowed his eyes, clearly lost. Akurava shrugged her shoulders. “What impressed me was not who’s backing him but how innately meticulous he is.”
“Meticulousness...?” Kaislan huffed like he found that ridiculous.
“Yes. Meticulousness. For example, what was he like during lunch? He already knew everything about us but acted like he didn’t, and he made a big show of being arrogant to get us to take his bait.”

That wasn’t all, either. He did the same during the battle, hiding various essences and abilities until the end and only pulling them out when they would give him the best bang for his buck. Take Calla, for example. When he got knocked out at the start, that had put more of a burden on the three who remained.
“And this... can’t exactly be attributed to good judgment, but his senses, at least during the battle, were almost godlike.”
“...He was a natural,” said Calla.

Though that man had looked like he was burning himself out, by the time they came to their senses, they were the ones actually engulfed in flames. And after all that, the man had smiled in contentment.
“At the time, I thought his battle strategy was based solely on instinct, but now that I’m looking back on it, he made decisions based on thoroughly rational deductions,” said Jun.
“If that’s true, that truly is amazing. To think giving up an eye and taking down Sir Kaislan with a hammer was a rational decision.”
“Since that’s when our battle line started to collapse, he benefitted a lot from doing so.”
As Calla and the paladin exchanged words of praise, Kaislan gritted his teeth. He couldn’t understand them at all.
What’s wrong with these people? They should know how important the position of Commander is, yet they’re still acting like this?
He was almost starting to wonder whether they made a secret pact with the marquess while he was unconscious. But despite his concerns, the conversation continued.
“To be honest... the thing I find the most praiseworthy is his determination to achieve his goals.”
Ha, now it’s resolve?

Kaislan snorted but the paladin continued without acknowledging him at all. “As Mr. Calla said, he was not significantly stronger than the four of us. But despite that, he provoked us to the point of arrogance.”

His bones were shattered countless times, his intestines cooked, and he even ended up with an arrow embedded in one eye, but he never went down. He let his skin burn to cross through walls of fire and spat out blood after biting his tongue. Even when his shoulder blades caved in and his arm was left hanging, he kept swinging his hammer.
“Is there anyone else here who could go that far?”
“I’m embarrassed to say that I’ve never seen anyone fight in such a state without any hesitation.”

Even a man like that couldn’t have enjoyed that slog. It must have been painful. All of them would have understood if he had chosen to give up. That was how obvious it was that he had reached his limit.

“A normal person is bound to start faltering in a situation like that. ‘Yes, this is enough. I’ve done enough.’ They’ll start making compromises and excuses to convince themselves that they tried their best.” But that man didn’t do that. How was that possible? As a follower of god, the paladin found the answer to be faith. “He has a faith that he will never fall. And because he has such a strong faith in himself, he was able to avoid breaking down, and overcame the trials in front of him to achieve victory.”
“I guess that means you also agree that that man should become commander, Sir Jun,” Kaislan grumbled, his tone almost scornful.
The paladin responded without a hint of hesitation. “Yes. If I must follow anyone here, he is the one I trust the most. Even at a time when anyone else would give in, that man will stand strong.”
It seemed the paladin had properly fallen for the man. Calla, meanwhile, was worried about the marquess, and Akurava didn’t seem to want to renege on their agreement with Schuitz out of pride.

“Just admit it,” said Akurava. “We lost. He never complained even when one of us healed and returned to the front lines after going down. At the time, we were too busy fighting to think about it, but that’s really no different from cheating.”
“The reason he kept quiet was probably that he figured we’d need something like that to accept he won.”
As long as the other three agreed, there was nothing Kaislan could do anymore.
That’s a relief, Calla thought. If that man protested the outcome and requested a rematch, there’s no way a man like the marquess would take that lying down.
Crisis averted, Calla let out a sigh as he looked at Kaislan, whose lips were pursed. Of course, that didn’t mean there wasn’t still friction.

“Since you are all in agreement, I won’t speak on this anymore. Just know that this is a mistake. As I said before, only discipline and strong control can create a strong group. I refuse to believe he has that level of control.” His stubborn attitude made it impossible for him to acknowledge his opponent to the bitter end. It was clear he’d use whatever excuse he could to challenge the status quo if the opportunity arose. If that happened to be inside the labyrinth, it could turn into a big problem.
Knock, knock.
They heard a knock from outside the door.

“Ah, I guess everyone is awake.” The man entered the room without even waiting for permission, and Calla rid himself of even the slightest hint of anxiety. “Since you’re my subordinates now, I’ll speak casually,” the man muttered, even though he never used honorifics with them in the first place. His eyes shifted to the side and he tilted his head. “Knight, why are you blinking like that? Did that hit you took earlier mess up your head?”

It was truly an incredible thing. Calla didn’t know when exactly it happened, but the knight who had just been shouting about the importance of control at the top of his lungs had all of a sudden lowered his eyes.
“Answer me. I’m asking you.”
“N-No...” It looked like a very natural thing to do.

chapters.title: Chapter 396: Expedition (1)
paragraphs: After giving the knight a long, stony look, I let the tense lines of my face relax. “I guess that was my bad.”
The knight seemed relieved to see me soften, yet he also seemed to be wondering what I was talking about.
“Ah, I’m saying I’m glad there doesn’t seem to be anything wrong with your head.”

Then, patting the knight on the shoulder, I checked to see if the other three had any objections to me being the leader. I didn’t think they had the guts to break a promise made in front of the marquess, but you never knew. I figured follow-up treatment might be necessary.
“No.”
“Me neither. Those were the terms of our agreement, after all.”
“Since things panned out like this, please feel free to call on me any time you need help.”

Surprisingly, the other three didn’t express any dissent. I guessed they were cooler than I thought. Since this matter involved the interests of their backers, I figured there would be at least one greedy schmuck who refused to back down. Well, that was good since it meant less work for me.
“I’m glad there are no complaints. Then I’ll be leaving now.”
“Sorry? Leaving?” When I tried to turn around, the four looked at me with obvious bafflement. Now that the leader was decided, I guessed they assumed I’d want to talk to them more.
“I’m hungry. See you later.” On that note, I exited the room, leaving behind four people with dumbfounded expressions on their faces.

This was a way of laying the groundwork. I wasn’t going to live as Riehen Schuitz forever, right? All would be revealed in three months. So I figured I should show them this side of me in advance to make things easier for them later. No wonder he acted like such a barbarian. So that’s why that was.
“You’re here?” My next destination was the marquess’s office. I figured I owed him a report before I left. “How did it go?”
“Nothing much happened.”
“Are you saying everyone readily accepted it?”
“It’s not like they had any other option.”
“That... is true. Well, if you need my help with anything, let me know any time.”
“How reassuring.” Then that should be the end of my progress report—
“Ah, and one more thing. Now that the commander has been selected, we will be holding an inauguration ceremony soon.”
“Inauguration ceremony?”
“All of you should have an occasion to get acquainted with each other before entering the labyrinth. The backers of this project will also want to meet with you.”
“Then when will that be?”
“I will let you know the date as soon as it’s finalized.”

It was kind of funny. There were less than ten days until we entered the labyrinth. We were going to go from meeting at an inauguration ceremony straight to going into the labyrinth together? This was almost lightning speed.
What’s their reason for pushing things forward in such a hurry?
