The question occurred to me but it was very easy to guess the answer.
He probably wanted to make sure this all happened after the 15th. Since that is the easiest time for information to be passed on to people on Noark’s side.

The higher-ups must have wanted to minimize the spread of information as much as possible. In fact, when I asked some questions about the ceremony, the marquess answered that it would be unfeasible for us to hold a grand event with hundreds of people for security reasons.
“Anyway, I get the inauguration ceremony, but what about the two people who are going to be on my team? Will I only meet them at the ceremony?”
“Of course not. If you want, I can make arrangements for you to meet tomorrow.”
“Then can you send them to my house tomorrow?”
“Of course.” The marquess readily nodded in response to my request.
Then I guess we’ve said everything we needed to say?
While I was looking for a way to end the conversation, the marquess suddenly broached a new topic. “I want to ask you something.”
“What is it?”
“When you made that bet during lunch...” The marquess paused to take a breath before continuing. “Were you confident you could win against the four of them?”
“Why are you only wondering that now?”

“I’ve been wondering from the beginning. You must have seen the files I prepared on them, so you would have known their personal information in detail. That’s why when you first made that bet, I thought it was because you were confident you could win.”
“So?”
“But as I watched, I realized that wasn’t the case. Do you know how many close calls you had?”

I thought I had a rough idea of what he really wanted to ask. Why would I risk making a bet like that if I was only going to win by a hair? I decided to give an honest answer. “Marquess, it’s as you suspect.”

The decisive factor behind my victory was stage seven of the Immortality Imprint. Restorative Power, the main stat it gave you, was a special stat that increased regeneration speed. Without it, I wouldn’t have been able to last as long as I did with just my base healing factor. More importantly, I might’ve run out of MP earlier, as Restorative Power also applied to MP regeneration. In other words, thanks to my new tattoos, my MP recovery from Soul Dive also went up. With all that in mind, I figured fighting was worth a shot.
“Victory wasn’t guaranteed.”
Nevertheless, I wasn’t 100 percent confident that I’d win. That was how fights were. There were way too many cases of lucky shots sending people to early graves to even mention.
“I just don’t understand. How could you do something so bold when you weren’t sure?”
I shrugged and turned to leave the room. “I don’t know—why do you think?”
Why are you asking such an obvious question? I picked the fight because even if I lost, I never planned to roll over and admit defeat in the first place.
You should never let other people know your Plan B.
Around noon the next day, our two new party members visited our home on the marquess’s invitation.
“You must be Riehen Schuitz. It’s nice to meet you. I am Riard Ashed, a rank-three wizard from the Lengman School.” He was a friendly-looking man in his mid-thirties who was rather tall for a wizard.
“You’re young. I’m Guold Aldidi.” The magician in his sixties looked to be in much better shape than I expected.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Riehen Schuitz.”
“...Did you used to be a soldier, by any chance?”
“No, why do you ask?”
“Because talking informally seems so natural to you.”
Was this his way of asking me to respect my elders? The question came to mind but I didn’t dwell on it. Whatever the answer, it didn’t matter much.

“Aldidi, if you came here thinking this was going to be an ordinary team of adventurers, it’s not too late to back out. First off, we will be working as members of the military for a while and for this to work, informal top-down communication is key.” It was always important to set the tone in the first meeting.

When I firmly put my foot down, Guold Aldidi, or Old Didi for short, gracefully backed off. “Haha, of course not. I was just curious. I don’t have any complaints about being informal with each other. I’ve been working as an adventurer into old age—do you think I’ve never worked under someone younger than me? I’m used to it.”
“Then I’m glad. Wizard...”
“Riard Ashed. You can call me by my first or last name, whichever is more convenient.”
“Then I’ll go with Ashed. Ashed, do you think the same way as this old man?”
“Of course. Not only is being treated according to your abilities the norm in the Magic Tower... but this team is also an opportunity I don’t want to miss out on.”
“An opportunity, huh?”
“Even just participating in this expedition promises many rewards. But I heard from Lord Tercerion that... you have become the commander of this unit, is that right?”
Ah, did the marquess tell him that already?
“It seems we’ve joined the right team. Being under the team of the commander will give us more opportunities to achieve great things. Isn’t that right, Mr. Aldidi?” Ashed asked with a kind smile.
Old Didi cleared his throat and expressed his agreement. “Ahem-hem, you could say that...”
I studied the two of them.
Not bad, in terms of first impressions.

First, Wizard Ashed. Though we hadn’t exchanged many words, he seemed competent. Well, I was sure there wasn’t a wizard out there who wasn’t, but intelligence and social skills were two different things.
The old man doesn’t seem stubborn, either, despite his age.
Of course, Ashed deserved some credit for that as well. Calling the expedition an opportunity, he showed his lofty side to make the old man realize he wasn’t top dog here.
“Then Mr. Schuitz, would you please introduce the two people behind you?” Ashed cautiously asked, and I glanced at Erwen and Amelia in a gesture for them to briefly introduce themselves.
“I’m Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.”
“Emily Raines.”
While they exclaimed “Blood Spirit!” during Erwen’s introduction, they tilted their head at Amelia’s name.
I’m sure they’re curious who she is, but it’s good they didn’t ask any unnecessary questions. Hmm, it looks like our luck of the draw was pretty good?
“Now, come in.” Once introductions were over, I brought the two men into the house. We prepared plenty of food for everyone to eat together. “Oh, I forgot to ask this. Have you eaten?”
“When I heard you invited us to your home, I didn’t eat just in case.”
“It’s better to deal with important matters on an empty stomach.”
So, they both hadn’t eaten. “We didn’t prepare much, but eat as much as you want. If you have anything you want to discuss, we can talk while we eat.”
Once everyone was seated, we ate and chatted.
“I don’t know who did the cooking but the food tastes great.”
“Hehe, I prepared it. Thank you.”
“No, thank you.”
“Oh my, it’s nothing special. Haha.”

Ashed and Erwen’s conversation served to break the ice, but I just kept my mouth shut and ate my food. That was because all the food was takeout. I supposed it wasn’t a lie that she prepared it, though, since she went to buy it in the morning and set it out on the plates herself.
If it were Missha, she would’ve been in a tizzy trying to cook everything herself since morning...

I was suddenly hit with the memory of Missha, but I didn’t mean to belittle Erwen’s hard work. I was always one for buying takeout because I didn’t want to make anyone go to all that trouble. Missha had always been stubborn, though.
I wonder if she’s doing all right...
Although we were only going to be working together for a short while, I felt weird about the idea of bringing on new party members.
“Schuitz, what are you thinking so hard about?” Amelia poked me in the side.
“Nothing. You were talking about your career, right?”
Tuning back in, I actively participated in the conversation and started scrutinizing my new teammates. They weren’t too different from what I heard from the marquess.
“The last time I entered the labyrinth was seven years ago. After the clan I was a part of for five years broke up, I devoted myself to research at the Magic Tower.”
“Why did you change your mind now?”
“The same reason why adventurers work so hard to climb the floors.”
For a better life, for more opportunities—rather than strange personal conviction, this was a far more believable explanation. “What can you do in the labyrinth?”

“For a wizard, what’s important is not what they can do, but what they can’t.” Ashed grinned at my question and gave me some insight into his bag of tricks. “I can only cast a small number of curse spells rank five and above. As for support spells, I can go up to rank four. Other than that, aside from magic unique to other schools, you can assume I know everything. Ah, I’m also very interested in the labyrinth, so you could say my other strength is I have significant knowledge about items and how to collect them.”
Ashed was a kind of all-rounder. Although his curse and support magic were lacking, that wasn’t a glaring flaw.
“If you asked what I’m confident in, I would say attack magic.”
“Your attribute?”
“I wouldn’t say I have a particular preference.”
Wow, he’s even balanced when it comes to different attributes?
“Does the Lengman School study combat magic?”
“No. They specialize in curse-type spells.”
What? This guy’s weird, then. He went to study curses but is the best at attacking? Sounds like there’s a backstory there...
“Then if you don’t have any more questions, I’d like to hear about Mr. Aldidi.” Just as I was contemplating asking for his story, Ashed naturally passed the baton off to Old Didi.
...Did he do that on purpose?
Even if he did, it didn’t bother me or anything. I wasn’t going to ask since it sounded like a personal story in the first place.
“I am a healer.”

Healers were a subcategory of magicians. Those who could mimic the healing power of priests became healers. Those who could replace a wizard’s firepower were called special ability users, or benders. If they used poison, they were poison benders, and if they used fire, they were fire benders. If their main specialty was doping people up on buffs, they were a support sorcerer. If they did the opposite, they were debuff sorcerers. These were the rough categories. The higher you climbed the ranks as an adventurer, the more detailed and extensive this classification system became. In fact, if I were to submit my resume to the guild, I would have to write Guardian instead of Barbarian Warrior.

“A healer... we have a good balance.” Ashed seemed pleased about Old Didi’s job, as he kept nodding his head. After all, Erwen was famous for her archery and since Amelia wore leather clothes and carried a dagger even at home, it was obvious what her role was. As for me, the marquess would have filled him in.
“I’ve acquired mostly healing abilities but I also have two support-type spells under my belt.”
Put simply, he also had a buff-type supporting skill. Old Didi filled us in on the essences he possessed and how they could be used, after which it was our turn.

Of course, since we were not magicians and understanding our every ability wasn’t essential for the team, we didn’t need to go into detail about our essences. Each person’s role, what they could do, and mentioning Amelia’s aura and Self-Replication and Erwen’s Spirit of Darkness as key features should be enough.
“Then I think we’ve learned most of what we can learn through conversation. What do you want us to do next?”
“If possible, I want us to meet every day to establish teamwork.”
“Okay, is there a training ground you usually go to?”
“There is, but it went bankrupt not long ago and disappeared.”
“Then I’ll find us a spot at a place I know. Ah, in case I need to contact you all in the future, will everyone tell me their address?”
“Here.”

Was this what it felt like to have a competent butler? Ashed took care of the trivial details that were necessary for coordinating team activities so that I wouldn’t have to worry about them, and thanks to that, we were able to gather at the training grounds every day. Time passed...
“Schuitz, you have a message from the marquess.”
...And the day of the inauguration ceremony finally came.
Just how do these bastards get anything done?
There were three days left until we entered the labyrinth.

chapters.title: Chapter 397: Expedition (2)
paragraphs: The inauguration ceremony was held at an empty mansion in the royal capital. Apparently, it was a building some count once used as a villa but put up for sale because he urgently needed the money. Since the building didn’t require any particular repairs, it could host a banquet without issue. Just the thirty members of our new unit and their patrons were invited for a quiet ceremony.
It really went fast.
It took about thirty minutes for the marquess and other patrons to take the podium one by one and offer words of encouragement and support.

“Since everyone else already talked about saving the country and becoming heroes, I’ll keep this short. Let’s kill a lot and earn a lot.” The last speech by the team leader (me) lasted about ten seconds. With that, the formal event ended, and we moved on to the banquet part.

The prime minister, Duke Kealunus, an alliance of small-time and medium-time nobles, the three churches, the Alminus Company, and the Adventurers’ Guild—although the banquet was full of all kinds of influential figures and their supporters, you could argue the party itself was lacking for an event with so many big names in attendance. The food was plentiful but cold because it had been prepared in advance. There wasn’t even a band to play music, servants to fill drinks, or crowds of spectators to watch the proceedings—things that were the norm for banquets. But not one person was displeased with this. Everyone knew this wasn’t a place to get drunk on wine, laugh, talk, or shake their bodies.
“Nice to meet you, Mr. Schuitz.”
“I heard you fought those four. How did you win?”
“‘Fought those four?’ What’s all that about?”
“Ah, you’re a member of Sir Kaislan’s team, right? Didn’t Sir Kaislan tell you? About what happened the other day.”
“It’s been a while, Blood Spirit.”
I was just sitting there quietly, but numerous members of our expedition came over to my seat to say hello first.
Whew, is this the life of a powerful man?
“Nice to meet you. I’m the leader of this mission, Riehen Schuitz. What’s your name?”
“Ventis Gerod. I hope we’ll do good work together.”

Instead of turning away those who came forward, I greeted them one by one and introduced myself to familiarize myself with their faces. I was going to be responsible for them from now on. I should at least know their names.

I had been greeting people for quite a while when a woman with a familiar face approached me. “I never thought I’d see the name Riehen Schuitz at this inauguration ceremony. Nice to meet you. Versyl Gowland.”
Wow, I never thought I’d see you here, either.
“Riehen Schuitz.”
“Was my introduction enough? I’m—”
“I know. The deputy commander of Clan Larer?”

The first time I met this woman was the day the first floor’s Crystal Cave was turned into a war zone. The teleport to take everyone to the safe zone was fifteen slots short, and this woman had essentially flipped a coin to pick who to leave behind. Among the unlucky few was our team.
We almost died trying to make it through Noark’s forces with fifteen people.

“I’m flattered you recognized me, but it seems your news is a bit outdated. I’m no longer deputy commander.” Versyl flashed a pained smile, her tone self-deprecating. “I guess I’ve been sleeping too long. By the time I woke up, my position was gone.”
“Ah... I heard you were caught up in that explosion.”
“Yes. I was asleep for over a year after that.”
“Still, I’m glad you woke up.”
“Yes... if it weren’t for the Representative, I would still be in that state...”
“Representative” was the nickname of the Tovera Church’s high priest. Apparently, no other priest could compete when it came to recovery-type divine spells.
But something about the way she worded that feels off.
To be exact, her complexion and the look on her face weren’t so great. She didn’t seem like someone who had recently been on the receiving end of an act of kindness.
“Versyl Gowland, what team are you a part of?”
“Team Four.”
“Team Four...” That was Paladin Jun’s team. I had been able to learn the identities of four of its members before the inauguration ceremony, and all of them were members of a religious faction.
But a random wizard is there too? She must be in their debt, then.

I could roughly deduce the situation this woman was in, and she seemed to notice the exact moment I figured it out. She looked at me with an unreadable look in her eyes, nodding. “...You are different from how you seem at first glance.”
“How do I seem?”
“Don’t be offended. Anyone who heard that speech earlier would have gotten the same impression I did.”
Hmph, when it came to speeches, the shorter the better. This was a universal truth I reached while listening to my principal’s lectures in middle school.
Erwen jumped into our conversation from the sidelines. “How long are you going to talk to him?”
“Blood Spirit...”
“It’s been a while. The last time we saw each other was when you abandoned us, right?”
“...I regret what happened back then. Truly.”

“As you should. The end result of you abandoning us was that, after all.” Her sharp tone suggested she still harbored a grudge. Versyl glanced my way, bowed, and excused herself. “Did I do a good job?” Erwen smiled bashfully like she had done all that for me. I wasn’t sure what to say to that so I just laughed it off.

“Um... nice to meet you. I’m Pyke Neldine.” As soon as my conversation with Versyl was over, the team members wandering around nearby gathered around me again, and I introduced myself and held short conversations with each of them.
“You guys relax here a bit.”
“Where are you going?”
“There are some people I haven’t greeted yet.”
“They didn’t come up to you first, so why bother?”
“What are you so angry about? If they don’t come to me, I can just go to them.”
“It just... feels like you’re admitting defeat, then, Mister.”
Erwen looked dissatisfied but my decision remained unchanged. What would pride do for me? I had to do what I had to do and move on.
“You are...”
“Nice to meet you. Riehen Schuitz.”
“...McKelly Rayothers.”

I went up to the people who didn’t approach me first and held brief conversations. There had only been twenty people in the file the marquess gave me. That wasn’t because there was a lack of information on them but because not all the members of our squadron had been finalized at the time.
What the—why is this guy here?
As I was walking around the banquet hall greeting people I hadn’t met yet, a man caught my eye. “...Sven Parav.” The deputy commander of the Church of Reatlas’s Second Order of Paladins.
The paladin, who was sipping his drink in a corner with a somewhat uncomfortable look on his face, seemed surprised to see me. “Do you know me?”

Of course I did. Not only had I seen him several times during my visits to the church as Bjorn Yandel, but thanks to certain events, I was convinced he was Goblin. “Don’t underestimate the marquess’s sources.”
“...I didn’t mean to underestimate him.”
“Then I’m glad.”
“If you want to sit here, I can move out of—”
“Let’s talk for a moment.”
“Sorry...?”
“Do you not want to?”
“No, that’s not it...”
Are you sure? The look on your face definitely says you don’t want to. Hmm, to be more exact, he looks extremely nervous.
“Did Jun tell you about me?”
“If you mean the bet... yes, he did.” Ah, no wonder he looked nervous. It was because he heard about all that. “But why...?”
“What do you mean why? We’ll be entering the labyrinth together soon, but we haven’t even said hello yet. I hope to do good work with you inside.”
“Yes, I hope so as well.”
After a brief conversation with Sven Parav, I turned around, feeling a complicated mix of emotions.
Ha, this is funny...
Sven Parav was a goblin. In other words, there was a high chance he’d be leaking information from our squadron like a broken faucet.
Those religious bastards had to pick him?

Man, how could I keep his mouth shut? Maybe if I hinted that I was suspicious he was an evil spirit and made a point of monitoring him on the 15th of every month, I could force him to log out right away.
...I’ll revisit this later.

Afterward, I continued to walk around the banquet hall and spoke to all the members I hadn’t been able to learn anything about in advance. Sven Parav was admittedly a negative but there were still positives. I especially couldn’t emphasize this enough: No Hans, No Problem. The absence of a Hans was a very encouraging sign.

The banquet went on until dinner finished, after which the inauguration ceremony came to an official end. We, however, remained in the mansion. Since the existence of our team was classified and most of its members were celebrities, it was decided we would stay here and work on our teamwork until the day the labyrinth opened.
Teamwork, my ass.

What difference would it make for the thirty of us to work together for just two days? Each individual party would be entering the labyrinth separately, and it would take weeks for us to all meet up on the sixth floor. It wouldn’t be a surprise if everyone forgot everything we went over today in the meantime.

“I think our best option is to leave battles to each party’s discretion and have everyone help each other out in emergencies.” This was the conclusion we reached during our leadership meeting, after judging that forcing thirty people to operate as one unit would only be a recipe for disaster.
“Still, shouldn’t we devise a formation just in case?”

We decided to come up with some ways of banding together in case of an emergency: wizards with wizards, healers with healers. It’d be easy to teach them their positions after we placed a mark on their chests to differentiate them.
“Warriors wearing shield marks will stand on the perimeter, and warriors with sword marks will stand right behind them.”
“And the healers?”

“They’ll be in the very center, of course. They have to survive to be able to treat the injured. Long-rangers wearing bow marks will stand in formation to protect the healers and any healer-type special ability users.”
Yeah, that should be good enough for a two-day training session, especially since everyone already had experience working in group settings.
“Sir Schuitz, are you listening?”
“...Of course.”
Jeez, I only rested my chin in my hand for a minute.

As commander, I really only had two commands anyway: “Fall out,” to get the parties to split up and operate separately, and “Gather together,” to bring the squadron together into one large group. Well, given time, my commands would expand to “Assault,” “Concentrated Bombardment,” “Shield Wall,” etcetera. But for now, it was only the two, so there was nothing to memorize.
“Then let’s leave it at that for now and decide on the rest of the formation when we reconvene on the sixth floor. We can train in our spare time there. I mean, if you think that’s a good idea.”
“Fine,” I said. “Let’s do that.”

The structure of the meeting was one in which the others discussed things amongst themselves and asked for my permission at the very end. Once it was over, James Calla, a former deputy commander of a clan, worked hard to instill the Fall Out and Gather Together commands into our squadron.
Two more days passed. It was time to enter the labyrinth.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
The Crystal Cave was filled with brilliant light. All team members moved swiftly while wearing robes that covered their entire bodies. It was best to avoid being seen as much as possible.
Dash, dash.
Although we had a wizard and special ability user on the team who weren’t all that physically powerful, we made decent time. That was because they each had their own means of transportation.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-four mutation spell Fox Lantern.]
The wizard turned into a ball of light and followed us in the air.
[Guold Aldidi has used Lukberta’s Pigeon Boots.]
The special ability user covered this with an item.
Amelia was visibly fascinated as she watched the old man keep pace with her. “Is that a Numbers Item?”
“Lukberta’s Pigeon Boots is a Numbered Item in the 3000s. Though it’s limited to non-combat use... It’s very useful in the labyrinth for someone like me.”
“If you keep going this fast, won’t you run out of Soul Power?”

“Haha, you underestimate special ability users.” It was essential for special ability users to maximize their Soul Power in the cultivation stage, so they had higher MP than most. “Don’t worry. I normally only use this up to the third floor. The fifth floor is too narrow and the sixth... since I’m on a boat anyway, there’s not much use for it.”
Was it because he was a high-level adventurer? He seemed prepared for anything.
With this, we should be able to speedrun.
“Emily, increase your speed.” I gave a new order and was promptly seized by a truly incredible feeling.
Whooom!
The light sphere rocketed forward like a comet.
Whip!
Old Didi floated slightly above the ground and sped forward in a lean.
“...Schuitz, why are you going farther and farther back?”
“Just in case... an enemy... comes from... behind...”
Ugh, I’m so out of breath. To think I’d be the slowest one out of the five of us.

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Expedition (3)
paragraphs: In simple terms, the speedrun ended up being a failure. When we arrived at our destination, the portal connecting to the second floor was already open and we weren’t able to obtain the Portal Opening achievement. And I really thought it might work this time.
“How much slower were we than the previous team?”
“About ten minutes.”
What, that long?
The time we took would have been considered a speedrun in the game. It felt like we were playing in the big leagues now.
But if it’s ten minutes... it should be possible to bridge that gap as long as I just speed up.

Once our speedrunning capabilities became more reliable, it was very important to get on track and start accumulating free XP with each expedition. That was probably why that dragon tribe woman had asked to work individually.
I wonder if her speedrun was a success.

The last member of our team was the dragonian Ravien. That woman had only participated in the inauguration ceremony and left without enjoying the banquet, and she even entered the labyrinth separately. Her logic was that traveling alone was several times faster for her and we were going to meet up with her on the sixth floor anyway.
Ugh, honestly, if it weren’t for the marquess...

Her thought process clearly indicated that something was wrong with her head. I felt the need to fix it for her but unfortunately failed due to the intervention of the marquess. Apparently, he’d made her some personal promise separate from our mission so I needed to respect her autonomy. He then said he wouldn’t stop me from trying to rein her in but asked me to refrain from using force. Put simply, he was asking me not to beat her up.
What is she, some princess?

Of course, I wasn’t going to give up on getting control just because the most convenient way to do so wasn’t available to me. Correcting her attitude would make things easier in the future too. So I’d do it—whatever it took.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]
[You have entered the Tower of Heavens on the fourth floor.]

Anyway, even without our wayward party member, the quest itself wasn’t difficult so we proceeded as planned without any issues. We headed straight up to the fourth floor, making good time. Starting in the Tower, where avoiding battle was no longer possible, we improved our understanding of each other by practicing our teamwork. As a result, we naturally ended up having a lot of conversations.
“Hmm, so it’s true the three of them were living in the same house...”

There was some personal chit-chat like this in the mix but no one said anything that crossed the line. For example, whether mine and Erwen’s relationship was as the rumors said, or anything about my relationship to the marquess, how people like us could have flown under the radar all this time, etcetera. Old Didi showed curiosity about these things from time to time but was cut off by the wizard Ashed before he could voice his questions out loud.
“But by any chance—”
“Ms. Raines, I’ve been wondering something after observing a few of your battles: can your clones also use Auras?”
“No, it’s impossible.”
“Really? From what I’ve seen, the clones can use your other abilities. Since it is such a rare essence, this is sparking my passion for learning.”
At first, I thought it was a coincidence, but now I was certain. This wizard stepped forward every time Old Didi tried to bring up an uncomfortable topic.
Such a smart man.

I didn’t know why, maybe because he was a wizard and a man, but Riard Ashed kept reminding me of Dwalkie. Of course, unlike him, Ashed spoke in a soft voice, said everything he wanted to say, and had much better social skills. His temperament was different as well. He was quick-witted and much more mature. But because of that...
“What is it, Mr. Schuitz?”
“I wasn’t looking.”
As I watched him, a thought suddenly came to mind. Riol Warb Dwalkie... if that guy had gotten a chance to grow up, over time, would I have felt the same way about him?
[You have entered the Great Sea on the sixth floor.]

It was Day Eighteen of our trip into the labyrinth. Except for the Tower of Heavens, we were able to speed through the rest of the floors to arrive at Laemia, the Island of Beginnings, which was very quiet. That was to be expected. While our team ran to get here, how many other people could be here at this point in the expedition? There was a military scouting team made up of quick-footed people, some elites from large clans awaiting the arrival of the rest of their members, and other teams from our expedition who only greeted us with a look, mindful of the eyes around us.
Wow, there were two teams here before us.
I expected this from the dwarf woman’s team since it was made up of veteran adventurers, but I didn’t expect Paladin Jun to be faster than us too.
“...Ah, there she is.”

Anyway, it was easy to find people since it wasn’t busy. I quickly spotted the dragonian Ravien, the woman who was added to our team as part of my deal with the prime minister, and a business associate whose full name I hadn’t even heard yet.
“You guys rest here for a moment.” After telling my team to wait, I approached the woman, who sat on a chair in the shade, staring blankly at the shore.
When I approached, Ravien spoke without even turning her head. “Day eighteen... you got here earlier than I expected.”
What the—? Does she have eyes on the back of her head?
“I’m sure I said the rendezvous point is on the eastern region of the island?”
“The departure date is the twentieth, anyway. Looks like the other teams who got here early are also just resting nearby.”
Well, that was true. I didn’t actually intend to scold her about where she set up shop. “When did you arrive?”
“Two days ago.”
“Two days ago...?”

That meant she had arrived on the sixteenth day. She traveled from the first to the sixth floor in almost fifteen days. Aside from being displeased with having such an individualistic team member, I had to admit...
“...I see why you wanted to travel alone.”

At that speed, she must have succeeded in speedrunning all the floors. From this woman’s perspective, it made sense not to enter the labyrinth with us. If she had, she would’ve had to give up a whopping twelve free EXP.
This will make it harder to persuade her.
My troubles compounded. The thought of forcing her to travel with us the whole time just because we were a team made me feel like a boomer.
“Anyway, get up.”
“Why?”
“We didn’t get to talk in the city, since you were so busy.”
“All right.”

I didn’t know what I was going to say if she said she was going to stay here until the 20th. But surprisingly, she readily accepted my request and headed to the eastern part of the island where the rendezvous point was located with me.
“Nice to see you again. This is our first time meeting since the inauguration ceremony, right?” said Ashed.
“I’m sorry about that. There was a situation within my tribe. I’ll try to make time in the city as much as possible from now on.”
“I’m grateful. Shall we call you Ms. Ravien from now on?”
“Sure. Address me however you feel comfortable, Mr. Ashed.”
The conversation went more smoothly than I expected.
“May I call you Miss Ravien?” Knowing dragonians aged differently than humans, Old Didi’s tone was cautious as he asked this.
Ravien nodded coolly. “What about you two? How should I address you?” She turned to Amelia and Erwen.
“Emily, Raines, whatever you want.”
“I’ll go with Ms. Raines.”
“I’m Tersia.”
When Erwen drew a line in the sand, her tone sharp, Ravien gave her a strange look and smiled. “All right, Ms. Tersia.”
Okay, now that we’ve figured out names... But why are we only figuring out names on the sixth floor? Can this really be considered a team?
Even with those questions in mind, I got straight to the point. “We worked on our teamwork in the city, and learned more about each other on the way up here.”
“I know what you’re getting at. You want to know more about me, too, right?”
“We have to know who we’re trusting to watch our backs.”
“Okay.”

Ravien pulled out the sword on her hip and demonstrated some of her skills, explaining what role she could play in battle. It seemed like she was omitting a few things, but this was a common practice for those in occupations besides wizard, priest, and special ability user, so that wasn’t anything new.
“So where should I stand when we’re on the move?”
“The rear.”
“And during battle?”
“Emily will take my left rear guard and you’ll take my right rear guard.”
“It’s standard.”
“We don’t know enough about each other to do anything complicated.”
I guessed she noticed an edge in my tone because Ravien chuckled.
“Are you going to keep doing that?” I asked.
“I didn’t say anything wrong, did I?”
Well, let’s end our battle of wills here.

After that, the wizard and special ability user also went through the process of helping Ravien understand their roles. It didn’t take long but it was frustrating to watch. Why do something twice when it could’ve just been done once in the city? Perhaps individualism was a synonym for inefficiency.
“You’re here.”
“We can’t be fooling around on the beach when the commander is over here, can we?”
Before long, Akurava’s and the paladin’s teams, which were resting on the coast, joined us at the rendezvous point on the eastern part of the island. More time passed, and then...
“Team Three has just arrived.”

Because the eastern part of the island was at a slightly higher elevation, we could see the next one of our squadron’s teams enter the sixth floor in real time. It was the team led by James Calla, the deputy commander of the Sawtooth Clan.
“They look like a mess.”
“I guess they overdid themselves trying to go faster.”

I understood their thought process. The gathering date was the 20th but they probably thought being the last team to arrive would be seen as indicative of their skill level. This, too, was a kind of battle of wills.
I didn’t realize I was running an army in the Tang Dynasty.

Healthy competition within the group? This was a good leadership tool but it would only have a positive effect after we established unity. With the way things were now, competing with each other would only lead to in-fighting.
How can I unite them as one?
As I spent my time thinking about things all leaders were fated to contemplate, the day came to an end. Team Five, the team led by Kaislan the Knight, arrived around then.
“Damn it...!” Although he had arrived two days ahead of schedule, he clenched his fists in anger when he realized he was still last.
Huh, did this guy’s control snap again?
“What are you doing over there? Come sit here, quickly.”
“...O-Okay.” When I gestured to him, he jumped and came closer. Getting angry like that only left you with wrinkles.
Tap, tap.

I patted Kaislan on the shoulder to encourage him, then used him to support my weight as I got up. “I know we have two more days before we’re officially scheduled to leave, but since everyone is already here, I see no reason to waste time.”
“Oh wow, are we finally learning what our missions will be now?”
“Ah, wouldn’t it be best to leave the others out of this discussion?”
“It’s fine, it’s not anything we need to hide from each other. Besides, it’s not like they can leak the information to anyone else, considering everyone is constantly together.”

At my words, the other members of our squadron, who were exchanging awkward looks nearby, came closer to the circle. Since they had my permission, they must have figured they could listen with more confidence.

“Now, tell us. What on earth is our mission that it’s been kept so secret? As the leader, you’re the only one who knows the mission, right?” I could see Akurava’s curious eyes through the flickering bonfire.
I really wish dwarves wouldn’t sit on chairs. Look, I can’t even see her face properly because of the bonfire. The fire’s not even that big. Anyway, that’s not important.

“Ahem-hem.” Clearing my throat for the sake of my dignity as a commander, I said, “Everyone must have wondered this exact thing before. If Noark is coming to the Dark Continent through portals, where are those portals opening?”
“Yes. If they’ve been given a particular starting point like the Crystal Cave, they’re surely using that as a home base.”
“Did the palace finally figure out where it is?”
“Yes.” When I brought up the top-secret information the marquess gave me, the group began to murmur. This was no time to be surprised yet, though. “Our mission is to hit their stronghold.”
In military terms, we were a mobile strike force, targeting and destroying the enemy’s key troops or bases while our main unit was distracting them on the battlefield.
“...Um, there’s one thing I don’t understand. If that is our mission, why did we set such a tight schedule?”
“Could it be that we’re meant to get through the Canyon of Vengeful Spirits on our own?”
“That’s ridiculous! Unless we join the main unit and travel together, we cannot cross that canyon with a single ship!”
Huh, I’m not even done talking yet.

I supposed another similarity to the Tang Dynasty’s military was that the local news sprung to life every time I spoke a single word. Before the misunderstanding could get any worse, I clarified. “We won’t be crossing through the Canyon of Vengeful Spirits.”
“What? You said we’re attacking their home base on the Dark Continent, so what do you—”
“This is your final warning. Stop cutting me off.”
Whew, now it’s nice and quiet.
In the peaceful silence, I explained our mission in detail. “The Canyon of Vengeful Spirits isn’t the only path to the Dark Continent.”
“Ah! Could it be...?”
Yes, I guessed they’d realized it now. Why did they think we gathered on the eastern part of the island in the first place?
“We’re heading to Ice Rock in the east.”

Goblin Forest, Den of Beasts, Rock Desert, the Land of the Dead—just as the four separate areas that made up the second floor all connected to Pilgrim’s Path on the third, the Dark Continent wasn’t the only area on the seventh.
“After that, we’ll enter the Dark Continent via the eighth floor and attack them from behind when their guard is down.”
The mission was like a piece of cake... that was frozen solid. It was hard to swallow and at times made your teeth numb.
“If anyone doesn’t understand, speak up.”
No answer.
“I’m glad there don’t seem to be any cowards here.”
Though there were going to be many times when we questioned whether we really had to eat the cake like this, nevertheless, the end result would be sweet.

chapters.title: Chapter 399: Expedition (4)
paragraphs: It was Day Eighteen of our quest.
Shaaaaaaaaa!

A medium-sized warship carrying thirty passengers sailed across the current. For reference, this was a warship supplied by the palace, and the owner’s seal had been temporarily transferred to me, the leader of this expedition. While all our team members went to their assigned cabins to unpack their luggage, Amelia approached the sailor-slash-navigator at the helm.
“Excuse me.”
“Oh... Ms. Raines. What can I help you with?”
“How long does it take to reach Ice Rock?”
“I’m anticipating it’ll take about twelve days.”
“Is Ice Rock closer than the Dark Continent, then? It took us fifteen days to reach it on the warship we took.”
“The distance itself is similar but the ship is different. This Class Seven warship we’re on may be a medium-sized ship, but it has excellent speed.”
“I don’t understand how it can be all that superior if it’s only a three-day difference.”
“The far Eastern Coast isn’t a regular old sea.”
“Hmm, I see.” Amelia, who had recently shown a keen interest in sailing, nodded in understanding. “You seem to know a lot about warships, is that right?”
“Haha, I have to. I’ve sailed warships half my life.” The sole sailor in our expedition was a member of Team Five who was originally a member of the royal military.
Hmm, when you take that into account, it makes sense that Kaislan’s team arrived on the sixth floor last. He just did a speedrun with a navigator.
“Can you tell me more about how warships work?”
“I’m sorry, information on warships cannot be leaked.”
“I see...”
“...But while we’re on the same boat, I can’t stop you from taking a peek at what I’m doing.”
“I won’t get in your way.” While Amelia expressed her gratitude to the navigator for his kindness, I went inside the ship to a room located deep in the center.
“Oh, everyone’s here.”
“It was an order from our commander, after all. You told us to gather here once we were done settling in.”

Inside the room, which was designed to host leadership meetings, each team’s leader was already waiting for me. “Has anyone been to Ice Rock?” I asked, getting down to business right away. The only ones who raised their hands were Akurava and James Calla. “No one except these two?”
“It’s not a region people often visit.”
“Yeah. Aside from a few expeditions to earn achievements as a clan, we rarely went to Ice Rock.”
True, it wasn’t an environment conducive to hunting. I was sure not even half of the all-star adventurers on this boat had experienced Ice Rock firsthand.
“I see.” I nodded and then launched into a brief explanation of the tasks I had for them. “James Calla, you’ll be in charge of drilling the crew while we sail.”
“What kind of drills?”
“Formations and things like that. We only had a few days together in the city. Since everyone is experienced, they should all be able to measure up in live combat with even a little practice.”
“All right.”

First, it was critical to increase the number of commands I could employ as the leader of this squadron. Otherwise, we might end up running into unexpected issues in unexpected situations. We didn’t have a proper formation for flights or retreats yet.
“Since our destination is Ice Rock, I’ll prioritize things that will be useful there.”

“I’m glad you’ve saved me the work of explaining.” Since he was from a large clan familiar with all types of formations, he’d be able to take care of it. “Titana Akurava, you will be in charge of managing supplies as soon as move-in is complete.”
“Does that mean you’re giving me full jurisdiction over the process?”
“Yes. I’ll leave everything to you from now on.”

I entrusted the management of expedition-related consumables and equipment to Akurava. If Jun, a member of a religious faction, or Kaislan, an inflexible soldier, took that position, there was sure to be backlash. On the other hand, Akurava was a legendary adventurer who was older and had years of experience, so she should be able to smooth over the occasional complaint from the crew.
“Melend Kaislan.” Next was the knight. Perhaps because the two before him had been given missions, he gulped in anticipation.
He can be kind of cute sometimes...
“You are in charge of the cohesion of our unit. I need you to be the first to rush in and mediate disputes among team members, and if something goes wrong, you need to resolve it.”
“So you want me to serve as your right-hand man. Okay. I’ll do that.”
Uh, how did you get a right-hand man from that? I guess soldiers have a different way of thinking.
“I guess I’m the last up.” Once Kaislan was given his role, Paladin Jun smiled at me. “How can I help you?”
After our fight that day, he’d become strangely friendly toward me. Sometimes I even found myself wondering, Is this guy...? but I didn’t voice my suspicions aloud.
“I heard adventurers often reach out to priests during and after expeditions.”
“Yes, I’ve heard something similar. People accumulate mental fatigue in the labyrinth, after all.”
“Hear the group out and keep your ears as open as possible. And if there is anything I need to know, tell me. That is your objective.”
“The other races will not come to me.”
Yeah, I figured. The Three Churches were human religions.

“That alone is enough.” But humans made up more than half of our squadron and were even distributed rather evenly across each team. Just listening to them would be of great help in understanding public opinion.
“Then are those all of your instructions?” When I nodded at Akurava, she cautiously asked if she could ask me a question.
“Question? Go ahead.”
“Why are you handing so much power over to us? We’re not even your deputies.”
I couldn’t help chuckling at that.
I thought you were going to ask something big.
There was no reason to even think this through so I answered immediately. “Because it’s most efficient that way.” After all, we were already in the same boat.

Passing through windless waters, we crossed Grand Rock, the reef-filled region in the far east, and finally arrived at our destination. In total, the voyage took twelve days and seven hours. We were able to follow the schedule the navigator laid out to a tee thanks to the fact that we took the shortest route possible without stopping at any islands along the way.
A warship is definitely nice.

Aside from being able to cross through the Windless Zone in an instant, the way the ship sailed forward on the eastern coast—the way we were able to trust in its durability as we drove it straight through the reef—was very impressive. The icebreaking device attached to the front also looked very sturdy.
Kakakak! Kakakakakak!
Although this place wasn’t classified as a special area like the Ice Sea, the ship plowed forward, smashing floating pieces of ice along the way.
“We’re really here...”

The crew gathered on the deck and exhaled as they watched the continent gradually grow closer. Whether it was leather, sheet metal, or cloth, everyone was wearing thick clothes over their equipment. These were also supplies given to us by the palace.
Hmm, I’m someone who does better with heat than cold...
Like the other crew members, I finished mentally preparing myself as well.
“Hold on tight! The ship is now entering the portal!” the navigator shouted at the top of his lungs right as the blue light of the portal enveloped our ship.
[You have entered Ice Rock on the seventh floor.]
Well, even without the portal’s light making it clear that we were moving someplace else, it was immediately, physically obvious to everyone when we arrived in Ice Rock.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Ice Rock has activated. Your Cold Resistance decreases by -100.]

As our resistance stats dropped drastically, the chill began to creep in. For now, that was the only change we could feel, but those damned status effects would surely have been applied to us as well by now. They were what really made adventurers avoid Ice Rock.
[The status effect Frozen World is now active. All Space-type items have been disabled.]
Sub-space included, this status effect made even expandable backpacks useless. This short bit of code drove everyone who came up here up the wall.

“Now, now! Don’t just stand there, let’s unload our supplies first!” Akurava, who was in charge of supply management, oversaw the unloading of the supply boxes enchanted with preservation magic onto land. From now on, we would have to drag these things around. No, that wasn’t all. There was even a ridiculous added effect we’d have to contend with.
[The status effect Starvation is now active. The effects of any resources you consume are reduced by 3 times.]

Here, even if you ate the same food as usual, your stomach emptied three times faster. That was why you needed so many supplies. This was the biggest reason why most adventurers didn’t consider this place as a hunting ground. Even if you could withstand the cold, you couldn’t withstand the hunger. Because food was limited, the time you could be active here was as well.
With our supplies, we have one month. Of course, that’s assuming nothing goes wrong.
“Mister! They told me to tell you that we’re ready to leave.”

Anyway, with our crew members moving with a single-minded purpose, it didn’t take long to unload all of the supplies from the ship. The five sleds we had laid out on the frozen ground were soon loaded up with boxes.
“Then let’s head back quick.”
Once the supplies were unloaded, I and the navigator split off from the group and took the ship back to the sixth floor. Transferring to a small boat, we reverse-summoned the warship.
[You have entered Ice Rock on the seventh floor.]
After that, we took the smaller boat back to our previous location. The process was a little cumbersome but ultimately necessary. After all, we couldn’t just leave the warship here, could we?
“What are you going to do with this boat?”
What do you think? Of course we’re going to leave it here.
Just in case, we hid it in a secluded area so it wouldn’t drift away. And with that, all preparations for our mission were complete.
“Each team in formation!” The members of our squadron, who all seemed well-trained now, moved in perfect formation. “Depart!”
At my command, the first march of our expedition began.

The squadron traveled in a wide, flat formation, and its arrangement was simple: us, Team One, in the front; Teams Three and Five on our left and right; Team Four in the rear; and Team Two, which was in charge of supplies, following us in the center.
Boom, boom, boom!
Heavy thuds followed us.
“Mister, those are Ice Trolls, right?”

Dragging five sleds piled high with supply boxes, three Ice Trolls followed the march. They were the handiwork of the summoner on Akurava’s team. Without them, we would have had to pull the sleds ourselves.
“Halt!”
Just as we were marching east and about to leave the beginning portion of Ice Rock, Team One stopped. There was no need to explain why.
Dddddd.
What looked to be a cliff made of ice split in half and a giant monster emerged from the gaping hole.
“It’s a Stone Winter!” The rank-three monster Stone Winter was classified as super-large, and there were a whopping three of them in our path.
Booom!
Huh, this may be Ice Rock, but... Rank-three monsters crawling out from the woodwork right at the beginning?
“All troops prepare for battle!” I shouted.

The squadron mobilized fast and took up battle formation. Thankfully, no one froze in fear. With this much manpower, rank three should be a breeze, right? I led the battle with that thought in mind, but it didn’t take long for my expectations to get shattered.
[You have defeated a Stone Winter. EXP +7]
Even after the first battle ended, there were no cheers from the team—only a funeral-like silence.
“...Damage report,” I asked the leaders of each team, trying to swallow back the wretched feeling in the pit of my stomach. They cautiously answered.
“Four lightly injured and three seriously injured. We’re treating the seriously injured first.”

People getting hurt was fine. Yeah, that happened. This was our first time fighting together, after all. It was understandable that there’d be some growing pains considering we had been faced with three rank-three monsters at once. All they needed to do was get treated by a priest and they would be fine.
“And?”
“...One of the sleds is destroyed, and the supplies loaded on it were lost.”

That was the far bigger problem. A super-large monster had succeeded in getting to our supplies and unfortunately, the ground below the sled collapsed, unable to withstand the load. In an instant, one-fifth of our supplies were gone.
“What percentage of the load was food?”
“...All of it.”
The moment the words I least wanted to hear came out of Akurava’s mouth, a curse leapt from my throat. “God damn it.” This was only our first day in Ice Rock. “We’re speeding up from here.”
An arduous march began.

chapters.title: Chapter 400: Ice Rock (1)
paragraphs: A grand procession that moves through the eighth floor and heads toward the Dark Continent. According to our schedule, we were meant to cover Ice Rock in twenty days, and we brought about three months’ worth of food with us. Our abundant reserves weren’t an attempt at preparing for an emergency, though. Ice Rock was not a place that allowed such luxuries as extra supplies. The additional food was essential. Not only did each person consume three times more food in this place due to Starvation, but if you weren’t careful, the food could also end up spoiling because of this goddamned thing.
“Ice storm!”
A snowstorm blew through every thirty minutes at the earliest, or every six hours at the latest.
[Field Effect – Festering Chill has activated. The rate of decay of all affected targets accelerates.]
This blasted storm could make even frozen food spoil. There was only one way to stop it: prioritize food over people and protect it with magic. Of course, that had its own problems.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-four spacetime spell Obstruct.]
[McKelly Rayothers has cast the rank-four spacetime spell Obstruct.]
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-four spacetime spell Obstruct.]

The rank-four Obstruct spell consumed significant mana, and if you had to be prepared to use it at any time, the already large amount it consumed increased even more. Taking shifts even through the night was a given.
“Ashed, go rest by the sleds.”
“Sorry? But—”
“Don’t worry. I’ll call you if there’s an emergency.”
“...I’m sorry.”
What are you sorry for? The wizards from the other teams are already resting on a sled too.
[Field Effect – Festering Chill has been deactivated.]
After the snowstorm ended, we resumed our journey.
Crunch, crunch.
Every time I took a step, the snow came up to my ankles.
Growl.

I felt like I was going to starve to death, but since the food was being distributed as sparingly as possible, we couldn’t fill our stomachs all the way. The Obstruct magic had been doing a good job of preserving the food up to this point, but we didn’t know what would happen in the future. What if a blizzard blew in and we didn’t have enough mana to protect one of the sleds? Then things would get serious.
Well, it’s hard to say we’re in good condition right now, either.

It was our third day of exploring Ice Rock. Because everyone was exhausted, there were no silly jokes or even chatter from the crew. Everyone just walked at a steady pace, allocating their stamina to moving. The relaxed vibe of our voyage through the sixth floor was nowhere to be found, and a sharp tension settled over the squadron.
I have to take these guys to war with Noark later?
Some say morale is the most important thing in war, but in this state, it wasn’t clear whether we’d even accomplish our mission. The only positive was that we were quickly racking up EXP.
[You have defeated a Frozen Soul. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Contaminated Snow Spirit. EXP +6]
[You have defeated a Frost Guardian. EXP +7]
[You have defeated a Lich. EXP +6]
[You have defeated an Ice Giant. EXP +7]
[You have defeated a Frostfire Turtle...]

Since most of the monsters in Ice Rock were high-ranking, the XP accumulation was astonishing. There was still a long way to go, though. Even if I defeated all the monsters that spawned in Ice Rock, that wouldn’t get me to level eight.
Still, I should hunt as much as possible since this place is hard to get to.

I didn’t know how many more monsters I fought as I dragged this tired body across the tundra. As the day slowly wound down, we set up camp on the cliffside. We pitched the tents that were stored in the boxes loaded on the sleds, then put our sleeping bags inside.
[You have used an Insulating Stone.]
Then, with the addition of a few magical items, the tents became a cozy home.
“No one on our team is on night watch today, so rest up.”

There were a total of two night watches scheduled over the course of the entire expedition. Because our turn was tomorrow, we could rest easy today. This was possible because we had four priests. As long as those guys cast Destruction of Evil in turns, the monsters couldn’t even come close. There was also no way a team of plunderers was operating in this barren tundra. And even if they were, they wouldn’t have the courage to attack such a large group. At least not if they had brains in their skulls.
“Good night and see you tomorrow, Mister.”

The tents were made for three people, and divided into male tents and female tents. Adventurers may not differentiate between men and women, but there were still differences. I also felt more comfortable sleeping with men. Well, I did feel a bit cramped sleeping with the frail old man and wizard, though.
“Ashed, Aldidi. You guys sleep first.”
“Are you going on patrol?”
“I am the leader, after all.”

Leaving Old Didi and Ashed to go to bed after a hard day’s work, I walked around the campsite to check for any issues. Not long after the camp was set up, I could hear people start to snore. I was sure everyone must have been tired.
Looks like everything’s okay. I should go to sleep now. I turned toward my team’s tent and was met with a familiar face.
Crunch.
“Kaislan, you were awake?”
“I had something to say to you.”
“What is it?”
“Let’s walk for a minute as we talk.”
So we took a big lap around the edge of the campsite and talked.
“There’s been growing dissatisfaction among the squadron recently.”
Dissatisfaction, huh?
It was obvious what kind of dissatisfaction he was talking about. “I’m guessing they’re mostly cursing my name?”

Kaislan confirmed this, looking apologetic. “People don’t look for a reason to complain when they’re happy, but when they’re suffering, they always do.” His grumbling featured a deep, philosophical contemplation of human nature.
“Is that all?”
At my question, Kaislan shook his head. “If it were, I wouldn’t have come looking for you in the middle of the night.”
“So there’s something more.”
“...Someone in the squadron is spreading malicious rumors.”
“Rumors? What about?”
“That while everyone else’s food supply has been reduced, Team One is secretly prioritizing their own stomachs.”
“I see...” I unwittingly sighed in front of Kaislan. I couldn’t help it.
Jeez, we’re not a bunch of kids playing around here. This is supposed to be a collection of the kingdom’s best and brightest?
“Do you know who the source is?”
“It was Pyke Neldine.”
“A member of James Calla’s team.”
For reference, he was a warrior like me and had been one of the first to greet me at the banquet with a smile.
Jeez, such cowardly behavior for such a big man. Ah, is it because he’s so big and hungry that his brain isn’t functioning right?
“What are you going to do?”
“Well...”
When I trailed off, Kaislan recommended a few countermeasures. “If you’re going to discipline him, the best thing would be to do it through me.”
“Because that could make him resent me more?”
“If you want, I’ll make a big scene in front of the entire crew. So that he won’t even think of hating you.”
I never thought this guy would be such a loyal subordinate. I honestly felt kind of strange about it, but I made sure to hear what he said next.
“Or you can use Akurava. Supply management is her job and whatever the reason may be, this happened because she failed to carry out her duties properly.”
He wasn’t wrong. Whether or not the formation broke, Akurava should have protected the supplies.
“Everyone may be keeping quiet for now because she’s a renowned adventurer, but if someone brings it up, they’ll be eager to place the blame on her.”

I didn’t like this option either. Before I gave him my answer, I decided to ask Kaislan one question. “Kaislan, why are you willing to become a scapegoat to help me?” I asked this in case he had a hidden agenda.

Kaislan stared at me straight in the eyes and answered without hesitation. “Whether I like it or not, you’re the one leading this expedition now.” Huh. I didn’t expect that. “If we waver now, this mission will not succeed.”

To be honest, I thought he’d be the first to gun for my position if it was jeopardized. I guessed a soldier was a soldier after all. Kaislan was the type of person who prioritized the bigger picture over personal greed.
“Now, tell me. What will you do?”

He presented me with two options but when you looked closely, they were actually the same. Whether it was Akurava or this guy, in the end, in both cases I’d be making someone else public enemy number one. I was grateful for the advice he offered but my decision was already set in stone.
“I’m not going to do anything.”
Kaislan didn’t seem to understand. “If you keep quiet, the crew will hold you responsible every time something goes wrong,” he carefully pointed out.
Yeah, I’m sure. But, so what?
“It doesn’t matter what they say. That’s why they’re the crew, and I’m the captain.”
After all, it wasn’t like I expected to only enjoy the perks of being in charge and not the pitfalls.

On day eight after entering Ice Rock, we dragged our misfortune-ridden expedition forward in a white-knuckle grip and eventually reached the midway point. Now that we’d cleared the tundra, we were faced with a massive mountain made of ice. From now on, our objective was not to climb the mountain but rather to go below it.
“The entrance is here!” James Calla’s team was in charge of the search and soon discovered the path leading to the next area. We followed them and headed underground through a huge, icy cave.
Step, step.

The sound of boots echoed on the hard ground but the mood within the group wasn’t as somber as before. It had been like this back when I was going through training too. When you went through difficult times together, relationships were bound to get stronger.
“With ice as transparent as glass on all sides, it feels like we’re in some kind of dream.”
“Haha, I feel the same way.”

Of course, the mood was able to change in large part thanks to an improvement in the team’s stamina. Half of the crew were Ice Rock first-timers so there was a lot of trial and error in the beginning, but now, everyone had adjusted to it to some extent.
“Ugh, I’m starving. I see why everyone stays away from Ice Rock now.”

“I usually look at a portrait of my kid when times are tough but I can’t even do that here. If I knew in advance how this place worked, I would’ve taken it out of sub-space before getting off the ship.”
“Oh, you have kids? How old?”
It wasn’t just the atmosphere that had changed, either. The squadron, which had been out of step up to this point, now moved smoothly as one—just like now.
“Monsters from the side and front!”
“While Team One fights them from the front, Teams Two and Three will take out the enemies on the flanks!”
When orders were given, the crew carried them out quickly and without any fuss.
[You have defeated a Frozen Webter. EXP +5]
[You have defeated an Unmelting Cocoon. EXP +6]
[You have defeated a Frostfire Goblin. EXP +5]

Battles were much easier than before. We were finally fighting like a team of elites now. As our teamwork started to come together, everyone was able to demonstrate their usual fighting skill. And there was another positive.
“Schuitz, that man... the way he fights is mind-boggling.”

Since the adventuring industry respected the strong, people’s evaluations of me naturally began to improve as I took on the most dangerous jobs at the forefront of our team. The strange rumor that I was digging into the food supply in the middle of the night disappeared before I knew it. After all, one needed to prove themselves with actions, not words.
Crackkk...
My instincts sounded the alarm as a sudden creaking filled my ear. “Erwen, what was that sound just now?”
“I don’t know. I think it came from the back...”
From the back?
I hurriedly turned around and was soon able to see for myself what was going on.
Crackkk.
Perhaps unable to withstand our weight, cracks were beginning to spread across the floor like spider webs.
God damn it!
And they happened to be in the exact spot where the sled-pulling Trolls were. “The summons! Cancel the summons, now!” I bellowed.
The startled summoner reverse-summoned the Trolls as per my orders. But it was already too late.
Crackkk!
Another crack, this one even louder than the last.
“...Everyone, get out of the way!”
The adventurers in the vicinity of the cracks hurriedly fled, though a few courageous ones prioritized the supplies over their own safety.
“Supplies! Get the supplies!”
“We’re dead without them!”
“Move it!”
Being careful not to add more weight, the adventurers pulled on the sleds with all their might, but the floor collapsed faster than they could get clear.
Rummmble!
As if a sinkhole had formed, the ground sagged in and collapsed. One of the sleds and the two adventurers pushing it promptly plummeted into the abyss below.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-four support spell Float.]
Right at that moment, the two adventurers miraculously floated back upward. Their expressions went from despair to relief, and at the same moment, a sound rang out from below.
Splash!
Ha, there was water flowing under the ice? That means we can’t even rescue the sled.
Despite my misery, I quickly doled out orders. “Everyone, get as far away from the hole as possible! Just in case, don’t stick too close together!”

The frozen crew only got moving after I commanded them to. I carefully approached the edge and looked down. Using a light spell from a wizard, I was able to see the water flowing beneath us. There was no trace of the sled anywhere in sight.
“Akurava!”
“Y-Yes!”
“What proportion of the supplies on that sled was food?”
“A-About half!”
So, our already insufficient food supply was reduced yet again. When my jaw clenched, Akurava carefully studied me.
“Be quiet. I’m thinking.”
I just couldn’t understand it.
The ground collapsed the first time too, and now it’s happened again here?
No matter how I looked at it, it didn’t make any sense. Which was why...
“Akurava.”
“Yes. I’m listening.”
“Go around and ask every member of the crew right now whether any of them has ever changed their name, and if their original name happened to be Hans.”
I decided to run through the important checks first. Once they were done, it’d be easier to determine whether this was a series of unfortunate coincidences...
“Find out as soon as possible. This is important.”
...or if this was a man-made disaster caused by someone with malicious intent.

chapters.title: Chapter 401: Ice Rock (2)
paragraphs: The investigation found that two people had in fact changed their names. However, the names those two had used were Margery and Dick, which were a far cry from that cursed name. So, put simply, there was no (former) Hans among them.
But what is this feeling? It feels weird that there really wasn’t one...

It wasn’t that I wasn’t relieved there wasn’t a (former) Hans here, but with that relief came a certain amount of disappointment. If one existed, this series of events might really have been a mere coincidence. And if that wasn’t the case, we would have at least been able to narrow down our list of suspects significantly.
...No, wait.
“The Trolls.”
“Yes?”

“What are the names of the three Trolls you summoned?” I asked just in case but to no avail. Apparently, their names were Pippi, Poppy, and Yeppi in order from tallest to shortest. As a layman, I couldn’t understand the thought process behind that naming scheme.
Anyway, this confirms that someone deliberately caused this.

A coincidental fluke? Although that possibility couldn’t be completely ruled out, I didn’t really believe in such coincidences—not unless a Hans was somehow involved. Not to mention, the ground in Ice Rock collapsing wasn’t a common enough phenomenon to occur twice during a single expedition.
I have a guess too.
I carefully tucked the ring I’d just quickly put on and taken off again back into my pocket.
“Looks like that’s pretty much settled, then.”
“Yes.”
“What are our losses?”
“It’s hard to call anything about this lucky, but the proportion of food on that sled wasn’t that large.”
In that case, it was. The other items we brought on this expedition were also important for our survival but not as important as food.
“...What will you do now?”
“What is there to do? We’re going to keep moving.”

After confirming the extent of the damage, I got our squadron moving again. We were on a tight timeline. It wasn’t like the culprit was going to pop out of the woodwork if we killed more time here. I needed to think on my feet.
“How far can you send the Ice Trolls?”
“...A-Anywhere, as long as it’s within my line of sight!” the summoner immediately replied. It seemed she was worried she was going to be held responsible for this incident.
...Is it an act?
He was the most suspicious one. But I didn’t dig too deep, deciding now wasn’t the right time to do so.
“From now on, the remaining three sleds will travel in the front, center, and rear.”
To guard against any more unexpected complications, the sleds were divided up in a wider formation.
Step, step.

As we continued to march through the cave with its transparent ice walls, I continued to contemplate the situation. If someone among us really had destroyed our supplies, who could the culprit be? The problem was there were too many suspects. But in case there was a traitor, the first people I should consider were those who would have the most means and motive. For example, the leaders of each team.
“...Schuitz, I’m sorry. This was my fault. I should’ve divided up the sleds a long time ago.”
First, Titana Akurava. It went without saying that the woman was suspicious. She was in charge of managing the supplies, and every time something bad happened, she was always closest to the sleds.

“I’m sure Lady Akurava didn’t mean to do it on purpose, but this is the second time already,” said Kaislan, coming up next to me. “Whether you like it or not, everyone will look down on you if you don’t do something.” He was just as suspicious. I appreciated his kind advice and sacrificial mindset, but that was honestly even more suspicious to me. On top of that, he was the one who most coveted the position of commander.

“I think it’s hard to call this accident anyone’s fault. But... I believe holding someone accountable this time is one way to fix things.” James Calla, although the least suspicious, wasn’t without motive either. He had the lowest status of the four. His sponsors could easily bully him into doing what they wanted.
“...Do whatever you wish. That is your duty and right as the leader.” Last was Paladin Jun. He’d been strangely friendly toward me for a while, which I felt pretty awkward about.
“Mr. Schuitz, the squadron is extremely tired.”
The march lasted two hours longer than scheduled.
“Set up camp!”
While the rest of the group got our camp up and running, we held a leadership meeting.
The first matter of business was this. “The loss of potions and consumables for maintaining body temperature is also an issue, but the biggest problem is the loss of our tents and sleeping bags.”
“We’re already hungry. If we can’t sleep either, everyone’s discontent is sure to skyrocket.”
“We have to resolve this in a way that won’t raise any issues about unfairness. If some sleep well while others don’t, everyone will start to resent each other.”
The number of tents and sleeping bags left could not accommodate all thirty of us. The solution I decided to go with was simple.
“What will you do about this problem?”
“Increase the number of people on night watch in proportion to the shortage of beds.”
“...Night watch?”
Well, the number of sleeping bags didn’t measure up, right? But if the number of lookouts outside went up, the number of people who could sleep inside would go up too.
“...That’s too extreme.”
“We’ll burn through more energy this way.”
“Why don’t we take turns using the sleeping bags and tents?”
The team leaders expressed their concerns, but with my authority as the commander behind me, I ignored them and ratified the motion.
“Schuitz, this will only make the resentment toward you grow more.”

It wasn’t that I couldn’t understand what they were saying. This solution eliminated the problem rather than actually solving it. Tomorrow, the squadron would probably start calling me barbaric and criticize me for knowing nothing about strategy. People would say I didn’t have the qualities of a proper leader.
“I don’t care. Let everyone know. Each team can choose who will be on watch and the order they’ll take their shifts.”

Increasing the number of people on night watch was mandatory. If the number of those not sleeping went up, nighttime security would also go up, right? From now on, I had to be on guard against traitors within our squadron.
“Ravien,” I said, stopping the tired dragon tribe woman from heading into a tent.
“What’s the matter?” This woman was also a bit suspicious. I was curious about her exact relationship to the marquess too.
“I wondered if we could talk for a minute.”
“Is this because of what happened earlier today?”
“Yes, what are your thoughts?”
“Sounds like you think someone did it on purpose.”
“I have to leave all possibilities open.” Having worked together for a while, the conversation between us flowed much more naturally than before, but I unfortunately didn’t learn much from it.
“Even if you ask, I’m not sure. I don’t know anything about things like that.”
“I see...”
“Is that all?”

“Yes, you must be tired. Go sleep.” I debated talking some more but it didn’t seem anything would come out of it, so I let Ravien go. Then, heading behind a tent and away from prying eyes, I put on the ring from my pocket.
[You have equipped No. 6111: Destiny Seeker.]
In keeping with all the times I wore it over the past few days, a light appeared on the ring as soon as I put it on.
[The ring has detected your destiny.]
Said light was a very vivid red. I quickly took it off in case someone saw it.
God damn it.
It had been like this ever since we entered the seventh floor.

When it came to Numbers Items, there were some that couldn’t be used in the city, such as No. 399: Cage of Silence. Destiny Seeker was one of these items. So as soon as I entered the labyrinth, the first thing I did was put on this ring.
There was no red light then.

The same went for when I met up with the other members of our mission on the sixth floor, and even during the voyage through the eastern seas. But the moment we reached Ice Rock, the ring began to glow red.
Shaaaaaaa!
That meant there was something that would negatively impact me nearby, something that I had no chance of turning into a positive. At the time, a traitor didn’t even come to mind.
If their plan was to betray us only once we got to the seventh floor, it makes sense why the red light only came on now.

Throughout the journey, we’d been faced with disaster after disaster, and yet the light on the ring remained the same. That meant this wasn’t over yet, and more negative events remained on my horizon.
“Mister, how long are you going to sleep!”
When I opened my eyes, I could see Erwen above me. I’d reduced the number of insulation stones in each tent since our supply was now limited, so my body temperature had dropped overnight.
“Where are Old Didi and Ashed?”
“They’re up already and getting ready.”
“Why didn’t they wake me earlier?”
“I guess you looked tired.”
Hmm... I’m grateful, but it’s embarrassing as a warrior to have a wizard and special ability user, of all people, worried about my stamina.
“Do you want me to shave you?” Erwen asked with a grin as I sat up. I subconsciously touched my chin and felt a thick beard there. I didn’t particularly mind it, though.
“It’s fine. It’s not uncomfortable.” Rather, having a beard was beneficial in this climate. This was hair, too, so it should keep me warm, right?
“Oh... that’s too bad. What a shame. You’re much more handsome without a beard, Mister...”
I ignored Erwen’s whining and headed outside. The cold air enveloped my skin and filled my lungs. But by far the biggest problem was hunger.
Growwwl!
I noticed the emptiness in my stomach the moment I woke up.
“You’re awake.”
“First things first, let’s pack up the tent.”
Old Didi and Ashed, who were waiting outside, took down the tent we spent the night in and put it on the sled.
Chew, chew.

After gnawing on the piece of beef jerky I was provided for breakfast as slowly as possible, we resumed our journey. It was our tenth day in Ice Rock. The rest of our route was straightforward. Once we got through this maze-like cave connecting to the center of the region, a massive sinkhole hidden deep inside Ice Rock, otherwise known as the Glacier Eye, would appear. From then on, you could consider us halfway through this level, as we were headed to the end of Glacier Eye. Put simply, there was a portal underground that connected to the eighth floor.
Suddenly, I heard a commotion behind me. “An essence... there’s an essence!”
“Did it come from the Meran we just killed?”
“What? Wait, then it’s a rank-three essence!”
Actually, it wasn’t just a rank-three essence. It was a rare essence that could only be obtained here in Ice Rock.
“Everyone out of the way!”

First moving the crew out of the way, I sent a wizard over to store the essence in a test tube. She confirmed it was indeed a Meran’s essence. Was this good luck the universe’s way of making up for yesterday? Although these were high-ranking adventurers, everyone seemed to covet the rank-three essence with gleams in their eyes.

“Everyone, calm down. If anyone wants to purchase this essence later, we’ll grant you the right to do so after figuring out the average price of it in the test tube! And if there are any competitors, we will hold an auction!” Kaislan quickly infused some of his military discipline into the situation before things could escalate into a big uproar.

Some of the adventurers smacked their lips in disappointment but most weren’t too fussed about it and were genuinely happy. There had been a few essences during the expedition so far, but they were all lower-rank. Rank three had a different price tag. Of course, it wouldn’t be too much once it was split between thirty people, but money was money.
“...They said the loot from Noark is going to be distributed equally later too.”
“Plus, depending on our war achievements, we’ll get rewards from the palace. Can’t forget that.”
“Anyone who’s after that essence will have to accumulate a lot of achievements, though. If not, they won’t have the money for it.”
“Either way, we’ll be rewarded for our hard work.”
“That’s only if the mission is successful.”

Still, thanks to our first bit of good fortune in a while, the morale of the squadron was now quite high despite the incident yesterday. They were probably still cursing me out behind my back, of course, but if that helped them keep going, then oh well. As the leader of this expedition, there was no reason for me to be mad about that.
Every group needs a bad guy, right?
