Three more days passed like that. By some stroke of divine intervention, no more supplies or lives were lost in that time.
[The ring has detected your destiny.]

However, the color of the ring was still red. Because of that, I continued my investigation into the traitor, interrogating the summoner and looking into the other squad members’ alibis and potential motives over and over again as we pressed forward.
“It’s Glacier Eye!”
It was the thirteenth day of our trip through Ice Rock when we finally approached the second half of the seventh floor.
“What’s wrong? It’s still early—why are we preparing camp...?”
After giving the rest of the squad orders to set up camp, I called all the team leaders together. The reason was simple.
“There is a traitor among us.”
There was still time until night fell, but I thought I finally knew who the bastard was.

chapters.title: Chapter 402: Ice Rock (3)
paragraphs: “A traitor...?”
“What do you mean by that?”
The team leaders frowned at my abruptness, but it seemed they understood what I was getting at despite the lack of context.
James Calla carefully parted his lips. “...Is this about the lost supplies?”
I didn’t bother beating around the bush and confirmed it. “Yes, that’s right.”
“But that incident was—”
“A coincidence? Judging by your reaction as soon as I brought up the word ‘traitor,’ it looks like you suspected something about this was off as well.”
“That’s...” Calla quieted down. Apparently he had nothing to say to that.

As if to defend him, Akurava jumped in, making no secret of how displeased she was. “Thinking it to yourself and saying it aloud are two different things. Betrayal? That’s an extremely risky and dangerous allegation to make based on a hunch.”
Everything she said was correct. However, she was still missing the most important thing. “So, what’s your point?”
“Whichever one of us you suspect, you’ll have to have physical evidence capable of convincing us all.”
Whew, hitting me where it hurts. Does she think I suspect her? Well, managing the supplies was her job. That might be why she’s on the defensive right now.
Before this misunderstanding could go on any longer, I cut her off. “Don’t worry. I don’t suspect you guys.”
“Sorry? But earlier you said—”
“If I doubted you, I wouldn’t have called you here to talk to you about it.”
To be honest, I had considered all of them suspects at first but that wasn’t the case any longer. I found the culprit, and thankfully, he wasn’t one of our precious team leaders.
“Then... who do you suspect is the traitor?”
“Pyke Neldine.”
As soon as the words left my mouth, everyone’s eyes shifted to Calla.
“...That’s the warrior on your team, right?” asked Akurava.
“And also the guy who’s been running around gossiping about the commander whenever he gets the chance,” said Kaislan.
“Hmm... then his goal could be to sabotage the commander,” said Jun.
Entertaining the thought that I was telling the truth, the other three seemed to be putting the pieces together in their heads.
Calla, however, hurriedly defended his team. “W-Wait! Th-there must be some sort of misunderstanding here. Neldine might be rude, but—”

“Interesting. I wonder how well you must know him to be confident enough to say that. I’ve already finished investigating him. The Adventurers’ Guild recommended he join this operation, right? And you also met him for the first time then.”
“Yes, but...”
When Calla was left tongue-tied, Akurava stepped forward to help him. “Schuitz, I think we need to hear why you think he’s a traitor first. It would be best if you had evidence.”

Ugh, that damned evidence. I was getting sick of hearing about it, but I laid out the list of reasons I had compiled for why Pyke Neldine was a traitor in detail. When I was done, all the leaders accepted my suspicions as reasonable.
“That’s undoubtedly...”
“I can see you’re not just working off a hunch.”
“Although it’s still only a theory, these are definitely suspicious circumstances.”

Ah, except for that guy Calla, of course. “But you don’t have the most important thing: physical evidence. You won’t be able to convince anyone with a list of what might be coincidences! Some might even think you’re retaliating against someone who criticized you!” This was the first time this guy had ever raised his voice at me, but I wasn’t particularly offended by it. It was natural for a party leader to protect his teammates.
“Calm down. I know that, which was why I’m having a candid conversation with you guys.” I turned to Calla. “Answer this. Do you still think my doubts are unreasonable?”
“All right, that’s that, then.” Before he could say anything else, I clapped loudly to lift the mood. “Listen carefully. From now on, I’m going to need everyone’s help.”
“By help...”
“I’ll explain.” I shared the plan I made with the team leaders and got everyone to agree to it. “The sun should have set by now.”
It was night. Well, inside this cave, it was equally dark during the day as it was at night.
“Okay, that’s over and done with, then. You guys go get Pyke Neldine.”
Now that it was night, we should start the trial soon.

The ceiling and walls around us were frozen. A massive sinkhole was located in the center of the large cavity we were in, and the thirty members of our squadron were gathered in the camp built next to it.
“...God, I’m tired. What’s going on? Does anyone know?”
“Apparently there’s a traitor in the squadron.”
“...Traitor?”
“Yeah, apparently they made it so we lost all that food.”

It sounded like the team leaders had spread some of the information I told them to. Shock appeared on the faces of the gathered crew members. However, it didn’t take long for it to turn into curiosity.
“So, who’s the traitor?”
“I guess we’ll find out soon enough.”
“True. If they called everyone here at a time when we should be sleeping, that must be because they figured it out.”
The murmurs subsided and eyes began to settle on me. I completely ignored them all and kept my attention on one person in particular.
“Neldine, what’s wrong?” Pyke Neldine, the warrior from Calla’s team, was the one who had been constantly talking behind my back.
What a chicken.

When he first sat down, he flinched and averted his eyes, but now he made a point of keeping them on me without looking away. It was a common habit of liars. They always worried their opponent would assume they were hiding something if they averted their eyes.
“Now, now, everyone be quiet!” When I glanced at him, Kaislan stepped forward to capture the squad’s attention and a cold silence soon fell. It was the perfect atmosphere for a one-sided monologue.
“Pyke Neldine, come forward.” As soon as I spoke, everyone’s eyes flew to the back of the group.
“...What? It was that bastard?”
“Don’t call him a bastard. We don’t know anything for sure yet.”
Whispers could be heard all around.
“Aren’t you going to come over here?” I asked, and those standing around Neldine parted to clear the way for him.
Step, step.
The guy stopped in front of me, his head held high and a frown on his face. “...I’m here.”
“You’re very confident.”
“Why shouldn’t I be? Whatever, let’s hear it. Why did you single me out?” He glared at me with obvious belligerence in his eyes.
I somewhat expected that. I didn’t think for one second that setting the stage and scaring him would make him break down and confess. “Pyke Neldine.”
“I’m listening. Speak.”
“You are currently being accused of committing high treason.”
“...Treason?”
“Since you have caused serious damage to an expedition team established under the king’s orders, it would be safe to regard this crime as treason.”
“I don’t understand what’s going on here at all. What are you saying I did? If this is because I criticized you behind your back—”

“Pyke Neldine!” I wasn’t going to let him waste time so I cut him off and raised my voice. “You have destroyed the ice below us twice during this expedition, causing the loss of vital supplies! How do you plead?”
“Not guilty, obviously. Because it’s not true.”
“You’re going to keep denying it until the end?”

“Why are you all just standing there?! Is it reasonable for a man considered the leader of this operation to persecute his crew like this without any evidence?” Neldine shouted at his fellow squad members, swaying public opinion little by little.
“It... kind of is unreasonable.”
“Dragging someone onto the stand like that...”
“Come to think of it, this is the same guy who’s always cursing the commander, right?”
“Even if he calls him a traitor out of the blue unless there’s clear evidence...”
“Wasn’t it only a coincidence that the ice broke anyway?”
It was clear what this guy wanted: to make people think I was acting on a personal grudge.
“Schuitz, you just made a big mistake.” Neldine looked at me with confidence in his eyes. “If you want to frame and persecute me, shouldn’t you at least have evidence that everyone here can accept?”
“Evidence, huh?”

To be honest, this had been the biggest thorn in my side since I figured him out. I couldn’t get a confession out of him using torture, for obvious reasons. It wasn’t like I had Misplaced Trust on me, either. Lie-detection magic? Most adventurers who operated above the fifth floor were immune to verification spells, so how many of these people would magic like that even work on? I turned the issue over in my mind over and over again.
There’s no solution.
I eventually came to a conclusion. Unless I somehow tricked him into confessing using leading questions, there was only one other way.
“Looks like you don’t even have—”
[You have cast Giantization.]
My body instantly grew.
Grab.

In a flash, I threw a hand out and grabbed the guy’s neck. The entire squadron looked surprised by this, but no one immediately went to move. This was a habit adventurers had. Unless they already had a full grasp of the situation, most people took a wait-and-see approach.
“Keugh—what are you—!”
“Looks like you like making friends. But none of them are coming out of the woodwork to help you when you’re in trouble, huh?”
“S-Stop—!”
I haven’t even started yet.
Squeeze.
I gripped his neck tighter and obstructed his airways.
Smack! Smack!
He punched my arm as hard as he could. In my opinion, it was the most pointless escape attempt in the world.
Slide.
Ignoring his flailing, I bent my elbow and pulled him toward me.
“Neldine, did you know?”
“I don’t need any evidence. The commander has the authority to summarily execute any member of the squadron in an emergency.”
“K-K-Keugh!”
“I think this is an emergency.”
When I relaxed my hand even slightly, he didn’t miss the opportunity to let out a desperate shout. “You think... the outside world will believe—!”
“I’m sure they won’t believe it.”
Nobles weren’t stupid, and there were plenty of witnesses here. The moment I executed this guy, Tercerion’s rivals would all hold me responsible and force me to resign from my position.
“But that’s none of my business. I don’t care about those things.” With the sincere intention of killing him, I applied force to his windpipe.

Before long, Neldine’s veins began to protrude, and his entire head turned bright red as it filled up with blood. He no longer looked at me as he tried his best not to lose consciousness. He instead looked around for salvation.
“Um... is it okay to let this go on?”
“This is definitely an issue...”
“Sir Kaislan! Shouldn’t we stop him now?”

The crew expressed their concern, but the team leaders all kept their mouths shut and watched the situation unfold. That was the promise they made me, after all. And, was it because the team leaders stood back and silently showed their support for my decision? Before long, the concerns and insistence on stopping me disappeared.
“Ah... no...” The one who was hit the hardest by this realization was none other than the guy in front of me.
What do you mean ‘no’?
“Just die.” I let murderous intent from deep within my chest loose and poured all my strength into the hand around his neck.
Crack!
His neckbone gave way. His eyes rolled back to reveal the whites, and his eyeballs bulged.
“Damn it!”
An onlooker cursed, and another screamed. And then...
[Pyke Neldine has cast Overload.]
Unable to withstand the way his weight exponentially skyrocketed, my arm started to bend.
So, you finally used it.
Kwaaang!
As the angle changed, Neldine’s feet touched the ground.
Gasp...!

When I released his neck from my grip, he slumped down and took a deep, agonized breath. “Y-You piece of shit!” he shouted the moment he had enough air in his lungs. “W-What are you all doing?! We have... to stop... this savage!”
The crew began to stir at the cries of a man who came back from the dead, wondering if they should step in now.
“Why are you all just standing there?!” Neldine yelled, looking to the team leaders for help. But their faces were as cold as the ice around us.
“I hoped it wasn’t true.”
“He really has Overload. Something a warrior would have no reason to possess.”
“Let’s tie him up first. If he commits suicide, we won’t be able to hear the backstory.”
Today’s lesson: If you had a hunch, you could make the evidence you lacked.

chapters.title: Chapter 403: Ice Rock (4)
paragraphs: Once convinced that there was a traitor in our midst, I walked around investigating people. Of course, I didn’t act too much like a detective. I just wandered around casually during breaks or whenever we camped, striking up conversations. I had known that if I wasn’t careful, the traitor could run and hide.
“W-Wait! Please explain so that we can understand what’s going on too!” one of the onlooking members of our squad piped up when all the team leaders ran forward to seize Pyke Neldine.
“Explain, huh?”
No reason I can’t. It’ll help untangle this mess too.
“It was thanks to Milburn Naria that I first suspected Pyke Neldine.”
“Naria...”
“The summoner on Ms. Akurava’s team?”
I guessed the summoner was a shy one because she flinched and looked startled when everyone turned to look at her.
“Uhh, huh? B-Because of me?”
“Yes. When I went to ask you a few questions, you mentioned that the Trolls are getting tired rather quickly.”
“Ah, yes. I did say that, but...”
Hey, why are you being so hesitant? Are you worried you’ll end up under fire? If so, that’s a pointless concern. There’s no way I’d harm the person who contributed the most to solving this case.
“Anyway! That’s how it started.”

You could say that conversation became a catalyst that changed my entire thought process. If I previously assumed the ground had cracked thanks to magic or skill, my thoughts on the matter were different after that. I began focusing on the Trolls themselves rather than the ground.

“Thinking there was something wrong with the Trolls, I began to check to see if anyone had approached them before or after the incident.” I relayed my deductions in front of the crowd in what would henceforth be called Barbarian Detective Mode. “Up until then, I was suspicious of Akurava’s team and the wizards who were always waiting near the sleds to cast preservation spells. But after investigating, I found there was only one other person who approached the Trolls.” I pointed to the guy tied up with rope on the floor. “That was Pyke Neldine. This guy came up with all kinds of excuses to casually come into contact with the Trolls, and then magically stopped doing so after the cave in.”
Just then, the captured Pyke Neldine objected. “Th-that’s only circumstantial evidence! You’d do all this to someone just because of that?”
Haha, I’m not finished talking yet.
Paladin Jun tried to gag him but I stayed his hand with a look. No need to stop this guy when he was digging his own grave.
“Evidence! So you’re saying you have no evidence after all!”
Yeah, I didn’t have evidence. That’s why I had to use this annoying plan instead. Because people only want to believe things they see for themselves.
Without needing to even step forward, Akurava entered the fray. “The ability you used just now was Overload.”
“S-So! What about it?”
“Why have you been hiding that ability until now?”
“E-Everyone has their own trump card!”
“Hmm, that’s the trump card of a warrior like yourself? Rank-seven Overload?”

Neldine clammed up at Akurava’s acidic tone. In exchange for temporarily increasing the user’s weight and reducing their movement speed, Overload increased the damage of long-distance attack skills. It wasn’t a useful skill for a warrior. “D-Don’t obfuscate the point! Overload is an ability that only applies to the user!” As expected, he tried to find a way out of this.
“Yeah, wait, I’ve seen him use Overload before.”
“He’s right... it isn’t an ability you can use on other people.”
“What, then he’s innocent?”
The crew began to murmur again, deceived by his logic.
“This man is trying to persecute an innocent member of his team with faulty, ridiculous reasoning! Everyone, help me. If you don’t, you might be next!” Neldine shouted louder.
Thank you very much.

As a matter of fact, I was waiting for him to whip that out. The argument he just used to protect himself would end up snaring him instead. From now on, he wouldn’t be able to escape regardless of what he did. It was about time to draw the knife.
“Hey, can you lend me your knife?” I forcefully borrowed a knife from another member of the squadron and approached Neldine.
“W-What are you trying to do... S-Someone, help—”
“Everyone stay where you are!”
Choke!
Grabbing the bound man by the nape of his neck, I lifted him high so that everyone could see. The crew flinched, hesitating. They seemed to be debating whether they should band together and stop me.

Before they could come to a unanimous decision, I hurriedly shouted, “A skill that only applies to oneself? That’s definitely true for Overload. However!” This prick—who was he trying to fool? Did he know how many years I spent playing Dungeon and Stone? “It’s a different story if you have Endow, a conversion-type skill.”
At that moment, I dug the knife deep into Neldine’s forearm. No, to be more precise, his vein.
Drip.
Fresh blood flowed out. Because the cut I made was wide, there wasn’t enough of a pressure difference for the blood to gush out of him, but the amount of blood pouring from the wound was significant.
“He won’t last more than a few minutes with that kind of bleeding.”
“...T-Treatment... P-Priest!” The squad looked panicked at what seemed to be a sudden execution.
“Everyone stay put!”
“Please trust us and wait. I know what you’re thinking, but it’s okay.”

When the onlooking team leaders intervened, no one was willing to do anything hasty. One minute, two minutes, three minutes. Time crawled by, and some sharp-eyed members of our crew started to notice something was off.
“...Why isn’t he dying?”
“With that much bleeding, he’s still conscious?”
“Look at the blood pooled on the floor. Even if you took all the blood in his body out, you wouldn’t get that much...”
Perhaps this was to be expected, as adventurers were experts in hunting and killing. They noticed it much sooner than I thought.
Anyway, I think the situation should be ripe now...

“Ahem-hem.” I cleared my throat, which was hoarse from the cold. Then I shouted again so everyone could hear me. “What you’ve just seen in action is the passive ability of the rank-five monster Blood Roar—a skill called Blood Fountain!”
“...Blood Fountain?”
“What’s that?”
“I’ve read about it in a book before. It’s a passive ability that ensures its users never die from blood loss.”
“Wait, Blood Roar? Isn’t that one of the monsters with Endow?”
“That’s right. Those guys always team up with other demonic beasts, making that skill real tricky to go up against.”
“If that’s true...!”
The crew started to accept my logic without further persuasion. Soon, I tossed Neldine to the ground.
Boom.
Although it must have been quite a shock, he didn’t even groan. He probably realized he didn’t have time for that.
“W-Wait! I-It’s true I have the essence of a Blood Roar, but that’s not proof I have Endow.”
Jeez, you’re going to try the ‘proof’ angle even now?
I didn’t need to step forward this time either. “Then use one of Blood Roar’s other skills,” a voice called from the crowd.
“Th-that’s...”
“There are four. And I remember each was easy to identify with the naked eye.”
“I-I admit it! I actually do have Endow! But that doesn’t mean I betrayed you!”
“Then why did you deny it at first?”

“B-Because I was just afraid...! I was afraid of being labeled a traitor!” His final argument was made while trembling all over. The sight of Neldine rolling around on the floor tied up with rope and covered in blood was gruesome, but I wasn’t bothered. “W-Why are you all doing this?! Just because I have that skill doesn’t mean I’m the perpetrator!”

Basically, he was arguing for “innocent until proven guilty.” That would have worked if this were a modern trial. No, though Rafdonia may have been a bit barbaric, it also would have worked in a trial in the city, where laws existed.
“Pyke Neldine, how long are you going to play innocent?”
However, this was the labyrinth. And above all, adventurers weren’t fools.
“Why are you all hesitating? It’s obvious from his face and tone of voice that he’s lying.”
“True, it was strange that the ground collapsed twice. Nothing like that ever happened the last time I came here.”
At this point, everyone had accepted it.
“Yeah, so it was all because of this bastard?”
Pyke Neldine really was the traitor. And all of the hunger and discomfort they had suffered over the course of this journey was because of him.
Step, step.
Neldine, who had been crawling toward the crew and away from me, quickly turned around and came my way. “H-Hey! H-Help me! I will answer all your questions honestly!”
Okay, then let’s move on to the interrogation.
The rank-four adventurer Pyke Neldine had been an active member of all kinds of parties and groups, from small elite teams to large clans. So why did this guy betray our squadron?
No, to be precise...
“Who are you working for? Noark? Alminus Company? Or the Adventurers’ Guild?”
Now, now, say something. If you tell the truth, I’ll hit the happy button on top of your head with my hammer. Hmm?
“...I-I’m not working for anyone! I just didn’t like you.”
Haha, this guy still hasn’t smartened up.
“Jun.” When I called for him, Jun, who was on standby, mercilessly drove a long awl under Neldine’s fingernail.
“Arghhh!”
“A person who doesn’t die no matter how much they bleed, how rare.”
“Ugh—guh—ugh!”
“He may be able to withstand the bleeding, but if his organs are damaged, he won’t last. Be careful.”
“Don’t worry. The Lord wouldn’t want this man to die yet.”
This guy’s a paladin...?
Jun’s words were heartless and he was strangely skilled when it came to torture.
Who is this guy... did he have a job questioning heretics or something in the past?

It was a question worth asking. The fact that he abandoned his last name and that the name Jun wasn’t known throughout the city... That was all a bit suspicious, wasn’t it? Well, for now, I stood to benefit from his shady past.
“S-Stop...! I’ll tell you everything...!” The guy lasted over an hour before finally breaking and starting to confess.
“Who are you working for?”
“Illya Adnus...”
“The Guild Master of the Adventurers’ Guild.”
Mother—that big of a fish?
“Give it to me straight. Are you sure?”
“I-I’m sure! I haven’t met him in person, but it was his aide who commissioned me for this job!”
Ha, I don’t think he’s lying.
Leaving the matter of the Guild Master behind, I continued the interrogation. “So, what orders did you receive?”
Neldine hesitated.
“Jun?”
“I-I was ordered to ensure this quest fails!”
“What were the exact orders?”

I got a more detailed grasp of the situation. To summarize, it was like this: the Guild Master knew we were heading to Ice Rock, and he sent someone to tamper with the food and supplies to ensure the mission failed.
“I-I swear, I never intended to hurt anyone. If I knew that, I wouldn’t have agreed to it!”
“What are you saying? Two of our team members almost fell and died. If the wizard on my team didn’t step forward, they definitely would have.”
“Th-that’s...! I didn’t know they would go to such lengths to protect the supplies!” Neldine sounded like he was truly regretful.
Tsk, this doesn’t seem like a lie, either...
Punch!

Once I heard everything I needed to know, I drove my fist into his jaw to put him to sleep. Then, calling for the team leaders who were outside, I shared this information and talked it over with them.
“To think he was the traitor...”
“But if he’s working for the Guild Master, this is even bigger than we thought. Who knows what will happen once we get back to the city...?”
“It would’ve been better if he was working for Noark instead.”

Although they had agreed to offer me their help in finding the traitor, I guessed they had also secretly hoped I was wrong. Their expressions were all dark. But if there was one way in which their reactions differed from those of our ordinary team members, it was in that they were quicker to accept reality.
“Let’s discuss this first. Why do you think the Guild Master wanted the mission to fail?”
“The biggest motivation would be political. If this expedition fails, he’ll be able to place the blame on the marquess.”
“Perhaps the Adventurers’ Guild doesn’t want this war to lean in favor of Noark or the palace.”
“I wonder if that’s true, but... it’s not completely unrealistic. The people who are profiting from this war the most are adventurers, after all.”
“Jun, what about you? Any thoughts?”
The meeting wasn’t particularly fruitful. Many theories were tossed around, but there was no way for us to know which one was right yet.
“Um... what do you plan to do with Pyke Neldine?” James Calla asked carefully, and the other leaders threw in their two cents.
“He should be executed, of course. If someone who disturbed the peace remains alive and active, morale is bound to fall,” said Melend Kaislan.
“I disagree. If we return with him alive, we can use him as a way to corner the Guild Master. Jun, why are you being so quiet?” asked Titana Akurava.
“This matter is for Mr. Schuitz alone to decide,” said Paladin Jun.
Their eyes all fell on me.
Jeez, isn’t it obvious what I’m going to do?
“He will be executed.”
There’s still a long way to go and I don’t have the energy to bring a rat along with me.

The execution was held that night in front of all the members of our squadron. The punishment we went with was beheading, the most convenient method of execution in wartime. Hanging required lots of preparation and I could tell everyone was craving blood.
Slice!
The execution was over in literally a single swing. Some people still seemed angry, as they even went up to the corpse to spit on it. Well, adventurers hated traitors even more than plunderers.
“Where are you going...?”
“Patrol.”
Once the execution was over, I immediately headed to the outskirts of our camp.
[You have equipped No. 6111: Destiny Seeker.]
I put on the ring in my pocket again.
[The ring has detected your destiny.]
Now that the traitor was caught, I figured the light would turn off entirely. But as soon as I put it on, the ring emitted a soft glow.
Shaaa!
When I saw the color, I froze.
What the... why is it still red?

chapters.title: Chapter 404: Ice Rock (5)
paragraphs: When a red light appeared on the Traffic Light Ring, that could only mean one thing. Something that was likely to harm the wearer was nearby.
No way... is there another traitor?
That was the first thought that popped into my mind. He didn’t mention an accomplice during the interrogation but there may have been another spy I didn’t know about.
...Well, maybe the light isn’t about a traitor this time.

As I was responsible for the lives of multiple people, I decided to keep the worst-case scenario in mind and not get too caught up in it. After all, nothing was set in stone yet. I decided to just remain alert and keep a careful eye on my surroundings.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Glacier Eye is now active.]

The day after the execution, we packed up camp and entered the deep pit that seemed to lead into the inner core of the cave. It was a large, cylindrical structure with what looked like a spiral staircase on the wall that went round and round to the bottom, but as it was the final area before the eighth floor, its difficulty was quite high. The monsters that spawned here weren’t much stronger than the ones we’d already dealt with, but...
[Status effect – Whisper of Immortality is now active.]
If you died here, a curse resurrected you from the dead and made you kill your own team.
[All healing and recovery effects are now reversed.]
And even worse, this goddamned debuff was piled on too.
What am I supposed to do about reverse healing?

In this place, even the smallest of wounds didn’t heal. No, on the contrary, they continued to fester and worsen. The higher the character’s Natural Regeneration stat, the faster the effect. This place was practically a tank’s graveyard.
How many Shield Barbarians did I lose here again...? I don’t know, I don’t even want to think about it.
I couldn’t be sure, but the number must have been in the hundreds. Before I finally figured out the right strategy, anyway.
“This place is even spookier.”
“Erwen, cut the chitchat and stay alert. There will be demons here soon. As I said before—”
“Be careful not to get hurt as much as I can. Hehe, okay.”

Since the width of the staircase was so narrow, everyone divided into their teams and followed each other in a line. From here, the role of long-rangers became critical. Nearly 90 percent of the monsters that appeared here were capable of flight.
“It’s a Gargoyle...!” This wasn’t the rank-eight Gargoyle Statue I saw in the Bloody Citadel, but the real deal.
“A Death Knight too!”
Death Knights with spears in their hands rode in on the Gargoyles.
“Kihehehe!” Queen Banshees and various spirit-type undead monsters danced around in the air and showered us with debuffs.

Flight-type monsters, which pretty much served to neutralize close-range fighters, appeared from all over, but they were all intercepted and turned into bursts of light before they could even get near us.
[James Calla has cast Piercing Light.]
[Titana Akurava has used No. 1911: Fabler’s Broken Pocket Watch. Up to five minutes of cooldown time has disappeared.]
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Element Synthesis.]
Archers, special ability users, wizards, etcetera—not only were there plenty of long-rangers in our party comp, but with as many as four priests, there was no shortage of firepower.
[Niaro Campbell has cast Healing Wave.]
[Benjamin Orman has cast Emergency Regeneration.]
Divine spells dealt a whopping 1.5 times more damage to the undead. Of course, not all the monsters that appeared here were undead, but that wasn’t a huge issue. It dealt enough damage either way.
[All healing and recovery effects are reversed.]
You couldn’t heal your allies in this place anyway, so priests were basically long-range damagers here.
[You have defeated a Gargoyle. EXP +6]
[You have defeated a Ghost Horse. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a White Wyvern. EXP +6]
[You have defeated a Blue Flame Bird...]
The monsters were melted by the high healing factor and wide-range divine spells. The melee fighters focused on defense and dealt with the various monsters climbing the cliff.
“The battle is over!”
“We’ll keep moving after a ten-minute break!”

Any time a wave ended, we took a quick moment to regroup and then continued down. Overcoming wave after wave without a single casualty, we finally arrived at the first obstacle a while later. The narrow slope came to an end, and a wide, rocky ledge jutted out of the cliff.
“This is nuts. We have to avoid getting injured while fighting all those things?”
Hundreds of monsters filled the space. The interior of the cave in that cliff was a respawn point, so it couldn’t be helped.

“What are you grumbling about? We’ve been resting the whole trip down, so it’s our turn to work hard.” If the long-rangers took the more active role on the decline, it was time for the close-range damagers to throw their hats in the ring. “In formation!”
“Make sure to focus! Unless you want to ride out this journey with a rotting arm for the rest of the week!”
After taking up a line formation, the warriors moved to the front to set up a shield wall.
“Let’s go!”

We secured space by shoving away as many monsters as we could. After that, a melee broke out. While the warriors fended off the enemy from the front, the long-rangers bombarded them with firepower. Perhaps because we were overwhelmingly powerful, the battle itself was relatively easy.
“Damn it, my arm! Agh!”
Nevertheless, some ended up injured.

The total number of injured was four. Three of these four had sustained what could be classified as minor injuries. These were only scratches, unlikely to result in death. According to the plan, we’d reach the eighth floor in six days. Unless they sustained more injuries on top of that, they should be able to hold out until treatment was possible, even if the wounds rotted and festered. The problem was the one person who was seriously injured.
“A-Am I... g-going to die like this?” Rick Jugusta was the close-range fighter from James Calla’s team, which was already down a man thanks to Pyke Neldine’s removal.
“Of course not!” Calla shouted beside the writhing man, who was clutching the place where his bone peeked out from his thigh. “That’s not going to happen, don’t worry!”
Right, these two are old friends.
“Fiona! Please use a curse, quickly!”

Calla requested a curse from one of the wizards. The wizard seemed to wonder what he was thinking, but after he explained, she saw what his plan was. So did I. Was it because he was the deputy commander of a large clan? It seemed he knew the fundamentals of dealing with injuries here from his previous trip to Ice Rock.
[Fiona Amos has cast the rank-five curse spell Regeneration Prevention.]

It was a method I once used as well. If you could lower the injured person’s Natural Regeneration using a curse, you could at least stop the wound from getting worse. For a long while, I used this strategy to clear Ice Rock, blindly plowing through while trying to minimize injuries as much as possible. Until I figured out the real strategy, anyway.
As soon as the emergency patch job with curse magic was complete, Calla turned to me. “Schuitz! We have to turn the group around and head up immediately!”
His tone was urgent but I only shrugged. “Why?”
“W-Why? What do you mean? If we leave him like this, he’ll never make it to the eighth floor.”

I couldn’t help chuckling at his tenacity. Would he have acted like this if it was someone else who was hurt? I didn’t know, but I was sure he would’ve at least assessed the situation more calmly, just like Akurava over there.
“We already spent the whole day coming down. If we go up and down again, we’ll waste a total of two days,” said Akurava.
In other words, twenty-eight people would have to burn through two whole days to save a single person. Well, that in itself wouldn’t be an issue, but...
“Sir Calla, I’m sorry, but our food supply is only enough for the next five days. As it stands, we’ll already have to starve through the entirety of the final stretch.”

As Kaislan said, it wasn’t just time we would be sacrificing to save this one man. It was the success of this mission. We may be able to handle starving for one day, but we wouldn’t be able to continue this journey after starving for three.
“Ah, that’s thanks to the traitor from a certain someone’s team, right?” Jun chimed in.
Is this guy really a paladin? Where is this sarcasm coming from...

“Enough about the traitor. Let me ask you one thing: Sir Calla, did you really think we’d be able to complete this mission without any sacrifices?” Calla fell quiet, clearly speechless, and Kaislan continued heartlessly. “Besides, there will continue to be more injuries—what will we do then? Go up every time?”
Calla wasn’t able to say anything to that, either.
Grit.
He simply gritted his teeth, unable to hide his anger. The reality of having no one on his side was too cruel.
“Why don’t we let him return to god’s embrace in peace? If it’d be too difficult for you to handle yourself, I can help.” Jun suggested turning off life support entirely.
At this, Calla looked at me, shaking pitifully. “Schuitz. Do you think the same way...?”

I neither confirmed nor denied it. “Kaislan didn’t say anything untrue.” Everything he said was usually the case in extreme situations. There came a moment when you had to make a choice and make sacrifices.
“All right. I’ll do it.”
What are you saying?
“No, it’s not time for that yet.”
I couldn’t let a precious member of this expedition die. While they may die during the mission itself, I wouldn’t let it happen here, at least.
“...Sorry?”

I glanced down at Calla, who was staring up at me in bewilderment, and shrugged. “We are neither going up nor letting our comrade die here.” Each team leader gave me the same look at that proclamation.
What the hell is this bastard talking about?
That kind of look.
Tsk, tsk, this is the problem with newbies.
“We’ll continue to head down.”
It was time to use the strategy. Glacier Eye was an area I used to avoid as much as possible. At least, as I said before, until I figured out how to deal with it.
[All healing and recovery effects are reversed.]

The journey through Glacier Cave was long and took up to a week. There was only one reason Dungeon and Stone would hit adventures with such a ridiculous penalty here. Figuring there had to be a means to get around it hidden somewhere, I finally found it after countless attempts. The solution was simpler than I thought it’d be.
“Distortion magic...?”
“Yes, from now on, we’re going to use the Distortion spell against all the demonic monsters we fight.”
“The wizards are tired enough already from using Preservation over and over. Why would you increase their burden?”

That was because the key to this strategy was Distortion. Monsters targeted by it didn’t spit out mana stones or essences, but instead, their corpses had a certain probability of being preserved when they died. Wyvern leather, adamantium, Troll blood (which was a raw material for potions), and various materials used in high-level Spirit Imprints were all acquired using Distortion.
The monsters that appear in Glacier Eye can all be hunted on different floors.

That was the reason why it took me so long to figure out Distortion was the answer. Why bother using Distortion to farm materials in a place where you already had a shortage of inventory thanks to sub-space being blocked? When it was easier to catch those monsters on another floor? It was extremely inefficient. Well, as always, the answer was buried in this goddamn game.
“...To think there was a technique like that to treat injuries here.”
When I gave a brief outline of the strategy, everyone let out exclamations of surprise. Although this was the first they were ever hearing of this, no one doubted my intel.
“Lord Tercerion’s sources are truly amazing. Or, should I say this goes to show how strong the palace is? To think they would know a strategy even I don’t.”

Just as they assumed there had to be another strategist on my team when I turned detective mode on to catch the traitor, they seemed to believe the source of this information was someone else as well.
...Maybe it’s better that they believe that? Hmm, that might be better. Showing off doesn’t help anyone, right? That’s why our Confucian humility is a virtue.
“That’s it, then. Since everyone’s exhausted today, we’ll camp here and set off again tomorrow.”
Figuring Calla’s friend would last at least two more days, we spent the night on the ledge and resumed our journey early the next morning.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
[McKelly Rayothers has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]

Spamming High-Level Distortion, which had a 1.5 times higher probability of succeeding than regular Distortion, we continued to kill monsters. As a result, we were lucky enough to produce a preserved body by afternoon.
“S-Schuitz! Is this the thing you were talking about?” Calla, who was the first to run up and rummage through the body, found a bead and quickly fed it to the injured man before it melted.
[Rick Jugusta has taken Frozen Traces of Life.]
Okay, that’s one person healed...
“Um... what are we doing with the rest of the remains?”

I decided to throw away the rest of the monster’s corpse. It’d sell for a good price back in the city, but it was impossible to take more stuff with us at this point. It was obviously better to just throw it away...
Growl.
Hmm, but why can’t I move my feet?
Searching for the cause of my subconscious resistance, a thought occurred to me.
This is still meat, right? Although it seems a bit rotten...
Thinking I hit paydirt, I rushed over to Amelia and shared my idea. “Emily! I found a way to solve the food problem!”
“What hare-brained scheme have you come up with now?”
“This one isn’t weird, really!”
She sighed. “Tell me what it is first.”
“Well...” I proceeded to explain the food supply plan I came up with.
Slap!
For my troubles, I just ended up getting smacked in the back.
...Was it that bad? Well, I thought it was a good idea...

chapters.title: Chapter 405: Inevitability (1)
paragraphs: The abyss below was shrouded in darkness. The woman looking into it, into a place filled with nothing but the sound of swirling cold, parted her lips to speak. “Six, they’ve completely entered the lower levels of Glacier Eye.”
“The attempt at external intervention had me worried, but I guess they decided to continue the expedition regardless.”
“So, what are you going to do now?”
“Everyone will remain on standby except the security team.”
The woman nodded silently at the command of the person named Six. Then she asked carefully, in a voice that contained a hint of human emotion, “But, Six?”
“Speak.”
“Do you think those people will come back?”
Six didn’t answer that question. There was no point. Whether those people came back or not, what did it matter?
Shaaaaaaa!
All they had to do was follow orders.
Chew, chew.

I walked forward, chewing on beef jerky. It was specially-made, high-calorie beef jerky made specifically for adventurers that was distributed this morning. If anyone was wondering why I was eating breakfast only now, the answer was simple. This was the last of our supply.
Chew, chew.
As of today, all our food was gone. Put simply, we had no more food until we reached the eighth floor. Was that why?
Chew, chew.
Today’s jerky tasted several times better than usual.
What the...? Why did it disappear?
I only had a moment to savor the taste of the beef jerky, and anger came over me when I realized my hand was empty. “I... ate it all already?”
For real? This is our last meal! I’m still starving! Why are we distributing the same amount for each person when everyone consumes different amounts to begin with?
Growwwl!

This is discrimination. Am I wrong? Those pencil-like wizards and priests will have lower metabolisms, and all they have to do is wave their wands in the back, so they consume less energy. Yet we’re still enforcing a one-beef-jerky-per-person policy? This is an insult and a hate crime against the warriors who sweat and bleed on the front lines. If our leader was in their right mind, this kind of policy would never—
Ah, I’m the leader.

Yeah, what could you do? Honestly, I didn’t want to do this, either. But if I gave the warriors special treatment, people were bound to object, saying I was only doing so out of self-interest. So I took the initiative to implement this policy.
Well, looks like it’s a failure.
Through this policy, I’d earned neither gratitude nor hatred from the other classes and the hatred of the warriors. Ah, how did I know the warriors hated me? The source was me. I hated me right now.
“Hehehe.”
“Mister, what’s wrong?”
“Warriors laugh when times are tough.”
“You... call that laughing?” Erwen, who broke formation to walk beside me, shot me a disturbed look before holding something out.
“Beef... jerky...?”
“Yes!”
“You’re... giving this... to me?” I asked in disbelief.
Erwen nodded, her expression unchanged. “Yes!”
I took the jerky in a daze before belatedly coming to my senses. “I-It’s fine! I’m not hungry, you eat it!”
“If you’re going to say that, why don’t you get rid of that smile first?”
Uh, smile?

Just as I was wondering what she was talking about, Erwen summoned a water spirit and turned it into a mirror. On the other end of the reflection was me, smiling like an idiot. “Look, this is real laughter! Hehe! Come on, eat it. I’m fine. Everyone else is giving their share to others who need it.”
“...What?”

At my look of confusion, Amelia chimed in from behind me to provide an answer. “People in the rear, who have enough stamina to spare, have been saving up their food little by little instead of eating it.”
“Saving it? How? It would have spoiled fast.”
“I’m talking about after we entered the cave. There haven’t been any ice storms since then.”

“Oh, right...” Was it because I’d been suffering so much from hunger? I couldn’t believe I hadn’t been able to figure out something so simple right away. Anyway, none of that was important. “But is that true? That people are giving away the little food they have?”
“If you can’t believe it, you can see for yourself later.”
Hmm, I need to see it right now.
“Halt!” I used my authority as commander to stop the march. It was time for a break anyway.
“Oh, a break!”
“I can catch my breath!”
“Ahhh! Provisions Officer! Give me a blanket! I need to rest my eyes even if it’s only for a moment!”
A priest activated Destruction of Evil to turn this spot into a safe zone. The crew immediately took advantage of the opportunity to lie down and recover their stamina.
I pretended to be on patrol so I could step back and observe. As it turned out, what Erwen said was true.
“Here, take this.” A priest was giving her food to some warriors.
“...J-J-Jerky? For me?” The warrior was stunned, a look of deep disbelief on his face.
“Yes. You must be tired.”
“A-Are you in love with me? If so, I cannot take this jerky. I have a wife and children in the city—”
“That’s not why I’m giving it to you, don’t worry.”
“What? You’re willing to give me beef jerky even though you don’t love me...?”
The warriors were shocked but still ate the beef jerky they received, and the same scene played out over the entire group.
“Mmm, this... debt! I will repay my debt to you someday, I swear it on my life!”
Numerous warriors steeled their resolve and made similar declarations, even shedding tears over a single piece of jerky. It was a very moving scene, even for me.
“My policy... was not a failure...”
The squadron had truly become one, helping each other out.
“Mr. Schuitz? Did you just say something to me?”
“Ah, Jun... It’s nothing.”
“All right. But what brings you here? Is it related to why you suddenly stopped the procession?”
Actually, I was only over here to see what was going on because I felt too guilty to accept Erwen’s jerky, but I took it. A commander had to save face, after all. “How is morale today?”
“Today...?”
“The food supply ran out this morning. Has anyone expressed any grievances?”
“Everyone is strong. They’ve all experienced far worse things than this, so starving for a single day is nothing. Everyone considers it unavoidable.”
“I see...” Since I didn’t come over here because I was actually curious, I just nodded and left. I was heading back to the front line, where my team was.
“Oh, Schuitz! Thanks for last time!”
“Why do you look like you’re getting thinner by the day?”
“I was eating this, but do you want some?”

Familiar warriors greeted me. This may have been the biggest change since Pyke Neldine’s execution. Regardless of party affiliation, we all had to take out our shields and run out together whenever a major battle broke out, so we inevitably developed a sense of camaraderie. It wasn’t just my relationship with my fellow warriors that had improved, either. Although not as friendly as the warriors who joked around with me, everyone else’s eyes were warmer. It was deeply moving, because just a while ago, they were busy eyeing me and whispering every time I walked by.
This is probably thanks to Neldine.

An outside enemy had brought the group together. When his betrayal was revealed, all the resentment directed at me turned to him. I had been the one to discover the traitor too. My reputation had naturally improved as a result.
“Schuitz, that man... I can’t tell if he’s a genius or a moron.”
“I heard he was scolded by his teammate the other day for suggesting we eat monster meat...”
“He’s kind of slow, but I don’t think he’s foolish. Seeing as he tracked down the traitor.”
“Ah, that? But... I heard he only took credit after his wizard figured it all out.”
Haha, to think there were more traitors here.
I wondered if I should beat them down right away, but I changed my mind at the conversation that followed.
“But having capable subordinates is also a reflection of one’s abilities. Besides, he seems like a good one.”
“That’s... true. I haven’t spoken to him much but he seemed kind.”
“Having the title of commander means he could just yell out orders if he wanted, but instead he always takes on the tough jobs.”
“Mm-hmm, people like that are the most reliable allies in tough situations.”
What the—? They were just ordinary comrades.
Step, step.
When I finally returned to my position, pretending not to hear their conversation on the way, our twenty-minute break—as per unspoken rule—was almost over.
“Mister! How did it go? I was right, right?”
“You were.”
“Okay, then eat. Okay? Don’t feel bad, everyone’s doing it.”
“Ah, that... I already ate it on the way back over here.”
“Hehe, good job! I’m the best, right?”
“Yeah, you’re the best,” I said benevolently.
With that, I leaned against the wall and fiddled with the ring for the remainder of the break. While I was doing so, Amelia approached me.
“Are you wondering why the light disappeared?”
“Ah, yeah, I guess...”
No. 6111: Destiny Seeker, the ring I called the Traffic Light Ring, had suddenly lost its light. It happened about four days ago.
“That definitely is strange,” said Amelia with a frown. “A fate once sensed wouldn’t disappear for no reason.”
“That’s what I’m saying.”
No matter how I looked at it, it was extremely weird. I didn’t recall anything bad happening...
On Day Twenty of our trip through Ice Rock, we finally reached the end.
I didn’t think we’d really arrive on the twentieth day.

In the planning stages, we’d allocated ourselves twenty days to cover Ice Rock. Despite several unfortunate events on the one hand and moving as fast as we could on the other, we still arrived on the exact date.
Maybe the timeline was too tight from the start.

I wasn’t sure, but I got the sense that if we had tried to follow the original schedule, we would have arrived here two or three days late. I had also attended the royal meetings as the commander, so if I had to explain it, it was that there were too many unexpected variables.

The fact that most of the crew were first-timers to Ice Rock had been taken into consideration during the planning stages, of course. But that was only on paper. I hadn’t known their exact capabilities back then. Although their hunting speed was exceptional, the squadron was a bit lacking when it came to speed. I guessed that was only natural considering this team was created for the purpose of war, not adventuring.
“Mister, what are you thinking so hard about?”
“...Nothing.”
I ended my musings there and glanced around. The lowest part of Glacier Eye had a symbol reminiscent of a human eye on the ground.
“Now, now, everyone calm down and wait your turn! We’ll draw lots in order!”

All we had to do now was take the portal to the eighth floor, but the squadron was currently in a state of chaos. The reason for that was rather simple. Because this was Ice Rock, a rough terrain that no one ever came to, we were of course the first to arrive at its portal.
“How are we going to decide the order?”
“I don’t care who gets it, so can’t we just go through? I’m starving.”
“What? Then you’re out!”
“What? Out? I never wanted in from the start! I’m a wizard!”

The maximum number of people who could be connected by a single Bind spell was six. As such, the number of people who could claim the experience points for opening a portal was six as well. We decided to do a fair draw to determine who these people would be regardless of position or merit, based purely on luck.
“Ahh! Damn it! Why is it blank?!”
“Hey! Don’t even think about using your skill to look inside the box! I have my eye on you!”
“Woohoo! Eighth-Floor Portal Opening! I live to see the day!”
The long line shrank person by person, and cheers and sighs rang out periodically.
While I was watching this all from the very back, Ravien, who was standing next to me, spoke. “Aren’t you upset?”
“What do you mean?”
“You are the commander of this mission. No one would have been able to argue if you used your position to claim a spot.”
“Ah, that.”

This had actually been discussed among the team leaders, that we should take the experience points for ourselves and draw lots for the remaining spot. Kaislan added that the remaining spot should be awarded to the person who contributed the most, rather than by draw. That was how you were supposed to treat subordinates.
“...Um, you are listening to me, right?”
“Ah, I’m listening.”
“Why did you give it up so easily?” Ravien asked, and I simply shrugged in answer. What kind of response was she looking for in the first place? She clearly knew why I did it.
“Tsk, blank,” Amelia, who had pulled a ticket before me, tutted. When she came back, she patted me on the shoulder. “Schuitz, it’s your turn now.”
“How many tickets are left?”
“One.”
One, huh...
I turned my head as discreetly as possible to check the number of people still left in line. Including me, there were four. Put simply, the probability was 25 percent.
There are no Hanses among them.
With good fortune on my back, I stepped forward.
Shaaaaaa!
A cold wind descended from above and swept the ground before rising up again.
Slide.
I took off the ring on my finger. There was no need for it now.
Step, step.
Destiny was something you carved on your own.
“Good luck.” When I stopped in front of the box, Kaislan spoke words of encouragement.
It was now time to see the payoff.
“Ahhh!” I let out a manly roar and drew a ticket.
“That’s too bad. It’s blank.”
Of course it didn’t work. Ha, is it because there’s no background music? It’s a rule of thumb that you have to let the cool soundtrack play during big moments.
Step, step.
As I spiritlessly turned around to make room for the next person, Ravien passed me. Ah, so it was her turn next.
She’s not going to pull it, right?
“It’s the one with the round mark, right? This one?”
“That’s right. Congratulations.”
Man, she did? I should’ve waited one more turn...
I was starting to turn green with envy.
“Can this ticket be transferred to someone else?”
“I guess you didn’t hear the explanation earlier. After a long discussion, we agreed to allow it.”
“Really?” After that brief exchange with Kaislan, Ravien turned around without hesitation and approached me. “Here, take it.” She suddenly handed me the ticket.

I couldn’t understand. This was the same person who entered the labyrinth on her own and only met up with us on the sixth floor so that she could do a speedrun. I had been sure it was because she was in a hurry to gain XP.
“Why are you giving this to me...?”
“I just don’t think this should be mine.”
“...What?”
When I tilted my head in confusion, Ravien stiltedly and awkwardly replied. “I’ve been by your side this whole time, so I know for a fact that you suffered the most.”
What is this...?
Whistle!
“Yeah, yeah! You’re the one who brought us all the way here, so you should get to open it!”
“What a shame. I was going to give him mine if no one else did.”
“Liar! You were so happy earlier!”
“I-It’s true! During the discussion earlier, I was one of the people arguing that we should allow transfers!”
“Whatever, hurry up and take it! An adventurer should look after their own interests where they can!”
In this deep underground place where the wind was so cold it froze your nose, I felt like I was going to cry.
It’s warm...

chapters.title: Chapter 406: Inevitability (2)
paragraphs: Once the draw was over, the winners gathered together and formed a Bind. Then everyone gathered up and headed to the monument in the center.
Whooom!
When I placed my hand on top, the portal opened with a brilliant, rainbow burst of light.
“Oh, how fascinating. It’s clear how the mana flows but there’s a distinct difference from the flow of typical space-time mana.”
“Is this your first time seeing a portal open?”
“Yes. Wizards have no reason to obsess over feats like that, right?”
While the crew watched the portal open and gave idle commentary, the light clusters spreading in all directions soon glommed together to form a distinct shape.
[You are the first to open this portal. EXP +2]
I always thought this, but it really was unfair that opening the eighth-floor portal was worth the same as opening the first-floor portal.
Whooom!

The cluster of rainbow-colored lights transformed into a disk and shimmered. When I turned around, everyone was staring at me without a word. So, they wanted me to be the one to open it and the first to go in too?
“In formation!” In case someone was on the other side of the portal, we took up our formation, and I stepped through the portal first.
Flash!
White light filled my field of vision. Before long, the fragmented pieces of the world beyond it came into focus.
[You have entered the Land of Dawn on the eighth floor.]
These were the depths of the labyrinth referred to in the game as the Land of Dawn.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Reach the eighth floor.]
[Reward: Your Soul Power has permanently increased by +50.]

Just like when I first entered the Great Demon Realm on the fifth floor, an achievement was reached and I could feel my soul expand. These guys called this a baptism, I think? This was a mysterious phenomenon where the labyrinth granted an adventurer a blessing when they accomplished certain tasks.
Whooom!
I went in first and took in my surroundings. The squad followed suit.
“There... are no enemies.”
“That’s a relief. I was worried the enemy would be waiting for us like during the battle of the Goblin Forest.”
“I finally get to see the eighth floor.”
“This alone makes my participation in this mission worth it.”

About half the crew got baptized, indicating this was their first time here. No, since the wizards and priests were excluded, it was safe to say it was more than half. Well, that was to be expected—the eighth floor was classified as a deep floor.
“What a fascinating place...” It looked like this was Erwen’s first time on the eighth floor too. The most experienced among us would be Amelia or Ravien.
“Enemy or not, let’s eat!”
“Woohoo!”
“Injuries first! Please, someone, treat this quickly! It started noticeably festering yesterday and now I can’t feel my fingertips!”
It seemed a riot would ensue at any moment, so a break was quickly ordered. The food on the sleds had run out, but everything we had stored in sub-space was still fine.

As soon as permission was given, everyone on the crew took out food from their sub-spaces and stuffed their mouths. Those whose injuries were classified as minor gnawed on beef jerky as they looked around for a priest.
“Mister, we should eat too.”
“Yeah.” I was starving just as much so I quickly pulled out the food and ate with my teammates.
“I’ve only ever heard about it, but I didn’t know this was such a peaceful place.”
“You mean the Land of Dawn?”
“Yes. Since it’s called a deep floor, I thought it would be much scarier...”

Well, the sentiment had merit. We were on a towering green hill. The only thing that surrounded us was a vast meadow, and a warm breeze brushed our skin. Just a moment ago we were wearing thick fur clothes and trembling from the cold, so the difference was stark.

“You guys rest over here. I’m going to go look around for a moment.” Once my stomach was somewhat full, I walked away from the group. A leader had duties to attend to, right? I could eat beef jerky while I walked.

Shoving five pieces of jerky into my mouth at once, a luxury greater than any I could have dreamed up a few hours ago, I chewed as I wandered around. But my heart was too heavy for pure happiness. That was the reason why I wasn’t able to stay put and was instead roaming around.
I don’t see a rift...

The Land of Dawn was a very small place. In terms of area, it was probably the smallest of all the floors in the labyrinth. There were no monsters here, either; at least, not until you went into the Rift.
In that case... it would be safe to assume someone went in first.

The eighth floor always had one rift open. It was randomly generated, and when the Rift was completely cleared, two portals opened for your choosing. You could head up to the ninth floor, or return to the eighth floor. Whichever option you chose, the moment it was cleared, another Rift regenerated on the eighth floor and that cycle continued.
The problem here is... The people inside that Rift right now have to be from Noark.

Would those guys head to the ninth floor? Or would they return to the eighth and choose to hunt in a different type of rift? If they went for the latter, even resting here right now was a considerable risk. If they were active on the eighth floor it meant they’d be in squadron-sized units, with a skill level similar to ours.
Anyway, I see why the palace was in a hurry...

Now that I’d come to the eighth floor myself, it hit me that the palace had lost many high-ranking adventurers throughout this two-year war. Of course, thanks to plenty of political support, a supply of stockpiled essences, and the return of many retired adventurers, their forces had been restored to some extent.
But if things continue like this, it’ll only get worse.

Noark was basically using a cheat code. Starting on the seventh floor from the first day? They could go straight to the eighth floor to scour it for the highest-ranking essences. If this continued for even a few more years, the gap between Noark and Rafdonia’s top adventurers would widen exponentially.
...But since they can’t erase essences, they could end up with bad combinations.

That would be the case for most of them, actually. I hadn’t met anyone in this world who planned their essence combos as meticulously as I did. Ninety percent of them would have random specs. But, as always, there would be exceptions.
...In any case, that isn’t something to worry about right now.

I tried to let go of my anxiety about the distant future. I may have been working for the palace right now, but it wasn’t like I planned to sacrifice my life out of loyalty to the king. While I was in the labyrinth, even focusing everything I had on what was in front of me wasn’t enough.
“We’re leaving in five minutes, so get ready!”
Our long-awaited break came to an end. We were going to enter the middle of enemy territory, and it wasn’t a good idea to relax too much.
“Goodbye to this horrible sled!”

Sleds and supply boxes were placed in sub-space, and the potions, scrolls, and various battle consumables that had been sealed in boxes until now were distributed to each team appropriately. With that, we were ready to resume our journey.
When it came time to leave, everyone lined up in their positions. At first, we had looked like a bunch of misfits, but now we looked more like a proper, elite fighting force.
“Depart!”

The process of going from the eighth floor down to the Dark Continent was uneventful. That was because as long as you didn’t go into a Rift, the eighth floor had no monsters and was a safe zone, and the portal itself was close enough to be visible from the hill.
Step, step.
We arrived at our destination after walking for about thirty minutes.
“Once we walk through, we’ll be in the Dark Continent, right?”

I confirmed it from a distance with my naked eye, but even up close, there didn’t seem to be anything wrong with the portal. This was a relief. If Noark hadn’t opened the eighth-floor portal and instead left it alone, we would have been stuck here twiddling our thumbs.
Well, even if they hadn’t come up to the eighth floor to hunt, I considered the possibility someone would open it on the seventh just for the XP.
Maintaining formation, I walked over to the portal first and everyone gulped. It looked like everyone had a mild case of the jitters now that Noark’s territory was right in front of us.
“Schuitz.” Just as I was about to enter, Kaislan spoke up. “Why don’t you say a word or two before we go? Coming from you, it should boost the squad’s morale.”
Hmm, I don’t really feel like it. It’s a waste of time too.

When I looked indifferent, Kaislan blinked and quickly added, “Th-think carefully. This is a historic moment. If this mission succeeds and we play an important role in winning the war... whatever you say here will be recorded for generations to come.”
I didn’t know about “historic.” But given the way his eyes were burning with an obvious desire for glory, I could tell this guy was jealous out of his mind.
If I don’t say anything, he’ll probably keep whining about it... It would be better to say something quick.
“Ahem-hem.”

When I cleared my throat, Kaislan straightened his back like a guard and yelled to get the group’s attention, his voice full of gravitas. “Troops, listen! We now stand at a great crossroads. Success or failure! Will we lose it all, or gain it all? I’m sure some of you are anxiously wondering the same thing! However! I, Melend Kaislan, have no doubt we will go down in history as the victors!”
“Ooooooh!”
While Kaislan’s teammates cheered, the others wore sour expressions. Why is he saying all this? That was what they seemed to be asking.

I guessed Kaislan intuitively picked up on that as well. “On that note! Everyone, listen carefully! I’m sure Sir Schuitz will have something to say before we execute this grand mission bestowed on us by the palace!”
Kaislan passed the baton to me in a flash. It was ridiculous.
What the—? I thought you wanted me to do it, so why are you handing me the mic after saying whatever you wanted? I guess he wants to be recorded in history somehow too.

I couldn’t understand what was running through his head at all, but everyone had different motivations. Turning my back to the portal connecting to the Dark Continent, I looked at the crew. Everyone seemed curious about what I would say, unlike Kaislan. I wondered if this was why that American CEO was always trolling on social media. People at least paid attention that way, wondering what kind of trouble he was going to cause.
Anyway, I have more important things to focus on right now.

“Ahem...” I cleared my throat and scanned the crowd. Before me I could see the faces of the crew, faces I was now very well acquainted with after going through hardships day and night together. Was that why? At that moment, I thought of something I wanted to say. “I won’t speak for long this time, either!”
Yeah. Since I already said “Let’s kill a lot and earn a lot” back then, this should suffice for today:
“Let’s come back with as many alive as possible!”
[You have entered the Dark Continent on the seventh floor.]

Dragon Pit was one of the later stages of the Dark Continent. Almost as if we had entered a museum, the skeletons of huge vertebrae were scattered all around the ruins and the ground was full of skulls and bone fragments.
Rattle, rattle.
We moved forward, making as little noise as possible. No one spoke.
Rattle.
There wasn’t a single light illuminating our surroundings. Of course, that wasn’t a major hurdle to securing visibility. The issue of darkness was solved with magic.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-five support spell Insight.]
Using this too often consumed significant mana, but it was unavoidable. We were in the middle of enemy territory, after all. We had to move as carefully as possible.
Clack.
Amelia, who had taken the position in front of me once we reached the seventh floor, suddenly stopped in her tracks.
Whip, whip.

She sent urgent hand signals my way. The enemy was nearby. The team leaders following behind joined me at the forefront and immediately activated a team communication spell so we could all speak without Noark hearing us.
“How many enemies?”
“Fifteen.”
Hmm, only the size of a small clan. Well, you need to operate with at least that many people in a place like this.
“What’s your plan? Battling them?” asked Akurava.
“Isn’t that obvious?” said Kaislan. “Those people are enemies threatening our kingdom. Let’s attack them right away!”
“I agree with Sir Kaislan. War achievements are great, but it’s also safer to gradually reduce their numbers as much as possible starting now.”
The leaders came to a unanimous agreement and it was decided we would ambush the enemy. As the commander, I didn’t disagree.
“Okay, let’s attack them quickly.”

“Wait. We need to prepare more if we’re going to pull off a surprise attack. If the wizards and special ability users release their firepower in one concentrated burst, this battle will be much easier,” said Akurava.
“Oh, that’s true. Since this is the first battle, we’ll lead,” said Kaislan.
What are these guys talking so seriously about?
“Do you guys know what an ambush is?”
When I poured cold water on their discussion, the team leaders tilted their heads at me.
Jeez, all of them seemed so experienced at killing. I guess they’ve never looted anyone before?
“Wizard or not, the first thing we’ll do is wait.”
“Wait for what?” asked Kaislan.
Isn’t that obvious?
“When they start fighting monsters, we’ll attack them from behind.”
These were the basics of Player Killing.

chapters.title: Chapter 407: Inevitability (3)
paragraphs: The online game I used to enjoy before finding Dungeon and Stone was a game with PVP as its main component. In the game, you chose from one of two factions and grew up in a different continent depending on which one you selected, then went to the other to fight for dominance. I remembered the feeling of leading a small army into enemy territory and stealing the level’s boss right from under their noses was very gratifying. PKing passionately, taking down the boss with a big, awesome blow, and getting to hear all kinds of rave reviews in the voice chat from players in the enemy faction?
It was a pretty fun game.
If I hadn’t come across Dungeon and Stone, I might’ve still been playing that game. Of all the games I played, it was the best one.
Wait, if I kept playing that game, I wouldn’t have been dragged here...

Aside from those regrets, the reason I had suddenly remembered a game I had almost completely forgotten about was simple. In a way, there were a lot of similarities between it and our current situation. Currently, the Dark Continent was occupied by Noark, and our expedition team had secretly set foot on their territory.
And more importantly... The method I used there works well here too.
I felt the same feeling I felt while playing that game here.
“...A-Ambush!”
“How the hell did they get here?!”
“Take care of the monsters up front first!”
“A-Ahhh!”
Our panicked enemies didn’t know how to react.
“Eeek! You cowards...!”
“Taking advantage of a moment like that!”
“I’ll take you with me!”
Praise poured in.
[You have defeated a Bone Dragonian. EXP +7]
On top of that, I killed a bunch of rank-three monsters like it was a piece of cake. Of course, the icing on said cake was something else.
“A-An essence!”

Not only did we succeed at ambushing and PKing a whole bunch of people without a single injury, but as a bonus, one of the monsters dropped an essence—the second rank-three essence we had acquired during this expedition. To be honest, I was more dazed than happy.
What is this...?

Rank-three essences weren’t something that could be obtained this easily. That was because there were very few rank-three monsters on the seventh floor. Taking into account both here and Ice Rock combined, the total number of rank-three monsters we’d hunted didn’t even reach twenty.
But two already, huh? Is luck on our side? Well, I’m sure this is a net positive.
“Ashed, go collect the essence.”
“Okay.”
I sent our wizard over to store the essence in a test tube while I took stock of the battlefield. The essence wasn’t our only loot. As always, the piece de resistance of PKing was something else.
Choke...
“H-Help...”
“You know I can’t save you.”
Why was this guy talking to a corpse? “Stop babbling and get out of the way.” I hefted my hammer to press the happy button on the bastards still clinging to their lifelines.
Smash, smash, smash!
As flesh was pounded, bodies went limp. After personally confirming the kills myself, I had the crew strip their equipment and store it in the expedition’s shared sub-space.
“Whew, considering the equipment they’ll have in their sub-spaces, this is no joke.”
“Everyone will get a good share once we get back.”

The crew seemed to have done the math and were now burning up with enthusiasm. It made sense. A rank-three essence was valuable, too, but not as valuable as the equipment of fifteen people who were active on the seventh floor. More importantly, the effort we had to put into the battle was minimal.
“We finished collecting the loot,” said Akurava.
“Any injured?”
“None.”
“I see.” I couldn’t hide my pleasure and raised the corners of my lips. The battle had ended cleanly without a single person injured.
“...Do you plan to continue fighting like this?”
“Is there a problem?”

“No. But...” Akurava trailed off and pursed her lips. Having experienced it for herself, she now knew that this was the best way to ambush an enemy when they were hunting in their territory with their guards down. Well, that didn’t mean there weren’t drawbacks.
Thirty minutes, huh?

The battle itself had ended in five minutes, but the time it had taken for our opponents to first encounter a monster was considerable. Of course, the disadvantages weren’t worth considering compared to the advantages. If someone got hurt or died during a fight, that was a far bigger loss, right? But it seemed there were still some regrets to be had.
Kaislan offered a bit of cautious advice. “Schuitz, killing everyone was hasty. We should’ve captured at least one to obtain information.”
Ah, that’s true too.
“We’ll do that starting with the next ambush.” Kaislan’s expression suddenly brightened, probably because I was considering his advice. “Wizards, burn the bodies and erase all traces of us!”

After we finished cleaning up the surrounding area, we slipped back into the darkness and got moving. But because our surroundings were so silent, I was able to hear a conversation between some crew members that made me chuckle to myself.
“Did you see that earlier? Their equipment?”
“If we do ten more of these... how much will that be?”
I don’t know, I guess we’ll find out soon enough.
Our routine since arriving on the Dark Continent was as follows:
Step, step.
We traveled while shrouded in darkness.
“The enemy.”
We waited until the enemy fought a monster, giving us an opportunity to strike.
“Now!”
Then, we took advantage of their distraction to launch an all-out ambush.
Bang, bang, bang!
Whiiip!
Boom!
Things got even easier once we started bombarding them with long-range firepower at the get-go and blowing up the entire rear guard first.
“Let’s go!”
“Wipe them all out!”

Even when our close-range warriors closed in, their front line wasn’t free to offer their rear guard support thanks to the monsters they were dealing with up front. For that reason, the battle ended fast this time as well.
This makes ten, right?
Repeating this process as we moved, the number of ambushes we’d pulled off reached double digits right as we were getting out of the Dragon Pit.
“Wizard! Put up a soundproof barrier first!”
“Hey! Be careful when you take the gear off! It keeps coming with flesh attached!”
When the battle ended, the squadron began collecting the loot and erasing our tracks again. As I oversaw the process, one of our team members dragged a survivor in front of me.
“Commander! Here is the survivor you asked for!”
“Good job.”
“It was nothing.”

Starting from the second battle, we made sure to always keep one person alive to extract information from them. You never knew. Anything could happen in the labyrinth at any time. We couldn’t neglect regularly collecting intelligence. I wasn’t the one conducting the interrogations, anyway.
“Jun.”
“Leave it to me.”

If I just left it to Jun, the expedition’s official information extractor, the information tumbled out of them on its own, and all I had to do was piece it together. For example, the people hunting on the eighth floor were Noark’s most elite fighters. Because of that, their main base was currently empty. Useful information like that came to light. The problem was none of the recent survivors knew much more than that, so we hadn’t gotten any new intelligence in a while.
“Schuitz, please come here a moment. It’s urgent.”

It’d been a while since Jun called for me during an interrogation. I wondered what was up, so I quickly headed over and found that the tied-up survivor was still alive. This meant some important information had come up during questioning.
“Go ahead. What did you find out?”
“It’d be a bit inaccurate to say I found anything out.”
“Inaccurate...?”
I tilted my head and Jun’s eyes shifted to the side. When I followed his line of sight, I could see a stone glowing and vibrating faintly nearby—an item any adventurer was bound to recognize.
“A message stone...?”
“It was in his possession.”
“That means...”
“Yes, someone is trying to contact this man. What are you going to do?”
The moment the question left Jun’s mouth, the message stone vibrated once more.
Jiiiiiing!
I wondered how many more times it would ring before stopping. There was no way to know, which was why I had to make a decision, fast.
Slide.
I raised my hand slightly to ask for some time, then gathered my thoughts.
Is this communication from nearby, or somewhere far away?

The radius of a message stone was limited, though the exact range depended on the quality of the stone. But this was Noark’s territory, which meant this call could very well be coming from far away. This was tied to the reason the palace had formed an expeditionary force to attack the main base in the first place—the mana wave emitter.

To put it in modern terms, a mana wave emitter was a structure that operated similarly to a transmission tower. These guys had used their cheat code to enter the seventh floor directly and then upgraded their forces by bringing along a huge device that had to have been too big to ever fit into a sub-space. Thanks to that, Noark was able to freely communicate with troops scattered across the continent and actively hindered the royal army.
Jiiiiiing!
The damn ringing echoed once more. I finished thinking things over and asked a few questions. “Hey, you, where do you think this call is coming from?”
“...I-It’s probably a routine communication. To check on the status of each troop!”
Hmm, I see.
“Jun, what are the chances this guy is fucking with us?”
“I think it’s very unlikely.” If he was able to sound that certain in a situation where it was difficult to be sure about anything, that meant he was very confident.
“...I-I’ll do it! I’ll do as you say! S-So, please, k-kill me...!”
