As I listened to the guy plead for death instead of life, I passed my judgment. Yeah, I was willing to trust that. “All right, pick up the call. If they ask if anything’s wrong, tell them nothing is.” I grabbed the message stone and shoved it in his face.
Click.

The moment I pressed the button to take the call, a man’s voice rang out from beyond the glowing stone. “Finally reached you.” It was a deep, bass voice, and the second it hit my ears, my heart started pounding violently.
Thump, thump, thump!
That voice was one I could never forget.
“R-Regal Vagos... is that you?” stuttered our prisoner.
Grit.
So, you’re somewhere on the eighth floor too.

I’d encountered many enemies since coming into this world. Most got their heads bashed in, but unfortunately, I lacked the strength to take care of some of the others. Riakis, the Lord of Chaos; Abed Necrapeto, the Corpse Collector; Belbev Ruingenes, the Fallen Scholar. Those names immediately came to mind, but the person I held the biggest grudge against was this guy—Regal Vagos, the Dragon Slayer. As soon as I heard that voice, my mind went blank and my blood boiled.
Squeeze.
Now wasn’t the time for that, though. Clenching my fists even tighter, I cooled my head and concentrated on the conversation.
“Meiras, where are you right now?”
“I-I’m hunting with the other members of my team in the Dragon Pit!”
“...Really? Then do you know something?”
“Know something about...?”
“We can’t reach anyone who went into the Dragon Pit.”
“I-I-Is that right? I’m not sure. W-We’re doing all right and haven’t run into any issues. Really!”
His tone was over-the-top and practically begging for Vagos to catch on. I could let the stuttering slide, but wasn’t this way too much?
Just then, Jun quietly picked up an awl next to him, immediately straightened up, and got his act together.
Slide.
“But that’s weird. No one is reachable? Perhaps they were attacked by monsters?” His pronunciation was clear as if he’d never been stuttering at all.
“No matter how pathetic they are, there’s no way all of them were killed.”
“...That’s true. But is there any news on your end?” The guy took things a step further and even showed an interest in asking for information from Vagos.
“Not yet.”
“I’m glad. I’ll look around and check to see what’s happened on this end, so don’t worry.”
“You? Don’t do anything stupid and just wait. We’ve already sent troops over there. Join them and do as they say.”
“Yes, all right.”
“Tsk, useless bastards.” The prick then tutted and cut off the transmission.
“That’s a shame,” said Jun. “It would have been nice to know how many troops were sent this way.”
“Yeah, it would have...”
“...Is something wrong? You don’t look well.”
“Don’t worry about it. It’s nothing.” It was just getting harder to hold back my anger. While I was listening to that voice, the events of that day flashed through my mind in vivid detail.
Just then, I heard a sound from behind me. “N-No.”
Whip.
When I turned around, I saw Erwen standing there.
Tap.

It looked like she had been holding something in her hands, but that item fell to the ground. Normally, if it were a regular mistake, she would have bent down to pick it back up again, but Erwen instead just stopped and stared at me.
“Erwen? Why are you here?” As I got closer, I realized something was very wrong. “Wait, you’re shaking...”
“Th-that v-voice...”
“Calm down. Are you okay?”
“Just now! Th-th-that was... him, right? T-The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos...”
I didn’t know why, but Erwen was terrified.

chapters.title: Chapter 408: Inevitability (4)
paragraphs: Only a few people knew about my ill-fated relationship with the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos. Aside from the members of my party at the time, there were a few high-ranking members of the Church of Reatlas and the leaders of the dragon tribe. Of course, Erwen knew nothing about the vine ring or Reatlas’s blessing, only that a wizard named Dwalkie suffered great misfortune in the labyrinth.
Does she have some sort of ax to grind with him too?
If so, that was strange. When the marquess shared that one of our missions was to help Ravien kill the Dragon Slayer, she hadn’t reacted like this.
...Hmm, actually, the look on her face wasn’t all that great back then, either.

No, now that I thought about it, the look on her face hadn’t been good at all. Amelia had noticed the way her lips were pressed together and asked if she was in pain. She said it was nothing and left in a hurry. I hadn’t dug deeper back then.
But I should check it out now.
I couldn’t just stand by and watch as my teammate broke down. I excused myself from Jun, immediately walked over to calm Erwen down, and got the story.
“I-I’m sorry. F-For acting like this all of a sudden...”
“I’m not here for an apology. I’m just worried. Did something happen with that piece of shit Dragon Slayer?”
“Well...” Erwen hesitated for a long moment before finally opening her mouth. “It happened when I was ten years old.”

“Ten years old...” That was about thirteen years ago now. In other words, a year after the war between the barbarians and elves ended. Immediately, something came to mind. “Does this... have something to do with the massacre?”
There had been a terror attack targeting the elves’ holy land. The perpetrator was Regal Vagos, and the number of elves killed that day was over a thousand. And if my assumptions were correct...
“Yes, that was the day my parents passed away. In front of me... to protect me, Daria, and our younger sister...”
“...I see.”

Erwen had lost her parents that day. Her uncle adopted all three sisters and raised them with love, but that hole in their lives could never be filled. Even still, Erwen had persevered. It was all thanks to the eldest, Daria, doing her best to fill that hole.
“That young lady was born with the most destiny after you.”
This cruel world had then taken even Daria away from her. Although it hadn’t been the Dragon Slayer, coincidentally, it had been Fallen Scholar, another member of Orcules.
“Goddamn it.”

“I-I’m sorry. As soon as I heard that voice, I got scared. That man is clearly my enemy... a-and I know I have to fight if I don’t want to lose any more people I care about... But part of me was... afraid those damn bastards were coming to take them from me again...” It was understandable that Erwen was in a state of panic. “I-It’s pathetic, right...? When I’m so much stronger now... I promised myself I’d get revenge someday, but I’m still like this...”
That was what trauma was—emotion over reason. No, to be more precise, it was the memories of that event overriding your every thought and filling you with fear.
“Pathetic? Of course not. The pathetic one... is me.”
“What? P-Pathetic? There’s no way! Mister, do you know how great you are?”
Uh... well, everyone has their own standards, I guess.
I thought I had spent quite some time with Erwen, yet I didn’t know anything about this past of hers. No, actually, I didn’t even make an effort to.
“To be honest, I’ve noticed as well... that there’s something wrong with me...”
If, when I first learned about Erwen’s symptoms of anxiety, I hadn’t dismissed them as simply a side effect of her stats and essences, things would have been different.
“You must’ve had a hard time. I know... what it feels like to lose something.”
When I returned to the city after losing Dwalkie, if I had thought more deeply about the meaning behind her words of comfort, I would’ve figured out what the real problem was earlier on.
“Mister...”
Still, it was not like me to be so doom and gloom. If there was a problematic problem, all I had to do was eliminate said problem.
“Erwen.”
When I called her name, Erwen looked up at me with watery eyes and reached out to grab my hand, like she was waiting with bated breath for whatever I’d say next.
So, you were hoping for me to say this, huh?
“Don’t be so anxious. Whether it’s Fallen Scholar, Corpse Collector, or that goddamn lizard bastard,” I quietly vowed, “I will slaughter them all one day.”
...Huh? This isn’t the reaction I was expecting.
“What, you don’t believe me?”
When I glared at her, Erwen’s shoulders jumped. “O-Of course not! I-I believe you!”
It was a weak answer but I wasn’t too pressed about it. Erwen’s eyes, which had been filled with anxiety, were now blank. It seemed I managed to calm her down a bit.
After calming Erwen down and sending her back over to the team, I took a moment to get my thoughts in order.
This is strange.

The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos... there were as many as four people on my team who had a bone to pick with that guy. Me and Ravien, who was from the dragon tribe, went without saying, but as our conversation had revealed, he was also enemies with Erwen.
Amelia said she was in a similar situation.

Of course, Amelia was in a slightly different boat than the three of us. Hers was closer to a one-sided grudge on the Dragon Slayer’s end. Apparently, she found the bastard beneath a portal, stole his equipment, and drugged him with a memory-loss pill.
“If he’s regained his memories, he will be dying to kill me.”
If there was a part of her story that had surprised me, it was the timing. That had been the same day the first vine broke off of my ring.
In a way, Amelia kind of helped me back then.
The coincidence could only be described as remarkable. I chuckled and went off to find Jun.
“Arghhh!” I heard the scream as soon as I opened the flap of the tent, which had a noise-blocking spell on it. “Y-You said you’d k-kill me! Arghhh!”
“Because I believed you confessed all your sins and that your heart was once again pure. But I was deceived.”
“I-I didn’t lie about anything!”
“Then why didn’t you tell me about the Dragon Slayer? It sounds like that man is waiting at your base.”
“Th-that’s...!”
“There’s still a hint of evil in your eyes—”
“I-I didn’t know! I didn’t know! Those people never tell me where they are or when! Aghhh! Kill me! Just kill me!”

The man, whose limbs were convulsing despite being tied up, suddenly clamped his mouth shut. In response, Jun violently grabbed his jaw and pried it open. When he did, blood poured out. The man had bitten his own tongue in an attempt to kill himself.
“Well... it seems he lacks enough virtue to find the light yet,” Jun said darkly, then summoned his divine power to heal the man’s injuries in an instant.
“...N-Nooo!”
“Don’t worry. I will help you regain your purity and find the light one day.”
“...Demon! You demon! You demon!”
“...Hm.” Jun’s kind smile didn’t disappear despite the insults, and he quietly picked up one of the awls. “Ah! You’re here.” When he spotted me, he quickly shoved a gag in the man’s mouth.
“Mm—mmp—!”
“...Did you learn anything?”
“Unfortunately, still not enough. Only that there are more troops on standby at their main base than we expected.”
“They have more troops? How many?”
“According to this man, about twice as many as we thought.”
“What? Twice?” That was kind of a problem. “Why didn’t the others tell us about that? Did they lie?”
“No. They didn’t seem like the kind of people who would sacrifice their lives for loyalty. It’s just... they truly believed they had the right numbers.”
Hmm, that makes sense.
“But by that logic, it’s possible this guy has it wrong and the others are right.”

“Yes, that’s right. I can’t deny that. But... this fellow only figured it out after receiving the call. Normally, routine transmissions are sent from the main base, so he realized that if the Dragon Slayer is there, there’s a high probability his unit is there as well. What are you going to do? I’ll continue to dig up information for now, but if the enemy has twice as many forces as we expected, the likelihood of our mission failing increases as well.”
“And even if we do succeed, we’ll take more damage.”
“...Yes, that’s right.”
Hm, then what should we do? Stick with the original plan no matter how much ruin it results in?
I deliberated for a moment before making a decision. “Jun, stop the interrogation for now and gather the other leaders.”
“You’re going to hold a meeting?”
“Yes.”
As the saying went, two heads were better than one. You never knew if someone else might have a good idea.
We’d held countless leadership meetings over the course of this expedition. As soon as the information Jun obtained through his interrogation was relayed, I was immediately bombarded with opinions.
“It’s hard to say their forces have doubled. Even the Dragon Slayer’s squadron is only a small to medium clan, right?” said Kaislan.
“If you look at it in terms of just numbers, it’s about twenty additional men, but we shouldn’t underestimate them,” Akurava warned. “After all, there’s also only thirty of us.”
“Yes. Unlike the small fish we ran into in this area, it’s likely each member of his squadron is an elite,” said Jun.
“So, you want to abandon the mission?” Kaislan demanded.
“No one said that. I’m saying we should consider alternative strategies. I’m sure that’s why Mr. Schuitz called us here,” said Akurava.
When my name was invoked as commander of this expedition, Kaislan quieted down. Regardless of time and circumstance, the authority of the powerful was always respected.

“Anyway, at this rate, the damage we’ll suffer will be significant even if we succeed in the mission. Does anyone have a good plan?” I asked candidly, and various ideas were immediately thrown around.
“Why don’t we hide out nearby and gradually whittle down their numbers?” suggested Kaislan.
“No. If we do that, we won’t be able to meet up with the main unit at the scheduled time,” said Akurava.

“Besides, by that point, the enemy will realize what’s going on, no matter how oblivious they are. We’ll lose the advantage of an ambush and it might get even harder to pull this mission off since the enemy will have time to prepare for our arrival,” said Calla.
“Then Calla, do you have a better idea?” asked Kaislan.
“...Why don’t we infiltrate their base? If we use that man who’s under interrogation to go undercover, we might be able to pull it off.”
“But the moment he screws up, everyone will be dead, and the mission will fail as well. It’s too risky. It would be better to...”

From ambushing to infiltration to baiting to assassination, there were several suggestions. Not a single one was good enough to garner unanimous support, but humanity’s whole thing was collective intelligence.
“Luring some of the enemies’ forces away and splitting up their troops would be best,” said Akurava.
“If we use the enemy’s message stone, that’ll be a piece of cake.”
In the end, we put our heads together and came up with a plan that everyone could agree on. The group soon split on the execution, though.
“I think it would be smart to lure out the Dragon Slayer and attack him first. We can target the main base after that,” said Akurava.
“No, we have to lure the troops out, but then we should attack the base first. That’s our mission.”
Should we deal with the Dragon Slayer first? Or should we prioritize our mission? Both had pros and cons. If we went with the former and succeeded, we could kill two birds with one stone.

“Akurava, this is not the time to get hung up on war achievements,” Kaislan said. “Do you think these people will be like the ones we’ve run into so far? That they’ll let us defeat them without calling for backup? Even if they die in the process, they will definitely make our presence known.”
“Besides, there’s no guarantee the ambush will be successful. If they’re able to maintain their composure and fight us on equal ground, we’ll take even worse damage,” said Calla.
“Yes, that’s what I was trying to say! Then, even if we win, everyone will be exhausted. How will we be able to attack the main base in that state?” asked Kaislan.

If things went wrong with Akurava’s Dragon Slayer plan, the mission itself would fail. But in the case of the other option—attacking the base while the troops were gone—at least we’d have carried out the mission.
“Now, now, everyone, calm yourselves. This is for Schuitz to decide, after all.” Jun stepped in as things were getting tense, and all eyes immediately turned to me.
Ha, what to choose.

For the first time in a long time, this genuinely wasn’t an easy decision. Of course, I knew in my head that choosing the latter was the right thing to do. If it weren’t for the existence of the Dragon Slayer, I would’ve chosen it without any hesitation.
Tap, tap.
As I subconsciously tapped my fingers on my knee, the team leaders gulped.
“Looks like Schuitz has made his decision.”
“He always does that when he’s made up his mind.”
Uh... I have a tell like that?

This was the first I heard of it, but I didn’t have time to worry about it right now. I announced my decision. “We will focus on the mission.” After all, we didn’t have time to pursue both the mission and the Dragon Slayer.
Kaislan rejoiced. “Good idea! If the mission is successful, the palace will grant us a generous reward anyway!”
“A reward, huh?” I chuckled.
Did she sense something off in that laugh? “Schuitz,” Akurava said cautiously, “can we hear your reasoning? I thought you would be bolder than that.”

She wasn’t wrong. If I were alone, I would have chosen to go after the Dragon Slayer. “Because your lives depend on my decision. One less battle means that the number of people who survive will be greater.” That’s why I had abandoned my greed. That was all there was to my decision. “Now, is that enough of an answer?”
“...Yes, quite enough.” Akurava nodded compliantly and I ditched the last of my regrets.
The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos.
It didn’t have to be today. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t disappointed, but...
“We will meet again, dragon man.”
The vow I made that day would definitely come true.

chapters.title: Chapter 409: Dilemma (1)
paragraphs: Luring the Dragon Slayer and his subordinates away was easy. After all, the scariest call was the kind that came from inside the house, right? We made Lighty, the adventurer from Noark who Jun had helped find the light, give them false information. They fell for the bait instantly.
“...There are about thirty royal adventurers?”
“Yes! I think they came over from Ice Rock!”
“You said you were secretly tailing them, right? Keep doing that until I arrive.”
“Yes sir!”
Haha, fooled again, you moron?

I noticed this in the Labyrinth of Larcaz as well, but in some ways, this guy was naïve. If he had given up on Restrained Wish and refused to give me the time I asked for, he wouldn’t have found himself in that position and had his sword taken away back then.
“Okay, let’s move.”
After luring away the Dragon Slayer, we headed south of the Dragon Pit. There was no need to worry about our paths crossing because we had Lighty.
“Current location?”
“Western region of the Dragon Pit.”
“Looks like you’re continuing to move west. Are they trying to get to Iron Falls?”
“Based on the direction they’re traveling now, it seems so!”
“Okay. We’ll head that way too. If they change course, contact me right away.”
“Yes sir!”
At this rate, we would reach the enemy base by the time he arrived in Iron Falls. Even if he got a call for backup and tried to hastily return, we would be long gone.
“Group of Noarks ahead.”
“Halt. We’ll hide here until they pass by.”

We continued our forced march for two days with minimal contact with either the enemy or monsters and a vast wilderness finally appeared before us. The flora limited our field of vision, so it was hard to see too far inside. Anyway, that wasn’t the important thing.
“We’re finally in Gray Field.”

Gray Field was the area that served as a midpoint between the Dragon’s Mountains at the center of the continent and the Dragon Pit in the northernmost region. It was also the place where Noark’s spawn point was located, the one that allowed them direct access to the seventh floor.
“It’s quieter than I expected. I thought there would be more people wandering around the base.”
“That means the main unit is keeping them busy.”

The plan this mission hinged on was a kind of diversionary operation. While the royal army entered the Dark Continent through the standard route and engaged in combat with Noark’s main unit on the border of the Dragon’s Mountains, we’d hit them from behind.
“From now on, we’ll move as stealthily as possible, even if that means reducing our speed.”
“I will instruct the scouts to widen their distance from the main unit. So that we can detect the enemy’s presence from farther away.”
“Yes, I’ll leave the details of our formation to you.”

We’d been moving with more caution since entering Gray Field but even so, combat continued to occur. That was because the labyrinth was full of monsters. Even if we could avoid people, we couldn’t avoid them.
[You have defeated a Void Ant. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Dark Crystal. EXP +6]
[You have defeated a Mynum. EXP +5]
[You have defeated a Hell Ghoul. EXP +4]
[You have defeated a Jambet...」
Various monsters crawled out of the wide-open cracks, which were reminiscent of a rice field during a drought. Among them were rank-three monsters.
“It’s a Vol-Herchan!”
This monster was one of the ones that made it to the final version of my Shield Barbarian skill tree. Of course, the battle itself wasn’t all that hard.
“What are you all doing? First time fighting one? Spread out first!”
“Warriors, just block it! The wizards will deal the final blow, anyway!”
In Ice Rock, we had to take down three rank-three monsters at a time. This was just one. Plus, our stomachs were even full now.
Boom!
It held out for as long as you’d expect from a monster with one of the highest levels of defense in the game, but the Vol-Herchan eventually collapsed and turned into flecks of light.
[You have defeated a Vol-Herchan. EXP +7]
There was no essence but I wasn’t particularly disappointed about it. After all, I already had this guy’s essence.
It is a bit ironic, though.
I never expected I’d end up getting this guy’s essence before ever killing one. Unlike the steady progress I used to make in the game, in real life, the order I was completing my build was arbitrary.
Is this a snowball effect from getting my hands on an Ogre essence in the early stages?

The thought came to mind but when I actually thought about it, the place where all of this abnormal growth started had to be the Corpse Golem. If that essence hadn’t appeared, I wouldn’t have been able to kill the Vampire Duke Cambormere.
“Schuitz, we’ve received word that the scouts have discovered their main base,” said Kaislan.

After traveling through Gray Field for another day, we finally arrived near our destination. There was a giant tower-shaped structure standing there and about a hundred adventurers protecting it, so we were definitely at the right spot.
“...Their numbers are smaller than I expected.”
“It looks like Regal Vagos took more troops to catch us than we thought,” said Akurava.
“Really? That would be great for us, but since we don’t know for sure if that’s true, we’ll start with information gathering.”
“Then I’ll send the scouts out again,” said Kaislan.
“What should we do about the rest of the squad members?” asked Akurava.
“We’re going to have to fight soon so tell them to rest and recover their energy as much as possible.”
“What about Destruction of Evil?”
“Tell them not to use it, since the enemy might spot us if we do. We can’t lose everything to avoid a little inconvenience. If there are any monsters, tell them to kill them as quietly as possible.”
“Will do.”

While the scouts, a.k.a the people with the highest Agility and best stealth skills in our group, went off to explore our surroundings, the rest hid near the bottom of the cliff to recover their energy. As did I.
“You look tired.” As I rested my back against the wall, Amelia came up and handed me a piece of jerky.
Jeez, you didn’t give me a single one in Ice Rock. Now you have extra?
I accepted it and was just starting to gnaw on it when Amelia said something ominous. “Schuitz, things are going way too smoothly.”
“God damn it...”
You finally said it.
I’d often heard that you speak things into existence, which was why I’d only been thinking about it in the privacy of my own mind.
I sighed and returned my attention to Amelia. “That wasn’t directed at you, don’t worry. So, what were you trying to say? Did you notice something strange?”
“No, but...” Amelia trailed off at my question. It seemed she didn’t have any basis for her suspicions, either.
“Don’t worry, things aren’t going too smoothly. We just went through all the hard work in advance already.”
“Went through it in advance?”
“We went through all kinds of things crossing Ice Rock, right? There was even a traitorous bastard in our midst.”
“That’s... true. Sorry. Forget about what I said.”
It was too late for that since she had already made me extremely nervous, but I didn’t let it show. I kept my thoughts internal.
A hundred people, huh?
Against a group of that size, we could accomplish the mission successfully and without difficulty. The scouts only saw the base from a distance, but there didn’t seem to be any big names there.
This is probably because they didn’t expect the enemy to come at them from behind.

Noark’s main unit was dedicating all its energy to keeping the royal army from crossing the mountain. Of course, since it was a key base, they did leave some troops on standby with the Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos, as their commander.
But that guy just led some of the troops out.
It was currently an empty house.
There are no Hanses around, either.
Now, the only problem was whether the scouts would throw us a curveball.
“Schuitz, the scouts have returned.”
“What did they say?”
“They say there’s no one around within a three-mile radius.”

This confirmed there was nothing of note in the surrounding area to worry about. I was worried they might have set up some traps because things were going too smoothly, but I soon shook off the ominous feeling.
“Tell those who went out that they did a good job and let them rest. Though, they won’t be able to rest for long.”
“...Are we mobilizing?”
“Yes, get everyone ready.”
It was time to end this long expedition.

I was standing still in the dark forest. Although I couldn’t confirm with the naked eye in the darkness of the labyrinth, Noark’s base was beyond it. I waited in silence for the right moment with the members of my squadron, ready to run out at any time.
Boom, boom, boom, boom!
Before long, a loud noise thundered through the darkness. Anyone with adventuring experience would recognize this sound as the footsteps of a large monster.
“D-Demons!”
“Everyone get out here!”
The quiet beyond the darkness started to get noisy. Although I couldn’t see them with my own eyes, I could picture each one of their expressions.
“Fuck, what the hell is with these numbers?!”
Bewilderment.
“Ugh, damn our luck. What are you all doing? Take out your weapons!”
Annoyance.
“How did all these monsters flock over here?”
Suspicion.
“Snap out of it! It’s the enemy! Someone led these things here!”
Of course, among them, some even had the correct answer. Was it because they were from Noark, where they studied all kinds of looting strategies? They were quick.

It of course wasn’t a coincidence that hordes of monsters were pouring in from all directions. After confirming no one was within a three-mile radius, I sent the scouts to round up all the monsters nearby. Now that the aggro had passed onto Noark’s fighters, the scouts should have turned on stealth to return.
“What?”
“The enemy...?”
“Damn it, is it the people Vagos was talking about?”
“Hurry up and request support!”
Who do you think you’re calling for support? It’s going to be over by the time they get here, anyway.
“Kaislan.”
When I said his name, Kaislan lifted a flag with the royal family’s coat of arms and shouted, “Shoot!”
At that moment, the wizards, archers, and special ability users who had finished casting fired their finishers at once.
Kabooom!

The attack was made in the middle of a monster invasion. One section of the enemy’s formation was immediately wiped out, creating a hole, and the clever monsters didn’t miss their opportunity to strike.
“Damn it, where are they?! Where are you?!”
“Aaagh!” Monsters crossed the collapsed front line and attacked their middle.
“Block that area first!” The enemy scrambled to regroup but there was no way we would sit by and watch that happen.
“Kaislan, one more time.”
We dedicated all our firepower to long-range bombardment as soon as everyone was done casting, and the enemy figured out our location soon after.
“That way!”
“The bastards are over there!”
Even if you know that, what are you going to do? You’re too busy fighting monsters, anyway.
Kwaaang! Bang! Whiiiiiip!
Long-range artillery fire continued like that for a while, and in the middle of it all, the message stone I kept on me vibrated.
Jiiiiiing!
It was obvious who was calling. The entire way here, only one person had called on this message stone.
Click.
I had nothing else to do right now other than watch so I accepted the call.
“You! Where are you right now?!”
The voice on the other end unleashed its anger on me as soon as the connection was made. Come to think of it, we told him to head to the edge of the continent during the last call.
“I’m at the spot you mentioned and no one’s here! There are also reports that a battle is taking place at the Eye of the Sky.”
The Eye of the Sky was the name given to the mana wave emitter that served as Noark’s transmission tower.
Welp, I guess the news already reached him.
I could see why the palace was so adamant about destroying the Eye of the Sky. More than a few of the losses they suffered could be attributed to Noark’s extensive communication network.
“Are you ignoring me right now? Answer me! Where are you right now?”
There was no need to lie anymore, so I answered honestly. “Me? In your front yard.”

Provocation, when appropriately applied, was undoubtedly a valid war tactic. I waited for an entertaining reaction but the caller was surprisingly quiet for a long while. The words that crackled through the stone as he checked if I disconnected weren’t particularly interesting either.
“...Who are you?”
Jeez, cat got your tongue? No need to act all high and mighty.
“Why, are you going to come find me?”
“...So this was your plan from the start.”
“Why are you stating the obvious? Hey, I’m busy right now so I’ll see you later. Get a nice view of the ocean while you’re there.”

“Whoever you are, don’t even think about dying a peaceful death. Even death won’t be able to save you.” His voice was full of murderous intent but I just picked my ears and tuned it out. Even death can’t save me? He’d already used that line on me before.
“All right, do your best.”
“What? Does this sound like a joke to you? I will make sure to—”
It was time to move on to the next phase so I hung up.
At that moment, a report came in from Akurava. “Schuitz, the monsters are almost all taken care of!” The enemies had fought desperately and already killed most of the monsters.
“Assault formation!”
“All lines forward!”
Before the enemy could regroup, we stormed the battlefield.
“Attack!”
Veteran warriors were positioned in the forefront of the formation. Noark created a wall of warriors to stop us—a basic shield wall used in battles between large troops.
“Stop them!”
“Die!”
The warriors at the forefront clashed with each other and a full-scale power struggle began.
“Woahhh!”
The victor of that struggle was, of course, us. Not only was the average rank of our warriors higher than theirs, but more importantly, their side had no priests.
[Niaro Campbell has cast Healing Wave.]
[Benjamin Orman has cast Moonlight of Regeneration.]
How could they stop our reckless charge when we weren’t even worried about the risk of injury?
“We’re through!”

The warriors broke through their front line with the force of one hundred soldiers, and our expeditionary force quickly plowed into that opening. Although their formation wasn’t completely full of holes, the center was.
“Shield wall!”
We changed our formation to a circular all-around defense.
“Maintain formation as we move!”
Now the tables had turned and we were dealing with enemy troops coming at us from all directions as we made our way to the center. That was because our objective was not a massacre, but a strike.
“Th-the enemy is headed toward the Eye of the Sky!”
“Stop them!”

Realizing what our objective was, the enemy attacked us even more aggressively. It wasn’t enough to break the hard-won, unified line we’d built by overcoming Ice Rock together. Plus we had a lot of priests backing us up.
“Halt!”

As we moved and dealt with our enemies, we soon arrived in front of the Eye of the Sky. We stood with our backs toward it and desperately held position. There was something we had to do before we destroyed this thing.
Just then, Akurava shouted for me. “Schuitz! Come this way, quick! Hurry! There’s a problem!”
What? A problem?
“Gregson. Take this side.”
“Yup, leave it to me!”

I left my position to the warrior next to me and headed to the rear. Akurava was standing in front of the Eye of the Sky we were surrounding, waiting for me with obvious unease written all over her face.
“What is it?”
“I-I entered the communication coordinates we were given and tried contacting the main unit several times, but I can’t reach them!”
Hmm, that’s kind of a huge problem, actually.

chapters.title: Chapter 410: Dilemma (2)
paragraphs: As the number of attempts to establish a connection with the main unit increased, an ominous feeling threatened to swallow me whole.
“Again.”
“Okay...”
There was nothing else I could do except keep trying. But no matter how many times we tried to contact them, no connection could be made with the main unit.
...What the hell is going on?
The original plan for this expedition was as follows:
1. Ambush and infiltrate Noark’s base.
2. Use the Eye of the Sky to contact the main unit located in the Dragon’s Mountains.
3. After destroying the tower and escaping, join up with the main unit, which will come to meet us.
The key to the strike plan’s success was the main unit temporarily mustering the strength needed to penetrate Noark’s front lines and meet us at the rendezvous point to retreat.
“It didn’t go through.”
We couldn’t contact the main unit, which was the most important part of this plan.
Did they... abandon us?

The worst-case scenario came to mind but I quickly shook my head. What, throw away troops like us after using us once? The palace wouldn’t do such a thing. It made sense to assume something had gone wrong at the front lines. But even in the worst-case scenario, there was only one thing for me to do—the same thing I had done since the day I woke up in this body.
Kwaaang!
Survive.
“Captain! How long do we have to hold out?”
Before making a decision, I thought it through one last time.
“Priest Campbell can’t go on for much longer!”

Because we no longer had time, I had to choose the best possible move we could pull off with our limited resources. What would up our chances of survival the most? It didn’t take me long to make a decision, although I had no way of knowing if it was the best one.
Tap, tap.
Okay, let’s go with this for now. It’s not like I can think of a better way, anyway.
“Akurava.”
“I’m listening.”
“Stop trying to input coordinates for this transmission entirely.” So far, we had only attempted to make contact through a designated phone number.
“I’m sorry? But then our message will be broadcast to the entire region without exception...?”
“That’s what I want.” There was no point leaving a missed call for someone who wouldn’t even answer, right?

“...Okay.” Akurava seemed to understand exactly what I meant. She thought about it for a moment but ultimately agreed. “It’s done. I’ve also maximized the bandwidth.” Akurava then handed me the message stone.
Click.

I carefully pressed the button on its surface. I was a bit nervous. It was currently set to what was essentially radio transmission mode. Friend or foe, anyone in the continent with their message stone turned on would receive this transmission.
But so what?
“Listen, everyone.”
“Listen, everyone.”

The sound transmitted through the active message stones nearby all at once like an echo. This was all the main unit’s fault for not picking up the call. I didn’t know what was keeping them so busy, but what else could a barbarian do when the main unit wasn’t listening?
“The Eye of the Sky has been destroyed.”
“The Eye of the Sky has been destroyed.”
I’d shout it directly into their ears.
It was a barren plot of land with dull colors and a shattered Eye of the Sky sitting in its center.
Slide.
The man took off his cloak, revealing the face hidden beneath his hood. His skin was grotesque like acid had been poured onto it.

“...How did this happen?” When the man with a monstrous appearance looked around, those whose eyes he tried to catch were busy looking down. “You.” The man reached out his hand and grabbed the nearest adventurer by the neck.
“P-Please don’t kill me! S-Sir!”
“If you want to live, tell me what happened here right now.”
“I-I’ll tell you...! Everything! Without hiding a single detail!”
When the strangled adventurer cried out desperately, Regal Vagos relaxed his grip. Punishment could wait until after he figured out what happened.
“I repeat: the Eye of the Sky has been destroyed. We will now head to the rendezvous point.”
The message stones stopped working after that transmission so Vagos wasn’t able to learn what exactly happened as he and his troops retreated.

The longer the man in his grip went on, the more his anger surged like a tidal wave. “To summarize: the bastards openly invaded our base and destroyed the Eye of the Sky, then used a Multi Teleportation spell to escape, and you guys did nothing?”
“W-Well... that’s because you mobilized the troops and left so there weren’t many—”
“Are you saying this is my fault?”
Choke!
“N-No! The enemies brought monsters with them like cowards...! I-I meant that we weren’t... strong enough!”
“...You piece of trash.”
When Vagos gripped tighter, the frightened adventurer blurted out a name. “T-Titana Akurava!”
“Titana Akurava...?” This was a woman he knew. Around the time he joined Orcules, she was one of the most renowned adventurers of the era. “That old lady was here?”

“N-Not only her! G-Golden Hawk James Calla! White Sword Kaislan! There were so many other famous adventurers! Please have mercy...!” Sensing his impending doom, the adventurer pled for salvation in a trembling tone.
Just then, a man in the distance slowly walked forward. “Vagos, please stop. There was nothing they could do.”

Kayle Elbad Zenegger was the advisor of the squadron Vagos led. When they first heard that an expeditionary force from the palace had infiltrated Ice Rock, he was also the one who suggested they not do anything rash and protect the tower. Was that why? On the one hand, Vagos could admit he should have listened to this guy, but on the other, he felt repulsed by the thought.
“Kayle, back off. This is a well-deserved punishment.”
“Then why that man? Everyone here shares the blame for not protecting this place. This isn’t fair.”
“Then I’ll just punish everyone here.”

The adventurers flinched at those words. The advisor sighed and pulled out his trump card. “The commander won’t stay quiet if you do that.” By ‘commander,’ he meant the head of Orcules: the Traitor, Ricardo Lüchenprague.
“You son of a bitch...!” Vagos got angry and grabbed his advisor by the collar, but that was all. Even he couldn’t ignore the weight of that name.
“Since something of this scale has happened, the commander will soon return from the front lines to take stock of the situation. Let’s not do anything rash and wait for now.”
“...Tsk.” Eventually, Vagos’s anger cooled. He didn’t want to cause any more trouble by ignoring his advisor’s advice again. However, the man in his grip kept talking and soon said something strange.
“Blood Spirit’s Man? Riehen Schuitz?”
“Y-Yes! I’m sure of it. He was leading the expedition. I clearly heard them call him Schuitz! More importantly, he used Giantization!”
Vagos had regained his composure and was investigating the man who deceived him when he flinched. As soon as he heard the word Giantization, he experienced an inexplicable sense of déjà vu.
“Kayle!”
“What is it?”
“Give me the message stone.”
The advisor didn’t even question his orders. He took out a message stone, and Vagos snatched it from his hand.
Click.
He pressed the button and played a recording.
“Me? In your front yard... Why, are you going to come find me...? All right, do your best.”
Just the sound of the voice made his hands ball up into tight fists. At the same time, he had the strange feeling he had heard it somewhere before.
Click, click, click.
Vagos played the recording over and over again and soon burst into laughter. “...No wonder it sounded familiar.” Eventually, he realized exactly who the owner of that voice was.
“I repeat: the Eye of the Sky has been destroyed. We will now head to the rendezvous point.”

This was the enemy he’d been unable to remember for over three years before recovering his health and the memories he’d lost thanks to Amelia Rainwales’s betrayal—the thief who had stolen his precious sword, which he had acquired at great personal cost. Up to this point, he had thought the man dead.
“He was alive?”

The palace probably knew his true identity. They may have been the ones to fake his death in the first place. Otherwise, there was no way they would have appointed a man with a reputation like “Blood Spirit’s Man” as the leader of an expedition team that included big names like Akurava.
“Bjorn Yandel.” Recalling the rage he’d experienced that day, Vagos quietly uttered the name and stood up. “Kayle! Gather all the troops! We’re going to track down the bastards who ran away!”
“But the commander hasn’t arrived yet—”
“It’s fine. I’ll take full responsibility.”
It was time to meet again.

Deadwood was an area located to the west of the Dragon’s Mountains. It was Noark’s territory and they had never once allowed the royal army to invade it. It was also our agreed-upon rendezvous point with the palace. We had been lying there in wait with bated breath, believing there was no way they hadn’t heard our message and that they’d definitely come to our rescue.
We continued to pass the time anxiously curled up on the giant branches of lifeless trees. It’d been three days.
“If the main unit mobilized immediately after receiving our message, they should have arrived yesterday.”
“Why... aren’t they coming?!”
“Sir Kaislan, lower your voice. We don’t have the resources needed to use Voice Control magic anymore.”

Up until yesterday, these people had been encouraging each other, assuring their neighbors that the main unit would arrive soon, but the tension was slowly mounting. That was only natural. The first death had occurred this morning.
Philip Aintropi.

He was an adventurer who had belonged to Melend Kaislan’s team, a navigator. This man—who had mainly learned skills that were helpful for sailing like Ocean Current Control, Lightweight, and Oversupply—died during the battle this morning. Although they had plenty of mana, our stealth spells had temporarily lifted when our wizards ran out of stamina. Noark was searching below and noticed us. During a long, drawn-out battle, he took a headshot and died instantly. That had been several hours ago.
“Schuitz, this place is no longer safe,” said Akurava.

The crew’s anxiety was reaching its peak, and rightfully so. Noark would have also noticed the absence of the people who died this morning by now. The more time passed, the more their search of this area would intensify. The number of enemies walking around below us had already increased significantly.
“You have to make a call,” she pressed.
“Wait, a call? What do you mean?” asked Kaislan.
“We can’t stay here forever. If the rescue team doesn’t come, it’d be best to abandon this place.”
“...W-What are you talking about?! Are you saying the palace abandoned us?”
“I didn’t say that. But... we couldn’t contact them and... if they’re in trouble as well, we need to be proactive.”
“You have a point, but I’m against it. How far will we be able to get when everyone is so exhausted? If we’re discovered along the way, we’ll be annihilated.”
“So, what? You want to wait? Until when? The wizards will run out of mana in two days. Then we’ll end up annihilated anyway.”
As was always the case in emergencies, opinions were divided.
Sigh...
Even without Akurava’s questioning, I already knew. It was now time to make a decision one way or another.
I’m going to lose it.
There were a total of three choices I could make. First, lie in wait here. In the best-case scenario, we would all be rescued unharmed.
But on the other hand, in the worst possible outcome... We’ll die in vain.

Second, don’t wait and travel directly to the royal army’s territory. Deadwood was much less important than the Dragon’s Mountains so the front lines were thin and the troops were few. That was why we chose it as our rendezvous point. It wasn’t blind optimism.
It’d still be tough to pull off with less than thirty people, though.
It’d be a miracle if even 10 percent of us made it out alive. The worst-case scenario for this one would be the same as the first.
Then I guess we have no choice but to go somewhere else.

The third option was a kind of survival strategy. As the base Noark had far from the front line was likely empty at this point, if we hid there instead, we might be able to hold out until the labyrinth closed.
Since the Eye of the Sky has been destroyed, information on us won’t have spread far.

This option exposed us to risk for the longest amount of time, so it was obvious we’d be hit with numerous curveballs. Even if we made the best possible moves in every situation we ended up in along the way, countless sacrifices would follow.
Whichever one we choose, the worst outcome is total annihilation.
As my thoughts reached that low point, I couldn’t help but laugh. It suddenly hit me.

If the worst-case scenario is a massacre anyway... Isn’t it smarter to choose the first option, where the best-case scenario is that everyone survives? Since this was the palace’s fault, we can foist the responsibility for this off on them too.
“...Yeah right.”
“If we leave and the main unit arrives, would you be willing to take responsibility for—huh? What did you just say?”
I ignored Kaislan’s question and spoke. Though I may not have been sure of my choice...
Tap, tap.
Someone had to make a decision.
“Everyone, get ready, we’re getting out of here.”
“A-Are you saying you aren’t going to wait for the main unit?” asked Kaislan.
“Yes, we’ve already been stood up long enough. Ah, and don’t worry.” I smirked at Kaislan. “I’ll take full responsibility.”

chapters.title: Chapter 411: Dilemma (3)
paragraphs: When a hopeless situation arose, most people tried to think of the positives first. Do this, and do that, and if you handle this, then everything might work out. Overwhelmed by countless what-ifs, they became blinded by the slim possibility that things might be okay and missed the golden opportunity to improve their situation. From several years to even decades, all of us may have been working in the labyrinth for a long time, but the members of this expedition were only human.
“...We’re leaving?”
As soon as my decision was announced to the crew, chaos descended.
“That’s an impulsive decision!”
“Sh-shouldn’t we wait here some more? It could turn out that something went wrong on the army’s end and they’re just a little late.”
“That’s right! There are enemies all over the place, how far could we possibly go?!”

Dissent spread quickly like an infectious disease. That was only natural because staying was the most hopeful of all our options. If the rescue team came, everyone would be able to return home alive. This nightmare would be over, and all that remained would be to return to the city and be happy. The hardships we experienced throughout this journey would be reduced to stories told over drinks.
That’s a dangerous thought.

If there was one thing I knew, it was that the situation wasn’t that hopeless yet. Real despair would come when that golden window of opportunity disappeared and even the slightest glimmer of hope was trampled underfoot. When that time came, we wouldn’t be able to do anything even if we wanted to. That was why this was the only time to do it.

“What are you all saying? Do you all have brain damage or something?” I used strong wording that was sure to attract backlash. It was a method of shock therapy. “There was a rat in Ice Rock. When we arrived at Eye of the Sky, no matter how many times we tried, we couldn’t get in touch with the royal army. And what about now? It’s been three days with no news. ‘A little late?’ ‘The rescue team is coming?’ Don’t make me laugh. If they were, there’s no way this place would still be crawling with Noark soldiers. They would have been sent to the front line to stop the royal army a long time ago.” I took a breath and continued. “Everyone, listen carefully. We were abandoned.”
I didn’t really think that was the case, but I knew that if I didn’t say that, I wouldn’t be able to destroy the vain hope they were harboring.
“W-Why would the palace abandon us?!”

I didn’t know, either. Perhaps something dire did come up and they couldn’t come. I actually thought that was far more likely than them leaving us here on purpose. But so what? Whatever their circumstances, that didn’t change the situation we were in.
“If we weren’t abandoned, why haven’t they come yet?”
“That’s...” The squad member gritted her teeth. “So you want us to go somewhere else?”
“Yes.”
“When everyone is this exhausted? You think that will work? Everyone will—!”

“What difference would waiting here make?!” As our voices grew louder, the wizards used their little remaining mana to cast a team communication spell, so I shouted to my heart’s content. “Open your eyes, everyone! Whatever the reason, that doesn’t change the fact that they aren’t coming to save us!”

The crew fell silent at my shout. They could argue if they wanted to, but deep down, everyone secretly felt that what I was saying could be true. If it weren’t for those doubts, they wouldn’t have been so anxious in the first place.
I opened my mouth and broke the silence. “I don’t plan on dying here. Do you feel differently?”
It was one of Kaislan’s teammates who answered that question. “...Who wants to die?”

“That’s that, then. Follow me. Kill the enemy and protect your comrades. At least that’s more worthwhile than waiting to die here.” I looked around at the squadron as they sat there on the thick branches.

Judging by the looks on their faces, it didn’t seem my speech had resonated with them much. Well, that made sense if you thought about it. Riehen Schuitz was a mysterious adventurer whose name and face had been unknown until he joined this expedition. Though I may have shown them various sides of myself throughout our quest, how trustworthy could I be in a situation like this? They naturally looked to their team leaders.

The first to step forward was Jun. He looked at me with such excessive respect that it seemed he was deliberately trying to help me out. “Let us head where the light leads. Team Four will walk the path of hardship you’ve chosen.”

Next was Kaislan. “The kingdom of Rafdonia has appointed Riehen Schuitz as the leader of this expedition. Doubting his judgment and presenting differing opinions could be interpreted as treason against the king.” Although it was lengthy, his speech could be summed up in one sentence. “Team Five will follow your orders.” Was he trying to lend me credibility like Jun? Kaislan ceremoniously went down on one knee despite the uncomfortable branch he was on. This was kind of a surprise. He’d looked so disapproving during the leadership meeting earlier.

Just then, Akurava spoke up. “Team Two thinks differently. It’s not because we have blind faith or because we’re afraid of the kingdom’s martial law. We just agree with his opinion. It seems difficult to believe the royal army will come to save us.”
“So?”
Akurava laughed at my prodding. “Team Two will follow you too.”
Okay, then just one team left: Team Three, led by James Calla, the deputy commander of the Sawtooth Clan.

When all eyes turned to him, Calla looked flustered. “I...” It seemed the previous performances of the team leaders had set the bar a bit high, but I guessed he figured those things didn’t suit him. “What they said. It’s not like an objection from me will change anything. Ordinary people like me need to follow the trends.” Although a bit boring, those words were very like him. The sincerity mixed into his joking tone seemed to have gotten through to the other crew members too.
“...It’s already set in stone, huh.”
“Well, what do they want us to say when they’ve already decided?”
“Hahaha, I never liked the look of this from the start. This isn’t the first time the palace hasn’t done its job. We have to find a way to survive on our own.”
“I will hold the palace firmly responsible for this matter. But for that to happen, we need to get back alive first.”
I looked around at the muttering members of my squadron and clenched my fists.
Squeeze.
Okay, let’s give it a try.
“The number of troops patrolling the area has increased. Looks like they’ve noticed we killed the others... What do we do?”
What else was there to do? The plan from here on out was simple. “We’re going to use Mass Teleportation.”
First, use a Mass Teleport spell to escape from the center of enemy territory. Well, this part of the plan wasn’t without its issues, though.
“If we use a spell as large as that, the wizards will be out of mana for a while. And our location will also be discovered.”

Noark’s scouts would no doubt follow the traces of mana to track us down, but we had no other choice. “We have to take on that risk. Even if we try to move discreetly, there’s no way we won’t get caught by the enemy with this many people.”
“That’s true...”
“Now that the Eye of the Sky has been destroyed, they won’t be able to communicate as well. It’s best to widen the distance with Mass Teleportation.”
The team leaders clearly had some concerns about my decision but they did not voice them.
Okay, that’s settled.
“What happens next?”
The plan from here was also very simple. “Whether the people tracking us catch up or not, we’ll go north.” Our destination was the northern hemisphere of the Dark Continent.
“...Not the south, where our allies are?”
“Yes.”
There was only one reason why I chose the north instead of the south. The scouts would only be able to track where we teleported to. They’d have no way of knowing where we went next.
“You’re going to trick the enemy into thinking we went south. If they send their troops south, the north will be all the more empty.”
“That’s right. We’re going to hide right under their noses until the day the labyrinth closes.”
“Understood. Did your advisor come up with this too?”
Jeez, they don’t believe I thought of it myself. Whatever, that doesn’t matter.
“Tell everyone to get ready. Once we start casting the spell, Noark will be on us like a pack of bloodhounds.”
“...Okay.”
I shared the strategy with the team leaders and they delivered the instructions to their teams. With this, we were prepared to execute the plan.
Dash.
We came down from the tree we were hiding in since we wouldn’t be able to hide ourselves while the Mass Teleportation spell was being cast, anyway.
“Stepping on land for the first time in three days.” While the sensation felt strange, the squadron’s five wizards immediately split up and began drawing magic circles on the floor.
Shaaaaaaaaa!

Two Mass Teleportation spells were required to transport twenty-eight people. As this required vast amounts of mana, someone with a decent ability to sense energy would soon notice something was out of the ordinary.
Hah, I just hope they notice a little late.
With our backs to the large tree, we fanned out in a protective semicircle to guard the wizards.

“Mister, someone’s coming. Very quickly,” Erwen, who had an acute energy sense herself, muttered in a low voice. After another moment, she added, “They spotted us and stopped. Now they’re hurrying backward.”
So, they’re trying to call for backup.
Whiiiiiip!
Before I could even order her to, Erwen fired an arrow into the dark.
“Did you kill them?”
“No. It hit a tree.”
“I see.”

Well, even if she got them, it would only have bought us a little more time. I licked my lips and shouted, “Everyone, prepare for battle!” There was no need to keep our mouths shut when we were caught anyway, right? Noark would soon flock here in a frenzy, and we’d hold out somehow until the Mass Teleportation was complete.
Slide.
While I had some time, I did one final check. “Coordinates! The coordinates you’ve input are incorrect!”

“Ah, sorry. I’ll fix it now!” Knowing the situation was more urgent than ever, the wizards drew the magic circles even faster. I was grateful for their hard work, but I’d be lying if I said I had no regrets.
...It would be so nice if that was a Portal spell.

Of course, I knew this couldn’t be helped. In the game, only an archmage who had reached rank one could use a Portal spell, and the cost of doing so was the caster’s life. Now, more than a hundred years later, the portals commonly used by wizards in the labyrinth were an improved version of the original. Or, to be more accurate, they were a downgraded version, an improved Portal that even rank-four wizards could use. Although this spell could only be used once in a lifetime, in exchange, you didn’t have to sacrifice your life for it.
But it’s impossible to use on the seventh floor or higher.
The improved portals had that huge drawback. That was why I was regretting something else.
I should’ve asked them to find a rank one wizard, whatever it took...

I did ask, actually, but I was rejected by the marquess. Rank-one wizards were very rare even in the Magic Tower, and there was only one affiliated with the palace. Even if the Eye of the Sky was destroyed and all members of our expedition returned alive, the loss of a rank-one wizard would be monumental. In their minds, it was better to abandon the entire rest of the expedition team.
Holy shit, is that it?

The thought came to mind but I shook my head. The premise was faulty to begin with. Weighing our lives against that of a rank-one wizard was silly. In the end, the final plan they’d come up with had been to send the main unit to rescue us. Of course, the rescue team would incur some losses in the process, but considering the reputation of each member of the expedition, the palace saw us as worth the sacrifice.
That’s why there has to be another reason why... I should stop thinking about this.

Why didn’t the rescue team come? It was a question I’d asked myself countless times over the past few days, but I decided not to worry about it anymore. We would find out if we got back alive, and if we didn’t, it didn’t matter anyway.
“They’re coming!”
Boom, boom!
We felt a faint vibration through the ground.
“Woahhh!”
“Die!”
As soon as the enemy emerged from the darkness, I cleared my head.
[You have cast Giantization.]
[You have used a transformation-type ability. Due to the effect of Evolving Shell, the amount of Soul Power consumed by the ability is reduced by half, and your highest stat increases by 1.5 times.]
Right now I had just one thing to worry about: surviving.

chapters.title: Chapter 412: Dilemma (4)
paragraphs: Enemies were coming at us from all sides and our squadron took up a defensive formation to block them.
“Kill them!”
“Stop them!”

It was like playing a tower defense game. There was a stark difference between those games and reality, though. Normally in a tower defense game, the enemies that flocked to you in droves only had close-combat abilities.
Shooot!
Arrows rained down on us.
“Revival Ascender!”
Kwaang!

Unluckily for us, we had to deal with black magic and various essence skills consisting of lightning, ice, fire, and all other kinds of attributes. Normally, long-range attacks like this would be blocked by wizards, but our wizards were using all of their remaining mana to complete Multi Teleportation. In the end, there was only one thing for us to do. To prevent these long-range attacks from hitting the glass-like, fragile bodies behind us, we had to endure the onslaught.
[You have been hit by Permeating Chill. The damage of the next Cold-type attack you take will be doubled, and Cold Resistance temporarily decreases in proportion to the amount of damage taken.]
We took Lightning damage that exceeded our Mana Resistance and Lightning Resistance thresholds.
[You have been hit by Penetrating Light.]
[You are now under the Paralysis (Intermediate) effect.]
Debuffs quickly accumulated. However, despite it all, I used my giantized body as a shield, serving as a wall to protect our rear guard.
Grit.
Just in case, I clenched my jaw and bit down on my tongue.
Kwaaang!
Then I used my body to block the attacks coming at us from straight ahead. It wasn’t just me, either—the entire vanguard was doing the same.
[Benjamin Orman has cast Moonlight of Purification. The Paralysis effect has been removed from all characters within range.]
[Niaro Campbell has cast Blessing of Light. The effectiveness of any healing effects used on characters within range has increased.]

Although support from the priests continued to come in, it wasn’t enough. They had simply acquired the right to use a sliver of divine power in exchange for their faith. Reviving the dead remained the domain of the gods.
“Might—!”
When we died, we didn’t die screaming.
“E-Everyone get back!” cried Might Million, the warrior from Team Two to the left of me.
Stab!
A black thorn flying toward us pierced his shield and went right through his heart.
“No!”
It was a perfectly clean death, with no countdown required. As if to make his fate clear to all onlookers, the divine light covering his body dispersed.
Shaaaaaaaaa!
Skills and abilities didn’t work on the dead.

“M-Might—!” An archer on the same team as the dead warrior ran forward and tried to pull the black thorn out of his body. It was a reckless and foolish thing to do. There was no way it’d come out so easily, and even if it did, he wouldn’t come back to life.
...A friend of his? I don’t know, but that’s not important.
“Emily, I’ll be back.”
“...What?”
I gave Amelia a heads-up and moved slightly out of formation to grab the archer by the neck. “Don’t be stupid and stay back.” Then I threw the archer toward Akurava in the rear.
Slump!
An angry shout rang out behind me. “...W-What are you—M-Might is—!”
“Might died. To save you guys.”

Might Million clearly saw the black thorn flying in. He could have avoided it. With his battle instincts, he definitely could have. But he chose instead to block it and protect his comrades because that was his role. Of course, he probably didn’t know things would turn out the way they did, either. He might have figured he could take a single hit. With how chaotic the battle was, I was sure it would have been difficult for him to recognize Black Thorn and realize it was a skill that ranked in the top tier of rank-two essences.
...Or maybe he knew and blocked it anyway.
Whatever the case, the truth of what Might thought was lost to us, probably forever.
“So stay back. I’ll take over this spot from here. Emily! Join Team Two!”
Since Team Two’s sole warrior was dead, I filled the void. I was pretty much in charge of a space that should have been occupied by two teams, but I felt more relieved about that than frustrated.
I’m glad I’m so big.
I debated using Transcendence while I was at it to make my body even bigger, but I stopped myself. I couldn’t just sit here and be a punching bag forever, right?
[You have cast Liability of Risk. Any damage received and reflected by Probabilistic Retaliation will be doubled.]
After testing it out a bit, I concluded I could survive double damage.

[By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in the skill is now unlocked. In exchange for the temporary deactivation of Probabilistic Retaliation’s Damage Immunity effect, the odds of activation have been set at 100%.]
As soon as I activated Transcendence, skeletons rose up behind me, making clattering sounds. “Gahhhcha!” They returned the various attacks I took back to their casters.
“W-What the hell?!”
“Gachabone! It’s the essence of Gachabone!”
“What? But that skill shouldn’t be this powerful!”
Confusion ensued as the attacks launched by their troops were countered.
Maybe I should’ve turned this on sooner.

I guessed the best defense really was a good offense. I had turned on Liability of Risk fully prepared to take a more painful beating, but instead the number of attacks decreased. Thankfully, that made it even easier for me to fill the hole in our formation by myself.
Okay, now we just have to complete the teleport...
“Get out of the way, scum!” Just then, a man and his squadron shoved through the enemy soldiers who were unable to approach us. He was as unwelcome a sight as ever.
“Regal Vagos!”
“The Dragon Slayer...!”
He was here.
Kwaaang!

The explosions, the urgent shouts of my comrades, the screams, and the spattering of blood—those noises all disappeared as silence fell on the battlefield. Or, well, my surroundings were still loud, but it at least felt that way to me. It was probably the same for this guy. We stood at a distance, staring at each other without a word.
Did he recognize me?
Just as the thought popped into my mind, he spoke. “I told you back then. Even death won’t be able to save you.”
So, you did recognize me.
I guessed he somehow managed to get his memories back. It seemed he’d figured out my Gachabone essence, too, because he didn’t seem phased by the fact that I was now shorter.
Great, so shall we say hello after all this time?
“That’s an expensive-looking sword.” I glanced down at the sword strapped to his waist. “Are you here to give that one to me too?”
The reaction was immediate. “You—!” His fingertips shook with rage.
But, uh-oh, don’t get too mad yet. I’m about to give you plenty of things to be pissed about.
“How long until the spell is complete?”
“One minute!”
Our team communication spell was no longer active, so everyone was able to hear that announcement.
“Did you hear that—”
“One minute is enough.” At that moment, he kicked off the ground and ran at me.
[Regal Vagos has cast High-Rank Acceleration.]
[Regal Vagos has cast Afterimage.]
His skill combo temporarily increased his Agility, but it was different from the last time when we met in the Labyrinth of Larcaz.
He’s much faster.
This was about what you’d expect from a man with his stats, especially when Larcaz wasn’t redistributing them.
But no problem.
Bang!
I was no longer the old Bjorn, either.
Sword and shield collided and his eyes narrowed. It was obvious what he was thinking.
“What, you thought you could fill me with holes like last time? Because we’re not in the maze anymore?”
He didn’t answer and instead swung his sword once more.
[Regal Vagos has cast Divine Blade.]
White light shimmered down the sword’s surface. But that was old news too.
Boom!
I can take an aura easily now—do you think that makes any difference?
“How are you still the same?” Not that I was complaining, of course. I’d just been wracking my brain trying to figure out how to gauge how much stronger he’d gotten in those two years.
“You—!”
Blocking several strikes of his sword, I shoved my shield to swat him away like a fly. My Strength was higher than his now—overwhelmingly so.
“...Ugh!” It seemed the force behind my push was unexpected as the Dragon Slayer stumbled back in confusion.
Just then, someone behind me shouted, “Ten seconds left now!” That meant the spell would be completed soon.
“I’ve seen everything I need to see, so get lost. You’re weaker than me now.”

It must have been a great shock to hear that coming from me because he didn’t reply at all. For a moment, I wondered if he might have lost it, but that didn’t seem to be the case. I brought my hammer down, just to see if it would work, and he quickly dodged it.
Bang!
Looking down at the hammer embedded in the ground, I bit my lip. If it weren’t for the ever-increasing number of enemies swarming us, I could have ended this ill-fated relationship here and now.
“Schuitz! Come quick!”

Amelia’s voice rang out from behind me and the magic circle on the ground began to glow. The teleportation spell had been completed without me even realizing. The warriors on the front lines, including me, rushed to the center.
“You think I’ll let you go?!”
You think someone like you can stop me? I’m the disappointed one here.
“You bastaaard!”
“Vagos! If you stand there, you might get sucked into the Multi Teleportation spell!”
The guy about to rush me stopped on his lackey’s advice. If he came even a bit closer, I would’ve been able to take him along on the teleport and we could’ve ganged up on him.
Shaaaaaa!
Once I stepped on it, the magic circle got even brighter.
“See you next time. Take good care of your head until then.”
Soon, a multi-colored light flashed.
Flash!

The light filling my eyes disappeared, and my vision returned. The first things I saw were huge trees that had been drained of all life. It was a similar environment to the one we were in a while ago. This was only natural. It was impossible to skip an entire zone with a single Multi Teleportation.
“...There’s no one here.”

We were in the western region of the Deadwood, one of the central zones of the Dark Continent, but there weren’t any signs of life around. That was probably because all the troops in the area had gathered in one spot to catch us.
“Priests, treat the wounded, quick. We’ll leave as soon as you’re done.”
We may have cleared one hurdle, but there was no time to waste. After regrouping, we immediately started marching—north this time, not south to where our troops were located.
Forcing my exhausted body to move, I stopped avoiding the inevitable and decided to get this over with. “...Casualties?”
“Three deaths.”
So, in that short period of time, two more people were hit besides the guy next to me. “Who are the deceased?”
Kaislan reported the losses we’d incurred in a somber tone. “Might Million, Fiona Amos, and Niaro Campbell.” One warrior from Team Two, one priest from Team Four, and even the wizard from Team Three.
“A wizard was hit...?”
“It seems he was hit by a lucky shot right at the end after the Dragon Slayer and his men arrived. The magic circle was pretty much completed at that point so no issues were pulling off the spell.”
Damn that useless Dragon Slayer.
Grit.

Our squadron, which had started with thirty people, had been reduced to twenty-five in short order. Among them, Team Three had suffered the most damage. Following the traitor Pyke Neldine, their wizard had now fallen in battle as well, reducing their number to four.
“Team Two is just as much at risk. Million was their sole warrior.”

Akurava’s team, which specialized in firepower, had also taken a blow. Since they had a summoner, they could possibly use the three Trolls on the front line, but that summoner woman of hers was more a nuker than anything.
“We’ll have to switch up the formation.”
“It seems so. No one will argue about that in a situation like this.”

Until now, each team moved and operated independently. We considered this to be more efficient unless there were special circumstances like our attack on the Eye of the Sky or the battle just now. But that wouldn’t work anymore. Instead of an alliance of several teams, we needed to become a single squadron in the truest sense of the word.
“With your permission, I’ll divide everyone by roles and create a new formation,” said Kaislan.
“I’m fine with that. Our team members will understand too. I’ll leave the formation to you, so discuss with the other leaders and decide amongst yourselves.”
“Okay. I’ll do that.”

Although the first impression he gave off wasn’t so great, Kaislan was a very useful, skilled guy. It wasn’t long after I gave him the order that he organized the teams into one unit. The classes with fewer physical abilities were gathered in the center and high-agility classes like archers, swordsmen, and rogues were placed around them. During battle, their role would be to serve as escorts. While we moved, they would carry those who lacked stamina or were slow walkers.
“Ugh, I’m already tired as it is...”
“S-Sorry.”
“It’s fine. It can’t be helped. Just treat my injuries if I get hurt later, okay?”
Surprisingly, those being treated as human stretchers weren’t too upset about it. They knew, too, that we had to group up like this to survive.
“Mister... take care of yourself. If you need help, yell out.”
“You be careful too. Don’t do anything dangerous.”
Anyway, that’s how our team ended up split up. I was a warrior in the tank position. I naturally had to be in the front.
As we resumed our journey in our new formation, Ravien spoke up behind me. “Everyone is very tight-knit,” she noted.
I had something to say to her too. “Thanks.”
“...Sorry?”
“For holding position when the Dragon Slayer appeared.”

Ravien was strong. Though it may have depended on the situation, in general, it was safe to say she was one level above Amelia and Erwen. If this woman had decided to do something unexpected, there could have been injuries or even deaths on our team too.
“...I’m not so foolish that I can’t distinguish between business and personal affairs.”
“That’s a relief.” There was nothing else to say after that so the conversation petered out there.
“We’ll rest here for a while!” Before our stamina could reach its breaking point, we took a sorely needed rest.
“Ahh! Finally!” As soon as the march stopped, each member of our squad dropped to the ground in exhaustion and lay down.
But one man was different. “Um...” The man approached me carefully, deep bags under his eyes.
“Sven Parav.” In other words, Goblin. This guy was interesting too. He didn’t seem all that powerful in battle but he surprisingly never got injured. “What’s going on? Why aren’t you resting?”
In response to my question, he answered in a somewhat jittery tone, “U-Um, well, actually...”
“If you have something to say, say it quick. I need to rest too.”
He winced at the obvious annoyance in my voice. “Um... can’t we just keep going?”

“You don’t want to rest?” I thought he was just being an annoying shit at first, but I changed my mind. He probably wouldn’t say something like that without some sort of justification. “Is there a reason you’re asking?”
“No, but...”
“But?”
“I-I feel uneasy for some reason... Ever since you told us to rest, I’ve been having trouble breathing. I-It feels like someone’s poking my heart with a needle.”
...What the hell is with this bastard?
He was freaking me out.

chapters.title: Chapter 414
paragraphs: Chapter 413: Dilemma (5)
“Um... to be honest, ever since I was a kid, I’ve had really good intuition...”

When I shot him a disbelieving look, Goblin provided examples. His explanation was all over the place, to the point where I wondered if he even knew what he was saying right now, but there was one thing he said that left an impression.
“The same thing happened on the day the pillars of fire appeared! I was supposed to go into the labyrinth that day but felt the same thing I’m feeling today...”

At first, I thought he might be a bit off his rocker, but if he’d genuinely experienced all the things he just listed, that was tough to ignore. After all, Sixth Sense was a real stat that existed in Dungeon and Stone.
“Okay, go back to your position.”
“A-Are we leaving then?”
“I can’t force a march based on groundless anxiety.”
“...I-I guess that’s true, huh?”
“Yes. But I will think about it.”
Goblin left with an expression that said, Okay, I’ve done the best I can do.
Only then did my comrades say something, starting with the healer Old Didi. He settled on a politer version of, Is that guy right in the head? “What an interesting fellow.”
The wizard Ashed spoke up in his defense. “Perhaps he received a revelation. Since he’s a paladin who serves god.”
Erwen, for her part, looked somewhat peeved. “Who is that guy? He’s ruining everyone’s break when we’re all tired.”
“Now, now, let’s calm down.”
As I was encouraging Erwen to relax, Amelia came up to me as well. “Schuitz, what are you thinking? It doesn’t seem like you dismissed what he said as nonsense.”
“There’s a reason why adventurers believe in superstitions.”
“So you intend to heed his warning?”
“Well...” I’d have to think about it. To be honest, I’d started having a bad feeling too as soon as I heard what he had to say.
Slide.
With that in mind, I glanced down at the Traffic Light Ring on my finger. It still wasn’t glowing, but I couldn’t let down my guard based on that alone.
This ring doesn’t predict everything.

The Traffic Light Ring had been like that in the game too. Even if there was an event in the area, it wasn’t like it had a 100 percent probability of activating. Instead, it turned on randomly. If there was a green light, there was definitely something good in your vicinity. But just because the light didn’t turn on didn’t mean there weren’t any good things nearby. And vice versa.
What should I do?
Just as my worries were reaching a boiling point, the ring activated and began to shine.
[The ring has detected your destiny.]
Shaaaaaaa.
I hurriedly looked down and saw that the color of the light was a very vivid red.
“Mister...?”
I stood up quickly, leaving behind a confused Erwen. “Everyone get ready to move!” I ended the short break and got the group moving again.
“...We haven’t even been stopped for ten minutes yet.”
“The squad members are having a hard time.”
The team leaders expressed concerns but there was nothing I could do. A little exhaustion was better than going through a red-light-worthy event, right? “In formation! We’re leaving now!”
We started marching again. About thirty minutes later, the light on the ring went out.
Shaaaaa.
There was no way to know what kind of negative force had been approaching us. I was dazed but also dumbfounded.
Sven Parav, who the hell is that bastard? Is this just a coincidence? No matter how good someone’s Sixth Sense may be, their radius can’t be wider than the Traffic Light Ring’s, right?

Even as I was thinking that, I kept remembering the look on Sven’s face as he earnestly tried to convince me that he had good instincts. So while we traveled, I fell back for a moment to march by Goblin’s side.

“What about now? Do you feel fine?” If he still felt anxious, I figured the incident could just be dismissed as a coincidence, since he didn’t know about the Traffic Light Ring or the fact that its light had already gone out.
“Ah, yes... I-I feel more at ease now.”
What the hell...?
On the seventh floor’s Dark Continent, a human man with a body as stocky as a barbarian bent down and touched the ground. “Baekho, there are tracks here!”
“Really? How many people?”
“I think over twenty but I can’t be sure! But it’s clear they didn’t leave too long ago!” he shouted, his voice as loud as you’d expect from a man of his large stature.
“It might be them,” said the old man, barely able to hear himself through the ringing in his ears.
“Them?”
“You know. The people who destroyed the Eye of the Sky and fled.”
“Ah, those guys...”
“Do you plan to follow them? If it really is them, we’ll be able to demand a fair amount of payment from Noark this time.”
“Hmm.” The blond man stroked his chin and thought it over. Then he chuckled and turned to the other member of their party. “Kitty, what do you think we should do?” he asked in a playful tone.
The beastwoman at the receiving end of the question only frowned in displeasure. She didn’t answer.
