“Well, I can tell just by your expression. That’s a no, right?”
“...It’s a waste of time,” she said.
“Waste of time? I know you just don’t want to harm anyone from the city. How boring.”
When their conversation ended, the warrior who first discovered the tracks prodded Baekho for an answer. “So what are you going to do? Follow them?”
“No. Why bother?” The blond man shrugged. “We’re not sure it’s them anyway, right? What if we go and then realize we followed some random bastards hunting in the area?”
“It’d admittedly be a waste of time. But isn’t it also a waste to let them go without checking? If we follow them now, we might be able to catch up quickly,” said the old man.

“Eh, whatever. It’s not like we’ll get anything amazing for catching them.” The blond man waved his hand in annoyance and pulled a chair out from the sub-space. “If we ran into them here by coincidence, then maybe. But there’s no need to follow them and check. Let’s do our own job. Don’t worry about the others. They’ll figure it out.”
“If that’s what you want, okay.”
“Okay, then let’s shelf that and take a break to eat before we get moving again. Hey, Aures!”
“Haha! Just a moment! I’ll cook up some delicious meat in no time!”
Before long, the smell of grilling meat began to waft around them.
It was our sixtieth day in the labyrinth. In other words, there were fifteen days left until the seventh floor closed.
“We somehow ended up all the way over here.” We arrived at the western zone of the Dragon Pit, the Loser’s Resting Place.
Shaaaaaaaaaa.

A black fog filled the surrounding area, refusing to disperse despite the strong winds. Through it, we could see tens of thousands of rusted swords embedded in a seemingly endless field. This place gave off a spooky vibe but no one commented on it. No one had the time to indulge in such sentiments.
“Schuitz, we have to keep moving. If we stop and end up surrounded—”
“I know, shut up.”
Hmm, was that too harsh? The thought came to me afterward but I didn’t offer an apology. I didn’t have the luxury to.
“Schuitz, don’t be such a worrywart. If the commander falters, everyone else is bound to falter too.”
Huh, I didn’t expect to be the one getting consoled. I let out a bitter huff of laughter and sighed.
Isn’t it too much to tell me not to worry?

My plan had already gone sideways. We headed north into the enemy’s sphere of influence, not south where our allies were. I thought if I chose this place, we’d be able to survive. After all, as the saying went, you often couldn’t see things when they were right under your nose. But in reality?
Stubborn bastards.
Whenever we slowed down for even a moment, our pursuers quickly caught up with us. Because of these guys, we’d been forced to march for days on end without rest, let alone sleep.

“I just don’t understand. How are they finding our exact location every time?” Kaislan questioned how Noark’s troops were able to follow us without fail but I knew the answer. I’d experienced this once before.
“If we didn’t cut off another arm, we might’ve missed it.”

In the Labyrinth of Larcaz, the Dragon Slayer used a priest of Karui to track us down. He was probably using a similar method this time since these guys were willing to sacrifice anything to achieve their goals.
“Parav. How are you feeling now?”
“I-I think I’m okay for now...”

Goblin had played a big role in avoiding any deaths up to this point. Somehow, he always sensed when our pursuers were nearby every time we took a break. And every time we were moving and he meekly asked if we could go in another direction, it always turned out that the enemy was lying in wait to ambush us up ahead. Once I realized that, I started making him walk beside me even as we were moving.
“Then we can rest a bit longer. Tell me right away if anything feels off.”
“Okay.”

All at once, he dropped to the ground. If he was acting like that, that meant that our surroundings really were safe. Frankly, I wanted to collapse on the spot as well and close my eyes for even a mere moment.
But I can’t do the same.

Shoving aside my weak thoughts, I gathered the team leaders for a meeting. “Calla, Kaislan, Jun, Akurava, let me start by saying I’m sorry. I thought we could hide out until closing day here but I was wrong.”
Was the apology a bit out of character? The other team leaders looked rather startled and offered words of comfort one by one.
“I don’t think that’s something you need to apologize for,” said Calla.
“Yes. Just look at our pursuers. Even if we waited for the rescue team back there, we wouldn’t have lasted even a day,” Jun added.
“If it weren’t for you, more people would’ve died,” said Akurava.
“I’m embarrassed to say this, but when things turned out the way they did, I was glad I wasn’t the commander. As I said before, the commander is someone who can never falter...” said Kaislan.
Oh, that takes a bit of weight off my shoulders.

I’d actually been thinking a lot about that lately—that maybe we should’ve waited in Deadwood for rescue. Or perhaps we should’ve headed south and fought to escape enemy territory even if it meant sacrificing a lot of lives along the way. What if everyone died because I’d made the wrong call here?
Boom.
It felt like living with a mountain-sized rock on my chest, but that didn’t mean I could ignore my responsibilities. Even if that meant adding an even bigger rock to my chest.
“Ahem.”
“You look embarrassed.”
Whatever.
Tap, tap.
I tapped my knee and said to the leaders, “Anyway, that’s why I called you here. To ask for your thoughts.”
“Looks like you’ve already made a decision,” said Akurava.
Oh, that’s true.

Still, I was just thinking about it—I hadn’t fully made the decision myself yet. “I’m sure you’re all well aware of this already, but we won’t be able to last long hiding here.” Before getting to the point, I covered the basics. “If we don’t keep moving, the enemy will catch up with us soon and we’ll be surrounded.”

We were like sharks that could only breathe as long as we kept swimming forward. Slipping up or stopping meant game-over. If we gave the enemy time to organize a full-scale siege against us, our tired troops wouldn’t be able to hold out.
“Then where do you plan on going?”
I looked at the curious team leaders and bit my lip ruefully.
“From what you’re saying, it looks like you have a place in mind.”

It was as they said. I did have a place in mind. Actually, it was a place I’d had in mind during the planning stage—not one I’d thought of since arriving here. Put simply, this was Plan B—an option I hadn’t wanted to go with unless things were extremely dire.
“I’m curious. Where on earth do you plan on leading us in a situation like this?” asked Akurava.
Ultimately, I voiced the option out loud. “We’re going back to Ice Rock.” A tiring journey for us would be a tiring journey for the enemy as well.
Let’s see how far they can follow us in there.

chapters.title: Chapter 414: Uphill Road (1)
paragraphs: It was our sixty-second day in the labyrinth, and we were now in the Dragon Pit. There were only about thirty minutes left until we reached the portal connecting to the eighth floor.
[The ring has detected your destiny.]
The Traffic Light Ring lit up.
“Mister, i-it’s red!”
So, only negative things lie ahead, huh? I thought there might be some green in the mix. Jeez, how draining.

“...What do we do? Shouldn’t we change direction now?” Erwen muttered anxiously. Up to this point, whenever the red light came on or Sven Parav’s Sixth Sense was triggered, we immediately changed direction to avoid whatever lay ahead.
“Erwen, changing our destination now won’t make any difference.”
“That’s... true...”

The fact of the matter was that our surroundings were basically a minefield of red-hot flames. Even if we tried to flee elsewhere, the fire would slowly close in and suffocate us. There was only one way to escape it entirely: risk everything to cross through the flames before it was too late.
Just then, Goblin came up to me with an embarrassed look on his face.
“Parav, what is it?”
“Um... I feel a bit safer next to you...”
Only a bit? That kind of hurt my feelings, but I let it slide since he’d been the most helpful member of the unit so far. “So, how do you feel now?”
“Suffocated. L-Like I’m walking into a burning forest and can’t breathe.”
“Really? But you didn’t say anything. You always suggest we run away whenever you feel like that.”
“Well... it’s true that I’m getting an ominous feeling, but I can’t shake the thought that we’re on the right path.”
So we were. “We’ll reach the portal soon. Everyone, speed up!” I kicked off the final sprint.
“The portal!”
A while later, a shimmering portal appeared in the distance, scattering multicolored light.
“...Enemies!”
I could see enemies in the light of the portal. A unit consisting of approximately forty people was also heading toward it with the intention of securing it.
“It’s those royal bastards!”
“They really came this way!”
The moment we spotted the enemy, the enemy let out shouts that indicated they spotted us as well.
Man, how did they know about this place?
Just as I was asking myself this question, I saw a familiar face in the crowd.
“You...!” Regal Vagos, the Dragon Slayer. “Yes, I knew you would come this way!”
Yeah, I guess you know me a little, just like I know you. What an ill-fated—
“Your attempt to run away like a rat ends here!”
Says you—you guys just got here too. Anyone listening would think you’ve already completely blocked our path or something. Good thing we picked up the pace.

I patted myself on the back for the decision I made twenty minutes ago. If I had hesitated even a moment when the ring turned red, those guys would have already been positioned in front of us. It would have taken huge sacrifices for us to get through the portal.
“What are you hesitating for? Run!”

This wasn’t just a final sprint—I pumped my legs with all my might. The structure of this encounter was simple. Our unit was heading east toward the portal. The Dragon Slayer and his friends (the Dragon Slayer Group, for short) were running north toward the portal.
“Ruuun!”
Whoever got there first would have a huge advantage. Perhaps they knew that too, because the Dragon Slayer Group ran toward it with desperation.
Okay, we’re faster.
As of right now, we were closer to the portal.
“Damn it, what are you all doing?! Attack!”

In an attempt to trip us up, the Dragon Slayer Group started bombarding us with long-range artillery fire. That was something they could afford to do because they had numbers on their side. Leaving behind the long-rangers who needed to cast in place to keep us in check, the close-combat fighters who were adept in hand-to-hand combat tried to secure the portal.
Whiiish! Baaang! Du-du-du-du-du-du.
Man, it feels like we’re on a real battlefield.
An untold number of arrows and special abilities poured down from the sky like rain.
“What are you guys doing?! Move faster! If you fall behind, it’s all over!”
“M-My legs...!”
“Jeez, are you serious?! Damn it, get on!”
“But—”
“Hurry!”
I could push through ranged damage like this, but the same could not be said for every other member of our squadron.
Choke!
One of them was injured by a stray arrow.
“Hang in there! I’ll treat you soon!” Another slung the injured person onto his back and kept running.
Damn it, at this rate, a lot of people are going to die here...
As my jaw was instinctively tightening at the thought, the shadow of a giant woman materialized above our sprinting group.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned Dicloe, the Elemental Ruler of Darkness.]
This was the powerful summon that had earned Erwen the nickname Blood Spirit: the Elemental Ruler of Darkness, Dicloe. She started firing huge balls of pure darkness at the enemy.
Boom, boom, boom!

It was the kind of overwhelming firepower that even an explosive fighter like Akurava couldn’t replicate, but the amount of time it could be sustained was proportionately short. Erwen could only use it at full power for about five seconds. But five seconds was enough.
“Run!”
“We’re fine on our end, go in first!”
The moment the Dragon Slayer Group stopped to block the counterattack, our group rushed into the portal starting with those in the lead.
Kwaaang!
Dicloe finished throwing the last of her dark spheres and Erwen stumbled as her summon dispelled. “Oh, Mister, you’re here...”
“I wouldn’t leave you behind.”
“...That’s right. Because that’s the kind of person you are.”
“Good work.”
Aside from the two of us, the entire crew had already gone up to the eighth floor. I picked up Erwen, who was in a state of exhaustion, and hurried toward the portal.
A moment later, I heard a man’s voice right behind me. “You think I’ll let you go?”
He’s definitely fast, probably because he’s a high-agility character. When did he get here? Well, he’s still way too late.
Dash.
I flung my body forward, and the light of the portal wrapped around me in a warm embrace.
[You have entered the Land of Dawn on the eighth floor.]
I hit the dirt and rolled, and when I opened my eyes, I saw the rest of the unit waiting for me in front of the portal.
“I-It’s the captain.” They lowered their weapons once they saw that it was me, but only for a moment.
“Th-the portal is glowing again!”

As soon as I stood up, the relieved members of our unit readjusted their grips on their weapons. That was because our entire squad had already entered. It was obvious who was coming through the portal now.
Huh, didn’t think he’d actually follow us in here.
Was he fearless, or just nuts? Either way, we had nothing to worry about. After all, there was a reason we were so desperate to get here first.
“Prepare for battle!”
“Kill everyone who comes through!”
“Th-they’re here.”
“Let’s kill them!”
Door camping made you invincible.

I was standing in front of the portal. No, to be more precise, I was standing guard in front of it with a hammer in one hand and a shield in the other. My squadron was ready to activate their skills and wield their weapons at any time.
“...It’s too quiet. It’s making me anxious,” said Kaislan.

More than an hour had passed since we first occupied the portal’s entrance. So far, the portal had only spat out enemies once: when the Dragon Slayer and his subordinates came through right after I got to the eighth floor.
I wish we managed to kill him then.

Although we killed eight of his team members, the Dragon Slayer unfortunately slipped through our fingers. After getting his ass kicked at the entrance, he ran right back to the seventh floor, abandoning his subordinates. Since then, we’d been in this stalemate. It was like the calm before the storm.
They’ll probably try to storm the portal once they gather enough troops.
Once they did, we wouldn’t be able to hold onto this place. But it wasn’t like we were planning on blocking this entrance for the rest of our lives. What I was really after was time to regroup.
“Schuitz, the injured have all recovered.”
“Food and supplies?”
“We’ve gathered everything we have and everything we need and loaded it on the sled.”
Put simply, that meant we could enter Ice Rock right now if we wanted to, but I decided to push our luck a little more.
“We’ll keep guarding this place. Everyone should take turns resting.”
“...All right.” Kaislan let the squad members who were in bad condition take a break first.

Akurava noticed this and approached me. “Shouldn’t we get going? Staying here is too dangerous.” Things had been peaceful thus far but Akurava didn’t seem reassured. She kept glancing over her shoulder in a way that spoke to her nervousness, and it was obvious what she was worried about. “...Schuitz, I’m sure you’re well aware of this already, but we don’t know when they’ll come back.”
Some of Noark’s elites were currently in the Rift on the eighth floor. If those guys cleared the Rift and came out while we were here, we’d be surrounded on both sides.
Still, luck has been on our side so far.

The thing I had been most concerned about was the risk that said elites would already be out of the Rift when we entered the eighth floor. Although it was about as likely as being struck by lightning, we couldn’t rule out the possibility completely.
The problem is we have no way of knowing when they’ll come back...
This was a lot like lying in a minefield. If we were unlucky, those guys could come out of the Rift right now, and it’d be game over for us.
“We’ve been marching for days without sleep. If we go into Ice Rock like this, we’ll be killed before we can even get all that far.”
We had no other choice. Knowing this, Akurava accepted my decision as well and left.
Shaaaaaa!

About twelve hours later, the portal shimmered and spat out a single adventurer from Noark. The adventurer, who wasn’t even properly equipped, was killed instantly by the troops we had guarding the entrance.
“Just one...?”
“...Was it a scout?”

It was a truly Noark-like way of gathering information. If the person they sent in as a sacrifice died, that meant we were still blocking the entrance. If not, they’d return alive and inform the rest of the troops that the coast was clear.
But even Noark won’t keep sending scouts in indefinitely.
I deliberated for a moment before coming to a decision. If another scout came, it’d be at least an hour to three hours later. Besides, we’d gotten enough rest.
“Everyone pack up your stuff and get dressed!” We had thirteen days until the labyrinth closed. “We’re going to Ice Rock!”
It was time to head into the last chapter of this game.

The eighth floor’s Land of Dawn was a peaceful place with green meadows and mountains, but the situation there was currently far from peaceful. This was because of the thick scent of blood coming off of the adventurers filling the area.
“Say that one more time. Kayle Elbad Zenegger, what did you just say to me?”
“Give up. Vagos, we already lost them.”
“What?!” The Dragon Slayer lunged forward to grab him by the collar, but the man refused to be cowed.
“Following them won’t change anything. Going into Ice Rock without any preparation is suicide.”
“What are you talking about?! We have several times more troops than them—are you saying we can’t do what they did?”

“You’re only saying that because you don’t know what Ice Rock is like. More numbers will just slow us down in there. And in case you’re about to ask if we can just take the elites, that would also be dangerous. The only reason they’ve been running so far was because they were surrounded on all sides by the enemy.”
“If we follow them... we’ll end up being defeated instead. Is that what you’re trying to say?”

“Yes. They’re... That leader in particular is a monster,” the man answered firmly despite the Dragon Slayer’s angry tone. He was immediately rewarded for his conviction with tight pressure around his windpipe.
Choke...!
“You piece of trash.” The Dragon Slayer’s eyes were filled with murderous intent.
But it seemed the man had never expected the Dragon Slayer to actually try to kill him, no matter how reckless he tended to be. “I-If the commander finds out about this—” the strangled man rasped.
“Commander, that damned commander.”
Choke!
“Who do you think the commander will choose between the two of us, you or me? You think he’ll kill me just because I killed you?”
“N-No...” Soon, the flow of blood to his head was cut off entirely and the strangled man went limp. A few more seconds and he’d definitely be dead.
Spit.

Instead, the Dragon Slayer threw him on the floor and spat on him. It angered him that his advisor kept opposing him, but he couldn’t kill him. Despite the fact that he talked too much, he was useful. That was why the commander held him in high esteem as well.
“Damn it.”
The Dragon Slayer clenched his fists. No matter how much he vented it, his anger remained. The other subordinates all lowered their eyes to avoid his heated gaze, but his mind was cool.
...He’s not wrong.

If they couldn’t get through Ice Rock with numbers alone, it’d be too dangerous for them to go in like this. It wouldn’t have been a problem if everyone on his team were on his level, but even the so-called ‘elites’ were still trash to him. The only decent one here was the guy who just passed out. If he overexerted himself and ended up having to use his Dragon Speech, his barely-recovered body would be forced to rest again for several months.
That commander will bitch about it too.
For many reasons, going in would undoubtedly be a loss.
So I have to let that blasted son of a bitch go like this?
He didn’t like that option either. It wasn’t simply because this was a personal matter—it was a feeling born of experience. Looking back, he had felt the same way in the Labyrinth of Larcaz.
“Want to know why you lose money every time? You only bet and raise as much as you need each round. Even during moments when you need a big win.”

Vagos had made gradual sacrifices one by one to avoid losses only to eventually end up in that position. His body had been destroyed. He even lost his memory and had to spend over a year living as a semi-invalid. Let the culprit behind it all go? The longer he spent going over it in his head, the more his heart leaned toward not letting that happen. This wasn’t a simple matter of revenge anymore.
He’s gotten this much stronger since last time.

What would he be like the next time they met? It was clear the palace would grant him a big reward once he got back from destroying the Eye of the Sky. If that man got even stronger, would he be able to beat him? Vagos made up his mind.
I have to do it now.
He could not waste any more time. Whatever losses he incurred, he had to end his ill-fated relationship with that man as soon as possible. That was the wisest decision.
Squeeze.
The moment he made up his mind, the heavens seemed to validate his conviction.
Shaaaaaa!
A strong, warm wind blew around them and a halo of light materialized in the empty air. This could only mean one thing.
“The Rift! The Rift is opening!”

Noark’s most elite unit was currently being trained in secret. Apparently, they didn’t take any essences lower than rank-four. There was even a rumor going around in Noark that the power dynamics in Orcules would shift as well once they began operations.
Lucky bastards who happened to be born at the right time.

That was the Dragon Slayer’s assessment of them. While others had to work their way up from the first floor through all that hardship, these guys received abundant support just because they had some potential and empty slots for essences.
Well, still, this works out in my favor.
Despite being butt-hurt, the Dragon Slayer walked forward with a smile. Before long, the portal opened and the raid party appeared. They looked worn out from an arduous battle.
“You’re... Regal Vagos? What are you doing here?”
The Dragon Slayer smirked at the raid party’s question. “The Eye of the Sky has been destroyed.”
“...What? The Eye of the Sky?”
“And the people who destroyed it escaped to Ice Rock.”
“But why...?”
“The commander has ordered me to lead you in hunting them down.”

chapters.title: Chapter 415: Uphill Road (2)
paragraphs: That was how we returned to Ice Rock on the seventh floor—namely to Glacier Eye, its innermost zone.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Glacier Eye is now active. All healing and recovery effects are now reversed.]
[Status effect Whisper of Immortality is now active. In the event of death, the character will be resurrected as an Undead.]

The frozen air bit into my lungs. It felt like the warm sunlight on the eighth floor had been a mere illusion. We didn’t even have time to adapt to the change in environment, as we had to move quickly.
“Naria, summon the Trolls!”

The three Ice Trolls each took a sled and began to pull. There were about thirteen days’ worth of food on the sleds. If we had requisitioned all the food stored in our personal sub-spaces, we could have sustained ourselves here for months, but I deliberately only pulled out enough to make it until closing day. We had to fill the remaining space with as many combat and expedition supplies as possible.
“Travel formation!”
Our unit currently had twenty-five members. Though this may sound cold, I judged that we’d be unlikely to run into a food shortage issue even with thirteen days’ worth of food.
“Depart!”

As soon as we were in formation, we headed back up Glacier Eye, which we had previously taken ten days to travel down. It was like climbing a narrow, spiral-shaped, uphill road on the edge of a cliff, but we made better time than before. Since the portal was open, no monsters spawned here. At most, we’d be able to leave this area in five days. The problem would be the people pursuing us.
Any sane person would just let us go.

That was because entering Ice Rock required a lot of preparation. You needed thick fur clothing to block the cold, insulating stones which were a type of magical device, food, and a sled to carry all these things. An adventurer in the habit of only carrying items in their sub-space would end up in huge trouble the moment they entered this place.
But if it’s him... he’ll definitely come.
It was too soon to let my guard down. It wasn’t just my life at stake here—it was the lives of my comrades and the rest of our squadron. I had to assume the worst and react accordingly.
Step, step.
I forced the crew, who were still tired even after the break we took in the Land of Dawn, to pick up the pace.

About eight hours later, the wizard on Kaislan’s team came to me, urgently shouting my name. “Mr. Schuitz!” She was from the Second Division of the Magic Corps. I’d only spoken to her a few times but I remembered her clearly because of her un-soldier-like voice. “Mr. Schuitz! Mr. Schuitz! There’s a big problem! A really, really big problem!”
She was much taller than Raven and looked normal enough, so I didn’t know why she talked like that. Well, that wasn’t important right now.
“Big problem? Is it that thing?”
“Yes! The detection spell installed in front of the portal went off!”
“I see...” That meant the enemy had followed us into Ice Rock. I’d sort of been expecting it, but they really did it. “How many?”
“I switched to astral projection mode as soon as the detection spell was triggered and I counted at least more than twenty people!”
“What do you mean ‘at least’?”
“Well... the enemy noticed the spell sooner than I expected. The Magic Eye was destroyed so I wasn’t able to see who else entered.”
I clicked my tongue at those words. That was incredibly disappointing. Knowing how many troops our enemy had would’ve been a big help in making future decisions. “Their appearance—how did they look?”
“Hehe, you want to know if they were as thoroughly prepared as we are, right?”
“Yes.”

When I nodded, the wizard grinned. “They looked totally sloppy! All they had were thin capes over their equipment. They were carrying big backpacks which probably contained food. Since they can’t be expandable backpacks, maybe they’ll starve soon and leave?”
She looked like she was going to cry when she first came up to me but based on the way she was smiling now, I guessed she thought this was good news. In truth, it was good news.
Capes, fine, but the backpacks...? Well, to be fair, what adventurer carries around a sled or cart on their person at all times?

Backpacks had an obvious limit to their carrying capacity. In a place where hunger was worsened threefold, it was impossible to stow thirteen days’ worth of food in backpacks alone. They were even disadvantageous during combat. The weight was one thing, but they restricted movement too. On the early floors where it was hard to pull together enough mana stones to afford a sub-space, some parties even brought a porter around to avoid the inconvenience of lugging their backpacks everywhere.
“Okay. Anyway, since we confirmed someone is tracking us, let’s install another one of those spells here before we go. We need to get a more accurate sense of how many there are.”
“Okay!”
We stopped for a moment to install another detection spell. As soon as that was done, we resumed our journey, increasing our speed to make up for the break.
“Mr. Schuitz! Mr. Schuitz!” Six hours later the wizard came running up to me again. “The detection spell activated!” As was obvious from the tremble in the wizard’s voice, this was bad news.

“...That’s much sooner than I thought.” The spell, which had been installed at a point on the map that should take about eight hours to travel to, had been triggered in just six hours. That meant they were faster than us. If things continued like this, they’d catch up to us within two days.
“I-I guess it’s because they don’t have to pull a sled or anything... I-I think that’s why.”

I was starting to understand the mindset they were chasing us with. Since they didn’t have enough food, they were probably trying to catch up as soon as possible and finish this while they still had supplies.
“How many of them are there?”
“Ah! I confirmed that. F-forty-six people.”
“That’s good news. Thanks.”

“Of course, that’s my job!” The wizard gave a playful salute and turned around, but I guessed she suddenly remembered something else she had to report. “Oh, right. Um...” She did another 180, looking cautious. “There were some unusual people among them. Based on equipment alone, they were different from the others... The dark wizard who first noticed my detection spell was one of them. O-Of course, that’s just my opinion, so take it with a grain of salt!”
“Okay, I’ll keep that in mind.”
“Right... Oh, and one more thing! What should I do about the spell? Cast another one?”
“Please. Now that we know roughly how many there are, we need to know when they pass by.”
“Okay!”
Once the wizard finished delivering the message and returned to her position, Goblin let out a strange sigh from beside me. “Miss Marrone is always so full of life,” he said, his voice low.
What the hell is this prick talking about? You have time to care about stuff like that in a situation like this?

I was going to scold him and tell him to focus, but I was stopped in my tracks by the next thing out of his mouth. “It would be so nice if she could get home alive...” he said sadly, staring at the wizard’s back.
I couldn’t help but agree with him. “Yeah, it would be great if she could.” A silence fell between me and Goblin.
At this, Ravien spoke up from beside us. “In that sense, Mr. Parav, how are you feeling now?”
Jeez, and you treated me like a nutjob earlier.
Now she was the one asking him for his opinion first. Well, she had also gotten to see Parav’s scarily accurate intuition in action with her own two eyes while traveling beside me.
“Well... I’m not sure anymore. All I know is that we need to keep moving forward no matter how tired we are.”
“...I see.” The mood instantly darkened. I cleared my throat and changed the subject. “Parav, why did you join this unit?”
“...Sorry?”
“With your good intuition, shouldn’t you have been able to avoid something like this?”

I’d actually been curious about this for a while now. He told me that he had avoided the war that broke out on the first floor entirely by not entering the labyrinth that month, so why did he end up coming this time around?
“Well, to be honest... I never wanted to join.”
“What?”
“You’re not just saying that in hindsight, are you?” asked Ravien.
“It’s the truth. The archbishop kept trying to persuade me with the rewards but I still didn’t feel like it. So I tried using a lot of excuses to get out of it, but...”
“But?” Ravien asked.

“The archbishop looked at me and sighed. I felt a chill run down my spine so I quickly said I’d go. After all... it’s better to walk a thorny path than to walk myself right onto the execution scaffold, right?”
“...I’m sorry?” said Ravien. “Execution scaffold? I don’t understand.”

“Well... this will probably sound strange, but for some reason, it felt like I’d be killed on the spot if I refused. That was the sense I got. Enough so that I figured my best bet was to go into the labyrinth instead.”

“Well, I’m regretting it now. There’s no way the archbishop would really have tried to kill me. Hahaha...” Goblin let out an awkward laugh and Ravien, still skeptical about his intuition, accepted his words at face value.
But that’s kind of weird.
Something about this felt off. I couldn’t say for sure what it was, though. “Parav, do you have any idea why you got that feeling from the archbishop?”
“Hmm, I don’t know. I haven’t thought about it... I wonder if he was planning to send me on another, more dangerous mission...”

We continued to converse as we marched but we never managed to pinpoint the exact nature of his discomfort. At some point, we stopped talking entirely to preserve our stamina and continued our journey in silence. I had plenty of things to think about already.
At this rate, the enemy will catch up to us in two days.
Speeding up wouldn’t make a difference. Either way, they would catch up to us before we left Glacier Eye.
Then what do I have to do? What can I do to make my teammates, my squad, and myself a little safer?
Thump, thump, thump.
Right now, that question was enough to overwhelm me.
Shink, shink.
The sound of a sword being sharpened on a whetstone.
Chew, chew.
The sound of someone filling their stomach with beef jerky.
“Haha, is that true?”
“Yes. Let’s head there together once we’re back in the city. I didn’t believe it at first, either.”
Some people conversed with friends, and others sat upright and exhaled at regular intervals. Everyone had their way of resting.
“...Mister, why don’t you get some rest too?”
“I’ll rest here. You go back to your position.”
“Go on.”
At my firm command, Erwen returned to her spot with slumped shoulders, leaving me to gaze down the dark road below.
“She was only being considerate. Did you really need to be so cold?”
“Ravien, don’t overstep.”
“...Okay.” Ravien, who had been about to say something else, immediately shut up when she saw the look on my face. I ignored her and stared out into the endless darkness.

Our current location was the middle of Glacier Eye. As soon as we arrived here, our endless uphill slog halted, not by our own free will, but by someone else’s. According to my simple calculations, our pursuers would arrive here in one hour.
Thump, thump, thump.

My heart raced, not with anticipation for the battle ahead, but with anxiety. I’d tried brainstorming countless ways to avoid a fight but had been unable to come up with any clever methods. The battle itself was an inevitability. I ordered a break so the crew could get a short rest before then. But was that why?
“Haha!”
Step, step.
Chew, chew.

Those peaceful, everyday sounds felt like the calm breeze before a coming storm. That was probably why I could not properly relax and instead stared into the darkness. There were forty-six enemies, about twice as many people as our squadron currently had. According to the wizard’s report, ten of the enemies were particularly strong. Judging by equipment alone, they were on a similar level to the Dragon Slayer.
Maybe they brought along some of the people raiding the eighth-floor rift.

If so, this situation had gotten a lot more dangerous. To pull your weight on the eighth floor, you had to be on at least Amelia’s level. We had no chance of beating them in an all-out war. But there was no other way. The battle was already going to happen whether we liked it or not. However strong the enemy was, we had no choice but to do our best.
Well, if we fail, everyone will die.
Whip, whip.

I shook my head to dislodge the distracting thoughts. From now on, I decided to think as positively as possible. For example, the enemy might end up being weaker than expected. In that case, it’d actually be possible for us to defeat them here. Of course, there would still be sacrifices... but the moment we won, this quest would be over. With no need to make any more difficult climbs, we could just sit here, eat our remaining food, and wait this out.
Squeeze.
Yeah, that possibility definitely existed.
“The detection spell! The detection spell went off!”
Let’s do this.
“Everyone in formation!”
Though we didn’t yet know what would remain of us after the storm contained in that ominous, quiet darkness passed, there was only one thing we could do.
“...The enemy is coming!”
“Prepare for battle!”

chapters.title: Chapter 416: Uphill Road (3)
paragraphs: Hah.
Exhale.
Hah.
Inhale.
Each time I did this, my breath puffed out like I was smoking a cigarette.
Drip.
Beads of sweat fell to the ground in the form of ice droplets. My muscles screamed and my vision blurred. But, so what?
Step, step.
One step, and then another. I focused on my breathing more than ever as I trudged forward. I was in front of the two connected sleds, clinging onto the rope tightly so as not to drop it.
Step, step.
I was dragging the sleds forward without pause. The reason was simple. The Troll summoner who was in charge of the sleds had fallen.
“How’s Milburn Naria doing?”
“...She won’t last long.”
“I see...”
Grit.
My jaw involuntarily clenched as I recalled the battle just a while ago. It hadn’t been so bad at first.
[You have cast Giantization.]
I used Giantization to block the path like a boulder.
“Teirun Sheardiem.” The wizards used mana shields.
[Jun Arshen has cast Light of Protection.]
[Periton Eriaboti has cast Divine Skin.]
[Benjamin Orman has cast Damage Reduction.]
Priests assisted me with various shields and buffs, concentrating a medley of divine magic on me. This strategy could otherwise be described as “all-in.” And the strategy had worked.
[All healing and recovery effects are reversed.]

Where one hit could turn fatal, the enemy could no longer land a decisive hit on me. Leveraging that, we used our uphill advantage to bombard the enemy with every last firepower we had. Skills weren’t enough so we even used healing potions. In between benevolently plying them with the best modern medicine had to offer, we grabbed the enemy by the neck and threw them down the cliff whenever we got the chance.
[Status effect Whisper of Immortality is now active. In the event of death, the character will be resurrected as an Undead.]
Deceased enemy soldiers turned into Undead and attacked their allies, and we continued our offensive while maintaining a strong formation.
“There’s no doubt... he would have been a difficult opponent for you to handle alone, Regal Vagos.”
But once they entered the battle, things changed.
[Manua Repeles has cast Iron Fist.]
[Ricky Aymond has cast Walk of Punishment.]
[Puran Cullen has cast Possession.]
There were about fifteen adventurers on Noark’s side armed with high-ranking essences acquired from the eighth floor and above. The moment those guys entered the battle, the front line collapsed.
“Schuitz, Rayothers has run out of mana!”

The wizards who were supplying me with mana shields gave out one by one, and as if that wasn’t enough, the enemies jumped over me into the middle of our squadron’s formation. There were three paladins on the main tank line, two knights acting as secondary tanks, and one warrior from Team Three. Close-range damagers like Amelia and Ravien did their best to work together and drive them out, but even that wasn’t enough.
“W-We must retreat!”

The entire unit, including me, sensed our impending defeat. The fact of the matter was that they were much more powerful than us. If we continued and fought to the death, our opponents would suffer considerable damage as well, but that was all I could say. Ultimately, it’d end in a total party kill.
We have to give up on killing all of these bastards here.
I immediately implemented Plan B. The key to Plan B was the summoner from Team Two, Milburn Naria. This woman was a long-range nuker summoner who commanded three Ice Troll sorcerers.
[Milburn Naria has cast Cruel Command.]
[Milburn Naria has cast Beast Training.]
[Milburn Naria has cast Latent Instinct.]
[Milburn Naria has cast Stability.]
She cast buffs on her summoned beasts as soon as I gave the order.
[Summoned Beast Pippi has cast Avalanche.]
[Summoned Beast Poppy has cast Avalanche.]
[Summoned Beast Yeppi has cast Avalanche.]
The Ice Trolls, stacked with buffs that made them a dozen times stronger, simultaneously used the same active, buying us time to retreat.
“Kyaaa!”

Naria was injured in the process. She had gone out to the front lines with the Trolls to keep them within range of Stability, which increased the range of the summoned beasts’ skills by three times. She ended up getting hit. Thankfully, she had doled out commands to her summoned beasts even as she was injured, and we had been able to retreat successfully. Which was how we reached the present.
“Schuitz, are you okay...?”
“Don’t talk to me.”
After Naria lost consciousness, the entire unit took to carrying the backpacks and food, but that accounted for only one sled.
Slide, slide.
I climbed uphill while pulling the other two. I’d have to switch with the other warriors once it got too difficult, but I still had strength left in me.

While I cleared my head and kept moving, Naria regained consciousness on the sled. “Ugh...” Covered in several layers of thick fur clothing filled with insulating stones, the first thing she said was, “I-I’m cold...”
“Just hold on a little longer. That’s because your body is in bad shape. You’ll feel better once you get a heal up there.”
“Y-You think so...?”
Cough!
“...Yeah, I’m sure of it.”
There was no answer. Judging from the sound of her breathing, it seemed she’d lost consciousness again.
Boom.
It was like a cannonball had hit my heart, a feeling so suffocating that I felt like I was going to lose it.
What do you mean ‘I’m sure of it...?’
I hoped this woman wouldn’t die. That was the truth. But I knew all too well that despite my best wishes, that outcome was impossible in reality.
No, this woman is probably the one who knows that best...
Her body was as cold as ice. Death was slowly approaching.
“Home...” Just then, I heard her voice behind me again. “I want to... go home...”
I gritted my teeth and forced out a lie in response to her weak muttering. “You’ll go home. I’m sure of it.”
“Do you... think so?”
“Yes. If you can hold on.”
Naria went quiet after that. It was only a long time later that she spoke again. “Mr. Schuitz... Please, leave me here.”
“What are you talking about?”
“That will be... better for you all. That’s how... this place is...”

I didn’t answer, but not because I didn’t understand what she was saying. Whisper of Immortality was a terrible effect that resurrected you as an Undead several times stronger than your original self upon death. She wanted to help us by staying in the enemy’s path.
Silence fell.
“Please... answer me.”
With that, I ended up accepting it. Continued hypocrisy wasn’t going to help this woman.
Yeah, so instead of that...
Squeeze.
I clenched my fists and just barely managed to part my lips. “Okay. I’ll respect your wishes. Is there someone in the city you want to send a message to?”
It took a long while for her to answer. “...No. You can’t.”
“What do you mean I can’t?”

“I-I don’t deserve...” Her voice was shaky and her words incoherent. This was a behavioral change often seen right before a person died. “Ahh... I’m so sorry... I didn’t want... to fool... I didn’t want to either... I-I-If I... instead...!”
Sob.
Naria began to cry.

I didn’t dig deep, figuring this woman must have had her own burdens to bear. I just wordlessly listened to her sorrows as they tumbled out of her, continuing my march forward for who knows how long until—
“Please, let me down now...” Her pronunciation was clearer now.
“Damn it.” At this, the warrior beside me cursed.

The paladin closed his eyes and made the sign of the cross. “May the warm light embrace your soul.” As someone who had witnessed countless deaths, he had noticed the last of her embers were burning out.
“Miss Naria... You did a good job.” Her team leader, Akurava, smoothed back her disheveled hair. She carefully lifted Naria’s body and began to lower it.
“Thank you, Ms. Akurava...”

“Thank me? That’s...” Akurava gnawed on her lip as if physically biting something back. Then she laid Naria’s body down on the fur clothes the other members of our squadron had spread out on the floor for her.
“...Go. Don’t look at me like that.” Despite Naria’s words, we were having trouble leaving. “It isn’t safe. I’m fine, so... Go.”
Fuck.
Grit.
Something hot filled my chest, but my head knew to face the facts.
“Schuitz, she’s right. We have to go now.”
I forced myself to take a step and started walking again, dragging the sled.
“I’m... not scared...” Naria closed her eyes weakly. “I’m going home now...” The more I walked, the more distant her muttering became. “My real home... that smells like coffee... in the morning...”
Damn it.
“Well, I’m regretting it now. There’s no way the archbishop would really have tried to kill me. Hahaha...”
I finally figured out the nature of that discomfort.
With twenty-four survivors, the unit of what was originally thirty people advanced forward, carrying with us a discomfort that was hard to shake even when our lives were at stake.
“What Miss Naria said earlier...”
“Home... must be that place, right?”
Adventurers experienced a variety of things during their countless years in the labyrinth. So many of them knew, of course, what the earnest final wish of a dying evil spirit sounded like.
“Then Miss Naria was an evil spirit...?”
“Shh! Be quiet. We don’t know that for sure yet.”
Suspicion spread among the crew. Some were angered by the question itself.

“Are all of you out of your minds? She was injured trying to save us and tried to help us even as she was dying! She chose to die a lonely death for us! Evil spirit? Even if she is, what does that matter?”
This was a bad sign.
“No, we were just... it’s weird! Why would an evil spirit do that for us...?”
“You fucking bastard! If you really don’t know, I’ll show you myself, personally!”
What a shitshow.
“Stop!” Before a rift could form between the crew, Kaislan intervened with a shout. “Have you all lost it? We need to keep going as one unit!”
I didn’t bother to stop his tirade. This incident was making me realize that leading a group sometimes required total domination.
“If anyone utters another useless word, I will be the first to carry out their prompt execution under the kingdom’s martial law! Got it?”

It was a forceful command that was closer to a desperate attempt at dressing a gaping wound than anything. It seemed to snap everyone to their senses, and they returned to attention. Well, not everyone.
“...Try it,” someone muttered, bringing the silence to an end. The owner of the voice was Futa Rickerburn, the close-range damage dealer from Team Two who served as a scout.
“...Try it?”
“Don’t you all know? We’re already done for!”
“P-Please stop, Sir Kaislan!”
Kaislan immediately raised his sword but was stopped by the knights around him.

Rickerburn’s voice grew even louder at that. “Didn’t you see those people earlier? They’re much stronger than us! And there are more of them too! What difference would running make? They’re going to catch up with us soon, anyway.”
“...Let go. That’s an order.” The knights restraining him sighed and stepped back at Kaislan’s command.
Yikes, we’ll really see bloodshed within the team at this rate.
“Kaislan, move.” I had no choice but to stop the sled and head to the center where the commotion was.
Squeeze.
I stomped over and grabbed the guy by the collar.
“Ugh!”
“So, what are you trying to say? Everything’s hopeless so you’re just going to give up and die? Is that what you really want? If that’s the case, I can kill you before they do.”
Cough!
The guy I grabbed choked, but the defiant fire in his glare persisted. “Try it, if you can.” I was taken aback by the look in his eyes. He truly didn’t care if he lived or died.
“...What?” I subconsciously loosened my grip and he dropped back to the ground.

“What difference will it make if we somehow miraculously get rid of those bastards?” he shouted, the sound verging on a wail of despair. “What, are you picturing a future of laughing and joking around back in the city? Do you really think a future like that exists for us?”
I have to shut this asshole up even if it means killing him.

The thought came a second too late—he had already blurted out everything I didn’t want him to voice aloud. “Don’t you know why the main unit didn’t come to save us? We were abandoned! It wasn’t because something happened, either—that was their plan from the very beginning!”
“...W-What are you talking about? What do you mean that was their plan from the beginning?”
“N-Nonsense! The palace has no reason to throw away all these people!”
“Yeah! I thought so too! Because each one of us is accomplished and influential! But that was the trap!”
“...Trap?”
It was already far too late for me to fix this. I just sighed and decided to watch the train wreck unfold.

“I, Futa Rickerburn, belong to the Kealunus Dukedom! I ended up owing a big debt to the duke, so I did his dirty work as his hitman! When I finally got fed up and told him I wanted to retire, the last thing he asked me for was this expedition! Don’t you see? I was thrown away! There were too many eyes to just kill me himself so he was kind enough to gift me a title before throwing me in the trash!” He looked around at the faces of the people around him and laughed. “Hahaha! Looks like I’m not the only one who got screwed. Don’t you all have similar stories?”
He finished talking, and for a moment, a silence heavier than I’d ever experienced settled over the unit. It was like the calm before a storm.

“Th-the company abandoned me...? N-No. No way. They said they’d forgive my embezzlement if I carried out this job...” someone muttered in a state of panic. As a result, all eyes turned to their neighbors.
Are you in the same boat? their gazes seemed to ask.
It was the team leaders who received the bulk of the looks. They had the most prestige of all of us. Everyone probably wanted them to come forward and say that there was no way that was the case.

“...Perhaps we really were abandoned,” said Akurava. Reality was cruel. “I, Titana Akurava, continuously raised questions about a potential dimensional collapse of the palace and demanded strict management of the portal. Perhaps that put me in their bad books.”

Second to speak was James Calla, deputy commander of the Sawtooth Clan. “Recently, I noticed the clan’s commander seemed to be trying to undermine my authority more often. But just because of that...”

“Hah... if I had to choose something, I’d say my case is similar to Calla’s. I’m not interested in my family’s title but perhaps my older brother felt threatened. That’s why I joined the military when I was young too...” said Kaislan.

Finally, Jun’s confession. “I was the Inquisitor for the Church of Tovera. Our mission was to hunt down and execute members of Karui’s cult living in the city... But I grew disillusioned and resigned once I saw political opponents who had nothing to do with Karui being falsely accused and executed. It turns out there are quite a few bishops who want their secrets kept hidden.”
Each time one of the team leaders spoke, the faces of the unit grew more and more despairing. But it seemed they hadn’t given up hope yet, because they redirected their attention to a new target.
“Schuitz, what about you?”
“Not only were you recommended by the marquess himself, but you got the position of leader of this expedition.”
“Are you really just like us?”
The crew turned to me.
Well, there’s no reason to hide it now.
After a moment’s thought, I spoke. There was no need to give a whole detailed explanation like those before me. One sentence was enough.
“...I am Bjorn Yandel.”

chapters.title: Chapter 417: Uphill Road (4)
paragraphs: I’d only said as many words as I needed to reveal my name, but the impact each of them had was by no means small.
“Holy—!” someone shouted, stunned.
Some immediately accepted this as fact. “No wonder you were able to do all those things as easy as breathing.”
Others seemed wary. “But wait, isn’t this a big deal? If he’s Baronet Bjorn Yandel...”

I quickly continued before this conversation could hit another snag. “Don’t worry, the rumors that I’m an evil spirit are not true. I can’t give you all the details, but the palace arranged for me to fake my death so I could go undercover.” Of course, that was a total lie. But it seemed it was believable enough because the team took it in more calmly than I expected.
“It all makes sense now. There’s no way the position of expedition leader would be entrusted to some no-name adventurer...”
“Is that why Blood Spirit has been following him this whole time?”
“It never sat well with me that someone like him randomly died in the labyrinth, either.”
“But what reason could they have to have spread false information like that...?”
It was in an adventurer’s nature to be curious, but I didn’t have the time to sit here and patiently answer all their questions.
“I’ll explain more later when I get the chance. That’s not important right now.”
Once I dispelled the whispers, James Calla, who stood there with a gaping mouth, came to his senses and stammered, “Schuitz—no, Bjorn Yandel... no, Baronet Bjorn Yandel!”
It’s cute that he has no idea what to do with himself.
“I-I don’t understand. Why would the palace throw you away?”

I chuckled at his question. “Well...” I had a lot of guesses. “Someone considered a hero by those in the adventuring industry and the first adventurer in decades to earn a noble title in return for saving countless lives...” It felt a lot like I was tooting my own horn, but it was an accurate description. “To them, it would be much better if I quietly disappeared. Especially if the alternative is that they’d have to publicly retract the announcement that I’m an evil spirit.”
“Ah...” Calla seemed to readily accept that explanation, but in truth, there was more to it.

I couldn’t tell these people about my real suspicion, though—that there was a good chance the marquess had clocked me as an evil spirit a long time ago. No, actually, he most definitely did. Sending his son to my room in the middle of the night to check whether I was an evil spirit or not was simply a ploy to lull me into a false sense of security. After all, it was hard to notice when someone was tricking you when you were convinced you were the one tricking them.
“Anyway, that’s the end of my story.” I looked around at the rest of the unit with a question in my eyes. What about you guys?
Ravien started us off. “The marquess promised me something in return for this job, but I guess... he never intended to keep that promise.”

Versyl Gowland. “I... was in a coma for a long time and finally regained consciousness thanks to the Representative from the Church of Tovera. In return, I ended up bound in service to the church. If they were looking for a wizard they’d be willing to discard on this mission, there would’ve been no better option than me.”

Old Didi, our team’s healer. “My granddaughter was killed last year. There was no proof, but it was a knight working for the marquess. I’ve been looking for that knight. Perhaps the marquess was aware of that when he approached me.”

“I happened to find out that the lord of the Magic Tower is colluding with the palace. To make this public, I needed power. Which was why I participated in this quest for money. But it seems he figured out what I was doing,” said wizard Riard Ashed from the Lengman School, whose master was the lord of the entire Magic Tower.
“Wait! I-I really can’t think of anything. My motto in life is to live without attachments!” shouted Sven Parav.
Yeah okay, the heavens and I both know that you’re an evil spirit.
His secret probably ended up getting exposed somehow. I ignored Goblin’s whining and looked around at the rest of the group.

Most of them shared their personal experiences as soon as my eyes met theirs. Of course, some chose to remain silent. But I could tell they were only keeping their mouths shut so as not to reveal their secrets, not because they didn’t have any. They also had an inkling as to why they were placed in this unit.
Our untimely confession session was interrupted by a sudden shout of protest.

“Wait! I-I... have no reason to be abandoned by the church!” It was a priestess from Kaislan’s team named Periton Eriabosti. “T-There must be some mistake. I-I only applied to this position because I thought I could help people...” She didn’t seem to be lying. No, it probably wasn’t a lie.
“I’m sorry to hear that,” I said, genuinely remorseful. “It was probably bad luck that you got caught up in this.”
“Wait! Bad luck—”
“There are others in a similar boat.”

For example, there were Erwen and Amelia, along with the knight who had been serving as Kaislan’s subordinate for almost ten years, Percival Eric Coulson. Not to mention Calla’s old friend Rick Jugusta. Well, as these people’s crime was making friends with the wrong people and following them into a tight spot, even they probably didn’t feel as cheated as this luckless woman.

“That’s...” The priestess, who seemed to genuinely be innocent, dropped her head. She wasn’t the only one, either. As expected, the atmosphere of the expedition team was steadily approaching that of a funeral home.
“We... were really abandoned?”
“How can we deny it now...?”
“Then... even if we make it back alive, the palace will still try to kill us somehow?”
“God damn it!”
Like a kite with a broken string, their eyes began to waver with panic.
“Are we going to die? Really? Here, like this...?” Some despaired.
“I... I still have things I need to do!” Some were angry.
“...There’s something about this that doesn’t make logical sense. If all of this is true, what was Pyke Neldine for?” Some expressed doubts and clung to any sliver of hope they could find.
“Yeah! If they were planning on abandoning all of us, why would they try to sabotage the mission by throwing in a traitor?”
Oh, that.

That was something I had been wondering too. As far as I could tell, there were two possible explanations. The first was that the Guild Master simply didn’t want to let the marquess get all the glory for this mission. As I was the leader of this squadron, once the Eye of the Sky was destroyed and all of us were massacred, most of the credit for our achievements would go to the marquess. So what if someone wanted to stop that from happening?
It’s quite plausible. If we lost all our food in Ice Rock, we would’ve died before we even got past this spot, let alone to Eye of the Sky. It’s a definite possibility. But...
Tap, tap.
It was probably best not to mention my other suspicion. I soon came to a decision. We only needed one person worrying about the worst-case scenario, and I could be that person.

“Why did someone send a spy?” Only the team leaders knew that the Guild Master was behind Neldine’s actions, so for now, I decided to tell the team only what they needed to hear at this moment. “Isn’t it obvious?” And this was probably what everyone wanted to hear. “There’s someone out there in the city!” I said enthusiastically. “Someone who doesn’t want us to die senseless deaths in here! As long as we get back alive, there’s someone out there who can help us stand up against the palace!”
Even if that hope was futile, we had to use it to keep moving forward. That was what it meant to be alive.
Right now, we were in a closed-up mansion with all the windows boarded up, allowing no light in. That was the current situation of our squadron, and it was half intentional on my part.

“What difference will it make if we somehow miraculously get rid of those bastards? What, are you picturing a future of laughing and joking around back in the city? Do you really think a future like that exists for us?”
When that guy said that to the rest of the squadron, I didn’t stop him.
“...I am Bjorn Yandel.”
I even uttered my real name, which would’ve sounded like a death sentence to these people.
“We... were really abandoned?”
“How can we deny it now...?”

I had manipulated the situation to stamp out all traces of hope from the crew’s heads, closing the windows in the already dark room one by one. My reason for doing so was simple. Those who dreamed of a bright future were easy to break.

But now I had purposefully cracked a window open so a faint sliver of light could stream through. For now, it would have to be enough. With this, I could make everyone focus on the same goal as they pushed forward.
“We can go back...?”
“But... we don’t even know who they are. How do we know if whoever it is really has that kind of power?”
These people could see the light. Though they may have been questioning whether it was an illusion, that, at least, was indisputable.

“Listen up, everyone!” I had no choice but to encourage them to move toward the light together, even if it meant crawling through the darkness. Although we weren’t sure whether an even darker abyss lay at the other end of it, we at least had to see it for ourselves. “I am Bjorn Yandel! Have you heard of me?”
“How can we not know that name?” the crew replied.
“The first adventurer in decades to become a nobleman...”
“There was no small uproar when news of his death went around.”
Their voices were weak and lacked fervor. In response, I raised my energy levels even more.

“I’m glad you heard of it! I won’t talk for long! We’re in the worst possible situation right now! We have annoyingly strong sons of bitches on our tail and a pack of wolves waiting for us back in the city! However! I have never once given up in my life, and that includes now!” I shouted. “So I, Bjorn Yandel, promise you this on the heart and honor of a warrior.” I didn’t dare vow that I’d keep everyone alive, but... “I will take on the hardest work. I will do the dirty work no one else wants to do. I will be the first to wade into the bloodbath, and if someone has to get hurt, I will be that person. So!” I let my volume drop and made a sincere request. “Follow me.”
Although I didn’t shout that time, I knew they’d heard me. There was no answer, though. Everyone was busy eyeing each other despite my earnest plea.
Jeez, this is pissing me off.
“If your lives are going to be thrown in the trash anyway, I’m saying throw them at me instead!”
So I have to yell to get them to listen, huh?
“Anyway, if anyone’s with me, get ready. We’re leaving in one minute.” With that, I turned around.
Someone immediately joined me. “Mister, take me with you!” It was Erwen.
“Good. I was planning to leave on my own if we stayed here any longer,” said Amelia. These were my precious comrades who would follow me into the fire.

“Jun, you were right in the end.” Next was Kaislan. “You said that when everyone else is ready to give in, this man will stand strong. I don’t know what lies at the end of this tunnel, but I will follow you through it.” He fell into place behind me.
Next was Akurava. “I was never planning to give up here from the start. I’ve faced worse situations than this. If I gave up every time I did, I wouldn’t even be standing here.”
After Akurava stood Jun, and once Calla joined in, the rest of the squadron followed one by one.
“Bjorn Yandel... he’s even more of a blockhead than the rumors say.”
“Hehe, I thought he was going to say something cool, but he just yelled at the end.”
“We’ve rested enough. Let’s get moving again.”
“He said he’ll do all the dangerous work, right? No self-respecting adventurer would stay behind after getting a guarantee like that.”
“Well, we can’t let ourselves die here, so...”
“Wait! Don’t stand anywhere you want, let’s stand in formation! Formation! Huh?”

Before the minute I mentioned was even up, the whole crew was behind me. It wasn’t a particularly touching scene, though. Humans tended to change their minds on the precipice of death. Even if I had started walking out of here entirely on my own, everyone would have followed.
“Yandel! So when are we leaving?”
“Hey, you... don’t speak to the commander that way!”
“Jeez, who cares? We’re all going to die if something goes wrong, anyway.”

This was why you had to dot your I’s and cross your T’s. Life began to stir in the eyes of people who had previously seemed unable to cut down even an Orc. They were either terrified of being left alone or didn’t want to be abandoned a second time. This shift wouldn’t have happened if they had only chosen to follow me reluctantly.
“Great, then we just need to take care of one more thing before we leave.”
“Take care of something?” Parav tilted his head beside me, looking anxious. I ignored him entirely and headed toward the sleds.
A warrior rushed over to me. “Wait! You’ve been dragging it all on your own until now. We’ll help you from now on—”
What is he saying? Who said I’m going to drag it anymore?
“Wait... why are you taking the food off the sled?”
“I think we can shove this much in our stomachs.”
“...Huh? Shove it in our stomachs? Then the rest...?”
What else? Throw it away.
Whoom!
With that, I pushed the two sleds I was barely able to pull off the cliff. We were so high up that it took more than ten seconds for the impact to echo. Even then, the sound was faint.
“...W-What the hell?!”
“What did you just do?!”
What do you think? Why do you think the enemy is moving faster than us?
“They’ll overtake us in no time if we drag a sled around.”
“Y-Yeah, but... still, the food...”
“What’s the problem? The food in our backpacks will be enough until we get out of the Glacier Eye.”
“B-But what are you going to do after that?”
It was a legitimate question and concern. Even if we managed to get through Glacier Eye in two days thanks to our lighter load, we’d have to last eight more until the labyrinth closed.
Jeez, so cranky. You think I did that without thinking?
Before an all-out riot could start, I quickly shared my plan. “There will be monsters after Glacier Eye.”
“Monsters...?”
“No way, are you...?”
I didn’t deny it. “Yes, from there, we’ll use distortion magic to get meat.”
That seemed to cause even more unrest.
“Looks like you’re being serious...”
“This is outrageous.”
“Um... I... think I might prefer to just die here then.”
But this was our best shot.

chapters.title: Chapter 418: Uphill Road (5)
paragraphs: I chewed on beef jerky as I walked. Not just me, but the entire crew.
“Ugh... I-I think I’m going to throw up. I ate too much, I can’t anymore...”

Some had complaints but that was only a small number. Even as we speed-walked uphill, everyone forced themselves to gnaw on the jerky. We were all well aware that this was the last time any of us would have a full stomach.
“Mr. Schuitz! N-No... Baronet Yandel!” We were still stuffing our faces when Marrone, the wizard from Team Five, came up to me. “The detection spell we installed ten minutes ago was triggered!”

“They were much closer than we thought, then.” If they ran at full force, they’d reach us in just a few minutes. “Everyone, throw away the boxes of food!” I shouted and threw the box of jerky I was holding in one of my arms down the cliff. We had to reduce our load as much as possible if we wanted to increase our speed.
Whip!

Most threw the boxes without hesitation as soon as my orders were issued, but some people’s hands twitched in clear distress at the thought of throwing out food—namely those in the melee roles such as paladins and knights.
“Damn it, I can still eat more...!”
It was funny watching them say that with jerky stuffed into all of their pockets but it wasn’t like I didn’t get where they were coming from. I felt the same way.
Why do I feel like my stomach is already empty?
This fuel-inefficient body of mine cried out for more food no matter how much I ate.
Looks like the good times are over, then.
“Marrone, cast a new detection spell so we can figure out how fast they’re moving.”
“Okay!”

Once Marrone installed a new spell, we officially began picking up speed. Of course, the increase wasn’t that drastic. If we were speed-walking along the banks of the Han River earlier, now we were basically running a slow marathon. About seven minutes of jogging passed us by.
“The spell went off!” Even though we’d picked up the pace, they managed to narrow the distance by three minutes.
“This is a headache.”
The squishy priests and wizards were already being transported on piggyback, so we only had one other option now. After all, survival was determined by what you were willing to sacrifice.
“Throw away all the backpacks containing insulation stones.”

I gave up on the insulating stones that helped us maintain our body temperature. If you didn’t count the tents and sleeping bags that already got thrown away with the sleds, these were the heaviest of our supplies. The food would naturally go away as we ate.
“Damn it, now we have to fight against the cold too?”
“What are you all doing?! Throw it all away!”
“We have to keep running anyway, so let’s not dwell on it too much!”

When we gave up on the insulating stones, we were able to speed up, as expected. This was thanks to the lessened burden on the non-combat crew, who had been carrying it all on their backs. Before long, good news rolled in.
“The spell was triggered. This time it was exactly seven minutes and thirty-seven seconds!”
The distance issue started to resolve itself. Of course, moving faster meant we felt even more like death, though.
But they’ll be in the same boat.

From now on, it was a battle to see who could hold out the longest. This harsh environment put us on a level playing field. Just as we’d had to make sacrifices., they’d soon have to make a choice too. Case in point:
“...W-What do we do? Th-they suddenly got faster. There’s only a six-minute difference now!”

We’d been running without letting up for five minutes, snacking on beef jerky as we went. Yet the seven-minute barrier we’d managed to maintain so far had been broken. How could that be? The answer was simple.
“Their numbers went down! To twelve people!”
The enemy had given up their biggest advantage, their numbers, to catch us.
Did they hand over all the food and send the rest of their people back down?

That seemed like the most likely possibility. The ones still chasing us would starve on the way back, but if they pushed through three days of hunger and managed to reach the bottom, they’d be able to eat until their stomachs exploded.
But twelve, huh?
Somehow, we ended up with double the amount of people.
I still don’t know if we can win.
Of course, we’d have to bump into each other at some point. However, now was not the time for that.
“W-What do we do? They’ll catch up to us in no time!”
What do you mean what do we do? Since they gave up one thing, we need to give up one more. That’s fair, right?
“Throw away all heavy metal equipment. Of course, we have to be able to fight so leave the shields and weapons.”
“What?!”
Without another word, I was the first to take off the equipment covering my body and throw it down the cliff.
“Y-You’re really going to go that far?”
“You were screaming about how we’re all going to die earlier, but now you think it’s a waste?”
“No, but—”
“Good. Then throw it. You can pay for new equipment with the loot you have stored up in sub-space.”
“Man... Throwing away equipment while being chased by the enemy... You really are nuts.”
The front line, for whom metal armor served as a lifeline, grumbled but ultimately followed my instructions to take it all off and replace it with thick fur clothing.
“Six minutes! Same as before!”
As a result, we were able to maintain our distance of six minutes. The enemy would probably be shocked right about now, wondering why they weren’t closing in.
I wonder what kind of expressions they’ll be wearing when they meet up with us naked later.
Okay, picturing that gave me a little more strength.
Step. Step.
We ran uphill like that for another long while.
“...This is my first time learning that people can actually sleep while running.”
“One minute... I just need a one-minute nap...”
Just then, the status quo changed.
“What the heck? The spell should’ve been triggered by now...”
The detection spell that had been activating every six minutes up to this point didn’t go off. Why? Did they have a way of avoiding detection?
No. If they did, they would’ve used it a long time ago.
I ran uphill for another ten minutes while puzzling over this, but the detection spell remained silent.
Looks like the enemy is reaching their limits too.
They’d stopped to rest. In other words...
“Halt!”
We could rest and take a breather too.
“Everyone rest! You can sleep if you want! I’ll wake you when it’s time to leave!”
As soon as I gave the order, the crew collapsed on the spot, not even able to cheer. Those who were particularly exhausted practically passed out.
“Mister, aren’t you resting too?”
“I’m going to look around for a moment.”
“I’m sorry. I want to go with you but I don’t think I can...”
“Don’t be sorry. Get some rest, quick.”
“Okay...”

Erwen soon turned around, looking exhausted, and plopped down next to Amelia. Though she didn’t get along very well with her, they fell asleep right next to each other. We had to share body heat now that we had no insulating stones. I chuckled at the sight for a moment before taking a walk around the perimeter. While most of the crew was either eating or knocked out, I noticed someone doing something unusual.
“Kaislan, what are you writing down?”
“Ah! I was recording what you said earlier, Schui—no, Yandel.”
“What I said?”
Kaislan held out his notebook instead of answering.

“I will take on the hardest work. I will do even the dirty work no one else wants to do. I will be the first to wade into the bloodbath and if someone has to get hurt, I will be that person. So, follow me. If your lives are going to be thrown in the trash anyway, I’m saying throw them at me instead!”
Jeez, reading it in writing was making me self-conscious. Still, it wasn’t like I could scold him when he was recording these events with such sincerity.
“...You have a good memory.”
“Well, what else is a good memory good for? I’ll probably never forget these words for the rest of my life.”
This guy needed better hobbies. Feeling embarrassed, I scolded him for wasting our precious break writing this down, saying it was pointless.
Kaislan only shrugged with a quiet laugh. “You never know.”
“Huh?”
“If this record will end up capturing a great moment in history.”
Jeez, there he goes, going on about history again. Come to think of it, this guy has always liked that sort of thing.
I straightened my back and patted him on the shoulder. “We have to get back home alive if we want to be recorded in the history books.”
“Ah, that’s also true. Yes, we have to get back alive...”
“Get some rest. You can write that all down once you’re back in the city.”
“I will.”
After my conversation with Kaislan, I headed toward Erwen.
A wizard who had been curled up nearby with her head on her backpack opened her eyes. “Baronet Bjorn Yandel.” It was Versyl Gowland.
“Ah, did I wake you? Sorry—”
“I’m the one who should apologize.”
“I’m sorry. For leaving you guys on the first floor that day.”
I wondered what she was talking about. That was a long time ago.

“Do you remember when I said I sincerely regret that at the banquet? I really meant it. After I woke up, when I heard about the things you achieved in the Crystal Cave, I felt so ashamed and embarrassed.”
“What’s there to be embarrassed about? It was a call any leader would make. I would have done the same.”
Versyl Gowland’s expression tightened at my sincere words. “Don’t joke. You never would have done that.”

Her evaluation of my character was undeserved. If I had been given a ticket out of there with enough seats for all my party members, I would’ve taken the portal out right away. It was only because I was abandoned that I’d worked so hard to survive, not because I had some sort of heroic mission driving me.
But I guessed she thought differently. “You are like the eye of the storm. No matter how strong the winds are blowing at you from all directions, you never get caught up in them.”
Jeez, why are you wasting such complicated metaphors on a barbarian?

I stared at her blankly, wondering if maybe this was some weird attempt to gauge whether I was an evil spirit, but Versyl let out a self-deprecating laugh. “Maybe that’s why... why people gather around you even in the fiercest of storms.”
“It... just turned out that way.”
“...Maybe I shouldn’t have said that. I wasn’t trying to add to the weight on your shoulders. You were going over there to rest, right? Sorry for taking up your time.”
“It’s okay. You get some rest too.”

That was how my conversation with Versyl ended. Afterward, I passed some of the other sprawled-out members of our squadron and lay down near Erwen. The wizard would wake me when the detection spell went off so I was going to get some shut-eye in the meantime.
Eye of the storm, huh?
It was a compliment that didn’t suit me all that well. Unless what she meant was that my life was surrounded by bad luck—that everyone around me got swept up in my misfortune.
“Mister! Wake up!”
It felt like I had only closed my eyes for a few seconds. “Was the spell triggered?”
“Yes. We have to leave quickly.”
God damn it.
Instead of going away, my fatigue seemed even worse.
“In formation!” I wished I could sleep longer but I quickly got up and ready to leave.
How long has it been since, again?
“Marrone, time?”
“Five minutes... Five minutes!”
As the chase continued, the distance between us and the enemy gradually began to narrow. Their speed didn’t necessarily increase, either. We were just that much slower.
Huff... Huff...
It seemed it was impossible for us to recover our stamina with such a short rest. Well, the fatigue we accumulated from over two months of arduous travel was on a whole other level than theirs.
“W-What do we do? They’ll catch up in no time!”
“Why don’t we fight instead? If we tire ourselves out any more, we won’t even be able to fight back properly later.”
Anxiety grew among the crew. I checked the time. It was right after midnight. In other words, only one day left until we escaped Glacier Eye entirely.
One day... might be cutting it close, but it’s possible.

I didn’t have to think it over for long. I always said this, but survival was a series of choices. Those who stood at a crossroads always had to make a decision: what would I give up this time? My answer to this question was very simple.
“McKelly Rayothers!” I immediately stopped the march and called out to one of the wizards. He was the only one in this expedition who knew how to use the spell I needed.
“What’s wrong?” the wizard asked, clearly nervous about the fact that I stopped everyone to talk to him.
“You said you could use the Portal spell when I asked last time. Is that right?”
“Yes... I did say that... but what about the Portal spell?”
Oh, that. It’s nothing big.
“Use it. Right now.”
At my command, a look of confusion appeared on the wizard’s face. “The... Portal? Here?”

It wasn’t that I didn’t get it. The Portal spell commonly used in the labyrinth these days was the improved version. It could only be used once in a lifetime. Of course, considering our current situation, I was sure he wouldn’t complain about using up his one shot here.
“I don’t understand why you’re making such a request. The Portal spell doesn’t work past the sixth floor.”
The improved Portal spell only worked up to the sixth floor. If you used the Portal spell on the seventh floor, you were only wasting a precious, once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
What a polite explanation. You think I don’t know that?
“McKelly Rayothers.” There wasn’t much time so I skipped the exposition and lowered my voice. “I’ll explain why later so do as I say for now. We need that spell right now.”
“...Okay. I’ll prepare it right away.”
“How long will it take?”
“Considering the mana density of our surroundings, one minute should be enough.”
