“Then please get on that.”

As soon as the conversation ended, the wizard started casting and I quickly fired off new instructions to the squad members staring at me blankly. “We’ll be moving as soon as the Portal spell is complete so get ready! From now on, we’re traveling in a breakthrough formation!”
“...Breakthrough formation?”
“Is he planning on fighting them here?”
The rest of the crew had questions about my commands too. However, the team leaders at least set up the formation according to my wishes before approaching me.
“Why are you using Portal magic all of a sudden?”
“Especially when we’re running out of time to escape?”
“I’m most curious about the breakthrough formation. Are you thinking of changing directions?”
They carried out my instructions out of trust but it seemed they were still curious as to the why. “The route we’ll be taking from now on will be more difficult.”
“...More difficult?”
“A difficult path for us will also be a difficult path for the enemy.”
“...Wait, what are you talking about?” Kaislan tilted his head in a way that told me he still didn’t understand. And that was when it happened.
[McKelly Rayothers has cast the rank-one space-time spell Portal.]
The spell was completed and a powerful cluster of light began to form, though only for about a second.
[The darkness of the labyrinth has interfered with space-time.]

The portal fizzled out before it could even properly take shape. As a result, McKelly would never be able to use Portal magic again in his life. That was probably why he was looking at me in such despair right now.
Dddddd!
But I hadn’t been aiming to get out of here with a portal in the first place.
“W-What the—?”
The entire canyon shook with what felt like an earthquake and the crew stood on high alert.
[Special Condition – Momentary Stimulation has been met.]
I knew the improved version of the spell would work. Though it came with many drawbacks, it was still technically classified as rank-one space-time magic.
Whew... it worked...
Things had gone according to plan for now, but I still couldn’t shake the grim curl of my lips. My warrior’s intuition was already telling me that today was going to be an especially difficult day.
[The Glacier Wizard Cariathea has appeared in the area.]

chapters.title: Chapter 419: Eye of the Storm (1)
paragraphs: The Glacier Wizard Cariathea was a rank-three mutant of the Elder Lich class. The conditions for summoning this guy were very simple.
[Special Condition – Momentary Stimulation has been satisfied.]
Sometime between five and ten days before the seventh floor closed, all you had to do was use the rank-one space-time spell in Glacier Eye.
Ddddddddd.
As soon as the canyon stopped violently shaking, monsters crawled up from the cliff below, claws outstretched.
“What the hell? Why are there monsters?”
“Wait, these aren’t the same ones that showed up here before.”
“Skeletons...? There are Skeletons here?”
Momentarily confused by the monsters appearing out of nowhere, our squad members who were already in battle formation hurriedly started swinging their weapons to push them back.
“Yandel, what the hell have you done!?” the team leaders around me asked urgently.
“I used space-time magic to activate one of the Achievements of Gabrielius.”
“Because when it comes to fighting monsters, we have an advantage over Noark.”
Jun spoke up instead of James this time. “What you’re saying is that if we have to fight against the same monsters, we’re in a comparatively better position.”
“Yes. Since they don’t have a priest or wizard, we should be able to maintain this distance until we leave Glacier Eye.”

Not just maintain, actually—we might even be able to widen the distance further since the Skeletons were coming up from below. Since Noark was behind us, they’d have to deal with any Skeletons we left behind. The only wildcard here was Cariathea, who was basically a boss monster.
It’ll take him a day to get up here from down there, though, so we don’t have to worry about him yet.
“Okay, do you understand now?”
“Yes.” Jun nodded and agreed my plan was logical, but Calla seemed to have issues with it.
“Is this what you meant about taking the hard road? The front line isn’t properly equipped—there will be untold amounts of damage!”
He definitely wasn’t wrong. Most of the warriors had taken off their equipment. There would inevitably be casualties.
“Still, I think this is better than fighting them head-on considering the state we’re in, so get back in position.”
I told him I wouldn’t be taking any notes, but Calla still tried his luck one last time. “What... difference will reaching the top of Glacier Eye like this make?”
Are you being serious?

“It’ll make a huge difference.” It seemed he hadn’t expected such a confident answer as Calla stared at me blankly. Maybe he wasn’t good with people being firm with him. I didn’t know, but rather than explaining myself in detail, I infused more confidence into my tone. “So trust and follow me.”
“...Okay.”
Okay, are we done now?
“What are you all looking at? Go take care of your party members.”
I sent the team leaders around me back to their positions and headed to the front of the group. That was my position.
“Mister, don’t push yourself too much.”
“What? You’re not going to try to stop me this time?”
“Well... you have the same look in your eyes as you did in Crystal Cave back then...”
I hadn’t been able to look in a mirror back then so I had no way of knowing if that was true. I did hope to achieve a similar result, though.
[You have cast Giantization.]
After turning on my now-default battle mode, I raised my shield and hammer. Maybe it was because I threw out my armor and was currently only wearing fur clothes over my bare skin, but...
Wow, I’m no different from a real barbarian.
This was True Barbarian Mode.
“Yandel, we can depart now!” As soon as Kaislan gave me the okay from his position near the back, I moved forward.
“Ah.” I jerked when I saw the Skeleton blocking my path.
Right, I don’t have to hide anymore. Okay, that’s one positive, at least. Then here I go.
“Behel–ahhh!” I believed that the blessing of my ancestors was with me.
Boom! Boom!
I ran forward with thundering footfalls and covered my entire upper body for a shield charge.
Kwaaang!

Using my shoulder to add weight to the shield, I pushed the bone bastards away. For reference, I was the only one on the front line. The rest of the front line, including the close-range damage dealers, had been sent to the back to defend the flanks and rear.
“Push them back!”
The crew followed me, taking care of the Skeletons climbing up the cliff as they did.
“Agh!”
“Get lost, you son of a bitch!”
Peppered into the sounds of fierce battle was the occasional groan. This was to be expected, considering the vanguard had tossed out all their armor.
Slide!
One of the Skeletons slashed through someone’s skin with its rib as it passed by.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-five curse spell Regeneration Prevention.]

Concerned that people’s Natural Regeneration could work against them, the wizards continued to cast curse spells on their allies, but it was the equivalent of peeing your pants to stay warm in the winter. It only briefly prevented the wounds from worsening. It didn’t heal the injury itself.
Slice!

Cuts opened wider with each violent movement and our unhealed wounds continued to ooze blood. In the meantime, injuries festered and deteriorated. No amount of curses could reduce Natural Regeneration to zero.
“Ahhhhhh!”

One hour, two hours, three hours. As the amount of time we spent pushing through the monsters increased, the number of injuries sustained by the squadron went up as well. It was a vicious cycle where even the smallest of injuries slowed you down, leading to even more injuries. Of course, they wouldn’t be getting hurt like this if mana shields were protecting them.
But that’d be like drinking seawater to quench your thirst.
How could you cover this many people with mana shields? If we did that, our wizards would run out of mana in three hours.
Kwaaang!
Damn it, I really can’t let my attention slip for even a second.
The situation in the back was pretty dire too, but mine wasn’t all that better.
“Behel–ahhh!”

I was clearing the path ahead by using all the force I was capable of to push the monsters out of our way. The amount of energy that burned was extreme. No, energy wasn’t even the problem. If it weren’t for Primordial Cell and Soul Dive, I would’ve run out of MP a long time ago and Giantization would’ve been deactivated.
Ugh.

Not only that, but injuries were accumulating on my body as well. My Physical Resistance made me essentially immune to these trash mobs, but Skeletons didn’t just use physical attacks. Even someone like me ended up bloodied if they took ice damage from a Bone Blast to the face.
“Yandel! Another one in front of you!”

Not long after I killed one, another huge Skeleton appeared. Since it was four heads taller than me in Giantization mode, it wouldn’t be far-fetched to call it large, but in reality, this guy fell into the medium-sized category. The large Skeleton was a whole other beast.
Boom! Boom!
Case in point, a super-huge Skeleton climbed up the cliff, its red eyes glowing in the dark.
“B-Below! It’s coming up again!”
“Prieeest!”
Before this guy could reach us, the priests used a series of divine powers to knock him down like last time.

“Kwohhhhhh!” The super-huge Skeleton let out a bloodthirsty howl that echoed through the entire chamber before disappearing. That wasn’t much of a relief, though. We all knew it would come back up again in a few minutes to see if there was something to eat.
Crack!
For now, I used Swing to crush the skull of the medium-sized Skeleton blocking my path. Then, using my shield again, I pushed back the rest of the bony pricks to clear the way.

“Hehehe.” As I was slogging forward without so much as a moment to catch my breath, I found myself laughing for some reason. Not because I was happy, but because I felt like I’d have a breakdown if I didn’t.
Squeeze!
My muscles screamed.
Crack!
My mind was blank.
“Ahhhhhh!”
But despite it all, my body steadfastly repeated the same routine over and over, and my brain kept my thoughts as positive as possible.
The good news is there’s no sign of the enemy catching up with us yet.

It had been about four hours since this wave of monsters began. Inferring our distance using detection magic was no longer possible because of the monsters, but our pursuers hadn’t caught up with us yet. I was sure those bastards were trying to avoid getting hurt.
They’re probably moving forward as cautiously as possible.

On the other hand, we were burning our bodies like blocks of coal just before they turned into ash. Even if I got hurt, getting the squadron up this hill came first. It wouldn’t be fair if they were to catch up when we were operating under a mindset like that.
Wobble!
Just then, my legs momentarily buckled before I managed to regain my balance.
...Did I lose too much blood? Hmm, I think so.
My body was like a mangled water balloon right now. Wounds that would normally have crusted over within a few seconds were gushing blood all over.
This is getting dangerous.
I made a snap judgment. That was what survival was all about—choosing the lesser of the available evils. “Marrone, burn my wounds with fire.”
“...W-What did you say?”
“I think I need to stop the bleeding now.”

“S-Stop the bleeding? What kind of bizarre... How can you say something like that with such a straight face?!” The wizard was shocked by my request. Aside from the pain, the burns could fester and worsen until they were unhealable.
That wouldn’t leave me any worse off than I was now, though. The wounds were rotting already. “It’ll get better once we reach the top, anyway.” Our priority right now was reaching our destination.

Realizing she wouldn’t be able to convince me otherwise, Marrone issued a disclaimer. “If anything goes wrong, this may turn into an injury that can’t be resolved even with divine power. It can lead to permanent damage to the body...”
Jeez, you sound like a doctor telling me not to drink or smoke for three days.
I let her words go in one ear and out the other like the barbarian I was. “Still, it’s better than dying here.”
“I’ll do it. I’ll do it. But I don’t understand. Why on earth are you so...?” She clenched her fists like she didn’t get it.
Jeez, she has a bad memory for a wizard. What doesn’t she understand?
“I promised before we left that I’ll do the hardest work, so you all just have to follow me.”
“Ah...” Marrone’s jaw dropped. She stared at me blankly for a moment before shutting her mouth and seemingly making up her mind. Then, she cast the fire spell on her hand.
“Hehehe...” I sob-laughed and tried to look at the bright side as much as possible.
Yeah, at least it’s not cold anymore.

One hour, two hours, three hours. As the grueling journey continued, I was able to see another side of the crew with my own eyes. I used to think they were as spineless as jellyfish. But now I could see that they were more like baby birds, and pretty tough ones.
“Can you burn my wounds with fire too?”
“Please use an ice spell on mine. I think that’ll hurt less.”
They called me nuts for cauterizing the bleeding without a potion, but now the rest of the front line was copying my actions. Among them was an even worse patient than me.
“Just take this arm off.”
At Futa Rickerburn’s words, the priest froze. “...I’m sorry?”
“I’m not thick. Even divine power can’t fix this much rot. I lost feeling in it earlier too.”
“Um... s-still, you should rethink this...”

“Oh, don’t look at me like that. Is there a one-armed adventurer in this world without a story to tell at the bar? I’ve seen a lot of people without an arm, but losing one in a situation like this isn’t too bad a deal.”

It was the kind of pros-cons calculation that left even the barbarian next to him (me) dumbfounded. But it must have been because of that kind of thinking that we were finally able to reach the top of Glacier Eye.
[Field Effect – Glacier Eye has been deactivated.]
This was the moment I’d been desperately waiting for.
Slump!
Upon cresting the last hill, the warriors collapsed immediately, on the verge of exhaustion. Terrible wasn’t enough to describe the way they all looked, but huge smiles decorated each of their faces.
“We’re here...”
“Fuck, fuck, fuck... We’re... really here...”

“What are you all doing? Wizards! Remove the curse spells, quick! We need to start treatments right away!” The priests who’d been forced to helplessly watch our desperate struggle the whole way here gathered all the divine power they had despite also looking like they could collapse at any moment.
“...You did well. Really.”
“This arm... will be difficult to heal. I’m sorry.”
The priests gave the front line guilty looks as they began treatment.
“Hmm, is that so? It’s fine, don’t worry about it,” said one of the front liners on the receiving end of these looks.
Kaislan cautiously made a request of one of the priests. “Hey, I know you’re tired but I want to ask you a favor...”
“I’m listening.”
“I just need one, sincere prayer.”
“A prayer...?”
“Yes, for those who died along the way.”
“...Of course.”

The priests kneeled with their hands clasped together reverently. At this, the human members of our squadron who were lying down climbed to their feet and made the sign of the cross. Dwarves, beastpeople, elves, and even the sole barbarian, who didn’t believe in human gods, did the same. Though we didn’t make the sign of the cross over our chests as they did, we closed our eyes and meditated, making a sincere prayer to our ancestral gods, guardian spirits, or the World Tree.
“...Rest in peace.”
Whoever is listening... please lead them to the sanctuary they each believe in.

Our squadron currently had twenty-two surviving members. While crossing Glacier Eye, two more people died on top of summoner Milburn Naria. That was because it was a harsh environment that you couldn’t conquer with the determination to burn flesh and cut off an arm alone. Matt Hybriham had been a paladin from Team Four. Percival Eric Coulson had been a knight from Team Five. He was Kaislan’s subordinate and a friend who had been in the same unit as him for over ten years.
“Kaislan...”
“Haha, don’t look at me like that. He fulfilled his duty as a soldier. I’m sure he doesn’t regret it.”
“...Doesn’t regret it? How could that be?”

“Because you were there. Thanks to that, he got to die while fighting to live until the bitter end. A death like that... can never be meaningless. He died not for the palace but while following me... and following in your footsteps.”
“I see...”
“I’m fine, so you do what you have to do.”
After our short prayer, we got back to work. The priests continued treating the warriors and the wizards drew magic circles on the ground.
“Wait! You can’t move yet!”
“It’s fine. Treat the others first.”
“What are you talking about? You’re the one in the worst condition right now!”
What do you mean? If it was really that bad, I wouldn’t even be able to move.
Ignoring the priest’s protests, I checked on the rest of the team. Until now, I’d been too busy clearing the path forward to pay attention to what was behind me.
“Akurava.” As I looked around, I headed over to her. “How much food do we have left?”
“None anymore.”
“Looks like they ate the rest of the beef jerky even while they fought, then.”
“...You were the one who forced us to eat it.”
Jeez, don’t scold me.
“I’m saying everyone did a good job.” I changed the subject. “Where do you think they are now?”
“I don’t know... I’m wondering that too. Considering how tenacious they were about following us, I don’t think they’ll give up all that easily.”
“I see...”
“I’ll keep an eye on Glacier Eye. So go rest. If you fall, that’s it for our squadron.”
“Right...”
After my conversation with Akurava, I walked over to the nearest priest to finish receiving treatment and sat down near the entrance to Glacier Eye.
“You did well, Mister...”
The peace and quiet around us made the hell we were in earlier seem like a distant dream. Even the cold snow on my back felt cozy. But as always, these tranquil moments passed in the blink of an eye.
“Yandel! It’s them!”
The moment the shout left Akurava’s lips, our squadron all got up from their naps and stood in formation.
Pyuuu! Pop!

We shot a signal flare into the bottom of Glacier Eye. The space under the dark cliff brightened to reveal our twelve pursuers climbing the hill. The enemy looked better off than I expected. They maintained their formation while they moved and patiently fought off the Skeletons. They had no noticeable injuries either. It looked like they were well-fed, too, because they didn’t look thin. Unlike us, who arrived here on half-rotted legs. Well, that made sense, though.
Yeah, it’s because they came up so carefully that they only got here now.

I gritted my teeth and looked down. They were looking up at us in turn, their eyes full of questions. It was obvious what they were thinking. It must have seemed strange to them that the frontline warriors blocking their path weren’t wearing any armor.
Smirk.
The Dragon Slayer whispered something to his comrades before looking up at me with the corner of his mouth raised.
What, is he mocking me? If so, that’s a bit funny. Do they still not realize the situation they’re in?

Does he know why I threw all my equipment away and ran all the way here in the first place? It had been an entirely forward-looking decision. In Ice Rock, the value of the field trumped the value of your equipment any day.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect – Glacier Eye has activated.]
Okay, the field effect starts right here.
Step.
I took just one step back and stopped right at that border before shouting at my squadron with a smirk. “Prepare for battle!”
Now it’s your turn to suffer a little.

chapters.title: Chapter 420: Eye of the Storm (2)
paragraphs: In the Dragon’s Mountains, Noark’s troops and the palace’s army had formed a long battle frontier as they engaged in a full-scale power struggle.
“There’s a report that the Traitor has appeared on the Western Front!”
Eltora Tercerion, the commander of the Third Corps, frowned when he received this report from his subordinate. The man hadn’t been seen for a while. “Traitor, huh? All right, you may leave now.”
“Yes sir!”
The subordinate believed the Traitor’s presence had upset his superior, but the real reason for Eltora’s frown was something else.
The Traitor has reappeared, huh?

Eltora wasn’t an idiot. A few days ago, Noark’s western troops were spotted heading north. It was highly likely they had redirected their forces to chase the expedition team that was attempting to escape on their own.
Does that mean the chase is over?
Eltora subconsciously clenched his fists.
Father... Damn it, what the hell is the marquess thinking?
Right before leading the army into the labyrinth, Eltora received two secret orders from his father. The first was to ignore the squadron’s request for rescue. And the other...
“If they return alive anyway, kill them without anyone knowing.”
He didn’t know if he should feel relieved about it, but Eltora at least hadn’t had to carry out the second secret mission. The squadron had gone in the opposite direction as the one they were in.
Are they really all dead?
It was truly a contradictory feeling. Eltora had helped abandon them. He also would have been in a tight spot if the expedition came back alive.
Thump!

But he couldn’t believe it. Were they really dead? The same Bjorn Yandel who somehow came back from the Crystal Cave? Eltora closed his eyes, lost in thought. He tried to imagine what he would do if he were the commander of the squadron.
The reason they fled north instead of south where their allies were must have been to catch the enemy off guard.
It wasn’t a bad move, especially in that it allowed them to dodge two bullets at once.
Did he know?
Well, Eltora had no way of finding out. But even if Yandel somehow did know, that didn’t change the outcome. There didn’t seem to be an escape route in the north.

In enemy territory with no hope of reinforcements arriving, an army closing in, and a tired crew... If that were me, what would I decide? No, if I were Bjorn Yandel, that ridiculously decisive man, what would I choose?
...Ice Rock.
Suddenly, his thoughts ended up there. If they intended to keep running and not give up, there was no other option than that.
Even if they really went there, though, they won’t be returning alive.

No matter what theories he came up with, none of them seemed to have optimistic prospects. That was by no means because Eltora underestimated Bjorn Yandel’s abilities. Ice Rock? Glacier Eye? He could definitely overcome those hurdles. Considering the competence he showed in the Crystal Cave, it made no sense for that man to be bested by hardships like those. However, he’d run up against the wrong enemy.
There’s no way the marquess didn’t know he might do this.

Anyone would consider heading to Ice Rock an unconventional move. But ultimately, it was a move even Eltora could think of. Of course his father would have prepared for the possibility. That man prepared for every situation to the point of exaggeration.
The chances of Bjorn Yandel coming back alive... are nonexistent.
This was what Eltora Tercerion concluded as he tried to ignore the inexplicable pounding of his heart.
Thump!
Our current formation was simple. There was a narrow side road just wide enough for about four people to stand.
“Schuitz, are you sure about this?”
“I told you. It’ll be too tight if you’re all here too.”
Our first line of defense against the enemy was me and me alone. This was the solution I’d come up with to the problem of how to bring as many people as possible back home.
“Don’t run yourself to the ground. We’re right behind you.”
“That’s reassuring. I’ll trust—”

Just then, a bloodthirsty shout from the Dragon Slayer ricocheted off the walls. “Bjorn Yandel! This is where you’ve run away to?” Judging by the confidence in his voice, it seemed he still hadn’t realized the situation he was in.
Unfortunately, not everyone was as empty-headed as him. “Vagos, calm down.” One adventurer reached a hand out in front of the Dragon Slayer, who seemed liable to run forward at any moment.
Grit.
Someone behind me gritted their teeth at the sight of his face. I understood the sentiment.
“That bastard killed Miss Naria...”
Whether Troll Summoner Milburn Naria was an evil spirit or not, she was a woman whose only wish was for us to get home alive, even as she stood on death’s door herself. And this man had killed her.
“Bjorn Yandel, right?” The guy who stopped the Dragon Slayer walked forward and spoke to me.
Is this guy the real leader?

The way he carried himself was confident enough to warrant that question. Normally, if you didn’t have authority, you would be concerned with what others thought when you did something like that. But it looked like even that Dragon Slayer bastard was keeping his mouth shut and letting this guy talk.
After some thought, I decided to accept the conversation request. “Yes, I’m Bjorn Yandel.” I was curious too. “And who are you?”
He answered without much hesitation. “Manua Repeles.”
I intended to cross that name off my kill list.
“I’m going to kill that bastard...”
No, the name would be written in all of our kill lists. The moment the guy started talking to us, murderous intent began to radiate from my squad members behind me. But no one did anything rash.
“Manua Repeles... never heard of you.”
“Well, I’m sure. I’m currently considered a secret weapon.”

This added more credibility to my earlier hypothesis. I first began to speculate when I saw that they were armed with high-ranking essences that only appeared on the eighth floor and up. It seemed these guys were more than likely the eighth-floor raiders.
“So, what do you want?” Now that I had his name on the kill list, I decided to hear him out.
It seemed he wasn’t the type to beat around the bush either as he immediately opened his mouth. “I have a proposal for you.”
“A proposal...?”
“As I said before, we are a secret weapon. Even if we succeed in taking you all out, it’ll be a huge loss if one or two of us die in the process.”
“Get to your point.”

At my words, he lifted a hand and showed me his palm. “Five. So we can save face, hand over five people. If you do, we’ll be satisfied with that and leave the rest of you alone. Ah, of course, you don’t have to be one of the five, Bjorn Yandel.”
Haha, I was wondering what he was going to say...
There were times in your life when you ended up so dumbfounded that you couldn’t even get mad. That was exactly how I felt at the moment.
“It’s by no means a bad offer. If you give us just five people, the rest of you can all go home alive.”

“I don’t know, that sounds like a suggestion I should be making instead. Give me five of your heads and I’ll send the rest of you back alive. Ah, of course, you and Regal Vagos need to be included in those five.”
“So you choose punishment,” said Repeles. “I hope you won’t regret it.”
What is this dimwitted son of a bitch talking about? Alcohol is always alcohol no matter how smooth it goes down, and poison is always poison no matter how sweet it is.
“Regret is something your mom does.”
“...What?” The man blinked. It seemed he’d never heard this kind of insult before even in foul-mouthed Noark.

This wasn’t the time for laughter so I plowed forward, staring at his bald head as it reddened under the light of the flare. “After all, your mom probably didn’t know that the child she went through the trouble of birthing would end up being a coward who was all talk in front of the enemy. Did you pee yourself when you saw us? You guys smell so rotten that I can’t really tell. Why aren’t you saying anything? Ah, is it because you don’t have a mother—”
“You bastard!”

“Wow, I guess you really don’t, considering how worked up you are. Don’t be so upset. I understand. The reason you grew up into such a coward is probably because you didn’t have a proper upbringing when you were younger. And the reason you lost all your hair was probably from all the heartache—”
“I’ll kill you!”
Jeez, why do you keep interrupting me? Now I see he’s not just reckless but also rude.
I was a bit annoyed but I had achieved my goal. After all, this was how the world had always worked.
“Yeah, no, I’m not gonna die.”
The one who gets pissed off first loses.
Case in point, Baldy Repeles was baited by my thoroughly provocative comments and kicked off the ground.
Surprisingly, the Dragon Slayer lunged forward to restrain him. “Repeles! He’s just like that, don’t get worked up! If you fall for his manipulation, you’re only doing him a favor.”
Smirk.
You think that’s going to work? When his bald head is flushed that red?
Dash.

Soon, the guy broke away from the Dragon Slayer and ran at me with clenched fists. His class was Boxer. This was a rare class in the labyrinth. Though useful on the lower floors, this class didn’t have any core essences that were particularly beneficial once you hit the middle floors. They did get some good active skills later on, though. A prime example was the one he was using now.
[Manua Repeles has cast Iron Fist.]
Iron Fist could be obtained from the eighth-floor Rift. Its effects were simple.
Flash!
It provided the user the ability to make a thirteen-foot dash that verged on teleportation and a knockback that ignored the laws of physics.
Kwaaaang!
[A fixed amount of damage is taken in proportion to the caster’s Strength and the target’s Physical Resistance.]

The damage was more painful the sturdier you were. This skill was the reason everything had gone wrong for us in the last battle. Our mana shield had shattered after a few punches, and our battle line collapsed as they were knocked back. Meanwhile, having to choose dodge over defense meant I was unable to properly execute the tank’s main mission of stopping the enemy in its tracks. But this time, things were different.
A blow so bad I could feel my intestines shaking? Though the pain was excruciating without a mana shield... so what?
[Roita Mamander has cast Emergency Regeneration.]
A heal came in immediately afterward.
[Benjamin Orman has cast Moonlight Shrine.]
The border between increased Natural Regeneration and Glacier Eye’s hellish status effects lay right between me and the enemy.
Slide.
I looked down at the fist embedded in my abdomen and yelled, “Behel–aaah!”

The man flinched at the sudden shout. When I brought my hammer down on top of him, he stepped back. He was definitely going to use Iron Fist again once he put some space between us. That skill was good and all and didn’t have a cooldown time, but it was only effective if you rushed in from a certain distance.
You think I’ll let you do that?
I immediately linked Transcendence and Eye of the Storm. Earlier, the battle line had collapsed and numerous enemies had broken past me, so I hadn’t been able to use this combo.
Shaaaaaaaaa!

Making sure to get my timing just right, I swung my hammer at the guy as he was sucked toward me with a confused look on his face. Unfortunately, I didn’t get to have much fun. This guy was a tank too.
[Manua Repeles has cast Invincible.]
He crossed his hands over his head and blocked the hammer. As soon as the brief exchange was over, the people behind him started running in too.
[Ricky Aymond has cast Target of Thunder.]
[Kayle Elbad Zenegger has cast Land’s End Thorn.]
Skills were shot at me. Some bypassed my Physical Resistance and slammed into my body, but I recovered quickly thanks to concentrated healing from our priests.
[Anne Parvela has cast Thunder Rush.]
Between one instant and the next, a close-combat fighter passed me by before I could stop her.
[Anne Parvela has cast Gather.]
That combo of skills allowed her to teleport two comrades within a certain distance over to her.
[Puran Cullen has cast Possession.]
[Marione Trider has cast Dance of Cataclysm.]

They were like some sort of tactical assault unit. Well, their logic was probably that if they got over here, at least the field effect would be lifted. They likely figured it would be better to fight here, even if it was in the middle of enemy territory.
Looks like they’re underestimating us a lot.
Even if their skills were a bit better than ours individually, did they really think three of them could take us down alone?
“Don’t worry about things on this end! I won’t let anyone else through!”

I decided to leave the assault unit to my comrades. Even if they managed to stab me from behind, I was confident I wouldn’t die so long as I stood on the healing side of the barrier. I didn’t think they’d get the chance to hit me in the first place.
“Kill them! It’s time to wield the sword of vengeance!”
“You think we’ll be defeated like last time?!”
“Rahhhhhh!”

The melee began. The enemies beyond the border, including Baldy, ran forward to try to get through me. The three people who crossed the border had their backs to each other, intending to somehow break our formation.
Shaaaaaa!
The priests located on a safe hill a short distance away cast divine spells indiscriminately, healing and dealing damage at the same time.
“Get rid of the priests first!”
As a result, the enemy tried to aim for the priests first and fired off various skills.
Shaaaaaa!

However, none of their attacks were able to reach the hill where the priests and wizards stood and instead vanished into thin air. That was because of the magic circle they’d been working hard to draw as soon as we arrived up here. As long as the priests were protected, we couldn’t lose this fight.
“Barrier magic...!”
Realizing their projectiles weren’t working, the enemy began devising other methods.
[Mike Roymus has cast Slime Walk.]
[Lia Andes has cast Flame Walk.]
The enemy used their skills to try and climb the cliff themselves.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast High-Speed Fire.]
Of course, they were stopped by our long-rangers.
As the battle progressed, the tide was far more in our favor than I expected.
“...You worthless bastards!”

The three people who had come over with such enthusiasm were unable to overcome their lack of numbers and were getting beaten up. I stood my ground like an iron wall to keep the remainder of their group from crossing over and providing backup.
“Damn it...!”
“Why doesn’t that monster ever get tired?!”
“Kill him! Kill him somehow!”

The more unfavorable the situation became, the more aggressively our opponents attacked us. The reason was very simple. Everyone, including them, was injured. They realized if they retreated now, they wouldn’t get another opportunity to win this fight.
“Don’t hold back!”
“No matter how much you get hurt, if we win this battle, it’s over!”
The attacks turned even more intense as injuries accumulated. Like those of the Dragon Slayer, who was swinging his sword at me in tandem with Baldy.
“Hey, let me ask you a question. I’m just curious, but when is it coming? That time when even death won’t be able to save me.”
...Grit.

Finally forced to face the facts, the bastard stopped trying to stab me with his knife so he could step back and glare at me. “You always did force me to make sacrifices,” the prick muttered, then whipped out his ultimate finisher with a determined look on his face.
[Regal Vagos has cast Dragon Speech: Silence of the Soul.]
Oh, you’re finally using that.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has deactivated.]
My body shrank in an instant. The hammer and shield that once felt as light as a feather to me now felt as heavy as a thousand pounds.
[You have fallen into a state of Soul Exhaustion. All of your stats have temporarily decreased by 70%.]
It was the same status effect I experienced in the Labyrinth of Larcaz.
Wow, this takes me back. At the time I really thought this was the end.
Cough! Cough! Karrrgh...!
What the fuck? Why is he coughing up blood all of a sudden? Ah, did using Dragon Speech just now put a strain on his body? Huh, he’s like a bee that dies after one sting.
“Regal Vagos! Are you okay?”
“I’m fine... kill him... Hehehe...” It was strange watching him shoot me such a hateful look even while staggering like that.
[You have cast Soul Dive. Your Soul Power will regenerate at a rate proportional to the amount of Soul Power you have consumed.]
Would it be weird to say I kind of felt sorry for him?
[Your state of Soul Exhaustion has been lifted.]
I could deal with this with a single skill.

chapters.title: Chapter 421: Eye of the Storm (3)
paragraphs: Dragon Speech: Silence of the Soul was an incredibly overpowered skill that burned through a certain amount of the target’s MP to put them in a state of Soul Exhaustion. But even this skill had its weaknesses. The dragon tribe gramps had laid it out for me during our conversation all those years ago. Apparently, it could only burn up to 50 percent of your maximum MP. In other words, if you maintained an amount that was higher than that, your MP wouldn’t hit zero and you wouldn’t end up having to deal with Soul Exhaustion.
That’s probably why he’s been saving it.

After escaping Glacier Eye, my body had mostly recovered thanks to the healing I received from the priests, but MP was a different story. My MP was already at almost half. Using Giantization to fight these guys and using Swing willy-nilly, I had consumed a significant amount. That was why I’d deliberately provoked the guy.
“I’m just curious, but when is it coming? That time when even death won’t be able to save me.”

At this rate, I’d run out of MP. I had Soul Dive, of course, but it had a cooldown time. The moment I used it, I lost another way to counter his Dragon Speech. That was why I forced him to use Dragon Speech now.
Cough! Cough! Karrrgh...!

As a result, the Dragon Slayer was now incapable of combat. I’d noticed he seemed to have a hard time whenever he used Dragon Speech in the Labyrinth of Larcaz too. But to think he’d become this incapacitated. That was unexpected.
[You have cast Soul Dive.]
[You have cast Giantization.]
However, with the enemy’s ultimate finisher gone and my MP recovered, I had nothing left to worry about.
“H-How...?” His picture-perfect expression was the icing on the cake.
“Behel—aaaaaah!” It felt like the spirit of my ancestors was surging through my body.
[Manua Repeles has cast Iron Fist.]
I took Baldy’s next jab with a laugh.
Hmm, so just as I thought, the Dragon Speech didn’t affect these guys. Well, if he was planning to use Dragon Speech, he would’ve already made a Bind with the others in advance.
Noark’s front line, including Baldy, hadn’t been exposed to Silence of the Soul. The rear line seemed to be outside its range too.
Thankfully, my squadron was out of range as well.

This was actually the main reason why I sent the rest of the group back. Acting as a second line of defense against the assault unit was important, too, but I had to keep them away from Dragon Speech at all costs.

The reason why he didn’t use Dragon Speech in the middle of our squadron was probably because he figured I was the biggest threat. He probably also did the math and realized that his life would be in danger if he ended up incapacitated in the middle of our formation.
When I thought about it like that, this couldn’t have been funnier.
“You always did force me to make sacrifices.”
This is a sacrifice? If you’ve decided to cut your arm off, then you should be prepared to cut off the entire shoulder blade too.
To throw the ace up his sleeve away so carelessly... if he were really determined to make a sacrifice, it would’ve been an extremely big issue for us.
This is a good thing. But...
Despite being a relief, it also felt incredibly unfair. No, more accurately, it felt... senseless.
Because of someone like this, Dwalkie was...

He was a high-ranking member of Orcules, a top dog and notorious criminal who killed the ancient elder dragon. Nevertheless, that didn’t change who he really was. Dwalkie had been a much greater person than he ever could be.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm. By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
I used my grab skill to pull the Dragon Slayer in. He was dragged in by the strong gust of wind, still weak and coughing up blood.
Crack!
The moment my hammer came down, his left shoulder was pulverized. “Ahhh—!”
Oops, I was aiming for the head. I guess he twisted his body there.
Well, I was sure there would be another chance. Setting my regrets aside, I blocked Baldy, who had rushed in to save the Dragon Slayer. No, wait, it wasn’t just him.
[Mike Roymus has cast Earth Leveling. Damage taken by allies within a certain radius is reduced by half, and the remaining half is taken by the caster instead.]
He was a blunt weapon warrior who served a similar function to a tank.
[Lia Andes has cast Wave of Fire. All Fire damage temporarily significantly increases, and additional effects are applied the closer you are to the center of the damage.]
She was a rare case: a close-combat fire ability user. It seemed these three had been working together for some time as they deftly swept in to pester me once the Dragon Slayer fell back.
[Kayle Elbad Zenegger has cast Land’s End Thorn.]
The long-range attacks coming in from the rear from time to time were the cherry on top. Since I had no armor, they pierced and sliced through my body.
[Roita Mamander has cast Advanced Healing.]
[Benjamin Orman has cast Advanced Healing.]
But thanks to the buffs the priests were slathering on me, their efforts weren’t enough to push me back.
[Kelvus Ayrne has cast the rank-four black magic spell Mark of Evil. The efficacy of all regeneration effects applied to the target is significantly reduced.]
[Benjamin Orman has cast Moonlight of Purification. All negative effects applied to the target are removed.]
The dark wizards persistently cast curse spells on me but these kinds of things were easier lifted than cast.
“Don’t overdo it, just block!”

I might have been able to take down one or two if I attacked them more proactively, but we maintained a tight-knit defensive formation. That was what tower defense games were all about, right? As long as the opponent didn’t penetrate your line, you won the game. Our current situation wasn’t much different.
It’s not like they can retreat, anyway.

To be exact, it didn’t matter if the enemy ran because their escape route was blocked. Monsters crawled out of the woodwork behind them, and even the boss monster was coming up with hunger in its eyes. I didn’t know about the others, but the three who got past me and were currently on the receiving end of a good beating would see their bodies rot within a few days of returning to Glacier Eye. Would they be able to escape to the eighth floor in that condition when they clearly didn’t even have food anymore?

“Damn it, where did this guy...?!” The blunt weapon warrior who started a reckless power struggle with me was thrown back with a single kick, a despondent look on his face. “I thought no one outside could stop us!”

Ah, so that was the hope they’d been harboring while cultivating themselves on the eighth floor without the palace’s knowledge. Well, it wasn’t a completely futile hope. The eighth floor was riddled with essences that could each become the basis of someone’s build.
But at least get the combination right.

For a Shield Barbarian, the core skill needed was Giantization. It was a rank-five essence that could be obtained by hunting an Orc Hero, and when used in combination with Union, it was incredibly efficient. But blindly stacking random essences on top of each other wasn’t a good recipe for success.
“Repeles! Let’s retreat for now!”
Did they lose morale upon seeing the way I refused to budge? The blunt weapon warrior requested a retreat but Baldy did not grant it.
“To where?!”
“We need to at least regroup—!”
“Stop spouting nonsense and fight!”
They knew if they stepped back for a moment to regroup, they’d end up having to fight a more difficult battle after. Ultimately, they had only one choice.
“W-We just have to kill this guy!”
“The rest are easy!”
Break through and move forward.
“Behell—aaaaaah!” Of course, I didn’t intend to let them through.
The battle continued, and the pendulum, once swung, never moved in the opposite direction again.
“...We can’t take anymore!”
Two of the adventurers in the “assault unit” who broke past me to attack the main unit ran by me to rejoin their troops.
“Cullen...?”
“Isn’t it obvious? He’s dead!”
The three fought desperately, but once one of them died, they were unable to keep going and fled.
Okay, that makes eleven people.

The number of enemies had gone down. Our side, on the other hand, had suffered no casualties. There was a squad member who was injured as the heals were all focused on me at the moment, but even that was mostly a minor injury.
The real fight starts now.
Rather than letting down my guard, I raised it even higher. That was because they’d definitely have realized it now. At this rate, everyone here could die.
“...To think we have to risk our lives in a place like this.”
Humans were calculative creatures. That was why, when standing at a crossroads, they ultimately chose to give up everything besides the possibility of survival.
This is the scariest state for an enemy to be in.
To put it in boss monster terms, this was a frenzy pattern, where the enemy was fighting with everything they had to survive.
[Your Soul Power is insufficient. Giantization has deactivated.]
Just in time, my MP ran out and my body shrank.
“Yandel, go rest in the back for a bit.” Amelia immediately came up to my right.
“That’s right. We’ll handle things here.” Ravien stood on my left.
“We’ll take your place.” Jun and Kaislan also walked out from the back group to join us.
Yeah, I don’t know about Kaislan but Jun should be able to take on the tank position.

Deciding it would be a better use of my energy to trust my comrades instead of being stubborn, I quickly withdrew from the front line and moved to the second. I planned to run forward immediately if anything happened.
“That monster has retreated!”
“Now, now’s our chance!”
As soon as the thorn in their side was gone, Noark regained their fighting spirit and rushed forward. However, it didn’t take long for that spirit to break.
[Jun Arshen has cast Divine Opening.]
When he activated all his skills, Jun turned into a monster tanker just like me. As for Kaislan, Ravien, and Amelia, if any of those three cut you the wrong way, you’d die.
Whooom!
“Be careful!”
As a good offense was said to be the best defense, sharp counterattacks aimed at the enemy’s weak spots were applied liberally. The enemy was left unable to launch offensives as actively as before.
“Repeles, Ricky Aymond is down!”
Before long, we secured an additional win. The long-range line composed of Erwen, Akurava, and others finally won the tug of war and killed one of the enemy’s ranged damagers. This was great for us.
[Status effect Whisper of Immortality is now active.]
Unlike the people on our side who died earlier, one of Glacier Eye’s field effects activated and this guy rose up as a zombie.
“H-Hurry, push him out! Drop him—”
“Arghhh!” The special ability user who turned into a Lich began indiscriminately attacking his allies before finally being taken down and knocked off the cliff.

We weren’t able to score any additional bonus points thanks to their fast response, unfortunately, but the remaining long-rangers were two dark wizards, one special ability user, and one priest of Karui. After that, an even fiercer battle ensued. Kaislan retreated from the front line after a serious injury but a tank waiting in the second row immediately filled his spot to block the way.
Pant, pant, pant...

The way Sven Parav was nervously hyperventilating didn’t make him seem all that dependable, but he was still a paladin. Excluding Jun and I, he was the only main tank here. There was only one main replacement for a close-range damager too.
“Emily, come back!”

Amelia returned to the second line once her MP ran out, and the warrior from Team Three, Rick Jugusta, stepped up. We made use of every advantage our superior numbers granted us in this narrow passage to deal with the enemy.
Stab!
Still, sacrifices were made. A sharp, black thorn stabbed through Jugusta’s upper body. It was the same move that had killed Might Million, a tank, instantly during the battle in Deadwood.
Grit...
Rick Jugusta died soon after being sent forward. Since he was outside Glacier Eye’s boundary, the Whisper of Immortality didn’t activate.
“N-No! Rick...!”
Right, he... was Calla’s friend.
“Futa Rickerburn! What are you doing? Stop them!”

The scout and close-range damage dealer from Team Two hurriedly filled the empty spot. This wasn’t the kind of situation where he could rest in the back just because he was missing an arm. He himself said he could fight.
“Rick...!” As soon as Rickerburn filled the empty slot on the front line, Calla ran forward from the back to gather his dead friend in his arms.
“Calla, go back to your position,” I said coldly. Perhaps what he needed right now were words of comfort, but what he needed and what he needed to do were two different things.

Thankfully, Calla knew this too. “Okay...” With those short words of acknowledgment, he moved to the rear line carrying his friend’s body. I couldn’t say anything when I saw him force his shaking feet forward with gritted teeth. I averted my eyes to look at the battlefield.
Slice!
Though there was a sacrifice, we secured another win just in time.
“Repeles! M-Mike is hit!”

We got rid of the blunt weapon warrior serving as their tank. It was Ravien who got him, but she was injured in the process. She wouldn’t die since she got a heal from one of the priests, but she needed time to recover.
[Status effect Whisper of Immortality is now active.]
This time again, the field effect worked to turn the enemy into an undead. But it wasn’t all that fun for us this time.
“What are you doing? Get back!”
The aggro was directed at us, which pushed the front line back. Thanks to that, we had to go through the trouble of taking down a guy we already took down.
Ten people now... No, the Dragon Slayer is incapacitated so it’s nine...

The number of enemies was steadily decreasing. Victory was getting closer and closer. Just as the amount of people running out of MP went up on our side, their side was starting to run out of all kinds of resources.
“C-Curse magic! Cast curse spells, quick!”

The dark wizard’s curse magic, which was decreasing their Natural Regeneration, lifted. Their bodies began to rot and deteriorate. This was because the dark wizard antagonizing the priests had finally run out of mana.
Good, we just have to keep going like this.
After confirming Paladin Jun’s doping was fading and his tank power was decreasing, I pushed the line back and stepped forward.
“...Damn it, he’s recovered already!”
Actually, I still had a long way to go until my MP was sufficiently refilled, but it was enough to maintain Giantization. Soul Dive’s cooldown would end soon too.
More importantly, now that the curse spells are gone, we don’t have to deal any more damage.
The dam had finally burst. From now on, so long as we blocked their path and let Glacier Eye’s effects work their magic on them, the enemy would collapse on their own.
“Push him back! Push!”
The enemy also knew this and tried their best to make our front line budge, but I held on with gritted teeth.
“It looks like their priests ran out of divine power!”

It didn’t matter anymore that the heals that had been serving as a powerful support were finished. These guys were out of juice too. They were still managing to swing their weapons even as their arms and legs quickly rotted, but that was it. I was able to hold on with that thought in mind.
Thump!
But as the saying went, tragedy always struck without warning.
“Aaaaaah!” Suddenly, I heard a scream from behind us—a sound there was no reason I should be hearing when we were winning.
“Y-Yandel!” Kaislan urgently shouted because I wasn’t able to look back. “New enemies have appeared!”
A new variable had entered the picture.

chapters.title: Chapter 422: Eye of the Storm (4)
paragraphs: The moment my comrade shouted out those words behind me, my mind went blank like a lightbulb inside my skull had gone out.
“New enemies have appeared!”
What... kind of bullshit is this...?
It sounded incredibly fake but acceptance came sooner than I thought it would.
New... enemies...?
I was sure this wasn’t a joke. It couldn’t be a misunderstanding, either. Which meant that Kaislan’s report was the truth.
Squeeze.
My fists tightened. At the same time, my brain started scrambling for an explanation.
What the hell did I do for something like this to happen? There aren’t any Hanses in our group. Was there a Hans I didn’t notice? Not among us, but maybe the enemy?
Slap!
Before my thoughts could go any further down that road, I slapped my cheeks with both hands. Since slapping too hard could be dangerous, I did it just hard enough to make me come to my senses.
Hansu Lee, don’t be ridiculous.
This was a kind of avoidance mechanism, looking for a Hans whenever something bad happened.
It happened, that’s all there is to it.

In the Labyrinth of Larkaz, when I encountered the Dragon Slayer by coincidence and even lost a precious teammate, what was the cause? Was there a Hans then? What about in the first floor’s Crystal Cave when the Lord of the Abyss appeared? It was a miracle that there hadn’t been a single Hans among nearly a thousand people, but did that mean things had gone smoothly? Looking back, that was always how things went. Whenever something really shitty happened, there was no Hans, like the heavens themselves were refusing me the opportunity to foist the blame on someone else.
...Then were the Hanses actually a sign of good luck?
The thought came to mind but I had no way of knowing. That didn’t seem to be it, either. But thanks to those useless musings, I felt much more refreshed.
Smirk.
Who cares if there’s a Hans or not? I just have to do my job.

So, with that in mind, I started to think. I gave up on the hope of being rescued. I gave up food and even equipment. Even as we fled, I had to watch helplessly as my comrades dropped like flies. That was what survival was about, giving up, and giving up again. Tricking yourself into thinking that that was the most reasonable choice in an unreasonable situation.
“Yandel! Give us an order or something, quick!”
Now then, what else should I give up?
Unfortunately, I already knew the answer.
“Jun, I’m temporarily leaving this side to you.”
I quickly handed off the baton and headed to the rear. As soon as I turned around, I could see the long-range unit running toward us from behind. The enemy was following suit.
“Mister...!”
“Erwen!”

“There’s about fifteen people! They don’t look like knights but they use auras! Mr. Gerod is holding them off on his own right now!” Ventis Gerod was the special ability user from Team Three, a man everyone liked because he was always smiling and overly positive.
“Thanks for letting me know. Go follow Akurava and join the main unit, quick.”
“...Be careful!”
After Erwen passed me by, I arrived at the rear to find Gerod lying on the ground, gushing blood.
Shaaaaaaaaa!
His blood steamed as it made contact with the cold air.
So... another person dead.
If it weren’t for this man, even more people would’ve been hurt and killed.
Thump.
My heart squeezed but this harsh world I was living in didn’t even give me time to grieve.
Slide.
I raised my head to look forward. I could see about fifteen enemies standing above Gerod’s body. As soon as I saw them, I remembered a conversation I’d had with the commander of Orcules.
“A human woman with an awl-shape aura that appears to specialize in daggers... All characteristics of the Order of the Rose.”
This was a special unit that worked directly under the palace, responsible for secret missions such as assassinations, infiltrations, and special maneuvers.
So, I finally get to meet them.
Drip, drip, drip.
A woman holding a dagger dripping with blood stood and stared at me. It was reminiscent of my first meeting with Amelia. Her eyes didn’t convey any emotion.

“Baronet Bjorn Yandel.” Her utterly blank tone couldn’t even be described as dull. “According to our information, he has at least rank-two defensive capabilities against swords. Our estimates put him at two levels higher than each of us so deal with him with caution.”

As soon as the woman’s business-like briefing was over, they stood there ready to pounce at any moment. It’d been a while since I’d felt this way with an enemy but the sight truly sent shivers down my spine. Someone who knew nothing about me screaming that they were going to kill me wasn’t scary, but that wasn’t the case here. These were experts trained solely in the art of murder.
Thump!
Even though we hadn’t exchanged any attacks yet, my warrior’s heart picked up speed, sensing a difficult battle ahead.
Squeeze.
But so what?
“Did the marquess send you?” I asked in a defensive stance, ready to react at any time. There was no answer.
Jeez, look at that glare. Not going to bother talking to someone you’re going to kill in a minute, huh?

I pretty much abandoned all hope of a reply in the face of their unshakable professionalism but I did wish they would tell me this one thing. “How on earth did you know to wait here? Huh? Tell me. That’s the only thing I can’t explain. Come on, at least give me that. Don’t you feel a little sorry for us?”

The woman’s expression didn’t so much as twitch at my joking tone. “We were only lying in wait because someone was insistent we do so,” she said quietly. “We determined the chances of you coming here were slim.”
“Slim, huh?”

I ended up chuckling at that. Well, what were the chances of us completing the mission after an arduous journey, being abandoned by our allies in the middle of enemy territory, and yet still finding a way out and managing to get here? Especially as a squadron who met for the first time a few days after it was hastily assembled? “Slim chances” were an understatement.
“...Why do you laugh?”
“I just can’t win against you guys.”

After all, in what world did it make sense to deploy a unit like this to block off even the remotest escape route? It felt like a great wall was closing in on me from all directions, like there was no way out no matter where I went.
“Then this conversation has been a failure,” the woman muttered.
“Failure?”
“The eyes of a person whose will has been broken do not look like that.”
What, so you only answered because you wanted to crush my spirit?
“That’s strange,” I said crossly. “I’m definitely in a lot of despair right now.”
“Then will you die now?”
“No, I’m still going to do whatever I can not to.”

“I see people like you from time to time. People who never treat death as the escape it is.” The woman’s expression changed for the first time. It was very subtle, but she almost seemed sad. Of course, I had no way of knowing if that was true. It could be a trick of the light. But even if I was reading her right, it wasn’t like it made a difference.
“Looks like our conversation is now over,” I said. The woman didn’t answer. We both knew there was nothing else to say. “Behel–ahhh!”

Thanks to the essence I had to counter auras, Vol-Herchan, I had been able to evolve into any knight’s nightmare. But that didn’t mean I was invincible. There was no such thing as invincible in Dungeon and Stone.
Slice, slice, stab!

I may not have cut like tofu, but each time their daggers touched my body, I accumulated small injuries. The priests had run out of divine power a long time ago so I couldn’t expect any heals, either.
[You have been poisoned by Royal Poison. Your Physique is over 700. Your Poison Tolerance is over 100. The poison’s effects are reduced by 70%.]

It seemed they’d lathered a bunch of stuff on their knives because the wounds became numb and a tingling sensation spread to the surrounding areas. Apparently, there was some sort of Wound Exacerbation effect in the mix because my Natural Regeneration was inhibited too. That allowed the injuries to steadily increase.
Whooom!

I swung my hammer to swat away the flies but once again, it only swiped through empty air. I climbed walls, somersaulted in the air, suddenly stopped and changed directions, used abilities that defied the laws of physics, etcetera. But my opponents evaded all my attacks and sliced me with their daggers whenever they got the slightest of opportunities. Of course, the injuries themselves weren’t serious, but...
Slice, slice.

My body had already slowed down but as it slowed more and more, the number of injuries increased. If there was a bit more space and all fifteen of them had been able to attack me from all sides, I would’ve been torn into a pile of ribbons on the ground a long time ago.
“...Ugh!” I stumbled forward. Immediately, a dagger swung at my neck.
Yes, now!
As the moment I was waiting for came, I pushed up through my feet and upper-cut one of them with my hammer.
What the—that didn’t work either? Ugh, just let me hit you!
It felt like I was dealing with a bot, not a person. They were too freaking good at this game.
[You have cast Soul Dive. Your Soul Power will regenerate at a rate proportional to the amount of Soul Power you have consumed.]
I first used Soul Dive, which had run through its cooldown time, and recovered some of my cratering MP.
“We’ll help!” Then, reinforcements arrived. It was Ravien and Amelia, who should have been fighting Noark on the front line.
“What about the front line? What happened there?”
“They retreated from the boundary of Glacier Eye and are maintaining a standoff,” Amelia reported.
So, the enemy was recovering, waiting for us to waste our energy fighting these guys. Well, while they didn’t know if the Order of the Rose was a friend or foe, that was a wise decision.
Damn it, why did we get stuck in the middle?
I raised my shield to protect my upper body.
Boom!

A dagger bounced off as if blocked by an iron wall. But I noticed that even as the seconds ticked by, I didn’t feel any accompanying pain in the lower half of my body. They normally took advantage of moments like this to poke me down there, so what was up? I watched the Order of the Rose vaguely distance themselves and realized why.
Ah, it’s thanks to these guys.
They were wary of Amelia and Ravien so they couldn’t poke around like before.
Right, you need a high-Agility character to fight a high-Agility character. Whew, that gives me some breathing room.

I shouted loud enough for Akurava to hear me behind her. I had to fulfill two roles at once right now—both tank and commander. “Akurava, tell the others to maintain the standoff with Noark if they can!”
It broke my heart to give Noark time to regroup when all that had been left was to finish them off, but there was nothing I could do.
Huh? But what’s this?
Even though I shouted, there was no response from the Order of the Rose. They weren’t just ignoring me, either—it looked like they didn’t hear anything at all.
“Emily, is there a team communication spell active right now?”
“Ah, I guess the wizards who came down used it.”
“...Came down?”
Ravien answered while parrying a dagger aimed at my shoulder. “As soon as the ambush began, the priest and wizards used Floatation spells and fled down here.”
“Fled? There... were enemies up there too?”
“Yes. Priest Roita Mamander was killed in the ambush.”
“I see...” Somehow, the bad news kept coming. Not only were there more than fifteen new enemies, but one of our priests was killed.
That makes nineteen people now.
Our thirty-person squadron had shrunk this much. At this point, even if we managed to make it back alive, it’d be with less than half our original members.
Squeeze.

The anger I had been repressing welled up in my heart. We continued to sacrifice and sacrifice, and it wasn’t like we were picturing some rosy future as we did. We were giving our blood, sweat, and tears for a future that was no different from rolling in dog shit. So why were we being subject to all of this nonsense? I wanted to curse and blame the gods this instant.

“Ahhhhhh!” I vented my anger in a shout and forced myself to dispel the heat fogging up my head. What our team needed right now wasn’t hot anger. At least at this moment, I couldn’t give into that. “Akurava!”
“Yes, I’m listening!”
“No need to help here—you all recover as much as you can. You’re going to have to exert a lot of energy soon.”
We only had one shot to get this right.
It was a ridiculous plan. If they followed it, everyone would die. No one said those things to me at that moment.

“...All right. I’ll do as you say.” Akurava immediately carried out my orders and the other members of the squad did the same. It seemed I’d finally been recognized as the leader of this expedition. If that was the case, I felt sort of proud. That meant my hard work hadn’t gone completely unacknowledged.
“Behel—aaah!”
As support from the rear ranks ended, the Order of the Rose intensified their attack.
“Yandel is fighting more than ten enemies on his own! Hold them off!”
To make matters worse, Noark finished regrouping and also ended the standoff to officially start attacking again. There was only one thing we could do.
“Hold out!”
In a situation where our priests were out of divine power and long-range support had ceased, we had to buy time and maintain a battle line in the front and back.
“Aaaaaargh!”
Although we were surrounded and battered from both sides, it was surprisingly more manageable than I thought it would be.
They’re treating us like corpses now.
Both Noark and the Order of the Rose, who had each accepted our annihilation as inevitable, were engaged in a silent war of nerves.
If we all die, they’ll have to fight each other after.
Well, it didn’t matter if I felt left out. The enemy’s carelessness worked out in our favor. Thanks to that, the time finally came.
Dddddd.
The canyon shook with what felt like an earthquake.
Shaaaaaa!
A pure white chill rose up like a fog from the dark abyss beneath the cliff.
[You have been exposed to Chill of Hatred. Additional effects will be applied to all status effects cast by Glacier Wizard Cariathea.]
Glacier Wizard Cariathea had finally climbed up from the bottom of Glacier Eye.
I didn’t plan on using him like this, though... I guess this is what they mean when they say plans never work out the way you expect them to.
“Damn it! Push through!” An urgent cry sounded from Noark’s ranks.
Though they were much calmer, the Order of the Rose was also unhappy about this development. “Let’s finish this as quickly as possible.”
I ended up chuckling.
Can’t believe I’m the only one here who calculated when the boss would arrive. Well, that must be why they were so relaxed.
“Gruhhhhhh!” Thousands of skeletal arms emerged from the gathering fog. In the center, the Elder Lich Cariathea glared at us with red-hot eyes.
“Yandel, we’re all prepared!”
The big request I’d made of the long-range damagers was fulfilled just in time. Now all that was left was to try it. “Shoot.”
[James Calla has cast Piercing Light.]
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Element Synthesis.]
[Titana Akurava has used No. 1911: Fabler’s Broken Pocket Watch.]
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-three attack spell Flame of Evil Destruction.]
[McKelly Rayothers has cast the rank-three attack spell Punishment.]
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-three attack spell Magic Ray.]

Everyone with at least one ranged skill, not just the long-rangers, did their best to fire off attacks with as much juice as their cooldown and MP allowed—not toward Noark or the Order of the Rose, but toward the Elder Lich who’d crashed the party.
Kablam!
[Glacier Wizard Cariathea’s first Soul Chest has been destroyed.]
It seemed their firepower was sufficient.
“Kyeeeeeek!” The Banshees pulled out of the fog shrieked in pain and went into a frenzy.
Rattle, drag, rattle, clack.
The Elder Lich restored his shattered bones in an instant and extended his hand toward us.
[Glacier Wizard Cariathea has cast Soul Extraction.]
Soul Extraction was the pattern used in Phase Two. I gathered my breath and closed my eyes. “Whew...” That was the only thing I could do. The die had already been thrown.
[All characters within range will be rendered unconscious.]
I could only hope for a good result.

chapters.title: Chapter 423: Teaming (1)
paragraphs: The effect of Elder Lich’s active skill, Soul Extraction, was simple. If someone had acquired the skill through an essence, or an Elder Lich you encountered in an ordinary area was casting it, you just lost consciousness.
[You have fallen into a state of Unconsciousness.]
This wasn’t a wide-range skill but one designated to certain targets, and it could be countered with Mental Resistance, Mana Resistance, or a variety of other skills.
[You have been exposed to Chill of Hatred. Additional effects will be applied to all status effects cast by Glacier Wizard Cariathea.]
[Glacier Wizard Cariathea guides the extracted souls to the Box of Punishment.]
Flash!
When I next opened my eyes, I saw the Crystal Cave and a man illuminated by a soft, purple light.

“Hey,” he said, holding a hammer covered in Goblin blood. “Are you looking for a night companion?” He was human. I estimated him to be in his early thirties. He was a little over six feet tall and he had a good-natured, friendly air to him.
...His feet were big for his height.
So this was what he looked like. My memory of his appearance had since faded, but now that I was seeing him again, I could remember.
The man laughed and revealed his name. “Oh, I didn’t introduce myself. My name is Hans.”

This was Hans A, the first of the Hanses, and the man who’d taught me the type of mindset I’d need to have to live in this world, which I was grateful for. He’d also gifted a stranger like me a hammer, compass, canteen, and shoes to help me evolve from a barbarian into a civilized man.
“Why did you kill me?” he suddenly asked with a demonic look on his face. Blood was flowing from his red, bloodshot eyes. But, so what?
“I don’t know, because you deserved it?”
“You could’ve forgiven me.”
“Forgiven you, huh?”
“I had a daughter and wife.”
Right, that...

“I know.” How could I not? I’d seen the portrait of his family in the bag I took from him. In it had been a young girl who looked about three years old and a wife who looked a few years younger than him.
“When you saw that... did you regret killing me?”

I answered without a moment’s hesitation. “No.” This was the honest truth. Why would I regret it? “Even if I went back in time, I’d kill you just the same. I wasn’t the first person you looted. You think those people didn’t have families?”
And even if they didn’t, it didn’t matter. There was no orphan in the world without a sob story.
“Don’t worry. You can survive just fine without a mom and dad. Your wife and daughter will too.”
My proof? Me. So you can trust that’s true.
Crack!
There was no point in making any further conversation so I immediately sprung forward and bashed his head in with the Demon Grinder.
“...You changed. You weren’t like this back then,” Hans A gurgled calmly, despite the fact that the only thing left on his head was his chin.
What the...? This is scary.
Was this always how Soul Extraction worked? I thought it was just when all the characters you’d killed so far came out to attack you. This was a level of drama I never saw in the game.
“Changed? What do you mean?”
I was curious what he was talking about but when I asked, he snickered. “You were shaking when you killed me.”
“Yeah, so?”
“Now it’s like nothing to you.”
“Ah.”

“I’m sure you’ll be even worse in the future. Even if you need to kill someone’s precious parents and their children, and destroy an entire family, you’d do it. Just because the target was your enemy.”
Jeez, tell me how you really feel, why don’t you?
I wondered if it had been a waste of a question but I’d at least learned one thing.

“You already know, don’t you? That you’re becoming a monster.” This guy was able to read my mind and hit me where it hurt with pinpoint accuracy. “Of course, up to now, your targets have all been your enemies so you could deceive yourself into thinking that you’re not a monster yet.”
Crack!
I slammed the hammer into his chin but the voice would not stop.
“Jeez, you’re a tough one.”
“If they’re not an enemy, if the person you have to kill to survive is someone who has done nothing wrong... No, if it’s a comrade you want to protect more than anyone else, how would you feel then?”
I didn’t answer. I knew it was pointless because this voice was coming from inside of me.
“You are already a monster.”
In order to survive, I shoved these doubts and anxieties into the far reaches of my heart and completely ignored them.
“You’re no different from the monsters you’ve killed up to now. You are already of this world.” With that, Hans A disappeared in a burst of light.

My uncle had been a useless person, a gambling addict who couldn’t hold down a job. Whenever he won money, he would give me a good amount to pocket, but whenever he lost money, he grew violent and used me as his punching bag. But as the saying went, even a broken clock was right twice a day. My uncle was the same. Of course, this wasn’t the kind of wisdom you should impart to an eight-year-old kid whose father passed away less than a year before.
“If you have to roll the dice anyway, roll them on a board you created yourself, not one created by someone else.”
This advice had been etched into my mind and had been of considerable help while living in this world.
Step. Step.
I walked through the Crystal Cave. This wasn’t a real space. It was an imaginary place Soul Extraction had dragged me into.
I didn’t know the setting would be the Crystal Cave.

In the game, the setting was always different. It was Rock Desert on the second floor, Tower of Heavens on the fourth, and the Great Sea on the sixth. I once woke up in the palace. How did it pick where you’d go?
Maybe it’s the place that left the greatest impression on the target.

That was a reasonable hypothesis. This was the place where I’d almost died after stepping on a trap, met Erwen, and killed someone for the first time. And I’d never be able to forget the hardships I went through when Berzak, the Lord of the Abyss, spawned here, either.
Still, my stamina and MP were all restored upon entering the Box of Punishment so this isn’t too bad. That means those bastards will be recovered too, though.
Tap.

While I was taking stock of my physical state, I turned at the sound of something behind me and saw three familiar faces: a mustachioed man holding a shield, a blond spearman with a large physique, and a woman in priest robes laughing with her head half caved in.
“Kiheeheehee!” cackled the (Former) Elisa in Half-Head Mode.
“Wow, it’s been a while.”
Unlike Hans A, these guys started attacking straight away without even initiating a conversation.
Smash, smash, smash!
They all turned into light within ten seconds.
Do you know what level I am and how many essences I have now?

The enemies I ran into here even had the penalty of only possessing half their original strength, so they were virtually no different from goblins at this point. They could be knocked down with just one hit.
“Whew... then how many are left now?”

I tried to recount the number of enemies I’d killed since waking up for the first time in Crystal Cave but I wasn’t sure. How could you remember all the pieces of bread you’d ever had, right? I couldn’t tell you how many people I’d killed so far because working as an adventurer meant killing people left and right.
...I think I used to remember it.
Hans A’s words took on more weight. In truth, I hadn’t even remembered his face until running into him in here. To be exact, I’d completely forgotten it.
“Elisa. I remember her because she left an impression...”
What was the name of the spearman again? Taser Gun? Dyson? It was something like that...
I was trying to remember the names of the trio I’d just defeated when I winced. I remembered the name of the mustachioed man.
“Hans Argo.”
His Hans code was C.
“God damn it.”
Now that I thought about it, I’d have to meet all the Hanses I’d killed so far. A chill went down my spine.
What is this, Hans Hell? How many Hanses have I killed so far?

Thankfully, looking back, there weren’t very many. The last one I killed wasn’t all that recently. Hans E, who I ran into in the sewer system while tracking down Elisa, was used as a meat shield when a trap was triggered. Hans J, who betrayed us on Farune Island, ended up getting killed by Erwen. The rest I met in passing and parted ways with me alive, except for one person.
“My name... is H-Hans Chrisen...” He was the evil spirit and summoner I’d killed in Doppelganger Forest.
Wow, he came out straight away. Better to face the music quickly, I guess?

“Why... d-did you kill me? We were... both players...” Hans G, who appeared at one of the crossroads with his partner Elf Archer, was speaking strangely for some reason. Was he stuttering because that was how I best remembered him that day? Well, it had been a pretty shocking, memorable moment. “I didn’t even betray you! It’s because that guy exposed me as an evil spirit—!”
So what?
Smash, smash!

I bashed his head in before he could drag this out too long. It was a barbarian way of living that made life much easier. Afterward, as I wandered the cave again, the people I’d killed came at me in the form of reconstructions derived from my memory.

“You know now! Why I had to become a plunderer! I had to do it to survive in that goddamn place!” cried Jencia Nephrin, the player I killed in Glacier Cave. I didn’t know it at the time, though. No, I had no clue at all that there were players who started in Noark.

“I-I said it was an honest mistake, but just because of that you—! Die! I said die!” That was the religious trio who were tricked by Elisa, the priestess of Karui, into attacking Team Half-Wit. I had killed them when we ran into them again in the Witch’s Hut. Killing these guys made me truly realize something. The more I shed the skin of a modern man, the more I could live like a proper person here.
Smash, smash, smash!

Other than that, numerous plunderers I met in the labyrinth appeared, each expressing their resentment. The people I ran into in the beginning all had their heads bashed in one blow, but those in the latter half were different.
Poppp!
There was Lighthouse Keeper from Orcules.
Whooom!
The knight I met in Noark twenty years in the past.
“I was just trying to help you guys!” said Pyke Neldine, who was executed on charges of treason during the expedition.
None of them were scary individually, but as more of them attacked me at once, the burden on me grew. It was much like the weight of my sins.
“I’ve... killed this many people...?”
It had to be at least a few hundred. And those were only the lives I directly took myself. But...
“Yeah, this is a good thing.”

If someone who lived a robust lifestyle like me was facing down this many people, how bad would the Order of the Rose or those bastards from Noark have it? I used the misfortune of others as motivation to push forward in this dark cave with no end in sight.
Step. Step.
Endlessly.
[Your last enemy has been defeated.]
[Your state of unconsciousness has lifted.]
[The Glacier Wizard will punish the vengeful spirits who failed to achieve their objective. A random penalty will be applied until the labyrinth is closed.]
