When I opened my eyes, I was being dragged. Someone was holding onto both my legs, and my back was scraping against the cold, sharp ground.
“Ugh...! This guy isn’t even wearing any equipment, why is he so heavy?” It was Sven Parav’s voice.
So you’re the one dragging me. Since we’re not in Glacier Eye, I guess that means the plan sort of worked...?
I glanced around at our surroundings as I was dragged along and was met with a strange, never-before-seen sight.
“Uhhh...!”
Huff... huff... huff...

In a surprising reversal, priests and wizards were struggling to carry unconscious muscle-bound adventurers on their backs. After staring for a moment, the first thing I did was check the watch on my hip.
About fifteen minutes...
That was the time since Phase Two started and I fell unconscious.
“Parav, let me go now.”
“Huh? Are you awake?”
“Yes.”
I didn’t want to be a burden any longer so I quickly woke up and got on my feet. I instructed Sven Parav to carry someone else.
“Priest Orman! Great work. From now on, I will carry them. Please help the others. It’ll be easier if you carry them together.”
“Phew... I’m sorry. I’m sure you are struggling, too, Paladin Parav.”
“Haha, this is nothing.”
I soon got up, blinked the spots out of my vision, and quickly took in our surroundings to grasp the situation.
Two priests, three wizards, two special ability users, one close-range damage dealer, two paladins, and one archer.

A total of twelve people including me were awake. There would have been a surplus of people if each person were capable of carrying another person on their own, but things hadn’t worked out that way so some warriors were being carried by two or three people. That made sense, though. There was a reason I considered the Soul Extraction pattern to be a gamble.
Erwen and Amelia are still asleep...
I took over the two limp women and draped them on each of my shoulders. Then I headed over to Jun, who was being carried by Futa Rickerburn.
“Jun.”
“...Ah, you’re awake.” When I approached, Jun raised his head, looking embarrassed. “Unfortunately, I’m unable to use one of my legs.”

A penalty was inflicted on those who regained consciousness. This penalty was entirely random, and if you were lucky it was something small like not being able to taste anything. However, when it was severe, it could leave the target—like Jun—incapacitated. This was probably the case for everyone conscious but still being carried.
“Yandel, are you okay?” he asked.
“For now... nothing seems out of the ordinary.”
“I’m glad you’re all right. Truly.”
“When did you wake up? I want a status report.”
“I’m the fifth.”
“That’s sooner than I expected.”

Jun laughed bitterly at my words. “The number of actual priests of Karui I personally killed while working as an inquisitor wasn’t many. Most were ordinary people without any real power. Thanks to that, it was easy to deal with them in there.”
“I see...” He didn’t seem to be looking for comfort so I quickly got to the point. “I want to hear what happened while I was unconscious.”
“The first person to wake up was Priest Orman, followed by Periton Eriabosti. It seems they really don’t have a single drop of dirty blood on their hands.”
Well, you never know. How many chances does a priest have to deliver the final blow? Even when we were fighting in Glacier Eye, it was always others who dealt the last blow.
“But because the two of them couldn’t move all of us, they waited and only started moving once enough people woke up.”
“How long did that take?”
“Eleven minutes.”
“Was anyone awake then?”
“No one from Noark or the Order of the Rose when we woke up, but I don’t know about now.”
So that’s how it is...
“Yandel, you were right. I tried attacking them just in case, but the ice surrounding them was so frozen over that it wouldn’t budge.”

I wasn’t particularly disappointed about the report that followed. Upon being hit with Soul Extraction, all targets were immediately trapped in ice, leaving them impervious to attack during Phase Two. Even Cariathea didn’t attack then. The boss battle resumed about thirty minutes after Soul Extraction started. Anyone who didn’t return before that would die. The same went if they died inside the illusion.
Erwen will be fine, but Amelia... will she be all right?
I was very worried but all I could do was trust her. Setting aside problems that couldn’t be solved right away, I focused on the conversation I was having.
“But... how did you know what would happen?” Jun cautiously expressed some suspicion. The subject line was missing but I knew what was being asked.
He must be asking about that.

The only people who got trapped in ice and rendered invulnerable due to Soul Extraction were the enemy. No one in our squadron froze. That was why those who woke up earlier were able to carry those still unconscious away.
“The fact that such a phenomenon can be resisted using the Spark of Life is information even the Tovera Church is unaware of.”
“Really?”
“How on earth did you know? Same with the method for summoning that evil Lich...”

The answer to that question was very easy. Once you took down that Lich bastard about a hundred times, you naturally learned his attack patterns and how to summon him. At first, I thought his spawning there was a bug, but after experiencing it firsthand, I realized there was no such thing in Dungeon and Stone. I was sure that would be true here as well.
This part always bothers me.
Since I couldn’t tell him the truth, I made up an excuse. It’d be weird to say I’d heard it from the marquess when it was clear he abandoned us, so...
“I heard it from the chieftain.”
Yeah, there’s no way Jun can refute that, right?
“The chieftain... of the barbarian tribe?”

“Yes. While talking about the old days, he mentioned he experienced something like that.” Jun’s reaction to my excuse was unclear. To be exact, his expression was unreadable. I quickly changed the subject. “Anyway, how are the others?”
“Ah... I’ll tell you now.”

Since this was an urgent situation, Jun set his suspicions aside and started delivering his report. According to him, there were a total of three people who had suffered major penalties. Jun was paralyzed, archer James Calla was blinded, and Old Didi’s right hand had turned gray and hard as stone. I didn’t know what penalties the unconscious members of our squad would wake up with, but that was the case for now.
Then... What’s mine?
What penalty was I given? I ran a few tests as I walked, and before long my jaw clenched.
Of all the penalties, I had to get this one.
[Your use of active skills is restricted.]
Was this the curse of all the Hanses I ran into in the cave?

chapters.title: Chapter 424: Teaming (2)
paragraphs: Needless to say, getting my active skills sealed was one of the worst penalties there was. It was still better than being blind like James Calla, though.
I wish I just lost the use of one arm like Old Didi.

This penalty reduced my combat power to the point where even losing an arm would leave me better off, but I had no choice but to bear it. What could I do when this was the fate I was assigned by the dice? I just had to hope the rolls were as bad on their side too.
Besides... except for my penalty, this isn’t too bad.

Soul Extraction was a very tricky attack pattern, especially for special ability users and wizards. Since they were capable of dealing wide-range damage, they would have dealt many final blows in their lifetimes, but Soul Extraction forced them to fight alone without a front line backing them up as usual.
I guess all of them have lived kind lives, huh?
Both priests safely survived. The wizards were all awake except for one, and the only unconscious special ability user was Akurava.
The fact that most of our wizards have been at the Magic Tower for a long time must have worked in our favor.
At this rate, I considered the gambit a success. Though we’d gone through all kinds of hardships together as a team, I’d had no way of knowing what kind of lives these people had lived before then.
Step. Step.
The sound of firm steps echoed through the ice cave. As we moved as far away from the entrance of Glacier Eye as possible, I felt movement on one of my shoulders.
“Mister...”

“You’re awake...” Feeling deeply relieved, I carefully set Erwen down. She stumbled a bit, but since she found her balance, it seemed whatever penalty she got hadn’t affected her legs. “How are you feeling? Any pain?”
“I don’t know...” Erwen looked somewhat dazed. Did something happen inside? I wasn’t sure but I didn’t dig. The first thing to do was figure out what kind of penalty she got.
God damn it.
As I experimented with random penalties in order from bad to good, I soon let out a deep sigh.
The eighth one, huh?
Unfortunately, Erwen also got unlucky.
[All of Erwen Fornacci di Tersia’s resource recovery is now limited.]
Her resources could not be recovered. Put simply, she would only be able to consume her MP or energy. She couldn’t replenish it.
“Unless you have to protect yourself, conserve your strength as much as possible.”
“Okay... I’m sorry...”
“What are you sorry about? It’s bad luck, that’s all. I’m just glad you woke up.”
Anyway, as more time passed, the unconscious began to wake one by one.
“I’ve caused you trouble. I’ll walk on my own now.” Fortunately, Melend Kaislan got a weak penalty.
“Ugh...! Why is this...?” Ravien was restricted from using weapons so her body jolted like it was being shocked with electricity whenever she placed her hand on her sword.
“Um... why isn’t anyone talking?” Tsuon Irivan, an archer from Team Two, had lost his hearing.
“It was... a terrible place.” Akurava, meanwhile, was white as a sheet.
Two people now...
By the time twenty-five minutes had passed since Soul Extraction was activated, there were only two people left: Amelia and the wizard from Team Two, McKelly Rayothers.
“Please, be strong...”
As the clock ticked down, the crew shot anxious glances at the two people still asleep. I felt like I was going to freak out too.
Why is this woman not waking up?
It wasn’t because she died in there. If she had, her heart would’ve stopped already.
Thump, thump.
My own heart continued to constrict tighter and tighter as the seconds ticked by.
“Mr. McKelly, there’s only one minute left. Please, be strong...”
“Mm...” Amelia finally opened her eyes.
“Emily... God damn it.”
The other one never did.

We had eighteen survivors, but the number of those capable of combat was much smaller. Many of the crew including me had received significant penalties. In truth, it was safe to say our firepower had been reduced by more than half.
I wonder how the other side is doing.
As happiness was said to be relative, the same went for misfortune.
[The Glacier Wizard Cariathea gains new power in proportion to the total number of souls absorbed.]
Thirty minutes had passed now, which meant Phase Two was over. I wondered how many people survived on the enemy’s side and what penalties the survivors had received.
Actually, I wish the bastards who survived would all die fighting the boss... Tsk, but that can’t realistically happen, right?

Cariathea didn’t chase you beyond Glacier Eye, and we had been fighting Noark and the Order of the Rose on the summit. I didn’t know how many people woke up but I was sure they’d all escaped Glacier Eye by now.
Dragon Slayer... I wonder what happened to him.

He had killed the ancient elder dragon who had served as the leader of the dragon tribe, after all. Even then, he’d only narrowly managed to pull it off, so there was a chance the version of the elder dragon that appeared thanks to Soul Exhaustion had defeated him, even at half-power. He wouldn’t have only been fighting the ancient elder dragon, either. The number of people he’d killed must have been in the thousands.
No, wait.
While I was thinking about the Dragon Slayer, my body stiffened.
Fuck, then Dwalkie would’ve been there too.

The realization that the Dragon Slayer got to see Dwalkie filled me with a sudden wave of resentment. At the same time, the following thought came to mind: the people who appeared in my imagination could all have been precious to someone else too.
...Is it because of Soul Extraction? I’m thinking too much.
I cut that train of thought off there and opened my eyes.
Whoosh!

There was a nearby fire radiating warmth. The priest kneeling in front of it continued to recite a prayer, the others listening and taking part in a moment of silence. This was the silver lining of our current situation: we at least had the luxury of holding a funeral for our dead comrades now. The flames created by the wizards instantly melted their flesh and skin, and the remaining bones were enchanted with distortion magic and crushed by the warriors to store in pouches. We hoped this would at least provide some comfort to the bereaved families they left behind.
With that, the brief funeral came to an end. The hot flames went out, and my momentarily warm body was cooled by the wind. Now, it was time to come back to reality.
“...Yandel, what will you do now?”

As soon as Kaislan asked me this, the entire crew looked my way. I’d only filled them in on my plan up to a certain point—for those who woke first from Soul Extraction to drag the others and flee. There were no instructions after that.

“If we continue to widen the distance, we might be able to hold out until the closing date.” Seeing how stony his expression was as he said this, it seemed Kaislan already knew what I was thinking. That was probably why he mentioned it first, so I’d have an easier time explaining. “But Yandel, you would know. Even if we run, it’s going to be a dead end.”
One of the crew flinched at Kaislan’s words and raised her voice. “D-Dead end? What do you mean? I thought we were all safe now?”
“I thought you said we can hold out until the closing date? Isn’t that enough? What are you worrying about?”
I felt bad for those who thought it was all over now, but we still hadn’t cleared the most important hurdle. If we had, I wouldn’t have called this a gamble.

Kaislan shot me a silent look and I let out a rueful laugh before stepping forward. No matter how capable Kaislan was, I couldn’t foist this on him too. “We are not running away. No, to be more exact, we can’t run away.”
When I finished talking, the crew’s eyes widened. They were full of shock and questions.
“The enemy that appeared behind us back there was the Order of the Rose.”
“Are you saying we won’t be able to shake them?”
“No, that’s not it.”
“Then why...”

No one seemed to understand me so I continued. The gist was this: the palace would already have an excuse prepared for if we returned alive. Perhaps something went wrong with the main unit so they couldn’t come to rescue us. Even still, they’d claim they were glad we survived. As if burying their heads in the sand, they’d try to hide the elephant in the room. And we’d have to ignore it too—that was our only way out.
“Ignore? What do you mean?”

“If we pretended not to realize we were abandoned at all, the palace wouldn’t resort to extreme measures.” It may have been cowardly, but that had been my original plan. “But we can’t use that method anymore. The moment the Order of the Rose reports the events that transpired here, the palace will definitely try to get rid of any potential future complications.”
“...They could try and negotiate to keep us quiet instead.”
Hmm, yeah, that’s a possibility but...
“Do you really think they will?”
There was no answer. Someone posed a new question. “So what? If we’re not going to die here, shouldn’t we try our best to at least get to the city?” It was Futa Rickerburn from the Kealunus Dukedom.
There was something incredibly funny about that statement. “I didn’t expect to hear you say something like that when you gave up earlier, saying it was all pointless.”
“Well, you dragged us all here by the collar. You think I’ll give up here after all that hard work?”

True, he even cut off his arm with the determination to get through Glacier Eye. It’d be unfair to die like this. I chuckled. “That was a compliment, so don’t get so touchy. And I never said we were going to give up.”
“Ah...” He took a step back.
“Don’t worry too much, everyone,” I said. “There is a way.”
“A way?”
“Yes. If no one returns alive, who would know? What happened in this place, that is.”
Of course, there might be suspicions, but as I knew intimately, there was a difference between assumptions and physical evidence.
“I suggest we kill both Noark and the Order of the Rose.”
From now on, we were the ones who had to bury the elephant in the room. So would we try to flee, or fight once more? The consensus on that came sooner than I expected.
“I... don’t know what the right decision is.”
“Haha, there’s no reason to stress out about it. Everything we’ve experienced up to this point has been life-or-death too.”
“But in all those moments, he was the one who made the call.”
“Bjorn Yandel, I will trust your decision. That is my decision.”
“I’m with you too. Although it may seem kind of silly to you, leaving things to you is easier for someone like me.”

Once the squadron had come to a decision, everything became clear. We wandered the cave, putting detection spells down in various places and casting distortion magic to hunt monsters and grow our food supply.
“This... is pretty good?”
Monster meat was surprisingly edible. Some parts were so bad that they couldn’t even be considered food, though.
“Aside from the taste, this is such a waste. We could sell the leftovers for some good money.”
“We have no choice. We need to lighten our load as much as possible now...”
The expensive remains obtained with distortion magic were discarded with teary eyes. While we had to carry comrades who had trouble moving, we didn’t have the luxury to take such things with us.
We spent half the day killing monsters and roaming the cave.
“Lord Yandel! Lord Yandel!” Wizard Marrone from Team Five hurriedly ran up to me. There was only one reason why she ever did this.
“Did the detection spell activate?”
“Y-Yes! It did!”
The news Marrone brought me could be broadly classified into three categories.

First, good news. “It was the Order of the Rose. And there were only ten of them!” The Order of the Rose had shrunk significantly. It seemed they’d suffered a considerable amount of damage since they killed for a living.
“How are the remaining ones looking?”
“Um, well...” The second was neutral news. “Four seem to be in bad condition and are being carried by their colleagues. One was just limping.”

Just as a third of our expedition team had been hit with major penalties, they seemed to have suffered significantly too. I guessed this meant we were tied in terms of luck. Well, it was too early to say anything for sure since we didn’t know how they were doing.

“Um... a-anyway, that isn’t the important part!” The long-awaited third category was bad news. And not just any bad news, but news that could be the worst. “I-I don’t know how or why but they’re traveling with Noark!”
Oil and water had come together.

chapters.title: Chapter 425: Teaming (3)
paragraphs: Teaming was a term often used in competitive online multiplayer games to refer to a temporary alliance between players who were classified as enemies in the game.
Ha, they’re teaming here?

Each game had its own perspective on teaming. While some viewed teaming as part of the game, others saw it as cheating and actively cracked down on it. Of course, regardless of the game, intentional teaming was considered cheating on the level of using hacks or bots. That was because it tipped the scales immensely and made the lives of ordinary users a lot harder.
Damn it, what the hell is the admin doing? Kick these bastards!
The complaints popped into my head on instinct. I had worked hard to make this a three-way match. To think they would team up here... Didn’t Noark hate the palace? Things just got very complicated.
This makes divide and conquer impossible...

Plan A had already gone awry. Come to think of it, this was always how it went. There had never been a time when I was actually able to use my original plan to deal with a situation. It wasn’t like I was an aggressive planner or anything, but for some reason, things always turned out this way.
“Um...” Marrone’s hesitant voice jarred me from my thoughts.
“Ah, I was distracted for a second.”
“It’s all right.”
“So how many are on Noark’s side?”
“Six people.”
“Who are they?” Not that we knew their names, but we did fight them twice already.

Marrone briefly explained who she saw, focusing on their abilities. “Um... the special ability user who threw black spears, and the woman who ran like lightning. Ah! And there was that bald boxer too.” On top of that, there was one priest of Karui and one dark wizard. “And finally...”
“Regal Vagos. He’s with them too, right?”
“Y-Yes!”
The Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos. I knew it was in vain but I’d been hoping he died from Soul Extraction. It looked like he managed to survive somehow.
I know his body was technically recovered since he was in a spirit world, but it still couldn’t have been easy. Was the ancient elder dragon weaker than I thought?
When Marrone’s report was over, Ravien muttered, “That’s a relief. That he’s alive...”
“I need his heart to save Pen.”

I completely forgot about that. It was the little dragon Pen who had cursed Vagos and rendered his Dragon Speech nearly unusable. As a result of the strenuous curse, time stopped in her body, and she was now unable to take a single step out of the dragon temple for the rest of her life.
“...Looks like you just remembered.”
“Sorry. I had a lot on my mind.”
“You’ll have to remember. If you save Pen, you may be able to receive my father’s protection.”
“I can’t receive yours?”
“I have no authority within the tribe. But my father is different.”

Put simply, if I completed this quest, there was a chance I could secure the dragon tribe as an ally. I didn’t know how it would end up playing out in reality, but I couldn’t pass up on this opportunity when I was going to have to confront the palace soon.
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
“That’s enough for me. But don’t push yourself too hard. There will always be another chance. If he’s alive...”
What are you saying? We’re going to have to kill him to survive.
Still, she’d gotten her point across. Whatever we did from now on, all she asked was that I didn’t forget to prioritize Pen.
“Okay, let’s move again!”

We installed detection spells throughout the passages as we moved. The enemy would think we were running away, but in order to get a bit more of an advantage in this fight, we had to lure them into a battlefield of our choosing.
Time passed, and soon it was Day Seventy, five days before the labyrinth closed. We wandered the cave and settled in one spot.
“Rest up as much as possible. This will be our last break.”
It was time to prepare for battle. We spotted the enemy chewing on beef jerky with the last detection spell.
It’s probably food from the Order of the Rose.
It was unfair how jealous I was. While we were stuck chewing on monster meat, they were having a normal meal. Well, that seemed to be why they weren’t speeding up their chase.
At this rate, we’re at more of a disadvantage if they take their time.

Thanks to the monster meat, we would have no issues surviving. But the distortion spell had to succeed for us to get our hands on meat so everyone couldn’t eat their fill. We may not have been starving to death, but our hunger was growing even at this moment. If we were going to end this, it should be now before we got more tired.
“Mr. Yandel, don’t stand there in the cold, come here!”
I followed Marrone’s call and obediently headed over to the fire. The concept of “teams” was meaningless to us now. The entire squadron gathered together around the flames of the campfire.
“Mm... meat definitely needs to be grilled! Yandel! You want one?”
No self-respecting barbarian would refuse an offer of meat so I quickly took it and shoved it in my mouth. I chewed on it as I listened to the squad’s conversation.
“This... will be our last fight, right?”

A woman wrapped her arms around her legs in anxiety. It was the priestess Periton Eriabosti from Team Five. Apparently, she grew up in the orphanage run by the Heindel Church and became a priestess. She also had a husband in the city. He wasn’t an adventurer but an ordinary office worker at the administrative office. They got close while doing volunteer work at the church.
I heard... she has a kid too...
This was a change that had occurred as our long quest neared its end. Having spent time with and overcome numerous crises together, we got to know each other too well.
“I’m... going back alive. I can’t let my child grow up like me.” It was a shaky yet firm show of resolve. Silence fell.
Crackle... crackle... crackle...
The sounds of the fire crackling continued, and the wizard on my team, Ashed, spoke. “My wife will be able to get by without me. She’s strong... but... I’m sure she’ll cry.”
“You’re... married? You never said anything.”
“Well, you never asked, Mr. Aldidi.”
“Huh—!” Old Didi gaped in apparent betrayal.

It was Futa Rickerburn who spoke next, the poor guy who had worked as a fixer for Duke Kealunus and was thrown into this place under the guise of retirement. “This is making me more miserable the more I listen.”
“...Sorry?”
“If I were to choose the most insignificant person here, it would be me.”
“Where’s this coming from?”

“I’m not married and no one is waiting for me in the city. I was sick of living that life and wanted out, but I ended up here instead. If the gods were to choose someone to die, they would choose me. But... I’m still going to survive. Wouldn’t it be terrible to let that misery be all there is to my existence?”
It was like a dam had broken. Anxious that this might be their last opportunity, everyone let out the emotions they had hidden away deep inside.
“That doesn’t sound like the guy who said it was all over for us.”
“Can... you forget about that now?”
“Hahaha! For free?”
Despite this, the conversation was bright. Although some of the people talking around this fire now may not be around to greet us the next day, everyone still talked about the future.
“Yandel, what are your plans once you get out of here? Revenge, I’m sure?” Some talked about payback.
“Ahh, I don’t care about that. I just want cake.” Some shared small wishes.
“I’m worried about my grandmother at home...” Some recalled a missed loved one and used their memory to strengthen their resolve.
“All of that aside, I just want a drink.”
“Me too. Truly.”
The general consensus was that we were all desperately in need of a drink. The conversation continued on.
“Um... why don’t we form a clan once we get back to the city?”
“Clan?”
“This is fate, isn’t it? And... it’s not like any of us can return to our old positions, so... um... I just thought if everyone worked together even in the city, maybe we could do something, so...”
We talked about our future, not just our individual ones.
“Calla, what kind of person was your friend?”
“You mean Rick...?”
“Come to think of it, I don’t think I got to talk to him much.”
This wasn’t just our story, but the story of those who couldn’t be with us here. We spoke aimlessly to remember, commemorate, and express regrets.
A long while later, Marrone called out to me, her expression steely. “Lord Yandel...The detection spell was triggered.”
At that sentence, we all smiled ruefully, got up from our seats, and extinguished the fire burning in the center of our group. It was time to return to cold reality.

The plan was simple. No, really—there wasn’t much of a plan at all. We decided on the location of our fight and would now fight fiercely against our enemies with the utmost determination. Whoever survived would win.
“...They’re here.”
“Numbers?”
“The same.”
I got the information I wanted from Erwen, who had her ear to the ground, but I still waited just in case.
Step, step.

About a minute later, they got near enough that even I could hear them. Before long, the enemy appeared from around the corner. Their numbers were a bit strange. There were only seven from the Order of the Rose and six from Noark, adding up to a total of thirteen enemies.

Did they leave behind those who were useless in battle because of the penalties? No, that doesn’t make sense. But even without taking into account the cold, the labyrinth is filled with monsters. If they didn’t leave them behind, did they abandon them...?
It was a very Noark-like response.

“...Dead end?” Upon seeing us in our defensive formation, the woman at the front tilted her head. She seemed glad to have finally caught up with us but sensed something was off. “Were you waiting for us?” She was quick to grasp the situation as someone who had experience in all kinds of battles. Not that that’d make a difference.
“Calla!” No sooner did the shout leave my lips than Calla activated his skill.
[James Calla has cast Swift Hands.]
He couldn’t aim it now that he was blind, but that wasn’t what we were after anyway. The important thing was that the ground shook as soon as the skill was cast.
[A skill has been used within range. The trap has been activated.]
Kablam!

Before long, a great crashing sound rang out from behind the enemy. The area we were currently standing in was a trap room, which you could find from time to time as you crossed through the icy cave system.
“...We’re trapped!”
The condition for setting it off was casting a skill. Once the trap activated, the room’s only entrance was covered with ice. This became a hidden room until it melted a day later.
Compared to Noark’s panic, the Order of the Rose was calm. The calmest among them was the leader. “Why did you make this decision?” Her question contained only curiosity.
The answer was simple. “There is no paradise for us to escape to.”
“How profound.”
It should be. Those are the words of my favorite author.
“I want to ask you something.”
“My name is Six.”
I didn’t want to know your name.
When I gave her an incredulous look, the woman named Six continued without so much as a twitch of the eyebrow. “So what do you want to ask?” She seemed somewhat embarrassed but I couldn’t blame her.
I just asked my question. “How were you guys able to stomach working with them?”

The answer came from an unexpected place. “Oh, that?” The Dragon Slayer Regal Vagos walked forward with a swagger, seemingly recovered to some extent. “These women knew that they needed our help catching all of you.”
Hmm, that did make sense from the Order of the Rose’s perspective. For them, their mission came first.

“But you guys didn’t have a reason to accept that offer.” I talked to the Baldy Boxer, not the Dragon Slayer. Vagos might have made this foolish choice because of his grudge against me, but this guy seemed to be the actual leader here. “You really don’t know? Once we’re dead, you guys are next.”

The question was asked with the intention of causing a break in their ranks. However, Baldy Boxer seemed unphased as he answered me. “It’s well known that the Order of the Rose cannot break an oath made in the king’s name.”
Ah, I see. I thought the oath was only a cheat code for the barbarians. Also, it’s funny that he’d say this is well-known. This is my first time hearing it.
“Besides, we had no choice. We ran out of food chasing you guys. Our only choice was to work with them to get you—and their food.” Now it made sense how these two groups became so cooperative.
“Now, does that answer all your questions?” the woman who seemed to be the leader, Six, asked, clearly intending to end this conversation.
“No, not yet. Was it Repeles? I have a suggestion for you.”
Baldy chuckled at my words. “Are you really going to try and appeal to me?”
Huh, how did you know?
I readily admitted it.
“Yes. Join our side. We’ll provide you with food.”
It’s monster meat, though.
“...What?” He seemed surprised like he never expected me to make the offer.
I quickly plowed on. “So what happened is the palace abandoned us. If possible, I want to take this opportunity to change my affiliation altogether. What do you think?”
“...There is nothing more foolish than trusting your enemy.”
“If you want an oath, I’ll make it. On a warrior’s honor.” Just like the Order of the Rose used their cheat code, I used my tribe’s.
“You... are you serious?” Baldy began considering this with a confused look on his face.

Of course, that didn’t last long. Come to think of it, there was a saboteur on their side. “Repeles, do not fall for the enemy’s tricks. That man has broken an oath once before. He’s a different breed who doesn’t care for a warrior’s honor or any of that.” The Dragon Slayer, who I once stabbed in the back in the Labyrinth of Larcaz, revealed his story.
Baldy’s expression hardened as he turned back to me. “Unfortunately, I will have to decline that offer. I have no way to control you in the city in the first place.”
Hmm, that’s a no-go, huh?
“That’s unfortunate. Then I guess we’ll have to kill you all.”

I covered my upper body with my shield and looked at the enemy. My line of sight was low because I couldn’t use Giantization anymore, but that didn’t matter. The barbarian way was to chew with your gums if you didn’t have any teeth.
“Erwen!” The moment my call went out, Erwen’s body blurred.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Elementalization.]
Since this place was riddled with aura users, the attribute we went with was Earth, obviously.

[Any damage received from Fire attribute attacks is reduced by half. Any damage received from water attribute attacks is doubled. Poison Immunity Bonus. When using blunt weapons, a Strength bonus is added to attacks. Your Physical Resistance has significantly increased.]
My Physical Resistance value soared and the second stage of Evolving Shell was activated even without Giantization.
[Your Physical Resistance stat is over 350. Damage is reduced by 50 percent for penetration-type wounds only.]
Yeah, let’s give this a try, shall we?
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

chapters.title: Chapter 426: Like Ice (1)
paragraphs: This was a completely different situation from Glacier Eye, where it only took four people to block the whole path. This place was an open space on all sides. The area the front line needed to block had widened, while the number of front liners in the squadron had decreased.
Me, Jun, and Goblin.
We were the only three real tanks left. On top of that, one of Jun’s legs was paralyzed, making it hard for him to utilize all his power.
Rickerburn, Kaislan, Ravien, Amelia...

Front liners belonging to the close-range damage-dealer category were spaced out to help form the wall as well. Of course, there were too many holes to call it a proper wall, but complaining about that wouldn’t solve anything. We chose the best option we had available to us. All that was left to do now was see how it played out.
Shaaaaaa!

Black fog spread in all directions, covering the space between our two groups. This was the work of the other side’s dark wizard. Although the fog had some debuff effects, its real purpose was probably to obscure our vision.
Visibility is about one yard.
My warrior’s body was on high alert thanks to my limited field of vision.

“Gruhhh...” Various undead monsters emerged from the darkness, baring their teeth and swinging their claws. These were summons courtesy of the priest of Karui. Throwing numbers at us was useless in Glacier Eye, considering its narrow path, but that wasn’t the case now.
Smash!
I swung my hammer every which way to push the approaching monsters back. Which was when...
“Mister—!”
Whip!
The moment Erwen’s warning reached my ears, with a brief whoosh, a sharp blade emerged from the darkness to swing at my neck.
Khak!
I was slower to react than usual because of my limited visibility, but I still managed to block it with my shield. Then, a second later, a white light emanated from the spot above my heart.
Whooom!
At first, I was bewildered, but I quickly pieced together what was happening.
[Periton Eriabosti has cast Undying Light.]
It was a buff from one of the priests—a skill that didn’t have much use in the game except to raise your Spirit stat.
Did he use it to improve our visibility? That’s smart.
I found myself chuckling.
Shaaaaaa!

The white light blooming from my heart pushed the darkness away, allowing me to see about three yards ahead. Of course, the darkness filling the empty spaces remained. I could just barely make out Sven Parav and Amelia to my left and right.
Khak!
I may not have been able to see their faces in the darkness, but the lights burning at their hearts were vivid as they moved with them, like fireflies gliding through the dark.
“Ahhhhhh!” I bounced back a blade flying in with my shield and swung my hammer wildly, checking on the lights floating around me all the while.
Shaaaaaaaaa!

The turbulent flickering indicated fierce battles. Though they may have made us easy-to-see targets for the enemy, they were also a signal to us that our comrades were still alive and fighting. It was evidence to back up our faith in each other.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]
Arrows were fired, casting away the darkness.
[Benjamin Orman has cast Moonlight of Purification.]
Particles of light fell from the sky and seeped into my body.
Stab!
The longer the fight dragged on, though, the more wounds accumulated on my person.
The woman who introduced herself as Six said, “You are much weaker than before.”

That was because I couldn’t use Iron Fortress right now. Even if Elemental Barbarian (Earth) Mode was activated, my ability to block auras was significantly reduced. That wasn’t all, either. I didn’t even have the Strength bonus that came with Giantization. I couldn’t use Swing, my sole attack skill, or Eye of the Storm, which caught enemies off guard and allowed me to keep them in check.
However, as I always said: “So what?” I grinned and added, “If you really think I’m weaker, then kill me. But I’ll never go down.”
I was dead set on that. Fights like these were won by the people who were still standing at the end.
“...You trust in your priests that much?”
Well, she wasn’t wrong for assuming that was where my confidence was coming from. If it weren’t for the heals coming in even as we spoke, it would have been tough for me to hold out.
What are you scoffing at? What a weird lady.
“Is it wrong to trust in my comrades?” Dungeon and Stone was a team game, after all.
Bang!
I struck my hammer down at the source of the loud sound. However, I didn’t feel the tell-tale sensation of a skull being crushed through my fingertips.
“You seem impatient for someone who trusts his comrades.”
Ugh, you really talk a lot.
“Are you anxious? That I’m the only one fighting you right now?”

It was obvious what she was trying to do—goad me into revealing even the slightest of weaknesses. If it weren’t for that, there would be no reason for this stone-cold woman to go on yapping. The problem was that it was kind of working.
Whoom!

I swung my hammer again, but my doubt and anxiety did not ease. Where were all the others? I had been sure more enemies would flock to me. I thought it would make things easier for my comrades if I was able to take them all on.
“Aaagh!” Through the sounds of weapons clashing, a scream caught my ear.
“Bjorn Yandel, you are the last one.”
Who did that scream belong to?
“Because I already knew that you wouldn’t be one to go down easily.”
The enemy? Or an ally? I had no way of knowing.
“So I hope you are not defeated until the—”
I forced my hot head to cool down. It wasn’t like I could go over there and check right now. “Behel—aaaaaah!”
I just had to have faith and do my job.

The archbishop who took him in at a young age told him, “You don’t have parents anymore. Your only parent is Tovera, the brilliant sun. Worldly attachments are meaningless to an agent of god, so cast away your human heart. From now on, your name is Jun.”
Jun, a former inquisitor of the Tovera Church, had thus abandoned his old surname, Arshen. From that day on, he had lived life not as a human being, but as a beast otherwise known as an agent of god.
“It must be done. You are a man too.”
He’d castrated himself of desire and recited prayers.
“I-It hurts...!”
“It seems your human heart still lingers.”
He underwent training that bordered on torture every day.
“You can get back up. As long as the light of the sun is with you.”

There were times he wished to just let himself break down, but the light of the sun forcibly healed him. By the time he became an adult, Jun had become something that could no longer be called a person. There was no room for doubt. He just did what the church instructed him to do in the name of their god.
Why was it...?

There was no particular catalyst. It had been an ordinary day. The sky was cloudy but the sunlight still felt warm on his skin. That day, Jun Arshen had been looking up at the sky blankly when he questioned his beliefs for the first time.
Am I right?

It was a long overdue question. Looking back, he didn’t know why it suddenly came to him at that moment. It might have been that the family of three he saw on the street that day had looked so bright. The one thing he knew for sure was that his life as a beast came to an end that day.
“...W-What?! How could you do such a thing?!”

He left his position as an inquisitor and returned to being an ordinary member of the church. Although he went about things in reverse order, it was only then that he became disillusioned with how the church was run. He didn’t hate his god. That question, the one that came to him like a revelation that cloudy day, had been the first time he’d felt the presence of god so intimately. If anything, it had only strengthened his faith.
I... am not right.

Frustration took precedence over anger. The weight of the sins being committed in god’s name finally began to press down on his shoulders. It seemed an ordinary life was out of his reach, but as a result, Jun yearned for it all the more. That was probably why.
“I will ask one last thing of you.”

Jun Arshen accepted one final mission from the archbishop, now the cardinal, before officially ending their professional relationship. As he genuinely believed this mission was for the good of the world, instead of creating non-existent sinners as he’d seen the church do in the past, he thought he could use it to atone for his sins in some small way.
Which brought him to this moment.
Baaang!
“Punishment.”

Perhaps this was a way of punishing a foolish child who had misinterpreted god’s will and had been manipulated by those swayed by twisted human hearts. Yes, there were times in the beginning when he thought that way. But he knew better now. If this was punishment, it was wrong.
“You... are wrong.”
Even if he had dragged himself out of the beastly life he’d been living, this was not right.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“H-How did they get here?!”
The light on his heart went out, the light of those who wished to run toward the future.
Slide.
His paralyzed right leg didn’t permit him to go forward, but...
Slide.
Jun dragged his leg and, even though his movements were shaky and it looked like he could fall at any moment, stumbled forward little by little.
Slide.
As he did so, he realized something. They may have only seemed like empty words, but it was true that those who wished to go forward could go forward, no matter the circumstance.
Slide.
If it weren’t for that man, I would have never known that.
Just then, a sound came from behind him. “Jun! W-What are you doing?!”
Periton Eriabosti was a woman who, unlike himself, had likely lived a very bright life and carried out pure, untainted justice. She fought to survive for the sake of her beloved child.
It wasn’t just her, either. “Barhatun Wiar!” The bearded wizard had a beloved wife.
[Guold Aldidi has used Invalidate.]
The old man who lost his child had a long-cherished wish to fulfill.
[Titana Akurava has cast Vampire Awl.]
The dwarf believed in a firm cause.
What Rickerburn said before the battle began popped into his mind. “This is making me more miserable the more I listen. If I were to choose the most insignificant person here, it would be me.”
He was wrong.
Of the eighteen people still alive right now—no, of all thirty people who started out on this journey, the most insignificant of them all is probably—no, it’s definitely... me.
Jun realized at that moment the role he had to play.
“Come back over here, quick!”

Born with only his parents’ names on his back, he became an inquisitor, then lost his way and arrived here. Everything he saw, heard, and felt on this lifelong journey was all leading up to this moment.
“I’m only doing what I have to do.”

This was like a revelation. The moment he realized it, his mind cleared. There was no more fear. It didn’t even occur to him that this moment was an ordeal. The fact that one of his legs wouldn’t move felt like all the more reason to stand right here in this spot.
“To think there was a tank here too.”
“He can’t use his leg.”
“Is that why he’s back here?”
“Get rid of him, quick.”
The enemies and their red-hot auras rushed toward him in unison. Jun raised his shield.
Kak-kak-kak!
Two daggers pierced the shield.
Stab!
Two daggers pierced his lungs. There was no pain, though. For the first time in his life, he felt grateful for the harsh training he received as a child.
[Jun Arshen has cast Holy Descent.]
The power of god dwelled in his body. He truly felt that he could accomplish anything in that moment. He let out a shout, though it may not have been a shout appropriate for a paladin.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
He couldn’t pay for all the sins he’d committed, anyway. So this one should be okay. Yes, just this once, perhaps it was okay to let out a shout because he wanted to let it out.
“We have to help Jun!”
The priest, wizard, and archer in the rear line behind him used their talents to start helping him as best they could. Despite this, Jun’s flame was quickly extinguished.
Rattle.
His shield dropped from his arm as his tendon was severed.
Stab, stab, stab!

Daggers cut through his upper body. Jun no longer thought about blocking or dodging these blows. He just focused on staying on his feet and standing tall. As they watched this unfold, the Order of the Rose exchanged incredulous commentary.
“He should’ve died from that injury a long time ago.”
“But why isn’t he dropping?”
“We’ve already wasted three minutes. Hurry up and get rid of him.”
The attacks became more intense.
Stab!

The blood on the floor formed a puddle and Jun’s mind went blank. He didn’t know how many minutes he stood there for. His sense of time was distorted and the enemy’s faces were blurry, but one thing was clear.
Shaaaaaa!
The lights swaying in the darkness... that man would be among them.
Bjorn Yandel.
Even at this moment, he was probably pushing forward one step after another, doing what he had to do.

“Clan...” Did they say they were going to form one back in the city? Jun was not afraid of death, but he did feel a sudden sense of regret. When the idea was first mentioned he hadn’t said anything, thinking it wasn’t his place, but... “It sounded fun...” It definitely would have been.
The palace, Noark, and the numerous other institutions that abandoned us... Even if all of them have turned against us...
Stab!

A sharp blade dug into and up his lungs. Jun intuitively realized that his flame had completely burned out. His noisy surroundings went quiet and his vision went black. The light swaying in the distance faded away, leaving a stain-like mark behind his eyes.
Shaaaaaaaaa!

The darkness receded and his surroundings were filled with a light that felt not unlike a parent coming to greet that young child who had finally completed his mission. A warm kind of light that embraced his entire body.
“Haha...” Jun chuckled. Even if this was just a hallucination he was seeing before he died, even if this was just vain hope and faith... “Save me... from my wandering...”
Do not punish this foolish sinner with whips. Please, embrace this tired soul...
It was the moment he had been yearning for for so long.
There were no strategies or tactics to be found. Just a series of struggles to survive.
Kwaaang!

The melee was full of explosions, the clash of weapons, shouts, and screams. It was so chaotic that I wouldn’t be surprised to hear anyone’s name on either the list of survivors or the list of the dead, and it dragged on for who knew how long.
Shaaaaaaaaa!
The fog surrounding us began to dissipate. It couldn’t be because the dark wizard had already run out of mana, though.
Did someone kill the dark wizard? Well, I guess I’ll find out soon.

Soon, the fog cleared completely and my vision returned to normal. The first thing I saw was a frowning woman in front of me. A knight was swinging his sword vigorously in the distance, where the enemy’s rear ranks were gathered, and I saw that it was Melend Kaislan. Near him, a robe-clad, scrawny body was slumped forward without a head.
When did he get there? I wasn’t expecting that at all, but this is great.

I looked to the left and right. There were no deaths on the front line, but everyone looked worse for wear. The worst was Ravien. She had claimed she fought well with her fists, but without her sword, she looked messed up.
Okay, no one’s dead yet. Then what about the rear? I think that’s where the scream earlier came from. It sounded like someone shouted the names of my ancestors too.
I couldn’t be sure. There was so much noise all around.
Dash.

I took advantage of the temporary distance between the woman and me and quickly glanced back. Despite what I was expecting, the rear looked the worst off. Three Order of the Rose members stood right in front of them. One body lay on the floor. My heart dropped the moment I saw it, but it was a member of the Order.
Jun stopped them.
I could see Jun standing in front of the rear line to protect them. As soon as I spotted him, I remembered the conversation we had before the battle began.
“You... want me to hide in the rear?”
He didn’t seem to like my request, but I convinced him that the real battle would begin once we got back to the city, and that I’d need his strength outside the labyrinth. He had reluctantly nodded.
He can’t even walk properly and he’s that torn up...

I let out a sharp breath when I saw the state Jun was in. His body was drenched in blood and it’d be harder to find a spot on him that wasn’t sliced to ribbons. He probably made the call that this was not the time to protect himself for the sake of the future.
If it weren’t for him, the rear would have been annihilated.
While the realization was enough to leave me lightheaded, it also brought me relief. Thanks to Jun’s fighting spirit, the rear line had been able to kill one of the Roses.
Thump!
I noticed the discrepancy a moment later.
“Why...?” Jun was still standing upright, though he wasn’t holding a shield. “Where is his light?”
Unlike the other members of our squadron, his light was not lit. And unlike my pounding heart, my mind provided an answer to my question right away.
So, he’s dead.

I wasn’t the only one who was late to notice his death. The members of the Order fighting Jun also realized he was dead and ran forward to ambush the rear, but their daggers did not reach their target.
Clang!
Amelia and her clone had moved back as soon as she saw what was going on and parried the two blades.
Six glanced around at the dead members of her order, her eyes emotionless. “The damage is greater than I thought,” she muttered.
Dash.
She immediately kicked off the ground and ran, but not toward me, her mark.
Motherfu—!
She went somewhere else entirely—back to the rear, which Amelia was narrowly managing to defend on her own.
“Mister...!”
Erwen’s shout served as a signal to follow Six. I felt like I could read this woman’s mind now.
That bitch must have noticed I can’t use my active skills by now.

I was a barbarian tank whose active skills were sealed. Of course, my body was tough thanks to Elementalization, but in a many-v-many scrum, I wasn’t as big of a threat. Meanwhile, my squadron’s performance was lacking. Using this as her basis, Six would’ve come to the decision that it was more efficient to ditch me to focus on other things than stay here trying to keep me in check.
“Erwen!” As soon as I shouted for help, spiritual energy was shot at our enemy.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]
The objective was to stop Six’s charge.
Whip!

Six nimbly jumped out of the way and flipped in the air, which meant the arrow had achieved its objective. I didn’t pass up on the opportunity to narrow the distance, and I fired off orders as I did. “Erwen, change attributes.”
“To what?”
When I told her the attribute I wanted, the change immediately began.
Shaaaaaa!
The attribute was not water, fire, earth, or wind. It was Blood Spirit’s main attribute.
[The Spirit of Darkness now dwells in your body.]
A thick, ominous darkness spread over my skin.

[All Resistance values are fixed at 0. Divine Resistance is fixed at -200. Darkness Resistance is fixed at +800. Abyssal Blessing Bonus. You receive immunity to all types of status effects. All types of attacks receive Unavoidable Strike Correction.]
This was Elemental Barbarian (Dark) Extreme Damage Mode.

chapters.title: Chapter 427: Like Ice (2)
paragraphs: Elemental Barbarian (Dark) Extreme Damage Mode—or Dark Mode for short—was the most extreme mode among many that you could use with Elementalization. All your resistances went down to zero, and you couldn’t be healed since divine power now dealt damage. In return, however, it had a ridiculous payoff: I was immune to all types of status effects including Bleeding, Poisoning, Unconsciousness, Paralysis, Blindness, and tons more. The random penalty from Soul Extraction still applied since it was categorized as a system effect instead of a status effect, but that was honestly a non-issue right now. The key upside to Dark Mode was something else.
[All types of attacks receive Unavoidable Strike Correction.]

Dark Mode was the only ability in all of Dungeon and Stone that had an auto lock-on feature. Of course, as the motto of this game was an eye for an eye, the price of that ability was a body that was even more fragile than glass.
[All resource consumption increases by 20x. The cooldown time for all skills increases by 5x.]

Those two debuffs could instantly turn any normal adventurer into a joke, but they weren’t currently much of an issue for me. I was already half a joke because of the random penalty from Soul Extraction. If there was one thing I needed to be concerned about, it would be this:
[You will receive Recoil in proportion to the time Elementalization is active.]
I had to reduce the recoil I took as much as possible. So, put simply, every moment was more precious than gold.
Okay, let’s do it.
When I took another step forward, Six quickly widened the distance between us.
Dash.
She seemed wary of my changed appearance. Since she didn’t know what was going on, it seemed she was going to stop what she was doing so she could reassess my threat level. Which I was grateful for.
Okay, now that I definitely have the aggro on me again...
I closed in and swung my hammer. It wasn’t considered a real attack if I just swung randomly into empty air. I’d already tested it and there had to be a clear target for the auto-lock to apply.
Leap.
As she had throughout this entire battle, the woman avoided my hammer with minimal movement.
[Activating Unavoidable Strike Correction.]
At the moment, the course correction effect was activated.
Rip!

A tear in space appeared in the direction the hammer swung. The woman stared at this with a sharp look in her eyes. Although she didn’t know what this move was, she was on high alert so she could respond at any moment.

The swung hammer plunged into the darkness and the whistle of it moving through the air ceased. Looking for any trace of the missing weapon, her eyes darted around to widen her line of sight. It was no use, though. The hammer appeared a split second later, transcending space to strike Six’s body with the force of the initial swing intact.
Smack!
Before long, a dull thud sounded. Unfortunately, the blow didn’t feel too satisfying as it jolted up my arm. That was because it landed in her abdomen.
Why is this woman so sturdy?
At first, I thought she was just an Agility-type, but it seemed she’d invested considerable stats into Defense too. Judging by her expression, that attack didn’t hurt her at all.
Man, if only I still had Swing... I could’ve crushed her.
It was too bad that the Demon Grinder’s increased damage only applied to blunt weapon skills and not the weapon itself.
Anyway, if once doesn’t work, I’ll do it again.
I’d have time for regrets later when I’d tried all the options available and failed.
Whoom!
So I threw those regrets away and swung the hammer again.
Dash.
Six widened the distance even more than before. It seemed she was wary after that first strike, but unfortunately for her, that wasn’t how you countered this move.
Smack!
My next attack struck true despite the distance.
Finally got her on the head.
The blow felt good this time but surprisingly, Six didn’t even let out a small groan. She just staggered a bit.
Slide.
She slowly lifted her head, which was bowed forward, to glare at me.
Spit.
The blood in her mouth was spat out with mechanical precision. “I remember now,” she said solemnly.
...Huh?
“The rank-five monster Flora’s special ability, Elementalization. This is its effect when it’s used in conjunction with the Spirit of Darkness.”
Uh... Does she go around memorizing the effects of essences too? I guess it’s possible. These are agents painstakingly trained by the palace, right?

“This is my first time seeing it so it took me a moment to realize, but...” Before she could get any further, I immediately kicked off the ground and ran forward. Unlike before, though, Six did not move back. “Things will be different from now on.”
Dash!
Instead, she rushed toward me recklessly. From that action alone, I could piece together that she wasn’t talking big.
Ha, I only got two hits in.
From now on, this was going to be hellish.
Whoom!
I swung my hammer down as soon as Six moved. She didn’t even avoid it. She’d made a calculated decision based on the information she had on hand.
If she doesn’t dodge it, she can at least choose where it hits.
The first thing to make contact was the hammer.
Smack!
The moment that it struck Six’s shoulder, a dagger coated with an aura sliced through my forearm like tofu.
Stab!
Yeah, this is why I was saving Dark Mode...
Though we exchanged the same number of blows, it was clear which of us had suffered more damage, as was obvious from the triumphant look in her eyes.
“You are more agile than I thought. I was aiming for your neck.”
God damn it.
If she had cursed me instead, I would’ve smiled at the praise. But, more agile than she thought? That was nothing short of the ultimate insult.
Throb.

Thanks to my Pain Resistance dropping to zero, I could feel a sharp burning in my stabbed forearm. I tried to look on the bright side, though. For taking an aura with zero resistance, this wasn’t too bad a wound. If it had struck somewhere other than my forearm or my skin, the injury would’ve been much more serious.
“Behel—aaaaaah!” I used even the stinging pain as fuel for my fighting spirit and let out a shout.
“Tough guy.”
This match would end soon.
One more time.
I brought my hammer down again. The exchange went about the same as before. Six didn’t dodge it this time either and extended her dagger.
Smack!
Slice.
We exchanged one blow each. Once again mine landed on Six’s shoulder—the same one.
God damn it.
In my case, though, she hit the hand holding my shield. I was hoping to use the shield to get through this one unscathed, but the aura-covered dagger went through the metal and even my palm.
Clunk.
It seemed she even cut off the strap securing the shield to my wrist because it dropped helplessly to the ground—along with my pinky and ring fingers.
One more time.

Either way, I swung the hammer again. This time, the structure of our fight changed slightly. Six didn’t dodge either this time but instead confronted the blow head-on, crossing her two daggers together to block the hammer’s trajectory.
Riiiiiip!
The hammer was sucked into the darkness before it could collide with the daggers. A moment later, it struck Six’s ankle.
Smack!
As thin as her ankle was, the impact must have been considerable, but the look in Six’s eyes remained unchanged.
“...So, this method isn’t working, huh?”
Jeez, I feel like a monster being hunted. One more time.
I swung the hammer.
Smack!
Stab.
I hit her and gained another stab wound in return. Once, twice, three times, four times—we exchanged many more attacks. I finally acknowledged her.
This woman... she’s much stronger than I thought.
Her natural abilities were obvious. She was able to use an aura, and her swordsmanship was as fierce as that of the commander of Orcules.
Smack!
She clearly wasn’t a fool either. After only a few exchanges, she was able to put her knowledge of Dark Mode to use.
Stab!
She also had good judgment.

“I can’t use this shoulder anymore.” As if to prove my point, Six dropped the dagger from her left hand after determining she couldn’t use it anyway. Ever since this exchange began, this woman had purposefully taken most of my attacks on her left forearm and shoulder. She’d made the pragmatic decision to concentrate the damage in one spot.
More than ten blows for one arm, huh?
Of course, compared to me, full of cuts and holes all over, she was pretty much unscathed. That was why I took a moment to let go of any overzealousness. I had wanted to go help my comrades, but...
All I have to do... is somehow finish her here and now...
With my goal simplified, my mind felt clearer. I could worry about what came next later, like the barbarian warrior I was.
Smack!

I watched her like a hawk, treating each moment as critical. Or, actually, I felt a lot like a wild dog. When this woman eventually slipped and showed even the slightest hint of weakness, I’d be able to lunge forward and sink my teeth into her.
Stab.
Forearm, flesh, wrist, thigh—the blade that had up to this point missed my vitals sank deep into my lower abdomen.
Hmm, this one seems a bit dangerous.
Zippp.
I forced my staggering body forward using the strength I had left in my legs and quickly took stock of the situation.
How much longer can I last? How many more seconds?
I had no way of knowing, but it wouldn’t be long.
Not yet.
I tried to suppress any impatience. Just a little longer and it would come—the moment to end this long fight once and for all.
Smack!
Stab.

The battle continued without pause. No, calling it a battle would be a farce. It was instead a series of clashes where each party ignored all concepts of defense for the sole objective of attacking and killing the other.
“The paladin that died earlier...” The woman busy chopping up my body suddenly spoke up. I wondered what she had to say. “Was he a close friend?”
I don’t know why she’d be curious about that.
Whooom!
I responded after another swing of my hammer. “No.” We had known each other for too short a time to be considered close.
“Then I don’t understand. Why are you going this far for him?”
“Because he’s not someone who should die in a place like this.”

I didn’t know much about him. What I had seen was only one of the many sides of him that happened to appear in the labyrinth. Which was why I felt an even keener sense of regret. I wondered what it would have been like to go adventuring with Jun. It wouldn’t have been bad, I thought. We would work well together most of the time and whenever his habits from his inquisitor days came out, I could just shoot him a warning look. Though his unconditional support would have been a burden some days, at times he would’ve been a more reliable comrade than anyone else.
Whoom!
What about at drinking parties? I wonder if he could handle his liquor. It’s always guys like that who completely change personalities once they chug a drink. I wonder what type of drinker he was.
Whoom!
I’d never know. These people had stolen that opportunity away from us. Not just Jun’s, but all of the other squad members, too.
Stab!
Their lives weren’t disposable, and they couldn’t be wasted here.
“Behel—aaah!” I forced my slack arm to move. I refused to let these guys take anything more from me.
Squeeze!
I forcibly tensed my torn-up thigh muscles to find my balance.
Whip.
A fierce aura flew toward my stomach, ignoring all air resistance as if determined to break my spirit. But then, the moment I’d been waiting for finally arrived.
[The Luck dwelling in your body has blocked the damage.]
Tap.
As if hit by a transparent barrier, the dagger stopped in mid-air.
So, it’s finally happened.
This was Probabilistic Retaliation, Gachabone’s passive ability. Passives worked regardless of whether your actives were sealed off.
[Your Ordinary Luck reflects 15% of your damage back to the enemy.]
The skeleton that popped into existence on my left side swung a dagger at Six. It wasn’t any old dagger either, but one with a blazing aura the same color as hers.
Dash.

In response, Six quickly adjusted her stance from lunging and retreated. It was a scene I had seen play out several times before. Probabilistic Retaliation had activated on several occasions even before I turned on Dark Mode, and Six had evaded the counterattacks with annoying agility.
Grin.
This was the first positive development in a while.
I guess she doesn’t know that much about Dark Mode.
If she did, she wouldn’t have made that split-second decision. Dark Mode’s auto-lock bonus applied to passives too—like this one.
Riiiiip.
The moment the summoned skeleton’s dagger sliced through the empty air where Six once was, a small rift appeared and swallowed it. Before long, it transcended space and sank into Six’s body.
Stab!
“Ugh.” For the first time in what felt like ages, a groan escaped that steely woman.
God damn it. All that work just to hit her thigh?

I wasn’t happy with that at all. If it had landed in her neck, heart, or between the eyebrows, it would’ve been an instant Game Over. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t disappointed by this outcome, but I shook off my regrets.
It’s not like I didn’t expect this to happen.
Starting with Hans A in the Crystal Cave, I’d encountered countless enemies.
Yeah, this is more my style.
Each time, Plan B had been the thing to lead me to victory. So, in that sense, just as I prepared, it was finally time to end this fight.
Dash.
Spew!
As I ran forward, I spat the blood in my mouth onto Six’s face. Although I didn’t have Acid Fluid from the Corpse Golem anymore, I could still block her vision.
Whoom!

The blood spewing and hammer swinging happened almost simultaneously, a combo beautifully wrecking her field of vision. Six stuck out her shoulder like she could see my trajectory anyway. It was the same shoulder that was already broken to the point that it was dangling.
Really making use of that one arm, huh?
Smack!
The hammer landed on her shoulder.
Whip!
Meanwhile, the woman thrust her dagger out at me. I didn’t avoid it.
Stab!
The dagger sank deep into my lower abdomen again.
Slide.

Ignoring the pain, I took advantage of the moment I’d been waiting for and threw my arm out—the same arm that normally had a shield on it, and that had been hanging limp since it was stabbed earlier. Six’s eyes hardened.
Oh, so you didn’t expect this either, huh? It was worth saving this until now, then.
Tap.
As soon as my fingertips touched Six’s neck, I used my thumb, index, and middle fingers to grip it tightly.
Squeeze.
Crack!
Then I drove my forehead into her face, which remained aloof despite the situation she was in.
Kwaaang!
Instead of holding Six’s body up as it fell back from the force, I piled on top of her to crush her under me.
Stab!
It felt like my side was on fire. This was kind of ridiculous. Did she really stab me even on the way down?
Whoom!
In the mount position, I brought down my hammer. Then, something incredible happened.
Ha... unbelievable.

Even while her upper body was being restrained, Six managed to avoid the hammer by using her reflexes to move just her neck. That was a surprise, but it didn’t make a huge difference. It wasn’t like Unavoidable Strike Correction didn’t apply to close-range attacks.
Crack!
The hammer I swung at her head tore through space and crushed her feet instead.
Stab!
In return, I got one more stab wound on my side. For a moment, I felt dizzy, like all the strength was leaving my body. But the more I felt that way, the harder I swung down.
Crack!
This time, the hammer struck a pretty good spot. It must have landed right on her wrist. The dagger she had clutched in her hand flew through the air and landed on the ground.
Okay, she has no weapon now.
Now that I didn’t need to worry about a counterattack, I brought my hammer down again.
Crack! Crack! Crack!
Six contorted her neck at strange angles three times to protect her head, but the fourth time was different. That was because that time, the hammer came down right on top of her skull.
Crack!

The strong shock the blow sent through her brain made her body go stiff like she was having a seizure. I didn’t stop and continued to bring the hammer down. There were no more auto-locks applied. Even a woman like her couldn’t move her neck to dodge the hammer while suffering from a concussion.
Smash, smash, smash!
One more time.

I lifted the hammer to bring it down for the fourth time and I saw Six’s eyes through the blood and crushed flesh of her face. It was quite a strange experience. I’d split countless heads before, but this had never happened.
Those calm eyes didn’t seem to match the predicament she was in at all. She looked up at me with those eyes and said, “...I lose.”
How nonchalant. She didn’t seem the type of woman to beg for her life, but I didn’t expect her to be this impassive either.
Well, either way, it doesn’t matter to me.
“Nia... Raf... donia...”
I brought down the hammer with all my might.
Crack!
With an eerie snap, Six’s body went stiff under me.
Huff, huff, huff...
My breath was so rapid that it was at the top of my throat rather than my lungs.
Is... she really dead?
It didn’t feel real. That was how strong of an enemy she had been. But I couldn’t stay here resting forever.
Slide.
After collecting my breath in a daze, I slowly got up. “Erwen, you can turn off—”
“Mister!”
It was like my blood pressure had plummeted. My vision turned white and my body staggered.
Motherfuck...
I needed to get up right now. There were still a lot of people to kill. I didn’t know what I’d end up losing if I fell asleep right now.
Slide.
My eyes fell shut.
[You have fallen into a state of Unconsciousness. Elementalization has been deactivated.]

[Remnants of the Abyss: you have received Recoil in proportion to the length of your bond with the Spirit of Darkness. Cast time: 318 seconds. All Resistance values are reduced by 50% for 3180 seconds. For 3180 seconds, all healing and regeneration effects targeting you are reduced by 90%.]

chapters.title: Chapter 428: Like Ice (3)
paragraphs: Regal Vagos witnessed Six’s defeat from afar and laughed to himself.
Thickheaded bitch. And she was so confident she could take him on her own.

He had been watching their battle closely ever since it began. If Six had succeeded, he intended to stop her from killing that barbarian bastard. A peaceful death was too kind a fate for that man. Vagos planned to use Subordination to turn him into his slave and make him live out the rest of his days in hell. If he got unlucky and that barbarian died before he could enact his plan, Vagos planned to at least absorb his soul and raise his stats.
Well, I guess it’s better this way. Since he’s down now too.
Vagos held the front line for a while, only pretending to fight before quietly retreating. He quickly headed over to the spot he’d been staring at.
Step. Step.
The distance narrowed rapidly.
Seizing him with Subordination and making him fight his own allies will be fun.
While he was moving forward, anticipation driving him, a small, trembling voice sounded nearby. “Regal Vagos...”
Whiiiiiip!
Before long, a threatening boom followed.
Clang!
He hurriedly turned around to block the arrow flying at him. There was an elf glaring at him from the direction it came from.
“...Right, I forgot about you.”
She was one of the Seven Powerful, known to most as Blood Spirit—Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.
Vagos licked his lips out of habit, feeling a strange sense of déjà vu.
For some reason, her face looks familiar every time I see it.
Of course, this thought wasn’t one he considered all that important.

Real tragedies were different from the tragedies found in stories. As evidence, it had neither rained nor thundered that day. It wasn’t the day a revolution began, nor was it a night so dark that even the stars didn’t twinkle. That day had been an ordinary day like any other.
“Erwen, if you keep making trouble, a scary barbarian man is going to come to scold you.” Her mother was chiding her as usual.
“Haha, enough of that. I’m sure she’s learned her lesson.” Her father was being his kind self.
“Wahhh!” Her younger sister was crying, as always.
“Daria? Where did that child go...?” And her naughty older sister had only come home early in the morning and was still sleeping in. Everything was normal that day.
Knock, knock.
Until the knock at the front door.
“Who is it?” Her father went to the door instead of her mother, who was doing housework, and the tragedy began right then. “A-A dragonian...? Why is a dragonian...?!”
“I need fame. And it seems killing some elves is the easiest way to get it.”
“Kyahhh!”
“M-Miriane! Take the kids and run!”

While her father stopped the man, her mother took the three sisters and fled. Before they could get far, though, the man caught up with them. The girls narrowly survived thanks to their uncle, who happened to be passing by.
“Please... take my children far away from here.”
“...Okay.”
“Thank you... my kind little brother.” Her mother had sacrificed herself like her husband, while the sisters were on the luckier side. The number of people who had died that day was over a thousand.
Erwen had had her older sister and her younger sister. They were the reason she was able to live.
“That young lady was born with the most destiny after you.”
Then her older sister died.
“Daria... isn’t here anymore?”
It had been her fault, and her relationship with her younger sister grew strained as a result. Still, she could keep going.
“I told you. I’m your guardian now.”
She met a man who sacrificed everything to protect her whenever there was danger, extended his hand, and helped her up whenever she felt like collapsing. But the world was too cruel.
“So Bjorn is dead.”
The moment she realized Bjorn had left her like her sister had, Erwen couldn’t hold back the tide of emotion.
Why is everything always taken away from me? Why is the little happiness I finally managed to hold in my hands crumbling so easily?
The reason was very simple: because she was weak. She was someone meant to be protected. These people had protected her, but she couldn’t protect them in return.
“The process of gaining the power of a pureblood is much more terrible than you imagine, and it’s also not something you can achieve just because you want it.”
She wanted to become stronger. Now that she had nothing left to protect, she wanted to show the people who stole from her the pain of something important being taken away from you.
[Elemental Ruler of Darkness Dicloe...]
That darkness gave her strength. With that strength, she took revenge. She was called a blood-thirsty bitch, but at her core, she remained the same.
Tremble...
Her fingers shook.
“Regal Vagos...”

At this rate, something else would be stolen from her. Even though she knew that, she found herself freezing. Though she was immeasurably stronger than she had been in the past, she was still the same weak, helpless girl she’d always been.
Slump.
But I can’t accept that. Rather than living with that regret again...
“Mister!”
It was better to die.
Zippp!
The bowstring was pulled.
Thud.
It was released.
Whiiip!
The arrow flew with terrifying speed, though it did not contain any special abilities.
Clang!
The man grabbed his sword and deflected it. “...Right, I forgot about you, bitch.”
Erwen forced her fear-filled body to move.
Dash.
The distance between them narrowed in an instant, proving how much she’d grown up to that point.
Whip!
This time, a dagger swung instead of an arrow.
“An archer fighting with a knife?”
That was because she couldn’t access the power of the spirits anymore. More importantly, Bjorn Yandel was right here. She couldn’t use an archer’s strategy of fighting from a distance.
Clang!
As soon as her dagger collided with his sword, she spun around to deliver a series of strikes.
Leap!
He hurriedly kicked off the ground and retreated, finding the blow fiercer than he expected.
Good, I was able to push him away and keep Mister safe.
“What the hell...?”
Erwen lowered her upper body and angled her short dagger forward. This was a basic stance her sister had taught her years ago. At the time, she had whined over needing to learn something like this.
“I told you. Even if you don’t have a bow or can’t use a spirit, you should be able to protect yourself.”
She realized it now. She had spent her whole life being protected.
“...Goddamn bastards.” There was no need for a lengthy exchange—Vagos cursed and charged at her. Erwen watched him approach, studying his movements without budging. Surprisingly, she felt calm.
Hah...

She couldn’t use her essences because she had used the passive skill Harmony to swap her Spirit Power out for Natural Power to aid Mister during his fight. Thanks to that, she had a smidge of Natural Power left, but it was too little to properly utilize. This was all she had left now.
One dagger.

All she had were the dagger techniques she learned from her older sister. Even those were probably nowhere near up to snuff compared to a close-combat adventurer like Amelia. No, they definitely weren’t enough. Compared to a warrior who had wielded a sword all his life, that much was obvious. But...
“So what?”
Until the bitterest of ends, she analyzed the enemy’s movements and gripped her dagger tight in pursuit of one goal, and one goal only.

“Mister...” In reality, he wasn’t even a “mister.” They were the same age, and she didn’t think he had a scary face anymore. Though others would probably think her strange if she voiced that out loud. “I’m going to protect Bjorn Yandel.”
She had decided to stop relying on others.
It’s easier to give up. This was a popular saying on the internet. Though the self-deprecating tone was uncomfortable, there was nothing untrue about the statement itself.
[Regal Vagos has cast Fear Imprint.]

It was easier to give up, and likewise, you couldn’t get hurt if you never had your hopes up. You could make quicker decisions and protect yourself from the challenges you knew you couldn’t overcome—like right now.
[Strong Willpower. Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has resisted Fear Imprint.]

The moment you let down your burdens, unparalleled peace came over you. The annoying buzzing in my ear dissipated, and a warm darkness embraced me, washing away the agonizing pain. It was a level of contentment that reminded me of my childhood. There were some people who found more comfort in a place like this than in a bright light.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has suffered damage.]
Of course, I wasn’t always like this. I had been an ordinary child, and like all ordinary children, I had idolized heroes.
[Regal Vagos roars loudly.]
