[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia does not back down and roars even louder.]

But at some point, I started hating hero stories. They were moronic. Why should I have to sacrifice myself for others? My life changed once I asked myself that question. It became more comfortable, more stable.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Asura’s Kick.]
[Fatal blow. The Eighth Rose has been defeated.]
But then... when did that start to change?
[You are still bleeding. Warning: Your health has dropped below 5%. You may die if your injury is not treated soon.]
A new question arose in my mind.
[Titana Akurava cries out to save her comrades.]
[Periton Eriabosti has cast Salvation.]
[Bogus Leichmont has cast Opposing Darkness. All divine power loses effectiveness due to the intervention of an evil god.]
Maybe it was some form of brain damage I contracted when I entered this barbarian body.
[Melend Kaislan has moved to rescue his comrade.]
[Anne Parvela has left the front line to block a knight’s path.]
[A stroke of powerful luck. Anne Parvela has been defeated.]
[The priest of the evil god who has lost his lover is greatly angered.]
What I knew for sure was that I didn’t want to give anything else up. Not just my life, but everything in it.
[Bogus Leichmont has cast Flesh Offering. The power of his next spell is increased by 5x in exchange for a right arm.]
[Bogus Leichmont has cast Corpse Flower.]
I was getting greedy.
[Melend Kaislan has suffered a serious injury and has been rendered incapable of combat.]
But even if that greed came back to hurt me, it was a deep desire that I couldn’t bring myself to fear or ignore any longer.
[Powerful Misfortune. Punishment – Exchange of Equivalence has been activated. Bogus Leichmont takes 50% of the damage from his last attack.]
[The priest of the evil god senses death approaching and spouts words of hatred.]
What was I doing right now again?
[Bogus Leichmont has cast Flesh Offering. The power of his next spell is increased by 5x in exchange for a left arm.]
[Bogus Leichmont has cast Flesh Offering. The power of his next spell is increased by 5x in exchange for two eyes.]
[Bogus Leichmont has cast Flesh Offering...]
The sound was distant and the pain was dull. My surroundings were dark and lonely.
[Bogus Leichmont has summoned the Executioner.]
[Ravieniastorous has suffered significant damage and has been rendered incapable of combat.]
[Sven Parav has fallen into a state of Fear.]
I felt like I was forgetting something.
[Strong Willpower. Sven Parav has resisted the Fear.]
[Sven Parav leaves the front line and defends against the Executioner’s attack. Sven Parav sweats profusely and shouts for help.]
I looked back on my memories.
[Amelia Rainwales has come to a decision after much consideration. She attacks Regal Vagos, not the Executioner.]
[Sven Parav is shocked.]
What had I forgotten?
[The Executioner has begun to rampage.]
[Sven Parav has been rendered incapable of combat.]
[Tsuon Irivan has died.]
[Lilith Marrone balls her fists and makes a decision.]
[Riard Ashed grabs Lilith Marrone’s wrist and shakes his head.]
I was sure there was something I had to do.
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-seven spirit spell Thought Acceleration.]
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-six energy spell Mana Amplification.]
[Riard Ashed has cast the rank-eight spell Heart Stimulation.]
I was sure there was something I vowed to never do again.
[Riard Ashed fires spells wildly.]
[The Executioner has suffered great damage and screams.]
Ugh, my head hurts.
[The Eleventh Rose has cast Absolute Sever.]
[Futa Rickerburn is seriously injured.]
[Unbelievable counterattack. The Eleventh Rose has been defeated.]
All I wanted to do was rest, but thoughts continued to pester me.
[The Ninth Rose has cast Absolute Sever.]
[Futa Rickerburn has been rendered incapable of combat.]
[Unbelievable counterattack. The Ninth Rose has been defeated.]
[Futa Rickerburn has died.]
[Titana Akurava has run out of MP. All active skills have been deactivated.]
[Manua Repeles has cast Iron Fist.]
[Amelia Rainwales has been pushed back significantly.]
[The Executioner has cast Great Earthquake.]
Booom!
[You have been damaged by falling rocks.]
While I was thinking long and hard about whatever I had forgotten about, the world around me shook and suddenly I felt suffocated.
[Warning: Your health has reached 0%. The countdown has begun.]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (493/496)]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (490/496)]
[Consuming 3 Spirit points per second (487/496)]
What is this?
[Periton Ariabos has decided to make a sacrifice.]
[Benjamin Orman has decided to make a sacrifice.]
[The Great Observer smiles at their noble will.]
I don’t know.
[Destruction.]
But I felt content with whatever happened.
[All characters and monsters within the radius have suffered significant damage.]
[The Executioner has been desummoned.]
[Periton Ariabos has died.]
[Benjamin Orman has died.]
Time passed.
[Riard Ashed fires spells wildly.]
[The Eighth Rose has been defeated.]
[The Thirteenth Rose has been defeated.]
My consciousness dulled.
[Riard Ashed has exhausted all of his mana. Riard Ashed smiles, asking you all to take care of the rest.]
In the silence that came over me, the faces of people I missed flashed behind my eyes like afterimages.
[Riard Ashed has died.]
[Guold Aldidi has moved toward Sven Parav. Sven Parav shakes his head, refusing treatment.]
I squeezed my eyes shut.
[Guold Aldidi has started running.]
[Manua Repeles has cast Wind Pressure.]
[Guold Aldidi has been seriously injured.]
[Amelia Rainwales has inflicted significant damage on Manua Repeles.]
I knew I had to open my eyes, but I grumbled at the thought like a child throwing a tantrum.
[Guold Aldidi has moved.]
I’ve done enough.
[Guold Aldidi has moved.]
I’ve done my best.
[Guold Aldidi has moved.]
[Guold Aldidi has stopped.]
Why?
[Guold Aldidi has cast Blood Transfusion.]
Thump!
[You have recovered.]
A warm energy embraced my cooling body.
[Your HP is now above 1%. The countdown has ended.]
That warmth made me instinctively realize.
Thump!
Yeah, it’s already much too late to quit midway through.
[You have awoken from your state of Unconsciousness.]
My eyes opened. The first thing I saw was Old Didi.
“Y-You’re awake... I’m gl... glad...” The old man was looking down at me, wheezing. There was a thick scent of blood in the air.
Slide.
My eyes slid down.
“Old man...”

“Ah, this... I got a little injured on the way here.” Old Didi covered his abdomen with his palm as if to hide it. It was a pointless attempt. This wasn’t a wound that could be hidden by a single hand.
“You need treatment quickly—”
Old Didi cut off my rambling. “That’s impossible. I used the last one to save you after you got hit with that boulder. There are no more potions.”
I just couldn’t understand. “Why... why would you...?”

“Sir Parav... told me that he could bear his own injuries, so I should save you first.” Old Didi laughed. “Everyone knows it. If you die, it’s over. Look, Yandel...” He coughed up blood and keeled over. But it seemed he still had something left to say. “Only you... can make our deaths mean something. Only you. I cannot do it. So...”
I couldn’t accept that. There was no such thing as a meaningless death. No matter the suffering you face, the struggle to survive always had meaning.
And yet... “You must survive,” Old Didi said to me. “You... are the Giant, after all.”
Giant. That was the nickname I’d earned from that bloody battle in the Crystal Cave.
“You’re the only one who can shoulder the burden of those who died here today and still move forward...”
“Old man, I’m no giant—”

“Don’t say that. I know you can do it. I... couldn’t bring myself to die because I wanted to live... to avenge my granddaughter! But I am standing here now to save you... because I believe you can do it for me...”
I was rendered completely speechless.
“So...” His faith in me became a boulder bearing down on my shoulders. “No matter what anyone says... you are the Giant.” Old Didi’s flame dimmed.
Squeeze.

I clenched my fists and forced myself to swallow down the weakness threatening to crawl up my throat. I wasn’t the Giant or anything like that. I was just an ordinary person who wanted to live. I wanted to fire back and ask why he was asking this of me, but I instead weathered the blow.

“...Don’t worry.” After all, this wasn’t the time to start an argument. Without averting my gaze, I said, “I will achieve everything you—no, all of you wanted on your behalf. You can trust me. I... swear it on the heart of a warrior.”
Although my voice was firm, I wasn’t confident. Would I be able to keep that promise? Even as I said it, inside I was filled with doubt.
But whether he was aware of that or not, Old Didi closed his eyes like that was enough for him. “Yes... that’s very... reassuring... You... will definitely... become a... Giant...”
“What are you saying? You told me a second ago that I’m already the Giant...”
There was no answer. And I knew that no matter how long I waited, the answer would never come.
Slide.

I peeled myself off the ground, wondering what had happened while I was unconscious. Many people were dead, both friend and foe. There were bodies crushed by ice fragments and boulders and a huge monster corpse in the center. The stench of death filled the area. The only ones still standing on their own two feet were six people, including me.
Khak!
Amelia was fighting the bald boxer named Repeles.
“Vagos! The barbarian is awake!” said a special ability user on Noark’s rear line.
“Don’t look over there! Kill this bitch first...!” The Dragon Slayer was swinging his sword.
An injured Erwen was fighting him off with only a dagger in hand. “M-Mister...!” Alerted to my consciousness by the special ability user’s shout, Erwen’s head turned.
That wasn’t a good move. Getting distracted during battle was tantamount to suicide.
[Kayle Elbad Zenegger has cast Land End Thorn.]

A black, thorny spear shot out from the special ability user’s hand, the same rank-two skill that killed Might Million in the Deadwood while we were in the process of casting Multi Teleportation. Belatedly sensing the surprise attack, Erwen’s eyes widened. At the same time, the mind of a warrior who had experienced numerous battles immediately recognized that Erwen wouldn’t be able to avoid it. This was nothing as grand as predicting the future—it was simply the kind of thing that you intrinsically understood, like how you knew a person would go flying if they were hit by a truck.
Whooom!
Time slowed down.
Slide.
My ankles bent and I prepared to dash toward her. But suddenly, my body froze. How come? I was ready to run forward immediately.
Thump.
It felt like something invisible was clinging to my ankles and shackling me to the ground. My heart went cold. I knew I shouldn’t be thinking this, but the thought still popped into my head anyway.
If I stop that... Will I survive?

There would definitely be consequences. In my current state, I might not be able to withstand a single thorn and could die instantly. Perhaps it was because I was under extreme stress, but I kept hearing a voice playing through my head.
“If the person you have to kill to survive is someone who has done nothing wrong...”
It was Hans A, with whom I was reunited recently.
“No, if it’s a comrade you want to protect more than anyone else...”
Maybe Hans A was right. I was already looking for reasons to save myself.
“How would you feel then?”

If I die, what will become of Old Didi? Jun? The other members of the squadron? I was able to come this far because they all sacrificed themselves. So... I can’t make a selfish call. I have to judge the situation rationally and lead us down a path that serves the collective rather than a single person. But...
Zippp.
So, what, I have to just watch Erwen die? Then what about Daria? The woman who asked me to be Erwen’s guardian on her deathbed?
Grit.

My thoughts were all jumbled up. How did I end up in this situation? The line between right and wrong was tangled, like a skein of thread that had gotten all twisted up. It felt impossible to make a good decision.
Squeeze.
My throat tightened.
So what? Fuck, I don’t know anymore. I’m just going to do what I want.
“You... will definitely... become a... Giant...”

I felt sorry for Old Didi, who had believed in me until the end. But right now, I was a barbarian. The Giant the old man spoke of wouldn’t sit back to ensure his own safety. I braced my frozen feet. Then I sprung forward like that momentary hesitation never happened at all.
Shaaaaaa.
A gust of wind blew and Erwen’s eyes met mine as I pulled her behind me. To the left, I could see the Dragon Slayer, looking surprised. Nearby, I could see Amelia fighting.
Khak!
And in the middle of it all, a sharp black thorn flew toward me.
Whooom!
My mind as I watched it approach was surprisingly calm. It wasn’t because I had given up. If I stayed alert and avoided getting hit in the vitals, there was a chance I could take one thorn.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Elementalization.]
...Huh?
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has proposed a contract with you.]
A familiar sensation spread through the spot where Erwen’s skin touched mine.

chapters.title: Chapter 429: Like Ice (4)
paragraphs: Immediately after Elementalization was activated, a translucent wind began to swirl around my skin.
[The Spirit of the Wind now dwells within your body.]
I couldn’t exchange a glance with Erwen, much less a conversation, but I could tell what she was aiming for.
[All damage you take will be adjusted for with improved dodging.]

With the Spirit of the Wind, dodging adjustments had a certain probability of activating. This probability was maxed out for attacks classified as magic, which was why the following condition was attached to Spirit of the Wind as well:
[Damage received from magic is doubled.]

This was the reason that Erwen didn’t usually turn on Wind Mode when dealing with wizards or special ability users—because she judged the risk to be greater than the potential reward. A dodging ability that had a 50 percent probability of working may sound nice, but if you took double the damage on hits, you could be putting yourself more at risk due to the nature of the gamble.
Whippp!
The coin had already been tossed, so there was only one thing I could do.
Thump.
Wait for the results.
Whiiip!
After a split second where everyone’s fate was on the line, the results were immediately apparent.
[You have succeeded in dodging.]
The Land’s End Thorn flying at me to skewer me only grazed my skin as if blown away by a gust of wind at the last second.
Kabooom!
The black thorn embedded itself in the ceiling with a thunderous rumble. The strength seemed to leave my body a moment later, and the wind enveloping my form died down.
[All of Erwen Fornacci di Tersia’s Natural Power has been consumed. Elementalization has been deactivated.]
So, this was all you had left in you... No, think about that later.
I rolled through the dirt and got up, still holding Erwen in my arms.
“Bjorn...”
Huh? Not Mister?

The sudden change in nicknames felt strange but I didn’t examine it too closely. Checking on her came first. “I know you’re tired, but can you deal with the special ability user on their side? You just have to hold him off.”
“...I can do it.”
Okay, the baton had been passed.
“You...!” As soon as I took my stance and turned around, a shock rattled my shield.
Khak!
Regal Vagos, the Dragon Slayer, was the person who first taught me what it meant to lose a comrade.
Khak!
I blocked each vigorous swing of his sword, though I noted they seemed somewhat haphazard.
I thought that when I saw him again, I would be so happy I could cry.
That wasn’t exactly the case. Well, I guessed that was to be expected. Though I’d been desperately waiting for this moment, I’d had to sacrifice many things to get here.
“You—you... how are you so stubborn?”
“I don’t think the bastard who came all this way to hunt me down has any right to ask that.”
“I’ll end you!”

Vagos’s sword was powerful. He seemed to be wringing every last bit of strength he had left into every fiery swing. The driving force behind each thrust was obvious. Wanting vengeance against me was one thing, but he also seemed to be aware that his only hope of getting out of this fight alive was killing me before I could kill him.
Khak!
The current lay of the land was simple. Erwen, who’d had a recent brush with death, used the last of her strength to mark the special ability user in the distance.
“Emily! I don’t have to worry about that guy, right?”
“...Don’t state the obvious.” Amelia, meanwhile, was engaged in battle with Baldy Repeles.
The rest of our enemies had fallen. Of course, there were some still alive among them, but they were hanging on by a thread. They had no energy to fight.
Khak!
The winner of this long battle would be decided now.
Khak!

I threw my weight behind my shield to push the sword away. Even though my Resistance stats had been wrecked by Recoil, I still had my Strength. I shoved my opponent back three steps with that slight movement alone. Now that I’d deflected his sword and gauged the shape he was in, it was my turn.
“Behel—aaaaaah!” I cried out to my ancestral gods and ran forward.
Even though Wild Outburst won’t activate no matter how hard I shout... It really isn’t the same running in without it. I don’t get as pumped.
Whooom!
I brought my hammer down with the power of my ancestral gods behind it.
Dash.
Vagos dodged it by taking two steps back, then thrust his sword into the slight gap that appeared as I swung the hammer. He had a lot of combat experience.
Which means his instincts are extremely sharp.
Soon, his sword was embedded deep in my side. If I couldn’t feel the negative effect Recoil had had on my Resistances before, I could definitely feel it now.
Stab!
It wasn’t that I couldn’t have avoided or blocked the stab. However, if I had done that, it would have only served to draw out this fight.
Whip.

Immediately after the sword struck, my arm shot forward right on cue. My target was his neck. Since the difference in our Strength stats was clear, I figured if I could get a hold of him, there would be no way for him to escape. But it seemed he was also well aware of this.
Dash.
Vagos quickly backpedaled. He was in such a hurry that he didn’t even take his stuff with him.

“Are you leaving this behind?” I pulled the sword out from my side with gritted teeth and smiled with a mouth full of blood. “I don’t need any more swords. Seriously, what kind of swordsman keeps losing his sword?”

I tutted like this was pathetic, and my opponent’s face hardened. His eyes were so full of hatred that it seemed they were liable to shoot daggers at any moment. But his actions told a different story than his eyes. Vagos looked panicked, clearly unsure what to do without his sword.
Leap.
Then, he ran, not toward me but to the side. Once again, his thought process was incredibly obvious.
Is he going to use that sword on the ground nearby?

Come to think of it, the same thing happened in the maze. Once he was unable to use his sword, he ran up to Missha and stole hers. Until Rotmiller took that sword with his own body, proclaimed it his, and put it in the Treasure Vault, I could only watch helplessly as the Dragon Slayer rampaged.
It’s different this time.
Back then, he gave me two options—the worst evil and a lesser one—and I’d had to choose one. But now, the situation was completely different. I wasn’t the one choosing—this guy was.
Dash.

As soon as Vagos took his feet off the ground, I ran forward too. The distance was narrowed in a second, and his eyes went wide. He seemed to be weighing whether it was a good idea to still go for the sword or not.
Whooom!
The choice he ended up making as he watched the hammer swing toward his head was pathetic.
Dash.
Vagos gave up on the sword on the ground and went into a roll.
I didn’t even need to worry about a fake-out.
If it were me, I would’ve pretended to pick up the sword and instead caught him off guard.

Well, I guess he’s not willing to do something like that since he’s a swordsman. Hmm, but if swords are really that important to him, he should’ve been willing to sacrifice a shoulder to get his hands on that one... Maybe he’s after something else.

I would be lying if I said I didn’t find his decision pitiful but I armed my mind with caution instead of carelessness. That was much smarter than underestimating the enemy and getting screwed as a result.
Whooom!
I swung my hammer again, careful to avoid getting too close.
Dash!
Vagos shuffled back again.
Tap.
We repeated this process several times, and his back finally touched the wall. At that moment, his slitted dragon pupils widened. It was then that I realized.
This bastard... he wasn’t even thinking about the wall.
The secret move I thought he was aiming for? It never existed. He was just running around like a headless chicken to avoid my hammer and ended up getting driven into this corner. That was all.
Crack!
As if to prove this, the hammer struck his left shoulder as it came down.
“Ugh!” Vagos threw himself to the side, groaning with bloodshot eyes. It felt like a weird move. More accurately, it felt futile.
“If you’ve given me your shoulder, you should at least take something in return.”
If you were going to end up letting me break your shoulder anyway, you could’ve risked it to take the sword earlier.
Instead of being happy with my enemy’s bad judgment, I felt angry.
Squeeze.
I dragged him in by the nape of the neck as he tried to escape like an eel and threw him against the wall.
Bang!
His mouth fell open and he coughed up blood.
Choke!
I swung my hammer once more. The target was the top of his head but he managed to fling himself to the side again and avoid it.
Crack!
Thanks to that, his left leg was completely crushed.
“Aaaaaagh!” He screamed. It didn’t feel satisfying at all. The woman I killed earlier, Six, didn’t lose her composure even as her head was pounded in.
This is one childish son of a bitch.
“Just... because of someone like you...”
But his desire to survive, at least, was formidable.
Drag.

Vagos tried to get away, crawling on the ground with his crushed leg. I looked to see where he was headed. It was where Amelia was engaged in a fierce battle with Baldy. Was he planning on relying on him for help?
Press.
I stepped on his back to stop him. I guessed that finally forced him to face the facts.
“...K-Kill me,” he said through gritted teeth. This was a very fortunate thing. Although he stuttered a little, he didn’t beg for his life. If he had, that would’ve put me in a really bad mood.
Kwaaang!
I quickly glanced at Amelia. She was still engaged in fierce combat as we spoke. I made a decision. Without delaying any longer, I was going to say what I wanted to say and then end it.
“Do you remember Riol Warb Dwalkie?”

“Heh, hehehe...” About to die, he sneered as he discovered my Achilles’ heel. Not that it would particularly make a difference at this point. “You’re not talking about that half-wizard from back then?”

That day, I hadn’t even been able to bring his body out of the labyrinth, so we had to hold a funeral with a few of his keepsakes and nothing more. That day, I had decided that someday, when this moment came, I would say this.

“You sit there and listen.” I broke his remaining shoulder with my hammer and said, “Riol Warb Dwalkie. That half-wizard who saved us all in the maze that day...” Though it took a long, long time—almost three years—“He did not lose. Because thanks to him, I get to kill you now. He won, you got it?”
He didn’t answer this time, either. Was it his last bit of pride making him hold his tongue? I flipped him around and grabbed his chin, forcing him to nod.
Hah, then is it all over now?
It didn’t feel real, but it seemed so.
Crack!
Now die, you son of a bitch.
Crack!
After dealing with the Dragon Slayer, I joined forces with Amelia to pound the bald boxer into dust too.
[Manua Repeles has been defeated.]
Next was the special ability user who was making a whole production of trying to evade Erwen. She persistently chased him around.
[Kayle Elbad Zenegger has been defeated.]
With that, all enemy skulls were crushed. The moment my brain recognized that fact, the heat of the arduous battle escaped my body in a rush and cold air enveloped me.
Shaaaaaaaaa!
Without the enemy around, this place was as quiet as the moment after a storm’s end. Was that why? It finally felt real.
“It’s over...”
Finally, the battle was over, but there was no time to rest.
“Amelia, you check and see if any of our enemies are still alive.”
“I-I’ll help too!” said Erwen.
“No. Resting is the most helpful thing you can do right now.”
I left the confirmation process to Amelia and forced Erwen to rest as she had exhausted her energy to the limit.
Grit.

I picked up the members of our squadron lying on the cold ground. I checked the extent of the injuries on the ones still breathing and closed the eyes of those who had lost their warmth. Horrible wasn’t a strong enough word to describe this situation.
Sven Parav, Melend Kaislan, Lilith Marrone, Titana Akurava, Ravien, James Calla, Versyl Gowland, Erwen, Amelia, and me.
“Ten people...” That was the number of team members who had survived this expedition. Everyone else was dead.
“Yandel... I found four potions.”
After searching the Order of the Rose and Noark, Amelia found some potions that were promptly divided and distributed between us based on the severity of our injuries.
“I’ll see if there are any more potions.”
“Thanks, Emily...”

The potions were nowhere near enough to grant all of the injured a full recovery. But thanks to the fact that we administered them in order of urgency, those who were at the crossroads of life and death were able to heal a little and came to their senses one by one.
“So... we’re really the only ones who survived.”

Darkness fell in the eyes of the squad members as they learned of the extent of the damages we’d suffered over the course of this expedition. The reason for that was simple. We knew too much about each other now to feel happy to have survived while the others died. Anger surged forward before relief ever got the chance.
Wail!
Though the rest of us didn’t burst into tears like the wizard Marrone, we weathered our sadness with clenched fists.
“Mr. Ashed... said his wife was waiting for him. Priestess Eriabosti... had a child.”
“Ventis Gerod dreamed of reaching the Abyss one day.”
“Mr. Iriban said he wanted to open up a shop after this quest was over.”
“None of them... should have died in a place like this. They shouldn’t have... but... but why...?!”
It didn’t take long for sadness to bleed into our anger.
“Lord Yandel... tell me. What... what did we... do so wrong? Why did everyone have to die here like this?”
After a long detour, we reached the question at the heart of all this.
“Did we... do something that bad? Bad enough... to be punished like this?”
“...The first thing I’m going to do is kill the commander of my clan. Even if I die in the process.”
“That won’t work. We have to get word about this out there and protest. Tell people what we had to go through!”
“It won’t be easy with the palace involved but... It might be possible. Ravien is a dragonian. And Akurava, you have quite a bit of sway with the dwarves.”
“Lord Yandel, you were a candidate for chieftain, right? And Miss Erwen holds a very important position with the elves.”
“Yes, if the four races come together and join forces...!”
The more they vented their emotions, the cooler my head and heart became. I wanted to unleash my anger like them, too, but I couldn’t.
“You... will definitely... become the... Giant...”
To become the kind of person Old Didi wanted me to be, I couldn’t act like that.
Squeeze.
“Lord Yandel! What do you think, Lord Yandel? You’re not going to stay quiet, right?”
I stared at all of them as they trembled with hot anger. Then I spoke. “I... no, we will, actually.”
“...Excuse me?”
“Because that’s the only way we’ll be able to survive. Kaislan, you’re a knight, so you would know. Even if the four races band together and barge into the palace, we’ll all die.”
Even Kaislan, who always swayed public opinion in my favor, didn’t respond this time.
So, you don’t want to answer.

I continued on regardless. “It’s impossible for the four races to join forces in the first place. If we ask them all for help, do you really think they’d risk their lives to fight alongside us? With the fate of their entire races on the line?”
I didn’t think so. This wasn’t a fairytale. The people who lived here made calculations and decisions on cold, hard grounds, not gardens of flowers.
“Still...! We have to do something!”
“Even if we all die as a result?”
“That’d still be better than not doing anything!”
“Marrone, do you really think that? Do you think the dead will be pleased if you waste your hard-won life like that?”
“Then... then what do you want me to do?!” It was strange seeing this wizard, who never seemed to lose the laugh in her voice no matter how difficult the situation was, scream at me like this.

I wasn’t cowed. “As I said before, we have to stay quiet. We can’t say anything, much less protest. We’ll have to pretend to believe there was some other reason why the main unit didn’t come. We’ll also have to act like we didn’t kill Noark’s secret eighth-floor trainees.”
It’d be considered a great military achievement if it became public knowledge, but we wouldn’t be able to reveal it to anyone.

“And the legendary Order of the Rose?” This was more of the same. Though confronting them was an achievement worthy of bragging about at drinking parties for the rest of our lives, this was how it had to be. “We never met them.”

We were the only ones who knew what transpired here. So, if we lied about what happened, the people who sent us here would piece the facts together on their own in a way that was palatable for them. Perhaps something went wrong. Perhaps the Order clashed with the enemies chasing after us, and we were lucky enough to survive as a result.
“Then... what about the people who died...?” Marrone asked through tears. “Those guys...”
I bit down on my lip before blurting, “Those guys were killed by monsters after escaping Glacier Eye.”
“Monsters...?”
“Yes, they were exhausted from the journey out of Glacier Eye. And with our equipment gone and our lack of food... It’s not totally unrealistic—”

“That’s a lie! They didn’t die like that! We fought powerful enemies! And it was so tiring that... I thought so many times that maybe... Maybe I should let myself die instead of fighting... But we still fought... until the bitter end, without anyone giving up. We fought and won... but... but—! Monsters? They were killed by monsters?”
“Stop it, Ms. Marrone...”
“Wahhh!” Kaislan held Marrone and soothed her as she cried.
This time, Sven Parav stepped forward. “Then... what happened next?”
“We hid like cowards until closing day and held out until we were the only ones who survived. That will be the ending we tell to the world.”

“I see. That certainly seems like the way most likely to secure our survival. But...” His eyes bored into mine. “I don’t like it at all.” His voice was firm in a way I’d never heard from him before, but there was no hostility in his gaze. Why was that? “But I will do as you say.”
“Why?”
“Because I can tell by the look in your eyes that you’re the one who likes this option the least.”
I was left speechless, and Akurava took the opportunity to come forward. “You’re not... planning on staying quiet forever... right?”
“Of course not.”
“Then I’ll wait.” Akurava stepped back.
Next was Calla. “I... will try too. Though I’ll have to face the clan leader and act like nothing happened... At least that’ll be better than today, when I couldn’t even watch my comrades die...”

I could feel his burning fervor even through his closed eyes. I went up to the rest of the crew and secured their support one by one. Once I’d spoken to all of them, I finally turned to the wizard slumped on the ground.
“Lilith Marrone.”
When our eyes met, she looked up at me and asked, “How long... How long do we have to wait?”
Well, I don’t know. But if I were to give an honest answer...
“A very long time.” It’d be more than a few years until we could draw our swords, but one thing was clear.
“...I see.”
It was the seventy-first day of our expedition inside an ice cave in Ice Rock on the seventh floor. A chill rose from the ice around us, but there was a wave of anger burning inside each of us.
“If I wait... if waiting will make it possible...! I... will wait.”
The chill ensured that anger was cold—the type of rage that wouldn’t burn out no matter how much time passed. We each kindled a cold flame in our hearts, where they would remain for a long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 430: Return of the Dead (1)
paragraphs: After our discussion concluded, I borrowed a dagger from Amelia to cut open the Dragon Slayer’s abdomen.
Slide.
The dagger sliced through his skin like a surgical scalpel. Once the laparotomy was over, I calmly took out his heart. Since it was so cold here, it was still fresh.
A dragonian’s heart looks different from an ordinary person’s.
It almost looked like a tropical fruit with a bumpy exterior. There were also chain marks on it for some reason.
As I curiously examined it, Ravien said, “The chain marks are probably traces of Pen’s curse.”
Hmm, really? Then it’s always been bumpy?
“Gowland, please cast preservation and distortion magic on this.”

After casting Distortion on the extracted heart, I stored it in a suitable container. Ravien seemed to want to guard the box herself, but I stopped her before she could grab it. “I’ll hold on to this for the next while.”
“It’ll be useful for negotiations.”
“You’re... not going to give it to them right away?”

“Exactly. After things calm down, I plan to meet with the ancient elder dragon myself and give it to him in exchange for him keeping it a secret. It’ll be a headache if news that we beat this guy and took his heart spreads.”

I was a bit worried about how this would go over with her, but Ravien willingly accepted my logic. “Okay. You’ll get much more out of it than I would. Of course, I feel bad for Pen, but since she won’t have to wait that long...”
“Thanks for understanding.”
Okay, that matter is settled.
Once we had our hands on his heart, we held a funeral. There were no more priests left to preside over it, but we cremated our dead comrades like last time.
Rattle.
Once it was over, we secured the ashes and bone fragments in a box. After that, we started looting Noark’s elites and the Order of the Rose, and gathering the gear of our dead comrades.
“Take all of the squadron’s equipment. Since we can’t use sub-space, stuff as much of it in your bags as possible.”
We collected all of our comrades’ equipment, which would serve as mementos to remember them by.
“Since we don’t have room, make sure to only take the valuables from Noark’s people.”

We decided to take a decent amount of Noark’s equipment. We’d killed a lot of Noark’s soldiers before coming back to Glacier Eye, and their loot currently lay dormant in our sub-spaces. This meant that even if someone asked us where we got this loot, there would be no way for them to tell when we obtained it or exactly from whom. Unlike the Order of the Rose.
“Collect the Roses’ items separately. Those need to be handled carefully.”
Their equipment and consumables were mostly military supplies, so our options for selling and using them were limited. The moment these items were put on the market, word would reach the palace.
Not to mention, if they suddenly decide they want to divvy up the loot on our behalf and look through our belongings when we get back, our plan to keep things quiet will go sideways.
It wasn’t a sure thing, but the risk of that happening existed.
We’ve made enough money off the military for now...
Kaislan, a former soldier, seemed rather satisfied with the jump in our budget. It was alarming to see him get teary-eyed about his dead comrades a second later, though. Was he all good, or...?
“Yandel, don’t feel too guilty. We’ll make their last wishes come true.”
“What are you saying? My nose is just runny from the cold.”
Whew, think other thoughts... other thoughts...
I moved toward the area where the bodies of the Roses and their equipment were sequestered. I didn’t plan on taking a single thing, of course.
But I can at least take a look...

I searched them thoroughly, figuring one of them might have something on them that might expose one of the palace’s weaknesses, or contain other important information. The more I looked, the more my stomach churned.
Wow, all these daggers are mystium. The leather is all Ogre... We have to leave all this behind? Can’t we figure out how to hide it so we can melt it or cut it up to make it into new equipment?
Greed crept up on me, but...
“We have to give this up.”

Even a 1 percent risk of exposure was unacceptable. I could always make up an excuse and claim that we obtained the Dragon Slayer’s heart while he was chasing us, but there was no way I could come up with a believable story for these.
“...Huh?” As I was rummaging through the Roses’ corpses, I found myself confused.
What are these rings?
All of the knights were wearing identical rings on their middle fingers.
Did these guys... always wear rings?
I combed through my memory, but that didn’t seem to be the case. While I was fighting the woman named Six, she hadn’t been wearing a ring.
What is this?
The moment the question occurred to me, I immediately removed the rings from all the corpses and took a closer look. They weren’t Numbers Items. So were they magic items?
“Marrone, Gowland.” Feeling the need to check, I asked the magic users to appraise them. It didn’t take long for their assessment to come in.
“These are binding-type magic devices. The moment you put one of these on, it disappears and becomes a part of your soul.”
“Binding-type magic devices?”
“You know. Like the summon imprints used to summon ships on the Great Sea on the sixth floor. That’s a prime example of a binding-type item.”
“Then... this ring...”

“Yes. It’s a sub-space ring. And it’s also several times higher quality than most similar magicology products on the market.” No wonder none of them had been wearing any sub-space rings or bracelets. “Binding-type magical devices usually leave some kind of imprint like a tattoo on the person’s body, but these don’t seem to have anything like that. Looks like there’s also a detection nullification circuit engraved on it.”
“Does that mean even the palace has no way of knowing whether someone has one of these?”
“Yes. I think so.”
I didn’t know what was inside these binding-type sub-spaces, but I knew one thing for sure: we’d hit the jackpot. With these rings, we wouldn’t have to throw out all of the Roses’ equipment.
“Take everything!”

We gathered all of the Roses’ equipment and put it in our backpacks. We could carry it like this for now and then put it in our new sub-spaces as soon as we arrived in the city. Those bastards would be none the wiser.
The problem is that there are only seven...
Currently, we had ten people. Three people wouldn’t get a ring. But surprisingly, the distribution of the rings ended in a blink of an eye without any dispute.
“...This is far more than I deserve when I did nothing in this battle.” James Calla, who had been unable to participate in the battle due to being temporarily blind, gracefully abstained.
“I will give up my claim too. I already have a binding-type sub-space.”
“Me too.”
Akurava and Ravien, who already had similar items, also conceded, thus settling the issue of ownership entirely.
[You have put on a Liar’s Rose Ring. The Liar’s Rose Ring now belongs to you.]
The rings began to glow and disappeared in flashes of light as soon as we put them on.
“How do we open the sub-space?”
“Brainwave recognition. If you think about opening the sub-space, it’ll open.”
Wow, is this the newest royal technology? This will be really useful in the future.
“Looks like we’re all set.” With that, the process of collecting mementos and loot alike was over.
[The wall of ice has melted.]
A day later, when the secret room was open, we all left the battlefield together. Though there was food in the Roses’ backpacks, it wasn’t enough to feed ten people.
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
[Lilith Marrone has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
We got our hands on as much monster meat as we could and headed back toward Glacier Eye.
“It’s a shame. If we could somehow take everything that’s down there too, we could buy ourselves mansions in the royal capital.”

However, with the Glacier Wizard Cariathea waiting for us, we had no chance of getting back in. There was no telling how much equipment was buried down there. The moment the labyrinth closed, it would all vanish into thin air.
“Now, let’s call it a day and rest here.”

Getting meat was important, but we didn’t rush it and took breaks as often as possible. Even if we went hungry for the remaining days, it wouldn’t kill us, and the squadron wasn’t exactly in fighting form right now.
“Kaislan, are you okay?”
“I’m okay, don’t worry. I can last until we get out.”

There were no priests and only four bottles of potion left. Everyone had survived, but for those who suffered serious injuries, there were obvious lingering consequences. Erwen, for one, was all out of MP and Natural Power so she couldn’t use a single skill. Only a few of us could fight at our usual level.
“Still... maybe it’s because we went through all that, but this really doesn’t feel all that hard at all...”
“Ha, I agree.”
“I thought I’d experienced pretty much everything there is to experience in life, but I didn’t realize how lucky I was.”
We chatted like this during the breaks, but mostly we discussed the future.
“The clan... will you form it right away?” Marrone asked quietly.
“Probably. But most people will have to join later.”
“True... Sir Kaislan is from the military. I’m sure he’ll have a tough time leaving.”

“Not just Kaislan. It’d seem strange for us to suddenly come together. We’ll have to leave some time in between. If we wait long enough, we’ll all end up getting kicked out or fired from our respective positions, anyway. It won’t be too late to band together a year from now.”
“...I have some ideas for the clan emblem.”
“Wow, you’re very talented, Ms. Marrone.”

Combing through the start of the expedition up to now, we crafted a cover according to the timeline of events and got our stories straight. If there were any inconsistencies or concerns, we discussed them together and ironed them out.
“Yandel, there’s one thing I’m worried about.”
“Hit me.”

“Even if we have our stories straight, will the palace really believe what we say? We’ve established that we’re all resistant to lie-detection spells, but that’s not the only way to ascertain the truth.”
I’d been mulling that over plenty too—a scenario in which the powers that be didn’t believe us. If they had the slightest suspicion and wanted to verify the facts, what would we do then?
“As I said before, the palace has no reason to do that. They won’t want to dig into this and leave a trail for us to follow.”
“Right... that would normally be the case. If we really were oblivious, asking those questions would give us reason to be suspicious of them... But what if they still risk it?”
“If they do... it doesn’t matter. The point of this plan isn’t to deceive the palace.” Plan A was ideal, of course, but having to switch to Plan B wouldn’t necessarily mean all was lost, either.
“Sorry? What do you mean?”

“To them, the fact that we got our stories straight and chose to be silent will be a message in itself. A sign that we’ll stay quiet, so there’s no need to mess with us from now on. A kind of appeal from the weak to the strong.”

This incident involved the duke, the marquess, an alliance of minor nobles, the Alminus Company, and even the Adventurers’ Guild. Even if they suspected something happened in the labyrinth, they wouldn’t try to confirm it. And even if they did, it was highly unlikely they’d do something so bold again. I was going to make a big splash before they ever got the chance. When there were more eyeballs on you, you had to be more careful. A prime example of that was the way they gave me a title without officially confirming I wasn’t an evil spirit. That was the royal way of dealing with things.
“We’ll need to build up our influence in that time so that turning a blind eye seems like a much better option than messing with us.”
“But isn’t that more dangerous? The bigger we get, the warier of us they’ll be.”
“I don’t think so.”
“Why is that?”
“No matter how big we get, we’re a drop in the ocean compared to the palace.”
The palace’s influence was enormous. No sane person would ever consider taking up arms against Rafdonia’s royal family.
“They’ll just assume we’re banding together because it’s our best shot at survival. They won’t realize we’re preparing to stick a knife in their backs.”

The members of this squadron had never met before our single trip into the labyrinth. Who would ever assume we planned to rally against the palace to seek revenge? Sadness and anger were fleeting emotions, after all. Normally, people were just grateful to have survived horrible situations and made smart decisions afterward.

“But on the off chance...” Akurava seemed somewhat convinced by my logic, but she still raised the worst-case scenario. “On the off chance that they decide we’re a nuisance and try to get rid of us... what then?”
The answer was simple.
Well, what can you do? You just have to move to Plan C.
It was our seventy-fifth day in the labyrinth, about four hours before the long-awaited closing.
“What is it?”
Versyl Gowland suddenly sat next to me during one of our breaks and asked me something. “Hey, Mr. Yandel, Ms. Naria was probably an evil spirit, right?”
“Probably?”

“Right... probably...?” Versyl muttered. I just stayed quiet because I had nothing else to say on the subject. After a moment of silence, Versyl spoke again. “Um... then what do you think of Ms. Naria?” Her question was full of caution.
“I think of her as a comrade who met an unfortunate end. But... what are you really trying to ask me?”
“I’ll reword the question. If Ms. Naria was still alive, would you still consider her a comrade?”
I could vaguely see what she was getting at, but I answered honestly anyway. “Of course.”
“...Even if she’s an evil spirit?”
“We’re already all enemies of the palace, so what does that matter? Evil spirit or not, I don’t care. All that matters to me is whether someone’s trustworthy.”
“...I see.” Versyl nodded, a strange look on her face, and left after some more idle conversation.

Hmm, I wonder what her objective was. Was she just curious about what kind of person I am? Did she maybe figure out that that punk Goblin is an evil spirit? And she’s wondering what I would do to him?
I thought that was a pretty plausible hypothesis—at least until Amelia pulled me aside two hours later.
“Yandel, I want to talk to you for a minute.”
“Did something happen?”
“It has to do with the thing you asked me to do.”
I blinked at her in confusion. “I asked you to do something?”
“You told me to investigate Sven Parav.”
Ah, that?

I definitely did ask her to do that. Considering his habit of carelessly running his mouth at the Round Table, I couldn’t shake the concern that he was going to end up spilling our squadron’s secrets there. I was planning to monitor him and take him well in hand.
“I meant for you to do that outside, though...?” I didn’t even use the term “investigate” myself. All it had been was a gentle request asking her to keep a close eye on him.
Amelia shrugged with a chuckle. “Then you should be grateful I misunderstood.” Her attitude suggested she had something useful for me.
I instantly sat up. “I guess you found something?”

“If you’re curious, see for yourself.” With that, Amelia unfastened her belt seemingly out of the blue. I blinked, alarmed, but all she did was fiddle with a hidden pouch and take out a small crystal ball.
“This is...”
“It’s a recording crystal.”
You think I don’t know that? I’m just surprised you managed to hide something like this in a belt you’re always wearing... She’d probably beat me up if I joked that she’s a voyeur, right?
I resisted the urge and activated the crystal ball Amelia gave me, figuring the first thing I needed to do was check it out.
...Chew, chew, chew.
The start of the video showed Sven Parav secretly gnawing on beef jerky he had hidden away in his jacket, away from the group. I was immediately filled with betrayal.
“That son of a bitch, he told me to my face that he didn’t steal any beef jerky—”
“Shut up and just watch. It’s coming.”
No sooner did Amelia scold me than something changed in the video.
“Mr. Sven Parav.” A woman approached Sven, who was turned around.
“Eek!” He was clearly surprised to be caught red-handed with the jerky.

“Can we talk for a moment?” To my surprise, the woman who approached him was Versyl. Sven glanced around uncomfortably and didn’t respond. “Ah, I’m not going to tell the others about the beef jerky. Don’t worry. I just want to have a quick conversation.”
“...Can’t we talk later?”
“Does that mean you don’t want to speak to me?”
“N-No, it’s not that... I j-just feel like something’s off...”
“You’re not making any sense.”
Versyl tilted her head like she had no clue what he was talking about, but I was impressed.
Did he instinctively pick up on the fact that Amelia was watching him?
I wasn’t sure, but the video continued to play.
“Anyway, I’ll cut this short and get to the point.”
“Sorry? Ah, right... go ahead. I’ll listen.”
What followed was a single sentence. “I know you’re an evil spirit.”
In response, both Sven and I adopted the same blank look on our faces.
...Cough! Cough!
“Be quiet. They’ll hear you.”
“B-But w-what are you talking about?! Me, an e-e-e-evil spirit—!”
The bombshells didn’t stop there.
“Don’t bother planning your getaway. I’m an evil spirit too.”
Holy shit, a coming out?
“...Eh? Wha... Ms. Gowland... an evil spirit...?” Sven was completely out of it.
Versyl, on the other hand, was utterly calm. “The reason I’m bringing this up is simple. With your personality, I figured you might slip up in the community.”
“U-Uh—”
“So don’t even think about saying a word about this squadron. I’ll be watching. Whether in the community bulletin board, or the Round Table.”
Dun-dun-dun!
There was no sound effect but both Sven and I seemed to hear it in our heads all the same.
“The R-Round Table? How do you...?”
“Because I’m one of its members. How else would I know you’re an evil spirit?”

“W-Wait... if you’re a woman... Q-Queen? No, that’s not your vibe...” Sven rambled in an obvious attempt to calm his mind. Then he raised a shaking finger to point at her. “N-No way... you’re... Fox?”
With that, I paused the video.
Versyl Gowland is Fox, huh?
This quest had borne some more fruit.
[The labyrinth is now closed. You are being transported to Rafdonia.]
The marquess was at his desk working when he paused to set his pen down and pick up a hot cup of tea. He took a sip and checked the time.
It’s almost time for the portal to open.

There were five minutes left until noon. The labyrinth would soon close and the empty Dimension Squares would be filled with adventurers who had completed their arduous quests. Though this was an event that took place every month, even he found today special.
“I hope the mission was successful.”
The Eye of the Sky was the device at the core of Noark’s strategy, and their biggest weapon against Rafdonia. A squadron of thirty people had been hastily assembled to destroy it.
“Well, it doesn’t matter if they fail.”

The marquess had prepared documents and official statements for two scenarios. The first was if the mission was successful but the expedition team did not survive. The other was if the mission was not successful and the team didn’t survive, either. There was no file prepared with their survival in mind. The marquess may have been a meticulous man, but he didn’t make a habit of doing pointless work.
“It seems that thorn in our side is finally gone.”
The marquess chuckled and set his teacup down on the desk. Then he picked up his pen again and started going through the piles of work in front of him. A little over ten minutes passed.
Whooom!
The message stone in the office vibrated. The call was coming from a checkpoint near the marquess’s home.
A frown appeared on the marquess’s face. “What is it?”
“...Sorry to disturb you. Some adventurers claiming to be a special forces team working for the royal family have arrived at the gate.”
“...Special forces?”
“Ah, yes... do you not know of them, then? I’m sorry. They’re each rather extraordinary people, so I hesitate to accuse them of lying...”
“I see...”
“Yes. And the man who appears to be their spokesperson won’t stop demanding we contact you... What should we do?”
“Is that so? All right. I’ll send someone out there soon. Keep them there. Ah... how many people were there?”
“Ten people... exactly ten people.”
“I see. All right,” the marquess said, his tone calm and collected. With that settled, he ended the call.
Riiiiiip.
The second it was over, he tore both documents that were on his desk and burned them.
“Ten people, huh? Things are getting interesting.”
He didn’t know what kind of trickery they used, but it seemed the dead had somehow come back to life.

chapters.title: Chapter 431: Return of the Dead (2)
paragraphs: The sky was a little gloomy. Nevertheless, sunlight peeked through the clouds, the warmth driving out the chill that had seeped into my bones. This was a place without shivering cold or hunger.
“It... feels real now. We really got back alive...”

As always, being in the city after the ordeals we faced in the labyrinth was a strange feeling. We were definitely glad to have survived, but our hearts were heavy. There were some who hadn’t been able to come home with us.
“If they lasted... if they lasted just a little longer...”
If they did, a few more people may have been here with us.
“Ms. Marrone,” Sven Parav called in a warning tone. Marrone stopped her mumbling and gritted her teeth.
Just because we were back in the city didn’t mean this was over. It was too early to let our guards down. We may be faced with tougher challenges than the ones we overcame in the labyrinth now.
Squeeze.

We swallowed down the complaints bubbling up inside of us, and not just because the place we were in now was the same mansion we stayed at for a few days before entering the labyrinth. It was simply that we couldn’t go there. No matter how high and steep the climb, no matter how hard it would be, we had to leave behind those people who fought to the bitter end to get us here.
“Kaislan, how are you feeling?”

“Ah, I couldn’t be better. But I guess I’m the last one?” Once Kaislan returned from his appointment with a priest who had been summoned to the mansion, the entire squadron gathered in the entrance hall.
“Why don’t we go for a walk instead of just staying here? Looks like it’s a nice day today.”
“I wish we could.”
“Wish we could?”
“You saw the knights in front of the hall, right? They’ll stop us from leaving even for a second,” Akurava explained.
“Ha! As if we’ve done something wrong!” the wizard Marrone huffed, resentful. “Being treated like this even after we completed our mission—we should be getting treated like heroes!”
“Um, Miss Marrone...”
“What! Did I say something wrong?”
Sven glanced at me but I didn’t really feel the need to stop her. It’d be weirder for us not to complain. I told them all to in the first place. The important thing here was something else.
“Haha, our squadron is part of the military, after all. Our journey can’t be considered complete until an official report is made to the higher-ups,” said Kaislan.
“Still. I also come from the military, but isn’t this too demanding?”
“Now, now, let’s all calm down. We’re the ones who accomplished the task of destroying the Eye of the Sky, right? Once the reports are completed, we’ll receive our long-awaited reward.”
“Hah, finally,” James Calla responded with a whistle.

Conversation between us flowed naturally. We spoke arrogantly about the reward, how impatient we were to get it, and what each person was going to ask for. Of course, this exchange was all for the benefit of our eavesdroppers. With their help, our words would be carried directly into the ears of all relevant high-ranking officials.
“Mister, at least they were able to find us something to eat fast. Try some of this.”

“Ah, thanks.” I bit into the meat on Erwen’s plate and reflected on everything that had happened since our return to the city. If we’d made any mistakes, we needed to prepare solutions as soon as possible.
The guys at the checkpoint didn’t seem to notice.

We stored our backpacks in our binding-type sub-spaces as soon as we got back to Dimension Square. We’d separated the equipment into gear we could show the royal officials and gear we couldn’t. From there, we arrived at the checkpoint. There, I loudly declared we were a special forces team under the royal family and asked to contact the marquess. This had been intentional.
Since the checkpoint was full of adventurers, talk of the special forces team would have spread through the city by now.

The checkpoint officer who contacted the marquess had seemed flustered at first, but he took the marquess’s instructions to “keep us there” to heart, as he then detained us for a while. Knights sent by the marquess arrived less than thirty minutes later.
“We will guide you from now on.”
They escorted us to the empty mansion in the royal capital where the inauguration ceremony had once been held.
“We will take your luggage.”
“Our luggage...?”
“Lord Tercerion’s orders. I can promise you on my honor as a knight that no items will go missing.”
The backpacks that held loot that was okay for the palace to see had thus been taken away. Once at the mansion, we were each treated by priests summoned by the knights. And that brought us to now.
Knock, knock.
There was a knock, and the door opened.
It’s about time. I guess he’s finally gotten a handle on the situation.
“Lord Tercerion has requested to meet with all of you.”
We needed to be on our toes now.

We followed the knights and arrived at a reception room similar to the one we were just in. The only unusual thing was that the seat at the head of the table was empty, and there was a crystal ball in its place.
A message stone, huh?

It was so ridiculous that I had to laugh. The marquess’s home wasn’t far from here but he was opting for long-distance communication. I guessed he knew that he’d committed an act terrible enough that he was liable to get his head bashed in the moment our eyes met.
“Please forgive me for greeting you this way. I have urgent business to attend to.”
“Well, I’m sure you do.”
As soon as I sat on the sofa, the marquess started in on me, his tone probing. “Hmm, seeing as you’re not using honorifics with me... I guess the squadron knows?”
Since I didn’t feel that was something to hide, I coolly admitted it. “I got caught. I’ve already told them I’m Bjorn Yandel. Ah, of course, I explained I was only disguised on the palace’s orders.”
“I’m glad to hear that.”

“Whatever. Don’t you have some explaining to do?” I ended the small talk there and got to the point, anger seeping into my tone. “Now, tell me: why didn’t the rescue team come?” In our remaining time, the squad and I had discussed what the most natural reaction we could have would be. “I’m sure they heard my voice—it was sent out to the entire region. What happened?”
“...The exact circumstances are still being investigated.”
“You still haven’t figured it out, and you’re contacting me through a crystal ball?”

“From what I’ve heard thus far, it seems there were more enemy troops in the Deadwood than we could have imagined. That’s why they had no choice but to give up on the rescue effort.” It was a rough, theoretical answer that sounded almost believable, but even I didn’t expect the follow-up. “It seems since you sent out your message to the entire region, Noark was also alerted to the existence of a rescue team.”
Wow, you’re really going to try to argue that I’m responsible for this? Just how shameless is this guy?
“Then why didn’t our initial transmissions reach them? If we got a hold of them the first time, none of that would’ve happened to begin with!”
“That... seems to have been a mistake on my son’s part.”
“...A mistake?” I echoed him, unsure if I’d heard him right.
“I apologize for this on his behalf. I’m sorry—”
My anger boiled over. “Behel—aaaaaah!” This outburst, of course, was not directed at the marquess or the palace, but the poor chess piece they were throwing under the bus. “Eltora Tercerion!”
“Wait, calm down—”
“So, this was all his fault. It was all because he was incompetent! He didn’t receive our call by mistake!”
“That’s—”

“Marquess!” I roared. “Where is that bastard? No, wait, don’t tell me. I feel like I’ll crack his skull by mistake the moment I find him.” I smashed the table in front of me like a man who couldn’t control his rage, then stood there huffing and puffing.
“...Have you calmed down now?”

There was an unease in the marquess’s eyes. Well, it wasn’t like me to get angry like this. I may have been slightly more aggressive than the average person, but I always acted rationally in pursuit of my best interests.

“Reward.” I cooled my head and spoke, though the anger was still there. I made it seem as if my show of open hostility was all for this. “You better have a proper reward prepared. I took on the role of commander like you wanted, and the mission was a success.”
“Ah... of course. The reward... of course you should be rewarded.”

As soon as we managed to extract a promise from the marquess, I turned to the crew and exchanged glances with them. Some of the members nodded back in approval. It was important to iron out the details when it came to things like this.
“Now, let’s postpone talking about your compensation for this mistake. Tell me what happened in the labyrinth.”
So, we’re at this part now.
I took a breath and recounted the story I had prepared. It took a bit longer because the marquess interrupted me throughout to ask questions, but I finished the story in less than an hour.
“You’ve had a hard time because of my foolish son.” This was his takeaway once the story was over.
A hard time, huh?
Blood rushed to my head when I heard our fight for survival summed up in that one sentence, but I managed to endure it.

“I will do my best to ensure you receive compensation for my son’s mistakes,” the marquess continued as if he really meant it. “And... I sincerely congratulate you on your return. We’ll speak again soon.”
Anyway, with that, our call with the marquess ended.
“I’ll lead you to your room.”
I wondered if our story worked. Well, only time would tell.

Afterward, the knights guided us each to our rooms. There was a large bed with soft blankets, and warm sunlight filtered through the windows. Considering I’d spent the past few weeks sleeping on ice, the room felt far too luxurious. However, though my body was exhausted from the past seventy-five days, it showed no signs of falling asleep any time soon. This was probably the case for all my comrades in the other rooms as well. They were likely worried about being attacked by knights the moment they closed their eyes too.
Despite that, the moment I lay down, my exhaustion crept up on me and I soon fell asleep.
My head is still attached to my body.
The next morning, I woke up unscathed.
Jeez, will I have to sleep with this kind of anxiety every night from now on? If so, this is going to be long and hard. Well, what can I do? I still have to do it.

That was how I greeted our second day back in the city. Once we were all up, we retrieved our backpacks, which were stolen from us the day before. When I asked why they had to take them in the first place, the marquess’s answer was truly impressive.

“My... I guess that’s how it must have seemed to you. All I did was instruct my knights to appraise the loot on behalf of your tired selves and purchase it above market price. I will let them know not to misrepresent my instructions from now on.”

It was ridiculous, but the marquess actually kept his word. He purchased the loot we were willing to sell at a much higher price, and we didn’t pass up this opportunity to get rid of any items we didn’t want. It seemed we’d have plenty of military funds in the future.
“Oh, and one more thing. The public is showing great interest in the expedition after you showed up at the checkpoint.”

That was good news. The radio transmission that the Eye of the Sky had been destroyed had been broadcast throughout the Dark Continent. A special forces team had appeared in the city. When these two pieces of information came together, it seemed word spread fast.
“There will be a ceremony in two days.”
“A ceremony?”
“It will be held at the royal palace. Your identities, which have been kept secret from both the kingdom’s nobility and its subjects, will be announced so all can praise your achievements.”
I expected this to happen, but two days seemed fast. Was it really possible for them to get things done this quickly? I had my doubts, but it soon clicked.
Ah, I guess he already had it prepared.

The ceremony must have been prepared a long time ago. After all, it wasn’t like he couldn’t have held one if there were no survivors. With the accomplishment of destroying the Eye of the Sky behind them, he and our other sponsors had probably planned to mourn the annihilated squadron and share the credit amongst themselves.
“So, get ready. I will send you the details of the event and ceremony so make sure to read what I’ve prepared. Ah, your clothing will all be provided by us, of course.”
“Okay. I will tell the team that.”

“As I said before, there is a significant amount of interest from the public. Though it may be inconvenient, I ask that you all stay hidden here for the next few days in order to ensure the ceremony’s success. If you need anything over the course of your stay, let your requests be known at any time.”
“Ah, there is something I want to request...”
I made a request of the marquess and after that, time passed quickly.
“Woahhh!”
“A parade of heroes!”
Just like that, it was the day of the ceremony.

chapters.title: Chapter 432: Return of the Dead (3)
paragraphs: The ceremony the marquess organized was simple. First, starting from the Dimension Square in Ravigion where we made our return, the parade passed through the commercial city of Kommelby and headed to the royal capital, Karnon.
Ba-bam, ba-bam, baba-ba-bam!
A uniformed military band gave a lively performance.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The carriage full of drums continued to beat loudly as it slowly advanced.
“Woohoo!”
The blessings and cheers of the people and the flowers they scattered filled the streets.
“A parade of heroes...!”
Wearing ceremonial armor similar to that of veteran warriors—the kind that could never be worn in real combat—we continued to move forward.
“Woahhh!”
The people of Rafdonia looked at us with bright, curious eyes.
“I heard they destroyed the Eye of the Sky. What an amazing contribution.”
“Thanks to them, the palace will have a huge advantage in the future.”
“It was our army’s biggest nuisance, after all.”
Some adventurers clapped as we passed them by. I also spotted a family with a young son sitting on his father’s shoulders who had simply come for the festival.
“Dad, what’s the Eye of the Sky?”
“Well, I’m not sure, but... it sounds like a very important item.”
“I want to be like those people one day!”
“Of course. You can do anything.”
Some had joined the crowd just to see a famous face.
“Akurava! Akurava is there!”
“I thought she retired. I never thought I’d hear about her again like this.”
“Melend Kaislan!”
“Ohh! That’s Blood Spirit!”
There was even a woman who ran up to the carriage in tears and held my hand. “Thanks to you all... my son can rest in peace! Thank you... thank you...!”
Did she lose a family member to Noark? But do these people even realize that the original ceremony the marquess planned was going to feature only empty coffins with our names written on them?
Beeeeeep!
I felt what might have been a panic attack coming on as I stared out at the large crowd of people. There was a ringing in my ears, and it was getting harder and harder to fake a smile.
Erwen, who was sitting next to me, grabbed my hand. “Mister...”
Even Kaislan, who was riding in the cart in front of me, turned around with worry in his eyes.
Jeez, you think I’m going to cause a scene?
“Woohoo! Yay!”

The triumphant procession down the main street passed through Ravigion and arrived at Kommelby. This place was different from Ravigion. The number of adventurers had gone up significantly and ordinary citizens wore much more formal attire than the average people of Ravigion. It was still nothing compared to the royal capital, though.
Drag, drag.
The wheels of the carriage continued to roll.
“Yeahhh!”

Huge crowds cheered, arms stretched up toward us. It was frustrating that I couldn’t just be happy at the sight. If there hadn’t been any trickery during this expedition, if our entire squadron had been able to come home, they would have gotten to see this with us. If that had happened, I would have shouted in joy too.
Boom!
It felt heavy.
Boom!
Very heavy.
Drag, drag.

The carriage plowed on without stopping. We eventually got out of Kommelby and entered the royal capital. Then we headed down the boulevard, straight to the royal palace. The palace gates, which were normally solemnly closed, were wide open today.
“The heroes have arrived!”
There were knights in formation at the gates. A military band was also positioned on top of the walls, joining in on the passionate performance as it reached its climax.
“Somehow, we ended up here again.”
Our endless carriage ride finally ended as we pulled up in front of the Palace of Glory, where I was once bestowed a title.
“Greet the heroes!”

Soon, the main doors of the palace swung open. We disembarked from the carriage and headed inside. Our formation was a little different from the parade. Earlier, I was in the center carriage, but this time I was at the very front.
“Woohoooooo!”
The cheers that erupted when we walked inside the palace were a little quieter than the ones on the street. Well, most of the people here were nobles or high-ranking guild execs, after all.
“What are you doing? Go in.” Kaislan poked me in the back as I stopped at the entrance and looked around blankly.
Tsk, don’t rush me.
Step, step.

I walked the red carpet that stretched all the way to the empty throne. As I did, I continuously scanned the room. The crowds shouted, whistled, and even took out binoculars to get a closer look at us. That was why it was easy to spot them in the crowd of thousands.
Tap.
In this blessed place full of happy people, only they sat in mourning, like uninvited guests among the laughing crowd.
So, there they are.

“W-Wait... where are you going?!” Ignoring Kaislan’s protests, I changed directions and headed toward the stands. I guessed he realized where I was going a moment later. “Damn it, I don’t even know if I should argue.” Kaislan no longer tried to stop me.
Step, step.
Our procession changed course. The military band following us was startled, but they changed directions as well like professionals.
Tap.

We eventually stood before them. Quietly wiping away their tears, they looked down at me with puzzled expressions on their faces. These were the bereaved families of the rest of the squadron, whom I requested the marquess allow into the Palace of Glory.
Ba-bam, ba-bam, baba-ba-bam!
Jeez, that’s so annoying. Can’t you turn that off now?

I wanted to complain, but it seemed the military band had neither the common sense nor the authority to stop. As a compromise, I just snatched the instruments out of their hands and threw them on the floor.
Kkkang!
The music abruptly stopped, leaving only a deafening silence. Only then did the crowd stop cheering. The sobs of the bereaved families in front of me now rang out loud and clear.
Tap.
I went down on one knee in front of them. “I’m sorry. For not bringing your precious loved ones home.”
When I lowered my head, the rest of the squadron followed suit. According to custom, we should have done this in front of the empty throne, but who cared? The king wasn’t even going to show up.
“Thank you...” Unable to make eye contact, I kept my head lowered and soon felt a gentle hand on the crown of it. “He... Ashed, how did he die?” So, this was Ashed’s wife.
“He... was like a wizard from a fairy tale. He was unafraid even in the face of death, and it was all because of him that we were able to come back alive.”

Ashed’s wife said nothing for a moment in response to my statement, which could have sounded to her like a superficial platitude. She just wept silently. “I... see...” Come to think of it, that guy was a liar. He said his wife was strong. “I... what do I... what do I do now? My poor... husband... how... Wahhh!” The woman who placed her hand on my head dropped to the ground, wailing in grief.
It was like a dam had burst. The loved ones rushed out of their seats to bombard us with questions.
“M-McKelly Rayothers. What happened to him? I-I wasn’t told anything. Only that he’s dead and I should come to the palace...”
“Ventis Gerod! He was my father! But I didn’t even know he was going on such a dangerous mission!”
“Mr. Calla! Please, tell me! Rick... why couldn’t Rick be here? Why did you come back alone?!”
We answered with bowed heads and made-up explanations. All the while, the crowd took in the sight with interest.
“What the—? Is this part of the event?”
“Wow, the palace knows how to pull out the stops.”
“I’ve never seen such an impressive ceremony!”
“It’s clearly a mess... Well, as long as it’s entertaining.”
I had no way of knowing how long said mess lasted.
“...We cannot delay the procession any longer.”

The knights came over to restore order on the marquess’s command and the ceremony resumed. We stepped back onto the red carpet after our short detour was over and headed to the empty throne. The marquess now stood in front of it.
So he finally shows himself after hiding inside that crystal ball for the past few days.

I took one look at him, then got down on my knee and bowed. Unlike earlier with the families, this wasn’t a sign of respect. I just knew it wouldn’t be easy for me to keep a handle on my emotions while making eye contact with him.
“You have walked an arduous path, heroes!” The marquess didn’t deviate from his script despite my unplanned interruption earlier.

He then summarized our quest in his own words. The thirty heroes completed their noble mission and, after numerous trials and tribulations, finally returned home. His speech was unnecessarily long due to the copious amounts of praise sprinkled in, but that was the gist of it. This was a story we made up, not the truth. After some negotiations with the marquess, we agreed to allow him to leave the part about the rescue team not coming to aid us out of his retelling entirely.
“Even the polar cold could not cool their burning passion. Even the underground traitors could not take their lives.” As the marquess spoke of our accomplishments and praised us, the crowd applauded.

Once the marques stepped back, the archbishop of the Tovera church appeared before us next. “Ahem, ahem... first, I’d like to speak on the nature of sacrifice.” The high-ranking priest suspected by many of having hair loss offered us words of comfort and made excessive mentions of the priests and paladin who were sacrificed.
Beeeeeep...
Next was the duke.
Beeeeeep...
Then the Adventurers’ Guild. Next... and next...
Beeeeeeep...
The people who had made plans to divvy up the rewards of this expedition walked in front of the crowd one by one and reaped what we had sown.
Squeeze...
Wow, I knew it wouldn’t be, but this really isn’t easy.
Luckily, thanks to my unexpected detour earlier, the ceremony was shortened and my need to be patient was short-lived. Finally, the ceremony reached its climax.
“Let the light of the king be with you all.”
In time with the marquess’s announcement, the music began again. In a school ceremony, this part would’ve essentially been the equivalent of saluting the nation’s flag.
This part takes three minutes, I think.
I counted exactly two minutes before speaking only loud enough for the marquess, about ten feet away, to hear. “Hey, marquess.”
When I spoke to him, the marquess looked at me like I had lost it. It probably wasn’t a great look for the star of this event to be distracted, and in a place where all the nobles were gathered too.
“I’ve been thinking, how is getting my name back going?”

I guessed he was worried I would ruin the event if he didn’t give me an answer. The marquess fixed his eyes on the empty throne and quickly responded. “As I said back then, it will take two more months.”
“Two months, huh?”
“That was our agreement.”
“It was,” I conceded with a chuckle. “But... now that I think about it, I think that’s too long. I want to push it forward a bit.”
The marquess didn’t answer. The performance had ended and it was time to resume the event. He shot me a scolding look and launched back into praising the palace.
Jeez, I get you’re busy but you should’ve answered. This gives me no choice. Barbarians don’t understand you unless you speak loud and clear.

The marquess, who was giving a long speech about how great and merciful the king was, finally shouted, “Let the light of the king be with you!” We had now reached the last part of the ceremony, according to the briefing the marquess sent me. “Now, squadron leader Riehen Schuitz, speak!”
This was a kind of ceremonial report. The moment we gave it, our long expedition would officially come to an end.
[You have cast Giantization. Your Physique increases in proportion to your Strength.]
That was why I used Transcendence to increase my size even more. I needed to be at least this big for people to see me, right? Thousands of eyes instantly flew to me as my body grew.
“How dare you use your abilities inside the palace?!”
“Do you know where you are?! This is an insult to the king!”
Some people were angry that I was using a skill. On the other hand, it was Bjorn Yandel’s signature skill.
“G-Giantization?”
“I-Is it a coincidence?”
“Wait, his face kind of looks similar...”
“But that man is dead.”
“More importantly, he was an evil spirit...”
Those in the crowd who had put two and two together raised questions. And the marquess? He fell backward as soon as I turned on Giantization.
What, you thought I was going to assassinate you here?
Slide.
I turned away from the marquess and calmly looked at the empty throne. “I will speak the truth in front of the one true monarch.”

My eyes were facing forward but I spoke loudly so that everyone in the hall could hear. I said each person’s name clearly, carrying the sentiments I couldn’t relay to the bereaved families in my heart.

“Pyke Neldine.” He was accused of being a traitor and had been executed in Ice Rock. At the time I thought that was for the best, but I regretted it now. If he really did wish for the expedition to fail, he could have been our ally.

“Philip Aintropi.” The navigator from Kaislan’s team had lost his life in the ambush in Deadwood while we were waiting to be rescued. His head was crushed.
