Though we didn’t exchange many words, I heard about him later from Kaislan. He was a dutiful son who never got married and took care of his elderly parents.

“Might Million.” He was struck by Land’s End Thorn and killed instantly while we were escaping Deadwood. He didn’t even scream. I’d probably be stuck wondering this for the rest of my life: was he unable to avoid that hit? Or did he let himself get hit on purpose even though he could have?
“Fiona Amos.” She had been killed by a lucky hit while casting Mass Teleport with the other wizards. “Niaro Campbell.” He had been a priest killed trying to help a wounded warrior on the front lines.

“Milburn Naria.” Our ever-polite Troll summoner. Though she saved everyone, she chose to die a lonely death to protect us one last time. I prayed she woke up in a house filled with the scent of coffee.

“Matt Hybridham.” He had been a paladin in a tank position, but I made him take off all his armor. While forcing our way forward, equipment-less, he lost his life just before we reached the top of Glacier Eye.

“Percival Eric Coulson.” He was Kaislan’s old friend and subordinate from the same unit. Even as he cried over his death, Kaislan comforted me and said that because I was there, he did not give up until the very end. That meant his death was meaningful.
That’s... the burden I’ll have to carry from now on.

I continued, “Rick Jugusta.” After regrouping, he was killed during our fight against Noark. His cause of death was the same Land’s End Thorn that killed Might Million. “Ventis Gerod.” When the Order of the Rose attacked us from behind, he stayed behind to buy other members of the squadron time to get to safety. He was a man who always talked about romance. Since he was a special ability user who had done the work of a warrior, I figured that guaranteed some luck in love.

“Roita Mamander.” Killed by the Order of the Rose while providing support from atop a cliff. He had been a very strict priest. “McKelly Rayothers.” The wizard on Akurava’s team. After being subjected to Soul Extraction, he never woke up. “Roan Veliaro.” He had been a humorous man whose motto was ‘here for a good time, not a long time.’ He was killed in the surprise attack the Order of the Rose carried out under the cover of darkness.
“Jun.” A noble paladin who had died standing. He was a great man until the very end, to the point where even his enemies didn’t realize he was dead until much later.

“Tsuon Irivan.” The archer from Team Two. When Sven Parav’s part of the line was broken, his body was torn apart by a monster summoned by the priest of Karui. But despite the state he was in, he had requested a priest before he died. If I remember right, he’d asked them to sing a hymn of hope, even though he couldn’t hear it because of Soul Extraction’s penalty.

“Futa Rickerburn.” The guy who worked as a fixer for the Duke of Kealunus. He was a jack-of-all-trades who served as both a scout and close-range damage dealer. His fighting skills had been so-so, but apparently, he managed to kill two Roses back-to-back in the end. I hadn’t been able to believe it when I heard about it later. If I could have filmed a video, it would’ve been played at his funeral. Duke, your fixer was a great son of a bitch.
“...What strength!” Before I knew it, I was surrounded by knights who grabbed my arms and tried to pull me down. But I guessed those weren’t great optics.
“Stop.” The marquess called off the knights.
Why are you doing something useful for once?

“Periton Ariabos, Benjamin Orman.” These two defeated the rampaging summons of the evil god with the ultimate finishers and self-sacrificial spells available to priests. If it weren’t for them, everyone would have died.

“Riard Ashed.” He’d used Awakening, just like Dwalkie. Not only did he deliver a critical blow to the evil god’s summons, but he’d killed three Roses too. Marrone told me this with tears the day before the labyrinth closed. She had been planning on casting the spell herself, but Ashed had stopped her.
“Guold Aldidi.” This man risked his life to run through the front lines to save me so I could get back to work. I was sure that old man had wanted to live too.
Yes, many people died.
As I recited their names one by one, I could feel the weight of each. But even so, I pressed on, calm and collected. I was making a final report, after all. “Twenty fatalities.”

Twenty of the people who took on this dangerous mission, twenty people with hopes and dreams, were dead. They died in that cold, icy place, miserable and alone, desperately longing for something better. Of course, not all of them were good people. There was one who embezzled public funds from his company, and even Jun admitted he tortured innocent people. Rickerburn probably did all kinds of dirty work during his tenure as a fixer for the duke. There were definitely some who would say their deaths were fitting. However, one thing was clear.
No one deserves to die like that.
We had survived thanks to them. This was why I could say this proudly, even if it was just another bid to survive.

“Lilith Marrone, Versyl Gowland, James Calla, Melend Kaislan, Sven Parav, Ravieniastorus, Emily Raines, Titana Akurava, Erwen Fornacci di Tersia...” Before I said the last name, I glanced up at the marquess. He was staring at me with a business-like smile affixed on his face. It seemed he decided there was no point in trying to stop me when I’d already used Giantization.
The marquess’s eyes bored into me as he spoke, his voice low and soft. “Tsk, if you just waited a little longer, things would have been better for both of us.”
Yeah, for you, maybe. But if I don’t reclaim my name soon, I’ll be a little too vulnerable. Let’s level the playing field a bit.
“Proud baronet of the kingdom,” I shouted grandly in front of thousands of nobles, “I, Bjorn, son of Yandel, have completed my mission and declare our return on behalf of the expedition!”
I’m back.

chapters.title: Chapter 433: Return of the Dead (4)
paragraphs: There was a tavern in District Seven that was always crowded with adventurers. It was the type of place where there were always empty bottles rolling around on the ground because they were sold for cheap, and drunkards got into fights with each other whenever they got the chance.
Kwaang!
The doors to the tavern flew open. No matter what world you were in, there were people who liked to talk—especially if it meant money.
“Extra! Extra!”
“What the—a newspaper boy?” At the boy’s arrival, the rugged owner rolled up his sleeves and walked out from behind the bar. “Hey, random solicitors are not welcome at our tavern.”
“I said it’s an extra! Breaking news!”
“What breaking news? It’s only news about the ceremony.”
A nearby patron laughed. “Haha, hey! You think the drunkards who’ve been drinking here since broad daylight will care about something like that?”
His neighbor scoffed. “But you’ve been grumbling about it since earlier! That the whole city is in an uproar over nothing.”
“Now, now, come back when you’re older, kid.” The owner lifted the boy over his shoulder and walked toward the door.
“You morons!” the kid shouted, much to the bargoers’ amusement.
“Hahaha!”
“Bjorn Yandel is alive!”
“Haha... ha...?”
For a moment, there was silence in the tavern. Of course, not for long.
“Don’t run around making up nonsense, little boy.”
“How can someone come back from the dead after two years?”
“Besides, he was an evil spirit anyway.”

“I’m saying he’s alive, and he’s not an evil spirit! While you guys were busy drinking yourselves to death in here, the city’s been in an uproar over this!” The boy’s sincere cries made the tavern owner pause.
“Wait, I want to hear more about that.” One of the adventurers expressed interest, and the owner let the boy down.
“Ugh, you reek of alcohol...” the boy grumbled, brushing off his wrinkled clothes and heading to the table where the adventurer was.
The man threw him a coin as pre-payment. “Tell me. Is it true Bjorn Yandel came back?”
“Of course. Iron Prime Minister Tercerion said so himself during a gathering of thousands of nobles!”
“The Iron Prime Minister?”
“So what happened is...”

The boy trailed off and glanced at all the nearby adventurers who were pretending not to listen. The adventurers sighed and tossed him additional coins, and he finally launched into his retelling. If you took away the seasoning thrown in by the well-spoken boy, the tale could be summed up in a few sentences.
“So... Bjorn Yandel played dead to carry out a mission for the royal family, and declaring him an evil spirit was necessary for its success?”
“But Riehen Schuitz? Isn’t that Blood Spirit’s man? He was the leader of this mission!”
“I was wondering why some random guy was put in charge of a group of big names like that.”
This was the return of a hero who had left a big mark on the hearts of the people even after all this time. Enraptured, the adventurers paid more to hear about what happened at the ceremony.
Kwaaang!
Then, suddenly, a loud rattling noise rang out from a corner table and the adventurers turned to look.
Step, step.
A large woman, whose eyes were clear despite the stench of alcohol clinging to her, was walking toward them.
“Um... w-what’s the matter all of a sudden...?” The nearby adventurers fell quiet at the intensity radiating from the large woman, and only the little boy asked what she wanted.
The woman then parted her lips. “Boy, I heard your stories from over there.”
“...I-Is that so?”
“Is it true? That Bjorn Yandel was alive this whole time? That he was Riehen Schuitz?” Her voice and the look in her eyes seemed almost desperate.
The boy was confused by this, but dutifully answered her. “...Y-Yes! That’s correct!”
“So... I see... That’s what happened...” The woman muttered, almost as if possessed, then handed the boy money before leaving the tavern.

The boy’s eyes widened when he saw the amount she gave him. “Ten thousand stones...?” It was the biggest sum he had ever received as a storyteller around taverns. This aroused the curiosity of the other patrons.
“Paying this much for a story?”
“To think someone that rich was in such a cheap bar.”
“Who is she?”
“Hey, why aren’t you saying anything?”
While everyone was curious about the identity of the woman who passed through their tavern, a man stared after her and breathed, “Holy...”
“Do you know who that woman was?”
“How many blonde lady barbarians can there be? And how many among them carry such huge swords on their backs?”
“So who is it?”
“The Wild Sword, Ainar Fenelin.” When the man revealed her identity, the eyes of everyone around him went wide.
“What, that woman was one of the Seven Powerful?”
“Wait, Wild Sword is... she’s one of Bjorn Yandel’s old teammates!”
“No way... is that why she was so curious?”
“That makes sense now!”
“What, so then even his former teammate didn’t know he was alive?”
The tavern was whipped into another frenzy as the customers eagerly shared their thoughts on this exciting new twist. The tavern owner, however, was on the verge of tears.
“That woman... she didn’t pay for her drinks...”
After that whirlwind of a ceremony, we all dispersed and returned to our respective homes. I was worried they might detain us there, but it seemed the marquess didn’t intend to go that far.
I guess things have worked out up to this point...
We returned to our mansion for the first time in a long time. I headed to my room on the second floor and thought back on the ceremony as I unpacked my stuff.
First, he was cooler about it than I expected.

Right after I came out in front of thousands of nobles, the marquess smoothly took the reins and sorted things out. He explained that my death was in fact faked, that it was all done to carry out a secret royal mission, and that even the announcement about my being an evil spirit was untrue. While this statement was originally meant to be made two months from now when he’d finished constructing a believable paper trail, it was instead given in front of everyone today. The marquess had had no choice.
If he denied my claim, the prestige of the palace would have gone down the toilet.

That was what I had been aiming for. After all, what else was this whole grand ceremony good for? It would be talked about for about a month and gradually forgotten afterward. I decided this was the best way to make a splash and get the most eyeballs possible on us. I didn’t know why, but the palace was sensitive to public opinion.
Okay, then they won’t be able to accuse me of any nonexistent crimes for at least a few months...

Either way, I’d started out on the right foot. The next step was expanding my influence as much as possible within the given timeframe so that even if they managed to uncover what really happened in the labyrinth, eliminating us would be seen as a bad political move.
There’s a lot of work to be done in the future.
With that in mind, I got changed and headed down to the first floor to see that the living room was now a complete mess. “Emily, what’s going on?”
“There was an intruder while we were away.”
“Huh?”
“The hair I placed on the doorknob the day we left for the labyrinth was gone. I searched everywhere except your room just in case, but I couldn’t find any wiretapping devices.”
“Wait, if there was an intruder, can’t you just check the recording on the crystal ball?” Erwen’s surveillance cameras were installed in our living room and entrance.

“Ah, I already destroyed them. The records are only stored for one day and it’s not difficult to manipulate them, anyway. Someone might have interfered with the magic circuits. I couldn’t leave them up.”
“...I see.”
“Whoever it was, though, they’re amateurs. They broke into an empty house and didn’t even touch the basement.”
“Basement? Ah, the navigator!” It was then that I remembered someone—the plundering sailor we acquired during our last trip into the labyrinth.
I heard Amelia left him plenty of food while we were training, but...
It had already been several days since the labyrinth closed. Had he been starving this whole time?
“Is he okay?”
“He was fine when I checked. A little skinny, though. But I like skinny better.”
No, I don’t think that’s the issue here...
“Besides, it was unintentional but he’s gotten a lot more obedient. Though he found out we lied about the fact that he had to take an antidote every day, he’s even more dependent on us now.”
“Will you go see him? He asked to be praised for holding his breath and staying quiet even when he heard noise from upstairs.”
“N-No... I’m fine.”
“Hmm, I think you should pay some attention to him, too, instead of leaving it all to me.”
“...Later.”

Anyway, since she said he was fine, I decided not to touch any thoughts about Auyen with a ten-foot pole. After that, Amelia went up to search my room. Once that was done, all three of us gathered in the living room.
“Um, is the house safe now?”
“For today.”
That was enough for Erwen. She slumped on the sofa, the tension draining out of her. “Coming home makes it all feel like a dream.”
“Yandel, can’t we open them now that it’s safe?”
“Ah, the sub-spaces?”
“Yes.” Amelia looked like a child on Christmas. Well, I must have looked the same. I wondered what items were stored in a sub-space owned by the Order of the Rose.
“Okay, let’s open it on three.” I quietly began to count, but just as I hit two—
Knock, knock.
There was a visitor. We postponed the sub-space haul for later and checked to see who it was. I was wary as soon as I heard the knock but fortunately, it was a friendly face.
“Raven.”
“Sorry, I know you must be busy. But I couldn’t sit still after hearing the news.”
“Come in.”

Raven came into the living room and peppered me with questions the second she sat down. “Was reclaiming your identity today planned? Have you thought about what you’re going to do from here?” And, “I’m glad you’re all right, really...”
Soon, the topic of the expedition also came to the fore.
“Mr. Yandel... are you okay?”
“Okay how?”
“A lot of people died. I was at the Palace of Glory for the ceremony too. I saw you apologizing in front of the bereaved families and heard you call each person by name.”
“...Really?”
“I’m just worried. Mr. Yandel... are you really okay?”
Okay? What should I say to that?
I paused for a moment before plastering on a wide smile and patting Raven’s slim shoulder. “Why wouldn’t I be okay? I’m alive, aren’t I?”
“...What happened in there?”
Only ten people survived the expedition. The things that happened there couldn’t be summed up in a few short words. “Nothing. It’s exactly as the marquess said.”

It would be best not to tell Raven. She already felt so guilty about helping me as a member of the military. She wasn’t even part of this squadron. I couldn’t burden her with our plan to oppose the palace. That was our cross to bear.
“You feel somehow more distant today, Mr. Yandel. Well, you have for a long time.”
“I’m sure you’re just imagining things.”
“Yes. I guess so.”
Awkwardness settled between us. Raven sipped her tea before getting up. Or, rather, she was about to.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
A noise that was too loud to be called a knock came from the door.
Who is it? The thieves from earlier?

As I stood up with that question in mind, I heard a familiar voice. “Bjorrrn! Bjorn! Come out this instant! Are you really alive?” It was a long-awaited visit from an old teammate. A truly magical feeling came over me. “Bjorrrrrrn!” Despite my solemn mood just a second ago, my lips immediately curled into a smile as soon as I heard that voice—and that name.
Smirk.
Yeah, I have my name back now. We’ve been separated long enough, in my opinion. Now it’s just Missha and Mr. Bear left.
It was time for us to come together again.
Rattle, rattle.
At a dining table filled only with the sound of dull cutlery, Baekho, who was nibbling on the end of his spoon, carefully spoke. “Hey, Kitty.”
“...I told you not to call me that.”
“Well, you don’t like being called by your last name, and you don’t like being called by your first name, either.”
“Don’t you get it? Just don’t call me.”

“Yikes, so cold...” Baekho pouted and looked to the side, though his eyes soon returned to her. It was an ordinary meal like any other, but while everyone else was awkwardly scooping up their food, one person wasn’t. “Kitty. Aren’t you going out? It’s not like you’re a real cat. Why do you never leave the house except to go into the labyrinth? Look, your skin is so pale—”
Slam!
The Red Cat Tribe woman slammed her spoon down on the table in irritation. “I’m done eating.” After putting away her dishes, she stormed up to her room on the second floor.
Rattle.
When the bang of a slamming door rang out in the distance, Baekho let out a long sigh and asked for the opinions of the others at the table. “She... doesn’t seem to know yet, right?”
The first to respond was Fallen Scholar. “You can’t hide it forever.”
“I know that... but I want everyone to watch your tongues until then. Okay?”
The scout nodded. “I will for now.”
“Okay, then dinner is over for today. Everyone, do your share.” Baekho grinned and stood up, leaving his dishes on the table.
Rattle.
The moment he returned to his room, his expression hardened as he lost the composure he’d managed to maintain in front of his comrades. It was only natural.
“Bjorn Yandel is alive, huh?”

To be honest, his feelings about Bjorn Yandel weren’t particularly negative. He was an evil spirit, too, after all. Watching him was like watching a promising junior come into his own. It reminded Baekho of himself in the good old days. That was why he took in Missha, who had been left like a cat out in the rain. Part of him was fascinated by her continued affection for Bjorn despite knowing he was an evil spirit. He sincerely regretted tearing the two apart.
But...
“Interesting.”

It was way too late now. Now, Baekho could no longer welcome his triumphant return. If he wasn’t careful, the ice swordswoman he’d worked so hard to cultivate for the past two years might end up going back to the wrong guy.
Ah, well, strictly speaking, she’s technically going back to her original owner... But then you should’ve come back a long time ago. You’re only a nuisance now.
Baekho genuinely thought it over. “Should I... just kill him?”
Eliminating anything that got in the way of his goals without letting emotions stop him was one of Baekho’s longest-standing ground rules.

chapters.title: Chapter 434: Return of the Dead (5)
paragraphs: Reuniting with Ainar went exactly like I expected it would. A tearful reunion didn’t suit barbarians, after all. Yeah, this was better.
“Bjorrrrrrn!”
“Yeah, Ainar. Long time no—”
“Behel—aaaaaah!” No sooner had I opened the gate than Ainar shoved me into the yard. “You lied to me!”

Immediately, a fistfight began. It seemed she was very angry at the fact that I’d faked my death for over two years and then pretended to be Riehen Schuitz when we met again in the library. Considering everything I put her through, I was honestly willing to take some punches, but I knew that probably wasn’t what Ainar wanted.
“Behel—aaah!” So I cried out to our ancestral gods and fought back.
Punch!
I punched her in the face.
“Rahhh!”

A dogfight ensued, the two of us rolling around on the lawn like wrestlers. I didn’t know how long the fight lasted, but when Ainar finally got worked up enough to pick up the greatsword she left on the ground, I shouted for Erwen to bring me my hammer.
“Both of you... stop!”
Erwen’s intervention put an end to our reunion fight. She was pissed that her well-maintained garden had become a mess, but I ignored her as best I could. Right now, Ainar came first.
Spit!
Ainar spat out the blood in her mouth and grinned. “You really are Bjorn...”
Was this what it meant to be a natural barbarian? I couldn’t believe she’d already gotten over it. Missha would’ve cursed me out for ages and jammed cold damage down my throat.
“Ainar, you haven’t changed at all.”

“Really? I think I’ve changed a lot.” Ainar shrugged and nudged my chest with her fist in a friendly jab. “Even if you explain what happened to you, I probably won’t understand. It was always like that. But, still...”
“Still?”
“I’m glad you’re alive, Bjorn.”
“Ah...” I was left momentarily speechless by the sincerity contained in that calm, simple statement.
But she must have found this touchy-feely vibe awkward, too. She looked down at me and changed the subject. “But... what’s up with your body? Why are you so skinny?”

I felt oddly ashamed by the question. Maybe my barbarian pride was hurt. The words flew from my mouth. “A-An essence!” I blurted. “It’s like the essence of the Bone Knight you took! Don’t worry! Now that I have my name back, I’ll erase it in no time!”

“Hmm, really? Do it as quickly as possible, then. Bjorn being shorter than me is too weird to bear.” Every word landed like a knife in the chest. “And... I guess I’ll have to hold myself back from dragging you to the holy land today. If our people see you like that... they’ll definitely be disappointed.” My heart shriveled. I would honestly feel less hurt if she told me I was a bad gamer.
Whew, I should really erase the Gachabone essence soon.
“So... is your reunion over now?” Raven interrupted the conversation and it was then that Ainar noticed her presence.
“Oh! Aruru! Long time no see too!”
“This is the first time we’ve seen each other in half a year, right?”
“Hahaha! You worry about weird little details! If you keep doing that, you won’t grow any taller.”
“I’m not getting any taller anyway!”
“Don’t lose hope. Look at me!”
“That’s because of your essences!” Raven shouted, annoyed, and Ainar chuckled and picked her ear. That only made Raven angrier. The scene was oddly touching.
It’s been a while...
I missed this. It wasn’t just me, either, because I could see Raven was grinning as she shouted at Ainar and stomped after her into the house.
“...I’m glad,” she said quietly as she passed me by.
“Huh?”
“You seem happier now.”
“...I don’t know what you mean. Let’s go in.”
“Okay.”
After being reunited in the garden, we moved into the house and continued our conversation. Ainar greeted Erwen as awkwardly as Raven did, and next came Amelia.
“Barbarian, long time no—”
Why are you pretending to be all buddy-buddy?
I quickly covered Amelia’s mouth and interrupted. “You already know each other, right?”

“We do...?” Ainar cocked her head. I was honestly dumbfounded. I could still remember how depressed she’d been that Amelia trampled on her warrior’s honor or whatever. Then again, she didn’t even recognize her on Farune Island, either. “A-Ahhh! I remember! You were the woman from Noark who got left behind with Bjorn!” It seemed Ainar at least still had memories of Farune Island because she nodded. “Your name was...”
“Emily Raines.”
“Ah, it was definitely something like that!”
What do you mean, “something like that?” You two never introduced yourselves back then.
At the time everyone just called Amelia a plunderer and a bitch—no one cared about her real name.
About her honor being trampled on the second floor... I should just pretend not to remember that, right?
As I was thinking this, Ainar addressed Amelia in a surprisingly friendly tone. “Did you say Emily Raines?”
“Yes?”
What followed was unexpected. “First, let me say thank you.”

“I don’t know much about you, but I’m sure Bjorn kept you by his side because you are reliable,” Ainar said, uncharacteristically serious. “Thanks. For being by Bjorn’s side during his biggest challenge yet.”
“...That’s not something worth thanking me for.”
“Haha! It is to me! I’m sad I wasn’t the one he relied on, but I’m sure it’s because of who I am! I’m not as smart as Aruru or blindly determined enough to turn my back on my tribe like that elf.”
Erwen thought that over for a moment and then frowned. “...Um, did you just insult me?”
Ainar wriggled out of trouble like a snake. “Haha, is that how it sounded?”
Wow, she’s not even denying it.
I didn’t know what happened but Ainar’s conversational skills had improved a lot.
“Anyway, enough about that. I came as soon as I heard your news at the tavern. What on earth happened to you?”
After that, I took the time to explain. Of course, it wasn’t 100 percent the truth—some things were filtered out. Ainar cycled through four particular reactions as she listened to my tale:
“Oh!”
“Ah!”
“Uh!”
“I see.”
Unlike with Erwen and Raven, I was done before long. One pro of barbarians was that conversations between them didn’t drag on.
“...That’s what’s happened so far.”
“Oh!”
At the same time, that was also the problem with talking to barbarians. I had no way of knowing if she understood anything I said unless I asked directly. “Did you understand?”
“Somewhat!”
“...That’s good enough for me.” The story ended there, and I moved on to the next topic as if on cue. “But Ainar, you must have been very surprised.”
“Huh?”
“The palace announced that I’m an evil spirit. I’m sure that must have come as a shock. Not just to you, but to our compatriots too.”
“Oh, that? It wasn’t really a big deal.”
“...It wasn’t?”
“Only to morons. How could you possibly be an evil spirit? No one in our tribe believed it. We just figured the palace made another mistake.”
Oh, I see...

That was a different answer than I expected, but I couldn’t just let it go without pushing a bit further. “By the way. I’m just asking this out of curiosity and no other reason but...” I kept my tone carefully light as I asked, “What would you do if I was an evil spirit?”

This was very critical information to have in deciding how I’d deal with Ainar going forward. Depending on her answer, I may take back everything I said earlier and tell her the truth. I wondered what she would say, and it seemed I wasn’t the only one. Erwen, Amelia, and Raven gulped silently along with me.
“Hahaha! Bjorn, you, an evil spirit? That’s funny!”
“Don’t just laugh it off as a joke—think about it. I want to know your answer.”
Ainar must have picked up on the strange vibe because she couldn’t seem to ignore my prompting. “Hmm, Bjorn an evil spirit... Well, there’s only one answer.”
“Which is...?” asked Erwen.
“Will you accept him regardless?” Raven prodded. “Since he’s your teammate whom you’ve shared time and affection with?”
Ainar tilted her head. “What are you both talking about? Of course I’d beat him to death!”
“Beat... to death...?”
“The chieftain said so himself! Evil spirits are meant to be beaten to death!”
Whew, yeah... She’s not going to be an easy sell.
Raven and Ainar’s visit went into the night. We drank tea and talked for a while, and then had a couple of drinks over dinner. This naturally evolved into a drinking party after dinner was over.
“It’s getting late... I should get going.” Raven picked up her coat and left late at night.
Ainar, who had been drinking like no tomorrow from the get-go, was already passed out. She left in the morning after a hangover meal.
“You said you had things to do starting today, right? Tell me when you’re all done. Come by the holy land too. I know what I said yesterday, but everyone will be happy if you come.”
“Sure...”
After sending Ainar off, Erwen also got ready to go out. Considering the things that happened in the labyrinth, apparently, she had to show her face at her holy land today as well.
“Then take good care of the house.” After Erwen headed out, I did too, leaving the house to Amelia. As I told Ainar yesterday, I had a lot of work to do starting today.

Just as Erwen warned me before she climbed the fence to go out, a large crowd was waiting in front of the house. I was sure my story had spread throughout the city by now. Some of the people were journalists, and others were curious passersby who had just come to get a look at me.
“Baronet Yandel...!”
“Ah... Baronet! Please say something!”
“Woahhh!”
“Please hold my hand!”
Wow, did Ainar get through this crowd? Well, I guess it isn’t that hard.
“Behel—aaah!” I cried the name of our ancestral god and pushed through the wall of people.
“Agh! H-He’s running away!”
“Follow him!”
Hey, running away? I’m just charging forward.
Sprint.
After breaking through the crowd with my overwhelming strength, I ran down the empty early-morning streets. Some people stubbornly followed me, but I was able to shake them all off soon enough.
Let’s go, then.
Putting on a large cloak in a dark alley, I followed the map to my destination.
So, the closest place is... Here.
It was a small house with a memorable red gate. Checking the name written on the door plate, I took a deep breath before carefully knocking.
Knock, knock.
After a while’s wait, a haggard-looking woman opened the door. “You are...!” She couldn’t hide her surprise when she spotted me. This was understandable.
“May I come in, Mrs. Ashed?”
She chewed her lip at my question, but still moved to make way. “Um... I have nothing prepared except tea...”
“It’s okay. I’m not here to be treated to a meal. I’m here to return something to you.”
“Return something?”
I pulled a box out of my sub-space instead of answering. The woman carefully unwrapped the cloth and burst into tears when she saw the remains in the box.
“A-Ah, ahh...”
“I’m sorry. This was the best we could do at the time. I wish I could’ve brought him to you intact.”

“These are the items Ashed had with him. I’ve stored them in sub-space, so take a look when you can. If there’s anything you think is missing, let me know anytime. Or if you need anything, I’ve written my address here so you can come visit anytime.”
Sob.
“If you’re uncomfortable with my presence, I’ll leave now.” There was no answer, but I accepted her silence as confirmation and slowly stood up.
“Wait... Please... wait a minute...” Mrs. Ashed stood, went into the kitchen, and came back with a fragrant cup of tea. “This... is the tea he always served to guests.”
“I see... I don’t know much about tea but it smells good. It’s calm, like him.”
“Tell me. How... he was...”
“I guess we’ll need more tea.”

I quenched my thirst with tea and told her about our quest. Most of the stories were anecdotal since I couldn’t tell her the full truth. Instead, I told her about the smaller incidents that occurred during the expedition, the passing conversations we had, the care and consideration behind his actions that duller people might have overlooked.
“That’s why everyone in the crew liked him. You would know. He may not stand out, but standing next to him feels comfortable and reassuring.”
“Yes... really.”
“He always listened to others but strangely never talked about himself. That’s why we were so surprised when he mentioned he had a wife.”
“Did he... talk about me...?”
“Yes.”
“What... did he say?”
“He said you’re a strong woman, but that you’ll definitely cry once he’s gone.”
Sob.
The woman who had been stubbornly holding back her tears since receiving his remains dropped her head. I said nothing, looking away as I waited for her to calm down.
A while later, she whispered, “Thank you... for... coming here.”
“No need to thank me. Thanks to you, I got to try some good tea.”
“...Are you going to visit the others?”
I nodded slightly. “There’s only so much we survivors can do.”

After I left Ashed’s house, I visited each squad member’s home one by one. The ashes of the people I was able to bring with me were returned. If there weren’t any, I gave the families a few of their belongings. If I didn’t even have those, I bowed my head and apologized. Their reactions were all different.
“Huh, aren’t you the great baronet? What brings you to this humble place?”

Some were sarcastic. Some just accepted the items and kicked me out. Some questioned the marquess’s version of events, and some were honored that a famous hero hadn’t forgotten them. But one thing was clear.
“Now, Meirin... say hello to your mom...”
“This... is my mom? Why?”
I was always the bad guy to them. Until the day I could confidently tell them the truth, I would probably have to live with this weight on my chest.
Time passed. One day, two days, three... A few days weren’t enough to send all our dead squad members home. Four, five, six days...
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
That day had come.

chapters.title: Chapter 435: Rival (1)
paragraphs: Hansu Lee’s room felt particularly foreign today.
It’s... kind of small.
This room had always felt cozy to me but now it felt stuffy for some reason.
And I’m not even a big barbarian right now. Whatever, let’s turn on the computer.
Momentarily distracted by the peculiarity, I quickly turned on the computer’s unit and entered the forum.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence – 0 people are online.]
I checked the Korean chat room first, but it was empty at the moment.
I guess Hyeonbyeol isn’t here yet.

There was no reason to enter an empty room so I used the mouse to click over to the bulletin board instead. Sure enough, the board was quickly filling up with everything from troll posts to advice. I clicked on the post that stood out to me most among the various topics.
[(Breaking news) Bjorn Yandel, who everyone thought was dead, is alive.]
Contents.

It was a post that clearly demonstrated the writer’s determination to be first, considering the only thing inside was the word “contents.” But as it was the first post on the subject, the comments were indeed flying in.
Harbinn: Wow! This is news that would shock the marquess and the palace!
└Sogeking33: Definitely. They’d be surprised that the writer had the audacity to call this two-week-old news “breaking.”
└these99: They only wrote “Contents” as the actual contents too.
└OP: But I was fast.

The comments were pretty much all the same. Since everyone had already heard the news of my return, I was sure it wasn’t earth-shattering enough for anyone to warrant a big reaction. However, some people acted like they were hearing it for the first time.
showmustgone: Eh? Is this true? How is Bjorn Yandel alive? I thought he died?
└Sogeking33: Are you locked up in a basement somewhere? Yandel announced his return at the Palace of Glory ages ago.
└IsABot: I was there when he announced his return and honestly I got goosebumps.

└arolf5205. He went to apologize to the families of his dead crew before even greeting the throne and honestly it was no joke. Until now, I thought I was a manly man but I realized that word is reserved for people like him.
└WingPizza: The looks on the nobles’ faces was really funny.
└showmustgone: Declaring his return at the Palace of Glory? What does that mean? He may be alive, but Bjorn Yandel is still an evil spirit.
└ReDCod: Apparently that’s not true. He was doing some secret mission for the king and only pretending to be dead.
These reactions were interesting, so I read through them all and clicked refresh one more time.
└vaman: But am I the only one who thinks this commenter is suspicious? They don’t know about a rumor that’s already spread throughout the city?
└vaman: Is this prick from Noark?

Oh, come to think of it, they really were suspicious. The upper echelons of Noark must have already been aware of my existence, but if they were controlling the flow of information, it made sense for some people not to know yet.
└WingPizza: I’m a bit suspicious too, so I sent the mods a quick message to let them know.
Others already seemed to be reporting them, and I left the thread once things reached that point.
Thump.
Then I froze, mouse in hand. It wasn’t necessarily shock, as I knew this moment would come.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence – 2 people are online.]
Two people were inside the chat even though I wasn’t. There were only three likely explanations for this. Someone entered by accident, the GM was meeting with Hyeonbyeol, or... Baekho was back.
Thump!
Hah...
If the GM had granted my request to drop Baekho’s ban within three months, there was a good chance that was Baekho in there.
“Okay, let’s go in.”
So what am I going to find, a house cat or a tiger? I guess I’ll only know for sure once I’m in there.
Click-click.
As soon as I double-clicked on the mouse, everything turned white and my surroundings changed to an elaborate mansion designed to the tastes of the original moderator, Baekho.
Crackle, crackle, crackle.
Two people were sitting on the sofa in front of the fireplace.

“Oh, Hansu!” One of them was Hyeonbyeol, as expected. “What took you so long?” Hyeonbyeol sounded relieved to see me, probably because I had been in such a hurry to leave last time because of the marquess. But before I greeted her in return, I glanced at the person next to her.
Slide.
Coincidentally, the person in question was looking at me too.
“Oh, right. You two should say hello. We’re all Koreans here.” Hyeonbyeol tried to facilitate the conversation, but unfortunately for her, we didn’t need her to do that.
“No need for introductions.”

“Yeah, no need, Sister. We know each other.” The man got up from the sofa and walked up to me with a grin. “It’s been a while. I missed you.” His attitude was completely different from when we ran into each other outside.
Although this one-eighty felt particularly odd, I greeted him without issue. “Yeah, it’s been a while, Baekho.” I wanted to see him, too, because I had a mountain of questions I wanted to ask.
Crackle, crackle, crackle.
The study’s fireplace crackled peacefully. The three of us sat on the sofa in front of it, engaged in friendly conversation. As far as outward appearances went, we were enjoying ourselves.
“What, so you’re saying you two knew each other in the real world and ran into each other again here?” asked Baekho.
“Yeah.”

“Wow, that’s awesome. If someone I knew showed up here, I’d treat them like royalty,” Baekho said. Then he nonchalantly tilted his head, his shrewd eyes darting back and forth between us. “So... how did you two know each other?”
Hyeonbyeol glanced at me before answering, “We were just friends.” Right, she never did like talking about her personal life. That really worked out for me.
“C’mon... I’m sure it was something more than that,” Baekho wheedled with a smirk.
That made the polite smile disappear from Hyeonbyeol’s face. “Excuse me, Mr. Lee.”
“What... yes?”
“Why are you speaking informally all of a sudden?”
“Uh... this isn’t informal... it’s, you know... half-casual. How you talk between close acquaintances.”
“Oh, I see... but are we close?” I hadn’t seen this in a while, her putting on this poker face.

Baekho seemed quite flustered by the question but only briefly played the part of a blithering fool. “You’re really sensitive about little things, huh?” His voice grew more aggressive as his outside personality slowly began to surface.
Of course, Hyeonbyeol did not care at all. “Shouldn’t I be the one to judge whether it’s a little thing or not?”
“Well, that’s true. But strictly speaking, I’m actually older than you.”
This argument would be unimaginable in a Confucian country like Korea. It was one only Baekho, who had lived in this world for over ten years, could make.
Hyeonbyeol sighed in annoyance. “First of all, you’re the one who said our real ages are more important and started calling me Sister.”
“But—”
“Second, I never asked you to call me that.”
“But—”
“Three, I never said I think of you as younger than me. Only a man I met for the first time today.”

“That’s why I’m still using formal speech, Mr. Lee.” Hyeonbyeol dropped her stony expression and smiled again. As a result, the cold, hard tension in the room suddenly softened. “So, I want you to respect people’s boundaries from now on. That shouldn’t be a very difficult request to fulfill, right?”
In the end, Baekho was overpowered by the force of her personality. “Uh... uhh...”
“You can do that, right?”
“Yes...” The opportunity to counterattack slipped past Baekho entirely, and he gave a meek nod, even as he laughed awkwardly.
Looks like he’s shocked by what just happened... Even he’s no match for Hyeonbyeol.
That was pretty useful information. Even now, when I felt I’d grown a lot as a person, I was once again reminded that I should never pick a fight with Hyeonbyeol.
“Ahaha... but Miss... Hyeonbyeol... and Mr. Hansu, do you two know each other?”
“Huh? What do you mean, do we know each other?”
Baekho seemed to want to change the subject because he quickly responded. “Ah, I mean, not in real life but in ‘real life’... Ah, fuck, how do I say this?”
“Are you asking if we’ve ever met in the city?”
“Yes! That. That’s it.”
I was about to answer honestly because I saw no reason to hide it when Hyeonbyeol jumped in. “Why do you want to know that?”
I immediately shut my mouth, and Baekho did the same.
“You ask a lot of questions, Mr. Lee. In fact, you’ve only been asking one-sided questions since you got here.”
“Ahahaha... Have I? I have?”
“Yes.”
Ugh, this is so uncomfortable it’s practically torture.
“Hyeonbyeol, stop picking on him.”
“But he keeps asking us for personal information.”
“...I’m sure he means well.”
“You don’t know that. We’re strangers who only met today.”
“S-Strangers? We’re still both Korean! Sister!” Baekho cried out, but his pleas didn’t sway Hyeonbyeol’s heart in the slightest.
“Are there no criminals in Korea? That’s not the Korea I remember. If you really want to know about me, you should go first. Who are you, what do you do, and where do you live right now?”
“What? Me? Why?”
“Well, wouldn’t I feel more comfortable sharing with you if I knew those things?”
“Uh... but still, that’s a bit...you know? A man should have a mysterious side... hahaha...”
“You’re an interesting person, Mr. Lee.” Hyeonbyeol’s eyes were not smiling at all as she said that, and an awkward silence ensued.
Yikes, this kid’s going to run away if this drags on any longer. We haven’t even gotten to the main issue yet.
“Hyeonbyeol.”
“What is it?”
“I’m sorry, but can you give us the room for a moment? I have something to talk about with Baekho.”
Baekho flinched at my request. Then he shot me a look that clearly asked, Have you lost it? That was because he didn’t know Hyeonbyeol very well.

“...Okay. You want me to come back later?” Hyeonbyeol hated it when lines were crossed without permission. That was why she never crossed someone else’s lines when they drew them in the sand. Well, actually, there was one particular day in my memory that proved even she had exceptions to her rule. “Don’t disappear on me again. I’m going to wait outside and come in as soon as the number of people inside goes down to one.”
“Okay. And thanks.”
Was it so weird for her to hear a thank you come out of my mouth? Hyeonbyeol shot me a strange look and left the chat. With that, Baekho and I were left alone in the mansion.
“Hansu... No, sir!” Baekho shot to his feet, apparently impressed. “So you’re the one in charge! Yes! I knew it!”
Yeah, okay...
I laughed because I had nothing to say to that, and Baekho changed the subject. “Ah! But what is it? You had something to say to me?”
“Oh, it’s nothing special. I just wanted to ask you a few things. It’s been a while since we last saw each other.”
“Really? Then why don’t we ask one question each? I have some questions for you too.”
A truth game where we take turns, huh? Why do all my conversations end up taking this format?
I didn’t know but I agreed anyway. “Then can I start?” I asked.
“Yes. Go ahead.”

Okay, I had the advantage here. I decided to start by asking easy questions. Or, well, these weren’t actually easy questions, but ones that would serve to hide my real motive. “Let me ask this one first. Is the Baekho Lee famous in the city... also you?”
“Ah... so you know now.” Baekho didn’t deny it, which made sense considering he’d been openly using his name in the first place. “But you must be pretty good. I’m actually not that famous.”
“Okay, it’s your turn.”
When I passed the baton to him, Baekho cautiously asked, “What was your real relationship to Hyeonbyeol?” This was an anticlimactic question.
“Why do you want to know?”
“Why wouldn’t I want to know? What else is there for me to ask about?” Baekho said flippantly, but I knew too much about him to let down my guard.
“She’s my ex-girlfriend.”
When I answered honestly, he jumped up from his seat again. “Of course! I knew it! I knew you guys had something from the start.”

After that, the Q&A session continued. I heard Noark left the castle walls, do you know anything about that? I heard a rumor that Auril Gavis is alive, do you know if that’s true? My questions were quite heavy, but Baekho only asked frivolous ones on his turns.
“How did you start dating someone like Hyeonbyeol? Did you ask her out first?”
Did this guy only suggest taking turns so he could ask stuff like this? The thought came to mind, but I didn’t let it show and gradually increased the difficulty of my questions.
“Why do you have so many questions about me? What about you?” I asked.
“Uh, me?”
“Yeah. Don’t you have a girlfriend? You’ve lived here for over ten years. Actually, forget a girlfriend—you could’ve gotten married if you wanted.”
“Hey. That’s crossing the line.”
“Uh... sorry... but I’m curious. You really don’t have one?”
“Well... it’s not like it’s easy.”
“Really? Because they’re NPCs?”
“I guess... you could see it that way.”

“Hey, you’re making this awkward by getting all gloomy on me. Man, you’re strangely cagey about certain things. Think about it. I was joking about the marriage part, but you could at least date, right?”
“Hmm... I’ll think about it.”
“Yeah, look for someone around you if possible. I heard you have a woman on your team.”
“Oh, Missha Karlstein?”
“Yeah, I think that was the name.”
“Hmm...” Baekho stared at me for a second. “But how do you know her?”

I figured he’d ask something like that. “That? I heard from the Watchers of the Round Table group you introduced me to. They said you used her to spread the rumor that Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit.”
“Yes, and...?”

“Now that I think about it, I’m curious,” I said, feigning some caution. “If that’s true... why did you do it?” This was one of the many questions I’d been wanting to ask and finally had the chance to. Why did Baekho do such a thing? “I never thought you’d do something to harm a fellow player.” I casually tacked that on as an explanation for why I was asking and calmly waited for an answer.
Before long, Baekho’s lips parted. “My friend... It’s my turn now.”
“You asked whether I had a girlfriend or not.”
Ah... Is that how this works?
“So right now, it’s my turn.”
“...Okay, go ahead.”

When I nodded, Baekho stared at me intently before letting out a frustrated sigh. “Ugh, I don’t like the idea of using this against you. This is meant to be done to enemies.” The atmosphere suddenly changed. Before I could even comment on it, Baekho continued. “Let’s stop feeling each other out now.”

“...Feeling each other out?” There was something wrong with his statement. I may have been feeling him out, but each other? That implied he had been feeling me out too. My heart thumped uneasily. Maybe because of the excessive blood flow to my head, it almost felt like time had slowed down.
Baekho was feeling me out.
For what? It was obvious.
Since when? I had my guesses.
What clues did I miss? It didn’t matter. What was important were my decisions going forward.
What would I do going forward? Exactly what I already had planned. The only thing that had changed was the order.
As soon as I finished using all available brainpower to take stock of the situation, I was forced back to reality.
“Ha, I can hear your gears turning, Hansu.” Baekho’s mouth was moving and he spoke in a voice that was much too calm for someone trying to start a fight. “Are you Bjorn Yandel?”
I answered after a short pause. “Yeah.”

chapters.title: Chapter 436: Rival (2)
paragraphs: Baekho Lee, age twenty-three, was a soldier fresh out of the military with a shaven head and the facial features of a young country boy. This guy had called me his friend.
“Me? It’s... been ten years.”
Since it’d been four years since he said that, he was a player who had survived in this city for at least fourteen years. At first, I thought he was a bit odd.
“You are already of this world.”
I was reminded of what Hans A said when I met him in the Box of Punishment. Suddenly, with them in mind, it finally hit me what the venom and tenacity I’d heard in Baekho’s voice before meant.
“We don’t say those things! I’m going back, so we should be counting by our real ages!”
Baekho wasn’t a weirdo. He was just more desperate than anyone else, which was why it was rather easy to see through him.
“Lift the ban, now. If you don’t, you’re going to die here.”
His tone of speech was frivolous.
“Hey, Dentures. Who said you could set a fire without permission?”
He believed he had omnipotent power and acted like a hooligan as a result.
“Wow, so you really were a player?”
But though it may seem like he acted solely in pursuit of his own selfish desires, ultimately, there was only one thing he wanted.
“I don’t do friends in this world.”

He wanted to escape this goddamn world and return to our original one. No one was easier to deal with than someone with clear motivations. I’d been wary of revealing my identity to Baekho this whole time, but...
There’s no need for that now.
This guy may not have known Bjorn Yandel was Hansu Lee, but he had already known Bjorn was an evil spirit.
“Holy shit...”
More importantly, now that time had passed, I had the confidence that I could protect myself from the worst-case scenario even against a monster like him.

“So... you really were Bjorn Yandel this whole time. And since Riehen Schuitz is Bjorn Yandel, you’re the one I met in Atlante back then.” After I revealed my identity, Baekho let out several exclamations of surprise before exhaling in apparent relief. “I’m really glad that I at least know now.”
That bothered me a bit. “Glad...? Why?”
“Ah... I think it’s best I don’t tell you.”
“I think that’s for me to hear and decide.”

When I was short with him, Baekho’s brows furrowed slightly. “But, buddy, why are you being so aggressive toward me?” Rather than angry, he sounded genuinely confused. But before I could say anything, he figured it out himself. “Ah... the way I acted...”
It seemed he remembered everything that had happened between him and Bjorn Yandel.

“I’m sorry, Hansu. I didn’t know it was you back then. You understand, right?” Before I could even decide whether to accept the apology or not, Baekho sighed again. “Jeez... you should’ve just told me back then. If you did, things wouldn’t have gotten so complicated.”
Hahaha... This kid really knows how to piss a guy off.
“Are you saying it’s my fault?”
“No, I didn’t say that. Ultimately, it’s my fault. As you said, it’s because of me that people know Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit.”

His calm tone of voice was honestly making me angrier, but I swallowed back my emotions and forced myself to focus on the conversation. “Now that we know each other’s identities, let me ask again: why did you do that?”
“I needed a figurehead for my plan. But, again, if I knew it was you, I would have never gone that route.”
I don’t know, I can’t really trust him when he says that. I know a bit about how this guy operates now.
“Even if I were really dead?” Would he really not have used me in that case?
My question was met with silence. Was he the type of person who didn’t like to lie? It was too early to know for sure. Maybe he just didn’t want to tell lies that were too obvious.
Baekho casually changed the subject. “But aren’t you curious about how I found out you were Bjorn Yandel? Honestly, I thought that would be the first thing you asked.”

The answer to that question was simple. I decided something else was more important right now. No matter the reason, the events of the past did not change. Even when you went back to the past and tried to change them.
“Ah, well, I don’t think I would’ve answered anyway,” Baekho admitted.
What the hell is this bastard saying?

“But to be clear, I wasn’t 100 percent sure. That’s why I wanted to use this opportunity to sound you out a little.” He didn’t need to explain his method for doing so. Even though he suspected me of being Bjorn Yandel, he had acted normal until I brought up Missha or Bjorn first.
That’s probably why he pretended to let Hyeonbyeol bully him. That way, I’d lower my guard more—
“Oh, but Hyeonbyeol is really scary. How did you date someone like that? Wow, I don’t know how long it’s been since I lost in a battle of wills. It was so ridiculous I had to laugh.
Hmm, then was that real? I couldn’t be sure, but I didn’t have time to think about stuff like that right now.
“Anyway, enough of that.” I cut that topic of conversation off there and decided to be blunt. “Why did you take Missha?”
“To clear the labyrinth, of course.”
So, that was the reason. I figured that was the case, but actually hearing him say it gave me an inexplicable sense of relief.
“Isn’t that why you were cultivating her too? Because it’s convenient to have an ice double sword master in the latter half of the ninth floor?”
Of course, I still had some questions. “I’m sure you had other candidates. Why did it have to be Missha?”
“I liked her unwavering conviction. I thought if I promised to resurrect you with the Stone of Revival, she would never betray me.”
“That’s it?”

“Well, there are other reasons... but they’re all trivial. To be honest, I did go back and forth about my decision. But I was fascinated by the fact that her feelings didn’t change despite knowing the truth about your identity.”
This didn’t seem like a lie. In fact, he really didn’t seem that interested in Missha herself. He seemed to think of her as more of a thing than a person.

“Oh, right! If you want her back, I’ll give her to you. I worked hard to cultivate her for a few years, and I feel weirdly like I’m betraying Hyeonbyeol for some reason, but...” The only person this guy was interested in right now was me. “It’s you and me, right?” Baekho grinned at me. “In that case, it’s worth it. Of course it is.”

His kindness was over-the-top. With this, it became obvious to me. The reason this guy was good to me wasn’t simply because I was Korean. There was something else. If not, there was no way someone whose goal was to return would give up on Missha so easily.
It would be best to pretend not to know.
Despite the temptation to dig, I didn’t even try to sound him out. Getting Missha back safely was my first priority.
“Then since the issue of Kitty is resolved, let’s talk about something else!”
“Something else?”

“I’m just curious about your story. I wasn’t as strong as you when I was at your stage. You even got the essence of a Sea Giant not too long ago. Based on my rough estimates, you have at least four rank-three essences.”

Baekho started asking me various questions. I kindly answered the things I could answer and left out the rest. Give and take. Since he’d been so agreeable about giving back Missha, I figured I could at least be this honest with him.
“But what really happened? Where were you for two and a half years?”
I gave this question a lot of thought. Was it a good idea to tell him I traveled twenty years into the past? It didn’t take long to make a decision.
He already knows I’m Bjorn Yandel, so there’s no reason to hide it. Maybe he’ll be able to give me helpful information.

Auril Gavis was the common enemy of all players, so it was important to share information and discuss ways to deal with him. And so, I told Baekho the story of how I got sucked into the past on Farune Island.
“The Fragment of Records Stone...? I’ve heard about it before, but I guess it really does exist.”
I told him about how I entered the community twenty years ago. This guy wouldn’t be interested in how I saved Amelia’s sister so I left that part out.
“...You met Auril Gavis?”
“Yeah, it turns out he was the founder of the community.”
“Oh, I knew that. I heard it from Old Man Ruingenes... huh? Wait... that old man mentioned Auril Gavis brought a weird man with him before the community blew up. Was that you?”
“Probably.”
“Wow... it’s like you’re the main character or something. Tell me more. And then? What happened after?”
“Auril Gavis was very interested in the fact that I was a player from the future.”

I recounted the conversation I had with Auril Gavis, leaving out the part where I beat the game in its original mode. Surprisingly, Baekho already knew most of this information. That was because one of his current teammates was the Fallen Scholar. Well, the reason I brought up the past in the first place was to get his intel.
“I know the Earth Witch is alive. I don’t know where she is, though.”
“The old man said she’s where everyone’s hopes go. Do you know anything about that?”
“Eh? He really said that? That’s easy. Could it be anywhere other than the end of the labyrinth?”
“But there was no final boss in the game.”

“That’s because it was only ever a tutorial. After living here this long, you must realize it too. This place is completely different from the game. Maybe the Earth Witch will appear as the final boss. Hmm, then how the heck do we prepare for that?”
Even disregarding the topic of the Earth Witch, this conversation with Baekho was useful. I was the one revealing information, but it felt like I was getting more too.
“Oh, that Kagureas guy you mentioned is the barbarian who collected the three Genesis Treasures, right?”
Uh, it was two when I left... Wait, before that.
“He’s a barbarian?”
“You didn’t know? You two are deeply connected. Little Balkan... that was your nickname, right?”
What?
“No way...”

“Yeah. Kagureas is Balkan. Or, he’s assumed to be, based on the circumstances. New World 134, April 2nd: shortly after Balkan died at the age of fifty-five, the missing Genesis Treasures all returned to their tribes.”
This was surprising news. To think my legendary predecessor and the original holder of my nickname was an evil spirit.
“Do you know about the portal in the palace basement too?”
“I’ve been looking into that for a while, but I haven’t learned much. Just that the portal there is not the entrance but the exit.”
“The exit?”
“You can’t go anywhere from that portal—it’s the opposite. You have to get into a portal somewhere else to travel to the portal in the palace basement.”
Hmm, I see... That’s definitely suspicious.
Anyway, we talked like that for a while, standing on the same side for the first time in a long time. Finally, as we reached the final round of our game of Truth, we touched on a new topic.
“Auril Gavis, do you feel the slightest bit of remorse for the deaths of the countless evil spirits who were brought here as a result of your greed?”
Baekho burst into laughter as soon as he heard this. “Ha! Pffft, ahahaha! Really? You really asked the old man that?”
“Why are you laughing?”
“Because... Let’s just say it’s a very ‘you’ question. Well, you are still innocent in your own way, after all...”
What? I’m innocent?
I was dumbfounded by that assertion, but Baekho genuinely seemed to believe it.
“So? What did that old man say?”
I told him exactly what Auril told me word for word, how he looked me straight in the eyes as he said it.
“How could I ever be at peace? Of course I feel sorry for you. I feel responsible as well. I will probably live with and atone for this for the rest of my life. Was that enough of an answer for you?”
I told him how the red light on the jewel lit up.
“Hmm...” I was sure Baekho would curse him out with me, calling him an old nutcase, but he had a weird look on his face. “That’s a bit ambiguous.”
“Ambiguous?”
“He purposefully gave a long-winded, over-the-top answer.”
“Huh?”
“That’s typically a strategy for hiding a lie inside a truth. Not to mention, you two could only answer yes or no in that situation...”
Baekho was suspicious of Auril Gavis’s motives. The problem was that the more I thought about it, the more I thought he might be right.
“Hmm, I wonder why that old man did something like that,” Baekho mused. “Is it just a coincidence that he talked that way, or was it on purpose? What do you think?”
“I don’t know... how could we hope to know what goes on in that old man’s head?”
“That’s... true.” Our discussion of Auril Gavis’s answer ended there. Baekho seemed to have more questions besides that. “Um...”
“What is it? It makes me anxious when you hesitate like that.”
“This might be a bit offensive.”
“Just ask.”
“You sure?”
“Yep.”
With my permission, Baekho asked, “What’s your goal?”
The question wasn’t entirely out of left field, but it still caught me a bit off guard. “Goal?”
“Do you want to go back to Earth?”
So, that’s what you’re wondering.
“You told me you didn’t know back when we met in Gnome Tree.”

Yeah, I did say that. And when I did, he asked if it was because of that Red Cat Tribe woman. When I answered with silence, he advised me not to expect too much from an NPC, because he felt like he was seeing his past self in me. But he probably dismissed it from his mind after that because he didn’t place much value on Bjorn Yandel.
“Still not sure?”
“I don’t know...”
“Give it some serious thought, then. You’re long past the stage where your goal is just to survive.”

It was obvious what Baekho was getting at, but I pretended to seriously mull it over. But, was it because I’d been thinking about this myself a lot lately? “My goal, huh?” I was only going to pretend, but I suddenly found all kinds of thoughts running through my mind. What was my goal?
“If it’s hard, try thinking about it like this. There’s a button. And if you press that button, you can immediately return to the world you came from. Now, what would you do?”

Baekho’s advice was more helpful than I thought. Though I didn’t know what decision my future self might make, I at least knew my gut instinct right now. If there really was a button like that, I would hesitate in front of it for a long time, my mind reeling.

If I went back home, what was there for me? There were a handful of things I could think of right away. Hamburgers, cola, games. Fun shows, and the convenience of countless modern devices. I wouldn’t have to kill anything, bleed every day, or feel so much pain or exhaustion. I may have to worry about living, but not surviving. The life of smooth sailing I longed for existed beyond that button.
But, though this game was surely damned, my feelings still hadn’t changed.
That... doesn’t change anything.
I wouldn’t be able to press the button. No, I’d choose not to press it. That was not the life I wanted right now.
“Looks like you’ve somewhat made your decision?”
“Yeah.”

I reached a conclusion. My goal was to survive in this place. Even if it was full of all kinds of threats, even if every day was like walking on thin ice... To survive, along with the numerous people I met here, was my sincerest desire.
“Can you tell me what you would do?”
I looked him right in the eye and answered, “I would press that button.”
I decided at that moment not to reveal my true intentions and instead give Baekho the answer he was looking for. It was obvious what he was waiting for me to say.
After hearing my answer, Baekho stared at me quietly. There was a moment of silence that felt strangely heavy.

“Tsk.” The sound of Baekho clicking his tongue sliced through the quiet. “Jeez, you’re getting on my nerves. Are you treating me like a moron because I can’t use my skills here?” The same guy who always laughed flippantly and joked around with people was now looking at me with eyes that were colder than I’d ever seen them. “You’re lying right to my face.”

chapters.title: Chapter 437: Rival (3)
paragraphs: Passives and actives were sealed when you were inside the community, which was why the lie detector skill that gave me such a hard time in the outside world didn’t work here. Plus, even if Baekho could use it, I could counter it with Auril Gavis’s gift. But none of that really mattered right now.
Is he putting out feelers?

There were two possibilities here. One, Baekho wasn’t sure if I was telling the truth about my intentions so he was pretending to be mad so he could double check one more time. Two, he was really confident I was lying.
Thump!
God damn it.

My heart pounded so fast it was practically vibrating. Maybe I’d underestimated him. This guy had lived in this harsh world for over a decade, right? Just because he didn’t have a lie detector didn’t make him a moron. No, rather, he would be more sensitive even without it. Thanks to his skill, he would be intimately familiar with the strategies liars used and accumulated a vast amount of data to subconsciously pull on.
The chances he’s only testing the waters are very low.
In that split second, I made my decision.
It’s better to cop to my mistake and apologize rather than assume an excuse will work.
Thankfully, it was Baekho who broke the silence. “Hansu.”
“...Yeah?”
“Sorry, I can’t give you Kitty back.”
“...What?”

Baekho’s lips curled into a cold sneer. “What, has living as a barbarian made you lose your hearing?” His tone was acidic in a way I’d never heard from Baekho while in Hansu’s form. He looked me straight in the eye and made a point to speak in an exaggerated tone. “I can’t give you back your precious Kitty.”
My mind went blank.
“Can’t you see? She’ll be more useful for helping me achieve my goals than yours. You want to stay in this world, right? Of course, don’t worry.”
Oddly, I didn’t find myself boiling over in anger.
“I’ll give her back once I’m done.”

Instead, I could only laugh. To be honest, I couldn’t tell you why. But even knowing he was obviously provoking me, and also knowing I should make an effort to ensure our relationship didn’t get any worse, the words burst out of me without filter. “Baekho, you... You’re really a broken bastard.”
I didn’t even regret it.
“Wow, now you’re showing your true colors. And you were always so careful.” Baekho laughed too. “You have no room to talk, do you?”
I smiled wider. As a result, everyone here was smiling.
Crackle, crackle, crackle.
Despite the warmth of the fireplace, a cold air settled between me and Baekho.
“Interesting.”
“Yeah, it is.”
We each muttered, and he opened his mouth to break our standoff first. “But there’s one thing I don’t understand. How am I the broken bastard?” He no longer bothered with polite speech or honorifics.
I scoffed. “Isn’t it obvious you’re the one who’s broken?”
“Think about it. Your real life is out there waiting, but you’re so infatuated with an NPC that you would want to do something as foolish as stay here.”
This wasn’t even worth answering. No matter what I said, he wouldn’t understand.

“Maybe I could accept that coming from some amateur, but you? Going back isn’t even a dream for you. You have power. You have pretty good comrades. You’ve done some impressive stuff, are famous, and what’s this? You even have a noble title—”
“What are you getting at?”

When I cut him off, Baekho got back to the point. “Don’t pretend you’re some normal guy. It’s disgusting. It’s obvious you’re the one who’s broken. Was it fun? Filling the void in your life with people? Getting powerful quickly with game knowledge, so you feel like you’re someone worthwhile now? But, let me guess, now that everyone’s treating you like a hero, you feel like you have to work even harder to live up to their expectations, right?”

Strictly speaking, he wasn’t wrong. If I were to look at the changes I’d undergone from a third-person point of view, I would definitely come to a conclusion like that too. But it didn’t matter whether he was right or not.
“Oh, I’m sure you’ll bow down to Auril Gavis and thank him in time.”
Jeez, this kid sure likes to talk. That’s not how a proper keyboard warrior fights, man.

“Hm. You seem like a very angry guy, Baekho.” I kept as much of a handle on my composure as possible and stared straight at Baekho. If this were a turn-based game, it’d be my turn to attack. And there was no need for a long-winded speech. “But I get it. You were the dumpee, not the dumper, right?”
“...Dumpee?” He didn’t seem to understand what I was saying.
I kindly elaborated. “Why are you playing dumb? The story of those girls running away from you when they found out you’re an evil spirit is well known.”
“That’s why, isn’t it? Why you’re so desperate to go back? Tsk, you childish prick.” I said that last part softly so that Baekho couldn’t hear, but it seemed he was listening in like a peeping Tom.
Baekho’s expression crumpled oddly, though it didn’t stay that way for long. “Haha, hahaha! Kh—puhahaha!”
Baekho burst into laughter as if I’d just told a genuinely hilarious joke. It was a common coping mechanism. You’re totally ridiculous, which is why I’m laughing like this—something like that.
I stood there staring at him, utterly silent, and Baekho’s laughter slowly tapered off. “My friend.”
“What.”
“Do you really like that Kitty that much? Enough to attack me like this all of a sudden?”
“I don’t care about all that.”

“Of course you do. That seems to be your biggest reason for not going back.” I once again stayed silent. “Wow, you can’t admit it even now. You’re surprisingly shy.” I judged that no matter what I said here, I’d only get sucked into his antics. “Oh, wait! I just came up with a good idea.”
The declaration sounded oddly ominous.
“About Kitty...” My instincts proved spot-on. “Why don’t I just kill her?”
Fuck.

“Honestly, you only want to stay in this world because you’re so satisfied with the status quo, right?” The more he talked, the more my heart tightened. “So it wouldn’t be a bad idea to just kill her. If this place becomes unbearable to you, you’ll naturally want to go back home. Like a baby rabbit seeking refuge when winter comes.”
This was the fundamental reason I hadn’t revealed my identity to Baekho.
“Hmm, I think that’s a really good idea.”
This guy would do anything to achieve his goal.

“Broken things can be repaired. Right?” He grinned at me. His smile was bright and didn’t match the tone of our conversation at all. I felt chills go down my spine, fear instinctively creeping up on me.
“Baekho.” But there was another, more powerful emotion than fear.
“What.”

It was murderous intent, the deep desire to kill someone. “If you keep saying that crap...” I didn’t even need to meditate and get myself in the mood like at the Round Table. I just had to release what I’d been suppressing, something that had already been building up for a while. “I’ll have to kill you.” My murderous intent was more intense than ever before.

Baekho flinched upon sensing my unrefined bloodlust. Of course, his hesitation was very brief. Before long, he began to speak again. What came out of his mouth showed just how different he was from the people I’d met in the past. It was not an apology or words of resentment or even a plea to stop.

Confronted with murderous intent that would have left Corpse Collector choking and squirming on the ground, he said, “Wow...” It was a sincere exclamation. “You’re unreal... other guys would piss their pants.” He threw out words of praise that weren’t really praise and slowly walked up to me, rolling his shoulders to relieve the tension there. “But Hansu.” One step. “Don’t you remember?” Two steps. “I taught you that.” Three steps. “Murderous intent.”
We came within arm’s reach, and I could suddenly feel with my whole body the murderous intent he held toward me.

Murderous intent was an unofficial technique used by pros to scare newbies. Although I had benefited from the use of murderous intent at the Round Table, I was never on the receiving end of it. To be more precise, I only found myself targeted by it exactly once, when Fox gave it a shot the day I became a member of the Round Table. It was a strange feeling—that had been my impression the first time I experienced it. It made my skin crawl and my heart kept pounding, but that was all.

“Now, then...” On the other hand, Baekho’s murderous intent was different, from its intensity to its ferocity. “Say that again.” I thought I could understand now why the Corpse Collector had been shaking so much that day.
Thumpthumpthumpthump!

My heart pounded so hard that I felt like it might explode at this rate. Cold sweat pooled and trickled down my face. In theory, this wasn’t a place where breathing was necessary, but my breath caught like someone had my neck in a vise-like grip. It was like every brain cell I had was on fire.
“What was it, again? You’ll have to kill me?”

It wasn’t to the point where I would collapse like Corpse Collector or Fox. Of course, it was tough and every part of me wanted to run away. I could end this all just by clicking out of the chatroom. But even so...
“Buddy, you don’t really think that’s possible, do you?”
I endured it anyway because I knew. I’d learned something while living as Bjorn Yandel. When you ran from your fears, an even more terrifying situation would be waiting for you on the other side.
I forced my muddled mind back to awareness and took a step forward.
Step.
Now slightly closer, I leaned down toward Baekho and whispered in his ear, “I don’t think it’s totally impossible.” This wasn’t just a bluff to win our battle of wills.
“Come on, didn’t you say you beat the game at Times Ten?”
I really was confident.
“In ten years, you’ll be like me.”
Though I may lack power compared to him now if I just had more time...
“Realistically, I have no more areas to improve, so...”
A measly Times Ten.
...I could beat Baekho.
But maybe my confidence came across. Baekho regained his composure, which had disappeared while I was speaking, and smirked. “Interesting.”
Yeah, right.

“You’re getting on my nerves.” I clicked my tongue and threw his own words back in his face. “Why are you lying all of a sudden?” Baekho tilted his head like he had no clue what I was talking about and I added, “You don’t find this interesting at all.”
If you did, why do you keep shuffling back?

“...Hey, hey! Stop, stop!” Baekho took three steps back with exaggerated hand gestures. “Ah! Hansu, honestly! I can’t even joke around with you!” Suddenly, his expression and personality did a total one-eighty. Baekho plowed on without giving me time to adjust. “There’s no way I’d really kill Kitty. I was just saying that. Just saying! Do you know how much I like you, Hansu? I’ve been so good to you since the moment we met!”
Yeah, right. No, well, I’m sure he does like me. Since he finds something about me useful.
“Is that why you threatened to kill Missha?”
“Relax, relax! Threatened? I told you. It was a joke!” Baekho’s tone was flippant, but facts were facts. That had been a threat. “Why would I kill Kitty? I have nothing to gain from doing that.”

Well, that logic was actually believable. He would be losing an ice-type double sword master and also making an enemy of me. Any way you looked at it, killing her was far from a rational thing to do. But...

“If your threat worked, you would’ve used that to control me in the future.” I was already lightheaded from almost losing our battle of wills earlier. If he’d managed to dominate me, the conversation we’d be having right now would be completely different.
“Honestly! Why would you think that, buddy?! I’m not that evil!”
He wouldn’t be laughing like he was now. He wouldn’t have called me “buddy” and started acting all friendly again.
“I’m glad you’re not evil. Then give Missha back.”
“I will. If you do me a favor.”
He would never have offered me a deal like this.
Then is this scenario this bastard’s Plan B?
As I stared at him with that thought in mind, Baekho sheepishly continued. “I won’t ask you to go back with me again. I know how serious you are now.”
“Your point.”
“We can still work together, right?” Baekho paused for a moment to give me a pleading look.
Of course, I didn’t intend to play along. “...Finish your sentence first.”
“You know the situation you’re in better than I do.”
Yes, better than his, at least. It was not good, full of troublesome things. No, actually, it was worse. Every day felt like skating on razor-thin ice. “So?”
“I’ll help you get through these tough times. Give you full support to turn things from bad to good. In return, help me beat the tenth floor later.”
Baekho’s offer wasn’t bad. Unlike me, he had nothing holding him back. To put it bluntly, if he assassinated the marquess, it would be of great help to me.
“Baekho.”
“Yes?”
“Shouldn’t you do something before asking me for help?” I kept this short. I still didn’t know why he wanted me so bad. “Bring me Missha first. Then we’ll talk. Your answer?”
Baekho went silent again. He seemed lost in thought. The moment he sent Missha my way, he’d lose his leverage.
Finally, he broke the silence. “Hansu, since we’re both worked up today, let’s end this conversation here.” He chose to hold off.
“What?”
“Can’t you see? My head’s too scrambled right now. So let’s talk again next time. In the meantime, I’ll carefully consider what to do with Kitty. Okay?”
“Okay—”
—my ass.
Before I could finish my sentence, however, he interrupted. “Ah, buddy, you said okay!”
“...What?”
“Then see you!”
“Hey, wait! Wait—” I hurriedly reached out, but there was nothing I could do physically in this spiritual world.
Tap.
As soon as my fingertips touched Baekho, his body disappeared in a halo of light.
Pop!

chapters.title: Chapter 438: Rival (4)
paragraphs: At first, I was in a total daze, but as I was standing there blankly following Baekho’s escape, it slowly dawned on me.
He was really gone. A piece of shit until the end.
Did he really say “pop” out loud?

Still, I felt much better now. Earlier I didn’t even realize how tired I was since I was so worked up. It really felt like I’d been drained of all energy. My head was pounding worse than the time I stayed up for three days on coffee during my college days.
Wait, is that why that bastard said his brain’s scrambled? Ugh, whatever. Who cares.
Slump.
I collapsed on the sofa. I desperately needed a break.
No. Rest comes later.
I spoke out loud to help process the events despite my muddled brain. “...I need to review all this before it’s too late.”
