From our initial reunion to the point when he ran away at the end, I looked back on my conversations with Baekho in detail. This was a habit of mine whenever something big happened, but this time, my head hurt to the point that it burned. I couldn’t clearly recall the look in Baekho’s eyes or his facial expressions during our conversation.
“Ugh, my head...”

The recall process was similar to stepping on the accelerator of a car that had run out of gas. Although I wanted to move forward, my engine was stalled. That was why I focused solely on running through the most important parts.
“Are you Bjorn Yandel?”
The bait he threw me.
“It’s you and me, right? In that case, it’s worth it. Of course it is.”
How he was willing to give up Missha as soon as he found out I was Bjorn Yandel.
“There’s a button. And if you press that button, you can immediately return to the world you came from.”
The clear expectations he had of me.
“You’re lying right to my face.”
His disappointment was as high as said expectations.
There was a lot...
My thoughts blurred as I slowly replayed our conversation. But I was maybe even a bit satisfied. Though I hadn’t gained anything, I hadn’t lost anything either, at least not today.
I planned to tell him I was Bjorn Yandel anyway.

Originally, I had been planning on testing the waters and then requesting he return Missha out of friendship. If that didn’t work, then I planned to threaten him. If I told him I was the one who got his ban lifted in the first place, that would imply that I could get him banned again. I didn’t get a chance to bring that up, though.
“Lift the ban, now. If you don’t, you’re going to die here.”
Since this guy had wreaked all sorts of havoc in the city just to get back here, I thought it was a pretty credible threat.
But why did Baekho go to such lengths to get the ban lifted?
The thought suddenly came to mind, but I didn’t let myself go too far down that rabbit hole. Who knew what went on inside that guy’s head? Maybe he just missed hanging out with other Koreans.
I closed my eyes and let the thoughts just come and go.
What was I expecting in the first place?
I didn’t really understand.
“Instead, help me beat the tenth floor later.”

Help him on the tenth floor? It was nice that he thought so highly of me, but was Bjorn Yandel really that strong? I supposed it wasn’t strange that he had such high expectations considering how fast I’d been climbing the ranks, but there was something that bothered me about that. At Gnome Tree, he discovered I was an evil spirit.
“By the way, we’re strangers the next time we meet. Got it?”
At the time, he’d been aloof about it. He drew a line between us without even attempting to build a friendship.
That’s definitely strange...

If it was simply that he came to the conclusion that Bjorn Yandel wasn’t worth much at the time, what had changed? My growth had been even more ridiculous back then. That was also when I first became famous, had been hailed as a hero, and even earned a noble title.
“I’ve been so good to you since the moment we met!”
Suddenly, something Baekho said flashed through my mind.
Since the moment we met...?
Yeah, now that I thought about it, he’d been good to me from the start. But why?
“It’s because I’m Hansu Lee, not Bjorn Yandel.”
No, that’s not right.
“I believe you. Anything else and you wouldn’t be Korean.”
Because I’m Korean? Hmm, that still doesn’t feel right.
That was probably part of it, of course. He had been waiting for a Korean in this empty channel for over three years, a Korean who might never come.
Would he waste so much time just because he’s lonely, though?
I didn’t think so. Hyeonbyeol was also Korean, but he was harsher with her than he was with me. So what was it? Why on earth had Baekho had no choice but to be nice to me from the beginning?
“Holy shit.” My eyes flew open and I jumped up from my seat. It was after I looked into the mirror on the wall that I realized. “My nickname.”
Yes, it was my nickname, the one I’d created by adding another letter to my original one, not knowing it had become famous in the community.
[Elfnunna]
There was no other explanation. It only took me this long to realize it because Baekho never mentioned it up to this point.
No, the fact that he never said a word about it is even weirder.
All the proof I needed was the newbie room I entered the first month using this nickname.
“Elfnuna?!”
“Holy—the guy who made the stat summary?”
“Uh... wasn’t that someone from the game company?”
“So you were Korean! I knew it!”
Everyone kicked up a big fuss when they saw me.
“You seem to be a fan of theirs too.” The GM, for his part, didn’t make a fuss, but he made a point to comment on and approve of it.
“Anyway, your nickname-making game is...” Even Hyeonbyeol, who knew nothing about my forum handle of Elfnuna, had frowned at my unusual nickname.
But Baekho, that playful guy who probably liked stuff like fart jokes and dinosaurs more than anything in the world, hadn’t commented on it once.
He said nothing about my nickname.
I wasn’t sure but maybe, maybe, he’d been lying in wait from the day we met until now, hiding his true motives behind a smile.
“Um...” The moment my train of thought reached that station, I heard a sound from somewhere near my shoulder. “What are you doing looking into that mirror?” It was Hyeonbyeol.
The issue with Baekho... I’ll finish thinking about it when my brain is back to normal. I didn’t end up getting much rest. Should I just bounce too?
“...You just had a bad thought.”
“No, I didn’t.” Yeah, never mind. I couldn’t cause trouble just because I was a little tired.
“Hmm, your expression definitely implied...”
“I said I didn’t. Anyway, you were so hard on Baekho earlier, but why are you half-casual with me?”

“What are you talking about? Are you really asking that between us, of all people?” Hyeonbyeol shot me a look that told me she found me pitiful and sat next to me on the sofa, one space away on the three-seater.
“Why are you sitting there out of all these seats?”
“Ah, there’s a line between you and me. I can’t go any further than this.”
...It seems she was offended by my request to change seats that one time. Jeez, then just say you don’t want to.

A silence ensued, with no one willing to break it. To be honest, my relationship with Hyeonbyeol almost always felt like this. Even when we were together, things were never noisy. That silence had once felt more comfortable than being alone. Of course, that had been when we were dating.
...This is seriously awkward.
In the end, I couldn’t stand it anymore and spoke first. “Hyeonbyeol.”
“Yes.”
“Why aren’t you saying anything?”
When I glanced at her, I could see her eyes were fixed on the fireplace, not me. Hyeonbyeol answered without even looking at me. “Because you look tired.”

“It’s written all over your face. You look like you used to when you got berated all day at work. Well, actually, you look even rougher than that right now,” she added, before glancing at me too. “What? You want me to keep blathering in your ear instead?”
“No.”
“Really? Then I’ll hold back.”
“Hold what back?”
“Well, to be honest, I have a lot of things I want to ask you, but I’m barely managing to keep them contained. Because I don’t want to burden you.”
Uh... Really? That’s, well...
“Thanks...?”
“...Whatever.” Hyeonbyeol coldly turned away despite my thanks.
...She’s embarrassed. Jeez, it’s not like I said anything. You’re making me embarrassed too.
“...Then I’m going to rest a bit.”
“Yes.”

To be honest, I felt like I was going to pass out so I decided to accept Hyeonbyeol’s kindness. Actually, to be more accurate, I felt like death. Overusing murderous intent was one thing, but this was also my first time being exposed to such terrible energy from someone else.

A peaceful silence ensued. For a moment, I felt like I was back on Earth. The only thing different was that instead of the sound of Hyeonbyeol reading a book, I could hear the crackle of the fireplace.
Crackle, crackle, crackle.
After a long while, I slowly opened my eyes to the sound of that crackling.
“Are you awake?”
“Ah, yeah...” I was kind of surprised. Apparently, you could fall asleep in the spiritual world. I genuinely felt a little less tired. “How long has it been?”
“About an hour and a half.”
Whew, then there’s still time left until the Round Table opens.
“You look better now.”
“Thanks to you.”
“Then I’ll start.”
“Huh?”
Start? Start what?
My unspoken question was immediately answered.
“Why the hell was he here?” She began her interrogation as if on cue.
“Who?”
“Baekho Lee. That was him, right?”
It wasn’t like I didn’t hear her the first time. I was just a little surprised. “Yeah.” So Hyeonbyeol knew about Baekho too.
When I confirmed it, Hyeonbyeol also nodded like I’d answered her question. “No wonder he had that weird look in his eyes.”
“But wait, Hyeonbyeol. You did all that even while knowing who he was?”
“Yeah? Is there a problem? No matter how strong he may be in the outside world, none of that matters here, right?”

“Uh, theoretically, yes...” I was definitely feeling her newbie status now. I should have warned her before she ran off and made a mistake. “But not necessarily. There’s a skill that can only be used here...” I explained murderous intent to Hyeonbyeol.

“So, your souls are linked together. That’s why intangible energy can be amplified and transmitted to your opponent. I get up to that part, but...” Always a quick learner, Hyeonbyeol seemed to understand the concept but didn’t have a grasp on how it actually worked in real life. “Honestly, I don’t know. Getting scared enough to feel like you’re dying? Can that really cause problems in real life?”
It was a valid question. Fox, a member of the Round Table, had murderous intent that only applied slight pressure on the opponent but caused no permanent damage.
“I can’t really explain it in words.”
“Aren’t you just lacking the words?”
Do you know how many novels I’ve read? Well, there’s no way it’s as many as her, though.
“Ah, it’ll be easier to explain if you experience it for yourself.”

This was a suggestion I would have never made if she wasn’t Hyeonbyeol. I’d only recovered a drop of my bottomed-out mental reserves. If I could, my instinct was to put this off until later and just rest for now.
But... It’s Hyeonbyeol.
I could do this for her.
“Then here I go.”
“W-Wait! Let me think about it—”
Think about what? This is faster and more accurate.
I immediately released murderous intent, hoping it’d help Hyeonbyeol avoid making a mistake outside.
“...Ugh!” The change was immediate. “S-Stop...” Hyeonbyeol’s face screwed up with pain like everyone except Baekho’s did.
That guy was fine. But yeah, no, my murderous intent isn’t broken—
“I... said... stop...!”
Ah... I was only going to give her a taste... I’m screwed.
Was it so jarring to experience murderous intent for the first time? I didn’t even release that much, but Hyeonbyeol complained of extreme fatigue even after a little taste of it.
“Still... I get what you mean... I get why it could leave side effects even back in reality.”
“Oh, then I’m glad—”
“But next time, I’m going to get very angry if you do something like that without getting my permission first.”
“Understood.”
“...Are you mad at me for something?”
“Huh? No? Why?”
Sigh...
Why was she being so weird now? Hyeonbyeol muttered to herself for a bit, then only asked a few quick questions before leaving because her head was hurting too much.
The first was this: “You know about Bjorn Yandel, right?”
I felt the hair on the back of my neck stand up the moment the name left her lips. What was this? Was she sounding me out like Baekho did? Thankfully, that didn’t seem to be the case.
“...I do know him, yeah.”
“Really? Then do you know this too? Whether or not he’s really an evil spirit?”
“Uh... I don’t know. I’ve never met him in person...”
“Hmm, really?”
Hyeonbyeol sounded disappointed. “Why do you want to know about Bjorn Yandel?” I carefully asked.
“Ah, for work. I have to know for sure whether he’s an evil spirit or not before I make any plans going forward.”
Plans going forward? This was unsettling. Based on what she told me, Hyeonbyeol seemed to be an office worker instead of an adventurer.
“My next goal after ensuring my financial freedom was to gain power.”
At the time, I thought using power to find a way to go back home was a strategy that was very ‘her.’
“And recently, I’ve made a connection with a powerful person.”
I wondered who the powerful person she mentioned was. If that person happened to be the marquess...
“Hyeonbyeol.”
“Yes?”
“Who are you working for right now?”
Hyeonbyeol frowned at my question, which contained zero playfulness. “I thought we agreed to not cross that line.”
“Things are different now.”
“...Sorry?”
“Because I might kill you by mistake if I don’t know. So tell me. Who is it?”
When I asked her again in a low voice, Hyeonbyeol stared at me intently. Then, she finally sighed and relented. “Countess Peprok.”
That was a name I didn’t expect to hear at all. Though I should have been glad she didn’t say Marquess Tercerion or the duke, I didn’t expect that woman to come up here. “...Countess Peprok?”
“Yes. We were connected by chance and now I’m working under her.”

Full name: Ragna Litaniel Peprok, the librarian I had once visited almost every day who was also a wizard. She was a member of the friendly gathering I attended regularly during my newbie days, back when information from rank-seven Shavin Emoor was still extremely valuable to me.
“Are you satisfied now?”
“Yeah.”

There was a lot I wanted to ask, but I didn’t want to dig so I just nodded. I’d at least confirmed she was not affiliated with the marquess. For now, Hyeonbyeol and I weren’t on opposing sides. I was satisfied with that.
“But, Hansu.” Just then, Hyeonbyeol placed her hand on the middle section of the sofa and said, “It was you...”
“Who crossed the line first again.” Before I could even reply, Hyeonbyeol stood up. “See you next month, then. I’m too tired to talk anymore today.”
Hyeonbyeol left the chat after that, and I returned to my room as I no longer needed to be there. I collapsed on the bed to rest for a while, and before long, it was time.
Whew...
To be honest, I longed to log out now and go to sleep, but...
Flash!
Yeah, I can’t miss this, no matter how tired I am.

chapters.title: Chapter 439: Giant Step (1)
paragraphs: As soon as the chatroom opened, the man quickly entered, put on the deer mask, and walked out into the hallway, hurriedly moving toward the room with the Round Table. Unlike usual, it was empty.
“Thank goodness I’m the first one.”

The man looked around for a minute before heading to a particular seat, four spots to the left of where Lion always sat. Unlike the early days, there were always empty seats around the table, so everyone sat one space away from each other. Assuming that all seven people attended, he was guaranteed to go second.
It’s always annoying to go first.
The quality of the information given each round was determined by the information provided on the first turn.
More importantly, that seat would be right next to him.
Yeah, the second spot was the safest. Third and fourth weren’t bad either, but location-wise, they meant you’d have to sit directly facing him. The last turn before his was high-pressure too.
Well, Clown seems to like the attention that comes from sitting there, but that’s the type of guy he is.
Anyway, unbeknownst to him, the seat he was currently sitting in was the seat most preferred by the other members. Was that why?

“Oh! Mr. Deer? You’re here this time.” As soon as Goblin entered the Round Table room, he greeted the man before glancing around and sitting one seat away from him. “I’m going to sit next to you.” That would make him third once the gathering began. “Anyway, did you have urgent business last time?” Goblin asked once he was seated.
Deer made up an excuse. “I didn’t come last month for personal reasons.”
“Oh, really?” Goblin asked. It seemed to be a polite question, though, as Goblin didn’t seem to care much about his answer.
Deer took the opportunity to carefully ask a question of his own. “Did anything noteworthy happen?”
“Sorry?”

“Last month. I was wondering if something noteworthy happened while I was away.” Deer’s tone was far too submissive to be directed at someone like Goblin, but he was aware that this kind of behavior was arguably shady. It was an unspoken rule of the Round Table not to tell people who didn’t attend what transpired during previous meetings.
Goblin might tell me, though.
That was the reason he came so early in the first place: to sneak in a question to someone before the other members arrived. And the first to arrive was Goblin. Luck was on his side.
Step.
Just then, there was a sound at the doorway. Someone else was here.
It has to be Fox.
That nosy woman would likely prevent Goblin from answering his question. He heaved a sigh.
“I couldn’t help but overhear you,” Fox said as she emerged from the hall. “Don’t worry. Nothing happened. Or I guess you could say nothing could happen.”
“What do you mean?”
“Lion didn’t attend the last meeting.”
“Lion didn’t attend...?”
“Yes. So naturally, Clown and Queen left immediately. And without them, the meeting naturally came to an end.”
“If that answers your question, don’t ask again next time,” she warned, sounding rather irritated. “The moment someone breaks a rule, it stops being a rule.”
“...I’ll be careful.”
When Deer obediently promised to watch himself, Fox’s eyes shifted to the man in the seat next to him. “You too, Mr. Goblin.”
“Eh? Huh? Why me?”
“Don’t tell people things just because they ask. No, to be blunt, watch your mouth.”

“Haha! Ms. Fox, you... watch my mouth... yes, I should... hahaha!” While Goblin laughed awkwardly, Fox scanned the empty seats and sat in the fourth one. “M-Ms. Fox, I guess that means Mr. Crescent will go first today?”
“If he attends, that is. But yes, he doesn’t seem to like the last seat.”
“...Hmm, Mr. Lion should show up today, right?”
“I don’t know. I guess we’ll find out.”
“H-Haha. Right...”
As he watched Fox and Goblin interact once they were both sat down, Deer frowned.
Something feels off.

Fox seemed to be comfortable with Goblin, but Goblin, on the other hand, seemed to be uncomfortable around Fox. Deer didn’t dwell on this matter too deeply, though. There were more important things for him to worry about.
Lion was absent, huh?

In a way, that was a good thing. He’d been disappointed that he had to miss the last meeting, but this meant he hadn’t missed anything important. It didn’t feel like a loss. However, there was one thing that bothered him.
“Lion is Bjorn Yandel.”

Queen had said this in front of the jewel during a previous gathering. Of course, the red light had cooled the heat a bit, but for a split second, this was a hot topic at the Round Table. There were many ways Lion and Bjorn Yandel paralleled each other.
...Well, I’m sure it’s a coincidence. There are just as many differences between them too.
First, Bjorn Yandel had only been an adventurer for four years. The first time Lion entered this community was about twenty years ago. They couldn’t be the same person.
But... What is this? It feels like I’m missing something...
Deer discreetly glanced at Goblin, who was conversing with Fox. “When’s Mr. Crescent coming?” Goblin was asking. “I think Mr. Clown and Lady Queen will come right at the end today like usual.”
“I’m sure they’ll come when it’s time. But... Mr. Goblin, why is Queen the only one you call a lady?”
“Haha... is she?”

Come to think of it, it had been this guy. He was the first at the Round Table to raise the theory that Bjorn Yandel and Lion could be the same person. Goblin’s basis was that if Bjorn Yandel was dead, the timing of Lion’s disappearance was very coincidental, but at the time they’d mocked him for even suggesting it.
“The honorific just comes out naturally... um... and her nickname is Queen, so...”
Deer joined their conversation. “Hey, Goblin.”
“Yes?”
“Do you still think Bjorn Yandel is Lion?”
“Uh... all of a sudden?”
“Yes, I’m suddenly curious.”
“Hmm...” Goblin didn’t seem to understand why he was asking but still answered, “No. I don’t think that.” His tone was very confident.
That was enough to convince Deer. “I see... Well, there’s no way he could be the same person as someone who got brought here twenty-two years ago, after all....”
“Pardon? Ahh... yeah, that’s definitely true...”
Deer tilted his head at that vague response. “Hmm? Is there another reason?”
“Well... I don’t really think Bjorn Yandel is an evil spirit to begin with.”
“Ah, that’s why.”

Announcing that Bjorn Yandel was an evil spirit had been a strategic move on the palace’s part. The news that this was not actually the case had already spread throughout the kingdom. That explained why Goblin believed he wasn’t.
“No. I have a different reason to think that too.”
What? That’s not it either.

When Deer shot him an inquisitive look, Goblin glanced at Fox before opening his mouth. “I can’t say much, but... Bjorn Yandel is definitely not an evil spirit. He can’t be. That’s for sure.” Afterward, Goblin clammed up in a way that implied he wouldn’t answer any more questions. Deer didn’t pry.
Come to think of it, Sven Parav was part of that squadron.

Perhaps he’d gotten some sort of premonition while working with Bjorn Yandel. Evil spirits were good at recognizing each other. He could not ignore the opinions of someone who’d personally gone through hell with that man.
Then... I guess Bjorn Yandel really isn’t an evil spirit.
Deer didn’t ponder this issue any further. Not only had his inkling already disappeared, but the other members were arriving, starting with Crescent, who came fourth and took the first seat.
“Everyone’s here.”
“Good to see everyone again today.” Queen arrived fifth and took the fifth seat.
“Pshehe.” Then came Clown.

Once everyone except one person was sat down, all eyes shifted to the doorway on cue. It was ridiculous when you thought about it. Somehow, the only thing a gathering of all these people could do was leave the seat at the head of the table open and wait for a single man to arrive.
“Ahh, I really hope he comes today.”
As if in answer to Clown’s wish, there was a noise from down the hall.
Step.
It was the sound of a quiet footstep. The moment he heard it, Deer felt his shoulders tense. It was a very strange thing.
Step.

It was just the usual sound of someone walking. That man hadn’t even appeared in the doorway yet. Why did he feel so intimidated? Deer idly wondered whether that man was using some kind of ability or skill, but he knew better than anyone that that couldn’t be the case.
Step.
That’s right. Those footsteps were nothing special. Anyone here would sound the same when they walked. Even still, the reason everyone clammed up as soon as they heard them was because they knew.
Step.
Though the sound may have been ordinary, the person making it was anything but.
Step.
There were a few more footsteps, and the man finally arrived.
“Pshehe, you’re here—”
Clown stood up to greet him like the henchman he was, but the man headed to the empty seat without paying him any mind. Then he sat in his seat and propped his chin in his hand without a word.
I should be extra careful today.
Deer found himself gulping. He got the sense that Lion wasn’t particularly amused today. And he definitely wasn’t the only one getting that feeling.
It was the kind of silence that made you want to roll over and take a nap.
Ugh, I’m so tired...

Propping my chin up, I fought to suppress the yawns that kept rising up my throat. Maybe I should’ve just skipped today. This went beyond exhaustion—I felt like I’d fall asleep the moment I closed my eyes for more than two seconds.
Why are they being so quiet today?
I couldn’t be bothered to talk so I decided to stay silent until the others took charge of the meeting. For some reason, however, the silence dragged on for a long time.
Why are they acting like this? I thought they’d be bursting with questions about why I didn’t come last time.
In the end, I spoke first. “How long are you going to just sit there?”
Get on with it, I’m tired as hell.
At my prodding, Goblin quickly answered, “Y-Yes! W-We’ll get started! M-Mr. Crescent will start us off... today... I think...”
Hmm, I thought Fox would lead the meeting.
Goblin’s stuttering didn’t exactly inspire confidence, but thanks to him, all eyes shifted to Crescent, who was first.
“...I should have sat somewhere else.” Crescent seemed troubled about having to go first but soon announced the start of the meeting. “All right, I’ll get started, then.”

The information he shared was about the elves. To be more specific, it was about Erwen. He received a green light for informing us that Blood Spirit had expressed an intention to retire from her role as Pureblood. Traditionally, the Pureblood was part of a sort of special unit in the elven tribe, and Erwen was currently on leave from it. She’d announced she would be fully stepping down soon.
Tap, tap.
So today’s first bit of info was something I already knew.

“The expedition led by Bjorn Yandel was organized with total annihilation in mind.” Deer went second and received a red light for the information that the expedition team had been discarded by the palace. After all, Fox, Goblin, and I already knew that. Deer, startled, tried again. “The palace has offered Bjorn Yandel a higher-ranked title for his contributions to the expedition.”

That news got him a green light, but there was no feedback. Normally someone would ask something like, Then is he going to be a baron instead of a baronet? That means he can pass it on to his children! Come to think of it, Crescent’s turn had been the same.
They really are unusually quiet today.
Fox, Goblin, and I may have known about the expedition already, but the others should have been shocked. Their reactions were a bit strange, but whatever. I was too tired to care.
Tap, tap.
Anyway, the second turn was also a bust.
Maybe I should’ve let Fox and Goblin know about my title in advance. Then it would’ve been another red light.

While I was busy regretting my decision, the third turn began. Goblin trembled and got on with it. I thought he would talk about the expedition, but luckily, he didn’t. Maybe it was because Fox had warned him to watch his mouth. He could still disclose information that might be beneficial to us, though.
This is about the churches’ internal affairs, which I’m not particularly interested in...
Typical Goblin. He sometimes disclosed important things, but on average the general quality of his information was low. But because it was a green light, he passed muster.
Yet another bust...
Something felt off today. Normally the others would’ve raised objections even if Goblin got a green light. Why was everyone being so quiet?
Tap, tap.
I don’t want to be the one to step in so I’ll let it go. Besides, Goblin’s technically my ally now too. Looks like it’s Fox’s turn.
To be honest, I didn’t really expect much, since she was with me the whole time in the labyrinth.
“The large clans are planning a mass boycott. It seems they’re unhappy that the palace organized an expeditionary force for a special mission without informing them.”

This had been reported to me in the city already. Though she got kicked out of her clan while in a coma, Fox had served as a deputy commander for a long time and could thus access a variety of information through her wide network of contacts. That information network was now being shared with me too.
Man, even the fourth turn was useless. I hope the next one is different.
Tap, tap.
When I turned to look at Queen, who was next, our eyes met for a moment. But it seemed she found my attention a bit oppressive.
Slide.
Queen, startled, averted her eyes before speaking in an unusually subdued tone. “The GM... has lifted the ban on Baekho Lee.”
She’d clearly announced this on the GM’s orders—it was an attempt to appeal to me by pointing out that he’d granted my favor.
Jeez, give us actual information instead of something redundant like this.
Tap, tap.
Anyway, since this was a tidbit that would get a green light from everyone except me, the round moved on to the next person.
“...It’s already my turn. Pshehe.” Was it because everyone had revealed their information without any small talk in between? We’d reached the sixth person several times faster than our usual tempo.
Hah, yeah, this guy was always the wild card.
Even though I felt like I could pass out from fatigue at any moment, I listened with wide-open ears.

“I’m sure everyone already knows that the Dragon Slayer Regal Vagos is dead...” Clown started as if to test the waters, but what followed still ended up being disappointing. “The news that Bjorn Yandel received a special royal mission to hide among us is completely false.”
Not only was it unhelpful, but it was actively inconvenient to me.
Tsk, I’ll have to explain myself to Fox and Goblin later. Since they both believe that to be true.

Anyway, regardless of how I felt about it, Clown easily received a green light. With that, my turn finally arrived. All eyes turned to me one by one. This was always how it went when it came time for my turn. There had been an unspoken rule at the Round Table since I joined: if they brought me interesting intelligence, I would reward them with information as I saw fit. So what was the verdict this time? Did I find any of that interesting?
Tap.

My answer to that question was simple. I placed my hand on the jewel and spoke. Normally I’d have run this through my mental filters so it’d come out much more refined, but honestly? I was too annoyed to care. “Everything you all just said was trash.”
This wasn’t an act—this was my sincere opinion.
Do you know how many yawns I swallowed back to listen to this?
“I would’ve benefited more from just sleeping.”
As soon as I took my hand off the jewel, a light came on.
Shaaaaaa.
Huh, that was weird.
“But it seems you guys didn’t already realize that? Seeing as the light is green right now.”
Man, I was so bored. I wanted to go home and get to bed.

chapters.title: Chapter 440: Giant Step (2)
paragraphs: The green light that flashed for a moment had already faded, but a heavy silence followed. They were like students being scolded by a scary teacher. I’d usually be able to pity grown adults who were acting like that, but somehow it only served to annoy me today.
If I had known this would happen, I would’ve stayed home and slept.
Everyone was so out of it. Just how much did they neglect collecting information this month? I didn’t drag my tired ass here to listen to this.
Ugh, I’m so tired...
Maybe I was grumpy because of my fatigue. No, that had to be it. If I were my usual self, I wouldn’t be this irritated, and even if I were, I’d never make it this obvious.
Tap, tap.
I frowned. Should I just end this now before I waste any more time? But that’d be a massive letdown.
Tap.
I finished deliberating and slowly said, “Again.”
Yeah, let’s do one more round. You never know what’ll come up.
“I’ll give you another chance.”

When I looked around, the members who made eye contact with me flinched and exchanged glances with each other. It was pretty satisfying. With this kind of atmosphere, the others were more likely to play cards they’d been holding close to their chests.
Thankfully no one’s pointing out what I did.
I was able to smoothly skip my turn. Using It’s all trash, I got a free pass this round.
If I look at it that way, I’m less pissed off now.
While I was waiting for them to start, one of the people at the table stopped exchanging glances with the others and took the lead.

“Then let’s go in reverse order for this round, pshehe.” Despite the tension, Clown met my eye and laughed his signature laugh. Still, I was looking forward to it. I could sense some determination in his voice. He probably took the first turn because he was at least slightly confident. “But, before we start...” Clown looked around at the other members and said, “I hope no one tries to wheedle their way out this time.”
For a second, I thought that was directed at me, but I quickly realized that wasn’t the case. Clown was issuing a warning right now. I’m going to play my ace, so you guys better do the same.
Unfortunately, none of the other members responded to the warning. But did he take that silence as agreement? Soon, Clown put his hand on the jewel. “Noark is planning to invade the city.”
As soon as the green light came on, the eyes of every single person at the table widened behind their masks. I was too exhausted to outwardly react, but I was pretty much in the same state.
“I-Invade the city?”
He wasn’t talking about a war inside the labyrinth but an invasion of the city. This meant that the people who left the city walls were making plans to invade Rafdonia.
“Why?” Fox was unable to hide her bafflement. “I thought the outside world was fine. Does Noark really need to go this far?”
This was a reasonable question and something I’d already been wondering for a while as well. First, Noark came back into the labyrinth to build up an army when the outside world was supposedly fine.
And now they’re planning an invasion of the city? Is the outside in worse condition than we thought? Or do they have some sort of reason they have to bring down the royal family?
There were many questions, but Clown reserved the right to stay silent. “I don’t know... my turn’s already over. Pshehe.”
Yeah, that was definitely enough to get him through a round.
Clown glanced at me before sitting back in his chair to signal his turn had come to an end.
As a result, it was now Queen’s turn. She remained silent for a moment. It seemed she was contemplating something.
Sensing this, Clown didn’t pass up the opportunity to mock her. “Hey, what are you worrying about? You’re not planning on doing another half-assed turn, are you?”
“I was just thinking for a moment,” Queen replied curtly before placing her hand on the jewel. One way or another, Clown’s remarks had pushed her act.
Nice assist.
As I waited, mentally giving Clown a gold star sticker, Queen soon opened her mouth. “This is a piece of information I was only recently able to confirm the validity of.”
What’s with the long intro?
“The Master of the Round Table is Auril Gavis.”
What?

The Master of the Round Table was the person who first created this secret gathering and recruited promising players to join. To be honest, I’d speculated that perhaps the old man I met that one time was Auril Gavis. My suspicions first started when I was back in the past.
“To add the capabilities you mentioned, I’ll have to imbue it with more of my power.”

After all, about twenty-two years ago, I created a system similar to the Round Table with that old man. Of course, it had only been a suspicion up to that point. I figured there was a good chance it was just a coincidence since this idea wasn’t particularly unique and could be thought up by anyone. What was really odd was something else.
They act the same way.
Auril Gavis had created this spiritual world and gathered promising players to help them grow, exactly like the Master did at this Round Table.
“W-What are you talking about? Th-that man is... Auril Gavis?” Fox stuttered, in utter disbelief as she was someone who had followed the Master from the beginning, but Queen’s answer did not change.
“It’s true.”
“Th-then he’s the one who brought us to this world...?”
“As per our investigation, yes.”
Knowing that the GM was backing Queen, Fox didn’t even bother with denial.
Shaaaaaa.
As soon as the green light on the jewel turned off, Queen took her hand off and glanced at Clown, shooting him a look that seemed to say, “How about that?”
It was kind of funny. Her pride must have been quite hurt by his comment earlier considering she sought out Clown’s reaction before mine.
These guys have good synergy. I should pit them against each other whenever I get the chance from now on. Anyway, the Master of the Round Table is Auril Gavis, huh?
Although I’d somewhat expected this, it was still a bit shocking. I decided to properly think about the old man later, though. I was too tired to think straight right now.
Let’s just worry about committing this all to memory so that I don’t forget anything.
While I was busy setting my new goal, the rest of the table regrouped and all attention turned to the next person. “Fox, it’s your turn now.”
We were already at the third turn. Was it because the last two pieces of information were so shocking? My mind was blank, but my concentration was sharper than ever.
Yeah, this is more like the Round Table.
As expected, people needed to be spurred on when they got lax. That little nudge had gotten me some good information.
Ah, but I hope Fox doesn’t spill any information about the expedition team because of the pressure... no, I’m sure she has something else.
As I watched her, half-worried and half-expectant, Fox finally revealed her info. It was related to the clan boycott she mentioned earlier, and it seemed no one knew it because the gem lit up green.
“Ms. Fox, are you kidding me?”
“If you keep doing this, you won’t be allowed to participate in these gatherings from now on.”
Clown and Queen, who had been sniping at each other up to this point, joined forces to raise an objection. That led to Fox having to try one more time. It was truly a shame.
“The Guild Master of the Adventurers’ Guild, Illya Adnus, added a saboteur to the squadron in the hopes that the expedition would fail.”
If it weren’t for that, information related to the expedition would have never been mentioned at the table.
Tsk... I guess you reap what you sow. Well, this isn’t too big a deal.

I decided to be optimistic. There was no guarantee the Guild Master was our ally in the first place. Besides, if this information was made public to the rest of the group, the other members might find something new as they investigated.
Hmm... maybe that’s why she mentioned it.

I let go of any lingering regrets and focused on studying everyone’s eyes. Clown’s look seemed to be asking, Guild Master? and I couldn’t tell what Queen was thinking. Goblin, meanwhile, glanced at Fox with concern.
“Sir Adnus... a spy...?” Deer, who presumably belonged to the palace, had a slightly stronger reaction.
So, I guess none of you knew anything.
“Now, it’s a green light, but...” Crescent, who had been quiet throughout the second round, spoke up. He was clearly checking to see if anyone was willing to raise an objection.
“Pshehe, well. It’s still very much lacking, but...”
“She got a green light during her first attempt as well.”
Fox managed to just barely scrape by with two pieces of information and ended her turn. So I supposed Goblin was the main problem now.
“...I-It’s my turn.”
Please don’t say anything weird.
“Why are you so nervous? Pshehe. No one expects anything from you.”
“Hm, I don’t know,” said Queen. “Isn’t that just your opinion?”
“Pshehe, I guess you think differently then, Queen?”
“Even squirrels keep an acorn or two hidden for the winter.”
It was unclear whether that was a compliment or an insult. Goblin seemed dubious as well. “Uh... thank you...?” he replied in a strange tone. It seemed he’d decided to take it as a compliment.
“Pshe, I really can’t tell if this guy is clueless or unflappable. Whatever, just go.”
“Ah, right... A revelation... there’s been a revelation—”
“Another revelation? That goddess Reatlas sure has a lot to say.”
“Th-this one isn’t from our church but from the Tovera Church!”
“Hmm? Tovera Church?”
“Yes! The Tovera Church. I don’t know if you know, but that church is known for rarely having revelations or oracles—”
“No need for useless details—why don’t you cut to the chase and tell us what the god said?”

Goblin sighed at Clown’s urging and got straight to the point. “The Sage of Eternal Life has returned.” It was a very short piece of information. Although there was a green light, the reaction from the table wasn’t great.
“...That’s it?”
“Yes... that’s what the revelation said.”

Clown let out an incredulous laugh and Queen asked a follow-up question. “Were there any interpretations of the message by the cardinals or high priests? I think that would help us judge the value of this information.”

“No. I-I was only able to hear the contents of the message... in the first place, so...” Goblin sounded bewildered. It seemed he hadn’t expected things to play out this way. Well, this round was a bit unusual. Normally a revelation was a free pass regardless of its contents.
Should I help him out this once? If I leave this be, I don’t know what kind of information he’ll blurt out next.
“Pshe. It seems everyone thinks that’s a bit lacking, so why not try again with something else—”
As soon as I came to a decision, I interrupted Clown and joined the conversation. “The Sage of Eternal Life...”
“...Sorry?”
It was the kind of bullshittery that only I could get away with at this table. “So he’s back...” Lion Style Form Five: Judged as Entertaining. “Interesting.”
If I say it’s fine, what are you guys going to do about it?
Dungeon and Stone was a team game, after all.

chapters.title: Chapter 441: Giant Step (3)
paragraphs: Silence momentarily fell over the Round Table. Any doubts about the value of Goblin’s information were long gone, and everyone was lost in thought. This was a bonus effect of something being Judged as Entertaining.
“Who could... the Sage of Eternal Life be?”
I had no idea who they were, either. Auril Gavis immediately came to mind, but there was no way of knowing for sure. At least this way, these guys would diligently investigate this on my behalf.
“...Pshehe, I’ll have to look into it as soon as I get out.”
“If you find any clues, let me know. I will pay accordingly,” said Queen.
“Why not? But only if you promise to do the same.”
“I promise.”
Okay, do your best. I expect a lot from the two of you. Anyway, is the Goblin problem resolved now? Hmm, it seems so, based on the stars in Clown’s eyes.
“Pshehe, you really can’t know how things will turn out. To think Mr. Goblin would hit the jackpot!”
Goblin nodded awkwardly, uncomfortable with Clown’s praise. “Oh... right... th-that’s right. It’s... hahaha...” It looked like he was having a hard time believing it too.

“...Then it’s my turn.” When the commotion died down, Deer’s turn began. I was planning on maintaining a poker face no matter what came out of his mouth, but that was actually kind of a challenge this time. “Countess Ragna Peprok is Marquess Tercerion’s illegitimate daughter.”
Once from Hyeonbyeol earlier and once again now—this was my second time hearing that name today.
Shaaaaaa.
Before long, the jewel lit up green and no one raised any objections.
“No wonder the marquess kept pushing her forward in government. So that was why,” Crescent commented.
Queen also reacted. “This is getting interesting,” she muttered, mostly to herself.
“Um, is it that important that she’s his illegitimate child?” Goblin cautiously joined in.
Queen smiled. “Well, it can be used as a political weapon, after all. Against the prime minister, who is essentially this country’s second-in-command.”
“Ah, right... I see...”
It was clear Queen was also interested for another reason, but it wasn’t like I could ask her. So, I focused on something else.
To think Ragna was the marquess’s daughter. No wonder she always gave off a rich girl vibe.
In terms of emotional impact, this was more shocking than Clown’s or Queen’s news. Ragna was one thing, but this meant Hyeonbyeol was also involved in this mess.
Ha... This is going to be trouble.
I’d have to look into it further, but I desperately hoped at this moment that Ragna wasn’t too solidly on the marquess’s side.
In the worst-case scenario, I’ll have to somehow force Hyeonbyeol to get out of there.
Anyway, when Deer’s turn ended, the attention naturally shifted to Crescent.
Hmm, I wonder what he’s going to say. Probably something about the elves.
“The Genesis Treasures.”
Huh?
“The dwarves are looking for a way to produce new Genesis Treasures and have achieved some success.”
Really?
“Pardon? Is that true? What do you mean produce?” Queen jumped up from her seat, bombarding him with questions. Her reaction made one thing clear:
I guess she and the GM are intent on going back.
Clown, on the other hand, didn’t seem to care. He seemed a little surprised but ultimately just accepted the information at face value.
Hmm, does this prick not want to go back? Maybe he likes his life as a toy collector.
“So what’s the methodology?”
“I already gave you a hint, so the rest is up to you.”
“Wait. Don’t you think your information is too vague for us to simply move on? It’s not like they’ve found a surefire way to do it—you only said there’s been some success.”

Crescent pretended to let Queen bully him into revealing additional details. “It takes numerous Rift Stones and even more blood. The dwarves believe if these two conditions are met, the Genesis Treasures can be created anew.”
Ha, are they mad scientists or something?
Regardless of whether the approach worked or not, the concept was impressive in itself.
Making Genesis Treasures, huh? Could that really be possible? These are items said to have existed since the creation of this world, after all. Well, let’s think about all that later.

I shook off any distracting thoughts. The other members may still have been preoccupied with Crescent’s information, but that wouldn’t last forever. Before long, eyes started to turn in my direction. Unlike earlier, there were almost no anxious looks. It seemed like my deeming Goblin’s information as interesting played a big role in shifting the mood at the table.
Now, what should I tell them?
I didn’t have to think for long. If you wanted to catch fish, it was only natural to go to the shore.
“The person who used the nickname Elfnuna in Stone Iven...”
So let’s throw in some bait.
“That person is already in this world.”
I was starting to get really curious now too. What was the big deal about that thoughtlessly chosen nickname that even Baekho and the GM were kicking up such a fuss about it?
Shaaaaaa.
As the green light on the jewel blinked on, the jaws of every person at this gathering beside me dropped as if on cue.
“Elfnuna... is that person, right? The person who’s said to have the highest chance of clearing the original version of the game,” said Queen.
“Pshehe, I guess half the rumors circulating around the community were true, then.”

I knew the rumors Clown was referring to. They said that Elfnuna was summoned to this world a long time ago and that they received huge perks here for clearing the original game. As the subject of said rumors, I had to laugh.
Perks... Are you joking? I was almost killed by a goblin trap as soon as I got here.
“Half?” said Queen.

“We don’t know for sure yet if they really cleared the original version. You never know. Maybe they realized it was impossible in the end and adjusted the mode,” Clown said with a shrug. He didn’t seem overly interested in Elfnuna, unlike Queen.
Soul Queen didn’t say a word. She just sat there, frozen like a statue. That showed me just how important this information was to her.
Okay, then this news will be conveyed to the GM too.

If I waited, the GM would inevitably try to contact me. He’d probably want to meet with me one-on-one to find out more about Elfnuna. From there, I’d only have to do one thing: take advantage of having the upper hand in our interaction and sneakily use it to dig for information.
“Anyway, thank you for more fascinating information. Pshehe.”
“Lion... have you met them—”

“Mr. Deer! Don’t you know it’s rude to ask a question like that?” Without me even having to intervene, Clown stepped forward and blocked any questions in my stead. “Pshehe, looks like another round would be pushing it.”

He snickered like he was mocking the other members for not having anything else to offer. But, and maybe this was just me, it seemed to me that he wanted this to end because he had no more information to share.
“Yes, I-I’ll stop here...”
“Me too.”
“Me as well.”
Goblin, Fox, and Crescent declared that they were opting out, and the meeting naturally came to an end. I walked out without looking back.
Whew...
Now free, I returned to Hansu Lee’s room. Maybe it was because the Round Table was over, but I was completely drained. It felt like a lot of things had happened in Ghost Busters this month.
It feels like I’ve been here a week.
I dragged myself over to the computer and sat down. Using the mouse, I moved my cursor to the logout button. Normally, I would’ve looked around the bulletin board for a while, but...
Let’s go back.
I just wanted to go home and sleep.
Click-click.
As soon as I clicked Logout, there was a flash of light, and space distorted around me.
[You are being transported to Rafdonia.]
When I opened my eyes again, I was in my room on the second floor of Erwen’s mansion. Once again, Amelia was beside me.
“You’re back early today.”
“Ah, it worked out that way this time.”
Jeez, I’m only gone a few seconds, but she guards me every time.
I felt reassured, grateful, and also kind of embarrassed at the same time.
“As long as you’re back. Get some rest. You look tired. I’ll tell the elf not to wake you up tomorrow.”
“Ah, thanks.”
Amelia coolly got up from her post and even turned off the lights before leaving. It was the optimal amount of quiet and darkness to fall asleep in.
...I was going to get some of my thoughts in order before going to bed, but...

When I laid my head on the pillow and closed my eyes, sleep came over me like a dam that had burst. With the whole murderous intent debacle and forcing myself to go to the Round Table after, I really felt like death.
I wonder if Baekho’s all right.
That was my last thought before I passed out.
It was a dark room where even the moonlight was blocked off by thick curtains.
“Whew, that’s much better.”
The first thing the blond man did when he opened his eyes was get up and check the door.
Okay, no signs of a break-in while I was there.
He never expected the ban to be lifted this month, and the man was quite startled about being dragged to that place all of a sudden. Normally, he prepared for everything well in advance.
“Ugh, my head...”
A wave of fatigue swept over the man after he was done checking the door, and he sat on the edge of his bed. He wanted to lie down and fall asleep right away.
“I feel like someone could kidnap me in my sleep tonight and I wouldn’t wake up...”
The man fought through his fatigue to open his sub-space. He took out a coffin-shaped metal box.
I haven’t used this in the outside world in a while.
No. 1577: Coffin of Eternal Rest was an item he often used in the labyrinth instead of a sleeping bag. It was tremendously durable in addition to speeding up the user’s stamina recovery.
Yeah, I’ll just sleep in here today.

The man squeezed himself into the coffin and shut it from the inside. It was probably funny that he was sleeping here instead of on the comfortable bed next to him, but he had no choice. Constantly being alert to potential dangers was this man’s longest-standing ground rule.

Though it was uncomfortable, he felt himself relax as his body registered that he was in a safe space. The man let his eyes fall shut and gathered his thoughts. There was one that kept running through his mind.
“I don’t think it’s totally impossible.”

The response his opponent gave when he asked if he truly thought he could kill him. As soon as the words left the guy’s mouth, the man instinctively sensed it. Just as he saw through his opponent’s lie about pressing the button, he immediately realized that that statement was the unmistakable truth.
He’s not an easy customer.
It still sent shivers down his spine. But on the other hand, the man felt himself laugh at the memory of his opponent unleashing his murderous intent.
“Ugh, I really need to sleep...”
He hadn’t expected all of that to happen, but it honestly just made him want even more.
Elfnunna... I hope this month flies by.
Baekho Lee fell asleep with that thought in mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 442: Giant Step (4)
paragraphs: When I opened my eyes again, it was the middle of the night. Deciding there was no point in waking up now, I went back to sleep. Which was why I thought I only slept for a total of two days.
“I slept for three days?”
I thought Amelia was joking at first. I was still exhausted despite sleeping three days straight. To be honest, I actually forced myself to get up today even though I could have slept more.
But it’s really been three days?
“Still, I’m glad you woke up now. I was going to force you awake if you didn’t wake up today. I’m sick of the elf making a fuss.”
“...So where’s Erwen?”
“Out.”
“Out?”
“She said she was going to her holy land. It seems things aren’t wrapping up there as easily as she thought they would.”

The context was missing from her sentence but I knew what she was talking about. This must have been about Erwen leaving the elves’ special forces unit and her role as Pureblood. Since Erwen had received considerable support from the elves while I was away, she’d have to make a lot of sacrifices to become a free woman again. A prime example would be the Sacred Bow. If not that, then the funds used to purchase this mansion, which she blackmailed from them by holding said Sacred Bow hostage.
Well, the real problem is the Pureblood part itself.

The elven role of Pureblood was a kind of race secret. Only one person could inherit the title at a time, and the successor’s Natural Power skyrocketed. That was the entire reason why Erwen had been able to make a contract with the Spirit King in the first place.
I should solve this problem ASAP. It doesn’t make sense to let Erwen handle it alone.
The time I spent sleeping suddenly felt like a waste. Although it hadn’t even been a month since I got back from Ice Rock, this was no time to rest.
Growl!
“...There’s food in the kitchen, you should go get some.”
Yeah, wait, let’s eat first.

After filling my stomach following three days of starvation, the first thing I did was parse through what I’d learned about Baekho, the GM, Hyeonbyeol, Ragna, Auril Gavis, and the numerous other pieces of information I’d obtained from the Round Table. I excused myself from Amelia and holed myself up in my room for a while to gather my thoughts.
Ha... my head’s actually going to explode.

I felt like I was back to being a student just before the start of term. I had a load of homework I needed to catch up on but I didn’t know what to tackle first. So I decided to rank everything in order of priority like I did when playing a game. What needed my immediate attention?
It’s easier now that I’ve organized it all like a quest.
After assigning forced rankings, my head felt clearer.
So, the quest I need to fulfill today is... finish creating the clan.
“Amelia, how did it go establishing the clan?”
“They finished reviewing the documents yesterday, so all you have to do is go in person and put your name on the list.”

I had actually considered reviving my old clan for a while. But since it was disbanded after I was presumed dead, the administrative process to reinstate it would be too complicated, so we decided to just create a new one instead. This was slightly disappointing. Being an older clan came with a lot of advantages.
Well, I guess I can use my noble title to compensate for that in the future.
Negotiating with the guild, at least, was something I was confident about. I changed my clothes and was about to leave to tackle today’s to-do list when Amelia followed me, her jacket already on.
“You want to come?”
“I think that’s for the best. Since I handled most of the paperwork.”
True, if we went together, there was less of a chance we’d miss anything. Raven normally took on this role.
It’ll take a long while before we can get that girl out of the military.
Of course, that didn’t mean I’d given up. What was most important was what Raven wanted, though.
“Wait.”
“Huh?”
“Use this. If you go out like that, there’ll be a big fuss.”
“Ah...” I put on the iron helmet Amelia passed me and headed out the door.
“It’s been a while since we headed out together like this,” Amelia commented.
Hmm, has it?

Well, now that I thought about it, the last time was when we went to the art gallery to buy the essence of Vol-Herchan at the auction. After returning to the present, we weren’t in a position to roam around freely.
“Oh, there it is.”

Because the mansion itself was located in the city center, it didn’t take long to walk to the nearest branch of the guild. We took a number and waited like the other adventurers. When our turn came, we presented our IDs.
“B-B-B-Bjo... ah—!”

We were led to a private reception area on the second floor by a member of staff who started hyperventilating as soon as they saw my ID. The branch manager came running and completed the remaining administrative procedures for us. It felt weird.
Commander, Bjorn Yandel
Deputy Commander, Vacant
Member, Vacant
Member, Emily Raines
Member, Ainar Fenelin
Member, Auyen Rockrobe
This was the minimum number of people required to create a clan. For reference, Erwen couldn’t join right now because we hadn’t yet dealt with the problem of her leaving the Purebloods.
“P-Please visit again soon!”
After a warm reception and farewell from the branch manager, we left the guild and headed to a nearby restaurant. Considering I hadn’t eaten for three days, I was already starving again.
“Amelia.”
“It’s Emily out here.”
Ah, right. I’m too hungry to think straight.
“So, what did you want to say to me?”
“Oh, nothing special. I’m just curious. Why did you tell me to leave the spot for the first member blank?” I did as she advised, but I hadn’t gotten an explanation yet. So, why?
“At times, impatience can make things fall apart.”
“While she’s busy withdrawing her title as a Pureblood, tell her you left the position empty on purpose. That will calm that elf down.”
“Uh...” What was I hearing right now? “...You left it open for Erwen?”
Amelia averted her eyes, looking somewhat embarrassed. “...She seemed upset,” she muttered before changing the subject. “Anyway, the clan name.”
“Huh?”
“Is there a reason you named it that? From what I can remember, that’s a well-known ancient word meaning ‘a group of wild beasts.’”
So, you assumed it was an ancient word as soon as you heard it too. Then I guess I’ve succeeded?
After a moment’s thought, I told Amelia the truth, leaning in close so that no one could overhear. “It’s actually not the ancient tongue. It’s Korean.”
When I whispered in her ear, Amelia shuddered. “Korean?” she whispered. “Are you saying it’s from your home country?”
“Yeah.” I nodded and told her the meaning while I was at it. “It’s a word that captures the spirit of working together with one heart and one mind toward a better future.”
“That’s what anabada means: reduce, reuse, recycle.”
That was also going to be our clan’s creed for the time being as, given the corner we had been driven into, we couldn’t afford to do anything else.

After the meal, Amelia left because she had some business to take care of. It was obvious where she was going. She was probably headed to her sister’s workplace to sneak a peek at her again, unable to bring herself to even speak with her.
Well, if she’s satisfied with that, it’s not like I can say anything.
My quest for today was over, but I walked somewhere else instead of home. There was something I wanted to do myself.
Jingle!
When I opened the shop door and entered, I saw a reasonably full restaurant. The tavern sold food during the day and drinks at night, with an inn on the second floor.
“Welcome! Are you here alone?” When I stepped through the door, a young waitress in her twenties led me to a table with a bright smile. “What can I get for you?”
“Something with a lot of meat, please. I’m hungry from walking here.”
“Sure, wait just a—”
“Wait, is the owner not here today?”
“Ah, the priest told her that she needs to start being careful. She doesn’t come in these days.”
...Is she sick?
I was a little worried about that, but I decided to correct the misunderstanding first. “I was asking about the male owner.”
“Ah! Mr. Urikfried will be coming in soon. Probably in about thirty minutes? He’s always all over the place, though, so don’t quote me on that!”
Okay, then I’ll get to see him if I wait for a while.
“Thanks for letting me know.”

I tipped the waitress for taking up her time and then sat at a table to kill time. I had finished my first serving and just ordered a new one when the door opened and the person I’d been waiting for arrived.
Jingle!
“You’re here, Mr. Urikfried!”
“Yes, did anything happen?”
“Your friend is here.”

“...Friend?” Mr. Bear turned around to scan the shop and froze as soon as his eyes met mine. It seemed he realized what was going on here. “Myla, don’t accept any more customers from here on out. And send away the customers who are here as soon as they’re done eating.”
“Sorry?”
“Ah, and after you send them all off, you and the chef can go home.”
“Ehh?”
“If you can, don’t let anyone come to my table,” Mr. Bear quickly instructed the waitress before approaching me. “It’s really you, then, Bjorn Yandel.”
“Long time no see, Abman.”
Mr. Bear stared at me for a long, quiet moment before sitting down without hesitation. There was a brief beat of silence. Mr. Bear was the first to break it.
“I heard... the news.”
Yikes, why is this so awkward?
“I still don’t understand what’s going on, but it seems something big happened to you.”
“Ah, yeah... it did...”
“Did you meet with... the others?”
“Everyone except Missha.”

“So... I see...” Mr. Bear seemed to think something over for a moment before continuing. “Actually, I went to your house a few times after I heard the news. But I left since there was no sign of you coming out.”
“You should’ve knocked. I would’ve let you in any time.”
“I don’t know, I changed my mind.”
Was there some kind of hidden meaning in his words or... No, I’m sure there wasn’t. Yeah, so... First off, let’s set the record straight.
“Abman, I never planned to deceive you guys. The reason why I couldn’t show up for two and a half years is all—”

“Stop. Bjorn, I think you misunderstood. I’m not angry at you for that. Of course, I’d be lying if I said I didn’t feel betrayed at all... But this has nothing to do with that.” Mr. Bear cleared that up right away. Then he stole my drink, chugged it down, and took a breath. “I just didn’t want to hear what the reason for your disappearance was. Because it could be linked to something dangerous. And that has nothing to do with me anymore, anyway.”
It felt like something was squeezing my chest. “Nothing to do with you, huh?”
“Sorry, but I think I should make this clear before we continue: if you’re here to get me back on your team, that’s going to be impossible.”
Was this what it meant to get dumped before even asking someone out? I was more curious than upset, though. “Sounds like you’re not saying that because you love the clan you’re in right now.”
“Yeah, I’m not.”
“Then can you tell me why?”
Mr. Bear exhaled deeply through his nose like he was suppressing a sigh. “The day we heard the news of your return... my wife pulled me aside. Very worriedly, she asked if I was going to go see you.”
“I see...”

“You know something, Bjorn? Two and a half years is a really long time. Enough to change the mind of an adventurer whose dream was once to see the end of the labyrinth,” Mr. Bear said solemnly. “So... my point is... I can’t go back to the life I lived before. If I continue working with you, I don’t think I’ll get to see my children get married.”
“Hm... I see...”

With that, I brushed off even the barest hints of lingering regret. No, there were no regrets to begin with. There was a reason I hadn’t classified today’s visit as a proper quest. I never planned to recruit him. In fact, I planned to stop myself from doing so. Think about it: how could I ask him to join a clan that might turn against the king one day? A married man with children?
“I’m sorry,” said Mr. Bear.
“Don’t be, let’s drink.” When he hesitated, I teasingly goaded him. “What? You can’t drink with me if we’re not going into the labyrinth together?”
“...Not at all.”

Mr. Bear then picked up his glass and we spent our time chatting about trivial things as the tavern gradually emptied out and all the employees went home. The sun set and night came. We talked about the past, laughed, and sometimes got into serious debates.
“...It’s late.”
“It’s only evening.”
“My wife will be waiting.”
“Then... that’s too bad.”
“Sorry. If my wife weren’t almost due, I would’ve stayed a little longer.”
Almost due?
My mind momentarily went blank, but it only took a second for me to process that.
So he has a second kid on the way.

This realization felt weird for some reason. Now that I thought about it, I hadn’t been able to be by his side when his first child was born. He used to talk about being their godfather whenever we drank.
“It’s raining. Take this. I should tidy up before I go.”
“...Ah, thanks.”
After exchanging a few more words, I put on the raincoat Mr. Bear offered and walked out into the street.
Tututututu.
It was pouring.
I’m not exactly sad, but...

Was it because this was the first time in a while I’d had so much to drink? The realization that two and a half years had passed by without me suddenly felt cruel. It felt like I’d missed out on something precious. But what could I do about it now? I had no choice but to accept it.
Splash, splash.
I walked down the rainy street.
Splash, splash.

Though I was concentrating on putting one foot in front of the other, my drunken body still stumbled here and there. I wondered if it was because of my shaky gait that I kept thinking about the end of our conversation.
“Bjorn Yandel... Make great strides. Don’t carry any regrets about a straggler like me.”
Jeez, there’s no such thing as stragglers in life.
“If you keep moving, I know you’ll be able to go anywhere you wish.”
Why does everyone treat me like I’m special?
Splash, splash.
I couldn’t be sure, but I walked forward anyway, repeating my to-do list for tomorrow over and over in my head.

chapters.title: Chapter 443: Giant Step (5)
paragraphs: The next morning after falling asleep drunk, I reached out of my blanket to grab the flask on the nightstand and gulped down the strangely sweet drink inside. It tasted like someone had sweetened it with honey.
Ugh, that feels much better.
After rolling around on the bed for a bit, I slowly got up. The first thing I saw was a neatly folded letter on the nightstand.
I’m heading out to go to the holy land. But don’t worry too much. I’ll be able to step down without much issue. Oh, and... if you’re having a hard time, be sure to tell me! Okay?
P.S. I heard you left the spot of the first clan member blank for me on purpose. Thank you. Really.
P.P.S. Oh, and it’s today, right? Be careful!
Your first clan mate, Erwen
So, Erwen’s off to the holy land again. If I came home earlier yesterday, we could have spoken. Jeez, why did I drink so much?

I sat there in bed for a while to give the stench of alcohol time to dissipate and revisited my memory of what happened after I parted with Mr. Bear. I remembered up to when Erwen and Amelia welcomed me home.
I think they helped me up to the second floor...

Was it because I drank while I was still exhausted? I was sure we talked about something on the way up, but I couldn’t remember it at all. I was sure I didn’t do anything bad, though. If I did, I would have definitely remembered it.
“Looks like you’re awake,” said Amelia from the doorway.
“Yeah, I just woke up now.”
“Go wash up a bit. You’re headed to the royal capital today.”
“...Okay.”
“I’m going out now, so good luck today.”
“Sure.”
I heard Amelia walk down the stairs. I went to the bathroom to wash up and get ready to go out myself. For today’s quest, I had to pay close attention to my clothes.
“...Tsk, I knew you’d do this.” After I washed up, Amelia snuck up on me as I was putting on my suit and helped me get dressed. It was kind of fascinating.
“Why are you so good at this?”
“Who do you think got the clothes you’re wearing?”
“Ah... you bought this, I forgot.” It seemed she’d learned how to put on the clothes when she bought them. Amelia was oddly meticulous about everything she did.
“All done. You can go now. Looks like the carriage arrived a while ago.”
“I should head out, then. See you in the evening.”
Amelia saw me off, and I took the carriage waiting for me in front of the house to the military platform. Then we used a teleportation circle to immediately arrive at the royal capital.
I think this every time, but this is really convenient. Aside from the slight motion sickness.
Anyway, another carriage was waiting for me in front of the platform, and before long, I was able to arrive at my destination.
It’s not really all that incredible anymore.
I’d visited the Palace of Glory several times over the past several years. A small event was being held here today, and my quest for today was related to that event.
“I am Mia Arbelto, first-class steward. I sincerely welcome you to the palace, Baronet Yandel.”
As I followed my guide inside, a great hall appeared. This was the place I announced the return of our squadron.
“This is my first time seeing it so empty.”
“There’s still time until the ceremony begins. The lords will be arriving soon.”
How many could there be, though? Even if everyone comes, there’ll only be enough to fill the front rows.
“Please come this way.”
Passing through the Palace of Glory, I moved to a private room reserved for me. There, the steward walked me through the program for today’s ceremony.
A long while later, the door opened with a knock.
Knock, knock.
An old man I’d never met came in. It seemed the steward who was lecturing me knew him, though, as he immediately stopped what he was doing in shock. “Your Excellency, what brings you here?”
“I thought I’d have a quick chat with the star of the event. If you’re not busy, do you mind giving us the room?”
“...I’ll wait outside.” The steward bowed politely at his superior and excused himself from the room. Only once he was gone did the formal meeting between the old man and I begin.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Duke Kealunus.”
I was wondering which duke you were. So it’s you.
“Bjorn, son of Yandel.” I formally introduced myself as well.
“Wrong.”
What the hell?
When I frowned, the old man burst into laughter. “It’s Bjorn Yandel. Not ‘son of Yandel.’ You are now a member of the court, no?”

I wondered if he had come all the way here just to pick a fight with me, but I didn’t particularly sense any hostility in his tone. Therefore, I held off on attacking him for now. I’d listen carefully to what came out of his mouth next so that I could make an accurate assessment of his personality.

“I may have no say over your unique way of speaking, for the king has officially allowed it, but you should make it clear to people who you are. Remember, you are not Bjorn, someone’s son. You’re not any old barbarian, either. You are Baronet Bjorn Yandel of Rafdonia. Ah, or would that be baron now? By the way, your tie is crooked.” The duke laughed heartily and patted me on my shoulder.

This was sort of depressing. Now that I was shorter, even an old man like this could reach my shoulder. “Thank you for your advice. But I don’t think you’re just here to say hello.” I couldn’t wreck a duke just because I was in a bad mood, so I cut to the chase.
But was he unused to this kind of directness? “What? Haha, hahaha! Ahem... I apologize for laughing. I didn’t mean to insult you in any way—I just find this fascinating.”
I could understand that. Nobles liked wordy conversations, right? I was sure he didn’t have much experience getting straight to the point right after introductions.
“Anyway... to answer your question, you are correct. If I just wanted to say hello, I could have come to see you another time. I came to find you now because I have a few questions for you.”
Ugh, he’s doing it again. Just say, “I have a question” and be done with it. Like I’m doing right now.
“What’s your question?” He didn’t respond. “...Are you hard of hearing?” I asked carefully.
The duke returned to his senses. “Sorry. I was distracted there for a second. No, not distracted... to be honest, I didn’t realize you were already done speaking.”
“Oh, I see. So, what’s your question?”

When I repeated my question, the duke finally got down to business. It seemed he’d figured out how to communicate with me. “I’ll keep this short. You are not the type to long for the life of an aristocrat. Why did you choose to ascend in peerage in return for your contributions to this mission?”
That wasn’t short at all, but it was still to the point.
“The palace has offered Bjorn Yandel a higher title for his contribution to the expedition.”

Deer had revealed that at the Round Table, but in truth, the promotion wasn’t the only reward the palace had offered me. There were a total of four options presented to me by the Ministry of Veteran Affairs: a large sum of money, enough to build an entire mansion from scratch; two rank-three essences; a double-digit Numbered Item; and the title. After much deliberation, I chose the promotion. The reason for that was simple. The first three were things I could achieve on my own, and this was much more useful in terms of my immediate survival.
“I want to hear the truth. Why did you want the promotion?”
What a funny old man. The truth? How long have we known each other again?
I chuckled at his prodding and answered like he’d asked the most obvious question in the world. “Because it’s good to have many wives!”
Though I’d deliberately shouted this with incredible enthusiasm, the duke’s expression went blank. “Wives...?”
Jeez, does he actually have bad hearing?
“Yes, wives,” I replied without a care in the world. “Barons can have three wives!”

In response, the look in the duke’s eyes shifted significantly. Is this son of a bitch serious? he seemed to be asking. But the reason he couldn’t bring himself to mount a counterattack was probably because he didn’t know if it was even worth it.
Burp!
I was his opponent, after all.
“Oh, sorry. I had too much breakfast.” I quickly apologized since this man obviously grew up with manners, but the duke didn’t seem to care at all.
He just muttered to himself like he was starting to piece something together. “Certainly... you are known to have many women.”
To be more accurate, I had comrades who were women, though lots of strange love stories and rumors had proliferated throughout the city. Perhaps it was because we lived together.
“So, does that answer your question?”
“At least half. There’s one more thing I want to ask.”
“Ask.”
It seemed he was really starting to take a shine to the direct barbarian way of speaking because, without warning, the duke posed the following question: “Do you work for the marquess?”

This was short—much too short. Nothing wrong with being direct, but since this seemed like an important question, I started off by asking for confirmation. “When you say marquess, are you talking about the prime minister?”
“I am. Including the period you were missing, it seems you’ve been working with the marquess a long time.”
“...I guess?”

This was a loaded question. Bjorn Yandel, who was believed to be dead, had actually been entrusted with various secret missions by the marquess over the two and a half years he was gone, and that was why the announcement that he was an evil spirit was made. As far as the public knew, this was the official story.
I didn’t think the truth would be kept from the duke too, though.
A strange prickle of wrongness crept over me.

“I’ve read all of the documents regarding your mission. You’ve done quite a lot of work. The documents are authentic as well. At first, I believed there might be some kind of deal in place between you two, but it seems the mission itself was real.”

The marquess had prepared the documents already? And made them look good enough to fool even the duke? He told me it’d take two more months at the ceremony... Is this the kind of thing being the prime minister of a country makes possible?
The question came to mind, but I focused on my conversation with the duke for now. First, I needed to make this clear. “I am not working for the marquess.”
“Then can you tell me your exact relationship?”
“We’re kind of friends. Friends that help each other out of tight spots from time to time.”

Maybe that was the answer he was waiting for because the duke’s expression grew warmer. “Friends... What an interesting word. You are smarter than I thought. And quite sensible,” the duke said, almost to himself, before asking another question. “Anyway, does your answer mean... that you are open to being friends with me too?”
His hand was already extended to me as if rejection was not even an option on the table. I wiped my hand on my thigh, then grabbed his. “Of course. The more friends, the better.”
Well, real friends don’t shake hands, though.

The fact was that Duke Kealunus was the third most powerful person in the kingdom after the king and prime minister. Though he did not hold political power as the prime minister did, his family had incredible sway. He sponsored dozens of clans, and among them were a surprising number of medium-sized ones. One of his younger brothers was even the lord of the Magic Tower.
Friends with a duke like that, huh?

The offer was unexpected, but there were no downsides to accepting it. It wasn’t like we were real friends in the first place. The duke was only suggesting a friendship to keep me from working for the marquess. I just had to do with him what I was already doing with the marquess—give what I could give and take what I could take. At least until I didn’t need ‘friendships’ like that anymore.

The duke chatted with me until right before the ceremony began. Most of it was small talk to build rapport, but some of the things he brought up were more important. According to him, the reason why our squadron survived was because the Order of the Rose clashed with Noark’s troops while on standby for another mission.
“It’s about time for me to go, so I will. See you later.”
“Sure.”
I still don’t know if he was feeling me out by mentioning the Order...

I wasn’t sure of the duke’s motives, but one thing was clear. At the very least, the kingdom’s Department of Intelligence was interpreting what had happened on the seventh floor the way I wanted them to.
I wonder what that son of a bitch marquess thinks.
Actually, that was the thing I was wondering the most. Ever since the return ceremony, I hadn’t seen the marquess once. Today would be our first reunion in weeks.
“Baronet Yandel.”
So, it’s begun.
I stood in front of the door and waited as instructed by the steward. As soon as the door opened, I slowly walked in.
Step. Step.
The Palace of Glory, which had been empty two hours ago, was now filled with quite the crowd. Or, well, the front two rows were, at least.
Step. Step.

It was different from our squadron’s return ceremony. Not all the seats within the hall were filled, and no loud music or soldiers was marching behind me. In terms of scale, it couldn’t compare to the previous ceremony at all.
Step, step.
Still, it would be wrong to describe this event as small. The people filling the seats were all titled nobles, after all.
“It’s really been a long time since everyone got together like this.”
“I was very surprised to see the notice of attendance. A promotion in rank for Baronet Bjorn Yandel...”
“Haha, this is actually my first time receiving a notice of attendance.”
“Oh, it hasn’t been long since you inherited a title, right?”
“I can’t say it hasn’t been long, but... yes, promotion ceremonies aren’t common in themselves.”
