The nobles whispered among themselves as I walked down the carpet. Some seemed to be enjoying the rare spectacle of a rank promotion, but some seemed to feel the opposite.
“...a mere barbarian...” Some despised me.
“...he was just born at the right time...” Some envied me.
“...I hope this is over soon.” Some were attending out of obligation and had no interest in me. They preferred that this end as soon as possible.
Step. Step.
I walked between the rows and arrived before the empty throne. The marquess stood in front of it this time too. And here I thought I might get to see the king’s face for once.

“Long time no see.” The marquess greeted me quietly so that only I could hear him, and immediately raised his voice to launch into a speech before I could even respond. Then he handed me an empty box. “Seal your family crest in this box.”

This was a ceremony that only occurred when a baronet was promoted to Baron. The titles of baronet and baron were worlds apart, so this was treated as the historic moment it was—another noble family being added to the thousands that uplifted the kingdom.
Slide.
As soon as the cloth I prepared was folded and placed inside the box, his dignified voice rang out through the hall. “With this, an eternal covenant has been made.”

The marquess sealed the box himself and handed it to the royal guards waiting next to him. They solemnly accepted it and left the Palace of Glory. That box would enter the Palace of Immortality and be stored under lock and key from now on, until either this kingdom burned to the ground and perished, or I committed treason.
“Baron Bjorn Yandel, rise.” I stood up. “Nobles, I hope you will be pleased to welcome the emergence of a new pillar that will serve to uplift the kingdom!”
I received quiet applause without any cheers or whistles.
“Now, this concludes the promotion ceremony!”
From there, the banquet began.
It seems I’ve just taken a big step forward.
So it was time to move on to the next step.

chapters.title: Chapter 444: Party (1)
paragraphs: The banquet held inside the Palace of Glory proceeded quietly. This was only natural. All of the attendees were heads of families. They had reputations to uphold, plus everyone was older to begin with.
The majority are in their fifties.
That made me laugh a bit. I couldn’t believe I was the star of this banquet but I was sitting here crying woe is me all by myself.
Munch, munch.

I wolfed down my meal with some annoyance. For someone who moved schools often, this was the exact type of environment that was liable to trigger my PTSD. It was now hitting me that I had just joined a new group with absolutely nothing to defend myself with. I felt like a monkey at the zoo.
Count Ferdehilt, Baron Serpia, Viscount Mülbark... oh? Even Baron Martoin is there.

Some of the lords eyeing me from afar were familiar, but not a single person approached me first. Jeez, and they were all asking to be my friend at the other banquets. Count Ferdehilt had even asked me to marry his daughter.
Well, I can understand where they’re coming from.
This was the animal kingdom, after all. Except here, brains ruled rather than brawn.
Munch, munch.

I may have been digging into this food pretending to be none the wiser, but I had a perfect understanding of the situation. This was a kind of hazing process, an unspoken warning for me to not even think about joining their ranks, as they were backed by thousands of years of history. However, there was a simple solution to this issue of being ignored. As the duke advised me earlier, all I had to do was go up and talk to them first. Then they’d smile and treat me kindly, like someone beneath them.
Ugh, don’t these bastards ever get tired of all this?

For reference, who I spoke to first would be a big deal. If I went up to the duke I met earlier, the nobles under the marquess, his rival, would start treating me like I was invisible. Everything I did and said here would have political implications.
Munch, munch.

But I just kept eating my meal. There were three reasons for this. First, I was really hungry. Second, this meat was really, really good. And third, I had no intention of joining their little cliques in the first place.
She’s finally here.

“I suppose there’s no point in waiting. It’s not like anyone else is coming over anyway.” I glanced at the woman who was approaching me and smiled inwardly. She had pale hair, pale eyes, and pale skin on top of that. Aside from her unique, colorful attire reminiscent of a hanbok, this woman was whiter than snow. Oh, and of course, there were rabbit ears on the top of her head. “Nice to meet you, Baron Yandel. Is this meal to your liking?”
“You want to try some?”
When I picked up a piece of meat and held it out to her, the woman stared at me blankly for a moment before managing to snap out of it and smile. “No, I’m all right. I’m not hungry.”
Jeez, so picky. And we’re both non-humans.
Tap.

I thought that was enough to give her a clear sense of who I was, so I set the meat back on the plate and settled in to have a conversation. Then I sucked my fingers clean. Suddenly, an intrusive thought popped into my head: would she shake my hand if I asked? I couldn’t be sure, but I wasn’t going to try. I was a well-mannered barbarian. At least when it was beneficial for me to be.
“Anyway, nice to meet you. I’m Baron Yandel.”
When I took the initiative to introduce myself first, the woman responded with a friendly smile. “Baroness Lirivia.”
I already knew this information, of course. There was only one noble family from the White Rabbit Tribe.
Age forty-three. She has three kids, I think?
“May I sit down for a moment?”
“Of course. I was getting bored.”

When I gave her permission, Baroness Lirivia, the Rabbit Baroness, sat in front of me. The eight-seat table I was at had someone else sitting at it for the first time. But no one applauded this monumental occasion. There was only sharp ridicule.
“Tsk, of course.”
“Well, there’s no reason to stop the lowborns from entertaining each other.”

Since that was loud enough to reach my barbarian ears, this rabbit woman had to have heard it too. But she didn’t even flinch. The baroness simply smiled like she was used to this treatment and spoke softly. “The founder of our family was a hero like you, Baron Yandel. During the Iron Wall Rebellion, he achieved the great feat of stopping the sacrilegious duke. Have you heard this story?”
“No, sorry. This is my first time hearing it.”

“Haha, don’t be. It’s only natural. Nowadays, it’s an old story only known by those who have studied history...” The baroness’s voice grew a bit melancholy. “It was as many as two thousand years ago when the Lirivia family’s crest was placed in the covenant box. It has been a very long time. The era of a king who was considered immortal had come to an end, and a new dawn had arrived.”
I thought I knew what she was getting at.
“So, Baron Yandel, you’ll have to get used to it fast. Even time won’t change these peoples’ minds.”
“Oh, really? That’s strange. To me, you don’t seem all that different to them.”
Especially since you have the same flowery, cunning way of speaking.
“...You are as funny as the rumors say.”
Ha, funny? I haven’t even gotten started yet.
“Anyway, I don’t think you’re here to give me advice, am I right?”
“You are remarkable, as expected. You’re right.”
“Then tell me.”

At my bluntness, the woman paused for a moment. This was why I said she was no different than them. She may have had those ears on her head, but she attended this event on behalf of her family as a full-fledged noblewoman, someone who regarded conversations outside of the realm of propriety as beneath her.
“I wouldn’t say I’m not here to help. We don’t want you working under another faction.”
“Because I’m the first noble from another race to be added to the court in six hundred years?”

The woman flinched at my question but soon took a deep breath. Then she looked me straight in the eyes, her tone shifting. “More importantly, one of barbarian origin. The first ever in Rafdonia’s history.” With that, I could see that this woman’s perception of me as a naïve barbarian had changed, unlike those human nobles watching us. “Just as Lirivia receives the full support of the beastpeople, you can lead the barbarians into politics.”
“Is that the only reason?”
“Of course, I would have approached you either way. We’re in need of each and every ally we can get.”
“Hmm, I see...”

“A total of thirty-one families including Lirivia are joining forces. Of course, we’re still a minority in the government, but it’s enough to have a voice.” As I propped my chin up in my hand, looking bored by her explanation, the Rabbit Baroness kicked off the negotiations first. “I won’t ask you to join us for a higher cause.” Beggars couldn’t be choosers, after all. “But if you join us, you will receive enormous support in establishing yourself as a nobleman.”
“I want you to elaborate on that.”
“For example, the decades it would normally take for you to purchase land, build an estate, and hire servants to maintain it will be shortened to just a few years.”

Was this what it meant to be an aristocrat? It was a staggering offer already. Even if I took just this, I’d make more than my money’s worth for choosing the promotion option as a reward instead of the cash.
“Of course, that’s not all. We started this alliance to survive,” she explained. “If you join us, our enemies will become your enemies. And your enemies will become ours.”

This was the reason why I’d waited for her to approach me instead of going to talk to the other nobles. Each person they managed to add to their alliance was invaluable, and they took care of each other accordingly.
“So, what do you think?” She asked me for an answer.
I nodded. “It’s certainly... not a bad offer.”
“You mean—”
“But it’s not enough.”
Even if you look at me like that, it won’t make a difference. It’s clear I can get more out of this—I can’t be satisfied with that alone.

The Rabbit Baroness’s expression hardened upon hearing my answer, though it soon returned to its original placidity. “Baron Yandel, I’m finding you to be a clever man. If there is anything you wish for, could you be frank and tell me?” she asked politely, refusing to give up.

I could tell just by her question exactly how much this woman—and by extension Melbeth, the alliance of non-human nobles—wanted me. Of course, I desperately wanted to join their group as well, but they didn’t know that.
If you’re going to sell something, sell it for the highest price you can. That’s the philosophy of a K-Barbarian.
“I’m going to continue to enter the labyrinth. I want support for that too.”
“Can you give me an example of what you mean by support?”
“I want you to sponsor the clan I’m going to create. High-ranking essences, precious Numbers Items, things like that.”
“...That won’t be easy. Especially in that it doesn’t benefit us.”
“Why not? You guys should know. This country begins and ends in the labyrinth.”
“If you’re trying to say you can get us some influence within the labyrinth, we already have plenty of alternatives.”
Tsk, playing hard to get, huh? It seems it’s time to bring out the barbarian again.
“Why?!”
“...Sorry?”
“You said you would buy me land and build me a house. This is cheaper than that!”
“Um... Baron Yandel? Please lower your voice...”
“Tell me why!” When I jumped out of my seat, all the nobles turned to look at us. It seemed that served to twist her arm.

“This is different from us supporting you as a noble. Becoming independent will help you later when you are active in politics. This is different,” the Rabbit Baroness quickly explained. But did she pick up on the fact that her response was lacking? “But you never know... If you become indispensable to us... We won’t consider any amount of support we can offer you a waste.”
“What! Then I’m useless to you now?!”
“No, that’s not what I meant!”
“Haha! I was only joking, Baroness Lirivia.”
“...Eh?” When I laughed and sat back down, the baroness stared blankly into space.
Jeez, it’s like I can’t even kid around with you.
“To put it simply, it sounds like you want me to prove my worth. That I’m useful in other ways than just as the first barbarian baron.”
“Yes... ah, yes. That’s right...?”
“Then that’s no problem. Because that’s way too easy for me.”
The woman looked confused by my confident answer, and the nobles around us began to murmur at the turn our conversation had taken.
“I thought they were fighting—now they’re laughing again?”
“These mutts... They truly are like beasts.”
“Anyway, I wonder what Baroness Lirivia said to calm the barbarian’s anger.”
“Hmm, you never know. I hear that barbarian has a liking for beastwomen.”
“Pardon? You mean...”
“Ahem, it’s not out of the realm of possibility, is it?”

Their whispers were crude even to a barbarian like me. Although she’d been on the receiving end of endless ridicule, it seemed the baroness had never heard this kind before, as her face turned red with shame. The sight left an impression.

“...Baron Yandel.” Even in this situation, though, it seemed she was worried I might cause a scene. “Just ignore them. You’ll have to hear such things countless times if you plan on being active in politics in the future.”
“Why?”

“Because there’s nothing to be done.” It was an honest answer that carried with it all the frustration of an underdog. But the expression on her face as she said it really made her look like an herbivore.
I chuckled. “You said you were used to it. But I guess you still get angry too?”
“How could I not? All I can do is endure their treatment while dreaming of a day when I won’t have to feel this misery anymore.”
“Dreaming, huh?” If dreams could come true just because you have them, there would be no such thing as unhappiness. “How much would that be worth?”
“What do you mean?”
“I may not be able to fulfill your wish, but I can at least make those bastards running their mouths disappear,” I said. “So I’m asking, how much is that worth?”

It seemed the Rabbit Baroness didn’t properly understand what I was getting at, because her response was faint. “I don’t know. I think that for something like that, I wouldn’t regret losing my entire fortune.” It was a very abstract and subjective answer, but it was enough for me.
“Okay, then. The deal is over.”
“Eh?”
“I’ve done some digging into you guys too, you know. The reason why people shit on all of you is because you let people shit on you all the time.”
“W-What do you mean!?”
What do you think? I mean that what you need is an attack dog.
Slide.
I stood up from my seat, not giving her time to respond. “Behel—aaaaaah!” After attracting aggro with a battle cry, I stomped away.
Step, step.
“B-Baron Yandel!”
I ignored the Rabbit Baroness’s panicked cries.
Step, step.
Within a few seconds, I came to a stop in front of the nobleman who was yapping about my supposed preference for beastwomen.
“What’s the matter? How noisy.” Unfortunately, it seemed this guy still hadn’t grasped the situation he was in, seeing as he was glaring at me like this.
“Baron Kypriot.” Though he didn’t introduce himself, I had no problem calling him by name. After I decided to take the noble route, I memorized all the noble families’ crests.
A baron of so-so standing. He’ll be a perfect example.
“You insulted me,” I declared.
“Insulted? Is this about what I said earlier? Ha! Ridiculous. Not only do I question whether you have any honor to insult in the first place, but even if you do, what are you going to do about it?
Jeez, pretending not to be scared, huh? It’s obvious he’s running his mouth because he’s freaked out.
“If you really can’t control your anger, write to the committee. Ah, assuming you can write!” When he finished speaking, the people next to him, who appeared to be his friends, started snickering.
Jeez, these are some third-rate bums. And who’s the lowborn one here?
“Now, if you have nothing more to say, I’d like to ask you to move—”
Why would I have nothing to say? I cut him off. “I challenge you to a duel.”

Duels were the sole means of conflict resolution in Rafdonia’s aristocratic society since ancient times. Of course, the number of times a titled nobleman had directly participated in a duel throughout the nation’s long history was less than ten.
“Are you scared?” I asked. “If you are, you can have a proxy. Ah, of course, I’m going to be representing myself in the fight.”
“...Are you serious?”
“Why, you want me to be joking?”

He didn’t answer my question. It was obvious what the baron was thinking. Not only was this completely unprecedented, but it must have been both insulting and intimidating. All he’d done was act as everyone always did and others were doing the same, so he must have been wondering why he was the only one being targeted like this.
They should be getting it now.
A barbarian had just ascended to noble status. It was time to inject some tension into this overly lax aristocratic court.
Step.

I took another step forward and looked down at him as I spoke. “Knight, adventurer, wizard—doesn’t matter.” The general rule was that mercenaries were not permitted as representatives for duels, but... “It doesn’t have to be someone from your family. Bring anyone. The strongest guy you can get.”
There was no answer.
“What, you’re not confident?”
Because I am. I’m confident I can kill anyone you put in front of me.

chapters.title: Chapter 445: Party (2)
paragraphs: Giving off a similar air to the one I did at the Round Table, I looked down at him like I was ready to rip his throat out at any given moment. But this wasn’t some chatroom that merely connected our minds. Right now, we were here in the flesh, which meant this was more than enough.
I continued to glare down at him, completely devoid of fear.
Yeah, this was how it should be. How would he, a born and bred noble, have ever experienced something like this before?

Silence hung over the room when he didn’t respond. Scandal-obsessed as they were, the other nobles silently observed our interaction from a safe distance. If they really saw my status as inferior to theirs, they would have come running to help him by now.
Sure enough, barbarians are incredibly OP.

If I had been an elf, dwarf, or beastman, some of them would surely have criticized me for my horrible manners. At the very least, they would have operated under the assumption that I could be reasoned with. But what could they say when faced with a barbarian?
The answer was nothing at all.
It was hard to take action without any data to back you up. In other words, they were wary of stepping forward and potentially adding fuel to the fire.
“...Is it really okay to leave them be?” Some of them voiced their concerns, but they all turned away as soon as our eyes met.

It wasn’t like I would suddenly attack all the nobles here just because we happened to make eye contact—that would defy all common sense. But they couldn’t be sure of that. After all, did common sense even apply to a barbarian who rushed to demand a duel after overhearing an insult?
“It’s about time you answer me.” I took another step forward when Baron Kypriot tried to put some space between us. “Do you not want to duel?”
At that, the other nobles who had been chatting with him only moments earlier slowly backed away. In the end, the baron realized that he had no choice but to clean up this mess on his own.

It didn’t take long for him to reach a decision. “...Set a date.” This decision wasn’t one he came to because he was confident in his ability to win. It was simply the only choice available to him. How could he refuse a duel from someone of a different race—someone he considered uncultured and inferior—in front of so many people? That was no different than a death sentence in the world of nobility, where reputations were their lifeblood.
“Since you want to set a date, that must mean you don’t have the guts to fight me yourself.”
“...One always uses a separate blade to slay beasts.”
Although he worded it eloquently, all that meant was that he was afraid to fight me. Instead, he would appoint someone to fight me on his behalf.
“That’s no problem. But you should have several people prepared just in case.”
“...Several people?”

What was with that clueless look? Did he really think this would be over after just one round? “Oh, did you not realize? From today on, I’m going to challenge you to a duel every day. Until I feel that the honor you spat on has been restored.”
A rabid dog doesn’t let go once he’s got his teeth in you.

“...What?” If this was how he was going to act when someone called him out, he should have watched what he said to begin with. Well, maybe it was just in his nature to be an arrogant prick. In that case, I’d have to take him down a peg. “Are you... sure you can handle that?”
What he was really trying to ask was if I really had to go so far. Well, from this guy’s point of view, it must have felt like he had just been struck by lightning on a sunny day.
“You ask strange questions. Can I handle it?” I spoke clearly for everyone there to hear. “Do I look like someone who cares about stuff like that?”
If you don’t want to get bitten in the future, then you all better be careful from now on.
Anyway, with that, the duel was made official. All that remained now was to set a date.
“I should be free this week. Why? Do you need more time to find someone?”
“No. That will be enough time.”
Was he slowly starting to adapt? The baron no longer acted like a buffoon or dragged his feet when answering me. He must have done the math in his head.
What, does he see this as an opportunity?

I was a savage who clearly didn’t know my place at all and had dared to act so atrociously in public. All he had to do was accept the duel, win with grace, and be the hero who preserved the dignity of the aristocracy. It was a reasonably plausible outcome.
Of course, that wouldn’t be happening.
He’ll probably use his connections and reputation to recruit a few different people to fight for him.

I couldn’t honestly say that I could predict what level my opponent would be. Even so, I was confident. No captain of the Royal Guard would be willing to stoop so low as to represent a baron in a duel, and I knew for a fact that I could beat anyone less powerful than that.
Unfortunately, however, someone suddenly interrupted before we could get down to business. “Now, now, that’s enough of that.”
Duke Kealunus.

He walked through the crowd, which parted like the Red Sea as he approached, and then patted me on the shoulder like he was soothing a petulant child. “Now, isn’t it a fine day? Why don’t we leave it at that? We’re all fellow pillars uplifting this kingdom, after all, aren’t we?”

The duke’s political intentions at that moment were made crystal clear. When no one else was willing to intervene, he would bravely step forward and successfully temper the savage’s rage before it could boil over. In doing so, Duke Kealunus’s status with the other nobles would rise.
He wants to play friends?

Friendships tended to fall apart when only one party enjoyed all the benefits while the other made all the sacrifices. If he wanted something from me, then he would naturally have to give up something in return.

“Baron Kypriot has insulted me.” The corners of the duke’s mouth pinched at my stubborn retort, but I pressed on despite how he may have felt about it. “He called me a mutt, no different than a wild beast.”
Technically, it was the person next to him who had said that, but whatever.

“I was having a conversation with Baroness Lirivia too, and they basically called her a prostitute just because she’s from a different race. And when I confronted him about it, he just scoffed at me, questioning whether I even had enough honor to be offended in the first place.”
They even called me illiterate, but I felt like that would be nitpicking, so I left that part out.

“Now, Duke Kealunus, that’s what Baron Kypriot did to me on this fine day you mentioned.” After reiterating my reasons for demanding a duel in front of everyone, I then asked, “Is there any reason why I should put up with all of that?”
The duke’s gaze snapped to the baron. It seemed that he had been observing from a distance but was unaware of the exact details and reason for the commotion until now.

The duke tutted, clicking his tongue as he glared at the baron, then quickly turned his attention back to me. He appeared to be regretting his fruitless attempt to mediate, but since he was already involved, he now had two options. He could simply step back without accomplishing anything despite his lofty intervention, or...
“It seems that Baron Kypriot has made a mistake, then.”
He could give me something as well.

The duke’s judgment was swift and decisive. “Let me make a promise to you. There will be no such mistakes going forward. Not just here and now, but at any point in the future either.” This was a promise made in the name of Duke Kealunus. “Isn’t that right, Baron Kypriot?”
The baron shuddered and quickly blurted, “Y-Yes... of course, Your Grace.”

These were obviously just empty words spoken to escape the mess he was currently in. Still, chances were that neither the baron nor any of the other nobles present would try anything similar after today. That was how much weight a promise from the duke held. If this were to happen again, it would be tantamount to sullying the duke’s name.
It’s a shame that there won’t be a duel, but... I’m sure another opportunity will present itself in the future.
I quickly came to a decision. After all, the duke himself had been willing to back off here.
“Now, was that enough to help alleviate some of your anger?”
If I were to refuse his olive branch, it would be no different than deliberately stirring up trouble.

“I haven’t even heard an apology from Baron Kypriot himself, though. And even if he does choose to apologize, that doesn’t change the fact that he has disrespected my name. However...” It was time to finally put things to rest. “I will let this go here.”
Phew... With that, all the nobles let out a sigh of relief.
But I wasn’t quite done yet. “It was a request from a friend, after all. Not just anyone.”
Everyone’s eyes widened at my closing remark.
Understandable. After all, calling the duke my friend implied that we were equals in an amicable relationship.
The moment the words left my mouth, the entire hall went dead silent.
A barbarian, friends with a duke?
A tense quiet settled over the room while everyone waited for some sort of clarification.

In the silence, the duke’s mouth twitched into a frown before quickly regaining its warm smile. “I’m glad to hear it.” His short response neither confirmed nor denied our status as ‘friends,’ but even that was enough to send my standing as the newest entrant to the Royal Club soaring.
I ended up turning an unexpected profit.

The duke would surely have made all the necessary political calculations in his head before responding to me. He’d already made me a vow in the name of his house in order to cover up another noble’s misstep, after all. In the end, he must have decided that elevating my reputation would benefit him as well.
“Well, I should be returning to my ducal duties. I’ll be in contact at a later date. Oh, and congratulations on becoming a baron.”
After promising to meet with me later in front of everyone, the duke left.
Him going this far makes things a bit problematic...
Still, I couldn’t argue with the results. I could already sense a drastic shift in the gazes of everyone watching me.
“...I guess he didn’t become a noble by pure luck.”
“His change of status was approved so easily... Was that because the duke was supporting him?”
Curiosity began to creep into their eyes. This was a good sign. After all that, I ended up attracting quite a bit of attention. Now, even the marquess wouldn’t be able to pull anything untoward.

After warning Baron Kypriot that I wouldn’t be so reasonable next time, I returned to my seat. The Rabbit Baroness stood frozen at the table, staring at me blankly. “There’s no reason for you to stand to greet me... Baroness Lirivia?” I prodded, waving my hand in front of her face.

She eventually snapped out of it and leaned in close. “W-Why would you go and do something like that...?!” she hissed into my ear. “H-His Grace even had to intervene. If things had gotten any more out of hand, you would have been in a lot of trouble.”
I guess she wasn’t the type to subscribe to the tank’s philosophy of throwing yourself into things headfirst. Still, shouldn’t she be praising or thanking me right now?
“It all ended well, though. The duke’s promise alone won’t do away with their discrimination, but at the very least, they won’t insult you behind your back anymore.”
This is what you’ve been dreaming of.
The Rabbit Baroness looked taken aback. “Did you... really do all that just for that one reason...?”
“Do I need some other reason?”
“That was far too reckless. If the duke had not stepped forward, things could have gotten so much worse. All the houses of Melbeth combined wouldn’t have been able to do anything to...!”
Her response left me feeling a bit disappointed. Did she think all of my accomplishments were pure luck? “I can’t say I agree with that.”

“...This goes without saying, but I think quite highly of you, Baron Yandel. The same cannot be said for all the houses of Melbeth, however. All eyes are on you, judging if you’re worthy of joining our ranks. If the others wind up deciding you’re unworthy because of this, then—”
“Enough.” What a pointless warning. That wasn’t even what I meant. “This had nothing to do with Melbeth.”
“...Pardon?”
“The same goes for the duke. Even if he hadn’t stepped in, the outcome wouldn’t have changed.”

The Rabbit Baroness couldn’t seem to comprehend what I was saying, so I kindly explained it to her. “You said it yourself, didn’t you? You told me to become indispensable to you. That’s why I requested a duel. You need at least one person like me making sure the others stay in their lane. Oh, and Baron Kypriot was the perfect target. His house isn’t particularly notable, and he doesn’t have the guts to back up his big mouth.”
“Wait! Then... are you saying that you took all that into account before taking action?”
“More or less.” I nodded, shocking the Rabbit Baroness.
Barely able to catch her breath, she then asked me another question. “But I don’t understand what any of this had to do with you becoming someone indispensable to us?”
Ah, that?
“During our talk earlier, what I heard was that you don’t think you have a way to change your circumstances.”
At that moment, I realized what this multi-racial alliance of nobles was lacking—something that only a tank main who had been through all sorts of trials and tribulations could clock.

“It’s not that you’ll never find a way out, though. There will always be a path forward, no matter what kind of situation you find yourself in,” I said firmly. “So if you find yourself on a path riddled with enemies you can’t get through, that simply means you’re missing something: someone who would tank an arrow for you and then still clear the road ahead after.”
The Rabbit Baroness remained silent as I finished. However, I could tell from her expression.
Okay. I think my self-promotion definitely had an effect.
At the end of the day, I was the one who got to decide my own worth.

After that, I continued my conversation with the Rabbit Baroness. She asked me all sorts of questions, so I must have left an impression on her. I felt like a door-to-door salesman selling dubious home remedies.

“You were right earlier...” As time went on, the look on her face gradually began to change as well. “What good has it done us to endure their constant snubbing for so long? All that time wasted... If only we’d pushed back even a bit each time, I’m certain we’d be in a much different position right now!”
There was no longer a meek herbivore in front of me. She had become a fierce beast full of determination.
“It’s about time Melbeth changes. Don’t worry, Baron Yandel. I will personally sponsor your clan and obtain guild approval. We in Melbeth need more people like you.”

With that, the Rabbit Baroness left the table. As I watched her go, a thought popped into my mind: Was she going to hide her teeth or bare them now? Perhaps the real difference between an herbivore and a carnivore lay simply in their mindset.
This is why your environment matters.
Anyway, was it because she was a rabbit? She was particularly easy to win over.
The table was now empty following her departure, and I continued to eat my meal, which had been put on hold for quite a while now. One by one, the other nobles began to meander over to speak with me.
“Baron Yandel, I heard that someone was speaking ill of you earlier. It’s only right that you would request a duel after that.”
“When I heard about what happened, I was utterly shocked.”
“Tsk, how are people still discriminating against other races in this day and age?”

I found it funny how quickly they’d changed their tunes and stopped viewing me as some simpleminded, lowly barbarian. Still, I pretended not to notice their posturing and continued happily socializing with them. From now on, networking was going to be an asset for me.
“Haha, thank you, everyone. If you invite me to your house, I will definitely make time to come and visit you.”
“Oh, is that so? I heard that you haven’t made an appearance since the banquet at Count Ferdehilt’s house a while back.”
“Back then, I was only a nobody, but how about we be friends now?”
“...Friends? Haha! With that zeal, you are most assuredly an adventurer. Yes, let’s be friends!”
Various people approached me for the same reason, but one of them happened to be Count Ferdehilt himself. He expressed his regret at being unable to marry his daughter off to me last time.
“If my daughter were to see you now, she would surely be pleased. It’s such a shame. She would have loved you...”
What the hell was he talking about? When he forcibly dragged his daughter in front of me back then, she’d been trembling.
“Haha, then I’ll take my leave. I’ll make sure to call on you soon, so don’t be a stranger!”
Even after Count Ferdehilt took his leave, I continued to greet and make friendly conversation with the other nobles.
All of a sudden, a middle-aged baron walked over to shake my hand. As he did, he shot me a furtive glance, slipping a note into my hand before disappearing into the crowd. A chill ran down my spine.
Don’t tell me that this bastard...
I was tempted to rip the note to shreds on the spot, but I hurried to the restroom to read it in private, just in case. When I read it over, I was glad I hadn’t torn it up.
In three days, I’ll meet you at the place where we first met.
—Your true friend
I didn’t expect this sort of cloak-and-dagger secrecy. Was this some kind of achievement for completing my status-raising side quest?
...Now I just need to meet with the marquess one last time.
I tore the note apart and swallowed it down with some tap water before leaving the restroom.

chapters.title: Chapter 446: Party (3)
paragraphs: The banquet began a little before noon and ended before sunset. The attendees were all the heads of their respective houses, so unlike other nobles who could spend their time fooling around, they had busy schedules.
People were already starting to leave just one or two hours into the banquet.

Most of them stayed just long enough to be polite and honor tradition before leaving. That said, since the banquet was packed with quite a few respectable and powerful individuals, others took advantage of the opportunity to actively network. But in the end, everyone wound up exhausted and left before sunset.
Is this what they mean when they say you start to act like a child when you get old? I thought to myself. It wasn’t like they were kids with a curfew.
Rattle, rattle.
As I stared out the carriage window, watching the royal palace grow smaller in the distance, I let my mind wander, imagining how convenient it would be to have a house in the capital someday.
In the end, I never got a chance to have a proper conversation with the marquess.

Unfortunately, my quest to talk to the marquess during the banquet had failed. I had gone over to his table to greet him, but there were far too many people around, and I didn’t want to stir up any more trouble with witnesses there. It was a shame, but I was ultimately forced to return to my table after exchanging brief hellos.
Though honestly, whatever the marquess might be thinking right now isn’t that important...

The important thing now was maintaining a certain balance. Whatever his intentions toward me may have been, now he wouldn’t be able to take action against me without thinking twice. I had to make sure that the line separating us couldn’t be crossed. However much power he may have, it no longer felt like he could do whatever he wanted to me.
Regardless, it’s great that I was able to join Melbeth.

My membership wouldn’t be made official until a few days from now when everyone could gather, but that wasn’t an issue. The bigger issue was what to do about Ragna now that she’d contacted me via note. If things went well, she could become the wild card I need in my confrontation with the marquess.
I sighed.
Having to think through things in this way made me a little depressed. It would have been better if she had just stayed a regular librarian. Then I could have enjoyed reuniting with her more.
Why does she have to be the marquess’s daughter?
On top of that, even Hyeonbyeol was connected to all this. The more I thought about it, the more it felt like my head was going to explode.
...Yeah. I’ll just have to figure things out after I meet up with her.
I heaved a sigh, and soon after, we arrived at the platform, where I caught a teleporter back to Ravigion. After changing carriages, I headed back home.
“You’re back early?”
“It ended earlier than I thought. Where’s Erwen?”
“She just came back as well. She should be washing up now.”

Oh, then we would finally get to see each other again after all this time. I went up to the second floor to bathe and change my clothes. When I came back down to the living room, Amelia and Erwen were sitting together on the sofa and talking. The two of them had gotten closer than I expected. Well, I figured after what they went through together in Ice Rock—
“Mister!” As soon as Erwen saw me, she jumped up and ran toward me.
I reached my hand out to stop her. “Erwen, I’m not just any mister.”
“...What?” Erwen was left dumbfounded by my rejection.
“I am Baron Bjorn Yandel.”
In response to my declaration, Erwen blurted out an awkward exclamation of her own. “Ah...”

It was so damn sad being a barbarian. I just couldn’t get used to it. If I were with Ainar, I would have been able to shout that out with a wide smile on my face, and she would have matched my energy perfectly.
“Bjorn, cut the crap and sit down.”
“...Okay.”
As soon as I took a seat on the sofa, our household meeting began. There were several items on the agenda to discuss since it had been a while, but among the items to address was Erwen.

“Fortunately, everything worked out. I returned my bow for now, and as for the money I used to buy the house... I promised to return it within the month.” Erwen spoke as if she had committed a grave sin. When I asked her why she was acting that way, she kept apologizing, saying it was her fault that we couldn’t keep this house full of precious memories.
“It’s fine. Why are you apologizing for that?”

To be honest, the thing I couldn’t understand was why the elves were okay with letting Erwen off the hook with just that. Was it because she was the only pureblood of her generation? I’d even been worrying that, in the worst-case scenario, her life might have been at risk.
It’s no exaggeration to say that this is actually the best possible outcome, but...
Unable to set my suspicions about how well things worked out aside, I asked Erwen to explain how things had panned out this way.
“When I was fighting with the elders, my uncle stepped in and helped me. I think that was the biggest factor.”
Because of her uncle, huh? Come to think of it, I did hear that her uncle was considered a hero by the elves. I hoped to meet him one day as well.

“But only a month to return all the money... That’s a pretty tight deadline.” Amelia was the first to bring up the logistical issues once Erwen finished explaining. “Even if we sell the house to pay off the debt, we’ll still need money to buy a new house in the future.”
“...Then why don’t we just buy this house ourselves?” asked Erwen. “What if we sell all the loot we got this time?”
“I’m not sure. Bjorn, what do you think?”

“Hm...” I thought it over and then offered my opinion. “I think it would be better for us to stay in an inn for the time being. Or we can rent a place each month, though it will be much smaller than the one we have here.”
“...I-I see.” Erwen seemed unwilling to sell the house, though she didn’t voice her opinion.

Even so, this was the time and place for some honesty. “Don’t worry too much. The house we live in now, the place we’ll move into—they’re all the same. They’re just places we will be staying in temporarily.”
When I brought up the idea of having Melbeth support us in buying some land and constructing a mansion, Erwen’s expression noticeably brightened. “Th-then you’ll really become Baron Bjorn Yandel!”
“Yeah, so tell me everything that you want added to the mansion in the future. You’ll be living there too, you know.”
Fortunately, judging by Erwen’s expression, whatever regrets she had about selling the house had now disappeared.
“You too, of course, Amelia,” I threw in just in case she felt left out, but for some reason, she just looked at me and let out a deep sigh.

I then went on to mention something I wanted for the new house as well. “...It would be great if we could make the navigator’s room a little bigger than it is now. And also, if we could get him a window with some sunlight.”
Our navigator had seemed quite depressed recently. Maybe some fresh air by the sea would do him some good?
“That should take care of the issue of our residence... Now, what should we do about exploring the labyrinth?”

As soon as we figured out what to do with the house, Amelia brought up the next problem: our party was currently incomplete. With Ainar, Erwin, Amelia, me, and our navigator, there was one spot open in our party of six. The problem was that we had no one to fill that vacancy. I was planning to have my entire party eventually join my clan one day, but I was wary of making a move prematurely. Plus, I didn’t think Ravien or the wizard Versyl Gowland would join quite yet.
Versyl said it would take at least a month before she could get independence, and Ravien said she wanted to take a break from adventuring for a while.

So in the meantime, we still had an open slot. However, taking a break for an entire month would be too much of a waste, so I made a decision. “I think it would be best if we just go by ourselves this time.”
“The five of us?”
“It’s not all that strange. Just a few years ago, five people was the norm.”
“That’s... true.”
“And we’re not going up to the seventh floor. We’re just going to explore the sixth, so it won’t be all that dangerous.”
“The sixth floor... All right. I’ll tell Rockrobe about it, then.”

That wrapped up our conversation about the labyrinth. Afterward, we had a simple dinner and chatted with each other before going to bed. Then the next morning, we all went to the nearest guild branch together to finish registering the members of our clan.
“Heh... thank you, Mister.”
I felt a spike of guilt considering Amelia carefully took care of all the documents instead of me. I felt like Erwen should be saying thanks to her instead.
Oh, I still need to fill the position of deputy commander.

When we first made the clan, I thought Amelia would be a perfect fit, but when I tried asking her, she rejected me in a heartbeat. Maybe she didn’t want to draw unnecessary attention to herself. That would make sense. After all, the name she was using, Emily Raines, was a pseudonym.
Then who should be the deputy commander?

I fell into deep contemplation. The position of deputy commander was a crucial one, so it would be best to register them and give them power of attorney sooner rather than later. That way, they’d be able to carry out administrative tasks without the commander present.
Ravien would have been the perfect deputy commander. She’s always been meticulous at handling annoying administrative things.
After we finished registering everyone, we went to a nearby restaurant to have a meal.
“Bjorn, are you going to Kommelby now?”
“No, I’m going to stop by the temple first.”
“...The temple?” Amelia tilted her head in confusion for a moment, but then quickly put two and two together. “You want to get rid of the Gachabone essence.”

“I don’t have to hide my appearance anymore.” Even then, though, I had still been debating whether or not to do it up until today. The Gachabone’s essence wasn’t all that bad. I did contemplate whether I should hold onto it until I started hunting for my next essence in earnest.
“Seems you have another reason as well.”

“Don’t Ainar and Abman still have my old equipment? Once I return to my original size, I’ll be able to use it. It would be a waste not to. Besides, we might stumble across a better essence while adventuring on the sixth floor. And when I finally get around to returning to the tribe, it wouldn’t be right for me to still look like this.”
“Hmph...”
Amelia for some reason let out a scoff at my answer while Erwen lamented the change.
“Then... does that mean you’ll be as big as you were before?”
“Yeah.”
“But I like the way you look now...”
I couldn’t understand her strange preferences at all. Where in the world would a slim build like this be considered good? “Then my condolences.”
After heading to the temple, I entered alone and went through the process of removing an essence.
[The Essence of the Gachabone that was absorbed into your soul has been removed.]
[Your Sixth Sense has decreased by -40. Your Physical Resistance has decreased by -15. Your Dark Resistance has decreased by -30. Your Accuracy has decreased by -45.]
My stats fell.
[Your Bone Density has decreased by -110.]
My height grew.
[Your Control has increased by +30.]
My mind cleared.
[Your Luck has increased by +50.]
And, most important of all, my luck improved a bit.
Stretch.
It took some time for me to stretch and get used to my new-old height. I quickly pulled on some clothes and checked myself out in the mirror.
Phew. I’m finally back in my normal body.

I’d already known, but it really hit me at this moment just how big I was. For some reason, I wanted to yell out the names of my ancestors, but I managed to hold the impulse back with superhuman self-control. I was in a temple, after all.
[Bjorn Yandel
Level: 7
Physique: 1390.55 (New -54.5)
Spirit: 521.3
Special Ability: 2197.65
Item Level: 6285 (New -2020)
General Combat Power: 5680.75 (New -575.58)
Acquired Essences: Orc Hero - Rank 5  Ogre - Rank 3  Bayon - Rank 3  Storm Gush - Rank 3  Vol-Herchan - Rank 3 / Deep Sea Giant - Rank 3]
The reactions of the two people waiting for me outside the temple were like night and day.
“Heh, Mister! This side of you is cool too! It’s just like the first day we met!” Erwen complimented my new appearance despite her open disappointment earlier.

“...You definitely looked better before.” Amelia, on the other hand, didn’t say much but still managed to stab me in the heart with each word. But then, in a strangely quiet murmur, she said, “But... in a way, this might be better.”
“Hm? What do you mean?”
“I’m saying it might be better now that you’re ugly.”
“I’m not ugly. Don’t you think I look more manly now?”
“Pfft...”
“...Are you laughing at me?”

When I noticed her laughing at me, I was immediately reminded of the importance of disciplining children. However, she was my precious colleague, not a child I was raising. As the head of our clan, this was probably something I should overlook.
...Thankfully my Control stat went up. Otherwise, things might have taken a turn for the worse.
In any case, we made our way to Kommelby as originally planned. The members of our squadron didn’t all live in District Seven, but we decided to meet there since it was the city center.
“Here we are.”
We walked into the building that Versyl had rented for the day and were greeted by friendly faces.
“Ohhh, he’s finally here. Our Baronet... No, I guess I should call him Baron Yandel now,” said Melend Kaislan.
“...Oh, you look different.”
Lilith Marrone, James Calla, Sven Parav, and the entire crew—all of the ones who managed to survive starving and freezing at Ice Rock—looked awed by my change of appearance.
“Versyl, where are Akurava and Ravien?”
“They said they couldn’t make it.”
“But everyone else managed to come.”
“Well, I’m sure it’s because we’ve all been curious.”
That made sense. I was curious myself, so they must have had it even worse than me.
“What about the perimeter?”
“Don’t worry about being spied on. I purposely chose a place with no windows, and I made sure to activate a Voice Control spell. Just in case, I’m also actively scanning for any use of magic.”
As expected of a wizard, she was good at her job. I should ask if she had any opinions on being the deputy commander when she joined my clan later.
“Baron Yandel!”
“Why are you calling me Baron? Just call me Captain.”
It’d been a while since we last reunited, so we had a good time catching each other up on how we were all doing.
“So... when are we planning to do it?”
Then, it was finally time to discuss the ceremonial opening of the sub-spaces we stole from the Order of the Rose.
“When I first opened it to store our bags, I thought there was nothing inside.”

I’d actually thought the same, but not too long ago, I discovered the truth: to take out a hidden object, you needed to adjust the sub-space’s magic formula accordingly. Well, at least according to what the wizard Versyl had discovered and told me.
“All right now, let’s open them one by one. I’ve already prepared plenty of neutralizing spells, just in case.”
Even I was a little nervous about opening them.
“Well then... let’s see what’s inside.”
“I was disappointed at first, so I’m looking forward to seeing what’s hidden in these.”
“Phew... I guess all of you have also been waiting to open yours? I didn’t even think about opening mine yet because I was afraid someone might be watching.”

What on earth were the Order of the Rose trying to hide by going to such lengths for their security? There was no way to know what it could be. So, just to be on the safe side, I’d decided to erase the Gachabone’s essence earlier today even though I could have put it off.
“Then... is everyone ready?”
“Yeah, let’s open it!”
Here’s hoping we’re lucky today.

chapters.title: Chapter 447: Party (4)
paragraphs: Since we didn’t know what would come out of the Order of the Rose’s sub-spaces, we decided to open them one by one.
First up was the wizard Lilith Marrone. “There’s a box...?” What came out was a small wooden box, just big enough to hold a book or two.
“You can go ahead and open it. There’s no traces of other magic on it.”
As soon as Versyl gave the okay, Marrone slowly opened the box.
“That’s...”
There were uneasy murmurs from all the members as they looked over Marrone’s shoulder to see what was inside. The contents were much different than expected.
“There’s some money, a few counterfeit IDs, and a picture...”
“Who is that a picture of? Maybe her family?”
“With how many fingerprints are on it, I would assume so.”
What was this?
“L-Let’s open the next one, then!”
While the excitement may have died down a little, the others and I didn’t relinquish all hope just yet and resumed opening the sub-spaces.
“It’s the same. Some money and IDs... and there’s a weird pill here as well?”
The pill found in the second box was all too familiar to me and Amelia. “It’s a drug called Blessing of Lethe.”
“...Do you recognize this, Ms. Raines?”
“Yeah. It erases the memory of the person who takes it. An alchemist in Noark invented it, though it seems the royal family has also discovered how to make it.”
“This... might come in handy someday. How many memories does it erase?”
“Hard to say. It looks a bit different from the one I remember. Maybe it’s been improved?”
“I see... They are all different sizes, so I assume the bigger the pill, the more memories it erases. But I’ll have to examine it further in my lab.”
We wound up going through the third, fourth, and fifth sub-spaces, and before we knew it, the entire opening ceremony was coming to a close.
“...It’s that Blessing of Lethe pill again.”
“Looks like there’s some kind of poison here too.”
“That’s a powerful acid used to destroy any and all traces of something like, for example, a corpse...”
The sub-spaces that were meant to be treasure chests were sadly a disappointment. Well, it wasn’t like everything within them was useless, though. There were even some Blessing of Lethe pills.
“Sir Kaislan, would you mind taking a look at this notebook?”
“It’s... a list of spies sent out by the royal family.”

One item from the sixth sub-space was a list of people who were operating as undercover informants for the royal family. I was once again struck by the unmitigated power the palace held as I read over the names.
“By the looks of it, this is probably just a mere fraction of all their sources.”
“There are so many... yet you’re saying this is only a fraction of them?”
“Look at this. The informants listed here are all centered around one noble in particular. That suggests the owner of this sub-space was on a special mission related to that noble.”
“You’re saying that all these names are the undercover agents needed to carry out a mission... related to one single individual?”
“Well, that’s just my guess,” Kaislan concluded.
I couldn’t help but agree. What other possibility could there be? “I heard that the royal family has eyes and ears everywhere, but I never imagined it would extend this far...”
Silence hung heavy over the room at that. Everyone there felt it—the sheer magnitude of the power that we would have to contend with in the future.
“Either way, this is good,” I said when the silence became unbearable, trying to sound nonchalant. “Versyl, I’ll hold onto this list. I might need to use it one day.”
After agreeing to set aside the list for me, we moved on.
“We’re finally on the last one.”
Their eyes lit up at my words. While the opening of the sub-spaces hadn’t yet lived up to our expectations, every one of us wondered if this one might be different.
“...This was her sub-space, right?”
We couldn’t be sure whether Six of the Order of the Rose was a commander, deputy commander, or just a regular member, but one thing was clear. That day, she had taken on the role of commander.
“It’s another wooden box.”
Still clinging to hope, we all prepared ourselves to open the final box.
Money, ID, a Blessing of Lethe, and... a single piece of paper within an opened envelope.
“Oh, wow...”
It was an order issued by the royal family to exterminate the expedition team at Ice Rock if they made it back alive.
“We can use this.”
It wasn’t a bad find.
Once we finished opening the sub-spaces, we all pulled out the equipment that we had taken from the labyrinth.
“What are we going to do with all this equipment?”
“First off, we should be careful and take our time getting rid of the equipment we got from Noark. We can use the money for our clan fund going forward.”
“That makes sense...”

In the end, most of the loot acquired during the expedition was handed over to me. They also gave me the authority to deal with it as I saw fit. Surprisingly, no one voiced any complaints. I was glad that they put so much trust in me, but at the same time, it worried me.
Damn. It would be so easy to scam all of them.
What if it were someone else seated at the helm and not a good, responsible barbarian like me?
“Yandel, what should we do with the equipment from the Order of the Rose? If we try to sell it off, it will surely catch the eye of the royal family.”
“Ah, when it comes to those, I think we should scrap them and re-forge them first. They might be dangerous to sell, but the raw materials are far too valuable to waste.”

Mystium was a metal as valuable as arc, so we would melt that down. As for the grade-five material Ogre leather, we could cut it into pieces and use it on other equipment. Of course, that wouldn’t leave us much to work with. Even if all the daggers were melted down, there wouldn’t be enough mystium to forge even a set of armor, and most of the leather would be scrapped in the process of repurposing it.
“We can decide what to do with the raw materials later, so if anyone wants some for themselves, please bring a convincing reason for the group the next time we meet.”

The mystium would be perfect to make myself a shield, but as the leader, I shouldn’t be greedy. It was only right to use the money we gathered as a group for the betterment of the group. Though, to be fair, it didn’t seem like any of them cared much either way.
“There’s something else I wanted to ask about instead. I heard that you founded a clan a few days ago... When would it be possible for us to join?”
“Ah, Versyl actually made a timeline for that, so she’ll be going over that briefly now.”
“Oh, really? Then when would I be able to join?”

“You should be able to join in about three months, Ms. Marrone. I think it would be best for you to retire from your current position on the grounds of friction with your superiors. If you think of a better reason, though, please let me know in advance.”
“Well then! What about me?”

“Sir Kaislan... you will be the last to join us. After all, you hold quite a high position already. We should wait until the royal family has somewhat lost interest in us before you move. I’d say joining a year from now would look the most natural.”
“I see...”

“Mr. Calla, didn’t you mention that you were released from your clan not too long ago? You should take a break for a couple of months and make a point of expressing your interest in joining another clan. There won’t be any other clan willing to accept you, anyway. You looked for another place to go, but couldn’t find anywhere willing to take you in, so naturally, you joined Yandel’s clan since you had already met previously on another quest. If you do that, then it will look as natural as possible and won’t pose any risk of attracting suspicion.”
“And if another clan accepts me... what then?”

“Then you ask them to recognize your previous position as deputy commander. If you demand a higher position, then they will end up rejecting you out of hand. You can trust me on this. I used to work in Personnel Management.”
James Calla said nothing in response, his spirit visibly crushed.
“Ah, and Sir Parav...”

Versyl’s briefing went on like that for some time. It was quite impressive to watch. Was it because she had the personality of a wizard, the experience of a former deputy commander, and had come from the modern world? She was extremely efficient.
I wonder what type of work she did on Earth.
The briefing eventually came to an end, and the next question was directed at me.
“Then how much does Ainar know about our situation?”
“She doesn’t know anything. So watch what you say when you meet her later.”
“I see...”
“Either way, the clan already has two members of the Seven Powerful, so once we join... Well, I guess it won’t be easy to avoid attracting attention, no matter how much we don’t want it, hahaha.”
“Hm, you think you’re already at that level, Parav?”
“Oh, uh. Not at all? No, I mean, I might not be that famous, but maybe just a hair behind? I... think.”
“I’m curious about the other member. Auyen Rockrobe, was it? I’ve never heard of them before. Are they trustworthy?”
Since the topic of our navigator was raised, Amelia replied in my stead. “He’s trustworthy. I can vouch for him.”

More questions of a similar vein were pumped out, but eventually, the topic changed to the banquet held to celebrate my elevation in status. I told them that we were going to team up with Melbeth and transitioned the discussion into the next step of our plan. However, since I couldn’t explain everything in detail right now, I kept things simple and only gave them broad strokes.
“For as many enemies as we have, they all have enemies of their own. And as the saying goes, the enemy of our enemy is our friend.”
Creating a clan and building up the reputation of my noble house would serve as protection as we gathered more allies. That was the crux of my plan.
All for the sake of getting back at those bastards who left us in hell.
After we exhausted the serious topics, our conversation regained its lighter, more comfortable tone.
“What happened to you, Sir Kaislan? Did they interrogate you when you returned?”
“Not exactly. They asked me some questions, but I wouldn’t call it an interrogation. They didn’t use any verification magic either.”
We talked about what was going on in our day-to-day lives.
“Ms. Gowland, do you happen to have any medicine that helps you sleep?”
“I do. I’ll give you some if you need it.”
“Are you not going to ask me why?”
“Well, the truth is that I can’t sleep all that well either. Not since that day.”
Some people turned to each other for help.
“Your name was Ms. Marrone, right? What did you use to paint your nails?”
“Oh, these? Aren’t they pretty? It’s popular among wizards these days. Would you like to try it yourself, Tersia?”
Others took the time to just talk about their hobbies. It was interesting to watch. Just a month ago, before we entered the labyrinth, we were all strangers to each other.

I glanced around before sitting on the sofa in the corner alone. Unlike the banquet, there were no fancy dishes or expensive wine. We simply rented an empty building to chat with each other. Still, this was much more enjoyable than a dazzling banquet.
“I should get going.”
Like always, the good times flew by. By evening, everyone began to trickle out one by one. When I got ready to leave with Erwen and Amelia to head back home, the party officially came to an end.
Two days later, I left the house bright and early, ignoring the suspicious gazes of Amelia and Erwen.
“You’re going to the library? This early in the morning?”
I had only just remembered.
In three days, I’ll meet you at the place where we first met.
There was no time written down on the note. Ragna always did seem like the type to forget important details like that.
I sighed as I made my way through the streets of District Seven, but eventually arrived at the National Library of Ravigion.

When I first woke up in the body of a barbarian, I’d spent most of my days here. By this point, it had become something of a childhood home for me. However, as soon as I arrived, I froze. There was a notice on the front of the library that it would be closed today.
...I never imagined this would happen.
What now? Should I just wait here? If I did, then at least I wouldn’t accidentally miss her.
Step, step.
The sound of shoes hitting the pavement interrupted my thoughts, and I looked up to see a woman slowly approaching. As soon as we made eye contact, I couldn’t help but flinch.
“It’s nice to meet you, Baron Yandel.”
From her black hair to her black eyes and black skirt, the woman was decked out in black from head to toe, aside from her white shirt.
“Please follow me. The countess is waiting—”
“Wrong.”
“...Pardon?”
I stared at the woman who was tilting her head in confusion, then said simply, “I’m not a baron today but a commander. A few days ago, I founded the Anabada clan.”

If she was surprised by my out-of-the-blue statement, she didn’t show it. Her response merely came packaged with a business-like smile. “I see. From now on, I will be more mindful of how I address you, Commander Yandel.”
“Thank you. For some reason, I just felt like being a commander today.”
“You... felt like it? What do you mean by that?”
“Oh, don’t you think a commander sounds stronger than a baron?”
“...I see,” she awkwardly agreed despite clearly not understanding the difference.
I decided to give her a nudge. “Do you happen to know what Anabada means?”
“To my knowledge, it’s a word from an ancient language that means ‘a group of savage beasts,’” came her immediate reply.
“R-Right... I guess you already knew that?”

I must have looked like a depressed barbarian who had just lost the opportunity to show off my knowledge. The woman pretended not to notice as she opened the locked library door. “Come this way. The countess is waiting for you.” She walked in front of me, and I followed close behind with a smack of my lips.
Step, step.
Going off first impressions alone, I couldn’t help but think she was Hyeonbyeol.

chapters.title: Chapter 448: Expanding (1)
paragraphs: Step, step.
Our footsteps echoed through the empty library.
“Woman, what is your name?”
“...I am Harin Savy.”
“Your name is as unique as you look.” Anyone listening would consider that comment borderline racist. Of course, that was only if the speaker were a regular person.
Being a barbarian sure is great.
My fellow barbarians and I had complete immunity when it came to being seen as discriminatory.

Perhaps that was why Harin answered me without taking any apparent offense. “You’re not the first to think my name and appearance are unique. There aren’t many people in the city who have blood from the East Continent as thick as mine.”
“Your ancestors were from the East Continent?”
“Yes. My ancestors were merchants who were lucky enough to be in this city when the calamity began. Thanks to that, they were able to survive and avoid the devastation.”
“...I see.”
It was a concise explanation that left me no room to ask questions and all the more puzzled for it. Normally, evil spirits wouldn’t have this much knowledge about their families and ancestors...
But if she’s Hyeonbyeol, that rule of thumb might not apply.
Still suspicious, I proceeded with my next question. “What is your relationship to Countess Peprok?”
“I’ve been lucky enough to be by her side for a little while now.”
So she hadn’t been with her that long. I was starting to grow even more convinced, but we unfortunately arrived at our destination before I had time to interrogate her any further.
“I will be taking my leave now.”
“All right. Thank you, Harin.”
With that, she politely left.

I set my suspicions about her identity aside for now and focused on the present, where I was met with a familiar figure with blue eyes and blue hair. Unlike before, however, she had a distinctly noble air about her. Maybe it was the way her hair was twisted into a flowy updo, revealing her neckline.
“It’s been a while, Bjorn Yandel.”

The way she talked was the same. Her unusual appearance threw me off for a moment, but it didn’t take long for a sense of familiarity to settle in. “Yeah, it’s been a while, Ragna. No, I guess I should be calling you Countess Peprok now?”
“I see you’re still making jokes like always.”

I wasn’t trying to make a joke, though. I was seriously asking. Well, given how she didn’t address me as Baron Yandel, I had a feeling I knew what kind of relationship she was after. “And you’ve changed a bit.”
“Is that so...?”
Was it because of the hair?

Ragna spoke the words in a mumble as she fiddled with her hair. Even taking her new hairstyle and outfit out of consideration, she still had a more mature vibe about her than before. She’d always seemed somewhat anxious back then, with an abrasive exterior that hid a soft side underneath. But now... how could I put it? She seemed much more approachable, yet somehow more serious at the same time.
“I never believed it was possible. I can’t believe you’re really alive, Yandel.”
“I couldn’t believe it when I heard about you either. I knew you had some story or another, but I never imagined you would turn out to be the daughter of the prime minister.”
“...What?”
Ragna’s face froze for a moment, and then she frowned. “What are you talking about? I’m the prime minister’s daughter?”
“...You’re not?”
“No! I mean, I don’t think so. Unless... Well, that would answer some of the questions that I have.”
What the hell was going on here?
“First, let’s set things straight. Yandel, where did you hear that I am the marquess’s daughter?”
“If you’re worried about revealing your source, at least tell me how certain you are that it’s true. I beg of you.”
“I was certain it was true, at least until right now.”
“That means the information came from a reliable source.”
Hm? Was that how she saw it? But I didn’t even know Deer’s real name or face.
Though I was a bit taken aback by this sudden plot twist, I tried to stay calm. “If possible... do you mind telling me your story? Then I might be able to offer you some advice.”

Ragna took a moment to think over my request but cautiously began to speak soon after. “All right. It’s not like I can hide it forever. More importantly, it isn’t something I feel needs to be kept hidden.”

Those words alone were enough to prove just how much Ragna had changed. In the past, no matter how many times I asked, she would refuse to talk about her backstory, looking glum all the while. It was clear that she had matured quite a bit since the last time I saw her.

As I was admiring her growth, Ragna slowly began to tell me her story. “When I was a child, there was one thing my governess used to tell me all the time: ‘Ragna, you must live a quiet life out of the public eye. That is the only way you can repay him.’ As you know, I’m not actually from the House of Peprok. My father simply had me borrow the name of a fallen house so I could live a quiet, independent life.”
“I see...”

“I don’t know who my father is, but my governess told me he is an extremely powerful noble, so if people knew I existed, it would lead to a lot of trouble. Ah, and she said that even though he couldn’t meet me in person because of that, he still loved me and was watching over me. I loved my governess, but I never believed her when she told me that he loved me. Even so, I still chose to listen to her. I lived a quiet, unobtrusive life and gave up on pursuing magic as anything more than a hobby. I had a lot of fun learning magic, but for some reason, I kept drawing other people’s attention when I used it.”
So that was why a wizard of her caliber, whose magic was rank-five or higher at such a young age, had been working at a mere library.
“I really did love her. I was willing to make some sacrifices to heed her advice.”
“Is the governess you’re talking about... named Litaniel?”
“Yes, that’s right.”
No wonder she was only listed under the name Countess Ragna Peprok. Her full name wasn’t actually her real name.
“Then what about your mother? Do you know what happened to her?”
“I heard she died the day she gave birth to me.”

“I see...” After quietly taking in Ragna’s story, most of the questions I had about her were answered. However, the thing of real importance here wasn’t the past but here on out. “So what happened after that?”
What happened to Ragna while I was stuck in the past? Why had the woman who wanted to live a quiet life away from prying eyes suddenly become a countess?
“Not long after you were declared an evil spirit, Marquess Tercerion approached me with an offer.”
“...The marquess did?”
“Yes. He offered me the chance to revive the fallen House of Peprok if I worked for him. I went and accepted his offer.”
That was completely unexpected. “Why would you do that? You didn’t even realize he might be your father at that point.”

“I, of course, refused him at first. Even though my governess had already passed away, I still wasn’t comfortable entering the public eye so openly, but... I changed my mind after hearing what the marquess wanted from me.”
“Can you tell me what that is?”
“He wanted me to step into the limelight so that we could begin the process of accepting evil spirits as regular members of society.”

For a moment, I found myself unable to respond. So that was why Ragna had revived the National Incorporation Bill. Still, there was a critical thing about this that didn’t make sense—why would the marquess suddenly make such an offer in the first place? And...
“Why did you change your mind after hearing what he wanted?”
Why would Ragna suddenly want evil spirits to be accepted? It didn’t take long for her to explain.

“It’s because I know.” Her answer was simple. “I know that there are also good people who are evil spirits... and I didn’t want my friend to be remembered in that way.” As I stared at her, struck speechless, Ragna avoided my eyes, her voice growing smaller. “Is that really so strange?”
I heaved out the sigh I’d been holding in and finally replied, “Yeah, that’s strange.”

To be blunt, Ragna and I weren’t all that close. We were something in between acquaintances and friends—nothing more, nothing less. We were happy to see each other when we had a chance to, but it wouldn’t have been strange for us to drift apart and lose contact entirely.
Right, that should have been the case...
“I-I see... Then maybe I was—”
Before she could misunderstand me any further, I blurted out, “But thank you, Ragna. I mean it.”
There was nothing else I could say to her.
We sat in awkward silence for an untold number of minutes. Eventually, I took the plunge and broke it.
“The letter you gave me. It didn’t have a time written down.”
“Oh... well... I forgot to write one down because I was in a hurry.”
Just as I thought. I smiled as I asked her another question. “Come to think of it, it seems you’ve been waiting here for a while. When did you get here?”
“...I didn’t wait that long. Don’t worry.”

Well, if she said so. In any case, the topic meandered to the closure of the library today. I was shocked to see that the entire library was closed. It wasn’t completely absurd to imagine that a countess might be able to rent the library for a whole day, but still...
“I didn’t expect you to do something like this.”
“No good comes from attracting unnecessary attention.”
“Hmm, then you could have just asked to meet me somewhere else.”
“That’s true... but I thought it would be nice if we could meet here again.”
Truthfully, I felt the same way. “So you decided to pull some strings?”

I’d said it with deliberate levity to tease her, but Ragna merely looked confused at my question and, surprisingly, brazenly fired back. “Yeah. Is there a problem? It’s fine, isn’t it, to act selfishly like this at least once in a while?”
“Oh, uh, yeah...” I was left speechless again.

It didn’t take long for the tension to ease up once more as we continued exchanging small talk. We even talked about Shavin Emoor, a mutual friend of ours. After laughing and having a good time together for a while, we eventually returned to more serious topics.

“Ragna, I have something to ask.” To be honest, I hadn’t come here today intending to ask her this. At first, I wanted to recruit her to our side so I could use her to get more information on the marquess. But... “Have you ever considered giving up your position as a countess?”
After hearing her story, I couldn’t bring myself to ask her that. All I wanted now was to help Ragna escape this power struggle.
Of course, my hopes were dashed right away. “I don’t know why you’re asking me that, but no. I have no intention of giving up my position.”
“What makes you say that? Because the marquess could be your father?”
“That’s irrelevant to me. I will now spend the rest of my life irrevocably tied to that man regardless.”
“That doesn’t explain why you insist on being a countess. I’ve returned and cleared myself of any suspicion. There’s no reason to go this far anymore, right?”
“Yes, there is, because this is the most important thing I could do.”
“...I don’t understand.”
“I’ve spent all this time combing through countless cases, all to help prove that evil spirits aren’t inherently evil.”
“...So you’re saying that whether or not I’m in the equation, you’re serious about this goal of yours?”
“You could think of it that way, yes.”

I’d never thought Ragna was doing all of this on a mere whim, but now, I could see just how serious she was about it. I sighed. I needed to change my approach. “Then why don’t you distance yourself from the marquess, at least? He doesn’t seem to have any intention of passing the agenda you are pushing, anyway.”
“...What do you mean?”
“I heard that when you brought it up at the royal assembly, the marquess was the one who was most opposed to the bill.”

“I... can admit that I found that odd too. However, he later explained to me that the foundation of my policy was too weak. If I tried to push it any further, the other nobles would attack me instead.”
“...What?”
“If I can come up with a better policy in the future that can also persuade some of the other nobles, he said he would openly support me.”
“And you believe that?”
“Why should I not? This was the reason the marquess approached me in the first place.”

“But...” Sure, that was how it looked from the outside, but no one could tell what the marquess’s real angle was. Ragna had been doing fine on her own, so why would he suddenly approach her with a proposal to accept evil spirits under the National Incorporation bill?
“Yandel, you seem to hate the marquess. Is that the case?” Ragna’s question was sudden, but unlike before, it carried a hint of scathing disapproval beneath the surface.
...Why did she say she would be with him forever? Is that because he might be her father?
Blood ties weren’t always so easy to sever, even when done willingly. Damn, this made things even more complicated.

“It’s not that I hate the marquess. It’s just that... I think his reasons for approaching you seem a bit suspicious.” I hurriedly tried to offer some sort of explanation before my relationship with Ragna fell apart.
Fortunately, Ragna seemed to believe me. “I see. I know all too well what you’re worried about... but don’t worry. I can take care of myself now.”
I was jealous that she could say that.
I should worry about myself first...
After all, I couldn’t say the same for myself yet.
It was just barely noon when I parted ways with Ragna and left the library. We had been busy chatting when she was suddenly pulled aside.
“Harin, did the marquess call for me?”
“Yes. He said he will explain why when you meet.”
“...Why are you looking at me?” I asked. “Don’t apologize. I was going to leave soon anyway since I was getting hungry.”
“I’ll be in touch soon, then.”
“All right. Like I said earlier, don’t tell the marquess that you met with me.”
“Of course. I don’t want the marquess to use our relationship for political gain. Oh, and don’t worry. Harin is also good at keeping her lips sealed.”
With that, Ragna left with Harin, the secretary whose ancestors hailed from the East Continent. I watched as the two of them slowly walked away.
Harin...

While talking with Ragna, I also acquired quite a bit of information about the woman named Harin. The two of them met about a year ago at this very library. Even after quitting her job as the librarian, Ragna frequently visited to do research for the National Incorporation bill. That was how she ended up meeting Harin and growing close to her.
“The more I got to know Harin, the more I started to like her. I realized she was even more talented than I first thought, so I hired her to be my secretary.”
That was the story Ragna told me of how the pair came to be.
Harin... Just as I suspected, she must be Hyeonbyeol.
I was now certain that Harin was Hyeonbyeol. Well, strictly speaking, there was no one else it could be since Ragna had no other assistants aside from Harin. The problem was...
