After leaving Shavin Emoor’s house, I headed straight to the dwarf’s forge. Fortunately, even though I didn’t make an appointment, I was still able to grab a meeting with him.
“Bjorn! What are you doing here?” Just as I thought, he was working today.
“I have some equipment to repair. Also, I want to show you that thing I mentioned a few days ago.”
“I see. Give me your equipment first. I guess you want me to repair these before your next expedition?”
“Of course.”
I handed the equipment that the former chieftain damaged to the dwarf, then went to the hallway to wait. A few moments later, he came back out and led me to the attic on the second floor.
“I usually take care of the administrative side of things here... It might be a bit uncomfortable for you, though.”
“It’s fine. I can just crawl.”
“It’s not that bad...”
“Don’t get mad at me for needing to lay down to talk to you.” Even at its highest point in the center of the room, the ceiling reached no higher than five feet off the ground.
As I lay down on the floor, the dwarf sighed as he sat on a sofa made for dwarves. “So, where’s the thing you mentioned before?”
“Ah, here it is,” I said, taking a big box out of my sub-space.
The dwarf swallowed hard at the sudden tension in the air. “Where did you get that?”
“It would be best if you don’t know.”
“...I-Is that so? I shouldn’t have asked, then.”

The dwarf examined the pieces of equipment we got from Noark one by one, his eyes wide as they flitted around frantically. For a second, I was worried, but he seemed more excited than anxious. Well, he was a blacksmith at the end of the day, and his attic was now filled with Numbers Items and even some items made from grade-three materials or higher. Even though our contract had been made in haste, I’d be losing 5 percent of the profits from this equipment to him.
“Take all the time you need, it’s fine. Just make sure to sell this equipment as discreetly as possible.”

“Oh, um, yes. I should...” With how his eyes were darting over all the gear sitting across the room, it was hard to tell if he was even listening to me. I figured there was no better time than the present, though, so I quickly took out the next box.
“Oh, was there something else besides all of this?!”
“I don’t want to sell these. I want you to use the materials to make new pieces of equipment instead. Turn the daggers into ingots and use the leather to replace the fabric on our other items.”

“That won’t be a problem. But what the hell is it?” The dwarf went over to the chest and peered inside, eyes brimming with curiosity. “I can’t believe you have Ogre leather... and even mystium? I heard that 90 percent of what’s on the market goes straight to the royal family. Where on earth did you get such a precious thing?”
Well, you see...
“Look carefully.”
“Hm?” I waved at the mystium dagger from where I was reclined on the floor, and the dwarf took a closer look at it. As soon as he recognized its origins, he yelped, “Th-th-this, this is—!”
“Not so loud. Somebody will hear you.”

“...This is the Order of the Rose’s equipment!” He quickly shoved the dagger and armor back into the chest when I motioned for him to shut up. With how much this dwarf screamed and shouted, what if someone came up to check on us? “B-Bjorn! Th-this is nuts. I don’t know how you got your hands on this, but... this is extremely d-dangerous!”
Even as he trembled from head to toe, he tried to offer me heartfelt advice. However, my reply was nonchalant. “Didn’t you expect that I would bring you stolen goods?”
“Yes, of course, but not something connected to the royal family!”
“So you’re not going to do it?” I asked bluntly.

He couldn’t even muster a proper response. “I, uh...” He glanced over all the equipment once more, trying to come up with something coherent to say. I could see his unwillingness to part with our hoard.
“If you don’t want to, just forget everything you saw here today. And make sure to burn the contract we signed a few days ago.”
As I reached for the equipment, he smacked my arm away. “...I never said I wouldn’t do it.”
“Hmmm? But you just said this was nuts?
“I still think it is, but... it’ll be fine as long as we don’t get caught!”
This dwarf was shaping up to be a great business partner after all.
It was June 28th of year 157, two days before the labyrinth opened again and this extremely busy month came to an end. However, I still had work to do.
“You’re here!”
First thing in the morning, I headed over to meet Shavin Emoor at her house for her first day of work. I expected her to be alone, but there were three others with her. “Who are these people?”
“Ah, they worked in administration with me. You said the more the merrier, right?”
“Yeah, I did, but... you were able to get three more already?”
“When our boss lost the election for commissioner, we were all forced to leave our jobs.”
Hm, I didn’t expect that to be why. “But how were you able to convince them to help?”
“It wasn’t hard. Baron Yandel’s clan is the talk of the town, you know? Everyone wants the chance to be a part of it.”
“...The clan?” I echoed, sensing that something was amiss.
Before I could comment on it, however, the people standing beside Shavin quickly began to introduce themselves.
“I-It’s an honor to meet you, Baron Yandel! My name is Rick Anderson. I used to work in civil engineering.”
“I’m Mary Jane... I worked in the same department as Ms. Emoor.”
“Shepherd Ramden. It’s an honor to meet you.”
Fortunately, there were no Hanses.
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel. I look forward to working with you,” I said by way of a brief introduction.
Our conversation turned to travel as we rode in the carriage.
“Wow... This is my first time riding in a noble’s carriage.”
“I... didn’t even know nobles rode in separate ones.”
“It makes sense. After all, ordinary citizens aren’t able to use them.”
“...It’s so convenient that they wait for you and take you directly to your destination.”
“Haha, just become a noble like me, and you can enjoy these things too.”
“No way... how could people like us become nobles?”
The vibe in the carriage was pretty lively.
“Anderson, you said you worked in civil engineering before, right?”
“Yes! Yes, I did, Your Lordship!”
“What exactly did you do there?” I asked, grilling each of them in turn on what their jobs entailed. We talked for a while, and I answered any questions that they had as well.
“But... this carriage is headed for the outskirts?” asked the confused Shavin Emoor as she looked out the window. “Is your clan house located outside the walls?”
“Clan house? What are you talking about?”
“...Oh? I heard that you recently made a clan. Isn’t that why you needed help with administrative duties?”
Only then did I realize why something seemed off.
No wonder none of them asked me questions about what their jobs would be.
I quickly corrected the misunderstanding. “Shavin Emoor, the place where you will be working isn’t the clan.”
“Huh? Then where are we going...?”
“The barbarians’ holy land.”
“Come again?” Shavin Emoor shook her head like she suspected she had misheard me. At that moment, the carriage at last arrived at our destination.

“For now, let’s get off.” I stepped outside, and they all followed after me in a speechless daze only to be faced with a massive wall. Well, I doubted they’d ever had any reason to come all the way here before.
“Behel—aaah!”
As soon as the gate opened, we were welcomed by a loud battle cry. The humans looked around, completely dumbfounded, as I shoved them into the holy land. Warriors came by to greet us on our way.
“Human! A human! The chieftain has brought back a human!”
“Ohhh!”
“Two men and two women!”

The administrative personnel stuck close behind me, trembling like they had just entered a lion’s den. It wasn’t until we’d walked down the long forest path and reached the chieftain’s tent that they finally came to their senses.

One of the people Shavin brought along gulped as he nervously asked me, “Th-then...what are we going to do?” It was Rick Anderson, a rank-six civil servant who had worked in the civil engineering department and the man who might just become our ace in the hole in our quest to pull this entire land redevelopment plan off.
I looked at him and kept my response brief. “All the work that uses numbers.”
That, of course, included selling the land.

chapters.title: Chapter 454: Barbarian Revolution (3)
paragraphs: When people come together, an organization forms—even with just four people.

Once we’d gathered four people to take care of the administrative side of things, I quickly dumped the full backlog of work on them to divide and conquer. They divided up the tasks by what best suited their specialties. Among the four of them, Shavin Emoor was due the highest credit.
“Mary, you’ll be overseeing the data organization and analysis on your own,” said Shavin. “For now, let’s focus on looking over all the data that the former elders left behind.”
“...A-Are you really sure I can manage that? I’m looking at some of the data, and it’s hard to understand any of it. I can barely even make out the handwriting.”
“Just do your best. I’ll come by and help you too.”
“All right...”
Mary Jane was in charge of statistics and managing the files.
“Mr. Ramden, I’ll have you take care of the coming-of-age ceremony taking place in a couple of days.”
“The... The coming-of-age ceremony...?”

“I know you’re new to it all, but it’s just a small event within the barbarian tribe. I’m sure you’ll handle it just fine. But if there’s anything you aren’t sure about, you can ask Ms. Fenelin. That’s all right with you, right, Ms. Fenelin?”
“R-Right! Of course! You can ask me!”
“...Then what should I do after preparing for the coming-of-age ceremony?”
“Once we have the data analyzed, please write up a budget. Not a yearly one—just month by month for now.”
“...All right.”
Shepherd Ramden was in charge of financial planning and management.
“Mr. Anderson... I don’t have to tell you what to do, right?”
“Yes... I’m in charge of land...”

“It seems that nothing has been done for this project yet. So for now, head into the woods and survey the land. We’ll be laying new roads there eventually, so try to clear a path if possible. Oh, and make sure to also set some land aside for a place to raise the children. We should go ahead and make them a new nursery.”
“...Isn’t this basically an entire city plan?! I-Is it really okay for me to be in charge of something so important?”

“I’m giving you the authority, so you can do whatever you want. Don’t worry, we’re not going to tackle the entirety of the holy land right away. We’ll start selling pieces of land from the outskirts, so you can just focus on that for the time being.”
“...I’ll do my best.”
Rick Anderson was in charge of transportation, infrastructure, and urban development.

“Right now, we’re just dividing the tasks amongst ourselves, but when we hire more people in the future, we’ll function as a proper organization. When that happens, you’ll all be the head of your respective departments.”

And naturally, Shavin Emoor would be the head of all of it. Hm, perhaps this was the place where all her passion for work came from. I never expected her work ethic and skills to be so impressive. She didn’t complain about starting from nothing and quickly assigned the staff tasks in accordance with their skill sets so they could tackle the largest problems ahead.
She’s an even better employee than I thought she’d be...

I’d only ever seen her as a woman who visited the dessert shop whenever she could. But as I stood on the sidelines and watched the barbarians’ administrative team slowly take form, it struck me that I’d had no idea she had this hidden side to her all this time.
“Excuse me...” Mary Jane, who was in charge of data, carefully raised her hand. “Wh-when do we get off work...?”

Instead of answering, Shavin glanced my way. I guess she felt she didn’t have the authority to answer that. Unfortunately for them, time was money right now, so I quickly responded, “Why would you get off work?”
“...Pardon?”
“Are you all not right in the head? If you work through the night, your salary will be doubled!”
They all stared at me blankly, unable to comprehend what I was saying.

Shavin Emoor had to step in on my behalf to interpret. “Right now, we have a lot of work to do in a short amount of time. It’s not like we haven’t worked overtime before, and luckily for us, we’ll be properly compensated this time. We’ve all rested long enough, anyway. It’s not so bad to be busy with work again, right?”
“...Right.”
With that, the barbarians were headed for new horizons.
After forming the administrative team, I headed over to the former chieftain’s tent. There was something I hadn’t been able to ask him during my last visit.
“Bjorn, son of Yan—”
“It’s Chieftain.”
“...Right, Chieftain. What is the matter?” He got straight to the point.
“I’d like to know more about Balkan.”
“Ah, the man behind your first title.”

Balkan, son of Shalik, also known as Kagureas, was a barbarian hero who died twenty-one years ago at the age of fifty-five. I’d only just recently found out his real name. Before that, I had always assumed he had died so long ago that there was no need to look any further into him.
“So what are you curious about?”
“Everything about him.”

“It’s going to be a long story. Go sit or lay down.” The former chieftain sighed in an obvious display of irritation but chose to answer me anyway. “By the time I underwent my coming-of-age ceremony, Balkan was already a famous warrior within the tribe. Back then, it was an undisputed fact that he was the strongest.”
“How strong was he?”
“I would be no match for him the way I am now.”
Well, with praise like that, it was safe to assume that he was also much stronger than I currently was.

“Some people thought he was ‘humanized’ because he didn’t socialize with his fellow warriors, but in my eyes, Balkan was more of a warrior than anyone else. The only thing he was interested in was becoming stronger.”
“Wasn’t everyone like that back then?”

“Haha! That’s true. Those sure were the days! Unlike today, there used to be hundreds of adventurers capable of exploring the eighth and ninth floors. The six races were all practically racing against each other to see who could get furthest into the labyrinth, and it was common for each one to lend their Genesis Treasure to their greatest warriors, who stood at the front lines. Balkan was one of those warriors.” Like everyone his age, the chieftain seemed to like to talk about the Golden Generation.

“But that all ended when a dimensional collapse wiped out most of the top adventurers, right?” I asked. Titana Akurava was also a member of that generation and had experienced the catastrophe firsthand and survived. Maybe that was why, even after all this time, the royal family was still looking into the cause of the dimensional collapse and enforcing strict control over the labyrinth.
“It was a terrible tragedy, but that had nothing to do with Balkan’s death.”
“Then how did he die?”
“Nobody knows. One day, he and his comrades entered the labyrinth, and they never returned.”
“I see. And since our Genesis Treasure returned to the tribe when he disappeared, no one looked into it.”
“Do you think he might still be alive?”
“Maybe he did something similar to what I did?”
“Pfft, haha! Well, knowing when and how to doubt is a good skill to have as a warrior.” The former chieftain seemed to disagree with my theory, but he didn’t criticize me or try to change my mind.
“Speaking of the Genesis Treasures, I heard that our tribe wasn’t the only one who lost theirs.”
He sighed. “I can’t believe you already know about that too. Is this what it means to have a noble’s information network?”
I’d actually heard about that from Baekho Lee, but there was no reason to tell him that. “Then who else lost theirs?”
“To my knowledge, the elves and the dwarves.”
“I see...” I probed further, asking if he had any other insight into the day of my coming-of-age ceremony when each race’s Genesis Treasure was stolen. Sadly, I didn’t get the answer I wanted.
“I can’t say for sure. From what I know, nobody has any idea where the Genesis Treasures are.”
Damn, I was hoping he would know something.
“Oh! But now that I think about it, there’s something I should tell you about the Genesis Treasures.”
“What is it?”

“Several years ago, a mystery person left a letter for us while the old chieftain was away. The letter predicted that there would be a war for the sacred relics in the near future and that someone would steal our Genesis Treasure on the first day of the third month of Year 153.”
Well, about that...
Ignorant of the truth, the former chieftain continued to explain. “Isn’t that fascinating? Our ancestors were surely looking after us that day! That’s what the shaman told us, anyway!”

I didn’t know why the shaman said something like that, but since we were on the subject, I decided to ask, “So what happened after the chieftain saw the letter?” I’d honestly assumed they had just never gotten my letter, but by the sounds of it, the barbarians did in fact read it. So what happened?

The ex-chieftain gave me the rundown. “At first, we thought the letter was just the young warriors playing a prank. However, when the War of Sacred Relics actually happened, the old chieftain realized that the letter was truly special.”
It did make sense that they wouldn’t believe it until war broke out. “Then what about the Genesis Treasure? If you knew about the theft beforehand, how was it stolen?”

“I’m not sure. I made sure we were well prepared to protect it, but when you and the others left for the city after your ceremony, the warriors that stayed behind in the holy land all fell unconscious.”
“And you didn’t share the letter with the other races?”
“No, we didn’t do that.”
“Why not?”
“Do you really think they would heed a warning from our ancestors?”
Yeah, fair enough.
The former chieftain then explained to me in detail what measures were taken to prevent the Genesis Treasure from being stolen.
They did all that, yet nobody knows what happened on the day of the coming-of-age ceremony?

What really happened that day? Now that I was the chieftain, I was going to have to dig deeper. If I could get a hold of our Genesis Treasure again, I would surely have the upper hand against Baekho Lee. After all, it was an end-game piece of equipment.
“But what happened to the letter? Do you still have it? I would like to read it myself.”
“I’m not sure? I heard the former chieftain had it, but he never gave it to me. He must have lost it.”

“I see...” If the letter had been lost in the past, then it was best to leave it at that. I asked my final question. “But what happened to the shaman? When I asked his apprentice about him a while ago, he told me that he retired.”
“Oh, if you’re talking about the old shaman, he got sick, so he’s bedridden.”
“Bedridden...?”

“He’s alive but in a coma. I figured we should just kill him since he wouldn’t wake up, but his apprentice begged me not to, insisting that he would wake up soon. So I’ve been leaving them alone for now.”
Hm, so that’s where he’s been.
“If you’re done asking questions, get out. I’ve been talking to you for so long that I’m getting hungry.”
“All right.” I could see his frustration with all my questions mounting by the second, so I hurried out of the tent, but not before asking where the old shaman’s tent was located.
Swish.

I pushed open the flap and stepped into a dark tent that was inundated with the thick, heavy scent of incense. I walked through the unpleasant, gross-smelling smoke clouds hanging in the air and walked over to the bed where the former shaman lay, still as a corpse.

“...Ch-Chieftain?!” The apprentice I’d met once before burst into the tent in a panicked flurry. “Y-You can’t! I-I still have so much left to learn from him! S-So please don’t kill him! I’m making sure to work extra hard to pay for his share as well!”
Uh... His tent was just on my way back, so I figured I’d say hello.
“I beg of you... he may be old and dying, but he’s still my precious teacher!”
In the end, I felt pressured to excuse myself from the tent and head back.

Having Shavin’s help in building an administrative team gave me some breathing room, but there were still plenty of things I needed to get done before my next quest. I was now a baron, the head of the Anabada clan, and the chieftain of the barbarians. I not only needed to prepare for the labyrinth but also care for my tribe.
I’m sure next month will be even busier...

Next month, I’d also have to sit in on a meeting with Melbeth, an association of non-human nobles. Then after that, I’d have to put my nose to the grindstone and start selling pieces of the holy land.
It’s nice that Melbeth is holding the meeting the day after the labyrinth closes...
If they’d decided to hold the meeting this month instead, I didn’t know how I would have found the time to take a day off and attend.

I heaved a sigh. The thought of my constantly growing workload was making me depressed. What else could I do, though? These were all quests I needed to complete, and skipping them was not an option. It was too late to turn back now.
“Chieftain, everything is ready,” Ainar called into the tent, interrupting my brooding.
It was already time. I quickly stepped out of the tent and walked with Ainar to our destination.
Fwooosh!
Deep within the forest, there was an open clearing illuminated not by LED streetlights but, instead, by flickering torches. Every corner of it was filled to the brim with muscular barbarians.
Step.
This was the very same place where I first opened my eyes to this world.
Step.

As I stepped into the clearing, which had a pile of various weapons sitting slightly to the side, the eyes of our young warriors all zeroed in on me. In those eyes, I saw a mixture of both excitement and nerves.
...What a strange feeling.
I looked around at the young warriors before shouting at the top of my lungs, “Congratulations, young warriors!”
Just like I had heard in the forest that day.
“As of today, you will leave the holy land and be reborn as true warriors!” There was no need for overdone explanations, so... “Now, step forward one by one and choose the weapon that suits you!”
Oh, but I had one more thing to say to them this time, of course.
“You will each be given two potions and leather boots too!”
It was time to enter a new era.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

The young warriors let out a roar of approval overjoyed that they would be the first generation to benefit from this new system. I didn’t purposefully rile them up, but thanks to that, it was easy to spot him.
There, standing in the middle of the shouting crowd, was a warrior who was nervously glancing around with a terrified look on his face.
Gulp.
As soon as I laid eyes on him, I bit my lip without even realizing it.
The odds are 100 percent.
That right there was a newbie.

chapters.title: Chapter 455: Barbarian Revolution (4)
paragraphs: The day I first awoke in this world still stood out in my mind, more vivid than any other memory. I was left reeling by the fact that I somehow understood a language totally unfamiliar to me, yet there was no time to waste, as I also had to quickly make sense of my situation and plan accordingly. That had been my grand entrance to the world of Dungeon and Stone.
Now, I was struck with a sense of déjà vu.
Right there... is where he died.

I still remembered his name: Oreum, son of Kadua. There was no telling the sort of life he might have lived before entering this world, but less than five minutes after opening his eyes, his throat was sliced clean open.
And there were many more like him.

Having seen the records passed down to me as the new chieftain, I now knew that an average of one player had been executed at each coming-of-age ceremony for the past ten years, though those numbers had been in decline. It seemed the once-popular modded version of the game had lost popularity.
But I guess there are still people playing the game.
It was such a shame.
Damn it, why did we ever play that damn thing?
None of this was our fault, of course. There was only one person to blame.
That old bastard screwed us.
It was Auril Gavis, the creator of Dungeon and Stone.
[You have reached the Abyss.]
[Tutorial complete.]
He was the true mastermind behind the kidnapping of countless players, with only those two paltry sentences to show for it.
If he was going to make a tutorial, he should have done it right.

The newbie’s expression brought back old memories. Well, they weren’t all that old if you ignored the time I got trapped in the past, and I figured there would continue to be even more warriors like him in the future.

“Everyone, quiet!” I boomed. The young barbarians quickly reined in their excitement and shut their mouths, allowing me to proceed with the ceremony. This month’s ceremony, however, would be unlike any other held in the past. I would use it as a chance to help the players hidden among the warriors. There might even be another newbie lurking unseen right now.
“Macal, second son of Putil!” I walked over to the young warrior myself and placed my hand on his shoulder as I called his name. “Come forth and pick your weapon!”
“I will!” the young warrior blurted in excitement, apparently moved by his chieftain’s warm support and encouragement.
“A two-handed ax! Excellent!”

I kept encouraging the young warriors by walking over to them and calling their names out in turn. Whenever I could, I tried to give the newbie hints to help him quickly adapt to the situation he was in.
“As of today, you are a warrior. May the blessing of Rafdonia be with you!”
Eventually, it was the turn of the newbie I’d been keeping an eye on. “Vector, third son of Kiltau!”
When I clamped my hand on his shoulder, I could feel his entire body trembling beneath my palm. I pretended not to notice and said, “Come forth and pick a weapon for the beginning of your journey!”
“...I will!” Compared to the other warriors, his response was slower and quieter.
But at least he figured out what to do.
Since he was imitating the other warriors off the bat, I had a good feeling that he would survive as he continued to accumulate experience—
Huh?
As soon as I saw the weapon he picked, I couldn’t help but let out a laugh. “A shield...”
The newbie flinched at my involuntary reaction, probably worried that he had made a major mistake.
I had no clue this would be a shield barbarian newbie.

I pushed past his frozen form and approached the display where the shield hung, then reached over and grabbed something else for him to take along. “Take this.” With my authority as the chieftain, I decided to provide the warriors who picked a shield with an additional small, one-handed hammer.
“Vector, third son of Kiltau, you are now a warrior!”

He was a bit taken aback, probably because this aspect of the ceremony was different from the game, but after taking the free hammer, he quickly returned to his spot. Even though he tried to act unfazed, his expression betrayed open panic.
I can’t really blame him. He probably needs some time alone to get his thoughts in order.
I turned my attention away from the newbie and continued with the ceremony until, eventually, the final warrior chose his weapon. It was time to move on to the next step.
“Warriors!” Before they headed into the city, however, I had prepared a brief speech. Well, it was more of a quick review than a speech. “Answer after me! Who are the only good plunderers?”
“Dead plunderers!”
“What do we think about the Adventurers’ Guild?”
“We don’t trust them!”
“What do we do when we meet a Hans in the labyrinth?”
“Say no! If you don’t want to die, scram!”
The reason I was having this quick review session with the young warriors was simple. The rest of them may have all practiced and memorized what to do, but there was a newbie among them who hadn’t.
“Now then...” There was one last piece of information I needed to review with them. “What do you do if you find out an ‘evil spirit’ has been living in the body of one of our people?”
It was the most important piece of information for any player’s survival.
“We kill them!”
If a player gets caught, they die.
“Open the gate!”

As soon as my voice rang out, the gate that separated the holy land from the city began to open. The young warriors who grew up in the holy land, dreaming countless times of the adventure that awaited them outside these gates, began to let out shouts of excitement.
“Rafdonia!”
Originally, this would have been the moment I sent them off with a final word of encouragement. However, I decided to lead the young warriors into the city myself.
“...What? The chieftain is going to lead us?”
I needed to go into the labyrinth too, so we were going the same way anyway.
“Behel—aaah!”
“We will surely become great warriors like him!”
The warriors were once again overjoyed after hearing that their chieftain would be personally guiding them. While admiring their innocence, I quickly led the warriors to the center of the district.

“Good evening, Baron Yandel,” someone called out to me. We followed the voice over to a guild wizard waiting in the agreed-upon spot, ready to cast a binding spell on the young warriors. As I clustered them into groups of three or four, some of the warriors began to question me.
“...But Chieftain! I thought it was tradition for us to go on our first expeditions alone!”
“That’s right! I’ve heard the stories ever since I was little!”

Tradition be damned. That shitty tradition was exactly why so many of our warriors had been killed and looted during their first expedition. How many of them could have been saved if we had just abandoned the old ways?
Before I could raise my voice to yell at them, someone beat me to it. “You fools!” It was our newest elder, Ainar. “Bjorn, son of Yandel, is our chieftain now!”
“He’s the chieftain, yeah, but what about tradition—?”
“From today on, everything the chieftain says will be tradition! And it’s our duty to do whatever he says!”
It was a bit authoritarian, but the logic was sound. After all, the barbarian race had its own systems in place to handle dissent.
“If you disagree with these new traditions, then become the chieftain yourself! Understand?”
In other words, if you had a problem, then put your fists where your mouth was. The young warriors had grown up under that very system, so thankfully, they were quick to accept it.
“...That makes sense!”
All right, then that was the end of that.
“Excuse me... About the payment...”
“Here you go.” After he finished casting the spell, I paid the guild’s wizard for his work. “Good work. I look forward to working with you again next month.”
“Ah... Of course, Your Lordship...”

Since the wizard had been forced to work overtime and come all the way out here to meet with a bunch of barbarians, it was no surprise he looked displeased and exhausted. Unfortunately for him, he was going to have to meet with us next month as well. I had personally gone to his branch of the guild to ask for a favor, after all. How could a mere wizard working there say no?
“The labyrinth!”
“Ohhh! It’s r-really here!”
“It’s like something is pulling my body toward it!”
In any case, after the payment was finalized, I led the warriors over to Dimension Square, and with that, my duties as chieftain had come to a close. There was nothing else to say other than:
“Go, warriors!”
The second I gave them permission, the young warriors pushed their way through the crowd, ran toward the portal, and threw themselves in.
“Hurraaah!”
Behind me, Ainar let out a laugh as she watched. “Bjorn, why do you look so worried?”
It felt like I was sending my kids off to school for the first time. As long as they came back alive, our tribe would become even stronger, but...
“Don’t worry. We came back alive, didn’t we? And we were dealing with way worse odds than them!”

It was a truly barbarian consolation despite her reminiscing tone. Strangely enough, it made me feel a lot better. The barbarian way of disciplining and training their kids had been too hardcore for much too long. I didn’t want things to be so difficult for our young warriors, though I also didn’t want to coddle them either. After all, the fastest way to grow was by facing adversity. Only in those moments when dread and fear were pounded into your bones by experience were you able to avoid making the same mistake in the future.
After sending the warriors off into the labyrinth, we walked around Dimension Square until we found the rest of our party.
“Mister!”
“You’re late.” Amelia glanced down at her watch before glaring daggers at me.

Auyen Rockrobe, our navigator, stood next to her and greeted me with an anxious look on his face. “You’re here, Clan Leader!” It had been a while since I’d seen him decked out in full gear. “Thank you for letting me follow you into the labyrinth again.” His voice was full of sincerity. It made sense given how he’d been stuck in the basement for the past few months.

Perhaps it was because he tried to loot me before, but I didn’t feel any sense of guilt or pity when I looked at him. The only good plunderer was a dead plunderer, so we needed to be harsh with him, in the beginning, to remind him of his place. Otherwise, it would have been impossible to trust him to watch our backs.
“Amelia.”
“Don’t worry. I’ll keep an eye on him in the labyrinth.”

We were openly talking about it right in front of him, but Auyen acted like he couldn’t hear a word. He didn’t bother saying we could trust him or that he would do a good job either. He simply kept his mouth shut.
He’s definitely able to read a room.
It remained to be seen whether that was a good or bad thing.
“Um... Bjorn? Shouldn’t we get going now?”
“Right. Let’s go.”
We hurried over to where the portal was gradually decreasing in size.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
Thus began the first quest of the Anabada Clan.
The Crystal Cave was bathed in a faint purple glow.
“This is the northern side.”
“So we’re in the north.”
“We’re over by the Goblin Forest.”
As soon as we entered, three of us spoke simultaneously—me, Rotmiller’s apprentice, Amelia, who was a scout, and Erwen, who had learned the basics of being an adventurer from her sister.
A beat of silence followed, and we were suddenly confronted with the awkward reality of having a team of five people that included three scouts.
Amelia cleared her throat while Erwen protested, “I was a bit faster than her.”

“Hahaha! Are you kids? Why would you compete over that?!” Ainar let out a loud laugh, and Erwen glared at her, making no effort to hide her displeasure. Of course, glaring at Ainar had no effect on her at all. “That’s a good look in your eyes, Erwen!”
Surprisingly, Erwen shook her head silently instead of firing back. She stared at Ainar like she was some incomprehensible creature and her best option was simply not to engage.
Ainar, on the other hand, just shrugged her shoulders and tilted her head, confused. “I’m saying you look happy, unlike the last time I saw you!”
I flinched at that. The last time they saw each other... She must have been talking about the day Raven had told me about. I thought Ainar had just stepped on a landmine.

“...That goes without saying.” However, in an even more surprising twist, Erwen wasn’t angered by her comment. If anything, she seemed somewhat embarrassed given how she was avoiding any and all eye contact.
Right, Erwen did always have this meek side to her...
It was a good thing that Ainar came with us, though if needed, Amelia would also have been more than able to handle Erwen herself.
It feels like Amelia has been a bit more relaxed these days too...
Either way, it was time to put those thoughts aside.
“All right, let’s get going! I can’t wait to explore the labyrinth with Bjorn again. My heart’s been pounding like a drum!”
Ainar took the lead as I tried to hold back a grin.
“Ainar, why are you going that way?”
“Huh? You said we were in the northern part, so I was heading north. I know the basics now too! I can even read a compass!”
I was proud of her growth over the past few years. However...
“We aren’t going to the Goblin Forest today,” Amelia interjected.
Ainar tilted her head. “...Oh? Really? Then where are we going? The Land of the Dead?”
“The Rock Desert. Hm, that’s strange. I’m sure I shared the plan with you in advance...”
“Ah, sorry! I forgot!”
“...I see.” Amelia, faced with her first encounter with a real barbarian, was rendered speechless.
I quickly joined the conversation to smooth things over. We couldn’t waste any more time here arguing. “Well, let’s see...”
Who should play the role of scout? Should it be Amelia, just like last time? Or should I have Erwen do it this month?

It was a tricky question to answer, but wanting to make the most of our time, I quickly came to a decision. “I’ll be the scout!” The main goal of today’s expedition was to get familiar with each other, and for that to happen, I needed to minimize the chances of anyone’s feelings getting hurt.
“What? But Mister, you don’t have to go out of your way to—”
“What are you saying?!” I quickly cut Erwen off and took the lead. “As a clan, it’s our job to all pitch in and share the workload. So let’s get going now!”
We had a lot of work to do this time around, though Ainar probably forgot all of it already...
At least she won’t be suspicious of me.
This actually worked out. Our previous team hadn’t been able to take advantage of the full extent of my game knowledge because I was wary of Raven.
[You have entered the Rock Desert on the second floor.]
Now, it was time to go all out and kick things off with a low-rank raid.

chapters.title: Chapter 456: Raid (1)
paragraphs: Dungeon and Stone was, at its core, a farming game. The main goal was to strengthen your character by amassing experience points, consuming essences, and acquiring equipment. Normally, you had to build up your stats by consuming essences so you were strong enough to go up to the next floor and get more XP. You only earned XP the first time you killed a new type of monster, after all. The natural consequence of that was that if you couldn’t get your hands on higher-quality essences, you wouldn’t be able to farm for new points on the next floor.
But oddly enough, even though I’m already level seven, I haven’t gotten stuck once.

That was largely due to the fact I’d had the rank-seven Corpse Golem, rank-five Vampire, and Orc Hero essences off the bat. Those alone made it a breeze to clear the lower floors and amass XP. By the time I reached the middle floors, I’d been lucky enough to upgrade to an Ogre essence through the Labyrinth of Larcaz. Ah, and it also helped that the royal family was at war. Otherwise, I would have been busy farming for the Bayon and its Transcendence ability right about now.
In that sense, this is actually the first time my progress has been stalled...

It had nothing to do with a lack of ability on my part, though. It was just that I needed to get past the seventh floor to get stronger, and that place had turned into a war zone. Honestly speaking, if I invested just a bit more time and effort in the clan, it wouldn’t be long before we would be capable of farming for a Bellarios.
“Bjorn, how much longer do we have to wait? The monsters here are too weak! This is boring!”

The majority of our expedition this month would be a low-rank raid. I’d thought it through over and over again, and every time, I arrived at the same conclusion. We would use this time to hunt the monsters that we didn’t have under our belts to make sure everyone on the team was on equal footing. Any essences we found along the way, we would consume. All of us had one empty essence slot at the moment.

“Be patient. Like I told you earlier, this is where the essence you need appears.” The monster we were currently hunting would drop a useful essence for Ainar. It wouldn’t be the best one to have come the home stretch, but for the time being, it would help her become 30 percent stronger.

“But still...” Ainar hesitated, not entirely convinced. Well, it was probably hard for her to believe that a second-floor essence would be of any use to her now, so— “Isn’t it just a rank-five monster?! Why can’t we keep going up instead? I want to show you just how strong I am now, and I can only do that if a stronger enemy appears!”
Ah, so that’s the issue.
I ignored her whining and carried on chewing my jerky.
Amelia was taking a break from auto-farming a group of monsters when she suddenly called out to me. “Yandel. We have company.”
“Yeah,” Erwen jumped in, “I can also sense them coming this way. There are—”
“Twelve of them.”
I sighed. It was a pain to listen to these two constantly cutting each other off. Why they felt the need to compete over something so trivial was beyond me.
“They’ll be here in about two minutes.”
“All right.”

With that update, we waited until the team of twelve adventurers slowly emerged from the darkness, though they were more of a clan than a team. On top of that, they were well-equipped for adventurers wandering around on the second floor.
The man I assumed was their captain stepped forward to speak the moment our eyes met. “...So there are others here.”

It looked like they had the same goal we did. The monster we were hunting was certainly famous enough to warrant more interested parties. However, since we were both after the same thing, the solution to our problem was simple. “Yeah, we were here first. So get lost.”
We’ll be taking these grounds as ours now.

When I claimed ownership of these hunting grounds, their leader shifted his eyes to our party, looking at each of them in turn. In the past, if I had seen someone do something like that, I would have been on high alert. Now, however, I wasn’t worried in the slightest.
“That’s a shame.”
Well, you being disappointed isn’t my problem.

“I guess we should just consider ourselves lucky that we got to meet a celebrity. May the blessings of Rafdonia be with you, Baron Yandel.” They turned around without another word, just as the three parties we had run into before them had done.
With that, our hunt resumed.
[You have killed a Sandworm.]
[You have killed a Sandworm.]
[You have killed a Sandworm.]
[You have killed...]
Once we’d killed all the Sandworms, a monster unique to the Rock Desert, the conditions were finally met.
“Whoa, the ground is shaking!”
The entire desert started to shake like there was an earthquake.
Shwaaaaaa!
A sandstorm whipped up, blocking our escape route, and in its center, a massive worm burst from the ground with its gaping maw wide open.
[A Death Worm has appeared.]
The rank-five Death Worm was a monster that was unique to the lower floors. I always made sure to hunt it down for the much-needed experience points.
“Gyeeeeeek!” With only its upper body out on the surface, it let out a terrifying roar.
“Behel—aaah!” Ainar leaped high into the sky with a roar of equal ferocity. Unfortunately for her, she was a beat too late.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Power of the Abyss.]
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
Before Ainar could strike, Amelia’s dagger and Erwen’s arrow pierced the Death Worm, causing it to collapse in the sand.
[You have killed a Death Worm. EXP +5]
[High-rank Mutant Bonus. EXP +1]
I had no idea we would defeat it in less than a second.
“It was weaker than I thought?”
“Mister! I killed it for you!”
“What are you talking about? Didn’t you see my blade cut it down before your arrow even hit it?”
“But it was my arrow that blew its head off.”
“Aghhh! What the hell was that? I’ve been waiting all this time for this?!”
I sighed. The essence didn’t drop.

After defeating the Death Worm, we exited the Rock Desert and returned to the Crystal Cave on the first floor for one reason and one reason alone. It had already been three months since we’d entered Green Coal Mine. This would be our chance to enter a rift on the first floor.
Come to think of it, I haven’t looked around here yet.

It suddenly struck me that I hadn’t explored every corner of this place. In fact, I’d basically skipped the entirety of the lower floors. The only other rifts I’d been in were the third floor’s White Temple and the fourth floor’s Doppelganger Forest. The second floor had practically been a footnote in my quest, to the point where I hadn’t even opened or gone into its rift yet.
I wonder if I’ll be able to go this time...
It was hard to say. Even though we made plans to enter the second floor’s rift, there was no guarantee we’d be able to. After all, rifts weren’t something you could simply enter whenever you pleased.
“Hahaha! It’s been a while since I’ve been here!” Ainar exclaimed the moment we arrived at the Great Sage’s statue in the center of the Crystal Cave. “It’s kind of nostalgic! Don’t you think, Bjorn?”

It was no wonder she felt like that. When I came here three months ago, I had that very same feeling. This was the place where I had entered my firstrrift with Ainar and met Raven and that dwarf, not to mention the place we’d suffered for days under Noark’s onslaught.
But I guess that was all three years ago now...
While I’d been trapped in the past for most of it, even I could sense just how much time had passed. Nevertheless, to me, it felt like it all happened only a few days ago.
Clink.
As soon as we placed the rank-eight mana stone we got in the Rock Desert on the altar, the portal opened and we hurried inside.
[You have entered the first-floor rift.]
Beyond the portal was the final rift on the first floor, the only one left for me to clear.
“This is the Iron Grave...”

Erwen used one of her spirits to illuminate the dark corridor before us. It felt as if we were entering one of those pyramids from those documentaries that always played on random channels late at night. It went without saying, however, that this was no pyramid.
The walls of this place were all made of metal.
“Mister, what language is this?”
“I have no idea.”
“Hahaha, don’t you think Aruru would have loved this place?”
“Let’s stop chatting and keep moving.”

There was no reason to waste any more time. As we moved forward, Ainar suddenly insisted on leading the way. Amelia and Erwen also pushed for her to stand in the front alone, as they were eager to see her new skills in action. To be honest, I wanted to see them myself.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

Ainar took point and quickly cleared the way. Usually, the Iron Grave was supposed to be cleared by dismantling the traps along the corridor, but all of that was meaningless against someone like Ainar. As long as you had the strength to pull it off, simply running over each trap was much easier than dismantling them one by one.
“Ainar, take a left!”
“Raaaaaah!”
I yelled out directions from behind while Ainar pressed onward. She stepped over all the traps as she sliced the monsters up with her sword.
Crash! Wham! Slam!
It was the kind of incredible performance you’d expect from a greatsword master.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Repeated Slash.]
[The same area has been struck twice. Blast Scars has activated.]
It was a basic combo that used Repeated Slash to its fullest potential, and showed just how much she’d grown over the past few years.
[Due to Mandel Oil, Blast Scars’ firepower has been doubled.]
On top of that, she threw in a fire-type passive skill from the rank-five monster Smug’s essence.
[Residual Heat has activated. Additional damage will be dealt in proportion to the damage done.]
Now came a rank-four skill that resulted in a 50 percent bonus to Damage Resistance if fire damage was dealt to multiple enemies in a short enough time frame.
Boom! Smash! Clash!
Each swing of Ainar’s sword brought with it dozens of explosions. I trailed after her, watching with pride.
I didn’t expect her to actually gather all of the essences I mentioned.

I felt like a teacher watching my students come back from vacation with all their homework done. I had recommended essences to her that would raise almost all of her Resistance stats evenly. That was why she was completely fine even after stepping on the traps or getting attacked by monsters, and even if she did get hurt, the wounds healed quickly.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Wings of Greed. Her Natural Regeneration has significantly increased.]

Because of the way Ainar was built, most of her damage dealing came from her passive skills, meaning she didn’t eat up much Soul Power. The notable exception, of course, was her finishing move, Repeated Slash. But as a result, even if she had to constantly heal herself, she had very little risk of draining her stores entirely.
[Ainar Fenelin has killed a rank-eight monster. Her Soul Power is restored in proportion to the monster’s rank.]

Thanks to the Satiation ability granted by the third stage of the Slayer Imprint, she was able to replenish both her MP and HP as she fought. And by the looks of it, she’d even reached the sixth stage.
[Ainar Fenelin is currently fighting a rank-eight monster. Her Physique increases in proportion to the monster’s rank.]
I never expected her to have Combat Study already. It made you stronger the more you fought—an ideal ability for barbarian warriors who were constantly trying to grow more powerful.
...It must be fun being able to fight like that.

I watched Ainar cheerfully throw herself at monsters on the front lines and felt jealousy creeping in, but I quickly squashed the feeling before it could grow. Shield barbarians were incredible in their own right. After all, Dungeon and Stone was a home for anyone who mained as a tank, since you couldn’t get anything done in-game without a proper tanker. You could do a raid without priests, wizards, or archers, but a main tank was irreplaceable.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
We continued to follow behind Ainar, left with nothing to do. As time went by, the experience we gained from hunting began to steadily pile up.
[You have killed a Mummy. EXP +1]
[You have killed an Iron Cavalry. EXP +3]
[You have killed a Viridian. EXP +2]
[You have killed the Eyes of the Guardian. EXP +2]
[You have killed an Iron Lizardman. EXP +3]
[You have killed a Riddler Gatekeeper...]
[You have killed...]
As we ran through the rift, I made sure to gather any hidden items to share with the rest of the party.
[You have taken a Mercurial Liquid. Your Mana Resistance has permanently increased by +3. This effect cannot be stacked.]
[You have taken an Iron Blessing. Your Physical Resistance has permanently increased by +3. This effect cannot be stacked.]
Since this was only a rift on the first floor, the stat increases were minor, but they would grow considerably as we continued to farm for them.
[You have entered the Iron Tomb.]
Even after taking the time to gather all the hidden elements, it didn’t take long for us to make it to the boss room—only about three hours in total.
Only three hours to reach the boss room while soloing in the front... That’s definitely fast.
Ainar had more than proved herself, but she wasn’t satisfied and demanded to fight the boss alone.
[You have killed the Iron Ildium. EXP +4]
[High-rank Mutant Bonus. EXP +1]
[Guardian Kill Bonus. EXP +3]

The boss battle wrapped up quickly, and the moment it ended, everyone honed in on the light that began to shine as the monster’s body disappeared. At the end of the day, we were all greedy adventurers, after all.
Shaaaaaa—
There was no essence, and the same went for any rift Stones, which could be sold for a good chunk of change.
“...A flower?”
“Huh? Is there a Numbered Item that’s a flower?”
However, in an incredibly rare event, a Numbered Item had dropped—No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck.

chapters.title: Chapter 457: Raid (2)
paragraphs: “Oh! What a strange looking—”
“Stop!” I yelled as soon as Ainar bent down to grab the flower. A sigh of relief escaped me when she jumped back, flustered.

“Wh-what is it?! I didn’t do anything!” Ainar quickly defended herself, confused about what she might have done wrong. I didn’t mind her tone, though. I didn’t shout at her to scold her. “I-Is there something strange about this flower?!”
Ignorance wasn’t a sin. Well, at least not for barbarians.
“That’s No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck.”
The only person to react to the name was Amelia. “...Something precious has already shown up.”
Yeah, it was precious, all right. It was an item not even money could buy.
“What is it?” Erwen asked.
“Hm...” Amelia hummed. “It’s one of the 109 Treasures of the Labyrinth. Didn’t you read a book about them when you were a kid?”
“...I didn’t ask you.”

I didn’t recognize whatever 109 Treasures of the Labyrinth book Amelia was talking about either, but I followed my gut and quickly stepped in before those two could bicker any longer. “Beginner’s Luck is a talisman item.”
Of course, in the game, the English descriptions said “Charm.”
“A talisman...”
Since none of them seemed familiar with the term, I first had to explain what a talisman was.
Fortunately, Erwen was quick to grasp the concept as a talented adventurer with a lot of experience under her belt. “Ah, so it’s an item whose effects activate as long as you have it on you, right?”

“Yeah.” There were a total of twelve talismans between all the Numbered Items, but if you had more than one in your possession, only one of them could be active at a time, even if they had different effects. “And Beginner’s Luck is unique in that it will belong to a set person.”
“...Like the Orb of Fire you’ve talked about?”
“Yeah.”

“Oh no! I-I didn’t know, I swear! I had no clue! Believe me!” As soon as she heard it was an item that bound itself to the first person who touched it, Ainar paled and suddenly started to plead her innocence. Of course, no one had suspected her of any wrongdoing in the first place, so we just ignored her as we continued to discuss what to do with it.
“What effect does the flower have?”

Ah, it was pretty simple, actually. It didn’t help you out in combat nor did it increase your Item Level or stats when worn. “Instead, it increases the probability of an essence dropping when you hunt a monster for the first time.”
“I see... what an incredible item!” Erwen looked unexpectedly excited to hear what it was.
Ainar, on the other hand, only seemed disappointed. “How incredible can it be? It doesn’t even guarantee an essence drop! And it only works on monsters you hunt for the first time?”
That wasn’t an unreasonable reaction. After all, they wouldn’t know the exact probability of essence drop rates.

According to the data that I gathered myself over the years, the drop rate of all essences increased by about 5 percent while wearing Beginner’s Luck, and that was a fixed rate, not a multiplier. For example, if a guardian’s essence had a drop rate of 33 percent, that rate would increase to 38 percent with Beginner’s Luck’s 5 percent bonus.
“So what’s the improved drop rate?”

The effects might seem lackluster on the surface, but it was a completely different story when you fought against regular monsters. You might not notice a difference between 33 percent and 38 percent, but the change from 0.01 percent to 5.01 percent was so drastic that anyone was bound to notice.
“I’d say roughly one in twenty.”
It wasn’t just Ainar who gawked at the approximation I offered. Even Erwen and Amelia looked surprised. “A-Are you serious?! One in twenty?!”
Another understandable reaction yet again. Even though they didn’t know the exact numbers, every adventurer had learned through experience just how horrendous the drop rates of essences could be.
“Oh, of course when I say one in twenty, I’m talking about rank-nine monsters,” I explained as an additional aside. “Though I heard that the higher the rank, the higher the drop rate.”

Monsters of higher ranks had slightly higher base drop rates. Some rank-three monsters even had a drop rate of 5 percent. To be fair, that was likely because it was harder to hunt them in the first place.
“Wow... it really is one of the 109 Treasures.”

“It certainly is. It may only work the first time you kill a new monster, but the probability of an essence dropping is too good, especially if you have a wizard with you. You could easily earn a lot of money.”

“Bjorn... I’m sorry. I had no idea, and I nearly took it without even thinking...” Ainar suddenly went back to apologize, but we all knew from the start she didn’t do it on purpose. Why did she keep apologizing to me?
I just chose to ignore her and move on to the topic at hand. “Now then... which of us will take it?”
It was time to decide the owner. Since the item would be bound to the first person who touched it, it would be impossible to sell afterward.
“You said that the person holding it doesn’t have to hunt the monsters themselves, so it should work for all of us so long as we’re bound by the binding spell, right?”
“Then it might be a good idea to give it to the person with the least experience fighting monsters.”

Amelia was right—the best person to give it to would be the lowest-level member of our party, as they would have killed the fewest types of monsters. Currently, Amelia was level eight while Erwen, Ainar, and I were level seven.
“Auyen, what level are you?”
“...Me? Oh! Um, I’m level six!”
We could just have Auyen hold onto the item and drag him along with us like a totem...
But during a real battle later on, we can’t risk such a precious item not taking effect. And with the way things are now, I have no plans to let Auyen take part in combat in the future.
After taking everything into consideration, I came to my decision. “Ainar, you take it.” Erwen already had experience fighting against Bellarios, but Ainar didn’t.
“...Huh? You’re giving it to me? I’m happy, b-but I think you should have it instead, Bjorn...!”

Didn’t I tell her already? You could only have one talisman item at a time, otherwise the effects wouldn’t activate. I wasn’t planning on wasting my precious talisman space on it when I wouldn’t even be able to get rid of it later.
“You’re a better fit for it than me, so you should have it, Ainar.”
“Bjooorn!”
Thankfully, Ainar seemed happy about it.
[The luck hidden in the flower’s petals seeps into Ainar Fenelin.]
After clearing Iron Grave, we headed straight to the Den of Beasts.
“Aaaaaagh! How long do we have to stay in this smelly place?! This isn’t the type of quest I had in mind!”

We waited up until the eighth day for any rifts to open. I did debate postponing things for next time, of course. We now had Beginner’s Luck, so the most efficient thing to do would be to bring along a wizard to sell any essences we might encounter.
But considering the price of a test tube, the essences of the monsters on this floor wouldn’t be worth it.

Ultimately, the only essence worth taking would be the guardian’s essence, and since I was planning to give it to Erwen anyway if it dropped, there was no need to postpone our plans any further. We could focus on raking in the cash with a wizard next time.
“...Really? Are we really going to the higher floors now after wasting all that time?!”
“That’s what we decided on beforehand. So stop whining.”

As we headed toward the portal on the eighth day, we started to encounter mid-to high-level adventurers. They were adventurers who were currently focused on hunting down rifts, like us. However, since second-floor rifts didn’t open after the seventh day, everyone planned on going up.
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]

Once on the third floor, we passed Ironrock Hill and headed straight to the Orc Colony to focus on farming. The monster we would be hunting now was one I was personally familiar with. It was the very same monster that the Dzarwi clan had been hunting when the Lord of Chaos was summoned: the Orc Hero.
“Ohhh! Giantization! Does that mean I’ll get the chance to do it now too?!”

Ainar was overjoyed to hear the identity of our target, but unfortunately for her, no one on our team would be absorbing its essence. Without the Immortality Imprint’s Union ability, the cons associated with Giantization far outweighed the pros. The plan was simply to get EXP for hunting the Orc Hero and hopefully get a Numbered Item drop as well.
But now that we have Beginner’s Luck, an essence drop is almost guaranteed for us.

I couldn’t live with the guilt of leaving an essence like that behind, so I spoke with every wizard we came across while grinding for the Mighty Orc Warrior mana stones that we needed for the altar. Luckily, we were able to convince one.
“A test tube? Of course I have one, but—”
“Great. If an essence drops, can we use your test tube? We’ll pay for the cost immediately, of course.”
“...What are you talking about? Just who do you think you—”
“Lewis! A-Are you nuts? That’s Baron Yandel!”

Because of my rather high Reputation stat, recruiting help turned out to be a lot easier than anticipated. Not only that, but they gave me some useful information. Apparently, the third floor’s rift hadn’t opened yet.
All right, in that case, we can stay here on the third floor until the thirteenth day...

After getting our affairs in order, we went back to mana stone farming. Our team was able to search for and hunt monsters individually, so we were able to collect all 777 mana stones in less than a day. Once we’d prepared all the stones, we met up with the wizard again as we waited.
“I’m telling you this just in case, but don’t come anywhere near me unless I give you the signal. If for some reason the Orc Lord suddenly appears, I won’t be able to protect you all.”
“An Orc Lord...”
“It’s a rank-two monster.”
“A... rank two?!”
“You’ll be safe as long as you don’t come close, so don’t worry.”
“I-I’ll keep that in mind...”
With that, preparations were complete. After explaining what to do if the Orc Lord made an appearance, I offered the mana stones to the altar.
[The spirit of a Mighty Warrior has been sacrificed to the warrior’s bowl.]
[The spirit of a Mighty Warrior has been sacrificed to the warrior’s bowl.]
[The spirit of a Mighty Warrior has been sacrificed to...]
The mana stones we placed on the altar quickly vanished into bursts of light.
[Special Condition—Warrior’s Bowl has been met.]
As if to signal the start of a boss battle, the outer layer of the stone statue behind the altar began to crumble away.
Craaaaaack.
Luckily, the stone statue of the Orc Lord remained intact. Well, considering the probability of an Orc Lord actually appearing, that was a given.
I always get nervous whenever there’s a chance of an impossible fight breaking out, though.
No matter how many times I experienced it, I could never get used to it.
“Get ready everyone!” I hurriedly shouted to my teammates, who were standing far away from the altar.
[The ancient hero Denish has awoken.]
[The ancient hero Belta has awoken.]
[The ancient hero Tarugas has awoken.]
They were the three Orc Heroes. As soon as the three heroes broke free of their statue, the battle began.
“Graaaaaawr!”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
The three ran at me, each wielding a different weapon—an axe, a hammer, and a sword. But thanks to my combo of Transcendence and Giantization, I was no pushover when it came to weight class.
Slam!
Even the attacks that I couldn’t block didn’t hurt me. At best, they only made my bones ache a bit. To be honest, if I had to, I felt like I could take an entire day of nonstop bombardment from them.
This will be the perfect battle to test our skills.

As long as I played my role and focused solely on tanking their attacks, this would turn into a long, drawn-out battle. After all, these three monsters were all rank five. It would be ridiculous to dismiss their difficulty level just because their attacks might not be hurting me right now.
“Graaaaaa!”
A horde of regular rank-seven Orcs rushed out from where they were hidden in the forest in never-ending waves as soon as the raid began.
Clang! Smash! Booom!

Like we planned in advance, Ainar would focus on dealing with those extra Orcs, meaning we only had two damage dealers to use in this boss battle. In other words, Erwen and Amelia would have to kill all three of them on their own. Then again, the two of them had completely destroyed the Death Worm in the Rock Desert.
[The Ancient Hero Denish has cast Agony.]
Orc Heroes were typically rank-five monsters, but as higher-rank mutants, these guys would drop rank-four essences. Not only that, but between the three of them, each essence was different.
[The Ancient Hero Belta has cast Sacred Battlefield.]
[The Ancient Hero Tarugas has cast Protective Shield.]
When combined, their essences complemented each other, compensating for the other’s weaknesses while maximizing their strengths.
That wasn’t all.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]
[The Ancient Hero Denish has used the Great Sword of Control. The trajectory of all long-range attacks has been modified.]
They also used Numbered Items.
[The Orc Sorcerer has cast Frenzy.]
[The Ancient Hero Denish’s Physical Resistance has increased threefold for 10 seconds.]
What was more, during the battle, they constantly got buffs to their resistances, making it even more difficult for them to deal damage.
[The Orc Sorcerer has cast Regeneration Imprint. The Ancient Hero Tarugas’s Natural Regeneration has increased significantly.]
They even got instant healing.

The monsters before us were strong, well beyond any regular Orc Hero an adventurer would ever meet by chance on another floor. The good thing was they gave bonus experience points since they were higher-rank mutants. Without that and their odds of dropping a Numbered Item, there would be absolutely no reason to fight them.
“What are you guys doing? Aren’t you going to kill them?! You killed that worm so easily, but you can’t deal with these guys?!”
“It’s not that easy!”
“Never mind our battle and focus on your own, barbarian.”
The moment push came to shove, the trio started to bicker with each other. Still, at the end of the day, they were all professionals.
“Ms. Ainar! Can you focus on getting rid of that Sorcerer first?”
“Tersia, go after the one with the hammer. I’ll deal with the one holding the sword.”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
After realizing that this would never end if they fought amongst themselves, they slowly started to cooperate, communicate, and create opportunities for others to attack.
“Ahhhh!”
Auyen, our rank-six teammate with a sordid past, also managed to help. He focused on dealing with the trash mobs that were trying to go after Erwen.
[You have killed the Ancient Hero Belta. EXP +5]
[High-rank Mutant Bonus. EXP +1]
At long last, we were able to defeat one of the three heroes, and from there, we had the upper hand needed to quickly end this fight.
[You have killed the Ancient Hero Denish.]
[High-rank Mutant Bonus. EXP +1]
[You have killed the Ancient Hero Tarugas.]
[High-rank Mutant Bonus. EXP +1]
When I checked my watch, our total battle time ended up being thirty-five minutes. Considering that it was a four-person raid, that was pretty fast. But...
“Even though we worked so hard, nothing dropped...”
There were absolutely no spoils. Neither an essence nor a Numbered Item dropped. It couldn’t be helped, though. That sort of luck was par for the course when you played Dungeon and Stone.
“Okay, let’s quickly collect the mana stones and move on. Oh, Amelia. You can go tell the wizard over there that he can leave now.”
After we gathered the mana stones by hand, we left the Orc Colony. So far, our expedition this month had been smooth sailing.
“Mister...?”
As we camped out by the Witch’s Forest while waiting for the thirteenth day to arrive, however, I was struck by a bad feeling.
[A fifth sacrifice has been made in the hut.]
[A sixth sacrifice has been made in the hut.]
[A seventh sacrifice has been made in the hut.]
The world around us began to shine with a light bright enough to render all torches useless. I looked up to see a bright red glow take form and start to spread along the ceiling.
[Special Condition – Seven Sacrifices has been satisfied.]
Tsk. Just my luck, some moron was starting shit again.
[The Lord of Chaos, Riakis, has begun to wander the floor.]
This was going to be a headache.

chapters.title: Chapter 458: Raid (3)
paragraphs: To properly enjoy Dungeon and Stone, you had to be good at adapting to anything that it threw your way. I wasn’t talking about getting familiar with the setting of the game, but rather, adapting to the playstyle it required. A rift suddenly opening while you were in the middle of hunting, a teammate betraying you when you crossed paths with a high-rank monster—you were bound to encounter unforeseen situations like that at some point or another while playing the game.
Like right now.
“Mister, that...”
“Yeah, that’s right.”
The Lord of the Floor had been summoned. In other words, someone on the third floor had sacrificed seven human bodies inside the Witch’s Hut, whether intentionally or otherwise.
Well, I had a feeling it was deliberate, of course.
...But sometimes, it really is by coincidence.

Exhibit A was none other than me. On the day Missha and I had accidentally taken part in summoning it, I had only decided to burn the bodies because we were desperate to take a break in the cabin. Unfortunately, somebody else had already done the same thing, so the Lord of the Floor ended up spawning. Either way, that wasn’t important right now.
“Yandel, what should we do?”

“First, let’s get out of the forest. We can’t go to the fourth floor now, anyway.” When Riakis, the Lord of Chaos, was summoned, all portals on the third floor were disabled, turning the entire third floor into a massive boss room.
While we were putting as much distance between us and the forest as possible, some familiar faces decided to appear.
“Bjorn! There’s some creepy gross thing crawling around over there. What is that?”
“A Spirit of Chaos.”
Once Riakis was summoned, those token monsters began to run rampant across the entire floor, and they pursued whoever drew their aggro until death. I sighed at the memory.
It’s been a long time since I’ve seen these bastards.
“I’ll take care of them.” Without even needing to shoot an arrow, Erwen used a fire spirit to killed three Spirits of Chaos in one go.
[The Spirit of Chaos has been destroyed. This location will now deteriorate.]
If we were planning to fight the boss, we’d have to be careful and keep track of which locations eroded away, but since we weren’t going to be hunting Riakis either way—
“Kwohhh!”
A familiar roar echoed from the Witch’s Forest. I was a bit disappointed. I thought the next time I heard that sound, I would be the one hunting him instead.
“Bjorn! Shouldn’t we do something instead of just running away?”
“What, you want the four of us to hunt a Lord of the Floor?”
Technically speaking, Auyen made five, but nobody bothered correcting me. It wasn’t like one more person would be enough to make the impossible possible.
“Bjorn, that’s not what I meant... I was just wondering if there was anything we could do? I heard that a lot of people died the last time this happened.”
Yeah... A lot of people did die, and since I was responsible for the incident, I felt genuinely guilty about it.
“Oh, and I heard that in a disaster situation, higher-level adventurers have a duty to help!”

Yes, that was the adventurer’s pledge. That was the reason why the Dzarwi clan, who happened to be on the third floor at the time, did their best to protect the lower-rank adventurers. Even the biggest clans couldn’t help but be wary of retribution from the guild.
Though they did extort money from the adventurers as a fee for protecting them...

One thing was clear, though. Without their help that day, many more people would have died. Even after the Lord of the Floor appeared, they still risked their lives to protect the low-rank adventurers gathered there for nearly four hours.
“I-I mean, I don’t know what we should do in a situation like this. I only know how to fight. But you’re different, Bjorn, so—”
“Ainar, calm down.”
She quickly shut her mouth, embarrassed. But even though she clearly felt like she’d said too much, she didn’t stop looking straight at me.

I could tell from her gaze alone. Ainar was righteous. There were only two things she despised in this world, and they were monsters and plunderers. As long as they weren’t one of those two things, she wanted to help others as much as possible.
“Don’t worry. I’m not going to let people die without doing anything.” The situation on the whole wasn’t all that bad. Helping others and giving back wasn’t always a loss, after all.
“Oh! I knew it!”
“Did you think I would just run away? I’m sure there are many fellow barbarians here on the third floor.”

That said, protecting the barbarians was barely even a factor for me at this point. I had planned to step in no matter what. How high was my Reputation stat now? It would tank if word got out that I ran away by myself on the third floor without helping anyone.
“Ahhh! Then what should we do? I’ll follow your lead, even if you ask me to jump into a fire!”
“We’ll stay here and observe the situation for the time being.”
“...What?”
My reason for going on standby at the edge of the forest was simple.
“...You think there’s a chance we won’t even have to do anything.”
“It’s nearly impossible to get permission to hunt the third floor’s Lord of the Floor from the Adventurers’ Guild, so maybe some clan just went and summoned it without permission instead.”
“Ah! That means that if they kill it themselves, there won’t be a problem!”
“That’s right.”
This was all speculation, of course. There was no way to confirm that was what was going on yet.
“Kwohhh!”
Watching from the outskirts of the forest as a ferocious roar rang out, I received real-time updates on the situation through Erwen.
“Riakis is heading toward the west side of the Witch’s Forest. We’d need to be closer for me to say for sure, but there seems to be quite a few people over there.”
“How many?”
“I don’t know. They’re too far away...”
“Then let’s get closer.”
We walked along the forest’s perimeter, heading west. Thanks to Erwen’s incredible detection skills, we were soon able to gather more detailed information.
“...There are about fifteen people, and it looks like they’re being chased by Riakis.”

Hm, were they really? I would wager that they were searching for a better place to fight. The forest’s terrain was littered with obstacles that blocked your field of view, making it an unfriendly environment for any party looking to battle a boss. More than that, though, there was something else that piqued my interest.

“Fifteen people...” That wasn’t enough people to defeat Riakis, though it might technically be possible with the perfect strategy and front line. “I think those fifteen people are the bait, while their main team is waiting somewhere else.”
“Y-You think so?”
“Can you hear what they’re saying?”
“No. I would guess they’re using a Voice Control spell because I can’t hear a single word.”
“Hm, I see.”

It was a shame we couldn’t eavesdrop on them, but I couldn’t help but feel relieved at how things had turned out. If it had really all been an unplanned disaster, I would have had to run into the fray and risk my life fighting that damn thing again.
Drip, drop, drip, drop.
Suddenly, rain began to fall from the sky.
Fshhhhhh!
My skin stung where the black rain fell, each drop like pure acid. This was Riakis’s passive aura skill.
[You are receiving continuous Chaos-type damage. Your Mana Resistance has drastically decreased.]
[Warning: When continuously exposed to Chaos-type damage, there is a chance that the status effect Confusion will be applied.]
That meant we were near him.
“We’ll have to move a little further back.” Without a priest, we didn’t have any way to counter his aura, so we decided to retreat a bit, just out of range of the rain. And a while later—
“We’ll be outside the forest soon!”
Although I didn’t have Erwen or Amelia’s incredible eyesight, I could still make out a group of about fifteen people running in the distance.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
And, of course, there was a massive monster chasing after them.
“Erwen, take a look. What clan are they with?”
“...They’re not wearing emblems.”
Huh, did they take them off? Well, they were trying to hunt the Lord of the Floor without permission, so that tracks.
They continued to draw Riakis away as they ran at full tilt.
“Yandel,” Amelia called out to me as she watched them go, “what are you planning to do now?”
“Follow them.”
“Why do that?”
“Because if they fail, then we’ll have a real disaster on our hands.”
In other words, if we didn’t go with them, we’d have no way of knowing whether we needed to take action.
After following the group of fifteen for a while, we arrived at Thorn Reed Field.
Yeah, I guess this would be the best place.

The field had no terrain features that could block your vision—just a nice, wide-open clearing—which made it a good battlefield. Normally, there would be thorns here that reached as high as your shoulders, but they had all been burned down and removed like someone had come here in advance to prepare this place for battle.
“Mister, the main group is over—” Erwen abruptly cut herself off.
“What’s the matter?”
“They’ve noticed our presence. One person is closing in on us and fast.”
“Can we outrun them?”
“...There’s a small chance we could, but only one person is coming.”
Hm, so that’s how it is. I guess there’s no point in worrying about it.

I made a snap decision. “Then we’ll wait here.” Why would we run away when we didn’t do anything wrong? Besides, I was curious. What kind of people started an unauthorized raid that was bound to harm innocent lives?
“They’re here.”

It didn’t take long for someone to come running across the barren Thorn Reed Field and reach us. From a distance, he looked like a faint dot, but it didn’t take long for that dot to grow and take human form.
Stomp.
Roughly ten yards away from us, the man stopped. He looked to be a quick-on-his-feet, agile type judging by the seven daggers lining his belt.
As soon as he saw me, he froze. When he didn’t speak a word, I was the one who was forced to speak first. “Why aren’t you saying anything? You’re the one who ran over here so quickly.”
“...I never expected to run into a celebrity here.”
Ah, so that’s why he looks so dumbstruck.
“It’s an honor to meet you, Baron Yandel. I never expected to meet someone as great as a baron on the third floor of the—”
“Enough. Who are you?”
After I cut him off, he seemed to hesitate for a moment before opening his mouth. “...I’m Malid Kevron.”

Whether or not that was his real name, I couldn’t tell, but that was all I had to go off of. I decided to instead just refer to him as Daggers as I asked another question. “What clan are you a part of?”
“...The Sawtooth clan.”
They were one of the ten largest clans in the city, now reduced to four because of the war, and the very same clan that James Calla used to be the vice captain of.
“Interesting,” I said with a smile. “You’re acting like it’s odd that I’m on the third floor, but a clan of your status being down here is even stranger, don’t you think?”
Daggers quickly countered, “That’s just how things panned out for us this time. Speaking of, by any chance, was it you who summoned the Lord of the Floor, Your Lordship?”
He was quick-footed and quick-witted. I never expected him to turn this around on me like that, without a single hint of fear.
“It wasn’t me.”
“Is that so?”
“But if I were to ask you the same question, I’m guessing you would say no as well.”
“It certainly wasn’t us.”
“Does that mean the people who were running around provoking Riakis have nothing to do with you?”
“They are a part of our clan, yes, but we were simply following the adventurer’s pledge and taking care of this since we happened to be nearby.”
He’s one hell of a smooth-talker.
“That’s good to hear. Then we’ll lend you guys a helping hand.”
