As soon as I offered our support, Dagger’s expression suddenly hardened. “...I am grateful for the offer, but we wouldn’t dare impose upon you and have you fight, Your Lordship.”
“Hm, and why is that?”
“Isn’t it only right for the dangerous work to be left to the adventurers?”
Huh. So he was treating me like I wasn’t a fellow adventurer just because I had become a noble? I had to fight back the sudden urge to bash his head in with my hammer.
“You wouldn’t want to undermine the prestige of the rest of Rafdonia’s nobility by taking part in such a lowly task meant for those beneath you.”
“...What?” What did I just hear? “When you say the rest of the nobility... are you talking about people like Count Alminus? One of the supporters of the Sawtooth clan?”
I asked the question just to confirm, but he responded with a brazen smile on his face. “Yes, that is correct.”
So I did hear him right the first time.
In that case, there was no point in trying to have a diplomatic conversation any longer. Was that what he was getting at, then? If you don’t want trouble, then don’t get greedy?
“What are you trying to say, you arrogant bastard?”
“...Pardon?” Daggers froze like a new recruit who was unsure how he’d pissed off his commanding officer. “Did I hear you right?”
I took a step forward. “Hey, Daggers.”
“Are your brains made of Goblin shit?”
“What? Wh-what are you talking about...?
Now that’s more like it.
He had been talking down to me this whole time, but now, he was breaking out in a cold sweat as he slowly backed away.
“Well, I guess I’ll find out once I crack it open.”
I stealthily lifted my hammer.

chapters.title: Chapter 459: Raid (4)
paragraphs: With my hammer held high, I cast Transcendence and Eye of the Storm, dragging Daggers over to me.
Shaaaaaa!
Caught off guard by the ambush, he couldn’t escape my grasp as I lifted him up with one hand, the soft flesh of his neck squishing under my fingers.

At that moment, Amelia called out to me. “Yandel.” Her voice was full of concern. Did she think I was going to kill him? That hurt my feelings a bit. There was no way I would actually crack open his skull over something like that. I wasn’t a real barbarian, after all.
Squeeze.
I was just putting on a show that happened to have a few of my true emotions woven in.
“Mister. They’re almost here.”
As expected, the moment I grabbed this guy’s throat, more adventurers suddenly appeared in the distance. It didn’t take long for them to arrive at our location.
“...What do you think you’re doing, Baron Yandel?!”
They already knew who I was. That wasn’t all that surprising. They must have been eavesdropping on our conversation through a message stone or something.
Daggers choked and started to thrash around more desperately as I tightened my grip.
“Let go of him this instant!”
“And why should I do that?”
“Even if you’re a noble, this is crossing the line! Do you think it’s acceptable to harm an innocent adventurer without reason?”
I was dumbfounded by the question. First off, I found it hard to see someone who might have deliberately summoned the Lord of the Floor without permission as an “innocent adventurer.”

“How is he innocent?” I spoke clearly so they could all hear me. Now came the second reason: “This man is a traitor. He shamelessly attempted an unforgivable act—to intimidate and humiliate me, a noble of Rafdonia! Do you think that’s acceptable?!”
“Wh-what are you talking about? When did he ever do—?”
“What? Are you looking down on me too?”
“No. That’s not what I meant...”
Throughout our conversation, Daggers was still trapped in my grasp, flailing like a fish. “Grk! Ergh...!”
He was more accommodating than I had expected. I was certain he would have drawn the dagger at his waist and stabbed me in the hand by now.
He must realize that would only make this situation worse.
“Th-then may I ask that you please let him go so we can talk about this? I’m sure there’s been a misunderstanding here, so—”
It didn’t seem like these guys had any intention of attacking me, so I decided to throw Daggers back toward his teammates.
“Vice Captain! Are y-you okay?”
Huh... so he was the vice captain. He must have been James Calla’s replacement.
...No wonder he didn’t try to fight back at all.
His sense of duty and loyalty toward his clan was impressive, but that didn’t mean there was anything good about him or the Sawtooth Clan either.
“Now then, tell me what the misunderstanding was,” I said.
The man who had shouted at me earlier to let his vice captain go tried to answer, but Daggers quickly stood up and slapped a hand over his mouth before he could.

“I would like to sincerely apologize to you, Baron Yandel. Please forgive me for the wrongdoing I’ve committed against you,” he said without offering any excuses. “I clearly made a mistake by mentioning Count Alminus.”
He certainly was sharp. With this swift and simple response, he managed to de-escalate the situation without stepping on any more landmines.
“If you believe I deserve to be punished, I will willingly submit myself to your judgment when we return to the city.”

Now that he’d said all of that, I would look like the bad guy if I continued to complain. It wasn’t like he had cursed me out or actually threatened me. Even if I personally asked the Mozlan to execute him, the request wouldn’t be granted.
And once we return to the city, this will also reach the ears of Count Alminus.
In fact, there was a high chance that people would interpret this situation as me strangling an innocent adventurer for no justifiable reason.

“Is your answer still the same?” I asked once more, refusing to accept his apology just yet. After all, what I was hoping for was neither an apology nor a punishment. “As a fellow adventurer, I want this situation to be dealt with as quickly as possible, which is why I want to contribute to this battle.”
“...I see.”
“So do you still plan on stopping me?”
Daggers took a moment to get his thoughts in order, then said, “With all due respect, what are your plans for after this incident is resolved?”
Translation: how would we distribute the loot?
“Aren’t we all adventurers? We’ll roll the dice, fair and square.”
“...I see.” Daggers let out a heavy sigh and then handed down his verdict. “Then we will not take part in this battle.”
“...What?”

“They say that an enemy you know is less dangerous than an ally you don’t. Even so, we have no way of convincing you to not interfere. I’m certain that fighting alongside you will only complicate the situation and result in greater losses for my clan.”
“So you’re backing down?”
“Yes. You are a reputable hero, after all. I’m sure I can put my complete faith in you, Baron Yandel.”
Hah, this punk.
“We will instead focus on helping the low-rank adventurers who are also stuck on the third floor right now.”
In other words, rather than giving us a piece of the pie, they would rather throw the whole thing on the ground.
What a stubborn little prick.

The problem was that I couldn’t do anything about it. If word of what happened here got out, some people might assume I forced them to leave out of my own greed, potentially resulting in the needless deaths of countless adventurers.
No, they’ll definitely make sure that’s what people think.
“So have you come to a decision?”
In the end, there was only one decision I could make. “We will leave Riakis to you.”
It was a shame I couldn’t get a piece of the pie, but it couldn’t be helped. It was more important to defeat the boss as quickly as possible before it killed anyone else.
“Then we will be on our way.”

Daggers tried to rush off the moment our conversation came to an end, but I left him with one last warning. “But remember this. If by chance you fail, your entire clan will be held accountable. After all, you were the ones who refused my help.”
After a brief pause, he responded. “...I’ll keep that in mind.”
He clearly had no intention of taking my warning seriously.
After hashing out who would be fighting the Lord of the Floor, we left Thorn Reed Field without any hesitation. What was the point of sticking around and watching them any longer?
[Lord of Chaos Riakis is drawing in the Power of Origin.]
If Riakis managed to eat all the marbles, things might take a turn for the extremely difficult as the moment that happened, one of us might end up being designated as Prey.
And if that happens, even if they fail, they’ll be able to put the blame on us.
At this point, however, there was no point in worrying over hypotheticals. All we could do was continue to move forward.
“Bjorn! Where are we going now?”
“Wherever there are other people.”
“...What?”
“No matter how I look at it, Sawtooth is planning on a long, drawn-out battle.”
My claim piqued Amelia’s curiosity and she jumped into the conversation. “Hm? What makes you say that?”
“The first reason is the date.”
“The date?”
“Yeah. If they thought they could beat it quickly, they wouldn’t have summoned it on the thirteenth day.”

They were putting their clan’s entire existence on the line with this unauthorized raid. Given that that was the case, the ideal strategy would be to quickly summon and defeat the boss right before the labyrinth closed to minimize the loss of innocent lives. But instead, they had been forced to summon it early, which told me that they couldn’t defeat it the ideal way. They were instead banking on a battle of attrition.
“...What is your second reason?”
“They had Purification Torches on their waistbands.”
“Purification Torches... Are you talking about that Numbered Item in the 8000s?”
It was No. 8645, to be exact, but that wasn’t the point. If everyone in their raid squad had one, they would be able to skip Riakis’s second phase for free.
“But why is that a problem?”

“Because using that item forces you to drag out the fight. It does lower the overall difficulty level, but if your goal is to defeat the boss as quickly as possible, that is one of the worst items you could use...” Since I felt like I was revealing too much, I quickly tacked on, “At least that’s what I read in a book.”
“Ohhh! Amazing!” Fortunately, Ainar didn’t seem to notice anything. I was always on alert around her, but in her mind, she probably didn’t have any reason to be suspicious of me.
“Ahem... Anyway! Things will probably stay like this until the day the labyrinth closes. So let’s focus on gathering as many people together as possible.”
“Of course!”

“Still... Just know that a lot of people will die here. I’m sure of it. This is one of the most dangerous Lords of the Floor, after all. Even parties working together in groups must be struggling to hold on...”
“It’s impossible to head up to another floor anyway, so I don’t mind either way... Why are you asking us for permission if you’ve already made up your mind as our leader?”
“It’s just standard procedure!”
“...I-I’m also fine with it!”
All right, it seemed we were all in agreement.
As soon as we began to search the floor, fellow barbarians started to recognize me and ask for help. Luckily, all of the barbarian adventurers we found could handle Spirits of Chaos on their own.
The same could not be said for other adventurers.
“B-Baron Yandel!”
“It’s really Baron Yandel...!”
“W-We’re going to live!”
They all probably knew that Riakis was roaming the third floor by now, so they must have been terrified.
“Th-thank you so much for taking us in...!”
“Ohhh! Chieftain! The chieftain has come to save us!”
Since there weren’t enough members of my team to protect the entirety of the camp we set up, I was forced to assign fellow barbarians to guard the outskirts. However, something unexpected happened.
“Baron Yandel! We would like to help you as well! Is there anything we can do?”
“Me too! I would also like to help!”
Other adventurers suddenly started to come forward and volunteer. It didn’t take long to set up a solid defense system where we only had to work in shifts.
...I don’t think there’s anything more we can do.

I decided to send Erwen and Amelia off to search the perimeter since we already had enough people at our camp to defend ourselves unless Riakis himself showed up. “Erwen, Amelia. Can I ask you to do something?”
“Yes, of course!”
“...Whenever you ask me that, it always ends up being a pain in the ass.”
These two had one mission: to run around outside our camp, find any isolated or lost adventurers, and bring them back to safety.
“Bjorn! What about me? What should I do?”
Unfortunately, Ainar would be unable to find her way back alone. Instead, I gave her the position of security commander of our camp.
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has...]
[Your Reputation has...]
Day Thirteen. Day Fourteen...
Time flew by, until finally, it was the day the labyrinth would close.
“Mister, I’m back!”
When I woke up, the first thing I saw was Erwen’s amber eyes right in front of my face.
“Good work. How many did you bring back this time?”
“Thirty-nine. I searched quite far, but it seems that there are no more adventurers left in our vicinity now.”
“I see. Go ahead and rest.”
“All right.”
“...I told you to rest?”
“Being next to you is resting, though?”
I didn’t know how to respond to that, so I just checked the time.

We had around eighteen hours left before the labyrinth closed. The once-panicky lower-rank adventurers seemed to have slowly regained their composure. Well, seeing nearly a thousand adventurers all gathered together, relying on and protecting each other, must have put them at ease. I, on the other hand, was starting to get more and more anxious.
They still haven’t finished him off...
The source of my anxiety was the Lord of the Floor. I had expected a prolonged battle, but I never expected them to not have defeated the boss by now.
The Spirits of Chaos disappeared a few hours ago, so they must have finally cleared the second phase, which is the longest...

How would things play out from here, though? They were annoying bastards, to be sure, but I genuinely hoped that nothing went awry during their raid. Their failure would be the absolute worst-case scenario, especially if Riakis was now wandering the floor in his third phase.
A sigh escaped me. I was dying to know what was happening.

In frustration, I walked around our refugee camp, acting like I was keeping an eye out for anything suspicious while really just needing some fresh air. Sure enough, there was nothing out of the ordinary. The Spirits of Chaos were no longer spawning, after all.
After my mock patrol, I gathered my party together for a meal for the first time in a while. By then, it was already 6:30 a.m.
Tremble!
The vibrations under our feet turned our expressions to stone.
“Bjorn, what was that just now...?”
“Guoooooo!”
Shit.
“I-It’s the Lord of the Floor...”
“He’s here...”
“I-I heard that last time, hundreds of people died in a single day...”
Fear and confusion instantly began to spread throughout the camp.
I stood up, taking a deep breath before shouting with all my might, “Everyone, be quiet!”
Phew, that was better.

I used Giantization so I could be seen by those in the back as well. Feeling the thousands of eyes watching me, waiting to hear what I had to say, the first thing I did was gather information. “Erwen, is it heading our way?”
Seriously? Well, that’s a relief.
Looking around, I then called out the name of the first familiar face I saw. “Lewis Seyur!”
It was the wizard I had met at the Orc Colony a few days ago.
“...Yes? W-Why did you call for me?”
“From now on, you are in charge of this place.”
“... W-What?”

We had run into each other again by chance after the Lord of the Floor spawned. After talking with him for a while, I realized that he was quite a smart, rational guy. “You will lead the people here and run as far away as you can.”
“Th-then what are you going to do, Baron?!”
Wasn’t it obvious? “I’m going to stop him.”
“Wh-what? B-but Ms. Tersia just said that he isn’t even coming toward us...”
“So you’re suggesting that we just leave it alone?”

There was no way this camp of ours held every single low-rank adventurer stuck on the third floor. There had to be hundreds more that were still hiding out there, and now that the second phase was over, Riakis’s rampage would begin in earnest. Even more people would become innocent victims.
“Y-Your Lordship...”
“If you have something to say, say it quickly.”
“You really are... exactly like I heard...”
What?
“I’ll take that as a compliment, then.” With that, I grabbed my hammer and ran in the direction Erwen pointed, the members of my party following close behind.
Stomp, stomp.
I moved with haste. As I pushed forward, the adventurers who were standing in our path quickly cleared the way to not block us.
“May the blessings of Rafdonia be with you...”
They quietly lowered their heads. Why were they acting like we were going to die?
“Lewis! What are you doing?! Take these guys and get out of here, fast!” I yelled out to the wizard one last time, but he didn’t respond. He must have been too far away to hear.

Feeling awkward about all that, I started to speed up. Amelia laughed and asked if I was embarrassed. Come to think of it, it was strange. Why did I feel so much pressure to save them? Would other higher-rank adventurers go this far for lower-rank adventurers? Not only that, I was even a noble.
Well, I can just say that I did it to garner their respect. It’s not like it cost me any money to do the right thing.
Thinking like that made me feel a bit better.
Stomp, stomp.
As we exited the camp, we continued to barrel forward at top speed. At this point, regret started to gnaw at me.
If I knew things were going to pan out like this, I would have forced their hand from the get-go.

I was confident that I could one, hold back the Lord of the Floor on my own while he was in the first phase, and two, run across the entire floor nonstop until the labyrinth closed if I ended up marked as Prey. However, it was Phase Three when my confidence disappeared.
And I thought this month’s expedition would be more relaxing.
This situation was nothing compared to Ice Rock, but it also wasn’t great either.
Is he on the third or fourth phase?
If it was the third, I was going to have to run around like a meat shield nonstop.
I really hope it’s the fourth phase.
If they just so happened to fail to land the final blow on it during the last phase—
Guoooooo!
The lone figure of Riakis appeared in the distance, and I quickly came to a stop with a wide grin on my face.
I’m starting to feel butterflies in my stomach.
Yeah, this was worth a shot.
“Get ready, everyone.”
“...You said we would just be trying to stop it, but now you want to defeat it?”
Well, yeah. How could I resist landing the final blow?

chapters.title: Chapter 460: Raid (5)
paragraphs: A Lord of the Floor was a type of boss monster on each floor that appeared when certain summoning conditions were met. Normally, they were considered targets for high-rank raids, as anyone attempting to defeat one would need the specs of an experienced seventh-floor Rift adventurer at the very least. However, that only applied to the fifth floor and below. From the sixth floor up, the difficulty of each Lord of the Floor jumped exponentially, to the point where they were considered end-game content only.
So why is our first raid against a Lord of the Floor?

Considering that the highest Rift we’d ever cleared was the fourth floor’s Doppelganger Forest, it was nuts to attempt to take on a Lord of the Floor. Not only that, there were only four of us. Not even enough people for a full party, let alone enough to form an attack squadron.
We do have several rank-three essences, though. I’m sure we can at least land the final blow on it.
As soon as I spotted Riakis alone in the distance, I came to a decision. At this point, it would be moronic to not be greedy.
I made a promise back then.
Like a child, I made a promise to myself that the next time I saw this bastard—
Guoooooo!
Things would be different.
“Yandel, what are we going to do?”
“Oh, I’ll block his attacks, so focus on attacking back.”
“...That’s it?”

After hearing my simple orders, Amelia stared at me in disbelief. However, that was the closest thing to a plan of attack anyone could manage when fighting Riakis in his fourth phase. There was no reason to come up with a strategy. All you needed to do was hit him and hit him hard.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has sensed a source of life.]
When we stepped within a certain radius of him, he suddenly stopped running amok on all fours and looked our way.
Guoooooo!
With a ferocious roar, he charged at us. The sound of his footfalls was noticeably different from the first phase.
Stomp, stomp, stomp!
They were still heavy, but now, he was much lighter than before, meaning the speed at which he was running was that much faster. Riakis’s Phase Four was all about agility, after all.
“Everyone, stand behind me.”
Once my teammates were behind me, I cast Transcendence and Giantization.
[Your Physique grows in proportion to your Strength.]

If Riakis were still in his first phase, I wouldn’t have even been able to reach his chin. However, now that he had shrunk in size and strength, I was a match for him. It was one of the many advantages of Giantization.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has sensed a great threat in you.]
When your Threat Level rose during a raid, you naturally drew the enemy’s aggro. And when would this guy have ever met a threat like me? His would-be prey was now at eye level.
“Behel—aaah!”
My Threat Level had risen even without me needing to activate Wild Outburst, but I still let out a fierce roar as I headed straight for him. This was a form I liked to call Giant Shield Charge.
Booom!

There was a powerful crash as my giant barbarian shield and the giant monster’s body collided. Unfortunately, I was the one who was forced backward, but I had expected as much. It would be absurd to think that I had muscle strength and stats comparable to a Lord of the Floor.
Whack!

I cast Swing and swung my hammer at him, but he didn’t even flinch. Shouldn’t he at least blink when someone bashed his chin in? Riakis then immediately clawed at me with his front paw, knocking me off balance.
Graaaaaawr!
Riakis’s Phase Four was way too agile. I had no chance of dodging the swipe, but there was no real reason to dodge it in the first place.
Whack!
He wasn’t the only one with tough skin. Just like my hammer didn’t hurt him, him hitting me wouldn’t hurt me either.
...But why is my head spinning?
I had to revise that assertion as soon as I took stock of my current condition. My Physical Resistance was strong enough to prevent my head from flying clean off my shoulders, but...
I can’t let him hit me in the head anymore.
The shock wave from the blow rattled through my skull and down my spine. The last time I had ever experienced a head injury this bad was when I was beaten by my middle school P.E. teacher.
“Bjorn!”
I tossed the childhood memories that were clouding my mind aside and focused on the present.
Fwooosh!
He pushed forward once more, swinging his front paw at me.
Clang!
This time, I was able to block it with my shield. The timing was perfect too, as my damage dealers could now go on the offensive.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Self-Replication.]
Amelia rushed in from either side with her clones.
Slash.
With no intention of holding back, she cast Power of the Abyss and slashed at Riakis’s ankles and thighs.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Repeated Slash.]

At the same time, Ainar leaped high into the air and brought her sword down on his shoulder. However, unlike before, no explosion followed. She was no longer fighting weak mob monsters that would die in one hit, after all.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Wildness Control.]
She whipped out a skill from the very essence I had recommended to her when we received our reward from the royal family all those years ago. The effect of this skill was rather simple.
[All effects applicable to her next attack will be converted into Cutting Force.]
The damage of her three conditional skills—Blast Scars, Mandel Oil, and Residual Heat—would all be converted into Cutting Force.
Slash.

In other words, she could freely switch between raid mode and hunting mode. Although it still wasn’t enough to land the final blow, she could finally tear into the boss’s thick skin, earning her a few drops of his black blood.
Guooooooooo!
I knew Amelia would be able to deal some damage, but Ainar was also holding up better than I expected. All that remained was Erwen.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Element Synthesis.]
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
Needless to say, she was doing fine.
“Mister, get out of the way!”
Since I had already fought alongside Erwen many times before, I moved to the side the moment I heard that. I knew exactly what she was aiming for.
Flash.
With a brilliant burst of light, a plant popped out of the ground.
Fwoosh!
The stalk shot forward at speeds that broke the sound barrier before smashing into Riakis.
Boooooom!
The entire area lit up from the resulting explosion.
Guoooooo!
As I watched the boss cry out in agony, I couldn’t help but grin. Erwen’s attack still wasn’t anywhere near enough to finish Riakis off.
But jeez. With that one shot, she cracked its skull.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has cast Corrupted Horns.]
Now, the real raid would begin.

The first phase of the Lord of Chaos’s attack pattern was quite simple. Due to his passive aura skill Rain of Despair and his Spirits of Chaos, the entire floor was gradually corroded away. From the deteriorating land, marbles that could restore his health would occasionally begin to appear. During this phase, there was only one real thing to worry about: Evil Hiatus.

It was an instant-kill ability that activated after Riakis ate a certain number of marbles, but one that was possible to avoid since all you had to do was run away. The problem was that once you left a specified radius, someone would be marked as Prey and fall into an incapacitated state. Riakis would focus his aggro on the designated Prey, and once he devoured them, his baseline stats would rise, further increasing the difficulty of the next phase.
Well, after the first phase, things get pretty simple since you go into pure combat.
The true battle began in the second phase.

Once his health dropped below a certain threshold, Riakis would feel threatened and open the Gate of Chaos, which would suck everyone within his vicinity inside. There, the ground would gradually, permanently corrode away, and each adventurer would be subject to an effect that significantly ate away at their mental state. The player had to track down Riakis in the worst possible conditions, and by the time you found him, Riakis would have already been buffed beyond belief with countless combat modifiers, making him even more difficult to fight. It was truly the most difficult phase by far.

However, it was a different story if you had a Purification Torch. So long as you managed to hold onto the torch for two days, the Gate of Chaos would close, and you would be returned to your original location.
Getting a torch for every single member of your clan is the tricky part, but if you can do it, it does make Phase Two much easier.

Of course, there was also a major drawback to this strategy. If you used that freebie to reach the third phase, Riakis would not only be in full health, but he would also be much stronger than before. Regardless, it was still better than not using the torch, which is why I used it myself back in the old days.

By the third phase, the Spirits of Chaos disappeared from the third floor. Instead, Rain of Despair began to intensify. Areas exposed to the rain would quickly erode, and the same went for your equipment. Until the labyrinth closed, your Numbered Items would lose any and all effectiveness, and the defensive capacity of even adamantium-level armor would be drastically reduced, right down to the level of ordinary iron equipment.
The third phase... That’s probably when the Sawtooth Clan ended up failing.

At that point, the torches were no longer able to protect you. You were simply forced to fight an even stronger Riakis. If I had to guess, I’d say that the Sawtooth Clan had planned to defeat Riakis through sheer numbers alone, making sure to carefully manage the aggro and damage dealt.
Otherwise, there’s no way their battle against him would have dragged on for so many hours in the third phase.

I wasn’t absolutely positive about where their raid went wrong. Something unexpected must have happened. Dungeon and Stone had always been that type of game, in which the smallest mistakes could result in irreversible damage.
Still, they must have done a good job of preparing for this. They even managed to get him to the fourth phase, somehow...

Thanks to that, their stroke of misfortune was my stroke of luck. The most difficult thing about Phase Four was having all your equipment ruined before the fight even began. Luckily for us, we didn’t have to worry about that.
How could I pass up on something as delicious as this?

It was like they’d hand-delivered me the entire pie for free. Even if I ended up with an upset stomach later, it was only right for me to indulge now. Who knew, an essence might even drop. And if it did, that would make things a hell of a lot easier for us going forward.
Booom!
The bloodbath lasted for over thirty minutes. Erwen shot an arrow that sank deep into Riakis’s left eye.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has cast Corrupt Left Eye.]
All right then, there went the second eye.
Whooosh!
An ominous black smoke arose from his eye socket. Beyond the smoke came a faint, eerie glow.
Even as we tore through his flesh and shot at his eyes, he no longer groaned. It was like he was growing more and more lifeless by the minute.
We’ve cut off quite a few of his claws already... I think that makes seven parts that’ve been corrupted.
The theme of the fourth phase was simple. As Riakis continued to take damage, he began to corrupt parts of his body to recover, becoming slightly stronger each time.
That makes eleven.
All we needed was one more. If you corrupted twelve of his thirty-six body parts, the battle would end.
“Everyone, get back!”
The moment my teammates got behind me, Riakis began to rush at us in a last-ditch attack.
[Riakis’s corrupted power has begun to overflow.]
It was only natural that a boss would have an explosive finishing move. Now, it was a race against time.
[Blessing for Pilgrims: a mysterious energy concealed in the Chaos has begun to purify Riakis’s corruption.]
It would only take about ten minutes for Riakis to completely purify his corrupted body. Before that happened, we needed to land one final—
“M-Mister!” Erwen shouted.
What was the problem? There shouldn’t have been any curveballs to worry about at this point.
“Th-there are a few dozen people heading this way! Very quickly as well!”
“What?” Dozens? Who the hell was it? Was it the barbarians we left back at the camp? Did they come because they were worried about us? That was the first possibility that came to mind.
“...I think it’s the Sawtooth Clan!”
Well, nothing in the world ever came easy, huh?
“What?! Didn’t they fail?” Ainar yelled, unable to hide her bewilderment. I felt the same way.
What... Why are they suddenly coming back?
I didn’t get it at all. Not only that, but they were coming in a group of dozens. If there were that many of them still alive, why was Riakis just wandering around alone? Didn’t they fail?
I had countless unanswered questions. However, right now, there was one thing I knew for sure.
They’re coming...
This was the worst-case scenario for us. There was no way they’d had a change of heart.
For them to come back just as we were about to land the final blow...
They wouldn’t just sit back and watch us kill him.
Yeah, but regardless...
This doesn’t change a thing.
[Purification Rate: 1%]
There were about ten minutes left until Riakis fully recovered. And our safest bet was to assume the actual time was even less than that.
Thus, I acted like the simple, fearless barbarian I now was.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
“M-Mister?”
“What are you doing?! Hurry up and kill it!”
We could worry about the future later.

chapters.title: Chapter 461: Proof (1)
paragraphs: The time limit on this destructive attack pattern was ten minutes, and once those ten minutes were up, Riakis would fully recover, nullifying any damage the player had inflicted on him thus far. Considering the countless ridiculous conditions Dungeon and Stone forced its players to deal with, this one was actually pretty reasonable.
[Purification Rate: 3%]
If you could just land one final blow within those ten minutes, the battle would be over. And there wouldn’t be any surprise attack patterns or new phases thrown at you in the meantime.
I tried to focus on being as calm, collected, and cautious as possible without getting too antsy.
Fwooosh!
Erwen shot an arrow at him at full power. Even as it sliced through the air, however, Riakis seemed to spot it with his upgraded corrupted eyes and dodged it.
Please, can’t you just die already? I really don’t have time to deal with you.
[Purification Rate: 7%]
The more Riakis continued to evade and defend against our attacks, the more anxious and impatient I became. On top of that, I wasn’t the only one losing my patience.
“Erwen! Don’t you know how to shoot an arrow?!”
“Why don’t you try shooting it, then?!”
“Behel—aaaaaah!” Ainar bellowed, leaping into the air like she always did when trying to land a finishing blow. When Riakis was within reach, she drove her sword into his shoulder blade.
Slash!
The cut wasn’t deep enough, though. Perhaps that was why Ainar was also getting more frustrated than usual.
Stab!
She steadied herself on his shoulder as she pulled out the sword and jammed it in again. However, no matter how hard she tried, it wasn’t doing any damage.

“Argh!” Suddenly, a tail wrapped around Ainar’s waist like a tentacle and effortlessly lifted her into the air. Fortunately, Amelia, who was nearby, managed to sprint forward and rescue Ainar by slashing through the tail with her dagger.
“Ugh! Th-thanks—”
“Calm yourself, barbarian. At least while we’re in battle.”
“Y-Yeah... sorry!”
“Apologize to that kid too. She’s been contributing the most to this fight after Yandel.”
“Erwen! Sorry! I’m sorry I yelled at you for missing!”
“...I didn’t care anyway.”

The sight of Amelia scolding Ainar and Erwen awkwardly accepting the apology warmed my heart. I couldn’t be prouder as their captain. However, this was neither the time nor the place for all that, especially when we were on a time limit.
“Hey! We just need to land one more attack!” I yelled out in irritation as everyone quickly wrapped up their conversations and concentrated on the battle.
Boom!
Riakis swung his front paw once more. Instead of trying to tank the attack with my shield, I decided to step back to negate some of the impact.
We can still pull this off.
I forcibly reigned in my mounting frustration before it could take on a mind of its own.
[Purification Rate: 9%]

We weren’t in bad condition at the moment, though after thirty minutes of nonstop battle, the MP of our DPSers was slowly bottoming out. However, that was the worst of it. This type of boss monster grew easier to deal with the longer you were able to hold it back.
Guoooooo!
The next scream told me his Purification Rate must be at 10 percent.
Not that that even mattered. Who cared about the Purification Rate when the Sawtooth Clan was on its way here?
“Erwen, how long until your next attack?”
“About seventy-five seconds!”
Damn. Then this would really be our last chance.
“Raaah!” I let out a war cry and ran at Riakis. I had to periodically use Wild Outburst to raise my Threat Level stat so his aggro never fell on anyone other than me.
Slam!
It was my job to block Riakis’s attacks before he could reach my damage dealers.
[Purification Rate: 15%]

A few good hits from Riakis’s paw would break even someone as tough as Ainar to pieces. He was so powerful that if this were Phase Three, even I would have had no choice but to simply draw aggro and run away from him. Luckily, the fact that this was Phase Four made it possible for me to hold my own against him even without the help of a priest or wizard.
“Mister!”
Hm? Did she already finish charging up her next attack? There should still be sixty-two seconds left, though.
“Here!” It was a clause without a subject, but I immediately understood what she was saying.
Just my luck.
It had been less than three minutes since we first noticed them. How did they run here so fast?
Erwen continued her briefing as I focused on tanking Riakis’s attacks. “From the right!”
I spared a sideways glance to see dozens of people in the distance quickly approaching.
Thud!
I dropped my shield and hammer onto the ground.

Amelia met my gaze, and her eyes flew wide open as soon as she processed what I’d done. To be fair, the sight of me dropping my weapons and gunning straight for Riakis would shock anyone. Where else would she have ever seen something so wild?
I wrapped my arms around the neck of the giant monster like I was trying to drag him down to the ground.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
My tight grip on him didn’t let up even as he tried to forcibly shake me off. Instead, I strangled him with all the strength I had in my arms.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

I called this move the Giant Barbarian Choke. It was similar to the move I used when wrestling that Troll on the fourth floor, but there were two key differences. One was that both I and the monster I was choking were several times larger.
What strength...
The second was that I couldn’t manage to get a perfect grip on his neck like with the Troll.
Guoooooo!
I was struggling to even defend against his attacks earlier, so of course I’d be struggling to hold onto him now. Just because we were in a similar weight class didn’t mean we shared a Strength stat.
“B-Bjorn!”
Rising up on his hind legs, he stood bipedally, using his front paws to grasp at my arms as they continued to clutch his neck in a stranglehold.
Seventy-two seconds.
The monster struggled to throw me aside as I tried to choke him out.
Seventy-three seconds.
I fought to hold on with every bit of strength I had left in me, but it wasn’t enough.
Crack.
The wrist guards of my already half-shattered lithinum armor buckled in his grip like tin cans, and the arms I had around his neck loosened their hold.
Seventy-four seconds.
But so what?
“It’s too late, you bastard.”
That was seventy-five seconds. Finally, Erwen was done charging. I couldn’t wait to see this wrist-crushing bastard blown to bits.
Seventy-six seconds...
What? Why wasn’t she shooting him? My confused gaze darted to where Erwen was pulling the string of her bow taut.
Phew, thankfully I didn’t get the timing wrong.
“Shoot!”
The second the shout left my lips, a giant flash filled the area.
Fwoosh!
From this angle, it truly looked like a bolt of lightning.
Kaboooooom!
The massive explosion was enough to knock me unconscious, and when I came to my senses a moment later, I was lying on the hard ground. My ears were ringing, but at this point, I didn’t care.
[Lord of Chaos Riakis has cast Corrupted Heart.]
I scrambled to my feet and watched him from a safe distance.
His entire body was pitch-black and he was shrieking in pain, though no sound could be heard.
[The corrupted power within Riakis has begun to overflow.]

Like a water balloon being squeezed, Riakis’s body distorted, growing and shrinking randomly. Ainar and Erwen held their weapons at the ready, still on guard, but there was no need for that. It was all over now.
[The ancient Pilgrim has rejected the corrupted power.]

With an unstable pop, the beast’s body finally burst in a violent flash of light, like a nuclear explosion. The dazzling rays eventually faded away, and my vision slowly returned. The changes to the entire floor were immediately apparent.
The labyrinth was no longer glowing red.
[You have killed the Lord of Chaos, Riakis. EXP +100]
[Lord of the Floor Kill Bonus. EXP +15]
In the spot where Riakis once lay were instead tens of thousands of light particles, all scattering into the air.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Defeat your first Lord of the Floor.]
[Reward: Your Soul Power has permanently increased by +50.]
With this, the hunt was finally over.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Defeat the Lord of Chaos, Riakis.]
[Reward: ???]

It was a strange feeling. Even though we’d only really landed the final blow, I’d still managed to defeat a monster that I’d had to run from, helpless, a few years ago. However, there was no time to bask in our victory. With the battle finished it was now time to collect the rewards.
Shaaaaaa.
I stared at the thousands of light particles fluttering away like cherry blossoms in the spring. What ended up dropping?
Ba-dum.
My heart raced in my chest.

There were three rewards that a Lord of the Floor could drop. The first was a Floor Treasure, which was even more valuable than a Numbered Item. The second was a Floor Stone, which could forcibly open a rift on the floor.
Please, please, please be an essence...!
Last but in no way least was a Floor Essence, which in a way, was even more valuable than one from a rank-one monster.
A Floor Treasure would be great, but please be an essence!
As I patiently waited and prayed, the particles of light eventually faded away as our reward materialized.
[No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck has been activated.]
...It was an essence. There was no Floor Treasure or Floor Stone to be seen.
“Bjorn... there...! It’s...!”
An essence had dropped, but now the problem was...
...Look at their faces.
The Sawtooth Clan had come close enough that even I could see their naked desperation and shock. I assumed they were urgently shouting at me, but unfortunately, I couldn’t hear them.
Now, what should we do? There was no need to waste any more precious time. As soon as I saw the essence drop, I moved.
“Erwen!”
Erwen said something to me, but I couldn’t make it out over the ringing in my ears either. Therefore I had no choice.
“The... me? But... you...!”
“I’ll explain later.”
I hoisted Erwen up by her delicate waist and threw her.
“...Eeek!”
I heard her let out a strangled cry as my hearing gradually returned, but I paid it no mind. I had quite a lot of experience with stuff like this by now.
What’s with this feeling of nostalgia?
Maybe it was because I fed her the Goblin Archer essence the same way.
[The Essence of Chaos has sunk deep into Erwen Fornacci di Tersia’s soul.]
“Uhhh...”
After absorbing the Essence of Chaos, that was the first noise to come out of Erwen’s mouth.
“Wh-why did you give it to me...? Y-You should have been the one to take it, M-Mister.”
So that was what she was trying to say earlier. I appreciated the gesture, but there was no need for her to worry about something like that.
“That was an essence I was planning to give you one day.”

More precisely, I’d wanted her to have this essence the moment I heard she signed a contract with each of the Four Great Spirits. Only after a character did so did the true value of this essence shine, though I never expected she would be able to obtain it so soon.
“S-Still, this is an essence from the Lord of the Floor, so...”
“Why? Are you planning to ditch me just like you did after I gave you that Goblin Archer essence before?”
“No! Never! I would never do that!”
All right, then it’s fine.

The Essence of Chaos didn’t suit a barbarian in the first place. Well, aside from the inherent value of possessing such a unique essence, of course. This one was even stronger than a core rank-three essence... However, there was a limit of one Floor Essence per character.
And it’s impossible to get rid of one once you take it, even if you go to the temple.
The one I planned to take for myself was upstairs.
“Yandel.”
Anyway, I needed to focus on the present. Those bastards happened to arrive at the perfect time.
“Baron Yandel, what the hell have you done?!” Daggers, who stood at the front of the group, launched into a tirade the moment he arrived. “I’m sure I told you to stop what you were doing!”
Oh, was he not even bothering with the whole respectful shtick now?
“Ah, about that. I couldn’t hear you.”
“That’s ridiculous!”
“But even if I did hear you, I wouldn’t have stopped anyway.”
The moment I pushed back, Daggers shut up and glowered at me.
Amelia then spoke up from nearby. “Yandel.”
“I know.”

It didn’t take long for the other members of the Sawtooth Clan to surround us. Judging by how smoothly they got into position, I got the sense that this wasn’t their first time. Maybe Daggers had given them some sort of signal in advance? Or maybe they had done this so often, it was practically second nature to them? Whatever the case, I didn’t back down.
“Malid Kevron, the vice captain of the Sawtooth Clan.”
“...Speak.”
“Do you even realize what the hell you’re doing right now?”

He glared daggers at me. “What are you talking about? I am simply asking you a question. Why did you suddenly choose to rob us when we were in the middle of our raid against Riakis? As a former adventurer yourself, I’m sure you know that in the labyrinth, adventurers show no mercy to plunderers.”
I sighed. I had expected them to confront us the moment we took the essence right in front of them, but still.
“Even though fighting you won’t benefit us in any way,” he grumbled, almost as an afterthought.
These guys really needed someone to set their heads straight.

chapters.title: Chapter 462: Proof (2)
paragraphs: My skin was still hot from the battle, but the cold air cooled it down as I met the hostile gazes circling me.
I never imagined they would come at us so blatantly.

The atmosphere was so ripe for a fight that I wouldn’t be surprised if a battle broke out right here and now, but I tried to remain coolheaded as I took stock of the situation. The worst was already behind us. Since they were threatening us, that meant they wanted something.
If they were really going to kill us, they would have pretended to let us leave and attacked us when we let our guard down.
So why were they bluffing? That was what I needed to find out. Not that I didn’t have a guess or two, but I couldn’t be certain yet.

“A plunderer...” As soon as I finished thinking things over, I let out a hearty laugh. “Then let me ask you this. On what grounds do you think I stole from you? Riakis was wandering around on his own when we saw him. Isn’t that right, Erwen?”

“Huh? Oh, that’s right! There were no other adventurers within a thousand-yard radius. Going off precedent, that alone would be reason enough for any claim over Riakis to be nullified.” Erwen kindly testified on my behalf, firing off facts.
Daggers, however, wasn’t the type of person to back down in the face of logic. “That might be the case against a regular monster, but this is the Lord of the Floor we are talking about.”
“So what are you trying to say?”
“Our clan being separated while fighting Riakis was inevitable and is no indication we ever intended to relinquish our claim.”
Judging by the equipment he was wearing, I had a feeling I knew exactly what had happened. After all, how else could all his gear be perfectly fine even after the third phase?
They retreated to change into the new equipment they had stored in their sub-spaces.

They must have sent out a team as bait to buy them time to put on new gear. Their plan was for that team to run around just long enough for the main team to change their equipment and rejoin them. However, surely they weren’t blind enough to miss the fact that not a single member of that bait team was here right now.
They must have realized at some point that all of them were dead. Once they found out, they ran back here, but by then it was already too late.
I figured those were the broad strokes of what happened, although it was impossible to know for sure. I couldn’t picture it playing out much differently, though.
“You purposely interfered in our raid against the Lord of the Floor. We are the ones who managed to deal all that damage and reduce him to that state.”
“How were we supposed to know what happened to you?”
“Regardless of that fact, you still ignored my attempts at conversation and took the essence for yourselves.”
“And what’s wrong with that? We killed the monster, so we get the loot.”
“But we were the ones who managed to get its health down to that point. Without us, you would have never been able to kill that beast.”

Well, even I couldn’t deny that. But given the context clues, wasn’t it obvious that these bastards were the ones who summoned the Lord of the Floor in the first place without permission? Since they had failed to kill it, I was perfectly within my rights to step forward and finish it off before any other innocent adventurers got hurt. All those things went without saying.
“So what do you want?” I got straight to the point. No matter how long we went back and forth debating this, neither side would acquiesce. This wasn’t a matter of mere logic, after all.

“Make a promise right here, right now, in the name of the glorious royal family of Rafdonia. Acknowledge your mistakes and promise to pay the price for the Floor Essence you stole when you return to the city.”
Whether in the labyrinth, in the city, or any other place people inhabited, it was always strength that decided the victor.
“If you promise us that, we will no longer consider your actions here today plundering.”

Simply put, if I didn’t make that promise to them, they would label me a plunderer and start PKing us. Sure enough, things would quickly escalate now that I’d cut to the chase. We now had three options to choose from.
One: make the promise and pay them back. Even with my hoard of savings, it would take me years of struggle to pay off the debt. Still, we had the essence, so it wouldn’t be a total loss.

Two: make the promise but break it later. However, there was a recording crystal filming us right now, so I couldn’t simply break the oath without facing future punishment. I would definitely be stripped of my noble title for besmirching the name of the royal family too.
Then did that leave me with just one option?
Three: prove that my logic was right.
There was no need to hesitate. The answer was obvious.
“Then, what do you say?”
What other choice did I have?
“No matter how I look at it...” I said, picking up my hammer and slinging it over my shoulder. “I don’t remember making any mistakes.”
“...So you’re choosing to drink the poisoned wine?”
“Who cares as long as it’s alcohol? Alcohol is never sweet anyway.”
“Your Lordship... you seem to think that we really won’t attack you?”
Well, no, that wasn’t true. After all, clan wars were just a natural part of the game.

“Ainar! Emily! Erwen!” I quickly called out the names of my comrades, only realizing a beat later that I had forgotten to call on our navigator, Auyen. It was too late now, though. It wasn’t like he would be much help in this situation anyway. “Everyone, prepare for battle!”

As soon as I gave the order, my team all grabbed their weapons in unison as they readied themselves. We all stood with our backs to each other. Even Auyen quickly came over and joined us after Amelia shot him a look.
“If anyone comes near you, kill them,” I spoke loud enough for everyone to hear, my eyes glued to Dagger’s. “I’ll take full responsibility.”
Now, what happened here was in his hands.
A tense silence fell as we leveled our weapons at each other. It dragged on for quite some time too.
I sighed inwardly.
I wish he would hurry up and decide. How long do we have to stay like this?

Even though I was getting frustrated, I didn’t make any moves to provoke them. The best-case scenario here would be no fighting. Though the individuals of our clan were far more skilled than theirs, they outnumbered us in essences by a landslide. There was a very high chance that one of us would get injured if a battle broke out. Nevertheless, I still chose to face them head-on for a very simple reason.
That bastard has just as much on the line here as we do.

If a Floor Treasure had dropped, then they would have been guaranteed to walk away with something after beating us. But now? They stood to gain nothing by fighting us. Even if they cut us open, it wasn’t like the essence would reappear. At best, they’d walk away with our equipment, but the consequences they’d face for killing a noble when they returned to the city wouldn’t be worth it.
But it must be eating at him to have to back down.
In short, this was a game of chicken. The first person who stopped running toward the cliff at full tilt was the loser, but if no one stopped, we would all fall off the cliff together.
“Half...” That was when Daggers opened his locked jaw. “I will ask for only half the value of the essence.”
A decent compromise was proposed right as we were both nearing the edge of the cliff.
“Half, hm...”
“Wouldn’t you agree that we were the ones who ended up taking the most damage while reducing the Lord of the Floor to that state?”

That was true. They’d suffered at least fourteen deaths on their side, and it would take them years and a ridiculous amount of money and effort to fill those vacancies. However, half the cost of the essence would be just enough to cover the cost of their damaged equipment and consumables.
Daggers continued to try and sell me on this deal. “Of course, the price of the essence will be based on a fair appraisal by the guild’s committee—”
“Thanks for the offer, but I refuse,” I said, as I saw no reason to let him keep going.
“You... refuse?” he echoed, dumbfounded.

Why did he look so surprised? The person who chickened out first always walked away with nothing. Adventurers didn’t put their lives and pride on the line for no reason. The moment he backed down an inch, it became clear to me that he didn’t have the guts to go all the way.
So why should I have to give up anything for him?
At this point, I would have to be born yesterday to not recognize that he was bluffing.

“I’m telling you this upfront. Even if you halve the price again, I still don’t plan on changing my answer,” I declared like I already knew what he was going to say next. “So stop talking and come at me.”

Even after my outright provocation, however, he didn’t rush to draw his weapon and attack me. Instead, all he could do was keep flapping those lips of his like before. “...Calm down and think this through rationally.”
“I’m being more rational than ever.”
“...You really are a reckless man, Baron Yandel.”
“Well, I don’t think that’s something that a man who called a baron of the royal family a plunderer should say.”
“Then... are you absolutely sure you can handle the consequences?”
What the hell was he going on about now? “Do you think I would be standing here if I was afraid of things like that?”
I’m not all bark and no bite like you.
“I’ll give you until the count of three. If you don’t approach me first, I’m going to treat you as an assassin who’s come to kill me.”
“Th-that’s ridiculous...”
“One.”

As soon as I started to count, Daggers froze. He was completely terrified, unsure of how to cope with the turn this situation had taken. What am I supposed to do, just step back? his face screamed. No, I don’t think they’ll actually attack us, especially when we have this many people on our side... But maybe he will. Barbarians aren’t known for their common sense.
“Two.”

Despite the million thoughts racing through his mind, he was still unable to come up with an answer. Well, I could understand why. It hadn’t been long since he became the vice captain, so he must have been feeling a lot of pressure to make the right call.
“And that’s three.” I stepped forward, intent on shoving him onto his back. If I swung my hammer at him, that might knock an answer into his head.
“Vice captain!”

However, the archer standing to the right of Daggers suddenly stepped forward and muttered something in his ear. I couldn’t hear what they were saying, so they must have activated Voice Control. I was curious about what had caused their archer to interrupt.
“Mister, other adventurers are approaching.”
“...What?”
“It seems that hundreds of them are...”
Hundreds? Where the hell did all these adventurers even come—
“I think they’re the ones who were with us earlier.”
Ah... them.
I never expected our friends to come to the rescue.
Well... doesn’t that work out in our favor?
Daggers turned to glare at me again, his teeth clenched and brows furrowed. It seemed he’d received a similar report. Since there was no way to handle this quietly anymore, he had only one choice.
“...Everyone, lower your weapons.”
Yeah, that’s right.

As soon as he gave the command, they all lowered their weapons and prepared to retreat. Perhaps because he was upset at leaving things at that, Daggers made one last parting shot as he turned away. “...I’ll see you in the city, Baron Yandel.”
I sighed. It looked like there was even more work waiting for me when we got back.
After the Sawtooth Clan left, we waited around for the few hundred low-rank adventurers to arrive.
“Ohhh! Chieftain! Congratulations on your incredible achievement!”
“Hahaha! As expected of our chieftain! Of course he could do it!”

The barbarian warriors let out celebratory shouts as they ran toward us in the distance. Since they were blocking the way, I had to cast Giantization to get a look at the rest of the crowd and find the one person who could tell me what was happening.
“Lewis Seyur! What’s going on here?”
“Well... as soon as we realized that the Lord of the Floor had been defeated, everyone here wanted to come and thank you...”
So they recklessly ran in the direction we had disappeared to earlier, huh? That wasn’t to say I didn’t appreciate it, of course.
Well, setting their goodwill aside, shouldn’t I be the one thanking them for helping us deal with that mess?
Thanks to them, we’d managed to get through our encounter with the Sawtooth Clan without any bloodshed.
Now that I think about it, when we get back to the city, I might need their testimony.
With that in mind, I began approaching the other adventurers present, exchanging brief conversations with them as I memorized their names.
“Bent Mahaylo, right? I remember you.”
“...I-It’s an honor!”
The more I talked with the low-rank adventurers, the stranger the look in their eyes became.
“How can he be so kind to people like us...?”
“Even though he’s a barbarian, he truly is an incredibly respectful man.”
“He is someone that deserves the title of hero.”
Um...
I was just doing this so I could take advantage of them later, but I didn’t bother trying to change their minds.
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has increased by +1.]
[Your Reputation has...]
Well, I need to raise my Reputation stat whenever I can, I guess.
“We’ll be going now!”
After memorizing their names and where they lived, I quickly got ready to leave.
“Going...? Oh, are you going upstairs?”
“No. There’s something else I need to do.”

There was no point in going to the fourth floor now. It was already the fifteenth day, so by the time we made it to the fifth floor, the labyrinth would be closing. Plus, I honestly wanted to take a break after all that hard work.
“Mister, where are we going now?” Erwen asked me as she continued to pack our belongings.
“The Witch’s Hut,” I replied.
“What? The hut...”
“You mean that shelter in the woods? Why do you want to go there?”
Why wouldn’t we? Tsk, that was the problem with these three. They didn’t know anything. Now that we’d defeated the Lord of Chaos...
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Defeat the Lord of Chaos, Riakis.]
[Reward: ???]
It was time to go and take our question-mark reward.

chapters.title: Chapter 463: Proof (3)
paragraphs: [You have entered the Witch’s Hut.]
This was my first time back at the Witch’s Hut since the ordeal Missha and I went through together. However, there were a lot of differences between then and now.
Shaaaaaa...
For one thing, we didn’t find ourselves in a grassy field full of flowers and trees rich with leaves.
“...Snow?”
Instead, those things were replaced by a white, snowy field. Through the bare, ice-covered branches of the trees, we could spy the hut in the distance.

“Wow! It’s snow! Whoa, it’s so cold!” Ainar displayed a childlike excitement at the sight of the snow on the ground. Well, it didn’t snow in Rafdonia. Aside from Ice Rock, some islands on the sixth floor, and a few Rifts, it was hard to come across snow. Even the Frost Canyon on the fifth floor was more a field made of ice than anything.
“Rockrock, come here!”
“...It’s not Rockrock. His name is Auyen Rockrobe,” Amelia tried to correct.
“Hey, why are you being so uptight? Aren’t we all friends now?” Ainar waved Amelia off, skipped over to Auyen, and dragged him away to start a snowball fight. “Anyway, get over here!”
“...H-Huh? Ack! Th-that hurts! Ms. Raines—!”
“Yandel, what are you planning to do about her?” Amelia asked scoldingly, but in my opinion, it was only natural that a barbarian would want to have a snowball fight.
“Dunno. I was planning on going and helping Erwen assess her new essence right now.”
“Yeah. I figured you wouldn’t bother to do anything.”
“No, that’s not what I was saying...”
“Whatever. Just go check out the essence. I’ll stay here and keep an eye on them.”
“...You’re not coming along?”
“I was going to have to discipline Ainar one of these days anyway.”
With that ominous declaration, Amelia jogged over to Auyen and Ainar.
“Oh! Are you joining us?!”
“Yeah.”
After activating Self-Replication, she quickly started to bombard Ainar with snowballs.
“Hahaha! Haha! Take this!”
At first, Ainar was happy to be playing with her new friends, but it didn’t take long for the joy to disappear.
“...Ow, owww! Wh-what are you—?!”
Amelia lunged forward and pinned Ainar to the floor, restraining her arms. She then pushed her face down, shoving it into the snow.
“Urgh!”
“This is the snow you love so much.”
“Th-this isn’t what I heard a snowball fight was!”
“If it’s a fight, why would there be rules?”
“Aaagh! I won’t just sit here and take this!” Ainar gathered all her brute force and stumbled to her feet.
Amelia countered by wrapping her legs around Ainar’s arms. “What can you do without your arms?”
Taking advantage of Ainar’s inability to guard herself, Amelia’s clone continued to throw snowballs straight into Ainar’s face.
Splat! Splat! Splat!
She looked like a professional baseball pitcher, each snowball right on target.
“...Mister?”
“...Yeah, let’s just go.”
“Okay.”

After watching them for a while, we finally left the three of them alone and headed toward the back of the cabin. The Witch’s Hut was the best place to train. Not only was it a private space, but there was no need to worry about breaking something and having to pay for it like the training grounds in the city.
“Erwen, have you started to get used to it?”
“Yes.”
“How do you feel?”
“I’m not sure. I feel like I’ve gotten more powerful overall, but I can’t pinpoint any areas where I feel a particular boost...”
“Is that it?”
“...I’ve also had a headache for a while now.”
She didn’t have a headache. She was just having a hard time restraining herself. Well, considering how she used to be, she had gotten a lot better at not letting it show.
“It’s because of the essence. Don’t worry too much.”
“What? Because of the essence...?” Erwen’s eyes lit up with curiosity. I slowly began to explain her new ability to her.

With Chaos, her negative stats were doubled, and all her positive stats increased proportionately to the negative stats. In the game, the only thing you were shown was your character’s basic stats, so like always, it had been up to me as the player to figure out the exact details and calculations for each essence and ability.
“Negative stats... Are you talking about my weakened stats?”
Ah, I guess I’ll have to explain that first.
“That’s part of it, but there’s also more to it.”

In Dungeon and Stone, each stat had a corresponding coefficient, and your Physical, Spirit or Special Ability stats increased according to that coefficient. For example, the coefficient of the Dexterity stat was set to 0.5, meaning that each time that stat increased by +1, the Special Ability stat rose by 0.5 in kind.
High-value stats can even have a coefficient of three.
That wasn’t the important part, though. Most stats had coefficients that were greater than zero. However, some went into the negatives. These were known as “minus stats.”
“For example, among your stats, you have Impulse and Distrust.”

Basically, when you got a plus-something to a stat with a negative coefficient, they had a negative effect on your Physical, Spirit, and Special Ability stats. Conversely, when you got a minus sign attached to a stat with a positive coefficient, they were what was known as “weakened stats,” like what Erwen mentioned. This was the case with the essence that gave her Rupture, which gave her a -30 to Control.
After giving her a basic rundown of the two kinds of negative stats, I quickly began to calculate what Erwen’s might be.

First off, her Evan essence decreased her Physical Resistance by -80. Ritcanon, which was the essence she received as a reward from the royal family and the one I had recommended to her, had a Soul Power Regeneration of -40. Rupture had a Control stat of -30. Lastly, Kalban had an Impulse of +30 and a Distrust of +30.

There was no need to calculate the Possessiveness stat that came with the Metcrow essence because the coefficient of that one is zero. She also erased her +40 Craving stat before entering the labyrinth to make room...
After multiplying her stats according to their respective coefficients and then taking the Essence of Chaos’s 0.2 coefficient into account, I finished my calculations.
That was the stat boost Erwen had received from the Chaos essence. Not that every single one of her stats had increased, of course. Innate stats like Luck and Bone Density weren’t affected.
...Still, the rate she’s developing is no joke.
I was shocked. I may have recommended that she obtain the Ritcanon essence all those years ago, but all of the other incredible essences she had were things she had obtained on her own.
I do think the negative impact on her mental state is a bit dangerous...
But she seemed to be doing fine. Even though each of those stats was now higher than before, she was still acting the same.
Still, I can’t help but worry. I should hurry and change out one of her other essences.

Spirit stats had low coefficients to begin with, so they weren’t all that effective when you used them in conjunction with the Essence of Chaos. Control wasn’t all that bad, but Distrust only had a coefficient of 0.6. Replacing it with a stat that had a higher coefficient value would be better in the long run. For example, if I gave her something with a Mana Resistance of -50, then all of her stats would grow by +30.

Whatever the case, thanks to its effect, the Essence of Chaos was great for any DPS main. On the flip side, there weren’t that many good essences for tanks, as most only raised their defense in exchange for lower damage dealt.
“I see... You once told me it’s best to specialize in what you’re good at...”
Hm? Did I tell her that? I couldn’t remember, but no big deal. We were no longer in that shabby old inn.
“Now, try and use your new abilities!”
It was time to reap the benefits of her new essence.

The Chaos essence came with two skills and two skills alone, one passive and one active. That might seem lackluster when compared to a Guardian’s essence, which could have up to five different active skills. However, it was way better to have one incredible skill rather than a hundred crappy ones.
[(P) Chaos Circuit: All resources available to the user are combined into one. After all resources are consumed, the user can utilize the power of Chaos.]

The passive skill was rather unique. Simply put, it put all resources—such as Mana, Natural Power, Soul Power, Divine Power, and more—together in a single gauge. That alone was an incredible skill to have. After all, it was incredibly hard to raise one’s Natural Power, which was essential for elemental abilities.
Maybe that’s why Erwen took the Ertes essence. She could use its passive skill to change her Soul Power into Natural Power.
But since she didn’t need it anymore, it would be best to get rid of it. The active skill Element Synthesis wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t something she would need in the end game.
“Um... Which ability should I use...?”
“Try using Concentrated Fire. The goal is to use up all the energy you have. Oh, you should summon a spirit while you’re at it.”
“...If that’s the goal, should I call on Dicloe? Doing so will use up my energy much quicker.”
Ah, that was a good point. I patted her on the back to encourage her as Erwen trembled, focusing on summoning Dicloe.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned Dicloe, the Elemental Ruler of Darkness].
A black blob appeared, taking the vague form of a person as it tore through reality itself. Erwen then commanded Dicloe to shoot countless dark spheres in the opposite direction of the hut.
Bang! Boom! Clash!
The dark spheres crashed into the barrier in the distance. As expected, it didn’t even leave a scratch on it.
[All resources have been exhausted.]
After roughly thirty seconds of going all out, she had completely exhausted all her energy. In the past, her limit had been five seconds.
Maybe it’s because she has more mana now, but she’s able to maintain that level of power for a lot longer.
Of course, that wasn’t what mattered now.
[A mysterious energy makes itself known following the exhaustion of all resources.]
Within a few seconds of her exhausting all of her energy, the Chaos Circuit kicked in and activated what I liked to call Infinite Power Mode.
[For one minute, Erwen Fornacci di Tersia will not consume any resources.]

“...My summon really isn’t dispelling?” Erwen marveled at the sight of Dicloe still firing off dark spheres at full power. Although I had already known how this ability worked, I was pretty shocked myself.
For one minute and thirty seconds, she can continuously wield this level of firepower...
That wasn’t all. Her MP in this mode was essentially infinite. She could let the Elemental Rulers do their jobs while she used her own skills.
“Erwen, try shooting Concentrated Fire now.”
Erwen quickly raised her bow without a word.
Whooosh!
A white light shined at the tip of her arrow. This skill had played an essential role in our fight against Riakis, and it had a rather simple effect.
Whoooooosh!

Though MP was rapidly consumed in proportion to the amount of time you spent charging it, the damage it dealt increased exponentially in return. Normally, the longest Erwen could charge it was no more than fifteen seconds. Any longer and the MP consumption would not be worth the damage boost. Instead, it was better to rest during the sixty-second cooldown time and then fire another shot afterward.
But with infinite MP, it’s a whole other story.
One second, two seconds, three seconds, four seconds... As time went by, the density of the energy gathered at the tip of the arrow continued to increase.
“Now.”
Erwen finally released her grip on the bowstring. A bright light tore through the air, slicing across the sky in a brilliant arc. The attack ultimately wouldn’t leave a mark on the barrier. But...
Y-Yes! This is it.
I could tell just by looking at it.
Boooooom!
Her firepower far exceeded Dicloe’s.
[The mysterious energy inside Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has drained away.]
[All stats are temporarily reduced by 70 percent.]
Erwen collapsed into my arms, completely exhausted. Suddenly, I started to hear urgent shouts in the distance.
“B-Bjorn! Where are you?! Bjorn!” They were coming from Ainar, who had been playing with Amelia. “Wh-what was that just now?! I-Is it a dimensional collapse?! Sh-shouldn’t we run away?!”
She was acting like a wild animal experiencing a natural disaster. I smirked at her innocent reaction. “Don’t worry. It’s not a dimensional collapse.”
“R-Really?! That really surprised me! All of a sudden, a bright light flashed and the ground shook!”
“Yeah, I know. But you can calm down now. Everything is fine.”
As I calmed Ainar down, Amelia came over to me and asked, “Just now... Was that Tersia’s doing?”
“Yeah.”
“...Impressive. So that’s the power of a Floor Essence.”
“Don’t worry. I’ll make sure you get one later as well.”
As I kindly reassured her, she turned away and scolded me for trying to placate her like a barbarian. Based on her expression, it seemed that she was looking forward to it.
“Then, are you all done now?”

“Oh, yeah. We’re done.” She hadn’t tried out her active skill yet, but we couldn’t check that here anyway. We would have to experiment with it later on in the city. It was quite an unusual skill, after all.
“Erwen, can you walk?”
“No... I don’t think I can.”

Since Erwen was exhausted, I decided to carry her. Before I could lift her, however, somebody came running over. “Ah! Then I’ll carry you!” It was Ainar, who had been an expert at playing the role of steed in the old days. “Hop on! Any day now.”
“...Okay. Th-thanks...”

With Ainar carrying Erwen on her back, we headed into the hut. Unlike the new wintery landscape outside, the interior of the cabin was the same as before, from the bookshelf to the dining table, the carpet, and even the small bed my feet hung off of when I laid down on it.
Crackle.
Last of all was the burning fireplace.
“Yandel, what do we need to do now?”
“We just need to go into the fire.”
That way we could get our reward. Afterward, the Witch’s Hut would close, and we would be moved back to the forest.
“...Bjorn.” Suddenly, Ainar turned to me, her expression uncharacteristically serious. “I don’t think it’s a good idea to go into those flames.”
What was she even talking about right now? There wasn’t any point in answering her, so I simply squatted down and went into the fire first.
Fwoosh!
The flames were warm, but by no means burning.
[Your Spirit Resistance has permanently increased by +50.]
Nice, there’s the stat boost...
I closed my eyes as I was enveloped by a comforting warmth.
However, when I opened them, I froze. I was no longer in the Witch’s Hut. Instead, I was in a place I had never been before.
“Who are you?”
And there was a girl with the complexion of a ghost staring right at me.

chapters.title: Chapter 464: Proof (4)
paragraphs: The reward you received for defeating Riakis was simple. After the raid, you needed to go back to the hut and crawl inside the flames. Upon doing so, your Spirit Resistance would rise significantly, and then your character would be transported back to the Witch’s Forest.
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Defeat the Lord of Chaos, Riakis.]
[Reward: Your Spirit Resistance permanently increases by +50.]

After reopening the achievement window, you would see that the question marks had been replaced. The fact that you could only get the reward after heading to a designated place made it unique among the other hidden features of Dungeon and Stone. There was also a time limit, so if you tried to come back later, you wouldn’t receive the reward.
[Your Spirit Resistance has permanently increased by +50.]
With that simple UI message lacking any explanation or emotion, your character was granted a mysterious power, like you were being blessed by something hidden from the naked eye.

Every time I received this hidden reward, I tried to see if there was anything else I was missing, but my experiments always came up empty. Ultimately, I just figured that I must be overthinking things and there was nothing else hidden here.
[An error has occurred.]
So where the hell am I?
This was clearly not the Witch’s Forest.
[Your location cannot be logged. Character log transmission has been temporarily suspended.]
And who was this girl?
Step, step, step.
I was in a grassy field lit by the faint glow of a bonfire. Since the girl in front of me wasn’t answering my question, all I could do was search our surroundings for answers.
Eventually, the girl broke the silence. “...Elise Groundia.” Her voice rang directly in my head rather than passing through my ears, but surprisingly, she sounded pretty normal otherwise.
“...Shit.” However, that name sent goosebumps rippling over my entire body. That was how famous it was. “Ah, I’m sorry for swearing. I’m a barbarian, so sometimes I do that when I get surprised.”
I took a deep breath as I studied her. Judging by her expression, she wasn’t joking when she said that. But that didn’t mean I had to take her statement at face value.
Is she really the Earth Witch?

Even so, I eventually caved and determined that I needed to accept it. There was no particular reason for me to not believe her. Didn’t I already know that the witch was alive? Besides, the fact that I’d met this girl under these circumstances was proof enough that she wasn’t an ordinary kid.
Yeah, that makes sense. In fact, this is good for me.
If she really was the Witch, this was the perfect opportunity to dig up as much info as I—
“Don’t open the Gate of the Abyss.”
Huh? What did she just say?
Shaaaaaa!
While I was in a daze, trying to process that, an eerie wind blew by and the field before me began to smudge and fade. I desperately reached my hand out toward the Witch, who I could barely see now.
“...Yandel, what the hell do you think you’re doing?”
Instead of the girl, however, my fingertips met Amelia’s pissed-off face.
[Your location has been confirmed. Character log transmission has been resumed.]

I was suddenly back in the Witch’s Forest. Feeling disturbingly like I had just been possessed or something, I asked my teammates if they’d also experienced something similar when they followed behind me.
“...A field covered in fog? What are you talking about?”
“We just ended up here when we crawled through the fire!”

So they didn’t experience the same thing. “I guess I must have just been confused.” I couldn’t figure out exactly what had happened, so I tabled the experience for now. Amelia shot me a suspicious look, but she didn’t ask any questions.
After checking the time, I decided to end our expedition here and spend the remaining time relaxing.
“Hey, Bjorn!”
“Fenelin, stop bothering him and leave him alone. It looks like he has a lot on his mind.”
“Oh, okay...”

Thanks to Amelia, I was able to spend a few minutes gathering my thoughts without interruption. The first thing I did was establish that that wasn’t just a dream—which meant that the girl I’d met really was the Earth Witch.
“Don’t open the Gate of the Abyss.”

Why would she tell me that? No, why was I the only one who’d experienced that phenomenon in the first place? It was the same with Auril Gavis as well—everyone seemed to have strange expectations of me.
...Is it because I cleared the original game?
I sighed. Every day, I put my all into getting things done, so why did it seem like the number of things on my plate kept growing?
[The labyrinth is now closed.]
No matter how thoroughly I analyzed the strange experience, I didn’t manage to come up with any answers to my many questions before we were sent back.
[You are being transported to Rafdonia.]
The dreary sky over the city was the same as always.
“Wait a minute, isn’t that man...?”
“It’s Baron Yandel...”
When I returned to Dimension Square, a lot of the adventurers seemed shocked to see me there. I didn’t pay them any mind since this had already become the norm for me.
“...Things were really dicey this time.”
“Thankfully, none of us died. Let’s head back home and rest.”
