I had no idea, and whatever choice I did end up making, I’d have no way of knowing for sure whether it was the right one. Well, that was why 99 percent of first attempts ended in failure.
“Five minutes have passed. I’ve given you enough time to think things through, so I’ll give each of you a chance.”
Suddenly, I regained full control of my body. It seemed the first one up was me.
Clang.
He threw a dagger that landed at my feet. “Pick it up. Goblin poison was applied to it, so your friends will be able to die painlessly.”
This bastard.
When I stayed put and just glared at him, he simply smiled and nodded his head. “If only everyone was like you.” With that, my body became immobile again.
Step, step.
He moved down the line to stand in front of someone else. “Pick it up.” He said the same line but Erwen remained silent.
Ba-bump, ba-bump, ba-bump.
My heart just wouldn’t calm. What a strange reaction. I trusted Erwen 100 percent, yet deep down, I couldn’t help but worry.
“One person. You just have to stab one of them, and you’ll walk away from here alive, cleansed of your sins.”
I flinched at his remark as a sudden, intrusive image of Erwen stabbing Versyl popped into my head...
“...Fuck off.”
“You’re a foul-mouthed woman.”
Thankfully, Erwen’s turn also passed without issue. Then it was Ainar’s turn.
“Pick it up.”
“Behel—Gah!” As soon as her body was released, Ainar tried to rush at him with a shout, but he easily kicked her down to the floor and moved on to the next person.
Finally, it came down to Versyl.
“It’s your turn.”
As soon as she regained control of her body, she picked up the dagger on the floor with shaky hands. “Just one...? I... just have to stab one person...?”
Damn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 486: Pilgrim (4)
paragraphs: In a cavern strewn with corpses, an old man strode slowly toward the chamber’s center, then swept his hand across the monument there.
[The Last Great Sage, Diplan Groundel Gabrielius. In honor of his great first step.]
The monument had been built to commemorate the achievements of a great hero from ages past.
“...It’s almost done,” the old man murmured under his breath as he withdrew his hand. He fished out a book from his pocket.
Fwooo!
The book floated into the air, defying gravity as its pages fluttered open and flipped past one by one. At last, the final page of The Complete Book of Lords I revealed itself.

And so the Pilgrim sullied his faith by succumbing to the fear that gripped his heart. By running for his life, he eventually met his end, where he discovered that he had fled from one fear into the jaws of another even greater than his last: the fear of no longer having anyone by his side.

The fear of solitude swallowed the Pilgrim unawares. It was a horror that no person could hope to escape, one that destroyed body and soul by turning anger and hatred inward. Not even the Mother Goddess herself could save the Pilgrim now.
As the Pilgrim’s soul was extinguished, a newfound power and authority began to possess him, imbuing the once-mortal man with a violent, cursed energy.
Thus was the birth of he who spreads terror and despises faith: Dreadfear, the Lord of Terror.
Thud.
The book snapped shut, an old story buried in the annals of history, no longer remembered.
“I... just have to stab one person...?”

Versyl’s question knocked the breath right out of me. I wanted to shout at her, to demand why she would even ask such a thing, but my entire body was still frozen, rendering me incapable of making even the slightest of noises.
“Of course,” the man answered with a wide smile, “just one person. As long as you kill one of them, the empire will accept you once more.”

After a beat of hesitation, Versyl spoke, her voice trembling. I thought she would try to alleviate her guilt by apologizing to us, but instead, what she said was completely unexpected. “Now I’m sure of it. Mr. Yandel... you’ve been doubting me since earlier, right?”
Doubt? No, what the hell is she—?
“It seems I have another skill besides hiding my presence and healing wounds... I don’t know exactly what monster’s ability it is, but I can sense your emotions toward me clear as day.”
Damn it, I can’t believe she had something like that.

“Ms. Tersia as well... you feel the same way. You doubted me and genuinely debated whether to kill me when he made the offer. Even though you chose not to, you didn’t come to that decision because you trust me.”
Erwen didn’t respond, for obvious reasons.
“Of course, Ms. Fenelin was the only one who didn’t harbor any doubts or suspicions toward me.”
The more Versyl went on, the faster my heart pounded. We were doomed. I couldn’t stop her. I couldn’t even try to dissuade her because my body was frozen and I couldn’t say a word.
Ba-dump!
I had truly reached a new level of despair, one that even surpassed the kind I felt when Dreadfear displayed the ability to use aura and an AoE stun.

“But I understand why you would feel that way. It makes sense that it’d be harder for you to trust me, as you haven’t known me as long as you have everyone else.” Versyl’s hand suddenly stopped shaking around the dagger. “...Which is why I’ve decided to do it. If I don’t, someone else will do it first.”
Shit.
I closed my eyes. Even then, though, I never stopped trying to think of ways out of this. What could I do to prevent this disaster? There had to be something.

Yet no matter how hard I tried, I couldn’t come up with a single thing. Even when I hadn’t been able to stand, even when my equipment, essences, and stats had all been taken away from me, I never once lost hope. I had been convinced that there would be a way to kill the boss monster and make it out of this place alive.
But not anymore.
Shit!
This was unfair. It was completely unreasonable. It wasn’t like I was dying because I was weaker than a monster, made a huge mistake, or had failed to complete a task within the set amount of time.
“Stab a pilgrim. Cover your dagger with their filthy blood to prove your purity.”
Did one of us really have to die like this? Without so much as an opportunity to talk her out of it?
Versyl took a step closer to where I was being forced to kneel, then bent down so we were eye to eye, giving me a clear view of her expression.
“Mr. Yandel...” She looked like she was on the verge of tears. “At this rate, we’re going to fail, right?”

So in the end, it seemed she was choosing to stab me. Since there was no way for all of us to make it out alive, she must have decided to escape on her own. She tightened her grip on the dagger as I squeezed my eyes shut.
“So this will ensure we don’t all die.”
I was startled by the sensation of a soft hand gently caressing my cheek.
...What?

When I opened my eyes, I saw Versyl pointing the dagger at her own neck. She was holding it at an angle where Dreadfear wouldn’t be able to see it from behind. “I’ve made the wrong choices too many times.”
No, wait a minute.
“But now, this is the obvious choice to make. Any one of you would have made the same decision eventually. I was just smart enough to think of it first.”
I tried to open my mouth to stop her, but I still couldn’t move.
“I considered every other option I could think of, but none of them ended well for us.” She lifted her hand from my cheek. “I won’t make the same mistake again.”

No, all she needed to do was wait. She didn’t have to do anything. Us refusing to take a life might be the key to getting through this alive. Why would she come to a conclusion like this instead? I didn’t get her logic at all.
“I told you. If I don’t do it first, someone else will.”
Suddenly, everything clicked into place with that one sentence.
“But you know, I think this is a situation where none of us can truly betray each other.”
Stab!
In the end, we were the ones who pushed her to sacrifice herself.
[The first Pilgrim has died. All surviving Pilgrims’ stats have increased by +400.]
Thud.
Her body went slack and collapsed to the cold, hard ground. All I could do was stare at her as the knight behind her scoffed. “...That foolish wench.”
All of the blood in my body rushed to my head, leaving me in a daze. I felt like the slightest touch would set me off and leave me screaming at the top of my lungs.
She’s really...
She was dead?
I felt like I had drunk myself sick and the contents of my stomach were now rising up my throat.
Beeeeee—
His voice cut through the ringing in my ears as a pitch-black fog began to billow from his body. “I’ll give you one last chance.”
[The White Captain, Dreadfear, has cast Time of Execution. The target’s level of Fear significantly increases.]

This skill had an effect similar to Bloodlust. It paralyzed your sense of reason, making it impossible for you to remain level-headed. Your body sensed danger coming and reacted accordingly, spiraling into a panic. The urge to run as far away from here as possible flooded my senses.
“Run away,” someone kept whispering into my ear.
But then, suddenly, a thought came to mind.
“Grab it.”
What if Versyl had made a different choice? In this state, would it have even been possible for all of us to have complete faith in each other and refuse to pick up that dagger?
Maybe.

But she must have made the decision she did because she was worried about what would come next. Like the Dungeon and Stone player she was, the first thing she did was try to figure out the game designer’s intentions for this level.
Drip.
Her blood was starting to pool on the floor.
Zeeeeee!
The moment her blood came into contact with the statue, the entire cave began to tremble like a Rift was opening.
[A mysterious presence has embraced the soul of the noble Pilgrim. The altar has been activated.]
Rumble!
A cluster of lights appeared on the stone statue at the center.
[Faith’s Light has driven out the terror within.]
At that moment, the ability that had been restraining our bodies disappeared.
Stomp.
I immediately rose to my feet and grabbed my weapon. The knight looked right at us, visibly annoyed yet wholly unconcerned. “Do you think this changes anything?”
I didn’t know, at least not yet. But there was one thing I was sure of, and it was that we had at least made it through the first stage.
What other skills does he have?

It was actually disgusting how powerful he was. All he had to do was say, “Believe me,” and suddenly we trusted him when he claimed he’d let us live if we just killed each other. There should be a limit to how overpowered a character could be.
“It’s not too late for you yet. But the only way you will make it out of this cave alive is by proving your innocence.”
What was he talking about? Who would still believe him after all that?
“Mister, I have my strength back, at least to some extent.”
Really? Thankfully, it seemed that I wasn’t the only one who got a buff.
“Ainar, grab Versyl.”
“...All right.” Ainar quickly picked Versyl up without a hint of complaint.
At the sight, the knight quickly narrowed the distance between us, swinging his sword.
Fwoosh.

It was a swift, strong strike, far superior to any attack made by the soldiers we met on the way here. However, perhaps because our power had somewhat returned now that the altar had activated, it wasn’t hard to track the trajectory of his swing.
Our legs...?
He wasn’t aiming for our hearts or necks, so he must still be planning on continuing his little prisoner’s dilemma game.
Tap!

Instead of trying to block his aura with my shield, I jumped high into the air to avoid his sword, then swung my mace down on his head. He wasn’t able to dodge it, probably because he hadn’t expected me to attack him in the first place.
Whack!

However, this guy was a tough bastard. Just as I expected, there was no chance beating him would be that easy. The only reason I was even able to get a hit in the first place was because he was being careless and not taking us seriously.
Not yet...
Fighting back my desire to kill him right then and there, I shouted, “What are you doing? Run!”
We couldn’t take him on yet. Luckily, thanks to the significant increase in our stats, the soldiers surrounding us were no longer a problem.
“Raaah!” Ainar charged forward like a rhino, plowing through the soldiers like a bunch of bowling pins. I quickly rushed after her and out of the central cavern.
“Out of the way!” The knight seemed to have recovered from the smack in the head I gave him, as he was now running after us. With that speed...
...He’s a little faster than us.
At this rate, he would absolutely catch us. Something had to be done.
We ran with all our might while I racked my brain. Why did our stats suddenly rise? Was it a buff from the altar activating? Or maybe there was another condition?
More importantly, what even is the condition for clearing this event?
Was it hide and seek? Maybe if we just kept running from him, our stats would rise over time and we would eventually be strong enough to take him down.
I couldn’t be sure of anything right now, but I could at least set up a short-term goal.
“...Wh-where are we going?”
“Out of the cave.”
Our first objective would be to get outside, just in case activating the altar and escaping the cave was the clear condition.
Things were never that simple or easy, though.
“...Mister, we can’t keep running like this.”
It was only a matter of time before he would catch up to us. Ainar and Erwen took turns offering me their opinions.
“Bjorn, let’s fight him. We have to avenge the wizard!”
“No. The three of us aren’t strong enough to beat him. I’ll stay back and throw him off our scent.”
Fighting him head-on or having one of us stay back as bait... They weren’t terrible options. “...All right,” I agreed. “I’ll stay back and distract him, then.”
“No,” Erwen countered. “I have to be the one to do it because I’m the only one capable of finding you guys again... I was actually given a skill when we arrived here.”
“Skill?”
“I can sense where everyone is. I didn’t know exactly what I was sensing until we all met up at the center, but now that I know, I’ll be able to find you two even after we split up...”
Was this like how some scouts had the ability to sense the location of the portal? If it was, then it definitely made sense for her to be the one to lure him away and catch up to us later.
“Trust me. I’m the right person for the job.”
What should I do? Was this really the best plan? As usual, I only had a split-second to make a call. “...Don’t get hurt.”
Despite hearing my orders, Erwen didn’t say anything in response. She simply slowed down, sending us off with a reassuring smile on her face.
Huff... Huff...
I did my best to steady my heavy breathing with each step I took. It had been about two hours since Erwen split off from the group.
We’re about halfway there...
It had taken me eight hours to make my way to the center of the cave back when the event first started, but now, we were able to cover half the distance in just two hours.
I think I’m at about a third of my usual power...
That was just in terms of raw stats, of course. That figure didn’t account for the fact that I didn’t have my usual essences at my disposal to fight this guy with.
The real problem is... our stats have shown no signs of rising any higher.

With no way of knowing whether that earlier increase was just a one-time thing, Ainar and I kept running toward the entrance of the cave as fast as we could. Sometime later, a thought I’d been trying for hours to suppress rose to the surface of my mind.
Erwen... When is she going to catch up? It’s been a while. Did something go wrong?
Just as anxiety was beginning to creep up my spine, another sensation suddenly flooded my senses.
[The second Pilgrim has died. All surviving Pilgrims’ stats have increased by +400.]
It was another stat boost.

chapters.title: Chapter 487: Pilgrim (5)
paragraphs: “The pilgrims! Stop them—!”
Whack!

As we sped through the cave, I cracked the skull of any soldier we came across. Every time I killed five of them, I got a slight stat increase, but the boost was so small that I hardly noticed it given the situation.
At this rate, we should reach the exit in about an hour...
As I continued to plow ahead, the anxiety throbbing in the back of my mind refused to dissipate.
“Bjorn... When is Erwen coming back?”
Even Ainar was worried. Just imagine how I felt.

Did something happen? Was she hurt or... did she die? Anxiety was gnawing away at me, but it was out of my hands now. All I could do was keep running as hard as I could and have faith that Erwen would catch up to us.
[You have killed 405 soldiers. All of your stats have risen by +1.]
[You have killed 410 soldiers. All of your stats have risen by +1.]
[You have killed 415 soldiers...]
How much longer now? Maybe thirty minutes?
As our destination slowly drew closer and closer, my worries over what had happened to Erwen grew in kind.
Stomp.
Despite not taking a single break since we started running, we were suddenly forced to come to a halt.
“Didn’t I tell you, pilgrims? There’s only one way for you to make it out of this cave alive.”
He was now standing in our way.

I didn’t understand. He’d been behind us this whole time, so how was it possible that he was here in front of us now, blocking our path? Our pace had even slowly increased over time as our stats rose.
So... how did he catch up?
Something was wrong. However, before I could worry about that, we had other things to take care of. “Get ready to fight, Ainar.”
After hearing my order, Ainar took our comrade, whose body she had been carrying this entire time, and laid her on the ground. “...Get some rest, wizard.”
Dreadfear watched us and let out a cold laugh. “How ridiculous.”
Maybe it was. However, the moment he appeared in our path, the only idea that came to mind was giving fighting a shot.
It might be possible now with our current stats.
Out of habit, I covered my upper body with my shield and lowered my stance, despite knowing that it would do me very little good. What could a cheap iron shield do against a knight who used aura?
We stared at each other in complete silence, waiting for the other to make the first move. After a moment, he spoke that same line. “My offer. It still stands.”
Was there something wrong with this guy? How the hell had he not given up on his little backstabbing game already?
Still, if he wanted to talk, I wouldn’t let the opportunity go to waste. “...What happened to Erwen?” I had to ask the question that had been eating away at my mind as we ran for hours straight.
“If you mean that pilgrim, then she’s dead,” he replied curtly.
“Bullshit.”
“I guess you’re in the business of denying what you already know.”
Why did I even bother asking him? It was ridiculous to think I could believe the words of a boss character whose whole theme was betrayal.
“Whether you believe me or not, that doesn’t change the truth. No matter how much you believe you are doing the right thing, in the end, you are nothing but a filthy piece of—”
There was no reason to listen to any more of this.
I ran forward with a shout of, “Ainar!” However, as soon as the distance between us narrowed, he drew his aura-coated blade.
Step.

Immediately, I stepped back and outside of his range. Taking advantage of the opening created when he took aim at me, Ainar closed in. “Behel—aaaaaah!” she cried, driving her sword at him in a powerful swing. He darted to the side.
Clang!

Her sword slammed into the ground where he had been standing just moments ago. It was too early to call our assault a failure, though. Fighting as a team meant breaking the enemy’s stance, alternating between attacking and defending, and looking for the right moment to strike.
Thud.

As he dodged Ainar’s strike, I chucked my useless shield at his ugly mug. Then, with his field of view blocked, I took a large step forward and swung my mace. Yet again, he was able to react in time, shifting his sword into my mace’s path. It was clear that, at this rate, he’d easily cut my mace in two.
Swoosh.
So, I used all the strength I had to quickly change the trajectory of my swing.
Fwoosh!
My mace cut through the air, evading his sword entirely, and—
Stab!
Ainar’s blade sunk into his shoulder right on time.
All right. We were able to land the first hit.
We couldn’t be satisfied with just that, though. There was no reason to let up on him and retreat now. After all, a battle was essentially just a game of who could make the most moves.

Attack, block, or dodge—you had a split second to choose one of these three options, and then your next move, and then your next. Thanks to our quick thinking, we were able to limit the number of moves he could make.
Step.

The man was forced to stay on the defensive and focus on either blocking or dodging. Because of the pressure we put on him, we were able to lower the risk of him attacking us. And the other two choices open to him were limited.
Left. Yeah, I knew you would move over to the left.
Whack!

He was forced to twist his body to dodge our attacks, making him fall out of his stance. As a result, he managed to limit the damage he took, but in return, the fight became easier for us and even harder on our opponent.

We all fell into a vicious cycle of exchanging blows. No matter how much of an upper hand we had, we couldn’t drop our guard. He was a knight who used aura. Just one attack from him would be enough to end us, and all battles inevitably came with unforeseen variables.
Fwoosh!

He raised his sword again, swinging at just the right trajectory to intercept my mace. This time, things played out differently. Seeing his blade approach my mace, I was forced to twist my body to dodge it, judging that losing my weapon would be the worst possible outcome here. However, that decision left me wide open.
Thud.

He didn’t pass up his chance and kicked me square in the stomach. I didn’t take any real damage, but the true threat lay in how he used that momentum to quickly turn the tide of this battle against us.
Slash!
Ainar slashed at his thigh, but it was too late.
Stab!
At the exact same moment, he buried his sword into my stomach.
Agh, that stings.
I really hadn’t expected him to attack me so recklessly.
Although she saw me get stabbed, Ainar didn’t bother asking if I was okay or not, instead continuing her onslaught like the veteran she was. “Aaah!”

I quickly forced myself back to my feet and jumped back into the fight. Lying on the ground in pain wasn’t going to stop me from bleeding out. It didn’t matter how many injuries I got in the process—I just had to kill this guy before he killed me. If killing him ended this raid, then I could get healed up once we were out.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

Thus, a bloody battle ensued. Even facing him two-v-one with improved stats, it was a tough fight, especially since our numerical advantage didn’t last for long. “For the empire!” Out of nowhere, a bunch of soldiers appeared and ran at us, making things even harder. Still, they weren’t all bad.
Slice!
Thanks to them, I had a stock of backup weapons.
Thud.

As soon as my mace fell to the ground, now sliced in two, I grabbed another weapon from a fallen soldier’s body. A sword, a hammer, a mace—the type of weapon didn’t matter. I just needed something long enough to swing at him at full strength.
Whack!
First my arms, then my legs, then my torso, shoulders, eyes, and ears—all over my body, the injuries continued to mount. Even so, it was clear he wasn’t faring much better.
Fwoosh!

His strikes, each of which contained the full power and skill of a knight, had gradually slowed and lost steam. Even his aura was smaller than before. One of his arms was heavily injured and his left leg, which Ainar had stabbed a couple of times, had gone so limp that he could barely use it.
Soon.
We would win. At this rate, he would fall before we did. With that thought in mind, I raised the hammer in my hands and put my full weight behind my next swing. But...
[The White Captain, Dreadfear, has dropped to less than 15% health.]

With a burst of energy not unlike a bomb going off, my body was flung to the side and crashed into a wall. Stars burst behind my eyelids from the impact, but I quickly forced myself to stand so I could see what had just happened through blurry eyes.
“Shit.”
I couldn’t not swear in a situation like this.
[The White Captain, Dreadfear, has cast Eternal Nightmare. His health has fully recovered.]
In an instant, his injuries fully healed as he took a step toward me. “My offer...” he said calmly. “It still stands.”
What the fuck is he talking about?
“Tell me...” I fired back. “Were you raised by parrots?”
He didn’t answer my question. Instead, without another word, he stabbed me in the stomach.
“This... broken... ass... game...”
My vision went black.
[Your health has dropped to less than 5 percent. Narcolepsy is now active. Your Natural Regeneration has temporarily significantly increased. You have fallen into a state of Unconsciousness.]
I felt like I was drifting down a river in complete darkness, buoyed only by my thoughts as they bobbed to the surface.
How the hell did they expect us to kill a bastard like the Lord of Terror, Dreadfear?
The answer was simple.

It was impossible. I misunderstood the situation because of the sudden spike in our stats, but it was nothing more than a trap from the jump. He wasn’t a character that was made to be fought in the first place.
I chose wrong.
I had interpreted this all wrong. We should have run toward the exit the moment we spotted him. We shouldn’t have tried to fight him.
This was meant to be a game of hide-and-seek.
Raising our stats was just a small buff granted to us to make things fairer as we ran away from him. A head-to-head battle was never an option.
I was now paying the price for making the wrong call.
[Your health has risen above 15%. Your Unconscious state has changed to a state of Paralysis. Your increase in Natural Regeneration has slightly decreased.]
When I opened my eyes, I was on Ainar’s back.
“Catch them—!” The soldiers’ shouts rang out behind us, but Ainar continued to run forward at full speed.
“Huh? B-Bjorn...? You’re awake? Are you... okay? Can you hear me?”
I forced my mouth open despite the fact that I could barely move. “I’m... fine... Explain... the situation...”

“Ah! O-Okay...” Ainar rushed to fill me in even as she kept fleeing. “You collapsed... and suddenly... the entire cave started to tremble. And that guy... stopped moving. I took advantage of the opportunity and grabbed you... and I quickly ran away with you on my back...”
He stopped moving? Was it because of the altar?
There was no telling. This was my first time experiencing this hidden level, so I had no clue what was happening, and I didn’t have a system log to tell me either.
“...Time?”
“I-I don’t know. Maybe five minutes...?”
So I was unconscious for about five minutes.
“But are you okay?” she asked frantically.
“I’m... fine. I just can’t move...”
What was up with me?

After thinking it over for a moment, there was one theory that seemed likely. Narcolepsy was a passive skill that activated when your health dropped below 5 percent. At 15 percent, your status changed to Paralyzed. Then, once you were back at 30 percent, the status effects disappeared altogether.
So... I also have skills.
It wasn’t just Versyl and Erwen—I had started with a skill too. But since it was a passive skill, I had only noticed now.
That means Ainar must also have one...
What was hers? No idea, but there was also no time to experiment and find out.
“Left...”
“Huh?”
“Go left...”
I fired off directions to Ainar as I tried to get my thoughts in order, still slumped against her back. However, a particularly loud sound soon caught my attention.
Huff, huff...
Her breathing was much heavier now than before, to the point where it was concerning.
“Ainar... are you all right?”
“I’m... fine...”
No, she didn’t look fine at all.
“It’s just... I can’t... use my hands... and I’m... a bit injured... but it’s fine...”

A question suddenly occurred to me. Since she was carrying me on her back, she couldn’t use her hands, so how was she dealing with the soldiers that got in our way? Had she been lucky enough to not encounter any soldiers in the past five minutes at all?
I didn’t need to wonder for long. She soon showed me exactly how she handled them.
“...Filthy pilgrims!” A group of soldiers jumped out from one of the crossroads, putting themselves right in our path.
Ainar’s way of dealing with them was straightforward. She just kept running. No, rather, she sped up and rammed straight through them.
Stab!

Their sharp weapons swung at her body, but with both arms behind her holding me up, all she could do was endure their attacks and protect her vitals as best she could. Her shoulders, arms, and legs ended up covered in injuries, some large wounds and others small nicks. In the end, though, Ainar was still able to get through.
The soldiers we passed joined the group chasing us from behind. As I watched all this unfold, I heard Ainar’s breathing grow even heavier than before.
Huff... Huff...
All the while, I couldn’t say a word.
Ainar immediately noticed my silence and asked, “Bjorn... were you... hurt?”
“...Stop.”

This was too risky. She was obviously on the verge of collapse. And at this rate, even if we did make it out of here, her injuries might end up impossible to treat. We didn’t even have a potion on us. Her best option was to put me down and wait for my Paralysis to end. That way, she wouldn’t need to carry me anymore.
“I can’t... do that.”
For some reason, however, Ainar stubbornly refused to stop.
“Wh-why...?”
“The moment you collapsed... I saw... the future.”
“...The future?”
“The wizard... When she died... I saw it then too. I thought it was just a random hallucination but... I now think that... it’s some sort of skill.”
Why was she acting like this, though? Just what did she see?
I asked her, but she wouldn’t tell me. “I... can’t stop. Just trust me on that.”
I was once again rendered speechless.
“I... definitely won’t... fall.”
Ainar’s voice was filled with determination. Knowing I had no hope of changing her mind, I held my tongue as she continued silently forging ahead.
Stomp, stomp.
No matter how many soldiers got in our way, she never stopped charging forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 488: Pilgrim (6)
paragraphs: Given the variety of skills available in the game, some were naturally ‘seeing the future’ themed. The primary example was Clock Hands of Regret, a rank-one skill that could be found on the ninth floor. The way it worked was simple. When a teammate died, the text “Memories of regret go backward in time” appeared on the screen, and you were sent back in time to the decisive moment right before their death took place.

Calling it a precognition skill didn’t quite do it justice, as it did much more than let you see the future, but even though it might seem overpowered, it also had obvious cons. For one thing, it would only be triggered if you and the target were connected by a Binding spell. Plus, the skill had a months-long cooldown time—and that was months in the city, not the labyrinth. Not only that, but it could only be used a maximum of three times and never on yourself.
This clearly isn’t that skill.

Ainar and I weren’t currently Bound or we would have spawned in the same place when we first got here, and based on what she just said, she had used her skill at least twice already. So it couldn’t possibly be Clock Hands of Regret.
Then the most plausible candidate is... Yeah, it must be that.

It didn’t take long to narrow things down to the next viable contender: Prophet of Misfortune. It was a rare rank-six skill that was difficult to acquire, and when triggered, a text box appeared that randomly showed you information about the future. For example:

[A vision of misfortune has appeared before the Prophet. In the not-too-distant future, Bjorn Yandel will lose his life to the White Captain, Dreadfear. Don’t grow complacent just because he is not in sight, as he will never stop chasing after you.]

I personally classified this skill as an information-gathering ability. I often used it to collect info around the middle of the game since it was great for revealing traps and telling you what types of monsters lay ahead when you entered unfamiliar territory.
But it must work differently in real life.
What was just a few lines of text in the game was being seen through someone’s eyes.
Huff... Huff...
“...Ainar, did you see me die?”
Again, she didn’t answer me, but the way she flinched spoke for itself.
So that’s why she’s not stopping...
I kept my mouth shut. No matter what I said at this point, it wouldn’t change her mind. There was little I could do.
“Left.”
Well, I could give her directions as she carried me on her back.
Grind.
I could clench my jaw too. It was the only part of me I could move.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
Otherwise, I could only lay there, helpless and limp against Ainar’s back, as she barreled through the soldiers without so much as a shield to protect her.
Stab!
An arrow sank into her leg.
“Die!”
Her skin was torn apart by spearheads and swords.
And all the while, all I could do was watch.
“C-Catch her! This is our chance...!”
“Ahhh!”
“...Wh-what strength!”
Ainar finally came to a stop only after another desperate charge. We still hadn’t reached the exit—far from it—but she couldn’t run anymore. Instead, she set me down and got ready to protect me.
Thud.

Her injuries had piled up with every group of soldiers we encountered and she had at last begun to slow down too much to outrun them. The soldiers on our tail had finally managed to catch up, and they were almost on top of us now. Ainar let out a breath and picked up her weapon.
“Don’t...worry.”
With that, she charged like a bull toward the soldiers as I sat there propped up against the wall, unable to tear my eyes away.
One, two, three, four, five, six...
After her seventh kill, an ax lodged into her arm.
Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen...
When she killed her eighteenth soldier, a spear sank into her collarbone.
Forty-three, forty-four, forty-five...
As the forty-sixth went down, an arrow skewered her left eye.
Seventy-one, seventy-two, seventy-three...
As time passed, the corpses on the ground continued to pile up, until—
One hundred.

A momentary silence fell over the cavern. She had arrows sticking out of every part of her body and blood gushing from her wounds. Yet she was still standing, an unyielding, immovable wall in the soldiers’ way.
The silence didn’t last long.
The soldiers ran at her again, weapons raised. “She’s tiring as well! Don’t back down!”
At one hundred and thirty, Ainar apologized to me.
“I’m sorry... My body can’t...”
Then, she collapsed on top of me like a puppet without strings.
Cough! Khh!
She shouldn’t sound like that, was all I could think. Those sounds shouldn’t be coming out of my teammate’s mouth.
It felt like I was trapped in a nightmare. My mind was blank. My ears were ringing. I wanted to throw up.
Cough! Khh!
And all the while, those horrific noises wouldn’t stop. I was trapped in my own body, helpless to do anything but watch her slowly die on top of me.
Nudge.
Then, suddenly, the tips of my fingers twitched and I could finally move again.
[Your health has reached 30 percent. Status effect Paralysis has been lifted.]
My hand whipped out, grabbing a hold of the first weapon I touched. Pushing Ainar’s limp form aside, I stumbled to my feet.
Fwoosh!

I swung my weapon. The soldiers jumped back on instinct, clearly taken by surprise. I took advantage of their hesitation to hoist Ainar onto my back, then immediately started running, carrying Ainar just as she had carried me.
“Ahhhhhh!”
I ran through the cave, barreling through any soldiers that got in our way.
“S-Stop them!”

They used every weapon at their disposal to stop me. With every step I took, injuries both big and small accumulated on my body. However, I didn’t stop to block or avoid their attacks. I sacrificed my body to protect Ainar’s as I brute-forced my way through them like the mindless tank I was, heedless of how many attacks came my way or how long I ran.
[Your health has dropped to less than 15%.]
My restored health had once again dropped, but that wouldn’t stop me.
Huff... Huff...
In a brief moment of respite where no soldiers appeared, I plowed forward and checked on Ainar. “Ainar! Are you all right?! Wake up! You can’t fall asleep now! You need to wake—”
“B-Bjorn...” A faint voice brushed my ear. “You have to survive...”

“Y-You’re alive! I know you must be tired, but you can’t fall asleep! Just ten more minutes. No, eight. Just stay awake eight more minutes for me!” If she could just do that, then we’d be home free. That being said, there was no guarantee that leaving the cave would mean clearing the level. However, given that the difficulty of escaping from this cave was so high, there was also a high probability that doing so would come with some sort of healing effect attached. “You have to...!”
You just need to trust in me and hang in there, just a little while longer.
But before I could form the words, Ainar murmured, “...Let me go.”
What was she saying? I had probably misheard her since we were both in rough shape, so—
“Let me...go...”

Never mind, I didn’t mishear her. I was furious she’d even suggest that, but I couldn’t bring myself to yell at her given the state she was in. Not now. Instead, I decided to ignore her. “Seems like the blood loss is making you loopy.”
She was quiet.
“Just hang in there. That’s all you need to do.”
I didn’t know if her silence meant agreement or if she simply didn’t have the strength to argue. Either way, she didn’t say another word.
...She’s not dead, right?

I swallowed, trying to shove down the anxiety creeping up my throat, and kept on running even as my heart threatened to give out at any moment. As the cave’s entrance appeared in the distance, I caught the scent of fresh air and foliage. Light leaked in through the opening, brightening the path ahead. Soon enough, the long-awaited entrance was right in front of us.
“Ainar! Ainar! Wake up! We’re almost there! Answer me!”
“...B-Be careful.”
What was she saying? Well, at least I knew she was still alive. Now we just needed to get out of here.

However, before I could barrel through the cave’s entrance, I skidded to a stop. I wasn’t sure how I knew, but... something was wrong. On instinct, I reached out a hand, my fingers bumping up against some kind of invisible barrier.
What’s going on?
The entrance was completely blocked off.
“...You have got to be shitting me.”
If the goal wasn’t to escape outside, then what was it? It wasn’t like we had any chance of beating a boss monster with impossibly high stats and overpowered abilities in a head-to-head fight.
“But then... what the hell were we supposed to do...?”
The hope I’d been clinging to crumbled away.
“B-Bjorn...”
Even so, I smiled for her sake. “A-Ainar? Don’t worry! I’ll break through this barrier and get us out of here in no time!”
When faced with a wall, you smashed it. That was the barbarian way.
Slam! Slam! Slam!
So I raised my fists and pounded them against the force field as hard as I could.
“B-Bjorn...”
Unfortunately, the barrier wouldn’t budge. Thankfully, being a barbarian also meant not knowing when to give up.
“S-Stop...”
Fist. Foot. Head. I used everything I could, every ounce of strength I possessed, to break it. I lunged at it, threw my weight at it, rammed my shoulder into it...
Slam!
Was there something about this thing that made it impervious to physical attacks?
Fine, then I’ll move on to Plan B.
I changed my strategy and targeted the wall next to the barrier instead. No matter how sturdy an iron door was, you could just break the stone wall surrounding it. That had to be what I needed to do.
“Stop...”
Slam!
“Go... Before he comes...”
I couldn’t stand it any longer.
Slam!

I slammed my forehead against the wall in a fit of anger. It didn’t make me feel the slightest bit better, though. In the end, I was still stuck inside this awful cave, drowning in a sea of frustration and despair.
“Over there...!”
Suddenly, soldiers appeared behind us. Already? I didn’t think they’d be able to catch up so soon. Rather than overthinking it, however, I immediately turned and stampeded toward them.
Whack!
I slammed the man in front straight into the wall before grabbing his weapon.
And then I proceeded to slaughter them all.
“...D-Devil!”
“Don’t stop attacking!”
“For the Empire...!”
One, two, three, four...
That’s five of them.
Six, seven, eight...
...How many was that?
I didn’t know. I had to start over. One, two, three...
Whack, whack, whack!
By the time I came to my senses, my surroundings were quiet. Not even the shallowest of breaths could be heard from the bodies littering the passageway. They were all dead.

Belatedly remembering what I had been fighting so hard to protect in the first place, I whipped around. “...Ainar.” Thankfully, when I rushed to her side, she was still breathing. The sound, however, was faint and ragged, like it was stuttering to a stop.
“B-Bjorn...”
Somehow sensing my presence, she struggled to force her eyes open.
I couldn’t speak.
Everything will be fine. Don’t worry. We’ll be home soon.
I should have been saying something like that.
“Bjorn... son of Yandel.”
But all I could do was stare down at her, unable to form a proper thought.
Ainar’s hazy eyes met mine, the corners of her mouth twitching up. “My... precious... friend...”
She may as well have driven a massive stake through my heart. How could she call me her precious friend now of all times?
“You will... become... a great... warrior...”
The dam inside me holding everything back began to crash down. Between the painful truth or a kind lie, it was obvious which one you should offer someone on their deathbed.
Precious friend...
Yet before I could even stop myself, my mouth opened on its own and out tumbled a mix of a confession and an apology. “I-I’m... I’m not...”

I was not the real Bjorn Yandel. I was just an evil spirit that took over his body, one of the very same evil spirits whose skulls you were supposed to crack open the moment you spotted them. That... that was who I really was. As I gazed down at Ainar, her eyes gradually losing focus, my lips moved, forming words I could barely hear.
At some point, I returned to my senses and had to face the truth.
Ainar was no longer breathing. Her eyes were still open, staring out at me, but there was no denying it.
[The third Pilgrim has died.]
Ainar was dead.
[The surviving Pilgrim’s stats have all increased by +400.]
My stats rose again, and at long last, I knew what I had to do.
[Special Condition – Unbreakable Bond has been met. All stats have increased by 3x.]
[Defeat the White Captain, Dreadfear.]
The objective of this secret level was finally clear to me.

chapters.title: Chapter 489: Pilgrim (7)
paragraphs: Regret washed over me.
I shouldn’t have ever attempted... a raid against a Lord of the Floor.
If I had just paid Sawtooth their fair share of the essence we took, then I wouldn’t have even thought about fighting a Lord of the Floor in the first place.
No, before that...
I wish I had never played this game.
If I had just stayed away from it, then I would have never been brought here.
And nothing like this would have ever happened.
I clenched my fists so hard that blood began to drip down my knuckles and forced myself to stand. This wasn’t the time for regrets—there was work to be done.
No, rather, there’d be time to wallow in regret later.
When my stats rose, a new option opened up before me.
Thud.
I stared past the countless corpses littering the cave.
Step, step.
There, beyond them, he slowly approached. “This is great. I was just starting to worry about being able to find you.”

The moment he appeared, I roared and ran at him. Since my usual build focused on muscle strength and various types of resistance, I never imagined I could move so quickly. The moment between me kicking off the ground and me reaching him was practically instantaneous.
Slam!
I no longer needed a weapon because my body itself had become a weapon. My skin alone was as hard as any iron mace or sword.
Slam!
He met my attack with his aura-covered sword. Yet as I tracked his movements now, he seemed ridiculously slow.
Step.

I easily avoided his attack and closed in once more, delivering another round of punches. It felt like I’d just used a cheat code. Even though I didn’t have any skills active, my base stats alone made me feel several times stronger than I usually did in Giantization mode.
I don’t think he can even hurt me with his aura at this point...
Still, there was no reason to risk getting hit by a sword that could easily be dodged. I continued to completely decimate him instead, careful to move in and out of his reach to avoid his blade.
Slam, slam, slam!
I didn’t even have to punch him all that much. Maybe about ten times in total? That was all it took for him to drop to the ground, unable to stand up to me.
Slam, slam!
He was in much worse condition now than he was when we cornered him before, yet he wasn’t recovering. Which meant my hypothesis was correct.
That healing skill must be a one-time-use ability...
And he might be the type of boss monster that could only be killed once he was alone and you faced him one-on-one.
Maybe...
Then maybe it wasn’t too late.
Squash!
I put all my determination into one last punch, completely crushing his skull like a watermelon.
[You have defeated the Lord of Terror, Dreadfear. EXP +100]
[Lord of the Floor Kill Bonus. EXP +15]
As the experience points flooded in, his body turned into flecks of light and began to float away.
...Is that it? Did I get my hopes up in vain?
Just as that horrifying thought began to fester in my mind, the cave began to cave in around me.
[You have passed the test more perfectly than anyone else. The Nameless Pilgrim admits defeat.]
[The fragments of a distorted memory have begun to piece themselves back together.]

Although I was flummoxed, I decided to watch the spectacle unfold for now. To be honest, there actually wasn’t anything else I could do. It wasn’t like I could run away when the entire cave was collapsing around me.
Rumble!
Plus, even outside the cave, I could see the bright sky and green bushes in the distance falling away. Everything had begun to dissipate into thin air, just like when a monster died.
Shaaaaaa.

The world itself started to collapse, dissolving into colorful particles of light. And once everything was gone, I was left alone in utter darkness. It wasn’t simply that I couldn’t see anything in front of me. It felt like “in front of me” didn’t exist.
Fwoosh!

Then, suddenly, there was a crackle of fire and my surroundings lit up. I was in a dark cave. Dozens of torches hung on walls that were crumbling to pieces just moments ago. In the center of the cave was a stone altar with a book laid out on top of it.
What does it want me to do now?
I didn’t know, but I walked over to it anyway. As I did, the book opened to its first chapter. It was written in an ancient language, but for some reason, I was able to read the text without issue.
If I were asked to draw a representation of terror, I wouldn’t hesitate to sketch his face on that white sheet of paper. The White Captain, Dreadfear. The one who taught me what true terror was...
As I concentrated on the words in front of me, the letters began to blur together as flashes of color and sound flooded my senses. I had never experienced anything like this before.
I met him moments before I was about to accomplish a great feat.
The memories of a stranger began to flood my mind.
I’m not afraid to die. In my final moments, I know I will die a greater person than any other.
Although I had lived my life with this conviction, such a delusion and reality were completely and utterly different.
“I swear on my name, Dreadfear, that whichever of you kills the other filthy pilgrims will have proven their innocence and shall thus be absolved of all sins.”

After our mission had failed, he offered us a devious proposition. No one believed him at first, of course. All five of us closed our eyes in unison, rejecting his offer. The cave was utterly silent as we awaited our demise, honorable to the very end.
Ba-dump, ba-dump!

Yet in that silence, our hearts pounded with the desperate longing to live. Were we really going to die like this? No matter what I had said in the past, I didn’t want to die. Still, betraying my own comrades would be...
“Believe me.”
How strange. It was just two words, but why did they not sound like a lie?
I gently opened my closed eyes. Next to me was a woman who had been tasked with the same quest as I. Her eyes were frantically darting around, looking just as frightened as I was sure mine did.
And the moment our eyes met, I knew it in my gut.
Ba-dump!
She was on the verge of succumbing to temptation. I didn’t have any proof, but I knew it to be true. After all, how long had we all known each other?
Ba-dump, ba-dump.
Blood rushed to my head. My breath caught in my throat and my vision began to blur.
Heh.
The woman flashed me an awkward smile. For some reason, the sight sent an ominous chill through me. As those budding doubts blossomed, fear began to gnaw away at my roots.
“Yeah... If I have to kill someone, I should kill him...”

All of a sudden, I heard the woman’s inner thoughts. The words were too vivid to dismiss as a mere auditory hallucination. Come to think of it, we never got along well. We’d even argued the last time we were drinking. On top of that, look where we were now—in the place where the Mother Goddess’s spirit dwelled.
A divine revelation... Yes, it must have been a revelation from Mother Goddess herself. She must have exposed that woman’s malicious intent toward me to save her vulnerable child.
Before I knew it, I’d accepted it as a fact that she was planning to betray and kill me to survive. Was that why?
Huff, huff, huff...
I let out a breath, and when I came to my senses, I was already picking up the dagger. I turned toward the woman, whose eyes were wide open in shock.
“Y-You... You thought about it, didn’t you...? You planned to kill me...”
“N-No, I didn’t. I didn’t!”
“D-Don’t lie! I-I already know the truth! I definitely heard it—!”
I thrust the dagger into her. My comrades swore and screamed at me, but I ignored them. It couldn’t be helped. If I didn’t do it now, she would have done it first.
“Pfft—hahaha!” The White Captain, Dreadfear, laughed in genuine joy at the sight. When he next spoke, his voice was light. “Well done. Now, who are you going to stab next?”
Filled with adrenaline, my body trembled as I stammered, “B-But I thought... You just said I had to stab one... And you would let me live...”
“Of course I’m not going to kill you anymore. But... are you sure you’ll be safe? If you put down the dagger, I plan on freeing all of your friends here as well. What do you think will happen then?”
My vision was tunneling. I knew that I was being deceived, but I was past the point of no return.
Ba-dump, ba-dump.

My heart drummed a vicious beat in my chest, more violent than ever before. My comrades continued to shout at me, begging me to not fall for his tricks. Yelling that I needed to come back to my senses and die with honor. Of course, I didn’t listen to any of it. At first, he’d tricked me with his words. Now, he didn’t even need to trick me into believing him.
Thud.
In the end, I couldn’t let go of the dagger now that it was in my hands.
Stab!

When I came to my senses, all of my comrades were dead except for me. Still in a daze, I asked him if he was going to let me live now, and in response, he told me to go. He told me that he would let me leave with my life.

I ran without ever looking back. I could feel him watching me go with the eyes of someone playing with an amusing toy. When I finally arrived at the entrance of the cave after hours of nonstop running, the reality of what I had done finally hit me. “N-No... I-I... No...”
A new fear began to sprout inside of me. And there was only one way to escape it.
Stab!
I stabbed myself with the same dagger I used to kill my comrades.

As I started to lose consciousness, I saw the White Captain’s blurry form appear in the distance, an appraising look on his face. “I knew it the moment I saw him. He’s going to be a good ingredient.” He called over a wizard, who approached my dying form and sprinkled a mysterious potion over the length of me.
Sizzle!

An unbearable pain consumed me like my fallen soul was being torn apart entirely. Then, in the middle of that endless agony, a sudden warmth caressed my tattered spirit. However, the warm energy was merely soothing the pain, incapable of piecing back together my now shattered soul.
“Phew... It’s done.”

I had abandoned my pathetic human body and been transformed into a new being—a creature imbued with infinite power and abilities that far surpassed those of a mere mortal, yet an empty shell capable of only the basest of desires and pure hatred.
“...What a peculiar case. It seems he still has some sense of reason left?”
“You’re right.”
At the wizard’s response, he approached, trying to hide his fear. “Tell me, what is your name?”
I answered.
“Dreadfear.”
“...What? But that’s my—”
Gulp.
I was no longer afraid.
[You have taken the Memory Fragments of a Nameless Pilgrim. You can now freely read and write in the ancient language.]
Fragmented memories filled my mind like a fleeting dream. However, the emotions and sensations I felt lingered, all too vivid.
Fwoosh!
As the book reached its last page, it was engulfed in flames. Soon, it was nothing but ashes.
Step.
I stepped back only to sense a presence behind me. I whipped around to see a man staring at me from about ten steps away.
“Dreadfear.”
Though I guess I should call him the Nameless Pilgrim instead.
This wasn’t Dreadfear but the man who, when given the power to do so, swallowed Dreadfear whole and stole his name from him.
...What the hell is going on?
I was a little—no, I was extremely confused. The raid was already over. I had definitely felt the experience points filling me. So why the hell was this guy standing in front of me now?
“I want to ask you something,” he said as if reading my mind. “You... Why weren’t you afraid?”

I sort of had a feeling he would ask me that. Now that I knew how he was born, I also had a grasp of what sorts of questions would drive him. We had experienced the very same doubt, terror, and hallucinations that he and his comrades had, after all. The Prophet of Misfortune allowed us to see foreboding futures, and one of us could sense other people’s emotions. It was the perfect setup to encourage betrayal. And that wasn’t all, either. On top of all that, the White Captain also used a skill to make us believe everything he said, and just when it looked like we might be able to take him in a fight, he suddenly whipped out ridiculously overpowered abilities.
“Because none of us were as weak as you.”
Yet, in the end, none of us had betrayed each other.
He nodded quietly despite my rude response. “I see...”

Since I’d never had a conversation with a boss monster in a game or real life, this was pretty weird for me. However, now wasn’t the time to dwell on that. There was something far more important to discuss.
“Enough of that. Tell me...” This lone possibility had been pervading my every thought since my comrades all died. “They’re all alive, right?”
“Before I answer that, I want to ask you something first: why do you think that?”
“Because this test was designed so that someone would definitely be left alone in the end, and it was impossible to change that.”

The design of this level had felt strange to me from the beginning. I’d played Dungeon and Stone for nearly a decade, but I’d never encountered a boss fight where survival was virtually impossible. Not only that, this guy’s entire theme was a major clue. Terror and hatred. In hindsight, it was clear that this was all designed to test our loyalty.
“...How surprising,” he exclaimed. “To think that someone like you understands the laws of this world.”
What laws? This was just raw data gathered through experience.
“Anyway, what’s your answer?” I demanded.
“...It’s up to you to choose.”
The moment those unexpected words left his mouth, my whole body shuddered. Still, at least I was right in assuming that my team hadn’t been unfairly killed off. “...What do you mean by that?”
“It’s as it sounds.” He reached out a pale hand and two stone gates appeared in front of us.
[The Nameless Pilgrim has made you an offer.]
He presented me with two options. “Go through that door and you’ll recover everything that you’ve lost here. Like awakening from a long nightmare.”
“And if I choose the other door?”
“Everything you experienced here will become reality. But in return, you will gain something far greater than what you have lost.”
Man, doesn’t he get tired of playing this game? I get that it’s his whole shtick, but why is he keeping it up ‘til the very end?
“Then,” I asked, staring at him unblinkingly, “What about if I crack open your skull instead?”
It was only natural that a gamer with a wealth of experience beating hidden events would start to wonder about hidden possibilities, right?
He peered at me for a moment before finally replying. “You will receive an even bigger reward because that is another law of this world.”
Yeah, that’s right.
It didn’t take long for me to make a decision.

chapters.title: Chapter 490: Declaration of War (1)
paragraphs: I only asked about the third option out of pure player curiosity and animosity toward him, but in truth, I had already made my choice. I didn’t know what kind of reward choosing that other door would get me, but whatever it might be, it couldn’t possibly be worth more than three comrades I could rely on.
And... I don’t think I can defeat that thing on my own.
After collecting my thoughts, I glanced up. Every time I met his eyes, I felt a strange sense of unease. It was as if I was looking at something entirely alien.
“It seems you have made a decision.”
“Yeah. I’m going out that door,” I declared, then walked toward my choice. He simply watched me go without a word. It felt almost like he was staying quiet out of respect for the decision I had made.
Step.

When I finally reached the door, I didn’t step through immediately, instead turning to ask him something. If I left things like this, I knew I’d be plagued by this question for the rest of my life. “If... If any of us had fallen for your tricks and betrayed each other, what would have happened?”
This had been my first time seeing this secret level. Thankfully, things had ended well, but I couldn’t shake the thought of the what-ifs.
Fortunately for me, he readily answered my question. “In accordance with established providence, my clone would have gained even more strength.”

“...So that’s what would’ve happened.” No wonder he kept trying to make us betray each other, even when he could have easily killed us from the start. I was slowly starting to understand the design of this event. The endgame was always a one-on-one boss battle, but in the event of a betrayal, the difficulty of said battle would rise significantly.
And if you lose the boss battle, it’s Game Over.

Since this was ultimately a game, I figured that even the Betrayal Route had to be beatable somehow, and likely had its own route-specific rewards as well. None of that mattered now, however. Thanks to him, I had been able to appease my curiosity.
Still, while I was at it, I decided to ask one final question. “What the hell... even are you?”
“What do you mean?”
“Don’t you already know exactly what I mean?”
This was not the first time I’d had a conversation with one of the labyrinth’s monsters.
“You are the first living beings I’ve seen in a long time. Where did you all come from?”
The first had been Vampire Duke Cambormere of the Bloody Citadel.
“Wild dogs of the empire, seized by greed... I will punish you today.”
There was also the Knight of the End from the White Temple.
“If it is... a lie... no one knows... how is it... any different from the truth?”
Even the Doppelganger had spoken to me, and that was just to name a few.

However, despite the fact that I’d had similar encounters in the past, I’d always gotten the sense during each one that the monsters were simply saying dialogue they had been programmed to say. In fact, they never seemed to have much sense of reason at all and attacked any adventurers near them with blind rage. However, this guy was different. It felt almost like he was a real being capable of conscious thought.
And he said something earlier that caught my attention...

He had stated plainly that in the case of betrayal, according to established providence, his “clone” would have gotten a power boost. I couldn’t quite wrap my head around it, but there was one thing I could say with some certainty after combining all the information I’d gathered thus far. Just like how Dungeon and Stone was modeled off this world, this labyrinth had to have been modeled after something as well.
“By any chance,” I carefully began, “do all the monsters here in the labyrinth have originals, and you happen to be one of them?”

He stared at me, silent. As I watched him contemplate the question, the strength seemed to drain out of him. Then, after a long moment, he shook his head. “Perhaps.” The moment that word left his mouth, I felt like I had gotten a step closer to unraveling the secrets of this labyrinth. “Perhaps you’ll uncover the truth one day.”
That was the end of my conversation with him.
Thud!
The moment the stone door in front of me creaked open, something shoved me in the back and pushed me through.
[You have perfectly overcome the labyrinth’s most terrifying ordeal. No.12: Trust has been permanently equipped to you.]
[The Nameless Pilgrim has vanished from the labyrinth forever. Special Condition – Distorted Memories have been permanently deleted. A hidden area has opened.]
[First Achievement Unlocked: The great feats you have accomplished will be engraved in the Stone of Honor, recorded forevermore.]
[The labyrinth is now closed. You are being transported to Rafdonia.]

A warm glow dusted my screwed-shut eyelids. As I slowly opened my eyes and raised my head, a gloomy sky welcomed me. I sat there for a while, staring up at the clouds blankly. I really made it back alive. It was like this every month, but whenever I returned and looked up at that familiar sky, I felt the tension drain right out of me.
Of course, the feeling never lasted long.
“...Bjorn Yandel.”
“Wasn’t he fighting the Lord of the Floor? I wonder what happened?”
“Did he really succeed with just five people?”

Nearby adventurers quickly recognized me and started to gossip. I shook myself out of my stupor and stood up to head to the checkpoint. However, only one person was waiting for me there. It was Amelia, who had stepped away from the group to interrogate the intruders.

“...I’m glad to see you got back alive. Do you know how worried I was? You didn’t show up until the labyrinth closed.” She had been frantically scanning the crowd from her spot near the checkpoint, but when she spotted me, she let out a sigh of relief. It wasn’t long before she tensed up again, though. “Any casualties?”

With no way of knowing what had happened to us, Amelia was more worried about potential losses than whether or not our raid was successful. Thankfully, I could answer that question, at least. “None. Well... there should be none.”
“Should be...? What does that mean?”
“...It’s hard to explain.” I was told that we would all return alive, but I doubted I’d be able to relax until I saw them with my own two eyes. “Let’s just wait here for now.”

Amelia nodded, opting not to badger me any further. I was sure she had plenty of questions, though. But she held her tongue as we waited there for what felt like years until finally, they began to show up one by one.
The first was Erwen.

“M-Mister...” She broke out into a run the moment she spotted me near the checkpoint, and when she finally reached us, her knees gave out in apparent exhaustion. “This... This isn’t a dream... right?”
“Don’t worry. This isn’t a dream.”
“What... What happened?”
Well, from her perspective, she had died while trying to draw aggro then opened her eyes to find herself here. It was no surprise that she was confused and struggling to process.
“When everyone gets here, I’ll explain everything.”
Soon after, Versyl Gowland appeared.
“Why are you so late? Weren’t you worried about us too?”
“S-Sorry. This j-just doesn’t make any sense... I-Is this... a dream? I’m c-certain that I died...” Versyl was acting the same way Erwen was.
Amelia stared at them, tilting her head in confusion. “...Died?”
“Like I said before, it’s a long story. I’ll explain when we are all together again.”
“...Okay.”
A while later, the last wayward member of our party finally appeared just as Versyl was calming down.

“B-Bjorn...!” Ainar, who had noticed us near the checkpoint, ran toward us with a shout. Only then was I able to breathe a sigh of relief, finally secure in the fact that everyone had returned alive. “...Wh-what?! What is this?! W-Was that all a dream earlier?! I’m sure that I died—”
I quickly slapped a hand over Ainar’s mouth.
“...Agh! Mm! Mph!”
“Be quiet! Everyone is looking at us because of you. Let’s move somewhere else first, then I’ll explain everything.”

Now that we were all gathered together, we quickly passed through the checkpoint and made our way down the street. As usual, the front of the checkpoint was full of close family and friends of the adventurers who went into the labyrinth this month.
“Versyl, would you be all right with finding your way home from our place in Kommelby?”
“I don’t mind. I would actually feel more comfortable if we discussed this there anyway.”
“All right, then.”

We headed toward the platform to wait for a noble carriage that would take us to Kommelby. This was the downside of living on a main street. When I lived in District Seven, the Dimension Square was close enough that I could just walk home.
“Captain! You’re back!” When we got home, Auyen was waiting for us, the scent of appetizing dishes permeating the air. Did he prepare all of this for our return?
“Thanks for this, but we need to talk amongst ourselves for a moment. Do you mind waiting upstairs?”
“...Of course. Please get some rest, and call me whenever you need me.”
Once he headed to his room, I asked Versyl to cast Voice Control. We talked while eating the delicious dishes, though in reality, Ainar and I were the only ones touching the food.
“Mr. Yandel... Please stop eating for a moment and tell us what happened. I was dying of curiosity on the way here.”
Oh, right. I guess I should explain.
After swallowing, I launched into a blow-by-blow account of everything that transpired.

“So you’re saying that... from the very beginning, the encounter was designed so that all but one of us would have to die? And that everyone would only be revived if the last survivor was able to defeat the enemy?”
“Right.”
Once I was done explaining everything, save for the final conversation I’d had with the real Dreadfear, I noticed a strange look in Amelia’s eyes. “Hey...” she said. “Are you okay?”
“Hm? What do you mean?”
“That must’ve been like torture for you, given your personality.”
Ah, that...

“I’m fine,” I replied with a lopsided smile. Though, if I were to be honest, I did nearly lose my mind while in the thick of it. But all’s well that ends well, right? In any case, it seemed I’d answered everyone’s questions, so now it was my turn. “But Amelia, what happened to you?”
Her expression darkened. “I didn’t get any evidence. They were commissioned through the black market, so they didn’t know who the client was.”
“I see...”

That was unfortunate, but it wasn’t Amelia’s fault. We would figure out some other way to deal with Count Alminus. He honestly felt like a non-issue in the face of my teammates dying and coming back to life.
However, it seemed she wasn’t done. “A-And...”
“Never mind. I’ll tell you later.”
I felt a sudden prickle of unease. She said she would tell me later, though, so I didn’t see a reason to force it out of her now.
“What about you, Erwen?”

“...Oh, me? I’m sorry. You trusted me to protect you, but I couldn’t escape from him. No matter how fast I ran and tried to shake him off, he always seemed to catch up to me somehow. It was like he was using teleportation magic.”
“Teleportation...” Maybe he really did have an ability like that, one that would trigger if you were a certain distance away from him.
“But the weird thing is that he spent every moment until he killed me trying to persuade me to betray you. He kept on saying that it wasn’t too late.”
Though her story was brief, I could feel the pain and suffering that she must have endured more keenly than anyone else. “Erwen, you went through a lot.”
“...N-No. I’m fine.”
Then it was Versyl’s turn.
“Versyl Gowland.”
“What the hell were you thinking? Don’t you ever—*ever*—do something like that again.”
“Okay...”
I made sure to scold her for a bit before moving on to the most critical thing I needed to address.
“Ainar...” I hedged carefully.
“...Hm?” Ainar was stuffing her face with food, but when she heard me call her name, she lifted her head for the first time since our conversation began.
I had a hard time getting the words out, but this was something I absolutely had to ask. “You know... at the end there... before you died... do you remember?”
“Remember? What are you talking about?”
“What I told you.” Specifically, I was asking if she remembered me confessing that I was an evil spirit.

Ainar continued to shovel pieces of meat into her mouth as she answered. “Oh, that? I thought you were telling me something... but I don’t remember what you said. Maybe I had trouble hearing you since I was about to die.”

Hm, is that true? I studied her expression closely, but nothing about it seemed off. She really must not have heard me. That made sense—if she had, she definitely would have freaked out on me the second she saw me in the square.
“Why? What did you say?”
“Never mind. It was nothing important.”
“Really?”
Ainar didn’t bother trying to figure out what I told her, instead happily letting it go so she could keep eating. Meanwhile, all the other women at the table were worked up for some reason.
“What did you tell her? Actually, wait, I already have an idea.”
“I suppose Yandel has always been an emotional guy.”
“...Why are you all saying things like that? He’s going to be embarrassed.”
What’s with them...?
Rather than responding, I took a page out of Ainar’s book and chose to just stuff my face with food instead. The rest joined in, and we settled into easy conversation as we ate.
“By the way, Mr. Yandel...” Versyl eventually said. “What is that bracelet? Have you always worn that?”
I didn’t even realize I was wearing something until she asked. “What is this...?”
There was an unfamiliar bracelet clasped on my wrist. This was news to me too, so I was just as confused as everyone else. Erwen and Amelia stopped eating and threw in their two cents.
“Huh...? I was going to ask, but I decided to wait until you told us first...”
“You’ve been wearing that this whole time and you really didn’t notice?”
Why did everyone notice but me?

“Then could that be the reward? The special reward you get if you complete the raid with five or fewer people?” Versyl asked, throwing out a perfectly reasonable explanation. But no, this wasn’t the reward I had been expecting. The standard reward for clearing Dreadfear with five people wasn’t a bracelet. Not only that, but I thought my reward this time around was getting to save all of my teammates.
...Then is this another reward on top of having everyone come back alive? Hm...
Well, maybe? I’d never found that particular level before, even after playing the game religiously for nearly ten years. But what was this thing? None of this made any sense to me.
Clink.

I took off the bracelet, and as I carefully examined it to figure out what it could be, a single item popped into my head. Since I wasn’t sure, I asked Versyl to confirm it for me. After all, Versyl had the Special Appraiser license that even Raven didn’t have. And like I thought, after just a few moments, she was able to determine exactly what it was.
“This is... a double-digit Numbered Item...”
So it really is that one.
Amelia, who loved these sorts of treasures, stared at it with sparkling eyes. “Wait, if it’s a double-digit Numbered Item in the shape of a bracelet...”
There was only one item it could be—No. 12: Trust.
Was it a set reward, or randomized? Well, considering the theme of the level, there was no item better suited to be its reward.

...So it was an event that rewarded you with a double-digit Numbered Item. But what the hell were the trigger conditions? If I can figure that out, then I can keep doing it again and again to reap the rewards.
Ding dong.
Suddenly, the doorbell rang.
Visitors, at this hour...?
I stopped eating and headed over to the door. Outside were a group of knights who seemed to be from Mozlan.

“Greetings, Baron Yandel.” Given the polite greeting they gave me as soon as I opened the door, they must not have come bearing bad news. I quickly said hello back and asked what was up. “...Two hours ago, a new achievement was inscribed on the Stone of Honor.”
A new achievement? But what did that have to do with me?
Apparently anticipating my question, the knight clarified without me even needing to ask. “An achievement attained by His Lordship, Baron Yandel.”

So that meant that saving my teammates and obtaining the bracelet weren’t the only rewards for clearing the secret level. I hastily asked what was written on the stone, and as I listened to their explanation, my jaw dropped more and more.
[In Year 157, the Great Barbarian Warrior, Bjorn Yandel, and his companions defeated Dreadfear, the Lord of Terror, and opened a hidden area of the labyrinth.]
Who would’ve thought that there were more hidden areas of the labyrinth yet to be explored?

chapters.title: Chapter 491: Declaration of War (2)
paragraphs: The Stone of Honor was a humongous monument located in the center of the capital of Karnon’s Hero Square. The stone, said to have been created when the first Dimension Square was built, recorded the achievements of heroes who had come and gone over the course of Rafdonia’s history.
The last achievement was, what, six hundred years ago...?

The feats weren’t inscribed on the monument by hand, by the way. The story went that the monument had been crafted using a long-forgotten ancient spell with close ties to the labyrinth. When a feat worthy of being recorded was achieved within the labyrinth, that feat was engraved on the stone automatically.
...At least, that’s according to the backstory given in the game.

I was baffled. In the game, I always thought the Stone of Honor was just a random decorative item there to help explain the setting of the world to the player. I played for ten years, and not once did it do anything.
I can’t believe it actually works.

Upon arriving at the square with a troop of knights escorting me, I stared up at the monument blankly. People were crammed around the outskirts of the square to see me, and the knights on guard duty were clearly struggling to control the chaos. Since this was Karnon, most of the onlookers were nobles dressed in expensive clothing.
“Bjorn Yandel! It’s Baron Bjorn Yandel...!”
“Wooooooh!”
I felt like a zoo animal in a cage. Still, I kept my quiet gaze locked on the stone, trying not to let my discomfort show as I read the achievement listed at the very top.
[...the Last Great Sage, Diplan Groundel Gabrielius, and his companions defeated all the monsters of the Crystal Cave and opened a hidden area of the labyrinth.]
According to the history books, this was the moment the four portals leading up to the second floor first appeared in the labyrinth. The next achievement was similar.
[The Valiant Beastman Warrior, Eamon Myulmarin, and his companions killed the Sea Dragons and discovered a new island.]
The first time an adventurer killed that particular boss monster, a previously nonexistent island suddenly came into view.
[The Great Navigator, Ordel Pikma, and his companions killed all the monsters in the Great Sea and opened a hidden area.]
The first person to completely clear the sixth floor heralded the creation of two new paths to explore, both leading to the seventh floor.
[The Human Adventurer, Ludel Limenin, and his companions reached the Abyss and awakened the spirits of the Lords.]

When someone successfully reached the tenth floor for the first time, the Lords of the Floor took residence in the labyrinth. Then, every time one of them was defeated, Rifts began to appear on their respective floors.
The Iron Hero, Juggernaut... I think he’s said to be the first one to ever defeat a Lord of the Floor.

Anyway, none of that was particularly important right now. From a gamer’s perspective, the stone was nothing more than a patch note. Essentially, whenever something in the labyrinth changed or got unlocked, a message praising the adventurer who achieved the feat was recorded. And now, one of the feats toward the bottom said my name.
[The Great Barbarian Warrior, Bjorn Yandel, and his companions defeated the Lord of Terror, Dreadfear, and opened a hidden area of the labyrinth.]
That meant that an entirely new area had been opened up because of me. Was that good or bad? Since I had no way of knowing, all I could do was stare up at the stone in a daze.
“Baron Yandel! Could you look over here?”
Without thinking, I turned my head when a man who appeared to be a civil servant called my name.
Click!
Suddenly, there was a bright flash from the recording crystal in the man’s hands.
“Please smile! This will go down in the history books forever, after all!”
The history books... Yeah, I guess playing along wouldn’t be so bad.
Since I had already been planning to build up my reputation and gather as much support as possible, things like this were a net positive.
Upon coming to that conclusion, I cast Giantization and flexed my arms with a roar of, “Behel—aaaaaah!”
Sure enough, there was another flash.
Click!
That should make the final cut, right?
[Your Reputation has risen by +10.]
[Your Reputation has risen by +10.]
[Your Reputation has risen by +10.]
[Your Reputation has risen...]
[Your Reputation has...]

Having my name engraved on the Stone of Honor turned out to be a bigger deal than I thought it’d be. The photographer, who I later learned was working directly under the royal family, made me do countless poses in front of the monument until he finally felt like he got the perfect shot.
“Natural lighting really does wonders for pictures and videos!”
After having my photo taken, I was called in for questioning. It wasn’t anything like an interrogation, however—though if I weren’t a noble, it absolutely would have been.
“Ah, I see... so you’re saying you can’t tell us.”
“Experience and knowledge are valuable assets for adventurers. Why should I have to tell you for free?”
“...Y-You’re right. According to the laws regarding the labyrinth, we can’t force you. Yet could you please reconsider for the sake of the kingdom and future generations?”
“Maybe. But I don’t seem to remember my fellow adventurers who accomplished similar feats answering all of your questions either.”
“W-Well...”
“I’m hungry, so I’m leaving.”

By the time I got out of there, it was evening, and the whole world looked different. When I first started to become famous, I was bestowed the nickname of Little Balkan, and when I made a significant contribution to the war against Noark, I was awarded the title of baron.
