In those instances, I also felt a lot like my entire world had changed overnight—but none of that compared to now.
“It’s Bjorn Yandel...!”

All I was doing was walking down the street, but countless people called out to me. Some gave me a round of applause while others ran up to me, asking for handshakes or hugs. One child in the back of the crowd waved at me and begged me to say his name.
What is this...?

Sure, I’d had similar experiences in the past, but this was entirely different. I was in Karnon, the capital. All of the people who lived here were nobles or upper-class citizens. They had never taken much interest in me before but they were different now.
“The Giant! It’s the Giant!”
“The Great Giant who will lead us into a new era...!”
“May you be the endless light Rafdonia needs!”

Even the aristocrats were praising me like excited fans. It did make some sense, in a way, why they were only acting like this now. Someone with heroic potential was completely different from an actual hero.
“I-I can’t believe a hero like him was born in my lifetime.”

The Great Sage, Gabrielius. The Abyss Seeker, Limenin. The Great Navigator, Pikma. The Iron Hero, Juggernaut. It was a point of pride to be in the company of such renowned names as those recorded on the Stone of Honor, and the people were ecstatic that within their lifetimes, they got to lay eyes on a hero who would be remembered and talked about for years to come. Even sharing the same space as me was enough to make them feel like they were a little part of history. Thus, I figured I should give them some fan service.
“Honey! The baron said our baby’s name...!”
“This kid is going to grow up to be someone incredible! I’m sure of it!”
It was time to activate Pope Barbarian Mode.

I continued to work the crowd until I reached the carriage platform. I couldn’t rest my eyes even in the carriage, however, because the people outside followed us, screaming my name. It took a long time to make it back home.
“Woooooh!”

By now, the news had spread throughout the empire. A massive crowd had gathered outside our house, an impromptu festival developing as they all celebrated. Thankfully, knights from Mozlan eventually came by that night to control the crowd and end the festivities.
I reclined on the sofa with a heavy sigh. “Phew... Finally some peace and quiet.”
Erwen walked over to me from where she had been peeping out the window through the curtain. “I guess everyone’s gone to bed now.”
“This is nuts. If today was this bad, what is it going to be like tomorrow?”
“Things will calm down sooner than you think. Surprisingly, people... forget quickly.”
“Like when everyone thought I was dead?”
Erwen sat down across from me, and Auyen spawned to serve us tea like he had been lying in wait.
“Ah, thank you.”

“Of course, Captain.” Auyen’s voice and the look in his eyes were different than usual. He had always been polite, but today, there was a strange level of respect in the way he addressed me. “It must be fate that I was lucky enough to have met you, Captain, and that you were willing to give me the chance to repent for my sins and stand behind you. Even though I can’t offer much, I will continue to support you on your path as best I can.”
Does this guy think he’s a porter for a legendary warrior’s party or something?
It was a little funny to see him sucking up like this, but I didn’t bother bullying him about it.
He left with a, “Have a good night,” and Versyl and Amelia entered the room together.
“I’m sorry,” I told Versyl. “Thanks to me, you can’t even go home and rest.”
“No, I’m glad I didn’t go back home. Given the situation, it would have been hard for me to make it back here tomorrow. I’m also a bit too tired to head all the way back anyway.”
“I see...”

Honestly, none of this felt real. Everyone was calling me a hero, but did I really do anything worthy of being recorded on the Stone of Honor? We only stumbled upon the hidden event by accident, and it was pure luck that we succeeded in the first place. The Ice Rock expedition was several times harder than what we just went through, and many more people died there.
In terms of difficulty, that was way harder...
I shook the thought away. “Anyway, did you get some rest?”
“No... I couldn’t sleep. But don’t worry about me. We were only there for seven days, and they were all pretty easy aside from that last day.”
Well, that’s true. I usually pass out from exhaustion after returning from the labyrinth too, but I’m relatively fine right now.
Ainar was the only one of us who was sleeping soundly.

“So, I examined it once more in my spare time...” Versyl took out No. 12: Trust, and placed it on the table. I had given her the item before following the knights to Karnon for my questioning. “First of all, it seems to be the type of item that binds itself to people’s souls.”
“Binds to the soul?”

“Yes, but strangely enough, it seems to be bound to multiple people. It seems that you, Ms. Fenelin, Ms. Tersia, and I can all use it.” To demonstrate, Versyl put the bracelet on Amelia’s wrist. It didn’t adjust to fit her and instead slid right off.
“You mean only those who went through the test can use it.”
“Yes. That’s very likely to be the case.”
As I mulled this over, Versyl cautiously spoke up. “But... only one of us can use it at a time. So who do you think should wear it?”

Trust was an extremely versatile item—so versatile, in fact, that it could be effectively wielded by tanks, DPSers, wizards, and priests alike. That was because it had three main effects and thus three ways to use it.
One, you are immune to damage dealt by allies you’re Bound to.

When a tank used the item, their teammates could bombard the frontlines with AoE attacks without worrying about them getting a single scratch. In other words, the biggest problem tanks faced was solved and more diverse tactics became available to the party.
Two, the damage you deal increases relative to the number of allies you’re Bound to.
When DPSers used the item, their damage increased dramatically.
Three, it doubles all beneficial effects applied to allies you’re Bound to.
When worn by a priest or support-type adventurer, their buffs, heals, and other helpful effects doubled in strength.
We can exclude the third use for our team, since it doesn’t apply...
In the end, there were only two options: give it to Erwen to take her damage output to an entirely new level, or keep it myself to increase the stability and durability of our party.
Then again, there’s no reason to overthink this.

In true barbarian fashion, when there were two types of food on the table, you just had to use both hands to eat all of it. As such, it didn’t take long for me to reach my verdict. I would wear it for the majority of the time, but when we needed more firepower, I’d have Erwen use it. “I’ll wear it for now and give it to either you, Erwen, or Ainar when necessary.”

Everyone nodded, seemingly satisfied with my decision. However, I noticed Amelia looked a little disheartened. It was an extremely minute shift, but I immediately caught it since Amelia normally didn’t have any expression on her face at all.
“Now that that’s settled, all of you should rest up. We can talk more tomorrow. Oh, but stay for a bit, Emily. I have something to talk to you about.”

Versyl and Erwen left the room without argument after noticing the strange look on Amelia’s face as well. Now it was just the two of us. After standing for the entirety of our previous conversation, Amelia came over to the sofa to sit down. “...If I’d known this would happen, I wouldn’t have left you guys to interrogate them.”

I couldn’t blame her for feeling upset. She wasn’t able to share in the spoils or have her name written down as my “companion” on the Stone of Honor. Still, I tried to console her with logic rather than comforting platitudes. “Try to see this as a positive. If your name was written down on the stone, things would have gotten tricky for us.”

When I went to see the monument today, I noticed that my party members’ names were listed underneath the word “companions” in very fine text. Simply put, if Amelia had gone through the test with us, her real name, Amelia Rainwales, would have been exposed to the public.
“I... I know that.”
“You do?”
“It’s just... I feel a bit bitter.”
When I tilted my head, Amelia raised her eyes to meet mine. “Because that means I can never stand by your side as my real self.”
Um...

Unable to come up with anything to say in response to that, all I could do was awkwardly fumble for the right words. Amelia then smoothly changed the subject, her strange mood apparently behind her. “Anyway, there’s some information you need to know.”
“Is this about that thing you mentioned you would tell me later?”
“Yes.”
I had told her to stay behind specifically so I could ask about this, but the grim look on her face was making me anxious all over again. “What is it?”
“There’s something wrong with my memory.”
“...What?” At first, I honestly thought she might be telling an out-of-character joke, but as she went on, it became more and more apparent how grave the situation was.

“There was a moment during the interrogation where I remember being in a daze, and when I came to my senses, the recording crystal was destroyed. I’m certain that I never lost consciousness or did anything to it, though.”
“I see.”

“I’ve compared how much time passed to how much I could remember, and there was a slight discrepancy.” A discrepancy of about ten minutes, she went on to say. In other words, she only remembered interrogating them for thirty-five minutes, but forty-five minutes in total had elapsed by the time she realized something had happened.
“What are the chances that you’re wrong about this?”

“Zero.” If she was that confident in her answer, then something had to have happened. “Thinking back on it, there’s even something strange about how I remember acting. Normally, I would have interrogated our captives thoroughly. But from what I can remember, I interrogated them casually and didn’t dig for any major pieces of information.”
I stayed quiet.
“That’s why I came up with the hypothesis that someone used magic on me. Someone must have manipulated my memory and implanted false information.”
“And is that what happened?”
“I still don’t know. I had Ms. Gowland examine me, but she said she couldn’t find any evidence that someone had cast a spell on me.”
Memory manipulation... Who on earth could be the culprit? Was there a wizard of that caliber working under Count Alminus? Or was it a third party?
I was deep in thought when Amelia offered up a final piece of information. “And one last thing: when I came to my senses and looked around, the weapons were all wiped clean.”
“...The weapons?”
“Yes, even the sword that stabbed you. It looked like someone had wiped it off with something.”
That was suspicious. What the hell happened? I was relieved that Amelia was safe, of course, but now there were even more things to worry about.

“Those guys... they said they took a request from the black market, right? That’s why they didn’t know who the client was.” I should start there. The black market was famous for its iron-clad security and the disturbing rumors that no one who stepped foot inside without permission survived. At the end of the day, however, a den of thieves was still just a kind of house. “I should pay them a visit.”
In other words, if I started wrecking the place, someone was sure to have something to say about it.

chapters.title: Chapter 492: Declaration of War (3)
paragraphs: It was two days since the labyrinth closed.
Did I really sleep for over thirty hours...?

While the hidden event at the end of this month’s quest was exhausting, I hadn’t exerted myself too hard in the labyrinth otherwise, so thirty hours of sleep was more than enough for me to feel fully refreshed.
Hoooooonk!
When I headed down to the first floor, I found Ainar still lying on the sofa sound asleep in the same position she was in before I went to sleep myself.
She’s really good at resting...

My first stop was the kitchen to satiate my hunger. Luckily, all sorts of dishes were already cooked and ready for us to eat. Did Auyen prepare them in advance knowing that we would all head to the kitchen to eat something immediately after waking up?
...Forget being an adventurer, that guy was born to be a butler.
I stuffed my mouth with the food he laid out, marveling at Auyen’s talents. Then I went out the front door to check the mailbox, only to find that a mountain of mail had arrived while I was asleep.
What is all of this...?

Sorting through the letters one by one revealed that most were invitations filled with flattering rhetoric and profuse praise for my accomplishments, each asking to meet with me. It reminded me of the old days. When I first started to gain fame, something similar had happened.
...There are quite a few applications to join our clan as well.

People had taken a sudden interest in joining our clan. As I looked through their résumés, I was surprised to see that some of the applicants were unexpectedly skilled. The most impressive of them was an older man who had made it to the ninth floor back in his prime. He was even a high-ranking enough adventurer to have his own nickname.
That’s too bad. If he weren’t a tank, I would have accepted him on the spot...

I planned to grow our clan in the future, but at the moment, we only consisted of a single party and weren’t looking for any more tanks. Plus, when we eventually added our second team, Sven Parav and Kaislan were already set to fill the tank slots.
I should probably reach out to him when I want to make a third team down the line.

Whatever the case, I was proud that such a high-rank adventurer had expressed interest in our clan. I hadn’t even needed to scout him. It hit me at that moment just how far I’d come from my Team Half-Wit days working under that dwarf.
...Well, even if I didn’t have much back then, it was a lot of fun.
I continued to read through the mail with a smile on my face. Unfortunately, it seemed there weren’t any priests among the applicants.

I’ve reached this level of fame, yet they still don’t plan on making the offer themselves, huh? It’s like they’re trying to say that if we want a priest, we still have to go to them and make an official request.

It was mind-boggling to think that despite going through so much and gaining this kind of reputation, not once had I ever officially had a priest on my party’s roster. Since potions didn’t do much for me anymore, it would be nice to have a healer.
I was still standing outside, enjoying the refreshing morning breeze as I checked the mail when a letter suddenly caught my eye.
Count Alminus...?

The second I saw that familiar golden wax seal, I tore open the envelope to see what was inside. The letter started with the standard too-long introduction typical of noble households, but what mattered was the main gist.
I would like to resolve the misunderstanding between us. Please visit me at your earliest convenience.
The count had extended an olive branch.
“Misunderstanding...”

Why had he suddenly changed his tune? If I had to guess, it was because of the Stone of Honor. Upon witnessing my fame skyrocket at a rate he never could have imagined, he must have determined that making an enemy of me would do him more harm than good. After all, the Riakis issue wasn’t a matter of money for him. It was purely a matter of pride. However, the possibility still remained that this was some sort of scheme.
Then I guess I should make an appointment to meet with him...

Since I had nothing to do until tonight, I went back up to my room to sleep. Then, when it started to get dark, I stepped out of the bedroom only to find Amelia waiting for me. “Can we really not go together?” she asked.
“It’s fine. It’ll be easier if I go alone.”
“All right, then.”

I put on an iron helmet and took off under the cover of nightfall to avoid garnering attention. My path took me down Main Street until I finally reached a pub down an alley on the outskirts of Kommelby.

“It’s not even a proper construction site,” I said under my breath. The building was old and on the verge of collapsing. The pub itself was closed, and the sign hanging outside was rusty and looked like it was on the verge of falling off.
Creeeak.

The inside looked even worse than the outside. All sorts of building materials were scattered around, and the entire place was covered in dirt and dust—that was, except for one clear path leading toward the back.
Those are footprints.

I meandered further into the building, following them until I was eventually met with a staircase leading to the basement. At the bottom of the stairs, there was an iron door with no guard or bouncer or anything in front of it. A place like this didn’t need protections like that anyway.
Now, then, what’s behind that door?
This was something I’d been curious about ever since I first started playing Dungeon and Stone. I marched right over to the door and used as much strength as I could to force it open.
Creak! Clang!
The door promptly fell completely off its hinges. However, despite what I was hoping, the only thing behind the door was another wall.
How lame.

The fact that there was no hidden area behind the door was disappointing. Still, not letting it get to me, I quickly took out the magic stone I brought with me, inserting it in the small groove next to the door.
Flash!

All of a sudden, I was standing in an entirely different location. The black market could only be reached through teleportation, which was why it had hundreds of entrances leading to it throughout the entire city.
I’m finally here.
I was now in a small stone room. Inside said room was another door connecting to a hallway, a sign with the number 217 bolted into it.
Shit. 217 is pretty far from Main Street.
I figured I should just start exploring and took a step toward the door.
Thud.
Suddenly, the door flung open from the other side, and three big, hulking masked men stormed into the room.
Hm? How strange. There wasn’t an escort service in the game.
“What can I do for you?”
“...Did you damage the door before coming here?”
“Oh, that?” I never imagined that they would have already noticed that, but I answered honestly. “I was curious what was behind it.”
“...You need to come with us.”
“What if I don’t want to?”
“I didn’t ask. I was telling you!” When Big Guy A raised his voice at me, the other two behind him started to close in. I felt a twinge of regret.
Maybe I shouldn’t have broken that door. I only wanted to take a look at what was behind it while I was there...
Well, what could I do? I was just going to have to adapt.
Thud.

I swung my arms, shoving the two men coming at me aside. It didn’t take much strength—in fact, it was like swatting away a mosquito. However, even after getting rammed into the wall, the two didn’t seem eager to rush at me in retaliation. Instead, they cautiously kept their distance. “You’re an adventurer?”
“You got a problem with that?”
“The only problem here is you. Looks like we’re going to have to do this the hard way.”
“Oh, really now?”
As I cleaned out my ear with my pinky finger, Big Guy A’s tone grew deeper and more threatening. “Judging by your build, you must be a barbarian or beastperson. Is this your first time here?”
“How’d you know?”
“Because if you knew anything about this place, you wouldn’t have done something so reckless.”
That kind of hurt my feelings a bit. Was there anyone out there who knew more about the black market than me?
Thud.
Before we started, I decided to take off the tight, suffocating helmet bothering me. There was no real reason to hide my identity any longer.
“...So you were a barbarian.”
Surprisingly, though, they didn’t recognize me. Not that it mattered.
Shiiink!

Big Guy A quickly unsheathed his sword, showcasing his fancy aura. Luckily for me, our current location wasn’t anything like the cave I was trapped in in the labyrinth. Since I had access to my skills now, something like an aura didn’t pose any threat to me.
Fwit!

Perhaps because we were in a tight space, he tried to stab me rather than slash. I didn’t have room to dodge, so I simply reached out my hand to grab his blade. The reaction of these aura-using bastards was the same every damn time—that look of shock and confusion on their faces and the slight trembling of their blades. I grinned as I tugged on the sword.
Punch!
I then promptly shoved my fist into his face.
All right, that’s one down.
“...R-Reinforcements!”

As soon as he dropped, the other two tried to retreat and call for backup. I quickly ran after them, grabbing them both by the backs of their necks in unison and shoving them into the walls on either side of me.
These two weren’t all that impressive.

I shook the blood off my hands. Along with the blood of the Big Men Trio, there was some of my own mixed in. I ended up getting a pretty deep wound when I grabbed his sword, probably because I didn’t use Giantization. Well, it was whatever. With my Natural Regeneration, the wound would heal given some time. It wouldn’t even leave a scar.
“Now, let’s go and take a look around.”

Before heading out, I squatted down and took off Big Guy A’s mask. Well, it was more like I brushed aside the smashed pieces of the mask that still remained. Unfortunately, it was impossible to make out his features considering his entire face got bashed in and was covered in blood.
“...I never imagined that the security in this place would be so high,” I muttered under my breath.

Suddenly, in a faint voice, he rasped, “B-Bjorn... Yandel...?” It would seem that getting punched in the face had knocked enough sense into him for him to recognize me. “Wh-what is... someone like you... doing here...?”
“Again, got a problem? I just came here for some business. Since you’re awake, let me ask you a few things. Where is the head of this—?”
What the—?
He passed out.

After leaving him there on the floor, not feeling guilty in the slightest, I headed out into the hallway. Some onlookers had gathered in front of the stone room, and they flinched and took a step back when I emerged. Their clothes suggested they were customers rather than employees here.
They wouldn’t know even if I asked them...

“Hey, over there! What’s going on?” Another large man appeared around the corner. He ran toward us after noticing the crowd and made a beeline for the open door, only to find bodies lying on the floor. “Wh-what is this...?”
His reaction made me feel like the culprit in a thriller movie.
I quickly grabbed the back of his head and lifted him off the ground. “Ahh—!”
“Where should I go to meet with the head of this place?”
“I can’t tell you...”
“Even if I’ll kill you if you don’t?”
I tried threatening him, but he just closed his eyes as if to accept death. “K-Kill me, then... That would be many times better than becoming a traitor...”
“Ah, is that so?”
Thud!
I let go of his limp form, letting him tumble onto the floor. Obtaining information through intimidation wasn’t going to work all that well, then. But no problem.
Ring! Ring! Ring!
The frantic ringing of alarm bells tore down the hall, heralding all-out war. “Intruder! Intruder!” All sorts of guys rushed toward me.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
Well, if I beat them all up, the head of this place would have to show their face eventually, right?
[You have cast Giantization.]

[You have used a transformation-type ability. Due to the effects of Evolving Shell, the amount of Soul Power consumed by the ability has been reduced by half, and your highest stat has increased by 1.5x.]

The black market supposedly existed somewhere underground, but no one knew its exact location, as it was treated by most people as more of a tall tale than anything else. After all, if there were an underground building the size of three soccer stadiums combined somewhere in the city, wouldn’t it have been discovered a lot sooner?
Ring! Ring! Ring!
Ahh, it’s too damn loud in here. When the hell are they going to turn that thing off?
How much farther did I need to walk to reach the main area again?
This place is disgustingly large.

The fact that the building was massive also had its advantages, though. Unlike the cramped stone room from earlier, the height and width of the rest of the place was astounding, allowing me to cast Giantization without any issue.
Stomp! Stomp! Stomp!
The people who suddenly found themselves in the same hallway as a rampaging giant fell neatly into two categories.
“R-Run away...!” One was customers, who only came here to make a purchase and fled the moment they spotted me.
“Stop him...!” The second category encompassed the group of large men running straight toward me to stop me.
I noticed earlier while facing the aura user—the level of the people down here was a lot higher than I had expected.
I’d say they’re about on par with most fourth-floor adventurers...?

And that was just on average—some of them would probably be fine even on the sixth floor. Even though I had an almost infinite healing factor, it was still objectively dangerous for me to take on such a large number of opponents without support. But strangely, this all felt about as dangerous as a relaxing stroll in the park to me.
That was because no matter what I did, I knew they couldn’t kill me—not because of my strength, but for another reason entirely.
“...S-Stop! W-We have orders from up above! We were told to capture him alive and avoid injuring him as much as possible!”
“What? W-We have to capture him alive?”
So news of my presence had reached the higher-ups.
Stomp! Stomp! Stomp!
I continued to run forward, destroying everything in my path. A small, trembling voice behind me made its way up to my ear.
“How? How are we supposed to capture a monster like that...?!”

Unfortunately for them, their hands were tied by their superiors’ mediocre orders. I took advantage of that to create as much of a scene as possible. The few of them who didn’t back away in fear dropped their weapons and ran forward to subdue me. They were easy to deal with, though. A full-speed charge was enough to send them flying into the walls.
Smash!

Their willingness to obey their boss’s orders was admirable but also extremely short-sighted. Even if they attacked me with all their strength and all the troops they had at their disposal, they’d never be able to subdue me without hurting me first.
“B-Baron Yandel! P-Please stop! The higher-ups want to have a conversation with you—”
What are they talking about? There’s no way I’m going to stop now. This is way too much fun.
Since I was currently untouchable, I decided to put even more oomph into my rampage.
Stomp! Stomp! Stomp!

None of their attacks ever landed a single scratch on my body. It was a religious experience. Even though I was just running, it felt like I was expertly deflecting each blow without even needing to blink.
This must be what it feels like to be a martial arts master in Murim.
“Hahaha!” I happily continued my stomping stroll around the building.

“Shield wall!” At some point, they built a shield wall in an attempt to stop me in my tracks. This must have been another order from above. If I ended up dying, that would be the end of the black market, after all. According to the rumors, this place thought itself above the laws of nobles, but in reality, an organization like this couldn’t run without buy-in from the nobility.
“We’ve received further orders! No attacking him no matter what!”

At least I now knew what this place’s higher-ups were thinking. They knew that if any harm were to come to me, their market would be doomed. Their only hope of actually dealing with me would have been to kill me behind the scenes, but there were already far too many witnesses for them to pull off a quiet assassination at this point.
“Hiding behind a shield, you cowards? Who is the leader of this evil den? Come out! I, Bjorn Yandel, shall punish you on behalf of the royal family!”
“Th-that’s what we’ve been saying! Our leader wants to talk to—”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

I ran rampant for a while longer as the number of people deployed to their shield wall increased, bolstering the wall’s sturdiness. They even brought wizards and special ability users in to cast support and debuff spells. Slowly, I was overwhelmed by their numbers.
Thud.

When I finally stopped running for the first time, I looked behind me to find I was sandwiched in by an identical shield wall made up of dozens of people. Even I’d have a hard time busting through all of them.
I sighed.
But if I get cornered like pathetic prey, he’s going to look down on me when I meet him...
As I mulled this over, the man who seemed to be in charge of security made his way through the shield wall. “...Baron! P-Please calm down for a moment so we can—”
“It’d be a waste to try to reason with evil bastards like you!”
“...But you have nowhere else to run!”
What was he talking about? Did these guys really not know how barbarians worked?
All right, that’s enough thinking.
I swung my hammer as hard as I could, not toward the people holding up their shields, but instead toward the wall on my left.
Craaash!
When you found the path ahead of you blocked, you just had to make yourself a new one.

chapters.title: Chapter 493: Declaration of War (4)
paragraphs: Boooooom!

I broke down the wall, crawled through it into a new, empty hallway, and proceeded to take up my jog again. Whenever I ended up surrounded, I would simply swing my hammer at another wall and continue on my merry way.
Boooooom!
Occasionally, one of the walls would lead to a dead end, but that wasn’t a problem. Because of the layout of the building, I could also go upstairs and downstairs as well.
Boooooom!

As I smashed through the ceiling and jumped upstairs, I found myself in an unusual place. It was a poorly lit corridor with dozens of steel bars spanning its length on both sides. Behind those bars were people of every race, including some barbarians. And every one of them was marked with an identical tattoo in a similar location.
Slaves...
Even though a massive barbarian had just burst through the floor, they all stared out into space blankly, looking utterly lifeless. As a twenty-first-century barbarian, it was an unsettling sight.
So slaves still exist in this world.

Slavery was illegal in Rafdonia. At one point in its history, those who committed grave sins had been legally forced into bondage, but that practice had long since disappeared after the law was revised about a hundred years ago. The slaves who had committed heinous crimes were promptly executed and the people who were enslaved for misdemeanors had been forced to pay a fine before being restored their status as ordinary citizens. In the end, though, most died shortly after, as an ex-slave had no hope of paying their taxes.

As I looked around, I noticed a little boy who still had some life in his eyes. I walked over to talk to him. “Hey.” When I called out to him, he skittered away until his back was up against the wall, clearly terrified. I ignored his reaction and continued. “How were you caught and put here?”
Unfortunately, the only response I got came from somewhere behind me. “...S-Stop! Baron Yandel!”
Don’t these guys know when to quit? They should know by now that they won’t be able to subdue me.

I ignored them too and stared at the little boy in front of me. Surprisingly, the shouts of the people chasing after me seemed to help elicit a response from the boy. “The Giant...?” he quietly murmured, his eyes going wide. “Giant... I heard you’re a hero who saves people and punishes bad guys... Is that true?”
“Well, sort of.”
“...Did you come here to save us too?”
“No,” I said honestly. “I just happened to find you. So tell me, how did you end up here?”

The big guy who had been chasing me and begging me to stop slowly drew near. The little boy flicked his gaze between the two of us before cautiously answering me. “My mom... she couldn’t pay her debt, so I had to pay it back instead.”
“Your mom? What happened to her?”
“Because she couldn’t pay her taxes... she died.”
“What about that elf girl next to you?” I asked, glancing down at the girl sitting next to him behind the bars.
“She couldn’t pay her debts back either,” the little boy quietly explained. “She had the money, but the bad guys wouldn’t take it. That’s why she was brought here.”
I said nothing.
“She actually managed to escape once and came back to save me, but... after the bad guys dragged her away a few times, she doesn’t talk anymore.”
“I see.”

That was why this kid was the only one with a spark of life left in his eyes. Those who tried to rebel and fight back must have faced intense abuse. It was easier to break a person’s spirit than most would assume.
Then that settles it...

After wrapping up my conversation with the little boy, I turned my attention to the big guys. The one at the front of the pack flinched when our eyes met. He looked like a bully who had just been caught picking on someone weaker than him.
Step.

I approached, my steps deliberately slow. “You know something?” I asked. He lifted his shield with a silent gulp. “I haven’t killed any of you so far.” I knew they were bad guys, so I beat them down without mercy, but I still moderated my strength so they at least wouldn’t die. “Why do you think that is?”
“...You don’t want to make an enemy of us either. That’s what the higher-ups have determined.”
“Is that so? That’s correct,” I calmly agreed.

The reason these guys hadn’t hurt me was because they had guessed my intentions from the start. Otherwise, they would have never treated an intruder like this. If I had been running around beating everyone to death, there was no way they would only be holding up shields and trying to subdue me. That was why I had planned to assert my dominance just a little bit, then have a peaceful conversation with the boss here to get what I wanted and leave.
However, things were different now.
“Please tell us what you want.”
Why did I always make a Plan B? Because this world was full of variables. There would always be something out there that might force me to change my plans—just like this.
“We are ready to have a conversation with—”
Before he could finish his sentence, I put all my strength into clocking him in the jaw.
Crack!
Despite his large size, he flew into the wall like a baseball and dropped to the ground with a thud, wriggling like a bug on its last legs.
“How resilient,” I said, looking down at him. “I even swung to kill.”
Everyone standing behind him immediately flinched in response. However, despite what I’d done to him, the bug still hadn’t figured out the situation he was in. “Why... did you do that?”
Oh, that?
“Didn’t you say so yourself, Your Lordship? That you don’t want to make an enemy of us?”
“Yeah, I did.” I stalked closer, lifting my hammer and staring down at him as he writhed in pain.
When he saw that I had my weapon raised, his expression shifted. “Stop. You are going to regret this...”
What a strange thing to say. “Why would I regret this?” I swung my hammer down as hard as I could.
Crack!
His squirming body stopped moving.
“You’ll be the ones regretting it.”
This was the right choice.

There was no further conversation to be had. After I was done bashing his face in with my hammer, the rest of them clamped their mouths shut and raised their guards, scrutinizing every little move I made.
Step.
As soon as I took a step forward, the group of large men took a step back in unison. But just as I was about to rush at all of them—
Creeeak!
Suddenly, the thick iron door behind me creaked open. When I turned around, I found a middle-aged man surrounded by a heavy escort of large guards walking into the room.
“Let’s stop here, Baron Yandel,” he called out to me.
“Who are you?”

“I am Mel, the current head of the Shadow Organization.” Simply put, he was in charge of this black market. The man who called himself Mel glanced over at his subordinate on the ground. “That friend of mine over there. Is he still alive?”
“...He’s still breathing, Boss.”
“That’s a relief.” Mel then turned back to me and asked, “Baron Yandel, before we begin our conversation, may I treat my friend over there first?”
“Do you think that I, a baron of Rafdonia, would accept the demands of a criminal who committed treason?”
“Haha, treason... It seems that you have a very low opinion of us.”
“Then is there another opinion I should have? You clearly disobey the strict laws of Rafdonia.”
“Hm, I see.” He nodded like I had a point. “Then, everyone, get out of the way.”
Our audience’s eyes bugged out at his orders.
“Boss!”
“It’s too dangerous!”
His underlings started to protest, but Mel was stubborn. “I won’t say it twice.”
I didn’t know how he normally disciplined them, but as soon as he said that, they all shut their mouths and started to leave.
Step, step.

Mel walked forward, approaching me. Now, the only two left in this hall full of cells was the two of us. To be honest, I was surprised by his gall. Was he incredibly strong? Confident enough that he could take me on? Or did he simply not care if he died here? There were a million possibilities that filled my head.
Step.
However, even as my mind reeled, he walked right past me and squatted down by his underling on the floor, leaving his back completely defenseless as he took out a potion from his pocket.
Sizzle!
Roiling bubbles started to boil up on his underling’s punched-in face. The big guy, who had been on the verge of death, began to tremble a bit.
“That’s a high-quality potion.”
“Yes, it is.”

I didn’t understand this at all. Just what in the world was happening? Unable to come up with an answer no matter how much I mulled it over, I decided to flat-out ask him. “What are you trying to do here?”
“I’m only saving someone that was about to die.”
“But you could have died instead.”
“Yes, that’s true. But this man is one of my people.”
I was momentarily rendered speechless. I had met countless leaders before, but I had never met someone like him. “You’re risking your life for a reason like that?”
“A person’s values and priorities are subjective. Just like how you changed your plan the moment you stumbled across these slaves here.”
“...You’re a funny guy.”

“Now, how about we go somewhere else? This place isn’t the most conducive to conversation.” He immediately turned back down the hallway, offering me his defenseless back again. I was dumbfounded, but all I could do for now was follow him.

After passing through several doors, we eventually reached a small room. “This is a private room reserved for our guests. All of our customers have already returned to the city for the day, so you don’t have to worry about anyone disrupting us.” He sat down at the table in the center of the room, then looked at me in an apparent invitation to sit down with him.
At this point, I couldn’t help but ask him, “Are you not afraid?”
“I am afraid.”
“Doesn’t look like it.”

“Well, it can’t be helped, can it? If I hurt you, Baron Yandel, then that will be the end of me. Both my family and this place will be wiped off the map. I am not so reckless as to risk such a thing happening.”
“Isn’t what you’re doing now reckless too?”

“Well, if I die, then I die. There’s nothing more to it. At the end of the day, someone else will step up and take my place, and though it might take some time, everything will return to the way it was. Dirty water always pools at the bottom, after all.”
I stared at him in silence.
“Oh, and killing me might help you vent your anger, but it would also mean you wouldn’t walk out of here with what you initially came here for.”

How could someone be so brave? Despite only having exchanged a few words with him, I could already tell just how impressive he was. However, there was no need to beat around the bush any longer. “So what do you want to say?”
“You should be the one to answer that, not me. Didn’t you come here because you wanted something?”
Oh. Damn, yeah, that’s true.

I was once again left speechless by his response. Still, since I didn’t want to look like the weaker party in this negotiation, I decided to launch right into my demands without a second thought. “Give me the identities of your clients.” That was my main motivation for visiting the black market today.
“Some of the wizards... are making requests through the black market.”
As supply dwindled, some wizards had been going to the black market to obtain barbarian hearts.
“Your Lordship! O-On the black market... there is also a bounty for your heart.”
Someone had asked for my heart.
“I-I’m not lying... I was just offered the job through the black market. I-I don’t know anything else... I-I don’t know who made the request, either...”
Someone else had made a request to sabotage our raid against the Lord of the Floor.
“I see... So that’s why you came all the way here.”
“I don’t need excuses, so give me an answer.”
“Asking for the personal information of our clients is a very difficult demand to make of someone in my position.”
“Are you saying you won’t do it?”
“No. I’m a merchant, after all. This will reduce the number of commissions we receive, but it would still be more beneficial to us than it would be to make an enemy of you.”
“So?”
“I will arrange for the personal information of our clients to be delivered to you within the day,” Mel said, calmly accepting my request.

This conversation wasn’t going how I had expected it would at all. The only reason I ran around causing all that mayhem beforehand was because I assumed our negotiations would be a long, drawn-out fight.
“Is that everything?” he inquired.
“No, there is one more thing.”
“Please tell me.”
I gave Mel my final request. “Free the slaves that are locked up here.”
I can’t just leave after seeing that.
“Hmmm. I see that you are the type who believes in universal dignity.”
“You’re asking a lot of questions and making a lot of noises, but all I need to hear from you is a yes or a no.”
“...May I think it over for a moment?”
“Go ahead.”

Once given my permission, Mel closed his eyes without any fear, mulling my request over. About three minutes later, he finally opened them. “All right. I will free the slaves and refrain from working in the slave industry from now on.”
“...You came to that decision quickly.”
He met my eye like a man with nothing to hide. “In truth, it’s a business I’ve wanted to part ways with myself.”
“You already wanted to leave it?”
“There have been quite a few instances where buyers have been unable to properly manage their slaves, and there have been a number of occasions where that nearly led to major issues and scandals.”

So he had tried to cut ties with the industry several times as a result, but had been unable to find the justification he needed to do so? Well, it must have been hard to just shut it down given the large profits this side of the business had garnered the black market for hundreds of years.
“However, since it’s by your request,” he continued, “now no one will be able to oppose my decision. This worked out rather well for us. Then, is that everything?”
“Yeah. I’ll get out of your way as soon as I am given your clients’ information and see the slaves released.”
“In that case, I will work toward fulfilling your requests as soon as possible.”
After wrapping up our conversation, he summoned his underlings back and doled out orders. By daybreak, I was given the information I needed, and the hundreds of slaves were all set free.
“Mel Asmond,” I asked as I was about to leave, “why were you willing to give in to my demands so easily?”
Rather than responding, he stared at me for a long moment, a strange look on his face. “...I see you are already aware of the house I hail from.”
That’s because I completed the Black Market event in the game.
As a result, I knew that House Asmond had reigned as king of this jungle for many years.
Still, I didn’t let him distract me. “That’s not what I asked you,” I said firmly.
In the face of my stubbornness, he freely spoke his mind. “Heroes are always short-lived. There’s no reason for us to be on the end of a falling blade.”
In other words, with the way I acted, he figured I wouldn’t live for much longer anyway.
Mel Asmond, the head of the black market. What an interesting guy.
For some reason, I had a feeling I would be seeing him again in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 494: Declaration of War (5)
paragraphs: There was a saying that went, “Check your partner’s room before getting married.” In other words, the things in a person’s room could tell you a lot about their personality. You could not only tell if someone preferred finery or being frugal but also if they were lazy or hard-working. You could figure out what colors they preferred, what hobbies they had, what type of job they worked, and more. Even if you knew nothing about a person going in, you could get a rough sense of what type of person they were just by looking at their room.
A prime example of this was the reception room I was currently sitting in.

The interior of the room immediately gave off luxurious vibes. Although the decor wasn’t gaudy or excessive, the few pieces of furniture and decorations present were clearly expensive. It was clear at a glance that the items must have cost a fortune.
Munch.
The snacks laid out on the table for me were plentiful too. It was hard to imagine that so many different kinds of delicious treats had been prepared for just one person.
Gulp.
There was even a servant who stood at the entrance at all times, refilling my half-empty glass each time I drank from it. And that wasn’t even the icing on the cake.
This might be the first time I’ve ever seen a reception room with its own elevator music.
In the corner of the room was a bald musician playing relaxing music on a stringed instrument.
He doesn’t act like a new hire brought on specifically for today, either.
Just looking around this reception room, I could clearly tell what kind of person the owner of this house was.
He has the heart of a merchant.

Everything about it told me in no uncertain terms that the owner put hospitality above all else, rather than simply prioritizing showing off their immense wealth. Well, if I waited here a bit longer, I’d be able to see just how well he actually ended up treating me when he arrived.
The meeting time we agreed on is five minutes from now. He’s definitely going to come in right on time.

I crossed my legs and opened a random newspaper from a nearby pile, only to find that the article on the front page was about me. To be fair, I figured the headline would have been the same regardless of which one I chose.
The Great Hero recorded on the Stone of Honor, Baron Yandel, has drawn his sword and pointed it at the traitors of the empire lurking in the underworld...!

It had been three days since my scene at the black market, and the story was finally making headlines. There was no way Mozlan didn’t try to keep the incident a secret, but it must have been impossible to hide the 397 slaves that had been set free from the public eye.
Though they did leave out the fact that most of the people who frequented the slave trade were nobles...

Even though the article was missing a few key details here and there, it still provided a decent overview of the situation. For example, it mentioned how the slaves had been able to regain their status as regular citizens and that they were currently staying in a temporary shelter that Mozlan had prepared. A five-year tax exemption policy had been created to help them out as well.
Oh, and there was an interview.
“...he told those guys that he wouldn’t regret it, but that they definitely would.”
The interviewee was anonymous, but judging by the statements they gave, it was clearly that kid I met, the one who had been trapped in the cage.
So the black market has completely closed? Well, I guess it makes sense for them to lay low for the time being.
While I was reading through the article, the servant suddenly moved from the entrance and politely approached me. “Count Alminus has arrived.”
“Is that so?” I closed the newspaper I was reading and set it down on the table. “Tell him to come in.”
It was time to get to work.
[Your Reputation has risen by +10.]
[Your Reputation has risen by +10.]
[Your Reputation has risen by +10.]
[Your Reputation has risen...]
[Your Reputation has...]
“Hahaha!”
“Haha!”

The room was filled with the crude yet hearty laughter of an old man. Next to the table was a photographer, who was passionately taking pictures of the two of us. So this was why he had wanted to meet with me—to have our picture taken by a paparazzo who charged 2.135 billion stones for top-of-the-line shots.
“Baron Yandel, just a little more... barbaric... No. Can you try smiling more like a man?”
“Of course! Hahaha!
“I would appreciate it if you could smile like that while looking over at the count.”
“Of course. Haha! Hahaha...!”

In return for dropping his 2.1-billion-stone lawsuit against me, Count Alminus agreed to settle things with a friendly photo shoot. These would go on to be photos that would be preserved through the ages, after all. Since he was an elderly man who didn’t have much time left, all he wanted was a way to be remembered after his death.

Of course, the second I heard that, I immediately assumed he had some kind of ulterior motive or scheme at work here. However, after thinking it through, I grew convinced that he didn’t. I mean, I would admittedly think it would be awesome if my grandfather had a picture with Einstein.
“Hahaha!”
“Haha! Hahaha...!”

Whatever the case, the two of us continued to smile widely and laugh together as the photographer took pictures. Said pictures would tell the story of a friendship that had transcended both age and race. Eventually, after trying out a few more poses, the photographer handed me a cheap bottle of beer and the count a glass of wine so we could make a toast.
“Perfect! Absolutely perfect!”
That was how we ended up with our shot. The count excitedly went over to see the picture himself and, satisfied with the results, gave the man a hefty bonus.
And that marked the end of our business with each other.
“Haha, good work, Your Lordship,” the count beamed. “You must be tired, so have something to eat before you go.”
“No, it’s fine. I’m not hungry.”
Wait, oops, my bad.
“Oh, uh,” I stuttered, “I mean, I have someone waiting for me at home, so I should head back now. It’s a shame, but we’ll have to share a meal some other time.”

“Haha, yes... it’s best to sit down to eat with family whenever you can.” Like the extraordinarily business-savvy old man he was, the count smiled and helped cover up my faux pas. Before I could take the out he gave me and leave, though, he suddenly spoke up. “By the way, I saw that you accomplished something quite extraordinary recently. Breaking into the black market to free those 397 slaves.”
“What you did for those people sent a surge of passion rushing through my old veins for the first time in a long while. Which is why I thought it would be prudent for me to offer my aid as well...”
Ah, I was wondering what he was getting at.

In the end, this was all a polite-sounding way of trying to get his hands on a slice of the pie. I went to refuse him, but what he said next immediately changed my mind. “There are nearly four hundred of them, and they still don’t have a proper place to live, correct?”
“...Right.”
“If you would allow me to do so, I would like to help them. Though they are exempt from taxes for the time being, they should still have a proper residence as they start anew.”
I found myself genuinely surprised at the offer, astounded that he was willing to provide housing for nearly four hundred people.
Well, I guess House Alminus isn’t considered the richest in the kingdom for nothing.

“Of course,” I readily accepted. “This world could use more heroes. Why would I ever refuse?” Even if he didn’t have the purest of intentions, that didn’t change the fact that this would be a great help to the slaves who had been freed.
“Not to worry. I’ll make sure not to steal your spotlight.”
With our conversation over, I left the count’s house. The following morning, there was an article on the front page of the newspaper that took up the entire page.
Count Alminus has pledged to donate two billion stones to the cause. When asked why, he said that it was simply to help an old friend—
Accompanying the article was the picture we took yesterday.
“Hah, he must be enjoying the fame.”

Just as I was setting down the newspaper, feeling strangely dirty, Shavin, the head of our administrative team, burst into my tent. “It’s been ages since the labyrinth closed, yet you decide to come here only now?” she scolded, frazzled.
“Y-Yeah...?”
“Take these documents first. From now on, don’t even think about stepping out of this tent until you’ve looked through and approved all of them!”
Shavin had grown a lot harsher than I remembered. However, that was probably thanks to the stress that came with overworking.

I smiled and made the conscious choice to overlook it. “All right. I’ll look through them, so don’t get upset, okay? But anyway, why are there so many of these? I delegated most of my power to you already.”

“...These are all things I can’t make decisions on with the power you’ve given me. Since our debt keeps growing larger, we’ve been forced to budget on a month-by-month basis. Except, I don’t have the power to set the budget, and since you weren’t showing up, all we could do was sign off on things provisionally and unofficially manage the ledger. What should have been a simple process needed to be divided into two or three parts, just because you weren’t here to sign off on it!”
“Oh. Really...?”
How can I get out of this?
Shavin glowered at me the moment the thought popped into my head. It was like she could read my mind. “Don’t even think about trying to run away right now.”
“...Can’t you just do it for me?”

“Ha! Well, there’s nothing I can’t do, huh! How about I just create the entire budget for the tribe? While I’m at it, I’ll go ahead and decide the cost of land without your approval and set my own salary too!” she shouted, her voice straining in a way that told me she was on the verge of snapping.
Still, I didn’t really understand why she was acting like this. She said so herself that she could do all that, so what was the issue? “Then why don’t you?”
“...What?”

“Shavin, I trust you. I don’t know about anyone else, but I have full faith in your decisions. And if you make a mistake, I won’t blame you—I’ll take full responsibility. The reason I gave you this position is because I trust you to do the job better than anyone else. And because I’m the chieftain, I have the power to do that.”
Shavin was speechless.

“So try trusting in yourself as well. No matter what anyone says, I know you’re the best at this sort of thing. I’m an expert when it comes to the labyrinth, and your calling is administration. No one will make better decisions when it comes to these things than you, including me.”
All right, judging from her expression, I’ve nearly won her over. Now it was time to land the final blow.
“So you don’t have to wait for my signature. I trust that you can take care of things on your own. And the same goes for your salary. You’re free to take as much as you feel is right.”
“...But surely it’s dangerous for you to give me a blank check?”
“I don’t think so. If that’s what you say you’re worth, then I won’t disagree.”

Shavin just stared at me without a word, until finally, she broke her silence to say, “...For years, I always thought to myself, ‘I wouldn’t do that if I was in their position. I would have done a better job.’ I always had those thoughts, but at the end of the day, I guess that was because I didn’t know how scary it was to take up such an important position myself.”
“Everyone is afraid at first.”

At my words of encouragement, she clenched her fists, apparently coming to a decision. “...I’ll give it a try. If I don’t at least try after hearing all that, then what’s the point? What excuse could I possibly have? I’m not the type to back down.”
“All right. I’m sure you’ll do a great job.”
After successfully executing my emergency escape, I ran out of the tent without looking back. My stroll had me cross paths with Ainar, so I took the opportunity to give her a new mission.
“You want me to gather all the warriors in the holy land?”
“Yes. I have something to tell them.”
I did feel sorry for the administrative team who was working around the clock, but the real reason I came here today wasn’t for them. Instead, it was time to put on a little show.
“Okay, I’ll gather them, but it’ll probably be a lot of people.”
“A lot?”
“Didn’t you know? These days, all the warriors are staying in the holy land to focus on building their houses.”
“But we should only have just made our third round of sales. There shouldn’t be that many warriors building houses.”
“Well, you can’t build a house by yourself, can you? Everyone’s working together. They are calling on their friends, and friends of friends, to help.”
Ah, so that’s what’s going on.
“Either way, bring them all here! Make sure to tell them that we’re going to have some fun!”
“You’ll see what I mean in a bit.”
“Wahoo! You’re planning something again! I don’t know what it is, but let’s get to it! I’m gonna go all out!” Ainar sped off, full of excitement, to gather the warriors.

I moved to the meeting place to wait. As time passed, the warriors began to trickle in one by one. It was strange seeing them walk around with hammers and nails in their hands instead of weapons, like big, buff carpenters.
“Chieftain!”
“Ohhh! It’s the great warrior whose name was written on the Stone of Honor!”
The warriors let out shouts of excitement as they arrived. I was honestly worried they would be angry that I called them here and interrupted them in the middle of their work.
“I heard we are going to have fun!”
“What’s the fun thing I heard about?!”
“Let’s get to it!”
The boring, menial work of building a house must have been draining them.
“Wait! I’ll tell you all when everyone has gathered!”
After about an hour, the entire forest was filled with barbarians. Similar to the festival from a few months ago, all of the warriors began to chant with a fiery passion.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
At some point, they even began to beat on their chests like they were drums.
“Bjorn.”
“When we’re in the holy land, call me Chieftain.”
“...Chieftain, I’ve gathered everyone.”
“I see.” Then it was time to begin.

There was no need to give these excited warriors a lengthy speech. “Everyone! Follow! Meeeeee!” I simply yelled out orders without even telling them where we were headed. However, as soon as I began to walk, the warriors automatically began to follow. By the time we hit the dirt road, I had a proper procession behind me.
“Woohoo!”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“Let’s go!”
It was a 100-percent-barbarian parade.
When we arrived at the city gates, the warriors standing guard immediately opened it without question or suspicion.
Clang, clang.

The gate began to open with a mechanical clunk, and just like on the first day I woke up in this body, a familiar grayish city appeared beyond its maw. And in the distance, tucked between its well-maintained roads and stone buildings, a tall spire speared the sky.
“Let’s go!”

As we marched toward our destination, the passersby on the streets began to dive for the sidewalks like we were a runaway wagon. At first, I figured we were a nuisance to them, but my expectations turned out to be wrong.
“Wow! It’s Baron Yandel! You are Baron Yandel, right?”
“I-It is him...!”
“Woohoo, wow!”
Surprisingly, the response of the onlookers wasn’t negative, but instead positive enough that even more citizens began to flock over to us to witness the pop-up parade.
Thud!

Windows opened as the city’s residents stuck their heads out of their homes to watch as we stomped through the streets. The sight of us passing by left them all with the same questions on their minds.
“But... where are they going?”
“I know, right...?”
“Shouldn’t we call someone? Is it really okay for such a large group of them to just march down the streets like that...?”
It didn’t take long before members of the Public Peace Agency were urgently dispatched to confront us. “I-It’s an honor to meet you, Baron Yandel.”
“Is there a reason you’re stopping me?”
“I-It’s because... we received... a report and...”
“Are you thinking of arresting me? Even though we’re just walking down the street?”
“N-No! Of course not! We would never do such a thing!”
“Good. Then get out of the way.”
At my command, the captain of the bunch scrambled out of our way, looking mystified.
“Behel—aaah!” I let out a mighty yell as we continued our march to the center of the district.

It didn’t take long before the knights finally appeared. “I-It’s an honor to meet you, Baron Yandel.” They were a group of knights from Mozlan, which was notorious for its authoritative approach to law enforcement. However, I didn’t have to worry about that anymore. “Pardon us, but may we ask where you are headed?”
“Why should I answer that?”
“We weren’t informed that there’d be an event like this today. Nor was any other organization, which is why we are simply... asking for confirmation.”
I had no reason to give them an honest explanation. “I’m just taking a walk, so don’t mind us.”

“...A walk?” The captain of the knights looked flummoxed. If I were an ordinary person, he definitely would have interrogated me more until I squealed. Or maybe even arrested me for disorderly conduct and refusing to cooperate with law enforcement.
“I told you we are just taking a walk. Are you doubting me?”
But I was now a baron of this kingdom.
“Of course not. We were just concerned after hearing that a group of a thousand barbarian warriors had gathered in the streets. I would ask that you kindly consider the position we’re in as well.”
“We aren’t going to leave Ravigion. Does that answer your question?”
Upon hearing that I had no intention of heading to the business district of Kommelby or the royal capital, the knights nodded with sighs of relief. “Then... do you mind if we follow you?”
“Well, I have no reason to stop you from walking down the streets too.”
“Thank you...”
In the end, the knights of Mozlan realized they couldn’t stop me and instead agreed to tag along.
“The barbarians!”
“The barbarians are here!”

As we continued our march through the streets, news began to spread across the city, and its residents were abuzz with excitement. People began to wait along the streets to watch us go by like we were a parade. We must have made quite the unusual sight.
“The Magic Tower...! The barbarians are headed for the Magic Tower!”
Eventually, they began to notice the direction we were headed. And the barbarians following behind me started to grow even more excited as their comments reached their ears.
“The Magic Tower? We’re headed to the Magic Tower?!”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, the Great Warrior!”
“The chieftain is leading us into sacred battle!”
“It’s time to feast on the flesh of the wizards!”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
Like a massive army making its way toward the battlefield, the roars of the warriors could be heard from miles away. And the citizens who heard them promptly went into a panic.
“H-Have they l-lost their minds...?!”
“Are they really trying to fight the Magic Tower?”
“What? But why?”
“Their hearts! It’s because of the barbarian hearts! The wizards are using them as magical ingredients!”
“...I don’t know what’s going to happen, but I have a feeling we’re all about to witness something incredible.”
No matter what the people around us said, we continued to march forward.
Stomp.

Eventually, I came to a stop as we reached our destination. Countless spectators had gathered in the square in front of the towering black spire, including hundreds of wizards who had come to meet us, apparently having heard the news of our march. As we came face to face, a wave of silence rippled over the square and the thousands of people packed inside. It was so quiet that I could hear someone nearby gulp at the tension. Then an old wizard stepped forward to serve as the representative of the Magic Tower.

“I am the Chief Wizard of the Lengman School, Wilbeth Gwollen.” The Chief Wizard was similar in rank to a long-term disciple of a martial arts master. In other words, since the master of the Lengman School was the head of the Magic Tower, this old man was its second-in-command. “How about you introduce yourself as well?”
Even though he already knew who I was, he still asked anyway. Maybe it was because he was a wizard, but this guy really seemed to like formalities.

“An introduction...” I grinned. The Giant, Head of the Anabada Clan, Chieftain of the Barbarians, Baron of Rafdonia—there was no need for me to list any of the titles that I’d earned. “Bjorn, son of Yandel.”

The old wizard took a deep breath at my brief introduction, then nodded his head. “I see. Well, it is an honor to meet the hero I had only heard tales of. But what brings you here to the Magic Tower?”
“I’m here to do what I should have done long ago.”
“Something you should have done long ago... Although I’m rather old myself, I’m not sure what you are referring to.”

“Really? Then I guess I’ll have to tell you.” With that, I raised my voice in a shout so that all the citizens gathered in the square, including the elderly and hard of hearing, could hear me. “I am Bjorn, son of Yandel! And I am demanding that the Magic Tower stop using our hearts as magical ingredients!”

“Is this really... all because of that...?” the old man murmured, rubbing the knot between his brows with a heavy sigh. “This is a legitimate area of research,” he said calmly, trying to appeal to me with logic. “You may be a baron of this kingdom and the chieftain of the barbarians, but that doesn’t give you the authority to halt research that’s being conducted for the betterment of society. If you still disagree, then I ask that you formally submit a complaint to the royal family and—”
“Too long!”
“...Pardon?”
“Don’t talk so long, old man.”

Did calling him an old man offend him? “Since it seems the baron doesn’t understand me when I ‘talk too long,’ I’ll keep it short.” His whole ‘patient and benevolent old man’ act fell away as he looked me dead in the eyes, his expression crumpling into a glare. Utterly unsympathetic to our plight, he spat, “We refuse.”
The disrespectful sneer never left his face. It was childish conduct unbefitting a man his age.
“So,” asked the old wizard, “what will you do now?”
After a brief moment, I lifted my chin and gave him my answer. “War.”
That one word was more than enough.
“It’s waaar!”
“Everyone grab your weapons!”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
I’d say we’ve played nice long enough, wouldn’t you?

chapters.title: Chapter 495: Declaration of War (6)
paragraphs: After over ten years of suffering, the barbarians had declared war.

Everyone—the wizards, the citizens who filled the square, and the knights of Mozlan—went wide-eyed at my declaration, their jaws dropping to the floor. Each one of them wore identical, dumbfounded expressions like they couldn’t believe their ears.
The old wizard, who looked equally as gobsmacked, barely managed to regain his composure. “...That word is far too heavy to throw around jokingly.”
Jokingly... Well, denial is a natural reaction to shocking news.
I didn’t even bother responding to him, instead standing there silently. Even the barbarians behind me needed some time to process as well—specifically about three seconds.
The moment a warrior near the back shouted, a powerful roar rippled through the rest of the barbarians.
“It’s waaar!”
“Everyone grab your weapons!”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

As more than a thousand barbarian warriors let out war cries, the wizards guarding the tower began to visibly panic, and I was not ignorant as to why. It’d be absurd to compare a barbarian’s physical strength to the sheer combat power of a wizard and their magic, but...
Visual marketing was a beast of its own.
“Raaah!”
“Wooh! Wooh! Wooh!”
It would be stranger if they weren’t scared of the sight of a bunch of massive, muscular barbarians causing a commotion and threatening to charge them at any given moment.
“Old man.” I took a big step forward, toward the hundred-strong group of wizards. “Do you still think I was joking?”
He just blinked at me, his expression shuttered and blank.
He was only human, after all.
Step.
When I took one more large step forward, the knights of Mozlan came running. “B-Baron Yandel! You can’t do this!”
So they finally remembered what their jobs were after getting caught up in the excited fervor radiating off of the barbarian warriors.
“H-How could you declare a war?! F-For now, how about we try to talk this through? For the sake of the royal family—!”

Despite how flustered he clearly was, the captain’s choice of words worked out for me. If he had used the royal family’s name to straight-up threaten us into not causing trouble, I would have lost a lot of ground.
“Talk...”
“Yes! I’m sure we can reach an agreement if we talk this through! After all, both the Magic Tower and barbarians are pillars that help protect this city, right...?”
At the knight’s plea to delay any acts of warfare, I pretended to consider his suggestion and then nodded my head. “Okay!”
“R-Really?!”
Yeah, I think that was enough for a show of force.

I didn’t have any intention of fighting the Magic Tower like this in the first place. Garnering the attention of everyone in the city was enough. After all, if we were to fight them right now, we’d look like the villains.

“Lewin Pastolm of the Egatil School!” So, after agreeing to diplomatic negotiations, I began calling out names one by one. “Lurendel Lungonerde of the Hulbunt School! Odwick Berthev of the Ulters School! Elenel Dwaynaine of the Galatir School!” Each name was of a wizard associated with the Magic Tower. The citizens hung on my every word, clearly wondering what was happening. “Toles Elin from the Ebound School! Ukla Tragic from the Ornstalt School!”
I continued until I’d rattled off the names of twenty-one people. Then, when I finished, I asked the old wizard, “Old man, do you know who these people are?”
“Of course. Most of them are great young wizards that will lead the next generation.”
“No, you’re wrong,” I asserted, shaking my head. “These people are wizards who made illegal commissions for the hearts of barbarians through the black market!”
In any war, what mattered most was the cause you were fighting for.
“I see! So that’s why the barbarians stormed the Magic Tower!”
“I heard he rescued some slaves from the black market. That must have been when he got that information!”

The bystanders finally began to nod their heads in agreement, now understanding why we had come all the way here. Most of them agreed that we were in the right and that they would have done the same in our position.
But I wouldn’t have gone this far if I was just going to stop there.
An appetizer was only an appetizer, after all. It could never be the main course.
“Lurendel Garlinbarret, Master of the Tritten School,” I announced one final name, my eyes never once leaving the old wizard’s. “Do you know who that is?”
She didn’t answer, much like someone whose lawyer had advised them to remain silent. Well, that wouldn’t stop the truth from coming out.
“She is another traitor who made a commission through the black market. But she’s no different from the rest. She asked for my heart.”

I dropped that bombshell without a moment’s hesitation. Putting in a request for the heart of a particular person was a completely different beast than simply trying to buy any old barbarian’s heart. It was tantamount to hiring an assassin.
“...Sir Gwollen, if this is true, not only will this woman be hanged, but the Magic Tower will also be held responsible for her actions.”

The Knights, who had been trying to stop me this entire time, suddenly changed their tune and began to question the old man. These were knights who worked for Mozlan, and Mozlan was a group that was made to protect the aristocracy, not wizards.

“...We do not know anything for sure yet. But I swear to you that the Magic Tower will investigate and that if this is true, we shall prosecute those involved to the fullest extent of our strict regulations.”

The old wizard tried to weasel his way out of this mess by making a vague promise that acknowledged the seriousness of the matter while also making it clear that he felt Mozlan didn’t have the authority to get involved.

I, of course, didn’t have to worry about any of that. “The Magic Tower is already under suspicion of working with those black market traitors. Even if you did your own investigation, we wouldn’t be able to trust it.”
“...But the reverse is true in that these accusations are entirely derived from your testimony, Your Lordship. That is not how we run things here. It’s not like there’s any evidence, now, is there?”
“Evidence...”
Yeah, I expected him to say something like that.
It was time to whip out the biggest trump card I could play as a barbarian.
“I swear as the chieftain of the barbarians, a baron of Rafdonia, and on my name of Bjorn, son of Yandel, that everything I have said here today is the truth!”
It was an empty oath, but it was more than enough to convince the crowd.
“He must be quite confident to make a declaration like that in front of all these people.”
“Just listen to all that. There’s no way the baron could be lying.”
“Dirty wizards! How dare they try to hurt Baron Yandel!”
“Bring out the criminals and punish them!”

My past heroic achievements gave more weight to my name, and this effect was only bolstered further by the favorable impression the city had of me. Most important of all, however, was that my actions today were backed by a just cause. That was more than enough to sway public opinion in my favor.
“Sir Gwollen, given the nature of the baron’s accusations, you are going to have to answer to us as well.”
“Didn’t I already tell you? We will be conducting our own investigation.”
“That is your choice to make, but are you sure that is how you want to go about this? If you just summon the relevant parties now, we can end this without further escalation.”
The old wizard didn’t dignify that with a response.

“My guess is that come evening, the higher-ups will approve an investigation by us, Mozlan, into the wizards of the Magic Tower. As you know, conspiracy to assassinate a noble is a serious charge. Is that what you really want?”

Once Mozlan had the green light, the Magic Tower would be thoroughly investigated and rendered unable to cover up whatever skeletons might be found in the process. There was surely more illicit activity lurking in the dark corners of that tower.
However, the old wizard flat-out rejected the offer. “I thank you for your consideration, but you needn’t worry. We will take care of this issue on our own.”
“You’re treading a dangerous path. All you have to do is call them out here so we can question them. Wouldn’t that be much easier?”
Despite the knight’s convincing argument, the old wizard exercised his right to remain silent. That alone was enough to seal the opinion of the public. Sometimes, silence was answer enough.
“Those dirty wizards! I knew it!”
“How dare you try and cover for people who tried to harm the baron?!”

Now, public opinion was firmly in our favor. The Magic Tower was inherently evil and the barbarians’ rage was justified. If that old man had simply ordered the wizards I mentioned earlier to step forward and submit to questioning, things would have never gotten to this point.
Still, if nothing’s done today, then they’ll simply bribe their way out of this mess or cover their tracks one way or another.
Thanks to the old wizard’s pigheadedness, however, I was able to take things a step further.

“Listen to the upstanding citizens of this city who believe in equal opportunity and the pursuit of justice!” The crowd, who had been heckling and cursing the Magic Tower’s wizards, suddenly went quiet as I spoke. It was time to use their discontent to my utmost advantage. “The wizards of the Magic Tower, who have fallen from grace, have no intention of admitting their sins! They’re desperate to protect their own! The wizards I named need only be called out from their labs and checked to see if they are truly innocent! But since they refuse such an easy request, that’s proof that they have done wrong! Isn’t that right?!”
“That’s right!”

I pushed the idea that we were on the side of justice once more. “They will probably destroy the evidence as soon as we leave or brazenly fabricate the results of their investigation. We’ve seen it happen countless times before, haven’t we?”
“That’s right!”
I continued to stoke the anger that had been smoldering deep in the hearts of this city’s citizens. “However, I no longer intend to sit helplessly on the sidelines as these criminals walk free.”
All I need to do is show them that I’ll take up the torch and carry the flames of pent-up anger that they’ve kept burning inside them for years with me.
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
I once again swore on my name.
“I promise you this. This city’s justice, the justice established by the royal laws of the mighty Rafdonia, will be set right again today!”
The second the oath left my lips, the citizens burst into a fervent roar.
“Woooooo!”
The stage is perfectly set. Since the civilians are in our camp now, the wizards won’t be able to attack us. All right, since everyone’s in their places, it’s time...
I let out a heavy exhale, took a deep breath, and then released an all-mighty roar. “Ready your weapooons!”

Ever since the war with the elves, the barbarians had kept their heads down and endured whatever treatment people saw fit to give them. It was time to once again remind this city exactly who the barbarian race was.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
We were a race that didn’t bother with small talk.

Alex Halo, the deputy archivist of the Third Magic Corps, had just finished up his regular report for the day and was about to leave the office. However, before he left, he snuck a glance at his boss. Even though she was swamped with work, her uniform was neatly ironed. Her blue eyes, though full of fatigue, were still whip-sharp. In her delicate hand, she held a pen.
“What are you doing? Are you not leaving?”
At his boss’s sudden question, he flinched, then quickly fumbled for an excuse. “I-It’s just that, it seems like you’ve been reading the newspaper a lot lately.”

“Oh, these?” Several newspapers from various outlets were piled up on her desk. When he pointed it out, she avoided eye contact and spoke in a soft, almost embarrassed tone. “It’s just... a hobby. It’s frustrating being trapped in here all the time, right? It’s important to know what’s going on out there in the world.”

“...I see.” The newspapers on his superior’s desk may have come from different sources, but each one covered the exact same story featuring the same protagonist. “Everyone’s been talking about it these days. The fact that Baron Yandel’s name has been etched into the Stone of Honor.”
“So they say. Back when we first met, he was nothing but a joke. But now he has really become a ‘great warrior.’”
Alex tilted his head in response to the hint of longing in her voice. “Aren’t you happy, though? Wasn’t Baron Yandel a former comrade of yours?”
“Former comrade...”
“Ah—”

Belatedly realizing his mistake, Alex quickly shut his mouth. The sight of her dejectedly looking down at the newspaper left him with a strange feeling of discomfort. He was just Subordinate A, a guy who couldn’t even do his job right. Someone who should never have been capable of putting that sort of expression on her face.
