His superior looked out the window with a faraway look in her eyes, silent and still. Alex stared at her blankly, unsure what to say.

“D-Deputy Commander! We’ve received an emergency deployment order...!” Just then, the office door swung open and someone ran inside. His superior immediately got a hold of herself and grabbed her coat, and he quickly followed her lead and pulled himself together as well. The Third Magic Corps wasn’t like the Public Peace Agency or Mozlan. They were a military group that operated under the direct control of the royal family. For them to be receiving an emergency deployment order meant that something bigger than a riot was taking place in the city.

“Fill me in.” His superior listened to the briefing as they made their way outside, asking the messenger clarifying questions. After hearing the full story, Alex personally felt the situation could be summed up in one sentence:
Baron Yandel was leading the barbarians toward the Magic Tower.
“They haven’t gotten there yet, but given their trajectory, it’s clear that they are heading in that direction.”
“Why? There must be a reason he’s doing this.”
“We are looking into it. However, more than a thousand barbarians are heading over there now. It seems that the Public Peace Agency has also requested the support of the military.”
“I see...”
Less than a minute after the emergency orders were given, all the soldiers had already gathered on the grounds and were making their way to the carriages.

“Is the situation really that dire, Deputy Commander?” Alex asked, staring out at the sea of people. “It looks like our corps wasn’t the only one that was ordered to go.” Numerous military carriages were pulling onto the road leading to the military base.
However, his superior didn’t respond. She simply bit her nails with an unusually anxious look in her eyes. “That guy... What is he going to end up doing this time...?”

He optimistically tried to reassure her. Baron Yandel was a smart man, and since he was a public figure with a lot to lose, he was probably only headed to the Magic Tower as a show of force. There wasn’t much to worry about.
These weren’t just words of consolation, but what he truthfully felt from the bottom of his heart. But the nervous look on his boss’s face didn’t disappear.
“...Alex. I think you’ve misunderstood. It’s not Baron Yandel that I’m worried about right now.”

“What...? B-But he’s going up against the Magic Tower.” Alex couldn’t follow her line of thought at all. The two of them were both from the Magic Tower, so they knew just how powerful the wizards there were. So why was she so concerned about them?
As he was trying to figure it out, his boss offered some insight into her logic. “Do you remember what happened at the Adventurers’ Guild because of him?”
“Are you talking about the false accusations against him...?”
“Yes. There was a massive prison break that day, and an entire branch of the guild was destroyed. The district chief faced backlash and lost the next election.”
“Still... the guild and the Magic Tower are two different things.” Compared to the Magic Tower, the guild was like a mom-and-pop shop.
“I... I was thinking the same thing... The guild and the Magic Tower are definitely different. The Magic Tower would never be swayed by a single barbarian...”
“But... you think that’s not the case anymore?”

Raven nodded without hesitation. “Yes. Now, he’s not just any barbarian. Back then when he completely flipped the guild on its head, he was a barbarian that had only just come of age two months prior. But what about now?”
Alex couldn’t say anything to that. How many years had passed since that day? Now, Bjorn Yandel was a baron of the kingdom and the chieftain of the barbarians.
“More than anything else, though... What worries me is the fact that I know him.”
He tilted his head in question.
“Trust me, Alex. No matter how reckless he seems, if he’s doing this, then I can guarantee he’s thought it through.”
Alex still didn’t really get what she meant, of course. However, he kept that thought to himself, as he didn’t want to be rude and tell his boss she was wrong.
Thunk, thunk.
The carriage continued down the road at a breakneck pace before arriving at the military teleportation platform.
Crackle!
At that moment, new information came in through a message stone.
“They’ve arrived. Baron Yandel and the barbarian warriors have reached the Magic Tower! Please hurry and send support!”
Despite the urgent message and the slightly nauseous look on her face, his superior simply took a deep breath, looking like someone who had already braced herself for what was to come.

chapters.title: Chapter 496: Quest (1)
paragraphs: Marco Toweo got his first-ever job working in the kitchens as a teenager. That experience sparked his interest in cooking, and he spent the years honing his talents until, two years ago at thirty years of age, he finally opened a small shop under his name on Ravigion Boulevard. He was also the husband of a beautiful wife and the father of two kids, and though he still felt like a kid on the inside, he did his best to take on the mantle of breadwinner without complaint. Whenever he felt wronged, he held it in, and if he could hold it in no longer, he would go somewhere far from others to let out his pent-up frustrations alone, and then head back home as his usual self.
But today...
“Ahhhhhh!”
By the time he came to his senses, he was already halfway up a flight of stairs with a shout tearing from his throat, surrounded by countless others.
“Today, we conquer the Magic Tower!”

Those words were what brought Marco Toweo crashing back down to reality. At that moment, he realized he was shoulder-to-shoulder with barbarian warriors, people he’d never imagined he would have cause to interact with within his lifetime. Not only that, but he was running straight toward a wizard who could easily stop them all with magic. He finally remembered where he was.
The Magic Tower...
He’d seen this place from afar all his life yet never once entered. How did this happen?
As he continued to climb the stairs, a wave of barbarians buoying him up from behind, the answer popped into his mind.
“Yandel! Bjorn Yandel is leading thousands of barbarian warriors to the Magic Tower!”

The famous hero, Bjorn, son of Yandel, had turned out to be just as incredible as all of the rumors said. Getting to see him in real life was exhilarating and electrifying. He seemed to radiate this unstoppable aura, his very presence warning off anyone who would get in his way from even trying.
“These people are wizards who made illegal commissions for the hearts of barbarians through the black market!”

The hero’s powerful declaration in the square sent Marco’s heart racing for the first time in a long time. Before he knew it, just like the rest of the crowd, he was also raising his voice and shouting at the Magic Tower. Yeah, thinking back, that was definitely when he joined in.
“A b-barrier...!”
“What do we do?”
“What do you mean?”
But how did he end up here? It wasn’t like someone like him would be of any help here in the first place.
“Just break through it!”
“Raaaaaah!”
Everything he did, he did to keep his family safe and happy, so why was he suddenly following these people up the stairs like he was a younger man with nothing to lose?
Slam! Slam! Slam!
A wall made of magic blocked their path. “Baron Yandel, stop! This is as far as you go!” an arrogant-looking wizard from beyond the translucent barrier yelled.
Slam!
Like he didn’t even hear him, Bjorn Yandel continued to swing his hammer. As he watched him up close, Marco finally realized something.
“Chieftain! You can’t break through magic like—”
“Haven’t I told you all before?
“...What?”
“If you can’t break through something, that just means you aren’t strong enough yet!”
The reason he ended up here was actually quite simple.
“But I am—we are—strong...!”
Because this man was strong.
Crack!
Strong enough that, no matter what stood in his path, he broke through it and pushed forward.
“Th-the barrier is cracking!”

And Marco wanted to see it. Even though today’s quest might just be one of many harrowing adventures this man conquered in his lifetime, and even if Marco couldn’t do much to help him on his journey...
Ba-dump!
He wanted to see it at least once.
Craaaaaash!
The Giant. Bjorn, son of Yandel.
He wanted to see what this man was made of.
The Magic Tower, home to this kingdom’s most valued subjects—its wizards—had never once been invaded despite its long history and was, thus, considered an impenetrable fortress.
I, however, disagreed with that.
‘Impenetrable’? They’re only saying that because no would-be invaders had ever had a reason to storm it.

The Tower was an organization entirely composed of wizards, meaning its party comp completely disregarded the delicate balance between damage dealers and tanks. Though the different types of magic making up its defenses were a pain in the ass to break through, it was nowhere near impenetrable.
What’s more, they don’t all seem to be on the same page.

Right now, justification and public opinion were on my side. Since the Magic Tower was composed of hundreds of different schools with their own interests, many of the wizards present didn’t even bother stepping forward to stop me even though I was technically leading an invasion.
“Don’t get in our way! We only want the criminals!”

Many of the schools that weren’t directly involved in this incident simply closed the doors to their labs, waiting for the storm to pass. Still, many wizards did step forward to stop us, since they couldn’t stand the idea of being humiliated by some uppity barbarians. However...
Your casting was interrupted, huh? Tough luck.

Most of the wizards of the Magic Tower were researchers, so they weren’t accustomed to battle. They instead spent day in and day out trapped in their labs, studying magic and magical theory. It would be ridiculous to expect them to perform on the same level as battle mages. Not only that, but they also had another major disadvantage stacked against them.
“...Master! L-Let’s just burn them all! B-Before they break through the barriers!”
“We can’t... Can’t you see?” Alongside the barbarian warriors storming into the Magic Tower was a group of civilians who had joined their cause.
“Master! They aren’t civilians. They’re just rioters!”
“We already received an official notice from the military. We are forbidden from harming any civilians.”
“But... we won’t last much longer if this continues! They’ve already gotten all the way up here!”
“...We just have to hold out a bit longer, until the military arrives. Then victory will be ours.”
Thanks to the civilians who joined us, the wizards were unable to use their greatest weapon—Area of Effect attacks. Instead, they could only cast defensive spells.
[You have cast Swing. The damage you deal with blunt weapons has increased significantly in proportion to your Muscle Strength.]
Thanks to that, we were able to make our way up the stairs one floor at a time while smashing through the barriers they shoved in our way.
“...Dirty savages! You will regret this!”
The wizards we captured were tied up with rope and made our prisoners.
“Bjorn! You go up! We’ll continue searching this floor!”
With each floor we climbed, a few warriors stayed behind to search for the wizards on our list.
“Ainar, don’t search through any of the schools that didn’t show up on the list until you’ve already checked everywhere else.”
“Huh? But those bastards might be hiding with another school!”
“Just do it last.”

There was a chance that we might search the entire tower and not find a single criminal on our list anyway. I also wanted to avoid making enemies of the other, innocent schools. What we had already achieved today would be enough to make these wizards quake in their boots every time they came across a barbarian for the rest of their lives.
But I have to make sure not to cross the line here. If I do, all of the schools within the Magic Tower may end up joining forces against us, which could end up being a major headache in the future.
“Remember, you can’t kill anyone. You can only capture them! Got it?”
That was why I continued to emphasize that whenever I could. If we slaughtered every wizard we encountered, we would be written off as violent trespassers without just cause.
Are we already on the thirtieth floor...?
As my march up the tower continued, I was met with even more barriers.

“It’s the baron! The baron is here...!” There was a gaggle of wizards gathered behind the translucent barrier, eyeing me nervously. “Baron! Turn around right now! Do you know how many laws you’ve broken?”
Again, they tried to persuade me and curse me out in the same breath. Unfortunately for them, I didn’t plan on stopping just yet, though.
Crack!

I bashed my hammer square into the barrier. After about ten uses of Swing, it slowly began to crack. However, I noticed that the higher I went, the stronger the barriers became. And that wasn’t the only bad news.
“Chieftain! The royal army! The royal army has arrived!”
Military backup had arrived. They’d shown up sooner than I expected them to.
They must have gotten orders to deploy the moment we stepped foot in the city... Damn it. This place is unnecessarily efficient when it comes to stuff like this.

“It’s over! Lay down your weapons and give up, warriors!” It seemed the wizards had also heard the news, because they brightened and started shouting at us again from beyond the barrier, looking much more confident. It made sense. Even if we tried to keep bulldozing through, the royal army was sure to stop us before we could conquer the entire tower.
Fine. That’s that, then.

Right on time, the barrier blocking the stairwell to the next floor was broken. The wizards who had been trying to maintain it with their mana scrambled upstairs in a panic, but the warriors were able to capture a few of them.
“Chieftain! What do we do?”
“We have to go higher, quickly!”

Now that the military was getting involved, the warriors were starting to get antsy. However, I stopped our attack on the next floor up and doled out new orders. “Bring me all the criminals we’ve captured so far.”
“O-Okay! We’ll bring them here!”

We’d done the best we could. From now on, it was up to chance. If we had been able to find at least one of the criminals on the list somewhere on the bottom thirty-one floors of the tower, then that would make things much easier for me from here on out. At the same time, however, things would get a lot harder if we didn’t.
I sighed.
So what was the outcome?

“Bjooorn!” It didn’t take long before Ainar appeared in the stairwell. Like someone showing off a successful hunt, she held up three wizards by the napes of their necks with one hand—Extelin Flacco from the Mailen School, Mohilo Ostquin of the Bebektalt School, and Kuol Memendrick of the Ulters School.

One of them was not one of the twenty-two wizards I had named in front of the crowd. Not that that was an issue. I hadn’t listed all of them back then. If I had said all their names, then I would have given them all time to escape to safety.
“Well done, Kharon, Ainar.”

I asked them if they ran into any trouble subduing them, but they said it wasn’t much of an issue. For some reason, these guys didn’t try to escape the tower and instead just hid within their own schools.
It’s a shame we couldn’t find the bastard who put in the request for my heart. But I can settle for this.
I’d get my hands on him eventually. In fact, everything we were doing now would help springboard us closer to that goal.
“Th-this is a misunderstanding, Your Lordship!”
“We’ll know soon enough if that’s true. What’s the situation downstairs, Ainar?”
“The warriors are blocking their way, but they won’t hold out long. When I was down there, the soldiers had already made it up to the fourth floor.”

“We’ll have to get started, then.” I activated the recording crystal ball I had on me then glanced around, catching the eye of a man standing nearby. He was a civilian who had followed us up to the thirty-first floor.
“What’s your name?”
“I-It’s Marco Toweo, Your L-Lordship!”

“Marco Toweo. I’ll remember that. Now, I have a favor to ask of you.” I handed him the crystal ball. “Can you stand over there and hold this? Make sure to hold it so it records both my face and theirs.”
“I-It would be an honor! B-But...can a regular person like me really be entrusted with such an important task...?” He trembled, clearly afraid of messing up.

I patted him on the shoulder with a smile on my face. “I trust you.” I did trust him much more than my fellow barbarians. How could I hand one of them a delicate device they’d never used before in their lives?
“Marco Toweo,” I repeated, taking a moment to commit his face and name to memory.
“...L-Leave it to me!”

Now that I had found my cameraman, it was time to hurry up and begin the interrogation. Although this place was bursting at the seams with wizards, there was no need to drag one here to cast a verification spell for us. I already had my own.
[You have activated No. 7234: Misplaced Trust.]
I’d been able to clear out quite a bit of my inventory recently, but this was an item I had lying around that I’d been wanting to use.
“Extelin Flacco, Mohilo Ostquin, Kuol Memendrick,” I said, looking down at the three wizards tied up in front of me. “Now, say it again. Has there been a misunderstanding here?”

When these guys were first arrested, they wouldn’t stop screaming and yelling about how they were being unfairly accused, but now, their mouths were glued shut. They knew it was impossible to lie when this item was active. Their silence was proof enough. However, for the sake of clear evidence, I needed a verbal response.
“You are being accused of treason.”
I tightened the leash, and they immediately started barking. “...T-Treason? That’s ridiculous!”
After all, it was difficult to hold your tongue when you were being accused of something that could result in the execution of your entire family.
“I-I never committed treason. I’ve never even thought of it. S-See how I’m answering you? Th-that means it’s the truth!”
The wizards quickly defended themselves, shooting sideways glances at the crystal ball recording them. It was obvious my mention of treason had spooked them.
“But your intentions were the same, no? Isn’t it true that you joined forces with traitors of the empire?”
“Joined forces with them—! I-I only made a request—”
Unfortunately, right when one of them was about to give me the answer I was looking for, things were cut short as someone rudely interrupted us.
“That’s enough, Baron Yandel.”
His grave voice reverberated through the entire floor. As he spoke, a magic circle appeared on the ground as if drawn by an invisible hand and began to emit a blue light.
Step, step.

I turned my head in the direction of the sound to see an old man walking down the stairs. It was my first time seeing him, but I recognized him at first glance. He was the Master of the Lengman School and the third brother of Duke Kealunus. In other words...
“Teshelan Lengman Kealunus.”
It was the Lord of the Magic Tower.

chapters.title: Chapter 497: Quest (2)
paragraphs: Some people in the world could cow others with just a glance and the force of their presence. Teshelan Lengman Kealunus seemed to be one of these people.
“L-Lord...!”

He was about 5′7″ with a typical wizard’s build and skin that had become rather wrinkly with age. To be honest, if it weren’t for that shoulder-high staff he was holding, I would think he was just an ordinary old man walking down the street.
Step.

However, as he slowly made his way down the stairs, not even the warriors could make a single peep. The look in his eyes was sharp despite his age. However, that wasn’t the true reason why the warriors were dead silent.
They too could instinctively sense it.
Although the areas of expertise wizards and warriors specialized in were vastly different, there was no doubt which of the two was stronger.
“Baron Bjorn Yandel.” When he finally reached the bottom step, he looked up at me and said, “You really are just like my older brother described. It’s a pleasure to meet you.”

His greeting caught me off guard. It was hard to believe that the lord of this tower would react to me, a barbarian, in such a polite way, especially after I broke into his workplace with thousands of warriors. One would think he’d lost his marbles.
Step.
As I took a large step forward, he took a step back. This confirmed a suspicion of mine.
He’s purposely staying out of range.

Right now, the lord of the Magic Tower was taking particular care to stay out of range of Misplaced Trust. However, I pretended I hadn’t noticed and grunted, “Well, I can’t say that I’m all that glad to see you here. I’m busy interrogating the criminals right now.”
While my tone was clearly hostile, he replied with a smile. “How about we set aside our emotions and have an honest conversation before all that?”
He sounded relaxed, like a man who knew he had the upper hand.
Honest conversation, my ass.
Did this old man not know anything? How could you ever expect a barbarian to understand someone who refused to say what he actually felt?
“I refuse! I told you, we are busy interrogating the criminals right now!”
“But surely you know that they won’t say a word now that I’ve arrived.”
That was true. The three wizards we had tied up all had a glimmer of hope in their eyes now that the old man was here.
If they weren’t going to talk, I was planning on using force. But since this old man is here, I guess that option is off the table...
“You can take your time deciding what to do. But at this rate, the royal army will soon arrive.”
I didn’t need much time. “All right. If there’s something you want to say, then say it.”
“First, will you send your people away?”
“Only the warriors. Marco will stay here.”
“Marco? Are you talking about that man over there?”

Marco, who was focused on filming everything, flinched when the lord of the Magic Tower glanced at him. It was only natural that he would get scared at the sight of such a powerful person looking his way.
“The royal family has a right to know everything that takes place here.”
“Hm, is that so?”
“Are you denying that?”
“Of course not. As a subject of this city, I wouldn’t dare interfere with the affairs of the royal family. But...” He slowly trailed off and glanced at Marco once more.
Crack!
“A-Ah!” The crystal ball in Marco’s hands broke, and he fell backward, startled.
“It seems your crystal has broken.”
So that was how he wanted to play things? “Huh. I bought it here at the Magic Tower too. I guess it was defective.”

“Magical devices are bound to occasionally malfunction, no matter how well-made they are. However, since you purchased it from us, I apologize on behalf of the Magic Tower. If you tell me the exact school you purchased it from, I will have them provide you with a new one.”
This old man was a real comedian.
“Ainar, take everyone downstairs. Including Marco.”
“Will you be okay...?”
I nodded at her and she quickly escorted everyone downstairs.

“As for you three, you should take a nap for the time being.” The three wizards sitting on the floor suddenly passed out all at once. The old man had used a basic sleeping spell on them. With that, only the two of us remained.
“All right, you’ve sent everyone away, now tell me,” I demanded, “what do you have to say?”

“I will be brief since there’s not much time.” He then took three steps forward, entering Misplaced Trust’s radius and looking directly at me as he said, “The Magic Tower will ban all research into or utilizing barbarian hearts from this day forward. That means that anyone who is caught researching them will be punished accordingly, just as they would for studying forbidden magics.”
“And?”
“As for those who went to the black market to buy them, they will also be punished.”
“What’s the punishment?”

“They will no longer be affiliated with the Magic Tower.” Simply put, they would be fired. “You may see that as a light punishment, but please understand our situation and know that we can’t punish them any further for such a crime.”

He was talking like he was worried I wouldn’t agree, but I was actually more than happy with his offer. I may have kicked up a fuss about execution and treason, but it would be impossible to prove a crime of that level had actually taken place.

“Of course, if anyone tries to buy a barbarian heart through the black market in the future, their punishment will be much worse,” he elaborated. “It will be no different than trying to obtain a banned item.”
All right, he even made sure to add a preventative clause for the future as well.
“And?”

“We will not submit any formal complaints about your unauthorized intrusion into the Magic Tower today. You broke inside to admonish us for our crimes, but after hearing your side of the story, we acknowledged our wrongdoings, and you eventually forgave us. That’s the story that will be known to the public.”

I was left speechless. Even though I knew he couldn’t lie within the radius of Misplaced Trust, I still couldn’t believe what he was saying. “...Are you serious?” This old man was willing to officially put it on record that the Magic Tower had been defeated by a bunch of barbarians.
“I am.”
Rather than feeling pleased, the only thing I felt was unease. Nothing in this world was ever free. “So what do you want in return?” I asked bluntly like the barbarian I was.

In turn, he responded with a name. “Master of the Tritten School, Lurendel Garlinbarret.” The same wizard that put in the request for my heart on the black market. “Please drop the charges you’ve made against her.”
I sighed. So this was all about her. I paused to collect my thoughts before asking him, “Is that woman really worth it?”
“She’s an incredible wizard. She was momentarily blinded by greed and ended up making a foolish decision, but I have no doubt that one day, her research will greatly benefit this world.”
I didn’t doubt him. Just from the way he was talking about her, it was clear that there was something special about this woman.
Lurendel Garlinbarret... It seems I might have caught a bigger fish than anticipated...
Whatever the case, I’d have to ask Amelia to look into her later.
“So, what do you think of my offer? I’m hoping to hear your answer now.”
“It’s good. I agree to it.”

With that, the negotiations came to an end. It was a shame to drop the charges against the woman who tried to have me killed, but all things considered, I’d still gotten more out of this than I’d initially hoped. There was no reason to be greedy.
For some reason, though, the old wizard still seemed uneasy. “Well then. I trust there are no hard feelings between us, right?”
He took the opportunity to gently question me, likely trying to take advantage of Misplaced Trust being active to get a sense of what I was thinking.
“What about you?” I countered. “Do you have hard feelings toward me?”

When I dodged the question and fired it back at him, he unexpectedly answered with a smile. “Of course I have no hard feelings toward you, Your Lordship. Nor did I have any to begin with. You are the chieftain of an entire race, so you’re only doing what you must, right?”
This was a very business-like mindset. His willingness to respond made it tough for me to refuse to answer him, as doing so would only make me look bad.
“So,” he probed, “may I hear how you feel?”
My honest feelings...

“I would be lying if I said I don’t have any hard feelings. Thousands of my kind died in the labyrinth because you wizards were greedy for their hearts. Of course I hate you. But!” I turned my wrist just slightly so that the compass on Misplaced Trust was hidden as I answered him. “Don’t worry. I promise that as long as you don’t come near us, we will not attack the Magic Tower again!”
This was a trick that only worked when I was the one using Misplaced Trust and the other person couldn’t see the needle.
“Plus, you ended up being a much better guy than I was expecting.”
Because when I lied, it stopped working.

Things were largely uneventful after that, and eventually, the royal army made their way to the floor we were waiting for them on. They were clearly shocked to see the wayward baron and the lord of the Magic Tower having a peaceful conversation. The lord looked their way as they arrived and immediately defended me, arguing that this whole mess was the wizards’ fault and that we barbarians were not to blame.
“So... Lord Kealunus, you’ve asked Baron Yandel for forgiveness, and he accepted it?”
“That’s right.”

The military commander stared at us in disbelief but didn’t pry any deeper than that. It didn’t matter to them what sort of deal we had ended up making. From the palace’s point of view, the fact that this incident hadn’t escalated into an even bigger issue was all that mattered.
“What are you doing? Get to work!”

The commander then ordered that all the barbarians and wizards being detained be set free while the lord of the Magic Tower summoned the thirty-six wizards who were suspected of using the black market and handed them over to Mozlan.
“But I’m afraid I don’t see the wizard who was aiming for your heart among these thirty-six, Baron Yandel?”
Using the black market was nothing but a misdemeanor, while the attempted assassination of a noble was a felony punishable by execution. However, it was easy enough to drop the charges against her.
“Oh, her? I thought about it some more, and I don’t know if I remembered her name right. There were so many names to remember, I got confused. I’ll tell you later if I ever remember who it was.”
“...I see.”
Master of the Tritten School, Lurendel Garlinbarret...
The commander seemed to notice that she was a part of whatever deal we made but simply left it at that. None of that actually mattered to them, after all.

“Thankfully, everything ended peacefully. Oh, but since you caused a disturbance in the city without royal permission with over a thousand warriors, you are unfortunately going to have to pay a fine. I hope you’re willing to be understanding of that,” he pled, begging me to pay the small fine and not cause any more trouble.

The commander and his men then began to escort the arrested wizards out of the Magic Tower, which told me it was about time for me to head home too. “Don’t worry, Your Lordship,” he said before he left. “If we find proof of wrongdoing, we will make sure they are punished appropriately.”
“All right, then I’m leaving. I’m hungry.”
With that, I started to walk back home. However, I didn’t get more than a few steps before Ainar appeared from where she had been waiting for me, and began dragging me back to the holy land herself.
Boom! Boom! Boom!

There was already a festival commemorating our victory against the Magic Tower in full swing by the time we got there. Even though we hadn’t planned the celebration, the warriors were happy enough just dancing, singing, and downing alcohol like it was water. The scale of it was bigger than any festival I had ever seen the barbarians throw. Even the barbarians scattered throughout the city came back to the holy land to celebrate.
“Bjorn!”
“Chieftain, you mean.”
“Chieftain! Say something! Everyone’s been waiting for you!”
As the festivities were reaching their climax, Ainar pushed me to give a celebratory speech. Of course, in good old barbarian fashion, I kept it short.
“We—”
“Wahoo!”
“—woooooon!”
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
My one-sentence speech was enough to whip up the already feverish crowd into an even bigger frenzy.
I can’t pass up this opportunity to advertise.
I ordered Kharon to have our moles talk up real estate to the other barbarians. They fanned out and brilliantly executed their duties, becoming perfect salespeople.
“Did you know? We can’t stop with just one victory! There’s something else we should do!”
“Now we barbarians will prosper even more. And the price of housing will rise even higher!”
“Everyone who doesn’t buy land now is a fool!”
“What? You’re going to spend your mana stones on a new weapon? What year is it? Why would you use it to buy a new weapon when you can buy land?!”
That’ll definitely help our real estate plan.
After enjoying the festival for a while longer, I snuck out of the holy land to return home. When I stepped inside, Amelia was waiting for me on the couch in the dark living room.
“Yandel.”
“Do you have some sort of disease? One that makes it impossible for you to have a single quiet day?”

Amelia seemed irritated for some reason. Maybe it was because I didn’t tell her my exact plan when I broke into the black market. Figuring that was the most likely explanation for her bad mood, I quickly jumped into an apology. “I’m sorry. I didn’t even discuss it with you beforehand and just went and did my own thing.”
Amelia’s expression softened, telling me I’d given the right answer. “...So you know.”
“Huh? You just smiled, right?”
“What are you talking about?”
“You smiled! I’m sure I saw it.”
“...Don’t insult me.”
What the hell did she mean by insult? When I plopped down on the sofa with a grin, Amelia cleared her throat, then asked, “So. Do you feel better?”
This woman can always read me like a book.
It was a strange feeling, but I gave her my honest answer. “Yeah. Very much so.”
Amelia nodded her head. “That’s good.”
After a moment of silence, we switched gears and filled each other in on our days. A while later, Erwen came downstairs too, rubbing the sleep out of her eyes as she joined us for a chat.
Then, the next morning...
“I-It’s me...Bjorn...”
The visitor that I’d been waiting for arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 498: Quest (3)
paragraphs: Despite the table of finely brewed tea and the handful of fancy appetizers that Auyen had prepared with the utmost hospitality, an awkward silence filled the room. Missha was the one to eventually break it.
“These snacks...”
“Hm?”
“These are snacks from Lubat’s Bakery... They’re not bad, but the ones from Nielon Bakery are cheaper and are probably more to your taste...”
Why was she talking about the snacks all of a sudden?

I thought this was very weird, but I figured that she must have just been trying to make small talk to ease some of the tension in the air. “Really? I don’t know much about stuff like that since Auyen takes care of it. Oh, right. You don’t know who—”
“No, I know. Auyen Rockrobe... He’s your navigator.”
“...Yeah?”
Once again, the conversation came to a screeching halt as the awkwardness came back with a vengeance.
Ugh, why am I so nervous?
If this was going to hurt anyway, I might as well just rip off the bandage. With that settled, I got straight to the main point. “Since you came here, you must have made up your mind, Missha?”
“...Yeah.”
“So what did you decide?” I asked bluntly.
Missha hesitated for a moment before replying, “Your new clan... I’ll join it.”
“Really?”
“Yeah...”

When she nodded, the tension finally melted from my shoulders. I was sure she was going to turn me down, given how she kept fidgeting and hesitating. I’d even prepared myself for rejection beforehand.
“As long as you... and your teammates are...”

I cut her off before she could even finish her sentence. “Of course everyone’s going to welcome you! Though, right, I forgot. You and Erwen didn’t part on good terms, huh? It’s fine. I’m sure you’ll be able to be close like you used to be. She’s doing a lot better now as well.”
“Oh... Is that so...?”
“Why don’t I call them down now?”
“You weren’t able to really chat with them last time. Since we’re all going to be heading into the labyrinth together now, we should all get along...”
Missha looked taken aback by my suggestion but eventually nodded her head in agreement. I left her and went upstairs to grab Amelia and Erwen.

However, once we were all gathered in the living room, the suffocating awkwardness raged on. After sitting in silence for an unbearable amount of time, Amelia let out a heavy sigh, and then glanced toward me.
We’ll just end up sitting here all night at this rate, so she must have decided to take the initiative.
“Yandel. Wait upstairs.”
“If you want us to get along, don’t talk back and get going. You’d only get in the way.”
I was kicked out from the get-go.

Amelia, Erwen, and Missha talked for about an hour. Eventually, Amelia came up to my room and knocked on my door, telling me it was okay to come down. I rushed back to the living room, but things there were completely different than I had expected.
They were neither getting along nor fighting. But the room was a mess, almost like a hurricane had just passed through.
“Um... Amelia?” I asked, dumbfounded. “What happened here?”
“After a long conversation, the three of us have decided to get along from now on,” Amelia replied like there was nothing amiss.
“Um, that’s great and all, but... that wasn’t what I meant. It looks like... some stuff is broken?”
“Oh, that? Don’t worry about it. While we were talking, my hand slipped.”
How could her hand slip so badly that she wrecked an entire living room?
When I glanced at the other two, Erwen quickly avoided my gaze. “...That’s right. Her hand slipped.”
So this was the excuse they were all going with? I then turned my gaze to Missha, but she kept her mouth shut without giving me a proper response.
Well, since nobody is hurt, I guess it’s fine...
I decided to stop interrogating them about the living room. I wasn’t that clueless.
They must have argued for a bit, but it looks like everything turned out all right.
Though if I had to be more exact, I would say that Missha and Erwen were probably still at odds, but Amelia had agreed to mediate between them.
“Then... I’ll head up first.” Erwen quickly fled to her room.
Missha also got up from her seat. “I w-will... go too, then...”
“Hm? Where are you going? Why don’t you just stay here? We have a lot of empty rooms.”
“W-Well... I’ve thought about it, but I think it would be better if I lived separately... Me being here would only make things awkward... I heard that Ainar was doing the same...?”
Ah, that’s true. Ainar told me things in the holy land are pretty interesting these days, so she prefers to spend her time there as First Elder.
“So... can you let me go?” I let go of Missha’s wrist, which I had grabbed. She gently cradled the part that I’d been touching like my grip had been too tight. “G-Goodbye, then...”
Missha quickly left through the front door. In the end, I was unable to overcome the distance between us.
“...The three of you. What did you talk about?”
I asked Amelia out of frustration, but once again, she didn’t give me a proper answer. “That’s a secret between us girls. There’s no need for you to know.”
There wasn’t even a single clue I could glean from that response to figure out what in the world those three had discussed.
The day after Missha’s visit, another guest showed up at our front door.
“...Raven?”
“Can I come in?”
“Yeah, of course.”
Ever since she ran tests on Erwen’s new essence, Raven had been busy with her job. It had been a while since her last visit.
“This house is smaller than your last one?”

“Oh, right. It’s your first time here.” I gave her a quick tour of the house as Auyen prepared refreshments for us. Then the two of us sat down to enjoy them as we talked. “I’m sure you didn’t come here just because you’re bored. What’s up?”
“‘What’s up?’ How can you ask me that after what you did?”
“So this is about the Magic Tower.”

She let out a heavy sigh but, surprisingly, didn’t give me too much of a hard time. She knew the context. Even though my way of handling it was a bit extreme, at the end of the day, I was just doing my job as chieftain of the barbarians. More importantly, everything ended peacefully. Which meant...
“What kind of magic did you use on him?”
This was the real reason she was here.
“I can’t understand why the lord of the Magic Tower would concede so much to you. To be honest, I thought for sure that this was going to lead to all-out war...”
“You came because you want to know how I convinced him?”
“...More or less.”
I hesitated for a moment but decided to tell her the full story, including the deal I made with the lord. Actually, I wanted her insight.
“Lurendel Garlinbarret...” she murmured. “He conceded all of that to protect her?”
“Do you know anything about her?”
“...Not really. In the past, we never had a reason to talk much since we were different ranks. And since joining the military, I barely visit the Magic Tower.”
“Still, you’re a wizard just like she is. I’m sure you know more about her than me. Any information you have will help.”

“Then...” Raven paused for a moment before admitting, “Lurendel Garlinbarret is the Magic Tower’s most prolific expert when it comes to researching barbarian hearts. In fact, the Tritten School itself is primarily focused on studying them.”
“Hm, so that’s why she wanted my heart.”
“Probably. There’s a good chance that she only made the request because she genuinely wanted to study your heart.”
“And that must mean there’s a good chance her research is something the Magic Tower is highly interested in.”
“It seems so... Otherwise, there’d be no reason for the lord of the Magic Tower to give up so much just to save her.”
“...Raven, could you look into it for me?”
“Hmmm... All right. I’m curious as well. I’ll do my own investigation and let you know if I find anything interesting.”
“Thanks.”

That was the end of that, but since Raven was already here, I decided to ask a question of my own. “Raven. Hypothetically, and I do mean this completely hypothetically... Has anyone ever gained... knowledge from the labyrinth?
“...Knowledge?”
“Yeah, knowledge. Like for example, someone suddenly gaining the ability to read and write in an ancient language even when they couldn’t before—”
Raven shot to her feet, her hands coming down on the table hard. “Ancient script? You can read it now?”
“N-No... I-I was just giving an example—”
“What do you mean, an example? You’re obviously talking about yourself!”
These women around me are all way too sharp.
I decided to fess up. She wouldn’t believe me if I said no, anyway. “Yeah, I can read in the ancient language now.”
“How much...?”
“I’m not sure? I haven’t tested it, so...”
Before I could finish my sentence, Raven once again jumped up and pulled out a book from her sub-space, forcing me to read what was, of course, a text written in Rafdonia’s ancient language.
“‘Mahniarsus earnestly begged for his wife’s return, but Kaprakadakh flatly refused his request. He believed that he could love her more than Mahniarsus ever could...’ What kind of book is this?”
“It doesn’t matter. Keep reading.”
“...‘So Mahniarsus drew his sword and stabbed it into his rival’s heart. As Kaprakadakh bled to death, he reached out his hand, but the only thing he could do was...’”
Raven’s expression grew more and more dejected as I continued to read the book to her. “Th-that’s a book even I can’t read properly without a dictionary...”
Hm, so that’s how it is...
Raven was even considered somewhat of an expert in ancient languages compared to most wizards.
“Muttin abiyur bukrath,” I replied.
“...What did you just say?”
“That means, ‘I can even speak in the ancient language.’”
When I shrugged my shoulders, she was left completely dumbfounded. It took a while before she could get a hold of herself enough to speak. “...Mr. Yandel, can I hit you?”
Raven raised her small fist, which didn’t look threatening at all, at me.
“Keeatho keekeehu kooekhu. Oh, that means, ‘I don’t want to get hit’ in—”
“Are you making fun of me?!”
In the end, I got punched. The only one who ended up with a bruise was the one who hit me, though.
“Ah, seriously... What’s wrong with you, Mr. Yandel?”
“Sorry. Anyway, back to my story, have you ever heard of a case like this before?”
“...As far as I know, no. Nothing like this has ever been recorded. But... what happened? Was it... a reward? Is it related to your name being written down on the Stone of Honor...?”
“Well, something like that.”
“...Can you tell me?” Raven asked hesitantly.

Despite her caution, I decided there was no need to keep this a secret from her. We may not have been as close now as we used to be back when we were teammates, but she’d still helped me out despite knowing that I was an evil spirit. Plus, I also needed a wizard’s insight.
“What you experienced there wasn’t just an illusion. No, it must have actually happened in the past! There is clearly some sort of connection between the Lord of the Floor and the Witch!”
Once I was done filling her in, Raven couldn’t hide her excitement.

“This is an incredible discovery! This substantiates the hypothesis that the labyrinth isn’t from another dimension! Maybe the labyrinth’s coordinates aren’t delineated by space, but rather, the axis of time!”
I, of course, didn’t understand a thing she was saying. Axis of space, time, whatever—none of it really made any sense to me. “Is that so?”
“Versyl Gowland! What did she say? She’s a wizard too, right? I’m sure she’s elbows deep in research after making such an unbelievable discovery!”
“No. She wasn’t all that interested in it, to be honest.”
“W-Whaaat?!”
That was because Versyl was also a player. Players like us didn’t have all that much interest in the history of this world. We pretty much just ignored it.
“N-No way... Even though she’s a wizard? If I were there—”
Raven, who had been shouting in apparent outrage, suddenly went quiet.
“If you were there?”
“...Never mind. It’s a pointless thought, anyway.”

The mood suddenly plummeted. For some reason, I felt like I had to change the subject, and fast. I hastily brought up some news that I was sure would make Raven happy. “Oh, that’s right! I have some other news to tell you.”
“...News?”
“Missha came back.”
I briefed her on our reunion with Missha and how she had decided to join our clan.
“...Is that so? That’s great.”
What’s with her reaction?
“I’ll tell you her address later, so you should visit her too. I’m sure Missha will be happy to—”
“Later.”
“I-I should get going now. I’ve got work to do.”
Raven then high-tailed it out of the house, a dark expression on her face.

Once Raven was gone, I started tackling my long to-do list for the day. First, I stopped by the holy land to see if Rotmiller was adjusting well. Then, I swung by the dwarf’s forge to check on his progress. I even summoned all the members of our clan to discuss our next quest too. Most of the days that followed were made up of similarly menial tasks, but they didn’t take up the entirety of my day.
Today, for example, I had something else to do.
“We are delighted to welcome you to the House of Viscount Goodrix.”
I visited Viscount Goodrix’s mansion after receiving a letter of invitation from him. He was one of the members of Melbeth, which was made up of thirty-one—No, thirty-two noble houses.
“Haha! It’s a pleasure to see you, Your Lordship. I am Viscount Goodrix. I’m sure you’re busy as it is, so I’m incredibly grateful that you took the time to accept my invitation.”

Since he was a dwarf, his tone was much more cheerful than most other nobles’. However, since he was still a noble, he spoke in the same roundabout way they all did, with no shortage of pleasantries. After I finally managed to convey to him that he could skip all of that, he finally got to the point.
“So,” I asked, “Why did you call me here?”
“On behalf of Melbeth, I have a request for you, Baron Yandel.”
I’d gotten my first Melbeth-exclusive quest.

chapters.title: Chapter 499: Quest (4)
paragraphs: Melbeth. An alliance made up of non-human noble houses.

Using my title as Baron Yandel, I was able to join them and acquire support for my Anabada Clan. In actuality, the clan itself didn’t receive much physical money from this deal. Instead, Melbeth simply provided a place for us to establish our clan house, and at a cheap rate. They also gave us the option of taking out loans through their shared fund in the future.
A request...
That was why this request was so critical. Even though he used the word “request,” it was more like a clause in our contract.
If I fulfill their request, they’ll be willing to treat me better. I’ll be that much more valuable to them.
In terms of the game, this was something like the Achievement system. By fulfilling a quest, you were able to rise in rank, and you gained new privileges accordingly.
Still, before blindly accepting their request, I first needed to check if it was even feasible.
“What is the request?”
Rather than asking about the reward, the details of the quest had to come first.
“Information.”
“...Information?”
What a complete curveball. Normally, a request was under one of three categories: hunting, gathering, or fighting. But they wanted information?
Viscount Goodrix sipped on his tea as he began, slow as ever, to fill me in. “So... as you know, something incredibly big has happened recently.”
“Don’t beat around the bush and be straight with me.”

The viscount, who was used to talking in a roundabout way like the noble he was, choked on his tea at my abrupt demand. He coughed to clear his throat. “Well, I’m talking about how your name was written on the Stone of Honor. As you know, it says that a hidden area of the labyrinth has been unlocked. And that likely refers to a new floor,” he said, finally getting to the point.
Well, he’s still not making the point all that clear, though.

Still, even though he wasn’t as direct as I would have liked, I knew what he was getting at. Since I was the one who had accomplished the feat in the first place, he wanted information directly from the source.

“Baron Yandel, aren’t you already planning to explore the new area next time? We would like you to share the results of your expedition with us. Whether it really is a new floor, where the entrance is, how to get in, what’s inside, and other such information.”
Hmmm...
As I mulled it over, he elaborated, “Ah, and like I said before, this is a request that has been formally recognized by Melbeth’s council. Upon completion, you will be paid accordingly.”
“What’s the reward?”

“It depends on the value and rarity of the knowledge you provide. After all, we don’t know anything about this new area yet. For all we know, the location of its entrance and how to get in might be something that any adventurer could find after a bit of searching, making it common knowledge. If that’s the case, there’s no reason to offer more than a common reward. On the other hand, if you can provide information nobody else knows, it becomes all the more priceless, and thirteen houses have already agreed to compensate you appropriately.”
“Thirteen?”

“Well, everyone has a different opinion on the value of this opportunity. But it’s already been decided that your reward will be paid through the shared funds of the thirteen houses that have opted in.”
In other words, the other houses had all deemed this request a waste.
“So that’s why you’re meeting with me as the representative of the thirteen instead of calling for a formal meeting with all the houses present.”

“That’s correct. Unfortunately, we were unable to gain the majority vote when the idea was first suggested. Ah, but there’s no need to worry. It has still been officially approved, and as such, shared funds will be set aside for the request, so there won’t be any issues with you receiving your reward.”
As he detailed the cumbersome process of securing funding, the downsides of working in politics became more and more apparent. Still, groups like this had their advantages.
“So... do you need time to consider?”
“Not so much time, but I would like to ask a few questions first.”
“Of course.”
“What are you planning to do with the information?”

Viscount Goodrix took a moment to think things over, then said, “Do you know what the most expensive rank-nine essence ever sold in history was? It was the Deep Salmon. It’s not even all that good compared to other rank-nine essences, yet it sold for 3.2 billion stones. Do you know why?”
It was my first time hearing this story, but I could easily guess.
“...Because it was the first of its kind.”
“Exactly. Because it was the first essence ever found in the ninth floor’s Rift, the Magic Tower paid as much as they could to get their hands on it. It was simply worth that much to them.”
Even so, when I asked him if they wanted my information so they could make money off of it, he shook his head, saying that wasn’t the case.

“Since ancient times, newly-opened areas of the labyrinth have always offered a wealth of both treasure and opportunities. Take, for example, Myulmarin, Slayer of Sea Dragons. Since he was the first to ever defeat the Sea Dragons, he gained incredible power and political influence. No one who has defeated the Sea Dragons since has received similar accolades for doing so.”
“So?”
“The information we receive from you will be given to other adventurers of each non-human race. Only those that can be fully trusted, of course.”
“You want to use my information to help make them stronger.”
“That’s right. The stronger non-human adventurers become, the stronger Melbeth will be as well.”
Although he kept talking in that long-winded, roundabout way, I now fully understood why Melbeth was making such a request of me. And their argument was convincing enough to sway me as well.

“Of course, I understand you might be displeased about sharing valuable adventuring knowledge that you worked so hard to acquire with us. Nevertheless, I promise that we will keep it confidential and only pass the information along to those we fully trust.”
With all the details laid out, he asked me once more if I would take on the request. My reply was instant. “All right. I accept.”
There’s not even a penalty for failing this quest. So there’s nothing to lose by accepting it, right?
“Then I’ll see you later.”

After leaving his house, I headed home and gathered my party members to share the news of our new quest. Some had concerns, but no one objected since we could always reevaluate later once we found the hidden area and scoped it out.
Tick, tock.
After discussing our plans until late into the night, I headed upstairs and laid down. Amelia and Erwen sat on two chairs by the bed, watching me.
“Tersia, you don’t have to be here as well.”
“I don’t want to leave. I’m going to stay here and protect Mister too.”
...Are they still not on good terms? We’ve been together for so long now. Why does nobody get along?
Tick, tock.
I closed my eyes and listened to the sound of the clock on the bedside table.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]
Half a month had already passed.
When I opened my eyes, I was back in Hansu Lee’s room. I headed over to the computer to turn it on and enter the forum.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 0 people are online.]
They’re not here yet...
I would just go in when the two of them showed up later. In the meantime, I checked the message board. As expected, people were already posting things.
[Did you all see the patch notes?]
I still can’t believe I’m using that term in this world. How the hell are there still hidden areas?
BurtusMaximus: Top reason why Dungeon and Stone is a god-tier game: over 10 years old, free, and still getting patched.
└these99: In return, it won’t let you go home.
└BurtusMaximus: Exactly. It really is a god-tier game. As in, dear god, please send me back home now.
Looks like this patch was even more shocking to the players than the natives of this world, I thought.
Even though there were also posts about what happened at the black market and Magic Tower, most people were talking about the new area of the labyrinth.
[But how come a new patch came out when Bjorn defeated the Lord of Terror?]
Did he do something wild like throw its dead body on a frying pan and eat it? Weird that there would suddenly be new DLC when all he did was beat it.
Futuralis: Because he did it in a team of 5.
└AI_DIDIGO: Fact 1: It wasn’t a team of 5, but rather 4.
└Futuralis: Then maybe the condition was defeating it in a group of 4?
└AI_DIDIGO: Fact 2: Bjorn Yandel wasn’t the first to clear it in a group of 4.
└Futuralis: So what’s the conclusion?
└AI_DIDIGO: Conclusion: There is a 92.24571% chance that Bjorn Yandel defeated the Lord of Terror after meeting a special condition.
└Writer: This guy’s whole schtick is hilarious.
└Nyacreeps: But it’s true though. Even the royal researchers think that Gabrielius’s Achievements activate when someone triggers a special condition.

The players talked with each other, throwing around multiple theories for why the labyrinth got a sudden update. I was hoping that something useful might come out of the discussion since everyone was working together to figure it out, but in the end, no one had any idea what the special condition I triggered could have possibly been.
Well... it doesn’t really matter at this point.
After looking through the forum, I scrolled back over to the chat room again.
[Long Live Korea’s Independence - 2 people are online.]
All right, both of them are in there.
I hurried into the room and when I entered, two heads turned in my direction.
“Big Bro! You’re here!” Baekho Lee ran over to me and bowed down in an exaggerated way.
Hyeonbyeol, meanwhile, simply glanced at me. “Oh, you’re here?”

When I walked past the two of them to sit on the sofa, Baekho quickly sat down next to me. “Big Bro! Did you know? Me and Hyeonbyeol were having a conversation before you came. And it turns out, she still has feelings for you!”
Baekho’s opener knocked the air right out of me.
I gulped, shooting a look at Hyeonbyeol, whose expression was stony. “...I never said that. You don’t believe him, right?”
“O-Of course not. Of course I don’t believe it.”
“Bro! Are you disappointed? I don’t know why Big Sis is acting so cold. When I asked her if she would ever date you again, she was blushing!”
Oh... So that’s what happened... What a relief.
I’d been seriously starting to wonder if I could ever look Hyeonbyeol in the eye again.
“...I wasn’t blushing. And even if I did, how was that the conclusion you came to?”
“Haha. Silence is practically a yes in itself.”
“Baekho Lee... you’re a piece of trash.” Hyeonbyeol ended the conversation right there, no longer falling for Baekho’s crap. She then glanced at me, a fierce look in her eyes.
“Hyeonbyeol, I got it. I never trusted this guy in the first place. And Baekho, stop fooling around.”
“All right!”
“He seriously pisses me off...”
Even as I smoothed things over, the annoyingly cheeky look on Baekho Lee’s face never faltered. Hyeonbyeol’s fists and jaw clenched at the sight of it.
When did the two of them become so close?

I was curious, but I didn’t bother asking. If I did, I worried that Hyeonbyeol would fly into another rage. Not to mention the fact that I could only meet with Baekho Lee here once a month for an hour, so I couldn’t waste any more time.
“Hyeonbyeol.”

I decided to send Hyeonbyeol away while I talked to him. When I called her name, she immediately cooled down, her brows unfurrowing. She already knew what I was going to ask her. Thanks to that, I didn’t need to say much.
“I have something to discuss with Baekho...”
“...I’ll be back in an hour.” Hyeonbyeol glared at Baekho one more time before leaving the chat room.
“Phew! She’s a funny lady, right? Even though she always acts so intimidating, whenever she’s with you she becomes so shy and quiet...”
“Baekho.”
“Yeah?”
“Don’t tease her too much.”
“...All right. I won’t play any more pranks on her.”
I sighed inwardly. How in the world could I control this kid?
While I was contemplating that, Baekho Lee switched gears. “By the way, bro.”
“Yeah?”
“So about Kitty... I mean, Missha Karlstein. Did you meet up with her?”

“Yeah. Thanks to you.” Of course, and maybe it was because so much time had passed, things between me and Missha were still awkward and distant. Still, I was sure that, with time, they would get better.
All right, then it was time to ask a question of my own...
“But Baekho.”
Now that Missha had been safely returned to me, I could finally pose the question I hadn’t been able to ask him last time.
“What is the Records Stone?”
It was time to stop being jerked around and written into corners by a story I didn’t even know.

chapters.title: Chapter 500: Age of Exploration (1)
paragraphs: The first time I heard about the Records Stone was during my conversation with the GM.
“There’s no reason for me not to believe him. At the very least, the Records Stone corroborates his claim, anyway.”

In answer to my question about why he believed Auril Gavis’s whole tale that a specific player would open the Gate of the Abyss in the future, he implied it was practically prophesied. The moment the words came out of his mouth, I knew that Baekho Lee probably had some connection to the Records Stone as well, because just like the GM, Baekho Lee was also obsessed with the user Elfnuna.
“Hm, is that so?”

That day, I didn’t want to risk doing anything that might set Baekho off, so I set my suspicions aside and didn’t mention it. I also figured I should look into it on my own first before asking him about it, but my findings simply confirmed what I already knew.
There’s no record of it in the library. Even Versyl looked like this was her first time hearing about it when I asked.
I spent some of my free time looking into it, but I couldn’t find any information about the Records Stone. Thus, I was left with only one option: ask someone who could give me an answer directly.
In response to my question, Baekho went silent. However, just as he had told Hyeonbyeol earlier, silence was an answer in itself.
Yeah, so he does know what the Records Stone is.

It made sense for him to keep quiet and think it over before answering me, but the window of time to make it look natural had already passed him by. Nevertheless, Baekho remained silent and stared at me like he was looking into my very soul.
“Bro.” He finally broke his silence. He didn’t even seem to realize that the smile he’d worn earlier had disappeared. In a cold, low voice, he asked, “Where did you hear about that?”
I felt a strange chill run down my spine, but I didn’t let it show. This guy always had hidden motivations lurking behind his every word. So why was he so interested in figuring out my source first?
He must be curious about how much I know.
Armed with that knowledge, I had only one option.
“I wonder.” I had to keep my answers vague and avoid being impatient. That was my best bet for getting the upper hand in this interaction. “Does it matter where I heard about it?”
Baekho’s eyes never left mine, studying me intently as I shrugged. He appeared to be deep in thought, likely wondering how to approach this conversation.

Was I asking because I really didn’t know what the Records Stone was? Or did I already know something, and I was just trying to cross-check information? In that case, how should he answer me? Or could he maybe not answer at all?

As time slowly ticked by, I could feel him carefully running through possibility after possibility and weighing his options. Figuring that giving him more time wouldn’t do me any good, I decided to double down. Even though this would seem totally out of left field to him, that just made this move all the more effective.
“Elfnuna.”
So I brought up the thing I knew would throw him the most off-balance. No matter how large the tree, if you continued to shake it, at least one leaf was bound to fall.
When I dropped the nickname for the first time in our years of encounters, Baekho’s eyes widened ever so slightly. His reaction wasn’t enough for me, though, which is why I quickly made my next move.
“You already know that that’s me.”
It was time to put one of my cards down on the table.
“What do you mean by that?”

His response, while almost instant, was neither positive nor negative—just a simple question. It was a pattern often seen in people who lie. Responding with a neutral question rather than another lie put them at ease.
That meant I needed to push harder.
“Baekho, haven’t you noticed? Ever since we first met, not once have I talked about Elfnuna with you.” I tapped my finger on the text above my head that said Elfnunna. “Don’t you think that’s weird?”
It was an inescapable trap. Checkmate.
Crackle.

The sound of burning firewood filled the heavy air between us. Instead of pushing him anymore, I gave Baekho some time to collect his thoughts. Normally in situations like these, the liar was the one least comfortable with prolonged silence.
“Bro...” After a long moment, Baekho finally cracked. “What do you want to ask me?”

It seemed this guy still intended to walk the tightrope. I was familiar with this mindset of his, wanting to give others the bare minimum while taking as much as he could in return. But there was a simple way around it.
“It’s not that I want to ask you something.”
When the opposition was tightly restricting the flow of information, it was best to put the ball in their court.
Where did I hear that word? How much do I know? None of that’s relevant.
“I just want to listen...”
Crackle.
“...and see what kind of answer you’re going to give me.”
The outcome of this conversation was now entirely in Baekho’s hands. And he made his choice faster than I anticipated.
“Hahaha, you’re seriously intense, bro! Seriously, I can never win against you!”

He suddenly snapped back to his usual self. From my point of view, it often seemed like there were two entirely different Baekhos who sometimes swapped places. I used to be taken aback by the way he could switch personalities at the drop of a hat, but I’d gotten pretty used to it by now.
“I’ll tell you everything. So what are you most curious about?”
Ha, this bastard is still trying to play games with me.
If I hadn’t had my guard up, I might have fallen for it. I didn’t answer him and, instead, just silently waited there, staring at him.

Baekho fidgeted a bit before letting out a heavy sigh. “...Were you really an office worker before?” When I remained silent, he continued, saying, “I’m just curious, that’s all. Just what kind of life do you have to live to end up like this?”
What is this guy talking about?

Finally picking up on the fact that I was going to keep silent no matter what he said, Baekho let out another deep sigh. “Hah... All right, I’ll tell you. Honestly, I’m pretty sure you’re just feeling me out... That must be why I’m so nervous... Well, maybe it would be best to fess up at this point.”
“Then answer me.”

“Okay. Do you believe in fate?” He paused and waited for me to respond, which I didn’t. “Ah, you’re not even going to answer that? Then I’m just going to explain this however I want, regardless of whether you understand me or not.”
“I told you already. All that’s important is what you want to tell me.”
“Fine. I got it.”
Baekho seemed to give in, noticing that I wasn’t planning to give him anything to work with anytime soon. After all, any question I answered, no matter how small, could lead to a major slip-up.

“I’m sure you already know that most ancient artifacts and their old myths were lost when this city was built, right? But did you know that one of those ancient artifacts wiped from the public record was the Records Stone? And that Records Stone is said to contain the entire history of this world. I’m not just talking about the past, but the future as well.”
Isn’t that just some sort of old myth?
That was what it felt like to me, at least, but I decided to hear his story out in its entirety.

“Anyway, even something like the Records Stone has an ending. Of course, that ending would mean the end of the world. And the beginning of the end was where the Witch came into play... Though I honestly don’t know much about that. There’s only one thing I really know for sure.”
I kept silent.
“Someone destroyed the Records Stone to prevent the end of the world. And because of that, this world still exists today.”
I took this in, my silence was not even an act anymore.
“The important thing here is this. The shards of the Records Stone are now scattered all over the world.”
As soon as I heard that, something clicked into place in my mind.
The Fragment of Records Stone.
A magical item left behind by Gabrielius. The very same one that sent both me and Amelia back in time.
“Some of the fragments have actually been found. And I’ve even seen some of them for myself.”
That news actually pissed me off a little, given something he said to me a few months ago.
“The Fragment of Records Stone...? I’ve heard about it before, but I guess it really does exist.”

So the bastard had been a liar from the start. I wanted to say something about that, but I didn’t want to interrupt him mid-story, so for now, I held my tongue as he continued. We were finally getting to the important bits.

“One of the fragments said this.” Baekho paused for a minute before reciting, “And so, blank, an evil spirit from a different world, was able to open the Gate of the Abyss and finally achieve his wish.”
The sentence seemed plucked right out of a storybook.

“Since this evil spirit’s name wasn’t written out in actual letters, it’s impossible to say for sure who it is. That’s because, in the Records Stone, people’s names are written with unique symbols. Something about how it’s the true name attached to your soul or something.” He paused to see if I had anything to say about that, then continued. “But that’s not the point. The main thing is that I’ve seen that same unique pattern written down on other fragments as well. And they said this.”
Ba-dump!
“Blank, who was the first to pass the original test, has opened their eyes in this world.”

Only after hearing that did I finally understand why Auril Gavis was so obsessed with the person who cleared the original version of the game. It also suddenly made sense why the GM was so interested in Elfnuna and, lastly, why Baekho Lee was so afraid of being on my bad side.

“Big Bro... You haven’t said a word this whole time. If you didn’t know anything about the Records Stone before this, then this part will pique your interest.” While I was still trying to gather my thoughts, Baekho continued his tale.” What’s so important about these records anyway? Aren’t they irrelevant now that the stone is broken? At first, that’s what I thought. But that’s not the case. In fact, something in the last fragment I saw came true.”
“...And what was that?”
When I finally opened my mouth, Baekho replied with a smirk, “That’s a secret.”
“...What?”

I glared at him, irritated by his cheeky attitude, but he acted like he didn’t care. “I’m not going to tell you. Believe it or not, it’s because it’s a personal matter. Don’t worry, it has nothing to do with you.”
If that was true, then there was no point in prying anymore. For some reason, when he said it was a “personal matter,” I was inclined to believe him.
“Yeah... I think that’s everything there is to say about the Records Stone... so how about I talk about Elfnuna next?”
When I nodded my head, Baekho moved on to the next item on the agenda.

“I made this chat room after learning about the Records Stone. And I waited all this time. That’s because I was certain that the person who had the highest chance of clearing the original version of the game was none other than Elfnuna, and obviously, Elfnuna had to be Korean. After that, well, it’s just like you guessed. All this time, I’ve thought that person might be you. But to think I was actually right...”
Baekho then looked at me with wide eyes and asked, “It is you, right?”

All this time, we’d been deceiving each other, unable to have an honest conversation. However, since he was willing to share this much with me, there was no reason for me to hide the truth from him any longer.
I calmly confirmed it for him. “Yeah.”
Although he was finally hearing it from my own mouth, Baekho didn’t have much of a reaction. He must have already been sure of it beforehand. He simply nodded his head.
“I think I told you everything I can. So, what do you think? Does that answer all your questions?”

“No, not yet.” I shook my head. Most of my questions were answered, but one important thing remained. And it might just be the most important question of all. “Why were you keeping this a secret from me this whole time?”
In other words, what was Baekho Lee’s angle?
“After hearing you out, none of this seems like something you needed to hide from me,” I said firmly.
As I confronted him head-on, Baekho responded with a bitter smile and a slight longing in his voice. “Fate is like a monkey’s paw.”
“...Monkey’s paw?”
I looked at him in confusion, urging him to elaborate, but he simply shrugged his shoulders like he’d already said everything he needed to say. “What? You don’t know what a monkey’s paw is?”
“I know what it is, but why are you suddenly bringing it up?”
“It’s exactly what I said. The things written on the Records Stone are bound to happen, no matter what. However, it’s impossible for me to know whether or not what I want will happen.”
“...Continue.”

“Big Bro, I’m certain that, one day, you will open the Gate of the Abyss. But does that guarantee a happy ending? Your wish might come true, but what about mine? That’s why I didn’t say anything about the stone until now. I wanted to buy some time to try and change your wish so it was the same as mine.”
I think I understood what he’d been thinking. After all, I’d done something similar before.
“Amelia’s older sister Laura died.”

Back then, I tried all sorts of things to change the future and ultimately succeeded. So maybe Baekho Lee had been trying to do the same. That was probably why he ended up showing his true colors the moment I told him that I didn’t want to return home.

“Then why did you team up with the Fallen Scholar?” If he was going to answer everything I asked, I figured I’d ask one more question. “I’m sure you didn’t just become buddy-buddy with him because you needed a wizard on your team.”
Baekho’s expression hardened for a moment before incredulous laughter burst from his throat. “Hahaha... Do you have some sort of lie detector in your head or something?”
A lie detector in my head? How the hell would that make any sense?
“Forget that and answer me. This is my last question.”
Although I urged him to get to it, Baekho was slow to respond. “I don’t know how this will sound to you, but...”
“It’s fine. Just say it.”
“That old man... You don’t have to worry about him. He’s just my Plan B.”
“Plan B...?”
“Yes. Things don’t always work out the way you want them to, right?”
Baekho smiled then, burying all his true thoughts and feelings deep inside.
“I need to have a backup in case I have to abandon Plan A. Because one way or another, I’m definitely getting out of this shitty place.”

chapters.title: Chapter 501: Age of Exploration (2)
paragraphs: Plan B. The moment I heard those words, I got a bad feeling.
“So, does that answer all your questions?”
“Yeah, pretty much.”

But otherwise, I no longer felt as hostile toward Baekho Lee as I once did. He had honestly answered all my questions rather than trying to deceive me and hide his true intentions behind a smile. If nothing else, that was an improvement.
“Even if I ask you what your Plan B is, you’re not going to tell me, right?”
“I really can’t tell you. I need to have at least one card left up my sleeve, right?”

I sighed. Still, he had a point. Although it was a shame I wouldn’t get to hear his plan, I understood why he couldn’t tell me about it and, instead, chose to move on. It wasn’t like I had told him everything either. We only ever showed each other as many of our cards as was necessary. That was enough for now.
“Then, does this make me your enemy or your friend?”
I answered without much hesitation. “I wonder. It feels like at best, we’re temporary partners.”
“...Temporary partners?”
“Yeah. That’s right.”
Baekho didn’t seem to quite get what I meant by that.
Well, it’s a good idea to clear the air between us.
“I will work with you to make sure you get back home,” I clarified.
“And in return, I help you whenever you need?”
“Something like that.”
“That’s not so bad, but what if we disagree on something or something goes wrong...?”

I smiled and shrugged my shoulders. It was unlike Baekho to sound so cautious and tentative. “Then we’ll just have to go our separate ways. There’s nothing else to it. I hope it won’t come to that, but as you said, it’s impossible to guarantee that things will turn out the way you want them to.”
“...Big Bro, you’re so cool.”
“Yeah. So that Plan B of yours, just keep working on it. I won’t get in the way. Meanwhile, I’ll keep working on my plans too.”
It was human instinct to prepare for the worst. And in my opinion, anyone who didn’t have that instinct was someone I wouldn’t want to work with in the first place.
“Temporary partners. All right, let’s do it.”
Baekho reached out a hand, apparently pleased with the agreement we came to. But why was he doing something so cringy now? Even though I hated it, I accepted his handshake.
“...Hey, bro, I just got goosebumps.”
“You don’t have to tell me twice. I feel the same way.”
After a short handshake, we each sat back down on the sofa with a smile on our faces.
“We should have done this from the start.”
“I know.”
This wasn’t all that bad of a feeling.
After that, I continued my conversation with Baekho. One of the topics we discussed was the new hidden area.
“You gotta tell me, bro. Just what in the world did you do?”
“I don’t know either. I think I activated a special condition somehow, but I really don’t know how it happened.”

“Really? That’s a shame, but... Even if you did know, I guess it wouldn’t make that much of a difference. After all, a feat recorded on the Stone of Honor can only be performed once. Whatever you did, it won’t work exactly the same way ever again.”
“Oh, really?”
“What, you didn’t know? I guess you really don’t know much aside from what was in the game...”
Well, that couldn’t be helped. I practically lived in the library for a while there when I first came to this world, but the only information I could find there was public and basic.
“...It’s already time. I should get going.” After chatting for a while longer, it was time for Baekho to log out.
“Hey,” I said before he could go, “why don’t we start meeting up with each other in the city from now on?”
“I’d love to, but I don’t think I’ll be able to for a while. I’m going to go outside for a bit.”
“...Outside. You mean outside the walls?”
“Yeah. I finally found a way out. I searched through the underground city for literal ages to find one.”
Wait a minute, this sounds important.

When I asked him to tell me more, he shook his head, expression pinched in regret. “I wish I could, but it’d be too tough to explain in the next two minutes. I’ll send a letter to your house before I head out. I’ll even give you the instructions in case you want to go out as well.”
“Thanks.”
Is this what people mean when they say that you should surround yourself with smart people?
Without lifting a finger, I’d procured a way to get out of the kingdom. Like Baekho, I’d been curious about the outside world for quite some time now.
Still, I got back to the point. “But why do you want to go out there?”
“Auril Gavis. I have a feeling he’s out there for some reason, so I’m going to look for him. I’m sure that old geezer has the answers to most of my questions.”
Come to think of it, I should have asked Baekho about the old man as well. Given the current state of our relationship, he would probably give me an honest answer now.
Well... I guess I can just ask him next time.
“Well then, I’m off. See you next month!”
“Yeah, see you. If you find him, let me know.”
“Yep.”
Just like that, Baekho Lee left. I sat there staring at the fireplace and collecting my thoughts for a while before Hyeonbyeol finally returned.
“You came back later than usual today.”
