“What, do you think I just wait outside and stare at the number of people in the chat until I can rejoin?”
Uh... did she not? I sort of thought that was what she did, given how she came back almost immediately every other time...
“So... your expression looks lighter than usual.”
“What?”
“You look like you took care of something that’s been weighing on your mind.”
“Oh... really?”

This woman was strangely sharp when it came to that sort of thing. I neither confirmed nor denied her suspicions, but she smiled like I had and reclined on the other side of the sofa. As she lay down, I didn’t know where to position my eyes.
“Hyeonbyeol...? You know you’re wearing a skirt, right...?”
“So? I’m wearing stockings.”
Th-then, does that make it okay?
For some reason, her argument worked, and I found myself convinced to stay put.

Hyeonbyeol watched me with that same smile on her face. “Look at you, acting like that over something so minor. Anyway, now that I’m here...” She whipped out a book from the middle of nowhere and, as if that wasn’t anything special at all, started reading.
“...What’s that book?” I asked. “Where did you get it?”
“Don’t you know? This book is quite popular around here these days.”
I just stared at her blankly.
“You really don’t know, huh? Well, you know how you can buy and sell clothes that can be used here in the community, right?”
“Yeah.”

Ghostbusters was surprisingly similar to certain online communities in that there was a currency system. You could use it for customization, such as furnishing chat rooms or styling your character, but I had never used it except to get a single new outfit.
“This book is just like that,” Hyeonbyeol said.
“Then it’s just an accessory with nothing written inside?”

“That’s not at all what I’m saying. No, this book was written by somebody who used to write a lot on the bulletin board for free. Since their posts were so popular, they consulted with the mods for permission to start making and selling books instead.”
“Huh... that’s interesting. Is it good?”
“Do you want to read it? Here, I have one of their older ones.”
“Yeah, let me read through it.”

I took the new book from her and flipped to the first page. It was a regular urban fantasy novel, but from the very start, it was addicting. Nevertheless, I was having a hard time concentrating on it.
...I’m going to lose my mind.
Hyeonbyeol was just reading her book, sure, but why did she keep wiggling her feet like that?
“I’m stretching. My legs are numb.”
“...Did I say that out loud?”
“No. I could just tell from the look on your face that that’s what you were thinking.”
...I really can’t do anything in front of this woman without her reading me.
I decided to turn my back to her so I could focus on the book. The two of us continued to read in silence for a long while.
“Hey.”
It took me a moment to realize Hyeonbyeol was talking to me. I blinked and glanced up. “...Huh?”
“Don’t you usually leave around now?”

Man, why was this book so interesting? I didn’t even notice the time—it was only thanks to Hyeonbyeol’s reminder that I hadn’t missed the Round Table entirely. I tossed her a quick apology over my shoulder as I said goodbye, and then I hurried into the private chat, practically throwing on my usual navy suit and lion mask since I was short on time.
By the time I entered the room, there were already eight other members inside.
“You’re here, Mr. Lion. Pshehe.”
Clown was the first to greet me in that overly familiar way of his. Next was Fox, Crescent, Deer, Queen, Butterfly, Wolf...
There are only eight people here?
Black Mask, one of the newbies from last time, didn’t seem to have come today. But just as I was thinking that—
Step.
Black Mask walked through the door on the opposite end of the room. She took a second to glance around the table for an empty seat before sitting down.
“It’s nice to see you, Ms. Black...”
Goblin, who was sitting next to her, greeted her politely. However, she simply crossed her arms and didn’t say a word in return. She gave off the vibe of someone with a lot of power.
Step.
In any case, I walked over to my usual seat, which had been left empty for me. The moment I sat down, the doors to the Round Table slammed shut.
“There are ten of us in total today...” Queen muttered to herself. “What a strange feeling, seeing so many people here.”
“It makes sense that you would feel that way, Queen,” Crescent replied, not unkindly.
“Are you saying you don’t feel the same way, Mr. Crescent?”

The one who replied to Queen was not Crescent but one of the Newbie Trio from last time. It was the one wearing the wolf mask, the same person who held the title of Returning User. “Hahaha! Back when Master was here, there were times when there were more than twenty of us! Ah, things back then were—”
“Back then, all you did was suck up to Master. Pshehe.”
Wolf went quiet.
“Clown, are you really one to talk?” scoffed Crescent.

“Pshehe. I guess elves must be quite attractive given that you’ve fallen completely head over heels for an NPC. So when are you going to try and find me, again? Aren’t you going to take revenge any time soon?”
“Wow! Are you two enemies? That’s awesome!” a cheery voice interrupted. “Please make sure to invite me when you guys finally fight!”
“Pshehe! Of course, Ms. Butterfly.”
I sighed. Now that there were so many people attending, things were getting quite chaotic.
When I turned my head toward Fox, she immediately caught my glare and rushed to establish order. “Since it seems like everyone is here, why don’t we start...?”
“Haha, let’s do that. We’re not just here to chat, after all.”

When things settled down, the attention naturally shifted to the person sitting next to me. After all, this was now an unspoken rule at the Round Table: the person next to me was always the first to go.
“Then I guess you’re first this time, Queen.”

“I guess so. I didn’t expect you all to sit over there, on the other side of the table.” Queen was actually sitting three seats down from me, but she was the first to go this time since everyone else sat across from us. She let out a heavy sigh and slowly began. “This is related to quite a hot topic these days. The person who made the Stone of Honor was none other than the Last Great Sage, Diplan Groundel Gabrielius himself.”

Given that the jewel on the table turned green, that meant the information was something she believed to be true, and less than half the people here knew about it. Nevertheless, it didn’t take long before people started to complain.
“Is it even important to know who made that thing? Pshehe.”
“Hehe, that’s what I was going to say. It’s not like I’m a wizard or something—why should I care about that?”
“In the first place, basically every strange or mysterious thing in this world ends up leading back to that guy, so it’s not like this is really news.”

Apparently having predicted this response, Queen didn’t try to defend herself at all, instead pivoting to offer up more information. “How about this, then? There is credible evidence that the Stone of Honor itself is an Achievement of Gabrielius. In other words, it’s proof of a hidden feature.”
A hidden feature...
“That’s not bad.”
It seemed that the other members of the group were also willing to accept Queen’s information. With her turn over, we moved on to the next.
“A meeting between all the races will be held next month. And it’s confirmed that the human representative, the Lord of the Magic Tower, will also be in attendance.”
Simply stating that a meeting between the races was going to occur would not have been enough. That was why Crescent made sure to specify who would represent the humans so that no one could complain.
So the Lord of the Magic Tower is the human representative...
Actually, besides that, I hadn’t even known there was going to be a meeting next month, and I was the chieftain. How did he already know about that when even I didn’t?
Just goes to show the difference between being a member of a race with power and one without.

In fact, aside from the barbarians, every race had connections to the royal family. The other houses of Melbeth hadn’t left their homelands for nothing. By distancing themselves from those beneath them, they were able to sidle closer to the top. And in return, they were able to provide information that improved their people’s standing overall.
“Missha Karlstein has joined the Anabada Clan.”
Suddenly, it was Fox’s turn. I was a little bit taken aback suddenly hearing that name at this table, but it wasn’t too jarring.
News of her joining will spread everywhere soon enough either way, so Fox must have decided that using her name as information this time was a safe bet.
She wasn’t wrong in thinking so. The value of the information was relatively low, but no one raised any objections. After all, anything related to Bjorn Yandel was considered useful here.
“Then that girl must have...”
“But... I thought she was on his team? Something must have happened.”
“Pshehe... Not bad at all, Ms. Fox. I didn’t know you had such good sources.”

After Fox’s turn, it was Goblin’s, then Black Mask’s, then Deer’s. However, there was nothing particularly shocking this time around, and I tuned them out like I would the nightly news at dinner time.
“About that woman, Missha Karlstein...”
What? What about her?
Just as I was about to doze off, Butterfly’s comment suddenly caught my attention. I blinked awake, on high alert, as she continued with a grin on her face.
“She’s a traitor.”
Even though I heard what she said clear as day, I couldn’t seem to process it. A traitor? Did she mean that from Baekho Lee’s point of view?
While I was scrambling to make sense of this, Butterfly, seemingly reading my mind, added, “Oh, and I mean to Bjorn Yandel, of course.”
What in the world is she talking about?
With that thought in mind, I quickly looked toward the center of the Round Table.
Shaaaaaa.
The jewel quietly radiated a bright green glow.

chapters.title: Chapter 502: Age of Exploration (3)
paragraphs: After Butterfly’s turn, the Round Table continued.
“The person who made the modded version of Dungeon and Stone wasn’t Auril Gavis.”
Wolf’s information was similar to last time, with the clear goal of trying to make the players hate Auril Gavis less.
“I wonder what you guys will think of this, pshehe. Noark was able to defeat the eighth floor’s Lord of the Floor last month.”
Clown was also able to easily get through his turn with information about Noark, which he was affiliated with.
Then it was finally my turn.
“If you defeat the boss of Skull Island and then go up to the tenth floor, you can trigger a special event.”
Everyone’s focus immediately honed in on me, wondering what I was going to say, but I quickly passed my turn with a random piece of information I had that wasn’t all that important.
“...A special event. I’m excited to see what it is. Ah, of course, I guess the war will have to end before I can experience it for myself. Pshehe.”

It had been a while since I’d last shared a piece of information about the game. The new members didn’t find this strange at all, of course. For these players, game knowledge that got the green light could be extremely valuable in its own right.

“All right, guys, let’s all do a bit better this time around.” The members who had known me for a while now, however, were quick to react. They tried to encourage each other to share more important information this time since they assumed that the previous turn must have bored me.
“Then... I guess it’s my turn again.”

Again, we went around the room sharing information, starting with Queen. I listened and made an effort to commit it all to memory. There were some genuinely shocking and useful pieces of information shared, but I wasn’t able to concentrate on any of them. And the reason was simple.
Missha Karlstein is a traitor. Not only that, but she’s a traitor to me.
Those words echoed through my head on repeat. Before I knew it, the second round had ended, and we were almost near the end of the third round.

...What the hell did she mean by that? Missha is a traitor? I thought I’d worked everything out with her and things were finally looking up. Baekho Lee... is that bastard trying to do something? Was this what he meant by Plan B?
All kinds of possibilities cluttered up my head.
I need to hear more.

Butterfly was the one who shared that information. However, despite what I was hoping, she made no mention of Missha in the second or third rounds. If I wanted to hear more, then I’d have to be the one to take action.
“Pshehe, why are you all so surprised? Is Rafdonia that afraid of Noark’s growth?”

How could I bring the topic up naturally? If I pressed for details on why she was a traitor, that would definitely raise suspicion. “Lion is Bjorn Yandel” rumors were already rampant at the Round Table. I had to carefully consider each and every move I—
Oh, it was already my turn. When I tuned back in, I realized that everyone was staring at me in complete silence.
...Let’s just wait one more round.

I decided that if there was still no mention of Missha in the next round, then I would take action. For now, I threw out, “If you defeat the Lord of the Floor Heavenly Sky by yourself, you can acquire an active effect of your choice.”
It was a difficult piece of information to acquire but one that didn’t do you any good even if you knew it.
Shaaaaaa—
When a green light appeared, there was a moment of silence around the Round Table. Of course, it didn’t last long.
“I-It’s possible... to defeat a Lord of the Floor alone...?”
“Well, if you played the game on Times One Hundred mode... then I guess it might be?”
“Pshehe. Do you really think Mr. Lion would have played the game in a mode like that? Why do you think he shared that with us?”

Since it was information related to a Lord of the Floor, there were no objections. Honestly, even if I shared a piece of complete bullshit with them, as long as a green light appeared, they would all assume it had some greater, secret meaning.
Then is it Queen’s turn again?

“I think I’ve heard everything worth hearing this month. I’ll stop here and take my leave then.” However, when I glanced at her, Queen suddenly announced she was leaving. And, unfortunately, it seemed the main reason was because of me. “...After all, even Mr. Lion looks bored.”

It wasn’t that I was bored, it was just that I was having trouble concentrating since my mind was elsewhere. And the reason I was sharing information about the game was because that way I wouldn’t have to overthink what I shared.

“That’s a shame... I really thought you’d be happy to hear about Noark defeating the Lord of the Floor. Pshehe...” Clown seemed to also be disappointed since he didn’t receive any praise or attention from me despite doing his best to bring me a worthwhile piece of information this month. “Well... I guess this kind of information isn’t anything special to Mr. Lion.”
Clown seemed pretty depressed but promised to come back next month with even more interesting intel.
Man, I can’t ask them to go another round with the mood like this.
So with that, the Round Table came to an end for the month.
The day after Ghostbusters, I awoke in the afternoon following a good night’s sleep, and Versyl Gowland dropped by the house to see me.
“What’s the matter?”
While I had a feeling I already knew why she was here, I feigned ignorance. Versyl asked to speak to me in private, saying she had urgent information for me.
“I... I don’t know what this will sound like to you, but... I received some information alleging Missha Karlstein is a traitor.”
I was right. The reason she ran over here to talk to me as soon as she woke up was this.
“A traitor?” I prompted.
“I don’t know for sure if it’s true. No, I am sure, but... I don’t know the details.”
Versyl then asked me to reconsider having Missha join our clan, but I flat-out refused. “I can’t make a decision like that without knowing more.”
“I see... That makes sense...”
“But that doesn’t mean I’m going to simply ignore your concerns. I will do my best to look into it, but can you also try and find out more as well?”
“...All right. I’ll look into it, then.”
“Thanks.”

Well, that settled that. At the next Round Table, she would put on her fox mask and work to dig up more info. Since I wouldn’t have to ask myself, this would definitely lower the risk of my identity being exposed.
“I’ll be heading out then. Contact me whenever you need me.”
“All right.”
Versyl left, and around evening time, a letter arrived at the house.
“Mister! You got a strange little letter,” Erwen said, holding the mail she’d retrieved from the mailbox. “I think you should look at it!”

On the surface of the envelope was a drawing of a white tiger. The envelope had already been opened, and when I read the note inside, it was filled with letters and symbols that didn’t exist in this world.
Here’s what you asked for, bro.

Why the hell did he send it in Korean? What if someone else had seen it? Or worse, recognized the characters? Even though I was fuming, I still read through the letter’s instructions on how to get outside the city walls.
...It’s a more complicated process than I thought.
This much information was impossible to memorize in one go, so I decided to fold the letter and store it away in my sub-space instead.
It’s nice to have options. After all, you never know what’s going to happen. That’s why you always need to prepare for the worst-case scenario. This is also why...
“Emily, can you look into Missha?”
“What do you mean?”
Afterward, I filled Amelia in on what happened at the Round Table and asked her to investigate.
“I’ll try, but there’s a good chance she’ll eventually catch on. Even catching her the first time wasn’t easy.”
“That bad? I figured you would be much better than her at stealth, given the essences you have.”
“If she did approach us with some sort of ulterior motive, then there’s a high chance she’s hiding an essence from us.”
That gave me pause. “Don’t get too close to her, then. Just keep an eye on her for the time being.”
“Will do.”
I let out a sigh. Even though she had set limits, now that Amelia was investigating Missha, we were sure to uncover the truth.

With that settled, I spent the rest of the day resting, then returned to my busy schedule the following morning. I stopped by the holy land again to sell plots of land and visited the former chieftain to hear how previous meetings among the heads of the races went. I also popped over to see Raven as well.
“Records Stone...? Do you mean the Fragment of Records Stone? The legacy of Gabrielius?”

“Both the Records Stone and its fragments. If you have a book or any other information about them, please tell me. It might attract you some unwanted attention, though, so don’t look too much into it.”
“All right, I’ll keep that in mind. But Mr. Yandel, are your preparations for your next quest going smoothly...?”
“There’ve been no issues so far, but I guess you can never be sure until you head into the labyrinth.”
“That’s true. After all, nobody knows anything for sure until the expedition starts. But about Versyl Gowland... how is she?”
“What do you mean?”
“What do you think? Wizards play the most critical role in expeditions like this! Last time I saw her, it seemed that she didn’t know much about history...”
“Well, that’s all right. She’s good at fighting, and she’s trustworthy. So that’s more than enough to make up for that.”
“...Is that so?”

Following my meeting with Raven, whenever I had the time, I gathered my clan members three times a week. On the surface, the purpose of the meetings was to work out the bad blood between Missha and the other members before our quest this month.
“...I haven’t found anything in particular yet.”
After each one, I received constant reports from Amelia about her investigation, but thus far, she hadn’t unearthed anything strange about Missha.
“...This is the most well-funded expedition I’ve ever been on.”

Sometime later, Melbeth sent us supplies for our upcoming quest—a mix of combat and support scrolls, all sorts of potions, navigation-related Numbered Items, and more. The supplies were versatile enough to be useful regardless of whatever environment we might find ourselves in—whether we ended up hiking a mountain, traveling over water, or traversing through fire. On top of that, they were also of the highest quality.
This must have cost a lot of money...

It also gave us insight into just how high Melbeth’s expectations were when it came to us finding information on this new hidden area. Still, though they were a bit overzealous, I was confident that we could live up to those expectations. As such, we continued to spend the days preparing for our quest.
“Bjorn...”
“Not Bjorn. It’s ‘Chieftain,’ First Elder.”
“Ah, because we’re in the holy land! I’ll keep that in mind.”

The sun was starting to set as Ainar and I made our way down the forest path. Eventually, we came across a clearing full of dozens of young warriors with bright, excited expressions on their faces. At the sight of them, I couldn’t help but smile. I then yelled out, “Congratulations, young warriors! As of today, you will leave the holy land and be reborn as true warriors!”
A quick scan of the crowd told me everything I needed to know.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
There were no newbies this time around.

Evolution was a constant, exponential process, and when looking at the entire history of humanity on Earth, the best example of this would be the Industrial Revolution. In just the past few hundred years, humanity enjoyed explosive growth and development. So then, what about the barbarians? When had the barbarians undergone their most radical period of development and evolution?
As of today, I could confidently answer.
Now.
Proof of that could be seen here in this field. Even the tutorial’s script had drastically changed.
“Now, step forward one by one and choose the weapon, as well as the armor, that suits you.”
Numerous weapons and pieces of armor lined the shelves of the armor stand. That, however, was only the beginning.
“Come here. You shouldn’t put your gaiters on like that. Here, do it like this.”
“Thank you... It’s my first time ever putting them on.”

Not only did we now provide them with a chest plate, but we also provided them other pieces of equipment as well, including a bag full of various basic supplies that were essential for any quest, including a compass, water bottle, and potions.
Roughly a million stones per person...
The amount of resources given to our young warriors had more than tripled, but that was no problem. After all, if we ever needed money, all we had to do was sell some more land.
With this level of support, they’ll surely progress quickly and earn lots of money that they can spend on buying land.
We were still in the beginning stages, but at this rate, the self-sustaining cycle I’d been striving toward would soon be achieved.
“Ugh... It’s so tight...!”

The young warriors seemed uncomfortable with the weight of their new armor, but they thankfully didn’t try to act cocky or brag about how they didn’t need it. That was all because they had a role model to look up to.
“Bear with it. You will get used to it in no time.”
“But still—”
“It’s not a choice! It’s only natural for a warrior to wear armor! Just look at the chieftain! If you want to be a great warrior as well, you must wear armor!”
There were no longer any warriors in our tribe who refused to wear protection.
“...I’m going to save up and buy lithinum armor!”
Even the lithinum armor I tended to use had turned into the mark of a skilled and respected warrior.
“Now, go forth! To where your destiny awaits!”
After giving them their basic equipment I had Versyl, who was waiting outside the holy land, group them together with the Binding spell. After that, they all headed into the labyrinth.
“...I hope everyone comes back safe.”
“Don’t worry, Ainar. I’m sure there won’t be nearly as many looters aiming for their hearts now that the Magic Tower labeled them a forbidden magical ingredient.”
“That makes sense...”
Barbarians were the type to survive no matter the circumstances. With the support and supplies we gave them this time, all of them would definitely come back alive.
I hope they grow up fast so we can raise the price of land even higher.
Anyway, after confirming that all our young warriors had entered the portal, I got ready myself. I had officially fulfilled my role of Chieftain for the night.
“Mister...”
“It’s not ‘Mister.’”
“...What?”
“From here on out, call me ‘Captain.’”
Now, it was time for our own quest to begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 503: Age of Exploration (4)
paragraphs: A familiar crystal cave covered with bright lights greeted me the moment I stepped through the portal and opened my eyes. I subconsciously felt myself hesitate. Perhaps it was because the last time we were here, we had fought for our lives against Dreadfear.
“I... just have to stab one person...?”
“You will... become... a great... warrior...”
God damn it.

No matter how hard I tried, I wasn’t sure I’d ever be able to forget that day. I never wanted to go through anything like it again. Yet, as long as I continued to explore the labyrinth, I’d almost certainly run into a similar situation again someday.
“Mister... what’s the matter?’
“...It’s nothing.”
I quickly pulled myself together after noticing the concerned look Erwen was shooting me and went to check on my other clan members, though only Erwen and Missha were nearby.
Missha, she’s been quiet for a while now. Does she still not feel comfortable around us?
“Missha.”
“...Oh, yes?”
“We should get going. Are you all right?”
“Yeah...”

For some reason, Missha only ever responded to me in a strangely awkward, quiet tone these days. But I shook off the thought and got moving. Our first destination was going to be the monument located in the center of the Crystal Cave. There, we would meet up with the rest of the clan. We’d had to split into two teams this time around.
...I need to increase our number of clan members as soon as possible.

The reason why we were forced to divvy up this month was because of our numbers. Our clan had a total of seven members now, so we had to split up into one group of three and another of four. Still, if we excluded Auyen, we could have had an even six.
...We might need a navigator, though.

After much discussion, we decided to include Auyen this time. We deemed it necessary to prepare for any eventuality, given that we didn’t know what to expect from this new map. Some environments needed a ship and navigator to traverse, like the sixth floor.
...And if we can’t find the hidden area this time around, we’ll have to head to a higher floor anyway.

Back in the city, I’d read through any book related to hidden areas I could get my hands on and learned that they all had one thing in common: the hidden area would always appear on the same floor where the achievement was unlocked. A good example was the achievement of the King of the Elves.
The Elf Archer, Armella Powell Merhenia, and her colleagues defeated the Coordinator, Gregory, and opened a hidden area of the labyrinth.

The hidden boss Gregory the Coordinator had a low spawn rate and could only be found if you continued to climb higher up the Tower of Heavens rather than heading up to the fifth floor. After being the first to defeat it, the King of the Elves’s party unlocked the Labyrinth of Larcaz, not to mention what were essentially three other distinct hidden areas on the fourth floor.

Well, whatever the case, that wasn’t important. What was important was that on the seventh day, the first floor of the labyrinth would close, so if we didn’t find anything by then, we’d have no choice but to head higher up.
“...There are a lot of people here.”

When we arrived at the heart of the cave, the place was brimming with adventurers. The bustling scene stood in stark contrast to the usual quiet of this area, but I supposed that wasn’t all that strange. This was the first place any smart adventurer who was searching for the hidden area would look. Case in point, most of the adventurers present were wearing high-quality gear and proudly showing off their clans’ emblems.
Still, there are more people than I thought there’d be...
As we entered the dark zone, the adventurers who spotted us scrambled to clear the way for us, awed looks on their faces.
“Look, it’s him.”
“It’s Bjorn Yandel...”
“Sure enough, even he’s searching here first...”
They continued to stare at me like I was some sort of celebrity. But some instead looked at me with a competitive glint in their eyes.
“...Does he know something because he unlocked the area?”
“He came here first. That must mean something has to be hidden here, right?”
In this situation, being famous was a disadvantage.
“Missha, don’t fall behind, and make sure to stay close.”
As we continued to walk down the dark pathway, we eventually reached the cavern that housed the monument to the Last Great Sage. Again, countless adventurers were gathered around it.
“Oh! It’s Bjorn! He’s here!”
“You’re finally here.”
“You’re here, Captain.”
As soon as we arrived, we met up with the second team, who were already there waiting. The first thing I did was ask Amelia for an update.
“Did anyone find anything?”
“Not yet. It seems like the wizards from the other clans are doing something, but they haven’t found anything yet.”
“I see...”
As we approached the monument, the wizards gathered in front of us quickly cleared the way.
Gulp!
Everyone immediately shut up, their eyes wide as they drank in every single move I made, clearly hoping I’d give them some sort of hint. It was actually hilarious.
I don’t have a single damn clue either.

It was strange to be standing in front of this monument again. Last I’d seen it, there was an alter to the Witch sitting in this exact spot instead. Just what other secrets were hidden in this labyrinth?
With that thought in mind, I began to read the text on the monument again.
[The Last Great Sage, Diplan Groundel Gabrielius. In honor of his great first step.]
It was the same text I’d read countless times before.
So the text didn’t change...

After that, I scanned the monument with a careful eye, but once again, I couldn’t find anything suspicious or different. The same went for when I touched the stone as well. After finding nothing, I returned to my teammates to discuss the situation.
“Versyl, did you activate Voice Control?”
“Yes, it’s turned on.”
“All right.”
“Yandel, have you found something?”
“Not yet.”

There were a lot of things I wanted to check out, but given how many eyes were on me, I couldn’t do a thing. Everyone here might revere me as some great hero, but the truth was that I wasn’t all that special—or nice enough to help them all out.
“Then let’s go.”
I decided to come back later when there were fewer people around. However, just as we were about to leave, someone came up to me.

“Baron Yandel.” The man had a sword, brown hair, and a strong-looking build. I looked down at him, wondering who he was, and he greeted me with aristocratic deference. “My name is Marnus Stilico. I’m the leader of the White Ivory Clan’s Ninth Team. It is an honor to meet you, Your Lordship.”
Ah, so that was the emblem of the White Ivory Clan. They were one of the four biggest clans left.
“Versyl, turn off Voice Control for a moment.”
“Yes.”
“So,” I asked politely once Voice Control was deactivated, “What do you want to talk about?”
The guy immediately slid into a careful proposal. “If you have any information about the hidden area, we would like to buy it at a reasonable price.”
Jeez, I was wondering what he wanted. But that’s it?
I had received countless proposals over the past few weeks to buy information about the hidden area. If memory served, one of the letters I ignored had actually been from the White Ivory Clan.

“Information, you say...” Even if I did have any to give, I’d never sell it for money. Still, I pretended to genuinely consider his offer before asking him a question on my mind. “Is the captain of the White Ivory Clan also here on the first floor?”
“...I’m sure he’s still here, but he’s probably not anywhere nearby.”
“Are you also searching the outskirts, then?”
“No, of the nine teams that make up the White Ivory Clan, we are the only ones tasked with exploring the hidden area.”
In other words, aside from these guys, the rest of the clan had headed straight for the higher floors like usual.
“I’m surprised. It looks like you’re not putting a lot of resources into the search?”
I decided to act like I was worried they wouldn’t offer much money for my information, seeing as only one of their teams was assigned to explore the hidden area.

“No one within our clan is taking this matter lightly,” he rushed to say. “Unfortunately, because of our wartime contract with the palace, we simply aren’t able to dedicate all of our resources to exploring the area right now.”
“In other words, the war comes first?”

“Yes. If this area can be found within a few days, our team alone will suffice. But likewise, if it’s not easy to find, then there’s no reason for us to go all-out from the start. Our clan isn’t the only one approaching the issue this way. I’m certain that all the other clans are doing something similar as well.”
“I see.”
“Then... will you sell us information...?”
It was time to end this conversation. “I’m sorry, but I won’t.” I’d already heard everything I wanted to hear from him.
“...I see. Yes, thank you for graciously lending me some of your precious time.”
After that conversation was over, we turned our backs to the monument and left the center of the cavern.
This war is surprisingly helpful.

I was worried that the entire first floor would be flooded with adventurers, but further away from the center, it was relatively empty. Most of our competition must have been tangled up in the war effort. That meant that even if the entrance ended up being easy to find, we wouldn’t have to worry too much about losing out on our share.
“Bjorn! Where are we going now?” Ainar asked excitedly.
“The outskirts...”
It was finally my turn to show off some skills I hadn’t used in a while. The quicker we found this place, the more treasures we could enjoy.

Dungeon and Stone was arguably the most player-hostile game I’d ever played. You had to bash your head into the keyboard to defeat its bosses. The various levels and Rifts you encountered were teeming with all sorts of bizarre mechanics that made them a pain in the ass to clear. On top of that, there were way too many hidden features in this game, so much so that you started to wonder if the entire point of the game was just to go looking for them.

I could rant about how hostile the game design was for three days straight, yet at the same time, the biggest reason I first got hooked on the game was that very same hostility. Those days, I’d been contending every day with unbearable boredom, and the only thing that had managed to grab my attention and light a fire in me had been this nightmarishly difficult game.
It’s been a while since I’ve searched for a hidden feature.

What made Dungeon and Stone tough was these hidden elements. In essence, your ability to progress in the game was completely reliant on how many hidden features you knew about. If you didn’t know a thing about them, it was practically impossible to progress up the floors like you’d be able to in most other games. That was why I developed a habit of searching for hidden features every time I played. It had become as natural to me as breathing.

If I saw a statue, I would look for a way to break it. Whenever I was on the move, I made sure to keep my character close to the wall while spamming buttons. If something seemed even slightly suspicious, I would cast all kinds of magic on it. I even burned, froze, and threw the bodies of plunderers around to see if there was a reward for doing so.
The result of doing that for nearly a decade was the discovery of countless hidden features. Oh, and of course, I gained a certain expertise in efficiently tracking them down.
The issue is that I haven’t invested in ways to find hidden features.

I didn’t have any characters near me with incredible luck or essences specifically tailored to searching. In fact, I’d trained up all of my current comrades to specialize in combat. After all, before last month, I’d been confident that I had already found every hidden feature that the game had to offer.
Thankfully, I can at least read the ancient language now...
Well, if the hidden area didn’t require the ancient language to find, then it was a useless skill to have.
Slam!
Still, what else could I do? If you didn’t have teeth, you just had to chew with your gums.
Like so.
Slam!
Just as I used to back when I played the game, I walked as close to the wall as I could and hit it as I went. It wasn’t just me either; the entire clan did the same.
Slam! Thud! Whack!
It was a symphony of hammers, daggers, and spirits attacking the walls of the Crystal Cave.
“Ohhh! This is fun! Just like a festival!”
Everyone aside from Ainar seemed reluctant, but they still diligently carried out my orders.
“Even if you hate it, there’s no other choice! This is the standard way to find an Achievement of Gabrielius.”
“...Standard way?”
“I read it in a book before!”
As we continued to make our way through Crystal Cave, I was forced to keep making similar excuses to Versyl, since she didn’t know that I was an evil spirit.

Besides that, whenever we came across certain areas, we made sure to perform a very thorough check. The three-way intersection, the pond next to a large rock, any unusual patches of moss or puddles of water we came across—and that was just to name a few.
For the most part, the topography of the Crystal Cave changed whenever the labyrinth reopened. However, there were a few things and locations that stayed the same every single time.
And usually, hidden features are found in places that don’t change.
We continued to whack the walls as we wandered through the caverns, finally reaching the dark zone on the outskirts of the cave.
Fwooosh!
Of course, the portal leading to Goblin Forest had already been opened by some other adventurers. We looked around, but there didn’t seem to be anything suspicious nearby.
Damn, it wasn’t by the portal either.
We then decided to split up and search the outskirts on our own for a bit before meeting up again.
Day one, day two...

Time continued to fly by without any changes. Then, with only two hours left before the third day began, something finally happened. Erwen discovered a smallish clan of about twenty people all gathered by a certain passageway, trying to block people from accessing it. Like they had discovered something and were trying to hide it.
“I thought I needed to tell you before anything else, Mister, so I didn’t approach them on my own. I kept my distance and made sure they didn’t spot me.”
So that’s the situation...
“Well done, Erwen.”
I led my team to the place Erwen described. When we arrived, we saw some adventurers who looked to be standing guard, blocking entry to a passageway.
Step, step.

I approached them without bothering to hide my presence, and the adventurers guarding the passageway recognized me almost immediately. They lifted their weapons, but their words and actions both oozed hesitance. “Stop! P-Please stop there... B-Baron Yandel...”
Yeah, it must be hard to be rude to me once they recognize me.
“I’m passing through. Is there a problem with that?” I asked, still approaching them.

The adventurers’ wariness shifted to visible fright, and they desperately tried to convince me to turn back around. “W-We are currently camping here... and according to the unwritten rules of adventuring... I-I must humbly ask you to please leave...”
Ha? They really expect me to buy that when they’re acting so suspicious?
“Unwritten rule... What’s that? Don’t use such complicated words with me!” With that, I charged forward and plowed right through them.
“W-Wait...!”
“Y-You can’t—”

Ultimately, all they could do was watch as I broke through their formation. And as soon as I barreled past them, I ran into about fifteen other adventurers who were gathered by the wall. They all flinched when they saw me like they’d just been caught doing something wrong.
A heavy silence filled the air.
“What’s all the fuss over here about... huh?” A man suddenly stuck his head out of a very small crack in the wall, and his eyes went wide as they met mine. “U-Uhhh... you’re...?”
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel. Are you the captain here?”
“That’s right, but...”
“What’s in there?”
“Oh, uh... th-there’s nothing here...”
“Hey. That doesn’t seem to be true.”
As I grinned at him, he screwed his eyes shut and shouted, “W-We found this place first!”
Well, gosh, that made it sound like we were the bad guys here.
“So, you found this place first...”
“Yes. And stealing the achievements of other adventurers will damage your reputation—”
“Did the adventurers you ran into earlier tell you the same thing?”
“...What? Wh-what do you mean—?”
Exactly what I said.
“Ow! Aaargh!”
I grabbed him by the hair and plucked him out of the wall like a radish. “Your sleeves. There’s human blood on them. Whose is it?”
It hadn’t even properly dried yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 504: Age of Exploration (5)
paragraphs: Did you know the most important factor of any successful lie? It wasn’t creating a logical, sensible excuse, nor was it the time and effort you put into fostering a sense of trust with the other party.
It was your expression.
“Th-this... This is all a misunderstanding!”
How was I supposed to believe a word he was saying when he was looking at me like that?
“I j-just didn’t realize I got blood splatter on me, and...”
There were some professional liars out there who were able to control even the tiniest of muscles in their faces. Fortunately for me, this guy wasn’t one of them.
“I-I’m telling you... This is a misunderstanding—!”
“Then explain. I’ll hear out whatever it is you have to say.”
There was no need to keep beating around the bush. I called Versyl over to cast a verification spell on him.
“...This man is stronger than he looks.”

Sadly, the spell failed. Well, I sort of expected it to, anyway. This type of magic didn’t work if someone’s Mana Resistance or Spirit stat was above a certain threshold, and this clan had over twenty members. Even if I didn’t recognize their name, it would be stranger if their captain wasn’t strong enough to resist a spell like this.
“What should we do now?”
What should we do, huh? Well, there was really no point in wasting our time trying to get an honest answer out of this guy—not when there were several other witnesses present.
“Try it on that guy.”
I pointed to an archer who was giving off weak vibes. Versyl went over to him and cast the fact-checking spell once more.
“It worked.”
Yeah, I figured it would work on him. “All right, you over there.”
“Yes, Your Lordship...”
“Tell me. What happened here?”
The archer paled. His eyes darted back and forth between me and his captain, unsure of how to answer. “Uh... well, we were, uh...”
It was time to raise the whip. “Seeing as you don’t want to answer me,” I drawled, my tone ice-cold, “I’m guessing that I didn’t misunderstand?”
The captain looked toward the archer and nodded his head. “Jason, you can tell him.”
“Okay... I’ll explain, then.”

Once he had his captain’s permission, the archer finally got to talking. Listening to the story, it seemed that I did somewhat misunderstand what had happened here. To sum it up, these guys hadn’t been lying when they said they found this place first. However, shortly after, a party of six adventurers approached them, and a fight broke out.
“Were they trying to steal your accomplishments?”
“It’s not like that, but...”
“Stop skirting around the issue and tell me.”
“Well...”

It would have been better if those six adventurers hadn’t seen them at all, but unfortunately, they were quick to notice that the clan had found something. Well, that was what the clan assumed, anyway. Afraid that the party would run away and leak information about their location to someone else, the clan subdued them.
“At which point there was an incident.”
“What kind of incident?”
“While we were subduing them, they violently resisted and ended up killing one of ours first...”
As a result, a full-on battle broke out and the smaller party met their end here in the dark cave.
“What about their bodies?”
“...After taking off their equipment, we melted them with acid.”
I see. No wonder there was a strange scent in the air.
“Everything I said is true. Please believe me. They attacked us first, so—”
What is this guy saying? “If you guys had managed to capture them, would you really have let them go without a fight?”
“But we...” Perhaps the archer knew he couldn’t answer that question without lying because he quickly clammed up.
Finally, the captain, who had been silent this entire time, spoke up. “What did we do that was so wrong?”
“What?”
“Do you think those six were any better? If we were the ones with fewer numbers, they would have killed us and stolen our discovery too.”
So that was what he was so eager to say. Not that he was completely wrong, but...
“That’s why no one can blame us for this. Not even you, Baron Yandel!” their captain yelled fearlessly, clearly convinced of his own argument.
“So what you’re saying is that it’s no problem if I kill you all here, right? After all, according to your logic, no one could blame us.”
When I threw his own logic back in his face, his eyes flew open in disbelief. “But if you did that, your reputation—!”
“What? Are you going to run around spreading rumors as a ghost?”
It was then that he finally seemed to realize that Baron Yandel wasn’t as noble a man as the rumors claimed.
“Whatever,” I said, swiftly ending the conversation now that I’d heard everything they had to say. “That’s enough.”

With that done, I gathered my team for a meeting, only one item on the agenda. “What do you think we should do with these guys? Don’t let your thoughts show on your face, though. Just tell me what you think.”
“I’m for killing them.”
Erwen was the first to give her two cents, no hesitation. Following her lead, the other members began to voice their opinions as well.
“Missha, what about you?”
“I’m not sure. I guess killing them... would be better...?”
“I agree with Ms. Karlstein.”
Missha and Versyl were also on the “kill them” side. Auyen and Ainar, meanwhile, wanted to let them live.
“I’m also for keeping them alive.”
Unexpectedly, Amelia voted to let them live as well.
I couldn’t stop myself from asking, “Why?”
“If we really want to hold them accountable for their actions, it’s only right to leave this matter to the guild.”
What’s with her...? I never expected to hear such a teacher’s pet kind of answer from her, of all people.
I stared at her, completely dumbfounded, as Amelia averted her gaze. “And... I think that would be better for you.”
“...What?”
“That’s just my opinion, so take it with a grain of salt.”
“No, that’s not it. What I’m wondering is what you mean by that being the better option for me?” I asked genuinely.
Amelia mulled over my question for a moment before finally opening her mouth. “Yandel, don’t get offended and just hear me out. You are very unstable right now.”
“...Unstable?”

“Have they hurt you? Did they try to kill you? No, they haven’t. And it’s not like they will pose any threat to you in the future if we let them live. Yet, as we speak, you’re still looking for a justification to kill them.”
So that was how she felt. Still, it wasn’t like I was some sort of savage out for blood or something. “Emily, I think we’re on different pages here. I’m not—”
“Am I wrong?”
But I’m really not trying to kill them for the hell of it.
However, when I met Amelia’s eyes to tell her that, I found I couldn’t get a single word out. The look in them wasn’t one of discussion or criticism. The only thing I found there was sincere worry.
“...I guess, in the end, there are three of us in favor of killing them and three of us in favor of keeping them alive,” she summarized. “So, Yandel. The choice is yours.”
What was I supposed to do?
To kill them or keep them alive... I never thought I’d have to agonize over a problem like this for so long.
But in the end...

It was probably because of what Amelia said. After hearing her out, I also began to feel a prickle of worry for Hansu Lee, the regular guy who had been trapped in the body of a warrior and forced to fight, to kill, for years to survive.
“You, the archer.”
I asked him one last thing. “Does anyone in your clan, including you, have any experience plundering?”
“...No, we don’t. We’re not that kind of clan. This time it’s just... Everyone was blinded by greed. We weren’t in our right minds for a moment.”
“He’s telling the truth.”
So that was that.

“Versyl, get their testimonies one more time and make sure to use a recording crystal when you do it. Emily, search through their belongings for the victims’ ID cards. And make sure to grab anything that should be submitted to the guild as evidence.”
“That means...”
“We will leave it to the guild to judge whether or not you are considered plunderers.”
This was an annoying and troublesome way to handle things. Even though that was my immediate thought, after making my decision and getting to work, everything went smoothly.
“Don’t get into any other trouble until the labyrinth closes. The guild will take over and investigate your actions during this expedition.”
“Of—Of course!”
All right, then that was the end of that. “So, what did you find inside?”
“Th-there’s a stone inside.”
“A stone?”

It would be quicker to just see it myself. While Amelia and Versyl took care of gathering testimonies and evidence, I approached the wall. The crack in it was so small, I had no hope of crawling through it.
Why does it feel like they’re discriminating against barbarians?
With that thought in mind, I slammed my hammer into the wall.
Boom! Crash!
Chunks of rock fell to the floor in a heap as I punched another hole through it. After a few more strikes, it eventually collapsed entirely, revealing a hidden path.
“Oh! It looks just like the portal stone!”
“How interesting.”
“Then will it also open a portal if we touch it?”
At the end of the path was a large stone about ten yards away. I immediately approached it and reached my hand out to touch it, but no portal opened.
Yeah, I had a feeling we found it too easy. Then does that mean there are special activation conditions?
Still, this at least seemed like the right place. After all, there wasn’t originally a secret area like this in the Crystal Cave. Not only that, but the broken walls were also not reforming.

That was precisely why the most fundamental strategy for searching for a hidden feature was destroying everything. If you broke something and it didn’t restore itself, then there was a high chance that you found an Easter egg.
“Have you found anything?”
“Not yet...”
“I see.”
Once Amelia and Versyl finished gathering evidence and testimonies, they joined the rest of us inside to search around. The clan had apparently scampered off the minute they were done.
“I-Is it really okay to just let them go?”
“Yeah. I told them to not cause any more trouble.”
“But are you really okay with that?” Versyl asked cautiously. “They might spread information.”
That was true. Actually, I’d also thought it would be cleaner to just kill them at the time, but... “It doesn’t matter even if they do.”
“It doesn’t matter?”

“A random clan was able to find this place before the third day. That means it wasn’t all that impressive a discovery in the first place. They were wrong to think it was such a valuable piece of information. It’s only a matter of time before everyone else finds this place too.”
“That... makes sense.”
“So stop worrying about it. And Versyl, come over here. I want to see if you can detect any magic around here. Something might be hidden.”
“Of course.”
We quickly finished a cursory magical search but unfortunately wound up empty-handed.
“Mr. Yandel, I think it would be better to get going. I don’t think there is anything to be found—”
“Bjorn!” Ainar shouted, interrupting Versyl. “Something is written over here!”
Suddenly, a clue was discovered in a completely unexpected place. Ainar, who was digging at the ground around the stone, had revealed some words hidden at its base.
“Good find.”
“Haha! A trained warrior’s intuition is no different than magic. That’s one of the many reasons why barbarians are the superior race!”
I squatted down to read the text, ignoring Ainar’s nonsense.
“It’s in the ancient language...”
“That’s fine,” I said, distracted. “I can read it.”
“Y-You can read that...?”
Oh, didn’t I tell them? I guess it would be faster to just show them.

I quickly read the ancient language that was written on the ground around the stone aloud. “One star, one sun, one moon. Every creature that exists here on this land is the same when you look at them from above. And I will look up at you.”
As soon as I finished reading it, twin expressions of disquiet appeared on Erwen and Versyl’s faces.
“Mr. Yandel, this...”
“It’s the same inscription from back then, right?”
“Yeah.”
It was the same text we’d seen written on the Witch’s Altar.
Sadly, Ainar didn’t seem to remember. “...What? Where did you hear that before? What are you talking about?”
“Forget it.”

We continued to dig around the stone to see if there was anything else, but there was nothing. Deciding that we’d found everything there was to find in there, we quickly covered the text with dirt again and exited through the broken wall.
“This isn’t good. I can’t believe after all of that, we didn’t find a single clue.”
Amelia seemed disheartened, but I didn’t feel that way at all. What did she mean we hadn’t found a single clue?
“One star, one sun, one moon.”
It was practically feeding us the answer.
“We need to head to the second floor.”
If we hurried, we might even be able to enter the hidden area before the labyrinth closed.

chapters.title: Chapter 505: Basement Floor One (1)
paragraphs: Stomp, stomp, stomp.
She was running through the cave with her new teammates, staring at their backs after offering the excuse that she’d watch the rear.
“Mister, please explain. Why are we going up to the second floor?”
There was a yawning gap between them, one that prevented her from getting too close to them. Still, she could overcome it in a second if she tried. Yeah, she was sure she could.
However...
“Not just anywhere on the second floor. We’re going to the Goblin Forest.”
Why did she suddenly feel like she could spend the rest of her life trying and still never be able to close that gap?
I thought for sure it would happen...that over time, things would eventually return to normal...
She’d been trying not to get impatient, but her confidence was starting to fade as the days went by. The interaction she witnessed just a little while ago spoke for itself.
“I think that would be better for you.”
“Yandel, don’t get offended and just hear me out. You are very unstable right now.”
As she watched those words get through to Bjorn, the first thought she had was, I should have been the one to say that.
She had lost.

It had never even occurred to her to say something like that. The answer she gave was the one she figured Bjorn wanted to hear. But after so many years, she wasn’t even sure what “what Bjorn wanted to hear” was anymore.
“I’m not sure. I guess killing them... would be better...?”

She hadn’t voiced her own opinion. No, she’d merely looked around the room and gave the answer she thought most of them would agree with. Now that she thought about it, things had always been like this. She’d never questioned Bjorn or advised him on what path he should take. She’d resolved to follow him silently, no matter what he did. That was all she had ever done.
Amelia Rainwales...

The fundamental difference between the two of them was palpable. She looked at Amelia and realized that she must be what people meant when they talked about a true companion. It wasn’t that Missha’s position in the group had disappeared while she was gone. She’d always felt like she could come back and reclaim her spot at any moment, but now she was realizing it hadn’t been all that special a spot in the first place.
“...Are you all right?” Amelia slowed down to join her in the back, falling into step next to her. “You’ve looked off for a while now.”
As she looked up at Amelia, she felt her teeth clench despite herself. “Don’t worry about me. I’m all right.”
It didn’t matter whether or not she still had a place here. Nor did it matter if he looked right through her.
“If you don’t, Bjorn Yandel will die.”
Because she had something more important to take care of.

About an hour after Day Three began, the entire cave began to shake as the crystals glowed red. That meant that the Lord of Terror, Dreadfear, had been summoned somewhere, likely the result of one of the eight raid requests that had already been submitted to the Adventurers’ Guild. The issue was how early they were summoning it.
It’s only been an hour and it’s already here. Just how many people are waiting for their turn to take it on?

Of course, none of that mattered to us since we had our sights set on something else. Still, the eight teams who had received a raid permit were likely thinking along the same lines. In fact, it was safe to say that most adventurers had considered the very same possibility.
What would happen if they defeated the Lord of Terror, Dreadfear, now?

While planning this month’s quest, I also considered the possibility that the key to accessing the hidden area might be defeating him again. Unfortunately, I couldn’t apply since the available slots were already all filled.
However, if the Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, was the actual key, then we would have to give up on reaching the hidden area entirely for now.
...They all have the common sense not to summon Berzak, though, right?

I wanted to believe that, but I wasn’t all that reassured. At a glance, there were dozens of parties all over the Crystal Cave, not just the eight who had applied for a raid permit. If even just one of those extra teams got a little greedy, the results would be catastrophic.
That doesn’t matter. We have our own mission to focus on.
It wasn’t like I could personally persuade every adventurer in the cave not to get greedy and summon Berzak, so in the end, we picked up the pace and got out of there.
[You have entered the Goblin Forest on the second floor.]
We quickly made our way to the second floor and then the third. Since we were running as fast as we could, we were able to make it up there before the end of the third day.
[You have entered the Pilgrim’s Path on the third floor.]

It was a massive floor with over ten different areas. After making our way through Goblin Forest, we appeared in Greentail Marsh, which was inhabited by Lizardmen. From there, we moved to one of the neighboring zones, Sculpture Temple.

This area was full of rubble from the ruins of collapsed stone buildings. It looked similar to the Panthelion Ruins on the seventh floor’s Dark Continent, but there were also some differences here and there. One of which was that this place was full of sculptures, though they were all broken from the neck up.
“This place gives me the creeps every time.”
“At least no one else ever comes here.”
Sculpture Temple was the most unpopular area on the third floor by an overwhelming margin. First off, there was only one type of monster that spawned here.
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
Unnamed Sculptures were rank-seven monsters that looked similar to Stone Golems. The main difference was that they were much smaller in size, more humanoid, and rather agile.
[The Unnamed Sculpture has cast Unanswered Prayer.]

The skill that came with their essence was also famous for being absolute trash. When a player used it, it consumed an insane amount of MP and failed pretty much every single time, not doing a thing. That said, when these things used it, they had a much higher chance of success.
[The Unnamed Sculpture has been imbued with great power.]

If the prayer succeeded, the user temporarily gained a random essence of rank-five or lower. Because of that, they were abnormally difficult to fight for rank-seven monsters. Well, actually, they were more tricky than they were difficult. There were numerous variables to take into account since predicting what type of skills they would get was impossible. Because of that, no adventurer ever chose to hunt or even pass by here. Why would they when even the essence drop was trash? If your goal was to get EXP, you could just kill one that was roaming the outskirts and then skip this area entirely.
What’s more, it’s totally out of the way.

If you wanted to go to the fourth floor, it was much easier to go down another route. As a result, no one ever took this path, to the point that most adventurers had never even laid eyes on this place.
The item drops aren’t that bad, though...

This place’s main selling point lay in the items the monsters dropped. If you used Distortion, you were sometimes able to get your hands on a Magic Power Crystal, which could be sold for a hefty price. Even then, though, it was more efficient to mine them on the fifth floor. As such, no one ever came here for those.
But we were here for another item that had a chance of dropping.
“Everyone, let’s get moving.”
Feeling short on time, I ordered everyone to go hunting.
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
Since we had more than enough combat power right now, I had our wizard focus on using distortion magic on the monsters’ remains to see what items dropped.
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
[You have killed an...]
I smashed every sculpture I saw to pieces. Then, since that was still taking too long, I ordered the team to fan out and attract the attention of the monsters so we could lure them all together.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”

Monsters, unlike humans, went into a frenzy and immediately charged when they saw someone with a high Threat Level. Using that to our advantage, we were able to gather them in one area and defeat a bunch in one fell swoop. Then we had Versyl cast distortion magic to grab the items. Once more started spawning, we ran around to attract their aggro and corralled them back to a specific spot again. Divvying our team up that way allowed us to swiftly take down countless monsters.
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
[You have killed an Unnamed Sculpture.]
[You have killed an...]
We continued to hunt with single-minded focus for a while, not taking any breaks. Only after we had collected six Magic Power Crystals were we able to finally find what we came here for.
“Bjooorn! Is this what you’re looking for?”
Ainar held up a small piece of rubble with a unique pattern on it.
[You have acquired an Unnamed Fragment.]
It was a drawing of the sun.

Unnamed Fragment was an item that had a certain probability of dropping when you cast Distortion on Unnamed Sculptures. It was unique in that you couldn’t have more than one in your inventory, and they randomly dropped with one of three patterns carved into their surface. It was also impossible to take one back to the city.
Since we found the sun, all that’s left is the moon and star.

I always had a feeling there was some secret behind these things, and I’d tried everything I could think of in the game to figure out what it was. To think that I’d finally found what they were for...
“Is this what you were looking for, Mr. Yandel?”
“That makes sense. From what I’ve heard, these appear in a sun, star, and moon pattern.”
“...I can’t say for sure, but it seems likely. Time is tight, but we might just make it.”

Getting to the third floor, defeating enough monsters to acquire these three specific items, and then making your way down to the first floor before it closed—this was a pretty difficult feat to achieve, but not impossible. In our case, however, we were cutting it close since we’d wasted more than two days on the first floor. We would have had a better chance of pulling it off if we had run straight to the third floor from the start.
“I think we’ll be able to do it next time,” Versyl offered in consolation.
I had to concede that it seemed very unlikely that we’d make it to the hidden area this time around. It took eight hours alone for just one of these Unnamed Fragments to drop.
This means if we want to find the other two, it’s going to take sixteen hours.

Simple math suggested that we would run out of time, and that was also under the assumption that none of the others that dropped were duplicates of ones we already had. Still, how were we supposed to go any faster? Even while going all out and running around the entire area aggroing every monster we saw, getting even one took us eight hours.
But more than that, at this rate, Versyl will run out of MP and won’t be able to use Distortion anymore.
Damn, was this too much to try to pull off this month? I thought it might be possible if we went as fast as we could, but maybe that was optimistic of—
“Oh! Bjorn! Another one!”
Huh?
I blinked down at the stone Ainar placed in my hand, completely dumbfounded.
[You have acquired an Unnamed Fragment.]
It had a star pattern on it. In other words, we now had an extra eight hours to find the last moon pattern piece.
What? How did Ainar randomly find this thing?
Ainar had Beginner’s Luck, yes, but that shouldn’t affect the drop rate of items—only essences. Whatever the case, it was best to take advantage of her inexplicable fortune while we could.
“Change of plans,” I called out. “From now on, Ainar will be in charge of defeating the monsters. Everyone else’s job is to run around and aggro them for her.”
Even if it wasn’t as efficient as before, I decided to leave Ainar in charge of defeating all the monsters. And lo and behold, about five hours later...
[You have acquired an Unnamed Fragment.]
“A moon pattern...”
It was time to admit it. “Ainar.”
“You can compliment me as much as you want!” she preened.
“You’re right! Barbarians are the superior race!”
“Woooooo!”
Instead of shutting down Ainar’s antics, I cast Giantization and threw her high in the air.
“Ahahaha!” As expected, Ainar was happier than ever.
Thud!
All right, that was enough playing around. With the Unnamed Fragments in hand, I quickly led the team back the way we came.
Day Five, Day Six, Day Seven...

Going back down the floors was even harder than climbing up in the first place. However, thanks to Ainar, we had extra time to camp, rest, and recover our stamina. As a result, we were able to reach the middle of the Goblin Forest by the afternoon of the seventh day. There, we stepped into the field housing the portal that led back down to the first floor’s Crystal Cave. This was the very same field we once fought a fierce battle against three of Noark’s top warriors, who had been guarding the entrance.
“...What is this?”

However, now, the place was packed with adventurers I didn’t recognize at all. There looked to be well over a hundred of them, and going by appearances alone, they didn’t seem like adventurers who had given up for the month and were heading back to the first floor to catch the labyrinth closure back home. If that were the case, they’d be going through the portal instead of just standing in front of it. They also didn’t look like adventurers who had only just managed to find their way out of the Crystal Cave.
“Priest! Is there a priest?! Please help!”
“Drink this!”
What the hell was going on? As I approached the portal, countless adventurers recognized me and began to whisper to each other.
“Bjorn Yandel...?”
“Wasn’t he on the first floor too?”

The crowd seemed confused to see me coming from behind them and not from the portal. I sighed. I’d wanted to sneak back to the first floor unnoticed instead of attracting attention like this, but since that was no longer an option, I called on someone who looked rather talkative to explain things.
“Hey! What’s going on?”
His response was immediate. “Berzak! That demon has appeared!”
Hah, yeah, I figured something like this might happen.
No wonder we’d gotten so strangely lucky earlier.

chapters.title: Chapter 506: Basement Floor One (2)
paragraphs: The Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, was a hidden boss who only appeared after the Lord of Terror was killed nine times.
I had a feeling this might happen... but to think it actually did.

I immediately grilled the adventurers gathered around the portal about the most important information. According to them, Berzak appeared around an hour ago. Because many of the adventurers on the first floor were worried this exact thing might happen, there thankfully weren’t that many casualties. In fact, nearly all of them realized how dangerous things were getting by the fourth day and quickly headed to the second floor.
“But all the new adventurers wouldn’t have had the skills to make it to the second floor alone.”
“Yes, that’s correct. Which is why we teamed up with ten other clans to find all the adventurers scattered around the first floor and help bring them to the second floor.”

While there were some people out there willing to summon the Lord of the Floor without sparing a second thought for all the lives they were endangering, there were conversely always those out there who would do whatever they could to save those lives even when there was nothing to gain. The majority of the adventurers lingering around the portal turned out to be ones who had been in the middle of escorting people to the second floor when Berzak appeared.
“So there’s no need to worry too much, Your Lordship. On the sixth day, we scoped out the entirety of the first floor and weren’t able to find any stragglers.”
So they had everything covered...
“Great work. I’m sure it wasn’t easy.”
“Easy or difficult, someone had to do it. And it’s nothing compared to what you’ve accomplished, Your Lordship.”

As he looked up at me, eyes full of respect, I felt my conscience start to eat away at me. After all, I wasn’t that great a person. I myself had had a bad feeling that Berzak might show up, yet I still ran off to the third floor in pursuit of my own goal.
Suddenly, one of the adventurers spoke up. “But since you came from that direction, does that mean you weren’t rescuing people like we were?”
Before I could answer him, the other adventurers burst into exclamations, quickly defending me.
“Hey, try using your brain! Why do you think he came from over there?!”
“Then... Not only did he help people get to the second floor, but he also personally guided them around to help them get used to it?”
“Unlike us, Baron Yandel doesn’t need recognition from the Guild... To think he’s still willing to go so far to help others.”
“I’m embarrassed. Actually, I was secretly hoping that the guild would recognize us for helping the new adventurers when Berzak appeared.”
Uh...
I just laughed awkwardly, keeping my mouth shut.
[Your Reputation has risen by +1.]
[Your Reputation has risen by +1.]
[Your Reputation has risen by +1.]
[Your Reputation has...]
I didn’t really care about my Reputation stat rising, but at least this misunderstanding would help provide me an alibi.
Now if we head down to unlock the hidden area, there won’t be many people questioning our whereabouts.
The feeling of guilt only grew worse, but I was able to push through it. After all, if I could bear the pain of pouring potions over my torn flesh, I could bear this.
“Well then,” I hedged, “we have something to discuss amongst ourselves for a bit.”
“Oh, of course! If you have any questions, please feel free to ask us!”

After explaining the situation to me, the group of adventurers then left us alone so we could have a team meeting. Given what was going on, I was curious what my party members were thinking. The first person I asked was Amelia, who was essentially our clan’s anchor and voice of reason. “Emily, what do you think we should do now?”
“...It’s dangerous to go any further. But at the same time, it would be a shame to give up like this.”

“Then do you think we should still give it a shot?” It would take us a little more than an hour to sprint to the portal stone from the Goblin Forest’s portal. Despite Berzak’s presence, we still had time to make it there...
Amelia’s voice sliced through my thoughts. “It depends on how certain you are that this will work. If you’re confident that this method will open the hidden area, then it might be worth a try.”

Her concerns were completely understandable. Even if we managed to make it there, if the portal to the new area didn’t work, we would have to run all the way back if we wanted to keep exploring this month. And given that that meant we’d be running around on the first floor for twice as long, the chances of us encountering Berzak would increase proportionately.
“So you’re saying that if I’m confident that this will open the portal, then you’re in favor of giving it a shot.”
“Yes, essentially.”
Okay, so Amelia is tentatively in favor...
I then heard out everyone else.
“Even if it doesn’t work, I still think it’s worth a shot. We’re not the same as we used to be.”
“I agree with the elf. We only went to the third floor this time. It’d be a waste to give up now!”
“I feel the same. Whether it works or not, there is still value in using this opportunity to at least test the method out. If it doesn’t work, we can avoid wasting time next month.”
Erwen, Ainar, and Versyl were in favor.
“I-I... will follow your lead, Captain.”
“I understand how you feel, but I want to hear your opinion. No one will judge you for it. You’re a member of this clan too, right?”
It seemed calling him a proper clan member swayed him. Auyen, who hesitated at first, eventually opened his mouth to carefully voice his opinion.
“Then... Then I’m against it. Berzak... That monster has killed thousands... If you or any of your women were to get hurt, that would be a great loss for future generations—”
What the hell was he rambling on about?
“Then you’re against it?” I pressed.
“Yes... that’s right. That’s just my opinion, though, so please take it with a grain of salt.”

Then that was three yesses, one conditional yes, and one no. If we wanted to go by majority vote, there was no need to discuss this any further. However, since there was one last member who hadn’t weighed in, I decided to ask her as well.

“Me? Um... I-I... So...” Missha, who had been acting strange this whole expedition, stuttered through her answer. I didn’t know why, but she was talking like she used to in the old days. “U-um, I-I think anything is fine. I-It is dangerous, b-but... if the portal does open, th-then that would be g-good. And e-even if it d-doesn’t, it would s-still be good that we tried... S-So what I-I’m saying is that either way is good? B-But, um... th-that’s just how I feel...”
What is she even trying to say? I just asked her to give me her opinion?
“Then does that mean you don’t want to vote?”
“Th-that’s not it...”
“Then what? You can be honest. I want to hear what you think.”

When I told her to stop beating around the bush and tell me how she really felt, Missha avoided eye contact and finally voiced her opinion. “Th-then I think it would be better to try... a-as long as you’re sure it will work...”
Simply put, Missha was also a conditional yes. Still, I didn’t know why she kept glancing at Amelia while answering me.
...Is that really her own opinion?
For some reason, I doubted it was, but I decided not to push right now. After all, she probably needed some time to get used to all of us.
“All right. Since there are three votes in favor, it’s decided.”
“Huh? What about your vote, Mr. Yandel?”
“What the clan wants, I want.”

On the other hand, that also meant that what I wanted was what the clan wanted. After all, the clan leader’s vote was worth seven. Ah, though, when we only had six members my vote was only worth six. It was worth seven today because there were seven of us. Anyway, moving on...
“All right, then let’s go.”
Through that portal, a mysterious world full of treasure awaited us.
...Probably.
[You have entered the Crystal Cave on the first floor.]
In reality, on the other side of the portal was the Crystal Cave. Since we were in the dark zone, where the crystals didn’t light up, nothing felt particularly different at first.
Fwoosh!
However, the moment I lit the torch attached to my helmet, we could all see a thick, dark fog surrounding us, a visual indication that something was wrong.

[Field Effect – Abyssal Fog has activated. All active skills have been disabled. Mana Efficiency has been reduced to 25%. Any monsters exposed to the Fog of the Abyss will evolve into superior beings.]
Ha, it’s been a while since I’ve seen this fog. I even thought it would be my tomb at one point. I never imagined I would ever willingly step foot in it again.
“What are you doing? Stick close. I’ll take care of the traps in the way, so make sure to stay behind me.”

I ran straight forward, taking the lead. This was a tactic only I could use as both a tank and scout. I did the same that day as well, as it was impossible to detect an Abyssal Goblin’s traps with the naked eye or with magic.
Snap.
A moment later, I heard the sound of something snapping as my foot hit the floor.
[You have stepped on a Random Trap.]
Once one of these traps was triggered, a random skill of rank-five or lower would activate.
Fwoosh!
Hm, judging by the damage and the type of attack, this must be the rank-six skill Tail Flame.
“Yandel, are you okay?”
To be honest, it stung quite a bit. Compared to back then, my overall stats were much higher. But there was one stat that had gotten lower.
Hah, I really need to raise my Mana Resistance soon.

When I erased the Manticore essence, I also lost a lot of my Mana Resistance. Giantization helped me make up for its absence, but I couldn’t use it right now since my active skills were sealed by the fog.
“Don’t worry about me. We’re only an hour away.”
I had no choice but to grin and bear it.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
Invoking the protection of my ancestral god, I ran through the passageway full of hidden traps. If nothing else, there was one major improvement from last time.
Snap!

The traps that caused physical damage barely hurt at all. In fact, they did little more than tingle. Because of that, the only attacks that were actually painful and that I was wary of were the magic-related ones.
Snap! Snap! Snap!

I plowed forward, activating so many traps that I lost count. Even though I wasn’t thirsty, I periodically made sure to chug down potions. However, unlike before, my body didn’t miraculously recover. The higher your stats were, the less effective potions became.
[Your health has dropped below 50%.]
After about forty minutes, one of my passives kicked in.
[All Resistance and Resilience stats have increased due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]

With my passive skill activated, it became a lot easier to handle the pain. Because of that, I could speed up even more. And as I did, I could hear my teammates’ footsteps pick up behind me, along with quiet whispering.
“So on that day, he... I can see why he became so famous.”
“I know. I’ve heard people talk about it, but... I didn’t know it was like this...”
I could sense Amelia and Versyl, who had only experienced what I did that day through word of mouth, looking at me in utter awe and respect.
Well, I know it’s a compliment, but...
