To be honest, it was a bit embarrassing. Back then, I did what I did because it was my only hope of survival. More importantly, I knew I could do so.
“A-All of you have lost it! You think others will recognize you for this?! Huh? As heroes?”
“Goddamn it... I’m still going. After all, someone has to do it.”

Unlike those who had stood on the front lines with me and died stepping on these traps, I knew from the start that I didn’t have to worry about that possibility. It was only because I knew I had the skills and stats I needed as a tank to take those hits that I was able to run forward without hesitation—just as I was doing now.
[Your health has dropped below 40%.]
My head started to spin, but I forced my eyes open even though they were beginning to lose focus. After all, the Abyssal Goblins weren’t the only things we had to look out for.
Berzak is... Fortunately, it seems to be somewhere far away from us.
We hadn’t encountered a Watcher of the Abyss, a monster that acted as Berzak’s eyes, yet. That meant he wasn’t anywhere near us right now.

“Excuse me, but... why didn’t we wait to come down here an hour before the labyrinth closed?” Versyl suddenly said, a thought abruptly occurring to her. “We could have left just enough time to test this method out, and then if it didn’t work, we could have safely returned to the city when the labyrinth closed.”
Her point was valid, but I had actually already considered it before we left the second floor. If we’d done that, we wouldn’t have had to worry about potentially making a round trip. However...

“If we did that, things would have been even more difficult. At that point, there would be barely anyone left alive on the first floor, meaning we would undoubtedly run into Berzak. I’m sure Yandel considered that before making his decision.”
So Amelia had figured it out too. I hadn’t made the call to come down here without thinking at least that far ahead.
[Your health has dropped below 30%.]
[Your health has dropped below 20%. All of your Resistance and Resilience stats have maxed out due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]

Eventually, my passive skill fully kicked in, allowing me to reap the maximum benefit. Thanks to that, we were able to safely make it to our destination after running for a little over an hour. I’d lost a lot of HP, but aside from that, there were no major hiccups. Best of all, we didn’t run into Berzak, and—excluding myself—every member of our clan was, without exaggeration, in perfect condition.
Shit.
However smooth the process, though, there was no guarantee that the results would be as desired. For us, a new problem reared its ugly head the moment we arrived at our destination.
“...Hey, is that Baron Yandel?”
“...I-It’s really him! He’s here with his teammates!”
“Then did he find a way to open the door?”
What the hell? Why were there so many people here? At a glance, it seemed like there were dozens.

I’d run all the way here with near-absolute confidence that this place would be deserted. Of course, it was true that this spot had already been discovered by a smallish clan on day three, and I had smashed the wall open, making it even easier to find. I never expected that it would remain a secret or anything, but still, why were there so many people loitering here right now of all times?
What are they all doing down here when Berzak’s on the loose?
I tried to hide my bafflement as I called out to the man closest to me. “You over there. The baldy.”
“M-Me?”
“What are you all doing here?”

The man tilted his head, confused by the question. “We’re waiting for this portal to open? We figured it might open if someone defeats the Lord of the Abyss, or maybe right before the labyrinth closes.”
“...But what if Berzak comes here?”
“Well, of course we’re all willing to take the risk! This is a new, unexplored area, after all!”
His plain, matter-of-fact answer rendered me speechless.
“Surely you feel the same way, Baron Yandel... Isn’t this what being an adventurer is all about?”
For the first time in my new life, I was skeptical of my chosen profession. I knew there were plenty of adventurers out there with a few screws loose, of course, but...
“Anyway, if you don’t mind us asking... did you happen to find a way to open the portal?”
I’d had no idea there were quite this many nutjobs.

chapters.title: Chapter 507: Basement Floor One (3)
paragraphs: If Berzak found us, 70 percent of us would meet our end, and that was assuming we all ran away the moment we spotted him. If we tried to fight him, then this would be the last expedition any of us ever went on.
These bastards... do they not value their lives at all?

The more I stared at them, the less I understood. With every passing second, Berzak was probably drawing nearer. Yet instead of running up to the second floor, more people were actively gathering here.
“...Just as I thought, other people had the same idea as us.”

A group of five adventurers stumbled toward us, in miserable shape. They seemed to have struggled to wade through all the traps scattered around the first floor. But the moment they spotted the crowd in the hidden room, they had only one question.
“Where’s the portal? Did it open?”
“Why didn’t it open? The Lord of Terror has already been defeated nine times and Berzak was summoned!”

Was there something wrong with these people? Why had they bet everything on the off chance that the portal might open instead of going up to the second floor? They weren’t even one of the parties who had been waiting here since Berzak first appeared. They had been somewhere else and had purposely forced their way through all those traps to get here rather than heading toward safety.
Likely noticing my obvious disbelief, Amelia came up beside me. “Yandel... what should we do?”
“I don’t know. I think I might have underestimated how tenacious and greedy adventurers could be.”
“It’s not just adventurers. All humans are like that. Regardless of time or place.”

These days, talking to Amelia felt a lot like talking to a wise sage. Even so, her words of wisdom didn’t help me out much this time. I needed advice on what we should do now. If she had expected something like this to happen, then she should have warned me in advance.
I let out a slow sigh.
Let’s calm down.
This situation was far from ideal, but there was no need to take it out on my teammates for no reason. Instead, my time was best spent trying to come up with a solution.
The biggest issue is that it’s going to be hard to open the portal discreetly with so many eyes on us...
If we opened the portal now, everyone here would obviously hitch a free ride. Just imagining how much loot they would steal from us gave me a headache.
But more importantly, word will spread.

Even if the number of people who could go through the portal was limited and only my teammates and I got inside, rumors about us getting into the hidden area would spread throughout the city. That meant that from next month onward, there would be countless people tailing us and watching our every move. Since I wanted us to quietly reap the rewards on our own, I’d prefer to avoid that outcome. However...
“I-It’s a Watcher of the Abyss! Berzak! That monster is here...!”

Just as I thought, the world wasn’t going to let me sit back, watch things play out, and brainstorm solutions. The moment you saw a Watcher of the Abyss, that meant Berzak was definitely coming for you.
“Ack! G-Get away!”
“D-Don’t get near me!”
“Aaaaaagh!”

As the Watcher of the Abyss floated closer, the group of adventurers devolved into panic. Didn’t they know acting like that would only aggro it more? It was ridiculous to watch a bunch of grown adults tremble in fear at the sight of a Watcher of the Abyss, a useless rank-nine monster, merely approaching them.
Splurt!
Poison shot out of its eyeball like a water gun.
“Argh! Get out of my way! Get out of my way!”

What a joke. These adventurers looked like they could easily be sixth-floor veterans or higher, so why were they freaking out so much about a rank-nine monster? Was this some kind of slapstick comedy?
Smack!
As I was quietly watching the amusing chaos unfold from a few steps away, one of the panicking adventurers accidentally slapped the Watcher of the Abyss.
Shaaaaaa!
It immediately burst into a cluster of lights, then disappeared.
A heavy silence quickly replaced the panic in the cave.
“Ahhh... n-no... wait...”
At the realization that he’d just killed a Watcher of the Abyss, the adventurer began to tremble. The situation had officially gone from bad to worse.
“H-Hurry up! Get away from us!”
People started to yell at the adventurer who killed it, trying to drive him away.
“If you stay here, Berzak will come! Run to the second floor before it catches you!”
“B-But... I-I can’t get there on my own...”
“Then why did you kill it?!”
Are all adventurers unfeeling bastards or something?
“Stop it.” Unable to watch this go on any longer, I stepped forward.
“Baron Yandel...?”
“Your Lordship! We’ll all die if this guy stays with us! We need him to leave as soon as possible!”

That logic was ridiculous. Were they trying to argue that we’d be fine as long as we got rid of him? The fact that the Watcher of the Abyss saw us meant that Berzak was going to come for us no matter what we did.

Whatever the case, I now had a firm grasp of the situation. It didn’t matter how much longer we waited around for them to change their minds—none of these people were willing to go to the second floor.
“I told you to stop.”
“But—!”
“I’m going to open the portal now.”
It was time to move on to Plan B.
As soon as I said that, the man quickly scrambled out of my way. The crowd of adventurers inside the hidden alcove near the stone also parted so I could walk through.
“All of you, stay out here for now.”
“...Pardon? O-Oh! Of course! We won’t get in the way. Everyone, come over here!”

They were all clearly shocked to hear me suddenly declare that I was going to open the portal, but thankfully, they were rather obliging given the situation and quickly vacated the small stone room for us.
“Versyl, can you create a curtain so they can’t see what happens in here? Make sure they can’t hear us either.”
Versyl quickly cast some spells, creating a barrier to ensure that no one could spy on us from the outside. With that, we were able to secure some manner of privacy.
Before I could get started, Amelia came over and stopped me. “Yandel, are you sure about this?”
“There’s no other choice. It’s not like we can let them all die here.”
“If we wait a bit longer, they might all head back up to the second floor on their own. No matter how reckless they may seem, they have to value their lives.”
Well, it’s not like that exact thought didn’t cross my mind, but...
“Unfortunately, I really don’t think they’re going to give up.”
“...You’re unexpectedly calm about this.”
Does it seem that way...?

It was more that I’d already given up on the possibility of them doing the reasonable thing and getting out of there. In truth, just imagining how many freeloaders were going to tag along once I opened this portal made my stomach churn and my head hurt.
Even so, I said, “If this method doesn’t work, we’ll need time to escape to the second floor. It’d be dangerous to wait any longer.”
Amelia seemed persuaded by my logic.
I hurried over to the portal stone with the fragments we found on the third floor. “Versyl. Cast the Binding spell on the six of us, excluding you.”
“What?”
“If the portal opens, there’s a high chance that there will be a reward for being the first to open it.”
“I see...!” Quickly catching on, Versyl cast the Binding spell without a word of complaint. It wasn’t like wizards needed experience points like we did. “All done.”
All right... then it’s time. Please work.
I swallowed, my mouth suddenly dry, as I touched the three carved fragments to the portal stone.
Fwoooooo!
A sudden breeze kicked up around the stone as a large burst of color blinded us.
[You are the first to open a portal to this hidden area. EXP +99]
Yeah, there we go.

The portal had opened. One that led to a mysterious new area of the labyrinth that no one in the history of Rafdonia had ever stepped foot in. Maybe that was why my mind was suddenly cluttered with all sorts of concerns. Still, I decided to stick to my guns and carry out the plan I’d already settled on.
“Versyl, recast the spell on us.”
“Who on?”

“You, me, and Erwen will be a part of Team One. Everyone else will be Team Two. If we go inside and the portal closes, Team Two is to immediately go up to the second floor. Do I make myself clear? And Emily, you’re in charge if that happens... got it?”

“Don’t worry. I’m sure those people outside will come to their senses if they see the portal close. But if they don’t, I’ll make sure to convince them all to work together so we can safely make our way to the second floor.”
“All right... And if you enter the portal and start in a different location than us, make sure to take care of each other. Got it?”
“I’ll do my best.”
Those were all the precautions I could possibly take.
“Then we’ll go in first.” With that, I forced myself to step forward and into the portal.
Fwoosh!
A bright light blinded me, even as I screwed my eyes shut. I felt like my body was floating as my vision slowly returned.
[You have entered the Archives on Basement Floor One.]
[First Achievement Unlocked: The great feat you have accomplished here will be engraved in the Stone of Honor, recorded forevermore.]
Since I was used to traveling via the portal by now, I was able to find my balance and safely land on my feet.
Thud!

I whipped my shield up to protect my upper body as I quickly scanned the area. The ground I was standing on was covered in tiles, and I could only see about one hundred yards ahead of me. Beyond that, however, there didn’t seem to be anything noteworthy, aside from a patch where the tiles turned into rocky terrain.
Shaaaaaa.
And was that the sound of ocean waves?
For now, there don’t seem to be any monsters around.
A burst of light overhead interrupted my assessment of the situation, bringing with it my teammates.
“W-Waaah...!”
First was the silent Erwen and outwardly shocked Versyl, who were both on Team One with me.
“Whoooa!”
Then came Ainar, who tumbled in yelling, along with Auyen, Missha, and Amelia.
...Thankfully, it seems the portal didn’t close behind the three of us.
But I only got to enjoy a moment of relief before I came to a sudden, belated realization.
“...We might not be able to get out of here.”
Just like when you entered a Rift, the portal above us was beginning to close after spitting us out.
A one-way entrance, with no way to go back where we came from...
There was something ominous about that, but I decided to think positively.
...It’s not like this really changes things.
We came from the first floor, so either way, it would have been impossible for us to return once the floor closed in a few hours.
The question is, when will this place close...?
That was the sort of information we would only be able to uncover by exploring. Still, unable to shake my lingering concerns, I walked over to Amelia.
“Emily, what were things like when you came in?”

“It was the same as when you went through. There was a slight difference in the color of the portal, but no other changes aside from that. Also, once Ms. Gowland’s barrier disappeared, the people outside rushed into the room after us.”
Hm, is that so...
“Then keep an eye on our surroundings and keep your guard up. If you notice anything, make sure to alert me. Even if it seems trivial.”
“Bjorn!” Ainar shouted, as if on cue. “I-I’m feeling strange!”
“Strange? What’s wrong?”
“Uh, my face is hot. And my heart is pounding!”
...That’s because you’re excited.
Still, I proceeded to check how my other teammates were doing as well to see if this place had any effects we had to worry about. As I did so, other adventurers started to rain down from above.
“Ohhh! A new floor! A new floor...!”
“Muahaha! My name will go down in history!”
Some of them indeed seemed to have a few screws loose, but some of them also seemed rather normal.
“Everyone, stay on alert! You can’t let your guard down! We don’t know what might come our way!”

These people grouped back up with their party members as soon as they were on solid ground. I wasn’t quite sure why, but for some reason, they all started to gather relatively close to us. Did they think they would be safer if we were nearby? I didn’t know myself, but eventually, the steady stream of adventurers stopped, and the portal in the sky blinked out of existence entirely.
“Wh-what?! Why aren’t the rest of them coming?”
“M-Mr. Zelton isn’t here yet...?”
“Kuredo! Kuredo, are you here?!”
A new piece of information was obtained. Unlike the portals that led to the other floors, this one seemed to close after certain conditions were met. But what were those conditions?
Well, I don’t think it’s some sort of a time limit...
I began to count the people present. The number of adventurers who had come in already was one, two, three, four, five, six...
Fifty-eight, fifty-nine, sixty...
I see. So the portal closed once sixty people were inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 508: Basement Floor One (4)
paragraphs: An occupancy limit of sixty people. Not only that, but once you came through the portal, there was no way for you to go back out.
While those two characteristics were definitely reminiscent of a Rift, other factors made it hard to classify this place as one.
First off, there was a portal stone.
Portal stones were used specifically to connect different floors, and we’d had to activate one in order to reach this hidden area.
What’s more, there’s never been a new hidden area that turned out to be a Rift.

Whenever the term “hidden area” was written on the Stone of Honor, it usually meant that a new floor or—in rare cases like with the Labyrinth of Larcaz—a new hidden map that was already a part of a certain floor had been unlocked.
And it’s not likely that this is just a new hidden map on the first floor.

For now, I decided to consider this place a new floor entirely since hidden maps closed at the same time that their corresponding floor did. To even open the portal to get here, we’d had to go all the way to the third floor and spend a decent amount of our time collecting Unnamed Fragments.
Considering how long it took to get there, do that, and get back, it’d take most adventurers six days to open this portal.

From a design perspective, it didn’t make sense to have a hidden map that people would only ever have a maximum of two days to explore. That was why I thought the chances of this place being a hidden map were rather low.
Then the most important question is once again when this place will close...
But we’d figure that out as the days went by.
“Versyl, are you done scoping them all out?”
“Yes.”
Before we began our full-scale expedition, I had Versyl investigate to determine how powerful the adventurers who had followed us here were.
“First,” she began, “I’ll talk about the two strongest groups. There are twenty members of the Silver Lion Clan and nineteen members of the Hektz Clan.”

“It sounds like both of them are missing members, then?” Clans normally traveled in as large a group as possible. Back when the maximum number of people able to be tied together with a single Binding spell was five, they operated in multiples of five. Now that you could make parties of six, however, each of their groups should have added up to some multiple of six.
“Yes. It seems that both of them are missing quite a few between them. Apparently, as soon as my barrier collapsed and the portal opened, everyone ran toward it in a frenzy.”
“I see. What about the rest?”
“There are two five-member parties and one team of four.”
Further investigation revealed that the four-person team was missing their leader and one of the five-person teams was down a warrior, which completely ruined their party comp.
“Is there anything else you want me to ask? They are all being cooperative right now, likely because they’re hoping to lean on us in the future.”
“No, this is more than enough,” I answered. “Thanks.”
“Oh, also...”
“Hm?”
When I tilted my head, Versyl carefully added, “All three of the smaller teams have asked if we’d be willing to protect them. It seems the other two clans are also interested in cooperating with us.”
“I understand the two clans cooperating with us, but what do the others mean by protection?”
“Nothing special. Essentially, they’re willing to do whatever we ask of them as long as we bring them along with us.”

They all greedily threw themselves in here without thinking twice, but now that they’re actually here, they must have come to their senses and realized how screwed they are. It must be even worse given that they’re missing members.
“What do you plan to do?”
“What is their average skill level?”
“On average, I would say about fifth-floor.”
“That’s all I need to hear. Tell them to take care of themselves.” Given their level, they’d only get in our way in a fight and wouldn’t be able to offer us much.
Plus, even if we don’t accept their request, I’m sure they’ll be able to take care of themselves. Or maybe they can leech off of one of the two bigger clans.
It wasn’t like I forced them to come down here. I’d simply opened the portal like they wanted me to, and that was it. As such, I wasn’t inclined to do any more for them.
“Versyl, recast Binding.”
“How do you want me to do it?”
“Make Emily and Auyen one team. The rest of us will be another.”

For now, I decided to divide us into two teams. To be honest, I was tempted to make one six-man team and just leave out Auyen, but I decided it would be better to let him get some EXP as well. Since this was a new floor, there were bound to be new monsters. This way, Auyen could sit back and take in free EXP while Amelia took care of the monsters on her own.
“Emily, are you all right with that?”
“I don’t mind. I understand the circumstances.”
“All right, then that’s settled.”
Right on time, too, because Ainar seemed to be running out of patience. “Bjorn! How much longer do we have to wait around here?”
“Everyone, get ready to head out,” I replied.
It was time to start exploring.

As soon as we started to move, all of the adventurers lingering at the starting point quickly took notice. One of them mustered up the courage to run over and ask me, “If you don’t mind... would it be all right if we follow you from a distance?”
In other words, they wanted to follow our lead because they were too scared to explore an unfamiliar floor on their own.
Ha, do these bastards have no conscience? Not only did I give them a free ride by opening the portal, but now they want to ride our coattails while we explore this place too?
“I do mind. Don’t follow us.” My firm answer brooked no argument.

The man, however, refused to back down, apparently determined to ride the wave of our success. “B-But... if you can help us even a little, then the number of people who end up dying in vain here will be significantly lower.”
Watching one of their own bravely make an appeal, other adventurers were quick to follow his lead and back him up.
“That’s right...!”
“In emergencies, adventurers have a duty to help one another...”
“And if you help us, it will certainly help improve your reputation even more—”
What are these morons talking about? Do they think I’m some sort of pushover because I opened the portal for them? “When did I ever tell you to go through the portal?”
They all went quiet.
“A real adventurer should be able to handle their own expedition.”
“But many of us are going to end up dead—”
“Surely you knew the risks before you came here? This is an expedition, after all.”
With that, I set off with my teammates. The other adventurers didn’t make any attempt to tail us, which suggested my speech had worked.
“Phew, I feel a bit better now. They all kept spouting nonsense.”
“But Captain, is this really all right?” Auyen asked in a worried tone. “If they make it back alive, they might spread some weird, false rumors about you...”
I merely pasted on a smile and patted him on the back. “You worry about everything. If you keep doing that, you’re going to give yourself headaches.”
“Haha... As expected, you’re incredible, Captain.”
“All right, enough chitchat—let’s focus on the expedition. We don’t know what awaits us ahead.”

We began our long trek away from the starting point, walking along the coastline as we tried to get a lay of the land. Surprisingly, it didn’t take long. The land we were currently standing on wasn’t all that big.
“I knew I heard the sound of waves...”
“So we were on an island.”

More specifically, we were on a small, rocky island whose perimeter took only thirty minutes to walk. It was decent enough in terms of size for a starting island, just like Laemia on the sixth floor. However, a look around revealed that this place was void of any and all monsters. No, forget monsters—there was practically nothing here at all.
On Laemia, there were at least trees we could cut down. But here, there’s nothing.
It was a shame. If there were a special material that could only be obtained here, then we could have sold it for a high price.
Of course, it was still too early to give up hope. Our real quest lay in the sea.
“Rockrobe, do you think it’ll be all right?”
I first decided to solicit the opinion of our navigator before we pulled out the boat. Even a cursory glance suggested that this ocean wasn’t an ordinary one.
“Yes. Even though it seems different from regular seawater, that piece of wood over there is floating. We’ll have to give it a try, but I think that our boat is buoyant enough to get by.”
“Good to hear.”
A silver wave crashed against the rocks on the shore. The ocean before us looked to be made of liquid mercury, and floating atop the water was a wide assortment of strange objects.
Shaaaaaa!

Each wave of silver water brought with it a wardrobe, a fireplace, a thick book, an old sword, a knight’s helmet, and more. What was that over there, socks? I didn’t know what any of it was doing in these waters, but after hearing Auyen’s professional opinion, we scouted out a good location to pull out the ship.
“Ohhh! The boat is floating!”

Thankfully, the boat was able to float on the water without any issues, but just in case, we watched it for ten minutes before boarding. After confirming that the water didn’t damage it, we got onboard and prepared for departure. Now, the success of this journey was in Auyen’s hands.
“What? M-Me?”
“Yeah. Just think of it like the first time you ever went up to the sixth floor, when you didn’t know how to get around yet.”
Auyen seemed troubled by the weight of this new responsibility at first, but my confidence seemed to win him over. “Then, we’ll start by investigating the surrounding waters first...”
“Do whatever you think is best. And you don’t have to run every little decision by me either. You are much better than me when it comes to navigation.”

That was how we began our voyage, carefully traversing the waters under the direction of our navigator, Auyen. As we slowly drifted away from the island, Auyen began to jot down a map, checking the depth of the water as we went in order to make sure there weren’t any hidden obstacles underneath. Amelia watched from over his shoulder, keenly interested.
“I’m jealous of that talent of yours,” she said.
“...What?”
“I’m saying you’re doing a good job. I’m sure your name and that map will go down in history. Just like the one of Pikma.”
Come to think of it, Amelia had a strange obsession with things like that. Was it because she’d never been able to—and would never be able to—proudly stamp her name on an achievement?
...I’ll have to figure out a way for her to use her real name again when we get back to the city.

Since Auyen was managing the ship just fine without me, I left them to their business and headed up to the deck. If Auyen was considered an expert in navigation, then I could be considered an expert in the labyrinth itself.
Our field of view has increased.

Standing on the rocky island, we could only see about one hundred yards in front of us. But now that we were sailing, our visibility was gradually widening. The sky was pretty dark, so we still couldn’t see all that far ahead, but you could at least tell that whatever had been limiting our vision before had now disappeared.
“Versyl, have you found anything yet?” Like the wizard she was, Versyl was fishing for any floating object she could get her hands on.
“No. Since I have no information about any of this... For now, I decided to focus on collecting samples rather than studying them.”
Unfortunately, she hadn’t found anything particularly interesting so far. “I see...”
If Raven were here, would things have been different?

Though the thought popped into my mind, I wasn’t terribly disappointed. What was really the point of studying, anyway? We were adventurers. Our job was simply to find something and sell it for a high price.
Then I’ll leave all of that to Versyl...

I went to check on the rest of our party members. Erwen was on the observation deck, using her keen eyesight to play lookout. Meanwhile, Ainar and I were handling ourselves a lot better on the seas than we used to and Missha was standing off to the side, seemingly enjoying her time alone. Right as I was about to walk over and talk to her, a voice sounded out.
“Island! It’s an island!”
A new area had been found.
This was our first discovery since coming to this hidden area. Excited, we quickly turned the ship in the direction Erwen was pointing in.
But then, still a good distance away from it, we all froze. The reason was simple.
“A m-monster...”
It wasn’t an island.
“...What should we do?”
“Oh! Are we fighting it? Isn’t this the first monster we’ve found in here? It might be weaker than we think!”
“A-Are you out of your mind? You’d have to be ridiculous to try and fight a monster of that size!”
A monster so massive that we mistook it for an island had appeared. The only people who seemed to recognize just how dangerous a situation we were in were me and Amelia.

“...Yandel.” Amelia, of all people, definitely had an idea of how strong that monster was thanks to her Crisis Detection skill. However, according to her, it didn’t give her much information aside from a rough estimate of the monster’s rank. “No, Auyen Rockrobe. Quick, turn the ship around right now. We need to get as far away from that thing as we can.”
“Wh-what? O-Oh! All right.” Auyen rushed to follow Amelia’s orders without question.
Amelia then turned to me. “Do you know what that is?”
I did.
That massive black shell, that elongated neck and dragon-like head, and that long beard attached to its snout...
“Tol-Lapupa. A rank-one monster.”
“Seriously...? That’s a rank-one monster?”

It made sense that this was the rest of the team’s first time ever seeing a monster like that. After all, 80 percent of all rank-one monsters, including Tol-Lapupa, could only be found on the tenth floor. Of course none of them would have any information on what they looked like.
On top of that, it’s a monster that only appears on a hidden map.
Even on the tenth floor, you had to go into a hidden area to find it.
Shit...
Even after we managed to turn the boat around and escape from Tol-Lapupa, a chill still ran down my spine.
I can’t believe there’s a rank-one monster in this place...
My mind was whirring on full overdrive. How could the first monster we saw down here be that thing? And just how strong would the other monsters we’d eventually come across be?
If we fought that beast, we would be annihilated in a second. Rank-one monsters were even stronger and more difficult to take down than any upper-floor Lord of the Floor.
Does that mean we should head back to the rocky island...?
The thought popped into my mind before I could stop it, but I decided it would be too much of a pity to give up now.
Thus, we continued our voyage.
The seventh day was now over. That meant the first floor had closed.
All right, then that confirms this place isn’t a hidden map connected to the first floor...
Like I thought, this must be an entirely new floor. As for what floor it had to be...
Basement Floor One.

Since the second floor already existed, I figured this floor must be some sort of basement floor. Hmm, but then what was its name? Normally when a new floor opened, the official name was written on the Stone of Honor.
I guess I’ll find out when I get out of here and see it.
As we continued to sail the open waters, my monster-related worries slowly started to fade away.
“Kyaaaaaa!”
That was, until Versyl suddenly let out a shriek while fishing for samples.
“A monster! It’s a monster!”
I rushed to her side and looked over the railing. Sure enough, there was a monster climbing up the side of the hull.
“Huh? What is that?” asked the very confused Ainar, who had also run over after hearing Versyl’s cry. “It doesn’t look like a Murloc or a Frogman.”
However, I had no answer for her. We were on a new floor, after all. I’d thought there was a possibility this might happen.
Crrroak! Crrroak!
This was a new type of monster—one whose rank, classification, and name were a complete mystery.

chapters.title: Chapter 509: Grave (1)
paragraphs: It looked a lot like a Frogman at first glance, especially if you were looking at its large belly, which seemed to be full of air. Or the suckers that were attached to its knuckles. Even their faces were quite similar. However, its skin was grayish, not green, and it wasn’t holding a harpoon, which Frogmen always did.
But most importantly...
Wings...?
On its back were a pair of wings that looked completely out of place. They looked as if they had been cut out with scissors and glued there.
Crrroak!
Suddenly, the one climbing up soared into the air before landing on the deck.
So those wings weren’t just for show, huh?
“Emily, what rank is it?” I knew she couldn’t give a completely accurate rating with Crisis Detection, but it would still give us a rough idea.
“It’s not even rank seven, given how I’m not picking it up as a threat at all.”
That was all the confirmation I needed.
“Under rank seven...”

There were now about fifteen of them, silently staring up at us from the silvery water. As more of them began to climb up onto the deck, I yelled out orders. “Don’t rush in and attack them yet! For now, we have to gather as much information about them as we can!”
“Ugh!” Ainar, who had tried to run straight at them, skidded to a stop at my command. Thankfully, she was a good listener.

“Behel—aaaaaah!” I quickly ran forward, raising my threat level with Wild Outburst. It didn’t take long before the mystery monsters started to attack me. However, their attack pattern was completely different from what I had expected.
They didn’t use their teeth or claws. They weren’t holding a weapon like a harpoon in their hands either. So how did they attack?
Swoosh.

Seemingly out of thin air, some sort of lightning-type projectile materialized and shot at us. Of course, since it was under rank seven, the attack didn’t do any damage to me. I blocked most of the bolts with my shield, but even those I couldn’t didn’t even manage to break through my skin.
What the hell...?
I froze. It wasn’t because of a status condition like Paralysis or anything like that, though. It was just because I was surprised.
“M-Mr. Yandel... J-Just now, that monster...”
Yeah. So I wasn’t the only one who noticed.
Erwen then spoke up, finishing Versyl’s sentence. “Wasn’t that Fleminas’s Thunderbone?”
The rank-seven monster Fleminas was a lightning-type monster that appeared in sections of the third and fourth floors. So why was this thing using a skill unique to another type of monster?
Is this thing a special mutant or mini-boss?
The thought flickered through my mind, but that was impossible. All fifteen of the monsters on our deck were using the exact same skill.
A type of monster that uses the same skill as another...
If that was the case, what about its other skills?
After a little more baiting and experimentation, I discovered another surprising fact.
“Th-that’s... Iron Falcon’s Ironclad Feather.”
“Oh! I know that one! That’s the rank-six Sea Worm’s Bubble!”
“Not rank six... That’s rank seven...”

All three of its active skills came from different monsters. I wondered what its passive skills were, but unfortunately, that was a little harder to find out. I swung my hammer, trying to get rid of one of them, only to be suddenly thwarted at the last second.
[Due to Rotten Mucus, your attack missed.]
So it has a Frogman’s passive? No wonder they looked similar. Well, that’s enough research for now. It’s time to get rid of them.
“That’s enough for now. You can kill them!”
“Are you sure?”
As soon as I gave the okay, Ainar ran forward and started to kill all of them off. We were the first ones ever to not only discover a new type of monster but also to defeat them as well.
[You have killed a Gullfrog. EXP +0]
What? I don’t think I got any EXP from that. Sure, it was lower than rank seven and wouldn’t give me much, but I should still feel something at least—
[No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck has been activated.]
My thoughts instantly derailed as soon as I saw what was happening.
“...An essence!”
Woah, it had really dropped an essence.
“...Versyl! Quick, grab a vial!” I hurriedly instructed our wizard, my mind buzzing.
Then will this essence give the user the Frogman’s Rotten Mucus or the Sea Worm’s, Iron Falcon’s, or Fleminas’s active skill? Or maybe all of them?
...This could irrevocably change the entire system of essence combinations.
Our first battle was over, and our spoils were one green essence. I needed to check later to confirm, but for now, it seemed to be the Iron Falcon’s Ironclad Feather, if the color was any indication.
“Versyl, how many essence vials are left?”
“Twenty-seven.”
“I thought that Melbeth only gave us twenty?”
“I brought everything I had as well, just in case.”
“I see...”
“What should I do with the vial?”

“You can hold onto it for now. They’ll be easier to keep track of if one person is in charge of all of them.” After deciding what to do with the vials, I turned to my teammates. “But more importantly, what did you guys feel? When Ainar killed the first one...?”
“Oh, are you talking about how there was no feeling of accomplishment? Like the one you usually get after you kill a monster for the first time?”
“Huh? Did everyone else feel the same way? I thought I was the only one...”
Seeing as none of them felt themselves gaining any EXP either, it was clear that there was none to be found in the first place.
So the concept of this floor is pretty strange...

On top of not providing any EXP, we’d confirmed that at least some of the monsters here had the characteristics of various monsters, like a chimera. The realization left me feeling a bit down. If all the monsters here were like that, we wouldn’t be able to find any yet-undiscovered skills. I was hoping that we would at least find something new. However, on the other hand...
“I can’t believe there are monsters here with the skills of various species. Once this information becomes public, things will plunge into chaos.”

This could end up causing a massive upheaval, revolutionizing the way people combined essences and skills and potentially opening up new, completely overpowered builds. It was like we’d just unlocked a secret customization feature.
If I can take advantage of the Steel Giant’s active skill without the passive... then I won’t have to worry about weapons constraints.

In that same vein, there were countless other active and passive skills that I’d like to get my hands on, but that weren’t featured in my final build because of the lackluster stats attached to their essences. But what if I could use Orc Hero’s Giantization with another passive skill? That meant my final build could become even stronger. Path of Heroes wasn’t bad, but it also wasn’t anything special since it was only rank-five. Overall, its performance and effects were simply lackluster. The total stats granted by the essence were also rather low. If it weren’t for the fact that Giantization and Union were a great combo, then I’d have chosen from a wide array of essences with even higher stats...
...Is there a monster that can give me the same skill with better stats?

I had no idea. There was also a chance that this type of monster was unique, and we wouldn’t run into anything like it again. At the same time, there was a chance we would come across new monsters with entirely new, never-before-seen essences.
This is fun.

As a player who loved Dungeon and Stone, my heart was racing with excitement. What awaited us ahead? I found myself looking forward to what else we would find. However, I knew I couldn’t get careless or over-eager. After all, the unknown was both an opportunity and a disaster waiting to happen.
“Lift the anchor!”

After getting rid of the monsters on the deck, we resumed our journey. It seemed that this entire area was home to these electric frogs. Every so often, they would suddenly pop out of the sea and climb their way up onto our boat. But this time, however, we hunted them with Distortion.
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-six space-time spell High-Level Distortion.]
These things were a new type of monster, so I was certain that whatever they dropped could be sold to the Magic Tower for a high price.
“Bjorn!”
“If you’re bored, you can at least swab the deck.”
“That’s not it, I have something to say!”
“...What is it?” Throughout this entire journey, Ainar had been peppering me with random questions out of the blue, apparently entirely unconcerned with the danger that could possibly be awaiting us.
Case in point: “What are you going to name them?”
“Name...?” Actually, I hadn’t even thought of that. How did monsters get named in the first place? “Erwen, do you know?”
“Um... I’m not sure...?”
Unexpectedly, Erwen also didn’t know how monsters got their names. Versyl, despite being a wizard who should know these things, was a player and didn’t seem to know either.
“That’s actually... I actually never thought about it... I guess whoever was the first person to find a monster was the one to name it?”
“Hm... probably.”
Having overheard the conversation we were having, Amelia left Auyen alone for a moment and approached us with open interest. “Nanari,” she declared.
“...What?”
“How about Nanari? It sounds good...and...I think it’s cute too.”
Huh. Surprisingly, she liked that sort of stuff.
“...We’re naming a monster right now. Why would we make it sound cute, Emily?”
“But can’t the name be anything? Whatever the person who found it wants it to be?”
“I guess.”

It didn’t take long before everyone was invested in naming the new monster. After all, we were all adventurers through and through. I figured the opportunity to name new species could act as motivation for them on future expeditions, so I encouraged their interest.
“Then let me know if you come up with any ideas. We can hold a vote and decide later.”
“A vote... That’s fair. Then I’ll go with Nanari. And I’ll give ten thousand stones to whoever else votes for it,” Amelia declared.
“I said we were going to vote. Why are you suddenly trying to buy everyone out...?”
“Well, it’s not like I’m forcing them to accept my offer.”
“...Fine, do as you please.”
It didn’t seem all that fair, to be honest, but I let it slide. With the tone now set, the other members of our clan quickly jumped in to voice their opinions as well.
“Ultimate Sundra! What do you think? Doesn’t that sound strong?”

“But it’s not even rank seven,” Versyl replied, shooting down Ainar’s suggestion. “Why don’t we name it based on its characteristics instead? Since we know it has the essences of a Sea Worm, an Iron Falcon, a Fleminas, and a Frogman...”
“You want to combine all of that...?”
“Sea Falcon Flemman!”
“...What?”
“Sea Falcon Flemman!” Versyl repeated eagerly. “Isn’t that pretty good?”
I felt my brain undergo a hard reboot at the name, but surprisingly, it was well received by our other clan members.
“Oh! That’s nice! That’s also a very strong name!”
“...It’s definitely catchy. I can even picture what it looks like just from the name.”
“Isn’t Nanari better? I’ll give you twenty thousand stones.”
After that, a few other names were added to the list of candidates. Eventually, it was time to vote, and the results were...
“Seven votes for Gullfrog. Sea... Falcon Flemman has three votes. Nanari has two votes. And Kiruru has one.”
“What? That doesn’t make any sense. How are there thirteen votes when there are only seven people?”
“Ah, Versyl, you didn’t know? It’s in our clan’s bylaws. The captain’s vote is worth the same as the number of people in the clan.”
“...How is that democratic?!”
My voice frosted over. “Democratic? What is that?”
“Oh, that’s...”
Versyl’s mouth snapped shut as she belatedly noticed her slip of the tongue.
That’s right. If you’re a player, you have to be careful not to say stuff like that. After all, the term ‘democracy’ doesn’t exist in this world.
“Then it’s decided. From now on their name is Gullfrog.”

Thus, the name of the first monster we discovered became Gullfrog. It was a half-assed name I came up with after seeing its frog-like appearance and seagull-like wings, but at the very least, it was better than Sea Falcon or whatever the hell they all voted for.
“All right, let’s all head back to our positions and get to work!”

After being dismissed, Erwen headed back to the bridge as Auyen and Amelia returned to the wheel to steer the boat. Versyl also went back to fishing again, trying to grab as many samples as she could.
“Ainar, stop messing around and go clean the deck.”
“...But Missha isn’t doing anything either!”
“Missha... has something else to do...”
“Missha... Stand on the deck over there and take care of any monsters that climb up.”
“Ohhh! I want that job! Let me do that!”
“Shoo!”
Eventually, everyone got back to work, and I walked around the ship making sure everything was going smoothly.
Suddenly, Versyl called out to me. “Mr. Yandel, can you come here for a moment?”
“Did you find something?”
I quickly walked over, and Versyl held out an object she had fished out of the sea. “I just found this. What do you think? Don’t you think it’ll sell for a good price back in the city?”
“...A painting?”
“Yes. Even though this place looks like an ocean, the portrait is completely fine. The paper isn’t even a little wet.”
Huh... a piece of art from the labyrinth would definitely be worth a lot...
“Let me take a look.”

Versyl handed the portrait to me so I could examine it. But the moment I saw it, I froze. It was a rough sketch of a man standing next to a woman who appeared to be his wife. Sandwiched in between them was a girl who was beaming up at the viewer.
“What...? What’s the matter? Do you...happen to know them?”
It would be a bit of a stretch to say that I knew them. And it was an even bigger ask for me to come up with a reason why a portrait of this man would be here of all places.
“Somewhat.”
The man in this family portrait... It had been a few years since I’d last seen him, but...
He was none other than Hans A, the man I had dispatched to the labyrinth during my first-ever expedition.

chapters.title: Chapter 510: Grave (2)
paragraphs: Hans A. He had been my first night companion, and the first person I ever killed in this world. Thanks to him, I was able to upgrade to a more civilized lifestyle and adapt to life in the labyrinth. In the process, I was also able to meet Erwen as well.
Is it because his name was Hans? He’s still a thorn in my side even in death.

His small family portrait had been the first thing I threw aside when I was looking through his bag after looting him. Was it like a cursed doll in a horror movie that would continue to haunt me no matter how many times I threw it away?
“Hm? So it’s an object that was left behind in the labyrinth...”

What the...? When did Amelia get here? When I blinked back to awareness, I realized that all my teammates had been listening in on our conversation while continuing to do their jobs. I guess that made sense—adventurers tended to have good hearing.

“...Then maybe this is a place where everything that’s been left behind in the labyrinth ends up.” Versyl quickly came up with a hypothesis, like a true wizard. Truthfully, after hearing my story about the family portrait, that was a theory anyone could have come up with.
“Oh! That’s amazing! Then will I be able to find my lost shoes now? They’re my favorite pair!”
“If you’re lucky, Ms. Ainar.”

“Wait a minute, Ms. Gowland,” Amelia interjected. “If we go by your hypothesis, what’s the explanation for all the furniture in the water? It doesn’t seem likely that all those dressers and tables were things that were left in the labyrinth by adventurers.”
The question tripped Versyl up. “Th-that’s... true,” she muttered, almost to herself. “Why are those there?”
Amelia’s observation seemed to disprove the hypothesis that this place was the labyrinth’s garbage dump. That was until, surprisingly, our navigator was able to offer up a plausible explanation.
“If I may... I think those might be pieces of furniture that were on large ships.”
“Large ships?”
“I heard that before sub-space magic was developed, ancient adventurers struggled to explore the sixth floor since they couldn’t summon ships out of thin air like we can now.”
“Oh, is that so?”
“Yes. So they would cut down trees on the Island of Beginnings and hand-build a ship themselves so they could sail the sixth floor’s seas. That’s the first bit of history that all navigators learn.”

“...How is that possible? If they built a new ship every time, they would only ever be able to reach nearby islands. And I can’t imagine they’d want to go through the trouble of building a new one every month just to throw it away after.”
“You’re right. Apparently, the issue was solved with magic. Back then, sub-space magic wasn’t as advanced as it is now, but that doesn’t mean other similar types of magic didn’t exist.”

Auyen didn’t know the details, but according to him, a type of magic automatically made the ship sail back to the Island of Beginnings, carried there by the tide regardless of what island you were currently on when you cast the spell.
“So they took advantage of the fact that time on the sixth floor continues to flow even when the labyrinth closes.”

“Yes,” Auyen confirmed. “However, I also heard that there were many disputes and cases of theft as a result of this practice. Ah, and also, sometimes the ships were wrecked by the time they found their way back to the Island of Beginnings, rather than in their usual—”

“I see. Thanks for the valuable information.” I felt bad about having to cut Auyen off while he was excitedly showing off his knowledge. I actually didn’t mind hearing him ramble, but right now, I needed him to concentrate on sailing. “But let’s focus on our jobs for now.”
“Ah... of course!”
“Erwen, stop letting us distract you too. And Ainar, your mop isn’t moving.”

I quickly ordered everyone to stop eavesdropping and get back to work. The chests or chairs floating out there on the sea may be interesting, but the actual reason they were there wasn’t in any way important to us. There was only one thing that mattered, and that was the fact that this place was apparently full of objects, maybe even treasures, that had been left behind when the labyrinth closed.
“Versyl, continue to grab whatever comes floating by the boat. There might be valuable stuff mixed in.”
“Yes, will do.”

Right now all we had was this useless family portrait of Hans A, but who knew what else we might end up coming across? There might be a Numbered Item or a high-quality piece of equipment. There would surely be countless long-forgotten treasures here, just like how we had to abandon untold amounts of gear at Ice Rock.
When you think of it that way, this place is more of a tomb than a dump. Since it’s full of all sorts of expensive stuff from the dead.

I was finally starting to get it. At first, I’d wondered why so many adventurers were risking their lives, waiting around for the portal to open even when they knew Berzak was on the loose. But this opportunity really was one worth putting your life on the line for.
New monsters, new essences, new experiences, and countless treasures floating around on the sea...
How much would we end up making once we returned to the city and sold everything we found?
“Mister!” Suddenly, Erwen, from her position on the bridge, shouted at the top of her lungs. “An island! There’s an island!”
...It wasn’t another rank-one monster again, right?
In the end, what Erwen saw was indeed an island. Or, well, ‘island’ wasn’t quite the right word for it. At the very least, though, it wasn’t a monster.
“...It looks like a temple.”

There was a building of sorts, one in the shape of two cylinders, floating on the water. We took the ship and did a loop around it to scout it out, but in the end, all we could see from the outside was an entrance leading inside. In other words, going inside was our only option if we wanted to find out what was in there.
“What should we do?”
“What else? We’re adventurers. We should go and explore it.”
Since the water level around it was shallow, we had to transfer to a smaller ship and paddle ourselves toward the building.
“...What a strange place.”
As we got off our rowboat and headed into the temple, we took a look around, but we couldn’t see much due to the lack of light.
I can only see about five yards ahead.

All we could see was a wide staircase leading somewhere down below. The height and width of each step was massive, almost like it was built for something that wasn’t human. Of course, that worked out perfectly for me.
[You have cast Giantization.]
A staircase that I could comfortably walk down even in Giantization mode? It was enough to make a grown man cry.
Stomp, stomp, stomp.
I took the lead as we headed down the stairs to tank any attacks that might come our way. But a long while later...
“It’s still going?”

We must have gone down at least two hundred steps by now. What the hell was this place? Spatially speaking, how did this make any sense? But I decided to not think too hard about it. After all, it’d be ridiculous to expect this world to follow the laws of physics.
Stomp!
Eventually, we reached the end of the staircase.
“Ugh... it’s so dusty.”
The chamber we entered had a musty smell to it. Due to poor visibility, it was hard to make much out, but as we ventured further inside, our surroundings began to brighten.
In fact, in a flash, the entire space lit up like someone had flicked the lights on.
The whole team flinched and immediately went on high alert, waiting for an enemy to appear. However, when nothing jumped out at us, we all turned to stare at each other with blank looks.
“This place...”
The ceiling was extremely high, approximately as tall as the stairs we took were long. Not only that but the entire room was lined with massive bookshelves that reached all the way up there.
“What is this place? It’s like a library...”

The first thing that came to mind was a library, but it was different than any we’d ever seen if only for its sheer size. The books were so big that you needed to use your full wingspan to hold a single one, and each bookshelf was full of thousands of them.
“Oh! It’s not as heavy as I thought it would be?”
But for some reason, each book was light enough that anyone with an adventurer’s strength could easily lift it.
“Ms. Fenelin, could you help me open this book?”
“Of course!” Ainar quickly grabbed a book off the bookshelf for Versyl, then placed it on the floor and opened it. “It’s empty...”
What? Are they just props, then?
“Versyl, you’ll be in charge of investigating the books here. Ainar, you’ll stay here and help her. And make sure to protect her if anything happens.”

I left Ainar and Versyl with the books as the rest of us headed off to investigate our surroundings a bit more. The chamber seemed to be cylindrical, and going around its outer walls were large, curved bookshelves that reached up to the ceiling.
“...What the hell is that thing for?”

In the center of the room, there was a stone slab crafted into the shape of a table. There was also a large stone door nestled between the bookshelves, opposite the staircase we came down. A thorough investigation didn’t reveal anything else.
This seems to be a place where we have to trigger something...
Since there didn’t seem to be any monsters or traps around, we all split up to investigate. Eventually, we finally found something.
“Mr. Yandel, I found a book over here with something written in it! But it’s in the ancient language, so I think you should come and read it for us.”

My knowledge of the ancient language was already paying off a lot. I jogged over to Versyl to look at the book she had laid out on the floor. It was open to a spread that had a picture on one page and a written passage on the other.
“The illustration looks like it’s of the rank-nine monster Wall-Mole Rat... but I can’t read what it says.”

Like Versyl speculated, the drawing was of a Wall-Mole Rat. It was written right there next to the picture—its name, its habitat, its skills. The description even went into the origins of its name, characteristics of its essences, its unique habits, and more.
“...It looks like a page from some kind of field guide. Is this the only thing inside?”
“Yes. No matter how many other pages I flipped through, they were all blank.”
I hummed. “I see...”
“You sound like you have an idea?”
“There’s just a lot to process.”

First of all, this book alone was incredibly valuable. If Raven were here, she’d be running around in excitement, rambling about what an unbelievable discovery this was like the history fanatic she was. I, however, wasn’t interested in all that. Adventurers weren’t like wizards. Instead, we valued other things above knowledge.
How can we use this?

Namely, we cared about what a new discovery could do for us. No, more than that, we tried to figure out why the thing—whether a magic item, a helpful bug, or a hidden feature—existed in the first place.
But instead of research, we did things the adventurer way: trying everything we could think of and seeing what worked.
“Everyone, gather up.” I immediately called a team meeting.
“Did you figure something out?”
“No, but I think I might have an idea worth trying.”
“Worth trying?” Amelia tilted her head, but it would be faster to just show them than to explain. Especially since I wasn’t even sure it would work.
Thud.
I grabbed the book that Versyl found and placed it on the stone plate in the center of the library.
Roughly three seconds later, Amelia broke the silence. “I guess there are times when even you are wrong—”
Shaaaaaa!
The slab suddenly began to glow a bright blue. That meant something was happening, and since this was Dungeon and Stone, chances were that whatever it was would be dangerous.
“Bjorn! Over there! The stone door is opening...!”
I ran in the direction Missha was pointing and positioned myself in front of the pack. “Everyone, prepare for battle!” I shouted urgently.
The team got into their stances, alert and ready to take on whatever came our way. The tension in the air was thick as the seconds ticked by.
One second. Two seconds. Three seconds...
After four seconds, the monster finally appeared, slowly emerging from the crack in the stone doors.
Squeak.
It was a Wall-Mole Rat.
Squeak!
And just one of them.
The first monster we encountered on this new floor was a whopping rank-one monster. As a result, everyone including myself had been extremely wary of whatever would be coming out of that stone door.
“A Wall-Mole Rat...?”
What we got instead was a singular rank-nine monster.
“Don’t lower your guard. Something else might come out.”
Even though I was the leader, I was momentarily at a loss as well. However, it didn’t take long before I was able to collect myself enough to figure out what was happening.
...So, that’s what’s going on.
There was a passage about Wall-Mole Rat written in that book. When we placed said book on the stone slab, a Wall-Mole Rat then appeared through the stone doors. How could that be a coincidence?
“Erwen.”

The moment her name left my mouth, Erwen let the arrow she had nocked fly. Was she a psychic or something? How did she know what I was going to ask the moment I said her name? I had no idea, but that didn’t really matter right now.
The Wall-Mole Rat, which had been running at us, died without so much as a squeak.
Shaaaaaa!

There was a burst of light as a singular rank-nine mana stone dropped where it had been standing. Since Beginner’s Luck didn’t kick in, it didn’t drop an essence. Though it was so low rank we probably would have just ignored it anyway.
Rumble!
As soon as the monster died, the stone doors began to close again.
“Oh! Mr. Yandel! Over there!”
Suddenly, a staircase leading up to the second row of the massive bookshelf appeared. In a game like Dungeon and Stone, this was an obvious cue to the player.
So it’s telling us to keep going up and summon more monsters.
However, before going up the stairs, I checked out the book I placed on the stone slab.
“The picture and text are all gone...”
That meant that a book couldn’t be used twice. I tossed the now empty book on the floor as I climbed up the stairs, and a sudden thought flashed through my mind.
Can’t I skip the stairs and go for a higher book?
If you had the thought, you might as well give it a shot.

I took advantage of my height to grab onto the bottom of the third row of shelves, which the stairs didn’t reach, and then used my arm strength to climb up. However, when I tried to take out a book, it didn’t budge in the slightest.
So even if we’re physically able to climb up to a higher level, we can’t take out a book.

But what would happen if I climbed all the way up? The curiosity ate away at me, but I decided to check it out later when we either reached a dead-end or had some extra time left. We had enough to do as it was.
“Everyone, grab a book and find a page with a drawing on it.”

Once I doled out orders, everyone quickly dispersed to pick up a book and flip through the pages. With all of us searching together, it only took a few minutes to hit pay dirt. This time, there were two monsters listed inside a singular book. One was the rank-eight Nightplar.
“Oh! I know this one! Isn’t that that monster with the same essence as that Vampire we met in the Bloody Citadel?”
The other monster in the book was Gullfrog, which we had run into quite a few times on our way here.
“...So, what’s written down about it?”
“I guess it already has an official name, huh? Then we voted for no reason.”
Since we’d been the first to discover this monster, everyone seemed curious about what might be written down about it.
Then let’s see its real name...
As soon as I read what was written at the top of the page, however, I stiffened.
“...Huh? Bjorn? What’s gotten into you all of a sudden?” Ainar, concerned by my sudden shift in demeanor, worriedly approached me.
Versyl, who was nearby, seemed worried too. “...Mr. Yandel? Is there a problem?”
I was slow to respond. “Gullfrog.”
“What?”
“In this book, the name written down is Gullfrog.”
“...What? What do you mean by that? I’m sure you were the one who came up with that name though, Captain...”
Exactly. It didn’t make sense.

“I-Isn’t that an unbelievable coincidence...? I can’t believe you picked the same name...” Auyen murmured to himself while I quietly stared down at the book. I understood where he was coming from, of course. It would absolutely make far more sense to assume this was just some sort of unbelievable coincidence.
However...
Name. Habitat. Essence.
I quickly skipped past the rest of the data and went straight to the origin of the name.
Bjorn, son of Yandel, who was the first adventurer to enter Basement Floor One’s Archives, named the monster after being the first to discover it.
What the hell was this?

chapters.title: Chapter 511: Grave (3)
paragraphs: It didn’t make any logical sense. How could this book contain a name that I made up less than a day ago?
“...How is that possible? We just got here.”
“To think this information would already be written down... Yandel, do you have any idea what’s going on?”
“I’m not sure...”
But even as I said that I got a strange inkling. I couldn’t put it into words, but somehow, I had a gut feeling I knew what was happening here.
The Records Stone...

A stone that had history from the beginning of time until the end of the world etched on its surface. This had to have something to do with that thing. The information was showing up here in the form of a book rather than a stone, but maybe this place had a similar purpose, serving as some kind of archive. The Records Archives.
The more I explore this labyrinth, the bigger the headache it gives me...
This development momentarily left me reeling, but I forced myself to snap out of it. I could always puzzle this over later.
“This must just be one of the labyrinth’s countless mysteries. Everyone, stop getting distracted and let’s get back to work.”
“That’s right! Let the wizards worry about boring things like studying and researching! Our only job is to explore!”

For the first time in a while, Ainar was right on the money. I couldn’t help but smile at that as I continued to skim through the book. Although the origin of the monster’s name was shocking, the entry itself had information that was extremely useful for me. Unlike the books in the city’s library, this one had exact numbers listed inside.
[Agility: +8
Lightning Resistance: +15
Jumping Power: +30
Soul Power: +20...]

The basic stats were assigned numerical values, rather than just the adjectives high, medium, or low. Not only that but there was information about the colors and effects of the different essences it could drop, which was something that I’d been wondering about.
The green essence is Ironclad Feather.
The yellow essence is Thunderbone.
The blue essence is Bubble.

Was there even a point in the Magic Tower anymore? Well, the researchers there could still gain recognition by writing papers about this stuff, of course, but these books would sell for a massive profit.
“All right! Let’s try this again!”
After reading through all the information inside, I once again used the book to summon some monsters.
[You have killed a Nightplar.]
[You have killed a Gullfrog.]

We didn’t waste a second and ended the battle in an instant. Just like last time, after we defeated the summons, the stone door closed and a staircase leading to the third row of the massive bookshelf appeared. We split up, one team heading up the stairs to pull out books and flip through the pages. When someone found one with a picture, they quickly threw it down to the other team waiting on the ground floor so they could put it on the stone and quickly summon and kill the monsters inside.
[You have killed a Frost Wolf.]
[You have killed an Ice Golem.]
[You have killed a Death Knight.]
[You have killed a Vaikundus.]
[You have killed a Minotaur.]
[You have killed...]

Like I thought, the number and ranks of the monsters increased as we went higher up the shelves. As a natural consequence of that, the difficulty of each fight also gradually increased. To be honest, this was a pretty decent hunting ground.
There haven’t been any new monsters, though...
Unfortunately, we didn’t manage to find a book that had information about an entirely new type of monster, which I was hoping for.
...Then that means we need to have met the monster first for it to show up in a book, huh?
That may well be the case, but our sample size was still too small to confirm that hypothesis. That, and we still had a long way up to go on the bookshelf.
One day, two days, three days...

Time quickly flew by as we lost ourselves in the rhythm of simple, repetitive labor. Aside from taking some time to sleep and eat, we focused solely on hunting to try and climb up the bookcase as fast as we could. Because of that, we were eventually able to build up a sufficient enough sample size to solidify some key facts.
One: there were no new monsters in these books.

It was hard to say whether that was because there were simply no other monsters in existence, or if only monsters that had been “discovered” before would show up in their pages. That was something we’d only figure out after exploring other areas of this floor.
Two: the library wasn’t a good hunting ground.

That was because it was an absolutely incredible hunting ground. In fact, while you might not get any EXP if you already defeated all the monsters in the book, if your goal was to farm mana stones and essences, this place might be the best place to do so in the entire labyrinth. The monsters came out of the stone door in an orderly fashion, one at a time, which made it easy for you to get in formation and attack them as a team. We also had all the time in the world to prepare ourselves before summoning them. That meant we could even activate skills and cast spells in advance if necessary.

Plus, by the time we were about halfway up the bookcase, a singular book could have over one hundred monsters listed in it. There was no need to explain how amazingly valuable that was. This place was perfect for mass hunting, with no unnecessary wait times or hunting permits to speak of. And once we finished a hunt, we could just summon another monster right then and there and keep going.

In just three days, we’d netted more than ten million mana stones and seven essences. Well, six of the essences were under rank six, though, so we discarded those and only used a vial on the rank-five essence.
Yeah, when it comes to hunting, this place isn’t bad at all...

Yet both me and my clanmates weren’t satisfied with just that. Our goal for this expedition wasn’t to kill mobs. We were the first people in history to ever step foot on this hidden floor. There was a lot more to be gained by exploring the unknown rather than just sitting around and hunting in one spot.
The other problem is... it’d be impossible to clear this entire bookcase at our current level.

Battle-wise, we were able to defeat most of the monsters on the middle shelves with relative ease. However, once we reached the beginning of the upper section, it became apparent that we wouldn’t be capable of clearing it all.
Rank-three monsters start to show up in the books around here. That means that if we keep going up, we’re eventually going to run into a rank-one monster.
Still, we would one day have to work toward clearing this entire library.
My thoughts were interrupted by a sudden shout from a bookshelf a little ways away.
“Bjooorn!” Ainar hollered. “I found a book with a new monster!”
Wait, seriously?

Our scattered clan members stopped searching the stacks to circle up, all of us wearing looks of half-anticipation and half-skepticism, considering who we were talking about here. Ainar didn’t seem to notice as she held the book up high to show us, clearly proud of herself.
The book featured a monster that was covered in tentacles. On its back were wings made of bones, though the creature seemed to walk on four legs.
“What do you think? Have you ever seen something like this before?”
“Definitely not... This is my first time seeing such a monster.”
“Yandel, what about you?”
“This is my first time as well.”
It seemed that this was, in fact, a new monster. But why did it suddenly show up now of all times?
“Hurry up and read it! What rank is it? It looks strong!”
I read the ancient text aloud for everyone to hear. Yet before the words even left my mouth, I started to get a strange feeling I knew what was going on here.
“Its name is Tentaculan. Its habitat is the Sea of Records—”
“Sea of Records? Isn’t that the same place where we discovered the Gullfrog?”
“Yes. But don’t interrupt me.”
“Oh! Sorry.”
“It’s a rank-four monster, and it’s classified as a beast-type.”
“Oh! Rank four?! The abilities! What abilities does it have?!”
I thought I told her not to interrupt me... Well... I guess there’s no point in getting on her case about it.
“It has the passive ability Pacifist, which is the same as the rank-four monster Sea Merchant. It also has a Gargoyle’s Evil Sound, Medusa’s Curse of Stone, and Riu Moby Dick’s Water Roar.”
“...So the monsters on this floor really are mixes of monsters from other floors.”
Yeah. At this point, that seemed like the most likely explanation. The natives of this place seemed to be new monsters made up of various combinations of other monster’s essences.
This find also helped us confirm something else.
“It also seems that the monsters that we find here in the library have to have been discovered by somebody at least once before.”
“Huh? But isn’t this a new monster?”
I nodded as I read the origin of the name that was written down. “Adventurer Maderkin Lilgreams named the monster after being the first to discover it while exploring Basement Floor One’s Archives.”
“Maderkin Lilgreams... That’s the captain of the Silver Lion Clan who came here with us...?”
“I thought he might have died without us, but I guess they’re getting around just fine on their own,” Amelia said, looking kind of bitter.

She must have been upset since it felt a bit like he’d stolen some of our glory. Still, it wasn’t like we got money for having our name written down in a book. Or, wait, was it that she was upset that her name hadn’t been written down anywhere, yet this freeloader would forever go down in history?
...If we find another new monster later, I should let her be the one to name it.
That was all the information written down about the monster, so we quickly headed back down to the bottom floor to summon it.
Grrr...
It was much bigger than in the picture. But something was weird. Aside from the tentacles spilling out from its body, it looked entirely like a wolf. So why was it living in the sea?
[You have killed a Tentaculan.]

There was no way to know, so we focused on hunting it instead. Since this was our first time ever encountering this thing, we took things slow to make sure it couldn’t land a hit on us. Still, it was only rank four, so it was an easy fight.
“That was... even easier than I was expecting.”
Come to think of it, Missha had gotten pretty strong... That was the only thought in my mind as I watched her step forward and cut down a rank-four monster with a single slash.
“All right, everyone, let’s group up for a minute.”
Once that was dealt with, I gathered up the members of my clan for a vote. There was just one item on the agenda.
“Please tell me what you want to do. We can stay here and continue climbing the library’s shelves, or head out and try exploring another area.”
However, my team members showed no enthusiasm for offering up their opinions.
“...What’s the point? You’re going to be the deciding vote anyway.”
“Exactly.”
I sighed. Did I play my trump card too early? I should have saved my voting power for something more important.
“Don’t worry. I won’t be taking part in this vote.”
They all eyed me with distrust, but after a moment, they gave in.
“Hmmm. fine.”
“I guess we can hold a vote, then.”
Once the vote began in earnest, the results were surprisingly unanimous.
We would stop exploring the library and try to find another area.
Honestly, I’d kind of expected that. Everyone was already bored of this simplistic hunting format, and finding Tentaculan in that book had just been fuel on the fire.
“This place isn’t bad, but given how we have competition, this feels like a waste of time.”
“At this very moment, they’re probably exploring new areas and finding new monsters to name.”
“And any essences they come across, they’ll be able to sell them to the Magic Tower for a high price.”
Yeah, this is the classic adventurer mindset.
However, even though the vote was unanimous, I still decided to have us stay here for another day or two.
“...We’re not leaving right away?”
“Why? You’re not the type to delay things for no reason.”
My clan shot me looks that suggested I was acting like a dictator again. Their distrust hurt my feelings. I was just trying to make the most optimal call as the leader of this clan.
“Right now, we can summon rank-three monsters from these books. We should try to hunt as many as we can first and then we can leave right after.”
Rank-two monsters would be difficult for us to take on, but we could still make quick work of most rank-three monsters at our current level.
“And Emily, aren’t there still quite a few rank-three monsters that even you haven’t had a chance to kill yet?”
“Th-that’s... right.”
“You too, Ainar. You still haven’t gotten that essence I told you about.”
Ainar wasn’t the only one, either. There were some rank-three essences that I also wanted Erwen and Missha to have. I still needed the essence of Bellarios as well.
“Then is everyone in agreement?”
I took their silence as consent. With our plan decided, we picked up the pace even more.
[You have killed a Mechanical Giant. EXP +7]
[You have killed a Phoenix. EXP +7]
[You have killed an Usbin. EXP +6]
[You have killed a Garcian. EXP +7]
[You have killed an Abyss Skeleton...]
[You have killed...]

Compared to the middle section of the library, the difficulty of the battles had risen several times over, yet in return, the rewards were all the sweeter. We were able to kill and get EXP for many of the rank-three and rank-four monsters on the seventh floor’s Dark Continent, which we hadn’t really been able to explore yet because of the war. The only disappointing thing was that Beginner’s Luck only kicked in once.
[No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck has been activated.]

Still, it at least activated for Abyss Skeleton, a monster that appeared exclusively on the tenth floor. Since none of us could take advantage of its essence, though, we would have to sell it. Luckily for us, essences from the tenth floor were worth an incredible amount.
But from the looks of it, it seems that monsters that are rarer or harder to find in the labyrinth don’t tend to pop up in these books too often.
Take, for example, Bellarios. I really wanted to get my hands on it, but we never managed to find it in any of the books even as our search came to a close.
“Let’s stop.”

Despite my disappointment, I eventually made the call that it was time to stop hunting. The difficulty of each battle was rising, and we were now being forced to face two rank-three monsters at once. Time-wise, that was hypothetically more efficient since we could hunt two monsters simultaneously. But in reality, because we’d been hunting without breaks for the past few hours and our fatigue was mounting, continuing on like this wasn’t sustainable.
“Everyone, grab the books, and let’s head out.”
It was time to get going.
“Grab the books?”

“Other people might come by here. If we take the books from the top shelves with us, that means it’ll be impossible for them to progress any further than we have. And it’s not like they can climb the bookshelves to reach for a higher book since they won’t come out.”
“But if we take all these books, our sub-spaces might fill up.”
“If they do, we’ll just have to throw them overboard into the sea.”
“What? Yandel, you...”
“What?”
“...are smart. Especially when it comes to things like this.”
Everyone, including Amelia, liked my plan. They all thought it was a smart strategy and not underhanded in the slightest. That was because all of us were adventurers.
This is nothing in this line of work.
After ensuring that nobody could go up any higher than us, we all started to head back the way we came.
Stomp! Stomp!
