There was no need to worry about complicated questions like that anymore. With a single swing of my hammer, this whole complex situation became much simpler. The chief and I were now unable to go back to the relationship we had before. So I would kill him right here and now, and if I failed to do so...
My allies and I will get out of this village.
It was a simple, elegant solution.
However, the chief was still staring at me like he couldn’t follow my logic at all. “There was no reason for you to do something so extreme.”
“Oh! Really?”
“You care for your allies dearly. Putting them in danger like this isn’t like you.”
I didn’t know what he was basing that declaration on considering he hadn’t even known me for all that long, but I had no intention of sticking around to find out.
“Behel—aaaaaah!” I shouted my battle cry and swung my hammer down again.
Boom!

Unfortunately, the chief was ready this time and managed to block my hammer with his sword. However, it seemed that blow had served to finally drive home the fact that I was done talking. “You’ll pay for making the wrong decision here,” he vowed, his voice low and cold.
Man, that line didn’t sound all that cool coming from someone with a fish head. Maybe he needed to take a look in the mirror before he went around acting all high and mighty.
Deciding to do him a favor, I pouted my lips like a fish and mimicked him in a nasal tone. “Wah, you’ll pay for making the wrong decision here.”
For some reason, his response was a beat late. “...You have lost your mind.”

Hmm, well, he could flatter me all he wanted—that didn’t mean I was going to go easy on him. Gripping my hammer with both my hands, I put more force behind my thrust, and the chief’s sword started to inch back.
Since he’s being pushed back when we’re both using two hands, he loses to me in strength.
Perhaps coming to the same conclusion himself, the chief ended our deadlock and tilted his sword to deflect my attack to the side.
Bang!
The hammer fell to the ground with a thud. At the same moment, the chief’s sword started to glow with a bright white light.
Vwoong!
This was the attack that killed a Hipramajent in one hit. From what I could tell, it was similar to an aura.
But there are too many skills in the labyrinth just like this one.
As a result, I had no way of knowing for sure what the skill he was using was, but to be honest, that was the least of my concerns right now.
[You have cast Iron Fortress. The effect of Evolving Shell has increased by 1.5 times.]
[You gain 75% resistance to bladed weapons.]
It was still just a bladed weapon in the end, right?
Clang!
The sword that had cut through the Hipramajent’s head like tofu was blocked by my shield and deflected. And as for the shield itself...
I guess there’s a small dent in it now?

Yeah, as always, there wasn’t an opponent scarier than one’s imagination. Now that I’d experienced his attack firsthand, I could say it was pretty manageable. Well, of course, that wasn’t to say everything was smooth sailing.
Vwoong!
His Agility stat seemed to be much higher than mine, as none of my attacks except for my first one landed on him.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm.]
Even using Eye of the Storm, which was especially effective in a small space like this one, I only had a 30 percent chance of landing a hit.
Boom!
And when I did manage to hit him, he didn’t take that much damage.
I think his Resistance is pretty low... Looks like his Regeneration is pretty good, though.
The biggest wound, the one I gave him with that first attack, had already completely healed. When I noticed that, I quickly reassessed my strategy.
I can’t kill him here one-on-one.
I gave up on trying to kill the chief alone and changed tactics.
“Chief, do you know the top two ways to make someone mad?” I first asked a completely unrelated question to disrupt his flow of thought. He stared at me, baffled.
Shatter!
Just as he was trying to figure out what the hell I was talking about, I pulled out a Molotov cocktail from my sub-space and threw it on the mountain of corpses.
Fwoosh. Dash.
Then, I left the flaming pile behind and sprinted up the stairs.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
It seemed the basement was pretty soundproof as there wasn’t a single monster warrior waiting for me on the stairs, and I made sure to bust up the ceiling as I ran to block the chief’s way.
Rumble, rumble!

This town wasn’t going to win any awards for its architecture, that was for sure. All I had to do was give it a few whacks, and the entire underground chamber started to collapse in on itself like dominoes.
Boom!
I shook off the debris and rocks falling on me and plowed forward.
Bang!

Thirty seconds or so later, I burst through the trapdoor and escaped above ground. In the living room on the first floor, I found the monster warriors on standby with my allies, who were waiting for me to reemerge.
“Something must’ve happened down there! We need to go down—”
“(We need to check to see if the chief is okay—)”
Both groups stopped talking the moment they noticed me, their mouths falling open in surprise. The first one to recover their wits was Versyl.
“Uh... Mr. Yandel? What’s going on right now—?”
What, you can’t tell just by looking?
I’d destroyed as much of the basement as I could, but I was sure the chief would be up here any minute now, so I had no time to explain.
Anyone with a functioning brain cell would be able to understand what was going on in a second, anyway.
Crunch!
I bashed the head of the nearest monster warrior with my hammer and shouted, “We’re getting out of this village right now!”

chapters.title: Chapter 534: Rainbow (1)
paragraphs: We barreled down Main Street from the chief’s house to the entrance of the village.
Boom! Boom! Boom!

With Giantization, each of my steps shook the earth and made it sound like we were in a construction zone, but I didn’t care about what the village’s residents thought. My noisiness was the least of their concerns right now.
“(Bring water over here!)”
They were too busy trying to put out the fires anyway. There wasn’t a single person here who cared about a barbarian stomping a little too loudly down their street.
Were they people?
Just as I was once again mulling over a thought I’d had multiple times now, a question interrupted me.
“...Is this really okay?” Versyl asked as she sat atop the traditional wizard-exclusive vehicle, Ainar.
“What do you mean?”
I had no idea what she was talking about, but Versyl glanced behind her in response. Flames had erupted from the center of the village and the smoke was consuming everything.
“Many of this village’s residents aren’t warriors...”
Ah, she was more soft-hearted than I thought. She was still treating those fish-headed monsters with empathy.
“So?”
My tone made it clear that comments were no longer welcome, and Versyl shut her mouth accordingly.
Yet for some reason, Missha took up the baton. “Why did you do that, Bjorn...? This isn’t like you...”
Not like me? That was the second time hearing that today.
“Yeah! I wanna know too! What did you see down there to make you do this?”
Ainar joined in on Missha’s questioning. Even with her lowered Aggression, it seemed she still had a barbarian’s curiosity.
Human bodies.

That alone technically summed up everything I saw down there. The chief showed me a pile of corpses and explained how he ended up with them in an effort to clear up some of my misunderstandings. To be honest, none of that was actually the issue.
However...
“(Since we hid this from you as well, I won’t ask you to take responsibility for your ally breaking the rules of the village or the mistake you made as a result. How about it?)”
He then proceeded to tell me that he would overlook Amelia’s trespassing and my cracking open Nuiachichi’s skull as well.
Wasn’t that a little suspicious? Hans A, my first night companion, had done something similar after I “fell asleep” during my shift on watch.
“... Fortunately, we didn’t have any problems while you were sleeping, so I’ll wipe the slate.”

The lesson I learned that day was one I still carried in my bones. If someone I didn’t know was nice to me, that was because I had something they wanted in return. And there was another lesson I’d picked up over the course of my adventures.
“Why?! Why did you harm Lady Elisa?! What did we do to you?!”

When I smacked Elisa the priestess of Karui in the middle of her innocent cleric act, I came to another realization: the best way to deal with sketchy people was to bust open their skulls first and ask questions later.
However, I didn’t feel the need to explain all this to my allies, though it wouldn’t be too hard to lay out my logic and win them over.
“Please, tell us. What did you see down there that you’re doing this?”
“Nothing much,” I replied. Just like with the chief, all I had to say was this: “I just felt like it.”
No evidence, no argument—just that.
Missha mumbled, as if to herself, “A feeling, then...was it?”
A gut feeling—that subconscious calculation that took into account all the experiences you had ever had.
“A feeling!” Ainar seemed satisfied with that answer and nodded. “Oh, then it can’t be helped!”
Erwen smirked and agreed. “You’re pretty spot on when it comes to things like this, Mister. We’ve survived more than a handful of times specifically thanks to your instincts.”
“Well...there’s probably a reason you got that gut feeling. To be honest, I was a little wary of the chief as well,” Versyl said, weighing in as well.
Wyatt Hektz and Myul Armin, who were running beside us and listening in, also offered their two cents. Well, it wasn’t like these guys had been with me for all that long, but still.
“It’s a relief to hear you say that, actually.”
“You are quite well-known for your animal-like instincts, Baron Yandel.”
They seemed to trust my judgment. After all, most adventurers were willing to excuse most things as long as they turned out okay in the end, and we were also a particularly superstitious bunch.
“Something was off here from the start.”
“Honestly, this makes me feel a lot better. I haven’t been able to sleep a wink because I’ve been so on edge.”
“Also, when you have a feeling like that, it’s much worse to ignore it when it could be a bad omen. I mean, what if you’re right?”
“Ah... I get what you mean. Every time something like this happens and you ignore your gut instinct, things always seem to go even worse.”
It seemed everyone else had sensed something off about the monsters as well.
Still, it wasn’t like I’d answered Versyl’s question expecting them to all agree with me like this.
“Let’s go!”
“Damn those monsters! Let them all burn!”

For some reason, morale improved in response. They seemed to genuinely believe that this was the right choice, almost as if a single word from me had erased everyone else’s doubts—even though I still wasn’t completely sure myself.
“...You guys are weird,” I said without thinking, and it seemed someone heard me.
“You’re the weird one, Yandel. You convinced everyone with an argument so ridiculous it’s not even funny.”
Uh, what?
That voice...
“Now that I think about it, though, you’ve always been like this. You have a talent for it. For making everyone believe that the direction you’re headed is the right one...”
“Emily?” When I whipped around, Amelia was peering back at me from her spot on Auyen’s back. “You should’ve said something if you were awake. When did you wake up?”
“Just now.”
“How are you feeling? Are you all right?”
“I’m fine.” Amelia immediately slid down from Auyen’s back and started running on her own two feet. “I think I’ve got the gist of what’s going on. We’re trying to escape from the village, right?”
“Yeah.”
She sighed. “You made quite the mess while I was asleep. Fill me in. What happened?”
Since this wasn’t a conversation we could take our time having over tea, I filled her in on the most important bits.

“The chief showed me what was under the house, but I still felt like he was scheming something, so I hit him over the head. And while running away, we set fire to the village. The chief is probably chasing us through the fire.”
That was about the long and short of it.
Amelia stared at me for a moment, at a loss for words. “...That’s just like you.”
I couldn’t help but laugh. This was probably the first time today someone had told me I was acting exactly like myself.
“Anyway,” I said, a laugh still in my voice, “now it’s your turn. What happened to you?”
“I tried to go down into the basement but ended up getting caught and captured. I was interrogated, and that was that.”
Was that it? I pressed her for more details just in case, but she didn’t offer any additional information. Not that additional information would have changed anything about our current situation.
“Mister, we’re almost there!”
The real challenge would begin. Like Noark, this village was built underground. The only way to get into it was through the entrance, which was likely sealed by magic or some other ability.
“What do we do now?”
The gate was currently closed, so all we could see in front of us was a solid stone wall. Only the chief could open or close it.
Well, officially, anyway.
“Step back.”
As I approached the wall with my hammer, our white-collar wizard Versyl asked, “Will that... even work?”
Man, this was why academics weren’t cut out for hard labor.
“I’ll know once I give it a shot.”
With that, I slammed my hammer into the wall with everything I had.
[You have cast Swing.]
Boom!
The shockwave was enough to kick up all the dust in the surrounding area. However, the wall looked completely unscathed.
“...I don’t think that worked.”
Yeah, so that wasn’t enough. Pretty embarrassing for a barbarian.
“Don’t worry. I have a way,” I assured them.
“You do?”
“Yeah.”

Whether we were talking about magic, skills, or some other fantasy game nonsense, there was nothing in the world that couldn’t be torn down with physical force. And if whatever you were hitting refused to break, that was only because you were too weak to break it.
So, I initiated Plan B.
“Erwen!”
Time to hit it even harder.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned the Elemental Ruler of Darkness, Dicloe.]
Bang, bang, bang!
Hundreds of balls of darkness slammed into the wall. However, the wall remained intact.
Ok, so that wasn’t enough either?
Looks like there’s no point in using more Swings.

Every time a ball of darkness struck the stone wall, it chipped and cracked a little, but it seemed there was a pretty impressive restoration ability at play here, as it immediately mended itself. It looked like the kind of thing that needed to be hit with one big attack rather than a bunch of small ones.
“Erwen.”
There was no need for me to say anything more than that. Once I called her name, light began to gather at the tip of Erwen’s arrow.
Yeah, there’s no better one-shot than Concentrated Fire.
The downside was that it would take a while for her to fully charge it.
One second, two seconds, three seconds...
As time ticked by, the color of the light grew ever more intense.
“Yandel.”
“You don’t need to say it. I can see it too.”

From the direction of the burning, smoke-filled village, something was quickly closing in on us. At first, it looked like a small dot on the horizon, but as it grew larger, it became obvious exactly what—or who—it was.
...So you aren’t going to be nice and let us go, huh?
Well, he got here later than I expected, so I wasn’t going to complain.
“Prepare for battle!” I roared as I ran up to meet him.
Clang!
The moment I lunged forward, my shield raised, that “something” that had been charging toward us crashed into me.
Fwoosh!
A cloud of dust burst outward at impact, like a bomb going off.

At that moment, our long-rangers opened fire—debuffs, wind spears, fireballs, arrows, energy blasts, and so on. Since they were fired by experienced adventurers, all of the projectiles flew right to their target. Unfortunately, however, none of the attacks landed.
Flash.
Every shot disappeared in bursts of light before they even hit his body. It looked pretty similar to Nullification, the skill favored by Orcules’s leader, but there was one big difference.
I was still able to use my skills in my fight with him earlier.
So if it isn’t Nullification...
There was only one essence out there that granted its user a similar ability.
Tol-Lapupa’s.

This had to be a skill from the rank-one monster Tol-Lapupa—namely, Cosmic Protection, an incredibly overpowered skill that completely neutralized all long-range attacks before they could hit you. On top of that, since Cosmic Protection was a passive, I had no way of knowing which of Tol-Lapupa’s active skills he might have.
I didn’t expect him to have a rank-one essence.
Even as the weight on my shoulders grew heavier, the first thing I did was order everyone to stop making ranged attacks. They were just a waste of MP at this point.
...Though if I’m right about what skill this is, his own MP should decrease relative to the damage nullified.

Still, since this wasn’t a fight I intended to drag out, there was no point in trying to wear him down and drain his MP. Especially considering we were the ones who were going to need to fight through a horde of monsters after getting out of this village.
“You’re later than I expected, village chief.”
So I started talking. Buying even one additional second was a win at this point.

“Someone needs to clean up after all of you.” Oh, I didn’t actually expect him to reply. Still, it seemed the chief wasn’t planning to humor me for long. “It’s raining outside, so where are you off to in such a hurry?”
“Ah, well, I think I’ve got a case of cabin fever from being stuck in the village twenty-four-seven.”
“Stop now. I’m saying this for your own good.”
That earned him a derisive smile. “For my own good, huh?”
The chief delivered his final warning. “It’s not too late. If you stop now, I will overlook everything that happened today.”
That offer would’ve been oh-so-sweet if I were a rat who had been driven into a corner. As it stood, however, his words were nothing more than a confidence boost.
I was honestly starting to get worried that I’d made the wrong call.
But this was proof that I hadn’t.
Here he was, telling me, the guy who had just cracked his skull open and burned down his village, that he was willing to forgive me. There was no way that was normal.

It was so suspicious, in fact, that I had a feeling that if I hadn’t decided to run away today, some sort of “mysterious accident” would have befallen me sometime soon and I wouldn’t even have been surprised.
“Could I take a moment to think it over?” I tried to buy more time by pretending to actually consider his offer.
The chief, however, seemed to have caught onto my act. “Do you... take me for a fool?”
Uh... “A little?”
“...I am going to count down from three. Decide in that time.”
“Three’s too short. Let’s do four.”
The chief didn’t dignify that with a response and instead began to count. “...Three.”
Well, I guess I still managed to buy a little time. I wasn’t going to let him count down all the way anyway, so it wasn’t like an extra second mattered.
“Two.”
Dash.
Just as the chief was about to shout “one,” I rushed to him. There was still quite a bit of time left before Erwen’s attack was fully charged, and if a fight was unavoidable anyway...
Let’s go all in.

I wanted to give it my all and look at myself through the lens of a veteran who had played this game for nine years straight and had experimented with all sorts of character combinations. I wanted to see how strong this character I had invested so much time into was.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
And I wanted to see what its weaknesses were.

chapters.title: Chapter 535: Rainbow (2)
paragraphs: From rank one to rank nine, monsters of all kinds appeared on this island thanks to the “rainy season” event, and the chief had spent practically an eternity here. In other words, he had been able to farm for essences as much and as often as he wanted.
But the odds of all of his essences being high-ranking are extremely low.
That was the type of game Dungeon and Stone was. You could only get your hands on high-rank essences by slowly and steadily developing your character and absorbing low-rank essences first.
He probably had an essence of every rank since this island didn’t have a temple to get rid of them with.
The problem is that having a rank-one as his best essence gives him a massive advantage over us.

From here on out, the outcome of this fight depended on how smart the chief had been. If he consumed a bunch of random early-game essences without planning ahead and then tried to give himself a late-game boost with a single high-ranking essence, then he was just a mutt with no pedigree.
And his weaknesses will be obvious.

Of course, there was also the possibility that he’d done the opposite. If he filled his first few slots with essences that were relatively low-rank but had skills that were useful later on in the game like I did with Giantization...
Hmm, I guess it wouldn’t make that big of a difference, actually.
All it would do was make it a bit more difficult for me to find his weakness. No matter how I looked at it, that was all. There was no such thing as an invincible character in Dungeon and Stone.
Well, except for my Shield Barbarian, of course.

In any case, the question was: which of those two strategies did this guy go with? I carefully analyzed his every move. The only skill I could confirm he had so far was Tol-Lapupa’s Cosmic Protection.
Along with some sort of movement-related skill.

The split second before we crossed weapons and clashed, it looked almost like the chief’s body split in two, as if moving in different directions. It was like when a game suddenly lagged and the frames got glitchy.
Dash!
However, since I was studying him so intently, I was able to pick up on some details that helped me piece together what was going on.
Steam seemed to billow from the places where his feet met the ground.
Lightning covered his body.
Crackle!
And there were bursts of yellow light every time he touched down.
It’s Storm Lord’s Steps.

This was a rank-two skill and one that was hard to write off as a pure movement type. Not unlike Blink, it was characterized by the quick, sharp movements of its users, but it also inflicted the Paralysis effect on anyone in the surrounding area when he landed.
Bzzzt!
Vwoong!
Also, it significantly increased the user’s speed.
“S-Stop him— Huh?”
Along with granting him temporary invulnerability, of course.
Vwoosh!
One of the melee fighters nearby tried to swing their weapon at the chief in a panic, but the weapon just passed right through him as he Stepped away.
Is he going for Erwen?
Hah, that vile little...
He was really dead set on keeping us in this village. But I didn’t intend to just roll over and let him do whatever he wanted.
There are two ways to get around Step’s invulnerability.
The first way was to get him to attack. This was probably why the chief was ignoring the rest of us and only charging toward Erwen. As for the second way...
Three seconds.

It was less a way and more a natural limitation of Step—namely the fact that its invulnerability effect only lasted for three seconds. Of course, three seconds was more than enough time for him to stab a sword into Erwen’s neck and end it all.
Well, he won’t get the chance.
Even as the chief charged toward Erwen, eyes narrowed, my heart rate was slow and steady. Erwen was now in what I liked to call her Focus state.
[While active, all damage she receives will be circumvented through the consumption of Soul Power.]
In this state, Erwen was invulnerable too.
But considering he must know we’re analyzing him right now...
There was probably a reason he was showing off this skill now when he could’ve whipped it out at a more opportune moment later.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm. By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
I chained Transcendence and Eye of the Storm together. Fortunately, this skill combination could counter his.
He’s only immune to damage, not immune to being grabbed.
Eye of the Storm didn’t do any damage, so it wouldn’t trigger his defenses.
Whoosh!
Powerful winds spun around me, and the chief, who had been charging toward Erwen, was yanked back and pulled in my direction.
Crackle!
His three seconds seemed to have run out, as a wave of electricity exploded out and around the chief. That also meant he was no longer immune to damage.
Since I was already using Transcendence anyway, I decided to cast Swing for good measure.
[The range of all your attacks is tripled.]
My hammer grew like the Monkey King’s staff and smashed into the chief’s side.
However, the chief’s body defied the laws of physics. Rather than getting flung away, he ended up flattened against the end of my hammer thanks to the winds still pulling him in my direction.
It’s been a while since I’ve used this combo.
I smoothly adjusted the trajectory of my hammer. Like an amusement park ride, I slowly swung, lifted the chief over my head...
Boom!
And then slammed him into the dirt on my other side.
After being grabbed, he was now even further from Erwen than he was when he started running toward her.

The chief coughed up blood from his spot on the ground. Of course, with his incredible healing factor, he’d probably be fully recovered soon enough, but I must have gotten a good hit in, considering the way he stumbled a little as he got to his feet.
“Right. You did have that.”
“Oh, did you hear that from someone? I don’t think I ever mentioned it to you.”
The chief didn’t answer, instead looking past me at Erwen.
I tutted. It seemed he still hadn’t gotten with the program.
“Get real,” I said firmly. “You’ll never be able to reach her.”
“Unless I deal with you first?”
“Exact—!”
The chief disappeared before my very eyes.
By the time I was able to find him again with my lacking Agility, he was already at my flank, sword at the ready.
Clang!
I barely managed to raise my shield in time to block his thrust.

As someone who fought with a shield every day, I could immediately tell just by the impact. Whereas before, he was only leaving chips or tiny dents, this time around he did a significant amount of damage to my shield.
I think it’s nearly been pierced through.
Of course, I didn’t have to scramble to figure out what was happening. It wasn’t that the chief had used a new, unidentified skill on me—it was just that I was weaker than I was earlier.
[You have one minute remaining before Transcendence can be activated again.]

The amount of bladed-weapon resistance my passive Evolving Shell gave me was 50 percent. If I wanted to increase that to 75 percent, I could do so by using Iron Fortress. Using Transcendence—which enhanced passive skills by 1.5 times—on top of that would practically make me immune to bladed weapons.
Unfortunately for me, however, there was a limit to how immune I could get.
The maximum amount of resistance any character could have to bladed weapons was 85 percent. And for the next minute, my maximum resistance of 85 percent had decreased to 75 percent.
In other words, the 15 percent damage I was taking earlier has gone up to 25 percent.
Simple math stated the damage had only increased by 10 percent of the total damage he was dealing with, but in practice, that meant I was experiencing nearly double the damage I was taking before.
Bang!
As I continued to block the chief’s flurry of slashes, reinforcements swept in to back me up.
“I’ll help you out now.”
“Ah! Ah! I will too...!”
“Me too! Me too!”
It was Amelia, Missha, and Ainar—our clan’s melee fighters.
“Be careful. Don’t underestimate him.” I was a little worried about how this would play out, but I decided to give it a shot and fight him side by side with them.
After all, you could learn a thing or two by taking a few hits.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Power of the Abyss.]
[Missha Karlstein has cast Glacial Soul.]
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Wildness Control.]
I took on the role of main tank, and the three melee fighters used me as a wall and swung their weapons in a tight formation.
In the process, we were able to identify another one of the chief’s abilities.
Rumble!
A black and gray fog spread around the chief, lightning streaking through it.
Thunder Cloud.
A rank-two skill. It dealt lightning damage in a certain radius around the caster, and depending on how many targets it managed to hit, the skill’s cooldown decreased.
Still, since the only ones to get hit by the lightning were the four of us, the cooldown didn’t decrease that much.
Step’s cooldown is probably over, though.
“Get as far away as you can!”
The moment I came to that realization, I ordered the other three to get back as quickly as possible.
Dash!
As expected, the chief charged, his body once again invulnerable as lightning danced around him.
It took me a second too long to realize the bastard had switched targets.
“Ainar!”
With how close he was to her, it was already too late for me to try and use my grab attack to stop him.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Curl Up.]
Yeah, she had that going for her, at least.
[For three minutes, all of her resistances increase by 20x.]
The shining sword struck Ainar’s body and made a deep enough wound to expose the bone. However, as long as she didn’t die in one hit, it shouldn’t be a problem.
[For three minutes, her Natural Regeneration increases by 20x.]
Curl Up’s true strength lay in its healing boost.
But that means one person on our side is out of the fight already...
Even though we had only been fighting for a few seconds, Ainar was already out of commission. Still, that didn’t mean we hadn’t gotten anything out of this exchange.
I’ve got the general gist of his build now.
The chief was a Lightning Warrior.

Storm Lord’s Steps wasn’t much of an indicator on its own, but I was now sure after seeing him use Thunder Cloud. Even though Thunder Cloud could pass as any old skill, the passive he was using in conjunction with it wasn’t.
Lightning Affinity.
It was a passive that stacked every time he used a lightning-type skill and boosted all other lightning-type abilities depending on the number of stacks he had.
In any case, figuring this out was a huge deal. If the chief was a Lightning Warrior, then I could take a guess as to what that shining sword of his was.
It’s probably Supercharge.

Just like Power of the Abyss, it was a transformation ability—more specifically, it was a weapon enhancement-type skill. Its key characteristic was that, along with dealing physical damage, it got a boost from the other lightning-type skills you had.
Like following a trail of breadcrumbs, this also granted me a new piece of information.
If he has Supercharge, he probably has that passive as well...
I’d essentially identified four of his essences in one fell swoop.
But how does he have four essences of rank two and above?
Did he figure out a way to erase his other essences? His average rank was higher than I expected.
Still, though, if I were to give him an overall rating...
“Five points.”
Out of a possible ten, of course.
Even though he’d gone all in on the lightning theme, the compatibility of his essences wasn’t all that impressive.
Yeah, does he know how many overpowered combos you can get with Thunder Cloud?
Still, thanks to his high-ranking essences, his raw power was pretty high. Even so, I was honestly hoping that the rest of his essences were high-ranking as well.
Characters without decent balance always had tons of weaknesses to exploit.
All right, then let’s wrap things up for today...
One.
I reached the last second of my silent countdown and—
Fwooong!
The entire world was bathed in bright white light as something sliced through the air.
At that moment, Versyl, who had been standing off to the side, let out a shout for everyone to hear. “...S-She did it! The gate is open!”
It was time to get out of this damn village.

A burning village, a shattered gate, and an empty field that lay abandoned now that the adventurers had run out in droves. As the chief stared out at the destruction, one of the warriors of his village came up behind him.
“(Chief, the fire in the village has been taken care of.)”

The warriors began to discuss the damage done to the village and the number of casualties, but the chief didn’t acknowledge them. Of course he didn’t. It didn’t make a difference that a few of these monsters had died. At that moment, there was only one thing that required the chief’s undivided attention.
“I don’t know how he noticed.”
Bjorn Yandel. The most prolific adventurer of this age and the chieftain of the barbarians, one of the six great races. Along with a baron of the kingdom.
“...Just a little bit more time and we would’ve been in the clear.”
Like a mountain face slowly worn away by the wind, the chief’s emotions, which had been dulled over the years, began to show signs of peeking through the cracks.
And what he was feeling right now was regret.
However, he easily let go of the human emotion, his first in a very long while.
“(Chief, we will form a search party to chase after them.)”
“(It’s fine.)”
“(...Pardon? But—)”
“(Securing the village is of higher priority. And is... that thing still all right?)”
“(Yes. It is safe, just as you confirmed earlier.)”
Right, then everything was fine. Nothing had changed.
Things had just gotten a little trickier, that was all.
The chief closed his eyes and thought of the barbarian he had engaged in intense combat with but a moment ago.
“Bjorn Yandel...” He was a beastly man in many ways. In some sense, even more so than the monsters of this village. “He’ll be even stronger when we meet again,” he mumbled, almost to himself.
And as he did, another faint emotion flickered to life in his eyes.
It was joy.

chapters.title: Chapter 536: Rainbow (3)
paragraphs: It had been five days since the beginning of the rainy season. We made quick work of escaping the village and soon reached the surface.
Graaaaaah!
Kiyeeeeeek!
Woof! Woof! Woof!

As expected, it was pandemonium above ground. Monsters were everywhere, flinging blood and flesh all over the place as they fought each other. However, there was one obvious difference from the first day of the rainy season.
Crunch!
Although monsters continued to fall from the sky...
“...The number has gone down quite a bit.”

“A bit” didn’t cover it. Compared to the first day, there were practically no monsters falling anymore. It was like saying the rain had gone down a bit from four inches the other day to 0.04 inches today.
“That damn chief.”
There was no way he didn’t know about this. He had just refused to tell me.
After all, he needs people to think the rainy season is dangerous so that everyone stays dependent on the village and he can keep them there for longer.

I cursed him out in my head as relief washed over me—I’d made the right call getting out of there immediately. Even so, I quickly squashed those thoughts. As someone currently responsible for the lives of dozens of people, I had more urgent matters to attend to.
Thankfully... the chief didn’t chase after us.
I still didn’t know what he was scheming, but that, at least, reduced the number of things I needed to worry about right now.
“Get in formation!” I ordered, quickly establishing a clear goal for my allies to work toward. “We’re getting off this island!”
I blocked incoming monster teeth with my shield.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
Then, I used my hammer to break their jaws and open up a path.
“Wizards!” I commanded. “Take as many mana stones as you can!”

I mean, it’d be a waste to leave them behind, right? What kind of adventurers would we be if we ignored the mana stones quite literally covering this island? Before, we weren’t able to grab too many of them since I was wary of the village chief.
...But there’s no need for that anymore.
I once again marveled at how good hammering people was for my social life, especially in that it let me set clear boundaries in any relationship.
Swoop!

The wizards got to work chain-casting farming spells to gather the mountains of mana stones. It would eat into our overall combat power a bit, but that wasn’t that big of an issue right now. Since the number of monsters raining from the sky had decreased considerably, we had a lot more breathing room.
At this rate... it might actually be possible for us to get out of here without anyone dying.

This came as great news to me, as I had ordered us to leave the village even while fearing the worst. Now I could concentrate solely on plowing forward on the front lines and taking down the dangerous monsters in our path.
[You have killed an Iron Spirit. EXP +6]
[You have killed a Baphomet.]
[You have killed an Ainicorn. EXP +6]
[You have killed a Mud Golem.]
[You have killed a Heavenly Tree. EXP +5]
[You have killed a Dachyon...]
Ten minutes into my whack-a-monster session, Ainar delivered some more good news.
“Oh, oh! My soul! My soul! It’s being filled!” I’d expected her to have her moment soon, and it seemed she had finally leveled up. “I’ve grown stronger once more!”

Well, right now she was only “stronger” in the sense that her Soul Power had gone up. But still, that was good to know since it meant she now had a free essence slot again after absorbing the Hipramajent’s essence.
I think some of the members of the Hektz Clan and Armin Adventurer Group are also leveling up pretty consistently.
Overall, it seemed our group’s average number of essence slots had increased by one or two.
“Um... Lord Baron! There’s a rank-four essence over there...”
“From now on,” I said, issuing a special order, “Anyone can absorb whatever essences show up! I won’t care about anything below rank three!”

It was a bit of a shame to relinquish the first dibs and favorable share I’d secured for us, but when I thought about it, it wasn’t even that big of a loss. It wasn’t like we had time to collect every single one in a magic vial right now anyway, so any increase in our combat abilities was something to be celebrated.
“Yeeeaaah!”

This order also served to significantly increase the morale of my fellow adventurers. Just like how you could interpret a half-filled glass of water in multiple ways, fighting through hordes of monsters had transformed from a life-or-death situation into an opportunity.
Not bad.
Our spirits seemed to have lifted.
However, you couldn’t overcome danger with optimism alone.
Kiyoooooo!
In the distance, what looked to be a huge bird let out a shriek and landed right in our path. Though calling it a bird was a bit of a stretch.
Boom!
Yeah, I’d been wondering if things were going too smoothly.
...So you’re not going to let us off the island that easy, huh?

I let out a long sigh and squeezed my eyes shut for a moment before opening them again a second later. While I wished I could say I had been mistaken, unfortunately, the sight in front of me hadn’t changed.
Pure white feathers and wide-open wings, the body of a drake funneling into a long, giraffe-like neck... And at the end of that long neck, what looked to be a human face.
It was a pretty famous monster, so rather than disgust at its appearance, fear was the far more dominant emotion.
“I-It’s a Man-Faced Bird...!”
The creature in our path was the rank-two flying-type monster Man-Faced Bird.
It was also the first hurdle standing in the way of us getting off this island.
After swooping in from the sky and landing on the ground, its expressionless face turned in our direction before its eyes narrowed and rolled in their sockets.
Kihihihihihi.
I groaned. Seriously, why did Dungeon and Stone have so many of these horrifying freaks of nature?

The sense of disgust it evoked was different from the kind I felt when I came face-to-face with my first Corpse Golem. If I hadn’t built up a tolerance for encountering and fighting all kinds of monsters, I would’ve broken out in chills right now, unable to dole out a single order.
“Wizards! Form a protective barrier!”
The number of adventurers in Rafdonia who had experience fighting rank-two or above monsters could be counted on a single hand. I, however, had killed an untold number of them.
Well, that was only in the game, of course, but it was enough to give me the experience needed to make a split-second decision when we ran into one.
Vwoong!
The moment our wizards’ barrier opened up above us like an umbrella, the whites of the Man-Faced Bird’s eyes went black.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Song of the End.]
Yellow beams of light fell from the sky, so many that we had no hope of counting them all.
Boom! Bang! Bang! Bang! Bang!

It was as if the heavens themselves were enacting righteous judgment on the land. The pillars of light fell for about ten straight seconds, destroying everything around us. The damage wasn’t as high as you’d expect considering all the theatrics, though, so they didn’t break through the barrier.
Kihihihihi!
However, everywhere a pillar of light made contact with the ground, a baby Man-Faced Bird rose to its feet. They were a token summons.
“What are you all doing? Kill those things, now!”
We were now in a race against time.

In a minute, those baby Man-Faced Birds would grow to full size and be able to use skills too. Theoretically, their number could grow exponentially from there. As soon as those babies started to cast Song of the End themselves, it would be impossible for us to deal with them and—
“Yandel, give us an order!”
Ah, now wasn’t the time for me to stand around lost in thought.
“Erwen—” I began out of habit before stopping myself. She was currently recovering from using up all her MP getting us out of the village. There wasn’t much she could do in this fight.
...When did I start relying so heavily on Erwen?
If you didn’t have teeth, you chewed with the gums—that was the barbarian way.

“Emily! Missha! You two, follow me!” I began to run, and Amelia and Missha fell into step close behind me. “Ainar, you protect the main forces... Versyl! Get back there and handle support—I’m trusting your judgment on this!”
With that, the three of us ran forward, Amelia on my right and Missha on my left.
Huh, wait...
This formation was a lot like...
“Yandel, I’m going to warn you now before you get any ideas.”
“Huh?”
“If you try to do something like you did the other day... I’ll kill you.”
Tsk, so that was a no. “...I wasn’t going to.”
“I’d be... all right with it...”

Regardless of whether or not Missha was okay with it, though, I couldn’t force Amelia to cooperate when she’d already vehemently refused. This bird wasn’t as big as the Hipramajent anyway, so I couldn’t use that as an excuse either.
Thud!

Using Transcendence and Giantization together put me around eye to eye with it. Given the way it was staring at me like it had fallen in love at first sight, it seemed I’d managed to attract its aggro.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
And with that, I immediately barreled forward in a shield charge.
Kiyaaaaaak!
The Man-Faced Bird stumbled as I slammed into it with my full body weight. Taking advantage of the opening, Missha and Amelia closed in on its flanks and attacked its legs from both sides.
Flash!
At which point the blackened eyes of the Man-Faced Bird fired off a beam of light.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Imprint of Destruction.]
Yeah, I knew you’d pick me as your target.
I felt a surge of fiery pain pierce my chest.
Fwoosh!
[You will lose 1% of your max HP per second.]
All right, so in theory, I was going to die in a hundred seconds.
Even just the thought of this skill pisses me off.

The Imprint of Destruction was a single-target debuff that was impossible to dodge or block. It also didn’t even have a time limit. In other words, if you got hit by it, your options were either dying or killing the caster before the curse could kill you.
However, the strategy for dealing with it was actually pretty simple.
“Raaagh!”
You just had to tank it with the help of your Natural Regeneration and the support of a priest.
“Yandel! Are you okay?”
“Don’t worry about me! Keep stabbing!”
The Man-Faced Bird was a creature designed with battles of attrition in mind. If this went on for too long, it was guaranteed to beat us.
I did my best to hold its aggro so the damage dealers could keep attacking it without issue, and not long after, our long-rangers joined in on the fight to help keep it in check.
Kihihihihi...!
As the battle dragged on, the Man-Faced Bird whipped out a different skill.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Mimicry.]
The huge face attached to its huge body instantly changed into a different one. It was much larger than the face I was used to seeing, but it wasn’t hard to clock who it was.
“Oh!” cried Ainar excitedly. “It’s Emily! The monster turned into Emily!”
Mimicry randomly copied the abilities of a character within a certain radius.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Self-Replication.]
You little... Why did it have to take that skill?
“Oh! There are two... No, three Emilys!”
We somehow ended up with two more boss monsters to deal with, the clones using their skills as well as they joined in on the fight.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Song of the End.]
A few more pillars of light rained down.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Imprint of Destruction.]
[You will lose 2% of your max HP per second.]
Hah, so that effect was doubled now. Was our priest going to be enough to stave it off?
Well, there was no use dwelling on it.
Why does bad news always come in batches?
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Song of the End.]
One of the baby Man-Faced Birds that managed to reach full maturity joined in on the fun.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Imprint of Destruction.]
[You will lose 3% of your max HP per second.]
With that, I now had a triple helping of the curse.
Great. A priest wouldn’t be able to counter that kind of constant damage.
We’d found ourselves stuck between a rock and a hard place, but running away wasn’t an option as long as I had Imprint of Destruction stacked on me.
Meaning there was only one option.
“Die, please die!”
As a proud K-Barbarian, I adopted the mindset of our Admiral Yi Sun-sin and put life and limb on the line as I charged into battle.
[Your HP has fallen below 50%. All Resistance and Resilience stats have increased due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]
I didn’t have a lot of time left, so I doubled down and fought even harder.
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Guide.]
[The Man-Faced Bird has cast Decree of Protection.]
As the battle grew fiercer, the Man-Faced Bird also began to hit back just as hard.
[Your HP has fallen below 20%. All Resistance and Resilience stats have maxed out due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]
Boom!
Just as I started to sense that this battle was on the verge of reaching its end one way or another, I found myself on the receiving end of four pieces of news. Two were good, while two were bad.
The good news was pretty straightforward if we wanted to start there.
[You have killed a Man-Faced Bird. EXP +8]
The Man-Faced Bird finally died.
[No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck has been activated.]
And an essence dropped. The color was white.
It’s Mimicry.
It was no good as a core essence like Song of the End could have been, but since it was incredibly adaptable, this was a decent drop.
As for the bad news...
“Wh-what?!”
“A spear...? Why did a spear suddenly come out of—”
We weren’t the ones who landed the final blow on the Man-Faced Bird.
Thud!
Something emerged from the darkness and grabbed the spear that was stuck in the ground where the Man-Faced Bird’s head used to be.
It was hard not to recognize it. A relatively small stature that reached about ten feet high, with smooth, stone-colored skin on a humanoid body that looked almost like a statue...
“Titanus...! It’s a Titanus!”
Another rank-two monster had appeared. That was the first of the two pieces of bad news.
Damn it.
The second was the red spear that the Titanus was holding—No. 7: Milayel’s Verdurous Giant Spear.
That thing... why is it in that bastard’s hands...?
My eyes really couldn’t comprehend what they were seeing, but the rest of me calmly accepted reality for what it was anyway.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, grows furious upon noticing the mortal.]
This guy was a Guardian of the Rift.

chapters.title: Chapter 537: Rainbow (4)
paragraphs: Kalheum, the City of Light, was one of the Rifts on the eighth floor, and in its boss lair sat its Guardian—the Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel. I had no clue why he’d spawned on a regular floor like this, but to keep things brief, his most unique trait was that he used a Numbered Item despite being a monster.
That, and the fact that the drop rate of the Verdurous Giant Spear is 3 percent.

Although he dropped other Numbered Items as well, he dropped the single-digit Verdurous Giant Spear at a pretty high rate. I had a ton of memories of killing this guy when I was testing out my Spear Barbarian build. That spear was the best one for spear users.
It didn’t hurt that his essence was pretty good too.
Anyway, the real issue is why this guy is here, of all places.

As previously stated, we were guaranteed to get a reward if we managed to kill him. It would be incredible if he dropped an essence, and the spear would be amazing as well. However, the problem was in our current condition.
We can’t kill him.
I came to this conclusion immediately. It wouldn’t be impossible for us to defeat him with our current party comp, but as it stood, things were weighed heavily against us right now.
I need to consider that our priests are already spent up...
Not to mention, our main damage dealer, Erwen, was also out of commission.
No, that wasn’t even all. Luckily for us, we hadn’t had any casualties yet, but everyone was exhausted.
Woof! Woof! Bark!
Gruaaaaaah!
Honestly, with the monsters still prowling around us, we needed to worry more about survival and less about potential rewards.
“Yandel, what are we going to do?” Amelia asked, her expression grim as she looked out at Milayel.
It wasn’t even up for debate. “We’re going to charge toward the beach now.”
“Beach...? Ah, so we’re going to run—”
“We’re going to charge toward the beach.”
That was our only option at this point.
But before that, there’s something we need to do.
Even if we were going to run away, I had to decide what to do with that. I couldn’t just leave a rank-two essence behind on the ground.
There’s no chance we’re going to be able to get it in a magic vial.

My desire to bottle it away was strong, but it was too dangerous no matter how I looked at it. Getting an essence into a vial took too long. There was too much of a risk that something might go wrong in the meantime.
We needed to put it into someone’s body, and then we needed to run.
But who do I feed it to?
This was a decision best made after careful thought, but we didn’t have the luxury of time.
Bang!
I slotted myself in front of Milayel, blocked his spear with my shield, and shouted into the crowd behind me, “Myul Armin!”

Myul Armin—the captain of the Armin Adventurer Group, the leader of his clan, and an adventurer unique for his decision to go down the necromancer route, which specialized in debuffs and curses. To be honest, leaving such a precious essence to someone who was practically a stranger to me felt like a waste, but...
“You will take the Man-Faced Bird’s essence.”
This guy was the best fit for it. Since he also seemed to have leveled up recently, he should have an open essence slot as well.
There was a long, dazed pause. “...Pardon?” Myul Armin asked, apparently assuming he must have misheard me.
“Did you not hear me? Hurry up! We don’t have time!”

“U-Understood!” He quickly gathered his wits again and ran forward. Amelia ran alongside him, protecting him to make sure he got there safely. “I-Is this really okay...?” he called. “I’m not even one of your clan members...”
Ah, what was this guy going on about? I was having a hard time paying attention to him on account of the monster in front of me trying to impale me with a spear.
“It doesn’t matter! Hurry!” I barked.
“A-All right!”
At my command, Myul Armin reached forward and absorbed the essence.
All right, then we got everything we needed to...

After double-checking to make sure that the essence was absorbed, I shoved Milayel as hard as I could to put some distance between us, then turned to give a new order to the rest of the group. “What are you all doing?! Assume formation and get ready to move!”
There was no response.
“We’re charging straight toward the beach right now!”
“What...?”
Seriously, were these fools asleep at the wheel?
“Run!” I commanded.
“Ah, yes—! Everyone, assume formation! We’re getting out of here now!”
Tsk, some respect for this barbarian baron, please.
Huff, huff...

I let out hot puffs of air as I ran. Ah, of course, I wasn’t at the front of the pack this time but rather at the very back. When you were being chased by something, the back was the most dangerous place to be.
“I will not let you go, mortal.”
Just like in the game, this guy spoke like a real person. The issue was that he only said that one sentence and kept repeating it like a parrot.
Man, how many times have I heard it at this point?
I ran a few tests by trying to talk to it as we fled, but I was never able to get it to say anything new. Honestly, I couldn’t even tell if it had any intelligence or not.
The monsters in the chief’s village definitely seemed like they were self-aware.

Once again, I found myself struck by how unique the chief’s village was. Honestly, most monsters were like this one behind me, even the Vampire Duke Kealunus in the Bloody Citadel. The Knight of the End I encountered in the White Temple also spoke like a person, but it wasn’t able to hold a conversation—
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Recursion.]
Excuse you, I was still thinking here.
When I heard that dangerous whooshing sound behind me, I whipped around to block the incoming attack with my shield.
Bang!
That damn spear. Every time I blocked it, I could feel my shield cracking in real-time, and since it was a single-digit Numbered Item with its unique skills, the force behind each thrust was deadly.
Well, it’s only using one skill at a time, so I guess things could be worse.

That was because Milayel had the Guardian role. Guardians of the Rift had a set pattern to their attacks as well as specific triggers to change patterns, such as taking damage or someone using equipment near them. As long as you didn’t trigger one of those conditions, they’d repeat the same set of actions indefinitely.
If this were a regular Titanus, I wouldn’t have even been able to run away like this.
That didn’t mean that Milayel was an easier opponent, however. The skill it used in its first phase was nothing to scoff at.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Recursion.]
Recursion was a simple throwing skill that amplified the damage dealt by a projectile and guaranteed a hit with target lock-on. However, it also had a far more troublesome trait.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has retrieved the Verdurous Giant Spear.]
When you used this skill, no matter how far away the projectile ended up, it always returned right to the caster’s hand.
[Until the end of combat, the strength of Recursion slightly increases.]
That, and it was a sort of stackable skill in a way, becoming stronger and stronger the more the caster used it.
Clang!
Because of that, my shield, which had even been able to block the chief’s sword, was starting to look like Swiss cheese.
Hah, and it’d be tough to mend it down here.

I spared a quick moment to sigh while looking at my messed-up shield, then checked on how the front of the pack was doing. Although I was following from the very back, thanks to Giantization, I could easily see over everyone’s heads.
They’re doing a good job.
It wasn’t like I’d expected them to break formation or have problems clearing the way just because I wasn’t out in front. Rather, I’d expected them to handle themselves fine, and they were.
So why was I feeling a little dejected about it?
Whatever...I need to focus on my own job.
Stoically doing your duty with or without the praise of others was the way of the warrior. And so, I continued to keep Milayel in check as he continued to hammer us from behind.
“It’s the ocean!”
From between the dense trees, the cliffside appeared, and as we sprinted down it, we saw the beach we dropped anchor on when we first got to the island.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Recursion.]
This guy wasn’t giving up. The spear embedded itself into my shield and immediately disappeared into particles of light, then flew right back at me at a frightening speed.
Stab!
For some reason, however, I felt a surge of pain from my shoulder this time around. I thought I had raised my shield enough to block it...
“Agh—!”
But it turned out the shield already had so many holes that it had just flown straight through one of them.
“B-Bjorn!”
“Yandel! Are you all right?”
Missha and Amelia, who had been out in front, rushed back to me in shock. Versyl also tagged in for the priest who had bottomed out on divine power and pulled out a potion.
I brushed them all off. “Later. We need to get the boat onto the water first.”
We still had some time before the spear got back to Milayel, so I rushed through the crowd and onto the beach before they could argue.
“Ummm...”
“Are you... okay?”

The adventurers who had been clearing the way looked surprised by my gaping wound. Well, it’d be weirder watching a barbarian with a huge spear in his shoulder running past them, so they could deal with a hole or two.
Splash!

After summoning the boat, I kept up Giantization long enough to scoop people up and onto the deck. Then, once everyone was on board, I snapped back to my normal size to get on myself, and we dumped a bunch of mana stones into the mana propulsion system so we could get the hell out of there.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Recursion.]
The spear flew in a final time and struck me right in the gut.
“M-Mr. Yandel...!”
“Baron!”
Ouch, what the—
Even as I doubled over, clutching my stomach, I lifted my head enough to glare up at the guy standing on the beach.
Yeah, I’ll remember your face...
“I’ll see you later.”
A barbarian never let go of a grudge.
Swoosh!

We sliced through the silver waves. The boat was cramped with so many people onboard, but no one complained. Just being able to sit down and take a break was an incredible relief right now, and we were all happy to plop down wherever there was space. However, I noticed a few of us had dark shadows on our faces.
“One death...”
During our escape from the island, one of the warriors from the Hektz Clan died.
I sighed. Warriors were always the ones who died at times like these. As a fellow warrior myself, I couldn’t help the bitter taste in my mouth at the news.
“This isn’t appropriate to say, I know... but it’s a miracle. It’s genuinely miraculous that only one person died.”
“Yeah, that’s true,” I conceded. “What was the name of the person who died?”
“Shellyan Emerton.”
I remembered her face as soon as I heard her name. Although I hadn’t talked with her much outside of battle, she caught my eye since warrior women were a bit of a rarity.
She had always had a bright smile on her face.
“And her body?”
“We were able to retrieve it.”
“That’s good to hear...”
With that, I gathered the others and held a funeral for the dead warrior. Although everyone was exhausted, no one argued.
Fwoosh!
Of course, since this was a funeral inside the labyrinth, and on a boat no less, we had to keep things simple. We laid her body on a fireproof cloth and burned her. We then put her ashes in an urn.
Boom! Crunch! Thud!
Throughout the funeral, monsters continued to fall periodically from the sky. Well, since we had a barrier around the boat, they just slid off and fell into the ocean.
Drip.
Like a window on a rainy day, the blood on the barrier pooled into droplets and dripped down the sides.
“Rest easy.”
“Haha, don’t mope too much. There’s no telling when we’ll follow her.”
“Tsk, haven’t you ever heard the phrase ‘don’t tempt fate’?”

Even in the most solemn of moments, adventurers could always make light of dark situations. We were people who lived our lives on the razor’s edge of death, after all. As such, no one chastised the ones joking around.
We all knew that people coped with loss in different ways.
“That’s it,” I said. “Take a break. And good work, everyone.”
Once the funeral was over, everyone went back to rest.

Well, the wizards weren’t able to relax completely since they had to maintain the barrier, but it was much easier than when they had to maintain it on the island. After we got out onto open waters, they were able to rig the boat’s mana propulsion system to connect to their mana circuits too.
We have enough mana stones now, and fewer monsters are falling from the sky than expected. If nothing goes terribly wrong, I think we can hold out pretty well until the rainy season ends...
Could I finally relax?

Even as I asked myself that, waves of interweaving thoughts continued to push and pull at my attention. In the end, I just leaned up against the wall, rooted through my sub-space for a temporary shield, and took it out. As a grade-three shield, it was naturally much worse than the shield I had been using. Back when I got it, I had limited funds, and I honestly doubted a day would ever come when I would need to use it.
But it seems today’s the day.
I was giving the shield a wry smile when someone approached me.
“Lord Baron,” greeted Myul, the captain of the Armin Adventurer Group.
“What’s wrong? Why aren’t you resting?”
“I apologize for interrupting your rest. But... I wish to ask you something.”
“Go on.”
Even after receiving my permission, Myul hesitated for a moment. “Why did you do that?”
“What do you mean?”
“I mean... the Man-Faced Bird’s essence. Why did you give it to me?”
Ah, so that was what he was losing sleep over, huh? The answer was actually pretty simple.

First of all, Ainar, Amelia, Erwen, and Missha weren’t even in the running for that essence. The essences they would absorb in the future had already been decided. Versyl, meanwhile, couldn’t absorb it in the first place since she was a wizard.
I guess Auyen could’ve been an option...

But it honestly wasn’t an essence that suited Auyen either. He could have used Mimicry to copy the skills of the monsters we were fighting and change up the battlefield, but that was pretty much it. Giving it to him would have been the equivalent of wasting the passive that formed the crowning jewel of the Man-Faced Bird’s essence.
And so, in the end, I decided to go with Myul.
“Of everyone here, you’re the one who can use that essence to its fullest potential.”
“Is that... Is that all?”
In truth, that wasn’t all.

According to our agreement, the Armin Adventurer Group had a certain claim over the loot. Since they had taken a rank-two essence now, I could use that to strong-arm them next time we got our hands on one later.
But there’s no need to admit that out loud.
So I shrugged. “Yeah, that’s all.”
“But! We’re strangers you just met—”
“How are we still strangers? We’re already comrades.”
“We’re... We’re comrades...?”
“Yeah, you got a problem with that?”
Myul Armin didn’t answer my innocent question for a long while.
“Lord Baron, you...” When he finally spoke, his voice was faint. He seemed like he had something to say, but after another beat, he shook his head. “No. I’ll be going now. Please rest.”
It was hard to tell for sure, but he looked like he had come to some sort of decision.
It had been six days since the start of the rainy season. After escaping from the island, our voyage had been pretty smooth.

Monsters were still falling from the sky, and we had to kill the ones that kept trying to climb up onto our ship from the ocean, but compared to what we had to go through to escape that island, this was nothing.
In any case, now that I had some peace and quiet, I finally had the time to regroup and rework our plan.
All right, I’ve decided.
I took out the pendant I had stored in my sub-space for safekeeping, and Missha, who was next to me, immediately perked up with sparkling eyes.
“Uh, Bjorn? That’s... Are you... giving that back to m-me...?”
What was she talking about? Had she been pining after it all this time?
Noticing the hunger in her eyes, I quickly put the pendant back into the sub-space before she could get her hands on it.
No. 7777: Garphas’s Necklace.
It was about time to get some use out of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 538: Rainbow (5)
paragraphs: Garphas’s Necklace.

This was the Numbered Item I obtained under the name of Knight Crusher at my first-ever noble banquet. However, because I had gotten my hands on it so early in the game, I hadn’t had any hope of actually using it for years. To do so, you needed to have a solid financial backing first.
But considering how many mana stones we’ve been getting...

I concluded that I would be able to collect the target amount within a month or two. Furthermore, there wasn’t a single thing on Basement Floor One that could give me as much of a boost as this item could right now. In a sense, the progress it could potentially afford far outclassed anything an essence could do.
So the most important thing from here on out is getting enough mana stones...

Even now, the mounds of mana stones that were no doubt littered around the chief’s island sparkled in my mind’s eye. If we could go back and sweep them all up after the rainy season was over, that would shorten my timeline considerably.
Still, that would be too dangerous, right?
...Wait.
A sudden thought struck me. “Wyatt Hektz. Come here for a second.”
“...You called?”
“It’s nothing big—I just want to ask you a few things. You said you arrived on that island of giants during the rainy season, right?”
“Yes, it was on the very first day.”
“I remembered right, then. Anyway, was Giant Island riddled with monsters like this island was?”

“...Yes?” Hektz confirmed, still looking confused by this line of questioning. Regardless, he proceeded to explain how they witnessed “monsters who left behind corpses” and “normal monsters” fighting to the death.
I took this in. “Isn’t that odd, though?”
“Pardon...?”
“If all the monsters were killing each other, shouldn’t the island have been covered with mana stones?” When we arrived on Giant Island, all we found were monster corpses—no mana stones.

“Now that you mention it, that’s true,” Hektz realized. “I didn’t give it any thought back then... but just like the island with the village, the island we were stuck on should have had plenty of mana stones as well.”
“When did you guys first start venturing out of the cave after taking shelter?”
“It was about ten days after the rainy season ended. But back then, we didn’t even know whether it actually had an ‘end.’”
“I see.”

I had even more questions now. Where did all those mana stones go? No, in the first place, if the rainy season happened on a regular schedule, the ocean floor should be covered in them as well by now.
Crunch!

Even now, monsters were falling into the ocean and dying on impact, disappearing into bursts of light. Over hundreds of years, the mana stones they left behind should have piled up and into underwater mountains.
But when I was down there, I didn’t see anything special.
Hmm, should I hop into the ocean for a second to take a peek?
The thought flashed through my mind, but I asked the wizards for their advice before committing to it.
“Yes... That’s something I’ve also been quite curious about.”
“Let’s check the bottom of the ocean right now!”
“But there’s all sorts of monsters in the water...”
“Does that matter? We could discover a new law of nature down there!”
“Wait!” a voice cried. “There’s a way to check without going underwater!”
At Versyl’s proclamation, the excited wizards who were just about to throw themselves overboard stopped to hear her out.

“Let’s use the mana stones we have to test it,” she said, taking out one of the mana stones she had on her, tying a string to it, and lowering it beneath the silver waves. After that, she used all sorts of spells to monitor its condition underwater.
Thanks to these tests, we were able to obtain a new piece of information. I had no idea why it took us so long to figure this out, but...
“...It’s gone?”
“The only thing left is the string.”
Mana stones that fell into the ocean apparently disappeared.
The experiment birthed all sorts of theories and questions.
“Could it be that the ocean’s silver coloring is because it absorbed all of those mana stones?”
“Hmm, I don’t think we have enough evidence to connect the two phenomena right now.”
“Agreed—if it’s because the ocean absorbed the mana stones, then the ocean should give off a mana signature of its own, but that’s not the case.”
“Hmm... So if the mana stones dissolve and disappear in the ocean, then what about the ones on land?”
I used to be someone who enjoyed intellectual discussions like this. Perhaps I had lost my taste for it after living as a barbarian for so long.
“Um... Lord Baron, what do you think of all this?”
“Ugh... My head...”
For some reason, my head started to pound the longer I listened to their back-and-forth, so I bowed out with the excuse that I wasn’t feeling well.
Well, the wizards should be able to handle the research side of things on their own.
I escaped from the wizards and chatted with my companions to pass the time.
Crunch!
On the seventh day of the rainy season, the number of monsters falling from the sky decreased even further.
After about 11:50 p.m., not a single monster fell.

Hmm... Is this clock off by ten minutes? The thought occurred to me, but we decided to wait and drop the barrier at the agreed-upon time anyway. If a single monster ended up falling on the boat, it would damage the deck. It was better to be safe than sorry.
Tick, tock.

The hand on the clock moved. Everything around me grew quiet as I focused on its ticking path. Slowly, I raised my head to look around and noticed that everyone was also looking at their own clocks. It was like we were all counting down to the new year.
Tick, tock.
We waited in silence, and as time continued its endless march, the moment we were waiting for finally arrived.
The end of this damned rainy season.
“It’s midnight!”
“Is it over?”
The adventurers on deck began to murmur amongst themselves, and I quickly gave the order.
“Drop the barrier!”

With that, the wizards undid the umbrella-like barrier surrounding the boat, and it felt like the world opened up around us. In a way, it kind of did, what with how the barrier had been drenched in blood from all the monsters falling and dying on it.
“M-Mister!” While I was walking up to the bow to enjoy the fresh air for the first time in several days, Erwen shouted down at me from the crow’s nest. “Look! Look over there!”

What now? I glanced up at the crow’s nest to see Erwen pointing into the distance. As I turned my head to look where she was pointing, I stopped in my tracks. It wasn’t just me, either. All the other adventurers who had turned to look froze too.
“...A rainbow?”
Over the wide, endless silver ocean, a rainbow had opened up as if to celebrate the end of the rainy season.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, purple...
The array of light was pleasant even at a glance. And since we were gazing up at it while standing atop a boat dotted with monster blood, the colors looked even more vibrant than usual.

However, we couldn’t just stand around staring at it with our mouths open. We were adventurers. Be it a rainbow or a piece of hell on earth, if we saw something unusual, our first instinct was to run over there to see if we could make money off of it.
“Auyen! Jot down the direction of the rainbow!”
“Pardon? Oh...Yes!”
We first figured out where the rainbow started. The timing of its appearance was way too suspicious to ignore.
Something that can only be seen if you’re out on the ocean right after the rainy season ends...

What were the odds this was just a natural phenomenon? What was more, the rainbow we were looking at had a rather unique shape. If regular rainbows formed arcs or curves, this one looked like a pillar of light that was shooting straight into the sky. It was like a marker in a game meant to notify the player that there was something special hidden there.
“Twenty-one degrees from our current position, and thirty-four degrees from Stone Island! As for the distance... I can’t tell yet!”
Auyen rattled off a few pieces of jargon I couldn’t follow, but there was one thing I understood. He had succeeded in ascertaining the direction it was in.
But we don’t know how far away it is yet...
That was a bit of a problem. Should we turn our boat in the direction of the rainbow right now, or should we keep heading toward our original destination?
“Huh? The rainbow is disappearing!”
Just as I was contemplating our next move, the rainbow in the distance began to fade away before vanishing entirely. The whole display only lasted about five minutes.
So, after the rainy season ends, we only get five minutes to see it...
Wasn’t that a sign that this was exactly what we were looking for? But even so, I didn’t give the order to turn the ship.
“Huh? Bjorn? Aren’t we heading toward the rainbow?”
Ainar seemed confused by my decision, but as the leader of this group, I felt it was the only logical choice.

Giant Island, Tree Island, or even Library Island—we hadn’t cleared any of them yet. We needed to improve our specs before anything else, and since we knew the general direction of the rainbow, we could always head there another time.
“Auyen, how long until we reach Giant Island?”
“We’ll arrive there in about three hours!”

And so, we maintained our course for three more hours. When we finally made landfall, the first thing we did was stand there, jaws dropped. Man, I knew I had a good feeling about coming straight here.
“...Mana stones.”
Thousands of mana stones littered the island’s beaches.

The reason I had chosen to visit this particular island again was simple. Of the islands we had seen so far, this was the only one with a portal stone. That really big giant we saw at the end still worried me a little, but I concluded that there were more secrets to be found here if we were willing to take the risk and explore it.
Ba-dump!
But forget whatever secrets this island may or may not have—my heart started to pound as soon as I saw the mana stones covering the beach.

Of course, compared to Chief Island, there were far fewer mana stones per square foot on the ground. But Giant Island was several times larger than Chief Island. What if we were able to collect all the mana stones here?
“This is unbelievable...”
There was a chance that I could even reach the amount I needed with this island alone.

With that, we all got off the boat and went to work picking up all the mana stones that were lying there waiting for us. Getting them wasn’t as easy as I was hoping it’d be, of course. The rainy season had just ended, so there were still monsters prowling around.
Maybe it’s because they’re the ones who survived the rainy season, but these monsters are all a pain to deal with.
The ones left were all at least rank four. On top of that, a few new monsters with weird essence combinations were also popping up, making for some incredibly tough fights.
However, we were also slowly but surely starting to get stronger. Myul Armin was the best example of that.
[Myul Armin has cast Supersensitive Skin. The damage taken by his target increases by 30%.]
[Myul Armin has cast Eternal Frailty. The target’s physical stats decrease by 30%, and the effectiveness of all curses used on it will increase by 1.5x.]
This guy was a necromancer who specialized in curses and debuffs. His active skills fell under that specialty, and his summons stuck to the theme as well.
[Myul Armin has summoned Spirinsect.]
Spirinsect, for example, was a summon that didn’t do any physical damage, but every hit it landed drained the target’s MP by a set amount.
[Myul Armin has summoned Corrosive Hound.]
Every time this one bit a target, it lowered its resistance by a set amount.
[Myul Armin has summoned the Self-Destructing Spirit of Vengeance.]

That one was a summon that closed in on its target before blowing itself up to inflict curses on everything in the surrounding area. This was why I gave him the Man-Faced Bird’s essence. Its passive skill Mother Bird was particularly useful for necromancers.
[A summon within your range has been dispelled. You have regained 80% of the Soul Power used to summon it. The corresponding skill’s cooldown has been decreased by 80%.]
It was an essential skill to pick up if you wanted to climb the necromancer ranks. With just this one essence, Myul Armin had become over five times stronger than before.
A rank-two core essence had that kind of effect on people.
[Myul Armin has summoned the Self-Destructing Spirit of Vengeance.]
[Myul Armin has summoned the Self-Destructing Spirit of Vengeance.]
[Myul Armin has summoned the Self-Destructing Spirit of Vengeance.]
[Myul Armin has summoned the Self-Destructing Spirit of Vengeance.]
[Myul Armin has summoned the Self-Destructing Spirit...]
With the MP refund and the decreased cooldown time, he was able to chain summon as many spirits as he wanted.
Boom!
Since this one didn’t deal physical damage, to begin with, there wasn’t much of a visible effect, but the curses were stacking as the explosions continued.
It’s so much easier to hunt monsters when they all have huge debuffs working against them.

Also, Myul Armin ended up being the perfect person to have around in our current situation. His was a class that shined more when you were fighting a single strong enemy rather than multiple weaker ones.
“You worked hard, Myul.”
“Worked hard... I’m not worthy of such praise.”
Hmm, recently, he seemed to be having trouble making eye contact with me. He also always called me Lord Baron and had been stiff and sort of distant.
Is he trying to pull back now that he got everything he needed out of me? Just in case I try to get him to pay me back?
The thought was kind of depressing, but since that could just be my own biases talking, I decided to keep an eye on him for a while longer before jumping to any conclusions.
One day, two days, three days...
We spent several days picking up all the mana stones we could get our hands on and fighting off all sorts of monsters.
Before we knew it, three days had passed since the end of the rainy season. And it was in the middle of gleefully scooping up even more mana stones that we got some bad news.
“The mana stones... They’re disappearing.”
The mana stones that hadn’t been picked up yet were starting to disappear like fruit rotting away back into the soil.
“How interesting... The mana is definitely being dispersed... but I can’t find even a trace of where it’s disappearing to.”
Whatever the reason, this was an unfortunate development for us, but there was also a bright side.
“Versyl, how many mana stones have we collected so far?”
“Uh, if I were to do the conversion according to the rates set by the exchange ... I think we have about a billion stones?”
In other words, a profit large enough to gamble on the necklace.

chapters.title: Chapter 539: Verdurous Giant Spear (1)
paragraphs: It had been three days since the end of our second rainy season. Though if I measured from the day we entered the labyrinth, today was day seventy-four.
We’ve gathered about a billion mana stones from this island, and that along with the six hundred million we gathered before that...
Made for a total of 1.6 billion mana stones.

Of course, that money had been gathered by dozens of people, and after we split it between all of us, my cut would be much lower. Thankfully, however, this problem was resolved by a simple discussion with the other members of our group.
Now, there was only one thing left to do.
