“Everyone can rest as much as they want! We won’t be doing anything for the rest of the day!”

After having finished collecting the mana stones across the whole of Giant Island, our group returned to the cave. Naturally, it was the very same cave that the Hektz Clan had been staying in when we first rescued them, and the one where we found the headstone.
Now that I think about it, we got really lucky.

We had completely mapped out Giant Island. There were quite a few other caves around, but this was the only one so deep that it went underground. It also had a special characteristic that meant monsters didn’t approach the entrance for some reason. It was honestly the safest place we could set up camp.
And the Hektz Clan had managed to find it in the middle of all that chaos.
Please let some of that luck rub off on me as well.
What I was about to do weighed heavily on my mind, as it relied almost entirely on luck. And the issue was that I wasn’t all that lucky. Or, well, in truth...
My luck is average.

It was only recently that I began thinking this way. After all the misfortunes I went through as a child, there had been multiple times throughout my life that I was convinced I was cursed. But thinking back on it, I wasn’t particularly unlucky. Even after going through all of those things, I was still alive.
“It seems he’s going to start soon.”
“Bjorn! I don’t know what you’re doing, but good luck!”
In fact, I was quite lucky to have met such great people during my lifetime.
Erwen, my night companion turned friend from my first adventure.
Ainar, my trustworthy fellow barbarian warrior.
The allies I made at the Bloody Citadel fighting against that mutant, Raven and Hikurod.
Team Half-Wit’s Missha, Rotmiller, and Dwalkie.
In those early years when I truly had nothing, meeting them went beyond something as simple as “luck.”
Let’s not get my hopes up.
I shook off my cowardly inclination to hand off this responsibility to my lucky teammates, like Ainar and Missha.
I am a lucky man.
I repeated that in my heart again and again. What I needed right now wasn’t doubt, but an unshakeable certainty.
I...was a lucky man.
It was then that the shift happened.

Something finally clicked in my mind. My jaw, which had been clenched with nerves, relaxed ever so slightly, and my hands stopped their subtle shaking. I’d reached what could only be described as a moment of enlightenment. The question of the half-full glass... It wasn’t up to the people around me to decide if the glass was happy or unhappy. The only person who could decide that was me and me alone.
“...I’m lucky.”
“Huh?”
“What’s he talking about? He hasn’t done anything yet.”
Hadn’t done anything?

Anything in this world was up for the taking if you just put your mind to it. Just as the future engraved on the Records Stone was bound to come true, the moment I made up my mind was the moment my future was decided. That was a universal truth and an unchanging fact.
“Heh heh...”
However, since there was no way these fools could understand all that even if I explained it, I simply laughed and saved my breath.
“There’s a cool breeze today.”
The spiritual energies of the universe embraced me like an old friend.
“The sun is warm.”
Certainty and certainty alone filled my heart.
“We’re inside a cave. What is he talking about the wind for...?”
“Maybe he’s trying to say he’s chilly?”
“But then he said the sun’s warm...”
“Mister... Are you sick?”

I ignored the ignorant questions of the unenlightened mortals around me and picked up one of the mana stones laid out on the ground. Then I slowly lifted it to the necklace. There wasn’t a single reason to rush.
Water is water, and the wind is the wind.
It was that obvious to me.
Shaaa!
My future was guaranteed.
[The gift of the Great Alchemist Garphas senses the power of creation in your offering.]
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
All right, let’s do this.
No. 7777: Garphas’s Necklace.
The way this necklace worked was simple. Whenever someone touched the necklace with a mana stone, it absorbed the stone and in turn randomly generated bread, water, metal, and other such things.
Like so.
[You have crafted Stonebread.]

Every time a mana stone went in, the item shown on the gem of the necklace changed, and you could take out the item if you wanted it. Since there was no point in taking out stonebreads, I didn’t bother and kept spinning the wheel.
But... why hasn’t the item changed yet?
What was happening?
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stone...]
Seriously, six stonebreads in a row? Even though these were rank-five mana stones and not even rank-nine ones?
When using rank-five mana stones, the probability of getting back stonebread is only around 4 percent. This means the probability of that happening six times in a row is...
I choked.

The moment I ran the numbers, my Zen Barbarian mode nearly shattered, but I managed to school myself with my disciplined mind. Early gacha rolls were all about stacking the odds in your favor, anyway.
“Bjorn! Are you all right? Clear your throat!”
“...Move. I’m fine.”
...Doubt was the mind-killer, a deadly poison that ate away at your heart and only made life harder.
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
That was why I set aside my feeling heart and continued to mechanically insert mana stones into the necklace.
Not just six times, but nine times in a row...?
No, that didn’t mean anything.
The future was already decided.
[You have crafted Steel Ingot.]
Yeah, the probability is just that—a probability.
The thing I was looking for was bound to show up. All I needed was to have faith.
“Oh! Bjorn’s expression changed...!”
“Oh, I’ve heard a tale of this! When His Lordship wears that expression, it is a sign that he truly believes in himself!”
No matter what happened, I kept my cool and kept on feeding the gacha mana stones.
Minutes passed.
I think it should start about now...
[You have crafted an Iron Longsword.]

Just then, the necklace that had been spitting out bread, metals, bricks, and other random nonsense finally produced some proper equipment. This didn’t particularly come as a surprise to me. Unbeknownst to most, there was a hidden trick to Garphas’s Necklace.
The equivalent of about 7,777 rank-nine mana stones, give or take.

In other words, around 1.55 million stones when converted to Rafdonia’s currency. Once you fed the necklace the mana stones needed to add up to that amount, it was guaranteed to spit out a random useful item.
[You have crafted a Lithinum Breastplate.]
This would repeat every 1.55 million stones. I must have already spent 3.1 million stones to get this lithinum breastplate.
That’s not too bad for an early roll, actually.
Of course, that was only a passing thought. I didn’t care about a good early roll since I had no intention of stopping here.
“Huh? Bjorn! Why are you putting more in? It’s not just a stonebread this time! What a waste.”
Yeah, no, if I stopped here and pulled out an item, I would need to start stacking from the bottom all over again.
I had a feeling Ainar would keep bugging me if I didn’t give her some kind of bare minimum response, but thankfully, Amelia spoke up in my stead before I even had to open my mouth.
“Fenelin, quiet down,” she said from her spot next to me. “Don’t disturb him.”
“Oh, but I just...I was just wondering why...”
“Zip it.”
“Ah, fine... I won’t bother him...”
This was perhaps the best demonstration of why establishing a proper hierarchy was important. After the beating she took in the Witch’s Hut, Ainar was especially reluctant to argue with Amelia.
Anyway, back to business.
[You have crafted a Redwood Longbow.]
Next up was a longbow made with grade-two materials.
[You have crafted an Iron Shield.]
Then came a plain old shield that came nowhere near approaching the quality of my own, and so on.

After rolling nine similarly useless pieces of equipment, it was about time for the tenth to pop up. More precisely, the moment I put around 15.55 million stones in cash, or something like 777,777 rank-nine mana stones, into the necklace, something new happened.
[You have crafted No. 9981: Castaway’s Ring of Vigor.]
A Numbered Item appeared for the first time.
Of course, financially speaking, this wasn’t exactly a big win. It wasn’t like all Numbered Items were worth a handsome sum.
This one was around two million stones, right?
I had somehow gotten an item that cost even less than the lithinum breastplate from earlier. Not that it mattered, of course. I kept going.
[You have crafted a Cloud Candy.]
[You have crafted a Training Magic Staff.]
[You have crafted a High-Density Mana Herb.]
[You have crafted Wyvern Leather Armor.]
[You have crafted a Temporary Use Spell (Light Orb) Scroll...]
It was all medicines, equipment, materials, and the like. I barely registered and skipped past most of them as I continued to pour mana stones into the necklace.
Then, suddenly, I froze for one reason and one reason alone.
[You have crafted Mystium Ingot.]
What the...? A grade-six metal?
Considering the common scroll that popped up right before it, I suppose you could call this regular gacha probability at play, but...
“I-It’s mystium!”
“I-Isn’t the price of one ingot in the hundreds of millions?”
If I stopped here, I would be able to profit tens of millions off of this thing.
Damn it.

I was trying to get all the trashy items out of the way now, so why was I getting so lucky in the early game? I sighed inwardly and let go of any lingering hesitation. And then, I went back to putting mana stones into the necklace.
“Ahhh!”
“Huh?!”
The crowd around me let out shouts of shock.
Hey, don’t jinx me.
Though I couldn’t really blame them. How could little minds hope to understand the thoughts of a giant? And so, I continued to push onward for quite a while despite their lack of support.
Flash!
About 155 million stones in cash, or 7,777,777 rank-nine mana stones later, the necklace suddenly turned red for the first time.
[Garphas’s gift has been damaged due to excess amounts of mana.]
Put simply, after this round of gacha was over, I wouldn’t be able to spin anymore.
“Bjorn... is the necklace okay? I think there’s a crack going through it now...”
It wasn’t okay at all. But like I said at the start, I had no intention of backing down.
Let’s look at what I got.
I checked the surface of the red gem. Probability-wise, there was a chance I might pull a single-digit Numbered Item here. If something good popped up now, I could cut my losses and quit while I was—
[You have crafted No. 535: Polar Region Shield.]
Polar Region Shield was a shield I used pretty often for my Shield Barbarians before I could get my hands on the best shield in the game.
Nah.
The shield wasn’t bad, but a triple-digit here?
Who’re you trying to scam?
I quickly passed on it.

Although it was the most valuable item of all the ones that appeared thus far, no one around me freaked out about what I’d done. They probably didn’t even know what it was. After all, there were very few weirdos in the world who went around memorizing every single Numbered Item.
Next.
I put in another mana stone and checked what I got.
Next.
I kept vetoing items. As the number of mana stones I used continued to climb, the number of high-quality items that popped up increased as well, including a few interesting ones.
[You have crafted No. 2988: Mark of the Guard Corps.]
The earrings I was already using.
[You have crafted a Staff Imbued with the World Tree’s Power.]
A staff created from the grade-six material, the World Tree, that had Versyl drooling.
[You have crafted Five Arc Ingots.]
I had even gotten the maximum amount of the grade-six material arc possible.
[You have crafted a Divine Elixir.]
Then came a special potion that I knew had a certain probability of appearing only on the ninth floor’s Rift.
[You have crafted No. 7777: Garphas’s Necklace.]
Now that, I didn’t know was possible. Was this like a matryoshka or something? In any case, the point was that I had seen plenty of items and had skipped them all.
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
I was nearing the finish line.
After putting in so many mana stones, I didn’t know what my exact count was anymore, but I could sense it.
Only ten more.
I would reach my goal after about ten more mana stones.
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
In cash, it was a grand total of around 1.55 billion stones.
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
Or about 77,777,777 rank-nine mana stones.
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
Hmm...
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
Huh?
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
Wait...
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stonebread.]
[You have crafted Stone...]
I got nine stonebreads in a row at the very end. Of course, it didn’t actually matter whether they were stonebreads or steel ingots or whatever, but...
Gulp.

My hands stopped for a second, my palms drenched in sweat for some reason. Revelation. The experience I was having right now felt like a revelation. Like the universe itself was trying to tell me what lay ahead.
...Nonsense.
I forcefully shook my head and steeled my mind. This was just a strange coincidence. There was no point trying to assign any meaning to it.
In fact, this could be a good thing.

From a different perspective, this could be an optimistic sign. Although I wasn’t the superstitious type, even I had a habit where sometimes when I played games, I’d invest time in upgrading a piece of equipment just so I could blow it up and go and upgrade my real gear after.
Yeah, so...
I inserted another mana stone with faith in my heart.
Flash!
The mana stone shattered and the necklace flashed with a blinding bright light.
[You have reached the limit of mana stones that can be absorbed by the necklace.]
[Please be wary. From this point on, the necklace may shatter at any moment.]
Now began the real test of luck. After absorbing 77,777,777 mana stones, Garphas’s Necklace turned into a guaranteed gacha. In other words, it now had a floor.
From this point on, I had a 100 percent probability of pulling the highest-ranked Numbered Items, from No. 1 to No. 35.
So, how did my first attempt go?
Tsk.
Yeah, I figured this wasn’t going to be easy.
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]

Of course, Rake of Naraka was an excellent item in its own right. It was a claw-type weapon that came in a set of two, and it had lots of great effects. Amelia would get a lot of use out of it in battle.
But am I going to settle for No. 35 after spending 1.5 billion?
The math just didn’t make sense.
One more time.
Since I had already reached the absorption limit, putting another mana stone into the necklace would definitely get me—
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
Huh?
Why didn’t the item change? I definitely used a mana stone...
...Am I dreaming right now?
Even as disbelief made my heart pound, my mind calmly took stock of things. The Rake of Naraka had appeared again.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump.
Blood rushed to my head and my vision began to narrow. My mouth felt strangely dry, and something like a chill crept down my spine. I slowly inserted another mana stone.
[Please be wary. From this point on, the necklace may shatter at any moment.]
Although that warning lingered in the back of my mind, I wasn’t particularly worried about it. I knew that the necklace wouldn’t self-destruct until after the third turn at the very least.
...Let’s not stress.
This was all stacking up, you know? My future was guaranteed to be full of sunshine and rainbows—
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
“...One more time.”
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
“What the fuck, are you kidding me?”

Curses flew from my mouth despite my best attempts to stay calm. I just couldn’t hold it in anymore. My mind was scrambled and every single thing that had happened so far was suddenly suspect. Especially those multiple stonebreads in a row.
Garphas’s Necklace.
Not to mention that item that popped up during one of my many rerolls. Maybe that had been a bad omen? A warning from the universe that today wasn’t my day and I should give up and try again later.
“...Yandel, are you all right?”
“Ah... Yeah, I’m fine.”
“You’re pretty pale...”
“...That’s not true. I’m lucky.”
I forcibly raised my spirits right as they began to sink into despair.
Four rakes in a row?
Who cared? This was just one more obstacle to overcome. The sweet fruits of victory were always hidden behind the thorns of hardship.
I need to believe in myself.
I repeated the revelation I came to earlier and inserted one more mana stone with full confidence.
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
It was still fine. It hadn’t blown up yet, right?
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
Hmm, considering it still wasn’t exploding, the universe was clearly just messing with me a bit—
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
...Maybe it’s broken?
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
...This was getting dangerous.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump!
My heart pounded at a rapid clip.
[You have crafted No. 35: Rake of Naraka.]
In the end, I raised the white flag.
“...A-Ainar?”
Ainar Fenelin—a woman who lived a life of very little critical thought but who always ended up fine thanks to sheer dumb luck.
“Hm? What is it?” she asked, tilting her head. She had stopped paying attention to what I was doing a while ago and was now gnawing on some jerky a short distance away.
“Yeah?”
“C-Could you come here... and put in a mana stone?” I asked politely.
“Oh! Really? I’ve been wanting to try it at least once!”
Thankfully, Ainar gladly took up my offer and rushed over.
[You have crafted No. 3: Wall of Aegis.]
I learned a new universal truth that day.
“...Oh? It’s a shield. Is it a good one?”
I should just let Ainar handle stuff like this from now on.

chapters.title: Chapter 540: Verdurous Giant Spear (2)
paragraphs: To be honest, No. 7777: Garphas’s Necklace, wasn’t all that fuel-efficient of an item. You were guaranteed to obtain a Numbered Item of No. 35 or better from it, sure, but before those odds kicked in, you needed to spend 1.5 billion stones.
You only turn a profit if you get a Numbered Item in the single digits.

Getting something in the teens—namely, No. 19 to No. 10—was breaking even, and anything No. 20 and above was a loss. Not only that but there was a non-zero chance that the necklace could self-destruct while rerolling, which would be the biggest loss of all.
In other words, it was a high-risk, high-reward gambling item.
“Bjorn...? Why aren’t you saying anything?” I shook myself out of my stupor at the sound of Ainar’s worried voice. “Is it... not a good one?” she asked hesitantly.
That was the furthest possible thing from the truth.
“Well done, Ainar. You’re the only one I can rely on.”
I was conveying my love to her as earnestly as I could, but Ainar didn’t seem to notice. “Oh! If you’re saying that, then the item must be good! What does this shield do?”
Oh. Was that all?
The way she brushed my feelings off so easily hurt just a little bit, but it was fine.
Right, this could’ve all ended with me getting stuck with the Rake of Naraka.
To be honest, I’d happily let her punch me in the face three times over and laugh it off with a smile if it meant getting this result. And on that note...
Let’s pull this now.
Just in case something went wrong, I rushed to pull out the selected item.
Flash!
As I pressed the confirm button, a spray of multicolored light erupted from the necklace. The shining rays coalesced in the air like clay and took shape.
[The selected item has been given form.]
No. 3: Wall of Aegis.
As obvious as it may seem, this was the best shield in the game for a Shield Barbarian like me.
I guess since I’ll exclusively be using this shield from now on, I’ve officially filled my shield slot...
Honestly, I hadn’t been expecting this to happen at all. No, realistically speaking, there were actually several other items I intended to stop at if I saw them.

There was the endgame armor in the teens that I always wore as part of my build; my second pick for an endgame shield, No.21; one of the single-digit Numbered Items that was core to the ice-type Double Sword Master build... Plus, if the Rift Maker—a helpful item for farming—appeared, I would’ve seriously considered taking it for its future usefulness alone. And if that one didn’t pop up, I had planned on stopping if I got any of the endgame weapons for Amelia or Erwen.
However...
I really didn’t expect to get this.
I still couldn’t tell if I was dreaming.
[Due to the excessive influx of mana, the necklace containing Garphas’s power has been permanently damaged.]
With that, the Numbered Item around my neck turned into a regular piece of jewelry. I barely paid it any mind as I carefully lifted up my new gray shield.
[You have equipped No. 3: Wall of Aegis. Your total Item Level has increased by +18600.]
I had become stronger.
A lot stronger at that.
The shield itself wasn’t too fancy. The color was gray, and it didn’t have a single decoration on its surface. But so what? All a shield needed to be was strong and sturdy.
“This shield...is a single-digit Numbered Item?”
“Wait... There are only two above No. 3... This is an incredible treasure!”
“Wall of Aegis! I’ve only ever heard about it in stories, but now I’m seeing it with my own eyes!”
I heard my comrades begin to whisper amongst themselves as they realized what my shield was. The last of them to speak, Amelia, seemed to be the most excited, strangely enough.
Ainar merrily joined in. “Oh! Since everyone’s saying stuff like that, I guess it’s some sort of valuable treasure!”
“Tsk, that’s not all,” Amelia scolded her. “The Wall of Aegis hasn’t once appeared since the adventurer who last had it died in the labyrinth 120 years ago.”
Actually, now that I thought about it, it wasn’t strange at all. This woman really liked stuff like this. If I had to put a label on it, she was something of a labyrinth geek.
“Right now, excluding the one that the palace has in their stores, Yandel, you are the only person with one in their possession. Also, according to past records, that shield is indestructible...”
She must have wanted to flaunt her knowledge or something because Amelia kindly gave everyone a rundown on the shield and its history. The explanation itself was professional enough...
But when it comes to information, this world is always missing a detail or two.
As a hardcore gamer, I couldn’t accept that. I proceeded to go over the item in my head myself.
High-quality to the point of indestructibility. Holding the shield in the guarding position grants me immunity to all damage.
Reduces all magical damage dealt to me and everyone within thirty feet of me by 30 percent and grants immunity to all spells rank-five and below.
All of my defensive stats increase by 20 percent the moment it’s equipped.
When using an aura skill, the range of the aura is doubled.
As long as my Threat Level is over five hundred, all monsters will prioritize attacking me first.
And finally...
One active effect.
Yes, this was what it was like to have an endgame piece of equipment.

My heart was pounding so hard, I wanted to run out and test this thing out in battle right now. But though I could feel myself itching for a fight, I had already told everyone that today was a rest day, so I held myself back.
Right, I needed time to get used to this thing too.
It’s pretty light.
It was much heavier than an ordinary steel shield, but somehow it still felt strangely lighter than I was used to. Though that might have just been because my last shield was ridiculously heavy.
Let me grab my hammer too.

Holding Demon Grinder in my other hand, I tested out the balance between the two. After all, this wasn’t a video game. Differences in weight and sensation were something that could end up backfiring on me pretty hard.
Whoosh! Swoosh!
And so, I was swinging my weapon at the empty air inside the cave to get used to the change in weight when a thought occurred to me.
Somehow, I ended up getting my top weapons already.

No. 87: Kraul’s Demon Grinder, and No. 3: Wall of Aegis—with these two, I honestly never had to look at another weapon again. Demon Grinder could technically be upgraded for a better item, but that would be a lot of work for diminishing returns, so I could just keep using this hammer.
I guess I only have my armor, shoes, and belt left.

Those were the core items for my final build, anyway. Although the barbarian tribe’s Genesis Treasure was another core item, that was something I likely wouldn’t be able to get my hands on despite being the one thing I really wished I could have. The Genesis Treasure was a big reason the Shield Barbarian was so overpowered.
Anyway, I think I’ve gotten used to this thing...
After getting acquainted with the feel of my new equipment, I started testing out a few things. I turned on the active effect and then checked the magic immunity aura as well.
A thirty-foot radius...
I made sure to ingrain in myself what thirty feet looked and felt like. This would be a critical metric in battle.
Once I’d ticked off a few more experiments, I rested for the remaining time we had and then gathered with the other leaders to discuss our plans moving forward.
Well, to be honest, it was closer to an announcement than a discussion.
“Lord Baron, are we going to continue exploring this island of giants again tomorrow?”
“No, for now, we’re going to leave this island be.”
“Pardon?”
“We spent all that time wandering around and getting beat up, yet we still haven’t found anything.”
I knew that Giant Island hid a secret. However, I got the sense that that secret would only be revealed to us after we defeated that huge giant we saw the last time we were here.
The problem is, we haven’t seen it since, and there’s no guarantee that we would be able to defeat it even if we found it.
“Then... where are you planning on going?”
“Our next destination will be Library Island.”
“Pardon? Ah... You mean that island you told me about before.”
“That’s right.”

Before all else, I wanted to head to that island to boost our stats. Back then, we were limited by the fact that we only had seven members and had had to leave after hitting the rank-threes, but things were different now. Also, I was a little curious about what the situation there was like now that some time had passed.
I’m pretty sure we cleared all of the books on the bottom shelves. Have those regenerated since?
Hmm, I’d find out when I got there.
As our meeting was coming to a close, Amelia asked me a question. “Yandel, then are we giving up on the Hipramajent?”
“We’re not giving up. We’re just putting it on hold for now.”
“But why? I remember you wanting its essence.”
That was true.

However, even if the distortion magic succeeded and another essence dropped, there was no guarantee that it would be one with Giantization. More than anything, even if we hit the jackpot and got the perfect drop, there wouldn’t be much of a payoff.
No matter how I look at it, I don’t think the skill will stack twice.

The Hipramajent’s essence was superior to the Orc Hero’s, but the active skill it would give me would be the same. As it was, I had two essence slots left. It would be more helpful for me to fill these slots with other essences that would help me get stronger. It wasn’t like I had any way of erasing the Orc Hero’s essence even if the Hipramajent’s did drop.
“Hmm, I see. Got it.”
Still, these were all excuses. They weren’t the main reason.
Since I’ve taken care of Erwen and Ainar somewhat...
I needed to up the specs of my other allies as well. They all had an open essence slot, and we should be able to fill them up with ease if we farmed for a bit at the library.
Ah, of course, this included Amelia.
It’s been a while since she’s gotten a power boost.
“...Why are you looking at me like that?”
“It’s nothing.”
I just had a thought.
Although I didn’t know when we’d get to escape from this place when that time did finally come...
It’s fun to imagine.
How much stronger would we be?

After announcing our plans, I spent our remaining rest time alone thinking more about my build, going over the things I needed to do to become an even bigger and stronger Shield Barbarian and my highest priorities in pursuit of that goal.
For now, only one thing on that list could be completed on Basement Floor One: get an essence at the library.

I was after one essence and one essence alone, and that was the rank-three monster Bellarios. Once I absorbed it, the next steps on the road to my final build would be possible only after we escaped from this place.

Switching out the Orc Hero’s essence for Hipramajent’s, reaching stage nine of the Spirit Imprint, going around the eighth-floor Rift to farm for Guardian essences and Numbered Items, and erasing the Storm Gush’s essence to farm for a Floor Essence... The rest of the things I needed to get done at level eight would only be feasible after I returned to the city.
With that, my rest day came to an end. As soon as the seventy-fifth day dawned, we left the cave, heading to the beach to make our way to Library Island.
Fwip!
But just as we were about to summon the boat, something suddenly flew at us from the ocean.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
Thankfully, I instinctively raised my shield to block it.
What was this?
“It’s an ambush!”

Positioning my shocked allies behind me, I glanced down in an attempt to figure out what was going on. There, where the silver waves ebbed and flowed at my feet, I could see a crimson spear lying on the sandy beach.
Verdurous Giant Spear...?
What the hell? Why was that thing here?
My question didn’t remain unanswered for long.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Recursion.]
In the distance, a figure emerged from the ocean’s silvery waves, trudging steadily and unerringly toward us.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has retrieved the Verdurous Giant Spear. Until the end of combat, the strength of Recursion slightly increases.]
As the spear in the sand shot back into its hand, it spoke in a rumbling voice. “(I will not let you go, mortal.)”
This was a line of dialogue I had heard countless times while running away from this guy in the game, but it hit differently this time around.
...Did it lose its mind?
Did this guy seriously walk across the ocean and all the way here?

The Guardian of the Rift of Kalheum, the City of Light, was the Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel. As I’d once again run into it somewhere I had never expected to, the first thing I felt was confusion.
However, as my shock subsided, I felt a different emotion entirely. It was a sense of welcome.
“Great.”
And a sense of joy.
“I thought I would never see you again.”
“I will not let you go, mortal.”
As Milayel responded with the same old phrase in the same old tone, I grinned.
I mean, I have no intention of running away this time.

Back then, Erwen had been out of commission, and we were surrounded by monsters on all sides. Hell, I wouldn’t have been surprised if another rank-two monster had chosen to join the fight. That was why we had barreled straight toward the beach without looking back.
However, things were different now, though I wasn’t sure if this moron had clued in yet. The rainy season had ended ages ago, and I had even picked up a fancy new shield recently.
This will be a good test of our combat level.
I turned toward my allies, who were awaiting my orders, and gave the command. “Prepare for battle! We’re going to take this guy down here and now!”
Yeah, it would be rude to reject a gift that had been kind enough to walk right into our laps.

chapters.title: Chapter 541: Verdurous Giant Spear (3)
paragraphs: Guardians of the Rift dropped Guardian Essences along with Rift Stones and Numbered Items. On top of that, you got bonus EXP for defeating a Guardian, so you could say this monster was juicier than other monsters.
The problem was that they were much tougher to beat.
But a big contributing factor to their difficulty is the effects active in their respective Rifts.

Take Glacier Cave, one of the first-floor Rifts, for example. There, we had to fight while under the Hypothermia effect. We had a similar experience in the third floor’s White Temple as well. The difficulty of those battles skyrocketed since we had to fight with a bunch of debuffs on us.
However, we weren’t in the City of Light right now.
A Milayel without Heavenly Magic Circle or any of the guardian angels?
It was an incredible advantage, so I was honestly a little disappointed when we had to run away from it earlier. And yet, it had followed me all the way here.
“Behel—aaah!” I raised my shield and gave it a warm charge in welcome.
Boom!

It tried to skewer me with its spear in an attempt to stop me, but there was no way something like that would work. As it was flung back by my body slam, its weapon flipped through the air before landing back in the water. It seemed like everyone was in their battle formations now.
Splish.

I didn’t bother chasing after it with my hammer and instead lowered my shield a little. If I combined Demon Grinder with Swing, I could deal a decent amount of damage, but DPS should be left to the DPS types.
[Myul Armin has cast Supersensitive Skin.]
[Myul Armin has cast Weaken Soul.]
[Myul Armin has cast Self-Destructing Spirit of Vengeance.]
As Myul Armin laid out his array of curses, the long-rangers began their volley.
[Jackson Janvil has cast Moving Target.]
[Sharlot Emblut has cast the rank-four attack spell Spiral Needle.]
[Nua Merbochi has cast Precise Shot.]
[Garton Cultner has cast Stone Cannon.]
Wizards, priests, special ability users, archers—all kinds of classes launched myriad attacks of all different colors.

Since Milayel had pretty thick skin, it continued to lunge at me with its spear even as it was bombarded on all sides, but I kept shoving it back out into the open so the long-rangers would have an easier time hitting it.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Blessing of Light.]
A minute later, light shot out from its poor, bullied body. This signaled the end of the first phase, which meant that it would start using things other than just Recursion from here on out.
This is so much easier without the guardian angels backing him up.

Of course, I’d need to keep track of several things during the second phase. Blessing of Light would let it recover a large percentage of its health, decrease its cooldowns, and increase its base resistances and stats. But more importantly, this guy would start using that combo during Phase Two.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Recursion.]
In other words, it was time for it to show off its most broken skill.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Splintering Comet. All projectiles are duplicated.]
The singular spear it shot into the air suddenly splintered into dozens more that rained down on us, instantly converting a guaranteed-hit and damage-amplified throw attack into a deadly AOE skill.
However, since I’d done a pretty good job of securing its aggro, things played out a bit differently.
Fwoong!
Like guided missiles, the dozens of spears all honed in on me rather than my comrades. And I had nothing to fear.
Clang, cling, clang!
Just by covering my head with the shield, the spears all ricocheted off like bullets.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
This was the reason Union and Giantization were such a critical combo.

When a shield increased in size, the area it guarded also increased. The biggest weakness of any shield, even one as incredible as this one, was that it couldn’t block attacks that were bigger than the shield itself or targeted a wide area.
Anyway, looks like I’ve gotten through the first round all right...
After that, just like in Phase One, its attack pattern repeated. It picked up the spear stuck in the ground to charge at me, and I shoved it back.
Clang, clang, clang!

Then, once there was some distance between us, the long-rangers hit it with everything they had. Normally when you were fighting Milayel, all sorts of monsters and guardian angels got in the way so targeting it with this sort of concentrated fire was impossible. But this was a normal map, not its home turf.
Sparkle!
As we attacked it with our combined might, the dozens of spears scattered around the beach suddenly disappeared.
This was the reason Splintering Comet was such an annoying skill. Its duplication ability gave rise to all sorts of ridiculous cheats.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has retrieved the Verdurous Giant Spear. Until the end of combat, the strength of Recursion slightly increases.]
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has retrieved the Verdurous Giant Spear. Until the end of combat, the strength of Recursion slightly increases.]
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has retrieved the Verdurous Giant Spear. Until the end of combat...]
With a single use of Splintering Comet, he got multiple buffs all at once.

Soon, Milayel tossed the spear into the air once more. This time, the combo would be twice as powerful as its previous attempt. However, that didn’t really make much of a difference to me. So what if it was stronger?
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
In front of the world’s strongest shield, it didn’t matter how strong his attacks got.
Yeah... Overgearing is the best.
I was withstanding an attack pattern that should’ve been cycled and distributed between multiple tanks. Honestly, I was basically keeping Phase Two’s main combo in check all by myself.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Splintering Comet. All projectiles are duplicated.]
After it got done casting the combo for the third time, we entered Phase Three.
It took us four minutes to get here...
Maybe we could wrap this up in six.
Milayel’s pattern in Phase Three was simple.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Descend.]
It used what I called a berserker pattern.
Fwoosh!

It curled up and began to glow, and wings of light suddenly burst from its back. They looked similar to Ainar’s Wings of Greed, but they were fundamentally different, and not just because they were much fancier-looking.
Fwoom!
These wings allowed for actual flight.
“Whoa! It has wings!”
While Ainar stared up at it in awe, Milayel continued to climb higher. However, and maybe it was because this wasn’t its usual map, but an island...
It doesn’t even look that cool.
Usually, the outer walls would break down at this point and an army of Light Spirits would rush in from the sides—
[The Light Spirits gather, sensing divine energies in the air.]
Wait, what?

It seemed that part was still the same even though we weren’t in the City of Light. This didn’t happen when an ordinary Titanus used Descend, so I always assumed it was some sort of field effect unique to Kalheum.
I guess this is a special ability it has as a Guardian of the Rift?

I couldn’t be sure, but keeping our melee fighters stationed in the back turned out to be a good idea. Though I wouldn’t exactly say I had expected this. It was more that I had put them in the back so we could focus on concentrated fire without bodies in the way.
“Stand in formation!”
“We just need to hold out, so don’t overdo it!”
In any case, Versyl seemed to be commanding the troops pretty well, so I didn’t need to worry about them. Instead, I craned my neck to look up at the guy soaring into the air.
“...The day of judgment has come.”

I felt like it didn’t really have the right to say something like that after being pushed to the brink in just four minutes, but it wasn’t like it could do anything else. It could only repeat the lines it was given.
But actually, what are these guys?

A thought crept up on me, and not for the first time. What exactly was this world? The people in the city all behaved like conscious, thinking beings with their own lives, so why did the monsters in the labyrinth all still act like they were being piloted by the game’s AI—?
Ah, so annoying.
Milayel threw another spear down at me, interrupting my thoughts.
I shook my head and refocused on our opponent. “Erwen, how much longer?” I shouted, concluding it was about time. There was a reason I had saved her until the very end. “Get ready!”
“Got it!”
As soon as Phase Three started, I made sure to prep Erwen’s lethal combo. Once the monster was in the air, its evasiveness skyrocketed.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned the Elemental Ruler of Darkness, Dicloe.]
As such, beating it down without giving it the time or space to dodge was the best way to handle it.
Bang, bang, bang!

Orbs of darkness flooded the sky and exploded like fireworks in a destructive but beautiful tableau. Even as she orchestrated this display, however, Erwen was also busy pulling her bow taut to cast Concentrated Fire. And so the countdown began.
[All of Erwen Fornacci di Tersia’s resources have been exhausted. A mysterious energy makes itself known following the exhaustion of all resources.]
Around the time I expected Chaos Circuit to activate, the monster’s cracked and beaten flesh crumbled away, revealing pale-white skin underneath.
[The Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, has cast Cracking Shell.]
Hmm, though calling it skin would be kind of inaccurate. It was glowing not unlike a fluorescent bulb.
Shaaa!

The dazzling light covered its body, and with the huge spear in one of its massive hands, it descended toward us with slow flaps of its wings. When I stared up at it at that moment, it truly looked like some sort of heavenly being. Well, it was still going to die, though.
“Mortals.” I wasn’t sure if it was aware of that as it began to speak. “Your greed has sowed the seeds of destruction.”
But, wait, had I ever heard these lines of dialogue before?
“Your arrogance has brought about the end of this world.”
I thought it only ever said, “I will judge you”—
“I will judge you.”
Yeah, that was usually its only line.
...Well, this isn’t the only time I’ve noticed something that’s different from the game.
I didn’t bother worrying too much about Milayel’s speech. What mattered now was its transformation—specifically, the transformation of the huge red spear it was holding.
[The Final Spearman, Milayel, summons the true form of the Verdurous Giant Spear.]
Just like how the monster changed its outer shell while entering its final phase, the spear also cracked to show its true form underneath—a giant spear bathed in a blinding, green light.
Bzzt, bzzzt!
Sparks jumped across the spear’s surface, and everything about it seemed to exude a power that no other weapon could hope to match.

Honestly, that wasn’t too far from the truth. While using this spear, all piercing damage dealt by the user increased by 1,200 percent. Their Natural Regeneration increased in proportion to the time spent in combat. It was nearly indestructible and came with an immunity to all damage dealt by divine power.

When you used a skill while holding the spear, you could recover 50 percent of any resources consumed over the course of a minute, and when you were attacked by a mental-type ability, it was negated and reflected back at the attacker in full. On top of that, when you used the spear’s innate active skill, three more traits kicked in.
All damage dealt by the spear was tripled.
All healing-type effects were tripled.
And finally...

You received the best piercing bonus in the game. The spear that could pierce through anything. If something like that really existed, the Verdurous Giant Spear would be the top contender for the title.
However, this raised an issue.
Bzzzt! Creak!
The all-piercing spear and the all-blocking shield—what would happen if they were to collide?
“...Disappear!”
In truth, I already knew the answer.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
The shield would win.
With that, I asked Milayel, whose attack had just been nullified, “Do you know what the most creative weapon in the world is?”
As expected, it made no effort to respond to my question, but that was no big deal. So what? I kept on talking.
“The answer...is the shield.”
Unfortunately, I didn’t get a chance to explain why that was.
“Ah, oops.”
Because Erwen was done casting.
It wasn’t a sound, per se, but...
Flash!
The second I registered the sensation of something whooshing by my ear, the island was dyed in a bright white light.
All right, let’s check the time...
Six minutes, seventeen seconds.
Damn it, didn’t manage that sub-six run.
[You have killed the Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel. EXP +8]
[Elite Guardian Kill Bonus. EXP +5]
Flash!
Then came another light—the light that signaled the defeat of a monster.

Dozens of adventurers stared at that bundle of light as someone starving might stare at a buffet. That was because I’d told everyone yesterday that this was not an ordinary monster but, instead, a Guardian that could be found in the eighth floor’s Rift.
Let’s see.
What did it drop?
Since everyone had their eyes glued to the same spot, we all saw when it happened.
Tap.
First, a Rift Stone, one of the three potential rewards a Guardian could leave behind, didn’t drop.
Neither did a rainbow essence.

Splintering Comet would’ve been great for Erwen, so I’d been hoping it would appear. But even though I had Beginner’s Luck on my side, no dice. Which was a shame, but that wasn’t to say it didn’t drop any loot at all.
To be honest, I found our actual reward pretty hard to believe.
“Uh, that’s—!”
After turning into light, the Spearman of the Heavens, Milayel, dropped a Numbered Item.
The probability of a Guardian dropping a Numbered Item is 33 percent.
On top of that, an item that would have only had a 3 percent chance of being that Numbered Item had ended up dropping.
“It’s the spear that guy was holding...!”
No. 7: Milayel’s Verdurous Giant Spear.

When I saw it, the feeling that washed over me was closer to restlessness than happiness. To be more precise, I’d call it unease. Because, you know. I had just gotten Wall of Aegis, but now we suddenly had another single-digit Numbered Item in our possession.
...Why am I getting so lucky?
This outcome was exactly what I’d been hoping for, but as my wish became reality, I felt a strange prickle of fear. It was the gut instinct of a child who had grown up used to misfortune.
However, people were thinking creatures. Even as my heart pounded with worry, my mind lit up with excitement.
Verdurous Giant Spear...
Our current party didn’t have anyone who used a spear. However, one of the joys of Dungeon and Stone was adapting to use the items that you were given to the best of your abilities.
So who should I give this to to best show off my excellent judgment?

chapters.title: Chapter 542: Verdurous Giant Spear (4)
paragraphs: Not only was No. 7: Milayel’s Verdurous Giant Spear the ideal endgame weapon for spear users, but the single-digit Numbered Item also struck a great balance between attack and defense. The reason I had started experimenting with a Spear Barbarian build was because of the protection that this very weapon provided.
But in the end, it just turned into something like a Berserker.

Of course, this wasn’t to say the Berserker class was bad. If the party had a tank of around the same level, the Berserker actually worked quite well, and they could even act as the secondary tank in emergencies.
“Hmm...” I mused.
However, the build was a little too unfocused.
I doled out orders. “Clean up the beach.”
“Pardon?”
“We’ll be heading out immediately!”
“Ah, oh. Yes!”

Everyone seemed to be wondering who was going to get to call this spear their own, but I decided to get the boat on the water first and think it over on our way off the island. This wasn’t a decision that should be made on a whim.
“Set sail!”
Once everyone was on the boat, we began to cut through the silver ocean.
“Mister! Look over there!”
Back over on the island, which was getting smaller and smaller in the distance, a colossus rose to its feet and roared at us.
Uraaaaaah!
...Why did it only ever do that when we were leaving?
While we voyaged toward Library Island, I sunk deep into thought over the question of who should get this spear.
Ah, we made eye contact again.

While glancing around, half hoping to find some sort of answer on the horizon, I met eyes with a man. He was the spearman of the Hektz Clan. As the only person among the many here trained to use a spear, even if he didn’t dare voice it aloud, I could tell part of him was feeling a little expectant somewhere deep down.
Fwip.
I quickly turned away.

The heart could want whatever it wanted, but the fact was that this weapon was the property of the Anabada Clan. That much had already been decided, so the only thing I was trying to figure out at this point was which of my clanmates to give it to.
First, I can take Erwen and Versyl off the table right off the bat.

The same went for Amelia and Missha. Missha was a dual wielder, and the way Amelia used her aura wasn’t well-suited for fighting with a spear. Auyen wasn’t a combat class to begin with. So by process of elimination, that only left Ainar.
“Hmm? You want some?”
When I met eyes with her, Ainar flashed me a bright smile and held out some of the jerky she was eating.
I accepted it and resumed pacing as I chewed.
...I guess she’s the one most suited to use the spear to its fullest potential.
[The user’s Natural Regeneration increases relative to time spent in combat.]
[All healing-type effects on the user are tripled.]

These two abilities worked great with the Slayer Imprint’s Combat Study and Predation. On top of that, since she had skills like Wings of Greed and Curl Up boosting her Natural Regeneration by quite a bit, combined with the spear, she would have a monstrous healing factor.
My Spear Barbarian build had also used the Slayer Imprint in that way and stocked up on a ton of similar recovery-type skills.
The moment she takes up the spear, though, she’ll need to abandon a few of her other skills.

The first one that came to mind was the rank-four skill Repeated Slash. It wasn’t impossible to cast with a spear, but she wouldn’t get the bonus of piercing damage the spear offered if she used it. In a similar vein, Wildness Control, which converted damage dealt by certain active effects to slashing damage, would become useless.
Without Repeated Slash, Blast Scars becomes useless too, and that means Mandel Oil and Residual Heat will also be useless.
Honestly, handing her the spear was essentially committing to swapping out every skill she had.
Still... Except for Hipramajent’s, all her essences are below rank four, right? If we’re already going to do this, how about we just change everything while we’re at it?
Dungeon and Stone was a game built for builds.

It was important to plan out the final build you were going for, but even more important was planning out the incremental builds you’d need to get there. If you didn’t select which items and essences you would use to get through each individual segment of the game, there was no way you would ever live long enough to reach your endgame build. It was important to keep the core character concept intact while steadily raising their stats.
Chew, chew, chew.

That was the reason I chose Repeated Slash as Ainar’s core skill. It was a rank-four skill we managed to obtain early on, and after she got what she needed out of it, I was hoping to change it to another similar high-ranking skill later.
...But it’s not like a change of plans would be a bad idea.

I had grown a lot. Erwen had too—after absorbing the Floor Essence, she had shot forward at an incredible pace. Missha had progressed a fair bit while traveling with Baekho Lee as well. Amelia had just been strong from the start.
To put it coldly, we could hunt just fine even without Ainar around. Which meant that right now, we could cut her from the team entirely if we wanted.
Theoretically, anyway. But all that is to say that using the spear definitely wouldn’t hurt her in battle, even if it doesn’t perfectly suit her build right now.

A single-digit Numbered Item was an endgame weapon without equal. The effects granted by this particular spear were more than enough to compensate for the skills she’d have to abandon to use it properly. Especially considering they were all from rank-four essences or lower.

A 1,200 percent piercing damage boost, triple damage for all attacks made with the spear, the ability to punch a hole through virtually any material... Even just taking into account those three bonuses, one could argue that she’d be able to deal even more damage with the spear than she currently could using her sword. And with all those regeneration buffs stacked on her, she would be even tougher to kill than she already was.
The problem then becomes, will she take it...? Let’s talk to her first and see.
There was nothing to lose by asking.
“Ainar.” In true barbarian fashion, I walked back over to her and got right into it. “Have you thought about using a spear instead of a sword?”
“...A spear?” Ainar stopped chewing on her jerky and lifted her head to stare at me.
I sighed.
Yeah, I figured it was a long shot.
Even ignoring her personal preferences, barbarians tended to hate weapons like this in general, claiming they were for cowards—
“Oh! If you’re talking about that spear, then yes! Give it to me!”
...Huh? What was with this reaction?
“Just to clarify,” I began slowly, “I’m saying you’ll need to use a spear for the rest of your life. Also, we’ll have to swap out all your essences.”
“Swap them out... You mean Semura’s essence too?”
The essence of Semura was the one that gave her Repeated Slash. The same essence that her old master passed down to her via Soul Succession before he died.
“Yeah,” I confirmed. “That one too.”
“I see...” Ainar’s eyes lost their shine for a second.
“You can take as much time as you—” I started to say, but it turned out she didn’t need much time to think it over at all.
“All right. I’ll switch to the spear.”
I was telling her she would need to change basically everything about herself, but it didn’t even take her a minute to agree to it.
Is this what it means to be a true barbarian...?
She was on a level I couldn’t even hope to aspire to.
However, it turned out that Ainar might not have made this decision on a whim.
“Why are you so surprised? From the start, aren’t all the essences I have right now the ones you recommended to me?”
“Uh... I guess?”

“Thanks to them, I’m well-known and respected in a way that I couldn’t have even dreamed of before. I can fight powerful enemies I couldn’t even imagine fighting and protect my comrades with my own two hands.”
Ainar looked directly into my eyes, resolute.
“So I will trust you.”
I was speechless.
“You’ve never done anything to cause me harm,” she concluded.
I see. She hadn’t made this decision on a whim at all. She was only willing to go down this path because she trusted in me wholeheartedly.
Would I be able to do the same?
I wasn’t sure I could ever manage that level of trust.

“And more than anything...” Ainar glanced away from me. To be more precise, she shifted her gaze from me to something else, a hungry gleam entering her eyes. “...th-that spear is really cool! It’s huge!”
“It’s nearly double the size of my greatsword!”
I was once again rendered speechless.
Just like how crows instinctively gravitated toward shiny objects, barbarians tended to like big things.
“It’s also cool how it sparkles!”
Even more so if those things were shiny too.
“And it seems like everyone with wings uses spears, anyway!”
Yeah... So you had plenty of reasons, huh?

After officially switching to the Spearman class, Ainar began training to figure out how to use the spear. She practiced spinning it in the air, thrusting it forward, maintaining her distance, and more. At first, she was clumsy and didn’t even know how to hold it properly, but she got used to it incredibly quickly.
“Eh heh, now I’m finally getting the hang of it again!”
“Again?”
“Don’t you remember? When we were kids, we were taught how to use all the weapons!”
“Ah, that... Yeah...”
Yikes, don’t bring up the good old days out of nowhere like that.
As always, I was quick to skirt around any mention of the past with a vague noise of agreement, but Ainar, unfortunately, wanted to keep reminiscing.
“Now that I think about it, it’s kind of interesting. I heard that my mother and my sister also used spears.”
Thankfully, that was a topic I could actually comment on. This was my first time hearing about the spear thing, but Ainar and I had talked about her sister before.
Ainar, second daughter of Fenelin. She had an older sister.
Or rather, she’d had an older sister.
“Huh? You have a sister?” Erwen, who also had an older sister, asked Ainar in surprise, but the latter just shrugged.
“Ah, did I never mention it? She became an adventurer four years before I did. She used to tell me all sorts of stories about her adventures while using her new skills to bully me, haha...”

“...What?” Erwen looked baffled by the fond tone with which Ainar recalled that particular memory. It seemed the cultural differences were tripping her up. “Ah, so, what is your older sister like? Is she famous?”
“She died. Two years before I had my coming-of-age ceremony.”
“Oh... I-I’m sorry...” Erwen paled and apologized, clearly worried that she had touched a nerve.
However, Ainar didn’t seem to mind at all. “Huh? Why are you apologizing? It’s not like it’s your fault she died.”
“Still... It’s a sad thing to think about.”
“Sad? What do you mean? I only have good memories of her. Of course, it’s a shame I can’t see her anymore, but I always smile whenever I remember the good times I had with my sister.”
Erwen blinked, at a momentary loss for words. “How... How can you think that way? Even now... whenever I think about my older sister, I feel my heart clench.”

The crack in her voice came out sounding a little accusatory, but Ainar thankfully didn’t seem to care. She tipped her head to the side in thought, as unbothered as ever. “Even if you ask how I can do it... I couldn’t really tell you. It’s just that being happy is better than being sad! My sister would say so too!”
It was a truly barbarian-like answer.
In the face of that logic, Erwen was left unable to muster a response. She just stared at Ainar for a long moment before quietly excusing herself to head back up to the crow’s nest.
Hah... I can finally breathe again.
As I let out the breath I was holding, Ainar looked at me in confusion. “...Did I do something wrong?”
“No. Just keep doing what you’re doing. We’re going to jump straight into real combat as soon as we land on the island.”
“Oh! All right!”

After leaving Ainar to auto-train by herself, I headed toward the helm of the boat. Once I was done checking in with Auyen about how long it would take for us to reach our destination, I leaned back against the mast and closed my eyes.
They should be able to take care of the random mob monsters with no problem, so they should only wake me if something strong shows up.
When I woke up from my nap a short while later, I took out my water bottle and went looking for Ainar. I was curious how much progress she’d made while I was sleeping.
Huh?
But for some reason, Ainar had stopped training and was currently resting on the deck.
With Erwen.
What is this?
The second the question popped into my mind, Amelia appeared at my side. “Leave them alone for a bit. Don’t try to butt in.”
“...I wasn’t planning to.” I was just curious what they were talking about.

To that end, I pricked my ears and focused on their conversation so I could hear what they were saying. I’d been a little worried about the two of them being alone together, but their exchange was decidedly normal.
“Haha, so you have a younger sister too? What’s she like? Is she an adventurer as well?”
“No, not yet. She’ll have her coming-of-age ceremony next year, but I’m a bit worried.”
“If you’re worried, you can make sure to teach her what you know.”
“It’s...not that simple.”
“Hmm? Oh, because we’re stuck in here?”
“No, not that... Honestly... ever since our older sister died... and after Mister suddenly disappeared... our relationship hasn’t been that great.”
“Oh yeah, I guess you would’ve been obsessed with going to battle and taking revenge. So it’s all your fault!”
I was horrified by Ainar’s accusation, but surprisingly enough, Erwen took it in stride. “My fault... Yes, you’re right. It is my fault.”
“Haha, as long as you know that, it’s fine. So can’t you just treat her better once you’re back home?”
“But I think it’s too late. I think she hates and resents me.”
“Did she say that to you herself?”
“No, but—”
“If she didn’t, stop wasting time worrying about it. Hate you? How could she when you’re family? She’s probably hoping for your relationship to go back to the way it used to be.”
“...Really?”
The two of them made a strange picture: an elf, of all people, getting lectured by a barbarian, her race’s sworn enemy.
But at the same time, it somehow made perfect sense.
“Yes, that is right! You can trust me!”
I also felt like I could finally understand how Ainar was able to make so many friends.
We reached Library Island on day seventy-six with the goal of farming as much as possible.
Bellarios would be great, but I hope we can get an essence we can give to Ainar.
With that thought in mind, we entered the building and began our long trek down the stairs before we were soon brought to a screeching halt.
“Yandel, there’s someone down there.”
“Only one person. No one else.”
“They’re curled up and seem to be asleep...”
“What will you do?”
Amelia and Erwen had delivered completely unexpected news.
Someone had gotten here before us.
Who could it be?
I had a few ideas for who could be down there, namely that clan that came down to Basement Floor One with the Armin Adventurer Group a few weeks ago. Their name was...
“I have a feeling they’re a part of the Ainpelial Clan.”
Ah, right. That was it.

“But the numbers don’t add up. Only one person? Where did everyone else in that huge group go...?” Myul furrowed his brow as he fell into thought, but I didn’t bother mulling over those questions myself.
Rather, I didn’t want to waste time wondering.
“It’s quicker to just ask them directly.”
We’d get a much clearer answer by going down there and talking to them than we would standing around speculating up here.
And so, we quickly made our way down the stairs.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Since we were so noisy, the figure who seemed to have been sleeping jolted upward at an awkward angle the second we reached the bottom.
“Uh...! Y-Your Lordship?”
And when the person spotted us, their eyes went wide in shock.
I could sympathize with the sentiment.
“...Maderkin Lilgreams.”
The man staring back at me was the Silver Lion Clan’s captain—the very same one we had split up with on the village chief’s island over a month ago and hadn’t seen alive since.

chapters.title: Chapter 543: Ghost (1)
paragraphs: Maderkin Lilgreams.
I didn’t expect it to be him, of all people...
The sight of his face didn’t spark any urge to celebrate his survival or interrogate him on how he managed it. The only thing I felt was confusion. “You...were killed by the village chief?”
“Sorry...?” He seemed to have heard my mumbling because he stared at me with confusion of his own. “Killed by the village chief...? What do you mean?”
“We discovered a shortsword with your clan’s insignia on it at the village forge,” I probed, figuring I might as well dig deeper now that we were on the subject.
“Why was it there?”

“Well...I don’t know. However, before we left the island, some of our clan members traded with the villagers. They handed over the majority of their nonessential items and obtained a large amount of mana stones in return.”
His testimony completely aligned with the chief’s claims, which only left me more mystified.
The chief really was innocent? Then why did I escape the village? Did I make that huge scene for no reason?

Despite the questions flooding my mind, I quickly shook my head to rid myself of those nagging doubts. I could come to a conclusion after I heard everything he had to say. “Speak. Tell me what you did after you left the island.”
“Pardon? Oh...Yes!” His relief at being rescued quickly faded at my cold interrogation. He rushed to answer my questions. “First, we left two days after you left the island, Your Lordship.”

There wasn’t anything special about his story. He had left the island with his clan because he felt like he needed to do something productive, but after being burned by his experience on Chief Island, fear drove him to set a course for Library Island in the hopes of taking advantage of its relative safety. Just as we were here to do some farming, it seemed he’d decided that he and his clan needed to get stronger as well.
However...

“It was a beast we had never seen before. It had horrid-looking wings attached to it, and its body was similar to that of a slime. However, it had all sorts of disgusting and twisted limbs protruding from all over its body.”
They encountered a new monster that even I didn’t have in my database.

It had wiped out the Silver Lion Clan entirely, and the boat they had been using was destroyed as well. But after plunging into the water, certain he was done for, Maderkin woke up on Library Island. His gear had snagged on some of the rocks near the shore just in time to save him from drowning.
“After that... Well, I was worried that it was too dangerous for me to stay out in the open, so I came down here. And then...I waited here alone for someone to find this place again...”

He had rationed his food and water as much as possible just in case and hadn’t fought any of the monsters, instead sitting here in total isolation and battling only his loneliness. That about summed up his tale.
“I see.”

But I didn’t find it a particularly sad tale. Reading between the lines, I got the sense that as soon as he concluded that his clan was going to be wiped out, he’d abandoned ship and jumped into the ocean to save himself.
That’s what it sounds like, at least.
From what I knew of Maderkin Lilgreams, he was definitely the type of guy to pull something like that.
Anyway, that’s enough questions.
I had heard his story, so now it was time to check if it was true.
“Versyl.”

I ordered our wizard to cast a verification spell. Unfortunately, due to Lilgream’s high Mana Resistance, the verification magic didn’t really work. Still, I didn’t get hung up on it and instead took out an item from my personal sub-space.
It feels like a bit of a waste to use the last charge here... but no matter how I look at it, this is way too suspicious.
“Maderkin Lilgreams.”
“Yes?”
“I am now going to check whether what you said is the truth.”
I didn’t bother asking for his consent. It wasn’t like he had a choice to begin with.
Clack.
I immediately activated Misplaced Trust. With this, even if he was hiding something, all would be revealed.
“All right, let’s start with a simple question.”
But what was this?
“Tell me. What is your name?”
Just like in Doppelganger Forest, I started with a test question to make sure it was working properly.
And the bastard said absolutely nothing. Why wasn’t he able to answer such a simple question?
Tick, tock.
The only sound to be heard was the steady, repetitive snick of the compass needle making its way around Misplaced Trust’s disk. As the silence stretched on, the tension in the room began to increase.

This warrior body of mine calmly carried out the actions I needed to take at that moment, even without my input. By the time I realized what was happening, my fingers were closing around the handle of the hammer on my back, driven by some subconscious instinct.
I blew out a breath. If nothing else, having a hand on my weapon served to calm me down a little.
“Speak, Lilgreams,” I demanded once more. “What is your name?”
He avoided my gaze. But the way his eyes shifted to the right was beyond strange. A sense of unease and wrongness crept over me.
“I’ll ask you one more time.” I pulled my hammer out and leveled it at him. “What is your name?”
Once again, he didn’t respond.
All right, so he’s going to stay silent until the end? In that case, I’ll break his arms and legs and try again.
Decision made, I tightened my grip on my hammer and readied a swing.
But at that moment, he broke his silence and spoke.
“I. Got. Caught.”
It was a single, short sentence, yet I immediately got the sense that there was something off about his voice. And that feeling ended up being spot on.
“Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught.”
Like a skipping CD, he repeated the same word over and over again, his pupils twitching unnaturally and his voice shrill with anxiety. He was panicking. Terrified.
“Caught. Caught. Caught. Caught—”
“What are you?”
My hand shot out to clamp around his neck and hoist him into the air. As he dangled there, his dialogue changed. “What do I do?”
I hesitated.
“What do? What do? What do? What do? What do? What do? What do? What do?”
This sensation was one I had never experienced before. I was the one holding him up by the neck, so why did I feel so unsettled?
“What do? What do? What do—”
And then, he suddenly cut himself off.
He raised his head to look at me. His pupils, which had been twisted to the right in an unnatural way, had bounced back to the front to meet mine. And slowly, haltingly, he began to speak.
“I know.”
He sounded like he’d come to some sort of realization. A fresh wave of unease washed over me as I raised my hammer.
“What I need to do.”
Boom!

The body I was holding promptly exploded. The explosion itself wasn’t anything to write home about. The hand I had wrapped around his neck stung a bit after, but even that felt less like a wound and more like a regular old rash.
However, that explosion had ripped the stranger’s flesh and blood right out of him and sent hundreds of little bone shards scattering across the room.
“A priest...won’t do much good here.”
The shock of being covered in human remains lasted only a moment before I let out a long sigh.
Damn it, I screwed up.

Although my mind rushed to provide excuses, in the end, I could only chalk up this failure to a lack of foresight on my end. I had always thought of myself as someone who acted with the worst-case scenario in mind at all times, but I hadn’t seen this coming at all.
...No, even then, how could I ever have anticipated that?

Even as I reflected on my shortcomings, I couldn’t shake that thought away. I would’ve been hard-pressed to predict that particular outcome, and it wasn’t something I would have been able to deal with even if I had known it was coming.
After all, how was I supposed to stop Emergency Escape?

It was a skill that defied all attempts to counter it. After all, unless you were a god, you couldn’t bring back the dead. Theoretically, you could call it the best escape skill in the game, but that was only because the cost of the skill was the caster’s own life—
Let’s stop that useless train of thought there and deal with the immediate problems.
“Yandel...!”
“I’m fine, so don’t freak out. Oh, and I need to think this over, so leave me alone for a second.”
I reassured my companions who rushed over to me in a panic, and then I replayed the situation again in my mind’s eye as I took some time to think.
The past few minutes could pretty much all be summed up in one sentence.
Something was pretending to be Maderkin Lilgreams.
So who was the culprit?
There was only one answer I could come up with.
The village chief. No, to be more precise, someone or something sent by the village chief.
I doubted the village chief would panic like that the moment he got caught.
In any case, with a potential culprit identified, my next step was to tackle the fundamental questions that formed the basis of any good hypothesis.
Why? And how?
For what reason, and with what method did he do this? Many possibilities crossed my mind, but no concrete answers. It was still too much of a mystery.
Was he trying to trick me into thinking that he was innocent? No, maybe he just wanted to keep an eye on me in secret...
It was still unclear what his goal was.
And what did he use to pull something like this off?

I couldn’t think of any essences that would have helped him do this. There were a few active skills that could steal another person’s body, but they didn’t fit the bill here. Most of them required the caster to be nearby, for one, and when the body was taken over, there was a string leading from the caster to the target that was visible to the naked eye.
Right. So it’s not an essence. Which means...
The thing I saw was probably functionally similar to an evil spirit.
The thought caused a cold sweat to slick my palms.

Still, I ignored the chill and forced myself to keep thinking this over, even asking my allies for their input, but it didn’t get me anywhere. All I had was a theory without a lot of supporting evidence.
The chief has a way of stealing other people’s bodies like an evil spirit.
Nevertheless, it didn’t hurt to be cautious.

Once we were done dealing with the fallout of Lilgreams’s Emergency Escape, as unsatisfying as it was, I led the group through the library. We immediately noticed two key differences from how we’d left the place.
The books... They’re back.

The summoning books we had used last time had restocked. By the time we departed the island, the lower bookshelves were virtually empty, but now even the books that we’d left scattered around had been cleaned up and put back in their proper places.
The stairs were reset too.
The stairs leading to the upper shelves with the books of rank-three monsters had disappeared as well, returning to their original state.
Hmm, then what triggers the reset? Is it time?
If that was the case, it was probably tied to the rainy season in some way, but there was no way to know for sure right now.
“Yandel, this is a good thing if you think about it. This means we’ll be able to get essences much more easily.”
“Ah... that’s true.”
As Amelia said, this was ultimately a positive. Although the stairs being reset was a little annoying, this practically confirmed that we could do unlimited, continuous farming here.
Well, that wasn’t to say there weren’t any downsides.
If it resets while we’re still making our way through the stacks, then it’ll be tough for us to ever reach the top of the bookshelf with hard work alone.

Library Island, which was already pretty difficult, now had a time limit on it as well. However, it was too early to start grumbling. We could complain later when our goal went from just farming for essences to actually clearing it.
Since we know it’ll reset at some point, let’s stop wasting time.
I brushed aside any lingering frustration or concern and decided to focus solely on the reason we came here in the first place.
To be honest, games that required grinding were my type of game. Once I got into the zone, it was like all of my thoughts went quiet, leaving me only with a steady sense of progress.
[You have killed a Frost Wolf.]
[You have killed a Stone Golem.]
[You have killed a Hobgoblin.]
[You have killed an Ice Orc Warrior.]
[You have killed a Yeti.]
[You have killed a Luture Talismancer...]
After that, we split our group into two teams: one dedicated to finding books with good prey, and one combat team.
Rank nine, rank eight, rank seven...
As the number of shelves we had climbed increased, so too did the difficulty, and once rank-fours started popping up, we shifted our focus and started looking for specific monsters in the books.
Mana stones were dropped.
Experience was gained.
And...
“An essence!”
Although none of the essences that popped up could be given to members of Anabada, as we accrued multiple essences per day, our group as a whole steadily grew stronger and stronger.
“That’s it for today! We’ll stop here for the night. Everyone, get some rest!”
On our eighty-fifth day in the labyrinth, the day finally came.
[Your soul has resonated and is being drawn into a different world.]

chapters.title: Chapter 544: Ghost (2)
paragraphs: In the city, the fifteenth of every month marked the meeting of the evil spirits. My routine was pretty much the same every time.
Vwing!
First, I’d start up my computer and log in before checking how many people were in the chatroom “Long Live Korea’s Independence.”
No one’s here yet.

After that, I’d head to the bulletin board and skim through some of the posts to get up to date on current events. From there, I’d enter the chat room to hang out with Baekho for about an hour. Once he left, I would spend the remaining time chatting with Hyeonbyeol before excusing myself when it was time for the Round Table to open.
Clack, clack.

There was nothing particularly different about my routine today. As always, my monitor displayed the bulletin board. I began reading through the titles of the posts that had already begun to pop up like someone else might read the morning newspaper with a coffee in hand.
No stress, just casually—
I doubled back to look at the first post of the day, and when I read the title, the sound tumbled out of my mouth unbidden.
[Rafdonia’s Palace: Basement Floor One Soon to Close.]
What was this?
Click, click.
Despite expecting it to be a simple troll post, I clicked the link repeatedly. This was news I couldn’t afford to ignore.

As expected, there was nothing in the main body of the post. These types of posts were usually just made to claim the honor of being the first poster of the night and were then fleshed out with further information after the fact with the edit function.
What was important was the comments, and just reading them was enough to let me fact-check a few things.
arolf5205: Man, I wanted to be first this time.
NIKAMOTO: Looks like this post is going to go viral.
AI_DIDIGO: Fact 1: A review of the first posts on the forum every month shows that 56% of them have more than 100 comments and go viral.
└Ki11Humans77: Wow, it’s didigo. Please let me get a rank 3 essence during my next adventure.
└MarkG: but what’s so good about having a viral post?
└Pawel: the admins give you a bit of GP. but I don’t think that’s the main reason people do it.
The users weren’t calling the post out for being bait and were instead talking about other topics. Their reaction told me one thing.
Damn it, it’s real.
The palace had declared Basement Floor One would soon be closed. The information was not only true but common knowledge to the people of the city at this point.
I quickly refreshed the post and scrolled down. The actual productive comments usually came later since they took a bit more time to write out.
Darkrealm93: but honestly i dont get the palace’s play here. why are they stopping other people from exploring the place next month?
└Akaistos: Didn’t you hear? They say it’s too dangerous.
└Darkrealm93: did you think i was asking because i didnt know that? im saying there must be a different reason
└WhyDoYouSniffShit: It’s obvious. They’re in the middle of a war but everyone is talking about going to the basement instead so they got pissy.
└funkinthetrunk: But most of us still don’t even know how to get to Basement Floor One. Why even bother giving an order to not go when we can’t anyway?
└WhyDoYouSniffShit: Because they want everyone to stop wasting time looking for it and go back to being moving targets for arrows.

In essence, the issue was that it had only been two months since the existence of Basement Floor One was made known to the outside world, and in the last cycle, two additional clans had managed to enter it as well.
And a lot of people from those two clans hadn’t been able to enter either.
