There were quite a few adventurers who had personally watched their allies go through the portal before returning to the city. They would’ve spread even more news about Basement Floor One to the world. People with good information networks might have even already figured out how to get in. Not even “might”—they almost certainly did know by now.
So everyone must’ve been getting ready to enter again, and that’s why the palace stepped in to stop them.
That, and if the information was something a large clan could get their hands on, the palace would definitely know how to open the portal by now as well.
This was getting pretty interesting.
Afterward, I continued to scroll through the comments and other posts flooding the bulletin board before finally letting go of my mouse.
Tap, tap.
Thoughts swirled through my mind. If the palace forbade it, then people wouldn’t be able to enter this floor for some time. Tsk, then was I going to have to change my plan and wait?
I ran through various scenarios in my head.
“Ah, right, they’re waiting for me.”
After a while, I noticed I’d spent quite a bit of time lost in thought, so I rushed to join the chat room.
“Hansu, you’re here?”
“Oh, bro! Late again, huh?”
Hyeonbyeol and Baekho greeted me as I entered.
“Sorry. I’m pretty late today.”
“It’s fine. I wasn’t worried.”
“...What?”
As I tilted my head, Baekho grinned.
“The main character always arrives last, or something like that, right? Not that that’s a bad thing. No, actually, it’s pretty cool...”
What was this guy going on about? I shouldn’t have given him any sort of reaction. I smirked as I sat down on the sofa. “So, how have the two of you been?”
“I’ve been fine, Hansu.”
“What about you, Baekho? You doing all right?”

It was a simple question that bypassed the need for a detailed answer. Even as I asked it, though, I couldn’t help but glance at Hyeonbyeol, wary of her presence in the room. It seemed Baekho noticed as well.
“It’s fine. Hyeonbyeol here already knows who I am anyway.”
“Hey, Big Bro! I’d say I’m a pretty smart guy, so how would I not know that? You can mention that I’m outside the walls right now in front of her. It’s fine.”
“...Heh.” When Baekho Lee declared what he was up to like it wasn’t anything special, excitement flashed through Hyeonbyeol’s eyes.
“...Baekho, are you really okay with this?” I asked.

“Why wouldn’t I be? All three of us here share common roots. It doesn’t matter to me. Honestly, I didn’t really like how we were keeping Sis in the dark. And it’s more fun to shoot the breeze with three people instead of two.”

That still left the question of whether he was really okay with it unanswered, but since he was claiming it was fine, it wasn’t my place to argue with him. I also kind of agreed with parts of his argument.
Yeah... when all three of us talk together, it’s almost like a spiritual experience...

To be more precise, it felt like being back in Korea. Talking about the army, politics, and our urge to eat kimchi was something we could only do here. Although I was genuinely satisfied with my life in this new world, there were some moments when I definitely missed getting to talk about the one I came from with people who got it.
“Well, then how is it out there? Did you find the Noarkians?”
“Yeah, it’s been about a week now, and for now I’m just wandering around and seeing what I can find. As for Auril Gavis, though—haven’t found the guy yet.”
“Auril Gavis...?”
“Ah, Hyeonbyeol probably doesn’t know. The reason I left the city was to find that bastard.”
“Oh... R-Really?”
Hyeonbyeol usually had an air of confidence and self-assurance about her, but she looked flustered as we brought up something this significant so casually right in front of her.
It’s been a while since I’ve seen her like this.
This, too, made me feel nostalgic, and Hyeonbyeol turned to glare at me like she could sense what I was thinking in my gaze.
“I wasn’t laughing.”
“I didn’t say you were.”
I made the wise decision to shut my mouth.

In any case, I asked Baekho the questions I had about life outside the castle walls, and he kindly filled me in on everything he discovered. Every single little detail was interesting to me since, even in the game, the area was inaccessible, but if I were to pick out the most interesting tidbit, it would definitely be this:
“You can actually plant things and farm out here.”
Unlike Rafdonia, the world outside could function without mana stones. However, that raised even more questions.
“Then why do those people keep dungeon crawling?”
Why was Noark still waging war? Why did they refuse to leave the labyrinth alone, to the point of even making their own portal out there?
Unfortunately, Baekho wasn’t able to give me a straight answer. “I don’t know. But there’s definitely a reason for it. And I think Auril Gavis is deeply involved.”
“That seems to be the case. All right, tell me more when you figure out more later.”
“Sure, Big Bro.”
By the time that conversation ended, we only had about ten minutes before Baekho Lee logged out, and so we spent the last few minutes talking about nothing in particular.
“Hah, I think I was the one who talked the most today. Next time, please tell me what you’ve been up to, bro. I’m pretty curious too. You know what I mean, right?”
“I do. I’ll tell you about it next time.”
“Then I’ll see you later!”
With that, Baekho left when his time ran out, and nothing of note happened once I was alone with Hyeonbyeol either.
“Considering how curious he seemed, looks like you’ve been up to something interesting?”
“Ahaha... Nothing like that...”
“You’re avoiding the question. But whatever, I’m going to read now—do you want a book?”
“Oh, sure. Thanks.”
I casually took the book Hyeonbyeol handed me. I’d had to stop at a pretty interesting point last time, so I kind of wanted to see where it was going to go next.
Why is this so good?
I found myself occasionally snickering to myself while reading, and shedding tears at the more emotional parts.
With how immersed I was in the story, it startled me when Hyeonbyeol, sprawled out on the other end of the sofa, kicked my knee.
“Huh, what?”
“Isn’t it about time?”
“Oh, right.” With a bit of regret in my heart, I closed the book and got up.
“If it’s that good, come back later. I’ll let you borrow the book again...”
“No, there’s no need. I have GP so I’ll just buy it and read it myself.”
She didn’t respond.
“I’ll see you later.”

With that, I left the chat room and stretched my arms over my head. To be honest, I probably didn’t need to stretch in this place, but it was a sort of habit of mine whenever I got done reading. It also just felt refreshing, like it woke up the mind.
“All right, let’s go.”
I had a lot to do at the Round Table today.

As I put on the outfit I always wore—a lion mask that completely covered my face and a sleek, navy suit underneath it—and stood in front of the mirror, I felt a mysterious sense of confidence well up within me.
It was like I had become someone who could do anything. However, setting that feeling aside, I took a moment to engage in some honest self-evaluation.
This is hard work.
I sighed. Having to keep up with so many different characters was tiring. Was I going to get eaten up by my own personas?
Not that I had any intentions of stopping.
Step, step.
After checking my clothes in the mirror, I walked through the hallway to the room that held the Round Table. As always, everyone else was here before me.
“Pshehe, you’re here.”
“Heh... Welcome, Mr. Lion!”
“You’re last today as well.”
As I ignored their greetings and headed straight for my seat, I was suddenly reminded of something Baekho said earlier.
“The main character always arrives last, or something like that, right?”

Honestly, in the context of the Round Table, at least, he was right. I did make a point of coming here last on purpose. However, to be fair, it wasn’t that I enjoyed the attention I got for being last, but that it couldn’t be helped.
It’d be even weirder if I came early.

The people who got here earlier passed the time talking to each other. There’d be no point in me joining them. It wasn’t like I was going to joke around and exchange small talk, and things would just get awkward if I sat next to them without saying anything.
So I did this instead.
“Then... since everyone is here... let’s begin the meeting...”
All I had done was sit down, lost in my own thoughts and ignoring everyone else, but Wolf carefully turned to me.
“Is that...a...a problem...?”
“Not particularly.”
“Then... let’s begin. We’re all busy people.”
For some reason, Wolf was the one leading the meeting today. Well, it didn’t really matter to me who did—
Yikes, why do I start thinking like this whenever I wear the mask?
While I did think it was a good thing to keep my guard up and be wary of others, I decided to revisit this thought later and focus on the proceedings for now.
Deer was the first to go.
“It has officially been confirmed that the palace is barring entry to Basement Floor One. Anyone who tries to go down and ignore this decree will be executed without mercy.”
“An awfully severe punishment.”
“Ah, of course, this severe punishment only applies to clans larger than a set size. We suspect that the punishments won’t be nearly as severe for individual adventurers or parties.”
Well, that was understandable, then. Just by stopping clans from going in, they’d be able to keep their front lines from collapsing.
Damn, these palace guys. They’ve never done anything helpful for anybody.
In any case, once Deer’s turn was done, the other members quickly went down the line, and a total of two had something memorable to say.
“If you use distortion magic on the Unnamed Sculptures on the third floor, you can obtain fragments with one of three different markings on them. They are the key to entering Basement Floor One.”
Queen shared the method for entering Basement Floor One, the Records Archives.
“Pshehe, in a sense, this may be good news for you. Unfortunately, the squadron we had clearing the eighth floor failed and took a big hit.”
Then came Clown.
His statement was something that I normally would’ve just skimmed past without a second thought, but this time it hit me like a bolt of lightning.
Their eighth-floor operation failed...?
Although I didn’t have any concrete reason to think so, it didn’t seem like a mere coincidence.
Without thinking, I unconsciously spoke aloud.
“Kalheum.”
Kalheum, the City of Light, was one of the Rifts on the eighth floor—the very same one whose Guardian was Milayel.
“Pshe... he...?” Clown’s empty laughter stuttered to a stop. “Mr. Lion... How did you...?”
What the...? It really was that specific Rift? Did that mean there was some sort of a connection between their failure and Milayel appearing in the basement?
As my mind began to whir, Clown suddenly shrunk back. “Ah—Ahem! T-That was a foolish question. Mr. Lion no doubt has ears on the ground in Noark as well.”
I hadn’t even had to say anything, and he came up with excuses for me all on his own. Was this one of the perks of having influence?
In any case, everyone’s eyes were on me now as Clown made a clown of himself in the background.
It’s already my turn. What should I share?

Today, I didn’t even need to ask myself that. Usually, even when interesting pieces of information cropped up, I pretended to be indifferent and got through my turn with random information that supposedly matched their quality.
But I’m not here to get information today.

Well, in truth, that had been my original intention, but that was before an unexpected hurdle was shoved into my path. The palace had thrown all my plans into disarray. At this rate, additional forces would stop coming down to the basement entirely.
That was why I had no choice but to be proactive.
Since Queen already told them how to open the door, I can’t use that...
And even though the palace had announced the death penalty, I wasn’t all that worried. After all, I knew a thing or two about adventurers, and this one was a well-known fact.
“In Basement Floor One, the Records Archives...”
Adventurers didn’t care about their lives.
“Bjorn Yandel has obtained two single-digit Numbered Items in the last two months.”
Not when there was money to be made.

chapters.title: Chapter 545: Ghost (3)
paragraphs: Once I said my piece, I sat back and studied the shocked looks on everyone’s faces.
All right, if even these guys are reacting like this, ordinary adventurers will lose their minds at this information.
“In just two months...”
“Single-digit Numbered Items...”
“...Two of them?”
Well, one of them was from Garphas’s Necklace, and the other was a lucky break from killing a Guardian, but...
I hadn’t lied.
Also, I never would have been able to obtain those items if not for the ridiculous number of mana stones in Basement Floor One or the fact that Guardians of the Rift can spawn there.
Shaaa!
As the jewel turned green, silence fell over the table. Their previously identical reactions now began to deviate. Just a moment earlier, all of them had been shocked by the announcement itself.
“How did you...? Even in a place like that...?”
“There are fewer than 120 people in Basement Floor One right now...”
“Heh... Really... In there?”
But now some of them were beginning to once again wonder who I was.

“Pshehe. How foolish. There is no place in the world that Lion’s eyes cannot reach. Weren’t you paying attention earlier? He even knew about what happened on the eighth floor with the Rift. That... That was a secret that not even fifty people knew about.”
“That’s true... Besides, the first piece of information we got about the basement came from a member of the Hektz Clan. We can’t dismiss the possibility that someone down there is his informant.”
Others accepted the fact that I knew about this without asking too many questions. And as for the rest...
“If that is the case, this informant must be someone close to Bjorn Yandel,” our resident member of the palace Deer said with a glint in his eyes, looking like a bloodhound that had caught a scent.
I mean, even if they are, what are you going to do about it?

I slid my gaze to the next seat over to gauge Fox’s—Versyl’s—reaction as well. Because she was wearing a mask, it was a little hard to read her, but I couldn’t see any suspicion in her eyes either. If anything, the emotions that were visible in her eyes were the exact opposite.
Confusion and panic. She’s probably worried one of our clan members is a mole.
Well, I’d get more insight into her thought process by seeing what she did after Ghost Busters closed today. She had immediately informed me about the traitor situation with Missha, at least.
In any case, it seemed I didn’t need to worry about Versyl, so I shifted my attention to Goblin.
Tsk, this guy is the one I’m most worried about.
Goblin hadn’t gotten swept up in all the excitement and had instead been silent this whole time as if lost in thought.
Yeah, he’s just sitting there... but I’ve still got a bad feeling about it.

I had fed the Round Table all sorts of information that would, to the outside observer, directly contradict the idea that Lion was Bjorn Yandel, but there were some people in this world who possessed unbelievable gut instincts.
For some reason, Goblin seemed to be one of those people.
“Deer.” I turned to the person who had started the meeting today before Goblin could have any more time to think. “How long are you going to sit there?”
I got a confused look in return.
“It’s your turn again.”
Anyway, let’s go another round. I have plenty more to tell you.
One round.
“All different kinds of monsters and Guardians of the Rift can appear in the Records Archives on Basement Floor One.”
Two rounds.
“The Records Archives has all new monsters, including mutant monsters.”
“Um... by mutants...?”

A question that I wouldn’t have even acknowledged before, I instead answered graciously. “A monster that possesses the skills of multiple different monsters. For example, a single monster that has both the passive of an Ogre and the actives of a Troll.”
“That’s unbelievable—!”
“B-But— Wouldn’t that mean entirely new combinations of essences are possible?”
A few members let out shouts of obvious disbelief, but I didn’t need to provide evidence to convince them. In the end, the jewel would confirm it for me.
Shaaa!
As the gem once again turned a bright green, the others grew louder and louder.
Glare!

Yet beyond its glow, eyes that shone an even greedier green gleamed around the table. That was only natural. What self-respecting player would be able to sit back and do nothing after hearing about such an incredible hunting ground?
“Pshehe... This is getting interesting.”
“Actually, I don’t see why Noark would be particularly interested in this. It’s not like you’ll be able to do much more than twiddle your thumbs anyway.”
A psychological battle ensued between the Clown of Noark and the Deer of the Palace. Of course, this was such a common occurrence at this point that I didn’t so much as twitch.
Well, it’s still fun to watch these two bicker.
And it seemed everyone else felt the same, as no one stepped in to stop them, instead watching with interest.
“Hah! Like the Rafdonian adventurers who haven’t been able to so much as touch the eighth and ninth floors—or their essences—in over a year at this point? Pshehe.”
“Didn’t you hear Lion? Based on what he said, there won’t even be any need for us to go up to the eighth or ninth floors anymore.”
“Ah, I did hear him. But so what about it?”

“...Do you really not get it? If this news spreads to the outside world, the palace will immediately revoke its embargo and even actively support any adventurers who want to travel down there. From there, it’ll only be a matter of time before Noark falls for good.”
“Hoh, is that so? I’m quaking in my boots,” Clown drawled.

His reaction only intensified Deer’s ridicule. “Well, now that I think about it, a clown like you might not be capable of the critical thinking required to see how screwed you are. After all, you’re the same guy who just bragged to your enemies about how your last quest failed. This is probably all a funny joke to you—”

“Oh, really? Even though the reason I said this was interesting news was completely different than yours?” Clown cut Deer off with his characteristic laugh. “Say, why are you assuming this news will benefit the palace?”
“What... do you mean?”

“Do you really not get it?” Clown gave an exaggerated shrug, waving his hand in the direction of my seat. His eyes met mine in a one-sided look of camaraderie before he turned back to Deer. “Why do you think Mr. Lion brought up information about Basement Floor One here at the Round Table? You have a brain somewhere in there, don’t you? Please consider using it today.”
Deer chose to remain silent. Someone else responded in his stead.
“To disrupt the palace.” It was Queen, who had been quiet since this discussion began. “That is the only explanation I can come up with.”
The other members seemed to agree with her logic.
“So I’m not the only one who thinks so.”
“...There’s no way Mr. Lion isn’t aware of what’ll happen if this news spreads.”
“He has never acted so openly before.”

I was sharing this information right after the palace put out an order to stop anyone from coming down to the basement. Not only that, but it was also information that was juicy enough to tempt people to go in even under the threat of punishment. It seemed all of the other members had managed to figure out what my intentions were based on that alone.
Well, it didn’t matter if they figured it out or not.
“Pshe, you were acting all high and mighty when you didn’t even realize something as simple as that. Doesn’t that make you a joke too?”

“...You’re interpreting things in a way that best suits your narrative. He could just as easily have said it to help the palace too. The palace was unaware that Basement Floor One was such an incredible place.”
“Hmm... really? Well, let’s see which one of us is misinterpreting things in our favor.”

All the members of the Round Table turned to me. Although they didn’t say anything aloud, I could tell what they were thinking by the expectant looks in their eyes. They were waiting for me to tell them which one of the two was right.
However, as my silence stretched on, one of them got impatient enough to speak up.
“So...” In the end, the person to break the silence first was none other than Black. “Which is it?”
It was a bit unexpected. I did figure someone would step up as their spokesperson, but I never expected it to be her. She tended to keep her mouth shut outside of her turns.
“Lion, are you on the side of the palace, or on the side of Noark?” Black boldly asked, her face unreadable under her pure black mask.
“Cocky of you,” I growled a bit in response.

I didn’t imbue any murderous intent into my words, but Black immediately broke eye contact and looked down. Though it seemed she snapped out of it a second later because she made a point of raising her head again and forcing her eyes to meet mine.
Looks like she has some backbone.
I filed that piece of information away, adding it to the little I knew about her. Then, to reward her for her guts, I declared, “But I will answer you.”
I kept my eyes on Black as I placed my hand on the gem.
Someone gulped. Everyone was looking at me. Clown seemed to hope that I was on Noark’s side, and Deer the exact opposite. The others seemed to care less about sides and more about the truth itself.
“The palace and Noark...”
So I decided to make my stance loud and clear.
“I’m not on either of their sides.”
These weren’t just empty words.

Noark was my enemy. The first time I lost a companion, it had been to Orcules’ Dragon Slayer, and they also put me through all kinds of crap on the first floor. In the process, Erwen’s older sister, Daria, had died.
I don’t even have to get into the palace.
The cold rage that had washed over me all those months ago was still festering in my heart. And I intended to get back at them for it someday.
Shaaa!
The Round Table’s jewel glowed green with the light of truth. It even seemed a little brighter than usual for some reason.

“Then why...” I heard someone ask faintly at the sight, almost as if possessed. I turned in the direction of the voice to find that the speaker was Deer. “Lion,” he pleaded. “Why did you tell us this?”

As someone from the palace, as someone who was used to the political power struggles and machinations of the royal court, it was only natural that Deer would be wondering what my angle was. Lion, this powerful, mysterious man in a mask, had declared he wasn’t on anyone’s side. So why did he do something that many would argue flouted the will of the royal family?
Lion’s answer to that question was simple.
As always.
Tap, tap.
I tapped my fingers against my armrest twice before opening my mouth to speak.
“Because it...”
As always...
“...seemed like it would be fun.”
That should be more than enough.
After that, the Round Table ended without further incident, but I had no complaints.
I had succeeded in relaying just how great of a hunting ground Basement Floor One was, and it seemed the others were also running out of information to share anyway.
It doesn’t seem like a bad idea to end on that note.
And so, I coolly excused myself and left.
Yeah, if I try and get another round going, it’ll just get annoying.

Once I was back in Hansu Lee’s room, I laid down on the bed and loafed around for a few minutes before getting back on the computer to do some more scrolling. It was a touch ironic, but the message board on my screen right now was my sole window to the outside world.
“Hehehe... Pfft, this guy, really...”
Oof, this was hurting my pride a little. Why were these pricks so funny?
As I browsed through the posts, snickering to myself, I noticed a new post rise to the top of the pinned section as the page refreshed.
[Complete collection of all the information about Basement Floor One, Records Archives.]
I clicked it immediately, and the contents were exactly what you’d expect.

Starting off with a step-by-step explanation of how to enter the Archives, it then went on to disclose the fact that monsters from all different floors—including Guardians of the Rift—could spawn there and took things a step further by revealing the existence of mutant monsters. Most importantly, it mentioned that Bjorn Yandel had obtained two single-digit Numbered Items down there.
In short, the post contained a concise summary of everything I had just said at the Round Table.
And the author of this post was someone I had never seen before—BFKILLER.
It’s definitely a member of the Round Table...
But who? There were ten members including me, so it was impossible to pinpoint who it might be.
I shared these pieces of information specifically so that they could spread them, so it’s not like this is a bad thing...
But I didn’t expect anyone would go quite so public.

This was completely different from what I had been anticipating, which was that those with good information networks would hear the news first, and then it’d trickle down to the rest of the masses the month after.
Well, even though we come together every month, we all have our own loyalties and individual agendas.
It wouldn’t be far-fetched to assume that someone in our group of ten had wanted this information to spread as quickly as possible for some reason. In any case, that wasn’t what mattered.
I quickly scrolled down to the comment section. Most of the earlier comments, the ones left before the post blew up, questioned its credibility.
YPPL: Wow. Just become an author at this rate.
goooooooooodd2: Someone’s desperate to go viral.
q1q2q3: So where is the proof? Who’s going to believe you if you’re not willing to put out? These claims are baseless.
The users deemed it clickbait and mocked the author accordingly.
However, over time, those reactions gradually phased out.
Amer91: I’ll need to drop by Sculpture Temple next month. I have a feeling the suckers who fall for this will be having a picnic there.
└AI_DIDIGO: Fact 1: That the Unnamed Fragments are the key to opening Basement Floor One is something the palace and many larger clans have already been made aware of.
└ScottBANE: wow, for real, sir DIDIGO?
└Adi: Wait, if they’re right about how to get in, then isn’t there a possibility that everything else this guy said is true too?
└Amer91: No, that’s unlikely... I think they’re just trying to get engagement by sharing one real piece of information to cover for the rest.

└Adi: No, think about it. If they just wanted engagement, why would they reveal so much extra information no one else was aware of? They could’ve just told us how to open the portal and that would’ve been more than enough to go viral.

└ScottBANE: also, the more I think about it, the more plausible this post gets. at least one of the people on basement floor one right now has to be a player, and it makes sense that they’d share information about what’s going on down there via GB.

From there, users who already knew the method for opening the portal began to chime in with comments of their own, and public perception slowly began to shift away from it being a simple troll post to a somewhat believable one.
All right, at this rate, the news should reach the city in—huh?
As I continued to scroll, feeling pleased with myself, a certain thread caught my eye and stopped me in my tracks.
Pnec: You idiots. Someone is trying to spoon-feed you information and you can’t even take it.
└bigD: what do you mean?
└Bling0_0: This guy’s always trolling. Ignore him.
└Pnec: Yeah, I was waiting for you to show up, asshole. You don’t know what you’re talking about.
Ah, these guys were fighting in the comments again. At this point, these were familiar nicknames to me, so I decided to scroll through the rest of their conversation.
└Bling0_0: Hm? I don’t know what I’m talking about, huh? Well I know that you’re the 1 incher with a 1KB brain, so.
└Pnec: More proof you’re talking out of your ass. Tsk tsk. Whether you trust this post or not, it’s the truth.
└Bling0_0: ...and how are you so sure?
└Pnec: Because I heard this same information from someone credible not too long ago. And if you dare try to insult that person too, I’ll come find you and kill you.
Huh?
Not too long ago?
Is this guy a member of the Round Table too?
Just as the theory crossed my mind, something strange happened.
└bigD: what do you mean?
└(Deleted Message.)
└Pnec: Yeah, I was waiting for you to show up, asshole. You don’t know what you’re talking about.
└(Deleted Message.)
└Pnec: More proof you’re talking out of your ass. Tsk tsk. Whether you trust this post or not, it’s the truth.
└(Deleted Message.)
└Pnec: Because I heard this same information from someone credible not too long ago. And if you dare try to insult that person too, I’ll come find you and kill you.
For some reason, the user by the name of Bling0_0 had deleted all their messages and disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 546: Ghost (4)
paragraphs: The morning after my visit to the community message boards, I felt a deep exhaustion in my bones as I opened my eyes and began running through my daily routine.
“Here, here. The food is here!”

Things had changed from back when our three groups were simply traveling together without a plan. We had group formations now, along with assigned roles for everyone outside of combat as well. For instance, a total of four people had been put on cooking duty and kept us all fed each day. Oh, and the one who oversaw this duty was Missha.
“How is it? Does it suit your tastes? Since it’s breakfast, I put in a little less spice.”
“Other than the fact that there isn’t much meat, it’s fine.”
“Ah... meat...”
“I was joking. We need to ration the meat since we don’t know what might happen.”
After I was done eating, I approached Versyl, who was in charge of inventory, and asked her about our food stores.
“We have enough to feed all thirty-eight people for sixty-one more days. If we downsize everyone’s portion sizes starting now, we might be able to increase that number by about four days.”
“No, that’s fine. If we reduce it any further, how will we have the energy to fight?”
We had about two months’ worth of food left.

In truth, this was mostly thanks to the Armin Adventuring Group coming in with considerable provisions. The Hektz Clan, on the other hand, had been shipwrecked and had used up all of their remaining food in a panic. Meanwhile, our Anabada Clan had only come prepared with enough food to feed our seven members for four months.
It’s the eighty-sixth day...
If we were on the seventh floor right now, it would have closed ten days ago. And yet we were still inside the labyrinth.
At this rate, there’s no guarantee we’ll get out of here before the two-hundredth day.

Of course, that didn’t mean I was necessarily worried about our food situation. Soon, new adventurers would come down here with their own supplies, and if those weren’t enough, we could hunt and cast distortion magic on the monsters, just like in Ice Rock.
“Got it. Anyway, besides food, feel free to be generous with our supplies whenever anyone asks for some.”
“I’m already doing that. Ah, also...”
“Yeah?”
“...Never mind. I’ll talk to you later when I’m a bit more certain.”

I could immediately tell what she had been about to say. She no doubt wanted to warn me that there was an undercover evil spirit in our group spying on me. But to tell me that, she would need to reveal the fact that she was an evil spirit too, so she was hesitating.
“Okay. Then I’ll be going.”
“Okay.”
After checking on our inventory, I went over to the head of security, Amelia, to ask if anything happened last night.
“Nothing special.”

Although that was always what she said, I couldn’t afford to not ask. You never knew when an enemy might pop out in the labyrinth. And we couldn’t be sure we were safe even when we were hidden from the outside world. Inside this mysterious place where anything could happen, we needed to stay vigilant at all times, as you never knew when a new problem might rear its ugly head.
Case in point:
“However, the Hektz Clan’s warrior, Vilkus, seems to have hit his limit. I don’t think he’s sleeping well these days.”

The expedition team’s security detail was honestly more of a patrol group that stayed awake at night to keep an eye out for any trouble while the rest were sleeping. It was made up of six people, and the old timer who had once been part of the palace’s investigation unit acted as Amelia’s right-hand man.
“Got it. I’ll go and talk to him myself later.”
“Then I won’t worry about him.”
“Huh?”
“You’re like an idol to the warriors. And he seems to respect you even more than most, so if you talk to him, the problem should sort itself out.”
After my morning chat with Amelia, I paid the wizard trio from the Armin Adventuring Group a visit.
“From what I heard from Emily, you were up all night doing research again. Were there any findings?”

The three of them acted as our group’s research team. The monsters’ corpses and essences, the library’s books and summoning altar, the stone gates the monsters came out of, and so on—everything we had discovered inside the labyrinth so far was under their careful review.
“Uh... I wouldn’t call it a ‘finding,’ per say...”
“We found something peculiar in the blood sample we collected from the Hipramajent...”
“If you give us a bit more time and funding...”
But for some reason, they always looked nervous whenever I asked them about their progress. I told them multiple times that I wasn’t trying to rush them, but their reactions never changed.
Was it a leftover habit from working for the Magic Tower?
“Heh, you’re our boss, though, Lord Baron.”
“So even if you tell us that... it’s hard for us to really relax.”
“Exactly. Plus, if we’re too comfortable, we won’t get results on time.”
Well, it wasn’t like I could argue with that. In any case, listening to the research team’s report marked the end of my morning to-do list.
“All right, if everyone’s done with breakfast, return to your posts!”
It was time to get back to work. Everyone got to eat their fill this morning and even had time to digest.
“Summon the monsters!”
So let’s get going.
My afternoon routine was just as simple as my morning one.
We gathered the books that we had selected the night before and hunted everything inside.
Splash!

Mana stones covered the library’s floor, and whenever an essence dropped, we would stop summoning for a bit to find out what it was. We didn’t even have to rely on eyewitness testimony like amateurs anymore. We had set up a recording crystal above us that was taping the entire hunting ground.
“It’s a Katanda’s essence.”
“A green Katanda essence must be Prophane Prophecy. What do you think, Your Lordship?”
“We don’t need it.”
“I see. Then is there anyone else who wants this essence?”
Once we confirmed the identity of an essence, I had first dibs, but if I passed, then the next person on the list had a chance to take it. If no one on the waiting list took it, it was discarded.
“Isn’t this kind of bizarre? We’ve got a rank-four essence sitting right in front of us, and no one wants it.”
“We’ve even been discarding some rank-three essences lately, so it’s not that big a surprise.”
“We can get even better essences by waiting a little, so there’s no need to be hasty whenever one pops up.”
“Heh, letting an essence right in front of us go and having it actually be a smart move. No one will believe us when we get out of here and tell them about this.”
“We’re not even putting them in magic vials, though. That’s such a shame. These essences are really valuable...”
“The baron said we need to use our magic vials sparingly, and I think that’s the wise choice.”

Unexpectedly, my fellow adventurers seemed even happier whenever an essence was discarded. That was likely because our hunt was put on pause until the essence naturally faded away. However, that didn’t mean they got to sit around resting.
“What are you doing? Go get more books while the essence is disappearing!”
I used even those windows of time efficiently, sending our troops to the bookshelves to gather more summoning books. Once our stock was replenished, we resumed our feast.
Using that approach, we continued to farm diligently. And ten days after our arrival on Library Island, we got an incredible drop.
“...Lord Baron?”
“We’ll take this one.”
Our clan had finally obtained an essence after passing up on dozens of others.
Spear Dipper.
It was a rank-three monster that had an extremely low probability of spawning in a special area on the sixth floor’s Great Sea.
Naturally, I already had someone in mind for it.
“Ainar.”
“Oh! Nice!”

As I called out to her, Ainar, who had been eyeing the essence since it appeared, quickly ran up to it. She’d had an expectant look in her eyes since I declared we were taking it, which made sense considering she was a spear user now.
However, just giving it to her wouldn’t be fun.
“Wait.”
“Ugh—! Why? Why are you making me wait? You’re going to give it to me anyway—”
“Hm?”
Her mouth snapped shut.
Yeah, that should have been your response from the start.
“All right, take it.”
“Yahoo!”
As soon as I gave her permission, Ainar ran right at the essence. Even though her Aggression had bottomed out, it seemed her Greed was still pretty high.
[The Essence of Spear Dipper has sunk deep into Ainar Fenelin’s soul.]

The light of the essence sunk into Ainar’s skin. Her eyes went wide in exhilaration, and she sounded like an addict as she shouted, “What is this? No way! It’s been a while since I’ve felt so much stronger...!”
Well, that made sense. This guy’s stats were all on the physical side. That said, the skills were where this essence really shined.

[(P) Speciesist—When attacking a target that isn’t of the same species as you, the damage you deal increases relative to the amount of time spent in combat. When attacking a target of the same species, damage is instead reduced.]
One was a perfect passive to go with Ainar’s Slayer Imprint.
[(A) Trident—When using a spear to attack, you deal the same amount of damage to two additional enemies within range.]

The other was an active skill with no cooldowns and barely any MP expenditure. That meant that the skill itself wasn’t all that powerful, but if you built your characters with only powerful skills, they’d collapse like a house of cards.
Trident was the bread-and-butter skill that would replace her Repeated Slash.
All right, then that’s Ainar done...

Of course, she still had a lot of essences that needed to be switched out, but since she didn’t have any empty slots left, there was no point in worrying about her until after we returned to the city.
I have one left, Erwen has one, and Amelia has two...

These were the slots we could work to fill here and now, and if I factored in the number of magic vials we still had left, the number of essences we could secure for our clan increased. It’d be great if, after we erased Ainar’s useless essences back in the city, we could immediately fill those slots with her new ones right after.
...If possible, I should look for Imprint materials as well.
The materials needed for the eighth stage of the Immortality Imprint were dropped by three different rank-three monsters. Not to say there weren’t more material requirements, but...
Those I can buy in the city with money.

Unlike lower-grade materials, the materials from rank-three monsters and higher couldn’t be bought at any price. Even Soul of the Dead, which I needed for the seventh stage, fell into that category. Although it was dropped by the rank-four monster Lich, only one of them had been up on the Central Exchange.
That was why, since I’d had no idea if or when I’d ever get the chance to get my hands on one again, I had used all my money to buy—
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Trident.]
Ainar had just about finished testing out her new essence and getting accustomed to the increase in strength when it happened.
“Captain!”
The only noncombatant among the thirty-eight people here, Navigator Auyen Rockrobe, rushed over to me with a huge summoning book bundled in his arms.
“I-I found it...! Finally!”
“Found what? Calm down before—”
“It’s a book that summons Bellarios!”
As soon as I heard the news, I closed my eyes and let out a long breath.
Finally, it was time.

Bellarios was a rank-three monster that looked just like an eastern dragon, typically found in the Dragon’s Mountains in the middle of the Dark Continent. However, that place was now a warzone, so while they were killable, no one had managed it in a long while.
“Versyl, call everyone at the bookshelves over here too.”
I had been looking forward to facing one of these from the moment I found this library, so I quickly gathered our forces and held a short briefing about how we were going to tackle Bellarios.
Someone, however, wasn’t all that enthusiastic.
“Excuse me...” In the middle of the crowd of adventurers who were listening intently to my plan, a hand carefully went up.
“What is it, Ainar? Are you hungry?”
“That’s not it... I haven’t really gotten used to the new essence I got...”
“So?” I truly couldn’t understand what she was getting at. “What could be better training than a real fight?”
That was a sentiment any barbarian warrior would agree with.
“Well... I... Instead of fighting, just practicing feels better... And more effective? I think it’s also more effective.”
Ah, right. That damn Aggression stat.
“Can’t I just practice here while you’re fighting?” If there was even a sliver of a chance she could avoid a fight, she would try to do so.
Naturally, my answer was already set in stone. “No. You’re joining us in battle this time.”
“...Got it.”
The pitiful look on her face suddenly made me feel like the bad guy here, but I coldly shut down those emotions before my resolve could waver.
“Mister...” whispered Erwen, coming up next to me. “It’s a rank three, but there won’t even be three monsters to fight, just two. Don’t we already have enough people?”

I didn’t know when the two of them got so close that she was willing to back Ainar up like this, but she wasn’t wrong. Ainar not joining the battle? That didn’t matter that much in this particular fight.
The problem is that other people will notice.
She was a member of my clan, and if I bent the rules and let her do whatever she wanted, members of the other clans would start to get resentful, even if they didn’t outwardly show it.
“The decision has already been made. Don’t try to argue.”
“...Yes. Sorry.”

After sternly vetoing Erwen’s appeal, I continued the briefing. Only when I felt that every member of our group perfectly understood the information I was conveying did I set the summoning book on top of the altar.
Rumble.
The stone gate, which had opened over a hundred times today alone, slid open once more to let two monsters through.
Fwoosh!
One was a goat-headed creature that lumbered out with a hammer in hand and a bag full of what looked like lava slung over its back.
Hellsmith.
The previous chieftain, who had been nicknamed the Flame Warrior, had this guy’s essence.
...And Bellarios.
As I stared at its smooth scales, I couldn’t help but lick my lips.
[Bellarios has cast Scales of Greed. Bellarios is now immune to all magic damage.]
Give me that.

chapters.title: Chapter 547: Ghost (5)
paragraphs: The Scales of Greed.
If you had a high enough resistance stat already, it was a powerful active skill that granted its user what amounted to magical immunity. It even had an additional effect on top of that.
[Bellarios will gain additional Physical Resistance relative to the magical damage nullified by this skill.]

The skill didn’t just stop at blocking magical damage but even raised the user’s Physical Resistance. Put simply, Bellarios was a creature whose scales grew stronger and stronger the more magic you threw at them. They truly lived up to their name.
Unfortunately for this Bellarios, however, it had encountered the wrong group of people today.
Because adventurers got stronger the greedier they got too.
That was why there was even a saying that what adventurers desired most was desire itself.
Ah, by the way, I made that up right now.
“Behel—aaah!” I charged, letting my greed drive me forward.
Essence, essence, essence, essence. Please drop an essence!

If I were to look in a mirror right now, I was sure I’d probably see a feverish glint in my eyes. It had been so long since I’d been this excited by the sight of a monster. But how could I be calm? I had suffered a ton thanks to my weakness to magic damage. Obtaining this skill would solve all those problems.
But first, this guy.
The goat-headed blacksmith got in my way.
I swung my hammer at the Hellsmith’s head.
Bang!
The blow knocked his chin to the side a bit, but the sturdy rank-three monster otherwise barely budged. Instead, it retaliated immediately.
[Hellsmith has cast Pounding. The flames deep within the earth awaken.]
The earth split and fire erupted from the cracks.

When our chieftain used it, it was more of a time-sensitive buff skill meant for stacking, but this goat seemed to be able to keep it active at all times. The skills you obtained through essences were usually less powerful than the originals used by the monsters they came from, so that was to be expected.

[The damage dealt by all Fire-type skills has significantly increased. Hellsmith’s Physique stats rise significantly in proportion to its Fire Sensitivity level. Its surroundings will constantly catch fire.]
Red and blue flames leaped up to cover its body, but the continuous damage was bearable. After all, adventurers lived and died by their equipment.
Oh, and I didn’t make that saying up, by the way.
[You have activated the Orb of Fire. All Fire-type damage within a radius of 15 yards will be reduced by 50%.]
The damage I was taking decreased significantly after Orb of Fire was activated. This effect also shielded all the melee fighters around me.
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-eight support spell Cold Blood. Your Fire Resistance has significantly increased.]
When Versyl cast Cold Blood on me on top of that, the damage decreased to the point that I could practically ignore it.
“Attack!”
Amelia unleashed her aura and Missha swung her ice-covered longsword.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Trident.]
Ainar, meanwhile, used her newly acquired skill in live combat for the first time.
Swish!

The spear lunged forward with the speed of a flying arrow, and as it did, two translucent spears appeared on either side of it. Typically, the additional spears would have flown at two adjacent enemies next to her target.
But it’s a rank-three essence, so it would be pretty sad if that was all it could do.
Although Trident was technically an Area of Effect skill, it was actually stronger when used against a single opponent.
[There are no additional enemies around the target. All attacks will land on the original target.]

Three spears struck the goat-headed monster. Since the blow didn’t register as hitting the same spot as with Repeated Slash, her other skills didn’t activate. However, that didn’t mean the attack was weak.
All damage using spears increases by 1,200%.
With just this one line of text, this attack allowed her to do more damage than her combination of rank-four and lower essences ever did.
Stab!
As the spear sank into the monster’s body and was ripped back out, the spear-sized holes it left behind began to spurt out blood.
However, that didn’t last long.
[Hellsmith has cast Patch.]
The wounded areas glowed magma-red before a silver film crept over them, sealing them. After instantly healing its injuries, Hellsmith let out a roar before casting another one of its main skills.
[Hellsmith has cast Hellfire.]
Hellfire was such a great attack skill that I’d once designed an entire build centered around it.
Bang! Boom! Fwoosh!
It was like a volcanic eruption. The bag of lava on its back suddenly exploded, gushing red liquid everywhere.
[Bellarios has cast Calamity.]
Then the raid officially began as Bellarios joined the battle. Calamity was a pretty unique skill, especially in that it applied an effect to the battle map itself.
[Field Effect – Storm is now active.]
Whenever the skill was turned on, a random field effect was activated.
Whoosh!
Powerful winds began to blow and gray clouds gathered and swirled overhead. Our field of vision dropped considerably as a result, but that was only a secondary side effect.
[The activation rate of all skills has decreased by 50%.]
The real issue was that if someone tried to use a skill in this storm, it wouldn’t work half the time.
This is a bit of a problem. We’re starting with a storm.
I was still grateful that we weren’t in Dragon’s Mountain, though. That place had a field effect of its own, which made any additional field effects that much more difficult to handle.

“Deal with the Hellsmith first!” I ordered, and the long-rangers began to fire off the attacks they prepared. The joint spells the wizards had been casting for the past few minutes were unleashed and they rained down on our target while avoiding the melee warriors.
[Bellarios has cast Dragon’s Orb. The resource usage of all characters in the area has increased by 12x.]
A divine yellow light flashed in the raging storm.
Yeah, I was waiting for this skill to come into play.
From what I can remember, it activates when the user has used up a set amount of their own resources.

Dragon’s Orb was a peculiar skill that was as unique as Calamity. It increased resource usage twelve times over, and the user replenished as much MP as the creatures around it wasted. In other words, it was an incredibly overpowered skill.
Of course, it only looked that way on the outside. This skill had a fatal flaw.
[Hellsmith has cast Patch.]
[Dragon’s Orb has increased resource usage by 12x.]
[Field Effect – Storm has caused the skill to fail.]
[Dragon’s Orb has stolen the wasted resource.]
Like Calamity, Dragon’s Orb didn’t differentiate between allies and enemies.

Since it was an interesting mechanic, I had designed a character around this skill before as well. It was a solo-carry build where I’d use Dragon’s Orb to steal all of my allies’ resources so I could super-power my attacks and do unbelievable levels of damage. Well, even then, it was only as strong as Erwen’s Fusion, so I used it for fun a few times and then abandoned it.
Anyway.
“Don’t stop!”
We ignored the storm and resource tax and continued to bombard Hellsmith.
[Field Effect – Earthquake is now active. All movement-related abilities have been sealed.]
Bellarios used the MP it had recovered to cast Calamity again, but we were still able to accomplish our initial goal regardless.
[You have killed a Hellsmith. EXP +7]
The goat, which had had its MP drained and even had its skills blocked by its own ally, died like a dog.
Shine!
Its body turned into flecks of light and disappeared, and our reward dropped.
Thud.
It was a rank-three mana stone.
I had my hopes up a bit since this is our first time killing one, but...
We didn’t end up getting an essence. That was a bit of a shame, but I didn’t linger too long on it. We still had the main course to get through.
And this is honestly better.
If Beginner’s Luck had been activated now, it only would’ve made me more nervous. Gacha required sacrifices, after all.
“One down, one more to go, huh?”
“You know what to do, right? Wizards, please only use support spells from here on out! No offensive magic!”

Once Hellsmith was dealt with, we focused all our attention on Bellarios. The wizards stopped attacking and switched to a support role, and the long-rangers let their attacks fly at the hovering dragon.
“It’s coming down!”
Whenever it swooped down from the air, our melee fighters took advantage of the opening and swung their weapons at its thick hide.
[Bellarios has cast Wandering Wave.]
[Bellarios has cast Breath of Death.]
[Bellarios has cast Shatter.]
The longer the battle dragged on, the more mangled its scales became.
[Bellarios has cast Calamity.]
[Field Effect – Drought is now active. All buffs have been removed, and all curses are now amplified.]
It had just cast its third Calamity when—
Swish!
—Erwen let an arrow fly and hit the beast dead on in the middle of its forehead, instantly ending the battle.
What was that, ten minutes?
While I was running the mental math, my eyes were laser-focused on the Bellarios as it began to fade.
[You have killed a Bellarios. EXP +7]
As its body disappeared, the flecks of light floating into the air promptly aggregated into a mana stone that fell to the ground.
Whump.
None of the adventurers paid it any mind, though.
[No. 9999: Beginner’s Luck has been activated.]
Not when an essence had dropped.
The problem was...
...It’s yellow.
It wasn’t Scales of Greed.
The yellow essence was the one with the active skill Shatter attached. It was a long-range attack that had an amplified effect when used in melee range. An unavoidable insta-hit skill.
“Ugh... That’s a shame. It’s yellow. That’s not the one you were after, right?”
“Hah... So what do we do with this essence? I feel like a lot of people are going to want it...”
While everyone was focused on the essence, Amelia came up to me, still wiping the blood off her shortsword. “Yandel, are you all right? It looked like you took a bit of a beating.”
“Ah, we’re all good. My equipment’s fine.”
She went quiet.

I’d barely been injured in my fight against Milayel, a rank-two monster and a Guardian of the Rift to boot, but I ended up getting sort of roughed up during this fight against Bellarios. Because Shatter dealt damage by firing off a wave of destruction at a set area, it was impossible to guard against it.
Shaaa.
However, since they were just minor wounds, a simple heal had me back on my feet in a second.
“As long as you’re fine. So, what are you going to do with the essence?”
“Ah, that...”
Once I was back to normal, I set to tackling our latest problem.
Why did it have to be Shatter, of all things?

The skill itself wasn’t bad. It was guaranteed to hit, instantaneous, and impossible to guard against. It dealt a pretty decent amount of damage, and the MP used and cooldown times were both low to boot.
However, it’s hard to make it any stronger than it already is.

Despite everything it had going for it, the skill had the fatal flaw of not meshing all that well with other skills. It didn’t matter how you designed your build around it—there was little room for growth.
“I’ve decided.”
As such, it didn’t take long for me to decide who would get this essence.
“Auyen Rockrobe,” I called out to our clan’s sole noncombatant, the navigator.
“You’ll take this one.”
“Why do you sound so surprised?”
“B-But... this isn’t an essence related to navigation...?”
Ah, so that was why he didn’t say anything when we discarded that rank-three essence earlier.
I smiled and patted him on the shoulder. “Even if you’re a navigator, you’re still a member of our clan. You should at least have one essence you can use to defend yourself.”

I’d been planning on giving him an essence pretty soon anyway, and since this was an essence that would perform about the same no matter who I gave it to, I figured our noncombatant Auyen would be able to use it as effectively as anyone else.
And the passive skill Circulation Loop can bring up his base stats too.
However, it seemed he still couldn’t believe it.
“Uh, um...” Auyen kept opening and closing his mouth in obvious shock. “Th-thank you. Thank you... Really... Thank you so much...”
For some reason, our navigator started to cry.
[The essence of Bellarios has sunk deep into Auyen Rockrobe’s soul.]
Huh? Why was he crying all of a sudden?

While I stood there struggling to process this turn of events, Amelia came up next to me. “If I had to guess, years of pent-up frustration finally caught up to him. From what he’s told me, it seemed he was usually ignored or taken for granted by his old clan. Most navigators are.”
...Really? I didn’t know that.
“And then, when you gave him an essence so he could protect himself, those emotions boiled over. This is probably the first time he’s ever officially been recognized as part of a group.”
Hmm, I still couldn’t fully understand where he was coming from despite the explanation. All this just because he had gone through some stuff in the past?
I lost interest and cleared my throat. “Ahem...”
“Oho! Bjorn is flustered!”
Hey, that wasn’t it.
And what’s with that smug smile Amelia’s wearing?
I didn’t want to encourage any misunderstandings, so I quickly changed the subject. “You can all take a break now!”
With that, I gave the group some time off. I’d just sat down myself when Erwen approached me.
“Mister, are you resting?”
“Yeah. What is it?”
“I’m curious about something.”
Curious about something? “Speak.”
“Why didn’t you let me do my thing in this battle? If we beat one of them at the very start, things would’ve been much easier.”
“Oh, that?”

She wasn’t wrong. If we used Erwen’s signature move, we would’ve been able to beat the two rank-three monsters much more quickly. Dicloe’s dark orbs would have quickly dealt with the Hellsmith, and Concentrated Fire would’ve killed Bellarios in one shot.
“There’s still plenty of daylight.”
“Pardon?”

But after using her ultimate, Erwen wouldn’t be able to fight for quite a while. Currently, it was only five in the afternoon. If a high-powered member of our group, Erwen, were knocked out of commission this early, the total number of monsters we’d be able to hunt today would decrease significantly.
All right, I think that’s enough of a break...

A while later, I got up and ordered everyone to circle up again, and then we got into formation and went back to summoning monsters. We ran through our usual hunting routine until eleven at night and ended the day after setting up camp.
“Eat up! We didn’t put as many vegetables in there today!”
The following day, I woke up, ate breakfast, and once again began my morning routine.
All right, the food today was pretty good.
“We have about sixty days’ worth of food for thirty-eight people.”
Our inventory looked fine.
“We found evidence of an odd stat in Ms. Fenelin’s body. It might relate to Hipramajent’s passive ability.”
And like always, the research team didn’t have any results for me yet.
Yeah, it was all business as usual this morning... Except for one thing.
“Yandel, we need to talk.”

I’d just digested breakfast when Amelia, head of night watch, called me over. She then hesitated a bit before saying, “There have been too many identical reports to write this off as someone seeing things.”
“What did they see?”
“Just to let you know, when I took a look, I couldn’t find anything.”
“Okay, so what did they see?”
Amelia glanced around and then leaned in close, her voice dropping. “Some people are saying... that they saw a ghost in the middle of the night.”
...A ghost?

chapters.title: Chapter 548: Secret Room (1)
paragraphs: On our eighty-seventh day in the labyrinth, I was going through my morning routine when Amelia came to me with an interesting piece of news.
A ghost...
She said that she wasn’t able to find anything when she checked, but since there were quite a few witnesses, we couldn’t just ignore the reports either.
Amelia told me that excluding her, every other member of the security team had seen a ghost at least once during their watch, so I called them all together for a short meeting.
“I felt a chill and turned to look in that direction, and something with white hair was looking back at me.”
Starting with Mihail Lectus, the man who had been part of the palace’s investigation department, I heard everyone’s ghostly testimonies, but surprisingly, it seemed everyone saw a different one.
“What I saw was a beast-type monster with protruding fangs...”
“Mine was a little different... It was a man who looked to be wearing rags. His eyes were completely black and he was crying tears of blood and staring daggers into me.”

“The thing I saw looked just like a slime. It was oozing on the ground like it had melted onto it, and it was slowly crawling toward me in the dark. But when I rubbed my eyes, it disappeared. I honestly thought I hallucinated it from exhaustion.”

Each of them had seen vastly different things. However, there was one similarity between all of them: the second they took their eyes off of them for even a moment, the ghosts all disappeared without a trace.
“Did this all happen yesterday?”
“No, everyone saw them on different days. Lectus alerted me after his watch last night, so I asked around and found out that everyone except me saw something similar at least once.”
I see. In that case...
As I scratched my chin in thought, I heard a grinding sound next to me.
Creak, crack, clatter!
When I turned to look, I noticed that the sound was coming from Ainar’s jaw. Barbarians tended to grind their teeth when they were afraid.
“A g-ghost... I-Isn’t this dangerous...?”

Now that I thought about it, Ainar had been terrified of stuff like this for as long as I’d known her. No, in truth, most barbarians were the same way. They felt an instinctive aversion to spirit-type monsters, and a few of them were even flat-out afraid of them like she was.
At one point, I was fascinated by this trait and asked Raven about it, and she gave me this explanation: it’s in the barbarians’ blood.

In other words, they might have had information about a natural predator impervious to physical attack encoded in their very genes. Considering barbarians relied so heavily on their instincts, she said that could be the reason the trait was seen in so many different people.
Well, that didn’t actually matter right now.
“This is fishy,” I mumbled to myself.
“Hmm? Fishy?” Ainar looked around, sniffing. “Fishy like meat...?”
Was her desire for meat stronger than her fear of ghosts?
I’d never understand her, but I decided to let it go. That wasn’t what I meant by fishy, anyway.
Meat is good too... but there were some things out there that were even tastier than meat.
And what I was smelling was one of those things.
A hidden element.
Any self-respecting Dungeon and Stone player had a gut instinct for these things, so when I heard about these ghosts, I caught a whiff of it right away.
Gulp.
The sweet, honeyed scent of a hidden element. And a strong scent at that.

In this world, hidden elements were called the Achievements of Gabrielius. As someone who had found quite a few hidden elements over the years, I immediately got to work. What I needed right now was information—a lot of information that I could consolidate into tangible data.
“...Time?”
“It was around one in the morning.”
“I was on first watch... so it was around eleven at night.”
When I asked the people who had seen the ghost, they all cited seeing it anywhere between eleven at night and three in the morning.
Was that just a coincidence?
Not a chance.
So the ghost of the library appeared between eleven and three in the morning.
“There! Over there. It was looking at me from there.”
“I saw mine above the bookshelf...”
“I saw one on the stairs leading outside.”
And the location seemed random.
Hmm, I guess it’s not so much that it’s random as it is that it has free range of the entire library.
“Mister, do you think that that ghost might be an Achievement of Gabrielius?” Erwen asked, face full of curiosity as my thorough investigation commenced. She wasn’t the only one either.
“Yeah, for now.”
The eyes of all the adventurers around us began to shine.
“An Achievement of Gabrielius!”
“It’s true!”
The members of the Armin Adventurer Group, who were pros at looking for hidden elements, and the members of the Hektz Clan all lit up excitedly.
I mean, what adventurer could restrain themself at a moment like this?

“So... if we find that ghost, we’ll be able to get the treasure? I heard that everyone who finds an achievement ends up rich.” Even Ainar, who was afraid of ghosts, let a bit of her true feelings shine through.
That wasn’t to say everyone was consumed by greed, though.
One person wasn’t. And they were the only ones to approach me and express concern.
“Yandel, I think it’d be dangerous to assume this is a positive..”
It was Amelia Rainwales, my companion through time itself.
“Dangerous?”
“Yes. I think you’re being uncharacteristically optimistic about all this.”

Ah, I could understand what she meant. In truth, it did occur to me when I first heard about this ghost that it was maybe some sort of fly on the wall sent here by someone and that we had only ended up noticing it by chance.
The village chief, for example.
After all, on the first day of our return to Library Island, we had the captain of the Silver Lion Clan use Emergency Escape on us.
Blindly treating the existence of this ghost as a good thing wasn’t in any way smart. Even if it wasn’t connected to the chief, there was no guarantee that it was at all “good” for us.
“Emily, I understand what you’re trying to say. But I’m being pretty cautious, so don’t worry about it.”
“...If you say so. Got it.”
“Yeah. Thanks for talking to me.”

My gut feeling still said that this ghost was connected to a hidden element, but I decided to heed Amelia’s warning and be a little bit more cautious. It was always best to be prepared for the worst-case scenario.
And by nightfall... I’ll know what scenario we’re dealing with.
After coming to that conclusion, I got back to business and spent the day summoning and killing monsters. We rested only as much as we needed to, but unfortunately, we didn’t get anything good today.
Just one rank-four essence that we can’t even use...
Usually, something like that would’ve been considered valuable enough to put into a magic vial, but we were now at the point where we couldn’t be satisfied with little wins like this.
Tsk.

The biggest shame was that we were lucky enough to find and kill two more Bellarios, but neither dropped an essence. Still, at our current pace, I’d definitely be able to get one before I left the basement. The higher up the shelves we got, the more books we could get our hands on.
In any case, what do I do with the last remaining essence slot?
I had two empty essence slots. One of them was reserved for the Bellarios’s essence, and since I planned to use a Hipramajent essence to replace my Orc Hero essence later on, that one didn’t count.
I took my time pondering what my last essence should be.

In truth, the last slot wouldn’t stay filled for long. I just felt that having the maximum number of essences I could help in my fight against the village chief, but it wasn’t like I could get any of my endgame essences right now. Unless another Guardian of the Rift from the eighth floor like Milayel spawned down here again, no matter what I took, it would have to be erased in a few months.
...I’ll keep it in the back of my mind when new essences drop. It’s not like I need to make a decision right away.

It would’ve been a different issue if I hadn’t obtained Wall of Aegis, but since I now had my endgame shield, facing the village chief didn’t seem nearly as worrying a prospect. I tabled that train of thought there.
Tick, tock.
The day was over, and we began to set up camp in the library as usual.
Night had come. Usually by eleven at night, everyone except our squadron’s hand-picked security team would be asleep recharging their energy, but a lot more people were awake tonight.
“An Achievement of the Great Sage...”
“Do you think it really is one?”
“Even if it isn’t, I’m curious. It could be a clue to help us get out of this place.”
The other adventurers were awake and talking like school children excited for a field trip the next day.
Hey, just go to sleep.
“Stop talking and shut your eyes! It might not show up if too many people are awake!”
I then went around telling off the ones who were still awake, and the library quickly quieted. Ah, of course, that only meant that they stopped talking. They were far from silent.
Snore!
Honk, shoo, honk.
Dozens of adventurers were snoring at various volumes.
“Everyone seems to be asleep.”
“So, what will you do now?”
“There’s only one thing to do. Look around and try to find it.”
After checking that everyone was asleep, I grabbed Amelia and Versyl and patrolled the area.

“So... we need to keep doing this until three in the morning?” Versyl asked after an hour of us walking around without finding anything. But I didn’t get the sense she was asking because she had a problem with being stuck on patrol. “How have you been these days, Mr. Yandel?”
Instead, it was just that she was getting bored of walking around in silence. Since I was thinking along the same lines, I accepted her attempt at small talk.
“What do you mean by ‘these days?’” I asked.
“Just in general. Everyone else is curious too.”
“What are they curious about?”
Versyl glanced at Amelia, who was patrolling alone a short distance away, before whispering, “So, who is it?”
“A little more context, please.”
“Jeez... you already know what I’m talking about.”
Well, that was true. I wasn’t completely clueless.
I smirked and answered, “No one.”
“What? Really? I don’t know about the others, but I thought you were dating Ms. Raines.”
“No way. We’re just comrades.”

“Heh... is that so?” Versyl said, her tone hinting that she didn’t believe me before she offered up another name. “Then what about Ms. Karlstein? I noticed that the amount of time you two spend together has increased a lot recently.”

“Not at all.” It was just that things between us were finally getting less awkward. That was why recently, the amount of time we spent talking to each other had gone up. They were mostly trivial conversations, though, like ones about how the food tasted and her insisting that I needed to eat more vegetables.
“Everyone’s been watching pretty closely, I guess. She’s the famous Lord Baron’s only ex, after all.”
Huh. After being in the labyrinth for so long, it seemed everyone was entertained by even the smallest of things.

I initially welcomed some small talk to help pass our patrol, but I didn’t want to talk about such a tense subject, so I ended things there. “Let’s quiet down. Everyone is still sleeping.” We had hard work to do tomorrow too, so we needed to let our precious fighters rest as much as they could.
A heavy silence ensued. What the...? Why isn’t she saying anything? Is she mad because I told her to shut up?
“...Mr. Yandel.”

I turned back toward Versyl to find that she was no longer right behind me and had instead stopped in her tracks a few feet away. When she spoke, she barely moved her lips, almost like a ventriloquist. “There,” she whispered. “Over there.” She was facing me head-on, her eyes just barely twitching to the side to tell me the direction. In turn, I kept my body just as still and only moved my eyes to look.
“R-Right?” she stammered. “Th-that’s the ghost night watch was talking about.”
“Hmm, I’m not really sure, but I guess it’s worth checking out.”
“...It’s pretty scary. No one mentioned it would look so terrifying.”
I couldn’t help but tilt my head at those words.
Looks terrifying...?
It seemed that Versyl and I were seeing two completely different things.
That’s interesting.
All I saw was a little mouse.

The mysterious creature that lived in the library appeared between eleven at night and three in the morning, and everyone who saw it saw something different. While it was an enigma in many ways, capturing it wasn’t particularly difficult.
[You have cast Eye of the Storm. By the authority of the transcendental body, the potential inherent in this skill is now unlocked.]
It flew straight toward me with one grab attack.
Squeak? S-Squeak!
It was so small that I could hold it in one hand without even using Giantization.
Squick! Squee! Squeak!
As the mouse squirmed in my grip, squeaking frantically, it started to turn transparent. I nearly dropped it in surprise.
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank-eight curse spell Materialization.]
However, thanks to some quick thinking from Versyl, the mouse’s body returned to normal.
“What was that sound...?” Amelia rushed over, alerted by the commotion, before frowning at the sight of me. “Yandel, what are you holding in your hand?”
“Well, what does it look like to you?”
“...It’s something that looks very soft and disgusting.”
“Really? What about you, Versyl?”
“It’s a man who’s covered in filth... He looks suspiciously like someone I know.”
“Someone you know...?”
“You wouldn’t know him.”
Hmm, I see...
S-Squeak! Squeak! Squeak!

I glanced back down at the thing in my hand. No matter how I looked at it, it was an ordinary mouse. Or, well, if I were to describe it, I’d say it looked a lot like a hamster standing on two legs. The only difference was that it was pretty big compared to an Earth hamster. This thing made a regular hamster look like a dwarf comparatively.
Squeak! Squeak! Squeeeak!
It was also kind of cute as it struggled, but I brushed the thought aside. We had things to do.
“For now, we should wake up... Oh, everyone.”
It seemed most of the group had been woken up by the noise and were now looking in my direction.
“...Is that the ghost?”
“It’s as terrifying as they said.”
“If I saw that thing in the middle of the night by myself, I would’ve had a heart attack...”
Ignoring their diverse range of reactions, I walked over to the center of the library with the mouse-slash-hamster in hand.
Tap.
I then set the mouse on top of the altar we had been putting our summoning books on.
“...I guess this isn’t it?”
Unfortunately, the altar didn’t react at all.
Squ—Squeak! Squeak! Squeeeak!
That meant I had two options left.
One: just kill it.
Two: cast distortion magic on it and kill it.
Which option should I test out?
Since we only had one ghost to work with, this was an important decision.
Squeak! Squeak! Squeeeak!
I let my thoughts wander as I began to tie the mouse to the altar like the lab rat it was.
“(Y-You wicked creature! Let me go already! Let me go!)”
But then, the mouse started to talk.

chapters.title: Chapter 549: Secret Room (2)
paragraphs: A giant hamster that spoke like a person.

Even in this fantasy world with magic and nonhuman races, this was a fantastical creature. You couldn’t just talk to monsters. There were a few rare instances where they could talk, but most of them only repeated specific lines.
“(Unhand me! Unhand me this instant! You damn traitors!)”
So then, what the hell was this thing?
My brow furrowed. This thing was talking in the ancient language. And I’d had the misfortune of meeting a “monster” who spoke in the ancient language not too long ago.
Was this a coincidence?
Doubt began to fester in my mind.
“Mr. Yandel, what is it?”
“Is there a problem?”
Huh? What was with these reactions?
Confused, I quickly asked them in return, “Can you guys not hear what this thing is saying?”
“...Pardon? Is it talking?”
“I didn’t hear anything like that. It’s just screaming rather unpleasantly.”
“Ah! That’s what I hear too!”
Huh, what was this?
I glanced back down at the hamster, which had gotten even more suspicious, and noticed that it had stopped struggling at some point and was now looking back up at me.
“(You...! Can you perhaps hear me?)”

What, was it asking if I could understand it? Something like that? I didn’t see any point in answering the question. Instead, I tightened my grip so that it couldn’t struggle even if it wanted to and initiated a conversation of my own. “(You.)”
“(Ugh...! Let me go...! You barbarian bastard... Don’t you know who I am?!)”
I did not, in fact, know who or what it was, no matter how high and mighty it acted.

“(What’s your relationship to the village chief?)” I demanded, getting right to the most important question. I decided that the first thing I needed to find out was whether this thing was an agent sent by the chief or not. However, it stared back at me like it had no idea what I was talking about, so I gave it the chief’s other name. “(Cornelius Bruingrid. What, does that name not ring a bell at all? Even though you’re both monsters who speak the ancient language?)”
If it once again pretended not to know what I was talking about, I was planning on calling in a specialist and turning this into a formal interrogation.
“(You wicked bastard! I am not a monster...!)”
“(Shut up. Just answer my question.)”
I flexed my hand to give it a warning squeeze, and the second my grip loosened, it blurted, “(I— I don’t know! I don’t know! So don’t squeeze me! I’m going to throw up...!)”
“(You don’t know? That’s unfortunate. Then I’ll have to look into it myself.)”
“(Look into it... yourself...?)”
You’ll know soon enough.
I called for Amelia, and she drew her blade and made a show of examining its razor edge for imperfections.
It seemed that the hamster saw its future flash before its eyes. “(W-Wait!)”
“(Did you already remember something?)”
“(The a-ancient language...! If we’re talking about a ‘monster’ who speaks the ancient language, I can think of one! You’re, uh, you’re talking about the one that flies around on the dragon!)”
...The one that what?
It was true that the chief’s title back when he was a person was the Dragon Knight...
“Emily, hold on a second.” I sent Amelia back before continuing our conversation in the ancient language. “(You, tell me more about this monster flying around on a dragon.)”
“(I-I don’t know much! But it came here before. It had blue skin and a huge eye on its head! It had a lot of subordinates... And it spoke! It spoke the same language I do!)”

Blue skin and one huge eye. That description did match the chief’s appearance. The odds of there being another race of monsters who looked like that and also spoke the ancient language were incredibly low.
This means that the bastard lied about something else after all.
He had told me that they couldn’t leave the island and as a result knew nothing about the outside world. But those were all just lies.
“(When did they come here?)” I demanded.
“(So long ago that it would be pointless to try to count.)”
“(I’ll decide whether it’s pointless or not. Give me a number.)”
“(I-I don’t know exactly! The sky’s opened up tens of thousands of times since those monsters last came here...)!”
The sky had opened up. That was probably the rainy season. If that was the case, I could agree with the hamster that it was pointless trying to count.
Ten thousand rainy seasons...would be about 833 years in the outside world.
But it had opened tens of thousands of times. That would mean the chief had visited this place thousands of years ago.
After running the numbers, I asked more questions. “(What did you mean by flying on a dragon?)”
“(Exactly what I said! Whenever it came here, it rode on a huge dragon and brought a bunch of buddies with it!)”
“(By whenever, are you saying it came here multiple times?)”
“(It used to come here pretty regularly, but at some point, it stopped showing up for some reason...)”
“(What did the chief do while he was here?)”
“(The same thing you’re doing! They ripped out all the books I painstakingly organized and tossed them around willy-nilly! Really, you—!)”
“(Wait, you organized the books?)”
What was this thing?

My gut was telling me it hadn’t lied to me yet, and to be honest, my suspicions that it was a spy sent by the chief were melting into pure curiosity. Now I just wanted to know more about whatever this thing was.
“(Why do you organize the books?)” I settled on asking. The most important factor in understanding people was their motivations, after all.
The answer that I received was unfortunately too vague to tell me anything conclusive. “(Th-that’s...! Because I need to!)”
“(Organizing the books... is what I need to do. That has been the case ever since I was born in this place!)”
“(So... the reason you exist is to organize the books?)”
“(I-It’s not that grand of a reason, I know... but that doesn’t change that it’s my duty.)”
