It didn’t seem to be trying to hide something from me. I asked it several more times to confirm, but its answer didn’t change.
“(...Ugh! You fool!)” it huffed. “(Do you think there needs to be a deeper reason for everything? Some things are exactly what they look like! They just are! And I just need to organize the books!)”
But why do you need to organize the books?
It sounded just as confused as I was when I kept asking it the same question, almost like this was the first time it ever had to think about it, and it eventually blew up on me.
It seems like even it can’t understand its own motivations.
I probably wouldn’t be able to get anything more out of it even if I kept harping on this, so I moved on.
“(Is there anything else here?)”
It blinked up at me, even more puzzled.
“(You know. Things like special books, treasures, or special monsters. Maybe a hidden area... If not, maybe something you want to hide from outsiders.)”
Its expression then went blank.
“(Nothing?)”
At my low, quiet question, the hamster blurted, “(N-N-No!)”
Sometimes, a strong denial was in itself a powerful confirmation.
“(As I thought... You do have something like that, don’t you?)”
I felt my mouth start to water. From there, the conversation proceeded to go in circles for a while.
“(I-I told you I don’t! What are you talking about?)”
The hamster continued to deny everything like a parrot.
“(Ah, I just want to take a look.)”
And I ignored him like any barbarian would.
“(H-How many times am I going to have to tell you? There isn’t a-anything like that here!)”
“(You know, we never said we would take it. I really just want to take a look at whatever it is. You’re starting to piss me off.)”
Really, why couldn’t this hamster just do as I said? I concluded that being nice to this hamster wouldn’t get me any closer to getting what I wanted.
“(Hey.)” I lowered my pitch ominously, and the hamster flinched before looking up at me nervously. “(Do you think we’re buddies or something? Do you not understand the situation you’re in?)”
“(...No, that’s not it. Th-there really isn’t anything... R-Really...)”
“(Ah, so tell me something else then.)”
“(Something... else...?)”
“(Yeah. for example, a way to get out of here. Do you know of one?)”
“(The chief’s weakness or a secret of his?)”
No response.
“(Then what do you want me to do? I need a reason, you know.)”
“(A reason...?)”
“(Yeah. I need to get something out of you first if I’m going to let you go or whatever. Actually, you know what? Should I just check if you drop an essence?)”
Oho. It had nothing to say to that, so it was keeping its mouth shut. Was whatever secret it was guarding really that precious?
Seeing as threats also weren’t working, I altered my approach a little. “(Hey, then at least tell me about yourself. What are you? Why are you here, and how did you learn to talk like a person?)”
“(Ah, that’s...)”
Maybe that topic was a more approachable one. It responded to my question quite agreeably, though there wasn’t much substance to its answer.
“(So to summarize, you’ve been here from the moment you were born, and you were already able to talk like a person back then as well?)”
“(Y-Yeah... That chief! That chief was the first other creature I saw.)”
“(Does the chief know about you?)”
“(He probably doesn’t. I saw that he could talk, so I tried to go up and talk to him... but that fool couldn’t understand a word I was saying.)”
“(Like the other people here who can’t understand you except for me?)”
“(By the way, what are you? How can you talk to me, and why are you not afraid of me?)”
What the... why was it acting so ballsy all of a sudden?
“(That’s my line. Are you the one asking the questions here?)”
Again, no response.
“(Whatever. Let’s deal with that first. Why are people afraid of you? Do you have some sort of ability that lets you scare them?)”

“(...I don’t know. That’s just how everyone acts around me. Even that chief guy pulled out his sword and swung it as soon as he saw me. You guys didn’t seem any different... That’s why I tried to scare you off...)”
“(But then you got caught.)”
It went quiet again.
“(Then why am I fine? To me, you just look like a tiny little hamster.)”
“(A h-hamster?! I’m not anything like a hamster!)”
“(Then what are you? Does your species have a name?)”
“(Then what about a name? Do you have a name?)”
“(...I don’t need something like a name.)”
I sighed. “(This is why hermits like you who are out of touch with society are so... Well, whatever. Names exist to make things easier for everyone. So I’ll just give you a name now.)”
“(...Give me a name?)”

“(Yeah.)” I found myself pitying this lonely creature that had lived in this library for thousands of years by itself, so I thought long and hard about what to call it. “(...Hamsick. Yeah, Hamsick. That’s your name from now on.)”
It stared at me in silence.
“(What? Do you have a problem with that?)”
“(N-No... Not really...)”
“(I am Bjorn, son of Yandel. Yandel is my surname, and Bjorn is my name. You can call me Bjorn.)”
“(Bjorn... Got it.)”
All right, then we’d officially introduced ourselves.
However, just as I was about to continue our earlier conversation, Hamsick suddenly asked a question of his own.
“(Then... are we friends now...?)”
It sounded both cautious and nervous.
As I tilted my head in question, Hamsick avoided eye contact as it mumbled, “(Well... from what I know, people who call each other by name are friends...)”
“(Where did you learn that?)”
“(I don’t know. I just knew it from the moment I was born. Like how I knew how to talk.)”
“(Really?)”
The more I talked to this creature, the more mysterious it became, but I also had a separate thought.
I think I understand how to handle this thing now.
I let the thought go and helped it back to its feet. And then, I met its eye and extended a hand. “(Hamsick, I’ll be in your care from now on.)”
It stared at my hand in confusion.
“(What, weren’t you the one who pointed out that exchanging names makes us friends? New friends usually shake hands. Ah, do you maybe not know what a handshake is?)”
“(I-I do! Why wouldn’t I?” With that, Hamsick shyly reached out a furry hand. “I-I’ll...also be i-in your care...?)”
Just how desperate for companionship was this little thing? But I’d successfully secured myself a new friend. Which meant...
“(All right, then tell me. Where is it? Where is that treasure you’re hiding?)”
It was time to start collecting my “friend tax.”
Hamsick looked up at me with eyes that screamed betrayal before scurrying back a few steps.
Hey, you’re going to make your new friend cry.
“(Hamsick, just to let you know, friends shouldn’t keep secrets from each other.)”
“(Am I not your friend?)”
“Eep...” Hamsick squeaked, troubled by my question.
I didn’t say anything else, instead choosing to wait.
“(G-Got it... I’ll show you...)” it finally conceded. “(B-But when you’re in there, don’t touch anything! Got it?)”
“(Ah, of course.)”
Hamsick seemed to have calmed down now that it had come to a decision. It twirled its index finger theatrically, almost like it was trying to show off for its new friend.
Swoosh.
All around the room, random books on the shelves began to slide out a bit, just enough that there was a noticeable difference between the books that were moved and the books that had been left alone.
Is this some sort of lock where you need to pull certain books out to reveal a hidden room?
While I stood there in a daze and watched all this unfold, the books suddenly stopped moving.
Rumble!
And then, the stone door opened to reveal a hidden area.

chapters.title: Chapter 550: Secret Room (3)
paragraphs: The stone gates opened wide.

It was different from when we used it to summon monsters. Usually, the only thing we could see beyond the gate was darkness. Our vision didn’t improve even when we approached the entryway, and some sort of mysterious force blocked us from stepping through.
Shaaa!
But this time, white light shined through the open gate, though we still weren’t able to see what was inside through the blinding rays.
“All right, follow me!”
Judging by how Hamsick was confidently leading the way, however, it seemed we could now go in.
“For some reason...I’m getting a bit nervous.”
“Can we really trust a monster like that...?”
“You’re all worried for nothing. We have the baron with us.”
Despite looking unsure and nervous, everyone trailed after me with an eager light in their eyes as I followed Hamsick.
“(I’ll go in first. See you there!)”
Hamsick walked into the light first, and I took a short moment to steel myself before quickly following it in.
Flash!
Like with a portal, the light swallowed up my body as I stepped inside.
[You have entered the First Records Archives.]
When I opened my eyes, I was in an unfamiliar place. The circular space was lined with bookshelves full of books of all colors.
“(B-Be careful! You’ll dent the ceiling!)”

The first thing to note was that the space was very small. Even though I wasn’t in Giantization mode, I needed to squat and bend my neck at an uncomfortable angle just to walk. It felt like I was inside a miniature model of a library, at least to me. A quick glance around told me there was only one other person who looked to be as uncomfortable as I was.
“Uwah! What’s this? It’s so cramped I feel like I’m going to die! And it’s full of books too!” Ainar cried out in discomfort.

Not for the first time, I found myself wondering at the way society showed such little care for barbarians. The world would be a beautiful place if the height of every ceiling could be raised by just a foot.
Despite my grousing, however, I made sure to carefully study my surroundings.
“(This is where I usually stay... You’re my first guest, so what do you think?)” Hamsick asked me.
“(It’s cool.)”
“(R-Really...?)”
“(Probably)” I said absently as I took a look around, but a cursory pass told me only one thing.
The only things here are books.
Books in bookshelves, books stacked on the ground like towers—the only distinguishing factor was their placement, but all I could see were books in this space.
However, it was too early to give up.
“(Hamsick.)”

I ignored how nervous Hamsick sounded when I called out to it and instead stepped forward and pulled a book out from underneath a pile of other books. “(What’s this book? It looks like you quickly hid it before I came in here.)”
“(Can’t— Can’t you tell? It’s just an ordinary book!)”
Wow, it was still acting like this even though we were friends now.
The book’s gilded cover immediately signaled to me that it was no ordinary book. “(Oh good, so it’s just an ordinary book. I’ll take this as a housewarming gift, then.)”
“(A h-housewarming gift? What do you take me for? The guests are supposed to give the housewarming gift to the host!)”
Tsk, it knew that? That made things a bit harder, but in the end, it didn’t end up being all that big a hurdle.
“(Hamsick, that’s the old way,)” I admonished. What could it do if I told it otherwise?
“(These days, the guests are the ones who receive the gifts... Maybe you don’t know that because you’ve been stuck in here for so long?)”
“(O-Oh! Right! Yep! I just got that tradition confused with something else!)”
“(Really! Don’t get the wrong idea! It was just a mistake!)”
No, that wasn’t the issue here. I didn’t expect that to work so well, so I had surprised even myself.
Hamsick cleared his throat when I didn’t answer. “(R-Really!)”
The obvious lie left me a little off-kilter. “(Got it, I’ll trust you,)” I said. “(Because we’re friends.)”
“(Yeah! Because we’re friends! Trust is important in a relationship between friends!)”
...Why did this hamster seem so cute all of a sudden? It was only a monster, and one I was planning to rob for all it had to boot.
I beat back any fondness I might feel for it and instead said, “(Then are you giving me this? The book?)”
“(N-Not that one! I-I’ll give you something else!)”
“(Why? Didn’t you say it’s an ordinary book?)”
Hamsick went silent, having driven itself into a corner of its own making. Was it the type to avoid conflict? It had a habit of going quiet whenever it was stumped.
“Lord Baron, there’s something written here in the ancient language. Would you mind translating it for us?”

Just as I was contemplating how to sneak this golden book out of this place, a member of the Armin Adventuring Group’s wizard trio approached me with another book in hand. I could tell at a glance that it was one of the ones from the shelves.
“(You uncivilized brutes! How dare you touch someone else’s property without their permission?)”
Only then did Hamsick look around and realize the situation it was in. To be honest, its anger was justified. Even I could tell that this was a little too much.
“Check every single thing here!”
“Ah! Sorry! I ripped the book while pulling it out.”
“Don’t worry about minor things like that. We should push the bookshelves over! There might be something hidden behind them!”

The other adventurers immediately jumped into exploring as soon as they entered and were currently turning the place upside down. I was reminded, not for the first time, that adventurers as a species were practically incarnations of destruction and greed.
“(You little—!)” Hamsick let out a wordless noise of rage, but no one in the group seemed to care.
“Um...I think the monster’s mad again.”
“What a frightening shriek...”
“Is this really all right?”

“Eh, we’ll be fine! Why are you all worried? Didn’t you see for yourselves earlier? When the baron subdued it and held it down, it was so overwhelmed by his greatness that it rushed to open the door for us!”

“Haha! No one will believe us if we tell this story when we leave this place—a presence grand enough to make a monster like that obey him? This is the kind of thing people make fun of in old legends!”
“Truly, the baron is no ordinary man...”
Ah, I supposed the past few minutes could look like that from the outside. But in reality, I was simply scamming a naive hamster who didn’t know anything about how the world worked.
It’s... better if they don’t know.
There was a reason the tales of Jumong and Bak Hyeokgeose and other such myths about old lords existed. It was because they were helpful in establishing rule over the people.
“(Hamsick, calm down.)”
“(What? Are you really telling me to calm down after seeing all this?)”
“(Isn’t cleaning things up what you were born to do anyway? Or do you actually hate cleaning?)”
“(Um... That’s not it...)”
“(Then it’s fine. Everyone’s doing their best to help you do the work you like doing, so why are you angry?)”
“(Uh, is that... Is that how that works...?)”
All right, it looked like that convinced it.
“(Could I open this?)” I asked.
“(Huh? Ah... Yeah... If you’re just opening it...)”

I also managed to extract permission from Hamsick while it was still in a daze, so I quickly threw open the golden book. Honestly, I had high expectations. This golden book looked like one of the summoning books.
What sort of monster is inside? Maybe a super-rare monster like a Mimic? Or a Guardian of the Rift like Milayel?
Hmm, maybe the way it works is that after I kill a specific monster, a reward will appear—Huh?
The first passage stopped me in my tracks.
A long long time ago, there was a brother and sister who lived happily in a rural village.
...What is this?

The story was written in the ancient language and seemed to be an entry in a child’s diary based on shaky handwriting. It didn’t take long for me to read through it all. Although the book was thick, the writing ended on the first page.
“Lord Baron, could we perhaps hear what it says?”
Everyone, not just the wizard trio, seemed to be interested in what I was reading, so I gave them a quick summary.
“Once upon a time, a brother and sister lived happily in a rural village. However, when the older brother decided to leave the village to become a wizard, the younger sister was very sad.”
“And?”
“That’s it.”
“...What?”

Well, that was all that was written here, so yeah. That was why I hadn’t even considered withholding the knowledge and simply told everyone what it said outright. The story wasn’t long enough to tell us anything, let alone long enough to decide whether it was worth hiding. I flipped to the back pages, but there wasn’t anything else written in the book.
This story probably isn’t nothing, though.

The importance of the tale I just read climbed a notch higher. Basement Floor One contained all sorts of mysteries and unknowns, and this mysterious monster I’d met, Hamsick, had been guarding this book in its hideout for thousands of years. There was no way its contents were mere nonsense.
I called everyone together for a brainstorming session. “Does anyone know who the siblings in the story are?”
“Hmm... A brother and a sister... The first thing that comes to mind is the Kailaje siblings.”
The Kailaje siblings were a famous adventuring party that had been active a few hundred years ago, so no.
“Is this perhaps related to mythology? Some time ago when I was studying theology, I read a theologian’s thesis arguing that Lord Reatlas and Lord Heindel were born from the same parents.”
But this didn’t seem like the story of a god, either.
“Well, my first thought was the Immortal King. Before he rose to the throne, he had many younger siblings.”

Well, since he had a large family, he would’ve had a younger sister, but the fact that the tale mentioned a rural village contradicted that theory. Even if Rafdonia was located at the edge of the continent, it was still said to have raked in a lot of money through trade back in the day.
“Emily, what about you? Can you think of anything?”
She took a moment to think before responding. “Rather than the siblings part, I’m more fixated on the part where the brother went off to learn magic.”
“Ah, that.”
“Is there a possibility that this is maybe a story about the Last Great Sage, Gabrielius?”
Hmm, that was also a possibility. The problem was that even if one of these guesses was right, we had no way of deducing which one.
Hmm...I guess that’s not entirely accurate, actually.
“(Hamsick, do you know who this story is about?)”
I asked just in case, but Hamsick didn’t seem to know anything either.
“(You’re saying you’ve been guarding this story for years and you don’t even know whose story it is?)” I asked accusingly, clearly warning the hamster not to lie.
Hamsick waved its hands in a show of innocence. “(I really don’t know! I just... felt like I needed to... That’s why I’ve been keeping it safe.)”
“(Hmm, really? Then I can take it, right?)”
“(But you— No! I’m supposed to give that book to someone someday!)”
“(Give it to someone...? Who?)”
“(Someone qualified to have it.)”
“(What are the qualifications?)”
“(I... don’t know that yet... but I’ll know when I see it. Rather, I have a strong feeling I’ll know.)”
The longer we spoke, the more curious I became about Hamsick. What was this thing? Who created it, and why did it have to spend so long by itself here in a place no one ever visited?
“(A-Anyway! You aren’t qualified, so don’t even dream of it! I need to hold onto this book until the time comes...!)”
“(Hamsick, friends share everything with each—)”
Squeak! “(Doesn’t matter, you still can’t take it!)”
Tsk, so that wasn’t going to work?

I set aside my interest in the golden book for now. Although I hadn’t completely given up on it, its ranking on my list of priorities had fallen after seeing that it only had one passage worth of information inside.
“Versyl! Have you found anything?”
“Anything? Come here! There are so many things I need to show you!”
Besides, the golden book wasn’t the only thing in this secret room.

Our process for investigating this secret area was quite simple. We pulled all the books off the shelves, pushed the empty bookshelves over on their sides, and then either physically hit or used magic to destroy the walls. It might seem a bit barbaric, but this was the official method used by adventurers faced with the unknown. Something was bound to show up as long as you did all this.
In fact, I also had a habit of going around breaking everything I could when I was playing the game, and that habit helped me find a lot of hidden secrets.
“(You... You oafs...!)”
Well, the one downside was that this method was bound to piss the homeowner off. In any case, thanks to the thorough investigation of my fellow adventurers, I was able to confirm one thing.
“(There isn’t anything hidden here,)” I mumbled. There wasn’t anything hidden behind the walls, below the floorboards, in the ceiling—nothing.
“(That’s what I said! There isn’t anything here!)”
Ah, but it wasn’t like I knew that earlier. “(I would’ve trusted you if you didn’t lie so much.)”
“(...When did I lie to you?)”
“(You said this room didn’t even exist at first.)”
Hamsick went quiet.
In any case, just because there was nothing hidden here didn’t mean we didn’t get anything out of this experience.
“Your Lordship! Look at this book! I think it’s a map of Basement Floor One!”
“I think this is a summoning book. There are more than ten Mimics in this book.”
“This is a fountain pen that was on the table, and we’ve detected unexplainable mana inside it. I think we should do further research...”
“This is an ordinary picture frame. It looked pretty out of place, so I did some physical damage to it, but it just broke—”
As my group started reporting the results of their investigation, I nodded with a satisfied smile.
Yeah, this was what adventuring was all about.

chapters.title: Chapter 551: Secret Room (4)
paragraphs: In summary, this was everything we found in the secret room:
A golden book containing the story of two unidentified siblings.
Well, that wasn’t much use to me right now. But the other loot we got was a different story.
Seven summoning books.

They weren’t regular old summoning books, either. Each book was one we hadn’t seen on the bookshelves outside. One had ten rare Mimics inside it, while in another, the pictures of the monsters in blue, red, and other colors instead of just black and white. Another still had pages where the art of the monsters inside was instead replaced with “???”.
Seven books, each with something peculiar about them.
And a suspicious fountain pen.
There was also the pen on Hamsick’s table.
“(Hamsick, how do you use this fountain pen?)”

“(W-Well...)” After hesitating for a long moment, Hamsick seemed to conclude that we were indeed friends and decided to be honest. “(If you use this pen to color over the pictures in the books... you can get an essence of that specific color.)”
“(What?!)”
“(D-Don’t shout! You scared me!)”
Then say it in a less surprising way.

A fountain pen that could be used to get whatever color essence I wanted? Was an item like that even allowed to exist? It was so overpowered that that was my immediate thought, but unfortunately, it did end up having limitations. It could only summon rank-threes and below, and it could only be used twice.
Yeah, there was no way something like that could be used an unlimited number of times.

I could feel the disappointment setting in, but since this was Dungeon and Stone, the emotion was tempered. I was the fool for getting my hopes up in the first place. In this game, an item like this was already amazing enough on its own.
Is this what it’s like to be the first to step foot in uncharted territory...?

I now understood why all those adventurers went nuts after hearing Basement Floor One was open. The fifth, sixth, and seventh floors... when those first opened, there must’ve been overpowered items like this one hidden there as well.
“(By the way, Hamsick,)” I began, “(how do you know how the fountain pen works? Did you use it before I came here?)”
“(No way!)”
“(Hmm, but your explanation was pretty detailed.)”
“(I just knew it! I’ve known it from the moment I was born!)”
It hadn’t used it itself, but Hamsick already knew how to use the fountain pen.
“(Why are you putting it in your pocket?!” Hamsick cried furiously as I tried to casually swipe it. “Th-that fountain pen is also something I need to give the right person...!)”
Oh, really? “(But can’t you use it twice?)”
“(How about I use it once and then you give it to that qualified person when they come?)”
“(B-But that’s ridiculous—!)”
“(Or is there a rule that says this thing needs to be given to them with all its charges?)”
“(Uh... Not that I know of...)”
“(Then there’s no problem!”)
All right, then the fountain pen problem was solved. After using it once, I could think long and hard about what to use it on next and then try to convince Hamsick to let me.
With that, I turned my attention to the last piece of loot.
“A map...” I murmured to myself.

We’d found a map of Basement Floor One, with Stone Island as the starting point in the center and a whole host of islands drawn around it. Although the fountain pen was pretty good, this map was a huge deal. This would save us a lot of time we would have otherwise spent wandering around creating a map of our own.
“Looks like there are two islands here that we haven’t been to yet.”
When I asked our navigator, Auyen, he informed me that one of them was about a week away from Library Island. The other one would take us about a month to get to.
“A month... This floor is bigger than I thought.”
“Yes...” he said, trailing off. “However, there is one thing that’s worrying me about that island... The location is in the direction we saw that rainbow that one time.”
“Then this island could be whatever was at the end of that rainbow?”
“Well...I can’t say for certain, but I don’t think it’s a coincidence.”
I was thinking along the same lines. As such, I hereby dubbed that particular island Rainbow Island.
“(Hamsick, do you know what lies beyond this map?)”
“(I don’t know!)” Hamsick snapped as it glared dejectedly at the mess we’d made of its room. It looked upset, but it didn’t seem to be lying.
Then it probably really doesn’t know...
For now, it would be wisest to assume that the map didn’t include every single thing on this floor.

My curiosity grew. What would we find if we tried to venture beyond the map’s borders? Was it even possible to go further in the first place? I found myself sympathizing with the people of the past who thought the world was flat—I could understand why they would be so interested in finding the edge of the world.
Anyway, I guess I’ll find out when we get there later...

“Mr. Yandel, look at this part,” Versyl said, pointing to a spot on the map. It was a part of Giant Island—to be precise, it was a mark right over the cave we stayed in while we were there. “Do you see this symbol on the map?”
“It... looks like it’s marking the location of the portal stone there.”
“That’s what I’m thinking as well.”
The map seemed to include a symbol for the portal stone in the cave. However, there was also a symbol below that one that was rather intuitive.
“An arrow pointing downward...”
What could that mean?
Basement Floor Two.
Everyone seemed to be thinking the same thing, but no one said it aloud.
Versyl broke the tense silence as she slid her finger to a different location on the map. “...Then shall we take a look at this one as well?”
The first person to figure out where she was pointing was Auyen. “This... is the chief’s island...”
“That’s right. There are only two portal stones drawn on the map, and one of them is here.”
As my eyes fell on the spot Versyl was pointing to, I felt my breath catch in my throat.
I couldn’t tell if this was good news or bad news.
“At least we found the exit.”

Below the portal symbol was an arrow pointing upward. We had officially found the way out of there. Well, to be more precise, we found a place we assumed might be the exit. Still, this was great news for us, considering we had been wandering around aimlessly without a clue.
It just had to be Chief Island, though...
That little fact was enough to make my throat tighten. That meant that if we were going to get out of here, we would need to face the village chief whether we wanted to or not.
“Th-then we can go back to the city?”
“We’re free! Yeaaah!”
A few of the members let out shouts of joy at the prospect of an exit, but there were, unfortunately, quite a few obstacles still standing in the way of us from using it.
“But...will it really work? That portal stone on Giant Island didn’t activate at all ...”
“That’s true. It seems we need to fulfill some sort of condition, just like when we first came down to this floor.”

As a few of our wiser members were pointing out, we weren’t in the clear just because we’d figured out where the exit portal was. We needed to figure out a way to activate the portal stone first. Getting past the chief would be another issue entirely.
“The rainbow! The island in the direction of that rainbow! Maybe that island will be the key?”
We had a few things we could try out. It wasn’t like we were sitting ducks or anything.
Rainbow Island has the highest probability of having some sort of clue, but even if there’s nothing there, we should be able to figure a few more things out as we clear the other islands.

On that note, I asked Hamsick one last question. “(Hamsick, what monsters appear on the highest bookshelves?)” In other words, how much stronger would we need to become to clear Library Island? Hamsick’s response to this question would help clarify things.
It didn’t answer using the ranks we adventurers favored, but...
“(Tol-Lapupa, Kashan, Leviathan, Plahel, Ridger...)”
I sighed. So we’d need to defeat rank-one monsters in the end after all. I supposed I should count myself lucky that we’d only have to fight one at a time.
“(What happens after we beat all of them?)”
Hamsick’s tone abruptly took a turn for the serious. “(I don’t know.)”
“(Is that maybe the ‘qualification’ you were talking about?)”
“(I’ll say it again, but I don’t know. I don’t have any knowledge of what will happen.)”
I see. So that was all I was going to get out of it, and I needed to figure out the rest myself.
“(Hamsick, what do we need to do to get out of here? Can I just walk through that portal thing?)”
We had finished investigating, and I concluded that we weren’t going to find anything else here.
However, at my question, Hamsick tilted its head. “(Huh? You can’t leave this place after entering it.)”
“(...What? Why the hell didn’t you mention that earlier—?!)”
“(Eep! I’m joking! You can leave through there!)”
Jeez, that really scared me.
As I gave a baffled laugh, Hamsick grinned in apparent amusement and let out a pleased squeak! “(Friends joke with each other!)”
I couldn’t even get mad when I saw how happy it looked.
I smirked and left the room with the rest of my group members. The wide-open stone gate kept glowing right up until Hamsick stepped out last. Then, the light disappeared and the gate closed.
“(But Hamsick,)” I asked, “(do you need to open the gate every time you want to go in?)”
“(Yeah?)”
“(It’s just, that room seems to be the place you live. Isn’t it annoying, having to open it up like that every time you want to go in?)”
“(Not really? It usually isn’t annoying at all! But then you showed up while I was organizing the books, so I wasn’t able to go back to my room at all!)”

Ah, so that was why it had been skulking around our camp—it was trying to get to its room and ended up getting caught. It probably chose to take its chances at night because that was when most of us were asleep.
“(We’re planning on taking a nap and then hunting some more, so what are you going to do now?)”
“(Watch you!)”
“(You’re not going to organize the books?)”
“(When no one is here... I’ll do it after you all leave.)”
“(Why? Oh, and I’m not trying to say you should do it now or anything. I’m just curious. You already revealed yourself to us, so can’t you just do it while we’re here?)”
“(...I’ll do it after you leave. So stop pestering me about it.)”

Well, in that case, I wasn’t going to argue with it. With our investigation of the secret room over, we returned to the library and rested for the rest of the night, then immediately began hunting again when we woke up the next day.
[You have killed a Mimic.]
[You have killed a Mimic.]
[You have killed a Mimic.]
[You have killed a Mimic.]
[You have...]

The first thing we summoned were the Mimics in the summoning book we found in the secret room. Unfortunately, even after defeating a dozen Mimics, not a single one of them dropped an essence. I was hoping to get our hands on that one so we could get an item from Treasure Vault.
Still, I’m unexpectedly at peace with this outcome.

Maybe it was because I knew that the best Treasure Vault drop was only worth about thirty million stones. I couldn’t help but feel indifferent about it. It wasn’t like this was the only summoning book we had gotten our hands on either.
I started opening up the remaining books.
“...Drake?”

The book with the entry marked “???” summoned the rank-four flying-type monster, Drake. I was honestly looking forward to this one, so that was kind of a letdown. Was the monster the book summoned completely random? Whatever the case, all it dropped was a mana stone.
“Then the last ones are the colored summoning books.”

The remaining five summoning books had monsters that were colored in. After going through all of them, I noticed a similarity between the entries. The monsters dropped essences that matched the color used to color them in—red essences from red-colored monsters and blue essences from blue-colored monsters.
The problem is that other than one rank-three, the rest are all monsters that are rank-five and below.
The rank-five and below essences were discarded without much thought, and the rank-three essence was handed off to the Armin Adventuring Group because they had a member who wanted it.
We’ve already used all of them.
We ended up going through all the summoning books we got from the secret room without much gain. Well, I still had the fountain pen, which was the main course, so to speak.
But I should hold onto this until absolutely necessary.

My first impulse was to use it right away to get the Bellarios essence, but I decided to be logical about this. Today wasn’t our last day hunting. I might end up getting the essence naturally, so using it now would be a huge waste.
[You have killed a Stone Watch.]
[You have killed a Mecharote. EXP +7]
[You have killed a Frost Guardian.]
[You have killed a Vol-Herchan.]
[You have killed a Mechanical Giant.]
[You have...]
Breakfast, then hunting.
Lunch, then hunting.
Dinner, then hunting until bedtime.
We cycled through this routine for days until we reached our ninety-ninth day in the labyrinth.
Looks like the labyrinth will be opening again tomorrow.
It was once again time for new blood to join the party.
“Vice-captain, did you hear the news?”
“Ah, right. That...” The vice-captain of the palace’s Third Magic Corps, Arua Raven, gave a bitter smile.
Basement Floor One, the Records Archives.

No matter where she went these days, that place was the only thing on people’s minds, as quite a shocking piece of news had been making its way around the city recently: Bjorn Yandel was still alive and well in there, and he had obtained two single-digit Numbered Items to boot. It was an unverifiable piece of gossip that seemed to have been spread by evil spirits.
“Vice-captain... do you think the rumors are true?”
“It doesn’t matter whether the rumors are true or not. We just need to do our jobs. I’m heading out.”
Raven dismissed her subordinate’s question, finished her meal, and returned to her office.
To her, whether or not the rumors were true wasn’t something worth losing sleep over because either way, what she wanted remained the same.
She wanted the rumors to be true. That would mean she wouldn’t have to spend so much time worrying every day.
She sighed. “But it being true would be annoying too.”

Basement Floor One was an unexplored area about which virtually nothing was known. There were most definitely plenty of secrets and mysteries to be uncovered down there. It stood to reason that Bjorn Yandel was having an epic adventure with his comrades as he worked to find them all.

She let out another sigh and lowered her head, her eyes dropping to the badge of the magic corps pinned to her chest. She had grown used to this uniform over the years, yet for some reason, today the outfit felt uncomfortable and constricting.
“Whatever, let’s just do what we need to do...”
She repeated the advice she had given her subordinate and got back to work.
“Vice-captain! We got a direct order from the palace!”

That same afternoon, she received an official order from the royal family. It was riddled with all sorts of jargon and flowery language, but after doing this job for such a long time, she was able to condense the order into three lines.
One: The palace wanted to explore Basement Floor One.
Two: They needed someone with adventuring experience.
Three: She seemed to be the perfect person for the job.
The second she reached the last sentence, Raven sprang up from her seat and hurried off to pack her bags.

chapters.title: Chapter 552: Deja Vu (1)
paragraphs: It was day 103 in the labyrinth. The number of days we had spent here had already crossed the three-digit mark, and it came time for us to stop our farming session at the library. At this point, we needed to return to Stone Island to greet the newcomers.
I hope a few good ones come down so we can aim for the books that are higher up.

At this point, whenever we used a summoning book, we had to fight against four rank-three monsters at once, and some rank-two monsters were sometimes mixed in too. So long as we had a decent match-up, I figured we would be able to defeat them, but it was impossible to continuously grind through monsters like a well-oiled machine anymore. I played my role as a tank to buy the others time during battle, but that meant I then needed to rest for a while afterward to recover my energy.
Plus we nearly had a death in the last fight...
In any case, that was why bolstering our numbers wasn’t just a choice, but a necessity.
After cleaning up our camp and preparing to leave, I felt eyes on me. I turned to see who it was, then noticed Hamsick staring at me from a ways away.

“(Are you leaving...?)” it asked, looking down as I approached. Although our first encounter wasn’t a particularly nice one, we ended up becoming friends in the end, and after a few chats during our time hunting in the library, it seemed to have grown attached to me.
“(Ah, don’t worry. We’ll be back soon. And I’m leaving the golden book here too.)”
“(But you’re taking my fountain pen...!)”
“(Haha, friends don’t sweat the small stuff like that. Okay?)” When it didn’t respond, I added, “(Either way, I’ll come back soon, so don’t worry.)”
“(Wh-who’s worried? Don’t come back at all! Things are much better without you people here! Much more quiet!)”
Haha, look at this hamster. I ignored Hamsick’s empty words like any barbarian would.
“Lord Baron, everyone is ready to leave!”
“Really? Got it.”
We were ready to head out, but for some reason, I couldn’t bring myself to move. I turned to the now-quiet hamster and said, “(Hey, Hamsick.)”

“(Clean up the books while I’m gone. And even if you’re not hungry, eat the jerky I gave you regularly. And if weird people show up, don’t let them see you, and hide behind the bookshelves until I get back—)”
“(I’m not some kid! You don’t need to say all of that, and if you’re going to leave, just leave already!)”
No, but still...
I sighed. Why was I getting so worried? Was it actually me who’d grown attached to it instead of the other way around? “(Well, then, I’m off. Hamsick...)”
“(I’ll be back soon.)”

With that, I turned my back on Hamsick and forced my legs to move, walking past the members of my group who had been watching us from a distance. They parted, shuffling aside so I could get to the front. As I stepped onto the stairs, the other adventurers fell into formation behind me as we headed out and boarded our summoned boats.
A few hours of travel later, we arrived on Stone Island.
“There aren’t any traces of any newcomers.”

We came early just in case, but as expected, there weren’t any adventurers on the island before our arrival. It had only been three days since the labyrinth first opened, and it would have been physically impossible for anyone to finish farming the third floor and come down to this one in that time.
Noticing something in my expression, Erwen asked, “What are you thinking about?”
“It’s just, I’m worried about Hamsick.”
“I’m really curious what you were seeing, Mister... No matter how I looked at it, its appearance really put me off ever approaching it...”
“What did you say it looked like to you?”
“...A wizard. It had a sunken face that looked more fearsome than a Lich’s, and it had a staff with a skull on it. It also made these horrific noises.”
Ah, that was right. I had heard as much and just let it slide back then, but now, I found myself revisiting that particular admission.
A wicked wizard holding a skull staff... Wasn’t that description a perfect blend of Corpse Collector and Fallen Scholar?
Needless to say, I didn’t say that out loud.
“Um...Lord Baron. Could I take my clan members and go to the beach?”
“The beach?”
“It’s just... Quite a few things are floating around in the ocean. We felt that maybe we could spend our free time picking some things up...”
“Do as you wish. We won’t be doing much other than waiting for a while.”

A few adventurers who were bored of waiting around got up, and a handful of the other members joined them over on the beach to pick up debris. The fact that we’d managed to pick up some equipment made from grade-three material on the boat a while back had turned into a big motivator. From that moment on, a certain sentiment started to circulate through the group.
If we got lucky, we could hit the jackpot. We might even pick up equipment used by the ancient heroes of yore themselves if fate allowed it.
Well, if we got really lucky, I guess those things could potentially happen...
To be honest, though, I was a bit skeptical. We had explored quite a bit down here, yet the most expensive thing we’d found was that grade-three armor we picked up.
I bet when Basement Floor One officially opens in the future, there will be some people whose only job is to pick through the debris.

That seemed a little too wasteful for my tastes, but I could see those types of scavengers appearing. On top of that, Stone Island also didn’t have any monsters on it. If they could manage to successfully weather the rainy season, farming on this island could become a stable source of income.
Anyway, time is still passing really slowly...

It didn’t take long for me to grow bored out of my mind of just sitting around at the starting point and doing nothing. Soon enough, I was joining the other members on the beach to pick up debris with them.
One day, two days, three days...
The 107th day came around. In other words, there were only a few hours left until the first floor would shut down.
...There’s no way nobody’s here yet. Did the palace really do something? Do they have troops stopping people from coming down?
Anxiety started to take root in my heart. I had spread so much tempting, juicy information that I’d been looking forward to more experienced and powerful adventurers coming down.
But if they still aren’t here... then something must have gone wrong up there. Tsk, will I have to clear this area without any new blood?
My stomach churned at the thought as I stared down at my watch.
Vwoong!
“Portals! The portals opened!”
But then, as if on cue, dozens of portals opened and let a stream of newcomers through.
How should I grill the newbies this time?

I didn’t have to think about it for very long. I just needed to take them around Basement Floor One under the guise of teaching them how it worked, and then after instilling in them that this place was quite dangerous, I could get them to sign their souls over to me.
But a moment later, I sighed.
And I was wondering why there was no one until the last day.
I had no choice but to accept that this plan of mine wouldn’t work as soon as I saw the newbies.
“Get in formation!”
“Formation!”
I sighed as I watched the group assume formation as soon as they arrived on Basement Floor One.
This is the worst-case scenario.

Far too many priests to be a regular clan, a squadron of wizards in uniform, and even an order of knights in shiny plate mail. Their classes could be separated into three distinct categories, but they all had one thing in common.
“Nia Rafdonia...!”
They had the mark of the palace on their chests.

After setting up their formations, the man who looked to be their commander noticed me and walked over to say hello. “It is truly an honor to meet you like this, Baron Yandel! I never could have imagined that I’d encounter you so soon, but it’s truly a relief to see you alive!”
“Who... are you?”
“Ah, it seems I haven’t introduced myself. I am a member of the First Royal Guard, Zylan Ebost.”
“Any relation to Baron Ebost?”
“He is my older brother.”

Okay, so the one silver lining was that the commander wasn’t too high status. He wasn’t even a baron, but the younger brother of one. If I managed to do a good enough job of leveraging my position of baron, I could probably manipulate this guy as I saw fit.
“Ah, and I am the deputy commander of this expedition group.”
My hope was shattered the moment those words left his mouth. “Deputy commander...?”
“Yes. Could we step back a little? The second group is going to be entering soon.”
I took a dazed step back at his request.
Vwoong!
The sky lit up once more as dozens more portals opened and dozens more adventurers entered the basement. After that, yet another round of portals opened up.
Since the portals opened three times, and sixty people came in each time...
That meant 180 people. Forget expedition group, expedition force was a far more accurate description based on sheer numbers alone.
However, the real problem lay elsewhere.
“Nia Rafdonia! All 180 members ordered by the palace have safely arrived at our destination, Commander!”
The commander received a report the minute he stepped foot on the island.

“We don’t currently detect any dangerous entities in the vicinity, and our highest priority target, Baron Bjorn Yandel, has been found. He has a total of thirty-eight members, and excluding the seven from his Anabada Clan, the remaining members seem to be from the Hektz Clan and the Armin Adventuring Group, who entered during the first and second waves!”
“I see.”

The commander approached me, his silver hair swaying behind him. His almost ghostly pale face was one I was all too familiar with. Though he had aged about twenty years since I last saw him as a young man.
“I remember seeing you at your ceremony from a distance,” said the man, “but I didn’t get a chance to converse with you.”
The commander of the First Royal Guard, and the palace’s top dog who held the title of Knight of Light.
“Nice to officially meet you, Baron Yandel. I am Jerome Saintred.”
Aka the same guy I met while active in Noark twenty years ago under the guise of an iron mask.
“Y-Yes,” I stuttered, “it is nice to meet you for the first time! Hello! I-I am Bjorn, son of Baron Yandel!”
He probably wouldn’t recognize me. Right?
On an unrelated note, there was a phenomenon called the spotlight effect, where a person assumed they were being noticed more than they actually were.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump!
So even though I was sure that he wouldn’t recognize me, my heart began to race.
“...Son of Baron Yandel? That’s a bit of a peculiar introduction.”
All right, it seemed that he hadn’t noticed anything yet.

I huffed to myself. I’d ended up blurting out whatever came to mind because I was so caught off guard. “I get that a lot,” I said, answering in the calm, nonchalant tone that characterized the barbarian people. Then I quickly got to work sorting this out.
Jerome Saintred. About twenty years ago, he had gone down to Noark to acquire the Fragment of Records Stone, forcing me to fight him.

Even setting aside the fact that I was nervous about him possibly recognizing me, this was approaching the worst-case scenario. This guy was a count, meaning my strategy of using my position of baron to bully people was now off the table.
I didn’t expect them to send such a big fish into a place with no obvious escape route yet.
No matter how I looked at it, this was out of character for the palace. I had expected them to take the back seat and be cautious like usual.
Regardless, I tried to laugh off my surprise. “Haha, in any case, it is great to encounter someone from home in a place like this! Is the city okay?”
“The city? Naturally, the city is safe under the protection of the palace...”

“That’s good! Well, we’ll be heading out now, then,” I called out casually in farewell, already walking in the opposite direction. “You guys enjoy your adventure! Stay safe! What are you all doing? Get ready to leave!”

However, he suddenly appeared right in front of me like he had teleported. This was the rank-three movement ability Light Gateway, which I had seen him use before. “Your Lordship, where are you going?”
“Oh... I’m a bit hungry...”
“Please forgive my rudeness. Your rations must be depleted. But do not worry anymore—we have plenty of supplies.”
Okay, so that’s how you’re planning to chain me to you?
I dropped the friendly act and lowered my voice. “Count Saintred, get out of my way,” I demanded, donning a frigidity that drew a line in the sand.

This guy didn’t seem to care about my obvious displeasure, though, as he continued without missing a beat. “That won’t do. You were the first adventurer to ever enter this floor, and one of our squadron’s goals is to rescue you, Your Lordship.”
“You’re acting like I requested a rescue.”
“You are that much of a precious treasure to our kingdom, Your Lordship. Please understand just how big of a loss it would be if we were to lose you.”
“So? What’s your plan?” I asked bluntly. “I am currently the leader of a clan, but you’re going to privately conscript me into your expedition group by force? On whose authority?”

Despite the hint of contempt in my voice, Saintred didn’t seem upset at all. Instead, he smiled. “Well, to start, I have no authority to forcibly conscript you into the military. There is a law that we can draft adventurers in times of disaster, of course, but that law doesn’t apply to our kingdom’s nobles—like a baron such as yourself. However...”
He pulled out a scroll from his pocket like he had expected me to argue with him from the beginning. I could tell exactly what it was the moment I saw it.
“This is a royal decree,” he said.
In other words, if I didn’t follow whatever was written on that roll of paper, I would be branded a traitor.

“Hear this, Bjorn Yandel, Baron of Rafdonia.” He opened the scroll and read its contents with solemnity and gravitas. “These are chaotic days where wicked traitors act without abandon. The light of the palace will always protect this beautiful city and its citizens without fail, but false rumors have swayed some adventurers toward the side of temptation, and it would be a great loss to our fair city for these people to disappear.”
Since the palace set the standard for etiquette, the document was quite wordy.
“As such, I as the monarch have concluded that these circumstances cannot be allowed to stand and have thus sent in my stead this expedition group...”
But if I had to summarize the whole thing in one sentence, it’d be:
“Baron Bjorn Yandel will join the First Expedition Group and will act ‘under’ Commander Jerome Saintred to chart all unexplored territory and find a way to return to the city.”
Aha, wow. This is fucked.

chapters.title: Chapter 553: Deja Vu (2)
paragraphs: A royal decree had been made. Officially, there was no way it was penned by the bedridden king, so instead, it had to have been made under the authority of the prime minister.
However, even if that was the case, I only had one option.
“...I will carry out the king’s orders.”
Unless I was willing to kill every witness here and then lie that I never received such a message, there was no way I could refuse.
“The palace will remember your loyalty, Baron Yandel.”
Jerome’s smooth smile was annoying, but I tried to look on the bright side despite the turn this situation had taken.

Joining their expedition and being ordered around by this guy? That meant that within Basement Floor One, my freedoms would be restricted and I wouldn’t be able to stop him even if he did something to put us all in danger. Plus, unlike now when I held all the power, I’d only get a certain percentage of the loot and would need to try to scrounge for whatever I could.
But we’ll be able to do whatever we need to with this much manpower.
In truth, it was like I had just gotten a cheat code.

At least for the foreseeable future, we wouldn’t have any issues on Basement Floor One born of a lack of manpower. Be it the uncleared Library Island, the mysterious Tree Island, or even Giant Island with that colossus still on it—with this many people, we could handle them all.
In other words, our chances of escaping this floor and returning to the city had increased dramatically.
“All right, then I wish to trade information first. Do you perhaps have a journal? I’ve heard that adventurers usually write in journals to record their experiences.”

I sighed. He was really going to milk me for everything I had. As this was a situation where information was more valuable than gold, this group felt more like a band of thieves than an army sent by the palace. “Before I share my information with you, I want to discuss how we’ll be handling loot.”
I wanted to hammer this part out before we went any further.
“Hmm, the loot?”
“Yeah. The royal decree says that I need to operate under your command, but there’s nothing that says we need to treat you a certain way.”
“That is definitely true. But do not worry. Our expedition group is not concerned with paltry gains. The palace itself has told us to be very generous with you, Your Lordship.”
“But I still want to make things clear before we continue.”
“Command of the adventurers currently under your command will remain with you. Also, aside from one exception, anything you obtain throughout this expedition will be yours to keep.”

My position would remain intact and they wouldn’t touch my loot. That was a spot of relief in an otherwise unfortunate situation, but sandwiched in the middle of that good news were two little words that left me uneasy. “One exception...?”

“We’re working on behalf of the palace to procure a brighter tomorrow for the nation. Essences, equipment, materials, and any special items shall be left to you. But if we encounter something that has never been seen before, we will be taking it for research purposes.”

In layman’s terms, they’d be claiming any discoveries for themselves. The second the words left his mouth, my first thought was that these people were crooks, but Jerome proved proficient at the carrot and stick method. “However, I will also let you maintain possession of anything you have found up to this point... How about it?”
I mean, that’s just a given, so I have no idea why he’s making it sound like he’s doing me a favor.
But, was it because he had a long career as a commander under his belt? Subconsciously, I felt almost relieved by the assurance. “I’ll take you up on that.”
“That’s good, then—”
I swiftly cut him off before he could try to steer this discussion toward a natural stopping point. “But one more thing.”
“I’m listening. Speak.”
“I want a share of the first discoveries as well.”
“That is impossible.”
“Even if I make an overwhelming contribution in the process of acquiring one?”
“Even so.”
Damn, then I guess that wasn’t going to work. Seeing as he was being sterner about this than I expected him to be, trying to keep arguing about it would only be a waste of time.
Well, that didn’t mean I was planning on rolling over and giving up.
“Then, give me priority for second discoveries.”
“Priority...”
“Yeah. If you’re only taking things for research purposes, don’t you only need one? And you also said that you didn’t care about the small gains.”
“Hmm... Could I discuss this with my second-in-command for a moment?”

When I nodded, Jerome went over to his deputy commander and began talking my request over with him. About five minutes later, Jerome waved a hand for a nearby wizard to deactivate their sound-dampening spell, allowing me to hear his voice again.
“If you play a significant role in the discovery of a given thing, Baron Yandel, I am willing to consider letting you have priority over those drops. How about it?”
“And who will be deciding if my contribution is significant enough?”
“Well...”

“Then let’s set a proper standard now rather than leaving it vague,” I said. “Exactly three, not counting the ones I acquire by my own power and merit. Give me priority over shared discoveries exactly three times.”
Jerome and his deputy commander exchanged a glance.
I guess this guy fills the role of Jerome’s personal advisor.
I wasn’t sure, but either way, it seemed he concluded that this wasn’t something that required a dedicated discussion.
“All right. For any discoveries that aren’t the first of their kind, we will give priority to you exactly three times, Baron Yandel,” Jerome agreed, reaching out for a handshake.
I accepted it. “I’ll be in your care until we return to the city.”
“Likewise.”
And with that, an uncomfortable alliance was formed.

Once we were done discussing the loot, the thirty-eight adventurers under the command of the Anabada Clan were integrated into the palace’s forces. Our official designation was Temporary Fourth Squadron of the First Expedition Group. Compared to the other three squads, which were made up of sixty people each, we were small in number, but it couldn’t be helped. This was the only way for me to retain any power.
Maybe that was why Jerome made no effort to redistribute his numbers and add some people to our squadron. I didn’t bother asking him to do so, either.
In any case, once our group was integrated, we began to officially share our information.
“Sir Versilus, go and review their research.”
“Certainly... It’s been a while, Lady Emblut.”
“Ah, yes... Hello...”
“Is your master well?”
“I mean... Probably...?”

“Haha, now that I think about it, I guess I should be the one sharing news like that with you instead of the other way around. Anyway, since we’ve gotten our hellos out of the way, can I have your research? I’ll make sure to read through everything before asking any questions, to make things easier on you.”
“...It’s all here.”
The highest-ranking wizard from the palace’s expedition group approached our squadron’s wizard trio and took their hard-earned research.
“All right, then let’s have a talk as well, Your Lordship. What all has happened to you in the months you’ve been here?”
I filled Jerome in on how this floor worked and described the islands we’d visited throughout our time here. The thing Jerome seemed most interested in was the rainy season.
“That is an interesting phenomenon. Monsters falling from the sky?”
“But don’t worry too much about it. There are a few places on this floor where we can take cover to avoid the worst of it.”

We had found three safe zones so far—Library Island, which Hamsick had confirmed was secure; the cave on Giant Island that the Hektz Clan had used as a hideout; and finally, the village under the control of the village chief.
“Commander.”
“Haha, you don’t have to call me by my title. Just call me by my family name.”
“Saintred... there is one more thing you should know.” I was a bit on the fence about it, but I ultimately decided to share our intel on the village chief with Jerome as well.
“You mean... the Dragon Knight Cornelius Bruingrid?”
“That’s what the creature claims to be, and we assume the same.”

I figured his identity could be something of a wild card in that I had no way of knowing how the palace’s army would react to it, but they would need to know at some point. Since the exit was on that island, we would need to get through the chief and his village to get out.

“Do you know anything about him? After spending some time with him, I have a lot of questions.” Figuring that I could maybe obtain some information from Jerome, I gave him all the details about my interactions with the village chief that I could, but unfortunately, he didn’t know anything more than I did.

“A monster who calls himself a companion of Gabrielius... quite suspicious.” Even though he wasn’t all that knowledgeable, no one could argue with the guy’s drive. “I believe that it’d be best for the expedition to head to that island first.”
“...You’re going straight for him?”

“Given how suspicious he is, yes. And since you said yourself that it’s possible to communicate with him, the wisest course of action would be to capture him and try to get information out of him through interrogation.”
Uh... That is true...
He said it like it was the most obvious thing in the world, and I found I couldn’t argue with his logic. To be fair, he wasn’t particularly wrong either.
...With a group this big, I think we’ll be fine heading over there.
Even the most foolish plan in the world could work if helmed by someone strong enough to pull it off. I knew that fact better than anyone.
But... why do I get the feeling this won’t go well?
I tried to persuade him otherwise. “Since we’re not in a rush, how about we explore the other islands first?”
“Hmm?”
“We think that the exit is on that island, but it seems we need to fulfill certain conditions if we want to open it. It wouldn’t be too late to go there after we satisfy them.”

I planned to go to the easy areas first to gauge how competent this group was before heading to Chief Island. In terms of numbers, we most likely had enough, but history had taught me that sheer military might wasn’t everything.

“I do wonder if there is truly a need to go about this in such a roundabout way, but I am not in a position to ignore your counsel when you’ve been here much longer than us. Understood. We will do as you suggest, Your Lordship.”
All right, he was actually pretty easy to convince.
“Then where do you think we should go first?” Jerome asked.
I didn’t even need to think before answering. “The library. Library Island would be best.”
After all, I hadn’t gotten EXP from those top-of-the-shelf monsters yet.

After settling on a destination, we headed to Stone Island’s beaches to summon our boats. There were a total of four vessels, with each squadron getting its own. Also, while that was happening, a personnel exchange took place.

“From what Sir Versilus said, he needs a bit more time to review all of your research. So could we have those three wizards board our boat? Ah, of course, we’ll fill the empty slots with other wizards.”
“...Sure.”
With that, the wizard trio got on a different boat, and three other wizards boarded our boat to make up for their absence.
“It’s... been a while?”
I unexpectedly came face to face with someone familiar. “Raven...? What are you doing here...?”
“What do you mean what am I doing here? I got orders from up high to join this expedition group.”
“Right... you’re a soldier.”
“But did you not notice me come in? You kept looking in my direction during your conversation earlier so I thought you recognized me.”
“I was just looking around in general.”
“Ah... I see.” Raven awkwardly twisted a lock of her hair around her finger.
I found myself baffled. There were over 180 people here, so why would she think I would recognize her in the crowd? She was so short she was almost impossible to spot.
“In any case, it’s good to see you, but get on the boat,” I said. “We’ll talk on the way there.”
Raven and the two new wizards did as I asked, and then Ainar, who had gotten on the boat before us, rushed over.
“Aruru! It’s Aruru! Aruru!”
“Ack! L-Let go! That hurts!”
“Oh, sorry!”
Once Ainar snapped out of it and let her go, Raven smoothed down her crumpled uniform with a sigh. “Ms. Fenelin... is the same as ever.”
“At least on the outside.”
“Outside...?”
“She absorbed an essence, and there was an issue... You’ll see for yourself later.”
“Really?”
As we were talking, I received word from Auyen that the commander’s boat had given us the signal to set out, so we hoisted anchor and cast off.
Splash!

With that, the boat of the Anabada clan began its voyage at the front of the fleet with the three other vessels following behind us. Although our boat wasn’t that bad, I couldn’t help but compare it to the other three. Perhaps it was just the size difference? Even though they had sixty people each on their boats, their decks didn’t look crowded at all.
“We meet again.”
“Yes. Hello, Ms. Raines.”
Once Raven was on board, the other members of my clan who knew her approached her to say hi. Things with Amelia were, of course, all business.
“It’s been a while...”
“Ah, yes. It has...”
On the other hand, there was a lot of awkward silence with Erwen.
Well, at least she wasn’t as bad as Missha.
“Hello...”
“Ah, yes... Hello, Ms. Missha...”
I sighed inwardly. The very sight of them frustrated me. They had seemed so close in the past.
“I heard the news from Mr. Yandel... but this is my first time seeing you since you got back, right?” Raven asked politely.
“Yeah... Sorry about that... About me just... disappearing without a word...”
“N-No...! You must’ve had your reasons, Ms. Missha.”
They hadn’t even argued like she had with Erwen back when the team disbanded, so I couldn’t understand why they were being so awkward.
Actually, I guess that’s exactly why it’s even more awkward.
Hmm, that might be it. Raven still didn’t even know where Missha had been the past two years, and this atmosphere wasn’t exactly ripe for that particular conversation.
“In any case, it’s a relief to see that you’re all all right. I was a little worried when you lost contact after coming down to Basement Floor One.”
“Only a little worried?” I said jokingly. “That’s a bit depressing.”

“...What are you even saying?” Raven asked, aggrieved. She usually just ignored my attempts at teasing her entirely and carried on with the conversation. But judging by her tone of voice right now, she must have been feeling a little stressed today. “More importantly, did you know?”
“Know what?”
“Sir Kaislan. The one you went on an expedition with all those months ago.”
“Kaislan? What about him? Did he cause a stir out in the city or something?”
“No. He’s in this expedition group as well. Looks like you didn’t notice him either.”
Oh... That was a completely unexpected piece of news. I never thought there’d be another friendly face around.
Kaislan is trustworthy.
Plus, considering his status, he would have some sort of leadership role. He’d more than likely keep me apprised of what the expedition group was scheming.
“What about Lilith Marrone? Isn’t she a military wizard as well?”
“I didn’t see her. Oh, but there’s someone else here!”
“Who?”
As I expressed my curiosity, Raven got to enjoy her favorite pastime—explaining things. “Sir Sven Parav. The paladin of Reatlas Church.”
Heh, I never expected him of all people to be here either.
“What’s wrong?” she asked. “Do you perhaps not remember him? You were in the same squad at some point.”
“No... I do. I remember him.”

Paladin Sven Parav. The goblin mask by another name. His most notable trait was that he had an unbelievably accurate sixth sense. During our Ice Rock adventure, he’d showcased his uncanny intuition multiple times. He’d even managed to avoid the Berzak incident entirely because he had a bad gut feeling and came up with an excuse to skip the labyrinth that month.
“Raven, have you heard any news about him from the rest of your squad? Like rumors that he tried to refuse the summons, or got a stomachache on the day you were all getting ready to come down here?”
I was only asking just in case, but Raven did a double take.
“Huh? How did you know that he got a stomachache?”
...Wait, for real?
I suddenly had a very bad feeling about this.

chapters.title: Chapter 554: Deja Vu (3)
paragraphs: “...Tell me more. What happened?” Before jumping to any conclusions, I asked for the full story.

“Oh, that?” Raven asked absently. “He disappeared on the day we were supposed to set out, so the commander personally went looking for him. When they found him, he came up with an excuse about having a stomachache or something to say that he couldn’t go. He whined so much that they ended up calling a wizard to check him over.”
“To what...?”

“I heard that they used magic to check his stomach, but they couldn’t find anything wrong with him. So based on that evidence, they threatened to punish him for attempted desertion, and he ended up joining us like he was meant to...”
“...And then?”
“Well, news of what happened spread, and the people in the expedition group don’t see him in a good light. From what I can tell, most of his fellow church members don’t even treat him like a person.”
“I see...” I trailed off, sighing. I shouldn’t have asked. If he tried that hard not to join the expedition, that could only mean his sixth sense had been triggered somehow.
Ba-dump!
But I wouldn’t have to go through hell again like I did in Ice Rock, right?

After setting sail from Stone Island, our four boats soon arrived on Library Island, and after establishing some basic formations, we immediately went down the stairs. Squad Four was at the head of this formation, meaning the thirty-eight of us were the ones standing on the front lines.
Maybe that was why I felt a little uneasy about all this. Still, I quickly shook my head to shake the thought nagging at me.
...The only reason they’re putting us at the front is because we were the first ones here.
Yeah, yeah. We weren’t being used as cannon fodder. I would’ve done the same thing if I were the strategist... But why did my back feel so prickly?
...Damn those palace nuts.
Between Berzak and Ice Rock, I had already been stabbed in the back by the palace twice, so I really couldn’t trust the bastards.
“We’ve arrived.”
Since I was more wary of my back than my front, we ended up arriving at the underground library before I even realized it. A glance around showed that the books had been cleaned up since last time.
“(...You’re here? You’re earlier than I... Huh...?)” Hamsick had come out to greet us, but it tilted its head when it noticed the expedition group behind me.
I sighed. Why was this guy out here?

I quickly shooed it away with my hand to tell it to go hide, but Hamsick still didn’t seem to understand what I meant. To help it out, I pointed to the expedition group with my thumb and pointed to Hamsick with my finger before slowly drawing a line across my neck.
These people weren’t as nice as I was. They would, without exaggeration, fire off spells at Hamsick as soon as they saw it and kill it before asking any questions.
My message seemed to have been received. “(Eep!)” Once Hamsick realized what I meant, it scurried away with a squeak.

“Your Lordship,” someone called out immediately after, “Is something wrong? I thought I heard a horrifying shriek from somewhere nearby.” The people from the main expedition group finally closed the distance between themselves and Squad Four.
Nice, it seemed they didn’t spot Hamsick. “It’s nothing.”
“Pardon?”
“I don’t know why, but you sometimes hear sounds like that when you’re here.”
“Ah, I see. Understood, I will relay that to the rest of our party.”

With that established, the expedition group shouldn’t find it suspicious if they heard noises when I met up with Hamsick in secret to talk to it. Well, if someone decided to, they could always investigate where the sound was coming from, so I would need to be careful.
“So this is the place you were talking about, Baron Yandel,” Jerome commented.
“What do you think?” I asked, not giving anything away.
“What do I think? What I think doesn’t matter. Let’s not waste any time and get to work. We are not just here on an adventure. The palace has bequeathed a sacred duty to us.”
Wow, look at this palace nut over here.

Jerome then doled out orders to the deputy commander, who proceeded to shout out a command to the rest of the group. “Attention! We will now start by surveying the area. Squads, fan out and search the entire room!”
And with that, they started with recon.

I approached Jerome. “You said yourself that we don’t have any time to waste, so is there any point in you searching the area again? We already did during our last few visits.” Even as I said that I had the thought that just as I didn’t trust the palace, Jerome might not trust me.

“Oho, our expedition group is exclusively made up of exploration experts handpicked by the palace. I am not questioning your skill as an adventurer, Baron Yandel. However, please sit back and observe. We may find something new.”
Reading between the lines, though, he was definitely looking down on us.
What exploration experts?
All I could see was a combat squadron made up of mostly knights and priests along with some wizards who were also part of the military. “Do as you wish, but we’ll stay here, then,” I said dryly.
“Sure. It’s unlikely you’d find anything new that you didn’t find before, anyway.”
...Can I smack him? At least once?
The thought seriously crossed my mind, but I managed to hold back with superhuman self-control.
“...We haven’t found anything of note.”
“Nothing here either.”
In the end, the ‘explorers’ returned with nothing, and only then did we begin the process of clearing the library.
“I think we should proceed with your initial recommendation. Unlike you, we have the capacity to get through even the top bookshelves.”
Even though every word out of his mouth was annoying, he proved incredibly proficient once we entered combat.
“So that’s how it works.”

After using the summoning books a few times, he quickly restructured our formations, effectively allocating all two hundred or so members of our battalion in the most efficient way possible. A few dozen people stayed near the bookshelves to carry books over to us, and twice as many people stood at the stone gate on standby to hunt the monsters that came through.
“This will take too long.” Jerome, however, felt that even this was too slow and pulled out one of his trump cards. “Ebost. Increase the pace.”
Necessity was the mother of invention, after all.
The aforementioned Ebost was openly shocked. “Pardon? We can only use one book at a time, so increasing our current pace is—”
“So find a different method.”
Zylan Ebost, befitting his station as deputy commander, quickly recovered his wits despite his boss’s nonsensical order and came up with a clever workaround.
“If we can decrease the time the door takes to open and close, we could increase our pace even further.”
“So?”
“How about we destroy the stone gate?”

This was a suggestion that made even the barbarian standing next to them jolt upright in surprise. However, Jerome seemed satisfied with the plan and gave Ebost a nod. “The idea holds some promise. Execute it immediately.”
The second the order left his mouth, the expedition group’s magical troops gathered up, and the dozens of wizards began to cast a mass spell.
“Mairti Esta Pioryuiev du Teila!”
The spell I heard them cast was one I had never heard before.
After all, where would I have gotten to see a rank-one attack spell being cast in person?
[Gahuin Versilus has cast the rank-one attack spell Orb of the New World.]

As soon as the spell was completed, the magic circle below them began to glow with blinding light. The surrounding mana grew so dense that even barbarian warriors like me, who were desensitized to most magics, could sense it.
As for the attack itself, it was impossible to see with my naked eye. There was a flash of light as something shot forward, and then the sound of an impact.
Fwoosh!
A blast of wind slapped my face, so hot that I thought it might scald me. However, I barely registered the sensation.
“...Fortunately, it worked.”
The huge stone gate, which was nearly five stories tall, had been obliterated without a trace, leaving only an endless void behind in its place.
That... worked...?
I felt like I had reached some form of enlightenment.
Anyway, with the stone gate successfully destroyed, the time the summoning process took was likewise cut down to a fraction of what it once was.
“Without the door, we can kill them as soon as they are summoned. Good work, Ebost.”
“I was only following the royal family’s will. There is no need to praise me, Commander.”
The two who had eliminated our wait time through sheer brute force picked up their conversation where they left off like this was the most natural thing in the world.
In the end, I had no choice but to step forward. “Wait, look over there! It’s already starting to reform.”

This was the nature of the labyrinth. Just like the Crystal Cave on the first floor, every section of the labyrinth save for a few select areas returned to their original states after a while. In other words, the wizards of the expedition group had just performed a rank-one waste of time.

“Is that a problem?” However, Jerome’s expression suggested that he didn’t understand what I was getting at, so I kindly explained my thought process in a way that was out of character for a barbarian. However, my explanation also proved to be a waste of time. “Well, despite all that, I still don’t see the problem. If it reforms, don’t we simply need to break it again?”
“Judging by the rate of its regeneration, I don’t think we’ll need to use another rank-one spell next time. And since we have plenty of wizards, they can take turns keeping the gate broken.”
“We’re currently fighting monsters who aren’t strong enough to force our wizards into battle, correct?”
Uh... that was true.
“Then did that answer all your questions?”
“Yeah. I’m good.”
In the end, I had no choice but to face the facts.
The problem here... was me...!

Just as a person with more power could inevitably accomplish more things, a person at the top of the food chain could look down and see more options. The reason I hadn’t been able to think this method up myself and thought it was a waste of energy was that I lacked the power needed to pull it off. This was a strength that came straight from the mind.
That’s why there is power in the power of imagination.
People thousands of years ago must have already figured that out long before I did, because that bit of wisdom had been around since ancient times.
“Then we shall resume our mission!”

In any case, oblivious to the revelation I was currently having, Jerome didn’t waste a single second and continued to farm. Perhaps this was to be expected from someone who got their orders straight from the palace itself, but thanks to his single-mindedness, our speed was unbelievable. If I thought we were moving like an assembly line before, our new rate was something else entirely.
“Ignore the mana stones! We’ll pick them up later.”

The expedition group didn’t pick up any mana stones nor did they debate who an essence would belong to whenever one dropped. Since most of them were long-rangers, no one accidentally picked up an essence, and when melee warriors were needed, those who already had their essence slots filled stepped forward to form the front line.
We’re at the rank-fours after just one day...

To be more precise, we had gotten to the point where we were seeing one or two rank-four monsters per book not even sixteen hours after our arrival. This was nearly five times faster than when the thirty-eight of us had been farming alone.
“We can proceed at a normal pace from tomorrow onward. And tell the wizards that they don’t need to stop the gate from regenerating anymore.”
“You mean...”
“We’ll stop here. Prepare for camp.”
