We had even taken our meals on rotation to keep the hunt going, but eventually, Jerome called things off and gave us the okay to take a long rest.

Despite the long day, the expedition members made camp with practiced ease, and as soon as our downtime began, a familiar face came over to greet me. “Haha, are you busy?” asked Melend Kaislan, the knight I had worked with during the Ice Rock expedition.
“Even if I was, I would make time for you.”

“That’s an honor to hear.” Kaislan grinned as he pushed out his fist, and I bumped it with my own in greeting. We had given each other nods of recognition whenever we happened to see each other in passing, but we hadn’t gotten a chance to talk like this in a long while.
“I didn’t expect it to take this long for us to find the time to talk.”
“I’d heard people say before that working under Count Saintred is hell... But I didn’t know it would be this bad.”
Now that I thought about it, it seemed Jerome was pretty notorious among his fellow soldiers.
“So, what happened to you?” I asked. “Did the palace order you to join?”

“That’s right. Heh heh, it seems they want to milk me for all I’m worth before my discharge. Well, since one of the goals of this mission was to save you, Your Lordship, I wasn’t too fussed about it.”
“Discharge? Did you put in a request?”
“I turned in my resignation over a month ago. It takes quite a while for these things to get processed... but I’m hoping it’ll be done by the time this expedition is over.”
“I see...”
“What’s with that look on your face?”

“It’s nothing. I’m just trying to figure out what I want to eat for supper.” I evaded the question, covering the concern that lanced through me the second he told me his story. It was just that hearing that Kaislan had been ordered to come here right before getting discharged reminded me of Ice Rock.
Marrone would’ve been put in this expedition group too if there was something else going on... but I should still keep an eye out.
Rather than dismissing everything as a mere coincidence, I needed to keep the worst-case scenarios front of mind.
“Sir Kaislan! We finally meet!”
After that, Versyl, Erwen, and Amelia came over to say hi to Kaislan too. Then, a new face appeared.
“My apologies. This is the archbishop’s first time camping, so I had to help out... I wanted to come over right away but ended up being late.”
It was Goblin, aka Sven Parav.
As soon as he reached us, Versyl marched over to him with a glare. “You’re here.”
“I-It’s been a while, Ms. Gowland...”
“Yes. It certainly has been a ‘while,’ Sir Parav.”
In reality, they saw each other at the Round Table not too long ago. As someone who knew their identities, it was cute watching them put on their little act.
“Could everyone step aside for a second?” I asked.
“Yes, of course. I also can’t stay long since the church—”
“Except you, Parav.”
“...Pardon?”
Once we were done saying hello and catching up a bit, I shooed everyone away and had a one-on-one talk with Parav. “So...” he began nervously. “Is there something...?”
“You didn’t want to join the expedition group so you faked a stomachache, right?”
“Did you hear that from Sir Kaislan?”
“No, I heard it from someone else.”
“...So, you heard it from the Golden Sorcerer.” He seemed to have reached that conclusion after remembering that Raven had gotten on my boat.
But I didn’t care about any of that.
“Why did you do it? Did you have a ‘weird feeling’ again?”
“Well... it was a little different this time...”
“Different? Explain in detail. I trust your instincts.”
“I... I don’t know how to put this...” Parav hesitated, then admitted in a quiet, miserable voice, “I think... that I received a revelation...”
What...?

In this world, gods existed. The people here sometimes heard the voices of the gods or received prophecies or messages from them. They were even sometimes given holy relics to help carry out these so-called prophecies.
But that wasn’t the point here.
I couldn’t help but blurt, “You received a revelation...?”
“P-Please keep your voice down! Someone will hear you!”
A revelation wasn’t something just anyone could get. That was why those who were blessed enough to hear the voices of the gods were called saints back in the city.
But this bastard’s a player.

Sven Parav was an evil spirit from Earth, and the Three Gods’ respective churches were as serious about hunting down evil spirits as the palace was. And yet, this guy had ended up getting a message straight from the head of those three gods even though he was an evil spirit.
“...Are you sure? That you received... that.”
“I-I think so, at least for now.”
I paused, unsure. What the hell were these gods thinking?
Then again, I myself had once received a sacred relic to help me out after I was nearly killed by the Dragon Slayer...
“So, what was the revelation? What did you hear to make you go to such lengths?”
I rushed to ask what exactly this revelation entailed, but an interruption unfortunately cut our conversation short.
“Sir Parav! The archbishop is looking for you! Come quickly!”

“Ah, oh...?” In his indecision, he glanced over at me to gauge my reaction, but when I gave him a nod, he quickly answered, “Ah, yes! Understood!” With that, he rushed back over to where the rest of the church members had set up camp.
...I can hear the rest later.
It was a shame I couldn’t hear what he had to say right then and there, but I chewed on some jerky until I was full, shut my eyes, and prepared myself for tomorrow.
I can’t sleep.

When I got up to drink some water in the middle of the night, I sensed eyes on me. I whipped my head around to look, ignoring the people on night watch, and spotted Hamsick hiding in the distance behind a bookshelf.
“Ahem...”
“Your Lordship, where are you going?”
“I can’t sleep. I need to work off some energy, but it’ll wake people up if I do it here.”
“Ah, sure...”
I gave a vague excuse to the soldiers on watch and approached the bookshelf. The second I was within earshot, Hamsick whisper-shouted, “(Who... Who are those deranged humans?!)”
“(Uh... They’re people from the kingdom... But they won’t hurt you, so don’t—)”

“(Won’t hurt me...?)” Staring out at the still slightly broken stone gate, Hamsick clenched its furry fists. Its voice grew sorrowful. “(Not just once... Why do I have to experience something like this a second time...? Why are all humans like this...?)”
There was nothing I could say to that.
“(I’m a barbarian, though...?)”
Nothing, except that.

chapters.title: Chapter 555: Deja Vu (4)
paragraphs: It was our 109th day in the labyrinth. To put it another way, it had been two days since we linked up with the expedition group sent by the palace and entered the library.
Tarantantara! Tararan! Tarantatara!
A morning bugle call from the military band marked the break of dawn.
Hah, why do armies always do things like this...? If I told Baekho, he’d probably be pissed.
Well, we were all working toward the same goal, so whatever.
In any case, the trumpets woke us up and didn’t give us an opportunity to roll over and stay asleep. As soon as the noise stopped, our day began.
“Distributing rations!”
As soon as the camp was packed up, the soldiers in charge of the kitchen started to hand out the breakfast they had prepared earlier in the morning. We then only had thirty minutes to finish eating.
“There is a morning meeting that the leaders of the squads will have to attend.”

There was a meeting to brief the leadership team on our plans for today and discuss our course of action. I thought someone might say something interesting and kept an ear out, but there was nothing like that.
So we’re just going to hunt like we did yesterday.

Of course, there were slight differences. Yesterday, we destroyed the gate and stopped it from regenerating to summon monsters at breakneck speeds, but as the monsters’ ranks increased, we decided to hunt the usual way instead. Naturally, the wizards would be joining the battle now.
“All right, then let us have another great day of work in pursuit of our mission!”

I questioned whether there was even a need to gather us like this to hold this meeting, but stuff like this was probably what the military was built on. Sticking to protocol could be inefficient in some situations, but having an established custom like this could help us avoid issues and mistakes down the line.
“Take your positions!”
After that, the squads took up their assigned posts and we began clearing the library once more.
“Looks like we’re going to alternate which groups are in active combat.”
“That’s the most efficient way.”
We had over two hundred people here, so having every single person join the battle would be overkill. Thus, Jerome decided on a squad rotation.
“Stop! Squad One and Squad Two will now switch with Squad Three and Temporary Squad Four!”

When the time came, Squad One and Squad Two moved away from where they had been stationed in front of the stone gate, and Squad Three and Squad Four stopped ferrying the books from the bookshelves to take their place. From there, Squad One and Squad Two walked over to carry the books in our stead and recover their stamina and resources.
I guess I won’t get to fight with Kaislan and Parav today either.

Those two were part of Squad One, which meant we also had our meals at different times as well. The fact that Raven was in Squad Three was a silver lining, but since she was a wizard, she stood at the very back of the pack, so I couldn’t really interact with her during the day either.
...In the end, I guess I’ll only be able to ask about the revelation tonight.
Our squads meshed together like cogs in a machine. As we worked, I noticed one of us getting pretty chummy with the knights from the expedition group.
“Hahaha! Do not lie! How could a mere wizard defeat a warrior like us?”
“That’s why it was so humiliating! Who would’ve thought that one of us would lose to a wizard in a duel?”
“So when did this happen?”
“A month ago! But I guess you wouldn’t have heard about it since you were in here, Wild Sword. It was the subject of quite a bit of gossip in high society.”
How the hell did she get so buddy-buddy with them? I was still amazed by how easily she made friends. But to be honest, this habit of hers was to my benefit.
I approached them quietly, then interrupted so I could join the conversation. “What’s so funny?”
“Oh! Lord B-Baron! Sorry, I’ll focus on the mission—”
“I’m not telling you off.”
“I’m sorry...?”
“We are all warriors here. I’m curious too. A warrior losing to a wizard? Who’s the dunce who lost like that?”

The knight’s eyes darted around for a second before he grinned and excitedly launched into his story. The other knights who were a part of Squad Three, perhaps noticing our amusement, also approached us to listen in, occasionally offering their two cents and correcting the storyteller at certain points.
I mean, working the factory line wouldn’t be fun for these guys either.
Once I showed that I could be casual with them, even those who had a hard time talking to me because of my baron status began to feel a kinship with me, and some even asked me personal questions.
“So... Lord Baron, there is something I’ve been wanting to ask...”
“Go on.”
“I heard that you challenged Baron Kypriot to a duel during your ennoblement ceremony. Could I ask what happened with that?”
“Oh, that? Nothing really happened. I heard that goblin-like guy chattering away behind my back. I wanted to punch him, but since I couldn’t do that, I challenged him instead.”
“Haha... is that true? Baron Kypriot must’ve been terrified when you called him out.”
“He deserved it. There are too many nobles who don’t know how the world works. They need to learn that when you screw around without thinking, you get hit with the consequences.”
This was a joke only I could make since I was also a noble. But the knights seemed to agree with me as they all nodded.
“Well... there’s no way we could ever do something like that to them.”
“There are too many people out there who don’t realize that people like us are the ones keeping them all safe...”

Still, they maintained their mask of knightliness and didn’t say anything too outrageous. However, as I continued to freely speak my mind and share my opinions with them, I could see a few people vicariously enjoying my story.
All right, I think this should be enough to gain their favor.
I continued to tell stories throughout our hunt and grew closer to the knights of the expedition group.
“Lord Baron... you are even greater than the rumors suggest! Ah, not to say the rumors don’t do you justice! But I never knew that you were this easygoing and funny...”
I laughed off his nerves. “Haha! What are you scrambling to make excuses for? Don’t worry, we’re already friends!”
“F-Friends! Haha, don’t say that! The commander will be pissed if he hears about this!”
“Then we can be comrades.”
“Comrades... Yes, if we’re comrades...”
“Then in times of danger, I’ll leave my back to you.”
“...Please put your trust in us, Lord Baron!”
Making friends was always useful.

When night finally fell after a long day of fighting and chatting with the knights, I left setting up camp with my clan members and headed over to Squad One’s camp to find Sven Parav. After asking for permission from the clergy members there, I pulled him aside.
“We didn’t finish our talk yesterday.”
“Oh... Ah, about that...”
“The revelation you received. What was it about?”

He flinched at the word “revelation” and immediately looked around to see if anyone else was within earshot. After confirming that no one seemed to have heard me say it, he let out a big sigh. He then lowered his voice and offered a disclaimer. “I... First of all, I want to warn you that I may be mistaken...”
“You said you were sure of it yesterday.”
“If I answered with yes or no, I could see why you might think that way... but there’s a difference between me saying I believe something and another person believing it... so in that sense...”
Wow, this was getting frustrating. “I got it. I’ll judge what I hear for myself, so you just give me the details.”
“If you say so...” After that, he closed his eyes for a while as if to gather his thoughts before slowly opening them. “When I was in the city, I had a dream.”
“A dream?”
“It’s difficult to say what it was... but I heard a very holy voice. And suddenly, I instinctively knew that the voice... was hers.”
“By ‘her,’ you mean Reatlas?”
“Yes... that’s right.”
A goddess had visited him in his sleep. I wondered for a moment why this guy thought something like a dream could be a revelation, but I decided to hear him out first. “So, what did she say?”
“She said there was something I needed to do and showed me a snippet of my future.”
A prophetic vision. That was the most common form of revelation that saints received, and Parav was claiming he got one that day.
“There was a scene where the archbishop was telling me to join the expedition group.”
That prophetic vision had come to pass the next day, and thanks to that, he was sure that what he’d seen wasn’t a simple dream but a prophecy.
“And then?”
“That’s... all.”
“What?”
“She said that she would appear once more when it was time and for me to be ready for her.”
Put simply, his main quest would only be given to him after he joined the expedition and entered the labyrinth.
To be honest, though, this still didn’t make sense to me. “...Then why did you act like you had a stomachache and try to escape your duty? Even after getting that message from the goddess?”
“Uh, so, about that...” He trailed off before squeezing his eyes shut and blurting, “A revelation—! It’s obvious that whatever is going to happen will be dangerous!”
“...What?”
I got whiplash from his sudden change in tone, but the guy continued to pour his heart out. “Even if it isn’t dangerous, it’ll be something troublesome. Th-that’s what my gut feeling said.”
Hah, what was with this guy? So that was the reason he hid the fact that he received a revelation. The moment other people found out, the clergy would bully him into fulfilling the prophecy.
A paladin trying to dodge his responsibilities over something like that?
Every word coming out of his mouth was unbelievable, but in another sense, I was grateful for each one. He had told me truthfully what he had hidden from everyone else.
In terms of loyalty... he’s passed the test.

“So... can I go now? They’re looking right at me,” he said, glancing at the group of clergy to the side. While they were in fact staring at us, I could sense that rather than glaring at him, they were looking at him with worry—the same way someone might keep an eye on a child standing precariously close to a lake.
So he’s treated like this even in the church...
“Got it. Tell me immediately the second you have another dream like that.”
“Got it.”
“Have a good night.”
“Yes. You too, Your Lordship.”
After finishing my conversation with Parav, I returned to my camp to get some shut-eye. However, sleep didn’t come easily today either.
A revelation...
The information he gave me wasn’t anything special. However, just like how Parav threw that tantrum to try to avoid entering the labyrinth, I too couldn’t escape a powerful sense of foreboding.
Something huge was coming. And if so, there was only one thing I could do.
Whether whatever was on the horizon was a tsunami or a hurricane, I needed to prepare for the worst to avoid getting swept away.
I honestly wanted to save it as long as possible before using it...
But in this situation, it couldn’t be helped. With that, I came to a decision while under my blankets that night.
The essence of Bellarios.
I needed to get my hands on one as soon as possible.
By our 111th day in the labyrinth, we had progressed quite far into the library and were now fighting mostly rank-three monsters.
It only took us five days to get here.

Once more, I was struck by just how powerful the palace was. Knights, wizards, priests—they were able to pick and choose the best of the best of those precious classes and create the perfect army. Their capability was off the charts.
If I had known they were this strong, we could’ve gone straight to the chief’s island.

I hesitated because I didn’t know how powerful of a group this was, but in hindsight, we should’ve gone to Chief Island and killed the village chief first. Even if he possessed the same essences he had while he was human, none of that would mean anything in the face of military might like this.
“Lord Baron! There’s a book with Bellarios inside!”

I was in the middle of eating lunch, my mind wandering, when a piece of good news reached my ears. The person who had relayed the message was one of the knights from Squad Three, whom I had asked to notify me if a Bellarios was discovered.
“Is it in that book you’re holding right now?”
“Yes! I brought it straight here as soon as I found it!”
“Thanks.”
“It’s nothing. We’re comrades, after all!”
This was my reward for having gained their favor.
I showed the greatest respect a barbarian could bestow to a knight as I handed him a handful of jerky.
Changing the color of the fountain pen to green, I quickly opened the book and scribbled over the picture of Bellarios before going off to find Commander Jerome Saintred.
“Hmm, you want to fight this one with only Squad Four?”
“It’s an essence we need. You said that anything we acquire ourselves would be ours, right?”
“That is true. But is this really necessary? We’re short on time, so fight it with the other squads. Ah, of course, you can have the essence either way. If one appears, that is.”
Jerome thought that the possibility of an essence dropping was low, as he easily allowed me to hunt it with their help.
“Summoning!”
I immediately went over to summon Bellarios.
“Defeat it!”
The shiny scales of the Bellarios that appeared through the stone gate were quickly tenderized by the knights and archers, and less than a minute later, it disappeared in a flash of light.
Shine!
A huge mana stone dropped where it had been standing. As did an essence.
“An essence...really did appear. Huh? Lord Baron, where are you going? Ah, wait... so the person who needed that essence—!”
“Yeah, it was me.”
I left behind a befuddled Jerome to speed-walk over to the essence and absorb it.
[The Essence of Bellarios is being absorbed into your soul.]
Yeah, it was finally mine.
“Behel—aaaaaah!”
My perfect shield barbarian wasn’t too far off.

chapters.title: Chapter 556: First Clear (1)
paragraphs: Bellarios—a rank-three monster that had the perfect magical defenses to make up for my sole weakness.
The base stats it possessed were as follows:
[Mana Resistance: +200]
Mana Resistance at a level that couldn’t be found in any other monster, and...
[General Attribute Sensitivity: +30]
Water, fire, air, earth, and so on—no matter the attribute of the skill I used, this increase in sensitivity would increase their effectiveness.
And that’s all.
Those two stats were the only ones attached to Bellarios. Honestly, if it had anything else, I’d question the dev’s ability to design a balanced game.
Damn.

This wasn’t the first time I’d had this thought, but I wondered once more what it would be like if that second stat were Resistance instead of Sensitivity. That said, Sensitivity was worth a lot and was a very important stat in this game, but that was only if I was building a Fire Barbarian or Earth Barbarian. I wouldn’t get much use out of it as a Shield Barbarian.
The only skill it applies to right now is Storm Gush.

Eye of the Storm was classified as a wind attribute skill, and Origin was water. These two were affected by the user’s Attribute Sensitivity, and they’d be more effective now that I had some to my name. But since they were skills I was going to erase later on anyway, this boost wouldn’t end up making much of a difference to me.
...What’s important are Bellarios’s skills.
Although it was a shame that I didn’t get resistance for both stats, I found I couldn’t really complain when I remembered the skill I did get. Stats, after all, could be supplemented.
[(P) Circulation Loop—Whenever a monster of rank-three or higher dies within a set radius, your stats have a certain probability of increasing.]
And I had gotten a passive that happened to increase my stats.

In some ways, this ability was similar to the Manticore’s Inheritance, which allowed the user to increase their stats by consuming mana stones, but the key difference here was this: Circulation Loop didn’t have a limit. Well, because the probability of it activating took a sharp nosedive as my stats increased, I would functionally hit a ceiling at around a total of 400 stat points, but still.
[(A) Scales of Greed—When activated, you gain additional Mana Resistance relative to your base Mana Resistance.]
In the end, though, the active was the core of this essence.

I got +35 from Deep Sea Giant, +20 from Bayon, +80 from Ogre, +200 from Bellarios, +40 from erasing Inheritance, and then another +8 from going around eating those potions around that Rift... So that’s 383 in total.
But that wasn’t all. When you added an additional 30 percent from the Earth Dragon’s Blessing on top of that 383 ...
A grand total of 497.9.
Regrettably, that number was just barely shy of five hundred.
However, there was a reason why Giantization was my main skill. Earth Dragon’s Blessing hadn’t even been part of my original Shield Barbarian build.
[You have cast Giantization. Your Threat Level and Physical Attributes increase in proportion to your increase in size.]
Even without using Transcendent Giantization or boosting my stats through Wild Outburst, my Mana Resistance would be over five hundred from this alone.
[You have cast Scales of Greed.]
As I activated my newly acquired skill, blue scales appeared over the thick skin I shared with my fellow barbarians.
“Oh! Bjorn is evolving into a Lizardman!”
Hey, don’t insult me like that.
I looked down at my transformed body with a grin.
[Your Mana Resistance is over 500. All magical damage received will be reduced by 50%. All Physical Resistance stats will increase in proportion to the amount of magical damage absorbed.]
I had finally obtained Barbarian Dragon Mode.
Unfortunately, I barely had a moment to take the essence, use its skill, and admire my new state before...
“I truly congratulate you on your achievement, Your Lordship. However, I wish to continue with the mission at hand.”

With those mood-killing words from Jerome, I stomped back over to the hunting grounds, huffing to myself. Everyone already knew that he was obsessed with the mission. It was a bit annoying, but considering just how good he was at his job, I decided to let it slide.
[You have killed a Bantao.]
[You have killed an Elder Wyvern.]
[You have killed a Fleetwonder...]
After all, the more rank-three monsters we defeated, the more we stood to gain.
Shaaa!

About seven monsters in, a halo appeared above my head and drew in the shining light of our most recent kill right before it disappeared. This was an effect that marked the activation of Circulation Loop.
[Your Mana Resistance has permanently increased by +1.]
[Your Natural Regeneration has permanently increased by +1.]

I’d seen this skill activate for Auyen multiple times already so I wasn’t too surprised, but since I couldn’t see the system messages, I couldn’t tell which stats I got. We would need to make regular visits to the Magic Tower to check our stats and find out which ones went up.
Either way, I could tell that physical stats were the most likely suspects.
That one might have been just within range. Let’s get a little closer.

Circulation Loop had a few activation conditions. When you were within one yard of the defeated monster, the increased stat had a high chance of being a physical stat, and if you were within five yards, it was totally random instead. If you were over ten yards away, research suggested that the stat was more likely to be related to your abilities.
Ah, of course, this research was all conducted by me firsthand.
“Stop! Squad Three and Temporary Squad Four will now switch places with Squad One and Squad Two!”

A short while later, the commander called out another order to the group. Relieved smiles danced across the faces of the knights who had been toiling away with me on the front lines, but I was an exception.
Ah... I just want to stay here and keep padding out my stats.
When would I ever get the chance to kill this many rank-three and above monsters en masse again? I wanted to grind for as many stats as I could while I was stuck working with this expedition group.
However, Commander Jerome sternly shut me down. “You may not know this because you have no experience leading an army, but rules are rules, Your Lordship. You need to follow them.”

Yeah, I supposed if exceptions were made, more people would come forward to challenge his authority. Sensing there was no point trying to convince him, I turned around and tended to my disappointed heart.
Boom! Bang! Crackle!
When I left the stone gate behind and moved over to the bookshelves, I had a bird’s-eye view of the battle unfolding below.
Vwoong!
The knights wielded auras of all colors of the rainbow.
Shaaa!
Heals cast by the priests brightened the battlefield, allowing the knights to fight without worrying about any injuries they might accrue.
“Ihilart Bendai Tiulon!”
Dozens of wizards used group spells in feats of overwhelming firepower.

In truth, they were the reason I had used the fountain pen early on to get the Bellarios essence despite planning to hold off on using it for as long as possible. It was to prepare for the worst-case scenario.
There are too many wizards here.
If they ended up becoming my enemies, I would have been screwed in my previous state.
But now... I’ll be able to at least fight back a little.

I sighed. On that note, I really needed to give Amelia her next essence as well, but it was too much of a waste to use the last remaining charge of the fountain pen on that. Maybe I would just get lucky if I waited long enough.
“Mister, what are you thinking so hard about?”
“Why are you always so curious about what I’m thinking?”
“Ahaha... am I? Why am I...?”
“It’s nothing...” I turned back to my task of removing books from the shelves, still lost in thought.
Finally, the time to switch rolled around, and around the time we would have needed to switch back, the day came to an end.
We repeated this routine a few more times until, before I knew it, it was four in the afternoon on our 114th day in the labyrinth, only around eight hours left before the rainy season began.
“...Commander, we’ve reached the final bookshelf.”
The library would soon be fully cleared.

Honestly, even I was kind of shocked. I never imagined it would be possible to reach the last stage of the library in just a week. Our group had to stop at around the rank-three and rank-two monsters the last time we visited, and even that took a month. Their speed was on a whole other level from ours.

However, I did have some excuses for that. Their group’s goal wasn’t to hunt, but to clear the floor. Unlike us, who hunted as many rank-three monsters as we could, these guys only ever took out a single book from each row so they could keep climbing the shelves.
“You may all rest until new orders are given!”
The palace’s army, which had spent the past week summoning and fighting monsters late into the night, was finally given a moment to rest as the mission was put on pause.
That, of course, wasn’t the case for the leaders.
“Then we will begin our meeting.”
While everyone else was splayed out and resting to recover their health and MP, the other leaders and I were gathered off to the side for a meeting. We all had grim looks on our faces.
I’d known from the start that the last few books would have rank-one monsters since Hamsick told me so himself. But these guys hadn’t known that.

“We had our suspicions, but it seems rank-one monsters do in fact appear on the last bookshelf,” the deputy commander, the one running the meeting, said cooly, though I noticed an ever-so-slight tremble in his voice. Not that that meant anything about our course of action. “Before anything else, I want to establish that the commander has decided that even if it means facing a rank-one monster, the mission will proceed as planned.”
I’d expected as much, but there was a bit of a commotion from some of the other leaders.
“A rank-one monster... We are sure to suffer severe casualties.”
“I am starting to wonder if this is worth all that.”
I understood how they felt. It wasn’t as if we hadn’t gotten here without sacrifices.
“Commander, seven people have already been killed in action!”

Seven people had died in battle the past week. Six of them were warriors from the expedition group. One of them was a warrior from the Armin Adventurer Group. No matter how many priests we had, even they couldn’t do anything when someone was killed instantly.
It also isn’t rare to see severed arms and legs strewn around the battlefield now.

The last summoning book we used had two rank-two monsters accompanied by four rank-threes and all of us were fighting it together rather than in shifts like usual, yet even then, the number of limbs that had been ripped off during that battle had been over twenty. Thankfully, the priests had managed to reattach them immediately after the battle was over, but what would happen against a rank-one?
Clearly thinking along the same lines, one of the knights spoke up. “If we suffer any more casualties here, this could become a major loss for the palace—”

“Stop.” Commander Jerome immediately cut him off. “This is a sacred mission given to us by the royal family of Rafdonia. Thus, we must do our duty. No matter the sacrifices that might need to be made on the way.”
As we were an army with a strict hierarchy, Jerome’s stern response shut the anxious knight right up.

The deputy commander quickly stepped in to resume the meeting. “Whether or not we will proceed with the mission isn’t the topic we are here to discuss.” Jerome had already decided we were going to fight, so there was only one other reason he’d call us over here. “We have identified seven monsters we can summon. Please feel free to share your opinions on which one we should fight.”
We were here to debate which monster would be the best to face.
As the meeting began in earnest, many different opinions were shared, but I stayed quiet at first to hear the others out.

“I believe the Leviathan is the best choice. We are currently not in the ocean. As it is a monster who gets a significant advantage from its native habitat, I suspect that it will be easier to defeat on land.”
First of all, Leviathan was the wrong choice. Although the logic was sound enough, we didn’t have the team comp needed to defeat that particular monster.
“How about Tol-Lapupa? It’s a monster that specializes heavily in defense, so if we invest time into preparation, we should be able to defeat it without taking much damage.”

That was also a no. We had plenty of knights on our side, but in the end, wizards made up the heart of this group’s damage-dealing forces. We would never be able to break through its shell with spells.
“I believe that the Kashan would be the best—”
“Well, I think a Ridger would be a better option than a Kashan—”

The leaders each offered their opinions and either supported or challenged the ideas of the others. Of course, every word out of their mouths was crap. Most people had never seen a rank-one monster in their lives and had only ever heard stories about them. They were essentially legendary, mythical creatures that most adventurers would only ever talk about in theory.
Am I going to need to step in?
Even though it was only in the game, I had plenty of experience defeating countless rank-one monsters. And frankly, from where I was standing, this meeting was pointless to begin with.

Just look at how this entire conversation was being framed—we were discussing which monster would be best to hunt to minimize the amount of damage we would take. None of them were entertaining the idea that we might fail. They truly believed that no matter which of the seven we summoned, we would be able to defeat it.
“Now that I think about it, you haven’t said anything for a while, Lord Baron.”
“...Are you talking about me?”
“Do you perhaps have an opinion to share?”
Ah, right. Honestly, I’d been about to speak up, and this guy had been kind enough to set the stage for me.
“I do.”
The other leaders in the meeting seemed intrigued, their attention immediately snapping to me.
“If we are to summon one, it needs to be Kashan,” I declared, cutting straight to the point. At my announcement, the eyes of the others lit up with interest.
“The Wolf of Prophecy?”
“So you are of the same opinion as me, Your Lordship.”
Some seemed surprised while others looked pleased that I agreed with them. On the other hand...

“If you do not mind, could I ask you to explain why it has to be Kashan?” the highest-ranking wizard in the expedition group asked me. He stared down his nose at me with a look that suggested that he saw me as nothing more than a mindless barbarian.
This guy is the one who wanted to summon Leviathan.
The old wizard went on lecturing me. “Kashan is the monster with the highest attack power of all the monsters we’ve discussed. It is guaranteed to cause the most damage to our group.”
Hey, don’t act like you know everything just because you’ve read some books and can do some magic.
“However, if there is a reason you feel we need to choose Kashan over the other monsters, do tell. If you cannot convince everyone here—”
“I do have a reason.”
I wasn’t sure why this old man looked so surprised when he was the one to ask me to explain myself in the first place. “Tol-Lapupa, Leviathan, or whatever—none of those are options.”
“...What do you mean?”
What do you mean, what do I mean?
“Kashan is the only one we have any hope of defeating.”
The others were impossible for us to beat in the first place.

chapters.title: Chapter 557: First Clear (2)
paragraphs: Even the monster world had its share of celebrities. For example, if I grabbed a regular person off the street and asked them about Bellarios, not one of them would have a single clue what I was talking about. Ogres, Orcs, Trolls, Goblins, and Minotaurs, however? Even a normal citizen of Rafdonia could conjure an image of those in their minds in perfect detail.
So then, what was the difference between the two groups?
Stories.
In my opinion, stories played a big role. Just as people from Earth learned about the Little Mermaid and the Nutcracker when they were kids, the people of this world also grew up hearing stories.
The Cunning Goblin.
The Savage Orc.
The Minotaur of the Labyrinth.
The Tyrant Ogre of the Forest.
The monsters with famous tales about them often had descriptors like that attached to them, and the same went for rank-one monsters.
“...Has everyone heard? It looks like we might have to fight either Kashan or Leviathan.”
“You mean the Wolf of Prophecy or the God of the Sea?”

The Wolf of Prophecy, Kashan, and the God of the Sea, Leviathan. Sometimes they were only referred to by their titles, so I’d had to look them up after arriving in this world to figure out what people were talking about. In any case, that wasn’t the important thing.
“...If we can defeat one of them in battle, this will truly be a legendary expedition.”
“I am a bit worried. Will we be able to take down monsters like those...?”
Everyone knew by now that we were going to have to fight a rank-one monster, yet even among the members of the palace’s expedition group, public opinion was split.

“Haha, you worry too much. Yes, they’re incredibly difficult to fight when you face them in their original territories, which is why they have legendary status. But aren’t they still just monsters? With our might, we’ll be able to take care of them no problem.”
“Hmm, I do hope that’s the case...”

Some were confident while others were openly worried. Jerome listened in a bit to gauge popular opinion before glancing at his wizard, who promptly cast another sound restriction spell so we could continue our discussion. “We won’t be able to defeat any of them except Kashan... Your Lordship, could you elaborate?”
“There’s nothing more for me to say. I’ve made my opinion clear, so make your decision. Will you put your trust in the word of your wizard, or the word of an adventurer?”

The old wizard next to me let out a chuckle at that. Or, well, his mouth was laughing, but his eyes were not. “I understand that you ascribe great importance to your experience, but we are the ones who have spent decades delving into firsthand accounts and becoming experts in these creatures.”
“So?”

“I can’t accept your assertion that Kashan is our only option. The most recent instance of a rank-one monster being defeated involved only forty combatants. And from where I stand...” The old man shrugged and looked out at the expedition group, and only then did I realize why he was so confident.
“So you think that just because forty people were able to do it, a group this big can do it too,” I deduced.
“That’s right. Gathered here, we have nearly two hundred talented individuals who were handpicked by the palace itself. What goal exists that we cannot accomplish?”
“Let’s make sure we’re on the same page first. Are the forty people you’re talking about the Boating Clan, who disbanded decades ago after a dimensional collapse?”
My question sent a hint of surprise flashing across the old man’s face. “...So you know the story?”
Of course I did. It wasn’t like I relied solely on my knowledge of the game—I studied a lot.

“From what I’ve heard,” I continued, “every single one of them was one of the best adventurers in the kingdom, and they prepared for that single hunt for over half a year. They also spent nearly a billion stones to buy all the items they needed.”
“If you’re worried about resources, our expedition group has more than enough—”
“Sir Versilus,” Jerome said pointedly. “Do not interrupt His Lordship.”
The old wizard fell silent, and I was thankfully able to continue my explanation unimpeded.

“You think we have enough supplies? There is no way. An hour ago, we didn’t even know we were going to have to face off against a rank-one monster. Do you really think that potions and scrolls alone will be enough to take one down?”
“If we go by your logic, Lord Baron, then what difference would fighting a Kashan make?” the old wizard replied, clearly annoyed. “We would be just as unprepared either way.”
Yeah, I figured you would say that.
I snatched up the opportunity I was given before he could get another word out. “The monster Kashan has the lowest resistances of all the rank-one monsters.”
“But in turn, its attack power is that much higher.”
“That’s the reason we have any chance of beating it.”
“...On what grounds are you basing that claim?”
“The fact that I am here.” I pointed at myself with my thumb. “I should be enough to hold back the wolf.”
“Hah!”
Before the speechless old wizard could grumble himself into a fit at my bold declaration, I quickly tacked on a more logical explanation.

“Also, there is no established method for hunting a Kashan. In other words, that means Kashans can be hunted without needing special preparations. Although we’ll have some casualties, the Kashan is definitely beatable.”
“What do you say to that, Sir Versilus?” Jerome inquired.
The old-timer was slow to respond. “...With that logic, you could argue that any monster is beatable or unbeatable depending on what’s most convenient for you.”
All he did was shoot down my argument without even bothering to engage with it.
However, Jerome didn’t seem to have anything to say about that. “I see,” he trailed off, nodding as he fell into thought.

Seeing an opportunity, the sneaky old wizard muttered, “Commander Saintred, how about we ask everyone? Ask them if we should summon the Leviathan like I suggested, or summon the Kashan as the baron suggests.”

In other words, he wanted to put this up for a vote. I couldn’t sit idly by and let that happen. It was obvious what the group would go with if they were forced to choose between trusting a barbarian’s advice and trusting a wizard’s.
So now he’s using his brains.
I needed to prevent a vote at all costs. But before I could so much as open my mouth, a stern voice sliced through our argument.
“I will not let that happen,” said Jerome.
“Won’t let it happen?” the old man echoed incredulously. “Why is that?”

“Forcing the responsibility of making a decision on my subordinates simply because I couldn’t choose between a mere two options myself? Sir Versilus, a leader willing to do such a thing could never earn the genuine trust of the people beneath him.”
“...It’s not about shifting responsibility. We’re just going to ask for their opinions—”

“That is the same thing,” Jerome said sharply, cutting the old wizard off. “A leader is someone who makes decisions and takes responsibility for those decisions.” With that, he ended the debate by declaring, “All right, I’ve decided.”
“And by decided, you mean...?”

“Kashan. We will summon the Wolf of Prophecy.” With an air about him that brooked no opposition, he forged ahead, adding, “This decision is solely mine, and any consequences will fall solely on my shoulders. Everyone would do well to remember that as we begin preparations.”
There was only one thing the other leaders could say in the face of such charisma.
“Nia Rafdonia!”
Heh, this kingdom really did have a lot of talented people.
While I was sharing the news with the members of Squad Four after the meeting, Jerome approached me. “Your Lordship, could I have a moment of your time?”
“Of course.”
The two of us didn’t need to go anywhere as everyone quickly scurried away to give us space. The wizards nearby even cast a sound-restricting spell so the two of us could talk in private.
The commander chuckled to himself. “I wasn’t planning on causing such a fuss.”
“There’s a saying that the more secretive the leader, the better.”
“...Is there?”
“No, I just made it up.”
He didn’t seem to have anything to say to that.
“So what is it?” I prompted.
Jerome quickly got down to business. “I’m here to tell you not to worry too much about Sir Versilus. I’ll deal with him.”
“Deal with him...?”
“I know that you and the Magic Tower had a bit of a disagreement a while ago. I could tell he was being petty and making a point of arguing against your suggestions on principle.”
“...Do you have information on Kashan?”
“Nothing that any adventurer wouldn’t already know. Honestly, I’d never even heard of the Boating Clan before you mentioned it since I myself am not an adventurer.”
“...Then how did you know that the wizard was only arguing with me because he wanted to and not because I was wrong?”
“What I lack in adventuring experience, I make up for by being plenty knowledgeable when it comes to people. And Sir Versilus is rather easy to read.”

This was an unexpected side of Jerome. I had assumed he was a muscle head who left all the thinking to his deputy commander considering how he ordered him to figure out the whole stone gate issue on his own.
Though I guess it doesn’t have to be one or the other.

Honestly, people like him were the trickiest to deal with. Deciding when to use their strength and when to use their brains was as easy as breathing to them. In some sense, I supposed I could say he and I were the same type of person.
“In any case, I ask that you don’t hold too much of a grudge,” Jerome implored. “Regardless of whether you like him or not, we’re all going to be allies until we leave this place.”
“Don’t worry. I wasn’t even mad to begin with.”
“Haha, is that so?”
“I mean... you’ve put up with quite a bit of crap too.”
“Well, I don’t think of it as ‘putting up with’ anything...”
“I guess you were born to be a soldier, then.”
He chuckled again. “How about you take this opportunity to join the army too, Your Lordship? I think you’d take to it like a fish in water.”
Don’t say something so ominous with such a straight face.
But still, how unexpected. I didn’t foresee us being able to relate to each other like this. Maybe we would be able to walk out of this with a friendly relationship—
“By the way, Your Lordship.”
“Could I perhaps make a request?”
“A request?”

“The more time I spend with you, the more you remind me of someone I once met. And so, although I know it’s impossible...” With that foreboding preface, Jerome held up an object he’d had tucked under his arm throughout our conversation. “Could you try this on for a second?”
It was a helmet that covered the entire face.
“...I-I’m hungry, so I’m going to get going now!”
Never mind, none of that “friendly” business. From here on out, I needed to stay as far away from that guy as possible.

The rank-one beast-type Wolf of Prophecy, Kashan... Although we’d decided to summon it, we didn’t immediately jump into a raid. Defeating a rank-one monster was no easy task. We needed to replenish our health and MP to ensure we’d be at the top of our game going into this fight.
“Attention all soldiers! Sir Versilus will now brief everyone on the monster we will soon be facing!”

We also needed to be primed on the strategy that we would be using against it. Unlike when we faced rank-two or three monsters, however, we couldn’t tune out the parts of the explanation that didn’t directly concern us—if we did, we wouldn’t be able to deal with the curveballs that might get lobbed our way during battle.

“Greetings, soldiers,” Grandpa said, clearing his throat. “As you all know, I am Gahuin Versilus, the lead wizard of the First Expedition Group. I have been tasked with imparting upon you the intelligence you need to face the Wolf of Prophecy, Kashan. But first, its name is derived from...”

Boring couldn’t even begin to describe how information-dense and long-winded the old wizard’s explanation was, but since everyone’s lives were on the line, we forced ourselves to stay awake and listen.
Oh, except for one person.
Honk!
Hooonk!
A vein pulsed on the old wizard’s forehead when he spotted Ainar not only sleeping but snoring loudly on top of that. It seemed he was wary of me, though, as he let it pass without comment.
I sighed. I’ll just have to explain things to her the barbarian way later.

Anyway, after that lesson, we had another leadership meeting. We ironed out formations, the items we would use, how we were going to cycle damage throughout the raid, and so on. The discussion took place over several hours, and unexpectedly, I had to make very few contributions to the conversation. There wasn’t any need for me to.
“Saintred, do you perhaps have experience fighting this type of monster?” I asked curiously.
“Hmm... if there’s anything you feel I’m missing, please tell me. My ears are open.”
Uh... that wasn’t meant to be criticism.

Once I explained that I was only asking because I couldn’t find any fault in his plan, Jerome flashed a joyful smile. “Haha, it seems the labyrinth tactics I learned back in my youth have come in handy,” he said humbly.
“Labyrinth tactics? Is that something you learn when you’re training to become a knight?”
“Not usually, but my father was a bit of a peculiar man.”
“...I see.”
Anyway, once that first meeting was over, we put our heads together to run some combat simulations and continuously brainstorm any variables or unexpected developments we might face.
With so many people contributing, it feels like I’m playing a tabletop RPG.
Maybe it was because when I used to play Dungeon and Stone, I played and thought things through all alone, but getting to talk things out with a group like this was fun in its own way.
“Then we can stop there for today. We will gather the whole team tomorrow for training and the fight will commence the day after, so make sure to go to bed early today.”
In any case, we’d nailed down our plan.
On the next day, we gathered everyone in front of the stone gate to assign formations and then spent the day rehearsing the raid.
“You over there! You’re in the wrong position! You should be here, not there!”
“Ah, sorry...!”
“You... what’s your name?”
“Celt Abys—”
“Wrong! Your name is A Disgrace to Humanity!”
“If ‘sorry’ could solve everything, what would we need martial law for? Is something wrong with your brain? Look over there! Even Ainar, a barbarian, knows where she should be!”
Even as I was wondering if this mock battle rehearsal would actually be useful, I made sure to be as strict with everyone as I could. Just in case.
Who knew? Someone who might’ve otherwise died might come out of this alive thanks to my yelling.
“...I didn’t realize the baron was so scary.”
“H-He’s making me remember my time as an apprentice knight.”
“Don’t look so betrayed. Don’t you know the type of person the baron is by now? He’s saying all this for our own sake!”
“Oh... I guess he must be feeling terrible about yelling at us, then.”
Thanks to the work I put into building a friendly relationship with them, none of them protested the way I was treating them.
“That is all. There won’t be anything else to do until midday tomorrow, so rest up until then and steel yourselves!”
Once the mock battle was over, we made camp earlier than usual and went to bed.
And then, it was noon the next day.
“Take your positions!”
“To your positions!”
“Lift the book onto the altar!”
Rumble!
Once we were all in formation, we watched, laser-focused, as the stone gate creaked open and a pair of eerie blue eyes flashed at us through the darkness.
Then, from the sinister shadows...
Boom!
A four-legged beast slowly crept out into the open.
[You have encountered Ominous Prophecy. Your Luck stat has been set to -200.]
All right, let’s do this.

chapters.title: Chapter 558: First Clear (3)
paragraphs: Each member of the group was currently standing in the formation that we’d devised during our long, arduous meeting. We’d stationed a few melee warriors with the long-range damage dealers, and we also had a strike team made up exclusively of knights in the back as well. This wasn’t a regular formation, where long-rangers stayed as far back as they could and melee dealers stuck solely to the front. Everyone was situated in a way that minimized risk and would allow us to react strategically no matter what might happen next.
I, of course, was no exception. I was standing right in front of the stone gate, all alone.
In other words, I was going to have to hold back this monster by myself, without anyone else to back me up. Of course, I wasn’t complaining. I had agreed that this was the best plan...
Grrr... The beast of legend that emerged from beyond the stone gates let out a low growl, then looked down as if inspecting me.
Well, it was probably a bit surprising to see a single guy standing under it, holding nothing but a shield.
Don’t stare at me like that.

I couldn’t help but tense up a little, maybe because this was the first rank-one monster I was facing in the flesh. Even so, the more formidable the opponent, the more fighting spirit we barbarians showed—that was our whole thing.
I tightened my grip on my shield and looked up at the beast.

The wolf was double my height even with Giantization active. Considering it was a quadruped, I’d wager that its total length was even more than double that. On top of how huge it was, it had red fur and eyes on each of its three tails, like something straight out of an ancient myth. It also emanated a dark red fog around itself that made it look even more otherworldly.
But so what?
“What? Is this your first time seeing a barbarian?”
Like a dog listening to its human, the huge wolf tilted its head a little. This was the best time to kick things off.
“Behel—ahhh!” I let out a battle cry and put all my power behind a Swing.
Boom!
Even though I whacked its nose at full force, the wolf didn’t so much as flinch, like my attack didn’t even tickle. However, it seemed I’d made the right call dealing the first blow.

The wolf must have moved, but it was impossible for me to track it with my naked eye. All I knew was that the next time I blinked, its huge maw was closed around my shield in an attempt to tear it to shreds with its teeth.
Despite my surprise, I couldn’t help but laugh. Any normal shield would’ve turned into scrap metal the moment it entered the wolf’s mouth, but this shield was different.
This one’s indestructible, you bastard.
Even a rank-one monster couldn’t break an unbreakable, single-digit Numbered Item. The problem here was that I was still losing to it in terms of strength.
Wha—Huh? This little...!

A moment later, the wolf lifted me by the shield and swung its head around in a frenzy. Nausea swept over me, but letting go now would be the equivalent of accepting my death, so I held on as best I could.
Thankfully, supporting fire soon flew in.
[Gahuin Versilus has cast the rank-one attack spell Orb of the New World.]
It was a rank-one attack spell cast by channeling the mana of the dozens of elite wizards in the expedition group.
A flash of light later, I opened my eyes to find I was on the ground without anything on top of me anymore. I sprang to my feet and turned to see the wolf had taken a lot of damage.
Graaah!

It seemed to have gotten hit on its hind leg as the fur there was incinerated and it had a visible limp. I, however, was perfectly fine. While the spell had fired pretty close to me, I hadn’t been turned into minced meat like back in the Bloody Citadel.
[You are taking damage from an ally you are Bound to. The Light of Trust protects you from the damage.]
Before the battle began, the old man and I set up a Binding spell.
This was the reason Trust was No. 12. Not getting hit by friendly fire was an incredible advantage in this world.
Since he’ll have to gather mana again before casting, the next shot will be in three minutes.
Until then, the rest of us would have to pick up the slack. Three minutes was by no means a short amount of time when facing a rank-one monster.
[Kashan has cast Three Eyes of Beauty.]
Its three tails fanned out behind it, and the eyes on the tips opened up.
Fwoong! Fwoong! Fwoong!
Then, like those railguns you see in movies, rays of light rocketed at us.

The left tail does magical damage and inflicts a curse on the target, the right tail does physical damage and shreds Resistance stats, and the middle tail deals mixed damage and summons token monsters.
I recalled the effects of each tail as I blocked the rays as best I could.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
Usually, this skill chose targets at random, but since my Threat Level was so high, all of the beams were aimed at me instead.
[You have lost your balance and are now prone.]

However, even while successfully blocking them, I ended up tripping over my own feet, my stance breaking. A ray of light took the opening and slammed into me, though thankfully, I didn’t take too much damage.
[All damage dealt to you increases by 10%.]
This was... the resistance shredding tail, right? If this effect stacked too many times, I’d be in trouble.
That damn Luck stat.

I never would’ve made that kind of rookie mistake under normal circumstances. However, I made sure not to be too hard on myself. In truth, rather than a mistake, it was simply the effect of one of its skills.
Ominous Prophecy set everyone’s Luck to -200. If you were within its aura while fighting against the beast, things like this were bound to happen.
Like so.
[Dodge unsuccessful.]
Attacks that I thought I dodged landed on my body...
[Critical hit. You have taken significant damage.]
And an attack that would’ve otherwise left me a little tingly dislocated my joint.
[Kashan has cast Life Steal.]

And in the middle of all this, what looked like translucent red threads extended out from every single person in the library and connected themselves to the wolf. This was the monster’s sole way of healing itself. Since there were over two hundred people around it, it was recovering from the damage it sustained reasonably quickly, but that wasn’t as big a problem as you’d think since we had taught the soldiers exactly how to handle this.
It just so happened that 80 percent of our melee damage dealers were knights.
“Cut the threads!”
“Aura! Use your aura!”

The moment the threads appeared, the knights we had stationed evenly throughout our formation sliced through them to stop the wolf from healing. The threads usually took around six hits to destroy, but they were instantly cut away by aura, which ignored 90 percent of all Physical and Mana Resistance.
All right, we’ve stopped it from recovering.
Since Life Steal had a cooldown, we had about two minutes until it tried healing itself again.
“Charge!”
On their commander’s orders, dozens of knights drew their swords and charged at the wolf.

Maybe it was because we had been fighting side by side for over a week now, but even though I was still worried that these people could end up becoming my enemies in the future, I couldn’t help the hope I held close to my chest.
“Nia Rafdonia...!”
I hoped that most of them survived.
Slash, stab! Clang!
The aura used by the knights was excellent at dealing damage and coupled with the long-ranged attacks from the handpicked members of this expedition group, Kashan’s pelt fell away in short order.
This was a strategy that could never be attempted under normal circumstances, not when the Threat Level required to hold a rank-one monster’s attention was exponentially higher than other ranks.
But with Wall of Aegis, so long as my Threat Level is over five hundred, all monsters will prioritize attacking me first.
If not for this effect, the knights fighting on the ground with me would’ve been getting shredded by teeth and claws right now.
Still, with how much damage they’re doing, I guess they could’ve defeated it even without me here.
Though about one hundred people would’ve died in the process.
Just how many soldiers were going to survive thanks to me? I hoped that the commander would notice my contribution—
[Kashan has cast Flames of the End.]
At that moment, red shadows appeared on the ground. While preparing for this fight, this was the attack we’d identified as the second most dangerous one we’d have to face.
“Dodge!” the deputy commander shouted, playing his role as a support coordinator in this fight.
Boom!
The areas where the shadows had flickered to life all erupted with pillars of fire a second later. Not even a second, actually—the AOE attack was practically instantaneous.
Raven was in that direction...
The moment I turned my head, just to check, I spotted Ainar dragging Raven out of danger by the scruff of her neck in the middle of the crowd of panicked wizards.
Hah... she’s safe.
Well, in truth, it was too early to be sure of that, since Flames of the End was a skill with additional effects.
“Wizards, form the barrier!”

As the deputy commander barked out another order, the wizards each did their part to create a protective barrier. Unlike the initial bombardment, the follow-up attacks were weak enough that we could block them with a wall of mana.
Fwoosh!
A massive barrier covered the ground where the pillars erupted.
Drip, drip, drip.
The soldiers quickly ran inside the barrier just as a rain of fire began to pour. Unfortunately, however, there were a few who failed to get to safety.

The cries came from a wizard and an archer who was trying to help him get out of the line of fire. The two were promptly swept away by the flames and disappeared into the downpour. A nearby knight who witnessed the death of his allies gritted his teeth and shouted, “Elton Pashire of Squad Two, Quilcan Bertlern of Squad Three—killed in action!”
Like the soldier he was, he deemed that delivering a status report was of the utmost importance, no matter the situation.
I should focus too.
Truthfully, we needed to treat every single skill a rank-one monster might cast as instant death. Even the rays of Three Eyes of Beauty could kill someone in one hit.
I needed to do my job properly to keep everyone alive.
“Behel—ahhh!”
I cast Wild Outburst to raise my Threat Level again and planted myself right in the wolf’s personal space.
“We’ve finished casting!”
“Melee unit! Move back!”
When we got the call sometime later that the spell was ready to go, the knights who were around me quickly retreated from the front lines.
And then, once more, the rank-one spell Orb of the New World fired and hit the monster head-on. But this time, it seemed to have landed a more critical blow.
[Kashan has cast Flames of the End.]
This time when it used its AOE attack again...
[Kashan has cast Death Sentence.]
It also threw in a new skill.

This was the skill that we had deemed to be the most dangerous when running our battle simulations: Death Sentence. Going by the name, you might assume it was a one-hit-kill skill, but it actually wasn’t. It just functionally behaved like one when Kashan used it.
[The damage dealt by Kashan’s next attack will significantly increase relative to its Luck stat.]
In reality, it was a damage amplifier based on the user’s Luck stat.
For every ten points of Luck, Death Sentence increases the damage dealt by 200 percent.
Exactly the kind of buff you’d expect from a rank-one.
However, the real problem here was Kashan’s base Luck stat. After hours and hours of research, I’d determined Kashan’s Luck stat had to be around five hundred.
In other words, 10000 percent.
Meaning that any attack that followed Death Sentence was essentially instant death.

Even a regular attack from a rank-one monster could kill a high-ranking knight in one or two hits. I had raised my Physical Resistance by leaps and bounds, but even my bones would break from one of those hits if I didn’t block with my shield. That said, if I managed to pull off a proper guard with Wall of Aegis, I wouldn’t take any damage at all.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
The problem was that this was all a matter of luck.

I sighed. Thankfully, I’d been able to block the first Death Sentence successfully. But in the aftermath, I could feel my heart pounding furiously and my knees wobble a bit, maybe because I knew that there was no way to know when the next attack would come.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump!
I forced my legs to still and calculated the amount of hits I would need to take.
Between three or four.
If we could defeat the wolf quickly, only three. If we were a little slower, four. That was the number of Death Sentences that I’d need to take.
Will I be able to block all of them?

I smirked at the thought. This wasn’t a matter of whether I could or not. If I couldn’t block it, I’d just have to push through it. If my legs and arms were torn off, if my organs burst, I’d just have to stay on my feet and keep fighting.
Then the problem would solve itself.
[Kashan has cast Life Steal.]
And with that, my first-ever large-scale raid continued. Everyone stuck to their positions and gave their all to their respective roles.
[Kashan has cast Flames of the End.]
Yet the pillars of fire still erupted and news of more deaths was still relayed. My only solace was that none of my companions were among the names mentioned.
[Gahuin Versilus has cast the rank-one attack spell Orb of the New World.]
We had managed to pull off our third successful spell, this one a headshot. But like the rank-one monster it was, it didn’t falter in the slightest and continued gunning for me.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
I was luckily able to block the second Death Sentence.
[Kashan has cast Crossed Fate.]
Then, when its HP fell below 50 percent, it whipped out a new skill.
Fwoong! Fwoong! Fwoong!
All the while, the rays from its tails continued to fire at me, and a few failed attempts at guarding on my part meant some of its attacks landed.
The damage I took increased, and the curses on me began to stack up.
[The Plague Wolves charge toward the most populous area on the battlefield.]
Token monsters popped into existence as well.

And in the middle of all the chaos, I barely managed to catch sight of a red shadow beneath my feet right before Flames of the End exploded upward. With the big wolf charging me, it was impossible for me to dodge the blast.
[Your HP has fallen below 20%. All of your Resistance and Resilience stats have maxed out due to the passive skill Path of Heroes.]

My entire body melted away, but not really. My flesh was charred and sloughed off, and it felt like my organs were cooked given how hard it was to breathe, But thankfully, my Mana Resistance kept me from dying instantly.
And since I wasn’t dead, that meant I wasn’t down yet.
Sparkle!
As heals from the priests flowed into me, I lifted my shield and limped forward.
[Kashan has cast Death Sentence.]

In that critical moment, the third Death Sentence was cast. It felt almost like time around me slowed down, my mind’s processing power accelerating as Kashan reared up. In that split-second, my only thought was this:
In my current state...will I be able to survive?
The answer was simple: no. It was as obvious as one plus one equaling two. The moment I realized that, my vision went white.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis has absorbed all damage.]
The wolf’s front claw slammed down...onto my shield.
I’d managed to keep my feet under me and, almost as if by accident, instinctively blocked the attack. I couldn’t believe it.
Did I... Did I really survive?
I gulped air through my gaping mouth. It seemed that I had forgotten to breathe for the past few seconds. The deep gasp scorched through me, as my lungs still weren’t healed all the way.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump!
Of course, all the while, my stubborn heart continued to race.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned the Elemental Ruler of Darkness, Dicloe.]
Familiar black orbs began to rain down on the wolf. Support arrived at the perfect time as every member of the expedition group doubled down to take advantage of the opening and end this fight.
Yeah, with this, we’ll be able to kill this thing before the fourth—
But accidents were called accidents because you could never see them coming.
The moment I stepped forward, my foot landed on something slippery and slid out from under me.
[You have tripped.]

When I blinked the stars out of my vision, now flat on my back, all I could see was one thing. It wasn’t the library’s high ceiling, but the maw of a beast that had been trying to snap me up in its jaws this entire fight.
Crunch, crunch.
Distantly, I registered the sound of the wolf chomping down on my head, its massive teeth scraping against my skull.
As I listened to it eat me, I had a thought.
Wasn’t expecting that.
Even though I could feel everything, it strangely didn’t hurt.
[Your brain has suffered significant damage.]
[You have fainted.]
That was the last thing I remembered.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]
[You have killed a Kashan. EXP +9]
[Achievement Unlocked]
[Condition: Defeat a rank-one monster for the first time.]
[Reward: Your Soul Power has permanently increased by +10.]
[The top contributor will have the authority to browse the records.]
[The hidden First Records Archives reveals itself to you.]
[You are being healed.]
[You are being healed.]
[You are being healed.]
[You are being healed.]
[You are...]

chapters.title: Chapter 559: First Clear (4)
paragraphs: Hearing came back to me in a jumbled cacophony.
“...Ritman Powel is confirmed dead!”
“Mailden Betimore of Squad Three is confirmed dead!”
“Garon Nilgrains of Squad One is confirmed dead!”
Desperate voices rang out around me.
“Mister! Are you awake? Hello?”
“Priest, why is he not waking up?”
“It’s... I think he’ll wake up if we wait a little longer...”
“He sustained a severe head injury. Is that why it’s taking so long?”
My companions were worriedly chattering right over my prone form. And beneath the din, I could pick out Missha’s voice, mumbling to herself.
“If something goes wrong... I’ll have to use that...”
What is she talking about? My brow furrowed, but I couldn’t focus past the ringing in my ears and the exhaustion still clinging to me.
“Well then... it seems the baron is all healed, so I will go and tend to the other—”
“What the hell are you saying? He hasn’t woken up yet! Where do you think you’re going?”
“Tersia, stop.”
“What do you mean stop? Are you not worried about Mister—”
“I mean that’s unnecessary. He’s awake.”
“...What?”

Ah, I got caught. I’d wanted to sort through some of the chaos cluttering my mind before opening my eyes. I needed to figure out our status, anyway. I could pretend to be asleep and procrastinate all I wanted, but I’d still have to face reality eventually.
“Captain!”
“Oh! Bjorrrn! I was worried!”
As I opened my eyes, my comrades all let out sighs of relief.

Rather than reassuring them that I was fine, I jumped straight to the most important question. “Did any of us...get hurt?” I wasn’t usually the type to be so indirect, but what I was really trying to ask was whether any of our people died.
Amelia instantly understood my question and answered, “Glow Isius died.”

Glow Isius was a member of the Armin Adventurer Group’s wizard trio. He was a young man in his thirties. Whenever he saw me, he always joked about how I needed to give him more time and funding if I wanted him to get anything done.
So, he had died.
“We didn’t have any other deaths. We had a few injuries, but aside from one exception, everyone else’s were minor.”

“I see...” I closed my eyes for a moment and let out a deep sigh. Everyone remained quiet as I did, granting me a moment of silence. Although what felt like hundreds of aborted thoughts were swirling through my mind, I focused on one and one alone.
The things I need to do... Let’s get to it.
“I remember that wolf chomping down on my head, but what happened after that?” I asked. “Tell me everything that happened after I lost consciousness.”
For some reason, Amelia seemed hesitant. “...As soon as you were bitten, Tersia fired her arrow.”
That meant that Concentrated Fire hadn’t been fully charged when Erwen let it fly.
“The hit made Kashan let go of you, and Karlstein and I took advantage of its surprise to run in and save you.”
That arrow had created enough of an opening for them to rescue me. However, things only went downhill from there.
“...After that, all of us faced off against Kashan together, and a lot of people died. That’s all. Oh, also, unfortunately, we weren’t able to get an essence—”
“Don’t skip over the details.”
All of us faced off against it together, and a lot of people died—this wasn’t a story that could be summed up in a single sentence. I needed to know.

Sensing my resolve, Amelia let out a sigh and gave me the answer I was seeking. “Yandel, after you fell unconscious, a huge vacuum appeared in the front line. We needed someone to fill that void, so... Dozens of knights ran in.”
“What about Jerome Saintred? What, did he stay in the back and watch this all happen?”

“Actually, he didn’t. He’d been waiting back there specifically for something to go wrong, and when you fell, he was the first to run forward. If it weren’t for him, we wouldn’t have been able to save you.”
“...I see. Sorry for interrupting you. Continue.”
“The commander joined the battle, but things still weren’t going well. And then, in the end, he changed our orders. He commanded the soldiers in the back to join the battle and fight too.”
The soldiers in the back were stationed next to the long-rangers—the wizards, priests, and special-ability users—to protect them. So even they had been mobilized.
It was a call I could see the merit in. The battle had already been nearly over when I’d fallen. Rushing to kill the wolf as fast as possible would have been the best way to decrease our casualties.

“But his plan had a fatal flaw.” The issue was that no one could manage the wolf’s aggro properly. “Kashan attacks the most threatening individuals first. As such, most of its attacks were aimed at the commander, but it was a very unstable situation.”
Every time it swatted at them with its massive paws, the neck of a knight flew off, and every time a wizard fired off a powerful blast, the wolf would turn to charge at them.
“That was when Glow Isius died.”
And with that, the wizard trio became a duo.
I was wondering why they didn’t want to tell me how he died...
Were they thinking that he wouldn’t have died if I had stayed up?
...Well, that was true.

“We faced the wolf for three minutes after you fell unconscious, and then the commander finally drove his sword through the wolf’s forehead and ended the battle. After that, the stone gate closed and then opened again, showering the area with light. It’s been about ten minutes since then.”
I paused to take that all in.
“How is that?” Amelia prompted. “Did that answer all of your questions?”
“For now.”
A knight I recognized from Squad Three approached us as our conversation trailed off into silence. “Lord Baron, you’re awake! The commander is calling for you!”
“...I’ll be gone for a bit.”
“I’ll be helping the injured,” said Amelia, “so don’t worry about us.”
I eventually followed the knight over to Jerome, who had lost one of his arms and was sporting a hole that punched clean through his gut. He was currently being healed by a priest.
So this guy took some pretty hard hits too.
“It’s a relief to see you looking well, Your Lordship.”
“I think you’re worse off than me right now, to be honest.”
Jerome let out a strained laugh and didn’t say anything to that, instead turning to his deputy commander. “All right, the baron is here as well... Ebost, report!”
With all the leaders in one place, the debrief began.

“The First Expedition Group has accomplished an amazing feat by defeating the Wolf of Prophecy, Kashan, today. It is an achievement that will surely be recorded in imperial history. Unfortunately, we weren’t able to acquire an essence that could be offered to the palace...”
As the report continued, I was once again reminded of just how dangerous rank-one monsters were.
“Twenty-seven people sustained moderate injuries and have already made full recoveries, four are still suffering from serious injuries, and a total of twenty-eight were killed in action.”

Twenty-eight dead soldiers, twenty-one of whom had died in the three minutes I was unconscious. Of those who died in battle, our Squad Four only suffered one casualty. No one could refute that this was nothing short of miraculous, but there was also a concrete reason our numbers looked like they did.

“Count Saintred,” I called. “I heard that you commanded Squad Four to retreat to the rear at the end of the battle.” After I fell unconscious and Kashan began running rampant, the commander sent Squad Four back to the relatively safer rear. “Why did you give that order?”
It wasn’t that I was displeased with the order—not by any means. In fact, I was incredibly grateful for it. But that didn’t mean I didn’t have questions about why he gave it.
“That’s because if you die, then we will have failed one of the objectives of this expedition, Your Lordship. For that reason, I commanded the entirety of Squad Four to fall back and protect you.”
“...What?”
“Your Lordship, our expedition group didn’t just come down here to hunt mere monsters. And I have never, save one time, ever failed a mission.”
This mindset was beyond all comprehension. Was his mission really that important to him?
“No matter how many people die in the process, if we save you and return to the city, the mission will be a success,” he concluded.
I genuinely didn’t know what to make of this guy anymore. The last time we talked, I’d had the thought that we could have been friends if not for the situation we were in.
I said the only thing I could. “Understood. That answered my questions.”
“That’s good to hear. Then can we continue with the meeting?”
When I nodded and took a step back, the deputy commander paused for a moment before resuming the meeting.
“Those are all the casualties we have to report, so I will move on to the next item on the agenda.”
The next topic of conversation was quite simple. We had successfully defeated Kashan, and since it didn’t drop an essence, we didn’t need to have a discussion about who would take it. Instead...

“As soon as Kashan disappeared, the stone gate opened again. The wizards have confirmed that the light it is emitting is similar in nature to a portal... Put simply, there is a very high chance that if we step into that light, we will end up somewhere new.”
What could be beyond that open stone gate? When should we pack up and leave this place to continue our expedition again?
These were the topics discussed during our meeting, and many different opinions were offered. I let their conversation wash over me without paying it much mind, engrossed in my own thoughts.
That was because I already knew what was beyond the gate.
...I didn’t realize that that was how the door was supposed to be opened.
It was the area we had already visited with Hamsick. Well, there was a possibility that it could be some other place, but I concluded that the probability of that was low.
I guess the way this is normally supposed to go is that you clear the library by defeating a rank-one monster, and then the gate opens to let you obtain the reward inside.

The many different types of summoning books would be the smaller rewards, and the fountain pen that allowed for a guaranteed essence drop was probably the main reward. Hmm, perhaps the golden book as well.
Anyway... I guess I somehow ended up skipping ahead.
If I hadn’t met Hamsick earlier and taken all the rewards beforehand, the fountain pen would’ve gotten taken by the palace as well.
So the secret to this place is that there’s a way to skip clearing the library and enter the reward room anyway.
