From the perspective of a player, that was probably the purpose Hamsick served. That said, there seemed to be even more hidden secrets here waiting to be found.
Then was that the reason why it told me I didn’t have the qualifications yet? Because I didn’t officially clear the area before entering the reward room.
I was only guessing, so I wasn’t completely sure. I would probably need to meet Hamsick again to gauge its reaction.

“Then we will end our meeting there. Until seven in the evening, the only people on duty will be those on the patrol team, so each leader should return to their squad and take care of them. Ah, and be advised, we will be redistributing personnel later.”
The meeting came to a close with all of us getting free time.
Seven in the evening...

These guys were intense. Even after a battle of this scale, we didn’t even get a full day of rest, only a few hours before we were going to have to tackle a new task. A sigh threatened to escape me, but I swallowed it back and headed over to my allies to relay the news.
“...Five hours isn’t long enough to sleep,” Ainar grumbled.
“Hmm? Not long enough? Can’t you just sleep?”
“For once, Ms. Fenelin is right. I think I need more sleep than that too.”
“But I don’t know if I’ll even be able to sleep. I’m still in shock... My heart is still racing in my chest right now.”
Many people were grateful that they were even being given some time to rest.
“You can sleep or rest or do whatever you want, but we should do what needs to be done first,” I stated.
“By ‘what needs to be done’...”
“One of our comrades has died.”
“Ah... that’s right.”
I led the entirety of Squad Four to a corner of the library, where we had laid the body of our only squad member who was killed in action.
The only woman in the wizard trio, Sharlot Emblut, sank to her knees in front of the corpse, her face blank with shock.
“Are you all right?” I asked.
“...No. I’m not all right at all.”
“I’m guessing this is your first time?”
A lot of things were condensed into that single question. Sharlot clenched her fists until they shook, but she didn’t say anything in response.
Her older brother, Brian Emblut, came over to guide her away from the body, and we began our small funeral service. As always, the process was over very quickly.
“His remains and his belongings will be taken back to the city to be given to his family.” We sorted through his belongings and cast distortion magic on his remains to keep them intact.
After the funeral ended, Sharlot approached me.
“Lord Baron... Someday...if...if enough time passes, will I be all right? Just like everyone always says?”
That was what everyone asked the first time they experienced something like this.
Hah, how should I answer that?
I took a moment to collect my thoughts before saying, “The definition of ‘all right’ is different depending on the person.”
“Ah, yes... you’re right. That was a foolish question—”

“But you know,” I continued, trying to sound as confident as I could for her sake. “One day when you remember him, if you remember the happy memories before the sad ones, and if that is what you define as being all right... then you’ll be all right. Even if you perhaps don’t want to be.”
She fell silent.
“Go rest now,” I said, then turned around. As I did, someone came up next to me. It was Missha, the only one of my companions here from my Team Half-Wit days.
“Just then... you were talking about Dwalkie...right?”
I didn’t deny it. “...Somewhat.”
Missha seemed to get lost in thought for a moment. “Back then... things were really good...” she murmured, a deep longing woven into her tone.
Of course, I was no different. “Yeah... they were.”

Now, I was a baron with countless people following my lead. Some might even see me as the hero who left his name on the Stone of Honor. But my mind still wandered back to those days from time to time.
Fighting for our lives every moment. Watching over our shoulders for plunderers. Struggling against rank-five monsters...
Looking up at the third floor’s night sky together.
“It’s a view that only adventurers who get here early enough can see. Isn’t it wonderful?”
I was now all right.
I had just taken out a single blanket to lie down and pass the time when an uninvited guest showed up.
“Yandel, the head wizard of the expedition group is here for you.”
“The head wizard...?”
“He says he wants to talk to you. What do you want to do?”
“...I can’t sleep anyway, so this is good. Bring him here.”
With that, I got up and packed up my blanket as Amelia escorted the old wizard over.
“Gahuin Versilus.”

“Lord Baron, my apologies for interrupting your rest. May I speak with you?” I glanced at Amelia, who was standing beside him, and she left without me needing to say anything. “I wish to cast a voice control spell as well. Is that all right with you?”
“Sure, go ahead.”
“...Ah, thank you. It’s all done.”
“So, what is it?” As always, I skipped the pleasantries and got straight to the point.
Which perhaps made the old wizard’s reply even more unexpected. “I came here to apologize to you, Lord Baron.”
“Hmm, apologize...?”
“That’s right. I was wrong, and you were right. However, I wasn’t able to accept that, and as a result, I nearly made a catastrophic mistake.”
Forget the apology for now—I was more curious about his sudden change of heart. “What made you change your mind?”

“It’s only natural that I’d reassess after what I witnessed today. Rank-one monsters... They are monstrous indeed. I was underestimating them. But Lord Baron, as an adventurer, you saw them for exactly what they are.”
“I see.”

“To be honest... before you fell unconscious, I still wasn’t afraid of it. No, in fact, I was convinced that if we had summoned Leviathan as I suggested, we wouldn’t have suffered any casualties at all. However...”
The old wizard trailed off, then spoke as if he was unloading a heavy burden.

“That things were going smoothly had nothing to do with me. My knowledge and my talent for magic had no bearing. Nor did the hundred elite soldiers handpicked by the palace. I saw that for myself during the three minutes you were out of commission.”
“Ah... I think you’re praising me a bit too much.”
“As a scholar, I am only stating facts. If you hadn’t been here today, the list of casualties would have been far, far longer.”
It was hard to come up with a coherent reply after someone said something like that right to your face. So, I stayed quiet. Just being present was half the battle, as the saying went.
He cleared his throat. “Ah, it seems I droned on for a while there. In any case, what I mean to say is just one thing.”
“Then say it.”

“Our expedition group needs your strength, knowledge, and decision-making skills, Lord Baron. I will take heed of any counsel you give in the future, so please share with us whatever is on your mind.”
In other words, he wasn’t going to try to shut me down anymore, so he wanted to work together from now on. This was one of the better pieces of news I had heard today.
“All right. Then I’ll be in your care, Gahuin.”
“...Gahuin?”
“Friends call each other by their names.”
“Ah, that’s right. Then... Bjor—”
“You can call me Lord Baron. I’m a noble.”
“...Ahaha. That’s true. Well, thank you for taking the time to talk to me during your break. I will be going now.”
After that, I got together with my comrades to share a meal, and once our break was over, the members of the expedition group all gathered around the open stone gate and stepped through it as one.
[You have entered the First Records Archives.]
A small seed of hope that we’d end up someplace new had been budding in my chest, but the place we unlocked after clearing the library was indeed Hamsick’s home.
“How ominous-looking.”
“It looks as if a storm passed through here.”
Unlike the clean mini-library we saw when we first entered, the place was practically in ruins now. However, I couldn’t see Hamsick or the golden book anywhere.
Well, I guess Hamsick was out in the main library the last time I saw it, so it’s probably still out there.
Honestly, that was for the best. If the golden book was here, possession of it would immediately go to the palace.
“It’s quite the odd place, isn’t it, Lord Baron?”
“It is. I wonder why it’s such a mess...” I said, tutting at the disrepair.
“Please tell us if you find anything.”
“Will do.”
After the expedition group checked the secret room and confirmed that there was nothing dangerous inside, they began to properly investigate the place.
“Everything in here is damaged. Is there even a reason to investigate...?”
“What are you saying? We are the first to ever step foot in this place!”
“There is definitely something here, so perform a thorough search!”

Ah, to clarify, the so-called “thorough” search these royal soldiers performed was a little different from the method favored by adventurers. They didn’t break anything, but what they did do was use their absurd inventory space to take everything they could get their hands on.
“These books are blank...”
“Everything found here is the property of the palace. Do not leave even a single thing behind!”
It didn’t take long for the wrecked room to turn into a vacant one.
“Investigation complete! There is nothing hidden here!”
...Sorry, Hamsick.

chapters.title: Chapter 560: First Clear (5)
paragraphs: After the search and seizure of Hamsick’s home was complete, we ended up having a lot of time to spare, as there wasn’t as much investigating to be done in the space beyond the stone gate as we expected.
“These are the items we found in the initial search, and I’m confident they’re not at all ordinary. Commander, please entrust this duty to us. We will study them and uncover all their secrets.”
“...We leave the library tomorrow, so unearth anything you can before then.”
“Understood!”

While the others were resting, the wizards of the expedition group gathered together and began a series of tests on the items they took from Hamsick’s home. Not that I expected them to get anything out of it, though.
And if they do find something, I should be able to sneak in a question to Raven about it.
With the interior of the library now converted into a research facility, I could see Raven among the other researchers doing all sorts of experiments.
She looked happy.
Is that really fun...?
As a barbarian warrior, I couldn’t understand her taste in hobbies at all, but I needed to respect her. Also, it was always good to have a few people like her around.
Plus, maybe because she’s a player, Versyl doesn’t show any interest in academics.
In any case, since we were free to do whatever we wanted until tomorrow, I decided to take it easy and rest.
“The squad reorganization plan has been finalized. All soldiers, check your new assignments on the poster we’ve created here!”

The redistribution of our forces went into effect sometime later. Between the seven people who died during our various battles in the library and the twenty-seven who died in the final fight, each squad needed to have members moved around and subbed out to ensure they were well-balanced.
“Squad Four doesn’t seem to have changed at all.”
Since our squad had low numbers to begin with, there were no changes made to our comp, while Squads One, Two, and Three each had some slight changes.
Squad One, forty-nine people.
Squad Two, forty-nine people.
Squad Three, forty-nine people.
Each squad originally had sixty people, but their numbers had been reduced to this. With Squad Four now at thirty-seven, there was only a ten-person difference between our squad and the others.
“We will be holding a meeting! All squad leaders and officers must attend!”
Once everyone had their new assignments, we had another meeting. These guys really liked their meetings. So after what ended up being a short break, I entered the tent right as it began.
“Only with your hard work and loyalty were we able to safely complete our campaign in this library. Nia Rafdonia.”
“Nia Rafdonia!”
For some reason, Jerome was leading this meeting instead of leaving it to the deputy commander as usual.

“The wizards are busy with their research, but they haven’t yet been able to find a single clue that will aid us in our escape from this floor. As such, we will put that issue on hold until their research is complete.”
“So this meeting is...”
“It is to discuss what we will do next.”

With that, we got down to business. Since we’d cleared the library, we needed to decide on our next destination. Naturally, the eyes of all the other leaders shifted to me. Since I was the one who had been here the longest, and since I was the one who supplied the map, they likely valued my input a great deal.
Where would be the best place to go next...?
There were three potential candidates.
One: Giant Island.
It’d be possible to farm for Hipramajent’s essence there, and that huge giant boss monster lived there too. Also, it had the portal stone that connected to Basement Floor Two.
Two: Rainbow Island.

This was the island in the direction of the rainbow we saw back when the rainy season came to an end. It was a complete mystery of an island, and my gamer senses were telling me that whatever it was, it was the key to Basement Floor One.
Three: Chief Island.

That option went without saying. If our intel was right, that place had the portal stone that connected back up to the first floor, and even if that wasn’t the case, I could tell that the village chief was hiding some sort of big secret. If we could capture him and figure out what exactly that secret was, that information would likely prove very helpful in the future.
Hmm, what do I do?

I had gotten to see the strength of the expedition group for myself while fighting alongside them in the library. They weren’t perfect, per se, but even I had to concede that they were an impressive task force. Also, considering that the group was composed of knights, wizards, and priests who specialized more in man-to-man combat than hunting monsters, I predicted that if we went, there was a good chance we’d be able to burn down the entire village with the village chief still inside before nightfall.
But oddly enough, something’s just not sitting right with me...
I decided to listen to my gut again, laying out the map I took from Hamsick’s home and pointing to an island. “...I think this would be the best place to visit next.”
It was the one island, other than Rainbow Island, that we hadn’t been to yet.
“We check this island out first, and if there is nothing there or if it’ll take too long to clear it, then we can immediately head for Rainbow Island after,” I suggested.
In other words, we could just drop by this island to fill in the map on the way to Rainbow Island.

“I see. Thank you for your input, Your Lordship.” Jerome nodded and accepted my input without giving any indication of whether he agreed or not. “What are you all doing? I didn’t call you all here to twiddle your thumbs and listen to the baron’s opinion. This is a discussion, so I want to hear your perspectives. Do not hold back.”
The other leaders began to share their thoughts, and Jerome listened intently to each one. Then, at long last, he declared what our next destination would be.
“Tomorrow morning, we will head toward the island where this so-called chief resides.”

I wondered why he even asked for our opinions if he was going to end up doing whatever he wanted anyway, but I knew that was a bit unfair of me. The only reason we came to Library Island in the first place was because he went with my suggestion.
Hm, I guess not obtaining anything here in the library was a big factor.

We had come here on my advice, but we hadn’t gotten anything out of this trip. In fact, we’d ended up losing troops instead. That was probably why Jerome was making this decision. We could capture the village chief, get information out of him, and then use that to plan our next move more efficiently.
I guess it came to this, then...
Besides my strange, lingering unease, I didn’t really have any reason to argue against this decision, so I kept my mouth shut and accepted it.
Though I did, of course, have a question. It was something I wanted to ask earlier, actually.
“...Tomorrow?” I asked. “It’s rainy season right now, so what do you mean by that?”
It wasn’t the tail end of the rainy season either. Since it was only the second day, dangerous monsters were still falling from the sky as we spoke.
However, Jerome dismissed my concerns. “You said yourself that you have experience traveling during the rainy season, Baron Yandel. There is no reason we can’t do the same.”
“Uh... but we only got moving when the rainy season was nearly over...”
“Taking an exhaustive survey of this floor is also one of the missions of this expedition. Shouldn’t we experience this ‘rainy season’ properly at least once?”
I felt it every time I talked to them, but these guys really were hardcore as hell.
Excluding the wizards, who were busy with their research, everyone went to sleep. The only people wandering around that dark, early morning were the select few on night watch.

I, on the other hand, was under a blanket and staring up at the ceiling in a daze. I had taken a nap that afternoon after the meeting so I didn’t feel sleepy at all. Sensing that I wasn’t going to nod off any time soon even if I forced my eyes closed for a while, I instead spent the time collecting my scattered thoughts.
Our first ever encounter with and defeat of a rank-one monster.
The deaths of dozens of soldiers.
The missing golden book and Hamsick.
Our next destination.
A lot of things happened today, and there were a lot of things still left to figure out.
I’m interested in what Jerome Saintred said earlier too.

The commander of the expedition group had made the following statement today: no matter how many people died in the process, so long as this expedition got me back to the city alive, the mission would be considered a success. Thanks to that, my anxieties about whether this trip would end up being a repeat of the one to Ice Rock had quieted a little.
If he were planning on killing me, he would have been strategically better off letting Squad Four suffer as many casualties as possible.
However, Jerome instead took pains to ensure the complete opposite. This was something he would’ve never done if he was scheming against me. Which left me with even more questions than I already had.
Why is the palace actually trying to save me this time? I’m a thorn in their side, so wouldn’t it be better for them if I die here?
I had no way of knowing the answer to that. The more I thought about it, the less any of this made sense to me.
The uncertainty pushed me to get up from my makeshift bed and get moving in an attempt to clear my mind.
“Lord Baron? Where are you going?”
“I can’t sleep, so I’m going to stretch my legs a little.”
“Ah, I see. Understood.”
After letting the night watch know what I was up to, I started walking around the outskirts of the large library, figuring that I might get lucky enough to run into Hamsick.
Lo and behold, ten minutes later, I heard a familiar sound from somewhere nearby.
Squeak...!
“(...Hamsick?)” I whispered in the ancient language.
“(Here! This way! Come up here...!)”

After glancing around a little to see if anyone was looking my way, I climbed the staircase to the second bookshelf as quietly as possible. Hamsick was hiding in one of the empty slots where a book had been taken out.
“(Why did it take you so long to come?)” it demanded.
“(Oh, I was waiting for nightfall.)”
“(You... are you okay? It looked like you were hurt pretty bad...)”
Uh... I didn’t expect it to ask me that right out of the gate. “(...I’m all healed now, so don’t worry.)”
“(How could I not worry? After so long, I finally found someone qualified!)”

I tilted my head. “(By qualified... do you mean for the golden book?)” Hamsick had once told me that he couldn’t give me the golden book because that item was something he had to save for the right person.
“(That’s right! The moment you defeated Kashan, you became qualified!)”
So, like I thought, clearing the library was the achievement I needed.
The joy of having my theory confirmed rushed through me, but I had a question. “(Wait, then is everyone here qualified now?)”
“(Huh? Not at all! You’re the only one who got the qualification!)”
“(Hmm, really?)” Then what was the condition that needed to be met? Was it contributing the most to the battle? If that was the case, it still didn’t make sense that I’d be picked.
Well, none of that mattered right now.
“(So? Now that I have the right qualifications, what next?)”
When I made it obvious that I was waiting for my reward, Hamsick rushed to say, “(Here, take it! This book is now yours.)”

It handed me the golden book with the boring story written inside. Wondering if I would be able to see some sort of hidden text now that I had the right achievement under my belt, I threw it open. “(...The writing is the same as last time.)”
“(Really?)”
“(What do you mean, really? If I’m qualified, shouldn’t you tell me how this book works or something? What, is your job done after you hand it to me?)”
“(Uh... yeah?)”
I sighed. Based on the look on its face, Hamsick seemed to have no idea how to use the book either.

To be honest, that wasn’t a big surprise to me. That was how cruel a game Dungeon and Stone was. It never explained anything, so its players had to test all sorts of solutions to figure out how anything worked.
...I think something might happen if I put this book on the altar.
I could already think of a few potential use cases, but I couldn’t test them right now. If it worked and something showed up, all the spoils would go to the palace. In the end, I had only one option.
“(Anyway, thanks for giving this to me.)” I took the golden book from Hamsick and hid it in my sub-space for safekeeping. “(So, is there anything else?)”
“(You know, a blessing or unique equipment you want to gift me or something.)”
“(You’ve already taken everything! My fountain pen and all those precious books I’ve been protecting!)”
Ah, right.
A moment of awkward silence settled between us, and I quickly changed the subject. “(Right. Well, I don’t know if you overheard, but we’re leaving tomorrow morning.)”
“(You’re... leaving...?)”
“(We have things we still need to do. I don’t know when, but I’ll definitely come back someday, so don’t get too lonely in the meantime.)”
“(Who said I’ll be lonely at all? Don’t be so full of yourself... you leaving is better for me, hmph! Now I’ll be able to relax in my own home!)”
I gulped. Judging by the way it was talking, Hamsick still didn’t know what happened to its house.
“(...Why are you so quiet all of a sudden?)”
“(I-It’s nothing. I’m going to go now. I’m hungry!)” With a very casual excuse, I booked it back to camp.
The next morning, all the members of the expedition group packed up camp and got ready to leave the library.
“Excuse me... Lord Baron...?”
And the Goblin Paladin, Sven Parav, came to me in those early hours with a bit of startling news.
“Last night... she showed me the future again.”
“What did you see?”

“Well...” Parav hesitated for a long moment before squeezing his eyes shut and explaining what he saw in his dreams. “You were surrounded on all sides by the expedition group... and they were in the process of brutally executing you...”
The goddess had shown him my death warrant.

chapters.title: Chapter 561: Destination (1)
paragraphs: The Goddess of the Stars had delivered to Sven Parav a revelation in the form of a prophetic dream. It outlined how I would die in the near future at the hands of the expedition group, who I had just been starting to believe I could trust.
Ba-dump!
The warrior’s heart in my chest began to pound a loud beat, sensing danger. However, before all else, I calmly clarified. “Are you sure?”
“...I’m sorry?”
“Are you sure that you saw me die? In that dream.”

This was quite the cliché in modern media. They’d show the actor getting shot in the trailer, but then in the movie, it was revealed they were wearing a bulletproof vest the whole time and the story would end happily ever after. Stuff like that happened all the time.

“I’m not sure.” Even in this situation, where certainty was of the utmost importance, he was still being wishy-washy. “But no matter how many potions were used on your body, none of them had any effect.”
Potions weren’t doing anything... Hmm, that was a problem.
Am I... really going to die...?
To be honest, it still hadn’t sunk in. My mind was a mess.
What do I do?
My first thought was that I could just pull the same trick I pulled for Amelia’s older sister. However, some logistical issues immediately sprung to mind.
If this were a situation with such an easy solution... why deliver a whole prophecy about it?
No, more importantly, how would a situation like the one Parav saw even come to pass? Wasn’t the expedition group’s whole objective to get me back to the city alive?
Damn, why do I have to deal with this so early in the morning...

“...Lord Baron!” While I was furiously wracking my brain for what the hell I was going to do about this, Parav shook me by the shoulders. “Didn’t you hear me? We don’t have time for this. You need to run away.”
“Run away...?”
“The goddess also told me this: your destiny is not yet written in stone. It is up to us to determine what our future holds.”
In other words, the future Parav saw was one I could avoid depending on the effort I was willing to put in.
“Why... didn’t you mention that earlier...?”
“Uh...? I-I don’t know...?”
Man, you should’ve led with that.
Now I understood why everyone else bullied this guy so much.
In any case, by not ‘written in stone’ yet, she’s probably talking about the Records Stone...

I finished assessing the situation. Reatlas was one of this world’s three main gods. If she, a goddess, was saying that I could change the future, then it had to be true. Which changed things a little.
What the—? This wasn’t that big a deal at all.
In a way, this was basically the equivalent of a red light on Destiny Seeker. I now knew that misfortune was lurking around the corner, but I could avoid it if I was careful.

“Thank you for telling me about this. However, I’m going to stay,” I sternly rejected Parav’s suggestion that I make a run for it, and for a very simple reason. “I’ll take care of this, so keep talking. Everything you saw in that dream, tell me every detail.”
Nothing ever got fixed by running away.
As soon as I rejoined my companions, Amelia pulled me aside.
“You looked pretty serious during that conversation. Was it important?”
“Not really. It wasn’t much.”
When I brushed her off, Amelia stopped pushing. Instead, she shut her mouth, narrowed her eyes at me in a glare, and whirled around.
...Was she mad at me? I was trying to be considerate and not worry her before I had time to make sense of this mess.
In the end, I couldn’t help but tell her the truth, though I did it in an uncharacteristically roundabout way for a barbarian.
“Emily, if I suddenly found myself in danger of being executed by the commander, what would you do?”
At first, she stared at me like I was speaking a different language, but then her jaw tightened. “Are those guys... scheming something?”
“I’m not sure yet. So, what’s your answer?”
The look on Amelia’s face suggested she thought it was obvious. “I’d stop them. Even if I had to risk everything to do it.”
“Even though they have more than a hundred people on their side?”
“Didn’t you hear me? I’d stop them with everything I have.”
I could hear a deep determination in her voice.
Yeah, so that’s your answer, huh...

Although I was grateful for her loyalty, her response also left a bitter taste in my mouth that was impossible to ignore. If things really did end up going south, this wouldn’t end with just my death. All of the people around me would get swept up in this too.
...Should I have run away?
That thought crept into my mind, but I quickly shook it away. There was a chance that running away might make things even worse.
Let’s just keep an eye on the situation for now. I still have time before I need to make any decisions.
I was basing this assessment on three key pieces of evidence I derived from Parav’s account of his dream.
One: The dream was set on an island.
From the description, I figured it was Chief Island. Since we weren’t there yet, I should be all right for now.
Two: It wasn’t set during the rainy season.
In other words, my safety was guaranteed for at least the next few days.
Three: For some reason, Erwen had short hair.
That particular detail would help tip me off as to when this might happen.
As such, it wouldn’t be too late to run away later, once I had a better grasp of the situation.
“Embark!”

After that, the expedition group got on the boats and left Library Island. Squad Four didn’t board our usual boat and was instead split among the three military vessels, as that would give us a much better chance of surviving the rainy season at its heaviest.
It’s still pretty intense since it’s only the third day.

Sure enough, monsters were pouring down from the sky. Of course, the ships themselves each had defensive magic circles inscribed on them that were currently being supplied with mana by dozens of wizards, so the monsters weren’t hitting us at all.
Boom! Crunch! Thud!
The monsters instead collided with the mana barriers and fell into the ocean, their blood dripping down the sides.
“It’s not as arduous as we anticipated. Ebost! What is our mana expenditure? Is the rate what we expected it to be?”
“Yes! We’re currently having no issues!”
The three ships cut through the silver waters and sailed forward.

Most of the monsters smashed into the barrier and harmlessly fell into the ocean, but not all of them. A few aquatic ones chased us through the water, and the ones that could fly obstructed us from the air.
Graaah!
At one point, a Hipramajent appeared from below the waves to grab our boat.
“It’s a Mobilus!”
On top of that, we also ran into a super-large type rank-two ocean monster. However, none of these encounters caused us any trouble since the ship was built to handle combat.
Boom! Boom! Boom!

The dozens of mana cannons installed on the ship cleared our way forward with blast after blast. These ships also had mana propulsion systems that were on an entirely different level from the one on our boat, and they were always on at maximum capacity to keep us moving at breakneck speeds.
“Emaze Lula Kini Pitia!”
The wizards used the magic circles engraved into our boat to fire attack spells.
Crack! Creak! Creak!
At the same time, the ice crusher at the helm designed to help the ship traverse through frozen stretches of sea was whirring away, grinding up all the small monsters in our path.
...How much would a boat like this cost?

It was completely different from the military vessel I boarded for the Dark Continent expedition, though I supposed that the ship’s purpose had been different, to begin with. That had been a boat designed to transport as many individuals as possible, while this ship was made solely for naval combat.
Six hours, twelve hours, eighteen hours...
Soon, we were around a day’s travel from Library Island.
“Commander! We can see our destination!”
Our destination had appeared on the horizon.
On our 118th day in the labyrinth, we pushed through the heaviest part of the rainy season and arrived at Chief Island, all without a single casualty.
With that, there was only one decision left to make.
“Count Saintred, what shall we do now? Are we going to disembark and begin traveling inland?”
We still had three days left until the rainy season was over. Still, I could tell that the worst of it was behind us and the strongest monsters weren’t dropping as often anymore.
“No. Until the rainy season is over, we will wait here.”
Jerome decided we should stay on the boats. It seemed that after experiencing the rainy season firsthand, he’d concluded that going out onto land at this point would be dangerous.
You know, you should’ve just trusted me from the start.
“So wouldn’t it have been better if we waited until after the rainy season like I suggested?”

“There is no guarantee we will be able to leave this floor anytime soon. A day might come when we might have no choice but to travel during the rainy season, so I reasoned that experiencing it at least once when we are fully prepared would be best.”
Well, when he put it that way, I couldn’t argue. Now that he’d seen it for himself, he would be able to make informed decisions even in an emergency.

“Also, one of the missions assigned to our expedition group is investigating this floor. We need to experience as much of it as possible to give the palace a thorough report. Including everything that happens during and after the rainy season.”

Or so he said, though I couldn’t help but feel that he was making things harder for no reason. Still, I figured a soldier’s perspective must be different from most people’s. The expedition group even had a specific knight who was in charge of recording all of our battles.
Then I guess we’ll weather the storm until the rainy season is over...
The most important factor now was Erwen. If her hair was still the same even after the rainy season was over, that would mean that the prophetic dream wasn’t going to come to pass just yet.
“Erwen, are you planning on cutting your hair short any time soon?”
“Huh? Well, I like how it looks right now... but if that’s what you want, M-Mister, I’ll—”
“What are you talking about? I like long hair! Don’t even think about cutting it! Got it?”
“Uh...? Ah... okay! I’ll never cut it!”
All right, with that, she probably wouldn’t cut it of her own volition. Even if it meant getting all my own hair burned off and going bald, I needed to keep her hair safe.
“Oh!” I heard Ainar shout. “Bjorn, so you’re that kind of guy?”
What was she talking about?
I chuckled at her nonsense, but for some reason, Amelia was looking at me appraisingly.
“Hmm, I didn’t think that was your type, Yandel.”
...Should I clear this up?
When I happened to meet eyes with Raven, she cleared her throat before twisting a curl of her chest-length hair around her finger.
Ah, whatever. They could think whatever they wanted to. It didn’t really matter either way. I had plenty of other things to worry about, so I didn’t intend to waste my energy on something like this.
“I’m going to sleep for a bit, so don’t disturb me unless it’s my turn on rotation.”
With that, I returned to my quarters so I wouldn’t be disturbed, laid back on the bed, and shut my eyes to think.
No matter how I look at it, they didn’t come here with orders to kill me... so why would I suddenly get executed?
How could something like that happen?
I think it’ll probably involve the village chief somehow...

I didn’t have any concrete evidence to back that up yet, but that was my immediate thought. I was still wary of the chief—I had a sneaking suspicion that he had some sort of method of stealing another person’s body like an evil spirit could.
If he does have an ability like that... the scenario in Parav’s dream is definitely plausible.
There were even two clear routes we could take on the way to that scene: Either Commander Jerome Saintred got his body taken, or...
My body gets taken.
Either of those situations could lead to the expedition group executing me, so now the most important question was this:
How do I stop that from happening?
Operating under the assumption that one of my hypotheses was correct for now, I started brainstorming solutions.
He said that Erwen had short hair...
So what if I just shaved her head entirely? Then would the dream not happen?
...That’s probably not how that works.
The goddess said so herself that the future could be changed. I was pretty sure that a difference in hair length wasn’t a big enough deal to alter the course of fate.
It had to be something else.
Yeah, something...
Something that would make a bigger difference.
Flash!
Suddenly, a thought struck my mind like lightning as it occurred to me that I might be making this more complicated than it needed to be.
In the prophetic dream Goblin had, Jerome Saintred was the one who killed me...
So wouldn’t everything be fine if I just got rid of him?

chapters.title: Chapter 562: Destination (2)
paragraphs: Jerome Saintred... There was a high probability that getting rid of him would solve all of my problems.

As the saying went, the flap of a butterfly’s wings could cause a storm on the other side of the world. In that sense, if I could dispose of the main antagonist of that prophetic dream, it would make a huge difference in terms of my survival.
Question is, how do I get rid of him?

The issue lay in the logistics. To start, luring him into a dark corner to kill him with the help of my companions would be practically impossible. He wouldn’t die such a senseless death. On top of that...
“He is probably not dead. He will likely wake up in the palace.”

During my trip into the past, I saw it with my own eyes. After dying by Auril Gavis’s hand, Jerome’s body turned into fluttering flecks of light and scattered to the wind. And I had a guess as to what ability he was using.
Iblus.
Iblus was a rank-two monster that served as the Guardian of one of the eighth-floor Rifts, and it had in its possession a unique active skill.
Heretic Altar.

It was one of the few respawn skills in Dungeon and Stone. Once activated, an altar would form in a spot chosen by the user. Then, if the user ever died, they would revive on top of it. Of course, you could only create this so-called altar once, and it would crumble after three uses.
In other words... even if we kill him, he’d just end up back in the city and inform the palace that I’m a traitor.

This skill was probably a big reason the palace gave Jerome Saintred the position of commander of this expedition group. Even in the worst-case scenario, he would be able to return to the city alone after dying.
Hah. Why did he have to have a skill like that...?
I couldn’t help but feel like some cosmic force was screwing with me.

Despite spending a long while trying to think up alternative ways to eliminate Jerome Saintred, nothing viable readily came to mind. In fact, the only thing I felt confident about was that the prophetic dream sequence was what followed the inevitable failure of each of these attempts.
Wait, does that mean... trying to kill Jerome might be the reason they’d execute me in the first place?
Maybe if I laid low and didn’t do anything at all, I’d be totally fine.
Two knocks on the door interrupted my thoughts, followed by a voice from the other side.
“Come out, Yandel. It’s time for our rotation.”
Right. Before anything else, let’s get some work done.
One day, two days, three days...

Time flew by like an arrow, and soon enough, the rainy season was over. Like last time, a rainbow appeared in the sky for a short while before fading, and the recording crystal captured the scene to preserve it. Once we’d given the wizards who’d been toiling the entirety of the rainy season a day’s worth of rest, we finally got off the ships we’d spent the last few days on and officially began our quest.
“We will now disembark!”
Just as Jeju Island, Korea’s largest island, was said to have an abundance of wind, women, and rocks, Chief Island also had an abundance of two distinct things right after the rainy season.
“We spotted a group of monsters ahead!”
“They’re variants!”
Those things were the monsters, and the thousands upon thousands of mana stones littering the ground.
“If people in the city hear about this, all hell will break loose.”
“With how many mana stones there are down here, won’t the palace take control of this place immediately? If they could obtain this many on a monthly basis...”

“Haha, that’s only how small fry like us think. Do you think a profit of this size will have any impact on the palace’s wealth? The amount of income they rake in from the inspection checkpoints alone is absurd.”

Still, even Jerome, who had stated very plainly that he wasn’t going to bother with mana stones, gave us all a stern warning. “If anyone secretly tries to pocket one, you will be punished severely for doing so, so the wizards who are in charge of collection should take the utmost care to ensure that no mistakes are made!”
Didn’t you say that you weren’t here to make money?

Either way, the incredible mana stone haul reignited the expedition group’s morale. The palace tended to default to adventurer customs when they sent troops into the labyrinth, so they let their soldiers distribute the mana stones amongst themselves accordingly.
“I’ll need to up my contributions to the mission.”
“Our earnings are going to be on a whole other level—at least ten times the usual. There’s a magic item I’ve had my eye on buying for a while, so this is great.”

While the other members daydreamed about full pockets, Jerome somehow became even more laser-focused on the mission after seeing the mana stones on the ground. Though we were picking up all the ones in our path, we stuck as closely to our planned route as we could and marched toward our destination.
“Your Lordship, is this the place?”
“Definitely.”
And then, we arrived at the entrance to the chief’s village. However, no matter how much we searched the roots where the entrance was hidden, all we saw was dirt.
“What is going on? Did they perhaps notice us coming?”
“Well, I’m not sure of that yet. They usually wait for a while after the rainy season is over—after most of the monsters are dead—to come out to collect the mana stones.”
“Hmm, then it seems we’ll have to wait a bit longer.”
“And even if they did notice our presence, they’ll have to come up at some point. They live off mana stones.”
Unless they wanted to starve to death, they couldn’t stay holed up in their village forever.
“Surround this tree!”

Jerome then had us circle the village entrance and gave the order for an indefinite siege. After that, a special unit was created to go around the island picking up the ownerless mana stones. This special unit was formed of agility-type adventurers, who were known for their speed, and wizards, who could pick up a lot of mana stones at once.
“Mister... you need to stay safe until I come back, okay...?”
“Don’t worry. I’ll keep Tersia safe.”
Amelia and Erwen were the people selected from our Squad Four. I tried to stop them from being sent away, but I couldn’t override the commander’s orders. His reasoning was sound.

“It is one thing to keep you safe, Your Lordship, but this request has nothing to do with that. Even if it is only temporary, you are a part of this expedition group, so I cannot give you any special treatment during this mission.”
My heart thudded when Erwen and Amelia went out with the special unit, but nothing happened during the two days they spent going around the island picking up mana stones.
Then tomorrow will already be the third day since the end of the rainy season...

The people left at the tree had nothing to do but wait for the village’s monsters to appear since most of the regular monsters had already culled themselves. However, while the other members of the expedition group were enjoying our rare moment of peace, this break only felt like the calm before the storm to me.
“Mr. Yandel, what are you staring at so intensely?”
“Can’t you tell? I’m staying vigilant,” I replied, keeping my eyes trained on the tree. In my peripheral, I could see Raven smirk a bit.
What was with that reaction?
“So why are you here?” I asked. “The wizards are all over there.”
“Even if I joined them, there’s nothing to do. We’ve already finished studying the things we got from the library.”
“Already? Did you find anything?”
“No, the opposite. We finally accepted that there was nothing to be gained from the items and stopped running experiments.”
“...I see.”

Raven seemed to be telling the truth about being bored as she continued to prattle on while taking a seat next to me. “Our best finds from the library might be the summoning books themselves. The origin of names and the traits of monsters that even years of research couldn’t identify were written in them, down to the very last detail.”
Yeah, I guess that would be your favorite thing.
“Huh? What’s with that look? Can’t you see what an incredible discovery this is? Even if you can’t, I guarantee when we bring this news back to the city, it’ll turn the academic world upside down!”
“...Why should I care if academia gets flipped upside down or sideways?” I deadpanned.
Raven seemed to finally pick up on my disinterest as she quickly changed the subject. “By the way... you said the locals of this village are monsters who call themselves humans, right?”
“You’re only asking that now?”

“It’s not like it’s a weird question. I’ve been curious ever since I first heard your story. Just what kind of creatures are they? Ah, I’m also curious about the village chief who calls himself the Dragon Knight. Is he really who he says he is? If that’s the case, there are a lot of things I want to ask him. It’s hard to find records from back then these days...”

She tried to bring up a topic that was relevant to both of us, but for some reason, I couldn’t get into or enjoy the conversation. Now that I thought about it, that was always how things went with her. It felt like she got more and more long-winded every time we spoke.
“Raven! B-Behind you...!”
She whipped around at my shout, startled.
“Oh, I guess nothing’s there?” I said pleasantly.
It took a moment for her to realize what had happened, and then she whirled back around in outrage, her fists clenched.
“Heh, what could you even do with those tiny fists anyway?”
“...So annoying. You’re a baron now. What are you, a little kid?”
“And you’re the deputy commander of the Third Magic Corps. Aren’t you way too gullible?”
“...I guess I’m the fool here for worrying about such a ridiculous human being.”
“Hey, I’m a barbarian, not a human. That’s something I’m sensitive about, so please be—”
“Agh! So annoying! Whatever, I’m leaving.”

With that, Raven stomped back over to her spot, fuming, and I let out a loud laugh as I watched her go. Now that I could call a productive conversation. It soothed my nerves, and more importantly, it was fun. She had honestly always been entertaining to poke—
“C-Captain!”
...Huh?
I turned my head in the direction of the call and laid eyes on Auyen, who was sweating profusely as he ran toward me.
My calm mind was immediately flooded with all sorts of worst-case scenarios.
“Trouble! We’re in trouble!”
What happened? Was there some sort of skirmish? Wait, but wasn’t the entrance to the village right here? Was there a different entrance somewhere else?
Many different thoughts whirred through me, but the next words that came flying out of Auyen Rockrobe’s mouth stopped them all in their tracks.
“Ms. Tersia! Ms. Tersia is trying to kill one of the wizards from the expedition group! Please stop her!”
“...What?”
I quickly ran to the location Auyen gave me, and lo and behold...
“Stop holding me back! I’m going to kill you, I’m going to kill you, I’m going to kill you! I’ll kill you—!”
Erwen was shouting at someone like she had lost her mind.
Amelia was physically restraining her with everything she had.
One of the wizards was cowering behind a nearby knight, hyperventilating in terror, and said knight had even drawn his sword to protect the wizard from her wrath.
And I, upon laying eyes on the scene, was frozen, my mind blank. I still had no idea what was going on, but somehow...
“Your hair...”
Erwen had short hair.
The incident in question could be summed up in a few neat lines.

Half of Squad Four, including Erwen, had been stationed on the perimeter of our siege formation for guard duty. During their shift, a random monster approached from a spot where the boundary between squads was a little unclear, so they ended up fighting it alongside members of Squad One, whose assigned territory shared a border with theirs.
“I-It was a mistake! An accident, I swear! And no one got hurt in the end either...!”
The problem was that one of the wizards from Squad One miscalculated his trajectory and ended up firing a spell at Erwen.
The friendly fire came without warning. Luckily, Erwen crouched quickly enough to dodge the attack, but her hair ended up getting caught in the crossfire, severing the flowing strands.
Damn it.
“No one... got hurt...?” she echoed, a murderous gleam in her eyes.
“B-Blood Spirit, calm down! Don’t you know that what you’re doing right now will come back to hurt the baron too?”
“Yandel!” Amelia shouted when she caught my eye. “What are you doing? If you’re here, then stop her, quick...!”
The words snapped me out of it. Erwen had gotten a haircut, sure, but that didn’t mean I was going to randomly get executed here.
Armed with that thought, I stepped forward to defuse the situation.
“Mister... is here...?” Erwen swiveled her head around, and when she finally caught sight of me, she let out a shriek and covered her face before collapsing to the ground. “No! D-Don’t look at me!”
Huh... I guess I managed to stop her?
Obliging her request, I turned around.
Rustle.
And when I did, I noticed something blue slip through the dense trees.
What was that? Wasn’t the entrance to the village behind me?
My mind went momentarily blank, but my mouth was one step ahead of it, already forming the words I needed to say.
“It’s an ambush!”
The monsters had escaped their village.

chapters.title: Chapter 563: Destination (3)
paragraphs: Monsters with blue skin, huge eyes, and an average height of ten feet—this mysterious species who called themselves “human”—emerged from the trees to face off against us real humans.
“So these are the monsters Lord Baron warned us about...”
“But why are they just standing there like that and not approaching us?”
The monsters holding position had tense looks on their faces despite the weapons in their hands, their group significantly smaller than our expedition group.
“It’s been a while, Bjorn, son of Yandel.”
In the ensuing standoff, the village chief stepped out from the group of monsters.
The newcomers from the expedition group were clearly surprised to hear a monster like the chief speak our language, and I stepped forward to position them safely behind me. “Yeah, it’s been a while.”
“Your allies have increased in number.”
“Yeah, things worked out that way.”

He seemed to want to talk for now, so I answered him while scanning the area. The rest of the expedition group, the people who had been stationed around the original entrance, were now closing in, and there was no way he hadn’t noticed.
So why is he so relaxed?

His casual greeting and utter lack of urgency just made me even more nervous. However, I hid those emotions to the best of my ability as I asked, “So, where did you come from? You told me that the village only had one entrance.”
“Don’t feel too bad. I couldn’t share all the village’s secrets with an outsider, could I?”
“Ah, like those bodies in the basement?”
The village chief didn’t have anything to say to that. He merely looked me up and down with those freaky eyes before asking me a question of his own.
“Did you know? The cleverest among us tend to pretend they’re unaware of the things happening around them. So I wonder, are you only pretending or are you truly clueless?”
Well, I wasn’t sure about that, but that was a pretty scary line to hear from someone glaring like he was. I almost swung my hammer at him on instinct.
“Your Lordship! Step back!” Commander Jerome Saintred demanded, arriving from the rear.
The village chief turned his beady eyes on him. “Hmm... and who are you?”
“I am Count Jerome Saintred, Captain of the First Royal Guard. I was awarded the position of commander of this expedition.”
“The royal guard... yes, I knew that the palace’s people would come down here soon enough—”

“Now it is your turn,” Jerome cut the chief off and launched into his interrogation. “Baron Yandel informed me that you introduced yourself to him as the Dragon Knight Cornelius Bruingrid. Is that true?”
The chief stared at him before replying, “Does that matter?”

“It does. Because depending on how you respond, I will be determining whether you are merely an unidentified entity we can communicate with or an ancient traitor who needs to be eliminated via execution immediately.”
Ancient traitor? What was this guy talking about?

While I tilted my head in confusion, the eyes of the chief, who didn’t usually show his emotions, hardened with killing intent. It looked like the dragon had just had his tail tickled. “Execution... you’re quite the comedian.”
“Is that so? That’s odd. My friends always say that I’m not a very funny man.”

“Even after all this time, those friends of yours haven’t changed at all. Quite the arrogant bunch. Like they are on top of the world...” The village chief’s voice grew colder. “Try it, then. That execution you’re so eager for.”
“Well, while I’d be happy to fulfill your wish, I can’t carry out an execution here and now.”
“Why? Are you scared? And after coming all—”
“I have a lot of answers to get from you first. But after we interrogate you and obtain all the information we need, I will personally deliver the execution you deserve.”
The conversation died there, after an electrifying exchange full of bombshells that left me mind-boggled, even though I was only spectating.
But the good thing is that they don’t seem to be buddy-buddy at all...
When I’d been running through possible scenarios in my head, there had been somewhere these two teamed up against me, so this was already going better than I worried it would.
“Wipe them out! Kill all of them other than their leader!”
“Nia Rafdonia!”
But, wait, what was this?
“(Split up and get back down to the village!)”
As soon as Jerome gave the order for an all-out attack, the monsters fled in all directions.
“Commander! The monsters are running away!”
“Chase them down and kill them! Capture their leader at all costs. You can kill it if you have to!”
Wait, was chasing them really a good idea?
Although the question flashed through my mind, it wasn’t like I could do anything to stop the operation. I had no reason to either.
“No one goes off on their own! Stick close to me!” I ordered Squad Four, then hurriedly joined the others in their pursuit.
Of course, I only acted like I was trying to chase the monsters down and didn’t give it my all. I mean, no matter how I looked at it, this was suspicious as hell.
“...Yandel. There’s a possibility that this is a trap.”

“I know. They’re trying to lure us somewhere, I’m sure of it.” There was no way Jerome didn’t know that. However, he probably concluded that either way, he couldn’t let the chief escape. He was also probably confident that even if there was a trap, he would be able to overpower the monsters.
“What are you going to do?” Amelia asked.
I answered without a moment’s hesitation. “We’ll split off from the main unit as naturally as we can.” That was the best way to ensure our survival.
However, it seemed that Amelia didn’t really get my logic, as she spoke again after a few seconds of silence. “...What do you mean? Split off?”
“Exactly what I said. While chasing the monsters, we’ll break away from the rest of the group as organically as possible.”
“And after that?”
“We will escape from this island. As far as they’ll know, we accidentally got separated from the main unit and retreated out of necessity.”
“Do you... really think we can do it?”
I could tell immediately that she wasn’t asking if we’d be able to pull this off. She was asking me if I’d be able to handle the aftermath.
Well, what difference does it make...? Either way, it’s too risky to stick around and keep chasing after them.

Erwen had ended up with short hair before I could figure out how I was going to deal with Jerome, and now that the village chief had appeared, the odds of something big happening had skyrocketed. What, was I supposed to just sit here and wait for whatever it was?
No, this is the best call.
With that, I shook off my self-doubt and hardened my resolve.
This was something that I usually would never do. My hope was that, by acting out of character, I could cause a big enough change that the scene that Parav saw could be avoided.
“The chief! It’s the chief!” I shouted. “The chief went that way! Squad Four, follow me!”
The moment I saw an opportunity, I began to lead Squad Four away from the main group.
“What? But I definitely saw him go that—”
“Are you saying I’m wrong? Follow me!”
The members of Squad Four who didn’t know my plan looked hesitant, but they thankfully still came with me. We quickly put distance between ourselves and the main group.
“Huh? Lord Baron is going that way...”
“But is there anything there?”
“But he said he saw something...”

The members of Squad Three, the group next to us, shot us all looks that clearly said they were confused about what we were doing and how they should react, but they didn’t try to actively stop us. I mean, who in their right mind would imagine that we were going to use this moment to escape with an entire squad?
“He’s heading that way? All forces, change course!”
...Huh?
“All forces, follow Baron Yandel!”
What the hell? Why were they following me?
The moment I thought I’d successfully escaped the main group, they changed direction to head in mine, making our squad the tip of a spear formation.
“Yandel, what do we do?”
“Act as natural as possible for now.”
“...Got it.”
Even if we tried to change directions again here, the main unit would just keep following us.

While I was busy contemplating where my life went wrong, Jerome, who had been moving with Squad One, instantly caught up to me. “Your Lordship! I’ve decided to trust your judgment for now and ordered them to follow you, but did you really see the monster?”
This was checkmate.
What could I say here?
With mounting panic, I pretended not to hear his question and kept running. “The village chief, he was definitely headed in this direction—”
“Your Lordship! It’s him! The creature we’re chasing is over there!”
My mouth snapped shut. I had absolutely no idea how, but suddenly, the village chief appeared directly in front of us, running in the very same direction I was headed in.
“Wait...” Jerome mused. “Were we perhaps chasing after a decoy?”
I didn’t say anything, opting not to disturb the pleasant forest ambiance.
“Hah! If not for you, we would’ve lost him, Baron Yandel! I will not forget the contribution you made here today.”
“...Yeah. Thanks.” I wasn’t sure if I got lucky since this meant I wouldn’t have to come up with an excuse, or if I’d truly screwed myself here.
Whatever the case, we saw the chief stop in front of a tree a short while later and then slip through a gap beneath it.
“There’s a path heading underground!”
It seemed that this was another entrance into the village.
“Count Saintred, what is your plan? There is a good possibility that this is a trap.”
“I know, but we cannot let him go now.”
I sighed. Yeah... Yeah, he was always going to go down. Well, fine. I could just send him down there and keep my eyes peeled for another chance to escape—
“So, Baron Yandel, could you perhaps lead the way?”
“...Even though we don’t know what might be down there?”

“That is why we need your strength more than ever. You were able to withstand the attacks of a rank-one monster by yourself. So long as you can hold them off for a little, our soldiers will be able to catch up and provide you support.”
What Jerome was saying made sense. Of all the members of the expedition group, I was the most durable. Sending me into danger first was the most logical decision a commander could make. However...
Ba-dump!

For some reason, my heart started to thump harder the second the suggestion left his mouth. Simultaneously, snippets of memories I’d collected over the course of the day overlapped each other. Each one of them was a small thing that could easily be ignored on their own, but...
I still need to check.
With that, I met Jerome’s eyes head-on and said, “Sure. I will take the lead.”
“Oho, that’s great! If you refused, I wasn’t sure who I would be able to send instead—”
“But only if you allow me to do something beforehand.”
When I cut him off to throw in a condition, Jerome shut his mouth and stared at me. The look in his eyes seemed to say ‘state your terms.’
“From what I remember,” I began, “one of the items you brought down with you was Misplaced Trust. Is that true?”
“It is...” he said, trailing off to encourage me to continue.
“If you let me use it to confirm a few things, I will gladly take point and lead us in.”
“I’m not sure what you’re trying to verify, but do you have to do it here and now? We don’t know what sort of trap that monster might be laying down there—”
“Then that’s that. I won’t take the lead.”
“Even if I order you to do so with my authority as commander?”
I shrugged in place of an answer.
A moment of silence ensued.
“...Things look weirdly tense between the two of them. I’m not the only one who sees it, right?”
“Fenelin, Karlsten, Tersia. Steel yourselves.”
“S-Steel ourselves?”
“Just do as you’re told.”
The friction between the two of us was palpable even to the bystanders. But after a few more moments of heavy silence, Jerome finally came to a decision.
“Fine. Sir Ebost! Bring Misplaced Trust over here! I don’t know what, but it seems the baron wishes to confirm something!”
As soon as the order was given, the deputy commander approached with the item, and I quickly took it and activated it.
Clack.
I sighed. With that, we were all set. Now, no one within a ten-yard radius could lie.
“Is your name Jerome Saintred?”
“It is.”
I started off with a simple test question before getting down to business. “I will now ask you a question, and all you need to do is answer ‘no.’”
“That’ll be easy. Go on.”
I met his confident gaze and slowly opened my mouth. “Besides today—No, to be more precise, excluding the meeting you had just a few minutes ago...”
The commander was quiet.
“Have you ever met that monster who calls himself Cornelius Bruingrid before?” I asked.
The answer I requested was “no.” However, no matter how long I waited, the response I desperately wanted never came.
As I slowly began to raise my hammer and shield, the silence was finally broken by his low voice, each word enunciated very carefully.
“How did you know?”
...Damn it.
This guy had met the chief before.

chapters.title: Chapter 564: Destination (4)
paragraphs: If Jerome was asking how I’d noticed, the answer was simple.
First, the two of them had been too quick to establish an antagonistic relationship.
“Try it, then. That execution you’re so eager for.”
“Wipe them out! Kill all of them other than their leader!”
We jumped straight into battle after a short exchange, and the village chief had cut and run with the rest of the monsters.
And then, the chase sequence happened.
“He’s heading that way? All forces, change course!”

Oddly enough, as soon as I changed course, the main unit did the same. It was almost as if Jerome had been keeping a close eye on me. Of course, that was only a gut feeling, but even if he just noticed I was running in a different direction by coincidence, that didn’t change the fact that it was odd that he followed me when he thought he had the chief in his sights.
Because if this was the same Jerome who always gave his all to the mission, the guy who just minutes before threatened this so-called “traitor” of a village chief...
Then he wouldn’t have stopped chasing him down until his objective was complete.
...Well, at that point, all I had was a weird feeling about the situation.
The final nail in the coffin was when Jerome made that request of me.
“Could you perhaps take the lead?”

This was the guy who had put my safety above the success of the battle when I collapsed during the fight against the Wolf of Prophecy, Kashan. The same guy who would discard the precious lives of the people under his command for the sake of his mission.
Yet this very same guy was trying to get me to walk into potential danger?
After picking up on the fact that something was quite wrong and going through all the possibilities, I could see only one likely explanation. The issue was that I ended up being right.
“You and your people shouldn’t have had any way of knowing that. It seems there are more rats than expected among these ranks.”

Jerome turned his cold eyes on the soldiers around him. He seemed to believe that the reason I’d managed to clock that something was off was because I had a spy somewhere in his squadron. Well, that would help explain why I tried to run away during the chase, at least.
And by “your people,” he’s probably talking about Raven and Kaislan as well...
My suspicions were now confirmed.

With that, I began to puzzle over what the conversation between the village chief and Jerome could have entailed. It must have taken place on this island when everyone except the night patrol was asleep.

If my hypothesis was correct, those two met up and spoke in secret, and the chief had used the opportunity to make Jerome some sort of an offer. Something that Jerome Saintred had then decided was worth more to him than his mission.
“What was it? What did the village chief promise you that you changed sides overnight?” I demanded outright.
Jerome, however, wasn’t inclined to be forthcoming. “This is where our conversation ends, Your Lordship. Now that I have given you your answer, take the lead and walk underground.”
It wasn’t a request or a suggestion. “I order you as your commander,” he announced.
“And what if I say I don’t want to?” I countered.
“I will take that as willful defiance of a royal decree.”
To be honest, I was kind of stunned. There were close to two hundred witnesses present, and he wasn’t even bothering to hide what he was doing.
He’s confident he can keep this under wraps...

He probably did have plenty of methods for doing so available to him. Money, fame, honor, power... The number of levers the palace could pull was close to infinite, and if he happened to stumble across someone on whom none of those tricks worked, it wouldn’t make much of a difference anyway.
In the end, he would get what he wanted, even if he had to resort to extremes.
I bit my lip, shooting a glance at my companions. They seemed to immediately pick up on my look
“Yandel, don’t waste your time worrying about us. We’re all already ready.” Cold determination laced Amelia’s words as she came forward to stand by my side.
“Even if you don’t want to, you still need to be ready to fight if the situation calls for it. You were the one who told me that, right, Bjorn?”
Even Ainar, with her tanked Aggression, drew her weapon and stepped up behind me.

“I hadn’t expected this to happen so soon...” Versyl admitted. Still, her resolve to take necessary action, no matter the consequences, made itself clear. “But this was always something we’d have to face eventually.”
The one that I was most surprised about, however, was Myul Armin.
“We will fight beside you as well, Lord Baron. It is the only way to repay our debt to you,” he boldly declared, seemingly unconcerned about being branded a traitor to the crown.
“Uhh... w-we... just... I don’t know, so l-let’s try and solve this peacefully first...”
On the other hand, Wyatt Hektz didn’t seem to be nearly as loyal. Although to be fair, that was the reaction any normal person would have had in this situation.
Anyway, those on the palace’s side seemed to waver once they realized they were now going to have to face me as an enemy.
“If what the baron said is true... is the count scheming with that monster...?”
“He probably has his reasons... but is sending the baron into danger like that really the right thing to do?”
“Wasn’t our mission to retrieve the baron and return with him alive? This goes against that objective.”

The achievements I had accrued, my fame as a hero and my position as a noble, and even the favorable reputation I had nurtured among the soldiers... Although those three factors combined weren’t enough to get them to go against their commander, they at least drove a wedge in the party, creating a schism between the members. I could already see it in my mind’s eye. Even if Jerome gave the order to kill me right now, their hesitation would stay their weapons.
Which would be the opening I needed. It was an opening as small as the eye of a needle for now, but from here on out, its size would depend on how I chose to proceed.

“I, Baron Bjorn Yandel, have this to say!” I lowered the shield I had raised defensively and shouted, “As a proud noble who supports the Royal House of Rafdonia, and as a warrior, I swear this on my honor! If it is for the good of the palace, I am not afraid of anything! Even giving my life!”

While shouting, I kept Misplaced Trust clenched firmly in my fist. Every time I spoke, it momentarily stopped ticking, but if I did a good enough job of hiding it, they wouldn’t be able to notice at this distance.

“I am always ready to throw myself into danger for the glorious future of the royal family!” I let out a roar of (false) loyalty and then proceeded to top it off with a final masterstroke. “However! I do not know for sure if this is in service of the palace! Or if you are making the wrong decision while believing you are right!”
My weapon of choice was a type of poison. A poison that would seep into everyone here and lead them down the road to destruction.
“You dare... call my loyalty to the royal family into question?” Jerome seethed.

“How can I not when you aren’t giving me a proper explanation? Explain it so I can understand! Then I—Bjorn, son of Yandel—will go down there immediately! Even if you are only doing it to get rid of me!”
I was going to cling to him like a leech and drag him down with me if I had to.
The silence stretched on as Jerome Saintred stayed quiet, and suspicion began to fester among the other members of the expedition group.
And it seemed he’d noticed as well.
“Speak, Jerome Saintred!” I demanded. “What is down there, and what deal did you make with the village chief?”
He was slow to answer, but indignation lifted his voice into a shout as he said, “...I cannot reveal military secrets to you. However, know this. All of this is for the good of the royal family!”
“I can’t trust that!”
He reared back. “Why not? Isn’t Misplaced Trust active? You know for a fact that everything I have said is the truth—”
“You might just think this is for the good of the royal family and be wrong!”
That shut him up again.

All right. Judging by the look on his face, he’d probably start spilling some information if I kept pushing. If I could get in one more decisive rebuttal, swaying public opinion to my side here might not be impossible.
“Then speak! Explain how sending me down there is for the sake of the royal family!”
Operating under that logic, I put my loyalty on full display with another shout.
However, out of nowhere, I heard a voice in my head.
[...You’re wrong. Opposing him here will only lead to a worse outcome.]
It was a gentle voice threaded with a sigh.
[You could have run away immediately. Why did you have to make everything so difficult...?]
Flash!
Just as I was wondering whose voice it was, a flash of silver blinded me and the world went dark.
[Bystander of Destiny has intervened.]
[With Sven Parav’s Stigma as a medium, Star’s Authority has been cast on you.]

[The Mark of the Star has been engraved deep into your skin. Your Divine Resistance stat has permanently increased by +100. All healing and positive effects cast on you by those under the authority of the Reatlas Church are reduced by half.]
[Be warned. If you are bestowed the power of a god one more time, your fragile mortal body will disintegrate...]
When I came to, I was still standing in the same place. No, to be more accurate, I was somehow staring at myself standing in the same place from a short distance away.
“Then speak! Explain how sending me down there is for the sake of the royal family!”
I was still shouting in Jerome’s face, which flushed red like a hot kettle.
What the hell...?
For some reason, I was watching this unfold from a third-person perspective.
Watch closely. You will find the answers you seek. The voice I heard earlier spoke to me in my ear again the moment I asked myself what was going on.
My mind whirred, growing foggy. It felt like I was drunk. Maybe that was why? Somehow, the question faded from my mind until only the thought of following the voice’s suggestion remained.
“Why can’t you answer me? Maybe it’s because you already know it too! That what you are trying to do here isn’t for the good of the royal family at all!”
The longer I watched the scene play out, the worse the situation became.
I didn’t stop talking, and the commander finally ended up snapping.
“How long do you plan on spitting in the face of the palace? You traitor!”
“Hah! Traitor! I am not going against the command of the king. I am only questioning your judgment—”
“Hah! Do you really think I don’t know? You’re nothing but a traitor acting like Bjorn, son of Yandel!”
“...What?”

When Jerome said that, the eyes of the other me went wide with surprise. Since this was my own face I was reading, it wasn’t difficult for me to figure out what I was thinking. I was probably scared that my identity as an evil spirit had been revealed.
“I was suspicious of you from the moment we met, but I’ve become certain since arriving on this island. You are the man who operated under the name of Iron Mask decades ago in Noark.”

“You must’ve been ordered by Noark to become a spy, posing as a barbarian who just recently came of age to infiltrate Rafdonia. I bet that during those two years and six months, you disappeared for that ‘special mission’ of yours, you simply returned home.”
“Uhhh...”
“Yet still, you stand there and dare to speak lies about the palace? I don’t know how you’re suppressing the effects of Misplaced Trust...”
“Suppressing? I’m not—”
“Then hold it so we can see it! There, look! It stops every time you talk!”
It was game over from there.

“If this means handing over a traitor like you and bringing prosperity to the palace, then I would do it a hundred times—no, a thousand times over. What are you all doing? Arrest this wicked traitor! If anyone tries to help him, treat them as traitors as well and kill them! I, Jerome Saintred, will take full responsibility for whatever happens here!”
The lies I was spreading through Misplaced Trust had been clocked, and before I could give anything resembling a proper explanation, Jerome immediately gave the order to attack.
“Everyone, get behind me!”
With the Hektz Clan and Armin Adventurer Group now out of the picture, the members of Clan Anabada readied themselves to take a final stand as time stuttered to a stop.
“What happens after this...?” I breathed, the words leaving my mouth unbidden.
That mysterious voice answered me again. Three of your precious companions die. And then things progress to the future I showed that child.

Only then did I finally realize whose voice this was. This was the Goddess of the Stars, who oversaw fate—Reatlas. I was an atheist communing with a real god in a faraway world, but this revelation didn’t have as much of a spiritual impact as I thought it might. There was only one thing that mattered right now.
“Then what should I have done? It was obvious that he was trying to set me up. Should I have just gone down there like he ordered without arguing?”
I wanted an answer. Just as other people looked to god when they were driven into a corner, I sought an answer from this god.
I told you. Watch until the end.
With that, time in the frozen world began to move backward.

chapters.title: Chapter 565: Destination (5)
paragraphs: Suddenly, time stopped rewinding.
“Could you perhaps lead the way?”
We were once again at the moment when Jerome asked me to go ahead of the rest of the troops.
“All right, but any items or essences we find from here on out, give me priority pick for four of them.”
“Four... Understood. That much can certainly be spared for you, Your Lordship.”
After a brief negotiation, I slid under the tree that the village chief had disappeared off into. I didn’t understand. How could I just go down there without giving it a second thought?
This was the fate I showed that child. In this timeline, I hadn’t delivered that prophecy. That is why you went down there without suspecting a thing. It was the voice again.
Ah...

That answered my questions. The prophecy had played a major role in my suspicion of Jerome. Because of it, I had already known that something bad was going to happen, so I had taken special care to keep an eye on everything going on around me with an almost obsessive attention to detail.
Fwoong!
Once I vanished down into the tree, the world went black in a blink before the scene changed.
We don’t have much time, so I’ll just show you the important parts.
We were now in some sort of cave. At its center was a portal stone, and I was slumped beside it, knocked unconscious. As I watched, the village chief approached me and began a strange ritual.

This place is hidden under the basement you saw last time you were here. After going down to the village, you fought long and hard against hundreds of enemies while waiting for reinforcements, but no one came. In the end, your exhaustion won out, and you were captured and dragged here.
So there’d been another space under that corpse-filled cellar. I didn’t expect something like this to be hidden there. I’d had to act fast back then, so I didn’t have time to get a good look around.
So what happens to me now? I thought.
Keep watching. It will be over soon, came the voice of the goddess.
Two times, three times, four times—time accelerated as if someone was pressing a fast-forward button. When the flow of time returned to normal, black smoke was billowing from the chief’s body.
Shaaaaaa!
The smoke slowly funneled into my unconscious form, and soon enough, the chief collapsed.
And then, my body opened its eyes. I watched as “I” got up and flexed my hands a little before my mouth opened to let out an unfamiliar voice.
“Finally...”
The scene changed once more. We weren’t in the village anymore, but at the center of the island in a dark labyrinth of trees. There, “I” was having a private conversation with Jerome Saintred.

“Now give me the item as agreed,” Jerome was demanding. “Or are you having second thoughts after coming all this way? If so, I suggest you rethink immediately. If you don’t, you’ll find it hard to have any sort of life out in the city, even with your new body.”
“It’s true... The palace does have the power to make my life quite difficult.”
“In that case—”
“So wouldn’t it be best if they don’t find out about what happened here at all?”
“What? You can’t be—!”
“Dead men don’t tell tales.”
The conversation ended there.
When the scene changed again, the first thing I saw was blood spattering everywhere.
“Ack!”
It was a battlefield. We were surrounded on all sides by hundreds of monsters, and while the expedition group was fighting back with everything they had, they were being overpowered.
It was all because of the village chief, who had taken over my body.
“I-I didn’t expect him to be this strong...”
“The baron...! Kill Baron Yandel!”

The village chief didn’t care about protecting anyone, not even the monsters dying around him. So the barbarian character I had painstakingly built to shield my allies was instead wielded as a war chariot, trampling across the battlefield.
Soon enough, there was no doubt who would emerge victorious.
“I” charged through the troops toward the rear, leaving a trail of bodies behind me as I massacred the members of the expedition group.
But then, just as I went to slam my hammer down on the head of a certain wizard, I suddenly froze.
