With a glance around the empty Round Table, Auril Gavis muttered, “I spent a lot of time preparing for this, so this is a tad disappointing. There are already only three left.” Yet rather than upset, the sense that I got was that he was more surprised than anything.
Well, I could understand how he felt. I also hadn’t expected things to pan out this way.
I didn’t think they would be willing to give up such a precious ticket home like that.

Losing your anonymity and having your real identity revealed? In this world where evil spirits were executed on the spot, that was an incredibly dangerous prospect. However, none of that mattered if you were the one who got to go home at the end. I had assumed this would turn into a game of chicken.

However, Clown and Black had disappeared before Auril Gavis had so much as mentioned the quiz, Butterfly had dropped out pretty early on, and Fox had decided that she didn’t mind living in this world and withdrew accordingly. Four people had left before the game could even really get started...
“Then let’s continue.”
And when Auril Gavis went to start the next round, Goblin carefully raised his hand as well. “I... I also want to stop here...”
This was already our third forfeit after Butterfly and Fox.
Auril Gavis clicked his tongue. “Is that so? Then leave.”
“Are you not going to ask me why...? That’s... Well, I-I’m not saying you have to... I’m just wondering...”
“...So, what’s your reason? Did you perhaps have a change of heart after hearing Ms. Fox’s speech?”
“Uh... that... I can’t say that wasn’t a factor, but...”
“But?”
“It’s... I’m not sure how to say this...”
“I don’t care, so go on and say it,” Auril Gavis snapped.
Goblin averted his eyes. “Something about this just feels off to me,” he mumbled.
Hmm, Goblin’s gut instincts are incredibly reliable.
That was my immediate thought the second the words left his mouth, but Auril Gavis didn’t seem to be on the same wavelength.
“I see. Well, now that you’ve informed me of your reasons, leave. Ah, do you also need time to say farewell?”
“Ah, yes... I just need a moment...”
With that, Goblin turned to the rest of us.

“In the past, a friend I met at a language class told me that even brushing past another person on the street was a connection formed. By that logic, being dragged into a strange world and meeting you all with masks on definitely wasn’t a normal way to form a relationship. S-Some of you probably even know who I am out there.”
At its core, what he was trying to say was very simple, even if he was using a lot of words to say it.
“So, even if some of you might have the opportunity to kill me in the future. When that time comes, please don’t. Aren’t we all players here?”
Seriously, Goblin?
“...Is that all?”
“Huh? Ah, yes... That’s all I wanted to say.”
“Then leave.”
“Oh... Right... Well then, everybody...”
Once Goblin was gone, Queen and Wolf glanced at each other with awkward looks on their faces. Somehow, we had our two finalists after only two rounds.
So are they going to duke it out to the end now?
Yet, the situation continued to unfold in a direction I never would have expected.
“I’m going to stop now too.”
For the first time, Auril Gavis let his true feelings show. Forget displeasure—his tone bordered on fury.
Not that I could blame him, exactly. He had apparently done a lot of work to get this quiz show ready, but it wasn’t going his way at all.
“It’s quite simple. I can’t trust you.”
“Distrust... I’m saying I have the ability to send you home.”

“Yes, you may very well be capable of that. In fact, I think there’s a high probability that you do have the power to do so. However, I still can’t trust you.” Queen glanced at Wolf and asked, “You two are quite friendly, aren’t you?”
It seemed that Queen suspected Auril Gavis of using everyone’s dreams of going back home as bait that he could use to throw us deeper into despair later.

“I have no way of knowing whether you might have designed this game so that Mr. Wolf would end up the winner in the end. Also, for me to win the game at this stage, Mr. Wolf would need to give up, but I don’t think he’ll do so willingly.”
Her decision was rooted in sound logic. However, it was clear that she had also been influenced by how quickly the others had dropped out, not just by her distrust in Auril.
“I don’t need to say any goodbyes. I’ll be leaving.”
With that, Queen left without another word, and the champion of the quiz game was decided in quite an anticlimactic way.
Wolf was the proud winner of an incredible reward. In apparent disbelief, he sat in a daze for a moment before snapping out of it. “Lord Gavis, then... does that mean I can go home now?”
Was this guy incapable of reading the room?
I wasn’t sure, but thanks to him, I got to see something incredibly entertaining.
“Of course. A promise is a promise.”
“Th-thank you...! I, truly, thank—”
“So can you shut up for a moment?”
He’d looked so excited when he pitched his quiz show to us.
He’s pissed. He’s so pissed.
What a beautiful sight.
Belatedly picking up on the mood, Wolf quickly shut his mouth, and a heavy silence descended on the room. However, it seemed his recent victory had given Wolf some courage.
“So then... when...? When can I receive the... reward...?” Wolf once more asked Auril Gavis about his prize.
“I will come look for you when the time comes.” His voice was tight with frustration and annoyance. “So can you leave the room?”
Wolf quickly bowed. “Of course... Then I will be waiting for you outside, Lord Gavis.” With that, Wolf left as well, and the two of us were finally alone at the Round Table.

Having quietly watched all of that unfold, I opened my mouth for the first time since Auril Gavis showed his face. “Are you really going to send him back?” I asked, trying to signal that he could speak freely now that it was just us two.
However, there was no way this shady old man would ever give me a straight answer. “Hmm, what do you think?”
“Well, to be honest, I don’t get the sense he’ll be getting the happy ending he’s after.”
“You have no trust in my character.”
What a baffling thing to say. If he wanted my trust, then he should’ve acted trustworthy to begin with.
“But more importantly, this is quite the shame,” Auril Gavis sighed. “If the game went on for one or two more rounds, you would’ve gotten some very interesting entertainment.”
“Interesting entertainment? You have peculiar tastes.”
“I will not refute that... but are you really one to talk here?”
Well, I couldn’t refute that either. When I wore this mask, I wasn’t all that different from this old man.
“So,” I asked bluntly, “why did you do all this?”
That whole excuse about making up for taking off their masks was a total lie, obviously, but I still couldn’t figure out why he’d prepared this whole quiz. What was the point?
“Trust is the same as gambling. You can only hope that the other person bets as much as you do.”
“Okay, and?”
“I wanted to show you something before I talked to you. However... now that things have turned out this way, it’d be ridiculous to try and explain it to you with words.”
“You have a knack for going on and on when all you really mean is that you’re not going to tell me.”
“Haha, then perhaps your talent lies in making things sound very simple after the fact.”

The old man was apparently determined to butt heads with me at every turn. The more I talked to him, the more pathetic he became, but the Confucian value of respecting my elders had been drilled into me since childhood, so I bit my tongue.
Well, there was that, and the fact that this was our first meeting in a long time. I couldn’t waste this opportunity.
“Whatever. I have a question.”
“A question?” he echoed. “Go on.”
“How did you figure me out?”
It was a question I had been waiting to ask the second we were alone. He hadn’t even made an effort to hide it earlier.
“After all, you practically founded this place, no?”
That was one of the first things the old man had said to me as soon as he entered the Round Table today. In other words, he somehow knew that Lion was the Nivelles Enze he met twenty years ago.
No, actually, it seems like he also knows that I’m Bjorn Yandel too.
In any case, before we officially got down to business, I needed to find out just how much this old man knew about me.
“Say, why does the way you speak to me change every time we meet?”
“What? Do you want me to start calling you ‘sir’ after all this time?”
I was smirking as I said it, but Auril Gavis actually seemed receptive to the idea. “Uh... could you? Now that everyone is gone, you don’t need to act like Lion anymore...”
So it seemed he’d been bothered by the rude way I’d been addressing him this whole time.
“Well, that’s fine. I can do that. It’s not that big of an ask. In any case, what’s your answer to my question? Or is that a secret too?”

“Ah, you asked how I figured out who you are, right? The answer is simple. I waited and waited for twenty years to pass. With the information I had, it was quite easy to figure out that you were Bjorn Yandel from there.”
Hmm, I see.
I could accept that logic, except for one discrepancy.
“But there’s one thing that doesn’t make sense about that. If that’s the case, why didn’t you recognize me right away when you saw me for the first time here at the Round Table?”
“Ah, in your mind, you hadn’t met me yet. I decided that it would be better for me to wait until the time was right.”
“And that time is now?”
“Something like that. Up to this point, I’ve been trying to avoid potential encounters with you... but there is something I wanted to ascertain as soon as possible.”
Right, now that I thought about it, he did say he was here to ask me something.
“Then please, go ahead. What is it that you’re wondering?” I asked with the even, agreeable tone of someone who would answer whatever questions he had.
The old man took the opportunity he was given.
“I believe you once mentioned here at the Round Table that you met with the Witch, correct?”
“Yes. So?”
“I want to hear more about where and how you met her.”
Was I having déjà vu? That was the exact same question Wolf had asked me earlier.
Ah, did he come here to ask me himself since I didn’t answer the first time?

Hmm, that seemed to be the most plausible explanation. This meant that this particular piece of information was important enough to the old man that he’d been willing to alter his original plan for it, meaning...
Don’t I have the upper hand right now?

The moment I realized that, I felt myself lean back in my chair arrogantly, my legs crossed. The instinctive reaction of a K-Barbarian who had caught on to the fact that he was in an advantageous position.
Auril Gavis seemed wary of the change in my posture, but he didn’t say anything about it out loud.
All right, so you’re willing to overlook at least that much?
Tap, tap.
Soon, the O and X paddles that had been left on the table caught my eye—the ones the old man had created with a single wave of his hands.
Come to think of it, he did say he recovered all of his powers, right?
With that, I licked my lips and made a request of my own. “Ah, sir? I’m a bit thirsty, so could you pour me a cup of soda?”
“Ah, and please make sure not to skimp out on the ice.”

chapters.title: Chapter 578: Return (4)
paragraphs: A proper ice to liquid ratio truly elevated a glass of soda to a whole new level of refreshing.
I swirled the cup a little to cool it down before chugging it all in one go. After all, the taste would end up watered down if I let the ice melt, right?

Yeah, that was the stuff. I’d missed this taste so much. Most things about this world were tolerable, but it didn’t have any soft drinks. I could get a ghost of that bubbly sensation in its beer, but even that was entirely different from the modern carbonation I craved.
...Should I go back?

The taste was enough to reignite my desire to go home, which had all but faded away. Someone should let Baekho know. In the time he spent cooking up that scheme with the Stone of Revival or whatever, he could’ve just given me a few cups of soda and I would’ve seriously reconsidered returning to the real world.
“Sir, please pour me another one.”
After downing one cup, I ordered myself a refill. However, I didn’t chug it this time, instead savoring the flavor.
“You... look really happy for some reason.”
Wow, way to sour the mood. I was the type of person to immediately get annoyed when people said stuff like that to me.
“All right, then do tell me,” Auril Gavis said after giving me some more time to enjoy my drink. “How did you meet her?”
“Ah, the Witch?”
“Yes. I truly can’t understand. No matter how I look at it, you were never in a position to have met with her...”
Hmm. “Why are you so sure about that, sir?” I said, narrowing my eyes.
He went quiet again, his own eyes darting away as he racked his brain for an excuse.
To be honest, it was disturbing. Had he really been watching my every move? This entire time? Just... how?

The old man opted to dodge my question. “Well, timeline-wise, I’m sure that you didn’t meet her on Basement Floor One. And from what I can remember, you were very busy before then—between establishing your clan and the Magic Tower and whatnot. Didn’t you also defeat two Lords of the Floor in that time?”

Well, it was true that I’d been busy back then. On top of everything else I needed to take care of, I’d also had to deal with Count Alminus’s charges against me. But that didn’t mean I bought his weak excuses.

“Oh, you’ve already drank it all. Give it here. I’ll pour you another one.” He quickly took my cup back to refill it again. Although it might sound strange, in a sense, this old man was pretty predictable in some ways. He was able to tell when he had the upper or lower hand in a given situation and always adjusted accordingly.
“Sir, even if you do that, I can’t answer you for free. I want something out of this too.”
As I set my terms, fury lit his expression, plain as day since he’d gotten rid of his mask as soon as we were alone. “Free?! What do you mean? Am I not giving you all of these drinks?”
“Yes, and I’m grateful for that.”
“When someone is genuinely grateful—”
Hey, don’t push it.
“If everything could be solved with soda, why would we have money and mana stones?” I asked mockingly. “In your world, wouldn’t giving someone a drink solve everything?”
His expression hardened. “Every time we meet, I’m once again reminded that you have a talent for pissing people off.”

The air in the room plummeted several degrees as the man who went around smiling like a friendly neighborhood grandpa did a sudden heel turn. But so what? This wasn’t my first rodeo, and at this point, I felt like I had a good sense of what made this guy tick.
“Don’t pretend you’re mad. It won’t work,” I said, brushing his anger off like it was nothing.
His expression smoothed out, returning to normal like he’d never been glaring at me to begin with. “Haha, you’re not an easy customer. So... what do you want from me?”
Since the stick wouldn’t work, he could only use the carrot.
“There must be something you’re after,” he hedged. “Isn’t that why you’re doing all this?”

To be honest, there wasn’t anything in particular. Or, rather, I had so many things I wanted to ask him that I was having a hard time narrowing down which one to choose. I needed to rank them by priority level.
I could ask him what he’s up to, but that would be too broad.
In the end, I settled on a more focused question.
“Why are you trying to shut down Ghost Busters?” I asked, honing in on his motives for his latest move.
“Hmm, do I just answer you? There’s no gem here to help you discern truth from lies anymore.”

His tone implied he would immediately make another gem if I asked him to, but I declined. “It’s fine, so just answer me. And it’s not like I’d be able to trust you 100 percent anyway, even with the gem.”
“So you’ll be deciding yourself whether what I say is the truth.”
“Yes, so please give me a proper answer. If you lie here and get caught, it’ll be your loss.”
“My loss?”
“Because I won’t believe a thing you say in the future.”
That might sound childish, but it would make a decent threat. If this old man wanted to pull my strings, he needed to maintain a friendly enough relationship with me to get close to them.
But why was this old man leering at me like that instead of saying anything?
“What is it?” I prompted. “Do you have something to say about that?”
“No.”
“If not, then why haven’t you started talking?”
As I shot him a look telling him to stop screwing around, Auril Gavis finally spoke. “It’s just that it’s quite admirable. Your outlook toward trust, that is.”
What the hell was he going on about now?
The old man continued, ignoring my obvious bafflement. “If someone betrays you, you make sure to punish them yourself. That is what trust means to you.”
Wasn’t everyone like that? What, were there people out there who got backstabbed and just laughed it off after?
Despite the questions running through my mind, I held my tongue and listened.
“Just like stricter laws reduce crime, your trust or lack thereof also acts as a deterrent which—”

Yeah, never mind, I couldn’t sit here and listen to this guy prattle on. He was trying to make it seem like I was a control freak who couldn’t trust anyone unless I had the upper hand over them at all times.
“Sir,” I asked him directly, “are you perhaps not right in the head? How did you jump to a conclusion like that from the question I asked?”
“Remember, you were the one who turned on me first. How could I trust anything about you after that?”
“Then are your companions different?”
Obviously.
...was the answer I tried to give, but for some reason, I couldn’t bring myself to say it. The old man’s words rang in my ears.
“If someone betrays you, you make sure to punish them yourself.”
Punishment. Maybe that was what I was doing to Missha. Regardless, I changed the subject.
“Let’s move on. Just answer the question I asked you. Why are you trying to close down the server?”
“If I answer you, will you answer me as well?”
“I’ll think about it,” I replied without missing a beat, “if the information you give me is worthwhile.”
In other words, I was ready to ditch him at any moment. Auril Gavis would no doubt be able to read between the lines and realize my response was vague and promised nothing.
“Sure. Then decide after hearing what I have to say.”
Despite that, he accepted my terms without argument.
“Wow, sir. You’re being pretty easygoing today,” I remarked.
“...Could you stop with the sudden tone shifts? It feels like you’re treating me like a child.”
“Oh, don’t mind me.” With a benevolent smile, I asked, “So, the answer?”
He let out a sigh. “The reason I’m shutting Ghost Busters down is simple. This place isn’t having a positive effect on the players. It isn’t doing what I intended it to do.”
“A positive effect?”
“This place is no different than a safe haven for the players. They get to talk about the homes they left behind and share their loneliness with people in the same situation as them.”
“And that’s bad how?”
“It’s a problem. People who are satisfied with the status quo are bound to settle for it.”

“Ah...” I sort of got what he was trying to say. Honestly, just a glance at the community bulletin board backed up his claim. There were plenty of posts on there talking about rent, getting married, or even having children here.
“Our friends from earlier are the same. Just a few years ago, they never would have given up an opportunity like this.”
So the old man was still sour about how bad his quiz show went. Well, fair enough.
“So you’re getting rid of it? Because if the server stays up, they won’t worry about going home?”
“Something like that.”
That meant he was definitely holding back a lot more information.
“There, how about it? Was that enough?” he asked.
“No. I would’ve answered your question if you gave me some big secret, but I’ve concluded that the quality of your information is too low for me to exchange my information about the Witch.”

Basically, I was going to dine and dash. However, unexpectedly, Auril Gavis took the news in stride, his expression serene. It was like the conversation could end right there and he’d have nothing to lose either way. Was he putting on an act to maintain his mask of control?

In the end, I was the first to break. I couldn’t leave without getting anything out of this, not when I had been granted the rare opportunity to sit down with him. “So... can’t you just leave the community be? I’ll give you information about the Witch if you do.”
In truth, I wasn’t saying that out of a genuine interest in preserving Ghost Busters. I was just curious how he’d respond to—
“That’s not possible, I’m afraid.”

Yeah, so he refused. Which meant that closing the community was of a higher priority to him than learning more about the Witch. But why? No matter how I looked at it, players getting complacent couldn’t be the only reason.
He chose to wrap this up. “Then it seems our meeting today has reached its end.”
“I guess so. It’s not like you’re going to give me more information even if I ask, right?”
“Haha, you need to trust in others more.”
“I do. But only the ones who deserve it.”
With those empty words, our conversation came to a natural stopping point.
“Then I’ll be going now,” he announced. “I have something else I need to do before the community closes its doors, but I will be seeing you later.”
“Right. I don’t know when that’ll be, but I hope you’ll be willing to tell me everything going on inside your head when the time comes,” I offered.
“That’s an odd way to look at it. I’d tell you everything right now if you were willing to trust what I say.”
Every word was a lie.
I scoffed at his nonsense, and Auril Gavis let out a laugh. Apparently, he expected that reaction. “I’m not sure if you’ll believe me, but I’ll offer you one last piece of advice.”
“Advice? I’ll hear you out, so go ahead.”
“Baekho Lee.”
“Don’t get too close to that friend of yours.” The advice genuinely blindsided me, but I didn’t get the chance to ask what the hell he meant. “That is all. I’ll be seeing you in the future.”
With that, Auril Gavis left the Round Table.
I stared vacantly at the spot where he’d been standing, then quickly shook myself out of my daze. A sudden possibility had crossed my mind.
Baekho Lee...
Maybe...
I wasn’t sure, but maybe...

Was he the reason that Auril Gavis had chosen to shut down Ghost Busters? In the same way someone might burn down a house to kill a spider, maybe he had destroyed the server to ensure Baekho Lee and I couldn’t communicate anymore.
Well, that was only a theory.
“You old crook. You didn’t say a single thing straight,” I grumbled, then let out a sigh that echoed inside the empty room.
On its heels was a sudden silence.
Vacant chairs surrounded the Round Table, now deprived of its gem.
It really does feel like the end of an era.
Even knowing that I needed to leave and get back to business, I couldn’t quite bring myself to move. Somehow, despite myself, I was still in disbelief.
Deer and Crescent had left after the first round, and with Auril Gavis’s sudden arrival, the rest followed suit one after another.
Tap.
I picked up the Lion mask I had taken off to drink my soda and slid it on my face again. This was probably the last time I would ever wear it.
I had grown fond of it.
“This is really the end...”

The words were slow to leave my tongue, and even once they were out, they couldn’t quite fill the empty room. I wasn’t expecting a joyful and friendly goodbye like a high school graduation or anything, but I never thought it would end like this.
Maybe that was why?
“However, I cannot seem to feel any gratitude toward you.”
“Do you think this is a game? Do you?”
For some reason, their words echoed through my mind.
I quickly shook my head to clear it.
Don’t think about that. It’s not like we came here to make friends.
I smiled ruefully and set the mask on the table before glancing around the empty room one last time.
“...No. Not fun at all.”
And with that, the final meeting of the Round Table came to a close.
After witnessing the end of the Round Table, I returned to Hansu Lee’s room. I lay on the bed and vegetated for a bit before steeling myself enough to get up and check my inbox.
I have a message...
Despite what I was hoping, though, it wasn’t from the GM.
[From: HS123]
HS123—the message was from Hyeonbyeol.
I guess we weren’t able to say a proper goodbye thanks to Baekho.
What was inside? As I opened it with a click, the text popped up on my screen.

[Before when I asked you about revealing our identities to each other, I know that you put your foot down, but I’ve decided I’m going to start doing whatever I please like you do. The admins might be able to look through our inboxes, so I can’t tell you who I am in this message, but...]
The heart of her message lay in the last line.
[Find me outside.]
Outside...
Well, if I was going to do that, I’d need to get out of the labyrinth first.

chapters.title: Chapter 579: Return (5)
paragraphs: Ghost Busters.
After popping into existence more than twenty years ago, this space became a safe haven for many a homesick player. Its final moments were just as abrupt as its first.
[Urgent Notice: The server will soon shut down.]
An error could occur if you are forcibly disconnected, so if any users are still logged in, please log out as soon as possible.
The notification appeared about five minutes after I opened Hyeonbyeol’s message.

When I refreshed the page, my feed was already littered with people preparing for the end times. From posts questioning why the server was shutting down early when there was still time left, to people looking for reassurance from others, to troll posts the likes of which I usually didn’t see thanks to the good moderation system.
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
I clicked on the post, curious about what this urgent question could possibly be, but it was nothing interesting.
[Very Urgent. Please respond.]
What happens if you don’t log out and stay here instead?
I sighed. I figured that would be it. Still, I was a little intrigued about that myself, so I scrolled down to the comments section.
these99: What do you think will happen? You’ll probably be logged out.
└OP: really? then I’m just going to wait here until I’m automatically logged out.

└fliccolo: didn’t you see the part where the admins said there could be an error? just press the log-out button yourself. If something does go wrong, you might live the rest of your life as a vegetable.

It was quite the frightening prospect—not logging out at the proper time and ending up brain-dead as a result. Of course, there was a question of whether or not that could even happen, but given the strange nature of this space, I’d say there was a non-zero chance that it could.
Plus, the wording of the GM’s message about an “error” that “could occur” kind of makes me nervous too.
Even without all that, though, there was no point in staying here until the end, so after reading a few more posts, I pressed the log-out button.
[Do you wish to log out?]
A selection window with the words “yes” and “no” greeted me, just like the one that appeared the day I first entered this world.
Click, click.
When I clicked yes, the room around me faded to black, and I could feel myself being transported somewhere else.
It was time to go back. Not to being the mysterious powerhouse Lion, or the ordinary office worker Hansu Lee...
“You’re here six seconds earlier than usual. Did something happen in there?”
But to being Bjorn Yandel.

Come to think of it, when did this start, again? At some point, Amelia began posting up next to my bedside whenever I went to Ghost Busters for the night. I’d told her multiple times that there was no need for her to do that, but I soon gave up arguing with her once I realized she would always be there when I opened my eyes no matter what I said.
And, to be honest, I couldn’t say that I wasn’t grateful.
“Didn’t you say you were going to go to bed? Are you lying to me now?” I probed.
“I did mean to.”
“But?”
“I couldn’t sleep.”
Couldn’t sleep, my ass. Even as I flashed her a smirk, Amelia continued to make excuses for herself. “...And you never know what might happen inside the labyrinth.”
Well, I couldn’t argue with that.
Amelia handed me a cup of water as I sat up. “So, did something happen?” she asked.
“The community has closed as of today.”
“Closed...?”

After gulping down the cold water, I gave her a more detailed breakdown of my night. I told her about the notice I saw as soon as I connected to the server and even the information I got from the Round Table related to the shutdown.
“Hmm, so Auril Gavis is involved...”
“His official reason is that he wants to stop us evil spirits from getting complacent, but there’s no way that is the whole truth. How about it? Do you have any theories?”
“Not really... I’ll tell you if I think of something, though.”
Hmm, so she didn’t have any ideas either.
I mean, I supposed that was to be expected considering she hadn’t actually had a proper conversation with Auril Gavis before.
“So, Yandel,” Amelia said, interrupting my thoughts. Her voice had taken on a tone I couldn’t quite place. “What else happened in there?”
“You wouldn’t have that look on your face if it were just that.”
I tilted my head. “A look on my face...?”
Carefully, Amelia said, “I might just be imagining things, but...”
“You don’t have to beat around the bush with me. Just give it to me straight.”
“You look like you went through something. Like you’re torn up inside.”
Ah...
“Did something else happen in there?” she asked.
I let out a sigh. I really couldn’t hide anything from her.
What should I do? Do I tell her or not?

I took a moment to think it over, but in the end, I told her everything. It wasn’t something I felt the need to hide anyway... and it was hard for me to lie to her when she was looking at me with those earnest eyes.
“Oh... so that’s what it was.”

It didn’t take long to get through the whole story. I did my best to eliminate my personal biases and only give her an objective summary of the events as they happened, yet despite my barebones description, Amelia could immediately tell what was bothering me. No, I’d even wager that she knew me better than I knew myself.
“Right now, you’re conflicted over whether or not you have the right to be angry at Missha Karlstein.”

Amelia had in one sentence summed up my entire emotional state, something that even I couldn’t fully wrap my head around. It felt like I’d been turned inside out, my heart exposed. Which was perhaps why I found myself responding without thinking.
“It’s not as simple as that. It’s not even just about Missha in the first place. It’s a complicated situation when you take everyone else into account—”
“But Missha Karlstein is the core of the problem.” I went quiet. “Am I wrong?”
I had nothing to say to that, so I stayed silent, and Amelia calmly continued.
“Could I hear what happened that day?”
I didn’t need to ask which day she was talking about. She meant the day I told her nothing happened. The day Missha stopped talking to everyone and started to sit in the corner alone.
...Where do I start?
After thinking it through, I decided to start from the very beginning.
“Do you know anything about the Stone of Revival?”
To explain my issue with Missha, I needed to explain that first. I hadn’t told any of my companions about its presence in our party yet.
“I know a bit,” she replied.
“Well, before Missha Karlstein returned to our clan, she apparently received a Stone of Revival from Baekho Lee. When I found out, I went to ask her about it.”
“And?”
“I asked her if she knew that the person the Stone of Revival is used on loses their memories, and she answered that no, she didn’t. I then told her I understood and asked her to leave.”
“So... what happened after that?”

I let out a sigh. “Missha didn’t leave. She wanted me to say something, even getting angry at her would be fine. So I told her the honest truth.” I paused, and when Amelia didn’t interrupt, I finally admitted, “That I couldn’t... trust her anymore. The first question that popped into my mind once she was done explaining was whether she was hiding anything else from me.”
There was a brief beat of silence.
“...And then?” she prompted.
“That’s it.”
Missha Karlstein had left the room without another word, and we hadn’t spoken since. That was the end of the story.

“I see.” Now that she had all the facts, Amelia went quiet, digesting my tale. But when she finally spoke, the question that came out of her mouth was one I never would have expected. “Why did you hide everything that happened with Missha Karlstein from us?”
Well... now that I thought about it, I wasn’t sure. Why had I? Why hadn’t I told Amelia about the Stone of Revival sooner?
Part of me wanted to plead ignorance and dodge the question, but in truth, I did know the answer.
“...Because I knew she would be shunned.”

Missha’s position in our clan was already shaky. Erwen’s interactions with her were colored by obvious displeasure, and Versyl had pinned her as a potential traitor and was thus wary of her. After two years of absence, her once-close friendship with Ainar had faded and, in the end, she was practically treated as an outsider by the rest of the clan. It was obvious what would happen to her if Baekho Lee’s orders were revealed on top of all that.
She would be even more of an outcast.
That sequence of events might end with her leaving the clan of her own volition, and...
I couldn’t help but laugh at my train of thought.
Just what do I want here?
I was getting even more confused about my own state of mind.

Amelia, meanwhile, nodded in apparent understanding. “I see. So that’s why you can’t bring yourself to use Misplaced Trust on Missha... Because you suspect she might be hiding something more from you.”
She had hit the nail right on the head.

Maybe it was paradoxical, but I couldn’t find it in me to use Misplaced Trust on Missha because I couldn’t trust her. It was like Schrodinger’s Cat. The moment the box was opened, its contents would be set in stone and there would be no turning back. That was why I was leaving the lid alone for now.
Taking note of my pitiful state, Amelia said, “That’s so like you.”
My first instinct was that that sounded a lot like an insult, but Amelia’s eyes were warm.

“Bjorn Yandel, when the day breaks, take Misplaced Trust and go to Missha Karlstein to see if she’s hiding anything else from you. And if she says she’s not, treat her as a companion, just as you did in the past.”
“And if she is hiding something else?”
“Well, we’ll cross that bridge when we get to it.”
“Isn’t that... a little irresponsible?”
“But you know as well as I do that we can’t keep putting this off forever.”
Well, that was true. I let out a frustrated sigh.
“Even if you don’t want to, do what needs to be done,” Amelia consoled. “Just like you always do, Bjorn Yandel.”
Like I always do...
When she pictured Bjorn Yandel in her mind, what did she see?
The thought made me contemplate what I saw in her in turn.
“...Why are you looking at me like that?”
“You just seem more mature than usual.”
This was the unfiltered truth, straight from the heart.
“Eh...?” For some reason, though, Amelia flinched like I just hit her over the head with my hammer. She then heaved a sigh. “I’ll choose to take that as a compliment.”
Uh... was there another way to take it?

I went back to bed, and when I awoke the next morning, I immediately tracked down the village chief to collect Misplaced Trust so I could use it on Missha. But once I had it in my hand, I fell deep into thought.
Is this the right thing to do...?

At this point, I was less worried about whether or not Missha was hiding something and more uncomfortable with the idea of using this item on one of my companions. If I used it now, what about the next time? What if after this, I became dependent on Misplaced Trust and used it on my comrades whenever I grew suspicious of them?
Could you even call that a friendship?
That was the question at the heart of the matter. However...
This will be the last time.
Although I had no way of knowing what might happen in the future, promising myself that this would be it brought me some comfort.
Bolstered, I raised my hand to knock on the door I had been loitering in front of for a while. There was no verbal response from the person inside, but I doubted she was still asleep.
I knocked again. “It’s me, Missha. Let’s talk.”
There was shuffling on the other end. “Eh? Huh? B-Bjorn? W-Wait just a second...”
It was a full five minutes later when the door opened.
“What... is it...? It’s still so early...”
Despite my concerns that she was living like a recluse, she looked quite clean. It seemed that she’d been taking a bath, as her hair was still slightly damp.
“May I come in?”
“Uh... it’s a little messy...”
“It’s fine.” I walked through the door, then immediately pulled out Misplaced Trust.

“That’s...” An array of emotions flitted across Missha’s face as she recognized the item. She seemed both relieved and almost pleased by the sight of it. She also seemed disappointed, and maybe a little scared too.
I couldn’t say for sure that was why, but I was suddenly having trouble finding my voice. Even so, I forced myself to dredge up the words anyway.
“I want to turn this on so we can have a talk. May I?”
After a short pause, she answered my question with one of her own. “And if I answer everything you ask after you turn it on... then can we go back to how we used to be? Like before?”
A thought popped into my mind.
What did she mean when she said “before?” Did she mean that brief moment when it felt like our hearts were aligned, or simply back when we were comrades in arms?
Well, it was probably the latter. After all, it was Missha who had turned me down and pushed me away, not the other way around.
“Maybe.” I gave a vague, but positive response.

It was only on the condition that Missha had nothing more to hide from me, but if that ended up being the case, then we might really be able to go back to how we used to be—before our relationship became such a complicated, painful mess.
“Then... you may.”
When Missha clenched her fists and nodded, I began my official interrogation.
[You have activated No. 7234: Misplaced Trust.]
I thought it every time, but this item really was aptly named.

chapters.title: Chapter 580: Opened Doors (1)
paragraphs: Even one.
Was there a person out there who could say they had never committed a single wrongdoing in their life? Someone who was perfectly innocent?

Missha Karlstein believed that to be impossible. Even the holiest of saints made a mistake at least once in their lifetime. Even someone with genuinely good intentions could end up achieving the wrong outcome by accident. Could end up hurting someone else. It couldn’t be helped.
If even great people like that can make mistakes, of course a loser like me is no exception—
“I...” Missha quietly mumbled to herself. “What am I doing...?”
She had been doing this on a loop for a few days now.

Things probably would have been better if she could at least fight monsters or something, but as it stood, there wasn’t much else she could do while holed up in her room all day. She ached to be able to shut her brain off and sleepwalk through life, but not wanting to think didn’t mean she didn’t have to think.

And so, over several long days, she thought and thought. The thoughts were always different, and yet always so similar. She would start to feel resentful, then grow disgusted at herself, and sometimes, she had flashes of clarity that seemed to put everything in perspective. When those particular thoughts came and went, the conclusion they left her with was the same every time.
“Let’s leave.”
Let’s leave Clan Anabada.

No, it wasn’t like she’d been an official member of the clan to begin with. That should make it even easier for her to leave. So, after this expedition was over and they were back in the city, she would disappear. She would remove herself from Bjorn Yandel’s life and not show her face in front of him ever again.
He...he probably wants that too.
That was the conclusion she had reached hundreds and hundreds of times now. The second she reached it again, it sent her curling inward as her hands grasped for her chest.
It hurt. Beyond a suffocating shortness of breath, her chest just hurt. It hurt so much that she thought it might hurt less if she got something sharp, closed her eyes, and stabbed at it.
However, Missha couldn’t translate those thoughts into reality. It wasn’t for lack of desire or resolve. It was just that she knew.
That’s not right...
He wouldn’t want that kind of ending for her. It would taint all the memories they shared in pitch-black hues and torment him for the rest of his life.
Dwalkie...
Without warning, the memory of him came to her—the noble wizard who gave his life to save all of theirs in the Labyrinth of Larcaz. Missha knew about the feelings that he had had for her.
Well, she hadn’t known while he was alive. But one day, many months after Dwalkie’s passing, the dwarven warrior Hikurod Murad had told her. That he had always had feelings for her...
At first, she couldn’t believe it. If that were really the case, why did Dwalkie hide his affections from her even as he was breathing his last?
She couldn’t wrap her head around it. If it were her, she would have used the final opportunity she’d been given to share her feelings.
However, when she voiced this aloud, Hikurod answered like he thought the question a bit silly.
“Isn’t it obvious what he was thinking? He probably didn’t want to leave a dark shadow behind.”

She found this a vague, unclear explanation. Yet despite that, she had accepted it, if only because she thought that was what Dwalkie would have wanted. But even then, she had never been able to fully understand his logic. Not, at least, until today.
“So... this is what you were feeling...”

Strictly speaking, she and Dwalkie were nothing alike. He had sacrificed his life to save everyone, while she was floundering in the wake of her own mistakes—her own failures—and trying to find a way out. If she weren’t in the labyrinth right now...
If she didn’t still cling to the smallest of hopes that she might be forgiven one day, she would’ve run a long time ago—
Knock, knock, knock.
At that moment, she heard a voice from beyond her locked door.
“It’s me, Missha. Let’s talk.”
It was Bjorn.
His visit sent both joy and fear swirling through her. However, she forced herself to calm down and do what she needed to do.

First things first: she couldn’t let him see her like this. She washed her hair and gave her face a quick rinse. She then rushed to tidy up her messy room. Thankfully, she had spent most of her time in here doing nothing, so there wasn’t much to clean.
“May I enter?”
She opened the door to reveal the man she hadn’t seen in far too long, and he walked in. Inexplicably, her heart began to pound.
Ba-dump.
Why is Bjorn here? Is he worried about me? I hope the room doesn’t smell...
While she had been withering away like a picked flower until just moments ago, for some reason, life returned to her body the second she was in his presence.
“I want to turn this on so we can have a talk. May I?”

Part of her wished he had started with some idle conversation, but the second he was past the threshold, Bjorn immediately got to the point. In his large hand, he was holding an item she immediately recognized.
Misplaced Trust.
That name... She couldn’t shake the sinking feeling that the name of that item seemed to describe her relationship with him perfectly right now.

However, the sight of it also lifted her spirits. This was an opportunity. After turning his back on her that day with cold finality, he was giving her another chance. A golden opportunity to fix things, to make up for all the mistakes she had made...
And maybe that meant Bjorn wanted things to go back to how they used to be too.
“Then... you may. Let’s talk.”
That was why Missha couldn’t let this opportunity pass her by. She had been in limbo for far too long.
Okay. With hands gripped into fists, she steeled her resolve. Whatever Bjorn asks, I’ll answer honestly.
And so, Bjorn began his investigation.
“After I disappeared from Farune Island, how did you end up following Baekho Lee?”
Starting with some longer questions she had answered before, many yes or no questions followed, and Missha answered all of them truthfully.

Right now, Bjorn was a lot like a clockmaker she’d once seen at work. Just as they had methodically taken every little piece of the clock out to find out what was wrong with it, Bjorn was asking her even the smallest of questions and inspecting every part.
“Baekho Lee... did he do anything bad to you?”
“Anything bad...?”
“Like... put his hands on you...”
“N-No! Nothing like that! I swear!”
There were some questions that both pained and warmed her, but they weren’t the important ones.
“Did you really not know that the Stone of Revival makes the target lose all their memories?”
“I didn’t...”
“Then why did you hide it from me?”
“Like I told you back then... I thought something bad would happen to you if you found out...”
This was the part that had set Bjorn off that day. She could still recall how stony his face had gone as he asked her if she’d hidden it from him simply because she’d taken Baekho Lee at his word.
The memory of their last conversation was fresh in her mind, and before Bjorn could say anything else, Missha quickly shouted, “And I-I thought it was worth the risk!”
“...Worth the risk?”
“I-I didn’t know back then that you would lose your memories... No, even if I did, I would’ve done the same...! Because that’s still better than you dying...”
“That’s why you were willing to put your faith in him?”
“...Baekho Lee is really strong. And something inside of him is broken beyond repair.”

That was the real reason she had accepted Baekho Lee’s offer: she didn’t know what he would have done to her if she refused. Maybe it would have even been ‘something bad.’ That was why she had accepted the Stone of Revival and returned to Bjorn’s side. It was an item that could save the life of someone she loved. In her mind, she had nothing to lose by taking it.
However...
“Huh, so that’s all?”
There was one thing she hadn’t mentioned yet.
She didn’t know how to tell him. Saying it out loud could ruin everything. But despite the risk, Missha screwed her eyes shut and forced the words through her teeth anyway.
“I-in exchange for taking the Stone of Revival, I agreed to give him information.”
“...Information?”

“He told me to stay and keep an eye on you...” Missha opened an eye to peek at Bjorn’s face. For now, he looked more shocked than angry. “D-Don’t worry, though! I haven’t given him any information yet. After leaving that day, I haven’t met up with him since.”
“And if he came looking for you? What were you going to do then?”

“...I don’t know. At the time, I wanted to just get out of there and figure out the rest later.” Yet the second the answer left her lips, Missha felt like she was making excuses, so she quickly added, “But...I think I would’ve given him the information. O-Of course, it would’ve been random little things that everyone already knows—!”

“Hmm...” Taking in Missha’s not-excuses, Bjorn let out a long breath and rubbed his chin. Thankfully, he didn’t seem too mad. He just nodded, acknowledging her response, before proceeding to the next question.
And then...
“Final question.” Bjorn looked directly into Missha’s eyes and spoke, every word deliberate. “Is there anything else you’re hiding from me?”
An open-ended question that covered the rest.
Nothing. She had answered everything he asked honestly. That was what she wanted to say, but for some reason, her mouth opened and closed without a sound.

Just a moment ago, it had felt like their relationship was slowly on the mend, but her hesitation was a bucket of ice water that froze the healing process in its tracks. A silence too heavy to be described as a mere absence of sound settled between the two.
Bjorn only said two things.
“Right... So there is something.”
He sounded resigned, like he had already assumed this would be the case.
Chest tight, Missha tried once again to speak.
To say that he was wrong. That she had told him everything there was to know. That there wasn’t anything she was hiding from him. Even though she wanted to say all that, the words refused to come.
Why? Was Misplaced Trust broken? Missha, who truly had nothing to hide anymore, was utterly baffled, but then...
Ah...

She finally came to a realization. Misplaced Trust was working fine. It wasn’t broken, and even now, it was operating exactly as it was meant to. Which meant that there was only one reason it’d prevent her from speaking.
There was something she was hiding from him.
“Is it...” Bjorn’s voice cut through the suffocating silence. “Is it... something you can’t tell me?”
She felt it instinctively. If she stayed quiet here, it was all over for her.
“...I-I’m not hiding anything related to Baekho Lee from you.”
“Then?” As she met Bjorn’s eyes, struck by the hope he still held for her despite everything, she sucked in a breath. “Then you’re hiding something else from me?”
“Yeah...” Even as she nodded, almost as if possessed, hesitation flooded her system.
Could she really say it?
While she’d been gone, he had filled his family with much better people than her. He’d made new promises with them. Maybe... Maybe it would be better for Bjorn if she just disappeared.
But even as she thought that, her mouth moved without her say-so.
As her frozen lips slowly parted, the sad, bitter truth she had been holding back all these years came spilling out. “I lied to you back then, Bjorn.”
Bjorn’s eyebrows furrowed at the word “lie.”
Come to think of it, he had always been this way. Being lied to was the thing he hated most in the world, yet she was now in the position of having to tell him what she’d been hiding from him.
I can’t shrink back from this.

She let go of the final thing holding her back and spoke. This was something she had intended to tell him back on Farune Island. She’d tried to kill her feelings for his sake, but driven by the fear that he might die at any moment, she’d decided to reveal that they still ran strong.
“When I told you that it would be best if we just stay teammates...”
Well, it had taken longer than expected, but she finally had the chance to tell him.
“That was a lie.”
It was best to start even when you thought it was too late. Hadn’t they had a conversation like that once?
“In hindsight... I don’t think I gave you a proper response back then...”
With that, Missha lifted her head to meet his eyes, making sure to carefully enunciate each word.
“Bjorn Yandel, I... like you too.”
These were the words she hadn’t been able to say back when she first learned about his feelings for her, too caught up in her own head to tell the truth.
Bjorn didn’t say a thing.

She continued on regardless. “I did on the day you said those words to me. And the days before you said them. And...” Missha’s voice was as small as a mouse, yet crystal-clear in the silence. “Even now...”
This was the one secret she had still been keeping from him.

There were some days you woke up with a weird feeling in your gut. Days when, even when the sky above was bright and sunny, you could somehow sense that there were storm clouds on the horizon, just waiting to drench you with rain.
For Erwen, today was one of those days.
“Mister! Are you a... wake?”
She had excitedly run over to his room at dawn, only to find it empty.
The sight of his empty bed left Erwen with an inexplicable sense of unease. She searched the entire house for him, but Bjorn wasn’t anywhere to be found.
“The captain? Who knows... He didn’t tell me he was going out... Is he not inside the building?”
“...Really? I went looking in all the rooms, but I didn’t see him.”
“Hmm, then maybe he headed out on some business...”
Anabada’s navigator, Auyen Rockrobe, assured her it was probably nothing, but for some reason, Erwen’s mouth went dry as sand.
In truth, there was one room she hadn’t checked yet.
Missha Karlstein’s.

The reason Erwen hadn’t checked her room was because she simply didn’t think there was any chance Bjorn would be in there. It also seemed like something had happened between the two recently. Missha had been spending most of her time in her room alone, and in the rare moments she came out for clan meetings, she’d looked upset.
However, that posed an interesting question.
Step, step.
Why, even as she was thinking that there was no way Bjorn would be there, was she moving toward Missha’s room?
She knew that it was far more likely that he was out on business, just as their navigator claimed. So why did she feel so uneasy, so worried that she might be wrong?
Step.
Despite the negative emotions battering her from all sides, Erwen reached her destination.
The room was located in the corner of the townhouse’s third floor. The door was firmly shut.
She considered knocking, but she didn’t because she figured it would be awkward if he wasn’t in there.
I can’t sense any magic.
There was no sound isolation magic or any sort of barrier around the room. Meaning, if she wanted to, she could hear everything that was happening inside.
Erwen usually made an effort to rein in her keen sense of hearing in her day-to-day life, but now she focused on it. The second she did, she heard a familiar voice.
“Bjorn Yandel, I... like you too.”
She immediately recognized the voice, but she couldn’t understand what it was saying.
Just... what the hell was that woman saying?
Convinced she might have misheard, she pricked her ears and leaned in.
“I did on the day you said those words to me. And even before you said them. And...”
Her brain refused to process it.
Because it was a love confession, wasn’t it? Something Erwen had never once in all her life been capable of voicing aloud. And yet...
Know your place, you—
It was unbelievable. It was infuriating.

Wasn’t this the same woman who had vanished without a trace instead of trying to avenge Mister after they thought he died? The innocent, kind Bjorn had been willing to take her back, probably blinded by lingering feelings of friendship, but Erwen had never forgotten.
Yet the words continued to echo through her mind.
“Bjorn Yandel, I... like you too.”
Only then did Erwen notice something odd.
Too...?
That Red Cat beastwoman had definitely said “too.”
And “too” was used to reciprocate a sentiment previously declared.
Which meant...
...Mister said it first?
The thought was so unbelievable that the fire burning in her mind suddenly went cold. And as the heat subsided, she could finally see the situation for what it was.
She couldn’t help but laugh.

The poor woman was clearly delusional. She was hallucinating an entire conversation with Mister. Backing up Erwen’s deduction was the fact that she hadn’t heard anything else from inside the room after that bombshell.
Still... I feel a bit bad for her.
It was the sort of bizarre behavior that would be difficult for most to understand, but Erwen had done something similar while in a delicate emotional state, so she could sympathize.
Hmm... so where has Mister run off to...?
With that, Erwen turned away and returned her heightened hearing back to its normal levels, feeling like she had heard something she wasn’t supposed to.
Or, well, she’d been about to do all that.
“...I see.”
But then a familiar voice spoke from inside the room.

chapters.title: Chapter 581: Opened Doors (2)
paragraphs: My mind went blank.
The mind, which had been running fine even after waking up in the body of an unfamiliar barbarian at a coming-of-age ceremony, refused to form a coherent thought, as if drunk.
With that, a moment of silence followed.
Missha looked at me with eyes shining with both fear and expectation, and I couldn’t resist those eyes any longer and ended up speaking.
“...I see.”
A meaningless mumbling that was neither accepting, refusing, or questioning her.
After such a long silence, all I could muster were those two words. It had been a while since I felt so embarrassed about myself. However, thanks to that, my mind began to work again.
Yes or no.

Right now, what I needed to do wasn’t to choose between those two. If what Missha had told me was true... No, since Misplaced Trust was active, it must be true... But that was why there was something that was even more difficult for me to understand.
“Then...”
“Then...why did you draw that line between us back then?”

It was a question I had held in my heart for so long. Why did Missha push me away back then? At that time, I could at least explain it as her not liking me as a man, but hearing this from her now, that didn’t seem to be the case.
Missha gave me a quiet answer. “Ah... That’s... It’s because back then, I realized that you’re an evil spirit... N-no, a player...?”
“Player...?”
When I tilted my head, Missha asked quietly, “I heard that you didn’t like being called an evil spirit... Do you?”
Hmm, I had never thought about it, but “player” did sound a little better than “evil spirit.” Still, did she hear that from Baekho Lee? If so, it pissed me off for some reason too.
“If...you don’t like it...I’ll stop. Sorry...”

I returned my focus to the conversation and said, “It’s fine. What does my being an evil spirit have to do with you? I mean...did you think that you can’t have a relationship with an evil spirit, regardless of what you felt?”
I’d tried to suppress my emotions as much as possible, but something might have leaked through, as Missha jolted and shouted, “I-it’s not like that, Bjorrrn!”
She must have been so shocked that her old self peaked through.
Missha seemed surprised and embarrassed to have raised her voice, turning her eyes away as she said, “It’s just... It was hard for me to watch you... To see you becoming weaker because of me...”
“I’ll need a bit more explanation for that.”
When I asked for more details, Missha scrambled for her words and explained her situation without hiding anything. In summary, it was pretty simple.

“You thought me taking my ‘duty’ even to the point of swapping appearances with Kharon was because of you, and you thought those actions weren’t helpful to me? Because they could expose my identity in the future?”
“Yeah...” Even as Missha lowered her head deeply like a student being punished, her eyes remained on me. “But maybe... Was it my misunderstanding...?”
Hah, how could I explain this to her? The reason I changed faces with Kharon using the golden mask was because of GM. I needed to create an alibi to avoid being suspected of being an evil spirit.
She’s not completely wrong, though.
This entire time, I had never completed my “duty” at the holy land. My first reason was because it was uncomfortable for me as a modern human, and the second reason was Missha.
It was because it felt like I was committing a grave sin.
“So it wasn’t my misunderstanding... That’s a relief...” Missha let out a sigh of release, seemingly having gotten her answer through my expression.

I checked the Misplaced Trust only to see that it didn’t have a lot of time left. I wondered if there even was a point with things as they were, but even if it seemed cruel, I wanted to use this opportunity to rid myself of all doubt.
“So is that all?” I questioned.
“I might be wrong, but...I think you might have more reasons for pushing me away...” I trailed off, still staring at her.
Missha looked surprised.
Yeah, so you did have something.
I sent her a look to hurry up, and her face flushed bright red as she admitted, “So...you know...I can’t have children...”
My mind was thrust back into that white void for a second. Not even an ogre would be this shocked if hit on the head with a tree.
“Children...?” I echoed hollowly.
“D-don’t misunderstand! I-I’m not saying that I can’t have any children, but that any children I have won’t be barbarian...”

I could understand what she was trying to say. She was talking about the racial characteristic of the barbarians, that barbarians could only be born of barbarian women. Yet the thing I understood was what she was trying to say, but not why she was saying it.
“Why does it matter if my child is a barbarian or not?” I asked, sounding baffled even to my own ears.
Missha flinched. “Huh...? Does it not matter?”
Obviously not, I wasn’t even a real barbarian. Whether my child was a barbarian or a Red Cat, I would give all my love to them.
“You’re lying...” Missha accused, unable to truly accept my words. “Men care about things like that...”
Well, that could be how it was in this world, and maybe that was “obvious” for Missha who was born and raised here. But not for me.
“The world I lived in was different.”
“But you’re even a n-noble now... E-everyone will definitely think it’s weird and talk behind your back—”

“Stop,” I demanded, putting a halt to the conversation there. Talking about kids was awkward in and of itself, and that ignored the minor embarrassment that came with it as well. “Let’s stop talking about this.”
“Ah... Yeah... R-right? I-it’s not like you l-like me still anyway...”
“I haven’t given you my proper answer yet.”
“...Then? What... What is your answer?”
“Before I say that.” I checked the time that was left first before asking, “Is there anything else you’re hiding?”
Missha spoke without hesitation in a calm voice. “No.”
Right, so that was all.
To think that I had believed that she was hiding something and couldn’t trust her. It was laughable, really.
Click.
Soon, the hand of the Misplaced Trust reached the end and the light faded.
“Then, can you...give me an answer?”
For some reason, it was difficult for me to meet her eyes. She was looking at me as if this question was the most important thing in the world for her.
I should answer...
Misplaced Trust had already been deactivated, yet it wouldn’t matter much to me even if it was still active.
“My answer...”
I told her the honest truth.
It felt as if she had been cursed—and cursed by a very sinister spell, at that.
“Bjorn Yandel. I...like you too.”
“Bjorn Yandel. I...like you too.”
“Bjorn Yandel. I...like you too.”
Even after drenching her head with cold water and slamming her helmeted head into the wall multiple times, that voice continued to echo in her mind. That, and even the last thing Bjorn said as well.
“...I see.”
It wasn’t an affirmation. But it wasn’t denial either.
Despite that, Erwen ended up feeling a deep sense of relief at his two little words. If what she sensed then was true, Bjorn had felt relieved in that moment.
At Missha Karlstein’s, at that ungrateful woman’s answer.
What had happened between those two? And what was the meaning of that “I see”?
They were questions that Erwen couldn’t find an answer to, not now. The moment she heard Bjorn’s voice from within the room, she had left as if fleeing.
Why did she do it?
Why did she run away and not listen to the whole thing?

Belated regret rushed in, but she wasn’t sure that she would do anything different if she were able to return to that moment in time. Even now, she was afraid. It felt as if hearing the truth had created something horrifying, an event horizon that could not be escaped.
“Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.”
That was why she didn’t immediately go to Bjorn to question him. No, after spiraling into thought by herself and wandering aimlessly, she ran to this place.
“How long are you going to stay like that?”
Amelia Rainwales.
Although she was a plunderer of Noark origin, after becoming connected with Bjorn, she was living a new life under the name of Emily Raines. Erwen had come to her room.
“If you’re lost in thought, put it into words already. I’ll try listening to you.”
“...It’s fine.”

In the end, Erwen turned away. Amelia didn’t stop her, merely telling Erwen to come to her if she changed her mind and wanted to talk. However, Erwen had no plans of returning. No, the reason she had come today was because she had lost her mind, and it had only been on a whim.
Erwen returned to her room and suffered by herself, and there, she came to a conclusion.
It couldn’t be. Bjorn forming a relationship like that with the Red Cat woman—it was impossible. Yeah, how could that woman be better than her?
After coming to that conclusion, her heart settled, and she was finally able to leave the room.
Yet after going down to the first floor, what met her eyes was the scene of a man and a woman sitting at the table and whispering affectionately to each other.

“Ack...don’t laugh! You told me to make this for you. It’s been a while since I’ve tried to, so I could’ve made some mistakes... Th-there aren’t that many ingredients because we’re in the labyrinth as well...but... Well, i-is it too salty?”
“Don’t worry. It’s delicious.”
The woman seemed to have made the man some nostalgic dish. After staring dazedly at the scene from the stairs, she ended up meeting eyes with that woman.

“Ah, Erwen...” The woman’s expression turned awkward when their eyes met, and she began to plate another plate of food. “It’s not mealtime yet, but do you want some? It’s... I made a lot so there’s some left...”
For some reason, it reminded her of a memory from the past.
“Ah! If it’s because of the helmet, you can take it to your room—”
“I don’t need it.”
After coldly cutting the woman off, Erwen went back up the stairs. She had done good enough by holding back the urge to grab the plate and throw it on the ground.
Clack.
Erwen opened Amelia’s door and entered the room. Amelia looked confused that she was no longer flustered after leaving not so long ago, but that wasn’t important right now.
“Amelia Rainwales.”
Erwen spoke the name of the woman that she usually didn’t speak.
The time when she had left Bjorn and was learning next to her older sister, when the Red Cat woman acted like the lady of the house and treated her like an unwelcome guest.
“...I need your help.”
Erwen never wanted to return to that time again.
After watching Erwen disappear up the stairs, Missha looked at me with worry in her eyes. “Will she...be okay...?”
“I’ll talk with Erwen, so don’t worry. And...good job.”
“Trying to give her food. It mustn’t have been easy, knowing she hates you.”
“Ah, that’s not... It’s nothing. We can’t stay like this forever... We’ll need to keep living together...”
Missha looked sheepish as she scratched the table. Even that looked admirable to me.
I had told her to not stay on the outskirts and live side-by-side with the members of the clan, and she was already trying hard to keep to her word.
Well, the mood did turn awkward for a reason unrelated to that.

Although it was far from natural, the silence didn’t feel unpleasant. I used the time to think about my last conversation with Missha. I was still embarrassed at myself for it, but there was only one answer I could give.
“You don’t know...? What do you mean?”
I definitely didn’t hate her. The remains of the feelings I had during that time still remained. However, that was all they were—remains.
“A lot of time has passed since then...”

From that day onward, I’d tried my best to get rid of the feelings I had for Missha, and I had succeeded. I didn’t know what would happen in the future, but the emotions I felt for her were closer to that of an ally than to that of a man to a woman.
Amelia, Erwen, Ainar, Raven—if any one of those four were in Missha’s situation, I would have found it just as difficult and reacted similarly.
Well, that wasn’t important.
“H-haha... Th-then it can’t be helped...” Even while looking hurt by my honest answer, Missha ended the situation like an adult. “Still...we can be friends, right?”
“Huh?”
“Right? B-back then as well...we started as friends...”
“Uh, um...”
And I ended up sounding ridiculous by responding, “I-I guess?” to that.
It was an embarrassing scene where I wanted to grab something and throw it as hard as I could. But what could be done about it? It had already happened.
Missha interrupted the silence, noticing that I’d cleaned my plate. “Did you finish? Should I get you more—?”

“Mr. Yandel.” Versyl seemed to have gone out in the morning as she appeared from the front door to say, “You were on the first floor? We were looking for you. Count Saintred is summoning you. It looks like the headstone research is nearly complete. He’s ordered you to go there.”
“The research is nearly complete... Do you know what the results are?”
“I don’t know the details, but I think they failed.”
“I see... Well, I guess I’ll hear it there. I’m off.”
“Alright... Have a safe trip.”
I got up from my seat, and Missha sent me off.
Seeing this, Versyl tilted her head. “You two...”
“Do you have something to say?”
“...No. Nothing.”
I smirked. She obviously did have something.
“After you come back, could we have a talk?” she asked.
“Sure.”
It was obvious what she wanted to say after I came back.
She must be worried since she suspected Missha to be a traitor, and she was probably thinking of revealing the thing that happened in the community yesterday as naturally as possible to me.
I think I can tell her she doesn’t have to worry anymore, then...
When I eventually arrived at the mansion where the dimensional headstone was, the village chief was waiting for me on the first floor.
“You’re here.”

“We can skip the greetings. Just say what it is you want to say,” I pressed. The village chief then told me that the research to open the dimensional headstone over the last ten days had failed and that we would leave the village today. “Today...?”
“Although I held hope, since it was a complete failure, we cannot waste any more time here.”
Well, that was true. I also didn’t expect things to work out this easily in the first place.
“So I’d like to hear your opinion before we leave. I have no intention of interfering with your adventuring. Where do you want the next destination to be?”
We had rested even more than intended.
Now, it was time to adventure again.

chapters.title: Chapter 582: Opened Doors (3)
paragraphs: Our next destination, huh?
I threw the question back at him, but the village chief only parroted that I should do as I pleased.
I can’t tell what he’s thinking.

In the end, I decided on a destination with a sigh, and the village chief said he would announce the decision in our next leadership meeting. So, he wasn’t lying when he said he had no intention of interfering with our exploration and was content in not making any decisions regarding it.
“So how did the research go?”
Before I left, I asked him one more time about the research, the project that began over ten days ago when the wizards said they might be able to forcibly activate the dimensional headstone.
“Hmm, weren’t you told that research ended in failure?”
“I thought maybe you got some results since you let them hold onto it for so long.”
“A result, you say...” The village chief trailed off before saying offhand, “It’s not as if we didn’t get anything.”
“...What was it?”
“I was able to obtain an assurance that I would be able to escape this place using the Heretic Altar.”

How did he come to that conclusion? Although he didn’t give a detailed explanation, he was probably telling the truth. In fact, that was probably the reason he gave the wizards over ten days to research.

Ultimately, I just directly asked him, “So when are you thinking of returning to the city?” In my mind, the only reason the village chief was still in the labyrinth was because of the uncertainty factor.

Basement Floor One was quite the peculiar floor. Take for example what happened when the expedition group first tried to open the dimensional door when coming here—the dimensional door didn’t open. That was why there was so much discussion around the floor, an exercise of thought in whether it could even be considered an ordinary labyrinth field. Days of back and forth between the wizards and the adventurers later, and in the end, the opinion leaned more toward “yes,” and the main evidence for this was the Stone of Honor.
The Great Barbarian Warrior, Bjorn Yandel, and his companions discovered Basement Floor One.

This place was special in many ways, but that one sentence removed all doubt that Basement Floor One was a location within the labyrinth. Nevertheless, we were unable to discover why the dimensional door couldn’t be opened. Well, it wasn’t as if this was the only special area within the labyrinth where the dimensional door couldn’t be opened.
“Can’t you just return right now since you’ve gotten certainty?” I probed, trying to shuffle him along.
The village chief only gave a stern shake of his head. “I haven’t finished my preparation yet. I’m not confident that I would be able to avoid all suspicion if I return now.”
Well, that was true. If I were in the chief’s position, I would have stayed in the body for a long time to obtain as much information about Jerome Saintred as possible.
“It seems you want me to leave as quickly as possible,” he noted.
“Heh, what made it obvious?”
“Why is it? We should be in the same boat now.”
What do you mean, why? Don’t ask questions you already know the answer to.
“Don’t try to lump us together. You haven’t told me anything about how to activate the dimensional headstone,” I complained.

“Well...it appears you still don’t trust me.” The village chief nodded in a show of understanding before tapping my arm like a boss of a company would. “There’s no need for such worry. I will certainly leave this place, and I will tell you everything when that time comes.”
How ironic.
Did the village chief know? Every time he gave me some cryptic reassurance like that, I felt even more uneasy.
...Should I just kill him now?
Though the impulse was tempting, I decided to hold back and watch how the situation unfolded.
The village chief stopped me when I tried to leave. “Ah, by the way, did you use the thing you took in the morning? That Misplaced Trust.”
“...Right, I nearly forgot to give—”
“You don’t have to give it back. You’ll need it more than me.”
Just openly curse me at this point.
I felt a flash of indignation at his subtle insult, but I still took Misplaced Trust with me and left the building.
When I returned to the house we were using as our lodging, Erwen and Amelia seemed to be doing something, as I couldn’t find them anywhere. The same went for Missha.
Instead, Versyl Gowland was waiting for me.
“You’re back?”
“Now that I think about it, I do remember you said you had something you wanted to talk about.”
It was obvious what she was going to tell me, but I acted oblivious and sat down. After the sound isolation barrier was put up, our conversation officially began, and it went as I expected.
“There’s a rumor that the assembly of the evil spirits has closed.”
Versyl first relayed the most important piece of information under the guise of a rumor.
To be honest, I was a bit dumbfounded. “A rumor?”
“Yes, because...it’s not like we have any evil spirits among us.”
No, but then where did you hear the rumor from?
A normal person would have asked, but I just feigned ignorance and nodded. Maybe because I never asked about where she got her information, Versyl seemed to have become complacent when talking to me.
I hope she doesn’t do this in other places...
It was something that worried me as a leader.
In any case, after talking about the so-called “rumor,” she naturally transitioned to the topic of Missha. “By the way, about this morning...what happened?”
“Are you talking about Missha?”
“Yes. The information about how Ms. Karlstein could be a traitor, that’s still in effect. Staying too close to her...”

Versyl carefully made her concern known, and that was why I sternly cut off her misconception right there. “You don’t have to worry about that anymore. I’ve confirmed myself that she was not a traitor just a bit ago.”
“...Pardon? Really? Then why didn’t you tell me?”
“It wasn’t anything serious. When I heard her situation, it didn’t seem like she was trying to hurt us either.”
“I understand that you want to trust Ms. Karlstein, but how could you be so sure?”
Hah, I knew she was going to ask this. “I used Misplaced Trust. I also confirmed after hearing her situation that she wasn’t hiding anything else.”

When she heard that I used Misplaced Trust, Versyl immediately closed her mouth and fell silent. If she continued to insist that we couldn’t trust her, she would just be forcing the issue. Of course, she probably was curious about what the thing I deemed “nothing serious” was, but I wasn’t planning on telling her.
“In any case, there isn’t any problem with Missha Karlstein now. You don’t have to keep surveillance on her, so just treat her like a regular ally from now on.”
“...Yes. I’ll do that.”
Alright, then that was the end of that topic.
I then asked Versyl to gather the rest of Temporary Squad 4, and when everyone got together, I ordered them to start packing up to leave the island today.
“Ah! Are we going to resume our expedition again?”
“Then it seems the dimensional headstone research failed...”
“Hah... My family is probably worried about me.”
A few people were saddened they couldn’t immediately return to the city, but the mood wasn’t too glum.
“I was honestly getting bored. This is good.”
“We still have a lot of places we haven’t been to yet.”
Everyone here was an adventurer.
Splash.
Four ships sailed through the silver waters, with the small and precious boat of the Anabada Clan at the very back behind the large military vessels.
Sitting at the bow, I sat and spaced out while watching the military ships in front of us.
How much more money do I need to earn to get a ship like that...?

Honestly, it wouldn’t be a problem if I just sold Wall of Aegis and the Verdurous Giant Spear, but I would just end up poor with a ship. Even if I bought something like that with cash, without a powerful basis of wealth backing me up, there was no point buying a boat like—

“Mr. Yandel! What are you doing there?!” While I flickered from thought to thought from where I sat at the front of the boat, a sharp voice from behind me cut through the haze. It was the vice-captain of the Third Magic Troops, Raven. “It’s dangerous! Come down quickly!”
She quickly ran onto the deck while shouting in an angry voice, and since she didn’t even come up to my chest in height, she looked like a child when she looked up at me.
You know, it’ll only make me laugh if you keep looking up at me like that.
“Huh? What’s that look in your eyes...?”
“...Nothing.”

I stretched my arms to the sky as I looked around at the deck and spotted a few more familiar faces—Melend Kaislan, Sven Parav, and a few of the knights who I got close to during the battles on Library Island. From now on, they were a part of the Temporary Squad 4 as well. I had asked the village chief before we left, and he allowed it without effect.
“By the way, Raven. I have something I want to ask you.”
“...What is it?”
“Did anything happen during the headstone research at the village? Weren’t you a part of that?”
“Oh, that?”
Since we had time to spare while sailing, I asked her something I was curious about, and Raven passionately explained everything while using all sorts of jargon.
I can’t understand a single thing she said.

A dimensional severance phenomenon, spatial coordinates, and all sorts of nonsense that a modern person wearing the skin of a barbarian had no hope of understanding. While I just sat there and allowed the words to enter in one ear and out the other, Raven seemed to notice my state as she became embarrassed and tried to change the topic.
“Ahem! I guess my explanation was too difficult for you... But Mr. Yandel, could I ask something as well?”
“Sure.”
“Where are we going right now? I thought you might know.”
