An incredibly dangerous event would soon befall us, and this was the last chance we had to avoid it.
...The Overseer was right.

We had only around a month until the half-a-year time limit the Research Station Overseer gave us arrived. Considering how long it would take to reach the village chief’s island, we were down to the wire.
“Lord Baron...” Parav said nervously. “How about we leave immediately? No, we must leave now!”
“Calm down and return to your station. I’ll deal with this.”
“Pardon? Ah... Yes! But please! Please deal with it quickly!”

This guy lived life with the perfect subordinate disposition. If he of all people was acting up like this, then his intuition must be blaring at him with all sorts of alarm bells. From what he told me, this was considerably worse than when he was dragged to Ice Rock.
...A situation worse than what happened during the Ice Rock Expedition.
Knowing that made me a little uneasy as well.
How many people collapsed in that cold place and disappeared forever during that expedition? I didn’t want to experience something like that ever again.
“Deputy commander, I’ll be going up for a moment.”
“....So suddenly, sir?”
“We may need to leave this place in a rush. I’ll tell you everything when I get back, so take command of this place until I return.”
After that, I got the deputy commander to proceed with the raid without me and also told him to prepare everyone for departure if needed. I then quickly moved up toward the control center.
Is this right?

Even as I moved, my contemplation continued. I would need to immediately take the Overseer’s offer to receive the qualification then immediately set sail toward Chief Island to leave before the time I was warned about arrived. If I did that, no one would get hurt. And I had no qualms admitting that it was the safest method.
But it’s too much of a loss to never be able to come back down here ever again.
The fact that I still didn’t know why the Overseer was trying to stop me from coming here again was also another reason that made it difficult for me to make the call.
But for Goblin to say that much, I can’t just ignore him either...
I was in a really sticky situation. My thoughts were all jumbled, and so because of that, I chose to think more simply.
Priorities. All decisions relied on what I would prioritize.
As I headed to the control room, I reflected on myself. And as I did, I could feel my heart lighten a little as I made my decision.
...Let’s accept the offer.

There could be many more treasure chests hidden on this first basement floor, but I had obtained many things already. I didn’t even know the floor existed in the first place. It felt more like a bonus stage.
And most importantly...there’s not much I can do here for the time being anyway.
We weren’t strong enough to keep looking for more secrets. We couldn’t even fight that super giant on Giant Island. There were far too many factors working against us.
Just as many people died during the rank 1 monster fight on Library Island, we would need to sacrifice even more people if we wanted to continue our exploration.
[(You’re here.)]
“(Yeah, I’m here.)” I slowly entered the control room for the first time in over a month.
[(It would seem you’ve finally made your decision?)]
Overseer also seemed to realize why I was here from where he floated on the screen as if he had been waiting for me.
He’s an odd guy in a lot of ways.

Surprisingly enough, after making that first offer some time ago, the Overseer had been waiting for me the entire time. Even after days turned into weeks turned into months, he didn’t try to press me into making a decision. It was as if he knew that the outcome wouldn’t change.
[(Alright, tell me. What did you decide?)]

It left a bitter taste in my mouth, perhaps because it seemed like everything went as he predicted. However, since I had made my decision already, I couldn’t let my emotions get in my way. My choice here wasn’t deciding the fate of just one person.
“(Give me that qualification or whatever. Then I won’t get anywhere close to here in the future.)”
[(A wise choice.)]
“(Just give it to me. Ah, do I have to sign a contract or something?)”
[(That won’t be necessary.)]
The lights on the screen flowed to the side.
[(The contract has already been set.)]
What was he talking about? It was already set?
I don’t feel any different.
It was when I had that thought.
[Achievement Unlocked
Condition: Achieve 15% progress in the Seventh Records Archives.
Reward: Permanently granted the qualification to enter and exit the Basement Floor One Records Archives.]
An imprint of a golden book glimmered on the back of my right hand before it melted into my skin and disappeared.
[A dimensional pact was formed. You will be permanently restricted from entering the Basement Floor One Records Archives.]
It was a feeling I had never felt before. Although I couldn’t see anything or feel any other effects appear... But it was as if something had clenched down on my heart.
However, that feeling lasted for only a short moment. When it disappeared without a trace, I even doubted if I had just imagined it or something. “(...What did you do to me?)”
[(Nothing. A pact was merely formed.)]
[(You can think of it as a special contract. As we formed an agreement within the labyrinth, a new rule that applies only to you and I have been created.)]
In any case, it seemed that the Overseer now had nothing more he wanted to do with me, as he quickly tried to end the conversation after the deal was made.
[(It seems our business here is over. You must be busy, so be on your way. You’ll have good news waiting for you down there as well.)]
“(Good news...?)”
[(You’ll know when you get there.)]
So mysterious for no reason. Overseer continued to make me feel like I had been taken for a fool even until the end.
[(Marx, have a good trip as well. It was great to see you again, even if it was for but a short while. Truly.)]
Hamsick let out a quiet mumble at Overseer’s short farewell. “(...No.)”
[(No? What do you mean?)]
Hamsick hesitated, then stood up straight on my shoulder. “(I’m not Marx. I’m Hamsick.)”
[(...Although I said this to you in the past, that name was given to you by the Witch. Before you lost your memories, it meant a lot to—)]
“(But that was the me before I lost my memories.)”
At those firm words, Overseer seemed to lose his words, as he remained quiet. Only after a decent amount of time passed did the voice speak again.
[(That’s right. Nothing is eternal even in this world... You have changed as well... And so have I.)]
The voice was still mechanical, but I could feel genuine emotions held in those words. It sounded both nostalgic and regretful.
[(If that is your decision, I understand. I wish for your success.)]
Overseer didn’t say anything else, so I left the control room with Hamsick on my shoulder.
As soon as we left, Hamsick worriedly asked me, “(Hey, are you alright? That pact. Is it really alright?)”
“(How would I know? Well, it doesn’t seem like it’s affecting me in any way right now.)”
“(You know that I went to talk with that guy every day while you were busy, right? Be careful. He’s a suspicious guy no matter how you look at him.)”
“(I will. Thanks for looking out for me.)”
“(...It’s only natural between friends.)”
I went quiet at the word “friends.”
Back when I visited the control room to obtain information, I had heard this from Overseer: Hamsick couldn’t leave Basement Floor One.
...And I can’t come back down ever again.
Although we both knew this fact, we didn’t talk about it.
As if it didn’t exist at all.
I understood as soon as I arrived in the underground factory what Overseer meant by “good news.”
“Mister! Come quickly! Quickly!”
“Is this...from that guy?”
“Yes! Congratulations! You said you wanted it!”
An essence had dropped while I had gone to the control room. It was the green color I wanted as well.
As I walked over in a daze, I met eyes with Raven before she shrugged. “I was going to wait a little longer and put it in a magic vial if you didn’t come soon, but you got here on time.”
“How many minutes have passed?”
“Ten minutes.”
Alright, that was good.
After checking that I still had time, I took off all the numbered items I had on me. I needed to do a bit of preparation before I ate the essence.
Step, step.
With my preparations complete, I slowly approached the essence.
Thanks to becoming level 8, I still had one essence slot open after eating the essence of Bellarios. If I could eat it without having to use a magic vial, that would be the best.
Problem is...will it work?
It was impossible to double up on essences in Dungeon and Stone, except, of course, when eating a guardian essence after having eaten the regular essence.
But in cases like that, the regular essence is just upgraded to a guardian essence. Then what about this case?
I soon learned of the result.
The moment my hand touched the essence that had floated into the air...
I can’t eat it at all in this state.
...my hand just reached through the essence, like there wasn’t a slot left in my soul for it to enter.
“Tsk.”
To be honest, I was looking forward to it. If it was possible to eat a duplicate essence, then I could have tested something then too.
Tested if it was possible to use the same skill multiple times.
It’s a shame in a lot of ways.
Giantization and Transcendence to Transcendent Giantization, and then using Giantization on top of that... It would’ve been amazing if I could’ve used Super Transcendent Giantization.
Then I’ll eat this essence after I remove the original one when I get out...
With that, I got Raven to store it in a magic vial and put aside thoughts of the essence.
“Deputy commander, are we ready to set off?”
“Yes. We can leave whenever you wish.”
“That’s good. Let’s go home.”
It was time to leave.

After leaving the Research Station and the temple, we passed through a forest and headed for our destination. A few days of travel later, we arrived at a wide lake, a place we had discovered during our search in the past.
No, to be precise, it was unlocked by us.
It had been originally blocked by a barrier before, but we were granted access after defeating a huge drone defending it.
“Get on your boats and head to your stations!”
Also, floating our boats here was the way to get off Rainbow Island. Well, this was our first time trying, at least, but since that was what Overseer told me, it was probably the case.
Tick, tock.

I activated the pocket watch that we obtained after defeating the giant drone and waited for it to make a full rotation. Then, bright lights in the colors of the rainbow tinged the lake just like they had when we first arrived at this place.
Flash!
When we regained consciousness, we were back in that windless zone we spent so hard surviving the rainy season in. I then headed to Library Island to drop Hamsick off.
“(I’m sorry. I wasn’t able to keep my promise. Even though I said I would help you find your memories.)”
“(...You still care about that? Don’t make that expression. I’ve already heard everything I needed to from Overseer... Goodbye.)”
Hamsick only said goodbye, and never said anything about seeing each other again.
So I said it instead.
“(See you... again...?)”
“(Yeah,)” I said. “(Nothing is set in stone in the world. I’m thinking of trying to find a way back here after I leave this place.)”
“(Will that be possible...?)”
“(I think it will be. And that’s why I agreed to Overseer’s offer in the first place.)”
“(...Hmph. You can if you want.)”
“(Stay safe until then. And don’t open your doors to strangers.)”

Although we didn’t have a lot of time left, I took my time to say my farewells to Hamsick before heading directly to Chief Island. Thanks to increasing our sailing pace as much as possible, we were able to arrive three days before the day Overseer warned me about.
“It’s the islaaand!”
After we got off our boats, I immediately went down into the village and touched the dimensional headstone just in case.
“The p-portal! The portal opened!”
“Th-then we can really go back home?!”
“Hurrah for Baron Yandel! Hurrah!”

Thankfully, Overseer’s promise was real, as the dimensional headstone, which previously didn’t react no matter what we did, finally activated and a blue portal was opened. However, I didn’t immediately take the portal.
I mean, I got curious, alright?
[(You will suffer a great plight if you do not escape this place within half a year. Because he will appear then.)]
Who was this “he” Overseer warned me about? Since he never told me everything in full to the very end, my curiosity couldn’t help but bubble up.
Since the portal’s opened...it wouldn’t be bad to wait a little before leaving.
I then stationed the main force in the village and went back up to the surface with only Sven Parav by my side.
“Wh-why me again...?”
“Focus. We’ll immediately go down to take the portal if you sense danger.”
“If it’s that, then I want to go down right now...and isn’t the rainy season about to begin?!”
“Since you’re leaving it at that, looks like we have some time.”
He didn’t respond.
And so, a day and another day passed, and it was now only a few hours until the time Overseer warned me about it.
Splash!
A strong wind began to blow from behind me as if warning that something would soon appear.
“Well...c-can we go down now?”
“Are you very uncomfortable right now?”
“I’ll just check one thing.” I quickly went up to the cliff to check the beachside. The silver ocean was roiling and being pulled away as if held by a powerful force.
“H-how about we get back? I’m starting to feel really scared...!”
I could tell that it was time since he was acting like that...
So lastly, I checked my map.
It’s in the direction of Stone Island...
The wind and waves were blowing and splashing in the direction of Stone Island.
If waves start to approach you during the rainy season, immediately stop whatever you’re doing and look for a place to hide.
Was it related to what was written in the village chief’s book of strange stories?
I couldn’t know, but I took Sven Parav back down to the village and then got everyone through the portal one by one.
And finally, it was my turn. I was last because of the fear that maybe the portal would disappear if I entered it first.
Rumble!
And right as I was about to take the portal, the entire village shook as if hit by an earthquake.
What’s this?
My curiosity as a gamer ignited for a second, but I didn’t go outside to check.
Yeah, if I can return someday, I could check it then. And if I couldn’t come back, there’s no need for me to know.
[Lord of Records, Recardo, begins to roam the floor.]
It was time to stop caring about it and get out of here.
Vwoong!
And with that, I thrust my body into the portal.
Basement Floor One, Records Archives.

Although there was a small difference, time flowed in here the same as it did outside the labyrinth. Around the time the rainy season began, the entire labyrinth, including the first-floor Crystal Cave would be closed...
But the portal thankfully opened.
The portal opened. But where would we end up if we took it? I expected that we would return to the first floor, but the labyrinth was already closed by this point.
It didn’t take long for my question to be answered.
[You are moved to Rafdonia.]
So when the labyrinth was closed, we were moved to the city.
Well, maybe we would be teleported to the city no matter what. Still, that wasn’t that important.
“M-Mister...”
We arrived at the Dimension Square of District Seven, the one we had used all those months ago to enter the labyrinth.
When we looked around, only me and the Anabada Clan were standing in the empty square.
Of course, that wasn’t too odd. I heard that the expedition group had used a different Dimension Square to enter the labyrinth. The same went for the Armin Adventurer Group and the Hektz Clan.
Yeah, nothing was wrong up to there. And it wasn’t as if I was waiting for people to greet us when we returned.
“Wh-why is the square so...?”
However, the square we returned to was much too different from the usual square we were all familiar with.
Fwoosh.
A suffocating smoky scent was carried in by the wind, drifting past the inspection offices that lined the street, all of which were destroyed and crumbling.
It was as if there had been a war here.
“It looks like something big happened to the city while we were away.” Amelia calmly analyzed the situation after taking in the surroundings.
“Captain! This way!” shouted a male voice from afar. “We just detected a portal signature...”
We then met eyes with the man who had climbed over the debris of the inspection office.
“Eh? Who the hell are you guys?”
After seeing the insignia on the man’s jacket, I couldn’t help but laugh.
“Where did you come from?”
Where did we come from? That was what I wanted to ask.
Just what happened here...?
Since when could these Noark bastards walk around the city as they pleased?

chapters.title: Chapter 623: District Seven (1)
paragraphs: After toiling away in the labyrinth for long enough, you could reach a point where you communicate with allies with looks alone.
Just like we were now.
I don’t know what’s going on, but let’s capture him first.
After receiving that message through my look, my allies nodded and drew their weapons.
“So you have no intention of being obedient and answering.”
Fortunately for us, the other leader seemed to have come to the same conclusion as their group charged us.
“Capture them for now!”
There were a total of fourteen enemies including their leader. Since it wasn’t a multiple of six, we couldn’t evenly divide our forces.
But well, this wasn’t the labyrinth, but the middle of the city.
[You have cast Giantization. Your threat level and physical value increase in proportion to growth in size.]
We didn’t know how strong our enemies were, so I increased my body’s size first. However, they seemed to have noticed something after seeing my enlargened body.
Our charging enemies suddenly stopped in shock.
“B-Bjorn Yandel...?”
“...It’s the Giant!”
“How is someone who went missing here...?”
Hey, thanks for recognizing me, but...
“R-run away!”
“Call for reinforcements—!”
Where do you think you’re going?
It didn’t take long to suppress the Noark forces we met in the destroyed Dimension Square.
Their numbers ended up decreasing from fourteen to twelve during the process. Ah, naturally, this wasn’t because a few of them ended up escaping. They just died while trying to run away.
There are a few skilled individuals here.
Judging by how quickly they spread out to run away, I assumed these guys trained together quite a bit. Two of their fastest members nearly got away with it when we tried to capture everyone alive.
“Good work, Erwen. Things could’ve turned messy if we let them get away.”
“...Don’t mention it.”
In any case, since we captured all of them, I approached one of them who was on his knees.
Twelve people.
It was a number I was much more comfortable with.
“Emily, take all their gear off, including from the dead two.”
I didn’t know how much time I would have, so I neutralized them while carrying out my interrogation.
And this guy seemed the perfect one to talk to.
I grabbed the leader, who had been staying silent and only looking at the ground, by his head and lifted him. “Hey, Stink Eye.”
Ainar tilted her head. “Huh? Bjorn, do you know this guy?”
“No?”
“Huh? Then how do you know his name?”
“... What are you talking about? I just called him Stink Eye because I don’t like how he’s looking at me.”
How the hell was Stink Eye the name of a person?
Every once in a while, I realized just how unaware Ainar was.
“Haha... I just...” Ainar scratched the back of her head, looking a little embarrassed, and I naturally turned my attention away from her.
“Anyway... Hey, Stink Eye.”
Even after calling out to him again, Stink Eye refused to talk, and I just carried on without waiting for him to reply.
“It’s been a while since we’ve been in the city. What are you guys doing here?”
Sure enough, he still didn’t answer me, and I immediately swung down with my hammer.
Not at the leader...
Crunch!
...but at the hand of one of his subordinates kneeling to the side.
“Aaaah!”
Subordinate A let out a pained cry at the sudden attack.

I started with him and went down the line, smashing one hand of all the other members with my hammer. I then asked the leader again, “It’s been a while since we’ve been in the city. What are you guys doing here?”
Naturally, I didn’t receive an answer, and I began to hammer down, starting from Subordinate A again. My target was nowhere else but the very same hand I destroyed on the previous rotation.
Crunch! Crunch! Crunch!

I asked the leader the same question again, and he didn’t give me an answer again. However, it seemed that the subordinates understood the method of interrogation now, as they clenched their eyes shut.
“Hold them properly this time as well, Auyen.”
As I mechanically struck down in order, one of the subordinates hurriedly spoke up. “I-I’ll—!”
I paused. “Hmm?”
“I’ll answer for you! That question!”
“Oh, really?”
Since this was the response I was aiming for, I wasn’t that surprised. The leader, however, didn’t expect his Subordinate G to betray him.
“You rat bastard...!” Stink Eye broke his silence and glared at Subordinate G.
However, as a macho member of Noark, Subordinate G didn’t take any crap either.
“What the hell do you want me to do, then? You can get through this by staying quiet, but we’re all getting pummeled here.”
“...What, do you think he’ll let you live if you answer?!”
“No. But if I’m going to die, I would rather die a painless death, no? What’s the point in staying loyal if I’m going to die anyway?”
“If your betrayal becomes known, your family in the village—”
“Fuck you!” He spat at his leader, snarling, “You bastard. Did you not even know your subordinate is an orphan with no family?”

From my perspective, Subordinate G had won this exchange. Stink Eye couldn’t retort to the logical and piercing words of his subordinate. Though, it did seem like he wanted to curse him out at the end.
“You son of a—”
I didn’t have the time to waste on watching them fight themselves. “Shut up.”
“Agh!”
“Alright, so tell me. Just why are you guys here?” I asked after shutting Stink Eye up.
Subordinate G began to explain everything that happened in the city while we were away, and the events could be summarized in two main points.

First was that around two months ago, the remnants of Noark had secretly returned to their old residence in the underground city after going outside the castle walls. And they had done it to invade Rafdonia.
“Invade...?”
“...They’re out of their minds.”
My allies were shocked as they listened to the story with me. Amelia even shook her head in disbelief, but I wasn’t that surprised. I had already heard this from Clown in the Round Table before.
But I didn’t expect them to carry it out this quickly.
Versyl looked much calmer than the rest of my allies as well, perhaps because she too had been there when Clown revealed his information.
“So? What’s the situation?” I pressed. “Did you guys win? Is that why District Seven is in this state?”
“No... We didn’t win. We’re in a bit of a standoff.”
...Tell me in detail.”
“Two days ago, we came through the sewers up into the city and successfully ambushed a few districts, and we succeeded in taking over them in a day.”

“Two days ago...?” I listened to more of his explanation and learned that today was exactly a day after the labyrinth closed. “So you aimed for when the adventurers entered the labyrinth. And a good chunk of the palace’s forces would’ve entered the labyrinth then too.”
“Yes, that’s right...”

After hearing all that, my first thought was how unlucky I was. We returned after barely scraping by, but that just happened to be when the city was being invaded. It was like I was always tripping only myself.
“I’m listening, so keep talking.”
“Ah, yes...”
Subordinate G went on to talk about the state of the battle.

They had aimed for between day one when the adventurers left for the labyrinth and day two when they returned. Thanks to that, they were able to deal with the guards of each district and had successfully taken over the city.
“We surrounded the adventurers who returned from the labyrinth yesterday and suppressed them from the square, and we’re now using them as hostages while fighting against the forces of the palace.”
That was the current situation.
“The palace also seems to value the lives of the adventurers more than regular citizens, so they haven’t pushed through yet.”
“Then why are you guys here?”

“We were on patrol. We figured the palace might send in infiltrators, and we were looking for any stragglers who were still hiding. The wizard of our patrol group said he suddenly felt something from the square...”
“Are there more patrols?”
“Not any nearby...”
From the way his words trailed off, I could tell there was something more that he was hesitating to say. It was time to use my secret weapon.
“It’s fine, you can tell me. If you are helpful, I wouldn’t be opposed to letting you live. No, I will swear upon my honor as a warrior that I will send you back alive.”
It was the warrior’s oath that I had used to quite a bit of success since the very start.

Subordinate G seemed to hesitate at that before revealing everything. “It’s around time to send in our scheduled report. If we don’t make a report at the set time, they might send another patrol group here—”
Even Stink Eye couldn’t hold back and shouted, “You son of a bitch...!”
That was probably the last lifeline they had.
Shut up, so annoying.
“This scheduled report, can you do it?”
“Yes, I can. I’ve done it a few times. He’s handed it to me a few times, saying it was annoying to do.”
“Really?”
“You bastard! Don’t you know how much I—!”
Then this guy was useless.
Crunch!
I crushed the head of his boss right in front of him, but Subordinate G only flinched before finding his calm again.
“There should be a message stone in the things you took from us. If you give it to me, I can deal with it.”
“Looks like it’s this thing.” Amelia, who had been watching from the side, immediately found the message stone and handed it to me.
“Alright, then do it. Don’t think about doing anything reckless.”
“Okay...”

With the message stone now in hand, Subordinate G reported to his higher-ups that nothing was going on with the area. Perhaps because he had done this multiple times before already, the report ended without much trouble.
And so, we resumed our conversation.
“Anyway, you said you took over a few districts. Which districts are they?”
“District Thirteen and District Seven.”
I let out a deep sigh.
“Wh-what is it...? Did I make a mistake or...?”
I was really unlucky. Among the many districts, they had successfully taken over two of them, but one of them just had to be our District Seven.
I couldn’t stop the sigh from escaping me, but I kept my emotions in check and continued with the conversation.
“It’s fine. Keep talking. What happened to the holy land?”
District Thirteen had the holy land of the beastpeople, and District Seven had the holy land of our barbarians. As the chieftain of the barbarians, I couldn’t help but be worried for my holy land.
“The holy land is currently cut off from the city.”
“Cut off?”

“I-I’m just a soldier, so I don’t know the details...but I heard that they used a magic circle created by the palace a long time ago. And I...I heard it was made to restrict the nonhumans...but I’m not sure since it’s just stuff we talk about in our group.”

Subordinate G seemed to belatedly remember that I was the chieftain of the barbarians as he quickly added on, “S-still, since it completely separated the holy land from the city, there must be relatively less damage there than here.”
Relatively.
From that word, I could tell that there was some damage done to the holy land. But well, it couldn’t be helped. I just needed to be thankful for the relativity.
“District Thirteen... What about the beastpeople, then?”
I asked that as well since I was worried for Missha’s homeland, but I couldn’t get a detailed response.
“That district is a little different, so I don’t really know...but that side probably isn’t any different.”
“Really... I see...”
Missha bit her lip. Even though they were people she hated, she seemed worried about her family.
“Yandel, it looks like we’ve got all the information we need here, so how about we move first?”
“Move?”
“Just in case. If we get surrounded here, even we’d have a difficult time.”
Following Amelia’s advice, we first decided to leave the area. The report was made without a problem, sure, but we could still be discovered by someone else.
“Then clean up everyone other than him. Don’t leave a single trace of them.”
Amelia glanced at Subordinate G. “What about him?”
“We’ll take him alive with us.”
Subordinate G immediately stood up at my answer. “I-I believed you, Lord Baron! I knew you would keep your promise!”
“Don’t make me laugh.” Amelia let out a dry laugh in disbelief.
I mean, she knew that I was a fake barbarian who didn’t care about any oaths like that.
Still, I can’t just ignore it when Ainar is here as well.
Of course, the biggest reason was that I still had more information I wanted to get out of this guy.
Pshhhh!

With Versyl’s magic and Amelia’s adventuring “gear,” the traces of the corpses were erased. We then moved as stealthily as possible. Since the entirety of District Seven was taken over by the Noarkans, we needed a hideout to stay in for the time being.
“How about that house we lived in in the past? I don’t think it’s too far from here...”

Following Erwen’s suggestion, we quickly moved to the mansion we’d once taken out a loan for. The fences were tall and there was a basement as well, so it was a pretty good location for us in many ways.
However, in the city-turned-battlefield, there was no way the mansion would have been safe.
“N-no... My house of memories... I wanted to get enough money to buy it back in the future...!”
After arriving at the building while avoiding other patrols, we saw that the second floor had collapsed from what looked to be flame magic. The surrounding area was heavily charred as well.

“Still, it’s not too bad. It just looks like this on the outside, the first floor is fine. Plus, with how it looks and all, we’ll be able to use it to hide for a while. The fences are destroyed in some places, but with the way the posts are angled, they won’t be able to get a look inside.”
Amelia gave a passing grade for the building, and we carefully stepped into it.
“Auyen. We’re going to have a meeting, so put that guy in the basement.”
“Yes.” Auyen immediately went to lock Subordinate G in the basement. “Sunlight won’t reach this place, but you’ll get your meals on time. Probably.”
He seemed really excited for some reason.

chapters.title: Chapter 624: District Seven (2)
paragraphs: After putting Subordinate G in the basement, we closed all the curtains and sat in the dark living room, then took a moment to freely share our thoughts.
“...The situation is bad.”
Versyl was the first to speak.
“Soon, they’ll realize that the patrol that found us has disappeared. When that happens, they’ll officially start searching the area. It’s only a matter of time until they find us here.”
Just waiting in this house was definitely too dangerous. Even we would have a hard time if we got surrounded.
It was the same feeling I got back during the Ice Rock Expedition. The high-ranking plunderers of Noark, including Orcules, weren’t to be underestimated.
Since they continued on to clearing the eighth floor after that, they should have gotten much stronger since then too.
I nodded, agreeing with Versyl’s assessment. “Don’t worry. I’m not planning on hiding here forever either. We need to quickly find a way to get out of here.”
“That’s a relief to hear.”
With District Seven having been taken over by Noark, we needed to escape.
Our conversation naturally flowed with that goal as the main point.
“Aren’t they occupying not just District Seven, but District Thirteen as well? It would be difficult for them to manage that wide castle wall by themselves.”
“So you want us to find an opening in their formation and go through it.”
“That’s right! If we can get over the walls, then that’s where we’ll find our allies, right?”
Erwen suggested we force our way through their encirclement.
“How about we use the sewers...? The paths are narrow, so even if we get caught, we might be able to fight them...”
Missha spoke of another path.
“...How about we don’t try anything annoying and just hide? If we hide here for a few days, the palace forces might be able to come save us...”
Ainar suggested just bunkering down due to her decreased Aggression levels.
“Auyen, tell us your ideas as well. Don’t just stay quiet.”
“Pardon? Me?”
“I’m not asking you to get a ‘right’ answer out of you. Just speak your mind and share what you would do if it were up to you. Don’t feel pressured either.”
“If I had the strength to... I would’ve gone to save the people.”
“The people...?”
“Yes... Most of the adventurers of District Seven have been taken as hostages...”
And navigator Auyen gave quite an unexpected answer as well.
As our attention fell on him, Auyen became startled and started to babble, “O-of course, I’m far from a hero like that...! P-please ignore what I said!”
However...
“It’s not a bad idea.”

Auyen’s idea seemed to have struck a chord with Amelia as she looked at me while saying, “Yandel, maybe this is an opportunity. They don’t know that we exist. They’re only aware of the forces of the palace situated beyond the walls.”
“So you’re saying we should use this opportunity to attack them from the inside.”

“That’s right. If we succeed, it’ll be a great accomplishment. Two cities of Ravigion and then some were taken over by a foreign adversary. You might even receive recognition greater than the nobles who stopped the Heretical Duke during the Iron Wall Rebellion.”

What Amelia said held some truth as well. In the long history of Rafdonia, there were only a handful of incidents as huge as this. If we succeeded, we would receive a myriad of rewards, and I could even aim for a promotion to my noble rank. My standing in the nonhuman noble alliance of Melbeth would increase greatly as well.
“...We’ll need to get a bit more information on this. Auyen, go grab the guy from the basement.”
I fell into deep contemplation.

After being freed from where he was locked in the basement, Subordinate G gave us the whole truth as if he were really on our side. Thanks to that, we were able to learn more about the current state of District Seven.
“The adventurers are imprisoned all over the district in small groups.”
The adventurers, who possess multiple times more combat power than ordinary citizens, and who usually worked as the guards of the city, were being held in three major spots.
The underground prison of the Adventurers’ Guild branches.
The underground prison of the temples of the Three Gods Church.
And the underground prisons of the Public Peace Agency of District Seven.

Really, those three covered the bases, but there were actually dozens of locations where they were being held. There were multiple temples and Adventurers’ Guild branches in District Seven, and the Public Peace Agency also had multiple lower-level branches as well.
“Since so many adventurers were taken hostage, this was the only way to imprison all of them...”
However, it was still too early to say if this was good or bad for us.
Since they are all so spread out, it might be easier for us to save any specific one of them...

But on the other hand, it was obvious that our intrusion would be noticed after hitting only a few locations. No matter how fast we moved, we couldn’t do anything about the distance between the prisons.
“But the upside is our forces will grow stronger every time we visit one.”
“P-pardon...?” Subordinate G stuttered. “A-are you perhaps planning on saving them...?”
“Why are you curious about that?”

In any case, the next piece of information we received was the routes of the patrols, including the number of soldiers stationed on the walls. Well, it wasn’t like a low-ranking soldier like him could tell us everything in detail.
“Oh, and the civilians would be grouped up near the walls. I heard they’re holding on by slowly freeing them whenever the pressure from the palace increases too much...”
Still, there was a difference between not knowing something and knowing at least a bit about something.
“Alright, then go back to your home.”
“...My home?”
“Auyen will guide you.”
After putting Subordinate G back in the basement, we resumed our meeting.
“From your expression, I can already tell that you’ve made your decision.”
“...Can you really?”
“Somewhat. So, what will you do?”
I could tell that this was more of a rhetorical question, so I didn’t drag it out and immediately answered her. “We’ll save the hostages and escape the city together.”
“Plan?” Amelia asked curtly.
I answered without a hint of hesitation. “We’ll have to think about that now. Everyone, together.”
I only made that decision because I concluded that it was doable, I hadn’t made a detailed plan yet. Plus, the more the merrier when it came to strategizing details like that.
“Alright, then let’s begin.”

With that, our plan-setting meeting was underway. We spent time deciding which prisons to attack first and which routes to use, and we discussed if it would be best to go through the castle wall for our escape or if we wanted to use the sewers. That, and if we chose the walls, then which part of the walls to take.
Eventually, the plan started to take shape.
In the silence of a short pause in our discussion, Missha carefully spoke up.
“Isn’t it...a little odd?” she mumbled to herself.
At that, Erwen asked with a displeased tone, “Odd?”
“I mean...what do the people from Noark want? There are a few things I just don’t get.”
“Isn’t what they want obvious? They just want to steal what is ours and they want themselves to become the masters of the world.”

“That’s true...but this is too reckless.” Missha quickly continued, saying, “They should know that no matter how long they resist using these hostages, they’re only delaying their defeat. Then why did they invade us?”
Erwen couldn’t give an easy answer to that question.

To be honest, everyone here had questioned what Missha brought up at least once after coming here. With their current structure, Noark could never win. Even if they had ten times the number of hostages with them, the palace wasn’t afraid to spill blood if need be.
And there’s no way that Noark doesn’t know that.
The invasion could only end with their defeat.
So then, why did the Noarkans do something so foolish? Did they just not think that far ahead?
No, the probability of that was close to zero.
“It’s also odd that they aimed for two districts at once. They’re so unstable that holding just one district would be difficult...”
“And there’s Bifron between District Seven and District Thirteen, so it’s even more difficult to defend their territories.”
“...That’s right. So why did they do this? Are they aiming to do something in Bifron?”
“I don’t know yet, but it’s clear that they’ve got a plan in motion.”
Yeah, at this point, it made more sense that they were moving with a hidden goal.
“Then what about them taking those hostages?”
“They need the time to carry out their plan.”
“Then we’ll need to move as quickly as possible. We don’t know what the situation will come to and what they’ll do if we give them the time.”
Really, seven heads were better than one.
As we continued to hash out points, we realized that we were also on a time limit. We couldn’t know for sure how much time we had, but everyone at least understood that we would need to move quickly.
“...Then our plan of attack is set. Did everyone memorize everything?”
“No, I’m not—”
“You’re fine, Ainar. You can just sit next to Versyl.”
“Oh! Really?”
Yeah. I never expected you to memorize this anyway.
The best course of action was to just put Ainar next to someone smart.
“Then our preparations are complete. Let’s get going.”
We finished our preparations and were about to set off when Ainar spoke up.
“Bjoooorn! The basement! What about that guy in the basement? You swore that you would save him!”
I sighed. Why was she so good at remembering useless things like this? Maybe she had a gene that made her never forget any oaths even though she couldn’t remember other things properly.
I couldn’t break my oaths in front of Ainar without problems arising, not when she didn’t know I was a player. However, the situation obviously didn’t turn into a huge problem this time either.
“What’s the problem? Didn’t I save him?”
“Then do I need to keep him around, continue feeding him, and take care of him forever?”
“Uh...not really...”
“Then it’s fine. Leave him be. He’ll do fine on his own. And if he starves to death, then that’s his fate.”
“Oh...really?”
“Ainar! Stop saying useless things and stand next to Versyl! That is your place!”
“Got it!”
Alright, with that, Ainar was convinced.
Creak, boom!
Alright, let’s go.
After leaving the damaged building, we moved as stealthily as possible to avoid the patrols. Based on their movement, our presence hadn’t been revealed yet.
“This way.”

Amelia was designated as our guide. She was our resident expert for things like stealth and infiltration. We stopped when she told us to stop and moved when she told us to move, and eventually, we arrived at our destination exactly at the time we estimated during our planning.
“Just like that guy said, there aren’t that many guards here.”
We were at the great temple of Reatlas I had visited often. It was the starting point of our rescue campaign today.
After scouting the area from the second floor of the building opposite it on the street, we officially put our plan into action.
Well, I said that, but all I had to do was wait.
“We’ll be back soon.”
Amelia and Missha had stealth skills, and Erwen was capable of ranged assassinations. Those three special operations members left the building as a group.
A short while later, we received a signal. As we came down from the building and approached the main gate of the temple, we could see the ones who had been defending it had collapsed.
Pshhhhh!
After using Amelia’s adventuring gear to remove any traces of them, we entered the great temple.
Stab! Crunch! Pshwoo!
We followed after Amelia and continued with the operation. However, a long tail was bound to be stepped on.
“Looks like...we got found out, right?” Erwen mumbled.
Amelia furrowed her brow and nodded. “It seems so. Considering how noisy it’s become now.”
So she said, but I couldn’t hear anything with my ears. But that didn’t mean I could dismiss her statement.
“Then how did we get discovered?”
“Who knows? There are plenty of ways, and people with mystical abilities everywhere. Ask questions later, let’s increase our pace.”
“Sure.”
Damn, I honestly wished we could have finished our business here quietly and had some time left over.
“The palace! The palace forces are here!”

As we went underground to where the prisons were, the soldiers that had been crawling around the temple appeared and attacked us. Killing them all before descending the steps could have been a method we took, but that would have taken us too long.
“Yandel, we’ll deal with this place, so keep going.”
“Alright.”
After leaving my allies to deal with those on the surface, I quickly headed down.
The underground prison was more spacious than the building above. The prison warden role must be taken on by shifts one by one because I only found one person down in the prison.
“D-don’t come closer!”
The warden seemed to have heard the news from above as well, as he charged at me with his weapon.
Crunch!
I merely crushed his head with a swing of my hammer. The adventurers who were trapped seemed to also realize the situation.
“A rescue team...?”
“Why is there only one person...?”
“Wait...he looks familiar...”
“Baron Yandel! It’s Baron Yandel!”
“The giant is here...!”
The cheers echoed throughout the underground were loud enough to hurt my ears, but I took it in stride.
Yeah, it was great to hear that they at least had the energy to shout. I should use the opportunity to raise my favorability with them.
“Wait for me! I, Bjorn, son of Yandel, am here to save you!”
“Yeah! Wahoo!”
After declaring myself their savior, I approached the dead warden and reached for the keys on his belt—
...He doesn’t have any keys?
That was a little unexpected, but I didn’t panic. No problem was impossible to solve in the world.
If one had enough strength, that was.
Creak!
I gathered some of my strength, and the steel bars bent like spoons.
“Th-thank you! Thank you!”
“Did the palace send you, Your Lordship?”
“I heard that you went missing...”
The trapped adventurers walked between the bent bars and each asked a question. Although it was good to see them act friendly with me, I didn’t have the time to kindly answer all their questions.
“Right, right. I’ll explain everything later, so hold out your hands.”
“Oh...! Yes!”

I first undid the shackles on the adventurers’ wrists with my bare hands like I was cracking open nuts. Since they were magic tools designed to seal essences, their physical durability was pretty low.
“Once you’re free, hurry above ground and help the ones outside. Don’t block the way.”
“Uh...do you perhaps know where my equipment is...?”
“Go ask that outside. I don’t know either.”
“Okay!”
I solved all the problems with my strength without having to go on an annoying quest to find the keys, so it didn’t take long to free all the adventurers.
“Below us! The priests and wizards are imprisoned on the second underground floor!”
Oh, so there was a second floor. I did wonder why there were only ordinary adventurers here.
“I, Bjorn, son of Yandel, have come to save you all!”
And so, I went down to the second underground floor to gain their favorability again before beginning my rescue operation.
After I saved everyone and returned to the surface, I saw they had dealt with their problems there too.
“You’ve worked hard, Mister.”
“You guys worked harder. It’s fine. More importantly, priest! Is there any priest here of archbishop rank or above? The more the merrier!”
I summoned the priests among the saved adventurers. Fortunately, due to our location, there were at least a dozen priests of archbishop rank and above.
“...Were you perhaps hurt anywhere?”
“Nothing like that. We need your help for the next phase of the plan.”
“Ah, I see! We’ll help you with everything we have. But...what do you need us to do?”
“Pray for us.”
“And by praying...you mean...?”
Hearing the dumbfounded reactions of the priests, I replied with a grin. “I want to erase my essence. Right now.”
Yeah, to do something great, we first needed to get stronger.

[The Essence of Orc Hero that seeped into your soul was removed. Strength has decreased by -70. Dexterity has decreased by -35. Aggression has decreased by -40. Physical Resistance has decreased by -20...]
[The Essence of ??? has seeped deep into your soul.]

chapters.title: Chapter 625: District Seven (3)
paragraphs: Erasing essences.

Although it was a skill that any priest who was archbishop rank or higher must possess, there was one additional condition to be met before they could remove an essence: It was a feat only possible inside a temple.

It was for that very reason that many Noarkans ended up turning into trash characters after eating the wrong essence. They needed to risk their lives if they wanted to open up a slot, even more so if their face was widely known.

With that, I staggered a little, sighing as I returned the blue shortsword I received from the priest. The emptiness I felt every time I erased an essence was too heavy to ignore. It was difficult to explain, not just the feeling of having my stats decreased, but...
It feels like a portion of my soul was cut away.
That was the closest comparison I could make.
I could understand why this world called MP “soul power.”
Figuring I might feel better if I filled the empty slot with something else, I quickly took out a magic vial from my sub-space.
Arbet and Oomdal plus the Giantization of the Orc Hero, all combined into one custom essence.
After taking out the stopper, I tossed it back into my mouth as if drinking a potion.
It left me wondering then. If I got this while playing the game, what would the name of the custom monster pop up as?
[The Essence of ??? has seeped deep into your soul.]
Hmm, well...they wouldn’t just put up a few question marks and call it a day, right?
With no way to find out, I stopped thinking about useless things and focused on the changes happening to my body.

There was a concept called “taming” an essence among adventurers. Something about how if one focused deeply on the changes happening to their body when consuming an essence, one would become more proficient with new abilities from the get-go.
[Strength has increased by +100.]
Flames that made me feel I could lift anything embedded themselves in my body. Considering just the base strength increase, it probably wasn’t at the level of an Ogre’s, though.
[Jumping Power has increased by +120.]
The muscles in my thighs strengthened.
[Physical Resistance has increased by +80.]
My tough skin became even tougher.
[Hearing has increased by +60.]
And the sounds permeating through the air became clearer.
No matter how much I focused, these were the only changes I could sense right off the bat. Not to say that was all there was to it, of course.

[Dark Resistance has increased by +40. Soul Power has increased by +50. Natural Regeneration has increased by +80. Endurance has increased by +60. Bone Strength has increased by +60. Absorption has increased by +60.]

Pure-stats-wise, Ogre was pretty high on the list of essences, but when taking into account all stats on the whole, nothing could compete with Arbet. The trade-off was that Arbet’s skills were terrible. However, that didn’t apply to me since I used the basement floor’s system to extract only the stats.

I sighed, and after getting used to the changes in my stats, I carefully opened my sub-space. I had stored all the numbered items I had been using there, specifically because of the passive skill of Oomdal.
[Soul Connection: The piece of equipment you first obtain becomes soul-bound and obtains additional abilities.]
It worked on the first piece of equipment you obtained after getting the skill.
Although that was the description of the skill in the game, the passive was only activated on numbered items.
And you can’t change which one it activates later if you connect to the wrong one.
Since I could only connect one item, I needed to be very careful when handling Oomdal’s essence. If I had eaten the essence while in my full loadout, it would randomly pick one of them.
With that, I reached into the sub-space and imagined the item I wanted to take out in detail, and held tightly onto that object.
No. 87, Karul’s Demon Grinder...is obviously not it.
The Demon Grinder was a high-quality weapon, so selecting it would definitely make it stronger.
But it’s not worth spending an entire passive slot for it.
Countless passives worked with the shield barbarian. I would have taken one of those passives instead of this one in my build order, but only if I didn’t have this one as well.
[You have equipped No. 3, Wall of Aegis.]
[General Item Level has increased by +18,600.]
I chose the strongest shield, the one I would only have been able to obtain much later.
[Call of the Soul. No. 3, Wall of Aegis, becomes permanently bound to the character.]
[Bound items cannot be destroyed.]

[All effects of the bound item are increased by 10 percent. When defeating monsters, the bound item will also receive separate experience points, and after it reaches a certain level, it will obtain a unique effect.]
This shield could now grow.

Soul Connection was a core skill I always picked up when I built my shield dwarf, which utilized synergies between numbered items. Naturally, I had done quite a bit of research for that build, and I understood most of the unique effects of the high-ranking equipment.
The unique effect is given when it reaches level nine.

Of course, the skill was pretty good even without unlocking the item’s unique effect. The effectiveness of the gear would increase by 5 percent per level. When grown to level nine, the initial 10 percent combined with the 40 percent gained from leveling up allowed for a total enhancement effect of 50 percent.
Still, it’s a bit of a waste that I doubled up on the indestructibility effect...

But honestly, since most of the high-ranking numbered items were indestructible, to begin with, it wasn’t all that bad of a concession. The binding effect, too, couldn’t be seen as a downside either since I never planned on selling the shield.
Giantization.

After checking that the active skill was also activated properly, I took a look around. It seemed that everyone else was finishing up with theirs as well. It wasn’t just me who had to reformat a few things, after all.
[The Essence of ??? has seeped into Amelia Rainwales’s soul.]
[The Essence of ??? has seeped into Missha Karlstein’s soul.]
[The Essence of ??? has seeped into Erwen Fornacci di Tersia’s soul.]
The three sisters(?) had their custom essences applied to them.
[The Essence of ??? has seeped into Ainar Fenelin’s soul.]
[The Essence of ??? has seeped into Ainar Fenelin’s soul.]
Ainar slotted in two custom essences, erasing the essence of Smug and Vitlan and losing Mandel Oil and Wildness Control in the process. The change was instantaneous.
I think the combined Aggression value of the two essences was around 100?
Theoretically, that should be able to perfectly cover the Aggression lost from eating the essence of Hipramajent.
It was not too difficult at all to recognize that Ainar had returned to normal.
“Behel-LAAAAAA!”
Yeah, that was what a barbarian battle cry sounded like.
I looked at her with pride as she roared loud enough to echo throughout the entire temple, and Amelia took the opportunity to approach me.
“How is your new essence? Do you like it?” I asked.
“We’ll talk about that later. We need to proceed to the next step before any more time passes.”
You know, you could show some joy at your new essence, even if you didn’t want to roar like Ainar.
“...Got it.”
She sighed. “I like it. Don’t look so sad.”
“Oh, really?”
In any case, since I agreed that we didn’t have a lot of time, I immediately proceeded to the next step.
“Everyone, attention!”
Before I took these guys to attack another prison, I needed to do something first.
“This is a historic moment!” I declared.
Everyone noticed that a speech was about to be given. They all shut their mouths and looked at me.
None of them found it boring. In fact, most looked on with excitement in their eyes.
“Rafdonia is currently under attack. Those dirty rat bastards who lived in the sewers have dared to lust after our city.”
I learned this during my life as a barbarian: Apparently, I had a knack for speeches. I was pretty sure Amelia said I was born for it or something.
“And now! We were lucky to be living here!”
“Lucky...?”
“Among the many districts of the city, aren’t we unlucky for it to have been ours?”
Question marks appeared over the heads of the audience as I continued my speech. They were all valid questions. However, that was why...
Now.
Right as the mood was about to fall, I barreled ahead with my speech.
“No! This is a blessing for us! We were given an opportunity! An opportunity to save the city and achieve a great accomplishment that has never been seen before!”
I didn’t need to explain. These guys were adventurers to their cores. I knew better than anyone else what they wanted.

“Also, I make this promise to you here and now. When everything is over, I, Bjorn, son of Yandel, will dare to declare it in front of the palace! That it wasn’t my accomplishment alone. That the city was saved with your blood, sweat, and tears as well!”
I raised my fist high, and cheers erupted as if they had been waiting for the signal.
“Yeaaah!”
Was it because I was now famous? Or was it because I had gotten used to it after so long?
Whatever the case, I got the feeling that shouting like this was becoming easier and easier.
Anyway, after putting on this performance, no one should doubt my intentions later...
Unlike the heated speech I gave, I looked coldly at the audience before raising my voice again.
“However!”
The adventurers closed their mouths again in anticipation of the rest of my speech.
“The enemy is strong! The rats have grown big by stealing from our homes, and we will need to spill our blood if we want to rout them out!”
Even as I gave words of warning, the adventurers only took this danger as a new opportunity.
“It doesn’t matter!”
“Kill them all!”
Well, that wasn’t all bad, but I needed to get to my point.

“Ahem! I understand your courage and spirit. However! As a noble of Rafdonia, as a warrior and an adventurer, and as one who loves this city more than anyone, I hope that you do not bleed more than necessary. I pray that you return alive to the arms of your family.”
This speech was just a setup for what I did next.
“With that, I, Bjorn, son of Yandel, have decided. I will now distribute essences to you all!”
You know the saying of more the merrier?
This was exactly that.
When I declared that I would freely distribute the essences, the expressions on the adventurers’ faces changed. An understandable reaction, given that what I was doing was incomprehensible.
Why did that barbarian say something so absurd after saying something so cool?
The reactions of my allies weren’t much different either.
“If you’re saying you’re distributing the essences...”
“Are you talking about the ones we got from Basement Floor One?”
“Why give out those precious...?”
Only Amelia stayed calm.
She knew. Freely giving these out would give me an even bigger gain in the end.
It may be obvious, but it wasn’t just to decrease the number of essences that would go to our dormant enemy, the palace.
Think about it.
If we distribute the essences here, who would be able to guess how many we have left?
In other words, I would hand out the bad essences to the adventurers and hold onto the precious ones to eat later. The palace had no way of knowing that we distributed only the low-quality ones.
It might be trashy for me to say this...but it’s inevitable for casualties to exist in war.
How would they investigate it? How would they know if someone who died had passed on with a good or bad essence?
My motive was clear as well. How could they fault me if I were to say that I gave them out for the good of the city?
Yeah, things are bound to disappear here and there during a war.
This was what we called “tax evasion.”
Like those Asian stores that only accept cash?
Anyway, that wasn’t important.
“Here, here! All of you, come here! Don’t push! There are enough essences to go around!”
I began to officially distribute the essences.

chapters.title: Chapter 626: District Seven (4)
paragraphs: After the surprise attack to reclaim the great temple of the Reatlas Church—our first target—we moved through our planned routes to save the adventurers who were imprisoned across the many facilities of the city.
“You are...giving us essences?”
“That’s right! You need to become stronger to increase our chances of saving this city! Here, take it!”
Every time we completed a rescue operation, we distributed essences.

I didn’t just give whatever to whomever, of course. I only gave one essence to the highest-ranking adventurers we saved. I needed to do this to keep some appearances up with the palace. It wasn’t as though we had that many essences from Basement Floor One either.
Alright, then that’s the end of the essence distribution.
After freeing the District Seven Public Peace Agency branch, the fourth operation on our route, we used up all the essences we had for distribution.
“So...” Auyen began. “Shouldn’t we at least record which essence we gave to whom?”
He and my other allies who still couldn’t understand my tax evasion scheme were concerned about my shocking actions, though the worry came belatedly.
“Since this is the property of the palace, they’ll definitely try to investigate this even though we did this with a good motive.”
Well, that was true. But so what?
Most people who made “mistakes” like this could look very suspicious, though.
“Nah, what’s the point in recording things like that? That’s tedious.”
I was a barbarian. It wasn’t odd for me to handle things as a barbarian would.
“If it’s too tedious for you, then I can go now and ask the others to start a record—”
“It’s fine!” I boomed. “We’re already busy. Are you going to spend your time checking up on all those little things one by one?”
“Still...”
I sighed. Really, this guy. I was thankful that he was worried for me.
“Auyen, I told you it’s fine,” I said sternly, lowering my voice.
Auyen caught himself and closed his mouth. It seemed that he had finally realized I had hidden intentions.
But it doesn’t look like he knows exactly what I’m trying to do.

I guess it wasn’t surprising since even Amelia of all people was shocked to all hell when I first told her of the plan. She said something about how I was the only person in the world who would try something so reckless against the palace.
“Bjooorn! So when are we moving to our next spot? I want to fight again! Raaah!”
I was getting ready to set out soon anyway, but Ainar couldn’t wait even that long and came to hurry me up.
...Maybe I should’ve only put half as much Aggression in?

After recovering her Aggression, Ainar seemed to be embarrassed about that dark period in her past, considering how she was being much more proactive than she ever was before. It gave me the feeling that she could have been at the level of a normal person if I only put half as much Aggression into her essence.
Nah, then she wouldn’t be a spear barbarian. Just a spearwoman.
This was how a barbarian should be. To be honest, as a barbarian lord, I was glad to see Ainar recover her active self.
I even changed Ainar’s position as a result. Originally, she was to stay next to Versyl and protect the rear.
“Roar, Ainar.”
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
But now, she was following after me and destroying everything on the frontlines and even using her new skills as well.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Indomitable Soul. Physical stats will greatly increase for a set duration. All status conditions that restrict actions are decreased by 80%.]

Her newly acquired battle buff allowed Ainar to plow through the battlefield like a chariot. Although it wasn’t a skill that gave her CC immunity or a cleansing effect, the 80 percent resistance practically made her unstoppable.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Focus Strike.]
However, she wasn’t able to put the core skill of the spear barbarian, Focus Strike, to effective use.
[When the next attack deals damage, the effects of all piercing-type skills will be applied.]
The only piercing skill she had was Trident, after all.
That was why I advised her not to use it too much so she could save her mana, but Ainar didn’t seem to want to listen to me. How could she hold back when her spear glowed bright like that?
As soon as the city problem is dealt with, I’ll need to and buy some attack skills to feed her.
If we could get just three piercing skills for her, Focus Strike would function on a level greater than a rank 5 skill. Even then, the true worth of this skill lay elsewhere.
I guess in a sense, this skill is also a switch type?

The condition for Focus Strike was that it utilized piercing-type skills. Because of that, she could utilize skills of other classes that could only be used with bows or ranged weapons. It was also why Focus Strike became the core skill of the spear barbarian build.
“Raaaaah!”

In any case, irrelevant to the inefficiencies of her current Focus Strike, Ainar continued to rampage around the battlefield, reminiscent of when she was called the Wild Sword. Actually, she put on an even greater show than that.
With the upgrades she received, her base stats had become incredibly high.
[Ainar Fenelin has used an attack skill for the tenth time. Passive skill War Machine temporarily greatly decreases the damage taken.]
[Ainar Fenelin has failed to defend. Passive skill Perseverance slightly increases all resistances.]
And thanks to getting two defensive passives, her battle stability had greatly improved.
Stab!
Her damage increased significantly as well.

She may have been better at fighting against hordes of weaker enemies in the past, but her single-target damage was incomparable at this point. Since the Verdurous Giant Spear was the peak of spear-type weapons, just stabbing at things allowed the weapon to pierce through most armor and shields.
“Since when...did Wild Sword start using spears?”
“But it looks like she’s stronger with it than when she used the sword...”
“...The Divine Spear! The Divine Spear has appeared!”
When she heard the adventurers make a fuss while giving her a new title, Ainar asked me, “Bjorn, what’s a divine spear?”
“It’s someone who’s good with the spear.”
“Whoa! I’m a divine speeeaaar!”
Ainar now had a new title.
[Ainar Fenelin’s Fame stat has increased by +1.]
[Ainar Fenelin’s Fame stat has increased by +1.]
[Ainar Fenelin’s Fame stat has increased by +1.]
[Ainar Fenelin’s Fame stat has increased by +1.]
[Ainar Fenelin’s Fame stat has...]
After we returned from the basement floor, we received a lot of attention from the adventurers who followed us, although most of them didn’t leave as big of an impact as Ainar did.
“What’s that shield...?”
“I don’t know. But I can tell it’s not any ordinary piece of equipment.”
“From what I can tell, the Giant’s women have also become stronger.”
It wasn’t just me either. Amelia, Missha, and Erwen had become much stronger with their new essences and were praised by the adventurers.
“...I don’t know what sort of adventuring he did there, but the Giant has wings on his back now.”
“What’s the point in getting surprised now? He’s an adventurer who has left his name on the Stone of Honor. Even when that man dies, he will be remembered as a legend of this city.”

It was a little embarrassing, but he wasn’t completely wrong either. Through this adventure, we gained power to progress even further. We would need to deal with our current predicament before I could think of any of that, of course.
“...It’s empty here as well.”
We reached the underground prison of the Adventurers’ Guild’s western branch, the ninth destination on our route. However, when we arrived, the underground prison had already been emptied.
“Looks like us defeating them handily in the last battle left a mark.”
“The other facilities should be looking similar to this.”

From the third facility onward, the Noarkans became aware of our presence and readied quite a bit to fight back, leading to fierce battles. However, after the seventh facility, their forces became weaker and weaker to the point where the ones who should be guarding the prisons and the ones who should be in them were both gone when we arrived.

It wasn’t unexpected by any means. No matter how much of a mess we made here, the Noarkans’ main concern was still the palace forces from beyond the walls. They needed to focus the majority of their forces around the walls just in case, and if they pulled too many people our way to suppress us, the palace would probably notice that something was happening in the district.
Simply put, they could neither ignore us nor try to overpower us at once.
Tsk, looks like it’s going to be difficult to get the palace’s help.
Honestly, there was a best-case scenario I was hoping would occur as we went about our plan. It was for palace soldiers to push through using the opening we created.

The news of the Basement Floor One expedition’s return would have already been relayed to the palace. They would know that we were in District Seven, and I hoped they would notice something was up when they saw the Noarkan soldiers being moved away from the castle walls.
“We’ll need to progress to the next step of the plan,” I determined.
However, you couldn’t expect everything to go your way in life. It was something I had confronted countless times in my years. All I could do here was to make my decisions quickly.
“By next step of the plan...”
“I’ve already told everyone, so why do you ask like you don’t know? We will use our current strength to break through the wall and leave the district.”
I shared this bit of information with my clan members during the planning process.
It looked like, however, I had perhaps forgotten to tell the adventurers who were just freed.
“Huh...? What do you mean?”
“From what I heard, the walls are crawling with those Noark bastards...”
The adventurers who overheard me grew unsettled.
“Will it work with just us?”
“We don’t even have proper gear on us!”
“I know that you think this is a good plan, but I can’t help but be a little wary and express to you my concern about this move...”
Honestly, I had a lot of ways I could persuade these guys.

We were strong enough to at least attempt it. Also, if we struck first and the palace soldiers got wind of it, there was a very high chance they would support us. No matter how injured we got, we would be healed if we could just get over the wall, and so on.
If I could just smooth out their fears with words like that, they would be convinced and follow me.
“Ah, shut up. I don’t know why you adults are whining so much.”
“...Pardon?”
Looking at the stunned adventurers, I spoke directly to them. “Those who are afraid can stay behind. Then isn’t that problem solved?”
“...What?”
“What are you confused about? Did you think I was going to try and persuade you or something?”
They probably did expect it, seeing how they became speechless.
Hey, I ain’t your dad.
“Set off!”
Without the need for any longer conversations, I stood at the front and started moving, and that was enough.
“...A-are you going to stay behind?”
“Are you nuts? We need to follow him!”
“The baron must have a plan if he’s acting like this. I trust in the baron!”
From what I could tell, I saved twenty minutes with that.

Since District Seven was practically my home, it wasn’t difficult to find the paths to move quickly through this ruined city. We could see the tall walls even from here, anyway. However, the problem was that the closer we got to the walls, the forces of Noark who noticed us began to approach us.
“Looks like there are at least twenty times more of them than us.”
“The problem is that this isn’t all of them. There will be more if we waste time here.”
It wasn’t just that their numbers were greater. The Noarkan squad who came to stop us had a level of aura to them, and one of them was someone I was quite familiar with.
“Looks like you ended up crawling back to life even from that place, Bjorn Yandel? It would’ve been better if you could’ve just died there.”
I smirked at the one who called out to me from afar.
“Pshe.”
This guy was still the same as ever.

chapters.title: Chapter 627: District Seven (5)
paragraphs: The Corpse Collector, Abed Necrapeto. A member of the criminal organization Orcules, who coveted elitism, and a member of the Round Table, which had now dissolved.
He wasn’t the only familiar face here.
“Th-the Wailing Witch...!”
The Black Wizard, Lyranne Vivian.
“An old warrior wearing dark red armor... That man must be...!”
The Blood Knight gained infamy after killing a palace knight captain and escaping long ago.
Alongside those I fought against on the Dark Continent were also criminals there whom I only knew through rumors and hearsay, confirmed by their appearances.
There were a few I had never seen before too, of course. Although I had been in researching and studying the members of Orcules, there were still a few people on whom I drew blanks.
...Are they new?
That was the sense I got for some reason, but still, they didn’t feel like fledglings to me at all. No, more than likely, they were difficult opponents to face.

Noark had invested a fair bit of its resources into nurturing the next generation after taking over the eighth floor for themselves. I had even fought against a few of their finest during the Ice Rock Expedition, so I knew their strengths well.
One point of relief was that the captain who possessed the tricky floor essence was nowhere to be seen.
However, as soon as we came face to face with them, Erwen’s eyes beamed with killing intent. To be honest, I was worried that she would do something reckless.
“I’m fine. Don’t worry about me.”

Despite that, her voice was calm, perhaps to reassure me, and her killing intent lessened in intensity. It had been a while since that day, after all. Or maybe, it was the result of the many things she had experienced since then. In the end, Erwen now seemed able to maturely control her emotions.
“Even if it’s not today...I’ll kill them all one day. So it’s fine.”
Well, it certainly didn’t seem like her emotions had faded much.
Still, what a good turn of events. And honestly, it wasn’t as if I was any different from her.
The palace looked worse at a passing glance because they offended me, but from pure resentment alone, these guys took the cake.
Dragon Slayer, Regal Vagos.
That guy, too, had been a member of Orcules.
A quiet standoff continued as the air grew thick with tension. Then, I took a step forward.
I mean, look at how many people were here for us. Since a sizable force had left the walls, those palace soldiers should have realized what was going on at some point if I had given them time.
“Ah, have you already given up? That’s not fun at all... Hmm? Can you at least say something—”
I cut off his haughty words as I said, “It’s been a while.”
“Pshehe, so now you use that slick mouth of—”
“Toy Collector.”

To be honest, I wanted to just charge in without thinking as I did against the Lighthouse Keeper on the Dark Continent, but there were too many factors to consider here. Our main goal was to escape. If this guy made up his mind to flee, then chasing after him would waste all my time.
...I need to pick up a movement option soon.
With that, I shelved my idea of beating this guy up.
“T-Toy Collector!” he burst in a move to pretend the personal attack didn’t affect him at all. “Well, that’s not too far off! I will treat you like a toy after I kill you!”
Raising his voice, of course, did nothing to help him look mature.
“How about you go and look for a new essence as well? If you look around the world long enough, you should be able to get one that increases the size of your—”
“Enough. Stop making fun of this man.”

As I went to say something even more hurtful, a man stopped me. However, considering how Clown, who had a pretty big ego, didn’t say anything to the interjection, I could tell this man held quite a high position.
Who is he?
Amelia, who was standing directly behind me, noticed my puzzlement and whispered in my ear, “He’s Roland Banozant. The vice-captain of Orcules.”
I didn’t notice him immediately due to his unassuming appearance, but he was quite the famous guy.
Demon Eyes, Roland Banozant.
He was the high-ranking ability user who one-shot beheaded the previous vice-captain and took the number two spot ten years ago.
“Is it true that this guy killed the previous vice-captain?” I whispered back.
“Yes. He’s the one who eliminated the previous vice-captain as soon as they were found to be communicating with the palace.”
“Hmm, I see...”
Anyway, that lessened my worry a little. If the vice-captain was in District Seven, it probably meant that the captain was in District Thirteen, which meant I wouldn’t be meeting the captain today.
Of course, that didn’t mean that the vice-captain was an easy opponent.
“Yandel, if possible, I advise that you don’t converse with that per—”
At that moment, I sensed a wave of mana swell between me and him, cutting off the sound of whatever Amelia was trying to say.
It’s not voice control magic...
So it was a skill.
I gestured to Amelia to not worry before turning to speak with the vice-captain.
“It seems that woman introduced me, so I will spare my breath,” he noted. “Bjorn, son of Yandel. I have an offer for you.”
“An offer...”

When I hinted that I would at least hear him out, the vice-captain immediately got to the point. “A storm will soon come that will devour everything. And a hole-ridden ship won’t ever be able to endure that storm.”
“Are you saying the palace is that hole-ridden ship?”
“Of course. If not, why would we be doing something like this? Abandon that sinking ship and join us.”
I was a little disappointed at the vice-captain’s offer. Too predictable, maybe? I had been genuinely curious about what sort of offer he would make me.
“...Could I take some time to think?”
The vice-captain smirked. “So you refuse.”
“No, how did you get that from what I said? I just said I wanted to think about it.”
“You are an enemy of interest for us. That is why we investigated you quite thoroughly. For you, isn’t asking for time to think just a strategy to buy time?”
What the hell was with this bastard?

Those piercing words left me speechless. However, I had to admit he wasn’t pulling them from nowhere. It was just how baseball players would research the behavior of pitchers. The guy had investigated my behavioral patterns as well.
Even so, I said, “You didn’t investigate shit. I mean, if you investigated properly, wouldn’t you already know? What my answer will be.”
The vice-captain didn’t react, not even as I mocked him. He just asked back with the same tone as before, “So, what is your answer?”
“I refuse.”
“Your reason?”
“Dunno? I just didn’t feel like it?”
I didn’t want to talk about my thought process, so I just brushed off his questions. However, it seemed that he had an idea as well.
“So it’s true that you treasure the lives of your allies as your own.”
He spoke with a calm certainty.
“Riol Warb Dwalkie. I heard the death of that man has affected you greatly.”
What was this bastard trying to say?
“However, it was Dragon Slayer who killed that man, and he did so of his own accord. And I heard that while chasing after you, he died after clashing with the Order of the Rose.”
That sounded a little insulting.
“Ah, maybe you didn’t know? It’s top secret, even within the palace...”
It sounded like he was trying to convince me of something.
“And from what I heard, you were too busy running away.”
And yet, it also sounded like a threat.
“But...aren’t you curious? Why the Order of the Rose was there?”
For him to be able to say all this, how much did he know?
Since I didn’t know if he was being truthful or not, I found it difficult to determine if his goal was to convince me or to threaten me. No, maybe...
Maybe he’s just saying all this to try and see how much I know.
I maintained my best poker face.
At that moment, the skill was canceled, and the background noise returned to me.

“Unlike other barbarians, you are intelligent. You will certainly find an answer to that at some point,” the vice-captain said loudly enough for everyone to hear. “That is why we will let you go today.”
Only then did I realize why he requested to have a discussion with me. He wanted to convince me with a very heavy-handed method, at that.
“Go now. We will not stop you.”
This guy was a completely different type of person from all the enemies I had faced before.
Hah, I should’ve just charged him as soon as I saw him.
The well had been poisoned.
The vice-captain dished out an order, and a path opened up to the wall like the parting of the Red Sea. It didn’t end with that either.
“Ah, if this situation is still too uncomfortable for you, we will take ourselves elsewhere.”
