“...You should be mindful of the situation when you make those jokes.”
“Nah, how could I not? I’ve finally reunited with my precious allies! No, but I never expected you would be down here. How could you go in without waiting for me?”
...What?
“Baron, you can’t really tell me off for joking when you—”
“What did you just say?” I demanded in a low voice.
Baekho seemed to notice that something was off and mirrored my confusion back at me.
I quickly checked one thing. “It’s an important question, so answer me seriously. No joking around. Are you the one who put up that cloth on the tree...?”
I had been sure of it until now. However, Baekho only scrunched his face a little at the question with a tilt of his head.
“What are you talking about? That cloth... Wasn’t it you who put that up...?”
A chill went down my spine.
If it wasn’t Baekho who put it there...
Then who the hell called us here?

chapters.title: Chapter 688: Mystery (2)
paragraphs: Everyone was confused. However, I decided to listen to Baekho’s story before drawing any conclusions.
“Me?”
“Yeah, tell me. You might give me some information that’ll help me understand the situation.”

“I don’t have anything like that... I woke up in the Toxic Lavascape and went around looking for anyone who might’ve fallen nearby... And when I saw that no one was here, I came over to the Primordial Land.”

He didn’t give any hints that could be useful for me. He only found the cloth a few days ago when he entered the Primordial Land, and he didn’t do much other than run over to the monument as fast as he could.
“But what do I find? When I came over, I could see traces of you being here, but I couldn’t see any of you.”
Baekho then explained that he noticed the odd entrance that wasn’t there before and that he saw our tracks leading inside, so he had come in not long ago.
“Ta-da, that’s the end of my story!”
He mocked a stretch before quickly changing his expression. He then looked around at us before asking with a low voice.
“So, where’s our bow guy...? He’s dead?”
At his direct question, my jaw dropped for a split second.
I mean, it wasn’t even my fault.
“Bryat is dead.”
“How?”
“He was alone, and his body was found on the way to the Primordial Forest. It seems he was done in by monsters.”
“...Really?”
Baekho took a moment of silence after he heard that.
Of course, that didn’t last long.
“Hmm, still. It’s a miracle that only one person died.”
He returned to his lively self as if nothing had happened.

“Did everyone have a hard time? Honestly, I thought everyone other than our baron and the gramps here would be dead... But what do we do about our missing archer? Even though he was kinda timid, his skills were pretty good.”
I truly couldn’t read what this guy was thinking.
Did he not feel anything? Even though he had spent at least the last three years with his now-deceased ally?
I couldn’t know, but our talk about Bryat ended there.
“Anyway, that’s not important... So what’s going on? So no one here was the one who put up that cloth?”
“That’s right. Unless you are making a joke out of us, Baekho.”
“Why would I do something like that? Hah... this is really very strange.”
I mean, was it that strange?
“Is there...perhaps a traitor among us?”
Baekho began to scan the group. As soon as Baekho’s eyes landed on him, Aures began to try and defend himself.
“It’s not me! I swear! I couldn’t make a complicated plan like that in the first place!”
This wasn’t a game of Mafia. There was no point wasting our energy here, so I quickly interjected, “How about not putting suspicions on your allies first?”
“Why not? There’s enough grounds for me to—”
What grounds? “If it’s none of us who put up that cloth, it makes more sense to suspect the other side.”
“The other side...?”
“Have you already forgotten? We’re not the only ones who are in this region.”
Baekho seemed to arrive at a realization. “Ah! That bastard who lured us here! Th-th-that name... Han... something? Ah, right! Dalan! That Han—!”
“Stop.” I cut him off before he could say that name which was like a beacon of misfortune.
Jaina stepped forward and asked, “But isn’t he already dead?”
“That’s right! He got turned into a Bayon, we killed him, and Mr. Ruingenes already butchered him as well,” Aures joined in agreement.
Fallen Gramps then spoke, saving me from having to defend myself. “I am also of the same opinion as the baron. He’s someone who could very well have lured us here with a plan. Han—”
“If possible, just refer to him by his surname.”
The gramps looked at me questioningly.
“You two weren’t that close. Be polite.”
He looked at me like I had lost it, but he seemed to not want to bother challenging me on it.
“In any case...” he began slowly. “There is a good chance that it was instead a mysterious entity that disguised itself as Dalan who went to meet us.”
“And what’s the goal of that mysterious entity?”
“I do not know. However, we should be able to learn that with time by investigating this place—the reason he brought us here.”
As Fallen Gramps said, it was something we would learn in time. We were stuck here anyway, and the only thing we could do was to continue through this mysterious space and explore it.
“Alright, then since we got all that out of the way, we’ll be careful of that mystery bastard and look into this area. Right, Baron?”
“Right.”

“If we’re done, shouldn’t we get moving? We might even see the guy if we’re fast enough. That rat bastard.” Baekho walked up to me as if to hasten me. However, I didn’t move out of his way and just shook my head. “Why aren’t you going...? Oh, yeah. You were coming up the stairs when I met you, right?”
Only then did Baekho notice it and ask me for my reasoning.
This was why the command chain needed to be solid. The others would follow me if I forced them, but this guy wasn’t like them.
“Something might appear if we keep going up,” I explained. “I figured we should at least check it out.”
“Something might appear if we keep going up...” Baekho mused. Then, with a slap to his knees, he cried, “Ah! Now that I think about it, this place is similar to the Golden Ruins!”
Man, was it because he had played the original mode for a long time? Even though he came here after beating the cheat version, he knew a fair bit.
“Heh, so you were aiming for that?” he chuckled. “Then sure, that’s worth checking!”
“Um... Did you two already talk about this before...?”
“We have. Just follow us.”
In any case, since our goals were aligned, Baekho joined the group again, and we continued up the stairs.
Ten minutes, twenty minutes, thirty minutes...
I didn’t know how long exactly, but it happened around the time I was starting to doubt if this place also had that event since we technically weren’t inside the labyrinth.
Step.
Finally, the stairs ended and a narrow pathway appeared.
“It really did end...? I naturally expected it to just be an illusion or something.”
“What’s going to come out of there...?”
They seemed to want an explanation, but when I silently began walking through the corridor, they quietly followed me.
Step, step.
Around ten yards in, the darkness disappeared and a stone door revealed itself at the end of the path. I wondered if I should do a short briefing before we entered, but I decided to skip it.
They can easily hunt rank 3 monsters, so do I even need to?
The Golden Ruins was a rift on the fourth floor. That, and the enemy here wasn’t even the Guardian of the Rift. He was more like a hidden mid-boss, so the battle itself shouldn’t be difficult.
“Then let’s begin.”
I raised my hammer and slammed it down on the stone door.
Boom!
The door shattered in that single strike.
...What?

Even though I was the one who struck it, I was caught off guard. This door had a pretty high durability in the game, after all. Even though my barbarian build was both a tank and a damage dealer, I expected at least five hits to be needed for it to break.
Fwoosh.
GM used wind magic to blow away the dust, and when our vision recovered, I carefully entered and checked the interior.
It was a rectangular room. Although it was better than the narrow pathway, it wasn’t much wider. The art on the walls spooked me for some reason.
Step.
In the center, there was a golden coffin that was ten feet long.
It was indeed the hidden secret that could be found if one continued to go up the stairs in the opposite direction.
Step.

When that coffin was opened, a rank 4 monster named Macairo would appear from within it. When it was defeated, it would give a battle buff that would last until one left the rift, and if the adventurers were lucky, they could even get a very special numbered item.
After kicking open the lid of the coffin, I quickly stepped back and put some distance between us.
Boom!
I lifted my shield and got into a battle stance, and the others also got in formation after me.
“...Isn’t something supposed to pop out?”
Even after the dust completely settled, the boss monster showed no signs of waking.
What’s going on?
I covered my torso with my shield and slowly approached the coffin to check inside it. When I did, I froze.
Baekho slid next to me, then mumbled, “What the? It’s already dead?”
The coffin only contained a pale skeleton of a corpse, the bones of which were situated in the funeral position inside the coffin.
As I stared at it in a daze, Baekho called for Fallen Gramps.
“Gramps, loot this thing first. Even though the precious eyes and ears are gone, Macairo’s bones should still fetch quite a bit.”
“There’s no need. The bones have already lost their worth.”
“What are you talking about?”

“The reason the bones of monsters have any worth is because of the mana that is contained within them. However...” Fallen Gramps picked up a bone and revealed, “I cannot sense any mana from this. These are even more worthless than the bones of a Goblin. They’ve already dried up and can’t even be used as canes.”
“...It’s my first time feeling absolutely nothing from the bones of a creature like this,” GM admitted. “There’s usually not enough time for the mana density to fall to zero.”
“In that sense, it will be worth it to take at least a few of them. As our friend here has said, it is a very peculiar case.”
Fallen Gramps promptly picked up a few of the larger bones before putting them in his pack, and GM followed suit.
“Whoa, then are you saying the only thing we got after coming here are just a few bones that are worth less than a Goblin’s?”
“Unfortunately, that is the case.”
“How did that happen?”
“Well, there are two theories we can work with.”
With that, Fallen Gramps put up two fingers.
“First is the way this monster died. A phenomenon like this can sometimes be seen when a body is drained of all its life and mana by dark magic or authority of Karui.”
“Then you’re saying the one who lured us could be a dark magician or a Karui worshiper? Alright, check. Then what’s the second one?”
“It is when a lot of time passes after it becomes a corpse. For the remains of all living creatures, as time passes, they will weather away and the mana within them will disperse.”
“Then why do we make equipment out of bones? The piece I saw last in the auction house was said to have been used by a pretty famous adventurer thousands of years ago and was pretty expensive.”
“That is because a spell is cast on those so their mana doesn’t disperse...”
“So how long does it take for bones to become useless like this?”
“Luckily, there is a recent example of an experiment in this vein by the magic tower.”
“Ah, you’re talking about Jaymetal’s Goblin bones. I heard that around four thousand years have passed since the experiment began as of last year.”
“Is that so? But it still contained mana within it.”
The talk about the bones extended for a little, but it could be summarized quickly enough.
“To put it simply, it’s been more than four thousand years since this guy died?”
“Unless he was killed by dark magic or others of a similar nature.”
It wasn’t something we needed to spend time debating, no matter which possibility ended up being the correct one. What was the point of knowing how it died or how long ago it died?
...It’s a bit of a shame to not get that buff. And I was honestly looking forward to fighting it since it had a low chance of dropping a good item—
“Hmm? Baron, what’s this? There’s a box or something here...”
“What? A box?” I flicked my head toward the direction of the voice to see Aures holding what looked like a cubic box. “Where...did you find that?”
“I wouldn’t say I ‘found’ it... It was just in that corner over there.”
“Hand it here.”
After practically swiping it out from under him, I quickly checked its exterior. This was a genuine item.
“What is it...?”
“No. 777, Macairo’s Storage Box.”
It was the item that was usually called the mystery box.

chapters.title: Chapter 689: Mystery (3)
paragraphs: No. 777, Macairo’s Storage Box.
It was one of the few consumable numbered items. However, even though it was a consumable item, it was completely different from Unnamed Divine Sculpture and Dragon Blood Wine.
The ones that allowed for mass-area heals or gave a strong combat buff were true one-use items, but this wasn’t like that.
In a sense, it’s similar to No. 7,777, Garphas’ Necklace.
When used, Macairo’s Storage Box would give a random item or a permanent buff—that was, if you ignored the very low chance of it being a dud.
“We’re seeing a lot of unexpectedly precious objects on this adventure.”

Starting from those countless precious material drops, we got the Siege Slaughterer, and now the “mystery box” as well. In terms of a regular labyrinth exploration, we were continuously getting luckier and luckier items.
This was why people were drawn to exploring the unknown.
“So what we get is random? That sounds pretty fun! Let’s roll our dice now!”

The one regretful part about all this was that every time we got a piece of loot, we had to compete for it since I was working with Baekho’s team now. If I had brought my clan members here, I would’ve been the one to distribute this as I wished.
“It’s been a while since I’ve rolled dice. This is exciting.”
“Baekho... How about we all roll our own this time? I want to roll as well... And your luck is pretty bad.”
“Me? My luck is bad?”
No one answered.
“Whatever. Everyone can roll their own this time.”
After it came to that, we quickly rolled dice without hesitation.
“Bahahaha! If we were going for low-rolls, you would’ve been first and second place!”
Baekho and I both got five.
Ah, “both” as in that was our numbers combined.
“A total of eleven... I-I’ve won!”
In any case, the result was that GM won the dice roll and obtained the mystery box.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you going to open it now?”
“R-right now...?”
“Wow, look at this guy’s manners. Then were you not going to open it?”
“Hahaha! Sir Havellion! Don’t be like that and open the box. We would at least have some entertainment, no?”
GM seemed to want to open the box privately when alone, but the others couldn’t hold back their demands, which he soon abided by.
“Alright, then... I will open it.”
GM put his hand on the box, looking pretty nervous. A moment later, the black box slowly began to float into the air.
[Yurven Havellion has used No. 777, Macairo’s Storage Box.]
From where it floated in the air, the sides of the black box began to open one by one in an unfurling motion.
Shine.
Soon, the object inside the box revealed itself.
“...Armor?”
It was armor.
“Was there a numbered item like this...?”
One I had never seen before.
[No. ????, Dragon Plate of Aegis is created.]
Describing the appearance of the armor was simple enough.

It was a jacket-type armor only covering the body—the farthest away from the adjective “fancy.” Rather than steel, it was closer to a gray color, and there wasn’t a single ornament on it. No gems, engravings, or imprints.
However, maybe that was why...?
...It looks like a set item.
It suited No. 3, Wall of Aegis, pretty well for some reason. And when I placed the shield next to it, the color seemed to match somewhat as well.
It’s about time I changed my armor...

I was still wearing the lithium breastplate. Since my stats were high and enough for my current goals, I figured that rather than waste money upgrading my armor, I would just wait around until something fitting appeared.
For some reason, though, I was drooling.
I knew nothing about that armor, but you know. It was something that came out of the mystery box, so there was no way it was worse than a lithium breastplate that cost only a few million stones—
“Wh-why are you looking at it like that...?”
What? Was I not allowed to look at it?
“Can I wear it once?”
“...Pardon?”
“No one here wears armor other than me, anyway.”
“N-no? After hearing about what Ms. Flyer is doing, I should also hold onto one backup piece of—”
Hoh? What kind of wizard wears heavy armor? Wizards should just wear things like cloth armor.
“So let me just wear it once. Did I say I would steal it from you or something?”
GM couldn’t bear my close-up glare and ended up nodding.
“And we’ll need to test out the armor anyway.”
“Yes... Then... You’re just going to try it on, okay...?”
“Have you ever seen me lie?”

Although by all appearances, it looked like I stole it from him, it wasn’t a bad deal for GM either. It was a mysterious piece of armor, to begin with. Someone needed to equip it and check its abilities.
And if my combat power increases, it’s good for the team as well, right?
Aures was the only other person who could wear heavy armor, but due to the mechanics of his skill, he opted against it. To put it simply, I was the only option left.
[You have equipped No. ????, Dragon Plate of Aegis.]
Oh? Right off the bat, the feeling of wearing it was pretty good.
[Overall Item Level has increased by +13,600.]
And I didn’t know if it was just a feeling I got, but I felt much stronger as well.
[You have equipped two or more pieces of Relic of Aegis.]
[A piece of the soul resonates. (2/3)]
[All regeneration speed is greatly increased.]
[The equipment is bound to the wearer.]
...Huh?
What was that? It felt like the armor just got stamped onto my skin...
“Not bad.”
But in any case, even though I was wearing it for the first time, the armor didn’t feel uncomfortable. It felt like it had become a part of my body as soon as I wore it.
As I stretched while wearing the armor, Baekho looked at me with a baffled expression.
“Whoa, the baron here just wears whatever without knowing what it is. What would you do if it’s a cursed item?”
I had nothing I could say. I never once felt any worry while handling it. As soon as I saw it, it felt like it was meant to be mine.
“In any case, you can check the capabilities of the armor later...” he concluded. “Let’s move first.”
“Sure.”
Honestly, I wanted to check the attributes of the new armor right away, but it would be a waste of everyone’s time to check that here.
“Right, right. Let’s get moving. If there’s a time limit gimmick to this place, things could get troublesome.”
I decided to look into the armor later and investigated the room one last time. However, we weren’t able to find anything in the end, and decided to walk down the stairs we had taken once more.
Step, step.
Although it took us multiple hours to climb up the steps, it didn’t take long for us to get back down.
We soon came to the last steps which led to a similarly narrow pathway, and a golden door was at the end of it.
“...The Golden Ruins?”
GM also seemed to recognize this place after seeing the golden door.
“Why are the Golden Ruins here...?”
“What are you surprised about? You’re acting like anything we encountered until now made sense.”
“That... That’s true.”

“Hey, I’m already ready to not get surprised even if the door beyond suddenly connects to a different area. That’s what being an adventurer is about,” Baekho said before walking forward and slowly opening the door.
“Yo, the fuck?”
He promptly froze on the spot and spouted off a random exclamation. I walked up to check on what made him say that, then ended up flinching myself.
It wasn’t connected to a completely different space like what Baekho said before.
“Why is everything open?”
Instead, there was nothing left to explore beyond the golden door.
Clearing the Golden Ruins was straightforward.
It began in a dense forest, and after completing a few missions there, a temple would appear. Upon entering that temple, something similar to the stairs that we just encountered would await us.
And then, it leads to this.
Just like this, the golden door would open to a main hall, and the clearing of the rift would officially begin.

Since it was a fourth-floor rift, it was a low-floor rift with a simple clear method. From the entrance, you just needed to enter the leftmost stone door to activate a mechanism inside. It would then summon a Guardian in the main hall and also open a sealed treasure room after clearing everything.
But everything, including the treasure room, is open.
Not to mention, when you entered after opening the golden door, a golden light should filter in from the ceiling and illuminate the surroundings, but that effect was missing as well.
“Whoa... What’s with all this dust?”
“It’s like we’re exploring an abandoned building!”
The ruins were covered in a thick layer of dust, and the walls that should have been shining with gold were damaged and cracked in multiple places.
“Get some light in first. I can’t see anything properly.”
At Baekho’s request, GM summoned multiple balls of light to light up the room, and we then began to carefully investigate the hall.
“As I thought, the treasure room is completely empty.”

The first place I checked was the treasure room that would be opened after defeating the Guardian of the Rift, Kalpion. Normally, three numbered items would be sealed here and you could choose one of them using a key obtained during the rift-clearing process. However, when we got there, it was empty.
“Should we check the snake room first or the mummy room?”
We investigated the left and right rooms, starting with the left one featuring the snake-type mid-boss.
...Even all the hidden secrets are completely gone.

From the Golden Marble that would appear after pressing the wall under the lion mural to the Eagle Candlestick hidden in the trap room, and so on. Even as we walked along the complex, maze-like paths, we weren’t able to get anything. The results were the same in the mid-boss room where the lever-locking mechanism was.
“It’s pretty spooky, seeing this much of nothing...”
The lever had been used, and the mid-boss was nowhere to be seen. The hidden secrets were taken from this place as well.
Unfortunately, the mummy room on the right wasn’t much different.
“At this point, I think we’ve investigated everything we could...”
“Haha! This is quite a problem!”
Even though we looked through the entire ruins, we couldn’t find anything. And this was a very big problem. Something needed to be here so we could at least do something.

It was like that in the game as well. The times when it was most difficult to advance within the game weren’t when you encountered a difficult problem. It was rather when you didn’t know what to do. If the player couldn’t find a path forward then, they would waste unnecessary time.
Just like us now.
“I...will go investigate the stairs again...”
“Me too. There may be a hidden path within the bricks, so I will check it over.”
Still, as top-level adventurers, they didn’t lose their morale and continued to look for work to do, but it didn’t mean much.
One day, two days, three days, four days...
Time passed and we began to lose things we could try investigating, and that began to increase the nervousness and unease of the group.
“...We’re not going to be stuck here forever, right?”
“Maybe it was trying to starve us to death.”
“I never knew someone could lose it from something like this...”
Everyone shared their weakest moment, and unexpectedly, the one who showed the most extreme reaction was Baekho.
“Fuck, what is everyone doing? If you have time to rest, look for a way out of here,” he berated the others with his sharp glare and words.
Why’s this guy’s mental fortitude so weak?
Still, I was relieved he didn’t direct that attitude toward me.
However, that ended a few days later.
“Baron, give me your armor.”
“...What?”
“I mean, we haven’t found anything here except that armor. Since we got it here, maybe the armor holds a way for us to escape?”
Although his attitude pissed me off a little...
If I didn’t let my emotions get in the way...
“...You’re not wrong.”
It sounded plausible enough.

chapters.title: Chapter 690: Mystery (4)
paragraphs: Following Baekho’s suggestion, we officially began our investigation into the armor we obtained, featuring two high-ranking wizards working with Baekho and I, who were gamers, and two more native, high-ranking adventurers.
Although none of us recognized the armor from the mystery box, we quickly obtained our first set of results once we were all set to work on it together.
“I’m sure that it’s a numbered item.”
“It is...? But I’ve never heard of anything like it.”
“I haven’t either, but surprisingly enough, there is no doubt in my mind. The way you identify numbered items is by testing for a specific mana reaction, after all.”
“But how could that be...?”
“If you look through the history of the labyrinth, you’ll find that not all numbers have treasures assigned to them. There was even a period where ‘numbers’ weren’t used at all.”
“Oh! An era without numbers? Something like that existed?”
“Yes. The numbers came to be after one appraiser compiled ten thousand of these treasures into a single book.”
“Then maybe this armor is a new numbered item that has never been discovered before.”
“A new numbered item...?”
“I feel like there will be more cases like that of this armor. With that, I propose we name them the no-numbered or, perhaps, the mystery numbered items...” GM suggested greedily.
Unfortunately for him, however, someone had beat him to the punch.
“The official name is secret numbered items,” I explained, cutting his path off before it could truly take shape.
“Pardon...?”
“Arua Raven discovered them first and named them as such.”
Yeah, she would be irritated if her discovery got swiped by someone else.
Rather than look sullen, though GM actually looked more interested. “So... There are more treasures like this?”
I took a moment to consider my reply, but since the information could help us out of this situation, I answered him honestly.
“Just one. One more has been discovered inside the labyrinth.”
“Could I see it?”
“Unfortunately, I don’t have it on me at the moment.”
“I-I see...”
Everyone seemed interested in what said item was, and I just told them it was something that was obtained during the basement floor expedition.
“A so-called secret numbered from a newly opened area... Maybe countless more numbered items have yet to be discovered.”
I thought the same thing, honestly.

First, the basement floor I’d been not long ago, and now, beyond the city walls—places that had long gone untraversed by adventurers were gradually beginning to reveal themselves over the past few years.
“Whoa, it was a binding item?”
In any case, the other piece of information we discovered about the secret numbered item was that it had already been bound to me.
“A-a binding imprint... Th-then I can’t get it back from you!”
GM fell into despair when he learned of it, but what could I do? I just picked my nose and acted like I didn’t hear him.
“Anyway, explain it to me. You say it’s a binding item... Are you sure?”

“Eh? Oh, yes... The automatic form adjustment doesn’t activate when someone else tries to wear it, and even if they force the unadjusted gear onto themselves, the armor displays no other special effects and operates only as an ordinary piece of gear. This is what all binding imprints entail...”
“So that odd wave of mana you and I talked about was the armor imprinting on its owner.”
“Yes, there’s a good chance that is the case.”
On top of the binding trait, it was also indestructible and featured a direct bonus to its wearer to boot.
Increase in all Regeneration speeds.
According to GM’s description, it was this characteristic that would earn the armor its laurels.
“It’s quite a rare trait. It’s not specific to Soul Power, mana, nor Divine Power—rather, any resource that can be ‘regenerated’ is boosted.”

This regeneration didn’t just affect finite resources like MP. The increased regeneration speed also affected Natural Regeneration and even boosted the regeneration of any special resources I might use if I got another skill.
“Still, it is a numbered item. Shouldn’t it have a fitting name?”
As Baekho said, we couldn’t just keep calling it “armor,” so we need to give it a proper name.
“Oh! Then can I name it something cool—”
“Dragon Plate of Aegis.”
“It’s the Dragon Plate of Aegis. That will be this armor’s name.”
Baekho nodded approvingly at my naming scheme. “Phew, that’s a pretty good name. And considering its color, these two look like a set.”
In contrast, Jaina just tilted her head in confusion. “I understand naming it Aegis, but why Dragon Plate? I don’t think it’s made from dragon leather or used a dragon heart in making it.”
Considering how non-serious the question was, I was put into a pickle. But, to answer her honestly...
“Isn’t it a little boring to just call it plate armor?”
“Ah, I guess...”
Although Jaina didn’t seem convinced, the other men of the group nodded. They all liked calling it Dragon Plate rather than just chestplate or armor.
Yeah, women just don’t get what men want.
In any case, the item was named the Dragon Plate of Aegis, and oddly enough, we ended up finding out something else as a result.
“It’s quite fortunate. On the off chance that it was correct, I performed a comparison check with the Wall of Aegis, but they do, in fact, resonate with each other.”
“So what you’re saying is that this armor is a set item with the shield?”
“Yes. Dragon Plate of Aegis and the Wall... Both of them are resonant treasures.”

Resonant treasures just meant that they were items in a set that gave an additional effect when equipped together. For example, No. 7611, Deceit of the Necromancer—the numbered item used by Mr. Bear—would grant a resonance effect when equipped with the skull belt No. 7612, Pride of the Necromancer.
When either of them is used, it would regenerate an additional 50 percent of blood.
The more knowledge we worked to glean, the more information cascaded out of the item.
“Then what’s the resonance effect of the armor and the shield?”
“Hmm... In hindsight, I’d theorize the Regeneration increase is the resonance effect.”
The increase in all Regeneration speeds was the resonance effect of the Aegis set.
“Oh, then you’re saying it has a different passive effect?”
“Yes... It seems that it has one constant ability and one activated ability.”
To put it simply, the armor itself had one passive and one active, and we were able to discern the passive after a few trials.
[Yurven Havellion has cast the rank 5 attack magic Lightning Spear.]
The effect was quite simple.
[Yurven Havellion has cast the rank 4 attack magic Storm Slash.]
As expected of an effect applied to armor, it was a defensive ability.
[Yurven Havellion has cast the rank 4 attack magic Ice Sword.]
I mean...
[You have used the Dragon Plate of Aegis.]
The best defense was a good offense, right?
[Reflecting all accumulated damage.]
The active effect of the Dragon Plate was quite similar to the counterattack of the essence of Gachabone.
A summon appeared behind me, just like how a temporary skeleton would be summoned for a counterattack.
Those two characteristics made it pretty similar to Gachabone. However, there was one key difference.
“Why is it so big?”
It was comparably more powerful than a mere skeleton.
“Is it an ability to summon something?”
“Uh... But it’s moving?”
The huge, spectral Viking warrior swung down with its huge sword toward GM, the one who had attacked me as a test.
“Shit! Block it!”
At Baekho’s shout, Fallen Gramps summoned a mana shield and intercepted the slash of the sword.
Crunch!
However, since it was a hasty cast, the barrier wasn’t strong enough to fully block the attack.
“Move!”
At that, Aures quickly moved in front and raised his shield, successfully blocking the attack. After he blocked the attack, the situation ended as Lek Aures coughed up some blood.
Clang!

The huge shield, now featuring a huge dent, that Aures lugged around with him was sent clattering to the ground as Aures coughed up blood. The spirit giant that had swung the sword disappeared as if its work was done.
“A-are you alright?”
Our healer Jaina ran up to check on Aures’s condition, and only then did GM fall to his rear, having just then processed everything that happened.
“Whoa... This is amazing.”
Baekho’s eyes sparkled as he observed the situation’s close.

“It’s clear that getting battered is the activation condition. Does that mean it reflects damage relative to damage dealt? Or is it not relative and it just does flat damage after hitting a cap? Hmm, depending on which one it is, the way to fight it will change. Well, still, it’s not a guaranteed reflection, so I doubt it’ll be too tricky.”
I sighed. This was why I wanted to investigate it privately in my own time.
“Hey, hey! What’s everyone doing? No one got hurt! Stop making a fuss and let’s keep investigating it.”
“Huh? Baekho? Did you not see it? I just coughed up blood—”
“But you’re not anymore.”
Aures didn’t respond.
After that, the investigation continued at Baekho’s insistence, and we looked more into the active skill.
“So you get stacks every time you get hit, and depending on the stacks you have, it does a certain level of physical damage.”

“Its cooldown is only five minutes, and there aren’t any special resources that get expended. But even just at four stacks, it does enough damage to rip through twenty mana barriers like they’re paper?”
“Ah, yeah. Indestructible is a given since it’s a numbered item.”
“But since it’s an item in a set, you get increased Regeneration when you equip them together, and it even has an additional passive effect that we haven’t been able to figure out?”
Uh, yeah...
That was pretty much the summary of it all.
“What the fuck? What’s with this cheat armor?”
I had nothing I could say. I agreed with his assessment, after all.

Depending on what the passive was, my opinion of it could change, but its active skill put it on par with the single-digit numbered items. If the passive was also on the level of a single-digit, then that could very well be me getting another single-digit numbered item.
“I-it... It was mine...”
I felt guilt poke at me as I heard GM’s mumbling, but what could I do? It wasn’t as if I could give it back to him at this point.
“Yurven Havellion. Stop whining.”
“B-but...”
“It can’t be helped. I didn’t bind it to myself because I wanted to. Or do you think that this expedition will be the last time we ever work together?”
“Th-that’s not what I...”
“Then it helps you too if I become stronger. I am not someone who forgets his debts.”
GM clenched his jaw shut at my logical persuasion. He did seem to be sulking a little, but that would resolve itself with time.
“Wow, you’re a master gaslighter, Baron.”
I ignored Baekho’s comment and continued the investigation of the gear. I wanted to check the passive that we hadn’t been able to figure out yet.
One day, two days, three days...
However, no matter how much time we spent on it, the passive of the Dragon Plate remained a mystery.
“Hah... Maybe we’ll figure something out when we fight a monster.”
“I believe we’ve done everything we can without resorting to that.”
“Unless it is a very specific condition or an unknowable effect, we may need to be fighting a monster.”

With that, we gave up on trying to figure out the passive. However, our work coming to an end only illuminated the sticky situation we were in. The reason we began our investigation into the Dragon Plate was to find clues to escape this place, after all.
“Then we’re back to square one?”
Baekho’s dejected comment echoed out, ringing in everyone’s ears.
Hey, being a leader means acting like everything is fine even when it’s not.
“Let’s start over and slowly work through our options,” I encouraged, trying to motivate them all.

We resumed our exploration of the Golden Ruins, going through all the pathways one more time and even utilizing some physical methods like breaking down walls. We even went back up the stairs and visited the hidden secret of the Golden Ruins, the chamber of Macairo.
“Huh?”
But what was this?
“Whoa... This is getting spooky.”
The corpse of Macairo, which should be inside his coffin, had gone missing.

chapters.title: Chapter 691: Mystery (5)
paragraphs: The chamber of Macairo was a hidden area that opened if you went up the seemingly infinite stairs, and it was also the place where we found the mystery box that gave me the new armor.
We had been caught by surprise the last time we came. We’d found the mid-boss Macairo already dead and turned into a meager pile of bones.
Once again, we found ourselves surprised but, this time, for a different reason.
“Where the hell did he go? It’s not like he could’ve gotten up and walked away.”
When we opened the coffin, his corpse was gone.
“Hey, Aures,” Baekho barked with piercing eyes. “You were the last one to come and investigate this place by yourself, right?”
“Was he here then? Inside the coffin.”
Aures avoided his gaze, unable to muster a full response. “I...”
“‘I’ what? Talk properly. Was the corpse in there or not?”
“...don’t know.”
“You don’t know? What do you mean, are you joking? You came all the way to the chamber and didn’t even check inside the coffin...? Or did you just waste time lounging about?”
“I didn’t do that!” Aures pleaded frantically, waving his hands to stave off Baekho’s interrogation. “I came here to check! It’s just, my legs hurt a little, so I climbed the steps slowly...!”
“Don’t tell him off too much. It’s a mistake.”

Jaina’s words of support from beside him seemed to give Aures confidence, as he raised his voice a little to say, “A-and! Did you think I wouldn’t notice how you are giving me the most tedious work? But even then, I didn’t complain and diligently did my job, but if you’re really going to accuse me now...!”

Although Baekho wasn’t completely innocent, as someone listening from the sidelines, I couldn’t help but be impressed at his audacity. Even though it was a long job, he was given that task because it was the easiest thing to investigate, but he hadn’t even done that properly.
“Hah! You think I’m taking it too far? How about I show you what ‘too far really is, huh?”

“Stop,” Fallen Gramps demanded. “We are the ones who sent Aures by himself. We should’ve expected he wouldn’t be able to accomplish something as simple as this, so it is our fault for not accounting for it.”
Aures seemed confused about whether Fallen Gramps was for or against him, but soon enough, he was nodding along.
“I-It’s just as Sir Ruingenes says!”
So he decided to take it as support.
The whole thing sent a wave of exhaustion barreling into me. Just as Fallen Gramps said, it honestly began to feel like this was our bad.
Baekho seemed to have thought the same as I did, as he just let out a deep sigh and left his berating there. “Fine... This isn’t the important part.”
“Just where did the corpse disappear off to...?”
The derailed topic reoriented itself as everyone began to present their own theories.
“This could be up to interpretation, but I believe that there is a possibility that someone else is hiding within these very ruins right now.”
“And there isn’t a guarantee it’s just one person either.”
“Yes. Also, if that is the case, they are likely quite talented in stealth. Even though we searched every nook and cranny of this place, we didn’t find a single strand of hair.”
“Oh...! From the way you said that this guy could be bald!”
Baekho nodded at GM’s theory. “Someone definitely could be hiding here.”
“Yes. We cannot ignore that possibility—”
“Well, I also think that someone among us could have some ulterior motives as well.”
This guy was the same as ever. Was doubting his allies just a habit of his?
It’s honestly an illness at this point...
Of course, I knew somewhat of Baekho’s painful past so it wasn’t totally inexplicable.
“Don’t suspect your allies,” I warned nevertheless. “That’s something you need to stow away as an absolute last resort.”
He was slow to respond, but clapped back with, “Did I say it was a definite thing? It’s just a possibility like I said, that’s all. You should always be open to all possibilities, no?”
I just let out a sigh inwardly and changed the topic. It was about time I heard an answer from him.
“Drop it, and actually answer me. And don’t even think about changing the topic this time.”
“When did I ever do that?”
What do you mean, when? “Always” would be the answer to that.
“What’s the reason you came outside the walls?”
Why did Baekho drag his allies outside the city walls?
Although I had asked him a few times in roundabout ways, I wasn’t able to get one proper answer out of him.
“Why’s that question relevant to our situation?”
“Of course it’s relevant. From what I can tell, everything we’ve encountered doesn’t seem to be aimed at either me or Havellion.”
The fact that someone destroyed the magic circle that led back to the city before killing himself.
The fact that an unknown man lured us to a dimensional headstone while we were walking around getting materials to recover the magic circle.
And even now that we were stuck inside the Golden Ruins.

“No matter who this mysterious actor is that’s messing with us, I believe they are aiming for you.” When he didn’t respond, I pressed him to answer in my deadly serious tone by demanding, “So just let it all out and tell me. I need to know what your goal is so that I can guess your enemy’s goals as well.”
Baekho looked at me from the corner of his eye for a second before defeatedly admitting, “It’s nothing grand. I just wanted to investigate the ‘gray world’ that you talked about, Baron.”
“Investigate? Keep talking.”
“I just wanted to go and check if that gray world really was expanding or not.”
“Isn’t that something you can check if you stay near it and watch it?”
“No. Not particularly. Even though it seems like it’s slowly getting closer, it’s further away if you come back another day. It’s like the tides.”
“So what was your conclusion?”
“I haven’t made one yet. I wanted to make a precise investigation out of it, so I just marked a few places and was about to go back.”
He was about to go back...
Something suddenly popped into my head at that.
Maybe this mysterious person wasn’t trying to stop Baekho from accomplishing his goals outside the city walls. No, there was a good chance that this person’s goals were...
“Ah, this is fucked. From what I heard from gramps, this is going to take at least a year to fix.”
To stop Baekho from returning to the city—that was why that person destroyed the return magic circle and removed all evidence of it.
But it just so happened that GM and I were outside as well so we lumped up together.
GM could fix the magic circle before the estimated time, so because he appeared and threw a wrench in this person’s plans, they lured us to the dimensional headstone to trap us here.
...Maybe that’s jumping to conclusions?
Hmm, well... I didn’t think it was complete nonsense, but I lacked the evidence to be perfectly certain this was how things were going.
I decided to ask a few more questions.
“That thing happening a year from now, the one you told me about.”
Maybe this would be the most important thing to help me understand our situation.
“Just what is going to happen then?”
He didn’t answer.
“Tell me,” I commanded. “I need to at least know that to be able to guess as to who destroyed the magic circle.”

“Hah... I’m going to die from this headache.” Baekho kneaded his forehead before shaking his head. However, he seemed to have concluded hiding the information from me wouldn’t be helpful for anyone. “I’ll only say this once, so listen closely.”
At that, Baekho slowly began to speak.
“It’s war.”
“When the Noarkans finish their preparations, they are going to head straight to the royal capital of Karnon and kill the king of Rafdonia.”
For some reason, I could already smell blood in the air.
Noark was planning to kill the king.
And Baekho was probably very closely related to this plan.
No, he might even have a core role in it. With one skill from this bastard, half the palace will get blown away.
However, the problem now was that there were too many people who might want to stop Baekho. Pinpointing who exactly it could be would be difficult.
And if we’re going this route, the most likely thing is that the palace obtained this information and took the initiative to act...
Dealing with people through sneaky and underhanded methods like this was also one of the core techniques of the palace as well.
“But Baron. If they really are aiming for us like you said, then you know that the story becomes even more fucked, right?”
I paused. “What do you mean?”
“It wasn’t like we told everyone that we would be going outside. We didn’t even tell the castellan of Noark that we were leaving.”
“So?”
“It means there really is a traitor among us. Either they are a complete lackey of the palace and are messing with us, or they leaked the information that we were leaving.”
Baekho used his tiger eyes to scan his allies as usual, and Aures was once again the one who flinched of his own accord.
Why does he have no guts despite being a warrior?
“He’s like that because he nearly got punched to death in the past,” Jaina whispered to me.
“By Baekho?”
“Who else?”
Aha, I did wonder why he reacted the most to Baekho’s glares even when the rest didn’t seem affected.
Baekho chose that moment to slowly step forward and stand in the middle of everyone.
“Anyway, that’s why I think I’ll need to interrogate you all. Anyone have any objections?”
“I don’t mind.”
“Me neither! I don’t mind either!”
“Getting this well and truly over with now may be for the best.”

Everyone agreed to Baekho’s suggestion without a question, something that would be hard to elicit if there really were a traitor present. However, he still seemed to want to confirm everything down to the last detail.
“Alright, since I got everyone’s consent...”
Baekho then pulled something out from his sub-space.
It was No. 7234, Misplaced Trust, an item I myself had used a few times at this point.
Still, did this guy make a habit of carrying one around even though he could tell whenever someone was lying?
“This is better for confirmation compared to my ability. I’m going to use it, and everyone is fine with it, correct?”
Even after Baekho pulled out Misplaced Trust, his allies remained calm.
Vwoong!
He clicked the on button, and the compass on top of the round plate began to move.
“Jaina Flyer, have you ever told anyone that we were leaving the city walls?”
“No, I have not.”

Baekho asked the question to each person in order. Although I expected it somewhat, everyone was able to answer him when they were asked the question. However, he didn’t seem fully satisfied with just that.
“Lek Aures. Are you sure you have no relation to why or how we are trapped here?”
To give them no wiggle room, Baekho changed the questions he was asking as he repeated the process. However, even after multiple rounds of this, the result was the same.
“No, I have never done that.”
“Baekho, stop. At this point, we’ve proven that everyone here is innocent.”
“I guess? Looks like we really don’t have a traitor here?”
Baekho’s suspicion seemed to have died down as well, judging by the reduced heat in his voice. However, he was even more stingy than me.
“B-Baekho? If that eased your mind, then we can stop—”
“No, we still have some time left. It’s a waste if we stop.”
“A waste? What do you—”

“Exactly like I said. Since I have it on now... Let’s take some time to get to know each other a little more... We have been together for a while, but we don’t really know much about each other, right?”
Baekho grinned, breaking his somewhat serious demeanor, then turned to Jaina Flyer.
“Alright, in that case, the first question: Jaina Flyer still wants to kill me, Baekho.”
I didn’t know why a question like that was suddenly asked.
“Answer yes if you do, no if you don’t.”
The humor had left his eyes and his words at some point.
At that, Jaina also turned more serious as she answered with a colder voice.
“Yes.”
...Just how were these guys working as allies?

chapters.title: Chapter 692: Wolf (1)
paragraphs: I couldn’t follow what either of them was trying to say in their conversation. Not Baekho, who suddenly asked her if she wanted to kill him, nor Jaina, who answered plainly without giving it a second thought.
What was the relationship between these two?
“Oh, looking at me with those eyes again?”
“S-stop, Baekho... If we fight in this situation, it’ll only be good for that person who trapped us here!” Aures pointed out, actually saying poignant as he tried to calm the tension in the air.
“Just shut it and stand to the side. Did you think I wouldn’t know you still talk with the castellan?”
“Wh-what do you m-mean?! I—!”
“Hey, you do know that you can’t lie here, right? Still, since you said you didn’t tell anyone that you were leaving this time, I’m letting you be.”
“Th-thank you...”
Something about their conversation gave me the feeling that that moron Aures was actually scheming something behind his back.
Why do these guys work together if they’re going to be like this?
It seemed that my idea of “allies” was completely different from Baekho’s.
“Lord Baron,” GM pleaded. “Maybe you should say something. If the group falls apart because of this...”
“Stay still for now. I’ll do something if it gets more serious,” I denied, deciding to just observe the situation for now.
I mean, you know, at first, I didn’t understand why Baekho suspected his allies. But yeah, it’s understandable if this is what was going on behind the scenes.
They seemed so friendly with each other that I nearly misunderstood, but in the end, all of them were the same type. They were only working together because each of their goals happened to align.
These guys weren’t “allies” at all.
“Gramps...” Baekho went to say something to Fallen Gramps before just letting out a sigh and shaking his head. “It’s fine. I already know you’ve been scheming something from the start.”
I didn’t know why, but I could tell he looked sick of all this. Did he suddenly get a reality check or something?
Clack.
No matter his reasoning, the duration of Misplaced Trust ran out.
Fallen Gramps spoke up to say, “Anything more will be a waste. This should’ve proved that there are no traitors among our group.”
Even with all said and done, Baekho seemed wary as he put Misplaced Trust back into his sub-space. Nevertheless, he added his usual unnecessary tidbit in the end.

“Still, I’m glad. Even I would feel a little bad if I had to kill a few people I’ve been traveling with for the last few years. But I don’t have to do that anymore.” Then Baekho looked up and smirked at Jaina. “Oh, but I guess you wouldn’t know what that feels like? Since you couldn’t even remember things properly back then.”
I didn’t know the details, but I could feel instinctively that these words were meant to pierce deep into her heart.
Jaina’s whole form was shaking as she silently took a step and then another toward Baekho before stopping.
“What?” he taunted. “You gonna hit me?”
Jaina gritted her teeth, glaring up at Baekho as she muttered, “Baekho... We are not toys for you to vent your anger on... So if you’re going to act like a child, go do it to your mother.”
It was a painful retort that made even GM and Aures flinch from their place on the sidelines.
“Oh, I guess you can’t? Since you’ll never be able to return to your original world—”
It was then that Jaina pushed him over the edge.
Baekho’s form suddenly disappeared from view—
Boom!
And an ear-piercing burst of sound accompanied the kicked-up dust.
“Heh, that’s fun.”
Put simply, Baekho had tried to attack Jaina, and Aures jumped in from beside her and stopped him with his shield.
“What the? You were talking about getting back your memories or whatever, but you already got someone to stick to?”
Even as an outsider, it was a cringe, third-rate villain thing to say. It felt like I had been confronted with the lowest point of this man named Baekho.
“Baekho, I understand that this is a problem, but get a hold of yourself. This isn’t like you,” Aures argued.
“And what is like me?”
“You’re always unpredictable and a headache, yeah, but you’re at least not someone who causes problems like this.”
Even as Baekho looked like he would go in for another hit, Aures confidently faced him and said what needed to be said.
Yeah, this is what being a tank means.
There were no bad tanks in the world.
Baekho took a while to respond. Finally, he sighed.
“I’m going to cool my head.”
He then left the room as if running away, and Aures let out a deep sigh. It seemed the situation had just hit him.
“Baekho’s killing intent is always scary to experience. I really thought I was going to choke to death.”
“Haha, even still, you didn’t show any signs of backing down. I’ve seen you in a new light.”
“Ahaha... It’s to protect an ally. How could I back down from that?”
Quietly, Jaina said, “Thank you.”
Aures scratched the back of his head, looking embarrassed.
“Then does everyone want to go first?” our priest asked. “I’ll follow after cooling my head a little.”
“Oh... Right! Should we?”
What do you mean, should we?
Before Aures could say something else, I quickly interjected, “I won’t allow anyone to act without getting the okay from me. There’s no guarantee that we’re safe just because we’re here.”
“Uh... But didn’t Baekho just leave by himself?”
Hey, don’t talk back to me. Do you think Baekho and the priest are the same?
“No is no.”
Although I sternly made my stance known, Aures asked once more, “If it’s a problem for her to be by herself, then I’ll be with her. That solves it, right?”
Uh...when he says it like that, there’s not much I can say back to him. Could this guy speak so logically all this time, and just didn’t do it?
Unrelated to my surprise, I wasn’t going to allow him. “No.”
“Why not?”
There were a few reasons. Firstly, leaving the priest with just this guy didn’t fill me with any confidence whatsoever.
“Didn’t you say that being alone is the problem? Then what’s the problem if I’m together with her?”
The second was a problem with the guy himself. If another relationship problem popped up when things were already as unstable as this, something irreversible would happen more likely than not.
“Answer me. If you don’t, I’ll never come back—”
Man, shut up.
“You can go first, then. I’ll stay with her.” Since I got the feeling he would never back down if I just told him no, I decided to take his place.
Sure enough, Aures was flustered. “Uh... Huh? Y-you don’t have to...”
“It’s fine. Aures,” Jaina said. “I’ll follow soon, so don’t worry.”
“Understood.”
With Jaina joining in, Aures had nothing more he could say and left with drooping shoulders. Once it was just the two of us left in the stone chamber, Jaina turned to me.
“He’s a funny guy, huh?” I began.
“He’s been like that for a while now. Even while joking, he keeps glancing at me from the side.”
“You knew?”
“How could I not? When he’s such a straightforward person.”
I guess?
To be honest, I didn’t really notice it until today.
“By the way, it’s just us two again.”
“Yeah, it worked out that way. I’ll be quiet on this side, so you can collect your thoughts yourself.” I sat down crossed-legged near the entrance, and Jaina leaned on a wall some distance away.
Silence ensued.
While I thought about a few things while chewing on the jerky, Jaina spoke to me again.
“Are you...not going to ask about it?”
Although it felt like it came out of nowhere, it didn’t affect the conversation itself.
“Didn’t you need time alone?” I questioned.
“But I’m not alone, anyway.”
Hmm, that was true.
“Then are you going to tell me if I ask?”
I didn’t put much thought into that question, and Jaina replied in a similar vein.
“It’s not like I can’t tell you. It’s not something I would bring up myself, but it’s not something I need to hide either. And didn’t you say you’d stay with me because you were curious about it?”
Well, that was one of the reasons. “The biggest reason is something else.”
“What is it?”
“Things could get messy if affection comes into play with how things are,” I answered honestly without hiding it.
Jaina laughed, seeming to have not expected to hear it before changing the topic. “No, as I thought. I’m not going to say it.”
“What? Suddenly?”
“Just because. It’s not that interesting of a story anyway.”
“Really? Do as you wish.”
Tsk, I got excited for no reason. I felt the tension leave my body as I sighed.
However, she seemed to feel a little guilty when she saw my reaction.
“Still, I’ll at least tell you this. I lied to you before, Baron. No, to be precise, I omitted a section on purpose.”
“What was it?”
“The person I saved while giving up my memories of them to Lord Karui. I was the one who killed them. Well, you might’ve guessed it after hearing what Baekho said.”
“Could I hear how that happened as well?”
“It’s nothing grand. It’s just that Karui asked them to be an offering. I was promised a new authority, and so I killed them.”
I didn’t respond.
“It’s a powerful authority that has saved my life a few times at this point, but... I shouldn’t have done it. If I knew I would feel this frustrated now, I would’ve never...”
A deep sense of regret laced Jaina’s voice, so I didn’t ask her anymore and let her have some time to herself.
Ten minutes, twenty minutes...
Around thirty minutes later, Jaina got up and said she was fine now before going back down the stairs.
“Are you feeling better now?”
As I stepped inside the ruins again, I could see Aures approach Jaina. The two were having a conversation, but I didn’t go out of my way to listen to them.
When I approached GM to ask where Baekho was, GM just told me he wasn’t back yet.
I sighed. Was this guy going through puberty or something?
“Should we go look for him?”
“It’s fine. There’s no point. He’ll come back if we keep waiting for him.”
“Still, couldn’t an unknown entity be here in the ruins with us?”
“We can wait a little more, and it won’t be too late to go look for him then if he doesn’t come back beforehand.”
More importantly, I had a conversation I needed to have while Baekho was away. I left my conversation with GM there and approached Fallen Gramps.
“Hey.”
“What is it, Lord Baron?”
“I have something I want to consult on with you.”
“Speak.”
Since this gramps wasn’t one to talk a lot, I went straight into the topic.
“About Baekho, did he seem normal to you?”

This was something I had been sensing for a while now. Even if Baekho wasn’t a normal person, he wasn’t someone who would act this recklessly. He only ever did something that would be of benefit to him.
“He probably isn’t in his right mind if you are also saying that.”
“So you sensed something off about him as well?”
“His point of reference isn’t something like good and evil. No matter the situation, he thinks and tries to act rationally. However, the things he did today were too emotional.”
“What’s the possibility he’s like that because he feels pressed for time?”
“That is a laughable theory. If he feels impatient because of something like this, he wouldn’t have been able to run toward his singular goal for close to twenty years.”
“I see...”
Then what made Baekho act this way? Was there a field effect in play that we weren’t aware of? But everyone other than Baekho was too normal for that to be the case.
While I was thinking it over, Fallen Gramps carefully approached me and presented a different topic.
“I am more curious about something else.”
“What else?”
“This is something I thought of as I continued to run through what happened. As I thought, the only explanation is that there is someone within the group who is leaking our information.”

“Haven’t we already resolved that?” We had even used Misplaced Trust to check not just Baekho’s teammates but also GM as well. Well, Baekho couldn’t use it on me because it didn’t work on me, but why was Fallen Gramps bringing it up now?
There was only one conclusion I could draw.
“Are you...doubting me and Baekho?” I asked in a lowered voice.
Fallen Gramps smirked. “That’s not it. Of course, you certainly have the motivation to get in our way... But there is someone I doubt more than you.”
“Don’t drag this out. Get to the point.”
“There is one more person we haven’t gotten answers from.”
What was this gramps talking about? If he kept spouting off like this—
“It’s Bryat.”
I paused. “What?”
“We didn’t hear from Bryat that he wasn’t the one leaking the information.”
“Do you...think he’s alive?”

“Well, as the one who saw his corpse myself, I see that possibility being very low... But his death doesn’t prove his innocence.” Fallen Gramps continued with a completely neutral tone to say, “I’ve reached the same conclusion multiple times even after thinking over it... If one of us is the traitor, then it can’t be anyone but Bryat.”
I didn’t know what proof he had, but Fallen Gramps seemed adamant that Bryat was the traitor.
With that, I took some time to think as well.
The priest wants to kill Baekho, the warrior is a pawn of the castellan, and the wizard is scheming something else. And the archer was now the traitor... Did Baekho even try to make a team?
I wasn’t even surprised at this point.

chapters.title: Chapter 693: Wolf (2)
paragraphs: As a woman creaked opened the front door and entered the building, the people gathered in the living room all got up from their seats.
“Emily...! How did it go?”
“Have you found it? Have you found a way yet?”
It had been almost four months since Bjorn Yandel went out to look for a way out of the city walls and disappeared.

At first, the people here expected him to have gotten caught up in something and that he would return late within a few days, but the situation changed after a week passed. As time passed and worry filled them, they even went underground themselves only to be met with the empty square.
From that point onward, they officially began a search mission for him.
“Yurven Havellion. What about him? Has he appeared yet?”
Even the whereabouts of the Magic Engineer, who had gone down to look at the magic circle under the introduction of Versyl were unknown, and they all grew even more nervous.

Of course, in the earlier days of his disappearance, most assumed that he had gone outside the city walls and would return soon enough. However, those opinions began to change the longer he stayed missing.

It was true that Bjorn had left the walls with the Magic Engineer. However, something unexpected had happened outside that was stopping them from returning. And in truth, it didn’t take long for that theory to become the dominant belief.
Not long after, the underground, which had been left barren, was teeming with the soldiers of the palace.
“I still haven’t found any way for Bjorn to return.”

Amelia had gone searching high and low to gather information as the representative of the clan, but she had only learned one thing: the teleportation magic circle in the underground city had been damaged.

It was information she gained nearly at her own expense by infiltrating the tents of the soldiers. Thanks to overhearing those pieces of information, she was able to formulate the reason why Bjorn hadn’t been able to return yet.
“I see...”
“Don’t worry. There were still some gains this time.”
“Some gains?”
“The way back is blocked, but leaving is still possible.”
“Really? Is that true?”
“Luckily enough, I’ve obtained a way to activate the magic circle as well. Though, we’ll only know if it is possible if you, Gowland, look at it yourself.”
Amelia then pulled out what looked to be a military document, and Versyl took it before quickly reading through it.
“It seems that the palace knew all about this magic circle. The activation method of the magic circle is written in detail here, just like a guide.”
“So? Can you do it?”
“Yes. With this, even I can activate the magic circle.”
Amelia nodded at Versyl’s confident answer. “That’s it, then.”
“What do you mean?”
“Be ready to leave in three days.”
Although the order was sudden, no one refuted her.
“Ooooh! So we’re finally going to do something!” shouted Ainar, who had been dozing off.
“Yeah... Since it’s already been a few months since he left home, we’ll just have to bring him back.” Missha nodded, strengthening her determination.

Versyl let out a tired sigh, as she had been the one put in charge of all administrative matters of the clan. “Yes. Will he know how tired I’ve been because he went up and disappeared after leaving all the work behind? From what I heard, even Ms. Shavin Emoor is going to kill him as soon as he comes back.”
“Let’s leave that all behind. This is a rare opportunity, right? For us to go save the captain.”
Hearing what the navigator Auyen said, Erwen closed her eyes and put her hand on her chest. “It was always Mister who came to save us and protect us.”
The Anabada Clan’s next expedition was decided.
Leyton Bryat was the archer of Team Baekho. Someone with a good personality and great skill.
If we were to presuppose that he was the traitor, there was one suspicious piece of evidence against him. It was the fact that he was also taking the role of the guide of our team.
“It’s not a monster. It’s a person.”
“There’s just one person... And surprisingly, it seems they are sleeping.”
Even though Baekho hadn’t been able to detect the person, Bryat was able to lead us to Hans L as his role intended.
Well, the unknown entity that had disguised itself as Hans L in a very natural way.
And when everyone was trying to stop Baekho from taking the dimensional headstone, he stayed silent...
Once I allowed the doubt to seep in, I became even more sure he was the traitor. That didn’t mean I was completely certain, of course, but—
Boom!
A sudden vibration rocked the earth.

I couldn’t tell which direction it came from. In situations like this, the agility-focused characters would normally give me the briefing, but there wasn’t anyone like that around me at that moment-two wizards, one priest, and two tanks.
“Where is it?”
“I think it came from that direction...”
“It’s far. I’ll need some time to confirm it using mana detection—”
Due to our shortage of expert opinions, we were hesitant to make a move, and the vibration returned.
Boom!
It was larger than before. Though, maybe because we were aware and observant of it...
“That way.”
However, I was able to detect where it came from and guided the other members in that direction.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
As we got closer, the vibrations and explosions grew clearer and clearer.
Even though it was faint, I also heard what sounded like someone talking. I could also easily recognize it as Baekho’s voice. The problem was...
“He’s fighting someone... Right?”
“Seems so.”
That seemed to be the situation.
At first, I just assumed Baekho was throwing a tantrum and destroying everything because he couldn’t hold back his fury.
“Hey, you son of a bitch! When I catch you—!”
From what I heard him say, he was clearly chasing someone.
With that, we increased our pace and ran as quickly as we could to the source of the commotion. I banged into the corner as I took the turn at full speed.
Flash!
Then, a bright light flashed in front of my eyes like a nuclear bomb had gone off. Rather than critically thinking about it with my head, my instinct as a tank acted first.
[You have cast Giantization.]
I quickly increased the size of my body to block the narrow pathway and held up my shield to protect my upper body.
Boom!
A formless mass of energy blasted my body with intense heat. It felt like my entire body was melting.

Like wearing sunscreen, the part I blocked with my shield was relatively fine, but when the light began to die down, smoke began to waft up from my heated armor. It felt like a bolt of lightning was traveling up my spine from my foot, but I checked the condition of those behind me first.
“Is everyone alright?”
“I-I’m fine... Ack!”
What the? Were they severely injured?
As I was about to turn around to check on them, I heard Fallen Gramps say, “Everyone is hurt, but nothing serious.”
People of his personality type were helpful in situations like this exactly for that reason. In emergencies, a concise and clean exchange of information was necessary.

I left my worries about those behind me and dashed forward. Although some sections were molten and destroyed, the structure of the walls was largely intact, just left smoking. It was something that surprised me since we had tested this once before.
Stellar Extinction couldn’t destroy the building we were in. Although there were a few weak points that could be physically destroyed, they were only a very small minority.
Well, I think he used a different skill this time.
Just how many lethal attacks did this guy have hidden?
As I turned another corner, I spotted Baekho standing there, panting for breath.
“Baekho.”
He sensed my presence and heard my voice, then turned around to say nonchalantly, “Ah, you’re here...?”
“Talk. What’s going on here?”
“It’s nothing much. I just tried to kill a rat bastard, but with how fast it was... I ended up getting angry and going overboard.”
“Rat bastard...?”
“But I don’t know if I got it or not. Do you want to come with me? Let’s check if I got that rat or not.”
“Step forward.”
“Ah, Roger that!”
Even while joking, Baekho hurried in front of me, and I followed him for around a minute.
“Whoa, it’s alive even after getting hit by that?”
All that was left of them in the empty hallway were bloodstains. The blood splatters led all the way to the other end of the path.
“But I don’t think it’s gone too far.”
Baekho grinned before slowly following the blood trail.
One step, two steps, three steps...
He stopped tracking it around three minutes in. The drops of blood had stopped.
Shouldn’t we try and see where it ran off to, rather than follow it slowly like this?
I was the one getting impatient, but Baekho just scanned our surroundings calmly.
“What are you doing? We need to track it down quickly—”
“Baron, did you know?”

I tilted my head as I listened to the question that cut me off, and Baekho explained, “In the world we used to live in, there is a creature called a chameleon. It’s pretty interesting, changing its skin color to match its surroundings to help it when it’s hunting.”
I wondered what nonsense he was talking about, but it didn’t take long for me to understand his intentions. In the first place, Baekho didn’t call me Baron unless we were in the company of others.
“But... the more I look at this guy, the more I’m reminded of the chameleon.”
Baekho threw a punch at the empty wall.
Crunch!
A crunch that sounded nothing like hitting a wall echoed out, and simultaneously, the “rat bastard” who had been hiding with invisibility showed itself with a pained gasp.
“Got you.”
Looking down with a frightening smile, Baekho lifted the rat by its collar.
Its body looked to be that of a regular male’s. And since we couldn’t see any fur or its ears protruding, it looked to be a human as well, though its body was covered with a ragged robe.
A wolf mask...?
That was the one thing that caught my attention. We could figure out more about him going forward—
“What’s this now?”
The body fell limp as if going unconscious. However, as I looked closely, I could see dark-colored blood dripping out of his mouth.
I was caught off guard and quickly put my hand up to his throat to check his pulse, but I couldn’t feel anything.
“It’s suicide...”
Baekho smirked before turning his head to look at me.
“Baron.”
He used that same title again, the one he never used unless someone else was around.
“No matter the world you go to, all small animals have something in common. Do you know what that is?”
Even though I had a feeling I could guess what he would say next, Baekho unfortunately didn’t give me time to answer him.
“When they get in an unfavorable situation, they all play dead...? Like this.”
Baekho threw another punch at the stomach of the corpse.
The man fell to the ground and writhed, gasping as he curled inward like a bug, Baekho reached out with his hand.
“Alright, let’s see who this is.”
It was time to take off the mask.

chapters.title: Chapter 694: Wolf (3)
paragraphs: Someone would be hard-pressed to describe the motion of Baekho’s hand taking off that mask as anything close to “kind” or “gentle.” His hand was stretched open as he grasped the wolf mask, before he ripped it away from the man’s face, ignoring all sorts of bindings clutching it together.
Then, the face behind the wolf mask was revealed to us.
Baekho remained silent for a moment as if to collect his thoughts before breaking that silence.
“Wow, you really were alive?”
Although it was the joking tone he usually used, his eyes were glacial as he looked at the target.
Well, it was understandable. For Baekho, “betrayal” was his trigger button.
“Leyton Bryat.”
And this guy was actually the second oldest team member of Baekho, right after Fallen Gramps.

“You bastard. Didn’t I at least treat you well?” Baekho mumbled. Then, he let out a deep sigh. “Well, that’s that... But tell me this. How are you, who I was told was dead, alive? And what’s with this wolf mask? And what were you scheming behind my back?”
Bryat didn’t answer.
“Also, every time you stop talking, I’m going to take one thing from your body, so keep that in mind.”
No reply.
“Talk,” Baekho pressed, commanding him to speak.
It may have been obvious, but there was no way the guy who had remained silent this entire time would speak just because of a little threat. Instead, Bryat looked up at Baekho with deep hostility.
Baekho remained stoic, but once the silence had lapsed for three more seconds, he leisurely reached out with his hand.
“Ack! Argh, ack—!”
He then pushed his fingers deep into Bryat’s left eye before gouging it out.
Tick, tip, tack...
He moved very slowly. Slow enough that we could hear many distinct snaps from his target’s head.
“Ack! Ahhh!”
Even as Bryat writhed on the ground in pain, Baekho showed no change in emotion and only said one thing.
“Talk.”

He didn’t do anything else other than say that. He didn’t add on any threats, any appeasements, or use any interrogation techniques. He just asked for him to talk, and after waiting for a few seconds, if the silence persisted, he repeated his actions.
“Aaaack—!”
He gouged out the eyes, ripped off the ears, and pulled out the organs.
And if Bryat fell into a critical condition during that process, Baekho would pour a potion on him to heal him.
Sizzle!

Baekho was pretty intense for continuing with this process without showing any change in emotion, but Bryat was no joke either. From what I could tell, it wasn’t like he couldn’t feel the pain either.
But he hasn’t said anything other than the screams.
Maybe he realized that it didn’t matter in the end?
He didn’t try making excuses for himself nor did he ask Baekho to kill him. His mental strength was admirable, but at this rate, this interrogation wouldn’t bear any fruit.
I think it’s about time for him to change his methods...
I thought about stopping Baekho, but I let go of that thought after seeing his face.
It wouldn’t be too late for us to look for a different method after he calmed down a little. And it wasn’t like I was the one hurting.
“Aaack!”
And so, as I continued to watch Bryat get “healed” by him, the others caught up to us.
“Ah, you’re here. Why are you so late?”
“We got lost. None of us was able to find the path.”
“So what’s going on here?”
“Wait! Bryat? Isn’t that Bryat over there?”
“Calm down. I’ll explain.”
Baekho showed no interest in the people who came, so I gave a quick explanation of the situation in his stead.
“So... there was a suspicious person here wearing a wolf mask, and Baekho caught him, took off his mask, and it was Bryat underneath it...”
“Sir Ruingenes! How can this be? Didn’t you say you saw Bryat dead with your own eyes!”
“I was sure when I saw him. However, seeing how he is alive and well...it seems he can fake his death, or use an item to the same effect.”
“That’s probably the case. He acted dead after getting caught not long ago.”
“Hmm... There are a few abilities I can think of.”
Well, it wasn’t important if he had an ability or an item. The main point was that Bryat acted dead in front of Fallen Gramps and had secretly hidden himself inside the ruins.
“This is even more suspicious. Just what is Mr. Bryat doing all this for?”
“We’ll have to hear that from him now.”
Baekho shouted in our direction, “Gramps! What are you doing? If you’re here, put that on him already! That thing!”
Fallen Gramps approached Bryat and cast a spell on him.
“Do you know what that is?”
GM gave a swift response to my question. “From the way the mana is being dispersed, I suspect it is a neural type acceleration and awakening—”
“To put it simply, you’re saying it’ll help with the interrogation?”
“Yes... In that state, his pain will be multiplied and he’ll be able to feel it more clearly.”
I should ask my wizard to do something like this next time I need to interrogate someone.

I unexpectedly obtained some good information. In any case, the effect of the spell was immediate. The screams became multiple times louder, and he was even starting to shed tears and snot. His voice gave out not long after, giving way to a shrill cry.
However, when Bryat said nothing until the very end and wound up falling unconscious, Baekho couldn’t help but comment as well.
“Wow, he was one intense bastard.”
To be honest, I thought Baekho was the more intense one, given that he was still pouring that healing potion while saying it.
Sizzle!
He seemed to have vented his anger somewhat as Baekho stopped his torture and returned to us. Seeing how his usual gentle smile had returned, I got the feeling he was ready to talk.
“What happened?”
“Huh? How am I supposed to take that question?”
“It’s a bit suspicious. How did you find the guy that we weren’t able to find even when we all searched the place?”
I thought that maybe Baekho had a way of finding this guy since the very beginning that he had just been hiding.
“Oh, that?” Baekho shrugged without a care, and the truth he revealed was even more shocking. “I drew in his aggro a ton on purpose. Acting like I was suddenly losing it and whatnot.”
“That...was all an act?”

“Yep. I got the feeling that he would come near me to observe me if I acted out of sorts. That’s why I went away by myself. I was talking to myself and slamming my head into the walls, and when I thought I drew enough attention... Boom!” Baekho mimicked an explosion with his hands. “I fired a ton of AOE effects around me. And someone ended up getting hit. The rest is what you saw, Baron.”
“Uh... I see...”
“How’s that? How was my plan? Wasn’t it genius?”
Well, I wasn’t sure if I could call it genius. One thing I was sure of was that this guy’s mental state wasn’t normal.
He’s actually just reckless...
As I stood there speechless, Baekho smirked before turning around. “Anyway, since I got some of my anger out...let’s dig ‘em up.”
He walked over to the unconscious Bryat before going through Bryat’s pockets.
“Damn it, looks like he’s put all his important things in his sub-space.”
“I don’t see his bow either. Isn’t it a numbered item? A pretty high number at that.”
“Hah, in the end, I can’t even loot him unless he cooperates... Hey, gramps! You got anything?”
