A healthy body meant a healthy mind, but that also meant a body pushed to its limits would make me have negative thoughts and resist my will as if to tell me that I could relax if I just gave up.
Shut the hell up.
I had survived until now.
Dying not because I got decapitated by a sword, or eaten by a monster, but simply because I ran out of oxygen?
Ring!
I wouldn’t be able to live with myself if I died like that.
Slap!
I smacked my face to wake up my fading consciousness.
Thud! Thud!
Then, I pressed forward.
Boom! Boom!
I had no idea how much time had passed.
The flow of time became indistinguishable, and I couldn’t even tell if I was moving forward anymore or not.
Swoosh.
Then, my legs gave out and I fell forward.
Boom!
My body crashed into a hard surface on the way to the ground, instantly waking my mind up.
“The... The wall?”
It was the city wall.
I didn’t know how long it took me to get all the way here.
“The...wall...”
However, the contact with something beyond myself and the flames reinvigorated my body, much to my surprise.
I didn’t have time to look for where the gate was. Besides, barbarians as a race specialized not in finding the path but in making one.
I clutched at the cracks between the heated bricks and climbed the wall like a cockroach. And as soon as I arrived on top of the wall...
I’m alive.
My body lost all strength after confirming that I had survived.
Even atop the wall, it was difficult to breathe. However, a drop of water was like an oasis to someone wandering the desert.
“Haah... Haah... Haah...”
I coughed due to the smoky air, trying to breathe in as much clean air as possible. With time, my body recovered somewhat.
I nearly died there. Really.

After making my way to my feet on the wall, I took a surveying look around the area. Since the walls were built tall enough to look down at the entire city on a sunny day, I could take in the true scale of how much of the city was burning.
“This is nuts...”
From the incredible amount of smoke I could see, the entirety of District 8 was burning.
“The fire spread to District 7.”
And District 7 was in a similar boat. As far as I could tell from up on the wall, around a third of District 7 was engulfed in flames.
“Damn it.”
I was suddenly reminded of the money I invested into those buildings, but I quickly pushed aside that regret.

I could always earn more money. I needed to remember the important things in dangerous situations such as this. The thing I needed to concern myself with wasn’t “money” or “clean up”, but how to end this war without more loss.
Hah... Then what do I do now?
Now that I’d made it out of that unexpectedly deadly ordeal, the previous problems returned to trouble me.
Astarota and Raven had disappeared. My clan members were hiding in the barbarian holy land. Amelia and Auyen were last seen in District 4 and were being chased down.
I’m worried for Raven...

Still, I decided on the barbarian holy land as my first destination. Diving back into that sea of fire to look for her all by myself would accomplish nothing. It would be better for me to regroup with my clan members in the holy land and search together with them.
Since Astarota is with her, I shouldn’t need to worry too much...
Decision made, I didn’t have any time to waste.
I dashed across the top of the wall, figuring it would be better to just use the wall to move around rather than jump down into the burning city below me.
Boom! Boom!
However, as I was continuing my mindless trek along the wall toward the holy land, I suddenly raised my guard and stopped, anxious.
Someone had emerged from the black smoke that had been obstructing my vision.
“You’re here.”
Or rather, someone had been waiting for me.
A black wolf mask...
The design was exactly the same as the mask that Baekho Lee’s former ally Bryat had in his possession. Thanks to that, I was able to immediately figure out this guy’s affiliation.
Heerkmuta—the ancient organization created by those who followed the Last Great Sage, Diplan Groundel Gabrielius.
The wolf mask figure who seemed a part of this organization shrugged and stared at me.
“It’s been a while, Bjorn Yandel. Ah, maybe I should call you Sir Lion? Hahaha!”
I quietly let out a sigh.
Hah, I have so much on my mind already.
So who was this bastard?

chapters.title: Chapter 739: Reversed Fate (2)
paragraphs: Gray clouds flew overhead, casting shadows across the open area that the barbarians used to commune and discuss topics of every sort.
The other races usually regulate indoor spaces to be their communal areas, citing concerns about formality and security, but the barbarians felt that was inefficient.
What was the point of gathering indoors and sitting on chairs when they could just stand on their legs and talk?

As a result, the holy land of the barbarians didn’t have a place officially designated as a meeting hall. It was for that reason that Versyl was guided to the common area, open to all, when she asked the head administrator about a place she could use to speak with dozens of people at once.
She couldn’t understand how a group of their population size didn’t have a single building they could use for such occasions.
“Don’t try to understand every little thing. It’ll be much healthier for you if you just accept them as they are.”

However, after she heard the resignation in the head administrator’s voice, Versyl simply nodded in agreement. She could tell that the advice was genuine, and the head administrator wasn’t wrong either. A huge meeting hall would make it more difficult to communicate with dozens of people simultaneously.
And with everyone gathered here like this, there is a sense of equality as well...
Maybe that was the true strength of the barbarians.

Accepting their customs for what they were allowed her to see the positive side of things. However, the many different clan leaders who were called out to the field weren’t so inclined to agree with her.
“Ahem...”
“Why have you called us to the field this morning?”
“Talking about a serious matter in a place like this... Do the barbarians not have a meeting hall of some sort?”
“They don’t.”
“Hah! I heard that they had evolved in some ways, but they still—”
Versyl decided to cut the leaders off there. “That will be enough.”
She could tell the people before her didn’t understand the situation they were in. They were not guests.
I’ll need to say this first.
Versyl decided to make one thing clear before the meeting began.

“It appears this might have gone unnoticed by everyone here, but we are refugees who have run away from the battlefield in search of safety. The barbarians who took us in are the masters of this land.”
One of the leaders cleared their throat uncomfortably.

“As such, I was thinking we take a moment to show them our gratitude for providing us with food and places to stay. What do you think?” When no one responded, she added, “Who knows? If they decide to expel us from here, we might have no choice but to return to District 7.”

Versyl glanced at Ainar, who grinned as she stepped forward. “That’s right, you parasites! You asked us to save you, feed you, and give you beds. If you aren’t completely shameless, you should at least let out a battle cry to show respect and say thanks!”
“B-battle cry?”
“You mean that...B-Behela thing?”
“Of course, you can refuse if you don’t want to do it!” Ainar belted obligingly. “We barbarians respect free will!”
“Ah... Th-then, for religious reasons, I’ll have to decline—”
“Oh! Then you can leave the holy land right now!”
“You said you’d respect my free will!”
“Freedom comes with great responsibility. Don’t you know that?”
The man was rendered mute as Ainar looked him over like he was scum, and the same went for all of the other leaders present.
It was time for Versyl to throw them a carrot.
“Ms. Ainar, please stop. That person over there only refused due to religious reasons. I am sure he is grateful to the barbarian tribe.”
“Oh, really?”
The man took the opportunity to nod. “O-of course. I have my conscience as well.”
The other clan leaders took the opportunity to express their thanks in turn.
“Ms. Fenelin. We truly thank you.”
“Same for us, the Partia Clan. We will never forget this kindness for as long as we live.”
Versyl smothered a satisfied smile at the sight.

More would be gained from allowing them to just say thanks rather than let out the battle cry. At a glance, it might only look like the display of gratitude was merely the bare minimum expected of them, but the small actions taken now would pile up to become the foundation of a closer relationship.
“Vice-captain Gowland.”
“Yes, Captain Erta.”
“Could I hear why you have gathered us all here this morning? I don’t expect it was just so that the many people here could show their gratitude.”

“Ah, this?” Sensing the opportunity, Versyl stepped forward, then spoke in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear. “As of one hour ago, the barrier between the holy land and District 7 has begun to weaken.”
That short statement served as a thunderous clap of realization to the adventurers, all of whom had let down their guard after coming to the holy land.
“Wh-what do you mean?” one stuttered.
“The Noarkans are the ones who put up that barrier around the holy land in the first place! They can’t afford to pay any attention to us while also fighting against the palace!”
It wasn’t their group the Noarkans were concerned about, but the barbarians who were still living in the holy land, Versyl corrected in her mind. However, that was neither here nor there.
“But why now? For what reason—”

“The reason isn’t important,” Versyl interjected and transitioned to her main point. “The fact remains that the barrier has begun to weaken. When I checked it, it was in the process of naturally dissipating because its supply of mana was severed.”
“Vice-captain. How much time do we have?” one man calmly asked Versyl.
Was he the captain of the Ravraim Clan? she wondered. He had remained steadfastly rational, even among this gaggle of clan leaders whom Versyl wanted to smack over the head—at least once.
She matched his tone in her answer. “It’s not definite, but I estimate we have about one hour.”
“Just one...”
“In any case, that is the situation, so we need to prepare ourselves. I, for my part, can think of only two reasons the barrier might suddenly be being taken down.”
“Could we hear what your thoughts are?”
“First is that there is a genuine problem and the mana supply has been cut off.”
“And the second?”
She turned to look at the man who shouted the question. “The Noarkans now have enough strength. They’ve grown strong enough to eliminate us.”
In truth, Versyl thought the latter was the more likely reason of the two, and it seemed her opinion on the matter was reflected in her words.
A heavy silence followed. The area went deadly quiet, far too quiet for there to be dozens of people present.
The silence ended up being broken by the words of one woman.
“Then what should we do now...?”
Who could say?
Versyl honestly just wanted to toss out an excuse like that, say she didn’t know either, and yet...
“From today onward, you are our clan’s vice-captain.”
That wouldn’t do.
She shut her eyes, took in a steadying breath, then opened her eyes once more and declared, “We need to get ready to fight.”
“What strategy will we be using, if I may ask?”
“We will prioritize defense first and foremost. If we make encampments in front of the gate, they won’t be able to get in easily.”
“I assume there is a step after that?”
“Yes. We will assess the tide of the battle and wait for an opportunity to arise. When it does, shouldn’t we push through their lines?”
“P-push through them...?”

It was a plan none of the leaders could have possibly conceived, as was evident by their wide-eyed stares. However, Versyl just shrugged. She might be a wizard and a ranged damage dealer, but she’d learned her lesson.
“Yes. The best defense is a good offense.”
If she truly wished to protect the things she held dear, she needed to know how to make her hits count.
The head administrator of the barbarian tribe, Shavin Emoor, was the busiest person on the land.
As was to be expected, really.

Yet again, the holy land had been swept into another battle, and unfortunately, she was (currently) the one responsible for everything that happened within their borders. Thus, she needed to stay focused and—
“Ms. Emoor, I’ve brought you some tea. Please have some before you continue.”
“E-eh?” she stammered, startled by the voice. “But look at the time! It’s—”
“You should have at least the time for a cup of tea. There’s no need to put yourself under so much pressure.”
“I-I understand your intentions, but our enemies will soon be pouring in. How could I possibly rest?”
Emoor felt like she was going to lose it. Her professional expertise lay in office work and administration, not war!

“In that case, I won’t push you... But I’ll leave this here at least. Do drink it when you can—for the effort I put into brewing it if not for anything else. Sometimes, you need to relax a little to be more productive with your work.”
“Ah... Yes, of course... Thank you, Mr. Rotmiller.”

It really did seem as though Rotmiller had come in for the sole purpose of delivering her the tea, as he just turned around to leave after setting the drink down. Only then did Shavin Emoor realize what had changed about Rotmiller.
“M-Mr. Rotmiller? What are you wearing?”
He always wore plain ordinary clothes, so why was he now armored and equipped as if he were about to go into the labyrinth?
“Oh... I suppose this must be your first time seeing me like this? I hadn’t gotten rid of my old gear just in case, and now I’m grateful that I didn’t.”
“Are you...” She struggled to get the words out. “Are you planning on fighting as well?”
“Shouldn’t I? They’ll need all the help they can get.”
“But you were an exploration member!”
Some might have viewed her words as a sign of disrespect. However, Rotmiller didn’t seem to take them as such, only giving a gentle smile.
“Haha, you don’t need to worry so much. Even as an explorer, I was still an adventurer. Someone who entered the labyrinth to protect what is important to him.”
Shavin Emoor found herself unable to respond. Objectively speaking, they weren’t close enough for her to realistically stop him either.
“In any case,” Rotmiller said after a beat of silence, “I came by just to see you one last time. It’ll be hard for us to see each other again once I go out onto the battlefield.”
In the end, there was only one thing she could say.
“Please be careful.”
Those few words held the true feelings from her heart, and he matched her short reply with one of his own.
“I’ll come back to you.”
With that, Rotmiller left the room, leaving Shavin Emoor with flushed cheeks.
C-come back...? To me...!
Even as she sipped the fragrant tea, her heart wouldn’t stop racing.
Sir Lion.
Only one person called him by that title at the Round Table. The very person who acted like they were the spokesperson of Auril Gavis.
Wolf.
Funnily enough, the Heerkmuta mask this person was wearing was also a black wolf. Though, to call it a funny coincidence was really a stretch.
So he was always a part of that organization.
Even if I didn’t have the whole picture, I could guess he had probably picked the wolf mask on purpose.
“Haha, please don’t be so wary,” he said to appease me. “I’m not your enemy.”
I wasn’t having it. “Then why are you in my way?”
“I don’t think I ever said I am?”
“You’re not? Then move.”
He made no attempt to step aside at my cold demand. “I told you, you don’t have to be so wary. I’m only here to relay a piece of advice from the elder.”
By elder, he was probably talking about that gramps, Auril Gavis.
“A piece of advice...” I echoed.
From Old French avis, based on Latin visum “to see.” A word that meant to help one see a better course of action to take.
But then, why did I always feel guarded when I heard that word? As if every time it was thrown my way, the “better” choice wouldn’t actually be better for me at all?
It was anyone’s guess. However, apparently taking my reply as permission to continue, he gave me the “advice.”
“Seeing you’ve come this way, I suppose you’re going to the holy land?”
I didn’t answer.
“Don’t go to the holy land, but there instead,” he said, pointing to the currently aflame District 7.
I was lost for words and couldn’t even laugh at what I just heard. “So you lied when you said you weren’t in my way.”
“I’m being genuine when I say I don’t plan on stopping you. If you say you will take this path and head toward the holy land, then I will move out of your way, Sir Lion.”
“Really? Then move.”
“If that is what you wish.”
I didn’t expect anything from him, but then he actually did move out of the way, stepping back against the corner of the path along the wall.
I stepped slowly toward him, still keeping my guard up just in case he tried to pull something.
“Ah, and one more thing,” he said, catching me just as I was about to walk past him. “It wasn’t a good decision for you to kill Clown.”
“What does my decision matter to you?”
“It does matter to you. Maybe not for anyone else, but the elder believes that Clown would’ve been of great help to you if he had been kept alive.”
“I don’t know if he would’ve been helpful. All I know is this elder of yours is too nosy.”
“He is a kind and noble being.”
Wow, as if anyone would doubt he wasn’t a fanatic of Auril Gavis.
I felt no urge whatsoever to continue the conversation and kept on moving past him.
Step.
One step.
Step.
Two steps.
Step.
I successfully made it three steps before I couldn’t squash the thought anymore.
Hah, this is driving me nuts...

“Why?” I demanded, turning around to ask. I didn’t like how his eyes curved into a smile behind the mask as soon as I spoke, but the question that had been bugging me the entire time would leave me. “Should I not go to the holy land?”

He seemed to have been waiting for that question. “Because depending on where you go, the people who die will change... So don’t go to the holy land but District 7 instead. That will be the decision most beneficial for you, Sir Lion.”
“Most beneficial for me...” I smirked as I confirmed one last thing. “That’s that, then. Did that elder of yours also tell you this future?”
“I don’t know what you’re asking about, but that was all I am able to tell you—”
Oh, I wasn’t actually asking for more advice.
My hand whipped out, choking him by his neck as I slammed him against the edge of the wall.
“Will you survive this or die?”
Maybe I would trust him if he got this right.

chapters.title: Chapter 740: Reversed Fate (3)
paragraphs: There once was an oracle named Cassandra who prophesied the fall of Troy. However, the city’s king did not believe her, and Troy was ultimately destroyed.

Of course, the king had his excuses as well. The god Apollo, unable to win Cassandra’s love, cast a petty curse on her so that no one would ever believe her words. That curse definitely played a part in others not taking her prophecies seriously.
Still...

Even if people could believe her, however, the outcome would probably have been the same. Who would want to believe in a negative prophecy, after all? To this day, someone might actively seek out fortune tellers, pay them, and present his hands to them all of his own accord, and yet still, he would decry the fortune teller as a fraud if he happened to get a bad reading.
Would the king of Troy just lazily accept certain ruin with a placid nod?
No.
And neither would I.
“Haha... C-could you calm down a little? I am not here to fight you, Sir Lion.”
“I’m not trying to fight you,” I rebutted coldly. “I’m trying to confirm whether or not I can trust your word.”
The panic on his face began to melt away into a smirk instead. It was as if his previous expression were just an act. “Shouldn’t you already know the power of the elder?”
“Yeah, I do know that old man’s abilities. He plays around with people’s lives and is completely full of himself,” I said sardonically.
That didn’t earn me much of a reaction, but he did ask in a quiet voice, “Then why did you stop?”
It was the question that hit the bull’s eye.

“You could’ve just walked past me and headed to the holy land. So why didn’t you?” When I didn’t respond, he continued, saying, “You know it in your heart as well, don’t you, Sir Lion? That you might regret it if you don’t listen to the elder’s advice.”
I really wanted to refute his claims.

All I did was hear out what that old man wanted to tell me, my mind argued. Even false information was information in the end. I was actually just reading between the lines to sound out the old man’s intentions.
I wanted to say all that, but what he said was right. None of those were the true reason I stopped.

“And you asked if I was going to live or die here, right? I haven’t received direct word from the elder. But, well, I don’t really see me dying here today. Seeing how our conversation is progressing... By the way, could you let go of me now? It’s getting a bit stuffy.”
Finally, I sighed. “Damn it.” I used the hand not gripping him by his neck to take off his mask.
Whoosh!
The face behind it was exceedingly ordinary. A beastman in his mid-thirties, someone I would be able to see anywhere in this city.
I clicked my tongue. I was hoping it would be someone I recognized.
He didn’t seem in any way panicked to have his face revealed. “Haha... Were you that interested in my face?”
“I’ll ask you one thing,” I said quietly.
“Go on.”
“You should know about the Records if you worked under the old man, right?”
“Of course.”
“Then why do you keep talking about choices that change the future? You people are the ones arguing that nothing will change anyway.”
It didn’t matter whether I believed in fate or not. I was just curious why a group that spoke so often of fate and destiny was so adamant about their position.
“Hmm...” he hummed. “You’ve given me quite a difficult question. It will take some time to explain. Will that be alright?”
“I don’t mind. Start talking.”
“Let’s say a man is in a bar playing a little game of cards with the other patrons. However, the dealer mistakenly didn’t give out the cards in the right order.”
I wondered what the hell he was going on about but opted to just listen for now.

“If the cards were given in the right order, the man would have been dealt a very weak hand, but due to the mistake, he was given a strong one. The other patrons are so drunk that they don’t even notice the mistake. So the man decides to sit quietly and reap the benefits of the outcome.”
I still didn’t understand where he was going with the story.
“So I ask you this.”
But then, he asked me a question.
“Was the man originally fated to have received that weak hand or the strong hand he eventually did get?”
Even though I didn’t understand why he was asking me the question, it wasn’t difficult to answer it.
“Receiving the strong hand was his original fate. Because it was also fate that the dealer made that mistake.”
He chuckled. “A good answer. You catch on quickly.”
Well, he could say that all he wanted. I still didn’t understand a word of what he was trying to say.
“As you said, even a reversed fate is still fate itself.”
“And...?” I prompted.
“What we’re trying to do is deal the wrong hand. So that someone can receive a stronger hand even within their ‘little game.’”
While the meaning wasn’t totally clear to me, I was starting to get the idea. I decided to ask him another question.
“So what happened to him?”

He looked slightly surprised at that but answered with a smirk. “In the end, the man lost quite a lot of money in gambling. But due to that one good hand, he was able to mitigate a tiny bit of his losses.”
“So not even that reversed fate could change that he ‘lost’ in the end.”

“So it goes.” He smiled like a teacher giving a student a sticker for doing a good job. “But don’t worry too much. After repeating those gains and losses multiple times, he eventually grew to be a great man.”
Needless to say, those words didn’t console me at all. It just made me all the more determined.
“Now, make your choice. The cards have already been dealt to you, Sir Lion.”
Determined to never talk about fate with these damn fanatics ever again.
Silence stretched between us, tangible even against the background of black smoke and scalding heat.
Finally, he couldn’t bear it anymore and spoke first.
“Is it that difficult to make your decision? Think about it. If you asked someone if they would rather lose their car or their house, everyone would choose their car.”
Well, that was because most people’s houses were more valuable than their cars. However, with how large the world was, there were bound to be people for whom the opposite was true.
I was the one who would decide what was important to me.
“I’ve decided.”
After a long moment of contemplation, I made my decision. His eyes sparkled with genuine curiosity.
“What will you do?”
Weren’t you just acting like you knew everything?
A perverse sense of satisfaction gripped me as I stared directly into his eyes and shrugged. “Why should I tell you? Piss off.”
“What do you—?”
Since I no longer had any business with him, I just dropped him into the burning District 7.
“—huh? Wha— Gaaaah!”
It wasn’t like a fall from this height would kill him. Still, judging by the look of complete shock on his face, he clearly wasn’t expecting the conversation to end like that for him.
Blam!
The sight of him falling into the sea of fire erased years of stress from me. I let out a great sigh, but that momentary expulsion didn’t last long.
A weight incomparably heavier than the stress release I just felt had settled in my heart. However, there was nothing I could do.
I stood dazedly atop the city wall, staring down at where I’d thrown him. Then, at last, I shook myself out of it and began to run again.
The holy land or District 7?
I made my way toward where I’d chosen.

Although his body had long ago begun to cramp, Sven Parav stayed in the comforting confines of the wardrobe. He’d already decided that even if he had to defecate in his pants, he would not leave until everything was over and done with.
However, maybe it was too optimistic of him to hope the same of his companion.
“Oh, um, are you uncomfortable?” Parav asked.
“Um... C-could I leave for a moment?”
Startled, the former paladin questioned, “Pardon? But it’s dangerous outside the wardrobe...?”
“I know that... B-but just for a moment, okay?” So said his companion in the wardrobe, Lilith Marrone, who was standing unsteadily upon her constantly shaking leg.
Even Parav, who usually had a hard time picking on cues, knew the reason she was trying to leave the wardrobe.
“Please come back quickly.”

He was worried over that small moment when the wardrobe door would open, but even he had no good reason to stop a woman’s physiological circumstances nor did he have the confidence to do so. Thus, he quickly and quietly opened the door.
“I-I’ll be back soon...!”

His companion left to go to the next room to deal with her situation, and Parav closed the door to wait, even for that short moment. It creaked open around four minutes later, later than he anticipated.
The sight that greeted him was Marrone’s inexplicably anxious expression.
“Mr. Parav...!” she gasped. “Fire, it’s fire!”
“What...?”
“The entire eastern area of District 7 is up in flames!”
The eastern area of District 7 was in the direction of District 8. Did something happen over there?
“Mr. Parav, you need to come out and see this as well!”
“Pardon?”
“Just come and see? It doesn’t look to be stopping... Maybe this entire area will start burning as well.”
“No, not ah! I’m saying we should move and relocate somewhere else.”
“I-I guess so...?”
Parav heard the logic in what Marrone was saying, yet he didn’t feel even an ounce of desire to leave the wardrobe. He decided to test his lingering sense of unease first.
“Could you close the wardrobe door for just a second...?”
Marrone froze. “Pardon?”
“Just for a moment,” he reassured, closing the door himself.
Ba-dump.
With the sound of the door closing, the uneasy feeling in his heart disappeared as he calmed down.
Sure, the door was immediately opened once again by Marrone, but he was able to confirm something with that short burst of peace he felt.
It didn’t matter if the eastern area was up in flames or not. He would be safe if he stayed in the wardrobe. It went beyond just a feeling into absolute certainty that dominated his body.
Of course, if someone else heard his theory, they would wonder if something was wrong with his head.
Yeah, I need to follow my gut feeling.
Nevertheless, he had been saved multiple times by his intuition. Even Yandel the Giant seemed to believe in his intuition and even relied on it from time to time.
“It’s fine, Ms. Marrone,” Parav concluded. “We’ll be safe here.”
“How are you so sure?”
“You are a wizard, and I am a paladin. If we use our abilities in alternating fashion, even if the entire city is on fire, we’ll be able to protect at least this one wardrobe from burning down.”
And it wasn’t like he was trying to force an impossible idea either. Paladins had multiple abilities like barriers, boundaries, holy enchantments, and others in similar veins, and so did wizards.
Marrone even seemed open to his logic—perhaps it made more sense than just pushing for his intuition. Parav didn’t let that opportunity slip him by.

“Aren’t Noarkans just teeming the streets right now? It’s too dangerous to move right now. And if we want to make that choice later on, it won’t be too late to do so after the fire reaches us here. The enemies will have no way of dealing with us due to the fire, anyway.”
“That is true... Then let’s wait for the time being.”
Marrone was about to arrive at the decision to just stay in the wardrobe and endure for the time being when, suddenly, her head whipped toward the window and stayed there.
For a moment, Parav wondered what she was doing. Then, he heard a piercing scream from outside the window.
“Eiyaaaah!”
“Captain! I’ve found a girl hiding here!”
“Aaaah! S-save me...!”
“Hahaha! She’s asking to be saved? What should we do with her?”
His heart immediately dropped.
Ba-dump!
No. No, no. It couldn’t be. Right...?
He hoped and hoped in his heart.
“M-Mr. Parav...!”
Ba-dump!
“W-we need to save her!”
But as always, his intuition was never wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 741: Reversed Fate (4)
paragraphs: He was standing in front of the city gate.
Boom! Boom!
The gate that existed as the sole pathway between the holy land and District 7.
Boom! Boom!
Thousands of barbarians were holding their weapons and slamming the ground in rhythm before that very gate.
Boom!
Somehow, the pounding pulse seemed to lend his body strength.
It was starting to really sink in now, the reality that battle was just around the corner.
Ba-dump!
Rotmiller looked over his equipment one last time.
Boom!
A bow for that one decisive blow.
A shortsword and a longsword for the fierce melee.
A round shield that he’d use to defend against ranged attacks—or that perhaps would’ve been used to defend someone important.
A gunpowder pouch that could be attached to an arrow, a smoke bomb to deny vision, a potion, scrolls...
Boom!
He even went over all the consumable items he had in his Treasure Vault. However, thanks to the meticulous, regular care he gave them, he found nothing out of order.
The deep sigh he let out lessened his nervousness somewhat.
Rotmiller settled into a stretch for the final time.
Did I...put on weight?

The equipment he had put on for the first time in a while felt tighter. Still, it was just mild discomfort. Wearing the equipment didn’t feel unfamiliar or awkward. No, rather, it felt like he finally put on his clothes.
I thought I would never wear this again.
Maybe he’d always known it subconsciously, though. Even when he was in dire need of funds, he had held onto his equipment and stashed the pieces away with care.
All for a day like this.
Boom!
After taking in his surroundings out of habit, Rotmiller’s eyes finally landed on the faces of those around him. Their expressions had all hardened with firm resolve. He thought it was very unusual.
Well, he wouldn’t have thought twice if he saw adventurers with those expressions.
Boom!

However, as the barbarians slammed the ground in rhythm like they were at some sort of festival, Rotmiller spied those all too familiar tremors raking their bodies. It was the trembling of those who were about to see battle.
Well, I suppose...
They were still people. They would bleed when stabbed with a weapon, and if they spilled too much blood, they wouldn’t be able to see their precious people again—
“The gate will open soon! Ready. For. Battle!” Ainar suddenly bellowed from the frontlines, loud enough to be heard a mile away.
The warriors who had been slamming the ground shouted in response as if they had been waiting for her signal.
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
His ears felt like they would burst from the shouting. However, he didn’t have any spare hands to block them.

Rotmiller gripped his equipment and looked directly forward. At the front of the gate stood the elite members who had been handpicked by Versyl Gowland. They, of course, had excellent gear on, and even the aura they gave off made them feel like they were on another level.

Seeing Ainar standing among them had him clutching his weapon tightly. She was protecting the gate while wielding that giant green spear that she obtained during her adventures. She looked more reliable than anyone else present.
However, the sight of her led Rotmiller to this thought.
Ah, so that’s it. So that’s what an ally of Bjorn Yandel looks like.
But there was nothing to torment himself over, no need to feel ashamed of the truth.
When had it ever been different?

He was always slow and was always left behind. People said he was thorough, but he wasn’t that way because he wanted to be either. Because he accepted his fate, Rotmiller gave up his labyrinth life and looked for a new job.

It was unproductive for him to imagine what it would be like to stand in that position over there. The people there, they had been chosen because they continued to push forward while he had stepped away.
Boom!
Most importantly, he was standing here for a different reason.
Clench.
He didn’t need to feel inferior to anyone else.
Ba-dump!
He even ignored the cries of his intuition that sensed danger.
“The barrier has fallen!”
Rotmiller raised his weapon to fight.
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
Just like those barbarians who cried out the name of their ancestral god as they faced combat, Rotmiller raised his weapons to protect something important to him.
What do I do? What do I do? What do I do?
That was the only thought taking up space in Sven Parav’s mind at that moment.
What do I do...?
As the same question continued to rattle his brain, demanding an answer.
“Huh? Did you hear me? We need to go save her.”
Save her or not?
Surprisingly enough, Parav’s conundrum wasn’t about answering that question. The answer to that was already decided.
Ba-dump!
He couldn’t save her. His intuition was screaming at him, telling him if he left the wardrobe to save that woman outside, something bad was guaranteed to happen.
No, Parav was contemplating something else entirely. Some might even think that he was the worst person in existence.
What do I do?
He was wondering what he would need to do to convince Lilith Marrone to abandon that woman alongside him. He thought it over again and again, but the answer never came to him.
And then, the golden time passed.
“We’d risk our location being discovered.”
In the end, that was all he could say.
Marrone was quiet for a moment. Then, with cold eyes and the frosty bite of betrayal in her voice, she replied, “I’m disappointed. I didn’t think you were this kind of person.”
It felt as if someone were stabbing his heart with needles. The truth came tumbling out of him as a result.

“You are more important to me than some nameless nobody, Ms. Marrone.” Even while feeling flustered at having admitted it, Parav quickly jumped to his next line. “And we need to survive to achieve that resolution we made on that day...”
Although he said it like it was an excuse, the reason still held some truth to it for him.
However, Marrone’s reaction was still distant and cold.
“If we follow our cause while ignoring the lives of others, what makes us any different from the palace?”
He couldn’t respond.
“Stay in the wardrobe, Mr. Parav. I’ll go save her alone.”
Marrone approached the window, then concentrated for a beat of silence.
“Nlia Kartetura!”
The spell that was cast with her chant fired through the shattered window and landed on the ground below.
“Eiyaaah!”
The only one left to scream was the woman. Marrone could credit her background as a military wizard for her ability to quickly and precisely spear two heads with a single spell.
She turned back to meet eyes with the man cowering away in the wardrobe.
Parav didn’t know what to say in the moment, but Marrone did.
“Don’t worry,” she said. “I won’t cause you any more trouble, Mr. Parav.”
“Pardon? What do you—?”
Before he could finish asking his question, Marrone jumped through the shattered window down onto the ground.
“Miss, please go back into the building you were in! I’ll clean up the corpses here...!”
“Huh? Oh! Okay? A-ah, I’ll help as well!”
“I’ll grab this part, so please hold the legs!”
As the hurried conversation trickled in from below, shame gnawed at him. But that didn’t change a thing.
Wham!
Parav slammed the wardrobe door shut.
The battle began not with a bang but a fizzle.
Vwoong!
The translucent barrier that once started at the walls and reached high into the sky slowly faded until it had fizzled away.
Then came the five seconds of silence.
Those five seconds were peculiar, something he had never once experienced.
Ba-dump, ba-dump.
Blood rushed to his head, his vision narrowed, and his heart beat so hard that it felt as if he would throw up.
Why aren’t they coming in?
Did the barrier just happen to dissolve because of something else?
Do I...not need to fight?
As hope budded fresh in his chest...
BANG!
A mana cannon shot destroyed the gate and dashed his hope with it.
Thankfully, thanks to the protective barrier that the wizards had cast over the area, the cannon did nothing but break the gate.
Fwoosh!
“They’re coming...!”
However, from beyond the kicked-up dirt and dust, he could hear the sounds of hundreds, maybe even thousands of soldiers running toward him.
The thudding stampede drew closer and closer.
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
Rotmiller’s first experience with war was wholly different from what he was expecting.

For instance, he’d assumed that the elite members at the front would stop the soldiers from coming in. That could hardly matter, though, when said soldiers numbered in the thousands. They were able to block the main river of foes, but they couldn’t possibly block every single stream.
“Raaaah!”
“Kill! Kill them!”
A small tributary broke through the front line and reached the second line.
“Ergh!”
“Ack!”
As if to spit upon the false peace of that odd silence, blood and screams tainted the area at the gate.
Total chaos without any strategy or tactics played out.
Right before his very eyes.
Vwoong!
An arrow shot just passed his ear, shaking him from his daze. Rotmiller then began swinging his weapon with everything he had.
Slash!
He slashed an enemy using his longsword.
Pwoong!
And fired his bow to pierce another head.
Bang!
He threw a pouch of gunpowder into the middle of the enemy, and even jumped and rolled to save an ally next to him.
He did everything he could.
That didn’t just go for Rotmiller either but everyone else present as well.
“It’s Ainar Fenelin!”
“So she’s the one we can get a rank 2 essence by killing?”
“Die!”
Ainar embodied the phrase “one-woman army” as she swung that green great spear to overpower everyone around her.
Boom!
Blood Spirit, Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.
Even if the others weren’t as famous as the two women, each clan demonstrated the teamwork they had forged over countless years.
The barbarian warriors, too, continued to fight without showing any signs of backing down.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“Kill all who came to the holy land!”
Maybe, just maybe, they would be able to stop the forces of Noark.
It didn’t take long for that hope to crumble.
Bang!
“Mana cannon! It’s the mana cannon!”
The forces of Noark had managed to claim the space above the city walls and finished setting up the mana cannons. They began to fire down at the battlefield.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Every time a mana cannon fired down at the concentrated frontline, dozens and sometimes even hundreds of people became gravely injured or died.
Ring!
Was life always something so fragile?
Rotmiller felt as if his soul were being chewed and spat out by the monster that was “war.”
“Haah... Haah...”
It hadn’t even been ten minutes since the battle began, and yet the breath struggled in his throat. His hands and legs shook with the effort it took to wield his weapons.
Maybe his ears had been damaged from the explosions too. At some point, he lost the ability to hear anything but a piercing ringing sound.
He couldn’t hear the screams of the warriors who were dying around him.
He couldn’t hear the shouting of the enemies who were charging him with the intent to kill.
There were only two sounds Rotmiller could hear.
Ring!
This piercing ringing sound that robbed him of his usual awareness, and...
Ba-dump!
The beating of his heart that yearned to live.
Surrounded by the silent tides of shouts and screams, Rotmiller swung his weapon...
Ba-dump!
All the while, ignoring the inexplicable uneasiness in his heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 742: Reversed Fate (5)
paragraphs: One minute, two minutes, three minutes...
Time crawled, slower than he had ever felt it pass before.
Four minutes, five minutes, six minutes...
The longer it went on, the more suffocated he felt. The interior of the wardrobe that had once been such a comfort began to strangle the air from his lungs and the easy rhythm from his heart.
He felt uneasy and worried.
Seven minutes, eight minutes, nine minutes...
Was she alright? Maybe she’d been discovered by other Noarkans and was in grave danger.
Tormenting scenes played behind his eyelids inside the darkness of the wardrobe.
Ba-dump!
This too was a sort of intuition. Just that this “intuition” wasn’t regarding him but someone else.
Ten minutes, eleven minutes, twelve minutes...
Sven Parav didn’t rest. Instead, he pressed his ear right up to the wardrobe door, straining to hear the sounds coming from outside.
The last thing he heard was Lilith Marrone and the woman she saved hiding the body and going into the building on the opposite side of the road. He couldn’t hear much at all after that.
They must have found a pretty good hiding place over there.
Clack, clack, clack.
Yet every time a unit of soldiers walked past them down the road, Parav felt chills go down his spine.
The wardrobe was still safe. His intuition told him that again and again—the same intuition that had saved his life many times over.
Twenty minutes, thirty minutes, forty minutes...
However, did that also apply to the building on the other side of the road?

The answer his intuition told him was no. Even without that, he could objectively deduce that it wasn’t safe. If it were, that woman wouldn’t have been caught by those lackeys and dragged out into the open streets.
Then came the “incident.”
Clack, clack, clack.
Another round of armored soldiers clanked their way down the road, then stopped.
Clack.
They had stopped in front of the building, he realized.
Damn it. He wanted them to just pass through, but his gut feeling was correct this time as well.
“They disappeared while patrolling this area?” a voice asked.
“Yes,” answered another. “Around here was the last place they put in their report.”
“Hah... Why would they bother coming all the way out here for a patrol if they were just going to mess around?”
“Well, they were using the patrol as an excuse to look for something to pawn off.”
“Well, they should’ve found themselves a woman instead.”
Unlike the proper military disciple of the Rafdonian army, the conversation was very Noarkan. That only worsened his anxiety.
It was obvious what the fate of anyone captured by those two out there would be.
Ba-dump!
In retrospect, though, the world had always been like that.
Every unlucky incident was nurtured by his worry and anxiety. The more afraid and uneasy he was, the more unfortunate events took place.
Just like now.
“Huh?” one of the voices outside suddenly wondered. “Wait, I can feel death energy.”
“Death energy...?”
“Too much time has passed, so the signature is faint... But it’s clear. Someone died here.”
“Do you have any details you can give?”
“Wait a second.” There was a long, tense silence before the man finally spoke again. “Around an hour ago, a total of three people died.”
His voice was much quieter than before, but Parav, who had finished strengthening his body with divine power, could hear him clearly. His partner spoke next.
“That matches the number of people who went missing and the time too—about an hour ago. That makes it more likely it was our men.”
“From what I can see, someone moved the corpses and used magic to erase the blood marks.”
“So not even your dark magic can figure out where the culprit went?” said the man whom Parav suspected to be the commander.
And Parav desperately hoped the dark wizard’s magic would fail him.
“Hmm... Dark magic is not omnipotent.”
“I see.”
“But I can at least see where the corpse went. It was moved into that building there.”
“The culprits could still be here. We’ll need to do a sweep of the area at least once.”

“Yes, we do. Seeing how cleanly they dealt with the corpse, they seemed to be pretty skilled... But even people of their caliber usually don’t know much about dark magic. If I didn’t detect the death energy, I wouldn’t have realized it either.”
“Just in case, let’s make a report before we go in. Hey, Lexton!”
The presumed commander called for another man, who stiffly rattled off something or another. From what Parav could tell, he was contacting the main forces.
Damn it.
His mind clouded with uncertainty once more.
Did he need to act now so that they couldn’t put in that report? Or should he stay put? The best-case scenario by far would be if they searched that house but didn’t find Marrone and the woman.
“Commander! I have finished reporting everything you told me.”
However, before he could even come to a conclusion, everything was already decided.
He lost the moment, and the only thing left he could do was observe.
“Battle formations. Since we don’t know how many enemies we are facing, we will search as carefully as we can.”
The Noarkans carefully entered the building, and minutes and seconds that felt like an eternity passed.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump...
An eternity of uncertainty over whether he’d made the right decision or not.
It was around seven minutes later when the outcome was revealed.
“C-commander!”
Boom!
“Aaaaack!”
Explosions and screams went off simultaneously to assault his ears.
With that, the battle began.
“Ergh!”
As expected of a former military wizard, Marrone responded accordingly even after being discovered. However, she was defeated in the end.
“Damn it all, we lost seven of us just because of this one woman...!”
The heavy thud of a punch was followed by the groan of a familiar voice.
“Ugh!”
“Wait, she looks familiar?”
“Lilith Marrone! She’s a military wizard and an ally of Bjorn Yandel!”
“What...? Haha! Hahaha! This is our lucky day! What an achievement!”
“If we capture her alive and bring her back, we’re sure to be rewarded for our great contribution!”
Capture her alive.
Those words sent hope soaring through Parav.
“Nah, what are you talking about?” one of the men scoffed. “That’s old news. It’s already been a while since the higher-ups said we don’t need to keep them alive.”
“Oh... Really?”
“But it’d be a waste to just kill her right here and now, right?”
“Of course! We can’t let her have an easy death when she killed seven of us.”
“I-I’ve lost an arm too!”
Even that tiny bit of hope crumbled into nothing.
There was another punch. Parav just closed his eyes and took deep, quiet breaths.
Ba-dump!
That intuition of his was playing with his heart and telling him clearly: if he blocked his ears and ignored her...
Ba-dump!
He would survive.
“Still, let’s get some information out of her. There could be allies hiding around the place.”
Even if Lilith Marrone, who put her life on the line to save another person, would die...
“Hey! Talk! Are you alone? Any allies?”
She was silent.
“Well, you’ll talk when you start hurting.”
He would live.
“Huh? Commander! There’s someone else here!”
“E-eiyaaaah!”
That innocent civilian would die.
“L-leave her alone!” came that familiar voice.
“Heh, look at how her expression changed.”
But he would live.
“Uwaaaah!”
“Huh? There’s a baby here too.”
“P-please! Not my child! Please spare my child!”
But was that right?
Parav didn’t ask himself again.
[Sven Parav has cast Sword of Condemnation.]
“Haah... Haah... Haah...”
He forced his labored breathing to relax and continued to run.
There were two reasons for doing so.
Regular breathing would let him run farther.
“Chase him!”
And he needed to run farther to live.
“Haah... Haah... Haah...”
Brown Rotmiller ran through the familiar forest paths with all his might.

He hadn’t deserted the battle or anything like that. The mana cannons firing down on them pushed their main fighting force to move away from the walls, and due to the overwhelming difference in numbers, their frontline had collapsed and a retreat order had been given.
It was a very logical plan of action.
The real plan was to act like they were retreating to expand the battle line as wide as possible, which the elite unit would then use to strike the enemy from the back.
He was able to learn that information because he had been a former ally of Yandel.
That specification of “former” felt heavier than it ever had before.
“It’s one of the ones Yandel keeps close!”
“Catch him! He’s a rank 3 essence if we catch him!”
They chased after him relentlessly. It was why he was running alone along this dense forest path.
He had been with other barbarian warriors at first, but it didn’t take long for him to realize that he was only putting them in more danger.
“Haah... Haah... Haah...”
And so, he ran and ran some more.
Unlike the true allies of Yandel, he didn’t have the power to fight against dozens of soldiers at once. However, if he continued to run, he could at least keep all those dozens of soldiers busy.
That was the most he could do as a retired scout adventurer.
“Haah... Haah... Haah...”
He forced his legs to move that were screaming at him to stop.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump!
He ignored the beating of his heart that told him he was at his limits.
Boom!
And he threw the final remaining smoke bomb in his possession—
Pshwoo!
An arrow whistled through the smoke cloud and struck his abdomen, throwing him off balance. His body slammed into the muddy ground from the impact.
It’s impossible to run.
After quickly coming to that conclusion, Rotmiller looked for a decent-looking tree and climbed it.
Fwoosh!
Immediately after, artificial winds blew away the smoke cloud, and his pursuers quickly stepped into his vicinity.
“Blast, where did he go?”
“Did we lose him?”
“I don’t see my arrow. I think it hit him!”
“Then he couldn’t have gone far. Find him!”
His pursuers quickly moved about below the tree.
Rotmiller made another calculated decision.
What did he need to do to ensure he survived?
Although he hadn’t climbed to the higher floors of the labyrinth, he had visited the labyrinth countless times and used his experience to come to the right conclusion.
I need to heal my body.

It didn’t look like they would give up their search. He would be found out sooner or later, and if they found him as he was, they would capture him against his will and there would be nothing he could do about it.
He needed to heal his body first, with one stipulation considering how his pursuers were still below him.
Do it as quietly as possible.
Rotmiller pulled out the arrow that had stabbed him in the stomach, then bit its shaft like a gag before pouring the potion onto his wound.
Sizzle.
It was the same pain as always, the pain that made him question if he was really being healed at all.
Rotmiller once again felt awe as he thought about Yandel.
He always fought while enduring this pain. How was that possible?
Ah...
Even though he himself had posed the question, he already knew the answer.
It was to survive.
His jaw reflexively tensed and the veins in his head popped as the blood flowed upward, but Rotmiller held back from making any sound.
“Huh?”
However, he was unlucky.
He’d made all the right decisions and did everything he could given the circumstances.
“Fuck! You scared me!”
But he just got unlucky.
The one who found him was the one guy among the pursuers who was lazing about and was taking a piss on the ground.
Pswhoo!
He had raised his head without a care after taking his business and ended up spotting Rotmiller. The moment the pursuer noticed him, he fired his crossbow at Rotmiller, and it pierced his thigh.
Thud!
He fell to the ground in a heap. When he regained his bearings, his pursuers were surrounding him.
“Wow, so this guy’s head is worth at least a rank 3 essence? What shall we do, Captain?”
“The order to capture them alive was rescinded a while ago. We just need to take his head and his ID, then return.”
The conversation they were having was too pedestrian to be a conversation about taking someone’s life, and the decision was made immediately.
“Can I do it?”
“You?” the captain echoed.
“When would someone like me be able to take the head of Bjorn Yandel’s ally?”
“Do what you want.”
With that, the sneaky-looking fellow was permitted to be the executioner. He approached Rotmiller while slowly rotating his dagger.
“It’ll hurt a little. I’ll need to saw through your neck since this is pretty short.”
Rather than pointlessly beg for his life, Rotmiller closed his eyes.
He only had a few more seconds to reminisce over this life he’d been given, and in those few seconds left to him, many different nostalgic faces passed through his mind.
His parents, who died when he was young because they couldn’t pay their taxes.
The director of the orphanage, who took him in and took care of him.
His master, who taught him the skills of a scout for free when he was a beginner adventurer.
They were the faces of people he was grateful to have met.
It was a tough life, but one with many things to enjoy. If he were to pick one moment from among them...
“Really, I think that time was the best.”
“Hmm?” The sneaky-looking fellow froze at Rotmiller’s muttering. “What’s this bastard talking about?”
What would Hikurod be up to while all this nonsense was going on? Did he get out safely?
Rotmiller hoped so. Even if that great forge of his was swept up in the war, survival was the highest priority.
I should’ve visited him more often.
Regret welled in his heart as other allies entered his mind.
Missha Karlstein.
Bjorn Yandel.
And...
Riol Warb Dwalkie.
Would his friend greet him with a grin? Or would he get angry that he’d come too early?
There was no telling, but Rotmiller also couldn’t help but smile.
“He’s smiling...?”
How could he not? It was only after his final moments came to him that he truly realized something.
“Really...” he murmured.
He had thought about it before. How if and when this very moment came to him, maybe he would be able to understand what that friend was feeling.
It was an absurd thought to have.
“What an amazing guy he was.”
But what about him?
Brown Rotmiller was too ordinary. He couldn’t remain with the people precious to him and had to retire as an adventurer. And ultimately, he faced an ending that was also very ordinary.
“What’s he saying?” his would-be executioner asked. “If you keep talking nonsense, I’m just going to start sawing, okay?”
He wanted to live.
He didn’t want to die.
There were too many things he had put off and too many things he had not been able to do yet, and there were many more things he probably could do in the future.
Schwing!
However, this was the end.
Rotmiller silently closed his eyes, and the face of one last person crossed his mind.
She wasn’t the savior who changed his life, or a precious ally, or someone he had spent all that much time with...
I should’ve been more honest.
Really.
Why did he have so many regrets?
“May the blessing of the twilight star be with you...”
As with any other ordinary person looking at their death, he called out for his god in his final moments.
Boom!
Then his eyes shot open at the sudden explosion.
He had no idea how it had come to be, but thankfully...
“What are you doing with my scout?”
It seemed he still had some stories left to tell.

chapters.title: Chapter 743: Reversed Fate (6)
paragraphs: Where did I need to go: District 7 or the holy land?
To be honest, it was a difficult decision to make.
“Because depending on where you go, the people who die will change...”
If I went to District 7, X would die, and if I went to the holy land, Y would die.
Although I didn’t know who exactly X or Y would be, I was certain they would both be allies who were equally precious to me.
“That will be the decision most beneficial for you, Sir Lion.”
But then, that damn “elder” gave me advice through Wolf.
That letting X die to save Y would be more beneficial to me. That I needed to head to District 7. And whatever that roundabout way analogy of a card game of fate was...
But in the end, I settled on staying the course and going to where I was originally heading: the holy land.
There wasn’t any specific reason for my choice. I even agreed with him that reversed fate was still fate in the end.
Don’t even think I’ll believe you for a second.
But Auril Gavis wasn’t someone to be trusted.

If I was destined to lose one person no matter what I did, I decided it would be better to just continue down the path of my own choice. Even if I came to regret it in the future, it would’ve been my own decision in the end.
That gramps still doesn’t know me.
He should know by now that I was resistant to blatant advice like that.
Huh?
Or was he aiming for that?

I hesitated briefly at the thought, but thinking about it more, that didn’t seem to be the case. Even without his advice, I would’ve headed for the holy land anyway. There was no reason for him to come and agitate me into making the same choice.
Whatever, let’s stop thinking about it.
Dwelling on it would only cloud my judgment, so I decided to clean the slate and focus solely on heading toward my destination.
Ten minutes, twenty minutes, thirty minutes of running later...
Boom! Bang!
I could hear the faint sound of explosions off in the distance, which sent a faint tremor through the wall that I was running on.
Just what was happening over there?
I increased my pace even more. Eventually, I spotted the part of the wall that met with the border of the holy land and went to run over to the gate.
“Huh?” I mumbled.
It was sheer coincidence that I noticed him.
I could hardly even see what was going on down there due to the dense canopy of the trees.
“Rotmiller?”
My first scout was kneeling in front of a tree, looking pretty worn out.
I wondered for a moment what was going on until I noticed some random guy approaching Rotmiller with a sword in his hand.
There was no need to think. I just leaped from the city wall with all my might.
Boom!
As if I had used Leap, the ground quaked when I landed. The ones surrounding Rotmiller went wide-eyed.
“What are you doing with my scout?”
Rotmiller also stared at me as if he had seen a ghost.
I knew it then.
“Yandel?”
X was Rotmiller.
It didn’t take long for the situation to resolve itself. Each swing of my hammer blew away one of their heads, and that was the end of it.
Well, except for the fact that they’d scattered off like cockroaches, so more than half of them got away. Still, the battle was over.
“Are you alright, Rotmiller?”
“Looks like you’re not.”
He hadn’t been able to get his bearings even then, but he came back to his senses when I poured a potion over his wounds.
Sizzle!
“Ack!”
Rotmiller regained all his energy with that potion.
“Argh! Ugh...!”
However, due to just how energetic he was, it took a while for him to calm down and return to normal.
“Yandel...”
“Looks like you’re awake now,” I observed.
“Th-thanks for saving me.”
“How are you? I have more potions.”
“I’m fine... I’m all cured.”
Hmm, if he said so.
“By the way, Yandel,” he began. “How are you here...?”
Oh, that? I understood that he was curious, but it would take too long to explain it to him. “Let’s talk about me later. I want to hear what the situation is here right now.”
Rotmiller also seemed to realize now wasn’t the time to sate his curiosity. He returned to his trustworthy self from the past and quickly briefed me on this situation.

“The Noarkans undid the barrier and invaded. Everyone retreated because the difference in numbers was too much, and when their troops were spread too thin, the elite on our side used the opening to hit the Noarkans from behind,” I summarized.
“But I have no idea if their plan succeeded or not... Now’s not the time for this. You need to go over there and help...”
I quickly put Rotmiller over my shoulder.
“Huh?” he gasped. He didn’t seem to understand why I was carrying him. “Why me? Leave me behind. I’ll only get in your way.”
Objectively speaking, Rotmiller was right. Although he was still the same, too much had changed about me from back when I was a part of Team Loser. He would only get in the way instead of helping.
“You’re my scout.”
However, I couldn’t bear to just leave him behind, and I had no guarantee he’d be safe just because I saved him this once.
“You’ll need to tell me where I’m going.”
Rotmiller froze at my joking tone, then smirked. “You really haven’t changed.”
“Isn’t there a saying that a person dies when they change? I’m going to live for a long time.”
It took him a moment to respond. “I don’t know what happened with their plan, but we should head toward the gate for now.”
With that, I hurriedly dashed toward the gate with Rotmiller over my shoulder.
Naturally, the path was teeming with Noarkans. Not to say they got in my way or anything.
Boom! Boom!

Although it was a soldier’s duty to block an enemy’s charge, the Noarkans all hurriedly rolled out of the way when they saw me roll in like a tank. Thanks to them being kind as always to those stronger than them, it didn’t take long for me to get through the forest and arrive in front of the gate, which was now riddled with battle scars.
A lot of people died...
The gate’s threshold was littered with corpses. Many of the bodies were Noarkans, but a significant number of them were my allies—most of them barbarian warriors.
Among the corpses, I could see the warriors I had become familiar with during my life as a barbarian.
The one who bought the very first house when the real estate market opened.
The one who I hit in the head when he complained about the quality of equipment improving at the coming-of-age ceremony and asked me to give him one.
And even the one who asked me to name his son so that he could grow up to become a great warrior.

As I took in their faces, I couldn’t help but clench my teeth. Still, I moved on to finish my survey of the area. For some weird reason, the Noarkans avoided meeting my gaze and backed away when I looked at them.
They’re not important. Ignore them.
There were only two things I needed to care about.
The place where the gate should be was completely blown away. Even the wall around it had crumbled. The debris pile was so high that it blocked the only path between the holy land and District 7.
That, and...
“Huh? Isn’t that Yandel?”
“What? Mister? It’s Mister! Mister!”
Much to my surprise, I found my allies looking down at me from atop the walls. The instant I saw them, I began to count.
Ainar, Versyl, Missha, Erwen, James Calla... Everyone was here except for Amelia, Auyen, Parav, and Marrone—
“Mister!”

Erwen leaped down from the high walls with a light step and ran toward me. Considering her physical ability, Erwen wouldn’t get injured from a jump of that height, but I instinctively reached out to catch her as she fell.
“Where were you, really? I was so worried about you!” she admonished.
“I’ll tell you everything later, so tell me the current situation.”

Although we were surrounded by Noarkans, I found no issue with opening the conversation here. Due to my reputation, they only stared at us and kept their distance, not showing even a hint of interest in getting closer.
“From what I heard from Rotmiller, you went and attacked the Noarkan command line at the back. Did you succeed?” I asked.
“Ah, that... That was a failure.”

Although Erwen described it as a failure, I realized the situation wasn’t as grim as that when I heard all the details. The group wasn’t able to kill the enemy leaders, but they did manage to collapse the gate and block off the entrance while leaving the Noarkan elites, who had chased after them, outside the walls.
“Now we are the ones with control of the wall! We won’t let the Noarkans send in reinforcements!”
Hmm, so that was why they were on the wall. If I hadn’t noticed Rotmiller back then, I would’ve met them on the wall here.
“Anyway, so Ms. Gowland...” Perhaps because I had been away for so long, Erwen rambled on to keep the conversation going even though we were in the middle of a war.
I smirked and cut her off there. “It’s fine. It’s obvious what the next step in the plan is.”
“Eh?”

What do you mean, eh? If we continued to hold the line at the wall, the enemy forces within the holy land could never increase in strength. Put another way, the forces that were already inside the holy land had been cut off from the main forces of Noark.
There was only one thing left to do.
“Isn’t the only thing left to do just wipe them out?”
“Ah! You’re really smart!”
I was used to Erwen’s blind praise, so I let it slip and just focused on taking another look around.
Maybe they heard that the gate had collapsed, or maybe I had drawn too much attention while running all the way here.
Either way, the once-open area in front of the gate had filled with Noarkans.
One, two, three, four...
There were too many of them to even count. It would take quite a long time if I wanted to hammer each one of their heads alone.
“Erwen, get ready.”
“Pardon?”
“We’ll be doing ‘that’ for the first time in a while.”
“A-ah... That...?”
Even though I had omitted the subject, Erwen recognized what I meant and immediately began to use a skill.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Elementalization.]
I didn’t need to mention the attribute either.

[The wind spirit dwells in your body. All damage is bestowed with dodging adjustments. Damage received from magic is doubled. You have received a bonus against penetration and cuts. Dexterity stat has risen significantly...]
Because nothing worked better to clear out hordes of mobs.
[The ranges of all attacks are tripled.]
[You have cast Swing.]
My hammer grew like the staff of the Monkey King and stretched toward my enemies.
Boom!
A refreshing sound echoed out over the entire battlefield, but it was drowned out by the sound of my mind racing.
“R-run away!”
“H-how are we supposed to fight something like that?!”
X was Rotmiller, and X survived because I came to the holy land.
Boom!
Then who was Y?

chapters.title: Chapter 744: Scout (1)
paragraphs: Sven Parav stepped beyond the wardrobe’s door and headed for the window.

His head was overheating from all the stress he was under, and his thought process had taken on a new life of its own. It was as if another personality that had been buried deep within his heart had arisen to control him.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump.
From the moment he left the wardrobe, his heart galloped but his mind sang with certainty.
He jumped out through the window.
Vwoong!

His first attack went for the unguarded dark wizard standing at the back. It wasn’t a logical decision he made but an unconscious reaction. He only began to think again after slashing the dark wizard’s neck.
Since the most dangerous variable here, the dark wizard, was dead, he wouldn’t have trouble with the rest of them. That expectation proved true enough shortly thereafter.
“Who are you?!”
“Kill him!”
The Noarkan soldiers only noticed the attack when the dark wizard’s head had already fallen to the ground. They all turned to attack Parav. Surprisingly, one among them recognized him as well.
“Sven Parav! He’s Yandel’s ally!”
So it was less that he’d gained somewhat of a reputation for himself, and more that the person he hung out with was plenty famous.
A natural phenomenon, really.
“You damn bitch! So you did have allies nearby!”
Although his identity had been revealed immediately, Parav didn’t falter. He just focused on swinging his sword.
Vwoong!
Slash!
With each swing of his sword, arms, legs, and even necks were severed.
It was a one-sided fight.
Slash!
When he regained his senses after the battle, there were no Noarkans left standing.
Parav silently lowered his head to look down at his white greatsword. He had recently acquired it after renouncing his affiliation with the Reatlas Church and his position as a paladin.
That once-white sword was stained dark red.
He looked sidelong at the corpses surrounding him on the ground. They were cold, lifeless.
“Mr. Parav?”

Curiosity grew in Parav’s heart. Although he didn’t know how strong that dark wizard he’d killed via ambush was, the Noarkan soldiers were unbelievably weak if they could be defeated by someone like him.
Just why were these people...?
So just why were they so bent on going around bullying those who were weaker than them?
“Mr. Parav!”
He regained his senses when he heard Marrone’s frightened voice.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump...
As his mind eased after the tidal wave of excessive stimulation, the intuition he had forgotten for a moment reactivated.
Ba-dump!
This place was dangerous. He could die if he stayed here.
Parav quickly raised his head and looked toward the window.
However, he knew it instinctively. Even if he went back and crouched in that wardrobe over there, he would no longer be safe.
The only place in the city he’d deemed “safe” was no longer so.
“Mr. Parav?”

However, he had no time to wallow in despair. The enemies had made a report before they discovered Marrone. Another unit would be sent their way as soon as the enemy forces realized that their contact had been cut off.
So what was the one thing he needed to do in the instant? His intuition always guided his decision-making was busy, so it was actually easier to come to a fast decision.
“We need to move now.”
He needed to get out of there. As quickly as possible.
He dashed through a bleak street, carrying a total of three people on his back.
A wizard, a mother, and her child.
“Where are we going? This is the direction of the fire.”
“That’s why we’re going this way.”
The reason he headed toward the eastern area of District 7, which was already half engulfed in flames, was simple:

The fire was less scary than other people. And this place was still acting as a source of the still spreading fire, there would be fewer soldiers. It was obvious at a glance that the fire was too large to stop at this point, after all.
Hiding nearby was the best choice they could make, and if something did go wrong, they could just jump into the fire and use divine power and magic to endure the flames.
Ba-dump, ba-dump!
Even while knowing it was dangerous, he ignored his intuition and ran.

With each step he took, he felt shockwaves rattle his spine, as if he were running atop an active earthquake. His spine shook from the weight of the three people he was carrying on his back. The mother’s body was also larger than a regular woman’s, so he needed to use both hands to carry everyone.
It would be a major problem if they were discovered by an enemy on the way.
“I’m sorry.”
After a while of running, he heard an apology from his back. It came from Lilith Marrone.
“About what?” he asked.
“About getting angry and saying you were something you were not.”
Hearing the deep guilt in her voice, Parav felt needles stab his heart. “You don’t need to apologize. You didn’t say anything wrong.”
“No, I was wrong. You ended up saving us. So what I’ve said is already disproven.”
Hmm... He supposed that was one way to take it?
It did feel like she was forcing an outcome from a pre-drawn conclusion, he didn’t deny what she said.
Having an in-depth discussion about it would be meaningless at this rate. Plus, it helped him lessen the regret a little.
Regret for having left the wardrobe.
“So...” said the mother. “Are we heading toward the eastern area? Where the fire is?”
Perhaps the situation before was too out of the ordinary for him. For the first time, he realized her voice sounded calm and refined. She also seemed to have some tenacity.
“I wasn’t able to say anything before due to the situation we were in, but thank you for saving me and my son...”
Hearing that made Parav uncomfortable. “I didn’t do it for any praise.”

In truth, he had just then been thinking that if the worst-case scenario were to come, he might need to abandon the mother and her son. It was a realistic thought to have, and one he hadn’t yet decided to act upon. However, even while contemplating, Parav knew that if such a situation were to come to pass, abandoning them and leaving with just Lilith Marrone was always the right—
“Still, thank you... Anyway, that’s not what I wanted to talk about... If we’re heading toward the eastern area, how about we head to the eastern branch of the Reatlas Church?”
It was a completely unexpected idea. “The...Reatlas Church?”
“Yes. My husband is an adventurer, and since the world has become quite a wicked place recently, he informed me frequently about where I should go to find shelter, depending on the situation.”
“But judging by that fire, there is a very good chance that the eastern branch has already been swallowed by the flames.”
“No, that’s even more reason to go there. From what my husband told me, the eastern branch of District 7 has a fire protection divine spell, or something like that applied to the entire building.”
He thought for a moment that maybe she was mistaken. Even though he had been a paladin of the Reatlas Church, he had never heard of such a thing.
“Do you perhaps know what rank your husband is?” he asked first.
“Rank 3.”

That greatly increased the trustworthiness of the information. The man wasn’t just any random guy, but a rank 3 adventurer. He wouldn’t have told his wife incorrect information about places she could find shelter in.

Also, maybe it was different for the bishops who worked in administration, but not all paladins knew about the situation in all branches. The information from an adventurer who looked around to ensure the safety of his wife was more trustworthy.
A building that can endure fire...
If that truly existed, then it would be the ideal shelter for them.
“The problem is if we can get there safely... Will it be possible? From what I heard, Mr. Yandel has something that lets him walk through fire without any problem.”
Ah, she was talking about the Orb of Fire...
It was pretty famous.
“If Ms. Marrone and I combine our strength, us three... No, us four including the child will be able to get there safely.”
That was if they didn’t encounter any enemies on the way. Parav purposefully left that little detail out.
“Goodness... Then that’s a relief. I am quite lucky to have met people like you...”
“Yes... But why were you hiding on that street, miss? District 7’s evacuation would’ve ended a long time ago... Why didn’t you evacuate with the others?”
He suddenly became curious about her situation, and she was quite unfortunate as well.

“No, I did evacuate. However, since the other districts were all overflowing with refugees, people like us could only stay around the outskirts. We were so close to the battle line that we could hear the sounds of fighting and people dying every day. And after some time...the palatial army was heavily pushed back and the Noarkans pushed into our territory.”
The Noarkans who flooded in like the tide also pulled back while kidnapping any civilian they could get their hands on.

From what she heard from the other civilians who were taken, they were going to be used as human shields, but she wasn’t sure of it. Before she was ever taken to the battle line to be used as such, she had already managed to escape.
“A huge ball of fire fell from the sky.”
The retaliation of the palace dealt a sizable blow to the enemy, but the attack seemed to hold no care for the civilians taken hostage. She was lucky to have survived and used the chaos to run away.
“There are probably a lot of people who are hiding in District 7 like me. A few thousand people were taken as hostages back then...”
“So something like that happened...”
War truly only bred tragedy.
After hearing the details of her situation, a question struck Parav as he continued to run.
What happened to this woman’s husband?

He thought on it for a bit but ultimately let that question remain just that—a question. Rather than sate his curiosity, he needed to focus more on running. There were truths in this world that could be unveiled even without asking for answers.
They were in the middle of a war, where it wouldn’t be odd for any one, single person to die. Why would push a rank 3 adventurer to leave behind his child and wife?
Parav didn’t ask.
However, the military wizard Lilith Marrone took a different approach.
“Do you...know what happened to your husband?”
She posed her question carefully. However, the woman unexpectedly gave a calm answer.
“I don’t know. When this whole thing happened, he was conscripted into the army. I truly hope that he is safe...” the mother mumbled with heartfelt desire.
“Your husband will definitely be fine,” Marrone consoled her. “He’d probably be running around looking for you after realizing that you’re gone.”
They were words that warmed the heart, and yet the mother’s reaction was tepid at best.
“Well... I hope that he doesn’t do anything reckless like that and remains in a safe place...”
“Pardon?”
Marrone tilted her head at the unexpected answer, and the mother’s ears peeked out from behind her black fur.
“Well, my husband is bad with directions... I’m worried he’ll go somewhere dangerous just to look for me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 745: Scout (2)
paragraphs: Unlike the comforting embrace of the wardrobe, the streets were bleak and plagued with death.
Parav continued to run, and then he ran even farther.
Lilith Marrone, the woman he still didn’t know the name of, and the child who tearfully clutched at him even still.
He was carrying all three people on his back.
Parav’s unease did not lighten with distance. Rather, his mind only grew increasingly more abuzz with different thoughts, each of which was small and insignificant.
It felt uncomfortable to run because both of his hands were occupied.
His hips felt stiff after being in the wardrobe for so long. He wanted to eat strawberries straight out of the fridge.
Why did the Goddess not grant her paladins any sort of movement ability?
If I had Giantization as well...
Then he could have easily carried three people on his back and run much more efficiently. There were quite a few essences with amazing abilities like that.
Despite his sudden jealousy, however, there was not much he could do. The faithful who possessed divine power couldn’t consume essences, like the wizards.
Why is that even the case?
The church said their souls were the Goddess’s and so mustn’t be tainted with the marks of other souls. But how did that even make sense—?
