Parav froze.

“Everyone, quiet,” he whispered, then quickly hid between the buildings. Simply put, they were less than five minutes away from the burning eastern area of District 7. “It seems the palatial army and the Noarkans are fighting.”
“How about we look for a different alley? We could go around them.”
“If we want to get to the eastern branch you talked about, going through this will be the quickest path.”
It would take around three times as long to go around the conflict, and there was the question of whether we could even find a suitable path when everything was on fire.
“Since it doesn’t seem like any one side has the upper hand, how about we use the opportunity to quickly push in?” Marrone suggested.
Parav thought it over for a moment, then nodded. “Alright. That will be a little dangerous, but considering everything, I think it will be the safest way forward.”
With that, the discussion was over.
Parav let out a deep breath before running from the alley into the battlefield. His two hands were already sealed away to hold the three on his back.
“I’ll leave it to you!” he whisper-shouted.

With that, Marrone was the only person on defense. Parav couldn’t help but be uneasy at the fact he was putting his safety in the hands of someone else, there was nothing he could do. He even considered just closing his eyes and running straight ahead blindly.
That might be too much, right?
In the end, though, he kept his eyes open as he charged into the bloody battlefield.
“Who are those guys?”
“Are they enemies?”
At first, neither side acted because they couldn’t tell if these newcomers were allies or foes, but that confusion didn’t last long.
“Lilith Marrone!”
“Sven Parav!”
“They’re allies of Yandel!”
“Kill them!”
The Noarkans recognized them and immediately began to attack them while the palace soldiers supported them in turn, and very enthusiastically, at that.
“Allies of Yandel! The palace is definitely scheming something! We need to kill them here!”
“Seeing how focused they are while charging in, there’s definitely a good reason for it! We need to give our all to protect them!”
It was a completely unexpected turn of events. He had just been planning on using the chaos of battle to sneak through.
I guess the positives and negatives cancel out?
He didn’t need to think too hard about it. He just needed to focus on going straight and breaking through to the other side.
Boom!
“Uwaaak!”
Stab!

The palace wizards deflected the spells flying in, and the soldiers defended against the swords aimed at his chest. The attacks that slipped through were blocked by the mana barrier Marrone had just barely managed to put up.
It was close call after close call.
Fwoosh!

The result was that he got through the battlefield without injury and arrived at the still-burning eastern area. Even then, the people trying to kill them and the people trying to protect them were all fighting behind him...
Well, they wouldn’t follow him into the flames.
[Sven Parav has cast Prayer of Protection.]
Parav cast the divine spell, as planned. After quickly confirming that a thick barrier had surrounded the four people protected by Marrone, he began to run into the fire.
“Huh?”
“Why is he going there?”
The allies and enemies all mumbled in defeat when they noticed him running into the flames.
Fwoosh!

After entering the fire, he began to quickly run down the street. It was difficult to see where he was going due to the flames and smoke, but since he just needed to go straight, he didn’t have much trouble.
“Over there!”
Sometime later, Parav finally spied the eastern branch of the Reatlas Church in the distance. The small temple had an all-too-familiar statue of the Goddess installed at the entrance.

It seemed that the adventurer husband’s words were true. Even though everything around it burned down, the church stood tall in its original form. A translucent barrier shimmered in the dancing flames yet blocked those flames from approaching the building.
After entering the barrier, he went to the large door of the entrance, and it opened without a key.
“Wh-who are you?”
However, surprisingly, there were people inside the temple. Quite a number of them, at that.
“How did you get here through the flames...?”
“I-I don’t think they’re Noarkans...”
“Stay behind me for now.”
As the four of them appeared, the evacuees put up their guards, worry clear in their eyes.
One, two, three, four, five, six...
A total of thirty-seven evacuees were here.
Of course, it wasn’t all that odd to see people hiding away from the flames and the war. The four of them had also come to find safety and shelter, after all.
No, the real problem was...
“I-it’ll be fine... Nothing will happen here...”
Parav instinctively felt it.
Ba-dump.
This place wasn’t safe either.
“Hmm? Ah! If you’re talking about the chieftain, I saw him in that forest over there! He’s breaking the heads of the corpses, saying they could be acting like corpses!”
“I see. But isn’t this entire area forested...?”
“No, are you even listening to what I am saying? That forest! That forest over there!”
“So... As I am rather busy, could you perhaps relay the message to Mr. Yandel for me? That since all the enemies in the holy land are dead, he should come over here to help.”
“Sure!” The warrior in his late twenties turned and went back the way he came.
How is he so simple and innocent while looking so rough...?
Versyl Gowland only smiled for a moment as she stared after the warrior’s retreating figure. Then, she quickly scanned the battlefield.
Although the battle was over, there were far too many things that needed to be done.
First of all, the enemies could launch another invasion, so she needed people vigilant and on the walls.
The corpses stacked up like mountains also needed to be dealt with. At this rate, they would start rotting and spreading their stench everywhere, and it wouldn’t be hygienic either.
“That one is a Noarkan! Just throw it to the side!”
“It’s difficult to tell between humans!”
“Hah... Then we’ll check if they’re a Noarkan or not so you can go and gather the barbarians instead!”
“Oh, good idea!”
Even though she hadn’t given a detailed order, the operation slowly evolved to be more efficient over time.
The way that different corpses were treated was like day and night. The allied remains were gathered with respect while the enemy corpses were just thrown into a pile.
“Gowland... No, vice-captain. What will we do with the Noarkan corpses? As ordered, we’ve looted them for their belongings and just thrown them in a mound...”
Versyl gave a short answer to Kaislan’s question. “We’ll burn them all. It’s not as if we will be giving them a burial when we don’t even know their names.”
“What about the belongings of the warriors and the adventurers that were recovered? What will we do with those?”

“Organize them next to their respective bodies. After most of them are gathered, we’ll apply preservation magic on them. We’ll have to send the belongings back to the family of the deceased once they’ve been identified, so be sure that no one puts their hands on them.”
“I don’t believe anyone would do such a thing, but I will ask them to be more careful.”

Versyl couldn’t help but let a wry smile slip as she looked down from the walls at the ground being cleaned up. Since she was looking down from an advantageous position, she could see more clearly the contrast in the treatment of the corpses, and that allowed her to once again realize why they needed to win this war no matter what.
If the Noarkans had won, the situation would’ve been the complete opposite—
“Behel—LAAAA!”
“Behel—LAAAA!”
A sudden outburst from below her startled her out of her thoughts.
It was obvious who had arrived.
“The strongest warriors in the world!”
“The guardian of the holy land has arrived!”
There was only one person those warriors would shout for and laud with such respect.
“Chieftain! It’s the chieftain!”
Versyl left the wall patrol to James Calla, the one with the best eyesight among the group, and went down to the ground.
“Mister... You’re not hurt anywhere, right? I was really worried about you...”
“I’m not. And I was worried for you as well.”
“R-really?”
“Hmm? Naturally.”
“Hehe... I guess it’s not unnatural... Or is it?”
Erwen was so happy to see him after all this time that she just attached herself to him. However, compared to her, Yandel looked somewhat exhausted.
“Good work,” Versyl greeted him.
“Ah, good work to you too. I’m sure it was a difficult position to be in.”
It was a short bit of encouragement, yet for some reason, she couldn’t muster a response.
The weight of the words “difficult position” weighed heavy on her. Although it hadn’t been her first time acting as the vice-captain of a clan, circumstances were completely different now.
Back then, there hadn’t been a war, and the bond between the members wasn’t this tight either.
But this man did this work every single day.
She felt once more just how much suffering this barbarian, who at first seemed simple-minded and ignorant, had endured for so long.
“I want to hear everything that happened up to now,” he said.
“Oh, sure.”
Versyl calmly explained everything that had happened. However, for some reason, she couldn’t help but mix her emotions into the report.
She would complain at some points while showing sadness in others. It was like she was a kid explaining to her father the bad things that happened at her school that day.
“I see.”
After the status report, the barbarian took a moment to think before dishing out an order as if the conclusion were obvious.
“Versyl, call all the members of all the clans. I have something to say.”

Funnily enough, that order of his gave her more relief than any order ever had before. It was unexpected considering her more proactive personality. Who could’ve guessed that just following orders without needing to carry any responsibility could be so freeing?

“I’ll gather them right away.” She didn’t add any comment and immediately summoned everyone to Yandel. Only once that was finished did she ask for the reason for the gathering. “So what are you going to tell us...?”
“I’m just thinking of going out and fighting with everyone. I heard that they are pretty skilled?”
“Skilled, well... They’d probably want to just stay here and stay safe?”
Versyl tried to be as careful with her words as possible, but the barbarian smiled as if he didn’t care about anything.
“Oh, that? Don’t worry about that.”
He then patted her on the shoulder to encourage her before stepping up in front of everyone.
“Greetings. I heard that you followed my vice-captain and remained in my holy land while I was away?”
“Pardon? Ah, yes... Thank you, Baron Yandel.”
“Yeah. You should be thankful. If you have any conscience.”
He didn’t mention anything about them risking their lives to protect the holy land and only mentioned the generosity shown to them as he continued.
“The reason I called you all here is simple.”
“What is it?”
“Oh, it’s nothing much. I’m planning on going out to fight now, and I want you guys to help me.”
“Us?”

The status as a baron, the reputation as the Giant. They couldn’t say anything since they were outmatched in those two respects. However, their eyes could at least shoot him looks that screamed, “And why would we do that?”
Yandel, however, was perceptive.
“Then do you want to be kicked out of the holy land instead?”
It was a proverbial stick that was only possible for him to use because he was a barbarian who didn’t care about empty formalities and pretenses.
“So you’re saying if we don’t follow you, you’ll kick us out of the holy land? How can you threaten us like that?”
“The evil traitors have waged war against us, and you plan on ensuring your safety and your safety alone? Is that something an honorable citizen of Rafdonia should do?”
Since he invoked the name of the palace as well, the adventurers couldn’t dare to oppose him. They all went silent instead.
The more surprising thing happened after that.
“Don’t worry too much,” Yandel reassured. “This is an opportunity for you to gain achievements.”
“And by achievements, you mean...?”
As soon as talks of gains were mentioned, the eyes of the adventurers began to sparkle.

“You might not know because you’ve been stuck in here, but the army from District 5 has been moved into District 7 at my request. The army is attacking from the north... And on my way here, I caused a fire, so the eastern area is a mess too. What do you think would happen if we now attack from where we are now, the south?”
“We’ll surround the enemy!”

“Yes, and why do you think their forces left their soldiers here and retreated? Do you think they just backed away because you managed to collapse the gate? No. They had no choice but to back away because they had something more serious to deal with at the back!”
“Ah! So something like that happened...!”
“I was curious about that as well, but now it all makes sense!”
After going hard with the stick at first, he then pulled out the carrot. The adventurers all listened to him as if hypnotized. It didn’t take long for them to completely come over to his side.
“So, I’m planning on taking everyone able to fight over to District 7...”
Versyl’s jaw dropped. She couldn’t help but be amazed at what she was seeing.
Are these the same people from before?

When she was acting as vice-captain, these adventurers did nothing but try to look for ways to skimp out on fighting, even when she argued that they needed to protect the holy land for their own survival. But now, their eyes were all sparkling with motivation.
“Anyone want to back out?”
It was as if they all believed success was the only outcome.

chapters.title: Chapter 746: Scout (3)
paragraphs: Parav decided to first earn the trust of the thirty-seven evacuees currently in the eastern branch. The task didn’t pose much of a challenge.
“Hello! My name is Sven Parav. While I am not a practicing member at the moment, I was once a paladin of the Reatlas Church and have since become an active member of the Anabada Clan!”
After all, he used to be a career clergyman and was now even a member of a clan that was quite famous among the civilians.
“Anabada... That’s Baron Yandel’s clan!”
“I don’t care about that, but a paladin! By the Goddess! We are saved!”
“But how do we know that he is telling the truth—?”
“Hey, shut up! Don’t you see that woman beside him? I don’t know her name, but I know I saw her back during the ceremony. She was with Baron Yandel!”
“W-we’re saved!”
It didn’t take long for caution to make way for relief. The consequence of that, however, was that people tended to get chatty once a weight of stress had been lifted off their shoulders.
“Um, Mr. Paladin! What’s happening outside?”
“Did you happen to see a boy about this tall on your way here?”
“What will happen to us now?”
“The palace sent you to save us, right?”
Dozens of evacuees asked him countless questions. Parav took the newly chaotic and directionless mood in stride, attempting to answer as much as he could and with as much grace as he could muster.
“The war is still ongoing outside. The palatial soldiers have entered District Seven, so we’ll need to wait and see how it plays out.”
“Sorry. I don’t think I’ve seen anyone of that description.”
“We need to stay here and wait it out.”
“Unfortunately, the palace didn’t send us here to save you. We wound up coming here to get away from the battle just like you.”
The hope in the eyes of the evacuees mellowed out at his brutally honest answers. However, Parav deemed this better than the alternative.
Nothing was more brutal than unfounded hope.
“You weren’t sent by the palace...?”
“Damn it!”
“I did find it odd. How would the palace even know that we’re here?”
“They wouldn’t send anyone even if they knew. Didn’t you see it before? Those balls of fire fell on where we were! The palace doesn’t care if we live or die!”
Anger filled in the gaps where hope had left.
Even so, some had a different perspective.
“I’m honestly glad you have nothing to do with the palace.”
“An ally of Baron Yandel... I’ll trust you.”
“Yes! It’s a relief that both of you are here, Mr. Paladin and Ms. Wizard! We were pretty scared just by ourselves...”
These few people were excessively optimistic compared to the angered evacuees.
Parav did, of course, wonder why these people who seemed so uneasy and afraid didn’t even bother locking the front door.
“Ha, haha...”
But he swallowed the question with an awkward laugh. Such minor things weren’t what was important.
“I want to understand the situation here,” he announced. “Is there an adventurer among you?”
With his identity revealed, Parav slipped easily into directing the conversation, using that to gauge the others’ combat strength. However, what he found was below expectations.
The evacuees just darted their eyes away at his question. Interestingly, those eyes all ended up glancing in the same direction, like they were looking at the one person with the answer.

Parav followed their gazes to find a middle-aged man whose eyes darted away as he let out a dry cough. “I-I’ve just had experience entering the labyrinth a few times! And it’s been a while since I’ve retired!”
“Okay, I see.”
One retired adventurer. One who seemed reluctant to speak up in the event they would be made to do dangerous things.
“Mister, what do you mean just a few times?! You told us you were pretty famous and powerful back in your day!”
“You brat!” the man scolded, clearing his throat. “Even so, how could I compare myself with Baron Yandel and his allies?”
“Could I ask what your rank was before you retired?”
“I... I was rank seven.”

“I see.” Parav gave a slow nod, then asked the retired rank seven adventurer to take care of the evacuees. He was probably better suited for that than fighting. Once that was settled, he said, “I’m planning on creating an encampment here just in case. Could I receive some help?”
“Just tell us what to do, Sir Paladin!”

“Then please gather anything that can be used to block the door. Chairs, tables, wardrobes...” He went around with the other evacuees to lock the entrance and even finished creating a rudimentary barricade in front of it.
“Mr. Parav,” Marrone called. “It’s good that we have a defensive line here, but wouldn’t this also block our exit if something were to happen?”
“Couldn’t we just leave through the windows in that case?”
“But all the windows are on the second floor. We could get out, but it’d be difficult for these people to leave with us. There are children and the elderly here.”
“That...”
Parav trailed off. She hadn’t said anything he could refute, but there was nothing he could do even if he agreed with her.

Even then, a certain thought wouldn’t leave him be. If such a situation were to come to pass, the church would be fully surrounded, anyway. Would it even be possible to escape with thirty-seven evacuees who are all noncombatants?

Here he was, a former paladin sheltered within a temple that housed the goddess statue of Reatlas, and yet if he was going to be stuck between a rock and a hard place, his choice between the two was simple: it would be impossible to take everyone.
I’m not a monster like Bjorn Yandel. I can’t do it.

“There’s no point thinking about escaping at this point,” Parav said instead. “The risk that the enemy will follow us here is low, to begin with... That, and we don’t need to worry about that risk in the first place if we can just block the entrance well enough.”
“I suppose that is true... If we can just defend our position, we won’t have a reason to run away.”

Marrone also didn’t seem to have a good enough reason to refute him. Rather than reply, she just began inscribing a magic circle that would help them defend the door. A small sigh escaped her as she worked.
A few moments later, Parav slowly turned and walked away without a destination.
“Where are you going?” she called from behind him.
“I’ll take a look around and check the structure of this building.”
“Ah, I see...”

Despite the excuse, there was no need for him to search the building. Most temples were built in the same way, after all. The worship hall on the first floor and the location of the stairs that led to the second floor were all familiar to him, and even the residences of the priests and the administration rooms on the second floor were the same as any of the other smaller branches.

After taking one long loop around the entire building, he returned to the worship hall on the first floor. All the chairs had been moved out for the barricade, so he just sat down on the barren floor.
For a reason he couldn’t quite name, he wanted to rest.
However, the others apparently misunderstood his intentions. The evacuees who came up to speak with him no matter what he was doing stepped away just this once without saying a word.
It was only for a moment that he found it odd.
As he opened his eyes and looked in front of him, he saw the statue of the Goddess Reatlas.
Did they think I was praying?
That was pretty funny. Although he had lived a long time with the title of paladin, he was far from a faithful person.
The goddess of the stars...
He looked upon the statue of the goddess that was said to rule over adventure and relationships and asked a silent question.
What is it that you want from me?
Naturally, he didn’t get a response back. Silence was the only thing that followed, one created by the evacuees who were all staying quiet so they didn’t interrupt his prayer.
As he peeked through half-closed eyes, he could see everyone facing his direction with closed eyes, while some were even repeatedly drawing the goddess’s symbol in the air with their hand.
Parav closed his eyes once more. Then, mumbling under his breath just as one would do when wishing upon a shooting star, he said this:
Please save us. Please?
He wasn’t any different from the other evacuees.

A total of fifteen clans were in the barbarian holy land, including Anabada. Excluding the rank seven adventurers in special positions, the rest of the clans also had members of rank 6 and above. In total, they numbered 207.
There were originally more than that, but most of the lower-ranking adventurers died on their way here. As such, the people present were the only ones left, or so I heard.
Whatever the case, adding Ainar and the 800 elite barbarian warriors I carefully selected gave us a military might of over a thousand people.
Considering the scale of the event, it probably wasn’t all that strong of a group, but still.
It can’t be helped.
Increasing the number would only increase the number of casualties. That was why our group only consisted of the elites wanting to follow me into the great battle and defend the holy land.
“The preparations are done,” Versyl said, interrupting my internal calculations.
“Really? Good work.”
I stood in front of the gate. All of the debris had already been moved away.
Even though I’m kind of sick of it at this point, it’s not like I can’t do it before we go either.
I looked at the thousand-strong army, who were looking to me for guidance.
“We will now head to District Seven.”
My voice wasn’t the bellow it could have been, but there shouldn’t be a problem since everyone was paying close attention to what I was saying.
“While fighting our enemies, some will die, and some will survive.”
My stoic declaration was too realistic and demoralizing to be a declaration that a war general might make right before going to battle. I knew that, but it couldn’t be helped.
“Some will lose their spouses because of this, and some will lose their parents.”
When had it changed?
At some point, I no longer wanted to use sweet talk to fool and impart false hope upon other people.
“That is why, you must know this! When you kill your enemies, know what cause you are killing them for! If you are killed by our enemies, know what cause you put your life on the line for!”
Inexplicably, excitement rose within me as I began to shout.
“I will head to District Seven to protect the people I hold dear! Tell me! For what cause are you going to District Seven?”
The answer would be different for everyone.
“Because we can’t let the chieftain fight by himself!”
Some were following me out of respect.
“Because I will become a great warrior!”
While some wanted to obtain fame and glory.
“Haha! You said this would be an opportunity to gain some achievements!”
While some wanted to sate their base desires.
“Those damn bastards need to disappear so that our families can rest easy once again!”
While others went to war to protect the ones they held dear, just like me.
And so, I made my stance clear.
“Even if everyone wants different things, our goals are the same. That is why we will walk the same path and fight while entrusting our backs to each other.”
I promised them.
“I will walk farther than everyone else. I will remember why you fought and died today. Follow me. Entrust your hope to me.”
There was nothing else for me to say. Ours was a cold-hearted world that didn’t allow one to live unless they fought.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
I was just the person to take the first steps.
Finally, we entered District Seven.
We might have been in the middle of a war, but the streets we ran down were all familiar to us.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“Raaaaah!”
“Grant me your protection!”
“Nia Rafdonia!”
With weapons clutched tightly in hand, we each let out our own battle cry.
“Ahhhhh!”

As we ran down the barren streets, we soon noticed a group of people in the distance, seemingly Noarkans. There were only around ten of them. From what I could tell, it seemed they were stationed here to keep watch of the holy land.
“E-emergency! Emergency! Around a thousand people came out from the holy land! Bjorn Yandel is charging from the front!”
After hurriedly sending some sort of message, they didn’t even bother to stop us and just ran away.
Well, “tried” to run away might be more accurate.
There was a saying.
If you see the beast, it’s already too late.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
[James Calla has cast Piercing Light.]
[Versyl Gowland has cast the rank 4 attack magic...]
The ranged attackers on my shoulders used the height advantage to aim down at the soldiers who were trying to run away.
Let’s name it Barbarian Bunker Mode.
We even had Rotmiller as one of the ranged attackers on the bunker.
Oh, he managed a headshot with an arrow at this range?
It seemed he wasn’t just reliant on his skills.
“Looks like you got more skilled?” I commented.
“The bow was the easiest to learn within the city limits.”
True, since training the sword required someone else to be there.
“But... is it right for me to be here?”
Rotmiller still seemed to be in disbelief that he was a part of Barbarian Bunker Mode. Or was he perhaps concerned?
“I’ll try my absolute best, but I could just be getting in your way.”
“It’s fine,” I said. “I’ve decided already.”
I was the one who put Rotmiller in this position.

It couldn’t be helped. He said he would hold up his own weight and begged me to let him follow me, so I couldn’t refuse him. In the end, I couldn’t just let him run around by himself, so I made him a part of Bunker Mode.
On the one hand, being at the forefront could be more dangerous to him. But on the other, he’ll be within my reach.
Even if something unexpected happened, I would be able to deal with it.
Also, Rotmiller wasn’t just decoration. He was genuinely helpful.
“That way! My Sixth Sense says that way is dangerous!”
Although I had forgotten about it momentarily, Rotmiller’s Sixth Sense stat was pretty high after eating the mimic essence.
Thanks to my first scout, Rotmiller, helping out with his navigation ability, I didn’t need to think too hard about deciding my route.
“Then we’ll need to go that way.”
That made him pause. “Hmm? What do you mean? I just told you that way is dangerous.”
Uh... “That’s why I said we should go that way. We’re here to fight.”
Danger was where the enemy would be.

chapters.title: Chapter 747: Scout (4)
paragraphs: Parav looked out at the burning city from the window of the second floor.

The flames surged in a crackling maelstrom, looking like they would burn everything to the ground. However, the fiery storm was stopped by what looked like a transparent glass wall and could not make contact with the building.
Almost like they were stopped by divine protection.

Of course, that level of uncertainty was only fitting when speaking from the perspective of a modern man. Because this was a world where fantastical and mystical beings did exist, a world in which its natives would see such a sight and think about protection magic circles, artifacts, or holy spells.
Uh, but since it is a holy spell... I guess it is divine protection?
He shook the thought away. As a former paladin who was well-versed in divine power, he knew the truth better than anyone else. Divine power was just a resource, no different than any other.
Of course, the church declared that divine power was the blessing of the goddess and that if one lost the qualifications to use it, their divine power would also be taken away.
Nonsense.
But Parav had seen otherwise countless times.
Believers who didn’t act like believers, archbishops who didn’t act like archbishops, cardinals who didn’t act like cardinals, and...
And paladins who didn’t act like paladins.
People who spoke of righteousness, mercy, and charity but whose hearts weren’t clean at all.
People just like him.
Sven Parav regularly had such thoughts.

If divine power wasn’t allowed to those unqualified for it, his would have been taken a long time ago. He was living proof to the contrary. In the first place, he was an evil spirit who unrightfully took the body of an innocent person, and on top of that, he never even lived a life befitting a paladin’s.
I’m not even a paladin anymore.
However, even after leaving the church, he didn’t lose this power that others called divine.
He was proof that divine power was not, in fact, granted only to those who were deemed worthy, yet ironically, he was also proof that the divine did exist.
“You received an oracle...?”

Surprisingly enough, he did experience hearing the voice of the goddess once before. It was in his dream, and the goddess had shown him a scene of an ominous future, which he was then able to avoid. However, that only gave him more questions.
Just what does she want from me...?
What do these gods want?
They truly did exist and seemed to possess supreme authority as the holy texts said, so then why was this world in such disrepair?
The thought continued to needle him as he looked out at the burning city from the windowsill.
Sometime later, however, although he couldn’t pinpoint why, he could tell the flames were burning in a different way than before. He concentrated as he looked at the burning city through the window.
“Damn it.”
The fires were being put out. And he would be hard-pressed to argue that was a good omen.

With the way things stood, the evacuees here were not afraid of the fire but of the people that the fire was protecting them from. Not to mention, the fire wasn’t going out naturally but was being put out intentionally by someone. It only heightened his unease.
Ba-dump!
It felt as if something had taken a leaping step toward him. Parav forced himself to ignore that feeling and quickly went to do what was necessary.
“Everyone, please come to the back.”
He first gathered the evacuees in one place.
“Ms. Marrone!”
He then requested Marrone to activate the magic circle she had prepared before going back up to the second floor to be on the lookout.
The flames were dying down quickly enough for him to see it with his eyes.
As the flames died down, he could see an army walking through it. A unit of soldiers wearing full suits of armor was marching in rhythm while putting out the flames.
Parav desperately hoped that they would be soldiers from the palace, but that hope never came to fruition. Easily more than a hundred soldiers were quickly marching toward his position.
He flattened himself to the wall so that he wouldn’t be seen from the outside and observed as carefully as he could. Finally, the soldiers arrived in front of the building.
Parav sank down to lean back against the wall below the window and focused only on the sounds.
Please, please, please, please, please... Please, just walk past.
Despite his desperate hope, there was no way it would come true.

And why should it? If he were a Noarkan soldier, he would have found it odd how that this one building wasn’t burning when the entire city was up in flames. He would have at least gone inside to see what was up.
Just like they did.
There was a rattle as someone tried to use the door on the first floor.
“Commander, it seems to be locked,” came the gravelly voice of a man.
That was the last sound he heard.
Parav crawled along the ground, peeking over the staircase. There, he saw the evacuees gathered in the worship hall and covering their mouths so that not a single sound escaped outside.
Suddenly, a thunderous boom sounded from the door.
Very quietly, one of the evacuees yelped.
However quiet they were, it seemed the soldiers outside were paying close attention to the noises on the other side of the door, just as the people inside were.
“Oh, looks like someone is inside?”
“Don’t let your guard down. It could be one of Yandel’s allies.”
Parav’s breath hitched.
Yandel’s allies... Are these people here because of the two of us? If so, then—
“Break down the door!”
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The Noarkans began to hammer much more energetically on the door. Fear began to cloud the eyes of the evacuees.
“Commander! It’s not breaking!”
“I don’t think it’s because of the material... There’s probably something magical about it.”
“Well... The temple hasn’t burned down even though everything around here has.”
“The second floor! Use the windows on the second floor to enter!”
Okay, so they were hell-bent on entering the building. There was no point in keeping their voices lowered and staying quiet.
“What do we do?”
“Ms. Marrone, I’ll leave the first floor to you. I’ll take the second!”
Parav stood back from his crouch...
“Oh! There’s someone here—!”
...and stabbed his sword straight through the face of the man who was looking through the window.
“Sven Parav! Sven Parav is on the second floor!”
“Get him!”
As he revealed his presence to the others, the Noarkans were filled with greed.
“His head is mine!”

If this were an ordinary battle in the Middle Ages, they would have needed to use ladders to get up to the second floor, but this was Rafdonia, where mystical powers existed. The soldier in full armor didn’t need ladders to get to the second-floor window.
Appearing like ninjas, the Noarkans shattered the windows and entered through the second floor. They looked at Parav and swung their weapons with killing intent.
“Die!”
A battle of one against dozens of people suddenly erupted on the second floor.
There was no strategy to deal with them.

He swung his white long sword to slash at his enemies and sometimes stab them. Whenever an attack was made against him, he would either block it with the shield on his other hand or move so that his vitals were not hit if he deemed it impossible to dodge.
He quickly used holy spells to heal his injuries. However, he couldn’t gain any terrain advantage while fighting against them.
Why did the stairs have to be in the middle?
Parav fought while standing right at the stairs that led down to the first floor. However, as the number of enemies continued to increase, he couldn’t hold on for long.
He was not Bjorn Yandel.
A bludgeon smacked him over the head with an ability, and the world began to spin around him.
He was in the middle of healing himself with a holy spell when he took a step back and lost his balance.
After taking one step down the stairs, the battle became more difficult. There was too much of a difference, fighting on stable and unstable ground.
Stab!
The thrown dagger stabbed him between the collarbone and ripped into his muscle.
Step.
He took one more step back.
Boom!
Was it a magic spell this time?
He raised his shield to avoid taking a direct hit, but the impact made him take another step back.
Walking forward was far too difficult, but taking a step back was far too easy.
Yeah, how can I block so many of them by myself?
His will was broken, and as if to prove that, he simply took another step back.

By the time he realized it, he was already halfway down the stairs, and he could see the evacuees just by turning his head to the side. They had shut their eyes and were praying that he could defeat the intruders.
However, reality was different from fiction.
Rather than awakening new powers after seeing their desperation, he powerlessly took another step back. This time, it wasn’t because he was hurt by an attack, but to dodge an attack.
Another step.
As he continued to get pushed back by the flood of enemies, Marrone, who was in charge of the first floor, came to his support.
[Lilith Marrone has cast the rank five defense magic Iron Wall.]
A huge wall was created between Parav and his enemies, and the stairs were blocked for the time being. Thanks to that, he was given some time to collect his breath.
Boom!
“It won’t last long!”
Even without her telling him that, he could tell from the explosions that the wall wouldn’t hold on for long.
“There are more than we expected! What do we do?”
Parav didn’t answer her.
What should we do? He didn’t know either.
Just what did they need to do to survive this situation?
Ba-dump!
His heart continued to beat loudly, screaming at him that there was no way out.
However, even if the sky was to fall, there was bound to be a silver lining.
After quickly looking around, Parav noticed the goddess statue again.
What is it?

Parav couldn’t take his eyes away from the statue. For some reason, he started to have a feeling. It was hard to describe it in any concrete terms, but... it felt like the goddess statue had some way for them to survive.
Run.
While the magically created wall was being maintained, Parav quickly ran toward the statue.
Huh?

After looking around all over and near the goddess statue, he saw what looked to be a small indent in a not-so-visible place. He pressed it deep, and when he touched the goddess statue, it smoothly moved back.
Is this...a secret pathway?
Of course, there was no guarantee that it was any sort of pathway. However, it was the only way for them to survive.
He turned to inform the evacuees.
Ba-dump!
Suddenly, his heart lurched hard again, strangling the words before they could leave his lips.
That damnable intuition was whispering to him.
Don’t tell them.
To not tell the others.
If you want to live.
Because that would be the only way for him to live.
There was no proof, no logic to back it up.
He couldn’t hold back anymore.
Fuck! Then what the hell do you want me to do?
It was playing with him. Was it fun for his own intuition to play with his heart like this? Rather than feeling relieved that there was a way, the emotions he was sick of sprouted first.
Then, something touched his right hand and it dangled limp beside him. Wondering what it was, he looked down and saw a small kid looking up at him. The kid looked as if he would cry at any moment.
“Mister Paladin... Are you hurt?”
Parav didn’t answer him. He didn’t ask himself either.
He just pushed open the goddess statue to reveal the pathway.
After revealing it fully so that everyone could see the opening underneath it, he shouted, “Everyone, go down here!”
Even as he shouted, he thought to himself, Ah, I’ve done it now...
No matter how he thought about it, he didn’t think he would become a great person. If he was going to do something right, he hoped he could have done it in a much cooler way.
Well, I guess this suits me better...?

The evacuees all went down the steps below the statue. No one thanked him or offered him anything close to gratitude, aside from the child who asked him if he was hurt or not. It was as if he was expected to have done it for their sakes all along.
He felt no sense of disappointment or betrayal at that.
Yeah... Everyone’s the same. Putting themselves first in everything.
Of course, not “everyone” was like that. If they were, then why hadn’t he too put himself first?
Why did he act for these people whom he had only met today? It wasn’t as if he was a truly noble paladin.
“Mr. Parav...?”
Why did he do that?
It’s not as if anyone will repay me for this.
“Why are you just standing there? Come on! The wall will collapse soon!”
Parav looked at the statue of the goddess.

The goddess of the stars, the one who was said to rule over adventure and relationships, and the one who always showed the path to one’s destiny. However, as always, that goddess didn’t tell him anything.
Unlike his intuition, which told him the path forward without his consent.
Ba-dump!
Now that he thought about it, what was this intuition in the first place?

He had never once questioned it before, assuming that he was usually pretty lucky and that his gut feeling was right most of the time. And yet it honestly didn’t even make sense. It shouldn’t be at this level.
Ba-dump!
Although he didn’t know why or how, his intuition was a blessing. Thanks to this intuition of his, he was able to avoid many dangers.
However, for some reason, a sudden thought ensnared him in the jaws of doubt.
Ba-dump!
Was this intuition always right?
Ba-dump!
Had he lost anything because he followed this intuition?
Ba-dump!
If he didn’t have this intuition...
Ba-dump!
If he didn’t have this intuition would he not have become the man who would curl up and shake in fear inside the wardrobe? Would he have become a much more noble person?
Ba-dump!
Maybe this ability was a shackle. A shackle that would stop him from going down the right path.
Boom!
At that moment, the wall blocking the stairs was broken, and Marrone shouted from the path below the statue.
“Mr. Parav...!”
At the same time, his intuition told him this.
Ba-dump!
That it wasn’t too late.
He should go down right this instant.
Ba-dump!
He should abandon those people and save himself.
It was a powerful feeling, more assured than he’d ever felt.
However, that was why he was able to make his decision more confidently than ever before.
“I’m sorry.”
Parav shoved Marrone down into the path and pushed the goddess statue back to its original shape.
[Go!]
Heart thumping had turned into a feeling, and that feeling had taken shape for itself and become a sound. His intuition turned into auditory hallucinations and began to speak to him.
[Follow them quickly! And survive by yourself!]
That was the reason that he didn’t follow Marrone down there. If he did go down, he knew he would fall for that temptation again.
[Quickly go down—!]
He slammed his chest, silencing his own beating heart, and spoke.
“Shut up.”
Ba-dump...
“I will decide where I go.”
He raised his sword and shield, then ran toward the enemies flooding down the stairs.
Ba-dump!
His heart beat.
Ba-dump!
More exhilarated than ever before.
[Tsk.]
[The Ancient Evil God licks his lips in disappointment.]

chapters.title: Chapter 748: Scout (5)
paragraphs: Rotmiller’s navigation ability was excellent.
Sixth Sense usually wasn’t as sensitive to fortune as it was to misfortune, and when I ran in the direction that Rotmiller told me would be dangerous, enemies appeared soon enough.
Around seventy of them...
Their numbers were overwhelmingly smaller than ours.
“Red Ax Jack! He’s a heinous criminal who’s said to have joined Orcules ten years ago, so you need to be—”
And there was no one I needed to be especially cautious of.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
Boom!
Considering how Rotmiller tried to tell me something, the guy was probably some infamous criminal or whatever. Either way, his head exploded with one arrow from Erwen.
“Did I do good?” she asked.
“Yeah, well done.”
“H-how did you defeat him so easily...?” Rotmiller mumbled in disbelief.

Well, his reaction was understandable. The battle that forced Rotmiller into retirement was that fight with the Dragon Slayer. We fought with our lives on the line and barely survived after making sacrifices.
That was years ago, though.
There was no point in being scared of Orcules as an organization at this point, and that went doubly so considering how the Corpse Collector and Dragon Slayer had been high-ranking members.
This Red Ax guy was someone I’d never even heard of before. He didn’t need to be taken into consideration.
“I’ve only heard through stories... You really have become stronger.”
Well, I’d been fighting to survive every moment of my life by that point, all while shouting out the name of the ancestral god.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
As I charged in like a tank, the enemy forces couldn’t even muster a proper response now that they had lost their commander.
“Jack! Mr. Jack is dead!”
“Run away!”

I barreled forward and crushed the heads of anyone in my way while the enemies tried to run away like headless chickens. Even if we chased them down, it would be pretty difficult to capture and kill everyone.
“Hey.”
Thus, I decided to just capture a few of the ones running away that seemed to hold some sort of position and interrogated them instead.
“What were you guys doing here? Especially with such a small group?”
“Th-that’s...”
“So you’re not going to talk!”
Crunch!
To make an example, I crushed one guy’s head while looking at the one next to him, and the information I wanted began to flow out before I could even ask.
“W-we’re a patrol unit!”
“A patrol unit?”
“Yes! We move around the battlefield in small groups to gather information and report them to our higher-ups. That was our mission!”
In other words, they were human radars. They were spread out across the warzone to see if an enemy or a new variable appeared and then reported their findings to headquarters.
“Oh, then you should know what’s going on over on the battlefield right now, right?”
“Yes! Of course!”
The guy answering all my questions was as knowledgeable as he was confident, and he helped me understand what was going on with the war.
The palatial army in District Five had entered District Seven, and the Noarkan main force of District Seven was having a direct confrontation against them.
Of course, the information itself was nothing to be surprised by. I was the one who requested military support that morning, after all. The most important piece of intel was the next one.
“The captain is still in District Seven?”
“Yes! I don’t know what he is doing since I’m just a soldier, but I am certain he is still in District Seven!”
“Then did you hear any news about Arua Raven?”
“You mean the Golden Wizard?”
“Yeah.”
“I apologize, but I don’t know much about that...”
Tsk, so no dice.
Just where did Raven and Astarota disappear off to?
I interrogated the other ones we captured as well, but they all gave similar answers. With that, the questioning session ended. Now I just needed to quickly deal with them and go—
At that moment, my interrogee suddenly asked, “Um... If it isn’t too much for you, could you let me live?”
Wow, I was wondering what he was going to say.
Although I couldn’t help but admire his ability to negotiate, I couldn’t help but laugh.
“If you just let me go, I’ll stay down the sewers and just stay there until all this is over. Really. Please trust me.”
It had to be my first time encountering someone of his type. Although many people had asked me to spare their lives in the past, none of them asked as politely as him.
“No.”
However, some things just weren’t allowed.
Even while looking quite afraid, the man gave out an awkward laugh as I sternly drew the line. “Ahaha. I-I suppose, right? Please just give me a painless death!”
Well, since he did answer all my questions. I guess I could at least do this for...
...No, wait. Something feels off.

I lowered my hammer. Rather than instinct, it was closer to a calling of experience. My experience of being betrayed countless times in my life was telling me something. Although I wasn’t sure what, I knew something was wrong here.
“Versyl,” I called. “Use your verification magic.”
“With his level, there’s a good chance it won’t work.”
“Just try it anyway.”
Versyl cast her spell. “As I thought, it doesn’t work.”
Although the verification magic didn’t work, there was no need to be disappointed. I was expecting it to fail in the first place.
I quietly tapped my thigh with my finger. “You’re a funny guy.”
I had been observing his expression and saw the face he made when I talked about verification magic and the spell was cast.
“Wh-what do you mean? I! I haven’t lied to you at all, I swear!”
Well, according to you.
“I’ll know soon enough,” I said, pulling Misplaced Trust from my sub-space. There was only one use of it left, so it was a bit of a waste. However, the situation felt too slimy to not use it.
Yeah, I can just get another one later... Let’s not hold onto it, and use it now instead.
Decision made, I moved to activate Misplaced Trust.
“Eh heh heh...”
Suddenly, he bent at the waist, sending cracking sounds along his spine. It was as if his behavior until now was all an act.
“What are you doing?” I asked warily.
“Heh heh, Bjorn Yandel...”
“Answer me.”
He looked me dead in the eye with a venomous glare before cursing, “This place will be your grave!”
Then, he collapsed forward in a heap.
Frightened by the display, Missha rushed over and checked his pulse. “Bjorn...? He’s dead.”
Argh, why did he have to do that?
Making me feel so uneasy.
Bright light cast the stone chamber into illustrious focus. Beneath that light was a mountain made of corpses.
One, two, three, four...
Counting them was a pointless endeavor.
The corpses that easily numbered in the thousands all had one thing in common. They were all crumpled up like dried vegetables.
Just then, dozens more corpses fell from above as the ceiling opened up. Once the downpour was over, the ceiling closed once more and another moment of silence filled the chamber.
The man standing at the entrance was used to this scene.
Although he was frowning like he was in pain, he continued to stare at the scene in front of him with steely conviction.
“Ah, here you are! It has been charged once more, Marquess Tercerion.”
“Is that so...? Let us go back up.”
The marquess left the underground chamber and returned to the surface where an open area surrounded by tall barriers greeted him. Dozens of pipes connected to a huge magic weapon.
Official name, Thunder. One of the three ancient Magic Weapons within the possession of the palace.
Well, properly speaking, it was only a part of Thunder, but no matter.
“Isn’t this quite the amazing instrument? Just by grinding up a few useless humans, it produces enough firepower to blow away an entire palace.”
Silently, the marquess turned his head to look at the man standing next to him.
“It’s all thanks to you, Lord Marquess. If the palace still had their hands on this, we wouldn’t have even been able to start the war.”
Although the man was aged, his constitution was healthy and his eyes brimmed with more passion than any young man.
He was the castellan of Noark.
“It may be odd to ask this now, but why did you think to oppose the palace, Lord Marquess?”
The marquess didn’t respond.

“Let’s talk freely with each other. We are in the same boat now. You contact me out of nowhere and say you’ll exfiltrate Thunder for us, that you would stand on our side when the war began. However, the fact that you have no desire for the throne can’t help but make us worry. Make us wonder about your true intentions.”
“Hate...”
“Pardon?”
“Let us say it is hatred.”

As the marquess gave that short reply, the castellan looked embarrassed for a moment before forcing a smile. “Ahaha! So that man, the King of the New World, did something to rightly anger our marquess?”
The marquess gave a bitter smile as his answer, and they fell into silence.
The castellan seemed to find that silence uncomfortable as he opened his mouth again to ask a new question.

“But why are we only leaving this charged? You have authority over Thunder, and I believe that you have some plan in mind, so I never asked... But we would’ve already had half of Rafdonia under our control if we used it.”
The marquess let out a deep sigh at the question. “I’m waiting for the right time. A more important time for it to be used.”
“Something more important than obtaining half of Rafdonia?”
“That’s right...”
The castellan seemed to grow bored of hanging around the marquess since, after another round of small talk, he went away, saying he had to be somewhere.
Sometime later, a man with the appearance of a knight entered the building and bowed low.
The marquess kept it brief. “Did you find him?”
The man nodded in response to the calm question.
“Yes, marquess. The location of Bjorn Yandel has been discovered.”
The time had come.
There was a sign for everything.

For example, if your hair suddenly stood on end, it meant that lightning was soon to strike. And if rats, insects, and birds suddenly scattered away from an area, it meant that there was a good chance there would be an earthquake.
So then, what did this sign mean?
“What’s their status?”
“They’re still just following and observing us.”
After the guy I interrogated killed himself in a burst of maniacal laughter, another group of soldiers began to stalk us in clever and wicked pursuit.
“What about capturing them?”
“Wouldn’t it be pretty difficult? They’re far enough away where even Ms. Erwen’s arrows wouldn’t reach them.”
Of course, they hadn’t caused us any harm yet. They were just maintaining their distance while following us.
However, the problem was that it only made me feel more uneasy.
Ba-dump.
The way that bastard died after saying something so ominous, and the way the soldiers were now following us. It was as if they were premonitions for some greater disaster.
“We’ll increase our pace as much as possible.”
We then increased our movement speed, but for some reason, we didn’t meet a single other enemy.
“Rotmiller.”
“I don’t know where we should be going either. I do feel that something bad is about to happen, however...”
Even the navigation I was relying on stopped working for some reason.
The true final nail, however, was this one.
“Bjorn...? They’ve suddenly stopped following us.”
Our pursuers suddenly disappeared.
“They’re not stopping their pursuit... Rather, they’re putting more distance between us and them.”
They had been chasing us the whole time. Why did they suddenly turn around and give us space? What could it mean?
I was suddenly reminded of a saying. If you ever saw water quickly recede from the shoreline, you needed to get away from the...
Pshwoong!
At that moment, the sound of what seemed to be a jet flying by echoed out, and everyone crouched their body in shock.
Ah, except me, of course.
What is it?
As the protector in charge of everyone’s safety, I raised my head high and looked around to check our surroundings.
I doubted my eyes for a moment.
I had heard that District Four had been taken over by Noarkans, and I saw what looked to be a huge projectile flying at us from that direction.
“Thunder... it’s Thunder!”
Unlike me, who was underground when Thunder hit, my allies instantly recognized what it was.
As soon as I heard that, I couldn’t help but swear.
“You fucking...”
Using missiles was cheating.

chapters.title: Chapter 749: Scout (6)
paragraphs: I remember seeing some war-related news clips in the past. It was of a country going through a civil war, and the video it came from was about a missile attack.

The clip that was shared for the segment was very short. There were buildings that seemed to have been built well and sturdily, and the day was bright. There was laundry drying on the veranda of the building to show off the peaceful atmosphere. And then...
Just one second was enough.
A missile came in at lightning speed from afar and blew up the building.
Exactly one second was enough for the destruction. Watching that short clip left me feeling powerless.
It didn’t matter if someone was an excellent athlete, a politician with multiple bodyguards, or a soldier who had lived decades on the battlefield. There was nothing anyone could do against that.
What could they do, really, when the attack flew in that quickly to strike the building? Dodge it? Block it?
The people in that video probably didn’t realize the missile had hit even as it exploded.
Okay, they could’ve gotten a missile warning beforehand. But that wasn’t what was important at the moment.
“You fucking...”
Currently, a missile was flying toward us at unbelievable speed, as if ignoring the very laws of physics. I stood, gaping in disbelief at the sight of it.
Focus.
However, I didn’t feel as powerless as when I saw that video. This was a world filled with adventurers who easily exceeded the physical prowess of those excellent athletes.
Well, that also meant Thunder wouldn’t be as easy to deal with.
“Stick close to me!”
I gathered all the allies to me. Since there were over a thousand people here, it would be impossible for me to cover everyone, but for some reason, I got a feeling.
Fwoong!
I sighed. That missile was aimed straight at me.
There were two decisions I could make.

One was I could chain Transcendence and Giantization to make myself as big as possible. Under the effects of Union, the Wall of Aegis would also grow in relative size to my body. If I could just Guard with it, I could block the missile without a problem.
But that won’t work.
I quickly changed my plan after looking at Thunder getting closer to us in real-time.
It’s not even a nuclear bomb. So why the hell is it so big?
Even if I could use Giantization twice in a row, I wouldn’t be big enough to Guard against it.
There was only one thing I could do.
[You have cast Transcendence. The next skill used will be amplified.]
I first used Transcendence, then used its effect on the next skill.
[You have cast Iron Fortress. By Transcendent Authority, the innate ability of the skill is awakened.]

Usually, the only effect of this active skill was to amplify the effect of Evolving Shell by 1.5 times. I had probably never used Transcendence on this ability in a real fight before—well, aside from a few enemies that couldn’t even be a real contender against me just out of pure curiosity. The skill had a critical weakness in that, once activated, it was impossible to deactivate it until all my soul power was exhausted.
[Evolving Shell is temporarily changed to Transformative Shell.]
And the result was dependent on luck as well.
[Physical Resistance is above 750. Three special effects are applied to the character.]
As soon as the skill was activated, a whirlwind formed around my body.
[Blessing of Storms. All damage received is increased by 70% but receives complete immunity to the wind attribute.]

The first was a dud. There was no way that Thunder was a wind attribute attack. In fact, it just increased the damage I received by a stupid amount so it could be considered one of the worst results I could’ve gotten.
The skin above the dead skin on my knuckles rippled, becoming sharper.
[Blood of the Fighter. When dealing damage with your fists, the damage is increased by 15X.]
Now this, I had fond memories of. It was pretty fun to drop my hammer and shield and just beat up monsters with my bare fists, and the allies watching from nearby also enjoyed the experience.
Hah, this is going to kill me...
But what could the effect do in this situation?
Still, it was a thousand times better than the first negative effect.
Onto the last effect.
“Yandel?” Rotmiller balked. “There’s a h-horn on your head!”
I cursed inwardly. There was no need to confirm what the effect was anymore.
[Demon Predator. When defeating dark attribute monsters, temporarily absorb their abilities.]
Okay, the last one was a dud as well.
I wasn’t even in the labyrinth. What could I do with this in the city?

It was the very reason I didn’t use Transformative Shell all this time. Each ability it gave was pretty strong, so if I got the right one for the occasion, it could be unbelievably strong, but I couldn’t guarantee the effects I wanted.
I’m done for.
It went beyond feeling defeated. My mind blanked with panic.
The second and third effects were somewhat fine, but the first was a definite problem.
All damage received increased by 70 percent.
I had figured that even when Thunder landed, maybe I could survive it, but that hope was squandered now.
However, it was the only choice available to me. Only Transformative Shell could have saved all these people around me.
That said, it was a gamble I normally would have never taken.
Those damned palm-readers.

The Record that three of my allies would die. If I wanted to interpret that optimistically, it could also mean that no more than three of my allies would die. I wanted to believe that a twist of good luck might appear as fate would will it because when considering the power of that attack that destroyed an entire palace, there was no way that only three people would die here.
But what could I do about it now? If I couldn’t run from it, I could only face it.

After checking on Thunder flying toward us one last time, I raised my shield to the sky as if I were opening an umbrella. Under it, my allies, including Rotmiller, all huddled closely together, and a few allies who were at the back hadn’t even been able to make it to me yet.
Please.
With a final prayer, I tensed all the muscles in my body in preparation for the coming impact.
Huh?
Just then, a bright light began to shine around me—from the armor I was wearing.
At first, I wondered if another person nearby had cast a spell or used an ability on me, but it didn’t take long to realize that neither was the case.
Dragon Plate of Aegis.
The passive—the constitutively active ability that I hadn’t been able to figure out even after being bound to it.
[The Noble Guardian has judged the life of the wearer is in danger.]
I didn’t know what the activation condition was.
[For 10 seconds, all Resistance stats of the wearer are increased 10X.]
I also didn’t know what its effect was.
Fwoosh!
Huge black wings appeared on my black and spread wide to each side. It was one of the hundreds of effects that Transformative Shell could produce.
[Your Physical Resistance stat is above 1,500. A special effect is applied.] It was the one I wanted: The Hanged Man.
The effect was simple.
[Soul power consumption is increased by 25 times. You share all damage taken. Your health cannot fall below 1%.]
With this special effect, I wouldn’t die no matter how much damage I took.
[You may cast Domain Declaration.]
An active ability I could only use once was unlocked for me. Naturally, I cast it immediately.
Domain Declaration.
As I said the command word in my mind, a black wave flashed out from around me as if a rock was thrown into a pond.
Whoosh!
The area the wave washed over lost its color, and the world turned black and white.

[The authority of the Great Martyr is imbued in the area. All damage taken by any creature within sight is taken by the character instead.] I relaxed a little and clenched my hand holding up the shield.
And then, Thunder fell.
I couldn’t see in front of me.
The world was just bright and soundless.
A sterile white universe.
I didn’t exist in that world.
There was no pain, no anguish, no sorrow in that world. Since time couldn’t be felt there, time didn’t exist either.
[The Noble Guardian’s soul loses its power.]
The white universe slowly faded away, its pure white canvas stained with darkness.
I began to hear faint sounds. Someone was shouting. Although I couldn’t make out what they were saying because the sound was so faint, the emotion in the voice was clear.
I blinked my eyes—though I was unable to tell if I actually blinked or not.
I could feel something touch me. Someone was shaking me. My body felt like it was being moved somewhere.
[You have taken damage. Damage is accumulated.]
[You have taken damage. Damage is accumulated...]
It didn’t feel like pain.
It just “felt” like my heart was exploding, my lungs ripping, my bones shattering, and my muscles twisting.
Why wasn’t there any pain?
It was like getting a tooth removed at the dentist. Even though I couldn’t feel the pain of the tooth being pulled out, the absence had an odd texture.
[You have taken damage. Damage is accumulated.]
[You have taken damage. Damage is accumulated...]
Of course, my body wasn’t entirely broken.
[Your body is quickly regenerated by the effects of Recovery (highest rank).]
[Your body is quickly regenerated by the effects of Recovery (highest rank).]
[Your body is quickly regenerated by the effects of Recovery...]
Even while both the internal and external parts of my body were being destroyed, I could feel it quickly regenerating.
Broken bones were fixed together. Flesh formed over the exploded heart. The lost blood quickly regenerated.
[You have taken damage. Damage is accumulated.]
[Your body is quickly regenerated by the effects of Recovery (highest rank).]
It felt like I was jumping between a hot spring and an ice bath a thousand times a second.
[Your soul power is below 10%.]
Still, as time passed, I slowly regained consciousness.
Who I was, what I did, and what I was going through.
The things I could only grasp with intense focus were easily returning to me, and so did information about the “outside world.”
“...this way!”
I heard someone shouting, but...
Whose voice was that?
I couldn’t tell. I could hear the sound of explosions.
My body felt as if it was floating in the air and then I was rolling on the ground.
However, I only felt those things. As if someone on anesthetics, I couldn’t control my own body—
“Damn it!”
“Th-the wounds aren’t healing!”
“Potion! Use more potions! It doesn’t have to be the highest-rank ones! Any of them!”
Everyone was working hard.
Well, not really, relative to what I did to become like this.
Amelia...
How would she react when she hears about this later?
Hmm, I don’t think she’ll praise me for it... I shouldn’t tell her.
Yeah, that would be the best option. She wouldn’t take it even if I told her that I had a good chance to live and that this was the only way to save them.
“...del! Yandel! Can you hear me?”
What the, why am I moving?
I couldn’t tell how much time had passed. Only one person was standing there when I opened my eyes.
“Wh-what a relief.”
Brown Rotmiller. The scout of Team Loser, my first party, and a former ally with whom I had spent precious time.
“How are you? Can you get up? We need to get out of here, quickly!”
He seemed panicked as he spoke to me, and I slowly stood. Although I didn’t know what was going on, the situation seemed pretty dire.
On the plus side, my body had recovered somewhat and I didn’t seem to have any trouble moving around.
“Don’t worry, I won’t have any problem moving-”
[You are lacking in soul power. Transformative Shell is canceled.]
The changes that had temporarily transformed my body all disappeared.
The whirlwind. The horns on my head. The sharpened knuckles bones. The black wings on my back.
Well, I didn’t care about the external changes. There was exactly only one problem that really mattered.
[The effects of The Hanged Man have ended. The accumulated damage is dealt.]
The debt I had been avoiding was repaid all at once.
Yeah, I was dead.
Pshwoo!
I felt something flow out of each and every one of the pores on my body, and I just fell straight back down into the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 750: Scout (7)
paragraphs: He swung his longsword.
He blocked with his shield.
He rolled on the ground whenever a blade flew in to hurt him.
“Ack!”
And when a lethal blade pierced his skin, he let out a scream he couldn’t hold back.

This story wouldn’t be heard by future generations, Parav thought to himself. Because the protagonists of those stories were all heroic and strong individuals. Not weak like him. And most importantly—
“Bahaha! Hey, paladin! I think you’re at death’s door!”
“So why did you stay here by yourself?”
They were winners. They would return alive to share their version of the story.
“Right, right. Just go to sleep now!”
No one would be sharing his story.
“Ack!”
That was why he could be as unsightly as he wanted to be.
He spat the bloodied spit into the eyes of the enemy, stumbled on exhausted legs, and threw the pieces of furniture that were used for the barricade.
“Ah! Over there!”
“Huh? Ack!”
He used childish feints to stab one more enemy in the neck.
“This cowardly bastard!”
“You’re the one ganging up on me,” he huffed.
Funnily enough, the trick worked really well. Was it because it was so unexpected? Well, either way, it stopped working after the second time.
Unexpectedly, though, being alone had many advantages, including one perk he found supremely satisfying above all others.
Ba-dump!
“Hah, I really don’t want to die like this...”

Fear could grip his heart in a vice grip all it wanted. Even if he didn’t have an ounce of courage in him, he could talk openly about that fear without needing to care about what anyone else would think.
Who cared if that didn’t sound like something a hero of a story would say? He wasn’t a hero to begin with.
“Just die already!”
He was afraid of dying, more afraid than anyone else.
“But what can I do about it?” he mused. “It’ll be a shame if I die alone...”
“Is he talking to himself—?!”
“So I’ll need to take you with me.”
And even more than that, he was a schemer who hated the idea of being the only one to die.
“Ack!”
It was funny in a sense. Rather than fighting with the determination to protect others, why did he feel more energized to fight because he didn’t want to die alone?
He didn’t know, and he didn’t care.
“I’ll be your guide to the afterlife, you bastards!”
He just swung his sword.
[Sven Parav has cast Twilight Compass. In exchange for taking more damage from the back, all damage dealt will be increased.]
He didn’t care how much divine power he had left and just used all the holy spells he could.
[Sven Parav has cast Undying Flames.]
He used flames inside the temple without care either. Since the holy magic enchantment on the temple only protected from external flames, it was weak to flames from within.
Ah, well, a paladin shouldn’t be using that particular skill either.
I’m not even a paladin anymore.
But that wasn’t something that could hold him back, not anymore.
“Ack! Th-this bastard...!”
He could use techniques that were banned.
“You bit my ear!”
He suddenly had a thought.
When he first entered the dungeon, a Goblin had bit his neck like this.
“Fuck, that’s salty.”
How could they bite like it was nothing?
Ah, to survive. Just like he was.
Ptui!
As he continued this brutal fight to the death, he wondered, what was the difference between him and a Goblin?
Goblins were mostly killed by beginner adventurers who stepped foot into the labyrinth for the first time, and also the monsters who killed the most adventurers in turn. A humanoid rank 9 monster.
Goblins walked on two feet.
Goblins used tools.
Goblins fought to survive.
Goblins acted on instinct.
And...
Ah, I guess this one’s different.
When goblins were in danger, they would abandon their allies and run.
At some point, the interior of the temple had become blanketed in pale flames.
Parav was hit on the head with a club that he couldn’t block and fell to the ground. He then took another hit in his powerlessly prone state.
“You...tenacious...bastard...!”
The moment he got hit, his brain went foggy.
“I’ll...kill...properly...!”
The sounds were starting to cut out.
The end.
This was the end for him.
As the legs of his enemies surrounded him, he caught sight of the half-destroyed statue of the goddess through the flames.
He suddenly became curious.
Where...?
Where would his soul go?
Would it go to Earth or the afterlife that Rafdonia talked about? If it went back to Earth, would it go to Hell? Or would he reincarnate like what the Buddhists claimed?
What would take his faithless soul?
Ba-dump!
His dying heart lurched.
[I will give you strength.]
What the hell was this now?

It took him a moment to realize, but everything around him had stopped. It was different from time flowing slowly when in extreme focus. The burning flames no longer danced, the ash floating in the air froze, and even those nameless thugs hammering in his head stood motionless.
[I will grant you the power to destroy those who hurt you so that you can achieve whatever you want.]
He felt it instinctively. Although he couldn’t tell who was talking to him, if he took the offer, he would truly be granted that power.
But I’d become a monster.
The one talking to him was an evil entity. A good entity wouldn’t have told him to abandon his allies and become the sole survivor.
That entity didn’t refute his words either. It just asked him this in return.
[How laughable. What is a monster?]
Hmm...
[If killing another person makes you a monster, then this world is already filled with them.]
That did make sense.
[Hear me. You are too weak to be called a monster, and too evil to be called a human.]
That voice held power.
[Hear me. You, who wishes to go forth by your own power but also wishes for someone else to guide you.]
Parav couldn’t help but smirk at what he heard next.
[I will guide you.]
No matter what power that voice held, it no longer held any persuasiveness. It was very simple.
[I will tell you the true path you must walk.]
Because he recognized who this voice belonged to.
Karui.
The ancient evil god didn’t deny it.
[Grab my hand.]
Another deep rumble echoed out in his mind, and Parav answered in his heart.
Nah.
Because it was a shorter refusal than any other, it reflected his will the best.
[The only way you can survive is to become my servant.]
Hmm, sure. Realistically speaking, that probably gave him the highest chance of success.
[But why?]
The reason was very simple this time as well.
Because I just got a feeling.
The feeling that he wouldn’t die even if he rejected this offer.
Ba-dump!

A strong feeling at that bloomed in his heart. However, it wasn’t an intuition given to him by someone anymore. Just like how the intuition of ordinary people was based on the unconscious condensation of their experiences and memories, his too was the same.
If you listened carefully to what your enemies said and did the exact opposite, it would get you far enough. That was what his clan leader had told him in the past while they shared a drink.

An ancient evil god who would only bring calamity and misfortune if I followed him, or a hero of the city who is still trying to achieve mythical achievements even at this moment while caring for his allies.
It was obvious who among these two that he should listen to.
Just piss off. Get out of my life, Parav declared, and the ancient evil god remained silent. He couldn’t tell how much time passed because everything was still, but the silence didn’t last long.
Above the stopped world, as if shattering layers and layers of glass, a crack in the world appeared. A warm ray of silver light leaked in.
[The intense light of dawning Twilight shines upon you.]
The starlight covered his entire body so warmly.
Parav knew it then.
[The mark of the evil god on the character’s soul has been cleansed.]
That existence was no longer here.
As soon as he realized it, the voice of kindness that contrasted with Karui’s voice echoed out.
[May this be of aid to the one who wishes to walk the path of my knight.]
He had heard this voice once in a dream before.
The moment that voice rang in his head, his body, which had nearly been unresponsive, began to surge with energy.
[The body is quickly regenerated by the effects of Recovery (EX-rank).]
[Character has obtained a new authority. Can now use the rank zero holy spell Agent of the Stars.]
[Character’s body has temporarily been imbued with the direct authority of a god. Divine power stat is permanently increased by +500. Character has permanently obtained the Perfection bonus.]
Uh...
He wasn’t sure, but it sure did feel like he just became much stronger.
Ah, whatever. Let’s just dodge this first.
Time began to flow again.
Parav rolled to the side to dodge the blunt weapon aimed at his head.
“Wh-what!”
“How—?”
“What was that light—?!”
As the prey they thought was already dead got back up like nothing happened, the Noarkans gaped in surprise.
Parav gave them a relaxed smile.
I guess it was worth living a good life.

Paladins and priests filled in accomplishments to receive holy spells from their gods. Due to that, some people could use these spells like wizards could, while others never experienced a situation where they could even use them.
In any case, that wasn’t important.
A new holy spell.
Paladins and priests who receive holy spells naturally knew what they were.
Even the name of the authority.
Agent of the Stars.
What spell was this? He hadn’t ever heard of it before.
Since the goddess even spoke to him while giving it to him, it was probably something pretty good, though. That was why Parav could laugh even in front of all these enemies.
“Pfft...”
Most of the enemies looked at him as if he had lost his head, and a few quick-witted among them noticed that something had changed.
They’re smarter than the rest...
He smirked. “But you need to pay for your crimes.”
With that, Parav cast the holy spell. Since it was a new spell he hadn’t used before, he also memorized the command on the spot.
“May the blessing of the twilight star be with me... Agent of the Stars.”
The moment he activated the authority with determination, his body began to shine with bright silver light. That bright and holy light made the Noarkan force step back in fear.
Huh?
Nothing happened.
The bright light dimmed back down, and the enemies were still standing. He also didn’t feel like he had gotten any stronger.
What just happened?
[The activation condition has not been met. Rank zero holy spell Agent of the Stars has failed to activate.]
There was no telling. He could only be sure of one thing.
I’m done for...
Ah, the one upside it seemed was that his enemies also looked confused.
Even as he sweated out a few beads in nervousness, Parav remained focused. He then gave an awkward laugh as he raised his sword high.
“Hahaha! You evil beings, hear me... I will show you mercy and let you go just this once. So g-get out of here already!”
Even though he spoke with as much authority as he could, the looks on his enemies’ faces were 0 percent terror and 100 percent confusion.
Was it because I stuttered on that last sentence?
He regretted his mistake, but it was already too late. His enemies had already drawn their conclusions.
“I think something went wrong?”
“Hah... I got surprised for nothing. I thought it’d be something big.”
“I don’t know how he recovered, but he’s still just one guy.”
“Kill him again!”
They charged him once again.
What do I do now?
Would he be able to escape if he tried?

Coldly speaking, it seemed impossible. Using the first-floor exit would only make him face more enemies, and there were too many enemies to get through if he wanted to jump out the second-floor window.
Man...
Was he really going to die after receiving a gift from the goddess? If this was going to happen anyway, she should’ve just let him die a heroic death!
Boom!
An explosion destroyed the goddess statue, shattering it and his flood of complaints to pieces as the way to the underground pathway opened.
“Graaaah!”
Something huge lept out from it and landed right next to him with a roar.
Boom!
Uh... What was this?
It seemed to be trying to help him.
A bear beastman riding a giant bear...?
Parav lost focus for a moment in shock. The ears of the beastman riding the bear perked up.
“I heard that my wife is indebted to you? I’m here to save you.”
“Oh, don’t be shy. Even if you didn’t save my wife, an ally of Yandel is an ally of mine.”
He still couldn’t tell what the beastman meant by that, but one thing was certain.
“Here, let’s go already. I’ll open the path.”
He survived.
