After falling from the ceiling, Amelia used her legs to bind around Eltora’s neck. She then used her one useable hand to strike down her dagger surrounded with blue aura-like lighting—
Fwip!
The dagger stopped right in front of Eltora’s enlarged pupils.
“You die if you make a sound. You also die if you move. You die if you try to scheme. If you understand, slowly kneel—”
“M-Ms. Emily!”
“You can thank me later—”
“H-he’s on our side! This man is...!”
Huh? Our side?
What was he talking about?
Ah, perhaps...
“So you got brainwashed already...”
“What? Brainwash? I-It’s nothing like that—!”
“Those evil bastards.”
“No, I’m actually completely fine!”
In the end, he had to explain the entire situation to Amelia, and it took her a long while to accept it.
“So... He betrayed his father and is trying to buddy up with us?”
“Yes! That’s right!”
Auyen nodded as hard as he could.

chapters.title: Chapter 757: Hostage (2)
paragraphs: The loud snoring reminiscent of an ogre’s served as the backing track of the destroyed Alminus Bank’s underground vault.
There, Amelia let out a sigh while looking at Ainar, and it certainly wasn’t because she was disappointed in Ainar.
They used a drug on her...
Although she had been talking to Ainar from a relatively close distance and for a significant amount of time, Ainar showed no signs of waking. Her being forcibly kept asleep by drugs was the only—
“U-ugh...”

Suddenly, Ainar grumbled out a breath in her sleep. Amelia hurried over to her side, concluding that she would need to help her out if Ainar couldn’t regulate her breathing back to a steady rhythm. However, her worry was for nothing.
“Mmph...”
Ainar rubbed her stomach a few times before rolling over onto her shoulder.
Hoooooonk!
Then, she began to snore even louder than before.
Amelia stared, wondering if the female barbarian wasn’t drugged at all and was just genuinely asleep.
There’s... There’s no way...
Nope. Not even a barbarian would be so clueless about danger when it came to personal safety.
“Well... Shouldn’t we wake her up now?”
“How? Ainar Fenelin is currently asleep under the influence of a drug.”
“Ah...” Auyen nodded as if he only just realized. “Is that so?”
Amelia steadfastly chose to ignore Eltora Tercerion, the man who would be recorded as a historically unfilial child, as well when he mumbled, “Drug? Was there a report like that?”
The drug excuse would be less embarrassing for everyone. Not that it might matter, considering the sticky situation they were in.
“Um... Could I continue with my story?” Eltora asked.
Amelia collected herself, pulling her attention from Ainar back to him. “Where were we at?”

Her short question was frigid in tone, and the look in her eyes proved she was still on guard against him. It was only natural since Eltora Tercerion was trying to abandon his father and join their side.
After a long conversation, she had come to accept he wasn’t doing this because he was brainwashed to do it. However, accepting the truth of the matter was a different problem entirely.
“I was talking about how beneficial it will be for the palace and the Anabada Clan if you agree to my suggestions.”
“Ah, that’s true... But that’s not necessary.”
Amelia didn’t care about gaining anything from the situation. Or more accurately, she didn’t feel the necessity of hearing him out anymore.

Her thought process was as such: Using the marquess’s son as a spy? It was pointless to waste time putting the strategic advantage that gave them into words. No, she decided to focus on something more important.
“Why are you trying to betray your father?”
Motivation—the factor that pushed people to act and create new situations.
“As I told you before, my biggest reason is to live.”
“Have you concluded the palace will win this war?”
“Of course they will. Going against the palace is asinine in the first place.”

At a glance, it seemed like a logical decision. However, Amelia knew that everyone held greed in their hearts, and even a small fragment of greed possessed enough power to drive someone to absurd lengths.
“But if you succeed,” she hedged to sound to him, “won’t you lose this princely life you enjoy?”

It was human nature to focus on the one reason for success rather than the ninety-nine reasons for failure. However, how was the marquess’s son able to make such a decision? From what she could tell, he made it as soon as the marquess collapsed. But how was that possible?
The answer to that was very simple.

“Not at all. Even if the revolt succeeds, it would be difficult for me to protect my current lifestyle. My father...” Eltora hesitated. “No, Marquess Ageni Lawton Tercerion wants to get rid of me as soon as he can.”
“I don’t understand. Why would the marquess want such a thing for his eldest son?”
“I didn’t understand it myself until much later. Marquess Tercerion treats me like this because he knows what I am.”
“And...what you are?”
Eltora gave a bitter smile at Amelia’s question. He then gave a short answer, as short as a barbarian would give.
“I am an evil spirit.”
In a sense, this was the first confession in his life.
“Hah, that actually wasn’t too hard.”
Even as his heart beat with adrenaline and thrill, Eltora also felt an unknown sense of freedom—a feeling that only he felt at the moment.
Auyen Rockrobe, the navigator who had gained the achievement of harming the marquess, was in shock at the information that the marquess’s son was an evil spirit.
“Oh?”
And Amelia Rainwales, a professional in hiding her emotions and an assassin of Noarkan origin, was openly interested in his revelation.
It started to make some sense. If what he said was true, then Eltora Tercerion’s betrayal wasn’t unexpected or odd. Rather, the cause and effect were absolutely clear and natural. However...
“At this point, I’ve practically placed my life in your hands. So could you trust me now?”
Even so, Amelia didn’t nod. It was simply part of her suspicious nature.
A confession was only a confession. There wasn’t any proof. What this too was also a lie?
Although she didn’t have Misplaced Trust, she had her own ways of discerning the truth, fortunately.
“A metal object that flies through the sky.”
“An airplane.”
“A dwarf fed a princess a poisoned apple, and she died. What’s the princess’s name?”
“Are you...talking about Snow White?”
“Squarepants.”
“Sponge... No, how do you know that?”
“I trust you. You are an evil spirit.”

Using the knowledge of the otherworld she obtained from Hansu Lee, she came to a final decision: Eltora Tercerion was definitely an evil spirit. Although he stumbled on knowledge of Snow White and couldn’t answer her, that was within the acceptable range of errors. Even people born in the same world would have differences in levels of knowledge. Eltora probably just didn’t have access to such resources.
Having been reminded of her time in Noark where she couldn’t receive education even when she wanted to, Amelia felt a sense of kinship with Eltora, but she didn’t mention it out loud.
“What?” he asked warily. “What’s with that look?”
“It’s nothing.”
“Whatever. Then do you trust me now?”
“Sure, I have resolved all doubts I had about you.”
Eltora was elated at that. After putting forth any and all proof he could muster, he had succeeded in proving his trustworthiness to this nonbeliever. “Then are you now going to accept me?”
His question born out of lingering traces of unease, however, was met with shocking and bleak news.
“That is...unfortunately, not my place to say.”
“Not your place? What do you mean?”
“It’s as it sounds. The captain of the Anabada Clan is Yandel, and the vice-captain is a different woman.”

“What are you—?!” Eltora felt more cheated now than he did when he was discarded without reason by the marquess. Knowing that his life hung in the balance, he tried to argue his case as best as he could. “Don’t try to lie to me! I know quite a lot about your organization as well!”
“No, even if you say that...”
“You are Yandel’s woman!”
Amelia blinked, taken aback. “Huh?”

“On top of that, from what I heard, among the many women that Yandel has, you are the one that he trusts and relies on the most! So he always asks you for advice and consultation on whatever he does! But you’re saying it’s not your place?”
“Uh... No, I wouldn’t go that far...”
“You’re practically one with Yandel!”
“So if you’re going to refuse to take me in, at least be honest about it! Everyone in the world already knows that if Baron Yandel starts taking in wives, you will be his first choice!”
“H-his first wife?”

“Then who else would it be? The Blood Spirit who’s lost herself to bloodlust with the war? Karlstein who has nothing to show for herself except that she was on his original team? Or Raven, who has already sided with the palace? Or that muscle-brained Divine Spear?”
“I’ve n-never even entertained the thought of—”
“Don’t even try to say you don’t have the power! I know that Yandel treasures you and relies on you the most!”

Perhaps because of the stress that was brought upon by this situation in which he was betraying his own father, Eltora laid out the entirety of how wronged he felt, swept up in his emotions for the first time in a long while.
“Welcome to the group.”
And somehow, that got him exactly what he wanted.
Ainair Feneliln had a thought while quietly keeping her eyes closed.
Can I wake up now...?
In truth, she hadn’t just woken up from her deep sleep. She regained consciousness a long time ago, but she acted like she was asleep. It was honestly for a very simple reason.
“Ah, that’s true... But that’s not necessary.”
When she woke up, she heard Amelia’s voice, and that meant the allies she was trusting to rescue her had come to her rescue.
Naturally, Ainar was very glad. However...
“Ainar Fenelin is currently asleep under the influence of a drug.”
After being educated on this once before, Ainar interpreted those words as orders that meant don’t wake up.

Thus, she kept her eyes firmly shut, and it didn’t seem like she needed to be in a hurry either. While she didn’t have any concrete proof of this, she didn’t doubt her decision. For barbarians, knowing when to lie down and sleep was as easy as knowing when cooked meat was ready to eat.
In any case, that was that.
“Where were we at?”
“I was talking about how beneficial it will be for the palace and the Anabada Clan if you agree to my suggestions.”
Amelia was having a pretty serious conversation with some mysterious man. She came to understand while listening that the man was the son of the marquess.
Ugh! My head!
With a sudden headache assaulting her, Ainar decided to act like she was sleeping for a while longer, and that led to the current situation: the silence that came to be after the conversation ended.
I think I should get up now...
After deciding it was the right time to act, Ainar yawned as naturally as she could and sat up.
“Ah, don’t worry! I’m on the same side as you now—”
The man met her eyes and tried to explain the situation as quickly as possible before any misunderstandings occurred.
Smash!
She punched him in the face anyway.
“Stop... He’s on our side.”
Emily naturally stopped her, and only then did Ainar calm down.
“Ah, really? Sorry! I didn’t know!”
It wasn’t like she really didn’t know.
She knew well enough that he was on her side after listening to their conversation. Still, she couldn’t quite figure out why she punched him even then.

After waking up from her sleep, Ainar had thought long and hard for the first time in forever, and as someone who had been told she was a bright person ever since she was young, she quickly found an answer.
“On top of that, from what I heard, among the many women that Yandel has, you are the one that he trusts and relies on the most!”
The fact that false information was shared? She didn’t mind. Humans were a wicked race who couldn’t live without lying.
“Everyone in the world already knows that if Baron Yandel starts taking in wives, you will be his first choice!”
In a similar vein, it was understandable why he would think the legal wife of the great warrior would be a human.
Because he was a human too. He just didn’t know any better.
“Or that muscle-brained Divine Spear?”
That should have been words of praise for her, but for some reason, she felt wounded by them.
Still, that wasn’t the reason either.
Just...
Just because.
“Behel-LAAAAA!”
“So suddenly?”
“I just felt like it!”
That was the answer Ainar came to.

chapters.title: Chapter 758: Hostage (3)
paragraphs: Rafdonia was a heartless city, even more so if the individual was an evil spirit.

Waking up in the body of another person without any knowledge of what was going on, the evil spirits needed to struggle as hard as they could to survive, and they could still end up dead just due to sheer, unfortunate luck.
However, it was different for Eltora.
He wasn’t especially bright, nor did he possess some outstanding talent. No, he had something even more special than anyone else: his surname was Tercerion.

Honestly, nothing more needed to be said. The surname of Tercerion meant that he was the son of the second most powerful man in the nation, and that was enough to turn Eltora’s story from one of survival to just living in another world.
It wasn’t as if he had no struggles of his own, but unlike the other evil spirits who needed to live like cockroaches at the bottom of the ladder, he enjoyed a comfortable life.
Until...
That damn marquess bastard.
The marquess suddenly went nuts, joined forces with Noark, and raised his weapons against the palace. After that point, Eltora’s starting point also reverted to the same as the other evil spirits.

Like the others, he became worried for his survival, and that was why even when he was told to lead the marquess’s forces and work with the Noarkans after being swept up in the war, he followed along obediently.

Who could blame him? Although Earth had mostly done away with guilt by association, this was a different world with a more medieval setting. There was no need to talk about what would happen to the son of the traitor who orchestrated the war. To put it simply, he had no choice but to side with the marquess.
However, thinking back on it, that was the biggest mistake of his life.
I never expected there to be a secret like that...

After he joined the Noarkans, he began secretly looking deeper into what was going on, spurred on by the uneasiness in his heart, and the result of his investigation was that he ended up uncovering a shocking secret hidden within the marquess’s mansion. A huge secret that could answer all the questions and suspicions he had held until that point. And that secret was—
Smash!
Eltora’s train of thought was interrupted by Ainar smacking him on his back.
“Ugh! What is the meaning of this?!” he barked in outrage.
“Huh? I just felt like it?”
He nearly flew into a rage, wondering how things had come to such a state when he saw that barbarian’s calm expression. However, he chose to collect himself instead.
The people before him—they were his sole lifeline.
If I can just prove to Baron Yandel that I betrayed the marquess and contributed greatly to his defeat...then I can survive.

It wasn’t just a distant hope—he was certain it could be. After all, that man was the most famous hero in the city. One word of the baron’s confidence in him and the traitor’s son could be transformed into the ally of the great hero who had stabbed his own father in the back for justice.
And so, Eltora held his tongue despite the pain racking his back. Even if he asked for a reason, she would just say she wanted to smack him.
“Knock it off... If you keep smirking like that, I’ll have no choice but to think you’ve got a few screws loose up there.”
This damn barbarian woman! Just why did Yandel keep a violent and foolish woman as his ally?
Oh, right. He’s a barbarian too.
As quickly as the thought came, it left when he quickly accepted the facts and just stopped resisting—mostly, ignoring the little glare he sent her way.
“Ainar, stop.”
Thankfully, Yandel’s “legal wife candidate” seemed to have common sense and saved him from further humiliation.
“If you act like that again, I have no choice but to do the same to you,” she admonished.
“F-fine! I won’t hit him!”
“Sorry,” the woman said, turning to Eltora. “She’s a bit childish at times.”
“Haha... It’s all right. We have much more important things to think about. I won’t pay attention to small things like that. So in that vein... What will we do from now on?”
“First, we’ll need to relay this news to Yandel. If that guy just charges in here, it’s bound to cause problems.”

“You don’t need to worry about that. The prime minister planned to spread the information about the Divine Spear’s location after all the traps were set in this place. Yandel would never have thought to come to this place before then.”
“Never, you say... But it’s best to prepare just in case.”
“Haha... As expected of the wife, you are quite wise. Now I can understand why he relies on you, madam.”
The sight of Amelia lost for words when he called her madam had Eltora smiling inside. A question he had was now answered.
She is weak to such words!
He needed to continue showering such praise onto her without making them too obvious so that she could vouch for him to Yandel later down the—
“Behel-LAAAAA!”
At that moment, a sudden battle cry echoed out—not from within the vault, but outside of it. It was loud enough to be heard clearly even through the heavy door.

“Bjoooorn! That shout was from Bjorn...!” The female barbarian warrior understood who had let out that battle cry, and she began to shout in return while looking quite moved. It was as if she became the rescue signal.
Eltora met eyes with Amelia as she snidely asked, “Didn’t you say he would never come here?”
He had no response to her short question.
How was this possible? After the mastermind that was the marquess collapsed, not even the first steps of the plan to form a trap using the Divine Spear as bait had been taken.
“Behel-LAAAAAAA!”
How the hell did he know to come here?

The palatial soldiers who had remained stationed in the imperial capital even while Ravigion and Kommelby were being destroyed finally began to move. It wasn’t for any grand reason such as not being able to endure the injustice happening in the rest of the city or a strategic moment to strike had come either.
It was because I asked them to move.
Well, to be precise, they were moved by the grand authority of someone holding the position of the King’s Knight, but I was the one who told him to do so.
“If it’s just to draw their attention.”

The amount of power Astarota held was astounding. Even without making an appointment, when he went over to the commander and shared a few words with him, he was able to change the orders of the standing army of Karnon. The same ones who had stubbornly not moved even when District 4 was taken over by the Noarkans while saying things such as “Our mission is to protect the imperial capital!”

Even though their new mission wasn’t as serious as full-scale counter-invasion but more like acting as a full-scale counter-invasion, I grew curious. If the King’s Knight had that much power, how absolute of an authority was the king?
I became depressed the more I thought about it, so I decided to just focus on the present.

While the palatial soldiers were drawing their attention, I quietly snuck into District 4 and arrived in front of the main gate of the Alminus Bank, though it was more just that I was standing around and thinking about what to do.
Main door, back door, fence jumping.
Which route did I need to take to safely rescue Ainar?
It didn’t take long for me to decide.
Main door.
There were two reasons for that. One, I would be found out no matter which route I took due to this big body of mine. And two, the main door was the closest to the underground vault.
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
I used my barbarian authority on the two guards yawning at the main gate.
[You have cast Swing. The destructive power of blunt weapons will greatly increase relative to strength.]
The barbarian authority specialized in crushing, destroying, and cleaving things.
“I-it’s Baron Yandel!”
“Stop him!”
“Why are you running after telling us to stop him?!”
“Run away!”
As my authority descended upon the Alminus Bank, the Noarkans standing guard couldn’t even think of opposing it and just ran away like headless chickens.
It wasn’t odd to see at all. Low-level mobs were expected to move in such patterns. Now, the real enemies should appear to stop me since I made such a big commotion.
What the...? Why is no one else coming out?

After breaking through the main door and entering the building, I quickly headed underground—though “quickly” was an exaggeration given how much time I spent running. However, not a single real enemy appeared before me.
Had the traps really not been set up yet?
I had just run as quickly as I could over here while aiming for exactly that, but still...
Why is this so easy?
I couldn’t believe it. It only made me think of the past, and my experience was telling me I was in grave danger. The moment the taut string went loose was when everything would start to fall apart.
Wait...
I assumed the worst.
Has the trap already been completed...?

My enemy had predicted everything. They made it seem like they were underprepared so that I would come alone, and even stationed small fries so I would lower my guard. I was even prepared for the absolute worst-case scenario where Ainar was already dead and I was only on the way to pick up a corpse, but that never happened in the end.
“Behel—!”
“Behel-LAAAAA!”
After heading to the underground while breaking everything in my path, I heard Ainar’s battle cry. That was the proof of her survival and my compass.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
When I shouted, Ainar shouted back from below. It seemed she was trying to tell me her location after hearing my shouts.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
In a sense, I was moving like a bat using echolocation. Okay, well, not really. Anyway, as we continued to get closer, our shouts continued in tandem.
“Bjooooorn!”

Thanks to that, I was able to move down the most efficient path in this unfamiliar underground vault to find Ainar. For some reason, she wasn’t trapped in the vault but was instead outside alive and well.
Amelia and Auyen...?
And there were more faces I was glad to see as well—and even one that incited the opposite reaction too.
“Eltora Tercerion?”
“Haha, it has been a while, Baron Yandel...”
What was this guy doing here?
It didn’t take long for me to understand the situation.
“So since you’ll die even if you stick with the marquess, you decided to stick to me? Like a bat.”
“W-well, more than that—”
“I won’t accept you if you try to give me some grand reason.”
“You are right.”
Yeah, he should’ve just done this from the start.
In any case, it was great that the marquess’s son came under my control. However, rather than think about how to use him...
“Emily, it’s good to see you safe.”
“You too.”
I shared a brief greeting with Amelia, whom I was finally able to see again, and then looked at Auyen. It was a really odd feeling.
“Well done. You’ve done something not even I or the palace was able to do.”
“P-please don’t say that! I-I really just got lucky! A-and you were the one who gave me that essence in the first place!”

“I’m not talking about your essence or your luck. It’s the fact that you were able to make that decision at all... Even if you put a hundred ordinary people in your position, they wouldn’t have been able to make the same choice as you at that moment.”
I was being genuine, but it seemed Amelia thought my words were too overbearing for Auyen, as she interjected herself back into our conversation.
“Stop. Auyen Rockrobe is a genuine member of the Anabada Clan. Isn’t it natural that he is different from ordinary people?”
“Oh...” I thought she was going to tell me to stop embarrassing him, but she wanted to praise him as well.
I couldn’t tell if it was from embarrassment or joy, but Auyen lowered his head and fidgeted by himself for quite a while.
Alright, time to leave my praises there.

“Bjooorn! It’s good to see you well! Praise me as well! If it wasn’t for me, Rotmiller wouldn’t have been able to take you all the way there! Oh, by the way! What happened to Rotmiller? Did you not bring him along this time?”
She didn’t know.

chapters.title: Chapter 759: Hostage (4)
paragraphs: Rotmiller was dead.

I was told that he dragged a cart toward the imperial capital to save me and jumped off the cart to protect the cart. Astarota even ever-so-kindly notified me that the Noarkans had taken Rotmiller’s head with them as well. However...
She doesn’t know yet.
I could immediately tell that Ainar, Amelia, and Auyen didn’t know about his fate. This Eltora guy was a different story, though.
When I froze up at the mention of Rotmiller, the others just silently looked at me.
What do I do?
For a moment, I wondered if I should mention Rotmiller’s fate or not. Ainar might very well up and go wild with shock and incite some unfortunate turn of events.
But I guess that outcome is unrelated to if she’s lost it or not.
With that thought, I came to a decision.
Yeah, let’s just tell them.
“Rotmiller is dead.”

I went straight to the point, just like a barbarian. There was no point telling them about how he jumped off the cart and his head was decapitated and taken as a trophy. The process didn’t change the result.
Rotmiller was dead. He died while leaving a short will to me.
That was the only thing I needed to remember.
Ainar flinched. “Huh?”
It seemed she expected Rotmiller to have come over to the imperial capital and that he was doing well, but unfortunately, his story didn’t have a happy ending.
“I see... He’s dead...”
However, contrary to my worries, Ainar was unexpectedly calm when she heard the news.
Well, it wasn’t all that unexpected, really. Sure, the two were close while staying in the holy land together.
But thinking about it, that’s all they were.
Ainar was quick to become close friends with other barbarians and other people. She would form strong bonds with them, and she had countless close friends other than just Rotmiller.
“May his soul be called to the place he wished to be,” Ainar said by way of a short prayer.
Death wasn’t an unfamiliar concept to her. Barbarians were a brutal race who were driven into a world of life and death as soon as they came of age.
No, not even just barbarians...
Although this was a damnable city with countless inequalities, one thing was equal among all: everyone in this city was equal in the shadow of death that constantly loomed near.
“He was a pretty good human, which is rare to see in this age... What a shame.”
That was the end of her mourning. Auyen, who hadn’t been that close with Rotmiller, didn’t have much of a reaction either. It was Amelia who couldn’t quite hold back her feelings.
“Brown Rotmiller died...? While trying to save you?” she mumbled as if she couldn’t believe it. Her eyes widened and her shoulders shook, even though she rarely reacted to most things.
The reason was simple.
“Are you...okay?”
She looked at me like I was a man on the brink of some extreme downfall, and I just shrugged as if it wasn’t affecting me. “I’m fine. Don’t worry.”
Although she shot me a disbelieving look, she didn’t ask further.

I wasn’t lying either—I really was fine. At least, I was now. There were too many things I needed to focus on, and solving each one of them one by one was my utmost priority. He wouldn’t want me to stumble while looking back at the past either.
Though my fists clenched at the thought, I decided to face Rotmiller’s death after everything was done.
Only after informing the people close to him, going through with the funeral, and contemplating how to honor his heavy will would I be able to truly feel what I lost.
I would have a few sleepless nights after that. As I always did.
“Don’t push yourself, Yandel.”
I partially ignored Amelia’s words of worry. Although I was thankful for her gesture, I needed to look forward.
I looked Eltora up and down as if I were window shopping. How could I use this son of the marquess to gain the most value out of him?
Eltora even began pitching himself to me.
“Currently, the Noarkan army is divided into three—Noark, Orcules, and the marquess’s faction. However, after my father collapsed, the command of the march was temporarily given to me.”
“So?”
“Just give me the order. Before my father awakens, I have the power to do anything you wish accomplished,” Eltora whispered to me like a devil to a downtrodden hero.
I declared my wish out loud as if I were a man possessed. “Then can I have a talk with the marquess? With my hammer?”
“Ah, that’s a bit...”
I clicked my tongue. I knew the answer would be no. Still, with how confident he was, I had hoped for the best, but it was to be expected that I wouldn’t be able to kill the marquess that easily.
When I glared a little at Eltora for giving me that fleeting hope, he became flustered. “S-still, there’s no guarantee that there is no way!”
Either there was a way or there was not a way. “What do you mean there’s no guarantee?”

Eltora went on to tell me the method while giving himself insurance by stating he had no idea if it would work or not. I listened to his plan without many expectations, but when he got around to telling me the whole thing...
“...I think it might work?”
As soon as I made my decision, I decided to carry out that plan.
Boom! Boom!

I confidently barreled up the stairs that led to the surface, raced through the lobby, and headed for the main gate—only to find it completely destroyed. As I stood in front of it, bright sunlight shined down on me, and I could see the street packed to the brim with Noarkan soldiers.
Reminds me of the old days for some reason.
Back in the day, I’d only had the essences of the Corpse Golem and the Vampire.
Boom!

I announced my presence and felt the piercing gazes of the soldiers land on me. As an experienced worker, I didn’t need to say anything fancy. I lifted Eltora into the air, wondering if this was the feeling that Moses had when he split the Red Sea.
“Young Lord Tercerion has been taken as a hostage!”
I succeeded in relaying my intentions without saying a single word.
Boom! Boom!
I continued my way down the street while maintaining Giantization with Amelia and Auyen riding on my shoulders.
“Oh!”
Ainar followed after me like a mastiff. I could technically carry Ainar as well, but Ainar said she didn’t want to be carried.
“Do I have to? Walking is much more comfortable!”
Yeah, as expected of a fellow barbarian.
Anyway.
Boom! Boom!
As I strode forward, Ainar followed me, and behind her were hundreds of Noarkans who looked worried and confused as to what they should be doing.
“Shouldn’t we do something?”
“And will you take responsibility if that man’s one and only son dies?”
“Then are we going to just keep following them like this?”
“A message has been sent to the higher-ups, so let’s wait for an order.”
A few of them showed signs of wanting to take action, but their words were drowned out by those waiting for orders from their superiors.
“I can see a few members of Orcules as well. I’ll tell you their appearance, characteristics, and the essences they are known to have, so memorize them.”
From what I heard from Amelia, it seemed this group of soldiers weren’t all part of the marquess’s faction, but they didn’t act rashly. Their situation wasn’t too different.
What if they acted up and the son of their alliance leader died? It would become a huge political problem.
Boom! Boom!
This odd procession continued.

At a glance, it looked like those Olympic torch relays. Although it wasn’t a torch, I was holding Eltora high into the air by his neck, and hundreds of people were following him. Also, the Olympic torch symbolized peace-yet another similarity it had with Eltora.
“Ugh... P-please, a little gentler...”
It seemed the man himself was having a hard time from the impact on his neck every time I took a step. Of course, peace always came at the sacrifice of a martyr.
Boom! Boom!
With that thought, I continued forward at a running pace. It would take hours to get to our destination if I just walked.
“H-he’s heading for the marquess!”
“Baron Yandel has taken Young Lord Tercerion and is aiming for the marquess!”
The soldiers seemed to have started to pick up on my intentions, but they didn’t try to oppose me yet.
Although I expected it somewhat, I was also a little amazed.
This really works.
The one who proposed this idea was the current symbol of peace, Eltora.

There was an organizational flaw in the Noarkan alliance in the fact that there were three command points, and the three commanders weren’t too loyal to each other. Also, it was human nature to put their safety before anyone else’s. That nature was also strengthened in the hearts of Noarkans. When all that came together, I concluded there was a good chance no one would stop me even if I just walked in, and that prediction came true.
“Baron Yandel is aiming for the marquess!”
“This fool dares! Please give us your order...!”
“The marquess is the one with the authority to do so, but he is unconscious!”
“Still, there should be a temporary commander in his stead!”
“That hostage there is the temporary commander.”
“Well, if you want to act of your own accord, I won’t stop you, but you’ll need to take responsibility for the consequences!”

Most conversations continued like this, leading to the current absurd situation. Ah, of course, the full-scale invasion by the standing army of the imperial capital probably contributed to this messy chaos and indecision.
“Huh?”

After moving along at a quick pace, I began to see my destination in the distance, only to find some people standing in our way. Usually, I would’ve just barreled through them, no matter who was trying to stop me. However, I unfortunately couldn’t do that this time—not to these particularly special folk.
Demon Eyes, Roland Banozant—the vice-captain of Orcules was personally leading this troupe, and he wasn’t alone. There were around a few dozen “true” members of Orcules standing behind him.
Demon Eyes didn’t shout anything unnecessary and just stood in my way, and I also silently slowed down to a halt. Then, I raised the symbol of peace higher so that people could see him better.
This symbol of peace had the benefit of being able to speak for himself, after all.
“Wh-what are you doing?! Get out of the way...!”
The human symbol shouted for peace as promised, but the target this time unfortunately didn’t buy it at all.
“Why should we?”
The one who answered in the stead of his vice-captain was a man who looked like his favorite pastime was reading and was someone talented in the way of speech.
“D-do you want infighting to occur? I currently hold the authority of the marquess faction! With just one word from me, you’ll need to fight all the soldiers standing behind me!”
“Well, I wonder if that’s the case...”
“Huh?”

“The Noarkan alliance has come to a decision. Although Eltora Tercerion certainly has the right to temporarily hold the authority of the marquess, he lost that authority when he was captured by the enemy as a hostage. Under the rightful laws of the alliance...”
Gulp!

“Eltora Tercerion’s authority will be stripped from him from this moment onward, and all forces under his command will be transferred to the alliance until the marquess regains consciousness,” Glasses said with an air of authority. Then, he asked Eltora, “This is a personal question, but...are you doing all this because you really got captured by them, or did you just decide to side with these people?”
No answer.
“Ah, you don’t need to answer. I’ve already got mine.”
Those words seemed to shock the symbol of peace quite a bit, but I wasn’t surprised at all. I just put down the symbol that expended its use and pulled out a different symbol of peace altogether.
In the end, peace was obtained by the strong.

chapters.title: Chapter 760: Secret Garden (1)
paragraphs: Demon Eyes, Roland Banozant.
In Orcules, where strength ruled above all, he obtained the vice-captain position by killing his predecessor in a single strike. He was one of the most powerful ability users within the organization.
His long and infamous career featured many accomplishments that were the subjects of rumor and legend, but his most recent feat stood out in my mind: defeating the Divine Spear, Ainar Fenelin.

Although it felt strange to admit it, Ainar had grown the most among my early allies aside from Erwen. Even back when she was the Wild Sword, she had been a part of the Seven Powerful. Ainar was, in no uncertain terms, powerful.
And yet, Roland Banozant defeated her without—and even taking minor injuries too. Most importantly, he successfully captured Ainar alive.
Managing to accomplish just one of those feats would be an undeniable indicator of the difference in power between them, but he accomplished both simultaneously.
There was no denying it. He was strong. Incredibly, absurdly strong.

Perhaps most would expect as much from the vice-captain of Orcules, but I found myself caught off guard. My last memory was still fresh in my mind, after all. This was the guy who nearly died in stupefaction after I smashed his head with a hammer. Granted, it was a sneak attack on my end, but still. It was hard to accept that someone like that had overpowered Ainar of all people.
“Yandel... Be careful. He uses some weird skills...” Ainar advised.
I couldn’t help but chuckle. So, I thought to myself, even she can be intimidated.
Then again, she probably didn’t know what essences Banozant had and the abilities they granted him. Of course they would have seemed very “weird” to her.
Let’s say I deal with Demon Eyes myself... Can Amelia and Ainar handle the rest on their own? And all while protecting two people?
I hummed in thought, it was going to be difficult.
Just as my doubts began to fester, Glasses—the very one who rattled the resolve of our symbol of peace—took a step closer to use and cleared his throat. Though “closer” was an exaggeration at best.
“Hear this, Baron Yandel!”
Huh? He’s singling me out this time?
“You are already surrounded. If you are counting on reinforcements from the imperial army, then I suggest you abandon that false hope. The forces of the capital are retreating as we speak.”
I stared at him, waiting for him to get to the point. “So?”
“The future is already decided, so I’ll make you an offer. Drop your weapon and surrender. I cannot disclose the details at present, but the castellan wishes to see you.”
So he was just trying to win me over. I turned away to look at Amelia, silently asking who the hell this guy was.
“He’s someone near the castellan,” she explained. “He doesn’t have a set role but is called whenever he’s needed to solve a problem.”
It was a vague description, but I understood the implication. Amelia had filled exactly that position in the past. Simply put, Glasses here played the same role that Amelia once played.
I did wonder why I’d never met the guy if he was so important.
Still, it was funny. The ones in my way were the core unit of Orcules, yet the one trying to win me over was the castellan.
“So then, how about it? We can’t wait forever, so decide right here and now.”
Glasses seemed convinced that I wouldn’t reject his offer, but his suggestion sparked only a single thought from me.
Looks like there’s no camaraderie in their group.
My answer was set from the beginning.
“I refuse.”
He was taken aback. “Huh?”
“Got a problem with your ears? I said I refuse.”
The marquess was nearly within my grasp. My mission would be over the moment I killed him.
That was the only mission I received from the king, after all. Once I killed the marquess, my allies and I could escape the ire of the palace.
Yet he expected me to surrender?
Does he have something wrong with his head?

Even if the marquess weren’t my goal, my answer wouldn’t have changed. The only reason a barbarian would bend a knee was to spring back up into a leap. And my instincts were telling me that this offer of his would never let me rise again.
Demon Eyes clicked his tongue as he glared at Glasses, who looked confused at my answer. “I told you. An offer like that won’t work on him.”
It seemed he had known all along that an offer like that wouldn’t work on me. I suppose it was to be expected of someone who survived getting his head crushed by my hammer.

“We’ve only wasted precious time.” Demon Eyes didn’t hide his disdain as he stepped forward past Glasses. The latter of the pair seemed to understand his intentions and slunk back in disappointment. “As long as we refuse to reconcile and meet each other halfway, there is no point in talking.”
“Reconcile? Don’t use difficult words.”
I cocked my head in mock ignorance, watching as the color of Demon Eyes’s pupils changed.
The tension that signaled an impending battle settled in the air around us. My grip tightened on my once-weapon, now the new symbol of peace.
Then suddenly, a sharp whistle cut through the tension. Once again, I was reminded just how unpredictable this world could be.
“Oi, Mister Vice-Captain!”
Demon Eyes broke eye contact first, gaze swinging toward the source of the whistle, and I followed suit to see who it was.
And then, I saw him.
Platinum blonde hair pushed back with styling oil.
Skin so pale it looked like it had never seen the light of day, paired with a chilling facial structure. All topped off with a villainous smile that didn’t fit the composition at all.
“Ah! I have entered the stage!”
The walking, talking human variable: Baekho Lee.

Baekho made his grand entrance atop a three—story inn, and he wasn’t alone. There he sat, legs dangling from the edge of the roof as familiar faces flanked him: Lek Aures, Jaina the priest of Karui, Fallen Gramps, and...
Who are those guys?
Dozens of cloaked figures I didn’t recognize stood exuding an aura that was altogether abnormal from head to toe.
Since when did Baekho have an army like that?
It was certainly a spectacular show of force, but Demon Eyes didn’t spare a glance at the people behind Baekho and glared directly at the man himself. “What business do you have here?”
The question sent a strange sense of kinship running through me. So the vice-captain knew as well as I did just how unpredictable this brat was.
“Oh, I’m just here to watch,” the subject of our attention snarked.
Demon Eyes didn’t respond. Instead, he simply stared at Baekho, as if trying to discern whether he was telling the truth.
For my part, I didn’t even know where to look.
I’m done for.
I felt more fucked than ever before.

My last encounter with Baekho had been an absolute disaster. It was nice to explore the world outside the city walls, but then things had gone awry while we were in the home stretch, and I’d ended up getting ganged up on by his allies. My allies had been forced to come looking for me beyond the walls, only to witness the battle’s aftermath.
In the end, I got him to kneel first.
“I...apologize...for threatening you...Baron...”
I couldn’t even imagine the humiliation he must have felt. He probably harbored an intense grudge against me.
Thus, Baekho could safely be filed under the “negative” variable to subtract from my circumstances.
“A lie.”
Demon Eyes’s voice brought me back to the present, and Baekho broke into a grin, shouting, “Correct!”
“Tell me. Why are you here?”
“Chilling and watching you two fight felt like it would get pretty boring.”
“Chill...?”
Naturally, the vice-captain couldn’t understand the slang, and rather than explaining it, Baekho just continued on to his main point.
“But aren’t the numbers too unbalanced for a fair fight?”
“What are you trying to say?”
“You two should just duke it out.”
His method spoke to no discernable logical train of thought between cause and effect. However primitive it was, though, the intent of his words was just as clear.
“And we’ll join Baron Yandel’s side if you refuse.”
“Are you saying you’ll go against the agreement?”

“Yep!” The cheery reply left the vice-captain speechless, and Baekho pounced on the opportunity. “What’s this? Vice-captain, were you gullible enough to actually put your faith in a measly scrap of paper?”
The childish insults hit true, causing Demon Eyes to grit his teeth. “This is why I said we shouldn’t trust a stray dog that bites every hand in sight...”
“Wow, rude. I know exactly who to bite!”
Demon Eyes quickly regained his composure despite Baekho’s continued needling. “So... What exactly does ‘duke it out’ mean?”

“Oh! I guess I should explain that first! To put it simply, a... No, not like that. So...” Baekho mulled over his words for a moment, then lowered his voice, as if to signify the joke was over. “Just duel each other.”
In other words, an ultimatum.
Demon Eyes calmly confirmed one thing. “And the reason?”
“The fight’s not fun if one side’s got all the numbers, right?”
Their conversation stalled for a moment. Demon Eyes went quiet as he seemingly weighed the pros and cons of the exchange, and I found myself in the same boat, head pounding as I tried to think.
Was Baekho Lee a positive variable or a negative one?
The answer didn’t come easily. Demon Eyes and I both knew that Baekho’s talk about being bored was just a lie. He undoubtedly had some ulterior motive.
Still, the math was adding up.
This might just push the odds in my favor for now...

If Baekho had interfered with the intent to choke me out, I wouldn’t have been able to do a thing. The fact that he didn’t take up an openly hostile stance against me was a positive, even if the end result remained to be seen.
“Right! Now that I think about it, I haven’t asked Baron Yandel for his opinion! Baron, how about it? Are you up for dueling him?”
“I don’t mind,” I answered.

“Haha! As expected of a barbarian—how cool!” Baekho exclaimed before turning to Demon Eyes to urge him even more. “Then what about our vice-captain here? Why aren’t you answering me? What are you, scared? Wow, you’re actually scared!”
His relentless taunts finally got Demon Eyes to break his silence.
“If I ‘duke it out’ against him, will you promise not to intervene?”

“Eh... Promise?” Baekho tilted his head. He probably hadn’t expected the word “promise” to be brought up when it had just been proven before how meaningless that word was to him. “Sure I will! I promise! Times a hundred!”
“Fine. I also accept.”
“Whoa, really?”
Although I didn’t know how he came to the decision, the vice-captain also agreed to “duke it out” with me. Clearly, it wasn’t because he believed in any promise.
What is he thinking?
When he spoke next, though, I got my answer.
“Keep your guard up against them,” Demon Eyes instructed. “And do not even attempt to help me under any circumstances. Just make sure that no one can intervene in our fight. Is that understood?”
“Yes, Vice-Captain, sir. Understood.”
The realization crashed over me, and I let out an involuntary gasp.
This guy. He genuinely believed he could defeat me.
I felt a twinge of insult at my bruised ego, but a smile soon crept across my face.
“How fun.”
Setting someone’s head straight was always a good time, especially when that person’s mind was a mess.

chapters.title: Chapter 761: Secret Garden (2)
paragraphs: The stage was set almost instantaneously.
Everyone stepped back, leaving a circular arena in the middle, and a few skilled spectators used their abilities to set up the rest.
[Lyte Naimon has cast the rank 4 defense magic Wall of Flowing Water.]
[Kelde Leous has cast the rank 4 dark magic Wall of the Dead.]
[Murta Elberita has cast Divine Protection Array.]

The makeshift army of wizards and ability users used their abilities to form a barrier that was dozens of layers thick. A few skills ended up lowering the crowd’s visibility, but they were quickly nullified when the spectators cried out.
“Hey, are you kidding me? I can’t see anything through the corpse wall!”
“Don’t use it unless it’s transparent!”
“W-well still, wouldn’t this be safer...?”
“Don’t do it! Just take the hit if it breaks through the barrier!”
The ones who had to cancel their skills sulked when they didn’t get to show off their own abilities, but consumers were a ruthless bunch. Others quickly filled in the gaps that were left behind.
“Rise! Twilight Curtain!”
“Oh! It’s got a yellowish tint, but it’s better than before!”
“But why did you say rise? From what I could tell, it’s just cloud’s gathering...”
“Don’t ask.”
In any case, a decently high-quality arena was created in a relatively short time frame. Except, aside from the professional-grade barrier, the setting was essentially just a street brawl.
Shouts of encouragement erupted from outside the barrier.
“Whoooa!”
“Vice-Captain! Show us!”
“I can finally see Demon Eyes with my own two eyes!”
A few of them were rooting for me as well. Though, by few, I meant one... Well, really two.
“Bjooorn! Great Warrior! Auyen! What are you doing? Why aren’t you shouting?!”
“I-I’ll root for you, Captain...!”
Auyen seemed to be saying something as well, but I couldn’t hear him above Ainar’s roaring voice and through the barrier in the way. It wasn’t that important, anyway.
I turned my body slightly to the side to look at Amelia.
When I stared, silently asking her why she wasn’t cheering, she let out a sigh before mumbling something under her breath. From the way her mouth moved, it seemed like she said, “Good luck.”
Heh, it’s always fun to mess with her.

Answering her cheer with a smirk, I tilted my head back to scan the roof of the three-story building. The figure there met my eyes, then grinned before shouting at me, “What are you doing? Go fight already!”
He acted like he was the school bully who was making two classmates fight.
It was pretty funny when I thought about it that way.
The vice-captain of Orcules versus me. This matchup ended up occurring in the middle of the street thanks to the intrusion of a certain troublemaker.
He sure is incredible, and not just in one way...
Although his antics seemed childish at times, I knew better than to underestimate him. It was a calculated act on his part—just like when I acted like an ignorant barbarian whenever it suited me.
It was all to obtain the things I wanted. If acting that way was more effective, I never hesitated.
But I’m going nuts trying to figure out what his angle is here.

I tore my gaze away from Baekho as he sat on the roof, chewing away at his jerky like he was eating popcorn. at a movie theater. Dwelling on his motivations wouldn’t yield an answer anytime soon, so I decided to leave the thinking to my future self.
Focus.
It was time to pour my all into solving my current problem.
Not much was publicly known about Demon Eyes, Roland Banozant. Among what was, the most important fact was that he was a special ability user and...
Taurboord.
...he possessed a rank 1 essence.

A Taurboord was similar to the Doppelganger in a way. Not because of its unique ability, but because it was a creature that could only be found within a special rift rather than on a regular field. It appeared as the Guardian of one of the rifts on the ninth floor, Hell Castle. In simpler terms, it only dropped a Guardian essence, just like the doppelgänger.
So just how did he obtain such a precious essence?
I didn’t need to question that at the moment.
This is why everyone’s talking about the golden age and whatever...

Just a few decades ago, this city had a few clans that could reach the eighth floor—some even making it to the ninth. Naturally, it was easier to obtain experience back then, and the prices of high-ranking essences were cheaper as well.
Even that Dragon Slayer bastard could reach level 9 back in those days. Of course, that all came to an end with a single dimensional collapse that divided the entire world.

“You seemed unaffected on the outside, but you have been pushed into a corner yourself,” Demon Eyes suddenly said from where he stood a fair distance away. “Seeing how you accepted this fight even knowing you’re at a disadvantage, you really must have no way out of this.”
I thought I misheard him at first. It took me a moment to process his words. “Huh?”
Is he serious...?

Well, I supposed it made sense from his perspective. He was a seasoned veteran, an elite even back during the golden age. Even if I was a rising star who was pretty famous nowadays, he would think I was just a brat who hadn’t even been to the ninth floor.
And there’s the issue of the matchup too.

Tanks were terrible in 1v1 duels. Well, they were fine when built for PvP, but there was no point playing a tank in that case. Tanks existed for team play, shining brightly only when backed by allies.
That was common sense in this world—or rather, the outdated wisdom of the old world.
So before this old sorcerer who had no idea how the world worked could get a full sentence out...
“Alright, then let us beg—”
“Behel-LAAAAA!”
I let out a roar as I charged him.
Boom!
My body enlarged by Giantization strode in leaps and bounds as I moved forward, closing the distance in an instant.
[You have cast Swing.]
Like a jab thrown by a boxer in round one, I used a basic attack against him.
“There are things that cannot be achieved through grit alone.”
Obviously, the attack didn’t land.
[Roland Banozant has cast Green Demon Eyes.]
The moments his eyes went green—
Bang!
A translucent green barrier appeared between us and blocked my hammer.
[Roland Banozant has cast Red Demon Eyes.]
Then his eyes shifted to red, and like a scene from a movie, red lasers began to blast out of them.
Fzzt!

Of course, it didn’t hurt that much. It was like getting hit with one of those electric shock toys at gift shops. Still, repeated blows would hurt eventually, so I raised my shield to guard against it.
“Uraaaaah!”
I charged him with my shield held up, and his eye color changed once more.
[Roland Banozant has cast Blue Demon Eyes.]
The moment his eyes turned blue, a similarly colored blue aura began to swirl around his body.
Vwoong!
He disappeared from sight.
However, he hadn’t gone far.
Behind me.
I sensed his presence and turned around, finding him glaring at me with his red eyes again.
“You cannot defeat me.”
Wow, we hadn’t even been fighting that long, but he was already running his mouth.
I wanted to shut him up tout suite, but rather than charge him like before, I just defended with my shield while quietly collecting my thoughts.
It really is a cheat essence.
The essence of Taurboord was truly unique. In exchange for not having a passive, it had over seven active skills.
Green Demon Eyes for defense, Red Demon Eyes for offense, and Blue Demon Eyes for movement. In other words, this one essence could fulfill most of his needs.
I wonder what he got for his other essences.
Dungeon and Stone wasn’t a game that could be completed with just one essence. The most important essences in a build were the supporting one that built your powerhouse up.
He could become a powerful damage dealer by filling the rest of his essence slots with those that empowered Red Demon Eyes, or he could increase his safety by building around his Green Demon Eyes.
So then, what did he do?
“That shield’s as tricky to deal with as I’ve heard.”
His grumbling was paired with a flare of intensity in his red gaze. I could tell what skill it was just by looking at it.
[Roland Banozant has cast Bend Light.]

A rank 3 transformative ability that turned a projectile into light and allowed that light to fly in a curve rather than a straight line. Also, if the projectile was already light, it increased the damage it dealt—and by a significant margin, at that.
Pwing!
Like guided missiles from video games, the lights that fired out from his eyes intelligently moved around my shield, striking my body directly.
That was when it hit me.
I’ve already been tricked.
In truth, I already had a rough idea of how he’d configured his Demon Eyes. I’d heard the gist of it from Ainar.
Those red eyes I was seeing weren’t real. They just looked like that to my eyes.
In reality, they were probably as white as paper.
[Roland Banozant has cast White Demon Eyes.]
Eyes that put an illusion over any target within its vision.
And of course, since it was a rank 1 essence, it wasn’t a simple illusion.
[The accumulated damage has exceeded the threshold.]
As long as I was still in the illusion, all the damage I took would be transferred to reality. And the broken part of this essence was yet to come.
As long as the target never breaks the illusion and escapes, he can use his skills without limit.

“Without limit” didn’t refer to cooldowns or soul power usage either. When this illusion was applied in the game, it allowed the caster to use nine essences of rank 3 and lower as much as they wanted.
[Roland Banozant has cast Bend Light.]
To put it simply, the way that the laser was bending wasn’t actually because of the Bend Light skill.
The story about how he killed the previous vice-captain in a single attack was probably because he used this illusion, and any observer wouldn’t be able to tell otherwise.
In any case, the important thing was that this guy had set his lower-ranked essences properly.
My mental stats were pretty high, but even I didn’t notice the illusion until I’d fallen into it.
He’s an illusionist, so he definitely has Escape from Reality, and he probably has a few skills that decrease mental resistances.
Most people would die without being able to resist.
Well, even though it wasn’t completely foolproof, it was exceedingly difficult to escape.
Option one: ignore the illusion and just overpower the caster with physical strength.
Option two: endure until the caster’s MP runs out.
Option three: break the illusion and escape.
These three were the only ways to get out, and naturally, my choice was already made.
[The accumulated damage has exceeded the threshold.]
I took the hit.
Pshwoong!
Took another again.
Vwoong!
And even charged and swung pointlessly once in a while so that my opponent wouldn’t suspect a thing.
[The accumulated damage has exceeded the threshold.]
I then got hit even more.

I wouldn’t need to do this if I still had those stacks of Dragon Plate I got after getting hit by Thunder, but unfortunately, the stacks faded with time. Since it had been hours since I got hit by Thunder, none of them remained.
[The accumulated damage has exceeded the threshold.]
I continued to diligently get my stacks.
Alright, that should be enough.
Then, I reached my desired stack count.
“I admit, you’re the first one to endure this—”
What was this guy talking about?
“Are those your final words?”
I looked like a complete mess, and rather than kindly explain to him who didn’t understand what I meant, I pulled out a piece of equipment from my sub-space and put it on my head.
Even as I did, he didn’t realize what I was doing.
What a relaxed guy.
Dungeon and Stone was a game where having good gear was as important as having good essences.
[You have equipped No. ????, Flower Crown of Anguish. You have obtained a mental immunity bonus.]
My mind cleared, as if a storm had passed.
When I looked ahead, I could see him looking back with pure white eyes.
Ugh, that’s gross.
It made him look like an alien. I was gripped with the feeling of looking at something in the uncanny valley and activated the effect of my second item.
[You have used Dragon Plate of Aegis.]
[Reflecting all accumulated damage.]

chapters.title: Chapter 762: Secret Garden (3)
paragraphs: Baekho Lee observed the battle with a sparkle in his eyes. His mouth was closed and his neck was jutted forward as if he was fixing every ounce of his attention on the scene.
Lek Aures was unfamiliar with this side of him.
“Baekho, who do you think will win?”
However, Baekho didn’t answer in his hyper-focused state, and Aures asked the same question when he realized the man didn’t hear him.
Finally, Baekho pulled his focus away from the fight and raised his head to look at Aures.
However, the look in his eyes was off, somehow. It was like he was trying to see what Aures’s problem was.
Cautiously, Aures asked, “Why are you looking at me like that?”
“I’m wondering if you’re genuinely asking or not.”
“I mean, how would I know what you’re thinking? I’m no god.”
“You don’t have to be a god to know this. We put our all into killing him. How’s that guy supposed to kill someone even we couldn’t take out?”
“B-but that’s the Demon Eyes.”
“And I’m Baekho Lee. And that gramps over there is the Fallen Scholar.”
“Enduring an ambush and winning a fight are two different things...” Aures responded genuinely. “Things might not turn out the way we expect.”
Baekho clicked his tongue in disgust. “Wow, I’m never going horse betting with you.”
“Horse betting...?”
“Shut up. Don’t talk to me.”
After dismissing him in annoyance, Baekho turned his attention back to the duel.

Time passed, all the while Aures waited for a good opportunity to talk to Baekho again. Since he was told not to interrupt, he didn’t actually want to engage the man in conversation, but he couldn’t hold back his curiosity.
“Um... Baekho?”
Baekho didn’t even pull his eyes away and just responded mechanically.
“What? Spit it out.”
“Why are you so focused on the fight? You said you already believe that Baron Yandel will win.”
Aures thought that maybe Baekho would realize he was acting out of character with that question and stumble over the answer.
“Why shouldn’t I focus on the match? Our baron here could be hiding more tricks up his sleeve.”
“Oh...” Aures said, momentarily speechless at Baekho’s easy assuredness. “I-I suppose so?”
Then, the “new trick” Baekho spoke of actually did appear.
“A flower crown...?! Was there an item like that? He escaped as soon as he put it on, so must be a mental defense type...”

Baekho’s eyes lit up, and before Aures knew it, he had whipped out a notebook and begun scribbling away. His pen flew across the page lightning-fast, accented by the harsh, excited breaths puffing in and out of his nose. As he wrote, he sometimes even licked his lips like someone who had just seen something delicious.
Aures watched from the side, then suppressed the emotion rising in his throat.
No... It’s not right to insult your allies.
Yet for some reason, he felt sorry for Baron Yandel.
Watching the changes in someone’s expression was entertainment at its finest. Even more so if that someone was my enemy and his expression was changing for the worse.
I grinned at my target, savoring the sight.

When I escaped the hallucination illusion by just wearing the Flower Crown of Anguish, his pure white eyes met mine as denial stole across his face. He escaped? the look seemed to demand. No, I must be mistaken.
Well, he soon awoke to the cold truth of reality.
“What... What is this?!”
Demon Eyes was intelligent enough to recognize that the flower crown had something to do with me escaping his illusion, and that realization enraged him.

After all, he would have had to eat many an essence to specialize in his White Demon Eyes and had to forfeit many things more. Yet all of that effort was nullified in an instant by a single item. He must have felt extremely cheated.
[You have used Dragon Plate of Aegis.]
[Reflecting all accumulated damage.]

The Dragon Plate’s ability activated, and the huge spirit of the warrior, tall enough to reach the ceiling of the barriers put up by the wizards, raised his giant sword. Demon Eyes abandoned his self-pity and regained his focus.
He wasn’t going to survive if he didn’t.
[Roland Banozant has cast Green Demon Eyes.]
He hurriedly put up a defensive barrier.
Shatter!
And when he saw that barrier be ripped apart like paper, he flinched but quickly used his blue eyes to dodge it.
Heh, this guy thinks I’m an ordinary barbarian.
[Roland Banozant has cast Blue Demon Eyes.]

Blue Demon Eyes was a blink-type skill that allowed him to instantly jump short distances, and it didn’t even take a second to cast. However, there was a fatal flaw to the skill: it didn’t activate if his movements were restricted.

Now, I had no crowd control I could use against him, but as a player who had played this game for an absurdly long time, I knew something. The restrictions that Blue Demon Eyes looked for weren’t simply roots or stuns.
[You have cast Transcendence.]
[You have cast Eye of the Storm.]
This grab that I used for combos was also designated as a movement restriction.
[Roland Banozant’s movement is restricted. Blue Demon Eyes failed to cast.]
To put it simply, his dodge was canceled.
As his path away from the giant spirit warrior’s greatsword was blocked, fear began to fill his eyes.
It was funny in a way.
‘Demon Eyes,’ huh?
But the eyes I was looking at now were nothing more than the eyes of a human.
The greatsword ripped through the air as it slashed down at him, and in his final moment, his expression changed one last time into a smile—or more specifically...
“Hah.”
A dry laugh of disbelief.
That was his end.

A deafening explosion kicked up a cloud of dirt and dust, and all the barriers around us shattered like windows in an earthquake. Over half the barriers were disabled from just the shockwave traveling along the ground.
As the barriers shattered, wind began to flow through the gaps, and the dust and dirt began to settle.
Everyone silently looked at the remains of what once was the vice-captain, smeared onto the ground.
“Raaaaaaah!” Ainar broke the silence with a triumphant roar. “Bjorn Yandel has killed the Demon Eyes! Now Bjorn Yandel is the strongest warrior in the world!”
That was the catalyst.
“A-attack...!”
The one who seemed to have the next highest authority after the vice-captain shouted the order, and the Noarkans that were standing aside all gathered together and charged.
To be honest, I expected as much to happen. In war, the entire purpose of a duel like this was to kill a skilled enemy leader without interruption so as to raise the morale of the troops.
That Glasses guy was probably thinking the same thing.
Demon Eyes’s original plan was probably to kill me on the stage Baekho had prepared for them and then use the victory to charge the people behind me.
Well, that plan became meaningless when he lost to me.
“Right, let’s go!”
As the elites of Orcules and the soldiers of Noark swarmed around us, Baekho finally stopped his spectating and jumped down from the roof, landing next to me.
“Been a while, hasn’t it?” he greeted me as if nothing was amiss.
I hesitated to respond. “What are you up to?”
“You think I’m up to something? That hurts. I came here to help you.”
Hah, he should stick to believable lies.
“By the way, that guy’s probably not dead yet.”
“What?” I balked.
“Oh, do you not know his essence?”
I didn’t.

When I was imprisoned in the underground cell, the Knight Gramps told me that Demon Eyes was able to survive having his head blown out thanks to an essence, but I wasn’t told exactly what essence it was. However, I could guess it was some sort of survival essence, and I also expected its cooldown to be pretty long and that it wouldn’t have rearmed itself yet.
“That guy ate the essence of Helasé.”
And with that, it clicked into place.
Ah... So that’s how it is.
The Helasé’s passive was a pretty unique survival skill. It didn’t raise defenses or give healing.
[Roland Banozant’s health is at 0%. Grace Period activates. A countdown of 900 seconds is given. During the countdown, all self-healing effects are disabled.]

That passive simply allowed him to escape true death for fifteen minutes. However, that didn’t make him invincible. It only delayed any instant death. Also, it was only useful if there was a healer or someone who could feed him a potion nearby.
But he ate that one when he’s not even a tank?
I was starting to get a good idea of just what type of person Demon Eyes was.
I did notice he just likes to show off a lot. He’s a weakling...
If it were me, I would have just used other essences to avoid situations in which I would require a lifeline in the first place.
“Oh, he’s being taken away,” Baekho remarked, pointing.

I whipped my head around to see members of Orcules carrying off the mostly dead vice-captain. The makeshift “transport team” all seemed to be agility-based characters, given how fast they were. I couldn’t even attempt to catch them.
That was why I looked at Baekho.
“What? Me? Why?”
“I haven’t said anything.”
“But you were gonna.”
Man. Why couldn’t this bastard be actually helpful if he was here to help?
I channeled my annoyance into my hammer as I crushed the head of a Noarkan that charged me. Amelia then appeared in front of me while holding Eltora up with one hand.
Oh, and Ainar popped up next to her with Auyen in hand too.
“Yandel.”
Alright, then we got everything we needed.
“Oh, been a while with you too, huh?” Baekho tried to greet Amelia, but she didn’t even look in his direction and just ignored him.
“Let’s hurry. We’ll leave this place to them.”
“Huh? You’re leaving us? Hey? Hello?”
Amelia completely ignored Baekho’s grumbling once. again. I joined her.
“Yeah, let’s. Get on.”
Once Giantified, I picked up my allies, and Baekho clicked his tongue.

“Hmph, look at these selfish people... How did my life. come to this?” Then Baekho smirked at my stare. “Hah, I don’t need your thanks, so just go. We’ll clean this place up nice and tidy like, then bounce—”
“I wasn’t planning on thanking you, though?”
“What?”
Ignoring his stunned disbelief, I shot him a word of warning to behave himself and that I would be watching. With that, I immediately left the battlefield.
Boom! Boom!
Using Eltora’s navigation function, I finally arrived at my destination. Once there, I stood in a daze.
Hah, I did wonder why there were no soldiers here even though it was the building the marquess was recovering in.
Damn it.
The marquess had already evacuated.
Of course he had. With how much time I wasted dueling the Demon Eyes, it would be stranger if he had stuck around. Still, that didn’t mean I was out of options.
I turned to Eltora. “Hey. Where’s your father at?”
“Wh-who knows? Wh-where could he be?”
“Don’t think about dodging the question.”
“Well... Maybe he moved to a different place while we were being kept busy?”
Did he think I didn’t know that?
“Think about it. Where might your father be? This may be your last opportunity.”
I told him in a roundabout way that he might just be abandoned if he didn’t give me any useful information, and Eltora quickly coughed up an answer.
“Oh! Th-there is one place!”
I realized the place he mentioned wasn’t too far away, so we immediately began running again.
And when we finally arrived at ‘that place’...
I reunited with someone I never expected.
“It has been a while, Baron Yandel.”
Harin Savy.
My ex-girlfriend.

chapters.title: Chapter 763: Secret Garden (4)
paragraphs: Nothing in my life was ever simple.
The building I arrived at after finishing that unplanned duel against Demon Eyes was completely empty. It seemed they had taken the marquess and ran.
“The villa! There is a villa not too far from here!”
At my light suggestion that he better think of a place that the marquess could have gone to, Eltora pointed to a villa.
“A villa?”
“A secret villa that only the marquess knows! It’s in District 4!”
“How is it a secret if you know about it?”
“It really is a place that no one knows about! I-I only know about it because I was there when I was young. No one within the family knows about it!”
“When you were young...?”

I furrowed my brow, and Eltora, realizing why I misunderstood, quickly amended, “I mean when this body was young. I found the diary written by the original person in my room, and there was a passage about a secret villa.”
Wow, so this bastard not only started as the son of the prime minister, but also had the diary of the original person? When I first opened my eyes, I needed to worry about whether I was getting axed.
“Father took me to the villa... There was a beautiful garden with blooming flowers, and I was surprised to see Father personally tend to it... That was what I read!”
“Hmm?”

“Anyway, I didn’t want to be caught for being an evil spirit, so I even looked into the location of the secret villa. But even when I looked through all the information available in the mansion, I couldn’t find a trace of the villa.”
“Oh, then how did you figure it out?”

“It was thanks to Countess Peprok. When she appeared, I investigated her, just in case. There was one piece of land under her name. Even the countess herself didn’t know she had it. When I visited, I saw a villa with only a single old gardener employed there. I spoke with him, and he didn’t even know that he was employed by the marquess.”
So that was what happened. It certainly sounded suspicious—if we ignored one little thing.
“But if it’s such a secret building, how could the marquess flee there? He’s unconscious right now.”
Eltora huffed out a breath of surprise when I pointed that problem out, apparently not having thought of that yet. However, he also seemed reluctant to give up.

“Still... wouldn’t there be at least one person among his close aides that knows about it?” he said, sneaking peeks at my reaction. When I just stared back at him, he realized how flimsy the argument sounded and avoided my gaze.
“Alright, let’s go there.”
Eltora took a moment to respond. “Really?”
“Yeah. Doing something is better than just standing around here.”
With that, I decided to go to this “secret villa” that Eltora spoke of.
After all, the prime minister already knew that his “son” was an evil spirit. One of the people in his inner circle might happen to know about the marquess’s villa and had taken him there.
Although, the probability of him not being there was higher in my mind.
Still, I get a feeling I’ll get something good if I search for a place like that.

Even if it became wasted steps now, there was value to searching through the marquess’s secret villa. I might even stumble across a secret there, just like when I searched the secret room in the marquess’s office.
“So tell me, where is this villa?”
“It’s not too far from here!”

With a new destination entered into my navigation system, it didn’t take long before we arrived at our destination. The villa was modest, a two-story building encircled by a tall fence. Something about it reminded me of that house—one I had shared with Erwen.
After crossing the fence and entering the grounds, I saw the garden, which was beautifully maintained, just as Eltora described.
As soon as we entered the garden, Amelia took a long scan of the area before gently touching the flowers.
“The garden being taken care of,” she noted. “Someone has tended to the flowers recently. Two days at most. Could’ve even been yesterday.”
Well, I had no idea how to tell when a garden was last tended to, but if Amelia said it, she was probably right.
“Either way, I feel like we’re at the wrong place... But let’s check inside just in case. There could be a hidden room in the building where the marquess is hiding.”
“Sure,” she agreed.
We were about to enter the building proper when Amelia suddenly whipped her head around toward the building. She glanced at me.
It seemed she sensed a presence from the inside.
I didn’t even need to try sensing the presence. Footsteps echoed from within the building.
It was just one person.
I wondered if it could be the old groundskeeper that Eltora talked about.
“Huh?”
However, the person that appeared was someone I could have never anticipated.
“It has been a while, Baron Yandel.”
The first person to react to the woman’s gentle greetings was Eltora.
“Harin Savy...? Why are you here?”
“Good to see you again as well, Lord Tercerion. You visited this place not long ago, yes?”
“Not long ago? Wait... So even back then, you...”
“Yes. I was hiding there and observing you—from the moment you went looking through the villa to the point you realized the secret.”
Eltora’s expression hardened as Hyeonbyeol openly admitted it.
“Woman, what are you scheming— Ack!”
His face promptly relaxed again after getting smacked.
“Don’t act up and stay still,” I warned.
“U-understood.”
Acting like that in front of another man’s ex-girlfriend was taboo.
With Eltora quieted down after one slap, I continued the conversation in Eltora’s stead.
“Harin Savy, why are you here?”
It was the question that needed to be answered first. Just why was Hyeonbyeol at the marquess’s secret villa?
“Pardon?”
“I’ll ask again. Why are you here?” I repeated, pressing for a clear answer from her.
Hyeonbyeol merely responded, “Uh... Didn’t you come here knowing that?”
“Huh?”
“I contacted you. To come here. On the paper.”
Oh, the Love Paper...
“Did you...not read it?” she asked cautiously.
Uh... I mean, I didn’t have time.
I cleared my throat, trying to wipe the embarrassment off my face, and Hyeonbyeol shook her head.
“It’s fine. In the end, you still ended up here. In fact, this is better. Like you were destined to be here.”
“Destined?”
Amelia was the one who mumbled that, causing Hyeonbyeol to shrug.
“Yes. No matter how twisted and branching the paths are, one will always meet again the other they are destined to meet.”
“That’s an...interesting thought.”
“Thank you for finding it interesting. Hello, Amel—” Hyeonbyeol paused awkwardly. “Ah, It’s Emily Raines, yes?”
Although it seemed like a mistake at first, I could tell she did it on purpose. She was quietly revealing the fact that she knew Amelia’s real name.
I don’t know why she revealed that fact, though.
“Yes... Hello to you too, Harin Savy.”
Greetings exchanged, Hyeonbyeol looked back at me and returned to the main topic.
“So you asked why I am here?”
“I did.”
“Come in. Let’s talk inside.”
With that, we stepped foot into the villa.
The interior of the villa was very plain.
Although each and every part of the interior would be expensive if they were priced individually, it wasn’t as fancy as the marquess’s secret villa that I had envisioned in my mind.
Honestly, the interior didn’t match my impression of the marquess at all. It was tame and warm, like the feeling you’d get from some cozy, affluent family home.

“I apologize, but could the others step away for a little?” Hyeonbyeol asked. “I have something very private I wish to say between just the two of us. If you see over that hall over there, there is a room that you can rest in—”
“I refuse,” Amelia interjected, resolute.
Hyeonbyeol silently looked at me.
I smothered a sigh before addressing Amelia. “Sorry, but step out for a bit. I need to hear what she has to say.”
“...Understood.”
With that, Amelia took the others into the room Hyeonbyeol pointed out, and I sat on the sofa as an inexplicable unease settled within me.
“Oh, just a sec.”

Hyeonbyeol pressed a button on something that looked like a recording device before putting it down on the table. Despite its appearance, however, it wasn’t a device for recording noise, but a magic tool that stopped sound from escaping a certain radius around the item.
“You’re the same as ever,” I said dryly.
“Pardon? What do you mean?”
“It’s like you always said: “The one who holds the power isn’t the one who makes the decision, but the one who creates the decision point.””
“You can loosen up a little around me, you know?”
“Yeah, it’s just a bit awkward with this body. Alright, so what’s this villa?” I asked, forcing myself to sound more like Hansu Lee.
Hyeonbyeol smiled in satisfaction. “Oh, I wonder. But hmm, to put it simply... It’s like Marquess Tercerion’s keepsake box? Something like that.”
“Keepsake box...?”
“You know, like those boxes that hold all the good memories you had in the past. Don’t you have anything like that?”
“Then what did you do with all the letters I gave you?”
...I threw them out. I thought it would only bring up unnecessary feelings if I kept them in my room.
