When I stayed silent, unable to tell her that, Hyeonbyeol nodded, seeming to understand all the same. “I wondered why I couldn’t find them no matter how much I looked through your room.”
“So. I think we’ve gone off topic.”
“Oh, sure... Anyway, this is a keepsake box. The place that the marquess comes to hide in whenever he’s having a hard time.”
“Then why are you in a place like this?”
“The marquess sent me here.”
“What do you mean? Can you please just get to the point?”
“Countess Peprok is sleeping in the underground bunker below this building. And the marquess told me to protect Countess Peprok and care for her.”
“So the marquess isn’t here?”
“No?”
“And you don’t know where he is?”
“No. How would I know that?”
“I asked just in case. You’re the one who told me that Ainar was going to be executed.”

“Oh, that was really just a coincidence. The marquess visited briefly around the same time that was happening. When I asked him how the war was going... Well, he just told me a few things, like he did whenever we chatted in the past.”
“You chatted with the marquess?”
“He’s unexpectedly gentle. A pure love type as well. He’s feeling quite lonely, fitting for his age.”
Well, I couldn’t really agree with that. Still, everyone had a side to them that didn’t quite fit the image they presented to the world.
“He loves his daughter very much. And he treats me pretty well too, probably because I am his daughter’s friend and right-hand woman.”
“Really?”
“Oh, have you not been paying attention? The reason the marquess started this war in the first place was for his daughter.”
I flinched, startled into looking straight at her. “What?”
Hyoenbyeol only shrugged and took out a book. When I looked at her, silently asking what it was, she just stared back at me to tell me to just read it.
I flipped open the cover as asked and began to read from the first page, then I realized what this book was.
There is a rumor in the Palace of Glory. When the ball commences and night falls, a nameless woman appears inside the ballroom.
From witness testimony, the girl is stunningly beautiful and petite, with innocent eyes and a musical voice.
However, when the smitten noblemen approach her and ask for her name, she stops her lively conversation and can’t answer them. Moments later, she vanishes before their very eyes like a ghost...
When I first heard about it, I laughed off the rumor. But surprisingly enough, it was true.
On the 16th day of the 7th month, in the middle of summer as hot winds persist even through the night, I went to the palace ball with my father and met that nameless girl.
It was the marquess’s diary.

chapters.title: Chapter 764: Secret Garden (5)
paragraphs: Before delving into the marquess’s diary, I asked Hyeonbyeol one more thing.
“Where did you get this?”
This wasn’t the first time I had seen the marquess’s diary—or at least, a coded book that I suspected was the marquess’s diary.
“Why? Are you worried I lied to you and gave you a suspicious book?”
“No. It’s just I can’t believe that this is real. How were you able to get it?”
“Are you mocking me right now? Saying I’m an incompetent woman?”
“Huh? No, that’s not what I—”

“I’m kidding,” Hyeonbyeol cut me off with a laugh. “And this isn’t something you can get just by being skilled, either.” Then without giving time for my bewilderment to turn into annoyance, she revealed, “He gave it to me. The marquess.”
“Huh?”
“I said he gave it to me. He forced Countess Peprok to sleep, locked her in here, then just plopped it in my lap.”
Just because she was talking like it was a simple thing didn’t mean it was easy to understand.
“Uh... So... He just gave you his diary?”

“Hmm, I suppose he didn’t ‘just’ give it to me? Marquess Tercerion had been subconsciously looking for someone to understand the life he has lived, even if only simple parts of it—his words, not mine.”
“And that person...is you?”

“Technically, it was Countess Peprok. The marquess told me to give this diary to her when she wakes up, no matter how this war ends. And if a situation comes about where I can’t give it to her, he told me to burn it.”
“But it’s suspicious he let you read it too.”
“That’s why I said he’s lonely. I asked what would happen if I read it, and he just told me I could if I wanted to.”
I didn’t have a response to that.

“The second most powerful man in the kingdom, the iron-blooded prime minister, the head of the march... No matter what he was called by the world, and no matter what he looked like to you. To me, he was just a simple father who loved his daughter. Even if we acknowledge that he couldn’t express it well.”
The further along we got in the conversation, the stronger the sense I got that the marquess I knew was different from the one Hyeonbyeol knew.
Maybe it’s to be expected.

Then again, the way I treated the marquess was also a lot different from the way I treated Hyeonbyeol. Everyone had an unexpected side to them, but there were limits to the side one was willing to share with certain people.
“So...” she prompted. “Are you not going to read it?”
“I should. This is an opportunity to read the secret diary of that marquess. Well, I wouldn’t be the first one I guess.”
“Not the second either.”
“Huh?”
“Eltora Tercerion. He came here a few days ago and was snooping around the place. It looked like he was looking for something, so I put this somewhere he could find.”
I flinched. “What?”
“Oh, don’t worry. This is the original copy. I have a magic tool that I use a lot whenever I’m doing administrative work, and I used that to make a few copies of key segments.”
The reason I flinched wasn’t because I was worried whether this was the original.
“You showed it to him? Why?” I asked with a tilt of my head.
Hyeonbyeol’s answer was nonchalant. “Because Eltora Tecerion would betray the marquess if he understood his thoughts. And that would be helpful to you, Hansu, yes?”
I was momentarily lost for words. Hyeonbyeol was right, of course, and things ended up in my favor because of it too. Still, I was baffled.
“Didn’t you just say the marquess is a lonely man?”
Hyeonbyeol seemed to not understand my point. “Yes, that’s right. But I’m a lonely person too.”
I let out a sigh. Yeah, there was no way I could beat her with words.
“Did I do good?” Hyeonbyeol asked, eying my smile.
I answered her.
“Good work.”
Now, let’s read the rest of this diary.
After reading the marquess’s diary, my first impression was that the diary spanned quite a long period of his life.
The 16th of the 7th month, 27th of the 8th, 22nd of the 9th...
The dates were far from each other.

Of course, it wasn’t because this was homework he forgot to do until the last day of summer vacation, nor was it because the marquess wasn’t the type to diligently write a diary every day. This diary was simply...
“This is just stitchwork.”

He had taken out specific parts from his daily journal and had stitched them together here. It was like cutting out only the articles you liked from the newspaper and storing them to have an easier time when looking for them later.
“Please stop just analyzing it,” Hyeonbyeol criticized. impatiently. “Can you just read the rest of it already?”
“Fine.”
I hid my embarrassment and continued to read the diary.
The structure of this diary was naturally one of a collection of essays. However, the genre of the story within the diary seemed to be romance—with maybe even a touch of a thriller thrown in to boot.
I went to the palace ball with my father and met that nameless girl.
This story began when the marquess met the rumored girl at the ball.
The marquess quickly ran over and asked the girl if she was the subject of the rumor, and the girl dissipated into thin air, seemingly overwhelmed by his question.
Upon returning home, the marquess wondered if what he had seen was real or a trick of the eye. He thought it over, then eventually decided to find the girl once again.
And then...
The 27th of the 8th month, at the end of summer when the cold winds of the night began to blow.
Inside a garden maze, filled with sleeping flowers, I found the nameless girl.
At last, once more.
The marquess met the girl again, and rather than running up to her immediately, he carefully approached her from afar.
He lowered her guard while keeping a distance, using the conversational methods he learned from a book he read on negotiation fundamentals to slowly get acquainted with her.

The more we spoke, the more I realized this nameless girl defied understanding. She was limited in knowledge, and that made it so our conversation ran in circles and wandered aimlessly. However, her pure eyes sparkling with curiosity told me this:
This nameless girl was no ghost.
The question that had tormented me for the past month was finally solved. However, a new question arose. Then what was this girl? For what reason does she walk such an odd path?
As dawn gradually kissed the sky, the girl disappeared without a word, and as if a man possessed, I returned home in a daze before realizing something as I stood in front of my mirror.
My eyes sparkled with the same light as that girl’s.
The marquess, now more intrigued than ever, visited the palace whenever possible, using whatever excuse he could give.
The 22nd of the 9th month. Our third meeting came to pass.
The marquess finally had the third encounter he had so looked forward to.
The conversation he shared with her was nothing special. It was mostly the marquess answering the girl’s questions. He didn’t even ask why she didn’t know such basic things.
In truth, he never asked any questions at all. He was afraid the girl would disappear into thin air just like before.
The marquess made sure to not scare her away with questions, then when dawn broke, he asked her one for the first time.
At that time, there was a question that mattered more to me than the name of this nameless girl.
Would I be able to see you again?
I asked that, and the nameless girl looked surprised before hesitating and finally giving an answer.
Probably.
Hyeonbyeol spoke up then.
“Pretty juicy, huh?”
“I mean, not really, considering I can only imagine the wrinkly face of the marquess.”
“Then look at that on the table. That’s the portrait of the marquess when he was young.”
“...Really?”
He was pretty handsome. I supposed he needed to be for the nameless girl to get a bit embarrassed when he asked to see her again.
“Anyway, I won’t interrupt you anymore, so keep reading. The stuff at the end is the real deal.”
I sensed some bitterness in Hyeonbyeol’s tone, almost like she was leading me into a trap that she had fallen into already.
I couldn’t know for sure, but I didn’t ask and continued to read the diary.
Summer passed, and so did fall, winter, spring...
Even as the seasons changed over and over, the marquess kept meeting with the girl, and the relationship between them slowly began to change as well.
The girl spoke while sitting at the edge of the fountain. I couldn’t hear her well due to the running water...
From the faraway entrance to the edge of the fountain.
From the edge of the fountain, just that little bit closer.
The distance between their conversations continued to shrink.
I’ll see you next time.
At some point, their meeting became a fact of life.
I think I can come out in the morning during the inauguration of General Arkan...
They even began promising to meet at specific times, and naturally, the distance between the dates in the diary shrunk as well.
However, the marquess didn’t know anything.
The name of the girl, her age, or her circumstances.

He knew nothing, but the marquess didn’t mind. Those days were so comfortable and precious to him that he never questioned her. He simply waited until the girl was comfortable to tell him herself one day.
At least, that was his intention.
The 19th of the 7th month.
A year passed, and summer came again.
The girl disappeared.
One day, the marquess arrived early at the garden of the palace where they always met, yet he was greeted only by the wind.
She probably couldn’t make it for some reason, he reasoned.
Yet even though the marquess headed to the garden whenever there was an official event at the palace, the girl never came back.

I once read in a book that all emotions stem from loss. When one loses something, that is when their true emotions are revealed, or something like that? I couldn’t understand when I first read it. Didn’t you just need to do well before losing it so that you didn’t regret it later? I thought that because I was unintelligent back then.
Yes, that was what I thought in the past.
The marquess finally realized his true feelings, but it was already too late.
He went around asking if anyone knew about the girl, and even made excuses to come into the palace, but he couldn’t find her.
“Do they meet again?”
“Do you think they wouldn’t?”
Well, considering the thickness of the book, there was still a lot of story left to go through.
I was suddenly reminded of a dilemma I saw on the internet.
Which was scarier: having a lot of story left but the remaining pages grow thinner and thinner OR the story should be coming to an end but there are a lot of pages left?
I was more afraid of the latter.
The fact that there were a lot more pages left also meant there could be a shift in genre. An unexpected twist was awaiting.
Like so.
When I finally met her again, she wasn’t a girl or a teen. The girl who grew up just like I imagined in my dreams had become a fine woman.
However, rather than being glad to see her again, I felt the weight of the ages crush my heart.
Six years... It was a long six years later when I met her once more.
After passing through six long years, the marquess finally reunited with the girl, now a woman.
I had imagined countless scenarios when imagining this moment.
I would reveal my heart to her, and when I asked her name, she would cry and enter my embrace.

After that, she would confess to me under circumstances more shocking than I could hope to fathom, then she would ask me if I was alright, and I would smile saying it was nothing, I could handle it...
I had imagined this scenario every night, hundreds and thousands of times, but on that day, I didn’t ask her anything.
Because I already had a pregnant wife.
I couldn’t help what I said when I read the final line of the page.
“No way, what the f—”
It seemed there needed to be another tag added to this story.
“Is this NTR?” I mumbled.
Hyeonbyeol shook her head.
“No? It’s a tragedy.”
Suddenly, I was scared to turn the page.

chapters.title: Chapter 765: Secret Garden (6)
paragraphs: As I continued to read the diary, Hyeonbyeol asked from beside me, “How is it? Isn’t it fun?”
“I mean...?”
To be honest, I couldn’t really say it was a fun read. I didn’t like the romance genre in the first place, and I wasn’t someone who cared about the love life of others either.
Still, I couldn’t deny it was a little entertaining. After all, the main character of this story was the marquess.
This book was going to tell me what the marquess had gone through that pushed him to make the reckless decision of going against the king.
But I can’t tell just yet...
However, with only the first half of the diary under my belt, I still couldn’t fully understand.
So I continued to read.
If I were to quickly skim the uninteresting parts and only summarize the main points...
When she saw me freeze as if I had seen a ghost, she asked me what happened. I answered that I had a pregnant wife waiting for me back home.
And so, the reunion after six years ended with that.
The girl remained quiet for a while before saying, “Then you’ll need to go early.” The marquess then replied that yes, he should, and did just that.
The thought refused to leave me. What was the meaning of that silence on that day? Maybe she had the same feelings that I had—
It wasn’t fun or important for me to know just how much the marquess suffered and ruminated over his feelings, so I just skipped that part.
With time, the marquess’s son was born to the world. His joy of raising his son was genuine.
Yet still, the thought still plagues me. What would the child look like if I had him with her? Maybe he would be as beautiful and lovely, perhaps even more beautiful and lovely than my son?
The marquess devoted even more of himself to his family to erase those sinful thoughts, and it was also around this time he became the head of the household in his sick father’s stead.
With his days consumed by both his work and his family, the marquess’s memories of his first love began to slowly fade. But then—
She appeared again. After another six years.
It happened on the day he went to the palace to officially claim his title of marquess. Nostalgia drew him to the garden, where he met her once more.

The first thing I thought when I met her again was that it was as if we last met only yesterday. It wasn’t a metaphor for my longing for her. Her appearance was exactly the same as when I saw her six years prior.
The passage of time had not touched her appearance.
Although he found it a little odd, the marquess didn’t dwell on it.
She congratulated me on my child and my inheritance, and I accepted her words with joy. Time had buried the emotions, and I was finally able to ask her.
What is your name, and why are you hiding in the palace like this?
She hesitated for a long time before finally speaking. It wasn’t the answer to my question, but a request. She asked me to take her outside.
The marquess debated the request for some time before finally accepting it.

No matter her situation, he believed that he would be able to handle the consequences now that he was the marquess. He also calculated he would be able to hear about her “situation” after he helped her out.

I successfully took her outside the palace walls, then used magic to change the color of her hair and eyes. Around the time Eltora was born, I took her to a secret safe house that I had prepared without anyone’s knowledge.
It wasn’t difficult to understand that the villa I was in was the safe house he was talking about.
It probably didn’t matter much in the story.
We spent a lot of time in that secret safe house, and I was finally able to hear her name.
My interest was reignited as I read that line. Although there were more pages left in the book, the moment I was waiting for had finally arrived.
Meirin Huinveina Rafdonia.
Huh?
That was her name.
Seriously?
Some time ago, I had seen the portrait of a woman that I suspected was Ragna’s mother inside the marquess’s hidden room.
Meirin Huinveina ———
The last name had been scratched out by something sharp and been left unreadable.
However, I now knew her full name.
Rafdonia.
The last name that was only permitted to those of the king’s bloodline in this kingdom.
Chills went down my spine as soon as I saw it.
There was a very good chance that Ragna’s mother was Meirin Huinveina Rafdonia, which also meant...
Ragna...is a descendant of the royal family?
Even given the fact that the princess bore her out of wedlock and in secret, it didn’t change the fact that she was born with the blood of the king.
Then why is the marquess revolting against the Crown?
Of course, this nameless princess probably had something to do with it, but it wasn’t like I knew any of the details of their situation.
Thus, I continued to read. Every answer I sought was probably here in these pages.
While she stayed in the secret safe house, I listened to her story. Her tale was much more shocking than I had ever imagined. I never expected the palace to be hiding secrets like that...
“Wait... Does he ever write what these secrets are?”
“No?”
I sighed. So the marquess didn’t put the details in on purpose when he stitched this diary together.
“Alright. I’ll just read the rest first.”
As shocking as the secrets were, the way she was raised to be a sacrificial lamb was what truly made me pity her. My sympathy for her continued to grow day by day.
As a man with a wife and child, I tried to resist it, but on the day tears fell from her eyes, I had no choice but to recognize my feelings went beyond mere sympathy.
Fortunately for me, I wasn’t the only one with these feelings. When I finally confirmed it, I experienced a sense of fulfillment that I would never again obtain in my life.
However, those sweet times between the marquess and Meirin didn’t last long.
Considering the absolute power of the palace, it was amazing that I was able to last a month with her. In the end, they found us, and I saw him in the audience hall.

He was nothing like I expected. I thought he was trying to intimidate me at first, but he laughed, said a joke, then made me an offer. He said something about needing at least one person among the people working under him who knew the secret as well as him.

He saw me favorably and offered me the position of prime minister, and I had no choice but to accept. It was a promotion that I had wished for, but as someone who now knew the secret of the palace, I couldn’t revel in whatever joy I might have felt.
The story after his meeting with the king could be summarized in just a few lines.
The marquess returned to the secret safe house and resumed his sweet times with her, and that love bore fruit in the end.
She became pregnant.
The marquess was overjoyed, incomparably so compared to when he had Eltora.
There’s no way this has a happy ending. Not with this many pages still left.
The incident that changed his life was something that even I, who had seen countless forms of media, could never have expected.
What shattered this happiness that I thought would last forever wasn’t a change of the king’s heart, a political scheme, or the betrayal of a subordinate. It was closer to divine judgment.
As we lay in our bed, whispering words of love to each other as I stroked her rounded belly, Meirin suddenly screamed.
Who am I? Who are you? Where am I?
She shouted out incomprehensible words, almost as if possessed. She then said something that should never have been uttered by her lips.
Dungeon and Stone.
An evil spirit had entered Meirin’s body.
As if struck by Thunder, I stiffened, shocked beyond all belief and mind utterly blank. Yet as time passed and my thoughts returned to me, I suddenly had a question.
I thought evil spirits could only possess people around when people become adults?

Although I wasn’t completely sure what Meirin’s age was when it happened to her, it would have been far after she became an adult. Six years had already passed since the marquess noted she had turned from a girl into a woman.
So how could such a thing happen?
Although the author of the diary, the marquess, didn’t mention anything about this problem, I could make an estimated guess using one of the passages he had written before.
*It was as if we last met only yesterday.*
As if six years hadn’t passed for her.

Perhaps, for some reason, some external factor made it so that Meirin’s biological time had truly stopped. The palace did possess that weird life-preservation device, so it wasn’t too far-fetched to imagine.
Now I get why Hyeonbyeol said this is a tragedy.
After Meirin’s body was overtaken by an evil spirit, the marquess’s life descended into hell.
He asked for advice from the king, yet the king only clicked his tongue and said there was no way, giving the marquess his blessing to do as pleased: kill her or save her.
It was as if the sky was falling for him.
However, time still passed in hell, and Meirin’s pregnancy came to its final stages.
Whatever “it” was—whether a man or a woman—killed itself while giving birth to my daughter.
The evil spirit died after giving birth to Ragna.
However, the marquess told the palace that she died while giving birth and whisked Ragna away behind their back.
He wished for this child, at least, to live a calm life.
But then...
“And then, even Eltora became an evil spirit...”
With time, even his eldest son—his only close relation left—became an evil spirit. Then, only Ragna remained.
“The marquess probably just wants to rip apart all the evil spirits in the world.”
I couldn’t even begin to fathom what he must have felt.
Yet still, from my perspective, the marquess did something foolish. It seemed he planned on leaving all he had accomplished down to Ragna.
The 21st of the 10th month.
The dates in the diary were getting closer to the present day, now a month before the marquess revolted against the palace.
Before my preparations were complete, the king awoke.
I need to protect that child, no matter what.
That was the final line in the diary, and I let out a deep sigh as soon as I closed the book.
“How was it?” Hyeonbyeol asked. “Fun?”
“Not really...”
My review upon reading the diary in full was that it “wasn’t fun.”
And why would it be?
“I thought something interesting would appear at the end, but it was a bit empty,” I added.
“Obviously, the marquess is still alive.”
“I read it myself just in case, but I should’ve just asked you to summarize it in three sentences.”
“Hah! How could I crunch all this into three sentences?”
“Huh? Isn’t it simple?”
One: The marquess fell in love with the princess.
Two: The princess became an evil spirit, then died after giving birth.
Three: Time passed, and the eldest son Eltora also became an evil spirit, and the marquess revolted to protect the one last child he had.
The story could be summarized pretty easily into that, and the recipient would be able to get everything they needed. The message could be condensed even more if said recipient was Ragna.
I love you, my daughter.
That one sentence would be enough.
Yeah... It definitely feels like a letter from him to Ragna.
He overlooked the secret of the palace, and even while reading the rest of the diary, I could tell there were many things he had excluded on purpose to hide. them.
Well, if those things were also written in here, he probably wouldn’t have said that Hyeonbyeol could read it as well.
I had more questions than before reading the entirety of the diary.
“What are you thinking about?” Hyeonbyeol wondered.
“I’m wondering what the marquess is thinking.”
“Why are you curious about that? Isn’t it obviously to succeed in his coup and protect his daughter?”
“Yeah, but that’s Plan A—a plan that he himself believes has a low chance of succeeding since he left this diary behind.”
“Hmm... I guess?”
“With his personality, he definitely has a Plan B to protect Ragna... I just can’t get a bead on what it could be. Just putting her to sleep in a secret villa like this? Isn’t that too complacent?”
Hyeonbyeol fell into thought, then said, “Maybe... You are Plan B, Hansu?”
“What?”

“I mean, doesn’t it make sense? The fact that he tried to marry you to her before...” Hyeonbyeol trailed off, then smirked. “And he knows better than anyone else. You are the kind of person who can raise your blade against the palace if it is to protect the people precious to you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 766: Setting Things Straight (1)
paragraphs: Hyeonbyeol suggesting that the marquess’s Plan B could be me left me momentarily stunned.
Only for a short moment, of course.

It’s not totally outside the realm of belief, I reasoned to myself. If the marquess loses, it means the palace wins, and if the palace wins, it means there’s a good chance that I’ve made some contribution to that victory... So he might assume I’d have enough power to at least protect Ragna...
The marquess definitely could have done the math up to that point. However, I still found it hard to believe that I was his Plan B.
Maybe his Plan C.
I’ll think about this more later...
“Is there anything else I should know?” I asked.
“Hmm, the fact that you need me if you want to go to the secret room that Countess Peprok is in?”
I nodded. “I see.”
“But about Countess Peprok...” Hyeonbyeol began carefully.
Hmm, why was she hesitating? Didn’t she say she had nothing else she needed to tell me?
When I sent her a suspicious look, Hyeonbyeol met my gaze, an inscrutable expression in her eyes.
“Isn’t she pretty?” she finished.
“Well, I guess...?”
“Then why did you turn her down?”
What was I supposed to do, marry every beautiful woman I saw? Besides, if I married her back then, I’d have gotten swept up in the marquess’s plans.
But Hyeonbyeol probably isn’t asking because she’s curious about those reasons.

With how much time I had spent with Hyeonbyeol in the past, I could tell. She wouldn’t accept any of the political reasons I could give her. Right now, she was asking this question to build up to a different one.
“Marriage is a major life event. I need to be even more cautious than ever before.”
I utilized my Confucianism mentality for the first time. in a while and spoke sternly to her. In truth, it was more of an expression to tell her that I didn’t want to talk more about this topic.
Picking up on my intentions, Hyeonbyeol didn’t press me any further, but she seemed a little sullen, given her next jab.
“Oh? So you like that doll that much?”
Why was that being brought up all of a sudden?
“Hyeonbyeol, you know that I had no choice but to lie—”
“Was it really a lie? Copies of that doll that you held back then are pretty popular among the nobles these days.”
I paused. “Really?”
“Yes, really. They’re like ‘Oh! So this is the doll that the Giant, Bjorn Yandel, likes so much—’”
“Stop.”
Please, stop talking about it. Man... Why did I do that?
Even I didn’t know why looking back on it now, but I decided to stop thinking about it. It wasn’t as if I could go back in time and fix it.
“Whatever, let’s get going. The others are waiting for us.”
I needed to move on from the past.
When we went back to the room where my allies were waiting, Amelia tossed me a question.
“So, did your conversation go well?”
It was in the same tone as usual, but having spent a long time with her, I noticed the undertone of hurt in her voice.
However, before I could respond, Hyeonbyeol answered in my stead from where she stood next to me. “Yes. Thanks to you, our private conversation went well. Thank you again, Ms. Emily.”
“I wasn’t asking you.”
“Oh my, weren’t you? So sorry.”
Amelia remained silent at Hyeonbyeol’s disingenuous apology. I sensed a sudden chill in the air and quickly changed the topic.
“Emily, anything happening outside?”
“It’s quiet. It seems he’s drawing attention so well that they don’t have the time to worry about us. And I’ve looked around the building while you were talking, but I couldn’t find anything that—”
“Hah, look at that,” Hyeonbyeol interrupted. “What would you do without me?”
Amelia took a moment to respond. “What do you mean?”
“There’s a hidden area in this villa. Most people would never be able to find it no matter how hard they looked.”

She was probably referring to the place where Ragna was sleeping. While I understood she wanted to emphasize how much I owed her, I really wished she would quit it. Amelia had been smiling for a while now—and not with her eyes, just her lips.
“You are an...interesting type of person.”
Amelia was probably wondering herself as well. This woman, whom she could stab to death without any resistance, had shown up without introduction and continued to mess with her even now.
I don’t know why she likes tormenting people so much when she’s so weak...
I was somewhat relieved that Hyeonbyeol was a noncombatant and quickly rushed to finish my thought.
“Even if the Noarkans aren’t actively on us right now, we don’t know what’ll happen in the future,” I said. “So, Harin Savy. Guide us to that room that you said holds Countess Peprok.”
“Sure.”
Despite its short length, I felt exhausted by the conversation. Shaking my head, I followed Hyeonbyeol as she led us to the outer walls of the building.
“There’s a hidden area here...?” Amelia asked with a
furrowed brow. She had followed us here too.
I shared her question. Usually, hidden areas were behind bookshelves or under carpets.
“Isn’t it the garden behind this wall?”
Just like what Eltora said, there was no room behind this wall.
However, I didn’t doubt Hyeonbyeol. This was another world where hopes, dreams, and magic existed.
Rather than answering us, Hyeonbyeol stretched out her long fingers to tap the wall before the bracelet on her wrist began to glow and resonate with the wall.
Blue light beamed out from the resonating wall. It was entirely different from the magic circles I had been seeing up to now.
Not to say the sight was unfamiliar to me.
“A portal...?” I muttered aloud as the shimmering gateway formed before us, rippling as though waving at us to enter.
“Looks like the marquess put a lot of effort into this,” Amelia remarked, straightforward and coldly logical now. “I couldn’t detect any mana until the portal started to be formed.”
Hyeonbyeol smirked. I worried the mood might get frosty again, but nothing ended up happening.
“I’ll go first,” I declared.
The area inside the portal was surprisingly ordinary. I’d expected something mystical, considering we needed a portal to enter here.
It’s just an ordinary room?
A cozy room with a bed, table, and wallpaper.
I only looked around for a moment before my eyes became glued to the bed. Ragna lay there, fast asleep and oblivious to the happenings of the world. I felt an odd emotion well up in me at the sight.
I could’ve never expected she’d be a princess...
Fate truly was mysterious. What were the odds that the librarian I met when I was a rank 9 barbarian adventurer would turn out to be royalty?
“Is there a way to wake her?” I asked Hyeonbyeol, who followed in after me.
“I guess there is? Either the marquess wakes her up himself, or he dies.”
“So...nothing we can do for now.”
“I guess?”
I sighed. That was that, then.
As I stood there quietly, watching Ragna, Amelia spoke to me.
“So we’ve confirmed the safety of Countess Peprok. What are you going to do now? Are you going to use this woman to find the marquess?”
“Something like that? What do you mean?”
Uh... Well.
I understood one fundamental truth after reading the diary: the marquess really loved his daughter.
“Just wait. He’ll come to us as soon as he wakes up.”
And we needed to prepare a little for his arrival.
The plan was very simple—especially since a barbarian was carrying it out.
Boom!
I swung my hammer in my Giantization size and destroyed the marquess’s keepsake box.
The roof, the walls, the beautifully tended garden, the fences...
It only took around ten minutes for this secret villa, which seemed to have been constructed by some famous architect, to be completely torn down.
“Wow, that was quick...”
“Whoa-hoh! It’s only natural!” Ainar boomed proudly. “Barbarians are experts in construction!”
“Construction...? Ah, well. I suppose demolition is also a part of construction...”
Hyeonbyeol was impressed as she observed my work, and the demolition work was all done with Ainar standing back proudly.
When the marquess saw his destroyed keepsake box, he probably wouldn’t be able to hold himself back, but I didn’t care about that.
After quickly destroying the villa, I approached the outer wall that was covered in debris. I had taken special care not to damage it in the process since it was where the portal entrance was.
“Harin Savy, open the portal.”
“Okay.”
We opened the portal and entered the room, and our preparations were complete.
Given that it was Auyen who struck him, the marquess would probably wake up around tomorrow afternoon, and he’d come here to check on the situation at hand.
And as soon as he learns that this place is destroyed?

With how much love he had for his daughter, he would definitely have someone check on her, and there was a good chance that he would come personally. Since the marquess hadn’t been transferred here after he lost consciousness, even his closest aides probably didn’t know about this place. For its continued safety and secrecy, he’d have no choice but to come himself.
It doesn’t even matter even if he doesn’t come himself.
Even if he sent a subordinate, we had a decent chance of figuring out where the marquess was by interrogating said subordinate.
I just need to get to the marquess.

Of course, I knew that simply defeating the marquess wasn’t going to end the war, but so what? By killing the marquess, my deal with the king would be fulfilled, and I would no longer need to care about the war.
They can take care of the rest.
We killed time, spending it quietly in the crowded room.
Though, I suppose it wasn’t all that quiet.
“It’s been a while since we’ve spent time like this in a room together. Isn’t that right, Lord Baron?”
Why was she still doing this? Did she enjoy messing with me that much?
Hooonk! Hooonk!
Since I knew that she’d only come on stronger if I gave her a reaction, I acted like I was sleeping. At that, Hyeonbyeol just snickered and let me go.
However, that was when Ainar came in with an unexpected attack.
“Stop pushing your luck, human female.”
“Human female...?”
“I understand that you’re in heat, but your body can’t birth a warrior in the first place.”
“What the hell are you talking about...?”
“I don’t know what sort of relationship you had with Bjorn. However, we won’t ignore you. We have no intention of putting you in line either. So don’t act up and just stay still.”
Hyeonbyeol seemed caught off guard and flustered at the barbarian’s direct way of speaking. However, she quickly gathered her wits and went to talk back at Ainar.
“Enough,” Ainar intervened, stopping the situation from escalating. “Ainar, you too. Just be quiet and eat this.”
“Hmm? I’m not trying to cause trouble... Oh! Th-this is jerky made from Ltaspa! You’re giving me something so precious...!”
What, Ltaspa? She never gave me those even when I asked...

Drool began to dribble from my mouth as the scent of the highest quality jerky filled the room, but I continued to act like I was sleeping. At some point, I actually fell asleep. I woke up later feeling hungry, and spent time messing with the marquess’s son.
Six hours, twelve hours, a day...
Soon enough, the period in which the marquess should have woken passed.
Two days, three days...
Even more time passed after that, and I began to think that my plan had gone awry.
Then, a bright light shone, and a visitor walked through the portal.

chapters.title: Chapter 767: Setting Things Straight (2)
paragraphs: The person who stepped through the shimmering portal was someone I never could have anticipated. Unlike my prediction, that it would be the marquess or one of his close aides, the one who arrived was unrelated to the march entirely.
Or could it be that they weren’t so “entirely” unrelated after all?
The man took one look around the room and, as though seeing a ghost, sputtered, “Bjorn Yandel...?”
My surprise mirrored his. “Glasses?”

It was the person who, only a few days ago, made me a certain offer before I had my duel against Demon Eyes. The man closest to the castellan and an unassuming confidant who assumed no specific role—ore of an as-needed fixer-upper than anything.
But that wasn’t the important thing at the moment.
I raised my hammer, holding it just shy of his nose, and demanded, “How does the castellan of Noark know about this place?”

“While the marquess was unconscious, all authority was transferred over to the castellan,” he answered nervously, going on to offer more information than I asked for. “As it stands, the marquess has been released of all his worldly desires and is under the castellan’s safeguard and protection.”
“So basically, you backstabbed the marquess while he was knocked out, and now you’re keeping him under your thumb?”
True to the pragmatically minded reputation of Noarkans, he calmly agreed with my direct accusation. “That’s right. The marquess was too swept up in emotion to work toward the ultimate goal.”
“Meaning?”

“Lord Baron, did he not fire multiple rounds of Thunder at you? Those shots could have been deployed at more strategic targets to ensure victory, but instead, he allowed himself to be blinded by his selfish desires. And even after all that, he still failed to capture you.”

How sly of him, to focus on the marquess’s ownership of Thunder. Considering that one bolt of Thunder reportedly required an obscene number of sacrifices, and the castellan’s Noarkan forces would have had a significant hand in procuring said sacrifices, it was a convenient oversight of their own complicity.
Still, it wasn’t as if I didn’t understand his point, and it wasn’t what mattered here and now.
“That wasn’t my question. How exactly did the castellan of Noark know to send you here?”
Realization flashed across the man’s face at my persistence, and he quickly gave me his answer.
“O-oh! The castellan didn’t know that you would be hiding here, Lord Baron. If I had known that, I wouldn’t have been so surprised to see you, yes?”
Great, that didn’t answer my question at all. Again. Seriously, how much of a waffler was this guy?
“The point,” I deadpanned.
“The castellan is very intelligent, and—”
“Didn’t I tell you to get to the point?”
Finally, he gave in. “The marquess made a...*request* while he was being held. He asked us to confirm whether or not Countess Ragna Peprok was here.”
“The marquess asked you personally to check?”
“More specifically, he asked us to see if she was here, safe and sound, and to leave her be if so. And if she was not here, we were to find her through any means necessary.”
“And the reward for carrying out this request?”
The man hesitated, a decision warring on his face. The answer he came to was short.
“Ownership of Thunder.”

The pieces were falling into place. The marquess awoke from his coma to find himself stripped of military authority. Realizing he had been swiftly lowered to a mere pawn, he knew he could no longer protect Ragna with his own power.
So he offered up Thunder for negotiation, I thought, reeling from the sheer absurdity of it. He wants to protect Ragna by any means necessary.

All Auyen did was to knock the marquess unconscious for two days, yet this was how everything ended up? That one incident had led to the marquess’s plans completely falling apart, unraveling beyond the point of repair before he could truly begin to carry them out.
Well, if the marquess and the castellan had been on better terms, being out for two days wouldn’t have led to a situation like this...

In this brutal world, any show of weakness was consent to being ripped apart down to the bone. Unfortunately, the marquess had exposed his vulnerability and now had no choice but to give up everything. It was a snowball of consequences far too big to have originated from one single captured navigator.
“Wh-why are you...? It’s just, y-you’re suddenly...” the navigator in question stammered when he saw the look on my face.
“I’m just proud of you.”
Auyen’s small act had birthed a guiding star that would forever shine in this era.
Anyway, leaving that there...

The marquess’s predicament aside, there still was one more question on my mind. I hadn’t even begun to truly interrogate the guy, so why was Glasses, the castellan’s problem solver, telling me all this information freely?
It wasn’t long before I heard the answer from the man himself.
“Isn’t it obvious? I’ve concluded that I cannot accomplish my goals without persuading you first.”
“You think you can convince me to help get you ownership of Thunder from the marquess?” I asked, nearly letting out a dry laugh.
“Why not?”
The audacity of his reply had me momentarily speechless. “Huh?”
“We know as well as you do that Noark isn’t your sworn enemy.”

It was an unspeakable offense, something that should never have been said to a titled noble of Rafdonia, let alone the man being hailed as the hero of the city. However, there was nothing I could say to defend myself. My goal in this war was to make it out to the other end with as many of my allies alive and well as possible, and killing the marquess would ensure it.
“Tell me what you want,” Glasses insisted. “Surely you and I can come to some sort of agreement.”
I sighed. How should I navigate this fork in the road?
Before making any decisions, I asked him about the situation outside—starting with how the war was going and then moving on to things that piqued my curiosity.

“Baekho Lee? He held the frontlines for a while after you left before eventually disappearing himself. Even with all those people with him running away with him, we weren’t able to catch them—they all just vanished.”
So Baekho had disappeared. Just what did that bastard hope to gain from this war? His motives continued to elude me.

Still, it sounded like some sort of ceasefire had been reached. The walls surrounding each district were being used as the battle lines, and everyone was just holding their ground, not daring to make a move.
“We require Countess Peprok,” Glasses wagered, “and if you give her to us, the castellan will grant you anything you desire.”
“Oh, even if I ask for his neck?” When he clammed up, I said, “I’m joking. Even I’m not that reckless.”
I figured it was about time to set the jokes aside and get down to confirming one last thing.
“What if I ask for the marquess? Would that be possible?”
“Of course,” the man replied. “We don’t care what you do with the marquess, so long as the transfer of Thunder’s ownership is carried out without issue.”
“Really now? I’ll keep that in mind.”

Glasses noticed my skepticism and added, “This isn’t just my opinion. The castellan will reach the same. conclusion when you speak with him. I have served him for a long time. You can trust me on this.”
“I’ll make that call when we get there.”

Ending the conversation there, I placed a blindfold over his eyes and noise—canceling headphones over his ears. They weren’t an actual set of headphones, of course—just a magic tool that could achieve a similar effect.
I needed some time to think.
“Emily,” I called. “What do you think?”
Amelia, having been listening to the entire story alongside me, made her stance on the matter clear. “I think it’s doable. Of course, that’s under the pretense that everything he told us was true.”
“What kind of person is the castellan of Noark? Is he trustworthy?”
“Not at all. He’s a respectable person, sure, but not because he’s worthy of trust. Still... He’s never been the type to make unnecessary enemies.”
“I do remember he tried to get on my good side before,” I mumbled. “Anyway, I take it that you agree to the plan?”
“In my personal opinion... We have a better chance of seeing this exchange through safely than any other plan we might come up with to position ourselves better.”
Amelia’s assessment was the final piece I needed.
“Hmm? What about me? Aren’t you going to ask me?”
I ignored Ainar’s random rambling and took the headgear off of Glasses. “I’ll talk with the castellan first. I’m guessing you have some way to contact him?”
“Of course,” he answered. “If you want to speak to him now... Ah, but it doesn’t work properly in here. We should head outside first.”
“Fine.”
It was taking a risk, but one thing kept me from dwelling on that thought. Even if the deal went sideways, I would at least learn where the marquess was being held.
“Let’s go.”

With that, we left the rubbles of the building together, then immediately contacted the castellan using a magic tool. The castellan seemed flustered to see me suddenly appear on his communications line, but it didn’t take long to explain the situation and seal the deal.
“You help convince the marquess to transfer ownership of Thunder to us, and in exchange, you will take the marquess. Are those all of your conditions?” he asked.
“Yeah.”
“Then there is no reason for me to refuse. Hand over Countess Peprok to him. When the ownership transfer is complete, I will transport the marquess to a place of your choosing.”
“No, I can’t trust that. I will meet with the marquess personally.”
The castellan took a moment to respond. “You are pushing your luck.”
“Shouldn’t I be saying that about you?” I countered, trying to hide my genuine surprise. “What, you think you can catch me if I take her and run?”

There was silence on the other end of the line before the castellan finally relented. “I will allow you to accompany him to the marquess’s location. However, understand that we must prepare quite a few things before you do.”
“Prepare?”
“You might harbor other intentions. Surely you understand that we need some way to stop you. I wouldn’t worry too much, though. If the exchange ends well, you won’t be in any danger.”
“Fine. But will I be seeing you face-to-face?”
The castellan laughed. “Well... I’m not foolish enough to meet with someone even the Demon Eyes couldn’t stop. Oh, and be sure to bring all your allies with you.”
“Huh...?” Usually, it would’ve been the opposite. I didn’t need to wonder for long, though.
“It’s our last line of defense,” he explained. “Not even you would be able to escape while ensuring the safety of all your allies.”
I sighed. Even a random back alley thug would know my weakness at this point.
“I hope for good news when we next talk.”

There was a short wait following that parting line from the castellan, then word came that the castellan’s “preparations” were complete, and we were off with Glasses leading the way. The marquess was being held in a building on the outskirts of District 4, near the wall bordering Bifron.
Once we had entered the building and began walking up the stairs, Amelia quietly whispered to me, “Yandel, this building... No, the entire area is swarming with enemies.”
“How many?”
“If it were just you, me, and Ainar, we might be fine... But if we want to keep the rest safe, there are too many of them of us to escape.”
So that was how it was. It seemed the castellan had made good use of his time.
“This is the room,” Glasses announced. He glanced back at us before slowly opening the door.
Inside, a middle-aged man lying on the bed quickly sat up, his eyes going wide at the sight of me.
He was the prime minister of Rafdonia, Ageni Lawton Tercerion.
Studying him with a closer eye, though, had my eyebrows in a frown. Something about him... It just felt off, almost like he was a different person entirely.
Was the marquess always this small...?
He didn’t look to have lost any weight. Yet somehow, I looked at him and saw a frail, old man. Was it his plain clothing?
However, I understood the reason for the dissonance as soon as we met eyes.
His eyes...
The look in his eyes had changed. Gone was the gaze of the predator I always saw there.
I guess it’s to be expected, I mused to myself. His military authority was taken away, and now he’s just stuck in this room.
While I eyed him from afar, the marquess nodded, appearing to grasp the situation.
“So, you’ve come at last,” he said, his tone suggesting this was something he had foreseen.
My reply was confident. “I told you I’d find you.”
I was a little shocked myself, to be fair. How could I have possibly anticipated we would meet again like this? Still, I knew an opening when I saw one.
“Good to see you,” I greeted.
Then, I smacked him in the back of the head.
Thwack!
I was a little surprised. So that was what the marquess’s head sounded like. I had been imagining the sound of it every day since the Ice Rock Expedition, and yet...
It’s not that satisfying.
Somehow, it didn’t feel that gratifying.

chapters.title: Chapter 768: Setting Things Straight (3)
paragraphs: My lived experiences proved that a barbarian’s hands were a cure for many things. I had personally cured many mental problems with these hands, and this time around proved no different.
Thwack!
Once my strike landed on the back of his head, life returned to the marquess’s previously glassy, dead eyes.
Well, rather than “life,” it was closer to humiliation and rage... But those negative emotions still proved that he was alive, so it wasn’t entirely the wrong word to use.
“Right, that feels better,” I said, unable to hide my satisfaction as I watched the marquess regain his zest for life.

He slowly turned to look up at me, a tangle of emotions behind those eyes. There was bewilderment at having his head get assaulted, humiliation at having to now look up at someone whom he had once towered over, and lastly...
“Ragna...”
There was love for his daughter. And shame for failing to protect her.
I had no reason to sympathize with him. The heart of a warrior wasn’t so weak as to pity his enemies, and I still remembered it—the marquess’s words from that fateful day.
“After that, any one of those precious allies of yours could die. No, they will die. I will make sure of that.”
“You must feel it as well. You must feel my pain.”
That curse, born from the depths of his heart, had come true. I was struck by Thunder, and while I lay unconscious, Rotmiller died trying to save me.
The one who killed Rotmiller was a nameless Noarkan soldier, but the marquess was also to blame.
I had no pity for this man.
I clenched my fist, the weight of the twenty who died in Ice Rock pressing down on me, far too heavy to allow room for such humane emotions as “empathy.”

While the two of us silently glared at each other, Glasses interrupted our conversation from the back. “Marquess... As promised, we have brought your daughter to you. So fulfill the end of your deal.”
“Are you talking about the ownership of Thunder?” the marquess clarified.

“That’s right. If you do, Noark will guarantee your daughter’s protection. Of course, you will not receive the same treatment. Baron Yandel has requested custody of you in exchange for giving your daughter.”
“I see... So that’s what happened.”
Only then did the marquess understand how I had ended up appearing with Glasses. He then turned back to me to ask a new question.
“Did you see?”
It was a short question, concise while still ambiguous. But I didn’t need to ask for clarification.
“I did.”

“I see...” The marquess’s voice trailed off into a pause before he spoke again. “I wish to have a private conversation with the baron. Could you leave the room for a moment? You may keep my daughter with you.”
Glasses looked conflicted at the marquess’s request but nodded soon after, allowing it.
“You can grant me this at least,” the marquess commented. “Just a short moment is all I ask.”
“You’ll need to keep your promise.”
Unexpectedly, Glasses granted his permission without much hassle. I glanced back to confirm with Amelia, who took the others and left with Glasses. With that, only the marquess and I were left.
“It’s been a while since we’ve had a private conversation like this.”
I took a moment before responding, “You’re calmer than I expected.”
“Fear is an emotion that arises within those who have something to their name. But look at me. Do I have anything left to lose?”
“Well, from what I saw in that diary, it looks like you do.”
The roundabout mention of Ragna brought a wry smile to the marquess’s face.
In some ways, the marquess wasn’t so different from me. Our weaknesses were painfully clear to the world.
“So, what is it? You suddenly asked for this one-on- one. Are you going to say something about leaving your daughter to me?”
I laced my words with sarcasm, but nothing in his demeanor suggested he had a retort prepared. What a boring guy.
“What? Is that really what you’re—”
“How much do you know about the royal house of Rafdonia?” he interrupted suddenly, catching me off guard.
“Huh? Why is the topic sliding in that direction?”
Admittedly, it was a topic that I intended to broach myself. The marquess had simply gotten to it first.
The royal house of Rafdonia.
If anyone could shed light on those great secrets veiling the royal house of Rafdonia, it was the marquess.
Just what were they so desperate to hide?
“Well, I know a few things that most others don’t know,” I said nonchalantly, trying to elicit an answer. “Why, you have something to tell me?”
The marquess nodded without hesitation.
“Then spit it out. Who knows? Maybe I’ll be so moved by your story that I’ll help Ragna.”
When I tossed in some bait to get him to talk, the marquess responded with a shocking confession.
“The Immortal King and the King of the New World are one and the same.”
“Huh?”
What did he just say?
The epic of the King of the New World was very famous.
When civil unrest was at an all-time high from the Immortal descending into madness and killing everyone in sight, the King of the New World seized the throne and ushered in a new era for the people.
The death of undeath and the birth of a new age.

The new king abolished many outdated traditions and implemented countless policies for the citizens’ welfare. His reforms earned him the ardent support of his people, who thus hailed him as the “wise king.”
Yet now, the marquess was telling me otherwise.
“They’re the same person?”
The revelation was shocking, but there was no time to stand around in stunned silence. I needed to verify the claim first.
“Is this reliable information?” I asked, knowing it might be a useless question. The marquess said only this in return.
“Judging by the fact that you’re not questioning whether it is even possible, it seems you already know something about the royal house.”
He was right.
After exploring the first basement floor and the world outside the walls, neither of which existed in the game, I learned a lot about the royal family.
“Ah, did you not know? After the Immortal had a child, he would steal the child’s body to continue his rule. It is also the reason the Immortal always acted with a mask on.”

I learned that secret of Rafdonia from the village chief, a hero from a bygone era. At the time, I assumed that was why the King of the New World wanted to usurp the throne. There was no motivation more pressing than one’s own survival. However, that was why...
“Just answer my question,” I demanded. “Is this information reliable?”
To be honest, it was hard to believe. I knew that the marquess’s claim was theoretically possible, and yet...
“I made up my mind that I would be different from him. That I would live as a human and die as a human.”
It didn’t seem like he was putting on a show when the King of the New World spoke those words to me.
Was everything he told me really a lie? For me to believe that, I would at least need—

“If you wish for proof, I have nothing of the sort,” the marquess said, anticipating my next demand. “The royal house of Rafdonia isn’t that careless. However, I have spent many years investigating the royal house, and I’ve come to the conclusion that it is far more likely than not that the two are one and the same.”
After listening intently to the marquess’s admission, I couldn’t help but sigh.
Great, so it was all just a gut feeling he had? I’d gotten worked up over nothing.
Well, I don’t really care if the two people are the same or not...
“Anyway, is that all you wanted to tell me? That there is a good chance the Immortal and the King of the New World are the same person?”
“Of course not. I’ve only mentioned this so that I could say the rest.”
“Then get to it. This will be the last opportunity you’ll have.”
“Do you know about the Heart of Karui?”
The Heart of Karui.

A treasure imbued with the authority of the ancient evil god, said to allow its wielder to steal another’s body. The Immortal used it to extend his life by stealing the body of his descendants, just like an evil spirit.
“I do,” I said.
“Then this should be quick. While taking over the body of the King of the New World, the Immortal lost the last remaining Heart of Karui in his possession.”
Wait.
“The last remaining?”

“I’ve seen you frequent the library, yet you seem to have skipped studying your ancient mythologies. Even the scriptures of the Three Gods Church have a verse about stabbing treasures into the two hearts of the evil god.”
“Skip the history lesson. So, to put it simply, the Heart of Karui... There are actually two treasures with that same name.”
“That’s right.”
That answered a question I had.
I’d always wondered how the king sustained his immortality even after the village chief made off with the Heart in ancient times.
“I got it, so keep talking.”
“In any case, after losing track of the last remaining heart, time passed and the body of the King of the New World was also coming to its end. Originally, he should’ve died then and there. However-”
“He’s still alive,” I said, casually finishing the marquess’s sentence. “Though he does need to sleep a lot more these days.”
An inscrutable look came over the marquess’s eyes. “I never expected you to know that much.”
“Luck is not on my side,” I deadpanned. All I wanted was to live, yet I kept getting swept up in all sorts of sticky situations. “I won’t cut you off, so keep going. What do you want to tell me?”

Slowly, he began again. “The royal house continued to look for the Heart of Karui. And just recently, the treasure resurfaced once more. Thankfully, it seems the palace doesn’t know of its location yet, but...”
“But?”
“It’s only a matter of time before they find it. That is why I’ve taken such reckless measures.”
“Because the king might take over Ragna’s body?”
“That’s right. There was no other way to protect my daughter.”
I see.
I had suspected something was pushing the plot forward, but I never expected the full story to be like this.
His lover and son had been taken away, and now, he was in danger of losing his daughter as well. There was no way he could just sit idly by and watch it happen.
However, it still left me with one question:
“But does it have to be Ragna?”
Why was the marquess so sure the king would take Ragna’s body?
“The king always only took over the bodies of his own blood. There must be a reason for this.”

“No, that’s not it...” I said, trailing off. “If I were the King of the New World, I probably would’ve had many different children. Can’t you convince him to take the body of a different kid, someone who isn’t your daughter?”

At that, the marquess gave a bitter smile. “At one point in time, It was just as you said. The King of the New World sired many children and ‘stored’ them. However... A mysterious organization relentlessly targeted them.”
“A mysterious organization?”
“Heerkmuta. They wear black wolf masks and claim to follow the Last Great Sage. I don’t know what their motives are, but they aimed for the king’s children while he slept, and now, none remain.”
And in that process, the knight captain of the Order of the Rose had also been slain. That wasn’t the important part, though.
“Do you understand what this means?”
“Ragna is the only one of royal blood that’s left.”
The marquess closed his eyes, quiet for a moment, then opened them again. “Alright, then I’ll give you my final offer.”
I waited for him to continue.
“Have you ever wanted to become a king?”
The words fell short of the tempting whisper of a devil.
The marquess’s expression was too desperate, too pitiful, for that.

chapters.title: Chapter 769: Setting Things Straight (4)
paragraphs: The world of males consisted of hierarchies.
Those who failed to grow from birth and become strong were exiled from the pack while those who climbed the hierarchy bettered their chances of finding an ideal mate.

Such was the law of nature, and no matter how much one denied it, it wasn’t any different for human males. Humans were also a part of nature, after all. Embedded in their DNA was the innate desire to be just that one rung higher in the pecking order.
Perhaps that was why boys were so drawn to games. Said instincts might simply be etched into their very being.
Well, not that it would matter if I was wrong.
“The king...”
I knew better than anyone else that heavy responsibility came with lofty positions, but still, the thought of becoming king was tempting.
Like I said, all men were born with at least a teaspoon of desire to wield absolute power and unchallenged authority, at least once.
However...
“What are you scheming?”
I wanted to make this point clear at least.

The marquess was the one who had so relentlessly cursed me not long ago. Why was he suddenly switching lanes to join my side? It didn’t seem like he was a man without and thus was simply desperate to survive.
“A scheme? Do you think I have the time to concoct such a thing?”
“Well, no one knows for sure.”
“What are you so afraid of? This is something you will have to do regardless of me and mine.”
Startled, I asked, “What?”
“Do you not understand?” the marquess demanded, not even flinching. “Think about it for a moment. If the king were to target that child with ill intent, would you really just stand by and watch?”
I hesitated, picturing the scenario before I answered. “That will depend on the situation.”
The marquess nodded as if that was all he needed to hear. “I can tell by that vague answer. You will do whatever you need to do to protect her.”
I had to admit, he was right. But still.
“I think you’ve got the wrong idea here. It’s true that I’m on friendly terms with Ragna, but I wouldn’t lay down everything I have for her,” I said, drawing a clear line in the sand.

Contrary to my expectations, though, the marquess merely agreed with me. “I know. Objectively speaking, your relationship with her isn’t to that point. That is why I am trying to make a deal with you... Surely you know this deep down. As long as the king is alive, the days you wish for, a time when you can live in true peace and safety, will never come.”
I flinched, frowning at the truth of his words.
This old man. He’s really got the mind of a snake.
I sighed. “Fine, then. Tell me. If I want to become King, are you saying I can?”
“It would seem you are somewhat interested?”
“Just curious for now. I can tell you plan to use Ragna for this, but
I don’t know exactly what you’re thinking.”
I shot him a look, daring him to speak. The marquess took a moment to compose himself before speaking.
“It is possible.”
“And you know this how?”
“For many reasons. However, the most important one...is me.”
“You?”
“I am still alive. Even after openly opposing the royal house. It is proof that the power of the royal house isn’t as absolute as it was in the past.”
“Well... Couldn’t this all be just a sick play by the royal family?”
“The very fact that they need to resort to such measures is proof that they have weakened. The king of old wouldn’t have needed to stoop to any of this.”
It was mere conjecture in the end, yet it sounded plausible enough—not baseless, complete nonsense at least.
Still, that didn’t mean much at the moment.
“If that’s all the evidence you have, I don’t have any reason to hear you out,” I informed him.
“I suppose I should be grateful the conversation will go longer, then.”
“Just get to the point. I hate wasting time.”

As the marquess stated before, we certainly weren’t cooperating but rather finalizing a deal, and our relationship in this needed to be clear. The role of convincing the other party fell to the marquess.
“First, if that child dies, you will never become king.”
“Hmm?”
“Even if it may seem like hollow loyalty, the people of this city will never accept a king without royal blood. Especially not if that person is a barbarian.”
“Are you saying I can use Ragna to mitigate the nobles’ resistance?”

“Precisely. Even if this is a flimsy pretext, there is a difference between having the king’s blood and not. Without it, the people will oppose anyone who would dare sit on the throne. Blood will be shed every single day.”
“I have a lot I want to say, but I get what you’re trying to tell me. Go on.”
“That child’s very existence will be of great help to you as you prepare to accomplish this deed.”
“You mean I can use Ragna to expand my forces beforehand.”
“As you know, this isn’t something you can accomplish on your own.”
I smirked at that. I told him to get to the point, what was he doing still talking in circles?
“I genuinely hope that you weren’t trying to convince me with just that,” I said snarkily. “I don’t particularly want to become king in the first place.”

“I understand. You are not the type to be truly interested in a position like that. However, you’ve listened so far because you understand. There are things in this world that must be done, even when one doesn’t want anything to do with them.”
Was this him seeing the light just before death?
For some reason, the marquess’s words felt heavier today, as if he was looking straight into my soul.
Of course, “taking the throne” wasn’t something “that must be done,” as he put it. Even so, I figured I should at least keep it in mind.
The more choices available to me, the better.
“Think of it this way. I’m not asking you to protect that child no matter the circumstances... But please, promise me this. Promise me that you will do your best, at least within reason.”
Only then did I realize it.
The marquess had stated before that he was making a deal with me, but...
“This isn’t a deal at all.”
Deals were an exchange where both give and both take.
But this? This couldn’t be a deal.
It was more like a tribute, a final prayer made with the last strand of hope he had left.
“Fine...” I conceded, still wary. “I promise. I’ll do my best, as long as it doesn’t harm what I already have.”
“That will suffice.”
With that, the marquess finally relaxed, his rigid expression softening as he let out a sigh.
And then, he offered me a “tribute” of his own that he hadn’t spoken a word of before.

The marquess spent a long while explaining the inner workings of the royal house to me, the things I needed to do if I wanted to become the king, and even told me the nobles whom I could contact if I wished to walk this path...
“The authority over Thunder is now yours.”
To my surprise, he even gave me Thunder.
I couldn’t believe it.
“So what you’re saying is... I just need this one thing to use Thunder?”
Contrary to the monstrous form I’d imagined, Thunder had no physical form.
“This is different from what I heard.”

“I don’t know what you’ve been told, but Thunder refers to the ancient magic circle laid beneath this city,” he explained. “With the proper authority and ammunition, anyone can use it. What you’ve heard about is most likely the extractor. Countless souls are required to fire Thunder even once.”
“How many times can I fire it now?”
“Five.”
Nothing staggering, but certainly nothing to scoff at either. One shot was powerful enough to destroy an entire palace, after all.
“However, Thunder cannot be used within the labyrinth. As I’ve told you, it is an ancient magic circle inscribed into the city’s foundation.”
“I see...”
“Oh, and one last thing.”
The marquess slowly lifted his arm, gazing at his hand as if reminiscing about something long past.
And then...
There was a shimmering light. When he closed his eyes and concentrated, a black ring appeared on his previously bare ring finger.
He stared at the ring for a long moment before taking it off and giving it to me.
“Take this as well. It is one of the treasures of the royal house.”
The words sparked a memory of a conversation I had with Baekho Lee.
“Even if I kill that bastard, he’s just going to revive in the palace.”
“Oh, right. I guess you didn’t know since it wasn’t in the game. Anyway, there’s a royal treasure that can revive you, and the marquess is currently holding onto it.”
So this was it.
“That’s quite valuable,” I mused. The marquess seemed surprised to hear it.
“You know what this is as well?”
“More or less. Doesn’t this revive you at the palace when you die? But only if you use it in the city.”
“So... You don’t know the full story of it.”
“Huh?”

“It is true that this ring allows its wearer to revive in the palace. However, it does not strictly require death as its trigger. Whether forced or intentional, when used, you are transported to a specific place within the palace. I have gone there only once before... However, it was a place that looked to contain some grand secret.”
A secret area...
Following my hunch, I told him about what we discovered beneath the palace, but the marquess shook his head.
“No, nothing like that. In any case, I have a feeling you may one day uncover its true purpose.”
“Maybe. No one knows what might happen.”
“Don’t wear it out and about. There will be people who recognize it.”
“Sure.”
I agreed with him on that point, so I stowed it away in my sub-space rather than put it on.
With that, our deal was done.
“Well then, I suggest you end it. You’ll find this head of mine will be important for your many goals ahead.”
The marquess closed his eyes, signaling his affairs had been settled.

His unnaturally composed demeanor stirred an odd feeling within me. I could have swung my hammer right then and there to end him, but instead, I asked, “Why are you giving me all this? Just a few days ago, you were fighting as hard as you could to live.”
“There is an order to everything. And I currently do not have a choice in the matter.”
Well, sure, but...
I exhaled softly, murmuring, “I won’t apologize.”

This man had sent me to Ice Rock, where countless lives that shouldn’t have been lost were taken. And that wasn’t enough for him—he had tried to kill me many times after, and even gotten Rotmiller killed in the process of one recent attempt.
“Neither will I.”
It was only natural. To him, evil spirits were loathsome creatures, more despicable than any other.

“Have you ever seen the mother of your child cry, begging to know why she had to give birth? Have you ever tied someone’s hands to stop them from striking their own swollen belly with clenched fists? Have you ever watched your son transform overnight into someone who only pretends to be the boy you love?”
I hadn’t...
And because I hadn’t, I couldn’t answer him.
No amount of reading one single diary of his would ever allow me to understand the depths of the marquess’s pain.
“An evil spirit like you,” he whispered, his voice thick with rage, “has no right to blame me.”
I couldn’t swallow the bitter laugh before it burst out of me.
“I don’t intend to.”
We were just on different sides.
There was a sharp, sickening crunch.
The marquess, lying atop the newly bloodied bed, drew his final breath.
I stood there for a moment, silently gazing down at the gruesome scene, repeatedly clenching and relaxing my hand holding the hammer.

For a long time now, I had thought that when this day finally came, I would feel exhilarated. But now that the moment I had been waiting for had come and gone, it felt less than exciting—disgusting, even.
Even so...
I slapped my cheeks with my palms to chase away the useless thoughts clouding my mind. There was no point in wasting time on such unproductive things. I just needed to do what I needed to do.
He’s lighter than I expected...
I lifted the limp body of the marquess and placed it into my sub-space.
I needed proof to show to the king.
I guess this is mission cleared...
Proof secured, I opened the door to leave the room only to be met with Glasses pacing the corridor. The moment he saw me, he rushed over.
“How did it go? Did you convince him to—”
He jolted back, flinching away from the bloody bed peeking through the gap in the door.
“Wh-what is that? Did you— Did you k-kill the marquess?” Glasses stuttered in shock.
I just patted him on the shoulder. “Don’t worry. I’ve received Thunder.”
“Well... That’s a relief,” he said, letting out a breath. Belatedly, he realized what I said and whipped around to stare at me with frazzled eyes. “Hmm? Received it?”
It was a frustrating response for a barbarian like myself. How couldn’t he understand something so simple?
“He gave me Thunder. What’s so hard to understand about that?”
I kindly explained it to him, but his reaction remained just as slow.
“Hand it over...”
His tone turned sharp as caution veiled his expression.
I couldn’t understand him at all.
“Give it to you? Why should I?”
Thunder was now mine.

chapters.title: Chapter 770: Setting Things Straight (5)
paragraphs: Unexpectedly, it didn’t take long for Glasses to come to terms with reality.
He took a single step back in fear, then met my gaze head-on.
“Baron Yandel...” he said, his voice heavy with warning. “You are making a grave mistake.”
Despite his genuine concern for me, the words sent me down memory lane.
Hmm, how many people have said those words to me so far?
“Do you have any idea how many soldiers are stationed in the vicinity? You’ll never make it out alive. If you were alone, perhaps it would be a different story, but with your allies here? Never.”

“Oh, I see,” I agreed with a nod. Then, my hand whipped out to squeeze his neck. I dragged him toward me and leaned in to get in his face. “And how many lives do you have to spare, thinking you can get away with threatening me like that?”
To be honest, I had been curious about it for some time now.
Was this guy not afraid of dying? If he really thought my allies were my weakness, then shouldn’t he have thought twice before poking at a potential trigger point like that?
“Hmm?” I hummed mockingly.
And why wasn’t he answering my question?
“Grgh... Grak!”
Oh, right. I was choking him.
I eased my grip just enough for him to speak. He coughed, sputtering in gasps of air, before he rushed out, “Wh-why are you doing this...?!”
“Huh?”
“We had an agreement! We would trade so that we both got what we wanted!”
Oh, that. True.
“But the situation’s changed,” I said, pointing out the obvious.
“What?”
“Oh, yeah. Sorry for not being able to keep my promise! I apologize—truly.”
Since I was the one who went against the promise, I offered him. an apology as recompense.
Somehow, though, he didn’t seem to take my heartfelt words to heart.
“You... You apologize? Do you think an apology will be enough?” he snapped.
His response had me tilting my big barbarian head. “Hmm? What do you mean? If apologies aren’t enough, what’s the point of them?”
“Huh?”
“I did something wrong, and I apologized for it. Isn’t that enough?”
“Wh-what kind of sophistry is that?!” Glasses shouted in frustration.
“Sophistry...” As a barbarian with a big heart, I decided to let his outburst slide with a small piece of advice. “Don’t use difficult words. It makes you look weak.”
No response.
“Anyway, I’ve apologized.”
Although the situation seemed plenty enough resolved to me, Glasses had apparently been struck by inspiration. He pulled out a different argument.
“If apologies are enough, why are there laws and prisons?!”
Oh, he was pretty sharp. Still, he chose the wrong opponent for this match.
“That’s why barbarians don’t like laws and prisons.” When bafflement shut Glasses right up, I gently pried the conversational reins back from his defiant hands. “That’s the end of our talk, then.”
Really, now. Conversations steeped in angry grudges and blame were far less productive than focusing on talks of joyful cooperation in the future.
So with that...
“Call all the soldiers nearby,” I ordered.
“Have you absolutely lost your mind? You’ve gone against our deal, and now you’re trying to make us—”
“If you don’t, I’ll rain Thunder on your office building in District.”
The moment I expressed my peace-loving, Korean barbarian resolve for peace, Glasses went deathly pale. The castellan of Noark was at the building in District 4, of course.
I was a bit worried but looks like he’s still there.

It had been a few days since I’d gotten that intel from the prime minister’s son, so I was worried he might have moved elsewhere. However, judging by the look on Glasses’s face, there was no need to move to Plan B.
“Well, it’s your call,” I said.
“G-give me a moment to talk with—”
“Nope.”
Glasses gritted his teeth at my firm interruption. “How could you force me to make such a big decision on my own?”
“You said you’ve worked with the castellan for a long time. Can’t you predict what decision he would make in a situation like this? You do it.”
He was in a predicament. On the one hand, he needed to retaliate against me for breaking the promise, but the castellan could die in the process if he did.
I wasn’t too worried, though. This guy was so loyal to the castellan that he brought up my allies to my face.
If he just so happened to be given an out, a chance to avoid responsibility by saying it was all to save the castellan’s life... And survive in the process as well?
It’ll be stranger if he didn’t take this chance.
