Regardless of his true desires, as long as the path was presented to him, he’d be a fool not to consider it at least once.

“Decide quickly. I’ve already apologized for breaking our one little promise. Decide if you want to shed blood over it or if we will part ways without any problems.” When he still didn’t respond, I added, “Believe me or don’t, but I swear I won’t fire it on you or Noark.”
“Not fire it at us...? Lord Baron, are you perhaps—?!”
“Shh. Enough words. So, your answer?”
Despite my urging, Glasses still hesitated. However, he only needed a moment longer before he gave me his answer.
“I refuse.”
He... What?
“Don’t take me for a fool, Baron Yandel.”
Before I could respond, the alarms stationed across the building began to blare.
Riiing! Riiing! Riiing!
From what I could tell, it seemed he pressed a hidden button of some kind.
“This is our way. We’d rather destroy it all than see it be taken from us.”
Clearly, I had underestimated the mindset of the Noarkans.
I sighed. With how much his appearance screamed intellect-heavy character model, I thought he’d come to a logical conclusion in the end.
“I didn’t expect you to bite the bullet like this...” I muttered under my breath. Still, even though I was admittedly a bit impressed, my hands continued their work.
“I’ll say this one more time. Don’t just take others for fools without—”
“Shut up. Die.”
Crunch!
After swiftly smashing his head in with my hammer, I headed toward the room where my allies were waiting.
Or at least, I tried to.
Where are they, anyway?
Standing there in the middle of the corridor blaring with alarms, I only had to wonder for a moment where to go.
“Yandel!”
The room at the end of the corridor burst open, and Amelia stepped out with the rest of the group. They must have rushed out after hearing the alarms go off.
“What’s going on?” Amelia asked.
I let out a sigh. Really, luck was never on my side.
“Things got a bit complicated.”
It was time for Plan B.
Plan A was simple: threaten the castellan by telling him I’d fire Thunder at him and escape with the group.
It was simple, peaceful, and didn’t require any violence.
Tsk, this is why you can’t do any business with thugs.
I’d underestimated the Noarkan mindset, and that plan fell apart.
With that, it was time for Plan B.
Surprisingly enough, Plan B was even simpler than Plan A: use Thunder.
Just those two words.
But how do I use it? Oh, is it like— Whoa, what the hell?
The moment I decided to use Thunder, it felt as if my soul had been yanked from my body and my vision soared upward, shooting past the ceiling and all objects in the way.
Vwoong!
When I came to my senses, I was in the sky looking down at the entirety of the city. It was a breathtaking spectacle, beyond anything I could experience looking down from the tall city walls.
Still, I didn’t have time to just look around in awe.
I turned my head and looked back at the building that I was in.
I could see a sea of Noarkan soldiers mobilized by Glasses surrounding the building. Even up this high, I could see the sheer number of them.
Firing it directly at the building would probably put me in danger too...
I adjusted my aim to a spot just a short distance away.
Do I just need to think it? Mentally say, “fire”?
The moment I thought it, I felt some unknown mass of energy that I couldn’t pinpoint shift away from me and aim.
Shwoong!
As if a rocket was fired from the building I was in, something huge shot into the sky.
That was the last thing I saw from my ghostly state.
“Whoa, what? What did you just do?”
I returned to my normal vision, dazed as if I’d just awoken from a dream.
My mind felt numb for a second, but I quickly regained my focus and tried to assess the situation.
“Ohhh! Something huge just erupted above Bjorn’s head!”
Oh, so I did fire it. It didn’t feel real to me after having seen that bird’s eye view before.
However, regardless of how I felt, we didn’t have time. Thunder would soon fall on this place.
“There...!”
Noarkan soldiers appeared from the stairwell. It seemed they all immediately ran over here after the alarm was raised.
Look at that excellent equipment.
There was a reason Glasses was so confident that he could at least take my allies with him.
Not that he was right, of course.
I looked at the approaching soldiers and raised my hammer.
“Grab my body! Emily, take Ragna. Ainar, take Harin!”
Once they were hovering close to my enlarged Giantization body, I smashed through the ground with my enlarged hammer.
Boom!
Someone screamed, and the floor made from stone and rebar crumbled away without resistance, allowing us to drop to the floor before.
Is this the third floor?
Of course, I had no intention of stopping there.
I recalled the 2D digging games I played in the past and continued to strike the ground—top to bottom as if using a pickaxe.
“What! Are! You! Doing!”
Boom!
Second floor.
“What is... Eiyaaah!”
Boom!
First floor.
We arrived at floor one, which happened to possess a vaulted ceiling, but I continued to dig into the ground.
With how many floors above this building had, there had to be a basement, right?
“Wow! A basement! We’re in the basement!”
Boom!
“Wait! Please at least tell me what you’re—!”
Boom!
And so we drilled through the first basement floor to the second one below.
I hammered once more, but my hammer left only a heavy dent in the floor, which didn’t collapse. Nevertheless, I continued to slam my hammer down to dig a hole.
Alright, this should be enough for everyone to fit.
The moment I decided there was enough room, I grabbed my allies and shoved them into the hole.
Then, with a heavy thud, I finished the underground bunker by putting the giant barbarian over it as the lid.
“Looks like I made it just in time.”
“Just what is going on?! Can’t you at least tell us now?” Hyeonbyeol shrieked from below where I was lying.
There was only one thing I could say in return.
“Please survive.”
Any second now, it would drop.
A deafening roar erupted, accompanied by the once-unyielding earth quivering in bouncing waves like jelly.
If the bedrock was moving like this, there was no way that the world above was safe.
KaBoom! Crash! Bang!
Chunks of debris from the collapsing building rained down, battering my back.
That much, I could handle.
The problem came after.
A blinding light flared, so intense it pierced through all the rubble on my back and sent searing pain over my entire body. It was so hot that I wondered if the ones I was covering were safe.
Fortunately, it didn’t last long.
It’s this intense when I’m two floors underground...
If I hadn’t fired it a bit away from us, it could have been a huge problem.
Right. I should check on them first.
The air was stiflingly hot, like I’d just stepped into a sauna, but it wasn’t so hot that it was a danger to their lives. I forced myself to focus and checked on my allies.
“Is everyone alright?”
“We should be asking you that,” came Amelia’s immediate reply. “Are you... Are you alright?”
“Feels like I broke a vertebra or two, but I’m fine. This much should heal soon enough. Answer my question now.”
“We’re fine... Harin Savy had a pretty good defense scroll.”
“Okay, but seriously, what even happened just now?!”
I sighed. She was persistent, alright. Why was that even important at this point?
“Nothing much. Just sit tight so I can think for a bit.”
Hyeonbyeol grumbled something under her breath, but I just ignored her and began to think.
We can use diving scrolls or a rotation of magic tools to deal with the oxygen problem...

It might take some time, but we could escape after slowly removing the rubble piece by piece. After that, I just needed to run through the city into Karnon, then show the body of the marquess to Astarota. That would be mission accomplished.
I’m nearly there...
My mind was telling me that this event was soon coming to an end, but a mysterious sense of uneasiness coiled around my heart.
Ba-dump!
Please, let nothing bad happen.

chapters.title: Chapter 771: Setting Things Straight (6)
paragraphs: In Greek mythology, there was a figure named Atlas.
When Zeus was warring against the Titans, Atlas fought against him and subsequently was on the losing side of the war, after which he was punished to forever hold up the sky for his offense.
He was a pretty simple man, all things considered.
But that wasn’t the point.
The reason I suddenly thought not about Korea, but the story of a bygone, foreign Greece was singlefold: I was in the same position as him.
I lowered my knee and bent my hips, then stretched my arms out to the side to hold up the heavy rubble on my back.
It was a pretty sad state of affairs, though I certainly hadn’t started like this.
Damn it.

Time passed quickly after testing out the effect of the marquess’s final gift to me, Thunder. Having multiple adults stuck in the same tiny hole in the ground was driving me up the wall, but thanks to the adventuring gear that Amelia always had on her, breathing wasn’t a problem.
Well, since they were all consumables, we did have a time limit. The real problem, however, was the falling debris.
The fifth to second basement floors of a building that fell squarely in the “large” category had all collapsed on top of me.
On the bright side, thanks to this debris, we were able to minimize the damage we took from Thunder.
But why is it so heavy?

Even after using Giantization and other similar skills in succession to boost my strength to the max, it wasn’t easy to hold the weight up. The rubble barely moved even when I used all my strength to push.
It might have been fine if there were space to move the rubble to the side piece by piece, but there wasn’t anything like that in this deep hole.
Still, I couldn’t just stand around doing nothing.
I tried lifting the rubble and even managed to clear some small fragments out of the massive pile. And as a result of those attempts...
I should’ve just stayed still.
The rubble collapsed even further.
If I moved even a little bit or let my arms drop, the pile would collapse and it would all be over.
“Bjorn! Are you alright? Y-you don’t look too good...” Ainar noted worriedly. “I’ll help!”
“I’m fine, so stop shouting. It’s hurting my head.”

I acted strong in front of my allies, but in truth, I thought I was going to die. The weight made me worry that another part of my spine would pop with how heavy it was. I also wanted to rest, just a little...
“Ainar, come here and scratch me. It’s itchy.”
And since I couldn’t use my arms, I couldn’t scratch myself and needed to ask one of my allies.
“No, a little higher...”
“Eugh... Your armpit? I don’t want to! It’s going to smell!”
Oh, what the hell?
“Uh... If you can’t, I guess I can?” she immediately backpedaled after noticing my mood.
“No, I’ll do it. Move, Ainar Fenelin.”
I sighed.
Please don’t make that face. I’m also embarrassed here.
Also, Ainar was the one I asked to scratch me, so why was Amelia scratching me instead? Though... She did get rid of the itch.
How did this end up like this?
Thinking back on it now, the biggest problem was my complacency.
Thunder would explode, we would hide underground, and when all was said and done, I would push the debris away and head to the imperial palace.
I just assumed everything would fall into place and happen in that order.
After all, not once had I ever felt lacking in the “strength” department. Even if a building were to collapse on me, the thought that it would be too heavy to push away never crossed my mind.
“This is no joke,” Amelia said grimly. “Even Yandel will run out of strength at some point.”
“If we don’t want to get crushed to death here, we’ll need to think of another way out before that happens.”
“Harin Savy, do you have any ideas?”
“No, not really...”

While I held up the rubble, my allies looked for an answer to our problem, though the exercise ultimately proved meaningless. Not that they failed to come up with an answer or anything. Rather, the answer came to us suddenly and unexpectedly from an external source.

“Wait. Everyone, be quiet,” I said, cutting off their brainstorming session. When I focused my hearing—really, all of my senses—I felt something faint. At first, I thought I was imagining it due to being under great stress...
“I’m sure of it. It’s getting lighter.”
Slight tremors rocked the pile above me, and every time they did, the weight of the debris I was holding lightened.
“Wow! Is it a rescue squad?”
“It could be the opposite. District 4 is under Noarkan control.”

As Hyeonbyeol and Amelia said, there were two possibilities. From what I could tell, Amelia’s scenario seemed more probable, but either way, it was a fortunate turn of events for us. Fighting Noarkans was hundreds and thousands of times better than just being stuck here.

I huffed out a breath. There was some relief there, but my nerves started to kick in too. I didn’t know what happened to the other allies I was separated from. I had only confirmed the death of one person: Rotmiller.
Two more...

There were still two more people left to die if what was written on the Records Stone was to be fulfilled. I couldn’t help but worry that maybe one of the people here would die in the process of getting out of this predicament.
“I think it’s light enough to lift now,” I told everyone.
I waited for the right time to push up, and when the moment came, I pushed the debris with all my might.
Boom!
Slowly but surely, my arms felt lighter until the debris suddenly shot upward as if a dam had broken.
The sun shining down on us was so bright that it made me squint, but the warmth was too good to pass up. However, I didn’t have time to bask in the rays of sunshine.
“Now!”
I scrambled to the surface, and my allies followed me and took their battle positions next to me. However, it didn’t take long for us to realize we were worried for nothing.
The soldiers moving the rubble looked at me and shouted with joy.
“Baron Yandel! It’s Baron Yandel!”
Palatial soldiers?

We rode in a huge military carriage large enough to fit more than twelve people if the space was used efficiently. It certainly lived up to its name as a military carriage—as in, built for function, not comfort—but I wasn’t going to be the one to fuss about that. I was just thankful I could return to the palace without having to fight my way there.
“If you would allow me to repeat myself, I have always respected and admired you, Lord Baron,” said a thin knight seated beside me. “It is an honor to be able to meet you in person.”
The knight’s name was Danez Akel Gyre. Although I had never seen him before, he had repeated this introduction so many times as if to inscribe it in my mind that I ended up remembering his name.
“Truly amazing. From what the soldiers say, even the remaining rubble that you pushed up when you escaped was at least a few tons!”
While he was a palatial knight from the House of Baron Gyre, his persistent flattery of me made me think he was more suited to politics than the knighthood.
Not to say I was looking down on him. No matter the organization, it all came down to politics in the end. One needed to do things they didn’t want to if they wanted to climb the ladder.
Also, this skinny guy was a pretty good conversation partner when he wasn’t trying to suck up to me. As a commander in the army, he had plenty of information on the latest happenings around the city.
“So the royal soldiers have reclaimed over half of District 4?”

“Yes. A battle line is being held with the Square as the boundary. Upon receiving intelligence of your last known location, I, Danez Akel Gyre, came personally to see to it that you were found. I never doubted for a second that even under such dire circumstances, you would survive and—”
“And you personally went and got approval from the commander to come with a unit to clear out the debris?”
“Yes. That’s precisely it, Lord Baron.”
Was he descended from a parrot or something? For some reason, he repeated the same things whenever he was given the chance.
Still, we did live in an age where one needed to sell themselves to get ahead.
“Ah, we’re finally on the imperial road. It seems there’s a checkpoint, but please do not worry. I will deal with it in your stead.”
And so, the military carriage finally trundled into the imperial capital, where we moved into a different carriage.
“Unfortunately, I, Danez Akel Gyre, have other missions to attend to, so I won’t be able to accompany you all the way to the imperial capital. Please forgive me.”
The skinny, sycophant knight who spent his first to his final moments sucking up to me sent me regretful glances over his shoulder before he finally turned and marched back toward District 4.
We then headed toward the palace on our new carriage. As I looked out of the window at the imperial road we were traveling on, an odd feeling swelled within me.
No, to be precise, it was a sense of emptiness.
Is this...really over? Just like that?
I couldn’t believe it. After being trapped under the rubble, I was even prepared to have a final showdown against the Noarkans. Yet everything ended just like that?
Don’t let your guard down... It’s not over until it’s over.
With that, I resumed the information gathering that I had paused, but the knight that was in this carriage was of a completely different type than that skinny guy from before.
He really didn’t talk at all.
“Which squad are you from?”
“I serve His Majesty.”

So he was a Guardian. That was why he wasn’t talking much. He didn’t need to curry favor with me. I tried to ask the knight a few questions to get some answers while we were on the road, but he only answered with this:
“We are currently heading to see Commander Berun. Please hold onto your questions and ask him when you two meet.”
The carriage traveled on and finally entered the palace.
“Let us depart.”
Then, we finally arrived at the Palace of the New World. Unfortunately, our group was split by the Order of the Guardians as soon as we entered.
“Only Baron Yandel was summoned by the commander. The others will be guided to the guest room.”
Since I had predicted it would happen, I just signaled to Amelia with my eyes that it was fine, and we went our separate ways.
“It’s been a while, Bjorn Yandel.”
A little while later, as I opened the door and entered the room, Astarota greeted me. As he said, we really hadn’t seen each other for a long time.
When the knight who guided me here left the room and closed the door, I took out the marquess’s corpse from my sub-space.
“Now there are only three left.”
At that, Astarota tilted his head. “Three left? Ah, you mean the deal you had with His Majesty?”
“What else?”
“I would argue your count is off. The first condition was for you to stay seven days, but you ran off before that happened. Under the condition that you killed the prime minister.”
Tsk, I suppose that could be seen like that. It was a decent attempt.
“So there are four left, Yandel. Understood?”
“I get it. No need to get all stiff on me,” I grumbled.
Astarota smirked, then changed the subject. “So... What exactly happened?”
“There are things that even you don’t know, huh?”
“Most of what I know is procured by the Department of Intelligence. And the Department of Intelligence isn’t omniscient. Even more so in times like this.”
Okay, so if I wanted to beat the palace, I needed to mess up their information network first. The marquess did say he blocked their eyes first when he began this war.
“Tell me, what happened there?”
I summarized only the most important parts to answer Astarota’s question.

I went to save Ainar, and there, I met the son of the marquess who betrayed him. We allied, fought against Demon Eyes, went to the marquess’s secret garden, and met Glasses there. In the end, I tricked Glasses to meet back up with the marquess.
I told him all the truths I could afford to tell him. The best place to hide a lie was in between truths, after all.
“While we were talking, having nothing else left to lose, the marquess fired Thunder and we went and hid underground.”
I needed to hide the deal I made with the marquess. It was already too late to hide Ragna—she had been exposed while we were escaping.
“Oh? And then?” Astarota prompted.
“That’s it. You should know what happened after that.”
“Hmm, I see...” Astarota put his hand on his chin in mock deliberation before saying, “Then Thunder thankfully didn’t go over to the Noarkans. If what you’re saying is true.”
He added that to sound out my true intentions. Knowing that, I simply gave him a nod and continued on to the next topic.
“More importantly, I have something I want to ask you.”
“Go on.”
With his permission granted, my heart felt like it was being squeezed.

Before I killed the marquess, I took a hit of Thunder right on my head, and all my allies were scattered throughout the city. A few of them landed in the safe regions controlled by the palace, but more than a couple had landed in dangerous grounds like how Ainar fell into the middle of District 4.
“Have you been able to confirm the status of all the people who got swept up in that teleportation?” I asked carefully.
Astrarota calmly nodded. “Ah, yes. That was completed some time ago.”
A wave of some unnamable emotion swept over me.
Okay, so we know what happened to everyone...
Since only Rotmiller had died among people near me, I really didn’t want to hear what Astarota would say next. However, denying reality wasn’t going to change anything.
I took a deep breath.
“Are you ready to listen?” he asked.
“Yeah, tell me.”
Tell me who lived. And who died.

chapters.title: Chapter 772: Setting Things Straight (7)
paragraphs: “Showing you will be faster than explaining it all,” Astarota said, producing a stack of documents to hand to me.
It was a pretty big stack, and honestly, I wasn’t all that surprised. There were nearly a thousand people around me when Thunder fell on us.
It’s pretty straightforward...
The document, clearly sourced from the palace’s Department of Intelligence, was impeccably organized, pristine from its formatting down to its style.
No. 1: Kyeldun Nilteon
Status: Deceased
Note: Body unable to be retrieved, but credible eyewitness testimony confirms death.
Each entry contained a name, status, and a short note related to the subject. For those marked “deceased,” the word was written in red pen so it was easy to skim through the document.
Although, just because the document was neat didn’t make it any less nerve-wracking for the person reading it.
No. 17: Anthony Bolton
Status: Deceased
Note: Body stored in the 7th mortuary. Belongings in the custody of a clan member.
I sighed. This person seemed to be a member of one of the medium-sized clans that left the holy land with us.
No. 19: Gelta Panun
Status: Deceased
Note: Body unable to be retrieved, but credible eyewitness testimony confirms death.
My heart sank every time I saw a name of someone that I didn’t just know, but had seen multiple times before, and yet...

My knuckles cracked as I clenched my fist. The people listed were under my responsibility, objectively speaking. But I had to acknowledge that these people weren’t the allies written about on the Records Stone.
I continued to read through the document.
“Wait, what’s this?” I said. “It says ‘missing’ on the status section.”
“It’s just as the word means?”
“Didn’t you say that you’ve gotten information on everyone?”

“The fact that the Department of Intelligence still hasn’t been able to confirm their status means they’re assumed deceased. It just says they’re missing because their body hasn’t been recovered or someone hasn’t seen them yet. And I’m pretty sure these aren’t the people you’re interested in.”
I couldn’t argue with that.
Since it was undeniable, I went back to reading through the document. Soon enough, I found the names I truly wanted to confirm.
No. 119: Sven Parav
Status: Alive
Note: Currently conscripted into the Seventh Corps. Stationed at Fourth Wall occupation forces.

I sighed. He survived. I was really worried because I heard he went missing during the initial skirmish. Still, with that impressive intuition of his, it would have been more surprising to see him dead just because a war occurred.

I asked the question that popped into my mind after reading the notes. “Are you involved with him being transferred to the Fourth Wall?” The unspoken implication being that the Fourth Wall occupation forces were stationed on the wall that was in contact with Gnome Tree. They were only deployed by technicality and were practically just on standby.
“Naturally,” Astarota confirmed. “Do you know how many people want to be deployed to that unit? I’ve transferred the others there as well, so they should be having a swell time together.”
“I see... Thank you.”
At my genuine show of gratitude, Astarota’s face scrunched in a weird expression that was difficult to parse.
Huh. Was he...embarrassed?
Well, now I was embarrassed too.
“Is it because you have a pretty name? You’re meticulous.”
Astarota clicked his tongue in disgust at the joke. With the mood successfully lightened, I went back to reading through the documents.
No. 170: Melend Kaislan
Alive.
No. 242: Lilith Marrone
Alive.
No. 310: Ainar Fenelin
Since she had just arrived at the imperial capital, the document listed her as missing. I knew she was actually alive, of course, so I just passed through the names of the people who were with me.
No. 381: Versyl Gowland
Alive.
No. 404: James Calla
He was dropped into the middle of the battlefield, had his arm cut off, and due to measures taken too late, he wouldn’t be able to get his arm back...
But he was alive.

My jaw clenched without me realizing it. There were two people I still had left to confirm: Erwen and Missha. The allies who had been with me from the beginning when I was just a random, boring old barbarian.
The tips of my fingers began to tremble slightly as I quickly turned the page.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, ba-dump...
No matter how I tried to calm my breathing, my heart raced in my chest.
No. 606: Missha Karlstein
The moment I saw the name I was looking for, my breath hitched for a second. And when I read the letters written in black ink below her name, I let out a deep breath that I had been holding.
Alive.
She was alive.
However, that moment of relief was too short. I quickly scanned through the lists and flipped through multiple pages, checking for the final name I needed to see.
There.
No. 777: Erwen Fornacci di Tersia
Status: Alive
Note: Currently conscripted into the Seventh Corps. Stationed at Fourth Wall occupation forces.
The moment I confirmed her status, it felt like all the strength in my body left me instantly.
She was alive. No one had died.
“Why are you making that face?” Astarota asked curiously. “Everyone’s alive.”
Despite my elation, I couldn’t smile. The main question at hand wouldn’t leave me.
Just how...?
How was everyone alive? Was what I saw on the Records Stone wrong, or did I perhaps misinterpret it?

There was no telling. However, that was why an even darker, more inexplicable fear began to creep up within me, slithering through me like smoke. But then, slowly, the fear clouding my thoughts began to take shape, molded by the weight of experiences in my subconscious mind.
Maybe it’s still...
Maybe everything wasn’t over yet?
Knock, knock, knock.
The sound of knocks rapping at the door snuffed out the thought as soon as it flared within me. The knight from the Order of Guardians who had guided me here entered the room.
There was no proof nor any evidence. However, a person’s sixth sense had a mysterious quality to it. The moment I saw the face of that knight, a choking dread took hold.
“What is it?” I croaked.
That damning instinct was right once more.
“There’s been an incident at the Fourth Wall,” the knight said.
“What sort of incident?”
“Well, Your Lordship... It’s...”
“Baron Yandel is fine,” I pressed. “Just give your report.”
The quiet member glanced at me even when permission was granted before carefully speaking.
“Two members of the Anabada Clan have died.”
Damn it.
When I came to, I was sprinting down the main street of the Imperial Capital Karnon. I was even using the abilities that were forbidden to use within the capital.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
I ran, and I ran.
When I reached the western wall of Karnon bordering Noarkan territory, a knight who seemed to be in charge of the area approached me.
“I was informed of your arrival. Come this way.”
Since I ran off on my own, it seemed Astarota had sent advance notice to the people here.
“Run.”
“Pardon?”
“Don’t walk,” I commanded. “Run.”
The knight’s dawdling and hesitating irritated me. Immediately understanding the underlying intention, he jumped from a walk straight into a run.
Following the knight led me to arrive at a tent, where I saw my allies gathered at its entrance.
“Yandel...?”
Melend Kaislan.
“B-Bjorn?!”
A surprised Missha.
“M-Mister!”
Erwen, Sven Parav, and others...

They all looked conflicted, wanting to run up to me in joy, yet an awkward stiffness stopped them from approaching. Their mouths were pressed into thin, grim lines, and their eyes didn’t know where to look.
“Could you move for a moment?” I asked, stamping down the emotion rising in my throat. My allies wordlessly stepped to the side.
“Lord B-Baron! We’re still conducting our initial investigation—”
What the hell is this guy talking about?
I shoved the knight in my way aside without a second thought and entered the tent.
The interior of the tent was as messy as a crime scene, and there were two mobile beds at the entrance. Each bed had a person on it whose entire body was covered by a long piece of white cloth.
“It’s the baron. Everyone, it’s fine, so could you all pause your investigation and leave for a moment?”
The surprised investigators heeded the instructions of the knight and slowly filed out of the tent.
I rushed forward and pulled back the cloth on the left bed. Although I only moved the cloth away from the top half of the body, the state of the body beneath was horrific.

One arm had clearly been torn away from its socket and crudely healed back in place. The neck was mangled, leaving the head barely attached, if that. It was as if the body had been reconstructed like a mini figure.
“James Calla...”
He joined my clan after we survived the Ice Rock Expedition. Although the time we spent together was short compared to my earliest allies, everyone liked him thanks to his affable personality.
I was no exception.
Silently, I placed the cloth back over his body and turned to the body next to his.
This time, I moved slowly, almost hesitantly, as I uncovered the second body. Her skin was pale and lifeless, but I had no trouble recognizing that face.
“Versyl Gowland...”
We had first crossed paths at the Round Table, each wearing masks to conceal our faces. Over time, our relationship had somehow progressed to the point where she joined my clan.
Being from Earth and boasting an excellent work ethic, she had been the ally I relied on the most after Amelia when it came to operating the clan.
That was why I gave her the position of vice captain when I had to leave.
For a long while, I stared at her face. Then gently, I placed the cloth back over her head.
The knight apparently took that action as his cue to speak after having stood there in awkward silence.

“We suspect this to be the work of a master assassin. When we first found Sir James Calla, he was laying on his bed, and seeing as how there was no injury other than blood loss and the cut on his neck, we suspect he was killed in his sleep.”
An assassination...
I couldn’t even laugh at the absurdity of it.
Fuck, are you joking? I thought dying in battle was the only possibility for this war. But this?
I never expected an end like this for anyone.
“And what about Versyl Gowland?”

“The opinions of the investigators are still split. The investigation hasn’t concluded yet, but... The most probable cause seems to be that the assassin initially aimed for James Calla and Ms. Gowland was swept up in it after unfortunately witnessing the act.”
“Swept up?”

“Yes. The first piece of evidence we have is that the scene of the crime was inside James Calla’s tent, and the second is that Ms. Gowland’s body was discovered near the entrance. The final piece is the signs of struggle found inside the tent and on Ms. Gowland’s body.”
“Anything else I should know?”
“Well, the investigation hasn’t concluded yet...”
“You don’t have to be sure of it, so just tell me everything you’ve found. If you need, you can call in the investigators that were sent out.”
The knight seemed to sense just how serious I was from my tone of voice, as he immediately took up my request.
I stayed on the scene and was briefed on every piece of evidence and every item found on site, the analysis of suspected steps the assassin took, and more.
“That’s enough. You can go back to your work.”
I then left the tent and headed toward the wall. The allies waiting at the front of the tent asked me where I was going, but I just gave an excuse about taking a look around the area.
What I really needed was time alone.
Wandering along the wall, I climbed to the rooftop of a decently tall building and just laid flat on my back while looking up at the sky.

Even though I wasn’t doing anything, time continued to pass and the color of the sky slowly changed. It started from a dull grey that momentarily became blue as the clouds parted, back to yellow during the evening, which then turned red...
Finally, as the sky turned jet-black with the night, a familiar voice broke the silence.
“Bro, have you eaten yet?”
There was no need to wonder who it was.
Sitting up, I turned to face him, greeting him with a cold stare rather than a warm welcome.
“Whoa, you’re not surprised?”
I had a feeling he’d show up if I waited here long enough.
Especially with your personality.
I stared at him silently, and he returned my gaze with equal quiet.
Baekho Lee.
To be honest, I had thought long and hard about what to do with this guy.

Although I knew the risk he presented to me, he was as useful as he was dangerous. In truth, I was able to take another step toward the secret of this world thanks to him, and thinking back on it, it was thanks to him that I was able to enter the Round Table as well.

That was why I treated him on a case-by-case basis rather than dealing with him on the whole. He had things he wanted from me too, and I genuinely believed that he wouldn’t cross the line. I figured that if he didn’t mess with me first, I wouldn’t need to mess with him either.
I guess that was my mistake.
After a prolonged silence, I finally spoke.
“Why did you kill them?”
We both knew what I meant.
For a moment, he seemed to debate the answer before a grin split his face.
That smile told me exactly how I needed to see him going forward.
“So you noticed.”
He was my enemy.
The enemy I needed to eliminate above all else.

chapters.title: Chapter 773: Setting Things Straight (8)
paragraphs: Baekho’s answer was different from what I expected.
The scenario in which he openly admitted to it wasn’t even a thought in my mind. I thought he would try to make excuses for himself.
But then again, is it really all that surprising?
Maybe things would be different if Baekho had never shown himself at all, but the fact he came of his own volition meant that he knew I suspected him.
Still, he hadn’t been entirely sure, so he came over to confirm it. That was just the type of person he was.
“I’ll ask you one last time.” I fought back the impulse to bash his skull in right then and there and asked, “Why did you kill them?”
Even though I was certain Baekho was the culprit, I had no clue what his motive was.
Why did Baekho Lee harm my allies?
The truth that spilled from his mouth was unbelievable.
“You really don’t know?”
“I don’t have time for games. Answer me.”
“You gotta know, don’t you? Everything I’ve done is all for you, big bro.”
It was unthinkable.
“Are you saying,” I began, suppressing the fury boiling deep within, “that you killed them for me?”
Baekho merely nodded, nonchalant as ever.

“By sheer coincidence, I heard about what was on those Records Stones. That you’ll realize the path you need to take after losing three of your allies? But you know, if you think about it another way, three people need to die. For you to realize the true path you need to take.”
Fuck...
“Is that why...? You killed them for that? Because the war only killed one of them?”
“Hmm? Oh, no. That’s not really it,” Baekho denied unexpectedly, shaking his head. “The Records said three people would die. So even if I did nothing, three people would’ve died regardless, right?”
“Then why—”

“James Calla,” he interrupted. “That guy got done in pretty so badly by a dark wizard that even a saint wouldn’t be able to heal his arm. That’s why I killed him. If three people need to die anyway, then wouldn’t it be best if the one who would be the least helpful to you died?”
“But I never expected that woman to show up. I mean, seriously. Why was she even there, and at that time too? Were the two of them, well, you know? Involved or something?”

“Man... Doesn’t matter what it was—that woman ruined everything. You figured it out because of her, right? Since I put that huge hole in her stomach. We spent all that time together outside the city walls, so I just knew you would recognize it. Agh, and I really wanted to clean everything up before leaving. But she just had to go and scream before she died, and I had to jet before I could finish it off.

“Anyway, I am sorry that things turned out like this. I did it out of the goodness of my heart—didn’t have a clue it would end up this way, okay? When I was killing her, I caught myself too. I only need to kill James Calla, I realized, ‘cause if I just did that, the other one would die in an accident or whatever. But it was fate that the third person died here, I guess... Eugh, seriously, this is so unfair—”
Baekho’s self-pity finally pushed me over the edge.
Boom!
The hammer rocketing toward his head struck the roof instead.
“Whoa... You’re really mad, huh, bro?”
I didn’t answer him.
“Conversations” were had between human beings. This guy was just a beast that I needed to put down.
Vwoong!
I swung the hammer again, but Baekho swiftly leaped high and landed in mid-air.
“Bro, let me ask you one last thing... Aw, come on. Don’t be like that, please. ‘Kay? Just answer me this: Can we... Do you think we can ever let bygones be bygones here? Make peace?”
I stared at him in disbelief. “Make peace?”
He wasn’t asking for forgiveness but peace? He had to be messing with me.
“Yeah. I mean, we’re still both Korean in the end. Maybe you could find it in that big heart of yours to overlook this one little thing—”
I lunged, swinging upward with my hammer, and he jumped higher once more before letting out a big sigh.

“Man... The world really is cruel to the unfortunate. And looks like I’m the unlucky one. Well, whatever. I’ve been looking into this new possibility I found... Oh, I guess you wouldn’t know about it?
“To be real with you, I thought you were the main character of this story this whole time... But now? I’m not so sure about that.”
With the moon shining behind his back, Baekho Lee looked down at me and spoke.
“Since it’s come to this, I’ve decided. Today, I quit. I’m done being the rival who makes the protagonist shine. And honestly? It’s been a drag.”
I couldn’t understand the whole of what Baekho was rambling on about, but one thing was abundantly clear.
[——— has cast Stellar Extinction.]
Our relationship could never go back to what it was.
When I opened my eyes, the memory of a blinding flash still burned into my mind. I was lying in the middle of a huge crater.
Baekho had already disappeared, and all that was left to me was the commotion of soldiers running over and peering over the crater’s edge.
I let out a long sigh and stood.
Argh, that hurt...
My entire body ached. What a cheat skill. With how good my build was, it shouldn’t have been possible to reduce me to this state from a base attack of a single essence.
“L-Lord Baron? Are y-you alright?” one knight called.
“What happened here...?” came another voice.
In any case, after regaining my senses, I informed the site commander that I had been ambushed, and after telling him the absurd story, I was able to return to the arms of my allies.

Amelia had rejoined us by the time I got back, even though I’d left her behind at the royal palace. Astarota had apparently stopped her and the others from leaving, then allowed Amelia, Ainar, and Auyen to come here.
“Baekho Lee is the assassin?”

The revelation that Baekho was the one who assassinated James Calla and Versyl Gowland left Amelia visibly shaken. It was the first time I’d seen her like that in a long while. When I told her that he had also attacked me, her expression grew dark with concern.
“We’ve made a dangerous enemy.”
I understood Amelia’s worry, but there was one thing I needed to amend.
“He’s not a new enemy. I was just too blind to realize it earlier.”
Baekho Lee had only ever intended to use me as a tool from the very beginning.
Sure, I’d seen some use in him, and that was why we had remained on tenuously good terms for so long.
But it was clear now. The thing I needed to do was formulate a realistic plan to deal with him.
“We don’t know what Baekho will do next, so we need to keep each other safe,” I concluded.
“Understood. Once our business here is done, we’ll need to look for a residence. One that will be difficult for our enemies to infiltrate.”
“We should. We don’t know when or how he’ll try to attack us.”
However, since there was nothing we could do to plan ahead when we didn’t even know when or what he would do, that discussion didn’t last long.
“So... Are those three still at the palace?” I asked.
“They are figures of political import. Oh, and just so you know, Harin Savy wished to be imprisoned. She said she’d need to stay by Countess Peprok’s side in case she woke up.”
“I see...”
I could understand Astarota’s perspective. There was no way he could let loose Eltora, the son of the traitor, and Ragna, the blood of the king, out into the world, not with things as they were.
I’ll need to talk to him about Ragna later in more detail...
I exhaled long and slow so Amelia couldn’t hear my sighs, but she patted my shoulder as she stepped out of the room.
“Rest for now. I’ll manage the other members for the time being.”

Maybe I was coming short as a clan leader, but I was grateful for how considerate she was being. It wasn’t as if I wasn’t curious about what happened to Missha, Erwen, and the other clan members after they were teleported away, but...
Later...
But for now, all I wanted was to rest.
After Amelia left, I lay down on the military cot and closed my eyes. My mind and body were screaming with exhaustion, but sleep didn’t come easily.
Brown Rotmiller.
James Calla.
Versyl Gowland.
My emotions flared every time I thought of them in surges of sorrow, guilt, and rage.
Baekho Lee.
Regret and anger choked me when I thought of him.
Ragna Litaniel Peprok.

And then there was the request left behind by the marquess, which haunted me. I couldn’t even begin to guess what the palace would do to her after this, and I had no idea how to stop them if they attempted to target her.
There were the warriors of my tribe who had fallen following me.
The war was still raging.
The king, who might wake at any moment or never again.
The mysterious organization of Heerkmuta.
Auril Gavis.
It all twisted around me like a vice, suffocating and tormenting me. By the time dawn broke, I hadn’t slept a wink.
Regardless, perhaps because I had my eyes closed, or maybe because I’d spent so long just thinking, I had been able to collect my thoughts and settle my feelings to a certain extent.
For some reason, I felt a little better.
It was too awkward of a time to fall asleep, so I decided to just get up and get on with my day.
“Bjooorn!”
But then, I heard Ainar’s shouting from a distance, booming closer to me by the second...
“Bjooorn! Wake up!”
Without so much as a knock or a warning, the entrance to the tent was swiped open and Ainar charged in.
“Big news! There’s big news!”
One of the problems I wrestled with all night was resolved.
Well, not completely, but half of it.
“The war is over!”
To be precise, it was a ceasefire.
Ceasefire.
Meaning, the two opposing forces came to an agreement to pause the war for a set period.
Truthfully speaking, though, it was hard to call the current agreement a true ceasefire since it was apparently forced.
The Noarkans had repeated the actions they’d taken when fortifying Bifron and hunkering down there for a while, and they locked their doors once again.
With the marquess’s death, Thunder stolen, and their battle line in District 4 being pushed back all the while, it was a decision they were forced to make.

Still, it was pretty funny. From the perspective of Noark, they were forced into their bunker with tears in their eyes because they had no other choice available to them. The perspective of the palace, however, was altogether different.

After losing Bifron, District 4 had been taken over, and so now, they were afraid that the imperial capital could be overtaken in the next attack. The opinion wasn’t limited to the ignorant masses either—even the supposed learned nobles shared this fear.
Well, even without that, the situation is pretty dire.

After all, what happened last time when Bifron was taken over? The palace argued that we couldn’t afford to give the Noarkans any more resources, and the labyrinth was closed. The price of goods continued to skyrocket, and the number of starving civilians increased. The palace knew this as well and enacted wartime measures like suspending tax collections. Now, here we were, with the war temporarily put on hold.
We weren’t able to farm mana stones for a year, and since the rest of their funding was subsidized by the royal treasury, even the palace must have run out of wiggle room.
I couldn’t even fathom how things would play out moving forward.
It wasn’t something I needed to think about at the moment, anyway.
“Chieftain! The chieftain has returned!”
Since the immediate crisis was somewhat averted, I rounded up my allies and the bodies of the fallen and returned to the holy land.
“You’re back? How was the situation outside? Is the war really over?”
Shavin Emoor, who had managed the situation at the holy land while I was away, bombarded me with questions as soon as she saw me.
I couldn’t blame her. It was only thanks to my barony that I knew exactly what this “ceasefire” was about.
Most people were relying on word of mouth and rumors.
Naturally, Emoor had no idea since she was inside the holy land the entire time.
Why the war was over, how it ended, and...
“But wait?”
And exactly who died.
“I don’t see Mr. Rotmiller with you. Is he perhaps at the back?”
Before the heavy words could leave me, I glanced at my palm once more. Even though I hadn’t washed them, the words had nearly faded away.
Of course, just because they were faded didn’t mean I couldn’t read them.
These words written on my palm were the truth he’d had no choice but to scrawl in haste from atop that cart.
Please be nice to Ms. Shavin. She’s a good woman.
I swore I would remember them for the rest of my life.

chapters.title: Chapter 774: The Thirteenth Month (1)
paragraphs: The long funeral service, which somehow still felt too short, came to an end.

The bodies of the warriors that could be recovered were laid to rest in the forest per the traditions of the tribe. For those whose bodies weren’t in a state to return, their names were collected and honored together in a group memorial.
As for the humans, they were given services that followed their own ways. A deep hole was dug into the ground for the bodies to be buried, and a headstone was placed to mark the grave.
“Will this really be okay?” someone muttered. “If he’s buried in this place, on barbarian land, then...”

I was a little worried about that myself, but surprisingly enough, James Calla’s family wanted him to be buried here. Something about there being nowhere else to lay him to rest in Rafdonia anyway. Only the nobles who could afford a plot of land in Gnome Tree would be buried there. Most were cremated and their remains were stored in their homes.
“You know, I...” warbled another, feminine voice on the other side of me. “I think he’ll like it more, being buried next to his allies. All he ever did was work...”

I stared at Calla’s younger sister, who took in the sight of her brother’s grave with watery eyes. “I don’t think so. We’re talking about the guy who would go out for drinks but always left early to go home to his family because he couldn’t stand making you wait.”
“Oh... So he... My brother was...”
She broke down in sobs. As I watched her, I was struck by a thought.
Why did the truth only ever come out when it was already too late? Were mortals doomed to a life of never realizing what they had until they lost it?
There was no telling, and the question lingered as I slowly turned my head.

There, right next to James Calla, lay another—Versyl Gowland. Her date of birth and the recent date of her passing were recorded on her headstone. Unlike Calla, however, whose resting place was surrounded by relatives both close and far-removed, no family members gathered around hers.
And I knew exactly why. She and I had been allies, after all.
“The reason I cut off contact with my family? Just ‘cause. They got in the way of my adventuring.”

Although that was the reason she gave, I knew that wasn’t really why. The truth was the Gowlands weren’t her real family. It wasn’t the fear of being discovered as an evil spirit wasn’t what drove her out, but instead, the torment of being forced to act like their family after taking over the body of their daughter.
“That’s why I said some harsh things when I cut them off. Well, even after that, I still decided to pay their taxes for them. I don’t regret it. It’s not that much money either.”
I needed to look into it after all this was over.
Versyl’s wealth should go to her family. The clan wasn’t struggling financially, and legally speaking, it was only right for the next of kin to receive the belongings of the dead.
I stared at the grave, lost in thought until Sven Parav quietly murmured to himself from beside me.
“May you be guided to wherever you wished to be...”
It was a simple, unadorned prayer of rest, but I understood what he was truly praying for and shared the sentiment. We both knew where they had truly come from, after all.
Vwoong!

But seriously, was he actually a saint or something? Even though all he did was talk, his voice seemed to carry some mysterious authority, as if divine power had been seamlessly woven into his words. It didn’t feel like he used a skill either, and yet whenever he fervently prayed, just like now, his body glowed with a subtle, white light.
I turned my attention past Gowland’s grave to see Rotmiller’s resting place.
The dwarf was drinking right in front of it, and Missha sniffled through quiet sobs as her fists clenched to hold back her anger.
And a little further away was a silent Shavin Emoor, gazing at the grave with a look devoid of all hope.

Normally, I would have left to give her some space, but remembering the words Rotmiller left me, I slowly made my way over to her. She didn’t say anything when I reached her, so I took the hint and just stood quietly by her side.
It was a while later before Shavin finally spoke.
“Mr. Yandel... It’d be a little weird if I cried, right?”
“What do you mean?”
“Mr. Rotmiller and I weren’t anything, not really.”
Ah. So that was what she meant.
I couldn’t deny that their relationship ended before it could properly begin.
“I’m jealous,” she admitted. “Ms. Karlstein over there, and Mr. Hikurod... They used to be on a team with him. They can cry whenever and however they want to... But I—”
I cut her off. “What does that matter?”
In truth, I had spent a while debating whether I should tell Shavin about the will that Rotmiller had left to me—and I hadn’t even decided yet. But seeing her now, the decision was made for me.
“Before he died, Rotmiller told me to take care of you,” I said, catching her off guard.
“Pardon?”
“Not Missha, or that dwarf, or anyone else... He told me to treat you well.”
Shavin bit her lip, trying to hold back the flood of emotions in any way she could. “But...”
What do you mean, but?
I sighed and grabbed Shavin’s shoulder. “So who cares what kind of relationship you two had? Cry if you’re sad, and smile if you’re happy. You’re now a member of our tribe as well.”
“Can I... Is it really okay for me to do that...?”
I answered with a silent nod, and only then did Shavin let the tears fall. Her shoulders trembled with quiet, unsteady breaths at first, but as time passed, they began to shake in heaving sobs.
I hid my hands in my pockets and clenched them.
No matter how many times I went through it, it never got any easier.
After the funeral, I visited the palace once more to talk to Astarota about how Ragna was doing in her pseudo-imprisonment and about what to do with Eltora.
However...
“I can’t send either of them out into the public eye. Not yet.”
“Why?” I demanded.
“The matter of Countess Peprok’s standing is to be the sole decision of His Majesty.”
“I knew that when I asked. All I’m saying is that I’ll hold onto her until he makes that decision.”
“Impossible.”
“And the reason is...?”
“Why should the actions of the royal family need a reason?”
Man. He was seriously inflexible when it came to this stuff. And he acted so relaxed at other times.
Whatever the case, it seemed I’d need to postpone getting Ragna out of the palace.
“Then why is Eltora not allowed to go?”

“He’s the son of the traitor. If we free him now, things could get messy in ways that are both unpredictable and unnecessary. Still, don’t worry. It is undeniable that he contributed greatly to the war. Just as I promised him, I will do my best to allow him his life.”
Well, then. I guess that’s that. I’ve done all I can, so I’ll leave the rest to him.
I didn’t actually care all that much about what happened to Eltora, so I didn’t press the issue.
“Then can I at least see Ragna one last time before I go?” I asked.
“You could, though it won’t mean much. She hasn’t woken up yet.”
“Still?”
“Yes, still. Do you still want to see her before you go?”
“When our talk is over.”
“Seems you still have a lot you want to say.”
“I mean, with the state of the world, it can’t be helped.”

Astarota smirked at that, then tilted the kettle to refill my half-empty teacup—his way of signaling he was willing to continue the conversation. Knowing him, though, there was no telling when he would cut it off, so I decided to prioritize the most important questions first.
“So, the labyrinth... Will it reopen?”
“Why are you asking me that? That is a decision for the next-elected prime minister to make.”
“Don’t play with me.”
“I can’t tell you exactly when, but the labyrinth will be reopened in the near future. We are at our limit as well, what with being unable to gather mana stones for the last year.”
“Then the Noarkans will come crawling into the labyrinth too. Is there anything in place for that?”
“A farmer does not refuse to farm for fear of pests.”
“So you have nothing.”

“Isn’t that something for the working class to handle?” he dismissed. Noticing the look I shot him, he sighed and added, “There will be certain restrictions. Being barred entry if you are below a certain rank or have no connection to the military—something like that. Those countermeasures are being discussed at the Palatial Meetings as well.”
“I see.”
“Speaking of, why didn’t you attend the last one? If you’re curious about these things, you should just attend them.”
“I had things to take care of.”

Although my answer was poised if vague, I was a little flabbergasted. He absolutely, without a doubt, knew where I was and what I was doing, yet here he was, still asking me these questions. What a weird guy.
“I’ll give you one piece of advice, Bjorn Yandel.”
I flinched, watching his expression suddenly harden. Did he read my mind or something?
From what he told me next, however, I didn’t need to worry about him being a mind reader.
Not to say I understood what he meant either.
“It will soon be the thirteenth month,” he continued. “By decree of His Majesty, the month always holds a grand festival, and given the times we find ourselves in, we need it now more than ever.”
Oh. I never knew that, actually.
“So what?” I asked, waiting for him to explain what that could possibly have to do with me.
Astarota narrowed his eyes before putting down his teacup. “Rest for the time being.”
What was this? Was he worried about me? But no, that wouldn’t make any sense.
“I’m already resting pretty well, though?” I hedged.

“Running all the way to the palace to ask me these questions right after a funeral is what you call resting?” he immediately countered. When I went silent, he continued. “I will inform you of any new intel we obtain about the labyrinth or the war. So until then... You require rest, Bjorn Yandel.”
I had nothing I could say. Not because I couldn’t think of a retort, but because his sudden concern was too awkward for me to handle.
When I stayed quiet, still speechless, he downed the steaming tea in one go, apparently just as embarrassed.
“That will be the end of our discussion. Go now. Ah, but you can talk to the guy out front about Countess Peprok. He’ll guide you to her.”
Well. I didn’t know what to say to that.
“Sure.”
Even Astarota had changed since we first met.
Once my conversation with Astarota ended, I paid Ragna a visit. As I was told, she was still asleep. I used the opportunity to speak with Hyeonbyeol about a few things, then left.
Oh, and Eltora showed up midway to whine and groan about how long he would need to stay stuck here, but that wasn’t actually important.
Taking a rest, huh?
I couldn’t get the thought out of my head as I made my way out of the palace and back to the holy land.

Could I really afford to rest? Baekho had suddenly declared himself the main character, the Noarkan army was still holding out in the next district over, and I didn’t even know when the king would wake.
No way...
In truth, after returning to the holy land, I spent my time doing everything but resting. In summary...
I visited the nonhuman noble alliance Melbeth to check whether they had gathered any new intelligence.
I attended the Palatial Meetings whenever they opened to assess the political situation.
I met with powerful nobles, like Count Alminus, to network and even met up with Sven Parav to discuss the new abilities he obtained.
I met with Mr. Bear for the first time in a while to share a drink.
And whenever I could, I made time to fulfill my duties as Chieftain.
Although the last point was work that Shavin Emoor had been doing in my absence, she needed rest too. I could handle the work myself, anyway.
My schedule’s pretty packed...
Time passed quickly as I endured my packed schedule of running around across the city. Oddly enough, however, my body and mind weren’t exhausted.
This barbarian body of mine is too strong to be exhausted by menial work. Plus, staying busy is actually easier on my mind because I’m not distracted by other thoughts.
People around me—notably, Amelia—wanted me to take a break like Astarota suggested, but I either avoided the topic or politely refused. Eventually, though, I reached my limit of excuses.
“Yandel.”
Amelia swept into my tent where I was working late into the night to finish up some work as the chieftain.
“You know that the festival will begin tomorrow morning, right?” she asked.
“Of course. That’s why I’m busy right now. Since our warriors have worked hard, they’ll need time to enjoy themselves.”
“But what about you?”

“Oh, my schedule tomorrow? After the festival within the tribe is over, I’ll need to visit the imperial capital in the evening for a bit. It looks like Count Alminus is holding some event, and he said he’d donate handsomely to our clan if I attended—”
“Enough of that.”
Amelia cut me off before abruptly throwing something at me. I looked down to find it was clothing.
“Tomorrow, nine in the morning,” she said. “Wear that and go out with me.”
“Huh? No, but like I told you, I already have plans tomorrow—”
“It’s your choice.”
“Oh, then—”
“But if you don’t come, I’m leaving the clan.”
So it wasn’t my choice?

chapters.title: Chapter 775: The Thirteenth Month (2)
paragraphs: Once again, I found myself walking through the ruins of District 7, this time wearing the special outfit that Amelia had gifted me.

As I made my way down the uneven streets—though calling them streets at this point was generous—soldiers rushed around to fulfill their duties, uninterested in the random passerby walking amongst them.
Well, not entirely uninterested. They did shoot me glances but quickly turned back to their tasks, shrugging as if they must’ve been mistaken.
It was all thanks to the clothes I was wearing.
The Scarlet Party Suit.

Much like the Golden Mask I once obtained in the Bloody Citadel, my outfit was a piece of equipment that could only be obtained within a rift. It didn’t have any bonus stats or combat effects, just the ability to alter the wearer’s physical appearance as desired. Even so, the item was quite rare, as it could only be found in the rifts on the ninth floor.
Plus, the conditions to trigger the hidden secret are pretty weird, so you can’t get it just because you happen to reach the floor.
I figured having one around would be useful, so I made a habit of checking the auction house and asking around, but not once had it ever gone on the market since I awoke in this body.
And yet somehow, Amelia had just so happened to acquire one. It was no wonder I was surprised when she gave it to me.
“No, but seriously, where did you get this?” I hounded her once again, unable to contain my curiosity.
Her face twitched and she let out a little hum. Where at first, I assumed she was getting annoyed at my incessant questioning, I realized then it was the exact opposite.
She was stalling to savor the moment, too amused by my amazement to answer.
“It’s nothing that important,” she said nonchalantly. “Why are you so curious?”
“I search all over for this thing, and then you show up with it out of nowhere. How could I not be curious?”
Seemingly satisfied with my reaction, Amelia finally cracked. “I asked Astarota Berun. I wanted to know if they had one on hand and if I could borrow it.”
Well, it was the palace, after all. If anyone had one of these lying around, it would be them.
While the truth was far less tantalizing than I hoped, a part of me was touched. She’d gone out of her way to meet up with that guy, just for me.
“Thanks.”
Amelia hesitated, then said, “Don’t mention it.”
“So... If I say I lost it, what are the chances I get to keep it?”
She shot me a withering look. “Do you think something like that would work on him?”
Well, he was a bit of a pushover sometimes. Still, better safe than sorry.
A bit sullen, I grumbled, “I guess we’ll return it later.”
“Smart move. Nothing good will come out of overcomplicating things. The palace already has a reputation for demanding twice the price of what they give.”

We kept chatting, jumping from topic to topic as we strolled through District 7, and through that alone, I felt the cloud hanging over me dissipate. The only thing that had changed about me was my height, reduced to the size of the average human, yet no one recognized me.
This is nice...
Yet despite the strange sense of freedom, my heart grew heavier with every step.

District 7, the place I’d come to call home, was destroyed once again, now in even worse condition than it had been after the first invasion. The eastern area was blackened, rendered entirely colorless by the fires, and the central part of District 7 had been obliterated by two hits from Thunder.
Well, I guess it’s still better off than District 8. Didn’t that get completely burned down?

Regardless, the war had caught several districts in its crosshairs this time around, and with District 4 being completely lost to the Noarkans, this small city had become even smaller. The remaining districts were so packed with displaced citizens that the palace was even contemplating temporarily opening up Gnome Tree.
But a festival now of all times...
I couldn’t help but wonder what the event was for. It wasn’t like the refugees who lost their homes would be in the mood to celebrate. Was it for the people who hadn’t lost anything, then?
Or I guess, for those who lost “less”...?

I didn’t know, but honestly, I couldn’t have cared less about the festivities. I just wanted to go back to work. The problem was that we had someone in our ranks who said she’d leave the clan if I didn’t go to the festival with her.
It can’t be helped...
One thought stuck with me as I looked at the city reduced to ash and rubble.
Everything might look beyond repair now, but I knew they’d rebuild it all in the end.
As they always did.
District 5 was in full, festive swing by the time we arrived.

While that didn’t surprise me, I had to admit a part of me had expected the mood to be a little dampened by the aftermath of the war. Instead, however, the streets were filled with people and the air alight with the lively voices of merchants and customers.
It was an unusual sight, to say the least. District 5 was the only district aside from District 4 that had become a major battlefield. Needless to say, recovery efforts were still underway.
“Watch your step! There’s a huge pit up ahead!”

On the district outskirts, ruined streets and collapsed buildings were still a common sight, yet for some reason, the people bustling about in the early morning were all smiling as they enjoyed the festival.
I decided to go along with them.
These people deserve to enjoy this.

The attendees had probably come to enjoy the festivities so they could forget about reality, if only for a fleeting moment. And if the opportunity to leave their woes behind for a day couldn’t draw them out, the free alcohol and heaping portions of food the palace had generously provided for the occasion certainly could.
“Yandel, what are you doing? Hurry up.”
“Oh, right,” I said, shaking myself out of it. “Coming.”
Even after we’d entered District 5, Amelia insisted on taking the lead, still dragging me along behind her. I could only assume she had some plan in mind for the event today.
Wait...
Amelia grabbed my hand when I froze and tugged at me to keep moving.
“Don’t tense up, just keep moving. It’ll be hard to find each other if we get separated in this sea of people, especially with how short you are right now.”
“Oh, uh, s-sure.”
Persuaded by the threat of separation in this crowd, I gave up on resisting and allowed Amelia to lead me down the streets.
After a while, I asked, “Emily... Where are we even going?”
“Wherever our feet take us.”
“Wait, what? Do you not have a plan?”
There was a pause. “Everyone should enjoy things like this every once in a while.”
Sure, but I thought she had something specific in mind. I even cleared my schedule to make sure I could do whatever it was with her.
Well, I guess this isn’t so bad...

While the revelation threw me for a bit of a loop, wandering around aimlessly wasn’t the worst way to spend the day. We people-watched, snacked whenever something caught our eye, and even went into shops to peruse before the price hike had us balking.
“Three-step transformation toy? Goblin to Orc, and then Orc to Ogre?”
That then led me to the limited-event sale at the Alminus Central Exchange, where I got scolded by Amelia for wasting money on useless things.
Even though we went in without a plan, time passed quickly as we went about, spending the time together. At the end of the day, we wandered into a bar to eat some dinner.
“Of course it’s Bjorn Yandel, you brat!”

We entered to find a drunk customer shouting as he had a heated debate with his friend. They happened to be seated near our table, and since they were talking about me, I couldn’t help but eavesdrop, growing more intrigued by the second.
“Is there any adventurer right now that has accomplished as much as Baron Yandel? The only reason we’re able to laugh and drink right now is because he went and killed that traitorous bastard!”

“I agree that he has accomplished great things. But I find it hard to believe that Baron Yandel is the strongest there is. Wasn’t the Great Navigator Pikma the same type of hero? He accomplished great deeds, but his combat skills left a lot to be desired.”
“Pikma? Did you just compare Baron Yandel to a mere navigator?”
“I’m just giving an example...”
The two were discussing who was the strongest. Thankfully, they weren’t debating the best in history, but just who held that title in the present day.
“Nah, I still think Baron Yandel has done enough to be considered the strongest,” the drunkard insisted. The other patrons began to join in.
“Yeah, everyone used to think all he was good for was fighting, but he proved that he’s strong in other ways this time.”
“I heard he defeated Demon Eyes. Is that true?”
“And the Corpse Collector too...”
“He even survived multiple blasts from Thunder...”
The argument was quickly settled when almost everyone seemed to agree.
“Looks like it caught your attention?”
“Oh, sorry,” I said, focusing back on Amelia. “It was just interesting.”
So, the image the people had of me had changed.
I’d already been lauded for my leadership skills, sacrificial mentality, courage, and achievements as an adventurer, and now, my combat prowess was being acknowledged too.
To be fair, I hadn’t defeated a strong opponent in a public duel until now.
The battles at Goblin Forest and the Ice Rock Expedition were both far from duels. But defeating the infamous Demon Eyes, in full view of all those people, had proven my abilities.
Amelia shook her head. “This topic is interesting to me too. So what do you think?”
“Hmm?”
“Do you think their assessment is correct?”
Argh, why was she asking something so embarrassing?
I smirked and kept it brief.
“Well... They aren’t wrong.”
I was now confident I wouldn’t lose to anyone.
My outing with Amelia began in the early morning and wrapped up around early evening, though by the time we returned to the holy land, it was late into the night.
After lightly rinsing off and changing, I left the tent again to wander. I didn’t have a specific destination in mind. I just enjoyed the open air and walked—and before I realized it, I’d arrived.
To my surprise, someone else had made their way there first.
“Hikurod?”
“Oh, Yandel. It’s you.”
“I saw you leave earlier today when we were heading out. When did you get back?”
“Not too long ago. I wanted to clear my head, but it didn’t work out as I hoped. How about you?”
I hesitated. “I think it helped me out a bit.”
“Haha, that’s good to hear.”
The dwarf’s back looked smaller today for some reason.
I sighed and took a seat next to him. “You have one more bottle, right? Give it to me.”
“Do you have a cup?”
“Do you carry a cup on you?”
“Haha, I really can’t beat you...”
He handed me the bottle, and we sat in companionable silence for a while, each nursing our drinks. Eventually, Hikurod broke the quiet.
“Do you remember? What we saw our first time on the third floor...”
“Dwalkie, right? You’re talking about when he was scared out of his mind.”
“An innocent friend. Being attacked by a plunderer was what made him realize that reality didn’t live up to his imagination.”
“All adventurers learn that at some point... That’s why Rotmiller woke everyone up in the middle of the night to console him.”
“He probably wanted him to know that even if there is sadness and suffering in the labyrinth, there are good things too... Hard to believe it’s already been years since that day.”
I stared down at the bottle. “I feel the same.”
Our conversation lapsed again, and we silently drank for a while.
The dwarf was the first to speak again.
“It’s getting a bit cold now that I’m getting tipsy. I’ll head back first.”
With that, he staggered off, leaving me to linger alone for a while longer before returning to the room prepared for me back in the holy land.
For some reason, though, someone was waiting for me there too.
“Missha? What are you doing at this time?”
Missha Karlstein, one of the three left from the original members of Team Loser, and my first, unfruitful love.
Hmm, I guess technically speaking, she isn’t my first love?
Maybe it was all the late-night drinking I’d done, but for a second there, I got all sentimental over the notion of love.
“Take some time off tomorrow for me,” she suddenly declared. “I have somewhere I want to go with you...”
I blinked. “Huh?”
“If you don’t come, th-then I’ll leave the clan too!”
What the hell?
Missha disappeared from sight before I could recover from my shock and answer.
I sighed. Just what was going on around here? Did they all have a secret community board of their own?
“At least tell me when to meet you tomorrow,” I muttered to the empty air.
Well, I’d better just wake up early.

chapters.title: Chapter 776: The Thirteenth Month (3)
paragraphs: My outing with Missha was quite different from the one with Amelia. She had a pre-planned schedule, and it was pretty packed.
“Wake up!”
So it began with waking up at seven in the morning.
I was given only twenty minutes to wash up, put on clothes, and get outside to leave the holy land. Barely managing to make the deadline, I stepped out to find Missha staring at me blankly.
“Are we going?” I prompted cautiously.
“Yes...” she answered almost robotically. Then she seemed to shake herself out of her stupor. “Wait! Come over here! Whoa... I can see your face now that you’re shorter!”
“Huh?”
“I only saw your chin because of the angle,” she admitted with a satisfied giggle. She then led me toward the wall. “Come quickly! The carriage is waiting for us!”
Missha had apparently booked a ride in advance, as a carriage was waiting for us atop the wall. Once settled inside, we began to cross the wall’s length in quick strides.

Speaking of, the wall carriage, once exclusively used only by the military, was now available to civilians with the proper permission. Because of the devastation in Districts 7 and 8, carriages couldn’t traverse their usual routes. Thus, even though we were taking a slight detour, moving on the walls was much faster.
It felt like I was on a highway again. The distance traveled was longer, yes, but the lack of any traffic or roadside obstacles along the city walls allowed us to go much faster.
“Can I sleep for a bit?” I asked groggily.
“Sure. I’ll wake you up when we get there.”
Thankfully, Missha let me sleep in the carriage, and by the time I blinked my blurry eyes open once again, we were already at District 5.
She giggled. “I figured you’d wake up around now from hunger.”
“Are you a mystic or something?”
“What are you talking about? Let’s go! We’re eating meat first!”

Although it was the same District 5 it had always been, Missha had brought me to the eastern area, which was far less scarred by the war than the western region bordering District 4. The roads were relatively clean, and the buildings appeared to be relatively intact too.
Any further east than this, and we’d reach Gnome Tree...
I thought it over as I followed Missha, but it didn’t take long for her confident strides to slow to a crawl.
“Um... It should be around here...”
“Are you lost right now?”
“No, no! It’s just— Since there are so many people...”
“What’s the address?” After getting the address from Missha, I took on the role of the pathfinder. “So, 300 Raymond Road... It should be over there.”
We reached our destination not even five minutes into me taking the lead, causing Missha to exclaim in surprise, “Bjorn, you’re pretty good at navigating the city, huh?”
“I’m decent at it. I even got scouting lessons from Rotmiller for... Ah...”
When I trailed off mid-sentence, Missha flushed like she had made a grave mistake in bringing up the topic.
Uh, it’s gotten a little awkward. She’s probably taking me out to make me feel better too.
“Whatever, let’s go in already,” I said, barreling ahead. “I’m hungry because you got lost along the way.”
“Oh. Yes, of course! Let’s go! I’ll buy you everything!”
We entered the first establishment on Missha’s list, only to bump into a familiar face at the entrance.
“Mrs. Bear...?”
“Huh? Who... Oh!” Mrs. Bear looked up from the counter at the entrance and seemed confused for a moment before her eyes went wide. “Y-Yan—”
“Shh.”
“What happened? I nearly didn’t recognize you with how small you’ve gotten.”
“It’s a magic tool. But why are you here?”
“Ah! This is my acquaintance’s place. They needed some help during the festival, so I came in to help.”
“Where’s Abman?”
“He’s here to work, naturally. The hall needs people too. Oh, he did step out for a moment to grab some ingredients because we were running out, but you’ll see him soon enough.”
“I see...”

Well, they probably did need the money considering they were raising three children. From what I heard, their store had been completely demolished in the war, and they couldn’t even turn to revenue from the labyrinth since it was still closed.
Still, for a rank three adventurer to be doing menial jobs...
At least I wouldn’t need to worry about any trouble while he was here.
“Take a seat inside, over in the corner toward the back. It should be the quietest spot.”
“Thank you for your generosity.”
After Mrs. Bear led us to our spot, she left without even taking our order.
“Um, for the order...”
“Don’t worry about it. I’ll give you our best. And don’t worry about paying either.”
“Huh? But—”
“We owe you a great deal after everything that’s happened. If you must give your thanks to someone, let it be to Mr. Parav.”
“Oh... Got it.”
Missha did look a little crestfallen as her attempt to buy me food was thwarted, but there was no helping it. Refusing Mrs. Bear’s generosity would only make things more awkward.
“B-but don’t worry! I’ll pay in the next shop we visit!”
“Yeah, yeah.”
While we were waiting for our food to arrive, I talked to Missha.
“So was this the place you wanted to come to?”
“Yeah. It’s pretty nice, right?”
I ended up smirking at her calm response. “Why the shop that Abman’s working at?”
“Hmm? I mean, we’re out to enjoy ourselves anyway. Why not take the chance to see our friends along the way?”
It was a response I would have expected of the ever-extroverted barbarian Ainar. But then again, Missha had always been a people-beastperson herself.
“Oh, so you are here!”

Mr. Bear’s booming voice interrupted us at some point, and he came over to our table with our food. The couple somehow seemed to have a perfect understanding of my tastes, as 80 percent of the food they brought out were meat dishes, and that was before mentioning the astronomical portion sizes, far too much for two people.
Asking for one more round of this would be shameless, right?
Well, if we were actually paying, I’d have no qualms with ordering more.
“Abman,” I called, “if you’re not busy, sit down with us.”
“Hmm... I wouldn’t mind taking a break from work for a bit. Are you sure?” Mr. Bear looked at Missha for permission, and she readily accepted him.
With that, the meal began. Naturally, the topic of the day was the war—more specifically, it was Sven Parav.
“I don’t know what you think of him, but Parav is a true hero. Word is he let everyone escape and stayed behind in the temple to buy time... That kind of resolve isn’t something most people have.”
The Sven Parav that Mr. Bear described to me was completely foreign to me. I’d heard the tale multiple times now, even once from the man himself, but...
He’s not the type of person to do that... Was there something wrong with him?
It was a head-scratcher every time I heard it, but I didn’t write it off.
People changed. I certainly had.
