“Grabbing a bite with the three of us here, it reminds me of the old times. If you were going to come over, why didn’t you bring Ainar as well?”
“Ainar? Ainar is busy these days, so no,” Missha immediately dismissed.
“Busy? Doing what?”
“Um... I think she’s writing an autobiography?”
“Ainar is?”
My incredulous expression mirrored Mr. Bear’s.
“Missha, what are you talking about?” I asked. I had never heard anything about that, and Missha didn’t seem to know much about it either.

“I don’t know the details. Still, I think she realized something during the war... She kept saying something about how memories are bound to fade in the end, and that she needed to record them while she could still remember them...”
“I-I see...?”

Mr. Bear and I shared a look of disbelief this time. I had no idea what Ainar was doing, but that made it more believable in the end. From the perspective of Mr. Bear and I, Ainar doing incomprehensible things was definitely normal.
He cleared his throat. “Still, it seems she can write well enough to author her own biography?”
This guy never once said he’d want to read what she wrote. Well, I was also in the same boat.
“Still, even if Ainar can’t make it, I invited one last person.”
“Hmm?”
“By the last person—”
“Who else would it be but me?” a newcomer asked. Argh, that scared me.
“Raven?” My eyes went wide as I noticed the small wizard who appeared next to the table. “What are you doing here?”
And after all the trouble I had trying to contact her after the war too.
“Ms. Karlstein called for me. I came over to unwind a little and enjoy the festival... Can I sit here?”
“Oh, of course. I-it’s been a while, hasn’t it...?”
After getting permission, Raven sat next to Mr. Bear and sent him a smirk. “Why are you being so awkward?”
He cleared his throat. “Nothing awkward about me...”

To be fair, the two of them hadn’t seen each other for quite some time. After the party disbanded, Raven only really met up with me. It seemed they hadn’t kept in touch yet still had an idea of each other’s circumstances.
“How’s your life in the magic troops? You’ve even gotten that title of Golden Wizard.”
“It’s terrible. I don’t know why all these incidents happened as soon as I joined... The thing that holds me back every day from handing in my resignation is a sheer sense of duty, you know?”
“I see...?”
“How about you, Mr. Urikfried? Isn’t the Golden Tree Clan quite famous? They have a good reputation.”
Mr. Bear flinched a little before letting out an awkward laugh. “Oh... The clan? Right. It’s a decent one, alright...”
Everyone at the table, myself included, tilted their hands in mild confusion. There was something off about the way he spoke.
Huh? Is there a problem in his clan?
I didn’t know, but I didn’t ask. If he didn’t want to talk about it, I would just wait until he felt comfortable enough to bring it up himself. Raven and Missha seemed to be of the same mind.
Thank goodness Ainar isn’t here...

If she were, she definitely would have ignored the mood and asked him directly without noticing the mood—though whether she would even pick up on the mood change in the first place was another question in and of itself.
“By the way, Raven,” I said, quickly changing the subject in a snap decision to save the mood, “What’ve you been doing all this time to make you so hard to get a hold of?”
“Oh, me? My master passed away so I was busy taking care of everything with that.”
Damn it. What the hell?
It felt like I backed into a landmine, but I just let the feeling go after a moment.
Yeah, it’s not like we’re strangers.
I knew both Mr. Bear and Raven. Constantly being on edge like this wasn’t like me, and it made me sad to realize we’d grown this far apart while everyone was away doing their own thing.
“My condolences.”
Missha and Mr. Bear followed suit in expressing their sympathies, and it ended with that.
“You should’ve called for us if something like that happened,” I argued gently.
“Well, it wasn’t exactly a happy occasion. Besides Mr. Yandel, you didn’t even like my master that much.”
“It’s not that I didn’t like him...”
But it wasn’t that I liked him either.
That old man was weirdly obsessed with evil spirits...
Since the topic was already out in the open, Raven must have felt the need to elaborate on what happened.
“You know how the war got pretty big this time? The palace sent out the wizards of the magic tower as soldiers... You just learn to expect it. He died in the line of battle.”
A short explanation, as if she didn’t want to delve deeper into it.
“I see...”

Regardless of whether I liked the man or not, I still had a connection to him. It felt a little strange to hear such a sudden, offhand report of his death. And whatever he’d been to me, he was absolutely someone important to Raven.
“Anyway, after my master passed away and his position was left vacant, I got super busy. So I’m sorry I couldn’t come see you earlier.”
“You don’t have to apologize. The ones left behind are always the most busy.”
“Haha, it sure feels like it...”
Raven gave a bitter smile, took a big swing of her alcohol, and then leaned forward to lie across the table. She pushed her face toward me.
“I’m asking just in case, Mr. Yandel.”
“Hmm?”
“Do you need a wizard?”
What was this now?

chapters.title: Chapter 777: The Thirteenth Month (4)
paragraphs: While the offer was completely out of left field, it wasn’t a bad one on its face.

Setting aside any emotions and only looking at it realistically, Versyl’s absence had created an opening in our clan for a wizard. Of course, we still had Lilith Marrone, but when we resumed adventuring in the future, our clan size would demand that we split into at least two teams, so we definitely needed more wizards.
And here was Raven, making the offer herself. She was a high-ranking wizard, and I had even tried to recruit her a few times in the past.
Of course I’ll welcome her...
But I still needed to check something. Whether or not she joined the clan, I thought of her as my ally first and foremost.
“What’s this about?” I asked gently, pushing the topic of recruitment to the side for a moment. “Are you... Are you doing alright?”
Maybe it was because I just heard her speak about losing her master. The sudden change of heart had me worried.
“I’m fine.”
“Then why are you suddenly saying you’d leave the magic troops...?”
Raven paused for a moment, seemingly debating what to say, before finally saying bitterly, “I want to take revenge with my own hands.”
“Revenge? You mean the person who killed your master?”
“Yes.”
I see...
It was a reasonable motivation. There wasn’t much the ones left behind could do.
“Who is it?” I asked.
“It’s one of the Orcules members. He revealed himself for the first time in this war, and he hasn’t made a title for himself yet.”
She went on to explain that not much was known about him, but he was very skilled—too skilled to be a new member—and that he seemed to hold a high position within Orcules.
A super rookie who appeared out of nowhere...
I didn’t waste time pondering where someone like that might have come from. I already knew the answer.
It’s just like the ones who chased us back during the Ice Rock Expedition.

In the past, Noark had spent more than a year attempting to clear the eighth floor, a process that created many high-ranking adventurers in a short timeframe. They then used high-ranking essences, even up to rank 2, and showcased overwhelming firepower. Of course, their builds weren’t balanced since they didn’t have low-ranking essences.
In any case, the one who killed Raven’s master was probably created through similar means.
I sighed and spoke plainly.

“Raven, if revenge is your goal, then I think you should remain in the magic troops. Our top priority is survival. If the palace sends us to the frontlines, I’m going to do my best to avoid that as much as possible. Do you understand?”
“I do. But I won’t change my mind.”
What?
“You were trying to avoid it, yet you still had to fight a lot, right? You even fought against Demon Eye.”
“Uh... I guess so, but—”

“My intuition is telling me that joining your group will get me a better chance at revenge and much faster too.” I tried to say something, but Raven put out her hand to stop me. “And if I stay in the magic troops, I’ll need to listen to orders from the higher-ups, right? Even if he appears, if they don’t give me the order to go, I’ll have no choice but to sit still and do nothing. So... how about it?”
I had nothing to counter Raven’s reasoning when she put it like that. I couldn’t find a reason to oppose her either.
Well, except for one small thing—those words Lyranne Vivian left to me.
“I-I don’t know if you know, but there’s a rank 1 dark magic called Future Sight, and I used it.”

She told me that she used Future Sight to see that on the day the imperial capital of Karnon burned, Raven would betray me. While the Palace of Glory was destroyed by Thunder, in the end, Karnon never ended up burning.
Raven betraying me...
If what Vivian told me was true, then putting Raven in my clan could be dangerous.
No... I guess it won’t change anything.
I realized that if it was going to happen anyway, then it didn’t matter whether I invited Raven into the clan.
“Sure,” I said finally. “You can join, so go and put in your resignation letter to the magic troops first.”
“It’ll take around a month to get everything settled.”
“That’s fine. We don’t even know when the labyrinth will reopen.”
With that, the topic of Raven’s recruitment came to a close.
I looked over at Missha, who had been wearing a displeased expression for some time. “Do you have a problem with Raven joining the clan?”
She flinched before shaking her head. “Ahaha... Not at all! Aruru is a great wizard! Sh-she’s always welcome! Welcome!”
“Really...?” Then why did her laugh sound so forced?
I stared at her, unconvinced, and Missha shook both her hands as if to wave away suspicion.
“I’m really not nervous or worried! Really!”
Nervous and worried...
But I’m pretty sure I only asked her if she had a problem with it?

After finishing our meal, we talked for another thirty minutes before leaving the area. There wasn’t anything notable that we talked about other than Raven’s recruitment, but if I had to pick one more thing to mention...
He’s got something going on too.
Missha wasn’t the only person who reacted oddly to Raven’s recruitment.

Mr. Bear had looked at Raven and me with a strange look in his eyes. It was as if he had something he wanted to say, yet he never said a word of it even when we were parting ways. It left me feeling a little uneasy.
Well, if he needed to say it, he would have.
I couldn’t exactly force the question on him if he didn’t want to bring it up himself. I figured I would revisit the subject if he decided to share later.
“We’re a little later than planned, but let’s go to our next place!”
“I’ll guide us there, so tell me the address.”
“But that’s no fun—”
“Efficiency always trumps fun. Now, hurry up.”
After finishing our meal, we continued to move as Missha’s plan dictated.

We went to a pottery workshop and tried our hands at pottery. Then, we went to a play near the square and a circus after that. And when the day came to a close, we went to a bar that doubled as an inn.
“Do you...remember this place?”
Missha’s question came as we were finishing our dinner, and I searched through my memory.
“We came here a long time ago,” I answered.
Not for anything weird. We’d come to sell my old adventuring gear and ended up missing the last carriage out, so we had to pay a handsome fee to sleep here.

The rooms had separate living rooms, bedrooms, and bathrooms. Lots of windows, terraces, even Arthian soaps, and so on. The pristine condition of the inn gave us culture shock, and we resolved ourselves to earn more money in the future.
“Um, Bjorn...?”
“What is it?”
“Should we sleep here for tonight? It’s late, and it reminds me of old times—”
What was she talking about?
“Don’t joke around,” I said sternly, unwilling to risk any misunderstandings.
Of course, Missha probably did just want to sleep here, but I couldn’t do that to her. Maybe if there was never anything between us, but I doubted I would sleep soundly as things were now.
“Uh... I wasn’t joking...”
“Doesn’t matter. Let’s go home.”
We ended our outing there and returned to the holy land.
It took us quite some time to get back, and I spent that time thinking back on yesterday’s and today’s outings, noting that there were a few differences between them.
My outing with Amelia was more like an escape, freedom, time to myself... Phrases like that.
The one with Missha was about memories and connecting with other people.
Maybe the difference just lay in how the two of them relieved stress. One was healed when they were alone, while the other was healed by laughing and talking with others.
Well, it was laughable for them to apply the same approach to me.
They’re like kids sometimes.
Young children acted this way. When their mother was sad, they would give up something they liked to her, such as a toy or candy. But in truth, the mother found joy in their thoughtfulness.
Thwack!
“Ahhh! Why did you smack me, you barbarian!”
Now this was more like the old days.
I smirked and told her my true feelings.
“Thank you for today.”
“Eh? Thank you?”
“You pushed yourself today and brought me out because you thought I’d be sad.”
“Okay, but if you’re grateful, why did you smack me on the back?”
“Don’t worry about the small things. Anyway, thank you for today.”
“Well... That’s a relief to hear...” A moment of silence passed before Missha carefully spoke again. “But, um... Was it that obvious?”
I wanted to ask her in return if she thought she wasn’t making it obvious, but I decided to hold back. “Go in and sleep. It’s cold, so pull your blanket up.”
“Whatever. I’m going in first.”
“Oh... Yeah! Sleep well!”
After parting ways with Missha, I went inside, freshened up, changed my clothes, and laid on my bed. However, sleep didn’t come to me, and I ended up going on a walk like I did the previous night.
By chance, I stopped at the same place I did last time.
Brown Rotmiller
Versyl Gowland
James Calla
At the graves of the three allies I lost during the war.
Unlike yesterday, I didn’t see the dwarf with his alcohol. I also didn’t see Shavin or Sven Parav, who sometimes come out here.
I let out a sigh and shifted on my feet. Was I feeling awkward because this was my first time being here alone? Not that that was bad or anything.
Whoosh!
I felt the cold wind on my skin and sat silently in front of their gravestones for a while.

Unlike the dwarf, I didn’t pull out any alcohol. Alcohol dulled the senses and made one lose track of reality. Plus, I wasn’t the type to drink by myself. I would rather drink when I was out enjoying myself with friends.
But a smoke... That might be nice.
As I sat there just breathing the air of the night, an intrusive thought about cigarettes suddenly crossed my mind. I had never smoked in my life.
If I’d known I would become a barbarian, I would’ve smoked at least once.
I suddenly wanted to ask the ones who left first.
What did you all want to do the most? What were you curious about? What did you regret in the end?
Well, it’s not going to change anything now...
They were already gone.
Although Rotmiller had an opportunity to leave something behind, the other two weren’t even granted that. And because of that, I had no idea what I was supposed to do now.
I let out another deep sigh.
Everything felt suffocating.
Every time I turned away from a daunting question, another question I had been avoiding would come into view.
An evil spirit from another world, —, after losing three of his allies, will realize the path he must take.
That was what the Records Stone had written about my fate, yet in reality, I had realized nothing.
Deciding Baekho Lee was my enemy?
Was that truly the path that the Records Stone was talking about?
The more I thought about it, the more that didn’t seem right.
Then becoming the king, like the marquess said?
Hmm, that didn’t make sense to me either. At best, it was a fantasy—something I could hope to achieve in the far-off future. It wasn’t a realization or a resolution.
Then what is it, really?
I sat there in front of the gloomy grave, turning the question over and over again in my mind, yet the only thing that came to me was the cold wind of the night.

chapters.title: Chapter 778: The Thirteenth Month (5)
paragraphs: What was the path I had to take?
I still couldn’t find the answer to that question, yet here I was, walking down a path anyway. A path that led not back to the barbarian holy land, but to the holy land of another race.
Even though the overall style of the buildings wasn’t different from the ones from the city, it somehow blended seamlessly with the surrounding nature.
Just a small tilt of my head revealed where I was as I saw the huge tree in the distance.
The holy land of the elves, Varharium.

Naturally, the people here were also enjoying the festive mood, but their celebration was quite different from the barbarians’. Since it was a festival, it was far from quiet, but there was a sense of tidiness to everything.
It started with the background music. The barbarians usually used percussion instruments like drums, where this place was filled with the gentle and clear sounds of strings.
No one is fighting either...
Hmm, was this just a difference in culture?
It was pretty interesting to see the festival of another race. However, Erwen, who was walking down the street with me, seemed to be pretty used to it.
“Mister! Isn’t this place so nice? Nothing smells burnt here!” Erwen chirped, liking that fact more than the festival itself.
Well, not that I disagreed.
“The air is clean... How did they do it?”

Although the festivals were ongoing, the large-scale fire in District 8 caused the smell of smoke to fill the entire city. District 5 had a magic circle for air purification operating around the clock, yet even they couldn’t get the smell out of the air. So how was the air in this place so clean?
Erwen pointed to the tree in the distance as her answer.
“It’s all thanks to Lord Divine Tree over there. Outsiders don’t know about it, but Lord Divine Tree has the power of purification.”
Now that I think about it, I did remember there being a piece of lore about that.
“But let’s stop looking around and go over there,” Erwen said firmly.
“Hmm? Weren’t we here for the festival?”
“What? Why would I do that? There’s nothing to do at a boring festival like this...”
“Then why did we come here?”
“Just follow me!”
Erwen dashed forward, but since we were still near the entrance of the holy land, we had no choice but to go through more of the festival streets.
“It’s Blood Spirit...”
“Who’s that human next to her?”
“A man who can stand next to the Blood Spirit... Is he Baron Yandel?”
“Isn’t he too short for that?”

Unlike the festival in the city, we were the focus of attention everywhere we went despite my altered appearance. There was the fact that other races were rare to see in the holy land of the elves, plus the person next to me was too famous.
“What a venomous woman.”
“She abandoned her duty as a pureblood and went out to chase a man, didn’t she?”
“What gall, to show her face here after abandoning her people...”
The words hissed through to air, aiming for Erwen.
Traitor, snake, embarrassment of the people...
So this is why she hasn’t been visiting the holy land recently...
A flurry of verbal attacks was hurled her way from every direction.
I was debating whether to speak up about it when I felt Erwen grab my sleeves.
“Let’s keep moving...”
Hah, yeah. It wouldn’t make sense for me to act up when she was choosing to stay quiet.
I held back as best as I could and followed after Erwen.
“Tsk, look at that.”
Some said that elves were all honest and kind while others claimed them incapable of the cruelty so often seen in humans. But none of that mattered to me.
No matter who it was, they would get smacked if they talked like that in front of me.
“Look at the way she holds that man’s hand. It’s like she’s one of the red-light district’s slu—”
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
I undid the effects of the Scarlet Party Suit and let out a shout while using both Union and Giantization.
[You have cast Wild Outburst. Your threat level will temporarily increase threefold, and physical stats will increase relative to the threat level.]
My threat level was also increased using Wild Outburst.
The shout I let out echoed through the air, and nothing within fifty meters of me dared to move. The dozens of people standing there froze like they would die if they twitched even a little.
It was pretty ironic. I didn’t even use a stun but had simply raised my threat level.
If this was how you were going to be, what made you so confident you could go around saying those things?
While I didn’t understand, I knew their inexplicable behavior was proof that elves were also people.
Thankfully, the main talent of barbarians was to deal with other people.
Boom!
I strode forward, gently pushing past the frozen crowd and heading in a certain direction. Soon, I arrived in front of a middle-aged elvish man who was frozen in fear as he looked at me.
It seemed he wanted to say something, but fear strangled the words before they could leave his mouth.
I spoke to him.
“Say that again. What did you say about my ally?”
He didn’t respond.
It was for the best. If he actually repeated what he said, my hand might have moved before my brain could catch up.
Still, noticing he had some sort of survival instinct, I gave him a piece of advice.
“If you want to live a long life, you should keep your mouth shut.”
“I-I’ll... I will do that.” The male elf nodded frantically as he was granted a way out, and the situation ended with that.
Erwen carefully walked up next to me before dragging me off by my sleeve again. “Mister...”
“Damn it.”
“Why is that man here?”
“But... Is it right for him to do that in the holy land of others?”
“How ignorant... He doesn’t even care whether this would strain diplomatic relations...”
“Don’t worry about them,” Erwen urged. She must have assumed I would respond to them too. “Let’s keep moving. Quickly.”
“Okay.”
She led me away, making me feel like I was a school bully trying to act cool in front of his girlfriend. Still, I had no regrets.
They were the ones in the wrong in the first place. Why should I feel bad about it? They should have been prepared if they were going to say such insulting things in front of a barbarian.
“But it seems he takes care of her because she’s his woman.”
“Blood Spirit is quite peculiar as well. What’s so good about a barbarian like that?”
Argh, really. Stop.
I felt genuinely sorry for Erwen, but I stopped following her and turned back to look at the people around us. As soon as I did, they stopped talking and tried to avoid my gaze.
They’re all saying this to her because of me. I can’t just ignore it.
Quickly coming to a decision, I shouted at the crowd, “Hear me! I swear in this place with all the honor I have! I, Bjorn, son of Yandel, have never slept with Erwen Fornacci di Tersia!”
I yelled that out in the hopes that I wouldn’t hear any more nonsense from the crowd, but I belatedly realized I said it wrong and had to correct myself.
“Oh! Let me clarify, we have never slept together! We just... We didn’t do that, and only slept! I swear on the honor of my mother and my father!”

The truthful declaration of a barbarian. But hmm, why was everyone staying quiet? Was it because I wasn’t direct enough about how I wouldn’t be doing it with her in the future either? But to say that directly was a little too much, even for me...
“Oh, uh, um...”
I momentarily even considered the extreme option of pulling out that doll again, but I immediately dismissed the thought.
I quickly used Plan B instead.
“E-Erwen is a virgin!”

Of course, that wasn’t the most accurate way of putting it either. Under the theory of quantum mechanics, as I had never been a witness to the act, two different worldviews existed in parallel at the same time at that moment.
“P-probably...!”
Yeah, that probably worked.
After that shocking declaration, the entire street was blanketed in silence.
“L-let’s go!” I stammered, grabbing Erwen’s wrist to run off. Something told me I’d just made some grave mistake.
“Uh, Erwen...?” I asked when we were far enough away. “I didn’t intend for it to end up like this...”
“No, it’s fine. You don’t need to try and explain yourself.”
“I said it’s fine.”
Hmm, was she really fine? If it were Missha or Amelia, I would’ve already been attacked by now. I couldn’t hear any anger in her voice, though.
“If anything, I’m grateful. You did that all for me, right?” she asked.
“Uh... Y-yeah?”
“Then it’s fine. Though, it did hurt my pride a little.”
I had nothing I could say to that.
And thus, I quickly changed the subject.
“Why isn’t there anyone here?”
After moving off the street, we ended up in the middle of the forest.
“This isn’t the residential or the commercial district. Not many people will come here during the festival.”
“I see...”
“But we were headed this way anyway. Shall we go?”
“Of course!”
Upon entering the forest, Erwen slowed her walking speed, and it ended up turning into a sort of hike.
But where are we actually headed?
That question belatedly appeared in my mind, but I decided to ask a different question first.
“So... Erwen?”
“Yes?”
“Does that happen often?”
“Oh, that? I mean, it can’t be helped. Even after receiving Pureblood, I haven’t devoted myself to the people...”
Okay, so the answer was yes.
I quickly checked one more thing, despite knowing it might be a question that Erwen didn’t want to hear.
“Are there people that say they need to kill you to hand over the pureblood to someone else?”
“I know that there are some people who do... Given the times, we need the power now more than ever. Well, you don’t need to worry about that. Thanks to you, even the elders can’t say much to me.”
“I see...”
I looked at Erwen as she sent me an awkward smile to appease me.
I might need to solve this problem before it becomes more serious...
Naturally, we couldn’t hand the pureblood back, so either I needed to give something of equal value or put the elves in my debt by helping them when they encountered danger.
“So where are we going?” I wondered.
“Oh, it’s just around the corner.”
“Sure.”

Even though I didn’t know where our destination lay, the fact that Erwen brought me to the holy land while enduring that treatment meant that there was a good reason for it. I decided to not ask any more questions and took the time to admire the environment around me instead.
As I did, I noticed something interesting.
“This place... It isn’t a simple forest.”
Erwen’s lips twitched into another awkward smile. “Ah... You noticed?”

“There are magic circles drawn on the trees, and it’s difficult to run because the ground is soft. There are even structures in the trees that make it easier to attack people below. Is this a defensive structure?”
“Yes. Or, it is now.”
“Now?”
“In the past, this entire place was a residential district as well. After being invaded once, the holy land was reduced to ashes, so this place was born anew with it.”
One invasion. I didn’t need to ask what the incident was.
She was talking about the Dragon Slayer incident.
From what I heard, Erwen lost her parents back then too.
“We used to live here... It still looks so similar, but it’s changed a lot too.”
“H-has it?”
She giggled. “Let’s stop talking about that and keep walking.”

I wondered if I made a mistake in bringing up the topic, but there was no use crying over spilled milk. After walking through the forest some more, we finally arrived at our destination—a small house built in front of a small pond.
“This is my home. The place that my older sister, my younger sister, and I lived in. Well, not that either me or my older sister live here anymore.”
“Then is it abandoned?”
“No, my younger sister lives here. The reason I went through all that to bring you here is for her...”
“You brought me here for your sister?”

From what I remember, Erwen didn’t have a good relationship with her younger sister. After Daria died and I went missing, Erwen neglected her home and only focused on getting revenge. She’d earned the title of Blood Spirit then as well.
“After coming back from the first basement floor, I visited her often. That’s how our relationship has gotten a little better... But she’s really curious about you, Mister.”
Hmm, I had a rough idea of what this was.
“So she’s worried that I’m a creep.”
“Well... There are some preconceptions due to you being a barbarian... I’m sorry.”
“It’s nothing for you to apologize for. Rather, it’s my mistake.”
“Pardon?”
“Your family is my family, and I’m only now seeing her. Is your sister inside? Let’s go.”
No matter what sort of person her sister was, I needed to meet her as quickly as possible and leave. Preferably before the news of what happened in town spread to her.

chapters.title: Chapter 779: The Thirteenth Month (6)
paragraphs: Erwen’s younger sister was nothing like what I had imagined.
Daria and Erwen, the first-and second-born sisters, were both tall and lithe, so I expected the third sister to be the same.
She’s small.
She was just shy of five feet tall, around the same height or even a little shorter than Raven. What set the wizard apart from the elf in front of me, though, was her cold expression.
The sister wasn’t chubby by any means, but she still hadn’t gotten rid of her baby fat.
She looks pretty squishy, but I probably can’t poke her without making her mad, right?
In any case, this petite girl didn’t look like a twenty-one-year-old at all. Such was my first impression of Erwen’s younger sister.
“That look in his eyes... I don’t like it.”
I ended up flinching without realizing it.
She’s a direct-and-honest type? With that appearance?
It was a pretty rare type to see in real life, but that wasn’t important at the moment.
“D-don’t say that. Here, do you want to introduce yourself first?”
At Erwen’s gentle words, the small and cute elf puffed out her cheeks and revealed her name.
“May Forwin di Tersia.”
“I am Bjorn, son of Yandel. It’s good to meet you, May.”

I was worried that she wouldn’t like me saying her name or anything like that, but May fortunately didn’t complain. Apparently, she was giving some thought to her behavior since I was her sister’s ally.
Although I didn’t know exactly what she was thinking, as an adult and her senior in adventuring years, I continued the conversation.
“May, how many times have you gone into the labyrinth?”
“Four times. Then the labyrinth was closed so I couldn’t go in anymore.”
“That must have been upsetting.”
“Not really... There’s nothing good about going into the labyrinth.”
“Huh?”

That was unexpected. I assumed that at her age, she would be interested in adventuring, and thought starting the conversation off there would be best for the both of us. Her reaction she gave wasn’t born out of annoyance either, but out of genuine disdain for adventuring.
“Do you... perhaps not want to become an adventurer?” I hedged.
“No.”
“Why not?”
“Why would I? You need to sleep in dirty, cold, and hard places every day. The food is terrible. And you need to spend time with other people, whether you like them or not...”
Hmm, that was true.

Thinking back, if you didn’t need a lot of money or have a specific goal to accomplish, there wasn’t much reason to become an adventurer. That was why there were exceedingly few nobles who became adventurers.
“And the labyrinth always takes from us... It would be better if the labyrinth didn’t exist at all.”
As someone who knew the familial history of Erwen’s home, I had nothing I could say in response to this small girl’s grumbling.
“Haha, but still, someone needs to go in there, right?” Erwen said cheerily. “The reason that we can all eat, sleep, and wear what we want is thanks to the mana stones we get from the labyrinth...”
“I know.”

Erwen seemed like she didn’t know what to do at May’s cold response. I got the feeling that her past transgressions against her younger sister meant that Erwen couldn’t afford to be harsh to this small child named May.
However, all conversation was born from experience.
I’m used to handling kids like this.

With that, I decided to draw her in with interest first. There was a good chance that she wouldn’t care if I talked about something too grand in scope, so I decided on a topic that she would be the most interested in.
“Say, Erwen. Have you told her about the story of when we first met?”
“Eh? Ah, a little. Well... Back when I was in trouble... M-Mr. Yandel helped me...”
“Mr. Yandel?
“Haha... Wh-what’s wrong, Mr. Yandel?”
Erwen looked at me with another awkward smile. It didn’t take long for me to understand what was going on.
She’s embarrassed to call me that in front of her sister.
Well, it was true that “Mister” was more of a pet name at this point. And since we were here to show May that I wasn’t an oddball, calling me just Mister could be a mistake.
“Is there something that I wasn’t told?” May pressed. It seemed she found some interest in the topic when she realized there could be something she didn’t know about my first meeting with Erwen.
“Well, I don’t know how much she told you...” I baited, trailing off. “Hmm, do you want to hear about it?”
The girl shifted.
“Then I’ll tell you.”
It was smooth sailing from that point.
I began with my first meeting with Erwen then continued in order with all the fun adventures we had. However, it seemed that she noticed the gaps that I was leaving out.
“What about the Goblin Forest?”
May asked for the full rundown first. Although many things happened in the Goblin Forest, I knew May was asking about when the first sister, Daria, died.
“You can tell me,” she insisted. “I know most of what happened.”
I glanced at Erwen to ask for her permission, and she gave me the good-to-go. I then calmly told her the story.
It was longer and more detailed than any other chapter in our adventuring story, yet it wasn’t difficult to summarize the entire thing in one sentence.
Daria saved her younger sister Erwen and died in the process.
Unfortunately, the barbarian storytime ended there.
May fell silent for a long while after that story, and Erwen and I both waited patiently for her to speak.
“If the labyrinth didn’t exist...” she mumbled eventually. “Daria would be here with me...”
I simply agreed with her. “Maybe that could’ve been the case.”
If Daria hadn’t become an adventurer, she probably wouldn’t have died like that. In return, she wouldn’t have been there to protect Erwen when she was in danger.
“Why is everyone so obsessed with the dungeon?”
I also answered May’s next question simply. “Because the city isn’t any different. They enter the labyrinth because they don’t want to be robbed anymore. Because the city takes from them every day.”
Daria and Erwen knew this very well. That was why the two of them became adventurers.
To not have things taken from them, to protect those precious to them.
“Isn’t this the reason you became an adventurer even when you say you hate it?”
May didn’t say anything.
From her expression, I could tell she agreed with me on some front but didn’t want to admit it.
I get it. At her age, it’s difficult to know what you’re feeling.
It wasn’t my place to say something like that to May. I didn’t know what my true feelings about my current situation were either. I smirked and gave her a piece of advice instead.
“May Forwin di Tersia. The labyrinth will open again soon, so try going in there again. You’ll realize that bad things aren’t the only things that happen in the labyrinth.”
A long period of silence ensued once again before she gave her answer.
“Will I really...?”
I answered without a moment of hesitation.
“Really.”
Because it was the same for me.
Erwen, May, and I talked about many more things to pass the time, and through our conversation, I came to understand what the relationship dynamic between the two sisters was.
“Do you want more cookies? I happened to have some from that famous bakery in the—”
“No, I’m fine.”
Whenever Erwen tried to do something for May, May would then try to get her to not do it. They were far from a close-knit family.
This is suffocating...
I could clearly see that they cared for each other, so why did they treat each other like this?
It was frustrating for me, but there wasn’t much I could do. I lacked the experience to advise on familial matters.
I’ll just sit tight and watch for now.
I took on that stance and continued listening.
Sometime later, a visitor came knocking.
“May, are you in?” came the voice of a man.
It sounded familiar somehow...
“Ah, uncle!”
May immediately stood and went to the door, and Erwen put on an awkward smile at the sight. She had noticed it too, that this reaction was completely different from when May greeted her.
“May, have you been well?”
“Heh, you haven’t even been gone for that long.”
“Haha... I can’t stop myself from worrying even though it’s only been a few hours.”
The elf male patted May’s head with the smile of a father before turning to me and giving his greetings. “It has been a while, Baron Yandel.”
Fortunately, I already knew him.
“It has been a while, Beleg Shucia di Tersia.”
The adventurer considered a hero among the elves, and the brother of Erwen’s mother.
I greeted him in passing the last time I attended the Races Summit.
“By the way, I did hear that you came with Erwen... So you really did come.”
“Were you looking for me?”
“Somewhat. I would’ve come here even if it weren’t for you. My precious niece returned home after so long. Erwen, have you been well?”
“That’s good to hear. May I sit here?”
“Do what you want. I’m not the owner of the house.”
When I shrugged, Beleg smiled before sitting opposite me. “I heard the story from the town on my way here.”
I couldn’t help but flinch as the culprit of the incident.
I mean, this man is Erwen’s uncle.
“I understand what your intentions were when you did it... But did it have to happen that way?”
“I have nothing to say to you.”
When I lowered my head in shame, Erwen was the one who shielded me.
“Uncle, I’m fine...” she said. “Honestly, I thanked him.”
It was a feeling that I hadn’t felt in a long time as a tank barbarian—the feeling of someone protecting me.
“What happened?”
May’s round eyes were opened wide, but none of us dared answer her.
“I’ll be outside for a bit,” she said, taking the social cue. “You can keep talking.”
May left the house, allowing us privacy to speak, and the tension eased for the moment.
“She’s a good kid,” Beleg said, turning back to me.
“Seems like it. She reminds me of her older sister too.”
“I wasn’t talking about May. I’m talking about Erwen.”
I blinked. “Oh...?”
“So please treat her well. No matter how you go about trying to explain her situation, she won’t get another chance to marry anyone else. So take responsibility and—”
“U-uncle!” Erwen cried. “What are you talking about?!”
“Erwen, I don’t know what you think of me, but I am your and May’s guardian. I need to say the things that must be said. Isn’t that right?”
I had nothing I could say back to him other than this. “Th-that’s right.”
“And I take it that you fully understand what I wanted to say to you?”
“O-of course.”
“Then that’s a relief. Please don’t take offense, and take it as the words of an adult who dearly loves and worries for Erwen.”
I had no choice but to just nod silently, and thankfully, Beleg didn’t pressure me any further and we were able to move on to ordinary topics.
“Beleg, I want to ask you something. Is the public opinion of her bad because she withdrew from the special forces unit?”
“I can’t even lie and say it’s fine, considering the words that come out of some of the elders.”
“You must have worked the hardest. Thank you.”
“I’ve only done what I should.”
“I want to help a little as well. Could I hear about the power structure of the elves?”
“Hmm... Sure. I can’t consider you an outsider anyway, Your Lordship.”

There were a few things thrown in here and there to force my hand, but the talk I had with Beleg was beneficial for me. It helped me formulate an outline of a plan of how to restore Erwen’s public image, and if I were to go on and create a more detailed plan—
“Erwen, could you step outside for a moment?”
Huh?
“I need to have a private talk with the baron. Just for a short while.”
“Okay...”
Around the time our conversation was about to come to an end, Beleg sent Erwen out.
I couldn’t help but get nervous. This was the guy who talked about taking responsibility right in front of Erwen, so what was he going to tell me now after he sent her out?
“Tell me. What is it you want to say?” I carefully asked him. Beleg hesitated for a moment before giving it to me straight.
“Lord Baron, I heard that you possess a Stone of Revival.”
It was a completely unexpected topic.

chapters.title: Chapter 780: The Thirteenth Month (7)
paragraphs: Stone of Revival.

Even filled with its many different types of items and abilities, the Stone of Revival was one of the very few items related to resurrection in Dungeon and Stone. Since it could only be obtained on the ninth floor under very low probability after fulfilling a very specific condition, its rarity couldn’t even be expressed.
Gathering all nine single-numbered items might be considered easier than obtaining one.

In truth, even in Rafdonia, with its thousands of years of history of exploring the labyrinth, the Stone of Revival was still treated like a legend or a rumor. People weren’t even sure if such an item existed.
Anyway, that wasn’t important at the moment.
This guy is talking about something like that...
The first emotion I felt when the Stone of Revival was mentioned by Erwen’s uncle was one of confusion.

It was an odd time to mention it, to say the least, and something I never actually expected him to mention in the first place. However, as I calmed myself and faced the situation head-on, a different emotion came to me.
Curiosity.
No, to be precise... Suspicion.
Wait, is this guy Crescent...?
The guess struck me out of the blue, but I couldn’t simply ignore it once it was there. My suspicion wasn’t completely baseless, after all.
Elf.
High floors.
Obsession with the Stone of Revival.
There weren’t many people who fit all three of these criteria.
Also, considering that the age range of the old evil spirits was around the mid-thirties to early-forties, this guy became even more suspicious.
Well, the problem remained. I couldn’t very well up and ask him if he was Crescent now, could I?
“I apologize if that was too sudden. However, Lord Baron. I heard that you do prefer a direct conversation like this...”
I had paused to sort out my thoughts, and Crescent gave a careful apology in response. I used the moment to think a little longer.
How should I respond?
There were two choices I could make. Either I deny what he was talking about or affirm his suspicions and listen to the details.
I debated for a moment, but I decided on the latter. I got the sense that he came to me not with an assumption but with certainty.
“Where did you hear that?”
Although it wasn’t a full confirmation, I gave a somewhat affirming answer to his question. When I did, I noticed a very subtle shift in Beleg’s expression.
A moment of relief. And a slight tinge of nervousness.
Beleg quietly let out the breath he was holding before answering, “I received an anonymous letter in the middle of the night.”
“An anonymous letter?”
“As said, I don’t know who sent it to me. However, it even had a detailed description of Ms. Karlstein’s story, and I concluded it wasn’t some random nonsense, so I came to ask you.”
“Could I perhaps take a look at it?”

Beleg didn’t even think and handed me the letter as if he had been waiting for me to ask him. Fortunately, it wasn’t like the ghost busters invitation letter where the words would disappear after a certain amount of time passed.
I quickly read through everything...
I knew it.
But it wasn’t difficult for me to realize who sent Beleg the letter. I had my theories going in, but...
lol
But that one word written at the end, as if to mock the reader, was unmistakable proof of the sender.
Baekho Lee...

I was always on guard because I had no idea what bullshit he could be planning, but I never even saw a trace of Baekho after that day. For him to have been scheming something like this in the background...
What is his goal?
I didn’t know, which made it all the more frustrating. Why did Baekho give Beleg information about the Stone of Revival?
I really can’t get a read on what this bastard’s trying to do.
Beleg seemed to notice that my attention was on the last word as he added, “From what I’ve heard, it’s one of the words used by evil spirits.”
“I see.”
“So, is it true? Do you have the Stone of Revival?”
“I do.”

It would be laughable to deny him at this point, so I just confessed to him. However, even with the certainty he held before coming here, the confirmation seemed to have been a shock to him, judging by his excited reaction.
“I-is that true?!”

I steeled my heart even more. I would probably never find another elf who showed this suspicious amount of interest in the Stone of Revival. This guy had to be Crescent. Not to say he was always normal in my eyes, but...
But for Erwen’s uncle to be an evil spirit...
If he was an evil spirit, why did he care so much about Erwen and her family? From what I heard, he treated them like his own nieces. No, more like they were his very own daughters—
At that moment, we heard the front door open with a clack. Voices filtered through. One was Erwen trying to stop May, and the other was May’s anger-filled outburst.
“Let’s continue this later. I will personally visit you in the near future.”
With that, Beleg ended the conversation, disappointment in his eyes, and I nodded in return.
Some time passed.
“M-May! Uncle and the baron are talking in the room—”

Accompanied by the sound of Erwen’s desperate voice, May flung open the door to our room and entered it. Her breathing was rough with rage, and when I felt the subtle level of threat coming off of her, I quietly nodded.
She heard what happened in the town.
Getting hit while knowing you’d get hit was much different from getting hit out of the blue. Due to having the time to ready my heart for the attack, the damage was low.
“I thought you were a decent person.” May looked at me with contempt before mumbling quietly, “Scumbag.”
The favorability I had barely built up was thrown into the trash.
We were practically kicked out to get away from May’s anger, after which we immediately returned to the holy land.
Whenever we came out far into the city for some business, we sometimes slept in the city, an option that Erwen asked me about this time around as well.
“Sleeping is done at home.”
I didn’t want to sleep out in the city when the festival had everyone outside, and I didn’t want to spend the money either.
There are only two more days of the festival left...
As we rode on the wall carriage and looked down at the city in its full festive mood, I had some time to think by myself.

Even though the day was coming to an end, the city below was bright enough for me to see everything, and it was so filled with laughter and voices that the joy from below could be felt all the way up here.
“Erwen, don’t you want to enjoy the festival as well?”
“Hmm, not really... I don’t really like loud things...”
“Really?”
“Well, I think it’ll be fun to walk around the streets with you, Mister... But let’s do that next year. I’ll skip this time.”
“Why?”
“I don’t think you’re ready yet, not like me.”
“What’s there to get ready for a festival?”
“Hehe... You do need to get ready! I needed to prepare myself too, you know!”
I couldn’t find my voice when her bright voice was paired with that sad smile.
“So let’s go later. Later...when we get tired of being sad and want to laugh and smile as much as we want.”
“Got it. Let’s do that.”
“Yep. I heard this from Daria in the past, but there’s a saying. If you get married during the festival, you’ll live your life in happiness without having to worry about money.”
“Ah... Really?”
Ignoring the saying, I sensed that Erwen had recovered a lot. Even though no one else had brought her up, she talked about her sister first and could even smile.
As we continued to share small talk, our carriage arrived at the holy land. Naturally, the holy land was also noisy and loud, what with the barbarians also enjoying our festivals.

Although there would be some warriors who went out into the city to enjoy themselves, it was tradition for warriors to mostly enjoy the festival in the holy land unless there was some reason to be elsewhere.
“Then I’ll be going in. I’m a bit tired...”
“Yeah, today was fun. Have a good rest.”
After separating from Erwen, I headed toward my quarters and listened as the noise started to fade away into the quiet.
Well, it was quiet compared to the forest that was filled with the sound of the festival, so not that quiet.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“B-be quiet! This is a quiet area. Emily Raines will come over if you’re too loud!”

The reason this place was able to be relatively quiet was thanks to Amelia. Something about the residential area here needed to be quieter since there were people who might want to sleep. Although the logic was sound, the true reason was probably for my sake.
“That woman is so cruel!”
“That’s right! This is a festival, how does that make sense? And no one here wants to sleep either!”
At that moment, a familiar voice cut through the noisy barbarians. “What did you just say?”
“Eiyaah! Emily Raines!”
When Amelia appeared like a ghost, the warriors who were venting their frustration as they pleased began to quickly point fingers.
“I didn’t talk! Really! I’m a good barbarian being quiet in the quiet area!”
“The only person who talked was Kizan, second son of Merik!”
“Kizan, second son of Merik, is a foolish warrior! He could’ve gone to the noisy area if he wanted to laugh and talk, but he just had to come to the quiet area!”

I was curious what she did that the warriors were all scared out of their minds just by her appearance, but it wasn’t completely unknown to me. Amelia was the one who could restrain even that Ainar. There was no way an ordinary warrior could handle her.
“Stay if you’re going to sleep, and go off to the noisy area if you want to talk.”
“G-got it! I’m going to go talk! Sorry!”
The warriors ran off as fast as they could.
Still, it was pretty funny. I could understand the barbarians doing it, but Amelia was also talking about quiet areas and noisy areas.
“You’re back?”
“Ah, uh...” I stammered, caught.
“Go in and rest.”
“Sure...”

I briefly met her eyes, then immediately went in to just wash up and go straight to bed. However, no matter how long I lay there with my eyes closed, sleep never came to me. At this point, I was struggling and trying to force my mind to clear.
“Bjoorrrrn!”
“Ainar?” I called. “What is it? It’s the middle of the night.”
“What are you doing in the quiet area? Everyone’s having fun! You’re too old to grow if you go to bed early!”
“I’m tired after going out.”
“You went out for three days! Come today and have some fun with us!”
I smirked as Ainar entered her begging mode.
But at least she doesn’t threaten to leave the Anabada Clan.
That didn’t mean I was going to go and enjoy the festival, though. Honestly, if I couldn’t sleep, I was planning on going to the graves like I did the past few days.
However...
“Bjorn, the warriors need you.”
That one sentence moved me.
I sighed. This was the first festival after such a huge incident, and I was the chieftain in name, so not even showing myself once was a bit...
“Got it. I’ll go so stop whining.”
“Oh, really?! That’s good! Everyone will love it!”
After sending Ainar out, I quickly donned the traditional barbarian garb.
Oh, though donning was probably the wrong verb to use.
To be precise, I took off my other clothes. The traditional clothes of barbarians began with taking the top off, after all.
“Hurry up! I’m sure that everyone will be excited to see you!”
No, I was hoping that doesn’t happen...
“Got it.”
With that, I was dragged by Ainar into the forest where the festival was ongoing, over to the aforementioned noisy area.
When I arrived, my breath hitched.
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“Oh! The chieftain! The chieftain is heeeere!”
“Bjorn, son of Yandeeeel! The greatest warrior in the world!”
“The most genius monster!”

I was only safe because the barbarian eardrum was sturdy. Most people would have lost their hearing from how loud these warriors were. I also understood why 99 percent of the people here were barbarians even though there was a significant number of humans in the holy land.
“Right, right! Over there! Someone is fighting over there!”
The first place that Ainar led me to in this festival was where two warriors were fighting as if to kill each other.
“Die! Die! I’ll rip out all your teeth!”
“Break his arm!”
“Doesn’t matter! He won’t die from that!”
Two warriors were having a serious go at each other, and countless other warriors were watching their battle.
At that, I just grabbed a warrior at the side and asked him, “But why are they fighting?”
“Who knows? I don’t. I’m not really curious about things like that.”
The warrior looked at me like I was a fool before looking back at the fight.

Okay, so the fight was more important than me, was it? It was pretty laughable how much they propped me up, saying I was the great warrior or whatever, but were ruthless whenever they were distracted.
But honestly, it was understandable. Fighting was the greatest form of entertainment for barbarians.
The criteria for how fun the festival was is how many times you fought...
Well, it was pretty fun. Our warriors wouldn’t lose to anyone else in close-quarters combat. And PvP was also much more fierce at low levels compared to higher levels.
“Raaaaaah!”
In the end, the red-headed warrior who countered with an elbow to the chin won the battle. However, before everyone lost interest and moved on to other things...
“Hear me!” Ainar suddenly shouted, catching the attention of everyone present. “As you saw, the chieftain is here!”
They probably had no idea where she was going with this, but the warriors reflexively reacted since something was about to happen.
“Whoa!”
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
Well, I thought something was going to happen as well, so I just stood there and waited.
Why am I feeling so uneasy?
And as always, that uneasiness bore fruit.
“The chieftain will face off all the warriors tonight!”
Wait, who said I would...?
“Ohhh?”
“But... The chieftain is the great warrior!”
“Not even I can defeat the chieftain!”
Thankfully, the warriors didn’t seem all that enthused. If this continued, this absurd plan had a good chance of just falling apart.
“Don’t worry! It doesn’t matter which part of his body it is! If you can make him bleed even one drop, you will be the victor!”
Ainar quickly put a handicap in place.
“Oh?”
“If it’s like that, it might be possible...”
Of course, the fundamental question was still unanswered.
“But why should we fight him?”
“We’re people as well! It hurts when we’re hit! Especially when it’s the chieftain hitting!”
For some reason, the warriors seemed more intelligent today, and it seemed Ainar hadn’t expected that either.
“Uh, well... It’s an opportunity to fight the chieftain! You honorable warriors should...naturally...want to...?”
After floundering for a moment, Ainar closed her eyes with determination before shouting, “A house! The winner will get three houses!”
Nothing else needed to be said.
“Houses.”
“It’s worth risking my life!”
The glint in the warriors’ eyes shifted.

chapters.title: Chapter 781: The Thirteenth Month (8)
paragraphs: Heavy breaths infused with heat.
Eyes fierce with unwavering battle spirit.
Fingers twitching and shoulders shaking from excitement.
The barbarian desire for real estate was as powerful as ever. Well, as powerful as it had been since I stoked the obsession in our holy land with the introduction of real estate.

From then on, the understanding that ownership of property equated to being a great warrior had been etched into each and every one of their minds, and that “common knowledge” had only become more deeply rooted in the culture with time.

It was the natural outcome, in hindsight. Most of the barbarians who lived outside the holy land usually settled down in the closest district to the holy land, District 7. However, both District 7 and District 8 had been reduced to ashes and rubble, and Kommelby, the next closest place to live, had become so expensive that the warriors couldn’t afford to stay there.
Still, while the next district over, District 9, had survived the war and was far better than the costly Kommelby as a result...
“I-if I have a house... I won’t have to sleep outside!”
“It costs five times as much to live in District 9 now!”
“That’s right! And it’s so far from the holy land that I don’t have any friends there!”
In truth, most of the barbarians had returned to the holy land, forced to live communally in what was barely one step above homelessness.

The war had displaced countless people, creating a frankly unmanageable number of refugees who packed all the lodgings in the city to the brim. With the prices of rooms skyrocketing and the labyrinth still closed, the warriors didn’t have any way of paying rent.
They are at least able to get by now because they know how to work in construction...
Most of the warriors were just barely making ends meet from manual labor jobs out in the city proper. And now, a house was put up as a prize?
“I-I’ll challenge him first!”
“No! Me! I’m going to challenge him!”
The words burst out of the warriors in waves, quickly spreading the news to all the barbarians in the holy land.
If I say I won’t participate, their trust in me will plummet. And...

If I were honest with myself, their approval of me did play a factor in my decision, but above all, I didn’t want to see my barbarian warriors slump in disappointment when we were meant to be celebrating.
“Ainar,” I called.
“N-no!” she rejected before I could say another word. “You need to fight them! A-and Bjorn, you—! You can at least give us one day of your time! You are our chieftain—!”
“Calm down. I’m not saying I won’t do it.”
“Huh? Wait, r-really?”
“Yeah, but let’s move somewhere else. The field is too small here.”
“Oh, then we can go to the Grounds of Testament!”
With that, we moved with all the warriors to the Grounds of Testament.
It’s been a while since I was last here...
The Grounds of Testament was a huge pit in the middle of the forest where warriors nobly battled each other, and the place where I ascended to the position of chieftain.
I dropped my weapon and held up my two fists. “Alright, come at me!”

The look in the warriors’ eyes changed from anxious resolve to proud defiance. I know we’re fighting because there’s a house on the line, they seemed to say, but fighting barehanded? Aren’t you underestimating us here?
“Not even the chieftain will be able to win with his bare hands!”
“Shut up and fight!”
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
And so, the competition began. Even though I wasn’t using a weapon, none of the warriors dared to go easy on me.
“Th-the challenger this time is Bellikta, son of Ryuman!”
“Dragon Hunter Bellikta!”
“Whoot!”
The warriors who had earned a name for themselves within the tribe challenged me first, and I faced them as best as I could. Maybe it went without saying, but...
Why is it so hard to make me bleed?
The fights dragged on longer than expected because while my opponents were tough themselves, no matter who I fought, they couldn’t spill a single drop of my blood.
The core aspect of the shield barbarian build was its strong Physical Resistance, so for most barbarians—who relied on dealing physical damage—it was close to impossible to put a scratch on me.
“It’s my loss. The chieftain is a mighty warrior!”
“You fought well.”
“Ugh... No one can defeat the chieftain!”
“He is a monster! A monster!”
As the named challengers all failed, the warriors who were looking on in excited anticipation began to lose hope as they realized the futility of their goal.
What do I do? I haven’t even used Giantization yet...
However, I wasn’t the only one who noticed the plummeting mood. When I looked over at Ainar, I could see her wrestling with the same problem.

I was reminded of Ainar after the coming-of-age ceremony, back when she became the “leader” of our graduating class and got lost while on the way to the city. She had the same expression now as she did back then.
Hmm, looks like I’ll need to help her out this time too.
“We’ll take a short break!” I announced, putting a pause on the fighting for a moment, and walked over to Ainar.
When I gave her an idea that could revitalize the morale of the warriors, she relayed it to them excitedly.
“We’ll stop the fighting there! Let’s all go for drinks instead!”
“Drinks?”
“The rules are simple! Everyone will drink at the same time, and the one who lasts the longest will win!”
“Are the prizes the same?!”
“Of course! If you can survive longer than Bjorn, then all the warriors will receive one house each!”
Wait, one house each? But I don’t remember ever saying anything like that?
“Uraaaaah!”
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
The sudden change in prize pools had me reeling, but there was no taking back the words now that they had been spoken.
“This will be named the drinking battle!” Ainar declared. “The sacred drinking battle!”
“Drinking battle! Drinking battle!”
“Uraaaaah!”
The warriors all let out a roar of approval at the name Ainar tossed out.
Hah, whatever...

I wasn’t confident enough to rain on their parade, so I stayed quiet. After a brief delay to prepare, the drinking battle—whoops—the sacred drinking battle that had the potential to become a new barbarian tradition began.
“Alright, the first drink!”
The thousands of warriors who had come down into the Grounds of Testament raised their cups to Ainar’s shout.
“The first drink!”
Then every glass was emptied in one gulp.
We then repeated this multiple times.
Two drinks, three drinks, four drinks, five drinks...
As we continued to drink, more and more warriors began to drop out.
“Ugh... Hic! Blergh!”
“Karubo, son of Bullak, has thrown up! Out!”
“Daaaamn iiiit!”
We’re drinking a lot quickly and many of the warriors were already drunk from enjoying the festival... I might beat them all at this rate.
The thought energized me even more.

Besides, if over a thousand barbarians somehow defeated me in this contest, that would send our barbarian tribe into immediate bankruptcy. As the chieftain, I needed to stop that future from coming to fruition no matter what.
“Alright, drink!”
Sixteen, seventeen, eighteen...
As the amount of liquid in my stomach continued to increase, I felt myself becoming tipsy.
How long has it been since I got this drunk?

I actually didn’t know what my limit was. I had never gotten black-out drunk before with this body. Plus, after raising my Natural Regeneration and Poison Resistance stats, I sobered up really quickly even after getting drunk, so it was even more difficult for me to pass out.
“Alright, this is the seventy-third drink!”

More and more warriors were disqualified because they vomited, passed out, or left their spots to go relieve themselves, and our drinking tempo sped up in kind. After all, fewer people meant less time needed to prepare a drink for everyone.
“Pour! It’s the hundredth drink!”
“Uraaaaaah!”
Huh? How were we at the hundredth drink already?
I took a look around, noticing that the number of warriors holding up their drinks had decreased significantly.
I think I see around...one hundred.

I didn’t know the exact number, but what I did know was that I was getting bloated. My stomach was throwing a tantrum, protesting that there was no more space left, and I could feel its contents slowly creep back up on me.
One hundred people mean one hundred houses, and in cash, that’s...
The total snapped me back to awareness. I quickly cast my ability.
It was the logical thing to do, really. If the problem was that my stomach was already too full of alcohol...
[You have cast Giantization.]
I just needed to increase the size of my stomach.
My enlarged stomach immediately felt better, and the pressure eased on my near-bursting bladder too.
Still, the second hurdle came earlier than I expected.
“The hundred and fiftieth drink!”
I was going to die.
Thirty people?
Who the hell were these guys? Did they have a sub-space for a stomach? Or were they drinking something other than alcohol?
Although my mind jumped to suspecting them, I fortunately noticed that they weren’t in their right minds.
“Eh heh heh...”
“A-another one... Heehee...”
“House! My house...! Urgh!”
Even with their rational minds gone, these warriors couldn’t let go of their desire for a house and were holding on.
I forced myself to concentrate on the sight of their zombified states.
Just a little more...
I was no stranger to endurance. Ice Rock was way more difficult than this.
“One hundred fifty-one!”
I drank. Even with my spinning vision, I saw a few warriors collapse.
“One hundred fifty-two!”
My intuition, honed through countless battles, was telling me that this was the turning point.
“One hundred fifty-three!”
Just a few more drinks.
These few would determine the victor.
“One hundred fifty-four!”
My intuition didn’t fail me. Many more warriors collapsed.
However, the next moment reminded me of a fundamental truth of the world.
“One hundred fifty-five!”
They were hurting as much as I was.
In this cold world of competitions, the winner and the loser were decided on just one moment of perseverance.
“One hundred fifty-six!”
And I always needed to be the winner. Because the loser would have something taken from them.
“One hun— fifty—!”
Uh oh. This was getting dangerous.
How many more people were left?
“One— sixty—!”
Sounds grew distant, and my vision narrowed into a tunnel of light.
“—dred eigh—!”
Ah...
The moment I realized I had reached my limit, my narrowed vision focused on one warrior.
I was planning on collapsing when there were around three people left, but because I’d gotten so drunk, I only now noticed there was only one.
Huh?
But then, I noticed something very odd as I looked at the remaining warrior.
That guy...
I was wondering how he was able to keep so much liquid down with a mortal body.
He’s drinking while pissing himself?
How could someone like that exist? Even barbarians had things they wouldn’t do.
My jaw dropped as I witnessed the actions that went against all forms of culture, civility, and morals that had been built up throughout the history of civilization.
Not in horror, but in amazement.
Shock.
Shock at his focus that ignored all natural laws, just for victory.
And hidden within it—
Pshwooo.
The flow.
To not stop anything entering his body, and let it out unimpeded.
“Uh huh...”
Yes, this was the sublime truth—the supreme, the ultimate duality of man.
This...
Nature wasn’t embarrassed.
Nature didn’t care about rules.
Nature just existed.
Just like the great mountains.
This was a lost battle from the beginning...
How could I defeat someone who had reached the point of becoming one with nature?
I accepted my loss with humility.
That was the last thing I remembered.
When I woke up, the sun had set.
My body felt stiff, but I didn’t feel as hungover as I expected. Actually, both my body and mind felt fine.
Well, relatively speaking.
Let’s go to the toilet first...
The image of heaven above heaven that I witnessed right before I passed out stayed with me as I took my trip to the “golden throne.”
However, my trip announced to the world that I was active once more.
“Looks like you’re finally awake,” a voice commented.
“Emily?”
“Drink this. It’s honey water.”
“Thanks... Were you waiting for me outside?”
“Of course not,” she answered after a beat of hesitation. “I suspected you would wake up around this time and happened to hear you when I was walking past.”
Oh, that was a relief to hear.
I quickly drank the honey water before asking her, “How long did I sleep?”
“A day.”
“So today’s the last day of the festival, right?”
“Are you disappointed? Because you spent the last day asleep?”
“Not at all. The festival needs to end for something new to begin. I’m actually glad.”
Amelia shot me a disgruntled look at that, and I quickly changed the subject. Besides, I was curious about something.

“So what’s the name of the guy who beat me?” I asked slyly. The scene of the unending flow was still cascading through my mind, but I unfortunately wasn’t able to catch his face during the competition.
“Vector. From what I heard, he’s the third son of Kiltau.”
“Vector, third son of Kiltau...”
Why did that sound familiar? Where have I heard that name before...?
“Oh!”
Now I remembered.
I’d seen him back when I first became the chieftain and oversaw the coming-of-age ceremony. I immediately pegged him as a newbie from the way he was scanning the area with a stiff expression.
“No, wait...”
I stiffened like I’d been poisoned by a basilisk, tensing as a cold sweat ran down my back. Amelia clocked the change in body language immediately.
“What is it?” she asked, worried. “Are you hurt?”
I couldn’t avoid the terrible truth that I had come to face.

Vector, third son of Kiltau. The barbarian who had demonstrated the sublime truth of the supreme ultimate duality of man by becoming one with nature. The absolute master who had made his mark in the history of beauty.
Hmm, yes, that had to be it...
“Nah, no way,” I said, scoffing to myself.
Maybe I had been wrong all along.
There’s no way he’s a modern guy.
No way.

chapters.title: Chapter 782: The Thirteenth Month (9)
paragraphs: After telling Amelia that I was going back to sleep and sending her away, I lay in my bed, but as I’d come to expect, sleep never came.

It wasn’t that my recent deep sleep had chased my tiredness away, it was just... I hadn’t been able to get a good night’s sleep lately. Time passed quickly during the daytime when I could keep busy, but the same couldn’t be said for the night. As darkness fell, thoughts began to weigh heavy on me.
I sighed, and as I had been doing for some time now, I went out for a walk and began my nightly stroll around the entire holy land.
Despite it being the final day of the festival, the holy land was still alive with noise.
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
“Bahahaha!”
I instinctively headed in the opposite direction of the roars of the barbarians, my feet naturally taking me to the same place I always ended up.
Maybe they were another reason I kept coming here.
The cold winds of the thirteenth month whooshed by, brushed against my skin.

I stopped, tilting my head back to look up at the sky, A crescent moon hung above. Staring at it, I could almost fool myself into believing I was back on Earth, yet the uncanny feeling announced that this world was completely different from the Earth I knew.
The reason was very simple. A closer look revealed the moon’s shape was just slightly off.
Because Rafdonia doesn’t have a full moon.
Every night, the sky always showed the same moon.
Not to say the full moon was completely absent. There was the occasional, very rare case, like total solar eclipses were back on Earth.
I wasn’t an astronomer, so I had no idea how or why it did that, and it really wasn’t a question I cared to get answered in this magical and mystical world.
A quiet crunch broke through the silence.
“Who’s there?”
My voice came out aggressive, prompting a barbarian warrior to emerge from the forest, scratching the back of his head sheepishly.
When I saw who it was, I was honestly surprised.
“You... Vector, third son of Kiltau?”
At least it wasn’t Baekho Lee.
I lowered my guard, but still. I’d never expected to meet him of all people by chance.
“Oh! I didn’t think you’d remember my name! It’s an honor, Chieftain!” he shouted enthusiastically into the quiet night, moved that I’d called him by his name.
His volume was nothing to fault him for, of course. It was just the barbarian way.
Since fate had led us to meet, I decided to take him up in conversation.
“Of course I remember. You’re the warrior who defeated me.”
“Hahaha!” he laughed after a slight pause. “If you drink like I did, Chieftain, you’d be able to keep down much more too!”
Yeah, no thanks.
If I did that, the news that Baron Yandel pissed himself drunk would leak to the entire city.
“So why are you here?”
He hesitated again. “Aha! This is the place where my house will soon be built, so I came to see it myself!”
“What?”
“Since I’m going to have a house now, I’m too excited to sleep! I will live here until my house is fully built! Because this is my house now!”
“Uh... R-right. But why did you choose this place to build it? This is by the burial grounds...”
“Because this place is nice and cool with the wind!”
The more we talked, the more it felt like I was losing to him somehow.
Had I really misunderstood him this entire time? The feeling only continued to grow.
Is this guy really from the modern age...?

Maybe this was what the Evil Spirit Hunters from the Ministry of Security felt like when they saw me. Since they hadn’t gotten to see me floundering during the coming-of-age ceremony and only seeing my current self, they wouldn’t even think that I was an evil spirit.
Which reminded me...
“By the way, did you choose the shield during your coming-of-age ceremony?”
“Oh! I did! I didn’t think you’d remember that too! I’m honored!”
“How’s it been? Are you still using the shield?”
“I’ve changed to the axe! I chose a shield because that’s what you chose, but it didn’t suit me!”
“You chose it because I did?”
“Bjorn, son of Yandel, is the greatest warrior in history! I wanted to follow in your footsteps! Well, I gave up because it was too hard to get essences!”
What a funny guy. How would someone who opened his eyes during the coming-of-age ceremony know who I was?
I smirked, glancing down at him.
But...I still think he’s a player.
I became even more sure of it after talking to him.
As a fellow modern man, it was a bit embarrassing to admit it, but...
I used to be just like him.
Not in terms of the supreme ultimate duality of man, of course.
But once, way back, I used to act like Vector was acting right now. Whenever I crossed paths with the chieftain, I always stiffened up and acted even more barbarian-like.
Although we hadn’t been talking for long, I got a feeling.
This guy’s going to live a long time...
Losing himself in the role of the barbarian, and that single-minded drive to do whatever it took to achieve what he wanted—people like him didn’t die easily.
“But what are you doing here, Chieftain?” he asked, changing the subject before seeming to realize something. “Oh, were you going to the burial grounds again?”
“Not really. I was just on patrol.”
“Oh! Then good luck! I’m hungry, so I’m going to sleep!”
Vector seemed uncomfortable being around me, but I had no intention of letting him off with just that.
“I’ll give you some jerky, so let’s talk for a bit.”
“O-oh...! Really! Thank you! As I thought, the chieftain is a great and wise warrior!”
A few points off for hesitating a little before responding...
Well, his act as a barbarian was still passable.
“So, what do you want to talk with me about...?”
Vector asked, trying to pry for more information.
Though he was trying to act like a clueless barbarian, his curiosity was plain to see.
I didn’t blame him. I had just sprung an impromptu conversation on him, after all. Of course he would be anxious and suspicious of my intentions.
“Nothing much. I just want to hear what troubles you.”
“What troubles me...?”
Vector looked confused.
Instead of airing my troubles to him, I was offering counsel for his troubles—counsel that he didn’t even ask for.
“Tell me!” I demanded cheerily. “What troubles you?”
“No, I don’t have anything like that...”
“Nonsense! Everyone has troubles! Speak! As your chieftain, I have the right to hear them!”
“Your...right? Not duty?” he muttered.
I must have misheard that last bit, but it wasn’t that important, so I ignored it.
Vector studied me with an odd look in his eyes, as if realizing, Huh, so this chieftain guy is a real barbarian...
It offended me a little, honestly. I didn’t want to be looked at like I was the weird one when he was the one who pissed his pants.
I cleared my throat and demanded, “Anyway, tell me!”
“Well...”
“Now!”
The weight of my right as the chieftain got to him, and Vector finally told me his worries.
“Well... I’m worried about my friend.”
“Oh? Who’s this friend of yours?”
“A human ally I worked in a team with before the labyrinth closed. His name is Hans Eliburn—”
“What?!”
Vector stared at me, taken aback. “Huh, why are you surprised? Do you know him?”
“No, I just felt like saying that. So what’s going on with this friend?”
“I met him in the city not long ago, and he told me he found a good opportunity and I should start a business with—”
“Don’t do it.”
“Huh? But I didn’t even tell you what the opportunity—”
Shut up about opportunities.
Did this guy have something wrong with his head? Why was he working with a Hans?
“I said don’t, so don’t.”
I laced my words with killing intent to shock him into submission, and Vector nodded in blind agreement, shaken.
“G-got it! I won’t do it!”
Good. You should’ve just folded from the start.
“B-but can you tell me the reason?” he stammered.
“That name is unlucky.”
He just shot me a look that said, What the hell is this guy talking about?
Still, it was only for an instant, so I didn’t pay it any mind.
“Alright, then that’s your first problem resolved. Tell me about your second.”
“Second?” he echoed in confusion. “But I don’t have anything like that—”
“No, you definitely have one.”
“Uh... Money? There aren’t many ways to get—”
“That doesn’t count.”
“Then what does count if—”
“Think about it. If you can’t think of one, remember. And if you can’t remember one, ask your heart. Do you really have nothing that troubles you?”

When I pressed him again, Vector hesitated, probably realizing he needed to say something to progress through this conversation. Fortunately, when he finally did speak, his next trouble was much more worth exploring.
“I want the labyrinth to open up again,” he admitted.
“Like I told you, troubles about money aren’t troubles—”
“That’s not what I mean,” he rushed out. “I want to become stronger. This war made me want it even more.”
“Oh?”
“A lot of my warrior friends... They died during this war. If I was stronger, I would’ve been able to protect them.”
I nodded, quiet as his genuine emotions aired.
As I’d thought, the house was just an excuse. He was hanging around the burial grounds just like I was.
“It’s not your fault that you couldn’t protect them.”

“I know that. I know. Everyone needs to do what they need to do to survive in this world. I just have so many regrets. If they were still alive, they would’ve been able to laugh and enjoy this festival too, and... And we always wanted to have a house.”
“And now you’ll get one soon.”
“Yeah. But I have no friends left to share it with.”
Something crossed my mind at that.
Maybe, just maybe, this was the reason he drank to the point of pissing himself.
Even when he felt like he was going to burst open, even when he felt like giving up or passing out, he was able to hold on to see that dream through.
“That’s my second trouble...”
“I see.”
Now that he had revealed his true thoughts to me, Vector’s expression had finally relaxed.
“What should I do? Tell me, Chieftain.”
There was even a hint of expectation in his eyes. An expectation that I might be able to banish his troubles with a clean and ingenious answer.
I answered that expectation of his.
“Make new friends.”
“And become stronger. So that you won’t lose them again.”
He didn’t respond.
“Alright, that’s your second trouble fixed. I’ll go now. I’m hungry!”
