After successfully resolving the troubles of a newbie warrior I’d happened upon by chance, my steps felt a little lighter as I walked to my destination.
The cold winds howled, sending the leaves dried by the chill of winter bristling into the air.

The barbarians had once looked at this dance and said that it was the warriors of old battling each other for entertainment after becoming spirits. It was a strangely metaphorical and poetic expression for barbarians.
Barbarians didn’t bury their dead. Instead, they practiced something called sky burials, where they let the wind and rain scatter their bodies until nothing remained.
A warrior’s remains became the nutrients for the land and the trees grown upon it.
Not that building a grave would have stopped that from happening.
Brown Rotmiller
Versyl Gowland
James Calla
Like every day before, I stood in front of these three gravestones, trying to find the answer to this suffocating feeling in my heart as the wind howled around me.
Of course, just standing there didn’t automatically give me an answer.
Even in this world where ghost-type monsters existed, the voices of the dead did not speak through the wind, whispering their final wishes to me in a way that I could hear and finally understand.
No, those spiritual events didn’t exist. I was living proof of it.
They were gone.
They no longer existed in this world.
And I was the one left behind, haunted by worries they’d never have again.
What would they want for me, the person who still remained?
Riol Warb Dwalkie.
His wish for me had been simple. He just told me to take care of Missha.
And yet, in the end, I hadn’t exactly done a great job of heeding his request either. He probably wouldn’t have wanted us to be so distant with each other.
At least I’d been able to avenge him.
Though thinking back on it now, that had been more for me than him.
Instead, I stood here at another’s resting place, silent as the grave.
Although the whole city was alive with the sounds of the festival, those who had already departed had no way to enjoy them.
Festivals were for the living.
The wind howled.
I suddenly remembered the conversation I had with Vector not long ago.
“If they were still alive, they would’ve been able to laugh and enjoy this festival too.”
I couldn’t have agreed more.
Every time something good happened to me, the first thing I thought of was those who were no longer here to experience it with me.
What would it be like if Dwalkie were still here?
The dwarf would’ve pulled some mischievous prank, and Dwalkie would’ve gotten red with anger.
What would it be like if Rotmiller were still alive?
Well, maybe he might have used the festival as a vehicle to deepen his relationship with Shavin Emoor.
If Versyl Gowland, and if James Calla, and if all those who had left this world before I did were still here...
What would it be like?
I stood there silently for a long time, lost in thoughts that screamed there was no answer.
It was all just a product of my imagination. No one could know what it would have been like.
That future was already gone, erased.
Maybe that was why I felt so much regret and disappointment whenever I remembered them.
“...I’m sick of it.”
At last, I gave voice to the resentment buried deep within my heart.
This world was wrong.
Earth or Rafdonia, it didn’t matter. In the end, the two were the same.
Maybe it was just how life worked, a fundamental truth that couldn’t be changed, but that didn’t change the fact that it was wrong.
Humans, barbarians, beastpeople, elves—
“I know that. I know. Everyone needs to do what they need to do to survive in this world.”
This was a world of survival.
I was getting sick of—
That was when it hit me.
A realization of what I truly wanted.
“Ahhh...”
I didn’t want to survive.
I wanted to live.
To live with the people precious to me.
A small, wry smile tugged at my lips.
It was just a wish, something any pessimist out there would scoff at, sneering, A kind world? How could something like that possibly exist?
But who cared what they think?
I was a barbarian.
If my teeth broke, I’d bite down with my gums.
If my head had a problem, I’d just fix it.
And if I wanted to shout, I’d shout.
There was no need to overthink it, not even something of this scale.
If that world didn’t exist, I’d just make it exist.
There’s a ton of things I’ll need to do.
The gravestones stood unmoved in front of me as my mind raced with daydreams of plans and what-ifs. Then from somewhere in the distance, cheers erupted.
I checked the time.
Tick.
Yeah, I’d guessed as much from how loud they were.
This troublesome year had finally come to an end.

chapters.title: Chapter 783: Upgrade (1)
paragraphs: What day did people make the most resolutions?
If someone asked that question, most people would point to the same day.
The first of January. The day when a year ends and a new one begins.
On this day, everyone was filled with hopes and dreams.
People who felt like they had gained weight made plans to diet and exercise, and people who stayed home and played around resolved themselves to find a job in the new year.
However, only a small minority actually carried through with those resolutions.
What they wanted was change, and the world wasn’t kind to those with such desires. If one wanted to shed their shell, one needed to break it first.
And, ironically, the path to hope was paved in pain.
Yeah, the words “short-lived resolution” exist for a reason.
A person’s resolve was a fragile thing, weak and soft enough to inevitably crumble to time no matter how stable it seemed at first.
Of course, some people actually could hold onto that hard resolution of theirs, but hmm... Would those people need an occasion like the New Year to go through with their change?
Anyway.
“Did you get some good rest during the end of last year?”
“Somewhat.”
I visited the palace on the first day of the year to meet up with Astarota. It was to fulfill the resolution I made the night prior.
Last night, it felt as if my sluggish brain had whirred back to life somehow.
Not surviving, but living. What did I need to do to achieve that dream in this heartless city?

After a full night’s worth of deliberation, I had my answer: either revolt and become king or obtain power that could rival the king’s. Only then would I be able to negotiate with him, take what I wanted, or really do anything from a position on equal ground.
That was why I came to this place today.
“Astarota Berun.”
“You calling me by my first name almost rattles me. What is it?”
“Is Countess Peprok still in the same state?”
“She is.”
I expected as much, but I still hardened my heart when I heard his answer.
The marquess had told me that Ragna would wake up of her own accord with time. That was why he had left his diary for her in the first place.
But she hasn’t woken up yet...
These people had definitely done something to keep her asleep. I just didn’t have any proof yet.
“Then am I allowed to stop by and see her again before I head off today?” I asked.
“Of course.”
I’d need to talk to Hyeonbyeol later to figure out what these people were doing to Ragna, though I wasn’t expecting a clear answer.
“By the way...” Astarota began with a curious look in his eyes. “When you killed the marquess, did you perhaps see a ring nearby?”
“A ring? I don’t think so.”
“Hmm, is that so...?”
“What ring is it?”
“It’s nothing much. Just one of the treasures of the palace. But it seems he took it off before he died. Or it was taken from him.”
“Either way, I didn’t see it.”
“I see. If you say so... Then it is most likely in the hands of a Noarkan now.”

I was a little relieved to hear him say that. It meant the palace trusted the story I’d given them. However, the fact that he brought it up now unprompted meant that their detailed investigation had come to an end.
Looks like I’ve avoided one potential crisis...
Thinking back on it, it was only natural that they would believe my words.

The palace knew that the marquess and I were sworn enemies. Whatever suspicions they had of me, from their perspective, the marquess had no reason to hand over Thunder to me. It would make more sense for him to have fired Thunder to take out everyone with him.
Maybe obsessing over Ragna was dangerous. There was a slim chance that they might catch wind of the offer the marquess made while giving up his life.
“Oh, did you hear the news?” Astarota asked, catching my attention again. “A new prime minister was selected at the Palatial Meeting that you missed.”
“Who is it?”
“Duke Kealunus.”
“I see.”
“You don’t seem surprised.”
“To be honest, there isn’t anyone other than the duke who fits the role.”
Noble society was separated into three major factions: the prime minister’s faction, the duke’s faction, and the lesser nobility faction.
Well, there was also Melbeth, the nonhuman faction that I was a part of, but its political influence was too small to be taken into account.

In any case, the prime minister’s faction had effectively dissolved after the marquess betrayed the country, and most of the lesser nobility’s power had been reduced to nothing because many nobles died when Thunder fell on the Palace of Glory.
Unlike the duke’s faction, which had been able to maintain its power even during the war.
“Yandel, what do you think about the duke?”
“I think he’s lucky. It doesn’t look like he’s done anything, but his biggest competitor, the marquess, went and killed himself. And it doesn’t look like he was hurt that much by the war either.”
“Lucky. I see...”
The way he mumbled that sounded off.
“Do you have information on him?” I asked warily.
“No, nothing like that. It’s just that from experience, people who seem lucky have dirty deals festering where no one can sniff them out. But, well, maybe he is truly just lucky, as you said.”
“Tell me if you find something.”
“Sure.”

Our conversation about the duke ended there, and I continued to talk to Astarota about a few more things. For the most part, it was me asking him questions and gathering information through him. To single out the most important piece of intel...
It would be this one.
“Oh, and Yandel... Your ennoblement has been decided.”
The House of Baron Yandel would now be the House of Viscount Yandel.
Not to say that my “house” had any mansion or servants to speak of.
Oh, I guess I do have servants, though?
When looking at sheer numbers, my house had more servants than any other noble house in the nation since I had taken all the refugees of Bifron into my house.
“Did the duke have anything to say about that?”

“He wouldn’t even if he did. You are the hero who ran alone into the middle of enemy territory, killed the marquess, and drew this war to a momentary end. Ah— Do you two have some bad blood between you?”
“Not really. But we aren’t friends either.”

“Even less of a reason for him to stop your ennoblement, then. However, it did seem that he had some complaints about the event. Due to the situation, your ennoblement ceremony and his inauguration as the prime minister will take place at the same time.”
“What does that matter?” I asked, confused. “I don’t see why he would have a complaint about that.”
Astarota just stared at me for a second before smirking. “Seems you genuinely haven’t realized yet. That’s a relief. If you weren’t genuine, it’d make you seem like an asshole.”
“Whatever. Just tell me.”
“Think about it. If both events happen at the same time, who do you think will be the main character of the event?”

I hadn’t thought that far. Still, it made sense that the star of the show would not be the person who became prime minister because the position happened to become vacant, but instead the war hero, me.

“From what I heard, he even said it was fine to delay his inauguration to a later date if it meant we could separate it into two distinct events, but our situation isn’t so flexible we could accommodate that.”
Whatever the case, it meant that my ennoblement and the duke’s inauguration would happen at the same place at the same time.
“Are you going to visit Countess Peprok before you go?”
“Only for a little bit.”
“How devoted.”
Around the time the conversation was coming to an end and I was getting up out of my seat, Astarota suddenly asked me something, as if he just remembered it.
“Oh, right. I have one more thing I want to ask. Are you close with Jerome Saintred?”
Why was the village chief brought up here?
“Not particularly,” I said dryly. “We were part of that basement floor expedition together, but that’s all. Why do you ask?”
“On the day Thunder fell on the Palace of Glory, Jerome Saintred also went missing.”
“So?”
“Although some people say that he should be filed under ‘killed-in-action,’ I have a feeling that there is another reason for this. I just asked you to see if you knew anything.”
“Unfortunately, I don’t know about him.”
“Then I’ve wasted your time... You may leave.”
With that, I left Astarota in the room.
Missing...
I also didn’t think that the village chief died in the war. Either he was swept up in something or decided to hide himself of his own free will.
I thought back to my final meeting with the village chief.
Right before Thunder fell, the village chief came to me in my underground prison and told me something ominous.
“It will soon begin. The day when everything burns.”
And sure enough, Thunder fell right then, and the village chief quickly ran off while saying this:
“Survive. I have something to tell you when you do.”
At the time, I’d been too preoccupied to think much of it, but it was odd thinking back on it now. Unlike what the village chief said, I couldn’t say that everything burned down during the war—
...I guess it did?
District 7 and District 8 had both been burned to the ground by the war.
However, I was the one who started the fire, and the way the village chief spoke pointed to something else on the horizon. He spoke as if the entire world was soon going to come to an end.
But in the end, the world didn’t end...
The war was stopped, and I was alive. However, even though he told me he had something to tell me, the village chief never came to visit me, and now I was hearing the news that he had hidden himself.
What did he know that made him so frantic?
I still didn’t know, but the one thing I was sure of was that I needed to find the village chief and at least stop the Heart of Karui from falling into the hands of the palace.
Because even though I had no idea what he was going to do with it, the village chief was the one in possession of the Heart of Karui.
I visited the room Ragna was in before I left the palace.
She was still sleeping like a princess, and Hyeonbyeol was at her side, protecting her.
“Are you really planning on staying here until she wakes up?”
“We don’t know what will happen if I leave.”
Hmm, but if the palace put their mind to doing something to her, Hyeonbyeol’s presence didn’t make much difference...
Of course, I didn’t say that out loud.
“Did anything happen while you were here?” I asked.
“Literally nothing happens. I’m bored out of my mind, you know? And that son of the prime minister is also freed now, so I have no one to talk to...”
“That...sure does sound boring.”
The son of the traitorous prime minister, Eltora Tercerion, had been tried and set free not long ago.
Even though his father was the traitor, the fact that he betrayed his father and helped me was taken into account...But honestly, Astarota was the most important factor.
Not that he personally vouched for him or anything.
What will he do now...?
As he wished, Eltora was able to save his life at least.
Although he lost all authority as a noble, that was to be expected.
Many people will hate him...
The war had created tens of thousands of refugees, so the surname “Tercerion” would only bring out the ire of the people.
Maybe it’d be easier for him to continue living his life if he abandoned his last name and just lived as ‘Eltora’.
Well, let’s just visit him later when I have the time...
I left my train of thought about Eltora there.
It was just personal curiosity regarding how he was doing. It wasn’t particularly important for me to know.
“I’ll see you later.”
“Eh... Already?”
“I’ll visit again soon.”
“So you say, but it’s been a really long time since the last time you visited us.”
“I’m serious this time. I’ll probably be visiting the palace a lot in the future.”
“The palace?”
Hyeonbyeol looked at me with a curious look. She then just straight up stared at me.
“I think...something’s changed about you,” she said slowly.
“Changed?”
“I don’t really know how to explain, it’s just a small change...”
“Good change or bad change?”
“Of course it’s a good one! And your face looks brighter than before. It’s good to see.”
Even while thinking she was too observant, I also agreed with her point. I had also seen that my reflection in the mirror hadn’t looked that good for the past however long.
“Then, I’ll be going.”
And so, after finishing my business at the palace and returning to the holy land, I noticed that a guest had come to find me.
“Ah, you’re finally here!”
It was Erwen’s uncle.

chapters.title: Chapter 784: Upgrade (2)
paragraphs: Beleg Shucia di Tersia.
Erwen’s uncle from her mother’s side, and an evil spirit from another world who operated as Crescent at the Round Table.
Honestly, I didn’t particularly want to meet with this guy.
In a sense... No, there was no sense to make of it. Even if I tried my best to justify my actions, it didn’t change the fact that I deceived him.
“It’s definitely different from the stories of legend...”
“Thanks to you, I am able to let go of this foolish dream of mine.”
“However, I cannot seem to thank you.”

The day Round Table came to an end, I revealed the conditions for using the Stone of Revival that I had been deliberately withholding from him. I’d watched as a deep sense of emptiness clouded his eyes.
And yet, he was still looking for the Stone of Revival, even now...
Maybe I got the wrong guy?
To clear my sudden doubt, I decided to let him sit and confirm one thing first.
“The Stone of Revival can only revive two people. However, to use it on someone, they need to not be dead for long, and the corpse needs to be present as well. Did you know these things?”
“I did.”
Hmm, so he knew...
This practically confirmed that he was Crescent.
I just asked him directly, “Who are you trying to revive?”
“Me.”
“Huh?”
“I want to use the Stone of Revival on myself.”
What?
My mind went blank at his absurd declaration. I couldn’t even believe I was hearing this...

He seemed to notice, as he quickly added, “As I am the one making the request, I will tell you everything honestly. The people I originally wanted to save with the Stone of Revival were Belua and Daria.”
“Belua?”
“The mother of these children. And my... My younger sister.”
“But?”

“But I don’t have the intact corpses of either. Just in case, I didn’t cremate the burnt body of Daria and buried her instead, and I even periodically and secretly went and dug up her body to apply preservation magic on it... However, when I learned that the recipient couldn’t have been dead for long, I stopped.”
I was shocked. So up until recently, Daria’s body had been preserved inside a box nearly perfectly.
Does this guy have a problem with his head?
Hearing him talk about these ludicrous things with such a calm voice, I felt a chill go down my spine.
However, that and this were different problems.
“I get that you’re grieving because you can’t bring either of them back...” I began. “But then, why did you come to the conclusion that you need to use the Stone of Revival on yourself?”
My logical faculties felt like they would break down at that unbelievable conclusion, but I actually ended up accepting the reasoning he gave me.
“Because I heard that when you use the Stone of Revival... you lose all memories you had when you were alive.”
Ah...
“I need the Stone of Revival,” he said, voice bold and unwavering. “If I want to keep living.”
I nodded.
In many ways, it was ironic. The Stone of Revival was needed to make a living person alive...
Even though it sounded nonsensical, it also made sense somehow. Probably because I’d experienced something similar before.
My head hurt.
It felt like my brain was being overloaded.
I knew the best way through something like this was to make the problem as simple as possible. He was a man suffering through life, but I was still just myself with no obligation to him.
“So that’s why you want the Stone of Revival from me?”
“That’s right.”
“And I know you’re not asking for it for free. What will you give me?”
“As I’ve lived my life without any desires, there isn’t much I can give you. Except this one body of mine.”
What?
Surely, I was just weird to think that there was something off about the way he said that, right?
Yeah, probably.
“You can command me as you wish. Be it in the labyrinth, the city, or even the world outside the city. I will follow you wherever you go and do whatever you want me to.”
To put it simply, he was willing to put himself into servitude for the Stone of Revival.
“I am confident in my skills, even as I am. Beyond not holding you back, I believe I will be of great help to you.”
“You would be helpful, yeah. But what if that isn’t worth as much as the Stone?”
He didn’t even have a moment of hesitation.
“I will stay with you until it is.”
It was enough to make me embarrassed to ask in the first place.
Hearing his quick and determined response, I let out an inward sigh.
He was still the same, back when he wore the Crescent mask, and even now. Even after being pushed around so much at the Round Table, he was still able to give an unbelievable deal like this.
“And what will you do if I abuse you for all you have and not hold up my word?”
“I know that you aren’t that type of person. And more importantly, it doesn’t matter even if you do.”
“It doesn’t matter?”
For the first time, he hesitated to answer me.
However, I decided not to ask him. I already had a guess as to why.

When one lived their life in the world, they would sometimes meet people like this. Those who live without thought, as if they have no desire for their own life. Most people like that had a certain look in their eyes, like him.
I sighed.
That was what made this even more complicated.
If it were anyone else, I wouldn’t need to even think this much because I would’ve refused them immediately.
Even though I had no idea how powerful Beleg was, there was no way it would be worth as much as the Stone of Revival.
However, the problem was...
He’s Erwen’s uncle.
The longer we talked, the more grim possibilities popped up in my mind.
If this guy suddenly hung himself, how would Erwen react?
And how would I feel? If the one I had deceived for so long at the Round Table couldn’t bear not achieving his goal and closed his eyes after a final moment of suffering...
It didn’t take long for me to make my decision.
The Stone of Revival was an item to save the dead, not the living.
“Alright. I’ll let you join the group. But, as you said, I’ll decide when I’ll give you the Stone of Revival.”
To save the living, I needed something a bit more warm than this stone.
It took only three days for Beleg’s membership to be finalized on paper.
He quickly severed all of the political and emotional ties he had in the holy land and officially joined the Anabada Clan.
However, he didn’t relocate to move in with us either.
His sole request was that if there was no urgent work, he wanted to spend time taking care of May, who would be staying alone in the holy land, and I allowed him to do so.
“Uncle joined our clan?”
I ended up only informing Erwen after everything was done, and her reaction was calmer than I worried.
To be precise, she gave a faint reaction.
“Well... He’ll be on a different team than me, right...?”
“Probably.”
“Then it doesn’t matter.”
Unrelated to her care and love for her uncle, she didn’t seem to want to see him often.
I had a feeling I knew why.
There were many cases where parents who lost their child ended up divorced. Even when they want to stay with each other, the hurt would become more noticeable when they saw each other.
I couldn’t understand that in the past, but I somewhat did at this point.
For the wound to heal, one sometimes needed to not pay the wound any attention. If you kept rubbing it, it could just get worse.
In any case, I decided to observe the two of them a bit more closely going forward.
“This is the document that has the list of all the items that were registered in the Alminus Central Exchange today. They’ll be put up tomorrow morning if nothing comes up during their inspections.”

Recently, I’d asked for Amelia’s help in checking on all the items that were being put up on the exchange every day. The reason was simple. Recently, there had been many rare items registered on the exchange that would never come up in the past.
“Oh, thanks. There’s a few that have caught my eye today too, even though I just scanned through it.”
“I thought it was a one-time thing, but there are a lot of things that are being put up on the market,” Amelia said, speaking as if she had no idea why. But I had a theory.
“Many nobles died during the war.”
Many different noble houses were destroyed after Thunder fell on the Palace of Glory. Many houses lost their house heads, and others even lost their successors as well.
But even through all this, the houses would select a suitable person to succeed the house.
“This is the effect of that phenomenon.”
This was a time when all noble houses were in a difficult position. And in such a time, what would be the first order of business for the newly appointed house heads?
They would sell off the expensive things they had no use for to acquire money.

However, since no one would be visiting the Heavenly Exchange that people of their league would’ve gone to, all their goods were being funneled into the central exchange that was still operating at a large scale.
Amelia nodded in understanding at my explanation.
“So something like the Ruby of Nomilat?”
I couldn’t hide my excitement, even knowing it would only encourage Amelia’s teasing. “Did you find a way to obtain it? I heard that someone else bid on it already.”
“There is a way if you just know where to look.” She grinned as if she actually obtained the item.
“Just how? Did another one get registered?”

“No way another one of that would get registered. I secretly infiltrated the exchange and checked on the registry. I then found the one who put up the item for sale and made a request to sell the item to us, and I told him we’d cover his fees to take it down.”
“And he accepted it?”
I regretted asking right after I did. If the seller hadn’t accepted, Amelia wouldn’t even have brought it up.
“I put your name forward and said you needed it, and he just agreed without asking about anything else. Ah, but he told me to tell you his name. Viscount Bertan.”
“Viscount Bertan...”
Although I hadn’t interacted with him, I knew of his house. House of Viscount Bertan had a long history, but they weren’t that powerful or famous. They were one of the houses in the lesser nobility.
“Oh, and I just asked out of curiosity, but the ruby’s apparently been used as a piece of decoration in the hall on the first floor.”
“What...?”
Using something that precious as decoration?
Tsk, this was why nobles were...
It wouldn’t have come up on the exchange if the situation wasn’t like this.
In any case, I was thankful.
Finding consumable items like this was the most difficult to do on the exchange.
“But... What are you going to use it for? I heard that it increases your strength if you eat it, but I don’t think you’d be this excited just for that.”
“Ah, what I’m going to use it for?” I grinned at Amelia’s question. “This is the final ingredient I need for Stage 8 spirit imprint.”
I had finally gathered all I needed.
Fifteen materials were needed for Stage 8 of the spirit imprint. However, most of them could easily be found in the city and bought with money.
All except three of them.
The three core materials of Stage 8 were all drops from rank three monsters, so it was extremely difficult to obtain them.
However, I was lucky enough to obtain two of the drops when I went outside the city walls...
I’ve finally got them all.
Through the help of Amelia’s excursion, I was able to obtain the final material to become one step stronger.
Well, I wasn’t getting that much stronger than before, but it was very important that I was only one step away from Stage 9.
Because that becomes possible at Stage 9.
After reaching Stage 9 and eating two more essences, my great and precious shield barbarian build would be complete...
[You have activated Immortality Imprint Stage 8.]
Only a few more steps to go.

chapters.title: Chapter 785: Upgrade (3)
paragraphs: Immortality Imprint’s Stage 8 didn’t have any boost in stats. Instead, it gave me an additional effect.
[The spirit imbued within the body is strengthened.]
[When casting Wild Outburst, damage will be dealt to all nearby undead types.]
[The effect Favorite Weapon has been added onto the unique effect Union.]
Now, I dealt additional damage to the undead whenever I used Wild Outburst, and an additional effect was added to Union.
Favorite Weapon was an effect that strengthened my weapon depending on how much I used said tool. The condition for getting these stacks was defeating a monster with that weapon at least once a day.
Unequipping the weapon didn’t remove all the stacks, but if I switched my primary weapon to something else, I’d need to begin stacking the buffs again.
It takes a thousand days to get full stacks of the weapon.

Although it’d take around three years to max out, my odds were pretty good. After all, shields were considered weapons in Dungeon and Stone. Plus, I already had Kraul’s Demon Grinder and Wall of Aegis. Since I’d gotten the graduation weapons early, I wouldn’t need to re-stack them later down the line.
If I just diligently began stacking them now, they’d be fully stacked at some point sooner than later.
The problem is that the labyrinth is still closed...
The conditions of killing at least one monster every day meant that there was no way for me to get any stacks right now.
Not that it was an easy condition to fulfill even when the labyrinth reopened.
Even if I do hundred-day expeditions, I’d need ten of them...
It definitely wasn’t an easy condition.
I had only ever done one hundred-day expedition, and it was the basement floor expedition.
But what about the monsters outside the city walls? Will those count as well?
That piqued my curiosity, but I couldn’t confirm for now. I decided to leave that to later.
I turned my head to the side to check on the shaman who had let out a deep breath. Beads of sweat ran down his cheek from how much he had exerted himself.
“It’s done, Chieftain. How about it? Do you like the new powers at your disposal?”
“I do.”

The operation for the Stage 8 imprint took longer than any other stage, done over three days. The shaman told me that it couldn’t be helped that a high-level imprint like this would take time, but from my perspective...
It didn’t take this long in the game.
From my perspective, it seemed to be an issue with this guy’s skill.
Still, the imprint itself seemed to have been upgraded just fine.
“By the way... Chieftain, there is something you should know.”
The shaman called out to me just as I was getting tired of sitting around and was about to leave the stuffy tent. Despite my unease at the way he said it, I looked back at the shaman.
“I can’t engrave the stage 9 imprint with my power...”
Then came the shocking news that I was expecting to hear.
“Can’t with your power? You’re a shaman.”
“It’s just that... I haven’t fully learned stage 9 from my master yet.”
“You couldn’t learn it?”
“N-not that I couldn’t... But I’m not confident. From stage 9 onward, the imprint is engraved deep within the soul, so it’s much much more difficult!”
The random piece of news was saddening, but this situation was even worse than I expected.
“I’ve learned the method somewhat, so I can attempt it... But if I fail, you’ll need to risk your life as well, Chieftain...!”
Ignoring the fact that I would need to risk my life for the stage 9 imprint, the state he was in made it clear that stage 10 would be an impossibility.

The small picture was that I would need to give up getting my imprint upgraded, but the big picture was that this was a threat to our barbarian race. The skills of spirit imprints, the most important to our race, could be permanently lost to history. It was something I couldn’t ignore as the chieftain.
“Is there a way?” I demanded.
“Well... There is one...”
“What? There is?”
What an unexpected piece of good news.
The feeling was somehow unfamiliar, what with all the unanswerable problems I’d been dealing with for so long.
Well, not that I was complaining.
“What is it? Tell me.”

“After I received my master’s skills, his health rapidly deteriorated. He was able to come to before and teach me some things here and there, but he can’t even wake up now. He won’t last long at this rate.”
“Just get to the point.”
“We just need to heal the master of his illness!”
Huh?

“My master, the previous shaman, can do the highest level spirit imprints without a problem. And he was the one who did the imprints on the former chieftain as well. And if I learn a bit more from him, I should be able to do the highest level imprints by myself too!”
Hmm... I understood what he was trying to say. Plus, it was beneficial for me if one of the only two shamans in the tribe got better as well. But was that even realistically possible?
“But how can we help heal him? I remember a priest saying he couldn’t do anything about it before.”
“That’s right, but I found a new method recently.”
“Then tell me what that is. Stop going around the topic like the humans.”
“But... It could be difficult for you.”
“Argh, just tell me!” I barked, letting a hint of my anger show to emphasize my point.
The young shaman flinched for a second before carefully revealing, “We need a dragon’s heart.”
Maybe I shouldn’t have asked him.
In a sense, this was a type of quest.
The category, if I were to give one, would be a “race” quest, and the contents would look something like this:
[Race Quest
Description: Heal the previous shaman.
Requires: Dragon’s Heart.
Reward: Unlocks Spirit Imprints of Stage 9 and above.
Penalty upon failure: The previous shaman will pass away and skills related to the highest level of spirit imprints will be lost forever within the barbarian race.]
The quest itself was simple. If I came back with the dragon’s heart, I would be rewarded. The problem was...
A dragon’s heart...
The quest difficulty was far too high.
There were frequent cases where people sold the hearts of dragon-like monsters like drakes and called them dragon hearts, but this quest was asking for an actual Dragon’s Heart.
First of all, true dragons started appearing from Floor 9. They also appear as rift Guardians on Floor 8, but... Even if I mobilized my entire clan, we didn’t have what it took to raid a dragon.
Well, maybe if we spent a long time doing it...
But we’d need to kill it with distortion magic on it too.
Considering the success rate of distortion magic, this was a quest that could only be completed if we were strong enough to kill not just one, but multiple dragons safely and reliably.
There was one more problem added to all this.
Will the previous shaman be able to hold out while we try to get the heart?
Well, my feeling was that there was a good chance he couldn’t.
I was wondering why I got the answer to the problem so easily.
This was practically a no-answer solution.
The other way I could complete this quest was to receive the dragon’s heart from someone else...
...the palace probably has at least one of them.
The problem was that there was no way the palace would hand over something that valuable for free.
I sighed. I was seriously contemplating just ignoring the future of the barbarian tribe and giving up early for the sake of my mental health.
Let’s think through this slowly. It feels like I need to get at it either today or tomorrow, but it’s not like the shaman is on the verge of death either.
With that, I decided to just hold onto the new quest I received and resolve the problems already in front of me over time.
As I always said, there was a priority to everything, and the highest priority work for me at the moment was definitely this.
“Yandel, a letter from the palace arrived.”
“What does it say?”
“The date for the ennoblement ceremony was decided.”
Strictly speaking, it wasn’t my ceremony.

Of course, my noble rank was being increased, but it was also the place for Duke Kealunus’s inauguration as prime minister, and also the succession ceremony for the many nobles who would be inducted as the head of their families...
It’s like a school function. Why are they doing so many events at the same time?
I didn’t know the details of the situation, but for some reason, I got the sense that Astarota, the man considered the proxy for the king, had a heavy hand in this.
I could tell he hated bothersome things just like I did.
“Ohhh! Then Bjorn is going to be a count now! Count Yandel! That’s a cool name!”
“It’s viscount, not count.”
“Huh? What’s a viscount?”
There was no point telling Ainar the order of nobles, so I didn’t waste my time on it.
“Hmm? Bjorn? Where are you going?”
“I’m going to sleep. I’m hungry.”
The ceremony would be held a week from today. Since there was some time left, I decided to not do much during the time and did some administrative work instead.
I met with Shavin Emoor, who oversaw most operations of the barbarian race and checked on how she was doing while chatting about professional matters.
From what I could tell, she seemed to have recovered somewhat.
She seemed worried and wished to see Ragna, the one person she could call her friend, but I didn’t mention her situation to her.
Ragna was royalty, so even if I told Shavin her situation in the palace, she would only get more stressed.
“These are cookies sold in the bakery in Karnon. Eat them while you work.”
“Ah... Thank you.”
With that, I concluded the conversation by handing her some thoughtful gifts I’d gotten for her.
After that, I spoke with Amelia to talk about our team compositions.
Due to the war, we had some open slots in our combat forces, though we did gain new members to fill those holes too.
“That’s surprising. For Arua Raven to leave the military and join us...”
“Hmm? Shouldn’t you be more surprised about Erwen’s uncle than Raven?”
“Not really. He’s just a regular old man.”
“Huh?”
Amelia seemed more focused on Raven’s “re-joining” than Beleg.
Well, Raven was the one prophesied to betray me, so it was understandable.
“Still, our numbers are the same as before, so we can still just operate in two teams.”
“That’s true. And the open vice-captain slot needs to be filled as well.”
“Vice-captain...”
“Do you not want to do it? If you can take that role and lead the second team, I’d feel—”
“Impossible.”
Tsk, I didn’t know what she hated so much about the position.
By personality and experience, Raven is perfect... But I can’t really give her that promotion when she just joined the clan again...
I fell into thought.
How should we separate and allocate our members into teams?

Although I could wait and see since we weren’t in much of a hurry, it was better to have things like this taken care of before they were needed. And from the rumors flying about, it wouldn’t be long until the labyrinth reopened—
“Chieftain! A human came to meet you at the gates!”
At that moment, one of the tribe warriors stationed as a guard at the gate quickly came over while shouting.
“Someone came to see me? Who?”
I asked for the person’s identity.

This was just the world we lived in. Some people who had enough fame and reputation could just rock up and ask for an audience without prior reservations. Yet even then, if the person who arrived was a nameless adventurer, they would’ve been turned away and treated like a weirdo.
To put it another way, the person who came to see me was someone of note...
“Illya Adnus! The guild master for the Adventurer’s Guild!”
An interesting guest had appeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 786: Upgrade (4)
paragraphs: Rafdonia’s economy relied on the mana stones mined by the adventurers risking their lives in the labyrinth. In this abomination of a system, the importance of adventurers in the city couldn’t be overstated, and naturally, the influence, power, and size of the guild that oversaw those adventures wasn’t comparable to any other organization.
Thousands upon thousands of guild members.
Hundreds of branch managers.
And regional managers who oversaw those branch managers.
And one guild master standing atop all those regional managers.
Even most nobles were expected to bow before the very name of this guild master, and they were also the one person that I had more difficulty seeing than other high-ranking nobles.
Yet that hard-to-see guy came here on his own two feet...
He was someone too important to send away just because he was here without an invitation.
My curiosity was piqued, and I sent the warrior who came to me with that message to go and bring him to me.
Honestly, I’d been wanting to have a decent conversation with the guy for a long time now. Not to mention, we had a bit of a delicate relationship.
“Who are you working for?”
“Illya Adnus...”

During the Ice Rock Expedition, one of the members, Pyke Neldine, had been ordered by the guild master to cause the expedition to fail and tried his best. He messed with the food and supplies we had, and back then, I thought that it was a political move to cause the expedition to fail so that our sponsor, the marquess, couldn’t be credited with success.
However...
The expedition itself was a sham.
In the end, when I realized that the marquess was planning on abandoning us from the beginning, my evaluation of the guild master couldn’t help but change as well.
Perhaps the guild master’s goal wasn’t to disrupt the expedition, but simply just to save us?
That was just a hypothesis, of course. Nothing had been confirmed.
Well, I’d be able to hear the truth this time if I got lucky.
“Ainar, go and play outside.”
“Sure!”
After sending Ainar out, the guest I was waiting for arrived shortly after.
“It has been some time, Baron Yandel. First, let me thank you for allowing this audience when I didn’t contact you prior to visiting.”
“I had some time open, so don’t worry about it.”
“Thank you.”
In truth, this wasn’t my first time meeting the guild master.
Given his position, it wasn’t odd to see him at official functions of the palace.
We’d exchanged greetings with him even at the ceremony that was held after the Ice Rock Expedition was complete.
“So, what is it? Such a sudden visit,” I asked directly as soon as he sat down.
The guild master seemed a little taken aback, apparently not used to getting straight into the thick of it even without being served a cup of tea.
“Just speak freely. I’m going to get hungry at this rate.”
The guild master only then seemed to realize who I was, as he smirked and matched my pace.
“I apologize for not being able to do more during the Ice Rock Expedition.”
He was practically confessing he knew exactly what intentions the marquess had for that expedition. I could also tell that he was trying to gauge just how much I knew about the situation.
Although it was far from the direct exchange of words that I wanted, it couldn’t be helped.
Compared to the people who would spend thirty minutes going over pleasantries, this was exceedingly direct already.
I spoke around the topic a little as well to match my guest.
“No, you’ve done as much as you could. And considering the amount of power the marquess held, I believe you’ve risked enough.”
These were words that revealed that I knew the happenings regarding Pyke Neldine, and that I had a general understanding of what happened in the background as well.
The guild master gave a bitter nod.
“I am thankful you think that way.”
Just how many times was this guy going to thank me?
“I don’t need that, so speak,” I said, waving him off. “What’s your business here today?”
The guild master began to speak, though it was more like the prologue to the main topic.
“I heard that as a reward for dealing with that traitor, your noble status would be elevated to that of a viscount...”
“So?”
“I will be frank with you. The labyrinth will reopen starting from next month.”
“Hmm, I see.”
He paused. “Did you perhaps know about that?”
“I heard that it would open soon, not the exact date it would.”
“Well, considering your position, I suppose it isn’t odd that you were notified in advance.”
“Are you saying you aren’t in that position?”

“Even as the guild master of the Adventurer’s Guild, I don’t have omnipotent authority nor am I treated as such,” the guild master said humbly in response. “I only receive information regarding the labyrinth earlier than the others.”
“From the way you said that, I suspect that you have more information other than the labyrinth opening.”
“We don’t know how long this will be in place, but the labyrinth will not open on the first day of the month.”
“Not on the first day?”

While the conversation overall was boring, I couldn’t help my shock at that particular reveal. Until now, the labyrinth always opened at midnight going into the first day, and the labyrinth would close at midday the next day and spit out all the adventurers.
Well, since the palace had full control of when the portals opened and closed, they could change the time it opened, but that only created questions to answer.
“Why are they doing that?”

“It is because of Noark, so that they can’t prepare themselves and enter the labyrinth. The palace will open the portal at random times and only allow a small group of adventurers whose skills and identity have been confirmed to enter the labyrinth.”
“Oh?”
“Since this must be kept top-secret, the portal also won’t be opened in the Dimensional Squares, but only in the imperial capital of Karnon.”
“Now that, I didn’t know.”

“We only heard the news first since we’d have to do some prior preparation such as selecting the adventurers. You would’ve heard it soon enough as well. Even the nobles aren’t so foolish that they would leave you out and discuss it amongst themselves.”
Foolish...
The use of that word told me that the guild master didn’t see the nobles in a good light. Since I was a barbarian, his perspective of me as a noble must have been different.
Of course, the important thing here wasn’t the guild master’s personality.
“So what are you trying to say?” I insisted. “I don’t think you’ve come here personally just to tell me this news.”
The guild master finally told me his true reason for being here. “I heard that the Anabada Clan has eleven members split into two teams and that you have one slot open.”
“And?”
“I want to take that slot.”
Was something in the water these days?
Illya Adnus, was, in truth, a well-known figure even among the regular citizens.
Before this round of dimensional collapses, during the time called the Golden Age, he was a famous high-ranking adventurer, but his true fame came about during his second life after his retirement.
I had gone and investigated this man as well.

At the age of thirty-seven, he joined the guild as an advisor. At thirty-eight, he became a branch manager and made many successful policies that were favored by the adventurers and even showed his ability by becoming the regional manager at age forty-one. At forty-seven, he defeated the former guild master and was voted into the highest position in the guild, and he had been maintaining that position ever since.
Guild master in just ten years...
His path in life alone made it so that no one could deny that this man was a person of extraordinary talent.
But so what?
“Why should I give you a spot in my clan?”
“You may not know... But I was also an adventurer for a long time. I won’t drag you down—”

“I know that. Illya Adnus, you were a rank 3 adventurer before you retired, right? Your nickname was the Black Hunter. I know that you started off as a scout before becoming a combat member in the middle.”
Illya Adnus would be a valuable addition to post parties. Of course, just because he was skilled, it didn’t mean I was going to enter the labyrinth with someone I didn’t know.
“You’ve investigated quite a bit. Not many know that I began my career as a scout.”
“You should’ve expected as much. You’re the guild master of the one and only Adventurer’s Guild.”
He let out a deep sigh at that.

Honestly, he probably wasn’t used to situations like this either. Usually, his position as the guild master probably let him have the upper hand in most conversations, but titles like that didn’t work at all against me.
The chieftain of the barbarians.
A baron of Rafdonia.
An adventurer who had left his name on the Stone of Honor, Bjorn, son of Yandel.
Just with these three, I had no reason to cower in front of a mere guild master.
And on top of all that, he was the one requesting something of me.
“Don’t hide anything and tell me straight. Then I will take serious consideration of your request,” I said. “Why are you making this request at all?”

I was planning on stopping the conversation there if he tried to talk around the subject or add on some conditions. However, he seemed to have gotten the picture, so he took some small breaths before slowly beginning to speak.
“I need an achievement.”
“Achievement?”

“The position of the guild has weakened quite a bit due to the labyrinth being closed for such a long time. It’s not the guild’s fault that the labyrinth was sealed, but they are looking for something to blame.”
Something to blame...
A grin crept over my face. “But the people aren’t blaming the guild, but you. Correct?”
The guild master didn’t respond.
I think I get the gist of the situation.
The fast-track second life of Illya Adnus had finally hit a wall.

The people who had been vying for his position even before this were now using this situation as a catalyst to drag him down. And that was why Illya himself was trying to break straight through as well.
“In any case, you’ve concluded that my clan is the only place you have hopes of getting an achievement.”
“That’s right...”
I couldn’t hide my disappointment at how easily he nodded to my deduction.

The image of this person I had in my head was different from reality. The fact that he put that spy into the expedition force even though he could’ve antagonized the marquess made me think he was someone working toward some great cause.
Maybe he was just in a political situation where he needed to take that action...
There was a chance I could see more sides of this man if I gave it the time, that was my feelings about him for the time being.
He was a guild master, and only a guild master.
I couldn’t sense anything special about his character or person whatsoever.
“What is in it for me if I agree to this request?”
“Firstly, the rank of the Anabada Clan will be raised to the highest rank under the authority of the guild master, and even outside that, your treatment within the guild—”
“You can stop them,” I interrupted, quickly cutting him off.

I’d asked just in case, but nothing was enticing enough for me. Raising the rank of the clan wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows either. Even if he said he’d treat the clan well within the guild, that was just changing how we were seen by others, and I could do that myself if I wanted to.
“Let’s stop there. It’s a shame, but you’ll need to look somewhere else to gain this achievement of yours.”
It was the cleanest refusal I could give him. However, the guild master couldn’t let go of his desire.
“What is it you want?”

He was asking as if he would provide me with anything I wanted. Maybe if he were the king I would take him seriously, but it was pretty funny hearing a guild master who was just about to get demoted say that.
“A Dragon’s Heart,” I said nonchalantly, figuring I’d throw it out there. “I’ll let you join if you give me one.”
“What?”
“You don’t have one? Then let’s stop here and—”
Right as I was about to tell him to leave, the guild master cut me off. “Alright. I’ll give it to you.”
“Huh?”
He had one?

chapters.title: Chapter 787: Upgrade (5)
paragraphs: I didn’t doubt my ears.
Honestly, rather than one of my bodily facilities malfunctioning, chances were better that he just gave me a blank check.
I lowered my voice and spoke coldly. “With the life you have lived, I trust that you understand the weight of your words.”
It was an unbelievable offer. The Dragon’s Heart was an invaluable treasure, so how could a mere guild master possess—
“Of course I understand.”
“Do you really have a Dragon’s Heart?”
“To be precise, the guild has one.”
What? Was he messing with me?

When I scoffed, the guild master just shrugged as he continued, saying, “It is an object that has been stored for hundreds of years at this point, so who would notice if it disappeared? And only the guild master has permission to check that particular treasure.”
“Wow...” I exclaimed, unable to hold it in.
I had a rough idea as to what he was trying to say.

If he could maintain his position as guild master for the rest of his life, nothing would happen to him even if he gave me the Dragon’s Heart that was in the guild’s vault. However, that just made his earlier declaration all the more shocking.
Eventually, I’d collected myself enough to ask, “How are you going to deal with the aftermath...?”
Was he only planning on living for a few more years?
No one could maintain the guild master position forever. Even if he could accomplish his goals in the time he had left, he would one day need to hand over his position to someone else.
“The moment it is discovered that you gave away the Dragon’s Heart, you and even your family will need to pay for that sin.”
“You don’t need to worry about that. My wife and children have already benefited greatly thanks to me. So they will need to share my weight in failure as well.”
That was the second exclamation I gave in this short exchange.
Did this guy have something really wrong with his head?
“And there is a saying famous amongst gamblers. Do you know it?”
“What is it?”
“You just need to win and pay it back. No matter how long it takes, I just need to procure a new Dragon’s Heart and put it in before I step down from my position as guild master. Isn’t that right?”
Wow...
I barely held back letting out a third exclamation in such a short timeframe, then confirmed one last thing.
“Was one of your ancestors a barbarian?”
“Not that I know of?”
Okay then...
I decided to allow the guild master to join our clan. When I asked Amelia to go look into it, it was confirmed that the guild did possess a Dragon’s Heart.
I still didn’t like the idea of taking someone I barely knew into the labyrinth with me, but...
I can’t afford to refuse him. I’ll never know when I can get another chance to obtain that item.
Of course, there was one more question I wasn’t able to answer yet.

The value didn’t add up. No matter how important the position of guild master was, it didn’t make sense that he would give me the Dragon’s Heart just for the opportunity to take up the empty slot in our clan. Even if it wasn’t his own property, it was the property of the guild, and from what I could tell, he was planning on replacing it later with his own means.
“I think there’s more than he let on...”
“His position within the guild did seem unstable. A lot of stagnation as well. This looks like his final gamble.”
“But if it’s still bothering you, I can look into it further.”
“I’ll leave it to you.”
I decided to let Amelia investigate more about the guild master...
“Let’s get going. The others should be waiting for us.”
“Got it.”
As we headed to the rendezvous point with Amelia, the other members waiting for us in the open field welcomed us.
I had gathered all the members of the Anabada Clan in one place for the first time in a while.
“Oh, you’re here?”
“It’s been a while, Kaislan. Have you rested well?”
“Well, I did rest quite well since I wasn’t called... But what’s with those three?”
“Two are new members joining the clan, and the third is an honorary member who will be going into the labyrinth with us.”
“An honorary member...?”
“I’ll explain it to everyone, so listen up.”
Kaislan’s eyes were veiled with doubt, but he decided to hold back his questions until my explanation was done.
“I apologize for calling you all when you were resting. There are just a few things I need to inform you all about. The most important one is that the labyrinth will soon open again.”
“Oh... Is that true?”
“We’ll be able to take in the labyrinth air for the first time in a while.”
The members grew excited when they heard the labyrinth would reopen soon.

Naturally, no one doubted the reliability of the information. I was a baron, the chieftain, and a reputed adventurer. Whenever I said something, everyone just expected I heard it from somewhere credible.
“And the second reason I called you all here is because we have new members joining us.”
I called them up one by one and introduced them.
Former Vice-Captain of the Magic Troops, Arua Raven.
Hero of the Elves, Beleg Shucia di Tersia.
Those two didn’t garner much of a reaction. Everyone knew that I had some connection with Raven in the past and that Beleg had a connection with Erwen at some point too.
“The vacant wizard and archer spots have been filled.”
“The Golden Wizard and the hero of the elves... It seems no ordinary person joins this clan anymore.”
Everyone was just a bit surprised by their skills, but they readily accepted the two into the clan. Or at least, they did until Raven pointed to the last person after giving her a short introduction.
“But why is the guild master here? Is he a new member as well?”
Raven seemed confused by the situation, and the other members reacted similarly.
“I heard that his position has been shaky recently...”
“Is he leaving all that behind just to join the clan...?”
I quickly stepped in before the situation got overblown.
“Illya Adnus isn’t officially joining us. He will just be entering the labyrinth with us for a while as an honorary member. I’m not going to bother telling you the reason, so don’t ask.”
A few people looked at me expectantly, but I completely ignored them as a shield barbarian should.
Still, there was one more topic to cover.
“In any case, the third reason that I called everyone here...is for us to remake our teams again. It will be two teams of six people entering the labyrinth together.”
As soon as the topic of team distribution was brought up, everyone turned their attention away from the guild master and back to me.

Even if we were going to combine back on the sixth floor, it was a very important topic for adventurers to know which team they would be a part of. There were instances where the twelve people would operate in one team, but we often operated in two teams depending on the situation.
“I’ve already formed the teams in advance. I will hear you out, but whether we implement those opinions or not will be made through a vote.”
I spoke of implementing democracy as a leader of the new age, but the reactions I got were surprisingly bad.
“Hah!”
“Um... Ms. Raven? Why is everyone like that?”
“Did you not check the clan rules before you joined, Mr. Adnus?”
“Ahem...”
“It’s written in the rules. The voting power of the captain is the same as the number of members in the clan. Meaning, even if we put it to a vote, if he doesn’t want it, it won’t be implemented.”
“Ah... I see...”
I cleared my throat.
If you want that, then you be the clan captain. Wouldn’t it be more unfair if I had the same voting power as a regular member when I’m the captain?
“Then I will now announce the members of Team 1.”
No matter what the members’ opinions were, I announced the squads, something I had put quite a lot of thought into. The members were as follows:
Anabada Clan Team 1:
- Vanguard, Me.
- Melee Damage Dealer 1, Missha Karlstein.
- Melee Damage Dealer 2, Kaislan.
- Ranged Damage Dealer, Beleg Shucia di Tersia (Scout).
- Wizard, Arua Raven.
- Noncombatant, Illya Adnus.
Anabada Clan Team 2:
- Vanguard, Sven Parav.
- Melee Damage Dealer 1, Ainar Fenelin.
- Melee Damage Dealer 2, Emily Raines (Scout)
- Ranged Damage Dealer, Erwen Fornacci di Tersia.
- Wizard, Lilith Marrone.
- Noncombatant, Auyen Rockrobe.
These were the best combinations I could think of.
Not that everyone agreed. As expected, Erwen protested the most.
“What? Isn’t there a mistake with this? Why am I in Team 2, and not Team 1? What? This isn’t right!”
“Please understand.”
In truth, I didn’t want to send Erwen to Team 2 either. However, this was unavoidable.
“You’re the one who said you didn’t want to be on the same team as your uncle.”
“B-but still...! Combine! Who are you going to combine with if I’m not there?!”
“Combine...? Yandel, have you combined with my niece?”
Argh, my head...
“It’s not what you think, so don’t get any weird ideas.”
The “combine” that Erwen was talking about was the Elf-Barbarian mode through her Elementalization skill.
I thought it over long and hard, but I still moved Erwen out. There wouldn’t be a need to use the combine skill until the sixth floor.
“At least give me a reason! Why am I in Team 2!”
I was more stern with Erwen’s whining than usual. “Stop.”
“Eh?”
“Request a vote if you want the change. Or be quiet.”
I was saddened to see her shocked face, but it couldn’t be helped. It wasn’t right for Erwen to act like this within the organization, and it would be even worse if I, as the leader, just let her be.
Also, on top of that...
“This is beyond expectations. I knew I would be on Team 2... But for them to be in my team as well.”
It wouldn’t be fruitful in the long run if people began to think that Team 1 and Team 2 were separated by power level. They were all members of my clan and my allies.

“Ms. Raines would be in Team 2 to lead it... And he probably sent the Blood Spirit to Team 2 so he could keep the new members closer for observations. And Ms. Fenelin was sent with us since she listens to Ms. Raines.”
“Ah, Ms. Marrone. So it was like that?”
“It’s just my guess! Hehe, but I’m glad that we’re on the same team.”
“The captain must have seen that we synergize very well.”
“Ah, maybe that’s the case? I’ll be in your care.”
By the way, these two.
Did they get really close recently?

After announcing the teams, we spent time eating together. I decided that we needed to all get a little closer before entering the labyrinth, but I didn’t expect the guild master to stay and dine with us as well.
“Ahaha... The reason I’ll be entering the labyrinth with everyone? I’m sorry. There are some extenuating circumstances... I will tell everyone later when I get the chance.”
Maybe it was because the guild master position was one achieved through politics, but he was very good with his words and wasn’t afraid to talk to people he didn’t know well.
I did wonder if it was right that the guild master was just here chatting and eating with us.
That’s his problem to deal with.
It wasn’t something I needed to concern myself with.
“Hah! You experienced something that unjust in Branch 17? I will check on it the moment I return to the guild. I truly apologize that you had to experience something like that.”
“N-no... There’s no need to do that... But thank you.”
After watching the guild master get to know the clan members better, I turned my attention to check on Raven.

As someone who had experience both as an adventurer and as a military personnel, she was mingling with the others smoothly, as expected. There were people she had known for a long time like Missha and Ainar too. We’d even explored the basement floor together.
The problem is him...

As expected, Erwen’s uncle was being left out. He didn’t drink alcohol even when offered, and whenever someone talked to him, he only responded kindly and didn’t show any effort to continue the conversation. It was as if he didn’t want to make any new deep relationships.
It’ll get better with time.
However, forcing him to do something he didn’t want to was probably counterproductive at this point. I decided to just watch him for now and spent time talking and having fun with the group myself.
And then...
“Please welcome, Baron Yandel!”
The day of the ceremony arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 788: Upgrade (6)
paragraphs: Although we left for the imperial capital of Karnon early in the morning, my ennoblement ceremony was due to start much later in the day. After all, the ceremony today wasn’t just for me.
Wondering when I’d be able to leave, I checked the schedule that the palace had sent me in advance.
The first period is...the address by the prime minister?
As all the nobles took their seats, the one who would rule this nation as the prime minister from today onward, took a step out to the podium and gave his address.
“Nia Rafdonia! May this great city have eternal glory and an unending future!”
Duke Kealunus began with a powerful bow and rallying cry. I could immediately tell he had practiced quite a bit for this moment.

From what I knew, Duke Kealunus had never been a soldier and was the type who generally kept things short and sweet with his words. His house also primarily produced a bloodline of wizards and scholars.
Oh, right. I should probably add “prime ministers” to that list.
In any case, while the opening lines of his address were pretty memorable, what followed was the usual fair.
“Those insolent traitors lusted for our impenetrable castle, but we protected our city...”
He insulted the Noarkans, prayed for the fallen, praised us for winning the war, and gave all the glory back to the palace—all of which took around an hour of our time.
With that, the first period concluded and we were off to the second: the succession ceremony.
“I ask all of you to keep this in your heart: your young blood and soul is the future of this city!”
The successors who were inheriting their houses from those killed during the war came up one by one and were given their noble titles.
Though the actual ceremony itself was boring, I had to admit I was shocked.
This many people died...?
Over two hundred people were taking over their houses.
“Ah! The future of Count Lumina is here with us! I, Duke Kealunus, acknowledge the succession of the now Count Metea Lumia in place of the royal house.”
“Haha, that young genius has become a man. I, Duke Kealunus, acknowledge the succession...”

Although the duke chose to officiate the event by keeping his personal congratulations for each successor short, the second period took a very long time. It felt like such a drag as a spectator, but the other nobles seemed to think otherwise.
“Tsk, tsk. For that wild brat to inherit the house... The House of Count Bolce has met its end.”

“And I’d argue the same with the House of Viscount Bertrand. To think a member of a branch family would inherit the title! They should have settled for announcing him as a standin until the true successor was of age, even if the child is only an infant...”
“From what I heard, their sole successor has a disability. That mongrel knew of it and set about to take the house in his hands. He even pushed for himself to become the successor.”
“Hah! What an outrageous move!”
“Save your anger. They have destroyed themselves, to be sure. Most houses will cease their business relations with the House of Viscount Bertrand.”
The veteran nobles each gave their piece about the newly appointed nobles despite the rapid-fire pace of each succession speech.
Was it because they’d spent their entire lives as nobles? They had a suspicious amount of information on the internal affairs of each house.
“They’ve all been replaced by new blood.”
“It’s the beginning of a new era...”
“What will become of this world?”
On the rare occasion, a noble would air their regrets, hopes, or worries for the new generation, yet even then...
I don’t think much is going to change just because they’ve moved on to the next generation.
Even the famous Socrates once complained that the new generation was impolite and foolish. In the end, history repeated itself.

“With that, the succession ceremony has come to an end. We thank our guests who have taken time out of their busy schedules to attend. A feast has been prepared, so please, enjoy it to your heart’s content!”

By the time it had finished, the succession ceremony had gone on much longer than expected, and everyone had lunch together. The royal orchestra continued to fill the air with their music as we ate, and dancers came out to put on an elegant show.
Not that I could enjoy them in peace.
“Lord Baron, please allow me to introduce myself. I am Metea Piesra. Is the food to your liking—?”
“Behel—LAAAAA!”
“Ah... Ahaha. That must have hit the spot...”
“It did. Because I can’t hit you in a spot.”
“Pardon?”
“I’m eating, so move.”
Nobles who I didn’t even know existed before today came to speak to me as I tried to eat my food. Most of them were the young nobles who had just inherited their house.
Well, looks like there’s a bit of a generational gap...

Maybe it was because they were young, but nobles usually didn’t want to get familiar with nonhuman nobles like me. Hmm, or maybe my reputation was so great that those discriminatory factors didn’t apply to me.
“Haha, my young friend! Have you been well? It’d be a great joy if you came to the next festival...”

Still, while most of the people who came to talk to me were young nobles, not all of them were. These exceptions included Count Alminus, who periodically paid me my friend fee, Count Ferdehilt, who offered me his daughter’s hand in marriage every time we met, and so on.
In other words, the nobles who had formed some sort of connection with me in the past. They would come over to me, and I had no choice but to pause my meal to share a conversation with them.
Among these people was the rabbit baroness.
“It has been a while, Baron Yandel. No, I suppose I should call you Viscount Yandel?”
“My ceremony hasn’t commenced yet. Anyway, it’s good to see you, Baroness Lirivia.”

We began with an initial greeting befitting of nobles before getting into a bit of small talk. However, when I made it abundantly clear that I wanted to go back to eating, the rabbit baroness left me, looking completely deflated as she left behind some pitiful words.
“Um... Your Lordship? You haven’t attended the Melbeth gatherings recently...”
“I’ve been busy.”
“B-but I heard that you’ve been visiting Count Alminus quite frequently...”
“What are you trying to say?”
“Um, w-well... You can’t abandon Melbeth...” She froze when he saw the look on my face. “Th-then, enjoy your meal...!”
Seeing the rabbit baroness scurry off in a sorry state, I felt an odd emotion grip my heart.
Melbeth...

At first, it was just a place I had to go to to solidify my standing as a noble. I even figured I could use the situation at Melbeth to my advantage to gain the most support possible, and it worked out exactly as planned.
But now...
Now it just feels like an obligation...
I didn’t really want to put it this way, but it felt as though I had a responsibility as a nonhuman to help them out.
Granted, I did receive quite a bit of help from them up to this point.
I should attend the next meeting.
I scarfed down the rest of my food as the meal ended and the third period began, this time hosted by Count Alminus.
The third period was the inauguration of the prime minister, after all.

Since I was full, I yawned and dozed off, which ultimately resulted in me skipping the entire inauguration ceremony. The duke, now the prime minister, proceeded as the host for the rest of the ceremonies.
Finally, the fourth and final period arrived.
“Countless heroes were born in this war. However, even among those countless heroes, there is one hero who has shone brighter than them all in his deeds.”
Namely, the elimination of Corpse Collector, my victory against Demon Eye, and the execution of the traitor and ultimate evil, Marquess Tercerion.
Kealunus went on for a while to explain each of my accomplishments while I stood backstage until I was given my cue.

Although this wasn’t my first ennoblement ceremony, it definitely felt different—as in, much more concise—from the previous one. Back then, I was ranking up from a baronet to a baron to join the thousands of official noble houses. It was closer to a welcoming ceremony than a—
“What are you doing? Hold the chest.”
Oh, right.
I broke out of my daze and took the chest as practiced before going down on one knee and lifting the chest high.
The duke removed the indigo cloth covering the chest and then used a blue cloth to cover it instead. That was the end of the ceremony.
Then suddenly, it was my turn to give a speech.
I wasn’t informed of it beforehand, but it wasn’t too much trouble. For some reason, though, I felt the gaze of Duke Kealunus piercing into me, like he was expecting me to praise him.
What do you expect from a barbarian?
I just ignored him and just said what I wanted. As a barbarian warrior, there was only one thing I could say in front of all these people.
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
Unfortunately, the reaction to my shout was pretty tame. To be precise, it fell completely flat.
“As expected.”
“I honestly knew he would do that from the moment he was asked to give the speech.”
“It’s nothing new at this point.”
No one clicked their tongues in disgust nor berated me, saying I didn’t know how to present myself in a social setting.
Still, what was this sudden wave of disappointment I was feeling?
I didn’t know, but I didn’t need to know either.
“If you are done, please step down.”
“Sure.”
With that, I became Viscount Yandel.
[Your fame has increased by +10.]
[Your fame has increased by +10.]
[Your fame has increased by +10.]
[Your fame has increased...]

Although I was promoted from a baron to a viscount, my daily life remained the same. The only difference between the two ranks was the benefits their house could receive, such as the number of soldiers under their name, but the House of Viscount Yandel didn’t have soldiers like that to begin with.
In the end, I just obtained more honor.
Maybe it’ll change if I become a count or a marquess?

Hmm, probably. I did hear counts enjoyed all sorts of advantages. However, even if I became one, I doubted there would be any dramatic changes. Making a noble group on the level of Melbeth was probably all I could do.
Let’s just focus on what I need to do.
After the ceremony was over, I quickly returned to my usual routine.

I attended the meetings at Melbeth and even had lunch with Duke Kealunus to discuss a variety of things. Having become the prime minister, the duke was keenly interested in maintaining a good relationship with me, and I was in the same boat. Keeping on good terms with the prime minister of Rafdonia meant gaining access to premium information, after all.
Take, for example, the date of the labyrinth’s opening, something that had yet to be revealed to even the guild.

I got to hear about how many adventurers would be allowed in, which clans would be participating, whether the palace was also going into the labyrinth, and other things in that vein. Plus, when I asked, the prime minister gave all those precious pieces of information to me for free.
It was clear that his goal was to gain favorability with me.
“Most material damages in the holy land have been restored, and we are going to be deploying the warriors for the restoration of District 7 and District 8 starting next month.”
Same as before, most of the administrative work within the holy land was being taken care of by Shavin Emoor.
Strangely, though, I noticed she was working even harder than before for some reason.
“Shavin, have you been sleeping enough?”
“Don’t worry. I can at least get some sleep before dawn.”
I was getting pretty worried seeing her push herself so much, but I also didn’t think it’d be a good idea if I forced her to rest.
Time will solve this.
Still, thanks to Shavin dealing with all the business within the holy land, I didn’t really have anything I needed to worry about.

With that, the time I had left was spent on planning for the next expedition. I made detailed routes for the expedition to take, and I continued to gather the members together to bring up our camaraderie.
Time passed by quickly.
“Wow, how long has it been since I’ve been inside the labyrinth?”
Finally, the day had come.

chapters.title: Chapter 789: Red Ocean (1)
paragraphs: This time around, the palace had put in a lot of work for the reopening of the labyrinth. The city’s resources were beginning to bottom out.
Well, the nobles and the wealthy can sustain their lifestyles without a problem, but the rest are all going to starve to death.
Refugees who lost their homes, the surging prices of goods.

Things were so bad that beggars appeared on every street corner, something that would have been unimaginable a mere year or two prior. After all, Rafdonia was a city nation that executed those they deemed unworthy—people who didn’t pay their taxes.

Needless to say, this situation had arisen due to the temporary lift on taxes for all citizens, which also meant the palace needed to unseal the labyrinth so that they could begin collecting taxes again and return to some sense of stability.
“It’s Bjorn Yandel...”
“It makes sense that they would be here.”
“Still, it’s impressive. Their group doesn’t even have twelve people, but they were still summoned here. From what I know, the second smallest clan still had around sixty people.”
“What’s impressive about it? It’s obvious. He’s an adventurer who engraved his name on the Stone of Honor.”
“And I heard that he became a viscount after the last ceremony.”
As soon as we arrived at the gathering point, the hundreds of adventurers already present looked at us with assessing eyes.
“So they’re the new members.”
“The Hero of the Elves and the Golden Wizard...”
“The Golden Wizard used to work with Viscount Yandel, but I guess you need to be on her level at least to be able to join them.”
“Did they release any recruitment advertisements? Just joining the Anabada Clan would make you known throughout the entire city.”
“Still, the large clans are better. Think about it, they’re just a small elite unit, so if you look away from their individual fame and skills, they can’t do what a large clan can do.”
“By the way, who’s that over there with the helmet? I thought they only had eleven people.”
Some looked at us with jealousy and envy, while others looked on with pure curiosity. Rather than respond to that attention, I took a look around instead.
This top-secret meeting of the adventurers who would be entering the labyrinth was held in a place I knew very well.
“It seems the palace has a perverted taste, seeing how they made us gather in the marquess’s mansion.”
I smirked at Amelia’s muttered commentary. “I don’t know about perverted. I think it was for efficiency. It’s hard to find such a large and secure place in the imperial capital.”
“Well... That is true.”
It was too well-kept to be a ruin and too dreary to be a residence.
It was odd.
Looking around the place got me thinking all over again about the nature of power and authority, and yet, I felt inexplicably hollow.
“This way, Viscount Yandel.”

A little further in, a worker from the labyrinth guide network appeared and guided us to a military tent. He looked a little too old to be a regular worker, so I asked him what his rank was, and it was higher than I anticipated. In modern terms, he would be like a department head.
Maybe someone like him had to come to the meeting as well for security’s sake?
“Hah... That feels better.”
As soon as we entered our tent, the members behind me slouched into comfortable seating positions. They had been tensing their backs to keep straight under the attention of the crowd.
