The one who seemed to have had it the worst was Raven.
“Is there a reason you need to wear heels like that?” I asked, genuinely a little baffled. “We’re going to be entering the labyrinth anyway.”
“You only say that because you don’t know, Mr. Yandel. It all ends the moment you let your presentation slip.”
Hmm... I don’t know if heels actually help with appearances in any way...
Still, I didn’t say anything. Other people were entitled to their opinions.
“Then are we going to rest here for a bit before going straight into the labyrinth?”
“No, we’ll be here a while. We’ll move at midnight. There is a Dimension Square in the imperial capital too.”
“You mean the first Dimension Square, right?” Kaislan asked. “The one that hasn’t been used for a long time.”
Raven put a hand on her chin and mumbled, “So they’re still opening it at midnight. Maybe that can’t change even though they can control what day the labyrinth opens?”
“Well, I don’t know that. I’m not a wizard.”
“But this does create another question. If they can open it whenever they want in secret, why haven’t they done it until now?”
Oh, that?
I could answer that. I was curious too and had asked Astarota about it myself.
“I don’t know the details, but it sounds like they needed time to make it work. The palace started prepping for this the day Noark took over Bifron and were now only able to finish it.”

“Hmm...” Raven hummed. “Maybe Noark knew that as well, so they tried to charge in as far as they could. No matter how much of a secret it was, the prime minister would’ve known everything. The information must have reached the Noarkans.”
“Could be. Whatever it was, we’ll be waiting for a while, so get as much rest as you can. We won’t have time for that when we enter the labyrinth.”
“Oh, one more thing.”
I paused. “You have more?” Raven seemed to have a lot of questions today for some reason.
“I looked at the expedition schedule, but is there a reason we need to move this quickly? You’ve shortened the time we have to get to the fifth floor to an insane level.”
“It’s a bit of a march, but it can’t be helped. We’re entering a labyrinth that was closed for over a year at this point.”

All sorts of hidden secrets existed in the labyrinth, and most of them had a cooldown period before they could be revealed again. The first-floor rift was one such secret. While it was possible to open a rift on the first floor using a mana stone from a monster on the second floor, the rift could only be opened once every few months.
And not just that...

“When you look through history, this isn’t the first time the labyrinth was sealed. The major examples were during the Iron Wall Rebellion and when the thirteenth month was created after the King of the New World ascended the throne.”
“So?”
“So when I looked through the records from back then, I noticed something interesting.”
“What was it?”
“When the labyrinth was reopened, the frequency of rifts was unnaturally high.”
“The important thing about all this is that the other clans that were called here today probably know about this too.”

Being an intelligent woman, Raven immediately picked up on what I wanted to say. “I got it. The other clans will be fighting to get as much as they can. I mean, everyone’s already desperate to earn one more coin at this point.”
“Even if the number of adventurers entering the labyrinth is small, the competition will be fierce. People will try to use this opportunity to climb to the higher floors too.”
That finally seemed to resonate with her. “I should probably take a nap in that case. I don’t think I’ll even be able to sleep in the labyrinth.”
“Alright.”
With that, the ball of curiosity that was Raven walked away, but I still didn’t rest. The guild master had finally gotten me what I’d asked for.
“This is the list of names that you requested. The clans and other parties that will be entering the labyrinth are summarized here.”
“Thank you.”
It was a bonus I could never have imagined obtaining unless I had the guild master, the person who managed all the adventurers, within my group.
I made it a goal to read through the entire list today. These people were all competing against us, after all.
There aren’t any small teams that joined, just like the duke told me.

That didn’t mean small adventuring groups wouldn’t be present, of course. From what the guild master told me, the small elite teams had apparently used their connections to join the large clans so they could get into the labyrinth.
“Thirty-one clans for a total of 2,517 people.”
Anyway, after looking through the entire list, there were another 1,700 members of the expedition force personally drafted by the palace.
Around 4,300 people would be entering the labyrinth this time, and as expected, the units made up of the palace soldiers were overwhelmingly larger than any of the other clans.
However, I didn’t need to worry about them. Their goals were too different from ours to be called competition.
Mana stones.

The top priority of the palace’s expedition force was to gather mana stones, and from the information I received from the duke, they were aiming for the sixth floor to mine them. The catch was, they planned to take over the three farming islands that were packed with the large clans and just farm the stones until the labyrinth closed.

While it would be detrimental for the large clans who were also aiming for those islands, it wasn’t a problem I needed to concern myself with. The important thing was that our goals were different, meaning we didn’t need to compete against the expedition force.
Our goal is the rift on the eighth floor.
How many would we have to compete for that? That was an answer I’d need to find out when I got there.
“Alright, we’ll now begin moving to the Dimension Square! Please take your carriages in order!”
As we closed in on midnight, the carriages that had been on standby in the marquess’s grand garden all began to move toward the Dimension Square.
And then...
Shine!
The portal finally began to open at the heart of the square.
My heart raced as I watched the scene play out for the first time in a very long time.
[You have entered the first-floor Crystal Cave.]
Just like how caterpillars needed leaves to eat, adventurers needed adventure to thrive.
Brilliant sparkles of light shone in the Crystal Cave.
I breathed in the cool, muddy air, finally feeling like I was inside the labyrinth.
It feels a little...off.
It was an odd sensation, one I didn’t remember having back when I had monthly trips into the labyrinth. Somehow, it felt like the place itself had changed ever so slightly.
Still, there was work to be done.

I touched the walls embedded with crystals and tried to discern the subtle feelings held within that sensation. It was a method I’d learned from Rotmiller, who had started his scouting life from the lowest point.
It took me a moment to puzzle through the sensation. It had been a while since I practiced.
Yeah, this feeling means...
“Judging by the distance between the portals, it seems we drifted a bit more north than the origin point. We will make the best time heading to the Goblin Forest.”
Oh, right. He was the scout.
Just talented people all around me.
I felt momentarily defeated but let the feeling drift away when I saw Beleg just open his compass for a split second and confirm the direction without having to touch the wall or taste the air.
“I will stand at the front.”
I quickly followed after him as he barreled forward. It wasn’t proper for the ranged damage dealer to be at the forefront of the group.
Honestly, though, it’s hard to get hurt by goblins at this point even if you tried.

While I didn’t know his full capabilities, I had a feeling Beleg could stand at the front even up to the fifth floor without any problems. Any further would probably depend on the island on the sixth floor.
It’ll get more difficult for him on the seventh floor.
Since I didn’t need to focus on finding the path, I was able to instead look over the members of Team 1 who were following behind Beleg. More specifically, I checked on Raven and the guild master.
The guild master was just running normally, and Raven was riding a device with a single wheel.
“Uh... Aruru? Is this the vehicle that you mentioned?”

“Yes. It’s a magic tool created by the military. You can fuel it with mana stones, but it can fuel itself using the mana in the air as well. Of course, mana stones are required if you want it to go faster.”
“Aha? O-oh! I see?”
“It’ll probably be as fast as you on flat ground, Ms. Karlstein.”
“R-really? Th-that’s impressive...” Missha stuttered, seeming embarrassed to have asked something unnecessary. The guild master picked up where she left off.
“Can you use it on ground that isn’t flat?”
“It’s possible if it’s not too bumpy, and if not, I’ll need to use something else.”
“Something else?”
“I’ll show it to you if that time comes,” Raven said curtly. Unlike when she told Missha everything about the device, she was deliberately cutting her conversation with the guild master short.
“Haha, I see... understood.”
Was there something going on between them?
Raven had always been a little on the defensive side, but she never let an opportunity to boast about her gear pass her by.
I’ll just keep an eye on them.
After that, we continued to run through the cave like we were speedrunning it.
“Unfortunately, we were one step too late.”
However, by the time we arrived at the dimensional headstone that connected to the Goblin Forest, we discovered that someone else had already opened the portal.
Hah, these adventurers really are fast. I thought we were making good time at this pace.
[You have entered the second-floor Goblin Forest.]
Either way, while we didn’t know who they were, the fact that someone was ahead of us boosted our motivation and helped us move even faster.
In the end, though, we never ended up catching up to that group.
[You have entered the third-floor Pilgrim’s Path.]

We once again used an already-opened portal to arrive at the third floor. Since the setting was a green swamp, we were able to quickly see the traces left behind by the people who arrived here before us.
“Looks like these are the ones in front of us.”
“Thankfully, they seemed to be just one team.”
“Yes. With how fast we were moving, if there were multiple groups faster than us... I would’ve been pissed.”
“Then, let’s continue moving—”
I stopped Beleg there. “Wait.”
“What is it?”
“The way these footsteps are headed. It’s not the fourth floor, is it?”
Beleg seemed to sense something was off then too, as he furrowed his brow.
“That...is odd. Only the Sculpture Temple is in that direction...”
However, because he didn’t know why they were going in that direction, he didn’t understand the full scope of the problem.
“Going to the Sculpture Temple after climbing to the third floor this quickly...”
It could only point to one thing.
I didn’t know who was reckless enough to try it, but someone was trying to get to that floor.
The first basement floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 790: Red Ocean (2)
paragraphs: The first basement floor was a sort of hidden field you could enter if you obtained three Unnamed Fragments from the Sculpture Temple, one of the fields on the third floor, and brought them to the dimensional headstone on the first floor. Very few people had actually explored the place, and it was the scarcity of primary sources that led to the spread of wild rumors.
Single-digit numbered items, never-before-seen essences, new monsters.
The stories going around made it seem as if the first basement floor was just bursting with jackpots waiting to be discovered.
Well, I can’t really argue with that considering the rewards you can get...
Still, from my perspective, it was all high risk, high return.
Despite our experience, even we had wondered if we’d ever be able to escape—and that was before we took into account all of the people who died along the way.
“What a bunch of fools...” Raven dismissed with a click of her tongue. “They’re willingly crawling back in. The palace even publicly declared it a no-go zone.”
While Raven wrote their efforts off, I could see what led them to venture down there.
The ambition of adventurers was a deep abyss. No matter how one tried to find the bottom, the chasm never ended.
It was like this when we first went down to the first basement floor as well...

It had been the same when we first discovered the floor too. Countless adventurers standing in front of the dimensional headstone, all of them just smiling and laughing. Even when the Lord of the Abyss, Berzak, had begun to roam the floor, they yammered away, confident that the Lord of the Floor’s presence meant the condition to open the portal had been fulfilled.
“You should know it as well, Baron Yandel... Isn’t this what being an adventurer is?!”
That was when I realized how truly reckless some people could be in the name of adventure. It was as if they had abandoned their very selves to their greed.

“In any case,” Raven continued, having mumbled her way through my thoughts, “it makes sense if their goal is the first basement floor. I was wondering who could possibly be pushing themselves to zoom through the floors, but they must’ve just been desperate.”
I nodded, agreeing with her assessment.

The biggest enemy in getting to the first basement floor was time. It was only accessible while the first floor was open, meaning anyone interested in exploring its depths needed to go up to the third floor, obtain three Unnamed Fragments, and then come back down to the first floor. Only after doing all that within seven days would the floor open to any willing would-be entrants.
“So, what are you thinking?” Kaislan asked, making me pause.
Admittedly, I was mildly curious about who would be rash enough to concoct such a reckless plan.
However, in the end, them going down to the basement floors wouldn’t change our plans. Plus, there was a decent chance they wouldn’t be able to return anyway.
“We’ll continue with our plan.”

Concluding that we didn’t need to waste our precious time to satisfy such a small curiosity, I put the thought of them aside and we pushed forward, focusing our full attention on quickly moving up the floors. On the morning of the sixth day, we were able to pass through the Witch’s Forest and arrive at the entrance to the fourth floor, the Tower in the Sky.
However, the problem was...
“There’s a lot of them.”
Problem was, dozens of adventuring teams were waiting at the center of the Witch’s Forest to enter the fourth floor.

That in itself wasn’t anything odd, of course. The times between the fastest speedruns weren’t that different, so it was only natural that the times participating adventurers arrived on the fourth floor would be similar too.
But the fact that we’re stuck waiting in line even though we’ve come up this quickly means that everyone’s just as serious about this.
I looked around for Team 2 but didn’t see them. They had either already gone up or hadn’t arrived yet.
As I led my team to stand in line, I could feel the gazes of the others looking over at me.
“It’s Viscount Yandel...”
“He’s only now here? Not as impressive as he seems.”
“I’ve told you before—without his fame and reputation, he’s just another ordinary adventurer.”

Surprisingly, I sensed hostility more than anything from them. Was it because only high-ranking adventures were here? Rather than looking up to me as a target of envy, they only saw me as competition.
I looked over each of the groups, ignoring their jabs to look for something else. “I don’t see many groups wearing the palace’s insignia,” I noted.
Like before, Raven was the one to respond. “It’s because the army specialized themselves for combat rather than travel.”
“Oh, true...”

The line continued to move quickly, getting noticeably short even during our brief chat. Given the nature of the situation we were in, we didn’t even need to wait five minutes for the color of the portal to change. Six people stepped forward together to fill out the slots, the portal would quickly change color, and then the next team would go in, making each iteration last about one minute per team.
Just then, the ground rumbled as though shaken by a passing earthquake.
True to the nature of high-ranking adventurers, though, no one around us was surprised by the phenomenon.
“A rift opened...” someone mused, immediately recognizing what had happened.
A rift had opened on the third floor. There were three reactions to this revelation.
“So, the stories were true. Since the labyrinth hadn’t been opened for a while—”
“Shush. Be quiet.”
“Anyway, looks like we can look forward to the fourth and fifth floors too.”
Some ignored the third-floor rift and looked onward with anticipation in their eyes.
“Brium! Where’s the rift located?”
“It’s not too far from here. If we move as fast as we can, we’ll get there in about an hour.”
“An hour... It’s risky. We won’t lose out on anything if we just can get into the rift...”
Some weighed their options after confirming the rift’s location.
“This way!”
“Run!”
“Captain, what should we do? They’re already running!”
“Damn it! We’re moving as well!”
Lastly, some immediately made their decision and began running.
Our reaction was the first one. There wasn’t anything in the White Temple that we needed, and since the guild master’s goal was an “achievement”, he didn’t say anything either.
Because really, how much of an achievement could clearing a third-floor rift be?
Nevertheless, the opening of the rift was a boon for us.
“Oh, it’s now our turn.”
Thanks to so many adventurers running off, we jumped far ahead in the line.
[You have entered the fourth-floor Tower in the Sky.]

Naturally, we didn’t encounter anything notable in the Tower in the Sky, with one possible exception being the rift that opened around the ten-day mark. We tried our best to look for the rift as soon as it opened, but we were unfortunately not able to enter it.
“That’s a shame...” Raven said, disappointed. “It wasn’t the Golden Ruins, right? That place is just raining money.”
“It was definitely the Doppelganger Forest...” I reassured her.
Although it was disappointing to miss out on the rift, as adventurers with healthy mindsets, we let go of those negative thoughts and continued to climb the tower.

Unlike the previous floors, where we were able to skip all combat, we were dragged into a few fights on the fourth, and I used those opportunities to closely observe the combat capabilities of our new members.
They’re pretty good.
Beleg Shucia di Tersia. The Hero of the Elves or, as he was known back in his adventuring days, the Pursuer.
I did hear he used to be called something else, but his alias changed when he doggedly pursued the Dragon Slayer following the destruction of the village of the elves a few decades ago.
Regardless, befitting his nickname, his main skills were tracking and detection.
He seems to be between a rank two and a rank three combat-wise...
Notably, despite taking up the role of archer, he didn’t use a bow. Instead, his combat style went something like this.
Whoosh!
He would call upon an army of spirits called “Summons.”
[Beleg Shucia di Tersia has cast Skill Transfer.]
Then using Skill Transfer, he would share his bow-type skills with his summons.
[Beleg Shucia di Tersia is not wielding a weapon.]
Then, using the effect of Sage King, the attack power of his summons would be exponentially amplified.
[Beleg Shucia di Tersia has cast Trumpet of the Soul. When Summons attack the same target, additional damage will be dealt.]
Support skills would then concentrate that firepower even more.
All in all, though, this technically made him more of a summoner or a special ability user than an archer.
If he fights well, what do I care?
Beleg’s character build was more complete than I anticipated. Maybe I should have expected as much from a player.
Yeah, he’s much better than the guild master.

The guild master, on the other hand, was at a much lower skill level than I expected. He had a few valuable essences and his combat power was objectively on the higher side, but that was it. I got the impression that he had just barely managed to claw his way up to his current level of skill. Even if it weren’t too late to completely change over his essence combinations, and it definitely was, he had nowhere near enough potential to cover for his shortcomings.
[You have entered the fifth-floor Great Demon Realm.]
As I carried on with my little “tests,” we eventually arrived at the fifth floor, only to find that it looked different the moment we entered it.
“No one is here?”
Since the fifth floor was a safe zone, there should have been a camp at the entrance where adventurers would gather and camp together...
Staying any longer wouldn’t change anything either. If an adventurer was weak enough to need a camp in the safe zone, they wouldn’t have even been invited to enter the labyrinth this month.
“There’s no mark. Looks like we’re here earlier than Team 2.”
“Unless someone already cleared it.”
We made a simple mark at the entrance for Team 2 to encounter before continuing our expedition, deciding to head for the tricky but shortest route through the Ghostly Canyon of Ghosts.
[You have entered a special area.]
[Field Effect—Ghostly Canyon of Ghosts is applied.]
[Status Effect—Restligeist is granted.]
[Dark Resistance and Physical Resistance are decreased by 100.]
The ground shook in periodic quakes as all around us echoed the spooky cries of ghosts. A disgusting feeling tainted the air, making my skin feel raw and sensitive.
Although it was creepier and nastier than going through the Frosty Canyon or the Hellfire Canyon, as adventurers who valued efficiency, this was the best choice.
“Why did this one have to be the quickest route...?”

In the labyrinth, time was money, a sentiment which was quickly affirmed when we began to see other adventurers here and there in the canyon with us. They were all trying to climb out of this floor as fast as possible.
Hmm, I wondered, suddenly curious. Since this isn’t a good hunting field, would we have seen adventurers who were here to hunt if we’d taken a different route instead?
The possibility was definitely there. The fifth floor could be decent for hunting if a team was capable of monopolizing it.
“We’ll reach the sixth floor tomorrow.”
Time quickly passed, and sixteen days after we entered the labyrinth, we were just around a day’s travel away from the sixth floor.
“Getting there in seventeen days is pretty quick, right?”
“Unbelievably quick. During the war, I think the average travel time was around twenty-five days?”
If we did end up getting there on the morning of the seventeenth day, it would be our best time yet.
It meant that we could have arrived on the sixteenth day if we’d just pushed ourselves as hard as we could.
Maybe it’s because the overall level of the team has significantly increased.
Either way, nothing much happened after we entered the fifth floor. The one thing was another rift opening.
“Looks like one is opening on every floor.”
“We can’t make it inside even though we have a scout... I guess everyone is just that on point.”
Even though the rift portal appeared close to our location, we weren’t able to enter the one on this floor either.
Maybe we won’t get a rift this time, I thought to myself as we made camp.
Then suddenly, the scout of our team, Beleg, lowered his voice and called for me.
“Yandel.”
It didn’t take long for me to realize why he suddenly went serious instead of going to sleep.
“Adventurers...” I muttered.
“There are quite a few of them. Easily more than forty.”
“Let’s wait for now. When they notice our presence, they’ll walk away as well.”
Though it should have been obvious by now, monsters weren’t the only things one needed to be aware of in the labyrinth. People were actually the far more dangerous threat.
Grimly, I realized, “They aren’t walking away.”
It was an unwritten rule of the labyrinth that you walked away instead of clashing with someone who made it someplace before you did, and yet the mysterious group was heading straight for us.
Everyone stood guard, wide awake, as the group of adventurers appeared from beyond the darkness of the labyrinth. When they saw us in the middle of setting up camp, they looked a little surprised.
“The Anabada Clan?”
I recognized the clan by their insignia, just as they were able to do the same for us—though we had a few notable characteristics that made us stand out beyond that.
“What are you looking at?” I grunted. “Move away.”
“Ah, my apologies. I know that there is an unwritten rule about this, but the captain wishes for us to move in a straight line.”
“I got it, so keep moving,” I repeated. However, he didn’t move away and chose to scan us over instead.
Things to lose and things to gain.
His eyes tacked onto each one of us, weighing the two things against each other.
It only made it feel all the more real.
“It seems you haven’t joined up with your Team 2 yet, then?”
Yeah, the labyrinth’s always been this way.

chapters.title: Chapter 791: Red Ocean (3)
paragraphs: Treasures begot conflict.
It was a saying true to daily life yet even more true when in the labyrinth.

Back in the days when I was a low-level adventurer, many people had turned against me for my sub-space bag. When the incidents became too frequent, I even considered taking off the seal of the sub-space and painting over my lithinum breastplate to dull its shine.
I thought those days were over.

As I gained more things, however—becoming famous, forming a team, promoting that team into a clan, becoming a noble, becoming the chieftain, and more—I no longer felt the need to hide what I had. Or rather, I revealed everything I had all the time. I thought it was the right move for where I was in my life.
So then, what was this?
The air grew heavy with tension as the head of the clean threw out that prodding question.
Neither he nor I spoke a word, but my allies one by one began to take out their weapons, readying for battle just as his allies were. We glared at each other through the piercing silence.

I could see the thought written across his face. Just imagine, all the things he could gain if only he could just kill me. It was common knowledge that I possessed a few numbered items, including even single-digit numbered items, and he would have sounded out that I had a few that I was probably keeping private.
People were creatures of imagination—imagination that usually benefited them.
Finally, he cut through the silence to ask, “Have those new members been working out for you?”

Our team composition probably played a hand in his growing greed as well. Erwen and Ainar, members of the Seven Powerful, weren’t here. Not to mention, Beleg had been retired for a while, and Missha wasn’t known for her combat prowess either.
Raven and Kaislan are pretty famous in their own right, but these guys probably think they can take us on with a decent chance of making it out the victors.
There were over forty of them and only six of us, after all.
“I have no reason to report the happenings of my clan to you. So what are you trying to say?”

“Haha, why are you being so aggressive? I just wanted to tell you to be careful.” When I shot him a dubious look, he explained, “Well, the stories about you fighting twenty members of Orcules by yourself, defeating the Demon Eye in just one strike... Maybe it’s different for those ignorant morons, but no one who would believe in empty nonsense like that is in the labyrinth right now.”
So that was why. I was wondering why he got so greedy when looking at me.
Finally, I understood. He just believed that my accomplishments were just inflated by rumors.
“Of course, we are upstanding gentlemen, so we will just pass by—”
Huh? He was a coward who backed out without trying because the risk was too great.

“Meiruta Clan,” I cut him off and quickly continued, “has a total of one hundred twenty-one members but entered this expedition with only forty-eight. It seems you’re in an alliance with the Dubord Clan who is of similar size to you, but seeing how you’re not with them, it seems you planned on joining them on the sixth floor.”
“How did you...?”

“You learn to pick up on certain things when you reach a position like mine. For example, your clan was freed without charges after being judged, but rumor has it that you’re suspected of plundering others... Are you after what I have?”
He didn’t answer my question.
It was honestly pretty funny. He underestimated me when I was standing idly by, but he didn’t know what to do when I attacked him right back.
“Haha... What do you mean? I only tried to advise that you be careful—”

“Ready for combat,” I interrupted, ordering my team members. “The captain of the Meiruta Clan will be judged here and now for plundering and attempting to murder a noble, and then he will be executed.”
“Wh-what are you saying?!”
“If anyone tries to help the captain, then you will be considered an accomplice and executed with him.”
“W-wait!” I ignored him, taking a step forward, and he took an equal step back. “A-are you saying you’re going to attack me?”
“I’m only dealing with a criminal.”
“Wh-what did I do? Rethink this! Even you won’t be able to—”
“To do what? You think I can’t handle the aftermath?”

He went silent, mouth bobbing open and closed as he searched for an answer. He knew as well as I did that even if I killed them all and even if they were all innocent, I had a very good chance of making it out fine.
To hammer the point home, I called out a name.
“Illya Adnus.”
The man in question took a deep breath. “So, it’s come to this in the end.” Though I’d only said two words, he understood what I was asking and took off his helmet.
“The g-guild master?” someone said with a gasp.
“Why is the guild master with the Anabada Clan?” demanded another.
No one could hide their shock. However, the real question they should have been asking wasn’t why the guild master was here.
With a practiced authority, he declared, “You are currently engaging in the act of plundering.”
“W-we’ve never done—”
“It was quite clear to me that you were trying to plunder, yet you say you weren’t. Then will you accompany your captain in this crime?”
The members of Meiruta Clan answered with their actions over words. They all took a step back, some without even realizing it.
That was it, then.
Never give the opponent any time to think.
As soon as the other side stepped back, I took a step forward. The leader of the Meiruta Clan yelped as I grabbed his head, then slammed it unceremoniously into the ground.

Naturally, none of the clan members lifted a finger to protest. More accurately, they couldn’t. Perhaps it would be a different story if the captain had been particularly charismatic and ordered them to act, but there wasn’t anyone left among them who could make such an important decision.

With that, another moment of silence settled over the labyrinth. However, like the last one, this silence felt less like a tense standoff where a battle could explode at any moment and more like the true winners and losers had been decided. The losers had no options left, and could only wait for the mercy of the winner.
“What’s your view on this?” I asked the guild master, who clicked his tongue as he walked over.

“You may execute him here without issue,” he confirmed. “He doesn’t have a good reputation, and if we dig deep enough when we go back to the city, something should come up. That, and he is also the one who broke the unwritten rule and approached you first.”
“P-please spare me...” the head of the clan muttered pitifully. “P-please... I was wrong.”
As if he didn’t hear the begging, the guild master turned to me and asked, “Now, what will you do?”
I ignored the pleas as well. “I will execute him.”
“What? No, how could you?!” the head of the clan cried. “I r-really haven’t done anything wrong!”
That was true enough. He hadn’t acted on anything quite yet. The problem was that he certainly intended to do so.
What if Team Two met people like these guys? What if they got ambushed on the way up the floors and someone died?
I had no intention of letting people like him run around, crying that their hands were tied whenever an incident did strike.
I needed to let everyone know. They must know what kind of person Bjorn Yandel was and what their end would be if they messed with us.
Crunch!
My hammer spoke for me, crunching down with a finality that summarily brought the situation to a close.
When I delivered my conclusion, the guild master approached me.
“Good work. These people are like cockroaches. If you leave them be, they’ll continue to spread without end.”
I didn’t care how the guild master tried to justify my actions. Instead, I chose to look at the expression of my allies.

Having spent quite some time in the military, Raven didn’t let her expression show her emotions, and neither did Beleg. Kaislan actually looked satisfied with my actions. However, the person who had been with me the longest time, Missha, was looking at me with a hint of worry, but she didn’t say anything.
Another nervous voice spoke up then.
“So... Um... What happens to us?”
“Are you the vice-captain?” I asked, curious.
“Th-that’s right, Lord Baron... No, Lord Viscount...”
The vice-captain shook, unable to even look me in the eyes.

Who could blame him, really? He had just lost his captain, and at such an unexpected time and place. He must have thought I was a demon or something. In truth, their group probably assumed that I’d gotten pissed off and killed him on a whim.
“I have a few things I want to ask you,” I began.
“W-we really didn’t intend anything! When we sensed you, I even told him to turn around, but the captain just—”
“I’m not asking about that.”
“Pardon? Then...”
“I get that you decided to regroup on the fifth floor, but how did you all get here so quickly?”
It was honestly one of the first questions I had when I saw them. We were moving pretty quickly ourselves, and yet they were able to arrive here before us—forty-eight of them, at that.
“Th-that’s thanks to the captain putting six people in the party who could use Flag of Haste! Oh, Flag of Haste is—”
“I don’t need the explanation.”

Flag of Haste was an aura-type skill that greatly increased the movement speed of all who were affected by it. The skill used quite a bit of MP, mostly because its effect was proportional to the number of people it affected, but that could be remedied by having multiple people use them in turns.
But is this strategy even worth it?
While I was lost in thought, the guild master interjected and put my doubts into words.
“You’ve used an outdated strategy.”
“What...?”

“In truth, it is one that only works once you can gather all your members on the fifth floor. It does mean that you can breeze quickly through the fifth floor, but that boost is nullified by the sixth floor since you’ll be on a boat, and safety is prioritized more than speed on the seventh floor. Needless to say, it was used some time ago for a short period before being scrapped.”
“Ah, i-is that so...? I didn’t know about that. The captain also bought the tools necessary for this at a hefty price...”
“Then he’s wasted that money.”
Either way, my question was answered. Honestly, I was a bit surprised to see such a large group on the fifth floor.
“Then we’ll...”
“Move together,” I finished for the vice-captain. “You’re heading for the sixth floor too, aren’t you?”
“Pardon...?”
“Is there a problem?”
Since it’d come to this, I just decided to get to the sixth floor and rest properly there.
[There are 53 characters in range. The effect of Flag of Haste increases to 315%. All stats related to movement are greatly increased, and stamina used when moving is greatly decreased.]
[You have entered the sixth-floor Great Sea.]
Once we switched over to moving alongside the Meiruta Clan using the buff, we were able to arrive on the sixth floor before the sixteenth day came to an end despite our detours along the way.
The starting island, Laemia. I spotted many clans along the coast who were getting ready to set off or who were waiting for their allies who hadn’t arrived yet.
“Looks like there aren’t that many ships who’ve finished setting off yet,” the vice-captain noted.
“Luck is on our side. Since it doesn’t look like Team Two is here yet, let’s go to the mountain first.”
“You guys will be coming with us.”
After arriving on the sixth floor, we used the Meiruta Clan to climb the mountain in the center of the island.
“I did notice it at the base...but I think this is the first time I’ve seen so many trees here.”
“Grab your axes.”
We immediately began cutting down the trees.

The trees that grew here were pretty valuable. Although there were usually only stumps here since everyone would have cut them down before us, it was pretty packed with actual trees this time around due to the circumstances.
But looks like everyone had the same idea.
Quite a few adventurers were cutting down the trees. I wondered why I only saw adventurers working on the boats or guarding their tents at the coast.
We still have the most people, though.

These trees were the reason we split into two teams to climb. The team that reached the floor first would start chopping the trees down. The people around here were probably farming the trees as well until all their members showed up.
Thunk! Thunk! Crash!

And so, we began to chop down the trees as if in a competition with the other adventurers. It was hard to discern whether we were in the labyrinth to explore it or if we were here for manual labor at this point.
The prices of these trees will skyrocket after the labyrinth officially opens.
Since the prize was definitely more money rather than a good hunt, my team, the forty-seven volunteers we got from the fifth floor, and I continued cutting down the trees.
One day, two days, three days, four days...

The problem was that more adventurers came up to cut down the trees, which led to the mountain getting balder much quicker, and when all the trees were cut down, the adventurers all left the mountain. But even after all that was said and done...
“Damn it.”
Team Two was still nowhere to be seen.

chapters.title: Chapter 792: Red Ocean (4)
paragraphs: Whenever a person was given something to consider, the first thing they did was imagine scenarios. The level of immersion could differ between people, but it was a universal truth that everyone imagined these scenarios at some point.
My imagination, for example, was going wild.
They’re five days over the estimated arrival date...

Neither team was faster than the other, and definitely not fast enough to result in such a time difference. Something had to have happened to Team Two. I just didn’t have any idea what that something could be.
Wait...
As someone who lived with a chronic case of pessimism, my imagination naturally led me to the worst-case scenario first.
Maybe they had encountered plunderers, just like the Meiruta Clan we met on the fifth floor. Some adventurers could have attacked Team Two when they were by themselves.
The part that pained me even more was the fact that these imaginary scenarios weren’t completely nonsensical. In reality, they were actually quite probable.

The Meiruta Clan had tried to walk away because they didn’t have the guts to go through with it, but not everyone was like them. What if Team Two got unlucky and met a group that was much more decisive? What if said group wasn’t intimidated by my reputation?
I grit my teeth at the thought of it.

It was the very reason I went a little harder on the captain of the Meiruta Clan. No matter the situation, I wanted to eliminate all variables that could threaten us. That was why I executed him, to make an example out of him. It was also why I told the vice-captain of the clan to spread word of the incident far and wide as soon as they left the labyrinth.
“B-Bjorn...?”
No, maybe I was thinking too narrowly.

Maybe they didn’t simply have a run-in with some random plunderers. I had enemies—Baekho Lee, Auril Gavis. If not them, maybe the Noarkans noticed the labyrinth had opened and sent in a team of their own—
“Bjorn!”
I came to my senses when I felt someone slap me on the back. “Missha?”
“Now you listen to me!” she complained.
Oh, she was talking to me.
“What is it?” I asked, eager to know what she wanted so I could go back to thinking. However, Missha wasn’t going to let that slide.
“Please! Please stop imagining the worst! They’ll be fine!”
Cautiously, I asked, “How could you be so sure?”
“Because I trust in them. Emily, Erwen, Ainar, and the rest... I’m a little worried about Mr. Rockrobe, but still! Everyone can take care of themselves!”
“No, well... It’s not that I don’t trust them—”
“Bjorn, I think you’re misunderstanding something. We’re your allies, not your children.”
That made me hesitant. “I’ll just... go and cool my head for a bit.”
“Yep, yep. Go for it.”
At Missha’s worried advice, I stepped away from the portal and went to cool off. However, that didn’t mean my anxiety went anywhere.
It was only natural. I took Missha’s advice because I needed a quiet place to myself. It wouldn’t be right for the captain to look so distressed in front of his team members.
“Bjorn!” Missha called for me from a distance.
How long had I been away?
“Just where did you go? I’ve been looking all over for you—”
“Go back and tell the team we’ll be leaving soon.”
“Huh? We’re leaving?”
She tilted her head in confusion, and I used the moment to inform her of the plan I had come up with after a quick but intense reflection.
“As soon as we’re prepared, we’ll leave for the fifth floor. Rather than waiting for them like this, we should go and—”
“What are you talking about? We don’t need to do that!”

“I’ll decide what we need or not,” I admonished. “We don’t know exactly what the situation with Team Two is, but if someone is chasing after them, or if they’re in hiding somewhere, we need to go and help—”
“No, you knucklehead! Team Two came up just now!”
“What?” I asked, momentarily dazed.
Seeing my reaction, Missha answered the questions I was most worried about.
“They’re all fine! They’re late because they had to go into a rift on the fourth floor! Argh, really. What did I tell you? Nothing happened!”
For a moment, I was overcome with relief. Then, another emotion I couldn’t quite name swept in as I headed to the portal—to the place Team Two was.
“Huh? Hey, I’m still talking to you!” Missha called after me. “Where are you going?!”

I approached the portal with quick strides to see the members of Team Two standing in front of it. Amelia seemed to be calmly explaining something to the other members, and Ainar was loudly boasting about something she gained.
Only then did I realize what this emotion I was feeling was: a hint of annoyance. What I didn’t understand, however, was why I was feeling it in the first place.
“Oh, Yandel? You’re here,” Amelia greeted, a trace of surprise leaking into her voice as she watched me rush over. “I heard that you were worried because we weren’t here on time.”
Erwen giggled. “Mister! Were you worried for us?”
Despite the hellos, I didn’t say anything back. I was afraid that if I said something, these emotions I was feeling would leak out.
Maybe they already had.
“Emily...” I began slowly. “Why are you so late?”

“Ah... Did Karlstein not tell you? A rift opened up right in front of us on the fourth floor. We discussed it amongst ourselves and decided to enter it.” Noticing I remained quiet, Amelia explained, “But wasn’t this discussed beforehand? We agreed to enter any rift from the fourth floor onward if we could.”

She was right. We did agree on that. That was why even though Team Two was late, my other team members tried to console me by proposing they went into a rift. They had done what I, as their captain, should have done for them.
“Still... Aren’t you a little too late?”
That meant the problem was probably me.
“What?” Amelia questioned, surprised again.
“At your level, it shouldn’t have taken over five days to clear a rift on the fourth floor, though.”
“We took a bit of time because we proceeded as safely as we could. Are you seriously blaming us for that right now?”
A slight frown creased Amelia’s brow as she sensed the underlying emotions that prompted me to question them, and only then did I feel my mind clear.
There was definitely something wrong with me.
No, to be precise...
“Yandel... What’s making you so impatient?”
There was something wrong with my head.

Twenty-one days after entering the labyrinth, we had an incident after arriving on the sixth floor, but it was resolved without a problem and we were finally able to get on a boat out into the open ocean. We also separated from the Meiruta Clan here.
“We’re finally sailing...”
“It looks like the teams from the palace are also starting to head off.”
As we looked back at the coast, we could see the expedition force from the palace slowly setting up a few military vessels. The sight honestly frustrated me a little.
Looks like those guys will be able to set off some time tomorrow.

I had to admit, I was a bit disappointed by the timing of it all. We had moved so quickly, and yet we were only setting sail a day earlier than the slow expedition force. To add insult to injury, all of the boats still on the island belonged to the palatial forces, excluding a handful from a select few clans who remained behind.
“We’re slower than planned, but don’t worry too much. We’ve gained a lot, and even cleared out a rift already,” Amelia said by way of consolation. Apparently, I had let my thoughts show on my face.
Still, there was an awkward air between us, probably because of the earlier incident. Neither Amelia nor I had brought up what happened back there.
“Yes, that’s right! In a way, we’ve gained more than if we hunted for those five days, right? Don’t worry too much about it, Mister!”
I sighed.
Erwen’s worried about me. What am I doing?
While I felt disappointed in myself, that feeling drove me to think more clearly, and if I wanted to do that, I needed to deal with the problem with my mind.
I took in the ocean breeze from where I stood on the deck and looked over the water splashing against the hull, taking a moment to reflect on myself.

I hadn’t been myself in that moment. No, in hindsight, something had been wrong all the way back when I was dealing with the Meiruta Clan. It was as if one of the gears that kept my mind turning had been damaged. My emotions took precedence over my logical mind, and I became much more sensitive and aggressive than I needed to be.
It was the sort of thing that happened to everyone, even ordinary people who seemed fine until a certain button was pressed.
Maybe I’m too stressed...
That could be the simple answer, but I could just write it off like that.
If the captain lost his rationality and acted on emotion, his entire group would be put in danger. It could lead to someone getting hurt.
So how could I go about fixing it? It wasn’t as if we had a psychologist here. Did I need to administer my physical cure to myself?
“Yandel,” Amelia called, interrupting my thoughts.
“Oh, Emily...”
“It’s fine. It’s natural.”
She seemed to have identified the root of my problem. She was a pretty observant woman for sure.
Silence fell over us, but the awkwardness from before was gone.
Ah, I realized a few minutes later. I never asked her about it. Bringing it up after that whole thing would’ve been too awkward.
Having suddenly remembered what I wanted to ask her, I wondered aloud, “So which rift did you go into on the fourth floor?”
“The Doppelganger Forest.”
“Really? It’s a shame it wasn’t the Golden Ruins.”
“From what I heard, didn’t you tell Raven that you were sure it was the Doppelganger Forest?”
That’s because I didn’t know it was our team who went in there.
Hah, maybe this was why people needed to have kind thoughts about others.

Twenty-nine days after entering the labyrinth and nine days after setting sail off the coast of Laemia, we finally made land on another island, our first after crossing the ocean. It was our first destination in our expedition route.
Of course, our schedule was delayed by five days, so I did think about just skipping it.
It’s too much of a waste to skip and it’s on the way anyway. We just needed to clear it quickly and be on our way.
“Ugh... I did hear about it before, but it’s much more spooky than I thought. The entire island is made of bones...”
“Oooooh! The skull island! Skull Island!”
“Its official designation is Catacoma, Ms. Fenelin.”
Skull Island, Catacoma.

While this was our first time visiting as a team, I had an odd relationship with the island. When I first visited Ghost Busters, one of the pieces of intel I sold for GP was about Skull Island, and I even shared information about it at the Round Table.
“Um... Captain?”
As soon as we got off the boat, Sven Parav approached me.
“Did you know? I heard that if you defeat the head monster of Skull Island and reach the tenth floor, you can experience something special...”
Wow, look at this obvious member of the Round Table. That was the information I shared.
I acted like I didn’t know as I responded, “A special experience?”
“Yes. I don’t know much about it either... but I heard it from a reliable source. I mean, I know we won’t be going to the tenth floor this time, but I thought it’d be nice if you knew...”
“Really? I’ll remember it. But as you said, we won’t be going to the tenth floor.”
We finished our conversation there and disembarked on the island. As we did, Beleg, who had gotten off the boat before us, came to me with some information.
“Someone got here before us.”
“Someone else...”
It was within expectations. Right now, every floor of the labyrinth was a gold mine. These run-ins weren’t happening on just this island, but all over the labyrinth.
Where there was treasure, there would be competition.
“How many of them?” I asked.
“I don’t know for sure... However, at least one other clan is already on this island. Look over there at the entrance. The flag of a clan is propped up as if to show everyone.”
“I know the type.”
“It looks like a warning, telling others to go away since they arrived first... What do you think?”
Regardless, we had spent precious time getting here, so we were at least going to take a look around. Still, we checked the necessary details before recklessly going in.
“Adnus, is that the insignia of the Golden Tree Clan?”
“It is. The one with one of the Seven Powerful, the Golden Ghost, as their captain.”
I thought it might be them when I saw the insignia, but it was true.
The Golden Tree Clan was a clan I knew quite a bit about. First of all, its captain was one of the Seven Powerful that Erwen and Ainar were also a part of.
“Huh? Golden Tree? Isn’t that clan the...?!”
When Missha looked at me for confirmation, I gave her a nod. “That’s right.”
It was the clan that Mr. Bear was a part of.

chapters.title: Chapter 793: Red Ocean (5)
paragraphs: The Ten Great Clans, the Five Great Clans, the Four Great Clans...

In the past, these big and famous clans were bundled together, but this culture has faded away with the times as a natural byproduct of countless clans disappearing or fusing after years of chaotic events.

In any case, in this era of great change, there was a clan that showed incredible growth and began to make a new name for themselves: the Golden Tree Clan. Just a few years ago, the only notable thing about them was their captain. However, they had absorbed multiple clans into their ranks after showing great ability during the war, resulting in exponential internal growth.
Raven’s assessment of their clan was as such.

“The Golden Tree Clan? Hmm, I heard that they did a few things during the war, but from what I can tell, they only fought easy battles. Still, their fighting power is pretty well-rounded... And if I had to rank them like in the past, they would be around the level of the weakest of the Ten Great Clans?”
I turned to the guild master. “Adnus, what do you think?”

“There is a lot of talk going around about that clan, but it can’t be denied that they hold an immense amount of power. Oh, I have also heard that they are very close with certain figures in the political and financial world. A bit of connection with Count Alminus... They’re practically soulmates with our number three branch manager.”
“I see...”
From what the guild master told us, a total of ninety people had entered the labyrinth under the Golden Tree Clan, making them the fourth largest clan currently in the labyrinth.
It just went to show how much support they were given by both the palace and the guild. If not, they wouldn’t have been given that many slots for their adventurers.
“But what do you mean there’s a lot of talk going around them?” I asked.

“A few rumors are circulating within the organization. Word is that they exploit their members heavily... However, no one has come forth and confessed or anything like that. It just means the clan is very secure and good at keeping the mouths of their members shut tight.”
“Exploitation...”
Was that why Mr. Bear looked distressed whenever we brought up his clan?

“Still, they are regarded in a positive light,” he continued. “In fact, they are seen as more positive than most. Their pay is good, and their essences are distributed among the members rather than sold. It seems they take care of growing the clan.”
Hmm, I see...
It seemed what the guild master was saying was true. From what I’d seen from him before, Mr. Bear had eaten a new essence and had ranked up to rank 3 thanks to that practice.
“Abman... He’ll be fine, right?”
Though Missha shared my worries, Ainar was just excited that she’d be able to meet Mr. Bear again on the island.
“Let’s go in already! Meeting Urikfried here is a good omen!”
Well, it didn’t seem that good of an omen from my perspective.
“So, what will you do, Yandel?” Amelia interjected.
“What else? We’ll be going in.”
“I see... Understood.”
I paused, noticing Amelia looked a little conflicted. It was like she was holding back saying something she wanted to. “Just say it. What is it?”
“Well... If we meet the Golden Ghost, you shouldn’t underestimate him too much.”
I couldn’t help but tilt my head in confusion at that. She gave me that advice even knowing just how careful I was before I made any moves.
“Do you know something about him?” I pressed, intrigued. However, she stuck to telling me about rumors and past deeds she overheard, which only further made my curiosity about Golden Ghost grow.
Why is she acting like this? Just what kind of guy is he?
Well, I’d know when I saw him.

The opinion about the Great Navigator Pikma among the later generations was quite split. Something about how unlike what his stories said he didn’t explore the secrets of all the islands and that all he did was visit the islands and complete the map of the Great Sea.
Well, they weren’t wrong. Pikma wasn’t able to uncover every hidden secret of all the islands during his lifetime.
But how would anyone do that?
I didn’t believe that was a factor that could diminish his great reputation.

The labyrinth only opened once a month, and the world of the labyrinth itself would collapse after a set period had passed. Paired with only living once and that life being finite, it was physically impossible to uncover every secret hidden on every island.
It might be a different story if dozens of games could be run at once through a medium called the computer.
That’s why I know the secret of Skull Island.
The Skull Island of Catacoma was one of the islands in the far eastern sea, the Grand Rock region. The Great Navigator Pikma had this to say about the island:
“Easy, or perhaps more difficult than any other island.”
It was the perfect description, the best that could possibly be given for the island.

On the surface, the difficulty level of Skull Island was very low, but that changed once you started digging deeper. The passage Pikma had left behind was also what led others to discover the hidden secret of Skull Island.
Well, I don’t think they’d know about that, though.
In truth, even the woman who bought the information about Skull Island on Ghost Busters knew only about the main boss.
“What the? Why are they so weak?!” Ainar suddenly shouted in frustration.
From what I could hear, it seemed she wasn’t satisfied by the toughness of the monsters that appeared on the island.
It was to be expected. Most of the monsters that appeared on Skull Island were only rank-six.
“Ugh! Just when are we going to fight something strong?!”
“Why, Ainar? Isn’t it nice if they’re weak?”
“Missha! I want to fight something strong that I can write down in my biography!”
“Ah... I s-see? I don’t know much, so ask Bjorn.”
“I don’t want to...”
“Why not?”
“If I ask Bjorn about something like that, I get punished by Emily Raines.”
“Huh?”

I felt a little sorry for Ainar as I watched her mood quickly drop-even as she stared at me with eyes that begged for pity-but Amelia had trained her well. If she became a mother, I was sure she’d be able to educate-
“Yandel.”
“I wasn’t thinking about anything weird.”
“What are you talking about?”
I cleared my throat. “So why did you call my name?”
“I think we’ve entered the territory of the Golden Tree Clan.”
“Are they nearby?”
“I don’t sense anyone, but there are traces that show that they’ve gone this way several times before.”
Well, that made sense. We were near the center point of the island.
“We’ll be on this island for a few days. I should go say hello.”
With that, we continued going straight and headed for the island’s heart. When we arrived at the cave entrance in the center of the island...
“No one is here.”
The only thing that greeted us was an empty campsite littered with traces of people.
However, we were only confused for a moment.
“My, my,” came a gentle voice. “What a valuable guest we’re having here.”
Dozens of presences revealed themselves from behind us.
At that moment, our human radar Amelia also spoke.
“Yandel... We’re surrounded.”
Didn’t even need to tell me that.
We were surrounded by a group of ninety adventurers, but I only froze up for a split second.
“We apologize if we surprised you, Viscount Yandel.”

A man in his mid-thirties spoke in that same gentle tone, and when a blond man appeared in the same direction as the voice had, Amelia quietly whispered to me, “That’s dyed hair by the way. His original hair color is black.”
Uh, I thought it was going to be something important. It looked pretty natural for a dye job, but whatever.
“I am the captain of the Golden Tree Clan, Bill Ironlad. Please call me Bill.”
He had a bright smile on as he introduced himself to us. Maybe that smiling face of his was what allowed him to mesh with the political and financial elites.
I couldn’t know for sure, but I got a sense that he was no small fry.
“Good to see you, Ironlad. I didn’t expect such a grand welcome,” I said, half-greeting and half-warning.
He let out a laugh. “I apologize once again if it surprised you. We also didn’t know you were here, Lord Viscount.”
That was such an obvious lie.
“I see.”

Even as I nodded, I looked around at the ninety people who revealed themselves from their hiding spots. Their presence could only point to one thing: they had noticed us before we noticed them. It meant their detection abilities were greater than ours.
They even successfully masked the presence of all those people from us.
Did they really not know that it was us? No, they had to have known. Even then, they used a stealth skill on all their members and hid themselves in the open around us.
They want to crush us.

Adventurers spent money recklessly and enjoyed themselves drinking in the city, but became completely different beasts as soon as they entered the labyrinth. They became a part of nature. To survive, they would hold poison in their body, make themselves look bigger and more menacing, and put on bright and threatening feathers to adorn themselves.
Because if you looked weak, you would be ripped apart.
“By the way, this is a huge problem for us... Is that guy your goal as well, Viscount Yandel?”
Although there was no real way to know who “that guy” was, I agreed as I asked back, “And if I am?”
Although I’d said it in a somewhat aggressive tone, he didn’t show any signs of being ticked off as he just smiled.
“Haha, then I suppose it can’t be helped.”
“Are you saying you’ll give it up?”
“The situation is less than ideal, but we can’t do that. We too have people we are responsible for.”
“So you’re saying we’ll compete for it.”
“The treasures of the labyrinth are masterless. Finders keepers.”
Although something felt off about that last bit, I agreed with what he was saying.
Competition itself wasn’t wrong. The problem was if one side refused to concede or attack the other group because they were blinded by greed.
But from the way he’s acting, I don’t think they’d do that...
Even with the situation as it was, we weren’t immediately antagonizing each other. Was it because of my position and reputation?
Probably. If we were less famous as a clan, we would have been treated completely differently.
“How about we promise each other just two things before we begin this competition?”
“Go on.”
“We won’t interfere with each other. And the one who opened the mouth of that cave first will have the right to challenge it first... How about it?”
“Sure.”
“Then since we’re on the same page, we can leave the talks there. Let’s go for it.”
“Let’s go for it’ is too casual for you to say to me.”
“Hahaha... You are quite a funny person, Lord Viscount.”
Hmm, I wasn’t joking when I said it, though.
“Well then, we will be going first now that this has become a competition.”
After that, he walked away first like a gentleman. Raven let out a snort when she saw it.
“Hmph, he’s as annoying as they say.”
“What do you not like about him?”
“He didn’t talk about working together or sharing the spoils at all. He must be confident that his side will win.”
Well, that made sense.
“But is that a bad thing?”
“Pardon? Uh, not really... But shouldn’t you agree with me when I say it? I’m a member, and you’re the captain.”
Huh? A captain didn’t need to be emotionally aligned with his team.
“Don’t worry. We’ll enter the cave first.”
What a captain needed to do was bring victory home for his clan.

chapters.title: Chapter 794: Skull Island (1)
paragraphs: We were moving around the central part of the island without a goal.
Crunch! Crunch! Cruuunch!
Of course, we were destroying every single monster that appeared in our way as we did so.
There was only one reason I said we were moving without a goal. It was because we weren’t even getting into proper battles.
“This is boring.”
“Yes... I’m starting to think I’d rather look at papers and documents than do this.”

The average rank of monsters that appeared on Skull Island was rank six, and that number was inflated because of a few high-ranking monsters that had a low chance of appearing. Most monsters actually ranged between rank seven and rank eight.
The monsters weren’t new either. The only monster here that we still could gain experience from was just the rank-six Skull Ghost.
“I hope that monster you mentioned appears soon, Captain.”
Since even the noncombatant Auyen was falling into the same mood, it must have been exceedingly boring to walk around “aimlessly” like this.
Where’s all the fire of competition from before?
Well, it wasn’t that I couldn’t understand where they were coming from. It had already been two days since that fateful encounter.
“They haven’t found anything either, right?”
“Probably not,” I said, trying to alleviate Raven’s suspicion. “We would know if the cave opened.”
“They might have a way to hide it or something like that.”
I nearly smirked and told off Raven for her nonsense. Still, on second thought, it was possible.
“I mean, they had that with them too,” she insisted. “And a lot of them, at that.”
“Ah, you’re talking about that thing...”
The thing Raven was referring to was a numbered item. We weren’t entirely positive they had them, but there was a very likely chance that they did.
“Yes,” she answered. “Didn’t you agree with me as well? If they didn’t have that item, it didn’t make sense how they were able to hide from us.”
Well, that was true.
Detection was an auxiliary ability. Since Erwen and Amelia were more geared toward combat, I could overlook them not noticing our opponents.

However, our new member, Beleg, was an adventurer who had earned himself the title of Pursuer. To put it simply, he was a professional in detecting things. However, the other clan still noticed us first, and they had even succeeded in hiding so many people successfully. So how had they managed it?
I discussed it with Beleg for a while and came to a single conclusion. It was all thanks to busted items. We even had an idea as to what that item could be.

No. 16, Ebony Insignia. When equipped, the user’s stealth skills would be strengthened significantly. Their stats would increase while under stealth, they would get bonuses when ambushing a target, and much more. It was practically a graduation item for assassins.

Anyway, the item had two characteristics that were important to know given the situation. If someone wore the item and stayed still, they would enter absolute stealth. And second, when using its active ability, it temporarily created twenty-nine tokens that could be distributed to other people, which also allowed them to use the first ability.
If they used that, that’d explain how they were able to hide from us.

When I thought back to that moment, I recalled that everyone had just been silently waiting for us. They only revealed themselves when we approached the mouth of the cave. Some of my other clan members even reported seeing similar insignias on them too.
But to hide ninety people like that, you need three of those items...

Even with that problem, if this hypothesis was true, then that raised even more questions. Not so much a question of how they were able to get something so precious, but about the nature and character of this Golden Ghost guy who was able to obtain three in the first place. No matter how I looked at it, his intentions couldn’t be—
At that moment, Beleg stopped moving and whispered in my ear, “Viscount Yandel.”
“I told you to call me captain.”
He paused, acknowledging the correction. “Someone’s approaching.”
“How many?”
“Six.”
I didn’t even need to ask who they were. It was probably one of the subdivisions under the Golden Tree Clan.
“We will meet them if we continue on our way.”

However, I still found myself surprised by the situation. We hadn’t actually interacted with them for the last two days. Even if our routes converged, we would both detect each other from a distance and move away from each other.
“Looks like they have some business with us. We’ll wait here for them,” I decided.
As we stood there waiting, an adventuring team bearing the insignia of the Golden Tree Clan appeared from between the bushes that were shaped ominously, as expected on Skull Island.
“Yandel?”
“Abman.”
A completely unexpected encounter unfolded. Although we glanced at each other from our respective groups back at the cave, that wasn’t exactly the time to catch up.
In any case, I couldn’t help but chuckle when I realized what was going on. Judging by the shock on his face, it didn’t seem like he sought me out deliberately either.
“Looks like you got lost.”
“Not at all... We were just making our way through.”
Hmm? It was obvious that he was the scout for that team considering his abilities.

Although Mr. Bear was a scout, he was prone to getting lost, and he didn’t have the basic detection abilities that most scouts had. His skills were so bad that during the Team Apple Narak period, I even got scouting lessons from Rotmiller despite having a perfectly good scout on the team.
Still, thinking back on it now, I was fortunate to learn from him back then.

“Again?” One of Mr. Bear’s team members let out a sigh. Their sigh was different from the affectionate ones we let loose during our time in Team Apple Narak, however. “Weren’t you listening? The captain told us to avoid contact if possible.”
“Did you do this on purpose? Just so you could meet an old friend and talk with him?”
“Th-that’s not it! There’s no way I would do that. Th-this is a coincidence. A coincidence!”
“Coincidence, my ass. You just don’t have the skill for this.”
The mood immediately turned a bit sour.
Even from that short exchange, I could get a glimpse into the relationship between Mr. Bear and his team. Perhaps knowing the same, Mr. Bear glanced at us with an uncomfortable look in his eyes.
He looked like someone who had something exposed that he wanted to keep secret.

And unfortunately, it did seem that way. No one wanted their friends or family to see them get berated by their superiors, and what was on display here was most likely not everything he experienced on a regular basis. Even he used to hold back when we were in front of the others.
It was an old truth that actions more brutal and humiliating would be done in places others couldn’t see.
“In any case, my apologies, Lord Viscount. We’re not here to interfere... As you can see, it is not our fault, but this man’s.”
“I’m not going to blame anyone, so don’t worry.”
“That’s a relief to hear. You got that? Let’s move.”

I did want to talk more with Mr. Bear, but that was the most we could manage given the circumstances. Even knowing I could probably force them to give us some time if I demanded it, I recognized that probably wouldn’t be good for him. He could be framed as a traitor if he gave over information to us.
Above all, though, it seemed like Mr. Bear wanted to get out of this situation as fast as he could.
However, just as I was about to send them off...
“Hah... How did a loser like him end up on our team?”
A jab that was clearly too loud to be classified as “under the breath” caught my attention.
[Missha Karlstein has cast Glacial Soul.]
With a slash of a sword, a wall of ice formed in front of the ones trying to leave.
“You... What did you just say?”
Missha had been agitated.
The cold winds created by the ice wall grazed my skin.
While it was an unexpected rash action, it was fine for now. She hadn’t taken a direct stance against them yet. However, the problem here was that this couldn’t escalate any further.
“Viscount Yandel,” the man who seemed to be the team’s leader called, opting not to say anything to Missha. “Could I take this as you going against the agreement?”

I could sense a deeply hostile energy spearing me from the team captain’s eyes, but honestly, I was completely baffled by the turn of events. After all, he wasn’t even the captain of the clan, just a team captain.
I stepped forward, about to speak when Missha interrupted once more.
“Whatever, you! Goblin Head! Answer me. What did you just call Abman? What, cat got your tongue?”
Despite hearing Missha, he didn’t even glance her way.
Missha’s breathing began to roughen at the snub. Seeing how her hand holding her sword was shaking, she seemed absolutely enraged. It had been a long time since I had seen her so angry.
“Answer me.”
Her pronunciation became clearer, perhaps because the pitch of her voice lowered. Only then did the team captain answer her, equally annoyed.
“Is this because I called him a loser?”
“You’re kidding. So it was that.”
“Take that back while I’m asking nicely.”
“To be honest, I don’t know what authority you think you have to ask me to take back whatever I say.”
“What?”
“I mean, I know that you were on a team with Urikfried in the past. However, he is now a member of our clan. You have no right to interfere with our internal affairs.”
“Then it’s fine if he’s not your clan member? Abman! Come over here! Leave that clan now and—”
“Stop, Missha.”
It wasn’t me nor the team captain who cut Missha off, but Mr. Bear. Missha seemed shocked by the sternness of his voice.
“Why?”
I was trying to help you, her eyes seemed to plead, so why did you cut me off so harshly?
Mr. Bear didn’t answer her. Instead, the one who did was actually the team captain.

“You call yourself his precious ally and you don’t even know why? Urikfried borrowed money from our clan. It couldn’t be helped since his store business wasn’t going well and the labyrinth was closed for a year.”
“Hah! How much? We can pay it back—”

“It doesn’t matter if you can pay back or not. The condition for borrowing the money was that he would come on a specific number of expeditions with us. This is the first one, and he only has twenty-three more to go after this.”
“Is that... Is that why you bully him? Because he can’t leave even if he wants to?”
“I really don’t have a clue what you’re—”

“Stop there,” I intervened. Although Missha seemed to have a lot of things she wanted to say, I stopped her with a look. “I have no intention of interfering with your business, and I have even less desire to break an agreement. Let’s end it here.”
“Thank you.”
As I took a step back, the team captain lowered his head to me, and the interaction ended there.
However, it seemed Missha still couldn’t let it go.
“Why do you do that?” she demanded of them as they were about to leave.
Amelia, who was standing next to her, tried to stop her, but I held her back. I could tell Missha wasn’t going to attack them this time.
“I don’t know what you mean,” replied the captain.
“Why are you like that? You’re in the same team, and you’re allies... So why do you harass and bully him? Is that...something fun for you?”
The team captain seemed caught off guard at such an innocent question, but his eyes soon filled with anger.
“How nice. You live in a world completely different from ours.”
“What?”
“If you’ll excuse me.”
With that, they went back into the brush and hid their presence. Missha bit down on her lips, visibly still overcome with anger.
“Bjorn...”
“Don’t worry. I have a plan as well.”
“R-really?!”
It wasn’t a plan I originally had. Just something I thought up in the moment.
Winning the competition against the Golden Tree Clan and monopolizing the Skull Island event.
If that was the main quest, then I suppose I just got a side quest? Even if Mr. Bear himself didn’t want it.
If the guild master leaves, that creates a vacancy, right?
I couldn’t just sit by when I saw what happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 795: Skull Island (2)
paragraphs: The hidden secret of Skull Island was very simple.

By going around the map hunting down monsters, you might eventually stumble upon a monster named Key Bearer at a very rare rate. Although it was a type of mid-boss, it wasn’t that strong, just barely a rank four monster, though it was closer to a strong rank 5 when only considering its attack power.
In any case, if you hunted this monster after casting distortion magic on it, you could get its key and use it to enter the cave at the island’s center.
And if you keep fighting your way to the very inner part, the boss room appears.

Within the inner chamber was what was recognized as the “boss” of Skull Island, and it was fairly difficult. Though it was merely a rank 3 monster, only one team could enter the boss room at once, making it impossible to raid with a full expedition force.
Its attack patterns are tricky too.
Back in my early days in Ghost Busters, I sold information about Skull Island, specifically the strategy for defeating this very boss.
I wondered, did that user succeed in killing it? I couldn’t remember ever seeing her name on the posts or comments section of Ghost Busters, even until the day it closed.
Well, not that I cared.
“Mr. Yandel, are you sure this is alright?”
“Hmm? What do you mean?”
“This situation. You were so sure that we would enter the cave before them, but we haven’t seen even a trace of that key.”
Sure, it was true that not seeing the monster even once over the past two days was a bummer. Still, I simply replied, “Just wait. We’ll be going in first.”

I wasn’t planning on going the standard route for this quest anyway. How could twelve people even hope to best a group of ninety people when the goal was finding something on this vast island? No, my confidence was rooted in something else—a method of guaranteeing a key drop.
“Ah, there it is.”

Luck really was not on my side. We had been scouring the island for two days already, and only did it appear before us. I was honestly getting a little scared there with how long it took to find. Thankfully, however bad my luck was, the other side seemed to have it worse. The cave door had yet to open.
I clacked and crunched my way over the shards of bone that made up the ground.

It was a terrain feature of Skull Island, that bones formed the land. The bones came from people, monsters, and whatever else was available, and the most important bone of all was a very special skull.
Like so.

I approached the bone, staring down at what honestly looked like more of a boulder than a skull. However, since bones of that size were common on the island, the one I had in my sights didn’t stand out too much against the others.
Two horns and a square jaw.
After confirming the characteristic features, I raised my hammer. Raven chose that moment to speak.
“This skull... Isn’t this a Key Bearer?”
“Huh?” I said, a little caught off guard. “It doesn’t look like one at all.”
“No, it does. I even happen to have its anatomical chart...”
“Why do you even have that on you?”
“I went and researched a little since I heard we might be going to Skull Island. Anyway, look at this! Doesn’t it match?”
It was a perfect match. “It does...”

“Maybe this was left behind by other adventurers who killed it after casting distortion magic?” she suggested. “Unlike the other floors, the Great Sea doesn’t return to its original state every time the labyrinth closes and opens, right?”

Hmm... That sounded plausible enough. The sixth floor didn’t get reset, but it would then follow that there should be multiple of these skulls just rolling about on this island. Why was it always just one?
As an adventurer who lived and breathed in this world, my curiosity for this phenomenon pecked its head up.
“That doesn’t matter to me.”

However, true to my particular adventuring nature, I let that curiosity go in favor of pushing forward. Gamers didn’t need to understand the phenomena—they just needed to use it, just as I would do now. There was only one thing that mattered.
Crunch!
When a skull with a specific shape was destroyed at the center of Skull Island, the key could always be obtained.
“Beleg, head toward the cave,” I commanded.
After obtaining the key, we quickly moved to the center of the island. Raven noticed me snickering the whole way there and asked, “What’s got you so giddy?”
“Nothing much.”
What face would the Golden Ghost make when I showed up with the key in hand?

When we arrived at the entrance to the cave, it was empty except for a single team who seemed to be standing guard. They eyed us with tilted heads as we approached, but those eyes soon went wide when they realized we were heading toward the cave entrance.
“D-did you obtain the key?”
“Yeah?” I asked like it should’ve been obvious. “Move.”
“P-please wait! Could you please wait a moment?”

When I kept walking like I was about to use the key and enter the cave, the makeshift guards tried to desperately stop me. I did expect something similar to happen, but I acted surprised and furrowed my brow.
“Why should I wait? From what it looks like, you haven’t gotten the key yet. I have. So we have the right to challenge the cave first. I’m sure that was the agreement, right?”
“Yes, that’s right. You are right. However... Just a moment! Just for a moment would do, so would you please talk with our captain first?”
“Hmm. I’ll give you ten minutes.”
“Pardon? Ten... Ten minutes?”
“Why? You got a problem?”
“No, no! Not at all. Thank you for this!”
