One of the guards quickly ran off. Soon enough, the Golden Ghost appeared, apparently having heard the report. It took around eight minutes for him to arrive.
Looks like he was waiting in the area. Not hunting, but just ordering people around.
Well, it wasn’t my place to say how a captain should command his people, but I preferred working with my team members on the ground.
The Golden Ghost sighed. “I heard the gist of it. Thank you for waiting. So, you’ve obtained the key?”
“Yeah? Are you thinking of stopping me?”

He waved his hands, shaking his head in denial at my accusation. “No, of course not. I just wanted the opportunity to discuss a deal with you, Lord Viscount. Again, I thank you for allowing me that chance.”
What a funny guy. I hadn’t even said I would take him up on his offer, and he was already thanking me.
“Whatever, just talk,” I deadpanned. “Time is still ticking, and as you know, time is money in the labyrinth.”
“Yes. As such, I will make my offer simple. How much do you want?”
“...Are you asking me to sell the key?”
“No. We obtained the key thirty minutes ago ourselves, so we don’t need it. We just want the opportunity to challenge the cave first. Naturally, if we fail, you will be given your own chance.”
Was it because his nickname was the Golden Ghost? He sure was quick to bring up money as soon as his plan failed.
“You say that, but we both know the first person to challenge it will succeed,” I argued.
“That’s why I’m asking how much you want.”
“Why are you even asking me for the amount?”
“That’s because we need your—”
“Will you give me ten billion stones if I ask for it?”
He went silent.
Yeah, you have nothing to say to that.

“Just tell me plainly the maximum amount you can give me. I’ll think about it after that,” I said. “And don’t even think about slowly raising the amount to see if I push you on it. I hate wasting time.”
Slowly, he offered, “How about four hundred million stones?”
“The essence of the boss sells for five hundred million stones by itself.”
“But there’s no guarantee that the essence will appear.”
Fair enough. I wouldn’t take the deal if I were him. If the boss didn’t drop the essence, it would be a complete loss.
But it does feel like he put out the maximum amount possible.
He seemed to have notified the members of his clan all over the island, as the members of the Golden Tree Clan began to slowly trickle in as we talked.
“Then what will you do?”
“Hmm...” I acted like I was contemplating my options before answering, “I’ll accept the deal.”
“Oh, that was a wise—”
“However, you need to give us Abman Urikfried as well.”
There was an almost imperceptible shift in the Golden Ghost’s expression. He was still smiling brightly, but his teeth glinted, like a hunter who found his prey.
“I know you two used to be close associates... It seems you are still close after all this time?”
“People you can trust in the labyrinth are valuable.”
“Haha, that is true.”
“And your answer?”
“I refuse. As you said, people you can trust in the labyrinth are valuable.”
Hah, trust? With the way he was letting Mr. Bear get treated in his own clan?
I wanted to smack that smiling face of his, but my modern upbringing just barely managed to keep me from losing my temper.
The Golden Ghost wasn’t finished either.
“Even rarer still is someone as willing to sacrifice themselves for the organization as Mr. Urikfried.”
Bastard. That was a threat, right? Saying he would force Mr. Bear into dangerous missions and treat him like a dog?
Breathing out a sigh, I held back with my inhuman levels of patience once more. “Fine. You can keep the money, so hand Abman over. Then we’ll give up that cave—”
“Apologies, but I’m afraid that will also be difficult.”
I froze. “What?”
“Considering the amount of money Mr. Urikfried borrowed from us, it wouldn’t be a fair trade for us.”
“What...?”
A four hundred million stone deal wasn’t enough? Just how much did he borrow?
“Then we can pay the difference—”
“No. We won’t be dissolving our contract with Mr. Urikfried.”
When I didn’t respond, he added, “You may go in first, Viscount.”
The Golden Ghost didn’t seem bothered by the trade. In fact, he seemed outright giddy by the exchange as he turned away.
I couldn’t help but grit my teeth at the sight.
Although we succeeded in our main quest of opening the cave before the Golden Tree Clan, we’d failed our subquest of extracting Mr. Bear from their clutches.
The cave entrance was a massive skull.
This felt exactly like one of those dinosaur-themed parks.
We entered through the opened jaw of the skull to find a singular steel door with a keyhole.
“Graaaaaagh!”
As we put the key in and turned it clockwise, a spooky and threatening roar of a beast echoed across the island.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you going in?”
I turned my head, meeting eyes with the Golden Ghost, who had been watching me as I studied the entrance.
...He’s smiling?
What an irritating guy. I had no idea what he was thinking either.
“Mr. Yandel?”
I sighed, knowing we had to focus on the main quest first. “I got it, so stop pushing me.” Then, I pushed aside the unsettling feeling and entered the cave.
The entrance closed behind us with a loud boom.

chapters.title: Chapter 796: Skull Island (3)
paragraphs: The moment the door in the cave closed and we were cut off from the outside, the torches lined up on the walls lit up one by one, trailing into the darkness. Still, the cavernous space was not fully illuminated, as the path ten yards in front of us was still shrouded in darkness.
“Leait.” Raven sent out an orb of light into the darkness before exclaiming, “Oh! So it really doesn’t get lit up. Seeing how my mana is being maintained, I don’t think the spell was cut off either.”

She seemed interested in the mechanics of the darkness, but I didn’t feel too drawn to it. I wasn’t a scholar, but a player. The thought of trying to discover why a field worked the way it did was honestly funny to me.
[You have entered a special area.]
[Field Effect—Catacoma is applied. Wound Exacerbation (High) is applied. While within the designated area, a random stat will decrease by 1 whenever you kill a monster.]
[Countdown is removed.]
[Only the light of the dead can defeat the darkness.]

Light spells or torches were of no use against the darkness within the cave. The keywords “light of the dead” had once pushed me to try using dark magic or similar items here, but they had all failed. The only things that could give us vision were the torches already lining the walls. Not all of them were activated along the passageway, but it was fine.
After all, the monsters soon began to appear.
“Oh! It’s wearing a skull!”
“Wait!” I quickly stopped Ainar who tried to run up to the first monster she saw. “Hold on.”
“Hmm? What is it, Bjorn?”
“Adnus will defeat any monsters that appear from now on.”
Ainar appeared confused, but the guild master immediately grasped the situation and smirked. “So you’ll be putting me up as the sacrifice.”
“What sacrifice? You won’t die from it,” I told him.
“Understood. I will willingly sacrifice myself for the group.”
Both of us knew what was going on here. Was he making noise about “sacrificing” himself just to emphasize the credit he should receive?
Adnus drew his sword.
“A sword…? Wasn’t he an archer?”
I ignored the question. He did use the bow too, but he was actually a hybrid. His skill set wasn’t locked into a specific weapon.

With that, the guild master killed four monsters in a single slash as they emerged from the darkness. Nothing too surprising, given how the monsters that appeared at this stage were around rank 7. What was truly difficult wasn’t the battle itself but rather the price of victory.
[Illya Adnus’s Natural Regeneration has decreased by 1.]
[Illya Adnus’s Strength has decreased by 1.]
[Illya Adnus’s Flexibility has decreased by 1.]
[Illya Adnus’s Fire Resistance has…]
The more monsters one defeated here, the lower one’s stats would become. However, that didn’t mean we could just walk by without killing them.
Fwoosh!
“Oh! The flame over there became bigger!”
Catacoma was created in such a way that we could only progress if we continued to kill monsters.
“I don’t know about the rest of you, but I can definitely feel this taking its toll,” Adnus huffed. “I just had to have my strength decreased early on.”
“Hmm? What do you mean?”
Raven was the one who answered Ainar. “Every time you kill a monster here, a random specific ability is decreased.”
“Specific ability…? What do you mean?”
“The things obtained through essences and the Achievements of Gabrielius. Strength, Agility, Resistances—those sorts of things.”
“Huh?! They’re decreased?” Ainar shouted with a look of disgust on her face. She was probably picturing how she nearly charged the monsters as soon as they appeared.
The guild master let out a bitter laugh. “Still, someone needs to make the sacrifice.”
“I respect you, Adnus! Taking something like that for the team! You are a trustworthy warrior!”
“Haha… Thank you.”
The entire thing played out like a skit to me.
Sacrifice? The stat decrease isn’t even permanent.
The penalties he accumulated would be lifted as soon as we left this place. Still, it wasn’t exactly like the experience was pleasant.

“You might be fine now, but be sure to ready your heart. From the testimonies of the people who’ve visited this place, they all said they went through something they never want to experience ever again.”
“Well, losing your abilities and becoming the same as an ordinary citizen would feel quite sobering.”
“Yes. Although, as a wizard, I wouldn’t know.”
After listening to their conversation, Missha piped up with a question. “Huh? Then shouldn’t we have the wizards kill the monsters?”
“I heard that wizards would have their mana decreased,” Raven explained, avoiding her gaze.
“Eh? Then wouldn’t wizards know how it feels as well?”
Raven didn’t say anything to Missha’s logical point. How rare. Missha one-upped Raven in logic and made her go silent.

Still, while it was an entertaining scene in a way, as the captain, I couldn’t just sit by and let everyone waste time. “Let’s stop talking and keep moving,” I said, cutting off the conversation there so we could continue our expedition.
[Illya Adnus’s Fire Resistance has decreased by 1.]
[Illya Adnus’s Aggression has decreased by 1.]
[Illya Adnus’s Soul Power has decreased by 1.]
[Illya Adnus’s Soul Power has…]

As we traveled further in and the guild master killed more and more monsters, he appeared visibly worse for wear. Unlike before, when he could kill four monsters with a single slash, he now needed to put in considerably more effort to kill each monster.
There was a reason I didn’t let Auyen take up the role with him. A certain base level of stats was necessary for this strategy.
“Bjorn, how about you help him a little…?” Ainar suggested. “He looks like he’s struggling. Can’t we help him and let the guild master deal the killing blow?”
I sternly shook my head. “Just watch him.”

Removing all variables was the play. If we helped him get the last hit but ended up making a mistake, we’d lose around half the reason we were even doing this. Even if it was hard on him, keeping on as we were was the best thing we could do for the guild master.
“Good work,” I told him as he heaved in breaths. “Let’s keep moving. This way.”

I needed to choose the right path to decrease our travel time, as Catacoma wasn’t a linear cave. It was a maze of sorts like the Crystal Cave, but unlike the first floor, if you got lost here, you would lose too many stats and fail the boss battle.
Not that it would matter much to a large expedition force that could afford many sacrifices.
“There’s a door there!”
“Oh! Then are we done?”
“What’s with that guy in front?”
Finally, our dungeon crawling led us to the threshold of the boss room.
I quickly calculated in my head. Three hundred seventeen—that was how many monsters the guild master had killed on our way here.
Alright, since it’s over three hundred, we’ve completed one condition…
Without wasting any time, we began our battle against the gatekeeper.

The battle against the mid-boss was pretty inconvenient. If we just wanted to kill it, we could just have Erwen fire a full-charge arrow, but that would lead to problems downstream during the next stage.
“Adnus! Kill it already!”
“Ugh! I’m trying! But I’ve taken on too many curses…”
“I know, but hurry!”
We made careful work of damaging the boss until it only had a sliver of health left before holding it in place so the guild master could land the final blow.
[You have defeated the Grave Keeper, Aleton.]
[Slaying an Elite Boss bonus. EXP +1]
The guild master successfully landed the final hit, and the mid-boss disappeared into a spray of light. This completed a hidden secret as well.
[The cursed one has defeated the Grave Keeper. The Curse of the Vengeful Spirit will not spread.]

Defeating the Grave Keeper usually caused the debuff of the character who had been cursed the most to spread to all characters. That was why the formal clearing method was for everyone to kill an equal number of monsters so that the curse was distributed equally among them after clearing the mid-boss. It was also the strategy that I’d sold once upon a time.

That woman didn’t even know about the existence of the hidden boss anyway. There was no reason to tell her that if you stacked all the debuffs onto one person so that they became the cursed one and then had them defeat the mid-boss, the curse wouldn’t spread.
“I don’t see an essence.”
“That’s a shame,” Raven replied sulkily to me.
“Not really. It’s a trash essence to begin with.”
“Still, it should cost a bit, how rare it is. It has some research value as well.”
Right. I did remember something about her being interested in things like that.
“Whatever, let’s just go in.”
After defeating the gatekeeper, we opened the door and entered the room beyond.
“There’s nothing here?”
“It’s because we have twelve people here.”

The cave’s overall design was similar to the island, with the wall, ceiling, and floor all made of skulls. Even the torches stuck to the walls were skulls burning with internal fire. This terrain feature extended to the interior of the boss room as well. The one special feature was that on the opposite wall to where we were, there was a skull of a monster that was much larger than the one we saw at the cave entrance.
“Oh, oh! Raven! What monster is that over there? It looks really strong!”
“Well, I don’t know. There shouldn’t be that many monsters of that size in the labyrinth… Maybe it’s not a monster?”
“Hmm… I wanted to fight one in the future! Oh well!”
We slowly moved forward in formation into the huge, open area.
“Erwen, begin.”
“Yes.”
At my command, Erwen closed her eyes and began to concentrate, and I didn’t move my eyes away from Erwen as she did.
[An unknown energy is revealed after all resources have been exhausted.]
“Now. Everyone, leave.”

I barked the order as soon as Chaos Circuit was activated. Everyone except the ones I had notified beforehand quickly left the boss room. Amelia, Ainar, Missha, Erwen, the guild master, and I were the only members fighting against the boss this time.
Rather than choosing the elites, I’d picked the members I wanted to get the achievement. This wasn’t going to be a fight anyway.
As soon as the other members left the room, the door slammed closed and the entire area began to shake as if an earthquake were passing through.
“Graaaaaaah!”
The howling we first heard when we entered the cave roared once more. Then, an intimidating-looking boss swam out of the skulls on the ground with a clatter and stood, and as soon as it did…
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Concentrated Fire.]
“Graaa…oh…?”
Three phases were skipped instantly.
The official clearing strategy for the Skull King was pretty tricky. As the raid slowly progressed, the gauge on the soul marble it carried around to show its HP would continually decrease.
When its health decreased to 80 percent, it would deal out an AOE curse.
At 60, it would summon minions.
At 40, it would activate its insta-kill ability.
And when it dropped to 20 percent health, it became momentarily invulnerable before recovering and obtaining an even stronger buff.
[Skull King’s soul reserves are below 20%.]
[Skull King has cast Absorb Soul.]
However, we skipped the first three phases and went straight to phase four.
Luckily, phase four wasn’t that difficult either. In her infinite MP state, Erwen had other things she could do beyond Concentrated Fire.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has summoned Elemental Ruler of Darkness, Dicloe.]
Boom! Bang!
As Erwen continued to dole out her firepower, the Skull King’s soul marble spilled out faster than it could refill.
[Skull King has absorbed all souls. All authorities held by the Skull King are significantly—]
[Skull King’s soul reserves are below 20%.]
[There are no souls to absorb.]
As soon as Absorb Soul ended, its health immediately fell below 20 percent, and we entered the final phase.
[Skull King has cast Eternal Freedom.]
Next was its berserk mode, one that all boss monsters were expected to have. The strategy for dealing with it was simple.
[Skull King is now immune to all damage.]
[Skull King’s soul marble reserves quickly deplete.]
We just needed to stay alive, and I was a professional at that.
[Skull King’s soul marble is nearly empty.]

After rampaging for about one minute, Skull King suddenly stopped. Although we hadn’t killed it yet, the raid was practically over. Even an ordinary person would be able to walk over to the stationary monster and crack the glass marble on the body.
Around two minutes after summoning it… So the regeneration from phase 4 and the berserk mode each took up a minute.
“Good work, Erwen. And as planned, Adnus, you’ll kill it.”
“Understood.”
The guild master then approached the stopped Skull King and destroyed the soul marble to end the raid.
[You have defeated Skull King. EXP +7]
[Elite Boss Defeat Bonus. EXP +1]
Unfortunately, it didn’t drop an essence, but I didn’t mind. The main dish would come later.
[The cursed one has defeated the Skull King.]
[A portion of the old story has been completed.]
As the Skull King’s bone shards dissipated into flashes of light, the entire space shook once more.
“Ugh… What’s this? Weren’t we done here?”
Without meaning to, I smirked. “Congratulations, Ainar.”
“Huh? What do you mean?”
Rather than giving her an answer, I pointed toward the skull of the huge monster decorating the back wall.
“Didn’t you say you wanted to fight one?”
It was time to defeat the secret boss.

chapters.title: Chapter 797: Skull Island (4)
paragraphs: The Skull King wasn’t a boss that appeared every time the labyrinth opened. The usual rate was about one out of every seven times, and when it did make an appearance, the cave entrance was simply kept open.
It was for the convenience of the gamers. If that hadn’t been the case, people would farm for the key every time and enter the boss room only to discover it was empty.
“Huh? The earthquake stopped!”

The tremors that appeared after Skull King died soon stopped. It meant that the path to the next chapter had opened. After all, to fight the secret boss, you needed the cursed one to kill both the Grave Keeper and the Skull King.
The entrance to the boss room rolled open again, and our allies who were waiting on standby outside entered.
“It’s already over?”
“It hasn’t even been three minutes...”
They couldn’t hide their shock.

To be fair to them, the Skull King was a pretty infamous boss. Not many teams could kill a rank three monster with just six people, as that would require all members of that team to be adventurers of rank three or above. Though, that was the case before the companionship spell was upgraded. It was much easier now.
“But it seems an essence didn’t appear.”
“As you can see.”
“What about the chest?”
“Not yet. We’ll look for it now.”

Looking together was the most efficient course of action. Treasures were the biggest drive for adventurers, so before we went on to the next chapter, my allies and I worked together to find the treasure chest, which was itself a hidden secret. Only after defeating the boss could we start rooting around for it.
“Gah! Why can’t they just give it to us? Why is it hidden?!”
“It’s all because of the Achievements of Gabrielius. Only those who are fated for it are allowed to find it.”
“Ugh... That Gabrielius guy, he must be a weird one!”
“Even so, this is a pretty famous achievement of his. Anyone who tries to defeat the Skull King would know. The Golden Tree Clan outside probably—”
“Oh! I found it! I found it!”
Already?
I shot a dubious glance at Ainar, only to find it really was the treasure chest.
She’s pretty good at this.

Ainar was honestly a pretty lucky person, the type to live a decent life without even trying. Another example would be Sven Parav, the man with the secret title of Golden Goblin. Still, there was something unsettling about his particular brand of luck. It was like his luck always put him in a desperate situation.
“Bjooorn! Can I open it?! No, I will open it! Give me permission!”
“Sure,” I said with a smirk, giving her an approving nod.
Ainar grabbed the padlock...
No, I guess it’s a bonelock?
Anyway, she punched the lock off the chest made of bone. Slowly, she opened the chest.
In comparison to the humongous size of the chest itself, the contents within were tiny. Raven pushed Ainar to the side and picked the item up to take a closer look at it.
“This is quite valuable... Looks like the Golden Ghost will get pretty mad if he hears about this.”
“Hmm? Aruru, what is it? Isn’t it just a letter?”
“Ah, this is a talisman-type item.”
Items like that were categorized as charms in the game. They were in the same category as Ainar’s No. 9999, Beginner’s Luck, and No. 1001, Alonso’s Travel Bag, that I had gifted Auyen.
“Oh! Then is this a numbered item too?”
“Yes, that’s right. No. 444, Dedrius’s Invitation.”

“A triple-digit numbered item! Amazing! But what is it used for?” Ainar looked at the letter that was sealed with wax and tilted her head, curious because it was a numbered item but completely ignorant of its possible uses.
I couldn’t exactly blame her. It was near-impossible to figure out what ability a talisman granted by appearances alone.
“If you carry this around, you won’t get attacked by undead-type monsters,” Raven explained.
“Okay, and?”
“That’s all.”
“Huh? Didn’t you say it’s valuable? I think the bag that our navigator has seems better than this.”
Even Missha looked disappointed by the item’s effect.
Well, to each their own. To truly understand the value of that one line of text, you needed to use it first.
“It is valuable. Unlike Alonso’s Travel Bag, the effects of this talisman are absolute. If you have this on you, you will never be attacked. Even if you attack first.”

As an example, one of the rifts on the eighth floor was called Necropolis. Approximately 99 percent of the monsters within were undead, so if a damage dealer equipped this item, they had the potential to solo-clear the rift. Not to mention the handful of rank 1 undead-type monsters there were out there.
“Really? What an interesting item... Could I take a look at it?”
“Yes. But you can never take off the seal on the letter.”
“Hmm? What happens if you do?”
“You die.”
“Eeek!”
Raven’s short but impactful explanation made Missha quickly let go of the invitation letter. I chuckled at the interaction.
Honestly, she only ever knows half the information.

Strictly speaking, it wasn’t a guaranteed death. If you opened that in the labyrinth, you would be dragged to a hidden field called Hell. Problem was, the difficulty there was so high that it was practically impossible to return alive. No matter how strong the character was, they wouldn’t be able to return if they opened the letter.
Unless they opened the letter at a specific location, of course.
“Then who should carry this?”

Hmm, now that was a good question. One thing was certain—it wasn’t an item that I should be holding. The role of the tank in the labyrinth was to get hit, so I shouldn’t even get close to items of that particular variety.
I thought for another moment, then made my decision.
“Emily Raines, you should keep this on you.”

Amelia was the best choice in my opinion. The amount of trust I had in her was on another level entirely. I would always feel a little anxious if I gave it to anyone else, but I could trust her to never break the seal and carry it with the proper safeguards.
Either way, we’ve got yet another valuable on our hands.
A triple-digit numbered item before our main dish. Our prognosis was looking good.
Or was it actually looking bad...? Bad things always followed good events.
Shrugging off a string of good luck would be too naive, considering everything I had gone through.
“I should check up on them, at least once,” I decided aloud.
“Check? On who?”
“The Golden Tree Clan.”
“Hmm... Wouldn’t they have left already? They have to have known we wouldn’t fail.”
I agreed with her on that point, but...
“Ainar, but we might need to wait a little longer before we fight that guy.”
“Huh?”
“Let’s go outside and check on them one last time before coming back to fight.”

The next chapter after the Skull King wasn’t through a portal and it wasn’t a closed door like the cave entrance either—it was just there for the taking. If they wanted to, they could follow us inside.
“We’re heading back.”
I didn’t ignore the ominous feeling creeping over me and marched my way back out of the cave.
“They aren’t here.”
When we arrived, the cave entrance was completely barren.
“What do you want to do now?”
There were two possibilities. Either they really just left without a second thought...
Or they’re hiding their presence on purpose and are waiting for us.
The latter option also split the potential motive into two different sub-scenarios.
One: they knew about the secret boss and were aiming for that like we were.
Two: they didn’t know about it, but they were waiting for us to finish just in case under the assumption that my presence might indicate some secret waiting to be unveiled.

Or maybe none of that was relevant and they just turned into plunderers to take our possessions, but honestly, the possibility of that was near zero. Even if they did succeed in killing all of us, how would they keep everyone quiet when they had so many members? Secrets were bound to leak, and the Golden Ghost would never be able to handle the aftermath.
“If it really bothers you, we can go out and check the coast as well. They wouldn’t be able to cover all their tracks if they used a boat to get off the island,” Amelia suggested.

I just shook my head, though. We wouldn’t be sure even with that anyway. False traces could be created, and if they were really determined to keep themselves hidden, we didn’t have the skill set required to spot them with our current abilities on hand.
“We’ll go back.”
I took a step into the cave again, but not before adding, “Marrone, Raven. Set up detection magic on the path so that we are immediately notified if someone enters.”
“Will that work? Their stealth skills seemed pretty good.”
“It will work. Those stealth skills are all thanks to their equipment.”

It might have been a different story if a stealth specialist were wearing that equipment, but if all those members wanted to enter the cave, they would be discovered in the end. The condition for absolute stealth was staying still, after all.
“It’s done.”
“How long can it be maintained?”
“At least twelve hours, easily. The caveat is that they will be able to detect that we’ve set up our spells.”
Good to know. Still, I said, “It doesn’t matter. We should be able to detect if they disable it.”
“That’s true.”
“Alright, let’s hurry.”
I took the members and quickly moved into the cave—not toward the boss room but instead through the paths near the entrance.
“It’s easy to move around since all the lights are on.”
“Those pesky monsters are gone too.”
“But when is the curse on me going to dissipate? From what I heard, it should be removed after defeating the Skull King... Is it related to whatever we’re looking for right now?”
“I’ll tell you later.”
We continued to roam around the path in the early section of the cave until we stumbled on a dead-end.
“Is this it?”
I didn’t answer Raven’s question. I just turned around to look at our backs.
It was a long, straight, empty path.
Alright, this should be enough...
“Wait here, just a bit longer,” I ordered. “A special condition needs to be fulfilled for the hidden path to appear.”
I approached the wall of the dead-end. Then, I made a show of looking for something as I touched the wall.
After all, this wasn’t actually the entrance.

Quietly, I handed Raven a note, the one I’d written in secret behind my shield on our way here. After reading through the note, she sent me a subtle nod and put the paper in her pocket. Her expression shifted to one of mild exasperation and resignation.
“So I need to do this to open it? Got it. I’ll prepare it right away.”
Given her immediate response, I could tell Raven understood what I was trying to do.
This is why working with veterans is nice. With how much time we’ve spent together, we can communicate ideas without having to spell them out.
“Hmm? Raven, what are you doing?”
“Mr. Yandel requested a specific spell.”
“Oh? Which one?”
“It’s a secret. If I tell you, you’ll go around telling everybody.”
“Wh-what are you saying?! I am an honorable warrior who can keep her mouth shut!”
“If you’re really curious, I’ll tell you later. It’s not like you really care though, right?”
“Hmm, that’s true. This feels like it will take a while, so I’ll be over there eating jerky.”
I made a point of asking Marrone about the state of the detection magic as I touched the wall. While everyone was waiting, Raven finished drawing the magic circle.
“It’s done.”
Her spell was ready.
“Alright, then let’s go.”
As I gave her the sign, Raven poured mana into her magic circle. Light flashed out of the circle, and my vision shifted.
The spell that I requested from her wasn’t a spell to find the secret door or anything like that.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank 4 space magic Mass Teleport.]
Mass Teleport. Specifically, teleporting us all back to the crossroads that connected to the long corridor we were currently in.
The reason was simple.
I was certain of it. Although we couldn’t see it with our eyes yet...
“Behel—LAAAAAA!”
A rat bastard was definitely tailing us.
[You have cast Transcendence.]
[You have cast Giantization.]

Immediately after we successfully teleported, I enlarged my body so that it filled the entire corridor. It was so cramped that I found it difficult to even walk, but that also meant that it was too tight for anyone to be able to walk past me.
Boom! Boom!
I then pushed my shield forward until it filled the entire path in front of me and ran toward the dead-end. Even so, I didn’t feel anything notable.
Is there really no one here?

I questioned my choice, even wondering if I was doing something useless again. However, it didn’t matter. Being smart enough to catch a rat was nice, but I’d take being foolish if it meant we had no rats at all.
Boom! Boom!
And so, regardless of what my shield didn’t run into, I charged forward.
Boom! Boom!
The moment I reached the wall at the end of the path, though, a smirk stole across my face.
Boom!
Wasn’t the sound I heard...
Crunch!
...the sound of something being smashed?
Yeah, I knew it. Got you, you bastard.

chapters.title: Chapter 798: Skull Island (5)
paragraphs: When I was young, I once grabbed a bug with my fingers. After pushing my palm up against the wall that the bug was on, I twisted my palm to crush it... then promptly ran over to the toilet to throw the bug into it before washing my hands.

As I got a little older, I learned that it felt a little disgusting to do it with my bare hands, so I began to use tissues to kill bugs. However, the method itself never changed, and now in my adult years, I was using a shield instead.
I pressed to crush.
“Urgh—!”
Then I twisted to burst the insect.
The important part here was to do the twisting procedure just right. If done wrong, the bug could get away.
As I slowly moved the shield off of the wall, a half-crushed woman flopped onto the ground.
“Looks like she didn’t die from that, thankfully,” I mumbled, staring down at her.
Raven scurried over to me. “But she will die at this rate.”
Well, there was no point in wasting money by using a potion on her.
“Parav!” I shouted, calling upon the one person associated with religion in our clan. “Come here and use a healing spell.”

Knowing she could run away the moment she was healed, I made sure to bind the woman thoroughly. We took off all her equipment, bound her arms and feet, and then put her on her stomach. I topped off our preparations by placing my foot on her back to apply a bit of pressure.

It wasn’t exactly a good look, but who cared? Barbarians were warriors of true equality. Not even just barbarians, really. It was the world at large. Regardless of who or what an adventurer was, they would face the appropriate consequences for their actions.
Speaking of, the woman was still lying face down and acting like she was unconscious.
“You’re awake.”
“Kill me,” she immediately answered. “I chose to do this of my own free will.”
Hmm, maybe “answer” wasn’t the right word to use?
It surprised me a bit, honestly. Even given her situation, I hadn’t expected those to be the first words out of her mouth the moment she woke up.
Kaislan let out a mocking laugh. “It’s like she thinks she’s a member of the Order of the Rose.”

Whatever her motivations, her behavior was outside of my expectations. It wasn’t like she was a soldier of the palace who had undergone intense brainwashing. This was a regular clan member we were dealing with.
“Why are you so loyal to Golden Ghost?”
She hesitated at my question. “As I said, I chose to do this.”
“Why did it have to be this type?” I grumbled, breathing out a deep sigh before taking a different angle. “What’s his goal?”
“As I said—”
“Then what is your goal?”
Another hesitation. “Just kill me.”
“What? Is he holding your family hostage or something?”
The woman flinched very slightly.
Huh? I said that just to say it, but it’s true? Just what kind of monster is this Golden Ghost bastard?
I had no way of knowing. However, what I did know was that the woman in front of me was different from those brainwashed soldiers. There was a way to extract information out of her.

“You reacted to the word family. Do you also owe him something? You know if you die, the debt will be passed onto your family, and then they will die since they won’t be able to pay their taxes, right?”
The woman’s shoulders flinched again.
That certainly made things a little easier.

“I swear upon my honor and name as a warrior. If you answer me truthfully, I will help you to the best of my ability. The moment we return to the city, we will protect your family. If you want, I could accept them as my vassals as well.”
The woman stayed silent for a long moment, and I gave her time to think and just waited.
“Kill me.”
However, I received the same answer again.
I didn’t understand. With my reputation and fame, didn’t it make more sense to ditch this Golden Ghost or whatever and side with me?
Just what did that bastard do to make her like this?

Still, we were in luck. The woman didn’t seem used to lying and was instead the type to wear her emotions on her sleeve. It wasn’t exactly easy to control your expression when standing face-to-face with death.
“Is the Golden Ghost still on the island?”
Flinch.
“Did the Golden Ghost send you to kill us?”
No reaction.
“Hmm, if that’s not the goal... So this is just him keeping an eye on us...”
Flinch.
“He thought that I didn’t come here to simply kill the Skull King.”
Flinch.

“If he did notice, it would’ve been back then... When I made the offer that I would grant him the right to enter first if he gave us Abman Urikfried. He was probably sure of it then, that we weren’t here for the Skull King. Looks like he was very curious what this other thing we were here for was.”
The woman seemed startled to hear my deduction, as she flinched once more before she just closed her eyes in apparent concession. She was trying to cut off any clues she could give to us.
“Raven,” I called.
“Yes?”
“Make it so she can’t hear us. Let’s talk for a bit.”
“All right. Just a second.”
With that, I got Raven to use magic to block our voices from reaching her, and we began our discussion. Missha was the first person to speak.
“I think it’s true that she has no intentions of harming us. But we need to figure out what she’s hiding.”

I agreed with her on that point. Assassinating a noble was a serious crime, and it would be close to impossible to stop the information from leaking when there were over ninety witnesses. Even if they succeeded in hurting us, the Golden Ghost would just be collaring himself with a ticking bomb just waiting to explode.
“What a wicked man.”
“We don’t have any evidence. Even if we file a case against him, the Golden Ghost won’t be punished.”
“Then what do we do with her? She seems like she has her own burdens to bear, but we can’t exactly let her go out of pity... The labyrinth isn’t so kind a place.”

That was true enough. I didn’t intend on just letting her walk away for free, anyway. Blackmailed or not, there was a very real possibility she could be here to harm us. That alone gave us all the moral right we needed to kill her if we wished.
“I’ll be borrowing this for a second.”
I took Amelia’s dagger and pierced the woman’s heart in a single stab, taking her life while she couldn’t see or hear anything.
“We can undo the sound isolation magic.”
It was the only mercy I could show her in the labyrinth.
“So...” Missha began eventually. “What do we do now?”
I was silent, my mind still swirling with thoughts.
“It’s obvious, isn’t it? We should go and confront him about it!” Erwen suggested. “Secretly trailing another adventurer in the labyrinth is a serious crime that can have him executed!”
“But do you think he’ll confess to it?”
“If he doesn’t, then we’ll make him confess!”
Noticing that Erwen was being more aggressive than usual, Missha gave a careful opposition.
“S-still... Wouldn’t it be better for us to do what we came to do and deal with them after we return to the city later?”
“Why?”
“There’s ninety of them. It’s too dangerous for us to handle them.”

“That is true...” the guild master said, agreeing with Missha. “There is also a rumor that is going around about the Golden Ghost. That he knows the weaknesses of each and every clan member and uses the people around him like slaves... Even if only half of that rumor is true, this encounter will be different from the clan we met on the fifth floor. They will charge us like their life is on the line.”
He was probably right. If anything, the woman was proof of it. I gave her multiple avenues to escape her situation, yet she held on until the end and refused me.
Mr. Bear was the same...
Although I had no idea what his situation was, Mr. Bear never asked me for help. If those ninety other people were just like him and we tried to fight them? There was bound to be bloodshed.
But it’s not something I can just choose to ignore until we return to the city...
While my worries grew, Amelia gave her opinion.
“I’ll stay behind and observe them.”
“Huh?” I asked, caught off guard.
“They won’t know yet that we caught this woman. They’ll just be waiting until she returns. I’ll go and watch their movements, so you go and do whatever it is you need to do.”
“It could be dangerous...”
“I’m fine. I have this.”

Amelia picked up one of the loot items that we got off the woman: No. 16, Ebony Insignia. When equipped, the user’s stealth-type skills would be boosted tremendously. It was the reason the detection spell at the entrance didn’t activate. Even Beleg couldn’t notice that we had a rat on our tail.
True... With that, Amelia wouldn’t get caught under most circumstances...
Still, I found it hard to give her the okay. Amelia noticed I was struggling and approached me.
“To be honest, it doesn’t feel bad to have you worry about me,” she said. Then, she placed her hand on mine. “Don’t worry. Nothing will happen.”
I hesitated. “Yeah.”
“Okay, then.”
Without giving me time to say anything else, Amelia let go of my hand and disappeared. I couldn’t even hear her footsteps as she left, but I could sense she was already running out of the cave.
I let out a sigh, eyes locked on the other end of the passageway that Amelia would have run out from, and I felt the eyes of several people on me.
“Why are you all looking at me like that?”
Kaislan answered for the entire group. “Are you asking because you don’t know?”
I didn’t respond.
“It’s fine. We don’t really mind it. But please only do that when you two are by yourselves. It was too much for us.”
“Too much?”
He sent me a sly look. “It’s fine. You don’t need to know yet.”
I felt a little wronged.
No, what did I even do...?
I was just showing how much I cared about my allies.

After Amelia left to spy on the Golden Tree Clan, we resumed our expedition, starting with making our way away from the unusual location where we’d ended up to catch the rat. Thankfully, the actual entrance was close by.
“This is the entrance? It doesn’t look that different.”
Once we were back out of the crossroads, we followed another short corridor to another dead end. However, something here was different.
Doesn’t look that different? There are forty-four torches in this hallway.

Just like the Crystal Cave of the first floor, the Skull Island cave changed its structure every cycle, but one thing stayed the same. The entrance to the next stage was always placed in the pathway that had forty-four torches lit up along its walls.
Still, other conditions needed to be met first if you wanted to open the entrance.
“Adnus. Go put your hand on the wall.”

With that, the guild master who had taken on the very “important” role during our expedition went up and touched the wall, and when he did, a light tremor took the ground as the wall moved to the side.
[The cursed one has discovered the Memories of the End.]
[A portion of the old story has been completed.]
The portal hiding beyond revealed itself. Unlike the dimensional headstones which fluctuated between various shades of blue, the color of this portal was as red as blood.
Vwoong!
I steadied my breathing, staring into the swirling pool of red.
So I’ve come here in the end.
Even though I had been the one to plan all this and come all the way here, my heart still squeezed, fighting against some inexplicable reaction.
Well, there is nothing else to be done.
We needed to enter it. There were three graduation essences here that my allies needed.
[You have entered the Memories of the End.]
How many will we get?
Something curious struck me then.
“Adnus, by the way, do you know what the name of the Golden Ghost is?”
“You don’t know?”
“Would I ask you if I did?”
“It’s just, you did exchange names with him. He’s Bill Ironlad.”
Right. Well, seeing how I didn’t remember him, his name wasn’t “that”. I’d asked something unnecessary.
“However, if my memory serves me right, he did change his name before.”
What?
Slowly, I asked, “What was it originally?”
“Hmm, I don’t know, but this was before he became famous. According to him, though, everything started working out for him after he changed his name.”
“R-really?”
“In any case, I’m certain that it was some common name. He said he changed it because he hated sharing it with so many people.”
My heart began to thump.
No...
“A common name...?”
Those three words made my heart race.
Not for a good reason, but a very bad one.
“That’s right,” the guild master confirmed. “Is there a problem?”
There’s no way... Right?

chapters.title: Chapter 799: Rank 1 (1)
paragraphs: Schrodinger’s Cat was a famous experiment in quantum mechanics, but I honestly didn’t know much about it. As a liberal arts major, I only knew that before opening the box, there were two futures, but once the box’s contents were observed, the future would be narrowed down to only one. I had no idea what was scientifically significant about that, but the experiment at least taught me one lesson:
Sometimes, not knowing what was in the box was for the best.
I barely swallowed the question that nearly burst out of my mouth.
A common name. Was it Hans?
The moment I asked that, I would receive my answer, and the future would be decided.
It would be one or the other. It probably wouldn’t come as a surprise, but I didn’t trust my luck.
I’ll leave it there.
Not knowing was in my best interest because that left me the possibility of the other future.
Ba-dump!
I chucked every thought of my racing heart right out the metaphorical window and focused on looking around instead.
[You have entered a special area.]
Although the bones that made up the floor, walls, and ceiling disappeared, we were still inside a cave with the same layout.
“Let’s get out of here first.”
We walked past the path where we killed that rat and back through the cave to go outside. As we did, entirely new scenery greeted us.
A blood-red sky, ground littered with crevices, and lava that flowed through those gaps.
Boom!
It was truly a field that befit the name of “The End.” Naturally, there was a special field effect in this area.
[Field Effect – The End is applied.]
[Status Effect – Eternal Burning is applied. You will periodically take fire damage, and the fire damage will increase as time passes.]
Continuous damage was common, so ignoring that...
[Status Effect – Terminus is applied. You will die after 24 hours.]

All characters would die twenty-four hours after entering the special field Memories of the End. There were ways to stop that from happening, of course. The status effect would be cancelled if we just took the same portal back.
But once you leave, you can’t come back.
Consequently, the general strategy for this area was to find and collect nearby items to reset the timer.
“Is that really the same island?”
“I’ve never seen something so horrible.”

The clan members couldn’t help but be awestruck as they watched the island blow up periodically like a bomb, and honestly, I was feeling the same. There was a difference between seeing it on the flat screen and seeing it in real life.
“Be careful not to stray too far from me,” I advised.
Before we officially began our expedition, I activated the Orb of Fire to counteract the Eternal Burning field effect.
[You have activated the Orb of Fire. All fire-type continuous damage within 15 yards will be reduced by 50%.]

The Orb of Fire was easily one of the top five items to use in the Memories of the End. As time passed, that item alone wouldn’t be enough, but with it, we’d practically doubled the amount of time we could spend here.
After we took care of Terminus, of course.
“All right, then let’s head off,” I commanded. “Stand in the order I listed out before. First thing we’re doing is leaving this island.”
“Huh? Leave the island?”
“You’ll know when we get there.”
With that, I led all my members and headed to the coast where we once disembarked. Even the coast also looked different from the original island.
“Either skulls or fire... What an extreme island this is.”

The entire island had become an active volcano, meaning lava flowed out from it, and the flowing lava hardened into black rock when it met the ocean. The smoke and steam that was created by their meeting made it difficult to see far ahead.
No ordinary adventurer bound by the chains of Terminus would think about going beyond that steam, but veteran players had a different way of thinking.
“Huh? We can summon the boat and leave the island? Then shouldn’t there be at least one thing hidden out there?”
This way of thinking proved correct.
I needed to try hundreds of times and sacrifice hundreds of characters to prove that, but still.
“All right, we’re setting off!”

As soon as everyone got on the boat we summoned, the vessel began to sail through the black smoke out into the ocean. We had prepared for situations like this by applying the fire-resistant paste on its underside.
Our vision was only hindered for a few minutes. After just travelling straight, the smoke soon dissipated, and we could see the exploding island behind us.
“But where are we going now?” Raven asked curiously.
“Oh, did you not hear?”
“He only told us what we’re looking for, not exactly how we’re going to look for it.”
Right, I’d only told Auyen. “We’re heading to Arta Island,” I explained.
“Arta Island?” She tilted her head before remembering something. “Oh! That island! One of the Seven Great Mysteries of the Labyrinth! The small island that only has those three weird pillars on it!”
“That’s right.”

Arta Island was pretty famous among adventurers and wizards, and for good reason. No monsters spawned there and its only notable feature was the aforementioned “three weird pillars.” Naturally, everyone expected something to be hidden there.
“Wow! Then are we going to find the secret achievement on the island? Can I write a thesis on this?”
“No.”
“But it’s one of the Seven Great Mysteries...”
“You can write it when I die. I won’t stop you then.”
Raven balked. “Why would you say it like that? Please don’t say that, even as a joke.”
For a moment, I was silent, feeling a little ashamed of myself. Maybe I shouldn’t have put it that way? I wasn’t really joking, though.

“Anyway,” I began again, pushing ahead, “as the rules of the clan state, all happenings of our expeditions are to be kept secret. If you want to write about it, you can organize your material for now and write that dissertation later when we’re all retired. Okay?”
“I got it. I swear I do... I just needed to say it. Anyway, is this island close to the other one?”
The one who answered Raven was Auyen at the helm. “Arta Island is the closest island to Catacoma, Ms. Raven.”
“Ah, really? Then how did we not see it on our way here?”
“Creating and travelling on the most efficient path is the job of the navigator.”
Just like how I was an expert in combat, Auyen excelled in his own field. There was a reason that I brought him: we needed to use boats.
Well, even if we didn’t have a navigator, we wouldn’t have much of a problem finding Arta Island, but with Terminus applied to us, every second counted.
[Auyen Rockrobe has cast Fair Winds. The riding vessel’s movement speed is increased by 50%, and all characters riding the vessel quickly regenerate soul power.]
[Auyen Rockrobe has cast Trade Route. While the helm is kept steady, the riding vessel’s movement speed is increased by 300%.]
[Auyen Rockrobe has cast Ghost Ship.]
Abilities were applied to our boat, causing its speed to greatly increase.
Even Raven was a bit surprised.
“Trade Route? Whoa, so you’re pretty good as a navigator, huh? You have some valuable essences,” she complimented.
Auyen laughed politely. “In truth, I only obtained it not long ago.”
“What? But the labyrinth was closed for so long. How?”
“I used the auction house. I’ve spent all the money that I saved up, but I should be able to do at least this much so that I don’t drag everyone down. Haha...”
Raven paused. “It must be tough on you. Having ended up in a place like this.”
“It’s fine. I am happy.”
Auyen seemed to have impressed Raven a little, as they struck up a friendly conversation. I stepped away to give them some space, and that was when Ainar walked up to me.
“Bjorn! I have a question!”
“Go on.”
“Where do you get abilities like that?”
Usually, I would’ve told her to go ask Raven, but since she was talking with Auyen, I answered her instead. “There are monsters who drive boats.”
“Eh? But I’ve never seen one like that.”
“Because they’re in areas we don’t usually go to.”

A classic example being the pirate-infested sea of the southwestern ocean, where seafaring orcs and goblins would ambush adventurers. Ghost Ships could also be seen around Ghost Island. Since neither of them were on the way to the seventh floor, we wouldn’t pass by them any time soon.
It’ll probably be difficult to feed him Airship too, right?

It occurred to me then that the graduation essence for navigators was found on the tenth floor, but I quickly let go of the thought. If I could feed it to Auyen, we would be able to use boats on all floors, not just the sixth floor, and we’d nearly halve all our travel time during expeditions. However, that was a monster that couldn’t even be found unless you got lucky. We didn’t have the specs to hunt for it yet either.
“Captain, we can now see the island!”
At Auyen’s shout, I shook myself out of my thoughts and headed to the bow of the ship to see the small island in the distance. Or rather, I saw the three pillars.
“Oh... So that’s one of the Great Mysteries of the Labyrinth!”
The island was bizarre-looking, with three pillars that felt larger than the land they stood on.
“It looks different from when I last saw it,” Kaislan noted.
Like he said, the pillars of Arta Island looked slightly different from usual. It wasn’t that big of a change.
“Were those pillars...always blue?”
“No, they’re originally black.”
The black pillars were now blue.
Well, the change in their appearance wasn’t that important.
“Anchor the ship.”
“Yes, Captain.”
After steering the boat onto the island, we got everyone off the boat.
Four hours and forty minutes...

If it took that much time to get back, that would total nine hours and twenty minutes. However, knowing the maximum time we had was twenty-four hours, I figured we should finish the expedition within ten hours if we wanted to be safe. It could take longer for us to return, and even if we wanted to reset the Terminus state after returning to the island, we’d need at least two hours to do that.
Once we’d stepped foot on the island, we went to the center of it.
“What do we do now?”
“Just wait,” I answered.
We stood in the middle of the three pillars that formed a triangle. There, on the small altar prepared at its center, blood would be...
“Parav, you do it.”
“Pardon?”
“Swords don’t work on me.”

Parav drew a line on his hand with a sword and dripped his blood onto the altar. Suddenly, light burst forth, shining from the pillars as unknown symbols—which I knew weren’t the ancient language—appeared on the sides of the pillars. Unstable mana sparked out, seemingly drawn to the pillars’ center as it began to form into a shape.
“Another portal?”
“It’s all there is in the labyrinth,” I said, unable to help my smirk.
It was just too much, honestly. Memories of the End was a hidden secret, yet there was a hidden secret within it as well.
I don’t know who made this labyrinth, but I can tell they really like secrets.
Well, I didn’t care where I was led as long as the reward was guaranteed.
“Then do we just go in now?”
“After I do this.”
I started a ten-hour timer.
Tick, tock.
We would need to exit before time ran out if we wanted to keep everyone alive.

chapters.title: Chapter 800: Rank 1 (2)
paragraphs: The moment we entered the portal, our vision flickered as a new area appeared before us once more.
“This place is...”
“What is it? It’s quiet...”
Our members tilted their heads in confusion. Instead of the waves of monsters they expected, a relatively quiet area greeted us.

I couldn’t blame them. Skull Island Catacoma was littered with bones and skeletons, yet despite the bombastic display of an entire island exploding and burning with lava, this place was the complete opposite—a little dark but still quiet with no discernable threats in sight.
The nerves that came with entering an unfamiliar space lasted only for a moment. Raven took a glance around and put her scholarly curiosity on for all to see.
“This place is interesting. It even looks like a research facility.”
For all her talk about avenging her master, people really don’t change that quickly.
That wasn’t even a bad thing. If I were being honest, I wanted her to drop the quest for revenge and just live life doing what she enjoyed.
Not that I’m doing that either.

We walked on, each step paired with a clang underfoot. The entire area was plated with metal and the walls lined with metal pipes, hatch handles, and thick mana circuits that looked like electrical pipes.
It felt like we were inside a huge submarine or perhaps a bunker.
“Oh! I kind of want to turn this—”
“No! Ms. Fenelin, don’t touch anything!”
“I-I didn’t touch them! I only thought about it!”
Ignoring Ainar being falsely accused, I continued rushing ahead. Time was still ticking, after all.
It’s about time they start talking...
Right on cue, I heard a voice.
“(Who are you? Pilgrims?)” asked a staticky voice that seemed to be coming through a speaker.
Most of my party flinched and raised their weapons, understandably on guard at the sound. After all, there were only two people here who would understand what was said.
“The ancient language?”
Raven knew some ancient language since she learned it in her many years of scholarly pursuit, and...
“(Greetings, Arta.)”
Although I had never learned the ancient language, I could speak it like a native.
There was a pause, then the voice said, “(You still haven’t answered my question. Who are you? Pilgrims?)”
I didn’t try to hide my smirk.

Even during the game, Arta Island was an interesting chapter to experience, as its titular character was the sole NPC that could be found within the labyrinth. Well, calling Arta an “NPC” was a little up in the air once you learned their backstory. Still, they could be conversed with and give out quests, making them a very special entity. Not to mention, the method of progressing through their quest was unique, to say the least.
“Bjorn! Is it an enemy? Just say the word, and I’ll destroy it!”
“Stand down, Ainar. There’s no point even if you try.”
“There’s no point? I-is it a ghost?! Don’t worry! I-I can kill ghosts now!”
“Yeah? Then go and hit that door over there.”
Ainar seemed confused at my command, but she still obediently went to carry it out. However...
“Huh?”
She froze, her spear held in midair. It was as if something invisible was stopping her from taking the action.
“Wh-what?! I can’t move my body! S-save me!”
“Don’t worry. You’ll be fine as soon as you drop the aggression.”
The specific interaction was that the attack button itself was disabled in this area, but that explanation was good enough for reality.
As soon as she processed what I said, Ainar returned to normal.
“Ack! What is that?!”
It was the field effect.
This place was pretty special among the hidden secrets of the labyrinth.
[You have entered a special area.]
[Field Effect—Arta Secret Base is applied. All hostile actions are forbidden within the field.]
No fighting could be had here, meaning we needed something other than force to clear this area.
“(What are you saying to them?)” Arta eventually demanded. “(Answer my question. If you do not, you will be ejected.)”

The way to clear it was to talk. Choices popped up on screen when you talked to this guy in the game, and the quest progressed if you chose the right options. That was all assuming you fulfilled the prerequisite of being proficient in the ancient language, of course.
I needed to try over a hundred times to even receive the quest...
To put it another way, I had already done my rounds of failures countless times, so at this point, obtaining the quest was easy as pie.
“(We are not pilgrims,)” I answered.
First, saying we were pilgrims was the wrong move. That would lead to the player trying to prove many things, and it was impossible to prove all of them.
However, the problem was...
“(Then how do you know my name?)”
Right. The name.
“(That’s...)” I trailed off, trying to think of an excuse.

Man, I’d said their name because I was happy to see them, but that seemed to have been a mistake. In the game, they would only say the lines they were programmed to say, and I would only say the lines that were given to me, so I forgot to think about the freedom reality granted.
Well, whatever.
Unfortunately for Arta, I wasn’t so useless that I’d just blank out as soon as a random variable popped up in my way.
Answer decided, I said, “(We are survivors of the destroyed empire.)”
I could only say that because I knew the story. Although the sequence was a little off, when Arta asked me for my identity, saying that was the only one that led to success.
“(We came to this place to stop the End, so we of course know who you are as well,)” I concluded.
“(I see... The survivors of the destroyed empire... Well, you wouldn’t want your world to be destroyed either.)”
“(Of course not. Could you help us?)”

“(Well... There is none that I can help you with. It is admirable that you wish to save your world, but if you truly wish for it, leave this place. I am attempting countless options to try and solve it.)”
Wait, what? Why were they just telling us to leave? Was it because I didn’t start the conversation with the right prompt?
Still, this wasn’t the first time that reality differed from the game. I’d just have to freestyle it.
After making up my mind, I quickly continued, saying, “(Arta, we know of a way to stop the End.)”
By the nature of the story, this sentence was one that Arta could never ignore.
“(Hah, yeah? You do?)”
Yet for some reason, they just laughed me off.

Was this another change because we were in reality? They weren’t anywhere near this annoying in the game. After confirming who we were, they were supposed to assess our abilities, then give us a quest if they deemed us useful.
Man... I just had to make that mistake at the start.
Still, since I knew the entire story, it shouldn’t be too much of a problem.
“(We know of a way to kill the Beast,)” I supplied.
“(The Beast isn’t something that can be killed. Even I am only aiming to seal it,)” Arta said, voice mocking as trying to say, What can something like you even do?
“(I don’t intend on trying to convince you. I will go and kill that snake.)”
“(You even know that?)”
“(Is it important that I do? What should be important to you is whether or not we can solve your problem.)”
“(You are not wrong, but—)”
“(Don’t worry, I also know that the snake is a rank 1 monster and that we need to activate a mechanism below it after defeating it too.)”
Arta no longer asked me how I knew as much as I did. Instead, their attitude toward me changed as they shifted into a much more serious tone when they realized I knew all these deep secrets.
“(Alright... I will trust you this once, survivors of a destroyed empire.)”
There was a hiss of gas escaping as a hidden hatch door opened on the floor.
Well, I somehow ended up skipping the storyline a little bit, but just getting to our destination was all that mattered, right?
We climbed down the ladder for what seemed like forever, as if the ladder itself was connected to purgatory.
“What did you two talk about? I heard something about the empire or some difficulty?”
“It was nothing much.”
“No, but seriously. How did you even know about this island in the first place?”
I just smiled to answer Raven’s question. She knew that I was a player. The members that didn’t know weren’t asking me those questions, anyway.
“He’s a viscount,” Kaislan said confidently. “It’s natural that he knows information that regular adventurers don’t! Isn’t that right, Mr. Parav?”
“Haha, yes... That’s right.”
“But this means that the palace knows about the secret of Arta Island as well...”

After listening into the discussion of the members who didn’t know that I was a player, I gave an awkward laugh. “Don’t think too hard about it. It’s not something you should be going around talking about.”
“I know that better than anyone, so don’t worry. I’m just curious why the palace left Arta Island as one of the Mysteries.”
Maybe it was because he himself was from the palace, but Kaislan tended to always doubt and suspect the palace of scheming.
Not that he was wrong.
“Everyone, listen up,” I called. “You should remember what I told you about the monster back in the city.”
“Oh... This is the place? The place where the Snake of the End, Sniktura, appears?”
“That’s right.”
“I’m getting a bit nervous... That Kashan was already quite the monster.”
Kaislan’s voice trembled as he remembered the Kashan that we hunted on the first basement floor. It was understandable. Even with those hundreds of elite soldiers, we suffered many casualties.

Because so few adventurers had ever seen a rank 1 monster, not many people knew just how much of a threat they posed, but all who experienced them never forgot those encounters. Rank 1 monsters were like natural disasters—not mortal, not monster, but an entirely different state of being.

“Don’t worry too much,” I reassured him. “Like I told you back at the city, we’ll be hunting the monster this time under very different circumstances than when we fought Kashan. Considering all the different conditions, the difficulty will only be around a high rank 2.”
“Um... Isn’t rank 2 a pretty strong monster as well?”

True enough. Honestly, it wasn’t rare to hear that a well-off and famous clan got wiped out by one rank 2 monster. However, the story changed when looked at from the perspective of an ambitious K-Gamer.
Fighting a rank 1 monster at a rank 2 difficulty? It was practically a jackpot.
Then, my foot finally found the bottom of the ladder.
[You have entered a special area.]
[Field Effect—Destroyed Core Testing Site is applied. The Origin of Earth swallows up all authorities. All resources you possess are set to 0.]
All my MP was drained and I couldn’t use any skills anymore.
“So... We’re fighting a rank one monster in this state?” Raven grumbled, having just become even less than a civilian with all of her mana drained.
I just shrugged. “Don’t worry. This applies to our enemy as well.”
The concept of this fight was a pure, ability-less brawl.

chapters.title: Chapter 801: Rank 1 (3)
paragraphs: The story of the Arta Secret Base was quite simple.

In short, House Arta created a secret base as close as they could to the Core of the Earth in a location near the island to seal the Beast, using something called the Divine Instrument to siphon the Core’s power to do so. The house’s duty had been passed down from generation to generation to the present day.
But then one day, the secret base was damaged.
“(Monsters entered the testing site where the Divine Instrument is being held! This was clearly perpetrated by someone who wishes for the world to end!)”

Making the right choices in the conversation would lead to that dialogue, and the player would be given their first quest. The objective was to eliminate the monsters that destroyed the testing site and re-arm the Divine Instrument.
As the player progressed through the quest, new dialogue would appear:
“(I’m afraid the lift was damaged in the chaos. You’ll need to use the emergency ladders and travel downward for a few hours to get there. I’ll open the entrance right away!)”
“(Be careful! While the Core is unstable, all authorities will disappear as soon as you enter! The catch is that this also applies to the Snake of the End!)”

However, when I met the NPC for real, they turned out to be a bit of a prick. Maybe it was because I didn’t progress through the standard method. Whatever the reason, as soon as we entered the research station, they used dialogue trees that didn’t exist in the game.
“(...What is your name?)”
After we’d been traveling down the ladder for around two hours, Arta finally spoke back to me through the speakers that were installed in the testing site.
“(Bjorn Yandel.)”
“(Is that a famous name in the empire?)”
“(Well, somewhat.)”
It was Rafdonia and not the empire, but I was famous. I wasn’t lying.
I think this is the first time I’ve ever been asked my name during this part of the chapter...
Well, it was probably another effect of us being in reality and not in the game.
Arta didn’t say much after I gave them my name, so I just focused on commanding my clan members as we slowly descended into the testing site.
Beep! Beep! Beep!
The ominous beeping of the siren continued to wail through the testing site, the echo magnified by the site’s domed shape and wide, empty interior.
“Where’s Sniktura?” someone murmured nervously. Everyone had their guards up as we entered, but seeing no sign of our target only put them even more on edge.
Fair enough, honestly. Physical brawl or not, a rank 1 was still a rank 1.
“Raven, Marrone, and Auyen. Go and wait there,” I ordered, pushing the three members who would be of no use in this fight into a corner.

Once they were safely situated, I walked up to the center of the testing site to find a sinkhole with no discernible bottom. As I approached it, harsh winds swooped in from behind me. It was the Core draining our mana and soul power down into the hole.
“Are you ready?”
At my question, rather than answer me, the members just nodded and took their stances.
Alright, then since it seemed everyone was ready...
“(Survivor of the destroyed empire, what you see before you is—)”
“(I know),” I interrupted casually, “(I just need to press this, right?)”
I pressed a button on one of the suspicious-looking machines around the testing site. When I did, the winds that were blowing within the room immediately stopped.
[(Command word input complete. Emergency restoration activated.)]
The blaring sirens stopped with the announcements in the ancient language—for a brief moment until they started up once more at an even more rapid pace.
Beep! Beep! Beep!
[(Restoration failed.)]
[(Unidentified materials discovered within the testing site.)]
[(Forced expulsion initiated.)]
A whirlwind was pushed out of the hole.
[(Forced expulsion complete.)]
Like a parasite that had been hiding in its hole, a snake was forced out into the open.
“Prepare for battle!” I shouted.
It was the rank 1 monster, Sniktura.
The Snake of the End, Sniktura, was one of the dozens of species of monsters that appeared on the tenth floor.

Admittedly, even when I was playing the game, I nearly always avoided the thing if I happened to encounter it on the tenth floor. The difficulty on the tenth floor was already pure hell, so while getting into some battles was inevitable, my usual clear strategy was to head to the Gate of the Abyss while avoiding as many fights as possible.
It’s cute seeing it here like this.
We weren’t on the no-limits tenth floor that it was used to, but a small colosseum where all active skills were sealed. In here, Sniktura was a small and cute snake.
Well, it was well over three meters tall when it raised its head, but still.

As soon as it popped out of the hole, Sniktura stopped in its slithering tracks, apparently surprised to see us. Given how its three-pronged tail repeatedly slammed the ground, it seemed to not like the situation it found itself in.
“It’s a little smaller than what I heard...” Raven marveled.

Sure it was. On the tenth floor, Sniktura was a tricky enemy who couldn’t just change its size, but change its shape into something completely different as well. However, here, it couldn’t use its active skill Shapeshift.
If only Shapeshift worked with Union, it would’ve been an upgrade skill to Giantization...
Thinking back, that was probably another reason I hadn’t hunted this snake that much. Even though it was a rank 1 monster, it didn’t have any abilities that worked with the shield barbarian build.
[(Unidentified material successfully expelled.)]
[(Destroying the exit—)]
[(Failed. Failed. Failed. Failed. Failed—)]
Argh, so noisy.
“What is it repeating?”
Oh, that? “It’s just telling us to fight it,” I said, right as Sniktura charged at us.
“Hissssss!”
With fangs as big as longswords, it looked far too threatening and powerful for us to be fighting it with our active skills sealed.
But active skills aren’t everything in a fight.
[Defense successful. Wall of Aegis absorbed all damage.]
Fangs that small were easily countered by Wall of Aegis, the cheat item that could block anything of the right size.
“Hiss!”
Sniktura reared back, seemingly shocked that I blocked its attack without an issue. Then, it spat out a glob of mucus at us.
Yep, I needed to dodge that one.
Sizzle!
A moment after I dodged it, the spit began to melt through the spot where it landed.

It was the effect of one of Sniktura’s passive skills, Ten-Thousand Poison Body. To put it simply, it granted it immunity to all poisons, applied the highest possible effect of Poison to all bodily liquids, and increased all poison damage the monster dealt. It was also the graduation essence of the Acid Fluid build that I previously used.
After I dodged its spit attack, Sniktura swung its heavy tail toward me.
Whoops, I don’t think I can guard against this one too. Maybe in Giantization mode, but I’m too small to get a perfect guard in against that tail.

It was already too late to dodge. Still, I raised my shield to my torso so that it would absorb as much of the shock as possible. It did nothing to alter my fate of being flung into the nearby wall, though.
Boom!

Unable to resist, I was slammed into the wall, my shield still gripped in hand. There was nothing I could do about it. The base stats of a rank 1 monster were practically a cheat themselves. No matter what combination I mustered, there was no way to beat a rank 1 monster by leveraging a pure stats difference in Dungeon and Stone.
Is it different in 100X mode? Hmm, maybe if I got around thirty or so essences...
I shook myself out of that pointless train of thought.
“Behel—LAAAAAAA!”
To redirect my attention back to the battle, I let out my battlecry and stepped up back with the vanguard. Ainar, Parav, and Kaislan were holding the frontline with me.
“What... Gah, what is this monster?!”
“Ugh! Bjoooorn! I don’t know what to do without my abilities!”

Everyone was holding on for dear life, overpowered by the monster’s base stats, but I wasn’t too worried. It wasn’t like this was their first time fighting a monster. They would get used to battling the snake soon enough. Plus, Sniktura’s active skills were sealed, which meant that its attack patterns were forced to be simple.
Fwip!
While the frontlines battled with everything they had, our backline tried to apply some supporting fire, but it was near impossible to deal any damage to it.
“Yandel! Is it even possible to kill this thing?” Kaislan shouted, his doubt growing as the battle stretched on. Even with arrows fired and swords swung, we had yet to make even a single dent.

To be honest, he wasn’t completely wrong in his assumption. The stats on this rank 1 monster were no joke. With our active skills sealed, there was no way we could deal any damage to it by just using our passives.
Should be right around now...
Just then, a voice spoke.
“(...I’ll initiate the restoration.)”
It wasn’t the computerized announcements we had been hearing, but Arta’s voice that traveled out of the speakers.
“(To initiate a manual restoration, I need the assistance of those within the testing site. I will tell you how to use the lights to—)”
“(So I just need to press the buttons that light up?)”
Arta was quiet for a moment. “(That’s right.)”
With that conversation over and done with, I informed our members in the back to press the buttons on the machines whenever they lit up.
[(Emergency Stabilization Module activated.)]
[(An error has occurred.)]
[(Mana Core must be repaired.)]
As we pressed the buttons, the announcements telling us our progress continued to periodically sound out, and as time passed, more and more buttons were pressed to fix the compounding problems.
“Kaislan,” I called out sometime later, “go to the back and heal up with potions.”
“I’m still fine—”
“That’s an order,” I said firmly, eyeing the bones through his melted skin.
“Understood...”
After fighting for over two hours, we had members rotate out to recover before returning to battle and repeated the process several times.
[(Emergency Stabilization has been completed.)]
With the whirring of something powering up, the dark interior of the testing site suddenly shone bright, signaling that the long and arduous first phase was finally over.
[Field Effect—Destroyed Core Testing Site has been altered.]
[Depending on the distance, your set resource amount will change.]
It was also our cue that the raid had officially begun.

Our backline could now start regenerating their MP. Not by too much—around ten percent maximum. However, the most important part of this phase was still the frontline. After all, we weren’t the only ones who would be able to regain MP the farther we got from that hole. If that snake bastard managed to crawl all the way out, it would be able to use its skills as well.
“Listen closely, we must never lose ground from this point on!” I shouted to our frontline once more. “Parav! Go to the backline!”
Our sole healer, Sven Parav, was stationed at the back and began his work as a priest.
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Elementalization.]
I also got Erwen to cast Elementalization rather than deal damage. Since our enemy’s element was poison, we naturally chose the earth element.
[All damage from the fire element is reduced by half. All damage from the water element is doubled.]
[Poison Immunity granted.]
[When using blunt weapons, a strong bonus is applied to environmental destruction.]
[Physical resistances stats are greatly increased...]
Now that the poison problem was dealt with, I could fight more actively in the battle. The added knockback effect meant it was a lot safer too.
We just need to slowly whittle away at its health and deal with its berserk state at the end, I thought to myself, intending to slowly continue with the raid without hurry.
But then...
“Huh?”
Sniktura’s body suddenly began to turn red.
[Sniktura has cast Seed of Destruction.]
It could only mean one thing.
[A random character within range will be dealt unavoidable damage.]
An accident occurred.
[—’s health has reached 0%. Beginning countdown.]

chapters.title: Chapter 802: Rank 1 (4)
paragraphs: An accident occurring during a raid wasn’t anything unusual. No matter how long I played the game and how much I knew about it... No, maybe because of how much I had played this game, I knew even better than most about those fateful moments.

Accidents were, by nature, unavoidable. That was just how the game Dungeon and Stone was created. They happened during the battle, and they always came with an allied character death event. However, cycling in new allies and moving forward toward the Gate of the Abyss without letting those losses hold you back was how the game was supposed to be played.
Like now.
[Sniktura has cast Seed of Destruction.]

Seed of Destruction was Sniktura’s basic ability, where it dealt unavoidable damage to a random enemy nearby. However, no matter how “basic” it was, the basic attack of a rank 1 monster was naturally on another level entirely, even more so if the target wasn’t the tank.
“Huh?”
I first heard a short exclamation of confusion from behind me—
Boom!
—before an explosion took place one instant later.
Who is it?
I didn’t know, but I didn’t turn around. I needed to stop any more accidents from happening, so I raised my shield and charged Sniktura.
It managed to sneak out a little, I noted while still pushing the monster so that it was moved back into the center. Only after taking those emergency measures did I hear who got hurt.
“Captain, Mr. Tersia was hit!” Marrone yelled, her voice high with worry.
My heart lurched for a moment.
Tersia? But she said “Mister”...
Marrone might call Erwen Miss Tersia but never “Mister.” Most importantly, Elementalization hadn’t ended yet, and that meant the accident had fallen upon...
Beleg Shucia di Tersia.
Erwen’s uncle, and one of our newest members. The man who joined the clan to obtain the Stone of Revival.
“I fed him a potion, but he’s badly injured!”
