“Then what ability does this essence have?” she asked, unable to hold back. “And how do they interact with the ones I already have?”
“Oh, you can ask Raven about that.”
Raven flinched. “Eh? Me?”
“I’m sure that you’ve already compiled all the information required.”
“Uh, I mean, that is true... Ugh! Fine! Here!”
Amelia took the skill document from Raven, then asked me for a few pieces of advice after internalizing the information.
“But what’s this? The name sounds pretty cool. Oho, Final Day, is it?”

I had no clue what was so cool about it, but I could at least tell her, “Oh, you don’t have to worry about that for now. With all the conditions it needs to activate it, you might not even use it your lifetime.”
“Really? Well, looking at the conditions here, it’ll be difficult to use it if you don’t prepare for it.”
“Yeah, so—”
“Final Day.”
Really, that curiosity of hers. She was never satisfied until she tested these things at least once. But even if she cast it, there was no way it would go through.
Flash!
Or at least, it shouldn’t have.
“Huh?”
What?
Booooooom!
“Bjorn! Over there! Look at the sky!”
Why were there meteorites falling from the sky?
BAAAAAAANG!
Although I had no idea, I became sure of one thing when I looked at Amelia’s obviously startled expression.
“...Did I make a mistake?” she asked sheepishly.
Things had gotten out of hand.
[Amelia Rainwales has cast Final Day. For the next 24 hours, random attacks will fall within an area of 6 miles.]

chapters.title: Chapter 809: Hidden Story (1)
paragraphs: Final Day was one of the active skills of the rank 1 monster Sniktura, and its effects were pretty diverse.
Boom!
Meteors fell from the sky.
Flash!
Lightning bolts that did the same damage as rank 3 attack magic struck the ground.
Rumble!
The ground also sometimes shook and caved in to inhibit your movement for a bit.
True to its name, the ability came with some terrifying effects—and all for an entire twenty-four hours within six miles of the caster.
After hearing the explanation, Ainar looked genuinely excited. “Hmm? Isn’t that a good thing? We can kill monsters without having to do a single thing!”
I didn’t bother trying to explain it to her. For barbarians, learning with their body was the best method.
Flash!
When the lightning bolt struck her, Ainar couldn’t even let out a squeal as she shivered in place.
Bang!

This was the biggest problem with Final Day. Although the meteors, lightning bolts, and other effects befitting the end times were certainly destructive, they didn’t distinguish between allies and enemies.
“Fenelin! A-are you alright?”
“U-ugh... I-I’m fine... I-I just can’t m-move my mouth—!”
Flash!
“Ainar got hit by another lightning bolt...! A-are you alright?”
“G-gugh... Uh... E-Emily...! S-stop this already! I-it hurts a lot...!”
Ainar somehow got unlucky and got hit twice by lightning already, leading her to quickly call for Amelia. However, the latter only had a shocked expression for her.
That would be because of the second problem with this skill. It was impossible to cancel it even as it struck indiscriminately between allies and enemies.
“Emily! You might not have heard me, but—”
“Stop, Ainar,” I admonished. “This isn’t something she can stop while it’s going on. It will be maintained for twenty-four hours no matter what she does.”
“What? Don’t lie to me! I’m not an idiot! What kind of ability doesn’t let you turn it off?!”

“Uh...” I trailed off, not knowing what to say. I wasn’t expecting her to shout that out like it was the most obvious thing in the world. However, judging by the others’ reactions, I wasn’t alone in my surprise.
“Raven? Aren’t most activated abilities not able to be canceled while they’re active...?”
“Oh, y-yes... I-I suppose? Even the Indomitable Soul skill that Ms. Ainar possesses continues on for its set duration after being activated.”
Once she heard it straight from Raven’s mouth, Ainar couldn’t come up with a retort.
Amelia, the cause of all this discussion in the first place, carefully took a look around at us. “Well... It’s still interesting. It maintains itself for twenty-four hours.”
“Not interesting. Terrifying.”
“But this is a big problem. If this is how Fenelin reacts to it, most normal people could die in one hit.”
“And the fact that this will continue for twenty-four hours, this is a problem...”
Amelia cleared her throat, knowing that she was the cause of the accident. Then, with a gentle voice and direct gaze, she spoke to me. “So... S-strictly speaking, it’s not all my fault.”
For a moment, I thought I might’ve heard her wrong. “Huh?” I was wondering what she was going to say, and she was pushing the blame onto someone else? Amelia was?
When I just stared at her, utterly baffled, she turned away from me and said, “I-I mean... Yandel, this shouldn’t have worked if the conditions you talked about were right...”
Oh. “Well, that’s true...”
“That’s right, Mr. Yandel!” Raven said, barreling straight ahead with curiosity. “Why was it cast successfully?”
The attention of the rest also fell on me.
“Hmm,” I hummed thoughtfully. “Who knows...?”
The problem was, I also had no idea why it was able to cast. In the game, there was exactly one condition that needed to be met for Final Day to be activated.
“What do you mean, who knows? Didn’t you say that this is only able to be activated on the day the labyrinth closes?”

Raven was right. The skill could only be used on the day the labyrinth closed—the seventh day for the first floor, the tenth day for the second floor, and so on. We may have been in a hidden field, but we were still on the sixth floor, so it should only be usable on the sixtieth day.
“Then how come it activated now?”
Good question.
Ignoring the fact that we were in trouble, wasn’t this a little weird? How could an ability that could only be used on the day the labyrinth closed be used now?
Boooooom!
Were there other hidden things about it that I wasn’t aware of?
To be honest, I’d been getting too lucky recently. We almost got wiped out by Sniktura, but then we were able to get out of that battle without anyone dying, and it even dropped an essence.
We were lucky. Far too lucky.
And because of that...
I feel even more uneasy.
From personal experience, good events were always followed by bad events, or vice versa.
I have a lot to think about... The Lord of the sixth floor being summoned, the activation of Final Day, and the decisions I should make. But as for right now... We’re not doing too bad.

That was my conclusion, anyway. If we ignored the happenings on the outside and just focused on clearing the hidden field, Memories of the End, the activation of Final Day was good for us. It would at least help us defeat the beast, which was the boss of this island.
[Over 10% of monsters within the region have been eliminated. The authority of the Ancient Beast is weakened.]
[Over 20% of monsters within the region have been eliminated. The authority of the Ancient Beast is weakened.]

Even though we were just walking around the outer regions of the island with Amelia, the monsters within the island were being defeated at a quick pace. It was like we were nuking everything around us.
[You have defeated a Fanatic Gatekeeper. +EXP 7]
[You have defeated a Frightening Memory. +EXP 6]
[You have defeated a Fascinating Flower. +EXP 6]
[You have defeated a Winter Hound...]
Judging by the feeling of experience welling up every once in a while, the monsters over rank 4 were also being crushed by these meteors and lightning bolts.
It might be possible to clear out the entire area in just one day.
Considering that I planned for this part of the expedition to take us a week, this was a much more accelerated pace.
Not that it didn’t bring a new variety of problems, though. Just like everything else in this world, haste made waste.
“Raaaah! This is the tenth time I got hit by lightning already!”
“Kyaaaa! Mr. Parav! Mr. Parav got hit by a meteor!”
Party members were fainting after getting hit by lightning and going into critical condition after getting hit by meteors. The biggest problem, however, was something else.
“Um... We have five people left now, right?”
“Since Ms. Raines doesn’t need it immediately, it’s four in reality.”
“Ah... I see.”

Memories of the End was a field that we needed to clear while continuously resetting Terminus. However, Final Day ended up getting in the way of that reset. After all, we needed to actually see the monster to be able to apply distortion magic on it. We tried to run around with our wizards to cast it on the monsters we saw, but due to the sheer number decrease in monsters we were encountering, our harvest was less than expected. This made everyone worry, especially the members who hadn’t been able to reset their timers yet.
“W-will we be okay? W-we only have two more hours left...”
“Haha, it’ll be fine, Ms. Marrone! Don’t worry so much!”
“Not worry... Mr. Parav, you can only say that with a smile because you’ve already reset your time!”
“I-I wasn’t smiling!”
There was a pause. “I’m sorry. I was too sensitive about it. It’s not even your fault, either.”
“I-it’s fine! I understand that you’re in a situation that could elicit a reaction like that, so you don’t have to apologize...”
Of course, in the worst-case scenario, I was planning on getting the members who weren’t able to reset through the portal onto Skull Island. That would at least cleanse their Terminus.
The problem is that the floor outside isn’t completely safe since the Lord of the Floor has been summoned...
Still, it was a hundred times better than being in a situation where you were 100 percent guaranteed to die.
[Time until death: 01:50:17]
With less than two hours left until Terminus activated, we moved with all our might and focused on applying distortion magic on the monsters.
[Lilith Marrone has consumed Original Sin.]
[Beleg Shucia di Tersia has consumed Original Sin.]
We were able to reset two people and succeeded in obtaining a third one as well. After that, we just needed one more...
“Oh!”
However, for some reason, the guild master Ilya Adnus’s expression brightened as soon as one dropped. Although I didn’t say much about it, I had a problem with what he mumbled afterward.
“Ahem! So it’s finally my turn...”
It was something I couldn’t ignore as the captain. “Your turn? There is one more person who hasn’t eaten Original Sin yet.”

“Oh, you mean him?” Adnus then glanced toward Auyen, who was standing next to Amelia. However, he didn’t look too worried. “Haha, please don’t joke around. I mean, you aren’t feeding this to people randomly, are you? From what I can tell, you first feed the vanguard, before feeding the backline. And then the ones who would be helpful to the expedition.”
Wow, he noticed that...?
Maybe I should have expected as much from someone in politics, but he was pretty quick with it. But how could someone so intelligent not notice this?
“Auyen is next.”
You’re the last in order, you punk.
Needless to say, the pecking order caused some amount of conflict in the group. Guild Master Adnus looked over at me with a look of dissatisfaction.
“What are you looking at?”
He hesitated. “I’m not looking at anything...”
I literally saw you.
“Are you saying you are more helpful to this expedition than Auyen?” I pressed.

Adnus jumped to respond, as if he had been waiting for permission. “Ahem... It has been a while since I retired, and I do understand we each have our talents... But I am not so unskilled as to lose to any random person...”
From what I could tell, he was a little miffed that his importance was being pushed down by a mere navigator in his eyes.
“Um... I’m okay. I can eat the last one...” Auyen volunteered.
I glanced his way. “What are you okay with here?”
“Well... Mr. Adnus is much more incredible than I am...”

Admittedly, I got a little pissed when I heard that. I couldn’t tell if he was saying that because he didn’t want to cause any strife or because he was genuinely that humble, but I wasn’t just going to sit back and let a member of my clan do that to himself. Who cared if Adnus was the guild master, honestly?
“Auyen, you are a member of our Anabada Clan, and he is not. Got anything else to say about that? If not, eat. I will give Adnus the next one we get.”
There was an order to everything.
“That ends the discussion there. We don’t have time, so no questions.”
Adnus didn’t say anything else. He knew as well that here, my word was law.
[Auyen Rockrobe has consumed Original Sin. Fire Resistance is permanently increased by +1.]
After resetting Auyen’s timer, I was able to continue with a bit of weight lifted off my chest. The same couldn’t be said for Adnus.
“H-haven’t we gotten too relaxed about this?”
“You’re imagining it.”
“N-no, I can tell that we are moving a little slower than before... And we are getting further away from the portal... Didn’t you say that we need to take that portal in the worst-case scenario?”
“Everyone is tired. Don’t whine so much when everyone’s exhausted.”
“I-I apologize. It wasn’t my intention to irritate you.”
You should’ve said that from the start.
I needed to correct his attitude every once in a while.
“Then we’ll increase our pace.”
After that, we continued to move as quickly as before to resume our hunt, and in the end, we were able to reset Adnus’s timer as well.
[Ilya Adnus has consumed Original Sin. Fire Resistance is permanently increased by +1.]
Some more time passed.
“Above!”
I raised my head at someone’s shouting, only to see a black portal being formed. It wasn’t that surprising to see.
“Again.”

In truth, that was one of the effects of Final Day as well. On top of meteor strikes and lightning bolts, the skill also sometimes summoned portals like this that dropped a random monster on the ground.
“I wonder what it’s going to be this time.”
“Don’t lower your guard too much! If what Mr. Yandel told us is right, it can summon up to rank 2 monsters!”
As soon as we discovered the portal, everyone got into their battle formation.
“It’s small?”
“Is it a miniature-type?”
“It doesn’t look that powerful.”
The monster slowly revealed its form from the portal.
“Huh?”
And that monster screamed as it fell to the ground.
“(Uwaaaaaaah...!)”
Thud!

Having fallen onto its butt, the monster rubbed its butt with both its hands before saying, “(O-ouch... But I succeeded! I was able to actually come here! Wahoo! My research in the mana-quantum-dynamical extraction-conversion-dynamical alignment was correct!)”
Wait, was this even a monster?
I had no idea, but the maybe-monster shouted in excitement before turning around—and then immediately startling itself when it noticed our presence.
“(Hieeeeek! Wh-who are you...?)”
That was what I wanted to ask. It was talking in the ancient language as well.
“(What are you?)” I asked back.
“(Me? I-I am called Arta...?)”
We found yet another hidden secret that I didn’t know about.

chapters.title: Chapter 810: Hidden Story (2)
paragraphs: There’s no way this is a coincidence.

Machine Monster Arta was the final boss of Arta Secret Base. My gamer instincts, honed through nearly a decade of playing Dungeon and Stone, were telling me that these two beings didn’t share a name by sheer happenstance.
Is using Final Day on this island the condition needed to meet this guy?
I’d had no way of knowing up to here, which just meant I needed to learn the answer now.
“Raven, use barrier magic,” I ordered.
“So suddenly?” she questioned in protest. “But you told me not to use it all this time around because of how much mana it costs to cast.”
“We’ll need to bear with it if we want to try talking to this thing here and now.”
“Understood.” Raven immediately created a dome-shaped barrier around us that sort of looked like an umbrella.
Boom! Flash! Rumble!
The translucent barrier successfully blocked the meteors and lightning strikes falling from the sky.
Alright, now that we have a quiet environment to talk in...

“(Oh, interesting. A language similar to the common tongue but different in its construction...)” The man looked at all of us up and down. “(Still, I suppose the language hasn’t completely been lost since someone is speaking it here? Well, the language itself doesn’t particularly matter.)”
Then suddenly, something changed about the words coming out of his mouth.
“Establish intent communication,” he mumbled. “Alright, can you hear me now?”
Marrone flinched in surprise. I turned to her and asked, “Huh? Can you understand him, Marrone?”
“Pardon? Yes... I don’t know how, but I can understand what that man is saying. Even though my brain knows that he’s speaking in a different language...”
Noticing Marrone’s reaction, the man-monster-thing carefully asked, “Um, excuse me... Is this perhaps your first time experiencing intent communication?”
“Pardon? Ah, yes... I’ve never heard of anything like this.”

He sighed. “I suspected as much when I saw your attire, but it seems a lot of technology has been lost. Do not be alarmed. I have only connected the waves emitted by our brains so that we can ‘understand’ each other. Though I d-do suppose it’s natural to find it unfamiliar at first.”
The man who identified himself as Arta then paused, looking at the meteor and lightning beyond the barrier that Raven had created.

“This truly is the final day of the world... It is exactly as I imagined it to be!” he marveled with sparkling eyes. He giggled to himself then. “With these research results, I won’t need to worry about next year’s budget!”

Many things about him remained very suspicious, least of which was the fact that he had come out of that mysterious portal, and yet I didn’t feel threatened by him. The way he looked, the way he spoke, and the way he dressed... Even though it all made him look slightly creepy, it also made him seem harmless.
“Hey, Arta was it?” I called.
He seemed to shake himself back to awareness. “Pardon? Ah, yes. I was distracted for a moment. But who are you lot? If possible, I would appreciate it if you would explain the current situation to—”
“We’ll be the ones to ask you questions.”
“Ah! Of course! You must have many questions as well. I will answer all your questions. However, could I make a request as well? Oh! It’s nothing major, so you don’t need to worry!”
I took a breath. “Talk.”
“If I answer all your questions, could you answer my questions as well? In truth, I have many questions regarding our current situation... Hahaha...”
What was with this guy? Was he hiding his true strength?
I was a little surprised by how daring he seemed to be, considering how weak he looked, but since obtaining information about him was the foremost priority, I nodded. “Understood, I promise.”
“Alright, then go on. What is it you want to ask?”
“Who are you?”

“As I said before, my name is Arta. Currently... No, I suppose I should say previously? Regardless, I am the top researcher at the First Magic Engineering Research Center. Haha, I’m not trying to brag, but only the vice-director and director of the research center are above me.”
“Research center...?” I echoed with a furrowed brow. Something about that term seemed familiar.
“Oh,” he began curiously, “do you perhaps know about our institute?”
Well, not particularly, but I did have a hunch. “Do you mean the research center that uses monsters as research material to create living weapons?”

“Pardon? We don’t do anything like that. Our research center truly focuses only on the development and progress of magic engineering. Although our research data is used to create weapons, we aren’t a research station made to make weapons.”
Hmm, I see...
Fair enough. The place I explored on the first basement floor was named the Panthelion Research Station, after all, not this “magic engineering” whatever.
I decided to move on to my next question. “So, what’s someone of your status doing here?”
“Well, what else is a research member of a research station to do except do research?”
“Don’t joke around. We don’t have time.”

“Ah, yes. I suppose from your perspective, you are running quite low on time. Considering that you are no expert on this, I will try to explain this as plainly as possible. The research we have been undertaking was on the observation of the time and space of the future.”
“The observation of time and space...?”
“That’s right. Observing the future to change the present... This was the core of our research.”
“Not the past?”

“Haha! You seem to be referring to time travel, but it has been quite some time since it was proven that changing the past to change the present is impossible. That is why we decided to focus on the future.”
What? Then was his plotline that his research succeeded, and now he was here?
Isn’t this supposed to be a fantasy setting?
It was pretty random, but I understood what the story was.
“So could I ask you a question in return? In truth, I’ve been dying to ask you this... What year are we in?”
We were the future.
RPG was short for Role-Playing Game, or to put it simply, a game where you played a role.

In a grand sense, the new reality I’d found myself in hadn’t changed that. If I kept up my role while continuing on with the story, the episode would come to a natural conclusion at some point, and then I would receive a reward. And that was why...
I need to find clues to progress with this new story.

Once I’d come to that decision, I talked with Arta for a while to get information from him. The difference was, this wasn’t like the game where I could just spam the spacebar to skip all the dialogue and go straight to completing the quest.
“New World Year...? My goodness! The name of the era itself has changed?”
“The world ended once due to the witch, and now, the city nation ruled by the Rafdonian royal family is the only thing that remains... I can’t believe my ears!”
“Ah, I gave you the impression that I knew of the situation here? Haha, it is true to some degree. The coordinates that I chose were the end of the infinite time—the final day, so to speak!”
“Pardon? Why did I do that? Well, who wouldn’t? I was curious about the end of the world I live in!”

“Oh? Haha! Am I not afraid? Well, if my heart stops or I end up in a dangerous situation, I will return to my original time. I am fine, so long as I don’t die there. The greatest magic engineers are waiting for me there, and they can even pull me from the brink.”
“Huh? Why do we have magic engineers and not priests? Has this era’s magic engineering fallen so far?”
“Well then, how did the world end up in this state? From what you said before, isn’t the witch who tried to end the world dead now?”
Arta gained information about our world and I about his through our conversation. In conclusion...

“For the end of the world to truly exist... I must learn the cause of the end and the method to stop it. People of the future! Could you help me? If you do, I will prepare something to stop this disaster from happening in the past!”
There it was, the basic layout of the quest. Needless to say, the most important thing about it was the reward.
“What do you mean, what reward will I give you? Don’t you want to stop the end of the world? There is nothing in particular I can give you...”
Hmm, then was the reward distributed in another way? Something like a treasure vault that only this guy could enter?
“I was joking. The world ends if we fail, so what good is a reward? I will do anything to stop the world from ending.”
With that, I ended the talk about the reward by playing it off. “I knew you were joking! Let’s continue our conversation as we move.”
“Yes, that sounds good. I don’t have much approved time on hand either.”
“Approved time?”
“Ah, I forgot to tell you this. There is a limit to how long I can stay here, so I must gather as much information during that time.”
“What happens if you don’t return within the approved time?”
“That won’t be happening... In that case, I will need to face the end of the world with you.”
“I see.”
I brushed the idea off as a simple curiosity for now. I couldn’t just say to his face that I was thinking of forcing him to stay if a special event or reward didn’t appear while we took him around.
Maybe the real quest will start if this guy doesn’t return to his original time.
Since this was a hidden secret that I had never encountered during my time playing the game, I needed to do everything I could to explore it.
“Raven!” I called. “Cancel the spell!”
After Raven dispelled her barrier, we officially resumed wandering around the island.
“Excuse me, Mr. Arta?”
Raven, who hadn’t been able to join in on the conversation because she had been focusing on her spell, began talking with Arta as well.
“Mr. Arta?”
Or, well, she tried to.
“Do you... not want to talk to me?”
Eventually, he revealed, “Ah, it’s not that... I am quite shy...”
“But you were pretty open with Mr. Yandel.”
I focused on this exchange to see if anything useful came of it, but all I learned was that Arta was terrible at talking to women, and...
“I am interested in magic engineering as well. Could you tell me a little about that?” Raven asked politely.
“Oh! Such a beautiful person as yourself is interested in magic engineering?! Is that true!”
“Huh? Oh, uh, yes. I am...”
“Haha! Ask me whatever questions you have. I’ll answer them all!”
...and it seemed that Arta was weak to women interested in magic engineering.
Alright, now I know to get Raven to ask him about whatever I need to get out of him.

I listened in for a few minutes more, but the magic engineering concepts they were talking about were completely alien to me, so skip. However, I didn’t stop them. Adding to Raven’s knowledge was a good thing, and I just focused on clearing out the island.
[Over 50% of monsters within the region have been eliminated. The authority of the Ancient Beast is weakened.]
[Over 60% of monsters within the region have been eliminated. The authority of the Ancient Beast is weakened.]
[Over 70% of monsters within the region have...]
“Ahem... M-my apologies, but I should really be using this time to focus on gathering information rather than conversing like this.”
“D-do not worry! I will do everything within my power to save you, Ms. Raven!”
Around the time that we had cleared about 70 percent of the island of monsters, Arta apparently regained his senses, as he stopped his conversation on magic engineering and returned to his main duty.
“So... Mr. Yandel, was it? You said that the cause of the end was a beast. Why are we not heading in that direction?”
Hah, now he asked. Just how weak was he to women who fit his type?
It was honestly baffling, but I still answered him. “We need to kill the monsters of the island to weaken the beast first.”
“Ah... I see.”
“Is there anything you’ve figured out while looking around?”
“Well... Not much yet.”
Yeah, no surprise there. He had been more focused on Raven the whole time, anyway.
“Ah! But there is one thing I noticed,” he noted.
“What is it?”
“The center of the island, where that end-bringing beast resides! I can sense powerful waves of mana emanating from it.”
Mana waves... Was it going to be a secret room that I hadn’t been able to find in the game? Or was it simply just the location of the boss?
Well, whatever it was, I would find out soon enough.
[Over 90% of monsters within the region have been eliminated. The authority of the Ancient Beast is weakened.]
It was time to take on the boss.

chapters.title: Chapter 811: Hidden Story (3)
paragraphs: Memories of the End was the hidden field that could be reached through Skull Island. In the game, fighting the boss of End Island, the beast, was all you needed to do on the island. However, you could enjoy additional content if you did the work of discovering and fulfilling certain hidden conditions.

For example, if you left the island and went to the secret base, you could fight in the raid against Sniktura. You could then receive a quest there, go back to End Island and defeat the beast, and then return to Arta Secret Base to obtain additional rewards. If you refused the additional reward at that point, you could fight against the real boss, the machine monster Arta.
I can just ignore the Arta raid since I was planning on skipping it, anyway.
All I needed to do now was complete the second part of the story by defeating the beast and receiving my additional rewards.
Or that was the plan, until this guy showed up.

“Hmm. I thought it was simply a difference in mana concentration at first, but now I can see that the mana infused within the air itself is different in nature. This distribution is usually only seen at artificial sites...”

Just what was this guy? Was there a hidden chapter on the island other than the fight against the machine monster Arta? My gamer instincts were telling me it was more likely than not, so I listened more intently to what he said.

“I’ll need to search for this island’s coordinates in my original time to look deeper into it. If the original island has the same distribution, then it could be considered a trait inherent to the island itself.”
It was common in games for hidden secrets to be first discovered through the random ramblings of NPCs.
Well, in this guy’s case, I honestly have no idea what he’s talking about.

The distribution and concentration of mana... No clue what that was all about. It wasn’t like I was a wizard. However, I was sure that taking Arta around and finishing off the beast raid was the right path to take, and the reason for it was quite simple.
“The center! We need to get to the center of the island! I need to observe the phenomenon closely so that when I return, I can compare—”
It had to be right if this guy kept trying to push us there.
“Don’t whine so much,” I warned. “The beast won’t appear just because we get to the center.”
“Pardon?”
“That’s just how it—”
“Graaaaaah!”
The howling of the beast shook the entire island. The ferocious roar echoed from all around us, making identifying the source of it an impossibly pointless task.
[You have entered the area of Song of the End.]
I quickly gestured for the group to stop and shouted, “Prepare for combat!”
Although it had come much earlier than anticipated, the beast had appeared.
The boss of End Island, Beast.

The method for summoning it was pretty simple: stay in its territory for long enough, and it would just show up. I should also explain that there was no other way to summon it—or at least, an alternative route didn’t exist in the game I played.
“Formations!”
That was why even as we hustled into formation, I grew suspicious.
It appeared this quickly?

This had never happened before in-game. I always needed to move around for at least an hour or two before the boss appeared. Yet somehow, this time, the boss appeared as soon as we entered its territory.
“Oh! Is it here?” Arta wondered.
Was it true, then? Was it because of him?
Either way, that wasn’t the point at the moment.
“Yeah, so go and stand over there,” I ordered, sending Arta to the back for his safety.
“Yes, understood!”
Then I turned forward, heart hot and racing with the threat of battle.

As always, I took deep breaths to calm myself. It was a routine of mine, like those rituals athletes did before competitions. In and out, I breathed until I felt myself instinctively relax, then clenched my hand. This small moment of calm would increase my chances of winning, however slightly.
Rumble!
“It’s coming!”
The ground swelled in waves before the Beast revealed itself from between the surging ripples of magma.
Boom!
Every minute, every second, counted. That was because its aura skill, Song of the End, had a very peculiar effect.
[All time is accelerated.]

The only description available was that one line. However, just like in those superhero comics, the shorter and simpler the ability description, the more powerful and cheat-like the heroes became. The same went for Song of the End.
[Time until death: 22:50:43]
[You will periodically take fire damage, and the fire damage will increase as time passes.]

From this point onward, the time remaining for Terminus would decrease at a much faster pace, and the damage of Eternal Burning would amp up much faster as well. The damage-halving effect of Orb of Fire wouldn’t be able to help me for as long as it had before.
I had decided how long we could spend defeating this boss way back when I created the expedition plans.
Thirty minutes.
Thirty minutes was the maximum time we could afford. If we took any longer than that, we’d forfeit the raid and just run without looking back.
But if things go well, we won’t have to do that.

Although the Beast was definitely a difficult boss, it was much easier to fight than the Snake of the End, Sniktura. That was, of course, under the assumption that someone knew the strategy to defeat it in the first place.
Seeing the Beast appear right before her, Ainar sounded weirdly excited as she shouted, “Oh! Bjorn! Is it that thing?”
She had made that big speech about fighting the bones she saw on Skull Island. Apparently, that desire hadn’t waned.
I honestly thought she’d be afraid when she saw its living form.
After casting Giantization, I observed the monster from behind my shield.

It was around thirty feet tall, large enough to be categorized as “very large” by monster standards. Its build was also similar to that of Lord of Chaos, Riakis, with that bipedal form and huge tail. From a modern perspective, it looked like a dinosaur.
“Graaaaah!”
It crouched, then roared directly at us, shaking the very air around me. It wasn’t a simple roar either, but a skill.
[Ancient Beast has cast Final Warning. The physical stats of all nearby characters will gradually decrease over 5 minutes.]

When hit by the skill, one’s physical stats would decrease for a set amount of time. Although it was an area-of-effect debuff, the stat decrease wasn’t substantial, and the time limit of only five minutes meant that the skill’s value wasn’t that high.
[All time is accelerated.]
But when compounded with the effect of Song of the End, it was practically a cheat skill.
“Ugh... What is this?! Strength is leaving my body! And I’m starting to hear weird voices too!”

The skill’s maximum effect would then take not the full five minutes to apply but instead just one minute. It also didn’t have a cast cooldown, so we were going to be dealing with the effects of it for basically the whole fight.
Well, we would be dealing with it if we hadn’t prepared any countermeasures.
“Ugh... Do we have to fight like this?”
Why was she like this again? I could vividly remember giving her the expedition briefing myself.
“Raven!”
At my short command, Raven cast the spell she had prepared beforehand.
[Arua Raven has cast the rank 5 curse magic White Noise. You are temporarily deafened.]
As soon as the spell was cast, silence filled my ears, as if I had put in earplugs in a quiet room. A complete silence where I couldn’t hear the rustling of my body or even my own breathing.
The reason for casting this spell was simple.
[Final Warning has been dispelled.]
When this spell was cast, a debuff would be applied that no magic tools, consumables, holy spells, or essence abilities could dispel.
And surprisingly... I had no idea how it worked. But was that even important to a gamer like me? Gamers didn’t ask questions like that—they just needed to know if something was effective or not.
So it actually works.

I just stumbled into this tactic while playing the game and figured it was a bug. However, after coming to Rafdonia and delving into the labyrinth countless times, I realized that there were no such things as bugs in this game.
But this does feel nice.
I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t a little worried. If this didn’t actually work, we would’ve needed to give up the raid immediately and run.
I turned back to my party members. Since we had entered total silence with the spell, I communicated using signals that we had discussed before and carried on with the raid.
[Ancient Beast has cast Ruin’s Resentment. Greatly decreases damage taken temporarily, and when the set time is up, greatly increases stats relative to damage taken...]
When I raised a closed fist, everyone stopped attacking.
[Ancient Beast has cast Predation.]
When I opened my palm and waved it front and back, everyone other than me stepped away to evade.
[Beleg Shucia di Tersia has cast Soul’s Trumpet. When summons attack the same target, additional damage is dealt.]
When I raised just my index finger, only the ranged damage dealers were to attack.
[Ainar Fenelin has cast Focus Strike.]
[Erwen Fornacci di Tersia has cast Rupture.]
When I raised my index and middle fingers, both ranged and melee members were to attack.
And when I raised just my middle finger like this...
Silence!
Everyone used their strongest ability to deal as much damage as possible.
Weird, feels like something’s missing. I guess it’s because I can’t hear anything?
Anyway, the raid progressed swimmingly.
[Ancient Beast has cast Earth Shake.]
Phase 1 ended.
[Ancient Beast has cast Bone Flute of the End.]
Then we safely cleared Phase 2 after using nearly an army’s worth of resources.
[Ancient Beast has cast Homecoming.]
Phase 3 was dealt with without much problem as well.
If I were to identify the moment of greatest danger, it was when Ainar fell unconscious after being struck by lightning, and we nearly took heavy damage because of that.
It’s only taken us eighteen minutes so far. We have time.
With that, we were able to reach the final phase 4 after only eighteen minutes of fighting.
[Ancient Beast’s health is below 20%.]
[Slowly recovering its lost authority.]

Phase 4 had two notable gimmicks to take note of. One was that the monster’s so-called “authority” that we had sealed away by clearing out the monsters on the island would slowly begin to recover, and the second...
[Ancient Beast has cast Authority of Loss.]
The second was that the first authority it used would target the Cursed One without fail.
Wow, using Loss from the start?
Surprisingly, it used its strongest authority first. It didn’t have a cast time, and it was impossible to block this single target instakill ability.
A hazy cloud took form around the Beast’s body, then flew toward its target.
I hadn’t mentioned it in a bit, but the target had already been decided. The one who obtained the title of Cursed One by dealing the final blow on the Skull Island boss, one might ask?
Guild Master, Ilya Adnus.

Of course, I didn’t put in the work of planning this raid just to make the guild master into a sacrifice. I wasn’t such a wicked barbarian. Plus, this was the first authority it used and it had been cast while the boss was recovering, so the effect wouldn’t be that powerful. Its other authorities would be stronger later on.
In any case, he wouldn’t get KO’d just by getting hit by that. However, he would “lose” something he possessed.
What could it be? What would the guild master lose? His ability to heal? His equipment? Or maybe one of his essences?
I whipped around to check on the guild master—then I couldn’t help the silent exclamation that escaped me.
Ah...
Lava, meteors, and lightning strikes all flashed across my vision. Perhaps it was because all of those things were lighting up the surroundings that light reflected off of him like a mirror.
So, even that can happen...
He had lost his hair.

chapters.title: Chapter 812: Hidden Story (4)
paragraphs: The guild master lost his hair.
It hadn’t receded. It hadn’t withered into any bald spots. It was just there, and then it was gone.
He “lost” it so thoroughly that his scalp looked like it was shiny and smooth.
Well. That worked out.

I forced myself to turn away and look on the bright side. If this were a cup, some would describe it as half-full while others would call it half-empty. I had come to realize with time and experience that the former was a much more productive mindset to have. And in truth, “good” would indeed be the word to use to describe what had just happened.
It’s not the best look for him... But still, he’s pretty lucky that his hair was all he lost.
The authority could have taken his equipment or even the skills and stats of his essence, so losing his hair was a much lesser penalty. He could just grow it back.
However, since I had absolutely no desire to go bald like him, I let out a roar and charged forward.
“Behel—LAAAAAAA!”
Although neither I nor my allies could hear my scream, that beast absolutely still could. It actually roared back at me as if to respond to my battle cry.
Not that I could hear it.
Argh, it’s spitting on me...

Getting spat on always felt worse than getting blood on my skin, seriously. Still, I didn’t have time to wipe my face, so I just kept charging as the spit dripped off my skin. I blocked its gargantuan attack one more time.
Bang!
[You have used Dragon Plate of Aegis.]
Then I used the effect of the armor that I obtained not in the labyrinth, but in the outside world.
The Beast’s eyes went wide. Of course it was surprised. A Viking warrior, much larger than it had appeared out of nowhere, and that warrior even slammed his greatsword directly onto its head.
I hope you like it.
The damage dealt by the spirit warrior was reflective of the damage I had been taking for the past eighteen minutes.
[Reflecting all accumulated damage.]
I was only giving back what I got.

It didn’t take long for the Beast raid to come to an end. Once the damage from my Dragon Plate dealt critical damage to the Beast, we dumped all the damage we could onto it for the next three minutes, and that was enough to make it collapse. If I were to pick out a few notable things that happened...
[Ancient Beast has cast Authority of Change.]

The frame before we killed it, the Beast managed to use one last authority. Unlike the first skill, this one’s target was completely random, and yet, surprisingly enough, it was once again the guild master.
What the hell?
If “surprising” was the word for seeing him targeted twice, the effect of the authority was altogether “unbelievable.”
He turned into a woman...
His still-bald frame slimmed down as feminine features were applied to his body. To put it simply, he became Ms. Ilya Adnus.
I watched him gesticulate, growing increasingly curious about what he was saying. When I signaled with my hand, Raven understood my intention and undid the spell applied to the group.
“Wh-what is this?!” came his shrieking voice. “F-f-first my hair and n-n-now... Why is my chest...?!”
“That’s not the only thing that changed.” He pulled out a mirror and started panicking, but I didn’t have the time to waste on consoling him. “Calm down. You can grow your hair back.”
“That isn’t the problem!”
“Then are you discriminating against women?”
“No, this isn’t discrimination—!”
“Don’t worry. You’ll return to normal after some time.”
He finally paused. “Is that true?”
“Yeah, I swear upon my warrior’s honor.”
I thought about feigning ignorance and tormenting him a little, but he’d probably grumble and complain the entire expedition, so I just told him the truth straight up. We still had things left to do.
“Oh, I can finally hear again!”
“But is it really over?”
“It doesn’t seem to be moving...”
“More importantly, the guild master...”
“Don’t talk about it. He’ll hear you...”
The members started buzzing with questions as they eyed the collapsed Beast. A few of them were understandably worried.
“You can relax,” I reassured them. “It’s all over.”
“But then... Why is the corpse not disappearing...?”

Oh, that? I didn’t know exactly why, but the Beast was an unranked monster. Even within the game, it didn’t give experience points, and the corpse didn’t disappear whether or not distortion magic was applied to it—unless it dropped its essence, of course.
Missha bit her lips in regret when I explained it to her. “Ah... So it’s not going to give us an essence this time...”
I could sympathize with her disappointment. The essence of the Beast would have been one of Missha’s graduation essences.
I could’ve just fed her the essences if it popped out this time...

That wasn’t to say that we would be coming back to this island multiple times to reattempt the raid and acquire the essence. It would take too long, and since the Ice Double Swordmaster was a core part of my late-game strategy, there were many different builds I had in mind. Using the essence of the Beast would be the A-build, and there was a B-build using a different essence as its core.
There’s a C-build too, but the ceiling for that is a bit low, so I don’t want to go there if possible...
Given the low essence drop rates in this game, I needed to create multiple builds and cultivate the characters in fluid ways to successfully reach the Gate of the Abyss.
It’s disappointing, but we’re not at a complete loss because of it.
While not as valuable as its essence, the Beast’s corpse could still fetch a pretty price.
“What are you all doing? Get the leather off its skin!”
Its leather, for example, was as effective as drake leather, a grade 4 material.
“D-Drake leather? You mean that famously expensive...?”
“I heard that you can only use the leather on a Drake’s back. Are you saying this entire monster’s body is covered in that leather...?”
“Then how much is all this?”
Well, if we sold everything, we’d probably get enough money to buy one or two rank 3 essences. Still, it was too early to rest on our laurels.
“Be careful about the leather on its head. That one’s similar in quality to ogre leather.”
“What?! You mean it’s a grade 5 material?”
“And be careful handling its bones, like you would with its skull. If you make swords out of them, they’ll be as sturdy as adamantium.”
“This thing was more of a treasure chest than I realized.”

It was a very large monster, one that couldn’t easily be handled by a handful of people, but with how skilled we all were as adventurers, it didn’t take long to loot the entire corpse. Skull, leather, organs such as the heart for Raven’s research, and much more.
After taking everything we could, I noticed Arta just standing there, blinking.
Oh, right. Him.
He had an odd expression on his face, so I approached and struck up a conversation.
“Is there a problem?”
After a moment, he began, “It’s odd.”
“What is?”

“If this beast truly was the cause of the end...you should’ve all died here. No, even if you didn’t die, you should’ve failed. That is the reason I followed after you, to try and observe the process of the world coming to an end and to find a clue as to how to stop it.”
What the—? Then was he just standing back and watching us, expecting us to all die?
“So what are you trying to say?” I demanded.
“It’s just... It’s too weird! My research mapped out the time to pinpoint coordinates along its course. I succeeded in my experiments and then arrived at today, the final day.”
“I got it, so get to the point.”

“If you succeeded in your battle...how is today the world’s last?” Then Arta answered his own question not with more questions, but with certainty. “I apologize, but that Beast you defeated just then... isn’t the cause of the End.”
Hmm, that was pretty interesting. In the secret base over the ocean, the machine monster Arta told us that the Beast was the cause. But now, a different Arta was telling us it wasn’t.
“Then what is the cause?” I asked.
“We’ll need to figure that out from now.”
“How?”

“Those powerful waves of mana that I mentioned before... I thought that the wave was coming from the Beast that you mentioned, but that’s not the case. Now, even after the Beast is defeated, I can still feel the waves.”
“So you want to go over to where you feel the waves coming from?”
“Yes, that’s right. I don’t have much time left—”
“Got it. Let’s get going.”
I didn’t need time to think. I had already expected something to happen after we defeated the Beast, and from what I could tell, he already had a destination in mind.
“How much time do you have left?” I checked first, and it seemed we were running lower on time than expected.
“Well... For some reason, the time I had remaining decreased significantly after that ‘Beast’ appeared...”
Oh, because of Song of the End. Then should I send him further away the next time we have this raid?

While the thought did cross my mind, I wondered if I would ever really need to use this hidden secret a second time. Plus, I still wasn’t completely sure of the conditions that needed to be met to summon him, or even how Final Day was able to be cast in the first place.
“I know everyone is tired, but hold on for a little longer. We’ll now resume moving at full speed.”
After taking all the loot we could, we quickly followed after Arta.
“Here...?”
“Yes, I can feel powerful waves of mana coming from within. Let’s go in!”
Surprisingly enough, the place we arrived at was the cave with the portal.
I don’t think there’s anything hidden here...
I was genuinely curious. I had searched this cave from end to end when playing the game, and I was confident that—
“It’s here! We’re approaching it at a rapid pace,” Arta cried soon enough.

I couldn’t help but tilt my head in confusion. “Are we?” I echoed, wondering if there was some hidden space yet unknown to me. However, just as suspected, we arrived right back at where the portal was located.
“Let’s quickly go in!”
Still, since we were already here, we moved toward the portal with Arta.
Vwoong!
Soon enough, the ominous dark red portal came into view. The moment he saw it, Arta let out a confused exclamation.
“Huh? A... A portal? Why is a portal here? How? Wh-what went wrong? There’s no way...”
He seemed to fall deeper and deeper into confusion. No, confusion wasn’t the word. It was like he began to panic as he started to mumble to himself.
“W-wait...”
He skittered back like a man afraid, and I figured now was as good of a time as ever to interject.
“What’s the problem? Isn’t it just a portal?”
His expression twisted into a weirder one at my own confusion before his eyes went wide with realization.
“I’ll ask you one question,” Arta said with a deeper voice than ever before. “Am I perhaps inside the labyrinth?”
I was speechless when I heard his question.
What was this now?

chapters.title: Chapter 813: Hidden Story (5)
paragraphs: As far as the game went, Arta was an NPC—a non-player character—through and through.
Then again, he was technically more of a hidden secret than anything... An “Achievement of Gabrielius,” as they called it in this world, then?
Anyway, I was getting distracted.
“Am I perhaps inside the labyrinth?”
Genuine surprise swept through me. It didn’t matter whether Arta was a hidden piece, an achievement, or an NPC. Those who were a part of the labyrinth couldn’t free themselves from its laws.

Monsters couldn’t use portals to move to other floors, not even the ones you could converse with or NPCs. Not only could they not move between the floors, but they even believed that the world of the labyrinth was the real world.
“You are the first living things I’ve seen in a long time. Where do you all come from?”
Not the vampire of the Bloody Citadel.
“Wild dogs of the empire seized by greed. I will punish you today.”
Nor the Knight of the End that I met at the White Temple.
“This is the labyrinth. And I am an adventurer who is going through the labyrinth.”
“What is...the labyrinth?”

Even when I met that vampire again in the first basement floor, the duke whom I presumed to be the original Cambormere wasn’t much different from the first vampire. It was why I went out of my way to not mention the labyrinth when I spoke of the history of our current era.

“As I said before, my name is Arta... I am the top researcher at the First Magic Engineering Research Center. Haha, I’m not trying to brag, but only the vice-director and director of the research center are above me.”
Arta also believed that the world inside the labyrinth was their real world.
So if all of that was true, what was this?
“Inside the labyrinth?” I repeated warily. “What do you mean?”
“It’s as it sounds. Please answer me. Am I currently standing inside the labyrinth?”
He knew of the labyrinth’s existence. Well, I’d have to figure out later if the labyrinth he knew and the labyrinth I knew were the same.
I paused, drawing out the silence before asking, “What is the labyrinth?”
“Could I...take that as you knowing nothing about the labyrinth?”
Hmm, well... If I just said yes here, I got the sense the conversation would just stop. I decided to give a more open-ended, ominous answer instead.
“Well, that’ll depend on what your answer to my question is.” I would no longer reveal my cards first.
Arta stared at me for a moment before quickly continuing.

“The labyrinth is an artificial dimension created using the Power of Origin, a place where we could create the laws of the world in our own design. Anything can be newly created within the labyrinth, and you can go anywhere you wish freely. And portals are a transportation method within the labyrinth that the former empire thought up.”
His quick explanation was baffling, yet for some reason, my heart lurched with a spike of fear. “The empire created the labyrinth?”

“That’s right. His Imperial Majesty wished for an immortal life, absolute authority, and a perfect world under him, one which could be controlled by him. Like a heaven on earth... Gods are beings with too many flaws, after all.”
Confusion washed over me. I couldn’t make sense of it, even as I took in his every word. Was what he was saying real? Or was it just the description that was given to him?
However, it did make me curious about one thing. Although it may be an entirely unrelated or unimportant question...
“But why labyrinth?”
Arta hesitated. “I don’t understand the question.”
“No, but if they wanted to create paradise, why did they name it the labyrinth?”
“I don’t know why that caught your interest, but I will answer you.” He didn’t even hesitate as he continued, “The end of the labyrinth always provides an answer.”
I stared at him in open confusion, prompting him to explain further.

“It is an old saying—very old even from my time’s standard. And the emperor spent his entire life looking for an answer to save the world. Under the will of that emperor, this massive project of creating an artificial dimension to create a paradise was named the ‘labyrinth’... And the day when the blood, sweat, and knowledge we poured into it lead us to the end of the labyrinth, we will enter an eternal paradise. That was a portion of the speech the emperor gave us when he visited our research station. Did that answer your question?”
“It did,” I said gravely.
“Alright, then please answer my question.” Arta stared at me and asked once more, “Are we inside the labyrinth?”
Well, I honestly still wasn’t sure. In fact, I was even more confused than before...
Still, that didn’t change the facts.
“Yeah, we’re inside the labyrinth.”
After I affirmed his suspicion, a long silence ensued. Arta seemed to be stuck in his own mind, not saying anything as his thoughts consumed him, and I let him continue without interrupting.
It wasn’t either Arta or I who broke that silence, nor was it the dense Ainar or the intellectually curious Raven.
Beep, beep, beep!
An alarm ran in a rhythmic pattern. The sound came from within Arta’s pockets.
As I reflexively looked in his direction, Arta came back to reality and said, “It means it’s nearly time for me to return.”
“I see.”

Even as I kept my response calm, I wrestled with a dilemma in my mind. Should I just continue with our conversation until he left, or should I carry out the plan I had thought of before and forcibly stop him from returning? At worst, the latter would just be an unnecessary detour if no special situation or reward appeared after carrying it out.
We’re already in that situation, anyway.

However, my opinion of Arta had changed. Before, I had only focused on rewards and events. With time, though, I’d come to find greater importance in the story he had rather than those rewards. It might even help me understand the secrets of the world.
If I need to knock him out...
Just as I was settling on my decision, Arta suddenly stopped me in my tracks.
“Stop.”
It was as if he’d heard what I was thinking.
I wondered for an instant if he had a magic tool that granted him telepathy or something, but that thankfully wasn’t the case.
“Any who have observed the future as long as I have are no stranger to that look in your eyes.”
“I wasn’t thinking about anything.”
I’d hesitated for a beat too long, and he laughed. “That would be nice if it were the case. I have my fair share of experience with this and have multiple different safeguards as a precaution.”
There was no way to know if he was telling the truth, but coming out with such a bold and open statement like that was pretty effective against me. It was making me hesitate even more than before.
What do I do?

The internal dilemma that I thought I’d resolved took form once more. But if this were just a run of the game, I wouldn’t have thought for so long. No matter what happened here, I just needed to try again later—
“How about letting go of that desire and using the remaining time as efficiently as possible? For both of our sakes.”
Arta once again derailed my thoughts, and I decided to just reveal my true thoughts in kind. Being honest suited barbarians more, right?
“I don’t know about you, but what’s in it for us?” I questioned.
“It’s because I know why today is the Final Day.”
“What?”
“I didn’t know before, but now that I know that this is inside the labyrinth, it came to me quite easily. I understand why all this happened.”
Hesitation tried to grip me again, and I threw it aside. “Alright. Let’s talk.”
I would go with the peaceful method.

His personality had shifted 180 degrees, as if that dopey attitude from before was an act. Plus, there were too many obstacles for me to just charge him. Lastly, I got the sense that it wasn’t a bluff when he said he had something prepared. As long as I wasn’t certain I could get through whatever he had prepared or know what his hidden ace up the sleeve was, I couldn’t know what risk trying to fight him would pose.
“Seeing as we don’t have time, let’s ask one question back and forth. That will make it fair,” Arta offered.
“Sure.”
The mode of conversation was decided as well.

Fortunately, it was a mode that I was very familiar with. I had experienced it many times in the past for one reason or another. From Auril Gavis to Baekho Lee to the Round Table... Everyone of this world, no matter who they were, tried to avoid taking losses at any cost, even when they had plenty they desired for themselves.
Not that I was any different.
It’s a shame that I don’t have Misplaced Trust anymore...
After I’d used the final charge on the last one, I’d planned on procuring another one just in case. However, the item wasn’t always out on the market, so I had failed to get one.
Well, I don’t even know if that will work on this guy, anyway.
I shrugged off any regret I might have felt.
“Then I—”
“No, I’ll go first.”
Arta paused, processing the fact that I had cut him off. “Quickly, then.”
With that, my turn began.
My first question had already been decided. However, since I didn’t know what sort of shocking answer I would get...
“(Continue with what you were saying before. How is today the Final Day?)”

For the security of the conversation, I decided that speaking in the ancient language would be safer. Arta thankfully seemed to understand my intention with it, as he turned off the translation device to answer me.
Needless to say, the answer I received wasn’t the one I wanted.
“(Ask another question.)”
“(What?)”
“(Don’t worry, I’m not saying I won’t answer that question,)” he assured me. “(I just want to move it back a little.)”
“(Why should I do that?)”
“(There is a good chance that you’ll only understand what I tell you when that time comes.)”

I was a little peeved, suspicious that he might be plotting something, but it didn’t seem like he would just come out with it for the sake of it, so I let it slide. “(Got it, then I’ll ask you something else. What is the name of that emperor you mentioned?)”
I asked it just in case the name of the Immortal or the King of the New World came up, but unfortunately...
“(That’s a name I haven’t heard before...)” I grumbled.
The name of the emperor was one I had never heard before.
Since the name of the dynasty is also different, is it a completely different entity from the Kingdom of Rafdonia?
In any case, that was the end of the first question.
“(Then it’s my turn.)”
It was now his turn to ask me a question.
As always, I listened intently to what he would say. In a conversation like this, the question itself was information as well.
What was he most curious about?
As he began to speak, that answer was revealed to me.
“(Bjorn Yandel. Have you perhaps seen a being who came from a different dimension, or have you ever heard of such an entity?)”
My mind blanked.
“(Please answer me. This is a very important question.)”
I had no clue why that, of all things, was so important to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 814: Hidden Story (6)
paragraphs: The question itself wasn’t anything special. The existence of evil spirits was a well-known truth within Rafdonia, after all.
But this is someone from the past asking about it...
While I was hesitating, Arta’s eyes flashed with sharp wit.
“(An answer given after giving the question so much thought is bound to be rife with lies.)”
Although he didn’t say it explicitly, that sure seemed like him telling me that he could end the conversation at whatever moment he pleased.
I decided to get on with it. “(I was just surprised. I have no intention of lying.)”
“(Answer me first. We don’t have much time.)”
Since we were running short on time, I couldn’t contemplate for as long as I’d want to either.
“(You’re right. They do exist,)” I affirmed, then jumped to my second question. “(How did you know about them?)”
I wanted to ask if evil spirits existed in the past as well, but I held back. In my experience, questions that could be answered with a simple yes or no should be avoided in these exchanges.
“(Is that your question?)”
“(Yeah, it is.)”
“(It’s not that I knew. I just had a theory about them. If I knew, then I wouldn’t have asked you.)”
“(I don’t like that vague answer of yours.)”
At my legitimate complaint, he seemed to concede the point a little, as he quickly gave additional context.

“(While carrying out the labyrinth project, there were a few unexpected variables we encountered. We discovered unidentified life forms within the labyrinth that we had not created. Their appearances were completely different from ours, but they had intelligence. And after a long period of research, our research team came to a conclusion: That ‘unidentified lifeform’ was a being who came over from a different dimension.)”
“(I understand what you’re trying to say. Then do—)”
“(I think that was enough of an answer for that question of yours.)”
Well, he did give me a long explanation. I couldn’t allow myself to get greedy here.
“(Then could I ask my question now?)” Arta inquired.
“(Go on.)”
“(Please describe to me the world you know outside of the labyrinth.)”

Well, that wasn’t anything difficult. I could go on forever if I tried giving him all the details, but the gist of it was pretty simple. The Palace, Noark, the labyrinth and the mana stones, adventurers, the Witch—these points were enough to give a basic outline of the world, and since I explained the events of things within the labyrinth last time already, the answer itself didn’t take long.
“(Hmm, then you adventurers are people who adventure through the labyrinth to provide resources for the enclosed city.)”
“(You got it. Then it’s my turn.)” With Arta’s nod as the signal, I presented my next question. “(What is the Power of Origin?)”
In a way, that was the heart of it all because, from what I could tell, this power was what was driving the labyrinth.
“(It is a power that exists in each dimension. Our empire found the Origin on accident, and after a long period of research, we discovered a way to harness the power that flowed out of it.)”
“(That’s a little too vague. Give me more.)”
“(When you use the Power of Origin, you can create new artificial dimensions. However, there is only a finite supply of it, so the power decreases equal to the power used.)”
“(What happens when you use all the power?)” I threw out the question, hoping for a bonus answer. Unexpectedly, Arta just gave it to me without a hassle.
“(Can’t you tell yourself? The end of a dimension will come. Like what you see now.)”
Only then did I start to get an idea of what was happening.
Arta continued to ask questions about my current world, and I asked questions about his world in turn.
“(I think I’ve waited long enough at this point. Tell me,)” I demanded. “(Why is today the Final Day?)”
“(You are hasty. Could I ask you one more question before I answer that one?)”
Although the order was broken, I didn’t mind. “(Go on.)”
“(Have you perhaps met or heard of a creature... No, an intelligence that proclaims and defines itself as Arta?)”
How did he know about that?
I took a moment to scan my surroundings, wondering if one of my party members had slipped up.
“(It seems I won’t need an answer from the looks of it, but could you still give me an answer?)”
“(As I thought.)” Arta donned a serious expression and fell into contemplation.
In the end, I couldn’t help but ask him, “(How did you know about that?)”

It was practically the same question as I’d asked before. This entire conversation, I’d felt like I was on the back foot. The questions I felt compelled to ask him kept changing the more I talked to him.
Thankfully, at least, I immediately received an answer.
“(The reason I know of this other ‘Arta’ is simple. It is because I have been formulating a plan regarding it in the present. But from what I can tell, it seems it has failed in the end.)”
“(Are you saying you’re the same Arta as the other one?)”
“(I cannot say that we are the same in the truest sense, but possibly yes, in a sense just below that. Could I perhaps meet him?)”
“(I’ll answer this as your next question, but that’s going to be impossible. It’d take hours to get there by boat from here.)”
“(I see. Then I have obtained all the answers I wanted. And the time lined up as well.)”
I’d gone out of my way to answer multiple questions in a row, and now he was thinking of running?
Feeling cheated, my hand was about to reach for my hammer when he continued, saying, “(So listen closely to what I have to say. It will be of great help to you.)”
“(Make it quick.)”
“(First, after I leave, go talk to the other Arta about my story and learn as much information as you can. He will know how history has passed much better than I have.)”
“(And then?)”
“(Second, if you can return to Rafdonia alive, go to these spatial coordinates that I will now tell you. I will hide a useful item there for you.)”
Hiding something in Rafdonia? Was that even possible?

I couldn’t wrap my head around any of this. Was this guy an NPC, or was he real? If what he just said really worked, then I couldn’t just treat him like he was a simple hidden secret of the labyrinth.
Stop. I got the coordinates, so I should just check them out later to confirm it.
Rather than getting my thoughts tangled in endless loops, I decided to check on something that caught my attention.
“(‘If we return to Rafdonia’?)” I quoted. “(What do you mean?)”
“(Ah, I haven’t told you that yet. While we were carrying out the labyrinth project, there were quite a few difficulties we’ve faced, but the greatest difficulty was this.)”
Arta didn’t show much emotion as he continued his story, but I couldn’t match his calm.
“(The thing that threatened us most wasn’t beings from other dimensions, nor was it terrorism by hostile forces who opposed the Labyrinth Project. It was simple a phenomenon.)”
“(A phenomenon...?)”
“(We haven’t been able to discover the cause of it yet, but as we worked, there were multiple times where the dimension itself twisted and killed all members of the research expedition.)”
Uh... Was he talking about a dimensional collapse?
“(You asked how I knew today was the Final Day, correct? This is the answer to that.)”
I was left speechless.
Wait, is this guy saying that today is when the dimensional collapse will happen?
I stood there in a daze, my mind wiped clean of all thought.
Beep! Beep! Beep!
The alarm inside Arta’s pocket rang once more, beeping faster and faster. Arta took notice of the sound just as I did and rushed over to me.
“(Third, changing the future is not an impossibility at all.)”
“(What?)” I managed, still dumbfounded. “(Give me a proper answer before you leave—)”

Arta grabbed my arm and blurted out, “(Alright, this is the last one. Keep this in mind: A being from a different dimension ordinarily cannot enter another dimension. The only way for a being such as that to enter another is—)”
I didn’t even have time to hear his answer before a flash of light blinded me.

Nothing much changed after that. The bolts of lightning and meteors caused by Amelia’s Final Day were still falling, and the island continued to spew hot lava like it was on the verge of exploding even after we slew the Beast.
However, there was exactly one thing that did change.
Please just finish what you say before you leave...
I had been sharing a conversation with Arta before the flash, and after it, Arta had vanished.
The other members had stayed quiet after I began speaking in the ancient language. Now, they just glanced at me, not seeming to understand the full extent of what happened.
In that uncomfortable silence, I took a moment to collect my thoughts.

Changing the future, beings from other dimensions, hiding a treasure in the city—it all seemed so distant in this moment. If I filed those ideas away and gathered only the important points, then this was the most important one of them all.
A dimensional collapse is going to happen.

It was just a hunch, but there seemed to be two conditions that needed to be met in order to encounter the Arta from the past: use Final Day on this island and do so on the day of a dimensional collapse. It was only a theory, of course. I had no way of testing those conditions.
By my guess... the dimensional collapse will probably happen the moment the Final Day’s duration ends...
We still had time. Some, but not much.
It won’t be enough for us to get down to the fifth floor.
If what Arta told me was true, we would need to face the first dimensional collapse on the sixth floor. There was only one thing we had to do at that moment.
“Auyen,” I called. “How long will it take from here to get to Arta island again?”
“We won’t be able to get there as quickly as when we first got there. We pushed the ship too hard on our way back...”
“Just tell me this: Can we get there and come back within nine hours?”
There was a pause. “Not with the regular boat we use. We also used most of the mana stones on our way here, and because medium-sized ships consume much more soul power than small ships...”
“I see.”
“But there is a smaller boat that I’ve prepared. With that, I should be able to use my abilities to let us make it in time...”
“But?”
“It can only carry three people at a time.”
“That’s good enough.” I turned to the others and announced, “Everyone except me and Auyen will wait here.”
“Wait, there’s one more spot left. Why are only the two of you going?” Amelia interjected, trying to suggest an alternative.
“We’re not going there to fight. And if a fight does occur, there’s no difference between two and three people being there.”
“That’s true, but—”
“We don’t have time. Emily, wait here on standby and prepare.”
“Prepare for what?”
I let out a wry laugh. I was the one who said it, but I had no idea what to prepare for either.
Maybe...
This might have just become my most difficult expedition yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 815: Hidden Story (7)
paragraphs: The small boat capable of only transporting three people rushed over the waves while receiving myriad buffs from our professional navigator.
[Auyen Rockrobe has cast Fair Wind.]
[Auyen Rockrobe has cast Trade Route.]
[Auyen Rockrobe has cast Ghost Ship.]
This boat’s speed wasn’t that different from our main ship’s when carrying all the members of our clan on it.
Swoosh!
In fact, it felt multiple times faster.
Boom! Splash! Bang!
Maybe because the ship was smaller?

As far as a passenger’s experience, though, this ride was by far the worst of the two. Every time we hit a wave, the boat shook and shuddered, leaping into the air like a dolphin. Honestly, if Ainar had gotten on with us, the ride would trigger her seasickness all over again and make her throw up all over the place.
Just like me right now.
“Blergh! Ugh!”
Unfortunately for me, barbarians were weak on the ocean.
“Sh-should I slow down a little?”
“N— No...” I warbled. “Don’t ever slow down.”

How was Auyen of all people fine with these conditions? Wouldn’t a regular person get dizzy and sick at this point? I didn’t know of any stats or skills that a navigator could have that would help with seasickness.
“Blerrrgh!”
“P-please hold on for a little longer! We’re nearly there!”
Nearly there...
I’d heard that quite a few times already. It’d given me strength at first, but now, it was only making me despair harder.
Let’s think.

It was just like that very first day, when I crawled around on the cave floor after stepping into a goblin trap. If I shifted my attention to a different thought, I’d arrive at my destination at some point. The problem was, the seasickness was making it difficult for me to think.
The machine monster Arta and the human Arta.
The past, present, and the future.
The Labyrinth Project.
The empire and the kingdom.
The dimensional collapse...

All the different pieces of information I had obtained during this expedition continued to fly around in my mind and tangle themselves up with each other. It felt like I was so close to reaching something big, yet I was still too far from the truth to know anything. Still, for some reason, I got the feeling that the moment I could untangle these strings of information, I would have the answer to everything.
That last thing he tried to tell me is bugging me too...
Even while my head felt like it was going to explode from all the thinking, I couldn’t help but recall his words and his expression.
“(Keep this in mind: A being from a different dimension ordinarily cannot enter another dimension. The only way for a being such as that to enter another is—)”
I couldn’t shake the feeling that he was going to tell me something very important. The fact that I wasn’t able to hear it was driving me up the wall with frustration.
Did he time that on purpose?
Stop.
My thoughts were going on a rampage like an unleashed bull. I reigned them in to stop them from crashing into the parts of my mind that needed to focus on what was most important at the moment.
A dimensional collapse...
How could we overcome the disaster that was likely soon to come? That was the problem I needed to solve first.
The Lord of the Sixth Floor has also been summoned...
Man, I hoped that the raid ended before the collapse began. If not, that guy would end up being a huge pain to deal with.
Maybe I shouldn’t have come here but gone outside to look for a wizard who could use Dimensional Door?
Despite my doubts, I decided not to dwell on them. It was practically impossible to find a wizard who could use a Dimensional Door on this endless ocean of a floor.
Arta.
Plus, I couldn’t help but feel that some very deep secret was hidden within Arta’s story. Before I left, I needed to figure out what that was.
“Captain, we’re here!”
I sighed in relief. We’d finally arrived.
“Yeah, good work... Blergh!”
I was already exhausted.
[You have entered a special area. Field Effect—Arta Secret Base is applied. All hostile actions are forbidden within the field.]
Hatches and pipings lined the walls from end to end. They were the mana circuits that looked like the electrical wiring of the Arta Secret Base.
However, even though we had entered the base, we didn’t hear a voice.
“(Artaaaaaaa!)” I bellowed, and a frantic reply quickly answered me.

“(Ah? Ah! You’re finally here! I wasn’t able to witness you fighting the beast. Some problems arose, you see. But now that I see the reaction has disappeared, I can tell that you have defeated the beast—!)”
“(How about coming here and thanking me personally?)”
“(Ah, yes. I should definitely do that. However, I must repair the testing site quickly—)”
“(Don’t do that later. Come here now. I have something important to discuss.)”
“(What does that even mean...? There is nothing more important than recovering the testing site. Have you forgotten? This testing site must be recovered to stop the end of the world—)”
What was he talking about?
I took out one of the drops from the Beast and held it up so that he could see it. “(If you don’t have this, you won’t even be able to restore your testing site, anyway.)”
“(Are you...threatening me?)”
“(Threatening? No, I’m persuading you. So how about you drop the testing site business and talk with me first?)”
“(I see... Understood. Speak. Just what is it that has you in such a hurry?)”
“(At this point, I feel that we should talk while looking at each other face to face.)”
“(That will be...problematic.)”
“(Why, because you’re not human?)”
The answer came back to me through the speakers after a momentary pause.
“(Do you know about me?)”
Yeah, I do.

I’d seen this guy multiple times during the game. When I progressed through the normal story, a moment would come when Arta would demand the remains of the hunted Beast, and that was when the player would be given a choice: give it to Arta or don’t give it to Arta.

The moment that the former was chosen, the story would end with the player obtaining the rewards from Arta. If the player attempted to speak to Arta after that point, he would just say he was busy with his work and tell the player to stop bothering him. If the player then left the secret base due to the time constraint of Terminus, the entrance would close and this place would become inaccessible forever.
Put simply, choosing to keep the rewards from Arta would end his storyline.
Well, not that the second choice gives that much of a story either.
If the player chose not to give Arta the drops, Arta would reveal his machine monster form and a battle would commence.
He’s as difficult to fight as the Lord of the Ninth Floor.

It probably went without saying that I was wiped out during my first attempt. My specs just weren’t up to it at all. From what I figured out later, Machine Monster Arta was a raid boss that was much more powerful even than Sniktura or the Beast. In the end, I created a team that could explore the tenth floor and brought them all the way to the sixth floor to attempt the raid, and even then, it took dozens of tries for me to finally defeat him.
The problem is that the reward I got wasn’t anything special, even after I defeated him.

The reward was one Machine Monster Heart, and I wasn’t completely sure what its use was. Sure, it could be consumed to be used as an elixir that greatly increased the character’s stats, and when used as a material, it was treated like the highest-quality mana core on the same level as a dragon heart. By that alone, it was definitely a valuable reward. However...
It didn’t feel like anything like a reward you’d get after defeating a monster on the same level as the Lord of the Ninth Floor.

That was why after I succeeded on my first clear, I wondered if there was a proper way to use the heart that I didn’t know about, so I continued to delve deeper into his story. There were a few things I was able to learn because of those attempts.
“(Answer me. Do you know about me?)”
Well...
“(I at least know that stopping the end of the world isn’t why you want this,)” I replied as bait.
He caught on immediately. “(Are you... Are you a pilgrim?)”
Pilgrim.
