In the context of this world’s history, the term referred to the betrayers of humanity who fought on the side of the Witch. Arta had asked us the same thing at the start as well.
“(Who are you? Pilgrims?)”
“(You still haven’t answered my question. Who are you? Pilgrims?)”
Important to note: I told him that we were not. Arta had a way to prove that we weren’t pilgrims, and the players had no way of proving they were pilgrims.
Then why did he keep asking us if we were pilgrims?

Although doubt surged within my heart, I didn’t make it obvious. The moment I asked him that question, he would know why I asked and immediately sounded out that we really weren’t pilgrims, ending the conversation there.
I decided to file that question away for later.

“(How about letting me see your face before we begin talking?)” When he didn’t respond, I pushed it further, saying, “(I really only want to talk. I will give you this after our conversation is over.)”

The offer was outwardly gentle, but looked at from a different interpretation, my sentence could mean that I wouldn’t give him what he wanted if he refused. Thankfully, it seemed Arta understood that subtext as well.
With a defeated voice, he said, “(Understood...)”

Even while all the doors were opening and closing randomly due to the damage done to the testing site, one door had remained closed all this time. That door finally opened with a hiss, and Arta revealed his true form.
Clank! Clank!
He stepped forward to the sound of metal on metal, a sound that human movement should never make.
“(I have revealed myself as you requested. What do you want from me?)”
From now on, above all, I had to stay focused.
Arta stood a couple of inches above six feet tall, looking similar to those humanoid robots made to look like humans in sci-fi movies. However, Arta’s particular design left much to be desired.
It really is disgusting to see him in real life.

His arms, legs, and body were all openly mechanical, as shown by the steel frames that made him up. Yet disturbingly, his face was all too human-like, almost as if a person’s face stretched over a machine.
Why is his face a real human face?

Back when I was playing the game, I didn’t really understand why Arta had chosen that form. I figured each person had their own preferences and left it at that. Well, he wasn’t really a “person” so much as a machine. Anyway, that wasn’t the point.
Seeing him like this, I can tell it’s the same face.
The secret base Arta and the researcher Arta I saw not long ago were one and the same.
“(Speak already.)”
Although we were face to face, he wasn’t speaking with his vocal cords but the speaker system he had been using to talk all this time.
“(You don’t seem like a survivor from the destroyed empire. What are you, really?)”
“(Well, what do you think?)” I asked back.
“(I will not answer that.)”
(“Then it’ll be difficult for me to just hand this over to you. Aren’t we here to talk?)”

Arta just stared at me. His slightly red eyes that looked like camera lenses made me feel chills down my spine for some reason. It was like the computer of his mind was calculating what was more efficient: continuing to talk to me here or just ignoring my request and taking the drop from me by force.
“(I lack information,)” he said eventually. “(As long as you don’t reveal your identity to me, all I can make about your identity are guesses.)”
“(But if you are to make that guess?)”
“(A pilgrim... But as I thought, there isn’t enough proof to make that judgment. Tell me. What are you?)”
Hearing the question repeated, I shrugged and answered, “(It’s not important if I’m a pilgrim or not.)”
I had already thought up how to steer this conversation to agitate his curiosity, plus how to gain even more than that and gain his favor.
“(Then could I take that as you declaring you are not a pilgrim—)”
Alright, let’s cut him off here.
“(Research member of the empire’s First Magic Engineering Research Center, Arta. I was sent here by you from the past.)”
Any person... No. Even a machine wouldn’t be able to hold back after that.

chapters.title: Chapter 816: Hidden Story (8)
paragraphs: Maybe it went without saying, but even with his mechanical heart, Arta couldn’t help but bite at the bait I tossed his way.
“(My past self...?)”
“(Arta, didn’t you say you had an idea as to who I am? Didn’t you come to this place when you were still human?)”
“(But back then...I didn’t meet any living beings like you—)”
“(Of course you wouldn’t.)”
“(Then—)”
“(Your past self told me that changing the future is not an impossibility.)”

That seemed to work as a passcode of some kind. After taking a moment to calculate quietly to himself, he slowly began to speak. “(So the actions of my past self have changed this present moment. That is not impossible, certainly. However, what proof do you have—)”
“(I think you’re mistaken here,)” I said, once again cutting him off. “(I’m not telling you to trust me.)”
I held up the quest item that he desired, the harvested remains of the beast, and observed his reaction. As long as I had this with me, he needed to answer my questions.
“(It doesn’t matter if you trust me or not,)” I argued, waving the remains in front of him. “(I just need to obtain the information I want from you. And isn’t that the same for you?)”
Unexpectedly, though, he accepted the proposition immediately. “(What do you want?)”
So then, he’d decided to assess what I truly wanted by seeing what my next question would be... Well, I didn’t mind.
“(Tell me about your story. What happened on this island? And what happened after you returned to the empire?)”
I had to hear it from him, this story that I didn’t know, to see if there was something hidden within.
“(Your question is quite unspecific, but I will attempt to answer it.)”
“(That’s a good attitude to have.)”

Arta paused one last time, then launched into his story. “(When the Final Day was calculated to befall on this day, there was nothing on this island. It was just a dimension on the verge of being destroyed after the Origin was damaged.)”
“(The Beast wasn’t here either?)”
“(The existence of the Beast was the greatest difference between the observation of the future and the future that came. May I continue?)”
“(Sure. I won’t cut you off anymore, so go on.)”

“(After our observations of the future concluded, I spent a long time wondering what the cause of the End could be. I then began to think that it had a close relation to the empire’s Labyrinth Project...and with time, I was able to confirm my hypothesis. As the world inside the labyrinth continued to grow, the Power of Origin held by the higher dimension continued to shrink.)”
Oh, I see.
“(Then what’s the higher dimension? Oh, sorry about interrupting,)” I tossed in at the end, noticing Arta go silent for a second. He quickly continued.
“(To put it simply, it could be considered the more real world.)”
“(The real world?)”
“(The concepts are a little different, but you will understand well enough with that conception in mind.)”
“(Then go right ahead.)”

“(The first problem occurred when the labyrinth grew to be larger than the higher dimension. Although it didn’t lead to a dimensional collapse, errors began to appear in the higher dimension. Having observed the horrifying sights in this place, I went and protested against the continuation of the Labyrinth Project, but no one heeded my advice.)”
Arta stood unmoving as he rattled off the facts of his explanation, not moving an inch to gesture or gesticulate.

“(The empire didn’t care what happened to the higher dimension—their goal was the construction of paradise, and that paradise was inside the labyrinth. In truth, the empire succeeded in the Project’s completion and was able to move the entire empire into the labyrinth. However, I did not leave with them. I abandoned my soul, leaving behind my knowledge alone within this vessel to await the End that would one day come. I believed that the moment the higher dimension came to an end, the labyrinth would also collapse.)”
“(So time passed, and now, here we are...)” I trailed off, jumping in when I thought the story was coming to a close. However, Arta sternly shook his head.
“(No, that is still just the story of the past.)”
I hesitated. “(What?)”
“(The higher dimension met its end in that way, and I wasn’t able to stop it. And so, I was forced into the labyrinth as well.)”
Wait, I couldn’t understand what he was saying.
I should keep listening for now...
I didn’t think it was the right time to cut him off, so I just closed my mouth and continued to listen to what Arta was saying.

“(The land within the labyrinth matched up perfectly with the land I had been born and raised in—a truly perfect replica of the world. Excluding a few people in power there, the residents of that world didn’t even realize that their world was inside the labyrinth. Of course, it differed in some ways from the base world. To create a perfect world, the emperor created four systems, and those systems were called ‘god’ by the residents, as they controlled and ruled the world.

“(However, this is where the second problem occurred. The labyrinth wasn’t the paradise the empire thought it was. Or at least, it wasn’t so after the higher dimension met its End. As if affected by the End of the higher dimension, many big and small errors began to appear within the labyrinth. One of the four systems created by the emperor went on a rampage and became an enemy. Even the absolute authority held by the emperor weakened as a result, and monsters of every sort, ones not created by the emperor, began to appear all over the world... And then, most astonishingly of all, the Earth Witch was born.)”
The moment the words were spoken, it felt as if someone had fired a shotgun at the back of my head.
“(W— W-wait...)”
The information was too much to take in at once to make perfect sense of it all, but if I was at least getting the gist of what he was saying...
“(G-give me a second to gather my thoughts.)”
So, what he was saying was...
If the Earth Witch was first born inside the labyrinth...
Wasn’t Rafdonia inside the labyrinth as well?
It turned out that I needed a lot more time than a second to think, yet even then, the shock of it didn’t seem to lessen at all.
I mean...I guess it doesn’t matter that much to me, though.

The more shocking the situation, the calmer I needed to be. And it wasn’t as if my way of thinking was wrong either. This wasn’t my original world, anyway, but one separate from Earth. Who cared if I was in the higher dimension or the labyrinth?
Still, it definitely caught me off guard...
Phew. That helped me calm down a little.
“(I’m fine now. You can continue. So what happened after the Earth Witch was born?)” I asked, pressing the metaphorical resume button. Arta continued right away like he’d been waiting for my signal.

“(A war began between the empire and the Witch. Many things happened, but the result was that the empire was defeated. It wasn’t a bad outcome for me. I believed that with the disappearance of the empire, the End would also cease to be. However, that was just my belief. I had no way of confirming it as a fact.)”
I agreed with the sentiment. A 99 percent chance and a 100 percent certainty were clearly different.

“(And so, I observed the Final Day once more. Yet for some reason, the Final Day wasn’t any different from what I had observed previously. I needed to stop it. And so, I created the base on this island and continued with my research...and finally, after nearly an eternity of study did I belatedly realize the truth.)”
“(What was it?)”
“(That there is no way to stop the End.)”
That short sentence went against all the stories I knew about Arta Island.
“(That is my story,)” Arta concluded his speech.
“(What?)” I balked. “(I haven’t even been able to ask you—)”
“(I have concluded that I have provided a sufficient enough answer to your nonsensical request. I will only allow three more questions from this point on.)”
“(That’s not—)”

“(There is no guarantee that the deal will be kept after our conversation ends. Continuing this conversation with someone whose identity I know nothing of is a waste of time. I might even be leaking my information to an enemy this very moment.)”
Wait, why did his tone change so suddenly? It was just like in the game, when he would change into the machine monster and go on a rampage.
“(If you refuse, use of armed force will be initialized, initialized, initialized, initialized...)” He began to repeat his words, as if an error had occurred.
A chill went down my spine. Arta was a raid boss on the same level of difficulty as the Lord of the Ninth Floor. If he went on a rampage, I had no chance of surviving.
“(S-stop!)” I stuttered. “(I understand! I’ll only ask three more questions, so calm down!)”
“(...Confirmed. Ask your question.)”
What a quick change in attitude. Did his CPU rust in his old age?
With no way of knowing, I focused on quickly formulating three questions.
“(H-h-hurry... Hurry, hurry, hurry...)”
After all, how was I supposed to relax when that was the state he was in?
“(First question.)”
Like a man being chased, I quickly asked my first question.

The four systems created by the emperor. The existence of Rafdonia. The research center is on the first basement floor. The nonhumans that ancient civilizations had never discovered, and this labyrinth where monsters appear and level-ups could take place.
I had many questions I wanted to ask, but I let them all go for now.
“(Just what is the Earth Witch?)”
His answer came the moment the first question was out of my mouth.

“(Earth Witch refers to the human female Elise Groundia. She was born with the Power of Origin, of which the cause is suspected to be an error created as a consequence of the End of the higher dimension. She is omnipotent, but she possesses too human a heart to be called a god.)”
It was as if he were reading from an encyclopedia. It wasn’t the answer I wanted. I only asked that generic question because I thought he’d go into more detail if I did.
“(Second question... H-hurry, hurry, hurry...)”
Damn it. Was I under a countdown or something?
“(Second question. What is a Records Stone, and where can I go to see it?)”
Depending on how you looked at it, this information was even more important than anything to do with the Witch.
“(No relevant information available.)”
I stiffened. “(What?)”
“(Third question... Hurry, hurry, hurry...)”
Wait, he didn’t know anything, but it still used up one of my questions? I stared at him, stumped and feeling cheated.
“(H-hurry...hurry...hurry...)”
However, considering the situation, I didn’t expect anything would change even if I complained.
Still, the fact that he has no information about the Records Stone is information itself.
I decided it was best to let go of my disappointment.

“(Alright, as you wished. This is my final question...)” I began. “(You said you realized there was no way to stop the End. Then what is your goal? You can’t stop it, so why did you want to kill the Beast?)”
Once again, Arta replied immediately.

“(The Beast is a being created by the Earth Witch by modifying Pilgrims to protect the Power of Origin. It has no relation to the End. However, Arta wished to eliminate the Beast because as long as the Beast is alive, none other than the Witch can access the Power of Origin. What’s more, Arta’s goal is—)”
Suddenly, Arta’s voice paused. Then a beat of silence later...
“(I...have been solely a bystander for all that long while.)”
I heard Arta’s voice.
The mechanical tinge was still there through the speakers, yet for some reason, his voice sounded more human than before. Had he returned to his original self? There was no telling.

“(I was only able to watch, unable to change anything with my own two hands,)” Arta said, his red eyes peering directly at me from his human face still attached to the machine body. “(That is why it will change this time... Because change is human.)”
Arta clanked up to me before opening up his metal palm. “(There, now hand it over.)”
“(Hmm... I haven’t heard what you are going to do with it yet, though.)”
“(I will use it to create a new labyrinth. If you wish to stop this—)”
I sensed anger starting to rise in him again, so I quickly cut him off. “(Here, take it. I don’t intend on stopping you.)”
The way Arta’s eyes bounced away and back told me he was confused about why I would hand it over so willingly, though I couldn’t really be sure. It might just be a hunch I got.
“(Are there any additional rewards?)” I asked slyly. “(I think you have something you wanted to give us at first.)”
“(The time you’ve spent here is reward enough.)”
Yeah, go figure. I couldn’t get the rewards from the game since I took a different route to get here.
“(Really? Then we’ll be going.)”
With that, I ended our conversation and left the secret base without looking back, then got on the boat we’d arrived in to hurry back to the original island.
Splash!

Auyen seemed to have a lot he wanted to ask me, but maybe out of the compassion in his heart, he didn’t say anything. Thanks to that, I was able to focus on my thoughts—and to evade the seasickness somewhat.
Arta...

There was a gap in history between the human Arta and the machine monster Arta. Although they were the same, they were also fundamentally different. Fortunately for me, I had an idea of how to make sense of that gap.
Making a new labyrinth...
I smirked.
It was pretty ironic. If my guess was correct, Arta wouldn’t be able to change a damn thing.
“Why are you smiling like that?”
I looked over at Auyen, surprised by the question. “Hmm?”
“It’s just... A very bitter smile is how I’d put it.”
My smirk widened, revealing a flash of bared teeth. The questions rolled in soon after.
“(That is why it will change this time... Because change is human.)”
What was Arta’s original self doing now? Was he dead, or was he still alive, waiting for someone to kill the Beast for him?
Did anything really, truly change?
Splash!
There was no telling.

chapters.title: Chapter 817: Lifeline (1)
paragraphs: “Bjorn!”
“You’re not hurt!”
“Good work. You too, Auyen.”
“Hahaha. It’s nothing, Madame— ahem, Ms. Raines. It is my greatest and only glory to be of help to the captain.”
As soon as we returned to the cave, the waiting members came up and greeted us.
“So Yandel, did you get what you wanted?”
“Sort of,” I answered Amelia vaguely. “How were things here?”
“Nothing special. Well, everyone was a bit restless…”
I couldn’t deny that I had been a bit worried, but other than not being able to rest properly due to Final Day, it seemed nothing else had happened.
“So…what will happen now? To be honest, I’ve been getting this ominous feeling for a while now…” Parav asked while shivering.
That wasn’t a good sign. His reactions gave some credence to my suspicion that the dimensional collapse was approaching.
“Yeah, it’s like Parav says. You just told us to prepare, but not what to prepare for. I think it’s about time you tell us.”
I sighed. Should I tell them or not? Although I hesitated, the moment didn’t last long.
“I’ve gotten information that a dimensional collapse could soon occur.”
It was just a short factual statement, but silence fell over everyone, then was quickly followed by an uproar.
“Pardon?”
“A dimensional collapse…?”
“But you’ve gotten information, right? What does that mean? Did you hear it from that guy who came from the past?”
“No, even more important than that is this: when will this happen?” Raven’s question pierced through the chaos, pushing me to give an honest answer.
“Emily,” I called, “how long has it been since you’ve cast Final Day?”
“Around twenty hours.”
“Then it’ll be in about four hours. If the information I received is correct, that is.”

“Four hours?!” Raven shouted, appalled. “But that’s so soon from now! Why are you telling us something so important only now?! And why did you go so far away despite knowing how little precious time we had?!”
“There was…reason enough for it.”
“But then at least tell us what that reason is—!”
“Stop, wizard,” Amelia intervened, stopping Raven before she went off on me.
“Excuse me?”
“Yandel said he had a reason for it. That is enough.”

I found myself, admittedly, a little surprised. If Raven hadn’t been here, Amelia would’ve been the one to question me. Then again, maybe it was a little different with her since she only did that when the two of us were alone?

Heedless of my thoughts, Amelia continued, “Yandel is our leader, and what you’re doing right now is going against the hierarchy order of our group. You’ve been in the military, so you should understand what I’m trying to say.”
Raven seemed to second-guess herself at Amelia’s stern scolding. “I… I apologize. I’ve overstepped.”
Well, it looked like no one here could truly win against Amelia. Whether or not that was actually the case, since she had used the stick, it was my turn to use the carrot.

“You don’t have to go that far, Emily. Everyone here, not just Raven, must be curious… To keep it simple, I obtained the information about the dimensional collapse before I left for the secret base. However, I concluded that nothing much would change whether or not I went, so I went to the secret base to get as much additional information as I could, even if that didn’t amount to much in the end.”
“What do you mean, nothing will change?”
“Think about it. The dimensional collapse will occur today, but so what if we leave this place a little early? The sixth floor is already in pandemonium now that the Lord of the Floor is out.”
None of the members seemed to have a retort to that. The silence stretched on until Kaislan stepped up as a representative of everyone else here to ask, “So, do you have a new plan now?”
I smirked. “No, nothing like that.”
The conversation I had at the secret base had nothing to do with surviving the danger of the dimensional collapse, and we had no strategy to beat the dimensional collapse in the first place, anyway.
“But are you all just going to lie down and die because we don’t have a plan? Let’s just face it head-on. Aren’t we adventurers?”
Just like we always did.
This time, I would do everything within my power to save them all. If there were a point of most danger, I would stand in that place.
However, I didn’t say those words out loud. I didn’t need to.
“I will always trust you and follow you, Captain.”
“Hah… I don’t know what dangerous thing you’re planning on doing this time…”
“It’s fine… So don’t be so reckless anymore, okay?”
Every person here—except maybe the guild master Beleg, who had come into the labyrinth with me for the first time—was a member of the clan who trusted me.
Well, there was one other exception.

“Hmm, but to just face it head-on… Didn’t you nearly give up on everything not long ago?” Kaislan asked with an exaggeratedly joking tone. He was obviously trying to poke fun at me a little, but his question was one worth considering.
“I did. So cheer up, everyone.”
Kaislan tilted his head, bemused by my reaction. “Huh?”
Ignoring that, I looked at the group and said, “When a barbarian says to hit something head-on, it’s because he’s already concluded that it’s possible to hit it head-on.”
Even if the sky were to collapse on us, there was bound to be a hole we could climb out of.
[You have entered the sixth-floor Great Sea.]
Around four hours before the dimensional collapse, we left the Memories of the End—aptly named for the many memories we now had of it—and returned to the original Skull Island.
Ah, well. Maybe “returned” wasn’t the right word for it.
Splash!

The portal spat us all out, then disappeared like its work had been done, plunging us into a deep, abyssal darkness. Sure enough, the entire cave system was underwater, but that was no problem for us.
Think about it. If we’d known it could be a problem and did nothing about it, the real problem would be with our intelligence.

As planned, Raveen used her magic to create an orb of light as soon as she was dropped out of the portal. With our vision restored, we communicated with hand signals while affixing the hooks of the ropes tied on our bodies.
Name: Anabada School Fish Formation.
It was a formation specialized for underwater travel, where the entire group could be led to the destination with just the person at the front swimming.
Speaking of, I was that person at the front. Even though barbarians couldn’t swim, they had an easier time walking underwater than other races.
Thud! Thud!

After using Giantization, I walked in steady steps against the current as if hiking up a mountain. Because we had cast diving magic on all the members before taking the portal, we didn’t need to think about breathing for a bit.
Thud!

Once we left the cave, I could see the whole of Skull Island submerged under the water. The drowned island possessed none of the calm energy that the submerged city of Atlantis did, but instead looked as if a storm was passing through it.
Swoosh!
The currents were extreme, incomparable to the flow I felt in the cave, and littered with pieces of debris.
I’ll need to change the plan.

Even though my body had been enlarged with Giantization, I was actually starting to float, unable to resist the flow of the torrents. I was able to grab hold of the ground to stabilize myself, but the rocks, trees, and other debris that were swirling around us were making it nearly impossible to do anything.
And so, I gave up on Plan A: walking to a safe location before summoning the boat.
Splash!
We immediately summoned the boat, and I immediately got on before clutching the pillar in a bear grip.

The Anabada Clan boat was a high-level vessel and even featured a mana propulsion system. It was constructed from the highest-quality, buoyant lumber, which had been further improved by the Empower Buoyancy spell applied to the entire boat.
Swooosh!
In other words, the moment it was summoned underwater, it automatically floated up to the surface like a block of packing peanuts pushed deep into water.
Soon enough, the world brightened, and air rushed into my lungs as I took in a deep breath.
“Auyen,” I said, once I’d caught my breath, “how’s the boat doing?”
“The sails are broken, and the mana propulsion system has taken a lot of damage! At this rate, just floating is all we can—”
“That’s fine.”
“…Pardon?”
“Just staying afloat is good enough.”
After checking up on my allies, I took a proper look around.

“Heavy” wasn’t enough to describe the rain pouring around us. It was as if the heavens themselves had opened up to dump water upon us. The ocean, too, had welled up with clear intent to take its spoils, and the waves sloshed around like tsunamis.
The falling meteors and lightning bolts were Final Day’s, so I didn’t bother with them.
Why did this guy have to be summoned right before the collapse?

The environmental effects we were experiencing were happening all because the Lord of the Sixth Floor had been summoned. Most Lords of the Floors had a special effect that applied over the entire floor they were summoned on, and he was no exception.
[Lord of Tears, Tetraseia, awakens from a deep slumber.]
The moment he was summoned, rain would begin to fall over the entire sixth floor and engulf all the islands in water.
[All waves head toward the Island of Beginnings.]
After they were submerged for long enough, the waves would crash down like tsunamis and summon all adventurers of the sixth floor to a single place.

The Golden Ghost probably knew this as well, which had forced him to leave the island before the island was submerged, to look for another. There were a few islands that were safe even after the Lord of Tears was summoned, after all.
Can’t say I’m not intrigued that he has precious information like that.
Either way, I had better things to focus on at the moment.
Since the waves’ patterns were fixed, it was already too late to look for a safe point to ride out the storm. Not that that mattered.
The dimensional collapse will soon begin, anyway.
“Captain? With the damage sustained by the mana propulsion engine, we cannot control the boat—!”
“It’s fine, so just stay put.”
“Pardon?”
“I already told you. Just being able to float is good enough.”
I settled back and just watched as our boat rocked and swayed with the waves to where the Lord of the floor would be waiting for us.

“But at this rate, we’ll just end up where the Lord of the Floor is.” Raven cautiously asked, noting my inaction. Maybe it was the scolding she got from Amelia before, but she seemed a little less sure of herself when asking this time.
“It’s fine. Getting there is my goal.”
“Oh,” she breathed, already much more relieved. “So you did have a plan?”
I didn’t answer her further and chose to remain silent, and Raven didn’t pester me for more answers either.
With enough time, we saw them.
“Oh! A ship!”
“Looks like they’re all panicking over there.”
“Of course they’re scared. How could they not be with all the islands submerging and the waves being this fierce?”

Soon enough, we began to see more and more ships that had been swept up in the waves just like we were. Unlike us, though, most of them were frantically trying to avoid the grasp the waves had on them instead of just drifting.
Resisting won’t let you escape.
Not to say they were struggling for nought. That helped decrease the speed at which they were being taken away. It was also the reason they were able to see us out here instead of at the island.
“There… There are so many ships here!”
As we were towed in by the waves, we finally arrived at our destination.
Shwoooooo!

The whirlpool was swirling savagely, as if to suck in all the waters of the sixth floor. And there in its throes were hundreds of vessels, each of them being dragged along into the whirlpool’s orbit. I recognized each of the ships’ clan flags, but none of them were any of the truly famous ones.
Well, the fact that they were dragged here means they’re small fries.
The highest-ranking clans would have either already gone up to the seventh floor or found one of the safe islands as soon as the Lord of the Floor was summoned.
Then again, we would all be on equal footing once the collapse began.
“Anabada Clan! It’s the flag of the Anabada Clan!” someone on one of the ships we were passing by shouted when they recognized the flag on our ship.
“The Anabada Clan? The one led by Viscount Yandel?”
“The great adventurer who defeated the Lord of Terror and etched his name on the Stone of Honor!”
“W-we’re saved!”

I could understand why they were so passionately calling out to me in support. These people had just been stuck here, waiting for their deaths to come when the second phase began. They surely felt like my arrival was the lifeline tossed their way to help them miraculously survive.
“But why? He’s got to have the ability to escape this place!”
“Are you kidding? It’s the Baron Yandel— No, the Viscount!”
“He’s the hero who defeated the Lord of the Floor to save other adventurers on the third floor, so he must be here to save us too!”
“We just need to follow his commands! That will increase our chances of survival!”
“Yeah!”

Before I could even talk to them, they began to maneuver their boats to latch on right next to us, but I didn’t dodge them or avoid them. The hundreds of vessels present here were the first reason I didn’t face the dimensional collapse inside the Memories of the End.
“Are you the captain?”
“Yes! I am Captain Mellder of the Small Hand Clan, Viscount Yandel! We’ll trust your judgment going forward, so please give us your orders!”
“I won’t be giving orders, but I’ll ask you one thing.”
“Yes, whatever it is, I will answer to the best of my—”
“Do you have a wizard who can use Dimensional Door?”
Captain Mellder of Small Hand Clan stumbled at the desperation in my voice.
“Huh?”
Yep. No way there was one here.

chapters.title: Chapter 818: Lifeline (2)
paragraphs: I was looking for a very particular someone as we floated along, being dragged in a circle by the gargantuan whirlpool.
“Oh! Viscount Yandel! Are you here to hunt the Lord of the—”
“Dimensional Door! Any wizard who can use Dimensional Door!”
I checked each boat as we passed them, but no one gave an affirmative answer.

I’d expected as much, honestly. I knew I was grasping at straws when I executed this plan. Wizards who could cast Dimensional Door were rare. Very few schools of magic taught their wizards to use the improved spell, and even if one of their members could manage it, a rank 4 wizard could cast it only once in their life.

Plus, that was before mentioning that said precious wizards were all nearly extinct, what with how long the war against Noark had dragged on. Each school was constantly trying to nurture new wizards to take their place, but that didn’t mean anything in the here and now. A rank 4 wizard couldn’t just be created in a few years. The supply could never meet the demand.
From a certain angle, they’re the most valuable human resource available these days...

Practically every clan was desperately trying to procure wizards who could cast Dimensional Door, and even though I declared that the Anabada Clan, who didn’t take in new members, would allow an exception for a wizard who could cast Dimensional Door, none came forward.
Sure, some responded, but they were all liars who just wanted the chance to meet me.
Whatever. That wasn’t important right now.
“If Viscount Yandel is looking for a Dimensional Door wizard, then...”
“That battle fiend wants to get out? Is the Lord of Tears really that fearsome of a monster?”
“The palace! Where are the palatial soldiers? They’ll surely come when they realize a situation is at hand!”
Somehow, the crowd started speculating in the wrong direction about my intentions, maybe because I’d randomly asked around for a Dimensional Door wizard.
I wouldn’t be here doing this if I had the time, you know.

Even if I’d immediately left the Memories of the End once I’d heard about the dimensional collapse, we wouldn’t have been able to defeat the Lord of the Sixth Floor. It should go without saying. Since its first phase wasn’t done yet, we just had to ride out this whirlpool while waiting for phase two to begin.
“The rain... It stopped?”
The heavy rain that poured out from the sky stopped instantaneously, and the sky opened up once more, buffeting great winds against our vessel.
Fwoosh!
To be precise with it, the sky didn’t actually “open.” It just looked that way as light began to shine down from between the parted clouds.

As the dense clouds dissipated, harsh sunlight poured directly into the center of the whirlpool, like a spotlight on a stage. The brilliant pillar of light shone even brighter and looked more divine compared to the washed-out grays of our surroundings.
“Whoa...”
I could see the adventurers around us staring in awe as they continued getting dragged around.
Of course, not everyone was drawn in by the sight.
“Damn it...”
“What are you all doing?! Wake up!”

It may be obvious, but there couldn’t be many among the groups present who knew exactly what that pillar of light meant. Even still, rather than just gaping in awe and watching the show, some adventurers showed caution against the new phenomenon. They knew from experience that the most dangerous thing within the labyrinth was the unknown.
“Something’s coming!”
Their suspicions were proven true.
When the rain stopped and light poured out from the sky, it only meant one thing.
Shwaaaaaa!
The waves finally stopped as phase two began.
“There! Something’s coming up?”
“What the hell is that?!”
From the center of the whirlpool where the sunlight shone, the water receded, and a relatively small island revealed itself.
“The Island of Beginnings... Laemia?”
I heard the mumblings of adventurers with keen eyesight, but their guesses were incorrect. Although it was indeed called the Island of Beginnings, and its shape was very similar...
Its location is completely different.

The Island of Beginnings we knew, Laemia, was much further south than where we were and also fully submerged. Needless to say, it’d be difficult to get to at this point. If so, then the island we could see down there had to be...
Honestly, only the names differ. It’s practically the same island and is only used for raids. That, and acting as the summoning altar.
To summon the Lord of Tears, you needed to anchor your boat at this location and dive down to that island, meaning someone had summoned the Lord of the Floor on purpose. But who?

With no way of knowing, I tossed the question aside. It wasn’t something I needed to concern myself with at the moment. No matter what their plans were, they couldn’t have anticipated the soon-to-come dimensional collapse—
Uh... Wait.
Could I really be certain that they wouldn’t have expected it? Or was there a possibility that they could have?
The doubt ate at me, but I quickly dismissed it. It was just a baseless hypothesis given how little information I had.
“Captain! The ship is being dragged down!” Auyen rushed out.
Although we weren’t in full-on panic mode, I could see that everyone was nervous and worried, so I needed to calm them down first.
“It’s fine,” I answered. “Don’t worry about it.”
“Oh... I-I got scared for no reason. So nothing much is—”
“The Lord of Tears will soon show itself.”
Funnily enough, as soon as I said that, something gigantic revealed itself from behind the cliff of waves.
Splash!
It started with its wrist, elbow, shoulder, and then...even the face with the cloth over its eyes and a gag in its mouth.
“It’s the Lord of Tears!”
“W-we need to run!”
The moment it revealed itself, everything fell into chaos.
Thinking about it, it was to be expected. No adventurer present would’ve seen a monster of that size before.
“H-how big is it?”
“We need to fight that?”

It was overwhelmingly massive, incomparably taller than even the thirty-foot-tall Hipramajent. I wasn’t sure, but it was probably bigger than that super giant that I saw on Giant Island back on the first basement floor.
After all, that thing wasn’t even standing yet.
After freezing the entire sea in fear just with its entrance, it ignored us and began to crawl toward the island.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Every time its knee hit the ground, a quake erupted beneath it.

As everyone just stared at the creature while its overpowering presence made them forget to even shiver in fear, the Lord of Tears arrived at the island, then embraced the island with its arms as if protecting something precious. Having covered the entire island with its enormous body, it turned its head and looked toward us.
Whoa...
Although “gaze” would be the wrong word to use due to the bindings on its eyes, I felt chills go down my spine as I felt like our gazes met. It seemed the feeling wasn’t just limited to me either.
“Uh, Captain? What happens now?”
“Like I told you, you don’t need to worry.”
“O-oh... I s-see?”
“It’ll just try to kill us now.”
“Pardon?”

Of course, it wouldn’t actively start hunting us. Phase two was just that thing hugging the island. The problem was that even though the Lord of Tears wouldn’t move, it would start using all sorts of skills against us, and the walls of water surrounding us would start spewing out monsters to attack us.

Raven, who had been a bit quiet after that talking to from Amelia, spoke up in confusion. “Th-then aren’t we in big trouble? I heard that the Lords of the Floor from the sixth floor and up are as strong as most rank 1 monsters.”
“The Wolf of Prophecy was terrifying... Just how fearsome will that monster be?”
The members shivered at the horrific memory.
“That’s why I’m telling you not to worry.” I spoke as I stared at the Lord of Tears, who seemed to also be staring back at me while hugging the island. “It’s about time.”

I still didn’t know whether I should be relieved. Honestly, I would’ve preferred a hundred times over for my prediction to have all been wrong and for us to have to just fight the Lord of Terror today. However...
Luck was never on my side.
Time to do this.
[Final Day’s duration has expired.]
[The labyrinth has closed.]
[You are moved to Rafdo—]
[You are moved to Rafdo—]
[You are moved to Rafdo—]
[An error has occurred...]
[Failed to move you to Rafdonia.]
The bolts of lightning and meteors falling from the sky all disappeared in a moment of quiet. However, that quiet was far from peaceful.
It was the calm before the storm.
At least I was able to sense that this was the silence before the great storm slammed into us.
Crack.
It began with a small sound.
Crack!
Then a small rift appeared in the world.
Rip! Crack!
Finally, those small cracks connected and branched out like spiderwebs.
The hundreds of adventurers previously at the mercy of the currents of the Lord of Tears witnessed an abnormal event that they had never experienced before.
Craaaaaaack!
At last came one more cracking sound that echoed throughout the world.
The world shattered into thousands of pieces, and on those fragments, I could see unfamiliar faces, monsters, and locations.
A wizard hunting in the Great Demon Realm.
A large clan traveling across the Dark Continent on the seventh floor.
A small, no-name team hiking through the snowstorm on Ice Rock.
These people moved across the reflections of the thousands of fragments, like pieces of a shattered mirror.
“What the— Who’s that?!”
“Bjorn...Yandel?”
“Wait, is that the Great Ocean behind him...?”
Some even spoke in my direction.
And then, a snowflake carried on the wind drifted over before melting on the back of my hand.
This was the dimensional collapse, an ordinary world forcibly twisted and crushed by an unknown power and turned into a scrunched piece of paper.
Crack!
Another cracking sound led to the thousands of fragments shattering into millions more.
So a dimensional collapse really is happening.
Even though I knew of it beforehand, my heart was pounding away in my chest. However, in contrast to my racing heart, my thoughts slowed and honed in instantly on my duty.
“Stick close to me!” I hurriedly shouted.
All the members on the boat rushed over to me.
Shatter!
With the sound of something shattering, the world crumbled again.
“This is...”
When I regained my senses and raised my head...
[Gate of the Abyss]
...a familiar stone gate greeted me.

chapters.title: Chapter 819: Lifeline (3)
paragraphs: If someone asked me to choose the worst disaster a player could encounter while playing Dungeon and Stone, I would immediately pick a dimensional collapse without hesitation, and for one big reason alone: You had no idea what would happen to you.

When a dimensional collapse occurred, the separation between each floor became meaningless, and the portals that connected all the floors stopped functioning too. It was as if all the tiles on the map turned into random portals. Whenever you pressed a movement key in the game—so every time you took a step in any direction—the surrounding area changed, and you were teleported to a random area in the labyrinth.
Ba-dump!
And that was why it wasn’t completely unbelievable that this was where I found myself.
[Gate of the Abyss]
Ba-dump!
Even though I had only ever seen it as a 2D sprite in the game, I could instinctively recognize that familiar stone gate.
The Gate of the Abyss...
The hope and dream of the evil spirits dragged into this otherworld and the place that led Baekho Lee to burn his life down in flames for a slim chance to open it.
[You have discovered the Gate of the Abyss.]

The moment this gate suddenly appeared before me, my mind went blank, but not because it was bereft of thoughts. It was more like I couldn’t focus on any single thought because of how many were firing off at once.
Ba-dump!
What were the chances that I would land in front of the Gate of Abyss, considering all those areas from the first floor to the tenth floor in this vast labyrinth?
Ba-dump!
Was this a hidden secret that I didn’t know about? No, more importantly, what would happen if I took a step forward and opened the gate?
Ba-dump!
What about the Earth Witch who told me not to open it?
What about the Palace that was definitely hiding some secret from me?
Ba-dump!
Did I not need to care about any of that? Would everything come to an end the moment I opened that gate? Would I really be able to return to my original world, just as Auril Gavis said?
Then again, that wasn’t what I wanted...
Ba-dump!
Thoughts immediately swirled through my mind, but the ending had already been decided.
It doesn’t matter, anyway...

All sorts of traps littered the area in front of the Gate of the Abyss. The moment I stepped beyond the tile I was currently on, I would face potential extermination. Not to mention, I didn’t know exactly which tile I had ended up on. The sheer fact that I had landed on a safe tile among the thousands here was something I needed to be grateful for.
That was what I should be feeling. But maybe, just maybe. If I could just get lucky once in my life and run up to that gate while only stepping on the safe tiles, what would happen?
“Yandel.”
Just then, Amelia’s voice dragged me back to reality.
“Just what are you thinking so hard about? You’ve been ignoring me.”
Ah, she was trying to talk to me. “Sorry,” I said after shaking myself out of it. “I just got distracted for a moment.”
“I don’t know what you were thinking, but you need to stay focused from this moment on. The dimensional collapse has begun, just like you said it would.”
“Understood.”
I just barely managed to wrench my attention away from the door, and when I looked back, I could see my clan members looking around on high alert.
Alright, there doesn’t seem to be anyone who was left behind...
“I can’t sense any monsters nearby.”
“That’s a relief to hear...but I have no idea where we are.”
“But...was there a place like this in the labyrinth?”
“I don’t know. I’ve never been to a place like this, at least.”

Although talk about what this place could be was beginning to circulate, I only told them to stay close and not stray too far without any additional explanation. There was no reason to cause a commotion by going out of my way to tell them that it was the Gate of the Abyss.
“...Mr. Parav? Do you know?”
“Haha, I have no idea either.”

As a player, Sven Parav definitely would’ve recognized the Gate of the Abyss, but he was acting dumb just like I was to avoid drawing any unnecessary suspicion. Although more people than just I knew the truth now, that only applied to the people closest to me, the ones I could trust most. Most of the members here didn’t know of my true identity.
It’s not like staying quiet will do us any harm, so there’s no need for me to step up. It’s not like we’re going to be here for long.
Like the universe had heard my thoughts, there was a blinding flash of light, and our surrounding area changed once more, replacing the darkness around us with bright light and cold, cutting winds.
Ice Rock this time...
I had arrived in the place where I had once fought for my life.
I took in the cold winds battering against my skin, recalling the declaration I made in this place.
But first, I need to check on the members.
I quickly looked around and did a headcount. Thankfully, no one was separated this time either.
“Mister!”
“Yandel!”
However, this time, a monster had appeared.
A monster right in front of us.
“Kyaaaaaak!”

The beast-type monster charged us right as I finished my count of the clan members. However, before the monster’s open jaws could reach me, Erwen fired an arrow that pierced straight through its neck. With a whooshing hiss, it disappeared in a burst of light, leaving behind a mana stone.
“A manticore?” someone mumbled in a daze.
It was the rank 5 monster that dropped the Leap, which was a personal favorite of mine.
Everyone was confused by its appearance.
“Why is that thing here?”
“Wait... Maybe we’re not at Ice Rock?”
No way. We definitely were at Ice Rock. There was a reason for that manticore’s sudden and unusual appearance.

“It’s because of the dimensional collapse,” Raven piped up. “Just like how we suddenly arrived here when we were on the sixth floor just a moment ago, that monster was also dragged here without being able to resist.”
Since Raven explained in my stead, I didn’t need to speak up again.

“By the way, everyone heard what Mr. Yandel said before, right? Everyone, come here. Even if we have monsters appearing around us, we need to stick together, as closely as we can. If you don’t, you might end up falling into a place all by—”
Flash!
“...yourself?”
Wow, it wasn’t even giving us time to talk.

When we opened our eyes this time, we were in a jungle with dense foliage. However, there were no other distinguishing features we could pick out, so it was difficult to say where we were. When we noticed how dark our surroundings were and took a closer look at the trees, though...
“It’s the Great Forest. On the seventh-floor Dark Continent.”

Of course, it didn’t really matter where exactly we were. This was a dimensional collapse. We weren’t going to be here for long, anyway. The real problem wasn’t our location, but what we could encounter here.
“Ready for combat!”
Unlike before, as soon as we opened our eyes, the monsters around us charged as if they had been waiting for us.
[You have defeated a Dead Bun.]
[You have defeated a Red Eye.]
[You have defeated an Ironrock Hill Guardian Soldier.]
[You have defeated an Orc Sorcerer...]
Thankfully, since the monsters were low-rank, our battles didn’t take that long.
Maybe that was why it happened.
“This dimensional collapse thing is easier than I thought?”
That damn guild master ended up planting a death flag. Every time someone said something like that, something worse was bound to happen.
“Shut up. It hasn’t even truly begun yet,” I snapped.
“Haha, there’s no need to say that—”
“Is this insubordination?”
“No, haha... It’s nothing like that—”

Before he could even finish, I punched the guild master straight in the face. While I held back because it was just a warning shot, the guild master still seemed shocked at being hit out of seemingly nowhere.

I stared him down and made myself clear. “It’s only been three minutes since the dimensional collapse began, but you think it’ll be easy? I don’t care if you think like that in your mind, but never speak it out loud again. I worry that your rotten mental state will infect the others.”
“Wait, that wasn’t my intention—”
“Then what was your intention? What if we hadn’t faced low-rank monsters, huh? What if it were a rank 1? Or even just a rank 2 monster? Then—”

I couldn’t continue my lecture before another flash of light engulfed us and changed the scenery—and then we were at the Dark Continent once more. Judging by the bones scattered about, we must have been at the entrance to the path into the Dragon Pit.
A Bone Dragonian.
There was no point in shouting out a direction, as the rank 3 monster just appeared right in the center of our formation.
Well, maybe “appeared” wasn’t the correct word to use? From its perspective, it’d look as if we were the ones who suddenly appeared and surrounded it.
“Kyaaaaaaak!”
“Behel—LAAAAAAAA!”
Before it could go on a rampage, I immediately jumped onto its body and tried to wrestle it into submission.
What the hell, already?
Although it had only been a few seconds since we were transferred, another flash of light blanketed us.
This time, I had no idea where we were. No, to be precise, I didn’t have the luxury of taking the time to assess our surroundings.
I was too busy suppressing the Bone Dragonian that had followed us.
“What are you doing?! Kill this thing already!”
“There are monsters outside the formation as well!”
“Team 2, take care of the monsters outside! We’ll deal with the Bone Dragonian!”

Thankfully, Amelia gave the orders in my stead to quickly and cleanly deal with the situation, and we continued our battle. However, before we could finish off the Bone Dragonian, our field changed once more. It was one of the most annoying parts about a dimensional collapse.
Argh, it’s too hectic.

It was like an infinite monster wave simulator. Our terrain changed constantly, and monsters rushed us at the same time. Of course, we wouldn’t have any problem if we could deal with them before the next jump...
Flash!
But when it took too long to deal with a rank 2 or a rank 3 monster, we needed to begin the next wave with the prior handicap in place, just like now.
“It’s another rank 3 monster!”
“We’ll deal with the Bone Dragonian first!”
The world continued to flicker in and out as our battles stretched on endlessly. Still, we were on the lucky side for now. We hadn’t encountered any rank 1 or rank 2 monsters yet.
Flash!
We even encountered reinforcements.
“Anabada Clan?”
“We’ll deal with the rest, so you guys take that side!”
“Oh— Alright!”

I recognized them as the Red Steel Clan from their insignia. There had been forty-two of them when they entered the labyrinth, but now, there were only eighteen of them left. Apparently, they hadn’t stuck as close to each other during the dimensional collapse as we had.
“Ah— Ahhh!”
One of the Red Steel Clan members rolled to the side to dodge a monster attack, and in the next instant, the man’s body disappeared as if he had rolled into an invisible portal.
“Damn it! Johnson got taken!”
“Don’t go! Shit, it’s already too late!”

This was another trait of the dimensional collapse. Although we couldn’t see them, we were surrounded by walls. The moment anyone crossed one of those invisible walls, they would be transported to a different area without any flashes of light, and unless they were extremely lucky, getting back to their original location was practically impossible.
[You have defeated a Frost Wolf.]
[You have defeated an Ice Golem.]
[You have defeated a Beldinos. EXP +7]
[You have defeated a Storm Gush.]
[You have defeated an Orc Hero.]
Still, thanks to the addition of the other clan who had been swept up in the dimensional collapse, we were able to slowly but surely deal with all the monsters that came our way.
We got a bit of time to catch our breath...
“It’s fate that we met like this. Let us at least introduce—”
Damn it.
Without any time to rest, there was another flash of light, and we were separated from the Red Steel Clan without any goodbyes, since they were standing a little ways away from us.
[You have defeated an Akeltas.]
[You have defeated a Slayer Knight. EXP +7]
[You have defeated a Garcian.]
[You have defeated a Luture Talismancer...]

This process continued on for a while. The field would change with a flash of light, which exposed us to new monsters, and when the flash came again, the monsters we weren’t able to kill followed us and kept piling on.
Grrrrrk!
Once, we were summoned into the middle of the deep sea and had to fight harder than we had ever fought before.
“Hold on for a little longer!”
We spent so long sticking close to each other and trying to endure the crushing currents.
“I don’t think I see any more of them.”
“I-is it over?”
Even though we defeated all the monsters around us, the world didn’t flash white. I hadn’t noticed because of how hectic everything had been.
I let out the breath I’d been holding in. “How long has it been since our last teleportation?”
“Uh... I think it’s been around ten minutes...?”
Okay, in that case...
“Oh, is that the end of it? It’s easier than I thought!” Ainar cheered unthinkingly.

I was about to tell her off, arguing that she didn’t know a thing, but I just let it slide since I had more important things to think about. I even ignored the guild master who looked at me with a pitiful expression as if I’d wronged him, and instead just picked up a pebble off the ground and tossed it.
The stone that I threw skittered across the ground, plopping and rolling and not disappearing or falling to the ground in the distance.
“Is it... Is it over?”
I nodded at Raven’s question. “Yeah.”
The first wave had completed.
Foreshock, mainshock, aftershock. Just like how earthquakes could be divided into these three stages, the dimensional collapse also had multiple stages of collapse.
We’re between two different waves.
It was a temporary period of safety, designated the Blank Period.
“From the records left behind by those who survived a dimensional collapse, this Blank Period was always of different lengths, but they were at least eight hours each,” Raven explained.
“Then...can we just rest now?”
“Well, if nothing happens before then.”
“Huh? Didn’t you say this was that Blank Period or whatever?”
At Ainar’s question, Raven gave a wry smile and shrugged. “If it was going to be that peaceful, it would’ve been named Rest Period instead of Blank Period.”
“Oh, I see! Explain it to me in simple terms!”

“...Although we’re better off than before, we’re still in danger. We have no idea where we are, and all sorts of monsters would’ve been dumped onto this floor as well. There might be a rank 1 monster wandering around here—if not worse.”
I smirked, ignoring the fact that she was able to stay so calm while saying something so terrifying, and took a look around. “Raven, do you really not know where we are?”
“What? Oh!”
Only then did she seem to recognize it.
“The Burning Forest!”
It was a place that was somewhat special to us.
The Burning Forest was the field that allowed entry into the special field Mirror of Fire through the use of the remains of a Mila Roden that appeared on the fifth-floor Great Demon Realm.
[You have activated Orb of Fire.]
It was also the place where I obtained my Orb of Fire, which I was using even now.
“From what I can tell...you don’t plan on sitting down and resting.”
“Eight hours is too long to waste on just resting. If we meet another group of adventurers, we could team up with them too.”
“Well...that is true.”
After catching our breaths somewhat, I led my members toward the Burning Forest, the acquisition point of the Orb of Fire.
It’ll be useful to have one more on layaway since we’re operating as two teams now.
As we traveled, we continued to encounter monsters that we would’ve never encountered here that blocked our path, but none of them were too threatening.
Fwoosh!
The continuous fire damage also wasn’t to the point where I needed to worry about it. The Orb of Fire was good enough even without Cold Blood to stack on top of it.
“We’re nearly there.”

As we passed by the trees into the heart of the Burning Forest, a huge monolith revealed itself. For note, this obelisk was only a landmark and didn’t have any special function in the game. That was why I only used it as a guidepost when looking for the hut where the Orb of Fire lay dormant.
“But was it always this white?”
It seemed I wasn’t the only one who thought something was off.
“I think something’s written on it as well...”
Hearing what Raven said, I approached the stone to look at it a little closer. “Huh?”
A woman appeared from the side of the monolith, wearing clothes that were way too ordinary-looking to be mistaken for adventurers’ gear.
“(Uwaaaaaah!)”
She was holding an infant who was crying their heart out.
“(You were here? I’ve been looking for you!)”
A man appeared from behind them to call for the woman...
“(Let’s go home already, Tarvian!)”
...and astonishingly called her by a name that I was familiar with.

chapters.title: Chapter 820: Lifeline (4)
paragraphs: Tarvian, Tarvian, Tarvian...
Where had I heard that name before? Why was it so familiar to me?
“Those two... What are they saying?”
While I was standing, observing the man and the woman, Raven’s question pierced through the dazed fog of my mind, and only then did I realize it.
Oh... They were speaking in the ancient language.
Although Raven could read it, her listening and speaking of the language weren’t up to par.
“(Wait. Let’s just wait here for a little longer. You don’t know... maybe someone will be here...)”
“(Travian. In this world, no one... Hah... Yeah, sure. Let’s wait a little bit before going back.)”
The three of them existed despite all rationale and reason, perhaps even as a mystery on a different playing field than even this bizarre-looking obelisk.

“They’re wearing regular clothes, use the ancient language, and are even holding an infant... Just who are those people?” Raven pressed. This time, I could sense something beyond her initial caution—fear. I didn’t blame her, though. Fearing the unknown was a very human reaction.
“Hmm, I don’t think they’re ordinary adventurers...”
“Maybe they’re an Achievement of Gabrielius?”
“How many of these have I experienced after following Viscount Yandel into the labyrinth?!”
I couldn’t tell if that last one was the guild master’s muttering to himself in joy or in regret, but I quieted everyone down. “I understand that everyone’s curious, but stand down for now.”

If we were too noisy, they could detect us. Thankfully, it didn’t seem their senses were heightened enough to have discovered us, so I just continued listening in on their conversation. Not that they had a lot to say. The woman just clutched her child close as she stared up at the stone monument while the young man looked at her with a bit of sadness in his eyes. When the baby cried, the woman consoled and calmed them down, and a conflicted expression stole through the man’s eyes as she did so.
“(...Let’s go back now, Zephyros.)”
Zephyros? Why did that name also sound familiar?
I was starting to get frustrated with trying to figure out where I’d heard of them.
But just then, a thought struck me like a bolt from the blue. However, since I wasn’t completely certain yet...
“Raven.”
“Yes?”
“Do you remember the names Tarvian and Zephyros?”
“Hmm... Not really?”
“There was that one diary we found in the cabin where we obtained the Orb of Fire.”
“Hmm? Oh, that diary! That’s right! I think those two were the names that were in that diary!”
“Lower your voice a little.”
“...So, why are you suddenly bringing it up?”
Oh, that? “It seems their names are Tarvian and Zephyros,” I answered flatly.
Raven took a moment before shouting out in surprise. “Ehhhhh?!”
Whoops. They probably heard that one.
I quickly shut her mouth with my hand and turned my head to look at the man and woman.
“(Zephyros, did you hear that?)”
The two, who had been on their way elsewhere, suddenly turned around in our direction, wary and on guard. Thanks to us crouching down between the burning trees, we fortunately weren’t spotted.
Ba-dump, ba-dump...
However, moments like these were always the most nerve-wracking when playing hide-and-seek.
Okay, but why am I even scared? Wouldn’t it be better if I just walked out to talk to them? It’d save time too, hmm...
“(We need to go check. Maybe there’s a survivor!)”
“(It must have been a demon who made that sound. Let’s go already.)”
“(The day will soon come to an end. Let’s go.)”
They concluded the sound must have come from “a demon” and turned around to head off.
“Looks like we won’t need to wander around this time,” I mused.
“What?”
“If we just follow them, we’ll arrive at that cabin where we got the Orb of Fire.”
Raven shot me a sidelong look and remained silent.
Did I sound too much like a villain just then?

The two-story stone cabin was situated in the middle of the forest. I had visited it both in the game and in reality, and unlike the stone monument, I could immediately tell the difference between the two versions the moment I saw it.

A whirring dome was shielding the building, producing a similar effect to the one produced by the Orb of Fire. Inside, the walls of the house were clean without a single blemish, and the wooden entrance also showed no signs of having been burned down, looking very well-kept. And on top of all that...
They’re living a pretty good life.
A single tree was growing in their small yard. It seemed to have been planted recently, as the tree was very small.
“Raven, do you remember the contents of the diary we read inside that house back then?”
“Give me a second. I think I wrote it down back then. Somewhere in my subspace... Oh, right... Here!”
Day 192. The rescue team did not come today either. Now, there are only three of us left in the expedition. Tarvian suggested building a house, and I agreed. Demon meat tasted disgusting, as usual...
No.
Day 271. A decent-looking house was comp...
No.
What’s the point of living when the world has ended, you ask? Even if everything burns down, there is still hope. As proof, we are still...
I didn’t care for the whining, so to just summarize the important parts...
Day 467. Tarvian is pregnant. Whose child could it be?
Day 672. No, 673? I don’t know, but something big happened. The Orb of Fire began to lose its power. Already, the outer walls are getting scorched by fire.
Only the wizard, Tarvian, can fix it. But even if she sacrifices her life to prolong the duration, what meaning is there?
Day 711. At long last, Zephyros and I agreed on something. Today, we die.
If the world has not ended by the witch’s hand and if someone, someday, finds this place, I hope you use the object in the basement to save the world...
Hmm, although I said they were important parts, these diary entries didn’t have anything that useful in them, so I decided to just use them as a reference.
“Erwen, can you overhear the conversation they’re having inside?”
“I can hear them...But I can’t understand what they’re saying.”
Oh. Right. They spoke in the ancient language.
Then what should we do now?
We did follow them all the way here, but I had no idea what I needed to do from this point on.
Should I just continue observing them?

It was the easiest choice available to us, but I was worried about our situation. After the Blank Period passed, we’d get swept up in the dimensional collapse once more. We’d already spent quite a bit of time coming all the way here, and the other members needed to rest for what time we had left.
“I’ll be right back,” I announced.
“What?”
“I’ll go and check by myself, so keep an eye out from here. Don’t do anything unless I call for you first.”
A few members looked at me as if to ask if I really needed to go over there, but it didn’t take long for me to convince them.
“From the situation, it’s clear that they’re an Achievement of Gabrielius... If we get lucky, we might be able to obtain something that’ll help us get through this predicament.”
“Still... If I sense that you’re in danger, I will act.”
“Got it. I’ll trust you.”
With that sorted, I steadied my breathing and headed toward the house.
The barrier whirred. It truly did seem to have the same functionality as the Orb of Fire. Even though it worked well in keeping the flame out, it offered up no resistance to me passing through.

Although I went out of my way not to hide my presence, I couldn’t hear anyone or anything being alerted from inside the house. Were their levels so low that they couldn’t even detect me? Or was it simply because they weren’t on guard against someone potentially invading their home?
I didn’t know, but soon enough, I was stepping up to the threshold of their door and gingerly lifting my hand.
Knock, knock, knock.

There came the sound of something crashing, and the conversation inside abruptly cut off. Clearly, they were startled. I didn’t agitate them any further than that and just waited in front of the door.
Soon enough, I felt a presence peek through the window next to me. So they were trying to observe me through that...
“(We...open...? Maybe...expedition...)”
“(It...be...demon...rather...ambush...I...)”
“(Fire...for...talk...later...hide...)”
Because of how quietly they were speaking, I couldn’t pick out their words.
Not looking directly at them might be best.
I acted like I couldn’t sense their presence either and grabbed the door knocker once more, knocking three times before speaking in the ancient language.
“(Anyone home?)”
I purposefully spoke to tell them that I was a conversable entity. This seemed to help a lot as I heard a response from beyond the door.
“(...Who are you?)”
Hmm, well... How should I respond to get the best reaction? If I said I came here to take the Orb of Fire, it would probably lead to a battle.
“(D-did you perhaps...see the signal? To save us...?)”
“(Signal?)” I echoed.
“(The mana wave emitter. Did you not see one on your way here? There were a few set up around the area...)”
Oh, was he talking about that monolith? So that was what it was, something like a radio tower.
“(Who... Who are you? Are you the rescue party?)”
Perhaps suspicious of my answer, the voice that spoke next was audibly more guarded.
Inwardly, I clicked my tongue, debating how to introduce myself.
“(I’m not from the rescue party,)” I replied eventually. Since it was obvious I would be found out if I lied, I decided to answer the question truthfully.

Immediately, I picked up on the resulting disappointed sigh. They had apparently still held onto hope despite their raised suspicions. I didn’t give the man any time to think and asked in return, “(By the way...are you from the expedition party?)”
“(Y-you know of us?)”
“(Somewhat.)”
I pulled from my memory of what I’d read in the diary, matching the details of their story as closely as possible. As a result, they seemed to come to the conclusion that I wasn’t their enemy.

“(By the way, could you open the door so we can chat? I have no intention of hurting you.)” When they didn’t respond, I added, “(You should know that I have no problem breaking the door down since I came all the way here without issue.)”
Even while saying that, I tried as carefully as I could not to make it sound like a threat, and my good intentions seemed to have reached them, as the door slowly creaked open a moment later.
“(P-please come in.)”
A man opened the door and guided me inside—the man named Zephyros, whom I had seen before. Given how I couldn’t see anyone else, he must have told the other two to hide.

Slowly, Zephyros began, “(If you’re not from the rescue party, just who are you? And how did you come to find this place when there are demons all over the place? Did the world... Could it be that it hasn’t ended yet?)”

Questions peppered me as soon as I entered. This was probably the reason that he let an utter stranger like me into his home. He was more desperate for a conversation than I was. Talking with another person was a potential lifeline that had found him in this world of despair.
Hah... Still, though, how should I answer him?

After thinking for a second, I decided to dodge his question. I had already personally experienced quite a lot of the story regarding the empire, and I’d heard the important parts from Arta not long ago as well. I could deceive him if we kept the conversation short.
“(Answer me, please! H-has the world not ended yet?!)”
“(...No, it hasn’t ended yet.)”
“(Oh, by the gods—!)”
“(Have you perhaps heard of Rafdonia?)”
“(I have! My best friend was from that territory! But why do you ask?)”
Damn, as I thought. This was the exact era and time I’d suspected it was.
Alright, looks like he’s taken the bait.
I went for a bold move in my story. “(Currently, all the survivors from across the world are gathering there to form a new kingdom.)”
“(How?! What about the curse? What are they doing about the curse?)”
“(The Witch’s curse cannot cross over into Rafdonia. That land is the final citadel.)”
“(I-is that true?! Then please take us there! Please!)”
In his excitement, he mistakenly revealed the others by saying “we,” but I didn’t pay it too much mind and continued, “(Hmm, well...)”
As I put my hand on my chin and looked down at him, he gulped in nervousness.
“(I cannot take someone I do not know there. You could do things that harm the territory instead.)”
Now, the roles had shifted.
“(N-no! We’re from the expedition! There’s no way we’d—!)”
“(Then tell me. Tell me everything that happened to you until now.)”
Alright. Let’s hear that story of yours.

chapters.title: Chapter 821: Lifeline (5)
paragraphs: Where should I begin...?

When the man began his story with that, I immediately cut him off and told him the answer plainly: from the very beginning. No reason to worry about a little bit of summarizing here or there, just tell me everything about your life.
It wasn’t a typical ask, of course, but under these special circumstances where I was practically interviewing him, it was plausible enough.
“(The Imperial Western Front. That is where I was born and raised.)”

Zephyros was part of the generation born at the end of the continental age when the war with the Witch was at its peak. To put it another way, he was born when the world didn’t have long until its end.
“(My mother joined the war as a nurse officer, and my father was an ordinary soldier.)”
Battles were waged every day, and every time one of those battles occurred, he lost someone close to him. His parents weren’t exempt from that brutal list.

“(When I became an orphan at eleven, I immediately volunteered for the army. I wasn’t motivated by anything like anger against the monsters or a sense of patriotism. It was just the only thing I could do—the only thing I knew how to do.)”

Fortunately, he was talented in the art of warfare. From a foot soldier to a unit leader, from a unit leader to a centurion... With every subsequent battle, he gained more of a reputation for his achievements and quickly rose up the ranks.
“(Well, it’s not so much that I accomplished anything great, but really that the people above me continued to die out one by one. I just happened to be able to fill that empty station.)”
Although that was how he saw it, I took his words to mean he was being humble. Honestly, even if it was odd to say, the fact that he survived meant that he was strong.

“(As you know, the situation out there isn’t good. The western front, where I grew up, was pushed until we just couldn’t possibly maintain that battleline any longer. In the end, we were absorbed into the central forces.)”
Even in this new environment, however, he did his absolute best to survive, and he continued to grow stronger.

“(Thankfully, there were many paths I could take. Since the world was coming to an end, we didn’t have any additional ladders we needed to climb. The martial arts of the ancient and historical dukedom, magic, even the crafting techniques that were passed down to specific units... All of them were things any common soldier could study.)”
Over time, Zephyros started to make a name for himself, and just as he began to receive some recognition from his higher-ups...

“(I heard a rumor that an expedition force was to be created. Naturally, I volunteered. You’re asking if it was because of the loathing I felt for the monsters? Well, I won’t deny it played some part in it. If I could, I would immediately go and rip apart that Witch and create a world where monsters like this didn’t exist. But...)”
The true reason that Zephyros joined the expedition force was because of one single sentence.

“(I heard that if this expedition succeeded, this war would end. That was enough for me. I was honestly getting pretty sick of this life of death and death alone. And I didn’t have a choice either. The world was already heading for its doom. I needed to do whatever I could.)”
And so, Zephyros joined the expedition force and headed out in hopes of saving the world.
“(The first destination of the expedition force was that cave where everything began. There, we defeated the First Lord of the Witch’s army.)”
“(And by the First Lord, you mean...)”
“(Dreadfear. That murderous monster. That thing born of an unexplainable mutation from consuming that transformative drug... The one that even the Witch wasn’t able to save.)”
A transformative drug. One that even the Witch wasn’t able to save...
While I didn’t know enough to understand everything he said, I certainly recognized one thing.
Dreadfear...
The Lord of the First Floor, given the title of Terror.
I had a few things I wanted to ask Zephyros, but I held back and continued to listen to his story.
“(But why do you ask about that? It’s as if this is the first time you’re hearing about the First Lord...)”
Because if I didn’t, he would begin to doubt my identity if I asked him something I should obviously know. There was a chance that his entire conversation could crumble if I made a mistake.
“(It’s nothing. Continue talking,)” I urged, waiting him out as he hesitated.
“(Well... Sure.)”
Zephyros talked for a while after that.
“(After defeating the First Lord, our next goal was to defeat the Second Lord. For that, we split our expedition force into four groups and each headed to different areas.)”
The Rock Desert. The Goblin Forest. The Den of Beasts. The Land of the Dead.
After heading to those four locations, the expedition force fought a fierce battle and was finally able to defeat the Lord of Regret in the end.
“(After that, we arrived at the Witch’s Hut. Then, as planned, we succeeded in fooling the Third Lord and summoning him too.)”

By that point, I didn’t even need to ask him leading questions. Although I had no idea how the two were connected, the route of the expedition force lined up with the route up the floors of the labyrinth.

“(The battle itself wasn’t difficult. As planned, we defeated the Third Lord...and we left to go defeat the Fourth. The ‘Tower in the Sky,’ they call it. That’s what those blasted pilgrims, who treat the earth and the sky the same, called it. To praise the Witch, they said, even though the building led into the ground. It’s not widely known, but that tower was constructed by the empire. They dug deep into the ground to seal the Evil God there and put a gatekeeper to watch over the seal. Well, in the end, the territory was taken over by the Witch and her pilgrims, who renamed it instead. In any case, the Fourth Lord was a very difficult enemy.)”
Zephyros shivered, as if just thinking about the Fourth Lord was enough to make him feel fear. Even so, the story continued with the expedition force defeating the Lord of the Heavenly Sky.
“(We then arrived at our final destination: the Great Demon Realm.)”
Only at this point did I learn the expedition’s true goal.
“(We went there to kill the Fifth Lord, Siliut, for the crime of betraying the empire and serving the Witch, and then to seal the Evil God once more. And after that, to kill the Witch.)”

However, that goal couldn’t be accomplished. After entering the Great Demon Realm, he and his group members were separated from the expedition force during combat, and after a few more died off, he had no choice but to sit around here and wait for a rescue party.
“(That is my story. Even I don’t think it’s that interesting.)”
“(I have a few questions,)” I began once he had finished.
“(Go for it. It seems my life is currently in your hands.)”
“(Why do you believe that the world ended? From what I could tell, all that happened to you was your team getting separated from the others.)”
“(That expedition force was the final hope of humanity. And if that expedition succeeded, this sea of fire that surrounds this building would’ve disappeared as well. The expedition failed.)”

The world ending just because the expedition failed... It was proof of how dire the situation had truly been and how the empire had brainwashed the expedition force before sending them out for their mission.
Then, Zephyros hesitantly asked for confirmation. “(Am I wrong?)”
I let a bitter laugh escape me. Oh, the expedition probably had failed in the end. However...
They wouldn’t have failed in the Great Demon Realm.
First floor, second floor, third floor, fourth floor, fifth floor... The route the expedition force had taken was in line with the floors of the labyrinth.
No, I suspected that the expedition had continued on for a while.

Past the Great Demon Realm, they would’ve set out into the open ocean, then gone past the Dark Continent and defeated the one called “Lord” in Ice Rock. They would’ve then made their way through the Land of Dawn and the Tomb of Stars and even reached the Abyss.
So what in the world happened?
