In the end, I was left disappointed, knowing I would not get to hear those stories from Zephyros, the man left behind on the fifth floor.
“(Tell me... Did the expedition fail?)”
“(You will naturally learn of it when you leave,)” I answered shortly. “(Alright, then I’ll ask the second question.)”
“(What are these Lords?)”
It was something that had caught my attention while listening to his story. Just what were these beings called Lords? I awaited his answer in anticipation.
“(How does this question help prove that I won’t be of harm to Rafdonia?)”
Well, that was true. But...
I widened my shoulders and glared down at him to intimidate him. “(Are you talking back?)”
“(No...)” Zephyros squeaked, hunching into himself a little more. “(It’s not that I don’t want to answer, but I have no idea why you’re asking me this question.)”
“(I’m not expecting you to understand. You just need to answer my question.)”
“(Is this...a test?)”
A test, huh? Not a bad assumption.
When I just stood my ground and stared down at him, he couldn’t bear the pressure and ended up speaking first.

“(I still don’t know what this is about, but I’ll tell you everything I know. The Lords... They are ‘pilgrims’ born through the authority of the Witch, and they possess power that exceeds the laws of the world. More than exceeds the natural laws—they can ignore them. However, not everyone agrees on how they were created. Even just the First Lord is a point of contention. Having been a prisoner of war, the imperial army forced him to consume a drug that would destroy his mind and body, then be reborn into a new living weapon. But for some reason...it went on a rampage and became the first among the Lords instead. They never leave their own territories, and since they’re practically the kings of those areas, they were named as the Lords of the Witch’s army. The Second, the Fourth, and the Fifth Lords obeyed the Witch with unquestioning loyalty while the First and the Third Lords were just murderous monsters moving on instinct, not making a distinction between friend and foe. Some even suggested that birth of the Lords was instigated by the Witch. And that they were created because the Witch wasn’t able to fully control the powers she possessed. That is all I know...)”

“(I see...)” The explanation he gave me was all over the place, but it didn’t seem like he had a concrete understanding of the lords either. “(Third question. Why did the expedition force go after the Lords and the Evil God?)”
“(Isn’t that obvious? The Lords were made to protect the Witch, and the Evil God is the Witch’s ally. But the way you asked that... Is there perhaps something that I don’t know?)”
I clicked my tongue. This guy kept parrying my questions with his own.
I’ll just ignore him.
“(Final question. Are you alone here?)”
Zephyros shut his mouth tight as a wary expression fell over his face.
He’s doubting me after all this time...

Well, I could understand why. Even though he decided to put his trust in me, he couldn’t make that decision for the others. He was hesitating out of concern for his allies, not wanting to make a reckless decision and bring them harm.
Finally, after a long pause, Zephyros began to speak. “(I—)”

“(He’s not alone,)” another man said, cutting Zephyros off as he appeared from above the stairs. The man looked to be more than six feet tall and in his mid-thirties, sporting a messy beard and stark facial features that made him look even stronger. I didn’t recognize him, but I did feel a sense of connection with him.
Zephyros is in front of me, Tarvian is a woman, and since he’s not a baby...
There was only one person left after the process of elimination.
“(Do excuse me, but I heard everything you said during the conversation from above.)”
He was the author of the diary.
“(Greetings. I am Ormi Noark.)”
...Huh?
My brain short-circuited at those two familiar names combined into one, but then rebooted itself nearly instantly.
The Ormi Revolutionary Corps and Noark...
“(For your reference, I am the one from Rafdonia that he was talking about.)”
And Rafdonia on top of all that?
This is getting very interesting.
There was no such thing as a coincidence.

chapters.title: Chapter 822: Lifeline (6)
paragraphs: Ormi Noark was a part of the expedition force and had ended up trapped in the burning Great Demon Realm after being separated from the main force with his two allies.
And I knew how he would die.
Day 711. At long last, Zephyros and I agreed on something. Today, we die.
In the end, this entire group would greet death in despair.
“(Do you know who I am?)”

The moment I realized the author of that diary was named Ormi Noark, my thoughts took a different turn. What if he didn’t die on that day? What if he escaped this place, reached the city of Rafdonia to create the Ormi Revolutionary Corps sometime later, and then ultimately succeeded in constructing the underground city of Noark?
Is that too much of a leap in logic?

Maybe, but I couldn’t just ignore the theory either. In the end, imagination was just a combination of accrued data. My imagination had created this plausible theory the moment I heard the name Ormi Noark and the keyword Rafdonia.
There are some inconsistencies, though.

The Ormi Revolutionary Corps and the city of Noark didn’t have a lot of history with them. At most, they’d been around for a few hundred years before our present time. There was an immense gap in time between this ancient era and the current world.
“(No, I don’t,)” I answered firmly. “(I thought I’d heard about you once before...but I don’t remember.)”
In the end, I decided to dig for more information. It was clear there was some connection between this man, Noark, and the Ormi Revolutionary Corps.
“(Hmm, it makes sense if you came from Rafdonia. Our family is one of the oldest vassal families of Rafdonia, so you may have interacted with one of the people of my family.)”

I could see the intense desire burning in Ormi Noark’s eyes when he said it, too—an unyielding will of sorts, to return alive no matter what. Of course, that didn’t snuff out all of his lingering doubts.

“(But...is it true that Rafdonia survived? That it became the sole citadel that stopped the Witch’s curse?)” He spoke as if he still couldn’t believe my words, but then quickly continued, “(Take us there, quickly! I wish to confirm it with my own eyes—)”
“(I have not finished my verification test.)”
“(Is there a need for that? If that man is still the lord, I’m certain he’ll welcome me with open arms when I—!)”

“(That is your opinion,)” I sternly cut him off. The man became flustered, not knowing how to respond. Seeing his reaction, I calmly asked him another question. “(What is the name of the lord of Rafdonia?)”
To be honest, I’d asked because I wasn’t sure myself. However, he seemed to think it was a confirmation question, so he gave me the answer I wanted.
“(Ravigion Kommelby Rafdonia.)”
Oh, so the Immortal was still the ruler.

As I checked another theory off my mental list as confirmed, he carried on to say, “(Any question will do. I will answer them all. So please, let us... No. No, we’re fine. There is a mother with her young child. Just those two. Please take them to Raf—)”

Suddenly, he cut himself off before he could speak the full name. An uncanny sense of unease fell over me as the silence settled between us. No, it was more than just unease. Something was off. His pleading voice and sorrowful expression had been wiped away completely, and now, he just stared at me.
I shot a glance at Zephyros, only to find the same was true for him as well.
As if time had stopped, the two men in front of me went deadly quiet and just looked at me with a blank expression. Like two broken robots.
Ba-dump!
In unexpected situations, my instinct always leaped before my reason. Rather than analyzing the situation I was in, my hand jumped to my shield, ready to lift it at any moment.
And then, the moment I entered my combat-ready stance, he spoke.
“Stop.”
The words were not in the ancient language we had been communicating in this entire time but in the Rafdonian language.
“I understand that you didn’t intend on coming here, but do not make fools out of these people any more than you already have.”
Ba-dump!
As the low beat of my heart thumped in my ears, I slowly parted my lips. Although I had no idea what had just happened...
“Who are you?”
His character had just changed.

The man didn’t immediately answer my question. Instead, he merely stared at me for a good long while as he collected his thoughts. Eventually, he revealed, “If you go into the basement, you will find the Orb of Fire. With that, it will empower the Orb of Fire you already possess by another step.”
Oh, there was an effect like that?

While I was still marveling a little at that fun fact, the man continued coldly, “So after you obtain that, leave this place immediately. That is the sole reward you will be able to gain from your visit to this place.”

To be honest, the entire situation was a surprise to me. I didn’t know what was actually going on, but it wasn’t as if I had any way of figuring out who this guy in front of me was. However, I knew one thing for sure...
Who the hell is he to boss me around?
This guy didn’t know how to deal with barbarians at all. With how much of an asshole he was being, I wouldn’t do what he asked me, even if I’d planned on doing it in the first place.
“Well, you’re wrong,” I rebutted. “Rewards aren’t just physical things. Now piss off and stop getting in my way. I need to finish my conversation with this man named Ormi Noark.”

Sure, I was beyond curious who this entity was, but I tried my best not to make it obvious, and it was for one very simple reason: The person who desired less was usually the one who would take control of the conversation.
“He was practically spilling all his beans for me, and now this weird guy appeared in his stead,” I complained, huffing to make my point.
I watched his brow twitch into a frown for a split second. From my experience, that was a sign that he was getting pissed with me. Despite being so offended, though, he wasn’t doing anything.
So talking is all he can do.
Because there was still some doubt in my mind, I decided to experiment a little bit.

“If you want me to leave, why didn’t you say this instead? ‘In exchange for taking the Orb of Fire, please leave this place without causing a scene...’ Something like that.” When he didn’t respond, I continued, “Can you not do that? Wow. I don’t know how you were raised, but you have no manners.” The entity went to speak, but I quickly interrupted him. “Whatever. Just bring that guy back. I have nothing to say to you.”
He remained silent for a while before asking, “If I say that, will you leave?”
Oh, was he actually going to do it? With no way of knowing for certain, I just shrugged. “I’ll see. One genuine word could be the thing that changes everything.”
“...In exchange for taking the Orb of Fire, please leave this place.”
Wow, he actually did it.
I tensed my facial muscles to stop the edges of my lips from curling up. “That’s better.”
“Then—”
“But isn’t it ‘common sense’ for you to introduce yourself when you’re requesting something?”
Having been caught in the trap of barbarian common sense, the entity began to shake in anger. However, it seemed that was all he could do, as soon enough, he was revealing his identity to me.
“I am Ormi Noark.”
“Oh, so you’re the original, then?”
“If you know that much, then this conversation will be quick. What you were just talking to was an entity that is a reenactment of my past self.”

I’d just tossed the word “original” out there without much thought, so the immediate response I got back was shocking enough to nearly make me shout. Still, there was something that pulled me straight back to reality.
“Since I’ve introduced myself, can you now—”
Heh, he was taking every opportunity he got. “Together.”
He shot me a confused look.
“Since you know now, make your request and your introduction together.”
“...I am the original Ormi Noark. Please do not taint this memory any further and leave with the Orb of Fire. Please.”
The request was extremely polite compared to before. Once again, I gave it a serious moment of thought before handing him an answer. “Hmm... I don’t want to.”
“What?”
“I’m not leaving.”
“That’s not what you promised—!”
“What promise? I said, ‘I’ll see.’”
“I... I am genuinely begging you.”
“And I took a genuine moment to consider it, and I’m not leaving.”
“You were planning on making a fool out of me from the beginning...”
“Make a fool out of you? What are you talking about? You made a sincere request, and I took a sincere amount of time to think before refusing your request. Is there a problem with your head?”
“You should know your place!”
Hmm, resorting to insults now...
Since this shameless individual had no intention of learning his manners despite my teachings and had even misinterpreted my genuine response, I no longer saw a reason to continue going easy on him.
Even as he shouted, I didn’t retreat but instead took a big step forward, using my barbarian figure to my advantage to look down at him. “What are you going to do about it?”
Size and battle strength didn’t have much correlation at our levels...
“From the looks of things, you can’t do much about me being here, can you?”
...but our conversation up to this point had proven to me that he posed me no threat.
“Because you would’ve kicked me out already. Am I wrong?”
As I expected, he fell quiet. However, it didn’t seem he was a complete fool, as he skipped past all the unnecessary dialogue and went straight to the point. “What do you want?”
“Information—or physical rewards equivalent to that.”
“That orb is all the physical reward you can take from here!”
“That would’ve been the case originally. But we aren’t in a normal situation now, are we?”

Things had progressed to the point that an entity claiming to be the original version of himself had appeared. It was clear that he’d cough up something if I continued to shake him down. Apparently, though, he had seen through my clear-as-day intentions.
He bit his lip in anger. “Shameless bastard.”
“To my ears, that’s a compliment.”
“There are no physical rewards I can give you. I don’t even have that authority in me to begin with.”
“Then you’ll need to give me information. I’ve met a few people like you who call themselves the ‘original.’ Just what are you...? Huh. Are you using your right to remain silent?”
He smirked. “And if I am? What will you do about it?”
Whoa, so that was the approach he was going to take?
“Well, I don’t know yet,” I admitted. “But if you keep staying quiet, I’ll go down and take the Orb of Fire from your basement.”
He snorted at that. That attitude of his didn’t last long, however.
“After that, I’ll destroy everything. I’ll destroy the house, destroy Zephyros, destroy your body, and even destroy that mother.”
“Even... Even the mother?” he mumbled in apparent shock.
So this guy didn’t know what true equality was.
“Didn’t you ask what I’d do? I’ve only told you the answer you wanted to hear. And if I happen to make good on my word...what can you do then?” I taunted.
“I will recreate everything. The Orb of Fire, this house, their lives... I can just recreate them again. This whole thing is but a play created by that child to begin with.”
Now I kept quiet, waiting for him to finish. Soon enough, he revealed, “However, even if I am able to restore everything, I cannot bear to see you beat Tarvian to death.”
“Oh?”
“Fine. You win, barbarian. Ask me something else. I will answer everything I can.”
“Then—”
“But I cannot tell you about my origins. That is something that I cannot share even if I wanted to, so don’t get it twisted.”
“Even so, my answers are sure to be better than the ones my past self was giving you. I know much more now than he did back then.”
Hmm, I guess that’s true...
Still, I couldn’t help but feel dissatisfied with my gains somehow.
“Now, choose. I have presented you with all the possible options.”
Those words were his final declaration.
After taking a moment to think, I gave a nod. “Sure.”
It was time to have an intelligent conversation.

chapters.title: Chapter 823: Lifeline (7)
paragraphs: The intelligent conversation that followed was peaceful and effective. I asked, and he answered—no tricks or tomfoolery to be had.
“Then I’ll ask this first. In the past, I happened to come across your diary and read it. On the final page of that diary, it said, ‘Today, we die.’ What happened after that?”
He answered my first question willingly, revealing to me a dark story that he wove in a calm and matter-of-fact tone.

“We all decided to die together, and so we ate the drug that Travian created for us. However, for some reason, I didn’t die. It may have been because of a resistance that I had built up after consuming all sorts of transformative drugs while I was a soldier.”
Their plans to die together on the same day failed when Ormi Noark survived.

“There weren’t any more drugs left...so I left this home where my allies slept and wandered out. I couldn’t find the demons that I was looking for, but it didn’t matter. The flames burned my skin, and the scalding air ruined my lungs. With this, I thought I’d be able to return to their sides soon enough.”
However, if this second plan had succeeded, he wouldn’t be here telling me this story.
“Even so, I survived.”
“How is that possible?” I wondered.

“While I was slowly being burned alive, a demon appeared. A welcome creature that would end my suffering. However, when I approached it with a smile, an arrow suddenly flew in and shot it in the back of its head.”

The man bit down on his lip in pain before continuing, “It was the rescue party. The people whom the four of us had been so desperately waiting for. Even as I lost consciousness due to the exhaustion of it all, I could hear that voice. That gentle voice, telling me not to worry, that I would survive.”
With that, the man closed his eyes in despair. And when he woke up later...
“A few days had passed, and I had been saved by the rescue party and was being transported out of this damn Great Demon Realm.”
He told the party to return to where he had been, to retrieve the remains of his allies at least, but the rescue party refused and said they didn’t have the luxury for something like that.
“A wave of regret swept over me. Just one day... If we had made our decision just one day later, everyone would’ve been rescued. We would have all survived.”
Having been rescued after years of waiting, the man contemplated what was left for him in this life.
“Should I live, or should I die?”

However, that decision had already been made for him as well. The living had their own responsibilities to fulfil, after all. In the end, he wasn’t able to throw himself down the cliff of despair, and so his story continued.
However, before I heard the rest of it, I asked one thing.
“This rescue party you’re talking about, who were they?”
“Rafdonia.”
“What?”
“Ravigion Kommelby Rafdonia.”
The Immortal, Ravigion III.
“More specifically, it was him and the allies he had been making history with.”

Fate had inexplicably twisted for the man who could welcome only death. In truth, the man had met the Immortal before this encounter. The Immortal was of the direct bloodline of the territory lord’s family, after all, and this man was a son of one of the vassal houses.
“However, when the war intensified, a conscription order was given to even the territories in the countryside, and I had to leave the territory before I was even of age.”
Because of that, there was a long gap of twenty years before this reunion.
Curious, I asked, “What was he like?”

“Even though it had been a while since I had seen him, he was the same as before. He hadn’t lost his cheerful persona and was still witty with his words. He had the energy of a prankster, but I could always sense the respect and care he had for those around him.”
“So he was normal.”

“Normal... Well, perhaps. I suppose you could see it that way. That is, if the world hadn’t been in that situation.” Then, the man said, “His laughter and bright energy didn’t suit this hopeless world. Having met him again... How do I put this? He had become great. Great enough that even an ordinary person like me could notice in an instant.”

Huh. I hadn’t expected a guy with the name of Noark to praise the Immortal. The strangeness of it left me reeling for a bit, but I decided to focus for now. I would get my chance to sort through the feeling after hearing the rest of his story.
“In this world without hope, he had been roaming around the continent with his allies to find that hope again. That was how he was able to find me in the Great Demon Realm.”
“What happened after that?”
“He took me to Rafdonia first so that they could restock their equipment.”
“That must’ve been nice. Being able to return home after so long.”

“Well, I don’t know if I’d call that place my home...” Noticing my obvious confusion, he explained, “It wasn’t the Rafdonia I knew. Instead, it was a shelter created deep in the underground to survive the End. The survivors there were struggling to just pass the day.”

“Ah...” The moment he said it, I got the feeling this “shelter” he was talking about was, in fact, Noark. I did hear that that city had been created by Rafdonia once upon a time, hence the dimensional square there. Only after their skills developed did they leave the underground, build the city walls, and create the grand kingdom of Rafdonia as it was now.

“In any case, I returned to that Rafdonia, and he parted with his group once more, leaving me the heavy burden of managing the shelter. I still have no idea what he saw in me to entrust such an important task to me. Maybe it was the historic vassal name of Noark that I possessed, or... Maybe he wanted to give me a purpose when I had been left to wander away my days, just waiting for death...”
The man couldn’t have known this, but while he had been left behind and did his best to manage the shelter, Ravigion had gone off for his grand adventure.

“Every time he returned, survivors from every corner of the world returned with him and gathered together. The shelter developed, and the number of people who left on his journeys with him increased as well.”
And so, time passed.
“He finally finished his great journey and discovered the hope for this world.”
“What was it?”
“I cannot answer any question related to my origin. However, you should already know what it is.”
I let out a quiet mumble. “The labyrinth...”
The man didn’t respond, but that was answer enough.
If I combine this with the information Arta gave me... Does that mean the Immortal obtained the Power of Origin at the end of his journey?
This secret ancient history was filled to the brim with interesting and exciting plot points. However, unfortunately for me, all the stories that followed were locked away beyond my reach.

“Did you know? Sometimes, hope only births even deeper despair. The hope that he discovered was no different from looking away from the despair in front of our eyes and toward a different source of despair.”
“How about you just tell me directly what this is, instead of going in circles with riddles?” I grunted.
“I cannot.”
I sighed. Was this another one of those questions related to the origin or something?
“Having learned all truths, he devised a plan to save the world. The uninformed were satisfied with this, but those who knew the truth could only be horrified at his plans.”
“And I suppose you can’t tell me what this plan was?”
He was silent.
“Yeah, figures. It’s fine, so just tell me everything else you can tell me.”

“Those who agreed to his plans were sick and tired of the underground. They left with him and created a kingdom above ground. Those who couldn’t agree to his plan, including me, remained in the underground city.”

Hmm... This felt like an itch I couldn’t scratch. Although I now knew why the underground refuge city of Rafdonia was called Noark, the questions that I actually wanted answered weren’t being answered.
“What about the Ormi Revolutionary Corps?” I pressed, getting impatient. “Can you not tell me anything about that either?”
“I have told you everything I can.”
“What about Gabrielius? What kind of bastard is that guy?”
“He was the greatest companion on the journey Ravigion took, and the man who executed that terrible plan. Well, in the end, he also seemed to have changed his mind and turned away.”
“What do you mean by turned away?”
Silence.
Man. I’d wanted to get a decent answer for that one at least. Still, combined with everything I’d heard from Arta, I got the sense that I was taking gradual steps toward the truth about this world.
“Alright, then I’ve told you everything I could. I hope that you can leave now.”
As he signaled that this conversation was over, I gave a stern shake of my head. “No.”
“No matter how much you push me, I have nothing else I can tell—”
“That’s not it. I’ll need to take what is mine before I go.”
Wasn’t he the one who told me I could upgrade my Orb of Fire?
“Pretty sure the basement is that way, correct?”
I was going to get what I could and then leave.
[You have obtained the Pristine Orb of Fire.]
[The Orb of Fire in your possession has evolved into a Perfect Orb of Fire.]

When I went down to the basement and grabbed the other Orb of Fire, it combined with the one I originally had and changed its appearance. Although its form didn’t change completely, the flame that was burning within the orb seemed to grow much more powerful.
I can test out its effects later...
Still, this was incredibly interesting to me. An event like this had never appeared, not even when I obtained two Orbs of Fire. Did it have to be the Orb of Fire from this place in particular?
Just then, a new question popped into my mind.
“Noark, where are we?”
Just what was this place? I could tell it wasn’t simply the Hidden World accessible through Mila Roden’s mirror.
“Shelter.”
Oh, the field name was different from the jump.
“How do you enter this place? What are the conditions?”
He took a pause, then said, “I cannot tell you. As the name suggests, this place is my shelter. One that I cannot allow anyone else entry into.”
“But then how did we end up here?”
“You can only access it if the entire labyrinth is unstable.”
“Must mean the method of entry is pretty difficult.” Was it something like gathering seven different Orbs of Fire like that one show? Well, not that it mattered now that I’d finished.
“Now leave. I have given you everything I have to give.”
“Hey, don’t rush me. I’ll be forced to leave at some point, whether or not I want to stay.”

Though Noark didn’t respond, I exited the basement back into the living room and took a moment to look around. Zephyros was still standing tall near the door like a broken robot. If I went upstairs, the woman named Tarvian and the child would probably be in a similar state.
“This whole thing is but a play created by that child to begin with.”
Suddenly, I recalled that phrase I heard from Noark. Why did that word “play” leave such an impression on me?

“A play just for one person... I think I get why this place is called Shelter.” Noark didn’t respond to my mumblings, and for some reason, I couldn’t help but say it when I saw his muted reaction. “Are you satisfied?”
No answer came this time either. However, his expression was an answer in and of itself.
It was one of bitterness, as if to ask back how I could even think he could be satisfied.
My instinctive barbarian repulsion to anyone who looked like that activated, and I ended up patting him strongly on his back.
Smack! Smack!
The slaps made quite a loud sound each time, too.
“Wh-what are you—?!”
He freaked out like a neutral monster who just got damaged, and I rushed to speak before the situation could escalate.
“Just hold on for a little longer.”
“What?”
“I don’t like how everything is now either.”
Honestly, I had nothing else I could say to him. I knew too little to make any promises to him.
“Were you perhaps trying to console me?” he asked, belatedly realizing my intentions. I just shrugged at that, then left the house.
Fwoosh!
Because the protection of the Orb of Fire was no longer present within, the building began to burn down as I moved farther away.
I took a moment to stop and watch—then clicked my tongue.
When we eventually left, that building would rebuild itself, and that guy would secretly watch the events of his past play out like some pervert.
My feelings were clear now.
I don’t like this at all.
And when I didn’t like something, I needed to get rid of it.
That was the way of the barbarian.

After leaving Noark’s Shelter, I regrouped with my allies, who had been carefully observing the area. We then began to reorganize ourselves before the dimensional collapse resumed. Those who needed to rest rested plentifully, and those who had some time freely talked with each other about what would soon happen and prepared for any and all scenarios to come.
As for me, I went with Raven to check on the effectiveness of the newly upgraded Orb of Fire.
“Th-there’s no way the numbers are wrong, right?”
“Why are you the one asking that?”
The results were surprising to say the least.
[All fire damage within 15 yards is decreased by 90%.]
The phrase “continuous damage” had disappeared. The effect now applied to all fire damage. A fifteen-yard radius where all fire damage within its aura would be decreased by 90 percent.
This is nuts...
Fire was nothing now.
